articles.title: Acute effects of weight-bearing high-intensity interval training before dinner on postprandial glucose concentrations in patients with type 2 diabetes: an exploratory crossover trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: In this study, we conducted an exploratory analysis to examine the effects of weight-bearing high-intensity interval training (HIIT) performed before evening meals on postprandial glucose concentrations, comparing it to pedaling exercise and sitting at rest.

METHODS: Eleven individuals with type 2 diabetes completed three experimental conditions: the H condition, in which they performed weight-bearing exercise-based HIIT before dinner; the P condition, in which they engaged in pedaling exercise before dinner; and the C condition, in which they consumed dinner without structured physical activity. The primary outcome was the incremental area under the curve of glucose concentration (iAUC) up to 3 h after dinner.

RESULTS: The main effect of condition on iAUC was not statistically significant (F[2, 18] = 2.35, p = 0.124). However, pairwise comparisons demonstrated large effect sizes favoring the intervention conditions over the C condition, with within-participant differences of 2845.3 (95% CI - 936.1 to 6626.8; adjusted p = 0.162; Cohen's d = 0.90) for H and 2857.0 (95% CI - 924.4 to 6638.4; adjusted p = 0.160; Cohen's d = 0.90) for P, while no difference was observed between H and P (adjusted p = 1.000). As a secondary outcome, systolic blood pressure immediately after exercise was significantly higher in the H condition than in the P condition.

CONCLUSION: In this preliminary study, an intervention involving weight-bearing exercise-based HIIT and pedaling exercise performed before dinner demonstrated an acute tendency to attenuate post-dinner glucose iAUC with large effect sizes in individuals with type 2 diabetes, despite not reaching statistical significance.

articles.title: Metastasis-directed therapy in addition to definitive locoregional radiotherapy for De novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: De novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (mNPC) carries a poor prognosis with systemic therapy alone. Locoregional radiotherapy (LRRT) improves survival in chemotherapy-responsive patients, but the incremental role of metastasis-directed therapy (MDT) remains undefined.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 54 patients with de novo mNPC treated between 2013 and 2024 at a tertiary cancer centre. All received platinum-based induction chemotherapy followed by definitive LRRT; selected patients underwent MDT to metastatic sites. Overall survival (OS), recurrence-free survival (RFS) and distant recurrence-free survival (DRFS) were estimated by Kaplan-Meier methods, with Cox regression for univariable and multivariable analysis.

RESULTS: At a median follow-up of 27 months, 2-year OS, RFS and DRFS were 67.5%, 45.4% and 52.7%. MDT was associated with improved 2-year OS (92.3% vs 55.2%; p = 0.0069), RFS (81.9% vs 28.2%; p < 0.001) and DRFS (93.8% vs 35.0%; p < 0.001). On multivariable analysis MDT remained associated with improved RFS (HR 0.27, 95% CI 0.08-0.98; p = 0.047), with consistent estimates in a 2-month landmark analysis (HR 0.26, 95% CI 0.075-0.90) and with MDT modelled as a time-varying covariate (HR 0.17, 95% CI 0.040-0.76); the association with OS was not statistically significant (HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.06-1.13; p = 0.072). Oligometastatic disease was more frequent among patients receiving MDT (88% vs 41%). The association was most evident in the oligometastatic subgroup. In exploratory analyses, detectable post-treatment plasma EBV DNA and elevated post-LRRT PET SUV were associated with inferior survival.

CONCLUSION: In chemotherapy-responsive de novo mNPC treated with definitive LRRT, consolidative MDT was associated with improved disease control in multivariable, landmark and time-varying analyses, with a directionally consistent but non-significant association with OS. As residual confounding cannot be excluded, these findings support prospective evaluation in selected patients.

articles.title: Microglia promote infiltration and polarization of macrophages in cerebral ischemia‑reperfusion via the reactive oxygen species‑SPI1‑CCL9 axis.
articles.abstract: The aim of the present study was to investigate the role of microglia in promoting macrophage infiltration and polarization during cerebral ischemia‑reperfusion (I/R) injury through the reactive oxygen species (ROS)‑Spi‑1 proto‑oncogene (SPI1)‑chemokine (C‑C motif) ligand 9 (CCL9) signalling axis. Using a cerebral I/R in vitro and in vivo model, microglial activation and macrophage dynamics were assessed. ROS levels were quantified, and SPI1 expression in microglia was analysed. CCL9 secretion was measured, and its impact on macrophage migration and polarization was evaluated in vitro. CCL9 antibody and RNA interference approaches were used to interrogate the signalling pathway. Following cerebral I/R, microglial activation led to increased ROS production, and increased SPI1 and CCL9 expression. This, in turn, increased CCL9 secretion, which attracted macrophages to the site of ischemia and promoted their polarization towards a pro‑inflammatory phenotype. Inhibition of the ROS‑SPI1‑CCL9 axis significantly reduced macrophage infiltration and altered their polarization state. The results of the present study demonstrated that microglia facilitated macrophage infiltration and polarization in cerebral I/R via the ROS‑SPI1‑CCL9 axis, highlighting a potential therapeutic target for mitigating neuroinflammatory damage after a cerebral ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Generating Real-World Evidence From AI Deployed in Health Systems.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Health systems increasingly deploy predictive and generative artificial intelligence (AI) to improve care delivery and outcomes. Predictive AI models estimate the risk of future events to inform targeted interventions, while generative AI systems extract, summarize, and communicate information and may automate selected tasks. Routine deployment generates clinical, operational, and interaction data that can support evaluation of the effectiveness and safety of AI-enabled workflows.

METHODS: We review approaches to generating real-world evidence (RWE) from routine deployment of predictive and generative AI across four implementation configurations: silent deployment, human-in-the-loop (HITL), human-on-the-loop (HOTL), and automated. For each configuration, we describe the evaluation questions, routinely generated data, and feasible study designs.

RESULTS: Each implementation configuration supports different forms of evidence about model performance, workflow effectiveness, human oversight, and safety. For both predictive and generative AI, silent deployment supports assessment of local performance and subgroup differences. Once predictive AI drives action, evaluating the effectiveness of an implemented workflow (HITL, HOTL, or automated) generally requires causal inference approaches. For generative AI, HITL implementations can generate data on edits, overrides, time on task, usability, cognitive burden, and safety-relevant failure modes. HOTL and automated generative AI implementations can generate data on escalation performance, human follow-up work, downstream outcomes, and safety signals.

CONCLUSION: AI implementation should be paired with methods for generating RWE on the effectiveness and safety of AI-enabled workflows. In HOTL and automated configurations, escalation performance and residual human workload become particularly important components of evaluation.

articles.title: DUF6383-domain containing protein from Parabacteroides distasonis predicts survival in patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis.
articles.abstract: Intestinal dysbiosis is a hallmark of alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) characterized by a higher abundance of unfavorable species and a reduction of beneficial species. In this study, we aimed to analyze the bacterial proteome of stool samples from patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) (n = 80), alcohol use disorder (AUD; n = 20), and controls (n = 19) from an international multicenter cohort using quantitative tandem mass tag (TMT)-based metaproteomic profiling. We validated our results in an independent multicenter cohort of 72 patients with AH at the genomic level using qPCR. We detected 2,364 bacterial proteins and identified distinct metaproteomic signatures separating controls, patients with AUD, and AH. Patients with AUD and AH were characterized by depletion of Firmicutes-derived proteins and enrichment of proteins from Bacteroidetes, Proteobacteria, and Actinobacteria. Eighteen bacterial proteins increased with disease severity, many with multifunctional "moonlighting" roles, including enolase and hexokinase. DUF6383 domain-containing protein from Parabacteroides distasonis is correlated with histological injury, inflammatory cell infiltration, and is linked to neutrophil degranulation in the host. Patients with a high abundance of DUF6383 domain-containing protein had significantly lower 90-day survival, and this association was validated by qPCR at the genomic level in a second cohort. Our findings show that microbial proteins are associated with disease severity and progression, and that DUF6383 domain-containing protein from P. distasonis is a potential prognostic biomarker for AH.

articles.title: Baseline depressive-symptom severity and divergent psychological trajectories during GIP and/or GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy: a prospective ecological momentary assessment study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The influence of baseline depressive-symptom severity on psychological trajectories during incretin receptor agonists (glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide [GIP] and/or glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists [GLP-1RA]) therapy remains unclear. We evaluated short-term changes in binge-eating tendency and depressive symptoms during GIP/GLP-1RA therapy, stratified by baseline severity.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Fifteen adults with type 2 diabetes or obesity (mean age 55.6 years; body weight 89.9 kg) initiating or switching GIP/GLP-1RA therapy completed daily ecological momentary assessment (EMA) of binge-eating tendency for 85 days and weekly Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) assessments. Longitudinal changes were analysed using linear mixed-effects models, stratified by baseline PHQ-9 severity (low: <10; high: ≥10).

RESULTS: Body weight and binge-eating tendency decreased significantly (both p < 0.001). A significant Week × Group interaction for depressive symptoms (p < 0.001) indicated divergent trajectories: scores decreased in the low baseline group (p = 0.026) but increased in the high baseline group (p = 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory study, baseline depressive-symptom severity was associated with divergent depressive-symptom trajectories during incretin receptor agonist therapy, whereas reductions in body weight and binge-eating tendency appeared independent of baseline mood.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13340-026-00942-1.

articles.title: Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression and changes in the fibrosis-4 index after luseogliflozin treatment in participants with type 2 diabetes and MASLD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is common in type 2 diabetes. We investigated the association between monocyte mRNA expression of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2), the molecular target of luseogliflozin, and changes in the fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index during treatment with this agent.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective observational study used prospectively collected peripheral blood monocyte samples from 82 participants with type 2 diabetes and MASLD who had received luseogliflozin for at least 6 months. Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was measured using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. Clinical and laboratory parameters, including FIB-4 index, were evaluated at baseline and 6 months after luseogliflozin initiation. Changes were calculated as the 6-month value minus the baseline value; therefore, negative values indicated reductions.

RESULTS: After 6 months, waist circumference, hemoglobin A1c, liver enzyme levels, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, and the FIB-4 index decreased significantly. Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was negatively correlated with the change in the FIB-4 index, indicating that higher baseline expression was associated with a greater reduction. In multiple regression analyses, natural-log-transformed baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression remained associated with the change in the FIB-4 index after adjustment for baseline clinical variables.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was associated with a greater reduction in the FIB-4 index after luseogliflozin treatment. This finding should be interpreted as an exploratory association between a cell-specific transcriptomic feature and changes in a fibrosis-related index, rather than as evidence of functional SGLT2 signaling in monocytes or histological fibrosis regression.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13340-026-00941-2.

articles.title: Baseline monocyte GIP receptor mRNA expression is associated with reductions in body weight and FIB-4 index after switching to tirzepatide in patients with type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tirzepatide improves body weight and glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes, but factors associated with inter-individual differences after switching remain unclear. We examined whether baseline monocyte glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor (GIPR) mRNA expression was associated with changes in body weight and the fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index after switching from glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) to tirzepatide.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 90 patients with type 2 diabetes who had received a GLP-1RA for at least 6 months before switching. Baseline monocyte GIPR mRNA expression was measured by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. Associations with percentage body-weight change and FIB-4 index change during the 6 months after tirzepatide initiation were assessed by correlation and multivariable regression. Exploratory ex vivo assays were performed to assess monocyte responses to native GIP.

RESULTS: Higher baseline monocyte GIPR mRNA expression was associated with greater reductions in body weight and the FIB-4 index and remained significant in multivariable models. The association with the FIB-4 index remained significant after additional adjustment for percentage body-weight change at 6 months after tirzepatide initiation. GIPR mRNA expression was not associated with body-weight change during the preceding 6 months of GLP-1RA therapy. Native GIP suppressed lipopolysaccharide-induced interleukin-6 and tumor necrosis factor-alpha responses in monocytes.

CONCLUSIONS: Baseline monocyte GIPR mRNA expression was associated with body-weight and FIB-4 index reductions after switching to tirzepatide. It may represent an exploratory marker of clinical changes, but treatment specificity, causal GIPR-dependent mechanisms, and structural liver fibrosis regression were not established.

GRAPHICAL ABSTRACT: Summary of the study design and main finding. Baseline GIPR mRNA expression in peripheral blood monocytes was associated with reductions in body weight and the FIB-4 index after switching to tirzepatide in patients with type 2 diabetes. In exploratory ex vivo assays, native GIP suppressed LPS-induced inflammatory responses, supporting monocyte GIPR expression as a candidate exploratory marker requiring further validation.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13340-026-00940-3.

articles.title: Persistent prefectural ordering of billed urinary albumin quantification in Japan: a nationwide longitudinal ecological study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nationwide Japanese claims studies have documented regional variation in quantitative urinary albumin or protein testing, but it is unclear whether geographic ordering persists over time or depends on the denominator used. We evaluated the persistence of prefectural ordering in billed urinary albumin quantification and examined its robustness using a population-based denominator.

METHODS: This ecological provider-location study used National Database Open Data for 47 prefectures. FY2015-FY2022 was the primary historical interval; FY2023-FY2024 was a scope-aligned extension. The primary metric was urinary albumin quantification billing counts per 1,000 HbA1c billing counts. A sensitivity analysis used counts per 100,000 total population. Equal-weight dispersion, endpoint Spearman correlations, Kendall's W across annual ranks, and cross-metric rank correspondence were calculated.

RESULTS: During FY2015-FY2022, the national primary metric increased from 26.20 to 33.54 (+ 28.0%). Prefectural ordering was highly persistent (Spearman rho = 0.904; Kendall's W = 0.964). The population-referenced rate increased from 1,480.7 to 2,270.9 per 100,000 (+ 53.4%) and showed comparable persistence (rho = 0.920; W = 0.967). Annual rank correlations between the two metrics ranged from 0.893 to 0.915. FY2024 extension values were 36.19 per 1,000 HbA1c counts and 2,570.4 per 100,000 population, with persistence maintained.

CONCLUSIONS: Prefectural ordering of billed urinary albumin quantification persisted under both HbA1c-referenced and population-referenced definitions. These findings identify a stable geographic billing pattern but do not establish its demographic, clinical, or organizational determinants or estimate patient-level albuminuria-testing coverage.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13340-026-00944-z.

articles.title: Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) Mapping and Visualization of Pre-Implementation Determinants for Sepsis Care Transitions.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: High-quality care transitions are essential for sepsis survivors at risk of readmission and long-term complications. These complex innovations require coordination across organizations, individuals, and processes. The Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) offers a systematic approach to identifying multi-level implementation determinants, but translating them into actionable strategies remains challenging. This study examines the representation of implementation determinants across CFIR domains and visualizes their cross-domain interconnectedness.

METHODS: CFIR-guided, semi-structured pre-implementation needs assessment interviews were conducted with stakeholders involved in sepsis care transitions across five hospital-home healthcare (HHC) dyads. Thirty-two themes identified through deductive-inductive coding were mapped to CFIR domains and constructs and visualized using node diagrams.

RESULTS: Sixty-one interviews with 91 stakeholders identified 32 themes spanning all five CFIR domains, with most themes mapping to multiple domains. Access to Care theme mapped across all five domains, while External Policies and Incentives and Informal Caregiving themes were represented only once. Implementation Process domain was most represented and Innovation least represented. All constructs within the Implementation Process and Individual Characteristics domains were captured. Node diagrams illustrated the depth and interconnected influence of determinants in sepsis care transitions.

CONCLUSIONS: Stakeholders identified complexity emerged across technical, structural, and policy domains as both an innovation feature and contextual determinants of sepsis care transitions. CFIR mapping and visualization provided a structured approach to characterizing pre-implementation complexity in sepsis care transitions. Examining determinant representation and cross-domain interconnectedness may help identify cross-cutting, potentially high-leverage implementation needs and inform strategy selection and tailoring for complex hospital-to-home interventions.

articles.title: Epstein-Barr Virus Serologic Profiles in Multiple Sclerosis and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Although the link between Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and multiple sclerosis (MS) is well established, geographic variation in EBV epidemiology warrants region-specific data from Asian populations. Beyond MS, the role of EBV in myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) remains far less studied. This study aimed to compare EBV serostatus and antibody titers in patients with MS, MOGAD, and controls in a Korean cohort.

METHODS: We analyzed MS (n = 130), MOGAD (n = 125), and untreated tumor controls without known EBV association (n = 132). MS and controls were frequency-matched to MOGAD by age at sampling. Serum Epstein-Barr nuclear antigen 1 (EBNA1) IgG, viral capsid antigen (VCA) IgG, VCA IgM, and early antigen (EA) IgG were measured using chemiluminescence immunoassays (LIAISON, DiaSorin). EBV seropositivity was defined as EBNA1 IgG or VCA IgG positivity, and serologic findings suggestive of possible recent infection/reactivation were defined as positivity for VCA IgM or EA IgG.

RESULTS: EBV seropositivity was nearly universal in MS, MOGAD, and controls (98.5%, 98.4%, and 99.2%, p = 0.751). EBNA1 responses differed across groups, with the frequency of EBNA1 IgG levels exceeding the upper reportable limit (>600 U/mL) being highest in MS, compared with MOGAD and controls (66.2% vs 33.6% vs 43.9%; p < 0.001). In three-group analyses using controls as reference, MS had higher EBNA1 IgG levels (adjusted geometric mean ratio [aGMR], 1.54; p = 0.006), whereas MOGAD did not. For VCA IgG, MS did not differ from controls, whereas MOGAD showed lower levels than controls (aGMR, 0.72; p = 0.018). Among patients with MS and MOGAD, models additionally adjusted for disease-related factors indicated that EBNA1 IgG and VCA IgG levels were higher in MS (aGMR, 1.97; p < 0.001 and aGMR, 1.42; p = 0.018, respectively), while ongoing treatment at sampling was associated with lower VCA IgG levels (aGMR, 0.64; p = 0.007). Serologic findings suggestive of possible recent EBV infection or reactivation were comparable across groups.

DISCUSSION: In this Korean cohort, MS showed stronger EBNA1 responses than MOGAD and controls, extending prior evidence on the relevance of EBNA1 in MS to an Asian population. The absence of a similar pattern in MOGAD suggests that the contribution of EBV may differ between the 2 diseases.

articles.title: Reciprocal regulation between NDP52 and PRRSV: a bidirectional host-virus interplay.
articles.abstract: Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV) is a major swine pathogen responsible for substantial economic losses worldwide. The selective autophagy receptor NDP52 plays a critical role in antiviral defense, yet its function during PRRSV infection remains poorly understood. In this study, we show that NDP52 restricts PRRSV replication: overexpression reduced viral titers and N protein levels, while knockdown enhanced replication. NDP52 specifically reduced Nsp12 protein levels, which was partially reversed by the autophagy inhibitor 3-methyladenine (3-MA). Conversely, PRRSV infection decreased NDP52 protein levels at late stages without affecting its mRNA levels. Screening of viral proteins identified Nsp1α, Nsp10, and GP3 as being associated with reduced NDP52 levels; this reduction was blocked by 3-MA. Together, these findings suggest a bidirectional host-virus interplay, in which NDP52 restricts viral replication by reducing Nsp12, while the virus counteracts this restriction via Nsp1α, Nsp10, and GP3.The precise mechanisms, including the role of autophagy, require further investigation.

articles.title: Endobronchial Valves for Persistent Air Leak and Bronchopleural Fistula in Children: A Systematic Review of Indications, Procedural Approaches, and Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent air leak (PAL) and bronchopleural fistula (BPF) are uncommon but important complications in children, particularly with necrotizing pneumonia, postoperative injury, malignancy, or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). When conservative therapy fails or surgery is high-risk, endobronchial or intrabronchial valve placement has emerged as a minimally invasive bronchoscopic option. This systematic review summarizes the published pediatric experience, focusing on indications, procedural approach, and outcomes.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to June 2026, with Google Scholar and reference lists screened; no language limits applied. Eligible studies reported pediatric or late-adolescent patients who underwent bronchoscopic valve placement for PAL, BPF, or pneumothorax with ongoing air leak. Case reports, case series, and observational studies with extractable pediatric data were included. Two reviewers independently screened, assessed eligibility, and abstracted data; findings were synthesized narratively.

RESULTS: Thirteen reports were included. Valve placement achieved rapid or eventual air-leak improvement in selected children, including those with necrotizing pneumonia, postoperative air leak, chronic ventilator dependence, malignancy, and ECMO support. Reported complications included valve migration or loosening, granulation tissue, minor hemoptysis, atelectasis, contralateral pneumothorax, and recurrent air leak, although many children underwent valve removal without complication.

CONCLUSION: Endobronchial or intrabronchial valve placement may be a useful rescue or bridge therapy for carefully selected children with refractory PAL or BPF. Evidence remains low certainty owing to small samples, retrospective design, inconsistent outcome definitions, and possible publication bias. Prospective multicenter registries with standardized reporting are needed to define optimal selection, timing, and safety.

articles.title: Comparison of the Safety and Efficacy of Remimazolam for Sedation in Adults Undergoing Fiberoptic Bronchoscopy: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fiberoptic bronchoscopy requires effective sedation to ensure patient comfort while preserving gas exchange, hemodynamic stability, and predictable recovery. Remimazolam, a novel ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine, has emerged as a potential alternative to traditional sedatives. However, its safety and efficacy compared with those of other sedatives remain under investigation. This meta-analysis evaluated the safety and efficacy of remimazolam versus dexmedetomidine, midazolam, and propofol in adults undergoing fiberoptic bronchoscopy.

METHODS: A systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was conducted using 5 databases through January 2026. Outcomes included respiratory depression, hypotension, bradycardia, time to target sedation depth, procedure success rate, emergence time, and postanesthesia care unit (PACU) stay. Relative risks (RR) or mean differences (MD) with 95% CI were calculated using a random-effects model.

RESULTS: Sixteen RCTs (2325 patients) were included. Remimazolam significantly reduced respiratory depression (RR: 0.51, 95% CI: 0.36-0.73, P<0.001), hypotension (RR: 0.50, 95% CI: 0.34-0.73, P<0.001), and bradycardia (RR: 0.37, 95% CI: 0.22-0.65, P=0.001) versus controls. Sedation onset was faster than dexmedetomidine (MD: -2.19 min), but slower than propofol (MD: 0.49 min). Success rates were comparable across groups (RR: 1.12, 95% CI: 0.98-1.28, P=0.097). Compared with dexmedetomidine and midazolam, remimazolam shortened emergence (MD: -1.79 and -4.37 min, respectively) and PACU stay (MD: -3.58 and -6.70 min).

CONCLUSION: Remimazolam provides effective sedation for fiberoptic bronchoscopy with advantages in terms of respiratory and hemodynamic safety, rapid recovery, and procedural efficiency.

articles.title: Valorisation of PET-rich mixed plastic waste using a cascading concept involving selective ammonolysis and catalytic pyrolysis.
articles.abstract: We report a cascading valorisation strategy for real polyethylene terephthalate (PET)-rich waste streams, combining selective ammonolysis of PET with catalytic pyrolysis of the non-PET residue. In this approach, PET-rich packaging waste is treated with ammonia in ethylene glycol to produce terephthaldiamide (TDA), while the remaining polyolefin (PO)-rich residue is subsequently upgraded to benzene, toluene, xylene (BTX), and light olefins over H-ZSM-5 catalyst. TDA is a valuable aromatic diamide and a potential precursor to p-phenylene diamine, a monomer used in the production of poly(p-phenyleneterephthalamide) (PPTA). For post-consumer PET trays, ammonolysis at 5 bar NH3, and 100 °C for 8 h, followed by a downstream separation procedure, resulted in an almost quantitative conversion of PET, yielding pure TDA as small crystals in 74 wt% (87 mol%) yield based on the PET content in the feed. The residue (mostly polyolefins) was converted to BTX (5 wt% on residue), and propene/butenes (19 wt%, on residue) using a catalytic in situ pyrolysis approach with H-ZSM-5 at 550 °C. The same strategy was applied to a PET-enriched, DKR-350 mixed-plastic packaging fraction, affording TDA in 71 wt% (87 mol%) yield based on the PET content, while catalytic pyrolysis of the residue produced BTX (3 wt%) and propene/isobutene (4 wt%) based on the residue. These results demonstrate that real PET-rich mixed plastic waste streams can be selectively upgraded into valuable aromatic diamide while retaining the non-PET fraction as a feedstock for petrochemical intermediates.

articles.title: Metformin Use Is Associated With Reduced Rates of Primary Nerve Decompression Surgery and Revision in Type 2 Diabetes: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of hand surgery global online
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Type 2 diabetes mellitus is a risk factor for compressive neuropathy. The purpose of this study was to determine whether metformin use is associated with reduced rates of compressive neuropathy, primary nerve decompression surgery, and revision after carpal tunnel release and cubital tunnel release, while controlling for concurrent diabetes medications.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX federated research network. Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus were stratified by metformin exposure, defined as at least 10 prescriptions over 5 years. The primary outcomes were incident compressive neuropathy and nerve decompression surgery. In a unilateral revision cohort, the outcome was ipsilateral revision between 30 days and 5 years after the index procedure. One-to-one propensity score matching balanced cohorts on demographics, comorbidities, and concurrent diabetes medications. Four prespecified medication-stratified sensitivity analyses addressed insulin, sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists. Carpal tunnel release and cubital tunnel release revision results were pooled via fixed-effect meta-analysis.

RESULTS: After matching, the primary analysis included 260,823 pairs. Metformin users had lower rates of nerve decompression surgery (0.60% vs 0.72%; odds ratio, OR, 0.831 [0.776-0.889]) and compressive neuropathy diagnosis (2.78% vs 3.05%; OR, 0.909 [0.879-0.941]). The surgery-level association was stronger without concurrent insulin (OR, 0.727 [0.662-0.799]) and attenuated to nonsignificance with concurrent insulin (OR, 0.948 [0.836-1.076]), though the diagnosis-level association persisted. Among patients with unilateral carpal or cubital tunnel syndrome, ipsilateral revision was less frequent in metformin users (pooled OR, 0.711 [0.533-0.950]). Metformin users also had lower vitamin B12 levels (mean, 646.4 vs 707.4 pg/mL), consistent with sustained metformin exposure.

CONCLUSIONS: Metformin use was associated with reduced incidence of nerve decompression surgery and ipsilateral revision after carpal tunnel release and cubital tunnel release in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, with directionally consistent effects across sensitivity analyses. These findings suggest that maintaining metformin therapy may carry benefit beyond glycemic control. Prospective studies are needed to validate these findings.

TYPE OF STUDY/LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Prognostic II.

articles.title: Liver fibrosis risk, missed follow-up, and inequitable specialist referral in the All of Us Research Program: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is highly prevalent and frequently undiagnosed, despite liver fibrosis being the strongest predictor of liver-related morbidity and mortality. We aimed to quantify Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index-based fibrosis risk and to evaluate guideline-recommended follow-up-FIB-4 documentation, confirmatory testing, and specialist referral-in a large US cohort.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of electronic health record data from the US All of Us Research Program. Among adults aged 35 years or older with sufficient laboratory data, FIB-4 scores were calculated from routinely captured biomarkers, classified as low (<1.3), indeterminate (1.3-2.67; 2.0-2.67 if aged ≥65 years), or high risk (>2.67), and described across sociodemographic and metabolic subgroups; associations with incident major adverse liver outcomes (MALO) were assessed with Cox proportional-hazards regression. We examined FIB-4 documentation, confirmatory testing, and specialty referrals within 365 days of the index FIB-4 date.

FINDINGS: Among 136,004 participants (mean age 60.8 years [SD 13.5]; 79,365 [58.4%] female; 81,420 [59.9%] White, 21,779 [16.0%] Hispanic or Latino, 20,076 [14.8%] Black), 26,971 (19.8%, 95% CI 19.6-20.0) had indeterminate and 11,217 (8.2%, 8.1-8.4) high FIB-4-based fibrosis risk. Elevated risk was more frequent with cardiovascular disease (41.7% vs 25.6%), hypertension (30.7% vs 23.4%), and type 2 diabetes (29.7% vs 27.4%), rising from 25.6% with no metabolic comorbidities to 36.6% with four. FIB-4 documentation was rare, and fewer than 1% of high-risk participants underwent confirmatory testing or referral; referral was low across risk categories (0.19% high, 0.19% indeterminate, 0.25% low risk). MALO occurred in 1308 (11.7%) high-risk vs 830 (0.8%) low-risk participants (adjusted hazard ratio 19.68, 95% CI 17.88-21.67).

INTERPRETATION: Routinely collected laboratory data identify substantial liver fibrosis risk in this volunteer US cohort, yet guideline-recommended follow-up is uncommon. Implementation strategies such as automated risk calculation and reflex-based testing pathways could reduce missed opportunities for earlier diagnosis and intervention.

FUNDING: No specific funding was received for this study.

articles.title: Burden of cardiovascular disease in Brazil, 1996-2023: a retrospective descriptive study of the epidemiology and impact on public healthcare.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) are the leading cause of death worldwide, and their epidemiology is correlated with genetic predisposition and exposure to risk. Brazil is a developing country with a vast territory, which leads to structural inequalities. We aimed to comprehensively characterise the epidemiology and burden of CVD in Brazil between 1996 and 2023, examining temporal trends, regional disparities, demographic patterns, healthcare costs, and heart transplantation.

METHODS: We conducted a nationwide retrospective descriptive ecological study using aggregated administrative data from the Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS), Brazil's publicly funded national health system. Mortality, hospitalization, and heart transplantation data from 1996 to 2023 were analysed according to sex, race/ethnicity, age, and geographic region. We estimated mortality rates for the major CVD, hospital length of stay, healthcare expenditures, and heart transplantation activity.

FINDINGS: Acute myocardial infarction remained the leading cause of cardiovascular mortality throughout the study period, while hypertensive diseases overtook heart failure after 2016 as the second leading cause of death. The overall CVD mortality rate-calculated as the number of CVD-related deaths divided by the total population and expressed as a percentage-increased from 7.3% in 1998 to 8.3% in 2023, peaking at 10.1% in 2021. Marked regional, age-, sex-, and race/ethnicity-related disparities were observed, including the complete absence of heart transplantation in the North region throughout the study period. Although hospitalization rates remained relatively stable, CVD-related healthcare expenditures and heart transplantation activity increased over time.

INTERPRETATION: CVD remains a major and growing public health challenge in Brazil, with substantial regional and demographic inequalities in disease burden and access to specialised care. These findings highlight the need for targeted public health strategies and more equitable allocation of healthcare resources to reduce cardiovascular morbidity and mortality.

FUNDING: This study was funded by CNPq, CAPES, FAPEMIG, INCT.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Mechanisms and precision intervention strategies of time-dependent dynamic regulation of matrix metalloproteinase-mediated cerebrovascular barrier disruption and neurovascular unit remodeling in stroke" [Exp. Neurol. 407 (2026) 116039].
Gut microbiota shaping fatty liver disease progression.
articles.abstract: The gut-liver axis is an important regulator of homeostasis, and its dysregulation has been implicated in the pathogenesis of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). In this review, we summarize current knowledge on both compositional alterations of the gut microbiome in MASLD and the functional consequences of these changes. We first discuss changes across major microbial domains, including bacteria, archaea, eukaryota, and bacteriophages, and then focus on microbiota-derived metabolites, such as short-chain fatty acids, trimethylamine and its derivative trimethylamine N-oxide, tryptophan-derived indoles, secondary bile acids, and other bioactive compounds. Their complex impacts on intestinal barrier integrity, inflammation, lipid and glucose metabolism, and immune and hormonal signaling in the liver are highlighted. We further examine mechanisms involving the translocation of microbial products and the modulation of nuclear and membrane receptors. Finally, we outline current challenges and knowledge gaps that need to be addressed to better understand the role of the gut microbiota in MASLD.

articles.title: Type 2 diabetes-associated gut microbial composition and short chain fatty acids differ across the epidemiologic transition in African origin populations.
articles.abstract: The gut microbiota and microbially produced short chain fatty acids (SCFAs) are increasingly linked to type 2 diabetes (T2D), particularly in the context of dietary transitions from fiber-rich to more ultra-processed foods. Data in African origin populations are lacking. We examined the cross-sectional relationships between the gut microbiota, SCFAs, and T2D by performing amplicon sequencing and targeted metabolomics from fecal samples and measuring fasting glucose, insulin, and C-peptide in 1505 African origin middle-aged adults from Ghana, South Africa, Jamaica, Seychelles, and the US. Microbial diversity and SCFAs were highest among Ghanaian and lowest among US participants. T2D was associated with lower microbial diversity, but not when stratifying by site. Differential abundance analysis (adjusted for site, sex, BMI, and age) identified microbes associated with T2D: Romboutsia was negatively associated with T2D, while positively associated taxa included Escherichia-Shigella sp., Dielma fastidiosa, Klebsiella, and Bacteroides vulgatus. Several species that were differentially abundant by T2D showed strong correlations with SCFA concentrations, although the significance varied by site. Our results suggest that associations between the gut microbiota, SCFAs, and T2D may differ by environmental, dietary, and ecological contexts. Amid the shifting global dietary patterns, further research is needed to inform gut microbiota-targeted approaches to address the global T2D burden.

articles.title: Identification of Tex and the Phage Shock Protein YthA as putative FtsH substrates associated with the cell envelope stress response in Lactococcus cremoris.
articles.abstract: As part of the Cell Envelope Stress (CES) response orchestrated by the two-component system CesSR in lactococci, the FtsH protease is expected to play a role in counteracting stress, as observed in other bacteria. However, neither its specific role nor its substrates have been identified in this genus. The primary objective of this study was therefore to elucidate the FtsH function in the context of CES. A Lactococcus cremoris NZ9000 ΔftsH exhibited an extended lag phase, increased salt and heat sensitivity and lysozyme resistance. However, only the salt and heat sensitive phenotype could be restored by complementation of the ftsH deletion. Whole-genome sequencing revealed putative compensatory mutations in ΔftsH, including genes encoding a transcriptional regulator and components of ABC transporters. Although awaiting experimental validation, these mutations may nevertheless underscore the broader physiological significance of FtsH in L. cremoris. Furthermore, a comparative proteomic analysis of L. cremoris NZ9000 ΔftsH under CES conditions identified putative FtsH substrates. In vivo degradation experiments demonstrated an extended half-life of the RNA-binding protein Tex and the Phage-Shock Protein YthA in a growth-phase dependent manner, thereby proposing these proteins as putative FtsH substrates in L. cremoris. While the specific function of Tex remains to be elucidated, the regulated degradation of YthA suggests that proteolysis may represent an additional regulatory layer within the lactococcal CES response.

articles.title: Predicting remission following repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation in treatment-resistant depression: a comparison of parsimonious and ensemble machine learning models.
articles.abstract: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) is resource-intensive, and prognostic models may estimate remission probability after treatment in treatment-resistant depression (TRD). Whether algorithmic complexity improves remission prediction over a parsimonious clinical model remains unclear. In a retrospective cohort of 263 adults treated with rTMS who met a baseline data-availability criterion, we compared a simple logistic regression model using age, sex, and baseline MADRS with tuned multivariable regression and SuperLearner ensembles across feature sets ranging from routine clinical variables to questionnaire scores, symptom dimensions, and individual items. Models were evaluated using 10 repeats of stratified 10-fold cross-validation; remission (follow-up MADRS ≤10) was the primary outcome. Seventy-one participants (27.0%) remitted. Across the 12 feature-set/model-strategy configurations, mean calibrated ROC-AUCs ranged from 0.685 to 0.711; LR_Simple yielded 0.707 (across-repeat SD 0.005), and the MADRS-only benchmark yielded 0.708 (0.004). Across eight paired comparisons of LR_Simple with richer or ensemble strategies, ROC-AUC differences ranged from -0.008 to 0.018, every 95% CI included zero, and none differed significantly after BH correction. Random-forest imputation produced similar remission discrimination, whereas models discriminated MADRS response less well than remission. At a 25% threshold, the Base-LR_Simple and Dimensions-SuperLearner configurations yielded 6.0 (95% CI 1.8-10.0) and 7.1 (3.3-10.9) net true-positive decisions per 100 versus treat-all. In this internally validated cohort, richer and ensemble strategies did not demonstrate improved remission discrimination over the a priori three-variable reference model; these findings do not establish equivalence or transportability.

articles.title: Interactive effect of childhood adversity and HPA-axis multilocus genetic variation on alexithymia in adolescents.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Childhood adversity increases risk for affective symptoms, including alexithymia, a transdiagnostic emotion-processing difficulty common in adolescence. Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis-related genetic variation may contribute to individual differences in sensitivity to adverse environments. This study examined whether an HPA-axis-related multilocus genetic profile score (MGPS) moderated the association between childhood adversity and adolescent alexithymia.

METHODS: The present study addressed this issue in a sample of 460 adolescents (Mage = 12.73, SD = 0.72; 54.1% female) who completed the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire and the Toronto Alexithymia Scale. Saliva samples were collected for deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) genotyping, and an HPA-axis-related multilocus genetic profile score (MGPS) was constructed from six candidate polymorphisms. Hierarchical regression and re-parameterized regression analyses were conducted.

RESULTS: Childhood adversity was positively associated with alexithymia. HPA-axis MGPS moderated this association. Specifically, adolescents with high HPA-axis MGPS exhibited higher levels of alexithymia when exposed to high childhood adversity but lower levels when exposed to low childhood adversity, providing preliminary support for the differential susceptibility model.

LIMITATIONS: The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, and the findings require replication in longitudinal, clinically enriched, and more diverse samples.

CONCLUSIONS: HPA-axis multilocus genetic variation may function as a biological sensitivity factor in the association between childhood adversity and adolescent alexithymia. These findings extend gene-environment interaction research to alexithymia and highlight individual differences in adolescents' emotional responses to adversity.

articles.title: Mapping reproducible brain-based depression stratification across clinical, cognitive, and neurotransmitter dimensions.
articles.abstract: Identifying reproducible brain-based stratifications across independent cohorts is critical for parsing heterogeneity in Major Depressive Disorder (MDD), yet robust profiles spanning micro- and macroscales remain poorly defined. We applied stability-based clustering to cortical thickness (CT) data from 1531 MDD individuals in UK Biobank (UKB), with replication in 144 inpatients from IRCCS San Raffaele Hospital (HSR). Two stable clusters emerged (normalized stability = 0.125) that generalized to a hold-out UKB sample with 96.5% accuracy (majority-cluster baseline = 59.5%). The clusters differed in widespread CT, largely reflected in global CT, with one showing cortical thinning, childhood trauma, and diabetes comorbidity. A two-cluster structure was independently replicated in HSR (normalized stability = 0.29), with a broadly similar cortical topography, although systematic CT differences between cohorts limited direct cross-cohort comparability. The clinical correlates identified in UKB did not replicate after correction for multiple comparisons. In UKB, mapping the CT differences between strata onto Neurosynth meta-analytic activation patterns revealed a ventral-dorsal gradient linked with emotion regulation, interoceptive, and motivational processes. Spatial correlations with 19 neurotransmitter receptors and transporters obtained from positron emission tomography identified the dopamine transporter as the dominant contributor in UKB, and the histamine H3 receptor in HSR. These findings provide a reproducible framework linking CT-based clusters in MDD to multiscale biological organization, although their clinical relevance warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Anp32e mediates histone variant H2A.Z-regulated TGF-β1 involvement in renal interstitial fibrosis.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
articles.abstract: Renal interstitial fibrosis (RIF), a key pathological feature of chronic kidney disease, often leads to end-stage renal failure. However, the mechanisms underlying RIF remain unclear, and effective targeted therapies are still lacking. Our prior research identified that acidic nuclear phosphorylated protein 32 E (Anp32e) aggravates RIF, though the mechanism was not fully clarified. Anp32e is known as a histone chaperone regulating the histone variant H2A.Z, yet the role of H2A.Z in RIF and its connection to Anp32e remain largely unexplored. In this study, we observed elevated nuclear Anp32e in renal tubular epithelial cells in an RIF model. We further confirmed that Anp32e forms a protein complex with H2A.Z and showed that Anp32e may facilitates H2A.Z degradation via the proteasome pathway. Mechanistically, this degradation may reduce H2A.Z occupancy at the TGF-β1 promoter, leading to increased TGF-β1 expression and subsequent upregulation of fibrosis markers FN and Col-I. Collectively, our findings suggest that Anp32e may induces the degradation of H2A.Z via the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, which contribute to increased transcriptional activity of TGF-β1 and subsequent promotion of RIF.

articles.title: Zinc silicate microspheres-mediated bacterial metabolic interference and microenvironment remodeling for chronic wound repair.
articles.abstract: Chronic wounds have presented a significant clinical challenge due to persistent infection, uncontrolled inflammation, and impaired tissue regeneration. Existing therapeutic platforms have failed to integrate these critical aspects into a single, cohesive strategy. To address this, a novel multifaceted agent, zinc silicate flower-like microsphere (ZnSi FMPs), was designed with controlled hierarchical architecture to achieve chronic wound repair by mediating bacterial metabolic interference and microenvironment remodeling. The unique nanosheet structure with sustained Zn2+ release endows ZnSi FMPs with favorable pH-independent antibacterial activity. This activity is mechanistically rooted in metabolic interference against Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus), including disruption of ABC transporters and inhibition of the biosynthesis of essential amino acids (valine, leucine, isoleucine) and ribosomes. Concurrently, ZnSi FMPs can promote microenvironment remodeling by modulating inflammatory responses and angiogenesis, evidenced by suppressed inflammation mediated by the complement and coagulation cascades pathway and robust activation of the Areg/HB-EGF-mediated ErbB signaling pathway. Hence, in both S. aureus-infected and diabetic wound models (mice and minipigs), ZnSi FMPs exhibited superior chronic wound healing capacity compared with commercial silver sulfadiazine® (AgSD) and 45S5 bioglass®. This improved healing was achieved through enhanced antibacterial activity, anti-inflammatory effects, and angiogenesis, accompanied by elevated expression of CD163, CD206, CD31 and α-SMA. By synergizing bacterial metabolic interference with microenvironment regulation, ZnSi FMPs effectively facilitate tissue healing and provide a promising candidate for clinical wound treatment.

articles.title: Continuity and Discontinuity in Artefact Distributions from Multi-Period Archaeological Sites.
articles.journal: Journal of archaeological method and theory
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Artefact finds recovered by metal detecting and reported by members of the public are a growing source of archaeological information, with over 1.2 million finds recorded to date by the Portable Antiquities Scheme in England and Wales. Heritage schemes in many other European countries where hobby detecting for archaeology is legal likewise report growing numbers of finds. Using point pattern analysis, this paper presents a worked-out set of computational methods to study diachronic processes within artefact assemblages at field or local (e.g. parish) levels. We present a simulated 'toy' example to illustrate the methodology and test it with two large artefact assemblages from the counties of North Yorkshire and Norfolk that differ in terms of finds record quality and known contextual archaeological landscape information. The proposed approach and example code can be reapplied to other archaeological point patterns. It formalises a spatial statistical workflow that produces an assessment regarding landscape persistence and reuse, and which can be used, for example, to assist fieldwork or planning decisions by identifying areas for further research. The case studies highlight the considerable need for formal analytical workflows in public finds research, which can be easily deployed at different sites and local assemblages. Moreover, while the proposed workflow has been designed with public finds scatters in mind, it is scale-agnostic and can be reapplied to investigate a range of archaeological phenomena from monument distributions across a larger region to investigating artefact scatters within an excavated area.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s10816-026-09821-0.

articles.title: Impact of Non-Tobacco Nicotine Products on Postoperative Outcomes in Soft Tissue Hand Surgery.
articles.journal: Journal of hand surgery global online
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Use of non-tobacco nicotine products (NTNP), including e-cigarettes, nicotine pouches, and oral nicotine devices, has risen sharply, yet their impact on postoperative outcomes across elective soft tissue hand surgeries remains poorly defined. Although nicotine from combustible tobacco impairs wound healing, whether NTNP exposure confers similar risk is unknown. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the association between preoperative NTNP use and postoperative complication rates following elective soft tissue hand surgery.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network identified adults (≥18 years) undergoing elective soft tissue hand surgery from 2004 to 2024. Patients with non-tobacco-specified nicotine dependence diagnoses documented within 1 year before surgery were compared with patients without any documented nicotine dependence. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed based on demographics and comorbidities. Postoperative complications at 1, 3, and 6 months included deep, superficial, and unspecified surgical site infection, wound dehiscence, and deep vein thrombosis/pulmonary embolism. Odds ratios with 95 percent confidence intervals were calculated, with P < .05 considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: After matching, 36,811 patients were included per cohort. NTNP use was associated with significantly increased rates of unspecified surgical site infection, deep vein thrombosis/pulmonary embolism, and wound dehiscence at all assessed postoperative time points. Deep and superficial surgical site infection rates did not differ significantly. Effect sizes were consistent across all intervals.

CONCLUSIONS: NTNP use within 1 year is independently associated with higher risks of wound dehiscence, thromboembolic events, and unspecified postoperative infection after soft tissue hand surgery. These findings suggest that nicotine exposure, regardless of delivery method, adversely affects postoperative healing and should be addressed through preoperative screening and cessation counseling.

TYPE OF STUDY/LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Retrospective cohort study III.

articles.title: Gas signaling molecule: a new research focus in the treatment of erectile dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Gas signaling molecules, including nitric oxide, carbon monoxide, and hydrogen sulfide, have recently gained attention in erectile dysfunction treatment research because of their roles in regulating blood vessel function, reducing oxidative stress, and protecting nerves and other cells. This article reviews how nitric oxide, carbon monoxide, and hydrogen sulfide are involved in the development of erectile dysfunction and their potential as treatments. The review focuses on how these gases improve blood vessel function, relax smooth muscles, repair nerve function, and reduce tissue scarring. Current research shows that methods of gas delivery, especially those using nanocarriers or prodrugs, greatly increase how well these gases are absorbed and where they act in the body. Early animal studies and initial clinical trials support the effectiveness of these gasotransmitters in treating various causes of erectile dysfunction, including diabetes, aging, and nerve damage. Although challenges remain in controlling the speed of delivery, determining the appropriate dosage, and tailoring treatment to individual patients, there is reason for optimism. The development of responsive delivery systems, combinations of multiple gases, and additional therapies for difficult cases suggests that gas signaling molecules could transform erectile dysfunction treatment.

articles.title: Molecular crosstalk between gas transmitters and catecholamine biosynthesis pathways: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: Catecholamines, particularly the hormone and neurotransmitter epinephrine, are important regulators of blood pressure and cardiovascular function. The expression of genes encoding catecholamine biosynthetic enzymes is subject to strict transcriptional regulation through both hormonal and neuronal mechanisms. These genes are also regulated by hypoxia and reactive oxygen species. A class of small gaseous transmitters, known as gas transmitters, serve as potent regulators of blood pressure and hypoxic signaling; however, their roles in catecholamine biosynthesis remain poorly understood. This manuscript reviews the current state of catecholamine and gas transmitter research, particularly their interactions in relation to hypertension. Current evidence shows that the gas transmitters nitric oxide, carbon monoxide, and hydrogen sulfide modulate catecholamine biosynthesis and release through both shared and distinct mechanisms. This regulation is highly dependent on concentration, cellular context, and mode of delivery. Additionally, this review explores hypoxic signaling as a link between catecholamines and gas transmitters. Together, these findings highlight a complex and context-dependent regulatory signaling between gas transmitters and catecholamines. Further mechanistic studies investigating endogenous signaling are required to elucidate these interactions and their therapeutic potential.

articles.title: Hyperbaric oxygen for the treatment of traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract: The therapeutic efficacy of hyperbaric oxygen therapy for traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury remains a subject of debate. To comprehensively evaluate the impact of hyperbaric oxygen on motor function, sensory function, and activities of daily living in patients with traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis. We performed a comprehensive search across PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and major Chinese databases for randomized controlled trials published through June 2025. A total of 15 randomized controlled trials were included. The pooled results indicated that hyperbaric oxygen therapy significantly improved the American Spinal Injury Association motor score (mean difference = 10.30, 95% confidence interval: 7.70-12.90), the total American Spinal Injury Association sensory score (mean difference = 29.29, 95% confidence interval: 18.82-39.75), the American Spinal Injury Association light touch score (mean difference = 9.84, 95% confidence interval: 6.15-13.53), and the American Spinal Injury Association pinprick score (mean difference = 8.75, 95% confidence interval: 4.40-13.11). Furthermore, hyperbaric oxygen therapy was associated with significant enhancements in the Barthel Index (mean difference = 16.60, 95% confidence interval: 10.51-22.68) and the Functional Independence Measure (mean difference = 17.41, 95% confidence interval: 10.83-23.98). In conclusion, adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy appears to improve motor function, sensory function, and activities of daily living in patients with traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury compared to conventional treatments alone. However, due to methodological limitations and potential publication bias in the included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution, and further high-quality, multi-center randomized controlled trials are warranted.

articles.title: Rectal ozone insufflation modulates gut microbiota: improving lung function in mice with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
articles.abstract: Ozone rectal insufflation possesses anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects and is used for the treatment and prevention of diseases. This study aimed to investigate the effects of ozone rectal insufflation on chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and explore the potential underlying mechanisms from the perspective of gut microbiology. A mouse chronic obstructive pulmonary disease model was established by intratracheal spraying of lipopolysaccharide and elastase. Mice received ozone rectal insufflation intervention following modeling. We found that ozone rectal insufflation improved pulmonary function, alleviated emphysema and pulmonary fibrosis, and reduced inflammatory cytokine levels in the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease mice. Additionally, ozone rectal insufflation modulated the pathogenic-to-beneficial gut bacteria ratio in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease mice. The treatment also led to an upregulation of short-chain fatty acids. The fecal microbiota transplantation results further confirmed that the gut microbiota of ozone rectal insufflation-treated mice was sufficient to attenuate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease symptoms. In summary, our findings indicate that ozone rectal insufflation enhances lung function and reduces inflammation in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease mice by modulating the gut microbiota and its associated metabolites.

articles.title: Hydrogen-rich water combined with traditional Chinese medicine compound in the treatment of kidney stones: a randomized controlled prospective clinical trial.
articles.abstract: The formation and development of kidney stones are related to abnormal urine metabolism, oxidative stress and inflammation. Hydrogen-rich water has clear efficacy in antioxidant and improving inflammatory status, while Ye-Shi-Shi-Lin-Formula is a clinically effective traditional Chinese medicine compound preparation for treating kidney stones. This randomized controlled prospective clinical trial from July 2025 to March 2026 at the Seventh People's Hospital Affiliated to Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine examined the effect of hydrogen-rich water and Ye-Shi-Shi-Lin-Formula on kidney stones. The included 100 patients with kidney stones were randomly divided into blank, hydrogen-rich water, hydrogen-rich water and Chinese medicine, and Chinese medicines groups. The patients received drinking hydrogen-rich water and/or Ye-Shi-Shi-Lin-Formula daily for 12 weeks. All subjects received basic treatment following the guidelines. Imaging examination, urine metabolism testing, renal function, inflammation and oxidative stress index, blood routine and liver function are used to detect the efficacy and safety of hydrogen-rich water and Ye-Shi-Shi-Lin-Formula. Results showed that the total effective rate of kidney stone treatment in blank group, Chinese medicines group, hydrogen-rich water and Chinese medicine group and hydrogen-rich water group was 28%, 76%, 80% and 32%. The Ye-Shi-Shi-Lin-Formula can partially alleviate the oxidative stress, uric acid metabolism and urinary magnesium levels of patients with kidney stone and improve the function of renal tubules. The hydrogen-rich water therapy showed only efficacy in improving glutathione reductase but the combination of hydrogen-rich water and Ye-Shi-Shi-Lin-Formula has shown superior efficacy in improving oxidative stress and related metabolic factors of blood uric acid and urine stones, as well as in renal tubular function. The results indicate that the addition of hydrogen-rich water can improve urinary metabolism and oxidative stress status in the treatment of kidney stones with Ye-Shi-Shi-Lin-Formula. The study was registered at the International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry (Registration No. ITMCTR2025001446).

articles.title: Ambient particulate matter pollution and stroke burden.
articles.abstract: As a major component of air pollution, ambient particulate matter pollution has rarely been studied with respect to its global stroke burden. This study aims to evaluate the global stroke incidence, mortality, and health inequalities related to ambient particulate matter pollution from 1990 to 2021. Utilizing the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021, we analyzed global stroke-related mortality, disability-adjusted life years, and their age-standardized rates. The estimated annual percentage change was calculated using a linear regression model. Health inequalities were measured using the concentration index and slope index of inequality. Between 1990 and 2021, global ambient particulate matter pollution-related stroke deaths and disability-adjusted life years increased by 107% and 101% respectively, yet age-standardized rates declined. China experienced the largest increases in deaths and disability-adjusted life years, Vietnam had the fastest rise in age-standardized mortality rates, the Russian Federation saw the steepest declines in deaths and disability-adjusted life years, and Estonia had the most rapid drop in age-standardized mortality rate. Middle socio-demographic index locations accounted for 46% of the global stroke burden, with age-standardized mortality rates and age-standardized disability-adjusted life years surpassing those in high socio-demographic index locations. From 1990 to 2021, age-standardized disability-adjusted life years rose in low-middle socio-demographic index locations but fell in high socio-demographic index locations. While the concentration index signaled an improvement in global inequality, the slope index of inequality in 2021 worsened compared with that in 1990. Between 1990 and 2021, the global burden of ambient particulate matter pollution-related stroke declined. However, substantial disparities persisted across different regions, sexes, and nations. For ongoing and future research efforts, priority should be given to high-risk populations and regions, while also developing innovative interventions to further reduce the incidence of ambient particulate matter pollution-related stroke and enhance patient outcomes.

articles.title: Microbeamformer-aware layout optimization of a 2D intracardiac echocardiography array for grating-lobe suppression.
articles.abstract: Three-dimensional intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) has emerged as a promising imaging modality for interventional cardiology. However, catheter-based 2D ICE probes are subject to strict vascular-access constraints, which limit the transducer aperture and independent channel count, leading to spatial undersampling and pronounced grating-lobe (GL) artifacts. This work investigates microbeamformer-aware array-layout optimization for GL suppression in 2D ICE arrays. Using a hybrid analog-digital microbeamformer architecture, the proposed design maps 768 array elements to 64 system channels while retaining the intended transmit focus. Under manufacturable kerf constraints, simulated annealing is used to optimize the element spacing along the elevational direction. With a minimum kerf width of 0.015 mm, the maximum GL level at a focal distance of 50 mm and a common steering angle of θ=φ=45° is reduced from -16.04 dB to -20.97 dB, with the main-lobe full width at half maximum nearly unchanged. Along the evaluated common-angle steering path, θ=φ=0°-45°, the GL reduction increases from 3.15 to 4.93 dB and is accompanied by a 5.60-6.90 dB increase in the maximum near-focus sidelobe level. Numerical phantom imaging simulations further demonstrate reduced GL-related artifacts, with the artifact-to-background contrast ratio decreased by up to 6.98 dB. As an exploratory, layout-preserving alternative to kerf optimization, nonuniform subaperture grouping reduces the maximum GL by 4.07 dB at θ=φ=45° without changing the physical element positions. These results demonstrate the potential of microbeamformer-aware layout optimization for balancing channel reduction, structured GL suppression, and fabrication constraints in miniaturized 2D ICE arrays.

articles.title: Breathing in harm: current insights into the effects of air pollution on cardiorespiratory health.
articles.abstract: Air pollution significantly contributes to cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, leading to increased morbidity and mortality. This review critically examines the mechanisms linking air pollution to higher cardiometabolic risk and cardiovascular death. It examines the impact of air pollution on respiratory health, specifically its role in exacerbating conditions such as heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and asthma. Special attention is given to vulnerable groups, including pregnant individuals, neonates, children, and patients with pre-existing cardiovascular or respiratory conditions, who are particularly susceptible and experience more severe health effects. Emerging evidence regarding the interactions between air pollution and coronavirus disease 2019 is also presented, showing how reductions in pollution levels during pandemic lockdowns were associated with improved cardiopulmonary health. Furthermore, the review discusses international differences in air quality standards and recent updates to exposure limits for air pollutants, as well as their implications for public health. It evaluates various mitigation strategies, including policy interventions, technological solutions, and approaches to reduce risk-based exposure. Lastly, the review emphasizes the need for comprehensive, evidence-based frameworks to minimize exposure and prevent diseases associated with pollution. Strengthening air quality management is essential for reducing the global burden of cardiovascular and respiratory diseases.

articles.title: ROS-responsive H2S-releasing quaternized chitosan dental implant coating for improved soft tissue integration, antibacterial and immunomodulatory capacities.
articles.abstract: Early and stable soft tissue integration is a prerequisite for the long-term success of dental implants. Crucially, the formation of this biological seal is closely associated with bacterial invasion and the modulation of the local immune microenvironment. Herein, we developed a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive hydrogen sulfide (H2S)-releasing quaternized chitosan (QCS) coating on the transmucosal interface of Ti-6Al-4V implants, termed TC4/PQCS/H2S. This coating exhibited favorable biocompatibility, enhancing the adhesion of human gingival epithelial cells (HGECs) and human gingival fibroblasts (HGFs), and improving soft tissue compatibility. Additionally, the TC4/PQCS/H2S possessed potent antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli, methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, and oral anaerobic pathogens, with effective suppression of biofilm formation. Furthermore, the TC4/PQCS/H2S enhanced cellular antioxidant defense and activated the Nrf2 pathway. It also promoted macrophage polarization toward the pro-healing M2 phenotype, with the involvement of the PI3K-Akt signaling pathway. Overall, this study presents an efficient surface modification strategy that integrates cell-adhesive, antibacterial, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory functions, demonstrating great potential for soft tissue integration.

articles.title: Synergistic antibacterial and osteogenic properties of micro-arc oxidation GO@Ag/SF composite coatings for the repair of infectious bone defects.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bacterial infection and insufficient osseointegration of titanium-based implants remain major clinical challenges. Conventional drug-loaded coatings often fail to simultaneously achieve long-term antibacterial activity and the construction of an osteogenic microenvironment.

METHODS: In this study, a graphene oxide-supported silver nanoparticle/silk fibroin (GO@Ag/SF) composite coating was developed and modified via micro-arc oxidation. By precisely controlling the GO/AgNO3 volume ratio, the antibacterial and osteogenic performances of the coatings were systematically evaluated. A rat model of infectious bone defect was employed to verify the in vivo therapeutic efficacy.

RESULTS: The optimized GO@Ag-2/SF coating exhibited pH-responsive sustained Ag+ release, with cumulative release increasing from 0.23 μg/mL under physiological conditions to 0.69 μg/mL under acidic conditions over 672 h. Under NIR irradiation, the coating reached 59.8°C within 10 min and achieved potent antibacterial activity against S. aureus and E. coli, with inhibition rates up to 98.3 ± 1.2%. The GO@Ag-2/SF coating also promoted osteogenic differentiation by enhancing ALP activity, collagen secretion, calcium mineralization, and the expression of RUNX-2, ALP, COL-I, and OCN. In vivo, GO@Ag-2/SF reduced inflammatory infiltration and improved peri-implant bone regeneration, with increased BIC, BV/TV, and Tb.Th and reduced Tb.Sp. Moreover, pull-out testing demonstrated the highest bone-implant mechanical fixation in the GO@Ag-2/SF group, confirming enhanced functional osseointegration in the infected bone defect model.

CONCLUSION: Through the synergistic effects of its components, the GO@Ag/SF coating established a dynamic antibacterial-osteogenic balance, offering a promising strategy for the repair of infectious bone defects.

articles.title: Photothermal-magnetic dual-activated Janus dressing for microenvironment purification and wireless electrically triggered healing with reduced scar formation.
articles.abstract: Hypertrophic scarring remains a major clinical challenge that impedes functional wound regeneration. Although electrical stimulation (ES) shows great promise in activating endogenous repair pathways and suppressing fibrosis, excessive exudate and bacterial infection in chronic wounds not only exacerbate inflammation but also disrupt interfacial electrical contact, thereby attenuating the efficacy of in situ-generated ES. To address this, we designed an electroactive and antibacterial Janus dressing that integrated active microenvironmental purification with wireless ES, ultimately inhibiting scar formation during wound healing. The dressing featured electroactive cotton gauze with asymmetric wettability, achieved via SiO2 and AgNPs@poly 5-hydroxytryptamine/polyethyleneimine (AgNPs@PHT/PEI) coatings to form a unidirectional fluidic gate. Enhanced by a near-infrared-driven mild photothermal effect, this design enabled rapid exudate pumping and evaporation while achieving > 99% antibacterial efficacy within 15 min. Leveraging electromagnetic induction, it delivered tunable wireless microcurrents (13.44-43.18 μA) that upregulated endogenous fibroblast growth factor 2 (FGF2) secretion, which contributes to the downregulation of TGF-β1-driven myofibroblast activation, as evidenced by reduced α-SMA expression. This strategy achieved 99.37% closure of large infected full-thickness rat wounds, featuring highly ordered collagen remodeling. Collectively, this study presents an innovative platform for rapid healing and scar inhibition in chronic wounds, holding promise for broader applications in mitigating fibrotic disorders.

articles.title: A multifunctional DECM/PLMA hydrogel incorporated with engineered PRP-derived exosomes enabling PHD2 silencing for skin wound repair.
articles.abstract: Skin defect repair remains a formidable clinical challenge, characterized by persistent infection risk, compromised angiogenesis, and dysregulated inflammatory responses. Existing hydrogel-based wound dressings fail to simultaneously address structural integrity, antimicrobial efficacy, and spatiotemporal coordination of tissue regeneration. Here, we report the development of a multifunctional bioactive hydrogel system fabricated by integrating decellularized tendon extracellular matrix (DECM) with Poly-L-lysine Methacryloyl (PLMA), and further functionalized with engineered platelet-rich plasma exosomes (PRP-Exos) loaded with siRNA targeting prolyl hydroxylase domain protein 2 (PHD2) via electroporation. The inherent cationic nature of PLMA confers robust, broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, while the sustained release of siRNA-PHD2-laden PRP-Exos achieves efficient PHD2 silencing, thereby stabilizing hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) and potentiating downstream pro-angiogenic signaling. Concurrently, bioactive cues released from the DECM-based matrix promote fibroblast-to-myofibroblast differentiation and type I collagen biosynthesis, fostering a regeneration-permissive microenvironment. In both normal and diabetic murine full-thickness skin defect models, DEPL@E-SI significantly accelerated wound closure by promoting angiogenesis, inflammation resolution, and extracellular matrix remodeling. These findings establish DEPL@E-SI as a promising therapeutic platform with translational potential for skin tissue engineering and clinical wound management.

articles.title: Orally activatable membrane fusion-mitochondria hitchhiking on intestinal macrophages for targeted therapy of bacterial meningitis and neuroinflammation.
articles.abstract: Targeting the formidable physiological barriers and neuronal damage refractory to conventional bactericidal agents for bacterial meningitis, we engineered an infection microenvironment-activatable membrane fusion-mitochondrial formulation (Mito@MFL-Glu). This formulation integrates endogenous macrophage hitchhiking, lysosomal exocytosis-driven cargo release, and in situ mitochondrial transplantation. Orally administered, its glucan shell is recognized by microfold cells, enabling macrophage-mediated transport across the blood-brain barrier and chemotactic accumulation at infectious foci. During macrophage uptake, stimulation of the Dectin-1 by the glucan shell sustains intracellular Ca2+ levels. Upon reaching the infectious lesion, the pro-inflammatory microenvironment induces macrophage polarization toward an M1 phenotype, which further elevates intracellular Ca2+ levels. The synergy of these two sequential Ca2+ concentration events cooperatively triggers TFEB-mediated lysosomal exocytosis, resulting in a cargo efflux efficiency of 43.3%. Elevated local reactive oxygen species (ROS) cleave the ROS-responsive linker, detaching the glucan shell and exposing the fusogenic lipid bilayer.
