This activated layer then directly fuses with damaged neuron and microglial membranes, delivering exogenous mitochondria into the cytosol while bypassing lysosomal degradation and achieving a transplantation efficiency exceeding 36% within 1 h, whereas naked mitochondria show much lower efficiency. Concurrently, the liberated cefotaxime eliminates pathogens, culminating in a synergistic and non-invasive oral closed-loop bactericidal and neuroreparative strategy in a murine meningitis model.

articles.title: Rosmarinic acid-cerium nanocatalysts enable oxygenation-enhanced ROS neutralization and PET imaging-guided therapy for acute kidney injury.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is driven by a vicious interplay among excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and persistent renal hypoxia, which collectively disrupt redox homeostasis and exacerbate tubular injury. However, current therapeutic strategies primarily provide supportive care and fail to simultaneously modulate these interconnected pathological stressors. Herein, we report a cerium-doped rosmarinic acid nanosystem (RA/Ce NPs) formed via self-polymerization that catalytically eliminates ROS while simultaneously generating oxygen to reprogram the pathological renal microenvironment. The ultrasmall RA/Ce NPs enable efficient chelator-free 89Zr radiolabeling for positron emission tomography (PET) imaging. Redox-switchable Ce3+/Ce4+ centers confer robust catalytic activity and ROS-responsive biodegradation, ensuring potent antioxidation with safe clearance. RA/Ce NPs suppress intracellular ROS, preserve mitochondrial membrane potential, and protect against oxidative injury in vitro. In rhabdomyolysis-induced AKI mice, PET imaging reveals pronounced renal accumulation, while treatment markedly alleviates tubular damage, oxidative stress and hypoxia, leading to restored renal function with excellent biocompatibility. This work presents a natural-product-derived catalytic nanoplatform integrating antioxidation, oxygenation, imaging and biodegradability, offering a promising strategy for precision therapy of AKI.

articles.title: Retrievable "sea-island" microstructured zwitterionic-silicone hydrogel devices: augmented oxygen transport and anti-fibrosis for sustaining islet survival.
articles.abstract: Islet encapsulation is a transformative strategy for type 1 diabetes (T1D) cellular therapy, enabling islet transplantation without lifelong immunosuppression. However, macroscale encapsulation faces prominent challenges: poor surgical retrieval, hypoxia, and foreign body response (FBR)-induced fibrosis, which severely compromise clinical translation. Herein, we develop a sea-island microstructured zwitterionic-silicone hydrogel device via copolymerization of siloxane monomer SiGMA, zwitterionic monomer carboxybetaine acrylamide (CBAA), and hydrogen-bonding monomer N-acryloyl glycinamide (NAGA). Notably, NAGA enhances hydrogel structural stability via strong H-bonds, reinforcing network and mechanical integrity to facilitate safe retrieval; importantly, NAGA's hydrogen bonding crosslinks allow the hydrogel device to be heat-sealed, preventing cell leakage and maintaining immunoisolation. The incorporation of SiGMA induces hydrophobic phase separation, generating silicone-rich polymer microdomains that enhance oxygen permeability to alleviate islet hypoxia, while zwitterionic CBAA significantly improves antifouling performance and mitigates fibrotic encapsulation by suppressing the host FBR. After 8 weeks of implantation in mice and beagle dogs, the device exhibits minimal fibrotic encapsulation and can be readily retrieved. Notably, even without pre-vascularization or immunosuppression, the transplanted islets in diabetic mice sustain normoglycemia for up to 400 days. These results demonstrate a robust retrievable encapsulation device that addresses key bottlenecks in islet transplantation, advancing its potential translation for T1D.

articles.title: A hierarchical, pH-responsive nanocomposite hydrogel platform for synergistic microenvironment reprogramming and attenuation of inflammatory periodontal bone loss.
articles.abstract: Conventional periodontitis therapies are limited by their inability to concurrently address the interconnected challenges of persistent bacterial infection, excessive oxidative stress, and immune dysregulation. To overcome this, we developed an injectable, pH-responsive nanocomposite polypeptide hydrogel, PepGel@ZnO-PLP, through rational molecular interface engineering. The system is constructed by integrating poly-L-proline (PLP)-functionalized zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO-PLP) into a poly-L-glutamate containing polypeptide network (PepGel) via dynamic Zn2+-carboxylate coordination. This critical PLP interface ensures colloidal stability of ZnO nanoparticles and enables the formation of a homogeneous, pH-responsive release network. In the acidic periodontal microenvironment, the hydrogel exhibits potent antibacterial and reactive oxygen species (ROS)-scavenging activities. Furthermore, via PLP-enabled interfacial engineering, PepGel@ZnO-PLP reprograms inflammatory macrophage immunometabolism by driving a glycolytic-suppressed metabolic state that establishes metabolic homeostasis toward a reparative M2 phenotype, a process in which the PI3K-Akt pathway may be involved. In a murine periodontitis model, PepGel@ZnO-PLP adheres to periodontal defects, effectively disrupting the infection-inflammation cycle and leading to significant alveolar bone preservation. This work underscores the power of precise molecular-level design for holistically reprogramming the pathological microenvironment and offers a novel nanocomposite hydrogel for ameliorating inflammatory periodontal bone loss.

articles.title: Biomimetic stress granules replenish lysosomal repair to reinstate macrophage immunometabolic antibacterial programs.
articles.abstract: Severe intracellular bacterial infection can progressively compromise lysosomal defence in macrophages, yet the underlying repair bottleneck remains unclear. Here we identify a time-dependent exhaustion of stress granule (SG)-associated lysosomal repair during sustained infection: progressive depletion of core SG components, including G3BP1 and galectin-3 (Gal-3), undermines lysosomal membrane resealing, resulting in lysosomal deacidification and persistent cytosolic acidification. This pH imbalance suppresses glycolytic metabolism and blunts macrophage pro-inflammatory antibacterial programs, thereby enabling intracellular bacterial persistence. Since this exhausted repair module cannot be readily reconstituted by conventional pharmacological or genetic approaches, we engineer biomimetic stress granules (BSGs), Gal-3-functionalized nanodiscs cloaked in acid-responsive fusogen-expressing macrophage membrane vesicles (Gal3-NDs@EF-MNVs), to achieve sequential targeting and cytosolic delivery to damaged lysosomes. BSGs stabilize membrane lesions, suppress lysosomal leakage and restore lysosomal acidification, pH homeostasis and metabolic fitness, thereby recapitulating the 'plugging' behavior of native stress granules at sites of membrane injury. This work establishes biomimetic organelle repair as a general, materials-driven paradigm to restore innate immunity against intracellular infections - without escalating antibiotics or genetic manipulation.

articles.title: Exosomes in brain diseases: Mechanisms, advances, and perspectives.
articles.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) remains a major biological obstacle limiting the effective delivery of therapeutics for central nervous system (CNS) disorders. Although conventional drug delivery approaches have achieved continuous advances, their clinical translation is frequently restricted by limited brain penetration, insufficient target specificity, and systemic adverse effects. Exosomes, endogenous extracellular vesicles (EVs) involved in intercellular communication, have emerged as promising candidates for CNS therapeutic delivery owing to their favorable biocompatibility, relatively low immunogenicity, and potential ability to interact with biological barriers. In this review, we first summarize the structural characteristics of the BBB and the mechanisms underlying exosome-BBB interactions and transport. We then discuss current strategies for exosome isolation, characterization, and engineering, highlighting how these approaches influence therapeutic performance and translational feasibility. Subsequently, we analyze recent advances in exosome-based therapies for major CNS disorders, including neurodegenerative diseases, brain tumors, and ischemic stroke, with emphasis on how distinct pathological environments guide the design of exosome cargos, targeting strategies, and functional modifications. Finally, we discuss key challenges associated with clinical translation, including manufacturing standardization, pharmacokinetic evaluation, safety assessment, and regulatory considerations. This review provides a pathology-driven and engineering-guided perspective for understanding the rational design and future development of exosome-based therapeutics for CNS disorders.

articles.title: Deep Learning-driven synergistic engineering of PET hydrolase for post-consumer PET depolymerization.
articles.abstract: Enzymatic depolymerization of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) offers a promising route to mitigate the increasingly severe problem of plastic pollution. However, the development of highly efficient PET hydrolases capable of processing post-consumer PET remains a critical challenge. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) provide new opportunities to accelerate the enzyme engineering of PET hydrolases. Here, we report a systematic computational redesign of the PET hydrolase NI (ThcCut1-AICCG-H185N/F189I) using the deep-learning framework, EITLEM-Kinetics. By integrating mutation free-energy constraints with kinetic parameter prediction, the framework enables simultaneous optimization of catalytic activity and thermostability. A total of nine beneficial substitution sites were identified and experimentally validated that overcoming the activity-stability trade-off. Combinatorial iteration yielded an optimal variant, NI-E65K/H107Y/A2R/L33F (NI-KYRF), which exhibited an 80% and 90% increase in depolymerization activity toward Gf-PET film and one-step pretreated post-consumer PET (pc-PET powder), respectively, along with a 2.61 °C increase in melting temperature (T m). NI-KYRF displayed a specific activity of 665 μmolTPAeq h-1 mgenzyme -1, representing 2.0- and 1.48-fold improvements over representative high-performance PET hydrolases ICCG and TurboPETase. The depolymerization performance of NI-KYRF towards various post-consumer PET wastes and polyester plastics was significantly improved. At 70 °C, it achieved a 95.5% depolymerization conversion of pc-PET powder within 24 h, and for untreated post-consumer PET film, the conversion reached 80.1%, representing a 2.1-fold improvement in depolymerization efficiency over the parental NI. In addition, enhanced activity toward polyesters plastics, including PBAT and PBT, indicates an expanded substrate scope. Molecular dynamics simulations and structural analysis reveal that these mutations enhance enzyme performance through synergistic mechanisms. Overall, this study establishes a deep learning-guided computational design framework based on EITLEM-Kinetics and demonstrates its effectiveness and broad potential for engineering high-performance PET hydrolases.

articles.title: Amino acid-based formula and Clostridioides difficile-associated disease in infants: concerns regarding causal interpretation.
authors: Subspecialty Group of Gastroenterology, the Society of Pediatrics, Chinese Medical Doctor Association
articles.abstract: Wang et al. recently reported an association between amino acid-based formula (AAF) feeding and Clostridioides difficile-associated disease (CDAD) in children younger than two years, integrating clinical observations, microbiome profiling, and fecal microbiota transplantation experiments. The authors appropriately framed their findings as associative; our aim is not to allege over-interpretation, but to delineate the evidentiary gap between their reported association and a causal claim. Several methodological and interpretative issues limit such inference, including confounding by the clinical indication for AAF, the difficulty of distinguishing C. difficile colonization from clinically attributable disease in young children, developmental differences in age and complementary feeding, and the selected nature of the fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) donor population. For example, the multivariable model included only 27 outcome events against approximately six predictors (events-per-variable ≈ 4.5, far below the accepted 10-20 threshold), rendering the adjusted odds ratios unstable. The cross-sectional microbiome data further cannot establish whether microbial alterations preceded disease or resulted from underlying clinical, dietary, or inflammatory states. We therefore suggest interpreting the findings as an association between AAF feeding and CDAD status, rather than evidence that AAF itself increases CDAD risk. Our skepticism concerns the causal link to CDAD specifically; we do not dispute that reduced Bifidobacterium with formula feeding is a well-established finding. This distinction has important clinical implications, as AAF remains an essential nutritional intervention for children with appropriate indications, and in young children microbiological detection and microbiome alterations must be interpreted alongside age, clinical symptoms, underlying disease, dietary history, and other relevant exposures. An overly causal interpretation could create unnecessary concern among families and complicate clinical decision-making. To make these considerations operational, we specify the elements of a decisive prospective study, including a minimum event count of ~60 adjudicated CDAD cases, a blinded tiered diagnostic algorithm, and detailed AAF exposure ascertainment.

articles.title: CYB2-knockout Saccharomyces cerevisiae exerts effective antibacterial activity via lactic acid accumulation.
articles.abstract: Bacterial infectious diseases pose a major threat to human health, and rising antibiotic resistance has complicated treatment. Probiotics are promising alternatives, but their mechanisms remain largely unclear. Here, we screened a randomly selected subset of 1,733 strains from the homozygous diploid Saccharomyces cerevisiae gene-knockout collection (YKOC) and identified CYB2-knockout (CYB2-KO) S. cerevisiae as a strain with potent antibacterial activity. CYB2-KO S. cerevisiae effectively inhibited the growth of pathogenic bacteria, including multidrug-resistant strains, and suppressed biofilm formation by reducing bacterial adhesion, EPS production, and cell surface hydrophobicity. It also increased bacterial cell wall and membrane permeability. The strain showed no hemolytic activity, tolerated acidic conditions and high bile salt concentrations, and exhibited superior auto-aggregation and co-aggregation with pathogenic bacteria. In mouse models of urinary tract infection and enteritis, CYB2-KO S. cerevisiae increased survival and reduced bacterial counts in the bladder, ileum, colon, and cecum. Mechanistically, CYB2 deletion led to lactic acid (LA) accumulation and environmental acidification. Dose-response experiments with exogenous LA, pH neutralization, and supplementation of BY4743 CFS with LA at the CFS-equivalent concentration provided direct causal evidence that LA is the key effector metabolite. These findings highlight CYB2-KO S. cerevisiae as a promising probiotic candidate with broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, with LA accumulation as the primary mechanism underlying its therapeutic effects.

articles.title: Clinical risk factors associated with acute hypertension-mediated organ damage in patients presenting with severe hypertension: A retrospective cohort study from Qatar.
articles.journal: Clinical and experimental hypertension (New York, N.Y. : 1993)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe hypertension is a common reason for emergency department (ED) visits and is associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Identifying factors associated with acute hypertension-mediated organ damage (HMOD) may improve risk stratification.

METHODS: A large retrospective cohort study across four hospitals in Qatar (January 2015-January 2020). Adults presenting to the ED with severe hypertension (systolic blood pressure [SBP] ≥ 180 mmHg and/or diastolic blood pressure [DBP] ≥ 110 mmHg) were included. In a cross-sectional primary analysis, the outcome was hypertensive emergency, defined as acute HMOD present at the index presentation, and univariable and multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with acute HMOD at presentation. A separate exploratory longitudinal secondary analysis described cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, and renal complications over three years of follow-up using descriptive statistics was conducted. Discrimination and calibration were assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and Hosmer-Lemeshow test.

RESULTS: Of 881 patients (median age 50 years [IQR 43-57]; 68.8% male), 94.7% had severe asymptomatic hypertension and 5.3% presented with hypertensive emergency. Independent factors associated with acute HMOD were higher admission SBP (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.016, 95% CI 1.000-1.033), higher DBP (aOR 1.027, 95% CI 1.006-1.049), chronic kidney disease (aOR 2.38, 95% CI 1.02-5.57), hypertensive retinopathy (aOR 3.82, 95% CI 1.14-12.83), and current smoking (aOR 2.83, 95% CI 1.32-6.06). The model showed good discrimination (AUC 0.77) and adequate calibration. Kidney disease progression was the most common follow-up complication.

CONCLUSIONS: Elevated admission blood pressure, chronic kidney disease, hypertensive retinopathy, and current smoking were independently associated with acute HMOD. These readily identifiable factors may support ED risk stratification in patients with severe hypertension.

articles.title: Association between health literacy and acceptance or refusal of surgical treatment in patients with benign prostatic obstruction.
articles.journal: The aging male : the official journal of the International Society for the Study of the Aging Male
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study investigated the association between health literacy and acceptance of surgery for benign prostatic obstruction (BPO).

MATERIAL AND METHODS: In this prospective observational study, 95 patients recommended surgery for BPO (May-September 2025) were classified as accepting (n = 61) or refusing (n = 34) surgery. Health literacy was assessed using the HLS-EU-Q47. Clinical characteristics and International Prostate Symptom Scores (IPSS) were compared.

RESULTS: Age, education, marital status, overall comorbidity prevalence, medical treatment duration, and uroflowmetry parameters did not differ significantly between groups. Smoking history (p < 0.001) and coronary artery disease (p = 0.002) differed significantly. Patients accepting surgery had higher IPSS scores (p < 0.001). Overall ASOY-TR health literacy scores were similar (p = 0.359), although health literacy category distributions differed (p = 0.035). In multivariable analysis, IPSS (adjusted OR = 1.158, p < 0.001) and family history of BPO surgery (adjusted OR = 3.725, p = 0.020) were independently associated with acceptance; the ASOY-TR index was not (adjusted OR = 1.036, p = 0.326).

DISCUSSION: Health literacy was not independently associated with surgical acceptance. Symptom severity and family history were associated with acceptance, underscoring their relevance to shared decision-making.

articles.title: Non-invasive vascular assessment in gestational hypertension and preeclampsia during pregnancy and the postpartum period: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate evidence on non-invasive vascular assessment techniques used during pregnancy and/or the postpartum period to identify vascular abnormalities associated with gestational hypertension and explore potential implications for long-term cardiovascular health.

METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE, PubMed, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, and gray literature (to May-2024) identified studies assessing vascular structure or function using pulse-wave velocity, carotid intima-media thickness, flow-mediated dilation, ophthalmic artery Doppler, and retinal imaging. Forty-nine studies involving 32,683 participants. Due to the heterogeneity in study design and methodology, findings were synthesized narratively.

RESULTS: Women with gestational hypertension generally demonstrated increased arterial stiffness (elevated pulse wave velocity and augmentation index), impaired endothelial function (reduced flow-mediated dilation), and increased intima-media thickness during pregnancy and the postpartum period. Several studies reported persistence of these abnormalities from weeks to years after delivery, although findings were inconsistent. Ophthalmic artery Doppler studies showed variable alterations in peak systolic velocity ratios and pulsatility index reported in hypertensive pregnancies. Retinal imaging identified alterations in retinal vessel caliber during pregnancy and the postpartum period, with some abnormalities reported up to six years postpartum.

CONCLUSION: Non-invasive vascular assessments can help identify macrovascular, microvascular, and endothelial abnormalities in women with gestational hypertension and preeclampsia during pregnancy and the postpartum period. Although some abnormalities persist beyond delivery and may contribute to long-term cardiovascular risk, evidence remains insufficient to support their use as independent predictors of future cardiovascular events. Further standardized, prospective longitudinal studies are needed to determine their prognostic and clinical value.

articles.title: Impact of Ruminococcus gnavus on lipid metabolism via isoCDCA.
articles.abstract: The gut microbiota is increasingly recognized as a regulator of host lipid metabolism, yet the specific strains and effector metabolites driving hyperlipidemia remain poorly defined. Here, we identified Ruminococcus gnavus (R. gnavus) as a candidate contributor to cholesterol-related dyslipidemia and delineated its metabolic mechanism. Comparing individuals with high versus normal TC/LDL-C (HTL vs NTL) in both normal-weight and overweight populations, we found that fecal R. gnavus was enriched in HTL individuals regardless of BMI stratum, a finding validated by species-specific qPCR in an independent cohort (n = 488). Administering R. gnavus to mice fed a normal or high-fat diet induced alterations in circulating lipids and liver function markers, accompanied by hepatic steatosis. Hepatic transcriptomics and targeted bile acid profiling converged on bile acid metabolism: R. gnavus downregulated key hepatic genes (Cyp7a1, Cyp8b1, Ldlr, and Ppara) and elevated isochenodeoxycholic acid (isoCDCA) levels both in vivo and in vitro. In vitro, R. gnavus directly converted chenodeoxycholic acid (CDCA) to isoCDCA. Clinically, serum isoCDCA was elevated in HTL individuals in an independent cohort (n = 1,137) and was positively associated with TC, TG, and LDL-C. Functionally, oral isoCDCA supplementation reproduced key lipid disturbances in mice, and isoCDCA downregulated lipid metabolism genes and promoted lipid accumulation in hepatocytes; heterologous expression of R. gnavus hydroxysteroid dehydrogenases conferred isoCDCA-producing capacity on E. coli and elevated circulating TC and LDL-C in colonized mice. These findings nominate isoCDCA as a microbial effector metabolite linking R. gnavus to hepatic lipid dysregulation and identify the R. gnavus-isoCDCA axis as a potential target for the prevention and treatment of hyperlipidemia.

articles.title: Promoting physical, mental, and social health during adolescence: a position statement and recommendations.
articles.journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
articles.abstract: Adolescence is a critical period of physical, psychological, and social development that shapes health trajectories across the life course. Despite its importance, adolescent health remains insufficiently prioritized within healthcare systems, while young people face increasingly complex challenges, including mental health disorders, sexually transmitted infections, social inequalities, climate change, and the deep influence of digital technologies. Although technology offers unprecedented opportunities to improve access to health information and care, it also introduces new risks that require coordinated, evidence-based responses. This position statement and its accompanying recommendations draw on the proceedings of an international workshop held in Athens in November 2025, organized by the International Academy of Human Reproduction and endorsed by leading international scientific societies. The statement addresses the biological, psychological, social, and gynecological challenges affecting adolescents in an evolving technological landscape. Its recommendations emphasize adolescent-responsive health systems, meaningful youth engagement, equitable access to care, and multidisciplinary collaboration. Investing in adolescent health represents a strategic priority, generating immediate benefits during adolescence while improving adult health and promoting better outcomes for future generations.

articles.title: A pathogen-derived small RNA modulates host immunity for chronic parasitism.
articles.abstract: Parasites that rely on prolonged host exploitation must balance immune evasion with host survival. The entomopathogenic fungus Ophiocordyceps sinensis maintains its insect host, Thitarodes xiaojinensis, for months before host death, but the mechanisms stabilizing host immunity during this period are unclear. Here, we identify a cross-kingdom regulatory strategy mediated by a fungal microRNA-like RNA (milRNA), Os-milRNA2, which is delivered into host immune tissues and directly targets the antimicrobial peptide gene attacin-1. Os-milRNA2 accumulates during mid-stage infection, repressing immune gene expression, whereas its inhibition restores host immunity and restricts fungal proliferation. Comparative analyses reveal lineage-specific retention of the Os-milRNA2 binding site in the T. xiaojinensis 3'UTR of attacin-1, indicating regulatory coevolution. Our findings show that a slow-killing parasite attenuates specific immune effectors to maintain host-pathogen homeostasis during chronic infection.

articles.title: Novel creatine formulation exhibits similar serum creatine concentrations and pharmacokinetics to creatine monohydrate in healthy adults.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Creatine monohydrate (CrM) is the most widely studied creatine form, demonstrating robust efficacy, bioavailability, and safety. With creatine growing in popularity, alternative formulations of creatine have been developed to target solubility and to optimize absorption pharmacokinetics (PK), as well as to reduce gastrointestinal (GI) intolerability. The purpose of the current study was to evaluate the acute effects of a novel creatine monohydrate (OptiCreatineTM; CrO) compared to CrM on serum creatine PK and GI tolerability in healthy adults.

METHODS: Healthy, recreationally active adults (age: 22 ± 3 years; males n = 8, females n = 9) consumed a single 5-gram dose of CrM or CrO across two separate visits following an overnight fast, in a randomized, double-blind, crossover design. Venous blood samples were collected at baseline and 30, 60, 90, 120, 180, 240, and 300 mins post-ingestion of their assigned treatment to assess serum creatine concentrations. PK parameters including peak concentration (Cmax), time to peak (Tmax), absorption rate constant (ka), elimination rate constant (kel; h-1), and area under the curve (AUC₀-T) were derived using nonlinear regression modeling. GI symptoms were assessed using validated questionnaires.

RESULTS: There was no difference in serum creatine concentrations between CrM or CrO across all participants (p = 0.707), males (p = 0.318), or females (p = 0.996) at any time point. Serum creatine increased over time regardless of treatment (p < 0.0001). No differences were observed between CrM and CrO for Cmax (mean difference ± standard deviation (MD ± SD): 7.66 ± 50.37μM; p = 0.82), Tmax (MD ± SD: -0.04 ± 0.13 h; p = 0.54), ka (MD ± SD: -0.15 ± 0.45 h-1; p = 0.51), kel (MD ± SD: 0.01 ± 0.03 h-1; p = 0.61), or AUC₀-T (MD ± SD: 22.09 ± 160.57 μM·h; p = 0.74), with no sex × treatment interactions (p ≥ 0.05). Descriptive evaluation showed similar GI symptom profiles between conditions, with low frequency and minimal severity reported across both treatments.

CONCLUSIONS: A single 5-gram dose of CrO produced similar serum creatine and PK characteristics to CrM in healthy adults. These findings support CrO as a viable delivery option, with no significant differences in acute pharmacokinetic profiles or GI tolerability compared to CrM.

articles.title: Colonoscopy-based Clostridioides difficile screening for inflammatory bowel disease patients.
articles.abstract: Patients with IBD have an increased risk for Clostridioides difficile infection, and the significance of asymptomatic colonization is poorly understood. Overlapping symptoms often complicate diagnosis, and there is a lack of validated screening methods. Colonic wash aspirates collected during routine colonoscopies may offer a convenient screening option. We aimed to evaluate culture methods for detecting C. difficile colonization in IBD patients using colonic wash samples. Patients with Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis undergoing outpatient colonoscopy were enrolled. Clinical characteristics, IBD activity indices, and endoscopic scores were recorded. Colonic wash aspirates were centrifuged and cultured on selective CHROMID® media with and without broth enrichment. Isolates were confirmed by Gram stain and MALDI-TOF. PCR/qPCR identified tcdB gene carriage. Whole-genome sequencing was performed on selected isolates, and associations between clinical factors and colonization were assessed. Of the 121 patients enrolled, 10.7% (13/121) were colonized. Crohn's patients were colonized more frequently than ulcerative colitis patients (13.3% CD, 8.2% UC). Among colonized patients, 53.8% (7/13) had C. difficile with detectable tcdB. Enrichment increased detection compared to direct plating. No clinical predictors of colonization were identified, but wash samples yielded sufficient DNA for sequencing with comparable depth to whole stool. Colonoscopy wash aspirates allow for the detection of asymptomatic C. difficile colonization in IBD. This screening method may provide a useful tool for investigating the prevalence, persistence, and clinical significance of C. difficile colonization in IBD and for informing future studies of CDI prevention.

articles.title: Bacteroides uniformis-generated ornithine alleviates alcohol-associated liver disease via Sirt4-mediated mitochondrial regulation.
articles.abstract: Gut microbiota plays a pivotal role in alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD), yet the contributions of individual bacterial strains and their metabolites remain poorly defined. Here, we analyzed 16S rDNA sequencing data from an ALD patient cohort and validated the findings using the NIAAA mouse model combined with multi-omics approaches. Bacteroides uniformis was significantly depleted in ALD patients, and supplementation with live B. uniformis alleviated ALD in mice by reducing hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and oxidative stress. Metabolomic analysis identified ornithine as a key metabolite produced by B. uniformis, and direct ornithine administration largely recapitulated the protective effects. Mechanistically, ornithine upregulated hepatic Sirt4, thereby restoring mitochondrial homeostasis, whereas pharmacological inhibition of Sirt4 abolished these effects. Dietary flaxseed oil increased intestinal B. uniformis abundance and hepatic Sirt4 expression, ameliorating ALD outcomes. These findings reveal a B. uniformis-ornithine-Sirt4 axis that modulates ALD via mitochondrial regulation and highlight potential microbial and metabolic therapeutic targets.

articles.title: A qualitative exploration of COPD lived experience, giving insight into symptom profile determinants and experiences of medical and non-medical interventions.
articles.journal: International journal of qualitative studies on health and well-being
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterised by a substantial symptom burden, including reduced physical activity, impaired sleep, diminished quality of life, and psychological distress. Despite established treatments, many individuals continue to experience persistent symptoms and functional limitations. This study aimed to explore symptom burden and how individuals manage COPD in daily life.

METHODS: Fifteen UK-based adults with a confirmed diagnosis of COPD (mean age 70 years, n = 10 females) participated in semi-structured interviews. Participants were recruited through clinical databases, research registries, and community support networks. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and analysed using inductive reflexive thematic analysis supported by NVivo.

RESULTS: Three themes were identified: (1) Interconnected symptom experiences, (2) Navigating treatment uncertainty and burden, and (3) Becoming an active manager of COPD. Breathlessness was described as the most debilitating symptom, closely interconnected with reduced functional capacity, and restricted social participation. Participants reported challenges with medication, including frequent treatment changes and limited perceived effectiveness. Self-management was central to daily life, with individuals employing pacing strategies, assistive devices, and self-directed learning.

CONCLUSIONS: COPD is experienced as a complexcondition shaped by interconnected symptoms and self-management demands. These findings highlight a need for responsive, patient-centred approaches to COPD care.

articles.title: Microbiota-derived indole-3-propionic acid regulates glucose homeostasis via remodeling of hepatic mitochondrial metabolism.
articles.abstract: The gut microbiota produces metabolites that circulate to host tissues and are increasingly linked to metabolic health, yet the mechanisms by which individual microbial products regulate liver glucose metabolism remain poorly defined. Here, we identify the tryptophan-derived microbial metabolite indole-3-propionic acid (IPA) as a direct modulator of hepatic glucose production. In primary hepatocytes, a focused screen of indole metabolites revealed that several indole-containing compounds suppress glucagon-stimulated glucose output, with IPA selected for further characterization. IPA selectively reduced glucose production from mitochondrial-dependent gluconeogenic substrates while largely preserving glycerol-supported glucose production, suggesting that it does not simply shut down gluconeogenesis but instead alters how hepatocytes use metabolic fuels. Mechanistic analyzes showed that IPA redirects lactate-derived carbon away from glucose production and reshapes mitochondrial metabolism, including redox balance, ATP availability, and urea cycle-linked metabolic activity. These effects occurred without detectable disruption of proximal insulin or glucagon signaling, supporting a model in which IPA acts primarily through intracellular metabolic remodeling. In mice, endogenous IPA levels varied with nutritional state, and short-term IPA administration improved fasting glycemia and glucose handling in Western diet-fed animals. Finally, microbiome-depleted mice colonized with IPA-producing Clostridium sporogenes displayed increased circulating IPA and improved glucose tolerance compared with mice colonized with an IPA-deficient mutant C. Sporogenes strain. Together, these findings identify IPA as a microbial metabolite that directly connects gut tryptophan metabolism to hepatic mitochondrial function and systemic glucose regulation, highlighting a mechanistic gut-liver pathway with potential therapeutic relevance to metabolic disease.

articles.title: Associations between allostatic load and osteoarthritis: a cross-sectional study from NHANES 1999-2020.
articles.abstract: This study aims to investigate the relationship between allostatic load score (AL score) and osteoarthritis. The study utilized cross-sectional data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES, 1999-2020), including 33,423 participants. Each of nine routinely measured indicators spanning the cardiovascular, metabolic, renal, nutritional and inflammatory domains was assigned one point if it fell within the highest-risk quartile. The points were then summed to calculate the AL score. Weighted logistic regression models assessed the association between AL score and the odds of osteoarthritis, with subgroup analyzes by age, sex, race/ethnicity, comorbidities and medication use. Elevated AL score was associated with an increased odds of osteoarthritis (odds ratio: 1.06, 95% confidence interval: 1.03-1.09). Compared to AL score < 3, participants with AL score ≥ 3 had higher odds of osteoarthritis. Consistent findings between AL score and osteoarthritis were found across subgroups of age, sex, cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and without medication use (analgesics, muscle relaxants, adrenal cortical steroids, and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory agents) (P < 0.05). Our results presented an association between elevated AL score and increased odds of osteoarthritis, suggesting that greater cumulative physiological stress burden is associated with higher odds of osteoarthritis. These findings provide new insights into osteoarthritis pathogenesis and highlight the potential value of managing stress and inflammation in osteoarthritis prevention. Future longitudinal and mechanistic studies are needed to verify our findings.

articles.title: Alteration of macrophage infiltrates in the tumor immune microenvironment following Janus kinase 1 (JAK) inhibition: analysis from a prospective clinical trial in Leiomyosarcoma.
articles.abstract: JAK1 signaling supports a suppressive tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) state and may also promote tumor-intrinsic oncogenic signaling. Leiomyosarcoma (LMS) is a soft tissue sarcoma (STS) subtype known to have abundant TAM infiltration, which is often polarized to an immunosuppressive M2 phenotype and contributes to immune evasion. We hypothesized that using a JAK1 inhibitor could alter TAM phenotypes in the LMS tumor microenvironment (TME), helping patients and potentially enabling future combination studies. Here, we present results from a pilot study of itacitinib, a JAK1 inhibitor, for LMS. We analyzed patients in the LMS cohort of a pilot study of the selective JAK1 inhibitor itacitinib (started at 300 mg daily in 28-day cycles) (NCT03670069). Serial tumor biopsies and peripheral blood samples were collected for correlative analysis. Despite the heavily pretreated LMS population, PFS rate at 3 and 6 months for LMS was 75% (95% CI: 50%-100%) and 25% (95% CI: 5%-100%), respectively, and the median OS was 101 weeks (range: 70-256). Six of eight patients with LMS achieved stable disease. Serial biopsies demonstrated a decrease in M2 TAM but without a corresponding inflammatory response and with a decrease of inflammatory infiltrates, suggesting that JAK1 inhibition may have direct anti-tumor effects in this subtype and that the impacts of the TAM reduction may be related to their tumor supportive and angiogenic functions, rather than immune inhibitory functions. These data support further investigation of JAK1 inhibition in LMS as part of rational immunotherapeutic combinations.

articles.title: In vitro study of gut microbiota-mediated response to Salmonella Typhimurium with a focus on dynamics and immune modulation.
articles.abstract: Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium is a major foodborne pathogen that disrupts gut microbial balance and induces intestinal inflammation. Microbial analysis revealed that S. Typhimurium infection increased the abundance of short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-producing bacteria, including Bacteroides, Parabacteroides, and members of the Clostridia group, while decreasing Escherichia-Shigella in an in vitro fecal fermentation model. Co‑culture experiments demonstrated that gut microbiota inhibited S. Typhimurium growth and host cell interactions while attenuating cytotoxicity and inflammatory responses (IL‑1β, IL‑6, and c‑Jun) in Caco-2 cells in a dose‑dependent manner. Interestingly, gut microbiota improved epithelial cell viability, indicating barrier‑protective and immunomodulatory functions. These findings demonstrate that human gut microbiota plays a crucial role in mitigating the pathogenicity of S. Typhimurium and maintaining intestinal homeostasis, supporting the potential of microbiota‑based strategies for infection control.

articles.title: Gut‒liver‒brain axis signature of cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment is consistent across multi-national cohorts.
articles.abstract: Cognitive impairment in cirrhosis is associated with an altered gut‒liver‒brain axis, but geographic variations in diet and clinical practices may limit generalizability. We investigated consistency of microbial signatures for cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment across four countries. We enrolled outpatients with cirrhosis from USA, Denmark, Lithuania, and Mexico who underwent Psychometric Hepatic Encephalopathy Score (PHES) testing for covert hepatic encephalopathy (CHE), and stool shotgun metagenomic sequencing. Taxonomic and functional associations with PHES were evaluated after adjustment for MELD, country, demographics, sex, proton pump inhibitor (PPI), lactulose, and rifaximin use. We enrolled 221 patients (median age 58 y, 57.9% men, median MELD 12). Cognitive performance varied by country despite adjustment for clinical covariates. Lithuania demonstrated greater microbial richness and better cognition despite higher MELD, accompanied by distinct dietary patterns including greater yogurt and tea consumption. In the entire cohort, increasing MELD was associated with reduced microbial richness and depletion of commensals. Worse PHES performance, however, showed a distinct microbiome signature with increased Streptococcus abundance independent of MELD, country, PPI use, and HE therapies. Twenty-two microbial pathways were associated with PHES, mostly related to amino-acid biosynthesis and nitrogen metabolism. Of these, ornithine degradation and heme B biosynthesis II were uniquely enriched with worse PHES and CHE, which mapped onto Enterobacteriaceae. We conclude that across four geographically and culturally disparate countries, cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment was associated with consistent microbial compositional and functional alterations distinct from advancing liver disease. These findings support a consistent gut‒liver‒brain axis signature involving oral-gut translocation and altered nitrogen metabolism.

articles.title: Experiences of family caregivers of older adults with stroke regarding caregiving competency: a qualitative study.
articles.journal: International journal of qualitative studies on health and well-being
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: With increasing life expectancy and the growing older adult population, stroke has become increasingly prevalent as one of the leading causes of long-term disability. A substantial proportion of the caregiving burden is borne by family caregivers. Caregiving competency plays a pivotal role in the quality of care, prevention of secondary complications, and improvement of patient outcomes.

PURPOSE: To elucidate the experiences of family caregivers of older adults with stroke regarding caregiving competency from the caregivers' perspective.

METHOD: This qualitative study was conducted in Iran from 2024 to 2025 using a conventional content analysis approach based on the method proposed by Elo and Kyngäs (2008). Participants consisted of 14 family caregivers of older adults with stroke who were selected purposively. Data were collected through in-depth semi-structured interviews, and data analysis was performed in three phases: preparation, organisation, and reporting.

RESULTS: A total of 14 subcategories and 5 main categories emerged, including: Management of Safety and Motor Functioning; Control of Essential Intake and Elimination Processes; Maintenance and Promotion of Psychological and Emotional Well-Being; Preparedness and Knowledge Updating; and Support for the Recovery of Cognitive Functioning.

CONCLUSIONS: Caregiving competency among family caregivers of older adults with stroke is multidimensional and extends beyond basic physical care to encompass emotional regulation, situational judgement, continuous learning, and cognitive support. In home-based care, caregivers function as active agents and continuous learners who play a complementary role in the rehabilitation process.

articles.title: Integrating physiological indicators and Precision Livestock Farming to support European animal welfare frameworks: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Animal welfare assessment in livestock production is increasingly supported by Precision Livestock Farming (PLF) technologies integrated with physiological monitoring. This Scopus-based systematic literature review, conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and synthesised using a narrative approach, examined physiological parameters relevant to animal welfare assessment and their integration into PLF across major livestock species, including cattle, pigs, poultry, sheep, and goats. Following the screening and eligibility assessment, 144 studies were selected from an initial dataset of 1386 records. Body surface temperature, heart rate, and respiratory rate were the most frequently investigated physiological parameters, while computer vision, wearable sensors, environmental sensing, and machine learning were the predominant technologies enabling continuous, non-invasive monitoring. The reviewed studies primarily addressed animal-based welfare indicators within European welfare assessment frameworks, whereas resource- and management-based indicators were comparatively underrepresented. No studies explicitly investigated antimicrobial use or the human-animal relationship using PLF technologies, highlighting important research gaps. Overall, the evidence indicates that physiological parameters provide complementary biological information that enhances the interpretation of animal-based welfare indicators, particularly when integrated with behavioural and environmental monitoring. Future research should prioritise multimodal approaches integrating physiological, behavioural, environmental, and management-related data to support more comprehensive and operationally feasible animal welfare assessment.

articles.title: Surface-functionalized Bifidobacterium bifidum alleviates Clostridioides difficile infection by coordinating host immune modulation and gut microbiota restoration☆.
articles.abstract: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a major ecological disruption of the gut ecosystem, characterized by loss of colonization resistance, persistent inflammatory feedback and incomplete microbial recovery. Meta-analysis of clinical cohorts identified Bifidobacterium depletion as a conserved feature of CDI-associated dysbiosis, suggesting that restoring this genus may promote recovery from CDI. Comparative in vitro assays identified B. bifidum as the most protective strain. This effect was not attributable to direct inhibition of C. difficile growth, but instead was associated with strong adhesion to intestinal mucus and epithelial cells and direct competition for epithelial attachment sites. However, B. bifidum alone was insufficient to counteract host inflammation and showed limited survival during gastrointestinal transit. To address these constraints, we integrated B. bifidum with β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB) to mitigate inflammation-associated habitat filtering and applied an outer hyaluronic-acid (HA) coating to protect B. bifidum viability and confer preferential targeting to the colon and inflamed mucosa. This sequential strategy, termed BB@PCB-HA, markedly alleviated inflammation and restored epithelial barrier integrity, microbial community structure and metabolic function in both CDI and recurrent CDI mouse models. These findings advance probiotic therapy from strain supplementation to programmable functionalized microecological intervention, providing a new paradigm for treating CDI and other gastrointestinal diseases.

articles.title: Therapeutic effects and mechanisms of neutrophil membrane-coated MXene (Ti 3 C 2 T x ) nanoparticles for sepsis treatment.
articles.abstract: Sepsis, a life-threatening organ dysfunction from a dysregulated infection response, remains a high-mortality global health burden characterized by the systemic overproduction of pro-inflammatory mediators and reactive oxygen and nitrogen species. Timely anti-infective/anti-inflammatory interventions in the early onset window drastically improve sepsis prognosis, yet current therapeutic efficacy remains severely constrained by the global antibiotic resistance crisis. As a two-dimensional nanomaterial, Ti3C2Tx MXene displays potent intrinsic antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory activities. We herein engineer a neutrophil membrane-coated Ti3C2Tx nanoplatform (NM@Ti3C2Tx NPs) for targeted sepsis therapy. Experimental validation confirms this formulation mitigates sepsis-triggered oxidative stress injury via synergistic antioxidant pathways, with favorable colloidal stability and confirmed in vitro biocompatibility. In CLP-induced murine sepsis models, it attenuates systemic pro-inflammatory cascades, alleviates hypothermia and multi-organ damage, and improves survival. Collectively, this multifunctional platform integrating targeted antibacterial action and oxidative stress modulation presents a promising candidate for sepsis translational therapy.

articles.title: Exploration of various administration routes for the nitric oxide donating organic nitrite, nitrosooxypropanol, in a porcine model.
articles.abstract: Organic nitrites are restricted to intravenous or inhaled administration. The aim was to explore novel administration routes for an organic nitrite, previously demonstrated to have pulmonary selectivity, in normal and elevated pulmonary vascular resistance. Hemodynamic and respiratory variables, including fraction of exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO), were measured in 13 anesthetized pigs. In naïve conditions, nitrosooxypropanol (PDNO) was given subcutaneously (100-1600 nmol/kg/min; 5 min/dose, 30 min interval), intramuscularly (50-400 nmol/kg/min; 5 min/dose, 30 min interval), intravenously (5-80 nmol/kg/min; 30 min infusion), intranasally (500-2000 nmol/kg boli), and sublingually (80-16,240 nmol/kg boli). In pulmonary hypertension (intravenous infusion of U46619), PDNO was given intravenously (5-45 nmol/kg/min; 15-20 mins infusion/dose) and subcutaneously (200-1800 nmol/kg/min; 5 min/dose at 20 min interval). Recovery was calculated using FeNO. PDNO, given by all administration routes, dose-dependently decreased systemic blood pressure and increased FeNO. Subcutaneous and intramuscular administration induced slow-onset (9 min to maximum effect) and long-lasting effects (~30 min). Intravenous administration induced rapid effects (1-2 min to steady state) and prompt decline after infusion cessation. The proportion of PDNO reaching exhaled gas (intravenous administration as reference; FeNO-based recovery) was 17% (intramuscularly) and 9% (subcutaneously). In pulmonary hypertension, intravenous and subcutaneous administration decreased the pulmonary/systemic vascular resistance-ratio. In this exploratory proof-of-concept study evaluating novel administration routes for organic nitrites, PDNO demonstrated measurable biological effects and acceptable FeNO-based recovery following intramuscular and subcutaneous administration. Furthermore, intranasal and tentatively sublingual administration showed biological effects. Future work on formulation and investigations into relevant disease models is warranted.

articles.title: Rational design of inhaled antibacterials targeting alveolar macrophages for efficient killing of resistant bacteria associated with lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs).
articles.abstract: Lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs), caused by antibiotic-resistant bacteria, are a leading cause of global death and morbidity. One of the principal limitations in treating respiratory bacterial infections is inefficient delivery and appropriate therapeutic drug concentrations to infected cells, as required to kill resistant bacteria. Inhaled antibiotic delivery technology specifically delivers antibacterials directly into the infected cells of the lungs and provides the required therapeutic concentration at a very low delivered dose, with a greatly reduced risk of systemic adverse effects. An alveolar macrophage (AM)-targeted antibiotic delivery strategy utilizing receptor-ligand interactions or stimuli-responsive mechanisms of drug release demonstrated efficient killing of intracellular bacteria. The rational design of antibacterials or formulations for inhalation is the key to achieving this goal. Based on ligand chemistry, decorating antibiotic carriers with ligands that target specific AM receptors is a novel strategy to ensure precise antibiotic delivery to the site of infection while reducing both the side effects associated with high systemic doses and the risk of further promoting antibiotic resistance. This review highlights advances in AM-targeted inhaled antibacterials, identification of appropriate ligands for specific AM receptors, mechanisms of interaction, and subsequent release of antibiotics through carrier degradation, pH-responsive behavior, or enzymatic cleavage to eradicate resistant bacteria. Finally, we discuss the ongoing challenges and future directions for AM-targeted inhaled antibacterials against LRTIs.

articles.title: Rifamycin use and gut microbial antibiotic resistance genes in cirrhosis: Results from a double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial.
articles.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance gene (ARG) carriage is associated with poor outcomes in patients with liver cirrhosis, which is worsened by repeated antibiotic exposure and hospitalizations. While the semi-synthetic rifamycin derivative, rifaximin, has recently been linked to ARG expansion preclinically, the effects of rifamycin SV MMX (RiVM) on the gut resistome remain unknown. We evaluated longitudinal resistome changes with RiVM in cirrhosis. The randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled RIVET trial (15 RiVM, 15 placebo) included compensated cirrhosis patients who underwent shotgun metagenomic sequencing before/after 30 days of therapy. ARGs were annotated using the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database. The longitudinal resistome was evaluated using univariable and multi-variable methods (LEfSe, paired-Wilcoxon testing, and MaAsLin3), and machine learning (ML) was used to determine ARG changes at subject and group levels. RiVM induced minimal perturbation of the gut resistome, without significant change in ARGs versus after FDR adjustment. Complementary approaches (univariable and multivariable) identified a trend towards lower vancomycin resistance ARGs, including vanW and vanT operon-associated genes, after RiVM exposure. In contrast, several Enterobacteriaceae-associated multidrug efflux regulators (including evgS, emrK, and mdtA) showed nominal increases post-rifamycin that did not withstand FDR. Group-level ML demonstrated limited discrimination between groups; however, within-subject longitudinal models achieved improved classification performance. No increase in infections or treatment-related safety concerns was observed. We conclude that rifamycin MMX was not associated with infections and did not enrich antimicrobial resistance genes compared to placebo in a small randomized 30-day clinical trial in patients with compensated cirrhosis. There was a tendency towards reduced vancomycin resistance and ARG reduction after rifamycin exposure. Registration: NCT04082780 www.clinicaltrials.gov.

articles.title: Hetrombopag in China: expanding indications, comparative positioning, and risk management - a critical narrative review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Hetrombopag is an oral nonpeptide thrombopoietin receptor agonist approved only in China. We critically appraised evidence across approved and investigational indications, compared it with other thrombopoietin receptor agonists, and assessed clinically relevant safety and risk management.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, the Cochrane Library, ClinicalTrials.gov, CNKI, and Wanfang were searched from inception through 18 October 2026, with citation tracing and regulatory/guideline review. Evidence was ranked by design and publication status.

RESULTS: A Chinese phase III adult immune thrombocytopenia trial reported week-8 platelet responses of 58.9% and 64.3% with two starting doses versus 5.9% with placebo. In refractory severe aplastic anemia, a single-arm phase II study reported week-18 hematologic response in at least one lineage of 41.8% (95% confidence interval 28.7-55.9). Randomized trials also underpin 2026 Chinese approvals for chronic immune thrombocytopenia in patients aged at least 6 years and adult solid-tumor treatment-induced thrombocytopenia; however, the pivotal phase III solid-tumor report remained a conference abstract and international validation was pending. No randomized head-to-head trial establishes superiority over eltrombopag, avatrombopag, or romiplostim. Safety data identify hepatic laboratory abnormalities, rare thrombosis and marrow fibrosis in adult immune thrombocytopenia, and clonal evolution in severe aplastic anemia.

DISCUSSION: Endpoint heterogeneity, sponsor involvement, abstract-only evidence, and limited multiethnic data constrain cross-trial inference. Food markedly reduces exposure; cyclosporine interaction data are reassuring but imprecise.

CONCLUSION: Use should follow local labels and disease guidelines, target clinically meaningful outcomes rather than platelet normalization, and include indication-specific hepatic, thrombotic, marrow, and discontinuation surveillance.

articles.title: Modelling and analysis of infectious diseases considering vaccination, mutation and quarantine strategies.
articles.abstract: From an experimental point of view, it is difficult to investigate the propagation mechanism of infectious disease and predict its trend. However, applying a nonlinear model offers a more straightforward and effective approach for analyzing transmission characteristics of infectious diseases. This paper proposes an SLVEIMQR dynamic model by dividing the population into susceptible (S), low-risk (L), vaccinated (V), exposed (E), infected (I), mutant (M), quarantined (Q) and recovered (R). The basic reproduction number and the equilibrium of the proposed model are computed, and the local asymptotic stability of the disease-free equilibrium is proved. Furthermore, the transcritical bifurcation at equilibrium and the sensitivity of key parameters are analyzed. To estimate the model parameters and predict the trend of infectious disease, the least squares method is applied by using epidemic data from different phases in Italy. The results show that the average relative errors of the model in the two prediction stages are 1.72% and 3.66%, respectively.

articles.title: Factors associated with self-reported health status among older adults in the Greater Kampala Metropolitan Area, Uganda: a cross-sectional survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Literature on the prevalence and factors associated with good self-reported health among older adults in the Greater Kampala Metropolitan Area (GKMA), including sex-stratified analyses, remains limited.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to examine the prevalence of good self-reported health and its associated factors among older adults (50-64 years) in the GKMA, with sex-stratified analyses.

METHODS: Data stem from the 'The Remaking of the Family in East Africa (FAMILEA)' survey of 2024. A set of cross-sectional variables from a subsample of 651 older adults (aged 50-64) was used. We applied frequency distributions for descriptive statistics and a multivariable modified Poisson regression model to investigate factors associated with self-reported health status among older adults in the GKMA, with sex-stratified patterns.

RESULTS: In the GKMA, 58% of older adults (64% of males and 52% of females) declared good health. Older adults living in Wakiso District, satisfied with accommodation, working, not living in a household-owned house, in the second and fourth quintiles, and not functionally constrained, reported good health. Accommodation satisfaction and non-limited functional status were positively associated with good health, irrespective of sex. Among males, living in a nuclear family, working, not reporting the lowest wealth quintile, and being affiliated with the Catholic religion were positively associated with good health. Among females, living in Wakiso District and never lacking companionship were positively associated with good health.

CONCLUSION: Good self-reported health was associated with various factors among older adults (50-64 years) in the GKMA, with some patterns observed in the sex-stratified models.

articles.title: A microbiota-metabolite-glial axis drives white matter repair via isorhamnetin-PSAP-GPR37 signaling after ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) induces persistent neuroinflammation and white matter injury that limit neurological recovery, yet effective repair-oriented therapies remain lacking. Although microbiota influences stroke outcomes, how microbial activity drives central nervous system repair is unclear. Here, we integrate clinical microbiome profiling, experimental stroke models, multi-omics analyses, and mechanistic validation to define a microbiota-metabolite-glial signaling axis that promotes post-stroke recovery. Akkermansia muciniphila (Akk) is associated with favorable outcomes in patients and improves recovery in mice without altering infarct size, supporting a repair-promoting rather than neuroprotective mechanism. Mechanistically, Akk increases circulating isorhamnetin (Iso), a key systemic mediator that suppresses lipid-laden, pro-inflammatory microglia and promotes oligodendrocyte maturation and white matter repair. Iso reprograms microglia to secrete PSAP, and conditioned medium-but not direct Iso-activates GPR37-ERK signaling in oligodendrocytes. In vitro knockdown of Psap or Gpr37 markedly attenuates these effects, demonstrating a microglia-dependent mechanism. In vivo adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated Gpr37 knockdown abolishes the beneficial effects of Akk and Iso on functional recovery and white matter repair, establishing the necessity of PSAP-GPR37 signaling. These findings identify a microbiota-driven metabolic pathway linking gut activity to white matter repair after IS.

articles.title: Mental distress and healthcare utilisation among sami and non-sami adults: a prospective registry-linked cohort study utilising data from the SAMINOR 2 questionnaire survey and the Norwegian control and payment of health reimbursements database (2012-2022).
articles.abstract: Mental distress is associated increased healthcare utilisation, but little is known about whether the relationship between mental distress and use of health care services differs between Sami and non-Sami populations in Norway. The aim of this study was to investigate whether level of mental distress was associated with a different pattern of use of primary and specialised healthcare services among Sami and non-Sami populations. Data from the SAMINOR 2 Questionnaire Survey were linked to data from the Norwegian Control and Payout of Health Refunds Database and Statistics Norway. Level of mental distress based on the 10 items Hopkins Symptom Checklist was the primary exposure variable. Participants were categorised as Sami or non-Sami and stratified by sex. Primary and specialist healthcare utilisation, and the interaction between mental distress and ethnicity, were assessed by estimating incidence rates and incidence rate ratios from Negative binomial generalised linear models with a log link. The primary model was adjusted for age, years of education, and chronic conditions. Mental distress was associated with increased utilisation of both primary and specialist healthcare services across all ethnic and sex groups. Only minor differences in use of health care were observed between the two ethnic groups. Ethnicity did not significantly modify the associations between mental distress and use of health care. The association between mental distress and healthcare use was largely similar across ethnic groups after adjustment for covariates. Comparable utilisation rates should not be interpreted as evidence of identical healthcare-seeking processes, as cultural, contextual, and structural factors may influence how individuals engage with healthcare services. Further research should explore pathways to healthcare among Sami and non-Sami populations.

articles.title: Local ablative treatment for oligoprogression during immunotherapy in metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Some patients with metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) receiving anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) progress at a few sites while disease elsewhere stays controlled, a pattern consistent with focal, oligo-acquired immune escape rather than systemic treatment failure. Ablating the escaping focus may eliminate the resistant clone and preserve an otherwise effective immunotherapy line. We performed a PRISMA 2020-compliant, PROSPERO-registered systematic review and meta-analysis of local ablative treatment (LAT) for oligoprogressive or oligo-resistant metastatic NSCLC during active ICI therapy, with continuation of the same immunotherapy line after LAT. MEDLINE, PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to March 8, 2026. From 1270 records, 22 studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Four studies, one randomized subgroup, and three retrospective cohorts contributed to each primary analysis. LAT-oriented management was associated with improved progression-free survival (PFS; pooled hazard ratio [HR] 0.45, 95% CI 0.33-0.62; 95% prediction interval [PI] 0.28-0.74; I2 = 0%) and overall survival (OS; pooled HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.27-0.63; 95% PI 0.24-0.69; I2 = 0%). PFS and OS estimates were consistent across sensitivity analyses, including the exclusion of the one PFS estimate measured to a second progression. The evidence is predominantly observational and of low certainty, reflecting the current absence of NSCLC-specific randomized trials. On this evidence, LAT, delivered predominantly as stereotactic body radiotherapy, may be considered a continuation-enabling option for carefully selected patients with focal progression on otherwise effective immunotherapy, pending ongoing randomized trials.

articles.title: Causal effects of physical activity and sedentary behaviors on hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: a two-sample Mendelian randomization study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDPs) are major causes of maternal and perinatal morbidity. While observational studies suggest physical activity may reduce HDP risk, confounding and reverse causality limit causal inference.

METHODS: We conducted a two-sample Mendelian randomization study using genetic instruments for 11 activity traits from UK Biobank and outcome data for gestational hypertension and pre-eclampsia from FinnGen.

RESULTS: Light do-it-yourself (DIY) activities were associated with lower risks of gestational hypertension (β[Formula: see text]  = -3.56, P = 0.002) and pre-eclampsia (β = -3.54, P = 0.029). Aerobic exercise was associated with lower pre-eclampsia risk (β = -3.56, P = 0.017). No significant associations were found for vigorous activity, moderate-to-vigorous activity, or the three specific sedentary behaviors examined (time spent using a computer, time spent watching television, and time spent driving).

CONCLUSION: This study provides causal evidence that specific physical activities confer protection against HDPs. Genetically predicted light DIY activities were associated with lower risks of both gestational hypertension and pre-eclampsia, while aerobic exercise was associated with lower pre-eclampsia risk. The three sedentary behaviors examined showed no causal associations. These findings highlight light-intensity domestic activities and aerobic exercise as accessible strategies for HDP prevention in prenatal care.

articles.title: Underdetected peripheral artery disease in people with hypertension: A narrative review of risk-stratified case-finding, diagnostic pathways, and equity in care.
articles.journal: Clinical and experimental hypertension (New York, N.Y. : 1993)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is common but often underrecognized in people with hypertension because symptoms are frequently absent or atypical and access to physiologic testing is uneven. This narrative review examines how hypertension care can support risk-stratified PAD recognition while keeping targeted case-finding distinct from universal screening.

METHODS: We conducted a structured narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE from inception through 31 July 2026, supplemented by citation searching and review of major US and European guidelines and relevant US policy and coverage sources. Evidence was interpreted according to the question it could answer: association/prognosis, diagnostic accuracy, treatment effect, implementation, or policy status.

RESULTS: Hypertension and PAD share age-related, metabolic, renal, and tobacco-related determinants, while pressure-related vascular injury provides biological plausibility for their association. Resting ankle-brachial index (ABI) is the initial physiologic test for appropriately selected people; toe-brachial index with waveforms is preferred for noncompressible ankle arteries, exercise ABI for persistent exertional symptoms despite normal or borderline resting values, and duplex ultrasound when anatomic definition will change management. Guideline-supported risk-based testing differs from universal screening of unselected asymptomatic adults, for which outcome benefit remains unproven. Detection is clinically meaningful only when linked to appropriate prevention, symptom management, foot protection, and referral.

CONCLUSION: This narrative review supports a risk-stratified, treatment-linked approach to PAD recognition in hypertension care, but the proposed case-finding pathway itself has not been proven to improve clinical outcomes. Pragmatic trials of the complete care pathway are needed.

articles.title: Metabolic, hormonal, and reproductive effects of GLP-1 receptor agonizts in hyperandrogenic insulin-resistant women: a systematic review.
articles.journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Hyperandrogenic insulin-resistant states, most commonly polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and severe phenotypes such as HAIR-AN syndrome, are characterized by metabolic dysfunction, androgen excess, and reproductive disturbance. Insulin resistance is a central pathogenic driver and therapeutic target.

OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonizts on metabolic, hormonal, and reproductive outcomes in adult women with hyperandrogenic insulin-resistant states. Data Sources and Study Selection: A systematic search identified randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and case series evaluating GLP-1 receptor agonizts in PCOS and HAIR-AN syndrome, reflecting the heterogeneity of the current evidence base.Data extraction and synthesis Outcomes were synthesized across metabolic (anthropometric and glycaemic), hormonal, reproductive, dermatologic, and safety domains, accounting for heterogeneity in interventions and study designs.

RESULTS: Metabolic responses appeared more consistent and robust than endocrine outcomes. Reproductive outcomes such as menstrual regularity were variably reported and showed inconsistent improvement across studies, limiting firm conclusions regarding fertility-related benefit. Evidence in severe phenotypes remains limited but suggestive of clinical benefit.

CONCLUSIONS: GLP-1 receptor agonizts are a promising adjunctive therapy in hyperandrogenic insulin-resistant states, with the strongest evidence for metabolic improvement. Reproductive and endocrine outcomes remain less consistent, likely reflecting heterogeneity in study design, populations, and outcome reporting. Further high-quality, phenotype-specific trials are required.

articles.title: Daratumumab in immune-mediated thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura: emerging evidence for plasma cell-targeted therapy.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Immune mediated thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura is a life threatening autoimmune thrombotic microangiopathy caused by severe ADAMTS13 deficiency due to inhibitory autoantibodies. Despite plasma exchange, corticosteroids, rituximab, and caplacizumab, some patients develop refractory disease or persistent and relapsing ADAMTS13 deficiency.

OBJECTIVES: To summarize the mechanistic rationale, clinical efficacy, safety, and potential therapeutic role of daratumumab in refractory or frequently relapsing immune mediated thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura.

METHODS: A structured narrative review was conducted across five major bibliographic databases, PubMed, EMBASE, the Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), and Web of Science, from database inception through September 13, 2026. Searches of major hematology journal databases were also performed. Case reports, case series, registry analyses, multicenter cohort studies, and conference abstracts describing the use of daratumumab in acquired immune-mediated thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (iTTP) were included. Clinical setting, treatment regimen, ADAMTS13 response, time to response, relapse, and adverse events were extracted and qualitatively synthesized. Because reports differ in populations, endpoints, concomitant therapy, and possible patient overlap, findings were synthesized qualitatively without a pooled response estimate.

RESULTS: Six key clinical reports involving more than 40 patients were identified. Most patients had received multiple previous therapies, including plasma exchange, corticosteroids, rituximab, and caplacizumab. Daratumumab was administered intravenously at 16 mg/kg or subcutaneously at 1,800 mg, usually weekly for two to six doses. Across the available reports, ADAMTS13 recovery was observed in a substantial proportion of treated patients, although reported response rates varied according to the populations studied and the thresholds used to define response. Recovery commonly occurred within several weeks. Multicenter reports also described sustained remission in a proportion of responders, although biochemical relapse remained frequent during follow-up. Adverse events were generally manageable, with predominantly mild infusion reactions and infrequent serious infections. Other individualized treatment strategies described after rituximab failure or intolerance include bortezomib, optimized or alternative anti-CD20 therapy, ciclosporin, azathioprine, and mycophenolate.

CONCLUSION: Daratumumab is a promising plasma cell directed therapy for rituximab refractory or frequently relapsing immune mediated thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura. Prospective studies are required to define its role within treatment algorithms.

articles.title: Coronavirus health beliefs and fetal health concerns: associations with preventive health behaviors during COVID-19.
articles.journal: Journal of psychosomatic obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: During infectious disease outbreaks, pregnant women and their fetuses may be especially vulnerable to health risks, emphasizing the importance of preventive health behaviors (PHB). The role of concerns about fetal health in shaping PHB during COVID-19 has never been examined. The present study examined the joint effect of concerns about fetal health and Coronavirus-related health beliefs (within the Health Belief Model) on PHB during COVID-19.

METHODS: During the COVID-19 pandemic (September-November 2021), 202 pregnant Israeli women completed online questionnaires that assessed concerns about fetal health, health beliefs (perceived susceptibility, severity, benefits, and barriers), and adherence to preventive health behaviors. Multiple hierarchical regression and mediation analyses were conducted.

RESULTS: Concerns about fetal health were positively associated with PHB. Perceived susceptibility and perceived benefits were also positively associated with PHB, whereas perceived barriers were negatively associated; perceived severity was not significant. Mediation analyses indicated that concerns about fetal health fully mediated the association between perceived susceptibility and PHB and partially mediated the associations between perceived severity and perceived benefits and PHB.

CONCLUSIONS: Concerns about fetal health play important direct and indirect roles in adhering to PHB during pregnancy. These findings may guide health services in developing tailored programs during pandemics.

articles.title: Polycystic ovary syndrome research in sub-Saharan Africa: a systematic review on current status and future directions.
articles.journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is one of the most prevalent disorders affecting women. The status of PCOS research in sub-Saharan Africa is unknown, where non-communicable diseases are prevalent but often underrecognized. To assess current knowledge about PCOS in sub-Saharan Africa and identify gaps in the literature.

METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, and African Journals Online through 9 August 2026 to identify original studies on PCOS in sub-Saharan Africa. Original research studies involving sub-Saharan African populations, without age-related constraints, were eligible. We excluded non-original studies and studies that did not focus on PCOS. Three independent reviewers (S.H., M.A., and C.C.M.) performed the searches.
