RESULTS: Of 1973 retrieved records, 40 studies met the inclusion criteria, predominantly from Nigeria, with additional contributions from South Africa, Cameroon, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Tanzania, Benin, Kenya, and Ethiopia. Most studies were observational and primarily focused on PCOS in the context of infertility. No population-based prevalence studies were identified; however, 13 studies reported PCOS prevalence, mostly in clinically selected populations.

CONCLUSIONS: PCOS remains understudied in sub-Saharan Africa, with substantial gaps in population-based epidemiology, diagnostic practices, phenotype distribution, management, and metabolic outcomes. Addressing these gaps through larger, well-designed studies is critical to accurately assess the disease burden, inform clinical guidelines, and optimize management strategies. Additionally, overcoming barriers such as cultural attitudes, cost, and limited accessibility to diagnostic tools and treatment options remains essential to improving PCOS care and research across the region.PROSPERO registration ID CRD420250649730 - 13 March 2025.

articles.title: Global stability analysis of within-host Zika virus-chikungunya virus co-infection with CTL immune responses.
articles.abstract: We formulate and analyse a mathematical model for the within-host co-infection dynamics of Zika virus (ZIKV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), incorporating latently infected cells and cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) immune responses. We establish the nonnegativity and boundedness of solutions. Using the next-generation matrix method, we derive the basic reproduction numbers (RZL) and (RCL) for the ZIKV and CHIKV submodels, respectively, and the overall reproduction number (R0L=max{RZL,RCL}). Invasion reproduction numbers, (RZL,inv) and (RCL,inv), are derived to characterise the ability of either virus to invade an established infection. Global stability of the equilibria is established using Lyapunov functions. We investigate three therapeutic protocols: antiviral treatment blocking viral entry, treatment reducing viral production, and IL-2 therapy enhancing CTL responses. Sensitivity analysis of (RZL) and (RCL) is performed, and numerical simulations support the stability results. Simulations indicate that combined antiviral and immune-based interventions suppress co-infection by reducing viral replication and enhancing immune-mediated clearance.

articles.title: A clinical-radiological model for predicting in-hospital mortality in acute exacerbation of COPD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quantitative computed tomography (QCT) has emerged as a promising tool for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) phenotyping. However, its prognostic value in acute exacerbations of COPD (AECOPD) remains insufficiently explored, and existing risk stratification models have limited integration of imaging-derived metrics. This study aimed to develop and validate a prognostic model that integrates multidimensional clinical variables with QCT-derived metrics, and to compare its predictive performance with traditional clinical scores for in-hospital mortality in AECOPD.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, consecutive patients aged ≥40 years hospitalized with severe AECOPD were enrolled from September 2010 to October 2024, with collection of demographic characteristics, clinical features, laboratory indices, and chest CT imaging data. The cohort was randomly split into training and testing sets (7:3). Candidate predictors were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression followed by multivariable logistic regression. Four classification models were developed and evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation. Discriminative performance was assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and compared with conventional clinical scores.

RESULTS: A total of 465 patients with AECOPD were included, of whom 47 (10.1%) died during hospitalization. Five independent predictors were identified: confusion, lymphocyte count <0.8 × 109/L, chronic heart failure, white blood cell count ≥10 × 109/L, and reduced pulmonary vascular fractal dimension. The logistic regression model demonstrated the best performance, achieving an AUC of 0.852 (95% CI, 0.738-0.965) in the testing set, significantly outperforming other models and established clinical scores.

CONCLUSIONS: A predictive model integrating QCT-derived metrics with clinical features improved AECOPD in-hospital mortality prediction over traditional scores, supporting its utility for individualized risk stratification and management.

articles.title: PmZapA orchestrates zinc homeostasis and pleiotropic stress responses to drive pathogenicity in Talaromyces marneffei.
articles.abstract: Zinc homeostasis is critical for pathogenic microbes during their interactions with hosts. In Aspergillus nidulans, the transcription factor ZapA serves as a key regulator of zinc uptake. However, the function of ZapA in the thermally dimorphic pathogen Talaromyces marneffei remains largely unexplored. In this study, we identified and characterized the ZapA homolog in T. marneffei. Our results demonstrate that PmZapA acts as a master regulator of zinc homeostasis by directly controlling the expression of the zinc transporter encoding genes. Deletion of PmzapA severely impaired growth under Zinc - conditions and reduced pigment production. Notably, in a Galleria mellonella larval infection model, the ΔPmzapA strain exhibited significantly attenuated virulence. However, the reduced pathogenicity was not solely attributable to defective zinc transport, as additional pleiotropic effects were detected. Specifically, the ΔPmzapA strain showed impaired reactive oxygen species (ROS) clearance capability, as well as increased susceptibility to cell wall stress and alkaline pH. Integrated RNA-seq and ChIP-seq analysis revealed that PmZapA governs a broad regulatory network, directly and indirectly modulating pathways involved in redox homeostasis, secondary metabolite biosynthesis, as well as carbon metabolism. Collectively, our work identifies PmZapA as a novel virulence determinant in T. marneffei.

articles.title: Translation and cross-cultural adaptation of the Palliative Care Knowledge Scale (PaCKS) into European Portuguese and its measurement properties in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and interstitial lung diseases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: No instruments exist to assess palliative care knowledge among Portuguese with chronic respiratory diseases.

AIM: To translate and cross-culturally adapt the Palliative Care Knowledge Scale (PaCKS) into European Portuguese and explore its measurement properties in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and interstitial lung diseases (ILD).

METHODS: Translation and cross-cultural adaptation procedures were followed. Internal consistency (Cronbach's α); test-retest reliability [intraclass correlation coefficient with 95% confidence interval (ICC2,1 [95% CI]), standard error of measurement (SEM/SEM%), minimal detectable change at 95% confidence level (MDC95/MDC%) and Bland-Altman method]; floor/ceiling effects; and, construct validity [convergent/divergent, correlation (Spearman's - rs) with the Bristol COPD Knowledge Questionnaire (BCKQ)/modified Medical Research Council dyspnoea questionnaire/lung function] were evaluated.

RESULTS: Two forward translations/back-translations were conducted. Five experts approved the prefinal version. Cognitive debriefing involved 12 participants. Measurement properties were analysed in 102 people with COPD and 54 with ILD (73.1% male; 67.6 ± 10.0 years). PaCKS score was 11.0 [9.0-12.0] and 10.0 [8.8-11.0] in COPD and ILD, respectively. Internal consistency was acceptable (αCOPD = 0.76; αILD = 0.80). The test-retest reliability was good in COPD (ICC2,1 0.84 [0.77-0.89]) and ranged from good to excellent in ILD (ICC2,1 0.89 [0.78-0.94]). SEM/SEM% and MDC95/MDC% were 1.0/9.6% and 2.8/26.6%, and 1.0/10.1% and 2.7/28.0% in COPD and ILD, respectively. The Bland-Altman method did not suggest systematic bias, with 95% limits of agreement of approximately ±3.0. No floor/ceiling effects were observed, except for a ceiling effect in COPD (20.6%). The PaCKS/BCKQ correlation was significant, positive and moderate (rs = 0.40, p < 0.001) in COPD. Other correlations were non-significant and ranged from negligible to weak.

CONCLUSION: The European Portuguese PaCKS is now available and provides reliable and valid data on palliative care knowledge in COPD and ILD.

articles.title: Gut virome remodeling after fecal microbiota transplantation is associated with virus-bacteria co-variation and metabolic response in obesity and type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) modifies gut bacterial composition and improves metabolic outcomes in subjects with obesity and type 2 diabetes (ObT2), but bacterial changes alone do not fully explain the heterogeneity in clinical response. We performed virus-like particle (VLP)-enriched metagenomic sequencing coupled with bulk-DNA metagenomic sequencing on longitudinal fecal samples from a randomized controlled FMT trial in ObT2. Using random forest classification, post-FMT virome changes showed accuracy comparable to bacteriome changes (84.8% vs 81.4%) in distinguishing LDL responders from non-responders. Donor-derived viral contig engraftment was detected in 64.7% (11/17) of recipients receiving FMT alone and 58.8% (10/17) receiving FMT with lifestyle intervention (LSI), versus 5.6% (1/18) in the sham with LSI group. FMT was associated with increased virome diversity, compositional shifts toward the donor virome, and coordinated virus-bacteria associations, with most responsive viral contigs classified as Caudoviricetes. FMT-responsive viral contigs that were shared between the two FMT groups were predicted to infect Roseburia and Bifidobacterium, while contigs associated with clinical responses were predicted to infect Escherichia, Roseburia, Blautia, and Enterococcus. These findings suggest that the gut virome is a complementary ecological component associated with FMT responses and metabolic outcomes in ObT2.

articles.title: High cardiometabolic burden among people with HIV and obesity in Peru.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiometabolic disease has been studied in people with HIV, but evidence focused on people with HIV and obesity remains limited. This study assessed atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, metabolic abnormalities, markers of inflammation, and cardiovascular risk scores among people with HIV and obesity.

METHODS: We conducted an observational, cross-sectional study in clinically stable people with HIV aged ≥35 years and BMI >30 kg/m² in Lima-Callao, Peru, in 2024.

RESULTS: Participants enroled were 126; 77.7% were male, mean age was 50.6 years, mean time on antiretroviral therapy (ART) was 12.4 years, mean CD4 count was 759.8 cells/µL, and 97.6% had HIV-RNA <200 copies/µL. Mean BMI was 34.0. Clinical cardiovascular disease history was uncommon (2.4%); however, carotid Doppler ultrasound showed atherosclerotic changes in 34.4% (increased CIMT or carotid plaque), which associated with older age and longer time of ART. Abnormal glucose metabolism was identified in 89.7%, dyslipidemia in 82.5%, metabolic syndrome in 50.8%, elevated inflammatory markers in 28.2%, and low apolipoprotein A1 in 22.6%. Only 8.1% had normal findings across all evaluations. High cardiovascular risk was observed in 19.4% by Framingham, 9.4% by ACC/AHA, and 75.4% by HIV-CARDIO-PREDICT score.

CONCLUSIONS: This population of middle-aged, clinically stable people with HIV and obesity presented substantial burden of subclinical atherosclerosis and metabolic abnormalities despite low reported cardiovascular disease history. Cardiovascular risk estimates varied substantially across scores, with an HIV-specific score identifying a much higher proportion of patients as high risk than general-population scores. Targeted evaluation and timely preventive management may help reduce cardiometabolic complications.

articles.title: Placental mitochondrial impairment in preeclampsia patients.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia is a pregnancy-specific hypertensive disorder characterized by new-onset hypertension after 20 weeks of gestation, accompanied by end-organ dysfunction with or without proteinuria. Affecting approximately 5-7% of pregnancies worldwide, it remains a leading cause of maternal and fetal morbidity and mortality. Despite decades of research, the underlying pathophysiology of preeclampsia remains incompletely understood. However, increasing evidence implicates placental mitochondrial oxidative stress in its pathogenesis. In this review, we summarize the current literature pertaining to ultrastructural evidence of mitochondrial damage, defects in oxidative phosphorylation and electron transport chain activity, and alterations in reactive oxygen species production, antioxidant defense, and mitochondrial biogenesis. Finally, we discuss translational considerations and highlight how therapeutic strategies targeted at restoring mitochondrial function may represent a promising approach for managing preeclampsia.

articles.title: Intratumoral Fusobacterium nucleatum promotes ferroptosis resistance and a disulfide-stress-associated vulnerability under glucose restriction.
articles.abstract: Fusobacterium nucleatum (Fn) is an intracellular oncogenic bacterium implicated in multiple cancers. Although Fn has been linked to resistance to anticancer therapies, its effects on therapies targeting metabolic cell-death programs remain unclear. Here, we show that intratumoral Fn abundance is positively associated with SLC7A11 expression and that Fn infection attenuates Era- and RSL3-induced ferroptosis in tumor cells. Live-versus-killed, donor-based, and pharmacological evidence suggests that H2S generated during Fn infection contributes to SLC7A11 induction and engagement of the downstream GSH/GPX4 axis. Fn infection also reduces lipid-peroxide and Fe2⁺ accumulation and is accompanied by ACSL4 downregulation and FTH1 upregulation. Fn-infected cells display increased glucose uptake and a heightened dependence on glucose. Under glucose-replete conditions, Fn-infected cells are relatively resistant to ferroptosis, whereas glucose deprivation exposes a conditional vulnerability accompanied by disulfide stress. RSL3 further sensitized Fn-infected cells to glucose restriction, and combined GPX4 inhibition with the GLUT1 inhibitor BAY876 enhanced antitumor activity in Fn-infected solid-tumor models. These findings identify a nutrient-dependent metabolic liability associated with Fn infection and support further evaluation of combined glucose-transport and GPX4 inhibition in appropriately controlled models.

articles.title: High ex vivo recombination rate of African swine fever virus in porcine alveolar macrophages.
articles.abstract: Using fluorescently labeled African Swine Fever Virus (ASFV) strains, a high (~0.2) quasi-recombinant frequency (qRF3-4) was detected ex vivo during 3-4 replication cycles in naïve porcine alveolar macrophages (PAM). While co-infection and recombination frequencies remained low in PAM, they increased sharply between the second and fourth viral cycles. Infection multiplicity and synchronicity significantly influenced ASFV recombination frequency, which correlated positively with genetic distance. Crossing the ASFV/Lv17/WB/Rie1 mutants yielded a saturation curve resembling the Haldane mapping function, plateauing at ~20% recombination frequency at 160 kbp. Crossing less homologous strains (ASFV/Lv17/WB/Rie1 × ASFV/NHV/P68) reduced the recombination frequency; however, at large marker distances (140 kbp), it approached values (0.18) observed in homologous strains. A novel mathematical model estimated the average co-infection rate to be 0.47 after three viral cycles. Empirical application of the model revealed that 1 centimorgan translates to ~550-1650 bp, meaning offspring virions from a single cell undergo an average of 1.15-3.45 recombination events. This high recombination rate is consistent with in vivo observations and has critical implications for ASFV prevention and vaccination strategies. Such genomic plasticity can facilitate rapid viral evolution, potentially undermining the efficacy of live-attenuated vaccines globally.

articles.title: D-enantiomeric β-casein 197 disrupts biofilm-associated infection of MDR Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii through superior LPS binding and host cell protection.
articles.abstract: Biofilms formed by multidrug-resistant (MDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii are a major cause of chronic nosocomial infections and therapeutic failure. L-form antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are rapidly degraded by proteases, whereas D-enantiomeric peptides offer enhanced resistance to proteases. Here, we synthesized L- and D-β-casein 197, a milk-derived AMP, and systematically compared their antibiofilm activities against eight clinical isolates of P. aeruginosa and A. baumannii. The D-form reduced biofilm biomass by up to 83% during formation and by up to 88% in preformed biofilms. Mechanistic analyses revealed that the D-form caused more extensive membrane disruption, as demonstrated by flow cytometry and transmission electron microscopy. Isothermal titration calorimetry showed that the D-form bound LPS with higher affinity (KD 0.8 μM vs 3.1 μM), and molecular docking identified additional hydrogen bonds with lipid A. The D-form also more effectively inhibited bacterial motility. Both peptides exhibited low cytotoxicity toward cells (>90% viability at 100 μM), and the D-form reduced bacteria-induced cytotoxicity and bacterial internalization in infected macrophages more effectively than the L-form. In a Galleria mellonella infection model, D-β-casein 197 significantly improved survival against P. aeruginosa no. R1 and A. baumannii no. 13 challenge over 96 h compared to the L-form and untreated infected controls, while larval survival remained comparable to PBS controls, indicating negligible host toxicity. These findings identify D-β-casein 197 as a potent antibiofilm peptide against MDR Gram-negative biofilms, with enhanced activity, and LPS-neutralization assays confirmed that its antimicrobial potency is, at least in part, attributable to its stronger LPS binding affinity.

articles.title: Pacak-Zhuang syndrome with EPAS1 p.Pro531Leu somatic variant: one case report and literature review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To report a case child of Pacak-Zhuang syndrome with EPAS1 p.Pro531Leu somatic variant in a child and to summarize the clinical characteristics, diagnosis, treatment methods, and prognosis of this syndrome based on a literature review.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on the clinical data of a child girl with Pacak-Zhuang syndrome admitted to Hebei Children's Hospital in July 2019. Using the search terms 'Pacak-Zhuang syndrome', 'EPAS1', 'HIF-2α', 'HIF-2A', and 'Polycythemia-paraganglioma syndrome', relevant literature was retrieved from PubMed and Web of Science. The clinical manifestations, diagnostic methods, treatment plans, and outcomes of patients with this syndrome were analyzed.

RESULTS: A 4-year-old girl had recurrent hypertension, polycythemia and renal hilar masses. Diagnosis was confirmed by imaging, biochemical detection and paraffin tissue genetic testing. She received three operations for paragangliomas; pathology showed CgA(+), Syn(+), NSE(+) and Ki‑67 ≤5%. Follow-up revealed tumor recurrence, but the condition improved with oral temozolomide. Combined with 10 retrieved articles, 18 patients (4 males,14 females, mean age 25 years) were analyzed. Polycythemia was the cardinal manifestation. All patients received surgery, and 10 suffered uncontrolled tumor recurrence.

CONCLUSION: Pacak-Zhuang syndrome is a rare disorder involving the neuroendocrine and hematopoietic systems, often initially presenting with 'polycythemia'. Most cases are sporadic, with no apparent familial inheritance or history of other neuroendocrine tumors. When encountering pediatric patients with unexplained hypertension accompanied by polycythemia symptoms, the possibility of this syndrome should be considered, and further imaging studies and genetic testing are required for definitive diagnosis.

articles.title: Acute liver injury is triggered by dysbiosis and microbial translocation involving gut-liver axis.
articles.abstract: Acute liver injury (ALI) is a severe clinical condition that can progress to chronic liver failure, cirrhosis, or hepatocellular carcinoma, yet therapeutic options remain limited. Here, we investigated how hepatotoxin-induced gut-liver dysbiosis drives hepatic inflammation through microbial crosstalk. Using three murine ALI models, we assessed liver injury, intestinal barrier integrity, microbial composition along the gut-liver axis, and immune activation. Each hepatotoxin recapitulated distinct features of human ALI and induced unique patterns of hepatic and intestinal injury, enabling the progressive translocation of live bacteria from the gut to the liver and bloodstream. ALI was consistently associated with depletion of commensal taxa (Lactobacillaceae, Ruminococcaceae, and Bifidobacteriaceae) and enrichment of opportunistic pathogens (Enterococcaceae, Clostridiaceae, Enterobacteriaceae, and Burkholderiaceae). Dysbiosis also involved reduced gut bacteriophages and the expansion of viral families, including Retroviridae and Herpesviridae, in the liver and blood. Transplantation of the fecal or liver microbiota from ALI mice into microbiota-depleted recipients reproduced liver injury, immune activation, and intestinal barrier disruption, demonstrating that dysbiotic microbial communities alone are sufficient to trigger hepatic inflammation. These communities activated Th1/Th17 associated pathways (NF-κB, IL-17, TGF-β, and antigen presentation networks) and expanded pro-inflammatory immune populations. A key advance of this study is the direct comparison of fecal- versus liver-derived microbiota, revealing distinct mechanistic roles for each in driving liver pathology. Across all models, hepatotoxin-induced intestinal barrier breakdown drives gut-liver dysbiosis, microbial translocation, and immune-mediated liver injury. These findings uncover a unifying mechanism by which microbial imbalance reprograms hepatic immunity and accelerates ALI progression.

articles.title: Association of serum creatinine-to-albumin ratio with hyperandrogenemia and low sex hormone-binding globulin in women of reproductive age: a cross-sectional analysis of NHANES 2013-2016.
articles.journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hyperandrogenemia (HA) and low sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) are core features of polycystic ovary syndrome. The creatinine-to-albumin ratio (CAR), a simple renal-nutritional marker linked to female infertility, has not been studied in relation to HA or low SHBG.

OBJECTIVE: To examine the association of CAR with low SHBG and HA, defined by the free androgen index (FAI), in U.S. women of reproductive age.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional analysis of NHANES 2013-2016, we included 683 women aged 18-49 years. CAR (serum creatinine/albumin) was categorized into tertiles; low SHBG was defined as < 30 nmol/L and HA as FAI ≥ 75th percentile. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression was used, with multiple imputation (m = 5) as a sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: In Model 1 (age, race/ethnicity, education, income), the highest CAR tertile was associated with low SHBG (OR 2.93, 95% CI 1.49-5.75; P = 0.003; P for trend = 0.004) and FAI-defined HA (OR 1.87, 95% CI 1.05-3.34; P = 0.036; P for trend = 0.044). In Model 2 (plus smoking, BMI, low HDL-C), associations attenuated (OR 1.95, 95% CI 1.05-3.64 for low SHBG; 1.24, 95% CI 0.65-2.34 for HA-FAI). HA defined by total testosterone was not associated with CAR.

CONCLUSION: Higher CAR was associated with low SHBG and FAI-defined HA after demographic adjustment, with attenuation after metabolic adjustment, suggesting confounding by shared metabolic factors. As CAR derives from routine laboratory tests, it may be a practical marker of reproductive metabolic risk; the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.

articles.title: Sustaining nursing practice in Greenland: insights from a positive deviance study on motivation, resilience, and holistic care in arctic healthcare.
articles.abstract: Health disparities in the Arctic remain substantial, with Inuit populations experiencing shorter life expectancy and higher morbidity than global averages. Nurse shortage exacerbates these challenges, and Greenland continues to rely on nurses from other countries. Despite these constraints, health outcomes have improved over time, including increased life expectancy, enhanced diabetes care, and better child growth indicators. To sustain professional well-being and retention in the Greenlandic nursing workforce, this study explores how nurses deliver high-quality care under constrained conditions, and what motivates them to remain in healthcare using a positive deviance framework. Ethnographic fieldwork was conducted across five Greenland regions, involving participant observations and interviews with nurses and students across professional roles. Across backgrounds and seniority, nurses demonstrated a shared passion for their work, with patient encounters central to practice. Resilient communities, shaped through collaboration and humour, supported creative problem-solving and a strong sense of responsibility, extending from individual patients to healthcare and society. Nurses sustain their practice through patient-centred values, community resilience, improvisational competencies, and commitment to societal well-being. Using a positive deviance perspective, insights from effective nursing practices can inform nursing education and Arctic healthcare, improving patient care, job satisfaction, staff retention, and long-term cost efficiency.

articles.title: Low health literacy among individuals with chronic disease in Kalaallit Nunaat: a cross-sectional study with implications for health literacy responsiveness.
articles.abstract: Chronic diseases are an increasing public health challenge in Greenland (Kalaallit Nunaat), requiring self-management and navigation in healthcare information. Health Literacy (HL) refers to the ability to access, understand, and use health information. Low HL is prevalent in other Indigenous populations, negatively affecting self-care, health outcomes, mortality and contributing to social inequalities. Despite health inequalities in Kalaallit Nunaat, HL has not been quantitatively assessed. The aim was to investigate HL among individuals with chronic diseases in Kalaallit Nunaat and assess the HLS19-Q12 questionnaire in Greenlandic (Kalaallisut). This cross-sectional study (25 February - 2 April 2025) included participants (≥18 years) with diabetes, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, hypertension, obesity, and/or asthma. HL was assessed using the concise HLS19-Q12 questionnaire in Kalaallisut and Danish. Internal consistency and test-retest reliability were evaluated using Cronbach's alpha and intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). 230 individuals completed the questionnaire, including 28 retests. HL levels were categorised into four levels: inadequate 32.2%, problematic 50%, sufficient 12.4% and excellent 5.4%. The Kalaallisut HLS19-Q12 demonstrated acceptable internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha = 0.88; 95% CI: 0.78-0.93) and test-retest reliability (ICC = 0.86; 95% CI: 0.71-0.94). Overall, 82.2% of participants had inadequate or problematic HL, highlighting the need for interventions to strengthen HL responsiveness in Kalaallit Nunaat.

articles.title: Reducing period poverty through interventions, innovations, policies and multilevel barriers and facilitators: A systematic review.
articles.abstract: Period poverty is a persistent global inequity that undermines health, dignity, education and socioeconomic participation. Although increasingly recognised, evidence on effective responses remains fragmented. This systematic review synthesised menstrual health interventions, innovations and policies, and examined the multilevel barriers and facilitators across low- and middle-income and high-income countries. Following PRISMA 2020 and the SPIDER framework ProQuest Central, Scopus, MEDLINE and PsycINFO were searched for English-language studies from inception to 15 December 2024, identifying 8385 records. After screening, 49 studies were included, comprising interventions, other initiatives, innovations and policy analyses across school, community, workplace, humanitarian and policy contexts. Given substantial heterogeneity, a narrative synthesis was undertaken. Effective responses were multidimensional, combining product provision, menstrual education, stigma reduction and enabling infrastructure. Education improved menstrual literacy and confidence, while product-access strategies reduced absenteeism and social withdrawal in specific studies. Innovations including biodegradable and reusable products and community-managed pantries, expanded access but faced WASH constraints, stigma and cultural concerns about insertable products. Policy measures showed promise, but persistent funding and implementation gaps remained. Sustainable progress requires integrated, context-sensitive action combining education, product choice, infrastructure, stigma reduction and effective policy implementation.

articles.title: Pharmacy students' knowledge and attitudes regarding GLP-1 receptor agonist adverse effects in obesity management: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are important therapeutic options for obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Despite their increasing use, safety concerns remain, and pharmacy students' knowledge of their adverse effects is unclear. This study evaluated pharmacy students' knowledge and attitudes regarding GLP-1 RA adverse effects in obesity management. A cross-sectional questionnaire-based study was conducted among undergraduate Doctor of Pharmacy (Pharm.D.) students (1st-7th year) at Umm Al-Qura University, Saudi Arabia, between November and December 2025. A newly developed questionnaire, reviewed by two experts and pilot-tested among 10 students, assessed 17 knowledge and five attitude items covering indications, mechanisms, adverse effects, and clinical scenarios. Of 1,118 eligible students, 296 completed the survey (response rate: 26.5%). Descriptive statistics and multivariable regression analyses were performed using RStudio (version 2024.9.1.394). Among participants (63.9% male), the mean knowledge score was 7.6 ± 4.0/17. Most agreed that adverse effects significantly impact clinical use (59.4%) and supported further education on less common side effects (61.1%). Nausea was the most frequently recognized adverse effect (59.1%), whereas thyroid C-cell tumors observed in rodent studies (25.0%) and diabetic retinopathy complications (36.5%) were less commonly identified. Only 37.2% correctly recognized that hypoglycemia is uncommon with GLP-1 RA monotherapy. Higher knowledge scores were significantly associated with greater confidence in knowledge (OR = 1.11, 95% CI: 1.06-1.17; p < 0.001) and stronger endorsement of further education on less common side effects (OR = 1.11, 95% CI: 1.06-1.18; p < 0.001), whereas gender and academic year were not significant predictors of any attitude item. Pharmacy students demonstrated limited knowledge but generally positive attitudes regarding GLP-1 RA safety. These findings highlight the need to strengthen pharmacovigilance and evidence-based medication safety education within pharmacy curricula to improve clinical preparedness and patient counseling.

articles.title: Electrocardiograms and screening echocardiograms in young adults who acquired HIV perinatally and non-perinatally: a pilot study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lifelong exposure to HIV and antiretroviral therapy (ART) may elevate cardiovascular risk as individuals with perinatally acquired HIV transition into adulthood. We evaluated subclinical electrocardiographic (ECG) and echocardiographic abnormalities in this population.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted in Thailand between 2022-2023. Young adults who acquired HIV perinatally were enroled, alongside age-matched adults who acquired HIV non-perinatally. Participants underwent standard ECG and screening echocardiography.

RESULTS: A total of 62 participants (31 who acquired HIV perinatally and 31 non-perinatally) were included in the study. Of these, 31 (50.0%) were men, and the median (interquartile range; IQR) age was 25.4 (23.9-27.0) years. The median (IQR) CD4 + count was 595 (453-835) cells/mm3. Yong adults with perinatal HIV had longer HIV/ART exposure and greater historical use of zidovudine, stavudine, and protease inhibitors. Abnormal ECG findings were present in participants with perinatally acquired HIV and non-perinatally acquired HIV, including sinus bradycardia (16.1% vs. 12.9%), low-voltage QRS (12.9% vs. 3.2%), ST-T abnormalities (6.5% vs. 3.2%), and QTc prolongation (3.2% vs. 3.2%). Abnormal echocardiograms were observed, including hyperdynamic left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF > 70%) occurring in 9.7% vs. 0.0% (p = 0.238). In multivariable analysis, incomplete virologic suppression (viral load ≥ 200 copies/mL) was independently associated with low-voltage ECG (odds ratio 8.57; 95% confidence interval 1.16-63.30; p = 0.035).

CONCLUSIONS: Subclinical cardiac abnormalities were infrequent and comparable between young adults with perinatally and non-perinatally acquired HIV. Low-voltage ECG was associated with incomplete virologic suppression. Optimising antiretroviral regimens to maintain a suppressed viral load may help reduce subclinical cardiac abnormalities in young people with HIV.

articles.title: A helminth-microbiota metabolic relay promotes disease tolerance.
articles.abstract: Persistent infection by helminths requires limiting inflammatory damage despite incomplete pathogen clearance, yet how helminths mobilize resident microbiota to establish this state remains unclear. Here we identify a cross-kingdom metabolic relay through which Trichinella spiralis promotes systemic disease tolerance. Infection selectively expanded Ligilactobacillus murinus and redirected microbial tryptophan metabolism toward indole-3-lactic acid (ILA), a direct ligand of the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR). Antibiotic perturbation abrogated ILA production, AhR activation and Treg-Th17 remodeling, whereas transfer of helminth-conditioned fecal preparations or supplementation with L. murinus or ILA restored these responses. Pharmacological inhibition or genetic deletion of AhR eliminated the protection conferred by T. spiralis, L. murinus and ILA against endotoxin-induced lung injury. In lethal SARS-CoV-2 infection, oral ILA improved survival and limited pulmonary immunopathology without reducing viral burden, thereby uncoupling host protection from pathogen control. In a human COVID-19 cohort, ILA relative abundance remained inversely associated with IFN-γ after adjustment for available clinical covariates. These findings reveal that helminths can reprogram commensal metabolism to govern systemic immune tolerance and identify microbial ILA production as a tractable postbiotic strategy for limiting inflammatory tissue damage.

articles.title: The impact of prophylactic azithromycin on the developing preterm gut microbiome and resistome.
articles.abstract: Early-life antibiotic exposure can profoundly impact the developing preterm gut microbiome and resistome, with short- and long-term consequences for health. In a large multi-center (n = 28) study of 693 preterm infants, we investigated the effects of 10 d of prophylactic intravenous azithromycin on the gut microbiome and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). The AZithromycin ThErapy for Chronic Lung Disease of Prematurity (AZTEC) study was a double blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of preterm infants (born < 30 weeks of gestation), treated from birth for 10 d with either intravenous azithromycin or placebo, and sampled longitudinally for 21 d or discharge. Using 16S rRNA gene sequencing, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and quantitative PCR, we show azithromycin reduced microbial diversity and the relative abundance of health-associated Bifidobacterium and increased relative abundances of pathobionts Staphylococcus and Enterobacter/Klebsiella. This early azithromycin treatment increased the number of macrolide-resistant genes, including the presence of erm (C), which persisted for the duration of the study. Probiotic use (at individual unit discretion) increased alpha diversity and Bifidobacterium relative abundance, but did not fully mitigate the effects of azithromycin receipt. Combined azithromycin and probiotics further increased the enrichment of Enterobacter/Klebsiella and total ARGs, including erm(C). These findings highlight the impacts of antibiotic and probiotic use, both important in balancing infection control issues and microbiome disruption and antimicrobial resistance.

articles.title: Telehealth-related education and training: a systematic review of recent developments since the COVID-19 pandemic.
articles.abstract: The pandemic showed the potential of existing telehealth to increase healthcare access but also the need for healthcare workers to be competent and skilled in delivering care through this modality. We undertook a systematic literature review to identify telehealth-related courses developed since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic and summarised study characteristics, learning objectives, and course content. Articles describing telehealth-related training and education programs implemented between 2020 and 2024 were included. Papers were required to list specific program content or learning objectives for any educational level or type of health professional. Two authors independently extracted data. Quality of articles was assessed against the SQUIRE 2.0 guidelines. Quantitative data was summarised and reported using frequencies and percentages, learning objectives were mapped across the six Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC) telehealth competency domains, and qualitative categories were thematically synthesised. Of 7547 articles identified, 51 were included. Most courses were implemented in the USA (82%), mostly targeted to undergraduate students (51%), and the number of articles per year increased over time. Most courses were developed by universities (53%), sometimes in collaboration with health services, and content was primarily applicable across multiple specialties. Participants nearly always evaluated the courses (90%). Content included basic knowledge and skills in telehealth, patient safety, and ethics, with learning objectives often on technology and communication. Only four programs included all AAMC telehealth competencies. This review highlights that telehealth education and training has expanded since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, however, current curricula are lacking experiential learning. Courses generally covered telehealth communication competencies in detail, but more content on the ethical and legal requirements, billing, physical examination, patient education, and eligibility for telehealth is required. For efficient resource use, standardised training can be applied across disciplines with addition of site or speciality-specific modules.

articles.title: Stability and structure-preserving numerical analysis of a stochastic delayed pine wilt disease model.
articles.abstract: Pine wilt disease is a destructive forest disease involving pine trees, pinewood nematodes, and insect vectors. This study develops deterministic and stochastic delayed host-vector models to examine waiting periods and variability in transmission. For the deterministic system, positivity, boundedness, equilibria, and the basic reproduction number R0 are established. The disease-free equilibrium is locally and globally asymptotically stable when R0<1, while the endemic equilibrium is assessed through delay-dependent local stability. The stochastic model includes multiplicative environmental noise and is shown to possess positive solutions with bounded first moments. Exact Itô logarithmic identities demonstrate that long-term infection behaviour depends on current and delayed host-vector states. A delay-aware stochastic nonstandard finite difference scheme is constructed using delayed indices, nonstandard denominator functions, and positive stochastic exponential factors. Numerical experiments illustrate the effects of delay, noise, and step size, with the proposed scheme showing controlled behaviour at larger steps.

articles.title: Modulation of the gut microbiome and resistome by antibiotic use, but not by subsequent 2'-fucosyllactose intake, in adults with overweight or obesity.
articles.abstract: Antibiotics are widely used to treat bacterial infections, yet overuse and misuse causes disruption of the gut microbiome and spread of antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Presence of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) could be a determinant of the response to antibiotics. Supplementation with prebiotics may limit the detrimental antibiotic-induced effects on the microbiome, but whether this results in changes in the gut resistome is unclear. This study investigated the impact of eight-week 2'-fucosyllactose (2'-FL) supplementation after seven-day vancomycin use in 18 adults with overweight/obesity, a subset from a double-blind placebo-controlled randomized intervention. Whole-metagenome shotgun sequencing was used to characterize the gut microbiome and resistome at baseline, after vancomycin use and after supplementation. Seven-day vancomycin use disrupted microbial richness and diversity (p < 0.001) and changed microbial composition. No improvements in microbial recovery were detected after eight week 2'-FL supplementation compared to placebo. Resistome richness and diversity were not affected by vancomycin use, although the presence of specific ARGs changed. No differential impact of 2'-FL supplementation on resistome richness, diversity and composition was detected. While vancomycin use disrupted the gut microbiome and affected the resistome, the detectable effects of 2'-FL supplementation were limited. Future research should investigate antibiotic- and prebiotic-induced changes in the gut resistome in more detail.

articles.title: Effects on health and antioxidant status of oral supplementation of hazelnut skin extract in dairy calves with neonatal diarrhea: a randomized clinical trial in hospitalized patients.
articles.abstract: Neonatal calf diarrhea (NCD) is a major contributor to morbidity and mortality in calves. Growing concern about antimicrobial resistance has spurred interest in phytotherapeutic alternatives, particularly polyphenol-rich extracts. Hazelnut skin (HS), a by-product of the confectionery sector, is a sustainable and underutilized source of polyphenols; however, its therapeutic efficacy in calves with NCD remains insufficiently investigated. This randomized, parallel-group clinical trial evaluated the effects of oral HS extract supplementation as an adjunct to standard medical therapy in hospitalized dairy calves with NCD. Sixty female Holstein calves were randomly allocated to a control group (CTRL; n = 30) or a treatment group (HS; n = 30) receiving 10 g/day of HS extract with milk for 5 days. All calves received standardized clinical management, including fluid therapy and antimicrobial administration. Clinical parameters, milk intake, body weight, hospitalization outcomes, sepsis scores, and blood oxidative stress biomarkers were monitored. No significant differences were detected between groups for clinical recovery, fecal score, hydration status, milk intake, weight gain, hospitalization duration, mortality, or oxidative stress markers. Clinical improvement over time was evident in both groups and was attributable to standard therapy. In conclusion, short-term oral supplementation with HS extract did not confer additional clinical or antioxidant benefits when added to conventional treatment in calves with NCD.

articles.title: Effects of centrifugation-based therapeutic plasma exchange on coagulation parameters in dogs with canine visceral leishmaniasis.
articles.abstract: As in humans, therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) has been investigated in veterinary medicine for managing immune-mediated diseases such as canine visceral leishmaniasis (CVL). TPE may improve clinical outcomes by removing circulating immune complexes and excess antibodies; however, its physiological effects must be understood to ensure safety. Given the scarcity of studies in animals, this study evaluated the effects of centrifugation-based TPE in dogs with CVL receiving fresh frozen plasma (FFP) as replacement fluid. Thirty-one dogs with CVL that failed to respond to conventional therapy were allocated to two groups: clinical treatment alone (n = 18) and clinical treatment plus TPE (n = 13). The TPE group underwent one daily session for three consecutive days. Coagulation profiles were assessed before and after each session. A progressive decrease in platelet counts occurred across sessions, but without significant thrombocytopenia or critical alterations in activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) or prothrombin time (PT), which remained within reference ranges. Transient hypocalcemia occurred after the first session and was promptly corrected with calcium gluconate supplementation. Fibrinogen levels decreased mildly without clinical evidence of bleeding. Clinical complications were minimal and effectively managed. In conclusion, TPE was well tolerated, producing predominantly transient and controllable effects on hemostasis and overall clinical homeostasis under the conditions of this study.

articles.title: Load and breath-hold: impact of 7-day creatine monohydrate loading on breath-hold exercise performance - a double-blind randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Creatine supplementation enhances anaerobic energy availability and buffering capacity; however, its impact on muscle work under voluntary breath-hold (BH) remains unexplored. BH exercise increases reliance on anaerobic ATP production and creates a metabolic environment in which phosphocreatine-derived ATP may be particularly valuable. The aim of this study was to determine whether creatine monohydrate loading improves BH exercise performance in trained BH divers.

METHODS: A double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study assessed the effects of a 7-day creatine monohydrate loading protocol (20 g/day) on performance outcomes and fatigue markers during BH exercise performed on a bicycle ergometer in 20 trained BH divers (18 males, 2 females; mean age 41.6 ± 8.6 years). The trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT07233707) on 16th November 2025 under the title Load and Hold: Impact of 7-Day Creatine Monohydrate Loading on Breath-Hold Cycling Performance (BREATHE-C). Testing consisted of a brief warm-up followed by a maximal cycling trial performed on a single breath, during which participants aimed to cover the greatest possible distance. Following pre-supplementation testing, participants were randomly assigned to either the creatine monohydrate (CR) or the placebo (PL) group. Pre- and post-supplementation measurements included total work (TW), time to exhaustion (TTE), peripheral blood lactate accumulation (LA), mean partial pressure of carbon dioxide (pCO₂) in exhaled air following BH exercise, and ratings of perceived exertions for BH (RPE-BH) and muscle fatigue (RPE-MF). In addition, participants underwent dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry to assess changes in body composition.

RESULTS: Significant Time × Group interactions were observed for TW (p = 0.011), TTE (p = 0.028), and fat-free mass (p = 0.017), with greater changes observed following creatine supplementation compared to PL. Furthermore, there was a significant Time × Group interaction for LA (p = 0.003), with greater changes observed in the PL group compared to CR. No significant between-group differences were observed for pCO₂, RPE-BH, RPE-MF, fat mass, or total body mass.

CONCLUSIONS: Creatine enhanced performance, as reflected by increases in TW and TTE, without elevating RPE-BH, although a slight increase in RPE-MF was observed. LA was lower in the CR compared to PL group, despite greater performance improvements. Overall, creatine appears to enhance BH exercise performance in trained BH divers, suggesting a potentially effective ergogenic strategy for BH-related sports.

articles.title: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: epidemiology, pathophysiology, therapeutic strategies, and maternal-offspring outcomes.
articles.abstract: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) encompass chronic hypertension, gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, and preeclampsia superimposed on chronic hypertension, affecting about 5% to 10% of pregnancies worldwide and remaining a major cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality. Their burden is increasing with rising obesity, advanced maternal age, evolving diagnostic criteria, and marked socioeconomic and racial-ethnic disparities. This review summarises current evidence on the epidemiology, pathophysiology, biomarkers, clinical management, and long-term outcomes of HDP, highlighting recent advances and unresolved questions. Mechanistically, HDP is characterised by systemic endothelial dysfunction and angiogenic imbalance, particularly involving soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1), placental growth factor (PlGF), and soluble endoglin (sEng), together with immune maladaptation, oxidative stress, and genetic and environmental contributors such as endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) and sleep-disordered breathing (SDB). The sFlt-1/PlGF ratio is among the most validated tools for short-term risk assessment in suspected preeclampsia, while retinal microvascular imaging may provide a non-invasive marker of systemic microvascular dysfunction. Clinically, trial evidence supports treating mild chronic hypertension to below 140/90 mmHg to reduce adverse outcomes without compromising foetal growth. Long-term maternal cardiovascular and metabolic risks vary according to HDP phenotype, severity, gestational age at onset, and associated preterm delivery or foetal growth restriction, whereas offspring neurodevelopmental associations are largely observational and may be influenced by prematurity and shared familial or socioeconomic factors. Experimental strategies supported primarily by preclinical or early translational evidence include PPARγ agonists, placenta-targeted nanomedicine, and transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation. Machine learning combined with longitudinal multi-omics data may support precision risk stratification and individualised management.

articles.title: Inhibin B as a biomarker for ovarian reserve and ovarian response: systematic reviews and meta-analyses of diagnostic test accuracy.
articles.journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the diagnostic accuracy of inhibin B in evaluating ovarian reserve and ovarian response.

METHODS: We searched EMBASE, PubMed, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and the Cochrane Library up to July 2, 2025, for diagnostic test accuracy studies comparing inhibin B with anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH). The review followed the PRISMA-DTA and MOOSE guidelines. The risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2. Pooled sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative likelihood ratios, diagnostic odds ratio (DOR), and diagnostic score were estimated using bivariate random-effects models. Summary receiver operating characteristic (SROC) curves, a Fagan nomogram (pre-test probability = 0.5), and Deeks' funnel plot were used to evaluate performance and publication bias. Subgroup analyses compared inhibin B's accuracy between ovarian reserve and response.

RESULTS: Eight studies (12 datasets; 2878 women) were included, all at low risk of bias. For ovarian reserve, inhibin B showed sensitivity of 0.69, specificity of 0.88, DOR of 16.52, and an SROC AUC of 0.89; for ovarian response: sensitivity of 0.60, specificity of 0.79, DOR of 5.80, and AUC of 0.77. No significant publication bias was detected (P = 0.78 for ovarian reserve; P = 0.21 for ovarian response). The sensitivity was significantly higher for ovarian reserve than for the response (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Inhibin B has moderate diagnostic accuracy for the ovarian reserve and lower accuracy for the ovarian response. It may be considered a complementary biomarker, but AMH remains superior.

articles.title: Entrustable professional activities in medical education: strategies and results - a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medical education has been marked in the last decades by the introduction of Competence-Based Medical Education (CBME). Despite its clear objectives, CBME has faced significant challenges and Entrustable Professional Activities (EPAs) have been conceptualised as an answer to some of those challenges.

AIMS/PURPOSES: This systematic review aimed primarily to summarise the evidence published on the strategies used for the development, implementation, and assessment of EPAs and their results. Secondarily this review also aimed to characterise the body of evidence produced on EPAs, assess its quality, and explore its limitations and future research paths.

METHODS: Systematic searches were conducted in six electronic databases in July 2021 and updated in March 2025. The data extracted included the quality assessment of the studies considered using the Quality Assessment Tool for Studies with Diverse Designs (QATSDD).

RESULTS: Four hundred and seventy-eight studies were included for data extraction and posterior analysis, most of which referred to Postgraduate programmes (59.6%, n = 285) and took place in the USA (51.5%, n = 246). A relevant diversity of methodologies and stakeholders involved was detected in the development, implementation, and assessment of EPAs. References to factors influencing the implementation of EPAs (50.8%, n = 243) and the potential of implementing EPAs for the improvement of learning and assessment practices (46.4%, n = 222) were found in a significant number of studies, but only a small number focused on the cost-effectiveness of the use of EPAs. The quality analysis of the included studies revealed modest results.

CONCLUSIONS: This broad systematic review highlights the increasing adoption of EPAs, showcasing the diversity of contexts and strategies for the development, implementation, and assessment of EPAs. Nevertheless, significant challenges persist, namely concerning study quality, warranting further research.

articles.title: Faith-based organisations in providing HIV services within low- and middle-income countries (LMICs): a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To end the acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS) epidemic by 2030, the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS) proposes that 95% of people living with HIV should be diagnosed, 95% of those with a diagnosis should be on treatment, and 95% of those on treatment should achieve viral suppression. To attain these targets, UNAIDS estimates that community-based HIV services should increase from 5% to 30%. Within low-and-middle-income countries (LMICs), faith-based organisations (FBOs) often possess broad societal influence and extensive reach. Thus, many major AIDS organisations expect the collaboration between health and faith sectors to strengthen community-based HIV services. However, limited research has been conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of existing FBO-based interventions in delivering HIV services.

OBJECTIVE: To assess and evaluate the role of FBOs in the provision of HIV services within LMICs, and the associated barriers and challenges they may face.

METHODS: This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines. A literature search of EMBASE, PubMed, and MEDLINE for relevant English-language studies was conducted on 23rd October 2025. Studies were limited to empirical publications providing data on outcomes of HIV interventions by FBOs within LMICs. Data were extracted and all studies were assessed for quality and risk of bias using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (ROB 2) tool, Risk of Bias In Non-randomised Studies-of Interventions (ROBINS-I) tool, the appraisal tool for Cross-Sectional Studies (AXIS) tool and the CASP qualitative checklist.

RESULTS: Sixteen studies were included in this review, including seven qualitative studies, six quantitative studies, and three studies of mixed methods. All studies were conducted within sub-Saharan Africa. FBO interventions were primarily behavioural and fell into four categories: (1) congregation-based teaching, (2) education of religious leaders, (3) comprehensive home-based care (HBC), and (4) bespoke interventions using FBO structures. Key challenges facing FBOs in HIV service provision included insufficient resources, cultural issues (e.g. stigma, traditional healing) and concerns regarding barrier contraception.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite cultural and resource-based challenges, FBO interventions showed significant potential for expanding community-based HIV care within LMICs in sub-Saharan Africa. This review discusses several recommendations to strengthen FBO activities, encourage effective partnerships with FBOs, and ultimately lead to better HIV outcomes within LMICs. However, given the heterogeneity and quality of studies included, recommendations should be interpreted with caution.

articles.title: Association between Chinese visceral adiposity index and prevalent hypertension among older adults in rural China: A cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: Clinical and experimental hypertension (New York, N.Y. : 1993)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Chinese visceral adiposity index (CVAI) has been shown to be a practical indicator of visceral adiposity, but its association with prevalent hypertension in older adults remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association between CVAI and prevalent hypertension and to compare the discriminatory ability of CVAI with conventional obesity indicators among older adults in rural China.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 3,280 adults aged 65 years or older who were recruited in Baima Town, Taizhou, China, in 2025. Logistic regression models with progressive adjustment were used to evaluate the association between CVAI and prevalent hypertension. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was performed to assess the dose-response relationship. Subgroup and sensitivity analyzes were conducted to examine the robustness of the findings. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyzes were performed to compare the discriminatory ability of CVAI with body mass index (BMI) and waist circumference (WC).

RESULTS: Of the 3,280 participants, 2,692 (82.1%) had hypertension. Participants with hypertension had higher CVAI values than those without hypertension [108.35 (79.80-134.24) vs 86.34 (55.72-112.39), P < 0.001]. After full adjustment, each 10-unit and 1-standard deviation increase in CVAI was associated with higher odds of prevalent hypertension (OR = 1.143, 95% CI:1.114-1.173 and OR = 1.709, 95% CI:1.528-1.915, respectively; both P < 0.001). RCS analysis demonstrated a positive association between CVAI and prevalent hypertension, with no evidence of significant nonlinearity (P for nonlinearity = 0.153).

CONCLUSION: CVAI was independently associated with prevalent hypertension among older adults in rural China. CVAI may provide information for cardiometabolic risk assessment among older adults in rural China.

articles.title: Balancing individual risks and collective benefits: Effects of vaccine price, message framing, and value orientations on influenza vaccination in China.
articles.abstract: Vaccines are widely recognized as effective tools for preventing infectious diseases; however, vaccine hesitancy remains a persistent global challenge that undermines herd immunity and public health efforts. This study investigates how message framing and value orientation impact Chinese university students' willingness to receive the influenza vaccination at different price points, aiming to inform strategies for promoting health behaviors. A 2 (framing: gain, loss) ×2 (value orientation: individualism, collectivism) experimental design was employed with 1,408 Chinese university students to examine influences on vaccination intention. Vaccination intention decreased significantly as vaccine price increased. Compared with the control group, persuasive messages generally increased vaccination intention, and this effect became more pronounced in paid scenarios. When the vaccine was free, differences among message types were not significant. In paid scenarios, loss-framed messages were more persuasive than gain-framed messages, and individualistic-oriented messages were more effective than collectivistic-oriented messages. Among the four message combinations, the individualistic-loss message showed the strongest persuasive effect. Mediation analyses further indicated that perceived severity of influenza and perceived vaccine effectiveness mediated the effect of the individualistic-loss message on vaccination intention. Vaccination intention is influenced by the interaction between vaccine price and message attributes. Free vaccination reduces the relative impact of message variations, whereas paid scenarios provide more room for persuasive messages to operate. In price-sensitive contexts, individualistic-loss messages that emphasize personal infection risks and vaccine effectiveness may be particularly useful for promoting influenza vaccination.

articles.title: From gut colonization to recurrence: E. coli secretion systems at the host-microbiota interface.
articles.abstract: Escherichia coli occupies a unique position between commensal colonization and infection. It is a common member of the intestinal microbiota, yet selected pathogenic or opportunistic lineages can persist in mucosal niches, interact with resident microbial communities, and in some cases seed recurrent extraintestinal diseases. The mechanisms enabling long-term colonization, survival under host and antibiotic pressure, and relapse are diverse, depending on pathotype, infection site, host environment, and microbial community structure. Here, we critically examine how T3SS, T5SS, and T6SS may contribute to persistence-associated biology in specific E. coli contexts. T3SS primarily mediates epithelial interaction in enteric pathotypes, T5SS drives adhesion, biofilm formation, mucosal colonization, and immune modulation, and T6SS functions as a microbiota-facing mechanism of interbacterial competition. We distinguish experimentally demonstrated roles from speculative links to chronicity and recurrence, framing these systems as context-dependent interaction modules rather than a unified network, while highlighting evidence gaps relative to established persistence determinants.

articles.title: Synbiotic supplementation leads to gut microbiome communities with functional capacity linked to better brain white matter development in preterm infants.
articles.abstract: Preterm birth, a major cause of brain injury, is often linked to dysregulated gut microbiome development. This association underscores microbial metabolic function as a modifiable target to support neurodevelopment. In this secondary analysis of data derived from a randomized controlled trial (Trial Registration: ISRCTN96620855), we tested whether daily nutritional supplementation with Bifidobacterium breve M-16V, short- and long-chain oligosaccharides, and L-glutamine could steer the gut microbiome of very and extremely preterm infants toward communities that support brain maturation. The gut microbiome was profiled with longitudinal shotgun metagenomics at nine time points during the intervention, which started at 48-72 h after birth and continued until 36 weeks postmenstrual age. Additionally, MRI scans were conducted when infants reached term-equivalent age to evaluate brain maturation. Supplementation promoted the early establishment of Bifidobacterium-rich communities in the test group, with enhanced capacity for amino acid biosynthesis and pyruvate fermentation towards acetate and lactate production. Integration of microbiome data with brain developmental markers post hoc showed that the same functions were markedly reduced in infants with delayed white-matter myelination. By integrating microbiome functional capacity profiling and evaluation of brain maturation via MRI, this study demonstrated that early microbial modulation could influence brain development, positioning the preterm gut microbiome as a clinically actionable target.

articles.title: Effect of tangeretin supplements on simulated precompetition weight loss in female combat sports athletes.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Weight reduction before competition has long been a major challenge for combat-sports athletes. Unscientific weight-loss practices not only increase the risk of hormonal imbalance, electrolyte disturbance, and impaired immune function but also compromise athletic capacities such as aerobic and anaerobic performance and explosive power. This study investigated the potential benefits of tangeretin, a natural citrus extract, on athletic performance. These benefits include the regulation of hormone secretion, the optimization of carbohydrate and lipid metabolism, and the promotion of muscle synthesis and lipid utilization, which may help athletes reach their target weight.

OBJECTIVE: To examine the effects of tangeretin supplementation on body-composition and sports-performance indicators in female combat-sports athletes, and to evaluate its efficacy for simulated precompetition weight loss.

METHODS: Thirty female combat-sports athletes (4 wrestlers, 3 boxers, 9 sanda athletes, 3 judokas, and 11 taekwondo athletes) were recruited. A paired, randomized, double-blind design was used. All 30 participants were first paired according to sport and competitive level, then randomly allocated to either a tangeretin group or a placebo group (15 per group). The 30-day intervention comprised a double-blind nutritional supplement, a dietary questionnaire, blood sampling and analysis, body-composition assessment, isokinetic muscle-strength testing, and aerobic-capacity testing, to evaluate the effects of tangeretin (400 mg/day) on performance and health-related outcomes. These outcomes included body-composition indicators (e.g. body-fat percentage, fat mass, lean-body mass), fat-distribution indicators (e.g. limb and regional fat mass, gynoid fat mass), glucose and lipid-metabolism indicators (e.g. LDL-C, total cholesterol, free fatty acids), hormone indicators (e.g. cortisol, testosterone), muscle-strength indicators (e.g. peak torque of hip, knee, and ankle flexors and extensors), and maximal-oxygen-uptake-derived indicators (e.g. VO2max heart rate, time to exhaustion). Statistical significance was assessed using two-way repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA).

RESULTS: (1) Body weight: 80.0% of athletes in the tangeretin group lost weight to varying degrees, and 33.3% (5 athletes) reached their competition weight class. (2) Body fat: body-fat percentage in the tangeretin group decreased from 23.92 ± 0.87% to 22.92 ± 0.89%; trunk, upper-limb, lower-limb, and android-region fat mass decreased by 6.77%, 8.77%, 4.43%, and 8.09%, respectively. (3) Glucose and lipid metabolism: HDL-C increased by 8.86% (P = 0.002), whereas triglycerides decreased by 25.00% (P = 0.048). (4) Sports performance: peak torque during hip, knee, and ankle flexion and extension increased significantly in the tangeretin group. VO2max also improved from 42.80 ± 1.13 to 43.46 ± 1.32 ml/kg/min.

CONCLUSION: Tangeretin supplementation effectively reduced body weight and fat mass (both overall and regionally) in female combat-sports athletes. Among the participants, 80.0% lost weight to varying degrees, and 33.3% reached their competition weight class, indicating a strong effect on precompetition weight loss. Moreover, tangeretin improved aerobic capacity and lower-limb joint muscle strength, thereby enhancing competitive performance.

articles.title: Participant experiences of stopping ART as part of a clinical trial; findings from a qualitative study within the RIO trial in the United Kingdom.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Evaluation of the efficacy of immunotherapeutic strategies aimed at achieving durable antiretroviral treatment (ART)-free control within a clinical trial relies on analytical treatment interruptions (ATIs). ATIs involve stopping ART to assess post-intervention efficacy with frequent viral load monitoring. These trials rely on participant commitment but also involve uncertainty about the timing and experience of viral rebound, transmission risk, and impacts on personal and sexual relationships. Understanding participants' lived experiences is critical to participant involvement and retention and to designing ATI studies that are ethical, feasible, and acceptable.

METHODS: We conducted a qualitative study involving semi-structured interviews with 20 cisgender men living with HIV enroled in the phase 2 double-blinded randomised placebo-controlled RIO trial of HIV-specific broadly neutralising antibodies between January and May 2025 in the United Kingdom. We transcribed, coded and analysed the interviews using thematic analysis.

RESULTS: The participants described being motivated by scientific altruism but had worries about stopping ART. During the ATI, participants found breaking their daily pill-taking routine challenging, yet a majority described feelings of liberation thereafter. The participants preferred once weekly viral load testing, as it reassured safety, which was coupled with support from researchers, who buffered anxiety during periods of viral rebound. ATIs had a notable impact on personal relationships, including avoidance of dating, reduced intimacy and sexual pleasure while off ART. Easy access for partners without HIV to free PrEP, PEP, and condoms was welcomed by all participants. Restarting ART was difficult following the ATI, but was resolved with pre-trial preparation supporting adherence. The participants with lengthy ATIs remained enthusiastic but were challenged by uncertainty that required adjustment of their life plans. Finally, participants expressed mixed views regarding the use of placebo arms in trials but accepted a second ATI period after receiving broadly neutralising antibodies open-label.

CONCLUSIONS: Participants described being part of an ATI trial as both liberating and demanding. The findings indicate that acceptability is influenced by predictable, frequent weekly HIV viral load monitoring, timely results communication, and access to free prevention, with clear concerns about relationship impacts during viral rebound, and clearly communicated pre-defined ART restart criteria.

articles.title: Efficacy and mechanistic insights of dapagliflozin in hypertension management.
articles.journal: Clinical and experimental hypertension (New York, N.Y. : 1993)
articles.abstract: Hypertension remains one of the leading modifiable risk factors for cardiovascular disease and premature mortality worldwide. Blood pressure (BP) management is particularly challenging in patients with coexisting type 2 diabetes (T2D), chronic kidney disease (CKD), or heart failure (HF). Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have become an integral component of contemporary cardiorenal therapy and have consistently demonstrated additional BP-lowering effects across diverse clinical settings. This narrative review synthesizes the current clinical evidence regarding the antihypertensive effects of dapagliflozin and summarizes the biological mechanisms that may contribute to these effects, including osmotic diuresis and natriuresis, weight reduction, modulation of the sympathetic nervous system, enhanced uric acid excretion, and attenuation of oxidative stress, inflammation, and vascular dysfunction. Across clinical studies, reductions in systolic BP (SBP) generally exceed those in diastolic BP (DBP), although the physiological basis underlying this differential response remains incompletely understood. Dapagliflozin has demonstrated good tolerability and antihypertensive effects in clinical applications, its long-term use may be limited by the risk of genital infections. Collectively, the available evidence supports dapagliflozin as a cardiorenal therapeutic agent that may provide additional BP-lowering benefits in patients with hypertension and concomitant T2D, CKD, or HF, rather than as a substitute for conventional antihypertensive therapy. Future hypertension-focused clinical studies are warranted to further define its role in hypertension management.

articles.title: Population-level effects of a community-based program on intimate partner violence: A stepped-wedge trial in South African informal settlements.
articles.abstract: Intimate partner violence (IPV) remains a widespread challenge in informal settlements, where poverty and unemployment are prevalent. The evidence for strategies to reduce IPV at the population level in such settings is limited. A stepped-wedge cluster randomised trial was conducted in 18 informal settlements in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, to evaluate the Asibonisane Community Responses (CR) program. The program included a ten-session Stepping Stones curriculum and community-wide HIV and IPV education. Four survey rounds were implemented with population-based samples of men aged 18-35 and women aged 18-24. The analytic sample comprised 549 women and 438 men in primary partnerships interviewed at least twice. At baseline, 22.8% of women reported physical IPV, 11.4% sexual IPV, and 21.3% emotional IPV; among men, 15.9% reported physical perpetration, 3.8% sexual, and 9.2% emotional. Intention-to-treat analysis showed significant reductions among women in emotional (aOR = 0.42, p < .001), physical (aOR = 0.70, p < .05), and sexual IPV (aOR = 0.27, p < .001), with similar reductions in the number and frequency of violent acts. Men reported decreases in emotional and physical IPV perpetration, though not sexual IPV. The findings demonstrate that multi-session community programming can reduce IPV in high-prevalence contexts, and that detailed tracking of multiple IPV forms helps capture meaningful progress toward population-level violence reduction.

articles.title: Creatine supplementation in soccer players: a systematic review.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
AIM: Soccer places repeated demands on short-duration, high-intensity performance, including sprints, accelerations, jumps, and technical actions performed over the course of a match. Because these efforts depend heavily on rapid adenosine triphosphate (ATP) resynthesis, creatine is a plausible ergogenic aid for soccer players. However, findings in soccer-specific studies have been inconsistent, and previous reviews have addressed narrower questions using smaller evidence sets. This systematic review therefore examined the effects of creatine supplementation on performance, body composition, and recovery/fatigue-related outcomes in soccer players.

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to 15 May 2025 in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. We included controlled clinical trials of creatine supplementation in male or female soccer players of any age or competitive level when an eligible placebo, control, or comparison condition was available. Outcomes were grouped into performance, body composition, and recovery/fatigue domains. Domains from the revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomised trials (RoB 2) and the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomised Studies - of Interventions (ROBINS-I) tool were used to produce study-level methodological summaries rather than formal result-specific risk-of-bias assessments. Because the studies differed substantially in design, supplementation protocols, populations, and outcomes, findings were synthesised qualitatively rather than pooled in a meta-analysis.

RESULTS: Source-level verification left 45 eligible reports representing 41 unique studies: 28 randomised parallel-group studies, 2 randomised crossover/repeated-condition studies, and 11 non-randomised or allocation-unverifiable controlled studies. Some trials reported favourable findings for repeated-sprint performance, anaerobic power, and muscular strength, but the comparative evidence was inconsistent and the certainty of evidence was very low. Findings for vertical jump performance and technical skills were mixed, while change-of-direction and endurance outcomes showed no consistent benefit. Recovery- and fatigue-related findings were also largely null or inconsistent. Body mass often increased, particularly after loading protocols, whereas evidence for gains in lean mass was limited and inconsistent.

CONCLUSION: The soccer-specific evidence for creatine supplementation remains suggestive rather than conclusive. Favourable findings have been reported for some repeated-sprint, anaerobic-power, and strength outcomes, but the comparative evidence is heterogeneous, often limited by unclear or nonsignificant between-group effects, and of very low certainty. Firm conclusions about efficacy are therefore not possible. Body mass commonly increased, especially after loading protocols, while effects on lean mass, endurance, change-of-direction ability, and recovery/fatigue-related outcomes remain uncertain.

articles.title: Antimicrobial resistance and social inequity: Why the one health approach must centre poverty.
articles.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is one of the most consequential threats to global public health. In 2021, bacterial AMR was associated with an estimated 4.71 million deaths globally, including 1.14 million directly attributable to resistance. Yet, despite its designation as a global emergency, policy responses remain heavily focused on surveillance, antimicrobial stewardship, diagnostics, and pharmaceutical innovation. These interventions are necessary but insufficient without sustained action on the social and structural conditions shaping infection exposure, access to care, and antibiotic use. This commentary argues that the One Health framework, as currently operationalised, does not sufficiently centre poverty and structural inequality as core determinants of AMR.
