Associations of mean BP, BP variability, and randomized intensive vs standard BP lowering strategy with clinical outcomes were examined, with sex being evaluated as an effect modifier. The primary outcome was the 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS).

RESULTS: Among 816 patients (mean age 67.6 ± 12.0 years; 38% female), intensive BP management was associated with worse 90-day ordinal mRS outcome among male participants (adjusted common odds ratio [acOR] 1.91; 95% CI 1.29-2.83), whereas the corresponding estimate among female participants was closer to null (acOR 0.94; 95% CI 0.56-1.57; ratio of acORs 0.49; 95% CI 0.26-0.94). In separate postrandomization BP exposure models, each 5 mm Hg higher mean SBP was associated with worse 90-day mRS outcome among male participants (acOR 1.11; 95% CI 1.03-1.20), whereas no clear adverse association was observed among female participants (acOR 0.95; 95% CI 0.85-1.05; ratio of acORs 0.85; 95% CI 0.75-0.97). SBP variability showed weaker and less consistent sex differential associations. Findings across secondary outcomes were directionally similar but exploratory.

DISCUSSION: In this exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, randomized BP management strategy and early post-thrombectomy BP dynamics showed sex-stratified associations with outcomes. These associations may reflect biological sex and sex-related differences in baseline clinical and vascular characteristics. These findings are hypothesis generating and should be confirmed in prospectively designed studies before informing sex-specific BP management after EVT.

TRIAL REGISTRATION INFORMATION: ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04140110; the Registration Date, October 22, 2019.

articles.title: Right Brain: Climbing an Infinite Mountain.
articles.abstract: This is the story of the events that transpired after I found out I had matched into neurology in the United States. It is not a story of triumph over adversity, but rather an honest admission of vulnerability-of anxiety and fear experienced during this process. It is the story of a migrant in an unfamiliar place, but also of the uncertainty that everyone feels before starting residency. I draw on childhood memories of the majestic Andean mountains to reflect on the idea that the climb never ends-and that with every step, our perspective expands.

articles.title: Toward Personalized Sex-Informed Management of Blood Pressure After Stroke Thrombectomy Reperfusion.
Overlooked Writings of Sir William Gowers on Neurology in General Practice, Shorthand, and Education.
articles.abstract: Sir William Richard Gowers (1845-1915), long hailed as the "Father of Clinical Neurology," has been the subject of 2 biographies and many essays relating to his contributions to the study of nervous disorders. Yet, despite extensive bibliographies, several of his publications have hitherto escaped notice. We reviewed archival sources and digital repositories to identify overlooked works. This led to the discovery of his contributions to George Alexander Gibson's 1901 Text-Book of Medicine, which distilled neurology for the general practitioner, as well as lectures and articles on shorthand and education, reflecting his interest in communication, educational practice, and the process of learning. Gowers advocated cultivating ambidexterity in youth, reasoning that it may confer resilience against neurologic injury later in life. Recovered only through primary source research, these writings broaden our understanding of Gowers' intellectual range, showing him not only as a pioneering specialist in the study of nervous disorders but also as a physician engaged with general medicine and educational reform.

articles.title: Association of LATE-NC With Neuropathologic Lesions and Cognitive Abilities: A Population-Based Autopsy Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Limbic-predominant age-related TDP-43 encephalopathy neuropathologic change (LATE-NC) is a common finding in aging brains. However, most previous studies were limited to ethnoracially homogeneous cohorts from high-income countries. The objective of this study was to investigate the associations between LATE-NC, cognitive performance, and coexisting neuropathologic lesions in a large, ethnoracially and socioeconomically diverse sample from Brazil.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study analyzed data from the Biobank for Aging Studies, a Brazilian population-based autopsy study based at the University of São Paulo. The study included a consecutive series of autopsies performed between 2004 and 2024. Inclusion criteria required participants to be at least 18 years old with a knowledgeable informant. LATE-NC, Alzheimer disease neuropathologic change (ADNC), Lewy body pathology (LBP), lacunar infarcts, small vessel disease, cerebral amyloid angiopathy, and hippocampal sclerosis were assessed following international criteria. Cognitive abilities were evaluated with the Clinical Dementia Rating Scale Sum of Boxes (CDR-SOB). Logistic and linear regression models were applied to examine associations of LATE-NC with comorbid neuropathologies and cognitive outcomes, with adjustments for sociodemographic, clinical, and neuropathologic covariates.

RESULTS: The sample comprised 1,860 participants (mean age = 72.6 ± 14.2 years; 49.1% female; 62.2% White; 35.4% Black). LATE-NC was present in 7.4% of participants (stage 1: 3.0%; stage 2: 4.0%; stage 3: 0.4%). After adjustment for sociodemographic, clinical, and other neuropathologic covariates, LATE-NC (stages 2-3) was associated with hippocampal sclerosis (OR = 14.95; 95% CI 7.42-30.27; p < 0.001), advanced Braak NFT stages (OR = 2.23; 95% CI 1.32-3.83; p = 0.003), and LBP (OR = 1.89; 95% CI 1.02-3.37; p = 0.036). Factoring in other pathologies, LATE-NC was associated with the CDR-SOB score (β = 4.06; 95% CI 2.95-5.18; p < 0.001), demonstrating a consistent association with cognition, similar to the one observed for moderate/severe ADNC (β = 3.78; 95% CI 3.14-4.42; p < 0.001) in the same sample.

DISCUSSION: LATE-NC was prevalent and associated with cognitive impairment in this ethnoracially and socioeconomically diverse sample. The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and some estimates had wide confidence intervals due to the small number of advanced-stage cases.

articles.title: Impact of 2024 Revisions of Multiple Sclerosis Diagnostic Criteria in People With Radiologically Isolated Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The biological onset of multiple sclerosis (MS) precedes its clinical onset by years, as shown by MRI and CSF biomarkers. The 2024 revisions of the McDonald criteria extend, for the first time, MS diagnosis to selected cases of radiologically isolated syndrome (RIS), that is, to people with incidentally discovered CNS lesions suggestive of autoimmune inflammatory demyelination, in the absence of typical symptoms. The aim of this multicenter study was to assess the proportion of patients with RIS reclassified as MS, after applying the 2024 criteria.

METHODS: Adult participants (≥18 years) fulfilling the 2023 Lebrun-Frénay RIS criteria were selected from 22 Italian MS tertiary centers. Real-world, registry-based data were retrospectively collected at both baseline and follow-up. Reclassification followed 2024 criteria, allowing a MS diagnosis in RIS cases with ≥1 T2-hyperintense lesion in ≥2 typical MS regions (i.e., dissemination in space [DIS]), plus either MRI evidence of dissemination in time (DIT), CSF positivity, or central vein sign (CVS) positivity. Descriptive statistics were used.

RESULTS: Among 236 patients with RIS (mean age 38.9 ± 11.6 years; 70.3% female; median follow-up 3.0 years [interquartile range {IQR}: 1.1-6]), at baseline, 228 (96.6%) fulfilled DIS, 51 (21.6%) fulfilled radiologic DIT, and 152 of 201 individuals with available CSF data were CSF-positive (75.6%). CVS data were available for 5 of 236 individuals; none were CVS-positive. At baseline, the 2024 criteria resulted in a MS diagnosis in 159 of 236 patients with RIS (67.4%). Of 42 patients with RIS experiencing a clinical event during follow-up, 88.1% would have been reclassified as MS a median of 2 years earlier (IQR: 1.0-5.5). During follow-up, 18 of 236 additional participants (7.6%) met the diagnostic criteria through radiologic DIT.

DISCUSSION: The introduction of the 2024 criteria results in an earlier diagnosis of MS, before clinical manifestations of focal CNS damage, in most people formerly classified as RIS. Study limitations include incomplete kappa free light chain index data and nonstandardized MRI acquisition protocols; particularly, retrospective CVS assessment was negligible in this real-life context. Future studies including the full spectrum of asymptomatic individuals with MRI abnormalities and available paraclinical diagnostic tools are needed to better define the impact of 2024 revised criteria in this population.

articles.title: Pearls & Oy-sters: The Price of Patency: Intractable Headache Subsequent to Fourth Ventricular Recanalization.
articles.abstract: Fourth ventricular hemorrhage is a devastating subtype of hemorrhagic stroke that can be primary or secondary to subarachnoid hemorrhage. In both cases, inflammatory reactions triggered by blood in the subarachnoid space peak in the first week. This report describes a 61-year-old woman with a secondary fourth ventricular hemorrhage managed with IRRAflow active irrigation and drainage system, which expedited recanalization of the fourth ventricle and clearance of cisternal subarachnoid hemorrhage on days 3 and 5, respectively. However, the patient developed an intractable headache on day 7, despite normal imaging, intracranial pressure, and laboratory investigations. This case highlights caudal sac inflammation as a hidden culprit of unremitting headache after recanalization of the fourth ventricle despite normal investigations.

articles.title: Blocking two host receptors is better than one: Insights from RSV infection in human respiratory organoids.
Early fate bias and TCR sequence shape CD8+ T cell differentiation and expansion.
articles.abstract: When a naive CD8+ T cell encounters an antigen, it proliferates into descendants with identical T cell receptors (TCRs), termed clones. Whether their differentiation toward effector or memory fates is stochastic or TCR-dependent has remained unclear, largely because the vast diversity of TCRs makes individual clones difficult to trace over time. Using single-cell RNA and TCR sequencing in acute LCMV Armstrong infection, we found that clonal distributions in blood reflect those in lymphoid organs, enabling nonlethal longitudinal tracking of clonal evolution. Tracing hundreds of clones, we found that memory clonal distribution is surprisingly uncoupled from early dominance; instead, early central memory precursor frequency predicts memory dominance. Leveraging convergent recombination, we identified clones with identical CDR3 amino acid sequences in mice and found that these natural biological replicates were more likely than chance to adopt similar fates, although substantial clone-to-clone variation remained. Applying the TCR distance algorithm, we further identified dominant motifs associated with enhanced expansion and effector-biased transcriptional programs, extending the TCR's role in shaping clonal differentiation.

articles.title: A nematode-trapping fungus orchestrates polarity cues, septins, and NOX signaling for trap formation.
articles.abstract: Reprogramming cell morphogenesis in response to environmental cues is fundamental to microbial adaptation and survival. The nematode-trapping fungus (NTF) Arthrobotrys oligospora exemplifies this plasticity by developing adhesive traps to capture nematodes. However, mechanisms underlying trap morphogenesis and host invasion remain unclear. Using live-cell imaging, genetics, and functional assays, we show trap morphogenesis proceeds through localized redirection of hyphal growth followed by site-specific hyphal fusion, whereas infection development involves a transition from isotropic infection bulb expansion to multipolar invasive growth. These transitions are coordinated by the reorganization of conserved polarity proteins, asymmetric septin localization at the trap cell inner rim, and actin remodeling. Nematode-induced Nox1 signaling is required to recruit polarity and cytoskeletal machinery to the trap cell fusion site. Together, these findings establish NTF as a powerful model for understanding how conserved morphogenetic machinery drives the transition from linear hyphae to hyphal loops to trap nematodes.

articles.title: Senkyunolide a from danggui buxue decoction protects podocytes against diabetic nephropathy via the mir-223-3p/nlrp3 inflammasome axis.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Danggui Buxue Decoction (DBD), a classical Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formula comprising Astragalus membranaceus (Fisch.) Bunge (Astragali Radix) and Angelica sinensis (Oliv.) Diels (Angelicae Sinensis Radix) in a 5:1 ratio, has been traditionally used to treat "Xiaoke" (wasting-thirst syndrome) and is increasingly applied as an adjunctive therapy for diabetic nephropathy (DN). DN is a major microvascular complication of diabetes mellitus for which effective curative therapies remain limited. Although DBD has demonstrated promising clinical efficacy in the prevention and management of DN, its pharmacologically active constituents and underlying mechanisms of action have yet to be fully elucidated.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to comprehensively profile the blood-entering bioactive constituents of DBD, identify the core active compound through integrated UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS and network pharmacology analyses, and elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which the core constituent protects against high glucose-induced podocyte injury, with particular focus on the miR-223-3p/NLRP3 inflammasome axis.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS was employed to globally characterize the chemical constituents of Danggui Buxue Decoction (DBD), and the absorbed components and in vivo metabolites were identified in a DN rat model. Network pharmacology combined with target intersection analysis was used to identify the core active constituents. Subsequently, PPI network construction, GO functional annotation, and KEGG pathway enrichment analyses were performed to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. In a high glucose-induced MPC5 podocyte model, CCK-8, TUNEL, and JC-1 assays were conducted to evaluate the cytoprotective effects of the major active constituents. Furthermore, Western blotting, qRT-PCR, and dual-luciferase reporter assays were performed to clarify the regulatory mechanism of the miR-223-3p/NLRP3 axis.

RESULTS: UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS identified a total of 1584 chemical constituents in DBD, among which 249 absorbed components and 155 in vivo metabolites were detected in the plasma of DN model rats. Network pharmacology analysis identified senkyunolide A (SA) as the core active constituent, which targeted 33 NLRP3 inflammasome-related proteins, covering the entire activation cascade of this pathway. PPI network construction and enrichment analyses further revealed that SA-associated targets were involved in key biological processes at the systems level, including oxidative stress and PI3K-Akt/NF-κB signaling pathways. In vitro experiments demonstrated that SA at a concentration of 50 μmol/L significantly ameliorated high glucose-induced podocyte injury, apoptosis, and mitochondrial dysfunction. Mechanistically, SA upregulated miR-223-3p expression, thereby directly inhibiting NLRP3 inflammasome activation, which in turn suppressed Caspase-1 cleavage and GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis. Meanwhile, SA maintained mitochondrial dynamic homeostasis and energy metabolism by regulating DRP1 phosphorylation, upregulating OPA1 and MFN2, and activating the PGC-1α/MnSOD pathway, ultimately exerting multi-level protective effects on podocytes.

CONCLUSIONS: SA is identified as the core bioactive constituent of DBD responsible for its therapeutic effects in DN. SA exerts multi-level renoprotective effects by upregulating miR-223-3p, suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation and GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis, and maintaining mitochondrial dynamic homeostasis via the PGC-1α/MnSOD pathway. These findings provide a scientific basis for the rational application of DBD in the clinical prevention and treatment of diabetic nephropathy and highlight the miR-223-3p/NLRP3 axis as a promising therapeutic target.

articles.title: Saururus chinensis (Lour.) Baill.: A comprehensive review of botany, traditional uses, phytochemistry, pharmacology, quality control, pharmacokinetics, and toxicology.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Saururus chinensis (Lour.) Baill. is a traditional medicinal herb widely used in East Asia, with a long history of use in traditional Chinese medicine and traditional Korean medicine. It is traditionally used to clear heat, detoxify, promote diuresis, and reduce swelling, particularly for damp-heat-related disorders. Given its long-standing ethnomedicinal use, S. chinensis has considerable potential for further development.

AIM OF THE REVIEW: Although studies on S. chinensis have increased rapidly, no comprehensive systematic review dedicated to this species is available. This review summarizes its botany, traditional uses, phytochemistry, pharmacology, quality control, pharmacokinetics, and toxicity, with the aim of evaluating its therapeutic potential and identifying current research gaps.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Relevant literature is systematically retrieved from PubMed, Web of Science, CNKI, and other major databases. The collected studies are screened, organized, and comprehensively analyzed.

RESULTS: A total of 232 compounds have been identified from S. chinensis, with lignans as the predominant class of constituents. Available studies indicate that S. chinensis exhibits antitumor, anti-inflammatory, cardiovascular-protective, neuroprotective, multiorgan-protective, metabolic-regulatory, antioxidant, antimicrobial, skin-protective, anti-asthmatic, anti-allergic, and bone-protective activities. However, several issues remain, including unclear toxic mechanisms, the lack of a well-defined safe dosage range, insufficient understanding of synergistic effects, low bioavailability, and incomplete quality control.

CONCLUSIONS: S. chinensis shows considerable potential for further development. Future studies should address these issues to support the safe, effective, and standardized development and application of this medicinal plant.

articles.title: Qufeng xuanbi formula attenuates HDM-induced allergic asthma by targeting the STING/HIF-1α/glycolysis axis.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Qufeng Xuanbi Formula (QFXBF), a traditional Chinese medicine prescription used for asthma-like respiratory disorders, has shown anti-asthmatic activity. However, whether it attenuates allergic airway remodeling through innate immune-metabolic regulation remains unknown.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to determine whether QFXBF alleviates house dust mite (HDM)-induced allergic airway inflammation and remodeling through targeting the STING/HIF-1α/glycolysis axis, and to evaluate the specific inhibitory potential of its constituent tectorigenin on STING-mediated immunometabolic signaling.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: An HDM-induced allergic asthma model was established in male C57BL/6 mice by intranasal sensitization and challenge, followed by oral administration of QFXBF at 12.5, 25, and 50 g/kg/day or dexamethasone at 2 mg/kg/day. Airway hyperresponsiveness, lung histopathology, mucus secretion, collagen deposition, α-SMA expression, inflammatory mediators in BALF and serum, and glycolytic metabolic indices were evaluated. BSMCs were stimulated with IL-4 and LPS, both at 5 ng/mL, and treated with QFXBF at 2, 4, and 8 mg/mL. Cell proliferation, migration, glucose consumption, lactate production, RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence were performed to assess airway smooth muscle activation and metabolic reprogramming. Transcriptomic analysis of lung tissue, STING overexpression, HIF-1α pharmacological inhibition, LC-MS/MS-based identification of tectorigenin, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were further used to investigate the STING/HIF-1α/glycolysis axis and the potential STING-targeting activity of tectorigenin.

RESULTS: QFXBF markedly reduced airway hyperresponsiveness, inflammatory infiltration, and collagen deposition in HDM-challenged mice, accompanied by decreased asthma-related markers in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid and serum. QFXBF also downregulated STING, HIF-1α, and key glycolytic enzymes at both mRNA and protein levels in lung tissue. In IL-4+LPS-stimulated BSMCs, QFXBF dose-dependently suppressed proliferation and migration, reduced glucose utilization and lactate accumulation, and concurrently inhibited STING/HIF-1α and glycolysis-associated factors. Mechanistically, QFXBF attenuated HIF-1α activity and glycolytic flux through suppression of STING. Liquid chromatography-based analysis identified tectorigenin as a bioavailable constituent of QFXBF. In STING-overexpressing BSMCs, tectorigenin significantly reduced STING expression, proliferative activity, and lactate metabolism, supporting STING inhibition as a key pharmacological basis of QFXBF.

CONCLUSION: QFXBF can alleviate allergic remodeling by suppressing the STING/HIF-1α-mediated glycolytic program. Tectorigenin may act as a potential STING inhibitor that disrupts innate immune-metabolic signaling, providing mechanistic support for QFXBF-derived therapeutic strategies in asthma.

articles.title: Iridoids in medicinal herbs for the treatment of cardiovascular diseases: Ethnopharmacology, phytochemistry, and pharmacology.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain a major challenge to global public health. Although various pharmacological and surgical interventions are available, their long-term use may be limited by adverse effects and dependence risks. Therefore, the development of safer and more effective therapeutic agents remains an important goal. Iridoids, a class of bioactive constituents widely distributed in medicinal plants, have shown considerable promise in cardiovascular protection.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This review summarizes current evidence regarding the cardioprotective effects of iridoids, explores their underlying mechanisms, and evaluates their prospects for clinical translation, with the aim of providing guidance for future research.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Wanfang, and CNKI from January 2015 to December 2025. A Boolean-based search strategy was used to identify studies involving representative iridoids (e.g., geniposide, catalpol, and aucubin) and cardiovascular disorders, including atherosclerosis, myocardial infarction, and heart failure. Eligible experimental studies were analyzed to clarify their chemical characteristics, pharmacological activities, and associated signaling pathways.

RESULTS: Iridoids exert cardiovascular protective effects through multiple mechanisms, including anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, anti-endoplasmic reticulum stress, and anti-apoptotic activities. Collectively, the available evidence highlights their potential as multi-target therapeutic agents for cardiovascular disorders.

CONCLUSION: Iridoids represent promising candidates for cardiovascular therapy. However, successful clinical translation will require further advances in improving bioavailability, clarifying toxicological profiles, and generating high-quality clinical evidence to validate their efficacy and safety.

articles.title: Targeting CREB1 in cardiac diseases therapy.
articles.abstract: Cyclic AMP-responsive element-binding protein 1 (CREB1) family is integral to the regulation of gene expression in response to diverse cellular signals, functioning as both an activator and a repressor depending on the cellular contest. The activity of CREB1 is tightly regulated by phosphorylation, alternative splicing, and co-activator interactions, enabling it to integrate multiple signaling pathways and precisely control processes. In the cardiac diseases, CREB1 emerges as a critical regulator. Evidence indicates that CREB1 upregulation reduces cardiomyocyte apoptosis and enhances cardiac function post-infarction. At the same time, its downregulation is linked to impaired contractility and dilated cardiomyopathy, highlighting its role as both a protective factor in cardiac pathology. This review examines the central CREB1-related signaling cascades, such as the CREB1/the homeodomain-interacting protein kinase 3 (HIPK3)/microRNA-17-3p/the adenylate cyclase type 6 (ADCY6) and CREB1- the bone morphogenetic proteins 10 (BMP10)-Smad1/5/8 axes, delineating their upstream activators and downstream targets in cardiac disease. Collectively, these findings underscore the therapeutic potential of targeting CREB1 and its regulatory networks for the management of diverse cardiac conditions.

articles.title: A paper-based electrochemical aptasensor functionalized with silver nanoparticles for the detection of African swine fever virus p30 protein.
articles.abstract: African swine fever (ASF) is a devastating viral disease of domestic pigs and wild boars. The etiological agent, African swine fever virus (ASFV), continues to pose a serious threat to the global swine industry, causing profound economic losses in many countries. Therefore, early and reliable detection of ASFV is essential to curb its transmission and mitigate the economic damage it causes. In the present study, the ASFV protein p30, which is expressed within 2-4 h post-infection and endures throughout the viral replication cycle, was expressed and purified. An aptamer targeting the ASFV p30 protein was screened and validated, which was then used to fabricate an electrochemical paper-based analytical device (PAD) aptasensor. To enhance the aptasensor's conductivity, silver nanoparticles were embedded, and the aptamer was immobilized on the working electrode for ASFV p30 detection. Optimization included testing various protein concentrations and characterizing the resulting electrochemical perturbations using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). The optimized biosensor enabled sensitive detection of ASFV p30 at low concentrations, achieving a limit of detection (LOD) of 1.09 ng/mL. These findings demonstrate the high sensitivity of the developed aptasensor and highlight its potential as a rapid and reliable platform for ASFV p30 protein detection. Overall, the proposed aptasensor provides a promising technical foundation for the development of rapid, sensitive, and accessible diagnostic approaches for ASFV.

articles.title: Loss of core 1-derived O-glycans disrupts GLUT2 cell-surface localization and glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in pancreatic β cells.
articles.abstract: Protein glycosylation is a major post-translational modification that regulates protein function. Core 1-derived O-GalNAc glycans (Galβ1-3GalNAcα1-Ser/Thr) are widely distributed across tissues and are present on membrane-bound and secreted proteins. Their synthesis is catalyzed by core 1 β1,3-galactosyltransferase (C1galt1) and requires the molecular chaperone Cosmc, encoded by C1galt1c1. Although core 1-derived O-GalNAc glycans are abundant on mucin-type glycoproteins, their physiological functions on non-mucin proteins remain poorly understood. Here, we used β cell-specific Cosmc conditional knockout (RIP-Cos) mice to investigate the physiological role of these glycans in pancreatic β cells. RIP-Cos mice exhibited impaired glucose tolerance and defective glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS), despite normal pancreatic insulin content. Because glucose uptake through glucose transporter 2 (GLUT2) contributes to glucose sensing and GSIS in mouse β cells, we examined GLUT2 in RIP-Cos islets. Immunofluorescence analysis revealed an apparent reduction in GLUT2 signal at the plasma membrane. Slc2a2 (GLUT2) mRNA expression was significantly decreased, and immunoblotting revealed a lower molecular weight form of GLUT2. These alterations were accompanied by reduced glucose-analog uptake in primary RIP-Cos islets. RIP-Cos mice also displayed resistance to streptozotocin-induced diabetes. Finally, liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry identified O-GalNAc glycosylation sites within the extracellular domain of recombinant mouse GLUT2. These findings suggest that core 1-derived O-GalNAc glycosylation contributes to maintaining GLUT2 molecular properties and localization, thereby supporting β-cell GSIS. Overall, this study supports an important role for core 1-derived O-GalNAc glycosylation in β-cell glucose responsiveness and identifies GLUT2 as a target of O-GalNAc glycosylation.

articles.title: Identification of candidate host susceptibility genes for viral myocarditis through integrated transcriptomic and mendelian randomization analyses.
articles.abstract: This study investigated the genetic mechanisms underlying myocardial inflammatory responses related to Coxsackievirus B3 (CVB3) infection through an integrative transcriptomic and genetic approach. Gene expression profiles from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database were analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between CVB3-infected and control myocardial tissues. These genes were subsequently evaluated using Mendelian randomization (MR) based on publicly available expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) data and genome-wide association study (GWAS) data for myocarditis. MR analysis prioritized four candidate genes whose genetically predicted expression levels were significantly associated with myocarditis susceptibility. To ensure the robustness of these findings, multiple sensitivity analyses were performed to assess potential pleiotropy and heterogeneity. Functional analyses suggested that the priority candidate genes (PCGs) were associated with immune regulation, inflammatory signaling, and cellular metabolic processes. In addition, immune cell infiltration analysis suggested alterations in the myocardial immune microenvironment and associations between PCG expression and estimated immune cell proportions. An independent GEO dataset was used for external validation, and in vitro experiments further confirmed the significant upregulation of these genes following CVB3 infection. This integrative strategy combining transcriptomic profiling, human genetic analyses, and experimental validation identified four genetically prioritized candidate genes associated with myocarditis susceptibility and provided preliminary insights into the immune-regulatory mechanisms underlying cardiac inflammatory responses.

articles.title: GAN diet-induced MASLD is associated with compartment-dependent transcriptional alterations in orthotopic hepatocellular carcinoma and adjacent liver.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is an important risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet how it is associated with transcriptional changes across tumor and adjacent liver compartments remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated hepatic immune remodeling and orthotopic HCC growth in mice fed a high-fat, high-fructose, and high-cholesterol Gubra-Amylin NASH (GAN) diet, and performed paired transcriptomic analyses of tumor and adjacent liver tissues. GAN feeding induced hepatic steatosis and collagen deposition, accompanied by increased CD4+, CD8+, and F4/80+ cell densities, reduced CD20+ cell density, and increased apoptosis in cells isolated from liver tissues. In the orthotopic HCC model, GAN-fed mice developed larger tumors with increased Ki-67 and reduced cleaved caspase-3 positivity. Notably, CD20+ cell density increased in tumors but decreased in adjacent liver tissues, whereas CD4+, CD8+, and F4/80+ cell densities increased in both compartments. Paired RNA sequencing identified 29 shared differentially expressed genes between the tumor and adjacent liver comparisons, including 27 concordantly downregulated and two concordantly upregulated genes. These shared transcriptional changes were associated with lipid and glutathione metabolism. In contrast, pathway enrichment patterns differed between the two compartments, particularly in fatty acid β-oxidation, bile acid metabolism, complement activation, and antigen processing and presentation. Together, these findings link GAN diet-induced MASLD with enhanced orthotopic HCC growth and hepatic immune remodeling, while revealing shared metabolic transcriptional changes and compartment-dependent pathway enrichment patterns in tumor and adjacent liver tissues.

articles.title: Effectiveness and sustainability of neonatal resuscitation training programs in reducing neonatal mortality rates in low- and middle-income countries: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Globally, 75% of neonatal deaths occur in the first week of life. Despite a 52% reduction in the neonatal mortality rate (1990-2022), significant disparities persist in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). This systematic review synthesises evidence on the effectiveness and sustainability of neonatal resuscitation training programs in LMICs, with a focus on training programs, design, provider competency outcomes, and sustainability features. Systematic searches of five electronic databases (Embase, PubMed, MEDLINE (Ovid), Scopus, and CINAHL) were conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines to identify studies published between January 2020 and January 2025. Studies evaluating neonatal resuscitation training for healthcare providers in LMICs and reporting competency or mortality outcomes were eligible. Risk of bias and methodological quality were assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Fifty-two studies across 23 LMICs met the inclusion criteria. The majority demonstrated immediate improvements in provider knowledge and skills, although the magnitude and durability of effects varied across study designs and settings. Helping Babies Breathe was the most evaluated training program. Multi-component interventions incorporating training, mentorship, and quality improvement were associated with greater mortality reductions than training alone in narrative comparisons. Limited long-term follow-up constrains sustainability conclusions. Neonatal resuscitation training programs improve healthcare providers' competencies and, when implemented with system-level support, are associated with reduced mortality. Future research should incorporate validated sustainability assessment frameworks and extended follow-up to strengthen the evidence base for long-term program impact. This review was registered on PROSPERO (CRD42024623116). This review received no external funding.

articles.title: Child grant receipt and birth registration in Nepal: evidence from the 2022 Nepal Demographic and Health Survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In Nepal, a child grant program was introduced in 2009 to improve education and nutrition among disadvantaged children under the age of five while linking grant eligibility to birth registration as part of efforts to strengthen civil registration and vital statistics systems.

OBJECTIVE: This study examined whether child grant receipt was associated with birth registration.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of data from the 2022 Nepal Demographic and Health Survey. The outcome was whether a child's birth had ever been registered with civil authorities. The main explanatory variable was whether the child had ever received a child grant. Child age, sex, maternal education, ethnicity, household wealth quintile, and province were included as covariates in multivariable logistic regression models.

RESULTS: Among 5,064 included children, 72.8% had a reported registered birth. Registration was higher among children reported to have received a grant than among nonrecipients (93.6% versus 65.9%). Children reported to have received a grant had higher adjusted odds of registration than nonrecipients (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.75; 95% CI 5.14 to 8.85). Registration was 71.8% among children whose mothers had no education, 68.3% for grades 1 to 8, and 77.0% for education above grade 8.

CONCLUSIONS: Child grant receipt was strongly associated with reported birth registration. Links between social protection and birth registration should be accompanied by accessible registration services and support for families facing documentation barriers.

articles.title: Piezo1 in acute and critical illnesses: From mechanosensing to organ dysfunction (Review).
articles.abstract: Acute and critical illnesses are typically accompanied by hemodynamic instability, tissue edema, mechanical ventilation and extracellular matrix remodeling. Abnormal shear stress, mechanical stretch, pressure loading and tissue deformation continuously reshape the local mechanical microenvironment. Piezo1 is a mechanosensitive cation channel that converts mechanical stimuli into intracellular signals dominated by Ca²+ influx and contributes to vascular homeostasis, immune regulation and tissue repair. In sepsis‑associated intestinal epithelial injury, pulmonary endothelial mechanical loading and infection‑related immune responses, Piezo1‑associated Ca²+ signaling has been implicated in intestinal barrier injury, mitochondrial stress and apoptosis, endothelial barrier disruption or protection, and enhanced host defense. The direction of its effects depends on the cell and experimental context and cannot be determined solely by the intensity or duration of activation. The present review summarizes the fundamental mechanisms of Piezo1‑mediated mechanosensing and mechanotransduction in sepsis, acute respiratory distress syndrome, acute kidney injury and trauma/hemorrhagic shock. It also discusses the therapeutic potential and translational challenges of targeting Piezo1. Mechanical alterations in acute and critical illnesses may influence cellular processes, including inflammatory regulation, endothelial barrier function, mitochondrial stress and cell injury, through Piezo1‑associated signaling. However, direct evidence and the direction of effects vary between diseases, and shared mechanisms across organs remain to be validated. Defining the cell‑specific and stimulus‑ and disease stage‑dependent effects of Piezo1 may deepen understanding of organ dysfunction in acute and critical illness and provide a basis for research into interventions targeting mechanical signaling.

articles.title: Discernible phenotypic alterations following linc-10 knockout in Caenorhabditis elegans.
articles.abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) are regulatory molecules that play vital roles in various cellular processes. Although the loss of function of most annotated lncRNAs in several model organisms does not result in severe phenotypes, suggesting they are not essential for survival or reproduction, lncRNAs may still act as responsive elements under diverse physiological and pathological conditions. In this study, we investigated the role of the linc-10 gene in Caenorhabditis elegans and found that its deletion is associated with altered gene expression and impaired reproductive fitness. Knockout (KO) mutants of linc-10 exhibited mild but notable abnormalities, including reduced brood size, altered developmental trajectories, and increased sensitivity to stress, along with occasional sterility and a slightly elevated male ratio. We characterized the expression patterns of linc-10 across developmental stages and performed high-throughput sequencing to detect differentially expressed genes (DEGs) following linc-10 deletion. We found that several immune-related genes were dysregulated. Notably, linc-10 mutants showed increased susceptibility to Pseudomonas aeruginosa PA14 infection and other stressors. Small RNA sequencing further revealed alterations in piRNA and miRNA profiles after linc-10 deletion. Importantly, CRISPR/Cas9-mediated insertion of a Plinc-10::linc-10 rescue transgene into a neutral intergenic site partially rescued the reduced brood size and stress-sensitive phenotypes of linc-10 mutants, supporting the functional relevance of the linc-10 transcript. Together, these findings suggest that linc-10 contributes to reproductive fitness, immune homeostasis, and stress resilience in C. elegans.

articles.title: Serum Calprotectin Demonstrates Moderate Diagnostic Performance for Detecting Periprosthetic Joint Infection in Hip and Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a serious complication after total hip and knee arthroplasty, with limited accuracy of conventional biomarkers. This study assessed serum calprotectin (CP) alongside established markers in revision arthroplasty.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 399 patients (232 total knee arthroplasty, 167 total hip arthroplasty). Based on Musculoskeletal Infection Society 2018 criteria, 132 patients were diagnosed with PJI and 267 were classified as non-PJI. All patients underwent serum CP, C-reactive protein (CRP), and interleukin-6 (IL-6) testing; microbiological analyses were performed when indicated.

RESULTS: Serum CP was significantly higher in PJI than aseptic revisions (median 11,700 ng/mL [interquartile range 8080-18,675] vs 5,440 ng/mL [interquartile range 3600-8300], P < .001). The optimal CP threshold for PJI was 8,330 ng/mL (area under the curve = 0.790, 95% CI, 0.741-0.838), providing a sensitivity of 65.2% (95% CI, 56.7-72.7%) and a specificity of 79.8% (95% CI, 74.6-84.2%). CRP and (IL)-6 showed higher diagnostic performance, with sensitivities of 69.0% (95% CI, 60.6-76.2%) and 73.6% (95% CI, 65.4-80.5%) and specificities of 88.4% (95% CI, 83.9-91.6%) and 85.0% (95% CI, 80.2-88.8%). Serum CP levels were not significantly influenced by joint type, sex, or age. In 8 patients with PJI, serum CP was above the cohort-derived threshold while both CRP and IL-6 remained below their respective thresholds. Conversely, in 10 cases, serum CP remained below the threshold despite elevated CRP and IL-6.

CONCLUSIONS: Serum calprotectin demonstrated moderate diagnostic performance and may may complement conventional serum markers in selected cases in which conventional serum markers are inconclusive.

articles.title: Utilization of a Lifestyle Medicine Program for Presurgical Health Optimization: Impact on Early Postoperative Outcomes of Hip and Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic systemic inflammation is associated with osteoarthritis and chronic diseases that increase surgical risk before total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA). This study compares early postoperative outcomes between patients who did and did not complete an intensive lifestyle medicine (LSM) program to reduce chronic systemic inflammation.

METHODS: Anthropometric variables, lifestyle measures, patient-reported outcome measures, and postoperative 90-day outcomes (ie, length of stay, infection, persistent pain, opioids) were obtained from an LSM repository. Comparisons were made between patients who completed the intensive LSM track (multiple visits, interprofessional providers) and those who declined behavior change preoperatively (selective track: single provider visit). A subanalysis evaluated glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) medication users.

RESULTS: Among 292 patients (72% women; 62 ± 9 years; 76% White), 154 completed the intensive track and 138 participated in the selective track. Most (91%) had ≥2 chronic diseases. Baseline characteristics were similar between tracks, except for higher anxiety/depression scores in the intensive track (3.3 ± 3.0 vs 1.8 ± 2.4[P < .001]). Postoperatively, the selective track reported significantly higher persistent pain rates (26% vs 10%[P < .001]) than the intensive track. GLP-1RA users were more likely to refill outpatient opioids than nonusers (57% vs 36%[P = .001]), with no differences in other outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative persistent pain rates were significantly lower in patients who completed an intensive LSM program before THA or TKA, compared to patients who did not engage in health improvement. GLP-1RA users showed no health benefits and required more opioid refills.

articles.title: Evaluation of serological changes of ESR, CRP, IL-6 and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-a) and hematologic parameters in pet dogs with pyometra.
articles.abstract: Canine pyometra is associated with systemic inflammation, but erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) has been less extensively evaluated alongside cytokines, C-reactive protein (CRP), and routine hematologic variables. This case-control study compared inflammatory and hematologic measurements in 15 dogs with closed pyometra and 15 clinically healthy controls. Interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), CRP, ESR, white blood cell (WBC) count, packed cell volume (PCV), and serum creatinine were assessed. Group differences were analyzed using independent-samples t-tests, with Welch correction when variance heterogeneity was detected. Mean differences were reported with 95% confidence intervals and Hedges' g effect sizes. Dogs with closed pyometra had higher IL-6, TNF-α, CRP, ESR, and WBC counts and lower PCV and serum creatinine than controls (all p ≤ 0.005). The largest standardized differences were observed for ESR (g = 2.39), PCV (g = -2.29), and serum creatinine (g = -1.94). Within the pyometra group, IL-6, TNF-α, and CRP were strongly correlated (r = 0.974-0.978; p < 0.001). These findings demonstrate a pronounced systemic inflammatory and hematologic phenotype in closed canine pyometra and identify ESR as a potentially informative component of multimarker inflammatory assessment. Prospective studies incorporating longitudinal measurements and clinical outcomes are required to determine diagnostic or prognostic utility.

articles.title: Spontaneous complete regression of a cervical macrocystic lymphatic malformation following infection in an infant: A case report.
articles.abstract: Lymphatic malformations most frequently involve the head and neck region, accounting for nearly two-thirds of all reported cases, and are often diagnosed in infancy or early childhood. Approximately half of the lesions are present at birth, while up to 90% become clinically evident before the age of two years. Clinically, these lesions typically present as soft, painless, compressible masses that may progressively enlarge and occasionally cause functional complications such as airway compression, dysphagia, or cosmetic deformity. Although lymphatic malformations are histologically benign, their clinical course can be unpredictable. Episodes of infection, hemorrhage, or sudden enlargement may occur and can significantly modify the presentation of the lesion. Imaging modalities such as ultrasonography, computed tomography, and magnetic resonance imaging are commonly used to confirm the diagnosis and evaluate the extent of the lesion and its relationship with adjacent structures. Management strategies include surgical excision, sclerotherapy with various agents such as bleomycin or OK-432, or a combination of both approaches depending on lesion size and location. Nevertheless, spontaneous regression of lymphatic malformations has occasionally been described in the literature and appears to occur in a small proportion of patients. In some cases, inflammatory or infectious episodes may induce endothelial damage and fibrosis of the cystic spaces, leading to a reduction in lesion size or even complete resolution. Herein, we report the case of a large congenital cervical macrocystic lymphatic malformation in an infant that underwent complete regression following a superinfection treated with antibiotic therapy alone.

articles.title: Evaluating a large language model-powered system for semi-structured interview in health research.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Conducting qualitative health research with marginalized populations presents persistent challenges related to trust, disclosure, and resource constraints. Traditional in-person interviews can be costly and difficult to scale, while participants may hesitate to share sensitive experiences openly. This study assessed the feasibility and acceptability of a large language model (LLM)-powered conversational interview system as an alternative to semi-structured qualitative interviews with marginalized populations in a community-engaged health research context.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We developed a web-based, LLM-powered interview system informed by a community-based participatory research framework. The system was tested with 28 caregivers of children with asthma living in subsidized housing. Postinterview evaluation sessions and researcher observation notes were analyzed to assess the system's feasibility and acceptability and identify usability, accessibility, technical, and implementation considerations.

RESULTS: Participants reported that the system was easy to use and appreciated its empathetic and nonjudgmental tone. They also rated the system positively for clarity, comfort, and accessibility, indicating that conversational artificial intelligence (AI) systems can be adapted to support qualitative data collection in underserved communities. Identified challenges included intermittent technical errors, limited contextual adaptability, and variations in participants' comfort with digital technology.

DISCUSSION: Large language model-powered conversational interview systems, when guided by community engagement, ethical design principles, and human support, offer a feasible and acceptable approach to qualitative health research with underserved populations. Hybrid human-AI models may offer a scalable yet inclusive pathway for expanding participation and advancing health equity in qualitative research.

CONCLUSION: These findings support further development and evaluation of LLM-powered interview systems for community-engaged qualitative research. Ongoing technical improvement, ethical safeguards, and participatory design will be critical to ensuring these systems are used responsibly and effectively to advance health equity.

articles.title: Shock Synopsis December 2026.
Comparison of Ultrasound Attenuation Imaging and Conventional Ultrasonography Detection Rates for Hepatosteatosis in Obese Children.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of ultrasound attenuation imaging (USAT) in detecting and grading hepatosteatosis in obese pediatric patients, and to compare its findings with conventional B-mode ultrasonography and relevant laboratory parameters.

METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study enrolled 95 obese or morbidly obese children aged 8 to 18 years who presented to a pediatric endocrinology clinic with a preliminary diagnosis of hepatosteatosis. All patients underwent both B-mode ultrasonography and USAT using the Mindray Resona9 device. Hepatosteatosis was graded using device-specific attenuation cutoff values for USAT and standard echogenicity-based criteria for B-mode ultrasonography. Laboratory parameters, including alanine aminotransferase (ALT), triglycerides (TG), and homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), were recorded for each patient.

RESULTS: USAT identified hepatosteatosis in 70 of 95 patients (73.7%), whereas B-mode ultrasonography detected steatosis in only 36 of 95 (37.9%). Among the 59 patients classified as steatosis-free by B-mode ultrasonography, USAT identified steatosis in 36 (61%; P<0.001). Interobserver agreement was excellent for USAT (ICC=0.939; 95% CI: 0.903-0.962) and substantial for B-mode ultrasonography (weighted kappa=0.793). Patients who were USAT-positive but B-mode-negative demonstrated significantly higher ALT and HOMA-IR values, as well as a greater prevalence of hepatomegaly (P<0.05 for all).

CONCLUSIONS: USAT is capable of detecting low-grade hepatic steatosis in obese children more effectively than conventional B-mode ultrasonography and shows significant correlations with key metabolic laboratory parameters. Given its objectivity, excellent reproducibility, and practical ease of use, routine incorporation of USAT alongside B-mode ultrasonography is warranted in the evaluation of hepatic steatosis in the pediatric population.

articles.title: PEth as a marker of alcohol consumption in relation to arterial cardiovascular risk factors.
articles.journal: Scandinavian journal of primary health care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alcohol has well-known detrimental effects on health. Phosphatidyl ethanol 16:0/18:1 (PEth) is a highly sensitive biomarker of alcohol consumption used in primary healthcare. The relationship between PEth concentrations and cardiovascular risk factors remains unclear. Our hypothesis was that high PEth concentrations would be associated with an unfavourable cardiovascular risk factor profile. This study aimed to investigate the associations between PEth concentrations and arterial cardiovascular risk factors.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study was based on data from the Västerbotten Intervention Programme and included 2820 individuals. Health examinations were conducted, including questionnaires collecting data on cardiovascular risk factors. PEth concentrations were analysed in packed erythrocytes from blood samples collected between 1985 and 2014 and stored at -80 °C until analysis. Participants were categorised into four groups. Logistic regression analysis was used to calculate odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the association between PEth concentrations and arterial cardiovascular risk factors.

RESULTS: The median age of participants was 50.2 years, and the median BMI was 25.9. High PEth concentrations (>0.30 μmol/L) were observed in 8.9% of participants and were associated with hypertension (OR 1.58 [95% CI 1.14-2.18]), diabetes (OR 1.89 [95% CI 1.08-3.28]), male sex (OR 2.58 [95% CI 1.90-3.50]), ever smoking (OR 5.31 [95% CI 3.75-7.52]) and lower education level (OR 2.06 [95% CI 1.32-3.22]) compared with PEth <0.01 μmol/L.

CONCLUSIONS: High PEth concentrations were associated with established risk factors for arterial cardiovascular disease. These findings should encourage a broader clinical focus when managing patients with elevated PEth concentrations.

articles.title: Dynamic prediction of early antibiotic treatment failure in ischemic stroke-associated pneumonia: development and internal validation of a 48-h landmark model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Existing stroke-associated pneumonia scores estimate pneumonia occurrence rather than early response after antibiotics have started. We aimed to develop and internally validate a baseline model and a 48-h landmark model for first antibiotic treatment failure between 48 and 72 h after treatment initiation.

METHODS: This single-center, retrospective cohort study included consecutive adults with acute ischemic stroke-associated pneumonia treated with empirical systemic antibiotics from December 1, 2021 to December 1, 2025. All included patients were event-free at completion of the 48-h landmark assessment. The primary outcome was first treatment failure by the nominal 72-h reassessment, comprising efficacy-driven antibiotic escalation, persistent clinical instability with evidence of uncontrolled pneumonia, or pneumonia-related death. Ridge logistic regression with a fixed inverse penalty strength (C = 1.0) was used, and 500 bootstrap resamples estimated optimism-corrected performance.

RESULTS: Among 199 patients, 102 (51.3%) experienced treatment failure. At baseline, mechanical ventilation before antibiotic initiation and a higher platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio were associated with failure. In the 48-h model, each 20 mg/L increase in C-reactive protein change was associated with greater failure odds (adjusted odds ratio 1.89, 95% confidence interval 1.52-2.34), as were each five-unit increase in neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio change (1.98, 1.25-3.13) and escalation of oxygen support (4.56, 1.09-19.01). The optimism-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve increased from 0.697 at baseline to 0.889 at 48 h. Treatment failure was associated with longer hospitalization, higher hospital cost, and longer antibiotic exposure.

CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center retrospective study, a structured 48-h reassessment combining routinely available inflammatory trajectories and oxygen-support change improved short-horizon prediction of antibiotic treatment failure. The model should prompt clinical review rather than automatic antibiotic escalation; multicenter external validation and prospective impact evaluation are required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Single Center, Single-Group Trial to Evaluate the Safety and Feasibility of 50 Hz Stimulation to Enhance Stroke Recovery of Upper Limb Function: The Motor Recovery Through Plasticity-Inducing Cortical Stimulation Open-Loop Protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: A previous study (the Everest trial) of epidural cortical stimulation showed improved rehabilitation outcomes in a subset of those with poststroke related disability as long as (1) the individual had a degree of surviving corticospinal tracts and (2) an electrode that when delivering stimulation could evoke a motor response. The goal of this study is to examine the safety and feasibility of new sense-and-stim capable implantable devices with configurable electrode arrays, using subdural stimulation, to improve stroke rehabilitation and associated motor functional outcomes.

METHODS: We will implant 4 patients who have chronic upper limb impairment after stroke to (1) demonstrate the safe usage of a cortical sensing-enabled stimulation system in a stroke rehabilitation protocol and (2) evaluate the system's capability to deliver activity-triggered stimulation for future clinical studies using neuroplasticity-inducing stimulation to enhance stroke rehabilitation outcomes. Each participant will receive 50 Hz stimulation delivered through the cortical, subdural, electrodes during clinical rehabilitation visits for 2 hours a day, 5 days a week, for 6 weeks. Devices are explanted approximately 9 months after implant.

EXPECTED OUTCOMES: We anticipate that the surgical implantation of the cortical stimulation device and use of the device to deliver stimulation to enhance rehabilitation outcomes will succeed without identifying unanticipated safety concerns or encountering unexpected adverse events.

DISCUSSION: Although the generalizability of the results will be limited based on the small number of study participants, it is nonetheless a crucial research milestone for reestablishing cortical stimulation as a potential method for enhancing poststroke rehabilitation.

articles.title: Ruptured pheochromocytoma during preoperative doxazosin treatment.
articles.abstract: Rupture of pheochromocytoma is rare but represents a life-threatening complication. A 43-year-old man with episodic hypertension, palpitations, and chest discomfort was incidentally found, during a computed tomography (CT) aortogram performed to rule out aortic dissection, to have a 5.2-cm right adrenal mass suspicious for pheochromocytoma. Biochemical testing confirmed catecholamine excess. He was started on oral doxazosin 1 mg daily, which was titrated to 2 mg daily after 1 week, followed by oral bisoprolol 2.5 mg daily in preparation for surgery. Five weeks later, he presented with severe right-sided abdominal pain and a blood pressure of 215/111 mmHg. Abdominal CT angiography showed interval enlargement of the adrenal mass with posterior rupture and a retroperitoneal hematoma without active bleeding. He was stabilized with conservative management and subsequently underwent robotic right adrenalectomy. Histopathology confirmed pheochromocytoma with necrosis, without angioinvasion or lymphatic invasion, and with negative margins. Pheochromocytoma rupture can occur despite appropriate α-blockade, and spontaneous hemorrhage remains the most likely proposed mechanism, although α-blockade may be a contributing factor in selected cases.

articles.title: A rare presentation of probable catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome with bilateral adrenal hemorrhage.
articles.abstract: Catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), a rare thrombotic manifestation of APS, is associated with high mortality. Rarely, it can present with bilateral adrenal hemorrhage (BAH). This case highlights a rare presentation of BAH due to probable catastrophic APS secondary to systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). A 57-year-old female with diabetes presented with hypovolemic shock, abdominal pain, and vomiting. Imaging revealed BAH; antiphospholipid antibodies were present in high titers in the blood. Antinuclear antibody and antidouble-stranded deoxyribonucleic acid antibody (anti-dsDNA) were positive in high titers. Catastrophic APS secondary to SLE was diagnosed. Serum morning cortisol was at 9.2 μg/dL (SI: 254 nmol/L) (reference range: 5-25 μg/dL [SI: 138-635 nmol/L]), and adrenocorticotropic hormone was at 180 pg/mL (SI: 39.6 pmol/L) (reference range: 10-60 pg/mL [SI: 1.6-13.9 pmol/L]); which indicated evolving primary adrenal insufficiency. The patient received pulse methylprednisolone, intravenous immunoglobulin, anticoagulants, and mycophenolate mofetil. Oral glucocorticoid was continued with regular monitoring of adrenal function. Mineralocorticoid replacement was not needed as the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system axis was intact. This report contributes to the sparse literature on catastrophic APS-related BAH, highlighting the need for early diagnosis and combined immunosuppressive and anticoagulant treatment.

articles.title: Next-generation microneedle platforms for transdermal therapeutics: a comprehensive review of innovations and challenges.
articles.abstract: Microneedle patches (MNPs) are becoming promising new opportunities to replace traditional methods of drug delivery like oral, topical, and injectable routes, due to their minimally invasive nature and their potential to deliver drugs transdermally. Compared to oral formulations, MNPs bypass gastrointestinal degradation and hepatic first-pass metabolism, thereby enhancing systemic bioavailability and therapeutic effects. These systems use micron-sized solid or hollow needles that can penetrate the stratum corneum, the major barrier to cutaneous penetration. MNPs can be used to deliver therapeutic agents directly to the viable epidermis and systemic circulation by forming transient microchannels in the skin. Recent developments in the field of engineering, such as 3D printing technologies, dissolving and hydrogel-forming polymers, and smart stimuli-responsive systems, have greatly broadened the therapeutic applications of the microneedle platform beyond passive drug diffusion. These technologies enable regulated, programmed, and feedback-controlled drug delivery, making MNPs the future of transdermal delivery for vaccines, biologics, metabolic disease, oncology, and precision medicine. This review critically and comparatively analyzes the strategies of microneedle design, fabrication techniques, drug-loading approaches, and clinical uses. Special attention is given to the barriers to translation, such as mechanical strength, dose reproducibility, scale production, sterilization, regulatory status as combination products, and long-term safety. In addition, new trends, including nano-integrated theranostic microneedles, closed-loop glucose-responsive systems, and AI-enabled personalized fabrication, are mentioned to map out a path towards clinical adoption. This review will establish the future of the microneedle-based drug delivery systems by combining engineering innovation with translational insight.

articles.title: NSAID use, osteoporosis, and trabecular bone score in community-dwelling older adults: the bushehr elderly health (BEH) ​program.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The relationship between nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) use and skeletal health remains uncertain. We examined reported NSAID use in relation to overall and site-specific osteoporosis and trabecular bone score (TBS) in community-dwelling older adults.

METHODS: This population-based cross-sectional analysis included 2,353 adults aged ≥ 60 years from the Bushehr Elderly Health Program, Iran. Osteoporosis was defined by a dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry T-score ≤ - 2.5 at the lumbar spine, femoral neck, or total hip. Sex-stratified logistic regression estimated prevalence odds ratios adjusted for age, body mass index, rheumatoid arthritis, and osteoarthritis. Sex interactions were tested for osteoporosis outcomes. Exploratory TBS analyses used ordinal and multinomial logistic regression; ordinal models adjusted for age, smoking, physical activity, body mass index, and diabetes.

RESULTS: NSAID use was reported by 369 participants (15.7%), and overall osteoporosis prevalence was 41.4%. Among women, NSAID use was associated with higher odds of overall osteoporosis (adjusted OR, 1.50; 95% CI, 1.10-2.05), femoral-neck osteoporosis (1.53; 1.13-2.07), and total-hip osteoporosis (1.53; 1.01-2.30). The lumbar-spine estimate was close to the null (1.07; 0.78-1.47). Associations in men were statistically inconclusive, and interaction tests did not establish differences by sex. Among women, adjusted ordinal logistic regression also identified an association between NSAID use and worse TBS categories (OR, 1.36; 95% CI, 1.00-1.85; p = 0.047). Category-specific multinomial comparisons were inconclusive.

CONCLUSION: Reported NSAID use was associated with higher prevalence odds of osteoporosis and poorer TBS status in older women after covariate adjustment. These findings support investigating how NSAID type, dose, and cumulative exposure relate to bone density and trabecular bone status in aging populations.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40200-026-02127-8.

articles.title: Diabetes mellitus and acute kidney failure-associated mortality in the United States: a retrospective analysis of CDC WONDER death records, 1999-2024.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe national trends in mortality involving both diabetes mellitus (DM) and acute kidney failure (AKF) among U.S. adults aged ≥55 years, including the COVID-19 period.

METHODS: Deaths listing both DM (ICD-10 E10-E14) and AKF (N17) during 1999-2024 were obtained from the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death databases. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 were stratified by demographic and geographic characteristics, and joinpoint regression estimated annual (APC) and average annual (AAPC) percent changes. Sensitivity analyses used underlying-cause definitions and excluded deaths listing COVID-19.

RESULTS: Among 206,290 deaths, the AAMR increased from 6.73 in 1999 to 13.90 in 2024 (AAPC 2.71%; 95% CI 1.54-3.88), rising until 2010, declining until 2018, increasing steeply from 2018 to 2021 (APC 32.96%), and declining thereafter. Mean AAMRs were higher in men than women (12.37 vs. 8.60), highest among non-Hispanic American Indian or Alaska Native (17.06) and Black (15.54) adults, lowest among non-Hispanic Asian or Pacific Islander adults (8.34), highest in the West (10.85) and South (10.76), and higher in nonmetropolitan areas (11.12 vs. 8.65). COVID-19 was listed on 17.4% of deaths during 2020-2024; excluding these deaths attenuated but did not eliminate the 2019-2022 increase (APC 23.25%), and the long-term increase persisted (AAPC 2.58%). Overall trends differed by cause-of-death definition.

CONCLUSIONS: Mortality involving both DM and AKF approximately doubled between 1999 and 2024. The pandemic-era surge was not fully explained by deaths certified with COVID-19, and rates differed by sex, race and ethnicity, and geography. These descriptive findings may help to target individual-level research and kidney-protective diabetes care.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40200-026-02128-7.

articles.title: Overcoming barriers for expanding market access to follow-on biologics in lower-middle-income countries.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Biologic therapies are highly effective for cancers, autoimmune and inflammatory conditions, diabetes, and other chronic diseases, yet remain largely out of reach in low- and lower-middle-income countries despite the rising non-communicable disease burden in these countries. Only about 1 billion of the world's 8 billion people can access biologics, concentrated in upper-middle- and high-income countries. Focusing on lower-middle-income countries (L-MICs), we assess barriers to originator and follow-on biologics (FOBs) and the opportunities to overcome them. Profiles of six geographically dispersed L-MICs serve as exemplars of the current capabilities and challenges of providing biological therapy in these countries.

AREAS COVERED: Regulatory, manufacturing and supply-chain, infrastructure, financing, and clinical constraints in L-MICs were identified as barriers to accessibility to biologics and FOBs. Actionable opportunities to overcome them include regulatory harmonization and reliance, technology transfer and local production, pooled procurement, income-indexed differential pricing, prescriber education, and clinician and patient trust campaigns. The cost-efficiencies that lower-cost FOBs can generate at equivalent clinical benefit could be reinvested to expand access on a budget-neutral basis. The profiles of the six selected L-MICs demonstrated heterogeneity with regards to population size, disease burden, and current capabilities and challenges to expand access to FOBs.

CONCLUSIONS: The access gap is now less about molecules than about the architecture around them. Aligning the fair-profit motive with the access imperative can make expansion a growth strategy rather than charity, with regulatory reliance and differential pricing as near-term unlocks and the coupling of cost-efficiency to expanded access as the organizing logic. Framing recommendations across micro, meso, and macro levels, we propose a shared, adaptable blueprint that lets each country copy and adapt to open new markets, close treatment gaps, and contribute meaningfully to global health equity.

articles.title: Cost-utility analysis of surgical revascularization versus conservative management for adult moyamoya disease patients with posterior hemorrhage in Japan.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This study evaluates the cost-effectiveness of surgical revascularization versus conservative management for adult moyamoya disease (MMD) patients with posterior hemorrhage from the perspective of the Japanese public healthcare payer.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We developed a combined decision tree and Markov model for adult posterior hemorrhagic MMD patients (mean age: 41 years; baseline modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-2) over a 60-year lifetime horizon with 1-year cycles. We estimated the treatment effect using the composite endpoint hazard ratio (0.07) from the JAM Trial posterior hemorrhage subgroup as a proxy for the effect on recurrent hemorrhage. We informed health utilities with recent EQ-5D-5L data from the Fukuoka Stroke Registry, weighted by the Japan Stroke Data Bank. We estimated direct medical costs based on the national fee schedule. We discounted costs and outcomes at 2% annually. We set the willingness-to-pay threshold at JPY 7,500,000 per quality-adjusted life year (QALY).

RESULTS: In the base case, surgical revascularization yielded 21.49 QALYs for JPY 6,323,426 (USD 40,302), compared with 15.59 QALYs and JPY 5,308,637 (USD 33,835) for conservative management. The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was JPY 172,220 (USD 1,098) per QALY, which falls below the reference value of JPY 7,500,000 per QALY. In scenario analyses with 5- and 10-year horizons, the ICERs were JPY 8,926,784 and JPY 2,031,693 per QALY, respectively. Probabilistic sensitivity analysis also favored surgical revascularization across the modeled parameter distributions.

LIMITATIONS: The base-case estimate of surgical efficacy was based on a composite outcome from a small subgroup, and long-term recurrence risks beyond the 5-year trial period remain uncertain.

CONCLUSION: Surgical revascularization is likely to be cost-effective for adult MMD patients with posterior hemorrhage within the Japanese healthcare system, although limited evidence leaves uncertainty about long-term rebleeding risks and the durability of surgical benefit.

articles.title: Predictive value of systemic inflammatory indices for new-onset atrial fibrillation after acute myocardial infarction: an interpretable machine learning study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: New-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF) after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is associated with adverse outcomes. Inflammation contributes to atrial fibrillation (AF) onset and progression. We developed an interpretable machine learning (ML) framework integrating complete blood count (CBC)-derived inflammatory indices with routine clinical parameters for NOAF risk assessment.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 3,077 AMI patients without prior AF (2018-2023). Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic splines (RCS), and threshold analyses evaluated six inflammatory indices: neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), and aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI). Boruta and LASSO selections were intersected. Eight ML models were evaluated, with Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) for interpretation.

RESULTS: NOAF incidence was 7.73%. Six indices were associated with NOAF in separate adjusted models (all p < 0.05). Estimated change points were approximately 5.5 (NLR), 1217 (SII), 2.9 (SIRI), and 430 (AISI). The support vector machine (SVM) achieved the highest mean training out-of-fold (OOF) area under the precision-recall curve (PR-AUC; 0.357) and a held-out test PR-AUC of 0.407. Mean absolute SHAP values were highest for left atrial diameter (LAD), age, and B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP); SIRI ranked first among inflammatory features. Fixed-feature ablation showed modest PR-AUC and Brier-score improvements, uncertain ROC-AUC gains, and no consistent net benefit on decision-curve analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: CBC-derived inflammatory indices were associated with NOAF, but their incremental predictive value beyond routine clinical variables remains uncertain. Given moderate predictive performance and no external validation, multicenter validation is needed before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Moving the furniture around - how herpes simplex virus 1 remodels the host nucleus.
articles.abstract: Herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) is a nuclear-replicating DNA virus that remodels the host cell nucleus to support viral gene expression, genome replication, and production of infectious progeny. During infection, HSV-1 alters chromatin organization, nuclear biophysical properties, and nuclear bodies composition and dynamics. These changes reflect viral strategies to counteract intrinsic anti-viral defenses and reorgenaize host nuclear functions to favor infection. Viral replication compartments reshape the nuclear environment and interact with nuclear bodies involved in RNA metabolism and gene regulation. HSV-1 mRNAs, many of which are intronless, rely on host export pathways adapted by viral factors such as ICP27, which links viral transcripts to host export receptors including NXF1. Recent evidence suggests that nuclear speckles may serve as specialized intranuclearhubs for immediate-early viral transcripts before export. This review discusses how HSV-1 reorganizes nuclear architecture and nuclear bodies, to regulate viral gene expression, RNA processing and nuclear export.

articles.title: Perioperative dynamics of selenoproteins and risk of cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury.
articles.abstract: Cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI) affects over 20% of patients and is associated with perioperative mortality and long-term renal impairment. Reliable early biomarkers remain limited. Selenoproteins, including glutathione peroxidases (GPX1, GPX3) and selenoprotein P (SEPP1), are critical for redox homeostasis, but their perioperative changes in CSA-AKI remain unclear. This study aimed to characterize selenoprotein dynamics and explore their association with renal function and CSA-AKI. In this prospective observational cohort study, 99 adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery were enrolled, serum and urine samples were collected preoperatively and at 24/48 h postoperatively. SEPP1, GPX1, GPX3, and KIM-1 were measured. Mixed-effects, correlation, and logistic regression assessed selenoprotein dynamics and associations with CSA-AKI, with an exploratory model including age and preoperative SEPP1. Among 89 analyzed patients, 22 (24.7%) developed AKI. Univariable analyses showed that lower perioperative SEPP1 levels, attenuated urinary SEPP1 increases, and greater serum GPX1 decreases were associated with higher odds of CSA-AKI; older age, hypertension, and longer operation time were also associated with CSA-AKI. Postoperatively, serum SEPP1 declined markedly, remaining lower in AKI patients. Urinary SEPP1 increased significantly in non-AKI patients. Changes in GPX1 and GPX3 differed between AKI and non-AKI groups. Serum SEPP1 correlated positively with eGFR and inversely with creatinine and cystatin C. An exploratory model incorporating age and preoperative serum SEPP1 yielded an apparent AUC of 0.818. In summary, perioperative alterations in selenoproteins (GPX1, GPX3, SEPP1) are closely linked to CSA-AKI. Preoperative SEPP1 combined with clinical variables may enable early risk prediction and support timely intervention.

articles.title: Variability in non-invasive tests: Challenges and implications for monitoring liver disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diagnostic and prognostic non-invasive fibrosis tests (NITs) are increasingly repurposed to monitor liver disease. However, their reproducibility and the minimal detectable change (MDC, ie, the smallest change that exceeds expected measurement variability) are poorly characterized.

METHODS: We retrospectively assessed variability of blood-based NITs and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) by vibration-controlled transient elastography on the same day (repeatability) and across use-cases when metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, fibrosis, or portal hypertension is suspected. Measurements were done within 90 days. Agreement and variability were quantified using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), Bland-Altman analyses, and MDC on the original (absolute) and relative (MDC%) scales.

RESULTS: Across 6 cohorts, ICCs were generally good to excellent, but within-subject variability remained substantial.
