Same-day LSM had a pooled MDC% of 24% on the m/s scale, corresponding to an asymmetric kPa-equivalent window of -43% to +54%. For longitudinal lab-based NITs, pooled MDC% was 47% for FIB-4 and 56% for APRI, while absolute MDC was 13-17 percentage points for LiverPRO and 3 percentage points for CORE. Optimistic estimates remained substantial after excluding the 10% most extreme paired differences. Variability increased with biomarker level for LSM, FIB-4, and APRI, whereas MDC windows for probability-based scores were strongly baseline-dependent and followed an inverse U-shaped pattern. When repeat testing was triggered by an elevated initial LSM, regression to the mean accounted for most or all of the observed decrease.

CONCLUSIONS: Good agreement in NITs does not guarantee high precision for disease monitoring. MDC depends on biomarker level, clinical setting, measurement scale, and selection for repeat testing. Universal thresholds should not be applied uncritically, and repeated measurements, baseline-dependent interpretation, and regression to the mean should guide monitoring decisions.

articles.title: Ascites fluid PMN counts below the SBP threshold predict 30-day mortality in a national hospitalized cirrhosis cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complications in patients with cirrhosis often result from bacterial and bacterial product translocation. This translocation can occur because of portal hypertension, alterations in the gut microbiome, and immune dysregulation. We aimed to re-evaluate admission ascites PMN/mm3 count as a biomarker of 30-day mortality.

METHODS: We identified veterans with cirrhosis using validated ICD-9/10 codes who had a paracentesis ≤24 hours of their index hospitalization in the Veterans Affairs Corporate Data Warehouse from 2009 to 2024. In multivariable analysis, we determined the prognostic significance of ascites PMN/mm3 <100, 100-249, and ≥250.

RESULTS: The 4111 veterans who met the inclusion criteria were mostly older (66 y) men (96.3%) with alcohol-associated liver disease (31.1%) who experienced 16.9% 30-day mortality. Most patients (~80%) had an ascites PMN/mm3 count <100. A roughly linear relationship between 30-day mortality was seen until the threshold of 100 PMN/mm3 was reached, when the relationship plateaued. The OR for 30-day mortality of a PMN/mm3 count 100-249 was 1.93 (95% CI: [1.55-2.38], p<0.001) after adjusting for age, CCI, liver disease etiology, admission lactulose use, SBP prophylaxis, serum WBC count, MELD-Na, and serum albumin. The 30-day mortality risk was not statistically different from the higher threshold of ≥250 PMN/mm3 (p=0.53).

CONCLUSIONS: Admission ascites PMN/mm3 count ≥100, compared with <100, independently predicts a doubling in 30-day mortality in a national cohort of hospitalized patients with cirrhosis. Larger prospective studies are needed to examine the optimal ascites fluid PMN (polymorphonuclear neutrophil) thresholds that increase mortality risk.

articles.title: Predictors and prognostic impact of spontaneous portal vein thrombosis recanalization in cirrhosis: An individual patient data meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Portal vein thrombosis (PVT) in cirrhosis has a quite unpredictable natural history. Spontaneous recanalization may occur, but predictors and prognostic impact remain uncertain. We performed an individual patient data (IPD) meta-analysis to evaluate survival according to spontaneous recanalization and to identify predictors of recanalization.

METHODS: We included cohort studies of patients with cirrhosis and PVT not receiving anticoagulation and obtained de-identified IPD. All-cause mortality was analyzed using a competing-risk model (competing event: liver transplantation) adjusted for prespecified baseline covariates. Predictors of recanalization were assessed with mixed-effects ordinal logistic regression including a random study intercept.

RESULTS: Eight studies contributed 586 patients. Spontaneous recanalization occurred in 264 (47.7%). Overall recanalization was independently associated with lower mortality (aSHR 0.51; 95% CI 0.28-0.90), with the benefit driven by complete recanalization (aSHR 0.45; 95% CI 0.21-0.94). Recanalization of PVT localized in the main portal vein trunk was linked to a strong survival benefit (interaction SHR 0.39; 95% CI 0.16-0.91; p=0.02), whereas no benefit was observed after recanalization of isolated intrahepatic branch thrombosis. PVT recanalization was more likely to occur in Child-Pugh A (aOR 2.63; 95% CI 1.18-5.88), partial thrombosis (aOR 1.69; 95% CI 1.09-2.56), and isolated intrahepatic location (aOR 2.04; 95% CI 1.23-3.33).

CONCLUSIONS: Spontaneous recanalization occurs in approximately half of patients with cirrhosis and PVT and is associated with improved survival, particularly when complete and involving the main portal vein trunk. These findings underscore its prognostic relevance and indirectly support anticoagulation to promote recanalization.

articles.title: Effects of COVID-19 vaccination type and vaccination-infection interval on viral clearance dynamics in Omicron BA.5 patients at Guangzhou Fangcang shelter hospitals: A propensity score matched multicenter retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: The Omicron BA.5 subvariant exhibited pronounced immune evasion and was associated with widespread breakthrough infections. Unlike settings where mRNA vaccines predominated, China mainly used inactivated vaccines, with the adenovirus type 5-vectored vaccine Ad5-nCoV also administered at scale. Real-world evidence on post-infection viral clearance associated with these platforms remains limited. This multicenter retrospective cohort study enrolled 16,533 mild or asymptomatic Omicron BA.5 cases from two Fangcang shelter hospitals in Guangzhou, China, from Novernber 5 to December 8, 2022. The primary objective was to compare viral-clearance time between unvaccinated and vaccinated participants. The secondary objective was to compare inactivated-vaccine recipients, or and Ad5-nCoV recipients, containing regimens in a propensity score-matched cohort; the last-dose-to-infection interval analysis was exploratory. Propensity score matching was performed using age, sex, marital status, occupation, and province as covariates to improve between-group comparability. All patients underwent standardized daily RT-PCR testing containing both N and ORF1ab genes, with Ct values > 35 defined as negative. The outcome was time to viral clearance, defined as two consecutive negative nasopharyngeal swabs ≥ 24 hours apart. In the overall cohort, vaccinated patients had significantly shorter shedding duration (9.05 vs… 10.42d; P < .001) compared with unvaccinated patients. The matched cohort included 228 unvaccinated, 228 inactivated vaccine recipients, and 114 Ad5-nCoV recipients. Median time to viral clearance differed across groups with 9.42, 8.56, and 8.48d, respectively. Prior vaccination was associated with shorter viral clearance but with no significant difference observed between inactivated vaccine and Ad5-nCoV recipients among the matched regimens.

articles.title: Delays in screening, diagnosis and monitoring are associated with worse clinical and economic outcomes for patients with chronic kidney disease: a narrative review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) has substantial associated morbidity, mortality and healthcare costs that increase as CKD progresses. Despite newer, more effective treatments, the global burden of CKD continues to increase.

OBJECTIVE: To understand patterns of screening, diagnosis, monitoring and treatment in CKD and how earlier treatment initiation could help mitigate CKD burden.

METHODS: Targeted searches of bibliographic databases and grey literature sources identified studies published 2015-2025. Eligible evidence comprised observational studies on CKD screening and diagnosis rates, factors associated with delayed treatment initiation, clinical and economic burden of delayed diagnosis/treatment, and economic evaluations of population-based CKD screening. Thirty-five studies were synthesized narratively according to the CKD care pathway; no meta-analysis or formal quality assessment was conducted.

DISCUSSION: Despite guideline recommendations, 19%-33% of patients in at-risk populations received neither kidney function nor albuminuria testing. Documented CKD diagnosis rates were often low, particularly in earlier stages. Documented CKD diagnosis was associated with increased monitoring and prescription fill rates, as well as slower decline of estimated glomerular filtration rate. Longer time to documented diagnosis and nephrology referral timing were associated with increased risk of kidney failure and cardiovascular events. Recent economic models that incorporated newer treatments and cardiovascular events generally produced found selected population-based screening strategies cost-effective. However, findings varied by target population, screening strategy/frequency, treatment, model assumptions, setting and willingness-to-pay threshold, and not all modelled scenarios were cost-effective.

CONCLUSIONS: Results from observational studies suggest an association between earlier CKD diagnosis and greater use of appropriate monitoring and nephrology referral, which may facilitate timely intervention to slow progression, improving long-term outcomes. However, many patients remain undiagnosed despite available laboratory data. Improvements in risk-based testing, screening, diagnosis, monitoring and nephrology referral may help patients access effective treatments, but stronger comparative evidence is needed to establish their effects on clinical outcomes and costs.

articles.title: Substrate-specific mitochondrial bioenergetics and metabolic flexibility in visceral adipose tissue across obesity-related glycemic states.
articles.abstract: Obesity is characterized by the expansion of metabolically dysfunctional visceral adipose tissue (VAT) and chronic low-grade inflammation, which contribute to the development of insulin resistance. However, to what extent VAT bioenergetics and substrate preferences differ across distinct obesity-related glycaemic status profiles remains poorly understood. The present study aimed to assess substrate utilization and metabolic flexibility of VAT from individuals with obesity across different glycaemic statuses, namely euglycemia, prediabetes, and type 2 diabetes (T2D). VAT from individuals with obesity with euglycemia (n = 11), prediabetes (n = 12) and T2D (n = 6) was harvested during bariatric surgery. VAT bioenergetics and mitochondrial substrate preferences under the influence of pyruvate, glutamine and fatty acids metabolism inhibitors, were assessed using the Seahorse Analyser. VAT expression of OB, GLS1, MPC1, CPT1a, HK2, PDHA1, RPII, β-actin genes was quantified by qRT-PCR. VAT basal mitochondrial respiration was similar across glycaemic groups. In VAT from euglycemic individuals, pyruvate inhibition decreased spare respiratory capacity. In contrast, in VAT from individuals with prediabetes and T2D, ATP-linked respiration increased when glutamine was the sole substrate available, which in individuals with prediabetes, was accompanied by an increase of non-mitochondrial oxygen consumption. There were no differences in the expression of genes related to energy metabolism across groups. These exploratory findings suggest that substrate-dependent VAT respiratory responses may vary across obesity-related glycaemic states despite the absence of detectable basal respiratory differences. The response observed under glutamine-only conditions raises the possibility of compensatory metabolic adaptations in prediabetes, although their mechanisms and potential alteration in T2D remain to be established.

articles.title: Potentially modifiable mediators of the association between child abuse and dementia.
articles.abstract: Background: Literature investigating mediation of the association between child abuse and dementia has largely considered composite adverse childhood experience scores rather than individual adverse experiences, despite evidence that different experiences have different impacts on dementia risk. Additionally, prior studies consider mediators in isolation, despite known associations between mediators which may impact indirect pathways from child abuse to dementia.Objectives: To investigate whether potentially modifiable health and lifestyle factors mediate the association between child abuse and dementia.Methods: We used data from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing to investigate associations between child abuse and dementia (N = 5,448). Indirect pathways through four mediator categories (education, health behaviours, mental health and cardiovascular health) were examined. We used regression modelling to estimate associations between child abuse, mediators and dementia, and causal mediation analysis using the g-formula to estimate the joint indirect effect through the mediators.Results: Individuals who experienced child abuse had, on average, an 80% higher hazard of dementia, compared to those who did not (RTE HR: 1.80, 95% CI: 1.21-2.39). Mental health mediators showed strong associations with both child abuse and dementia. Evidence for other mediators was weaker. Education, health behaviours, mental health and cardiovascular health mediated approximately 18% of the association. Sensitivity analysis revealed that almost all this mediation occurred through mental health.Conclusions: Child abuse was associated with higher risk of dementia. Joint mediation analysis suggested that education, health behaviours, cardiovascular health, and mental health accounted for a relatively small proportion of the observed association, with most mediation occurring through mental health. Future research must focus on other potential pathways from child abuse to dementia, including biological and social mechanisms.

articles.title: Factors Associated With Clinical Trial Discontinuation in Aesthetic and Reconstructive Breast Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Randomized controlled trials are the gold standard for investigating the safety and efficacy of a new intervention. In particular, clinical trials in aesthetic and reconstructive breast surgery are critical for the advancement of treatment modalities and device development. This study evaluates the factors associated with early discontinuation of breast reconstruction and aesthetic breast surgery-related studies.

METHODS: A cross-sectional analysis of all breast surgery-related clinical trials on the ClinicalTrials.gov registry was performed. Trials were categorized as aesthetic, reconstructive, or both. Clinical trials related to breast cancer surgery only, without reconstruction, were excluded. Trials listed as "suspended," "terminated," or "withdrawn" were defined as discontinued trials. Trials were then further subdivided into 7 study topics, which included: (1) anesthesia/pain management, (2) infection control/wound healing, (3) breast implant/tissue expanders, (4) general breast reconstruction, (5) fat grafting, (6) microsurgery, and (7) patient/surgical education. Additional factors examined included intervention type, funding source, enrollment size, subject gender, subject age, trial start date, and location.

RESULTS: A total of 3658 clinical trials were identified with start dates between January 1994 and July 2024. Of these, 565 trials were included in the final analysis. Seventy-eight percent of studies were reconstructive, 8% were aesthetic, and 14% were both. A total of 76 trials were prematurely discontinued, most commonly secondary to low patient accrual (24%), institutional/principal investigator decision (17%), and inadequate staffing (12%). Thirty-nine percent of discontinued trials were device-related, followed by drug/pharmaceutical (33%) and surgical technique (21%). Study category, topic, and study location were not associated with early discontinuation. Observational studies had a significantly lower likelihood of early discontinuation compared with randomized controlled trials [OR=0.23 (0.10-0.48), P<0.001]. Industry-funded studies had a higher likelihood of early discontinuation compared with nonindustry funded studies [OR=2.07 (1.17-3.59), P<0.001].

CONCLUSION: Successful completion of clinical trials in aesthetic and reconstructive breast surgery is essential for improving patient outcomes. Our study demonstrates that 13.5% of clinical trials did not reach fruition, largely secondary to poor patient recruitment and staffing issues. Targeted efforts to help support trial completion are necessary to help improve evidence-based practice within breast surgery.

articles.title: Multidrug-resistant (MDR) Salmonella Typhi spondylodiscitis with vertebral collapse: a case report.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND IMPORTANCE: Spondylodiscitis is an uncommon spinal infection that remains diagnostically challenging because of its non-specific symptoms and radiological overlap with tuberculosis and neoplasms. Among these, infections caused by Salmonella Typhi are extremely unusual, and the case becomes even more challenging when multidrug resistance (MDR) is present.

PRESENTATION OF CASE: We describe a 49-year-old woman with diabetes and hypertension who presented with persistent back pain following an episode of enteric fever. Imaging showed spondylodiscitis with vertebral collapse, initially suspected as tuberculosis or metastasis. A mammogram and tuberculosis (TB) workup were negative. Definitive diagnosis was only achieved during surgery. Intraoperative biopsy and culture confirmed Salmonella Typhi, resistant to multiple antibiotics but sensitive to imipenem and azithromycin. Targeted therapy led to clinical improvement.

CLINICAL DISCUSSION: This case underlines the diagnostic difficulty of spinal infections, where radiology alone cannot differentiate between infection and malignancy. Surgical biopsy and culture remain essential, aligning with current Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) and National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) recommendations.

CONCLUSION: Multidrug-resistant Salmonella Typhi spondylodiscitis is exceptionally rare. Early tissue diagnosis and tailored therapy are key to achieving favorable outcomes.

articles.title: Nutritional risk, inflammation, and hospitalization after hemodialysis initiation.
articles.abstract: Evidence linking nutritional and inflammatory markers at hemodialysis initiation to subsequent hospital stay remains limited. We examined whether the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) and C-reactive protein (CRP) at hemodialysis initiation were associated with prolonged post-initiation hospital stay. This single-center retrospective study included patients who initiated hemodialysis during hospitalization and transitioned to maintenance hemodialysis between 2004 and 2024. The primary outcome was hospitalization for 30 days or longer after hemodialysis initiation. Multivariable logistic regression was used with adjustment for age, sex, cardiovascular disease, diabetes mellitus, initiation modality, calendar period, and pre-hemodialysis vascular access status. Among 517 patients, 501 were included in multivariable analysis, and 166 patients (32.1%) experienced prolonged post-initiation stay. A higher GNRI was associated with lower odds of prolonged stay (odds ratio per 1-unit increase, 0.955; 95% confidence interval, 0.925-0.986; p = 0.005), whereas higher log-transformed CRP was associated with higher odds (odds ratio, 1.203; 95% confidence interval, 1.055-1.372; p = 0.006). The low GNRI/high CRP group had the highest odds of prolonged stay (odds ratio, 3.180; 95% confidence interval, 1.489-6.787; p = 0.003), without significant multiplicative interaction. Lower GNRI and higher CRP at hemodialysis initiation were independently and jointly associated with prolonged post-initiation stay. These findings describe associations rather than validated predictions, and prospective evaluation is required before these markers are applied to individual-level risk assessment.

articles.title: The role of digital health technologies in easing the burden of congenital heart disease beyond high-income countries.
How do domiciliary carers contribute to preventing the spread of antimicrobial resistance? A qualitative study in England.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a global problem that requires coordinated action. Most antibiotics in England are used in community settings, giving all community health and care professionals potentially important roles in antimicrobial stewardship (AMS). Currently little evidence exists on how the adult social care workforce, including domiciliary carers providing care at home, contribute to AMS, despite the unique opportunities of their role.

OBJECTIVES: To explore domiciliary care workers' knowledge of AMR and identify existing contributions and opportunities to improve AMS.

METHODS: We used a purposive sampling approach to recruit a diverse sample of domiciliary carers working in England and administered a semi-structured interview exploring their views and practices relating to AMS. Thematic analysis was applied.

RESULTS: We interviewed 30 domiciliary carers. Analysis of participants' responses indicated that carers supported AMS in the following ways: infection prevention and control (IPC), and signposting clients to healthcare and antibiotic administration. However, carers generally did not recognize themselves as actively contributing to AMS.

CONCLUSIONS: We identified unrecognized areas of good AMS practice, along with opportunities to enhance domiciliary carers' impact on AMS. Potential interventions include improving timeliness of adding antibiotics to care plans as well as inclusion of AMS behaviours in them, co-developing training with carers on AMR to reinforce their AMS practices, clear distinction of carers' contributions as part of a whole-system approach to tackling AMR, and embedding AMS competencies into the Care Certificate for greater reach and consistency.

articles.title: Unveiling the molecular and biological mechanisms of Tai Chi in chronic disease management: a bibliometric and visualized analysis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Tai Chi is widely utilized for chronic disease management, yet its underlying biological mechanisms remain fragmented. To objectively map the mechanistic knowledge structure and identify emerging frontiers, a bibliometric analysis was conducted on 348 mechanism-focused articles spanning from 2006 to 2026, retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. Data visualization and network analyses using VOSviewer and CiteSpace revealed a clear paradigm shift from macroscopic systemic responses to highly specific neurobiological targets. Early foundational research centered on psychoneuroimmunology, demonstrating that Tai Chi buffers the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis and downregulates pro-inflammatory cytokines, thereby alleviating osteoarthritis pain and cancer-related fatigue. Contemporary research frontiers are heavily concentrated on neuroplasticity and cellular defense. Objective evidence highlights the upregulation of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and the remodeling of cortico-limbic networks to preserve function in Parkinson's disease and mild cognitive impairment. Furthermore, strong recent keyword bursts for "oxidative stress" and "heart failure" underscore Tai Chi's potential in enhancing endogenous antioxidant defenses, reducing DNA damage, and improving endothelial function via systemic brain-body crosstalk. In conclusion, Tai Chi exerts its multidimensional clinical benefits through interconnected neuro-immune, neuroplastic, and anti-oxidative networks. To transition from associative findings to definitive causal mechanisms, future research must integrate multi-omics technologies and rigorously standardized longitudinal trials.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13205-026-05134-x.

articles.title: Therapeutic potential of herbal topical agents in evidence-based wound care: a systematic research review.
articles.abstract: Herbal interventions are increasingly investigated for wound infection due to their potential for antimicrobial, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, tissue-repair and angiogenic activities. Despite this, their clinical relevance is uncertain owing to substantial heterogeneity in botanical materials, phytochemical composition, formulations, experimental models and level of evidence. This systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020. Literature published between 2000 and 2025 was systematically searched in PubMed for original peer-reviewed studies evaluating herbal extracts or purified phytoconstituents, alone or incorporated into topical formulations, for wound infection. In vitro, animal, observational, and clinical studies were included and critically interpreted as per the evidence. Other than this, data on botanical authentication, extraction, standardization, bioactive constituents, wound type, formulation characteristics, and antimicrobial and antifilm activity, efficacy and safety were extracted. The evidence indicated that selected herbal interventions can modulate multiple processes involved in wound repair, including inflammation, oxidative stress, angiogenesis, fibroblast activity, collagen deposition, re-epithelialization, and microbial growth. Nevertheless, substantial heterogeneity in plant sources, extraction methods, concentrations, formulations, wound models, and outcome measures limited direct comparison. Evidence for activity against clinically relevant biofilms and chronic wounds was comparatively limited, while clinical evidence remained less extensive than preclinical evidence. Advanced formulations may improve delivery and wound-site retention, although their independent contribution to therapeutic efficacy requires further clarification. Herbal extracts and phytoconstituents represent potential candidates for topical wound management; however, current evidence does not support their routine replacement of established therapies. Standardized preparations, reproducible formulations, rigorous safety evaluation, clinically relevant chronic-wound models, and adequately powered clinical trials are required for translation into evidence-based wound care.

articles.title: Nanophytosomal encapsulation of Glaucium leiocarpum extract improves glycemic control and renal function in a streptozotocin-induced diabetic rat model.
articles.abstract: We compared the antidiabetic effects of Glaucium leiocarpum (horned poppy, HP) extract-loaded nanophytosomes with those of free HP extract in a streptozotocin (STZ) induced diabetic rat model. Phytochemical profiling of the HP extract was performed using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). Eight experimental groups (n = 6) were treated intraperitoneally for 21 consecutive days, and metabolic parameters including non-fasting blood glucose (non-FBG), body weight, water intake, serum biochemical markers, and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels were assessed. HP loaded nanophytosomes at the maximum non-lethal dose significantly reduced non-FBG levels to 289.33 ± 14.84 mg/dL (p ≤ 0.05). Body weight increased significantly from 270.83 ± 8.87 g to 303.67 ± 10.58 g during treatment (p ≤ 0.05), representing an approximately 12.1% increase. Furthermore, serum urea levels decreased from 95.17 ± 8.13 mg/dL in the diabetic control group to 60.17 ± 4.25 mg/dL in the group treated with HP (max) loaded nanophytosomes, representing a 36.8% reduction (p ≤ 0.05). No significant differences were observed in creatinine, albumin, or MDA levels among the groups. Notably, the nanophytosomal formulation outperformed the free HP extract in improving metabolic parameters in STZ-induced diabetic rats; however, further studies are necessary to elucidate the underlying mechanisms and evaluate long-term effects.

articles.title: Distinct associations of STK11 rs2301759 and SLC29A4 rs2685753 with metformin response among Saudi patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This study investigates the genotype and allele frequencies of solute carrier family 29 member 4 (SLC29A4) rs2685753 and serine/threonine kinase 11 (STK11) rs2301759 in the Saudi population and their association with metformin response in Saudi patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), while comparing the findings with other ethnic populations.

PATIENTS & METHODS: A prospective cohort study included 69 newly diagnosed Saudi adults with T2DM receiving metformin monotherapy for at least six months and 59 healthy controls. Genotyping was performed using TaqMan single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) assays. Associations between genetic variants and glycemic response were analyzed using chi-square tests and logistic regression.

RESULTS: Among patients, 55% achieved adequate glycemic control, whereas 45% were non-responders. SLC29A4 rs2685753 showed no significant association with the metformin response. In contrast, STK11 rs2301759 demonstrated significant genotypic and allelic associations, with the C/T genotype linked to improved glycemic response. Higher baseline glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) and family history of diabetes were associated with poorer response.

CONCLUSION: STK11 rs2301759 may influence metformin efficacy in Saudi patients with T2DM and could support personalized diabetes management.

articles.title: Awareness of the signs and symptoms of pancreatic cancer: a cross-sectional study from a developing country setting.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pancreatic cancer (PC) is associated with poor prognosis, largely due to delayed diagnosis and limited awareness of its risk factors, symptoms, and diagnostic approaches. This study aimed to assess public awareness, knowledge, and attitudes toward PC among adults.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 438 adults using a structured, validated questionnaire administered through face-to-face interviews. Participants' awareness, knowledge of risk factors and diagnostic methods, attitudes toward seeking medical care, and screening practices were assessed. Multivariate analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of PC awareness.

RESULTS: Among the 438 participants, 73.7% had heard of PC, and 98.6% recognized it as a serious disease. However, knowledge remained limited, particularly regarding symptoms and diagnostic approaches. Alcohol consumption (72.4%), chronic pancreatitis (65.5%), and family history (65.1%) were commonly recognized risk factors, while misconceptions regarding radiation exposure (34.5%) were evident. More than 70% of participants were unaware of PC diagnostic methods. Despite generally positive health-seeking attitudes, with 60.3% reporting that they would be very likely to consult a physician if they experienced alarming symptoms, only 2.7% had undergone screening, and 83.6% had never received information about PC from a healthcare provider. Multivariate analysis identified no independent predictors of PC awareness.

CONCLUSION: Although general awareness of PC was moderate and attitudes toward seeking medical care were positive, substantial knowledge gaps persisted regarding symptoms, risk factors, and diagnostic approaches. These findings highlight the need for targeted, evidence-based educational interventions integrated into primary healthcare and chronic disease management services to improve public understanding, promote timely medical consultation, and potentially reduce diagnostic delays.

articles.title: Correlation between proteinuria and cardiac biomarker levels in kidney transplant recipients.
articles.abstract: Kidney transplantation is the preferred treatment for end-stage kidney disease, with improved short-term outcomes; however, long-term graft and patient survival remain suboptimal. Proteinuria is a strong predictor of adverse graft and cardiovascular outcomes. We investigated the relationship between proteinuria and selected cardiac and inflammatory biomarkers, including the interleukin-33 (IL-33)/soluble ST2 (sST2) axis, malondialdehyde, neprilysin, growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF-15), and angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), in kidney transplant recipients, with a focus on patients with heart failure. Methods: Sixty-five transplant recipients were included: 15 kidney transplant recipients with heart failure and 49 controls consisting of kidney or heart transplant recipients without heart failure. Patients were followed between November 2023 and June 2024 at the Division of Nephrology at the University of Debrecen. Proteinuria was assessed using the urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio. Laboratory analyses included routine biochemical parameters, inflammatory markers, NT-proBNP, soluble IL-33 receptor (sST2), neprilysin, GDF-15, and ACE2 activity. Discrete data were described as percentages and analyzed with Fisher's exact test. Group comparisons were performed using the Kruskal-Wallis test, and correlations were assessed using non-parametric methods. Across all study groups, urinary protein excretion correlated weakly positively with sST2 levels (r = 0.27, p = 0.0448). Patients with heart failure had more pronounced anemia (p = 0.0470) and lower serum iron levels (p = 0.0041). Proteinuria was weakly positively associated with circulating sST2 concentrations. Further studies are needed to clarify the prognostic significance of this pathway in kidney transplant outcomes.

articles.title: Factors associated with neonatal intensive care unit admission in preterm prelabour rupture of membranes: a retrospective study.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study evaluated the independent associations of four prespecified variables readily available at the initial assessment (gestational age at preterm prelabour rupture of membranes [PPROM], admission C-reactive protein [CRP], white blood cell [WBC] count and oligohydramnios) with NICU admission in singleton pregnancies between 34 + 0 and 36 + 6 weeks. A secondary exploratory objective was to assess the discriminative performance of a multivariable logistic regression model incorporating these four variables.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 345 singleton pregnancies complicated by PPROM and managed at a tertiary care centre between January 2020 and December 2025. The four prespecified variables were entered simultaneously into a multivariable logistic regression model to evaluate their independent associations with NICU admission. Antenatal corticosteroid exposure was added in a sensitivity analysis. Model discrimination, calibration and bootstrap internal validation were assessed exploratorily.

RESULTS: NICU admission occurred in 89 neonates (25.8%). Gestational age at PPROM was independently associated with NICU admission (adjusted odds ratio 0.607, 95% confidence interval 0.445-0.830; p = 0.002), corresponding to a 39.3% reduction in the odds of NICU admission per 1-week increase. Admission CRP, WBC count and oligohydramnios were not independently associated with NICU admission. The association with gestational age persisted after adjustment for antenatal corticosteroid exposure. Model discrimination was modest (apparent AUC 0.611, 95% CI 0.541-0.681; optimism-corrected AUC 0.584); after bootstrap correction, the calibration slope was 0.796 and the Brier score was 0.191.

CONCLUSIONS: Gestational age at PPROM was the only prespecified variable independently associated with subsequent NICU admission, whereas admission CRP, WBC count and oligohydramnios were not independently associated with NICU admission. The exploratory model showed limited overall performance and should not be used for individual-level risk prediction.

articles.title: A Novel Method for the Temporary Treatment of Sunken Flap Syndrome: A Presentation of 3 Cases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND IMPORTANCE: Sunken flap syndrome (SFS) is a neurological decline that results from paradoxical brain shift following decompressive hemicraniectomy. It is thought to arise from a gradient between atmospheric and intracranial pressure and can cause neurological morbidity if not surgically corrected. In most cases, this involves autologous or synthetic cranioplasty. However, in select patient populations, this is not possible-either because of recent infection, availability of cranioplasty implant, anticoagulant use, or other patient-specific factors.

CLINICAL PRESENTATION: In this case report, we present 3 patients with SFS who could not undergo cranioplasty due to a recent surgical site infection. Instead, their SFS was managed nonoperatively with a makeshift "external cranioplasty" that resulted in significant improvement in their midline shift and mental status.

CONCLUSION: We believe this fast, economical approach can be applied to future patients with SFS who are unable to undergo surgical intervention.

articles.title: Preventive Linear Ablation Strategy for Intra-Atrial Reentrant Tachycardia Following Cardiac Surgery.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Intra-atrial reentrant tachycardia (IART) frequently occurs following cardiac surgery due to scar-related conduction abnormalities. While advances in mapping technologies have improved the acute success rate of catheter ablation, arrhythmia recurrence remains a significant clinical concern. This study aimed to evaluate whether a preventive linear ablation strategy guided by voltage mapping improves the long-term success rate of catheter ablation in patients with IART post-cardiac surgery.

METHODS AND RESULTS: A total of 46 consecutive patients following cardiac surgery who underwent atrial tachycardia ablation between 2022 and 2024 were enrolled in the study group. After activation mapping-guided ablation for ongoing IART, preventive linear ablation was performed based on voltage mapping. Fifty consecutive sex- and age-matched patients with cardiac surgery undergoing activation mapping-guided ablation alone served as the historical control group between 2018 and 2021. At a mean follow-up of 21 ± 4.9 months, the rate of freedom from atrial arrhythmias was significantly higher in the study group compared to the control group (82.6% vs. 64.0%; p = 0.019). Despite the improved outcomes, the study group had significantly longer total procedure times (192 ± 37 vs. 126 ± 25 min; p < 0.001) and radiofrequency ablation durations (29 ± 5 vs. 20 ± 6 min; p < 0.001). However, there were no significant differences in complication rates between the two groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Preventive linear ablation strategy was associated with improved arrhythmia-free survival in patients with IART post cardiac surgery, but these exploratory findings require confirmation in future prospective studies.

articles.title: Combined Transnasal and Transcranial Approach for a Complex Type IV Nasal Dermoid Sinus Cyst.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND IMPORTANCE: Nasal dermoid sinus cysts (NDSCs) are rare congenital midline anomalies caused by incomplete separation of ectoderm and neuroectoderm during embryogenesis. Intracranial extension, although uncommon, increases the risk of infection, recurrence, and neurological complications. Hartley type IV lesions involve the intradural compartment and represent the most complex subtype.

CLINICAL PRESENTATION: A 13-year-old boy presented with a congenital nasal tip pit associated with recurrent swelling and serous discharge since age 9. MRI and computed tomography revealed a midline fistulous tract extending through the foramen cecum, with extradural intrafalcine and intradural frontobasal components, consistent with a type IV NDSC. Complete excision was achieved through a combined transnasal interalar and transcranial transfrontal approach. The extracranial tract was dissected to the foramen cecum, and the intracranial component was removed by interhemispheric dissection. Endoscopic assistance confirmed a deformed foramen cecum, reconstructed with polymethylmethacrylate. The postoperative course was uneventful, with no neurological deficits. Imaging confirmed complete resection without recurrence. Histopathology demonstrated abundant keratinous debris, confirming a dermoid lesion.

CONCLUSION: This case highlights the importance of multidisciplinary planning and tailored craniofacial strategies in managing complex NDSCs with intracranial extension. The combined transnasal and transcranial approach enabled radical excision while preserving anatomic and functional integrity.

articles.title: Presence of Human Papillomaviruses in the Normal-Appearing Hypopharyngeal Mucosa: A Prospective Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a well-established etiological factor in oropharyngeal cancer, whereas its role in the hypopharynx is less well understood. This prospective study investigated the prevalence of HPV in normal-appearing hypopharyngeal mucosa using polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based HPV detection.

METHODS: Consecutive patients undergoing hypopharyngoscopy, laryngomicroscopy, or transnasal esophagogastroscopy for benign indications were prospectively recruited. Biopsies were obtained from normal-appearing hypopharyngeal mucosa and analyzed for HPV DNA by PCR-based genotyping. Participants completed a questionnaire addressing HPV-related risk factors.

RESULTS: Tissue samples were collected from 53 patients (median age, 51 years; range, 18-85 years), of whom 32 (60.4%) were female. One sample was excluded because of insufficient DNA quality. Among the remaining 52 evaluable samples, one was positive for a cutaneous HPV type and one for high-risk HPV18. The HPV18-positive sample originated from a patient who was subsequently diagnosed with a p16-positive squamous cell carcinoma arising in a vallecular cyst. RNA in situ hybridization confirmed transcriptionally active HPV within the tumor. A history of HPV-associated benign disease was reported by 18 of 53 patients (34%).

CONCLUSION: HPV DNA detection was rare in normal-appearing hypopharyngeal mucosa, even among individuals with a history of HPV-associated benign disease. Nevertheless, high-risk HPV18 was detected in the hypopharyngeal mucosa of a patient with an HPV-positive vallecular squamous cell carcinoma. These findings provide novel data on HPV prevalence in the hypopharynx and suggest that oncogenic HPV may occasionally be present in clinically normal hypopharyngeal mucosa.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: 4.

articles.title: Impedance-Based Contact Visualization for PulseSelect Pulmonary Vein Isolation: A Single-Center Feasibility Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: PulseSelect pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) lacks a dedicated contact indicator.

METHODS: We retrospectively compared 63 patients undergoing PVI before and after EnSite Contact Index (CI) implementation. Because electrical isolation does not confirm lesion transmurality, post-procedural unipolar electrograms (u-EGMs) were assessed as acute surrogate markers.

RESULTS: CI guidance was associated with more applications, shorter fluoroscopy, and in an exploratory analysis of analyzable patients, fewer residual high-voltage u-EGMs (1/20 vs. 8/24; p = 0.027). No complications occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: CI-guided PVI was feasible; these procedural and acute electrophysiological associations require prospective validation.

articles.title: Epidemiology of gestational diabetes mellitus in Latin America and the Caribbean: a scoping review.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a major maternal health concern associated with adverse outcomes for mothers and their offspring. In Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC), its burden is heightened by socioeconomic inequalities, limited prenatal care, and high obesity rates, while evidence for other determinants remains fragmented and heterogeneous. This scoping review aimed to identify, describe, and categorize existing research on the prevalence, incidence, determinants, and risk factors of GDM in LAC. We conducted a scoping review following JBI guidance and PRISMA-ScR. Embase, MEDLINE/PubMed, Web of Science, SciELO, and LILACS were searched from inception to December 2025. Eligible studies included observational studies reporting GDM prevalence, incidence, diagnostic criteria, or risk factors in LAC. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. Findings were synthesized descriptively. Fifty‑six studies from nine LAC countries were included, mainly from Brazil and Mexico. Studies were predominantly cross-sectional, cohort, and case-control designs conducted in hospital or prenatal care settings. Diagnostic approaches varied, with IADPSG (39.3%), WHO (25.0%), and ADA (16.1%) as the most frequently used criteria. GDM prevalence ranged from 3.0% to 61.0%, and incidence estimates varied substantially. The most frequently reported determinants and risk factors were advanced maternal age, overweight and obesity, family history of diabetes, previous GDM, prior macrosomia, and hypertension. Behavioral and social determinants were less frequently assessed. Variability in GDM prevalence across LAC highlights the need for standardized regional screening and prospective, population-based research. Reducing the regional GDM burden requires integrating clinical interventions targeting modifiable risk factors and improved continuity of care.

articles.title: Targeting mitochondrial quality control to disarm phytopathogenic fungi.
articles.abstract: Fungal diseases cause substantial crop losses worldwide, while increasing fungicide resistance highlights the need for new disease-control strategies. Mitochondrial quality control (MQC), comprising mitochondrial dynamics, biogenesis, proteostasis, and mitophagy, maintains mitochondrial integrity and functional capacity during infection. Evidence from phytopathogenic fungi links disruption of individual MQC mechanisms to defects in growth, stress adaptation, and pathogenicity. Here, we synthesize evidence across hemibiotrophic, vascular, and necrotrophic pathogens and across distinct stages of the infection cycle. Because mechanistic evidence is strongest in Magnaporthe oryzae, we use it as a principal reference system while highlighting conserved and lifestyle-specific requirements emerging from other fungi. This review proposes three complementary strategies for exploiting MQC vulnerabilities: targeting pathogen-specific regulatory features within conserved mitochondrial systems, exploiting interdependencies among MQC processes and mitochondrial stress responses, and targeting stage-specific mitochondrial requirements as potential intervention points. We also highlight some limitations that need resolution while considering MQC mechanisms as antifungal targets.

articles.title: Relationship between selected microRNAs, pentraxin 3 and uromodulin in pathophysiology of septic acute kidney injury.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common complication of sepsis and is associated with increased morbidity and mortality in critically ill patients. Combined assessment of serum pentraxin 3 (PTX3), uromodulin (UMOD), and circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) may improve understanding of the pathophysiology of septic AKI.

METHODS: In this study, 81 critically ill adults with sepsis were stratified into AKI and non-AKI groups, and 90 healthy volunteers served as controls. Blood samples were collected on days 1 and 4 after the diagnosis of sepsis. PTX3 and UMOD concentrations were measured by ELISA, and miRNA expression was assessed by RT-qPCR. Seven miRNAs were validated, and their target genes associations were analyzed using TargetScanHuman8.0.

RESULTS: PTX3 and UMOD distinguished healthy controls from septic patients, whereas only PTX3 differentiated patients with AKI from non-AKI. Baseline PTX3 and procalcitonin were independently associated with AKI on days 1 and 4. In AKI group, four analyzed miRNAs showed significant intercorrelations on day 1; however, these weakened by day 4 with changes in renal function and sepsis. Selected miRNAs were interpreted in the context of predicted target genes and pathways related to NF-κB signaling, renal cell apoptosis, and autophagy/mitophagy, rather than as direct causal regulators demonstrated in this study.

CONCLUSIONS: PTX3, UMOD, and selected miRNAs provide complementary information on septic AKI and support a multifactorial concept of its pathophysiology.The study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (ID: NCT06498336) on May 2, 2024 to March 31, 2026.

articles.title: Review of the 10-year kidney biopsy experience of the Szeged Nephrology and Hypertension Center: a comparison of pre-biopsy clinical and biopsy-proven histological diagnoses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kidney biopsy is essential for diagnosing kidney diseases, , but histological findings may differ from pre-biopsy clinical diagnoses.

METHODS: We retrospectively analysed 451 first percutaneous native kidney biopsies performed at the Szeged Nephrology and Hypertension Center between January 1, 2007, and December 31, 2016. Pre-biopsy clinical diagnoses were available for 303 patients.

RESULTS: Mean patient age was 48.7±15 years. Nephrotic syndrome was the most common biopsy indication (38.8%). The most frequent histological diagnoses were membranous glomerulonephritis (16.7%), IgA nephropathy (11.5%), and focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS; 10.9%). Among patients with available pre-biopsy diagnoses, at least one clinical diagnosis matched the histological findings in 71.9%, while no concordance was found in 28.1%. Clinical suspicion was more frequent than histological confirmation for both FSGS (35.3% vs. 11.8%) and diabetic nephropathy (12.2% vs. 7.5%). Minor and major complications occurred in 21.7% and 2.9% of cases, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Close communication between nephrologists and pathologists may help refine pre-biopsy clinical diagnoses and support interpretation of histological findings in the appropriate clinical context.

articles.title: Strengthening ties in the face of trauma: a study protocol for a naturalistic observation study of parent-child communication in refugee families' daily lives.
articles.abstract: Introduction: Parental mental health problems are a well-established risk factor for children's mental health, and the quality of parent-child communication is a suggested mechanism in the intergenerational transmission. Many refugees have been exposed to potentially traumatic events, which puts children growing up in forcibly displaced families especially at-risk. How refugee parents and their children communicate in everyday life remains, however, poorly understood. This protocol describes a pilot study with a multimethod case-series design that aims to investigate parent-child communication in refugee families affected by parental trauma, and link it to parental and child mental health and the quality of the parent-child relationship.Methods: We will recruit 10 refugee families with symptoms of posttraumatic stress in at least one parent. Data collection involves self-report measures and naturalistic observations of parent-child interactions with the Electronically Activated Recorder (EAR) on two consecutive days. The main analyses comprise reflexive thematic analysis complemented by coding of parental tone and word use, and descriptive statistics. Participating families will be involved in interpreting the findings.Discussion: With its combination of naturalistic observation and self-report in a hard-to-reach population, this study aims to advance our understanding of communication and mental health in trauma-affected forcibly displaced families. Findings are intended to inform a larger follow-up study planned in a participatory approach.

articles.title: A meta-analysis on the prevalence of parents' complicated grief and post-traumatic stress disorder following perinatal loss in East and Southeast Asia.
articles.abstract: Background: Previous reviews have reported high prevalence estimates of complicated grief (CG) and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) among parents following perinatal loss. However, evidence has predominantly focused on Western populations, leaving parents in East and Southeast Asia underexamined.Objective: This meta-analysis aims to estimate the prevalence of CG and PTSD among parents experiencing perinatal loss in East and Southeast Asia while identifying potential moderators, including types of loss, parental roles, trimester of loss, maternal age, marital status, and country.Method: This protocol was prepared based on the PRISMA-P 2015 Statement. PubMed, PsycINFO, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched using six search strings for peer-reviewed studies and preprints reporting parents' CG at 6 and/or 12 months or PTSD at least 1 month following perinatal loss. Searches will be supplemented manually via Google Scholar and key references. Two authors independently screened records and full texts, with study selection documented using the PRISMA flowchart. The quality of included studies will be assessed using appropriate Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tools. Random-effects meta-analyses will be performed to calculate pooled prevalence estimates for CG and PTSD. Subgroup analyses for parental roles, different types of perinatal loss, trimester of loss, maternal age, marital status, and country will also be conducted. Heterogeneity will be assessed by Cochran's Q and I2. Funnel plots, Egger's regression test, and Begg's correlation test will be used to assess publication bias.Results: Results will be reported following the completion of the meta-analysis.Conclusion: The study will provide a comprehensive view of the prevalence of CG and PTSD among parents following perinatal loss in East and Southeast Asia. Implications for researchers and practitioners will be provided. However, pooled prevalence may be inflated owing to publication bias, limited cultural validity, inconsistency in measurements, and the conceptualization of CG in this study.

articles.title: Activation of IgG antibody and mucosal T cell responses to MERS-CoV in human nasopharynx-associated lymphoid tissue by a ChAdOx1 vectored vaccine candidate and inactivated MERS-CoV.
articles.abstract: Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) causes serious infection in humans with up to 40% mortality. As MERS-CoV infects humans via nasopharyngeal mucosa, local mucosal immunization may provide an effective vaccination strategy. Nasopharynx-associated lymphoid tissues (NALT, comprising adenotonsillar tissues) are immune induction sites for intranasal vaccines. We studied the capacity of a viral vectored MERS candidate vaccine (ChAdOx1 MERS) and inactivated MERS-CoV in activating cellular and antibody responses in the NALT. Mononuclear cells isolated from adenotonsillar tissues from children and adults were stimulated with ChAdOx1 MERS and heat- or radiation-inactivated MERS-CoV, followed by analysis of anti-MERS IgG antibody and cytokines (IFNγ and TNFα) in cell culture supernatants by ELISA. CD4+ and CD8+ T cell responses, including proliferation and expression of cytokines and cytotoxic molecules were evaluated by flow cytometry. ChAdOx1 MERS induced marked spike-specific anti-MERS IgG antibody responses, which were significantly stronger than those induced by inactivated MERS-CoV. ChAdOx1 MERS also activated higher CD4+ and CD8+ T cell proliferative responses, cytokine expression (IFNγ, TNFα) by CD4+ T cells and cytotoxic perforin and granzyme B expression by CD8+ T cells than by inactivated MERS-CoV. Both antibody and T cell responses were shown stronger in adults than in children. There was a positive correlation between CD4+ T cell proliferation and the antibody response. Human NALT offers an efficient immune induction site for Spike-specific anti-MERS antibody and T cell response. Viral vectored ChAdOx1 MERS induces marked antibody and T cell responses in the NALT, supporting its potential as a mucosal (e.g. intranasal) vaccine against MERS.

articles.title: Barriers and facilitators to HPV vaccination among adult men: A systematic review and qualitative meta-synthesis.
articles.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is widespread and a leading cause of preventable cancers, yet HPV vaccination uptake among adult men remains suboptimal. Qualitative evidence on multilevel determinants of men's vaccination decisions and healthcare responses remains limited. This qualitative meta-synthesis aimed to synthesize barriers and facilitators to HPV vaccination among adult men guided by the Social Ecological Model (SEM), and to explore how vaccination-related health needs are reflected in healthcare resources and translated into service utilization using a health service evaluation framework informed by WHO health service concepts. Ten electronic databases, including PubMed, Embase, and PsycINFO, were searched from inception to December 2025 using controlled vocabulary and free-text terms. Ten studies across four countries were included. The evidence base was concentrated among sexual minority men, sex workers, and healthcare-engaged men, with fewer studies among general male populations; six of the ten studies were conducted in the United States, limiting generalizability to adult men more broadly. Thematic synthesis followed Thomas and Harden's approach, with findings organized across five SEM levels. Key barriers included gendered perceptions of HPV, low perceived susceptibility, stigma and disclosure concerns, provider communication failures, economic constraints, and structural access challenges. Facilitators included provider recommendation, supportive relationships, integrated care pathways, and health information access. Health service evaluation identified gaps between needs, resources, and utilization, particularly outside preventive care. These findings highlight that improving HPV vaccination among adult men requires multilevel behavioral strategies alongside healthcare system improvements that better recognize and respond to men's vaccination needs.

articles.title: How lipoproteins shape smooth muscle plasticity and cell state trajectories in atherosclerosis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Arterial smooth muscle cells (SMCs) can develop inflammatory and lipid-laden phenotypes during atherogenesis. The SMC lineage also undergoes extensive state transitions that lead to fibromyocyte and osteochondrogenic phenotypes with distinct effects on plaque biology. We review emerging evidence that different lipoprotein populations shape SMC plasticity and cell state trajectories.

RECENT FINDINGS: Lowering apolipoprotein B (APOB)-containing lipoproteins (triglyceride-rich lipoproteins, remnant lipoproteins, and LDL) suppresses inflammatory programs in SMCs and selectively depletes fibromyocytes and chondromyocytes while preserving fibrous cap SMCs, whereas aggregated LDL induces a fibromyocyte-derived SMC lipid-laden program. HDL can suppress the SMC lipid-laden transcriptomic program in a mouse model of lesion regression. High levels of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins and their remnants in mouse models of diabetes increase arterial free cholesterol accumulation and broad SMC inflammatory/stress programs that are largely prevented by silencing hepatic apolipoprotein C3 (APOC3). Importantly, specific smooth muscle-lineage cells can be targeted by immunotherapy in a mouse model, reducing atherosclerosis.

SUMMARY: Lipoproteins modulate SMC inflammatory and lipid-laden phenotypes and shape cell state trajectories, linking lipoprotein metabolism to SMC remodeling and potential opportunities for smooth muscle-lineage-directed imaging and therapy. Future research is needed to address the clinical implications of this new area of research.

articles.title: The pen-and-paper tube figures mental rotation task for patients with trauma-related disorders: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Introduction: Most patients with trauma-related disorders have intrusive memories (IMs) of trauma. Recently a new type of digital treatment (imagery-competing task intervention; ICTI) has been shown to reduce the rate of IMs and other symptoms. Here we examine a novel pen-and-paper ICTI called 'Tube figures' suitable for settings without digital resources.Methods and analysis: Forty patients with trauma-related disorders participated in a mono-centre, single-blind randomized controlled trial with two parallel arms (Intervention: Tube figures ICTI vs. Control: Wikipedia). Participants selected one IM to monitor daily for four weeks. After two weeks, a single intervention or control session was administered for the monitored IM. Primary outcome was the frequency of the IM monitored per week for the two weeks following the intervention. A mixed Poisson regression was fitted with intervention and study phase (baseline/pre- and post-intervention) as fixed effects and a random effect for patient. Severity of symptoms at study start and two weeks after randomization was assessed with the PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5).Results: The frequency of the monitored IM per week reduced significantly more after the intervention versus control (22% versus 2% reduction in the two weeks post-intervention compared to two weeks pre-intervention, respectively). PCL-5 score reduced significantly more after intervention (53-38) than control (55-47).Discussion: This single-session pen-and-paper Tube figures ICTI reduced IM frequency and trauma-related symptoms, consistent with digital ICTI studies. Limitations include the reliance on self-report measures and only having data for the two weeks after intervention. Future studies should explore the different components of the intervention and test practical aspects that could promote its use in low-resource settings.

articles.title: Economic evaluation and healthcare resource utilization in heart transplant in adults with congenital heart disease.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review is timely and relevant because the population of adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) in the United States continues to grow, and as more individuals survive into adulthood, heart failure has become the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in this population. There is a growing need to understand the economic impact of healthcare utilization and financial burden for patients with ACHD and end-stage heart failure.

RECENT FINDINGS: Recent literature highlights that adults with complex congenital heart disease face disproportionately high financial burden with lifetime direct and indirect costs reaching up to $3.35 million per patient. These costs include frequent hospitalizations, surgeries, diagnostic testing, and ongoing medical care, as well as lost income for patients and families. The cost burden increases further towards the end of life, and ACHD patients with heart failure experience longer hospital stays, and higher healthcare costs compared to non-ACHD populations. Early referrals can mitigate some of the increasing cost by implementing multidisciplinary care strategies and timely interventions to potentially improve the trajectory of ACHD patients with heart failure.

SUMMARY: The findings underscore the need for early referral to specialized, high-volume ACHD and heart transplant centers and the development of multidisciplinary care pathways to improve outcomes and reduce costs for ACHD patients with advanced heart failure.

articles.title: The relevance of genetic disease in kidney transplantation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Genetic disease is an increasingly recognized, but undiagnosed, cause of kidney failure. This review examines how genetics informs the evaluation and management of kidney transplant candidates and recipients.

RECENT FINDINGS: Monogenic disease accounts for 10-20% of adult chronic kidney disease. In kidney transplantation cohorts, diagnostic yield increases with clinical selection, from 11% among waitlisted patients tested after excluding those with a documented genetic cause of kidney disease, to 23% in unselected kidney transplant recipients including polycystic kidney disease, to 33-54% in highly selected cohorts. Genomic testing reclassifies the cause of kidney failure in about one-third of genetically diagnosed recipients, most often correcting focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, hypertensive nephrosclerosis, or chronic kidney disease of unknown cause. Because recurrence tracks disease mechanisms rather than histology, a molecular diagnosis distinguishes nonrecurrent intrinsic kidney disease from recurrent circulating-factor and complement-mediated disease. It also identifies conditions that recur but are preventable, such as primary hyperoxaluria and adenine phosphoribosyltransferase deficiency.

SUMMARY: Genetic testing, by targeted phenotype panels, comprehensive kidney-disease panels, or exome and genome sequencing as appropriate, should be integrated to the assessment of selected kidney transplant candidates and recipients, interpreted within a multidisciplinary team, and supported by periodic reanalysis.

articles.title: The role of genetic testing in heart transplant candidates.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Inherited cardiomyopathies are increasingly recognized among patients with advanced heart failure, yet genetic testing remains substantially underutilized. This review examines the evolving clinical utility of genetic testing across advanced heart failure and transplantation and highlights opportunities to integrate genetics into routine advanced heart failure care.

RECENT FINDINGS: Pathogenic or likely pathogenic cardiomyopathy variants are identified in approximately one-third of heart transplant recipients and in up to 44% of explanted hearts from patients with idiopathic cardiomyopathy. Recent studies have linked genotype to heart failure progression, ventricular arrhythmias, and outcomes after advanced therapies, including a higher risk of right ventricular failure following left ventricular assist device implantation. Genetic diagnoses can also uncover multisystem disease relevant to transplant evaluation and posttransplant management. At the same time, the emergence of gene replacement, gene editing, and RNA-based therapies is creating new therapeutic implications for establishing a molecular diagnosis before end-stage disease.

SUMMARY: Genetic testing is becoming an increasingly actionable component of advanced heart failure care. Integrating genetics into advanced heart failure programs may improve recognition of inherited disease, individualize management, and better position patients and their families for emerging precision therapies.

articles.title: Chronic lung disease for the ENT: a pulmonary perspective.
articles.journal: Current opinion in otolaryngology & head and neck surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review aims to highlight the key chronic lung diseases relevant to ENT specialists, elucidate shared pathophysiological mechanisms, and provide practical guidance on diagnosis, perioperative considerations, and multidisciplinary management.

RECENT FINDINGS: This review focuses on the intersections between chronic lung disease and otolaryngology practice, with a particular emphasis on bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), asthma, diffuse lung disease (DLD), and suppurative lung disease. Newer therapies have been recently approved, that have continued to change disease progression and prognosis.

SUMMARY: Chronic lung diseases (CLD) represent a significant source of morbidity across all age groups, with profound implications for both lower and upper airway health. By enhancing awareness of these intersections, ENT surgeons can better support this complex and vulnerable patient population.

articles.title: A plasma proteomic frailty signature for cardiovascular risk stratification: A multi-cohort study.
articles.journal: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty predicts adverse health outcomes, but its relationship with cardiovascular disease (CVD) requires further validation across diverse populations. The value of a circulating protein signature for cardiovascular risk assessment remains uncertain.

METHODS: We examined frailty-CVD associations in the XiDu2017 cohort (n = 4323) and UK Biobank (UKB; n = 84,276) using logistic and Cox regression, respectively. XiDu longitudinal analyses included 844 participants without baseline CVD. In the UKB proteomic subset, a 20-protein frailty (PF) score was compared with clinical frailty and a model of conventional cardiovascular risk factors.

RESULTS: Each higher frailty category was associated with prevalent CVD in XiDu (adjusted odds ratio, 1.120; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.004-1.251). In UKB, frail participants had a higher CVD hazard than robust participants (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.28-1.48). For heart failure, the 5-year area under the curve (AUC) was 0.756 for PF and 0.595 for clinical frailty. Adding PF to conventional risk factors increased the optimism-corrected heart failure AUC by 0.113 (95% CI, 0.077-0.142).

CONCLUSIONS: Clinical frailty was associated with cardiovascular outcomes in both cohorts. PF showed incremental discrimination for selected outcomes, particularly heart failure. External validation and evaluation of clinical utility are needed before clinical application.

articles.title: Adiposity and glycemic patterns among adults meeting measured cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic stage 1 criteria: a multicohort study.
articles.journal: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2026 AHA/ACC/ADA/ASN guideline defines cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) stage 1 by excess or dysfunctional adiposity. Whether adiposity and glycemic patterns distinguish subsequent risk is uncertain.

METHODS: Adults aged 45-79 years meeting measured stage 1 criteria were studied in CHARLS and CHNS. Four patterns combined body mass index (BMI), waist circumference, and prediabetes. Modified Poisson models estimated risk ratios (RRs). Progression and hypertension models used censoring weights; cumulative self-reported cardiovascular disease (CVD) models used baseline-covariate imputation. The nonglycemic composite was a key secondary outcome. NHANES assessed reclassification with ancestry-appropriate thresholds and age-sex standardization. Chinese cohorts lacked albuminuria and subclinical CVD assessment.

RESULTS: In CHARLS (model n = 965), adiposity plus prediabetes was associated with metabolic progression versus prediabetes only (RR, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.18-1.61). Corresponding RRs were 1.45 (1.21-1.74) for nonglycemic progression and 1.55 (1.21-1.98) for CHNS hypertension. Among 1824 participants, concordant BMI and waist adiposity was associated with cumulative reported CVD through 2020 (RR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.23-2.71). CVD associations attenuated in complete-case models and after additional adjustment for metabolic measures. Standardized NHANES reclassification ranged from 0.8% to 9.0%.

CONCLUSIONS: Adiposity and glycemic patterns identified prognostic heterogeneity among adults meeting measured CKM stage 1 criteria, supporting joint assessment of these features.

articles.title: Twenty-five-year imaging follow-up of an untreated giant Spetzler-Martin grade V Brain arteriovenous malformation associated with cerebral infarction and epilepsy.
articles.abstract: Brain arteriovenous malformations (BAVMs) are typically associated with intracranial hemorrhage, whereas ischemic stroke associated with a high-grade BAVM is an exceptionally rare complication. We present the 25-year long-term imaging follow-up of a 39-year-old male with a giant Spetzler-Martin grade V BAVM. Initially diagnosed at age 14 via magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) due to a visual deficit, the complex lesion was managed conservatively owing to prohibitive procedural risks. Twenty-five years later, the patient presented with acute left limb weakness and recurrent adult-onset epilepsy. Current diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) mapping demonstrated chronic ischemic changes in the bilateral frontal lobes and a new acute-to-subacute infarction in the left parietal lobe. Concurrent MRA and MRI demonstrated a massive 13.5 × 6.3 cm nidus with prominent vascular flow voids and deep venous involvement. The patient received supportive medical management and antiseizure therapy. Motor function showed near-complete recovery at 3 months, although recurrent minor seizures persisted during longer-term follow-up. This 25-year imaging follow-up documents the long-term imaging follow-up of a giant, untreated Spetzler-Martin grade V BAVM and documents the occurrence of delayed ischemic complications during long-term follow-up of a giant BAVM. In extreme-risk, unruptured cases, conservative management with imaging surveillance is a carefully considered option, though it carries ongoing long-term risks.

articles.title: Assessment of Medication Regimen Complexity and Adherence in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Patients at a Tertiary Care Teaching Hospital.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Medication regimen complexity and poor adherence are major barriers to optimal management, yet limited evidence exists in Nepal. This study aimed to assess medication regimen complexity and adherence among COPD patients attending a tertiary care hospital in Nepal.

METHODS: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from November 2023 to May 2024 at a tertiary care teaching hospital in Nepal. A total of 174 COPD patients aged ≥40 years were enrolled using convenience sampling. Medication regimen complexity was assessed using the validated 65-item Medication Regimen Complexity Index (MRCI), and adherence was evaluated with the Nepali version of the Morisky Medication Adherence Scale (MMAS-8). Pearson's chi-square test and binary logistic regression were performed at a 5% level of significance to examine factors associated with medication nonadherence.

RESULTS: Of the total, 46.6% demonstrated suboptimal adherence, strongly associated with smoking (adjusted odds ratios [aOR]: 7.5; 95% CI: 2.82-19.90; p < 0.001) and alcohol use (aOR: 3.66; 95% CI: 1.578-8.49; p = 0.003). COPD regimens exhibited higher complexity (mean MRCI: 10.296 ± 5.4) than non-COPD medications (3.66 ± 3.478). High COPD MRCI (aOR: 25.8; 95% CI: 14.7-38.5; p = 0.03) and high patient-level MRCI (aOR: 15.6; 95% CI: 6.7-33.9; p < 0.001) were significant predictors of nonadherence.

CONCLUSION: COPD-specific regimens were found to be more complex, and higher regimen complexity together with lifestyle factors, such as smoking and alcohol consumption, were strong determinants of nonadherence. Simplifying regimens through fixed-dose combinations, pharmacist-led interventions, and behavioral counseling may improve medication adherence and treatment outcomes in COPD patients.

articles.title: Association Between Periodontitis and Ischemic Heart Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic heart disease (IHD) is a leading cause of global mortality. This study examined the association between periodontitis severity, graded by clinical attachment loss (CAL), and IHD in a representative sample of US adults.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2013-2014 cycle, including a full-mouth periodontal examination, of participants aged ≥30 years with complete periodontal and IHD data (n = 2807; weighted n ≈ 122,396,066). Periodontal status was classified by maximum interdental CAL, using the severity thresholds of the 2018 classification of periodontal diseases: no-or-initial-attachment loss (CAL ≤2 mm; reference), Stage II periodontitis (CAL 3-4 mm), and Stage III/IV periodontitis (CAL ≥5 mm). IHD was defined as a composite of self-reported coronary heart disease, angina, or heart attack. Weighted prevalence of IHD was computed for each periodontal group, and survey-weighted logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) for IHD, adjusting sequentially for demographic characteristics (age, sex, race/ethnicity, and family income), smoking, diabetes, hypertension, and other cardiovascular risk factors.

RESULTS: The weighted prevalence of IHD was 5.71% overall and increased across periodontal groups: 2.45% (no-or-initial-attachment loss), 4.66% (Stage II), and 8.82% (Stage III/IV) (p = 0.0004). In unadjusted models, Stage III/IV periodontitis was associated with higher odds of IHD than no-or-initial-attachment-loss (OR 3.84; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.33-11.07; p = 0.003). After full adjustment, the association was attenuated, but the point estimate remained elevated (OR 1.47; 95% CI 0.40-5.39; p = 0.05). Older age, current smoking, diabetes, hypertension, and self-reported bone loss were independent predictors of IHD.

CONCLUSION: In this nationally representative study, Stage III/IV periodontitis was associated with a higher prevalence of IHD. Although the association was attenuated after multivariable adjustment, the findings suggest a potential link, possibly mediated by shared risk factors and inflammatory pathways.

articles.title: Ambient Air Pollution and Kawasaki Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Epidemiological Evidence.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kawasaki disease (KD) is a childhood vasculitis with a multifactorial etiology involving genetic susceptibility and environmental influences. Ambient air pollution has been proposed as a potential environmental trigger, but epidemiological findings have been inconsistent across pollutants, populations, and exposure periods. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to synthesize the association between ambient air pollution and KD.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from database inception through December 29, 2024, for observational studies evaluating associations between ambient air pollutants and KD. Multivariable-adjusted estimates were preferentially used for quantitative synthesis. Hazard ratios and odds ratios were interpreted as relative risks, and estimates were standardized to a 10 µg/m3 increase in pollutant concentration where applicable. Random-effects models were used to obtain pooled relative risks, with heterogeneity assessed using I 2 statistics.

RESULTS: Thirteen studies met the inclusion criteria. The studies included diverse epidemiological designs and were predominantly conducted in Asian populations, with additional studies from North America and Italy. Across the quantitative synthesis, no statistically significant association was observed between a standardized 10 µg/m3 increase in individual pollutants and KD occurrence. The pooled relative risks were 1.00 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.985-1.016) for PM2.5, 1.00 (95% CI, 0.983-1.022) for PM10, 1.008 (95% CI, 0.966-1.051) for SO2, 0.99 (95% CI, 0.989-1.009) for NO2, and 1.013 (95% CI, 0.981-1.046) for O3 and CO. For PM2.5, between-study heterogeneity was moderate (I 2 = 43.8%), whereas Egger's test showed no evidence of significant publication bias (p = 0.2703).
