articles.title: Effectiveness of incretin receptor agonists compared to metreleptin in partial lipodystrophy: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Lipodystrophy syndromes are rare disorders of abnormal fat distribution and metabolic disease. The only approved therapy for generalized lipodystrophy is recombinant leptin (metreleptin), which is not approved for partial lipodystrophy. Recent data suggest efficacy of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) dual agonists (collectively referred to as incretins) to treat complications of lipodystrophy.

OBJECTIVE: To compare metabolic outcomes of incretin therapies vs metreleptin in partial lipodystrophy.

DESIGN: Retrospective review of patients who received metreleptin as part of a clinical trial and incretins during routine care under a natural history study.

SETTING: NIH Clinical Center.

PATIENTS: Twelve female patients with partial lipodystrophy, aged 16-85 years. All but 1 patient had diabetes.

INTERVENTION: Eleven patients with partial lipodystrophy were treated with metreleptin (mean duration 104 ± 38 months) before switching to incretin therapy (duration 32 ± 13 months). A twelfth patient took metreleptin and an incretin concurrently.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Outcome measures included hemoglobin A1c, insulin dose, Matsuda index, insulinogenic index, disposition index, fasting glucose and insulin, homeostatic model of beta cell function (HOMA-B), homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), weight, lipids, liver elastography, and liver steatosis.

RESULTS: Hemoglobin A1c was significantly lower during incretin vs metreleptin treatment (mean difference -1.1 ± 0.4%, range -4.75% to -0.1%, P = .005), associated with modest weight reduction (mean difference -1.5 ± 3.9 kg, range -10.4 to 3 kg, P = .046). Most other metabolic parameters did not differ significantly between treatment periods.

CONCLUSION: In patients with partial lipodystrophy, incretins may provide better diabetes control than metreleptin, with comparable control of other metabolic parameters.

articles.title: Subarachnoid hemorrhage caused by a paradoxical septic embolism from pacemaker lead infection: A case report.
articles.abstract: Subarachnoid hemorrhage resulting from a paradoxical septic embolism associated with right-sided cardiac infection has not been previously reported. An 85-year-old woman with a history of aortic valve replacement and right ventricular pacemaker implantation 7 years earlier presented with sudden-onset left upper limb weakness and a small subarachnoid hemorrhage over the right frontal convexity. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a small aneurysm in the distal right middle cerebral artery. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed vegetation on the right ventricular pacemaker lead, and blood cultures showed growth of Listeria monocytogenes. Transesophageal echocardiography revealed a patent foramen ovale without evidence of infection in the left cardiac chambers or bioprosthetic aortic valve. The patient was diagnosed with subarachnoid hemorrhage due to the rupture of an infectious intracranial aneurysm, presumably caused by a paradoxical septic embolism originating from the pacemaker lead vegetation. After antibiotic therapy, follow-up transthoracic echocardiography revealed complete resolution of the lead vegetation. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of subarachnoid hemorrhage resulting from a presumed paradoxical septic embolism associated with a pacemaker lead infection.

articles.title: Long non-coding RNAs in monocyte/macrophage-mediated immune dysregulation and organ injury in sepsis: mechanistic insights and therapeutic potential.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening organ dysfunction characterized by a dysregulated host response that oscillates between hyperinflammation and immunosuppression. Monocytes and macrophages are pivotal players in the immunopathogenesis of sepsis, driving both the initial cytokine storm and the subsequent state of immunosuppression. There remains an urgent need for new therapeutic approaches that effectively target monocytes and macrophages. As some of the most promising targets for RNA therapeutics (RNATx), which regulate molecular networks in a cell type-restricted manner, long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are emerging as critical regulators of monocyte and macrophage functions, influencing their polarization and alterations during sepsis. This review systematically synthesizes current knowledge on how lncRNAs regulate the two immune states of sepsis-hyperinflammation and immunosuppression-in these monocytes and macrophages. We also examine the organ-specific effects of lncRNA-mediated macrophage dysfunction in sepsis-induced lung, liver, kidney, cardiac, and brain injury. By clarifying the molecular mechanisms of lncRNA action, we discuss their potential as therapeutic targets, providing insight into novel precision medicine strategies for sepsis management.

articles.title: Helicobacter pylori, Betel Quid Chewing, and Endoscopic Pathology in Dyspeptic Patients: A Cross-Sectional Analytical Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection and betel quid (BQ) chewing are both highly prevalent in South Asia and are independently implicated in upper gastrointestinal mucosal injury, yet their joint contribution to endoscopic pathology in dyspeptic patients is poorly characterised. We aimed to describe the exposure profile of dyspeptic patients with and without endoscopic pathology, quantify the individual and joint associations of H. pylori and BQ use with pathology and explore trends with BQ exposure.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional analytical study, 211 consecutive dyspeptic patients attending a tertiary gastroenterology department were classified as having endoscopic pathology (Group A, n = 141) or a normal endoscopic examination (Group B, n = 70). H. pylori status, BQ exposure (including a cumulative 'BQ-Quid-Years' index), and body mass index (BMI) were recorded, and multivariable logistic regression, additive-interaction analysis and dose-response modelling were performed.

RESULTS: Group A patients were older (median 40 vs. 31 years, p = 0.009) and more often male (58.2% vs. 41.4%, p = 0.039) than Group B. Pathology prevalence rose stepwise from 52.2% in patients negative for both H. pylori and BQ use to 72.5% in patients positive for both (trend p = 0.076). The relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI) showed no clear evidence of departure from additivity (-0.16, 95% confidence interval [CI] -1.14 to 0.39), although the wide interval does not exclude synergistic or sub-additive effects. After multivariable adjustment, male sex (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 3.01, 95% CI 1.50-6.04, p = 0.002) and, more modestly, age (aOR 1.02, 95% CI 1.00-1.05, p = 0.039) were independently associated with pathology; H. pylori (aOR 1.38, p = 0.353) and BQ use (aOR 1.66, p = 0.219) showed positive but non-significant associations.

CONCLUSIONS: Male sex was the most robust, independently associated correlate of endoscopic pathology in dyspeptic patients, and age showed a more modest, independent association.

articles.title: Serial metabolic profiling and liver transplantation in concurrent maple syrup urine disease and type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Maple syrup urine disease (MSUD) and type 1 diabetes (T1D) require careful attention to dietary composition and predispose to ketoacidosis. The co-occurrence of these metabolic disorders therefore compounds these challenges. Here, we present a 29-year-old man with prenatally diagnosed MSUD and childhood-onset T1D who, despite extreme metabolic vulnerability, did well until his mid-20s, when he was admitted to the hospital 8 times for metabolic decompensation, with the latter 7 times occurring within a 12-month period. Most laboratory evaluations were suggestive of MSUD crisis rather than diabetic ketoacidosis. Ultimately, the patient underwent liver transplantation for definitive treatment of MSUD. The case illustrates the complexity of comanaging T1D with an inborn error of metabolism requiring dietary modification that challenges glycemic management.

articles.title: Delayed recognition of primary thyroid lymphoma with progressive thyroid enlargement and cardiopulmonary symptoms.
articles.abstract: Primary thyroid lymphoma (PTL) is a rare thyroid malignancy that may present with respiratory symptoms overlapping with cardiopulmonary disease, contributing to delayed diagnosis. We report a 78-year-old woman with chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, heart failure, and prior lung cancer whose worsening dyspnea was repeatedly attributed to underlying cardiopulmonary conditions. She subsequently developed dysphonia and dysphagia with a rapidly enlarging thyroid mass requiring tracheostomy for airway protection. Prior computed tomography imaging obtained during multiple evaluations for cardiopulmonary symptoms incidentally demonstrated subtle thyroid enlargement with progressive interval growth on retrospective review. Core biopsy confirmed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, and staging established stage IIIE disease. Given her age and comorbidities, a dose-reduced regimen of rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone was initiated. Despite treatment, her condition deteriorated rapidly, and she died shortly thereafter. This case underscores how overlapping comorbidities can obscure PTL presentation until advanced airway compromise develops. In patients with persistent respiratory symptoms despite appropriate cardiopulmonary management, careful review of prior imaging is critical because subtle thyroid enlargement may otherwise be overlooked.

articles.title: Rethinking hypertension in the brain: from blood pressure control to temporal blood pressure stability-a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Temporal blood pressure variability (BPV) may contribute to cerebrovascular injury beyond mean blood pressure (BP), yet the mechanisms linking antihypertensive treatment patterns to temporal BP instability remain incompletely understood. This scoping review synthesised evidence linking treatment instability, pharmacodynamic determinants of BP control, temporal BPV, and cerebrovascular vulnerability.

METHODS: PubMed and Embase were searched for studies evaluating antihypertensive medication adherence, pharmacodynamic persistence, BPV, and cerebrovascular outcomes. Data were charted using a standardised form and synthesised narratively according to predefined thematic domains.

RESULTS: The available evidence suggests that inconsistent antihypertensive exposure and reduced pharmacodynamic persistence may contribute to increased temporal BPV. Generally BP fluctuations are associated with cerebral small vessel disease, white matter injury, vascular cognitive impairment, and other manifestations of cerebrovascular vulnerability independent of mean BP. This review investigates the relationship between treatment instability, pharmacodynamic determinants, and temporal BPV and proposes a hypothesis-generating conceptual framework to facilitate future individualised risk stratification and guide prospective investigation.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports expanding hypertension management beyond achieving mean BP targets to include optimisation of temporal BP stability. Recognising treatment persistence and pharmacodynamic coverage as determinants of BP stability provides a clinically relevant framework for improving cerebrovascular protection and individualised risk assessment. These findings support consideration of temporal BP stability as a potential complementary dimension of hypertension management for preventing chronic cerebrovascular injury and vascular cognitive dysfunction.

articles.title: Functional involvement of AMPK in Lumpy skin disease virus replication and associated cellular stress responses.
articles.abstract: Lumpy skin disease virus (LSDV) infection induces extensive cellular stress responses and metabolic reprogramming in host cells. However, the regulatory mechanisms linking these changes to viral replication remain unclear. In this study, MAC-T cells were used as an in vitro infection model to investigate LSDV-induced cellular stress responses and their impact on viral replication. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that LSDV infection activated pathways associated with energy stress, oxidative stress, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, suggesting disruption of cellular energy homeostasis and redox balance. Transmission electron microscopy further demonstrated mitochondrial structural damage in infected cells. Subsequent analyses showed that the ATP/AMP ratio and lactate metabolism decreased during infection, accompanied by elevated mitochondrial calcium levels and excessive reactive oxygen species accumulation. Mechanistically, LSDV infection activated the PERK-eIF2α-ATF4-CHOP and IRE1α-JNK-BECN1 pathways, indicating induction of ER stress-related signaling. Given the role of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) as a central metabolic stress sensor, we further examined its function during LSDV infection. LSDV infection enhanced AMPK activation, as evidenced by increased phosphorylation of Thr172. Inhibition of energy stress, oxidative stress, or ER stress reduced AMPK phosphorylation to varying degrees, suggesting that multiple stress responses collectively contribute to AMPK activation. Furthermore, AMPK inhibition impaired LSDV replication, while downstream analysis revealed that AMPK activation promotes autophagosome formation. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that LSDV-induced cellular stress responses activate AMPK signaling to facilitate viral replication, providing new insights into host metabolic regulation and identifying AMPK as a potential antiviral target.

articles.title: Obstetric pharmacometabolomics.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pregnancy-related physiologic and metabolic changes influence drug exposure and response. Yet therapeutic decisions often lack individualized biologic guidance. Obstetric pharmacometabolomics uses endogenous metabolic signatures to investigate and potentially predict and monitor drug response in pregnancy.

AREAS COVERED: PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar were searched from inception through October 12, 2026, using terms related to metabolomics, pharmacometabolomics, medication exposure, treatment response, maternal-placental-fetal metabolism, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and obstetric medications. Human pregnancy studies, longitudinal investigations, drug-perturbation experiments, and mechanistic preclinical studies were prioritized. This review examines pregnancy-specific metabolic adaptations, analytical approaches, and potential applications involving aspirin, antihypertensives, antidiabetic therapies, antiretrovirals, antimicrobials, corticosteroids, and psychiatric medications. It also considers pharmacometabolic approaches to preeclampsia, gestational diabetes mellitus, preterm birth, fetal growth disorders, obesity, and HIV-associated pregnancy.

EXPERT OPINION: Obstetric pharmacometabolomics offers a promising framework for individualized therapeutics, but clinical implementation requires longitudinal studies, standardized biospecimen collection, rigorous exposure assessment, validated biomarkers, and diverse populations. Integration with pharmacogenomics, pharmacomicrobiomics, pharmacoproteomics, and model-informed drug development can improve therapeutic precision, provided that clinical utility is demonstrated.

articles.title: Cervicovaginal microbiome modulates HPV genotype-specific clearance/persistence: role of bacterial dysbiosis in cervical carcinogenesis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study focuses on the distinct epidemiological features of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) genotypes in Asian populations: HPV52/56/58 show uniquely high prevalence and strong correlation with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, but their detection rates drop sharply in invasive cervical cancer, a pattern clearly different from the persistent dominance of HPV16/18 throughout malignant progression.

METHODS: To further elucidate the potential host-microbe interactions underlying these epidemiological observations, we integrated a 16S rRNA-sequenced cross-sectional discovery cohort and an independent longitudinal validation cohort from a Chinese population, with strict experimental quality control throughout the workflow.

RESULT: The preliminary analytical results demonstrate that a Lactobacillus-dominant cervicovaginal microbiome (CVM) is significantly and positively associated with HPV viral clearance, while enriched abundance of Gardnerella, Saccharofermentans and Atopobium exhibits a robust correlation with persistent HPV52/56/58 infection. Three undercharacterized microbial taxa-Chryseobacterium, Sphingobacterium and Enhydrobacter are closely linked to sustained HPV16/18 prevalence across advanced disease stages, and show negative correlation with the above obligate anaerobes, which aligns with the sharp decline of HPV52/56/58 in tumor tissues. A hormone-linked Chryseobacterium enrichment were also identified, a taxon with previously reported progesterone-degrading functional properties.

CONCLUSION: While further longitudinal studies are required to establish causal relationships, our results indicate that CVM dysbiosis may modulate the natural history of these high-burden HPV genotypes, and provide a foundational rationale for subsequent development of genotype-specific, microbiota-targeted cervical disease intervention strategies.

articles.title: Emodin ameliorates diabetic cardiomyopathy by regulating mitochondrial dynamics of fission and fusion and ferroptosis through the AHR‑Nrf2 pathway.
articles.abstract: Emodin, a natural anthraquinone with known antioxidant properties, has not been fully investigated in diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM), a condition marked by oxidative stress, ferroptosis and metabolic disturbance, and lacking specific therapies. A DCM model was induced by streptozotocin and a high‑fat diet. Cardiac function after emodin treatment was assessed via echocardiography, while myocardial injury, fibrosis and myocardial iron concentration were evaluated histologically. Mitochondrial fission‑fusion dynamics were examined using transmission electron microscopy and confocal imaging. In vitro functional rescue experiments using Ferrostatin‑1 and aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) knockdown via small interfering RNA or AAV9 was performed to determine its role in emodin‑regulated ferroptosis, lipid peroxidation, mitochondrial dynamics and Nrf2 signaling. Emodin improved left ventricular systolic function, attenuated metabolic disorders, reduced myocardial iron concentration and fibrosis, and suppressed excessive mitochondrial fission and lipid peroxidation in DCM mice. These effects were largely reversed by AHR knockdown. Mechanistically, emodin promoted Nrf2 nuclear translocation and upregulated antioxidant molecules, while AHR silencing abrogated these protective effects, thereby exacerbating ferroptosis and mitochondrial dynamic imbalance. In conclusion, emodin protects against high glucose‑induced cardiac injury and improves mitochondrial function by limiting ferroptosis and restoring mitochondrial fission‑fusion homeostasis, effects that are mediated through the AHR‑Nrf2 pathway. These findings suggest emodin and the AHR‑Nrf2 axis as potential therapeutic targets for DCM.

articles.title: Elabela in pregnancy: Physiology, associated disorders and translational perspectives (Review).
articles.abstract: Elabela (ELA) has emerged as a critical regulator of reproductive success, signaling through the cognate apelin receptor (APJ) (encoded by the APLNR gene) to orchestrate embryonic development and placental function. The present narrative review summarizes evidence spanning from molecular mechanisms to clinical phenotypes, evaluating the role of ELA in both physiological pregnancy and major complications, including preeclampsia, fetal growth restriction and gestational diabetes, as well as emerging associations with placental disorders and early pregnancy loss. The present review addresses three key challenges: i) The receptor paradox in APJ‑low or APJ‑negative contexts; ii) inconsistencies among clinical ELA measurements; and iii) the need to distinguish direct ELA evidence from inference drawn from apelin studies. Current findings position ELA as a candidate biomarker and experimental therapeutic target; however, its clinical utility remains unproven due to pre‑analytical variability across sample types (plasma vs. serum), inconsistencies between detection platforms (ELISA vs. immunohistochemistry), and biological heterogeneity across specific disease subtypes (such as preeclampsia and heart failure). Future work should focus on defining receptor‑ and isoform‑specific signaling, standardizing ELA measurement and establishing pharmacokinetics, dose‑response relationships, delivery strategies and maternal‑fetal safety.

articles.title: Roles of TRIM proteins in cardiovascular diseases: From pathogenesis to therapeutic targeting (Review).
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are driven by sustained mechanical stress, metabolic derangement, inflammation and oxidative injury, which progressively disrupt cellular homeostasis within the heart and vasculature. Although current therapeutic strategies have substantially improved clinical outcomes, most interventions primarily target downstream pathological manifestations rather than upstream regulatory mechanisms that determine stress adaptation and tissue remodeling. Tripartite motif (TRIM) proteins constitute a large family of E3 ubiquitin ligases characterized by a highly conserved RBCC domain architecture and diversified C‑terminal regions. By catalyzing distinct ubiquitin chain topologies and functioning as molecular scaffolds, TRIM proteins broadly regulate protein turnover, inflammatory signaling, metabolic adaptation and cell fate determination. Emerging evidence identifies TRIM proteins as context‑dependent regulators whose biological effects are shaped by cell type, disease stage and microenvironmental conditions. Multiple TRIM family members have been linked to a wide spectrum of cardiovascular diseases, including atherosclerosis, vascular calcification, myocardial infarction, cardiac hypertrophy and metabolic cardiomyopathy. At the cellular level, TRIM proteins influence disease initiation and progression by modulating endothelial dysfunction, vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic remodeling, cardiomyocyte survival and metabolic homeostasis, fibroblast activation and immune‑inflammatory responses. The present review summarized the biochemical characteristics and cell‑specific functions of TRIM proteins and delineates their mechanistic roles in cardiovascular pathogenesis. In addition, it discussed their emerging potential as diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets, highlighting both translational opportunities and context‑dependent challenges.

articles.title: Macrophage polarization reprogramming by resveratrol: A novel mechanism for protecting the intestinal mucosal barrier in sepsis (Review).
articles.abstract: Sepsis is characterized by a life‑threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection. A key clinical feature of sepsis is disruption of the intestinal mucosal barrier, which not only increases intestinal permeability but also facilitates the translocation of bacteria and toxins, thereby exacerbating systemic inflammatory responses. M1/M2 macrophage polarization imbalance as an important contributor to sepsis‑induced intestinal mucosal injury. M1 macrophages promote tissue damage primarily through proinflammatory mechanisms during sepsis, whereas M2 macrophages contribute to tissue repair and inflammation resolution through anti‑inflammatory responses. However, dysregulated M1/M2 macrophage polarization during sepsis may aggravate intestinal inflammation and impair barrier function. Resveratrol, a natural plant compound, has demonstrated anti‑inflammatory, antioxidant and immunomodulatory properties and has been reported to alleviate various pathological conditions, including sepsis‑induced intestinal mucosal barrier dysfunction. Resveratrol may mitigate the inflammatory environment in sepsis and promote intestinal mucosal barrier repair through modulation of macrophage polarization. However, most current evidence is derived from experimental studies and further investigation is required to clarify its clinical applicability. The present review aimed to comprehensively examine the mechanisms underlying sepsis‑induced intestinal mucosal barrier damage and its association with M1/M2 macrophage polarization and to explore the potential role of resveratrol in regulating macrophage polarization and alleviating sepsis‑associated intestinal injury. By synthesizing current research, the present review identified critical gaps in knowledge and discusses future directions for understanding the role of resveratrol‑mediated immunomodulation in sepsis‑associated intestinal barrier dysfunction.

articles.title: Fatty acid‑binding proteins at the inflammation‑cancer interface: Isoform‑specific metabolic‑immune mechanisms and therapeutic implications (Review).
articles.abstract: Fatty acid‑binding proteins (FABPs) comprise ten mammalian isoforms (FABP1‑FABP9 and FABP12), each a small intracellular lipid chaperone traditionally viewed as a mediator of fatty acid uptake, trafficking and metabolic partitioning. Evidence from metabolic disease, immunology and oncology indicates that selected FABP isoforms also regulate inflammatory signaling, immune‑cell metabolism and tumor‑stromal crosstalk. Prior reviews have mainly emphasized single isoforms of FABPs or single disease categories. The present narrative review organized FABP biology as a context‑specific evidence map across the inflammation‑cancer interface, in which each principal claim is reported together with the experimental system, with the outcome and limits of extrapolation described. The main mechanistic focus was FABP4, FABP5 and FABP7. The structural determinants of isoform specificity, ligand routing to nuclear receptors and the non‑classical secretion of FABP4 as a circulating adipokine were summarized. The evidence supports a model in which FABPs may contribute to, rather than fully explain, the progression from metabolic stress to chronic low‑grade inflammation, premalignant remodeling and the establishment of the tumor microenvironment. In the present model, FABP4 links adipocytes, macrophages, endothelial cells and tumor cells through fatty acid shuttling and inflammasome/cytokine signaling; FABP5 connects retinoic acid and peroxisome proliferator‑activated receptor β/δ signaling with tumor‑cell growth and T helper/regulatory T‑cell balance; and FABP7 regulates neural‑lineage tumor plasticity through ligand‑dependent retinoid X receptor α signaling. In addition, translational evidence was stratified into clinically observed biomarkers, preclinical therapeutic targets and conceptual future technologies. Particular attention was paid to biomarker confounding by obesity, diabetes, age and sex, and to the therapeutic paradox in which FABP5 inhibition may suppress T helper 17 cell‑driven inflammation while enhancing regulatory T‑cell‑mediated immunosuppression in cancer. This synthesis provides a restrained conceptual framework for stage‑, isoform‑ and cell‑type‑specific FABP research.

articles.title: MEX3B leads to aberrant expression of VCAN, aggravating the thoracic aortic dissection by contributing to the phenotype transformation of VSMCs.
articles.abstract: Thoracic aortic dissection (TAD) is a lethal condition due to the risk of aortic rupture and malperfusion of arterial branches. Currently, effective treatments are unavailable due to the unclear pathogenic mechanisms; therefore, it is essential to explore the underlying mechanisms of TAD to find novel therapeutic targets. The present study aimed to explore the effects of Mex3 RNA‑binding family member B (MEX3B) on TAD pathogenesis. A murine model of TAD was established with β‑aminopropionitrile monofumarate and angiotensin II. Hematoxylin and eosin and elastic Van Gieson staining were performed to assess the TAD formation and fragmentation of elastic fibers. Echocardiography was applied to measure the diameter of thoracic aorta. RT‑qPCR, western blot, and immunohistochemistry were employed to detect the expression of phenotypic transformation markers of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). mRNA sequencing was performed to further explore the downstream factors of MEX3B. MEX3B was upregulated following TAD induction. Knockdown of MEX3B alleviated TAD formation, as evidenced by decreased diameter and hematomas of thoracic aorta, as well as the enhanced integrity of the aortic structure and decreased thrombi in the false lumens. Loss of MEX3B mitigated the TAD‑induced depletion and fragmentation of elastic fibers. In vitro, small interfering RNA pool‑mediated MEX3B downregulation triggered VSMC switching from a synthetic towards a contractile phenotype. High‑throughput transcriptomics demonstrated that the MEX3B knockdown reduced the expression of versican (VCAN). MEX3B potentiated VCAN mRNA stability by binding to its 3'untranslated region. VCAN downregulation induced a contractile phenotype of VSMCs. In conclusion, the loss of MEX3B protected against TAD, potentially via its contribution to VSMC phenotype switching, which may be associated with the downregulation of VCAN. The present study preliminarily demonstrated the function and mechanism of MEX3B in TAD. These findings provide a theoretical basis for understanding TAD pathogenesis.

articles.title: Therapeutic plasma exchange improves survival in alcohol-related acute-on-chronic liver failure: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) is associated with high short-term mortality and limited therapeutic options. Therapeutic plasma exchange (PLEX) may improve outcomes by removing inflammatory mediators, but randomized evidence in ACLF is limited. This study evaluated the efficacy of PLEX in alcohol-related ACLF (A-ACLF).

METHODS: In this randomized controlled trial, 100 patients with A-ACLF were randomized (1 : 1) to PLEX plus standard medical therapy (SMT) or SMT alone. PLEX was performed for up to three sessions. Coprimary outcomes were in-hospital mortality and 30-day survival. Secondary outcomes included hospital stay, ventilator requirement, and longitudinal changes in disease severity scores and laboratory parameters.

RESULTS: All 100 patients (PLEX n = 50; SMT n = 50) completed follow-up. In-hospital mortality was lower with PLEX [24 vs. 52%; P = 0.007], with an absolute risk reduction of 28% (number needed to treat: 3.6). Thirty-day survival was higher with PLEX (72 vs. 36%; P < 0.001), with an adjusted hazard ratio for mortality of 0.43 (P = 0.003). Significant improvements were observed in the model for end-stage liver disease sodium, Asian Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver ACLF Research Consortium, and Child-Turcotte-Pugh scores, and in international normalized ratio, creatinine, lactate, ammonia, and von Willebrand factor (all P < 0.001 for interaction). Hospital stay was shorter with PLEX (19 vs. 24 days; P = 0.023). No major PLEX-related adverse events were observed.

CONCLUSION: PLEX improves short-term survival and disease severity in A-ACLF and may be a valuable therapeutic option where transplantation is limited.

articles.title: Real-World Treatment Patterns, Tolerability, and Outcomes Among Patients With CLL/SLL Treated With First-Line Ibrutinib, Acalabrutinib, or Zanubrutinib in the US Community Oncology Setting: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Covalent Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors (cBTKis) are standard first-line (1L) therapies for chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)/small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL). In clinical trials, second-generation (2G) cBTKis demonstrated better tolerability than ibrutinib, particularly regarding cardiotoxicity; however, real-world evidence on their use, discontinuation, and tolerability remains limited. This study examined treatment patterns and outcomes of cBTKis in the US community oncology setting.

METHODS: CLL/SLL patients who initiated 1L therapy between November 21, 2019 and July 31, 2023 were identified from electronic health records. Kaplan-Meier methods estimated time to treatment discontinuation (TTD), time to next treatment or death (TTNT-D), real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS), and overall survival (OS). Adverse events (AEs) were reported as proportions and incidence rates. Cox proportional hazards models assessed factors associated with TTD. Correlations between rwPFS and OS were evaluated with Kendall's tau.

RESULTS: Among 584 patients, 384 initiated ibrutinib, 150 acalabrutinib, and 50 zanubrutinib. Median follow-up durations were 35.6, 42.3, and 16.1 months, respectively. Overall, 51.2% discontinued 1L therapy by 24 months and 65.9% by end of follow-up, most commonly due to AEs (38.4%). Most patients who discontinued 1L treatment did not advance to 2L (61.8%; n = 238/385). Rates of AEs varied across cBTKis. Higher comorbidity burden, poorer performance status, del(17p), bleeding or infection, and ibrutinib (vs. acalabrutinib) were associated with shorter TTD. At 24 months, rwPFS and OS were 72.8% and 81.9%, respectively; medians were not reached. Older age (≥ 65 years) was associated with shorter TTD, TTNT-D, rwPFS, and OS. Notable correlations were observed between rwPFS and OS.

CONCLUSIONS: In this real‑world study, 1L cBTKi discontinuations occurred more frequently than in clinical trials, primarily driven by AEs. Many patients did not receive subsequent therapy. Tolerability was generally consistent with clinical trials, with variance across cBTKis. These findings highlight the unmet need for more tolerable treatment strategies to improve treatment durability and outcomes in real-world CLL/SLL populations.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The authors have confirmed clinical trial registration is not needed for this submission.

articles.title: The normal-weight metabolic syndrome: Clinical manifestations and pathogenic mechanisms.
articles.abstract: Metabolic syndrome (MetS), conventionally associated with obesity, also occurs in individuals with a normal body mass index (BMI), revealing an important discordance between body weight and metabolic health. This phenotype, variably described as normal-weight metabolic syndrome (NWMS), metabolically obese normal weight (MONW), or metabolically unhealthy normal weight (MUNW), is characterized by metabolic abnormalities despite the absence of generalized obesity. Reported prevalence varies substantially across populations because of heterogeneity in phenotype definitions, BMI thresholds, metabolic criteria, and population characteristics, and the global burden remains uncertain. Nevertheless, affected individuals have an increased risk of type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease compared with metabolically healthy normal-weight individuals. This review critically synthesizes current evidence on the epidemiology, clinical manifestations, diagnostic approaches, and pathogenic mechanisms of NWMS. Visceral and ectopic adiposity, insulin resistance, adipose tissue dysfunction, and chronic low-grade inflammation represent the most consistently supported pathogenic pathways. In contrast, gut microbiota dysbiosis, oxidative stress, ferroptosis, and related molecular processes remain emerging mechanisms with limited evidence specific to normal-weight populations. Recognition of metabolic risk beyond BMI is therefore important, particularly in susceptible populations. A risk-based approach incorporating conventional metabolic assessment, measures of central adiposity, and selective body-composition assessment may improve identification of affected individuals. Harmonized phenotype definitions and studies across geographically and ethnically diverse populations are needed to define the global burden and inform targeted prevention and management strategies.

articles.title: Ursolic acid as a multi-target therapeutic candidate in type 2 diabetes mellitus: a mechanistic and translational review.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is interconnected disturbances in insulin signaling, pancreatic β-cell function, redox and inflammatory homeostasis, lipid metabolism, mitochondrial function, and signaling mediated by advanced glycation end-product (AGE) and their receptors (RAGE). Although available antidiabetic therapies provide substantial clinical benefit, progressive β-cell dysfunction, and diabetes-associated tissue injury remain important clinical challenges. Ursolic acid (UA), a naturally occurring pentacyclic triterpenoid, has demonstrated broad preclinical metabolic and organ-protective effects, but the supporting evidence remains fragmented across individual pathways and experimental models. This review provides as updated, T2DM focussed in vitro, animal and limited human evidence, integrating UA-specific findings across insulin receptor/PTP1B signaling, β-cell preservation, redox regulation, inflammation, lipid metabolism, mitochondrial homeostasis and AGE-RAGE-associated injury. A key contribution is to stratify the mechanistic evidence rather than treating all pathway associations as equivalent, distinguishing direct or intervention-supported findings from expression-level associations, computational predictions and effects that may occur secondarily to improvements in glycaemia, insulin sensitivity, adiposity or oxidative stress. The review focus is comparatively stronger for the insulin-sensitising, lipid-regulatory, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects of UA, whereas direct AGE-RAGE modulation, circadian regulation and some pathway specific β-cell mechanisms remain preliminary. The translational development of UA is constrained by poor aqueous solubility, low oral bioavailability, uncertain dose exposure relationships, limited dose standardisation, insufficient long-term safety data, and lack of robust clinical validation in patients with T2DM. UA represents a multi-target preclinical candidate, rather than a clinically established antidiabetic therapy. Future research should prioritise pathway-specific validation, standardized diabetes-relevant models, pharmacokinetic pharmacodynamic correlation, controlled clinical studies, and long-term safety assessment.

articles.title: Characteristics and Hospital Outcomes of Patients Admitted to the Intensive Care Unit Because of Haematological Malignancy-A Service Evaluation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Intensive care unit (ICU) admission due to haematological malignancy (HM) has previously been questioned due to high mortality. While mortality-associated factors have been studied in HM patients to guide decision making and clinical practice, UK-based research remains limited. This single-centre retrospective service evaluation (SE) aimed to review characteristics and hospital outcomes of patients admitted to our ICU because of HM.

METHODS: Consecutive adults with HM-related admissions to a multi-specialty ICU between January 2022 and October 2024 were retrospectively identified. Data were extracted for patient characteristics, ICU interventions and hospital outcomes. Associations with ICU mortality rates were also assessed.

RESULTS: During the SE, there were 227 ICU admissions of HM patients, of which 168 were HM-related and, hence, included in subsequent analysis. The most common reasons for admission were respiratory failure (36.3%) and sepsis (26.2%). ICU and in-hospital mortality rates were 44.0% and 53.0%, respectively. ICU mortality rates increased significantly with APACHE II and SOFA scores (both p < 0.001), and in patients with leukaemia (p = 0.021), graft versus host disease (p = 0.001), treatment limitations (p < 0.001) or that were chemotherapy naïve (p = 0.044). In patients surviving to ICU discharge, 31.9% were unable to mobilise out of bed at this point. By hospital discharge, 94.9% of surviving patients were mobile; however, 25.3% required ongoing rehabilitation.

CONCLUSION: This SE describes the characteristics, outcomes and mortality-associated factors in patients with HM-related admissions to our ICU, which may be useful in aiding clinician understanding and guiding future practice. Prospective, robust studies are needed to validate findings and explore future opportunities to enhance patient outcomes in this cohort.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The authors have confirmed clinical trial registration is not needed for this submission.

articles.title: Sickle Cell Trait and Incident Ischemic Stroke Risk: A Whole-Genome Sequencing Study in the All of Us Research Program.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Sickle cell trait (SCT), the heterozygous hemoglobin variant (HbAS) genotype, affects approximately 300 million individuals worldwide and 8-10% of Black/African American individuals in the United States. Previous studies examining the association between SCT and ischemic stroke have yielded conflicting results, with effect estimates ranging from null to more than 2-fold increased risk. Interpretation of this literature has been limited by modest sample sizes, restricted ancestral diversity, and incomplete adjustment for genetic ancestry. We therefore evaluated whether whole-genome sequencing (WGS) confirmed SCT was independently associated with incident ischemic stroke after adjustment for genetic ancestry and vascular risk factors in the All of Us (AoU) cohort.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using WGS-confirmed hemoglobin subunit beta (HBB) genotypes at rs334 (HBB NM_000518.5:c.20A > T [p.Glu7Val]) from 414,830 participants in the NIH AoU Controlled Tier data set Curated Data Repository version 8 (CDR v8, C2024Q3R9). After restricting to eligible participants with WGS data, available electronic health record data, age 18-75 years, at least 12 months of follow-up, and no prior stroke or TIA at cohort entry, 275,530 participants comprised the incident ischemic stroke cohort. We used multivariable Cox proportional hazards models to compare incident ischemic stroke risk among participants with heterozygous HbAS SCT vs homozygous reference HbAA, adjusting for age, sex, hypertension, diabetes, atrial fibrillation, chronic kidney disease (CKD), body mass index (BMI), smoking, and genetic ancestry principal components 1-10 derived from AoU's precomputed WGS ancestry pipeline. Secondary analyses included competing risk modeling, multivariable logistic regression for prevalent stroke, Cox models for all secondary outcomes, 5 sensitivity analyses to test robustness of primary findings, and 12 prespecified subgroup analyses.

RESULTS: Among 275,530 participants contributing 3,374,790 person-years of follow-up (mean follow-up, 12.25 years), 5,876 had heterozygous HbAS SCT, 269,404 had homozygous reference HbAA, and 144 had homozygous variant HbSS sickle cell disease. The crude ischemic stroke incidence rate was 1.15 vs 0.67 per 1,000 person-years in HbAS vs HbAA (crude rate ratio, 1.70). After multivariable adjustment, SCT was not significantly associated with incident ischemic stroke (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.06; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.89-1.25; p = 0.53). The results were consistent across all 12 prespecified subgroups, the 5 sensitivity analyses, and additional missing data and time-varying covariate analyses assessing robustness to outcome definition, covariate timing, and ancestry restriction, including an African genetic ancestry subgroup analysis (HR = 0.97, 95% CI 0.81-1.16), a separate sensitivity analysis restricted to participants with African genetic ancestry (HR = 0.98, 95% CI 0.82-1.17), and strict baseline covariate definition (HR = 1.09, 95% CI 0.92-1.29). The results were also consistent in competing risk modeling (HR = 1.06), for hemorrhagic stroke (HR = 1.01), for TIA (TIA; HR = 1.06), and in the prespecified SCT × CKD interaction analysis (interaction HR = 1.13; p = 0.51). In contrast, HbSS was associated with a markedly elevated hazard of ischemic stroke (HR = 5.12, 95% CI 2.96-8.85; p < 0.001). The attenuation from the crude rate ratio to the ancestry-adjusted HR was consistent with substantial confounding by the higher proportion of African genetic ancestry among HbAS vs HbAA participants (88.1% vs 20.8%).

DISCUSSION: In a large WGS-confirmed, ancestry-adjusted cohort study, SCT was not significantly associated with incident ischemic stroke risk. The marked attenuation of the crude association after adjustment for genetic ancestry suggests that previously reported associations may, at least in part, reflect ancestry-related confounding and population structure rather than a strong independent effect of SCT. These findings do not support a clinically meaningful independent association between SCT and incident ischemic stroke in this cohort.

articles.title: Isolated vocal cord aspergillosis in an immunocompetent 60-year-old woman: A rare case report with radiological findings.
articles.abstract: Laryngeal aspergillosis is an uncommon manifestation of Aspergillus infection and is most frequently described in immunocompromised patients or in association with pulmonary or systemic disease. Isolated involvement of a vocal cord in an immunocompetent patient is particularly rare and may mimic a neoplastic or inflammatory laryngeal lesion. We report the case of a 60-year-old immunocompetent woman presenting with a four-month history of progressive hoarseness, throat discomfort, and intermittent globus sensation. Flexible laryngoscopy revealed a raised whitish-yellow exophytic lesion involving the middle third of the right true vocal cord, with preserved vocal cord mobility. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) of the neck demonstrated focal soft-tissue thickening of the right vocal cord measuring approximately 12 × 9 mm, without paraglottic extension, thyroid cartilage erosion, or cervical lymphadenopathy. The lesion was surgically excised. Histopathological examination demonstrated septate fungal hyphae with acute-angle branching, compatible with Aspergillus species. Fungal culture identified Aspergillus flavus. The patient had no identified immunodeficiency or other recognized predisposing condition. She was treated with oral itraconazole 200 mg twice daily for three weeks, with progressive clinical improvement and complete endoscopic resolution at three months. No recurrence was observed during six months of follow-up. Isolated vocal cord aspergillosis should be considered in the differential diagnosis of persistent hoarseness and focal vocal cord lesions, even in immunocompetent patients. CT is useful for defining the extent of laryngeal involvement and, particularly, for evaluating deep tissue extension, cartilage invasion, and cervical lymphadenopathy. However, imaging findings are nonspecific, and definitive diagnosis requires histopathological and microbiological confirmation.

articles.title: A Decade in Periprosthetic Joint Infection Care: Growing Referrals and High Resource Demands at a High-Volume Center.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The management of periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) requires a multidisciplinary approach that is not feasible in all healthcare settings. This study characterized the evolving burden of PJI referrals at an academic referral center over the past decade.

METHODS: A retrospective review was conducted of all referred patients who underwent treatment for hip or knee PJI at a single referral center between 2014 and 2024. Demographic data, initial operative time, hospital length of stay (LOS), and number and duration of subsequent surgeries were recorded.

RESULTS: In total, 523 referred patients were treated for PJI. The mean initial LOS was 7.0 days (standard deviation [SD] 5.7) and the mean operative time was 169.5 min (SD 75.9). Overall, 36% underwent irrigation and debridement with modular component exchange, single stage revision, or a spacer alone. Of the 335 who had at least 1 subsequent surgery, under half (N = 146, 43.5%), received stage two alone. On average, patients underwent 1.8 subsequent surgeries (SD 1.4), ranging from 1 to 14. The cumulative mean operative time for these subsequent surgeries was 306.4 min (SD 253.3). The number of PJIs nearly doubled from 2014-2017 (N = 112) to 2021-2024 (N = 221). There were no significant changes in LOS, number of subsequent surgeries, or cumulative operative time for reoperations during these intervals.

CONCLUSIONS: The volume of referred PJIs has increased substantially over the past decade at our referral center, underscoring the growing demand for PJI care and profound resource burden necessary to care for these patients.

articles.title: Vibration-Controlled Transient Elastography (VCTE)-Based Prevalence and Assessment of Hepatic Steatosis and Fibrosis in a UK Tertiary Hospital-Based Specialist Weight Management Service: A Real-World Evaluation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease is common in severe obesity; however, liver health assessment is inconsistently implemented in specialist weight management services and real-world data are scarce. This study evaluated the prevalence and severity of vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE)-defined hepatic steatosis and fibrosis risk in adults attending a UK-based Tier 3 specialist weight management service, and explored associations with clinical and metabolic characteristics.

METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 96 adults referred to a specialist weight management service who underwent baseline VCTE (FibroScan) between June 2024 and November 2025. Controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) estimated hepatic steatosis and fibrosis risk, respectively. Demographic, anthropometric, clinical, and biochemical variables were extracted from electronic records. Generalized linear models identified factors associated with CAP and LSM, with sensitivity analyses adjusting for incretin-based therapy use.

RESULTS: Participants were predominantly female (83.3%) and White European (81.3%), with mean age 48.7 ± 12.5 years and BMI 42.0 ± 9.4 kg/m2. VCTE-defined steatosis was present in 82.3% (CAP ≥ 248 dB·m-1), with 57.3% classified as severe (CAP ≥ 280 dB·m-1). Overall, 26.1% had elevated fibrosis risk (LSM ≥ 8 kPa), including 6.3% classified as high risk (LSM > 12 kPa). In multivariable analyses, higher BMI, HbA1c and ALT were independently associated with greater CAP, whereas BMI and HbA1c were independently associated with higher LSM. Further adjustment for incretin-based pharmacotherapy use did not alter these relationships.

CONCLUSIONS: Hepatic steatosis and elevated fibrosis risk are highly prevalent in adults attending specialist weight management services. Adiposity and glycemic burden appear to be key determinants, supporting the integration of non-invasive liver assessment into specialist obesity care pathways.

articles.title: Comparison of Effects of Pulsed Field Ablation and Cryoablation on Left Atrial Stiffness Using Invasively Derived Pressure-Volume Relationship.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute effects of pulsed field ablation (PFA) on passive atrial mechanical properties have not hitherto been assessed by reconstruction of pressure-volume relationship using invasive intracavitary pressure measurements.

METHODS: In a cohort of 38 first-time atrial fibrillation ablation patients, submitted to pulmonary vein isolation, we studied the effects of PFA and cryoballoon ablation on the left atrial elastic constant and passive elastic chamber stiffness constant, expressing baseline left atrial conditions and quantifying passive left atrial stiffness, respectively. Left atrial pressure was invasively measured immediately pre- and post-procedurally, while volume values were obtained echocardiographically.

RESULTS: No differences were noted in passive elastic chamber stiffness constant values, pre- and post-procedurally in either group. No differences were noted between CBA and PFA groups. There were no observable associations between Δα and Δb and either AF duration or preprocedural left atrial volume.

CONCLUSIONS: Based on the above, CBA and PFA demonstrated comparable effects on left atrial mechanical properties in the acute post-ablation setting.

articles.title: Tailor-Made Hybrid Pulsed-Field and Radiofrequency Ablation Guided by ExTRa Mapping for Refractory Long-Standing Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: First Experience With the Affera System Prism-2.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) alone is frequently insufficient for persistent atrial fibrillation (AF). Although pulsed-field ablation (PFA) ensures durable linear lesions, extensive transmural ablation risks iatrogenic atrial tachycardia. A tailored strategy combining PFA with titrated radiofrequency (RF) energy for mild substrate homogenization remains poorly defined.

CASE SUMMARY: A 77-year-old male with post-stroke refractory long-standing AF underwent a re-do ablation. Biatrial substrate evaluation was performed using the ExTRa mapping system, enabled by the Affera system (Prism-2) to visualize the nonmagnetic 20-pole spiral catheter. Areas with a mean non-passively activated ratio (%NP) ≥ 35% and low voltage (< 0.3 mV) were targeted. Following PFA-led posterior wall isolation, mild homogenization was performed using the Sphere-9 catheter with highly titrated RF energy (60%, 60°C, and 1-s duration). Although AF did not terminate directly, the AF cycle length significantly prolonged, and sinus rhythm was restored via cardioversion. Post-procedural mapping confirmed complete isolation without extensive dense scar formation at homogenization sites. The patient maintained sinus rhythm during follow-up.

CONCLUSION: The hybrid PFA/RF system integrated with AI-driven phase mapping enables a safe, non-destructive, tailor-made substrate modification strategy for refractory persistent AF.

articles.title: Personalised approach to venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in heavier critically ill patients (PROSPER): A randomised, parallel-group, electronic medical record (EMR)-embedded feasibility trial.
articles.journal: Critical care and resuscitation : journal of the Australasian Academy of Critical Care Medicine
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Data are limited regarding optimal low molecular weight heparin dosing for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in heavier critically ill patients. This trial evaluated the feasibility of a weight-based dynamic dosing algorithm.

DESIGN SETTING PARTICIPANTS: Open-label, electronic medical record-embedded randomised feasibility trial. Patients, weighing ≥100 kg who required thromboprophylaxis were eligible. Enoxaparin was commenced with weight-based dosing and anti-Xa level-guided adjustment (target peak anti-Xa level 0.2-0.4 IU/mL) or usual care (40 mg twice daily).

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was peak anti-Xa level at 'steady state' (after ≥3 enoxaparin doses). The feasibility threshold was set at 95% of steady state anti-Xa levels in the intervention group being less than the threshold for therapeutic anticoagulant effect (≤0.6 IU/mL).

RESULTS: Fifty participants (intervention n = 17, control n = 33) received 331 doses of enoxaparin (median of 4 [interquartile range {IQR}: 3-7] doses per participant, and a dose of 50 [IQR: 50-60] mg (intervention) and 40 [IQR: 40-40] mg (control)). Thirty-two 'steady state' peak anti-Xa measurements were recorded from 24 patients (12 intervention and 12 control). The proportion of peak anti-Xa levels that were ≤0.6 IU/mL was: 15 of 17 (88%) vs. 15 of 15 (100%). There were fewer peak anti-Xa measurements below the prophylactic range (<0.2 IU/mL) in the intervention group compared with the control group (2 of 17 [12%] vs. 5 of 15 [33%]). Six patients developed venous thrombosis or pulmonary embolism (2 of 17 [12%] vs. 4 of 33 [12%]). Major bleeding occurred in one patient in the intervention group.

CONCLUSIONS: A weight-based dynamic thromboprophylaxis algorithm was implemented via the electronic medical record but did not meet the predefined feasibility threshold.

articles.title: Schaalia odontolytica causing primary intraventricular brain abscess in a child- A case report.
articles.abstract: Primary intraventricular abscesses are very rare and may be mistaken for intraventricular tumors or other lesions with very few cases reported in literature. Although organisms from the oral cavity are recognized pathogens for brain abscess formation, reports of abscesses caused by Schaalia odontolytica previously known as Actinomyces odontolyticus remain uncommon. This is a case report of a 6-year-old boy with a congenital heart disease (ventricular septal defect and pulmonary atresia) who presented with headaches, fever, neck stiffness and vomiting. Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain showed central T1W hypointense, T2/FLAIR hyperintense collection in the dilated left lateral ventricle with associated periventricular vasogenic oedema indicating a primary intraventricular abscess. The main abscess was drained via a burr hole with persistent small abscesses in the occipital and temporal horns. A second burr hole attempt at draining the occipital and temporal lobe abscesses failed. Cultures of the pus yielded Schaalia odontolytica a known flora of the mouth. No oral lesions were observed in the patient. The patient was managed on 61 days of amoxicillin-clavulanic acid, with erythrocyte sedimentation rate falling from 6 mm/h to 1 mm/h after 2 months of therapy. Primary intraventricular abscess is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition that can present with nonspecific neurological symptoms. In children with cyanotic congenital heart disease, an intracranial abscess should be considered when compatible clinical and neuroimaging findings are present. This case highlights the importance of MRI for diagnosis and microbiological examination of drained material for identification of unusual pathogens such as Schaalia odontolytica.

articles.title: Recurrent papillary thyroid carcinoma with brachiocephalic vein tumor thrombus: A rare case report.
articles.abstract: Papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) generally has an excellent prognosis and an indolent clinical course. However, major vascular invasion with tumor thrombus formation is exceedingly rare. We report the case of a 63-year-old woman with recurrent PTC presenting five years after total thyroidectomy and radioactive iodine therapy. Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated recurrent disease within the thyroidectomy bed, extensive cervical nodal metastases, retrosternal extension, pulmonary nodules, and tumor thrombus involving the left brachiocephalic vein near the SVC junction. The patient underwent extensive surgical management, including left modified neck dissection, median sternotomy, en bloc resection of recurrent disease, thrombectomy, and primary repair of the brachiocephalic vein. Histopathological examination confirmed recurrent papillary thyroid carcinoma with vascular tumor thrombosis. Postoperatively, the patient received adjuvant radioactive iodine therapy. At 12-month follow-up, serum thyroglobulin levels were undetectable, and imaging studies demonstrated no evidence of locoregional recurrence. This case highlights a rare and aggressive presentation of recurrent PTC with major venous involvement and demonstrates that satisfactory short-term disease control can be achieved through aggressive multidisciplinary management.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of onabotulinumtoxinA versus topiramate in chronic migraine in the US: an economic analysis of the FORWARD randomized trial.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Assess the cost-effectiveness of onabotulinumtoxinA (OnabotA) versus topiramate for the preventive treatment of chronic migraine in US adult patients from a payer perspective.

METHODS: A multistate Markov model evaluated the incremental costs per headache-day avoided and quality adjusted life-year (QALY) over a 2-year period in patients treated with OnabotA versus topiramate. The FORWARD trial data informed model inputs, including reductions in headache-days, while patients receive OnabotA/topiramate. Treatment discontinuation for topiramate was modeled with data from FORWARD and a randomized controlled trial (RCT) to test a range of values for topiramate. Costs of drug acquisition, administration, and monitoring were calculated from prescribing information and physician fee schedules. The model estimated costs of healthcare resource utilization (HCRU) and acute migraine treatment by response level. Sensitivity and scenario analyses explored cost drivers and assessed model robustness.

RESULTS: Our model estimated that OnabotA-treated patients experience 122.56 fewer headache-days (0.34 years) than topiramate-treated patients over the 2-year time horizon. With an incremental cost of $4,639, the incremental cost per headache-day avoided was ∼ $37.85/day, and the incremental cost per QALY gained was $63,646. The estimated cost per avoided headache-day was less than half for patients treated with OnabotA in comparison with topiramate ($116 vs. $246). Sensitivity analyses showed that the incremental cost per headache-day avoided remained below $50 and the incremental cost per QALY gained remained below $100,000 across all tested ranges. Results were similar when using a lower, RCT-supported discontinuation rate for topiramate. In scenario analyses, a longer time horizon and a greater price discount for OnabotA substantially reduced the incremental cost-effectiveness ratios.

CONCLUSION: OnabotA was a cost-effective preventive treatment of chronic migraine versus topiramate. Although OnabotA had higher drug acquisition costs, these were offset by reduced HCRU costs due to fewer migraines, resulting in a low incremental cost per headache-day avoided versus topiramate.

articles.title: Open ilio-obturator lymphadenectomy for stage III cutaneous malignancies - a retrospective case series on cases with concurrent inguinal lymphadenectomy and a case report on the laparoscopic transperitoneal approach.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ilio-obturator lymphadenectomy (IOL) is used in the treatment of stage III melanoma. IOL can be performed using a conventional open approach, minimally invasive transperitoneal or extraperitoneal approach. IOL is traditionally combined with inguinal lymphadenectomy (IL). From 2010-2024, open IOL (O-IOL) was standard in our hospital. The first laparoscopic transperitoneal IOL (LT-IOL) for stage III melanoma we performed in our hospital, had a detrimental outcome. This prompted us to review our complications after O-IOL. The aim of this study is to assess surgical complication rates and safety of O-IOL when combined with IL.

METHODS: This was a single-center retrospective case series on O-IOL with concurrent IL. Primary outcome measures were complication rates and severity, readmissions and surgical reinterventions. Secondary outcome measures were technique for surgical approach, unplanned visits and oncological outcome.

RESULTS: Between 2010 and 2024, 11 patients underwent O-IOL combined with IL. One patient (9.1%) developed a surgical site infection after O-IOL, which was treated with antibiotics and outpatient wound debridement. No other complications were observed. All patients developed complications related to concurrent IL.

CONCLUSIONS: O-IOL using a Rutherford-Morrison incision for the retroperitoneal approach shows low complication rates in this case series. In our described case, combining LT-IOL with IL resulted in a disastrous outcome.

articles.title: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine recommendations for adults: a review of available global, regional, and country level recommendations.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) can cause serious disease in older adults (OAs), particularly those with underlying medical conditions. It can lead to acute respiratory illness and lower respiratory tract infections in adults ≥60 years and at increased risk groups. RSV morbidity, mortality, and health care burden are increasingly evident. This review aims to equip clinicians with practical guidance to support consistent implementation of RSV vaccination recommendations.

AREAS COVERED: We examined global implementation of RSV vaccination recommendations by extracting guidelines from national immunization technical advisory groups, ministries of health, global and regional recommendations, and local medical societies. We categorized guidance by age, risk factors and comorbidities. We compared differences in indications, age thresholds, and frameworks. Across >24 countries and >50 medical societies, a common recommendation supports RSV vaccination in ≥60 years and immunocompromised individuals. The set cutoff date was November 2025. However, significant heterogeneity exists across countries in age threshold indications and risk-based eligibility, as well as in implementation depending on health system infrastructure and resources.

EXPERT OPINION: Global guidance converges on prioritizing vaccination for OAs and individuals at high risk of severe disease. By synthesizing worldwide RSV vaccination recommendations, this review offers clinicians an accessible guide to support consistent RSV vaccination.

articles.title: Single nucleotide polymorphisms associated with glucocorticoid treatment response in immune thrombocytopenia: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Glucocorticoids (GCs) are the standard initial treatment for immune thrombocytopenia (ITP); however, some patients experience treatment failure. The role of genetic variants in distinguishing GC responders from non-responders remains unclear. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies in pediatric and adult ITP, identified in PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science up to July 14, 2026, that reported genotype-specific first-line GC responses. Eligible single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) studies with genotype-stratified outcomes were pooled to estimate odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (95% CI). Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) checklist, and the certainty of the evidence was rated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. Forty-five studies (n = 6158) met the inclusion criteria, and 21 were included in meta-analyses. IL-10 rs1800871 and rs1800872 were associated with higher odds of GC non-response, with 2.8-fold and 3.2-fold increases, respectively (rs1800871: OR 2.77, 95% CI 1.54-4.96; rs1800872: OR 3.18, 95% CI 1.77-5.70; both P < 0.001; I2 = 0%), and DNAM1 rs763361 was also associated with non-response (OR 2.00, 95% CI 1.05-3.80; P = 0.03; I2 = 27.5%), all of which were observed under the recessive model. Moreover, TNF-α rs1800629 was associated with GC non-response under the heterozygous model (OR 3.89, 95% CI 1.20-12.61; P = 0.02; I² = 0%). Other investigated polymorphisms demonstrated inconsistent or absent associations with treatment response and were rated as low or very low certainty. IL-10 rs1800871/rs1800872 and DNAM1 rs763361 emerged as the most consistently associated variants, supported by moderate-certainty evidence. However, these variants are hypothesis-generating and are not yet ready for clinical use. Validation in larger, prospective, and ethnically diverse cohorts is needed before any clinical application can be considered.
