Pathogenicity and virulence of Xanthomonas in plants: Toward understanding specificity and achieving durable genetic resistance.
articles.abstract: Plant pathogens in the bacterial genus Xanthomonas infect over 400 host species, including many economically important crop plants. In this review, we provide an overview of the genus, then highlight the infection and virulence strategies of Xanthomonas pathogens: how they survive in the phyllosphere, enter plant tissue, manipulate host immunity and physiology, and regulate virulence pathways, with a particular focus on host and tissue specificity. We then focus on host immunity against Xanthomonas pathogens, including cell surface, intracellular, and Xanthomonas-specific immunity, addressing the potential of discoveries in each compartment as foundations for engineered defense. While significant progress has been made, continued research on the diversity of Xanthomonas virulence mechanisms and counteracting plant defense will be instrumental for such engineering, promising at the same time deeper insight into pathogen-host interactions.

articles.title: Sono-enzymatically engineered tannic acid/doxycycline-lignin nanoparticles enable self-assembled bioactive chitosan hydrogels for chronic wound healing.
articles.abstract: Chronic wounds remain a major clinical challenge due to their multifactorial pathology, characterised by excessive proteolytic and oxidative enzyme activity, persistent inflammation, bacterial infection, and biofilm formation. Here, we report a green, nano-enabled hydrogel fabricated through the in situ self-assembly of thiolated chitosan (TCS), driven by tannic acid/doxycycline-functionalised lignin nanoparticles (PLD NPs). Doxycycline was incorporated at a sub-inhibitory concentration (12.5 μg/mL), enabling PLD NPs (0.5 mg/mL) to inhibit matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) activity by approximately 50 % without inducing antibacterial effects. Dynamic interactions between the polymer network and NPs produced injectable, self-healing hydrogels capable of stimuli-responsive NPs release under chronic wound-like conditions, including variations in pH, hydrogen peroxide, and lysozyme. Ex vivo evaluation using human chronic wound exudates demonstrated potent inhibition of MMP and myeloperoxidase activities by 73 % and 80 %, respectively. The hydrogels further exhibited strong antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, achieving 4.8- and 4.3-log reductions in bacterial viability while preventing 73 % and 65 % of biofilm formation, respectively. In vitro studies confirmed excellent biocompatibility with human keratinocytes and fibroblasts, together with up to 82 % cellular antioxidant activity and enhanced fibroblast migration. Importantly, in an in vivo full-thickness S. aureus-infected mouse wound model, the hydrogels achieved complete wound closure within 18 days, outperforming commercial antiseptic treatments. Overall, this work demonstrates a multifunctional hydrogel platform that simultaneously modulates the chronic wound microenvironment, controls infection and biofilm formation, reduces oxidative stress, and promotes tissue regeneration, offering a promising strategy for advanced chronic wound management.

articles.title: Strengthening antimicrobial stewardship through an international multicentre improvement programme of hospitals serving deprived populations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) is essential to addressing antimicrobial resistance, but its implementation remains variable, particularly in settings with resource limitations. Hospitals serving deprived or underserved populations often work with limited diagnostic capacity, workforce pressures and variable digital infrastructure, which shape stewardship delivery. The Antimicrobial Stewardship Disparities Programme (ASDP) was established to strengthen stewardship capability in such settings and to support progress towards accreditation under the Global AMS Accreditation Scheme (GAMSAS).

METHODS: A mixed-methods evaluation was undertaken across six centres in Botswana, Kenya, Lebanon, Mexico, Pakistan and the USA. Centres completed baseline and end of programme self-assessments against 17 AMS, infection prevention and control (IPC) and laboratory standards mapped to 4 pillars (structures, guidance, education and surveillance). Programme documentation was analysed to identify themes, contextual influences and barriers. All work was delivered within existing resources.

RESULTS: Centres achieved improvements across AMS, IPC and laboratory standards, with consistent progress in surveillance. Governance was strengthened through clearer AMS committee structures, and guidance improved through prescribing tools embedded in practice. Education and laboratory standards showed limited change, reflecting workforce pressures, lack of protected time and constrained diagnostic capacity. Three centres achieved GAMSAS accreditation. Qualitative findings highlighted strategies to advance stewardship within structural constraints, including surveillance systems, training and locally adapted guidance.

CONCLUSIONS: Local aims, supported by a standards framework and mentorship, enabled centres to strengthen stewardship capability within existing resources. Workforce capacity, diagnostic access and digital infrastructure remain key determinants. Structured assessment and shared learning support scalable AMS in underserved settings.

articles.title: Sequential blood-brain barrier-penetrating and microglial-mitochondria-targeting nanosystem for ischemic stroke therapy.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) causes severe neurological deficits closely linked to microglial overactivation after ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury, a process governed by mitochondrial homeostasis. However, restoring microglial mitochondrial function across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) remains challenging. Here, we report a sequentially targeted nanosystem, M-BPM@TGPB, for I/R injury therapy. It comprises a triphenylphosphonium (TPP)-modified, gadolinium-doped Prussian blue core and a mannose-modified BV2-platelet hybrid membrane shell. This design integrates mannose for BBB penetration, platelet membrane for lesion targeting, BV2 membrane for microglial uptake, and TPP for mitochondrial localization, enabling precise vascular-to-subcellular delivery. In vitro, the nanosystem crossed the BBB, localized to BV2 mitochondria, scavenged reactive oxygen species (ROS), restored mitochondrial function, and inhibited inflammation. In a mouse model of middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R), the intravenously administered nanosystem accumulated in microglial mitochondria, scavenged mitochondrial ROS (mtROS), restored mitochondrial homeostasis, promoted M1-to-M2 polarization, suppressed neuroinflammation, reduced neuronal apoptosis, and promoted angiogenesis, thereby reducing infarct volume from 36.61% to 10.57% and the modified neurological severity score (mNSS) from 14 to 2.5. It also exhibited favorable biocompatibility and enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contrast. Critically, rather than broadly scavenging ROS, this strategy specifically restores microglial mitochondrial function, shifting the therapeutic focus from general antioxidant approaches to organelle-specific intervention. This work may offer a promising design paradigm for nanotherapies targeting central nervous system disorders in which mitochondrial dysfunction and neuroinflammation are core pathological drivers.

articles.title: Strengthening emergency care research quality: A commentary on a mid-study PDSA in a multisite project in Ghana.
articles.journal: African journal of emergency medicine : Revue africaine de la medecine d'urgence
articles.abstract: Emergency medicine is rapidly evolving across Africa, yet the field continues to face significant gaps in research quality, particularly in study design and implementation. To generate actionable evidence that reflects the acute care needs of African populations, it is critical to embed quality management measures within clinical research processes. This commentary describes the use of the Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA), a simple and reproducible quality improvement (QI) tool, as a mid-study quality audit strategy during the implementation of the "Pathways to Care for Patients with Acute Infectious Illnesses in Ghana" (PATHCARE) study. Over two weeks, trained evaluators conducted structured observations and interviews with research assistants (RAs) across five study sites in Kumasi, Ghana. The audit revealed protocol deviations related to patient screening, recruitment, informed consent, and data collection that threatened data integrity and participant protection. Based on these findings, a targeted refresher training was conducted, leading to measurable improvements in RA knowledge of study protocol. This experience highlights the feasibility and impact of embedding low-cost, iterative quality audits within emergency care research. Especially in resource-constrained settings with limited research infrastructure, tools like the PDSA can serve as pragmatic solutions to enhance data reliability, safeguard ethical standards, and ultimately, improve the quality and utility of clinical research in African emergency medicine.

articles.title: Lipid phenotypes and diabetic kidney disease: a cluster-based study integrating traditional and nontraditional lipid parameters.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to identify lipid phenotypes integrating traditional and nontraditional lipid parameters and examine their associations with diabetic kidney disease (DKD).

METHODS: The study analyzed 4,936 Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus recruited from 24 primary medical institutions. K-means clustering was performed using triglycerides (TG), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL), atherogenic index of plasma, and remnant cholesterol (RC). Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate associations between lipid phenotypes and DKD and interactions with C-reactive protein were assessed on multiplicative and additive scales.

RESULTS: Two lipid phenotypes were identified: a relatively higher LDL/HDL phenotype (n = 4,095, 82.96%) and a higher TG/RC phenotype (n = 841, 17.04%). The higher TG/RC phenotype exhibited more severe metabolic-inflammatory status and a higher prevalence of DKD than the other phenotype (52.44% vs 44.00%). After full adjustment, the higher TG/RC phenotype was associated with higher odds of DKD (OR 1.370, 95% CI 1.172-1.602), early DKD (OR 1.238, 95% CI 1.059-1.446), and reduced eGFR (OR 2.062, 95% CI 1.420-2.994). Participants with both the higher TG/RC phenotype and elevated C-reactive protein levels showed the highest odds of DKD (OR 1.881, 95% CI 1.540-2.297), with significant multiplicative and additive interactions. The clustered phenotype also provided incremental discriminative information beyond individual lipid markers, and the findings remained consistent across sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: Integrating traditional and nontraditional lipid measures may help identify clinically relevant lipid phenotypes associated with DKD and support more targeted renal assessment in T2DM patients.

articles.title: Association between triglyceride-glucose index and treatment response in primary membranous nephropathy: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, a marker of insulin resistance, has been linked to chronic kidney disease and proteinuria severity, but its prognostic value for treatment response in primary membranous nephropathy (PMN) is unclear. We evaluated whether baseline TyG predicts 12-month proteinuria remission in PMN.

METHODS: We included 363 patients with PMN. The primary outcome was 12-month remission per 2021 KDIGO criteria. Missing covariates were handled by multiple imputation (20 datasets). Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for anti-PLA2R antibody (continuous, per 100 RU/mL), albumin, 24-hour urine protein, age, sex, comorbidities, and treatment group. Sensitivity analyses included TyG tertiles, restriction to standard immunotherapy, complete remission, binary anti-PLA2R status, eGFR adjustment, log-transformed and restricted cubic spline modeling of anti-PLA2R antibody, complete-case analysis, inverse probability of treatment weighting, post-hoc power analysis, and adjustment for treatment switching.

RESULTS: Among 363 patients, 267 (73.6%) achieved remission. Baseline TyG was not independently associated with remission (OR = 0.839, 95% CI: 0.544-1.293, p = 0.425). Higher anti-PLA2R antibody levels were associated with lower odds of remission when modeled continuously (OR per 100 RU/mL = 0.836, 95% CI: 0.704-0.992, p = 0.041), but not when dichotomized (OR = 0.666, 95% CI: 0.213-2.089, p = 0.484). Addition of TyG minimally improved model discrimination (AUC 0.714 to 0.716). Results were consistent across sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: Baseline TyG was not independently associated with 12-month remission in PMN and provided minimal incremental predictive value. However, a moderate association cannot be excluded given the confidence interval. Anti-PLA2R antibody level showed an inverse association when modeled continuously.

articles.title: Perinatal multidisciplinary management for neonates with prenatally-diagnosed congenital complete heart block undergoing early epicardial pacemaker implantation: a retrospective single-center case series.
articles.journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To report our single-center multidisciplinary perinatal experience for neonates with prenatally diagnosed isolated congenital complete heart block (CCHB) requiring early epicardial pacemaker implantation.

METHODS: This retrospective case series included four consecutive neonates with prenatally diagnosed isolated CCHB (2016-2020). A multidisciplinary team coordinated perinatal planning. Maternal data, fetal echocardiography, delivery-room resuscitation, vasoactive support, and short-term neonatal outcomes were analyzed descriptively.

RESULTS: Four neonates (gestation 35 + 6-37 + 6 weeks; birth weight 2270-2500 g) were delivered by cesarean section. Umbilical vein catheterization was achieved rapidly in all. All neonates had a heart rate <50 bpm at birth and received immediate vasoactive resuscitation. All neonates underwent successful epicardial permanent pacemaker implantation within 10 days after birth with improved cardiac function and were discharged home. One infant was readmitted 8 days after discharge due to pocket infection and ultimately died on postnatal day 46.

CONCLUSIONS: Multidisciplinary coordination, early umbilical-vein access, and individualized vasoactive support are critical for managing these high-risk neonates. Our findings provide practical guidance but require validation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Prevalence, clinical characteristics, and etiologic spectrum of extremely low levels of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol in Thai patients: a single-center study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extremely low high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) is uncommon and may result from secondary conditions or rare genetic disorders. Data on persistently low HDL-C in Southeast Asians remain limited. We aim to determine the prevalence, clinical characteristics, underlying etiologies, and clinical outcomes of patients with persistent low HDL-C.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study evaluated adults with persistently low HDL-C (<30 mg/dL) identified via laboratory and electronic medical records between January 2020 and December 2024. Patients were stratified into two phenotypes based on baseline HDL-C severity: markedly low (20-29 mg/dL) or extremely low (<20 mg/dL).

RESULTS: Among 217,481 individuals undergoing lipid testing (1,053,662 HDL-C measurements), 164 patients had persistently low HDL-C (mean age, 56.9 years; 68.9% male). The prevalence of persistently low and extremely low HDL-C was 0.08% and 0.008%, respectively. Concomitant hypertriglyceridemia affected ∼75% of patients. Most cases were associated with secondary conditions. Extremely low HDL-C was more frequently associated with liver disease (41.2%) and active malignancy (29.4%), whereas metabolic syndrome predominated among patients with markedly low HDL-C (42.2%). During a median follow-up of 2.57 years, all-cause mortality was higher in the extremely low HDL-C group (29.4% vs. 11.6%; hazard ratio, 4.33; 95% CI, 1.58-11.91; p = 0.004), while atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease rates were similar between groups (35.3% vs. 32.0%).

CONCLUSIONS: Persistently low HDL-C is an exceedingly rare phenotype driven primarily by secondary systemic conditions. An extremely low HDL-C level appears to be a marker of severe underlying systemic illness and was associated with higher short-term mortality.

articles.title: The PRIMARY Scoring System on PSMA PET for Clinically Significant Prostate Cancer Detection: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis: Erratum.
Disease burden of rotavirus infection and its complications among children under 14 years old with acute gastroenteritis in China: a multicentre and retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the positivity rate, disease burden, and complications of rotavirus gastroenteritis (RVGE) among Chinese children under 14 years of age presenting with acute gastroenteritis (AGE).

METHODS: A multicentre, observational, and retrospective study was conducted at 11 centres across China (July 2013 - June 2023). Data on RVGE prevalence, direct medical costs, and complications were analyzed, with projections of direct economic burden for 2025 - 2034.

RESULTS: Out of 505,987 AGE visits, the rotavirus positivity rate was 15.70%, peaked at 26.41% in the 12-month period from July 2016 to June 2017, and the annual positivity rate declined by 19.63% between 2017 and 2023. Among 7,113 RVGE cases, 28.57% of inpatients had recorded complications, and the estimated rate of recorded complications among all RVGE patients was 8.29%, most commonly recorded complications being myocardial damage, dehydration, respiratory infection, convulsion, and metabolic acidosis. The median cost of RVGE was CNY 272.80 (USD 40.68) for outpatients and CNY 5336.60 (USD 795.69) for inpatients, respectively. Projected economic burden is estimated to decrease from CNY 8.55 billion (USD 1.21 billion) in 2025 to CNY 3.96 billion (USD 559 million) in 2034.

CONCLUSIONS: RVGE was associated with high complication rates. The decrease in rotavirus prevalence since 2018, highlighting the public health value of a series of preventive measures during this period, including vaccination.

articles.title: Methodological and Theoretical Advances in Research on Grooming in Child Sexual Abuse.
articles.abstract: The science of the dynamics, consequences and treatment of child sexual abuse developed rapidly after passage of the Child Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act of 1974. However, the necessity for some set of methods to both evaluate and treat the unexpected number of survivors of child abuse led to both innovation and controversy. One contribution that has deepened our understanding of child abuse is the enhanced attention to the grooming process, a term first offered to the field by Jon Conte in 1984. Virtually all experts agree that knowledge and accurate identification of this process as it is occurring would aid prevention. However, the field suffers from definitional muddle, lack of accurate prevalence and descriptive data, and limited attention to ecological validity considerations. This paper is a review of the state of this subfield. Issues raised in the paper include the lumping of unlike behaviors (consensually inappropriate and situationally dependent actions), the problem of hindsight bias, and the lack of reliable norms. This paper attempts to address these issues and to propose some directions for further work.

articles.title: Clonal tree frequency analysis reveals affinity determinants and enables antibody lead optimization.
articles.abstract: Understanding the sequence determinants of antibody affinity within a clonal family is a central challenge in therapeutic antibody discovery. Here, we applied amino acid frequency analysis to a large phylogenetic clonal tree of anti-ST2 monoclonal antibodies, where V(D)J recombination is constant and only somatic hypermutations vary. We identified M33I and L100I in the heavy chain as key affinity-governing mutations, corroborated by AlphaFold2 structural modeling and molecular dynamics free‑energy decomposition. The I33/I100 genotype predicted significantly improved functional neutralization of IL-33-induced IL-6 release and was associated with a higher transcriptomic affinity score (Hiscore). Prospective mutagenesis of three low-affinity parent antibodies achieved up to 10-fold affinity improvement, establishing a workflow integrating sequence statistics, structural modeling, transcriptomics and MD simulation for rational lead optimization.

articles.title: Population level immunity to measles and rubella 5 years before and after the MR campaign in urban Vellore, South India.
articles.abstract: India aims to eliminate measles and rubella (MR) by 2026. Despite >90% vaccination coverage reported in NFHS-5 and NFHS-6, assessing population-level immunity gaps remains essential to guide strategies for protecting vulnerable groups. We leveraged biobanked samples from two community-based serosurveys conducted in urban Vellore in 2013 and 2022, representing periods 5 years before and after the nationwide MR vaccination campaign. Age- and sex-stratified participants were tested for measles- and rubella-specific IgG antibodies using ELISA. Seroprevalence estimates were compared across surveys, and generalized additive models (GAM) were used to assess age-specific seropositivity patterns. Effective reproduction numbers (Re) for measles and rubella were estimated using mixture modeling approaches. A total of 1,029 samples from 2013 and 718 samples from 2022 were analyzed. Measles seroprevalence increased from 33%, 41%, 47%, and 48% in the 1-5, 6-15, 16-40, and >40 years age groups in 2013 to 77%, 71%, 89%, and 96% respectively in 2022. Rubella seroprevalence increased from 32%, 67%, 76%, and 73% to 93%, 84%, 93%, and 98% across the same age groups. No significant sex-based differences were observed for either infection. The estimated Re declined from 7.4 to 3.6 for measles and from 1.8 to 0.8 for rubella following the MR campaign period. Population immunity improved by 2022, particularly for rubella. However, lower measles seroprevalence among children aged 1-15 years indicates persistent immunity gaps despite high vaccine coverage, highlighting the need for continued surveillance and targeted strategies to achieve measles-rubella elimination in India.

articles.title: Targeting Accelerated Aging in COPD: The AMICO (A Trial of Metformin In COpd) Trial Design.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is increasingly recognized as a disease of accelerated biological aging characterized by progressive lung function decline, emphysema progression and multiple age-related comorbidities. Current therapies improve symptoms and reduce exacerbations but have limited effects on disease progression. Metformin has demonstrated anti-aging properties through modulation of pathways involved in oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction and cellular senescence, making it a potential disease-modifying treatment in COPD.

METHODS: AMICO (A Trial of Metformin In COPD) is an investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase III trial conducted in anonymous. A total of 212 patients with clinically stable COPD, centrilobular emphysema on computed tomography, post-bronchodilator FEV1 40%-70% predicted and accelerated FEV1 decline (>40 mL·year-1) will be randomized (1:1) to receive metformin (850 mg twice daily) or matching placebo for 36 months in addition to standard COPD treatment. Assessments include pulmonary function, chest computed tomography, exercise capacity, health status, muscle strength, body composition, age associated comorbidities development and aging-related biomarkers.The primary endpoint is the annual rate of FEV1 decline over 36 months. Secondary endpoints include emphysema progression, changes in diffusing capacity, COPD Assessment Test score, 6-minute walk distance, BODE index, handgrip strength, exacerbations, major cardiovascular events, cancer incidence and renal dysfunction.

CONCLUSIONS: AMICO is the first randomized trial specifically designed to evaluate metformin as a gerotherapeutic and disease-modifying intervention in COPD. The study may provide novel evidence supporting geroscience-based approaches to slow disease progression and improve long-term outcomes in patients with COPD.

articles.title: Association of HIV infection with short-term major adverse cardiovascular events among Chinese patients with carotid atherosclerosis: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: People living with HIV (PLWH) suffer accelerated atherosclerotic injury, but real-world Chinese cohort data excluding patients with pre-existing cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases remain scarce regarding HIV-related incident major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). This study aimed to explore the independent associations between HIV infection and 2-year incident MACE among Chinese patients with carotid atherosclerosis free of prior cardiovascular events, and identify correlated metabolic and renal factors.

METHODS: A retrospective single-center cohort design was adopted. We enrolled patients with ultrasound-confirmed carotid atherosclerosis from January 2020 to June 2023, excluded individuals with prior coronary heart disease, ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack, and conducted standardized 2-year follow-up for all eligible participants. Univariate statistical tests screened variables correlated with MACE; variables with univariate p < 0.05 plus core clinical confounders (age, sex, hypertension, diabetes) were incorporated into multivariate binary logistic regression to identify independent correlates of new-onset MACE.

RESULTS: Patients with HIV infection showed significantly younger age compared with HIV-negative counterparts (63.55 ± 10.81 years vs 70.61 ± 9.75 years, p < 0.001). The cumulative 2-year occurrence rate of MACE was markedly higher in the HIV-positive group (40.4% versus 22.9%, p = 0.023). Multivariate regression analysis verified four independent risk markers for incident MACE: HIV seropositivity (OR = 2.24, 95%CI 1.19-4.22, p = 0.012), baseline active smoking (OR = 1.98, 95%CI 1.07-3.66, p = 0.028), reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) (OR = 2.15, 95%CI 1.15-4.02, p = 0.017) and hyperuricemia (OR = 1.89, 95%CI 1.02-3.51, p = 0.043).

CONCLUSION: Chinese people living with HIV (PLWH) combined with carotid atherosclerosis develop atherosclerotic lesions at an earlier age and carry elevated short-term MACE risk. Integrated intervention strategies covering HIV viral control, smoking cessation, renal function protection and serum uric acid management can effectively improve cardiovascular long-term prognosis for this special population.

Pulmonary Vein Anatomy, Cooling Kinetics, and Recurrence After Cryoballoon Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cryoballoon pulmonary vein isolation depends on balloon-to-ostium contact. We assessed whether computed tomography-derived pulmonary vein ostial area (OA) and ovality index (OI) were associated with cooling after accounting for pulmonary vein (PV) branch and within-patient clustering, and whether PV anatomy was associated with recurrence.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied 120 patients with symptomatic atrial fibrillation undergoing second-generation cryoballoon ablation. Vein-level associations with nadir temperature, 1 min temperature, and time to isolation were assessed using linear mixed-effects models with a patient random intercept and PV branch as a fixed effect; generalized estimating equations served as sensitivity analyses. Given 23 post-blanking recurrences, logistic models were limited to left atrial volume index (LAVI) and one clinically selected covariate, with Firth-penalized regression as a sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: All patients achieved acute PV isolation. Larger OA was associated with lower nadir temperature (β = -0.583°C per 50 mm2; 95% CI, -0.910 to -0.257; p < 0.001) and 1 min temperature (β = -0.441°C per 50 mm2; 95% CI, -0.764 to -0.118; p = 0.008) after branch and clustering adjustment. OI was not associated with either temperature outcome. Twenty-three patients (19.2%) developed recurrent atrial arrhythmia. LAVI was associated with recurrence (adjusted OR, 1.659 per 10 mL/m2; 95% CI, 1.250-2.201; p < 0.001), whereas persistent AF was not.

CONCLUSIONS: OA showed a modest association with cryoballoon temperatures but should not be used as a stand-alone prognostic marker. LAVI remained associated with recurrence in parsimonious patient-level analyses.

articles.title: Education Research: Strengthening the Neurology Pipeline: The American Academy of Neurology Medical Student Symposium (2018-2025).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The American Academy of Neurology (AAN) Medical Student Symposium (MSS) was established in 2018 to address the shortage of neurologists, with events consisting of keynote speakers, panel events, and networking opportunities to engage medical students with neurology. The aim of this study was to highlight the evolution of the MSS, to identify the elements participants perceived most beneficial, and to describe the longitudinal impact of the symposium on attendees.

METHODS: We describe the MSS, recruitment processes, and its evolution from 2018 to 2025. To determine the longitudinal impact of the MSS on medical student interest in neurology, 1,177 attendees of past MSS were invited to participate in an online survey. Data were collected using Qualtrics from August 25, 2025, to September 19, 2025.

RESULTS: MSS student attendance between 2018 and 2025 grew from 152 in 2018 to 353 participants in 2025. Most attendees were third-year medical students (MS3, 34%), followed by second-year (MS2, 19%) and fourth-year (MS4, 21%) medical students. In total, 129/1,079 individuals responded, and 120/129 respondents completed the survey. Interest in a neurology specialty increased after the MSS for 92% of participants. The components ranked as most influential included the networking lunch and subspecialty networking. As of 2025, 39% of 2018 MSS attendees were active AAN members, whereas 82% of 2025 attendees were active members.

DISCUSSION: Most participants expressed increased interest in neurology after the MSS, reporting that the networking components of the event were most influential. Participants highlighted increased knowledge of neurologic careers and opportunities for mentorship as the most impactful elements of the MSS. Longitudinal survey results indicated sustained interest in careers in neurology and continued AAN engagement. Study limitations include possible selection and response bias. Given the lack of a distinct comparison group, we are also unable to assess the MSS's impact on those with neutral or little preexisting interest in neurology. Future MSS iterations will continue to streamline the evaluation process to collect attendee feedback and adapt the agenda based on participant needs.

articles.title: Effect of Kunxian capsule, a novel Tripterygium wilfordii preparation, on reducing proteinuria and slowing renal function decline in diabetic kidney disease: a 48-week randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD), a leading cause of chronic kidney disease, remains a clinical challenge despite renin-angiotensin system blockade. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of adding Kunxian capsule to standard therapy with irbesartan in patients with DKD.

METHODS: Eighty patients with DKD were randomly assigned to either the experimental group (standard therapy with irbesartan plus Kunxian capsule) or the control group (standard therapy with irbesartan) for 48 weeks. Primary outcomes included the proteinuria remission rate, degree of proteinuria reduction, and median time to remission. Secondary outcomes included the slope of eGFR decline and the incidence of renal composite hard endpoint. Safety was assessed by monitoring adverse events. This trial was registered in ClinicalTrials.gov on March 2, 2021 (No. NCT04981613).

RESULTS: In the intention-to-treat analysis, the experimental group had a higher proteinuria remission rate (57.50% vs. 25.00%), a shorter median time to remission (5 months vs. not reached), and a greater reduction in 24-hour urinary protein than the control group. A lower incidence of renal composite hard endpoint was observed in the experimental group (10.00% vs. 32.50%), accompanied by a slower eGFR decline. No significant differences in the incidence of adverse events were observed between the two groups. Inflammatory markers, including C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate, were significantly reduced in the experimental group.

CONCLUSIONS: Adding Kunxian capsule to standard therapy with irbesartan improved the proteinuria remission rate and attenuated renal function decline in patients with DKD, supporting its potential as a promising adjunctive therapy.

articles.title: Urinary ubiquitin-specific protease 2 (USP2) as a diagnostic biomarker for chronic kidney disease: an integrated multi-omics and network analysis.
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with progressive metabolic and molecular dysregulation, yet reliable noninvasive biomarkers remain limited. Ubiquitin-specific protease 2 (USP2) regulates transforming growth factor-β signaling and ferroptosis through lactylation-dependent deubiquitinase activity, but its clinical relevance in CKD remains unclear. We enrolled 25 patients with CKD and 10 healthy controls and measured urinary USP2 levels using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Untargeted urine and serum metabolomics and plasma proteomics were integrated with weighted gene co-expression network analysis, mediation analysis, and pathway enrichment. Urinary USP2 was significantly higher in patients with CKD than in healthy controls and remained independently associated with CKD after adjustment for age and sex. USP2 achieved an AUC of 0.936, and the USP2 + Age + Sex model achieved an AUC of 0.972. Decision curve analysis supported the clinical utility of USP2-containing models. FDR-adjusted multi-omics analyses identified urinary and serum metabolite modules and plasma protein modules associated with USP2 and CKD. Mediation analysis suggested that selected urinary and serum metabolites may link USP2-related molecular alterations with CKD. Sensitivity analyses in age-matched and early-stage CKD subsets further supported the diagnostic performance of USP2 and its comparison with kidney injury molecule 1. These findings support urinary USP2 as a promising noninvasive biomarker for CKD and highlight USP2-associated metabolic and proteomic networks that warrant validation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Comparison of different transplantation routes and timing for stem cell therapy in stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stem cell transplantation holds therapeutic promise for stroke, yet its clinical translation is hindered by unresolved challenges in administration routes, timing, and poor cell engraftment and survival.

METHODS: This is a narrative (non-systematic) review. Registered clinical studies were identified in ClinicalTrials.gov, the European Union Clinical Trials Register and the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, and were supplemented by targeted PubMed searches for the preclinical and mechanistic literature. Records were eligible if they evaluated stem cell transplantation for ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke and reported the delivery route and/or the transplantation time window; records reporting neither were excluded. Because direct head-to-head clinical comparisons of routes and time windows are scarce, registry data and selected preclinical studies were synthesised descriptively rather than pooled, and no meta-analysis was performed.

RESULTS: Each administration route presents a distinct profile. Intravenous injection is minimally invasive and simple but limited by pulmonary sequestration, low cerebral engraftment, and high cell dose requirements. Intra-arterial infusion offers improved targeting but shares similar limitations. Intrathecal delivery allows direct central nervous system access with concentrated doses but carries risks of cerebrospinal fluid leakage and an inflammatory microenvironment. Intracerebral implantation ensures high local engraftment and long-term survival with minimal cell numbers but is invasive and poses risks of hemorrhage and further tissue injury. Intranasal administration is non-invasive with a wide therapeutic window yet exhibits extremely low delivery efficiency. Regarding timing, intravenous and intra-arterial routes are primary in the acute phase; in the subacute phase these routes remain common, alongside intrathecal administration; for chronic stroke, intracerebral and intrathecal transplantation are the predominant strategies in clinical trials.

CONCLUSION: This review synthesizes two decades of progress and persisting challenges in stem cell therapy for stroke, focusing on delivery strategies and timing. Successful clinical translation will require further large-scale, multicenter prospective studies to optimize these critical parameters.

articles.title: Catastrophic fetal-neonatal thrombosis: a thromboinflammatory concept and the role of antiphospholipid antibodies.
articles.journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Fetal and neonatal thrombosis comprises a heterogeneous spectrum of disorders ranging from localized vascular events to rapidly progressive systemic thrombosis involving multiple vascular beds and organs. This review examines thromboinflammation and antiphospholipid antibodies (aPL) in severe fetal-neonatal thrombosis.

METHODS: This narrative, hypothesis-generating review draws on a structured, non-systematic literature search through August 31, 2026, distinguishing direct fetal and neonatal evidence from adult and experimental findings.

RESULTS: Neonatal hemostasis is characterized by a physiologically balanced but vulnerable state that may become destabilized by infection, hypoxia, endothelial injury, inflammation, and genetic or immune-mediated factors. Current evidence suggests that interactions between endothelial dysfunction, innate immune activation, platelets, coagulation, neutrophil extracellular traps, and the complement system may promote a transition from localized thrombosis to a self-amplifying thromboinflammatory process. However, a common mechanism of such progression has not been established across different fetal and neonatal thrombotic disorders. Maternal IgG aPL may cross the placenta, whereas aPL detected in some neonates may reflect presumed de novo production. The presence of aPL does not necessarily result in neonatal thrombosis, and additional prothrombotic factors reported in selected cases are consistent with, but do not establish, a "second-hit" or "multiple-hit" model.

CONCLUSION: We propose catastrophic fetal-neonatal thrombosis as an unvalidated clinical and pathogenetic framework rather than a distinct disease entity. Paired maternal-neonatal testing and longitudinal antibody assessment may help clarify antibody origin, although delayed testing limits causal interpretation. Its potential value for earlier recognition and etiologically directed diagnostic evaluation requires prospective assessment.

articles.title: Whole-tumor dual-layer spectral detector CT quantification for preoperative identification of poorly differentiated cervical squamous cell carcinoma: An interpretable prediction model.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop an interpretable dual-layer spectral detector CT (DLCT) model for preoperative identification of poorly differentiated cervical squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC), and to compare two-dimensional region-of-interest (2D ROI) with whole-tumor three-dimensional volume-of-interest (3D VOI) parameter-extraction strategies.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 205 surgically treated patients with CSCC who underwent contrast-enhanced DLCT before surgery. Patients were assigned to training (n = 113), internal validation (n = 47), and temporal validation (n = 45) cohorts. Parameters were extracted using 2D ROI- and 3D VOI-based analyses. Clinical, 2D DLCT, 3D DLCT, and DLCT-clinical fusion models were developed using multivariable logistic regression and evaluated by discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis.

RESULTS: 3D VOI-based analysis showed higher interobserver reproducibility than 2D ROI-based analysis (mean intraclass correlation coefficient, 0.950 vs. 0.875; P < 0.001). The 3D DLCT model included arterial-phase 70-keV virtual monoenergetic attenuation (CT70keV-AP), arterial-phase normalized effective atomic number (NZeffAP), and venous-phase normalized iodine density (NIDVP). Its areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) were 0.897, 0.895, and 0.885 in the training, internal validation, and temporal validation cohorts, respectively. The 2D DLCT and 3D DLCT models did not differ significantly in AUCs after multiple-comparison correction. The fusion model achieved AUCs of 0.900, 0.916, and 0.881, respectively, outperforming the clinical model without significantly improving on the 3D DLCT model.

CONCLUSIONS: 3D DLCT quantification provides an interpretable and noninvasive imaging biomarker for preoperative identification of poorly differentiated CSCC and may support individualized risk stratification. External validation in larger multicenter cohorts is needed to confirm generalizability.

articles.title: Bodily Self Disturbances: A New Clinical Marker of Persistent Postural-Perceptual Dizziness.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Persistent Postural-Perceptual Dizziness (PPPD) is among the most prevalent chronic neuro-otologic disorders, affecting 15%-20% of adults seen in neurology and specialized dizziness clinics. Classified as a functional vestibular disorder with established diagnostic criteria, PPPD typically follows peripheral or central otoneurological disorders. However, the mechanisms underlying the transition to chronic perceptual dizziness remain unclear. Beyond maladaptive postural control and visual dependence, theoretical models implicate altered multisensory integration and disrupted predictive processing. Such mechanisms may extend to disturbances of the bodily self, a dimension increasingly recognized in functional neurologic disorders, but not yet systematically investigated in PPPD.

METHODS: We characterized bodily self disturbances in PPPD by assessing depersonalization-derealization (DD) symptoms in a large cross-sectional study (n = 455), including 100 patients with PPPD, 180 patients with other otoneurological disorders, and 175 healthy controls. DD symptoms were assessed using the Cambridge Depersonalization Scale, alongside measures of anxiety, depression, dizziness-related impairment, and PPPD symptom severity.

RESULTS: Patients with PPPD exhibited markedly elevated DD symptoms compared with both other otoneurological disorders and healthy controls. Notably, 20% of patients with PPPD met the threshold for clinical DD, compared with 7.2% of other otoneurological disorders and <1% of controls. DD severity in PPPD overlapped with levels observed in other functional neurologic disorders but remained lower than in primary dissociative disorders. Factor analyses identified 3 DD dimensions: bodily self disturbances, cognitive and affective detachment, and numbing. Only bodily self disturbances, capturing disruptions in self-location, agency, body ownership, and first-person perspective, robustly differentiated PPPD from other otoneurological disorders (η2 = 0.20, p < 0.001). This dimension predicted PPPD diagnosis (odds ratio = 1.40, p < 0.001) and showed significant discriminative ability (AUC = 0.66). Individuals in the highest decile of bodily self disturbances had nearly ten-fold increased odds of PPPD. Structural equation modelling confirmed a direct effect of PPPD on bodily self disturbances, partially mediated by depressive symptoms but independent of age, sex, migraine, and anxiety.

DISCUSSION: These findings identify DD as a previously unrecognized component of the PPPD phenotype and establish bodily self disturbances as a novel clinical marker for PPPD, refining phenotyping and informing pathophysiologic models.

articles.title: From Building Foundations to Shaping Practice: Fifteen Years of Neurology® Clinical Practice and a Vision for the Future.
Assessing policy readiness for climate-informed infectious disease early warning systems in Vietnam: a scoping review and stakeholder consultation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Climate change is reshaping infectious disease patterns, increasing the need for climate-informed early warning systems (EWSs). However, the extent to which Vietnam's governance frameworks support their development and implementation remains unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To assess policies and guidelines governing infectious disease EWSs in Vietnam and identify gaps and opportunities to strengthen system readiness.

METHODS: A policy review using a modified scoping review approach was supplemented by qualitative stakeholder consultations. National regulatory documents issued since 2000 and in effect as of July 2026 were identified through Vietnamese legal databases. Documents were analysed thematically and mapped against the core components of EWSs. Twelve key stakeholders were interviewed to contextualise policy findings and explore implementation challenges.

RESULTS: Fifteen policy documents met the inclusion criteria. Vietnam has established strong legal and policy foundations for disease reporting, outbreak investigation, emergency response, and intersectoral coordination. Recent policies increasingly recognise climate change adaptation, environmental risks, digital transformation, and cross-sector collaboration, creating an enabling environment for the development of EWSs. However, these policies primarily provide strategic direction and institutional support rather than operational guidance for implementing EWSs. Key gaps include fragmented governance arrangements for data sharing and integration across meteorological, epidemiological, vector, laboratory, and vulnerability datasets; limited guidance on model validation and adoption; weak mechanisms linking forecasts to authorised anticipatory actions; and constraints related to financing and workforce capacity.

CONCLUSIONS: Strengthening policies and operational guidance for forecasting, data integration, and forecast-based action will be critical to enhancing preparedness for and responses to climate-sensitive infectious diseases in Vietnam.

articles.title: Hepatitis B seroprevalence among children aged 0.6-14 years in Jiangsu, China, in 2023-2025.
articles.abstract: China has implemented universal hepatitis B vaccination in all neonates since 2002 and has enhanced prophylaxis against mother-to-child transmission of hepatitis B virus (HBV) by providing charge-free hepatitis B immunoglobulin in infants of HBV-infected mothers since 2011 and by recommending routine antiviral prophylaxis in HBV-infected mothers with high viral loads since 2020. We aimed to survey the seroprevalence of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) in children born from 2010 to 2024 in Jiangsu Province, based on convenience sampling in children who visited hospitals. We tested hepatitis B markers in 20,317 children aged 7.9 ± 4.1 years, with 11477 boys and 8840 girls, from 8 cities across Jiangsu during February 2023 to December 2025. Of them, 14 (0.069%, 95% CI: 0.038-0.116) were HBsAg positive. The positive rates of HBsAg in 0.5-<3, 3-<6, 6-<9, 9-<12, and 12-<15 years groups were 0% (0/2520), 0% (0/3858), 0.024% (1/4243), 0.136% (6/4401), and 0.132% (7/5295), respectively (P = .01489). The overall positive rate of antibody against HBsAg was 68.11% (12046/17686), with a decreasing trend over the ages (from 96.17% in 0.5-<3 year children to 48.41% in 12-<15 year children). In HBsAg-negative children, the positive rate of antibody against hepatitis B core antigen was 7.68% (1383/18007), increasing from 4.23% in 0.5-<3 year children to 7.84% in 12-<15 year children (Z = 5.0398, P < .0001). The present study showed that HBsAg prevalence among children in Jiangsu has substantially declined since the implementation of enhanced prevention of HBV perinatal infection.

articles.title: Pneumococcal vaccination for prevention of infection and diagnosis of antibody deficiency in the extended conjugated vaccine era.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCV) have transformed pneumococcal disease prevention. Recent expansion to higher-valency formulations (PCV15, PCV20, PCV21) and updated Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) recommendations extending coverage to all healthy PCV-naïve adults ≥50 years in the United States have introduced new complexity in vaccine selection, timing, and dosing. Concurrently, universal childhood conjugate priming complicates the diagnosis of specific antibody deficiency (SAD), as prior PCV immunization alters interpretation of the Pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccines (PPSV23) challenge. This review synthesizes recent evidence on vaccine effectiveness in invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) prevention, serotype dynamics, and the evolving diagnostic framework for SAD.

RECENT FINDINGS: In October 2024, ACIP expanded pneumococcal vaccination to all PCV-naïve adults ≥50 years. Higher-valency conjugate vaccines continue to reduce invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD), and pipeline data projects that candidate PCV31 vaccine would cover 85-94% of pediatric and adult IPD Accurate diagnosis of SAD remains challenging in the PCV vaccine era stressing the importance of finding a reliable polysaccharide antigen for vaccine challenge., PPSV23 responses must be assessed using non-PCV serotypes in conjugate-primed patients and alternative polysaccharide antigens such as Typhim Vi may offer complementary utility with high specificity but limited sensitivity.

SUMMARY: There has been a marked decline in PID in the pneumococcal conjugate vaccine era, yet serotype replacement persists. Vaccine selection now requires individualized decision-making, and SAD diagnosis must be adapted in PCV-primed patients to avoid incorrect interpretation.

articles.title: Home blood pressure monitoring reclassifies hypertension phenotypes and influences treatment decisions: real-world evidence from Saudi and Egyptian cohorts.
Proximal Femoral Cancellous Bone Density Distribution and Internal Fixation Failure in Intertrochanteric Fractures: A Radiological Study and Internally Validated Prediction Model.
articles.journal: Journal of investigative surgery : the official journal of the Academy of Surgical Research
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate proximal femoral cancellous bone density distribution and its association with fixation stability in intertrochanteric fractures, and to develop and internally validate a predictive model.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 220 patients with intertrochanteric fractures treated with proximal femoral nail anti-rotation (PFNA). Fixation failure was defined as cutout, blade migration >5 mm, neck-shaft angle loss >10°, rotational deformity >15°, implant failure, or revision surgery. Preoperative CT Hounsfield units (HU) were measured in the femoral head, intertrochanteric region, and calcar femorale. A predictive model incorporating age, tip-apex distance (TAD), and calcar HU was internally validated using 1,000 bootstrap resamples.

RESULTS: Fixation failure decreased across increasing density-gradient categories (P for trend = 0.037), although the overall difference was nonsignificant (P = 0.112). Age (OR = 1.17, 95% CI: 1.04-1.30), TAD (OR = 1.19, 95% CI: 1.08-1.30), and calcar HU (OR = 0.97, 95% CI: 0.95-0.98) were independently associated with failure. The model achieved an apparent AUC of 0.84 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.83.

CONCLUSION: Lower calcar HU was independently associated with fixation failure. The combined model showed good discrimination, but external validation is needed before clinical application.

articles.title: The American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association classification of chronic hypertension in pregnancy has better clinical applicability and risk assessment than the traditional severe and mild hypertension approach - lessons from a population-based study.
articles.journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic hypertension (CHTN) increases the risk of superimposed preeclampsia, contributing to maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality. Accurate hypertension classification is therefore essential for risk stratification, antenatal surveillance, prevention, and outcomes. The clinical impact of applying the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) classification, compared with the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) criteria, in pregnancy remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: To determine the impact of ACC/AHA versus ACOG hypertension classifications on the prevalence of CHTN and pregnancy outcomes.

STUDY DESIGN: This population-based retrospective cohort study used a computerized maternity database from a tertiary hospital. All parturients with singleton gestations initiating prenatal care in the first trimester were included (n = 136,606). CHTN was categorized according to ACOG and ACC/AHA criteria. Maternal, fetal, and neonatal outcomes were assessed. Statistical analyses were performed using R-Studio, with ANOVA and Poisson regression models evaluating associations between CHTN severity and outcomes.

RESULTS: The prevalence of CHTN was 2.9% (4,127/137,606) by ACOG criteria and 3.9% (5,424/137,606) by ACC/AHA criteria (p < 0.001). Under ACOG classification, both mild and severe range CHTN were independently associated with preeclampsia or eclampsia (RR 4.15, 95% CI 3.69-4.65; and RR 3.19, 95% CI 2.82-3.59, respectively). Using ACC/AHA criteria, elevated blood pressure (EBP), stage 1 CHTN (S1CHTN), and stage 2 CHTN (S2CHTN) were each independently associated with preeclampsia or eclampsia (EBP: RR 2.34, 95% CI 2.04-2.65; S1CHTN: RR 4.00, 95% CI 3.56-4.50; S2CHTN: RR 3.32, 95% CI 2.88-3.80). Mild CHTN, S1CHTN, and S2CHTN were independently associated with small-for-gestational-age neonates, while both ACOG-defined CHTN and ACC/AHA-defined EBP, S1CHTN, and S2CHTN were associated with preterm birth.

CONCLUSION: Application of the ACC/AHA classification identifies a larger proportion of pregnant individuals as having CHTN. Notably, even those with elevated blood pressure had a two-fold increased risk of preeclampsia compared with the general obstetric population. These findings support the clinical relevance of the ACC/AHA classification in pregnancy and suggest that its implementation may improve identification of patients who may benefit from targeted preeclampsia prevention strategies.

articles.title: Risk factors for cognitive impairment in patients undergoing hemodialysis: an umbrella review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Cognitive impairment is a common complication in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis. This umbrella review and meta-analysis systematically evaluated the factors associated with cognitive impairment and, separately, cognitive frailty in adults receiving hemodialysis. PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to January 2026. Five meta-analyses involving 97 associations were included; three evaluated cognitive impairment and two evaluated cognitive frailty. For cognitive impairment, older age, female sex, diabetes, cerebrovascular disease, multiple comorbidities, impaired physical performance, lower hemoglobin levels, and inflammatory markers were associated with increased risk, whereas higher educational attainment was associated with reduced risk (OR = 0.21, 95% CI: 0.13-0.34). For cognitive frailty, older age, female sex, depression (OR = 4.66, 95% CI: 2.98-7.27), stroke history (OR = 2.94, 95% CI: 1.72-5.03), comorbidities, malnutrition, longer dialysis duration (OR = 2.30, 95% CI: 1.49-3.53), low-flux hemodialysis (OR = 4.16, 95% CI: 1.97-8.79), and interdialytic hypotension (OR = 2.42, 95% CI: 1.53-4.21) were associated with increased risk, whereas higher education and serum albumin were protective. Only two associations had moderate-certainty evidence; all others were rated low or very low. Cognitive impairment and cognitive frailty are associated with multiple demographic, clinical, and dialysis-related factors but represent distinct outcomes that should be interpreted separately. Further high-quality prospective studies are warranted.

articles.title: Associations between psychiatric comorbidity and intensive care unit length of stay, hospital length of stay, and in-hospital mortality: A retrospective observational study.
articles.journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences
articles.abstract:
AIM: Psychiatric comorbidities are common among patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU), but findings regarding their impact on clinical outcomes remain inconsistent. Additionally, existing studies have often included patients admitted for suicide attempts or self-harm, leaving insufficient evidence about the independent effects of psychiatric comorbidity on clinical outcomes. To address this gap, this study investigated the independent association of psychiatric comorbidity with ICU length of stay, hospital length of stay, and in-hospital mortality among patients admitted to the ICU, excluding those admitted for suicide attempts or self-harm.

METHODS: Of the 2599 patients admitted to the ICU of a university hospital, 2192 were included in the analysis. After adjusting for age, sex, body mass index, admission category, and severity score, generalized linear models were used to evaluate ICU and hospital length of stay, and logistic regression analysis was used to assess in-hospital mortality.

RESULTS: Among the 2192 patients included in the analysis, 75 had psychiatric comorbidity. In adjusted analyses, psychiatric comorbidity was not significantly associated with ICU length of stay, hospital length of stay, or in-hospital mortality.

CONCLUSION: No participants were admitted to the ICU for suicide attempts or self-harm, and psychiatric comorbidity was not an independent predictor of ICU length of stay, hospital length of stay, or in-hospital mortality. Thus, in this ICU population, no statistically significant association was detected between psychiatric comorbidity and short-term clinical outcomes. Therefore, caution is needed when estimating ICU outcomes based solely on the presence of psychiatric comorbidity.

articles.title: When Quality Indicators Become Competencies: Indonesia's New Emergency Medicine Standard and the Core Components of CBME.
Learning Curve Cumulative Summation Method for Ocular Ultrasound.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The current American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP) guidelines recommend that trainees perform 25 ocular ultrasound scans before being considered competent. This threshold has not been substantiated for ocular ultrasound. The purpose of this study was to determine the number of ocular scans required to reach competency in ocular ultrasound using the learning curve cumulative sum (LC-CUSUM) analysis. A secondary objective was to evaluate whether individualized learning curve feedback influences competency attainment.

METHODS: Using the LC-CUSUM method with an 85% success threshold, we assessed the number of scans needed to achieve competency in both image acquisition and interpretation among first-year emergency medicine residents. For a secondary analysis, residents were then randomized into two groups: one receiving bimonthly personalized learning curve updates alongside standard feedback, and another receiving standard feedback alone. Competency attainment was compared between groups.

RESULTS: Twenty-six residents were included. LC-CUSUM analysis determined that 21 studies were needed to reach competency. The median number of scans per resident was 26.5 (IQR: 22-30). At the end of the academic year, 17 residents (65%) reached technical competency, 10 residents (35%) reached interpretation competency, and 10 residents (35%) reached competency in both domains. Fifteen residents (58%) remained in the learning phase. There was no significant difference between competency attainment or perceived feedback in the randomized feedback groups.

CONCLUSION: LC-CUSUM analysis suggests that competency in ocular ultrasound may be achieved after approximately 21 individual-eye scans, or approximately 10.5 bilateral ocular exams, fewer than half the 25 bilateral examinations recommended by ACEP. Individualized learning curve feedback did not improve competency attainment or perceptions of feedback compared with standard feedback.

articles.title: Analysis of adverse events following immunization after immunization schedule adjustment for acellular DTaP combined vaccine among 6-year-old children in Hangzhou.
articles.abstract: In 2025, China adjusted national immunization schedule to administer a booster dose of acellular diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis combined vaccine (DTaP) to 6-year-old children, replacing the previously used diphtheria-tetanus combined vaccine (DT). Post-marketing safety surveillance of this newly implemented schedule is critical to evaluate the tolerability and safety of DTaP in this age group. To evaluate the epidemiological characteristics and safety of adverse events following immunization (AEFI) among 6-year-old children after administration of DTaP following the 2025 national immunization schedule adjustment in Hangzhou. To compare the incidence of AEFI between DTaP and DT. AEFI surveillance and vaccination data of 6-year-old children who received DTaP or DT from 2024 to 2025 in Hangzhou were collected. The total sample size was 239 480 doses of diphtheria-tetanus-containing vaccines. Descriptive statistics, chi-square test, and reporting odds ratio disproportionality analysis were used for statistical analysis. The overall reporting rate of AEFI following vaccination with diphtheria- and tetanus-containing vaccines among 6-year-old children in Hangzhou was 466.01 per 100,000 doses. The AEFI reporting rate for DTaP (833.58 per 100,000 doses) was significantly higher than that for DT (181.49 per 100,000 doses) (χ2 = 539.95, P < .05). AEFIs after DTaP vaccination were predominantly general reactions (99.31%), and no severe AEFI was reported. Disproportionality analysis detected positive signals only for local redness/swelling as a general reaction for both DTaP and DT. DTaP vaccination is safe and well-tolerated after the immunization schedule adjustment. Most AEFIs are mild general reactions including fever, redness, and induration, with reporting rates within the expected range and no obvious safety risks.

articles.title: Modeling the cost-effectiveness of NVX-CoV2705 and the public health impact of vaccination for the prevention of seasonal COVID-19 in the US.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Older adults and those with comorbidities have increased risk of severe disease and mortality from COVID-19. This analysis estimated the cost-effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccination versus no vaccination in the US and potential impact of increased vaccine coverage.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: A Markov-based model was updated using the latest epidemiology and vaccine reactogenicity data. Cases, costs, and outcomes for individuals aged 18-64 with ≥1 comorbidity and ≥65 years were estimated for NVX-CoV2705 (Nuvaxovid) versus no vaccination from a third-party payer perspective. Scenario analyses considered the societal perspective and analogous comparisons for BNT162b2 (Comirnaty), mRNA-1273 (Spikevax), and mRNA-1283 (mNEXSPIKE). Results were scaled for public health impact analyses.

RESULTS: Base-case results associated NVX-CoV2705 with fewer cases (0.0447), hospitalizations (0.0037), and deaths (0.0004) per person on average. NVX-CoV2705 yielded an ICER of $9,840/QALY gained, reflecting fewer QALYs lost (0.0039) alongside increased direct costs ($38.09) per person. Differences for mRNA vaccines were driven by price and reactogenicity. Increasing vaccine coverage by 5-15 percentage points resulted in 114-341 hospitalizations and 11-33 deaths averted per 1,000,000 individuals.

CONCLUSIONS: NVX-CoV2705 was predicted to be cost-effective over no vaccination. This analysis included a more granular approach to modeling reactogenicity events, an important consideration in vaccine cost-effectiveness analyses.

articles.title: RACK1 links immune signaling and translation during host-pathogen interactions.
articles.abstract: The outcome of an infectious disease results from a dynamic interplay between host immune responses and pathogen virulence mechanisms. RACK1 is a highly conserved scaffold protein that integrates signal transduction, translational control, and cellular stress responses. Emerging evidence positions RACK1 as a central hub at the host-pathogen interface. It coordinates host immune responses, yet pathogens also exploit it to promote their survival and persistence. However, current knowledge of RACK1 in host-pathogen interactions remains fragmented, with most studies focusing on specific pathogens. This review summarizes the structural and cellular functions of RACK1 in host defense, examines the molecular strategies employed by pathogens to exploit RACK1-dependent pathways during infection, and integrates findings across diverse infectious systems to provide a comprehensive overview of RACK1-mediated host-pathogen interactions. We further discuss the role of RACK1 in infection outcomes, its therapeutic potential, and key directions for future research.

articles.title: HSC71 acetylation confers protection against Spiroplasma eriocheiris infection by inhibiting apoptosis and promoting ROS production in arthropods.
articles.abstract: Members of the HSP70 family are indispensable components of host innate immunity, and their functions are finely tuned by post-translational modifications. However, the role of HSP70 post-translational modifications in modulating immune functions during pathogenic infection remains poorly understood. This study investigated the mechanisms that underlie acetylation modification of heat shock cognate 71 kDa protein (HSC71)-mediated resistance to intracellular pathogen Spiroplasma eriocheiris infection in crabs. Mechanistically, carnitine O-acetyltransferase (Crat) acetylated HSC71 at lysine 579 (K579), which prevented its ubiquitination by promoting the dissociation of E3 ubiquitin ligase CHIP, thereby improving HSC71 stability. In HSC71-deficient or Crat-deficient crabs, hemocyte apoptosis was markedly enhanced, leading to higher host mortality upon S. eriocheiris challenge. Meanwhile, K579 acetylation on HSC71 weakened the interaction between HSC71 and superoxide dismutase (SOD), resulting in the accumulation of intracellular ROS and thereby restricting S. eriocheiris propagation. Pharmacological inhibition of the deacetylase SIRT1 with EX-527 enhanced HSC71 acetylation, elevated ROS production, and reduced host susceptibility to S. eriocheiris infection in crabs. Notably, EX-527 similarly enhanced the acetylation of Drosophila melanogaster HSC71 homolog, HSPA8, which in turn impaired its interaction with SOD. This led to elevated ROS levels and restricted intracellular proliferation of S. eriocheiris in Drosophila S2 cells. Therefore, this study established the modulation of HSC71 acetylation as a promising avenue to combat S. eriocheiris infection.

articles.title: Global burden of chronic kidney disease attributable to hypertension due to high body mass index: projections to 2050.
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects approximately 9.1% of the global population, equivalent to approximately 843 million individuals as of 2021, with hypertension (HTN) as a major contributor. High body mass index (BMI) exacerbates HTN-related kidney injury, but the global burden of HTN-related CKD attributable to high BMI remains poorly characterized. Using data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 study for 1990-2021, we estimated attributable deaths, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), the age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR), and the age-standardized disability-adjusted life-year rate (ASDR). Temporal trends were assessed using the estimated annual percentage change (EAPC), and a Bayesian age-period-cohort model was used to project rates to 2050. Attributable deaths increased from 36,476 in 1990 to 179,788 in 2021, and DALYs increased from 1.01 million to 4.26 million. ASMR increased from 1.09 to 2.19 per 100,000 (EAPC, 4.22%), and ASDR increased from 26.04 to 50.11 per 100,000 (EAPC, 3.63%). Central Sub-Saharan Africa had the highest ASMR (7.66 per 100,000), whereas High-income North America had the fastest increase in ASMR (EAPC, 5.63%). ASMR and ASDR were higher in men than in women. Death counts peaked at ages 85-89 years in both sexes, whereas DALYs peaked at ages 60-64 years in men and 65-69 years in women. Crude rates were higher in populations with a higher sociodemographic index (SDI), whereas the relative burden became more concentrated in lower-SDI populations; concentration indices changed from -0.10 to -0.17 for deaths and from -0.06 to -0.08 for DALYs. By 2050, ASMR is projected to reach 4.44 per 100,000 (95% credible interval [CI], 3.70-5.20), and ASDR is projected to reach 77.15 per 100,000 (95% CI, 1.81-152.49). The high BMI-attributable burden of HTN-related CKD is increasing and remains unequally distributed. These findings support integrated obesity prevention and hypertension control, with priority given to high-risk regions and older adults.

articles.title: Association between pancreatic ectopic fat deposition and QCT-assessed bone mass status in patients with chronic kidney disease: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) are at increased risk of bone abnormalities. Beyond disturbances in mineral metabolism, ectopic fat deposition may also be associated with skeletal abnormalities in CKD. However, the relationship between pancreatic fat and bone mass status remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between mean pancreatic fat fraction and quantitative computed tomography (QCT)-assessed bone mass status in patients with CKD.

METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 327 patients with CKD. Vertebral volumetric bone mineral density was measured using QCT to classify bone mass status as normal bone mass, osteopenia, or osteoporosis. Mean pancreatic fat fraction was quantified from CT images. Ordinal logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS), subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses were performed to evaluate its association with bone mass status.

RESULTS: Mean pancreatic fat fraction was highest in patients with osteoporosis (p < 0.001). In the fully adjusted model, each 5-percentage-point increase in mean pancreatic fat fraction was associated with higher odds of a more severe bone mass category (OR = 1.481, 95% CI: 1.152-1.905, p = 0.002). RCS analysis showed a significant overall association (p = 0.009), with no evidence of nonlinearity (p = 0.290). No statistically significant interactions were detected for sex, age, diabetes status, or CKD stage.

CONCLUSION: A higher mean pancreatic fat fraction was associated with more severe bone mass categories in patients with CKD after adjustment for the measured covariates. QCT-based pancreatic fat assessment may provide additional information on metabolic features associated with bone mass abnormalities in CKD.

articles.title: Integrative single cell and machine learning analysis identifies fibroblast centric hub genes and therapeutic candidates in lung adenocarcinoma and ischemic cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) are distinct diseases but may share fibroblast mediated mechanisms involving tissue remodeling and inflammation. However, their common molecular features at single cell resolution remain insufficiently defined.

METHODS: We integrated single cell RNA sequencing datasets from ICM and LUAD with bulk transcriptomic profiles from TCGA LUAD, GSE18842, and GSE48166. Differential expression analysis identified 36 shared core genes. A total of 127 combinations of machine learning algorithms and feature selection methods were benchmarked to identify six hub genes: KRTCAP3, RUNX2, DBF4B, C11orf80, COL3A1, and ZFP64. UCell, scMetabolism, SCISSOR, Monocle 3, CellChat, scTenifoldNet/scTenifoldKnk, virtual drug screening, and molecular docking were used for functional characterization.

RESULTS: Fibroblasts were the dominant cellular source of the six hub genes in both ICM and LUAD. COL3A1 progressively increased along fibroblast pseudotime trajectories. Virtual overexpression and knockout analyses showed convergence on extracellular matrix organization, inflammatory response, and immune regulation. Cell communication analysis identified fibroblasts as major senders of COLLAGEN signaling, with recipient cells shifting from inflammatory monocytes under normal conditions to proliferating macrophages in ICM and tumor cells in LUAD. Molecular docking nominated Digoxin, Ergotamine, and Ledipasvir as candidate RUNX2-binding compounds with favorable predicted docking scores.

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides a single cell framework linking ICM and LUAD through fibroblast driven extracellular matrix remodeling and inflammation, and identifies potential molecular targets and therapeutic candidates for further validation.

articles.title: From theory to practice: a "Clarify-Bridge-Practice" seminar model for graduate medical trainees entering cardiovascular research.
articles.abstract: Graduate students in clinical medicine often possess advanced theoretical knowledge but struggle to translate it into testable hypotheses and feasible experimental designs: a "knowing-doing" gap particularly pronounced in cardiovascular physiology. To address this, we developed and evaluated a "Clarify-Bridge-Practice" (CBP) seminar model in a cardiovascular course with 87 graduate students across 3 cohorts (2023-2025). The intervention comprised three 80-min seminars embedded within a 12-wk course, covering 1) causal inference and bias control, 2) critical literature synthesis, and 3) hypothesis-driven experimental design. Each seminar followed a three-phase structure: Clarify (15-min case-driven lecture distilling core concepts), Bridge (20-min structured scaffolding tools externalizing research reasoning), and Practice (45-min team-based application to realistic cardiovascular cases, culminating in a mock grant defense). Outcomes were assessed via a research literacy scale, core knowledge test, rubric-scored proposals, and thematic analysis of interviews. Research literacy scores increased from 58.7 (SD = 9.3) to 78.5 (SD = 7.0) (P < 0.001); knowledge test accuracy rose from 51.8% (SD = 12.9%) to 84.5% (SD = 9.2%) (P < 0.001). Rubric scores (max 5) ranged from 3.8 (feasibility) to 4.5 (writing quality). Qualitative data indicated that scaffolding tools reduced cognitive load, while peer critique and mock defenses fostered deeper reasoning and a shift toward a researcher identity. The CBP model appears to bridge the knowing-doing gap for graduate students entering cardiovascular research, offering a structured, replicable pedagogy applicable to other clinical and translational science training contexts.NEW & NOTEWORTHY This article presents a replicable "Clarify-Bridge-Practice" (CBP) seminar model that systematically bridges the knowing-doing gap in graduate cardiovascular research training. Unlike traditional lecture-based methodology instruction, the CBP model integrates focused conceptual teaching, structured scaffolding tools, and authentic team-based application within a single session. Mixed-methods evaluation demonstrates significant improvements in research literacy, knowledge, and experimental design quality, offering a transferable pedagogy for translational science education.

articles.title: Progress toward HIV-1 subtype C vaccines: understanding antiviral immune mechanisms and viral adaptation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: HIV-1 subtype C (HIV-1C) accounts for most infections globally, with sub-Saharan Africa bearing a disproportionate burden. Despite decades of research and multiple clinical trials, no effective prophylactic vaccine exists for this or any other HIV subtype - and candidate vaccines for subtype C are less well researched than for subtypes occurring most frequently in the developed world. The anticipated reduction in US funding for HIV treatment and prevention programs from 2026 in the regions where subtype C predominates makes the urgency of developing an effective vaccine or vaccines more acute than ever.

AREAS COVERED: This review explores the experimental vaccine investigations and clinical trials that have dealt specifically with vaccines for HIV-1 subtype C viruses, including coverage of the vectors and protein antigens used in pre- and clinical trials, vaccine regimes tested in animals and in humans, and modifications made to antigens to stabilize them and enhance immunogenicity, in the light of findings for other subtypes.

EXPERT OPINION: The appropriateness and feasibility of various vaccine approaches are discussed, and suggestions are made with regard to strategies for coping with the prevention of HIV infection in developing countries with high subtype C prevalence.

articles.title: Pharmacological treatment of bereavement-related distress: a systematic review.
