articles.abstract: Background: With the recent addition of prolonged grief disorder into diagnostic manuals both in the United States (i.e. DSM-5-TR) and internationally (i.e. ICD-11), interest in pharmacologic treatment for grief has increased.Objective: Here, we review how bereavement-related psychological distress, including treating depression secondary to bereavement, has been addressed pharmacologically and the efficacy of these treatments.Methods: Included studies focused on (1) patients bereaved by any cause, (2) patients suffering from bereavement-related mental health problems, and (3) pharmacotherapy interventions to treat those bereavement-related mental health problems. Six databases (MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, APA PsycInfo, Scopus, and Web of Science) were searched on 1 October 2020, and updated through 18 December 2024. Studies were selected by two independent reviewers and data were extracted and analysed qualitatively and quantitatively, with meta-analysis performed to calculate standardized mean differences (SMD) of treatment effects. Bias was assessed using the NIH Study Quality Assessment Tools.Results: Thirty-three studies (10 case series/studies, 7 cohort studies, 16 clinical trials) comprising 211,920 participants met eligibility criteria. Of nine medication classes represented, antidepressants were most commonly studied. No medications reduced grief symptomatology across any controlled studies; antidepressants and a beta blocker plus aspirin intervention appeared efficacious for depression symptomatology in bereaved individuals. SMD of effect of pharmacologic intervention on grief over control was negligible (-0.06 [95% CI, -0.31-0.19], data from three studies); SMD of effect of pharmacologic intervention on depression over control was small and not significant (-0.29 [95% CI, -0.68-0.10], data from two studies). Overall, study quality was low.Conclusions: Weak methodology and inconsistent data reporting presented challenges to synthesizing results. There is no evidence to support the use of current pharmacologic treatment for prolonged grief disorder, highlighting the need for further research to fill this gap in treatment options.

articles.title: Evolutionary perspectives on GLP-1 receptor agonists and the modern obesity, sedentary behaviour, and loneliness epidemics.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have transformed obesity and diabetes treatments and show promise for many other health conditions, warranting an examination of their broader health effects.

OBJECTIVE: We examine obesity, sedentary behaviour, and loneliness through an evolutionary medicine framework, assessing GLP-1RAs' role in buffering or exacerbating mismatches between novel environments and our evolved physiology.

METHODS: We searched for relevant GLP-1RA papers through PubMed utilising keywords such as "physical activity," "social," and "qualitative," and synthesise important findings in this narrative review.

RESULTS: GLP-1RAs buffer against the negative health effects of obesogenic foods through the drugs' effects on our neurobiology. These drugs may mitigate the effects of sedentary lifestyles, as it is easier to exercise without excess weight. However, rapid drug-induced weight loss may reduce fat-free mass if behavioural interventions (e.g. strength training) are not undertaken. Finally, we discuss the mismatch of reduced social eating and associated loneliness. While little data exists on the social effects of GLP-1RAs, emerging evidence suggests that GLP-1RAs may alleviate or intensify loneliness depending on an individual's milieu and specific drug response.

CONCLUSION: Our novel environments increasingly challenge human health. GLP-1RAs may help us manage these mismatches in some ways and exacerbate them in others.

articles.title: Surgical Management of Pediatric Nodular Lymphocyte-Predominant Hodgkin's Lymphoma: A Systematic Review of Surgical Outcomes and Case Report.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma (NLPHL) is a rare subtype, representing 5% of Hodgkin lymphoma cases. It is distinguished by lymphocyte-predominant cells expressing CD20 and CD79a but not CD15 and CD30. Pediatric NLPHL affects primarily males aged 4-17, often presenting with localized lymphadenopathy and favorable outcomes. NLPHL's distinct pathology makes treatment optimization critical. Long-term risks of chemotherapy and radiotherapy have led to interest in surgical resection for low-risk, early-stage disease. The objective of this study is to systematically review the available literature describing surgical management of pediatric NLPHL and summarize reported outcomes following surgical resection.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review of studies on pediatric NLPHL with a focus on surgical resection. PubMed and Scopus searches identified 37 studies, of which four met the inclusion criteria. Data regarding surgical outcomes, recurrence rates, and survival were extracted. Additionally, we analyzed our own case study of an 11-year-old male who underwent modified neck dissection followed by chemotherapy due to residual disease found on subsequent PET.

DISCUSSION: Surgical resection was associated with event-free survival rates of 57%-77% and 100% overall survival in low-risk patients across the limited available studies. Complete resection reduced recurrence risk, while incomplete resections required adjuvant therapies. Our case study demonstrated that adjunctive chemotherapy could achieve remission when residual disease is present after surgical resection as well as in cases of disease recurrence.

CONCLUSION: Surgical resection may represent a potential treatment option for carefully selected pediatric patients with localized NLPHL when complete resection is achievable. However, the current evidence base remains limited and further prospective research is needed to optimize patient selection.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of semaglutide versus placebo in adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes: updated meta-analysis of randomized trials.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity poses significant challenges for those seeking long-term weight loss through diet and exercise alone. Semaglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist approved for chronic weight management in eligible adults.

METHODS: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of semaglutide for treating obesity in adults without diabetes. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261338170). PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through February 28, 2026. We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing semaglutide with placebo in adults without diabetes with BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2 or ≥ 27 kg/m2 and at least one obesity-related comorbidity. The Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 Tool, GRADE methodology, RevMan v5.4, and CMA v3 were used for risk-of-bias assessment, certainty-of-evidence assessment, data analyses, and meta-regression analyses respectively.

RESULTS: We included 10 RCTs with a total of 7,131 participants. Risk-of-bias was judged at the level of each outcome: all included trials were at low risk-of-bias for the efficacy outcomes and the prespecified safety outcomes, while cardiovascular and psychiatric disorders raised some concerns. Compared to placebo, semaglutide produced significantly greater reductions in percentage change in body weight (WMD -12.29%, 95% CI -13.38 to -11.20, I2 88%, 95% PI -16.06 to -8.52; 10 studies, n = 6975), absolute change in body weight from baseline (WMD -12.67 kg, 95% CI -13.53 to -11.81, I2 77%, 95% PI -15.36 to -9.98; 10 studies, n = 6975), BMI (WMD -4.55 kg/m2, 95% CI -5.08 to -4.03, I2 86%, 95% PI -6.33 to -2.78; 8 studies, n = 6573), and waist circumference (WMD -9.42 cm, 95% CI -10.27 to -8.56, I2 79%, 95% PI -12.12 to -6.71; 10 studies, n = 6970). Participants assigned to semaglutide also had a higher probability of reaching a ≥ 5%, 10%, 15%, or 20% loss of body weight (9 studies, n = 6103). However, substantial between-study heterogeneity was observed for efficacy outcomes, indicating that the magnitude of benefit varied across trials. With semaglutide, individuals experienced a greater number of total adverse events (aggregate proportions 90.0% vs. 85.0%; RR 1.06, 95% CI 1.03 to 1.10, I2 72%; 9 studies, n = 6922) and discontinuation due to adverse events (aggregate proportions 6.0% vs. 3.0%; RR 1.86, 95% CI 1.41 to 2.45, I2 0%; 10 studies, n = 7129) than did individuals taking the placebo; while for serious adverse events (RR 1.16, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.51, I2 40%; 10 studies, n = 7129) the estimate was imprecise, did not establish a clear difference and the interval remains compatible with a potentially important increase in risk. These pooled figures represent average effects and may not apply equally across different semaglutide doses, formulations, treatment duration, or patient populations. Certainty-of-evidence was low for the primary outcome of percentage change in body weight and for absolute change in body weight and change in BMI, and very low for change in waist circumference.

CONCLUSION: Semaglutide was associated with clinically meaningful weight loss during trial treatment periods in adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes; however, low-certainty evidence and substantial between-study heterogeneity warrant cautious interpretation of the magnitude of benefit.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40200-026-02108-x.

articles.title: Hospital exposome and physiological resilience: Toward a new framework for understanding outcomes in peri-operative and critical care medicine.
Differences in circulating levels of non-classical monocytes and associated caspase 1 activation during Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli bacteremia.
articles.abstract: Bloodstream infections (BSI) caused by Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus are frequent and are associated with substantial mortality rate. The host immune response major determinant of the clinical outcomes during BSI. Here, we investigated the innate immune response, by characterizing peripheral blood myeloid cell subsets and caspase-1 activation as a surrogate marker of inflammasome activation in patients with E. coli or S. aureus bacteremia. We prospectively enrolled patients with monomicrobial bacteremia and analyzed peripheral blood samples by flow cytometry. We observed distinct alterations in myeloid cell composition and caspase-1 activation associated with E. coli bacteremia, including an expansion in intermediate and non-classical monocytes, and increased caspase-1 activation in non-classical monocytes. In contrast, these changes were not observed in patients with S. aureus bacteremia. Additionally, we found differences in myeloid cell subset frequencies and caspase-1 activation between patients with and without sepsis, revealing distinct profiles associated with disease severity. Importantly, the differences in myeloid cell subsets and caspase-1 activation between E. coli and S. aureus bacteremia were primarily attributable to the infecting bacteria rather than disease severity. Furthermore, our findings suggest that eosinophil counts, and caspase-1 activation may serve as potential markers to distinguish between bacterial BSI and viral infections. Overall, our study highlights the importance of considering both the infecting pathogen and disease severity when studying the host immune response during bacteremia and suggests that potential innate immune biomarkers may improve the diagnosis and clinical management of BSI.

articles.title: Extreme Thrombocytosis in Patients With Malignancy; Complications, Management and Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Extreme thrombocytosis (EXT; platelet count >1000 × 109/L) is a rare haematological abnormality that may be primary or reactive. Data on its incidence and management in patients with malignancy are limited. We retrospectively evaluated the incidence, management, and complications of EXT in patients with malignancy over a 12-year period.

METHODS: Two-hundred and twenty patients with malignancy experienced at least one episode of EXT during the study period. Patients with a known or subsequent diagnosis of myeloproliferative neoplasm (MPN) were excluded from analysis. Clinical data were collected from electronic patient records.

RESULTS: We identified 198 patients (57% female), with a median age of 55 years (range 1-86) and median follow-up of 55 months. The median peak platelet count was 1112 × 109/L (range 1001-2593). Most patients (77%) had solid tumours, lung cancer being most common (25%). MPN screening was performed in 11 patients (5.5%), with no positive results. Thrombocytosis resolved in 70% but persisted in 28%. Antiplatelets were prescribed in 16% and anticoagulation in 18%, almost exclusively for venous thrombosis. Thrombosis occurred in 42 patients (21%), predominantly venous (83%); 60% had concurrent thrombocytosis. This exceeds the reported 4%-6% thrombotic rate in patients with cancer. Among 44 paediatric patients, none received thromboprophylaxis, and four (9%) developed thrombosis. Overall mortality was 64.5%, predominantly from progressive malignancy.

CONCLUSIONS: EXT in patients with malignancy was associated with a higher-than-expected thrombotic risk. Persistent thrombocytosis was common, yet MPN screening was infrequent. These findings support further investigation of persistent EXT and evaluation of thromboprophylaxis in prospective studies.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The authors have confirmed clinical trial registration is not needed for this submission.

articles.title: Gastric Hypomotility Unmasking a Phytobezoar After Cryoballoon Pulmonary Vein Isolation.
articles.abstract: After cryoballoon pulmonary vein isolation, acute gastric hypomotility progressed to phytobezoar formation. The admission CT had already shown a mottled intragastric mass with entrapped gas, initially interpreted as retained food; when post-ablation symptoms persist, clinicians should re-examine the original imaging before escalating therapy.

articles.title: Necrotizing abdominal wall infection along a prior drain pathway: A case report and literature review.
articles.abstract: We report the case of a 37-year-old female with uncontrolled type 2 diabetes mellitus with an HbA1c of 106 mmol/mol who developed a necrotizing abdominal wall infection at the site of a prior percutaneous drain insertion for tubo-ovarian abscesses. The patient presented with recurrent flank pain, cellulitis, and a systemic inflammatory response, with imaging findings highly suspicious for necrotizing infection, which was confirmed at surgical exploration. Emergency surgical debridement, critical care support, and antibiotic therapy were required. This case highlights the need for awareness surrounding the rarity of a necrotizing infection along interventional radiology drain pathways, and we review the relevant literature.

articles.title: First evidence of an association between alexithymia and reduced humoral immunity following COVID-19 vaccination, independent of insomnia and metabolic factors in healthcare workers.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Psychological factors have been increasingly implicated in immune regulation; however, the role of emotional awareness in shaping vaccine responses remains unexplored. Alexithymia, characterized by the difficulty in identifying and describing emotions, represents a psychosomatic construct associated with chronic stress physiology and immune dysregulation. This study investigated for the first time whether alexithymia, alongside other psychological factors, is associated with vaccine-induced humoral immunity, especially serum SARS-CoV-2 anti-Spike (anti-S) IgG concentrations following vaccination.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 198 healthcare workers who received the BNT162b2 mRNA vaccine were evaluated 4-6 months post-vaccination. Alexithymia was assessed using the Toronto Alexithymia Scale-20 (TAS-20), insomnia using the Athens Insomnia Scale, and anxiety/depression using Hamilton scales. Self-reported positive thinking was also assessed. Anti-S IgG concentrations against the receptor-binding domain (RBD) of the S1 subunit were quantified, and multivariable linear regression (stepwise method) analyses were performed adjusting for demographic, metabolic, inflammatory, and behavioral covariates.

RESULTS: Higher alexithymia (p = 0.002) and insomnia scores (p < 0.001) were independently associated with lower anti-S IgG concentrations after adjustment for vaccination doses, prior COVID-19 infection, BMI, interleukin-6 (IL-6), smoking, and alcohol consumption. Among alexithymia subscales, difficulty identifying and difficulty describing feelings, but not externally oriented thinking, were inversely associated with anti-S IgG concentrations. Participants who reported post-vaccination fever exhibited higher anti-S IgG concentrations and lower alexithymia scores; this retrospective finding is exploratory and does not establish a difference in inflammatory activation.

CONCLUSION: Alexithymia and insomnia are independently associated with lower anti-S IgG concentrations in healthcare workers. Although these concentrations correlate with neutralizing activity, neutralization and clinical protection were not directly assessed in this study. Nevertheless, these findings suggest that alexithymia may represent an underrecognized psychosomatic correlate of post-vaccination antibody responses, meriting further investigation as a potential marker of variation in vaccine responses and protection. Prospective studies should determine whether the observed association extends to neutralizing activity or clinical protection.

articles.title: Left spheno-orbital en plaque meningioma revealed by progressive exophthalmos: imaging features and a compartment-based approach to spheno-orbital hyperostosis.
articles.abstract: En plaque meningioma is an uncommon variant of meningioma (2-9% of cases), defined by a thin carpet-like sheet of tumor spreading along the dura together with bone hyperostosis that is disproportionate to the intradural component. The spheno-orbital region is the site of election, and because the dominant abnormality on imaging is a sclerotic bone lesion rather than a mass, the diagnosis is frequently delayed or mistaken for fibrous dysplasia. We report the case of a 75-year-old woman with no history of malignancy, cranio-orbital trauma, or infection, who presented with slowly progressive left orbital swelling, unilateral exophthalmos, and ipsilateral visual loss. Magnetic resonance imaging showed a left spheno-orbital lesion with broad-based dural thickening, isointense to cortex on T1-weighted images, iso- to slightly hyperintense on T2/FLAIR, with intense and relatively homogeneous enhancement after gadolinium, exerting mass effect on the orbital contents without adjacent parenchymal signal abnormality. Computed tomography demonstrated marked hyperostosis along the left greater sphenoid wing with mild narrowing of the ipsilateral optic canal. The association of a broad-based enhancing dural sheet with disproportionate hyperostosis was highly suggestive of an en plaque meningioma of dural origin. Histopathologic examination of the resected specimen confirmed a meningothelial meningioma, CNS WHO grade 1, with bone invasion. This case illustrates a compartment-based reading of spheno-orbital hyperostosis (orbital, osseous, or meningeal) and the value of imaging-pathology correlation: bone invasion was histologically confirmed in this patient, although meningioma-associated hyperostosis does not necessarily reflect direct neoplastic invasion in every case.

articles.title: Integration of computed tomography and endoscopic findings in identifying pseudoaneurysm rupture associated with duodenal penetration by pancreatic head cancer: A case report.
articles.abstract: Pancreatic head cancer may cause life-threatening upper gastrointestinal bleeding through duodenal invasion and tumor-related arterial involvement. In such patients, differentiating between benign peptic ulcer disease and tumor invasion or penetration is clinically important because this distinction may influence whether endoscopic management or angiography with possible endovascular treatment is pursued. We report a 66-year-old man receiving chemotherapy for unresectable pancreatic head adenocarcinoma who presented with melena. Compared with pre-chemotherapy computed tomography, contrast-enhanced computed tomography on admission showed tumor shrinkage; however, air and a gas-containing low-attenuation area involving the residual pancreatic head lesion and adjacent peripancreatic region suggested tumor necrosis and/or communication with the gastrointestinal lumen. A focal aneurysmal lesion was also identified within the residual pancreatic head tumor. Endoscopy revealed a deep duodenal bulb ulcer without active bleeding. Together, these findings suggested duodenal penetration with tumor-related arterial involvement. The patient subsequently developed hemorrhagic shock, and emergency angiography demonstrated pseudoaneurysm rupture corresponding to the aneurysmal lesion seen on computed tomography. Transcatheter arterial embolization achieved hemostasis, and follow-up endoscopy showed coil exposure at the ulcer base. This case highlights that careful integration of computed tomography and endoscopic findings may help identify duodenal penetration with tumor-related pseudoaneurysm rupture, even when endoscopy shows no active bleeding.

articles.title: Modelling the transmission and burden of ESBL-producing Enterobacterales from a One Health perspective in Singapore.
articles.abstract: The long-term burden of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in hyper-urbanised settings, shaped by complex, multi-sectoral transmission dynamics across human, animal, and environmental reservoirs, remains poorly understood. Using Singapore as a case study, we applied a dynamic One Health modelling framework to explore how ESBL-producing Enterobacterales infections and deaths may evolve over the next decade and identify critical control pathways. We developed a deterministic, compartmental One Health transmission model, the first to integrate hospital, community, companion animal, and environmental reservoirs, calibrated to ten years of national hospital surveillance data (2012-2021) using Markov Chain Monte Carlo Bayesian methods. We projected the baseline disease burden over a 10-year reporting horizon and compared it with counterfactual scenarios while employing global and local sensitivity analyses to identify influential parameters. Over this period, the model projected a total burden of 208,179 clinical ESBL-producing Enterobacterales infections (95% uncertainty interval [UI] 121,669-307,053) and 5567 (95% UI 3660-7806) deaths, with 3491 deaths specifically attributable to ESBL-producing Enterobacterales. Community decolonization strongly influenced infection burdens in both community and hospital settings; a 100% reduction in this process was projected to add nearly 1.8 million additional infections and more than 45,000 resistant-infection deaths across hospital and community settings in Singapore over 10 years. Our dynamic One Health model quantifies these inter-sectoral transmission pathways and identifies clear intervention priorities. While preventing progression from colonisation to infection is vital for reducing hospital-specific mortality, comprehensive system-wide control may benefit from targeting the community reservoir. Ultimately, the modelling framework developed here provides a robust, transferable tool for other global cities to design and evaluate integrated One Health AMR control strategies to mitigate urgent public health threats and associated socio-economic consequences for urban populations and global healthcare systems.

articles.title: Disseminated CNS tuberculosis in SLE without anti-TNF exposure: implications for LTBI screening in endemic settings-case report.
articles.abstract: Patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) are vulnerable to tuberculosis (TB) because of disease-related immune dysfunction, immunosuppressive therapy, and background exposure in TB-endemic settings. Although latent TB infection (LTBI) screening is routinely recommended before biologic and targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs), guidance for glucocorticoids, conventional DMARDs, and other immunosuppressive therapies is less prescriptive. We report 2 HIV-negative Kenyan women with established SLE who developed disseminated extrapulmonary TB after approximately 12 and 20 months of mycophenolate mofetil therapy, respectively, while also receiving maintenance prednisolone 10 mg daily. The second patient had also received rituximab 7 months before TB diagnosis. In case 1, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) GeneXpert Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB)/rifampicin and gluteal-abscess culture-confirmed disseminated central nervous system (CNS) TB with bilateral gluteal involvement. In case 2, lymph-node histology and culture-confirmed TB in the setting of widespread lymphadenopathy and splenic microabscesses; despite negative CSF investigations, neuroimaging demonstrated a cerebral lesion radiologically consistent with tuberculoma. Both patients received anti-TB therapy with adjunctive corticosteroids for CNS disease. Both patients demonstrated eventual clinical and radiological improvement. These cases demonstrate that severe disseminated TB, including CNS involvement, may occur in patients with SLE receiving nontumour necrosis factor (TNF) immunosuppressive regimens in TB-endemic settings. Although causal effects of individual immunosuppressive agents cannot be established, the cases support structured TB-risk assessment and a low threshold for LTBI testing before prolonged corticosteroid exposure or combination immunosuppression. Risk-stratified national guidance specifying therapy-related triggers for LTBI assessment may improve implementation and reduce preventable TB morbidity in high-burden settings.

articles.title: Lipoprotein(a) and statin indications in low-risk patients based on the 2026 ACC/AHA dyslipidemia guideline.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Though elevated lipoprotein (a) (Lp[a]) is associated with ASCVD and testing is recommended for all adults, how to use Lp(a) for decision-making in low-risk patients remains uncertain.

METHODS: We studied low-risk adults in a large healthcare system, excluding those on statins or with statin indications in the 2026 ACC/AHA dyslipidemia guideline. ASCVD risk and statin eligibility were estimated using the PREVENT equations, incorporating Lp(a) using a calculation proposed by the AHA: ASCVD risk x (1.11^[(Lp[a] in nmol/L)/50]). Measured Lp(a) was used when available, and imputed values were used for all other adults.

RESULTS: The cohort included 124 low-risk patients with measured Lp(a) (median [25th-75th percentile] age 44 [38-50] years; 64.5% women) and 28,527 without Lp(a) (median age 42 [36-49] years, 73.3% women). Adding Lp(a) to 10-year risk equations made 3.3% of patients with measured Lp(a) ≥125 nmol/L and 0.1% with imputed Lp(a) of 125 nmol/L newly statin eligible. Eligibility rose with older age, higher Lp(a), and higher ASCVD risk. When Lp(a) was added to 30-year risk in exploratory analyses, 20.2% with measured Lp(a) and 19.6% with imputed Lp(a) of 125 nmol/L met statin eligibility, and 70.0-84.6% (measured cohort) and 33.1-54.2% (imputed cohort) at the highest Lp(a) quintile met eligibility as age increased.

CONCLUSIONS: Integrating Lp(a) into ASCVD risk equations changes predicted risk and potential statin eligibility in low-risk adults not indicated for therapy under current guidelines. Including Lp(a) in risk estimation and clinical decision-making, particularly for patients with elevated levels, could be considered in patients with low ASCVD risk.

articles.title: Targeted delivery of celastrol and siRNA via macrophage biomimetic nanoparticles for doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy therapy.
articles.abstract: Doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy (DIC) is a severe complication following anthracycline chemotherapy, and its main pathogenesis is inflammatory responses and ferroptosis. This study constructed hyaluronic acid-based macrophage biomimetic nanoparticles (M@HCDA) to co-delivery of Celastrol (Cel) and siADAM17 for the treatment of DIC. This research revealed that Cel exerted an anti-ferroptosis effect by regulating GPX4 and SLC7A11, while siADAM17 inhibited TAK1-MAPK pathway activation by silencing ADAM17. Meanwhile, the synergistic effect of Cel and siADAM17 significantly alleviated oxidative stress, myocardial fibrosis, apoptosis, and mitochondrial dysfunction, thereby relieving myocardial injury caused by DOX-induced cardiotoxicity and providing effective early cardioprotection. In vitro and in vivo experiments indicated that M@HCDA exhibited good stability, biocompatibility, and targeting capability, showing the clinical application potential. The design and development of M@HCDA provide new experimental evidence and candidate strategy for treating DIC.

articles.title: Arginine and homoarginine as predictors of cardiovascular mortality in chronic coronary syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Arginine (Arg) and homoarginine (hArg) are related to the nitric oxide pathway, which is important for vascular function. We investigated if serum concentrations of Arg and hArg predicted long-term cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality in patients with chronic coronary syndrome (CCS), and whether associations differed between non-obstructive coronary artery disease (NOCAD) and obstructive coronary artery disease (OCAD).

METHODS AND RESULTS: We included 4164 patients undergoing invasive coronary angiography for suspected CCS. Associations with CVD mortality were assessed using multivariable Cox regression, reporting hazard ratios (HRs) per standard deviation increase in log-transformed concentrations. During a median follow-up of 14.1 years, 586 (14.1%) patients died from CVD. Serum hArg was inversely associated with CVD mortality [HR (95% CI): 0.81 (0.74-0.88)] as was serum Arg [HR (95% CI): 0.90 (0.83-0.98)]. However, in Fine-Gray competing risk analyses, the association of serum Arg with CVD mortality was no longer statistically significant, whereas the inverse association for serum hArg persisted. Addition of serum hArg to the clinical model increased the C-statistic from 0.771 to 0.776, indicating a modest improvement in discrimination. In exploratory subgroup analyses, the association between serum hArg and CVD mortality was stronger in NOCAD than OCAD [0.54 (0.40-0.73) vs. 0.84 (0.77-0.92); P for interaction = 0.037].

CONCLUSION: Serum Arg and hArg were inversely associated with long-term CVD mortality in patients with CCS. However, the association of serum hArg was more robust than that of serum Arg. The stronger association observed in NOCAD requires independent validation.

articles.title: Components of institution-free days as a composite outcome after critical illness: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Critical care and resuscitation : journal of the Australasian Academy of Critical Care Medicine
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the components of institution-free days (IFD) after intensive care unit (ICU) admission and assess the distribution of IFD at 365 d across various admission categories.

DESIGN: Multicentre, retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: Adult patients (aged ≥18 y) admitted to 12 ICUs in Queensland from 2017 to 2020.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: IFD is the primary composite outcome defined as the number of days alive and free of healthcare institution exposure. IFD is calculated by subtracting total number of days with healthcare institution exposure from 365. Distribution of IFD and its components were evaluated across four prespecified subgroups-diagnostic category, comorbidity groups, age quartiles, and remoteness of area of residence.

RESULTS: 44 541 ICU admissions were analysed, of which 19 706 (44.2%), 17 488 (39.2%), and 7347 (16.5%) were medical, elective, and nonelective surgical admissions, respectively. The median IFD was higher for elective surgical patients as compared to nonelective surgical and medical admissions (348 d [interquartile range (IQR): 330-355] vs. 330 [IQR: 267-349] d vs. 325 [IQR: 185-349]). Hospital readmission days were the major contributor to IFD, with 60.4% of all survivors experiencing at least one hospital readmission day within 365 d. The mean hospital readmission days were highest for nonelective surgical admissions as compared to elective and medical admissions (18.5 [standard deviation (SD):18.4] vs. 13.9 [SD: 15.9] vs. 16.1 [SD: 19.2] days).

CONCLUSION: Hospital readmission days were the predominant contributor to institution-days and principal driver of lower IFD for ICU survivors. Medical ICU admissions had the least IFD, followed by nonelective surgical and elective surgical patients.

articles.title: Post-ischemic enteritis mimicking Crohn's disease with complex entero-enteric fistulization.
articles.abstract: Mesenteric venous thrombosis is an uncommon yet potentially life-threatening cause of mesenteric ischemia with an insidious clinical course. Delayed diagnosis of venous ischemia may lead to late complications such as bowel strictures, perforation, and fistulization. These sequelae can closely mimic Crohn's disease, posing significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. We report the case of a 33-year-old postpartum woman who presented with acute abdominal pain and was diagnosed with subacute thrombosis of the superior mesenteric vein and portal vein confluence on contrast-enhanced CT. Initial imaging demonstrated jejunal wall thickening without signs of transmural necrosis, and the patient was managed conservatively with anticoagulation. Despite treatment, she later developed recurrent abdominal pain, bowel obstruction, perforation, and complex small bowel fistulization. Serial imaging findings were initially interpreted as fibrostenotic Crohn's disease. Endoscopic evaluation and bowel biopsies were unremarkable. Ongoing recurrent obstruction ultimately necessitated limited small bowel resection, and histopathologic findings confirmed ischemic injury, characterized by ulceration, vascular congestion, granulation tissue, and full-thickness hyalinization and necrosis. The patient unfortunately died from postoperative complications seven months after the initial presentation. This case highlights chronic ischemic enteritis as an important masquerader of Crohn's disease, particularly in patients with a history of mesenteric venous thrombosis. Complex fistulization and fibrostenotic changes are not pathognomonic for inflammatory bowel disease and may represent late sequelae of missed or patchy bowel ischemia. Careful assessment of mesenteric vasculature and collateral formation on imaging is crucial to avoid misdiagnosis, inappropriate immunosuppressive therapy, and delayed definitive management.

articles.title: NOTIFY-DISCUSS: Patient and clinician perspectives on opportunistic screening for coronary artery calcification using artificial intelligence.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: NOTIFY-1 was a quality improvement study that utilized a validated deep learning algorithm to perform opportunistic coronary artery calcification (CAC) screening on previously acquired non-gated chest CT scans, significantly increasing statin prescribing and coronary artery disease testing. NOTIFY-DISCUSS explored patient and clinician perceptions of this real-world clinical application of an artificial intelligence (AI) tool.

METHODS: Semi-structured interviews and focus groups were conducted with n = 20 NOTIFY-1 participants (n = 11 patients, n = 9 clinicians). All patients had received their incidental CAC results prior to interviews. Topics included attitudes toward AI use in medicine, experiences with this AI-assisted tool, preferences for communicating incidental findings, and perceived barriers to guideline-directed statin prescribing. Transcripts were coded by a qualitative researcher in NVivo and reviewed by a qualitative expert; analysis of transcripts utilized thematic analysis and consensus approaches.

RESULTS: Most participants appreciated the notification tool for providing compelling personalized data to support shared decision-making and behavior change around statin initiation. Participants also noted its potential to improve identification of incidental findings and improve health equity. However, several themes indicated concerns: consent to the use of AI tools; data rights, usage, and security; the time-burden of discussing and contextualizing incidental CAC findings; potential for unintended harm; and need for timely notifications.

CONCLUSIONS: NOTIFY-DISCUSS offered a unique opportunity to assess perceptions of an implemented AI-driven opportunistic cardiovascular screening tool. Concerns around consent, security, burden and unintended harms will be essential to address when designing and deploying future AI tools, and patient perspectives should be included in ongoing monitoring efforts.

articles.title: Environmental contamination and molecular epidemiology of Giardia duodenalis around Korean cattle farms: Implications for One Health surveillance.
articles.abstract: Giardia duodenalis is an important enteric protozoan parasite transmitted via the fecal-oral route through the ingestion of environmentally resistant cysts, with contaminated soil and water serving as potential sources of infection. Although its molecular epidemiology has been extensively investigated in livestock, data on environmental contamination surrounding cattle farms remain limited in Korea. This study evaluated the occurrence and molecular characteristics of G. duodenalis in soil and water collected from cattle farm environments. Between July 2023 and June 2024, 364 environmental samples (185 soil and 179 water samples) were collected from beef and dairy cattle farms across three regions. Samples were screened for G. duodenalis by PCR targeting the small-subunit ribosomal RNA (SSU rRNA) gene. PCR-positive samples were subjected to sequencing and phylogenetic analysis, with additional PCR assays targeting the bg, gdh, and tpi genes performed for assemblage identification. G. duodenalis was detected in 2 of 364 samples (0.5%), comprising one soil sample and one water sample collected near beef cattle farms. Both positive samples were obtained in autumn and yielded identical SSU rRNA sequences that clustered phylogenetically with assemblage E; however, amplification of the bg, gdh, and tpi loci was unsuccessful. These findings provide the first molecular evidence of G. duodenalis DNA in environmental matrices surrounding Korean cattle farms. The detection of G. duodenalis DNA in soil and water provides preliminary evidence of environmental contamination. However, these findings do not establish cyst viability, infectivity, or zoonotic transmission, highlighting the need for further investigations within a One Health framework. This study provides baseline data for integrated One Health surveillance and underscores the importance of systematic environmental monitoring for elucidating transmission pathways, evaluating potential public health significance, and informing evidence-based biosecurity measures.

articles.title: An In Vitro Study Simulating Prophylactic Anticoagulation in Haemophilia A and B.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with haemophilia A (HA) and haemophilia B (HB) are at increased bleeding risk. A recent guidance document suggests considering pharmacological thromboprophylaxis on a case-by-case basis in these patients undergoing surgery at high-risk of venous thromboembolism. This study aimed to assess the effect of prophylactic doses of three anticoagulants (enoxaparin, rivaroxaban and unfractionated heparin [UFH]) on in vitro models of HA and HB.

METHODS: FVIII- and FIX-deficient plasma were spiked with FVIII and FIX concentrates to mimic severe, moderate and mild HA (FVIII concentrations < 1%, 1.2% and 17.0%, respectively) and HB (FIX concentrations < 1%, 3.9% and 22.9%, respectively). Each pool was spiked with enoxaparin (concentration range 0.3-0.4 IU/mL), rivaroxaban (50-100 ng/mL) and UFH (0.2-0.3 IU/mL). The following assays were performed: prothrombin time (PT), activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) and thrombin generation (using the semi-automated fluorogenic calibrated automated thrombin generation assay [CAT]).

RESULTS: The PT was not significantly affected by the anticoagulants. A significant prolongation of the APTT was observed; UFH showed the greatest increase, followed by rivaroxaban and enoxaparin. All anticoagulants impacted on the CAT curves. UFH showed the greatest reduction of the endogenous thrombin potential; rivaroxaban showed the greatest increase of lag time and time to peak. Peak thrombin and velocity index were similarly reduced by rivaroxaban and UFH, whereas enoxaparin was associated with smaller changes in all parameters.

CONCLUSION: A significant effect of three prophylactic anticoagulants was observed in factor-deficient plasmas. This study provides further insight into this topic and supports the concept of an individualised approach to haemophilia patients. Trial Registration: The authors have confirmed clinical trial registration is not needed for this submission.

articles.title: Reduced bi-atrial reservoir strain in patients with cardiac amyloidosis: a cardiac magnetic resonance feature-tracking study.
articles.journal: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although heart strain analysis is useful for diagnosing cardiac amyloidosis (CA), it remains unclear which chamber best distinguishes CA from hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). This study analyzed strain in all four cardiac chambers in patients with CA and HCM using cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) feature-tracking.

METHODS: We enrolled 30 patients with left ventricular hypertrophy (15 with CA and 15 with HCM) and 17 healthy volunteers as a reference. Participants underwent 1.5-Tesla CMR to assess volume, function, and strain parameters in both ventricles and atria. The primary analysis comprised four comparisons between CA and HCM, one representative parameter per chamber (bi-ventricular longitudinal strain and bi-atrial reservoir strain), with Bonferroni correction (P < 0.0125). Additionally, exploratory analyses of the other parameters were conducted comparing patients with CA to HCM.

RESULTS: Left atrial (LA) and right atrial (RA) reservoir strain were lower in CA than in HCM (LA: 7.1 ± 4.1% vs. 10.3 ± 3.9%, P = 0.035; RA: 10.8 ± 6.9% vs. 22.1 ± 12.9%, P = 0.005), whereas ventricular longitudinal strain did not differ. After Bonferroni correction, only RA reservoir strain remained significant. In an exploratory receiver operating characteristic analysis, the areas under the curve for LA and RA reservoir strain were 0.73 and 0.78, respectively, and did not differ significantly.

CONCLUSION: Bi-atrial reservoir strain was lower in CA than in HCM, and the difference in RA reservoir strain remained significant after accounting for multiplicity. Atrial reservoir strain may provide adjunctive, contrast-free functional information to help differentiate CA from HCM.

articles.title: False patency, true occlusion: perfusion imaging and dual stent-retriever thrombectomy for a calcified carotid terminus embolus.
articles.abstract: Calcified cerebral emboli are an uncommon cause of acute ischemic stroke and may produce a false-patency sign on computed tomography angiography because their high attenuation can mimic intravascular contrast material. We report the case of a 77-year-old woman who presented with a wake-up stroke approximately 14 hours after she was last known well, with right hemiplegia and global aphasia. Noncontrast computed tomography showed a markedly hyperattenuating intraluminal focus at the left carotid terminus and proximal M1 segment, suggesting a calcified cerebral embolus. Computed tomography angiography appeared to show severe stenosis with residual luminal patency, whereas computed tomography perfusion demonstrated extensive hypoperfusion involving the left middle cerebral artery and bilateral anterior cerebral artery territories. Because the severe neurologic deficit and perfusion abnormality were discordant with the apparent patency on computed tomography angiography, cerebral angiography was performed. Digital subtraction angiography demonstrated complete occlusion of the left M1 origin and near-complete occlusion of the left A1 segment; the right A1 segment was congenitally hypoplastic. A rigid calcified embolus spanning the carotid-terminus bifurcation was retrieved using a balloon guide catheter-assisted dual-stent technique under proximal flow arrest, achieving complete reperfusion in a single pass. Histopathologic examination confirmed calcified embolic material. This case highlights the value of multimodal imaging and confirmatory angiography when clinical and imaging findings are discordant. In this patient, balloon guide catheter-assisted dual-stent retrieval was a tailored and feasible strategy; however, a single case cannot establish its superiority over other thrombectomy approaches.

articles.title: Receptor-binding autoantibodies are not associated with post-COVID fatigue.
articles.abstract: Persistent fatigue is a common symptom following SARS-CoV-2 infection, but its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Autoantibodies targeting G-protein coupled receptors and other neurotransmitter-related receptors have been proposed as potential biomarkers or mediators of post-COVID symptoms. However, their association with post-COVID fatigue remains unclear. Therefore, in the current study, we investigated receptor-binding autoantibodies against 13 neurotransmitter-related receptors in 206 participants with prior infection with SARS-CoV-2. Three groups of patients were enrolled: controls with no persistent fatigue, patients experiencing new-onset post-infection fatigue, and a group of patients who already suffered from fatigue before their infection with SARS-CoV-2. Fatigue was assessed using a standardized self-reported fatigue questionnaire. We found no significant differences in the concentrations of the measured receptor-binding autoantibodies between participants with new-onset fatigue, pre-existing fatigue, and controls without persistent fatigue. In multivariable analyses, none of the individual antibody concentrations was significantly associated with new-onset fatigue after adjustment for age, sex, and time since infection and correction for multiple testing. Individual antibody concentrations were also not associated with fatigue severity. The proportion of participants exceeding manufacturer-defined reference values did not differ significantly between the study groups. Similarly, cumulative antibody positivity was not associated with fatigue severity. In conclusion, in this cohort of SARS-CoV-2-infected participants, we found no evidence that concentrations of the measured receptor-binding autoantibodies are associated with post-COVID fatigue or fatigue severity. These findings do not support the use of these antibodies as stand-alone biomarkers of post-COVID fatigue. Because all participants had previously experienced SARS-CoV-2 infection, the study cannot determine whether infection itself alters antibody concentrations. Furthermore, the binding assays do not establish whether the detected antibodies have functional receptor activity. These findings underscore the urgent need for longitudinal studies with comprehensive clinical phenotyping and functional antibody assays are needed to further investigate the potential role of receptor-binding autoantibodies in post-COVID symptoms.

articles.title: Cardiometabolic risk factors and Mediterranean diet adherence in patients with premature atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease in Iran.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Premature atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) is associated with a substantial burden of modifiable cardiovascular risk factors, but the dietary and cardiometabolic characteristics of affected patients remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to assess Mediterranean diet adherence, its associated factors, and the sex-specific distribution of cardiometabolic risk factors among patients with premature ASCVD in Iran.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 425 adults with premature ASCVD were recruited from a tertiary cardiovascular referral center in Alborz Province, Iran, using consecutive sampling on two scheduled data-collection days per week. Sociodemographic, lifestyle, anthropometric, and biochemical data were collected using standardized protocols. Mediterranean diet adherence was assessed using a culturally adapted 13-item Mediterranean Diet Adherence Screener (MEDAS). Principal component analysis was used to derive dietary adherence patterns from the MEDAS components, and the standardized score of the first principal component was dichotomized at its sample median (0.33) into lower- and higher-adherence groups. Cardiometabolic risk factors were defined according to established clinical criteria, with treated hypertension, diabetes, and dyslipidemia also identified based on relevant medication use. Sex-specific comparisons and multivariable logistic regression were performed. A sensitivity analysis compared participants with extremely premature ASCVD (< 40 years) with those with premature ASCVD (≥ 40 years).

RESULTS: Among the 425 participants, 70.1% were male and the mean age was 50.23 ± 6.54 years. The prevalence of excess weight was 81.6%, while the prevalence of metabolic syndrome ranged from 66.4% to 82.8% across the five diagnostic criteria examined. Women had higher prevalences of low HDL-C and elevated LDL-C and were more likely to meet several definitions of metabolic syndrome, whereas men had substantially higher rates of active smoking, cumulative tobacco exposure, and substance use. When participants were categorized according to Mediterranean diet adherence, higher adherence was more common among women, while most sociodemographic, lifestyle, anthropometric, biochemical, and cardiometabolic characteristics were similar between adherence groups. In the adjusted analysis, male sex was associated with lower odds of higher Mediterranean diet adherence (OR = 0.57, 95% CI: 0.33-0.99, P = 0.050), whereas age, BMI, socioeconomic status, tobacco exposure, and physical activity were not significantly associated with adherence. In the sensitivity analysis, participants with extremely premature ASCVD (< 40 years) had lower prevalences of elevated triglycerides, low HDL-C, elevated blood pressure, and metabolic syndrome than those with standard premature ASCVD.

CONCLUSIONS: Patients with premature ASCVD in this Iranian hospital-based population showed a substantial and heterogeneous burden of cardiometabolic and behavioral risk factors, with distinct patterns between men and women. Mediterranean diet adherence differed primarily according to sex and showed limited associations with other measured sociodemographic, lifestyle, and cardiometabolic characteristics. Extremely premature ASCVD was characterized by a different distribution of conventional cardiometabolic risk factors in the sensitivity analysis, although this finding requires confirmation given the small subgroup size. These findings support comprehensive and individualized secondary-prevention strategies that address dietary behavior alongside smoking, adiposity, metabolic abnormalities, and other modifiable cardiovascular risk factors.

articles.title: Warfarin After Seven Decades: Persistent Value and the Contemporary Role of Vitamin K Antagonism.
articles.abstract: Warfarin is one of the most enduring drugs in cardiovascular medicine. Although direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) have transformed anticoagulation, especially in atrial fibrillation (AF) eligible for DOAC therapy, their success cannot be extrapolated to every thrombotic substrate. This review examines the contemporary boundaries of warfarin and vitamin K antagonist (VKA) therapy. Mechanical heart valves remain the clearest setting in which lifelong international normalized ratio (INR)-guided VKA therapy is required; randomized attempts to substitute dabigatran or apixaban have failed. In rheumatic heart disease-associated AF, INVICTUS favored VKA therapy over rivaroxaban, supporting the VKA class rather than warfarin specifically. High-risk thrombotic antiphospholipid syndrome, particularly triple-positive disease, is another VKA-preferred setting. Left ventricular thrombus (LVT) occupies an evolving position in which warfarin remains established, while randomized evidence supports rivaroxaban as a potential alternative in selected acute post-myocardial infarction LVT. Pregnancy with mechanical valves requires dynamic maternal-fetal risk balancing, whereas advanced chronic kidney disease and dialysis represent areas of uncertainty rather than intrinsic indications for warfarin. The global relevance of warfarin also depends on total anticoagulation burden, including INR monitoring, travel, treatment continuity, quality of anticoagulation, and reversal capacity. The persistence of VKA efficacy in selected highly thrombogenic environments raises a biologically plausible hypothesis that broader suppression of vitamin K-dependent factors may matter, but this mechanism is not established by clinical trials. Contemporary anticoagulation should therefore be substrate-centered: VKA therapy remains necessary in some conditions, preferred in others, increasingly replaceable in several, and uncertain in a few.

articles.title: Virtual Assessment of Coronary Microcirculation Before and After Rotational Atherectomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Calcified coronary lesions remain a major challenge during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Rotational atherectomy (RA) (Boston Scientific) is a well-established tool used to modify calcified plaques and facilitate stent delivery. Despite its mechanical benefits, RA may adversely affect coronary microcirculation through distal plaque debris embolization. Angiography-derived microvascular resistance (AMR) (Pulse Medical) is a wire-free index correlated with invasive indices such as the index of microcirculatory resistance (IMR), which allows assessment of microcirculatory resistance directly from angiographic images, without a pressure wire or adenosine. The objective of this study is to evaluate changes in AMR before and after RA and to identify clinical, angiographic, and procedural predictors of postprocedural coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD).

METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center observational study including all patients who underwent RA between January 2023 and December 2024 at Clinique Saint-Hilaire in Rouen, France. AMR was measured before and after RA using the AngioPlus software (Pulse Medical). CMD was defined as postprocedural AMR > 250 mm Hg·s/m.

RESULTS: Of 49 RA procedures, 40 patients were included. AMR increased in all cases but CMD occurred in 42.5% of patients (n=17). Diabetes mellitus and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) were significantly more prevalent in the CMD group. Long coronary artery lesions (> 20 mm), larger plaque burden, and prolonged burr run time were associated with higher AMR values. Mean AMR rose from 176 to 315 mm Hg·s/m in the CMD group, versus 177 to 201 mm Hg·s/m in the non-CMD group.

CONCLUSIONS: Performing RA affects the coronary microcirculation, especially in cases of diabetes mellitus and reduced LVEF.

articles.title: Clinically Actionable Prevention and Management of Major Complications During Durable Left Ventricular Assist Device Support: A Contemporary Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Durable left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) have become an established therapy for selected patients with advanced heart failure as bridge-to-transplant or destination therapy. Despite major progress in continuous-flow pump design and perioperative care, long-term benefit remains constrained by a recurrent burden of right heart failure, aortic regurgitation, pump thrombosis, stroke, bleeding, infection, and end-organ dysfunction. Because these events often arise from the interaction of altered hemodynamics, hemocompatibility-related injury, chronic antithrombotic exposure, and the practical complexity of longitudinal device care, a complication-centered management framework is clinically useful. This contemporary narrative review focuses on actionable prevention, surveillance, and treatment strategies for the major complications encountered during durable LVAD support. Rather than providing a broad device-oriented overview, we emphasize clinically relevant decision points across the perioperative and long-term course, including right ventricular protection, antithrombotic balance, structured monitoring for aortic regurgitation and hemolysis, prevention of driveline infection, and multidisciplinary outpatient follow-up. By organizing current evidence around practical management pathways, this review aims to support earlier recognition of adverse events and more durable long-term support.

articles.title: Coffee and the Risk of Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.abstract: Most hospitals and cardiac rehabilitation facilities provide decaffeinated coffee to cardiac patients in place of regular coffee. Recent studies, however, suggest that coffee drinking may decrease the risk of developing cardiovascular diseases. Review of controlled studies shows that drinking regular coffee in moderation is safe. It may even lead to a decrease in atrial arrhythmias such as atrial fibrillation, and it is safe in patients with ventricular arrhythmias. This is particularly true in patients who drink coffee regularly and in moderation. Energy drinks, however, that contain large doses of caffeine may indeed be harmful and should be avoided. The policies of serving only decaffeinated coffee in hospitals and rehabilitation facilities should be revisited.

articles.title: Personalized Prevention of Cardiovascular Diseases Through Measurement of Plaque Burden in the Carotid Artery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study provides an overview of the results of carotid screening for the prevention of cardiovascular disease.

METHODS: Between 2009 and 2026, 11,540 individuals, 45% of whom were women, aged 20-65 years without clinical signs of cardiovascular disease, underwent carotid ultrasound examinations. Over 8,800 follow-up examinations were also performed. The total plaque area (TPA) and maximum plaque thickness were measured.

RESULTS: TPA was presented as percentile curves according to age and sex. In a second cohort, age-related TPA thresholds for coronary stenosis ≥ 50% were determined. Advanced atherosclerosis (type III/IVb) is associated with a high risk of cardiovascular disease. Early treatment with statins improves the prognosis of these patients. The individual course of the disease with rapid progression of plaque burden could not be predicted based on classic risk factors. Of 75 patients with advanced atherosclerosis who suffered a myocardial infarction or ischemic stroke, 35% had a low PROCAM risk (< 10%) and only 27% had a high PROCAM risk. Mortality (from any cause) was significantly lower in men treated with statins.

CONCLUSIONS: Measuring plaque burden in the carotid artery allows for a good estimation of an individual's risk of a cardiovascular event. In this non-randomized observational study, statin treatment significantly improved the prognosis in subjects with advanced carotid artery atherosclerosis (type III-IVb findings on ultrasound).

articles.title: Prognostic Value of Serum Albumin in Elderly Cardiovascular Disease Management.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide and represents a major contributor to disability and poor health among elderly individuals, particularly those aged ≥ 65 years. Age-related physiological changes, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and oxidative stress play critical roles in the development and progression of CVD. Identifying reliable prognostic biomarkers is therefore essential to improve risk stratification and clinical management in this vulnerable population. Serum albumin (SA), the most abundant plasma protein, has emerged as a potential prognostic marker in elderly patients with CVD. Accumulating evidence from observational studies indicates that hypoalbuminemia is associated with increased all-cause mortality across a wide spectrum of CVDs, including coronary artery disease, heart failure, hypertension, atrial fibrillation, stroke, peripheral artery disease, and in patients undergoing various cardiovascular interventions. Importantly, low SA levels have been shown to remain an independent prognostic marker of adverse outcomes in observational studies after adjustment for confounding factors, such as malnutrition, inflammation, and comorbid conditions, although these associations may partly reflect underlying disease burden and other clinical factors. Proposed mechanisms linking hypoalbuminemia to poor outcomes include impaired antioxidant capacity, increased inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and altered fluid balance. This review also highlights substantial heterogeneity in SA threshold values reported across studies, which may limit its standardized application in clinical practice. Although albumin supplementation has been suggested as a potential therapeutic strategy, current evidence regarding its clinical benefit remains inconclusive. SA may provide additional prognostic information in elderly patients with CVD and may support improved risk stratification across diverse clinical settings. At present, management strategies should prioritize identifying and addressing the underlying causes of hypoalbuminemia rather than routine albumin supplementation. Further well-designed studies are needed to establish standardized SA cut-off values and to clarify its role in guiding clinical decision-making in elderly cardiovascular populations.

articles.title: Digoxin Revisited: An Updated Review in the Light of Recent Trials.
articles.abstract: Isolated from Digitalis species following William Withering's 1785 work on foxglove, digoxin inhibits myocardial Na+/K+-ATPase, raising intracellular calcium and vagal tone to produce inotropic, rate-controlling, and neurohormonal-deactivating effects. The foundational DIG trial (1997) showed no mortality benefit but reduced heart failure hospitalizations, prompting a progressive guideline downgrade. Three decades later, DIGIT-HF (2025, digitoxin) and DECISION (2026, low dose digoxin) retested cardiac glycosides atop modern four pillar guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT). DIGIT-HF significantly reduced the composite of death or worsening heart failure (hazard ratio (HR), 0.82), while DECISION showed a numerical but nonsignificant benefit. A pooled meta-analysis of DIG, DIGIT-HF, and DECISION (9,013 patients) confirmed a consistent 15% reduction in worsening heart failure events across three decades of changing background therapy, without a significant mortality effect. The Dig-RHD trial addressed an unstudied population: symptomatic rheumatic heart disease (RHD), a chronic valvular heart disease that results from permanent damage to cardiac valves due to group A streptococcal infection. RHD affects roughly 40 million people and causes approximately 300,000 deaths annually, disproportionately in low- and middle-income countries. In 1,769 patients randomized across 12 Indian centers, digoxin significantly reduced the composite of death or new-onset/worsening heart failure (31.4% vs. 35.5%; HR, 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.70 to 0.97; P = 0.02), with greater benefit in atrial fibrillation, women, and patients with low body mass index (BMI), and a number needed to treat of approximately 14 over 2 years. Digoxin is not a mortality-reducing drug, but pooled contemporary evidence establishes it as a reproducible, low-cost tool for reducing heart failure events, now supported for the first time by high-quality randomized data in RHD, a population with substantial global burden and no prior evidence-based medical therapy. These findings warrant reconsideration of digoxin's guideline status and development of RHD-specific recommendations.

articles.title: Outcomes After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Using the Self-Expanding Allegra Valve in Daily Practice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Limited data are available of the self-expanding Allegra transcatheter heart valve (THV). The aim of this study was to investigate the safety and outcome of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) using the Allegra THV in daily practice.

METHODS: Between February 2018 and September 2024, 142 consecutive patients underwent Allegra TAVI at the Heart and Vascular Center, Bad Bevensen, Germany, either for native aortic stenosis (AS) (n = 117, median 82 (interquartile range 80-86) years) or degenerated aortic bioprostheses (n = 25, 80 (73-84) years) as valve-in-valve (ViV) procedures. Endpoints were defined according to Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 criteria.

RESULTS: The logistic EuroSCORE II was significantly higher in the cohort of patients with degenerated aortic bioprostheses than in those with native AS (14.4% (6.6-25.3%) versus 3.3% (2.5-5.7%), P < 0.01). Technical success was nearly identical in both cohorts (91.5% of patients with native AS and 92.0% of patients with ViV TAVI). Postinterventional aortic regurgitation ≥ moderate was found in 4.5% of patients with native AS and was not present in any patient with ViV TAVI. In the native AS cohort, mean and maximal aortic pressure gradients decreased from 44 (36-54) mm Hg and 72 (60-87) mm Hg before the intervention to 6 (5-9) mm Hg and 12 (9-15) mm Hg after Allegra TAVI. In the ViV cohort, mean and maximal transvalvular pressure gradients decreased from 34 (27-43) mm Hg and 59 (44-70) mm Hg to 9 (7-11) mm Hg and 16 (14-23) mm Hg, respectively. Periprocedural mortality rates (≤ 30 days) were 6.8% and 12.0% in the native AS and ViV cohorts, respectively. One-year and 3-year survival rates were 87.2% and 73.2% in the native AS cohort and 89.8% and 75.1% in the ViV cohort, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: TAVI using the self-expanding Allegra THV system is safe and leads to acute hemodynamic improvements in patients with native AS or degenerated aortic bioprostheses.

articles.title: Association Between Hepatitis C Virus Infection and Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection has been associated with cardiovascular disease, but its relationship with coronary artery disease (CAD) remains uncertain.

METHODS: This systematic review included observational studies reporting adjusted effect estimates for CAD outcomes among HCV-infected and HCV-uninfected adults. Adjusted hazard ratios, risk ratios, and odds ratios were combined on the logarithmic scale using a random-effects model and are presented as a summary relative association estimate with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Prespecified subgroup analyses were performed by study design, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) co-infection status, and CAD outcome type; meta-regression evaluated follow-up duration, mean age, and the proportion of male participants.

RESULTS: Twenty-one studies were included, representing diverse populations including veterans, people living with HIV, dialysis patients, and community-based cohorts. Fifteen studies contributed adjusted estimates to the quantitative synthesis. HCV infection was associated with a modest increase in the pooled relative estimate for CAD (summary estimate 1.21; 95% CI, 1.05-1.40; P = 0.007), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 72.1%). The association was statistically significant in cohort studies and in both HIV-specific and non-HIV-specific subgroups, although the HIV-specific subgroup was based on four studies. The myocardial infarction (MI)-specific subgroup was not statistically significant, whereas studies using broader CAD outcomes showed a significant association.

CONCLUSIONS: Chronic HCV infection was associated with a modest increase in the pooled relative estimate for CAD. However, substantial heterogeneity, differences in endpoint definitions and populations, residual confounding, and the combination of different effect measures limit causal interpretation and make the clinical importance uncertain. The nonsignificant MI-specific analysis further supports a cautious interpretation. These findings do not establish a cardiovascular benefit of antiviral therapy; prospective studies with standardized CAD endpoints and detailed data on renal disease, antiviral exposure, and lipid-lowering therapy are needed.

articles.title: Septal Reduction Therapy: Thinking Beyond the Conventional.
articles.abstract: For patients with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy who are refractory to medical treatment, the surgical myectomy is the treatment of choice, but for some patients, alcohol septal ablation (ASA) is an alternative. In the following case report, we described a patient that underwent ASA, but during the follow-up, the gradient came back. This patient did not have septal branches from left anterior descending artery; therefore, she underwent ablation of a marginal branch of the left circumflex artery using an ethylene-vinyl alcohol copolymer guided by evaluation of the invasive gradient (echocardiogram was not performed during the procedure). One year later, the patient presented with refractory symptoms, and color Doppler echocardiography revealed a mean resting left ventricle outflow tract (LVOT) gradient of 72 mm Hg, a basal septum thickness of 21 mm, and a mid- and apical-septal thickness of 10 mm. Coronary angiography showed a pattern similar to that observed at the end of the marginal branch occlusion procedure. A transcatheter treatment attempt was proposed to identify the vessel supplying the basal septum for potential ablation; however, the patient opted for surgical myomectomy, which was performed successfully and without complications. She was discharged on the fifth day of hospitalization. Based on this case, we conclude that septal ablation should not be performed without an echocardiographic assessment during the procedure, other branches than the septal branches may supply the interventricular septum (if ablation of these branches is performed, it must be as selective as possible), and the reduction of the invasive LVOT gradient should not be used as the sole criterion for deciding which branch to occlude.

articles.title: Endpoint-specific mortality associated with malignancy among adults with sepsis or septic shock: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis is a major global health challenge and increasingly affects patients with complex conditions such as malignancy. Prior studies suggest higher mortality in this population, but interpretation is limited by aggregation of heterogeneous endpoints. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to clarify endpoint-specific prognostic associations between malignancy and mortality in adults with sepsis or septic shock.

METHODS: This study was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251141216). PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library and Epistemonikos were searched through 16 September 2025, for studies comparing all-cause mortality between sepsis patients with and without malignancy. Mortality endpoints were grouped as ICU, in-hospital, early, intermediate and extended follow-up mortality. Crude odds ratios (ORs) were estimated using random-effects meta-analysis. Subgroup, meta-regression and sensitivity analyses were performed to explore heterogeneity and assess consistency.

RESULTS: Among 105 eligible studies comprising 20,089,138 participants, 85 studies contributing 101 endpoint estimates were included in the primary synthesis. Pooled estimates were elevated across endpoints: ICU (OR 1.21, 95% CI 0.94-1.56), in-hospital (OR 1.90, 95% CI 1.69-2.13), early (OR 1.81, 95% CI 1.59-2.06), intermediate (OR 2.28, 95% CI 1.72-3.03) and extended follow-up mortality (OR 2.41, 95% CI 1.70-3.42). Associations were sustained for haematologic malignancy, concentrated in in-hospital and early mortality for metastatic disease and more modest for solid tumours. Sensitivity analyses were directionally consistent, although risk ratio estimates were generally smaller than ORs. Exploratory meta-regression suggested that severity-related covariates may contribute to heterogeneity.

CONCLUSIONS: Malignancy was associated with higher mortality among adults with sepsis or septic shock, with variation across mortality endpoints and clinical contexts. These findings support endpoint-specific prognostic assessment and highlight the need for future studies to incorporate more granular cancer characteristics. Because the primary estimates were unadjusted, results represent overall prognostic associations rather than independent causal effects.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence and continuous renal replacement therapy.
articles.abstract: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is an important intervention in the treatment of acute kidney injury (AKI) in intensive care, and its application scope continues to expand alongside technological advancements and an increasing patient population. However, in current clinical practice, several factors, including individual patient differences, dynamic treatment needs, and the rational allocation of medical resources, pose challenges to CRRT implementation. The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) offers new approaches to address some of these challenges, and its applications in developing decision-support models, refining workflows, and supporting patient communication and education may contribute to more precise and efficient CRRT management. In this article, we discuss the current evidence and potential applications of AI in CRRT, as well as the challenges and strategies for clinical implementation, aiming to provide a reference for future research and clinical translation of AI-assisted CRRT.

articles.title: Comparison of 1-year costs of commercially insured patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing surgical vs. transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with aortic stenosis (AS) have been shown to have lower costs at 1 year with transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) compared with surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) in a Medicare population. The difference in costs between TAVR and SAVR in commercially insured patients with AS in the United States is unknown.

METHODS: Using the Optum claims database, AS patients receiving either TAVR or SAVR between 3/2019 and 9/2022 were identified. Patients were categorized into low, intermediate or high strata using the Hospital Frailty Risk Score (HFRS). The primary outcome was total 1-year cost, defined as the sum of index AVR hospitalization and 1-year follow-up costs. Risk-adjusted generalized linear models were used to assess the difference in the costs between TAVR and SAVR.

RESULTS: 3,623 patients (952 TAVR; 2,671 SAVR) were identified. TAVR patients had lower index hospitalization costs compared with SAVR patients across all HFRS strata (cost difference for low: $39,312, p < 0.01; intermediate: $42,006, p < 0.01; high: $39,431, p = 0.03). Cumulative costs through one year were significantly lower with TAVR in the low and intermediate HFRS strata (cost difference for low: $32,116, p < 0.01; intermediate $40,905, p < 0.01) and numerically lower in the high HFRS stratum (cost difference: $35,881, p = 0.15). When the analysis was restricted to isolated AVR, the 1-year difference was no longer significant in the low and intermediate HFRS strata ($8,064 and $11,314, respectively) and was numerically reversed in the high HFRS stratum (-$28,804).

CONCLUSIONS: In a commercial payor population of real-world patients with AS, TAVR was associated with lower standardized index hospitalization costs across all HFRS strata and lower standardized 1-year costs in the low and intermediate HFRS strata. These findings demonstrate that baseline frailty and procedural scope are critical determinants of short and intermediate-term cost differences between TAVR and SAVR for the treatment of AS in commercial populations.

articles.title: Association of non-methane volatile organic compound emission burden with chronic kidney disease: integrated epidemiological, transcriptomic and in vitro analyses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Environmental exposure to non-methane volatile organic compounds (NMVOCs) may contribute to chronic kidney disease (CKD), but the underlying molecular pathways remain unclear. We integrated epidemiological, transcriptomic, single-cell, and experimental analyses to identify candidate mechanisms linking NMVOCs to kidney injury.

METHODS: Province-level NMVOC emission burden was linked to residential province for 3,472 participants in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). CKD was defined as an eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2. Associations were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Putative NMVOC-CKD targets, kidney transcriptomic datasets, 113 machine-learning models, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to prioritize biomarkers. Single-cell transcriptomics, cell-communication analysis, virtual knockout, and hydroquinone-treated cell experiments were used to investigate candidate pathways.

RESULTS: Among 3,472 participants, 417 had CKD. In the fully adjusted model, higher province-level NMVOC emission burden was associated with greater odds of prevalent CKD (OR = 1.05). The best transcriptomic classifier achieved areas under the curve of 0.964 and 0.836 in the training and validation sets. Integrated analyses prioritized SLC9A3 and localized its expression to proximal tubular cells. Single-cell analysis predicted SPP1-ITGAV/ITGB1 signaling between proximal tubular cells and fibroblasts. In a benzene-metabolite model, hydroquinone increased tubular SLC9A3 and SPP1 expression; conditioned medium increased fibroblast ITGB1 and α-smooth muscle actin expression and migration.

CONCLUSIONS: Province-level NMVOC emission burden was associated with CKD. The findings nominate proximal-tubule SLC9A3/SPP1-integrin signaling as a candidate link between NMVOC emission burden and fibroblast activation, warranting validation through individual-level exposure assessment and targeted perturbation studies.

articles.title: Targeting ferroptosis in metabolic dysfunction‑associated steatotic liver disease: From mechanisms to cell type‑specific therapeutic strategies (Review).
