articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction‑associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) impacts >30% of the global population. Its progression to metabolic dysfunction‑associated steatohepatitis and liver fibrosis is the primary determinant for cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Ferroptosis depends on iron and is driven by lipid peroxidation and is involved in the development of MASLD. Effective anti‑fibrotic agents remain an unmet clinical need. The present review aimed to summarize the metabolic environment in MASLD, which is characterized by lipid overload, iron dysregulation and oxidative stress, and its role in facilitating ferroptosis using a cell type‑ and disease stage‑specific framework, integrating intercellular crosstalk and evidence grading for biomarkers and therapeutic agents, as well as knowledge gaps, such as the paucity of direct human evidence, unresolved spatiotemporal dynamics and the necessity for precision delivery systems. The present review positions ferroptosis as a key pathophysiological element in MASLD and a promising frontier for diagnostic and therapeutic innovation by combining mechanistic insight with translational perspectives.

articles.title: Emerging role of non‑coding RNAs in the progression of MASLD‑driven hepatocellular carcinoma (Review).
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction‑associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most prevalent chronic liver disease worldwide and a leading cause of liver‑related morbidity and mortality. MASLD encompasses a pathological spectrum ranging from metabolic dysfunction‑associated steatohepatitis to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), making it the fastest‑growing contributor to the global incidence of HCC. Non‑coding RNAs (ncRNAs), once regarded as 'genomic dark matter', are increasingly recognised as key regulatory molecules in a variety of liver diseases. However, their systematic involvement in the malignant progression from MASLD to HCC remains incompletely understood. Emerging evidence suggests that ncRNAs play critical roles in modulating the major pathophysiological processes underlying MASLD‑driven HCC progression, including dysregulated lipid metabolism, chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, immune imbalance and gut microbiota disruption. The present review systematically examines the specific functions of major ncRNA classes, including microRNAs, long ncRNAs and circular RNAs, in the pathogenesis of MASLD‑driven HCC. In addition, given their considerable diagnostic and therapeutic potential, the present review evaluates the prospects of ncRNAs as novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets to facilitate the early detection and precision treatment of MASLD‑driven HCC.

articles.title: Mitochondrial dysfunction in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: Mechanistic insights and therapeutic horizons (Review).
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction‑associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as a central driver of the global chronic liver disease burden. Its progression toward metabolic dysfunction‑associated steatohepatitis and advanced liver fibrosis is shifting from the traditional view of simple lipid accumulation to a dynamic pathogenic network centered on mitochondrial dysfunction. The present review systematically delineates the non‑linear kinetic evolution of mitochondrial alteration from early 'hormetic compensatory adaptation' to late 'bioenergetic collapse' during MASLD progression. The molecular basis of mitochondrial quality control, including fission/fusion dynamics, mitophagy, the mitochondrial unfolded protein response and inter‑organelle cross‑talk via mitochondria‑associated endoplasmic reticulum membranes are critically discussed. Focus is placed on the key homeostatic networks regulated by the sirtuin family (SIRT1‑SIRT7), dissecting their context‑dependent roles and current academic controversies. Finally, contemporary clinical and preclinical therapeutic strategies targeting mitochondrial metabolism are evaluated, providing a strict evidence‑graded translational perspective from basic research toward clinical precision medicine.

articles.title: S100 proteins in kidney disease: Inflammatory biomarkers, pathogenic mechanisms and therapeutic prospects (Review).
articles.abstract: The S100 protein family, particularly the calprotectin heterodimer S100A8/A9, is increasingly recognized as both an inflammatory readout and a context‑dependent mediator of kidney injury. Selected extracellular S100 proteins function as damage‑associated molecular patterns released during cellular stress, leukocyte activation and tissue injury. They can amplify sterile inflammation through the receptor for advanced glycation end‑products (RAGE), Toll‑like receptor 4 (TLR4) and related downstream pathways, although receptor usage and biological effects vary by cell type and disease setting. The present review examines S100 proteins in kidney disease across three related domains: Clinical biomarkers, disease mechanisms and therapeutic translation. Current evidence most strongly supports urinary S100A8/A9 for distinguishing intrinsic from pre‑renal acute kidney injury; circulating S100A8/A9 and S100A12 have mainly been studied as markers of inflammatory and cardiovascular risk in chronic kidney disease. S100‑associated signaling has been implicated in leukocyte recruitment, mesangial and macrophage activation, podocyte injury, tubular stress, tubulointerstitial fibrosis and uremia‑associated vascular calcification. Emerging studies also describe stress‑regulated and intracellular S100 functions, including gasdermin E (GSDME)‑regulated signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) signaling that controls S100A7A, S100‑annexin complexes and S100A16‑driven Wnt/β‑catenin or endoplasmic reticulum stress. However, therapeutic evidence remains largely preclinical, and clinical translation is constrained by ligand redundancy, disease heterogeneity and incomplete prospective validation. S100 proteins may therefore contribute to biomarker panels and targeted interventions, but their clinical utility requires prospective validation and clear separation of receptor‑mediated from intracellular effects.

articles.title: Role of glucagon‑like peptide‑1 receptor in cancer: Mechanisms and pharmacologic intervention (Review).
articles.abstract: The glucagon‑like peptide‑1 (GLP‑1) receptor, a G‑protein‑coupled receptor distributed in multiple tissues, can regulate the homeostasis of blood glucose and lipids. GLP‑1 receptor agonist (GLP‑1RA) has been recognized as an effective hypoglycemic drug. The disruption of metabolic processes in diabetes may lead to dysregulation of numerous signaling pathways, thereby promoting the development of malignant tumors. Therefore, the activity of the GLP‑1 receptor may contribute to the development of cancer. Over the years, advancements have been made in understanding the inhibitory effect of GLP‑1RAs on tumorigenesis. Activation of the GLP‑1 receptor can inhibit tumorigenesis by reducing neuroinflammation and oxidative stress, modulating the tumor immune microenvironment and enhancing the chemosensitivity. In addition, GLP‑1RAs also regulate the activity of several related signaling pathways involved in tumorigenesis (such as the AMPK, PI3K/Akt and cAMP/PKA pathways). In the present review, a comprehensive review of the distribution of GLP‑1 receptors and the pharmacological effects of GLP‑1RAs is provided. The intrinsic relationship between GLP‑1 receptors and cancer risk is also discussed, as well as the mechanisms of GLP‑1RAs in inhibiting cancer, with the aim to provide valuable insights for the treatment of cancer using GLP‑1RAs.

articles.title: Urological manifestations in obesity.
articles.journal: Current opinion in endocrinology, diabetes, and obesity
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The global prevalence of obesity continues to rise, with effects ranging across urology. This review summarizes recent evidence on obesity and its impact on various urological conditions, including malignancy, infections, stone disease, functional urology and male reproductive health, chronic kidney disease, and pediatric urology, to guide comprehensive management in this population.

RECENT FINDINGS: Obesity has a paradoxical survival benefit in patients with renal cell carcinoma, while its impact drives aggressive prostate cancer. Obesity increases kidney stone risk, with sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists showing divergent effects on lithogenesis and urinary tract infections. It is a modifiable risk factor for overactive bladder and stress urinary incontinence, both of which improve with weight loss/ bariatric surgery. Robotic surgery mitigates obesity-related perioperative risk. Hypogonadism secondary to obesity is a major reversible cause of male infertility. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA) reverse metabolic hypogonadism and helps in slowing chronic kidney progression. Maternal and childhood obesity may impair testicular descent and can also increase the risk of nocturnal enuresis.

SUMMARY: Obesity's urological effects are heterogeneous, paradoxical from pediatric to adults, mediated by insulin resistance, chronic inflammation, and hormonal dysregulation. Weight loss and the use of GLP-1 RA may offer a unique strategy for optimizing and treating urological conditions.

articles.title: Recent advances in polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome and obesity: a comprehensive review.
articles.journal: Current opinion in endocrinology, diabetes, and obesity
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review evaluates recent advances in polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), emphasizing its complex association with obesity and the ongoing transition toward precision medicine. The synthesis of current evidence addresses pathophysiology, emerging biomarkers, and multiomics approaches, highlighting their potential to enhance diagnosis, risk stratification, and individualized management.

RECENT FINDINGS: PMOS is a multifactorial disorder involving insulin resistance, hyperandrogenism, genetic predisposition, gut dysbiosis, and environmental factors. Obesity intensifies metabolic and reproductive dysfunction through mechanisms including chronic inflammation, adipose tissue dysfunction, and altered gut-ovary signalling. Traditional phenotype-based classifications do not adequately capture this biological heterogeneity. Multiomics approaches that integrate genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and microbiome data have identified distinct molecular subtypes, including insulin-resistant, steroidogenic, inflammatory, and neuroendocrine clusters. Novel biomarkers, including anti-Müllerian hormone, free androgen index, and specific metabolomic and lipidomic signatures, have the potential to improve diagnostic accuracy and phenotyping.

SUMMARY: The integration of multiomics represents a pivotal advancement toward patient-centred care in PMOS by enabling early risk prediction and mechanism-based therapies. While current evidence remains largely exploratory, these developments support a shift from uniform treatment strategies to precision endocrinology, with the potential to substantially improve long-term metabolic and reproductive outcomes.

articles.title: Early clinical and functional predictors of functional recovery after hemorrhagic stroke: a scoping review: Erratum.
articles.journal: International journal of rehabilitation research. Internationale Zeitschrift fur Rehabilitationsforschung. Revue internationale de recherches de readaptation

articles.title: One-stop photon-counting CT angiography for simultaneous assessment of cardio-cerebrovascular lesions: A case report.
articles.abstract: We report a 73-year-old male admitted for 2-year progressive dysuria, with incidental detection of abnormal cardiovascular signs on physical examination. Initial evaluation via energy-integrating detector computed tomography (EID-CT) coronary angiography and cranial magnetic resonance imaging identified key vascular abnormalities, while subsequent photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT) combined cardio-cerebral computed tomography angiography (CTA) provided more detailed assessment of stenosis severity, plaque composition, and the entire vascular bed. The combined PCD-CT scan delineated synchronous lesions in detail: proximal left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery plaque, ascending aortic dilatation with left coronary sinus aneurysm compressing the left atrium, and occlusion of the intracranial right vertebral artery. Importantly, PCD-CT cardio-cerebral CTA yielded a lower radiation dose compared with standalone EID-CT coronary angiography. With spectral reconstruction, the severity of LAD stenosis was re-evaluated and interpreted as mild stenosis, a lower grade than that assessed by EID-CT; meanwhile, 0.4 mm thin-slice imaging enabled detailed compositional analysis of the coronary plaque, with imaging features suggestive of a stable plaque. Based on multidisciplinary discussion integrating all imaging findings and clinical context, a treatment strategy was formulated: prioritize high-risk aortic lesion management, synchronously perform coronary artery bypass grafting for myocardial ischemia prevention, and electively address intracranial stenosis. This case demonstrates the preliminary clinical value of PCD-CT as a supportive imaging modality for the evaluation and multidisciplinary management of concurrent cardio-cerebrovascular diseases.

articles.title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitors in World Health Organization Group 1 Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: A REVEAL Lite 2-Matched Cohort With Time-Varying Exposure Analysis.
articles.journal: Mayo Clinic proceedings. Innovations, quality & outcomes
articles.abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) improve outcomes across several cardiometabolic conditions, but their role in World Health Organization group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains uncertain. We conducted a retrospective, single-center cohort study of adults with group 1 PAH. Patients prescribed SGLT2i were compared with patients without exposure. Propensity-score matching was performed 1:2 using age, sex, baseline REVEAL Lite 2 risk category, diabetes mellitus, and statin use. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality, and the secondary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events. Associations were evaluated using fixed-exposure and start-stop time-varying Cox models. The matched cohort included 366 patients: 122 (33%) receiving SGLT2i and 244 (67%) controls. Most patients were classified as high risk by REVEAL Lite 2 (106 SGLT2i recipients (87%) and 215 controls (88%), respectively). In the fixed-exposure analysis, SGLT2i use was associated with lower mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.53; 95% CI, 0.31-0.91; P=.018), without a significant difference in major adverse cardiovascular events (HR, 1.23; 95% CI, 0.93-1.63; P=.14). In the time-varying analysis, SGLT2i exposure was not significantly associated with mortality (HR, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.26-2.11; P=.57). The apparent survival association was attenuated after accounting for treatment timing, demonstrating the sensitivity of observational PAH estimates to exposure classification and supporting prospective randomized trials.

articles.title: Infective endocarditis presenting as febrile stroke and complicated with multi-territorial systemic embolization in a young woman: A case report.
articles.abstract: Infective endocarditis (IE) is a life-threatening condition frequently complicated by systemic embolization, most commonly involving the central nervous system, spleen, and kidneys. In a young patient, a febrile ischemic stroke should be considered infective endocarditis until proven otherwise, given the diagnostic and prognostic stakes of an early diagnosis. Multi-territorial embolic dissemination at presentation, however, remains uncommon and carries substantial clinical implications. We report the case of a 49-year-old woman with an undocumented mitral valve disease who presented with acute left hemiparesis and a one-month history of high-grade fever. Brain MRI revealed an acute ischemic stroke of the right middle cerebral artery territory. Transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography demonstrated mobile vegetations on the mitral valve, and blood cultures isolated Streptococcus species, establishing a definite diagnosis of infective endocarditis. Contrast-enhanced CT of the brain, chest, abdomen, and pelvis, together with spinal MRI, revealed extensive systemic embolization involving five distinct vascular territories: a cerebral septic embolic focus, splenic and renal infarction, a mycotic aneurysm of the ileocolic artery, and infectious spondylodiscitis. This case underscores that a febrile ischemic stroke in a young patient warrants urgent screening for infective endocarditis, and highlights the value of a systematic, whole-body imaging work-up in detecting clinically silent embolic complications and guiding patient management.

articles.title: A qualitative assessment of learner experiences with a novel Paediatric Emergency Medicine curriculum in Kenya.
articles.journal: African journal of emergency medicine : Revue africaine de la medecine d'urgence
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Paediatric emergency and critical care (PECC) services are essential in reducing childhood mortality from treatable conditions, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa where the burden remains high. Despite this need, access to subspecialty training in PECC has been limited in the region. Launched in 2019 at the University of Nairobi, the PECC-Kenya fellowship is a novel subspecialty training program for regional paediatricians in both paediatric emergency medicine (PEM) and critical care. Curricular elements for PEM within the fellowship were adapted from international guidelines for local context. The objective of this study was to explore the perspectives of current fellows and recent graduates on the content of the PEM portion of their curriculum to inform improvements and future development for the program and the region.

METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with current and former PECC-Kenya fellows. Program faculty developed an interview guide which included questions about perceptions on PEM, anticipated future practice, and strengths and opportunities within the curriculum. Interviews were conducted and recorded via Zoom by a non-faculty interviewer. Anonymized transcriptions were uploaded into Dedoose. After establishing inter-rater reliability, three reviewers coded the data, and key themes were identified.

RESULTS: Ten interviews were conducted in 2022 and 2023, revealing several themes. Fellows anticipated providing continuous care from the emergency department to the intensive care unit as the sole PECC specialist in their institution or region. They highlighted program strengths including high-quality live online lectures, in-person PEM intensive training, diverse clinical exposure, and establishment of a peer network. Fellows expressed a desire for more hands-on training and recognized the importance of point-of-care ultrasound in facilitating rapid diagnosis and assisting in procedures, with need for additional training.

DISCUSSION: Given the innovative nature of this training program and its distinctive demands, these themes and findings could serve as valuable guidance for similar initiatives emerging in the region.

articles.title: Lenticulostriate vasculopathy in neonates: An imaging marker with heterogeneous clinical significance.
articles.abstract: Lenticulostriate vasculopathy (LSV) is a relatively common cranial ultrasound finding in neonates, characterized by linear or branching hyperechogenic striations within the basal ganglia and/or thalamus along the lenticulostriate arteries. Although initially associated with congenital infections, particularly cytomegalovirus (CMV), LSV is now recognized in a broad range of clinical settings, and its prognostic significance remains controversial. We report 3 neonatal cases illustrating the heterogeneous contexts in which LSV may occur. The first case was a term male neonate with transient respiratory distress and normal neurological examination; cranial ultrasound on day 3 showed unilateral right-sided fine linear striations in the basal ganglia without parenchymal abnormalities. Infectious workup was negative and outcome was favorable. The second case involved a 36-week male neonate born after acute fetal distress, with severe respiratory distress requiring resuscitation. Cranial ultrasound demonstrated unilateral left-sided LSV without hemorrhagic or hypoxic-ischemic lesions; subsequent brain MRI was normal, with favorable follow-up and slight regression of the ultrasound abnormalities. The third case was a term female neonate with prolonged jaundice, hypotonia, hepatosplenomegaly, thrombocytopenia, and abnormal liver function tests. Cranial ultrasound revealed bilateral branching striations, and congenital CMV infection was confirmed by urine PCR. These cases highlight the nonspecific nature of LSV, which may occur as an isolated finding, with perinatal hypoxic or hemodynamic disturbances, or with congenital infection. Recognition of LSV should be interpreted in the clinical context, with targeted investigation when abnormalities are present, while isolated forms may have a favorable outcome.

articles.title: Predictors of Blood Culture Ordering and Results for Febrile Infants Aged 91 to 365 Days in the Emergency Department.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The risk of invasive bacterial infections has dropped significantly among febrile infants due to widespread vaccination efforts. In older infants (age 91 days and older), diagnostic guidance is limited, and blood culture ordering is based on clinical judgment. We sought to evaluate blood culture ordering practice, bacteremia incidence, and the patient characteristics of true positive blood culture results.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of febrile pediatric patients aged 91 to 365 days who presented to Kaiser Permanente Northern California emergency departments (EDs) between January 1, 2018, and December 31, 2019, who had blood cultures drawn. We identified variables related to blood culture ordering using a generalized linear mixed model and adjudicated all positive results to determine rates of true bacteremia or contamination, as well as clinical characteristics of children with true positive bacteremia.

RESULTS: Among 5543 febrile infants, 611 (11.0%) underwent blood culture testing. After adjustment for covariates, higher ED temperature (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.40, 95% CI, 1.30 to 1.50), presence of comorbidities (aOR 2.55, 95% CI, 2.00 to 3.25), and younger age (aOR 0.996, 95% CI, 0.995 to 0.998, P < .001) were associated with blood culture ordering. Of the 37 (6.1%) positive blood cultures, only 16 (2.6%) were true positives. All true positives occurred in infants with either an identifiable risk factor or a clinically evident source of infection. There were no cases of occult bacteremia identified.

CONCLUSION: In febrile infants aged 91 to 365 days, true bacteremia was rare and associated with significant comorbidities or an obvious infectious source. Our findings suggest a more directed approach to ED blood culture ordering.

articles.title: Use of Janus kinase inhibitors during early pregnancy in patients with rheumatic disease: a case series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi) are increasingly used to treat systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases in patients of reproductive age, but pregnancy safety data remain limited. Current guidelines recommend discontinuation before conception and avoidance during pregnancy; however, inadvertent early exposures occur and create counselling uncertainty.

CASE SUMMARY: We identified 3 pregnancies with confirmed postconception JAKi exposure among 111 patients followed in a specialised pregnancy and rheumatic diseases clinic between July 2021 and September 2024. Two patients with psoriatic or seronegative inflammatory arthritis were exposed to upadacitinib 15 mg daily for 16 and 13 days after conception, respectively. One patient with rheumatoid arthritis was exposed to tofacitinib 5 mg twice daily for 30 days after conception. All JAKi were discontinued when pregnancy was recognised. One patient remained off immunosuppression until postpartum flare. One required prednisone and transitioned to certolizumab for a second-trimester inflammatory arthritis flare. One transitioned to hydroxychloroquine with stable disease. All pregnancies resulted in live births at 37 + 6 to 39 weeks. No congenital anomalies were identified. One infant, delivered by emergency caesarean section complicated by difficult fetal extraction, developed respiratory distress at birth and was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit for 3 days for monitoring. The available documentation did not identify suspected or confirmed infection.

CONCLUSIONS: These 3 cases add to limited real-world evidence regarding inadvertent first-trimester JAKi exposure in rheumatic disease. The findings are reassuring but cannot establish safety, and prospective data with longer infant follow-up remain needed.

articles.title: Protocol for a phase I/II, open-label, single-arm trial of autologous chemically induced liver progenitor (CLiP) cell transplantation in patients with decompensated cirrhosis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Decompensated cirrhosis is associated with a poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options for patients who are not candidates for liver transplantation. Although various cell-based regenerative therapies have been investigated, their clinical benefits are limited. Autologous chemically-induced liver progenitor cells (CLiPs) are expandable progenitor-like cells generated from mature hepatocytes using small-molecule reprogramming and have demonstrated regenerative potential in multiple preclinical models. Because CLiPs are bipotent and can differentiate toward both hepatocytic and biliary epithelial lineages, their lineage fate after transplantation may be influenced by the recipient liver microenvironment, and whether transplanted CLiPs undergo hepatocytic maturation in the human decompensated cirrhotic liver to the extent observed in animal models remains unknown. We describe the rationale and design of the first-in-human clinical trial evaluating autologous CLiP transplantation for decompensated cirrhosis.

SETTING: Autologous CLiP cells (CLP-001) are manufactured from liver tissue obtained by laparoscopic partial hepatectomy and expanded in a certified Cell Processing Center under controlled conditions. Quality and safety assessment includes histopathological examination of the harvested liver tissue, sterility, endotoxin and mycoplasma testing, viable cell count, cell viability, cell-surface marker characterization, copy-number variation (CNV) analysis, and targeted cancer-related gene-panel testing (Table 1). The study is conducted under the Japanese Act on the Safety of Regenerative Medicine and has been approved by a Certified Special Committee for Regenerative Medicine.

METHODS: This is a first-in-human, single-center, open-label, single-arm phase I/II study. Three adults with Child-Pugh class B decompensated cirrhosis who are not candidates for liver transplantation will be enrolled. Approximately 30 g of liver tissue will be harvested laparoscopically and used for CLiP manufacturing over a 12-16 week period. Following successful quality and safety testing, CLP-001 will be administered into the portal venous system through surgical cannulation of the ileocolic vein. The primary endpoint is safety, defined as adverse events and product-related deficiencies from tissue procurement through 1 month after transplantation. Secondary and exploratory endpoints include safety through 12 months and descriptive changes in liver function, fibrosis-related biomarkers, liver stiffness, and clinical manifestations of cirrhosis.

CONCLUSION: This is, to our knowledge, the first clinical evaluation of autologous CLiP transplantation in patients with decompensated cirrhosis. The trial is designed to establish the safety and procedural feasibility of the entire therapeutic workflow, including tissue procurement, cell manufacturing, quality assurance, and portal venous administration. Efficacy-related observations are exploratory, and the lineage fate of transplanted CLiPs cannot be directly established in this study. The findings are expected to provide the first clinical evidence regarding the safety and feasibility of autologous CLiP transplantation and support the future development of CLiP-based regenerative therapy for advanced chronic liver disease. At the time of submission, patient enrollment has commenced, and no participant has yet undergone CLiP transplantation.

articles.title: Focal hyperinsulinism in ectopic pancreatic tissue: preoperative localization and curative resection.
articles.abstract: Ectopic pancreas (EP) is pancreatic tissue located outside the native pancreas. Most cases are asymptomatic and identified incidentally. Only a few cases of hyperinsulinism (HI) arising from EP have been reported. We describe an infant who had neonatal hypoglycemia which was not shown to be resolved and later presented at 5 months of age with recurrent abnormal limb movements associated with severe hypoglycemia. Following failure of diazoxide therapy, genetic testing identified a paternally inherited pathogenic variant in ABCC8. Preoperative fluorine-18-L-dihydroxyphenylalanine positron emission tomography/computed tomography (18F-DOPA PET/CT) revealed a focal area of uptake in the distal duodenum/proximal jejunum consistent with ectopic pancreatic tissue. Surgical resection of this lesion resulted in complete resolution of hypoglycemia while preserving the native pancreas. We review previously reported cases of congenital HI arising in ectopic pancreatic tissue, highlighting the novelty of preoperative 18F-DOPA PET/CT localization that enabled curative resection during the initial surgery for our patient.

articles.title: A stretchable liquid-metal bioelectric catheter for active management of catheter-associated urinary tract infections.
articles.abstract: Catheter-associated urinary tract infections (CAUTIs) continue to be a major clinical complication of indwelling catheterization, sustained by persistent bacterial colonization and dysregulated local immune responses. Most antimicrobial coatings provide passive protection and have limited capacity to address both bacterial persistence and the host response at the catheter-tissue interface. This study presents a stretchable urological catheter for electrical stimulation (SUCES) based on a liquid metal composite. SUCES consists of a stable gallium-10 vol% silver (Ga-Ag) circuit encapsulated within a silver-doped (5 vol%) polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS-Ag) layer. SUCES delivers low-voltage electrical stimulation (1.5 V for 5 min) in combination with sustained Ag release, resulting in effective combined antibacterial activity. In vitro testing demonstrates bacterial killing efficiencies of approximately 95% for E. coli and 94% for S. aureus. The same electrical input also promoted an M1-associated macrophage response. In a rabbit CAUTI model, seven days of treatment reduced the viable urinary bacterial burden by 93% (>1-log reduction). SUCES-treated tissues also showed less infection-associated inflammation and better-preserved urothelial barrier integrity. These findings support SUCES as an active bioelectric catheter interface that integrates antibacterial treatment with macrophage-associated immune modulation for catheter-associated infection management.

articles.title: QRISK3 Assessment Identified Essential Thrombocythemia Patients at High Risk of Thrombotic Events Regardless of Revised IPSET-T Score and JAK2 Mutational Status.

articles.title: Remimazolam for Procedural Sedation During Synchronized Electrical Cardioversion in the Emergency Department.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open
articles.abstract: Synchronized electrical cardioversion necessitates procedural sedation to ensure patient comfort and amnesia. Remimazolam is a novel, ultrashort-acting intravenous benzodiazepine with organ-independent esterase metabolism, a favorable safety profile, and flumazenil reversibility. Although, previously described in the electrophysiology laboratory, use of remimazolam has not been reported for electrical cardioversion in the emergency department. In this case, a 67-year-old man with sudden-onset paroxysmal atrial fibrillation presented in symptomatic atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. Following rate and rhythm optimization, the decision was made to proceed with synchronized electrical cardioversion under procedural sedation. After consent was obtained, remimazolam (5 mg intravenously) was administered as a single bolus. Sedation onset occurred at 49 seconds, with adequate depth achieved at 1 minute 37 seconds. A single synchronized biphasic 200 joule electric shock was successfully delivered at 2 minutes 20 seconds, converting the patient to normal sinus rhythm. Eye opening occurred at 3 minutes 50 seconds, with return to baseline orientation at 4 minutes 30 seconds. No apnea, hypoxia, hemodynamic instability, or procedural recall was observed. Continuous end-tidal carbon dioxide monitoring confirmed uninterrupted spontaneous ventilation throughout. The rapid onset, hemodynamic stability, and remarkably brief recovery time observed support its potential as a first-line sedative for emergency department cardioversion. Further prospective study in this setting is warranted.

articles.title: WHO Basic Emergency Care (BEC) training in Liberia: pre-course, post-course, and one-year outcomes.
articles.journal: African journal of emergency medicine : Revue africaine de la medecine d'urgence
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Liberia faces persistent gaps in emergency care training. The World Health Organization (WHO) Basic Emergency Care (BEC) Course was developed in 2018 to support training of frontline emergency care providers in resource-limited settings. While prior studies have shown short-term knowledge gains and confidence improvements, limited data exists regarding longer-term retention. This study sought to evaluate knowledge acquisition, knowledge retention, and self-reported confidence immediately after and one year following WHO Basic Emergency Care training.

METHODS: We conducted two four-day WHO BEC trainings for graduating medical students and practicing providers at A.M. Dogliotti School of Medicine in Monrovia, Liberia. Participants completed knowledge tests, self-assessment surveys, and course evaluations before training, immediately after training, and at one-year follow-up. Paired pre/post comparisons were analyzed using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, and cohort comparisons for post-course practical case scenarios and course evaluations used Fisher's exact test and unpaired t-tests, respectively.

RESULTS: Some 40 participants completed training, including 30 medical students, nine nurses, and one general practitioner. 33 of 40 participants (82.5%) completed the one-year follow-up assessment. Median knowledge scores increased from 76% pre-course to 96% immediately post-course and remained higher than baseline at one year (88%; all p < 0.0001). Self-reported confidence also improved substantially, including comfort managing emergency patients and preparedness to see emergency care patients, with gains sustained at one year. Improvements were observed across key emergency care domains, including shock, airway management, pediatric and adult emergencies, and emergency pharmacology. Course evaluations were highly positive across all domains, with mean ratings ranging from 3.8 to 5.0 out of 5.

DISCUSSION: WHO BEC training was associated with substantial improvements in emergency care knowledge and confidence among Liberian providers, with evidence of knowledge retention at one year. These findings support implementation of WHO BEC training as a sustainable strategy to strengthen emergency care capacity in resource-limited African settings.

articles.title: In-Hospital Outcomes and Mortality After Revascularization for Chronic Mesenteric Ischemia by Maintenance Dialysis Status: A National Inpatient Sample Analysis, 2006-2020.
articles.journal: Journal of investigative surgery : the official journal of the Academy of Surgical Research
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Evidence on in-hospital outcomes after chronic mesenteric ischemia (CMI) revascularization in patients receiving maintenance dialysis is limited.

METHODS: We analyzed adult CMI-coded hospitalizations undergoing endovascular or open revascularization in the 2006-2020 National Inpatient Sample. Hospitalizations with and without maintenance dialysis were compared using 1:2 propensity score matching and survey-weighted multivariable regression.

RESULTS: Of 7,962 eligible hospitalizations, 411 (5.2% of the unweighted sample) involved maintenance dialysis. Maintenance dialysis was associated with higher adjusted odds of in-hospital mortality (aOR 1.96), non-routine discharge (aOR 1.46), prolonged hospitalization (aOR 1.41), transfusion (aOR 1.43), sepsis (aOR 1.88), pneumonia (aOR 1.69), multiorgan failure or shock (aOR 1.80), and venous thromboembolism (aOR 2.06). Hospital charges were also higher (adjusted beta USD 17,497), whereas urinary tract infection odds were lower (aOR 0.68).

DISCUSSION: Maintenance dialysis was associated with greater in-hospital morbidity and mortality among CMI-coded revascularization hospitalizations. The inability to distinguish stable from acute-on-chronic CMI limits interpretation as an elective cohort. Findings support individualized perioperative assessment without establishing causation or optimal treatment timing.

articles.title: NLRP3 inflammasome in major swine viral infections: Host defense and viral antagonism.
articles.abstract: The NLRP3 inflammasome is a cytosolic signaling platform that drives caspase-1-dependent maturation of IL-1β and IL-18 and gasdermin D (GSDMD)-mediated pyroptosis. During infection with major porcine viruses - including African swine fever virus, porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus, pseudorabies virus, porcine epidemic diarrhea virus, transmissible gastroenteritis virus, and porcine circovirus type 2, NLRP3 exerts opposing effects: moderate activation restricts viral propagation, whereas sustained stimulation drives tissue injury. We review how structurally unrelated viral proteins converge on limited upstream events - endolysosomal damage, ion flux, mitochondrial injury, ER stress, and the ubiquitin-autophagy network. Because genetically distinct porcine pathogens exploit this same regulatory axis, it represents a shared point of vulnerability. We assess therapeutic options targeting NLRP3 assembly, GSDMD pore formation, and host proteostasis, and highlight questions requiring validation in porcine cells and pigs.

articles.title: A 2026 update on the epidemiology of obesity, related cardio-kidney-liver metabolic complications and beyond; a call to action.
articles.abstract: Obesity has become a major global public health challenge and is associated with an increasing burden of metabolic and non-metabolic comorbidities. We aimed to provide an updated assessment of the global prevalence of overweight and obesity and to examine temporal trends in selected associated with excess adiposity. Data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) Study were analyzed to estimate the prevalence of overweight and obesity among adults aged ≥20 years in 2023, stratified by sex and age group. We additionally examined age-standardized global prevalence trends for obesity and selected diseases associated with excess adiposity, including type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), cardiovascular disease (CVD), along with other chronic diseases associated with excess adiposity, such as dementias and obesity-related cancers, over 2000-2023.In 2023, the prevalence of overweight was generally higher in men, whereas obesity was more prevalent among women, particularly during middle age. Both overweight and obesity increased from early adulthood, peaked during middle age, and subsequently declined at older ages. Globally, obesity prevalence increased by approximately 95% between 2000 and 2023, reaching 19.5% in 2023. During the same period, the age-standardized prevalence of MASLD, T2DM, CKD, dementias, and obesity-related cancers increased. In contrast, age-standardized CVD prevalence decreased slightly and the divergent trends between obesity and age-standardized CVD prevalence highlight the multifactorial nature of cardiovascular risk and the potential impact of improvements in other cardiovascular risk factors. These findings underscore the urgent need for integrated, population-level strategies to prevent and effectively manage obesity and its complications.

articles.title: Neighbourhood health inequity and the incidence of stroke and transient ischemic attack.
articles.journal: Scandinavian journal of primary health care
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Despite generous welfare systems and equitable built environments previous research has shown clear differences in cardiovascular health between areas with different socioeconomic status (SES) in Sweden. To direct public health initiatives, there is a need for updated data of SES differences in stroke and whether transient ischemic attack (TIA) incidence also differs based on neighbourhood SES.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Within the Multimorbidity Integrated Registry Across Care Levels in Stockholm cohort (MIRACLE-S), encompassing healthcare visits and diagnoses from all care levels, we followed 1.4 million individuals without a history of stroke or TIA for 12 years (2014-2025). We used Cox and Poisson regression and analysed both the baseline risk prospectively and a time updated analysis in different neighbourhood-SES.

RESULTS: Neighbourhoods with low SES had a higher incidence of stroke. Among both men and women, SES difference in stroke incidence were greatest before age 65, with no significant differences at age 80 or older. For TIA, we observed a higher incidence in high SES neighbourhoods, particularly among men.

DISCUSSION: The higher stroke incidence in low SES neighbourhoods indicates a need for targeted prevention. Low awareness and underdiagnosis may explanation the lower risk of TIA in low SES neighbourhoods, supporting targeted efforts to improve TIA detection, which could in turn help prevent stroke. Effective mitigation likely requires geographically focused medical care and primary prevention in low-SES neighbourhoods.

articles.title: Clinical, metabolic, dermoscopic, and reflectance confocal microscopy features of prurigo pigmentosa: a retrospective case series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prurigo pigmentosa (PP) is a chronic, recurrent inflammatory dermatitis with nonspecific stage-dependent clinical features, leading to misdiagnosis. Noninvasive imaging may complement clinical and histopathological assessment. Metabolic abnormalities have been reported in PP, although their clinical significance remains unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To characterize the clinical, metabolic, dermoscopic, and reflectance confocal microscopy (RCM) features of PP and reduce misdiagnosis.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients with histopathologically confirmed PP and available metabolic screening data from July 2020 to April 2026. Clinical, dermoscopic, RCM, laboratory, treatment, and follow-up data were extracted from medical records.

RESULTS: Nine women aged 17-33 years had seasonal eruptions (June-September). Seven reported dietary triggers, including caloric restriction in four and ketogenic diets in three. Disease duration ranged from 0.5 to 37 months, with initial misdiagnoses as eczema or contact dermatitis. Metabolic abnormalities included dyslipidemia (n=8), type 2 diabetes (n=3), elevated urinary ketones (n=3), hepatic steatosis (n=7), and elevated body mass index (n=7). Lesions were classified as early (n=3), fully developed (n=5), and late stage (n=1). Dermoscopy identified punctate, linear, and reticular vascular patterns with granular, patchy, or honeycomb-like brown pigmentation. RCM revealed epidermal spongiosis, basal cell degeneration, melanophage infiltration, and dermal inflammatory infiltrates.

CONCLUSION: Nonspecific features and coexistence of lesions at different stages contribute to diagnostic difficulty. Dermoscopy and RCM may provide complementary noninvasive information for clinical and histopathological evaluation. Metabolic screening may be considered in patients with recurrent disease, dietary triggers, elevated BMI, ketonuria, or suspected lipid/glucose metabolism abnormalities.

articles.title: Acute‑on‑chronic kidney disease (AoCKD): a critical appraisal and call for action to define boundaries and optimize management.
articles.abstract: Acute‑on‑chronic kidney disease (AoCKD) refers to an acute decline in renal function occurring in individuals with established CKD. Despite its major clinical impact-including increased mortality, accelerated CKD progression, and higher cardiovascular risk-AoCKD remains underrepresented within major guideline frameworks (KDIGO, ADQI, NICE). Our review aims to critically appraise existing guideline frameworks, definitions, biomarkers, imaging recommendations, and research gaps related to AoCKD, and to highlight priorities for future harmonization and clinical integration. We conducted a targeted literature search of PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, to identify guidelines, consensus reports, observational studies, and systematic reviews describing acute deterioration in CKD. Extracted data included definitional criteria, epidemiology, biomarker performance, imaging guidance, and prognostic outcomes. Current KDIGO, ADQI, and NICE frameworks were evaluated in parallel. We report marked heterogeneity in definitions describing acute deterioration in CKD, with terms including AoCKD, AKI‑on‑CKD, acute pre‑existing kidney dysfunction, and cROCK‑based definitions. Reported incidence varies widely (1-33%) due to inconsistent criteria. Creatinine‑based definitions show reduced prognostic accuracy in CKD populations, whereas cystatin‑C-based eGFR demonstrates superior discrimination for mortality and progression. We propose an operational definition of AoCKD that includes functional criteria and biomarker-based criteria. The definition reflects the increased mortality in this phenotype even before reaching the KDIGO-AKI threshold. In conclusion, AoCKD is a clinically significant but poorly defined state within the kidney disease continuum. Harmonized definitions, incorporation of cystatin‑C-based markers, structured imaging pathways, and integration of early biomarkers are urgently needed.

articles.title: Beyond clinician time constraints: an organisational accountability framework for hypertension care.
Pregnancy and iron deficiency anemia are associated with COVID-19 severity: a retrospective cohort study from Gaza.
articles.journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: COVID-19 poses significant risks to pregnant women, with pregnancy recognized as a risk factor for severe disease. This vulnerability may be exacerbated by iron deficiency anemia (IDA) due to impaired immune function, reduced oxygen transport, and altered coagulation and endothelial function.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of 271 unvaccinated, otherwise healthy women aged 18-38 with COVID-19 was conducted at Al-Shifa Hospital, Gaza (2021). Pregnant (n = 97) and nonpregnant (n = 174) groups were stratified by IDA, investigating the impact of pregnancy and IDA on the severity of COVID-19. Iron deficiency was determined by transferrin saturation levels <20% measured during acute infection, whereas ferritin levels were not available.

RESULTS: Overall pregnancy was significantly associated with COVID-19 severity (p < 0.001), with pregnant women having higher odds of critical illness (OR = 4.61, 95% CI 2.27-9.39, p < 0.001) and death (OR = 5.25, 95% CI 1.91-14.44, p = 0.001) compared with moderate illness. All deaths were due to acute respiratory distress syndrome; no venous thromboembolism cases occurred. IDA was associated with COVID-19 severity in both pregnant (p = 0.015) and non-pregnant (p = 0.002) women. In a multivariable model including pregnancy, IDA was associated with higher odds of severe (OR = 3.57, 95% CI 1.97-6.48, p < 0.001), critical (OR = 2.25, 95% CI 1.09-4.64, p = 0.029), and fatal illness (OR = 7.23, 95% CI 1.96-26.74, p = 0.003) compared with moderate illness.

CONCLUSION: This study suggests that among young, otherwise healthy, unvaccinated women with COVID-19, pregnancy and IDA are associated with increased COVID-19 severity. However, interpretation requires caution considering the small number of events, particularly deaths, and the assessment of iron status during acute infection using transferrin saturation alone without ferritin measurements, which limits the ability to distinguish preexisting iron deficiency from inflammation-related changes in iron metabolism.

articles.title: Divergent epidemiologic, shared risks: a comparative global analysis of COPD, ischemic stroke, and intracerebral hemorrhage.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although COPD and stroke share pathological mechanisms and risk factors, their epidemiological patterns differ significantly. This study investigates the global burden of COPD and stroke, analyzing their shared risk factors and epidemiological disparities to inform targeted prevention strategies.

METHODS: Using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 estimates, we conducted a repeated cross-sectional comparison of COPD, IS, and ICH from 1990 to 2021. Historical age-standardized rates were taken directly from archived GBD records labelled 'Age-standardized', whereas age-specific analyses used groups aged ≥20 years. We examined temporal, geographical, age-specific, sex-specific, and Socio-demographic Index (SDI) patterns, shared risk-attributable DALY rates, and exploratory Bayesian age-period-cohort (BAPC) projections through 2050.

RESULTS: From 1990 to 2021, absolute incident cases for all three conditions increased, while age-standardized incidence rates declined. In 2021, COPD had the highest global ASIR, ASMR, and ASDR among the three diseases. Country-level first-place counts differed by metric: COPD had the highest ASIR in 187 countries and territories, IS the highest ASMR in 110, and ICH the highest ASDR in 95. Air pollution accounted for the largest global attributable DALY burden among the shared Level 2 categories, whereas tobacco predominated in high-SDI settings. Exploratory BAPC projections suggested continued ASDR declines through 2050, with IS potentially having the highest projected ASDR, while age-specific burden increasingly shifted toward older populations.

CONCLUSION: Prevention priorities should reflect disease burden and local resources, with sustained attention to tobacco exposure and air pollution. The observed geographical overlap supports population-level planning and motivates individual-level research, but it does not establish COPD-stroke comorbidity, causality, or clinical predictive value.

articles.title: Spatiotemporally coordinated immunometabolic-hyperthermia therapy for diabetic bone defect regeneration.
articles.abstract: Diabetic bone defects (DBDs) are typified by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, and microbial infection within the diabetic microenvironment, which collectively hinder osteogenesis and angiogenesis. Herein, we introduce an Immunometabolic-Hyperthermia Therapy (IMHT) strategy based on a dual-functional nanoplatform, namely a polydopamine/itaconate-incorporated agarose/gelatin (PIAG) hydrogel. This system is fabricated by incorporating itaconic acid (ITA) into polydopamine (PDA) nanoparticles through in situ polymerization, followed by encapsulation within a gelatin/agarose matrix. ITA primarily provides immunometabolic regulation, while PDA enables a tunable photothermal response. Upon localized photothermal heating (∼50 °C), the PIAG hydrogel effectively disrupts bacterial biofilms, with photothermal treatment providing the dominant antibacterial effect and ITA offering an additional supportive contribution. Upon mild photothermal activation (∼41 °C), IMHT mitigates excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, inhibits neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, and reprograms macrophages toward an M2-like reparative phenotype through JAK1/STAT1 pathway inhibition. The resulting pro-regenerative immune milieu enhances fibroblast growth factor-2 (FGF-2) secretion, while heat-induced activation of HSP90 stabilizes FGF-2/FGFR1 signaling, further promoting osteogenic differentiation and endothelial migration. Overall, the spatiotemporally coordinated antibacterial, immunometabolic, and regenerative regulation realized by IMHT offers a comprehensive and effective strategy for the repair of diabetic bone defects.

articles.title: The role of the microbiome in diabetic foot ulcers: Biofilm community dynamics differ with healing outcomes.
articles.abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers often develop into non-healing chronic wounds due to their high risk of infection resulting from exposure to various microbes, combined with a lowered immune response due to the patient's diabetic status. Recently, an increased understanding of the polymicrobial nature of chronic wound infections has given rise to questions on the role of the microbiome on healing outcomes. In our study, we aimed to investigate the microbiome composition and its pathological influence in 128 patients using the Oxford NanoPore Sequencing platform and the 16S rRNA region for sample amplification. Overall, the most abundant genera and species present in the microbiomes of these patients resembled other published studies, namely Cutibacteria, Staphylococcus and Pseudomonas. A key factor in healing outcomes was the presence of fungi, which was strongly correlated with pathogenic anaerobes such as Prevotella bivia and associated with negative outcomes. While we could not determine a direct causal link between fungi and outcomes, the data strongly suggests that fungal presence plays a role in the composition of bacterial communities in the wound environment and is potentially enabling infection persistence. Furthermore, we observed that certain bacterial species were present in all outcomes, but part of different microbial networks, hinting that healing success could be determined by these associations established in the community rather than presence of a specific pathobiont. In conclusion, while an initial look at the composition can provide an insight into the most abundant genus/species present in certain outcomes, when investigating deeper we see that associations among different taxa may play a more significant role in determining healing. We postulate that interfering with these interactions could potentially be the key to tipping the balance towards positive healing outcomes.

articles.title: Emerging concepts in the diagnosis and treatment of fracture-related infections.
articles.journal: OTA international : the open access journal of orthopaedic trauma
articles.abstract: Fracture-related infections (FRIs) remain a significant challenge in orthopaedic trauma, as they are a consistent source of poor patient outcomes and elevated health care costs. FRIs have traditionally been diagnosed using findings from physical examination, blood tests, and advanced imaging, and the mainstay of treatment has been bony debridement, removal of hardware, and local and systemic antibiotic therapy. Although patients with FRIs were historically treated with IV antibiotics, randomized clinical trials have since demonstrated that oral antibiotics can be just as effective while mitigating the risks associated with prolonged IV antibiotics. Emerging biomarkers for infection, including molecular methods such as transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and next-generation sequencing, offer the ability to more precisely identify infection from a wider range of microbes. Fluorescence-guided debridement surgery presents a strategy to better visualize infected tissue and decrease surgeon reliance on subjective intraoperative findings. The purpose of this review is to present emerging tools and treatment algorithms that might be able to increase the accuracy and precision with which FRIs are diagnosed and managed.

articles.title: The Rising Burden of Atrial Fibrillation and Respiratory Failure Mortality in the United States: A 25-Year Nationwide Retrospective Analysis of Death Certificate Data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) and respiratory failure (RF) frequently co-occur in critically ill patients, but long-term national trends in deaths recording both remain unknown.

METHODS: CDC WONDER multiple-cause-of-death data identified U.S. adults aged ≥ 55 years with both AF (including atrial flutter) and RF listed on death certificates from 1999 to 2024. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) and annual percent changes (APCs) were estimated using joinpoint regression. Sensitivity analyses included adults aged ≥ 25 years, exclusion of COVID-19-related deaths, and stratification by co-listed heart failure (HF).

RESULTS: A total of 462 284 deaths listed both AF and RF. The AAMR increased roughly five-fold (7.84 to 41.76 per 100 000), rising steadily through 2018 (APC 7.81), accelerating through 2021 (APC 18.78), and declining thereafter (APC -5.90). Excluding deaths listing COVID-19, the 2018-2021 acceleration was not detected, and AAMRs rose through 2024 (2017-2024 APC 5.25). AAMRs for deaths without HF recorded rose over fourfold. Mean AAMRs were higher in males (26.19) than in females (19.04) and in non-Hispanic (NH) White adults (24.06) than in other groups. The West and nonmetropolitan areas had the highest rates. The 2018-2021 surge was steepest among Hispanic (APC 25.62) and NH Black adults (APC 24.06).

CONCLUSIONS: Population mortality rates for deaths recording both AF and RF increased substantially over 25 years, beginning before the COVID-19 pandemic, persisting after excluding deaths listing COVID-19, and occurring with and without HF recorded. These data cannot separate changes in disease occurrence from changes in diagnosis or coding.

articles.title: Posterior Pulmonary Vein Isolation Lesion Spacing and Left Atrial Posterior Wall Narrowing During Pulsed Field Ablation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial posterior wall (LAPW) narrowing after excessive extension of bilateral pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) lines during pulsed field ablation (PFA) may create a proarrhythmic substrate. The CARTO 3-integrated variable-loop circular catheter (VLCC) provides real-time tissue proximity indication (TPI) and ablation-tag location, but their relationship with LAPW narrowing remains unclear. Therefore, we evaluated associations of TPI status and inter-tag distance (ITD) with acute LAPW narrowing and whether an ITD-guided workflow was associated with LAPW preservation.

METHODS: Fifty-two retrospective and 27 prospective atrial fibrillation patients underwent PFA using a VLCC. In the retrospective phase, we evaluated the association between ITD, measured using TPI-positive tags and all tags, and LAPW narrowing (< 10 mm) and derived a cutoff. In the prospective phase, the ITD-guided workflow was applied, and we assessed residual LAPW band width.

RESULTS: In the retrospective phase, both TPI-positive-tag ITD and all-tag ITD correlated with LAPW band width (r = 0.63 and 0.70, respectively; both p < 0.001). All-tag ITD showed a numerically higher AUC for LAPW narrowing than TPI-positive-tag ITD (0.869 vs. 0.795; p = 0.099), with an optimal all-tag ITD cutoff of 16.5 mm. In the prospective phase incorporating the all-tag ITD cutoff, residual LAPW band widths were wider at the roof (19.4 ± 7.9 vs. 25.1 ± 7.1 mm; p = 0.002) and carina (13.6 ± 7.1 vs. 20.8 ± 8.0 mm; p < 0.001) than in the retrospective phase.

CONCLUSIONS: An all-tag ITD-guided workflow was associated with greater preservation of the residual LAPW band width.

articles.title: Association between neuromuscular electrical stimulation and intermittent pneumatic compression for the prevention of deep venous thrombosis among neurosurgery patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) considerably affects the incidence and mortality rates in patients undergoing neurosurgery. Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) and intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) are frequently used as adjunct treatments to prevent DVT; however, their effects remain unclear. This study was conducted to compare the association of NMES and IPC as two mechanical prophylaxis strategies in neurosurgical patients who were ineligible for pharmacological prophylaxis.

METHODS: Postoperative neurosurgical patients were retrospectively enrolled from a single centre between January 2020 and December 2021. These patients were assessed to have a high bleeding risk and received either NMES or IPC as mechanical prophylaxis. Univariable analysis was used to explore the risk factors for DVT, and multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to determine the independent associations between DVT and potential variables after adjusting for confounding factors.

RESULTS: Among 232 patients who underwent neurosurgery, 131 received IPC and 101 received NMES, with no overlap between the two groups. DVT was diagnosed in 62 patients (11 received NMES and 51 received IPC). After controlling for sex, age, operation duration and length of hospital stay, NMES use was associated with a lower incidence of DVT (OR = 0.268, 95% CI = 0.125-0.576, p = .001). Moreover, men were less likely to have DVT than women (OR = 0.469, 95% CI = 0.242-0.910, p = .025), older age was associated with higher odds of DVT (OR = 3.419, 95% CI = 1.594-7.334, p = .002), and a longer operation duration was associated with higher odds of DVT (OR = 2.180, 95% CI = 1.042-4.560, p = .039).

CONCLUSION: This study found an association between NMES and reduced odds of DVT compared with IPC in neurosurgery patients. Although NMES may be more widely adopted in neurosurgery to decrease the incidence of DVT, further evidence is required to determine its effectiveness in clinical practice.

articles.title: Identification of ageing-related genes in prostate cancer with type 2 Diabetes using machine learning: a multi-omics study focusing on SOX4, PRNP, and FOXO4.
articles.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) demonstrates complex associations with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and ageing, though their interconnected molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. This study aimed to identify and validate diagnostic biomarkers at the intersection of these pathways to enable early detection and risk stratification in high-risk populations. Bioinformatic analysis was performed on PCa and T2DM transcriptomic data downloaded from the GEO database, followed by differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and functional enrichment. Eight machine learning algorithms were applied to identify hub ageing-related genes (ARGs), with SHAP analysis interpreting feature importance. A nomogram model was constructed and validated across multiple cohorts. Immune infiltration, drug sensitivity, single-cell RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomics were used for mechanistic exploration. Three key ARGs (SOX4, PRNP, and FOXO4) were identified and used to develop a diagnostic model with high accuracy (AUCs: 0.726-0.905). SOX4 promoted immune evasion, PRNP exhibited context-dependent duality, and FOXO4 functioned as a tumor suppressor. Spatial and single-cell analyses revealed cell-type-specific expression and fibroblast-epithelial communication via MIF, LRP1, and FZD1. Drug sensitivity profiling identified abiraterone and docetaxel as potential therapeutics for high- and low-risk patients, respectively. In conclusion, SOX4, PRNP, and FOXO4 are key biomarkers linking PCa, T2DM, and ageing, and the diagnostic model shows robust performance and clinical utility, providing insights into microenvironment-driven mechanisms and personalized treatment strategies for PCa patients with T2DM.

articles.title: Efficacy of a Gamified Training Program for Improving Occupational Health and Safety Knowledge Among Italian Secondary School Students: A Randomized Controlled Field Trial.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated the short-term effectiveness of an innovative gamified educational program based on the principles of the Italian Legislative Decree 81/2008 in improving occupational health and safety (OHS) knowledge among Italian secondary school students. A cluster-randomized controlled field trial was conducted in Italy from September 2024 to June 2025. Classes were randomized into experimental (EG) and control groups (CG). The intervention combined a seminar with three structured games (role-playing, board, and card games). Knowledge was assessed using a 15-item questionnaire (Q81) at baseline (T0) and post-intervention (T1). The primary endpoint was the between-group difference in Q81 score at post-intervention (T1). Of 930 eligible students, 927 participated (99.7%), 694 completed the study (74.6%), including 187 middle school and 507 high school students (NEG = 356; NCG = 338). Baseline Q81 scores were comparable between groups (EG: 5.6 ± 3.3 vs CG: 5.4 ± 2.9), whereas at T1, mean Q81 scores were significantly higher in the EG compared to the CG (9.0 ± 3.1 vs. 5.2 ± 2.9, P < 0.001; Cohen's d = 1.26). Within-group analysis showed a significant improvement in the EG (P < 0.001), but not in the CG. Reliability analysis yielded alpha = 0.804, indicating good internal consistency. Gamification training improved OHS knowledge among secondary school students and may represent an effective educational strategy for early safety education. These findings support the integration of gamified OHS training into secondary school curricula to strengthen early safety education in line with the principles of Legislative Decree 81/2008. . Future studies should include larger samples, address item-level weaknesses and explore long-term behavioural outcomes.

articles.title: Association of third-trimester maternal lipid levels with adverse pregnancy outcomes in women with gestational diabetes mellitus: a retrospective single-center study using intrapartum data.
articles.journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study investigates the relationships between maternal factors and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), as well as third‑trimester maternal lipids and adverse pregnancy outcomes among GDM patients.

METHODS: This study enrolled 3,973 pregnant women, divided into a control group (n = 3166) and a GDM group (n = 807). The GDM group was further divided into well-controlled (n = 152) and poorly controlled subgroups (n = 655). Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to evaluate factors associated with GDM risk. Baseline clinical/laboratory characteristics were compared across groups via parametric, nonparametric, and chi‑square tests to assess associations of third‑trimester maternal lipid levels with adverse pregnancy outcomes. Receiver operating characteristic analyses evaluated the predictive values of body mass index (BMI) and third‑trimester maternal lipid levels.

RESULTS: Age (OR = 1.069, 95% CI:1.050-1.087, p < .001), overweight (OR = 1.678 95% CI:1.396-2.013, p < .001), and obesity (OR = 2.018, 95% CI:1.511-2.677, p < .001) are key risk factors for GDM. Significant differences existed in age (p = .001), BMI (p < .001), fasting blood glucose (FBG, p < .001) and 2-hour postprandial plasma glucose (2hPPG, p = .001) across subgroups, as well as triglycerides (TG, p < .001), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C, p = .001), and free fatty acids (FFAs, p < .001) among the three groups. Subgroup analysis by lipid levels showed TG predominantly affected delivery mode (p = .031), neonatal birth weight (p = .005), and quantitative blood loss (QBL, p = .019) in GDM, while HDL-C mainly influenced fetal growth curve (p = .004) and neonatal birth weight (p = .002). Subgroup analysis by triglyceride-glucose index (TyG index) revealed significant differences in glycemic control (p = .002), delivery mode (p = .002), neonatal weight (p = .005), and QBL (p = .005). The area under the curve of pre-pregnancy BMI for GDM complicated by hypertensive disorders of pregnancy was 0.738, third-trimester BMI 0.720, and 0.709 for macrosomia prediction in non-advanced-age women with GDM.

CONCLUSION: Age, overweight, and obesity are independent risk factors for GDM. Among women with GDM, third-trimester lipid levels are associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes. Therefore, lipid levels should be considered in GDM clinical management, rather than focusing exclusively on glycemic control.

articles.title: Predicting 12- and 24-month documented CKD progression from routine laboratory data: a single-center temporal evaluation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Routine laboratory data may support CKD follow-up. We evaluated 12- and 24-month documented progression prediction and exploratory review outputs.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study used 2012-2025 hospital records. CKD required objective persistence for ≥90 days. Development used 2012-2021 indices; temporal evaluation used unseen patients indexed in 2022-2023. Among horizon-evaluable indices, the endpoint was documented sustained ≥40% estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline or kidney failure. Development selected 12-month and conditional second-year models combined for non-decreasing cumulative risk. Laboratory and documentation outputs were assessed separately.

RESULTS: Temporal evaluation of horizon-evaluable patients included 143 patients (10 event patients; 21/364 positive indices) at 12 months and 87 patients (22 event patients; 50/247 positive indices) at 24 months. Area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) was 0.510 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.217-0.789) and 0.677 (0.459-0.853), respectively. Incremental 12-month AUPRC over age, sex and current eGFR was uncertain (difference -0.009, 95% CI -0.171 to 0.123). At 24 months, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was higher than the core comparator (difference 0.057, 95% CI 0.007-0.121); clinical utility was not evaluated. Calibration slopes were 0.996 (0.689-1.640) and 1.028 (0.676-1.661); wide CIs precluded reliable individual-risk calibration. Documentation ranking did not improve on prior-mention strategies.

CONCLUSIONS: This study is proof of concept. Small event counts, follow-up selection and uncertain incremental value limit interpretation. Multisite validation is required before implementation.

articles.title: Assessing Access to Neurologists Using a Secret Shopper Survey in California and Pennsylvania.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Adequate provider networks and accurate provider directories are crucial to ensure access to medical care in managed care. Existing research suggests substantial barriers. These barriers have not been assessed for neurologic care and only in a limited way for the Affordable Care Act market. We sought to assess access to neurologic care in California and Pennsylvania.

METHODS: We conducted a simulated patient survey in which trained callers posed as patients seeking care on behalf of 1,085 simulated patients (4,328 calls) from May to November 2022 during initial implementation of the No Surprises Act directory accuracy provisions. When an appointment was successfully scheduled, callers recorded the appointment date. We also calculated the driving time. For unsuccessful contact attempts, callers recorded provider directory inaccuracies, provider capacity limitations, staff refusal to provide information, or failure to reach anyone capable of verifying information.

RESULTS: Only 2,316 of 4,328 calls (53.5%) reached a person capable of verifying provider information. Considering all 4,328 call attempts, including those that could not be verified, 15.7% resulted in a successfully scheduled appointment. Among verified calls, 29.3% successfully secured a nonemergency appointment, with substantial variation by state (California 37.4% vs Pennsylvania 21.6%), plan type (HMO 34.6% vs EPO 17.7%), insurer tax status (not-for-profit 41.7% vs for-profit 17.6%), and market presence (multistate 37.4% vs single state 18.5%). The mean wait time to appointment was 70.9 days overall and 103.4 days in Pennsylvania. The mean driving time was 32.9 minutes and nearly doubled for rural patients (55.3 vs 27.8 minutes). Provider directory inaccuracies were encountered in 58.2% of verified calls, most commonly incorrect contact information (35.3%), with higher rates in Pennsylvania than California (68.5% vs 49.3%) and for EPOs than HMOs (71.9% vs 51.3%). An additional 7.8% of calls encountered provider capacity limitations.

DISCUSSION: Practicing neurologists bear downstream costs from directory errors through misdirected calls. Referring clinicians should be aware that marketplace enrollees may face substantial delays in accessing neurology care. Current regulatory regimes may not fully protect patients. Differences across states as well as plan and insurer type suggest systematic variation in access. Rural patients face particular obstacles.

articles.title: 177 Lu-PSMA Therapy in Recurrent High-Grade Glioma : A Pilot Study With Dosimetric Insights.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Patients with recurrent high-grade glioma have poor prognosis and limited treatment options. This pilot study evaluated the feasibility and potential clinical benefit of 177 Lu-PSMA therapy in this patient population.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Eligible patients were selected for treatment based on positive 68 Ga-PSMA-PET findings. 177 Lu-PSMA (7.4 GBq/200 mCi) was administered at 6-8-week intervals and continued as long as well-tolerated. The safety, tolerability, and efficacy of 177 Lu-PSMA were assessed in each treatment cycle using PET/MRI, SPECT/CT, blood tests, neurological tests, and patient-reported outcome measures.

RESULTS: Ten patients were enrolled (WHO grade 4 glioblastoma, n=6; WHO grade 4 astrocytoma, n=1; WHO grade 3 astrocytoma, n=3). 68 Ga-PSMA-PET before treatment demonstrated tumor uptake in 9 patients (median SUV max : 6.4, IQR: 4.2-9.0). Six patients received treatment (20 cycles total; range: 1-7 per patient). Median absorbed dose per cycle was 0.9 Gy (IQR: 0.8-1.1) for tumors, 2.6 Gy (IQR: 1.9-3.2) for kidneys, and 1.7 Gy (IQR: 1.5-2.2) for parotid glands. No CTCAE grade 3-4 toxicities occurred. The most common patient-reported symptoms were fatigue, transient xerostomia, and nausea. Median survival from treatment initiation was 187 days (range: 87-756) and the median progression-free survival was 45 days (range: 41-335). MRI (RANO 2.0) demonstrated stable disease in half of the patients during all or part of the treatment course.

CONCLUSIONS: 177 Lu-PSMA therapy was feasible and well-tolerated. Radiologic stabilization was observed in a subset of patients, but strategies to increase tumor dose delivery may be needed to improve efficacy.

articles.title: Environmental and psychosocial factors in hypertension: an emerging landscape of cardiovascular risk.
articles.abstract: Environmental and psychosocial factors are increasingly recognised as important contributors to the development, progression, and control of hypertension (HTN) and cardiovascular (CV) disease. Within the exposome framework, these exposures converge on shared neuroendocrine, oxidative, and inflammatory pathways leading to endothelial dysfunction and blood pressure (BP) elevation. Among environmental pollutants, air pollution, particularly fine particulate matter (PM2.5), is a major modifiable risk factor; each 10 µg/m³ increase in PM2.5 is associated with a 4% rise in HTN prevalence. Transportation noise increases HTN risk through stress-related neurohormonal activation, oxidative stress, and sleep disruption. Artificial light at night and heavy metals are additional contributors, whereas micro- and nanoplastics remain an emerging concern awaiting robust human data. Physical and climatic stressors also influence BP regulation. Both heat and cold are associated with increased CV morbidity and mortality, with cold exerting the greater impact, and hypobaric hypoxia at high altitude activates sympathetic and neurohormonal pathways that promote BP elevation, particularly in hypertensive individuals. Among psychosocial and behavioural factors, sleep disturbances are associated with incident and resistant HTN. Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is an underrecognized determinant of HTN, especially among refugees, migrants, war veterans, and other trauma-exposed populations, through chronic sympathetic activation, inflammation, and adverse behavioural pathways. Finally, spaceflight provides a unique model of extreme environmental stress, inducing CV adaptations ranging from transient BP dysregulation and orthostatic intolerance to vascular remodelling resembling accelerated CV ageing. Recognising these determinants is essential to improve HTN prevention, optimise BP control, and reduce long-term CV risk.

articles.title: Impact of artificial intelligence-assisted health management on blood pressure and self-management efficacy in older adults with hypertension.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This paper examined the impacts of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted health management on blood pressure control and self-management effectiveness in older adults with hypertension.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Two hundred hypertensive patients were randomly assigned to a usual care group (routine health management) or an intervention group (AI-assisted health management, including aspects such as intelligent monitoring, early warning and proactive intervention, among others) (n = 100 each). Primary outcomes included blood pressure control rate (<140/<90 mm Hg) and systolic and diastolic blood pressure (SBP and DBP). Secondary outcomes included improvement in lifestyle behaviours, level of hypertension knowledge awareness, self-management efficacy, medication beliefs, quality of life, and management satisfaction.
