On multivariable analysis, GA grade IIIA (odds ratio [OR]: 36.2; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 4.21-90; P = 0.013), postoperative infection (OR: 20.2; 95% CI: 2.15-189; P = 0.023), and surgical delay beyond 48 hours (OR: 16.5; 95% CI: 1.88-144; P = 0.009) were independently associated with nonunion.

CONCLUSIONS: Primary SIGN IMN yielded a high union rate for GA I to IIIA open tibial shaft fractures in this low- and middle-income countries setting. GA grade, postoperative infection, and delay to surgery were the principal barriers to union. These findings support early surgical intervention and rigorous infection control in resource-limited settings.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Prognostic Level IV.

articles.title: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor-associated euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis in an adolescent with type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Youth-onset type 2 diabetes (T2D) is increasing, prompting expanded use of pharmacotherapies previously approved only for adults. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, approved for pediatric use in 2023, improve glycemic control by promoting glucosuria, but they carry a known risk of euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) in adults. We describe a unique pediatric case of SGLT2 inhibitor-associated euglycemic DKA in a 12-year-old female with T2D. The patient developed DKA with normal glucose shortly after initiating an SGLT2 inhibitor, leading to diagnostic uncertainty and recognition only after exclusion of more common etiologies. She was successfully treated with intravenous insulin and fluids with resolution of DKA and subsequently transitioned to subcutaneous insulin therapy. This case underscores that euglycemic DKA can occur in youth receiving SGLT2 inhibitors, particularly during puberty when physiologic insulin resistance may heighten risk, and that subtle presentations can complicate early recognition if clinicians rely on hyperglycemia alone. As SGLT2 inhibitors enter broader pediatric use, heightened diagnostic vigilance, guided assessment of ketones and acid-base status in symptomatic patients, and patient and family education are essential to ensure safe use in children and adolescents with T2D.

articles.title: Severe insulin-requiring diabetes in a noradrenergic giant pheochromocytoma: a secretory-metabolic phenotype paradox.
articles.abstract: Pheochromocytoma is a rare catecholamine-secreting neuroendocrine tumor associated with hypertension and dysglycemia in 20% to 40% of cases. Insulin-requiring diabetes has been reported in tumors with an adrenergic profile, owing to epinephrine-mediated inhibition of β-cell secretion. A 37-year-old man with a normal body mass index and an 18-year history of insulin-requiring diabetes and hypertension was found to have a right adrenal mass measuring 10.1 × 8.0 × 6.7 cm. Biochemical evaluation showed a noradrenergic profile, with urinary normetanephrine greater than 5000 μg/24 hours (SI: >26 400 nmol/day; reference range, 70-538 μg/24 hours [SI: 370-2841 nmol/day]) and normal urinary metanephrine. Right adrenalectomy and histopathology confirmed an intra-adrenal pheochromocytoma. After surgery, insulin was discontinued, and glycated hemoglobin remained below 6.1% (SI: 41-43 mmol/mol) without therapy. A preoperative insulin requirement of 0.83 units/kg/day, normal C-peptide, and negative glutamic acid decarboxylase antibodies supported a mixed and reversible mechanism involving catecholamine-induced insulin resistance and β-cell suppression. Severe postoperative hypoglycemia was attributed to reversal of catecholamine excess. This case challenges the association of severe diabetes with adrenergic pheochromocytomas and suggests that catecholamine burden and exposure duration may be more important determinants of metabolic severity than secretory profile alone, after prolonged exposure to high catecholamine concentrations.

articles.title: Persistent atherogenic lipoprotein changes during lorlatinib therapy.
articles.abstract: Lorlatinib, a third-generation anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)/ROS1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor, frequently induces hypercholesterolemia and hypertriglyceridemia, but longitudinal qualitative lipoprotein changes remain incompletely characterized. We describe a 52-year-old woman with ALK-rearranged non-small cell lung cancer who developed persistent dyslipidemia despite lipid-lowering therapy. Before lorlatinib, total cholesterol was 164 mg/dL (SI [International System of Units]: 4.24 mmol/L) (reference range, 148-248 mg/dL [SI: 3.83-6.41 mmol/L]), low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol was 52 mg/dL (SI: 1.34 mmol/L) (reference range, 65-139 mg/dL [SI: 1.68-3.59 mmol/L]), and triglycerides were 54 mg/dL (SI: 0.61 mmol/L) (reference range, 30-117 mg/dL [SI: 0.34-1.32 mmol/L]). Within 3 weeks after lorlatinib initiation, these increased to 340, 245, and 166 mg/dL, respectively. Longitudinal profiling showed persistent apolipoprotein B (ApoB) elevation, increased oxidized LDL, and a prominent pre-β-lipoprotein fraction. Subclinical hypothyroidism was later detected, and pitavastatin was switched to rosuvastatin. This case highlights the potential value of ApoB and qualitative lipid assessment during prolonged lorlatinib therapy.

articles.title: Post-traumatic stress disorder with comorbid obstructive sleep apnea after the Great East Japan Earthquake: A case report.
articles.journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is frequently accompanied by sleep disturbance, and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is an important potential comorbidity. Although PTSD-OSA coexistence has been reported mainly in military veterans, reports after natural disasters remain limited. We describe a patient who developed PTSD after the Great East Japan Earthquake (GEJE) and was subsequently diagnosed with severe OSA.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 55-year-old man with hypertension and dyslipidemia, but no prior psychiatric illness, experienced temporary burial under rubble during the GEJE. He subsequently developed persistent trauma-related nightmares, depressed mood, and panic responses to disaster-related cues and was diagnosed with PTSD. Paroxetine and alprazolam improved mood and panic symptoms, whereas nightmares, excessive daytime sleepiness, and impaired concentration persisted. Polysomnography later demonstrated severe OSA (apnea-hypopnea index, 41.6 events/h; rapid eye movement (REM) AHI, 47.6 events/h; minimum oxygen saturation, 79%). Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) was initiated without changes to psychiatric treatment. Daytime sleepiness improved, and nightmare frequency decreased from almost daily to approximately weekly during the period of CPAP treatment, although adherence was low and symptoms later recurred after treatment interruption.

CONCLUSION: This case illustrates that persistent nightmares, sleepiness, and impaired daytime functioning in a patient with PTSD may coexist with clinically significant OSA. Because longitudinal standardized PTSD measures were unavailable and CPAP adherence was limited, the observed improvement cannot be attributed to CPAP alone. Systematic assessment for sleep disorders, including OSA, should be considered when sleep-related or daytime symptoms persist during psychiatric treatment.

articles.title: Continuous caloric restriction and diet replacement but not alternate-day fasting may enhance susceptibility to glucose intolerance, dyslipidemia and cell stress under renewed high-fat diet.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Weight regain affects most individuals attempting to treat obesity and its comorbidities, and it is associated with increased risk of metabolic and cardiovascular diseases. Several strategies have been proposed to induce weight loss, including caloric restriction (CCR), diet replacement (DR) and alternate-day fasting (ADF).

AIM: To compare these approaches in terms of weight maintenance and metabolic, oxidative, and inflammatory outcomes.

METHODS: Male Wistar rats underwent a three-phase protocol. First, animals received a high-fat diet (HFD) for eight weeks to induce obesity. Second, they were divided into four groups: ad lib-HFD (continued HFD), R-HFD (30% reduction of HFD w/w), ADF-HFD (24 h fasting alternating with 24 h ad libitum HFD), and ad lib-LFD (DR via ad libitum access to low-fat chow) for six weeks. Finally, all groups returned to free access to HFD for four weeks.

RESULTS: All interventions delayed weight gain; however, discontinuation led to rapid weight regain. Under renewed HFD ad libitum exposure, CCR and DR induced higher susceptibility to dyslipidemia, as shown by the temporal analysis. These strategies also impaired hepatic and adipose antioxidant and anti-inflammatory responses and heightened lymph node stress upon return to unlimited offer of obesogenic diet. In contrast, ADF appeared to confer partial protection against the metabolic complications of weight rebound.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite similar weight-loss efficacy, ADF may better preserve metabolic homeostasis during weight regain.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40200-026-02112-1.

articles.title: Role of intestinal microbiota in pathogenesis and perspective therapeutics events for diabetes mellitus: A narrative review.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Diabetes mellitus is a widespread metabolic condition characterized by persistent high blood sugar, contributing significantly to global disease burden. Recent studies have turned attention to the intestinal microbiome as a critical factor influencing metabolic health and glucose control. Disruptions in normal microbial ecosystem, referred to as dysbiosis, are now linked to the development and worsening of diabetes. Gut bacteria and their metabolic outputs affect host energy use, immune responses, inflammation, digestive efficiency, and even genetic activity.

METHODS: A comprehensive search was performed in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar using relevant keywords such as "gut microbiota," "dysbiosis," "short-chain fatty acids," "bile acids," "probiotics," and both type 1 and type 2 diabetes (T1D, T2D), along with diabetic complications.

RESULTS: Evidence indicates that an increased Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio is commonly observed in T1D patients, underscoring the significance of microbial imbalance. In T2D, positive associations have been reported with genera such as Blautia and Ruminococcus, while genera like Bacteroides, Bifidobacterium, Faecalibacterium, and Roseburia show negative correlations. However, these findings are predominantly derived from cross-sectional studies, and definitive causal relationships remain to be established.

CONCLUSION: Elucidating the relationship between gut microbiota and diabetes not only clarifies the role of dysbiosis in metabolic disease and opens avenues for novel therapeutic strategies. Modulating the microbiome may improve insulin sensitivity and glycemic control. Future research could pave the way for innovative diagnostic tools, clinical assays, and treatment designed to alleviate diabetic symptoms. Nevertheless, translation of these findings into clinical practice requires further rigorous investigation.

articles.title: Effectiveness of outpatient financing reform from health savings accounts to pooling scheme in China: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Outpatient services are fundamental to safeguarding population health and promoting the efficient use of healthcare resources. However, China has long faced limited risk pooling and inadequate financial protection for outpatient services. In 2021, China launched a nationwide outpatient financing reform to address these limitations. This study examines the effectiveness of this reform, which shifted outpatient financing from individual health savings accounts (HSAs) to an outpatient pooling scheme. A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, and Chinese National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) was conducted for studies published between 1998 and December 2025. A total of 21 studies were included in this review. Overall, the reform was generally associated with increased outpatient utilization. Several studies suggested substitution between outpatient and inpatient care, whereas others indicated complementary effects. Findings on medical expenditure and out-of-pocket spending were mixed, while limited evidence suggested increased primary healthcare utilization and improved health-related behaviors. Overall, the effects varied across outcomes and policy settings, highlighting the importance of policy design and local healthcare contexts.

articles.title: Balloon-occluded ethylene vinyl alcohol copolymer embolization of a hemorrhagic renal mass in an octogenarian initially unfit for nephrectomy.
articles.abstract: Palliative transarterial embolization is an established option for symptomatic renal tumors in patients who are poor surgical candidates, but conventional particle or coil techniques sacrifice uninvolved parenchyma and permit reflux-related non-target embolization. We report an 89-year-old man with atrial fibrillation, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease who presented with one month of gross hematuria, transfusion-requiring anemia, and acute kidney injury secondary to a 5.8 × 4.6 × 3.4 cm hypervascular right upper-pole renal mass extending into the collecting system. Deemed unfit for nephrectomy during the index admission, he underwent super-selective balloon-occluded embolization with ethylene vinyl alcohol copolymer delivered through a balloon-occlusion microcatheter. Hematuria resolved, hemoglobin stabilized without further transfusion, and creatinine returned to near baseline by post-procedure day 2. He remained free of hematuria for approximately 12 weeks despite resumption of apixaban. Recurrent intermittent bleeding from a persistent enhancing collecting-system component prompted readmission; surveillance imaging demonstrated a devascularized cortical tumor bed with an approximately 69% reduction in tumor volume and preserved parenchymal enhancement of the treated kidney. After interval stabilization, he underwent elective robotic nephrectomy with minimal blood loss. Pathology demonstrated clear cell renal cell carcinoma (grade 3, stage pT3a) with 50% tumor necrosis and post-embolization changes; urothelial carcinoma was excluded. Balloon-occluded ethylene vinyl alcohol copolymer embolization may provide effective temporizing hemostasis and histologically confirmed tumor devascularization in nonsurgical patients, serving in this case as a bridge to elective nephrectomy.

articles.title: Urologically silent intravesical migration of a copper intrauterine device presenting as chronic pelvic pain: CT features and comparison with reported cases.
articles.abstract: Uterine perforation with migration of an intrauterine device (IUD) into the urinary bladder is a well-documented complication that usually presents with lower urinary tract symptoms, recurrent urinary tract infection, hematuria, or a secondary bladder calculus. We report a 35-year-old woman (G2P2) with a copper IUD inserted 5 years earlier who presented with progressive chronic pelvic pain and no urinary symptoms. Pelvic ultrasound showed an abnormally positioned device, and contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) demonstrated a T-shaped device of metallic density traversing the anterior uterine wall, with one arm protruding into the bladder dome and coated by a small encrustation. The fixed, non-dependent position of the linear metallic core, its continuity with the myometrium, and its T-shaped morphology distinguished the device from a primary bladder calculus. Cystoscopy confirmed partial intravesical protrusion of the encrusted arm, which was extracted intact with forceps without complication, and the patient was asymptomatic at follow-up. Compared with published intravesical cases, in which urinary complaints or a bladder stone usually prompt investigation, this case shows that bladder involvement may remain silent from a urinary perspective. In IUD users with unexplained pelvic pain, imaging should specifically assess the bladder, and a delayed excretory CT phase is advisable to evaluate bladder-wall integrity before removal.

articles.title: Impact of wildfire smoke waves on the association between long-term exposure to fine particulate matter and cardiovascular hospitalizations among older adults in the United States.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is a risk factor for cardiovascular disease (CVD), even at concentrations below U.S. air quality standards. The frequency and severity of wildfires are increasing, causing episodic PM2.5 spikes. Our study examined whether associations between long-term exposure to PM2.5 and cardiovascular hospitalizations differed in the presence and absence of wildfire smoke waves.

METHODS: We conducted a cohort study of 65.2 million U.S. Medicare beneficiaries aged ≥ 65 years across the contiguous U.S. during 2017-2022. Daily total and wildfire smoke PM2.5 concentrations were estimated at 1 km and 10 km spatial resolutions, respectively, using validated machine learning models that incorporated satellite, meteorological, emission, and land-use data. Exposure estimates were aggregated to beneficiaries' residential ZIP codes by population-weighted averaging. Wildfire smoke waves were defined as ≥ 2 consecutive days with daily smoke PM2.5 > 10 μg/m3. We applied quasi-Poisson regressions to estimate relative risks (RR) of first hospitalizations for overall CVD, ischemic heart disease, cerebrovascular disease, and hypertension in ZIP-years with and without smoke waves.

RESULTS: In the full cohort, an increase in two-year average PM2.5 from 5 μg/m3 (WHO annual air quality guideline) to 9 μg/m3 (current U.S. annual PM2.5 standard) was associated with increased risks of overall CVD, cerebrovascular, and hypertension hospitalizations, with stronger associations in ZIP-years without smoke waves than in those with smoke waves (overall CVD: RR 1.09, 95% CI 1.09-1.10 vs. RR 1.04, 95% CI 1.03-1.04; ratio of RR 1.05, 95% CI 1.04-1.06). Similar patterns were observed among beneficiaries residing in ZIP codes with annual PM2.5 concentrations below 9 μg/m3 throughout the study period. Smoke wave-related differences in PM2.5-CVD associations were greater among males, urban residents, and residents in the western region compared with their counterparts.

CONCLUSIONS: The association between long-term PM2.5 exposure and cardiovascular hospitalizations differed by wildfire smoke wave occurrence. These findings suggest that long-term average PM2.5 may not fully capture episodic high-intensity exposures and may underestimate the cardiovascular morbidity burden in smoke-affected areas, highlighting the need for risk assessments accounting for exposure patterns.

articles.title: Evaluation of carvacrol and quercetin against surgical site infection pathogen Escherichia coli: In silico target identification, anti-biofilm efficacy, and cellular safety.
articles.abstract: Surgical site infections (SSIs) are postoperative complications driven by biofilm development on surgical wounds or implanted medical equipment. SSIs create a risk in terms of morbidity, extended hospitalization, and in extreme cases may cause mortality. The multi-drug-resistant bacteria, which frequently exist as poly-microbial communities in biofilms, present multiple tolerance mechanisms that render SSIs extremely difficult to treat with standard antibiotics. Besides, biofilm development relies on genes/proteins which act as master regulators governing biofilm assembly. Thus, targeting these regulatory switches can effectively curb biofilm development. Phytochemicals have come up as a likely option that can be effective against biofilm-forming multi drug-resistant bacteria by interacting with biofilm forming master regulators. In this study, in silico approaches were implemented to compare the interacting efficiency of different phytochemicals on a master biofilm regulator protein in Escherichia coli (E. coli), a common SSI pathogen. Validation of the most potent phytochemicals after analyzing the in silico results were carried out under in vitro settings to confirm their antibacterial and antibiofilm potential against biofilm-forming bacteria. Furthermore, in vitro safety assessments on human embryonic kidney cells (HEK-293) demonstrated minimal cytotoxicity, confirming the bio-compatibility of the phytochemicals at the therapeutic concentrations. Thus, targeting central biofilm regulators with non-toxic phytochemicals may to reduce the incidence of biofilm associated infections in post-surgery patients.

articles.title: Infectious diseases in Italian amphibians and reptiles: state of the art and systematic review.
articles.journal: International journal for parasitology. Parasites and wildlife
articles.abstract: Infectious diseases are an important conservation concern for amphibians and reptiles, but evidence from free-ranging Italian herpetofauna has never been synthesised at national scale, despite the country's highly diverse herpetofauna, which includes numerous endemic and threatened taxa. We systematically reviewed primary studies on infectious agents in wild amphibians and non-marine reptiles in Italy, distinguishing host-level infectious disease from pathogen occurrence without documented disease and from targeted investigations with no evidence of detection. Searches of PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science, supplemented by Google Scholar and reference-list screening, identified 49 eligible studies published between August 2003 and July 2026: 39 on amphibians and 10 on reptiles, yielding 434 epidemiological records across 52 analytical host taxa and 16 pathogen entities. Of 84 investigated host-pathogen combinations, 21 included disease evidence, 14 positive occurrence only and 49 exclusively negative investigations. After reconciliation of overlapping records, 57 disease-evidence strata were identified: 23 confirmed, 21 presumptive and 13 suspected. Research effort was strongly concentrated: Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis accounted for 203 records from 25 studies and Ophidiomyces ophidiicola for 151 records from five studies, together representing 81.6% of all extracted records. Pathogens were detected in 16 of the 20 Italian regions, whereas disease evidence was available for eight. Of the 15 pathogen entities retained in the European eligibility framework, nine had been investigated in Italy; six had disease evidence, three were represented only by negative investigations, and six had no eligible Italian record. Overall methodological support was rated High for 44 of 49 studies. Infectious diseases are documented across multiple Italian amphibian and reptile taxa, but marked differences in research effort, host coverage and geographic representation prevent reliable estimates of disease frequency or its impact on free-ranging populations at national scale. Further work should prioritise epidemiologically relevant gaps and combine pathogen detection with clinical, pathological and longitudinal population-level evidence.

articles.title: Determinants of healthy dietary patterns among Iranian adults with type 2 diabetes: evidence from the stepwise approach to noncommunicable risk factor surveillance (STEPS 2021).
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Dietary behavior plays a critical role in the prevention and management of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Identifying factors associated with dietary patterns in individuals with T2DM may help improve DM management strategies and reduce the risk of long-term complications.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included adults aged ≥ 25 years with T2DM from the nationally representative 2021 Iranian STEPwise Approach to Noncommunicable Disease Risk Factor Surveillance (STEPS) survey. Dietary patterns were derived using principal component analysis of 15 dietary variables and categorized as healthy or unhealthy. Socioeconomic, lifestyle, clinical, and nutrition literacy factors were assessed as factors associated with dietary patterns. Multivariable logistic regression was applied to identify factors independently associated with a healthy dietary pattern.

RESULTS: Among 2,967 adults with T2DM, 56.7% had a healthy dietary pattern. Healthy dietary patterns were more common among participants with urban residence, higher educational attainment, higher wealth status, health insurance coverage, and who reported greater attention to Nutrition Facts labeling (all p < 0.05). In multivariable analysis, ≥ 12 years of education (OR = 1.53, 95% CI: 1.23, 1.90, p < 0.001), middle (OR = 1.24, 95% CI: 1.02, 1.51, p = 0.029) and highest wealth tertiles (OR = 1.65, 95% CI: 1.33, 2.05, p < 0.001), health insurance coverage (OR = 1.50, 95% CI: 1.07, 2.11, p = 0.020), and greater attention to Nutrition Facts labeling (OR = 1.45, 95% CI: 1.02, 2.06, p = 0.037) were independently associated with healthy dietary pattern.

CONCLUSION: Healthier dietary patterns among Iranian adults with T2DM were associated with greater household wealth, higher educational attainment, health insurance coverage, and greater attention to Nutrition Facts labels.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40200-026-02060-w.

articles.title: Integrated metabolomics and electronic tongue analysis reveal dynamic changes in taste characteristics and non-volatile metabolites during Xinyang Maojian green tea processing.
articles.abstract: As one of China's top ten famous teas, Xinyang Maojian (XYMJ) green tea lacks systematic research on dynamic variations of core taste metabolites throughout processing. This study combined metabolomics, multivariate statistics and electronic tongue evaluation to track its taste traits and metabolic fingerprints across sequential processing steps. 36 non-volatile metabolites were defined as pivotal differential metabolites. Fixation and initial drying were verified as decisive procedures shaping taste. Dynamic fluctuations of catechins, flavonoids, amino acids and carbohydrates jointly build sensory quality. Specifically, the improved in sweet taste attributed to the accumulation of soluble disaccharides (mainly sucrose), intensified umami was closely associated with the enrichment of glutamic acid, and the reduction in bitter and astringent aftertastes correlated with decreased levels of theobromine. Collectively, this study clarifies the key regulatory steps and target compounds during XYMJ green tea processing, providing theoretical basis for processing optimization and the directional improvement of its sensory quality.

articles.title: Visualizing orbital and arterial wall involvement in arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy with time-of-flight simultaneous [18F]FDG-PET/MRI: a novel supportive diagnostic imaging modality?
articles.journal: American journal of ophthalmology case reports

articles.title: Development and evaluation of a family-based graphical tool for longitudinal monitoring of poststroke sequelae.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medical information regarding patient health is traditionally managed by healthcare professionals, often leaving patients and families in a passive role during the recovery process.

OBJECTIVE: To describe and evaluate a family-based functional graphic tool-the Family Observation of Limits and Learning on Well-being (FOLLOW)-designed for the monthly assessment of post-stroke sequelae by nonprofessionals.

METHODS: The tool is a color-coded visual graphic (red for no improvement, yellow for stability, and green for improvement) designed for intuitive understanding without specialized training. It evaluates seven domains: motor independence, sleep patterns, cognition and language, family quality of life, patient quality of life, fatigue, and emotional state. This study included 51 patients and assessed the usability and proficiency evaluation among three groups: family caregivers, healthcare professionals, and poststroke individuals.

RESULTS: Significant differences were observed in the proficiency of completing the tool across the groups. Success rates were 94.1% for family caregivers and 100.0% for healthcare professionals, compared with 69.2% for poststroke individuals (p = 0.008). The graphic proved to be easily interpretable for both caregivers and professionals.

CONCLUSION: The functional graphic is an effective tool when completed by family members or caregivers, though it is less reliable when completed by patients themselves. It provides a practical, longitudinal overview of the patient's home environment and clinical needs, while also serving as a complementary monitoring aid that enables early identification of complications and facilitating prompt intervention.

articles.title: Menopause and Neurology: Clinical Essentials.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Menopause is a neurobiological transition with important implications for neurologic care. This review summarizes the physiology and hormonal changes of spontaneous menopause and its treatment as applied to cognition, epilepsy, migraine, multiple sclerosis (MS), and stroke. It aims to serve as a resource for neurologists when managing patients in this transitional life stage.

RECENT FINDINGS: Hormonal shifts associated with menopause, particularly declining estrogen and fluctuating estrogen-to-progesterone ratios, influence symptoms, disease expression, and treatment across multiple neurologic conditions. Perimenopause is often associated with subjective cognitive complaints, in part attributed to hypoestrogenism, along with secondary effects from sleep disturbance, vasomotor symptoms, and mood changes. Cognitive symptoms are often transient and rarely with objective neuropsychological deficits or progression. In epilepsy, menopause-related endogenous and exogenous hormones may influence seizure susceptibility and alter antiseizure medication metabolism. Migraine may worsen during perimenopause, especially in estrogen-sensitive phenotypes, with postmenopause stabilization once hormones plateau. In MS, perimenopause and postmenopause contribute to overlapping age-related and MS-related symptoms and is a period of high clinical need with potential acceleration in disability progression despite reduced relapse rate. Ischemic stroke risk rises sharply in postmenopausal women driven by advancing age, accumulation of cardiometabolic risk, and loss of estrogen's protective effects. Oral estrogen-containing systemic menopause hormone therapy (MHT) is associated with increased thromboembolic events (including stroke), whereas transdermal regimens seem safer and are preferred at low or standard doses (≤50 mcg estradiol patch or ≤1.5 mg [or 2 pumps] per day of 0.06% estradiol gel). Timing of initiation also modulates this risk and plays a critical role with a favorable risk:benefit window when initiated in women younger than 60 years or within 10 years of menopause onset.

SUMMARY: Neurologists should routinely consider reproductive history, menopausal stage, symptom burden, and disease risk factors when evaluating midlife and older female patients. When appropriately selected, MHT can be safely used in many neurologic populations, with nonoral routes for estrogen and nonhormonal options generally preferred. Incorporating menopausal considerations into neurologic practice offers an important opportunity to optimize care and advance precision medicine.

articles.title: In-Hospital Outcomes of Acyclovir With or Without Corticosteroid for Herpes Simplex Encephalitis: A Nationwide Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Acyclovir is the standard therapy for herpes simplex virus (HSV) encephalitis, yet mortality remains high. Secondary inflammatory responses triggered by viral infection potentially contribute to additional brain injury. Given their anti-inflammatory properties, corticosteroids are considered a biologically plausible adjunctive treatment for HSV encephalitis. However, evidence regarding their effects remains inconclusive, highlighting the need for large-scale evidence.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Japanese national inpatient Diagnosis Procedure Combination database. We included patients hospitalized with HSV encephalitis who received intravenous acyclovir within 2 days of admission. Patients were divided into the acyclovir plus corticosteroid group or the acyclovir-alone group based on whether they received intravenous corticosteroids at a prednisolone-equivalent dose of ≥30 mg/d within 2 days of admission. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included discharge alive with full consciousness, discharge alive with functional independence, length of hospital stay, and hospitalization costs. Outcomes were compared using multivariable regression models adjusted for baseline confounders.

RESULTS: A total of 3,933 patients (mean age, 58.9 years; 58.1% male) were included: 1,385 patients in the acyclovir plus corticosteroid group and 2,548 in the acyclovir-alone group. The adjusted outcomes in the acyclovir plus corticosteroid and acyclovir-alone groups were, respectively, in-hospital mortality, 4.2% and 3.2% (difference, 1.0%; 95% CI -0.6% to 2.1%); discharge with full consciousness, 75.3% and 75.0% (difference, 0.3%; 95% CI -2.6% to 2.6%); and discharge with functional independence, 62.7% and 61.9% (difference, 0.8%; 95% CI -1.8% to 3.7%). The adjusted length of hospital stay was longer (35.5 and 29.6 days; difference, 5.9 days; 95% CI 3.8-8.0 days), and hospitalization costs were higher ($14,704 and $12,174; difference, $2,530; 95% CI $1,774-$3,277) in the acyclovir plus corticosteroid group.

DISCUSSION: Early adjunctive corticosteroid therapy was not associated with lower in-hospital mortality or better functional outcomes in patients with HSV encephalitis. Although our findings do not support the routine use of early adjunctive corticosteroids, further studies evaluating the optimal indications, timing, and duration of corticosteroid administration are needed to clarify its potential role in the management of HSV encephalitis.

articles.title: Managing Plexiform Neurofibroma and Other Complications of Neurofibromatosis Type 1 in the Adult Neurology Clinic: A Review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Loss-of-function variants in the NF1 gene result in the development of neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1), a neurogenetic disease and multisystem disorder that includes a predilection for benign and malignant tumors of the central and peripheral nervous systems. Patients with NF1 experience a wide variety of comorbidities, such as chronic pain conditions, learning disabilities, and signs and symptoms that include migraines and NF1-associated plexiform neurofibromas (PNs), which can cause disfigurement and pain. All of these factors can severely affect health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Although treatment options are limited, advances in targeted therapies have led to the approval of the mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase 1 and 2 (MEK1/2) inhibitors selumetinib and mirdametinib, which reduce target PN volume and improve HRQoL in patients with NF1-PNs.

RECENT FINDINGS: A multidisciplinary team is necessary to evaluate patients and determine appropriate treatments that may reduce the burden of NF1. For adult patients with NF1, neurologists or neuro-oncologists may determine individual patient imaging and serial monitoring needs based on clinical evaluations and patient history. Imaging is useful to identify and determine the extent of potentially concerning tumors, although the specific imaging methods available depend on individual institutional capabilities. Biopsies may be conducted on areas of clinical or radiologic concern to determine the presence of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors or atypical neurofibromatous neoplasm of uncertain biological potential. Systemic treatment or surgical debulking may be recommended to reduce PN symptoms caused by tumor size, inflammation, and compression of vital organs. However, in patients with inoperable symptomatic NF1-PN, systemic MEK inhibitors may be considered to target PN volume reductions. Currently, 2 MEK1/2 inhibitors (selumetinib and mirdametinib) are approved by the US Food and Drug Administration and European Commission for the treatment of NF1-PN.

SUMMARY: Because of the complexity of how and when to administer treatment and the impact of symptoms on HRQoL, a multidisciplinary team is essential to manage the manifestations of NF1, including PN, to achieve the greatest benefit from currently available therapies.

articles.title: A Multidisciplinary Neuro-Lupus Program for the Evaluation and Management of Patients With SLE and Cognitive Concerns.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: To develop and implement a standardized, comprehensive multidisciplinary program for the evaluation and management of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and cognitive concerns that would lead to improved diagnosis and management.

METHODS: The Neuro-Lupus Program evaluated 50 patients with SLE referred for any neurocognitive concern over a 12-month period. A specific sequential work-up protocol was developed for standardized patient evaluation. Initial history and examination were performed by a dedicated lupus neurologist followed by referral for comprehensive neurocognitive testing. Patients with suspected mood or psychotic disorders were evaluated in a specialized autoimmune psychiatry clinic. MRI brain scans were performed in all patients. Patients with MRI evidence of inflammation or cognitive impairment were further assessed with CSF studies and FDG-PET/CT brain. Management of neuropsychiatric medications and immunotherapy was a collaboration between neurology, psychiatry, and rheumatology.

RESULTS: Full neurocognitive evaluation revealed a previously undiagnosed cognitive impairment in 46.4% of patients tested (mild 39.3%, major 7.1%), with an additional 39.3% demonstrating a normal cognitive profile with isolated weakness. MRI demonstrated white matter disease in 50% of patients and cerebral atrophy in 10%. Brain FDG-PET/CT was performed in 8 patients (16%), 7 (88%) of which were abnormal. CSF studies demonstrated normal protein and white cell counts, but 25% had elevated kappa free light chains. As a result of this program, neuropsychiatric medications were optimized in 86% of patients and 8% had an escalation in immunotherapy.

DISCUSSION: This multidisciplinary Neuro-Lupus Program model brings together neurologists, psychiatrists, rheumatologists, and neuropsychologists to standardize the approach to neurocognitive symptoms in SLE. Among the patients enrolled, this program detected previously undiagnosed cognitive impairment in the majority of those tested and was associated with changes in neuropsychiatric and immunotherapy management.

articles.title: Diagnostic evaluation of anemia in inflammatory bowel disease: the potential role of soluble hemojuvelin.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The differentiation of anemia types, particularly between iron deficiency anemia (IDA) and anemia of chronic disease, remains a major diagnostic challenge among patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of various iron parameters, with a specific focus on serum hemojuvelin (sHjv) as a potential biomarker of anemia in IBD.

METHODS: The study was conducted in the Gastroenterology Department of the University Hospital of Heraklion. Demographics, clinical and laboratory data, as well as sera from 152 consecutive IBD patients, were collected. Transferrin saturation, soluble transferrin receptor (sTFR), sTFR index, and hepcidin (Hpc) were assessed. In addition, sHjv levels were measured using a commercially available Elisa kit.

RESULTS: Eighty-nine patients (58.6%) had a history of anemia, whereas 40 (26.3%) were anemic at study entry. The majority of anemic patients (57.5%) had IDA. Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated that sTFR more than 1.64 mg/L [area under the curve (AUC): 0.774] and sTFR index more than 1.06 (AUC: 0.921) were significant predictors for IDA diagnosis (both P  < 0.001). Neither Hpc nor sHjv showed diagnostic utility for non-IDA anemia [cut-offs >31 317 pg/ml (AUC = 0.511, P  = 0.9107) and ≤227.04 ng/ml (AUC = 0.612, P  = 0.219), respectively]. Serum Hjv levels were negatively correlated with Hpc in all patients (-0.25) and in nonanemic patients (-0.29), both P  < 0.05.

CONCLUSION: sTFR and particularly sTFR index are valuable diagnostic tools for identifying true IDA, whereas sHjv appears to have no diagnostic role but shows a consistent negative correlation with Hpc.

articles.title: Prognostic value of systemic inflammatory markers for disease severity and mortality in cirrhosis: a MIMIC-IV-based cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The study aimed to investigate the associations between systemic inflammatory markers and disease severity and mortality in patients with cirrhosis and to identify robust prognostic indicators.

METHODS: Data from 2940 cirrhotic patients were obtained from the MIMIC-IV database(version 2.2). Generalized ordered logistic regression evaluated determinants of cirrhosis severity. Associations between inflammatory markers and mortality were examined using Cox proportional hazards models. Restricted cubic splines and two-piecewise Cox models were employed to explore nonlinear and threshold effects.

RESULTS: With increasing Child-Turcotte-Pugh class, inflammatory markers including neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and neutrophil-to-platelet ratio (NPR) increased progressively, whereas lymphocyte counts decreased. After collinearity assessment, aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index, NPR, NLR, age, and Simplified Acute Physiology Score were retained for multivariable analyses. In multivariable Cox regression, NPR emerged as an independent predictor of mortality, with each unit increase in NPR associated with a higher risk of 28-day mortality [hazard ratio = 1.55, 95% confidence interval (CI)= 1.30-1.84; P < 0.001] and 365-day mortality (hazard ratio = 1.31, 95% CI = 1.18-1.46; P < 0.001). Analyses demonstrated a significant J-shaped association between NPR and mortality, with a consistent inflection point at NPR = 0.05, above which mortality risk markedly increased.

CONCLUSION: NPR independently predicts short- and long-term all-cause mortality in cirrhosis, exhibiting a clinically meaningful nonlinear threshold relationship. These findings emphasize the role of systemic inflammation in cirrhosis progression and highlight NPR as a practical biomarker for clinical risk stratification.

articles.title: Portal venous system thrombosis after cyanoacrylate injection for gastric varices under endoscopic ultrasound versus conventional endoscopy: a propensity-matched study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the incidence of portal venous system thrombosis (PVST) following endoscopic ultrasound-guided cyanoacrylate injection (EUS-CYA) versus direct endoscopic cyanoacrylate injection (DEI-CYA) for gastric varices, and to identify associated risk factors.

METHODS: A total of 202 patients with cirrhosis who underwent either EUS-CYA or DEI-CYA for gastric varices were retrospectively enrolled. All patients were followed for at least 1 year after the procedure, and early PVST was assessed 3-5 months post-procedure. Propensity score matching was performed to balance baseline characteristics. The early and overall incidence of PVST was compared between groups, and an extended Cox proportional hazards model was used to identify risk factors.

RESULTS: After matching, 132 patients were included (66 per group). The incidence of post-procedural early PVST was significantly higher in the EUS-CYA group than in the DEI-CYA group (16.7% vs. 4.5%, hazard ratio = 3.62, P  = 0.035), while overall PVST during follow-up showed no difference (22.7% vs. 16.7%, P  = 0.340). Cumulative endoscopic treatment sessions [hazard ratio = 1.98, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.36-2.89, P  < 0.001], D-dimer (hazard ratio = 1.10, 95% CI = 1.02-1.20, P  = 0.015), and white blood cell count (hazard ratio = 0.87, 95% CI = 0.77-0.98, P  = 0.024) were independently associated with PVST.

CONCLUSION: EUS-CYA was associated with an increased risk of early PVST. Enhanced imaging surveillance, particularly 90-130 days after the procedure, is warranted. Cumulative endoscopic treatment sessions, D-dimer, and white blood cell count are independently associated with the development of PVST.

articles.title: Internal Jugular Compression Syndrome Because of Compression Between the Styloid Process and C1 Transverse Process: Clinical Presentation, Diagnosis, and Management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Internal jugular vein (IJV) compression at the skull base represents a rare cause of cerebral venous outflow obstruction and may mimic Eagle's syndrome. Unlike classic Eagle's syndrome, this condition results from venous compression between the hypertrophic C1 transverse process and the styloid process, producing symptoms such as pulsatile tinnitus, headache, and cognitive disturbances. We describe our experience highlighting the diagnostic protocol and management strategies.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 5 patients with symptomatic IJV compression syndrome. Demographics, clinical presentation, and treatment outcomes were analyzed. Diagnostic evaluation included computed tomography venography, duplex ultrasonography with head rotation, and cerebral angiography. Four (80%) patients underwent microsurgical decompression of the IJV through a posterolateral suboccipital approach with resection of the hypertrophic C1 transverse process and decompression of the V2-V3 vertebral artery. One patient was managed conservatively.

RESULTS: The mean age was 57 years (3 females, 2 males). The mean symptom duration was 7.2 years. Presenting symptoms included pulsatile tinnitus, headache, dizziness, syncope, ear pain, and cognitive complaints. Two patients (40%) had undergone previous treatment without symptom relief. Postoperatively, 3 patients (75%) experienced complete resolution of symptoms and one demonstrated partial symptom improvement with persistent tinnitus attributable to neurovascular compression of cranial nerve VIII. Imaging confirmed restoration of IJV patency in all cases. One patient had spontaneous symptom resolution because of extensive venous collaterals. One patient developed intraoperative vertebral artery dissection because of atherosclerosis which was managed by endarterectomy and reconstruction with Hemashield patch.

CONCLUSION: IJV compression syndrome caused by the hypertrophic C1 transverse process is a distinct clinical condition that should be considered in patients with refractory pulsatile tinnitus or suspected venous intracranial hypertension. Computed tomography venography of head and neck along with head rotation is critical for diagnosis. Microsurgical decompression through a posterolateral far-lateral approach provides effective symptom relief and durable restoration of venous outflow.

articles.title: Shunt-Dependent Hydrocephalus and Cognitive Outcomes After Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Hydrocephalus is a common complication after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH), frequently requiring permanent cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) diversion. The relationship between chronic, shunt-dependent hydrocephalus and cognitive outcomes after aSAH remains poorly defined. This study evaluated whether patients requiring permanent CSF diversion demonstrate worse cognitive outcomes at 90 days after aSAH.

METHODS: A post hoc analysis of the multicenter NEWTON-2 clinical trial data set was conducted. Patients with ruptured saccular aneurysms (World Federation Neurosurgical Societies 2-4) who had Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scores available at 90 days were included. Patients undergoing ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement were classified as having chronic hydrocephalus. The primary outcome was MoCA score at 90 days. Negative binomial regression was used to model MoCA scores, and logistic regression was performed using a clinically validated cutoff for cognitive impairment (MoCA ≤25). Multivariable models adjusted for age, sex, hypertension, World Federation Neurosurgical Societies grade, and delayed cerebral ischemia.

RESULTS: Among 215 patients with available 90-day MoCA scores, 77 (36%) required permanent CSF diversion. Median MoCA scores were lower in shunted patients compared with nonshunted patients (24 [IQR 16-26] vs 26 [IQR 22-28], P = .0007). Shunt placement was independently associated with increased odds of cognitive impairment at 90 days (odds ratio 2.13, 95% CI, 1.11-4.14) and an approximately 2.7-point reduction in MoCA scores after adjustment for covariates.

CONCLUSION: Permanent CSF diversion after aSAH is independently associated with worse cognitive performance at 90 days. Shunt-dependent hydrocephalus may identify patients at increased risk for persistent cognitive impairment who may benefit from enhanced monitoring and targeted rehabilitation.

articles.title: Leading the Way: An Overview of Leadership in Canadian Academic Neurosurgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Leadership is essential for advancing patient care, education, and health system performance within neurosurgery. However, the demographic composition, career pathways, and lived experiences of academic neurosurgical leaders in Canada remain poorly characterized. To describe the current landscape of formal leadership in Canadian academic neurosurgery and explore leadership pathways, competencies, barriers, and perspectives using a mixed-methods analysis.

METHODS: A mixed-methods study was conducted across 14 accredited Canadian academic neurosurgery programs. A cross-sectional analysis identified neurosurgeons holding formal leadership roles in 2024 to 2025 using publicly available data. Demographics, training background, subspecialty, advanced degrees, and scholarly productivity were analyzed using descriptive and comparative statistics. Eligible leaders were invited to participate in semistructured interviews, analyzed using inductive thematic analysis.

RESULTS: Forty-four neurosurgeons occupying formal leadership positions were identified. Leadership roles were predominantly held by males (n = 37, 84%), with no association between sex and leadership attainment (odds ratio 0.93, 95% CI [0.36-2.71], P = .82). Median publications were 61 (IQR 27-132), and the h-index was 19 (IQR 12-33). Twenty-five leaders (57%) participated in qualitative interviews. Seven interconnected themes emerged: (1) nonlinear leadership entry and career trajectory, (2) legitimacy grounded in clinical and academic credibility, (3) limited formal leadership training, (4) influence of identity and culture, (5) incentive structures shaping leadership engagement, (6) essential leadership competencies, and (7) consensus-based, service-oriented leadership styles.

CONCLUSION: Leadership in Canadian academic neurosurgery is shaped by informal career pathways, reliance on professional credibility, and limited structured leadership development. Structured mentorship, formal training, and institutional incentives are needed to support future neurosurgical leaders.

articles.title: Left main coronary artery-Pulmonary trunk fistula incidentally detected during acute coronary infarction: Complementary roles of coronary angiography and CCTA.
articles.abstract: Coronary artery fistulas (CAFs) are rare vascular anomalies, and fistulas originating from the left main coronary artery (LMCA) are particularly uncommon. A 63-year-old woman with hypertension and obesity presented with acute anterior myocardial infarction and left ventricular systolic dysfunction. Coronary angiography incidentally identified a tortuous vascular tract arising from the proximal LMCA, but couldn't define its drainage site. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) demonstrated a 3.9 cm fistulous tract with an origin and maximal diameter of 6 mm, coursing anteriorly and to the right of the pulmonary trunk before draining into it. No focal aneurysmal dilatation, mural thrombus, calcification, or secondary branches were identified. The pulmonary trunk measured 29 mm, the right-sided cardiac chambers were not dilated, and transthoracic echocardiography showed no noninvasive evidence of a large hemodynamically significant left-to-right shunt or right-sided volume overload. Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) was performed for the culprit left anterior descending lesion, after which the symptoms resolved. The clinical course favored the LAD lesion as the dominant cause of ischemia, although a contributory fistula-related steal phenomenon was not formally assessed. Following discussion among several cardiovascular experts, conservative clinical and echocardiographic surveillance was selected. This case highlights the complementary roles of coronary angiography and CCTA in defining fistula anatomy and supporting individualized management and follow-up planning.

articles.title: Acceptability and adherence to antiseptic gargling among Malaysian umrah pilgrims: A mixed-methods quasi-experimental pilot study.
articles.journal: Journal of Taibah University Medical Sciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Respiratory tract infections are common among Umrah pilgrims due to crowding, close interpersonal contact, shared accommodation, and prolonged exposure to respiratory pathogens. Gargling has been proposed as a simple non-pharmaceutical respiratory hygiene intervention, but evidence on its feasibility, adherence, and acceptability during pilgrimage remains limited.

METHODS: A mixed-methods, quasi-experimental pilot-controlled study was conducted among 90 Malaysian Umrah pilgrims from two travel batches, allocated by batch to an intervention group (n=46) or control group (n=44). The intervention group received mouthwash and was instructed to gargle with 20 mL twice daily. Quantitative outcomes included self-reported respiratory symptoms, coughing frequency, impact on Umrah activities, and adherence. Open-ended responses explored perceived benefits, facilitators, barriers, and user experiences.

RESULTS: Most participants were female (65.6%) and aged 40-59 years. Cough and sore throat were the most commonly reported symptoms in both groups. No statistically significant differences were observed between groups for individual respiratory symptoms, number of symptoms, coughing frequency, or impact on Umrah activities (all p > 0.05). The intervention group showed non-significant trends towards lower prevalence of runny nose and less disruption of activities. Among respondents, 68.2% reported gargling twice daily almost every day. However, only 22/46 intervention participants completed the post-pilgrimage adherence assessment, representing 52.2% loss to follow-up. Participants generally perceived gargling as beneficial for respiratory and oral health, while forgetfulness and busy schedules were the main barriers.

CONCLUSION: Significant reductions in respiratory symptoms were not observed, but antiseptic gargling was acceptable, feasible, and generally well received. Larger multicentre studies incorporating objective microbiological outcomes and adherence-enhancing strategies are warranted.

articles.title: Current practices and attitudes toward rectus sheath closure among surgeons: A cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: Journal of Taibah University Medical Sciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rectus sheath closure is a modifiable factor for incisional hernia, wound dehiscence, and surgical site infection. Guidelines recommend continuous small-bites closure using a slowly absorbable monofilament suture with a suture to wound length (SL:WL) ratio of at least 4:1. However, few data are available from obstetrics and gynecology, which is the specialty with the largest number of abdominal closures worldwide.

METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 58 surgeons with various levels of training and specialties to assess rectus sheath closure techniques, self-reported complications, and attitudes toward changing practice. Chi-square, Fisher's exact, and Mann-Whitney tests were used to compare professional levels. Predictors of complication occurrence were identified using logistic regression.

RESULTS: Most participants were obstetricians and gynecologists (84.48%) working in academic hospitals (72.41%). Only 5.17% achieved the recommended SL:WL ratio ≥4:1, whereas 29.31% reported a ratio of 1:1 and 18.97% adhered to no specific ratio. The mean bite size (0.87 cm) and inter-suture distance (0.98 cm) were approximately double the recommended standard of 5 mm. Two-thirds (67.24%) used both monofilament and braided sutures despite the recommendation to only use monofilament. Self-reported incidence of hernia (1.72%) was lower than prospective estimates (11-30%). Surgeons with 6-10 years of experience had significantly higher odds of reporting complications than those with >15 years (odds ratio = 33.54; 95% confidence interval = 1.42-1724.32; p = 0.041). Despite widespread non-compliance, 74.14% expressed high willingness to change their practice, and lack of training was identified as the primary barrier (36.21%).

CONCLUSION: Surgeons, mainly obstetricians and gynecologists, significantly deviated from the recommended rectus sheath closure techniques. The high level of non-compliance and willingness to change suggested a lack of infrastructure and training, and structured educational interventions were identified as a priority target.

articles.title: Mortality risk stratification in contemporary myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock: development of AMICS-ADMIT prediction model and benchmarking of established scores.
articles.journal: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mortality risk stratification in acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) remains challenging with heterogeneous temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS) use. We developed and temporally validated the admission-based AMICS-ADMIT model and bedside score and benchmarked them against established scores.

METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study, reported according to TRIPOD+AI, included 479 consecutive patients with AMI-CS undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) between January 2017 and July 2025. The primary endpoint was in-hospital mortality. AMICS-ADMIT was developed using multivariable logistic regression in the 2017-2022 cohort, internally evaluated by bootstrap resampling, and temporally validated in the 2023-2025 cohort. Missing data were multiply imputed. Performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, and Brier scores. Benchmarking against CardShock, IABP-SHOCK II, and GRACE was restricted to temporal validation; tMCS-stratified performance was exploratory.

RESULTS: In-hospital mortality was 42.6% (204/479). The final model included age, left ventricular ejection fraction, prior cardiopulmonary resuscitation, estimated glomerular filtration rate, vasoactive-inotropic score, and ST-segment elevation status. The continuous model achieved AUCs of 0.809 (95% CI 0.764-0.855) in development and 0.834 (95% CI 0.769-0.899) in temporal validation, with Brier scores of 0.176 and 0.167 and favourable calibration. The bedside score achieved AUCs of 0.777 (95% CI 0.728-0.826) and 0.775 (95% CI 0.699-0.851), respectively, with stepwise mortality separation across predefined risk categories. Discrimination did not differ significantly from CardShock, IABP-SHOCK II, or GRACE.

CONCLUSIONS: AMICS-ADMIT showed stable temporal performance and clinically interpretable early risk stratification in contemporary PCI-treated AMI-CS. External multicentre validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Maternal mental health and its intergenerational transmission in-utero: a scoping review.
articles.abstract: Maternal mental health during pregnancy is important for maternal wellbeing and offspring development. Prenatal depression, anxiety, stress, and psychological distress have been associated with offspring emotional, behavioural, cognitive, and mental health outcomes, but evidence remains dispersed across conditions, outcomes, and proposed mechanisms. This scoping review synthesises empirical evidence on maternal mental health during pregnancy as a potential intergenerational exposure, including potential in-utero pathways.Five databases (MEDLINE, Scopus, PsycInfo, CINAHL, and Embase) were searched from 1995 to 24 February 2026, following PRISMA-ScR guidance. Eligible sources of evidence examined maternal mental health during pregnancy in relation to postnatal offspring outcomes. Data were extracted using a structured framework and synthesised narratively. Twenty sources of evidence met the inclusion criteria. Across diverse designs and populations, prenatal depression, anxiety, stress, and psychological distress were commonly associated with adverse offspring outcomes, including emotional and behavioural difficulties, neurocognitive impairments, and increased risk of psychiatric conditions from childhood to adulthood. Several primary studies reported associations independent of traditional birth outcomes, consistent with potential in-utero pathways. Plausible mechanisms included stress-related neuroendocrine processes, inflammation, and epigenetic regulation. However, heterogeneity in exposure measurement, outcome definitions, and follow-up periods limited comparability and causal interpretation.Maternal mental health during pregnancy may be an important early-life and intergenerational exposure associated with offspring developmental trajectories, but observational evidence does not establish causal in-utero transmission. Stronger causal inference, longitudinal data linkage, and incorporation of economic and policy-relevant outcomes are priorities for future research.

articles.title: Safety and immunogenicity of the 24-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine in healthy Chinese adults: two single-center, randomized, double-blind Phase 1 and Phase 2 trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conventional pneumococcal vaccines cover limited serotypes. This study evaluated the safety and immunogenicity of 24-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV24) in Chinese adults aged ≥18 years.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Two single-center, randomized, double-blind Phase 1/2 trials were conducted. Two hundred forty Phase 1 participants were randomized with an overall allocation ratio of 1:1:1:1 to low/high dose PCV24, 23-valent pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine (PPSV23), or placebo. Nine hundred ninety‑two Phase 2 participants were randomized (1:1:1:1) to receive one of three PCV24 formulations (low-dose and low adjuvant, low-dose, high-dose) or PPSV23. Adverse events (AEs) within 30 days post-vaccination and study-wide serious adverse events (SAEs) were collected. Blood samples were tested for immunogenicity in Phase 2.

RESULTS: Post-vaccination adverse reactions (ARs) within 0-30 days were primarily grade 1-2, with rare grade 3 events limited to the 0-7 days. No vaccine-related SAEs occurred over 6 months. Immunogenicity analysis confirmed that in all participants aged ≥18 years, the PCV24 high-dose group met non-inferiority criteria for IgG seroconversion of all 24 serotypes compared with PPSV23.

CONCLUSIONS: The PCV24 vaccine exhibits a favorable safety profile and robust immunogenicity in Chinese adults aged ≥18 years, supporting further efficacy studies in larger populations.

CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: www.clinicaltrials.gov identifier: NCT07025876; NCT07035054.

articles.title: An interpretable machine learning model integrating mucosal and cellular immunity to predict SARS-CoV-2 reinfection: a multicenter cohort study.
articles.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 reinfection remains a significant public health challenge that requires accurate risk assessment across populations. Using prospectively collected data from two independent cohorts, we developed and externally validated an interpretable machine learning model for predicting symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 reinfection. The cohort comprised 1,156 adults from Wuxi and Nantong, China, with a median follow-up duration of 10 months. Reinfection occurred in 128 participants (11.1%). The model integrated eighteen clinical and immune features, and ultimately identified spike-specific nasal secretory immunoglobulin A (sIgA) and spike-specific CD4+ central memory T cells (TCM) as key predictors. Developed using the extreme gradient boosting (XGB) algorithm, the prediction model achieved an AUC of 0.835 in the internal validation cohort and demonstrated strong discrimination in the external validation cohort. SHAP analysis revealed that higher nasal spike-specific sIgA was associated with lower risk, while spike-specific CD4+ TCM cells exhibited a non-linear association with reinfection. This interpretable immune-based model provides a framework for immune-informed risk stratification, enabling better prediction and management of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection risk in settings with heterogeneous population immunity.

articles.title: Prevalence and Impact of Popliteal Artery Injury Associated with Knee Dislocations, Ligament Injuries, and Peri-Knee Fractures: Analysis of the Nationwide Readmission Database, 2016-2020.
articles.journal: Journal of investigative surgery : the official journal of the Academy of Surgical Research
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe knee trauma, including knee dislocations, ligament injuries, and peri-knee fractures, carries a risk of popliteal artery injury (PAI). We aimed to evaluate the prevalence and clinical impact of PAI in adult patients sustaining severe knee trauma.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adult inpatients (≥18 years) with peri-knee fracture, knee dislocation, or ligament injury, using data from the United States Nationwide Readmissions Database from 2016 to 2020. Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to balance baseline characteristics. Outcomes included length of stay (LOS), complications, amputations, and 30-day and 90-day unplanned readmissions. Multivariable regression analyses were conducted to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Among an estimated 211,108 hospitalizations nationwide, the weighted prevalence of PAI was 0.38% (95% CI, 0.33%-0.42%). Knee dislocation was the strongest predictor of PAI. After PSM, PAI was associated with higher risks of any medical complication (aOR 2.56, 95% CI 1.88-3.49), respiratory failure or mechanical ventilation (aOR 3.59, 95% CI 2.15-5.98), acute kidney injury (aOR 2.71, 95% CI 1.76-4.19), and any surgical complication (aOR 4.50, 95% CI 3.40-5.97) as well as increased risk of 30-day unplanned readmission (aOR 1.81, 95% CI 1.21-2.70) and longer LOS (adjusted β 9.15 days, 95% CI 7.57-10.72).

CONCLUSIONS: PAI is associated with substantial morbidity and increased healthcare utilization following severe knee trauma, reinforcing the need for comprehensive vascular assessment, particularly in knee dislocation-related injuries. Given the observational nature of this administrative database study, these associations should not be interpreted as causal.

articles.title: Evaluating a multi-vaccine respiratory immunization strategy involving SARS-CoV-2, pneumococcal, and influenza vaccines in adults: A randomized, open-label, multicenter, controlled, non-inferiority Phase IV trial in China.
articles.abstract: Co-administration of vaccines targeting multiple respiratory pathogens may enhance coverage and streamline adult immunization programs. We conducted a randomized, multicentre, open-label Phase IV trial registered at Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2100046227) in China to evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of co-administering an inactivated SARS-CoV-2 vaccine (WIBP-CorV) with the 23-valent pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine (PPV23) and a quadrivalent inactivated influenza vaccine (IIV4). A total of 1,404 adults aged ≥ 18 year, including equal numbers of adults aged 18-59 year and ≥60 year, were randomized 1:1:1 to receive WIBP-CorV + PPV23 on Day 0 followed by WIBP-CorV + IIV4 on Day 28, WIBP-CorV alone on Days 0 and 28, or PPV23 on Day 0 followed by IIV4 on Day 28. Co-administration preserved humoral immune responses across vaccine platforms. Non-inferiority in geometric mean titers or concentrations was demonstrated for SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibodies and pneumococcal serotype-specific IgG responses. Seroconversion rates were non-inferior to those following separate administration for all pneumococcal serotypes, though results were less consistent for SARS-CoV-2 (after the second dose) and influenza A(H1N1). Age-stratified analyses showed age- and strain-specific non-inferiority findings that should be interpreted cautiously. Co-administration demonstrated an acceptable safety profile, with only slightly higher rates of mild, transient local reactions and no vaccine-related serious adverse events (SAEs). These findings support the feasibility of co-administering WIBP-CorV with PPV23 and IIV4 while maintaining immunogenicity and safety in adults represented in this study.Trial registration The study was registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR) under registration number ChiCTR2100046227.

articles.title: The 'Upstairs-Downstairs' heart with complete main pulmonary artery agenesis and PDA-dependent pulmonary circulation: A rare structural intersection characterized by multi detector computed tomography.
articles.abstract: Superior-inferior ventricular arrangement is an exceedingly rare form of congenital cardiac malposition, representing fewer than 0.1% of all congenital heart diseases, and is almost invariably associated with complex intracardiac anomalies. We report a 3-year-old male who presented with persistent cyanosis, exertional dyspnea, and failure to thrive. Prospective ECG-gated CT angiography demonstrated situs solitus with levocardia. A superior-inferior ventricular arrangement was present, with the morphologic left ventricle positioned superior to the morphologic right ventricle. The great arteries were normally related, with a left-sided aortic arch. A large ventricular septal defect was identified. Pulmonary atresia was present, characterized by the absence of the right ventricular outflow tract, pulmonary valve, and main pulmonary artery. Native confluent branch pulmonary arteries were present and received pulmonary blood flow through a large patent ductus arteriosus supplying the left pulmonary artery, with additional small systemic-to-pulmonary collateral vessels. The morphologic right ventricle was dilated and hypertrophied, with associated enlargement of the right atrium. Pulmonary venous drainage was normal, and no abnormalities of the systemic venous drainage were identified. This case underscores the critical role of cardiac CT angiography in comprehensive anatomical delineation of rare and complex congenital cardiac malformations, with direct implications for surgical planning and prognostication.

articles.title: Vitamin D deficiency and oral health in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA): A public health perspective.
articles.journal: Journal of Taibah University Medical Sciences
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine evidence regarding the relationship between vitamin D deficiency and oral health in Middle East and North Africa (MENA) populations, where vitamin D deficiency and oral diseases remain important public health challenges, emphasizing biological mechanisms, dental caries, periodontal diseases, other oral outcomes, and public health implications.

METHODS: This narrative review synthesizes systematic reviews, meta-analyses, randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and regional public health reports identified in electronic databases and through reference screening, focusing on vitamin D deficiency, oral health outcomes, biological mechanisms, and preventive strategies relevant to MENA populations.

RESULTS: Evidence suggests that vitamin D contributes to oral health through tooth mineralization, calcium and phosphate homeostasis, immune regulation, antimicrobial defense, inflammation control, and alveolar bone maintenance. Low vitamin D status has been associated with dental caries, periodontal diseases, developmental enamel defects, alveolar bone loss, impaired wound healing, and oral mucosal conditions. Evidence regarding oral cancer remains insufficient to establish a relationship. Periodontal disease shares inflammatory and metabolic pathways with systemic conditions, particularly diabetes, and emerging evidence suggests a possible association with cognitive decline and dementia. However, evidence remains heterogeneous and predominantly observational; therefore, causality has not been established. The coexistence of vitamin D deficiency and a high oral disease burden in MENA supports integrated public health strategies based on shared risk factors and the Common Risk Factor Approach.

CONCLUSION: Vitamin D deficiency should be considered a potentially modifiable component of oral health promotion rather than a standalone cause or treatment of oral diseases. Integrating nutritional strategies with established oral disease prevention programs may strengthen public health efforts throughout the MENA. Longitudinal studies and randomized controlled trials are needed to clarify causal relationships and guide evidence-based policy and clinical practice.

articles.title: Co-circulation of H5N1 and H5N6 high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses in migratory birds at a coastal wintering site in China.
articles.abstract: Since 2020, H5Nx high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs) belonging to hemagglutinin (HA) clade 2.3.4.4b have undergone widespread dispersal in wild birds, posing substantial threats to global poultry populations and mammals worldwide. In this study, we report the co-circulation of clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 and H5N6 HPAIVs associated with mortality events in Anseriformes and Charadriiformes at a coastal wintering site in Fujian Province, China. H5N1 and H5N6 viruses were identified in four species of waterfowl (Bean Goose, Eastern Spot-billed Duck, Eurasian Wigeon, and Eurasian Curlew). Phylogenetic analysis indicated that these H5N1 and H5N6 isolates were clade 2.3.4.4b strains circulating within Eurasia and lacked known mammalian adaptation markers in key proteins. The infected birds exhibited severe systemic multi-organ pathology, with the most pronounced damage observed in the lungs. H5N6 and H5N1 viruses caused lethal injury in BALB/c mice, with H5N1 leading to systemic infection. Environmental sampling also revealed the presence of H5N1 HPAIVs alongside low-pathogenicity avian influenza viruses (LPAIVs) such as H3N1 and H6N1. Our findings highlight the complex and dynamic transmission patterns of H5 HPAIV in wild bird populations and the substantial threat they pose to mammals, underscoring the critical importance of sustained surveillance for high pathogenicity avian influenza in wild birds.

articles.title: Variable transmission efficiency of mammalian origin HPAI D1.1 H5N1 strains in ferrets.
articles.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 2.3.4.4b genotype D1.1 lineage continues to predominate in the United States wild bird population and has spilled over into dairy cattle three independent times. To assess the transmission risk of this sublineage, we performed direct-contact transmission experiments for three distinct D1.1 strains in ferrets. Two of these strains were isolated from humans and one from a lethal cat infection. We found that only one human isolate (A/NV/10/2025) was able to transmit efficiently between ferrets. Compared to the other strains, this isolate harboured the mammalian adaptive PB2 D701N mutation, suggesting this mutation may be a candidate contributing to enhanced transmission efficiency of D1.1 as opposed to the PB2 E627 K substitution present in the lethal cat isolate. Based on these data, we conclude that the transmission fitness of D1.1 strains is modest, but special attention should be paid to emergence of adaptation at the PB2 701 position.

articles.title: Temporal trends in incidence, clinical characteristics and outcomes of pyogenic vertebral osteomyelitis in Southern Denmark from 2009 to 2022: a retrospective population-based cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pyogenic vertebral osteomyelitis (PVO) is a severe infection with increasing incidence. We aimed to describe long-term population-based temporal trends in incidence, clinical presentation, diagnostic approaches, microbiology, and outcomes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study including 1,017 adults with multidisciplinary team-verified PVO diagnosed at a tertiary infectious diseases referral centre in the Region of Southern Denmark between 2009 and 2022. Incidence rates (IRs) per 100,000 person-years (PY) were calculated using regional population data and compared across three calendar periods (2009-2013, 2014-2018, 2019-2022). Temporal changes in clinical characteristics, microbiology, diagnostic strategies, and outcomes were assessed.

RESULTS: In total, 1,017 patients were included. The crude IR increased from 4.7 per 100,000 PY in 2009-2013 to 11.0 in 2019-2022, with the largest increase among patients aged ≥70 years. Mean age and comorbidity burden rose over time. Pain was common, fever was often absent, and neurological deficits occurred in 33.5% (n = 341). Postsurgical infection was the most frequent primary focus, and concomitant endocarditis occurred in 8.3% (n = 84). A microbiological diagnosis was established in 64.8% (n = 635) of cases, most commonly Staphylococcus aureus. Use of Fluorine-18 Fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography ([18F]FDG-PET/CT) increased over time. Median hospital stay remained 33 days. One-year mortality increased from 9.5% to 18.2%, while relapse declined, resulting in a stable composite risk of death or relapse (20.7%).

CONCLUSIONS: The incidence of PVO increased markedly from 2009 to 2022, predominantly in older patients with comorbidities. Despite improved diagnostics, microbiologically-negative cases remain frequent. Mortality remained high and increased over time.

articles.title: Potential roles for transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
articles.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous syndrome in which diastolic dysfunction develops against a background of interacting mechanisms: inflammation, oxidative stress, impaired calcium homeostasis, myocardial fibrosis, coronary microvascular dysfunction, mitochondrial impairment, and neurohumoral activation. Effective mechanism-targeted therapies remain limited.
