Transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) is a nonselective cation channel expressed in cardiac sensory nerves, vascular endothelial cells, immune cells, and possibly other cardiovascular cell populations. It responds to diverse physical and chemical stimuli and may influence calcium handling, inflammatory signaling, oxidative stress, myocardial fibrosis, mitophagy, and ferroptosis. Preclinical studies have linked altered TRPV1 expression or activity to myocardial remodeling, impaired relaxation, microvascular dysfunction, and heart failure progression, but direct evidence in HFpEF is still sparse. This review summarizes the biological properties of TRPV1, considers how its signaling might intersect with HFpEF pathophysiology, reviews experimental TRPV1-targeted interventions, and identifies the evidence needed before TRPV1 can be evaluated as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Maternal kidney disease and composite kidney outcomes in the offspring.
articles.abstract: Maternal chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, but its relationship with long-term offspring kidney health remains uncertain. This retrospective maternal-child cohort study examined whether maternal CKD or reduced kidney function before or during pregnancy was associated with a composite kidney outcome in offspring. Live births in the Taiwan Mother and Child Health cohort from 2007 to 2017 were followed through 2018. In the primary cohort, maternal kidney disease was defined as claims-based CKD meeting chronicity criteria before or during pregnancy; the maternal eGFR subcohort additionally included eGFR-defined reduced kidney function. The primary outcome comprised ICD-defined CKD, reduced eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2 or ≥30% eGFR decline at age ≥2 years, or kidney replacement therapy. Laboratory components were interpreted as reduced kidney function rather than definitive CKD unless diagnostic chronicity was documented. Models adjusted for maternal, pregnancy, offspring, and perinatal covariates. Among 79,036 children, 4,687 (5.9%) met the composite kidney outcome. Maternal kidney disease was associated with modestly higher odds of the composite outcome (aOR, 1.29; 95% CI, 1.00-1.66) and offspring all-cause mortality (aOR, 1.88; 95% CI, 1.15-3.09). Analyses of individual components of the composite outcome, sex-stratified subgroups, and trimester-specific exposure windows were exploratory, imprecise, and not adjusted for multiplicity. Maternal CKD or reduced kidney function may identify dyads who warrant long-term kidney surveillance, although causal pathways require confirmation.

articles.title: Investigating the role of drama-based strategies in addressing psychological trauma: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Background: Drama-based techniques have been increasingly implemented with trauma-exposed populations. However, the evidence base remains conceptually and methodologically heterogeneous, with substantial variation in how trauma is defined, how interventions are described, and which trauma-related outcomes are assessed.Objective: This review aimed to synthesise empirical studies examining drama-based interventions for individuals exposed to trauma. The review describes the characteristics of drama-based interventions, the types of trauma addressed, the pattern and range of trauma-related psychological outcomes assessed, and the methodological quality and certainty of the available evidence.Methods: A search was conducted across Scopus, PsycINFO, MEDLINE, and Web of Science Core Collection databases on 29 October 2025. Studies published in English within the past 20 years were eligible if they examined a drama-based intervention in a trauma-exposed population and reported trauma-related psychological outcomes. Methodological quality was appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool and certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE.Results: Twenty-six studies met inclusion criteria out of 1,461 screened papers. Interventions were grouped as psychodrama, dramatherapy, applied theatre, other drama-based psychotherapeutic interventions, and other. The most commonly examined outcomes were depression, anxiety, and PTSD symptoms. Across intervention types, some studies reported improvements in trauma-related and broader psychological outcomes. However, findings were mixed and frequently constrained by small samples, uncontrolled designs, heterogeneous outcome measurement, limited intervention reporting and inconsistent use of terminology. Certainty of evidence was rated as very low.Conclusions: Drama-based interventions show preliminary potential for supporting trauma-exposed populations, but the evidence base remains limited by substantial heterogeneity and low methodological quality. More rigorous study designs, clearer reporting of intervention content and delivery, and greater consistency in outcome assessment are needed to strengthen the evidence base and clarify how drama-based strategies may contribute to trauma-related mental health care.

articles.title: Complex post-traumatic stress disorder in refugees, asylum seekers, and internally displaced people: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Background: Forcibly displaced populations, including refugees, asylum seekers, and internally displaced persons, are frequently exposed to severe, prolonged and repeated trauma from which escape is difficult or impossible. Such exposures increase the risk for complex post-traumatic stress disorder (CPTSD), defined by core PTSD symptoms alongside disturbances in self-organisation (DSO), including affective dysregulation, negative self-concept, and relational difficulties. However, the prevalence of CPTSD in forcibly displaced populations has not yet been quantitatively synthesised, and the added value of the CPTSD construct over PTSD in this population has not been examined.Methods: This systematic review and meta-analysis searched five databases from inception to January 2026. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to estimate pooled CPTSD prevalence, with pre-specified subgroup analyses, meta-regression, and sensitivity analyses.Results: Twenty studies met inclusion criteria, representing 17 independent samples (n = 12,504). Reported CPTSD prevalence varied from 3.0% to 74.6%. The random-effects pooled prevalence, retained as a descriptive summary of the included studies, was 20.9% (95% CI [12.6%, 32.6%]), the 95% prediction interval was [1.7%, 80.3%]. Between-study heterogeneity was very high (I² = 98.3%). Recruitment context was strongly associated with prevalence: estimates averaged 10.6% in community-based samples and 55.2% in treatment-seeking samples. Asylum seekers exhibited markedly higher prevalence than refugees. Across four studies, post-migration living difficulties, including legal insecurity, poverty, and marginalisation, were more strongly associated with DSO symptoms than with core PTSD symptoms, suggesting that ongoing structural adversity actively perpetuates complex trauma psychopathology beyond pre-migration trauma alone.Conclusion: Available evidence indicates marked variation in CPTSD prevalence across forcibly displaced populations rather than a single generalisable prevalence rate. Recruitment context accounts for part of this variation, but the limited and geographically uneven evidence base prevents global population-level inference. Future studies should use representative sampling and consistently report displacement, trauma, and post-migration characteristics to permit more informative explanations of between-population variation.

articles.title: Race-neutral GLI-2022 interpretation in GOLD-positive COPD: reclassification in a Jordanian clinical cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diagnostic interpretation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) depends on the reference equation used to define airflow obstruction. This study examined how often race-neutral Global Lung Initiative (GLI-2022) lower-limit-of-normal (LLN) interpretation reclassified clinically confirmed COPD patients meeting Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) criteria as non-obstructed. GLI-2012 Caucasian, GLI-2012 Other/Mixed, and local Jordanian equations were secondary comparators.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 845 patients aged ≥40 years with newly diagnosed, clinically confirmed COPD attending Jordan University Hospital, Amman, between August 2025 and March 2026. Diagnosis incorporated compatible symptoms, clinical history, post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC <0.70, and additional investigations when clinically indicated. Patients with asthma or suspected asthma-COPD overlap were excluded. Predicted values, LLNs, and z scores were computed for each reference equation. Reclassification was examined across FEV1/FVC bands and using an adjusted bias-reduced logistic model.

RESULTS: Of 845 clinically confirmed COPD patients, 224 (26.5%) did not meet the GLI-2022 LLN criterion for airflow obstruction, compared with 262 (31.0%) using GLI-2012 Caucasian, 174 (20.6%) using GLI-2012 Other/Mixed, and 13 (1.5%) using the Jordanian equation. GLI-2022 classified 621 patients as obstructed (73.5%; 95% CI 70.4-76.4), and all three paired comparisons with GLI-2022 were statistically significant (exact McNemar p < 0.001). GLI-2022 reclassification increased from 2.8% at ages 40-49 years to 46.0% at ≥80 years and was concentrated in the post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC 0.65-0.699 band.

CONCLUSION: Over a quarter of patients with clinically confirmed COPD in this cohort did not meet the GLI-2022 LLN criterion for airflow obstruction. GLI-2022 LLN-negative status should not be used in isolation to negate a COPD diagnosis established through guideline-based clinical assessment.

articles.title: Hepatic biomarker trajectories and mortality in septic adults with type 2 diabetes and recorded dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor exposure versus metformin-based therapy: A propensity-score-matched cohort study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To determine whether recorded dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor exposure, compared with metformin, is associated with worse hepatic biomarker trajectories or mortality in adults with type 2 diabetes and sepsis.

METHODS: In three critical care databases (MIMIC-IV, eICU-CRD, NWICU), adults with type 2 diabetes and sepsis with a DPP-4 inhibitor record were matched 1:3 within each database to metformin comparators on age, sex, body mass index, 24-h SOFA and day-1 estimated glomerular filtration rate. The day 1-7 total bilirubin trajectory was analysed by linear mixed-effects regression under nine specifications including log transformation, flexible day terms, doubly robust adjustment and inverse-probability-of-observation weighting.

RESULTS: Matching yielded 105 DPP-4 inhibitor and 297 metformin patients; a pre-admission exposure record was present in 60.0%. The between-group difference in bilirubin slope was +0.048 mg/dL/day (95% CI -0.029 to 0.126; p = 0.221), with p between 0.109 and 0.436 across specifications. No other hepatic outcome survived multiplicity correction. Alkaline phosphatase rose more steeply on the primary specification (+6.97 U/L/day; q = 0.005) but was fragile: 12 of 28 sensitivity analyses retained p < 0.05. In-hospital mortality was 21.0% versus 13.5% (risk ratio 1.56, 95% CI 0.97-2.49), attenuating to 1.23 (0.67-2.29) with documented pre-admission exposure.

CONCLUSIONS: There was no statistically detectable difference in bilirubin trajectory between recorded DPP-4 inhibitor and metformin exposure, although differences below the cohort's detectable-effect threshold cannot be excluded. An ALP signal was fragile and hypothesis-generating. Mortality findings are exploratory and non-causal. These associations with recorded exposure cannot inform inpatient management.

articles.title: Sex-specific outcomes in methotrexate therapy among patients with psoriatic arthritis and psoriasis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this paper is to identify sex-specific patterns in methotrexate (MTX) therapy among patients with psoriatic arthritis (PsA) and psoriasis (PsO).

METHODS: Data from adult patients treated with MTX monotherapy included in the Dutch southwest Early Psoriatic Arthritis Registry (rheumatology) or Continuous Assessment of Psoriasis Treatment Use REgistry with Methotrexate (dermatology) registries were obtained to create 2 cohorts of patients with PsA or PsO, respectively. Drug survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses. Disease activity, dosing, adverse events, and subsequent treatments were evaluated.

RESULTS: A total of 525 (50.1% female) patients were included in the PsA cohort and 217 (41.1% female) patients in the PsO cohort. In the PsA cohort, female sex was associated with shorter drug survival (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] = 2.5; 95% CI, 1.6-4.1; P < .001), whereas in the PsO cohort, female sex was associated with longer drug survival (HR = 0.6; 95% CI, 0.4-0.9; P = .008). Disease activity at MTX discontinuation was higher in females than males in the PsA cohort (Psoriatic Arthritis Disease Activity Score: 3.9 [1.0] vs 3.1 [1.5], P = 0.037), whereas in the PsO cohort, disease activity was higher in males than females (Psoriasis Area and Severity Index: 4.8 [6.4] vs 3.5 [3.7], P = .032). MTX dosing was comparable between sexes, though average doses were higher in the PsA than in the PsO cohort (18.2 [7.5] vs 15.0 [3.3] mg/wk, P < .001).

CONCLUSIONS: Drug survival and treatment response of MTX vary between PsA and PsO, with females in the PsA cohort while males in the PsO cohort having worse outcomes.

articles.title: Late-onset hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction in a childhood cancer survivor treated with cranial irradiation.
articles.abstract: Hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction is a well-recognized late complication in childhood cancer survivors (CCSs) treated with cranial irradiation. We report a 42-year-old male with a history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia diagnosed at 5 years of age and treated with chemotherapy and 26 Gray whole-brain irradiation. He presented with right upper extremity paresis due to bilateral chronic subdural hematomas. Following burr-hole drainage for the left chronic subdural hematoma, he developed anorexia, fatigue, and hyponatremia and was referred to the endocrinology department. Endocrine evaluation demonstrated hypothalamic adrenal insufficiency, severe adult growth hormone deficiency, mild gonadal dysfunction, and mixed hypothyroidism. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed a suprasellar arachnoid cyst with compression of the pituitary gland. To our knowledge, this represents one of the longest reported intervals between childhood cancer treatment and the diagnosis of hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction, which became clinically apparent 37 years after treatment following a prolonged asymptomatic period. This case suggests that hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction may remain clinically silent and gradually progress for decades before becoming unmasked by the physiological stress, highlighting the need for prolonged, potentially lifelong, endocrine surveillance in CCS.

articles.title: Non-eligibility for highly effective modulator therapy with elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor in cystic fibrosis: What about Portugal?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is an autosomal recessive disease caused by mutations in cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene. CFTR modulators are drugs developed to target the defective protein. All over the world, there are patients considered non-eligible for this therapy according to local regulatory policies.

METHODS: To characterise the Portuguese CF patients defined as non-eligible according to genotype for highly effective modulator therapy (HEMT) with elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI), the authors conducted a multicentre observational study based on a retrospective analysis of the Portuguese CF population.

RESULTS: Based on the current prescribing policy in Portugal, the prevalence of non-eligible patients in Portugal in 2023 was 18.7%, similar to that reported in Europe. However, the regulatory acceleration in the CFTR modulator landscape in 2025 will most likely decrease the expected prevalence to 1.2% under national regulatory adoption of EMA criteria. R334W, G85E, N1303K, G542X, A561E, R1066C and P205S are the most prevalent variants. Most patients are young adults with established pulmonary disease. CF therapies impose a considerable burden on this population.

CONCLUSION: This study provides a deeper understanding of the Portuguese CF population currently ineligible for ETI and enables the projection of the potential impact that forthcoming changes in HEMT eligibility criteria may have across Portugal. With the anticipated expansion of these criteria, the number of patients remaining ineligible for HEMT is expected to become residual. Furthermore, the present work offers a characterisation of patients likely to remain ineligible for HEMT in the future, who could be suitable candidates for clinical trials exploring alternative therapeutic approaches.

articles.title: POCUS Image Archiving in Emergency Medicine: A Systematic Review of Clinical and Financial Impacts.
articles.abstract: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) has become an essential diagnostic tool in emergency medicine, providing rapid bedside information that supports clinical decision-making. However, the full potential of POCUS may extend beyond image acquisition, with effective documentation and integration into electronic health record (EHR) systems potentially contributing to improved clinical and operational outcomes. This systematic review evaluated the clinical, operational, and financial impacts of POCUS image archiving within EHRs in emergency department settings. Following PRISMA guidelines, a comprehensive search was performed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science, eligible studies included emergency department-based research reporting original data on POCUS image storage or archiving within EHR systems, whereas studies without specific archiving outcomes were excluded. Two independent reviewers conducted study selection and data extraction, with risk of bias assessed using an adapted NIH quality assessment tool. A total of 225 records were identified, and 11 studies met the inclusion criteria. The included studies demonstrated that structured POCUS image archiving improved documentation completeness, image quality, accessibility to prior examinations, and clinical review processes. Implementation of automated or semi-automated workflows was consistently associated with improved compliance, enhanced organization of ultrasound services, and more efficient resource management. Financial outcomes were also positively affected, with reported increases in billing compliance, reimbursement, and institutional revenue after workflow integration. Despite these benefits, substantial heterogeneity among studies and limitations regarding study design, confounding factors, and generalizability remain. Future research should focus on standardized implementation strategies, cost-effectiveness analyses, and adoption models applicable to diverse health care settings, including low-resource environments.

articles.title: Cost‑effectiveness analysis of the mRNA‑1345 RSV vaccine for older adults in Italy.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate the potential public health impact and cost-effectiveness of vaccination using mRNA-1345 administered as a single dose compared with no vaccination in Italian high-risk adults aged 60-74 years and all adults aged ≥75 years.

METHODS: A static decision-analytic model was developed to project clinical and economic outcomes over a five-year time horizon, assuming 50% vaccination coverage among eligible adults. Economic outcomes were evaluated from the Italian National Health Service (Servizio Sanitario Nazionale, SSN) perspective. Model inputs were informed by the most recent Italian epidemiological, clinical, and economic evidence, supplemented by published international data when necessary. Deterministic, probabilistic, and scenario analyses were conducted to assess the impact of uncertainty in model inputs and assumptions on the study results.

RESULTS: Vaccination with mRNA-1345 in high-risk adults aged 60-74 years and all adults aged ≥75 years was projected to avert over 19,800 hospitalizations, 4,000 emergency department visits, 381,000 outpatient visits, 6,000 RSV-attributable deaths, and 212,000 antibiotic prescriptions compared with no vaccination over a five-year period. The total incremental cost of €1,143 million and the additional 47,477 QALYs gained resulted in an ICER of €24,078 per QALY gained, which was below the commonly referenced willingness-to-pay range of €33,000-40,000/QALY. Sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness of the analysis results.

LIMITATIONS: Due to limited epidemiological evidence for Italy, selected epidemiological inputs were informed by studies conducted in other high-income countries. In addition, vaccine efficacy beyond the two-year clinical trial follow-up was projected to five years using nonlinear waning curves fitted to the observed trial data.

CONCLUSIONS: Vaccination with mRNA-1345 is a cost-effective strategy for the prevention of RSV in high-risk adults aged 60-74 years and all adults ≥75 years in Italy, in comparison to no vaccination, and has the potential to provide substantial public health benefits.

articles.title: External validation of the MOG-AR score in pediatric myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Predicting the risk of relapse in myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease is essential for guiding early treatment decisions. A score evaluating onset age, sex, attack phenotype, and treatment received (MOG-AR) has been proposed to identify patients at high relapse risk since disease onset, but has never been validated in a pediatric population. This study aimed to externally validate the MOG-AR score in an exclusively pediatric cohort.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively identified 139 children with myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (age <18 years) within the past decade. The MOG-AR score was calculated and the patients were stratified into four risk grades. Discrimination and calibration were assessed using multiple complementary metrics, and univariable analyses were performed for each score component. Sensitivity analyses included exploratory reclassification using modified MOG-AR grade thresholds and the development of an exploratory phenotype-based model.

RESULTS: We included 139 children with a median follow-up of 43 months; relapse occurred in 28.8% of patients. Harrell's concordance index was 0.472 (95% confidence interval, 0.366-0.577), and the time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve ranged from 0.467 to 0.510 over 1-5 years. Calibration assessment indicated limited variation in predicted probabilities across risk grades. Modified MOG-AR grade thresholds did not improve risk group separation (log-rank p = 0.359) or alter continuous scores or rankings. The exploratory phenotype-based model showed group separation on log-rank testing (p = 0.031) but poor discrimination (C-index, 0.394).

CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center pediatric cohort, the MOG-AR score did not provide clinically useful stratification of first-relapse risk. Limited variability in the age and treatment-related components may have contributed to its limited performance. Further multicenter validation in pediatric cohorts with broader case-mix and treatment patterns is warranted. The exploratory phenotype-based model requires independent prospective validation.

articles.title: GMMA as adjuvant and carrier for mucosal delivery of group A streptococcus glycoconjugate vaccine.
articles.abstract: Group A streptococcus (GAS) infection is usually initiated by colonization of mucosal sites such as the pharynx, followed by invasion and systemic dissemination. Development of a vaccine that can prevent colonization is enticing as it would prevent subsequent infections and all associated autoimmune sequalae such as rheumatic heart disease (RHD). In this study we investigated the mucosal adjuvanticity of GMMA when used as a carrier protein for GAS carbohydrate (GAC) conjugate vaccine (GAC-GMMA). Mice were immunized sublingually or intranasally with GAC-GMMA or GAC-CRM197, in the presence or absence of cholera toxin B subunit (CTB). The anti-GAC systemic and mucosal immune responses were evaluated and compared. Our results showed that, in addition to being a good carrier, GMMA is also a good mucosal adjuvant and mediated the induction of substantial levels of serum IgG median titer: 1,050-3,200) and of mucosal IgA (512-2,560) in the mouth, (640) in the nose, (768-1,024) in the intestines and (1,024-1,280) in the vagina. The induced response was similar or better than the response induced by the GAC-CRM197 conjugate administered in combination with the mucosal adjuvant CTB. Furthermore, mucosal delivery of GAC-GMMA and GAC-CRM197 induced IL-17 and IFNγ secretion by immune spleen cells, which are known to mediate neutrophils recruitment and nitric oxide production by macrophages necessary for controlling infections at mucosal surfaces. We demonstrated that GMMA could work both as a carrier and adjuvant for the mucosal delivery of GAC and mediates induction of both systemic and mucosal immune responses against GAS.

articles.title: Long-term efficacy of lebrikizumab in treating head, neck and face involvement in patients with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Head, neck, and face (HNF) atopic dermatitis (AD) substantially impairs quality of life, yet long-term biologic efficacy data in HNF areas remain limited.

METHODS: This post hoc analysis evaluates HNF efficacy of lebrikizumab across phase 3 trials (ADvocate 1&2, ADjoin) and targeted populations (ADmirable, ADapt) in adolescents (≥12 years, ≥40 kg) and adults with moderate-to-severe AD. Outcomes included HN EASI sub-scores and Face Investigator's Global Assessment (F-IGA).

RESULTS: Lebrikizumab 250 mg Q4W provided durable efficacy through 3 years among week 16 responders. At week 152, 94.8%, 82.9%, and 85.3% maintained HN EASI 75, 90, and 100 responses, respectively.Stable response (maintaining ≥80% of attended visits) through week 152 was observed in 88.8% (HN EASI 75), 80.0% (HN EASI 90), and 74.0% (HN EASI 100) of patients. Additionally, 93.8% achieved absolute HN EASI ≤1 and 69.2% achieved HN EASI = 0 at week 152 in week 16 responders. In ADmirable (skin of color), 61% of Lebri-treated patients achieved F-IGA 0 at week 24. In ADapt (prior dupilumab exposure), 55% achieved F-IGA 0 at week 24.

CONCLUSIONS: Lebrikizumab provided durable, stable long-term HNF efficacy across diverse populations, including systemic-naive patients and those with prior biologic exposure.

articles.title: Clinical, Cytological, and Virological Factors Associated with Histological Severity and Recurrence in Vaginal Intraepithelial Neoplasia: A Retrospective Observational Study.
articles.journal: Journal of investigative surgery : the official journal of the Academy of Surgical Research
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia (VAIN) is a rare HPV-related condition with heterogeneous behavior and a relevant recurrence risk. Factors associated with severity and recurrence remain incompletely defined.

OBJECTIVE: To explore clinical, cytological, virological, and colposcopic features associated with high-grade VAIN and recurrence.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 42 women with histologically confirmed VAIN at a tertiary center between January 2020 and January 2026. All underwent vaginal cytology, high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) genotyping, colposcopy, and biopsy. Histology was classified as VAIN1 or VAIN2-3. Recurrence was defined as a histologically confirmed lesion after treatment and documented disease-free assessment. Associations were assessed using bivariate and exact analyses.

RESULTS: VAIN2-3 was diagnosed in 31 women (73.8%). Among HR-HPV-positive women, HPV16-related infection was more frequent in VAIN2-3 than VAIN1 (65.4% vs 18.2%; OR 8.50, 95% CI 1.27-91.56; p = 0.013). Cytology was associated with histological grade (p = 0.024); all women with HSIL/ASC-H had VAIN2-3, although sensitivity was limited. Over a median follow-up of 24 months, eight women (19.0%) recurred after a median of 11.5 months. HPV16-related infection was more frequent with recurrence (75.0% vs 38.2%; OR 4.85, 95% CI 0.70-54.01; p = 0.112), but the evidence was not definitive. HPV16-only infection showed borderline evidence of association (p = 0.050), while no clear outcome pattern emerged for multiple-genotype infection. No other significant associations with recurrence were observed.

CONCLUSION: HPV16-related infection was associated with high-grade histology among HR-HPV-positive women, while its prognostic relevance for recurrence remains uncertain. The limited sensitivity of cytology underscores the value of multimodal assessment. These exploratory signals warrant prospective validation.

articles.title: Atorvastatin improves hyperlipidemia-induced erectile dysfunction via PKA-associated eNOS phosphorylation at the Ser633 site.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hyperlipidemia contributes to vasculogenic erectile dysfunction (ED) by reducing endothelial nitric oxide bioavailability. Although atorvastatin has been reported to improve ED, the upstream mechanism by which it restores endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) activity remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic effect of atorvastatin in hyperlipidemia-induced erectile dysfunction (HLED) and to determine whether protein kinase A (PKA)-associated phosphorylation of eNOS at Ser633 contributes to this effect.

METHODS: Hyperlipidemia-induced erectile dysfunction was induced in rats by a high-fat diet. Animals received low- or high-dose atorvastatin, with tadalafil as a positive control. Erectile function, serum lipid profiles, oxidative stress, penile fibrosis, and cavernosal eNOS signaling were assessed. In parallel, oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL)-injured rat corpus cavernosum endothelial cells (RCECs) were treated with atorvastatin in the presence or absence of the PKA inhibitor H89.

RESULTS: Atorvastatin improved dyslipidemia, reduced systemic oxidative stress, attenuated penile fibrosis, and partially restored erectile function in HLED rats. Hyperlipidemia-induced erectile dysfunction was associated with decreased eNOS phosphorylation at Ser1177 and Ser633 and increased phosphorylation at Thr495. Atorvastatin enhanced PKA activation and eNOS Ser633 phosphorylation while reducing inhibitory Thr495 phosphorylation in penile tissue. In ox-LDL-treated RCECs, atorvastatin reduced intracellular lipid and ROS accumulation and improved endothelial function, accompanied by increased PKA Thr197 and eNOS Ser633 phosphorylation. These effects were largely blunted by H89.

DISCUSSION: These findings suggest that atorvastatin ameliorates HLED by restoring endothelial function through a PKA-associated increase in eNOS Ser633 phosphorylation. This upstream endothelial mechanism may complement the action of phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitors and provide additional benefit for hyperlipidemia-associated vasculogenic ED. The combined in vivo and in vitro design supports mechanistic relevance, although pathway inference relies partly on pharmacological inhibition with H89 and limited time-point analyses. Collectively, our results identify PKA-associated eNOS Ser633 activation as an important mechanism underlying the endothelial-protective effect of atorvastatin in HLED.

articles.title: Timing matters: a life-course review of midlife type 2 diabetes, exposure duration, and late-life dementia risk.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This review synthesizes the evidence regarding Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) as a critical modifiable risk factor for dementia through a life-course lens. The primary purpose is to move beyond the general association and determine how the timing and severity of T2DM, specifically age at onset, duration of disease, and glycemic instability, influence cognitive decline. Consequently, this paper seeks to answer the central research question: How do midlife versus late-life T2DM onset and cumulative glycemic exposure independently contribute to the long-term risk and biological pathways of late-life dementia?

METHODS: A structured narrative review was conducted using predefined search strategies and study selection criteria, focusing on peer-reviewed studies published 2020-2025 and key longitudinal cohorts. Studies included large prospective cohorts, population-based analyses, or meta-analyses reporting hazard ratios (HRs), relative risks (RRs), or odds ratios (ORs) for incident dementia, Alzheimer's disease (AD), or vascular dementia (VaD). Key exposures included midlife onset, duration, cumulative glycemic measures, and severe hypoglycemia.

RESULTS: T2DM was associated with a 1.3-1.8-fold increased risk of incident dementia. Earlier onset and longer duration showed graded risk increases, while higher cumulative glycemic burden and severe hypoglycemia were linked to greater dementia incidence. Associations were stronger for VaD than AD.

CONCLUSIONS: Midlife T2DM appears to be a strong exposure-dependent risk factor for late-life dementia. Preventing T2DM onset, maintaining stable glycemic control, and minimizing hypoglycemia may be associated with lower future dementia risk, pending confirmation in interventional studies.

articles.title: IRP2 contributes to COPD-associated hypoxic epithelial injury through regulation of Sestrin2-related stress responses and ferroptosis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by persistent oxidative stress and airway epithelial injury. However, the molecular mechanisms linking iron metabolism and cellular stress responses in COPD remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the role of iron regulatory protein 2 (IRP2) in COPD-associated epithelial injury. 16HBE and A549 cells were exposed to cigarette smoke extract (CSE) under a COPD-associated hypoxic microenvironment. IRP2 was silenced using shRNA, and Sestrin2 restoration experiments were performed. Cellular injury was evaluated by cell viability, ROS production, inflammatory cytokines, intracellular Fe²⁺ accumulation, ferroptosis-related proteins, and NRF2 activation. CSE exposure under a COPD-associated hypoxic microenvironment induced epithelial injury, accompanied by increased oxidative stress, inflammation, iron accumulation, and ferroptosis-related changes. IRP2 silencing alleviated these alterations and enhanced NRF2 nuclear activation with increased expression of antioxidant proteins. Restoration of Sestrin2 partially reversed the protective effects induced by IRP2 depletion. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition of ferroptosis attenuated epithelial injury. IRP2 contributes to COPD-associated epithelial injury by regulating oxidative stress, iron homeostasis, and ferroptosis-related responses, providing new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying COPD progression.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s10616-026-01066-9.

articles.title: Economic evaluation of tirzepatide, semaglutide, and liraglutide in the treatment of obese and overweight patients without diabetes: a short-term cost-effectiveness analysis in Iran.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: GLP-1 and dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists have improved obesity treatment, but their high cost requires economic evaluation to guide resource allocation. To assess the short-term cost-effectiveness of subcutaneous tirzepatide, semaglutide, and liraglutide for treating adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes in Iran.

METHODS: A decision-tree model was developed to compare tirzepatide, semaglutide, and liraglutide over 68 weeks in adults aged ≥ 18 years with BMI ≥ 30 kg/m² or ≥ 27 kg/m² with at least one additional weight-related complication, excluding those with diabetes, from the payer perspective. Clinical effectiveness, adverse event (AE), and treatment discontinuation data were obtained from published literatures. Quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) were estimated based on BMI changes and AE-related disutility. Direct medical costs included drug acquisition and AE management costs. Deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Compared with semaglutide, tirzepatide generated greater health benefits but at higher costs, resulting in an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of US$34,423.89/QALY. Liraglutide was dominated by semaglutide. Semaglutide was cost-effective at the Iranian willingness-to-pay threshold of US$ (Purchasing power parity (PPP) 15,558.5/QALY, equal to one time GDP per capita in 2026. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the findings.

CONCLUSION: Semaglutide was the cost-effective injectable GLP-1-based therapy in Iran. Although tirzepatide provided greater health benefits, its higher cost limited its cost-effectiveness at current prices.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40200-026-02114-z.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of high-sensitivity point-of-care troponin assays in emergency department for patients presenting with chest pain: a systematic review.
articles.journal: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine
articles.abstract: Background High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays have significantly enhanced the diagnosis in patients suspected of acute coronary syndrome (ACS). New hs-cTn point-of-care (POC) devices (turnaround time <20 min) may significantly reduce time to diagnosis. Purpose We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of four currently commercially available hs-cTn POC devices to assess their potential for clinical implementation at the emergency department (ED). Methods We conducted a search in PubMed Central on 20 November, 2025. Studies were included if they investigated patients greater than or equal to 18 years presenting with chest pain suggestive of ACS and evaluated commercially available hs-cTn POC devices. Studies had to report diagnostic accuracy [sensitivity, specificity, negative predictive value (NPV), positive predictive value] for the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Studies were assessed for risk of bias and applicability using the QUADAS-3 tool. Results We identified 436 articles. The 11 included studies consisted of both derivation and validation studies, including a total of 10 115 patients. The hs-cTn POC assays demonstrated the best diagnostic accuracy when applied as a single-test rule-out upon arrival at the ED, showing the following sensitivity and NPV: Atellica VTLi sensitivity 98.8-100% for troponin less than 4 ng/L (NPV: 99.8-100%) and 100% for troponin less than 7 ng/L (NPV 100%). Pathfast sensitivity 96.3-100% for troponin less than 3 ng/L (NPV: 98.1-100%). i-STAT sensitivity of 99.8% for troponin less than 5 ng/L (NPV: 100%). TriageTrue sensitivity of 100% for troponin less than 3 ng/L (NPV 100%). VTLi, Pathfast, and TriageTrue were also tested using the 99 th percentile with a 0 + 1/2/3 h troponin protocol. Reported sensitivities: VTLi 64.8-100%, Pathfast 87% for plasma and 83% for whole blood, and TriageTrue 79.8%. Conclusion Hs-cTn POC assays are reliable for integration into the diagnostic pathways for patients presenting with chest pain at the ED, mainly when used for rapid rule-out of AMI in patients with very low troponin values upon arrival.

articles.title: Perinatal outcomes among pregnancies with diabetes by rural, suburban, and urban birth location.
articles.journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Rates of perinatal diabetes are increasing, most rapidly in rural communities. There is a gap in knowledge related to how birth location impacts parental and neonatal outcomes in pregnant individuals with diabetes. We assessed differences in clinical outcomes among individuals with perinatal diabetes in rural, suburban and urban settings within a large academic community health system.

METHODS: This is a retrospective cohort study using an obstetric outcomes database including singleton, non-anomalous pregnancies with Type 1, Type 2 and Gestational Diabetes within a 11-birthing hospital system in 2023. Births were classified as rural, suburban or urban by delivery location. Baseline clinical characteristics and birth outcomes were collected. Our primary outcome was a composite of neonatal respiratory support and hypoglycemia.

RESULTS: A total of 1220 births affected by perinatal diabetes were identified in rural (n = 139), suburban (n = 856), and urban (n = 225) hospitals. There were significant differences in types of diabetes and mode of birth between sites. There were significantly more White individuals in rural settings (p < 0.001). There was no significant difference in the composite outcome of neonatal respiratory support needs and hypoglycemia. However, the odds of neonatal hypoglycemia at suburban hospitals were lower (aOR 0.66 (0.45, 0.98), p = 0.037) than those for rural hospitals after adjustment for diabetes type. This did not lead to a difference in rates of interventions for hypoglycemia, with no significant difference in rate of D10 bolus or dextrose gel use within the first 48 h of life.

CONCLUSIONS: There was no difference in the primary composite outcome, but there was a small but statistically significant difference in rates of hypoglycemia at rural compared to suburban sites when adjusting for clinical differences between groups. This did not lead to an increase in need for interventions for hypoglycemia. Overall similar outcomes suggest a potential benefit to shared resources within the same hospital system for management of perinatal diabetes.

articles.title: Use of vaginal estrogens in urogynecology: current evidence, controversies and clinical applications.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) is a prevalent yet underrecognized condition in postmenopausal women, characterized by progressive vulvovaginal and lower urinary tract symptoms from estrogen deficiency. Vaginal estrogen therapy is the first-line pharmacologic treatment for GSM. However, as new evidence emerges, understanding of its efficacy, safety, and use in special populations continues to evolve. This review summarizes current evidence on vaginal estrogen formulations, clinical effectiveness, safety, and therapeutic applications.

RECENT FINDINGS: Recent randomized controlled trials confirm that low-dose vaginal estrogen significantly improves GSM symptoms - including vaginal dryness, dyspareunia, and irritation - while restoring epithelial integrity and normalizing pH. Evidence also supports its role in reducing recurrent urinary tract infections by restoring lactobacilli-dominant flora, reinforced by a 2025 multisociety clinical guideline recommending topical, but not systemic, estrogen for this indication. Comparative studies show similar efficacy across creams, tablets, inserts, and rings, differing primarily in convenience and absorption rather than effectiveness. Large cohort studies indicate no increased risk of cardiovascular disease, venous thromboembolism, or malignancy. Use in breast cancer survivors remains controversial, but emerging data suggest minimal systemic absorption and no clear increase in recurrence risk, supporting shared decision-making. In addition, long-term outcomes show that adjunctive vaginal estrogen does not improve anatomic surgical success after native tissue apical prolapse repair. Nonhormonal therapies and agents like ospemifene or prasterone offer alternative options, though they demonstrate lower or more variable efficacy than vaginal estrogen.

SUMMARY: Vaginal estrogen therapy is the most effective, evidence-based treatment for GSM and helps prevent recurrent urinary tract infections in postmenopausal women. Its favorable safety profile and multiple formulations enable individualized care. Recent evidence clarifies that while overall safety is reassuring, caution is necessary for breast cancer survivors using aromatase inhibitors. Additionally, longer-term perioperative trial data temper expectations regarding surgical-recurrence benefits, while confirming its value for local tissue optimization. Ongoing research should focus on long-term safety in high-risk groups and the effectiveness of emerging non-estrogen alternatives.

articles.title: Erratum: Education Research: Educational Informatics: Characterizing Child Neurology Resident Clinical Experiences Using Electronic Health Record Data.
articles.abstract: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.1212/NE9.0000000000200334.].

articles.title: Automated Calculation of the Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network (PECARN) Intra-Abdominal Injury Rule from Unstructured Emergency Department Notes Using a Large Language Model.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network (PECARN) intra-abdominal injury clinical prediction rule identifies children at very low risk for clinically significant intra-abdominal injury after blunt abdominal trauma. However, retrospective evaluation of the rule's use in practice requires resource-intensive chart review. We investigated whether large language models (LLMs) can automatically calculate PECARN intra-abdominal injury risk scores from real-world unstructured emergency department (ED) notes.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective secondary analysis of children after blunt abdominal trauma presenting to 2 urban pediatric EDs. The LLM, OpenAI o1, was compared with clinician-derived standards for PECARN risk scores and predictor variable extraction from unstructured physician ED notes. Performance was assessed using standard diagnostic test characteristics.

RESULTS: Among 196 children with complete ED notes, the LLM calculated binary PECARN risk scores with 95.4% accuracy (95% confidence interval [CI] 92.5 to 98.3), 94.4% sensitivity (95% CI 90.6 to 98.2), 98.2% specificity (95% CI 94.6 to 100), and an F1 score of 0.97 (95% CI 0.90 to 0.98). Agreement by weighted Cohen's kappa between multicategorical LLM-derived risk scores and clinician-derived risk scores was high, 0.96 (95% CI 0.92 to 1.00). Predictor variable extraction demonstrated strong performance across all PECARN variables, with accuracy greater than 94%.

CONCLUSION: The LLM had comparable performance to clinicians in calculating binary and multicategorical PECARN intra-abdominal injury risk scores and extracting predictor variables from unstructured ED notes. LLMs may enable automated calculation of clinical prediction rules from clinical documentation.

articles.title: Education Research: Career, Research, and Mentorship Outcomes of an International Neuroimmunology Education Exchange Program.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Subspecialty exchange programs in neuroimmunology are scarce and have not been formally evaluated. We assessed participant-reported outcomes of the Neuroimmunology Exchange Scholarship Program (PROBEN), a 1-month immersive placement sponsored by the Brazilian Committee for Treatment and Research in Multiple Sclerosis, covering career trajectory, research engagement, and mentorship.

METHODS: Cross-sectional online survey of all 39 Brazilian neurology residents, fellows, and early-career neurologists who completed a PROBEN placement during the 3 most recent cycles (2023-2025) at 13 host centers (9 in Brazil, 4 abroad); 30 responded (77%). Outcomes were compared by career stage at placement (early career, residents or general neurologists, vs later stage, neuroimmunology fellows or neuroimmunologists) and by location (national vs international), using the Kruskal-Wallis, chi-square (Yates correction), and Fisher exact tests. Analyses were exploratory and unadjusted for multiple comparisons.

RESULTS: The mean age was 30 years (range 26-38); 18 respondents (60%) were early career and 18 (60%) trained at national centers. Satisfaction was high (17 of 30 [57%] excellent), all 30 would recommend the program, and 18 of 29 (62%, 95% CI 44-77) reported that it influenced their decision to continue in neuroimmunology, with no difference by location (p = 0.94). Perceived clinical (p = 0.71) and scientific (p = 0.46) knowledge gains were similar across settings. International placement was associated with more post-program conference presentations (9 of 12 vs 2 of 18; odds ratio 24.0, 95% CI 3.4-171.6; p = 0.001) and maintained mentor contact (11 of 12 vs 9 of 18; odds ratio 11.0, 95% CI 1.2-104.0; p = 0.02). Research activity (p = 0.009; epsilon-squared 0.23) and mentor engagement (p = 0.03; epsilon-squared 0.16) were higher among later-stage participants. Overall, 11 of 30 (37%) reported research output and 1 of 30 (3%) a completed or published manuscript.

DISCUSSION: Participants in this 1-month neuroimmunology exchange reported sustained subspecialty interest, ongoing mentorship, and academic engagement. Later career stage and international placement were associated with greater academic engagement in this cohort. Because participants were competitively selected and largely self-selected into placement location, these associations should not be read as causal effects of the program.

articles.title: Incidence and mortality of invasive fungal infections among patients admitted in intensive care units in India: findings from a multicentric registry-based study (2023-25).
articles.journal: The Lancet regional health. Southeast Asia
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Invasive fungal infections (IFIs) are challenging to treat in critical care, particularly among patients treated in Intensive care units (ICUs). The existing evidence on IFIs from India remains fragmented. This study characterises IFI incidence, risk factors, resistance pattern, treatment and outcome among patients admitted to ICUs.

METHODS: This multicentre observational study leveraged registry data on IFIs among patients admitted to 63 ICUs in eight Advanced Mycology Diagnostic and Research centres in India between January 2023 and November 2025. Patients with proven and probable IFI according to European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer/Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium (EORTC/MSGERC) 2020 and the modified Aspergillus intensive care unit (AspICU) 2020 criteria were included. IFI incidence to hospital admission, all-cause in-hospital mortality, pathogen distribution and antifungal susceptibility were recorded. Mortality-associated factors were estimated using multivariable logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards analysis.

FINDINGS: Among 178,417 ICU admissions, 2500 IFI patients were identified with an incidence of 14/1000 admissions (95% CI 13.5-14.6) and all-cause mortality of 53.6% (95% CI 51.7-55.6%). Invasive candidiasis was the most frequently reported (57.1%), followed by invasive aspergillosis (37%), mucormycosis (3.4%), trichosporonosis (1.8%), pneumocystis pneumonia (1.1%), and cryptococcosis (1.2%). Median age of the patients was 45 years (IQR: 26-60), with 61.9% males and 38.1% females. Among candidiasis, Candida tropicalis predominated (35.6%), while Candida auris exhibited high fluconazole resistance (61.7%) and elevated amphotericin B minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) (40.7%). Aspergillus fumigatus (50.8%) and Aspergillus flavus (38.7%) predominated among culture-positive aspergillosis, with generally low MICs. Exploratory multivariable analyses showed that sepsis, chronic liver disease, immunosuppression, corticosteroid exposure, and total parenteral nutrition were associated with higher mortality in invasive candidiasis, whereas mechanical ventilation, corticosteroid exposure, and immunosuppression were associated with higher mortality in invasive aspergillosis.

INTERPRETATION: The study findings highlight a high IFI burden and mortality among patients admitted in ICUs of India, with mortality exceeding 50%, underscoring the need for continuous surveillance, rapid diagnostics, infection control and antifungal stewardship.

FUNDING: This study was funded by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Delhi (Grant ID: 157401).

articles.title: Stellate ganglion block for ventricular arrhythmia disease states: Emerging treatment options.
articles.journal: Journal of anesthesia and translational medicine
articles.abstract: Autonomic modulation has emerged as an effective therapeutic target in the management of ventricular arrhythmias and electrical storm (e.g., refractory ventricular arrhythmias), in a background of growing evidence of the link between the autonomic nervous system and arrhythmias. Stellate ganglion blockade (SGB) is a minimally invasive procedure targeting the stellate ganglion with an anesthetic agent that has emerged as a temporizing treatment option for management of refractory and hemodynamically unstable ventricular arrhythmias and electrical storm (ES). SGB which can be performed with fluoroscopy-guidance or at the bedside with anatomic landmark approach or ultrasound guidance, has shown potential efficacy in short-term reduction of arrhythmic burden and termination of electrical storm, based on data from case series and observational studies. In the current review, we highlight the role of the autonomic nervous system in arrhythmogenesis and the clinical applications as well as current limitations and future directions of SGB in management of ventricular arrhythmia and electrical storm.

articles.title: Delayed deterioration after surgical treatment of a spinal dural arteriovenous fistula detected by three spinal angiographies: Case report.
articles.abstract: Spinal dural arteriovenous fistulas (DAVFs) are the most common subtype of spinal arteriovenous malformations, and they often cause progressive myelopathy. Early detection and intervention are critical to preventing irreversible neurological deficits. Selective spinal angiography remains the gold standard for diagnosing this condition. However, for some patients with typical clinical features and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings consistent with DAVF, the initial angiography may fail to detect the lesion. In this article, we report a case of T4 low-flow spinal DAVF that was only identified after three rounds of spinal angiography. The fistula was successfully occluded via surgery, and the patient's symptoms gradually improved postoperatively. Nevertheless, the patient later developed recurrent, aggravated symptoms. The delayed deterioration of previously resolved symptoms was attributed to venous thrombosis, and the condition improved after systemic anticoagulation therapy with heparin. The patients fluctuating symptoms stabilized one month after combined therapy with anticoagulants and antiplatelet drugs. For patients with a high clinical suspicion of spinal DAVF, required to confirm the final diagnosis. Delayed deterioration can occur secondary to progressive venous thrombosis, so preventive anticoagulation is indicated for selected patient's, and this intervention should be individualized.

articles.title: Nasopharyngeal diffuse large b-cell lymphoma in a teenage presenting with cavernous sinus syndrome: A case report.
articles.abstract: Primary lymphoma of the nasopharynx is uncommon and is more commonly seen as an association with other primary pathologies. Nasopharyngeal lymphoma is an aggressive tumor and can affect all age groups but is more commonly seen in middle-aged and older individuals. Majority of these tumors belong to the non-Hodgkin's group. Cavernous sinus syndrome (CSS) is a rare but severe complication indicating advanced aggressive stage of disease with direct extension of tumor into the cavernous sinus. Our patient is a young teenage 18-years old presented to emergency department with the symptoms of left jaw pain (4 months), facial swelling (1 month), bilateral nasal obstruction, dysphagia (1 month), visual loss in left eye and proptosis (1 week) along with weight loss. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) face and neck with contrast performed immediately revealed a nasopharyngeal mass with extension of disease into the left cavernous sinus encasing cavernous part of the left internal carotid artery (ICA), involvement of the left orbital apex, optic chiasm and pituitary gland. Histopathology later confirmed diffuse large B cell lymphoma (DLBCL). Laboratory investigations were unremarkable except for an elevated ESR. The patient underwent multidisciplinary management with combined chemotherapy and radiotherapy, demonstrating an excellent response on follow-up MRI and PET-CT, and was discharged with appropriate follow-up instructions. This case highlights early recognition with MRI and histopathological confirmation enables timely chemotherapy, improving outcomes and reducing the risk of permanent neurological sequelae.

articles.title: Type 2 diabetes mellitus and risk of incident peptic ulcer disease: a large-scale prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Prospective evidence on the association between type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and incident peptic ulcer disease (PUD) remains limited, particularly after accounting for comorbidities and medications related to ulcer risk. We examined this association in the UK Biobank.

METHODS: We analysed 344,612 participants, including 13,193 with T2DM at baseline, during up to 17.7 years of follow-up. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models estimated associations of T2DM with incident PUD, gastric ulcer (GU), and duodenal ulcer (DU).

RESULTS: Participants with T2DM had a higher cumulative incidence of PUD (log-rank P < 0.001). In the fully adjusted model, T2DM was associated with higher risks of PUD (hazard ratio [HR] 1.40, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.27-1.54), GU (HR 1.34, 95% CI 1.19-1.51), and DU (HR 1.56, 95% CI 1.34-1.82). There was no evidence of interaction by regular pain medication use (P for interaction = 0.473). The associations were similar in three sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSION: Baseline T2DM was associated with a higher risk of incident PUD and its anatomical subtypes. Residual confounding, selection and detection biases, and the lack of systematic Helicobacter pylori data preclude causal interpretation.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40200-026-02106-z.

articles.title: Longitudinal BCR repertoire dynamics reveal the evolution of broadly binding antibodies following heterologous SARS-CoV-2 vaccination and breakthrough infection: a single-donor case study.
articles.abstract: Continued SARS-CoV-2 antigenic drift and the persistent risk of zoonotic sarbecovirus spillover highlight the need for broadly protective countermeasures. Here, we longitudinally profiled the B cell receptor (BCR) repertoire of a single volunteer who received heterologous booster vaccination followed by Omicron BF.7 breakthrough infection, integrating bulk BCR sequencing with single B cell culture and antibody binding analysis. Breakthrough infection was associated with broadened serum neutralization across SARS-CoV-2 variants and related sarbecoviruses, consistent with recall of antibodies targeting conserved epitopes. Repertoire analysis revealed stage-specific remodelling, with high-affinity binding antibodies shifting from an IGHV1-46-enriched profile after vaccination to preferential representation of IGHV3-30-3 after infection. Isolated monoclonal antibodies exhibited nanomolar-to-picomolar binding affinities to diverse animal-derived sarbecovirus spikes, with broad binding commonly, but not universally, associated with CDRH3 lengths of 14-16 amino acids. Phylogenetic and sequence analyses defined divergent evolutionary trajectories for IGHV1-46 and IGHV3-30-3 lineages, highlighting candidate genetic features that warrant validation in larger cohorts. Together, these findings describe how sequential heterologous antigen exposures can reshape the humoral repertoire in one individual and generate hypotheses for future pan-sarbecovirus antibody and vaccine studies.

articles.title: Mortality dynamics of West Nile virus and Lyme disease in the United States: Temporal, spatial, and socioeconomic dimensions (2003-2021).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: West Nile virus (WNV) and Lyme disease pose a growing public health threat in the United States. This study investigated spatial and temporal mortality trends of WNV and Lyme disease and evaluated associations with individual and county-level factors.

METHODS: We utilized National Center for Health Statistics data to identify WNV- and Lyme-related deaths (2003-2021), including demographics and the decedent's county of residence. County-level insurance status was sourced from the U.S. Census Bureau, and urbanicity was defined using the 2013 National Center For Health Statistics classification. We applied negative binomial regression models to identify predictors of mortality.

RESULTS: Our analysis of 3694 deaths (WNV: 2,628 [71.2%]; Lyme: 1,066 [28.8%]) revealed WNV peaks occurred in 2003 (246 deaths, 9.4% of WNV deaths) and 2012 (281 deaths, 10.7%), and an increasing trend for Lyme (103 deaths, 9.7% in 2021). Overall, deaths were highest in 2012 (343, 9.3%) and lowest in 2009 (105, 2.6%). Age ≥65 (rate ratio [RR] = 1.5, confidence interval [CI] = 1.27, 1.48), male sex (RR = 1.2, CI = 1.04, 1.26), and White race (RR = 1.7, CI = 1.37, 1.73) were associated with increased mortality. Spatial analysis indicated high WNV mortality in California, Colorado, Arizona, and Texas, and states along the Mississippi River. In contrast, Lyme disease deaths were concentrated in the Northeast and the Upper Midwest.

CONCLUSION: Our results suggest that age, sex, race, and urbanicity are important factors influencing mortality from WNV and Lyme disease. More research is needed to link exposures and incidence to mortality of WNV and Lyme to better understand the drivers of regional variation, given the spatial and temporal variability.

articles.title: Diagnostic challenges of masked arginine vasopressin deficiency in neurosarcoidosis complicated by sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor use.
articles.abstract: A wide variety of endocrine disorders caused by sarcoidosis have been reported to date. We report the case of an 82-year-old male patient who presented with hypercalcemia and anterior pituitary hormone deficiency at the time of his sarcoidosis diagnosis and was subsequently diagnosed with arginine vasopressin deficiency (AVP-D) 6 months after the initiation of glucocorticoid therapy. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed an enlarged pituitary gland, thickened pituitary stalk, and loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot, raising the suspicion of hypothalamic-pituitary sarcoidosis. Despite improvement in hypercalcemia, anterior pituitary function, and pituitary enlargement and stalk thickening with glucocorticoid therapy, subjective symptoms of dry mouth and polyuria gradually became apparent several months after the start of treatment. While the characteristic hypotonic polyuria of AVP-D was not prominent, we surmised that these typical clinical features were masked by adrenal insufficiency, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and concurrent use of a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor for type 2 diabetes. This case highlights the fact that the typical presentation of AVP-D can be masked by concurrent SGLT2 inhibitor use and CKD, emphasizing careful assessment of water balance in such patients.

articles.title: Early parathyroid hormone elevation after denosumab therapy following parathyroidectomy: a diagnostic pitfall.
articles.abstract: Persistently elevated parathyroid hormone (PTH) after parathyroidectomy is often attributed to residual disease but may reflect altered calcium (Ca) homeostasis. The impact of denosumab on perioperative PTH interpretation remains unclear. A 77-year-old woman presented with a hypercalcemic crisis and was initially managed at another hospital. During treatment with hydration and elcatonin (40 units twice daily), denosumab (60 mg) was administered, resulting in a rapid decline in corrected Ca (c-Ca). Eleven days later, at presentation to our institution, her c-Ca was 9.9 mg/dL (SI: 2.48 mmol/L; reference range, 8.8-10.1 mg/dL [SI: 2.20-2.53 mmol/L]), and intact PTH was 195 pg/mL (SI: 20.7 pmol/L; reference range, 10-65 pg/mL [SI: 1.1-6.9 pmol/L]). At admission, c-Ca decreased further while PTH increased. The patient had chronic kidney disease and vitamin D deficiency. A focused parathyroidectomy was performed for a single adenoma. Thirty minutes after excision, PTH remained above the surgical success threshold and increased further the morning after surgery, while c-Ca levels decreased. Calcium and vitamin D supplementation subsequently normalized both parameters. Denosumab exposure, together with vitamin D deficiency and renal impairment, may cause transient postoperative PTH elevation despite successful parathyroidectomy. Persistent disease should not be assumed when Ca declines despite elevated PTH.

articles.title: A self-organizing developmental framework for the head direction ring attractor.
articles.abstract: The head direction (HD) system provides a continuous representation of the animal's facing direction and is a core component of the spatial navigation network. Although mature HD circuits have been studied extensively, their developmental origin remains unclear, particularly because young animals already show attractor-like internal coherence before stable visual anchoring is established. Here we propose a developmental computational framework of the lateral mammillary nucleus and dorsal tegmental nucleus (LMN-DTN) circuit, in which a functional HD ring attractor emerges through staged self-organization without preconfigured topology or early external supervision. In the model, a randomly connected LMN network first generates stable travelling waves through relative refractoriness. These waves provide a temporal scaffold for subsequent learning. Local STDP-like and structural plasticity then consolidate wave-based statistics into locally enhanced recurrent connectivity, followed by direction-selective shift-feedback learning in the DTN→LMN pathway. At a later stage, recruited long-range inhibition transforms the travelling-wave manifold into a stable single activity profile (bump) attractor. Visual input acts mainly as a late calibration signal for global integration gain: it improves short-timescale path integration, but does not remove long-term drift. The framework provides a testable account of the developmental dissociation between early internal organization and later sensory anchoring. More broadly, it suggests that key components of classical ring attractor models, including local recurrent structure, direction-selective shift feedback, and late stabilizing mechanisms, can arise through a staged developmental process rather than relying on a preconfigured network architecture.

articles.title: The macroeconomic burden of four alcohol-attributable diseases in China, 1990-2023, and projections to 2030: results from GBD 2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alcohol consumption contributes markedly to the global burden of disease, but macroeconomic assessments of alcohol-attributable diseases in China remain limited. Using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) data, this study quantified the macroeconomic burden of four alcohol-attributable diseases in China: alcohol use disorders (AUD), alcoholic cardiomyopathy (ACM), cirrhosis and other chronic liver diseases due to alcohol use (ALD), and liver cancer due to alcohol use (LCA).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Disability-adjusted life year (DALY) data for the four diseases from 1990 to 2023 were extracted from GBD 2023. The macroeconomic burden was estimated using the value of lost welfare (VLW) approach, which combined DALYs with age-adjusted value of a statistical life year (VSLY) estimates derived from willingness-to-pay methodology. Results are expressed in 2021 international dollars and as a percentage of GDP. Temporal trends were evaluated using Joinpoint regression analysis, and exploratory forecasts to 2030 were generated using ARIMA, XGBoost, and LightGBM models.

RESULTS: From 1990 to 2023, VLW increased substantially for all four diseases: AUD from $1.84 billion to $32.40 billion; ACM, $0.04 to $0.53 billion; ALD, $0.22 to $3.26 billion; and LCA, $0.09 to $2.48 billion. Joinpoint regression confirmed continuously increasing trends (all AAPC > 0, all p < 0.001). Males predominated across all conditions, with male-to-female VLW ratios of 7:1 (AUD), 10:1 (ALD), 3:1 (LCA), and 14:1 (ACM) in 2023. Age at peak VLW varied: 35-39 years for AUD, 50-59 years for ALD, 65-69 years for LCA, and 50-54 years for ACM (shifted from 35-39 years in 1990). Conditional on the continuation of their respective historical trends, the three models produced divergent exploratory projections to 2030.

CONCLUSION: The macroeconomic burden of four alcohol-attributable diseases in China increased markedly from 1990 to 2023, with AUD consistently dominating and the burden overwhelmingly concentrated among males aged 35-64 years.

articles.title: Interpretable machine learning analysis of immune-inflammatory biomarkers for predicting no-reflow in patients with acute myocardial infarction after percutaneous coronary intervention.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether routine immune-inflammatory biomarkers predict no-reflow (NR) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) patients, quantify their incremental predictive value over clinical variables, and build an interpretable peri-procedural prediction model.

METHODS: This prospective cohort recruited 382 AMI patients undergoing PCI. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression identified independent correlates; confounder-adjusted restricted cubic splines (RCS) assessed nonlinear associations. LASSO regression selected core predictors with variance inflation factor (VIF) assessing multicollinearity. Four machine-learning models underwent 1000-iteration bootstrap internal validation and SHAP interpretation. Incremental value was tested via ΔAUC (DeLong test), continuous NRI, and IDI. Stratified regression and interaction tests evaluated AMI-subtype effect modification.

RESULTS: NR occurred in 91 patients (23.8%). Multiple neutrophil-centred indices independently correlated with NR after adjustment. Seven predictors constituted the final model (all VIF < 2.5). LightGBM yielded optimal discrimination and modest net clinical benefit (AUC 0.799, 95% CI 0.699-0.899); AMI subtype and neutrophil-related markers dominated SHAP outputs. Neutrophil count, NAR, NHR, SII, and PIV significantly improved discrimination. Seven of the 16 tested markers yielded significant continuous NRI, and ten demonstrated significant IDI gains. In stratified analyses, neutrophil count, NLR, and MHR were associated with NR in STEMI but not NSTEMI patients; interaction tests found no significant AMI-subtype effect modification.

CONCLUSION: Pre-procedural neutrophil-centred inflammatory biomarkers are independent correlates of post-PCI NR and offer incremental predictive value over conventional clinical variables. The interpretable LightGBM model supports peri-procedural NR risk stratification, though external validation and recalibration are mandatory before clinical application.

articles.title: A baseline cross-sectional survey of women's and household-level health indicators in Tsakare Community, Mount Darwin District, Zimbabwe: findings to inform targeted public health interventions.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A clear understanding of community health is essential for guiding public health interventions. This baseline survey was conducted within the University of Zimbabwe's Education 5.0 initiative to generate foundational evidence for targeted interventions in the Tsakare Community, Mount Darwin District, Zimbabwe.

OBJECTIVE: To describe sociodemographic characteristics, maternal and child health, sexual and reproductive health, knowledge of hypertension and diabetes mellitus, HIV awareness, and household management of childhood illnesses among women in the Tsakare Community.

METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional design was used, targeting women knowledgeable about household health issues. Participants were randomly selected and data collected via a structured questionnaire. Descriptive statistics were applied for analysis.

RESULTS: Data from 401 women were analysed. The median age was 31 years and median age at first marriage was 18 years. Hypertension symptom awareness was low, with only 41.7% recognising severe headaches as a symptom, while 17.1% had elevated blood pressure. For diabetes, 53.4% identified fatigue as a symptom, yet only 11.8% recognised genetic predisposition as a risk factor. HIV knowledge was moderate, with persistent misconceptions about non-risk behaviours. Most caregivers relied on clinic medication for childhood illnesses, though home and traditional remedies remained common.

CONCLUSION: These findings highlight gaps in health literacy, early marriage practices, and limited awareness of chronic and infectious diseases in Tsakare. Targeted, Education 5.0 driven interventions are needed to improve health literacy, strengthen maternal and child health services, and scale up prevention and screening for chronic and infectious diseases.

articles.title: Subverting colonization resistance: Salmonella pathogenesis at the interface of microbiota, metabolism and inflammasome.
articles.abstract: The intestinal tract is a key immune organ and microecological system, where colonization resistance (CR) mediated by gut microbiota prevents pathogen invasion. Salmonella disrupts CR via type VI and type III secretion systems (T6SS/T3SS), inducing dysbiosis, inflammasome-driven inflammation, and intestinal barrier damage. This creates a self-reinforcing cycle:dysbiosis alters microbial metabolites, sustains inflammation, and enhances pathogen fitness, favoring chronic infection. This review integrates molecular mechanisms of microbiota disruption, inflammasome activation, and metabolic imbalance to explain how Salmonella overcomes CR. We also highlight microbiota-based countermeasures, including probiotics, natural antimicrobials, and phage therapy, as promising strategies to restore gut homeostasis.

articles.title: Pathogenicity and virulence of Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
articles.abstract: Neisseria gonorrhoeae causes the sexually transmitted infection gonorrhea and is an obligate human pathogen, colonizing the mucosal epithelia of the male urethra and the female endo/ectocervix, resulting in urethritis and cervicitis. These manifestations represent uncomplicated gonorrhea and highlight the gonococcus as a primarily mucosal pathogen. However, gonococci can ascend the female reproductive tract to cause pelvic inflammatory disease and may disseminate to distant anatomical sites. The gonococcus expresses a diverse array of virulence factors that mediate transmission, mucosal colonization, immune modulation, and disease progression. In this review, we outline the mechanisms of gonococcal transmission and colonization of the genital tract epithelium, and examine host-pathogen interactions that drive inflammation, immune evasion, and immune suppression. We also discuss the mechanisms underlying dissemination and the resulting spectrum of clinical outcomes. Continued investigation of gonococcal biology and host interactions will advance understanding of pathogenesis and support the development of improved treatments and preventative vaccines.

articles.title: Evaluation of the impact of virtual reality as a non-pharmacological intervention for pain and anxiety during hematology procedures and chemotherapy: a controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study aims to assess the efficacy of Virtual Reality (VR) during painful procedures and chemotherapy (CT) in reducing pain and anxiety for patients with hematologic malignancies.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A crossover design with an external control group was carried out. Participants were assigned to two groups: an intervention group, with a crossover design (n patients/procedures = 112), where patients underwent the procedure with standard care only, followed by washout period, then underwent the same procedure with VR. An external control group (n patients = 94, n procedures = 101) was matched to the intervention group based on age and procedure type. Pain and anxiety were assessed subjectively before and after the procedure, with intra-individual and intergroups comparisons. Side effects were captured objectively.

RESULTS: A total of 206 participants were included in this study, with a total of 213 invasive procedures. Anxiety and pain decreased more during VR period than the without VR period and external control group. VR was effective in anxiety and pain reduction during all procedure, except pain during CT (p > 0.05). Two side effects (1.8%) related to intervention were reported.

CONCLUSION: VR effectiveness was demonstrated in reducing pain and anxiety during painful procedures. It was effective in reducing anxiety during CT.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: [ClinicalTrials.gov] identifier is [NCT07085065].

articles.title: Six3 promoting the migration and neural differentiation of BMSCs via Btg2‑mediated Akt signaling pathway activation: A therapeutic strategy for stroke.
articles.abstract: Bone marrow‑derived mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC) transplantation holds therapeutic potential for stroke; however, but its effectiveness requires optimization. The transcription factor Sine Oculis Homeobox Homolog 3 (Six3) regulates processes crucial for BMSC therapy, such as neural cell proliferation and differentiation. However, whether Six3‑modified BMSCs exert enhanced therapeutic effects on stroke remains unknown. In the present study, mouse BMSCs were isolated and identified using surface markers. Six3‑overexpressing BMSCs exhibited enhanced proliferative, migratory and neural differentiation capacities. RNA‑sequencing analysis comparing the gene expression profiles of BMSCs with and without Six3 overexpression identified BTG Anti‑Proliferation Factor 2 (Btg2) as an upregulated gene (log2FC=1.45, P<0.05) in Six3‑overexpressing cells. Further investigations revealed that Six3 directly binds to the TGATACTGTCT sequence within the Btg2 promoter and activates its transcription.
