Btg2 knockdown abolished the effects of Six3 overexpression. Mechanistically, Six3 promoted Akt phosphorylation via Btg2, enhancing BMSC viability and neural differentiation. A mouse model of stroke was established using transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO, 1.5‑h occlusion and 24‑h reperfusion). BMSCs were administered via tail vein injection at the onset of reperfusion. GFP expression detected in brain tissue at 24 h post‑reperfusion confirmed successful the homing of BMSCs to the brain. The transplantation of Six3‑overexpressing BMSCs ameliorated brain pathology, reducing apoptosis and cerebral infarct volume. Notably, Six3‑modified BMSCs demonstrated a significantly greater therapeutic efficacy than unmodified BMSCs. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that Six3 enhances the therapeutic properties of BMSCs by transcriptionally activating Btg2, which promotes Akt phosphorylation. These findings provide novel mechanistic insight into the optimization of stem cell therapy in stroke.

articles.title: Erbin deficiency exacerbates sepsis‑induced liver injury through mitochondrial ROS/NLRP3‑mediated inflammatory responses.
articles.abstract: Sepsis‑induced liver injury (SLI) is a life‑threatening complication of sepsis characterized by microcirculatory dysfunction, oxidative stress, excessive inflammation, and immune dysregulation. However, the role of ErbB2 interacting protein (Erbin) in SLI remains unclear. In the present study, the functional role and underlying mechanism of Erbin were investigated in a cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)‑induced mouse model of SLI using wild‑type and Erbin‑knockout (Erbin‑/‑) mice, together with lipopolysaccharide (LPS)/adenosine triphosphate (ATP)‑stimulated bone marrow‑derived macrophages (BMDMs). Liver histopathology, mitochondrial ultrastructure, oxidative stress, inflammatory cytokine production, and pyroptosis‑related signaling were assessed using H&E staining, transmission electron microscopy, biochemical assays, ELISA, quantitative PCR, immunohistochemistry, and western blotting. Erbin deficiency markedly aggravated CLP‑induced liver injury, as evidenced by more severe histopathological damage, mitochondrial disruption, oxidative stress, NOD‑like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation, and pro‑inflammatory cytokine production. Mechanistically, Erbin deficiency promoted mitochondrial ROS accumulation, enhanced thioredoxin‑interacting protein (TXNIP)‑NLRP3 interactions, and intensified inflammatory activation and pyroptotic responses. Mitochondrial ROS scavenging with MitoQ substantially attenuated the pro‑pyroptotic and pro‑inflammatory effects of Erbin deficiency in LPS/ATP‑stimulated BMDMs. Collectively, these findings identify Erbin as an endogenous protective regulator that mitigates SLI by suppressing mitochondrial ROS‑driven TXNIP/NLRP3 inflammasome activation and inflammatory responses.

articles.title: Epigallocatechin gallate and thermal cycling‑stimulation synergistically promote apoptosis in A549 cells via endoplasmic reticulum stress‑induced calcium ion dysregulation and oxidative stress.
articles.abstract: Non‑small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), as the predominant subtype of lung cancer, presents a considerable clinical challenge due to its high rates of recurrence and the significant adverse effects associated with conventional therapeutic modalities. In response to these challenges, the present study has explored the combined anticancer effects of epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) together with thermal cycling‑stimulation (TCS). The findings obtained demonstrated that the combination of EGCG and TCS led to a synergistic decrease in the viability of A549 and NCI‑H460 NSCLC cells, whereas IMR‑90 normal lung fibroblasts exhibited minimal cytotoxic effects. Further investigations revealed that EGCG could mitigate the TCS‑induced upregulation of the heat shock proteins (HSPs) HSP70 and HSP105, whereas the expression levels of proteasome subunits were concurrently decreased. These alterations were accompanied by the disruption of proteostasis, and also by the activation of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress‑associated pathways. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition studies suggested a mutual interplay between inositol 1,4,5‑trisphosphate receptor‑mediated ER Ca2+ release and an excessive production of reactive oxygen species, ultimately causing the cells to undergo mitochondrial apoptosis. In summary, the present study has shown that the combined treatment of EGCG and TCS reduces the required dosage of EGCG, while also attenuating TCS‑induced heat shock responses. Consequently, the present study offers a novel and promising in vitro proof‑of‑concept strategy for treating NSCLC.

articles.title: Multiple strategies to improve the therapeutic efficacy of mesenchymal stem cell‑derived exosome transplantation in ischemic stroke (Review).
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) is a common cause of physical disability and death worldwide. Although it has been indicated that mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) can treat IS through mechanisms such as immunomodulation, angiogenesis and neuroprotection, their clinical application is limited by inherent drawbacks, such as immune rejection risk and tumorigenic potential. Notably, MSC‑derived exosomes (MSC‑Exos) possess advantages, such as a smaller volume, low immunogenicity and low tumorigenicity, enabling therapeutic effects similar to those of the parent cells. Furthermore, MSC‑Exos can carry various bioactive substances and cross the blood‑brain barrier (BBB), thus indicating their potential in the diagnosis, treatment and prognostic assessment of IS. The present review comprehensively elaborates on the principles by which MSC‑Exos may treat IS through mechanisms such as inhibiting inflammatory responses, suppressing apoptosis, promoting angiogenesis, regulating ferroptosis and maintaining BBB integrity. However, the therapeutic efficacy of MSC‑Exo monotherapy is restricted by its low brain bioavailability, short lesion retention time, insufficient in vivo stability and inability to remain at the lesion site for an extended period of time to exert its effect. Furthermore, the review summarizes the recent optimization strategies involving the combination of MSC‑Exos with microRNAs, traditional Chinese medicine, hydrogels, exosome pretreatment and electroacupuncture to enhance the efficacy of MSC‑Exo therapy for IS, and systematically reviews their synergistic therapeutic mechanisms. In addition, the current status of clinical translation, technical breakthrough obstacles and future development directions for MSC‑Exo combination therapies in neurological diseases is outlined, providing a theoretical reference for innovative treatments of IS.

articles.title: Itaconate as an immunometabolic hub in host-pathogen interactions: Mechanisms, resistance, and therapeutic opportunities.
articles.abstract: Produced by IRG1 in macrophages, itaconate has emerged as an immunometabolic hub at the host-pathogen interface. This review integrates itaconate's roles in antimicrobial defense. We first examine how itaconate inhibits pathogen metabolism by targeting key enzymes including isocitrate lyase, fructose-bisphosphate aldolase, and inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase. Beyond direct inhibition, itaconate reprograms host immunity through SDH suppression, Nrf2 activation, ATF3 induction, and context-dependent NLRP3 regulation, and promotes lysosomal biogenesis via TFEB. Conversely, pathogens have evolved counter strategies including enzymatic degradation, biofilm formation, and immune microenvironment remodeling. We also summarize preclinical evidence supporting itaconate and derivatives' therapeutic potential for infection-associated conditions. Finally, we appraise theoretical gaps and methodological challenges, offering guidance for future investigation in this rapidly advancing field.

articles.title: Endoscopic ultrasound-guided selective inflow vessel devascularization and multi-point venous occlusion for gastric varices due to left-sided portal hypertension.
Metagenomic insights into the pulmonary microbiome of drug-sensitive and multidrug-resistant tuberculosis patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While the pulmonary microbiota may influence TB pathogenesis, direct comparisons between drug-sensitive (DS-TB) and multidrug-resistant (MDR-TB) patients remain scarce. This study explored microbiome differences between these groups.

METHODS: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) from 30 prospective patients (11 DS-TB, 19 MDR-TB) was analysed via metagenomic sequencing.

RESULTS: Patients with MDR-TB showed lower α-diversity and distinct β-diversity compared with patients with DS-TB. Streptococcus and Prevotella were relatively enriched in DS-TB, whereas Staphylococcus, Cutibacterium, and Mycobacterium were more abundant in MDR-TB. DS-TB showed enrichment of 45 carbohydrate-active enzyme families and core metabolic annotations, whereas MDR-TB showed enrichment of infection- and immunity-related functional annotations and a less connected taxonomic network. An exploratory random forest analysis identified six candidate genera and yielded an internally cross-validated AUC of 0.957.

CONCLUSIONS: MDR-TB was associated with lower pulmonary microbial diversity, altered community composition, and shifts in predicted microbial functions. These findings characterise lower-airway microbiome differences between DS-TB and MDR-TB and provide a basis for further validation.

articles.title: Psychoeducational interventions for children and adolescents with potentially traumatic experiences: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Background: Children and adolescents with potentially traumatic experiences (PTEs; e.g. violence, severe injuries, displacement) are at considerable risk for psychological distress. Psychoeducation is frequently used to reduce stress and enhance coping; however, evidence of its effectiveness for PTEs, particularly as a stand-alone intervention, remains inconclusive.Objective: This systematic review aimed to summarise existing evidence on stand-alone psychoeducational interventions for children and adolescents with PTEs, focusing on three child outcomes: trauma-related knowledge, psychopathological symptoms and disorders, and psychosocial functioning.Method: A systematic search was conducted in six databases, following PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024532660). We included peer-reviewed experimental and observational studies investigating psychoeducation delivered as a stand-alone intervention to children and adolescents exposed to PTEs, either directly or through caregivers, with a focus on child outcomes.Results: Out of 9,214 records screened for title and abstract, 114 were eligible, and seven met inclusion criteria (k = 7). Interventions were delivered in print, digital, or in-person formats across hospital and school settings. Two studies reported improvements in knowledge of posttraumatic stress disorder and posttraumatic growth, while one showed no effect. Among five studies on psychopathological symptoms, two suggested reduced anxiety and one suggested reduced posttraumatic stress symptoms in highly distressed children, while the remaining findings, including on sleep disturbances, depression, anger, and dissociation, were not significant. One study indicated improved psychosocial functioning. No studies addressed interpersonal or complex trauma, highlighting evidence gaps.Conclusions: These sparse and mixed findings call for further research on the short- and long-term effects of stand-alone psychoeducation. Based on the current evidence, psychoeducation appears to be a low-threshold and accessible approach with potential preventive value for children and adolescents with PTEs.

articles.title: Safety and immunogenicity of a first-generation modified vaccinia virus Ankara-vectored SARS-CoV-2 vaccine candidate with mRNA-based booster vaccination: A phase 1 trial.
articles.abstract: The rapid development of effective COVID-19 vaccines was enabled by the parallel assessment of multiple candidates early in the pandemic, including candidates based on the Modified Vaccinia virus Ankara (MVA) vector platform. This Phase 1 trial (NCT04569383) evaluated the MVA-based vaccine candidate MVA-SARS-2-S, expressing the full-length native SARS-CoV-2 spike glycoprotein (Wuhan-HU-1). Between October 2020 and May 2021, 30 healthy, SARS-CoV-2-naive adults received two doses of either 107 or 108 international units (IU) of MVA-SARS-2-S 28 days apart, with 6-month follow-up. A subgroup (n = 12) received two BNT162b2 booster vaccinations. Safety and reactogenicity were primary objectives; secondary and exploratory objectives included S1 seroconversion rates, S-domain-specific antibodies, SARS-CoV-2-neutralizing antibodies, and spike-specific T cell responses. MVA-SARS-2-S demonstrated a good safety profile. No severe or serious adverse events occurred. Immunogenicity was poor: S1-specific seroconversion occurred in 0/15 (107 IU group) and 3/15 (108 IU group) participants. Binding antibodies were predominantly directed against the S2 subunit, with peak median anti-S2 fold changes of 6.0 and 5.2 in the 107 IU and 108 IU groups, respectively. Neutralizing antibodies were detected in one participant (108 IU group); spike-specific T cell responses were observed in 5/15 (107 IU group) and 2/13 (108 IU group) participants. Heterologous BNT162b2 vaccination induced S1 seroconversion and detectable neutralizing antibody and T cell responses in all boosted participants, without safety concerns. In conclusion, while MVA-SARS-2-S was well tolerated and did not adversely affect subsequent BNT162b2 boosting, the vaccine candidate elicited insufficient immunogenicity, underscoring the need for optimized antigen design.

articles.title: Glycocalicin is contained inside the thrombus.
articles.abstract: Glycoprotein Ibα (GPIbα) is a platelet-specific receptor that is subjected to proteolytic shedding by ADAM17, releasing its ectodomain glycocalicin. GPIbα proteolysis is induced by strong platelet activation in a process too slow to be crucial in primary hemostasis. The spatiotemporal fate of glycocalicin was assessed during thrombosis using human and murine samples, integrating in vitro approaches and an inferior vena cava (IVC) ligation model. We found that the glycocalicin concentration inside human thrombi was 4-fold higher than in initial plasma (4.0 ± 0.8 µg/mL vs 0.9 ± 0.0 µg/mL, respectively). This was confirmed in vitro starting from human platelet-rich plasma or murine whole blood, with 6-fold and 3-fold increases, respectively. In vivo, containment of glycocalicin inside thrombi following IVC ligation was even more pronounced with glycocalicin levels reaching 135.1 ± 44.3 µg/mL in thrombi compared to 8.2 ± 1.0 µg/mL in plasma. In the presence of ADAM17 inhibitors, the glycocalicin concentration inside human thrombi was 3-fold lower than in thrombi with competent ADAM17. In contrast, inhibition of ADAM17 in mice, either pharmacologically or genetically, had no limiting effect on intrathrombic GPIbα shedding. In conclusion, GPIbα shedding occurs inside thrombi and results in maximal retention of glycocalicin. Intrathrombic GPIbα shedding is conserved between species, but is regulated differently.KEY POINTS Glycocalicin is contained within the thrombus microenvironmentRegulation of GPIbα ectodomain shedding is species-dependent and not universally mediated by ADAM17.

articles.title: Treatment patterns, healthcare utilization, and healthcare costs in patients with newly diagnosed type 1 diabetes: a retrospective real-world study in Tianjin, China.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Data on healthcare among people with type 1 diabetes (T1D) in mainland China are limited. This real-world study evaluated treatment patterns, healthcare resource utilization (HCRU) and healthcare costs among people with newly diagnosed T1D in Tianjin, China.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from a medical records database. The objective was to evaluate clinical characteristics, treatment patterns, HCRU, and healthcare costs in people with newly diagnosed T1D between January 1, 2019 and December 31, 2023.

RESULTS: In total, 1396 people with newly diagnosed T1D were included (mean ± standard deviation age 30.6 ± 22.2 years; 38.8% aged <18 years [mean age 9 years]). At diagnosis, 70.3% required hospitalization or emergency care and 43.3% had diabetic ketoacidosis, with a higher prevalence in children and adolescents (65.7%). The three most common initial insulin regimens were insulin pump (30.4%), basal-bolus insulin (24.3%), and bolus insulin only (20.9%). During follow-up, the mean total all-cause HCRU was 14.32 clinical visits per person per year (PPPY) and the mean length of all-cause hospitalization was 14.14 days PPPY. Mean total all-cause healthcare costs were 28256.13 Chinese Yuan Renminbi (CNY) PPPY.

CONCLUSIONS: People with T1D in Tianjin, China presented with severe conditions at diagnosis and had substantial ongoing HCRU and healthcare costs; actual costs may have been underestimated due to database limitations. These findings highlight the considerable clinical complexity and healthcare expenditure observed in individuals with T1D in China and emphasize the urgent need for effective strategies to improve T1D management and address the healthcare system burden.

articles.title: Prevalence and Correlates of Nomophobia and Insomnia Among Health Sciences Students: Evidence From a Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nomophobia is a behavioral condition characterized by fear or anxiety resulting from inability to access mobile phones. Excessive smartphone use has been associated with psychological and sleep-related disturbances. University students, particularly health sciences students, may be especially vulnerable due to academic stress and high digital exposure.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to determine the prevalence of nomophobia and insomnia symptoms among health sciences students and to assess the association between nomophobia severity and insomnia symptom severity.

METHODOLOGY: A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted among undergraduate health sciences students at Batterjee Medical College (BMC), Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. Data were collected using a structured electronic questionnaire including sociodemographic variables, the Nomophobia Questionnaire (NMP-Q), and the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI). A total of 702 participants were included. Descriptive statistics, chi-square test, Spearman's rank correlation, and binary logistic regression analysis were performed.

RESULTS: The mean nomophobia score was 77.21 ± 31.7. Overall, 96.6% of participants demonstrated nomophobia, with moderate nomophobia being the most prevalent category (45.3%), followed by severe nomophobia (26.1%). The mean insomnia score was 10.86 ± 5.7, and 71.4% of participants exhibited elevated insomnia symptoms, predominantly at the subthreshold level (46.3%). A statistically significant association was observed between nomophobia and insomnia symptoms (p < 0.001). Using continuous total scores, a weak positive correlation was identified between nomophobia severity and insomnia symptom severity (Spearman's ρ = 0.290, p < 0.001). Female gender was significantly associated with higher nomophobia prevalence (p = 0.014). In multivariable logistic regression analysis treating nomophobia as a continuous predictor, each 10-point increase in NMP-Q score was associated with significantly higher adjusted odds of insomnia symptoms (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 1.20, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.13-1.27, p < 0.001) after adjustment for sociodemographic factors.

CONCLUSION: Nomophobia and insomnia symptoms are highly prevalent among health sciences students. A weak but statistically significant association was observed; however, the cross-sectional design and convenience sampling warrant cautious interpretation. These findings highlight the need for interventions promoting healthy smartphone use and sleep hygiene.

articles.title: Awareness of Community Members in Sudan Toward Stroke in 2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sudan ranks 27th globally in stroke-related deaths, with an age-adjusted death rate of 136.47 per 100,000 people. Adequate knowledge among the population, particularly during times of conflict, can improve stroke outcomes.

OBJECTIVES: To assess the Sudanese population's knowledge toward stroke in 2024.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted from April to May 2024 among the Sudanese population who were aged more than 18 years. The study participants filled out a self-administered online questionnaire that was composed of two sections: sociodemographic characteristics and knowledge toward stroke. The data were collected through convenience sampling. Frequencies, percentages, and associations were calculated through SPSS 28. Linear regression analysis was used to measure the association between the sociodemographic factors associated with stroke knowledge.

RESULTS: We received 1124 responses; 56.9% (n = 639) were female, and 80.8% (n = 908) were aged 18-36 years. High blood pressure (85.2%, n = 958) and previous history of stroke (72.3%, n = 813) were the most identified risk factors, whereas difficulty speaking (76.1%, n = 855) and severe unexplained headache (76.1%, n = 855) were the most recognized symptoms. However, 39.9% (n = 448), 46.6% (n = 524), and 43.3% (n = 487) did not recognize personality changes, depression, and bladder dysfunction, respectively, as possible complications of stroke.

CONCLUSION: Awareness of stroke risk factors and the appropriate emergency response was generally adequate, but the recognition of warning symptoms and complications, such as personality changes, depression, and bladder dysfunction, was incomplete. As the sample was predominantly educated, awareness is likely lower in the general population, highlighting the need for targeted health-education efforts on symptom and complication recognition, especially among less-educated and rural groups.

articles.title: Predicting neurodevelopmental delay among two-year-old infants in Northern Uganda.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Data on neurodevelopmental disabilities in sub-Saharan Africa are scarce. Identifying children at the highest risk of neurodevelopmental delay could enable health workers to target these groups more effectively, improve resource allocation and programmatic focus.

OBJECTIVE: To develop and assess a model for predicting neurodevelopmental delay among two-year-old infants in Northern Uganda using easily obtainable predictors.

METHODS: We studied children born to women enrolled in a cluster randomized controlled trial (January 2018-March 2019) evaluating the effect of peer counseling on health facility births. At the trial's final visit (day 50), 1,804 children were enrolled. In November 2020, we followed up 1,421 children (78.8%) and assessed their neurodevelopment at 2 years using the Malawi Developmental Assessment Tool. We used least absolute shrinkage and selection operator penalized regression with 10-fold cross-validation to select the best subset of predictors and assessed model performance using the area under the curve (AUC).

RESULTS: Of the 1,421 children, 70 (4.9%; 95% CI: 3.6-6.7%) had neurodevelopmental delays. Of the 19 candidate predictors, six were retained in the final model (lambda = 0.0076): moderate wasting, prolonged neonatal hospitalization (up to 28 days), maternal education, place of birth, preterm birth, and absence of skin-to-skin contact at birth. The model showed strong discriminative power (AUC 0.75) and reasonable calibration (calibration slope 1.37; calibration belt 0.536-0.727).

CONCLUSION: We developed a promising tool for identifying infants at increased risk of neurodevelopmental delay in low-resource settings, which could help prioritize children for follow-up and specialized interventions.

articles.title: Association of the triglyceride-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio with kidney stone status: cross-sectional and machine-learning analyses.
articles.abstract: This study investigated the association between triglyceride-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (TG/HDL-C) and kidney stone status and evaluated its contribution to multivariable classification models. A total of 1,174 patients from the First Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University were included, with kidney stone status confirmed by urological imaging. Multivariable analyses were used to assess the association between TG/HDL-C and kidney stone status. Supplementary population-based analyses were conducted using weighted data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). Seven machine-learning models were developed and internally evaluated within the clinical cohort, and SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) were used to interpret model outputs. In the clinical cohort, a higher TG/HDL-C ratio was associated with greater odds of kidney stone status after multivariable adjustment (OR, 2.16; 95% CI, 1.73-2.70). The association was generally consistent across subgroups defined by age, sex, body mass index, hypertension, and diabetes, with no significant interactions observed. A directionally similar association was identified in the weighted NHANES analysis (OR, 1.04; 95% CI, 1.01-1.07). Among the evaluated machine-learning models, the random forest model achieved the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve in the internal validation set (AUROC, 0.818; 95% CI, 0.775-0.859). SHAP analysis identified the TG/HDL-C ratio as an important contributor to model classification. These findings indicate that the TG/HDL-C ratio is an accessible metabolic marker associated with kidney stone status. However, the observational design precludes causal inference, and prospective studies with external model validation are warranted.

articles.title: External validation and comparative performance of four risk scores for acute kidney injury in critically ill adults.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Several parsimonious scores predict acute kidney injury (AKI), but their comparative performance in critically ill adults is uncertain. We hypothesized that the ICU-derived UCSD-Mayo score would show higher discrimination than three scores developed in broader acute-care populations.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective validation study included 1,723 emergency ICU patients admitted from 2014 to 2021. We compared the UCSD-Mayo, AKI-RiSc, Bell, and APS scores for in-hospital AKI, AKI within 7 days, and stages 2 and 3 AKI. Analyses included AUROC with paired DeLong comparisons, cross-validated local recalibration, calibration plots, IDI, categorical NRI at the event rate, decision-curve analysis, and prespecified sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: In-hospital AKI occurred in 406 patients (23.6%), 281 (16.3%) developed AKI within 7 days, and 169 (9.8%) developed stages 2 and 3 AKI. UCSD-Mayo had the highest observed AUROC for in-hospital AKI (0.713, 95%CI 0.685-0.740), 7-day AKI (0.690, 0.658-0.723), and stages 2 and 3 AKI (0.706, 0.665-0.746). Its 7-day AUROC did not differ significantly from AKI-RiSc (difference 0.029, 95%CI -0.006 to 0.064; p = 0.103). Reclassification and net benefit varied by outcome and threshold; sensitivity analyses did not materially change the overall pattern.

CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center Chinese emergency ICU cohort, UCSD-Mayo showed the highest observed discrimination, but improvements were modest and were not uniform across all outcomes, metrics, or decision thresholds. These scores may support risk awareness and monitoring but should not be used as stand-alone treatment rules.

articles.title: A novel CXCL8(3-72) K11R/G31P-BPI233 hybrid protein modulates neutrophil-driven inflammation and protects against carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii infection.
articles.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacteria (CRGNB) pose a severe global health threat. Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) is one of the most critical threats among CRGNB, and effective non-antibiotic therapeutic strategies are urgently needed. Bactericidal/permeability-increasing protein (BPI)-derived molecules display antibacterial and endotoxin-neutralizing activities against Gram-negative bacteria, whereas CXCL8(3-72) K11R/G31P (G31P), an analog of CXCL8 with the mutations of CXCL8 at K11 and G31 positions, could antagonize ELR-CXC chemokine-mediated neutrophil chemotaxis. Here, we engineered a dual-function fusion protein, G31P-BPI233, to combine BPI-mediated antibacterial activity with modulation of neutrophil-driven inflammation. Recombinant G31P-BPI233 was expressed in CHO-K1 cells and characterized through safety evaluation, endotoxin neutralization, bactericidal, serum killing, neutrophil killing, chemotaxis, cytokine, phagocytosis, and NET-associated marker assays, followed by validation in mouse models of CRAB septicemia and pneumonia. Short-term safety assessment suggested preliminary tolerability over 24 h, while G31P-BPI233 reduced residual endotoxin activity and exhibited concentration-dependent bactericidal activity against multiple Gram-negative bacteria. At molar-matched doses, it retained G31P-mediated inhibition of neutrophil migration and BPI233-associated bactericidal and cytokine-suppressive activities. In CRAB models, G31P-BPI233 improved septicemia survival and reduced pneumonia-associated bacterial burden and inflammatory injury, with endpoint-specific advantages over G31P, BPI233, or their equimolar mixture. Several pneumonia outcomes did not differ significantly between G31P-BPI233 and colistin. Mechanistic studies using BPI-deficient mice further demonstrated that endogenous BPI contributes to bacterial clearance, endotoxin control, and neutrophil maturation and effector function during CRAB infection. Collectively, these findings identify G31P-BPI233 as a promising host-directed antibacterial fusion protein for severe CRAB infection, with potential translational implications for the broader management of CRGNB.

articles.title: Perceived severity and benefits show a preliminary conditional association with kidney-protective behaviors in type 2 diabetes with early kidney function decline: an exploratory health belief model analysis.
articles.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a leading cause of chronic kidney disease (CKD) and end-stage kidney disease, and early-stage CKD represents a critical window to slow progression through self-management behaviors. The Health Belief Model (HBM) posits that perceived severity, benefits, barriers, and self-efficacy shape health behaviors; however, whether these constructs operate independently or interact in adults with type 2 diabetes and early kidney function decline remains unclear. This cross-sectional study examined four selected HBM constructs-perceived severity, perceived benefits, perceived barriers, and self-efficacy-both individually and through their interaction, as predictors of self-reported kidney-protective health behaviors, assessed simultaneously via questionnaires, among 123 adults with type 2 diabetes and early-stage CKD or at high risk for CKD (eGFR 45-89 mL/min/1.73m2; G3a, n = 26; G2 without albuminuria confirmation, n = 97) at a tertiary hospital in Bangkok. The four HBM constructs did not independently predict behaviors (F = 2.161, p = 0.078). Simple slopes analysis revealed that perceived severity was significantly associated with health behaviors at high perceived benefits (+1 SD: slope = 0.187, p = 0.041) but not at low levels (-1 SD: p = 0.524). These preliminary, hypothesis-generating findings suggest a potential conditional association between perceived severity and perceived benefits; however, the interaction term did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.289). Educational strategies targeting both disease severity awareness and self-management benefits may warrant further investigation. Longitudinal and adequately powered studies are needed to confirm these interaction patterns and establish directionality.

articles.title: Acute kidney disease after acute kidney injury: incidence, risk factors, and association with de novo chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract: Acute Kidney Disease (AKD) is defined as acute kidney injury (AKI) persisting for 7 to 90 days and represents a window for interventions to improve renal outcomes. However, data on AKD remain underexplored. This retrospective cohort study at Tongji Hospital, China, included 23,868 adult patients who survived at least one AKI episode between January 2015 and April 2024. Using electronic medical record data, we aimed to quantify the incidence of AKD among AKI survivors, identify independent risk factors, and evaluate the association between AKD and de novo chronic kidney disease (CKD). Among the cohort, 10,884 patients (45.6%) progressed to AKD. Multivariable logistic regression revealed that advanced age, preexisting hypertension, heart failure, cirrhosis, recent diuretic use, hepatorenal syndrome, higher baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate, higher AKI stage, and dialysis-requiring AKI were independent risk factors for AKD. Fine-Gray competing-risk analysis accounting for acute-phase mortality confirmed that higher AKI severity was independently associated with AKD progression. In a subcohort of 6597 patients without preexisting CKD who had at least one year of follow-up, 19.8% developed de novo CKD. Cox proportional hazards analysis demonstrated that patients with AKD had a significantly increased risk of de novo CKD compared to those without AKD (HR 1.92, 95% CI 1.70-2.17). These findings highlight the high proportion of AKD among patients with AKI, and emphasize the importance of early detection and targeted management for high-risk groups. It is critical to strengthen post-discharge renal function monitoring and intervention strategies for AKI patients to improve long-term renal outcomes.

articles.title: Characterizing vaginal misoprostol induction in individuals with and without severe obesity.
articles.journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare labor induction characteristics and delivery outcomes among individuals with body mass index < 40 versus ≥ 40 kg/m2 undergoing induction at term.

STUDY DESIGN: This secondary analysis utilized data from the vaginal misoprostol arm of a cluster randomized controlled trial comparing vaginal to oral misoprostol for induction. Individuals at ≥ 37 weeks gestation with cervical dilation ≤ 2 cm undergoing induction using a standardized protocol were included. Vaginal misoprostol was given in 25 µg doses every three hours for up to five doses, followed by a standardized oxytocin protocol. We compared labor progression among individuals with BMI < 40 and ≥ 40 kg/m2 at delivery, including labor duration, misoprostol use, and obstetric and neonatal outcomes. Generalized estimating equations were used to account for clustering and comorbid conditions. Effect sizes were presented as odds ratios and adjusted mean differences with 95% confidence intervals.

RESULTS: From May 2021 to September 2022, 1,322 patients received vaginal misoprostol for labor induction at term. Among these, 1,058 (80.0%) had a BMI < 40 kg/m2 and 264 (20.0%) had a BMI ≥ 40 kg/m2. Individuals with severe obesity were more likely to start induction with a closed cervix. After adjustment for clustering, initial cervical dilation, hypertension, and diabetes, inductions in the group with severe obesity had longer total durations (adjusted mean difference 3.5h, 95% CI 1.9-4.8), first stage of labor (adjusted mean difference 2.2h, 95% CI 0.6-3.8), and duration of oxytocin use (adjusted mean difference 2.5, 95% CI 1.1-3.8). Individuals with BMI ≥ 40 kg/m2 also had lower odds of vaginal delivery (aOR 0.6, 95% CI 0.4-0.8) and required more doses of misoprostol for induction.

CONCLUSION: Severe obesity, defined as BMI ≥ 40 kg/m2, is associated with longer time to delivery, increased misoprostol requirement, longer duration of oxytocin use, and lower odds of vaginal delivery compared to individuals with lower BMI. Consideration of alternative labor induction protocols must be balanced with increased comorbidities and overall obstetric morbidity in this group.

articles.title: Fecal microbiota transplantation for the treatment of neurogenic rosacea: protocol of a randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled explorer study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Neurogenic rosacea is a distinct phenotype of rosacea characterized by persistent facial erythema, flushing, burning, and stinging, and it often responds poorly to conventional therapies. Increasing evidence suggests that gut microbiota dysbiosis may be involved in the pathogenesis of NR. Fecal microbiota transplantation may provide a novel therapeutic strategy by restoring microbial homeostasis.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of FMT in patients with NR and to explore its potential mechanisms through modulation of the gut microbiota.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: This is a single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled exploratory trial. Sixty patients with NR will be randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either FMT capsules or placebo capsules for 3 consecutive weeks and followed for 12 weeks. The primary outcome is the proportion of participants achieving CEA success at week 12, defined as a CEA score of 0 or 1 or a reduction of ≥2 grades from baseline. Secondary outcomes include flushing severity, symptom scores, quality of life, psychological status, objective erythema index, and safety. Exploratory analyses will assess gut microbiota composition, fecal and serum metabolomics, and neurovascular-related cytokines.

DISCUSSION: This study is the first clinical trial to explore the effects of fecal microbiota transplantation in the treatment of neurogenic rosacea. The trial may provide clinical evidence for the application of fecal microbiota transplantation as a novel therapeutic strategy for refractory neurogenic rosacea.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500109957) on September 28, 2025.

articles.title: SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein hijacks host transcription by targeting eEF1A1.
articles.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 variants display substantial genetic and phenotypic diversity, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying their effects on host gene regulation need further investigation. We performed a transcriptomic analysis of host responses to multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants, including Delta and Omicron. Despite their divergence, all variants induced a conserved transcriptional program in human lung epithelial cells characterized by activation of interferon regulatory factors (IRFs), immediate-early genes, and downstream cytokines. We identify the viral nucleocapsid (N) protein as a central driver of this transcriptional reprogramming, as N expression alone partially recapitulated the host response to infection. Mechanistically, N promotes recruitment of interferon regulatory factors and AP-1 transcription factors, RNA polymerase II, and the elongation factor eEF1A1 to promoters of pro-inflammatory genes, revealing a previously unrecognized nuclear role for eEF1A1. Disruption of the N-eEF1A1 interaction, genetically or pharmacologically using the eEF1A interactant plitidepsin, abolished transcriptional complex formation and reversed host gene dysregulation, identifying a conserved host-virus regulatory axis and potential pan-variant therapeutic target.

articles.title: Severity-dependent and sex-biased dysregulation of A-to-I RNA editing in COVID-19 reveals CTSS as a key regulatory target.
articles.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 infection causes diverse clinical outcomes, with men facing higher risks of severe disease. Adenosine-to-inosine (A-to-I) RNA editing mediated by ADAR enzymes governs innate antiviral immunity, yet its contribution to COVID-19 severity and sex-biased disease remains unclear. We performed epitranscriptomic profiling on 126 blood samples from non-COVID controls and COVID-19 patients spanning different disease severities. We detected 1,466 differentially RNA-edited sites in 514 genes linked to clinical outcomes. Although ADAR expression increased in COVID-19 patients overall, it was strongly reduced in ICU patients compared with non-ICU patients, and this shift was far more prominent in males. This severity-associated and sex-biased ADAR/ADARB1 downregulation coincided with decreased global RNA editing and perturbed expression of immune-related edited transcripts. Cathepsin S (CTSS) was identified as a central regulatory node: elevated A-to-I editing within its 3' UTR in ICU patients stabilizes CTSS mRNA. Without stratifying by disease severity, ADAR expression and global editing showed no significant sex differences; the large sex divergence only appeared among ICU patients. This indicates severity-dependent, not infection-innate, disruption of A-to-I editing, disproportionately amplified in critically ill males. CTSS 3'UTR editing may serve as a biomarker for patient stratification, revealing a mechanistic connection between epitranscriptomic changes and male-biased severe COVID-19.

articles.title: Epidemiology of uncontrolled and treatment‑resistant hypertension: a registry‑based observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to describe blood pressure control rates and prevalence of treatment resistant hypertension among diagnosed individuals.

METHODS: Randomly selected adults who had at least one primary or secondary healthcare visit and who were registered residents of Stockholm County, Sweden, on December 31st, 2019, were included. Blood pressure control in diagnosed individuals was assessed using two targets: <140/90 mmHg and <130/80 mmHg. The prevalence of treatment-resistant hypertension defined by three commonly used criteria was calculated and its association with clinical characteristics, drug treatment patterns, and comorbidities were assessed.

RESULTS: By the end of 2019, among those with a hypertension diagnosis, 57% (<140/90 mmHg) or 19% (<130/80 mmHg) had controlled blood pressure depending on the threshold used. The point prevalence of treatment-resistant hypertension ranged from <1% to 17% depending on definition and was associated with older age, higher body mass index, and multiple comorbidities including type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease.

CONCLUSION: Blood pressure control remains a major clinical challenge, with fewer than one in five patients with a hypertension diagnosis achieving <130/80 mmHg. The prevalence of treatment-resistant hypertension varied widely depending on the definition used and was closely associated with a greater burden of comorbidities, indicating an unmet need for improved strategies for this clinically challenging subgroup.

articles.title: Influencing factors analysis and prediction model development for ROSC in adult non-traumatic OHCA: a retrospective study based on pre-hospital emergency settings.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac arrest is a major global public health problem. This study aimed to explore factors influencing return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) and develop a prediction model for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients.

METHODS: We retrospectively collected electronic medical records of adult non-traumatic OHCA patients at Tianjin Emergency Medical Center from January 1, 2023 to December 31, 2024. The primary outcome was sustained ROSC up to emergency department arrival and handover to receiving-hospital staff. Multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression with clinician ID as random intercept adjusted clustering bias; predictors with p < 0.05 formed the nomogram. Patients were randomly split 7:3 for training and internal testing. Discrimination was assessed by ROC-AUC (acceptable threshold >0.7). We performed 1000 bootstrap resampling to correct C-index against overfitting. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA) further evaluated predictive consistency and net clinical benefit.

RESULTS: Among 9,386 included cases, 678 (7.2%) achieved ROSC. Mixed-effects regression identified independent ROSC predictors: public location (aOR = 1.285, 95% CI:1.038-1.592), 06:00-12:00 onset (aOR = 1.308, 95% CI:1.018-1.682), prolonged emergency response time (aOR = 0.971, 95% CI:0.945-0.999), extended onset-to-ambulance intervals (5-10 min: aOR = 0.758;10-30 min: aOR = 0.578;>30 min:aOR = 0.498 vs ≤5 min), no OHCA occurred at emergency call (aOR = 1.540, 95% CI:1.048-2.262), male attending physicians (aOR = 1.255, 95% CI:1.077-1.464), longer physician practice years (aOR = 1.043, 95%CI: 1.022-1.065), intermediate physician title (aOR = 1.236, 95% CI:1.047-1.459), shockable initial rhythm (aOR = 2.850, 95% CI:2.390-3.397), endotracheal intubation (aOR = 2.294, 95% CI:1.936-2.718), epinephrine >5 mg (aOR = 0.765,95% CI:0.626-0.935). The nomogram AUC reached 0.775 (95% CI:0.756-0.794) in the training set and 0.775 (95% CI:0.745-0.805) in the test set; 1000 bootstrap internal validation gave an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.7679 with minimal optimism of 0.0071, showing negligible overfitting, good calibration and favorable net clinical benefit via DCA.

CONCLUSION: This study identified multiple factors significantly associated with ROSC in OHCA patients; the constructed model showed good predictive value.

articles.title: Hemocytometric Parameters Associated with Bacterial and Viral Etiology in COPD Exacerbations: An Exploratory Analysis.

Intermittent theta-burst stimulation versus sham stimulation for suicidal ideation and psychiatric symptoms in depressive disorders: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences
articles.abstract: Suicidal ideation, depressive symptoms, anxiety, and sleep disturbance remain difficult to manage in psychiatric populations, and intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) has emerged as an accelerated, non-invasive neuromodulation strategy for these outcomes. This meta-analysis compares iTBS versus sham-iTBS across suicidal ideation, depression severity, anxiety severity, and sleep quality to guide clinical decision-making. We systematically searched relevant electronic databases in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Continuous outcomes were pooled as standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals using random-effects inverse-variance models in RevMan 5.4. Heterogeneity was assessed using I 2 and χ 2 statistics, and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed. A p value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Six studies were included. iTBS significantly reduced suicidal ideation versus sham-iTBS (SMD = -0.51; 95% CI: -0.93 to -0.09; p = 0.02; I 2 = 70%; n = 181 vs. 157), and the effect remained significant with lower heterogeneity after exclusion of Qin et al. (p = 0.02; I 2 = 29%). Depression severity improved with iTBS (SMD = -1.06; 95% CI: -1.64 to -0.48; p = 0.0003; I 2 = 80%; n = 162 vs. 142), with heterogeneity decreasing to 24% after exclusion of Huang et al. Anxiety severity also improved (SMD = -0.68; 95% CI: -1.27 to -0.09; p = 0.02; I 2 = 79%; n = 139 vs. 120), and heterogeneity decreased to 38% after exclusion of Huang et al. Sleep quality did not differ significantly between groups (SMD = -0.32; 95% CI: -0.98 to 0.34; p = 0.35; I 2 = 67%; n = 75 vs. 49), based on two trials. iTBS was associated with a reduction in suicidal ideation compared with sham stimulation, but the small evidence base and between-study heterogeneity limit certainty. Secondary analyses suggested improvements in depression and anxiety severity, whereas sleep quality did not differ between groups. Larger, standardized randomized controlled trials with longer follow-up are needed to determine the magnitude and durability of any antisuicidal effect.

articles.title: Does chronic occupational demand alter EEG stress biomarkers during cognitive challenge? a study of emergency physicians.
articles.abstract: Acute cognitive challenge produces consistent changes in several EEG indices, including alpha-band desynchronization, frontocentral theta enhancement, beta-band activity, and the theta/beta ratio. These measures serve as common biomarkers of cognitive workload and stress. It is not yet clear whether chronic occupational exposure to high cognitive demand alters these responses. Emergency physicians offer a useful test case, since their work involves repeated cognitive control under time pressure and high-stakes decision-making. We recorded 19-channel electroencephalography from 17 board-certified emergency physicians and 18 non-healthcare comparison participants during eyes-open rest and a standardized composite challenge combining Stroop interference, serial subtraction, time pressure, and evaluative feedback. Spectral power was estimated with Welch's method, log-transformed, and analyzed using a hierarchical framework combining six a priori regional features with electrode-wise topographic mapping. Across groups, the challenge produced robust frontal and posterior alpha suppression and increased frontocentral theta, consistent with workload-related cortical engagement. No Group x Condition interaction survived false discovery rate correction for the regional features, and no exploratory electrode-wise interaction survived correction across the full feature set. A complementary Bayesian analysis yielded moderate evidence for the null for the alpha and theta features, but inconclusive evidence for the beta and theta/beta features. Sub-band decomposition showed the challenge-related beta increase was specific to high beta (20-30 Hz), while low and mid beta decreased in emergency physicians. These results indicate an absence of detectable large group differences in EEG stress biomarkers following prolonged occupational exposure to high cognitive demand, although the sample constrains this conclusion to large effects.

articles.title: Clinical, economic, and health-related quality of life impact of intrapartum group B Streptococcus (GBS) tests for prevention of neonatal GBS infection: a systematic literature review.
articles.journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) contributes majorly to neonatal morbidity and mortality. Although antenatal culture screening and risk-based intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis (IAP) reduce neonatal early-onset GBS (EOGBS) compared to no screening, limitations hinder further reduction of EOGBS incidence. Point-of-care polymerase chain reaction (PCR) tests can address these limitations and offer an alternative to detect intrapartum GBS colonization in near-patient settings. Despite European clinical consensus recommending PCR-based intrapartum screening, adoption remains limited, partly due to lack of health economic evidence. This systematic literature review (SLR) evaluated the clinical effectiveness and economic impact of GBS tests for intrapartum screening, and the health-related quality of life (HRQoL) associated with EOGBS.

METHODS: Systematic searches were conducted on 19 March 2025 in Embase®, MEDLINE®, EBM Reviews, and EconLit® via OVID SP®, without geographic restriction. Eligible studies included pregnant women undergoing intrapartum GBS screening compared with intrapartum culture as the reference standard. Two reviewers independently screened studies using pre-defined eligibility criteria; a third resolved discrepancies. Study quality was appraised using Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy studies tool for clinical studies and Drummond and Jefferson checklist for economic studies. Sixty-six studies were included: 38 clinical, 17 economic, and 11 HRQoL/utility.

RESULTS: Clinical evidence demonstrated that intrapartum PCR tests provide high diagnostic accuracy and operational reliability by delivering results in <60 min (significantly faster than antenatal cultures). Four assays (Xpert® GBS, Revogene® DBS GS, GenomEra®, and IDI-Strep B™) met the European clinical expert consensus criteria for reliable and effective intrapartum GBS screening (≥90% sensitivity and ≥95% specificity) in at least one study; only Xpert® GBS met these criteria in more than one study. Economic evidence indicated potential cost-neutrality or savings with intrapartum PCR, compared with antepartum culture. Higher PCR test costs were offset by cost-savings from reduced EOGBS cases and associated resource utilization (e.g. hospitalization/neonatal intensive care, treatment, long-term sequelae), in some studies resulting in dominant ICERs in cost-effectiveness analyses. HRQoL studies reported considerable risk of physical impairment due to long-term sequelae among neonates surviving EOGBS.

CONCLUSION: Point-of-care intrapartum PCR-based screening methods offer potential to improve prevention strategies for neonatal infection and reduce the clinical, economic, and HRQoL burden of GBS disease. Limited primary HRQoL evidence highlights the need for further research.

articles.title: Exploring undergraduates' knowledge, attitude, and perception of male infertility in Osun State University: a mixed method study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infertility has traditionally been seen as a female problem, causing misconceptions, stigma, and limited attention to male infertility. This study examined undergraduates' knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions of male infertility at Osun State University, Nigeria, and associated factors.

METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional mixed-methods design was used. Quantitative data came from 300 undergraduates selected by multistage sampling using a self-administered questionnaire; qualitative data came from focus group discussions. Quantitative analysis used IBM SPSS Statistics 27; qualitative analysis used thematic analysis in NVivo. Findings were integrated through a joint display matrix and narrative synthesis.

RESULTS: The mean knowledge score was 7.12 ± 1.88, and the mean attitude score was 1.96 ± 1.12. Formal education on male infertility was a significant positive predictor of both knowledge (p < 0.001) and attitude (p < 0.001). Faculty affiliation (p = 0.009) and level of study (p = 0.012) were significantly associated with attitude scores. Qualitative findings showed functional understanding but culturally shaped attitudes involving marriage, masculinity, and gender roles, with women disproportionately blamed.

CONCLUSIONS: Understanding was moderate but incomplete. Formal education was a strong modifiable predictor. Comprehensive, gender-inclusive reproductive health education should be integrated into university curricula, with open dialogue to reduce stigma.

articles.title: Genome-wide CRISPR screens identify shared and context-specific regulators of podocyte resistance to oxidative injury.
articles.abstract: Podocyte injury is a convergent driver of glomerular disease progression, yet the genetic determinants that govern podocyte vulnerability to oxidative stress remain incompletely defined. Here, we performed genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 knockout screens in differentiated human podocytes exposed to two complementary injury models: Adriamycin (ADR), a clinically relevant inducer of podocyte damage, and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), a direct oxidative stress challenge. Human podocytes were transduced with a genome-wide sgRNA library, differentiated under non-permissive conditions and subjected to optimized stress conditions that imposed selective pressure while preserving library complexity. Across five independent replicates per condition, sequencing-based sgRNA profiling demonstrated high reproducibility, balanced library representation and clear treatment-specific selection. The ADR screen identified 819 depleted and 456 enriched genes, whereas the H2O2 screen identified 277 depleted and 215 enriched genes. Integrated analysis revealed both model-specific dependencies and 27 shared depleted genes across the two injury conditions, implicating stress adaptation, chromatin regulation, mitochondrial metabolism, inflammatory signaling and cytoskeletal organization as candidate processes required for podocyte survival. These genome-wide screens provide a functional framework for prioritizing genes that regulate podocyte resilience to oxidative injury and offer a resource for mechanistic studies of glomerular disease.

articles.title: Intelligent thermoregulation strategy versus routine thermal management on myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery during gastrointestinal tumor resection in elderly patients (SAGE): a multicenter, parallel-group, superiority trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inadvertent perioperative hypothermia is associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, but adequately powered trials using high-sensitivity troponin endpoints is lacking. The SAGE trial evaluates whether an intelligent, closed-loop thermoregulation strategy reduces myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery (MINS) in high-risk elderly patients.

METHODS: This prospective, multicenter, parallel-group, randomized controlled superiority trial conducted at seven tertiary hospitals in China. Participants aged ≥65 years scheduled for elective gastrointestinal tumor resection under general anesthesia are randomly assigned (1:1) to intelligent closed-loop warming (target 36.8 °C, upper limit 37.0 °C) or routine thermal management (active warming only if core temperature ≤35.5 °C). The primary outcome is the incidence of MINS within the first 2 postoperative days , adjudicated using high-sensitivity troponin thresholds per AHA criteria. Secondary outcomes include surgical site infection, transfusion requirement, hypothermia burden, emergence delirium, delayed emergence, and postoperative shivering. With 695 participants per group (total 1,390, accounting for 10% dropout), the trial has 80% power at a one-sided significance level of 0.05 to detect a 6 absolute percentage point reduction in MINS (12% to 6%) with a superiority margin of -2 percentage points.

DISCUSSION: The SAGE trial is designed to generate new evidence on the relationship between intraoperative hypothermia exposure and postoperative cardiovascular complications. It will evaluate whether closed-loop targeted normothermia reduces myocardial injury and will explore hypothermia exposure thresholds that may inform individualized perioperative management for geriatric surgical patients.

TRIAL ACRONYM: Intelligent Thermoregulation Strategy for Advanced-Age Elders undergoing gastrointestinal tumor resection (SAGE).

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR), identifier: ChiCTR2600117264. Registered on January 21, 2026 (http://www.chictr.org.cn).

articles.title: The long noncoding RNA MAPKAPK5-AS1 promotes the formation of hepatitis B virus cccDNA by modulating the expression of NABP1.
articles.abstract: Cellular long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) have been shown to participate in diverse biological pathways, including the regulation of virus infections. However, their functions in the hepatitis B virus (HBV) life cycle still need to be explored. Here, we conducted a loss-of-function screen targeting 1779 human lncRNAs and identified 19 lncRNAs associated with HBV infection. One lncRNA, named MAPKAPK5-AS1 (lnc-MAAS), was identified as a host factor required for HBV infection. Our data suggest that lnc-MAAS is involved in the conversion of HBV relaxed circular DNA into covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA). Furthermore, mechanistic experiments revealed that lnc-MAAS affects cccDNA formation by modulating the expression of nucleic acid binding protein 1 (NABP1). Together, our findings shed light on the roles of host lnc-MAAS and NABP1 in HBV cccDNA formation, which may contribute to the development of novel anti-HBV therapeutics.

articles.title: Statement of Retraction: High-frequency hearing loss in chronic kidney disease: a frequency-specific analysis across renal function stages.
Akabane virus reprograms the PKR‑eIF2α‑SGs/PBs axis to fine-tune cap-snatching efficiency.
articles.abstract: Akabane virus (AKAV) initiates transcription in the cytoplasm via the cap-snatching mechanism. Cytoplasmic host mRNAs act as the primary cap donors, whereas the impact of their subcellular localization on the cap-snatching process remains unclear. Herein, we demonstrate that the AKAV-induced disassembly of polysomes, stress granules (SGs), and processing bodies (PBs) collectively facilitates viral cap-snatching. Mechanistically, AKAV infection activates the PKR-eIF2α signaling axis, leading to the disassembly of polysomes and subsequent translational shutoff. Intriguingly, the viral N protein disassembles SGs and PBs by competing for sequestered RNAs within these granules, whereas mutations of its RNA-binding residues abolish this activity. Moreover, PKR-eIF2α inhibition impairs AKAV replication and cap-snatching efficacy. In contrast, inhibition of SGs via G3BP1 knockdown or chemical agents significantly enhances viral replication and cap-snatching efficiency, indicating that polysomes and SGs disassembly favor caps acquisition. Additionally, N protein-mediated PBs disassembly protects mRNA from degradation, and PBs inhibition enhances cap-snatching. Taken together, AKAV has evolved a sophisticated strategy to reprogram mRNA distribution to create an optimal cellular environment for viral cap-snatching.

articles.title: Re: "Prevalence and prognostic significance of untreated, uncontrolled and resistant hypertension among American adults with prediabetes" (Lin et al., Blood Pressure, 2026; DOI: 10.1080/08037051.2026.2698913).
Progress on the related mechanisms of vascular calcification in autogenous arteriovenous fistula in hemodialysis patients.
articles.abstract: Autologous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for end-stage renal disease patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis as a replacement therapy. As the duration of dialysis increases, the risk of vascular access-related complications such as AVF stenosis, thrombosis, vascular calcification (VC), and aneurysm formation gradually rises. Among these, VC has been proven to be independently associated with the occurrence and mortality of cardiovascular diseases in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). VC in the AVF of dialysis patients can lead to AVF failure, severely limiting its usability and increasing the risk of mortality among dialysis patients. Unlike previous reviews that predominantly focused on isolated mechanisms such as mineral metabolism or arterial calcification, this narrative review innovatively integrates the crosstalk among hemodynamic stress, inflammation, oxidative stress, deficiency of endogenous calcification inhibitors and pathological matrix remodeling, thereby providing a multidimensional perspective on AVF-VC. This review reframes the current understanding of AVF-VC, shifting it from a generalized complication of CKD-mineral and bone disorder to a distinct, fistula-specific pathological entity. This conceptual advancement offers a theoretical foundation for developing precision intervention strategies tailored to the unique microenvironment of the AVF.

articles.title: Single-cell transcriptomic atlas uncovers immune/structural lineage remodeling and fibrosis in Klebsiella pneumoniae-infected porcine lungs.
articles.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae (KP) is a predominant pathogen in respiratory infections, whose widespread antibiotic resistance poses severe public health risks and economic burdens. As the primary target of KP infection, the lung contains diverse immune cells, while pulmonary cellular responses to KP remain poorly understood. This study integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, RT-qPCR, and immunofluorescence to investigate porcine lung cell response from healthy pigs and those infected with multidrug-resistant, highly virulent KP. Post-infection, myeloid cells (neutrophils, monocytes, and interstitial macrophages) were rapidly activated with upregulated signatures related to neutrophil migration and interferon production. Alveolar macrophages (AM) exhibited marked heterogeneity: KP infection was associated with apoptosis in proliferating, monocyte-derived, and tissue-resident AM subsets, indicating a disruption of homeostasis, while infection-specific subsets (AM_MHCII, AM_CXCL2) displayed enhanced antigen presentation, inflammatory activity, and pro-fibrotic potential. Under homeostasis, γδ T and CD8αα+ T cells were the predominant T cell populations. After infection, CX3CR1-CD8αα+ T cells were activated, and CD8+ γδ T cells increased their interactions with myeloid cells, predominantly through ligand-receptor pairs such as TNF-TNFRSF1B and IFNG-IFNGR1/2. Furthermore, KP induced lung fibroblast proliferation and activation via the ROS-mediated TGF-β/SMAD pathway, WNT pathway, and aerobic glycolysis. Concurrently, infection reduced the proportion of ATII and transitional AT0 cells, which may impair their differentiation into ATI cells and compromise epithelial barrier function. Thus, this study is the first to characterize the dynamics of KP infection in porcine lungs at single-cell resolution. It advances our understanding of KP-host interactions and provides a framework for anti-KP therapeutic development.

articles.title: Knowledge‑Attitude‑Practice breastfeeding-based model is associated with better outcomes: a retrospective comparative study.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sustaining exclusive breastfeeding remains challenging, and integrated antenatal education targeting knowledge, attitudes, and practical skills may improve outcomes.

METHODS: This is a single-centre retrospective study. Women receiving conventional education (January-August 2024) were compared with women receiving a multicomponent knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP)-based breastfeeding education programme after its formal implementation (September 2024-June 2025). After 1:1 matching by maternal age, parity, and gestational age at enrolment, 640 women were included. Primary outcomes were KAP total score at 37-39 weeks of gestation and exclusive breastfeeding status at six months postpartum based on a structured 24-hour dietary recall; secondary outcomes included Breastfeeding Self-Efficacy Scale-Short Form (BSES-SF) score, early initiation, interim breastfeeding status, and lactation complications.

RESULTS: The matched cohort included 320 women per group. The multicomponent KAP-based programme group showed higher KAP scores (80.8 ± 5.6 vs 63.4 ± 6.9; p < .001), BSES-SF scores (58.2 ± 4.8 vs 48.6 ± 5.4; p < .001), and a higher prevalence of exclusive breastfeeding at six months based on 24-hour recall (55.9% vs 31.6%; p < .001). Early initiation was increased, while nipple pain, engorgement, and mastitis were reduced (all p < .01). Exposure to the multicomponent KAP-based programme was independently associated with exclusive breastfeeding status at six months based on 24-hour recall (aOR 2.84, 95% CI 1.98-4.07; p < .001).

CONCLUSIONS: Participation in a multicomponent KAP-based breastfeeding education programme was associated with better breastfeeding outcomes and fewer lactation complications. Multicentre studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Epidemiology, clinical profile, and outcomes of older patients with active cancer attending at Spanish emergency departments (EDEN-56 study).
articles.journal: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Older adults with active cancer are increasing, clinically complex emergency department (ED) population, but large multicenter European data are limited.

OBJECTIVE: To describe the epidemiology, baseline characteristics, diagnoses, and outcomes of older patients with active cancer attending Spanish EDs, and assess whether associations between active cancer and short-term outcomes varied with age and sex.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Secondary analysis of the Emergency Department and Elder Needs retrospective multicenter registry, including all patients aged greater than or equal to 65 years attending 52 Spanish EDs during 1-7 April 2019. Patients with and without active cancer were compared. Annualized incidence was extrapolated overall, by sex, and by age. Age-related patterns were modeled using restricted cubic splines.

OUTCOME AND ANALYSIS: ED length of stay, hospitalization, length of hospitalization, and index-episode death. Age-by-cancer and age-by-sex interactions were assessed in unadjusted and multivariable models.

MAIN RESULTS: Among 25 557 older ED patients, 4701 (18.4%) had active cancer. The estimated annualized incidence of ED presentations was 10 885 per 100 000 inhabitants aged greater than or equal to 65 years [95% confidence interval (CI): 10 576-11 200], higher in men (annualized rate ratio: 1.80, 95% CI: 1.70-1.91) and in the mid-to-late 80s. Patients with cancer had more severe comorbidity (58.9 vs. 12.9%), polypharmacy (26.6 vs. 21.3%), and walking handicaps (31.5 vs. 28.2%). Malignancy accounted for only 7.7% of ED diagnoses in the cancer group; infections, heart failure, and respiratory conditions were frequent. Active cancer was associated with longer median ED stay (4.0 vs. 3.3 h; adjusted difference: 0.3, 95% CI: 0.1-0.4), higher hospitalization [32.5 vs. 24.0%; adjusted odds ratio (OR): 1.34, 95% CI: 1.25-1.44], longer median hospitalization (7.5 vs. 6.9 days; adjusted difference: 0.5, 0.1-0.9), and higher index-episode mortality (5.5 vs. 2.5%; adjusted OR: 2.12, 95% CI: 1.81-2.50). Age significantly modified ED length of stay, hospitalization, and mortality, with significantly different age-related changes between patients with and without cancer. Among patients with cancer, age-related trajectories did not significantly differ by sex.

CONCLUSION: Active cancer is common among older ED patients and associated with substantial resource use and worse short-term outcomes. These associations vary with age, supporting multidimensional assessment beyond chronological age or cancer status alone.

articles.title: Developing a Comprehensive Model for Explaining Treatment Adherence Behaviour: Evidence From the International Beamer Consortium.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Optimizing treatment adherence behaviour has become a focus in healthcare, as improved adherence enhances clinical outcomes, patient experiences and health system sustainability. For this optimization endeavour scholars have posited diverse variables divided into two clusters. The first variable cluster emphasizes treatment priority, treatment concerns and health consciousness. The second variable cluster highlights acceptance, control and subjective health experience. Although some of these variables have been tested in isolation, few comprehensive models have been established. Therefore, this study aims at establishing a comprehensive model for explaining treatment adherence behaviour.

METHOD: An online questionnaire was administered to 4081 participants from six different countries. This questionnaire covered sample characteristics as well as instruments measuring health consciousness, treatment priority, treatment concerns, acceptance, control, subjective health experiences, medication compliance, health behaviour and treatment adherence behaviour. Data were analysed using descriptive, reliability, validity and model statistics.

RESULT: All concepts in the established model were measured reliably and showed sufficient validity. Most associations between concepts were stable and statistically significant across the overall and segmented models, except for those associating treatment concerns with adherence behaviour and control with subjective health experience in the previous month. The analysis shows that health consciousness is modestly to moderately positively associated with treatment adherence indirectly via 12 intermediary pathways, four of which were consistently significant, two were largely nonsignificant, and the remaining pathways exhibited mixed patterns. Between 22.6% and 38.5% of variance was explained by the models.

CONCLUSION: This model offers valuable insights into treatment adherence behaviour yet remains open to further refinement and development, either by striving for greater parsimony or by embracing relational complexity through data-driven machine learning approaches.

articles.title: Multifunctional hydrogel scaffolds for endogenous osteochondral regeneration.
articles.abstract: Osteochondral defects, frequently resulting from trauma, infection, or degenerative joint disease, present a significant clinical challenge due to their limited intrinsic healing capacity. Conventional cell-based therapies face limitations including immune rejection, high costs, and regulatory hurdles. Endogenous tissue engineering, which harnesses the body's own repair machinery through biomaterial-mediated recruitment and differentiation of host stem cells, offers a promising alternative. Hydrogel scaffolds, owing to their extracellular matrix-mimetic architecture, tunable physicochemical properties, and capacity for bioactive factor delivery, have emerged as versatile platforms for endogenous osteochondral regeneration. This review provides a strategic overview of hydrogel-based endogenous tissue engineering, covering: (1) the biological rationale for leveraging host cell sources; (2) the design of hydrogels as extracellular matrix -mimetic niches; (3) key regulatory factors; (4) innovative material design strategies. We also discuss current challenges related to long-term functionality, scaffold integration, and clinical translation, offering insights into the development of next-generation hydrogel systems for minimally invasive and effective osteochondral regeneration.

articles.title: Root canal microbiota in diabetic versus non-diabetic patients with apical periodontitis: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review aimed to evaluate the differences in root canal microbiota composition and microbial load between diabetic and non-diabetic individuals with apical periodontitis.

METHODS: Electronic searches were conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, the Cochrane Library and EBSCO up to 9 April 2026.Clinical studies using culture-dependent or molecular methods to identify microbial taxa in infected root canals of diabetic and non-diabetic individuals were included. Data on diabetes status, infection type, microbiological method, identified taxa, and quantitative microbial outcomes were extracted. Methodological quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tool.

RESULTS: Sixteen studies were included. Most used molecular methods, while few used culture or combined culture/molecular approaches. The studies varied in infection type, microbiological method, glycemic status reporting, and outcome metrics. Several studies reported differences in the prevalence or relative abundance of selected bacterial taxa in diabetic patients, including Peptostreptococcus spp., Porphyromonas gingivalis, Eubacterium infirmum, Enterococcus faecalis, Olsenella, Pseudoramibacter, and Fannyhessea. Fungal and archaeal findings were also reported in a limited number of studies. However, quantitative microbial findings could not be directly compared because different measures were used, including CFU counts, PCR-based detection, qPCR-derived bacterial counts, and sequencing-based relative abundance data.

CONCLUSION: Diabetes mellitus may be associated with differences in the reported endodontic microbial profile of teeth with apical periodontitis. However, the evidence is observational, clinically heterogeneous, and limited by small sample sizes, inconsistent glycemic reporting, and inadequate control of confounding factors.

articles.title: Comparative analysis of postoperative complications and 30-day readmissions after CABG in diabetic vs. non-diabetic patients: a nationwide readmissions database study.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus is a known risk factor for long-term adverse outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG); however, its impact on 30-day readmission is less characterized. This study aimed to compare 30-day readmission rates and index hospitalization outcomes between diabetic and non-diabetic patients undergoing CABG and to identify independent predictors of readmission.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the 2016 and 2017 Nationwide Readmissions Database (NRD). In keeping with HCUP guidance, each data year was analyzed as a separate sample rather than pooled. Adult patients undergoing CABG were identified in each year and stratified by diabetes status. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause readmission. Secondary outcomes included in-hospital mortality, length of stay (LOS), hospital charges, and complications. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression, adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, hospital, and comorbidity characteristics as well as index-hospitalization complications and discharge disposition, was used to identify independent risk factors for readmission.

RESULTS: In the 2016 (weighted N = 100,010) and 2017 (weighted N = 100,669) cohorts, diabetes was present in 47.7% and 48.9% of patients, respectively. In both years the 30-day readmission rate was higher among patients with diabetes (2016: 10.0% vs. 8.3%; 2017: 9.3% vs. 7.3%; both p < 0.001), corresponding to adjusted odds ratios of 1.14 (95% CI 1.07-1.22) in 2016 and 1.15 (95% CI 1.07-1.24) in 2017. In each year, patients with diabetes had more complex index hospitalizations, with longer stays, higher complication rates, and greater hospital charges. Non-home discharge was the strongest independent predictor of readmission in both years (OR 1.66 in 2016 and 1.67 in 2017), with anemia, congestive heart failure, and chronic pulmonary disease also independently associated.

CONCLUSION: In both the 2016 and 2017 cohorts, diabetes was independently associated with 30-day readmission after CABG, even after accounting for index complications and discharge disposition, and was accompanied by a greater comorbidity burden and postoperative complexity. The strong association with non-home discharge suggests that care transitions warrant further study. These findings identify a high-risk population that may benefit from enhanced discharge planning and close post-discharge monitoring, although whether such measures reduce readmission requires prospective evaluation.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40200-026-02103-2.
