articles.title: Diagnostic value of dual-time-point 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/computed tomography in differentiating benign and malignant extrahepatic bile duct occupying lesions.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the diagnostic value of dual-time-point 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/computed tomography (CT) in characterizing extrahepatic bile duct occupying lesions.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on 157 patients with suspected extrahepatic bile duct occupying lesions who underwent dual-time-point 18 F-FDG PET/CT at the Affiliated Hospital of Chengde Medical University between January 2021 and February 2026. According to lesion nature, patients were divided into a malignant group and a benign group. The Mann-Whitney U test and χ2 test were used to compare clinical characteristics, laboratory indices, PET parameters, and diagnostic efficacy between groups. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was used to identify independent risk factors for diagnosing extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. A logistic regression model was established based on the selected variables, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to evaluate diagnostic performance. A P value is less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: Among the 157 patients with suspected extrahepatic bile duct occupying lesions, 126 cases (80.2%) were malignant and 31 cases (19.8%) were benign. Compared with the benign group, the malignant group showed statistically significant differences in jaundice (yes/no), intrahepatic bile duct dilatation (yes/no), extrahepatic bile duct dilatation (yes/no), CA19-9, retention index, maximum standard uptake value, early lesion-to-liver ratio (LLR), and delayed LLR (all P  < 0.05). These variables were included in stepwise multivariate logistic regression to construct a regression equation. The area under the ROC curve was 0.912. The sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value of dual-time-point 18 F-FDG PET/CT for evaluating lesion nature were 95.10, 90.00, 85.10, 97.50, and 81.80%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Dual-time-point 18 F-FDG PET/CT combined with CA19-9 and jaundice (yes/no) has important value in diagnosing the nature of extrahepatic bile duct occupying lesions.

articles.title: Comment on: 'Health literacy and its role in promoting medication adherence among hypertension patients'.
Making the case for Paediatric Emergency Medicine in Europe.
articles.journal: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine

articles.title: Extracellular vesicles participate in proteostasis and heat shock adaptation in Plasmodium falciparum.
articles.abstract: Heat shock is a hallmark of clinical malaria, where Plasmodium falciparum parasites are exposed to recurrent febrile episodes exceeding 40 °C, which lead to acute proteotoxic stress. Parasite survival under these conditions relies on efficient proteostasis mechanisms and molecular chaperones, yet how stress resilience is coordinated beyond chaperone responses remains poorly understood.Here, we identify a stress-associated role for extracellular vesicles (EVs) in parasite heat shock adaptation linked to vesicular trafficking mediated by PfVps60, an Endosomal Sorting Complex Required for Transport (ESCRT) protein. Using a PfVps60 knockout (PfVps60KO) line, we show that disruption of ESCRT-dependent vesicular trafficking affects EV cargo composition during thermal stress. Proteomic profiling revealed that 44.8% of EV-associated proteins from P. falciparum 3D7 overlapped with a previously defined set of aggregation-prone proteins. Loss of PfVps60 impaired EV-mediated export of the chaperones PfHsp70-x and PfHsp110, altered aggregation dynamics and induced the redistribution of protein aggregates near the parasitophorous vacuole, reduced induction of the cytosolic chaperone PfHsp70-1, and resulted in early loss of parasite viability following heat shock. Supplementation of PfVps60KO parasites with EVs derived from heat-stressed 3D7 parasites partially rescued heat shock tolerance in a dose-dependent manner. EVs released shortly after thermal stress were enriched in aggregation-prone proteins and associated with neighbouring uninfected erythrocytes, suggesting EV-mediated intercellular communication during febrile episodes. Together, these findings support a role for EV-associated cargo as a previously unexplored component of P. falciparum proteostasis during heat shock adaptation, identifying stress-induced EVs as a potential parasite vulnerability for malaria intervention.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of intralesional versus intracoronary administration of glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitors during percutaneous coronary intervention for acute coronary syndromes: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intracoronary glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitors (GPIs) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) have shown better outcomes than intravenous administration. However, limited data exist comparing intracoronary versus intralesional GPI delivery during PCI for acute coronary syndromes (ACS).

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched for randomized controlled trials comparing intralesional and intracoronary GPI administration in ACS patients undergoing PCI. Odds ratios (ORs) and mean differences were used to combine dichotomous and continuous outcomes, respectively, using a random-effects model. Analyses were conducted in RevMan 5.4 and CRAN-R.

RESULTS: Nine randomized controlled trials comparing the intralesional ( n = 509) with intracoronary route ( n = 486) were included. In the primary analysis, the intralesional route demonstrated significantly better postprocedural thrombolysis in myocardial infarction (TIMI) grade 3 flow [OR = 2.38, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.52-3.72, P = 0.0001], corrected TIMI frame count (mean difference = -4.63, 95% CI = -8.83 to -0.43, P = 0.03), myocardial blush grade 3 (OR = 2.60, 95% CI = 1.51-4.49, P = 0.0006), and complete ST-segment resolution (OR = 1.64, 95% CI = 1.16-2.33, P = 0.005). After Hartung-Knapp restricted maximum likelihood adjustment, only TIMI grade 3 flow remained significant (OR = 2.38, 95% CI = 1.36-4.15, P = 0.009). No significant differences were observed in major adverse cardiovascular events, bleeding, or thrombocytopenia ( P > 0.05).

CONCLUSION: During PCI for ACS, intralesional GPI administration improves postprocedural TIMI grade 3 flow, with no significant differences in corrected TIMI frame count, complete ST-segment resolution, or hard clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Clinical inertia in the management of hypertension: a national survey of French general practitioners.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension remains a leading modifiable cardiovascular risk factor, yet blood pressure (BP) control in France and across Europe remains suboptimal. Although poor patient adherence is frequently cited, physician-related factors, particularly therapeutic inertia, may also contribute substantially. In this national survey, we assessed whether French general practitioners (GPs) have updated their perceptions of BP targets and treatment thresholds in the context of evolving European recommendations.

METHODS: Between May 2023 and December 2024, a structured questionnaire was administered by telephone to a representative sample of 503 French GPs. The findings were compared with those of a similar survey conducted in 2010 (SHARE study) in order to evaluate temporal changes in physicians' perceptions and clinical attitudes towards hypertension management.

RESULTS: Most respondents perceived current BP targets as overly stringent and estimated that most of their patients were adequately controlled. The reported BP thresholds for satisfaction (136/85 mmHg), concern (148/93 mmHg), and therapeutic intervention (166/101 mmHg) were strikingly similar to those observed in 2010, suggesting limited evolution in clinical perceptions despite increasingly stringent guideline recommendations. Younger physicians more frequently prioritised home BP monitoring and adopted lower treatment thresholds, whereas older GPs more commonly preferred office-based measurements and tolerated higher BP levels.

CONCLUSIONS: The limited evolution in GPs' perceptions over time suggests persistent therapeutic inertia in hypertension management. Targeted strategies to improve adherence to guideline-recommended BP control in this setting appear warranted.

articles.title: The effect of blood flow training restriction on endothelial function and arterial stiffness: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood flow restriction training (BFRT) is used to enhance low-load exercise, but vascular effects remain uncertain. We compared BFRT with matched non-BFRT exercise on endothelial function, arterial stiffness, and vascular structure.

METHODS: This PRISMA 2020 review was preregistered (PROSPERO CRD420251118357). PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and Chinese National Knowledge Infrastructure were searched on 2 October 2025, with systematic snowballing. Randomised parallel-group, crossover, or within-subject controlled trials were pooled using random-effects models (three-level or conventional) to estimate Hedges' g; subgroup/meta-regression examined moderators; RoB2, PEDro, and GRADE assessed study quality.

RESULTS: Thirty-five trials (n = 764) were included. Overall, BFRT showed no advantage for flow-mediated dilation (FMD; k = 30; g = -0.10) or pulse wave velocity (PWV; k = 32; g = -0.04); pooled effects were also non-significant for blood flow, AIx, CAVI, arterial diameter, and ankle-brachial index. Effects depended on protocol: resistance BFRT improved FMD (g = 0.56), whereas handgrip (g = -0.85) and some interval/aerobic BFRT reduced FMD; interventions <4 weeks decreased FMD (g = -0.69). Low-load BFRT reduced PWV versus high-load resistance training (g = -0.76). Age positively moderated FMD responses; certainty ranged from very low to moderate.

CONCLUSIONS: Evidence does not support a generalised vascular benefit of BFRT. Low-load resistance BFR may be most favourable, while small-muscle and moderate-to-high-intensity protocols warrant caution. Larger trials, especially in women and clinical populations, are needed.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence-driven Biomarker Discovery for Precision Psychiatry.
articles.journal: Clinical psychopharmacology and neuroscience : the official scientific journal of the Korean College of Neuropsychopharmacology
articles.abstract: Poor phenotype quality and small cohorts remain major constraints in psychiatric biomarker research, and recent methodological advances increasingly address them. Language models turn clinical text into analysable variables at a scale manual chart review cannot reach. Self-supervised models learn from the unlabelled signals psychiatry already collects. Variant-effect prediction makes molecular interpretation computable, and research agents have generated and experimentally confirmed candidates outside psychiatry. These capabilities act early, on what is measured, what can be learned from it and which candidates are proposed. None of the artificial intelligence capabilities reviewed here yet reaches the stages at which a candidate becomes a clinical test. Producing candidates is becoming cheap while qualifying them is not. This review is organised around that asymmetry rather than by disorder or marker catalogue. It separates the measured characteristic, the prediction model and the intended clinical use, and treats method family as distinct from evidential stage. Across the selected evidence, discrimination is supported more strongly in development data than in independent evaluation, and prospective evidence that model-guided use improves care is scarce. Many reported metrics also address a simpler task than the intended decision: diagnosis instead of differential diagnosis, general prognosis instead of differential treatment benefit. The review proposes a six-stage framework linking intended use, measurement validity, model evaluation, comparative utility and monitored deployment, and places each capability on it, clarifying where methodological progress can accelerate discovery and where conventional clinical validation remains indispensable.

articles.title: Intuitive knowledge of object acoustics enables perceptual separation of physical variables from impact sounds.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Upon hearing objects collide, humans can estimate physical attributes such as material and mass. Although the physics of sound generation is well established, the inverse problem that listeners solve-of inferring physical parameters from sound-remains poorly understood. Classical accounts posit the use of acoustic cues that correlate with physical variables but do not explain how humans might distinguish multiple concurrent physical causes. To study this problem, we measured impulse responses from hundreds of everyday objects, extracted their resonances, and used statistics of the resonances to build a probabilistic generative model of impact sounds. We then used the model to synthesize and manipulate stimuli for experiments measuring judgments of physical variables. Humans accurately judged object properties from collision sounds. However, when both of the colliding objects varied, performance was impaired if the distribution of object resonances deviated from those measured in real-world objects. The results suggest that humans have internalized the statistical regularities of real-world object acoustics, and use this knowledge to separate the acoustic contributions of the distinct objects in the world that give rise to sounds.

articles.title: From the Mailbox to the Microphone: The Neurology Podcast and the Evolution of Medical Education.
articles.abstract: When the Neurology® Podcast debuted in September 2007, podcasting occupied the fringes of academic medicine. Smartphones had only just emerged, and streaming audio was uncommon. Nearly 2 decades later, the Neurology Podcast stands among the longest-running physician-hosted podcasts in medicine and has fundamentally expanded how one of the world's leading neurology journals educates its readers. Although the technologies through which neurologists consume information have changed dramatically since 2007, the podcast's enduring success reflects a remarkably constant mission: to deliver practical, clinically relevant education through authentic conversation. This article traces the origins and evolution of the Neurology Podcast through archival documents, contemporaneous publications, and personal recollections from those who created it.

articles.title: Germline Genetic Variants and Epilepsy Surgery Response: Individual Participant Pooled Analysis of 272 Patients.
authors: Pediatric Epilepsy Research Consortium (PERC) Surgery Workgroup, and the Pediatric Epilepsy Research Consortium (PERC) Genetics Workgroup
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Genetic testing is increasingly used in presurgical evaluation, but the yield of resection and ablation across germline genetic epilepsies remains uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review of MEDLINE (PubMed) and Scopus and added cases from 3 institutional cohorts and the Pediatric Epilepsy Research Consortium (PERC) databases, including individuals with pathogenic/likely pathogenic germline variants besides tuberous sclerosis who underwent resection or laser ablation. Etiologies were grouped into biologically informed categories (GATORopathies, vascular, overgrowth, copy number variants (CNVs), channelopathies, synaptopathies, and other). Primary outcome was seizure freedom (Engel I) at the last follow-up. Group comparisons used Fisher exact and Kruskal-Wallis tests (α = 0.05; Bonferroni when applicable). Prespecified sensitivity analyses stratified by lesional status, excluded GATORopathies, and restricted to literature-only cases.

RESULTS: We included 224 literature cases (65 studies), 36 institutional cases, and 12 PERC cases (n = 272). The median follow-up was 24 months (interquartile range 12-48.0). Seizure freedom was achieved in vascular disorders 14/19 (73.6%), GATORopathies 79/120 (65.8%), CNVs 18/31 (58.0%), overgrowth 9/16 (56.6%), channelopathies 13/43 (30.0%), synaptopathies 4/18 (22.2%), and other 11/25 (44.0%) (overall p < 0.001). Among cases with available imaging results, 208/253 (82.2%) had epileptogenic MRI lesions, including 64% of channelopathies and 80% of the synaptopathies. In univariate contrasts (each category vs all others), odds of seizure freedom were higher for vascular disorders (2.64-fold, 95% CI 0.87-9.65) and GATORopathies (2.41-fold, 95% CI 1.44-4.09), and lower for synaptopathies (∼4.2-fold lower, OR 0.23, 95% CI 0.05-0.77) and channelopathies (∼4.5-fold lower, OR 0.22, 95% CI 0.09-0.48). Direction and magnitude were consistent across prespecified sensitivity analyses (lesional only, literature only, exclusion of GATORopathies).

DISCUSSION: Resective surgeries can be effective in germline genetic epilepsies, but outcomes vary by pathway. Disorders with discrete, lesional substrates (GATORopathies, vascular) show the highest likelihood of seizure freedom, whereas channelopathies and synaptopathies, despite the presence of MRI lesions, have substantially lower yields even in lesional cases. Prospective, genotype-aware surgical registries with standardized reporting (EEG, imaging, and pathology) and time-to-event outcomes are needed to refine the selection of surgical candidates and quantify seizure and non-seizure-related outcomes.

articles.title: Maternal and Fetal Safety Outcomes of Thrombolytics for Ischemic Stroke in Pregnancy: A Systematic Review and Aggregated Case Series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The safety of intravenous thrombolytics for ischemic stroke in pregnancy is largely unknown. We performed a systematic review to identify published use of thrombolytics for stroke during pregnancy, with the aim of assessing maternal and fetal safety outcomes. To provide additional safety data, we included cases of thrombolysis for deep vein thrombosis, mechanical valve thrombosis, and pulmonary embolism in pregnancy.

METHODS: We used the PRISMA and MOOSE guidelines to conduct the review. We searched 3 databases (OVID Medline, EMBASE, Scopus) for studies published up to October 2025. We analyzed outcomes in a Bayesian aggregated case series to compare rates of adverse outcomes in our cohort with those in the general population. Elective termination and spontaneous abortion were grouped together, given that it was often difficult to determine whether complications of thrombolysis may have played a role in the decision for termination.

RESULTS: We included 123 studies of 216 patients (median age 31 years) treated with thrombolytics during pregnancy, of whom 85 had ischemic stroke. Six of the 32 total fetal deaths were deemed likely to be causally related to thrombolytics (3 in stroke). The risk of miscarriage in our thrombolysis population was 12.4% higher (95% credible interval [CrI]: 2.6%, 23.2%) than published general pregnant population rates, and the risk of stillbirth was 5.9% higher (95% CrI: 1.6%, 12.7%). The proportion of pregnant patients with symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage was similar between our pregnant cohort and young, nonpregnant patients receiving thrombolytics (risk difference -0.4%; 95% CrI: -0.8%, 2.7%).

DISCUSSION: Thrombolytics were likely causally associated with a small minority of published cases of fetal death after thrombolysis in pregnancy. There was no signal of increased harm from thrombolysis to the mother, including similar rates of symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage. In many cases, it was difficult to discern effects of thrombolytics on fetal outcomes from the effects of the disease itself; hence, our results should be interpreted with caution. Nonetheless, our findings broadly support the use of thrombolytics in otherwise-eligible pregnant patients but underscore the importance of the risk-benefit assessment in such patients.

TRIAL REGISTRATION INFORMATION: The study protocol was pre-registered on PROSPERO (registration number: CRD42024605043).

articles.title: IV Thrombolysis in Maternal Stroke: It Should Still Be Considered.
Editors' Note: Endovascular Treatment in Acute Ischemic Stroke Due to Occlusion of Medium or Distal Vessels: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Author Response: Endovascular Treatment in Acute Ischemic Stroke Due to Occlusion of Medium or Distal Vessels: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

Establishing Potosi Virus as a Human Pathogen: Fatal Neuroinvasive Disease in a B-Cell-Depleted Patient.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To establish Potosi virus, a mosquito-borne member of the family Peribunyaviridae, as a neuroinvasive human pathogen.

METHODS: Case report.

RESULTS: A 37-year-old woman with multiple sclerosis on long-term rituximab developed rapidly progressive dementia. Serial MRI demonstrated progressive generalized atrophy. CSF showed transient, minimal lymphocytic pleocytosis. Extensive infectious, autoimmune, and prion evaluations were unrevealing, but CSF metagenomic sequencing detected all 3 genome segments for Potosi virus. Postmortem examination revealed diffuse meningoencephalitis with T-cell-predominant leptomeningeal and perivascular inflammation. Molecular analyses confirmed multiple nucleotide sequences with >99+% concordance with a known Potosi strain, with widespread viral infection confirmed by immunohistochemistry demonstrating intracellular and extracellular viral antigen. Electron microscopy demonstrated particles of a size consistent with the Peribunyaviridae family. Metagenomic sequencing of RNA extracted from frozen brain tissue identified all 3 Potosi virus gene segments without other infectious entities. Findings were concordant across multiple laboratories and institutions.

DISCUSSION: Potosi virus can cause fatal neuroinvasive disease in humans, as evidenced by convergent postmortem neuropathologic, molecular, and ultrastructural evidence. Chronic B-cell depletion may increase susceptibility to severe disease with arboviral infections, which may present without conventional CNS inflammatory markers. CSF metagenomic sequencing should be considered in immunocompromised patients with unexplained progressive neurologic decline.

articles.title: Resting-State Functional MRI and Clinical Outcomes After Acute Disorders of Consciousness: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Accurate assessment and prognostication of patients with acute disorders of consciousness (DoC) after severe brain injury remain a substantial clinical challenge. Resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) measures spontaneous, temporally correlated brain activity in the absence of external stimulation and provides objective insight into the integrity of large-scale neural networks that support brain function. Emerging evidence suggests that assessing neural integrity using rs-fMRI may improve outcome prediction in patients with acute DoC. This review summarizes the current evidence of rs-fMRI as an assessment tool during the acute phase of severe brain injury.

METHODS: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, we conducted a systematic literature search using MEDLINE and Embase databases from January 2006 to March 2026. Eligible studies included peer-reviewed empirical investigations of adult patients with acute DoC (<28 days postinjury) that examined associations between rs-fMRI measures and clinical outcomes. The systematic review protocol was registered in the PROSPERO International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420251085923).

RESULTS: Of 396 studies screened, 30 met eligibility criteria. Across these studies, a total of 800 patients (mean age = 48, 69% male) were scanned at a weighted average of 9.31 days after intensive care unit admission. Ten studies included patients exclusively with traumatic brain injury, 8 with cardiac arrest, 2 with encephalopathy, and 10 included mixed etiologies. The most frequently assessed resting-state networks were the default mode (n = 20) and executive control networks (n = 11), followed by visual (n = 6), salience (n = 6), sensorimotor (n = 6), and auditory (n = 5) networks. Across studies, significant associations between rs-fMRI measures and outcome were consistently reported, despite heterogeneity in methodology. The most commonly reported patient outcomes were functional or neurologic status, assessed at hospital discharge or between 3 and 12 months postinjury.

DISCUSSION: Current evidence consistently demonstrates that rs-fMRI acquired during the acute phase of brain injury is associated with neurologic and functional outcomes in patients with DoC. In addition, rs-fMRI may help identify patients more likely to recover consciousness and achieve favorable functional outcomes by characterizing the integrity of large-scale brain networks. However, substantial heterogeneity and small sample sizes limit comparability across studies. Standardized acquisition and analysis frameworks, along with larger prospective studies, are needed to validate the clinical utility of rs-fMRI and support translation into an assessment tool after brain injury.

articles.title: Wearable Technology and Its Role in Neurologic Care: Emerging Issues in Neurology.
Pearls & Oy-sters: Beyond the Bone Marrow-VEXAS Syndrome Presenting as Subacute Encephalomyelitis.
articles.abstract: Vacuoles, E1 enzyme, X-linked, Autoinflammatory, Somatic (VEXAS) syndrome is an adult-onset autoinflammatory disease caused by acquired somatic UBA1 mutations, typically presenting with systemic inflammation and myelodysplastic syndrome. Although infrequent, neurologic manifestations can include peripheral neuropathy, stroke, or encephalopathy. Notably, spinal cord involvement remains poorly documented. Here, we present the case of a 70-year-old man with myelodysplastic syndrome and confirmed VEXAS (UBA1 p.Met41Thr) presenting with subacute ascending paresthesia, Lhermitte sign, and urinary hesitancy suggestive of myelopathy. 3T MRI demonstrated multifocal T2-hyperintense spinal cord and brain lesions, some with contrast enhancement, consistent with inflammatory encephalomyelitis. CSF analysis showed mild lymphocytic pleocytosis (33 cells/µL), elevated protein (55 mg/dL), and numerous CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands. Negative infectious PCR testing and the absence of aquaporin 4 and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibodies argued against infection or other inflammatory demyelinating condition. The patient received high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone (1 g/d for 3 days), resulting in rapid clinical improvement. Follow-up MRI performed 1 month after presentation showed resolution of contrast enhancement and partial disappearance of spinal T2 hyperintense lesions.

articles.title: Racial Disparity in Stroke and Chronic Kidney Disease Mortality Among Black Population in the United States (P12-14.002).
Blood-Based Biomarkers as Predictors of All-Cause Dementia: A 13-Year Follow-Up in the Whitehall II Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Blood-based biomarkers are strongly correlated with amyloid positivity in research settings, but their long-term performance in heterogeneous populations remains unclear. Our aim was to determine their long-term prediction accuracy for incident all-cause dementia on their own and when used alongside known risk factors in community-dwelling older adults.

METHODS: This was a retrospective study based on the UK Whitehall II longitudinal, population-based cohort study established in 1985 among civil servants that includes a clinical examination every 4-5 years. Blood samples stored at the 2013-2013 wave were assayed in 2024 for measures of amyloid-beta (Aβ) 42 and 40, glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament light (NfL), and phosphorylated tau protein 217 (p-tau217). Incident all-cause dementia, from 2012 to 2013 to 2025, was ascertained from linked medical records, and Cox regression was used to examine associations of biomarkers with dementia, followed by estimation of prediction statistics.

RESULTS: Of the 5,225 (27.2% female) participants (mean age in 2012-2013, 69.4 ± 5.7 years), 516 (30.0% female) had a dementia diagnosis over a 12.2-year median follow-up. Participants with values in the worst quartile of amyloid-beta 42 (Aβ42)/40 ratio (hazard ratio [HR] 1.88; 95% CI 1.57-2.24), p-tau217 (HR 3.74; 95% CI 3.12-4.50), NfL (HR 1.88; 95% CI 1.56-2.28), and GFAP (HR 2.25; 95% CI 1.87-2.72) had higher risk of dementia. The C-index for predicting dementia was highest for p-tau217 (0.693; 95% CI 0.672-0.714), lowest for Aβ42/40 ratio (0.587; 95% CI 0.566-0.608), and was 0.760 (0.738, 0.781) for all biomarkers together. Sensitivity (between 41.7% and 59.5%) and positive predictive value (between 16.4% and 23.5%) of all biomarkers were modest, but specificity (between 76.8% and 78.8%) and negative predictive value (92.3%-94.7%) were good. A second approach to prediction modeling showed a model containing sociodemographic, behavioral, and health-related risk factors to have a C-index of 0.765 (95% CI 0.746-0.785); adding all biomarkers to this model led to a C-index of 0.813 (95% CI 0.795-0.830).

DISCUSSION: The long-term predictive ability of blood-based biomarkers for incident dementia in community-dwelling older adults was modest due to poor sensitivity and similar to that of a model containing known risk factors.

articles.title: Beyond Clinical Outcomes: What Antidopaminergic Medications Teach Us About Causal Inference in Huntington Disease.
Antidopaminergic Medications and Clinical Outcomes in Huntington Disease: Evidence From the PROOF-HD Placebo-Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Antidopaminergic medications (ADMs), including vesicular monoamine transporter-2 (VMAT2) inhibitors and antipsychotics, are widely used to manage motor and psychiatric symptoms in Huntington disease (HD). Observational evidence suggests that ADM use may be associated with accelerated worsening of clinical outcome measures used in HD trials, but this relationship has not been examined in a controlled trial setting. We assessed the association between ADM exposure and longitudinal clinical outcomes in the Pridopidine's Outcome On Function in Huntington Disease (PROOF-HD) placebo arm.

METHODS: This post hoc analysis included placebo-arm participants from PROOF-HD (NCT04556656), a randomized controlled trial in adults with Total Functional Capacity (TFC) 7-13 and cytosine-adenine-guanine (CAG) ≥36. Participants were categorized as on-ADMs or off-ADMs based on concurrent medication use across the study period. Outcomes included TFC, composite Unified Huntington's Disease Rating Scale (cUHDRS), Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT), Stroop Word Reading (SWR), and Total Motor Score (TMS). Primary analyses used mixed-effects models for repeated measures, corroborated by propensity score weighting (PSW) and time-varying sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: Of 247 placebo-arm participants (mean age 52.6 years [SD 11.4]; 51% female), 135 (54.7%) were on-ADMs and 112 (45.3%) were off-ADMs. On-ADM participants demonstrated faster clinical decline across multiple outcome measures. Between-group differences in cUHDRS and TFC favored off-ADMs from weeks 39-78; at week 52, the difference in mean change was 0.66 (95% CI 0.31-1.01; p = 0.0002) for cUHDRS and 0.85 (95% CI 0.47-1.22; p < 0.0001) for TFC as compared with on-ADMs. Significant or directionally consistent findings for SDMT, SWR, and TMS emerged from week 39 onward. All TMS subdomain scores, except chorea, directionally favored off-ADMs at all visits. Antipsychotic-only, VMAT2 inhibitor-only, and higher-dose ADMs were each associated with greater clinical decline in cUHDRS and TFC as compared with off-ADMs. PSW-adjusted and time-varying analyses were directionally consistent with primary findings.

DISCUSSION: In this study of the PROOF-HD placebo arm, ADM use was associated with greater worsening across global, functional, cognitive, and motor outcome measures as compared with off-ADM participants. Residual confounding by disease severity cannot be fully excluded, although sensitivity analyses were directionally consistent. Taken together, ADM exposure, class, and dose should be systematically considered when designing and interpreting HD clinical trials.

TRIAL REGISTRATION INFORMATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04556656.

CLASSIFICATION OF EVIDENCE: This study provides Class II evidence that in patients with HD, the use of ADMs is associated with greater worsening across global, functional, cognitive, and motor outcome measures as compared with patients not on ADMs.

articles.title: Analyzing the Neurology Residency Matching Outcomes in the Texas STAR Database (P5-1.002).
Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation With Previous Intracranial Bleeding: Competing Adverse Events in a Nationwide Cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and previous intracranial bleeding are at high risk of ischemic and bleeding events, and the benefits and risks of oral anticoagulation (OAC) remain uncertain. We investigated competing risks of recurrent intracranial bleeding, ischemic stroke (IS), and death from other causes according to anticoagulation strategy.

METHODS: This nationwide Finnish cohort study using linked administrative registries included patients with first-ever AF diagnosed in 2010-2018 and intracranial bleeding at least 120 days earlier. Follow-up began 90 days after AF diagnosis. Patients were categorized as receiving direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), warfarin, or no OAC based on drug purchases. Warfarin users were further stratified by time in therapeutic range (TTR). Inverse probability of treatment weighting balanced baseline characteristics. Competing risks were analyzed using adjusted cumulative incidence functions and cause-specific Cox regression.

RESULTS: Among 1,502 patients (median age 78 years [IQR 71-85], 44% female, 41% with only traumatic intracranial bleeding), 15% received DOACs, 29% warfarin, and 56% no OAC. At 1 year, adjusted absolute risks of IS were 0.7%, 2.1%, and 4.1%; intracranial bleeding, 1.2%, 2.7%, and 1.9%; and death from other causes, 4.7%, 8.6%, and 14.7%, respectively. Compared with no OAC, DOAC use was associated with lower risks of IS (HR 0.17, 95% CI 0.04-0.71) and death (HR 0.20, 95% CI 0.09-0.46) without increased intracranial bleeding risk (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.19-2.50). Warfarin use was associated with lower risks of IS (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.26-0.93) and death (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.44-0.80), but increased intracranial bleeding risk (HR 1.85, 95% CI 1.01-3.41). Among warfarin users, TTR ≥70% was associated with lower risks of IS (HR 0.24, 95% CI 0.08-0.79) and death (HR 0.19, 95% CI 0.10-0.36); associations were attenuated with poorer or missing TTR.

DISCUSSION: In patients with AF and previous intracranial bleeding, OAC was associated with lower risks of IS and death. DOAC use was not associated with increased intracranial bleeding risk, whereas warfarin use was. Limited information on previous intracranial bleeding and potential residual confounding warrant cautious interpretation. These findings support individualized anticoagulation decisions in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Early Rhythm Control vs Usual Care After Acute Ischemic Stroke in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Early rhythm control reduces cardiovascular events in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF); however, its effectiveness in the setting of acute ischemic stroke remains uncertain. We aimed to examine whether early rhythm control after acute ischemic stroke is associated with a lower risk of recurrent stroke or systemic embolism (SE) in patients with AF.

METHODS: This nationwide cohort study used the DeSC-IQVIA integrated database, an administrative claims database covering approximately 16 million individuals in Japan. Adults hospitalized for acute ischemic stroke with AF present at admission between 2014 and 2025 were included. The exposure was initiation of rhythm control (antiarrhythmic drugs, catheter ablation, or electrical cardioversion) within 8 weeks of admission (early rhythm control) vs no initiation (usual care), assessed at a landmark. The primary outcome was hospitalization for recurrent ischemic stroke or SE. Secondary outcomes included major bleeding, heart failure (HF) hospitalization, and all-cause mortality. Baseline differences were adjusted using propensity score overlap weighting. Cause-specific hazard ratios (HRs), cumulative incidence with death as a competing risk, and risk differences at 5 years were estimated.

RESULTS: Among 14,355 patients who survived event-free through the 8-week landmark (median age, 83 years [IQR, 78-88]; 6,935 [48.3%] women), 268 (1.9%) received early rhythm control. During 23,583 person-years, early rhythm control was associated with a lower risk of stroke/SE (HR, 0.56; 95% CI 0.32-0.97; weighted 5-year cumulative incidence, 8.0% vs 13.8%; risk difference, -5.9 percentage points [95% CI -11.0 to 0.8]). Among secondary outcomes, no association was observed with major bleeding (HR, 1.44; 95% CI 0.74-2.82) or HF hospitalization (HR, 0.73; 95% CI 0.39-1.38); early rhythm control was associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR, 0.72; 95% CI 0.53-0.97). Results were consistent across landmark periods of 4-24 weeks.

DISCUSSION: In this nationwide cohort study, early rhythm control after acute ischemic stroke in patients with AF was associated with a reduced risk of recurrent stroke or SE. These findings suggest that early rhythm control may serve as an additional secondary prevention strategy for ischemic stroke, with flexible timing of initiation. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in randomized controlled trials.

articles.title: Association Between Plasma N-Terminal Tau, Cognitive Decline, and Neurodegeneration in the ADNI Cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Blood-based biomarkers offer a cost-effective, minimally invasive alternative to neuroimaging and CSF biomarkers. Newly developed fluid biomarkers, including the N-terminal tau fragment (NT1), show promise for identifying individuals at risk for Alzheimer disease (AD) and for monitoring disease progression. Here, we determine whether NT1 levels are associated with key clinical and biomarker measures in a large, well-characterized cohort.

METHODS: Participants from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort with available plasma NT1, β-amyloid (Aβ)-PET, MRI, and clinical measures (Clinical Dementia Rating) were included in this observational study. NT1 was measured using the Quanterix Simoa HD-X platform. PET, MRI, clinical, and other plasma measures were obtained using established ADNI procedures. A subset also had NULISA-based plasma measures of amyloid and tau and tau-PET assessed. Linear regression and linear mixed-effects models were used to assess cross-sectional and longitudinal associations between NT1 and clinical or biomarker measures, adjusting for relevant covariates. Multivariable-adjusted Cox regression was performed to evaluate the association between baseline NT1 levels and risk of clinically diagnosed mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or AD. Mediation analysis was conducted to examine whether hippocampal atrophy mediates the relationship between NT1 and memory decline. Spearman correlations were used to examine continuous relationships between plasma NT1 and continuous fluid and neuroimaging markers.

RESULTS: A total of 755 participants (mean age: 72.9 [7.0], female: 375 [50%]) were included in the study. Plasma NT1 levels were elevated in MCI/AD individuals (BMCI/AD [SE] = 0.09 [0.022], p = 1.98 × 10-4) and were cross-sectionally associated with worse memory performance (B [SE] = -0.25 [0.09], p = 0.005). Aβ moderated the association between elevated NT1 and greater cognitive decline across multiple domains (memory: B [SE] = -0.17 [0.074], p = 0.022; executive function: B [SE] = -0.24 [0.082], p = 0.004; language: B [SE] = -0.21 [0.075], p = 0.006). NT1 levels were negatively associated with hippocampal volume (B [SE] = -264.49 [125.99], p = 0.036) and predicted longitudinal atrophy (B [SE] = -42.00 [16.90], p = 0.013). Accelerated hippocampal atrophy largely mediated the association between higher baseline NT1 level and greater memory decline (B [95% CI]indirect effect = -0.082 [-0.135 to -0.03], p = 0.003, B [95% CI]proportion mediated = 70.1% [32.6%-155.3%], p = 0.004). Higher NT1 levels were associated with higher levels of plasma biomarkers, including NULISA-based brain-derived (BD) plasma pTau (BD-pTau181, BD-pTau217, BD-pTau231: p's < 5.01 × 10-6) and Simoa-Based pTau181 (p < 4.51 × 10-15) and neurofilament light chain (p < 5.34 × 10-7).

DISCUSSION: Plasma NT1 may be useful in assessing amyloid-dependent cognitive decline and neurodegeneration.

articles.title: Association Between Systemic Fluoroquinolones and Risk of Peripheral Neuropathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Fluoroquinolone use has been associated with peripheral neuropathy in case reports, but there have been few noninterventional studies validating this association, and causality is unclear. The aim of this study was to estimate the association between systemic fluoroquinolone prescription and incident peripheral neuropathy relative to a comparator class of antibiotics, cephalosporins, using multiple databases to increase precision and assess the robustness of the results.

METHODS: Cohort studies were conducted using data from 2 databases of UK electronic primary care records, Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum and GOLD, from April 1, 1997, to December 31, 2019. Among adults (age ≥18 years) without diabetes mellitus or previously recorded peripheral neuropathy prescribed systemic fluoroquinolones or cephalosporins, hazard ratios were estimated between fluoroquinolone prescription and incident peripheral neuropathy within 60 days of prescription using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighted Cox regression. Hazard ratios were similarly estimated for a positive control outcome of incident tendon rupture within 60 days of prescription. Risk differences for peripheral neuropathy were estimated using a weighted Aalen-Johansen estimator. Estimates were pooled across databases using fixed-effects meta-analysis.

RESULTS: In total, 2,933,982 individuals prescribed fluoroquinolones or cephalosporins in Aurum (63.7% [n = 1,868,793] female; median age 49.5 years [interquartile range (IQR) 34.1-67.5]) and 995,457 in GOLD (63.5% [n = 632,033] female, median age 51.5 years [IQR 35.6-68.0]) were included. Of these individuals, at first treatment episode, 1,002,004 (34.2%) in Aurum and 381,734 (38.3%) in GOLD were prescribed fluoroquinolones. The estimated association between fluoroquinolones and peripheral neuropathy was close to the null at first treatment episode (pooled adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.96, 95% CI 0.77-1.20) and over all treatment episodes (pooled aHR 1.05, 95% CI 0.92-1.20). Hazard ratios were elevated for a positive control outcome of tendon rupture at first treatment episode (pooled aHR 1.98, 95% CI 1.55-2.53) and over all treatment episodes (1.76, 95% CI 1.52-2.04).

DISCUSSION: Findings were not indicative of a substantive difference in risk of peripheral neuropathy between those prescribed fluoroquinolones and cephalosporins. Potential residual confounding is a study limitation. Study results provide some reassurance to clinicians regarding risk of peripheral neuropathy with fluoroquinolones relative to a comparator antibiotic.

articles.title: Sequential syntax of EEG microstates captures the temporal dynamics of inhibitory control.
articles.abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG) microstates are successive global brain states whose temporal organization may reflect cognitive dynamics that conventional summary statistics do not capture. We applied a sequence-based framework, combining conditional successor analysis with multiple sequence alignment adapted from genomics, to microstate sequences recorded during a Go/NoGo task in 30 healthy adults. Generalized estimating equations showed no condition-level differences in standard microstate metrics. Conditional successor analysis identified three motifs enriched in the NoGo-early window (100-500 ms): A-C-D (p FDR = 0.013), B-A-D (p FDR = 0.029), and E-A-D (p FDR = 0.040), all passing through microstate A and ending in microstate D, consistent with fronto-central engagement. Multiple sequence alignment showed non-random temporal organization in all conditions (all z > 11.5 and p < 0.001). These results support sequence syntax as a framework for linking millisecond-scale brain dynamics to cognitive function.

articles.title: Oleoyl-L-carnitine regulates PPM1B through BIRC6, inducing tumor concomitant cardiac fibrosis.
articles.abstract: Cancer increases the risk of heart failure progression, and cancer survivors face elevated odds of adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Clinical observations link breast cancer severity to left ventricular diastolic dysfunction in patients undergoing surgical resection. Using metabolomic profiling of human breast cancer tissues and quantification in both patients and mouse models, we identified elevated levels of the tumor metabolite oleoyl-L-carnitine (OLcarn). Using affinity-enrichment proteomics with biotin-OLcarn in cardiac fibroblasts, we identified baculoviral IAP repeat-containing protein 6 (BIRC6) as a candidate interacting protein. Furthermore, binding of OLcarn to BIRC6 promoted ubiquitination of the protein phosphatase PPM1B and increased SMAD3 phosphorylation, thus activating pro-fibrotic signaling cascades. These results define a mechanism whereby a tumor-derived metabolite promotes cardiac fibrosis via the BIRC6/PPM1B/SMAD3 axis. This pathway reveals a key mode of tumor-heart crosstalk and may inform potential therapeutic strategies for cancer-associated cardiac fibrosis.

articles.title: Machine learning-based classification of healthcare-associated infections in rehabilitation settings.
articles.abstract: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) represent a challenge in rehabilitation settings, where prolonged stays and complex clinical conditions increase infection risk. This retrospective observational study applied a machine learning (ML) approach to classify HAI presence in patients undergoing rehabilitation. Cross-sectional surveillance data were collected at three time points across 22 facilities. An elastic-net logistic regression model was internally cross-validated on an initial cohort (2,966 patients) and temporally validated on an independent cohort (1,459 patients), with model interpretability assessed using SHAP analysis. Balanced accuracy was 72% and 74.5%, sensitivity 71% and 77%, and specificity 73% and 72% in internal and temporal external validation, respectively. Vascular and urinary catheterization emerged as the strongest predictors, while incontinence, pressure ulcers, and variables related to care setting and healthcare pathways showed additional contributions. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of ML-based HAI classification in rehabilitation and provide insights into infection-associated factors that may help prioritize prevention efforts.

articles.title: Osteopontin influences weight gain and immune cell composition during ART-treated chronic HIV infection.
articles.abstract: Despite the ability of antiretroviral therapy (ART) to effectively suppress but not cure, human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV), people with HIV (PWH) remain at increased risk for metabolic and inflammatory comorbidities that worsen with age. Here, we identify osteopontin (OPN) as a modulator of weight change in a humanized HIV-infected mouse model of ART-treated, chronic infection. Knockdown of OPN (OPNkd) completely abolished weight gain observed in untreated HIV-infected males. In contrast, untreated OPNkd females showed a 3-fold increase in body weight relative to OPN-expressing controls. ART-containing chow initiation was associated with an OPN-dependent 10% increase in female body weight despite a concurrent decrease in food intake. Longitudinal analyses revealed sex- and treatment-dependent shifts in myeloid and CD4+ T cell frequencies. Collectively, these findings highlight an undiscovered role for OPN, in interactions with other key study variables, in mediating immune and weight-related outcomes in chronic HIV infection.

articles.title: From epidemiology to mechanisms of inflammation in hypertensive cardiac damage.
articles.abstract: Hypertension-induced cardiac damage is a progressive, high-burden disease driven in part by immune mechanisms. We characterized global hypertensive heart disease (HHD) trends using GBD 2021 data, which revealed steadily rising prevalence and mortality. We next evaluated the associations between inflammatory indices and cardiovascular disease (CVD) in National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) data (2013-2018) with weighted logistic regression, validated by ordinal logistic regression and survival analyses. Neutrophil-to-platelet ratio (NPR), C-reactive protein (CRP)/high-density lipoprotein (HDL) ratio, systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), and neutrophil-to-monocyte-plus-lymphocyte ratio (NMLR) were independently associated with prevalent CVD among hypertensive individuals and had prognostic value for survival, suggesting utility for cardiovascular risk stratification. Transcriptomic and CIBERSORT analyses of hypertensive rat hearts revealed 830 dysregulated genes and distinct immune infiltration patterns. In an angiotensin II-induced murine model, validation confirmed cardiac dysfunction, elevated inflammation, and a pro-inflammatory macrophage shift. These findings link immune-inflammatory mechanisms to hypertension-induced cardiac damage and inform future risk assessment and therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: SARS-CoV-2 infection and genomic diversity in Quilombola communities during Brazil's gamma VOC wave.
articles.abstract: COVID-19 has disproportionately affected vulnerable populations worldwide; yet, data on SARS-CoV-2 transmission and variant diversity in Brazil's descendants of enslaved individuals, known as Quilombola, remain scarce. We conducted a cross-sectional study in Cachoeira, Bahia, in people seeking care, between February and March 2021, testing 700 oropharyngeal swabs by RT-qPCR and 591 plasma samples for IgM/IgG antibodies. Positive samples with Cq < 25 underwent genomic sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. SARS-CoV-2 infection burden was comparable between urban (31.4%) and rural (32.0%) zones in Quilombola communities. Genomic analysis of 39 sequences identified multiple lineages, predominantly the Gamma variant (P.1), with phylogenetic evidence of numerous introductions and both local and external transmission. These results reveal complex transmission dynamics and variant diversity within marginalized Quilombola populations, underscoring the need for targeted public health interventions, expanded diagnostic coverage, and prioritization of these communities in vaccination campaigns to address health inequities.

articles.title: ESX-5 paralog deletions in Mycobacterium tuberculosis alter macrophage cytokine signaling and bacterial heavy metal response.
articles.abstract: The ESX-5 secretion system is critical for Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) viability and pathogenesis. However, a functional understanding of its impact on the host is unknown. ESX-5 is encoded at a single site with small putative virulence paralogs (ESX-5a, ESX-5b, and ESX-5c) spaced throughout the genome. To examine host-pathogen interactions of these putative virulence clusters, we made deletion mutants lacking these paralogs and infected primary human macrophages. Independent infection with any deletion mutant led to reduced cytokine secretion. This defect was dependent on viable bacteria and is mediated by an unresolved post-transcriptional mechanism. In bacterial transcriptomic analyses, each mutant downregulated heavy metal response genes compared with the wild type. Treatment of wild-type Mtb with heavy metals led to increased ESX-5a and ESX-5c expression, driving concurrent TNF and IL-6 secretion in macrophages compared with untreated bacilli, indicating a putative link between ESX-5 cargo export and cellular cytokine levels.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Consensus recommendations for neurofibromatosis type 1 management in Asia Pacific" [iScience 29 (2026) 117002].
articles.abstract: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.1016/j.isci.2026.117002.].

articles.title: Kidney dysfunction under cardiometabolic stress promotes calorie-intake-independent wasting and frailty-like muscle phenotypes.
articles.abstract: Although age-related sarcopenia and frailty are linked to impaired metabolic flexibility and disrupted energy homeostasis, whether this framework explains chronic kidney disease (CKD)-related wasting remains unclear. We show that superimposed nephron loss redirects cardiometabolic stress from obesity and glucose intolerance toward calorie-intake-independent wasting with sarcopenic and physical frailty features. This switch was accompanied by impaired skeletal muscle glucose-utilization programs, a blunted glycemic response to gluconeogenic substrates, and altered hepatic-renal gluconeogenic programs. Integrated omics revealed suppressed glucose programs, impaired fatty acid utilization-related compensation, and amino acid catabolic signatures in skeletal muscle. Similar features occurred with aging plus nephron loss and in older human CKD kidneys with reduced renal PCK1 expression. Cornstarch-based nutritional modulation improved exercise capacity, muscle mass, and serum albumin, highlighting slow-release carbohydrate modulation as a potential therapeutic entry point. These findings support a model in which kidney dysfunction promotes wasting by limiting systemic metabolic reserve and skeletal muscle metabolic flexibility.

articles.title: Deficiency of peripheral serotonin caused by Tph1 abrogation attenuates cerebral malaria severity.
articles.abstract: In cerebral malaria (CM), the most severe neurological complication caused by Plasmodium falciparum infection, accumulating evidence suggests that tryptophan metabolism mediates disease severity by modulating inflammation and, consequently, blood-brain barrier disruption. Here, we have established an experimental CM mouse model to dissect the differential role of the host tryptophan-serotonin metabolic axis in regulating disease pathogenesis. Peripheral serotonin-deficient mice (Tph1 -/- ) displayed reduced mortality and blood-brain barrier permeability defects. In addition, we found that in the absence of serotonin synthesis via the enzyme Tph1, mice develop inflammation characterized by a mixed type 1 and type 2 cytokine signature. Pharmacological depletion of peripheral serotonin through injection of the Tph1 inhibitor telotristat in wild-type mice significantly improved resistance against CM. Thus, we propose that targeting serotonin synthesis through Tph1 antagonism could have a therapeutic role in P. falciparum infection and may act as a potential treatment strategy for CM.

articles.title: Intestinal epithelial Casd1 regulates mucus sialic acid O-acetylation and limits tissue damage from large-intestinal mucosal insults.
articles.abstract: Recent studies show that intestinal epithelial sialylation is essential for homeostasis, but whether this protection depends on sialic acid O-acetylation is unclear. CAS1 domain-containing protein 1 (Casd1) governs sialic acid O-acetylation, a natural inhibitor of sialidase activity. We hypothesized that epithelial mucin O-acetylation protects the colon by limiting sialidase-mediated mucus degradation and dysbiosis. Human MUC2 and murine Muc2 were richly O-acetylated, while intestinal epithelial-specific Casd1 deletion abolished mucin O-acetylation. Unexpectedly, intestinal epithelial cell (IEC) Casd1 -/- mice maintained normal mucus structure, barrier function, physiology, and overall Muc2 sialylation, with only subtle sex-specific microbiota changes. However, IEC Casd1 -/- mice developed significantly greater ulceration during dextran sulfate sodium colitis and increased cecal and distal colonic injury following Citrobacter rodentium infection despite equivalent pathogen burdens. Thus, epithelial sialic acid O-acetylation is dispensable for baseline mucus homeostasis but critically limits tissue damage during inflammatory and infectious insults.

articles.title: Adenoviral vector co-expressing ALDH1 and ADH1 mitigates alcohol toxicity and modulates glucose and lipid metabolism.
articles.abstract: Excessive alcohol consumption remains a global health concern, with ethanol and its toxic metabolite, acetaldehyde, causing significant physiological harm. Current hangover remedies fail to enhance alcohol metabolism at a fundamental level. In this study, we engineered a recombinant adenovirus, catalase 68-acetaldehyde dehydrogenase 1-alcohol dehydrogenase 1 (C68-ALDH1-ADH1), co-expressing dehydrogenases ALDH1 and ADH1 to improve alcohol metabolic capacity. In vitro and in vivo evaluations demonstrated that C68-ALDH1-ADH1 significantly reduced hepatic alcohol and acetaldehyde levels and alleviated liver injury. Overexpression of ALDH1 and ADH1 also improved glucose and lipid metabolism. Notably, the lipid metabolism related gene fatty acyl-CoA reductase 2 (FAR2) was found to be associated with ALDH1/ADH1 expression, linking it to alcohol detoxification and the fatty alcohol cycle. C68-ALDH1-ADH1 further ameliorated non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) through this pathway. These findings supported a potential protective effect of C68-ALDH1-ADH1 in treating alcohol-related disorders.

articles.title: Targeting TRP channels in hearing loss from mechanisms to otoprotection.
articles.abstract: Hearing loss, a highly prevalent global disease with complex pathogenic mechanisms, poses significant challenges due to limited treatment options and secondary complications. Recent research highlights the crucial roles of transient receptor potential (TRP) channels in auditory physiology and pathology, including cochlear electrophysiology, endolymph ionic homeostasis, neurotransmitter release, inflammation, and sensorineural injury responses. Although previous reviews synthesized TRP-mediated pathological mechanisms in hearing loss, clinical translation and otoprotective drug discovery remain underexplored. This review characterizes inner ear TRP spatiotemporal expression, traces the hair cell mechanoelectrical transduction (MET) channel research trajectory, details their dual regulatory mechanisms, and compiles emerging TRP-targeting otoprotective candidates. It further highlights limitations including restricted preclinical models, scarce otoprotective drugs, and limited target diversity among existing agents. Finally, it proposes new research directions for future basic and clinical studies on TRP channels and auditory function.

articles.title: Left atrial appendage occlusion versus antithrombotic therapy in nonvalvular AF with ASCVD and prior embolism.
articles.abstract: Managing nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and prior embolism is challenging. This retrospective study evaluated long-term outcomes of left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) compared with oral anticoagulation (OAC) and antiplatelet therapy (APT) in primary (n = 647) and external validation (n = 570) cohorts. The primary composite outcome included recurrent ischemic stroke or systemic embolism, major bleeding, and all-cause mortality. After inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), risks of the primary outcome, major bleeding, and mortality for LAAO were comparable with or lower than those of OAC and APT. For recurrent embolism, competing-risk analyses showed both OAC (SHR = 3.578, p = 0.003) and APT (SHR = 2.494, p = 0.040) carried a higher risk than LAAO. Results were consistent in the external validation cohort. These findings suggest LAAO may be a reasonable option for this high-risk population, offering a lower risk of recurrent embolism and comparable risk of major bleeding relative to pharmacological therapies.

articles.title: PP2A-dependent downregulation of GABAB receptors modulates somatostatin interneurons function and plasticity.
articles.abstract: Cortical circuits require precise inhibitory and excitatory neurotransmission to encode information and prevent pathology. Metabotropic GABAB receptors (GABABRs) are key inhibitory regulators in mammalian neurons. In GABAergic interneurons (INs), GABABR activation reduces inhibition, leading to disinhibitory mechanisms. Hippocampal somatostatin-expressing (SST) INs provide feedback inhibition to distal dendrites of principal cells (PCs) and other INs. Plasticity of SST INs is well established to control hippocampal circuit function dependent on metabotropic glutamate receptors (mGluRs) and GABABRs. Whether GABABRs regulate SST INs function over longer time scales and if this influences circuit function remains unclear. We combine quantitative freeze-fracture replica immunoelectron microscopy, ex vivo electrophysiology, and pharmacology to show that GABABR activation regulates long-term potentiation (LTP) of SST INs through protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A)-dependent loss of cell-surface GABABR, mGluR1α receptors, and Cav1.2 (L-type) Ca2+ channels. GABABR loss in SST INs shifts hippocampal activity toward greater plasticity of long-range inputs to CA1.

articles.title: β7-Integrin worsens diet-induced metabolic syndrome in mice by altering intestinal lipid handling and colonic inflammatory monocyte infiltration.
articles.abstract: Western diet (WD)-induced metabolic syndrome (MetS) involves obesity, insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, and low-grade inflammation. While β7 integrin-expressing adaptive immune cells contribute to WD-induced MetS, the role of β7 integrin in innate immunity remains unclear. To address this, the effect of antibody-mediated β7 integrin blockade or β7 integrin deficiency on WD-induced MetS was studied in recombination activating gene-2-deficient mice. Loss or inhibition of β7 integrin protected mice from WD-induced obesity, dyslipidemia, and glucose intolerance, partially via loss of β7 integrin-MAdCAM-1 interactions. β7 integrin deficiency altered intestinal lipid handling and monocyte infiltration into the colon and adipose tissue. Adoptive transfer confirmed that β7-expressing monocytes promote metabolic dysfunction in WD-fed recipients. Phospho-signaling analyses revealed attenuated PI3K-Akt pathway activation in β7 integrin-deficient colonic macrophages, and antibody treatments caused minor shifts in fecal microbiota profiles. Thus, β7 integrin-expressing innate immune cells drive WD-induced metabolic inflammation through monocyte recruitment, macrophage activation, and altered intestinal fat metabolism.

articles.title: Mucin-rich environment shapes Pseudomonas aeruginosa cytotoxicity and phage-mediated epithelial protection.
articles.abstract: Chronic respiratory diseases (CRDs) are characterized by excessive mucin accumulation that alters host-pathogen interactions within airway epithelia. Although bacteriophage therapy is increasingly considered as an alternative to antibiotics, it remains unclear how mucin-rich environments influence bacterial virulence and phage efficacy. Here, we show that exogenous mucin reshapes outcomes during Pseudomonas aeruginosa in epithelial cells. Mucin exposure induces transcriptional changes, increases epithelial susceptibility to bacterial cytotoxicity, and reduces bacterial adhesion and internalization. Surprisingly, mucin simultaneously enhances phage-mediated protection, preserving epithelial viability without impairing phage amplification. Moreover, prolonged bacterial exposure to mucin increases the cytotoxicity activity of cell-free secretomes, while altering the phenotypic and genotypic characteristics of phage-resistant bacteria. Together, these findings reveal that mucin-rich environments exert opposing effects on infection dynamics by increasing host vulnerability while enhancing phage-mediated control of bacterial infection. Our results highlight the mucosal environment as a key determinant of phage therapy outcomes and bacterial adaptation.

articles.title: Chitosan-stabilized electrospun nanofiber dressings with embedded flame-made nanosilver for the treatment of resistant infections.
articles.abstract: Wound healing can be severely compromised by infections, particularly those caused by antibiotic-resistant bacteria such as methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. We developed antibacterial wound dressings based on electrospun polyvinyl alcohol-chitosan nanofibers containing flame-made silver nanoparticles (Ag NPs). The 2-10 nm Ag NPs are embedded within ∼200 nm fibers, enabling a high and sustained Ag+ ion release with no detectable nanoparticle release, which may help mitigate concerns associated with nanoparticle exposure. Chitosan structurally stabilizes the fibers while modulating swelling and local pH to enhance Ag+ diffusion. The dressings achieved >99.9999% bacterial reduction in vitro and up to 99% ex vivo using freshly excised human skin. Crucially, the dressings maintained >90% viability of human keratinocytes and fibroblasts and showed no detectable impairment of short-term wound healing. This study introduces a scalable, safe-by-design nanofiber platform for infection-resistant and healing-compatible wound care and supports its further evaluation in preclinical studies.

articles.title: Vagal maneuvers and pharmacological cardioversion in stable PSVT: A systematic review with implications for emergency nursing practice.
articles.abstract: Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT) is a common arrhythmic emergency for which vagal maneuvers offer a non-pharmacological route to cardioversion before drug escalation. This systematic review compared the effectiveness and safety of vagal maneuvers-particularly the standard and modified Valsalva maneuvers-against pharmacological cardioversion in adults with stable PSVT. Following PRISMA 2020 guidance, eleven studies published between 2014 and 2024 were identified across six databases and synthesized narratively owing to clinical and methodological heterogeneity. The modified Valsalva maneuver consistently achieved higher cardioversion rates than the standard technique and carotid sinus massage, with a favorable safety profile, while adenosine remained effective but more frequently associated with recurrence and discomfort. Effectiveness varied by age, arrhythmia subtype, and care setting. Collectively, the evidence supports the modified Valsalva maneuver as a safe, low-cost, first-line option before pharmacological escalation, with particular relevance to nurse-led management in emergency and prehospital care.

articles.title: Diet-attributable vascular/metabolic disease burden comparisons and public health implications in Western Europe and North America.
articles.abstract: Ischemic heart disease (IHD), ischemic stroke (IS), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), and lower-extremity vascular disease are leading causes of disability in Western Europe and North America, but their diet-attributable burden remains unclear. Using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 data, we assessed the association between the Socio-demographic Index (SDI) and the vascular/metabolic disease burden and compared the cross-regional burden through multi-dimensional time-trend, risk contribution, and projection analyses. Mendelian randomization (MR) tested causal diet effects on disease subtypes. Frontier analysis showed diet-related IHD and IS burden declined with SDI, while T2DM increased. By 2023, Western Europe had a lower burden than North America. Processed meat and whole grain dominated T2DM and IHD burden, respectively. Joinpoint analysis revealed declining trends. Projections to 2035 indicated North America remains higher. MR identified several potential causal links. This study provides a basis for vascular/metabolic disease prevention policies and dietary interventions in Western Europe and North America.

articles.title: Periodontitis as a potential contributor to lung cancer: Epidemiological evidence, proposed mechanisms, and clinical implications.
articles.abstract: Periodontitis has been proposed as a potential contributor to lung cancer (LC), but the epidemiological, mechanistic, and clinical evidence remains heterogeneous. This structured narrative review evaluates the association between periodontitis and LC, the directness of proposed biological mechanisms, and the implications for risk assessment and supportive care. Observational studies generally report positive associations, although effect estimates vary according to periodontal ascertainment, study population, and adjustment for smoking. Clinically assessed periodontitis, self-reported or administrative diagnoses, tooth loss, periodontal-associated microbial markers, and general oral microbiome profiles represent distinct exposure domains and should not be interpreted interchangeably. The absence of a clear association among lifelong never smokers and the lack of supportive Mendelian randomization evidence further limit causal inference. Human studies demonstrate oral-lower airway microbial overlap, while experimental LC models support microbiota-related inflammatory and oncogenic signaling; however, periodontal origin, directional microbial transmission, and a continuous causal pathway from periodontitis to LC have not been established. Clinically, periodontitis should not modify current eligibility for low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) screening, and oral or respiratory microbiome biomarkers remain investigational. Perioperative oral care has comparatively stronger evidence for reducing postoperative pulmonary infectious complications, but this benefit should not be extrapolated to tumor recurrence or survival. Overall, current evidence supports an observational association and biological plausibility, whereas independent causality and an oncologic benefit of periodontal treatment remain unproven.

articles.title: Non-invasive glycemic control leveraging ultrasound dose window activation of MscL in diabetic mice.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes is characterized by impaired glucose homeostasis and progressive pancreatic β cell dysfunction, highlighting the need for externally controllable strategies for metabolic regulation. Here, we combined low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) with the mechanosensitive channel MscL-G22S to establish a tunable sonogenetic system for glucose regulation. Graded ultrasound stimulation was evaluated in MscL-G22S-expressing β cells and diabetic db/db mice to define an effective acoustic dose range. Within an intermediate dose window, LIPUS increased intracellular Ca2+ levels and glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in vitro and improved glycemic control, insulin sensitivity, islet morphology, and systemic metabolic profiles in vivo. Serum metabolomics further identified metabolic pathway alterations associated with combined LIPUS and MscL-G22S activation. These findings establish a quantitative framework for relating ultrasound dose to sonogenetic metabolic responses and support further investigation of ultrasound-controlled regulation of glucose homeostasis.

articles.title: IgM monoclonal antibodies reduce IgG-mediated antibody-dependent enhancement of Zika and dengue virus infectivity.
articles.abstract: Zika virus (ZIKV) is an arthropod-borne flavivirus endemic to Latin America, Africa, and Southeast Asia for which IgG-mediated antibody-dependent enhancement of infectivity (ADE) is a phenomenon of concern. The dynamics between flavivirus-specific antibodies of the IgG and IgM isotypes are mostly unknown. Here, we used DH1017.IgM, a previously described human-derived, pentameric, ultrapotent neutralizing ZIKV IgM monoclonal antibody (mAb) and a recombinantly produced IgM version of neutralizing EDE1 mAb C8 (C8.IgM) to assess if IgM antibodies can interfere with IgG-mediated ADE in vitro. Both mAbs consistently reduced IgG-mediated ADE across a panel of ZIKV-binding IgG mAbs in a dose-dependent manner. ADE mitigation was achieved at DH1017.IgM sub-neutralizing concentrations. C8.IgM also mitigated IgG-mediated ADE for ZIKV and dengue virus (DENV), demonstrating generalizability. Finally, DH1017.IgM confirmed inhibition of ADE at sub-neutralizing concentrations in sera of ZIKV-infected individuals. In conclusion, mAbs of the IgM isotype may potently counter the adverse effects of IgG-mediated ADE.

articles.title: Metabolic network restoration, not donor microbial engraftment, associates with resolution of recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection.
articles.abstract: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) effectively prevents recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection (rCDI). However, the mechanisms underpinning FMT efficacy are incompletely understood. We used proximity-ligation metagenomics, metaproteomics, and metabolomics to profile dynamic changes in rCDI. We analyzed samples collected from the first 7 responders during a clinical trial comparing two donor-based treatments (lyophilized FMT [LFMT] or lyophilized sterile fecal filtrate [LSFF], free of intact microorganisms) to prevent rCDI. LSFF is enriched in Caudoviricetes, lipids, fatty acids, and human and extracellular bacterial proteins compared with LFMT. LFMT recipients had donor microbial engraftment, while LSFF recipients achieved only partial microbial community recovery without donor's contribution. Our multi-omics analyses identified a functional convergence following both treatments, shifting away from oxidative and antibiotic stress survival pathways toward enhanced carbon-nitrogen utilization pathways, suggesting that FMT mechanisms may involve metabolic reprogramming and host-microbial amino acid co-metabolism. Our findings provide important hypothesis-generating insights that warrant further validation.

articles.title: Pharmacological AhR activation attenuates airway hyperresponsiveness and remodeling in a mixed allergen asthma model.
articles.abstract: Airway hyperresponsiveness and remodeling are major features of asthma. We investigated whether pharmacological activation of the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) modifies these responses in a mixed allergen (MA) mouse model of asthma. MA exposure increased airway resistance, contractility, inflammation, and remodeling, with elevated AhR expression in whole lung and airway smooth muscle but limited canonical AhR target gene activation. Treatment with the high-affinity AhR agonist 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin (TCDD) improved lung mechanics, reduced inflammatory cell and cytokine accumulation, attenuated airway remodeling, and decreased airway narrowing in precision-cut lung slices. Bulk lung RNA sequencing further showed suppression of inflammatory, neutrophil-associated, and remodeling pathways following TCDD treatment, together with induction of canonical AhR target genes. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that AhR activation suppresses inflammatory gene networks, limits airway remodeling, and improves airway mechanics in experimental asthma, supporting the therapeutic potential of targeting AhR signaling to mitigate airway dysfunction and structural remodeling.

articles.title: Generation of hypoimmunogenic cardiomyocytes from human induced pluripotent stem cells with TAPBP knockout.
articles.abstract: Immunological rejection is a challenge for the transplantation of cardiomyocytes (CMs) derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs). TAP-binding protein knockout (TAPBP-KO) hiPSC-derived CMs (hiPSC-CMs) were used to reduce human leukocyte antigen class I expression and their hypoimmunogenic potential was determined. TAPBP-KO hiPSC-CMs exhibited CM differentiation efficiency and functional properties comparable to those of controls. The immunological responses against cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) or natural killer cells (NK cells) were measured using the production of inflammatory cytokines, the expression of degranulation markers, and cell viability upon co-cultivation with hiPSC-CMs. The CTL-mediated cytotoxicity was lower in TAPBP-KO hiPSC-CMs than in controls. TAPBP-KO hiPSC-CMs did not induce cytotoxicity from NK cells. This approach can preclude immunological rejection from CTLs without initiating the innate immune response from NK cells, thereby expanding the access to cell therapy for patients with heart failure.

articles.title: StrokeTime: A comprehensive longitudinal scRNA-seq atlas of the ischemic mouse brain.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke triggers profound, dynamic changes in the brain's cellular landscape. To systematically characterize these dynamics, we integrated single-cell RNA-sequencing data from 21 mouse stroke studies (103 samples; 414,359 cells) spanning multiple models and post-stroke intervals. Using a harmonized computational workflow, we constructed StrokeTime, a single-cell mouse brain atlas covering hyperacute, acute, subacute, and chronic stages post-ischemia. The atlas contains 17 major cell classes and 120 fine-grained transcriptional states within myeloid, lymphoid, vascular, epithelial, neuronal, and glial populations. Myeloid cells showed the greatest plasticity, including disease-associated microglia/macrophage programs shared across resident and infiltrating cells, whereas lymphocytes featured activation and regulatory signatures within lineage constraints. Vascular and mural cells shifted from early inflammatory and barrier-disruptive programs to later fibrotic and angiogenic states. StrokeTime delineates both convergent and cell type-specific injury responses, offering a resource for studying post-ischemic brain immunity, tissue remodeling, and benchmarking future single-cell and single-nucleus studies of cerebrovascular disease.

articles.title: Stable truncating mutations in plakophilin-2 induce arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy-like phenotypes in adult zebrafish.
articles.abstract: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM) is an inherited cardiac disorder characterized by arrhythmias and fibrofatty myocardial remodeling, often leading to heart failure and sudden cardiac death. Mutations in plakophilin-2 (PKP2) represent the most prevalent genetic cause of ACM. Here, we establish zebrafish (Danio rerio) as a complementary vertebrate model for PKP2 mutation-based ACM. Comparative single-cell RNA-seq analyses revealed distinct cardiac expression patterns of PKP2 and its homologs across species. Using CRISPR-Cas9, we generated two truncating mutations in zebrafish pkp2, resulting in frameshifts and premature terminations (p.Glu250Glyfs∗17 and p.Glu31Glyfs∗72, respectively).
