Mutant zebrafish exhibited impaired cardiac contractility, arrhythmias, lipid accumulation on the ventricular surface, ultrastructural abnormalities of intercalated discs, and increased susceptibility to swimming exercise-induced sudden death. Transcriptomic analyses identified transcriptional alterations in genes involved in muscle contraction and lipid metabolism. Together, these data establish zebrafish as a useful complementary vertebrate model for studying PKP2-based ACM and gene-environment interactions underlying disease progression.

articles.title: Lactate-driven histone lactylation by AARS1 promotes pulmonary arterial hypertension.
articles.abstract: Glycolytic reprogramming drives lactate accumulation in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). We used a monocrotaline-induced rat PAH model and platelet-derived growth factor-BB (PDGF-BB)-stimulated pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs), together with oxamate intervention and molecular assays, to investigate lactate-mediated histone lactylation. PAH tissues exhibited increased lactate, MCT4, and histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la), accompanied by reduced HDAC1. Oxamate reversed these alterations and alleviated pulmonary vascular remodeling. Manipulating MCT4 expression modulated H3K18la levels. Upregulated alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1 (AARS1) displayed enhanced nuclear localization after lactate exposure; AARS1 depletion suppressed lactate-triggered H3K18la and PASMC proliferation. H3K18la was enriched at the Ctnnb1 promoter and correlated with enhanced Ctnnb1 transcription. These findings suggest that lactate may act as an epigenetic signal, linking glycolysis to Ctnnb1 activation through AARS1-associated H3K18la, thereby offering a potential target for PAH treatment.

articles.title: Proteomic and extracellular particle changes in preterm neonates with suspected late-onset sepsis.
articles.abstract: Neonatal sepsis remains an important cause of morbidity and mortality in neonates. In this prospective, multisite observational study, proteomics and extracellular particle analysis were performed on platelet-poor plasma from neonates at the point of clinical suspicion for sepsis (n = 110). Neonates were then classified by their clinical teams into three groups: culture-proven sepsis, culture-negative sepsis, or non-sepsis. Neonates with culture-proven sepsis demonstrated statistically significant differences in their analyzed proteome compared to neonates deemed to have non-sepsis, while those with culture-negative sepsis did not. Extracellular particle concentration and type, as determined by flow cytometry, did not differ between the three groups. This study provides further evidence that culture-proven sepsis and culture-negative sepsis are not equivalent diagnoses in the neonatal population without a consensus definition for sepsis. The proteins identified in the culture-positive group may be of utility in determining neonatal sepsis endotypes, but this would require further validation.

articles.title: Paleogenomics reveals leprosy at the late antique burial site of Fallward in northern Germany.
articles.abstract: The coastal settlement of Fallward in northwestern Germany (3rd-5th century CE) is renowned for exceptionally preserved wooden and textile grave goods, yet the genetic and pathogen landscape of its inhabitants has remained unstudied. We conducted metagenomic analyses on skeletal samples from 11 individuals to investigate their genetic affinities and infectious disease history. Three individuals yielded sufficient data for population genetic analysis: two clustered with northwestern European Iron Age and Anglo-Saxon groups, while one adult male might have originated from a Roman frontier population. This man was also infected with a strain of Mycobacterium leprae belonging to phylogenetic branch 4 and was buried in a boat accompanied by Roman-influenced grave goods, including carved furniture and a military belt. Together, these findings point to possible long-distance connections linking remote communities, such as Fallward, to the wider Roman world during Late Antiquity.

articles.title: Low-frequency parasitized cells in bone marrow alter myelopoiesis following immunization with the live attenuated Leishmania major Cen -/- vaccine.
articles.abstract: Leishmaniasis lacks an effective vaccine. We developed a live-attenuated Leishmania major Centrin-deficient strain (LmCen -/-) that is safe and protective in murine and canine models through IFN-γ-producing effector T cells. Because persistent low-level infection supports durable immunity, we investigated latent parasites and immune remodeling in the bone marrow. Dual single-cell RNA sequencing detected parasitized bone marrow cells 28 days after intradermal inoculation with either virulent LmWT or attenuated LmCen -/-. Flow cytometry showed increased myelopoiesis following LmCen -/- immunization compared with LmWT infection. Cell-cell communication analysis implicated enhanced granulin-Sort3 signaling as a potential driver of this response. Bone marrow monocytes from LmCen -/--immunized mice efficiently cleared virulent LmWT parasites in co-culture, consistent with the induction of trained innate immunity. These findings identify the bone marrow as an active site of anti-Leishmania immune programming and suggest that LmCen -/- vaccination promotes durable protection through coordinated adaptive and innate mechanisms.

articles.title: A hierarchical framework of representational emergence: From feature binding to supramodal emergence.
articles.abstract: Multisensory integration is traditionally conceptualized as transient, stimulus-driven feature binding. Here, we propose a hierarchical framework that reconceptualizes multisensory processing as a continuum of representational emergence across three distinct levels: level I (multimodal binding), where features are integrated via probabilistic causal inference; level II (supramodal representation), where recurrent co-activation and value-guided selection establish consolidated, perceptual-semantic engrams that act as emergent modalities; and level III (amodal concepts), where meaning becomes increasingly detached from sensory form and is represented within transmodal semantic networks. Drawing on recent mammalian evidence for cross-modal associative memory neurons and experience-dependent network reorganization, this framework proposes how local synaptic selection may scale into increasingly autonomous cognitive modules. Finally, we delineate an empirical roadmap and outline implications for supramodal AI, toward architectures capable of more autonomous semantic representation and generation.

articles.title: Single-cell-resolved dynamic immune remodeling following Omicron infection and recovery in vaccinated individuals.
articles.abstract: Breakthrough SARS-CoV-2 Omicron infections occur despite vaccination, yet post-infection immune recovery remains incompletely understood. Here, we performed longitudinal single-cell transcriptomic and targeted proteomic profiling of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from healthy individuals and vaccinated patients during infection, early recovery, and 3-month post-recovery. Omicron infection induced coordinated immune remodeling with contraction of T and B cell compartments; expansion of plasma, regulatory T, and dendritic cells; and suppression of inflammatory and metabolic pathways, including TNFα-NF-κB and mTORC1 signaling. Innate populations rebounded rapidly, whereas adaptive compartments recovered slowly with sustained suppression of IL-2, IL-12, and IL-15 modules. Chemokine surges (CXCL1, CXCL5, and CXCL8) resolved during convalescence, whereas selective cytokines (CCL5 and CCL8) and interleukins (IL-6, IL-18, and IL-24) persisted. Trajectory analysis revealed non-uniform remodeling of T cell states with persistent differentiation signatures across naive, effector, and memory compartments. Overall, vaccination tempered early immune collapse and accelerated innate rebound, highlighting interleukin-linked checkpoints and metabolic regulation underlying post-vaccination immune resilience.

articles.title: Evidence for climate-mediated range expansion of hybrid wood ants.
articles.abstract: Climate change challenges many species. To persist, species can shift ranges, respond plastically, and adapt, which all require variation. Hybridization can quickly increase genetic variation, potentially facilitating climate adaptation; however, it is unclear how hybrids respond to climatic changes. Here, we combine whole-genome, life-history, acute heat-shock, and climatic data of 69 wood ant populations across Finland to assess whether F. aquilonia × F. polyctena hybrids outperform their cold-adapted parent F. aquilonia in warming climates. Compared to F. aquilonia, hybrids are active and their offspring emerge earlier in spring, and they withstand acute temperatures relevant in nature better. Further, the hybrids' border has shifted 200 km northwards, coinciding with the expansion of climatic conditions suitable for hybrids. Our results provide evidence that hybrids have an adaptive advantage over F. aquilonia due to their admixed ancestry, and recent climatic changes can lead to range expansion of hybrids.

articles.title: Long COVID is associated with lipoxygenase-catalyzed metabolism of essential polyunsaturated fatty acids.
articles.abstract: Long COVID (LC) represents a failure of healthy resolution mechanisms for inflammation after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Dietary essential polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) and their downstream metabolites can orchestrate inflammation resolution, suggesting these pathways may be altered in LC. In this study, plasma samples from two independent participant cohorts totaling 106 participants (designated by chart review as LC or Recovered) were collected longitudinally in the 12 months following SARS-CoV-2 infection and analyzed by mass spectrometry for targeted PUFA metabolites. In the acute phase of SARS-CoV-2 infection, upregulation of PUFA metabolites downstream of 12-lipoxygenase was associated with later development of LC. In the months following infection, LC participants displayed uncoupling of PUFA-related lipid metabolism and altered lipoxygenase-driven metabolism over time compared to recovered participants. These results provide new mechanistic insights for the development of LC and suggest potential therapeutic strategies for this prevalent and debilitating disorder.

articles.title: Gammaherpesvirus infection of myeloid cells reveals divergent outcomes regulated by host and viral factors.
articles.abstract: The gammaherpesviruses establish a lifelong infection, with the cellular outcome of infection intimately regulated by cell type. Myeloid cells are an early infection target characterized by diverse outcomes. To investigate this, we use murine gammaherpesvirus 68 to demonstrate that macrophages are readily infectable, resulting in three divergent infection outcomes dictated by viral and host factors. Infection in vivo and in a cell culture model results in a high frequency of viable cells characterized by restricted viral transcription and unexpected transcription of the ORF75 locus, with rare cells initiating lytic replication. Restricted infection can be fully converted to productive lytic replication by pre-treatment with the host cytokine interleukin 4 (IL-4). Finally, infection with a high viral dose also results in productive infection, but it triggers increased cell death. These studies demonstrate stepwise regulation of virus infection and identify virus and host factors that dictate divergent outcomes in a single cell type.

articles.title: L-Histidine alleviates tacrolimus-induced islet dysfunction via the gut-pancreas axis.
articles.abstract: Tacrolimus is widely used after organ transplantation but can impair pancreatic β-cell function and glucose homeostasis. Using rodent models, antibiotic-mediated microbiota depletion, fecal microbiota transplantation, 16S rRNA sequencing, metabolomic profiling, and MIN-6 cells, we examined whether microbiota-associated L-histidine contributes to β-cell protection. Tacrolimus altered gut microbial composition and increased histidine-associated microbial and metabolic signals. L-histidine supplementation improved glucose tolerance and insulin secretion, reduced β-cell apoptosis, and increased PI3K/Akt/mTOR/p70S6K signaling and PDX-1, NeuroD1, and MafA expression. Microbiota depletion attenuated several protective effects of L-histidine, supporting a contribution of the gut microbiota to this response. These findings connect a microbiota-associated amino acid with tacrolimus-related β-cell dysfunction and provide a framework for investigating microbiota-metabolite contributions to metabolic complications of immunosuppression.

articles.title: Multi-omics characterization of white matter free water reveals genetic and vascular determinants of neurological disorders.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: White matter free water (FW-WM), quantified using diffusion MRI, reflects extracellular water content and microstructural alterations within water matter, but its genetic architecture and clinical relevance remain largely uncharted. We conducted a multi-omics study integrating 42,039 individuals from the UK Biobank and Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative cohorts to characterize tract-specific FW-WM across genetic, phenotypic, and proteomic dimensions. Genome-wide association analyses identified 27 independent loci and prioritized 88 genes, which were enriched in the genomic functional elements of vascular endothelial cells, pericytes, and astrocytes. Notably, 20 loci (74%) were novel compared to conventional white matter metrics. Both genetic predisposition to higher FW-WM and imaging-derived FW-WM were associated with a spectrum of neurological disorders. Specifically, imaging-derived FW-WM showed strong associations with stroke (OR = 3.14) and dementia (OR = 4.15), while higher baseline FW-WM predicted progression from MCI to AD (HR = 2.58). Bidirectional Mendelian randomization analyses further supported genetically predicted associations between hypertension and FW-WM, which were together associated with increased risks of stroke and cognitive impairment. Integrative proteomic analyses further nominated PEAR1 and ANGL3 as candidate proteins potentially linking hypertension-related vascular processes to FW-WM variation. Together, these findings provide a multi-omics characterization of FW-WM that connects genetic susceptibility, vascular factors, and neurological outcomes, supporting FW-WM as a tract-specific imaging phenotype with potential utility for neurological risk stratification.

articles.title: PPP1R1B differentially modulates alcohol intake and emotional comorbidity through distinct prefrontal circuits.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Excessive alcohol consumption frequently co-occurs with anxiety and depression in alcohol use disorder (AUD), yet the specific neural circuits and molecular mechanisms coordinating these comorbid conditions remain poorly defined. The medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), particularly its prelimbic (PL) and infralimbic (IL) subregions, projects to key reward and emotion centers like the nucleus accumbens (Nac) and basolateral amygdala (BLA), but the functional heterogeneity of these projections is unclear. Using chemogenetics, retrograde tracing, electrophysiology, spatial proteomics, and cell-type-specific gene editing in mice subjected to a 4-wk intermittent access to alcohol (IAA) paradigm, we selectively manipulated glutamatergic projections from the PL and IL to the Nac core, Nac shell, and BLA and assessed alcohol intake, anxiety-like, and depression-like behaviors. Chemogenetic activation of PL-Nac core projections reduced short-term alcohol intake, anxiety-, and depression-like behaviors, while IL-BLA activation decreased alcohol consumption and anxiety-like behaviors only. Retrograde tracing revealed mirror-image anatomical segregation of projection-defined neuronal subpopulations within PL/IL linking spatial organization to functional divergence. IAA induced pathway-specific synaptic adaptations. Spatial proteomics nominated protein phosphatase 1 regulatory subunit 1B (PPP1R1B) as a candidate molecule in PL-Nac core neurons. Independent immunostaining confirmed PPP1R1B downregulation, and circuit-specific knockout recapitulated alcohol-related and affective phenotypes, whereas overexpression reversed them. In IL-BLA neurons, PPP1R1B manipulation modulated alcohol intake and anxiety, but not depression. These findings define a subregion- and projection-specific organizational logic in the mPFC for differentially regulating alcohol consumption and emotional comorbidity, with PPP1R1B as a key molecular determinant. This provides a neural pathway-molecule framework for targeted intervention in AUD.

articles.title: Structural basis of hypervariable region 1 dynamics on HCV envelope glycoproteins in immune evasion.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: The hypervariable region 1 (HVR1) of the hepatitis C virus E1E2 glycoprotein plays a crucial role in immune evasion through rapid mutation and shielding of conserved neutralizing epitopes. Despite its important role, the structural properties of HVR1 remain poorly understood, particularly how its conformation influences shielding mechanisms and receptor recognition. To date in all published E1E2 or E2 structures, the C-terminal part of HVR1 (394 to 411) remains unresolved. Using neutralizing antibody (nAb) RM1-38, which targets C-terminal HVR1 (residues 399 to 409), we investigated the folding, positioning, flexibility, and shielding function of the RM1-38 epitope, or antigenic site 399 (AS399), on HVR1 by X-ray crystallography and negative-stain electron microscopy (nsEM). The crystal structure of RM1-38 Fab with the HVR1 AS399 peptide, combined with mutagenesis analysis, delineated the molecular basis of its strain-specific recognition and neutralization. nsEM and competition enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay revealed that HVR1 exhibits pronounced conformational flexibility even in the presence of other nAbs bound to E1E2. Virus neutralization assays using a combination of RM1-38 and broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) demonstrated antagonistic effects of RM1-38 with the bnAbs. Furthermore, RM1-38 reduced E1E2 binding to cells expressing the scavenger receptor SR-BI, an HVR1-dependent receptor, but did not affect binding to CD81 tetraspanin. Together, these findings support a model in which HVR1 functions as a dynamic shield, where its conformational plasticity contributes to both receptor engagement and evasion of humoral immunity in persistent infection.

articles.title: Genetic disruptions of Hsp90-encoding genes impacted short-term evolutionary trajectories of antifungal resistance in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
articles.abstract: Laboratory evolution has been a powerful approach to address questions about evolvability. It has been debated whether the molecular chaperone heat shock protein 90 (Hsp90) buffers or potentiates the effects of variation and, consequently, constrains or accelerates evolution. In this study, we experimentally evolved yeast strains carrying mutant alleles of Hsp90-encoding genes under mild clotrimazole selection. We found that knockout of HSC82, which encodes a constitutively expressed Hsp90 chaperone, led to slower evolution of clotrimazole resistance in the short term. However, all strains generally evolved resistance within seven transfers, regardless of Hsp90 status. Through whole-genome sequencing, we identified genetic changes associated with clotrimazole resistance, including prevalent mitochondrial genome loss, as well as chromosomal duplications and point mutations. HSC82 knockout populations specifically showed convergent chromosomal duplications of chrVIII and chrXV. Taken together, our results demonstrate that disruption of Hsp90 in yeast may not alter the overall outcome of evolution but may shape its evolutionary trajectories at both the phenotypic and genotypic levels.

articles.title: Validation of an open-source hardware for cardio-physiological studies in fish: A statistical equivalence study with a widely used research-grade electrophysiological recording system.
articles.abstract: Monitoring heart rate (fH) accurately is fundamental for fish eco-physiological studies. However, these measurements rely heavily on expensive experimental tools. Here, we aimed to validate BITalino, an inexpensive, open-hardware biosignal acquisition system for measuring fH that could help to democratize research in fish physiology. BITalino is a modular electrophysiological system with a dedicated electrocardiogram (ECG) module that records ECG signals through electrodes connected to the module via lead wires and attached directly to the subject. We compared BITalino with a widely used research-grade physiological recording system (BIOPAC) by measuring fH in fish using both devices simultaneously. Heart rate measurements did not differ significantly between devices, and there was no significant Device×Time interaction, indicating that both systems tracked temporal variation similarly. The intra-class correlation coefficient showed that 89.2% of the variance was due to biological differences between fish. These results confirm that BITalino can be effectively used for fH monitoring in fish physiology studies. Beyond its low cost, its portability, modular design, open-hardware architecture and compatibility with third-party analysis software make it easily adaptable for different experimental applications and may facilitate its use in resource-limited research settings.

articles.title: Corrigendum to 'Association between long-term air pollutant exposure and blood pressure and hypertension: A stratified analysis based on vitamin D status' [Environ. Res. 397 (2026) 127935].
Co-administration of empagliflozin and curcumin attenuates the development of MASLD by modulating lipid metabolism and adipose tissue browning in HFD-fed C57BL/6J mice.
articles.abstract: The increasing global incidence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) highlights the need for effective treatment strategies. This study investigated the combined effects of empagliflozin (EMPA), a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor, and curcumin (Cur), a natural polyphenol, on MASLD development in mice. Male C57BL/6J mice were fed a normal chow diet (NCD) or a high-fat diet (HFD) for 23 weeks. HFD-fed mice received EMPA, Cur, or their combination throughout the dietary intervention. Markers of lipid metabolism, thermogenesis, and oxidative stress were evaluated. In vivo adipose tissue browning was assessed via 18F-FDG PET/CT imaging. Co-administration of EMPA and Cur significantly attenuated body weight gain (p < 0.001 vs. HFD) and adipose tissue expansion without altering food intake. Glucose tolerance and hepatic AKT phosphorylation were markedly improved (p < 0.001). Hepatic TG content and MASLD Activity Score were substantially reduced (p < 0.001), accompanied by AMPK activation, FAS suppression, and CPT1A upregulation. Fecal TG content was elevated with combination treatment (p < 0.001 vs. HFD), indicating reduced intestinal lipid absorption. BAT thermogenic activity, confirmed by 18F-FDG PET/CT and cold tolerance testing, and sWAT browning were most pronounced in the combination group. Hepatic oxidative stress markers were most improved by the combination, accompanied by Nrf2 pathway activation. Co-administration of EMPA and Cur represents a multi-target approach for mitigating MASLD development. This effect entails comprehensive improvement of metabolic homeostasis, reduced hepatic steatosis, and increased systemic energy expenditure. Formal combination interaction analysis indicated synergistic effects across key metabolic endpoints.

articles.title: Statistical fragility in the meta-analytic evidence base of animal cognition: a meta-meta-analytic reappraisal.
articles.abstract: How reliable is the meta-analytic evidence base in animal cognition? We conducted a pre-registered second-order meta-analysis of 28 published meta-analytical papers, comprising 48 eligible models and 5740 effect-size observations from primary studies. We assessed statistical power, Type M magnitude error, and Type S sign error at both primary-study and meta-analysis levels. Because these quantities depend on the assumed underlying effect, we compared the results based on uncorrected pooled effects, a regression-based bias correction, and a sensitivity analysis using a bias-robust fixed-effect model incorporating a within-study variance-covariance matrix (FE+VCV). At the primary-study level, estimated power was low under all three empirically estimated effect proxies: 17.4%, 9.0%, and 13.4%, respectively. Type M and Type S errors were also sensitive to the assumed effect and correction method. Power increased when larger externally specified effects were assumed, confirming that these quantities are conditional on the assumed effect. Meta-analysis-level results were generally more favourable but also sensitive to analytical choices. The evidence base was concentrated in experimental rodent studies of learning and memory, limiting field-wide generalisation. These findings support improving study design and reporting within the represented literature while expanding meta-analytic coverage across taxa and cognitive domains.

articles.title: Data-centric, robust, and explainable multimodal deep learning for clinical decision support: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Multimodal deep learning is increasingly proposed for clinical decision support (CDS) under a "data-centric" framing that prioritizes label quality, missing-modality robustness, distribution shift, calibration, and explainability. Prior reviews have examined multimodal medical AI, CDS, and data-centric methods separately, but none address their intersection. We mapped the modalities, fusion strategies, and data-centric and explainability techniques used in this recent literature, quantified how often each is implemented rather than merely mentioned, assessed deployment-relevant evidence (external validation, clinical-outcome measurement, equity), and formally appraised study-level risk of bias.

METHODS: Following the PRISMA 2020 statement (PROSPERO CRD420261427815; registered retrospectively), we screened 150 records and included primary, clinical, multimodal studies that applied machine or deep learning to a decision-support task and reported at least one quantitative result. Two reviewers screened and extracted data with consensus adjudication. Each study was coded against pre-specified operational definitions, separating implemented or empirically evaluated techniques from those only mentioned. Study-level risk of bias was assessed with PROBAST + AI. Synthesis was narrative.

RESULTS: Thirty-one studies met inclusion; 30 (97%) were published between 2024 and 2026, with a median of three modalities (range 2-6), most commonly structured EHR (71%) and imaging (39%). Data-centric techniques were frequently reported (74-84% across label-noise, distribution-shift, calibration, missing-modality and class-imbalance handling; equity 61%). However, external validation was reported in only 4/31 studies (13%), a clinical or provider outcome in 3/31 (10%), and no study reported routine deployment. Overall risk of bias was high in 27/31 studies (87%), driven by the analysis domain.

CONCLUSION: Within this recent, self-selected slice of the field, technical robustness and explainability techniques are widely reported but rarely validated out-of-distribution or against clinical outcomes, and the underlying evidence is at high risk of bias. Progress requires external multi-site validation, clinical-outcome measurement, formal bias appraisal, and adherence to AI reporting standards (e.g., TRIPOD + AI) before deployment can be justified.

articles.title: Clinician-led, AI-assisted clinical software development: multi-domain verification of a deployed ePROM application.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Generative AI lowers the technical barrier to clinician-led software development, but functional success and usability do not establish clinical or technical assurance.

OBJECTIVE: To characterise defects that survived deployment in a clinician-built, AI-assisted ePROM application and the assurance activities that detected them.

METHODS: Single-case retrospective development-and-assurance report of STUIapp, a browser-accessible application integrating six validated lower urinary tract symptom instruments. Assurance comprised structured post-hoc code audit, independent clinical review of a frozen 78-case scoring matrix, WCAG 2.1 parameter measurement, a 23-canary persistent-storage study, formative usability evaluation with 14 clinicians, 26 patients and 12 older adults, preliminary MDR positioning, and targeted post-hoc requirements traceability across 926 attributable author messages with independent classification. Descriptive statistics only.

RESULTS: Mean SUS was 92.3 (SD 8.8) in clinicians and 92.0 (SD 10.8) in patients. Although all 78 original automated cases passed, independent review found 17 expected results requiring clinical or methodological correction. Technical findings included instrument mislabelling, a manifest that failed installability validation, and a third-party analytics tag contradicting the local-only privacy claim. Accessibility measurement found 10-px text and 2.56:1 contrast. Persistent-storage permission was denied in all browser-tab canaries (10/10) and granted in all installed canaries (13/13); no eviction was observed through 38.3 days. Home-screen addition was unaided in 7/12 older adults and 0/4 with limited smartphone use. Within selected defect classes, requirement traceability showed heterogeneous failure patterns.

CONCLUSIONS: Usability and functional success did not establish clinical correctness, privacy, standards-based accessibility or regulatory preparedness. These findings support independent, domain-specific assurance of both implementation and the clinical expectations and non-functional requirements encoded in clinician-led AI-assisted clinical software.

articles.title: Ultrafast and ultrasensitive electrochemical aptasensor for multiplexed monitoring of hemorrhagic transformation biomarker in acute ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Hemorrhagic transformation (HT) remains a life-threatening complication after acute ischemic stroke (AIS), yet no active predictive tool is available for early risk assessment. Herein, we develop an integrated triplex electrochemical aptasensing platform for the parallel and simultaneous quantification of three HT-associated biomarkers-matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9), fibronectin (FN), and plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1). The system enables parallel detection by inserting three independent screen-printed carbon electrodes (SPCEs) into a multi-channel electrochemical workstation, each functionalized with a distinct aptamer, allowing simultaneous quantification of MMP-9, FN, and PAI-1 within 30 min. Each SPCE is modified with a conductive polypyrrole/poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrene sulfonate/polyvinyl alcohol hydrogel and gold nanoparticles, followed by immobilization of specific thiolated aptamers via Au-S bonds. Upon target binding, aptamer conformational changes induce a concentration-dependent decrease in differential pulse voltammetry current. The sensor achieves ultralow detection limits of 4.04 fg/mL, 0.30 fg/mL, and 2.79 fg/mL for MMP-9, FN, and PAI-1, respectively, with a total assay time of 30 min. Clinical validation using plasma from 12 AIS patients demonstrates excellent agreement with enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (mean bias <10%) and high reproducibility (RSD <5%). This work presents the first electrochemical aptasensor for FN and PAI-1 detection and provides a clinically validated, point-of-care-compatible platform for personalized HT risk prediction in thrombolytic therapy.

articles.title: Serum brain-derived neurotrophic factor following oral esketamine in treatment-resistant depression: Results from a randomized placebo-controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ketamine and its enantiomer esketamine are efficacious in 30-35% of the patients with treatment-resistant depression (TRD). Increased serum brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) following treatment has been proposed as a potential biomarker of antidepressant response. This is based on studies evaluating single intravenous ketamine treatment. BDNF expression at different treatment schedules remains unclear.

METHODS: This study investigated the effects of daily, low-dose, oral (PO) esketamine on serum BDNF levels in TRD. Biomaterials were obtained from a randomized, placebo-controlled trial investigating six-week PO esketamine treatment (90 mg/day, three 30 mg intakes) that found no difference between conditions on the primary outcome (Hamilton Depression Rating Scale). Depression severity and serum BDNF levels were assessed in 54 patients at baseline, end of treatment, and after a four-week washout period. Repeated measures analyses of variance (ANOVA) were conducted to test the effect of treatment on depression severity and BDNF. Pearson's correlation analysis evaluated the association between changes in depression severity, ketamine metabolites and BDNF.

RESULTS: The change in BDNF levels during treatment did not significantly differ between the esketamine and placebo group during treatment or washout. An increase in BDNF (F(1,50) = 4.606, p = 0.037) was found irrespective of treatment condition. In the esketamine arm, BDNF changes did not correlate with changes in depression severity, nor with metabolites levels.

CONCLUSION: Repeated, low-dose, PO esketamine did not increase serum BDNF relative to placebo. While consistent with its limited clinical efficacy, it remains uncertain whether this reflects an unreached pharmacological threshold to engage synaptic plasticity.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness analysis and cost-utility analysis of a model of integrated mental health video consultations (PROVIDE-C randomised controlled trial) for people with depression and anxiety.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We conducted a health economic evaluation alongside the PROVIDE-C randomised controlled trial which analysed the effectiveness of a model of integrated mental health video consultations for people with depression and anxiety in primary care in Germany in comparison to treatment as usual (TAU).

METHODS: A cost-effectiveness (CEA) and cost-utility analysis (CUA) were performed six and twelve months after baseline from a societal perspective. Bootstrap procedure was applied and for each bootstrap replication, multiple imputation was conducted, and incremental costs and effects were estimated using generalised linear models.

RESULTS: In total 376 participants (18 to 81 years) with depression and/or anxiety were included in the analysis. We found that €3662 would be required for an additional person who experienced a clinically minimum important reduction of 5 points at the Patient Health Questionnaire Anxiety and Depression Scale (PHQ-ADS) and €1622 would be required for an additional person with a PHQ-ADS score below 10 points (persons with not more than mild symptom severity) six months after baseline. At twelve months after baseline, PROVIDE-C was dominant compared to TAU. While 6 months after baseline the probability of cost-effectiveness was approximately 36%, 40% and 56% in terms of quality adjusted life years (QALYs) for the respective willingness-to-pay threshold of €0, €20,000, and €100,000, at 12 months after baseline the respective probabilities of cost-effectiveness increased to approximately 71%, 78%, and 86%.

CONCLUSIONS: While the PROVIDE-C intervention is less likely cost-effective 6 months after baseline, it was likely cost-effective 12 months after baseline.

articles.title: Effectiveness of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation in alleviating postpartum blues following cesarean delivery: A randomized double-blind controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Postpartum blues (PPB) is considered a prodromal stage of postpartum depression. This randomized controlled trial evaluated the effectiveness of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) in alleviating PPB following cesarean delivery. One hundred participants were randomly assigned to receive active (n = 50) or sham (n = 50) taVNS over 5 days, with outcomes monitored through three months postpartum. The primary outcome demonstrated a significantly smaller increase in visual analogue scale scores, reflecting PPB severity, after the mood induction procedure in the active group than in the sham group on postpartum day 5 (median difference, 4.13 cm; 95% CI, 3.39-4.93; mixed-effects model, p < 0.001). The taVNS also significantly improved general postpartum mood on day 5, as assessed by Profile of Mood States (mixed-effects model, p < 0.001) and Stein Maternity Blues Scale (p < 0.001). At 1 month postpartum, the proportion of participants with Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale scores ≥13 was lower in the active group than in the sham group (4% vs. 26%; p = 0.003). Active taVNS also lowered postoperative pain scores at 4, 12, 24, 48, and 72 h (all p < 0.001) and improved sleep quality (assessed by the Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire) on postoperative days 1 to 4 (all p < 0.001). These findings indicated that a 5-day taVNS intervention mitigated PPB severity after cesarean delivery and were associated with improved general mood, lower rates of Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale scores ≥13 at 1 month postpartum, reduced acute postoperative pain, and improved sleep quality. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (https://www.chictr.org.cn/indexEN.html), ChiCTR2500108903.

articles.title: A personalised online parenting intervention for adolescents at high risk of affective disorders: Results from the UK PIPA randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depression and anxiety commonly emerge during adolescence and are associated with substantial personal, social, and economic burden. Parenting practices are well-established modifiable risk and protective factors for adolescent affective disorders, yet many parents lack access to evidence-based guidance. Digital parenting interventions offer a potentially scalable approach, but evidence for their effectiveness in high-risk adolescent populations remains limited.

METHODS: The PIPA Trial was a school-based, UK-wide, two-arm randomised controlled trial evaluating a personalised online parenting programme compared with a standard educational parenting package. Parent-adolescent dyads were eligible if adolescents aged 11-15 years scored ≥7 on the Short Mood and Feelings Questionnaire (SMFQ). The primary outcome was change in parent-reported adolescent depressive symptoms (SMFQ) from baseline to 15 months. Secondary outcomes included parenting practices, parent-child attachment, adolescent anxiety, wellbeing, and parent wellbeing.

RESULTS: A total of 512 dyads were randomised, with 510 included in intention-to-treat analyses. Adolescents presented with elevated baseline depressive symptoms and substantial prior mental health difficulties. Depressive symptoms declined over time in both trial arms, with no significant between-group difference at 15 months (adjusted difference - 0.12 SMFQ points, 95% CI -1.23 to 0.98). In contrast, parents allocated to the personalised programme showed greater improvements in guideline-concordant parenting practices and parent-child attachment. Engagement was modest, and over 40% of adolescents triggered duty-of-care procedures due to elevated risk during the trial.

CONCLUSIONS: In this high-risk UK sample, a personalised digital parenting programme improved parenting practices but did not reduce adolescent depressive symptoms beyond an active educational control. These findings highlight the importance of matching intervention intensity to baseline symptom severity and support the role of digital parenting programmes as part of stepped prevention and early intervention frameworks.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ISRCTN63358736.

articles.title: Combination pharmacotherapy in psychotic depression: A systematic review and pairwise meta-analysis of randomized trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Psychotic depression is a severe and under-researched subtype of major depressive disorder. Although antidepressant-antipsychotic combination therapy is widely recommended, the limited number of randomized controlled trials and heterogeneity of outcome definitions complicate interpretation of the evidence available.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and pairwise meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials evaluating pharmacological treatment of psychotic depression. Electronic searches were performed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, and Cochrane CENTRAL from database inception up to February 13, 2026. Eligible studies compared combination pharmacotherapy with non-combination treatment during the acute phase. Risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using random-effects models. The primary outcome was clinical improvement, defined according to each trial's prespecified dichotomous endpoint (response or remission). Sensitivity analyses were also conducted for response-only and remission-only outcomes.

RESULTS: Four acute trials (five comparisons) were included. Combination pharmacotherapy was associated with a significantly higher likelihood of clinical improvement compared with non-combination treatment (RR 1.93, 95% CI 1.53-2.43). Findings were consistent in response-only (RR 2.03, 95% CI 1.51-2.75) and remission-only analyses (RR 1.78, 95% CI 1.27-2.49).

CONCLUSIONS: Antidepressant-antipsychotic combination therapy is associated with substantially superior acute outcomes in psychotic depression. These findings are consistent with current guideline recommendations and highlight the need for contemporary randomized trials using standardized outcome measures.

articles.title: Efficacy of psychological interventions for premenstrual syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) is common among reproductive-aged women. Pharmacological treatments often cause side effects. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy of psychological interventions for PMS symptom severity and related emotional distress.

METHODS: We systematically searched seven electronic databases from their inception to March 2026 to screen randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of psychological interventions for premenstrual syndrome (PMS). We used Review Manager 5.4 software to evaluate the risk of bias in included studies in accordance with the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool. Data were pooled using the DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model in Stata 18.0, and standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated. The study was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines and registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261345418).

RESULTS: A total of 20 RCTs involving 1369 women were included. The meta-analysis indicated that psychological interventions reduced the severity of PMS symptoms. One trial (Çitil and Çitil Canbay, 2024) was identified as an extreme outlier based on non overlapping confidence intervals. After excluding it in a sensitivity analysis, the pooled effect remained significant. (SMD = -1.57, 95% CI [-1.94, -1.21], p < 0.001). The interventions significantly alleviated PMS-related depressive symptoms (SMD = -1.08, 95% CI [-1.46, -0.70], p < 0.001), anxiety symptoms (SMD = -1.03, 95% CI [-1.36, -0.69], p < 0.001), and anger/irritability symptoms (SMD = -0.85, 95% CI [-1.47, -0.24], p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Psychological interventions may reduce PMS symptoms and related emotional distress. Psychological interventions may represent a useful non-pharmacological option for PMS management.

articles.title: Comparative risk of early-onset dementia with lithium versus valproate in bipolar disorder: A real-world cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bipolar disorder is associated with an elevated risk of dementia. While lithium may exert neuroprotective effects, its comparative impact on early-onset dementia versus valproate, a mood stabilizer with potential neurotoxicity remains unclear in younger populations. This study aimed to compare the risk of early-onset dementia between patients with bipolar disorder initiating lithium versus valproate therapy.

METHODS: This retrospective, active-comparator, new-user cohort study using the TriNetX global health research network. The study period was from January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2024. We identified patients aged 18-60 years newly diagnosed with bipolar disorder who initiated either lithium or valproate. Patients with prevalent dementia were excluded. Propensity score matching (1:1) was used to balance baseline characteristics including comorbidities and renal function. The primary outcome was incident dementia within 5 years of the index date. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: The matched cohort included 82,172 patients (41,086 per group; mean age 37.4 years; 54.4% female). Over the 5-year follow-up, lithium initiation was associated with a lower risk of dementia compared with valproate (HR 0.815, 95% CI 0.717-0.926; p = 0.002). This comparative association remained consistent across extended 10-year follow-up, complete-case, and all-cause mortality sensitivity analyses.

LIMITATIONS: Observational design precludes causal inference; lack of granular dosage data prevents dose-response analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Lithium is associated with a lower risk of early-onset dementia compared to valproate.

articles.title: Pharmacologic and expectancy effects in depression: Associations with inter-network resting-state connectivity.
articles.abstract: Depression involves dysregulation across large-scale neural networks, yet substantial heterogeneity in resting-state functional connectivity (rsFC) across patients limits our understanding of treatment mechanisms. A key unresolved question is whether baseline network architecture differentially predicts response to pharmacological versus expectancy-driven treatment effects. In this mechanistic, hypothesis-generating study, 60 depressed participants completed resting-state fMRI at baseline and after 8 weeks of double-blind randomization to an SSRI or placebo. We tested whether connectivity between three networks - the dorsal attention (DAN), salience (SN), and default mode (DMN) networks - predicted treatment response as a function of drug assignment and treatment beliefs. We identified dissociable neural pathways for pharmacological and expectancy effects. Baseline connectivity between attention and salience networks, circuits involved in contextual processing, predicted response specifically among participants who developed placebo beliefs. Baseline connectivity between salience and default mode networks, circuits involved in mood regulation and internal state prediction, showed a double dissociation by drug assignment: higher connectivity predicted better outcomes with the SSRI, while lower connectivity predicted better outcomes with placebo. Network reorganization over treatment followed rather than predicted mood improvement and occurred only when drug assignment and belief aligned. These findings suggest that baseline connectivity patterns serve as trait-like neural markers differentiating pharmacological from expectancy-driven response pathways, and that network reorganization reflects a consequence of aligned pharmacological and psychological treatment effects. Replication in larger samples is warranted, but these results offer a novel framework for understanding and ultimately resolving heterogeneity in antidepressant treatment response.

articles.title: Resistance exercise training compared to a low-intensity sham for depressive symptoms in young women with analogue generalized anxiety disorder: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This randomized controlled trial (RCT) quantified the effects of resistance exercise training (RET) compared to low-intensity sham RET attention-control (SHAM) on depressive symptoms among young women (18-40y) with analogue Generalized Anxiety Disorder (AGAD).

METHODS: Fifty-five participants (21.8 ± 2.2y) with AGAD (Psychiatric Diagnostic Screening Questionnaire GAD subscale (≥6) and Penn State Worry Questionnaire (≥45)) were randomized to eight weeks of World Health Organization and American College of Sports Medicine guidelines-based, progressive, moderate-to-high-intensity (70-80% one-repetition maximum (1RM)) RET (PRET) with two sets of 8-12 repetitions of eight exercises, or a SHAM (20% 1RM), both preceded by a two-week familiarization. The 16-item Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology (QIDS) measured depressive symptoms at baseline, post-familiarization, week four, eight, and one-month follow-up. A two (group) by five (time-point) repeated measures ANOVA quantified differences between groups. Standardized mean difference (SMD) quantified the magnitude of within-condition change. Hedges' d effect sizes quantified the magnitude of difference in change between groups.

RESULTS: No significant group by time interaction was found for depressive symptoms (F(3.2167) = 0.34, p = 0.806; d = 0.17[95%CI: -0.36 to 0.70]). A significant main effect for time was found (F(3.2167) = 42.19, p < 0.001); PRET (SMD = 1.53[95%CI: 0.92 to 2.13]) and SHAM (SMD = 1.04[95%CI: 0.49 to 1.60]) induced large-magnitude reductions in depressive symptoms, that were maintained (SMD: PRET: 1.64[95%CI: 1.02 to 2.26]; SHAM: 1.15[95%CI: 0.59 to 1.72]) at one-month follow-up.

CONCLUSION: PRET and low-intensity RET can induce large antidepressant benefits. Although the difference between PRET and SHAM was unconfirmed, larger within-condition effects indicate greater benefits of PRET; however, benefits can also occur following lower-intensity RET.

articles.title: Neural correlates of early- and late-onset nonsuicidal self-injury: Distinctions in resting-state functional connectivity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nonsuicidal self-injury (NSSI) is a major global health concern, yet the neurophysiological significance of the age of onset remains poorly understood. This cross-sectional study (2019-2022) examined differences in resting-state functional connectivity (rsFC) among young Korean adults (aged 19-29) with early-onset NSSI, late-onset NSSI, and healthy controls, with a focus on emotion regulation networks.

METHODS: Following screening of 215 individuals, 91 unmedicated participants with NSSI and 84 healthy controls were included in the rsFC analysis. The NSSI group was subdivided into early-onset (onset before age 14) and late-onset (onset at or after age 14) groups.

RESULTS: The early-onset NSSI group exhibited increased rsFC within the sensorimotor network (SMN), specifically between the postcentral and pre/postcentral gyri, relative to the late-onset NSSI group at the permutation level (pperm < 0.001; matrix-wide q_FDR = 0.211). Nominal permutation-level associations between DERS scores and rsFC were also observed, but these did not reach the threshold for matrix-wide FDR correction and should be interpreted as exploratory.

LIMITATIONS: The exploratory, cross-sectional design and reliance on retrospective self-report of NSSI onset limit causal inference. The modest subgroup sample sizes and the exploratory nature of the findings may also affect the robustness of the results, highlighting the need for larger longitudinal studies.

CONCLUSIONS: These exploratory findings suggest that the age of NSSI onset may be associated with potentially distinct rsFC profiles. Pending longitudinal replication, onset age represents a key candidate variable for understanding the neurobiology of NSSI.

articles.title: Topological architecture and cross-domain co-occurrence of chronic diseases and depressive symptoms in elderly Chinese adults: A real-world network analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study employed network analysis to characterize the co-occurrence between chronic diseases and depressive symptoms, found sex-based disparities, and delineated distinct co-occurrence patterns in elderly Chinese adults.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted between July and November 2024, enrolling 6785 participants aged 60 years and above from four Chinese provinces. Absolute co-occurrence frequency matrices between chronic diseases and depressive symptoms were visualized using heatmaps. Network analysis was employed to estimate centrality and bridge metrics, identifying highly central and bridge nodes, while network stability and accuracy were evaluated. Furthermore, the network comparison test was utilized to investigate sex-based disparities, and symptom co-occurrence patterns were explored.

RESULTS: The prevalence of chronic diseases and depressive symptoms co-occurrence reached 61.95%, with females exhibiting a higher symptom co-occurrence burden than males. Network analysis found "depressed" (D3) and "bothered" (D1) as potentially central symptoms, while asthma (C10) and "lonely" (D9) were found to be potentially key bridge nodes linking the chronic disease and depressive domains. The female network demonstrated higher global strength compared to the male network (48.07 vs. 32.27, P = 0.010). Among the five identified symptom co-occurrence patterns, "Systemic Cardio-Metabolic-Inflammatory Load" was the most prevalent (37.12%), followed by "Severe Organ Dysfunction and Survival Distress" (17.57%) and three independent depressive symptom sub-clusters.

CONCLUSION: This study found potential central and bridge nodes. The observed sex disparities and heterogeneous symptom co-occurrence patterns.

articles.title: Multiplexed plasmon-enhanced lateral flow assay for early diagnosis of acute kidney injury.
articles.abstract: Early diagnosis of acute kidney injury (AKI) remains a major clinical challenge due to the delayed and insensitive nature of conventional markers such as serum creatinine. Urinary protein biomarkers, including neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL) and cystatin C (CysC), provide earlier and complementary information on kidney injury, but their clinical translation is limited by the lack of rapid, quantitative, and multiplexed point-of-care (POC) diagnostic tests. Here, we report a multiplexed plasmonic-fluor-based lateral flow assay (p-LFA) that enables sensitive, quantitative, and simultaneous detection of NGAL and CysC. By harnessing ultrabright plasmonic-fluor nanolabels and ratiometric fluorescence analysis, the p-LFA achieves picogram-per-milliliter analytical sensitivity comparable to that of the enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). In addition, the simplified assay format enables sample-to-answer times as short as 10 min, while maintaining sensitivity sufficient for accurate AKI detection. Clinical validation using pediatric urine samples demonstrates a strong correlation with ELISA measurements for both biomarkers. Combined analysis of NGAL and CysC significantly improves AKI diagnostic performance, yielding an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.973 with a clinical sensitivity of 90.9% and specificity of 91.2% in the studied cohort. Furthermore, a low-cost, portable fluorescence reader enables quantitative performance equivalent to benchtop imaging while dramatically reducing instrument cost and complexity. Collectively, this work establishes a scalable and adaptable p-LFA platform that bridges laboratory-grade immunoassays and practical POC diagnostics, offering a promising solution for early AKI detection and multiplexed biomarker analysis in decentralized healthcare settings.

articles.title: Randomized controlled trial of a modular, transdiagnostic, cognitive-behavioral anxiety intervention versus primary care behavioral health treatment as usual.
articles.abstract: Offering behavioral treatment for anxiety in primary care will help to address the anxiety treatment gap. Modular Anxiety Skills Training (MAST) is a transdiagnostic cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) intervention for Primary Care Behavioral Health (PCBH) settings. This multi-site randomized controlled trial compared the effects of MAST versus PCBH treatment as usual (TAU), both delivered by frontline clinicians, on anxiety severity and impairment. Participants (N = 167, 70% male, 89% White, 9% Hispanic, M age 51 [16] years) were recruited from primary care at two Veterans Health Administration healthcare systems. Contrary to our hypothesis, intent-to-treat analyses found no differences by condition at 16-weeks post-treatment. Participants in both conditions improved significantly on overall anxiety severity and impairment (OASIS) as well as anxiety and depression symptom severity, functional disability, and quality of life, with small to medium effect sizes (0.21-0.61). All gains were maintained at 28-week follow-up, and participants receiving MAST demonstrated further significant reduction in OASIS. Post hoc analyses suggested baseline depression severity moderated the condition effect; participants with moderate and severe comorbid depression responded better to MAST than PCBH TAU. While MAST was not superior to PCBH TAU at post-treatment as hypothesized, it may potentially yield a more enduring impact and work better with comorbid depression; however, these findings require prospective replication. This study advances the literature by comparing brief CBT for anxiety in primary care to a strong active comparison comprising behavioral treatment. MAST may offer implementation advantages due to being manualized and modular. Further research on modular CBT for anxiety is warranted.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of Dimdazenil in primary insomnia and depressive episodes/bipolar depressive episode with insomnia: A post-marketing, randomized, open-label, positive-controlled study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the efficacy and safety of Dimdazenil in primary insomnia and depressive episodes/bipolar depressive episode with insomnia.

METHODS: In this post-marketing, positive-controlled study, eligible patients were assigned 1:1 to receive either Dimdazenil 2.5 mg or Midazolam 15 mg (minimum 3 doses/week) over 14 days. The primary endpoint was the between-group difference in subjective total sleep time (sTST) on Day 14.

RESULTS: 185 patients were included (Dimdazenil, N = 93; Midazolam, N = 92). Dimdazenil significantly increased sTST from baseline (LSM difference, +113.33 min, P < 0.001), with a mean between-group difference of +7.36 min versus Midazolam. A higher proportion of patients in the Dimdazenil group achieved sTST≥390 min (59.49% vs. 48.72%) and sTST≥8 h (34.8% vs. 23.1%). Significant reductions from baseline were also observed in sSL and ISI (both P < 0.001). Daytime functioning was significantly improved with Dimdazenil, as evidenced by marked reductions in ESS, FFS, and TMT-A completion time (all P < 0.001). Moreover, FFS decreased more from baseline with Dimdazenil than Midazolam (-3.86 vs. -2.48). Descriptive improvements in sWASO, sNAW, and FFS scores were observed in patients with depressive episodes/bipolar depressive episode with insomnia. Most TEAEs in the Dimdazenil group were mild (89.66%, 26/29), with no severe TEAE or death reported.

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory study, Dimdazenil was associated with improvements in subjective sleep parameters and daytime functioning in patients with primary insomnia and depressive episodes/bipolar depressive episode with insomnia. Improvements in sleep maintenance outcomes and in patients with depressive episodes/bipolar depressive episode with insomnia warrant further investigation in adequately powered confirmatory studies.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered on the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (https://www.chictr.org.cn; registration number: ChiCTR2400085915).

articles.title: The longitudinal relationship between co-rumination and depressive symptoms in adolescents: A systematic review and meta-analytic structural equation modeling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Co-rumination is associated with depressive symptoms in adolescents, yet the temporal directionality remains unclear because previous meta-analyses have relied largely on cross-sectional evidence. This study examined the longitudinal associations between co-rumination and depressive symptoms and tested moderators using meta-analytic structural equation modeling.

METHODS: Following a preregistered protocol, seven databases were systematically searched for longitudinal studies. Forty-six datasets comprising 18,222 participants were included. One-stage meta-analytic structural equation modeling was used to estimate cross-lagged panel models from pooled correlation matrices. Moderators included age, gender, publication year, individualism, time lag, study quality, co-rumination partner, co-rumination modality, and measurement instruments. Sensitivity analyses examined T1-Tlast associations and modeled co-brooding and co-reflection separately.

RESULTS: T1 co-rumination prospectively predicted T2 depressive symptoms (β = 0.036, p = .020), and T1 depressive symptoms showed a small association with T2 co-rumination (β = 0.031, p = .0495). The forward pathway was consistent across sensitivity analyses, with co-brooding showing the most robust forward association; the reverse pathway was attenuated under T1-Tlast extraction. After Benjamini-Hochberg correction, only measurement instruments significantly moderated the cross-lagged paths; publication year showed a suggestive but non-significant omnibus effect. Gender, age, time lag, study quality, individualism, co-rumination partner, and co-rumination modality were not significant moderators.

CONCLUSIONS: Co-rumination is a small but reliable prospective predictor of adolescent depressive symptoms, with co-brooding showing the most consistent forward prediction. The weaker, less robust reverse pathway argues against a strong reciprocal cycle. Future research should examine whether targeting maladaptive, repetitive co-brooding in close peer relationships may benefit prevention efforts.

articles.title: Anxiety and depression associated oral health problems in pediatric populations: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Anxiety and depression are common mental disorders and frequently coexist with oral health problems (OHPs) that impair overall well-being and quality of life. While the association of mood disorders and OHPs is well documented in adults, evidence regarding their association in pediatric populations remains unclear.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and reference lists to identify eligible studies. Risk of bias was evaluated using the Newcastle-Ottawa Quality Assessment Scale. Pooled estimations, including odds ratios (ORs) and standardized mean differences, were calculated with random- or fixed-effects models determined by I2-assessed heterogeneity.

RESULTS: A total of 33 studies were included, 27 of which were eligible for meta-analysis, involving a total of 31,834 participants across 15 countries. The pooled prevalence of anxiety and depression were 57% (95% CI: 41%-73%) and 38% (95% CI: 20%-56%), respectively, among individuals with OHPs, with considerable heterogeneity. The pooled estimations tended to support the hypothesis that anxiety and depression were significantly associated with OHPs, with Odds Ratios (ORs) of 2.67 (95% CI: 1.43-4.97, I2 = 89.2%) and 1.93 (95% CI: 1.22-3.04, I2 = 71.1%). In subgroup analyses, both anxiety and depression appeared to be associated with bruxism and temporomandibular disorders (TMDs).

CONCLUSION: Based on the available evidence, anxiety and depression were associated with OHPs, particularly bruxism and TMDs, in pediatric populations. Given the high heterogeneity and methodological variability across included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution. Multidisciplinary collaboration is recommended to promote both mental and dental health at an early age.

articles.title: Consensus by design: Conflict of interest and the intravenous ketamine Delphi guidelines.
Transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation enhances reward-effort efficiency in severe major depressive disorder.
articles.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a highly prevalent psychiatric disorder with changes in motivation to work for rewards being a core symptom. Transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation (tVNS) has emerged as a promising therapy but its effects on the core features of MDD, such as changes in motivation, remained relatively unexplored. In this randomised, single-blind, cross-over, controlled trial, we used a grip strength effort task to investigate how tVNS impacted choices to exert different levels of physical effort for varying monetary rewards in MDD patients (n = 53) and a non-depressed control group (n = 45). The primary analyses showed no interaction between condition (sham versus tVNS) and group (control versus MDD). However, secondary analyses showed that tVNS effects were dependent on symptom severity. Compared to sham stimulation, tVNS enhanced the efficiency with which participants with severe depressive symptoms allocated physical effort for rewards (reward-effort efficiency). These effects were not seen in healthy participants or MDD patients with less severe symptoms. The effect of tVNS on reward-effort efficiency was driven by reduced unnecessary effort in those with severe MDD symptoms - a reduction in choices to exert additional effort when this was not required to gain a larger reward. This suggests a motivational mechanism by which tVNS exerts its therapeutic effects in severe MDD but these remain secondary findings which should be interpreted with caution. Determining whether the effects of tVNS are linked to broader changes in executive functioning, such as improvements in cognitive flexibility in MDD, should be a key aim for future work.

articles.title: Acupuncture improves depressive symptoms and prefrontal cortical function in mild to moderate depressive disorder: A randomized sham-controlled trial and fNIRS study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depressive disorder is a common mental illness associated with substantial functional impairment. Although pharmacotherapy is widely used, its effectiveness is often limited by adverse effects and poor adherence. Acupuncture has been increasingly applied as a complementary treatment for depression, and its neurobiological characteristics remain unclear.

OBJECTIVE: This randomized, sham-controlled trial aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy of acupuncture for mild to moderate depressive disorder and to investigate its effects on prefrontal cortical function using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS).

METHODS: Patients with mild to moderate depressive disorder were randomly assigned to a real acupuncture (RA) group or a sham acupuncture (SA) group and received standardized treatment for 8 weeks. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS), Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS), Short Form-36 Health Survey (SF-36), and a traditional Chinese medicine syndrome score. A subset of participants underwent fNIRS assessment during resting-state and task-based conditions to evaluate prefrontal cortical activation and functional connectivity.

RESULTS: Compared with baseline, the RA group showed significant reductions in SDS and SAS scores and significant improvements in SF-36 emotional domains, with effects emerging at Week 4 and persisting up to 12 weeks after treatment. Improvements were greater and more stable in the RA group than in the SA group. fNIRS analyses revealed enhanced activation in dorsolateral and medial prefrontal regions and strengthened prefrontal functional connectivity following acupuncture, whereas neural changes in the SA group were limited.

CONCLUSION: Acupuncture is effective for improving depressive and anxiety symptoms and quality of life in patients with mild to moderate depressive disorder. Modulation of prefrontal cortical activation and connectivity may underlie its antidepressant effects.

articles.title: Aripiprazole once-monthly for patients diagnosed with bipolar I disorder: Number needed to treat, number needed to harm, and likelihood to be helped or harmed.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This post hoc analysis assessed the benefit-risk profile of aripiprazole once-monthly 400 mg (AOM 400) as a long-term maintenance treatment in patients diagnosed with bipolar I disorder (BP-I), using the evidence-based metrics of number needed to treat (NNT), number needed to harm (NNH), and the likelihood to be helped or harmed (LHH).

METHODS: Data were derived from a double-blind, randomized withdrawal study that evaluated the efficacy and safety/tolerability of AOM 400 versus placebo over 52 weeks (NCT01567527). The main efficacy outcome was the proportion of patients free from recurrence of any mood episode, while the main safety/tolerability outcome was the incidence of patient discontinuation due to treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs).

RESULTS: Overall, 73.5% of 132 patients randomized to AOM 400 and 48.9% of 133 patients randomized to placebo were free from recurrence of any mood episode at Week 52 (NNT = 5 [95% CI: 3,8]). NNT (95% CI) values were 5 (4, 9), 4 (3, 7), and-116 (not significant) for patients free from recurrence of a manic mood episode, mixed mood episode, and depressive mood episode, respectively. Discontinuation due to TEAEs was lower with AOM 400 (17.4%) versus placebo (25.6%), resulting in a negative NNH. Using an imputed NNH versus placebo of 1000, LHH was 200 for patients free from recurrence of any mood episode relative to discontinuation due to any TEAE at 52 weeks.

CONCLUSIONS: Data suggest a favorable benefit-risk profile for AOM 400 versus placebo as a long-term maintenance treatment for BP-I.

articles.title: Single-cell eQTL and Mendelian randomization analyses of shared genetic architecture in major depressive disorder and schizophrenia.
articles.abstract: Schizophrenia (SCZ) and major depressive disorder (MDD) are severe psychiatric disorders with substantial shared genetic liability and frequent clinical co-occurrence, yet their shared cell type-specific genetic mechanisms remain unclear. We integrated single-cell expression quantitative trait locus (sc-eQTL) data from eight major brain cell types with large-scale genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics for SCZ and MDD. Cell type-specific genetically regulated gene expression was evaluated using Mendelian randomization (MR) and Bayesian colocalization analyses, followed by validation in independent single-cell RNA sequencing datasets and functional characterization using virtual gene knockout and phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) analyses. Integrative analyses prioritized three shared candidate genes, ZSCAN31, BTN3A2, and YLPM1, all showing strong colocalization support (PP·H4 > 0.8). Single-cell transcriptomic validation supported distinct cell type-specific patterns, with ZSCAN31 enriched in astrocytes and endothelial cells, BTN3A2 in microglia, and YLPM1 in oligodendrocytes. Virtual knockout of YLPM1 suggested perturbation of neurodevelopment-related pathways in SCZ and synaptic signaling pathways in MDD. These findings provide a cell type-resolved view of shared genetic architecture between SCZ and MDD and highlight candidate genes for further mechanistic and translational investigation.

articles.title: Measurement stability and differential domain-specific trajectories of the PHQ-9 in late-life depression: Evidence from a collaborative care trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) is routinely used to monitor depressive symptoms. However, whether its empirically derived two-factor structure remains stable across repeated assessments in clinically depressed populations is not well established.

METHODS: Using item-level data from a secondary analysis of the PROACTIVE cluster-randomised controlled trial (N=558; PHQ-9 ≥10 at baseline; aged ≥60 years), we evaluated longitudinal measurement invariance of an empirically derived two-factor PHQ-9 structure across three assessment points using WLSMV structural equation modelling with multiple imputation. We then modelled domain-specific latent growth trajectories by trial arm and examined within-person temporal dynamics using a random intercept cross-lagged panel model (RI-CLPM).

RESULTS: Metric invariance was supported and partial scalar invariance achieved across all three time points, after freeing thresholds for three interpretable items (sleep disturbance, fatigue, and suicidal ideation). The intervention was associated with a steeper improvement in cognitive-affective symptoms but showed no significant effect on somatic symptom trajectories. Within-person somatic deviations at baseline were temporally associated with subsequent cognitive-affective deviations, whereas the reverse was not.

CONCLUSIONS: The two-factor structure of the PHQ-9 is metrically stable through clinical recovery in older adults with moderate-to-severe depression. Domain-specific subscores capture differential treatment response and temporal symptom dynamics that total scores conceal, and can be calculated from existing PHQ-9 items at no additional burden. These findings support the routine use of domain-level monitoring in collaborative care programmes serving older adults in low- and middle-income country (LMIC) settings.

articles.title: Impact of amyloid-Beta on the functional hierarchies and clinical outcomes in late-life depression.
articles.abstract: Late-life depression (LLD) is characterized by high treatment resistance, particularly in patients with significant cerebral amyloid-beta (Aβ) deposition. However, the underlying mechanisms through which Aβ compromises clinical recovery remain poorly understood. We investigated whether Aβ burden drives treatment resistance by inducing hierarchical rigidity in the brain's macroscale functional organization. We analyzed longitudinal resting-state fMRI and amyloid-PET data from 93 LLD patients (44 Aβ+, 49 Aβ-) around a one-year treatment interval. Functional connectivity (FC) gradients were constructed using diffusion map embedding to characterize the sensory-to-transmodal cortical hierarchy. At baseline, Aβ+ patients exhibited widespread FC gradient aberrations, primarily within the frontoparietal control and default mode networks, despite equivalent depression severity to Aβ- patients. Following treatment, the Aβ+ group showed significantly poorer clinical remission (p < 0.001). Longitudinal analysis revealed a lack of significant group × time interaction, indicating that gradient disorganization in Aβ+ LLD remained unresolved. Cerebral Aβ acts as a physiological constraint on the hierarchical plasticity required for antidepressant response. This "hierarchical rigidity" suggests that Aβ anchors the brain in a dysfunctional, compressed state, precluding the adaptive reorganization necessary for recovery. Baseline functional gradients may serve as a potent prognostic marker for identifying amyloid-associated treatment resistance in LLD.

articles.title: Prospective controlled study of the recombinant zoster vaccine in autoimmune rheumatic disease: robust seroconversion despite intravenous cyclophosphamide.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV) prevents shingles in autoimmune rheumatic diseases (ARD), but intravenous cyclophosphamide (IVCYC) impact on immunogenicity is unknown. Given cell depletion/cytotoxicity, IVCYC is expected to induce profound immunogenicity impairment, we therefore evaluated its impact.

METHODS: This subanalysis of prospective, randomized, placebo-controlled trial included ARD patients receiving IVCYC (ARD-IVCYC) compared with patients without IVCYC (ARD-no IVCYC) and healthy-controls. RZV was administered in two doses. Humoral response (≥4-fold), geometric mean titers (GMT) and cellular response were assessed after second dose. Disease activity and adverse events (AEs) were recorded.

RESULTS: Forty-one ARD-IVCYC, 164 ARD-no IVCYC, and 164 controls were included. Seroconversion did not differ between ARD-IVCYC and ARD-no IVCYC (91.9% vs. 91.5%) and were lower than controls (99.4%, p = 0.022). Post-vaccination GMTs were comparable between ARD groups (p > 0.999), but lower than controls (p = 0.006). Cellular response and ARDs flares did not differ between groups (p > 0.05), with no severe AEs.

CONCLUSION: RZV elicited >90% humoral response in IVCYC-treated patients, supporting it during IVCYC when warranted (NCT05879419).

articles.title: Ethnic disparities in COVID-19 vaccine uptake among among 55+ year-old Canadians: Exploring the role of racial discrimination, chronic disease comorbidities, and conspiracy beliefs.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Canada's COVID-19 vaccination program achieved high overall coverage, yet older racialized and Indigenous people experienced lower uptake and far higher infection and mortality rates. Structural inequities, low health literacy, mistrust, and misinformation contributed to these gaps. Despite early vaccine prioritization, little disaggregated data exist for racialized and Indigenous older adults. This study examines vaccine uptake in these underserved groups to inform more equitable public health strategies and strengthen future pandemic responses.

METHODS: We conducted a Canada-wide cross-sectional online survey of adults aged ≥55 years in March 2025 using Computer-Assisted Web Interviewing. Participants completed measures assessing COVID-19 vaccination doses, experiences of major racial discrimination, conspiracy beliefs, health literacy, chronic conditions, and sociodemographic characteristics.

RESULTS: Of the 581participants, 90,3% received at least one dose. Black and Indigenous people were more often unvaccinated (17%), compared to 5.5-6% for Asians and Arabs. Receipt of ≥5 doses was observed in 50% of White, 41.8% of Asian and 13.8% of Black individuals. Older adults (≥65 years) had greater uptake (OR=1.58, 95%CI: 1.07-2.32), as did retirees (OR=2.47) and more highly educated participants (college OR=2.29; Bachelor OR=2.77). Higher conspiracy belief scores were significantly associated with lower odds of receiving higher doses (OR=0.91, 95%CI: 0.89-0.93; p<0.001). Additionally, a greater number of chronic diseases was associated with higher odds of being in a higher vaccine-dose category (OR = 1.09, 95% CI: 1.02-1.18).

CONCLUSION: Despite pandemic efforts, substantial ethnic disparities in COVID-19 vaccine uptake persisted, with lower coverage in racialized and Indigenous groups.
