Addressing structural inequities, comorbidities, and misinformation is critical to achieving more equitable, culturally responsive vaccination strategies.

articles.title: Assessment of the Fasciola hepatica saposin-like protein 2 (rFhSAP2) vaccine candidate in sheep: Immunogenicity without protective efficacy.
articles.abstract: Fasciolosis caused by Fasciola hepatica is an economically important parasitic disease of livestock and a major zoonotic disease in humans. Vaccination is a promising strategy to reduce the impact of fasciolosis and dependence on fasciolicides. Saposin-like protein 2 (FhSAP2) has previously shown high immunogenicity and reductions in fluke burden in experimental animal models; however, its efficacy has not been evaluated in sheep. Twenty-one female sheep were randomly assigned to three groups (n = 7): vaccinated, adjuvant control, and infection control. The vaccinated group received 400 μg of rtFhSAP2 formulated with Montanide ISA 201 VG, the adjuvant control received Montanide ISA 201 VG alone, and the infection control received saline. Animals received three subcutaneous immunizations at four-week intervals and were subsequently challenged orally with 200 F. hepatica metacercariae. Vaccine efficacy was evaluated based on fluke burden, fecal egg counts, and egg viability. Antigen-specific IgG, IgG1, and IgG2 antibody responses were assessed by ELISA. Vaccination with rtFhSAP2 resulted in a 16.4% reduction in fluke burden compared with the infection control group (p > 0.05). Reductions in fecal egg counts ranged from 8.9% to 34.5% (p > 0.05). Fecal egg viability remained high, ranging from 88.9% to 91.3% among groups (p > 0.05). Gallbladder-derived egg viability was lower in vaccinated sheep (56.9%) than in the infection control (75.9%) and adjuvant control (73.6%) groups (p > 0.05). Vaccination induced a strong and sustained humoral response. IgG and IgG1 levels were significantly higher in vaccinated sheep than in both control groups from weeks 4-24 and 4-32, respectively. IgG2 levels were also significantly higher from weeks 4-24, although the response was lower than that of IgG1. Overall, rtFhSAP2 formulated with Montanide ISA 201 VG was highly immunogenic in sheep, but the humoral response did not translate into significant protection against F. hepatica.

articles.title: A phase III randomized study: Immunogenicity and safety of a quadrivalent meningococcal conjugate vaccine in healthy adults, adolescents, and children in India and healthy adolescents and children in South Africa.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: MenACYW-TT is a quadrivalent meningococcal conjugate vaccine approved for individuals aged ≥6 weeks. This Phase III study evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of a single dose of MenACYW-TT versus MenACYW-DT and MenPS-ACWY in healthy adults, adolescents, and children in India and in healthy adolescents and children in South Africa.

METHODS: In total, 1,328 participants were randomized by age into three cohorts (Cohort Ia: adults aged 18-55 years, India [N=198]; Cohort Ib: adults aged ≥56 years, India [N=200]; Cohort II: children and adolescents aged 2-17 years, India [N=465] and South Africa [N=465]). The immunogenicity of vaccines was assessed with a serum bactericidal assay using human complement (hSBA). The primary objective was to demonstrate the non-inferiority of immunogenicity of a single dose of MenACYW-TT versus MenACYW-DT in children and adolescents aged 2-17 years in terms of hSBA titers in India and South Africa.

RESULTS: The primary objective was met. The non-inferiority of MenACYW-TT versus MenACYW-DT was demonstrated on post-vaccination Day 30 in participants aged 2-17 years. The lower limit of the 95% confidence interval for the difference in the percentages of the participants achieving seroprotection (hSBA titers ≥1:8) against all four serogroups was greater than -10%. MenACYW-TT demonstrated robust immunogenicity in adults aged 18-55 years and ≥56 years in India. The rates of solicited injection site and systemic reactions were comparable between the participants who received MenACYW-TT versus licensed comparator vaccines. No vaccine-related serious adverse events, study discontinuations, or deaths were reported.

CONCLUSIONS: A single dose of MenACYW-TT induced non-inferior immune responses and a comparable safety profile versus MenACYW-DT in children and adolescents aged 2-17 years. MenACYW-TT was well tolerated and immunogenic in adults, adolescents, and children in India and in adolescents and children in South Africa.

articles.title: Tomato Brown Rugose Fruit Virus and Pepino Mosaic Virus Differentially Modulate Disease Severity of Bacterial Pith Necrosis and Bacterial Canker in Tomato.
articles.abstract: Worldwide tomato production is increasingly challenged by complex disease outbreaks involving multiple interacting pathogens. In Israel, recent years have seen a marked rise in vascular collapse symptoms in greenhouse-grown tomatoes, coinciding with the widespread emergence of tomato brown rugose fruit virus (ToBRFV) and pepino mosaic virus (PepMV). Here, we investigated the bacterial and viral agents associated with these outbreaks and examined how viral infection influences the development and severity of bacterial diseases that cause vascular collapse. Surveys conducted between 2021 and 2026 revealed that tomato pith necrosis outbreaks were associated with a diverse bacterial community dominated by members of the Pseudomonadales and Enterobacterales, while bacterial canker outbreaks were exclusively linked to Clavibacter michiganensis. Multilocus sequence analysis showed that pith necrosis-associated Pseudomonas isolates clustered primarily within the P. syringae, and P. corrugata phylogroups. Pathogenicity assays demonstrated that only a subset of pith necrosis-associated bacteria, P. mediterranea, P. capsici, P. viridiflava, and Xanthomonas euvesicatoria pv. perforans, induced pith necrosis under controlled conditions, with high variability in symptom severity. Co-inoculation experiments showed that ToBRFV- and PepMV-infected plants exhibited a 40-100% increase in lesion size following inoculation with pith necrosis-associated bacteria, without a corresponding increase in bacterial colonization, whereas the same viral infections attenuated wilt symptoms caused by C. michiganensis. Together, our findings demonstrate that endemic viral infections differentially modulate bacterial disease outcomes, either exacerbating or attenuating symptoms depending on the pathogen. These results highlight the importance of multi-pathogen interactions in disease severity and have important implications for tomato disease management.

articles.title: Internal Seed Colonization, Flower-to-Seed Transmission, and Seedling Association of Didymella tanaceti in Pyrethrum.
articles.abstract: Seedborne inoculum has been proposed as a potential source of primary infection for Didymella tanaceti in pyrethrum (Tanacetum cinerariifolium). However, the location of the pathogen within seed associated tissues - that include the pericarp, seed coat and embryo - and the role of seedborne inoculum in disease establishment remain unclear. This study investigated seed colonization, internal survival, and seed-to-seedling transmission of D. tanaceti using light microscopy, histopathology, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and a fluorescently labeled isolate. In naturally infected seeds, following surface sterilization and culture-based identification, putative D. tanaceti was recovered from the outer seed layer of 27.5% of seeds, from internal tissues (inner seed layer and embryo) of 7.5% of seeds, and from both outer and internal tissues of 3.8% of seeds. Histological and SEM analyses revealed the presence of fungal propagules associated with inner tissues, particularly within inter-tegumentary spaces. In a separate flower inoculation experiment, fluorescent D. tanaceti was detected in 37.3% and 36.0% of seeds from pre- and post-anthesis inoculated treatments, respectively. Among D. tanaceti-positive seeds recovered following post-anthesis inoculation, 40.7% appeared externally asymptomatic despite lacking embryos. Finally, in a separate seed-to-seedling assay, fluorescent D. tanaceti was detected on cotyledons of 64% of seedlings emerging from inoculated seeds. These findings highlight the epidemiological importance of seedborne inoculum in pyrethrum production systems.

articles.title: Safety and Efficacy of Transvenous Lead Extraction Using a Right-Sided Approach.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite extensive experience with transvenous lead extraction (TLE) overall, outcomes for systems implanted on the right chest remain underexplored, largely because of their low incidence.

OBJECTIVES: The objective was to evaluate whether system laterality influences TLE outcomes.

METHODS: Using our institutional, prospectively maintained ExTRACT registry, we analyzed all consecutive patients undergoing TLE procedures at the Cleveland Clinic between 1996 and 2022. Patients were categorized by system laterality. Baseline characteristics, procedural characteristics, and complications were assessed. Multivariable logistic regression models evaluated the association between right-sided TLE and adverse events.

RESULTS: Among 4,989 patients, 494 (9.9%) had right-sided and 4,495 (90.1%) had left-sided TLE. Compared with left-sided cases, right-sided cases had longer total lead dwell times (13.83 vs 9.26 years, P < 0.001) and were more likely to be extracted because of infection (47.57% vs 39.71%, P = 0.001). Fluoroscopy time was longer (15.95 vs 12.1 minutes; P < 0.001), and femoral workstation use more frequent (7.89% vs 4.05%, P < 0.001), yet complete extraction was lower (94.53% vs 96.44%, P = 0.034). Right-sided TLE had higher rates of sternotomy (2.83% vs 1.25%, P = 0.004) and superior vena cava or right atrial tear/perforation (2.49% vs 1.10%, P = 0.009). Thirty-day mortality was low and comparable (0.61% vs 0.47%, P = 0.727). Multivariable regression showed that right-sided TLE was associated with higher odds of sternotomy (OR = 1.92, 95% CI: 1.01-3.46, P = 0.037) and superior vena cava or right atrial tear/perforation (OR = 2.02, 95% CI: 1.01-3.78, P = 0.037).

CONCLUSIONS: Right-sided TLE is associated with a lower rate of complete extraction and increased procedural risk, particularly sternotomy and major vascular injury, compared with left-sided TLE. These findings should be carefully weighed when implanting or extracting right-sided systems.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonists Across Geographic Regions in Heart Failure: A Patient-Level Pooled Analysis.
The Gut-Heart-Muscle Hypothesis in Heart Failure: Emerging Associations, Mechanistic Uncertainty, and the Potential Role of Exercise.
Cone-beam computed tomography in endodontics: patient perceptions, outcomes, and radiation awareness: A cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Dental Association (1939)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) on patient-reported outcome measures in endodontics remains largely unexplored. This study aimed to identify patients' perceived values in diagnostic imaging, investigate the impact of CBCT vs periapical radiography (PR), and assess patient knowledge of ionizing radiation.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted with 117 patients referred for endodontic assessment. Participants underwent a clinical assessment with PR and CBCT. A 2-part questionnaire was used to assess radiation knowledge (post-PR) and changes in perception, confidence, and treatment acceptance (post-CBCT). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and χ2 tests (P < .05).

RESULTS: Baseline radiation knowledge was limited, with 59% of participants rating their understanding as poor or very poor. Despite this, patients prioritized diagnostic accuracy over a low radiation dose. The inclusion of CBCT considerably improved patient-reported outcome measures. Overall, 79.5% of participants considered CBCT more useful and helpful than PR, 60.7% reported increased confidence in their treatment plans, and 59.0% reported greater trust in clinicians compared with PR alone. Most participants (89.7%) indicated that they would undergo CBCT for future care if clinically indicated.

CONCLUSIONS: Patients perceived CBCT as superior to PR for understanding their diagnosis and for building confidence in the treatment plan, despite having limited knowledge of ionizing radiation. This suggests that patients perceive the diagnostic benefits of CBCT as outweighing its risks.

PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS: CBCT may enhance patient confidence beyond diagnostics. Clinicians should explain CBCT's diagnostic advantages and radiation risks and enhance the personalized consent process to address gaps in patients' limited knowledge of ionizing radiation.

articles.title: Atrial Flutter in Adolescence Due to Invasive Cardiac Lipoma: A Rare Presentation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary cardiac tumors are rare, with lipomas comprising ∼10% of benign cases. Although typically asymptomatic, invasive variants may infiltrate myocardium and generate significant arrhythmogenic substrate.

CASE SUMMARY: A 14-year-old previously healthy male patient presented with atrial flutter and was found to have a large, infiltrative lipomatous mass involving the right atrium, right ventricle, and tricuspid valve. Biopsy and partial debulking confirmed invasive cardiac lipoma, but complete excision was precluded by extensive myocardial infiltration. Despite antiarrhythmic therapy, he developed recurrent atrial flutter and ventricular dysfunction. Electrophysiology study identified a cavotricuspid isthmus-dependent flutter that was successfully ablated; however, a second tumor-associated circuit was not amenable to ablation because of anatomical barriers. Sinus rhythm was restored with cardioversion and amiodarone with subsequent recovery of ventricular function.

DISCUSSION: Invasive cardiac lipomas present unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, often requiring multimodal imaging, multidisciplinary management, aggressive rhythm control, and consideration of cardiac transplantation in select patients.

articles.title: Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement in an Incomplete Ring With LAMPOON Facilitated By Aortic Prosthesis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter mitral valve replacement in large incomplete flexible mitral bands is high risk because limited anchoring and anterior leaflet displacement may cause embolization or left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction.

CASE SUMMARY: A 54-year-old man with ischemic cardiomyopathy, prior coronary artery bypass grafting, aortic valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement, mitral repair with a 31-mm Duran AnCore band, and tricuspid annuloplasty presented with NYHA functional class IV heart failure from severe recurrent mitral regurgitation. Computed tomography excluded SAPIEN M3 (predicted neo-LVOT 0 mm2) and showed a long anterior mitral leaflet, raising concern for dynamic obstruction despite a predicted neo-LVOT of 347.6 mm2 for a 29-mm balloon-expandable valve. He underwent antegrade base-to-tip laceration of the anterior mitral leaflet to prevent outflow obstruction, followed by valve-in-ring transcatheter mitral valve replacement, with no paravalvular leak or significant LVOT gradient.

DISCUSSION: Anterior aortic prosthetic anatomy facilitated valve anchoring despite the incomplete flexible band, which would have been prohibitive in the absence of anterior bioprosthesis.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Adjacent prosthetic anatomy may be leveraged in selected complex valve-in-ring procedures after meticulous multimodality planning and procedural expertise.

articles.title: Transcatheter Closure of Congenital Aorto-Pulmonary Vein Fistula Causing Recurrent Hemoptysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital descending aorta-pulmonary vein fistula is an exceedingly rare vascular malformation creating a high-pressure left-to-left shunt, most commonly presenting as recurrent hemoptysis.

CASE SUMMARY: A young man presented with a 2-year history of recurrent hemoptysis. Echocardiography revealed turbulent high-velocity flow entering the left atrium via a dilated left inferior pulmonary vein. Computed tomography angiography confirmed an anomalous fistulous vessel from the descending thoracic aorta to the left inferior pulmonary vein. Transcatheter closure was performed using an Amplatzer Vascular Plug 2 (22 mm) delivered through an 8.5-F deflectable sheath, after conventional catheter systems failed because of the acute angle of the fistula origin.

DISCUSSION: Congenital descending aorta-pulmonary vein fistula (cDAPVF) must be distinguished from pulmonary sequestration and pulmonary arteriovenous malformation. This is one of the first reported transcatheter closures of cDAPVF in an adult.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: cDAPVF should be considered in young adults with unexplained recurrent hemoptysis. It can be safely treated with transcatheter device closure using a deflectable sheath and AVP2 (Amplatzer Vascular Plug 2) as an alternative to surgery.

articles.title: Concomitant Wire-Loop Repositioning and Transapical Valve Replacement for a Migrated Sutureless Aortic Valve.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sutureless aortic prosthesis migration is rare but potentially catastrophic.

CASE SUMMARY: A 78-year-old woman on hemodialysis underwent minimally invasive double valve replacement using a sutureless aortic bioprosthesis. Failure to wean from cardiopulmonary bypass prompted intraoperative angiography, which raised suspicion of cranial migration of the aortic prosthesis, with bilateral coronary hypoperfusion; subsequent computed tomography confirmed the diagnosis. Because repositioning after surgical excision of the native leaflets would cause severe aortic regurgitation, a transapical transcatheter valve was prepositioned before transfemoral wire-loop repositioning. Coronary flow was restored, the failed valve was replaced, and 5-month follow-up showed preserved ventricular function and stable frame position.

DISCUSSION: Prepositioning a transapical transcatheter valve before wire-loop repositioning enabled immediate valve replacement while minimizing the empty-annulus interval.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Failed passage of a Perceval sizer should preclude sutureless implantation; prepositioned transapical valve replacement with wire-loop repositioning is a viable bailout.

articles.title: Endoaortic Balloon Occlusion for Minimally Invasive Mitral Valve Replacement After Previous Balloon-Expandable TAVI.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prior transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) may complicate minimally invasive mitral valve surgery when endoaortic balloon occlusion (EABO) is considered. Guidance for EABO after TAVI remains limited.

CASE SUMMARY: A 56-year-old woman with radiation-induced multivalvular disease underwent staged transfemoral balloon-expandable TAVI and coronary revascularization, followed by minimally invasive mitral valve replacement using EABO. Pre-TAVI computed tomography identified a potential ascending-aortic landing zone, and continuous TEE confirmed balloon positioning above the TAVI frame. EABO achieved complete aortic occlusion without migration, frame contact, or evidence of cerebral malperfusion.

DISCUSSION: Prior balloon-expandable TAVI may not preclude EABO in carefully selected patients with favorable ascending-aortic anatomy. Imaging-based selection, continuous TEE surveillance, and controlled inflation are central to safety.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Prior balloon-expandable TAVI does not preclude EABO in selected patients with a suitable ascending-aortic landing zone.

articles.title: Impact of Guideline-Based Acute Kidney Injury Care Processes on Outcomes in Hospitalized Patients With Decompensated Cirrhosis.
articles.abstract:
GOALS: We evaluated whether adherence to acute kidney injury (AKI) specific process measures (PMs) improves outcomes in hospitalized patients with cirrhosis and AKI.

BACKGROUND: Expert bodies recommend PMs for the management of AKI in cirrhosis, but the link between PMs and outcomes is unclear.

STUDY: We performed a retrospective cohort study of patients hospitalized with ascites and AKI at Veterans Administration hospitals. We examined the relationship between PMs [avoidance of diuretics, nonselective beta-blockers (NSBB), and other vasodilators, volume expansion with albumin/crystalloids, infectious work-up, subspecialty consultation, and postdischarge outpatient visit] and patient outcomes. Outcomes were in-hospital AKI resolution and 90-day mortality, adjusted for patient demographics, comorbidities, cirrhosis complications, Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) 3.0 score, and AKI stage.

RESULTS: Among 2221 patients, adherence to PMs varied: NSBB, diuretics, and other vasodilators were avoided in 97%, 79%, and 80% of cases, respectively. Volume expansion with albumin and crystalloids was administered in 21% and 29% of cases, while 47% had an infectious workup and 29% had subspecialty consultation. Postdischarge follow-up rates within 15 days were low: 28% for primary care, 6% for gastroenterology/hepatology, and 1% for nephrology. Overall, 53% achieved AKI resolution, and 40% died within 90 days. Diuretic avoidance was associated with increased likelihood of AKI resolution (OR: 1.14, 95% CI: 1.02-1.28). Timely postdischarge outpatient visits with primary care [hazard ratio (HR): 0.53, 95% CI: 0.43-0.67] or gastroenterology/hepatology (HR: 0.44, 95% CI: 0.29-0.66) were independently associated with reduced 90-day mortality risk.

CONCLUSION: Targeting specific PMs, especially diuretic avoidance and timely postdischarge outpatient visit, may improve outcomes in cirrhosis-associated AKI.

articles.title: Multi-level neurophysiological perspectives on impaired lower-limb muscle synergies during walking after stroke. A systematic scoping review.
articles.journal: European journal of physical and rehabilitation medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gait impairment is one of the most common and disabling consequences of stroke. Abnormal lower-limb muscle synergies represent a key constraint on poststroke gait recovery, yet their underlying neurophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely understood.

METHODS: This systematic scoping review synthesizes evidence on impaired lower-limb muscle synergies during poststroke walking from a multilevel neural control perspective, with a particular focus on supraspinal and spinal regulatory processes. Following the Joanna Briggs Institute methodological framework and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, three databases were systematically searched, and nine studies were ultimately included.

RESULTS: The available evidence suggests that stroke-related alterations in descending motor system interactions, particularly involving corticospinal and corticoreticulospinal pathways, may be associated with abnormalities in the spatial organization and gain modulation of rhythmic neural signals within spinal networks. Although the temporal structure associated with gait rhythm generation may remain relatively preserved after stroke, altered spatial organization within these networks has been associated with reduced and merged muscle synergy modules, altered muscle weightings, and disordered activation timing. Given the limited and heterogeneous evidence currently available, this review proposes a hypothesis-generating multilevel neurophysiological framework in which the spinal networks may represent a potential integrative component contributing to poststroke muscle synergy impairments.

CONCLUSIONS: From this perspective, muscle synergy abnormalities may reflect functional signatures of imbalanced sensorimotor network reorganization rather than purely descriptive gait features. This hypothesis-generating framework may help inform future multimodal assessments and future mechanism-oriented rehabilitation research.

articles.title: 2026 ETA Consensus Statement on the Interpretation and Management of Calcitonin Levels in Patients with Thyroid Nodules.
articles.abstract: Calcitonin (Ctn) is widely recognized as the most accurate test for the early detection of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC). Nevertheless, universal agreement on whether to routinely measure serum Ctn in all patients with thyroid nodules has not been achieved, mainly due to the perceived limited cost-effectiveness, the strict preanalytical workup needed for Ctn measurements, and the difficulties in interpreting borderline or mildly elevated Ctn concentrations in the presence of not fully interchangeable Ctn immunoassays. Although MTC is a rare malignancy, its prognosis is strongly dependent on the stage at diagnosis, that is strictly correlated to Ctn levels that reflect both the presence and burden of MTC. For these reasons the interpretation of preoperative Ctn concentrations, whenever performed, is critically important. This consensus aims to support clinicians who perform Ctn in the work up of thyroid nodules, either routinely or in accordance to the ETA guidelines, in decision-making when Ctn concentrations are above the upper reference limit, but not yet approaching or reaching the diagnostic levels, by identifying those who require surgery, those suitable for follow-up, and those who do not require further investigation.

articles.title: Principal component analysis in analytical chemistry: finding patterns in complex data.
articles.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
articles.abstract: Modern analytical instruments routinely generate datasets with hundreds or thousands of measured variables per sample, far too many to examine by eye or with simple univariate statistics. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is the most widely used method for making sense of such data. It reduces a complex, high-dimensional dataset to a small number of new summary variables, called principal components, which capture the most important patterns of variation. These can be plotted and inspected visually, allowing the analyst to spot clusters of similar samples, detect outliers and identify which measured variables are driving the differences between groups. This Technical Brief explains what PCA is, how it works, the contexts in which it is most useful, and what software is available to carry it out.

articles.title: Hepatic Steatosis in Primary Aldosteronism, Cushing's Syndrome, and Mild Autonomous cortisol secretion: Metabolic and Hormonal Associations.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is closely linked to obesity, diabetes mellitus (DM), and dyslipidemia. Patients with primary aldosteronism (PA), Cushing's syndrome (CS) and mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS) exhibit metabolic abnormalities, but the relative contributions of hormonal and metabolic factors to hepatic steatosis remain unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate MASLD prevalence and determinants in PA, CS, and MACS.

DESIGN: Single-center retrospective cross-sectional study.

METHODS: 243 treatment-naive patients underwent unenhanced abdominal computed tomography: 102 isolated PA, 60 CS, 47 MACS, and 34 PA with cortisol co-secretion. Hepatic steatosis was assessed using liver-to-spleen (L/S) attenuation ratio. Hepatic steatosis index (HSI), and triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index were calculated.

RESULTS: MASLD prevalence was 28.4% in isolated PA, 26.6% in CS, 31.9% in MACS and 26.4% in PA with cortisol co-secretion. Liver attenuation and L/S ratio were similar across groups but correlated with visceral adiposity, glucose, HbA1c, triglycerides, HSI, and TyG index (all r>0.5, p<0.05). DM was independently associated with lower liver attenuation after adjustment for age, sex, and BMI (β = -11.10 HU, 95% CI: -16.40 to -5.79). Serum cortisol, cortisol after the 1-mg DST, aldosterone, and renin were not independently associated with hepatic steatosis, whereas UFC was independently associated with the L/S attenuation ratio in the hypercortisolism subgroup.

CONCLUSIONS: Hepatic steatosis was similarly prevalent across PA, CS, and MACS, and was associated with metabolic factors, particularly DM, BMI, visceral adiposity, and hypertriglyceridemia. These findings support consideration of hepatic steatosis assessment in patients with functional adrenal disorders and metabolic risk factors.

articles.title: GB-79, Leelamine Isonitrile, Defines a New Antifungal Scaffold Active against Drug-Resistant Candida Species.
articles.abstract: The global rise in invasive fungal infections and antifungal resistance highlights an urgent need for new antifungal scaffolds. Using a focused phenotypic screening approach in yeast, we identified the leelamine isonitrile GB-79 as a potent inhibitor of fungal growth. The compound displayed potent antifungal activity in vitro across genetically diverse strains, with lower IC50 values than fluconazole under the experimental conditions tested. Importantly, GB-79 showed strong activity against clinical isolates of Candida albicans, Candida parapsilosis, and Nakaseomyces glabratus (formerly known as Candida glabrata), including strains with reduced susceptibility to existing antifungal agents. In vivo, GB-79 was well tolerated in mice following single-dose oral administration at doses up to 100 mg/kg, with no mortality or marked body-weight changes. Despite high systemic clearance, low exposure after intravenous dosing, and poor oral bioavailability, GB-79 reduced renal fungal burden in C. albicans-infected animals. These findings establish GB-79 as a promising antifungal scaffold and demonstrate the value of phenotypic screening strategies for uncovering new chemical entities with translational potential. GB-79 provides a promising foundation for medicinal chemistry optimization and further development of next-generation antifungal therapeutics.

articles.title: Identification of Secreted Copper-Binding Peptides Associated with Virulence in Pathogenic Pseudomonas and Bordetella.
articles.abstract: Peptides that contain 5-thiooxazole post-translational modifications have recently been identified from various bacteria and implicated in copper homeostasis and virulence. However, knowledge of their copper-binding affinities is limited, and their roles in virulence are not well understood. In this work, we discovered three new 5-thiooxazole-containing peptides from two opportunistic human pathogens, Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Bordetella bronchiseptica. We heterologously produced and structurally characterized two different peptides that originate from P. aeruginosa, pseudomonin and pseudomonin-efh, the latter of which also contains two EF-hand domains for calcium binding. We show that 5-thiooxazole modification in both peptides enables strong Cu(I) binding at 10-16-10-17 M affinity and weaker Cu(II) binding at 10-7 M affinity. Pseudomonin-efh undergoes calcium-dependent changes of overall secondary structure that are negated by copper. Genetic studies revealed the 5-thiooxazole modification of pseudomonin-efh is required for calcium-dependent virulence regulation in a lettuce infection model for P. aeruginosa. Further, we identified and characterized a related 5-thiooxazole-containing peptide, bordetellin, secreted by its native producer, B. bronchiseptica, in the virulent phase. Our work demonstrates a strong preference for Cu(I) binding by 5-thiooxazole-containing peptides and uncovers a role of these peptides in Ca/Cu-dependent virulence regulation. Identifying 5-thiooxazole-containing peptides from pathogenic bacteria and detecting their secretion in the native producer is a critical step toward understanding the functions of these peptides in virulence and pathogen-host interactions.

articles.title: Targeting Force-Regulated FimH Adhesin: Assays, Mannosides, and Biologics for Anti-Virulence Therapy of UPEC Infection.
articles.abstract: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are among the most common bacterial infections, and recurrent UTIs caused by uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC) drive antibiotic use and antimicrobial resistance. FimH, the mannose-binding adhesin at the tip of type 1 pili, is a central UPEC virulence factor. Under shear force, FimH switches from a low-affinity, tense state to a high-affinity, relaxed state, strengthening adhesion during urine flow. This catch-bond behavior makes FimH a promising anti-virulence target, though a difficult one to drug. Here, we review strategies to target FimH, including monovalent and multivalent mannosides, vaccines, conformation-selective monoclonal antibodies, and de novo engineered miniproteins, together with the assays used to quantify FimH-ligand binding and UPEC adhesion. Clinical translation has been limited by assay-dependent potency, urinary pharmacokinetics, and intracellular reservoirs. We posit that effective FimH-targeted therapy requires alignment among inhibitor mechanism, FimH conformational state, bladder lumen exposure, and infection stage, which in turn defines realistic roles in prevention, early intervention, and combination therapy.

articles.title: ATR-FTIR Spectroscopy Combined with Machine Learning Enables Detection of Schistosomiasis-Associated Biochemical Signatures in Human Serum.
articles.abstract: Schistosomiasis, caused by Schistosoma mansoni, remains a major public health burden in endemic regions, demanding rapid and reliable diagnostic strategies. Here, we report a label-free diagnostic platform based on attenuated total reflectance Fourier transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy combined with machine learning for the detection of infection-associated biochemical signatures in human serum. A total of 112 serum samples (54 infected and 58 noninfected individuals) were analyzed, with parasitological examination revealing only S. mansoni eggs in all positive samples, with no other parasitic coinfections detected. Spectral data were preprocessed and classified using supervised machine learning algorithms. First-derivative preprocessing combined with a Random Forest classifier showed the best performance in the initial cross-validation analysis, achieving 0.80 accuracy, 0.81 sensitivity, 0.79 specificity, an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.83, and an F1-score of 0.80. To further assess model robustness, nested cross-validation yielded an accuracy of 0.76 ± 0.07, sensitivity of 0.76 ± 0.16, specificity of 0.77 ± 0.19, AUC of 0.83 ± 0.11, and F1-score of 0.76 ± 0.08, providing a more conservative estimate of performance. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis identified spectral regions associated with proteins, nucleic acids, and carbohydrates that contributed to model predictions. Additional sensitivity analyses indicated spectral differences between endemic-area and nonendemic-area controls and reduced performance in cross-site evaluation, highlighting geographic and cohort-related variation as a potential limitation to model generalizability. Overall, ATR-FTIR spectroscopy combined with machine learning shows potential as a rapid, reagent-free, and minimally sample-intensive complementary approach for schistosomiasis screening, warranting validation in larger, geographically diverse cohorts.

articles.title: Fungal Phosphatase-Dependent Induction of Host Cell Pyroptosis by Candidalysin.
articles.abstract: Fungal infections pose a major public health threat and can cause host cell damage through diverse forms of regulated cell death. However, our understanding of how fungal pathogens interact with host to elicit pyroptosis remains in its infancy. Here, we show that candidalysin, the cytolytic peptide toxin of Candida albicans, induces cell type-specific pyroptosis in epithelial cells and macrophages through GSDME and GSDMD activation, respectively. Dynamic dual transcriptomic profiling of host-fungal interaction suggested associations of candidalysin-induced pyroptosis with CCND1 in macrophages and BHLHE40 in epithelial cells, together with shared changes in phosphatase-related genes in C. albicans. In vivo, C. albicans infection induced a biphasic pyroptosis in kidney, characterized by early Caspase-3-GSDME and later Caspase-1-GSDMD activation. Candidalysin deficiency reduced pyroptotic responses and increased host CCND1 expression, whereas CCND1 knockdown enhanced pyroptosis. Furthermore, PHO100-mediated phosphate regulation contributed to fungal growth and hyphal development under phosphate limitation and influenced host pyroptotic responses. Together, these findings highlight a potential role for fungal phosphate-related regulation in candidalysin-associated pyroptosis and C. albicans pathogenicity.

articles.title: Hypothyroidism Improves Survival in Experimental Peritonitis.
articles.abstract: Hypothyroidism decreases the basal metabolic rate. Using three models of peritonitis, intraperitoneal LPS plus Zymosan challenge, cecal slurry-induced intraperitoneal infection, and cecal ligation and puncture, we demonstrate that hypothyroid mice show enhanced survival compared to euthyroid mice. Hypothyroid mice show lower energy expenditure, reduced CO2/O2 exchange, and decreased movements prior to treatment. However, they maintain greater physiological stability following LPS plus zymosan challenge and are capable of recovering homeostatic values. In contrast, euthyroid mice, which begin with higher energy expenditure and CO2/O2 exchange rates, show a rapid sharp decline and severe hypoglycemia after treatment, not observed in hypothyroid mice. Two days postchallenge, hypothyroid mice exhibit decreased levels of circulating proinflammatory cytokines and tissue-specific IL-6 in liver, lung, and kidney. Consequently, hypothyroid mice exhibit significantly lower circulating levels of systemic, hepatic, renal, and pulmonary tissue-damage markers. These findings correlate with a decrease in ferroptosis and an attenuation of hepatic phospholipid peroxidation. In the early hours following peritoneal cecal slurry-induced infection, hypothyroid mice display a significant decrease in peritoneal levels of proinflammatory cytokines and circulating neutrophil counts. Crucially, both groups show comparable intraperitoneal bacterial proliferation, similar counts of both large and small peritoneal macrophages, with an analogous phagocytic capacity and similar disappearance rate. In conclusion, hypothyroidism increases tolerance to polymicrobial peritoneal infection, specifically by mitigating inflammation and disease severity while leaving bacterial dynamics unaffected.

articles.title: From First Symptoms to Multidisciplinary Care: Results of a patient-centred European Survey on Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia.
articles.abstract: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia (MEN) syndromes are rare hereditary endocrine disorders with multisystem tumour burden, complex surveillance requirements, and significant psychosocial impact. Patient-centred data on diagnostic experiences and on information-provision quality remain limited. The online survey of 133 European MEN patients was administered from 10.11.2023 to 01.09.2025. Participants reported diagnostic journeys, information adequacy, specialist knowledge, care structure, current health status, and their research and care priorities utilizing mainly Likert scales and multiple-choice formats. Statistical analysis included descriptive statistics. Time from first symptom to diagnosis exceeded twelve months in 48.9% and five years in 26.3% with 50.0% of respondents reporting straightforward referral. Only 42.1% rated disease information and 48.1% their physician's MEN knowledge as good/excellent, prompting reliance on non-clinical channels like advocacy groups (72.2%). Centres of Expertise (CoE) involvement was most frequent in patients with 1-5 years diagnostic delay (53.3%) while Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) care was most frequent in patients with incidental diagnosis (64.0%). Of the respondents with incidental diagnosis, 28.0% reported their physical health as "bad" compared to 57.1% in patients experiencing a delay exceeding five years. Unmet needs are according to patients diagnosed incidentally or within 0-12 months "Knowledge & Information," whereas patients experiencing diagnostic delays exceeding five years prioritized "Research & Cure" and "Early Diagnosis".This survey reveals substantial unmet needs in diagnostic timing, information provision, specialist knowledge and access to specialized care. Interventions including enhanced primary care education, standardized patient information materials, CoE expansion, and mandatory MDT involvement could improve diagnostic delay and treatment quality.

articles.title: Non-invasive and invasive imaging for guiding PCI of chronic total occlusions.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for chronic total occlusions (CTO) remains technically challenging, with lower technical success than non-CTO PCI. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) and intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) may improve procedural and stent-related outcomes by supporting procedural planning, lesion crossing, and stent optimization.

AREAS COVERED: A literature search of PubMed, Google scholar, identified randomized trials, registries, observational studies, meta-analyses, and consensus documents on CCTA and IVUS in CTO PCI. CCTA enables three-dimensional assessment of cap morphology, occlusion length, tortuosity, calcification, and distal vessel quality, refining complexity assessment and strategy selection. IVUS provides real-time guidance for proximal cap identification, guidewire position, reentry techniques, vessel sizing, and stent optimization. Artificial intelligence and image co-registration are also discussed.

EXPERT OPINION: CCTA and IVUS provide complementary information across the stages of CTO PCI. Selective preprocedural CCTA may be most valuable in anatomically complex lesions, whereas IVUS supports lesion crossing and should be strongly considered for stent optimization. Wider adoption will depend on workflow integration, operator training, automated image analysis, and prospective validation of imaging-guided strategies.

articles.title: Preimplantation genetic testing in Italy: a single-cycle retrospective analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preimplantation genetic testing (PGT) is a diagnostic procedure performed during assisted reproductive technology (ART) to detect chromosomal and monogenic abnormalities before embryo transfer. In Italy, the Italian ART Register (IARTR) monitors ART and PGT activity. Within a National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR) project, entitled "Development of the Italian Preimplantation Genetic Testing (PGT) Network", we developed a monitoring system based on ART single-cycles in which PGT was performed.

METHODS: Data on ART-PGT cycles performed in 2024 were collected from 24 Italian ART centers. A relational database was developed including cycle-level and embryo-level variables. Statistical analyses were performed using IBM SPSS Statistics, Version 29 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA).

RESULTS: Overall, 2181 ART-PGT cycles involving 1358 patients were analyzed. Genetic testing was performed in 1195 cycles during 2024, and next-generation sequencing was the most frequent technology (96.5%). PGT for aneuploidies (PGT-A) was the most frequent procedure (1065 cycles), followed by PGT for monogenic/single gene defects (PGT-M) (114 cycles) and PGT for structural rearrangements (PGT-SR) (110 cycles). The main indication for PGT-A was advanced maternal age (59.4%), for PGT-M was beta-thalassemia (29.6%), for PGT-SR reciprocal chromosomal rearrangements (61.3%). A total of 3771 embryos were analyzed, of which 7% yielded no result. Most blastocysts were biopsied on day 5 or 6 and were classified as having good or optimal quality. Embryo transfer was performed in 761 cycles, most as single embryo transfer, resulting in a clinical pregnancy rate of 49.1%.

CONCLUSIONS: The single-cycle monitoring system for ART-PGT was feasible and effective in collecting detailed clinical and laboratory data. This approach represents an innovation in epidemiological surveillance and may be useful in quality assessment and standardization of ART-PGT practices in Italy.

articles.title: The Impact of Early Changes in Albumin Levels on Long-Term Kidney and Mortality Outcomes in Patients With Acute Kidney Injury Undergoing Continuous Kidney Replacement Therapy.
authors: LINking health medical records, biospecimens, and biosignals in Korean patients with Acute kidney injury consortium (LINKA) investigators
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the association between early changes in the levels of serum albumin during continuous kidney replacement therapy (CKRT) and long-term dialysis dependence and mortality in patients with acute kidney injury who survived for 90 days or more days after CKRT initiation.

DESIGN: A multicenter retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: Eight university-affiliated tertiary hospitals in South Korea participating in the LINking health medical records, biospecimens, and biosignals in Korean patients with Acute kidney injury consortium cohort.

PATIENTS: The study involved 1087 adult patients with acute kidney injury who survived for 90 or more days after CKRT initiation between January 2017 and June 2022.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Based on albumin levels at CKRT initiation and on day 7, patients were categorized into the persistent, resolved, new-onset, and no hypoalbuminemia groups. A composite of progression to end-stage kidney disease and all-cause mortality within 365 days was the primary outcome. The composite outcome occurred in 33.4% (363/1087) of the patients. The adjusted odds ratio (aOR) for the primary outcome was significantly higher in all groups when compared with the no hypoalbuminemia group (persistent: aOR, 2.64; 95% CI, 1.73-4.04; p < 0.001; resolved: aOR, 2.27; 95% CI, 1.38-3.75; p < 0.001; new-onset: aOR, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.06-2.68; p = 0.028). No hypoalbuminemia group was associated with the most favorable prognosis, whereas persistent hypoalbuminemia was associated with the worst outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: During CKRT, early albumin level changes are associated with long-term kidney failure and mortality risk. Persistent hypoalbuminemia predicts the worst outcomes. Even in patients without baseline hypoalbuminemia, early decline in albumin is associated with worse prognosis.

articles.title: Causal Machine Learning for Treatment Effect Heterogeneity: Interpretation, Benchmarking, Validation.
articles.abstract: Causal machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising approach for predicting individualized treatment effects and advancing precision medicine, moving beyond the limitations of conventional one-variable-at-a-time subgroup analyses of randomized trials. A recent benchmarking study by Chen and colleagues evaluated several causal ML learners across two large trials and concluded that current methods do not yet demonstrate reliable performance for clinical application. While such applied methodological investigations are valuable, this conclusion warrants a more nuanced examination. Multiple independent research groups have successfully applied causal ML across respiratory medicine and critical care, identifying clinically meaningful treatment effect heterogeneity that prior subgroup analyses had not resolved, although these applications have methodological limitations and do not yet establish that the detected heterogeneity is robust across internal and external validation. We outline four sequential and iterative dimensions central to credible causal ML analyses: choice of learner, model training with cross-fitting, internal validation using calibration-for-benefit and rank-weighted metrics, and external validation aligned with the original causal question. With careful methodological execution, causal ML holds considerable promise for personalized treatment decisions and warrants continued development; dismissing the field prematurely risks overlooking a powerful tool for personalized treatment decisions.

articles.title: Development and Internal Validation of a Two-Year Prognostic Risk Index for Functional Decline in Adults Aging with HIV.
articles.journal: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: People with HIV (PWH) are at risk for functional decline and disability due to a complex interplay of factors, yet longitudinal studies of everyday functioning in this population are lacking. To identify individuals at risk for functional decline, we developed an internally validated, point-based prognostic risk index.

METHODS: 742 PWH were assessed in the CNS HIV Anti-Retroviral Therapy Effects Research (CHARTER) study at five visits over two years. To select predictors of self-reported functional dependence, a binary logistic regression was performed using Akaike information criterion-guided backward stepwise selection. Model performance, discrimination, and calibration were assessed. The final model was internally validated by bootstrapping and optimism corrected. Risk index scores were generated using adjusted beta coefficients and a risk score cut-off was determined.

RESULTS: Baseline predictors of functional dependence included elevated depressive symptoms, thrombocytopenia (platelets <150x103/μL), fine motor skills impairment, older age, and unemployment. White race, chronic pulmonary disease, and lifetime major depressive disorder were also retained. The risk score ranged from 0-63 points with a threshold value having good sensitivity (81%) and discriminability (c-statistic = 0.80) for functional dependence. However, it also had only moderate specificity (70%) with a high false positive rate.

CONCLUSIONS: A combination of demographics, fine motor skills, depression, and medical conditions predict functional decline. Additional studies examining external validity of the index in large, age-diverse samples of PWH with functional impairment are required before deployment in clinical settings.

articles.title: Electronic Children's Hospital Early Warning Score: Development and Validation of a Novel Machine Learning Algorithm Predicting Critical Deterioration Events in a Retrospective, Single-Center Cohort.
articles.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and validate a novel, machine learning prediction model for critical deterioration events.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: Single quaternary care freestanding pediatric hospital.

PATIENTS: All patients up to 21 years old admitted to acute care wards (excluding cardiac and psychiatry units) between January 2012 and June 2023.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The primary outcome was a critical deterioration, defined as utilization of advanced respiratory support or continuous IV medication infusions not administered on acute care units. Secondary outcome was ICU transfer. Each outcome was evaluated between 6 and 30 hours after each prediction score. Among 179,074 unique hospitalizations with 2,803,017 windows of scoring data, 10,656 (0.4%) had a subsequent critical deterioration event. Compared with the legacy Children's Hospital Early Warning Score (CHEWS), the model, which we call electronic CHEWS (eCHEWS), had a higher area under the precision-recall curve (0.157; 95% CI [0.150-0.164]) vs. 0.017; 95% CI [0.013-0.027]). At sensitivity approximately 44%, CHEWS had positive predictive value (PPV) 1.8% (number needed to alert [NNA] 55), whereas eCHEWS had PPV 11.4% (NNA 9).

CONCLUSIONS: eCHEWS outperforms traditional early warning scores for predicting critical deterioration among acute care inpatients and can detect critical deterioration at least 6 hours before occurrence. If prospectively validated, eCHEWS could serve as an early warning trigger integrated into the electronic health record to support proactive rounding, escalation decisions, and timely transfer to ICUs.

articles.title: Language Concordance in Critical Care: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Language barriers are associated with differences in care delivery processes and outcomes in critical care settings, with differences despite language assistance services. Less is known about outcomes associated with language concordant care. Language concordance is a linguistic match between a patient's preferred language and the language used by their care team. We undertook a systematic review to examine the measurement and impact of language concordant care delivery during critical illness, inclusive of the critical care recovery period after hospitalization.

DATA SOURCES AND STUDY SELECTION: A systematic review was conducted in PubMed, CINAHL, PsycINFO, Embase, and Cochrane of English-language publications from database inception to March 3, 2026. Studies that investigated adults in critical care and post-ICU recovery clinic settings that included measurement of language concordance were included. Study quality was evaluated by the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist.

DATA SYNTHESIS: Of 1,682 unique records identified, 11 were eligible for inclusion (128,181 total patients; mean [sd] age, 68.4 [17.9 yr]; 72,872 [56.9%] male and 55,082 [43.1%] female). Six studies assessed clinical decision-making. Reported outcomes included code status changes, family conferences, communication complexity, delirium, length of stay, mechanical ventilation, and mortality. Due to significant heterogeneity in study analyses and reported outcomes, data were not pooled for quantitative analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence suggests that language-concordant care may influence clinically meaningful processes of critical care, warranting interventional studies to guide care delivery recommendations.

articles.title: Sepsis Point Prevalence Across Ibero-Latin America PICUs: The 2024 Sepsis Prevalence Assessment Database in Pediatrics (SPREAD PED IBERO-LATAM).
authors: and the SPREAD PED IBERO-LATAM Investigators
articles.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the prevalence and outcome of sepsis in PICUs across Ibero-Latin America; to identify patient- and institution-level factors associated with mortality; and to explore the prognostic performance of pediatric sepsis definitions.

DESIGN: Multinational, multicenter, prospective point prevalence study with follow-up to hospital discharge.

SETTING: One hundred sixty-eight PICUs in 21 countries across Latin America, Spain, and Portugal.

PATIENTS: Children of 28 days to 18 years with a clinical diagnosis of sepsis or septic shock admitted to participating PICUs between September 9 and September 13, 2024.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Among 1318 screened PICU patients, 340 met criteria for clinical sepsis, yielding a point prevalence of 25.8% (95% CI, 23.5-28.2%). Complete outcome data were available for 324 patients. PICU mortality was 42 of 324 (13.0% [95% CI, 9.5-17.1%), and total in-hospital mortality was 49 of 324 (15.1% [95% CI, 11.4-19.4%]). Cardiovascular and respiratory dysfunction were most frequent, whereas multivariable logistic regression identified greater odds of PICU mortality associated with renal dysfunction (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 3.2 [95% CI, 1.5-7.5]) and immunologic dysfunction (aOR, 12.7 [95% CI, 4.6-37.5]).In multivariable analysis, abnormal nutritional status, lack of vaccination, renal dysfunction, and admission to PICUs with intermediate or low resource availability were associated with greater odds of PICU mortality. In exploratory analyses, the Phoenix sepsis criteria identified 95.2% of PICU deaths, but the positive predictive value of the score for mortality was no different from the 2005 International Pediatric Sepsis Consensus Conference criteria.

CONCLUSIONS: In 2024, in Ibero-Latin American PICUs, sepsis affected approximately one in four admissions, and the diagnosis was associated with mortality. Both patient vulnerability and institutional resource availability were associated with greater odds of mortality, underscoring the potential influence of health system capacity on pediatric sepsis outcomes in the region.

articles.title: Who Counts in Pediatric Sepsis? Lessons From Ibero-Latin America.
articles.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies

articles.title: Predicting Motor Recovery in the Subacute Phase of Stroke: The Role of Passive Motor Task and Electroencephalogram Brain Networks.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: In stroke rehabilitation, the identification of reliable prognostic factors remains a challenge for effective rehabilitation strategies. This study investigates which motor task has the most predictive utility based on electroencephalogram (EEG) characteristics during the subacute phase of stroke.

METHODS: Data were collected from 10 subacute stroke patients performed different motor tasks (passive, robotic movement; active, voluntary execution; motor imagery [MI]) and a nonmotor task (No-Go) at two time points: T1, approximately 3 weeks after stroke onset, and T2, 2 months after T1. EEG power and network characteristics were extracted for each task, and prognostic models were constructed with nested leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) cross-validation (CV) to avoid information leakage.

RESULTS: Our findings show that the passive task model produced the strongest internal predictive performance across all task conditions (root-mean-square error 5.94; nested LOSO CV-R2, 0.91), with ipsilesional/contralesional motor area event-related desynchronization, characteristic path length, and clustering coefficient emerging as consistent prognostic features. The passive task also showed less overactivation and hyperconnectivity in the early subacute phase relative to the active and MI tasks. This performance advantage was replicated across six analytic procedures (2 feature-selection × 3 regression strategies), supporting the robustness of the task comparison within the present dataset.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that EEG features obtained during a robot-assisted passive task may provide exploratory prognostic utility for motor recovery prediction in the early subacute phase of stroke.Impact StatementThe passive task may offer a practical approach for assessing neurophysiological markers of recovery potential, supporting the development of more personalized rehabilitation strategies and earlier prognostic evaluation in stroke patients.

articles.title: GFR Measured with Computed Tomography for Platinum Treatment Decision-Making in Urothelial Carcinoma: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate assessment of glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is essential for cisplatin eligibility and carboplatin dosing. We recently demonstrated that GFR measured using iodinated contrast agent clearance derived from 4-phase CT urography (CT-mGFR) showed good agreement with iohexol clearance in both healthy individuals and patients with chronic kidney disease. We aimed to evaluate the impact of CT-mGFR on platinum selection and whether CT-mGFR-based carboplatin dosing might reduce toxicity in urothelial carcinoma.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients with urothelial carcinoma treated with platinum-based chemotherapy who had 4-phase CT urography within 6 months before cancer treatment and stable estimated GFR (eGFR). Primary endpoints were, first, the proportion of patients in whom CT-mGFR would have changed the choice between cisplatin and carboplatin compared with 2009 CKD-EPIcr based decision-making (equation used in routine clinical practice in France) using a 60 ml/min/1.73m2 threshold, and second, the association between grade 3-4 carboplatin-related hematologic toxicity and the relative dose difference between CT-mGFR-predicted and administered doses. Relative dose differences within ±15% were considered concordant. Severe hematologic toxicity was defined as Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events grade 3-4. Associations were assessed using Fisher's exact test and logistic regression.

RESULTS: Forty-seven patients were included (79% male), with a median age of 69 years (IQR, 62-75). CT-mGFR and 2009 CKD-EPIcr-based eGFR led to discordant platinum treatment decisions in 10 patients (21%). The sensitivity and specificity of 2009 CKD-EPIcr for identifying CT-mGFR <60 mL/min/1.73m2 were 68.4% and 85.7%, respectively. CT-mGFR-based carboplatin dosing identified potential overdosing in 4 patients, 3 of whom developed severe hematologic toxicity, compared with 1 of 9 patients with concordant dosing and none of 6 with underdosing (p=0.02).

CONCLUSIONS: CT-mGFR may help optimize platinum treatment decision-making and carboplatin dosing in urothelial carcinoma. These findings should be confirmed in larger prospective multicenter studies.

articles.title: Sphingolipids as Mediators of the Markers of Kidney Function/Heart Failure Association: The Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure is a common complication of CKD. Sphingolipids, including ceramides and sphingomyelins, are lipid molecules with regulatory and signaling properties. Sphingolipids associated with kidney function and incident heart failure. We previously demonstrated that sphingolipids partially mediate the association between kidney function and incident heart failure. We sought to confirm this finding in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.

METHODS: All sphingolipids were measured at baseline using tandem-mass spectrometry. Baseline kidney function was assessed using albuminuria and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Associations of albuminuria and eGFR with heart failure were tested by Cox and Weibull regressions. We tested the mediation effect of sphingolipids on the associations of eGFR and albuminuria with heart failure via quasi-Bayesian Monte Carlo method based on normal approximation with 2,000 simulations. Analyses tested Bonferroni-corrected p-values 0.00625 (0.05/8 sphingolipids).

RESULTS: Among 3,959 participants, the mean (SD) eGFR was 95 (17) mL/min/1.73 m2, and median (Q1, Q3) albuminuria was 5.10 (3.20, 10.2) mg/g creatinine. We observed 438 incident heart failure events over a median (Q1, Q3) follow-up of 18.9 (15.0, 19.6) years. Greater ceramide and sphingomyelin 16:0 and lesser sphingomyelin 20:0 were associated with higher heart failure risk. Sphingomyelin 16:0 was associated with partial 9%, 95% CI 3%, 30%) mediation of the association between eGFR and heart failure, and 4% (1%, 9%) mediation of the association between albuminuria and heart failure. Sphingomyelin 20:0 partially mediated the eGFR/heart failure association (6%, 95% CI 1%, 21% of association mediated).

CONCLUSIONS: Plasma sphingomyelins were associated with partial mediation of the associations of eGFR and albuminuria with incident heart failure.

articles.title: Serologic Discrimination of Histologic Classes in Lupus Nephritis: A Cross-Sectional Analysis with Exploratory 12-Month Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anti-dsDNA positivity and hypocomplementemia are markers of active lupus nephritis (LN), but their ability to discriminate between histologic phenotypes remains underexplored, particularly for mixed proliferative/membranous LN (mixed LN). We compared baseline serologic markers across proliferative LN, membranous LN, and mixed LN, and evaluated their discriminative performance for histologic class.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study of 132 patients with biopsy-proven LN, categorized according to the International Society of Nephrology/Renal Pathology Society (ISN/RPS) classification into proliferative LN (class III/IV), membranous LN (class V), and mixed LN (class III/IV+V). Baseline anti-dsDNA and complements C3 and C4 were compared across groups. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis assessed the ability of individual and combined markers to discriminate between histologic classes. Kidney outcomes at 12 months were explored in a secondary cohort (n=88).

RESULTS: Of 132 patients, 57 had proliferative LN, 32 had membranous LN, and 43 had mixed LN. Anti-dsDNA was significantly higher, and C3 and C4 significantly lower, in proliferative and mixed LN compared to membranous LN (P<0.05 for all), while proliferative and mixed LN did not differ significantly. On ROC analysis, individual markers achieved AUCs of 0.68-0.71 for distinguishing proliferative or mixed LN from membranous LN, with combined models yielding AUCs of 0.73. However, discrimination between proliferative and mixed LN was poor (combined AUC 0.62). At 12 months, kidney outcomes were comparable across groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Mixed LN exhibits a serologic profile resembling proliferative LN, both sharing elevated anti-dsDNA and low complement levels, but distinct from membranous LN. Serology could inform suspicion for LN class but cannot replace kidney biopsy.

articles.title: Ten-Year Neonatal Intensive Care Cohort of Pulmonary Adaptation Failure: Sepsis Incidence and Antibiotic Treatments.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Pulmonary adaptation failure, a mild neonatal respiratory distress, is diagnosed clinically. Many guidelines recommend antibiotics for all respiratory symptoms to cover potential septicaemia. However, early antibiotic exposure may have long-term adverse effects. We investigated management of neonatal respiratory symptoms compared to incidence of early onset sepsis (EOS) in a 10-year intensive care cohort.

METHODS: This population-based observational study included neonates (gestation > 32 weeks) admitted early to intensive care for respiratory distress, suspected infection, or sepsis, between January 2013 and December 2022 at Oulu University Hospital, Oulu, Finland. Clinical data were obtained from hospital databases.

RESULTS: During a decade, 79 003 infants were born alive in Northern Finland and 6377 required early intensive care. After database screening with preset diagnoses, 2957 mother-infant-dyads' records were reviewed manually; 513 were excluded and 2444 analysed. Early antibiotic use was common (n = 1575; 64.4%) whereas true EOS was rare (n = 17; 0.7%). Incidences of respiratory symptoms and EOS were 30.9 and 0.215 per 1000 live-born, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Empirical antibiotic treatment was common, although mild respiratory symptoms likely did not justify initiation of antibiotics. More precise diagnostics of neonatal clinical entities are required for more judicious antibiotic stewardship, updating future guidelines and preventing bacterial resistance.

articles.title: CHD4 promotes hepatitis B virus transcription by facilitating RNA polymerase II recruitment to cccDNA.
articles.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major global health burden, largely due to the persistence of covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA), which serves as the template for viral transcription. Although host factors involved in regulating cccDNA transcription have been increasingly recognized, the molecular mechanisms controlling HBV minichromosome activity remain incompletely understood. Chromodomain helicase DNA-binding protein 4 (CHD4), the catalytic component of the nucleosome remodeling and deacetylase (NuRD) complex, is a key regulator of chromatin remodeling and transcriptional regulation. In this study, we demonstrate that CHD4 facilitates efficient HBV transcription. Depletion of CHD4 in HBV-infected hepatoma cells markedly reduced viral RNA levels and antigen production without affecting HBV uptake, nuclear import, cccDNA establishment, or cccDNA stability. Mechanistically, CHD4 was recruited to HBV cccDNA and promoted the occupancy of RNA polymerase II (RNA Pol II) on the viral minichromosome. Loss of CHD4 impaired RNA Pol II recruitment to cccDNA, resulting in reduced viral transcription. Furthermore, domain mapping identified the CT2 region of CHD4 as essential for its interaction with RNA Pol II. Collectively, our findings reveal a previously unrecognized role of CHD4 in regulating HBV cccDNA transcription and establish CHD4-mediated RNA Pol II recruitment as a critical mechanism controlling HBV gene expression.IMPORTANCEHepatitis B virus (HBV) infection affects hundreds of millions of people worldwide and can lead to severe liver diseases, including cirrhosis and liver cancer. A major challenge in curing HBV infection is the persistence of a stable viral DNA structure inside infected liver cells that continuously produces viral components. Understanding how this viral DNA is controlled by host cells is essential for developing new therapeutic strategies. In this study, we identified chromodomain helicase DNA-binding protein 4 (CHD4) as a host factor that supports HBV gene production by helping the virus recruit the cellular machinery required for viral RNA synthesis. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism by which human liver cells regulate HBV persistence and provide new insights into virus-host interactions that may guide future approaches to achieve durable HBV control.

articles.title: Comparative analysis of first-time pulmonary vein isolation in atrial fibrillation patients with heart failure with reduced versus non-reduced ejection fraction: A retrospective single-center study.
Predominance of viral core functions over auxiliary metabolism among carbohydrate-active enzymes annotated in the global soil virosphere.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Soil viruses are increasingly recognized as components of microbial communities with the potential to alter ecosystem functioning, yet the frequency and functional distribution of virus-encoded metabolic genes in soils remain poorly understood. Here, the Global Soil Virus Atlas gene catalog, comprising 1,432,147 viral genes from 1,223 samples across 12 ecosystem types, was searched against KEGG, Pfam, and CAZy for functions related to carbon cycling, nitrogen cycling, and antimicrobial resistance. Annotations associated with host entry or cell-wall lysis were separated from putative auxiliary metabolic functions. Of 5,020 initial gene-level functional annotations across the three categories, 3,322 (66.2%) were classified as peptidoglycanases. Their exclusion left 1,698 genes (0.14% of the gene catalog restricted to contigs ≥10 kb), and carbon-cycling functions represented 96.7% of the enzyme-resolved annotations. Chitinase-associated genes formed the largest carbon category, but 78.0% belonged to GH19, a family containing both chitinases and phage endolysins. Among GH19 genes on contigs encoding detectable holins or spanins, 84.2% occurred within three genes of these lysis components, a distribution comparable to that of canonical phage lysozymes. Across six matched metagenomic studies, estimated viral contributions to the targeted functions ranged from 0.00% to 8.45% (mean: 2.27%). Two of the three estimates exceeding 2% were GH19-associated chitinase estimates from rhizosphere soils and were therefore treated as upper estimates. Thus, the putative soil viral metabolic inventory was sparse and concentrated in carbon-degradation functions, whereas much of the initial carbohydrate-active enzyme signal reflected core viral lysis functions rather than auxiliary metabolism.

IMPORTANCE: Soil microorganisms drive decomposition and nutrient cycling, and the viruses that infect them may alter these processes by carrying genes that affect host metabolism. However, genes annotated as carbohydrate-degradation enzymes may instead help viruses enter cells or break host cell walls when new virus particles are released. In a worldwide catalog of soil viruses, approximately two-thirds of the initial functional assignments represented these infection or release activities. After their removal, putative viral auxiliary metabolic genes were uncommon and concentrated mainly in carbon degradation. Genes potentially involved in chitin degradation were most frequent, but many occurred near viral genes used to break host cells; their estimated contribution should therefore be viewed as an upper limit. Distinguishing core viral functions from host metabolic modification is essential to avoid overestimating viral contributions to soil processes and to identify the strongest candidates for experimental testing.

articles.title: Rhodococcus rhodnii boosts host tolerance and mitigates virulence of Serratia species in Rhodnius prolixus.
articles.abstract: Insects contend with myriad microbes throughout their lives. These microbial interactions, ranging from beneficial to pathogenic, have important consequences for the insect host, and simultaneous infection with multiple microbes is the norm. We are increasingly aware of how within-host interactions between the endogenous microbiota and invading pathogens can influence host infection outcomes. In this study, we examined how symbiont-pathogen interactions influence pathogen infection in the insect Rhodnius prolixus and how virulence can vary drastically with the context of infection, including cases where the endogenous microbiota is disrupted. Leveraging our ability to rear symbiont-free, or aposymbiotic, individuals, we first challenged symbiotic and aposymbiotic R. prolixus with three Serratia strains of varying virulence (two virulent Serratia marcescens strains and one avirulent Serratia ureilytica strain). We further altered the context of infection by varying the order of symbiont and pathogen colonization, as well as the method of inoculation (i.e., ingestion vs injection). Within R. prolixus, we showed a strong mitigating effect on virulence with the presence of Rhodococcus rhodnii, a well-established R. prolixus symbiont, despite high Serratia burdens. Virulence varied not only by Serratia strain but also by host species, with R. prolixus being particularly susceptible to infection among the four insect species tested. Our findings corroborate the importance of context in determining pathogen virulence, with symbiont presence, in particular, playing a key role in the outcome of pathogen infection for R. prolixus.IMPORTANCEThroughout their lives, insects encounter many bacteria, some beneficial and some detrimental. Increasingly, we are aware of how resident bacteria in the insect gut impact the ability of pathogenic microbes to establish and cause harm. Understanding the factors that underlie the specificity of these interactions is important in furthering our ability to leverage pathogenic microbes for the control of insect pests. This study focuses on the kissing bug, Rhodnius prolixus, a medically important insect that transmits Chagas disease. We tested the impact of different conditions in determining the virulence of the pathogen Serratia marcescens. Kissing bugs suffered high levels of mortality when infected with Serratia, particularly compared to other insect species. We determined that the presence of a beneficial bacterium (Rhodococcus rhodnii) in the kissing bug mitigated the ill effects of infection with Serratia. Early establishment of the beneficial bacteria was key to maximizing this effect.

articles.title: Renal Outcomes and Variant Effects in Monoallelic COL4A3/COL4A4-Related Alport Syndrome: A Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autosomal dominant Alport syndrome (AD-AS) is caused by pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants in COL4A3 and COL4A4. Its clinical spectrum ranges from isolated hematuria to proteinuric chronic kidney disease (CKD) eventually progressing to kidney failure (KF). We aimed to characterize the clinical and genetic profile of AD-AS in northwest Portugal, with particular focus on the recurrent COL4A3 c.1219G>C p.(Gly407Arg) variant.

METHODS: We conducted an observational cohort study at a major university hospital. Eligible participants were heterozygous for COL4A3 or COL4A4 variants. Demographic, clinical, and genetic data were collected. Time to CKD≥3 and CKD5/KF was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Subcohorts were defined by gene, variant type, and variant of interest.

RESULTS: A total of 218 individuals (16 children) from 123 families were included. Definitive molecular diagnosis was obtained in 75%. Among COL4A3 carriers, 117 had P/LP variants, predominantly missense; among COL4A4 carriers, 47 had P/LP variants, predominantly truncating. COL4A3 p.(Gly407Arg) represented 62% of COL4A3 P/LP variants and 44% of the patient cohort. History of microscopic hematuria was present in 93% of patients, whereas history of significant proteinuria was documented in 68% and hypertension in 48%. CKD≥3 developed in 33%, and 21% progressed to CKD5/KF. Proteinuria independently predicted CKD progression (p=0.001). Carriers of COL4A3 p.(Gly407Arg) had earlier onset of hypertension and higher prevalence of proteinuria than carriers of other COL4A3 P/LP variants. Glomerular basement membrane thinning was noted on electron microscopy in all biopsy specimens. Extrarenal manifestations were uncommon.

CONCLUSIONS: Heterozygous COL4A3/4 P/LP variants are frequently associated with progressive CKD. COL4A3 p.(Gly407Arg) apparently confers a more penetrant renal phenotype. AD-AS demonstrates a continuum of phenotypes even among relatives, underscoring the importance of early identification, longitudinal monitoring, and renoprotective therapy.

articles.title: An aggressive insulin titration pattern is associated with better glycemic control during short-term intensive insulin therapy.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To investigate the associations between insulin titration patterns and glycemic outcomes in continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII)-based short-term intensive insulin therapy (IIT).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Medical records of newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes (2001-2022) were stratified by time to achieve maximum dose (Tmax) into ascending/descending groups, with the latter split into aggressive/non-aggressive cohorts by median Tmax, to compare glucose-derived time in range (dTIR; 3.9-10.0 mmol/L), time below range (dTBR1; <3.9 mmol/L), post-therapy fasting glucose (FG), and to identify predictors of FG <6.1 mmol/L.

RESULTS: A total of 1,916 patients were stratified into ascending (n = 514) or descending (n = 1,402) groups, and aggressive (n = 681) or non-aggressive (n = 721) cohorts. dTIR was highest in the aggressive group, followed by the non-aggressive and ascending groups (89.7% [84.5, 93.6], 85.7% [79.6, 90.8], 76.2% [64.3, 84.9], respectively). Compared with the non-aggressive group, the aggressive group had a 1.73-percentage-point higher dTIR after adjustment (95% CI 0.91-2.56; P < 0.001), lower glucose variability, lower maximum and pump-suspension insulin doses, greater dose reduction, and shorter CSII treatment and hospitalization, with similar dTBR1 and post-therapy FG (6.1 ± 1.2 vs. 6.3 ± 1.2 mmol/L, P = 0.056). Predictors of post-therapy FG <6.1 mmol/L included higher BMI, greater dTIR and dTBR1 in both trajectory groups; younger age, lower HbA1c, longer CSII duration, and lower final insulin dose in the descending group.
