CONCLUSIONS: An aggressive titration pattern was associated with better glycemic control without increasing detected hypoglycemia relative to the non-aggressive pattern, suggesting a potential benefit of timely insulin titration that requires prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Pharmacogenomic Determinants of Asparaginase-Induced Hypersensitivity, Pancreatitis, Thrombosis, and Hepatotoxicity in Children: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Asparaginase is a common treatment for childhood hematological malignancies, but its use may be limited by toxicities including hypersensitivity, pancreatitis, thrombosis, and hepatotoxicity. Pharmacogenomic testing may identify children who are genetically predisposed to these toxicities, thus enabling personalized treatment. We performed a systematic review to synthesize and critically appraise available evidence for pharmacogenomic associations with asparaginase-induced toxicities in pediatric oncology patients. Literature searches of MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science were performed to identify studies investigating genetic associations with asparaginase-induced hypersensitivity, pancreatitis, thrombosis, or hepatotoxicity in children. Data extraction and risk of bias assessment using the Q-GENIE tool were performed independently by two reviewers. Forty studies met inclusion criteria. Evidence was the strongest for hypersensitivity, with consistent replication of associations involving HLA class II alleles, particularly the HLA-DRB1*07:01-HLA-DQA1*02:01-HLA-DQB1*02:02 haplotype, although risk alleles differed by ancestry. For hepatotoxicity, evidence was limited to three studies, but PNPLA3 rs738409 was identified and independently replicated. Associations with pancreatitis and thrombosis were heterogeneous, with numerous candidate loci reported but limited validation across independent cohorts. The overall evidence base was highly heterogeneous, characterized by varying toxicity definitions, inconsistent reporting of statistical power, and limited replication. Current evidence supports HLA class II alleles and PNPLA3 as the most promising pharmacogenomic markers of asparaginase hypersensitivity and hepatotoxicity respectively, but larger, ancestrally diverse studies with standardized toxicity definitions and independent validation are required before routine clinical implementation.

articles.title: Three-Year Polymerase Chain Reaction-Based Surveillance of Respiratory Tract Infections in Adults and Seasonal Patterns.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the aetiological composition, seasonal variation and risk factors of adult respiratory tract infections in Ganzhou, Jiangxi Province, during 2023-2025.

METHODS: A total of 8,493 adults (≥18 years) with respiratory symptoms were enrolled from a tertiary hospital during 2023-2025. Oropharyngeal and nasopharyngeal swabs were tested using multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) panels targeting six categories of seven respiratory pathogens: influenza A and B viruses, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), parainfluenza virus types I and III, adenovirus and Mycoplasma pneumoniae. Mixed infections (two or more pathogens) were reported separately. Data were analysed by univariate analysis and multivariate logistic regression.

RESULTS: The overall pathogen detection rate was 4.14% (352/8,493), comprising 325 single infections (92.33%) and 27 mixed infections (7.67%). Among single infections, M. pneumoniae (39.69%), influenza A virus (28.00%) and RSV (16.00%) predominated. Infections peaked in winter-spring (December-March). Age ≥65 years (OR = 2.35, 95% CI: 1.78-3.09), underlying diseases (OR = 2.41, 95% CI: 1.89-3.08) and emergency department admission (OR = 1.58, 95% CI: 1.24-2.01) were independent risk factors.

CONCLUSION: Adult respiratory infections in Ganzhou show clear winter-spring seasonality, with M. pneumoniae, influenza A virus and RSV as leading pathogens. These findings support seasonally targeted surveillance - with enhanced monitoring for M. pneumoniae and influenza during winter-spring months - and prioritised vaccination, expanded diagnostic panels and early PCR-based diagnosis for adults aged ≥65 years and those with underlying diseases, thereby strengthening local respiratory infection prevention and control strategies.

articles.title: Faecal microbiota transplantation for severe, refractory Clostridioides difficile infection: a multicentre real-world experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Although most patients respond to CDI-directed antimicrobial therapy, a subset develops refractory disease. Faecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) is established for recurrent CDI, but data supporting its use in severe, refractory CDI remain limited.

AIMS: To evaluate the safety and effectiveness of FMT in hospitalised patients with severe, refractory CDI across tertiary centres.

METHODS: This was a retrospective multicentre study of adults with severe, refractory CDI who underwent FMT at three tertiary hospitals in Western Australia between January 2021 and April 2025. Severe CDI was defined according to Australasian Society of Infectious Diseases criteria and refractory disease as failure to demonstrate clinical improvement following appropriate CDI-directed antimicrobial therapy. Primary cure was defined as resolution without recurrence within 90 days following a single FMT. Secondary outcomes included secondary cure, colectomy, FMT-related complications and hospital length of stay.

RESULTS: Fourteen patients underwent FMT for severe, refractory CDI. Median age was 68.5 years (range 32-84), 57.1% were female, and 71.4% were immunosuppressed. Median Charlson Comorbidity Index was 5.5 (range 0-11). FMT was delivered via colonoscopy, flexible sigmoidoscopy or nasogastric tube. Median sessions was 1.5 (range 1-4); five (35.7%) patients received consolidative antibiotics following repeat FMT. Primary cure after a single FMT was achieved in seven (50%) patients. The remaining seven required repeat FMT, with a secondary cure rate of 100% at 3 months. One patient died from an unrelated cause. No patients required colectomy, experienced recurrence or FMT-related complications. Median hospital stay was 24.5 days (range 7-65).

CONCLUSION: FMT was associated with high rates of clinical cure as salvage therapy for hospitalised patients with severe, refractory CDI. While only half achieved primary cure after a single FMT, sequential FMT achieved a secondary cure rate of 100%. Further studies are needed to define optimal treatment protocols.

articles.title: In vivo toxicity, with immunodysregulatory potentials, of polytetrafluorethylene nanoplastics to rats administered intragastrically for 90 d.
articles.journal: Journal of toxicology and environmental health. Part A
articles.abstract: Polytetrafluorethylene (PTFE), also known as Teflon, constitutes the most utilized fluoropolymer and comprises approximately 60% of the total international fluoropolymer market. The aim of the present study was to assess the oral toxicity attributed to exposure to 260 nm PTFE-nanoparticle (NPs) in Sprague-Dawley rats following OECD TG 408 guidelines. Over a 90-d period, rats received daily doses of 250, 500, or 1000 mg/kg, representing low, intermediate, and high exposure levels, to determine the influence of the NPs. There were no specific clinical signs associated with PTFE NP administration, as determined by general and detailed clinical observations, ophthalmology, and functional observational battery. No significant alterations related to PTFE-NP administration were detected by hematology, urinalysis, or clinical biochemistry, except that dose-dependently higher levels of serum aspartate aminotransferase, blood urea nitrogen, and triglyceride were observed in males, all within the normal range. There were no abnormalities in gross necropsy, no alterations in organ weights, and no histopathological changes in any PTFE-NP‑administered group for either gender, except for more pituitary cysts and ultimobranchial body cysts in the male high‑dose group. Considering no significant differences in other hepatic or renal function biomarkers and no abnormalities in hepatic or renal histopathology in high‑dose males, those changes were considered unrelated to PTFE-NP administration. Administration of PTFE-NPs preferentially suppressed type-1 helper T cell reactivity, most notably in females, and a downregulation of age-dependent increase of serum IgG levels, regardless of gender. Overall, based upon our findings, the no-observed-adverse-effect level is estimated at 1000 mg/kg body weight or less for both genders.

articles.title: Association between ABO blood groups and major disease categories in a retrospective cohort of 1.7 million blood donors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: ABO blood groups have a certain correlation with the incidence of many diseases. We aimed to explore the association between ABO blood groups and the top 25 fatal diseases in China.

METHODS: We constructed a retrospective cohort of 1,704,333 blood donors to investigate the association between ABO blood groups and the top 25 fatal diseases among Chinese individuals. We summarised differences in disease patterns across blood groups using multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression models.

RESULTS: Among the enrolled participants, type A (HR = 1.07; 95% CI = 1.03-1.09, P = 0.004) and type B (HR = 1.06; 95% CI = 1.02-1.09, P = 0.045) donors were more likely to develop ischaemic heart disease (I20-25) than type O donors. Compared with type O, type A (HR = 1.10; 95% CI = 1.06-1.13, P < 0.00067) and B (HR = 1.12; 95% CI = 1.08-1.14, P < 0.00067) donors were found to have more likely to develop diabetes mellitus (E10-14) (significant after Bonferroni correction). Type AB (HR = 1.84; 95% CI = 1.40-2.13, P = 0.05) and B (HR = 1.44; 95% CI = 1.19-1.71, P = 0.036) were more likely to develop colorectal cancer (C18-C20).Type A (HR = 0.93; 95% CI = 0.90-0.96, P = 0.025) and type B (HR = 0.93; 95% CI = 0.88-0.96, P = 0.020) were less likely to develop influenza, pneumonia, and acute lower respiratory tract infections (J09-22). Mean hospital stay differed significantly among blood groups for C18-20 (P = 0.045) and I20-25 (P = 0.008).

CONCLUSIONS: We found a significant correlation between ABO blood groups and the top 25 fatal diseases in China, including ischaemic heart disease, diabetes, and colorectal cancer among blood donors. The associations should be considered exploratory and require independent validation for the general population.

REGISTRATION: China National Medical Research Register: MR-61-21-011750; Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: ChiCTR2200055983.

articles.title: Mild aortic regurgitation as an independent predictor of major adverse cardiovascular events in non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome: insights from a multicentre propensity score-matched cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS) remains a leading cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide, making accurate risk stratification beyond conventional clinical parameters a critical need. Mild aortic regurgitation (AR) is frequently detected on routine echocardiography in patients with coronary artery disease, yet its prognostic significance in the high-risk context of NSTE-ACS remains poorly defined.

METHODS: This multicentre retrospective cohort study included 1,290 patients with NSTE-ACS and mild AR from six tertiary cardiovascular centres in China. Propensity score matching targeting an approximately 1:3 ratio identified 3,872 matched controls without AR or other valvular heart disease. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs), comprising cardiac death, heart failure rehospitalisation, and unplanned coronary revascularisation, over a median follow-up of 50 months.

RESULTS: Covariates included in the propensity-score model were adequately balanced after propensity score matching (absolute standardised mean difference <0.10). Mild AR was associated with higher risks of MACEs (HR = 1.47; 95% CI = 1.26-1.72, P < 0.001), cardiac death (HR = 1.51; 95% CI = 1.13-2.02, P = 0.002), heart failure rehospitalisation (HR = 1.57; 95% CI = 1.12-2.20, P = 0.004), and unplanned coronary revascularisation (HR = 1.34; 95% CI = 1.08-1.67, P = 0.004). After multivariable adjustment, mild AR remained independently associated with MACEs (HR = 1.329; 95% CI = 1.144-1.545, P < 0.001). Mild AR was also associated with higher neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (β = 0.56; 95% CI = 0.37-0.74, P < 0.001), systemic immune-inflammation index (β = 161.73; 95% CI = 119.36-204.10, P < 0.001), and remnant cholesterol (β = 0.21; 95% CI = 0.16-0.26, P < 0.001). Exploratory mediation analyses showed modest statistical indirect associations between mild AR and MACEs (~6.8%) and between mild AR and cardiac death (~10.0%), operating through left atrial diameter.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with NSTE-ACS, mild AR was independently associated with MACEs and modest differences in inflammatory indices and remnant cholesterol. Mild AR may, therefore, be a readily available marker for risk stratification in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Predictors of Thrombotic Events and Mortality in Patients Treated With Andexanet: A Pooled Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Andexanet reduces hematoma expansion compared with usual care for acute FXa (factor Xa) inhibitor-associated intracerebral hemorrhage but is associated with a risk of thrombotic events (TE). We pooled data from andexanet-treated trial participants to determine baseline predictors of TE.

METHODS: Secondary analyses of andexanet-treated participants in ANNEXA-I (Andexanet Alfa, a Novel Antidote to the Anticoagulant Effects of Factor Xa Inhibitors in ICH) and ANNEXA-4 (Andexanet Alfa, a Novel Antidote to the Anticoagulation Effects of Factor Xa Inhibitors), which included adults with acute life-threatening hemorrhage on FXa inhibitors. Stratified Cox proportional hazards models were used to examine associations between baseline variables and arterial or all TE and mortality. A stratified Cox regression model with arterial events as time-dependent covariates was used to examine associations of arterial events with mortality, adjusted for clinical covariates.

RESULTS: Of 741 participants (mean age, 78.5 years; 54.5% male), 593 (80.0%) had intracranial hemorrhage and 109 (14.7%) had gastrointestinal hemorrhage. Seventy-seven (10.4%) participants had ≥1 TE, and 147 (19.8%) died. Arterial and venous thromboembolism events occurred a median of 3.5 days (interquartile range, 2.0-12.0) and 14.0 days (interquartile range, 10.0-20.0), respectively, after randomization. No baseline factors were associated with all TE. Arterial TE were associated with prior myocardial infarction (hazard ratio [HR], 2.64 [95% CI, 1.33-5.26]), high-dose eligibility (HR, 2.44 [95% CI, 1.33-4.48]), female sex (HR, 1.78 [95% CI, 1.00-3.16]), and age (HR per year, 1.04 [95% CI, 1.00-1.08]). Mortality was associated with arterial TE (HR, 2.68 [95% CI, 1.64-4.36]), prior congestive heart failure (HR, 2.53 [95% CI, 1.76-3.63]), intracerebral hemorrhage or intraventricular hemorrhage (HR, 1.90 [95% CI, 1.20-3.01]), and age (HR per year, 1.06 [95% CI, 1.03-1.08]). The initiation of anticoagulation after randomization was associated with a reduction in TE.

CONCLUSIONS: In FXa inhibitor-associated hemorrhage treated with andexanet, baseline factors are associated with arterial TE and can be used to inform treatment decisions. Initiation of anticoagulation reduces the occurrence of TE.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02313909. URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02329327.

articles.title: mRNA-based anti-COVID-19 vaccines induced higher B cells and IgG levels than whole virus-based: A pilot study on Egyptian individuals.
articles.abstract: BackgroundB cells are critical components of vaccine-induced humoral immunity. However, circulating total B-cell measurements do not by themselves establish antigen specificity, memory differentiation, neutralizing activity, or protection. Aim: This exploratory observational study compared circulating CD19+ B-cell numbers and anti-SARS-CoV-2 spike receptor-binding domain (RBD) binding antibody levels according to COVID-19 vaccine platform and time since vaccination.MethodsSixty-one participants were included: 52 vaccinated participants and 9 non-vaccinated participants. Vaccinated participants had received Pfizer (BNT162b2), ChAdOx1 nCoV-19, or inactivated-virus vaccines (Sinopharm or Sinovac). Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were analyzed by flow cytometry using CD19 to quantify total circulating B cells, while anti-SARS-CoV-2 spike-RBD binding antibodies were measured using the Elecsys Anti-SARS-CoV-2 S assay.ResultsTotal CD19+ B-cell percentages and absolute numbers were not significantly different between the vaccinated platform groups and the non-vaccinated controls. Anti-SARS-CoV-2 spike-RBD binding antibody levels were significantly higher in vaccinated participants than in controls. The relationship between circulating CD19+ B-cell frequency and antibody concentration was weak.ConclusionThese exploratory findings suggest persistent humoral immune responses after COVID-19 vaccination but do not establish superiority of one vaccine platform. Because the study was limited by sample size, heterogeneous. vaccination histories, incomplete objective ascertainment of previous SARS-CoV-2 infection, and use of a binding-antibody assay rather than a functional neutralization assay, the findings should be interpreted as preliminary and require confirmation in larger, adequately powered studies.

articles.title: ROX Index for Prediction of 48-h Reintubation After Extubation in Medical ICU Patients Receiving High-Flow Nasal Cannula.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: The respiratory rate-oxygenation (ROX) index predicts HFNC failure in pneumonia with hypoxemic respiratory failure, but its utility in the post-extubation HFNC setting remains unclear.

METHODS: We retrospectively analysed data from a prospectively enrolled observational ICU cohort at Samsung Medical Center (Seoul, Korea). Among 1881 mechanically ventilated adults, we analysed 726 extubation episodes managed with post-extubation HFNC. The primary outcome was reintubation within 48 h. ROX was calculated hourly for 24 h after extubation. Diagnostic discrimination was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and clustered receiver operating characteristic methods, stratified by PaO2/FiO2 on the day of extubation.

RESULTS: Reintubation occurred in 112/726 extubation episodes (15.4%). Overall, ROX demonstrated limited discrimination (AUROC 0.681 at 2 h, 0.681 at 6 h, 0.677 at 12 h, 0.730 at 18 h, and 0.614 at 24 h). Clustered AUROC varied according to hypoxaemia severity: 0.545 (PaO2/FiO2 ≥ 300; n = 118), 0.684 (PaO2/FiO2 200-< 300; n = 460), and 0.762 (PaO2/FiO2 < 200; n = 148). In PaO2/FiO2 < 200, even-hour-derived ROX thresholds performed similarly in odd hours: rule-in 4.21 and 6.60, balanced 9.70 (Youden), and rule-out 12.50 and 16.96. Median time from ROX < 9.7 to reintubation was 14.1 h.

CONCLUSION: ROX demonstrated limited discriminative performance for predicting reintubation after extubation in patients receiving post-extubation HFNC. However, discrimination varied by hypoxaemia severity, and ROX may serve as an adjunct for post-extubation risk stratification in patients with PaO2/FiO2 < 200.

articles.title: Physician Job Choice and Support for Abortion Access in the Post Dobbs Landscape: a Survey Study of High-Risk Specialty Trainees.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physicians have always had to balance personal ethics, professional obligations, and legal constraints when providing abortion care; however, since the United States Supreme Court ruling in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization, the legal framework governing this care has shifted substantially, raising concerns about physician workforce stability. The primary aim in our pilot study was to assess how likely states' abortion laws will influence where physicians accept their first job after residency or fellowship. Our other objectives were to assess physician support for abortion access and well-being post Dobbs. We hypothesized that the majority of physicians would be likely to consider states' abortion laws when looking for first post training jobs, would support abortion access, and would have had their well-being affected.

METHODS: We surveyed anesthesiology, emergency medicine, and obstetrics-gynecology (OB-GYN) residents and fellows.

RESULTS: We achieved only a 1.2% response rate. In this small data set, a majority (65.6%) of residents and fellows said that they are likely to consider state abortion laws when deciding where to accept their first post-training job, with OB-GYNs (90.7%) having the greatest majority. Eight out of ten physicians were supportive of medical and surgical abortion access (87.2%; 86.1%). A majority of physicians were supportive of abortion across all demographics, even Catholics, deviating only when assessed by political party affiliation. A majority of physicians (56.5%) were negatively affected by the Dobbs decision, regardless of the abortion law where they practice. Cisgender women and OB-GYN trainees were most impacted.

CONCLUSIONS: The response rate limits any generalizability of our findings, and future research is needed. In this pilot study, the majority of physicians indicated that they will consider states' abortion laws when accepting their first job, and a minority of physicians may be willing to work in states with abortion bans. To promote physician retention and recruitment, future research should investigate how access to reproductive care impacts physicians' professional and personal well-being.

articles.title: Dysregulated apoptosis in the spleen from patients with splenomegaly due to cirrhosis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Splenomegaly (SM) secondary to portal hypertension is characterized by the pathological enlargement of the spleen due to chronically elevated portal venous pressure. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying its pathogenesis remain largely unclear.

MATERIAL: AND M: ETHODS: Sixteen patients with hepatitis B-related liver cirrhosis and SM who underwent subtotal splenectomy with omental plasty and retroperitoneal fixation were enrolled in the SM group, whereas 15 patients who underwent splenectomy for traumatic splenic rupture (without SM) served as the traumatic splenic rupture control (TSRC) group. Splenic tissue samples were collected for hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining, terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick-end labeling (TUNEL) assay, immunohistochemistry (IHC), quantitative reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction, and Western blotting (WB).

RESULTS: H&E staining revealed dilated red pulp, fibrotic splenic cords, atrophic white pulp, and a thickened splenic capsule in the SM group. A significant increase in the proportion of apoptotic cells was noted in the spleens of patients with SM. Moreover, differences were observed in apoptotic protein expression assessed by IHC between the two groups. The expression of apoptosis-related genes, including BAX, CASP3, and CASP9, was significantly upregulated, whereas BCL2 expression was significantly reduced in the SM group. WB confirmed that the levels of BAX, cleaved CASP3, and cleaved CASP9 were elevated in the SM group, whereas splenic BCL2 expression was below the detection limit in both groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Apoptosis was dysregulated in the spleen of patients with portal hypertension-associated SM secondary to liver cirrhosis. Our findings suggest that SM contributes to a pro-apoptotic environment in the spleen of patients with liver cirrhosis.

articles.title: Cellular and Molecular Mechanisms of Wound Healing and Therapeutics Innovations.
articles.journal: Cellular physiology and biochemistry : international journal of experimental cellular physiology, biochemistry, and pharmacology
articles.abstract: Chronic wounds are a significant and growing global clinical problem owing to increasing rates of diabetes, vascular diseases, ageing, and metabolic disorders. In contrast to acute wounds, which follow a coordinated sequence of haemostasis, inflammation, proliferation and remodelling, chronic wounds fail to progress through the healing process, leading to delayed or unfinished recovery. There is mounting evidence that this malfunction lies primarily in dysregulated intracellular signalling and is not necessarily in a lack of growth factors or cellular components. There is prolonged stimulation of pro-inflammatory pathways, disrupted angiogenic and regenerative signalling, excessive extracellular matrix degradation, cellular senescence and impaired immune resolution in chronic wound environments. The most important signalling networks, such as TGF-b/Smad, PI3K/Akt/mTOR, MAPK, NF-kB, Wnt/b-catenin, JAK/STAT, Hippo-YAP/TAZ, Notch, and hypoxia-inducible factor-1a, are crucial in the coordination of wound repair, but are functionally impaired in chronic pathological diseases. The pathways demonstrate a widespread crosstalk, forming a self-maintaining feedback loop that drives inflammation, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, and a lack of cellular responsiveness. This review provides a detailed description of the physiology of normal wound healing, compares acute and chronic wound pathology, and critically discusses the molecular signalling defects that promote the persistence of chronic wounds. Additionally, it identifies emerging therapeutic approaches aimed at regulating dysregulated signalling networks, such as small-molecule modulators, biologics, biomaterials, gene- and cell-based therapies and exosome-mediated therapies.

articles.title: The Effect of Progressive Relaxation Exercise on Life Satisfaction, Comfort, and Burnout Levels of Nurses: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nurses experience occupational and personal stress, which can reduce well-being and life satisfaction and contribute to burnout. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the effect of progressive relaxation exercises (PRE) on nurses' life satisfaction, comfort, and burnout.

METHODS: This randomized controlled trial included nurses from a tertiary care hospital. The intervention consisted of PRE involving the sequential contraction and relaxation of major muscle groups. The intervention group performed PRE for 5 weeks, three times a week, with each session lasting 20 minutes, outside active working hours. Outcomes were assessed using the Satisfaction with Life Scale, Nurse Comfort Questionnaire, and Maslach Burnout Inventory. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, chi-square, t-tests, and repeated-measures ANOVA in SPSS 25.0.

RESULTS: After five weeks, the intervention group showed significantly higher life satisfaction (18.06±2.97 vs. 12.50±2.52, p < 0.001), total comfort (115.63±14.64 vs. 100.73±13.49, p < 0.001), and personal accomplishment (30.26±3.35 vs. 27.30±5.01, p = 0.009) scores than the control group. In contrast, emotional exhaustion (25.76±5.59 vs. 29.63±5.82, p = 0.011) and depersonalization (11.23±3.51 vs. 15.13±3.13, p < 0.001) were significantly lower in the intervention group.

CONCLUSIONS/APPLICATION TO PRACTICE: PRE reduced nurses' burnout and enhanced their life satisfaction and comfort. It can be recommended as a simple and reliable complementary method to support nurses' well-being. Occupational health professionals can integrate brief, structured PRE sessions into workplace wellness programs, enabling nurses to perform standardized exercises independently during breaks or outside working hours. This practical approach may support nurses' psychological well-being without disrupting patient care or workflow.

articles.title: Robotic magnetic navigation for atrial fibrillation ablation in older adults: is chronological age still the main concern?
GluN3 Subunits of NMDA Receptors are Functionally Expressed in Neurons of the Suprachiasmatic Nucleus of Mice.
articles.abstract: The suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) is the principal circadian clock in the mammalian brain. This structure is synchronized to the light-dark cycle through the retinohypothalamic tract (RHT), which releases glutamate onto the ventral SCN. Glutamate activates N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) and α-Amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA)/kainate receptors, increasing intracellular calcium levels and activating signaling pathways required for light-induced phase shifts. NMDA receptors are composed of different subunits: GluN1, GluN2 (A-D), and GluN3 (A-B). However, it remains unknown whether GluN3-containing NMDA receptors are present in SCN neurons and, if so, whether these subunits are functional and contribute to glutamatergic signaling in the ventral SCN. To address these questions, we used immunohistochemistry to assess GluN3 expression in the ventral and dorsal SCN and whole-cell patch-clamp recordings in the ventral SCN to monitor stimulus-evoked asynchronous excitatory postsynaptic currents (aEPSCs) following repetitive electrical stimulation of the RHT. Analyses of GluN3A and GluN3B expression disclosed higher levels of both subunits, as well as higher numbers of immunopositive particles during daytime vs nighttime in the ventral SCN. In contrast, the dorsal SCN showed a reversed pattern, with higher GluN3A expression during the night. Electrophysiological experiments showed that CGP-78608, an antagonist of the GluN1 glycine-binding site and a positive allosteric modulator of GluN3A-mediated responses, reduced the frequency and amplitude of aEPSCs during daytime, but not during nighttime. Moreover, bath application of glycine, which activates the GluN3 subunit, increased the frequency and amplitude of aEPSCs during the day, but not during the night. Finally, the antagonist 5,7-Dichlorokynurenic acid (DCKA) completely abolished the remaining aEPSCs at both times analyzed, further supporting the contribution of GluN3-containing NMDA receptors to these responses. Our findings support that GluN3 subunits are expressed in both ventral and dorsal SCN neurons and that GluN3-containing receptors are functionally involved in the glutamatergic signaling of the ventral SCN, depending on the circadian time (day vs night, at least).

articles.title: Development and validation of a text-mining-based algorithm for detection of rare hereditary periodic fever syndromes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Periodic fever syndromes (PFS) are rare and have variable clinical manifestations, leading to missed diagnoses. Familial Mediterranean fever (FMF), hyperimmunoglobulin D syndrome (HIDS) and tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated periodic syndrome (TRAPS) are among the most frequently occurring monogenetic PFS. In this retrospective case-control study, we developed a diagnostic prediction model using text from the electronic health record (EHR).

METHODS: We identified potential PFS cases from the EHR of a tertiary care hospital and subsequently screened for Eurofever/PRINTO classification criteria for PFS. Controls consisted of patients with billing codes corresponding to overlapping diagnoses, and/or other codes for diagnoses with symptoms also occurring in PFS. We used text mining to capture 60 distinguishing features and trained a naïve Bayes model on the presence of these features to discriminate cases from controls. External validation was performed on a secondary care hospital cohort.

RESULTS: 194 cases (145 FMF) and 14,435 controls were included in the development cohort; 120 cases (118 FMF) and 34,315 controls in the external validation cohort. The model showed an AUC ROC of 0.90 during internal validation, and 0.88 [95%CI 0.84-0.91] in the external validation cohort. Restricting external validation to pre-diagnostic data (50 PFS cases) substantially decreased performance (AUC ROC 0.66 [95%CI 0.56-0.75].

CONCLUSION: Text-mined EHR data contains valuable information to distinguish PFS from related diagnoses. Pending further validation in the pre-diagnostic setting, and a strategy to keep false positive rates manageable, machine learning models may contribute to identification of undiagnosed patients with PFS.

articles.title: Multimodal Validation and Disease Stage Dependency of ATTR Cardiomyopathy Red Flags in Patients With LV Thickening.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Timely diagnosis of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is critical to improving outcomes and remains challenging. Guidelines recommend assessing for red flags (RFs) to facilitate ATTR-CM detection, but their diagnostic validation remains incomplete. This study aimed to multidimensionally validate these RFs in patients with left ventricular thickening (LVT).

METHODS: Prospective registry study including all patients with LVT and standardized workup at tertiary amyloidosis center. For validated RFs, "high-risk" (specificity for ATTR-CM>90%) and "low-risk" (false-negative rate<5%) findings were predefined.

RESULTS: 425 patients (321 ATTR-CM,104 control group) were included. Heart failure (97%) and polyneuropathies (78%) were among most sensitive clinical findings, while bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome (bCTS) was more specific (80%) but less sensitive (45%). Diverse ECG changes were common, yet mostly unspecific. Marked elevations of NT-proBNP and troponin were most discriminative among non-imaging RFs (Youden's index[YI]:59%). Apical sparing (Apical-to-Basal-strain-ratio≥2.0) was the most effective, stage-independent echocardiographic parameter (YI62%), followed by biatrial enlargement, advanced diastolic dysfunction, and LVGLS impairment (YI48-55%). Normal ECG without conduction disorders history and normal levels of both NT-proBNP and hs-troponin-T constituted "low-risk" findings. Heart failure with concomitant bCTS, peripheral low voltage, right ventricular dysfunction, 5-5-5 sign, restrictive filling pattern and apical sparing with LVGLS impairment represented "high-risk" RFs. Contrary to most non-imaging RFs, most echocardiographic RFs showed association with advancing disease stage (p<0.05). All aforementioned RFs were associated with ATTR-CM independently of age, sex, and LVT-severity (p<0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: ATTR-CM is frequently associated with validated RFs that differ in their diagnostic characteristics, which should be considered when evaluating for ATTR-CM.

articles.title: Racial cuts: Explanations of race inequities in cesarean births in U.S. government and medical discourse.
articles.abstract: Cesarean births are increasingly common worldwide, constituting what some experts call a cesarean epidemic and attracting public health initiatives to reduce cesarean rates. The U.S. cesarean epidemic is racialized, consisting of cesarean overuse in low-risk contexts and underuse in high-risk contexts for Black birthing people. Research shows health initiatives portray Black women as non-compliant with health directives, justifying inequitable outcomes in reproductive contexts, including birth, breastfeeding, and pre-pregnancy health. However, research has not examined initiatives to reduce cesareans, which are distinct because they occur within hospitals and are authorized by medical professionals. This study used critical discourse analysis to investigate constructions of race inequities in cesareans across 59 documents published between 2010 and 2025 by U.S. government agencies and medical organizations. Findings revealed cesareans are constructed as lifesaving procedures that carry inherent risks of detrimental outcomes, including death. Documents acknowledged race inequities in cesareans, but associated them with comorbidities (e.g. hypertension) rather than structural or obstetric racism; explaining and eradicating race inequities was rarely addressed. By centering behavioral and biomedical risk factors, discourses reproduce Black birthing people as inherently "high-risk," thereby legitimizing cesarean overuse. Centering cesareans as a discursive site of racialization, this study shows how surgical intervention is justified through language that marks Black bodies as pathologically susceptible to "risk." These findings illustrate that cesarean birth functions not only as a medical intervention but also as a site of racialized reproductive governance.

articles.title: Two Decades of Cardiovascular Prevention Science at CDC: A Bibliometric Analysis, 2006-2025.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's Division for Heart Disease and Stroke Prevention (DHDSP) provides national leadership for cardiovascular disease (CVD) prevention, including efforts to improve hypertension control. Scientific publications document surveillance, program implementation, evaluation, and dissemination of evidence-based strategies. This study describes DHDSP's scientific productivity, focus, and reach across two decades of CVD prevention work.

METHODS: We conducted a bibliometric analysis of publications authored or coauthored by DHDSP staff during 2006-2025. Publications were identified from internal records and PubMed searches, verified for eligibility, and categorized by condition and topic area. Citation metrics, Relative Citation Ratio (RCR), Altmetric Attention Scores, policy and guideline mentions, authorship role, and collaboration indicators were summarized descriptively.

RESULTS: DHDSP contributed to 841 publications ranging annually from 12 in 2006 to 67 in 2017. Publications accrued 88,636 citations (median: 19; 25-75 percentiles: 7;48). Median RCR was 1.15 (25-75 percentiles: 0.50-2.53), and median Altmetric Attention Score was 6.0 (25-75 percentiles: 0.5-23.5). DHDSP publications were cited or mentioned in 637 policy documents and 410 guidelines indexed by Altmetric. Most focused on core DHDSP conditions, including hypertension, with surveillance and epidemiology the most common topic. Overall, 240 publications (28.5%) included a focus on hypertension.

CONCLUSIONS: DHDSP's publication portfolio demonstrates sustained scientific productivity and broad dissemination across two decades of CVD prevention. Hypertension was an important component, alongside research addressing heart disease, stroke, and other cardiovascular risk factors and outcomes. The portfolio documents the evolution of public health science and contributes to the evidence base for cardiovascular disease prevention and control.

articles.title: How Specialty Shapes Burnout in the Medical ICU: A Qualitative Study of Resident Experiences.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The negative impacts of burnout in resident physicians have been widely documented, and burnout rates in the Medical Intensive Care Unit (MICU) are high. While burnout has been studied in physicians and other personnel in Intensive Care Units (ICUs), little attention has been given to resident physicians in the MICU. Our prior study demonstrated very high rates of burnout in residents in the MICU and was suggestive that non-internal medicine (non-IM) residents may be at an even higher risk of burnout than their internal medicine (IM) colleagues.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to determine and compare drivers and mitigators of burnout experienced by IM and non-IM (Family Medicine (FM) and Emergency Medicine (EM)) resident physicians rotating in the MICU. It also sought to identify drivers and mitigators of burnout that may be amenable to intervention strategies.

METHODS: Three different resident disciplines (IM, EM, and FM) hosted trained investigators who mediated focus groups of 4-12 trainees during protected teaching time between April 2022 and May 2023. The focus groups aimed at identifying contributors to and mitigators of burnout in the MICU. Trained scribes recorded notes from the conversation, which were later parsed into themes and compared across groups to determine if similar themes existed in other resident specialties.

RESULTS: In this study, we identified common themes in the focus groups from residents of all specialties and themes unique to each specialty. Universal drivers of burnout included moral distress and ethical concerns and insufficient orientation. Multiple unique drivers for FM and EM residents were identified including decreased gratification (FM), guilt (FM),  communicating uncertainty to families (EM), managing chronic medical diseases (EM), and hierarchical relationships (FM & IM). Universal mitigators across all three specialties include meaningful patient experiences, time and access to food, and positive team dynamics.

CONCLUSION: Drivers and mitigators of burnout vary across residency training specialties in the MICU, though common themes exist amongst different specialties. Identifying these themes creates opportunities for intervention strategies with the potential to improve resident satisfaction, training quality, and patient outcomes.

articles.title: New anti-inflammatory and remodelling drugs for unmet clinical needs in severe asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
articles.abstract: There have been several step-changes in asthma therapy, with the first being the use of inhaled short-acting β2-agonists as bronchodilators and the introduction of inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) to reduce airway inflammation. The next revolution was the advent of inhaled combinations of long-acting bronchodilators together with inhaled corticosteroids in the same inhalation device for improved asthma control. The most recent step-change is the introduction of targeted monoclonal antibodies in patients with severe asthma and frequent exacerbations with biomarkers reflecting high levels of Type 2 (T2) inflammation. In chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), advances in bronchodilator therapy have been made, but limited advances in treating the inflammation and lung remodelling changes are present. We need new therapeutic agents for patients with a sub-optimal response to current drugs. The aim of this narrative review is to provide a summary of the potential future anti-inflammatory approaches undergoing testing for asthma and COPD rather than provide a systematic review. These approaches aim to optimize current treatment regimens and to develop novel agents against differing aspects of asthma and COPD pathophysiology. However, clinical trial results highlight our limited understanding of the biology of asthma and COPD subtypes. Furthermore, failed studies provide insight into disease pathophysiology and may indicate responder/non-responder populations. Various aspects of cytokine- and environment-activated intracellular pathways are being targeted. These include receptor agonists and antagonists and inhibitors of the Janus kinase (JAK) and Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) pathways for use against both stable disease and for reducing disease exacerbations or 'attacks'. New or better use of current biomarkers will provide non-invasive means of patients most likely to respond to any one specific or combination of drugs.

articles.title: Digital Quantification of Stromal Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocytes in Lung Adenocarcinoma: Associations With Histologic Grade and PET-Derived Metabolic Parameters.
articles.abstract: Background/AimTumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) are important components of the tumor immune microenvironment in lung adenocarcinoma. However, their relationship with fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography (PET)/computed tomography (CT)-derived metabolic parameters remains unclear. This study investigated the association between digitally quantified stromal TIL density and clinicopathologic as well as metabolic imaging parameters in resected lung adenocarcinoma.Materials and MethodsThis retrospective study included 57 patients with surgically resected lung adenocarcinoma who underwent preoperative FDG PET/CT. Stromal TIL density was quantified digitally using QuPath (version 0.6.0) in selected stromal hotspot regions and expressed as cells/mm2. PET parameters included SUVmax, SUVmean, SULpeak, metabolic tumor volume (MTV), and total lesion glycolysis (TLG). Correlation and multivariable regression analyses were performed.ResultsStromal TIL density showed a weak inverse correlation with MTV (ρ = -0.287, nominal P = .039); however, this association did not remain statistically significant after FDR correction (q = .109). No significant associations were observed with SUV-based parameters or TLG. Histologic grade demonstrated a moderate inverse correlation with TIL density (ρ = -0.36, P = .007) and remained independently associated in multivariable analysis, although the association was borderline (P = .046). Higher-grade tumors exhibited significantly increased metabolic activity. Lower stromal TIL density was also associated with advanced clinical stage and N1 lymph node metastasis (P = .008). Tumor size correlated positively with all PET-derived metabolic parameters, most strongly with TLG (ρ = 0.91, P < .001).ConclusionDigitally quantified stromal TIL density was associated with histologic grade and more advanced disease in resected lung adenocarcinoma, whereas its relationship with PET-derived metabolic parameters was limited. These exploratory findings require validation in larger cohorts using spatially representative immune assessment methods.

articles.title: Methylation-sensitive binding of BraBPC2.A08 to the BraCYP707A3.A02 promoter regulates Brassica clubroot resistance by ABA catabolism.
articles.abstract: Clubroot disease, caused by Plasmodiophora brassicae, seriously threatens global production of cruciferous crops. Epigenetic regulation, particularly DNA methylation, is increasingly recognized as important in plant-pathogen interactions, but its role in clubroot resistance remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated whole-genome bisulfite sequencing and transcriptome profiling of resistant and susceptible Brassica rapa lines following P. brassicae infection. The resistant line exhibited global hypomethylation, predominantly in the CHH context, whereas the susceptible line showed progressive hypermethylation. A key abscisic acid (ABA) catabolic gene, BraCYP707A3.A02, was downregulated and its promoter hypermethylated in susceptible plants, leading to ABA accumulation and increased susceptibility. Chemical demethylation with 5-azacytidine or overexpression of the DNA demethylase gene DME reduced promoter methylation, restored BraCYP707A3.A02 expression, lowered ABA levels, and enhanced clubroot resistance in both B. rapa and B. napus. Furthermore, the transcription factor BraBPC2.A08 specifically bound to the GA-rich motif in the BraCYP707A3.A02 promoter to activate its expression, and this binding was abolished by cytosine methylation. Our findings reveal a novel epigenetic regulatory module where DNA methylation fine-tunes ABA homeostasis by modulating BraCYP707A3.A02 expression, thereby determining B. rapa resistance to clubroot. Our findings uncover a methylation-sensitive transcriptional activation mechanism and provide a potential target for epigenome-assisted breeding of clubroot-resistant Brassica crops.

articles.title: A secreted protein UvWSC1 from Ustilaginoidea virens elicits plant immunity in an OsCPK13-dependent manner.
articles.abstract: During infection, plant pathogens secrete a large number of proteins that may either function as virulence factors to facilitate infection or be recognized by the host plant to trigger immune responses. The secretome of Ustilaginoidea virens contains numerous functionally uncharacterized proteins. Which of these secreted proteins possess functions in both pathogenicity and immune activation remains largely unknown. Here, we show that UvWSC1, a water-soluble carbohydrate-containing protein from U. virens that localizes to the cell wall, induces cell death in Nicotiana benthamiana. UvWSC1(1-113) functions as a minimal immunogenic epitope that triggers cell death across multiple plant species. Both knockout and overexpression of UvWSC1 attenuate fungal pathogenicity, revealing its role as both a virulence factor and an immune elicitor recognized by plants. Heterologous expression of UvWSC1 in rice confers broad-spectrum resistance against diverse pathogens without compromising agronomic traits, while simultaneously activating plant basal immunity. Mechanistically, UvWSC1(1-113)-triggered cell death depends on the calcium-dependent protein kinase OsCPK13 and the co-receptor SOBIR1. UvWSC1 does not directly interact with OsCPK13 or SOBIR1; however, UvWSC1(1-113) enhances the interaction between OsCPK13 and OsSOBIR1. Our results suggest that UvWSC1(1-113) may act as an activating signal that promotes the recruitment of the SOBIR1-OsCPK13 complex. Overexpression of OsCPK13 in rice enhances the immune response triggered by UvWSC1(1-113), whereas knockout of OsCPK13 attenuates this response, confirming that OsCPK13 is required for UvWSC1(1-113)-triggered immune responses. The broad-spectrum resistance conferred by UvWSC1 highlights its potential as a molecular tool for breeding disease-resistant crops and for developing environmentally friendly green pesticides.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes of Patients With Atrial Septal Defect and Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
articles.journal: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
articles.abstract: BackgroundIndications for atrial septal defect (ASD) closure in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) have not been established. We evaluated medium-term outcomes in such patients with regard to the effect of ASD closure and prognostic predictors.MethodsThis single-center retrospective study included 39 patients with pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) ≥ 2 Wood units (WU). The primary adverse outcome was defined as a composite of major cardiovascular events, including cardiac death or hospitalization for heart failure.ResultsOf the 39 patients, 32 underwent shunt closure, whereas 7 did not. Among patients with PVR ≥ 5 WU, over a median follow-up of 3.8 years, 3-year clinical event rates were 27.3% (3/11) in the closure group (n = 11) and 14.3% (1/7) in the no-closure group (n = 7); the difference was not statistically significant. The maximal velocity of tricuspid regurgitation significantly decreased during follow-up in the closure group; no significant change was observed in the no-closure group. In patients with PVR ≥ 5 WU, systemic arterial oxygen saturation (SaO2) showed a significant association with the primary composite outcome; ASD closure and PVR were not. Among patients with PVR ≥ 5 WU who underwent ASD closure, those with SaO2 < 93% (n = 4) had a significantly higher rate of adverse outcomes than those with SaO2 ≥ 93% (n = 7) (hazard ratio, 17.8; P = .014), whereas no composite adverse events occurred in patients with SaO2 ≥ 93%.ConclusionsIn patients with ASD and severe PAH, SaO2 < 93% showed a significant association with adverse outcomes and may complement PVR in risk stratification. These exploratory findings require prospective validation.

articles.title: Beyond Surgical Palliation Success: Uncovering the Profound Mental Health Burden Among Children With Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome in the United States.
articles.journal: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
articles.abstract: ObjectiveMajor initiatives have assessed the burden of mental health in children, but longitudinal analysis of incidences in hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) is limited. We performed an analysis of neurodevelopmental and mental health conditions (NDMHC) on the single-ventricle journey.MethodsThe Pediatric Health Information System (PHIS) registry was queried for pediatric patients (<18 years of age) with International Classification of Diseases codes for HLHS from 2004 to 2024. Patients without birth admission and no Stage-I-palliation were excluded.ResultsThe study included 9348 children and 2617 were diagnosed with an NDMHC. A 1-year-old child had an NDMHC incidence of 2% [1%-2%], a 5-year-old of 12% [11%-13%], a 10-year-old of 27% [25%-20%], and an 18-year-old of 55% [48%-62%]. If overall in-hospital days increase above the 75th percentile, the incidence increases to over 65%. Children with NDMHC were more likely treated at low-volume centers (NDMHC: 34% vs No NDMHC: 23%, P < .001) and came from low household income environments (NDMHC Low Income: 27% vs No NDMC Low Income: 24%, P < .001). Cox regression for the development NDMHC revealed prolonged hospitalization (75th total hospitalization length of stay) (2.26 [2.01-3.53], P < .001), treatment at low-volume centers (4.30 [2.72-6.81], P < .001) and low-income household (3.84 [3.10-5.71], P < .001) were predictors for NDMHC development.ConclusionAs a successfully palliated child enters adulthood, over half will have a neurodevelopmental and mental health condition. This percentage increase significantly as the overall days spent in-hospital increases. This report urges congenital cardiac providers to explore strategies to mitigate the mental health burden.

articles.title: Heart Failure in Anthracycline Cardiotoxicity: From Mechanisms to Clinical Management.
articles.abstract: Anthracyclines remain a cornerstone therapy for haematological malignancies and solid tumours, but their use is limited by cardiotoxicity, ranging from asymptomatic left ventricular dysfunction to overt heart failure (HF). The risk increases with cumulative doxorubicin-equivalent exposure exceeding 250-300 mg/m2, although susceptibility varies substantially according to patient characteristics, pre-existing cardiovascular disease, genetic predisposition, and modifiable risk factors. Clinically overt HF occurs in ∼6-9% of patients, while subclinical cardiac dysfunction develops in up to 18%. The pathophysiology is multifactorial, involving interconnected mechanisms that disrupt cardiomyocyte homeostasis and promote endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, fibrosis, and adverse remodelling. Yet evidence connecting molecular mechanisms with long-term HF outcomes in humans remains incomplete. Risk stratification, incorporating clinical variables, cardiac biomarkers, echocardiography and, when appropriate, cardiac magnetic resonance enables earlier recognition of cardiac dysfunction. Trials of preventive neurohormonal treatment and statins have produced heterogeneous results, often relying on imaging rather than clinical HF endpoints. Once cardiac dysfunction develops, prompt initiation of foundational HF treatment and multidisciplinary decisions on cancer therapy are essential. Early detection and prompt initiation of HF therapies may reverse myocardial dysfunction, whereas delayed recognition is associated with a poorer treatment response and prognosis. This narrative review integrates current evidence on the mechanisms, risk stratification, surveillance, prevention, and management of anthracycline cardiotoxicity and HF, while highlighting gaps in knowledge, emerging therapeutic strategies, and future directions for clinically meaningful, risk-guided research.

articles.title: Design features and implementation of virtual operating-theatre orientation for elective surgical patients: A scoping review.
articles.abstract: Virtual operating room orientation is commonly evaluated for anxiety reduction, leaving uncertainty about programme design and integration into perioperative care. Guided by Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews, this review searched PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Scopus, Web of Science and IEEE Xplore through June 2026; Google Scholar and citation searching supplemented retrieval. Eleven studies described screen-based, immersive or interactive orientation across preoperative timepoints. Operating-theatre and anaesthesia preparation predominated; recovery, discharge, cultural adaptation and accessible alternatives were less represented. Implementation considerations included cybersickness, younger-child non-completion, language and sensory exclusions, technical failures, scheduling, equipment cleaning, staff support and cost. Clinical usefulness depended on matching timing, content and delivery method to a defined purpose. Implementation requires accessible alternatives, clear staff responsibilities, infection-control procedures and evaluation of feasibility, workload, costs and patient-centred outcomes across surgical populations and age groups.

articles.title: FANIN/Zfp148, the upstream regulator of pioneer factor paralogs Foxa1 and Foxa2, controls hepatocyte identity.
articles.abstract: Numerous attempts involving combinations of transcription factors to create functional hepatocytes to enable implantation into patients with chronic and end-stage liver disease have been promising but not yet successful. We identified the upstream regulator of pioneer factor paralogs Foxa1 and Foxa2 in Mus Musculus, critical to hepatogenesis and adult physiological function, we named FANIN. Winged-helix (forkhead) factor paralogs Foxa1 and Foxa2, originally named HNF3α and HNF3β, are called pioneer factors for their ability to independently bind closed chromatin and change chromatin accessibility allowing other factors to bind. Foxa1 and Foxa2, unlike a close homolog Foxa3, are required for life. Deletion of FANIN, encoded by Zfp148, leads to loss of Foxa1 and Foxa2 expression in the liver. FANIN affects global changes in chromatin accessibility, not observed in Foxa2 or Foxa1/Foxa2 double mutants, in particular at regions with enriched HNF4α motif. FANIN controls hepatocyte identity through regulating Foxa1 & Foxa2 expression, as well as activity/binding of HNF4α. Hence, FANIN modulates master regulators that control hepatocyte-specific gene expression and identity. In particular, reduced synergistic Foxa2/HNF4α function in FANIN mutants leads to destabilization of the hepatocyte, resulting in hepatic vacuolization, proliferation, and severe injury. We have uncovered a novel genetic circuit involving master regulators of the hepatocyte, which has significant implications for regeneration of these cells in patients with severe liver disease.

articles.title: Modified Posterior Wall Ablation in Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: the BOX-AF Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The efficacy of left atrial posterior wall isolation (PWI) for persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) is controversial. We propose a modified left atrial posterior wall ablation strategy.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of modified posterior wall ablation in patients with persistent AF who underwent first-time radiofrequency catheter ablation.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this multicenter, single-blind randomized trial, 276 patients with persistent AF were assigned 1:1 to pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) with (BOX+) or without modified posterior wall ablation (BOX-). Seven participants withdrew, leaving 269 (BOX+, n=139; BOX-, n=130) for primary endpoint analysis. The primary endpoint was freedom from any documented atrial arrhythmia lasting > 30 seconds without antiarrhythmic drugs after a 3 -month blanking period. At 12-month follow-up, the primary endpoint occurred in 120 of 139 patients (86.3%) in the BOX+ group and 113 of 130 (86.9%) in the BOX- group (hazard ratio 1.046, 95% CI, 0.54 - 2.01; P = 0.894). The BOX+ group exhibited longer procedure time and ablation time. Acute successful PWI was achieved in 91 (65.5%) patients assigned to BOX+. In a nonprespecified, post-randomization analysis, arrhythmia-free survival was 93.4% in patients with acute successful PWI, 72.9% in those with attempted but unsuccessful PWI, and 86.9% in controls without attempted PWI (overall log-rank P=0.002). Adverse events were similar between groups.

CONCLUSION: Routine addition of modified posterior wall ablation did not improve overall outcomes of first-time ablation in persistent AF. However, achieving successful PWI was associated with significantly lower recurrence.

articles.title: Estimating Dehydration Survival Limits from Plausible Mortality Thresholds.
articles.abstract: The limits of human survival during dehydration are not well defined and are infrequently based on physiological endpoints. We evaluated dehydration survivability using thresholds for hypernatremia and hypovolemia that are consistent with known mechanisms of mortality.MethodsA mass balance approach was used to model changes in blood sodium concentration and blood volume in a 75 kg adult with total body water of 43.7 L. Dehydration was scaled at a 10% loss of body mass (7.5 L). Water and electrolyte losses were modeled under conditions of sweating in warm (∼32 °C) and cool (∼4 °C) environments and during gastrointestinal illness. Blood sodium and blood volume responses were calculated based on volume-weighted sodium losses and standard compartmental assumptions.ResultsThe time to reach 10% dehydration ranged from 2.5 days (eccrine warm) to 5.9 days (eccrine cool) and 3.0 days with gastrointestinal losses. Blood sodium increased to 160 mmol·L-1 with sweating and 146 mmol·L-1 with gastrointestinal losses. Estimated blood volume reductions were 0.844 (sweating) and 1.327 L (gastrointestinal). These values reach or approach those associated with fatal hypernatremia and circulatory shock.DiscussionA dehydration level of approximately 10% body mass (17% total body water) produces physiological conditions consistent with mortality from both hypernatremia and hypovolemia. Survival without water is therefore likely limited to approximately 3 to 6 days under passive conditions, depending on environmental exposure, fluid loss pathways, and individual variability.ConclusionsHypernatremia and hypovolemia provide physiologically grounded thresholds for estimating dehydration survivability. These findings refine existing survival estimates and highlight the critical importance of minimizing fluid loss in austere environments.

articles.title: Association of subjective workload on burnout in village midwives: A NASA TLX-based investigation.
articles.abstract: BackgroundVillage midwives play a central role in delivering maternal and primary healthcare services in rural Indonesia, where professional demands are extensive and resources are limited. Understanding the relationship between subjective workload and burnout is essential to support their occupational well-being.ObjectiveThis study examined the association between multidimensional subjective workload and burnout among village midwives using the NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX).MethodsA cross-sectional survey was conducted among 209 village midwives in Kediri District, Indonesia, selected through simple random sampling from the official registry. Subjective workload was assessed using the six NASA-TLX dimensions: mental demand, physical demand, temporal demand, performance, effort, and frustration. Burnout was measured using the Maslach Burnout Inventory. Ordinal logistic regression was used to evaluate associations between workload dimensions and burnout levels.ResultsMost respondents reported moderate workload and moderate burnout. Mental demand, physical demand, temporal demand, performance pressure, and effort were significantly associated with higher burnout levels, whereas frustration was not statistically significant.ConclusionsMultiple dimensions of subjective workload were associated with burnout among village midwives. These findings support systematic workload assessment to identify occupational strain and inform institutional strategies to promote midwives' well-being in rural healthcare settings. The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.

articles.title: Preconception Mycoplasma genitalium Seropositivity and Risk of Impaired Fecundity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mycoplasma genitalium (MG) is an emerging sexually transmitted infection (STI) associated with pelvic inflammatory disease. Its relationship with impaired fecundity remains unclear and is rarely examined in the context of co-seropositivity with other STIs.

METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of the Effects of Aspirin in Gestation and Reproduction (EAGeR) trial, a prospective preconception cohort of women with proven fecundity and prior pregnancy loss. MG serostatus was determined using Western blot-based IgG assays on 1146 stored serum specimens. Chlamydia trachomatis (CT) and other STIs were also measured. Associations between MG seropositivity and measures of impaired fecundity were assessed.Pregnancy loss and live birth were modeled using inverse-probability weighted quasi-Poisson and unweighted log-binomial models to calculate relative risks (RR). Fecundability-odds-ratio (FOR) was estimated using a discrete Cox proportional hazards model accounting for left truncation and right censoring. Propensity score (PS) weighted versions of these models assessed risks associated with CT co-seropositivity. Analyses were adjusted for demographic and reproductive history variables.

RESULTS: Overall, 17.1% (n=210) of participants were MG seropositive, with 27.6% (n=58) co-seropositive with CT. Compared to STI-seronegative women, MG seropositivity was not associated with any outcome, although trends were observed for reduced fecundability (FORadj: 0.87, 95% CI 0.70-1.08) and live birth (RRadj: 0.94, 95% CI 0.79-1.11). Co-seropositivity with CT was associated with lower likelihood of live birth [RRPS-weighted: 0.82, 95% CI: 0.70-0.96]. Sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of these findings.

CONCLUSIONS: Being co-seropositive for MG and CT preconception was associated with impaired fecundity.

articles.title: Left ventricular arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy presenting as a "hot phase" mimicking acute myocarditis.
Letter: Response to "Roadmap to Fully Closing the Loop" and Call for a Charter for Consensus Statements in Diabetes.
Multimodal neuroimaging in Alzheimer's disease: A practical, case-illustrated review of quantitative MRI and molecular PET.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) accounts for 60-70% of dementia cases worldwide. Current diagnostic pathways rely on structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to exclude secondary causes, amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) to confirm pathology, and tau PET for disease staging. However, these approaches are limited by subjectivity, cost, accessibility, and variability in interpretation. Quantitative imaging tools such as volumetric MRI and NeuroQuant offer reproducible metrics that may enhance diagnostic precision and standardization. This review synthesizes literature published between 2000 and 2026 evaluating structural MRI, quantitative volumetric MRI, amyloid PET, tau PET, FDG PET, and emerging adjunctive imaging techniques, supplemented by illustrative clinical cases demonstrating multimodal integration in practice. Particular emphasis is placed on the role of NeuroQuant in standardized atrophy quantification and its integration with molecular imaging modalities. Volumetric MRI enhances PET-based diagnosis and staging by contextualizing amyloid and tau pathology within patterns of selective neurodegeneration. Quantitative metrics correlate with cognitive decline and disease progression. Multimodal imaging strategies improve diagnostic specificity, longitudinal monitoring, and phenotypic stratification across the AD. Multimodal imaging provides a comprehensive framework for AD management. Quantitative MRI using NeuroQuant bridges structural and molecular domains, supporting standardized assessment and integration with emerging precision diagnostic approaches.

articles.title: Predicting Multidrug-Resistant Infection upon Admission to Hospitals: A Prospective Interventional Multicenter Crossover Trial.
articles.abstract: Delayed initiation of appropriate antimicrobial therapy (DAAT) is the strongest modifiable independent predictor of mortality in severe sepsis and occurs frequently in patients with multidrug-resistant organism infections upon hospital admission (MDR-UA). This study evaluated whether a bedside MDR-UA prediction calculator reduces DAAT and improves clinical outcomes. A prospective interventional crossover trial was conducted (July 2023-September 2024) across two large academic hospitals in central Israel. Adult inpatients with sepsis were enrolled; during intervention periods, the calculator score was communicated to Infectious Diseases consultants within 48 hours. DAAT and hospitalization outcomes were compared by using multivariable regressions. Of 1,524 enrolled patients, 514 (33%) had microbiologically confirmed infection, of whom 200 (39%) had MDR-UA. The calculator demonstrated suboptimal performances (ROC-AUC: 0.68), and the intervention had no impact on DAAT (p = 0.50). The intervention was independently associated with reduced discharge rates to long-term care facilities among survivors of the index stay who were admitted from home (aOR = 2.0; 95% CI: 1.3-3.2), but did not affect mortality or other hospitalization's outcomes. This prospective trial demonstrates that an MDR-UA calculator exhibiting lower-than-expected predictive performance did not reduce DAAT in routine clinical practice, highlighting the importance of prospective validation of clinical prediction tools. AI-based adaptive platforms may offer an alternative to current static prediction models.

articles.title: Assessing the Utility of a Capillary-Adjusted Oral Glucose Tolerance Test for the Early Detection of Type 1 Diabetes in Childhood.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) is the gold standard for staging and monitoring type 1 diabetes (T1D), but it requires venous sampling in a health care setting, limiting its accessibility. We assessed the utility of a capillary-adjusted OGTT (cOGTT) method in children and young people (CYP).

METHODS: Study 1-OGTT method comparison: CYP across the glycemic range underwent contemporaneous venous (vGluc) and capillary (cGluc) glucose sampling at 0-min, 60-min (subgroup), and 120-min after a standard oral glucose load. Agreement between vGluc and cGluc was assessed using Bland-Altman between 3.5 and 15 mmol/L. Glycemic status was assessed using established thresholds and acceptability by questionnaire. Study 2-At-home OGTT feasibility: CYP with early-stage T1D undertook home cOGTT testing (0, 120 min) and completed acceptability questionnaires.

RESULTS: Study 1: Forty-five CYP participated (mean [SD] age 12.2 [3.2] years; range 5-17), with 20 undergoing additional 60-min sampling. cGluc and vGluc showed reasonable agreement across the glycemic range of 3.5-15 mmol/L, (bias, -0.22 mmol/L; 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.51 to 0.07; 95% limits of agreement, -2.91 to 2.47 mmol/L). cGluc performed well at normoglycemia: 21/22 (95% sensitivity; 95% CI: 77%-100%), 14/17 (82% specificity; 57%-96%); and hyperglycemia: 9/10 (90% sensitivity; 55%-100%), 29/29 (100% specificity; 88%-100%); but less well for dysglycemia: 4/7 (57% sensitivity; 18%-90%), 30/32 (94% specificity; 79%-99%). In 76% (32/42), cOGTT was preferred for future testing. Study 2: 45 CYP participated (10.4 [3.1] years; range 4-17). In 91% (41/45), home cOGTT tests were completed successfully (3 device failures, 1 incomplete test). Home testing was acceptable in 98% (44 of 45). Two CYP were identified with stage 3 T1D with no evidence of DKA.

CONCLUSIONS: The cOGTT method is feasible and acceptable compared with venous OGTT in CYP, with promising performance for detecting hyperglycemia, but further assessment is needed before it can be used for glycemic staging.

articles.title: Epidemiology, Etiology, and Outcomes of Cardioembolic Stroke in Young Adults 2014-2025: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardioembolic (CE) stroke is an important and potentially preventable cause of young-onset ischemic stroke, yet its global prevalence, causes, diagnostic practices, and outcomes are incompletely defined. Better characterization of CE burden in adults aged 15-55 years is needed to guide investigation and secondary prevention.

METHODS: We registered the review with PROSPERO CRD420251047443 and followed PRISMA 2020. We searched PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, Web of Science and Cochrane for observational studies from January 2014 to May 2025 on cardioembolic stroke proportions in patients aged 15 to 55. Two reviewers screened and extracted data in Rayyan with a third reviewer resolving disagreements. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Analysis comprised descriptive and stratified synthesis of overall and regional CE proportions, subgroup analyses by age, sex, region and period, and tabulated summaries of CE sources and outcomes.

RESULTS: Twenty-three studies (n = 16,301 patients) met inclusion (median NOS = 6). The pooled mean proportion of CE stroke was 18.0%, with regional means of Europe 19.9%, Asia 11.5%, the Americas 22.0%, and Middle East & Africa 24.8%. Younger patients (<40 years) more often had structural causes (e.g., PFO, cardiomyopathy), while older patients had higher AF-related proportions. Diagnostic intensity varied, limited use of TEE and prolonged rhythm monitoring in some regions likely underestimated CE detection. CE strokes were associated with higher initial severity, greater recurrence (5-14% across cohorts), and worse functional outcomes compared with many non-cardioembolic subtypes; mortality was comparable overall but higher when AF was present.

CONCLUSION: CE stroke accounts for 18% of ischemic stroke in young adults but shows wide geographic and diagnostic variability driven by regional cardiac disease patterns and access to advanced cardiac testing. Standardized, tiered cardiac evaluation (including TEE and prolonged rhythm monitoring) and consistent reporting are needed to improve etiologic attribution and reduce recurrence through timely anticoagulation and targeted interventions.

articles.title: Glucocorticoid purchases and methotrexate persistence in early rheumatoid arthritis in Finland.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore purchases of methotrexate (MTX), biological disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (bDMARDs), Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKis), and glucocorticoids (GCs) in early rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in Finland.

METHOD: The study included 3046 monitored patients with early RA, who obtained reimbursement for RA medication during 2016-2020. The patients were divided into three groups according to the number of GC tablet purchases during 6 months after the reimbursement day: Group 0, no GC purchases; Group 1, purchased < 90 tablets; Group 2, purchased ≥ 90 tablets. Medication purchases were tracked in 6 month periods until the end of 2021.

RESULTS: Of the monitored early RA patients, 68% purchased GCs during the initial 6 months and 43% during 6-11 months after the reimbursement date. Over 90% of the patients purchased MTX during the first year in all groups. Patients in Group 2 had the highest baseline disease activity. After the first year, the percentage of bDMARD purchasers (11% vs 6.8%, p = 0.03) and MTX users (79% vs 74%, p = 0.06) was higher in Group 2 than in Group 0. Nevertheless, persistence with analysed anti-rheumatic medications remained similar, with no statistically significant differences, during the whole follow-up period in all groups.

CONCLUSION: In early RA, the use of oral GCs is common and continues longer than recommended by the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR). Persistence with treatment with MTX, bDMARDs, and JAKis in patients who continued medication was not influenced by the initial GC regimen.

articles.title: Helicobacter pylori eradication and gastric cancer prevention: current evidence and future perspectives.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Helicobacter pylori infection is recognized as the principal etiological factor in gastric carcinogenesis, and despite the widespread implementation of H. pylori eradication strategies, the global burden of gastric cancer remains substantial.

AREAS COVERED: This review summarizes the role of H. pylori (through key bacterial survival mechanisms, epithelial colonization, immune evasion, and virulence factors that promote persistent inflammation and mucosal injury) in gastric carcinogenesis, focusing on the sequential gastric mucosal alterations described in the Correa cascade that are accompanied by activation of oncogenic signaling pathways. Relevant literature was identified from databases (including PubMed and Scopus).

EXPERT OPINION: Recent translational studies have highlighted the complexity of H. pylori-related determinants of GC progression, including bacterial virulence factors, alterations in the gastric environment, gastric microbiota, and host genetic susceptibility. However, the precise mechanisms underlying each determinant are still being elucidated. Therefore, in recent clinical practice, the early detection and eradication strategies remain the most realistic and impactful interventions. In the future, eradication-focused management may shift to a more stratified model that includes earlier screening in high-risk populations, wider use of susceptibility-guided or region-adapted therapy, and molecular risk surveillance after eradication, refining recent practice.

articles.title: Zero-Contrast Transcatheter Aortic Valve-in-Valve Replacement Guided by Continuous Hemodynamic Monitoring.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: An 89-year-old man with structural deterioration of a surgical aortic bioprosthesis and renal dysfunction underwent zero-contrast transcatheter aortic valve-in-surgical valve (TAV-in-SAV) implantation. A SavvyWire provided continuous left ventricular pressure monitoring and rapid pacing during the procedure. After implantation of a 23-mm self-expanding valve, a residual transvalvular gradient was detected, prompting balloon postdilatation under rapid pacing. Repeat invasive hemodynamic assessment showed improvement, and echocardiography demonstrated a mean gradient of 12 mmHg. At 12 months, the patient was in New York Heart Association class I, with preserved renal function and a mean gradient of 8 mmHg. Continuous pressure monitoring may support intraprocedural assessment and guide valve optimization when contrast exposure is being avoided in patients with renal dysfunction.

articles.title: Predictive Value of PET-Derived Myocardial Flow Reserve for New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) commonly coexists with coronary artery disease, heart failure, and coronary microvascular dysfunction, sharing common risk factors and pathophysiologic mechanisms. Whether myocardial flow reserve (MFR), a positron emission tomography-derived measure of epicardial and microvascular function, predicts incident AF remains uncertain.

METHODS: We included 10 500 patients without prior AF who underwent positron emission tomography MPI at 2 centers. The primary outcome was new-onset AF during follow-up.
