Multivariable Cox models adjusted for demographics, comorbidities, resting left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and LVEF reserve were used to evaluate the association between MFR and incident AF. Incremental predictive value was assessed using χ2, Akaike's information criterion, Bayesian information criterion, C-index, and a likelihood ratio test comparing models with and without MFR.

RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 640 days, 288 patients (2.74%) developed AF. Impaired MFR (<2) was associated with a higher incidence of AF (20.5 versus 8.3 per 1000 person years). In multivariable analysis, MFR was a significant predictor of AF (hazard ratio per 1 interquartile range increase, 0.58 [95% CI, 0.47-0.72]; P<0.0001), whereas stress and rest myocardial blood flow were not. MFR improved risk prediction beyond clinical variables and LVEF (C-index increased from 0.675-0.726 when added to clinical variables and from 0.758-0.770 when added to clinical variables, LVEF, and summed stress score; P<0.001). Similar incremental improvement was observed when MFR was added to the Cohorts for Heart and Aging Research in Genomic Epidemiology-Atrial Fibrillation risk score (C-index increased from 0.638 to 0.711). The association between MFR and incident AF was numerically greater in patients with preserved EF, although the interaction term was not statistically significant.

CONCLUSIONS: Impaired positron emission tomography-derived MFR is independently associated with increased risk of new-onset AF and enhances risk prediction beyond clinical factors and LVEF, suggesting a role for coronary microvascular dysfunction in early AF pathogenesis.

articles.title: A Novel Double Kissing Nano Culotte Stenting for Coronary Bifurcation Lesions: A Detailed Technical Evaluation and Clinical Outcomes.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) of coronary bifurcation lesions (CBL) remains one of the most technically demanding procedures in interventional cardiology, and the optimal two-stent stratgy has yet to be established. A technique that minimizes stent overlap while ensuring complete side branch osteal scaffolding may improve procedural and clinical outcomes.

AIMS: Our aim in this study is to evaluate the feasibility, procedural performance, and 1-year clinical outcomes of the novel double kissing (DK) nano culotte technique for the treatment of CBL.

METHODS: In this prospective, single-center observational study, 43 patients with true de novo CBLs underwent PCI using the DK nano-culotte technique, with OCT guidance used in 30 patients (69.7%). Eligible lesions had distal main-vessel and side-branch reference diameters ≥ 2.5 and ≥ 2.25 mm, respectively. Bench testing preceded first-in-human application, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) analysis was performed. The primary endpoint was 1-year target lesion failure (TLF), defined as the composite of target lesion revascularization (TLR), target vessel myocardial infarction (TVMI), and cardiac death.

RESULTS: Procedural and technical success were achieved in 100.0% and 97.6% of cases, respectively, with a mean procedure time of 48.0 ± 14.9 min. Residual diameter stenosis remained low across all treated segments, and no significant stent malapposition (> 500 μm) was identified by OCT. CFD demonstrated favorable post-procedural hemodynamic remodeling with significant improvement in time-averaged wall shear stress. At 1 year, TLF occurred in one patient (2.38%) owing to silent ischemia associated with in-stent restenosis requiring repeat revascularization. No TVMI, cardiac death, or stent thrombosis was observed.

CONCLUSIONS: The DK nano culotte technique demonstrated excellent procedural feasibility, precise stent optimization, favorable flow dynamics, and encouraging 1-year clinical outcomes. These findings support further evaluation of this OCT-guided bifurcation strategy in larger multicenter studies (DK Nano-Culotte Stenting For Coronary Bifurcation Lesion; NCT05406284).

articles.title: Nonculprit Lesion Complexity and Timing of Complete Revascularization in Patients Presenting With Acute Coronary Syndrome and Multivessel Disease: Insights From the BIOVASC Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal timing of complete revascularization for patients with acute coronary syndrome, multivessel disease and complex nonculprit coronary lesions (NCL) remains unclear.

METHODS: The BIOVASC trial randomized patients with acute coronary syndrome and multivessel disease to immediate complete revascularization and staged complete revascularization. The primary end point was a composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, unplanned ischemia-driven revascularization, or cerebrovascular events at 2-year follow-up. In this exploratory post hoc analysis, patients were classified as having complex NCL if at least 1 nonculprit lesion met the following criteria: true bifurcation; severe calcification; lesion length >20 mm; aorto-ostial lesion; left main lesion. We aimed to compare a strategy of immediate complete revascularization and staged complete revascularization in patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome and multivessel disease with complex NCL. Moreover, we sought to compare patients with complex and noncomplex NCLs in terms of clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: Among the 1525 patients enrolled in the BIOVASC trial, 550 (36.1%) had a complex NCL. The presence of a complex NCL was associated with a significantly higher incidence of the primary end point compared with noncomplex NCL (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.49 [95% CI, 1.11-2.02]; P=0.01), including spontaneous myocardial infarction (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.86 [95% CI, 1.12-3.09]; P=0.02). In patients with complex NCL, the cumulative incidence of the primary end point was 15.7% in the immediate complete revascularization group and 17.5% in the staged complete revascularization group (hazard ratio, 0.86 [95% CI, 0.57-1.31]; P=0.49). No significant interaction was observed between the presence of a complex NCL and revascularization strategy for the primary end point (P for interaction=0.40).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with acute coronary syndrome and multivessel disease, patients with complex NCL experienced worse clinical outcomes at 2-year follow-up, driven by higher rates of myocardial infarction. However, no statistically significant interaction was observed between NCL complexity and the effect of immediate complete revascularization versus staged complete revascularization.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT03621501.

articles.title: Impact of Coronary Sinus Reducer on the Extent of Ischemia in Functional Stress Tests.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The coronary sinus reducer is an established therapy for patients with refractory angina due to obstructive coronary artery disease who are not candidates for further revascularization. Although symptomatic benefits are well documented, its effect on objective measures of ischemia remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between coronary sinus reducer implantation and inducible myocardial ischemia assessed by functional stress testing.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a prospectively maintained registry of consecutive patients undergoing coronary sinus reducer implantation between 2011 and 2024. Baseline assessment included Canadian Cardiovascular Society angina class, 6-minute walk test, stress echocardiography, and dipyridamole single-photon emission computed tomography imaging, repeated at 6 months. Coprimary outcomes were changes in stress wall motion score index and in the proportion of patients with moderate or severe ischemia on single-photon emission computed tomography. Clinical nonresponders were defined as no improvement in Canadian Cardiovascular Society class at 12 months.

RESULTS: Among 153 treated patients, 118 had complete imaging data. Median stress wall motion score index improved from 1.38 to 1.23 (P<0.001), and stress left ventricular ejection fraction increased from 55% to 60% (P=0.019). The proportion of patients with moderate or severe ischemia on single-photon emission computed tomography decreased from 52% to 24% (P<0.001). The summed difference score, available in 45 patients, did not change significantly. Clinically, 86% improved by ≥1 Canadian Cardiovascular Society class at 6 months.

CONCLUSIONS: Coronary sinus reducer implantation was associated with reduced inducible ischemia on stress echocardiography and with clinical improvement. The proportion of patients with moderate or severe ischemia on single-photon emission computed tomography decreased following Reducer implantation.

articles.title: Study on the denitrification performance and mechanism of high-Salinity wastewater treated by anaerobic ammonia oxidation driven by exogenous L-Proline.
articles.abstract: To address the inhibition of nitrogen removal performance in anaerobic ammonium oxidation systems under high salinity conditions, this study investigated the regulatory effects and mechanisms of exogenous L-proline through a 42-day salinity gradient shock experiment. Results indicate that at a total nitrogen load of 255 mg/L in influent, a salinity of 5 g/L enhances the system's nitrogen removal efficiency. However, prolonged exposure to high salinity (10 g/L) causes a gradual decline in denitrification performance. When salinity exceeded 15 g/L, system functionality deteriorated significantly, with average total nitrogen removal efficiency dropping to 43.14% and the stoichiometric ratio deviating from theoretical values (Rs value as low as 0.22). In contrast, adding 0.7 mM L-proline under 15 g/L salinity stress stabilized total nitrogen removal efficiency at approximately 92.96%, with stoichiometry aligning with normal anaerobic ammonium oxidation patterns. High-throughput monitoring revealed that exogenous L-proline maintained community diversity, increasing the abundance of the core bacterium Candidatus Brocadia from 1.18% to 5.99% and significantly boosting denitrifying bacteria like Thauera (from 0.1% to 24.20%). Analysis concluded that L-proline alleviates salinity inhibition in anaerobic ammonium oxidation treatment of saline wastewater.

articles.title: When Risk Becomes a Diagnosis: Biomarker-Driven CKM Stage Migration in Chronic Kidney Disease.

Older Adults Seeking Publicly Funded Long-Term Care in a Super-ageing Society: Trends in Functional Impairments and Multimorbidity Burden Based on InterRAI-Home Care Data From 2001 to 2019 in Hong Kong.
articles.abstract: BackgroundUnderstanding changes in long-term care (LTC) applicants' needs informs service planning.ObjectiveTo examine trends in functional impairment and multimorbidity among Hong Kong's publicly funded LTC applicants during 2001-2019.MethodsWe analyzed interRAI assessments from 315,556 applicants aged ≥60. Hierarchical mixed-effects models estimated trends in physical and cognitive impairment, loneliness, and multimorbidity, adjusting for age, birth cohort, and sociodemographic factors. Subgroup analyses examined differences by age, disease, and living status.ResultsCognitive impairment and multimorbidity increased, physical impairment plateaued, and loneliness declined. Stroke was associated with greater physical and cognitive impairment, and cataract with greater loneliness. Applicants aged ≥85 had more functional impairments but less multimorbidity.ConclusionsApplicants' functional and health needs became more complex and varied over time, differing by age, living arrangements, and disease profiles. These findings support integrated, tailored strategies to address changing health and social needs of older adults applying for publicly funded LTC services.

articles.title: Osteoarticular Infection in Immunocompromised Children and Neonates: A Retrospective Case Series Emphasising Diagnostic Challenges and Multimodal Management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osteoarticular infections (OAIs) in neonates and immunocompromised children present distinct diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Atypical clinical presentations, attenuated inflammatory responses, and a broader spectrum of pathogens complicate early recognition and management. This study characterizes the clinical presentation, microbiology, management, and outcomes of OAIs in this highly vulnerable population.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective case series of patients younger than 16 years with osteomyelitis and/or septic arthritis managed at a tertiary pediatric center between February 2017 and February 2024. The cohort comprised neonates and children with primary or secondary immunodeficiency. Clinical presentation, inflammatory markers, microbiology, antimicrobial and surgical treatment, immune-directed therapy, and outcomes were analyzed descriptively. Ethical approval was obtained from the SingHealth Centralized Institutional Review Board (CIRB Ref: 2023-2559).

RESULTS: Eighteen patients were included; 6 (33.3%) were neonates. All patients had reduced active limb mobility, and 14 (77.8%) had localized swelling. Twelve patients (66.7%) had fever, whereas 6 (33.3%), predominantly neonates, remained afebrile. CRP was elevated in all patients despite variable white blood cell responses. Staphylococcus aureus was the most frequently identified pathogen [6/18 (33.3%)]; other organisms included Streptococci, Mycobacteria, Candida tropicalis, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, and Bacillus spp. Fifteen patients (83.3%) underwent surgical intervention, and 6 (33.3%) received immune-directed therapy. At last follow-up, 14 patients (77.8%) had complete resolution, 2 died from causes unrelated to the OAI, 1 was lost to follow-up, and 1 had persistent or recurrent infection. Two patients developed chronic musculoskeletal sequelae.

CONCLUSION: OIAs in this heterogeneous cohort were frequently accompanied by attenuated systemic features and diverse microbiology. Fever and leucocytosis were not invariably present, whereas CRP was elevated in all cases and provided supplementary information alongside clinical assessment. Favorable outcomes were observed in the context of multidisciplinary, multimodal management, but the retrospective design, small sample, and population heterogeneity preclude causal or subgroup-specific conclusions. These findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV-retrospective case series.

articles.title: Microdosing, fractional and split dosing of injectable GLP-1-based drugs: balancing potential benefits and risks.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based drugs (also known as incretin receptor agonists) have revolutionized the management of type 2 diabetes and overweight/obesity. Microdosing, fractional dosing and split dosing of GLP-1-based drugs administered by subcutaneous injection (particularly the newer incretin receptor agonists semaglutide and tirzepatide) have recently emerged as alternative off-label dosing strategies used to improve long-term treatment tolerability while preserving or optimizing the therapeutic benefits of these agents. Evidence regarding these practices is mostly anecdotal and their use is not supported by manufacturers, scientific societies, drug regulatory agencies and official clinical guidelines. Fractional dosing of injectable incretin receptor agonists is the off-label administration of injectable GLP-1-based drugs at a fraction of a given standard approved drug dose by counting the audible and tactile clicks generated as the dose selector dial of pre-filled multi-dose injection pens (MDPs) is turned forward (off-label "click-counting" method). Microdosing of injectable incretin receptor agonists represents a form of fractional dosing that consists of administering subtherapeutic doses ["microdoses": doses lower than the lowest standard approved drug dose (starting dose)] of injectable GLP-1-based drugs with pre-filled MDPs through the "click-counting" method. Split dosing of injectable once-weekly incretin receptor agonists consists of administering smaller doses of an injectable once-weekly GLP-1-based drug more frequently than once per week with pre-filled MDPs through the "click-counting" method. This Special Article aims to provide a critical appraisal of the potential benefits and risks of microdosing, fractional dosing and split dosing of injectable GLP-1-based drugs, which warrant thorough investigation in future pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic studies and clinical trials.

articles.title: Adverse Childhood Experiences and the Occupational Performance of U.S. Service Members-A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Scholars and providers continue to study Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs)-abuse, neglect, or household challenges occurring before the age of 18-because of their significant dose-response relationship with negative adult outcomes across all domains of physical and mental health. However, there is minimal literature evaluating the relationship between ACEs and occupational performance (here defined as one's subjective assessment of their success with daily activities and functions) and specifically focused on military service members (SMs). This study sought to fill these gaps through a cross-sectional survey of U.S. military adults at 1 military treatment facility in Texas. The goal was to inform and facilitate relevant and effective interventions, bolstering larger-scale efforts to improve warfighter readiness and resilience.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: The Carl R. Darnall Army Medical Center Institutional Review Board approved this cross-sectional study (eIRB CRDAMC.23-68). The researchers used convenience sampling to invite participants. Clinic administrators provided de-identified surveys to patients that comprised demographics, ACE screening, and self-assessment of performance and value for 21 occupations (meaningful activities/functions). Researchers used descriptive statistics and Spearman's Rho correlations to explore potential relationships between ACE scores and performance in occupations. Further analyses assessed whether routinely collected demographics had predictive value in determining a participant's occupational performance.

RESULTS: The sample's (n = 76) mean ACE score was 3.82. Participants identified "expressing myself to others," "concentrating on my tasks," and "relaxing and enjoying myself" as the most difficult occupations to perform. Participants reported the least difficulty in "taking care of others for whom I am responsible." Overall occupational performance across the 21 categories of occupations did not significantly correlate with ACEs, with 1 exception: a weak positive relationship existed between ACE score and taking care of others (rs = 0.235, P = .040). Participants with higher ACE scores reported higher performance in taking care of others.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite recruiting only health-seeking SMs at 1 medical facility, demographics nearly matched the population of U.S. military adults. This adds some confidence in considering similar associations in the greater population, though convenience sampling and overall sample size warrant further study to reasonably generalize findings. Consistent with previous research, results show SMs are more likely to report at least 1 ACE and to report higher ACE scores than non-SMs. Participants did not seem to perceive extreme ease or difficulty with daily occupations, nor did their valuation of surveyed occupations skew toward apathy or significant importance. Though a clear correlation was not identified between ACEs and overall performance, the positive relationship between ACE scores and caretaking warrants further investigation. Ultimately, the relationship between ACEs and SM performance remains unclear. This may be because of the complex nature of occupational performance-a result of the dynamic interaction between bodily systems, personal and contextual factors, and environmental influences. ACE screening may yet prove clinically valuable for improving provider-client collaboration and developing effective, occupation-based interventions that validate the patient experience.

articles.title: Pharmacogenomics of antidiabetic agents: current evidence and implications for precision medicine.
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus, a noncommunicable disease, is controlled with antidiabetic medications. However, interindividual variations require tailored therapy with suitable drugs to achieve glycemic control. Very few studies have focused on candidate genes that regulate drug transport and the target sensitivity of antidiabetic drugs. These genes help predict treatment efficacy, adverse reactions, and long-term maintenance of glycemic control, particularly by reducing the risk of severe hypoglycemia and therapeutic failure. Pharmacogenomics has paved the way for personalized therapy and the identification of novel targets. This review will cover the genes involved in type 2 diabetes mellitus, mainly SLC2A2, SLC47A1, SLC47A2, CYP2C9, SUR1, GLP1R, TCF7L2, ABCC8, and KCNQ1, associated with various antidiabetic drugs.

articles.title: Halochromic composite materials for self-indicating wound-healing textiles: a review.
articles.journal: Zeitschrift fur Naturforschung. C, Journal of biosciences
articles.abstract: Wound healing is a dynamic and multifactorial process that requires timely assessment to identify changes in the wound microenvironment and to support appropriate clinical management. Conventional wound dressings primarily provide physical protection but generally lack the ability to provide continuous visual information about changing wound conditions. Halochromic composite materials have been investigated as smart wound-healing textiles because they can generate visible, pH-responsive colour changes associated with changes in the wound microenvironment. This review summarizes wound-healing phases, wound types, and factors that influence wound pH, and discusses the chemistry, classification, and pH-responsive behaviour of major halochromic dye systems, including phthalein, azo, fluoran, styryl, and leucotriarylmethane dyes. Recent strategies for integrating pH-responsive dyes into textile-based wound dressings, including conventional dyeing, coating, sol-gel processing, encapsulation, and electrospinning, are also reviewed. Importantly, a colour change in a halochromic material is an indirect indicator of the wound microenvironment and may provide information relevant to infection-associated alkalinization; it should not be interpreted as a direct measurement of wound healing. The review further considers biocompatibility, dye migration, sterilization, and other translational issues that must be addressed before clinical application.

articles.title: Lipoprotein(a) in Cardiovascular Disease: Integrating Epidemiology, Clinical Guidelines, Molar Measurement, and Emerging Therapies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD = myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, peripheral artery disease) and aortic valve stenosis. Plasma concentrations of Lp(a) are >90% genetically determined. Multiple drugs in development reduce lipoprotein(a) by 80% to 98%. While the recently announced topline results, the phase 3 Lp(a)HORIZON trial of pelacarsen did not meet its primary cardiovascular endpoint despite lowering Lp(a), and 3 other cardiovascular outcomes trials remain ongoing. Lipoprotein(a) testing is currently increasing rapidly in many countries.

CONTENT: Most guidelines on dyslipidemia and prevention of cardiovascular disease worldwide now advise that Lp(a) should be measured once in all adults, ideally jointly with the first lipid profile ordered. If previous lipid profiles were taken, then Lp(a) should be included in the next lipid profile. Lipoprotein(a) should ideally be measured in nmol/L, and repeat measurements are relevant if drugs are given to lower Lp(a) concentrations, initially at suspected acute coronary syndrome or stroke and again after 1 month, and sometimes in women after menopause. Measuring Lp(a) levels alongside a standard lipid profile provides a more comprehensive initial assessment of a patient's overall cardiovascular risk. Clinical chemistry laboratories that measure lipid profiles should therefore also offer Lp(a) testing. This is easily done as Lp(a) assays can be run on most major clinical chemistry platforms. High Lp(a) is >105 nmol/L (>50 mg/dL).

SUMMARY: As use of Lp(a) testing is increasing rapidly worldwide, more clinical chemistry laboratories will likely offer this test locally. Measuring Lp(a) levels alongside a standard lipid profile provides a more comprehensive initial lipid assessment of a patient's cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: Astragaloside IV Mitigates Hepatocyte Apoptosis in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Fatty Liver Disease Through Inhibition of CASP3-Dependent PARP1 Cleavage.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is associated with hepatic lipid accumulation, inflammation, and hepatocyte apoptosis. Astragaloside IV (AS-IV) has been reported to regulate lipid metabolism, but its effects on hepatocyte apoptosis in MAFLD remain unclear. We investigated the effects of AS-IV in db/db mice and free fatty acid (FFA)-treated HepG2 cells using biochemical assays, histological staining, measurements of inflammatory markers and reactive oxygen species, and apoptosis assays. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were used to identify candidate targets, followed by analyses of CASP3 and PARP1 expression and cleavage and CASP3 overexpression experiments. AS-IV reduced hepatic and cellular triglyceride accumulation, inflammatory markers, and hepatocyte apoptosis, and improved liver histology and serum markers of liver injury in db/db mice. These effects were accompanied by reduced CASP3 activation and PARP1 cleavage. In HepG2 cells, AS-IV also attenuated the changes associated with CASP3 overexpression. Together, these findings suggest that suppression of CASP3-associated PARP1 cleavage may contribute to the protective effects of AS-IV in these experimental models of MAFLD.

articles.title: Hemodynamic effects of a novel counter-pulsatile system for extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.
articles.abstract: Background and aimsMortality from heart failure is still high despite all the recent advances. Continuous-flow (CF) Veno-arterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (VA-ECMO) can temporarily maintain systemic and pulmonary hemodynamics, at the cost of overloading the left ventricle (LV). A new Pulsatile Ventricular Assist Platform (pVAP) could offer a more physiological hemodynamic support.Methods6 large porcine models of acute ischemic left ventricular (LV) failure received the pVAP in a VA-ECMO configuration. Invasive systemic and intraventricular hemodynamic measurements were taken with synchronized counter-pulsatile flow (SCPF) and CF support at the same flow rate. The measurements were compared with no support (ON vs OFF) in both modalities.ResultsThe pVAP successfully delivered VA-ECMO in acute ischemic heart failure. The device maintained stable hemodynamics and increased the forward cardiac output (COF) without overloading the LV and with no change in the LV pressure-volume area (PVA). SCPF, but not CF, was associated with improved LV afterload and ventricular-arterial coupling compared to no support.ConclusionThe findings suggest that the pVAP is feasible also in a VA-ECMO configuration, supporting hemodynamics with more physiological effect on effect on the LV dynamics.

articles.title: Evo2VED: a database of DNA large language model-derived scores for variant interpretation.
articles.abstract: The Evo2 Variant Effect Database (Evo2VED; https://dnallmved.org/) is a publicly accessible resource cataloging precomputed Evo2-derived variant effect scores, defined as allelic score differences, for 6.48 million human variants common in the gnomAD non-Finnish European population. Evo2VED includes scores from the 7B and 40B models under three scoring schemes, alongside annotations of variant function, evolutionary constraint, allele age, and disease associations. It integrates genome-wide association study (GWAS) data from UK Biobank, FinnGen, and the Million Veteran Program. Three complementary modules support variant-level interpretation, regional and region-set exploration, and trait-level analysis through flexible queries, interactive visualizations, and downloadable results. Evo2VED also catalogs associations between Evo2 annotations and per-SNP heritability across thousands of traits from these biobanks. A guided workflow connects GWAS with associated regions and individual variant evidence. Case studies of hypertension and depression illustrate how regional comparisons of Evo2 scores and GWAS signals can guide candidate variant prioritization. Evaluations using massively parallel reporter assays, molecular QTLs, fine-mapping probabilities, and clinical annotations assess associations with Evo2 scores alone and their added value beyond conservation and regulatory annotations. By providing accessible scores, contextual annotations, and comparative analyses, Evo2VED facilitates exploration and application of genomic language model predictions in human genetics research.

articles.title: Beyond Complete Revascularization in STEMI: Revisiting the Vulnerable Plaque Hypothesis and the Emerging Role of Preventive PCI in Non-Culprit Coronary Arteries.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Complete revascularization is the preferred treatment strategy for hemodynamically stable patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and multivessel coronary artery disease. However, substantial residual cardiovascular risk persists despite successful treatment of angiographically or physiologically significant lesions, highlighting the limitations of revascularization strategies based solely on stenosis severity or ischemia. Increasing evidence demonstrates that many subsequent acute coronary syndromes originate from biologically high-risk, non-flow-limiting non-culprit plaques rather than flow-limiting lesions. In this review, we discuss the evolution of STEMI management from the recent focus on complete revascularization toward plaque-guided strategies, including the role of invasive and non-invasive imaging for vulnerable plaque assessment, the emerging evidence supporting preventive PCI of high-risk non-culprit lesions, and ongoing clinical trials shaping this field. Collectively, these advances provide a framework for investigating precision revascularization strategies that integrate plaque morphology, coronary physiology, multimodality imaging, and patient-level cardiovascular risk. Ongoing randomized trials are essential to determine whether plaque-guided preventive intervention improves clinically meaningful outcomes beyond contemporary approaches to revascularization and optimal medical therapy.

articles.title: Longitudinal evolution of O-(2-[18F]-fluoroethyl)-L-tyrosine PET metrics in serial imaging during glioblastoma progression.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Most studies evaluating O-(2-[18F]-fluoroethyl)-L-tyrosine (FET) PET for glioblastoma progression rely on single-scan assessments, leaving diagnostic uncertainties in cases with borderline tracer uptake. We evaluated metabolic activity evolution during the transition of glioblastoma progression using serial FET PET to determine whether longitudinal parameter changes improve diagnostic certainty.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Between 2016 and 2026, 182 patients with glioblastoma undergoing 690 dynamic FET PET scans (median, 3; range, 2-12) were retrospectively evaluated. Eligible cases required documented progressive disease according to RANO 2.0 criteria and serial FET PET at least 2 time points (at suspected progression and within a 6-month prior window). Static PET parameters, ie tumor-to-brain ratios (TBRmean, TBRmax) and metabolic tumor volume (MTV), and their longitudinal changes were evaluated according to PET RANO 1.0 criteria, alongside additional dynamic PET parameters (time-to-peak). Single-scan metrics and serial changes were compared in cases with borderline uptake.

RESULTS: Ninety patients with 102 confirmed progression events met all selection criteria (median interscan interval, 2.7 months). At progression, TBRmean, TBRmax, and MTV increased significantly (P < .001). Median percentage increases were modest for TBRmean (+4%) and TBRmax (+17%), whereas MTV exhibited a substantial expansion (+182%). In cases with borderline uptake, applying a longitudinal MTV increase criterion of ≥40% per PET RANO 1.0 substantially improved progression detection to up to 89%, yielding a 14% higher diagnostic detection rate compared to single-scan thresholds.

CONCLUSIONS: In glioblastomas with documented RANO 2.0 progression, integrating longitudinal MTV changes markedly improves diagnostic certainty over single-scan uptake metrics, particularly in challenging cases with borderline uptake.

articles.title: Correction to "Classification of glucose profile in Japanese patients with type 1 diabetes and its association with complications".
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

articles.title: Inverse association between serum osteocalcin and pericardial adipose tissue in Koreans: cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osteocalcin (OC), a bone matrix protein of osteoblastic origin, is thought to play a role in systemic metabolic function. However, the relationship between serum OC levels and pericardial adipose tissue (PAT) volume remains unclear.

METHODS: Using a cross-sectional design, 438 participants (88 females, 350 males) who underwent cardiac CT imaging were enrolled. Simple and partial correlation analyses were performed. OC levels were divided into tertile groups to assess their relationship with PAT, adjusting for age, sex, smoking, hypertension and type 2 diabetes. Linear and logistic regression models were also applied.

RESULTS: The mean participant age was 55.7 years. The average serum OC level was 15.9 ng/mL, and the mean PAT volume was 127.6 cm3. OC level and PAT volume showed an inverse correlation that was significant in both unadjusted (r=-0.158, P=0.001) and covariate-adjusted (r=-0.106, P=0.032) analyses. Inter-tertile PAT differences remained significant after stratification (P<0.05). In multivariate regression analysis, the inverse association remained statistically significant after adjustment for age, sex and smoking (P=0.019), but not after additional adjustment for body mass index (P=0.656). After adjustment, relative to the highest OC tertile, the odds ratios for being classified into the highest PAT tertile were 2.73 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.43-5.21) for the lowest and 2.99 (95% CI, 1.59-5.66) for the middle OC tertile.

CONCLUSION: Serum OC level was inversely associated with PAT volume; however, this association was attenuated after adjusting for adiposity-related variables, suggesting that shared metabolic or body composition factors may partly account for the observed relationship.

articles.title: Substrate Adhesion Method (SAM): Ultracentrifugation-Free Electron Microscopy of Influenza A virus (H3N2) Morphology and Disinfectant-Induced Changes.
articles.abstract: Electron microscopy (EM) is crucial for resolving viral ultrastructure, but conventional ultracentrifugation used for sample concentration can induce structural artifacts, particularly in enveloped viruses like influenza A virus. To overcome this, we developed and validated the Substrate Adhesion Method (SAM). This simple technique bypasses ultracentrifugation by utilizing the natural adhesion of influenza A virus (H3N2) to cell culture substrates during infection, enabling effective multimodal EM (SEM, TEM, STEM) visualization of progeny virus particles without prior concentration. SAM-enabled SEM revealed a distinct topographical "wavy" pattern on H3N2 virus particle surfaces, which is interpreted as a preparation-induced artifact arising from critical point drying (CPD) shrinkage. Ultra-high-voltage electron tomography confirmed that spike-containing envelope structures contribute to this observed morphology. Thus, SAM-facilitated SEM offers wide-field morphological insights complementing TEM's high-resolution internal structural analysis. Virus particle adhesion to the substrate via SAM was significantly enhanced by infected cells, suggesting a key role for cell-associated factors in this immobilization. Furthermore, SAM's compatibility with negative staining allowed direct visualization of ethanol-induced H3N2 virus inactivation via distinct envelope deformations such as disruption and roughening. This feature makes SAM a valuable tool for direct morphological assessment of disinfectant efficacy, complementing infectivity assays. In conclusion, SAM provides a simple, rapid, artifact-mitigating approach for detailed morphological studies of H3N2 virus and antiviral agent evaluation, opening new perspectives in virological EM.

articles.title: CT-based Epicardial Adipose Tissue Change as a Promising Biomarker of Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease Progression: A Longitudinal Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between CT-based longitudinal changes in epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) volume and obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) progression.

METHODS: We included 583 suspected CAD patients (median age, 60 years; 348 men) who underwent coronary CT angiography (CCTA) between June 2010 and June 2017, and received follow-up CCTA at an interval of ≥ 2 years (median interval, 3.33 years; IQR, 2.67 to 4.33 years). 107 patients progressed to obstructive CAD. EAT volume and coronary artery calcium score (CACS) were measured on non-contrast CCTA. Annualised EAT volume change was calculated as the difference between follow-up and baseline scans divided by the follow-up duration. Obstructive CAD progression was defined as new-onset ≥50% stenosis in initially non-obstructive patients. The association of EAT with obstructive CAD progression was evaluated by univariate and multivariate logistic regression.

RESULTS: Annualised EAT volume change was 3.47 cm³ in the obstructive progression group and 2.07 cm³ in the no obstructive progression group (P = 0.006). In univariate analysis, only age, CACS, baseline largest luminal diameter stenosis and annualised EAT volume change were significantly associated with obstructive CAD progression. Annualised EAT volume change remained independently associated with obstructive CAD progression (adjusted OR = 1.06, P = 0.007) after adjustment for variables significant in univariate analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Annualised EAT volume change was independently associated with obstructive CAD progression.

ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: Annualised EAT volume change may represent a CT-based imaging marker of obstructive CAD progression.

articles.title: Current Diabetes Technologies and Everyday School Life of Children and Adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes: Did We Do Our Homework?
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Automated insulin delivery (AID) systems have been rapidly adopted among children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes (T1D) in Germany. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of AID use on glycemic control, school participation, and parental burden.

METHODS: A cross-sectional multicenter survey was conducted among parents of school-aged children (6-16 years). Participants completed questionnaires covering demographic and clinical characteristics, diabetes support during school hours, participation in school activities, and school-related disruptions (calls, pick-ups).

RESULTS: A total of 775 parents participated (77.6% mothers); children attended primary (n = 203), secondary (n = 554) and special needs schools (n = 13). Among primary school children, 76% received external support during school hours. Although secondary school students were more likely to participate in school activities, 10%-28% of them and 24%-61% of primary school students were still unable to participate in certain activities. HbA1c levels were lower among AID users; however, AID use did not improve participation and was associated with more frequent school phone calls (p = .042) and early pick-ups (p < .001). Approximately one-third of parents reduced their working hours immediately following their child's diabetes diagnosis.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite a well-resourced healthcare system, schools lack integrated standardized diabetes support. Although AID use improved glycemic control, this did not translate into better school participation and was associated with increased school-related contacts, suggesting a shift in burden to parents, possibly due to insufficient support for AID use in school. Structured, integrated support adapted to new diabetes technologies is needed.

articles.title: Defining and managing NF1-related peripheral nerve sheath tumors at risk for malignant transformation: Consensus from the Atypical Neurofibroma Symposium.
authors: Symposium on Atypical Neurofibroma: State of the Science Members
articles.abstract: People with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) are at risk for developing peripheral nerve sheath tumors (PNSTs) ranging from benign neurofibromas to high-grade sarcomas. PNSTs known as atypical neurofibromas are at increased risk for malignant transformation. In 2017 the term ANNUBP (atypical neurofibromatous neoplasm of uncertain biologic potential) was proposed for PNSTs at increased risk for malignant transformation based on histopathologic features. Subsequently it was recognized that PNSTs not meeting ANNUBP criteria could still have concerning clinical, imaging and molecular features. A State of the Science conference addressed how to define these pre-cancerous PNSTs and reached consensus regarding clinical management and priority areas of research. Key recommendations from this symposium include: (1) using a combination of histologic, molecular and imaging features to define pre-malignant "at-risk" PNST; (2) recognizing that people with NF1 may be divided into "higher-risk" and "average-risk" for MPNST based on features such as their germline NF1 variant, internal tumor burden and history of malignancy or radiotherapy and; (3) the need to validate consensus screening and surveillance strategies based on personal and tumor-related risk factors. These recommendations will advance the ability to standardize care, and potentially fuel research that enables early diagnosis, prevention of malignant transformation and improved outcomes.

articles.title: Comparison of JAK inhibitors and biologics with respect to pain reduction in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: data from the KOBIO registry.
articles.journal: The Korean journal of internal medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: To compare the pain-reducing efficacy of Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKis) and biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (bDMARDs) in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA).

METHODS: Patients with RA enrolled in the Korean College of Rheumatology Biologics and Targeted Therapy (KOBIO) registry were grouped according to use of JAKis, TNFis, and non-TNFi bDMARDs. The primary outcome was to compare the changes in pain on a numeric rating scale (NRS, range 0-10) between enrolment and first follow-up. Logistic regression analysis was performed to identify the factors associated with a low pain NRS score (< 2) and retention at the 1-year follow-up.

RESULTS: The analysis included 2,415 patients with RA in the JAKis (n = 422), TNFis (n = 1,148), and non-TNFi bDMARDs groups (n = 845). The change in pain NRS was significantly greater in the JAKis group than in the TNFis group (2.8 ± 2.5 vs. 2.3 ± 2.9, respectively; p < 0.01). The adjusted mean additional pain reduction was significantly greater in the JAKis than in the TNFis group (-0.42, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.73 to -0.10). The adjusted odds ratio (OR) for achieving a pain NRS score < 2 with initial drug retention at 1 year follow-up was significantly lower in the TNFis (OR = 0.515; 95% CI: 0.406-0.652) and non-TNFi bDMARDs (OR = 0.586; 95% CI: 0.458-0.751) groups than in the JAKis group.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients who achieved treatment response and remained on therapy, JAKis were associated with greater improvement in pain control than TNFis.

articles.title: Differential characteristics of takotsubo cardiomyopathy according to clinical context.
articles.journal: The Korean journal of internal medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (TC) occurs in diverse clinical settings and generally has a favorable prognosis; however, little is known about its characteristics and outcomes across different contexts. We evaluated the clinical features and in-hospital mortality of TC according to clinical setting.

METHODS: A total of 153 patients diagnosed with TC from 2008 to 2020 were included. Patients were classified as having primary TC (presenting as the primary reason for care, n = 31) or secondary TC (n = 122), which was further subdivided into infection (n = 58), medical/surgical illness (n = 38), and stroke (n = 26).

RESULTS: Prior cerebrovascular accident was more frequent in the infection and stroke groups. Length of hospital stay, intenincludsive care unit stay, and ventilator use were greatest in the stroke group, whereas inotropic agent use was most frequent in the infection group. N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels differed across groups, with the highest levels observed in the primary form (p = 0.025). Echocardiographic parameters were generally comparable, although left atrial diameter was larger in the primary form and smaller in the stroke group. Overall in-hospital mortality was 13.1% and occurred exclusively in secondary TC. Mortality was highest in the infection group, but the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.053). In multivariate regression analysis, age, bacteremia, and follow-up right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP) were independently associated with in-hospital mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: The prognosis of primary form of TC was excellent, while the patients with infection had higher tendency of in-hospital death. Age, bacteremia, and follow-up RVSP were independent predictors of in-hospital death in TC patients.

articles.title: Image clues to a gynecologic procedure-triggered pheochromocytoma crisis presenting as stress cardiomyopathy with cardiogenic shock.
articles.journal: The Korean journal of internal medicine

articles.title: Machine learning-based experimental access to photon-by-photon arrival times in scintillation detectors.
articles.abstract: Objective. Scintillation detectors with excellent timing resolution enable more precise localization of radiation sources in positron emission tomography, leading to substantial improvements in diagnostic capability for diseases such as cancer and dementia. At the timing precision required for such applications at the picosecond scale, detector performance is governed by the dynamics of scintillation photons generated within the detector and their subsequent detection processes. However, detector signals have conventionally been treated only as collective responses of many photons due to structural constraints inherent to photodetectors. In this study, we overcome this fundamental limitation using deep learning framework.Approach. The proposed method estimates photon-by-photon arrival times directly from detector waveforms without requiring any modification to the detector structure; the method operates on an event-by-event basis without ground-truth labels by integrating an unsupervised learning framework with a physically informed detector-response model.Main results. Through comprehensive validation combining Monte Carlo simulation and experimental measurements across various detector configurations, we experimentally demonstrate improved timing resolution, visualized depth-of-interaction-dependent photon transport, and classified Cherenkov and scintillation photons based on the estimated photon-level timing information using a unified deep learning-based framework.Significance. These results provide experimental access to photon dynamics, bridging the gap between theoretical modeling and experimental observation, and they open a new data-driven pathway for discovery in detector physics and optimization.

articles.title: Neuropeptide signaling regulates mitochondrial UPR activity and extended lifespan resulting from methionine restriction.
articles.abstract: Mild disruptions to mitochondrial function can lead to the activation of an adaptive program that extends animal lifespan. The mitochondrial unfolded protein response (UPRmt) is associated with such conditions that prolong lifespan. We previously discovered that methionine restriction, resulting from the genetic loss of methionine synthase in C. elegans, activated the UPRmt and extended lifespan. Here, we demonstrate that methionine restriction activates the UPRmt and delays aging within the intestine of C. elegans. Using a forward genetics approach, we identified a role for PKC-1, the C. elegans ortholog of protein kinase C epsilon/eta (PKC???), in regulating methionine restriction-associated UPRmt (MetR-UPRmt). PKC-1 activity was required for the increased lifespan and host resistance during infection that was associated with methionine restriction. Strikingly, PKC-1 was not required for UPRmt activation resulting from dysfunctional oxidative phosphorylation, mitochondrial protein translation, or mitochondrial protein import. We find that secretion of neuropeptides from dense-core vesicles is required for MetR-UPRmt activity, consistent with the role of PKC-1 in regulating this form of neurotransmission. We also identify specific neuropeptides (INS-27, INS-34, and INS-35) that positively regulate MetR-UPRmt activity and associated lifespan extension. Mechanistically, we find that neuropeptide signaling regulates MetR-UPRmt activity in part by altering mitochondrial network dynamics. Together, our data suggest a model in which neuropeptide signaling preferentially regulates UPRmt activity and lifespan extension induced by intestinal methionine restriction, but not by other forms of mitochondrial dysfunction.

articles.title: Incidental Findings in Asymptomatic Healthy Individuals Screened with Total-Body Ultra-Low-Dose 18F-FDG-PET/Low-Dose CT.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the prevalence and clinical significance of incidental findings (IF) detected by Total-body 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography (FDG-PET/CT) in a genuinely asymptomatic cohort of blood donors.

METHODS: 117 healthy, asymptomatic blood donors underwent ultra-low-dose FDG-PET/low-dose CT. The primary objective was to create an atlas of glucose metabolism in healthy individuals. A secondary objective was to assess the frequency and nature of IF, informing future considerations of the clinical value of potential screening programs. Here we report on IF.

RESULTS: IF were detected in 64 participants (55%), with 51 (44%) presenting clinically insignificant IF and 13 (11%) clinically significant IF. Common insignificant IF included benign or inflammatory metabolic activity in the esophagus or lung parenchyma (n = 19), metabolically active reactive lymph nodes (n = 14), and degenerative skeletal changes (n = 13). Clinically significant IF comprised pathologically metabolically active cysts and polyps (n = 8), significantly enlarged vessels (n = 1), suspected malignant tumors (n = 1), large lipomas (n = 1), sarcoidosis (n = 1), and liver steatosis (n = 1).

CONCLUSIONS: This is the first study to systematically investigate incidental findings in an asymptomatic cohort using ultra-low-dose total-body FDG-PET/CT. Even in this highly selected population, numerous IFs were revealed, underscoring the need for risk-stratified, data-driven screening strategies integrating genetic biomarkers identifying individuals who will truly benefit.

ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This first study of ultra-low-dose total-body FDG-PET/CT in asymptomatic donors found frequent incidental findings (55%, 11% clinically significant), establishing lower-bound estimates and supporting risk-stratified screening approaches.

articles.title: ICU utilization, capacity strain, and mortality before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic.
articles.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: The COVID-19 pandemic created a unique instance of hospital capacity strain including deviations in ICU bed utilization.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate trends in ICU utilization among patients with common critical illness syndromes before, during, and after the pandemic, and across degrees of hospital capacity strain.

METHODS: At 26 U.S. hospitals across two health systems, 2013-2024, we performed a retrospective cohort study among high-acuity patients with sepsis and/or acute respiratory failure (ARF) who did not require mechanical ventilation or vasopressor support in the emergency department. We modeled ICU admission rates and hospital mortality across eras and associations between validated hospital strain indices and ICU admission.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: ICU admission rates decreased markedly from the pre-pandemic to the pandemic era and were sustained in the post-pandemic era: sepsis (n = 136,153) 24% (24-24%) pre-pandemic, 16% (15-16%) pandemic, and 14% (14-14%) post-pandemic; ARF (n = 63,290) 36% (35-36%) pre-pandemic, 25% (25-26%) pandemic, and 23% (22-24%) post-pandemic; all p < 0.001. Increasing hospital capacity strain was associated with reduced predicted probability of ICU admission (sepsis: 29% [29-30%] ICU admission at lowest strain to 9% [8-9%] at highest strain; ARF: 51% [49-52%] at lowest strain to 15% [14-16%] at highest strain; all p < 0.001). Compared to the pre-pandemic era, in the post-pandemic era patients with sepsis (11% [11-11%] vs. 14% [13-14%]) and ARF (12% [11-12%] vs. 14% [14-15%]) had reduced mortality (both p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Among high acuity patients with sepsis and ARF who did not require initial life support, ICU admission rates decreased during and after the pandemic.

articles.title: Statin-Ezetimibe Therapy and Incident Myocardial Infarction Across Modified Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Risk Groups: A Nationwide Target Trial Emulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome integrates metabolic risk, kidney dysfunction, and cardiovascular disease. Whether statin-ezetimibe combination therapy is associated with lower subsequent myocardial infarction risk than statin monotherapy among patients across modified cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic risk groups remains uncertain.

METHODS: Using the Korean National Health Insurance Service database, we emulated separate two-arm landmark target trials within modified early and late cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic risk groups. Adults aged 30-74 years with dyslipidemia who received prescriptions covering a total of 180 days with statin monotherapy or a fixed-dose statin-ezetimibe combination were eligible. Treatment was assigned at the 180-day landmark. Stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting and cause-specific Cox regression were used to calculate hazard ratio (HR) and 95% confidence interval (CI), with death treated as a competing event for cumulative incidence estimation.

RESULTS: Among 309,371 treated participants, 239,954 had modified early risk and 69,417 had modified late risk. Compared with statin monotherapy, statin-ezetimibe therapy was associated with lower myocardial infarction risk after weighting in both early-risk participants (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.81-0.95) and late-risk participants (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.79-0.98). 10-year weighted cumulative incidence was 1.97% versus 2.23% in the early-risk group and 3.52% versus 3.94% in the late-risk group. In same-intensity comparisons, the association was most evident with moderate-intensity therapy, particularly in the early CKM group (HR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.79-0.95).

CONCLUSION: Among adults with dyslipidemia who received prescriptions covering a total of 180 days, statin-ezetimibe combination therapy was associated with a lower subsequent risk of myocardial infarction than statin monotherapy across modified CKM risk groups. The association was most evident in moderate-intensity comparisons.

articles.title: Creatinine-Cystatin C eGFR Discordance Identifies Long-Term Cardiorenal Risk in Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Discordance between creatinine- and cystatin C-based estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is common and has been associated with adverse outcomes in population-based cohorts. However, its relevance in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study including 808 patients with ACS admitted to the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit of Marqués de Valdecilla University Hospital (Santander, Spain) between 1 January, 2012 and 31 December, 2015, for whom measurements of creatinine and cystatin C at admission were available. Discordance between creatinine- and cystatin C-based eGFR was assessed using continuous indices (eGFR difference and ratio) and categorical definitions based on a threshold of 15 mL/min/1.73m². Associations with all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and kidney function decline were evaluated using Cox regression models adjusted for cardiovascular risk factors and creatinine-cystatin C eGFR.

RESULTS: Creatinine-cystatin C eGFR discordance was present in 44.2% of patients. Over a median follow-up of 8.4 years, lower cystatin C-based relative to creatinine-based eGFR was associated with higher risks of all-cause mortality, MACE, and kidney function decline. These associations persisted among patients with preserved creatinine-based kidney function. In adjusted models, each 10 mL/min/1.73 m² increase in eGFR difference, indicating higher eGFRcys relative to eGFRcr, was associated with lower risks of mortality (Hazard Ratio [HR] 0.88, 95% Confidence Interval [CI] 0.80-0.96) and kidney function decline (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.71-0.91), with a similar trend for MACE (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.83-1.00).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients hospitalised with ACS, eGFR discordance reflecting lower cystatin C-based eGFR than creatinine-based eGFR is associated with adverse long-term cardiorenal outcomes, even among patients with preserved creatinine-based kidney function.

articles.title: Periodontitis as a Modifiable Risk Factor for Dementia: Mechanistic Pathways Linking Oral Inflammation to Neurodegeneration.
articles.journal: The Canadian journal of neurological sciences. Le journal canadien des sciences neurologiques
articles.abstract: Emerging evidence increasingly implicates chronic periodontal disease as a contributor to age-related cognitive decline and dementia, including Alzheimer's disease (AD). Periodontitis is defined by persistent oral microbial dysbiosis, ulcerated gingival epithelium, repeated bacteremia and sustained systemic inflammatory signaling - factors that plausibly influence neuroimmune pathways and cerebrovascular integrity. This review synthesizes findings from epidemiological studies, systematic reviews, mechanistic analyses and experimental models to examine the biological links between oral inflammation and neurodegeneration. Collectively, the literature suggests a stepwise oral-brain axis: first gingival inflammation promotes local and systemic pro-inflammatory cytokine release, second repeated bacteremia allows oral pathogens and microbial byproducts to enter circulation, third these signals and agents access and compromise the blood-brain barrier, then fourth microglia in the brain become primed and hyper-reactive and at last enhanced neuroinflammation accelerates amyloid-β and tau pathology. Although causal inference remains limited by the predominance of observational data, emerging intervention studies and mechanistic evidence suggest that periodontal health is a potentially modifiable factor in dementia prevention strategies.

articles.title: Liver radiomics on routine cardiac CT identifies hepatic stress states that predict heart failure.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Heart failure (HF) prevention remains limited because early multisystem cardiometabolic dysfunction is not captured by conventional risk tools. We evaluated whether liver radiomic phenotypes derived opportunistically from coronary artery calcium computed tomography (CAC-CT) identify imaging-defined hepatic stress states associated with incident HF.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We analysed 59 237 individuals undergoing CAC-CT (CLARIFY: 46 028; Houston Methodist: 13 209). Liver regions were segmented and radiomic features extracted to derive a Liver Radiomics Score (LRS). The model was trained in a CLARIFY derivation cohort (Dtr, n = 9205), validated in a hold-out cohort (Dts, n = 36 823), and externally evaluated in Houston Methodist (Dext, n = 13 209). The mean follow-up was 1411 days (SD 760.1) in the pooled Dtr and Dts cohorts (1144 HF events) and 470 days (SD 596) in Dext (212 HF events). Continuous LRS was associated with incident HF [Dts: hazard ratio (HR) 1.63, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.52-1.74; P < 0.001; Dext: HR 1.04, 95% CI 1.01-1.07; P = 0.004] and remained significant after multivariable adjustment in Dts. Increasing LRS quartiles showed progressively adverse hepatic, haemodynamic, and cardiometabolic profiles and higher HF risk. Among 17 806 Dts participants with PREVENT data, adding LRS modestly improved discrimination across CAC- and PREVENT-based models (P < 0.001) and improved reclassification metrics (7-year net reclassification improvement up to 0.25; including integrated discrimination improvement up to 0.015). High LRS identified elevated risk in low-risk groups: among participants with CAC=0, high LRS conferred ∼2.5-fold higher 5-year HF incidence, and ∼2.9-fold in PREVENT-low individuals.

CONCLUSION: In this large multicentre cohort, liver radiomics from CAC-CT captured hepatic stress states linked to HF risk and modestly improved risk stratification beyond CAC and PREVENT scores.

articles.title: Radiomic consultation of the hepatic stress oracle predicts heart failure.
Temporal stability of an electronic health record-driven machine learning model predicting type 2 diabetes among patients with mental illness.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We previously trained and tested a machine learning model to predict incident type 2 diabetes (T2D) in patients with mental illness using electronic health record (EHR) data from routine clinical practice. This hyperparameter-tuned XGBoost model - based on information on sex, age and mean HbA1c within the past two years - predicts whether a patient will meet criteria for T2D in the two years following each contact to psychiatric services. The performance of such a model may drift over time due to changes in standards of care, baseline risk, registration procedures, etc. Therefore, we set out to examine its temporal stability.

METHODS: In the present study, we fitted the model described above on EHR data from January 1, 2013 to December 31, 2017, and examined its stability in predicting T2D two years into the future for patients with contacts in 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, and 2023, respectively. Performance was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC).

RESULTS: The model showed good discriminative performance across all years (AUROC for 2018 = 0.84, 2019 = 0.83, 2020 = 0.87, 2021 = 0.80, 2022 = 0.84, 2023 = 0.80), with a linear model estimating a decrease in AUROC for T2D prediction of only 0.004 per year (95%CI: -0.024; 0.016). Secondary analyses suggested that models trained on recent data (past year) may achieve similar or better discrimination than models trained on longer historical periods.

CONCLUSIONS: The temporal stability of the T2D prediction model supports its potential for clinical implementation, facilitating early detection and tailored interventions, while highlighting the importance of continued evaluation.

articles.title: Pericarditis in COVID-19: a focus on the paediatric population.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: COVID-19, caused by SARS-CoV-2, is primarily a respiratory illness but may cause cardiovascular complications, including pericarditis. Pediatric SARS-CoV-2-associated pericarditis remains uncommon and likely underreported. This review summarizes the epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, diagnosis, management, and outcomes of pericarditis associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection in children.

METHODS: We narratively reviewed the available literature on SARS-CoV-2-associated pericarditis in the pediatric population, including isolated acute pericarditis, myopericarditis, pericardial effusion, cardiac tamponade, and pericardial involvement in multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C).

RESULTS: The true incidence of pediatric SARS-CoV-2-associated pericarditis remains unclear. Reported cases suggest that older children and adolescents are more commonly affected, typically presenting with chest pain, fever, dyspnea, or tachycardia, whereas younger children may exhibit nonspecific symptoms. Diagnosis relies on clinical criteria supported by electrocardiography, echocardiography, inflammatory markers, and cardiac biomarkers, with cardiac magnetic resonance imaging useful when myocardial involvement is suspected. Available evidence suggests a predominantly immune-mediated pathophysiology involving cytokine dysregulation and systemic inflammation, with limited evidence of direct viral invasion. Management is largely extrapolated from established pediatric pericarditis principles and adult data. Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and colchicine are first-line therapies, while corticosteroids or intravenous immunoglobulin may be considered in selected inflammatory or MIS-C-associated cases, and interleukin-1 blockade in refractory or recurrent disease. Most affected children recover, although severe pericardial effusion, tamponade, and recurrence have been reported.

CONCLUSION: Pediatric SARS-CoV-2-associated pericarditis encompasses a spectrum of clinical presentations and generally carries a favorable prognosis. Nevertheless, potentially serious complications emphasize the importance of early recognition, differentiation from myocarditis and MIS-C, and structured follow-up.

articles.title: Muscle Strength Trajectories According to Preoperative Temporary Mechanical Circulatory Support Use in Patients Undergoing Durable Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation.
Endovascular versus medical treatment in large-core stroke within 24 hours in Vietnam.
articles.journal: Journal of the Chinese Medical Association : JCMA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The efficacy and safety of endovascular treatment (EVT) in large ischemic core stroke remain understudied in developing countries.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter prospective cohort study in Vietnam from August 2023 to September 2024, screening consecutive cases of patients with large vessel occlusion treated within 24 hours. Patients with large ischemic core (ASPECTS ≤5) and large vessel occlusion within 24 hours were included. The primary outcome was independent ambulation, defined as an mRS score of 0-3, at 90 days. Secondary outcomes included ordinal mRS shift, successful reperfusion, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH), as defined by SITS-MOST, and the 90-day mortality rate. Propensity-score overlap weighting was performed to adjust for baseline imbalances.

RESULTS: Among 491 patients (36.9% women, median age 64 years), 403 (82.1%) underwent endovascular treatment (EVT), while 88 (17.9%) received best medical treatment (BMT) alone. After propensity score overlap weighting was estimated and applied, 385 EVT and 79 BMT patients were included in a balanced cohort. EVT was associated with improved functional outcome rate of mRS 0-3 (50.2% vs 26.8%, OR = 2.75, 95% CI = 1.42-5.33; p = 0.003), and a favorable shift in mRS score (3.00 [interquartile range (IQR), 2-5] vs 5.00 [IQR, 3-6], OR = 2.61, 95% CI = 1.49-4.58; p < 0.001). Successful reperfusion (mTICI 2b-3) was achieved in 93.7% of patients who underwent EVT. EVT was also associated with lower 90-day mortality (15.0% vs 38.2%, OR = 0.29, 95% CI = 0.15-0.56; p < 0.001). However, any intracranial hemorrhage was significantly more frequent in the EVT group (75.6% vs 37.3%, OR = 5.21, 95% CI = 2.51-10.82; p < 0.001). Notably, sICH occurred numerically more often with EVT (9.4%) than with BMT (5.1%), but this difference was not statistically significant (OR = 1.94, 95% CI = 0.41-9.13; p = 0.402).

CONCLUSION: EVT was associated with improved functional outcomes and reduced mortality compared to BMT in patients with large ischemic core stroke presenting within 24 hours of symptom onset, but had more intracranial hemorrhages. These findings support the potential benefit of EVT for patients with large ischemic cores in low- and middle-income countries; however, further validation is warranted given residual confounding by indication and incomplete follow-up imaging.

articles.title: The cath lab readiness gap: a national survey of technology-driven role shifts and training needs among nurses and radiographers in France.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Rapid technological change in cath labs is redistributing operational responsibilities towards nurses and radiographers. We aimed to quantify this redistribution, and to assess whether training, regulatory framing, and professional recognition have kept pace.

METHODS AND RESULTS: A national cross-sectional online survey was conducted in 2025 among 371 professionals in French catheterisation or electrophysiology laboratories (207 nurses, 60 radiographers, 78 cardiologists, 26 nurse managers). The primary outcome - perceived change in responsibilities - was analysed as binary (moderate or strong increase vs other responses) by logistic regression adjusted for profession, age, sex, and seniority. A strong increase in responsibilities of nurses and radiographers was reported by 54.6% of nurses and 48.3% of radiographers, versus 25.6% of cardiologists and 38.5% of nurse managers. Nurse/radiographer status was the strongest predictor (adjusted OR 6.11 [95% CI 2.86-13.66] vs cardiologists and nurse managers; p < 0.001). Training was predominantly apprenticeship-based (on-the-job mentoring, 66.3%); the perceived adequacy of nurses' and radiographers' initial training was rated 20/100 by nurses and 31.5/100 by radiographers, versus 40/100 by cardiologists (p < 0.001). About half of nurses and radiographers considered that procedures are often performed outside the formal regulatory scope (52% and 45%, respectively); 93% of nurses and 90% of radiographers demanded regulatory clarification.

CONCLUSION: Technology is redistributing responsibilities towards nurses and radiographers faster than training, regulatory framing, or recognition - a readiness gap perceived far more acutely by paramedical than medical professionals. Every technology deployment should integrate team readiness, regulatory clarification, and recognition commensurate with current practice.

articles.title: Global disparities in dengue, climate, and extreme weather research: a bibliometric analysis of alignment with disease burden and climate-driven vector suitability.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dengue is a climate-sensitive vector-borne disease that imposes a substantial public health burden in tropical and subtropical regions. Temperature, rainfall, and extreme weather can affect mosquito ecology, human exposure, and the environmental suitability for transmission. This study characterized the global research landscape of dengue and extreme weather and examined whether country-level research output corresponded to dengue burden and climate-driven vector suitability.

METHODS: The Web of Science Core Collection was searched on 22 May 2026. Publication trends, collaboration networks, journals, authors, co-cited references, citation bursts, keyword patterns, and thematic evolution were examined using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and the bibliometrix R package. Country-level publication output was linked to estimates from the Global Burden of Disease 2023 dataset, the socio-demographic index for 2021, and mean index-p values for 1990-2022. Associations between publication output and dengue burden were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation among countries classified as dengue-endemic.

RESULTS: A total of 290 publications from 2008 to 2026 met the eligibility criteria. Annual publication output increased overall and remained comparatively high after 2020. The United States contributed the largest number of publications, followed by China, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Brazil. The literature connected tropical medicine and infectious disease epidemiology with environmental health, climate science, vector ecology, modeling, and public health. Major themes included climate change, temperature, rainfall, the El Niño-Southern Oscillation, extreme weather, Aedes vectors, transmission modeling, risk prediction, and early warning. Among 80 countries classified as dengue-endemic, publication output was positively correlated with the age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) in 2023 (Spearman's ρ = 0.32, P = 0.004, n = 80) and the disability-adjusted life-year (DALY) rate in 2023 (ρ = 0.36, P < 0.001, n = 80). In contrast, its association with the estimated annual percentage change (EAPC) in ASIR from 1990 to 2023 was not statistically significant (ρ = 0.20, P = 0.070, n = 80). Several dengue-endemic countries with comparatively high disease burden or long-term climate-driven vector suitability had no eligible Web of Science-indexed publications in the present dataset.

CONCLUSIONS: Research on dengue and extreme weather has expanded, and publication output showed modest positive associations with contemporary dengue burden among dengue-endemic countries. However, research output was not significantly associated with the long-term trend in dengue incidence, and substantial geographic disparities remained. The separate assessment of burden, research output, and climate-driven vector suitability identified geographic areas that may warrant closer consideration when research capacity, surveillance support, and equitable international partnerships are developed.

articles.title: The occult hypoperfusion index: a bedside formula to identify undetected critical illness.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prehospital modified Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (mSOFA) score identifies patients with organ dysfunction but cannot detect normotensive occult hypoperfusion. To characterize the physiological correlation structure of mSOFA misclassification groups and to derive, internally validate and externally validate a bedside Occult Hypoperfusion Index (OHI) targeting undetected critical illness in patients classified as low acuity by the mSOFA.

METHODS: Prospective multicenter cohort study. Consecutive adults with acute illness attended by three physician-led emergency medical services. Prehospital mSOFA score computed from five point-of-care variables (mean arterial pressure, Glasgow Coma Scale [GCS], SpO₂/FiO₂ ratio, creatinine, and lactate). Primary outcome was all-cause mortality within 48 h of the index event. The index was then applied without refitting to an independent prospective cohort from Graz, Austria.

RESULTS: Of 16,106 enrolled patients, 933 (5.8%) died within 48 h. Cross-tabulation of mSOFA threshold and mortality yielded 848 true positives (5.3%), 85 false negatives (FN, 0.5%), 2,136 false positives (13.3%), and 13,037 true negatives (80.9%). Correlation analysis revealed that the FN group was uniquely sparse, with a dominant lactate-GCS coupling of ρ=+0.616 (p<.001). This co-variation was formalized as OHI=lactate × (16 - GCS). Applied to the mSOFA < 5 subgroup (n = 13,122), the OHI achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.851 (95% CI, 0.816-0.885), outperforming lactate alone (0.755; DeLong p = .004) and GCS alone (0.630; DeLong p < .001). In the external cohort (n = 802; 67 deaths), the OHI at the pre-specified threshold achieved an area under the curve of 0.861 (95% CI, 0.699-0.990), with sensitivity 80.0% and specificity 74.8%, and showed no evidence of miscalibration.

CONCLUSIONS: In a large prospective prehospital cohort, a multiplicative index derived from correlation analysis of mSOFA misclassification identified patients who died within 48 h despite being classified as low acuity. These findings are hypothesis-generating: the index was derived in one health system and externally validated in another, but the external estimates rest on few events and prospective evaluation before clinical use remains necessary. Consistent discrimination across three geographically distinct EMS systems in a leave-one-region-out analysis supports, but does not establish, its generalisability; this has now been extended to an independent cohort from a different country.

articles.title: Not all days are equal after preterm prelabor rupture of membranes: a time-dependent analysis of adverse perinatal outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Preterm prelabor rupture of membranes (PPROM) is associated with significant perinatal morbidity and mortality. Clinical management is typically based on inpatient monitoring, although the optimal duration and the potential role of outpatient care remain unclear.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, all women with PPROM between 15 + 0 and < 37 + 0 weeks' gestation managed as inpatients at a tertiary center (07/2019-04/2024) were included. The primary outcome was a composite severe adverse perinatal outcome (SAPO), comprising fetal or neonatal death, neonatal sepsis, intrauterine inflammation or infection, and major obstetric complications. Time-dependent risk was analyzed using latency stratification and landmark analyses. Independent predictors were identified via multivariable logistic regression. Longitudinal clinical and laboratory changes in the five days before delivery were assessed, and predictive performance was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).

RESULTS: A total of 300 women were included, of whom 46 (15.3%) experienced SAPO. Lower gestational age at PPROM, non-cephalic presentation, and estimated fetal weight below the 10th percentile were independently associated with SAPO, while inflammatory markers at admission showed no statistically significant independent association. The highest adjusted odds of SAPO were observed in the 6-7-day latency group (adjusted OR 6.10, 95% CI 1.45-25.62), although this subgroup comprised only 11 pregnancies. No statistically significant increase was detected in the group with latency exceeding seven days. Longitudinal increases in C-reactive protein (CRP) and leukocyte levels preceded delivery in complicated cases, but predictive performance remained limited (AUC 0.59-0.61).
