CONCLUSION: These findings highlight the importance of gestational age, fetal condition, and dynamic selection during expectant management of PPROM. Prospective studies are needed to evaluate individualized monitoring strategies and the potential role of outpatient management in carefully selected patients.

articles.title: ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT reveals fibroblast activation beyond biochemical fibrosis scores in chronic liver disease.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the role of ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT in assessing fibroblast activity in patients with chronic liver disease (CLD). We studied FAPI liver uptake and its relationship with functional disease severity (Child-Pugh score) and biochemical fibrosis indices (APRI and FIB-4).

METHODS: This prospective study included 10 control subjects without liver disease and 33 patients with CLD across Child-Pugh classes A-C. Biochemical evaluation included liver function tests, APRI, and FIB-4 scores. Participants underwent ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT, and SUVmax, SUVmean, FAPI-avid liver volume (FLV), and total liver FAPI activity (TLFA) were quantified. Correlation and regression analyses were done between PET parameters, biochemical markers, and Child-Pugh classes. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis and effect size estimation. Discordance analysis was done for PET-derived fibroblast activity, Child-Pugh classes, and biochemical fibrosis indices.

RESULT: CLD patients demonstrated significantly raised PET-derived parameters and deranged biochemical markers compared to controls (p < 0.05). Biochemical markers worsened progressively across Child-Pugh classes (p < 0.05), whereas SUVmax showed a non-significant increasing trend. Compared with controls, Child-Pugh A patients had significantly higher SUVmax, FIB-4, and APRI indices with high discrimination (AUC = 1.00, 1.00, and 0.965, respectively). No significant association was noted between PET parameters, Child-Pugh class, or biochemical fibrosis indices. Only 17% of SUVmax variance was explained by biochemical parameters. Discordance analysis showed High SUVmax in 37.5% and 58.3% of patients with intermediate FIB-4 and mild-moderate APRI categories, respectively. All patients with advanced fibrosis had persistently raised FAPI uptake.

CONCLUSION: ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT shows significant fibroblast activation in early CLD with intrahepatic heterogeneity. It shows concordance with the severity of biochemical fibrosis indices at extremes. PET-derived fibroblast activity shows discordance with functional disease severity and intermediate-grade biochemical fibrosis. These findings suggest a complementary role for FAPI PET in characterizing FAP-associated stromal activity beyond conventional biochemical fibrosis indices in CLD.

articles.title: SGLT2 Inhibitors in Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: The Kidney and Heart Perspective.
articles.abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have become a cornerstone of cardio-kidney protection in type 2 diabetes, yet their role in type 1 diabetes remains incompletely defined. While randomized controlled trials in type 1 diabetes have consistently demonstrated improvements in glycemic control, body weight, and insulin requirements, they were not designed to assess cardiovascular or kidney outcomes. Consequently, current evidence for cardio-kidney protection in type 1 diabetes is derived largely from physiological studies, surrogate biomarkers, and observational data.Accumulating evidence however suggests potential kidney benefits in type 1 diabetes. Across clinical and real-world studies, SGLT2i has been associated with up to 40% reduction in albuminuria and attenuation of the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline. These observations are consistent with mechanistic studies demonstrating restoration of the tubuloglomerular feedback and reduction of the intraglomerular pressure as the principal kidney-protective mechanisms of SGLT2i. However, evidence for cardiovascular protection remains substantially more limited. Studies demonstrate improvements in several established cardiovascular risk factors, including reductions in body weight (up to 3.4 kg), systolic blood pressure (approximately 2-4 mmHg), and fasting glucose. Yet direct evidence for reductions of cardiovascular events, kidney failure, or mortality is currently unavailable.Despite these limitations, the potential for early kidney protection in type 1 diabetes is particularly attractive, given the long natural history of diabetic kidney disease and the opportunity for intervention before irreversible kidney damage occurs. However, the increased risk of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) remains the major obstacle to widespread use and regulatory approval of SGLT2i in this population. Careful patient selection, structured education, ketone body monitoring, and implementation of DKA risk-mitigation strategies are therefore essential when considering this therapy. Future studies incorporating dedicated cardio-kidney endpoints and advances such as continuous ketone body monitoring may help clarify the benefit-risk balance and determine whether SGLT2i can ultimately assume a broader role as adjunctive cardio-kidney protective therapy in type 1 diabetes.

articles.title: FGF13 attenuates myocardial infarction-induced cardiac injury by modulating oxidative stress and NF-κB signaling.
articles.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) is a major cause of heart failure characterized by cardiomyocyte loss, adverse remodeling, and oxidative stress, with limited effective therapeutic targets. Fibroblast growth factor 13 (FGF13), an intracellular FGF family member, has not been fully explored in MI. Integrated transcriptomic analyses, including single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing datasets, revealed that FGF13 is predominantly expressed in cardiomyocytes and is downregulated following MI. In an MI model with AAV-mediated FGF13 overexpression, FGF13 improved cardiac function, as evidenced by increased ejection fraction and fractional shortening, reduced ventricular dilation, and attenuated fibrosis and apoptosis in vivo. In vitro, hypoxia decreased FGF13 expression in a time-dependent manner, accompanied by increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) and activation of NF-κB signaling. FGF13 overexpression reduced ROS accumulation, suppressed p65 phosphorylation, and restored SOD2 expression. Moreover, TNF-α-induced NF-κB activation promoted oxidative stress, whereas FGF13 partially reversed these effects. Collectively, FGF13 alleviates MI-induced cardiac injury and adverse remodeling, accompanied by reduced oxidative stress and NF-κB activation, highlighting its potential role in the response to ischemic cardiac injury.

articles.title: Translating pathogen biology into diagnostic and management strategies for gummy stem blight in cucumber production.
articles.abstract: Gummy stem blight (GSB) is a major disease of cucurbits caused by Stagonosporopsis spp. and is increasingly problematic in intensive cucumber production systems, particularly where warm, humid environments favour infection, sporulation and rapid disease spread. GSB can infect vegetative and reproductive tissues and remain latent in fruit for several days before visible symptoms develop, creating a distinctive commercial challenge: disease may be difficult to detect before harvest yet cause significant post-harvest losses, reducing grower and retailer confidence. Compounding these problems, current diagnostic tools for detecting pre-symptomatic infection are often insufficiently validated for species specificity, sensitivity, turnaround time, cost, crude-sample compatibility and practical use by production staff. Many of these limitations reflect the relative lack of genomic resources for Stagonosporopsis. Therefore, this review integrates evidence from other pathosystems with current knowledge of Stagonosporopsis taxonomy, infection biology, epidemiology, diagnostics, fungicide resistance, effector biology and host resistance to identify pathways towards grower-ready tools. Specifically, we focus on how recent advances in genomics, paired with previously designed detection systems such as loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) and clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats/CRISPR-associated proteins (CRISPR/Cas), could be adapted for species-specific detection of the causal pathogen and, simultaneously, provide a regional profile of fungicide resistance. In parallel, we explore how a deeper functional genomic understanding of the disease, particularly of effector proteins expressed during the early stages of infection, could provide valuable insights into the dynamics of this host-pathogen interaction and support strategies to disrupt these interactions through novel fungistatic compounds and the development of disease-resistant cultivars. Together, these approaches could support a staged technology-development and adoption roadmap for more precise, rapid and sustainable GSB management in cucumber production.

articles.title: Microglial Metabolic Reprogramming Regulated by HIF-1α/HK2 Positive Feedback Inhibits Adult Hippocampal Neurogenesis in Diabetes-Associated Cognitive Dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Diabetes-associated cognitive dysfunction (DACD) is a significant complication with few effective treatments and unclear underlying mechanism. The aim of this study was to investigate how hyperglycemia disrupts adult hippocampal neurogenesis (AHN) through metabolic-immune interactions, seeking to identify potential treatment targets for DACD. DACD models were developed using db/db mice or streptozotocin-induced mice, and their cognitive function was assessed through behavioral tests. Next, we integrated multi-omics analyses (transcriptomic, single-cell, and lactylome profiling) with metabolic studies in BV2 cells exposed to diabetic conditions. Pharmacological modulators (3-BP, C646, TSA) were used to clarify the underlying mechanisms. The mice with DACD demonstrated cognitive deficits, impaired AHN, and activation of hippocampal microglia. Transcriptomic analysis revealed glycolysis as the primary dysregulated pathway. Mechanistically, hyperglycemia/AGEs induced glycolytic reprogramming and increased lactate levels, which promoted HIF-1α lactylation at lysine residues-a modification catalyzed by p300 and opposed by histone deacetylases. This posttranslational modification was associated with HIF-1α stabilisation and with enhanced transcriptional occupancy at the HK2 promoter. This established a self-amplifying feedback loop, perpetuating microglial activation and disrupting the blood-brain barrier via CXCL10 secretion, which led to CD8+ T-cell infiltration. Systemic administration of the glycolytic inhibitor 3-BP disrupted the pathogenic circuit, thereby normalizing metabolism, attenuating neuroinflammation, and restoring cognitive function. HIF-1α lactylation is associated with HIF-1α stabilisation, acting as a potential metabolic-epigenetic mechanism that links glycolytic flux to sustained microglial activation, neuroinflammation and impaired AHN in DACD. Pharmacological inhibition of this axis attenuated neuroinflammation and improved cognitive outcomes in our model, suggesting a candidate therapeutic strategy for DACD.

articles.title: Early Treadmill Exercise Promotes Neurological Recovery and Parkin-related Mitochondrial Quality Control After Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction constitutes a fundamental pathological mechanism contributing to neurological impairment in ischemic stroke (IS) patients. Parkin-related mitophagy is involved in mitochondrial quality control, but whether early post-ischemic exercise is associated with changes in Parkin-related mitochondrial quality control signaling remains incompletely understood. A middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model was established in male C57BL/6 mice, which were randomly assigned to a sham-operated control group (control), an MCAO model group (model), or an MCAO plus physical exercise group (PE) and subjected to treadmill training. Neurological function was evaluated via the Zea Longa score; cerebral blood flow was assessed via laser speckle contrast imaging; tissue pathology was examined via H&E/Nissl staining; and mitochondrial respiratory chain protein autophagy markers and Parkin pathway molecules were detected via Western blotting and immunofluorescence. Exercise significantly improved neurological deficits (P < 0.01), accompanied by attenuated histopathological alterations and improved perfusion recovery in the ischemic region (P < 0.05). At the molecular level, exercise increased NDUFB8 and ATP5A (P < 0.05), decreased HSP60 (P < 0.001), and was associated with restoration of mitochondrial energy metabolism-related profiles. Exercise was also associated with changes in autophagy-lysosomal markers, including increased total LC3 expression (P < 0.01), increased spatial correlation between LC3 and LAMP1 (P < 0.05), and reduced p62 (P < 0.01). Exercise training was associated with changes in Parkin-related mitophagy markers, consistent with enhanced mitochondrial quality control signaling, which may contribute to mitochondrial homeostasis following ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Resting sympathetic spectra as a window into orthostatic blood pressure dysregulation in hypertension.
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension

articles.title: Pulse wave analysis detected by a computerized method using the cardio-ankle vascular index in aortic stenosis.
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract: Although pulsus parvus et tardus is a classical physical finding in aortic stenosis (AS), objective quantitative assessment of pulse waveform morphology has been limited. We developed a novel computerized pulse waveform parameter, initial upstroke time (iUT), derived from cardio-ankle vascular index (CAVI) pulse waveforms to quantify the delay in the initial systolic upstroke. We analyzed 158 patients with mild or greater AS who underwent CAVI measurement and echocardiography. Associations of conventional upstroke time (UT) and iUT with echocardiographic measures of AS severity, including aortic valve area (AVA), peak aortic jet velocity (Vmax), and mean pressure gradient (MPG), were evaluated using multivariable regression analyses. Diagnostic performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic analysis. Both UT and iUT were significantly correlated with AVA and Vmax; however, iUT showed stronger correlations. In multivariable analyses including both parameters, iUT remained independently associated with AVA (standardized β = -0.488, P < 0.001) and Vmax (standardized β = 0.573, P < 0.001), whereas UT was not associated with Vmax and showed only a borderline association with AVA. Compared with UT, iUT also demonstrated superior diagnostic performance for identifying severe AS defined by Vmax ≥4.0 m/s (area under the curve [AUC], 0.843 vs. 0.678; P = 0.005) and MPG ≥ 40 mmHg (AUC, 0.795 vs. 0.637; P = 0.003), but not for AVA ≤ 1.0 cm². A novel computerized pulse waveform parameter reflecting the initial systolic upstroke was more strongly associated with echocardiographic measures of AS severity than conventional UT. Automated analysis of CAVI pulse waveforms may provide an objective adjunct for assessing AS without additional testing.

articles.title: Outcomes of heart transplantation with or without pre-transplant mechanical circulatory support: a single-center cohort study in Korea.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart transplantation is considered the definitive treatment for patients with end-stage heart failure (HF). Many patients with end-stage HF progress to cardiogenic shock or severe low cardiac output states while on the waiting list and require mechanical circulatory support (MCS) as a bridge to transplantation. The primary endpoint of this study was to assess overall survival after heart transplantation according to pre-transplant MCS use. The secondary outcomes included postoperative complications, intensive care utilization, and perioperative transfusion requirements.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included recipients of heart transplantation. A total of 100 consecutive patients were categorized into three groups according to pre-transplant MCS use (ECMO, LVAD, and non-MCS groups). Follow-up was censored on February 28, 2026.

RESULTS: The mortality was significantly higher and the overall survival was significantly lower in the ECMO group than in the non-MCS group. Overall survival significantly differed among the three groups (log-rank P = 0.001), driven mainly by worse survival in the ECMO group than in the non-MCS group, whereas survival did not significantly differ between the ECMO and LVAD groups.

CONCLUSIONS: The ECMO group showed a significantly worse survival than the non-MCS group, whereas survival did not significantly differ between the ECMO and LVAD groups, which was likely attributed to the small sample size of the LVAD group. Postoperative continuous renal replacement therapy and other markers of organ dysfunction were more frequent in the ECMO group and likely reflected the greater severity of illness in these patients rather than the independent risk factors.

articles.title: Beyond Croup: A Phenotype-Based Perspective on Parainfluenza Virus Types in Children.
articles.abstract: Human parainfluenza viruses (PIVs) caused an estimated 18.8 million acute lower respiratory infection episodes, 725 000 hospitalizations, and 34 400 deaths among children under 5 in 2018, ranking second only to respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Despite this burden, clinical attention has historically focused on croup, leading to the common perception that parainfluenza is a single disease entity. However, the 4 types differ substantially in taxonomy, tropism, clinical syndrome, and severity. PIV-1, the most common cause of croup, drives biennial epidemics in toddlers, whereas PIV-2 is less frequent but can cause severe disease, particularly in children with underlying conditions. PIV-3 predominates in young infants, causing bronchiolitis and pneumonia clinically like RSV infection, reflecting its early postnatal susceptibility, which may relate to earlier and more frequent viral exposure. PIV-4, historically underrecognized due to culture limitations, usually does not cause croup but is linked to lower respiratory tract disease, hypoxemia, and occasional neurologic complications. PIV infections are most severe in infants, immunocompromised children, and those in low-resource settings. Seasonal patterns vary by type and geography. Advances in multiplex molecular diagnostics now allow rapid type-specific detection, improving clinical interpretation and management. No vaccine or antiviral is licensed. Emerging therapeutics include sialidase-based antivirals with Food and Drug Administration Breakthrough designation; monoclonal antibodies capable of cross-neutralizing PIV-1, PIV-3, RSV, and human metapneumovirus; and messenger RNA vaccines showing early immunogenicity in children. Recognizing the distinct epidemiology, clinical features, and immune responses of each type is critical for informed pediatric care and the development of targeted preventive and therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Equity in general practice training in Aotearoa New Zealand: a national descriptive study of rurality and socioeconomic deprivation in GPEP1 placements (2016-2025).
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Rural Aotearoa New Zealand (NZ) experiences poorer health outcomes than urban areas, driven by the unequal distribution of the social determinants of health and persistent workforce shortages. Postgraduate rural exposure predicts future rural practice. Accordingly, the Royal New Zealand College of General Practitioners (RNZCGP) aims to place GP registrars in rural and high-needs practices.

AIM: This study aims to describe the distribution of first-year general practice (GPEP1) registrar placements by rurality and socioeconomic deprivation.

METHODS: De-identified data from 1896 registrars completing 3792 placements between 2016 and 2025 were analysed. Rurality and socioeconomic deprivation were classified using the Geographic Classification for Health (GCH) and the NZ Index of Deprivation (NZDep), respectively. Descriptive statistics evaluated placement distribution over time.

RESULTS: Overall, 17.4% of placements occurred in rural practices, and 74% of registrars completed no rural placement during GPEP1 training. Rural placement proportions remained stable over time and were slightly below the rural proportion of the total NZ population. In contrast, placements were concentrated in areas of high socioeconomic deprivation: approximately 58% occurred in NZDep deciles 8-10 areas, home to 30% of the population. Across the study period, 81.3% of registrars completed at least one placement in either a rural or high-deprivation practice.

DISCUSSION: Most registrars met programme objectives through placements in high-deprivation communities, although rural exposure remained below population share. Expanding rural training has the potential to improve equitable workforce distribution and access to primary care in underserved rural NZ, particularly as GPEP1 employment transitions to Health New Zealand from 2027.

articles.title: Long-term outcomes of biodegradable- versus durable-polymer drug-eluting stents in patients with advanced chronic kidney disease undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a 7-year retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Patients with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) or end-stage renal disease (ESRD) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) have high event rates, but long-term outcomes after contemporary drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation remain insufficiently defined. This study compared 7-year outcomes between biodegradable polymer DES (BP-DES) and durable polymer DES (DP-DES) in patients with stage 5 CKD or ESRD undergoing PCI.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients with stage 5 CKD or ESRD who underwent PCI with DES implantation between 2010 and 2019. The primary outcome was target lesion failure (TLF), defined as cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction, or clinically driven target lesion revascularization. The secondary outcome was all-cause mortality. Outcomes were compared using Cox regression, competing-risk analysis, and overlap-weighted propensity score analysis.

RESULTS: Among 417 patients, the mean age was 66.8 ± 10.4 years, 60.4% were male, and the median follow-up was 80 months. The 84-month cumulative incidence of TLF was 49% with BP-DES and 39% with DP-DES (Gray's test, P = 0.235). The observed 7-year mortality was 37.5 and 32.6%, respectively. DP-DES was not significantly associated with TLF [adjusted hazard ratio vs. BP-DES: 0.79, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.54-1.14; P = 0.207] or mortality (adjusted hazard ratio: 0.91, 95% CI: 0.63-1.33; P = 0.634). Older age and diabetes mellitus independently predicted mortality.

CONCLUSION: In patients with stage 5 CKD or ESRD undergoing PCI, 7-year TLF and mortality were frequent and did not differ significantly by DES polymer type.

articles.title: Single-cell profiling of the duodenum during chronic human norovirus infection.
articles.abstract: Human noroviruses are a major cause of diarrheal disease, yet their pathogenesis remains poorly defined. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing of duodenal biopsies and matched stem cell-derived enteroids from immunodeficient individuals with chronic norovirus infection. Norovirus RNA was detected primarily in enterocytes, enteroendocrine cells, and macrophages, with the highest proportion of viral RNA-positive cells observed among M2 macrophages, followed by late enterocytes. Despite this distribution, late enterocytes produced higher viral yields than differentiated M2 macrophages in vitro. Norovirus infection was associated with the up-regulation of MHC class I-related genes and IL15 in duodenal macrophages and late enterocytes, together with increased IFNG expression by CD8 T cells. Macrophages and late enterocytes up-regulated CXCL9 and CXCL10/11, respectively, consistent with CD8 and CD4 T cell recruitment to the duodenum. These findings show that noroviruses infect and persist across multiple permissive cell types during chronic infection, resulting in marked dysregulation of innate and adaptive immune responses that may drive pathogenesis.

articles.title: Neuromelanin-inspired metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks restore neuronal excitability in radiation-induced brain injury.
articles.abstract: Radiation-induced brain injury (RIBI) affects up to 30% of patients receiving cranial radiotherapy, representing an irreversible complication lacking effective therapies. Research advances are limited by poor blood-brain barrier drug penetration and overreliance on ex vivo pathology, which cannot resolve dynamic neuronal dysfunction. Inspired by neuromelanin, we fabricated metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks (MSMNs), combined with in vivo electrophysiology to investigate and mitigate radiation-triggered neural dysfunction. In 6-gray whole body-irradiated mice, MSMN normalized neuronal excitability and restored medium spiny neuron firing and striatal circuit activity, improving locomotor and anxiety-related behaviors. Besides central functional recovery, MSMN provides systemic radioprotection, ensuring full 30-day survival, protecting radiosensitive organs and facilitating hematopoietic recovery. This work identifies neuronal excitability as an underexplored therapeutic target for RIBI, establishing neuromelanin-mimetic selenomelanin nanonetworks as a bioinspired platform linking molecular radioprotection to circuit-level restoration for radiation-induced neurological injury.

articles.title: Mechanical forces enable human stem cell modeling of protein aggregation cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract: Inherited cardiomyopathies are the leading cause of heart failure in young adults, with limited therapeutic options. Desmin-related cardiomyopathy (DRM), caused by mutations to cytoskeletal proteins and their chaperones, exemplifies this challenge: Here, protein quality control is compromised, leading to toxic protein aggregates that destroy cardiomyocyte contractile machinery. One of the deadliest DRM mutations in the chaperone protein αB crystallin (CRYAB-R120G) lacks a genetically matched preclinical model: Mouse models require massive overexpression of mutant CRYAB, raising questions about physiological relevance. Here, we establish a human model of CRYAB-linked DRM, using induced pluripotent stem cells expressing CRYAB-R120G at near-endogenous levels. We show that three-dimensional mechanical loading, but not fatty acid-based metabolic maturation media, is essential for expressing Desmin, whose aggregation defines DRM. Using microengineered heart tissues, we found that contractile deficits are associated with impaired calcium handling, pointing to electromechanical uncoupling in DRM. Treatment with the Janus kinase 1 inhibitor itacitinib partially rescued contractility, providing a functional validation of this emerging therapeutic strategy.

articles.title: Patient-referenced and trajectory features from serial ECGs for haemodynamic monitoring: an in silico study with external feasibility analysis.
articles.abstract: Objective.Physiological measurements are read against population thresholds, although the within-person change that signals deterioration is smaller than the spread between people. We asked, in simulation, whether serial electrocardiograms read against a patient's own earlier recording carry information about haemodynamic state, and whether the trajectory of that change adds to its current value, in acute haemorrhage.Approach.A nine-dimensional circulatory state-space model generated 600 synthetic subjects in whom haemorrhage reached the waveform only through subject-specific couplings. Results were audited against elapsed time and heart rate, repeated under alternative observation models and with an unknown bleeding onset, and examined in an external feasibility analysis of 77 intraoperative recordings.Main results.Under the generative model, a personal reference raised state discrimination from 0.847 to 0.951 but helped event prediction less than the slope and curvature of the change, which raised five-minute decompensation discrimination from 0.876 to 0.953. Elapsed time, patient characteristics and heart rate reached 0.930 without any electrocardiogram; with onset randomised that shortcut disappeared and the waveform still added +0.084. This division of labour held in all 7 observation models and 24 sampled coupling sets. Intraoperatively, patient-referenced features discriminated concurrent hypotension better (0.683) than absolute features or heart rate, but added nothing distinguishable from zero to the recorded anaesthetic and ventilatory state.Significance.Under the stated assumptions, a personal reference estimates where a patient is and its trajectory where they are going. The external cohort provides preliminary evidence for the portability of the patient-referenced representation but is insufficient to establish clinical performance.

articles.title: Augmented reality paradigm and EA-DGCNN decoding algorithm for motor imagery in stroke patients.
articles.abstract: Objective.Stroke represents one of the leading causes of long-term motor dysfunction on a global scale. Existing motor imagery (MI) brain-computer interface (BCI) rehabilitation training systems face critical challenges of suboptimal patient engagement and limited electroencephalography (EEG) feature decoding capacity. To overcome these challenges, this study presents two primary original contributions: an independently designed wearable augmented reality (AR) MI training paradigm and a novel Euclidean alignment-based Dynamic Graph Convolutional Neural Network (EA-DGCNN) end-to-end decoding architecture.Approach.The immersive AR-MI paradigm heightens patient engagement and enhances MI performance. The EA-DGCNN model incorporates Euclidean alignment to minimize inter-subject variability in EEG distributions. The model extracts multi-dimensional spatiotemporal features via convolutional block attention, dynamic graph attention, and multi-scale convolutions, incorporating a Broad Learning System to achieve precise classification results.Main results.Experimental results demonstrate that the model achieves an accuracy of 85.13 ± 10.53% on the public BCI Competition IV 2a dataset. On a custom clinical dataset of 20 stroke patients, the AR paradigm yields a classification accuracy of 71.9 ± 8.9%, outperforming the 68.9 ± 8.0% of the traditional 2D paradigm. Furthermore, evaluations on the 64-channel PhysioNet benchmark demonstrate robust cross-subject transferability with a superior grand-average accuracy of 83.67 ± 8.52%. Neurophysiological feature analysis indicates that the AR paradigm elicits more pronounced event-related desynchronization and event-related synchronization responses. The t-SNE visualization demonstrates that the AR paradigm, coupled with the proposed model, produces highly discriminative feature clustering patterns.Significance.This study delivers a more effective paradigm and a robust decoding solution for clinical BCI rehabilitation.

articles.title: Beam-width-corrected DOI resolution measurement of dual-ended readout PET detectors.
articles.abstract: Objective.Dual-ended readout PET detectors provide depth-of-interaction (DOI) information for reducing parallax errors in high-resolution PET imaging. This study compared LYSO detectors with different inter-crystal reflectors and investigated the effect of irradiation beam width on DOI resolution measurements under electronic collimation.Approach.Two 28 × 28 LYSO arrays with 0.75 × 0.75 × 10 mm3crystals and BaSO4or E60 reflectors were characterized in terms of flood-map quality, energy resolution, and DOI resolution. Part of E60 detector (8 × 8 crystals) was further measured using three irradiation geometries with beam widths of 0.80 mm, 0.62 mm, and 0.46 mm. A beam-width correction was applied to the measured DOI resolution, and the effects of energy selection and empirical flood-map-based inter-crystal scattering (ICS) filtering were evaluated.Main results.The BaSO4detector showed better flood-map quality and energy resolution, whereas the E60 detector showed better DOI resolution. In the 400-650 keV energy window, the measured average DOI resolutions of entire 28 × 28 LYSO pixels with irradiation beam width of 1.00 mm were 1.92 and 1.75 mm for the BaSO4and E60 detectors, respectively. For the selected 8 × 8 crystal region of the E60 detector, the corrected DOI resolution by subtracting the irradiation beam width improved from 1.19 mm for all events to 1.01 mm after energy selection, and further to 0.86 mm after additional empirical flood-map-based ICS filtering.Significance.Irradiation beam width introduces a geometry-dependent contribution to DOI resolution measurements. Beam-width correction enables more consistent DOI characterization under different irradiation geometries.

articles.title: Photoacoustic technologies for exhaled-breath analysis: a systematic review of analytical performance and reporting quality.
articles.abstract: Photoacoustic breath sensing is usually assessed mainly on the basis of its detection limit, even though the review of the literature presented here shows that analytical sensitivity is no longer the only factor that affects the comparison of studies across different sources. This review, which is aligned with PRISMA and focuses on the instrument, comprised 131 independent study families providing a total of 209 study-analyte entries. When operating under conventional real-time conditions, the lowest detection limits recorded were 1 ppbv for ammonia, 2.1 ppbv for methane, 6 ppbv for ethylene, and 1.5 ppbv for carbon monoxide. Systems that used adsorbents or enrichment reported even lower values, such as 0.465 ppbv for nitric oxide and 0.0235 ppbv for acetone, but these measurements cover the entire detection cycle and were therefore kept apart from the uninterrupted real-time measurements. Reporting completeness was much less consistent: in 59 of the 212 entries the averaging time was given, humidity control was mentioned in 54, and end-tidal sampling was reported in only 9; just 48 entries satisfied the criterion of having comparable units with a stated time base. By applying a five-domain framework for assessing reporting quality with predefined scoring rules, 66% of the study families were rated as having a High concern regarding analytical validity and 65% had a High concern about sampling control, while only one family provided all of the environmental conditions at the measurement cell. The evidence also divided into three different operational regimes, each with its own figure of merit, so that a single ranking according to detection limit is not appropriate. We therefore suggest an eight-item minimum reporting set and identify normalized noise-equivalent absorption, Allan-deviation reporting, and inter-laboratory round-robin studies as the most practical priorities for improving comparability in future breath-sensing studies.

articles.title: A phase-calibrated combined electrical-sensory neuromodulation platform for short-term frontoparietal network modulation and cognitive fatigue resistance.
articles.abstract: Objective.Non-invasive combined electrical-sensory neuromodulation may be limited by cross-modal timing discrepancies arising from modality-specific conduction delays. This pilot study aimed to develop and evaluate an individualized delay-calibrated stimulation platform integrating transcranial alternating current stimulation with rhythmic visual and auditory inputs for modulating cognitive-fatigue-related frontoparietal network dynamics.Approach.We developed a microcontroller-based combined electrical-sensory stimulation platform and implemented a feedforward delay-compensation strategy based on individualized ERP latencies, including visualP1 and auditoryN1. The system was evaluated in a randomized, sham-controlled crossover study involving 17 participants, of whom 15 provided complete electroencephalographic datasets.Main results.Across the three tested protocols, the combined electrical-sensory condition showed larger immediate post-intervention theta-power changes than the audiovisual and sham conditions and a theta- weighted phase lag index difference relative to sham. During the subsequent high-load cognitive task, the combined condition showed a shallower mean parietal alpha accumulation trajectory. Together, these findings characterize the short-term neurodynamic profile associated with the integrated protocol. Exploratory brain-behavior analysis showed a positive full-sample association that was sensitive to individual observations.Significance.These findings support the feasibility of the timing-informed combined electrical-sensory platform and provide preliminary evidence of short-term condition-associated frontoparietal modulation.

articles.title: Granular hydrogel bioink for macroporous pancreatic spheroid scaffolds.
articles.abstract: Cells positioned more than several hundred microns away from a vascular network experience insufficient oxygen and nutrient supply due to diffusion limitations, leading to compromised viability and impaired function. This challenge is especially relevant in large, engineered 3D constructs which exceed the diffusion limitation of 100-200µm, resulting in necrotic cores. Granular hydrogels have emerged as a promising approach for tissue engineering due to their inherent porosity. Their interconnected pores can facilitate mass transport of oxygen and nutrients, and therefore support cellular function. In this work, we developed a facile method to prepare bioprintable granular hydrogel bioink containing microparticles with tunable diameters, that can form porous scaffolds with different pore sizes and porosities. The bioink remained shelf-stable for at least 60 d when stored at 4 °C, as determined by the melt temperature. The macroporous granular hydrogel scaffold has inherent void spaces between the hydrogel microparticles, in which spheroids can be embedded. Pancreatic spheroids incorporated into the scaffold showed improved viability compared to free spheroids, indicating the granular microenvironment supports spheroid survival. Furthermore, functional studies of embedded pancreatic spheroids with glucose-stimulated insulin secretion demonstrated preserved insulin secretion functionality. Our approach thus serves as a tunable platform for supporting the culture of functional spheroids and organoids, that has potential regenerative medicine applications in restoration of physiological functions when implanted.

articles.title: The Ataxias as an Example of Rare Diseases: Diagnosis, Genetics, and Treatment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ataxias are a group of rare diseases. In the European Union, a disease is defined as rare if its prevalence is less than 5 per 10 000 people. Ataxias are rarer than this threshold, although reliable prevalence estimates are largely lacking. The worldwide mean prevalence of autosomal dominant hereditary ataxias is approximately 2.7 per 100 000 people (95% confidence interval [1.5; 4.0/100 000]), and that of autosomal-recessive ataxias is approximately 3.3 per 100 000 people [1.8; 4.9/100 000]. Ataxias include hereditary (genetic), sporadic degenerative, and acquired types.

METHODS: This narrative review is based on the guidelines of the German Society for Neurology (Deutsche Gesellschaft für Neurologie) and on other current reviews, supplemented by the findings of targeted PubMed searches.

RESULTS: In the more common types of hereditary ataxia, a presumptive diagnosis (spot diagnosis) can already be made on the basis of the history, neurological examination, and brain MRI findings and can then be confirmed by genetic testing. These include Friedreich ataxia, the RFC1-CANVAS syndrome (cerebellar ataxia, neuropathy, and vestibular areflexia), and spinocerebellar ataxia types 3 and 27B (SCA3 and SCA27B). When a spot diagnosis is not possible, the diagnosis can often be established by genetic testing (preferably genome-based). Multisystem atrophy of the cerebellar type (MSA-C) arises sporadically. Ataxia with a subacute course suggests an acquired type of ataxia-in particular, immune-mediated ataxias and vitamin B1 deficiency (Wernicke) encephalopathy. Omaveloxolone has been approved for the treatment of Friedreich ataxia. In a phase 2 trial with 103 patients, the clinical severity score (mFARS value, maximum 99 points) improved by a mean of 1.55 points after 48 weeks of treatment, compared with worsening by 0.85 points with placebo. Fampridine is used off-label to treat episodic ataxias, downbeat nystagmus, and SCA27B. Randomized trials have documented the benefit of physiotherapy and regular exercise training for patients with ataxia.

CONCLUSION: An increasing number of ataxias can be diagnosed with the improved genetic and immunological diagnostic techniques that are now available. Opportunities for treatment remain limited, but many new therapies are under development, including gene therapy.

articles.title: Indications for Dose Adjustment of Thyroid Hormones in Older Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thyroid dysfunction is common in older people (persons aged 65 and above). A meta-analysis of data from European countries revealed a 4.1% prevalence of undiagnosed subclinical hypothyroidism. It was found in a primary care study from the United Kingdom that approximately 10 percent of people over age 70 were under treatment for hypothyroidism.

METHODS: This narrative review is based on findings in relevant publications retrieved by a PubMed search and on the guidelines of the European Thyroid Association and the American Thyroid Association.

RESULTS: Overtreatment with levothyroxine increases the risk of cardiovascular, cognitive, and skeletal complications (hazard ratio 1.37-2.02). Randomized controlled trials have not shown that treatment with levothyroxine (T4) improves presumed symptoms of hypothyroidism, body weight, or fatigue. In patients who are now taking levothyroxine, lowering the dose or stopping the drug should be considered; in older patients, the target range for thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) should be 4-10 mU/L. After levothyroxine is stopped, some patients remain euthyroid; in the absence of an indication, gradual tapering may be considered. Levothyroxine should not be given over the long term to patients with thyroid nodules. Subclinical hyperthyroidism in older people is associated with clinically relevant risks, particularly atrial fibrillation and bone fractures, and should therefore be treated. Its most common cause, however, is levothyroxine treatment that is either not indicated or improperly dosed.

CONCLUSION: While overt hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism must be treated at any age, the need to treat subclinical hypothyroidism should be individually assessed; subclinical hyperthyroidism, by contrast, generally warrants treatment given its associated risks. In view of the risks of inadequately treated hyperthyroidism and excessively dosed levothyroxine, physicians should regularly review the indication for treatment, the dosage, and the possibility of lowering the dose or discontinuing the drug.

articles.title: Atypical survey response patterns as early indicators of dementia onset: a coordinated analysis across longitudinal aging cohorts.
articles.journal: The journals of gerontology. Series B, Psychological sciences and social sciences
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Atypical survey response patterns, such as inconsistent or implausible responses, have been linked to lower cognitive functioning in later life. This study examined whether these behaviors predict future dementia onset across diverse longitudinal studies of aging.

METHODS: We conducted a coordinated analysis of data from eight longitudinal studies of aging (total N = 76,350). We derived 5 common types of atypical response pattern indicators from participants' questionnaire data. Associations with subsequent dementia risk were examined within each cohort using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for demographic covariates and accounting for death as a competing risk. Results were synthesized using random-effects meta-analysis methods.

RESULTS: Across cohorts, significant associations with incident dementia were observed for item-nonresponse (overall hazard ratio [HR] per SD increase = 1.06), random response errors (HR = 1.25), multivariate outlier responses (HR = 1.31), and incompatible response patterns indexed by Guttman errors and person-fit statistics (HRs = 1.22-1.25). Extreme responding was not significantly associated with dementia risk. Secondary analyses suggested stronger associations among individuals younger than 75 years and those with higher levels of education.

DISCUSSION: Routine survey responses contain behavioral signals associated with emerging dementia risk. Because these indicators can be derived from existing survey data without additional testing burden, they may provide a scalable complement to traditional approaches for studying cognitive aging in large population-based cohorts.

articles.title: Antibiotic Treatment of Severe Infections with Multiresistant Bacteria.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Approximately 10 000 people die in Germany each year because of infections with multidrug-resistant organisms (MDRO) such as carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE), difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (DTR-PA), carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB), methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), and vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE). Such infections are a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge. This clinical practice guideline contains evidence-based recommendations for the antibiotic treatment of severe MDRO infections.

METHODS: This guideline is based on findings in publications retrieved by a systematic search in PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library. The evidence was evaluated according to the GRADE system, and a structured nominal group process was carried out under moderation by the Association of the Scientific Medical Societies in Germany (Arbeitsgemeinschaft der Wissenschaftlichen Medizinischen Fachgesellschaften, AWMF).

RESULTS: In cases of suspected MDRO, the species of the pathogen and its MDRO-defining resistance should be identified and confirmed, and sensitivity to other antibiotics should be tested. In cases of severe Gram-negative MDRO infection, metallo-β-lactamases must be either detected or ruled out. Treatment tailored to the pathogen and its sensitivity pattern increases the likelihood of success and lowers selection pressure that can lead to the development of resistance. For MDRO not involving metallo-β-lactamase, the drugs of first choice are ceftazidime-avibactam, meropenem-vaborbactam, and imipenem-relebactam; for MDRO with metallo-β-lactamase or drug resistance, cefiderocol or aztreonam-avibactam may be considered. Ceftolozan-tazobactam, ceftazidime-avibactam, imipenem-relebactam, and cefiderocol are suitable for DTR-PA; ceftolozan-tazobactam is the preferred choice, while cefiderocol should be reserved for metallo-β-lactamase-producing strains. For CRAB, cefiderocol is recommended; sulbactam-durlobactam plus a carbapenem is an alternative that is not approved in Europe. MRSA bloodstream infections should be treated with intravenous daptomycin or vancomycin, and MRSA pneumonia with linezolid or vancomycin. For VRE bloodstream infections, linezolid or daptomycin at a dosage of 10-12 mg/kg is indicated.

CONCLUSION: The treatment should be tailored in consideration of the site of infection, the antibiotic sensitivity profile, the resistance mechanism, and the clinical situation. New reserve antibiotics should be used selectively and in the framework of antimicrobial stewardship.

articles.title: The Detection of Atrial Fibrillation by Implantable Event Recorders: A Study of Patients Who Have Had a Cryptogenic Stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Arial fibrillation (AF) plays a role in approximately one-third of ischemic strokes. In embolic strokes of undetermined source (ESUS), paroxysmal atrial fibrillation often escapes detection; if detected, it could be an indication for oral anticoagulation. In the ARTESiA trial, the absolute benefit of anticoagulation was higher in patients who had already had a stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA) than in those who had not.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed data from 233 consecutive ESUS patients at the Jena University Hospital who had received an implanted loop recorder (ILR) over the period 2021-2025. We additionally provide a narrative review on the detection rates associated with various monitoring strategies based on pertinent publications that were retrieved by a literature search.

RESULTS: The 12-month detection rate of paroxysmal AF was 24.0% (56/233, 95% confidence interval [19.0; 29.9]). 73.2% of the initial detections were within the first 90 days. All patients in whom AF was detected were orally anticoagulated. The 12-month detection rate was higher than in the CRYSTAL-AF trial (12.4%) and the PER-DIEM trial (15.3%), but lower than was reported by Pikija et al. (31.3%). The cutoff values with the highest positive predictive value were a stroke risk analysis (SRA) index of 2 or above (38.4%) and age 75 or above (37.9%).

CONCLUSION: Early, risk-adapted diagnostic testing with ILR in selected ESUS patients can detect clinically relevant AF. Advanced age and an elevated SRA index may be useful patient selection criteria. A robust number needed to treat (NNT) for the ILR strategy cannot be derived from the available one-armed registry data. The indication for ILR should be linked to its therapeutic relevance, the probability of detecting AF, and the individual hemorrhagic risk.

articles.title: Plasminogen Recruitment by Staphylococcus aureus SdrC Reveals a Tractable Antivirulence Target.
articles.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus exploits host extracellular matrix components to promote tissue invasion and dissemination. Here, we identify the serine-aspartate repeat protein C (SdrC) as a previously unrecognized plasminogen-binding protein on the S. aureus surface. Using recombinant domains and isogenic mutants, we show that SdrC is a major determinant of plasminogen recruitment at the cellular level. Biochemical and biophysical analyses demonstrate that plasminogen recognition is enhanced by the cooperative action of the SdrC N2 and N3 domains, which together bind plasminogen with submicromolar to low-micromolar affinity. This interaction is lysine-dependent and is selectively inhibited by lysine and 6-aminocaproic acid, with measurable IC50 values, and requires plasminogen kringle domain 4. Importantly, SdrC-bound plasminogen remains readily activatable by host plasminogen activators, generating active plasmin capable of degrading fibrinogen. Consistently, heterologous expression of SdrC enhances plasminogen binding and promotes plasmin activity at the bacterial surface. These findings link a defined staphylococcal adhesin to localized engagement of the host fibrinolytic system and suggest that SdrC-mediated plasminogen recruitment may contribute to persistence and tissue dissemination during invasive infection. Overall, our results establish the SdrC-plasminogen axis as a mechanistically characterized and pharmacologically tractable antivirulence target.

articles.title: Ablation With Dual-Energy Lattice-Tip Catheter for Refractory Ventricular Tachycardia Adjacent to VSD Closure Device.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Safety regarding pulsed field ablation (PFA) and radiofrequency ablation (RFA) using the Sphere-9 Catheter for ventricular tachycardia (VT) near ventricular septal defect (VSD) closure devices is unknown.

CASE SUMMARY: A 64-year-old man with extensive cardiac history including VSD closure with an Amplatzer device and complete heart block status post biventricular cardioverter-defibrillator with abandoned RV lead because of fracture presented with recurrent, symptomatic VT. Electroanatomical mapping showed VT in the basal septum adjacent to the Amplatzer device. Using the Sphere-9 catheter, RFA terminated the tachycardia, and PFA was successful near the VSD closure device without apparent complication. VT was noninducible postablation.

DISCUSSION: We describe procedural reasoning and considerations to optimize safe delivery of PFA and RFA using the Sphere-9 catheter for septal VT near intracardiac hardware.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Colocalized PFA/RFA using the Sphere-9 catheter may be an effective treatment option for persistent VT near intracardiac devices for highly selected patients.

articles.title: Left Bundle Branch Optimized Resynchronization Therapy for Persistent Ventricular Dysfunction After Complex PCI and TAVR.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe aortic stenosis with complex coronary artery disease presents challenges in patients unsuitable for surgery. Persistent left bundle branch block (LBBB) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) may impair ventricular recovery.

CASE SUMMARY: A 67-year-old man underwent high-risk left main-left anterior descending percutaneous coronary intervention, complicated by cardiogenic shock and severe left ventricular (LV) dysfunction. Subsequent TAVR achieved favorable valve hemodynamics but was followed by new-onset left bundle branch block and persistent LV dysfunction. Left bundle branch pacing achieved complete correction only at high output. A coronary sinus lead was added for left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy with a defibrillator (LOT-CRTD). At 3 months, LV function fully recovered with reverse remodeling and marked symptom improvement. Why Beyond the Guideline: Optimal percutaneous coronary intervention-TAVR timing and device strategies for post-TAVR LBBB with LV dysfunction remain poorly defined in current guidelines.

DISCUSSION: LOT-CRTD may provide effective cardiac resynchronization when isolated left bundle branch pacing cannot achieve optimal correction.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Sequence of PCI-TAVR remained individualized. LOT-CRT is a viable strategy to facilitate ventricular recovery for post-TAVR LBBB.

articles.title: "Whiplash Motion" in Cardiac Intimal Sarcoma With Functional Mitral Stenosis and Dynamic LVOT Obstruction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac intimal sarcoma (CIS) usually presents as an isolated left atrial mass; pan-left-heart involvement producing simultaneous inflow and outflow obstruction is rare.

CASE SUMMARY: A 43-year-old man presented in acute heart failure (B-type natriuretic peptide 948.8 pg/mL; right ventricular systolic pressure 59 mm Hg). Imaging showed a tumor in the left atrium and ventricle: an atrial mass infiltrated the mitral leaflet, causing functional mitral stenosis, whereas a mobile papillary-muscle component showed a "whiplash motion," prolapsing into the left ventricular outflow tract and protruding through the aortic valve in systole. Emergency debulking and mechanical mitral valve replacement followed; histopathology confirmed CIS (mouse double minute 2 homolog/cyclin-dependent kinase 4 positive, mouse double minute 2 homolog-amplified). Although adjuvant carbon-ion radiotherapy provided temporary control, the patient died 20 months later.

DISCUSSION: We propose the "whiplash motion" sign and highlight the trade-off between mechanical-valve durability and bleeding risk during thoracic radiotherapy.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: CIS can cause dual left-heart obstruction through multicomponent tumor dynamics; prosthetic valve choice should anticipate multimodality oncologic management.

articles.title: Extensive Native Aortic Valve Infiltration and Early Bioprosthetic Valve Degeneration in Low-Grade Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac manifestations of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) are extremely rare, particularly involving valves.

CASE SUMMARY: A patient with low-grade CLL presented with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis. Following surgical aortic valve replacement, the patient experienced rapid degeneration of her surgical bioprosthetic aortic valve, necessitating valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Re-evaluation of her excised native aortic valve tissue on histology with immunohistochemical confirmation revealed extensive CLL infiltration.

DISCUSSION: Extensive CLL infiltration of the aortic valve is an extremely rare phenomenon. This case raises the hypothesis that a clonal lymphoproliferative process may contribute to calcific aortic stenosis and possibly early bioprosthetic structural valve deterioration. Additional studies are needed to further evaluate this association.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: CLL can rarely affect cardiac valves and may contribute to the development of native valve stenosis. Additional studies are required to determine whether CLL is a risk factor for early prosthetic structural valve deterioration.

articles.title: Lived Experiences, Coping Behaviors, and Impacts of the 2022 Infant Formula Shortage on Caregivers in the United States.
articles.journal: Journal of nutrition education and behavior
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Assess and explore associations between lived experiences, coping behaviors, and perceived impacts on caregivers affected by the 2022 infant formula shortage in the United States (US), referred to as the shortage.

DESIGN: Convergent mixed methods study design with cross-sectional online survey (n = 243) and semi-structured interviews (n = 14).

SETTING: National.

PARTICIPANTS: US caregivers responsible for an infant during the shortage and affected by the shortage.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES (S): Lived experiences, coping behaviors, perceived impacts of shortage.

ANALYSIS: Descriptive statistics conducted. Associations tested using Pearson's Chi-Squared tests with a post hoc analysis of adjusted call residuals. Qualitative content analysis of semi-structured interviews performed.

RESULTS: Caregivers reported unmet information needs and both positive and negative social support experiences as they navigated the shortage. The most frequently reported coping behavior (55.1%) was changing planned infant feeding practices (e.g., breastfed longer than intended) because of the shortage, which were correlated with perceived impacts of the household being negatively effected (p = 0.003) and that caregiver mental health was negatively effected (p = 0.002) by the shortage. Caregiver interviews revealed detrimental physical effects on infants due to switching infant formulas, negative mental health impacts on caregivers, financial strains, and concerns about future shortages.

CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Efforts that link support, resources, and information to caregivers are needed to protect infant feeding, promote caregiver mental health, and safeguard against future infant formula shortages.

articles.title: A Web-Based Risk Calculator for Psychological Distress in Stable Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: Development and Validation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with stable chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) experience psychological distress that evolves in dynamic and heterogeneous patterns. Conventional cross-sectional screening and baseline-only prediction models fail to capture longitudinal heterogeneity, and few tools integrate trajectory analysis with machine learning (ML) for individualized risk stratification. This study aimed to identify longitudinal trajectories of psychological distress and develop, validate, and deploy a web-based ML risk calculator for clinical use.

METHODS: We enrolled 323 stable COPD outpatients from three tertiary hospitals in Chongqing, China, between March and December 2024. Baseline data included sociodemographic, clinical, and key psychosocial variables. Psychological distress was reassessed at 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months. Growth mixture modeling (GMM) identified distinct longitudinal trajectory classes. The trajectory outcome was dichotomized for prediction: patients in the persistent low-distress group were defined as low-risk, and all others as high-risk. Candidate predictors were screened using univariate analysis and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Eight ML algorithms were trained, internally validated, and compared, and the best-performing model was selected for final development.

RESULTS: GMM revealed four trajectories: persistent high distress (8.0%), transient threshold-exceeding distress with rapid decline (15.2%), persistent near-threshold distress with gradual decline (65.0%), and persistent low distress (11.8%). Using the persistent low-distress group as reference, nine predictors were retained: symptom burden, number of children, negative coping, payment method, perceived stress, acute exacerbation frequency, dyspnea severity, educational level, and gender. The XGBoost model achieved the best-balanced performance, with AUC values of 0.859 (training), 0.686 (validation), and 0.739 (test), indicating moderate discriminative ability. The model showed high positive predictive value but limited negative predictive value, constraining its utility for ruling out distress. A web-based calculator was subsequently developed for clinical implementation.

CONCLUSION: Stable COPD patients follow four distinct longitudinal trajectories of psychological distress. The XGBoost model provides moderate predictive performance as an exploratory risk-stratification tool. The web-based calculator may support clinicians in early identification of individuals at elevated risk of persistent psychological distress, but further validation in independent, diverse cohorts is required before widespread clinical adoption.

articles.title: Race-Neutral Spirometry to Predict Residual Volume in COPD Patients: The Pittsburgh Residual Volume Calculator.
articles.abstract: Body plethysmography, the accepted standard for measuring residual volume (RV), a marker of hyperinflation used in selection for lung volume reduction procedures, has limited availability in resource-constrained settings. We previously developed and validated a spirometry-based model to estimate RV in COPD; however, that model predated race-neutral GLI reference equations and was not easily applied to real world decision making. Applying GLI global reference equations to spirometric measures from 450 adults with COPD from the University of Pittsburgh SCCOR cohort, we used fractional polynomial multiple regression analysis to determine an estimated RV % predicted (RVest%) from spirometric and demographic data:  RVest% = 909.17+4.09*FVC% - 93.15*-208.12*FEV1/FVC-2.01*Age-11.05*1(if male). This demonstrated strong predictive accuracy (R² = 0.72). For RV ≥150%, ≥175%, and ≥200% predicted, AUCs:  0.89, 0.92, and 0.91, respectively.  At RVest% ≥172, sensitivity for RV ≥175% (the most accepted inclusion threshold for volume reduction procedures)  was 94% and specificity was 90Predicted probability for a given patient's RVest%  at various true RV cutpoints, corresponding to e.g., lung volume reduction selection thresholds, can then be determined using a second provided formula. This race-neutral "Pittsburgh RV Calculator" prediction model to estimate RV can support referral decisions for lung volume reduction in under-resourced environments. (see https://www.estimaterv.com/).

articles.title: Scaling and Sustaining Diabetes Self-Management Education in Community Pharmacies: A Statewide Collaborative Evaluation of Clinical and Operational Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE AND OBJECTIVES: Community pharmacies are distinctively positioned to deliver diabetes self-management education and support (DSMES) to populations vulnerable to diabetes-related complications, prompting this evaluation of the program reach, clinical outcomes, patient-reported quality of life (QoL), implementation barriers, and cost efficiency of a statewide collaborative initiative in New York.

INTERVENTION APPROACH: The statewide DSMES initiative was designed to expand access to accredited DSMES services in community pharmacies and support long-term sustainability and included 1) pharmacy recruitment and accreditation, 2) a sustainability program, and 3) workforce innovation.

EVALUATION METHODS: The mixed-methods evaluation included 44 accredited community pharmacies. Program reach was estimated using geospatial mapping and paired clinical and QoL outcomes were assessed through a continuous quality improvement framework. To evaluate a paraprofessional-supported hybrid workforce pilot, a comparative financial analysis was conducted using the 2024 Medicare Part B Physician Fee Schedule.

RESULTS: The initiative successfully reached priority populations, with 91% of participating pharmacies located in tracts that scored moderate to high on the Social Vulnerability Index. The program also yielded significant improvements in participant hemoglobin A1c and median QoL scores. Additionally, it demonstrated that delegating administrative workflows to paraprofessionals reduced personnel costs from $6,592 to $2,169 per 6-patient cohort, transforming an estimated $4,318 net loss into a break-even financial model.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PUBLIC HEALTH: Integrating this paraprofessional workforce model provides a financially sustainable pathway for community pharmacies to deliver accessible and clinically effective DSMES to priority populations.

articles.title: Technology Priorities for Diabetes Care in Rural Georgia: Findings of a Problem Discovery Workshop.
Age-Stratified Disproportionality Analysis of Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors in FAERS and VigiBase.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Bruton's Tyrosine Kinase inhibitors (BTKis) are increasingly used because of their efficacy; however, safety concerns are emerging.

METHODS: This study extracted data from FAERS and VigiBase and divided patients into four age groups. The Reporting Odds Ratio (ROR) was used to identify safety signals.

RESULTS: Regarding cardiac disorders, zanubrutinib showed a specific cardiac arrest signal in the 0-60-year age group in FAERS, and the Atrial Fibrillation (AF) signal intensity increased with age in VigiBase. Conversely, the AF signals decreased across successive age groups for acalabrutinib in VigiBase and for ibrutinib in both databases. Several cardiac PTs for acalabrutinib met the signal criteria in the 61-70-year group. For skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders, multiple nail-related Adverse Drug Events (ADEs) were observed in all age groups for ibrutinib; acalabrutinib and zanubrutinib exhibited no nail-related signals, whereas other skin-related signals were primarily detected in patients aged >60 years. Regarding bleeding ADEs, thirty types were detected for ibrutinib and four for acalabrutinib; zanubrutinib showed no age-specific bleeding signals. For infections and infestations, among the PTs detected in three or more age groups, aspergillus infection, bronchopulmonary aspergillosis, and onychomycosis were consistently ranked among the top ten signals for ibrutinib based on VigiBase ROR025 across all four age groups, with ROR025 values decreasing with increasing age. Signals for different types of pneumonia were detected in all age groups for the BTKis, except in the 0-60- year age group of zanubrutinib. Moreover, the specific signals warrant further attention.

DISCUSSION: This comprehensive analysis of FAERS and VigiBase data highlights age-related differences in ADE reporting across BTKi therapies. These findings identify age-stratified reporting patterns that may help prioritize further safety investigations. A limitation of this study is the lack of integration of potential biological mechanisms underlying BTKi-related ADEs.

CONCLUSION: This study identified age-stratified reporting patterns for three BTKis in two spontaneous reporting systems. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish differences in clinical risk across age groups or causal relationships.

articles.title: Corrigendum to: Revealing the Future of Pharmacovigilance in Precision Pharmaceutical Monitoring.
articles.abstract: Following publication of the article entitled "Revealing the Future of Pharmacovigilance in Precision Pharmaceutical Monitoring" [1], certain phrases and expressions were identified that were unclear or inconsistent with established scientific terminology. To ensure accuracy and clarity of the published record, these expressions have been corrected using terminology that more accurately conveys the intended scientific meaning. These corrections are limited to the wording and terminology of the affected passages and do not alter the data, results, scientific interpretations, or conclusions of the article. The specific corrections are provided below: Table 1, Column 3, Row 6 Original text: In order to quantify the complexity of coronary illness and detect major cardiovascular events, this research focused on metabolomics indicators [74]. Corrected text: In order to quantify the complexity of coronary artery disease and detect major cardiovascular events, this research focused on metabolomics indicators [74]. The original article has been updated accordingly. This corrigendum is published to ensure transparency and accuracy of the scholarly record. The correct version of the article is available online at: https://www.eurekaselect.com/article/147119 The authors regret these errors and apologise for any inconvenience they may have caused.

articles.title: Target-triggered DNAzyme hydrogels with boron-doped atomically dispersed Fe nanozymes for one-step bacterial colorimetric sensing.
articles.abstract: Nanozyme-based bacterial detection faces two long-standing challenges: (1) dependence on multi-step enzymatic cascades that complicate assay workflows, and (2) insufficient sensitivity originating from the intrinsic low catalytic activity of nanozymes and the lack of target pre-amplification for bacterial biomarkers. To address these bottlenecks, we construct a target-triggered DNAzyme hydrogel platform integrated with boron-doped nanozymes (HCFe-B). This platform synergistically couples stimuli-responsive hydrogel-mediated controlled-release and heteroatom-doped nanozyme engineering, enabling one-step ultrasensitive bacterial detection. Upon recognition of bacterial biomarkers, the rationally designed DNAzyme hydrogel triggers one-step nanozyme release, which fully obviates the requirement for multi-step enzymatic cascades. DFT calculations verify that boron doping lowers the energy barrier of the rate-determining O-O cleavage step for atomically dispersed Fe nanozymes, greatly boosting their peroxidase-like activity. As a result, nearly 1000-fold enhancement in detection sensitivity is accomplished without any target pre-amplification. Furthermore, a convolutional neural network (CNN) machine-learning model is implemented to process the readout signals. High-accuracy blind tests on human faecal samples yield an AUC value of 98.25%, alongside 100% sensitivity and 95% specificity. These results underscore the practical promise of our platform for clinical bacterial infection prevention and public-health surveillance.

articles.title: Beyond clinical training: Addressing financial literacy gaps in pediatric gastroenterology fellowship.
A dual-barrier sustained-release hydrogel based on Cu-exchanged Y zeolite and sodium alginate for infected wound healing.
articles.abstract: Bacterial wound infection and the growing crisis of antibiotic resistance urgently demand non-antibiotic wound dressings that integrate long-term antibacterial activity and high biosafety. Herein, we designed a dual-barrier sustained-release antibacterial hydrogel (CuY@SA) by embedding Cu2+-exchanged Y zeolite (CuY) into a calcium-crosslinked sodium alginate (SA) matrix. The ordered microporous zeolite acts as the first-stage reservoir to enable intrinsic Cu2+ sustained release via ion exchange, while the alginate network serves as a second physical diffusion barrier to suppress burst release and prolong delivery. The resulting CuY@SA hydrogel eliminated the initial burst and achieved nearly-linear Cu2+ release over 48 h, with an equilibrium swelling ratio of approximately 28 g g-1 in pH 7.4 PBS. In vitro, CuY@SA exhibited over 99.9% bactericidal efficacy against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, while maintaining >98% cytocompatibility with NIH-3T3 fibroblasts at hydrogel concentrations up to 10 mg mL-1. In a mouse full-thickness infected wound model, CuY@SA significantly accelerated wound closure to over 98% by day 14, promoted collagen deposition and re-epithelialization, reduced local inflammation, and caused no obvious organ toxicity or cuproptosis. Compared with the control hydrogel (Cu@SA) containing directly added free Cu2+, CuY@SA showed remarkably lower cytotoxicity and superior in vivo antibacterial activity, confirming the critical role of zeolite in precise controlled release. This work demonstrates that combining an inorganic zeolite carrier with a biopolymer hydrogel provides a simple, scalable, and effective strategy for developing safe and long-acting antibacterial wound dressings. More broadly, it highlights the untapped potential of zeolites as versatile and tunable controlled-release platforms for advanced biomedical applications.

articles.title: Ultrasonographic assessment of gastrointestinal motility and structural alterations in patients with diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate gastrointestinal contractility and structure using ultrasonography and to assess abdominal symptoms in diabetic patients.

METHODS: The study included 95 diabetic patients and 96 healthy controls. Demographic and clinical data were collected, and all participants completed the Gastrointestinal Symptom Rating Scale (GSRS). Ultrasonography was performed to assess gastrointestinal wall thickness, cardiac orifice and pyloric widths, and gastrointestinal motor function, and to detect structural abnormalities. Statistical analyses included between-group comparisons and correlation analyses.

RESULTS: Compared with controls, diabetic patients had a significantly thicker duodenal wall (Z = 2.462, p = 0.014) and wider cardiac orifice and pylorus (Z = 2.386, p = 0.017; Z = 2.264, p = 0.024), larger minimum antral systolic and maximum antral diastolic areas (Z = 5.378 and 4.105, both p < 0.001), but lower antral contraction amplitude and motility index (t = 4.207, p < 0.001; t = 2.874, p = 0.005). Ultrasonography suggested a higher prevalence of gastric ulcers in diabetic patients (χ² = 4.264, p = 0.039). Diabetic patients reported higher total GSRS, upper abdominal symptom, and constipation scores (Z = 2.568, p = 0.010; Z = 2.326, p = 0.020; Z = 2.615, p = 0.009). Duodenogastric reflux correlated positively with the GSRS total score and several domain scores, including upper abdominal, lower abdominal, reflux, and dyspepsia (r = 0.231-0.326 and p = 0.001-0.024 for all).

CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that ultrasonography can assess gastrointestinal structure and motility and may aid clinical diagnosis and management in diabetic patients.

articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine

articles.title: When an 8-mm Coronary Artery Has No Appropriate Stent: Bailout PCI and Dual-Balloon Optimization in Giant Right Coronary Artery Ectasia.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Giant coronary artery ectasia with acute thrombotic occlusion presents a difficult interventional challenge because of the large thrombus burden, impaired washout, distal embolization, and lack of appropriately sized coronary stents. A 69-year-old woman presented with inferior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction caused by thrombotic subtotal occlusion of an approximately 8-mm dominant right coronary artery (RCA). Primary percutaneous coronary intervention was complicated by recurrent thrombotic no-reflow despite sequential balloon angioplasty, selective aspiration thrombectomy, large-lumen aspiration, and intracoronary antiplatelet and fibrinolytic therapy. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) demonstrated extensive residual thrombus and a true vessel diameter substantially larger than available coronary stent platforms. Because balloon deflation repeatedly resulted in vessel collapse with persistent TIMI 0-1 flow and hemodynamic instability, a 5.0-mm drug-eluting stent was implanted as a bailout scaffold. Persistent proximal malapposition was subsequently improved using simultaneous inflation of 6.0- and 4.0-mm noncompliant balloons, restoring TIMI 3 flow. Three days later, the patient developed a large left cerebellar intracranial hemorrhage requiring surgical evacuation and external ventricular drainage. Antithrombotic therapy was withheld and subsequently reintroduced in a staged, imaging-guided manner. Follow-up angiography and IVUS demonstrated preserved TIMI 3 flow, satisfactory stent expansion and apposition, and residual non-flow-limiting thrombotic material. This case highlights the limitations of conventional coronary stenting in giant ectatic arteries and the role of IVUS in guiding bailout stent optimization and follow-up assessment. It also emphasizes the need to balance stent thrombosis against recurrent intracranial bleeding. A 69-year-old woman presented with inferior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction caused by thrombotic subtotal occlusion of an approximately 8-mm dominant right coronary artery (RCA). Primary percutaneous coronary intervention was complicated by recurrent thrombotic no-reflow despite sequential balloon angioplasty, selective aspiration thrombectomy, large-lumen aspiration, and intracoronary antiplatelet and fibrinolytic therapy. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) demonstrated extensive residual thrombus and a true vessel diameter substantially larger than available coronary stent platforms. Because balloon deflation repeatedly resulted in vessel collapse with persistent TIMI 0-1 flow and hemodynamic instability, a 5.0-mm drug-eluting stent was implanted as a bailout scaffold. Persistent proximal malapposition was subsequently improved using simultaneous inflation of 6.0- and 4.0-mm noncompliant balloons. TIMI 3 flow was restored. Three days later, the patient developed a large left cerebellar intracranial hemorrhage with fourth-ventricular compression requiring suboccipital craniectomy, hematoma evacuation, and external ventricular drainage. Antithrombotic therapy was withheld and subsequently reintroduced in a staged, imaging-guided manner. Follow-up angiography and IVUS demonstrated preserved TIMI 3 flow, satisfactory stent expansion and apposition, and residual non-flow-limiting thrombotic material.

articles.title: C5a receptor inhibition and minimal steroids for induction of remission in ANCA-associated vasculitis.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
