articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: C5a receptor (C5aR) inhibition with avacopan has enabled cumulative glucocorticoid (GC) dose reduction in ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV); however, real-world steroid use remains high. This study evaluates a minimal-GC plus avacopan-based regimen against standard-of-care GC for clinical efficacy, renal recovery, urinary biomarkers, and patient-reported outcomes (AAV-PRO). We hypothesised that this regimen would permit substantial GC reduction while maintaining clinical disease control and renal recovery.

METHODS: This two-centre retrospective study included 126 patients with newly diagnosed or relapsing AAV (70 avacopan; 56 GC). The avacopan group followed the minimal-GC plus avacopan-based regimen: prednisolone 30 mg daily for one week, then 20 mg for one week, with no protocolised upfront intravenous methylprednisolone; the GC group received a standard high-dose oral GC taper (from 1 mg/kg, capped at 60 mg/day). Both received standard induction with rituximab or cyclophosphamide. Outcomes included 12-month sustained remission, eGFR change, safety, AAV-PRO scores, and urinary sCD163, MCP-1 and C5a trajectories.

RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable, with median presenting eGFR 23 versus 25 mL/min/1.73 m² (P = 0.31). Median 12-month cumulative prednisolone was 390 mg with avacopan versus 3535 mg with GC (P < 0.001). Observed sustained remission was 93% versus 91% (P = 0.75) and relapse 6% versus 11% (P = 0.30). Median eGFR increase was 20 versus 18 mL/min/1.73 m² (P = 0.32), with no significant difference among those presenting with eGFR < 15 (P = 0.20). Severe infection rates did not differ significantly (6% versus 9%). AAV-PRO scores were significantly lower with avacopan (median 97 versus 197; P = 0.04). No significant between-group difference in biomarker trajectories was detected.

CONCLUSIONS: In this observational cohort, the minimal-GC plus avacopan-based regimen showed no statistically significant differences in clinical or renal outcomes versus high-dose steroids while reducing cumulative GC exposure by ∼90%. These real-world observations support the feasibility of substantial upfront GC minimisation but should be regarded as supportive rather than confirmatory.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Blood-free full quantification of dynamic TSPO PET imaging with [11C]PBR28.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quantitative dynamic PET imaging requires metabolite-corrected arterial input functions, traditionally obtained through invasive arterial blood sampling, limiting broader adoption of quantitative kinetic modelling. Achieving generalisability across datasets, scanners, and imaging centres remains a major challenge for data-driven alternatives.

METHODS: We developed ASTRA, a deep-learning-based framework for arterial input function estimation from dynamic brain TSPO PET. ASTRA was developed and validated using arterial measurements in one dataset (n=90), then transfer-learned and evaluated against arterial measurements at a second centre (n=52). Building upon this, ASTRA was applied to an independent clinical cohort (n=32) from the second site but without arterial reference data, where quantitative analyses had therefore not been performed, to assess whether it could reproduce previously reported semi-quantitative cross-sectional group differences. Robustness to altered tracer kinetics was evaluated in an out-of-distribution pharmacological blockade cohort (n=5).

RESULTS: ASTRA-derived quantitative estimates agreed with arterial measurements (VT: CCC=0.658-0.805), with higher uncertainty associated with greater error. In the clinical cohort, ASTRA reproduced SUVR-based group differences using DVR (p<0.001), except in the pituitary gland (p=0.12). Finally, ASTRA yielded receptor occupancy estimates (0.92±0.17) closely matching arterial values (0.94±0.12) in the blocking cohort.

CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate the feasibility of multi-site, non-invasive quantitative TSPO PET.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Oligodendrocyte precursor cells in ischemic stroke: from biological properties and glial interactions to therapeutic implications.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke remains a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide. Although revascularization therapies have improved outcomes in certain patients, effective interventions for neurological deficits are still lacking. White matter injury plays a central role in driving persistent functional impairments. As the cellular foundation for myelin regeneration, oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs) have emerged as a promising therapeutic target. This review systematically examines the pathophysiological alterations of OPCs following ischemic stroke, including their proliferation, migration, differentiation, and maturation into myelinating oligodendrocytes, and explores their dynamic interactions with the surrounding microenvironment, including microglia, astrocytes, neurons, and endothelial cells. Accumulating evidence indicates that OPCs not only facilitate myelin repair through differentiation into oligodendrocytes but also contribute to neuroprotection and vascular remodeling by secreting neurotrophic and pro-angiogenic factors. Therapeutic strategies aimed at preserving OPCs and enhancing their differentiation, including pharmacological therapy, cell transplantation, gene therapy, bioengineering and biomaterials technology, as well as rehabilitation and physical therapy, hold considerable promise for improving neurological recovery. By positioning OPC dysfunction as a driver of persistent disability, this review outlines a translational pathway toward therapies that restore white matter integrity and functional recovery after ischemic stroke.

articles.title: When Statistical Mediation Meets Frailty Theory: Rethinking the Hypertension-Frailty Relationship in Indian Adults.
Serglycin regulates macrophage differentiation and is associated with human atherosclerotic plaque stability.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology
articles.abstract: Inflammation contributes to the destabilization of atherosclerotic plaques and increases the risk of cardiovascular events such as myocardial infarction and stroke. Extracellular matrix components modulate inflammation and immune responses within the plaque microenvironment. Serglycin (SRGN), is a proteoglycan primarily expressed by immune cells that regulates inflammation, but its role in human atherosclerotic plaques remains unclear. SRGN protein levels were quantified by ELISA in carotid endarterectomy samples from patients in the Atherosclerotic Plaque Imaging Project and compared between symptomatic and asymptomatic plaques. SRGN spatial localization was evaluated by multispectral imaging and histology. Glycosylation patterns were examined by immunoprecipitation and immunoblotting. Functional effects were investigated using CRISPR-mediated SRGN knockout in THP-1 monocytes differentiated into macrophages and exposed to oxidized low-density lipoprotein (oxLDL). SRGN levels were higher in plaques from asymptomatic patients compared with plaques from symptomatic patients and localized primarily to macrophage- and lipid-rich regions. Plaque SRGN was positively associated with histological markers of plaque stability, displayed heterogeneous molecular forms and showed an inverse association with the plaque vulnerability index. In vitro, SRGN deficiency was associated with a more pro-inflammatory macrophage profile, impaired M2-like polarization, and increased lipid retention following oxLDL exposure. These findings indicate that SRGN is associated with inflammatory cell presence, lipid accumulation, and features of plaque stability in human plaques, and suggest a role for SRGN in macrophage differentiation and lipid handling in atherosclerotic lesions.

articles.title: Early Reintervention After Superior Cavopulmonary Connection Operation and Its Association With Outcomes.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite low operative mortality, superior cavopulmonary connection (SCPC) surgeries are associated with residual lesions and a burden of reintervention. Current practice has trended toward increased utilization of tactics to delay initial surgery (e.g., ductal stent or hybrid strategies). To our knowledge, the effects of these associations on likelihood of residual lesions and post-SCPC diagnostic and interventional catheterization (and their outcomes) have not been described.

AIMS: To describe the likelihood of post-SCPC catheterization, reintervention, and outcomes of these procedures.

METHODS: A single-center case series of patients undergoing SCPC 1/1/2020-3/30/2024 was performed describing the likelihood of requiring catheterization before hospital discharge, interventions performed, and outcomes (adverse events, length of stay, and mortality). Secondary analyses explored differences between patients undergoing transcatheter interventions versus diagnostic studies, regarding both indications and outcomes.

RESULTS: Of 170 total SCPC operations, 26% underwent catheterization during that hospitalization, with 19% requiring reintervention. Prematurity, shorter height, younger age, and ongoing enteral feeding were associated with a higher likelihood of a post-SCPC catheterization (p < 0.05). The majority of interventions were on the left pulmonary artery (47%) or cavopulmonary anastomosis (33%). Surgical mortality was not significantly different between subjects who underwent transcatheter intervention after SCPC (3%) and those who did not undergo catheterization (1%, p = 0.38), but the likelihood was higher in those who underwent catheterization but did not undergo intervention (17%, p = 0.01). Hospital and intensive care unit length of stay were longer for subjects who underwent catheterization (p = 0.001) and intervention (p = 0.01) compared to those who did not.

CONCLUSION: Catheterization remains common after SCPC, with the majority identifying a residual lesion that was treated. With treatment of residual lesions, survival to discharge is not significantly different than unaffected patients, but length of stay is prolonged which may indicate persistent morbidity.

articles.title: Peridialytic and Home Blood Pressure in Relation to Left Ventricular Geometry in Hemodialysis Patients.
articles.journal: Hemodialysis international. International Symposium on Home Hemodialysis
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In hemodialysis, the blood pressure measure that best reflects the chronic blood pressure burden related to left ventricular remodeling remains uncertain. We compared the associations of peridialytic and home blood pressure with left ventricular mass, left ventricular hypertrophy, and left ventricular geometry in maintenance hemodialysis patients.

METHODS: In this multicenter cross-sectional study, 265 adults on thrice-weekly hemodialysis underwent 1-week predialysis, intradialytic, postdialysis blood pressure and home blood pressure monitoring. Echocardiograms interpreted by readers blinded to blood pressure data assessed left ventricular mass index, relative wall thickness, left ventricular hypertrophy, left ventricular concentricity, and concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. Associations were evaluated using multivariable linear and logistic regression, with models adjusted for relevant clinical covariates.

FINDINGS: Predialysis, intradialytic, postdialysis, and home blood pressure were 147/77 ± 24/13, 142/75 ± 22/12, 144/75 ± 23/14, and 132/79 ± 22/12 mmHg. Left ventricular hypertrophy, left ventricular concentricity, and concentric left ventricular hypertrophy were present in 48%, 38%, and 25%, respectively. Systolic home blood pressure showed the strongest association with left ventricular mass index (β = 0.278; R2 = 0.113; p < 0.001), whereas systolic predialysis blood pressure showed the strongest association with relative wall thickness (β = 0.211; R2 = 0.116; p = 0.002). In logistic regression analyses, home blood pressure was the blood pressure approach most consistently associated with left ventricular hypertrophy, left ventricular concentricity, and concentric left ventricular hypertrophy, with odds ratios ranging from 1.030 to 1.048.

DISCUSSION: In maintenance hemodialysis patients, home blood pressure was more consistently associated with adverse left ventricular remodeling, particularly left ventricular mass index, left ventricular hypertrophy, and concentric left ventricular hypertrophy, whereas predialysis systolic blood pressure showed the strongest association with relative wall thickness. The associations observed for selected peridialytic blood pressure measurements support a complementary role for home and dialysis-unit blood pressure assessment in evaluating left ventricular remodeling in this population.

articles.title: Standards Defining Echocardiography Core Laboratory (ECL) in Clinical Practice and Research.
articles.abstract: Echocardiography is extensively utilized in both clinical practice and research due to its accessibility. Echocardiography core laboratories (ECLs) adhering to societal guidelines offer superior readings and interpretations compared with the on-site assessments by reducing measurement variability and enhancing study precision. In the present work, we aim to define minimum standards for clinical echocardiography laboratories and research ECLs based on recommendations from the American Society of Echocardiography and the European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging, as well as on expert opinion and our experience in European countries. Accurate acquisition of high-quality images is crucial for ensuring reproducibility, repeatability and reliability of the echocardiographic measurements. In addition to the commonly used workstations, an academic ECL must also possess the necessary capacities and skilled personnel to conduct sophisticated research projects. Personnel should hold advanced certification in echocardiography, indicating postgraduate training and experience beyond the basic cardiovascular ultrasound education. They should be capable of designing, performing, and interpreting complex echocardiography studies. Reproducibility of the ECL should be validated using a small, randomly selected sample, preferably in the early analytic phase. ECL readings and interpretations are superior to site-reported measurements and serve as the gold standard in observational studies and clinical trials. To ensure internal validity, an academic ECL should continuously evaluate/report reproducibility, repeatability and reliability. ECL should be formally acknowledged and accredited by an international scientific imaging society.

articles.title: Prognostic relevance of protein prescriptions based on adjusted body weight in critically ill overweight or obese patients - analysis of a large international database.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: ESPEN currently recommends using adjusted body weight (aBW) to guide protein prescriptions for critically ill overweight or obese patients. The prognostic relevance of this concept is unknown.

METHODS: We analyzed a subset of a large international point prevalence survey of nutritional practice in 785 intensive care units (ICUs) worldwide. Patients were included if they had been in the ICU for at least 96 h and had a BMI ≥ 25 kg/m². We modelled the association between early average protein intake (days 1-4 after ICU admission) and the cause-specific adjusted hazards of in-ICU death and ICU discharge alive within a competing risks framework. Intake was normalized to aBW, defined as ideal body weight plus 25% of the difference between actual and ideal body weight.

RESULTS: 9,068 patients were analyzed. There was no evidence of an association between early protein intake and ICU discharge alive. In contrast, very low protein intake (below approximately 0.45 g/kg aBW/day) was associated with a higher hazard of in-ICU death. Above this threshold, there was no clear evidence of a further association between protein intake and the hazard of in-ICU death. The strongest association was observed at 0 g/kg aBW/day (adjusted hazard rate 1.41 i.e. an estimated 38% higher risk, 95% confidence interval 1.17-1.69).

CONCLUSIONS: Early protein intake does not appear to be associated with time to ICU discharge among survivors. However, in critically ill patients with overweight or obesity, very low protein intake during the early acute phase may be associated with less favorable in-ICU outcomes.

articles.title: Infant mortality related to congenital heart disease in the United States, 1999-2025: trends, disparities, and projections to 2040.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Congenital heart disease remains a leading congenital cause of infant mortality in the United States despite major advances in diagnosis and neonatal care. This study evaluated national mortality trends from 1999 to 2025, examined sex and racial disparities, and projected future burden through 2040 using time-series forecasting.

METHODS: A retrospective CDC WONDER analysis examined U.S. infant (< 1 year) CHD mortality from 1999 to 2025 using ICD-10 codes Q20-Q26. Deaths listing CHD as underlying or contributing cause were included. Crude mortality rates (CMRs) per 100,000 with 95% CIs were calculated. Trends were evaluated using Joinpoint regression analysis to estimate annual percent change (APC) and average annual percent change (AAPC). Forecasts to 2040 used ARIMA and ETS models, stratified by sex and race/ethnicity.

RESULTS: From 1999 to 2025, 55,719 infant deaths related to CHD were recorded in the United States, 92.16% in medical facilities. The CMRs declined from 69.66 in 1999 to 46.44 in 2025 (AAPC - 1.32%) and is projected at 37.51 by 2040. Male mortality remained higher than female (54.86 vs. 52.04). NH Black infants had the highest mean mortality (71.87), while NH Asian/Pacific Islander infants showed the steepest decline (AAPC - 2.30%). Recent increases appeared in NH White infants after 2018 (APC 1.56%) and Hispanic infants after 2020 (APC 3.48%) overall.

CONCLUSION: Infant CHD related mortality declined substantially from 1999 to 2025 and is projected to continue decreasing through 2040; however, persistent excess mortality in male, NH Black, and Hispanic infants underscores enduring demographic disparities in outcomes.

articles.title: A clinicopathological-MRI model for predicting pathological complete response after neoadjuvant therapy in breast cancer: a single-center retrospective study with transcriptomic pathway exploration.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate pretreatment prediction of pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant therapy may help guide individualized decision-making in breast cancer. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a practical and interpretable pCR prediction model based on routinely available clinicopathological indicators and MRI-report features, and to explore potential pCR-related biological pathways using a public transcriptomic dataset.

METHODS: This was a single-center retrospective study, including 201 patients with breast cancer who received neoadjuvant therapy followed by surgery at the General Hospital of Northern Theater Command from April 2021 to April 2025. Patients were divided into pCR and non-pCR groups according to postoperative pathology. Pretreatment clinicopathological and MRI-report features were collected. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify pCR-related factors, and a clinicopathological model, an MRI-report model, and a combined clinicopathological-MRI model were constructed. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, the DeLong test, calibration curves, the Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test, decision curve analysis (DCA), and 1000-times bootstrap internal validation. A nomogram was then constructed based on the combined model, and exploratory subgroup applicability was assessed using the single-center cohort. In addition, Hallmark gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) was performed using the available public transcriptome data, serving as a preliminary exploration of the biological functional context associated with pCR in breast cancer, and providing an exploratory biological complement to the predictive model.

RESULTS: Among the 201 patients, 60 achieved pCR and 141 had non-pCR. Multivariable logistic regression showed that HER2-positive status, Ki-67 index, and MRI maximum tumor diameter were associated with pCR. The AUC values of the clinicopathological model, MRI-report model, and combined model were 0.880, 0.703, and 0.910, respectively. Although the combined model showed improved AUC compared with the clinicopathological and MRI-report models, the incremental improvement over the clinicopathological model was limited; therefore, its clinical benefit still requires further confirmation by external validation. Calibration analysis, DCA, and bootstrap internal validation suggested good internal stability of the combined model. The nomogram showed favorable performance within the single-center cohort. Exploratory GSEA suggested that differences between pCR and non-pCR may involve TGF-beta signaling, TNF-alpha/NF-kappaB signaling, estrogen response, KRAS-related pathways, and coagulation-related pathways, with heterogeneity across HR/HER2 subgroups.

CONCLUSIONS: A clinicopathological-MRI combined model incorporating HER2 status, Ki-67 index, and MRI maximum tumor diameter, together with nomogram construction, may provide a simple and interpretable research tool for predicting pCR after neoadjuvant therapy in breast cancer.

articles.title: PD-1/PD-L1 expression in pediatric duodenal biopsies: Association with mucosal activity and diagnostic performance in celiac disease.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The role of immune checkpoint molecules (ICMs) in celiac disease (CD) remains incompletely understood despite their expected function in limiting mucosal immune-mediated injury. This study aimed to evaluate duodenal PD-1 and PD-L1 expression in pediatric duodenal samples, investigate associations with histologic/serologic activity, and assess their diagnostic performance.

METHODS: Patients' files who applied to the pediatric gastroenterology clinic and underwent esophagogastroduodenoscopy between 01.01.2022 and 31.12.2023 were retrospectively reviewed. CD was defined by European Society for Paediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition (ESPGHAN)-based clinicopathologic correlation. PD-1/PD-L1 immunohistochemistry was quantified as the number of positive mononuclear cells per HPF (40x) in the lamina propria in hot spot areas. The diagnostic potential in differentiating CD and non-CD cases was investigated with receiver operating characteristics (ROC) analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 142 children (mean age 10.3 ± 4.4 years; 64.8% male); 68 (47.9%) had CD, and 74 (52.1%) served as non-CD controls. Both markers were significantly elevated in CD tissues (p < 0.001). In ROC analysis, PD-L1 outperformed PD-1 for identifying CD (area under the curve: 0.933 vs. 0.809). A PD-L1 > 6.5/HPF cut-off yielded 92.6% sensitivity and 83.8% specificity. PD-L1 was associated with an increase in Marsh grade in CD samples (p = 0.033) and with an increase in IEL in non-CD cases (p = 0.016).

CONCLUSION: PD-1 and PD-L1 are specifically increased in CD, and PD-L1 could be a candidate diagnostic marker for CD. In autoimmune disorders such as CD, elucidating the interactions, functional capacities, and degrees of involvement of these molecules can provide insights into the pathogenesis, diagnosis, and treatment.

articles.title: Incidence, predictors, and mortality of necrotizing enterocolitis among neonates admitted to two regional referral hospitals in Uganda: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a life-threatening gastrointestinal condition affecting neonates, characterized by abdominal distension, feeding intolerance, and bloody stools, with or without radiological signs such as pneumatosis intestinalis, portal venous gas, or pneumoperitoneum. Despite its significant contribution to neonatal morbidity and mortality, most epidemiological data originate from high-income countries, leaving a gap in evidence from low-resource settings.

OBJECTIVE: To determine the incidence, associated risk factors, and mortality of NEC among neonates aged ≤ 28 days in two regional referral hospitals in Uganda.

METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted among neonates admitted to Mubende and Fort Portal Regional Referral Hospitals between April 2025 and June 2025. NEC was diagnosed using modified Bell's criteria and participants were followed until discharge or 28 days of life. Neonates with major gastrointestinal malformations or referred to other facilities were excluded. NEC diagnosis was based on modified Bell's criteria. A total of 424 neonates were enrolled, comprising 38.9% term and 61.1% preterm infants.

RESULTS: Thirty neonates developed NEC, yielding an incidence proportion of 7.1%, significantly higher among preterm neonates (p < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression identified the following independent risk factors (p < 0.05 for all): maternal chronic illness (particularly HIV), history of preeclampsia, presentation after 14 days of life, very preterm birth, extremely low birth weight, very low birth weight, and neonatal sepsis. Mortality was markedly elevated in neonates with NEC compared to those without (26.8% vs. 2.3%, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: NEC incidence in this low-resource setting is notably high, especially among preterm neonates. These findings underscore the urgent need for targeted interventions to reduce neonatal sepsis, prevent preterm births, address intrauterine growth restriction, and strengthen maternal HIV control measures to improve neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Pediatric inflammatory bowel diseases in patients with genetic syndromes: A case-control multicentre SIGENP study.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterize the clinical phenotype and long-term outcomes of pediatric inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) in patients with genetic syndromes.

METHODS: Multicenter observational case-control study using data from the Italian Society of Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Nutrition IBD registry. Patients diagnosed with pediatric-onset IBD (<18 years) between 2009 and 2024 were included. Syndromic cases were matched 1:2 with non-syndromic controls by gender, age at diagnosis, IBD type, and follow-up duration. Demographic, clinical, and therapeutic data were analyzed.

RESULTS: Sixty-nine patients were included (23 syndromic and 46 controls). At diagnosis, syndromic patients had lower weight (-1.16 z-score, p = 0.004) and height (-1.43 z-score, p < 0.001); these differences persisted at follow-up. Diagnostic delay was longer in syndromic patients (+6.5 months, p = 0.045). Abdominal pain was less frequent at presentation (p = 0.01). Syndromic patients had more hospitalizations (IBD-related incidence rate ratio [IRR] 1.23, p = 0.033; non-IBD IRR 1.65, p < 0.001), more comorbidities (odds ratio [OR] 18.2, p < 0.001), and greater use of non-IBD medications (OR 8.17, p = 0.004). The risk of additional autoimmune diseases was higher but not statistically significant.

CONCLUSIONS: Pediatric IBD patients with genetic syndromes show impaired growth and delayed diagnosis, while intestinal disease activity and treatment exposure are comparable to non-syndromic peers. The higher burden of comorbidities and hospitalizations indicates greater healthcare complexity and diagnostic challenges; early recognition and coordinated multidisciplinary care are reasonable clinical considerations, but their impact on outcomes requires prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Functional assessment of the NLRP3 inflammasome activity in sepsis: a missing component of precision medicine.
A lens on salutogenic concepts as resources for oral health among adults: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To effectively address the global burden of oral health disease, a broader and more sustainable approach focusing of health factors is suggested. The salutogenic approach, which emphasizes psychosocial health resources, offers a promising framework for health promotion. However, there is currently a lack of synthesized evidence on how salutogenic concepts are applied in adult oral health. This scoping review therefore aims to identify and map the existing scientific research on the use of salutogenic concepts as oral health resources among adults.

METHODS: This scoping view followed established guidelines. A systematic search was conducted across four databases (PubMed, Web of Science, PsycInfo, and CINAHL) using a search string strategy based on three key elements: Population (adults aged 18-59), Concept (salutogenic concepts), and Context (oral health). The outcomes of interest included dental caries, periodontitis, and self-reported oral health. A total of 2,503 articles were identified and screened for eligibility, followed by data extraction from the relevant studies.

RESULTS: A total of 28 studies were included in the review, most of which were cross-sectional and published between 1996 and 2025. The studies were conducted across multiple regions worldwide. Based on the salutogenic umbrella framework, 12 key concepts were identified: self-efficacy, sense of coherence, social capital, coping, locus of control, social support, optimism, emotional intelligence, motivation, positive emotionality, resilience, and well-being. These studies varied in how these concepts were defined, the instruments used, the populations studied, and the settings in which the research was conducted.

CONCLUSIONS: There is a growing research interest in applying salutogenic approaches to adult oral health, although concentrated on a few salutogenic constructs and inconsistent in measurement. The findings highlight the relevance of salutogenic concepts for oral health promotion research. Future research using well-defined concepts and robust methodological designs is needed to strengthen the evidence base.

articles.title: Genetic diversity and resistance profiles of MRSA in community and healthcare settings.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to characterize and compare methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) strains isolated from community members and healthcare workers (HCWs) in Egypt using antibiotic susceptibility testing, mecA gene detection, SCCmec typing, and ERIC-PCR fingerprinting. A cross-sectional study was conducted between September 2024 and January 2025, during which 450 specimens were collected from Mansoura University Hospitals and the local community, where 71 specimens (30.8%) were confirmed as MRSA. MRSA prevalence was significantly higher among HCWs, 62.5% (50/80), than among community members, 14% (21/150). In general, antibiotic resistance rates were higher in HCW strains. All isolates were resistant to cefoxitin and sensitive to vancomycin.The methicillin-resistant phenotype of the 71 MRSA isolates was confirmed by positive mecA gene tests, with SCCmec Type III prevalent among healthcare workers and SCCmec Type IV predominating in the community. ERIC-PCR fingerprinting demonstrated the isolates' genetic diversity. The dendrogram based on ERIC patterns showed distinct clusters between community and hospital strains, though with some overlap, suggesting possible transmission between the two populations.In conclusion, MRSA strains from HCWs displayed broader antibiotic resistance and greater clonal similarity, while community strains were more diverse and less resistant. The presence of intermixed clusters between community-acquired (CA-MRSA) and (HCW-MRSA) suggested a possible bidirectional transmission pathway, underscoring the blurring of epidemiological boundaries.These results underline the necessity of ongoing molecular surveillance and integrated infection control strategies to track the spread of MRSA in community and clinical settings.

articles.title: Advancing Health Equity Through Community Ownership, Small-Scale Built Modification, and Meaningful Engagement: the JUMP Initiative.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.abstract:
ISSUE: Chronic diseases like diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease are among the main causes of illness and death in the United States, and they hit Black and Hispanic communities especially hard. Food insecurity and limited access to nutritious foods play a major role in these disparities by making healthy eating and exercise harder and reducing the effectiveness of disease prevention efforts. Although lifestyle interventions are often used to address chronic disease, they usually depend on education or individual counseling and often do not address the bigger social and structural factors that shape people's choices.

DESCRIPTION: The Just Us Moving Program (JUMP) was designed to fill these gaps through a connected, community-engaged approach to sustainable health promotion in food-insecure communities. JUMP incorporates small-scale, community-driven change within trusted community settings, culturally responsive lifestyle education, immersive educational experiences, train-the-trainer capacity-building, and ongoing community work. The approach to JUMP is based on an integrated conceptual framework that includes community-based participatory research (CBPR), the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR), and the Assessing Community Engagement (ACE) framework. Core program components include community aeroponic gardens, experiential and community-based learning activities, SMART goal-setting, motivational interviewing, and iterative community feedback processes.

LESSONS LEARNED: Current evidence applicable to JUMP is formative and derived from early research, community engagement, and pilot studies rather than a formal effectiveness trial. Formative evidence from pilot activities and community outreach suggested interest in lifestyle change, relevance of structural food access supports, and the importance of trust-building, long-term partnership, cultural responsiveness, shared stewardship, and ongoing community involvement. Current findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and encouraging for next-phase implementation and assessment rather than conclusive proof of impact.

CONCLUSION: JUMP represents a theory-informed, community-engaged model for sustainable health promotion in food-insecure communities. The initiative integrates structural supports, culturally responsive education, implementation science, and meaningful community engagement within a community-rooted framework intended to support future evaluation of sustainability, community ownership, implementation outcomes, and health-related impacts over time.

articles.title: Molecular Imaging of Liver Fibrosis using [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT: A Prospective head-to-head comparison with Transient Elastography, Serum Biomarkers & Metavir Histopathological Staging.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Chronic liver disease (CLD) leading to cirrhosis is a major cause of global morbidity and mortality. Histopathological evaluation by liver biopsy remains the gold standard for fibrosis staging, but its invasive nature limits routine use. Non-invasive tools such as serum biomarkers and transient elastography (TE) are widely used but they have recognised limitations. This prospective study performed a comprehensive head-to-head comparison of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT uptake with serum fibrosis scores, TE, and histopathology across all stages of liver fibrosis in a well-characterised CLD cohort.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Fifty-four patients with CLD of different etiologies (51.9% non-alcoholic fatty liver disease [NAFLD], 29.6% viral hepatitis, 11.1% autoimmune hepatitis) underwent [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT together with clinical and biochemical evaluation. Serum fibrosis markers (APRI, FIB-4, and NFS) were calculated, and TE was performed in 52 patients. Liver biopsy (n = 22) was obtained when clinically indicated, or in cases of discordance between non-invasive tests. Hepatic tracer uptake was quantified employing two methodologies (a) a four-region-of-interest (4-ROI) approach as well as (b) whole-liver segmentation approach. Correlations between FAPI uptake and fibrosis markers were assessed using the Spearman rank correlation coefficient. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis determined diagnostic performance for clinically significant fibrosis (≥ F2) and cirrhosis (F4). Patients with discrepant results underwent systematic re-evaluation with repeat TE and/or histopathology to establish a conclusive diagnosis. Additionally, an agreement analysis between the 4-ROI method and whole-liver segmentation was assessed for background-corrected SUVmean using Bland-Altman analysis. The strength of agreement was quantified using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC).

RESULTS: Hepatic [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-04 uptake increased progressively with advancing fibrosis, being visually evident in advanced stages (F3-F4) and rising in parallel with liver stiffness measurement (LSM). Uptake correlated moderately with LSM, APRI, and FIB-4. For clinically significant fibrosis (≥ F2), an average SUVmean threshold (4-ROI) of 0.76 yielded 86.0% sensitivity and 88.9% specificity (AUC 0.88). For cirrhosis (F4), an average SUVmax threshold of 3.13 provided 90.9% specificity (AUC 0.79). The simplified 4-ROI method showed excellent agreement with whole-liver segmentation for background-corrected SUVmean (ICC 0.96, Lin's CCC 0.95, no significant proportional bias) and statistically equivalent diagnostic performance (DeLong p ≥ 0.33). Among discrepant cases, molecular imaging correctly reclassified the majority of patients in whom elastography and FAPI PET disagreed, which was confirmed by repeat TE or biopsy.

CONCLUSION: This prospective study provides evidence that [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT is a reliable non-invasive biomarker of hepatic stellate cell activation, that outperforms conventional methods in clinically discrepant cases of liver fibrosis, while offering whole-liver imaging that is less affected by common confounders. It reliably excludes advanced fibrosis and may help avoid unnecessary liver biopsy. These findings position FAPI PET as a problem-solving tool in CLD management.

articles.title: Changing with the climate: A review of on-farm adaptation behaviour dynamics for research, practice, and policy.
articles.abstract: Understanding behavioural dynamics behind farm-level climate adaptation is crucial for research, policy, and practice. This systematic scoping review synthesises 72 empirical studies (2013-2024) across high-income countries in Europe, North America, Australia, and New Zealand to resolve evidence fragmentation across disciplines and sectors. Based on PRISMA guidelines and combining narrative synthesis and content analysis, we analyse drivers and barriers of farm-level behaviour across five key thematic categories: cognitive-perceptual, experiential-identity, structural-environmental, social-normative, and informational. We establish an integrative conceptual framework revealing two core psychosocial decision pathways: one via attitude-shaped by climate change appraisal, beliefs, and risk perceptions-and another driven by perceived behavioural control (PBC), influenced by structural, financial, policy, and social conditions. Incremental adaptations rely heavily on the practical PBC-pathway, whereas transformative adaptations are more shock-driven and ideological, operating through the attitude-pathway. The framework provides actionable leverage points for context-specific policies, multi-actor knowledge exchange, and social learning.

articles.title: Covert brain infarction in the emergency department: incidence and outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Covert brain infarction (CBI) is defined by neuroimaging evidence of cerebral infarction without history of stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA). The prevalence and management of covert brain infarction in the emergency department (ED) is not well understood. This study aimed to examine the prevalence, management, and one-year outcomes of patients with covert brain infarction detected during ED neuroimaging for non-stroke or TIA reasons.

METHODS: This retrospective observational cohort study included ED patients from two academic hospitals with 24/7 access to computed tomography (CT). The primary outcome was detection of covert brain infarction on CT; secondary outcomes included stroke prevention therapy initiation or modification, specialist referral, and one-year adverse outcomes. Eligible patients were 50 years or older without history of stroke, TIA, or intracranial hemorrhage, who underwent CT in the ED for reasons unrelated to stroke or TIA from January 1 to December 31, 2022. Exclusion criteria included evidence of intracranial hemorrhage or final ED diagnosis of stroke/TIA.

RESULTS: Of 6,535 eligible individuals, a total of 102 patients (1.6%) had covert brain infarction detected on neuroimaging. These patients (age: 78.5 ±10.7 years; 61% male) had substantial vascular risk factors, including hypertension (62.7%), dyslipidemia (45.1%), atrial fibrillation (26.5%), diabetes (20.6%), and smoking (41.2%). Prior to ED visit, 18.6% of patients were on antiplatelets and 23.5% were on anticoagulation. Among those with covert brain infarction discharged from the ED, 91.7% received no change in therapy. In one year after the index visit, 1 patient had a stroke/TIA (1.0%), 4 had a myocardial infarction (3.9%), 2 were diagnosed with new atrial fibrillation (2.0%), and 14 died (13.7%).

CONCLUSION: Patients with covert brain infarction detected in the ED had multiple vascular risk factors, and ED physician initiation or modification of new stroke therapy was uncommon, underscoring the need for further characterization and ED-specific pathways for management of this population.

articles.title: Respiratory-compensated non-contrast vs breath-hold contrast-enhanced MR angiography in pediatric Fontan patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare a highly accelerated ECG-triggered and navigator-gated, non-contrast respiratory-compensated 3D magnetic resonance angiography with Dixon water-fat separation (NC-MRA) to respiratory-suspended non-ECG-triggered multiphase contrast-enhanced MRA (CE-MRA) in pediatric patients with partial or total cavopulmonary connection (PCPC/TCPC).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective single-center study, between 02/2021 and 09/2023, 30 consecutive pediatric patients (mean age 3.6 ± 0.8 years) with PCPC or TCPC underwent 1.5 T cardiovascular MRI under deep sedation and mechanical ventilation. NC-MRA was acquired before contrast administration alongside standard CE-MRA. Two blinded readers independently evaluated image quality using a 5-point Likert scale and measured vascular diameters of predefined aortic segments, the Glenn anastomosis, Fontan conduit, and pulmonary arteries in consensus. Datasets were presented in randomized order. We used paired statistical testing for method comparison and Cohen's kappa to assess inter-rater agreement.

RESULTS: Mean NC-MRA acquisition time (5:55 ± 2:19 min) was comparable to that of multiphase CE-MRA (5:48 ± 3:03 min), including pre-contrast acquisition p = 0.54). Overall image quality was generally comparable between techniques for most vascular segments (NC-MRA median 5, IQR 5-5, CE-MRA median 5, IQR 4-5, p = 0.06-0.52). No significant differences were found in vascular diameter measurements across all segments (p = 0.06-0.59). Inter-reader agreement was at least substantial (κ > 0.65).

CONCLUSION: Respiratory-compensated NC-MRA at 1.5 T provides image quality and vascular diameter measurements comparable to CE-MRA in pediatric PCPC/TCPC patients. Eliminating breath-holds and contrast administration, the technique simplifies workflow, avoids mechanical ventilation, and improves patient safety in this vulnerable population.

KEY POINTS: Question Is a non-contrast, ECG-triggered, and navigator-gated 3D MRA sequence diagnostically equivalent to conventional breath-hold CE-MRA for vascular assessment in pediatric Fontan patients? Findings There were no significant differences in vascular diameters, and image quality was comparable between both sequences in most segments, showing substantial inter-rater agreement and diagnostic reliability. Clinical relevance Non-contrast, ECG-triggered, and navigator-gated MRA enables reliable vascular assessment in pediatric Fontan patients without gadolinium or breath-holds, reducing anesthesia requirements, improving safety, and simplifying workflow in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Systematic Literature Review on the Impact of Hospitalisation and Associated Complications on Patients with Bacterial Infections Receiving Intravenous Antibiotics.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hospitalisation, which carries a risk of hospital-acquired complications (HAC), is common for intravenous (IV) antibiotic treatment and is recommended for serious infections, including complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI). We conducted two systematic literature reviews (SLR) to evaluate IV-line complications (IVLC) associated with short-term IV antibiotic treatment in patients with bacterial infections and assess hospitalisation-related and hospital-acquired complications (including infections).

METHODS: Studies of patients hospitalised with any bacterial infection treated with short-term (≤ 30 days) IV antibiotics, published during 2013-2023, were identified in MEDLINE, Embase and other sources. SLR1 included prevalence and incidence rate of IVLC and impact on outcomes and healthcare resource utilisation (HCRU). SLR2 included prevalence of HAC, length of stay (LOS), readmission and costs.

RESULTS: In SLR1 (36 primary studies), median prevalence and incidence rate of any IVLC for all patients were 6.1% (18 studies) and 3.4 per 1000 catheter/outpatient antimicrobial treatment-days (7 studies), respectively. In patients with cUTI, median prevalence of any IVLC was 1.7% (1 study). Prevalence of IVLC was lower in patients who transitioned from IV-to-oral antibiotics versus IV cohort (5 studies). IVLC increased HCRU, including rehospitalisation, LOS, emergency department visits and IV-line replacement. In SLR2 (36 primary studies), median prevalence of HAC (25 studies) ranged from 0.2% (UTI) to 11.5% (fall) and for hospital-acquired infections in patients with cUTI (5 studies) from 0.2% (Clostridium difficile infection) to 5.4% (new infection). In all patients, each additional day in hospital was associated with a 1.4-1.6% increase in the probability of a hospital-acquired infection, while having a HAC increased LOS by up to 28 days (range: 0-28 days; 12 studies) and was associated with readmission and additional healthcare costs.

CONCLUSION: Hospital-acquired complications, including IVLC, are common and associated with increased HCRU among patients receiving < 30 days of IV antibiotics for bacterial infections.

articles.title: Intensive Pharmaceutical versus Routine Care on Antifungal Drug Therapy Safety in Adult Hematology-Oncology Patients: A Prospective Multicenter Pre-Post Study (MAAMy).
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Invasive fungal diseases (IFDs) are associated with high mortality in hematology-oncology patients. Nevertheless, inappropriate antifungal use remains common. Thus, this study investigated the impact of intensive pharmaceutical care independent of antifungal stewardship programs on drug therapy safety and patient-relevant outcomes in hematology-oncology patients receiving systemic antifungal drugs.

METHODS: A prospective pre-post study was conducted in adult patients receiving systemic antifungal drugs on hematology-oncology general wards at three German tertiary teaching hospitals, consisting of a 12-month observation phase within routine care (OPh) and a 12-month consultation phase with intensive pharmaceutical care (CPh). The CPh included ward pharmacists reviewing antifungal prescriptions and distributing pocket cards summarizing appropriate antifungal prescribing. Primary endpoints were unresolved systemic antifungal drug-related problems (DRPAF, i.e. medication errors and side effects) and the Medication Appropriateness Index of systemic antifungal drugs (MAIAF) per patient case. Secondary endpoints included IFD-related deaths on study wards, intensive care unit (ICU) admissions, and postponed anticancer therapies.

RESULTS: A total of 158 and 151 patients were included in the OPh and CPh, respectively, resulting in 273 and 270 patient cases due to multiple hospital admissions. Unresolved DRPAF and MAIAF per patient case were lower in the CPh compared with the OPh [median (IQR), adjusted regression coefficient B (95% CI): 0 (0-1) versus 1 (0-2), -0.923 (-1.160 to -0.686), P < 0.001; 0 (0-0) versus 2 (0-2), -1.125 (-1.398 to -0.853), P < 0.001]. 180 (47.5%) antifungal prescriptions were rated as inappropriate in the OPh versus 66 (16.6%) in the CPh (P < 0.001). The odds ratio for the composite endpoint of IFD-related death, ICU admission, or postponed anticancer therapy was 0.407 (95% CI 0.140-1.181, P = 0.098), with numerically lower odds of these events in the CPh.

CONCLUSIONS: Intensive pharmaceutical care substantially improved antifungal drug therapy safety and suggested a beneficial impact on patient-relevant outcomes, supporting its implementation in clinical practice.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: DRKS.de, DRKS00022878.

articles.title: Aztreonam-Avibactam for Patients Who are Critically Ill with Gram-Negative Bacterial Infections: Comparison with Colistin Plus Meropenem Subgroup from the Phase 3 REVISIT Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The phase 3 REVISIT trial evaluated aztreonam-avibactam versus meropenem ± colistin for complicated intra-abdominal infection (cIAI), hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP), or ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP). This descriptive post hoc analysis explored efficacy and safety of aztreonam-avibactam versus colistin plus meropenem in patients with cIAI or HAP/VAP.

METHODS: This post hoc analysis included patients who received colistin plus meropenem (all with baseline Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II [APACHE II] scores ≥ 8) and patients who received aztreonam-avibactam with baseline APACHE II scores ≥ 8, for comparable baseline severity. The primary efficacy endpoint was adjudicated clinical cure rate at the test-of-cure (TOC) visit in the intent-to-treat (ITT) and clinically evaluable (CE) analysis sets. Secondary endpoints included clinical cure rate at TOC by infection type, favorable microbiological response at TOC, 28-day mortality, and safety. Efficacy and safety outcomes were compared descriptively.

RESULTS: Overall, we included 186 patients in the ITT population (aztreonam-avibactam, n = 160; colistin plus meropenem, n = 26). Clinical cure rates (95% CI) were 63.1% (55.5-70.3) and 53.8% (35.1-71.8) for aztreonam-avibactam and colistin plus meropenem, respectively (ITT). Results were similar in the CE analysis set. Clinical cure rates in both cIAI and HAP/VAP subgroups were consistent with the overall results, although 95% CIs were wide and the number of patients treated with colistin plus meropenem was small. Microbiological response rate was 71.7% for aztreonam-avibactam and 46.7% for colistin plus meropenem (microbiological ITT). Twenty-eight-day mortality was similar for aztreonam-avibactam (7.5%) and colistin plus meropenem (11.5%; ITT). Proportions of patients with all-cause adverse events (AEs) and serious AEs were generally similar in both groups, with fewer treatment-related AEs for aztreonam-avibactam.

CONCLUSIONS: This exploratory post hoc analysis provides further insights into the efficacy and safety of aztreonam-avibactam versus colistin plus meropenem in patients with cIAI or HAP/VAP who were critically ill.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT number: NCT03329092.

articles.title: Efficacy of Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir in High-Risk Adults with Preexisting SARS-CoV-2 Immunity: A Pooled Analysis of Two Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir (NMV/r) is an oral antiviral treatment approved to treat mild-to-moderate COVID-19 among adults at high risk of severe disease. We conducted a pooled analysis of NMV/r efficacy among high-risk participants from two clinical trials who had evidence of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) immunity through vaccination or previous infection.

METHODS: Data were pooled from a subset of participants from the Evaluation of Protease Inhibition for COVID-19 in High-Risk Patients (EPIC-HR) trial (high-risk, unvaccinated) who were baseline seropositive for SARS-CoV-2 antibodies and high-risk Evaluation of Protease Inhibition for COVID-19 in Standard-Risk Patients (EPIC-SR) participants who were vaccinated against SARS-CoV-2. In both trials, participants were randomized within 5 days of symptom onset to twice-daily NMV/r 300/100 mg or placebo for 5 days. Endpoints included coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19)-related hospitalization or all-cause death through day 28, number of medical visits, time to symptom alleviation, and percentage of participants with severe symptoms.

RESULTS: Overall, 1600 participants were included in the pooled analysis (NMV/r, 807 [EPIC-HR, n = 490; EPIC-SR, n = 317]; placebo, 793 [EPIC-HR, n = 479; EPIC-SR, n = 314]). NMV/r significantly reduced COVID-19-related hospitalization or all-cause death by 73.7% compared with placebo (0.5% versus 1.9%, P = 0.0104). Relative to placebo, NMV/r was also associated with fewer medical visits (21 versus 53, P = 0.0076) and a 2-day reduction in time to symptom alleviation (12 versus 14 days, P = 0.0470). Participants treated with NMV/r were less likely to report severe targeted COVID-19 symptoms compared with placebo (22.1% relative reduction on days 2-6 [P = 0.0441]; 46.6% relative reduction on days 7-28 [P = 0.0011]).

CONCLUSIONS: NMV/r reduced hospitalization and death, medical visits, time to symptom alleviation, and severe symptoms among high-risk participants with preexisting SARS-CoV-2 immunity.

CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: NCT04960202; NCT05011513.

articles.title: Greater stent expansion at the maximally calcified segment with cutting balloon versus noncompliant balloon preparation: the randomized PREDICTION trial.
articles.abstract: Coronary calcification can limit stent expansion during percutaneous coronary intervention. Cutting balloons concentrate mechanical stress at the blade-plaque interface, but randomized in vivo evidence comparing cutting balloon with conventional noncompliant balloon preparation is limited. To compare cutting balloon (CB) preparation with conventional noncompliant balloon angioplasty (BA) for lesion preparation in calcified coronary lesions. PREDICTION was a prospective, multicenter, open-label randomized trial at eight Japanese centers. Patients with de novo coronary lesions and angiographically significant calcification were randomized 1:1 to CB preparation or BA. PCI was NIRS-IVUS-guided. The primary endpoint was post-PCI minimum stent area at the preintervention maximally calcified segment. The trial was registered in the Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (jRCTs052200044). Of 170 randomized patients, 152 had evaluable primary endpoint data and were analyzed according to randomized treatment assignment (CB, n = 77; BA, n = 75). Mean predilatation pressure was lower with CB than BA (10.7 ± 3.3 vs. 16.1 ± 4.2 atm; p < 0.001). MSA at the maximally calcified segment was greater in the CB group (6.4 [5.8-7.5] vs. 5.9 [4.8-7.3] mm²; p = 0.013), as was MSA (6.1 [5.2-6.8] vs. 5.2 [4.2-6.7] mm²; p = 0.03). Clinically driven 9-month TLR occurred in 1 CB patient and no BA patients. One coronary perforation occurred during postdilatation in the CB group. In this multicenter randomized trial, CB preparation resulted in greater IVUS-derived stent expansion at the maximally calcified segment than conventional BA. The trial was not powered to assess differences in clinical outcomes or infrequent procedural complications.

articles.title: Endpoint selection in clinical trials of revascularization devices for chronic limb-threatening ischemia: evolution of Japanese clinical evaluation guidance and regulatory perspectives.
articles.abstract: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is a heterogeneous clinical syndrome characterized by ischemia, wounds, and infection and is associated with substantial risks of mortality, major amputation, pain, functional impairment, and diminished quality of life. These diverse clinical manifestations pose considerable challenges for selecting appropriate endpoints in clinical trials of revascularization devices. This article examines the selection and interpretation of clinical endpoints from a regulatory perspective, with particular emphasis on the evolution of Japanese clinical evaluation guidance, the regulatory review of Esprit BTK, and the characteristics of the Japanese CLTI population. The Esprit BTK case highlights a persistent evidentiary gap between demonstrating superior device performance, such as reduced restenosis, and determining whether such improvements translate into clinically meaningful benefits for patients and their limbs. To address this gap, we propose a six-step framework that is grouped into clinical conceptualization (Steps 1-2), endpoint design (Steps 3-5), and estimand and statistical strategy (Step 6). Dialysis status should be considered primarily when defining the target population, interpreting treatment effects, and evaluating the generalizability of trial findings, rather than as a determinant of endpoint selection. This framework is intended to promote greater consistency and interpretability in endpoint selection and to facilitate regulatory assessment of the benefit-risk profile of revascularization devices for CLTI.

articles.title: Feature-Level Fourier Amplitude Modulation to Reduce Domain-Specific Spectral Bias for Cross-Domain Polyp Segmentation.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: Accurate polyp segmentation is critical for early colorectal cancer detection, yet models trained on one endoscopic dataset often degrade during cross-domain evaluation. One major source of this gap is acquisition-induced appearance variation, where imaging settings and post-processing pipelines introduce color shifts that encourage models to rely on domain-specific cues. Existing image-level Fourier amplitude approaches reduce global appearance discrepancy but align the entire image spectrum before feature extraction, which risks coupling mucosal background statistics with polyp-relevant signals. We instead modulate the Fourier amplitude of encoder features. Specifically, we decompose the feature amplitude into low- and high-frequency bands and recalibrate their second-order amplitude statistics in a projected space, while preserving the original phase. Since spectral modulation can attenuate fine boundary-related high-frequency responses, we complement it with directional edge refinement guided by an auxiliary luminance signal. Extensive experiments across five polyp segmentation benchmarks under cross-domain protocols show consistent improvements over strong baselines. Quantitatively, the proposed method attains the highest Dice on all five benchmarks (0.930 on Kvasir-SEG and 0.938 on CVC-ClinicDB in-domain; 0.891, 0.805, and 0.830 on the unseen CVC-300, CVC-ColonDB, and ETIS datasets).

articles.title: ConvFormer3D: A Hybrid 3D-CNN-Transformer Front-End for Cine cMRI View Classification Pipelines.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: It is vital to reliably identify the views of standard cine cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (cine cMRI), since each determines which cardiac anatomy will be observed and undergo quantitative analysis. If the view is incorrectly identified, whether by a human observer or by an automated system, errors can propagate into subsequent analyses that give rise to the volumetric assessment, strain analysis, evaluation of the valves, and thus diagnostics. Accurate classification remains a challenge due to clinical variation between scanner manufacturers, differences in acquisition protocols, and motion artifacts. This study presents ConvFormer3D, a hybrid spatiotemporal architecture that includes a Kinetics-400-pretrained 3D residual encoder (R3D-18), modified to handle single-channel cine input, combined with a lightweight temporal transformer and attention-based token pooling. The convolutional stages supply local anatomical and motion priors, while the temporal transformer captures time dependencies throughout the cardiac cycle at full temporal resolution. The network is trained using deep auxiliary supervision, label smoothing, an exponential moving average of the parameters, and mixed-precision optimization. The model's predicted probabilities are then calibrated by temperature scaling. To prevent data leakage, the different partitions are created at the level of the individual patient, and all reported metrics are recorded at patient-clustered bootstraps at the 95% confidence interval, together with formal paired significance testing between the various models. On a separate patient-level test partition, ConvFormer3D achieved an accuracy of 0.983 and an expected calibration error of 0.003 after temperature scaling.

articles.title: Thirst as a mediator between depression and oral frailty in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine whether thirst statistically mediates the association between depression and oral frailty among individuals undergoing maintenance hemodialysis.

METHODS: A cross-sectional design was used. Using convenience sampling, 302 patients were enrolled from the hemodialysis unit of a tertiary care hospital in China. Data were collected using a sociodemographic intake form, the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), the Dialysis Thirst Inventory (DTI), and the Oral Frailty Index-8 (OFI-8). PHQ-9 scores were categorized into three groups: minimal (0-4), mild (5-9), and moderate-to-severe depression (≥ 10). Statistical analyses were performed in SPSS 29.0 using the PROCESS macro (Model 4) with a bootstrap-based approach to estimate and test indirect effects.

RESULTS: Oral frailty was identified in 32.78% of participants; 70.53% had minimal depressive symptoms, 21.85% had mild depression, and 7.62% had moderate-to-severe depression. The median DTI score was 13.00 (interquartile range [IQR]: 9.75-15.00), and the median OFI-8 score was 3.00 (IQR: 2.00-4.00). After controlling for age, diabetes, and education level, a statistically significant indirect association between depression and oral frailty through thirst was observed. Using the minimal depression group as the reference, the indirect effect of thirst was 0.126 (accounting for 12.28% of the total effect; bootstrap 95% CI: 0.030-0.255) for the mild depression group and 0.357 (accounting for 14.74% of the total effect; bootstrap 95% CI: 0.132-0.640) for the moderate-to-severe depression group.

CONCLUSIONS: Thirst accounted for a modest but statistically significant proportion of the association between depression severity and oral frailty in cross-sectional mediation analyses. This study suggests that interventions targeting thirst may be a useful component of comprehensive strategies to improve patients' psychological well-being and oral function.

articles.title: Predicting prolonged operative duration and recurrence after emergency incisional ventral hernia repair: a leakage-aware machine learning analysis of the ACTIVE cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Operative duration in emergency incisional ventral hernia repair may reflect the combined burden of patient frailty, emergency presentation, defect complexity, and intraoperative decision-making. Machine learning can capture these nonlinear interactions, but prediction of long-term recurrence remains challenging due to low event rates and follow-up dependence.

METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of the multicenter ACTIVE cohort. Operative time was analyzed as a binary endpoint (> 90 vs ≤90 min), and recurrence as a binary long-term outcome. Predictors were restricted to preoperative and intraoperative variables. Raw operative time was used only to define the duration endpoint and excluded from its predictor set, but retained for recurrence prediction as an intraoperative variable. Models were developed using an 80/20 stratified train-test split. Preprocessing, imputation, scaling, encoding, and any oversampling were performed within training pipelines. Operative duration models were selected by cross-validated ROC-AUC, and recurrence models by cross-validated PR-AUC.

RESULTS: A total of 556 patients were included. Procedures lasting >90 min were associated with larger defect width, higher BMI, sepsis, bowel obstruction, open approach, additional procedures, and mesh repair. The selected operative duration model (SVC RBF) achieved held-out ROC-AUC 0.807 and PR-AUC 0.875. Logistic regression showed similar performance but was not selected due to prespecified criteria. The recurrence model (ExtraTrees Balanced) achieved ROC-AUC 0.764 and PR-AUC 0.314. At the F1-optimized threshold, sensitivity was 0.429 and specificity 0.816.

CONCLUSION: Leakage-aware machine learning predicted prolonged operative duration with useful discrimination, supporting operative time as a surrogate of intraoperative complexity. Recurrence prediction showed moderate ROC discrimination but limited precision-recall performance, reflecting the low number of events. These findings should be considered exploratory and require external validation before clinical application.

articles.title: ATM safeguards liver homeostasis by mitigating mitochondrial hypermetabolism and bioenergetic crisis in MASLD.
articles.abstract: The rising incidence of Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and its progressive stage, Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), represents the most prevalent chronic liver condition and a major health problem. Key molecular mechanisms driving this progression remain unclear. We demonstrate that Replication stress (RS) is a dominant hallmark across all stages of human MASLD, while an ATM-mediated DNA Damage Response (DDR) signature is specifically associated with advanced, fibrosing MASH. Using a preclinical MASLD model, we show that ATM (Ataxia-Telangiectasia Mutated) serves as a critical metabolic safeguard. Hepatocyte-specific deletion of ATM significantly worsens liver damage and fibrosis. Mechanistically, ATM-deficient MASLD hepatocytes exhibit increased oxygen consumption and accelerated TCA cycle flux, driving a metabolic surge accompanied by proton leak, ROS production and mitophagy. This mitochondrial dysfunction results in severe hepatic nucleotide pool imbalance, energy deficit and toxic lipid accumulation. Together, these findings reveal that, beyond its canonical role in DNA repair, ATM safeguards liver homeostasis by restraining mitochondrial hypermetabolism and preventing bioenergetic crisis during MASLD progression.

articles.title: Record-breaking Ebola outbreak: phone data reconstruct first weeks of spread.
Spirituality and death anxiety in cancer caregivers: the mediating role of quality of life.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the relationships among spirituality levels, death anxiety, and quality of life in family caregivers of cancer patients, and to determine the mediating role of quality of life in the relationship between spiritual orientation and death anxiety.

METHODS: This descriptive study was conducted at the Erzurum Regional Training and Research Hospital between June and December 2024. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews with 322 family caregivers of cancer patients, determined by power analysis. The Personal Information Form (22 items), Spiritual Orientation Scale (16 items, 7-point Likert, range 16-112; Cronbach's α = 0.88), Death Anxiety Scale (15 items, yes/no format, range 0-15, scores ≥ 7 indicating death anxiety; Cronbach's α = 0.90), and Caregiver Quality of Life Index-Cancer (CQOLC; 35 items, 5-point Likert, range 0-140; Cronbach's α = 0.87) were used. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, and Hayes Process Macro (Model 4) with 5000 bootstrap resampling were employed for data analysis.

RESULTS: The mean spiritual orientation score was 72.18 ± 5.88, the death anxiety score was 7.46 ± 2.78, and the CQOLC score was 64.28 ± 7.52. Spiritual orientation was positively correlated with quality of life (r = 0.422) and negatively correlated with death anxiety (r =-0.361). Mediation analysis revealed that quality of life partially mediated the relationship between spiritual orientation and death anxiety (indirect effect B = -0.1063, 95% CI [-0.1584, -0.0603]). Spiritual orientation explained 15% of the variance in quality of life, and the model explained 28% of the variance in death anxiety. The mediation effect reached a medium effect size (standardized effect =  - 0.1134).

CONCLUSION: Spiritual orientation improves quality of life and reduces death anxiety among cancer caregivers. Quality of life partially mediates this relationship. Integrating spiritual support into psychosocial care programs for caregivers may enhance quality of life and reduce death anxiety.

articles.title: Portal Vein Recanalization in Children with Extrahepatic Portal Vein Obstruction: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To synthesize the technical success, safety, durability, and clinical efficacy of percutaneous portal vein recanalization in children with non-cirrhotic extrahepatic portal vein obstruction without underlying liver disease.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception to May 2026 for pediatric patients with non-cirrhotic extrahepatic portal vein obstruction who underwent percutaneous portal vein recanalization. Random-effects meta-analyses estimated pooled proportions with 95% confidence intervals and prediction intervals.

RESULTS: Five retrospective single-center cohorts (73 children; variceal bleeding, hypersplenism, or both) were included. Pooled denominators were 67 for technical success, 54 for safety and mortality (Pimpalwar contributed to technical success only), and 16 for post-recanalization durability. Technical success was 55.0% (95% confidence interval 41.0-68.0; prediction interval 28.6-79.4). Procedure-related and all-cause mortality were both 0% (0/54); procedure-related hemorrhage 7% (95% confidence interval 2-23); and portal-biliary fistula 3% (95% confidence interval 0-27). Among the 16 children with successful recanalization and imaging follow-up, assisted portal vein patency was 87% (95% confidence interval 61-97); 50.8% required at least one endovascular re-intervention during surveillance, without surgical conversion; freedom from recurrent variceal or gastrointestinal bleeding among those with variceal bleeding as indication was 100% (prediction interval 73.8-100).

CONCLUSION: In children with chronic native-vessel extrahepatic portal vein obstruction, percutaneous portal vein recanalization may be feasible. No procedure-related mortality was observed, bleeding events were infrequent, and no recurrent variceal bleeding occurred after successful recanalization in patients for whom this outcome was reported.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 4, meta-analysis of case series and retrospective cohort studies.

TRIAL / PROTOCOL REGISTRATION: Prospectively registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO): CRD420261395918.

articles.title: Stroke outcomes in patients with obesity undergoing recanalization therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The influence of obesity on stroke outcomes remains controversial. Some studies suggest a phenomenon known as the "obesity paradox", where patients with obesity may recover better. This study investigated the association between obesity and functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients undergoing recanalization therapy.

METHODS: The ISOT Study was a prospective cohort study conducted at two comprehensive Stroke Centers in Switzerland between 01/2016 and 09/2021. The study enrolled patients treated with intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) and/or endovascular therapy (EVT) who were functionally independent prior to AIS (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-2). Patients were classified into three weight groups: normal weight (BMI < 25 kg/m²), overweight (BMI 25.0-29.9 kg/m²), and obesity (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²). Functional outcome was assessed after 3 months and 1 year. Logistic regression analyses adjusted for age and sex were performed.

RESULTS: Of the 271 patients enrolled (median age 70 years, 65% male, median NIHSS 5 [interquartile range 3-11]), 153 (56%) were treated with IVT, 56 (21%) with EVT and 62 (23%) with IVT + EVT). A total of 96 (35%) had normal weight, 113 (42%) were overweight and 62 (23%) had obesity. Obesity, when compared to normal weight, was associated with poor functional outcomes (mRS 3-6) at three months (24% vs 12%, p = 0.03; adjusted Odds Ratio [aOR] 2.82, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.16-6.88). At 1 year there was still a trend toward poorer outcomes (aOR 2.50, 95% CI 0.98-6.34). There was no difference between patients with normal weight and those who were overweight.

CONCLUSION: In this prospective cohort study, obesity was associated with worse functional outcomes at 3 months with a persistent trend at 1 year in AIS patients undergoing recanalization therapy. These findings provide exploratory, preliminary, hypothesis-generating evidence against the theory of the "obesity paradox" and warrant confirmation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Gestational diabetes mellitus and risk of long-term cardiometabolic disease.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), or hyperglycaemia first diagnosed during pregnancy, is associated with adverse outcomes for the mother and offspring. In this narrative review, we first summarize the epidemiological evidence regarding long-term maternal and offspring cardiometabolic consequences of GDM, including the role of heterogeneity in the aetiology of GDM in shaping the long-term effects of GDM exposure. Next, we discuss established mechanistic processes, such as β-cell stress, vascular dysfunction and developmental programming, that link GDM to long-term maternal and offspring outcomes and, accordingly, hold potential to be therapeutic targets. We also discuss emerging evidence for connections between other processes, such as placental signalling, and cardiometabolic risk after GDM. Finally, we discuss the role of potential avenues for cardiometabolic risk mitigation following GDM exposure, including lactation and breastfeeding, postpartum monitoring and lifestyle interventions.

articles.title: Risk prediction for neonatal resuscitation and intensive care admission after cesarean under general anesthesia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonates delivered by cesarean under general anesthesia (GA) may require resuscitation or neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission. This study aimed to develop and validate clinical prediction models for these outcomes.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included singleton cesarean deliveries under GA at four tertiary centers from January 2009 to August 2023. Patients were randomly split into development and validation cohorts (7:3). Candidate clinical and anesthesia-related variables were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, decision curve analysis, and risk stratification.

RESULTS: Among 1523 neonates, 1067 were assigned to the development cohort and 456 to the validation cohort. Neonatal resuscitation occurred in 212 neonates (13.9%), and NICU admission occurred in 482 (31.6%). The resuscitation model yielded development/validation AUCs of 0.834/0.682, versus 0.810/0.773 for NICU admission. Earlier gestational age was a major predictor of both outcomes, with anesthetic regimen, dexamethasone exposure, and gestational diabetes also contributing to risk estimation.

CONCLUSION: Routinely available perinatal and anesthesia-related variables may help estimate neonatal resuscitation and NICU admission risk after cesarean under GA. These models may support neonatal team preparedness and delivery-room resource planning.

IMPACT: Routinely available perinatal and anesthesia-related data may help estimate neonatal resuscitation and neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission risk after cesarean delivery under general anesthesia. This multicenter study focuses on neonates already exposed to general anesthesia rather than comparing anesthetic techniques. The models incorporate maternal, obstetric, fetal, and anesthesia-related variables, including the induction-to-delivery interval, for individualized pre-delivery risk estimation. The NICU admission model showed more consistent validation performance than the neonatal resuscitation model. These tools may support neonatal team notification, delivery-room readiness, and multidisciplinary planning in high-acuity cesarean deliveries.

articles.title: A roadmap for therapeutic innovation in paediatric chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract: Paediatric chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a progressive and life-altering condition that is associated with substantial comorbidities, reduced life expectancy and considerable burdens on children, families and health care systems. Despite advances in supportive medical management, therapeutic development in paediatric CKD remains sparse. Breakthroughs in the treatment of adult CKD have further exposed the therapeutic and regulatory challenges in paediatric care, underscoring an urgent need for coordinated innovation across the discovery-to-translation continuum.
