In this Roadmap, which was developed through an international, multidisciplinary collaboration involving paediatric and adult nephrologists, paediatric pharmacologists, biostatisticians, experts in regulatory science and health technology assessment, industry representatives and patient advocates, we articulate the therapeutic needs of children with CKD, summarize the current landscape and delineate critical constraints in clinical trial design. We also highlight the need for surrogate end-point qualification, innovative and adaptive trial methodologies, and coordinated global efforts to accelerate therapeutic innovation and address unmet needs in this underserved population.

articles.title: GLADEL-PANLAR clinical practice guidelines for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2025 update.
articles.abstract: The treatment of systemic lupus erythematosus has evolved rapidly over the past decade, particularly in lupus nephritis and in the musculoskeletal and cutaneous domains. These advances are especially relevant in Latin America, where patients face unique challenges related to health care access and resource availability. These evidence-based Latin American Group for the Study of Lupus-Pan-American League of Associations for Rheumatology guidelines provide an update of the 2018 recommendations, incorporating newly approved therapies and new evidence from randomized controlled trials into organ-based treatment algorithms that support earlier integration of biologic drugs when appropriate. The recommendations are complemented by overarching good-practice statements. The recommendations support individualized management according to organ involvement and disease severity, promoting earlier therapeutic optimization, including biologic drugs and targeted therapies when appropriate, the selective use of combination therapies and strategies to minimize glucocorticoid exposure. These updated guidelines reinforce a treat-to-target strategy in which remission or low disease activity are the primary therapeutic goals, and sustained remission represents the optimal long-term outcome. The recommendations also emphasize the need to implement evidence-based care within the realities of Latin American health care systems, where variability in access to treatment and health care resources might influence treatment.

articles.title: Cardiovascular risk, evaluation and management in patients with hypertriglyceridaemia: a Consensus Statement from the International Atherosclerosis Society.
articles.abstract: The prevalence of hypertriglyceridaemia is increasing globally owing to high rates of obesity and diabetes mellitus. Hypertriglyceridaemia is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, mediated through the cholesterol content of triglyceride-rich lipoprotein remnant particles rather than through triglycerides per se. Although plasma levels of triglycerides can be measured with a simple blood test, hypertriglyceridaemia remains underdiagnosed and undertreated. Hypertriglyceridaemia can result from various primary or secondary aetiologies, the identification and management of which is an important first step. Hypertriglyceridaemia can be managed with lifestyle measures, lipid-lowering therapy with statins in indicated patients to reduce cholesterol levels and, in refractory situations, with the addition of triglyceride-specific pharmacological therapies. Emerging therapies with considerable promise for the management of hypertriglyceridaemia include those targeting apolipoprotein C-III, angiopoietin-related protein 3 or fibroblast growth factor 21. However, so far, there is no evidence from randomized clinical trials that pharmacotherapies targeting triglycerides can reduce the occurrence of cardiovascular events, suggesting that elevated levels of triglycerides serve as a marker of atherosclerotic risk that should prompt optimization of modifiable cardiovascular risk factors. In this Consensus Statement, we provide clinical context and evidence for the evaluation, diagnosis and management of hypertriglyceridaemia.

articles.title: Neonatal sepsis.
articles.abstract: Neonatal sepsis and preterm birth are leading contributors to childhood death and disability in sepsis survivors. Whereas deaths from infectious diseases of childhood have declined substantially worldwide, progress in reducing neonatal sepsis burden and impact has stagnated in many low-income and middle-income countries. Efforts to track and prevent neonatal sepsis are hampered by the lack of a universally accepted case definition, gaps in global surveillance programmes, varied clinical presentations, and paucity of accurate and affordable sepsis diagnostics. The changing epidemiology of neonatal sepsis with predominance of Gram-negative pathogens, antimicrobial resistance, scarcity of and inequitable access to novel antibiotics, and under-representation of neonates in antibiotic clinical trials, are key issues impeding optimal treatment. Research and programmatic interventions to accelerate neonatal sepsis prevention and treatment should be prioritized alongside preterm birth prevention. Key actions include improving clinical care and infection prevention practices, and developing new diagnostic tests and vaccines that target the most common neonatal sepsis pathogens, particularly those responsible for the greatest morbidity and mortality.

articles.title: Neonatal sepsis.
One battle after another: orthoflavivirus receptors start to be revealed.
articles.abstract: Orthoflaviviruses, members of the genus Orthoflavivirus in the family Flaviviridae, include major arthropod-borne pathogens, such as dengue, Zika, yellow fever, Japanese encephalitis, and West Nile viruses. Their continued emergence and re-emergence are shaped by viral evolution, vector ecology, urbanization, climate change, human mobility, and uneven population immunity. Understanding the infection biology of these viruses will pave the way for developing therapeutic and preventive countermeasures. Recent discoveries identifying members of the low-density lipoprotein receptor family as functional entry receptors for yellow fever virus and tick-borne encephalitis virus have reshaped our understanding of orthoflavivirus entry. In this review, we analyze these new developments in the context of prior knowledge of orthoflavivirus receptors. We also discuss the evolutionary implications of receptor usage and how receptor identification may accelerate the development of antiviral drugs and vaccines. We propose a framework of orthoflavivirus-host receptor evolution that can be tested experimentally and can guide the development of prediction tools for comprehensive viral receptor usage.

articles.title: Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection in children: A retrospective study in a pediatric care unit.
articles.journal: Enfermedades infecciosas y microbiologia clinica (English ed.)
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) is a recognized cause of respiratory infection in school-aged children. Recent evidence suggests that younger children may also be frequently affected. This study aimed to describe the clinical, radiological, and laboratory characteristics of children with positive respiratory polymerase chain reaction (PCR) results for MP.

METHODS: This retrospective study included children aged one month to 18 years with a positive respiratory PCR panel for MP between January 2019 and December 2024. Clinical, radiological, and laboratory findings were analyzed.

RESULTS: A total of 93 children were included. The median age was three years [interquartile range (IQR): 1-6 years]. The most common symptoms were cough (n=86, 92.5%) and fever (n=80, 86.0%). Respiratory distress was present in 45 (48.4%) patients. Preschool age was significantly associated with nasal obstruction (p=0.006), rhinorrhea (p=0.012), respiratory distress (p=0.010), and hypoxemia (p=0.021). Bilateral infiltrates on chest radiography were more frequent among preschool-aged children, whereas consolidation predominated in school-aged children (p=0.025). Extrapulmonary manifestations were identified in 26 (28.0%) patients, most commonly gastrointestinal symptoms (n=16, 17.2%). Hospitalization was required in 70 (75.3%) children. Coinfection with other respiratory pathogens was more frequent among preschool-aged children (p<0.001) but was not associated with clinical severity (p=0.215) or hospitalization (p=0.185).

CONCLUSIONS: Although MP infection is classically associated with school-aged children, our findings highlight the importance of considering this diagnosis in younger children presenting with compatible clinical features. Focal radiological or auscultatory findings should not exclude MP infection, particularly in the presence of extrapulmonary manifestations. Rapid PCR-based respiratory panel testing available may facilitate early diagnosis and appropriate therapeutic management.

articles.title: Implementing Sepsis Code in Latin American health systems: What works, what is missing, and what should be done now. A narrative review and proposal of a conceptual framework for implementation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the available evidence on the implementation of Sepsis Code programs and to describe a conceptual framework for their application in Latin America.

METHODS: A narrative literature review was conducted using databases and technical documents, including publications from 2010 to 2025. The analysis was structured around thematic axes.

RESULTS: Sepsis represents a disproportionate burden in Latin America, with mortality rates higher than those reported in high-income countries. Evidence consistently shows that the systematic application of care bundles and the activation of specialized response teams improve clinical outcomes. In addition, common organizational elements were identified across successful implementation experiences and served as the basis for the development of a multilevel conceptual framework for the region.

CONCLUSIONS: The available literature identifies organizational components associated with successful Sepsis Code implementation. These findings support a multilevel conceptual framework that may guide the adaptation and implementation of Sepsis Code programs across different healthcare settings in Latin America.

articles.title: Assessment of eligibility for evidence-based pharmacological therapies in acute heart failure across heart failure with reduced and non-reduced ejection fraction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Initiation of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) after stabilization of an acute heart failure (AHF) episode is well-tolerated and improves outcomes. In this study, we evaluated GDMT eligibility across the spectrum of left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) in a contemporary AHF population.

METHODS: Data from VancOuver CoastAL Acute Heart Failure Audit (VOCAL-AHF) of patients discharged with AHF were retrospectively analyzed. Eligibility for GDMT was determined based on major society guidelines. Heart failure phenotypes were defined as HFrEF (LVEF ≤40%), HFmrEF (41-49%), and HFpEF (≥50%).

RESULTS: Among 1587 patients in VOCAL-AHF, there were 782 (49.3%) HFrEF, 132 (8.3%) HFmrEF, and 673 (42.4%) HFpEF. Mean age was 73±15 years and 58% were men. In HFrEF, eligibility for angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors (ARNI) was 64.4%, β-blockers 89.6%, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRA) 73.8%, and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) 82.2%. Overall, 64.5% were eligible for quadruple therapy. In HFmrEF, 60.6% were eligible for steroidal MRA, 66.7% for SGLT2i, and 56.8% for ARNI with 56% candidate for initiation of all three agents. Eligibility for finerenone was 62.1% based on clinical criteria and 34.1% based on strict trial criteria. Corresponding values in HFpEF were 67.4%, and 37.1%. Overall, 66.6% of patients with non-reduced EF were eligible for dual-therapy with finerenone and SGLT2i.

CONCLUSION: Most patients with AHF, across LVEF categories, are eligible for in-hospital GDMT initiation, with a substantial proportion of those with non-reduced EF also meeting criteria for contemporary disease-modifying therapies, highlighting an important and previously underrecognized therapeutic opportunity in this population.

articles.title: Personalised mobile health coaching from early pregnancy to 12-months postpartum for females at risk of gestational diabetes (Bump2Baby and Me): a multicentre, randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal overweight and obesity increase the risk of gestational diabetes and adverse pregnancy outcomes. Digital health interventions offer scalable, personalised support, but evidence for interventions spanning both pregnancy and postpartum remains scarce. We evaluated the effectiveness of a personalised mobile health (mHealth) coaching intervention for females at increased risk of gestational diabetes.

METHODS: This multicentre, randomised controlled trial conducted in Australia, Ireland, Spain, and the UK enrolled pregnant females aged 18 years and older between 12-24 weeks of gestation with increased risk of gestational diabetes (Monash GDM risk tool score ≥3; tool risk factors were maternal age, BMI, ethnicity, family history of diabetes, and past history of gestational diabetes). Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) using computer-generated block randomisation (block size 200; stratified by site) to receive either personalised mHealth coaching via smartphone providing synchronous and asynchronous support through pregnancy to 12 months postpartum alongside usual maternity care, or usual maternity care alone. Usual maternity care, including gestational diabetes screening and management, continued unchanged in both groups, and both groups received Bluetooth-enabled scales. Participants and health coaches could not be masked to allocation; clinical staff providing usual care, laboratory staff, and trial statisticians were masked. The primary outcome was the between-group mean difference in BMI at 12 months postpartum among females at risk of gestational diabetes. The trial was registered at Australia and New Zealand Clinical Trials Register, ACTRN12620001240932.

FINDINGS: Between Feb 9, 2021, and Oct 22, 2023, 4386 females were screened, 3521 were excluded, and 865 were randomly assigned (437 to the mHealth intervention group and 428 to the control group). The mean age of participants was 35·2 years (SD 4·3), and most participants were White (588 [73%] of 804). Mean BMI change did not differ between groups (intervention, -0·04 kg/m2 [SE 0·12] vs control, 0·04 kg/m2 [0·13]). Adverse events were recorded in 18% (79 of 437) of participants in the intervention group and 25% (106 of 428) of participants in the control group; serious adverse events occurred in 6% (28 of 437) of participants in the intervention group and 9% (40 of 428) of participants in the control group. No adverse or serious adverse events were considered related to the intervention.

INTERPRETATION: Personalised mHealth coaching spanning pregnancy and an extended postpartum support period did not reduce mean maternal BMI at 12 months compared with usual care. Findings suggest that mHealth interventions targeting at-risk females might benefit from addressing a broader range of maternal health outcomes beyond weight management.

FUNDING: European Union Commission Horizon 2020 and National Health and Medical Research Council of Australia.

articles.title: Surgical management of osteoradionecrosis of the head and neck region using microvascular free flaps: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: International journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery
articles.abstract: Osteoradionecrosis (ORN) is a rare but severe complication of radiotherapy, significantly impacting patient quality of life. This systematic review and meta-analysis was performed to evaluate whether microvascular tissue transfer is a viable treatment option for ORN in the medium and long term. A comprehensive search of the MEDLINE, Embase, AMED, and Cochrane CENTRAL databases was conducted using broad search terms. Relevant studies were reviewed, and data were extracted based on predefined outcomes. Thirty studies were included for quantitative analysis, encompassing 851 patients and 896 microvascular free flap reconstructions. Flaps included anterolateral thigh, fibula, iliac crest, scapula, and radial forearm, among others. The pooled flap failure rate was 10% (95% confidence interval 8-13%), while the pooled ORN recurrence rate was 6% (95% confidence interval 4-9%). Complications reported included fistula, infection, wound dehiscence, haematoma, and non-union, among others. The mean follow-up duration across studies was 35.8 months (range 1.6-180 months). The certainty of the evidence based on a GRADE assessment was judged to be very low, and the findings should be interpreted with caution. Microvascular free flap reconstruction remains an important option for the management of ORN, offering functional improvement but demonstrating greater variability in flap survival when compared to flaps used in general head and neck reconstruction. The predominance of retrospective evidence, inconsistent reporting (particularly of recurrence), and marked heterogeneity highlight the need for caution when interpreting the results. Prospective studies with standardized outcome definitions and long-term follow-up are required to better define predictors of success and optimize reconstructive strategies.

articles.title: Superficial fascial plane flap elevation: A versatile point of technique for Fournier's gangrene reconstruction.
articles.journal: Annales de chirurgie plastique et esthetique
articles.abstract: Fournier's gangrene is a rapidly progressive necrotizing infection of the perineal and genital regions that requires, from a surgical point of view, urgent debridement followed by reliable soft tissue reconstruction. Flap-based reconstruction is commonly employed to restore form and function; however, conventional flap elevation techniques may result in excessive tissue bulk and increased donor-site morbidity, compromising contour and aesthetic outcomes. This article describes a practical and reproducible flap elevation technique based on the superficial fascial plane for reconstruction following Fournier's gangrene. Following adequate debridement, reconstruction is performed with the patient in the supine position using perforator-based flaps elevated in the superficial fascial plane. Flap planning is guided by defect size and anatomical location. Flap elevation in the superficial fascial plane allows preservation of deep fat lobules and lymphatic structures. Vascular perforators are identified preoperatively using handheld Doppler ultrasonography and confirmed intraoperatively. Depending on defect location, groin-based or posterior thigh-based perforator flaps can be selected for penile or scrotal reconstruction. The flaps are transferred in a propeller fashion to facilitate tension-free inset. Donor-site closure is assessed using the pinch test to ensure primary, tension-free closure. Elevation in the superficial fascial plane facilitates harvest of thin, pliable flaps while minimizing donor-site morbidity. The technique reduces the need for secondary debulking by preserving natural contour. Superficial fascial plane flap elevation represents a reliable and versatile point of technique for reconstruction following Fournier's gangrene, offering thin, pliable coverage while reducing donor-site morbidity.

articles.title: ERN-RITA/PReS recommendations for the diagnosis, classification, monitoring, and treatment of childhood idiopathic (primary) angiitis of the central nervous system.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Childhood central nervous system (CNS) vasculitis is a rare and serious disease for which no evidence-based consensus guidance, standardised terminology, or definitions of treatment response exist. We aimed to develop the first international recommendations for the diagnosis, classification, monitoring, and treatment of CNS vasculitis in children.

METHODS: Adapting the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology standardised operating procedures, an international multidisciplinary panel of 42 experts from 15 countries was assembled through the European Reference Network on Rare Immunodeficiency, Autoinflammatory, Autoimmune and Paediatric Rheumatic Diseases, and the Paediatric Rheumatology European Society. A systematic literature review across 4 databases identified 182 eligible studies, graded per the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine hierarchy. A modified Delphi survey (42 respondents) was followed by a 2-day face-to-face consensus conference (26 voting members; ≥70% agreement required).

RESULTS: The panel formulated 83 consensus statements (3 overarching principles, 14 principles, and 66 recommendations) across 7 clinical domains. Of 182 included articles, 152 (83.5%) reported paediatric data; no level 1 evidence was identified. Key advances include an 8-domain nomenclature system replacing the 'primary/secondary' dichotomy with 'idiopathic/disease-associated' terminology, a paediatric-specific vessel wall imaging interpretive principle, a prospective risk-stratification model for disease progression, genome-wide sequencing as the preferred genetic testing approach, and formal definitions of remission, relapse, and refractory disease. None of these elements had been previously codified for childhood CNS vasculitis.

CONCLUSIONS: These recommendations establish a comprehensive, evidence-graded framework for childhood CNS vasculitis. The absence of level 1 evidence across all domains points to the need for an international prospective registry and collaborative clinical trials.

articles.title: Validation of rheumatoid arthritis low inflammatory activity: a novel clinical target quantifying inflammatory disease activity.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to define and validate a state of rheumatoid arthritis low inflammatory activity (RALI) based on previously validated modified disease activity scores, a tool aimed at improving precision of management.

METHODS: We used data from 3 clinical trials (N = 960) and a large real-world study (Veterans Affairs Rheumatoid Arthritis [VARA] Registry; N = 3423). We determined the optimal discriminatory cutoff using receiver-operating-characteristic analyses for each modified score compared with traditional remission at month 6 in a large clinical trial. We then validated each threshold by evaluating clinical characteristics and prognosis (radiographic progression, cardiovascular disease, and death) among those defined as RALI, comparing its performance to traditional clinical remission using descriptive statistics and Cox regression.

RESULTS: Thresholds for RALI for the Modified Disease Activity Score in 28 Joints (M-DAS28), the Modified Simplified Disease Activity Index, and the Modified Clinical Disease Activity Index were determined to be <1.4, ≤3, and ≤2, respectively. In 3 datasets, a greater number were in RALI compared with the number in remission by traditional scores. RALI was similarly predictive of radiographic progression compared with remission defined by traditional scores. In VARA, M-DAS28 RALI was more common than DAS28 remission (44.0% vs 32.1%). Those in RALI but with high traditional scores had higher rates of comorbidity (eg, anxiety and depression) and lower rates of seropositivity and erosive disease. RALI was a stronger predictor of cardiovascular disease and death than traditional scores.

CONCLUSIONS: More patients achieved RALI than traditional remission with similar or lower rates of radiographic progression as well as low rates of high-risk characteristics and adverse long-term outcomes. These results support RALI as a point-of-care clinical target to inform management.

articles.title: Special ventilation modes and techniques: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation.
articles.abstract: Severe acute respiratory failure in pediatric patients may require advanced respiratory support strategies when conventional mechanical ventilation fails to maintain adequate gas exchange. Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) allows for the maintenance of gas exchange independently of pulmonary and/or cardiac function. It is indicated in refractory respiratory failure, enabling lung rest and protection strategies. It can be used as a bridge to recovery, in transplantation, or for support in potentially reversible situations. The survival to hospital discharge reported in observational case series ranges between 50% and 62%. Its use requires appropriate patient selection, specialized care teams, and early activation of referral centers to optimize its use and minimize complications. High-frequency oscillatory ventilation (HFOV) optimizes alveolar recruitment and CO2 washout through the delivery of very low tidal volumes at supraphysiological frequencies within an "open lung" lung protection strategy. It is of particular interest in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and air leak. However, the evidence to date has not demonstrated its superiority over optimized conventional ventilation in ARDS.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance of Nectin-4-targeted [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-N188 PET/CT versus [18F]-FDG PET/CT for Staging of Locally Advanced and Metastatic Urothelial Carcinoma: A Prospective, Single-center, Phase 2 Feasibility Trial.
articles.abstract: Enfortumab vedotin (EV), an anti-nectin-4 antibody-drug conjugate, alone and with pembrolizumab (EV plus pembrolizumab [EV/P]), has transformed the treatment of locally advanced/metastatic urothelial carcinoma (la/mUC), yet remains biomarker agnostic. We prospectively evaluated [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-N188 PET/CT ([68Ga]-N188 PET/CT) as a whole-body alternative for nectin-4 imaging, with [18F]-FDG PET/CT as an active comparator and conventional computed tomography as the reference standard for staging la/mUC in 25 patients planned for EV/P. [18F]-FDG PET/CT showed a higher maximum standardized uptake value and tumor-to-background ratio than [68Ga]-N188 PET/CT across most lesion types (primary tumor, visceral, and osseous), except for lymph nodes. The overall tracer correlation was weak (Spearman r = 0.196), strongest in lymph nodes (r = 0.657), and absent in primary tumors and bone lesions. For primary tumor detection, [68Ga]-N188 PET/CT had higher specificity (86% vs 57%) and positive predictive value (92% vs 83%) than FDG, which had higher sensitivity (88% vs 67%). Nodal staging performance was similar in the tracers. For distant metastases, both achieved 100% sensitivity and negative predictive value, with [68Ga]-N188 PET/CT showing marginally higher specificity. [68Ga]-N188 PET/CT is feasible for whole-body nectin-4 assessment in la/mUC and supports a distinct biodistribution from FDG, suggesting complementary rather than interchangeable roles. Further prospective evaluation with treatment-outcome correlation is warranted before its use as a biomarker to guide EV-based therapy selection.

articles.title: Beyond the worm: engineering the next generation of nematode-inspired antimicrobials.
articles.abstract: The global crisis of multidrug-resistant bacteria and parasitic nematodes demands new approaches to infectious disease control. Emerging evidence suggests that gastrointestinal nematodes and the host gut microbiota are inextricably linked in a complex 'holobiont'. Parasitic nematodes have evolved in microbe-rich environments for millennia, developing innate immune defenses. This evolutionary 'arms race' has produced a diverse repertoire of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) that can target bacteria and other gut microbiota. With over 5000 AMP and AMP-like domain-encoding genes identified via computational mining, the bottleneck is validation. The integration of machine learning algorithms with advanced in vitro and ex vivo models will allow prediction of AMP mode of action, spectrum of activity, and efficacy, followed by testing in organoids to address some of the limitations of animal models.

Helicobacter pylori antibiotic resistance in Egypt exceeds eradication thresholds: systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Arab journal of gastroenterology : the official publication of the Pan-Arab Association of Gastroenterology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND STUDY AIMS: Eradicating Helicobacter pylori in Egypt is severely hindered by escalating antibiotic resistance. Comprehensive national resistance data are essential for optimizing failing treatment protocols. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to determine the pooled prevalence of Helicobacter pylori resistance to key antibiotics in Egypt to inform national treatment guidelines.

METHODS: Data sources: We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and the Egyptian Knowledge Bank (EKB).

STUDY ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Primary studies published between 2000 and 2025 reporting H. pylori antibiotic resistance prevalence in Egypt were included.

PARTICIPANTS: Human subjects with documented H. pylori infection.

INTERVENTIONS: Resistance was assessed for metronidazole, amoxicillin, clarithromycin, tetracycline, and fluoroquinolones. Assessment of risk of bias: The Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklist for Prevalence Studies was used. Methods of data synthesis: Pooled prevalence and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using a random-effects model with Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation.

RESULTS: Thirty studies comprising 5019 observations were included. The resistance rate for clarithromycin was 42.8% (95% CI: 34.7-51.1%), nearly tripling the 15% Maastricht clinical threshold for abandoning empirical clarithromycin-containing regimens. Rates for other primary antibiotics were also critically high: metronidazole 79.1% (95% CI: 64.7-90.8%) and amoxicillin 45.8% (95% CI: 29.1-62.9%), both far exceeding rates typical for standard empirical therapies. Resistance to tetracycline (23.4%), ciprofloxacin (20.0%), and levofloxacin (18.8%) also surpassed clinical cutoffs. Significant geographic disparities were observed across governorates, with metronidazole resistance reaching 100% in some regions. Meta-regression indicated that these high resistance levels have remained stable over the past two decades.

CONCLUSIONS: Egypt Delta and the Cairo metropolitan areas face a critical burden of Helicobacter pylori resistance, rendering standard empirical triple therapies suboptimal. National guidelines should prioritise quadruple therapy or susceptibility-guided treatments to improve eradication outcomes.

REGISTRATION: PROSPERO (CRD420251249967).

Enteral Clonidine for the Management of Rigors in Pediatric Oncology.
articles.abstract: Rigors are a distressing symptom commonly experienced by oncology patients and may occur secondary to infection, medications, or the disease process itself. Historically, meperidine has been used in the symptomatic management of patients experiencing rigors, but utilization and availability of this medication have declined due to safety concerns. We report the case of a 14-year-old male with acute myeloid leukemia who experienced recurrent severe rigors associated with fever throughout his illness. Enteral clonidine was initiated at a dose of 100 µg every six hours as needed for rigor management and was titrated as high as 100 µg every six hours scheduled during prolonged fever periods. The patient experienced rapid improvement in the severity of rigors following the initiation of clonidine after a single dose. These fevers had been present throughout the duration of his illness and could not always be correlated with specific infections or treatment elements. This case supports the use of enteral clonidine as a possible therapy for patients experiencing painful or distressing rigors.

articles.title: Streptococcus thoraltensis in a Postoperative Wound Infection and a Therapeutic Regimen Associated with Successful Eradication.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Streptococcus thoraltensis is commonly isolated from swine and rabbits; however, over the past decade, it has caused various infections in human beings. The treatment of these infections is typically complex because of an association with antibiotic resistance.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 20-year-old female patient presented with a postoperative surgical site infection and a positive culture for Streptococcus thoraltensis, representing a clinical combination not previously described. A favorable response was achieved by implementing a treatment regimen based on surgical wound cleansing with an isotonic and stabilized 0.057% sodium hypochlorite antimicrobial solution, followed by the application of a gel of the same composition, broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy, and the use of a Negative Pressure Wound Therapy.

CONCLUSION: The relevance of this case lies in its presentation of a new clinical manifestation of the infection, marking the third report and fifth case described within the Mexican population. Above all, it outlines a therapeutic protocol that achieved favorable outcomes, providing a valuable reference for future cases.

Respiratory-Lymphatic Coupling in Edema: A Mechanism-Based Narrative Review and Clinical Framework.
articles.abstract: Background: Edema is a multifactorial clinical condition traditionally attributed to disturbances in vascular and lymphatic fluid dynamics. However, the contribution of respiratory mechanics to fluid regulation remains underrecognized.Objective: This narrative review explores the concept of respiratory-lymphatic coupling and its relevance to edema formation and persistence.Methods: Keyphysiological mechanisms linking breathing dynamics with lymphatic transport are examined, including the role of respiratory-induced pressure gradients and the thoracoabdominal pump in facilitating venous return and lymphatic flow. Disruption of these processes is discussed across clinical conditions where respiratory dysfunction and edema frequently coexist, such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, postoperative states and cardiorespiratory disorders. Results: Across these contexts, impaired respiratory mechanics may reduce lymphatic transport efficiency and contribute to fluid accumulation. Rather than representing a primary cause of edema, respiratory-lymphatic coupling is proposed as a modulatory mechanism influencing the severity and progression of fluid imbalance.Conclusions: Based on this conceptual framework, a mechanism-based approach to clinical decision-making is presented. This approach emphasizes identification of dominant pathophysiological drivers, assessment of physiological stability and individualized prioritization of therapeutic interventions. The integration of respiratory and lymphatic strategies is highlighted as a key component of management. These findings support a more integrated understanding of fluid homeostasis and suggest that incorporating respiratory considerations into edema management may enhance clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Total-Body 18F-FAPI PET/CT for Assessment of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Pilot Study.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: Liver biopsy remains the gold standard for fibrosis assessment; however, its invasiveness limits its suitability for routine clinical use. The rising prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) as a leading cause of chronic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma underscores the need for reliable noninvasive assessment. Current noninvasive imaging methods provide surrogate measures of fibrosis but do not directly assess fibrogenic activity. In contrast, fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET enables molecular imaging of activated fibroblasts, a key driver of fibrosis. This study evaluates dynamic 18F-FAPI-74 PET imaging to assess hepatic fibrogenic activity in MASLD. Methods: In this prospective pilot study, 10 subjects (3 healthy volunteers, 4 patients with mild-moderate fibrosis, and 3 patients with advanced fibrosis) underwent 60-min dynamic 18F-FAPI-74 PET/CT. SUV and blood-normalized SUV ratio (SUVR) were quantified across time frames, and the net influx rate was derived from dynamic data. MR elastography-derived liver stiffness values were obtained for comparison. Correlations with histologic fibrosis scoring of biopsy tissue were assessed using Spearman analysis. Results: At 5 min postinjection, SUVR correlated strongly with histologic fibrosis score (ρ = 0.95; 95% CI, 0.75-1.00; P = 1.89 × 10-5), followed by SUV (ρ = 0.78; 95% CI, 0.23-0.98; P = 0.0077) and net influx rate from kinetic modeling (ρ = 0.84; 95% CI, 0.41-0.98; P = 0.0022). SUVR at the 4- to 5-min interval allowed clearer differentiation among healthy volunteers, patients with mild fibrosis, and patients with advanced fibrosis. Conclusion: Dynamic 18F-FAPI-74 PET enables quantitative visualization of hepatic fibroblast activation in MASLD. SUVR at the 4- to 5-min interval correlates more strongly with fibrosis severity, supporting 18F-FAPI-74 PET as a promising molecular biomarker for assessing and potentially monitoring metabolic fibrosis.

articles.title: A SPECT-Guided, PET-Sparing Algorithm for PSMA Radiopharmaceutical Therapy Evaluation (SPARE).
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: [177Lu]Lu-PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy is delivered as repeated cycles, yet the decision to continue or adapt treatment after the second cycle is not standardized. Posttherapy SPECT/CT is routinely performed but rarely used formally for response assessment. We developed a multimodality, response-adapted algorithm applied after cycle 2 and tested its concordance with real-world decisions. Methods: We studied 142 men with metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant prostate cancer (formerly metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer) who completed at least 2 cycles of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA and underwent posttherapy SPECT/CT, baseline and 12-wk prostate-specific antigen (PSA) testing, and baseline and interim prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET and [18F]FDG PET. Response was assessed in accordance with Prostate Cancer Working Group 4 recommendations for PSA and with RECIP 1.0 for SPECT and PSMA PET. The algorithm combined SPECT/CT and PSA, used PSMA PET only when both were stable, and yielded 3 recommendations: continue [177Lu]Lu-PSMA, discontinue [177Lu]Lu-PSMA, or consider [18F]FDG PET. The primary endpoints were the number of interim PSMA PET studies avoided and the concordance between algorithm recommendations (continue vs. discontinue) and real-world decisions. The secondary endpoint was intermodality response evaluation concordance. Results: The algorithm recommended continuation in 74 patients (52.1%), discontinuation in 49 patients (34.5%), and [18F]FDG PET in 19 patients (13.4%). Interim PSMA PET/CT could be avoided in 120 patients (84.5%) (95% CI, 77.7%-89.5%). Among patients with a definitive recommendation, conditional agreement of the algorithm with real-world management decisions was 91.1% (95% CI, 84.7%-94.9%), with a κ of 0.81 (95% CI, 0.69-0.91). All 74 patients (100%) with an algorithm recommendation to continue treatment had matching real-world decisions for treatment continuation, whereas 38 (78%) of 49 patients with an algorithm recommendation to discontinue treatment had matching real-world decisions for treatment discontinuation. Response classification on SPECT agreed only moderately with PSA level (κ = 0.45) and PSMA PET (κ = 0.47), but the combination of SPECT and PSA raised agreement with PSMA PET to "substantial" (κ = 0.67), approaching that of PSMA PET with PSA level (κ = 0.70). Every discordant decision (n = 11) occurred when the algorithm recommended treatment discontinuation in a patient who nonetheless continued treatment, most commonly because [177Lu]Lu-PSMA was being used as a last line of therapy (7/11, 64%). Conclusion: A SPECT-guided algorithm could have avoided most interim PSMA PET studies and reproduced real-world treatment decisions after 2 cycles of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA with high agreement. This algorithm may serve as the basis for a standardized treatment management framework, pending independent, prospective outcome-based validation.

articles.title: PSMA Total Tumor Volume: A Simple Quantifiable Biomarker for Overall Survival Prediction-Results from the International PROMISE PET Registry.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET is an accurate prognostic imaging biomarker of survival in patients with prostate cancer when assessed using Prostate Cancer Molecular Imaging Standardized Evaluation (PROMISE) criteria. Previously, PSMA PET PROMISE risk nomograms were created that surpassed clinical prediction tools. In this study, we focused on the evaluation of quantifiable biomarkers to simplify and facilitate overall survival (OS) prediction. Methods: Data from patients with histologically proven prostate cancer who underwent PSMA PET between December 2012 and April 2024 at participating imaging centers worldwide and who were included in the PROMISE PET Registry by January 31, 2026, were analyzed. Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels at PSMA PET, disease stage, and OS follow-up data were collected. PSMA total tumor volume (PSMA TTV) and whole-body SUVmean were assessed using predefined SUV thresholds. PSMA total lesion uptake (PSMA TL) was calculated as PSMA TTV × SUVmean PSA level at PSMA PET adjusted for PSMA TTV was calculated as PSA × TTV. Univariate regression analysis was conducted to identify potential predictors. Prognostic accuracy of quantitative biomarkers was compared using Harrell C-indices and time-dependent concordance in the development cohort. Probabilities for 3-, 5-, and 7-y OS across PSMA TTV quartiles were derived from Kaplan-Meier curves. Subgroup analysis was conducted by cancer stage. Results: In total, 13,893 patients were included in the analysis and divided 2:1 into development (n = 9271) and validation (n = 4622) cohorts. The prognostic accuracy of PSMA TTV in the validation cohort (C-index, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.77-0.80) was superior to SUVmean (C-index, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.61-0.64) and PSA level at PET (C-index, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.69-0.72) and similar to PSMA TL (C-index, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.76-0.79) and PSA × TTV (C-index, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.75-0.78). In the entire cohort, the median OS for PSMA TTV quartile 1 (0 mL) and quartile 2 (>0-2.1 mL) was not reached. The median OS was 11.4 y (interquartile range, 10.1 y to not reached) for PSMA TTV quartile 3 (>2.1-16.2 mL) and 4.4 y (interquartile range, 4.2-4.6 y) for quartile 4 (>16.17 mL). Conclusion: Among quantifiable PET metrics, PSMA TTV had the highest prognostic accuracy for OS in patients with prostate cancer. Automated PSMA TTV assessment may facilitate fast and reproducible outcome prediction in the future.

articles.title: Test-Retest Repeatability of Peripheral Ganglion Uptake on 18F-DCFPyL PET/CT: Implications for Interpreting Benign Uptake on PSMA PET.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: Repeatability of uptake in benign structures on prostate-specific membrane antigen PET is unexplored and poorly understood. We used a post hoc analysis of a test-retest cohort to assess repeatability of uptake in peripheral ganglia. Methods: Twenty-two patients were included. Spheric volumes of interest were manually placed on the cervical and lumbosacral dorsal root ganglia, the cervicothoracic ganglia, and the celiac ganglia. Repeatability was quantified using intraclass correlation coefficient, within-subject coefficient of variation, and Bland-Altman limits of agreement. Results: Ganglion uptake demonstrated an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.82 and a within-subject coefficient of variation of 13.1%. Bland-Altman analysis on a relative scale demonstrated that the mean bias was 0.9%, with 95% limits of agreement ranging from -35.8% to 37.6%, broadly comparable to the repeatability of prostate cancer tumors previously reported. Conclusion: The repeatability of uptake in peripheral ganglia on prostate-specific membrane antigen PET scans is similar to the repeatability of uptake in prostate cancer tumors. As such, isolated changes in uptake cannot be used as de facto evidence of a malignant lesion.

articles.title: Science, Mentorship, and Total-Body PET: A Conversation Between Simon Cherry and Johannes Czernin.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine

articles.title: Prostate-Specific Membrane Antigen PET/CT Segmentation Guided by Vision Language Models Embedding Clinical Report Semantics.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: Whole-body prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET/CT segmentation remains challenging: manual contouring is unsustainable, and image-only artificial intelligence models often misclassify physiologic uptake as malignant, causing high false-positive rates. These limitations underscore the need for segmentation strategies that incorporate the nuclear medicine expertise encoded in PET/CT reports but not used by current models. We investigated whether routine PET/CT reports improve automated lesion segmentation for prostate cancer. Methods: We developed a language-guided 3-dimensional SegResNet fusing report text with 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT image features, encoding report semantics via 4 strategies (BiomedVLP, RadGraph, GPT-raw, GPT-engineered) compared with an image-only model (baseline). Of 320 patients who underwent 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT, 297 studies were available; 13 were excluded for missing reports or incomplete image-mask pairs, leaving 284 for analysis, split at the patient level into 243 development cases and a fixed 41-case held-out test set. Metrics included Dice, intersection over union (IoU), precision, recall, average symmetric surface distance, 95th percentile Hausdorff distance, surface Dice similarity at 5 mm, and lesion-level false positives, using 3 matching criteria (any overlap; 1-to-1 maximum IoU matching, IoU ≥ 0.5; and correct localization of the SUVmax voxel). Significance was assessed using paired 1-sided Wilcoxon tests with Holm adjustment. Results: Report guidance consistently reduced false positives and improved whole-mask boundary agreement. False-positive lesions were reduced by nearly 4 per patient with BiomedVLP and by approximately 3 per patient with RadGraph and GPT-raw. Average symmetric surface distance decreased from 105.4 ± 62.5 mm (image only) to 23.4 ± 18.2 mm with BiomedVLP, 36.9 ± 22.4 mm with RadGraph, and 36.3 ± 26.4 mm with GPT-raw; 95th percentile Hausdorff distance improved from 455.0 ± 169.3 mm to 123.8 ± 80.3 mm with BiomedVLP, and surface Dice similarity at 5 mm increased from 0.638 ± 0.172 to 0.705 ± 0.181. However, when these surface metrics were recomputed on matched true-positive lesions only using the same 3 criteria, no language-guided model differed significantly from the image-only model for any surface metric (all Holm-adjusted P = 1.0), indicating that the whole-mask improvements were attributable to false-positive suppression rather than genuine gains in contour accuracy on correctly detected lesions. Precision increased for BiomedVLP (0.099) and RadGraph (0.060), with a modest decrease in voxel-level recall (-0.051, BiomedVLP), reflecting a precision-recall trade-off from suppression of spurious uptake. Dice improved by 0.032 but was borderline significant; IoU increased for BiomedVLP (0.036). Lesion-level sensitivity changed by no more than 0.04 for all models and did not reach significance. Total lesion PSMA remained highly correlated with manual measurements (r ≥ 0.85), whereas PSMA tumor volume correlations were more variable across models (r = 0.37-0.70). Conclusion: The integration of PET/CT report semantics into automated PSMA PET/CT segmentation substantially reduced false-positive lesions and preserved total lesion PSMA agreement with manual measurements; a matched true-positive-only reanalysis indicated that the accompanying whole-mask boundary-agreement gains reflected false-positive suppression rather than improved contour accuracy on correctly detected lesions. This approach may reduce manual cleanup and support more reliable quantitative workflows, although precision gains should be weighed against a modest recall reduction. External validation, extension of the true-positive-only analysis to independent cohorts, and PSMA-specific language pretraining are warranted.

articles.title: Effect of intensive blood pressure control on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes: prespecified analysis of secondary outcomes of BPROAD randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of intensive compared with standard treatment of systolic blood pressure (SBP) on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes.

DESIGN: Multicentre, open label, outcome assessor masked, randomised controlled trial.

SETTING: 145 clinical centres across seven geographical regions in China.

PARTICIPANTS: 12 821 adults aged ≥50 years with type 2 diabetes, raised SBP, and increased cardiovascular risk, of whom 12 434 without probable dementia at baseline were included in this cognitive ancillary study. Further assessments were performed annually and at the end of study.

INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomly assigned to receive intensive treatment targeting SBP <120 mm Hg or standard treatment targeting SBP <140 mm Hg for up to five years.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary cognitive outcome was a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment. Secondary cognitive outcomes included all cause dementia, mild cognitive impairment, changes in cognitive functions, and changes in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics. A subset of participants underwent brain MRI at baseline (n=862) and at the end of study (n=605) to assess changes in white matter lesion volume and total brain volume.

RESULTS: 6219 participants were assigned to receive intensive treatment and 6215 to receive standard treatment. Baseline mean age was 63.7 years, and 5567 (44.8%) participants were women. After one year, mean SBP was 121.6 mm Hg in the intensive treatment group and 133.2 mm Hg in the standard treatment group. During a median follow-up of 3.8 years, the primary cognitive outcome of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment occurred in 747 participants (3.69 events per 100 person years) in the intensive treatment group and 783 participants (3.89 events per 100 person years) in the standard treatment group (hazard ratio 0.96, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.86 to 1.06; P=0.38). In the MRI substudy (428 intensive treatment v 434 standard treatment), the intensive treatment group had a smaller increase in white matter lesion volume compared with the standard treatment group (between group difference -0.09 inverse hyperbolic sine (asinh) transformed cm3, 95% CI -0.15 to -0.02; P=0.01).

CONCLUSIONS: Over a median of about four years, no statistically significant difference in incidence of a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment was observed among adults with type 2 diabetes receiving standard treatment of SBP (target <140 mm Hg) and intensive treatment (target <120 mm Hg). Intensive treatment was, however, associated with a reduction in the accrual of cerebral white matter lesion volume.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03808311.

From disease prevention to transmission blocking: Building the translational pathway for mucosal respiratory vaccines.
articles.abstract: Respiratory vaccines have transformed prevention of severe disease, but many provide incomplete protection against mucosal infection, carriage and onward transmission. Next-generation respiratory vaccine development should therefore treat mucosal immunity as a primary design objective rather than an exploratory add-on. In this Perspective, we outline a translational pathway for respiratory mucosal vaccines, linking rational antigen and formulation design, route-specific delivery devices, standardised airway sampling, functional mucosal assays, controlled human infection models and endpoints capturing infection, shedding and onward transmission. We argue that progress will depend not only on better immunology, but on development infrastructure capable of generating comparable mucosal data across platforms, pathogens and clinical settings. Building this pathway is essential if respiratory vaccines are to move beyond mitigation of severe disease toward prevention or reduction of mucosal infection and, ultimately, reduced onward transmission.

articles.title: Reading Hormones Through The Failing Kidney: Pitfalls in Endocrine Test Interpretation in Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) alters the clearance, protein binding, secretion and measurement of many hormones, so endocrine test results in patients with reduced kidney function often cannot be interpreted using conventional reference intervals. Misinterpretation can lead to unnecessary investigation and treatment or to missed endocrine disease. In this review, we adopt a test-centered approach to endocrine evaluation in adults with CKD stages G3-G5. We summarize how CKD affects glycemic markers, thyroid function tests, adrenal cortical and medullary tests, prolactin, the growth hormone-insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) axis, gonadal hormones and human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), parathyroid hormone (PTH) and bone turnover markers, and calcitonin and chromogranin A. For each, we identify the dominant mechanism (reduced renal clearance, altered binding proteins, genuine axis dysregulation, analytical interference, or treatment effects) and the tests that remain reliable. Key recommendations include pairing glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) with continuous glucose monitoring in advanced CKD, assessing thyroid function before dialysis and heparin, applying CKD stage-specific cut-offs to the dexamethasone suppression test, relying on renin suppression when screening for primary aldosteronism, avoiding urinary free cortisol and urinary metanephrines, interpreting PTH as a trend using a single assay, and using non-renally cleared bone turnover markers. We conclude with a practical approach that includes shared decision-making and research priorities for CKD-specific reference intervals.

articles.title: Individualized Glucocorticoid Replacement with Prednisone in Central Adrenal Insufficiency Using a Clinical Dose-Finding Algorithm.
articles.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: For over 30 years, we have treated patients with central adrenal insufficiency (CAI) using an in-house clinical algorithm (based exclusively on signs/symptoms) to individualize prednisone replacement within a predefined low dose range. The aim of this study is to describe prednisone dose distribution produced by this algorithm, determine associations between doses and patient characteristics, and compare long-term outcomes across dose groups.

METHODS: Retrospective study. Seventy-seven patients with CAI (63 years; 64% men) on long-term prednisone use were selected in their last visit (2021-2022). Long-term outcomes were extracted from records; quality of life (QoL SF-36), health events, and patient education/self-management were assessed by recent in-person questionnaires.

RESULTS: Algorithm dose distribution was 2.5mg in 70%, 3.75mg in 14%, and 5.0mg in 16% (P=0.001). Allocation to 2.5 mg was associated with older age and lower body weight/surface area (P<0.0001). No significant differences were observed, respectively, between 2.5mg and 5.0mg doses for: incidence of diabetes (P=0.74), hypertension (P=0.24), dyslipidemia (P=0.78); bone mineral density in lumbar spine (1.013 vs 0.911 g/cm2, P=0.19), total femur(0.930 vs. 0.952 g/cm2, P=0.70), and femoral neck(0.808 vs. 0.816 g/cm2, P=0.88); prevalence of weight gain (51% vs. 33%, P=0.25), weight gained [5.5(2.25-9.75) vs. 5.0(3.0-14.5)kg], health events(0.45<P<0.70), self-management of prednisone(P>0.99), and QoL(0.13<P<0.96).

CONCLUSIONS: Individualizing low-range prednisone replacement with a structured algorithm produced a dose distribution tied to patient age and body size, with comparable long-term outcomes. These findings support the use of tailored low-dose prednisone through a clinical algorithm as a safe method to avoid glucocorticoid over-and under replacement in CAI.

articles.title: Real-world effectiveness of tirzepatide in individuals with obesity: weight response, treatment-related factors and diabetes status.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tirzepatide reduces body weight and improves glycemic control, but real-world comparisons between individuals with obesity with and without type 2 diabetes (T2D) remain limited, as well as the potential influence on weight-loss response of baseline characteristics (especially sex and previous treatment exposure). We aimed to compare anthropometric and metabolic outcomes in these populations, as well as treatment persistence, discontinuation, and the influence of prior GLP-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) exposure.

METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included adults with overweight/obesity without T2D (Ob) or with T2D (ObT2D) treated with tirzepatide. Data were collected at baseline and after 2-4 (T1), 5-8 (T2), and 9-15 (T3) months. Longitudinal changes were assessed using linear mixed-effects models, and multivariable analyses identified predictors of weight loss.

RESULTS: Ob participants (n=210, 74.8% female) were younger, had higher BMI, better glycemic control, and less previous GLP-1RA exposure than ObT2D participants (n=378, 49.7% female) (45.7% vs 79.3%; p<0.001). Weight loss was greater in Ob than ObT2D at all follow-ups (-5.0% vs -2.8%, -10.1% vs -3.3%, and -14.2% vs -4.7%; all p≤0.011), with mixed-effects models confirming different trajectories. This difference was attenuated and no longer statistically significant when analyses were restricted to treatment-naïve participants. Prior GLP-1RA exposure was independently associated with lower weight loss, while an interaction between prior GLP-1RA exposure and T2D status emerged at longer follow-up. No effect modification by sex or age was clearly detectable in this cohort. Discontinuation was more frequent in Ob, with adverse events, and financial barriers among the main reported reasons. Adverse events occurred in 16.9%, were mainly mild, transient gastrointestinal events, more frequent in Ob than ObT2D (26.9% vs 11.1%; p<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Tirzepatide was effective and well tolerated in routine practice. Greater weight loss occurred in obesity without T2D, while prior GLP-1RA exposure was independently associated with a reduced weight response. Previous GLP1-RA exposure may partly account for the different weight-loss trajectories observed between obesity with and without T2D. Residual differences at longer follow-up may reflect additional unmeasured clinical, metabolic, and treatment-related factors.

articles.title: Coronary Perfusion Pressure During Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation is Associated with Outcomes from Pediatric In-hospital Cardiac Arrest.
authors: ICU-Resuscitation Project (ICU-RESUS) Investigators and the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development Collaborative Pediatric Critical Care Research Network Investigators
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multiple animal studies and one adult study establish that coronary perfusion pressure (CoPP) during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is associated with survival outcomes, such as return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). Yet, CoPP during pediatric in-hospital cardiac arrest (pIHCA) has not been investigated. We hypothesized that an average CoPP ≥20mmHg during the first 10 minutes of CPR for pIHCA would be associated with higher rates of ROSC.

METHODS: We performed a secondary analysis of the ICU-RESUScitation trial, a cluster randomized, step-wedged trial of a physiology-focused quality improvement bundle in pIHCA. Index CPR events among patients ≥37 weeks corrected gestational age and <18 years with invasive arterial blood pressure (BP) and central venous pressure (CVP) monitoring were eligible for inclusion. The primary exposure was event-level average CoPP (≥20mmHg vs <20mmHg) during the first 10 minutes of CPR; secondary exposure was CoPP <10 mmHg. The primary outcome was sustained ROSC ≥20 minutes. Multivariable modified Poisson regression with adjustment for confounders evaluated the relationship between CoPP and outcomes.

RESULTS: Among 111 included patients, median age was 0.2 years [0.0, 0.6]. Seventy-one (64%) achieved ROSC. Thirty (27%) had CoPP ≥20mmHg. Patients with CoPP ≥20mmHg were more frequently ≥1 year of age and less frequently had congenital heart disease. In adjusted models, average CoPP ≥20mmHg was associated with higher rates of ROSC (aRR 1.48 [95%CI 1.12, 1.95]; p=0.005). CoPP <10 mmHg was associated with lower rates of ROSC.

CONCLUSIONS: In this first investigation of CoPP during CPR for pIHCA, CoPP ≥20mmHg was associated with ROSC.

articles.title: Cycle-to-Cycle Prediction of Return of Spontaneous Circulation Using End-Tidal Carbon Dioxide Dynamics in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prognostication in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) commonly relies on static pre-resuscitation variables, although resuscitation is a rapidly evolving physiologic process. End-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2) is continuously available during cardiopulmonary resuscitation, but its sequential information has not been fully used for real-time prediction. We aim to develop and internally validate a cycle-to-cycle time-updated prediction model using sequential EtCO2 values to estimate the probability of return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) in the subsequent 2-minute resuscitation cycle.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective study of adult OHCA patients from the NTUH-HYCARD database between 2016 and 2023. Event-level EtCO2 sequences were extracted from resuscitation records and standardized into 2-minute intervals for up to 30 minutes, consistent with Advanced Cardiac Life Support reassessment cycles. At each prediction time point, the model used EtCO2 values available from event onset to the current time point, without using future values. A two-layer long short-term memory model estimated the probability of ROSC in the subsequent cycle. Performance was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation at two levels: the event level (one prediction per event) and the cycle level (one prediction per 2-minute cycle).

RESULTS: The final analysis included 1,651 event-level EtCO2 sequences from 1,480 patients; 583 events ended with ROSC. At the event level, the model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.876 (95% CI, 0.863-0.890) and a Brier score of 0.140 (95% CI, 0.131-0.149). When applied to every 2-minute cycle (17,029 prediction points; ROSC prevalence, 3.4%), the AUROC was 0.685 (95% CI, 0.664-0.706), and the model systematically overestimated ROSC probability (Brier score, 0.285; 95% CI, 0.268-0.303).

CONCLUSION: Sequential EtCO2 dynamics showed good event-level discrimination for predicting ROSC in the subsequent cycle. When applied at each cycle, the model retained modest discrimination but overestimated ROSC probability, indicating that recalibration is required before cycle-to-cycle use.

articles.title: Trends in Outcomes and Regional Rates of Pulmonary Thromboendarterectomy: A National Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary thromboendarterectomy (PTE) is the guideline-recommended treatment for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH). Here, we report modern-era national-level outcomes and identify regions that lack access to PTE.

METHODS: The STS Adult Cardiac Surgery Database was queried from 2012 to 2024 for patients in the USA who underwent PTE with circulatory arrest for chronic disease. Patient characteristics, region, travel distance, area deprivation index (ADI), temporal trends (2012-2018 vs 2019-2024), and center volume (≤15/year vs >15/year) were described and evaluated for association with 30-day mortality. Multivariable logistic regression was conducted, reported as adjusted odds ratios (aORs).

RESULTS: Over the study period, 4,101 PTEs were performed; 1,238 in 2012-2018 and 2,863 in 2019-2024. Between the two periods, 25 centers closed and 35 centers opened. Higher volume centers (>15 PTE/ year) had significantly lower 30-day post-operative mortality rates compared to lower-volume centers (2.6% vs. 5.5%, p<0.001) including after adjustment for preoperative characteristics, ADI, and patient travel distance, low center volume (aOR=1.81, p<0.001). Patients from the Mountain and Great Lakes regions had the highest rate of PTE, while patients from the East South Central region appeared to have disparately low access to PTE.

CONCLUSIONS: The volume-outcome relationship for 30-day mortality after PTE persists over time and there is regional variation in rates of PTE. Development of regional centers of excellence is imperative to ensure access to high-quality CTEPH treatment.

articles.title: Trends and Variation in Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Use for Myocarditis in the U.S. (2015-2025).
Prognostic Value of Tissue Doppler Late Diastolic Velocity (TDI-a') in Patients with Severe Aortic Stenosis Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
articles.abstract: Risk stratification after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) in severe aortic stenosis (AS) remains suboptimal. Beyond valvular hemodynamics, a number of standard echocardiographic parameters of function are associated to outcome. Mitral annular late diastolic velocity (TDI-a') is proven to have prognostic value in multiple clinical settings, but its role after TAVI is unresolved. In a single-center retrospective observational study we included adult patients with isolated severe AS (aortic valve area < 1.0 cm²) undergoing TAVI, between December 2013 and August 2025. Pre-procedural transthoracic echocardiography was reviewed offline by blinded investigators to measure TDI-a' velocities. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Logistic regression, Cox proportional hazards models, and ROC analysis were performed. A total of 805 patients (median age 81 years; 44.8% male) were included. During a median follow-up of 36.5 months, 196 deaths (24.3%) occurred. On univariable analysis, left ventricular ejection fraction, E/e' ratio, left atrioventricular coupling index (LACI), and TDI-a' were associated with mortality. In multivariable analysis, average TDI-a' remained the only independent echocardiographic predictor of mortality in both logistic regression (OR 0.88, 95% CI 0.821-0.944; p < 0.001) and Cox analysis (HR 0.934, 95% CI 0.881-0.991; p = 0.023). ROC analysis showed modest discrimination (AUC 0.585), with an optimal cut-off ≤ 8.4 cm/s (sensitivity 65%, specificity 49%). Reduced TDI-a' is independently associated with mortality after TAVI, beyond conventional echocardiographic predictors. Despite modest discrimination, it is a simple prognostic marker that may improve pre-procedural risk stratification and warrants further prospective validation.

articles.title: County-Level Poverty, Primary Care Availability, and Trends in Adult Preventable Hospitalizations: A Multi-State Analysis, 2013-2023.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To examine trends in preventable hospitalizations (PH) across multiple states and evaluate associations between county-level poverty and primary care physician (PCP) availability and rates of preventable hospitalizations in US counties.

METHODS: A repeated cross-sectional analysis was conducted to examine county-level adult PH rates overall and by subtype (acute, chronic, diabetes-related), as well as trends in PHs over time. Data from Health Care Utilization Project (HCUP) State Inpatient Databases from 13 states from 2013-2023 were analyzed in 2025 and yielded 9,691 county-year observations from 881 counties. Negative binomial models were used to estimate associations between PCP availability, poverty rate, and PH outcomes while controlling for county demographics, rurality, and year.

RESULTS: From 2013-2023, age-adjusted acute PH rates decreased substantially, and chronic PH rates declined moderately, while diabetes-related PH increased significantly through 2019 before declining modestly. In adjusted models, high-poverty counties experienced 79% higher PH rates versus low-poverty counties (IRR: 1.79, 95% CI: 1.38-2.31), and the highest PCP tertile counties had 14% lower PH rates than the lowest tertile (IRR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.80-0.93).

CONCLUSIONS: Higher county-level poverty and lower PCP availability were associated with increased adult PH rates, particularly chronic and diabetes-related hospitalizations. These findings highlight the importance of structural socioeconomic conditions and local primary care resources in understanding variation in potentially avoidable hospitalizations.

articles.title: Curcumin-mediated antimicrobial photodynamic therapy attenuates MRSA skin infection in hyperuricemic mice.
articles.abstract: Hyperuricemia is associated with chronic inflammation, redox imbalance, and alterations in innate immune responses that may influence susceptibility to bacterial infections. Whether antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT) retains its antibacterial activity under hyperuricemic conditions remains poorly understood. This study evaluated curcumin-mediated aPDT against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) skin infection in hyperuricemic mice. Hyperuricemia was induced in BALB/c mice by intraperitoneal administration of potassium oxonate, followed by intradermal MRSA infection in the left ear. Infected hyperuricemic animals received topical curcumin (100 μg), followed by blue LED irradiation (13.5 J/cm2). Curcumin-mediated aPDT significantly reduced viable bacterial burden in regional draining lymph nodes by approximately 2.44 log10 CFU/mL compared with untreated hyperuricemic infected animals. Treatment was also associated with changes in cutaneous lesion parameters and inflammatory-cell infiltration. MPO immunohistochemistry revealed variations in tissue immunoreactivity, without a corresponding reduction in MPO-positive area in treated animals relative to untreated hyperuricemic infected mice. In draining lymph nodes, aPDT was associated with reductions in IL-17A (∼75%; HINF/HIPDT p=0.0472) and an increase in IL-10 (∼260%; HINF/HIPDT p=0.0176), whereas TNF-α and IL-1β exhibited a non-significant numerical reduction of approximately 29 and 50%, respectively. These findings demonstrate that curcumin-mediated aPDT retains antibacterial activity in hyperuricemic mice and is associated with modulation of regional inflammatory mediators. Further studies are warranted to characterize bacterial clearance at the primary infection site and determine whether hyperuricemia modifies treatment responsiveness.

articles.title: Differential expression of Galectin-7 in the clinical course of arboviral diseases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: We evaluated Galectin-7 (Gal-7) production and its correlation with clinical arboviral disease parameters, exploring both, its role as a host molecule acting during the effector response and its potential as a new biomarker in arboviral diseases.

METHODS: We determined serum Gal-7 levels in patients with confirmed dengue, chikungunya, and Zika infection. We compared serum Gal-7 levels across symptom-day-defined clinical phases and their correlation with hematological/biochemical parameters. We used ROC curves to evaluate Gal-7, both individually and alongside Glutamic Oxaloacetic Transaminase (GOT), as biomarkers to distinguish healthy individuals from patients and to discriminate between arboviruses.

RESULTS: Serum Gal-7 levels were significantly higher in patients with dengue and chikungunya compared to those with Zika or healthy controls. In dengue patients, Gal-7 positively correlated with clinical signs like exanthema and hematological parameters, specifically lymphocytes and basophils. This Gal-7 elevation was evident within the first five days of symptom onset in dengue patients. While Gal-7 effectively discriminated dengue patients from healthy controls, it had limited ability to differentiate among the three arboviruses. However, combining Gal-7 with GOT into a dual-marker diagnostic panel significantly enhanced the differentiation of dengue virus infections from both Zika and Chikungunya.

CONCLUSIONS: Our results demonstrate, for the first time, significant elevations in Gal-7 serum levels in dengue and chikungunya but not Zika patients. When integrated into a dual-marker panel with GOT, it offers a robust diagnostic tool for the accurate differential discrimination of co-circulating arboviruses.

articles.title: Loss of Macrophage-Derived Wnt Signaling Coupled with mTORC1-Mediated Inhibition of β-Catenin Activation Drives Acute Liver Injury in Severe Ehrlichiosis.
articles.abstract: Severe ehrlichiosis is characterized by fulminant acute liver injury that frequently culminates in multi-organ failure, yet the mechanisms governing defective hepatic regeneration remain poorly understood. Using complementary in vitro systems and established murine models of mild (Ehrlichia muris) and severe (Ehrlichia japonica) infection, we identified differential regulation of the canonical Wnt/β-catenin pathway as a central determinant of disease outcome. Mild E. muris infection elicited robust activation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling through macrophage-derived Wnt ligands, promoting β-catenin nuclear translocation in hepatocytes, transcription of regenerative target genes, and marked hepatocyte proliferation. In contrast, severe E. japonica infection profoundly suppressed Wnt/β-catenin signaling despite extensive hepatic macrophage accumulation, resulting in impaired liver regeneration, progressive liver injury, and fatal disease. Mechanistically, this suppression was driven by diminished macrophage-derived Wnt ligand production, aberrant hepatocyte mTORC1 activation that inhibited β-catenin signaling, and potentially the absence of a Wnt-mimetic Ehrlichia effector capable of engaging Frizzled receptors and sustaining regenerative signaling. Therapeutically, pharmacologic activation of β-catenin combined with doxycycline treatment of E. japonica infected mice restored canonical Wnt signaling, reduced bacterial burden and hepatic injury, and significantly improved survival. Collectively, these findings establish impaired Wnt/β-catenin signaling as a pivotal mechanism underlying impaired liver regeneration during severe ehrlichiosis and identify restoration of this pathway as a promising host-directed therapeutic strategy that complements antimicrobial therapy by simultaneously promoting pathogen clearance and hepatic repair.

articles.title: Unintended methanogenesis associated with spatial niche disruption: Re-evaluating permanganate dosing strategies in sewer sediments.
articles.abstract: Mitigating sewer sulfide and methane emissions demands dosing strategies that account for sediment depth-dependent microbiomes and diffusion limits. While conventional "shock dosing" effectively controls sulfide, this study reveals a critical overlooked risk: it inadvertently stimulates deep-sediment methanogenesis. The efficacy and mechanisms of daily low-dose versus single high-dose shock potassium permanganate (PM) strategies were investigated. Single high-dose dosing effectively suppressed sulfide production but was associated with higher effluent methane concentrations (2.0-4.3 mg/L) than daily low-dose dosing (0.6-1.7 mg/L), potentially due to altered sediment niches and increased methanogenic potential in deeper layers. In contrast, daily low-dose dosing reduced sulfide and methane production by approximately 50%. Sulfide suppression was associated with reduced surface sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) abundance, whereas methane mitigation was linked to the downward transport and accumulation of in situ-generated colloidal Mn(IV), which maintained a Mn(IV) fraction of approximately 34% across the sediment profile. By integrating depth-resolved physicochemical profiles with stratified microbial analyses, this work highlights the necessity of transitioning from conventional shock strategy to intelligent, continuous application for optimized sewer management.

articles.title: Advanced Thinking and Reasoning Paradigms in the Architecture of Preclinical and Clinical Pharmacology Research.
articles.abstract: To conduct scientific research, researchers need methodological expertise and a range of cognitive skills. Nevertheless, researchers treat these cognitive processes implicitly and do not regard them as an explicit element of research methodology. This article examines the structure of scientific inquiry, focusing on thinking: creative, divergent, lateral, vertical, convergent, critical, Janusian, and reasoning: abductive, deductive, inductive. It examines how these processes identify knowledge gaps, formulate research questions and hypotheses, select study designs, and interpret evidence. Instead of viewing thinking and reasoning as sequential stages, we propose an integrated, iterative approach in which these processes interact at all stages of the research cycle. This framework addresses the cognitive gap between conceptualizing a research problem and conducting a study. It also stresses that methodological accuracy, reproducibility, and dependability depend on the quality of the cognitive decisions that accompany experimental and clinical investigation. Since artificial intelligence is widely used to speed up literature analysis, hypothesis generation, data analysis, and experimental design, human judgment is still needed to assess the significance of the questions, the plausibility of the explanations, the validity of the study designs, and the adequacy of the evidence. This article provides a unified conceptual structure for incorporating thinking and reasoning processes in preclinical and clinical research.

articles.title: Sympathetic neuroeffector remodeling and cardiomyocyte ferroptosis in heart failure: A stage- and compartment-specific framework for β-adrenergic/cAMP signaling.
articles.abstract: Heart failure is characterized by sympathetic remodeling, altered myocardial adrenergic responsiveness, and cardiomyocyte injury, with ferroptosis emerging as a potential contributor to adverse cardiac remodeling.
