This review proposes a dynamic "sympathetic-ferroptosis continuum" within a "nerve terminal-cardiomyocyte" dual-compartment framework linking cardiac sympathetic dysfunction, β1-adrenergic receptor (β1-AR)/cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) signaling, and cardiomyocyte ferroptosis susceptibility. Sustained sympathetic drive can coexist with altered norepinephrine (NE) homeostasis at cardiac nerve terminals and myocardial β1-AR desensitization, creating a functional mismatch between sympathetic activity and myocardial signaling responsiveness. At sympathetic nerve terminals, altered β1-AR/cAMP signaling may influence tyrosine hydroxylase-dependent NE synthesis and synapsin 1/RIM1α-associated vesicle mobilization and release, alongside changes in NE transporter-mediated reuptake. In cardiomyocytes, dysregulated compartment-specific cAMP signaling may affect YAP-associated iron homeostasis, LPCAT3-mediated phospholipid remodeling, SLC7A11/GSH/GPX4-dependent antioxidant defenses, and NOX4-related oxidative stress, thereby modifying ferroptosis susceptibility. Together, these pathways provide an integrated mechanistic framework linking neurocardiac signaling imbalance with cardiomyocyte ferroptosis susceptibility. This framework identifies potential targets for preserving adaptive cAMP signaling, improving sympathetic neurotransmitter homeostasis, and limiting ferroptosis-related injury, providing new directions for compartment-specific cardioprotective strategies in heart failure.

articles.title: Net Prolongation of Life with Ventricular Assist Device Support in Teenagers: Are We There Yet?
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
articles.abstract: Heart transplantation prolongs survival in children with end-stage heart disease, yet a single donor heart does not provide a normal lifespan. Contemporary graft survival for teenagers is approximately 15 years, the shortest of any pediatric age group, and re-transplantation remains uncommon. For most patients, the first allograft is the only allograft. Recent adult data demonstrating survival with durable mechanical circulatory support comparable to transplantation raise an important question for adolescents: could intentionally extending ventricular assist device (VAD) support through the teenage years, with transplantation deferred to adulthood, increase total life-years? This perspective examines that hypothesis for adolescents with dilated cardiomyopathy. We review the heightened risks of rejection, graft loss, and treatment nonadherence during adolescence; contemporary outcomes with dischargeable durable VADs in children; the potential for myocardial recovery during extended support; and organ allocation policies that may unintentionally discourage a prolonged-support strategy. We also examine patient and family perspectives and discuss unresolved questions regarding stroke risk, allosensitization, long-term quality of life, and optimal timing of transplantation. No prospective data currently support intentional long-term VAD support as a bridge to transplantation in teenagers, and this concept should be viewed as a hypothesis rather than a practice recommendation. However, for carefully selected adolescents who are clinically stable on durable VAD support, delayed transplantation may be a reasonable topic for shared decision-making discussions while acknowledging the substantial uncertainties that remain. As durable device technology continues to improve, evaluating whether prolonged VAD support can achieve net prolongation of life in teenagers warrants prospective investigation.

articles.title: Measured Left Ventricular Mass Ratio for Size-Matching Identifies Graft Failure Risk in Obese Heart Transplantation.
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal donor-recipient size-matching in heart transplantation with obese donors and/or recipients remains uncertain. We sought to validate the measured left ventricular mass (mLVM) ratio using local donor hospital echocardiograms, determine whether obesity modifies the association with 1-year graft failure compared to the predicted heart mass (PHM), and assess the clinical implications of discordance.

METHODS: The Donor Heart Study prospectively collected echocardiograms from donation-after-brain-death donors. The associations of local mLVM ratio (donor measured LVM/recipient predicted LVM) and PHM ratio with 1-year graft failure (death or retransplantation) were assessed by adjusted Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic splines with obesity interaction terms.

RESULTS: Among 2,036 heart transplants, size-matching ratios differed significantly by metric within and across obesity groups (all p<0.001). Obesity significantly modified the association between mLVM ratio and 1-year graft failure (interaction: p=0.009), but not PHM ratio. In obese transplants, the mLVM ratio demonstrated a U-shaped (nonlinear interaction: p=0.011) association with 1-year graft failure, with significant adjusted risk at low and high mLVM ratios; where the mLVM ratio captured a unique phenotype associated with graft failure when oversized (>1.20, aHR: 2.50 [95% CI: 1.30-4.82]). Reclassification from PHM to mLVM ratio improved risk classification by 10.4% and concordantly abnormal PHM and mLVM ratios more than doubled the risk of graft failure (aHR: 2.15 [95% CI: 1.10-4.22]) in obese transplantation.

CONCLUSION: In obese transplants, locally derived mLVM ratio may identify high-risk donor-recipient mismatches not captured by the PHM ratio, with increased graft failure risk at both low and high mLVM ratios.

articles.title: Autophagy negatively regulates apoptosis in Bacillus Calmette-Guérin-infected macrophages.
articles.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection triggers immune responses in macrophages. Autophagy and apoptosis, two critical cellular processes, are essential for host clearance of pathogens. However, the relationship between autophagy and apoptosis in Mtb-infected macrophages remains unclear. In this study, Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) was used to induce autophagy and apoptosis in RAW264.7 macrophages, aiming to investigate the regulatory effect of autophagy on BCG-induced apoptosis in RAW264.7 macrophages. In this study, the mouse macrophages line RAW264.7 was used to establish a BCG infection model to evaluate cellular autophagy and apoptosis. The autophagy activator Rapamycin (RAPA) and inhibitor 3-Methyladenine (3-MA) were used to intervene in autophagy, and siRNA was used to silence the key autophagy gene Atg5, after which changes in macrophages autophagy and apoptosis were analyzed. The results showed that BCG infection significantly upregulated the expression of LC3-II, Beclin1, Atg5, and Atg12 in RAW264.7 cells, decreased p62 levels, and increased the numbers of intracellular autophagosomes and autolysosomes. Meanwhile, BCG infection can also induce cell apoptosis, manifested by the upregulation of Bax, Caspase 3, and PARP1 expression, the downregulation of Bcl-2 expression, and an increased apoptosis rate. However, RAPA further promoted autophagy and inhibited apoptosis in BCG-infected RAW264.7 cells, whereas 3-MA and siRNA-Atg5 had the opposite effects, inhibiting autophagy and promoting apoptosis in BCG-infected RAW264.7 cells. This suggests that autophagy may be involved in regulating BCG-induced apoptosis of RAW264.7 cells, and that an antagonistic relationship may exist between autophagy and apoptosis, providing new insights for understanding the pathogenesis of tuberculosis and identifying targets for drug intervention.

articles.title: The Complementary Impact of Amino Acid PET with Diffusion and Perfusion MRI for Glioblastoma Tumor Delineation.
articles.journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While standard MRI imaging is known to underestimate glioblastoma tumor extent, advanced imaging techniques including 18-FDOPA PET, dynamic contrast enhanced (DCE) perfusion MRI, and diffusion weighted MRI (DWI) have been utilized on clinical trials to identify tumor within and beyond gadolinium enhancement for radiation targeting. This clinical trial analysis quantifies how DCE, DWI and 18-FDOPA PET identify tumor beyond standard imaging, and whether these techniques are complementary and feasible.

METHODS: Patients with newly diagnosed glioblastoma enrolled on a phase II clinical trial underwent pre-radiation 18-FDOPA PET/CT, DCE, DWI, and standard MRI sequences. Tumor volumes were separately delineated using each imaging modality and incorporated into radiation target volumes, and were compared for overlapping and non-overlapping segments.

RESULTS: In 153 enrolled patients included in this analysis, tumor was identified beyond conventionally used radiation volume expansions of 5-, 10-, 15-, and 20 mm from standard MRI tumor volumes in 86%, 56%, 38% and 20% of patients, respectively. Advanced imaging techniques identified partially overlapping tumor volumes; PET identified tumor outside of the advanced MRI subvolumes in 88%, while DWI and DCE identified tumor outside of standard MRI and PET in 95% cases, indicating these imaging techniques are complementary.

CONCLUSIONS: Advanced imaging techniques including DCE, DWI, and 18-FDOPA PET allow complementary delineation of glioblastoma beyond contrast-enhancing tumor from standard MRI, and may be most valuable when used in combination. These advanced imaging methods can potentially facilitate accurate tumor targeting with reduced CTV expansions to spare normal tissue and enable safe hypofractionated radiation therapy.

articles.title: Step change in glaucoma polygenic risk score performance enables clinical utility.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Open-angle glaucoma (OAG) is the leading cause of irreversible blindness and is highly heritable. Despite effective treatments, approximately 50% of cases remain undiagnosed. We aimed to develop and validate a clinically applicable, genetics-based risk prediction tool for OAG across diverse ancestries.

DESIGN: Genetic association study and risk prediction analysis.

PARTICIPANTS: More than 6 million individuals contributing genome-wide association study data from multiple ancestry groups.

METHODS: We constructed a comprehensive polygenic risk score (PRS) for OAG using a multitrait modeling framework that integrated glaucoma-related traits, including intraocular pressure, optic disc parameters, and ocular hypertension. PRS performance was evaluated for OAG risk across major ancestry groups and assessed for associations with age at diagnosis, treatment escalation, surgical outcomes, and familial risk.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Odds ratios (ORs) for OAG by PRS percentile, age at disease onset, absolute risk estimates, treatment escalation, glaucoma surgery, and OAG risk in first-degree relatives.

RESULTS: In Australian individuals of European ancestry, those in the top 10% of the PRS distribution had a 10-fold increased risk of OAG compared with the remainder (OR 10.04, 95% CI 7.43-13.59), substantially outperforming our previously published PRS (OR 4.2). Similar performance was observed in U.S. European ancestry data (OR 9.09, 95% CI 5.09-16.26). In UK Biobank Europeans the OR for the top 10% versus the remainder was 4.91 (95% CI 4.25-5.69). Although performance was attenuated in other ancestry groups (OR top 10% vs. remainder: 4.01 in South Asian, 3.39 in East Asian, and ranging from 2.26 to 3.81 in African ancestry populations depending on cohort), high PRS percentiles corresponded to elevated absolute risk across all groups. On average, individuals in the highest-risk decile developed glaucoma approximately 25 years earlier than those in the lowest decile and had ∼100-fold (OR 96.83, 95% CI 52.61-178.21) higher risk. The PRS also predicted treatment escalation in early disease, prevalent and incident glaucoma surgery, and OAG risk among first-degree relatives.

CONCLUSIONS: This enhanced PRS, available for clinical use through an accredited genotyping workflow, enables effective risk stratification for OAG across diverse ancestries, facilitating earlier identification and treatment of high-risk individuals while supporting resource rationalisation for those at low risk. Performance is strongest in European ancestry populations, and further work is needed to improve equity of performance across ancestries.

articles.title: A useful failure? Requiem for the middle child of heart failure.
MhAFB2-MhIAA1_like module mediates auxin-associated modulation of apple immunity against Alternaria alternata.
articles.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
articles.abstract: Alternaria alternata is a devastating pathogenic fungus in apple, leading to leaf necrosis and premature defoliation. Although auxin signaling is known to participate in plant immunity, the specific roles of the TIR1/AFB-Aux/IAA signaling module in apple-pathogen interactions remain largely elusive. Here, we identified and characterized MhAFB2 (a TIR1/AFB auxin receptor homolog) and MhIAA1_like (an Aux/IAA transcriptional repressor homolog) cloned from Malus hupehensis. Protein interaction assays, including yeast two-hybrid, GST pull-down, BiFC, and LCI, demonstrated that MhAFB2 interacted with MhIAA1_like in an auxin-dependent or auxin-promoted manner, exhibiting a more robust and readily detectable interaction tendency compared to MhTIR1. Using transgenic 'Orin' calli and transiently transformed 'Gala' leaves as the functional evaluation system, we conducted genetic manipulation that revealed distinct disease phenotypes. MhAFB2 overexpression compromised apple resistance to A. alternata, whereas the RNAi-mediated silencing conferred an enhancement. Conversely, overexpression of MhIAA1_like significantly restricted lesion expansion, while its silencing increased the susceptibility. These altered disease phenotypes were tightly coupled with physiological and transcriptional defense responses. Resistant lines maintained higher levels of H2O2 accumulation and exhibited elevated expression of key salicylic acid- (PR1, PAD4, and EDS1), jasmonic acid-, and ethylene- defense pathway genes, whereas susceptible lines showed opposite patterns alongside increased expression of early auxin-responsive genes (GH3.1 and ARF4). Furthermore, exogenous indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) treatment suppresses immune responses primed by A. alternata infection, an effect that is partially attenuated upon MhAFB2 silencing. Together, these findings reveal that MhAFB2 and MhIAA1_like act as core components in the auxin-associated modulation of apple immunity, and the MhAFB2-MhIAA1_like module is involved in coordinating the balance between auxin signaling and multi-hormone-associated defenses, providing new insights into the roles of auxin receptor-repressor pairs in fine-tuning plant immune responses.

articles.title: Risk Assessment for Transmission of Porcine Endogenous Retrovirus in Clinical Xenotransplantation.
articles.journal: American journal of transplantation : official journal of the American Society of Transplantation and the American Society of Transplant Surgeons
articles.abstract: Porcine to human xenotransplantation clinical trials are underway. Concerns remain regarding potential transmission of infections including porcine endogenous retroviruses (PERVs) to human xenotransplant recipients with adverse health outcomes. All pigs contain subtypes PERV-A and PERV-B, and some also carry PERV-C. Human cells carry receptors for PERV-A and -B but not for PERV-C. PERV-A can recombine with PERV-B to form PERV-A/B hybrids and recombine with PERV-C to form PERV-A/C hybrids in vivo and in vitro. No evidence of PERV transmission to non-human primates or other laboratory animals, human primary cells, or to humans from surgical or non-surgical exposures has been reported, although transmission of PERV A/C hybrids has been observed in certain permissive transformed human cell lines. PERV inactivation has been achieved via genetic editing in some pig lines. Here, we review the data related to the potential for PERV infection in human xenograft recipients based on published data on PERV structure and host cellular and species tropisms. Despite the lack of evidence regarding transmissibility of PERVs to humans, we advocate the rigorous monitoring of patients and, possibly, their close contacts in initial clinical trials for possible PERV transmission following xenotransplantation.

articles.title: Anthropometry, Body Composition, and Airway Dysanapsis in Youth with and without Asthma.
articles.journal: Annals of allergy, asthma & immunology : official publication of the American College of Allergy, Asthma, & Immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity has been associated with airway dysanapsis, but it is unclear if this is driven by adiposity measures beyond body mass index (BMI).

OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between body composition, adiposity distribution, and dysanapsis in youth with and without asthma.

METHODS: We analyzed data from Genomics of Obesity and Asthma (GenOA), a case-control study of obesity-related asthma in youths aged 6-20 years. In addition to BMI, we measured waist and hip circumference, skin fold thickness, and percent body fat (PBF) and basal metabolic rate (BMR) by bioelectrical impedance. Dysanapsis was defined as normal FEV1 (z-score ≥ LLN), normal-to-high FVC (z-score ≥0.674), and low FEV1/FVC (<80%). The dysanapsis ratio (DR) was calculated as FEF25-75/FVC. We used multivariable regression models to obtain odds ratios (ORs) or beta coefficients and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: 139 GenOA participants were included in the analysis (mean age=14 years, 46% female, 18% non-White, 16.5% with dysanapsis). We found higher odds of dysanapsis with higher BMI (OR=1.33 [95%CI=1.02-1.77], p=0.036), BMR (OR=1.60 [1.12-2.39], p=0.009), waist circumference (WC, OR=1.54 [1.10-2.21], p=0.012), and waist-to-height ratio (WHtR, OR=1.54 [1.10-2.22], p=0.012) z-scores. Similarly, higher BMI, BMR, WC, and WHtR z-scores were associated with ∼2.3% to 3.5% lower DR (i.e. more dysanapsis). We found significant effect modification by sex, with most significant results in female participants. We found no effect modification by asthma status.

CONCLUSION: Anthropometry and body composition indices were associated with dysanapsis in youth with and without asthma. Notably, most significant results were driven by female participants.

articles.title: Challenges and prospects for applying pseudomonas and chromobacterium in biological pest control programs.
articles.abstract: The use of microorganisms for biological pest control has expanded considerably, but practical applications of non-spore-forming Gram-negative bacteria remain limited compared with Bacillus thuringiensis. Among them, Pseudomonas and Chromobacterium species have attracted attention for their insecticidal activity against pests across several orders. This review examines current knowledge on these genera, focusing on modes of action, efficacy, production constraints, and safety aspects relevant to large-scale pest management. A systematic survey identified 60 studies on Pseudomonas and 36 on Chromobacterium published up to April 2026. Evidence indicates that both genera display multifactorial pathogenicity, involving bacterial cells, secreted metabolites, toxins, enzymes, and secretion systems. Research on Pseudomonas has advanced substantially, particularly regarding infection mechanisms, ecological interactions, and virulence factors such as Fit toxins, monalysin, hydrogen cyanide, chitinases, and cyclic lipopeptides. In contrast, Chromobacterium remains less characterized, although insecticidal compounds such as hydrogen cyanide, violacein, GNIP1Aa, and chitinase-like enzymes have been reported. Despite these advances, most studies were conducted under laboratory conditions using artificial infection routes, such as injection or incorporation into artificial diets, which poorly reflect field exposure. Field trials are scarce and have produced inconsistent results, especially for commercial products based on Chromobacterium subtsugae. Key bottlenecks include limited knowledge of production processes, low-cost industrial media, formulation strategies, shelf life, and economically viable application rates. Safety must also be carefully assessed, as some species from both genera are associated with opportunistic infections in vertebrates. Overall, the practical use of Pseudomonas and Chromobacterium requires integrated efforts in genomics, microbiology, fermentation, formulation, and biosafety.

articles.title: A unifying perspective on EBV-triggered CNS autoimmune diseases: from permissive conditions to intrathecal B-cell activation.
articles.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is a major environmental risk factor for multiple sclerosis (MS) and has also been linked-though with limited evidence-to other central nervous system (CNS) autoimmune diseases. The paradox of ubiquitous infection yet rare disease, along with fragmented hypotheses (molecular mimicry, Pender, Aloisi, driver, and hit-and-run hypotheses), highlights the need for a unifying model. Here, we propose a hypothetical "permissive-to-intrathecal activation model" in which genetic susceptibility, age at primary infection, and environmental exposures collectively lead to immune control failure of EBV-infected B cells (impaired immune surveillance and self-tolerance), allowing them to reprogram, migrate to the CNS, and become the central pathological hub, where intrathecal B-cell activation drives T-cell-mediated injury. Within this model, existing hypotheses can be integrated as specific components of this cascade. Based on the model, we outline three therapeutic strategies (primary prevention, EBV-directed, and B-cell-directed). Beyond MS, its core concepts-permissive conditions, immune control failure, and intrathecal activation-might provide a conceptual framework for other EBV-associated CNS autoimmune diseases, including neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD), myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD), and autoimmune glial fibrillary acidic protein astrocytopathy (GFAP-A), despite limited epidemiological evidence. In this framework, disease-specific permissive conditions shape distinct patterns of immune control failure, which determines EBV's divergent roles, while intrathecal B-cell activation remains a shared process. This review may advance mechanistic understanding of EBV-driven CNS autoimmunity and provide a theoretical basis for precision intervention.

articles.title: The MDA5-RNA-autoantibody axis in anti-MDA5 dermatomyositis: Structural biology, pathogenic mechanisms, and mechanism-guided therapy.
articles.abstract: Anti-MDA5+ dermatomyositis is among the most severe subtypes of idiopathic inflammatory myopathy, characterized by a vasculopathic skin phenotype and a high risk of rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease (RP-ILD). Mortality is not a single fixed value: it varies with the presence of RP-ILD, age, oxygenation, pulmonary function, ferritin, inflammatory status, disease severity at enrolment, treatment, and the time point at which outcomes are assessed, and exceeds 50% at 6-months in patients who progress to respiratory failure. The autoantigen MDA5 is a cytosolic dsRNA sensor that assembles cooperatively into helical filaments on long duplexes and nucleates MAVS-driven type I interferon signaling. Anti-MDA5 antibody titer tracks disease activity and treatment response, the type I interferon signature is elevated in blood, skin and muscle, and IFIH1 gain-of-function mutations that stabilize MDA5 filaments on endogenous RNA cause interferonopathies that share a mechanistic node-impaired filament turnover-with this disease, although their clinical phenotypes differ substantially. This review synthesizes structural, genetic, immunological, and therapeutic evidence to reframe anti-MDA5+ DM as an acquired, autoantibody-amplified disorder of MDA5-RNA sensing. We propose a dual-axis hypothesis: an intracellular route, which is a structural prediction that has not been experimentally validated, in which antibody binding may modulate MDA5 filament dynamics; and an extracellular route, supported by peer-reviewed evidence that RNA-containing anti-MDA5 immune complexes induce IFN-α and, for its FcγRI-dependent uptake and multi-sensor amplification steps, by preliminary findings reported in a preprint, in which MDA5-RNA-antibody complexes are captured by Fcγ receptor-expressing cells. The framework is consistent with existing clinical and mechanistic data and identifies four candidate therapeutic nodes: antibody clearance, FcγR/TLR blockade, RLR modulation, and JAK-STAT inhibition. Among current therapies, JAK inhibition is supported by the strongest available comparative evidence, although that evidence is observational and of low certainty rather than randomized. The medium-term agenda requires structural validation of the intracellular axis, mapping of the self-dsRNA ligand pool, and randomized trials of antibody- and Fc-receptor-directed therapies. TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Anti-MDA5+ dermatomyositis is associated with a high risk of rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease and substantial early mortality, particularly in patients with severe or progressive lung disease. We propose that a type I interferon amplification loop, sustained by MDA5-RNA-autoantibody immune complexes, is central to this process. On the basis of observational, non-randomized comparative evidence, we suggest that a JAK inhibitor be considered early as part of combination induction therapy in patients with active or progressive interstitial lung disease, and that antibody-directed therapy be escalated in those with persistent or rising autoantibody titers. These are author-proposed recommendations derived from low-certainty evidence; randomized comparative data are not yet available.

articles.title: Acute deltamethrin exposure impairs resistance against bacterial and viral infections by compromising the gill-intestinal mucosal barriers in black carp (Mylopharyngodon piceus).
articles.abstract: Previous studies have examined deltamethrin (DEL) toxicity in individual mucosal organs. However, few have assessed its effects on both gill and intestinal barriers alongside resistance to bacterial and viral infections. This study examined gill and intestinal responses in black carp (Mylopharyngodon piceus) exposed to DEL at 0.75 or 1.22 μg/L for 48 and 96 h. DEL caused epithelial injury in the gills and intestine, with earlier and more pronounced lesions in the gills. At 96 h, superoxide dismutase and glutathione peroxidase activities and malondialdehyde levels increased in both tissues. DEL reduced tight junction gene expression and altered the transcript levels of caspase-1, caspase-3, and IL-1β and corresponding protein levels, with responses varying by tissue and time. The relative abundance of Acinetobacter spp. increased in both tissues at 96 h. Following DEL exposure at 1.22 μg/L for 96 h, mortality after Aeromonas hydrophila and grass carp reovirus (GCRV) challenge increased from 30% to 60% and from 40% to 70%, respectively, accompanied by reduced expression of several immune genes relative to infection alone. These findings demonstrate that acute DEL exposure disrupts mucosal homeostasis and increases disease susceptibility, supporting the inclusion of mucosal health and infection outcomes in pesticide safety assessments in aquaculture.

articles.title: Management of Orthostatic Hypotension in Hospitalised Patients: Empirical Evidence, Expert Opinion, and Open Questions.
articles.abstract: Orthostatic hypotension (OH) is prevalent yet underappreciated among hospitalised adults, affecting more than two-thirds of older inpatients and carrying a considerable burden of falls, cardiovascular events, mortality, prolonged hospitalisations, and readmissions. This article presents practical frameworks for inpatient OH evaluation and management. Standardised measurement protocols and a systematic diagnostic approach aid in identifying neurogenic and non-neurogenic causes. Medication review and nonpharmacological interventions-including fluid administration, behavioural modifications, compression garments, and graduated mobilisation-form the cornerstones of management. Pharmacotherapy should be reserved for refractory cases, guided by autonomic phenotype and side-effect profiles. Coexistent supine hypertension warrants careful consideration. Disposition planning, patient education, and structured follow-up are essential components of care. Important knowledge gaps persist: inpatient OH phenotypes are incompletely characterised, evidence for inpatient interventions is sparse, and validated discharge frameworks are lacking. Greater clinical awareness and translational research are needed to improve outcomes for this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Usefulness of the Current of Injury Function in a Pacing System Analyzers for Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing Implantation : A Case Report.
articles.abstract: During left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP), the current of injury (COI) follows a characteristic depth-dependent course: it rises as the lead advances through the interventricular septum, then falls as the tip approaches the left ventricular endocardium. This transition has been proposed as a practical procedural endpoint. Such monitoring has conventionally required an electrophysiology (EP) laboratory system, as pacing system analyzers (PSAs) were thought to lack real-time capability. This report describes a 76-year-old man with complete atrioventricular block and preserved ejection fraction (70%) who underwent LBBAP because a high pacing burden was anticipated. An INGEVITY lead and SSPC NXT guiding catheter were used, with simultaneous recording by an EP system and a Boston Scientific PSA equipped with beat-by-beat COI monitoring and a reference-waveform storage function. After the initial screw-in, the COI waveform was stored as a reference at the right ventricular septal position. During subsequent body turns, the COI rose sharply relative to this reference and then declined within tens of seconds. Lead V1 showed a right bundle branch block-like morphology with stable threshold and impedance, and this position was accepted as final. Waveforms from the PSA and the EP system showed comparable temporal patterns. Because absolute COI amplitude varies widely between patients, within-patient comparison against a stored reference allows assessment not only of whether the COI has begun to fall, but how far it has fallen - relevant to the risk of endocardial penetration. Limitations include the single-case design and absence of quantitative analysis.

articles.title: Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Infants With Omphalocele: A Contemporary ELSO Registry Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Omphalocele is a rare congenital abdominal wall defect frequently associated with pulmonary hypoplasia, pulmonary hypertension, congenital heart disease, and severe respiratory failure. Infants with omphalocele requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) represent a high-risk population; however, contemporary multicenter data evaluating survival and predictors of mortality remain limited. We aimed to characterize outcomes and identify factors associated with mortality among infants with omphalocele requiring ECMO.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization Registry from 2000-2025. Demographic, clinical, ECMO-related, and complication variables were compared between survivors and non-survivors, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was performed to identify independent predictors of mortality.

RESULTS: 88 infants with omphalocele requiring ECMO were identified, with 41% overall survival to hospital discharge. On bivariate analysis, cannulation at <28 days of age (p=0.048) and female sex (p=0.047) were associated with mortality. ECMO-related complications occurred in 70% of patients and were associated with decreased survival probability. On multivariable analysis, the presence of any ECMO-related complication remained independently associated with mortality (HR 2.33, 95% CI 1.23-4.34, p=0.009). When compared to congenital lung malformations and congenital diaphragmatic hernia, omphalocele ECMO cases demonstrated a more pronounced increase in frequency over time.

CONCLUSION: Infants with omphalocele requiring ECMO experience substantial mortality despite advances in neonatal and ECMO care. ECMO-related complications were independently associated with mortality. These findings add to risk stratification and multidisciplinary perinatal planning for this population. Further studies evaluating long-term outcomes and optimal patient selection are needed.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III (Retrospective Cohort Study.

articles.title: Spontaneous right coronary dissection with delayed false-lumen thrombosis.
Very low-gradient aortic stenosis: defining the phenotype and recovery after TAVI-Response.
Patients with ischemic stroke despite anticoagulation: outcomes after left atrial appendage occlusion in a high-risk cohort.
Quercetin suppresses radial glial stem-like cell functions through an HSPB1-associated mechanism in glioma.
articles.abstract: Glioma is a highly malignant tumor characterized by pronounced intratumoral heterogeneity. By integrating multi-omics analyses, we identified radial glial stem-like (RG-like) cells as a putative upstream developmental-like state in inferred glioma differentiation trajectories. Integrated spatial transcriptomic and histopathological analyses further linked the molecular features of RG-like cells to their spatial distribution and associated tissue morphology. A CRISPR-based knockout screen highlighted heat shock protein beta-1 (HSPB1) as a potential molecular target associated with RG-like cell functions. We subsequently investigated quercetin (QUE) and found that it inhibited glioma cell growth and suppressed mitotic somal translocation (MST), a characteristic RG-like cellular behavior. Mechanistic analyses showed that QUE reduced HSPB1 protein expression and was associated with a reduced detectable interaction between HSPB1 and vimentin (VIM). Together, these findings characterize RG-like cells at the molecular and histopathological levels and suggest that QUE may represent a potential pharmacological approach for modulating their associated functions in glioma.

articles.title: Oxygen concentration modulates cortical excitability in humans.
articles.abstract: Cortical excitability is fundamental to neuroplasticity, particularly relevant in conditions like stroke and neurodegeneration. Although oxygen is essential for brain metabolism, its effects on cortical excitability remain poorly understood, representing a fundamental gap in neuromodulation research. This study is the first to directly examine the effects of both hypoxia and hyperoxia on corticospinal excitability (CSE) in humans, utilising non-linear analysis of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) recruitment curves. In a single-blinded, randomised, within-subjects design, 37 participants were exposed to hypoxia (10.5% O2), normoxia (21% O2), and hyperoxia (100% O2). TMS was applied at varying intensities to generate motor-evoked potentials (MEPs), using a Boltzmann Sigmoidal Curve (BSC) approach to optimise estimation of CSE from recruitment curves. Hypoxia enhanced CSE sensitivity at lower intensities, whereas responsiveness was attenuated at higher intensities within the sampled range, potentially due to metabolic constraints. Hyperoxia increased CSE at higher intensities within the sampled range, while saturation could not be accurately estimated with the current sampling. Recruitment curves demonstrated distinct mechanisms, with hypoxia lowering the half-maximal intensity and hyperoxia increasing maximum excitability and slope steepness. These findings show that oxygen levels can modulate CSE in humans, revealing a critical mechanism for enhancing plasticity. Oxygen-based interventions may offer a promising route for improving neurorehabilitation outcomes in clinical populations.

articles.title: Selective C4-5 Foraminotomy for Severe Foraminal Stenosis is Not Associated with Lower Rates of C5 Palsy After Posterior Cervical Decompression and Fusion.
articles.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND CONTEXT: C5 nerve palsy is a common complication of cervical spine surgery. There is currently limited data evaluating prophylactic C4-5 foraminotomy on instrumented posterior cervical decompression and fusion (PCDF), where greater posterior cord migration may theoretically increase traction on the C5 nerve root.

PURPOSE: This study aimed to compare perioperative outcomes between patients who underwent a C4-5 foraminotomy and those who did not, evaluating the effect of foraminotomy on postoperative C5 nerve palsy incidence, and describe its effects on C5 nerve palsy recovery.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective chart review PATIENT SAMPLE: Patients undergoing PCDF from 2017 to 2022 with and without prophylactic C4-5 foraminotomy.

OUTCOME MEASURES: C5 palsy incidence, degree of foraminal stenosis, and postoperative motor scores and recovery.

METHODS: All patients who underwent PCDF with C4-5 foraminotomy were identified and matched 1:1 to control patients who underwent PCDF without C4-5 foraminotomy. Descriptive statistics and bivariate analysis were performed. Statistical significance was set at P<0.05.

RESULTS: A total of 176 patients were included (88 without foraminotomy and 88 with foraminotomy). After matching, there were no significant demographic or perioperative differences between groups. Foraminotomy patients had higher rates of foraminal stenosis (P=0.001). Foraminotomy was not associated with a lower rate of postoperative C5 nerve palsy incidence (P=0.429) or improved recovery among patients who developed C5 palsy at 6 and 12 months (P>0.28).

CONCLUSION: In patients undergoing PCDF, prophylactic C4-5 foraminotomy did not appear to be associated with reduced C5 palsy incidence or improved recovery if a palsy occurred. Further studies evaluating motor recovery in patients that underwent foraminotomy and sustained a C5 palsy are warranted.

articles.title: Radiation in Spine Care: A Comprehensive Review of Radiation Sources, Emerging Technology, Cancer Risk, and Radiation Stewardship.
articles.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
articles.abstract: Radiation from medical imaging is increasingly recognized as a modifiable carcinogenic exposure. The precise population-level cancer burden remains debated, but the oncologic cost is real, unevenly distributed by patient age and sex and largely controllable at the point of clinical decision-making. Spine care occupies a central position in this discussion because many patients are exposed to ionizing radiation repeatedly over the course of their care. This includes patients within a wide age range undergoing surgery, fluoroscopic- or computerized tomography (CT)-guided percutaneous interventions, and serial imaging. In younger patients, the attributable cancer risk per unit dose is greater and the latency period for radiation-induced malignancy is longer; in patients requiring repeated interventions, cumulative lifetime radiation exposure may also become substantial. These concerns are increasingly relevant as navigation, robotics, and augmented reality platforms have expanded the use of preoperative and intraoperative CT. In this context, we sought to synthesize the current evidence across radiation physics, carcinogenesis risk modeling, perioperative radiation sources, patient-level risk heterogeneity, surgeon and operating room personnel exposure, and technology-specific evidence. Particular attention is paid to patient-level heterogeneity as cancer risk per unit dose varies by nearly an order of magnitude across age and sex strata such that oncologic implications of an otherwise identical imaging protocol may differ substantially depending on the patient receiving it. Building on the evidence, we introduce a radiation budgeting framework that treats the full perioperative episode as the unit of radiation accountability and propose radiation stewardship in spine care as a structural analog to antibiotic stewardship in infectious disease.

articles.title: Health-related quality of life in early-stage type 2 diabetes: A cross-sectional study within the SMARTEST trial.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Normative health-related quality of life (HRQoL) data for people with early-stage, well-controlled type 2 diabetes are lacking. We aimed to describe the HRQoL profile of SMARTEST trial participants, contextualised against general population benchmarks.

METHODS: Baseline RAND-36 data (n = 1,501; domain scores range 0-100) were compared with population-based reference data using multiple linear regression adjusted for sex, age and education. Participants with < 4 years diabetes duration, no macrovascular complications, and at most monotherapy were included. A significant group × age interaction was identified, and analyses were stratified by age group. Pandemic-related differences were explored in subgroup analyses.

RESULTS: HRQoL differed markedly by age group. SMARTEST participants aged < 55 years, reported lower HRQoL in three domains, including general health (β = -7.7, 95% CI -10.5; -5.0). No differences were observed for participants aged 55-65 years. Among those aged > 65 years, HRQoL exceeded reference population levels across several domains, particularly physical role functioning (β = 9.8, 95% CI 5.6; 13.9). Participants included during the pandemic reported a lower mental composite score (β = -2.5, 95% CI -4.5; -0.6).

CONCLUSIONS: HRQoL in this early-stage type 2 diabetes cohort showed a distinct age-related pattern relative to general population benchmarks. Mental HRQoL during periods of societal disruptions merits further study.

articles.title: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors and risk of acute kidney injury in type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease: Nationwide target trial emulation.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate the 90-day acute kidney injury (AKI) risk after initiation of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) versus dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4i) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and chronic kidney disease (CKD).

METHODS: Using South Korean claims data (2015-2024), we emulated a target trial in adults aged ≥30 years with T2DM and CKD initiating SGLT2i or DPP-4i during 2016-2023. The primary outcome was 90-day AKI occurrence. Inverse probability of treatment weighting and weighted Cox models estimated adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Pre-specified subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Among 43,502 new users (8,253 SGLT2i and 35,249 DPP-4i), weighted AKI incidence rates were 10.5 and 15.6 per 100,000 person-days, respectively. SGLT2i initiation was not associated with increased 90-day AKI risk (aHR, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.50-1.10), with consistent findings in competing-risk and propensity-score-matched analyses. Subgroup findings were generally consistent, including among older adults; however, estimates for prior AKI and advanced CKD had wide CIs.

CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2i initiation was not associated with higher 90-day AKI risk than DPP-4i initiation in patients with T2DM and CKD. However, findings in certain high-risk subgroups remain uncertain and warrant further study.

articles.title: Menstrual phase variations in glycemic control and insulin requirements in females with type 1 diabetes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To systematically evaluate the impact of menstrual cycle phases on continuous glucose monitoring (CGM)-derived glycemic metrics and insulin requirements in adolescent girls and women with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM).

METHODS: This PRISMA-compliant, PROSPERO-registered meta-analysis searched MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov up to 1st August 2026 for studies comparing follicular and luteal phase glycemic outcomes in females with T1DM. Random-effects models evaluated CGM metrics and insulin parameters. Subgroup/sensitivity analyses assessed the impact of insulin modality, cycle definition, and study quality.

RESULTS: Among the 18 studies identified (with 16 contributing to overall pooled estimates), the luteal phase was associated with reduced time in range (TIR), increased time above range (TAR 180-250 and >250 mg/dL), and higher mean sensor glucose. Hypoglycemia (TBR) and glycemic variability remained unchanged. Total daily insulin and bolus percentages did not differ significantly between phases, indicating that compensatory insulin adaptations to luteal-phase dysglycemia are highly variable and individualized. Overall basal insulin proportions remained stable, though adaptation patterns differed between automated insulin delivery (AID) and conventional therapies.

CONCLUSIONS: The luteal phase is associated with a modest but consistent worsening of glycemic control, while compensatory insulin adaptations remain highly heterogeneous. Differences observed between insulin-delivery subgroups are exploratory and do not establish a protective effect of AID; the findings support further evaluation of personalized, cycle-aware management strategies.

articles.title: Beyond BMI: A multiparametric approach to cardiometabolic risk detection in young adults. Integrating body fat percentage and the FINDRISC score.
articles.abstract: Body mass index (BMI) may not adequately identify excess adiposity and cardiometabolic risk, particularly in young adults. This narrative non-systematic review evaluates the complementary roles of body fat percentage (BFP), the Finnish Diabetes Risk Score (FINDRISC), and the Clínica Universidad de Navarra Body Adiposity Estimator (CUN-BAE) in cardiometabolic risk assessment. Clinical practice guidelines, peer-reviewed studies, and the illustrative conference abstract by Mezzano et al. (2026 American Diabetes Association Scientific Sessions) were reviewed, focusing on normal-weight obesity, the utility of BFP and CUN-BAE, BMI limitations, and FINDRISC for assessing behavioral and familial diabetes risk. In the Mezzano et al. illustrative cohort of 152 medical students, BMI and BFP classified 7% and 22% as high risk, respectively, while 30% and 29% were classified as intermediate risk. Overall, 41% had at least one intermediate- or high-risk trait using combined BMI, CUN-BAE-derived BFP, and FINDRISC assessment. These findings are hypothesis-generating and limited by small sample size and cross-sectional design. BMI alone may inadequately characterize cardiometabolic risk. Combining CUN-BAE-estimated BFP with FINDRISC may improve detection of risk factors missed by BMI and offers a potentially feasible, low-cost approach for primary-care screening; however, prospective validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Not every neuropathy in diabetes is diabetic: A practical guide to treatable alternatives.
articles.abstract: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy is a common complication of diabetes mellitus (DM), but not all neuropathies occurring in individuals with diabetes are attributable to DM. Alternative or coexisting causes are frequently overlooked, potentially delaying the diagnosis and treatment of reversible or treatable conditions. This narrative review provides a practical framework for the differential diagnosis of peripheral neuropathy in individuals with diabetes, emphasizing clinical features that should prompt further investigation. We outline a structured diagnostic approach based on the distribution, predominant neurological deficits, temporal progression, electrophysiological findings, and relevant clinical and laboratory investigations. Particular emphasis is given to vitamin B12 deficiency, monoclonal gammopathies, plasma cell dyscrasias, paraneoplastic neuropathies, and inflammatory polyneuropathies, including chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy (CIDP), autoimmune nodopathies, and Guillain-Barré syndrome. We also discuss the diagnostic challenges in distinguishing diabetic distal symmetric polyneuropathy from inflammatory neuropathies and the potential role of complementary diagnostic investigations. Atypical features, including prominent motor weakness, rapid progression, asymmetry, sensory ataxia, and electrophysiological evidence of demyelination, should raise suspicion of an alternative diagnosis. Recognizing these features is essential, as several non-diabetic neuropathies have effective disease-specific treatments. A systematic, clinically guided approach can prevent diagnostic misclassification, facilitate timely referral, and improve patient management.

articles.title: Ask, don't assume: Editorial and Data Integrity Triage (EDIT), an editor's practice-based checklist for screening manuscripts at submission.
articles.abstract: As an editor, I regularly find problems in submitted manuscripts that need explaining before peer review can begin. A reference cannot be found, participant numbers in the abstract differ from those in the tables, or the methods do not explain the results. Most have an honest explanation, but some do not, and paper mills and text produced by artificial intelligence (AI) add to the pressure on editors. My message in this paper is simple. When something does not add up, editors should ask the authors a specific question before assuming anything, and they should judge the work itself and leave aside who wrote it. I describe Editorial and Data Integrity Triage (EDIT), a checklist I developed from my editorial work at the Journal of Hospital Infection and from academic integrity practice. EDIT has 20 checks in five domains covering reporting, methods and data, references, authorship and declarations, and submission files. Ten core checks can be applied to every submission and the others when they are relevant. Each finding leads to routine handling, a request for clarification or a pause for senior assessment. Writing style, a free email account, an incomplete author profile, the authors' country and unusually tidy data are not treated as evidence of a problem. A fictional example follows one submission from the first checks to an editorial decision, and I identify the checks that peer reviewers can use. EDIT reflects one editor's practice, and independent review and testing are needed before it is used routinely.

articles.title: Genomic Insights into Early Catheter-Associated UTIs in a Clinical Setting: High-Risk Clones, Hidden Diversity and Limited Catheter-Urine Genomic Divergence.
articles.abstract: Catheter-associated urinary tract infections (CAUTIs) are major contributor to healthcare-associated morbidity and are increasingly associated with multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens. We performed whole-genome sequencing of paired catheter and urine-derived isolates from five CAUTI cases identified prospectively in a Portuguese hospital (February-July 2024) to characterize species diversity, resistomes, virulence, strain relatedness and genomic variation. Substantial heterogeneity was observed in bacterial species and genomic profiles. Escherichia coli predominated in catheter (57%) and urine (67%) samples, consistent with its recognized role in early colonization under the short dwell times observed (median: 5 days). Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Proteus mirabilis occurred sporadically, mainly in catheter associated samples. Four patients harboured isogenic or near-isogenic catheter-urine pairs, consistent with closely related strains across compartments, whereas ondistinct E. coli lineages (ST12 vs. ST131) were identified in one patient. AMR profiles ranged from limited repertoires to extensive MDR. High-risk E. coli ST131 isolated carried characteristic ESBL and fluoroquinolone-resistance determinants but were genomically distinct. Virulence repertoires encompassed factors associated with adhesion, biofilm formation, iron acquisition, immune evasion and epithelial injury (including colibactin in one catheter isolate), alongside biocide- and stress-response determinants. Matched catheter-urine pairs showed limited genomic divergence, with few or no detected variants and no predicted variant-associated changes in antimicrobial susceptibility. These findings illustrate that early CAUTI cases may involve MDR high-risk clones and heterogeneous catheter-urine genomic profiles. Genomic characterization may complement conventional microbiology in the investigation of CAUTI, supporting future studies of pathogen-source assessment, antimicrobial management and infection-control strategies.

articles.title: Using direct carbapenemase detection to guide Acinetobacter baumannii infection control.
Cost-Effectiveness of Cabotegravir Long-Acting HIV Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP): A Systematic Review of Modelling Studies.
articles.journal: Value in health : the journal of the International Society for Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cabotegravir long-acting injectable (CAB-LA) is a promising non-oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for HIV prevention, especially where daily oral adherence is poor. Despite superior efficacy, CAB-LA's high price raises concerns about economic value and implementation across settings. This study reviewed modelling studies on CAB-LA's cost-effectiveness as PrEP across diverse populations and settings.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase and Cochrane Library (2015-2025), assessing CAB-LA's cost-effectiveness versus oral PrEP or no PrEP. Eligible studies reported incremental cost-effectiveness ratios, cost per HIV infection averted, or cost per quality-adjusted life year (QALY) or disability-adjusted life year gained. Reporting quality was assessed using the CHEERS 2022 checklist. Results were narratively synthesized due to heterogeneity.

RESULTS: Eleven modelling studies across sub-Saharan Africa, the United States, and Asia-Pacific showed that CAB-LA averted more HIV infections than oral PrEP, especially in high-incidence, low-adherence populations. In high-risk U.S. populations, CAB-LA averted about 71,000 infections and gained 4.65 million QALYs. In Africa, CAB-LA became economically favourable under lower acquisition-cost assumptions, although cost-effective prices varied across models, populations, price years and thresholds. U.S. and Asia-Pacific models found CAB-LA not cost-effective at current prices, requiring 24-88% price reductions. Sensitivity and scenario analyses showed that cost-effectiveness estimates were responsive to CAB-LA price, HIV incidence, ART coverage, adherence, persistence, and programme-delivery assumptions.

CONCLUSION: CAB-LA cost-effectiveness is context dependent and generally more favourable at lower prices, higher-incidence populations, and poor oral PrEP adherence. Wider adoption may require strategies to improve economic value, equitable access, and implementation, especially in resource-constrained settings.

articles.title: Wavelength-dependent stress tolerance and transcriptional responses of Escherichia coli O157:H7 after illumination with 465, 520 and 625nm light-emitting diodes.
articles.abstract: Light-emitting diodes (LEDs) are increasingly used in food production and processing, but their effects on subsequent stress tolerance of foodborne pathogens remain unclear. Escherichia coli O157:H7 was grown under blue (465nm), green (520nm), or red (625nm) LED illumination (300 μmol m⁻² s⁻¹) to early stationary phase (17-29h), or in the dark, and subsequently challenged with heat (60 °C), simulated gastric fluid (SGF; pH 2.5), and free chlorine. Illumination at 465nm increased heat tolerance (time to the first decimal reduction, δ1, 3.7 vs 2.1min in dark controls), whereas 520 and 625nm decreased it (1.2 and 0.7min; p < 0.05). Illumination at all three wavelengths increased sensitivity to SGF (δ1, 48-58 vs 82min). At 0.5μg/mL free chlorine, log reductions were smaller in illuminated cells (≤0.12 vs 0.62log), although the differences were not consistently statistically significant. At 1.0-2.5μg/mL, bacterial populations declined below the detection limit. Count-based reanalysis of RNA-seq data (DESeq2; false discovery rate < 0.05, ≥2-fold change) identified 1,109, 296, and 23 differentially expressed genes following illumination at 465, 520, and 625nm, respectively. Illumination at 465nm was associated with increased expression of chaperone (ibpA, ibpB, dnaK, clpB) and respiratory genes and decreased expression of acid-resistance, osmoprotectant-uptake (proVWX), and motility genes. Illumination at 520nm altered expression of heat-shock and acid-resistance genes, indicating wavelength-dependent differences in transcriptional responses. Overall, prior LED illumination altered the subsequent stress tolerance of E. coli O157:H7 in a wavelength- and stress-dependent manner.

articles.title: Cisplatin activates ERK1/2-EGR1-MMP10 axis to promote renal inflammation and injury.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nephrotoxicity caused by cisplatin is a common complication in patients undergoing chemotherapy. This study investigated whether cisplatin induces sustained activation of the extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 (ERK1/2) and early growth response 1 (EGR1) pathways, thereby modulating the expression of inflammatory mediators and matrix metalloproteinase 10 (MMP10). To address this question, both in vivo and in vitro cisplatin models were employed.

METHODS: In the in vivo model, nine-week-old male Balb/c mice received a single intraperitoneal injection of cisplatin (15 mg/kg), diluted in 0.9% saline. They were then compared to control mice that received only 0.9% saline. The mice were euthanized four days later. In vitro experiments were performed using TKPTS cells (a mouse kidney proximal tubular epithelial cell line) treated with cisplatin (25 μM) for 24 h.

RESULTS: Cisplatin induced severe proximal tubular injury and inflammation in animals, as well as increased ERK1/2 phosphorylation (pERK1/2) and elevated EGR1 and MMP10 protein immunostaining. Similarly, exposure to cisplatin in vitro induced ERK1/2 phosphorylation and associated upregulation of EGR1 protein and MMP10 transcription. Previously, inhibiting pERK1/2 with the MEK inhibitor PD98059 (2'-amino-3'-methoxyflavone) or knocking down Egr1 in TKPTS cells reduced the expression of inflammatory markers (Il6, Cxcl1 and Cxcl10) and Mmp10.

CONCLUSION: Overall, these results suggest that kidney injury in cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity is associated with inflammatory processes and increased MMP10 expression, potentially via the pERK1/2-EGR1-MMP10 signaling pathway.

articles.title: Vertebral osteomyelitis in adults: a Danish multicenter observational cohort study (DASPODISC).
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pyogenic vertebral osteomyelitis (PVO) is a serious spinal infection with considerable morbidity and increasing incidence. Evidence to guide optimal diagnosis and management remains limited. In this Danish multicenter prospective cohort study, we describe clinical characteristics, microbiology, management, and outcomes of PVO with the purpose of identifying opportunities for optimization.

METHODS: Adults with PVO diagnosed between May 2023 and September 2025 were identified across departments in the Danish Spondylodiscitis Consortium (DASPODISC). Data from electronic health records were entered into REDCap and analyzed using descriptive statistics and Kaplan-Meier methods.

RESULTS: A total of 282 patients were included. Staphylococcus aureus was the most frequently identified pathogen, while 77/268 (29%) patients had culture‑negative infections. The median length of hospital stay was 30 days (IQR 17, 44) and 73/282 (26%) underwent surgery. Inadequate treatment response was reported in 37/282 (13%). Six‑months survival was 90%, and 40/73 (55%) of responding patients reported persistent back pain.

CONCLUSIONS: This multicenter study indicates ongoing challenges in identifying causative pathogens to promote targeted treatment warranting studies and strategies to promote identification of causative bacteria. Furthermore, the prevalence of long-term pain and continued lengthy admission underscores the need for studies to further explore and mitigate these challenges.

articles.title: Pleural empyema and perisplenic abscess caused by Clostridioides difficile in a patient with liver cirrhosis and previous C. difficile colitis: a case report.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clostridioides difficile is a leading cause of healthcare-associated diarrhea, whereas extraintestinal infection is rare and pleural involvement is exceptional, with only a handful of cases reported to date. Patients with liver cirrhosis are at increased risk of bacterial infection and of C. difficile infection, but C. difficile pleural empyema has been reported only once in this population.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 43-year-old man with alcohol-related liver cirrhosis (Child-Pugh class C) and C. difficile colitis two years earlier was admitted with hepatic decompensation and a C-reactive protein of 151 mg/L, without gastrointestinal symptoms. Computed tomography showed a large left-sided pleural collection. The aspirate contained 6,870 cells/µL with 94.2% granulocytes and had a pH of 6.97, consistent with empyema. Piperacillin/tazobactam was started empirically and empyemectomy was performed. Intraoperative swabs yielded C. difficile on MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry and toxin PCR was positive; histopathology showed acute purulent pleuritis. Two weeks later the empyema recurred and a new perisplenic collection appeared; C. difficile toxin was again detected at both sites. Treatment was escalated to meropenem, vancomycin and metronidazole, combined with repeat surgical evacuation and percutaneous drainage. Repeated stool testing for C. difficile antigen and toxin remained negative. After a prolonged intensive care stay requiring tracheostomy, the patient recovered and was discharged to a rehabilitation facility.

CONCLUSIONS: C. difficile should be considered as a cause of pleural empyema, particularly in patients with liver cirrhosis and previous C. difficile infection. Recovery of C. difficile from extraintestinal specimens should not be dismissed as contamination; timely source control combined with targeted antimicrobial therapy is essential for a favorable outcome.

articles.title: One Team to Prevent AMR now.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases

articles.title: Epidemiological Characteristics of Acinetobacter baumannii: An 11-Year Longitudinal Study at a Tertiary Hospital in Northern China.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) is a critical-priority pathogen. We investigated the epidemiological characteristics and clinical outcomes of Acinetobacter baumannii infections over an 11-year period at a tertiary hospital in northern China.

METHODS: We analysed 4,028 A. baumannii isolates from a single tertiary hospital (2014-2024; first isolate per patient-year), calculating resistance rates, annual CRAB proportion, antibiotic consumption (DDDs/100 patient-days, 2018-2024) and in-hospital mortality; testing used the Cochran-Armitage test and Spearman correlation.

RESULTS: The CRAB proportion fell from 62.2% (2014) to 37.8% (2024; p<0.001) while antibiotic consumption rose by 29.2%. Resistance was near-universal, sparing only minocycline (4.6%) and polymyxin (0.3%). No agent's resistance rate was significantly correlated with its consumption (|ρ| ≤ 0.71; all p ≥ 0.09). In 1,811 patient-episodes (35.2% mortality), older age (OR 1.20 per 10 years), intensive-care admission (1.86), mechanical ventilation (1.74) and male sex (1.25) each independently predicted death; empirical therapy covered only 2.6% of isolates.

CONCLUSIONS: CRAB was predominantly detected in intensive care units and was closely associated with mechanical ventilation, representing a major nosocomial pathogen. Given its high associated mortality, continuous surveillance of its epidemiological characteristics is warranted.

articles.title: Identification of leachates from synthetic and modified natural textiles during in vitro human digestion.
articles.abstract: Plastic-associated chemicals are often considered a black box, as consumer products reach the market with little public or scientific understanding of their chemical composition. Non-target chemical screening can shed light on final composition, but identification requires suspect compound libraries for comparison. This study investigated solvent extracts and aqueous leachates from four clothing items: recycled polyethylene terephthalate (rPET), polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyamide (PA), and cotton, to identify potentially hazardous chemicals present within the garments. Leaching was also conducted in a simulated human digestion system to determine whether ingestion of micro-fibres represents an exposure route for harmful chemicals. Chemical features were tentatively identified using a combined workflow incorporating an in-house in silico library and commercially available libraries. All four clothing items contained numerous chemical features. Solvent extraction yielded 699 (PA), 1001 (cotton), 1024 (rPET) and 1037 (PET) chemical features, whereas aqueous leaching yielded fewer features: 113 (rPET), 117 (PET), 170 (cotton) and 190 (PA). Approximately 80% of solvent-extracted features were identifiable using existing libraries; however, fewer than 10% of aqueously leached features were identifiable, highlighting the challenging nature of non-target analysis in LC-MS workflows. Comparatively few chemicals were extracted from the simulated digestion leachates, 110 remained unidentified and 32 were unattributable to any garment. This suggests that human digestion may release chemicals from microfibres which are not readily liberated by aqueous or polar solvents. Overall, considerable ambiguity remains regarding chemicals used and produced during textile manufacturing, and future work is needed to clarify this complex supply chain.

articles.title: Intracardiac Echocardiography and Selective Pulsed-Field Energy Delivery: A Practical Strategy to Mitigate Steam-Pop Risk with the Sphere-9 Lattice-Tip Catheter.
Gender and Racial Disparities in Patients with Portopulmonary Hypertension: A Three-Year National Inpatient Sample Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Portopulmonary hypertension (POPH) carries a poor prognosis, yet the influence of gender and race on inpatient outcomes is not well defined. Prior registry data suggested that POPH occurred more frequently in Hispanic patients and was associated with higher all-cause mortality. We examined whether gender and race were associated with inpatient outcomes in POPH hospitalizations.

METHODS: We analyzed the 2017-2019 National Inpatient Sample. Adult hospitalizations carrying concurrent Group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension and portal hypertension codes were identified using the International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision. Multivariable logistic and linear regression models estimated the independent association of gender and race with in-hospital mortality, length of stay, total hospital charges, shock, and sepsis.

RESULTS: We identified a weighted total of 36,090 POPH hospitalizations. After multivariable adjustment, neither gender nor race was independently associated with in-hospital mortality, length of stay, shock, or sepsis. The only significant disparity was in total hospital charges, which were higher among Hispanic than White patients (adjusted difference $17,585; 95% CI $2015-$33,155; p = 0.027).

CONCLUSIONS: In this contemporary national cohort, gender and race were not independently associated with in-hospital mortality or major complications in POPH, in contrast to prior reports. The higher hospital charges observed for Hispanic patients, in the absence of differences in clinical outcomes, warrant further study of resource utilization and access to care.

articles.title: A Retrospective Study on High-Flow Nasal Cannula Oxygen Therapy for Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure: Clinical Characteristics and Treatment Failure Predictors.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize HFNC use in AHRF, identify factors associated with treatment failure, and develop a prediction model.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 350 patients receiving HFNC for the first time between October 2023 and December 2025; 82 experienced treatment failure and 268 succeeded. Eight candidate predictors were selected based on univariable associations, clinical relevance, confounding, information overlap, and events per parameter, and all were entered into multivariable logistic regression. Restricted cubic splines assessed nonlinear associations. Performance was evaluated by discrimination, calibration, 1,000-resample bootstrap validation, and decision curve analysis (DCA).

RESULTS: The final model included age, cardiovascular disease, APACHE II score, AHRF etiology, RALE score, ROX index, heart rate (HR), and thoracoabdominal asynchrony. Higher APACHE II (OR = 1.217, 95% CI: 1.126-1.315), extrapulmonary etiology (OR = 2.444, 95% CI: 1.061-5.631), and higher RALE score (OR = 1.121, 95% CI: 1.053-1.194) were associated with increased odds of failure, whereas higher ROX index was associated with lower odds (OR = 0.239, 95% CI: 0.157-0.363). HR showed a nonlinear association (P for nonlinearity = 0.018). The apparent and bootstrap-corrected C-indices were 0.912 and 0.899, respectively. The optimism-corrected calibration intercept and slope were -0.077 and 0.895, and the corrected Brier score was 0.102. DCA indicated clinical net benefit across evaluated thresholds.

CONCLUSION: The eight-predictor model showed good discrimination and acceptable internally validated calibration. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Association Between Regular Black Tea Consumption and Acute Asthma Exacerbations in Children: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asthma is a common chronic disease in childhood. Black tea contains caffeine and polyphenols with potential bronchodilatory, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory properties, but evidence regarding habitual tea consumption and asthma outcomes in children is limited.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between regular black tea consumption and asthma outcomes in children receiving standard asthma therapy.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study enrolled 200 children aged 5-12 years with physician-diagnosed asthma, of whom 140 completed 24 months of follow-up (70 in the tea group and 70 in the non-tea group). Participants were classified according to habitual black tea consumption into a tea group () and a non-tea group (n=70). Outcomes included acute asthma exacerbations, emergency department visits, systemic corticosteroid use, Childhood Asthma Control Test (C-ACT) scores, and spirometric parameters. Multivariable Negative Binomial regression was used to model exacerbation rates. Baseline-adjusted linear regression (ANCOVA) was used for continuous end-of-study outcomes (C-ACT, FEV1, FEV1/FVC), and binary logistic regression for binary utilization outcomes, adjusting for age, sex, baseline GINA asthma severity step, baseline medication adherence, environmental tobacco smoke exposure, and baseline outcome values.

RESULTS: Annualized exacerbation rates were significantly lower in tea consumers than non-consumers vs. episodes/year; p < 0.001). In multivariable Negative Binomial regression, tea consumption was associated with a lower incidence rate of exacerbations (Incidence Rate Ratio [IRR] = 0.35; 95% CI, 0.22 to 0.56; p < 0.001). Tea consumption was also associated with lower odds of emergency department visits (aOR= 0.22; 95% CI, 0.09-0.51; p = 0.001) and systemic corticosteroid use (aOR = 0.24; 95% CI, 0.10-0.57; p = 0.001). In baseline-adjusted ANCOVA models, post-study C-ACT score ( ; 95% CI, +2.35 to +3.89; p < 0.001), post-study (; 95% CI, +2.20 to +6.82%; ), and (; 95% CI, +1.35 to +5.05%; ) were significantly higher in the tea group.

CONCLUSIONS: Regular black tea consumption was associated with fewer exacerbations, lower asthma-related healthcare utilization, and better asthma control and lung function. The observational design does not establish causality. These findings represent observed cultural habits and do not constitute a clinical recommendation for pediatric caffeine consumption.

articles.title: Ultrasound transcranial brain pulsatility in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus: a prospective exploratory study.
articles.abstract:
STUDY DESIGN: A prospective cohort of patients with suspected idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) OBJECTIVE: To assess multiple clinical, physiological and radiological parameters, including an original ultrasound transcranial brain pulsatility measurement, to help the surgical decision for cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) shunting in patients with suspected iNPH.

BACKGROUND: Gait, cognitive and urinary assessment before-after substractive lumbar puncture (LP) of CSF are clinical parameters commonly used to indicate CSF shunting surgery. It is well documented that this decision remains a challenge in iNPH treatment, due to the poor predictive value of the effect of CSF substraction on the classical clinical parameters. However, CSF shunt surgery is fraught with numerous complications in this frail, elderly population. Therefore, the need to find objective and robust diagnostic tools is crucial.

METHODS: Between 2014 and 2018, 35 patients with a suspected iNPH were enrolled for a prospective evaluation in our institution. They benefited from a computerized recording of gait analysis, a physiotherapist assessment of walking, a cognitive assessment by a speech therapist, a urinary assessment, MRI morphological and flow sequences, and ultrasound tissue pulsatility imaging (TPI). All these data were recorded before and after substractive LP. The decision of CSF shunting surgery, which was the main endpoint of the study, was taken independently by a blinded committee of 4 to 5 neurosurgeons, only based on the classical clinical parameters, i.e., without considering the original parameters recorded for the study: computerized recording of gait analysis, MRI flow sequences, and ultrasound TPI.

RESULTS: The median age was 76 years old with a median duration of symptoms prior to inclusion of 20.5 months. For 17/35 patients (46.8%) a CSF shunting decision was taken. We found a trend towards a correlation between post-LP improvement in "Stride Time" (p= 0.068), Tinetti test (p=0.076), global cognitive assessment (p=0.062) and the committee's decision to proceed with CSF shunt surgery. Some of the pre-LP dynamic parameters showed a tendency to correlate with the shunting decision: MRI "acqueducal maximal stroke volume" (p=0.052) and ultrasound measures of brain pulsatility, in particular maximum peak amplitude (p=0.078) and mean peak amplitude (p=0.072). In addition, the mean cerebral pulsatility (maximum peak amplitude (p=0.033), mean peak amplitude (p=0.017) and root mean square (p=0.023)) significantly decreased after substractive LP, underlining the direct relationship between CSF volume and cerebral pulsatility.

CONCLUSION: The exploratory design of our study made it possible to highlight one promising parameter to help in the surgical decision of CSF shunting: the mean brain pulsatility amplitude measured with an exocranial ultrasound probe. The non-invasive nature of this technique makes it possible to consider further explorations on larger samples of patients. However, the exploratory nature of the study was intended for signal detection rather than definitive inference, and larger multicenter studies will be necessary to confirm these preliminary observations.
