Perillaldehyde (PAE) Regulates Ovarian Cancer by Modulating HSP70 and Regulating the PI3K/AKT Signaling Pathway.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Perillaldehyde (PAE), a major active component of Perilla frutescens, possesses potential anti-tumor activity. However, its effects and mechanisms in ovarian cancer remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the impact of PAE on ovarian cancer cells and a subcutaneous xenograft model, and explore the possible mechanisms involved.

METHODS: The effects of PAE on proliferation, migration, and invasion of SKOV3 and A2780 cells were assessed using CCK-8, colony formation, EdU, wound healing, and Transwell assays. Expression levels of HSP70, EMT-related proteins (E-cadherin, Vimentin, N-cadherin, MMP2/9), and PI3K/AKT pathway proteins were detected by Western blot. The role of HSP70 was validated by shRNA knockdown and plasmid overexpression. A nude mouse xenograft model was established to evaluate the in vivo anti-tumor effect.

RESULTS: PAE reduced cell viability, colony number, and EdU-positive cells in a concentration-dependent manner. PAE downregulated HSP70, Vimentin, N-cadherin, MMP2/9, decreased the ratios of p-PI3K/PI3K and p-AKT/AKT, while upregulating E-cadherin. HSP70 knockdown enhanced these effects, whereas overexpression weakened them. In vivo, PAE decreased tumor volume and weight, reduced Ki67-positive cells, and increased necrotic areas; protein changes were consistent with cell experiments.

CONCLUSION: PAE inhibits proliferation, migration, and invasion of ovarian cancer cells and slows tumor growth. The mechanism may involve HSP70 downregulation, PI3K/AKT inhibition, and EMT reversal, providing evidence for PAE as a candidate anti-ovarian cancer agent.

articles.title: Reframing the gut-muscle axis through the lens of functional redundancy: A conceptual framework for chronic sarcopenia, acute muscle wasting, and microbiota-related interventions.
articles.abstract: Sarcopenia is a progressive systemic skeletal muscle disorder that predominantly affects older adults, and its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Research on sarcopenia has largely followed two lines of inquiry. The first concerns chronic, age-associated sarcopenia, which involves anabolic resistance, chronic low-grade inflammation, neuromuscular junction degeneration, and hormonal alterations. The second concerns acute sarcopenia and related rapid muscle wasting during severe illness (e.g. sepsis, trauma, major surgery), which must be distinguished from ICU-acquired weakness and cancer cachexia. The gut-muscle axis has attracted interest as a potential contributor to sarcopenia onset and progression. This narrative review integrates heterogeneous cell, animal, observational human, and intervention evidence through four proposed functional modules: anabolic support, anti-catabolic protection, redox/mitochondrial homeostasis, and inflammatory-immune regulation. From the perspective of functional redundancy, we discuss a hypothetical "sarcopenia-susceptible state" and stage-informed research questions; these are conceptual constructs rather than validated disease stages or treatment algorithms. Microbiota-related interventions are candidate adjuncts to nutrition and exercise. Purified metabolites are distinguished from postbiotics, and direct clinical efficacy in acute critical-illness sarcopenia remains unestablished.

articles.title: Addressing health-related social needs and providing care coordination for patients with cardiovascular disease.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rural communities in the U.S. Stroke Belt experience disproportionately high rates of cardiovascular disease and stroke, compounded by limited access to preventive care and unmet health-related social needs (HRSNs). Community pharmacies, supported by pharmacy-based community health workers (PCHWs), offer an accessible, team-based model for cardiovascular risk screening, transitions-of-care support, and longitudinal care coordination to improve population health in underserved communities.

OBJECTIVE: The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the implementation of a pharmacy-based cardiovascular disease screening and care coordination program across rural community pharmacies participating in CPESN Community Health. Secondary objectives were to describe patient characteristics, screening activities, identified HRSNs, and care coordination services provided by rural pharmacies supported by pharmacy-based community health workers.

METHODS: This retrospective program evaluation included data from 25 rural community pharmacies participating in a multi-state cardiovascular disease screening initiative. Pharmacy teams, consisting of pharmacists and PCHWs, documented patient encounters using the Pharmacist eCare Plan data standard. Program data were analyzed descriptively to characterize implementation, patient reach, cardiovascular screening activities, transitions-of-care interventions, HRSN screening, and referrals generated during routine care.

RESULTS: The 25 pharmacies included in the program were from six states and employed 111 PCHWs. 11,188 encounters were logged for 9820 patients in 694 different zip codes, documenting 9,845 American Heart Association (AHA) stroke screenings, 2,434 atrial fibrillation screenings, 8,207 HRSN screenings, and 195 TOC screenings.

CONCLUSION: Community pharmacies have a critical role in access to screenings that are needed, especially for those who are in rural, socially vulnerable communities. CHWs on the pharmacy team can increase the opportunity to identify and assist with the execution and operation of these services.

articles.title: Early versus delayed surgery to prevent hemorrhagic transformation in patients with septic cerebral emboli from infective endocarditis.
articles.journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The optimal timing of cardiac surgery in patients with infective endocarditis and ischemic septic cerebral embolism remains uncertain, largely because of concern for perioperative hemorrhagic transformation. This study evaluates the association between surgical timing and outcomes in this population.

METHODS: Patients with infective endocarditis and preoperative septic cerebral emboli who underwent cardiac surgery were identified from an institutional database (1999-2025). After excluding those with preoperative cerebral hemorrhage, 240 patients with ischemic stroke were stratified by interval from stroke to surgery: early (≤7 days, n=109) versus delayed (8-30 days, n=131). Propensity score matching was used to balance baseline confounders. The primary outcome was postoperative hemorrhagic transformation; secondary outcomes included new postoperative stroke, intensive care unit and hospital length of stay, four-year survival assessed by Kaplan-Meier analysis, and mortality assessed by Cox proportional hazards modeling.

RESULTS: Matching yielded 194 patients. Postoperative hemorrhagic transformation occurred in 10 of 194 (5.2%) patients and did not differ by timing (6.2% early vs. 4.1% delayed, p=0.73). New postoperative stroke occurred in 19 of 194 patients (9.8%) and was similar (10.3% early vs. 9.3% delayed, p>0.99), as was 30-day mortality (6.2% early vs. 10.3% delayed, p=0.42). Four-year survival did not differ by timing (68.0% early vs. 57.4% delayed, p=0.07), and there was no significant association between surgical timing and mortality (HR 0.67 [0.44-1.03]; p=0.07).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with infective endocarditis and ischemic stroke, early surgery (≤7 days) was not associated with increased rates of postoperative hemorrhagic transformation, new stroke, or 30-day or long-term mortality compared with delayed surgery.

articles.title: Loss of solubility of NDC80 complex components contributes to spindle assembly checkpoint failure under severe heat shock.
articles.abstract: Heat shock is a proteotoxic stress that induces various cellular responses in a temperature-dependent manner. We recently reported that heat shock treatment of cells at 42 °C prolongs the duration of M phase but that at 44 °C (severe heat shock) induces premature M phase exit, possibly through dysfunction of the spindle assembly checkpoint (SAC). However, the mechanisms underlying the severe heat shock-induced mitotic slippage remain unclear. In this study, we investigated the effects of severe heat shock on SAC-related proteins. Exposure of asynchronous cells to severe heat shock increased >4 N DNA content populations, indicating mitotic failure. In the presence of vincristine (VCR), mitotic cells were accumulated during 16 h of culture, but this accumulation was drastically reduced under severe heat shock, suggesting SAC failure; this was confirmed by time-lapse imaging. Severe heat shock inhibited the kinetochore localization of NDC80 kinetochore complex component (NDC80) and mitotic arrest deficient 2 like 1 (MAD2L1), a component of the mitotic checkpoint complex (MCC) and blocked KNL1 phosphorylation. Partial knockdown of NDC80 reduced the kinetochore localization of NDC80 and MAD2L1 and was associated with an increased frequency of mitotic slippage in the presence of nocodazole. Fractionation of cell lysates revealed that NDC80 and NUF2 accumulated in the insoluble fraction after severe heat shock. These results suggest that severe heat shock inhibits SAC by inducing insolubilization of NDC80 complex components, thereby blocking KNL1 phosphorylation and disrupting MAD2L1 kinetochore localization. Because heat shock is sometimes used clinically (e.g., hyperthermia therapy), understanding its impact on cell division and on the efficacy of anticancer therapies is important.

articles.title: Applicability of Prediction Models: Aligning Models with Clinical Use.
articles.abstract: Doctors increasingly rely on models that predict a patient's risk of future health problems. These models only work well when the patients they were built on resemble the patients being treated now, in illness type, care setting, and stage of disease. This is easy to see when the mismatch is obvious: a model built on hospital patients may not suit those seen in a family doctor's office. The same problem is harder to appreciate when it comes from where a patient sits on a chronic illness journey. Using severe chronic kidney disease as an example, this review shows that a model built from patients who have recently progressed to this more severe stage works better for patients at that same point, while a model built from patients who have lived with the disease for years works better for those further along. This review offers practical steps to keep predictions aligned with the patients they serve.

articles.title: Pooled cohort analysis of renin-angiotensin system inhibition and the risk of kidney outcomes in APOL1-mediated chronic kidney disease in the CRIC and SPRINT studies.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Apolipoprotein L1 (APOL1) variants are common in individuals of African descent and increase risk of chronic kidney disease (CKD). Renin-angiotensin system inhibitors (RASis) are a mainstay of therapy for hypertension and proteinuric CKD but were not historically recommended as first-line anti-hypertensive therapy in Black individuals. Here, we evaluated RASis versus other antihypertensive therapy on kidney outcomes in Black individuals by APOL1 genotype.

METHODS: We included Black participants with APOL1 genotyping on first-line anti-hypertensive therapy from the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) and Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT). We evaluated whether the impact of RASi-prescription on kidney outcomes was modified by APOL1 risk allele number or baseline albuminuria, using Cox models with inverse probability of treatment weighting and marginal structural models.

RESULTS: A total of 3418 participants (62% from SPRINT), 40%, 44% and 16% carrying zero, one and two APOL1 risk alleles, respectively, were included. RASi-use compared to other first-line antihypertensive therapy was associated with a comparably lower risk of the kidney outcome in individuals with zero (hazard ratio (HR) 0.62 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.44-0.87]), one (HR 0.68 [95% CI 0.49-0.94]) or two risk alleles (HR 0.59 [95% CI 0.40-0.86]). This benefit was driven by albuminuric participants, but estimates were similarly low for RASi-use compared to other antihypertensive therapy in albuminuric (HR 0.62, 95% CI [0.41-0.93]) and non-albuminuric (HR 0.37, 95% CI [0.13-1.08]) participants with two APOL1 risk alleles, although the estimate was imprecise in non-albuminuric participants.

CONCLUSIONS: RASi-based therapy, addressed as a time-updated pooled treatment, provided similar benefit across APOL1 genotypes, driven by albuminuric participants. Among individuals with two APOL1 risk alleles, outcomes were similar regardless of baseline albuminuria. However, further studies are needed due to small sample sizes and the inability of statistical methods to capture clinical variables that may have affected prescription changes.

articles.title: Healthy Homes (HHOMES): Integrated Environmental Screening Program in an Urban Asthma Program.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Community- and home-level environmental exposures are established as contributors to asthma, but clinically integrated environmental screening is lacking. This study aimed to develop an environmental health screening program and investigate environmental risks for patients.

METHODS: This retrospective, cross-sectional study developed an environmental hazard (EH) screening tool (HHOMES) in an urban primary care asthma program from 2022-2023. Patient responses and electronic-medical record (EMR) data were examined, using descriptive statistics to characterize sociodemographic and clinical factors. Primary and secondary analyses examining associations between asthma severity, EH and health-related social needs (HRSN) factors were performed using logistic regression.

RESULTS: Of 461 patients who received the HHOMES screening tool, 172 (37%) submitted responses. 71% (n=122) of respondents reported at least one EH, with 29% reporting three or more. Exposure to at least one EH was associated with a 2.57-fold increase in the odds of moderate to severe persistent asthma relative to the intermittent asthma group (p < 0.05). Individuals reporting living in public housing had 2.55 times the odds of experiencing any EH compared to those not residing in public housing, (p < 0.05). Those reporting food insecurity had 3.68 times the odds of EHs compared to those who did not report this concern (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Standardized environmental screening identified environmental factors reported by the majority of our patient population and showed that exposure to EHs is associated with greater asthma severity. The HHOMES approach provides an avenue to identify and address EHs within clinical encounters. Further work is needed to understand how environmental exposures relate to HRSN and health outcomes.

articles.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Use and Risk of Pain-Related Medical Encounters Among Patients with Comorbid Type 2 Diabetes and Opioid Use Disorder: A Target Trial Emulation Study.
articles.abstract: While GLP-1 receptor agonists (RAs) are postulated to alleviate pain, limited data exist to support the drugs' benefits in reducing pain-related medical encounters, particularly in patients with opioid use disorder (OUD), who have a high prevalence of pain. This study aims to examine the associations of GLP-1 RAs use with risk of emergency department (ED) visits or hospitalizations for pain among patients with comorbid type 2 diabetes (T2D) and OUD. We conducted a retrospective cohort study design in a target trial emulation framework using Merative MarketScan claims data between 2016 and 2023. Participants included adults between 18 and 64 years of age with a diagnosis of T2D and OUD who initiated GLP-1 RA or other second-line antidiabetic medication. Key outcomes included counts of incident pain-related ED visits, hospitalizations, or a composite outcome of either medical encounter, with a primary or secondary diagnosis coded for pain. Of 5842 eligible patients, those with use of GLP-1 RAs (vs. second-line antidiabetic medications) had a lower adjusted incident rate of pain-related ED visits (adjusted incidence rate ratio [aIRR]: 0.81; 95% CI: 0.69, 0.96, P=.01), pain-related hospitalizations (aIRR: 0.92; 95% CI: 0.68, 1.24, P=.56), although non-significant, and composite outcome of pain-related ED visit or hospitalization (aIRR: 0.83; 95% CI: 0.72, 0.97, P=.02). Initiation of GLP-1 RA therapy compared with second-line antidiabetic medication was associated with reduced risk of the composite outcome of pain-related ED visits or hospitalizations, indicating potential benefit of GLP-1 RA use for reducing pain-related medical encounters. Perspective In this cohort study, use of GLP1-1 RAs vs second-line drugs for T2D was associated with a lower risk of pain-related ED visits or hospitalizations among adults with comorbid T2D and OUD. GLP-1 RAs may be repurposed as a non-opioid pharmacological treatment for pain in patients with OUD.

articles.title: Physiochemical and biological evaluation of curcumin-derived carbon dots conjugated with chenodeoxycholic acid in streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice.
articles.abstract: Diabetes related neuropathy and cognitive impairment remain challenging to treat with current therapies. This study focused on synthesizing and evaluating curcumin-derived carbon nanodots conjugated with chenodeoxycholic acid (Cur-CDCA) in streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice. The formulation of Cur-CDCA was supported by physiochemical characterization, resulting in a calculated drug-loading efficiency (DLE) of 97.78% and minimal hemolysis at 0.5-30 μg/ml. pH-dependent and time-dependent UV-Vis experiments revealed formulation-related absorbance changes. Cur-CDCA administered at a low dose of 10 mg/kg on days 1 and 7 was associated with reduced blood glucose levels, restoring thermal and mechanical thresholds, and improved cognitive function like spatial learning and cognitive behavioral outcomes. Treatment associated morphological preservation was observed in qualitative histology, while MPZ and BDNF expression improved to control levels. These findings support the potential of Cur-CDCA as a nanotherapeutic formulation for diabetes-related neurological complications, necessitating further preclinical testing.

articles.title: Nanotherapeutic interventions for infectious and chronic diseases: From rational design to clinical translation.
articles.abstract: Nanoformulations represent a transformative advancement in biomedical science, offering precise, efficient, and safer approaches for disease diagnosis and therapy. Nanoscale systems successfully address many of the drawbacks of conventional therapies and offer promising strategies for efficient treatment against important infectious diseases by improving drug penetration, increasing antimicrobial concentrations at infected sites, and facilitating intracellular drug delivery. Similarly, in non-infectious diseases, nanocarriers like liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles, and lipid-based systems provide localised drug delivery, improve therapeutic efficacy, and reduce systemic side effects in the treatment of cancer, diabetes, neurodegenerative, cardiovascular, and arthritic disorders. This review critically evaluates therapeutic applications of nanoformulations across infectious and non-infectious diseases, focussing on design strategies, delivery mechanisms, and clinical progress. It also identifies key challenges and research gaps in translating promising research into effective treatment strategies. Together, these insights underscore the critical role of nanotechnology in next-generation diagnostics, targeted drug delivery, and precision therapeutics.

articles.title: Association of Cutaneous Keloids and Hypertrophic Scarring with Risk of Postoperative Arthrofibrosis After Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Arthrofibrosis is a debilitating postoperative complication and a leading cause of readmission, failure, and revision surgery. The purpose of this study was to assess the association between cutaneous keloids, hypertrophic scarring, and risk of arthrofibrosis after primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA).

METHODS: Patients undergoing TKA (n = 248,094) were identified using a large national database. Exclusions included a TKA for fracture, post-traumatic osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, or congenital deformity, or a second TKA within two years. Remaining patients were assigned to a keloid cohort (prior diagnoses of hypertrophic scarring, acne keloids, or scar fibrosis; n = 6,307) and matched 1:1 to controls by demographics and comorbidities. After propensity score matching, 6,305 patients remained per cohort with no significant baseline differences. Outcomes were compared using Chi-square tests at 30 days, 60 days, one year, and two years postoperatively, with significance set at P < 0.0083 (0.05 of 6).

RESULTS: The Keloid cohort demonstrated significantly higher rates of arthrofibrosis at 60 days (odds ratio (OR) = 2.06, P < 0.001), one year (OR = 1.54, P < 0.001), and two years (OR = 1.55, P < 0.001); revision TKA at one year (OR = 1.74, P = 0.002), and two years (OR = 1.50, P = 0.006); manipulation under anesthesia at 60 days, one year, and two years (P < 0.001); and periprosthetic joint infection within 30 days (OR = 2.05, P < 0.001). There were no significant associations found for lysis of adhesions or deep vein thrombosis (DVT).

CONCLUSION: Patients who had preoperative cutaneous keloids or hypertrophic scarring demonstrate significantly higher rates of arthrofibrosis, revision TKA, manipulation under anesthesia, and periprosthetic joint infection following primary TKA. A dermatologic history of keloids and hypertrophic scarring may serve as a risk factor for identifying high-risk TKA patients.

articles.title: Pre-puncture EUS-based prediction of technical failure during EUS-guided hepaticogastrostomy: development and internal validation of a three-factor model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Technical failure during EUS-guided hepaticogastrostomy (EUS-HGS) remains clinically relevant, yet most previously reported predictors are assessed only after bile duct puncture or guidewire manipulation has already been attempted. We aimed to identify EUS-assessable anatomical factors measurable before bile duct puncture and to develop an internally validated model for predicting first-attempt technical failure during EUS-HGS.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients who underwent attempted EUS-HGS between January 2015 and December 2025 at a single tertiary center. The primary outcome was first-attempt technical failure of EUS-HGS. Pre-puncture EUS images were reviewed to measure bile duct diameter at the intended puncture site, needle-duct angle, and hepatic parenchymal length. Independent predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression, and a three-factor prediction model was developed. Discrimination, calibration, and internal validation with 2,000 bootstrap resamples were assessed.

RESULTS: Among 453 attempted EUS-HGS procedures, first-attempt technical success was achieved in 400 (88.3%) and first-attempt technical failure occurred in 53 (11.7%). Smaller bile duct diameter (OR 0.282 per 1-mm increase; 95% CI 0.181-0.440), a more acute needle-duct angle (OR 0.632 per 10° increase; 95% CI 0.533-0.748), and longer hepatic parenchymal length (OR 1.144 per 1-mm increase; 95% CI 1.080-1.212) were independently associated with first-attempt technical failure. The combined three-factor model showed excellent apparent discrimination (AUC 0.932; 95% CI 0.897-0.961), with an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.927 after bootstrap validation. The optimal cutoff probability was 0.130, yielding 86.8% sensitivity and 85.5% specificity. Observed failure rates were 1.7% in the low-risk group, 9.0% in the intermediate-risk group, and 51.9% in the high-risk group.

CONCLUSIONS: A three-factor model based on anatomical variables assessable on EUS before bile duct puncture showed excellent apparent discrimination and good calibration for predicting first-attempt technical failure during EUS-HGS. This internally validated model provides a preliminary framework for pre-puncture risk estimation; however, its clinical application remains hypothesis-generating and requires prospective multicenter external validation before implementation in clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Atrial fibrillation begets atrial fibrillation revisited: Early entrenchment of AF episodes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 7-day threshold defining persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) is clinically entrenched but biologically arbitrary. Whether episode termination follows scale-free dynamics or time-dependent entrenchment remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: To quantify the probability of spontaneous termination and assess its dependence on episode duration using large-scale pacemaker monitoring.

METHODS: Continuous pacemaker monitoring data from the ACaSA study were analyzed. Device-detected AF episodes were reconstructed from daily burden using predefined continuity rules. Termination was modelled as the conditional probability that an ongoing episode would terminate within the subsequent 24 hours. Duration dependence was assessed using a shared frailty Weibull survival model, and episode duration distributions were compared using the Vuong likelihood-ratio test.

RESULTS: After excluding patients with single-chamber devices or 100% baseline AF burden, 251 of 281 pacemaker recipients contributed 204,775 patient-days. Device-detected AF occurred in 154 patients, who contributed 7002 reconstructed episodes. Termination probability declined from 91.1% at 1 hour to 72.1% at 12 hours, 33.3% at 24 hours, and 4.3% at 7 days. Episode durations were better described by a lognormal distribution than by a scale-free power-law model.

CONCLUSION: Device-detected AF episodes show marked early entrenchment, with spontaneous termination becoming progressively less likely as episode duration increases. These findings support the concept that "AF begets AF" even at short timescales and suggest that persistence beyond 24 hours identifies a state with a substantially reduced likelihood of near-term spontaneous termination.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetics of Prostate Cancer Lesions on Dual Time-Point PET/CT﻿: A Predictive Factor for Response to PSMA Radioligand Therapy?
articles.abstract:
AIM: Prostate cancer (PC) lesions usually show increasing uptake of prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) ligands over time. We investigated whether the intensity changes of PSMA-ligand uptake on dual-time-point positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) can predict the response to [177Lu]Lu-PSMA radioligand therapy (PSMA-RLT).

METHODS: Nineteen patients who underwent dual-time-point [18F]PSMA-1007 PET/CT before PSMA-RLT were retrospectively analysed. Standardised uptake values were measured for local prostate cancer lesions and lymph node, bone, and organ metastases. These groups were compared for maximum standardised uptake value (SUVmax) differences between standard and late scans. Using Firth's bias-reduced logistic regression, we assessed whether change in SUVmax between standard and late scans (ΔSUVmax) correlates with long-term biochemical response to PSMA-RLT.

RESULTS: We analysed 355 PC lesions (14 local tumours, 171 bone, 132 lymph node, and 38 organ metastases). Across all lesions, the median SUVmax in late scans was 15.2% higher than that in standard scans (p<0.001). A mixed-effects model accounting for clustering within patients suggested differences in relative ΔSUVmax across metastasis types, although these did not reach statistical significance (p=0.058). Logistic regression showed no correlation of ΔSUVmax to therapy response likelihood (odds ratio=1.01, p=0.85). In contrast, the SUVmax of the hottest measured lesion significantly predicted the therapy response (odds ratio=1.11 per unit increase, 95% confidence interval: 1.02-1.26, p=0.005).

CONCLUSION: PC lesions exhibited significantly higher PSMA-ligand uptake in late scans. However, the magnitude of this increase neither differed significantly across PC lesion types nor correlated with response to PSMA-RLT. Notably, higher SUVmax during standard time-point imaging were associated with an increased likelihood of biochemical response to PSMA-RLT.

articles.title: A lysosomal DRAM1-GLUT1-NADPH axis coordinates glucose sensing with metabolic reprogramming.
articles.abstract: Perturbed glucose homeostasis is a hallmark of metabolic disease and cancer, and cellular responses to excess glucose are tightly controlled. We report here a lysosomal glucose sensing axis linking the transporter GLUT1 with the lysosomal protein DRAM1. Pathophysiological glucose induces DRAM1 via the MLX/ChREBP transcriptional complex. DRAM1 then binds newly synthesized GLUT1 and promotes its traffic to lysosomes without degradation, reducing surface GLUT1 and acting as a reversible brake on glucose entry. Hexokinase or glucose-6-phosphate (G6P) dehydrogenase disruption weakens DRAM1-GLUT1 complex formation, whereas nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate(NADPH) oxidase (NOX) inhibition enhances assembly, implicating NADPH as a key metabolic signal downstream of elevated glucose. Sequestration of GLUT1 suppresses glucose uptake and glycolysis and rewires metabolism toward glutamine anaplerosis, creating vulnerability to glutaminase (GLS) inhibition. In vivo, Dram1-/- tumors display a glycolytic metabolite profile, consistent with loss of this brake. Together, these data define an mTORC1- and AMPK-independent lysosomal mechanism that protects metabolic homeostasis under hyperglycemic conditions.

articles.title: CONCLAVE: A consensus clustering with annotation-validation extrapolation for cyclic multiplexed immunofluorescence data.
articles.abstract: High-dimensional cyclic multiplexed immunofluorescence (cMIF) enables single-cell phenotyping within intact tissues. Cell annotations rely on a multi-step pipeline involving normalization, sampling, dimensionality reduction, and clustering, but the absence of standardized benchmarks for method selection, especially at the clustering stage, leads to inconsistent and less reproducible phenotyping. To address this, we developed CONCLAVE, a consensus-clustering-based workflow that optimizes upstream steps and integrates results from multiple clustering algorithms retaining only those cell labels supported by at least two independent methods. Through in silico simulations and real-world cMIF datasets, CONCLAVE consistently outperformed single-clustering-method approaches in agreement with expert-curated references, reproducibility, and robustness, with improvements becoming more evident when mapped within spatial tissue contexts. Additionally, CONCLAVE includes a scoring module that flags regions likely to contain unreliable or inconsistent data, facilitating targeted quality control. In summary, CONCLAVE offers a robust framework for cell annotation in cMIF datasets, enhancing the reliability of downstream spatial proteomics analyses.

articles.title: Human neocortical glutamatergic neurons revealed through multimodal profiling.
articles.abstract: The human neocortex underlies higher cognition, yet our understanding of its neuronal diversity is limited by sparse access to viable tissue, inconsistent cell-type definitions, and limited multimodal data. Although single-cell transcriptomics has transformed our understanding of cell type diversity, transcriptomic data alone cannot explain neuronal function. Here, we introduce a multimodal patch sequencing (patch-seq) resource of human neocortical glutamatergic neurons spanning cortical layers 2-6. Combining morphoelectric features with spatial transcriptomic data to provide laminar context, we sampled 39 of 42 transcriptomically defined glutamatergic neuron types. This systematic approach enabled the identification of unique phenotypes for understudied populations in the human neocortex including L4 intratelencephalic, L5/6 near-projecting, and diverse L6 neurons. Human, macaque, and mouse comparisons of transcriptomically homologous L5 neurons reveal that morphoelectric differences across species were subclass specific. This dataset provides a unified multimodal reference for studying human cortical circuitry and neuronal diversity.

articles.title: A consensus spinal cord cell-type atlas across mouse, macaque, and human.
articles.abstract: The spinal cord contains cell types critical for motor, sensory, and autonomic function, many of which are implicated in neurological disease and injury. Yet no shared molecular framework links human spinal cord cell types to the animal models used to study them. Here, we present a cross-species atlas integrating single-nucleus gene expression, chromatin accessibility, and spatial transcriptomics from over one million nuclei spanning cervical to sacral segments in human, macaque, and mouse. Consensus clustering resolves 111 cell type groups replicable across all three species, whose spatial distributions map spinal laminae and nuclei, including Clarke's column. Identity and laminar organization are highly conserved, yet abundance and expression are allometrically scaled, with the dorsal horn being the principal site of divergence, concentrated in neurotransmitter receptor genes and including a primate-specific glycine receptor subunit switch. Sequence models uncover a conserved transcription factor grammar and nominate motifs underlying enhancer-adeno-associated virus (AAV) access to a divergent dorsal horn population.

articles.title: Accumulation characteristics, driving mechanisms, and simulation prediction of PAHs in soils surrounding typical industrial parks in Beijing.
articles.abstract: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) accumulate persistently in soils around industrial parks, yet most studies capture only a static snapshot and overlook how contamination evolves. Shifting from static assessment to accumulation dynamics, we tracked PAH accumulation across three campaigns (2018, 2022, 2026) around four industrial parks in Beijing, identified its drivers, and developed an interpretable, scenario-based prediction model. The average Σ16PAHs was 1.01 mg/kg; high-molecular-weight (4- to 5-ring) PAHs were abundant, and benzo[a]pyrene contributed 45.26% of the toxicity risk. Contamination decreased as YSSH > JJJS > LHJJ > FSGY, with the petroleum park YSSH most contaminated. Positive matrix factorization, isomer ratios, and machine learning identified industrial production, traffic, and soil factors (e.g., fungus) as the main drivers. Capturing the temporal dynamics, concentrations around JJJS, LHJJ, and FSGY were significantly lower in 2022 and 2026 than in 2018, whereas YSSH increased slightly; accumulation during 2018-2022 exceeded 2022-2026, with increases occurring downwind rather than downstream. An interpretable XGBoost model showed smoke positively drives accumulation, and Monte Carlo scenario analysis indicated that policy-driven emission reductions can effectively reduce it. By shifting the focus from static contamination levels to accumulation dynamics and their drivers, this study supports proactive, source-oriented soil pollution control.

articles.title: Effects of high-protein intake on renal function: a narrative mini review.
articles.abstract: High-protein diets (HPDs) are increasingly used for weight management, metabolic health, physical performance, and healthy aging, yet their effects on renal function remain uncertain, particularly in individuals with chronic kidney disease (CKD). This narrative mini-review examines the relationship between high dietary protein intake and renal outcomes and critically evaluates the evidence underlying concerns regarding HPD-associated kidney injury. A narrative literature review was conducted using PubMed and Google Scholar, focusing primarily on studies published during the past two decades while also incorporating relevant landmark studies. Searches combined terms related to HPDs, dietary protein intake, renal function, glomerular filtration rate, renal hyperfiltration, and CKD. Observational studies, randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses evaluating renal outcomes in individuals with and without CKD were considered. The available evidence remains heterogeneous and inconsistent. Observational studies have reported associations between higher protein intake and accelerated decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate, particularly among individuals with pre-existing CKD or cardiometabolic risk factors. In contrast, randomized controlled trials have generally not demonstrated clinically significant deterioration in renal function over short- to medium-term follow-up. Emerging evidence suggests that protein source and overall dietary pattern may modify renal risk, with plant-based and fish-derived proteins potentially associated with more favorable outcomes than red and processed meat. Current evidence does not establish that high-protein intake uniformly accelerates renal decline, but the long-term renal safety of HPDs, particularly in established CKD, remains uncertain. Clinical dietary recommendations should therefore consider CKD stage, comorbidities, nutritional status, protein source, and overall dietary pattern rather than focusing solely on total protein intake.

articles.title: Before Metabolic Syndrome: Moving Cardiovascular Prevention Earlier.
The PELICANS Registry: Peripartum Cardiomyopathy Extended Longitudinal Investigation of Clinical Outcomes-Adverse Events, Nonrecovery, and Survival.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) disproportionately affects Black women, yet long-term outcome data in socially vulnerable, predominantly Black cohorts remain limited.

OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to characterize long-term outcomes and baseline predictors of survival, major adverse events (MAEs), and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) recovery in a U.S. PPCM cohort.

METHODS: This retrospective-prospective registry included 159 women with PPCM (1982-2024). Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality, MAEs, and LVEF recovery (≥50%). Multivariable and extended Cox models evaluated predictors, adjusting for LVEF recovery and subsequent pregnancy.

RESULTS: The cohort was 80.5% Black. Over a median 9.0-year follow-up (IQR: 3.4-15.5), 41 patients (25.8%) died and 64 (40.3%) had MAEs. Among 148 patients with echocardiographic follow-up, 69 (46.6%) had sustained LVEF recovery, though 23 (25.0% of initially recovered) declined to LVEF <50%. Independent mortality predictors included elevated creatinine (adjusted HR [aHR]: 2.86; 95% CI: 1.37-5.97), lower index LVEF (aHR: 0.94; 95% CI: 0.90-0.98), family history of cardiomyopathy or heart failure (aHR: 3.27; 95% CI: 1.41-7.56), and non-O blood type (aHR: 2.36; 95% CI: 1.04-5.33), retaining significance after adjusting for LVEF recovery and subsequent pregnancy (n = 62). Elevated creatinine increased MAE odds (adjusted OR: 7.09; 95% CI: 1.98-32.9), while higher LVEF, parity, and obesity reduced them. Baseline LV dilation (≥60 mm), Black race, older age, and family history of cardiomyopathy or heart failure predicted lower LVEF recovery odds.

CONCLUSIONS: This long-term predominantly Black PPCM cohort had high mortality, low LVEF recovery, and frequent late relapse. These findings highlight the importance of baseline risk stratification and sustained echocardiographic surveillance to guide clinical decision-making.

articles.title: PKP2-Associated ARVC Is a Structural and Metabolic Cardiomyopathy.
Diffuse dermal angiomatosis complicating aortic thrombosis.
articles.journal: Annales de dermatologie et de venereologie

articles.title: Acculturation and adjustment: Factors affecting acculturation and psychosocial adjustment among international students in China.
articles.abstract: Most acculturation research has focused on Western societies, leaving limited evidence from non-Western contexts such as China. This cross-sectional study addressed that gap by examining the associations of integration and contextual factors with international students' psychosocial adjustment in China. Using a bidimensional framework, we assessed mainstream and heritage cultural orientations, a derived integration index, and contextual variables including English and Chinese proficiency, perceived cultural distance, and anticipated acceptance. A total of 461 international students enrolled in Chinese universities, predominantly Pakistani (70.5%), completed measures of depression, sociocultural difficulties, and acculturative stress. Hierarchical regression analyses revealed that integration was associated with fewer sociocultural difficulties (β = - 0.22, p = .043), lower acculturative stress (β = -0.34, p = .001), and better overall adjustment (β = 0.26, p = .011). Integration accounted for modest additional variance in these outcomes (ΔR2 = 0.008-0.023). Neither mainstream nor heritage orientation was significantly associated with overall adjustment in the final model. Anticipated acceptance (β = 0.13, p = .010) and English proficiency (β = 0.11, p = .020) were positively associated with overall adjustment, whereas Chinese proficiency (β = - 0.25, p < .001) and perceived cultural distance (β = - 0.16, p = .001) showed negative adjusted associations. The unexpected association with Chinese proficiency warrants further investigation. These findings provide context specific evidence on acculturation and adjustment, while the cross sectional design and sample composition limit causal inference and generalizability.

articles.title: Early-onset epilepsy and inborn errors of metabolism: A large retrospective pediatric cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inborn errors of metabolism (IEM) are an under-recognised cause of childhood epilepsy. Early diagnosis is critical because specific treatments can substantially alter the disease course.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective study on 21,072 children evaluated for epilepsy in two Child Neurology referral centres in Eastern Sicily (i.e. Messina, Catania, and Enna) between January 2001 and December 2025. Medical records were reviewed to identify patients with a confirmed IEM diagnosis. Clinical, electrophysiological, neuroimaging, and treatment data were collected and analysed.

RESULTS: Fifty-seven children (0.27%) had a co-diagnosis of epilepsy and IEM (28 males, 29 females). Lysosomal storage disorders were the most common category (31.6%), followed by aminoacidopathies (22.8%), mitochondrial disorders (15.8%), congenital disorders of glycosylation (CDG, 12.3%), and organic acidaemias (7.0%). Seizure onset occurred before the age of three years in 83.3% of IEM cases, compared with 27.6% of children with non-metabolic epilepsy (OR 12.3; 95% CI 6.2-24.4; p < 0.001). Diagnostic delay exceeded 3.5 years from first seizure in half the cohort. Approximately 50% of patients showed drug-resistant epilepsy despite multi-drug anti-seizure medication therapy.

CONCLUSIONS: IEM should be systematically considered in any child presenting with epilepsy, particularly when onset occurs in the first three years of life. A structured stepwise diagnostic approach can substantially reduce diagnostic delay and facilitate access to disease-specific therapies.

articles.title: HPV vaccination initiation among preadolescents in Veneto, Italy: associations with chronic conditions and socioeconomic disadvantage.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Identifying population groups with lower human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination uptake is essential for developing targeted public health interventions. This study examined whether chronic conditions and sociodemographic factors were associated with HPV vaccination initiation among preadolescents in the Veneto Region of Italy.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using data from Pedianet, an Italian primary-care pediatric database. The study included children born between 2008 and 2011 who were followed between 9 and 12 years of age. Vaccination initiation was defined as receipt of at least one HPV vaccine dose from the ninth birthday to the day before the thirteenth birthday. Associations with sex, birth cohort, selected chronic conditions, disability, income-based healthcare exemption, and pediatric healthcare utilization were assessed using multivariable multilevel logistic regression, with a random intercept for family pediatrician.

RESULTS: Among 19,245 children followed by 93 pediatricians, 53.6% received at least one HPV vaccine dose. Asthma was associated with higher odds of vaccination initiation (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.36; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.12-1.67), whereas disability (aOR 0.71; 95% CI 0.58-0.88), income-based healthcare exemption (aOR 0.81; 95% CI 0.76-0.86), and male sex (aOR 0.79; 95% CI 0.74-0.84) were associated with lower odds of initiation. Associations with receipt of two HPV vaccine doses within the same age window were broadly consistent with those for initiation.

CONCLUSIONS: HPV vaccination initiation was associated with health-related and sociodemographic factors. Lower uptake among children with administratively recognized disability, those with income-based healthcare exemptions, and boys identifies groups that may benefit from targeted vaccination support. Further research should clarify the barriers underlying these associations.

articles.title: Oncologist perspectives on a novel geriatric assessment tool for older adults with cancer - The Comprehensive Health Assessment for My Plan (CHAMP): A multimethod study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Geriatric assessment (GA) is recommended for all older adults with cancer considering treatment, yet its availability in cancer settings remains limited. To provide an accessible alternative to the GA, an electronic self-completed abbreviated GA (the Comprehensive Health Assessment for My Plan - CHAMP) tool was co-created with oncologists and patients. Oncologists receive their patient's results and recommendations, which they can use to inform patient care. As oncologists are key end-users of the tool, an understanding of their perspectives is essential to determine the tool's feasibility and acceptability in cancer care settings. For this, a study was conducted to answer the following questions: (1) How do oncologists use CHAMP to inform patient care? (2) How do oncologists describe their satisfaction with CHAMP? (3) What are the perspectives of oncologists about using CHAMP?

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We employed a multimethod approach to answer the research questions. Phase one consisted of three separate surveys: a demographic survey, a post-tool survey, and a satisfaction survey. Phase two consisted of brief semi-structured interviews that elicited oncologist perspectives regarding CHAMP. Closed-ended survey responses were analyzed using descriptive statistics, while open-ended survey responses and interviews were analyzed using inductive thematic analysis.

RESULTS: Of the 53 oncologists approached, 44 (83.0%) consented to participate in the study. Amongst the sample (n = 44), medical oncologists (17, 38.6%) were the most common specialty. The CHAMP tool was considered at least somewhat helpful in 63.9% of cases and increased the confidence in decision-making in 44.4% of cases. In most cases (96.2%), the tool did not result in a change of the treatment plan. Overall, 90.0% of oncologists were satisfied with the tool. Fifteen oncologists participated in interviews, from which four main themes were identified: (1) insight into the patient, (2) barriers to tool use, (3) responsibility of implementing recommendations, and (4) optimizing the tool for practice.

DISCUSSION: Oncologists were satisfied with the content of the CHAMP tool and provided suggestions (e.g., optimizing delivery, engagement of other clinicians) for its adoption into cancer care settings. Future work will aim to address suggestions and evaluate additional strategies to support the tool's adoption.

articles.title: The Blueprint's nine domains of acute and critical care nursing practice: Results of the What Nurses Do Survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current patient outcomes, derived from the work of nursing in hospitals, are narrow in scope and focused on harm. To appreciate the value of the unique contributions made by nurses, nursing's work must be fully articulated.

PURPOSE: The nine domains of acute and critical care practice in the Call to Action: Blueprint for Change in Acute and Critical Care Nursing were articulated for this purpose but require validation from nurses practicing in hospitals. The nine domains include creating safe healing environments, building caring relationships, managing symptoms, administering care, surveillance, teaching patients and families, interprofessional collaboration, advocacy, and navigating patient transitions in care.

METHODS: In the national, cross-sectional What Nurses Do Survey, 987 nurses actively practicing in the hospital setting rated the relevance, frequency, and importance of each Blueprint for Change domain and identified any core practice activities absent from the nine domains.

DISCUSSION: Nurse respondents overwhelmingly endorsed all nine practice domains and indicated that they fully captured the scope and breadth of nursing practice in the inpatient environment. Symptom management was the highest-rated domain, followed by interprofessional collaboration and advocacy. Additional practice activities identified by respondents align with current scope and standards of professional practice that serve as a foundation for the nine practice domains.

CONCLUSION: Results confirm the face validity of the domains. Once fully validated with nurses, patients, and families, the Blueprint for Change nine domains can be used to guide the selection or development of new nurse-sensitive patient outcome measures that fully represent the work of acute and critical care nurses.

articles.title: Finite-temperature disorder physics in high-entropy carbides: collective response and carbon diffusion.
articles.journal: Journal of physics. Condensed matter : an Institute of Physics journal
articles.abstract: Chemical disorder in rocksalt (Hf,Zr,Ta,Nb,Ti)C produces heterogeneous local environments that can affect collective thermomechanical response and activated carbon transport differently. We examine this contrast using the unmodified MACE-MP-0 potential, with explicit limits on its transferability. Binary optical phonons are 4-16 meV softer than density-functional perturbation theory, multicomponent lattice parameters exceed density functional theory (DFT) values by 0.14-0.31%, and binary melting estimates deviate from experiment by -21% to +35%. Thermal expansion of nineteen compositions is nearly additive (α = 5.4-6.7 × 10-6K-1, within ±5% of the binary rule of mixtures), and elastic softening to 2000 K is mode-selective (C11decreases by 18-37%, C44by 3-7%). Along a group-IV-rich to group-V-rich composition path, the nominal two-phase melting estimates rise by about 1000 K. A linear composition weighting of the binary errors leaves about 460 K in the same direction, but this sensitivity estimate does not establish robustness to unmeasured multicomponent bias. Twenty static single-vacancy carbon-migration paths have a mean barrier of 2.53 ± 0.40 eV. At 12.5% carbon vacancies, fitted MD Arrhenius barriers are 1.36-1.54 eV, below the sampled ensemble minimum of 1.89 eV. These point estimates do not distinguish local-environment effects from vacancy concentration, correlated motion, finite cell size, or limited diffusion statistics. A matched DFT comparison finds a MACE barrier underestimate of 1.22 eV. The results identify near-additive expansion and mode-selective collective softening, while showing why a static barrier ensemble alone cannot determine the interpretation of finite-concentration carbon transport.

articles.title: Heterogeneous safety effects of right-turn protection and two-stage crossing treatments on non-motorized vehicle crashes at intersections.
articles.abstract: Non-motorized vehicle (NMV) crashes remain prevalent at intersections, posing a critical challenge for urban traffic safety. To address this issue, several cities in China have implemented intersection treatments, including right-turn protection measures (solid physical separation and right-turn warning zones) and two-stage crossing treatments for left-turning NMVs. However, the extent to which the safety effects of these treatments vary across different intersection contexts remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates the heterogeneous safety effects of these treatments and identifies intersection characteristics that moderate their effectiveness. A causal forest model, a machine learning-based causal inference approach, is employed to estimate treatment effects using NMV crash data. The results indicate that solid physical separation and right-turn warning zone treatments are associated with significant reductions in NMV crashes, whereas the two-stage crossing treatment does not exhibit a consistent overall safety benefit. Heterogeneity is observed in the effects of solid physical separation and two-stage crossing treatments across intersection characteristics, while the effects of right-turn warning zones remain relatively stable. Specifically, the safety benefits of solid physical separation are more pronounced at smaller intersections, at locations with shorter crossing distances, and where bicycle lane widths are at least 2.5 m. The two-stage crossing treatment shows safety benefits under specific conditions, including larger intersections, locations with longer crossing distances on major and minor roads, and the presence of medians on minor approaches. Across combinations of intersection characteristics, the estimated reductions in NMV crashes range from 0.86 % to 28.35 % for solid physical separation and from 7.05 % to 13.31 % for right-turn warning zones, while the estimated effects of two-stage crossing treatments range from a 4.04 % reduction to a 41.07 % increase in NMV crashes. Greater safety benefits of solid physical separation are observed at intersections with wide bicycle lanes (at least 2.5 m), limited median presence, and short crossing distances. This study highlights the importance of accounting for treatment effect heterogeneity in intersection safety analysis and provides empirical evidence that may inform the context-specific selection and implementation of NMV safety treatments.

articles.title: From stomatal movements to immunity and long-distance signaling: Ion channels mark the spot.
articles.abstract: Beyond their established role in mineral nutrition, ion channels have been increasingly recognized as central hubs of plant signaling across multiple scales. Early research revealed functions in stomatal regulation and nutrient transport, with recent breakthroughs highlighting their critical involvement in immunity, development, and long-distance signaling via membrane potential dynamics and diverse ion fluxes. Multiple channels have been characterized as ligand, voltage, or mechanosensitive gated, often modulated by phosphorylation, effectively functioning as integrative hubs of defined stimuli. Structural characterization is now complementing electrophysiology, live-cell imaging, and mass spectrometry, allowing new levels of mechanistic characterization of ion channels in the context of signaling networks and offering new opportunities to engineer plant resilience to stress.

articles.title: Paternal exposure to decabromodiphenyl ethane (DBDPE) accelerates aging in offspring mice: Intergenerational effects and underlying mechanisms.
articles.abstract: Decabromodiphenyl ethane (DBDPE), an emerging brominated flame retardant widely used as a replacement for legacy flame retardants, is persistent in the environment and increasingly detected in humans. However, whether long-term DBDPE exposure impairs male reproductive function and consequently affects offspring health remains largely unknown. Here, male mice were orally exposed to DBDPE (0, 0.01, 0.1, 1, and 10 mg/kg body weight/day) for 6 months. Chronic DBDPE exposure resulted in dose-dependent testicular accumulation, impaired sperm quality, and reduced fertilization capacity. Paternal DBDPE exposure also induced aging-like pathological alterations and shortened lifespan in F1 offspring. Sperm small non-coding RNA sequencing identified marked alterations in the sperm PIWI-interacting RNA (piRNA) profile, including increased abundance of the database-annotated piRNA piR-001169. Mechanistically, piR-001169 suppressed ten-eleven translocation 3 (Tet3) expression during early embryonic development, leading to increased methylation of the heat shock protein family A member 1 A (Hspa1a) and Hspa1b promoters and reduced heat shock protein 70 (Hsp70) expression in multiple offspring tissues. This dysregulation of the Hsp70/proteostasis axis was accompanied by increased protein aggregation and aging-related tissue injury. Restoration of Hsp70 expression partially ameliorated proteostasis disruption and aging-related pathological changes, supporting a functional role of impaired Hsp70-dependent proteostasis in the offspring phenotype. Notably, the aging-related phenotypes observed in F1 offspring were not detectable in F2 offspring. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that chronic paternal DBDPE exposure impairs male reproductive function and induces aging-like phenotypes in F1 offspring, with sperm piR-001169-Tet3 regulation and subsequent disruption of Hsp70-dependent proteostasis representing a potential paternal epigenetic mechanism.

articles.title: Outcomes of elderly hospitalized patients with influenza after the COVID-19 pandemic: decline of functional independence and frailty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Influenza remains a heavy burden to the elderly and the situation has been affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. The objective of this study was to clarify outcomes of elderly hospitalized patients with influenza after the COVID-19 pandemic.

METHODS: The clinical data of patients 65 years of age or older who were severely ill with influenza and required hospitalization in one center were gathered between September 2023 and March 2026 (3 influenza seasons after the COVID-19 pandemic). The outcomes, functional independence, and frailty of them were analyzed.

RESULTS: A total of 210 elderly patients were enrolled. The median age was 79 and 32 cases were judged as having mild or more frailty by the clinical frailty scale (CFS) before admission. Pneumonia was the most common disease indicated as cause for hospitalization, followed by a poor general condition and heart failure. The median duration of hospitalization was 13 days and in-hospital deaths were recorded for 17 patients (8.1%). Sixty cases changed hospital due to further treatment or deterioration of activity of daily living, and the functional independence measure (FIM) of 37 cases (17.6%) remained under a score of 70 even after rehabilitation. The CFSs worsened in 19 cases (9.0%) at the time of discharge.

CONCLUSIONS: Influenza infection remains a heavy burden among the elderly after the COVID-19 pandemic. The elderly tend to lose functional independence and fail to frailty even after recovery from acute illness. Preventive measures for influenza to avoid admission, including vaccination, will be essential. (Influenza Internet Survey, UMIN000015989).

articles.title: Effects of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus on the Offspring's Neurodevelopment.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a major global health concern that affects up to 14% of pregnancies. Traditionally, it has been characterized by hyperglycemia and insulin resistance. However, GDM can also lead to long-term health consequences in offspring, particularly affecting neurodevelopment. It has been associated with an increased risk of cognitive deficits, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and emotional dysregulation in GDM-exposed offspring. Findings from human and experimental studies suggest that GDM disrupts cortical and hippocampal architecture, impairs synaptic plasticity, and induces epigenetic alterations in key neurodevelopmental genes. These mechanistic pathways include oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and altered neurotrophin expression and receptor signaling. Maternal metabolism, diet, and genetic background may negatively affect neurotrophin expression, which could impact fetal brain development. Lower levels of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and nerve growth factor (NGF) in maternal blood, placental tissue, and cord blood have been linked to poor neurodevelopmental outcomes. This suggests that neurotrophins could be considered potential biomarkers. This narrative review compiles the latest evidence on the effects of GDM on fetal brain development, emphasizing the role of neurotrophins, especially BDNF and NGF, as critical mediators in this process. Emerging data also suggest that glycemic control during pregnancy may partially restore neurotrophin levels and improve neurodevelopmental outcomes. Understanding the interaction between maternal glucose metabolism and fetal brain signaling pathways is essential for pregnancy care and the design of neuroprotective strategies.

articles.title: Forward Stroke Volume and Ejection Fraction Estimation in Mitral Regurgitation: A Computational Hemodynamic Approach.
articles.abstract: Mitral regurgitation (MR) is a common valvular heart disease in which con-ventional measures such as left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) can bemisleading, as they do not distinguish between effective forward flow andregurgitant volume. This limitation may result in underestimation of the truehemodynamic burden of the disease. In this study, we develop a computationalframework based on a closed-loop lumped-parameter cardiovascular model toevaluate forward cardiac function in MR. The model incorporates a regurgitantpathway across the mitral valve together with flow calculations at the left ventric-ular outflow tract (LVOT), allowing estimation of forward stroke volume (FSV)and forward ejection fraction (FEF).The model was first assessed against published physiological reference values andthen used to simulate different levels of mitral leakage. As simulated regurgitantfraction increased from 0% to 58.30%, FSV decreased from 65.35 to 51.37 mLand FEF from 60.22% to 35.21%, while LVEF increased from 60.17% to 84.40%.These results illustrate how increased LVEF can coexist with reduced forwardoutput in modeled MR.Overall, the proposed approach provides a physiologically interpretable andcomputationally efficient tool for analyzing MR hemodynamics. The frameworkprovides a research tool for investigating MR hemodynamics and compar-ing conventional and forward-flow-based measures. Further validation usingpatient-specific clinical data is required before it can be considered for clinicalapplication.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance of the Hematology Analyzer XN-31 for Detecting Plasmodium Infections in School-Based Surveillance in Western Kenya.
articles.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.abstract: Despite significant progress in malaria control, asymptomatic and submicroscopic infections remain important reservoirs sustaining transmission and are often undetected by conventional microscopy or rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs). The Automated Hematology Analyzer XN-31 (Sysmex, Kobe, Japan) has shown high diagnostic accuracy in clinical settings, but performance under active surveillance, particularly among asymptomatic individuals, has not been evaluated. In this study, we assessed XN-31 using samples from school-based active surveillance in western Kenya, where asymptomatic and submicroscopic infections are highly prevalent. Among 1,237 samples, 564 (45.6%) were positive for Plasmodium spp. by polymerase chain reaction (PCR), including 511 afebrile infections. Using PCR as the reference, XN-31 detected infections with a sensitivity of 70.2%, slightly higher than microscopy (65.1%), and a specificity of 98.4%, higher than RDT (79.8%) and similar to microscopy (98.7%). It detected 43 of 197 submicroscopic infections (21.8%), with a median parasite density of 57 parasites/µL (interquartile range: 38-202). XN-31 identified 11 of 76 mixed infections of Plasmodium falciparum and non-P. falciparum compared with 5 by microscopy and 0 by RDT. Importantly, it also detected 8 of 14 P. falciparum infections suspected to carry hrp2/3 deletions, which caused false-negative RDT results, comparable with microscopy. This is the first study to evaluate XN-31 for detecting asymptomatic infections, non-P. falciparum species, and hrp2/3-deleted parasites, which are key diagnostic challenges in endemic settings. Our findings support the potential of XN-31 as a practical and reliable surveillance tool that bridges between RDTs and PCR for enhanced parasite detection and accelerated malaria control efforts.

articles.title: Scapular Gouty Tophus Mimicking Malignancy on 18F-FDG PET/CT in a Patient Without Prior Gout History.
articles.abstract: A gouty tophus found in the scapula is exceedingly rare. Here, we report on a 62-year-old asymptomatic woman with no history of gout or hyperuricemia who was incidentally found on chest CT screening to have a localized osteolytic lesion in the left scapula. 18F-FDG PET/CT demonstrated abnormally increased FDG uptake within this lesion, concerning for a neoplasm. Subsequent biopsy confirmed a gouty tophus, a rare mimic of malignancy in this location.

articles.title: Notice of Retraction: "Diabetes Testing Immediately Postpartum After Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: A Randomized Controlled Trial" (Field et al) and "Diabetes Testing Immediately Postpartum After Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: A Randomized Controlled Trial: Correction".
Serum Calcium and Respiratory Mechanics as Independent Correlates of Extubation Beyond 24 Hours in Postoperative Surgical ICU Patients: A Two-Cohort Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Timely airway extubation is central to recovery in the surgical intensive care unit (SICU), but its objective correlates remain incompletely defined, and the role of metabolic factors such as calcium is unclear. This two-cohort retrospective study included 204 postoperative SICU patients in Taiwan and 6,016 patients from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database, grouped by extubation within or beyond 24 hours, a local workflow benchmark. Candidate variables defined a priori and associated with the outcome in univariable analysis were entered into multivariable logistic regression. Multicollinearity was assessed with the variance inflation factor (VIF). Extubation beyond 24 hours occurred in 82 (40.2%) Taiwan and 4,599 (76.4%) MIMIC-IV patients. After adjustment, serum calcium and the rapid shallow breathing index (RSBI) were the only variables independently associated with the outcome in both cohorts, with odds ratios of 2.564 (95% CI 1.169-5.622) and 1.063 (95% CI 1.041-1.084) in Taiwan and 2.171 (95% CI 1.851-2.547) and 1.005 (95% CI 1.001-1.009) in MIMIC-IV, respectively. In MIMIC-IV, the calcium association was nonlinear (p < 0.001), with odds increasing across calcium quartiles in an exploratory model adjusted only for RSBI, so the per-unit odds ratio reflects an average trend. All VIF values were below 5. Calcium and RSBI were associated with the outcome in two cohorts with different surgical case mix. Because calcium was measured close to extubation, as total rather than ionized calcium, and showed a nonlinear association, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective evaluation before clinical use.

articles.title: Intense Focal Renal 18F-MFBG Uptake Attributable to Radiation in a Pediatric Patient With Neuroblastoma.
articles.abstract: A 9-year-old boy with neuroblastoma was enrolled in a clinical trial. After radiotherapy to the primary tumor site, 18F-MFBG PET/CT was performed 2 months later. No abnormal radiotracer accumulation suggestive of metastatic disease was identified. However, focal intense 18F-MFBG uptake was observed in the upper pole of the left kidney, within the previously irradiated field. No structural renal lesion was identified on cross-sectional imaging, and no evidence of renal tumor was found during 12 months of clinical and imaging follow-up. This case illustrates that intense localized renal 18F-MFBG uptake may result from radiation and should be recognized as a potential pitfall in post-radiotherapy 18F-MFBG PET/CT interpretation.

articles.title: Primary Brain Sarcoma Presented on FDG PET/CT.
articles.abstract: A 62-year-old man had dizziness and dysarthria for 4 months and limited mobility of the left upper extremity for 1 month. An outside enhanced MR showed a space-occupying lesion in the right frontal lobe. Since the patient had pancreaticoduodenectomy, gastrostomy, and jejunostomy 8.5 years ago for poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of the small intestine, brain metastasis was suspected. FDG PET/CT demonstrated increased FDG activity in the right frontal lobe lesion, but no FDG-avid lesion was found in other parts of the body. Following surgical resection, histopathology examination indicated sarcoma. The patient underwent brain radiotherapy afterward.

articles.title: Implementation Strategies to Improve CKD Testing and Delivery of Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy: A Scoping Review.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains underdiagnosed and undertreated despite substantial cardiovascular and mortality risks. Guidelines recommend annual testing with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) in at-risk populations, and a growing number of guideline-directed medical therapies (GDMT) improve kidney and cardiovascular outcomes in CKD. We conducted a scoping review of controlled implementation studies to identify effective strategies for improving CKD testing and GDMT delivery and define priorities for future implementation trials.

METHODS: Following a registered protocol and PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidance, we searched MEDLINE, Embase, and the Web of Science Core Collection from database inception through June 9, 2026 for English-language prospective controlled studies. Eligible studies compared an implementation strategy with usual care or another control condition. We charted study characteristics and outcomes using standardized templates and synthesized findings by objective, strategy, setting, design, and target population.

RESULTS: We included 26 reports from 24 studies (N=7 testing, N=17 treatment). Six of 7 studies increased CKD testing, with the largest gains from patient-directed home testing and automated laboratory ordering paired with clinical decision support. However, increased testing seldom translated into increased CKD diagnosis or GDMT prescriptions. Of implementation efforts focused on CKD treatment, only 5 of 17 studies increased GDMT prescribing. Passive, single-touch strategies, including isolated alerts, one-time prompts, and registries without active outreach, rarely changed prescribing. In contrast, longitudinal strategies that incorporated pharmacist- or advanced practice provider-led management, nephrologist-supported multidisciplinary care, or proactive registry-based outreach more consistently increased GDMT exposure and sometimes improved intermediate clinical outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Among 24 prospective controlled studies, patient-directed home testing and automated laboratory ordering paired with clinical decision support increased CKD testing, but increased testing seldom led to CKD diagnosis or GDMT prescribing. Only 5 of 17 treatment studies increased GDMT prescribing, all through longitudinal, team-based care.

articles.title: Unconfirmed Linear 18F-MFBG Uptake Along the Spinal Canal in a Pediatric Patient With Neuroblastoma: A Potential Diagnostic Pitfall.
articles.abstract: A 1-year-old girl with clinical and imaging features suggestive of neuroblastoma was enrolled in our prospective diagnostic trial. She underwent 18F-MFBG PET/CT for tumor characterization. On tomographic images, focal 18F-MFBG uptake, manifesting as an elongated linear pattern, was observed along the left aspect of the spinal canal spanning vertebral levels L2-L5. Contrast-enhanced MRI revealed no structural correlate. The source of this linear uptake remains uncertain. It may represent benign vascular activity, possibly involving the vertebral venous plexus, although this remains unconfirmed. Recognition of this potential pitfall is important to avoid misinterpretation as metastasis.

articles.title: Integrating Large Language Models Into Patient Health Education: Interview Study Among Nurses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Large language models (LLMs) have shown potential to support patient education, improve information accessibility, and assist with repetitive clinical communication tasks. However, the clinical integration of LLMs depends not only on technological capabilities but also on how these tools fit within existing health care workflows. Existing studies have largely focused on technical performance of LLMs or the experiences of physicians and patients, and little is known about how frontline nurses, who play a central role in patient education, experience LLM-supported education workflows in clinical practice settings.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore frontline nurses' experiences with an LLM-assisted patient education workflow, including perceived benefits, changes, challenges, and considerations for clinical practice.

METHODS: Semistructured interviews were conducted with 16 frontline hematological nurses between December 2025 and March 2026 at the Institute of Hematology and Blood Diseases Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences to explore their experiences. Data were analyzed using an inductive codebook thematic analysis, with codes and themes iteratively reviewed and refined through researcher discussions.

RESULTS: Nurses' experiences were characterized by 3 interconnected tensions. First, nurses perceived a balance between efficiency gains and information safety concerns, as the LLM-assisted workflow supported more efficient and standardized information delivery while requiring additional oversight. Second, nurses perceived changes in their roles and responsibilities, accompanied by increased demands for professional knowledge and competencies. Third, nurses perceived potential patient benefits of LLM use particularly in facilitating access to specialized health information, while identifying barriers related to limited health literacy and limited familiarity with LLM-based tools.

CONCLUSIONS: From nurses' perspectives, LLM use was perceived to support more efficient delivery of patient health information while also requiring attention to information safety, professional responsibility, and patient-related challenges. These findings highlight that nurses' roles remain important in supporting the safe and appropriate use of LLM-assisted education. Future research and implementation efforts should explore workflow-oriented design strategies for integrating LLMs into clinical nursing practice while considering nurse oversight, support clinical workflow adaptation, and address patient needs to support safe and appropriate use.

articles.title: Explainable AI to Guide the Design of Interpretable Prediction Models From High-Dimensional Data, Applied to Falls and Related Injuries in Adults Aged 50 Years or Older: Algorithm Development and Validation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transparent prediction models, such as Cox regression, remain the standard for clinical risk prediction. However, they are challenging to design optimally by hand when tens or even hundreds of features require selection, transformation, or interaction modeling. While complex machine learning models offer high performance, their "black-box" nature limits the clinical trust, transparency, and interpretability required for decision-making.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop an explainable AI-based recommender that provides data-driven feature-related recommendations that, when incorporated, improve the predictive performance of existing interpretable statistical models on high-dimensional data, and to demonstrate it by developing and internally validating a Cox model for the 1-year risk of falls or related injuries (FRIs).

METHODS: We used linked primary and secondary care records from DataLoch (Lothian, Scotland) for adults aged 50 years or older registered with a contributing general practice between January 2015 and February 2020. The outcome was the first FRI within 1 year of the index date. A random survival forest was explained with Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP), and its feature attributions were translated into recommendations for a Cox model: feature exclusions, nonlinear terms, and interactions. Data were split 80/20 into training and test sets. We compared the recommendations-augmented Cox model with the baseline Cox model, a Cox model with restricted cubic splines, and a penalized Cox model with all pairwise interactions. The metrics were Harrell concordance index (C-index), Uno C, calibration slope, and integrated Brier score. We repeated the analysis with all 409 available features and in 3 public datasets (German Breast Cancer Study Group 2 [GBSG2], AIDS Clinical Trial [ACT], and PeakVO2).

RESULTS: Of 220,341 patients (mean age 64, SD 12 years), 8489 (3.85%) had an FRI within 1 year. From 59 candidate features, the recommender excluded 15 (8 medication classes and 7 comorbidities). The final model retained 44 predictors (demographic and lifestyle factors, frailty, 21 comorbidities, and 15 medication classes), with nonlinear terms for age, frailty, BMI, and area deprivation, and interactions of age with stroke, osteoporosis, loop diuretics, and frailty. The augmented model had a C-index of 0.719 (95% CI 0.708-0.731) compared with 0.715 (95% CI 0.702-0.727) for the baseline model (difference 0.004, 95% CI 0.001-0.007), with 70 vs 73 parameters, and similar calibration (slope 0.962 vs 0.961). With all 409 features, the recommender recommended 304 exclusions, 4 nonlinear terms, and 2 interactions. The augmented model had a C-index of 0.722 compared with 0.713, with 129 vs 423 parameters, and better calibration (slope 0.952 vs 0.846). The method also proved effective on 3 additional public datasets, demonstrating wider applicability.

CONCLUSIONS: The proposed exploratory AI recommender demonstrates the potential of explainable AI to guide the design of transparent predictive models.

articles.title: Mobile Health Apps for Individuals Who Are Blind or Have Low Vision: Systematic Review of Evidence, Accessibility, and App Quality.
articles.abstract:
