BACKGROUND: Individuals who are blind or have low vision experience disproportionate burdens in both physical and psychological functioning, and mobile health apps may help address some of these needs. However, their availability, accessibility, and empirical support for this population remain unclear.

OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aimed to identify mobile health apps relevant to supporting physical and psychological functioning in individuals who are blind or have low vision, summarize the empirical evidence available for these apps, and examine their accessibility and quality.

METHODS: We used a multicomponent approach that combined (1) identification of apps through organizational recommendations; (2) a systematic search of the scientific literature, conducted and reported in accordance with PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidelines; and (3) an exploratory accessibility and app quality appraisal using the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.1 and the Mobile App Development and Assessment Guide.

RESULTS: A total of 19 unique mobile health apps were identified after combining and deduplicating apps identified through organizational recommendations and scientific literature. Fifteen apps were identified through organizational recommendations, and 14 empirical studies evaluating 11 apps were included in the qualitative synthesis. Only a subset of these studies specifically involved blind or low-vision participants; several evaluated apps in broader clinical or general populations where visual impairment status was not reported. The identified apps focused primarily on physical functioning, particularly medication management, glucose monitoring, pharmaceutical information access, and health care access. No apps primarily designed to support psychological functioning in individuals who are blind or have low vision were identified. Of 14 studies, 6 (43%) were rated as being of good methodological quality. The exploratory user-informed accessibility appraisal showed variability across apps: MyPills received the most favorable accessibility profile, with "High" ratings across all 4 Web Content Accessibility Guidelines principles, whereas several organizationally recommended apps received low ratings across most principles. Mobile App Development and Assessment Guide scores ranged from 8/39 to 34/39, with Medisafe scoring highest.

CONCLUSIONS: The current landscape of mobile health apps for individuals who are blind or have low vision remains limited, uneven in accessibility and quality, and supported by a limited and heterogeneous evidence base. The absence of identified apps targeting psychological functioning represents a particularly important gap. Improving the development and implementation of mobile health apps for individuals who are blind or have low vision will require more than increasing the number of available apps; it will require apps that are accessible from the outset, rigorously evaluated, and developed with the people they are intended to serve.

articles.title: Ocular Inflammation in Solid Organ Transplant Patients Receiving Maintenance Immunosuppression.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Patients are maintained on lifelong immunomodulatory therapy (IMT) after organ transplantation; however, new inflammatory conditions have developed in transplant recipients despite systemic immunosuppression. A prior study reported uveitis in transplant patients on IMT but did not describe clinical courses. We report the first case series describing nine cases of presumed non-infectious uveitis/scleritis in transplant recipients on IMT.

METHODS: Patients with a history of a solid organ transplantation who were diagnosed with uveitis and/or scleritis from June 2014 to June 2026 were identified. Inclusion required transplantation prior to uveitis/scleritis occurrence and ongoing IMT. Cases with a history of uveitis/scleritis prior to transplant, trauma/surgery, infection, or a history of autoimmune conditions causing uveitis were excluded. Nine cases met the criteria, and clinical characteristics-including transplant history and ocular disease course-were abstracted.

RESULTS: Nine transplant patients, including kidney (n = 6), pancreas and kidney (n = 1), and liver (n = 2) transplants, were included. The mean age was 46.9 years; patients developed uveitis or scleritis a median of 4 years after the most recent transplant. All patients were treated with topical or oral corticosteroids at a minimum. Six patients had a single episode of ocular inflammation, and three patients had recurrences. All episodes were corticosteroid responsive.

CONCLUSION: This case series describes presumed non-infectious ocular inflammation in solid organ transplant recipients receiving IMT, supporting a possibility of a broader pattern of post-transplant immune dysregulation. While patients in this series had steroid-responsive ocular inflammation, this phenomenon warrants further investigation to clarify mechanisms underlying new inflammation despite systemic immunosuppression, particularly because IMT agents are often employed in treating chronic uveitis.

articles.title: Rethinking Digital Outcome Measures for Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Trials: Consensus Priorities for Actigraphy Harmonization, Validation, and Regulatory Readiness.
articles.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) clinical trials need outcome measures that complement established end points while capturing how people function in daily life. In this viewpoint, we draw on our collective experience in ALS research, clinical trials, digital-measure development, and regulatory science, together with published evidence, a preliminary patient survey, stakeholder discussions, and experience from multisite actigraphy studies. We argue that the field now has a substantial base of longitudinal data and candidate measures, but lacks the coordinated framework needed to compare, prioritize, and validate them across studies. We identify 4 linked priorities: adopt fit-for-purpose measures in stages and within defined contexts of use; harmonize data collection and analysis; use data to shortlist and validate measures across cohorts; and prepare actigraphy methods for trial adoption through early industry and regulatory engagement. Across these priorities, actigraphy should complement rather than replace established clinical outcomes, with its integration guided by patient relevance, ALS phenotypic heterogeneity, participant, and caregiver burden, and the intended context of use. Our central message is that progress now depends less on generating additional isolated datasets or measures than on coordinating the evaluation of existing assets, and aligning future evidence generation.

articles.title: From patient to purpose: How a cancer diagnosis creates existential liminality to motivate crafting for work-related generativity.
articles.abstract: The life-threatening nature of cancer makes it a unique work-life shock event with distinctive implications for one's work and life. Drawing on inductive analysis of 50 employees with cancer, we theorize how this life-threatening, dynamic work-life shock event forces a reckoning with mortality that existing theory has not captured. This occurs through a process we label existential liminality, where people grapple with tensions of time and meaning, reflecting on what is meaningful in paid and unpaid work within an unknowable mortal timeline. When people have the cognitive space to engage in this process (i.e., when demands are manageable and resources are sufficient), existential liminality can catalyze crafting for generativity across paid and unpaid work. This work extends work-life shock events theory by revealing existential liminality as a unique sensemaking process that differs meaningfully from the identity-focused processes this theory describes. We also challenge the dominant death anxiety-based paradigm in the death awareness research by centering death reflection, a positive but undertheorized pathway with significant consequences for how people invest in work activities. Confronting death, we find, can prompt people to pursue a positive, lasting impact on others through work-related crafting for generativity. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

articles.title: Why Felids Are Prone to Chronic Kidney Disease: Micronutrient Cycling, Lipid Biology, and Water Conservation.
articles.abstract: The prevalence of chronic kidney disease (CKD) in aging felids is three- to four-fold higher than in other mammals, including humans. Regardless of species, serum and urinary biomarkers of CKD become effective only when little can be done to reverse progression. We propose that felids, as super water conservers and obligate hyper-carnivores, are naturally prone to form cytoplasmic lipid droplets (LDs) in their kidney cells, which predisposes felids to age-associated CKD. Furthermore, we offer a novel mechanistic basis for renal LD formation in felids. Presence of LDs in felid urine-lipuria, which is uncommon in all other mammals-could be the earliest biomarker of metabolic events in kidney cells that underpin CKD. Felids have unique anatomical, physiological, nutritional, and metabolic features, including synthesis and subsequent excretion of felinine together with branched-chain fatty acids into urine. These features offer a unique opportunity for early intervention but also are of interest in the context of comparative biology, nephrology, and renal disease.

articles.title: Rapidly Evolving Insulin Landscape: Ultrashort Acting and Ultralong Acting.
articles.abstract: Since the discovery of insulin in 1921, there has been remarkable evolution in insulin treatment for diabetes, with modern insulin analogues utilizing highly engineered recombinant technology. The purpose of this review is to focus on two revolutionary developments in contemporary insulin therapy: once-weekly ultralong-acting basal insulins and ultrashort-acting bolus insulins. Insulin icodec and insulin efsitora alfa represent a unique shift in basal insulin delivery, offering the convenience of once-weekly administration, flat pharmacokinetic profiles, and glycemic efficacy and safety comparable to those of daily basal analogues while reducing injection burden and improving patient satisfaction. With regard to bolus therapy, faster-acting aspart and ultrarapid lispro achieve accelerated absorption through novel excipient engineering, enabling more flexible mealtime dosing and improved postprandial glucose control compared to their traditional counterparts. Looking ahead, there are promising innovations on the horizon, including glucose-responsive insulins, artificial intelligence-driven automated insulin delivery, and the continued pursuit of oral insulin. Together, these advances represent an accelerating trajectory toward more physiological, convenient, and, most importantly, safe insulin therapy.

articles.title: Enhancing sexual health in women with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE): A mixed-methods systematic review of effective strategies.
articles.abstract: IntroductionSexual dysfunction is highly prevalent among women with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and significantly impairs quality of life, intimate relationships, and psychological well-being. Despite its clinical relevance, sexual health is rarely addressed in routine rheumatology care, and evidence on effective interventions remains fragmented.ObjectivesThis mixed-methods systematic review aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions for improving sexual health outcomes in women with SLE while qualitatively synthesizing barriers and patient perspectives to inform multidisciplinary care.MethodsThis review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines (PROSPERO ID: CRD420250652901). PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and ScienceDirect were searched for original studies published between 2000 and 2025. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials and qualitative research evaluating sexual health interventions in women with SLE. Methodological quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT, 2018). Due to heterogeneity in study populations, interventions, and outcome measures, findings were narratively synthesized.ResultsFive studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising four randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and one qualitative descriptive study. Non-pharmacological interventions-including Extended Permission, Limited Information, Specific Suggestions, and Intensive Therapy (EX-PLISSIT)-based sexual counseling, supportive-expressive psychotherapy and patient education-consistently improved sexual function and intimacy. Pharmacological interventions demonstrated mixed effects: low-dose dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) was associated with improvements in sexual function and mental well-being, whereas transdermal testosterone patches showed no significant benefit. Inadequate communication and lack of routine sexual health assessment by rheumatologists were identified as major barriers to care.ConclusionSexual dysfunction in women with SLE is common yet underrecognized. Non-pharmacological interventions, particularly psychosexual counseling, appear effective and accessible, while pharmacological evidence remains inconclusive. Integrating sexual health into multidisciplinary rheumatology care through systematic screening, education, and interprofessional collaboration is essential.

articles.title: AI-monitored bioadhesive for sutureless microvascular anastomosis.
articles.abstract: Microvascular anastomosis, the surgical suturing of small-caliber blood vessels, is technically demanding, time-consuming, and prone to failure from complications such as thrombosis. Existing adhesives are ineffective in the dynamic, wet surgical field, particularly for the limited cross-sectional interface of blood vessels. We present an integrated microneedle-interlocking adhesive system (iMAS) bioinspired by plant root anchoring. This platform combines a hydrophobic polymeric matrix with tetrahedral microneedles, creating robust, three-dimensional bonding for rapid, secure anastomosis. An embedded artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted wireless sensor enables continuous, real-time monitoring of vascular hemodynamics and cardiac graft health, facilitating predictive identification of complications such as stenosis and transplant rejection. In rat models, iMAS reduced procedural time by 78% and suppressed neointimal hyperplasia. iMAS streamlines microvascular anastomosis and enables proactive graft monitoring in transplantation.

articles.title: Outcomes and Prognostic Factors in Ectopic Cushing Syndrome: The Experience of Two Tertiary Referral Centers.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Ectopic Cushing syndrome (ECS) is an uncommon cause of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)-dependent Cushing syndrome associated with high morbidity and mortality. The aim of this study was to characterize patients with ECS and to identify potential prognostic factors associated with outcomes, including the clinical utility of serum inflammation-based scores (SIBS).

DESIGN: A retrospective observational study of 30 patients with ECS managed at two tertiary endocrinology referral centers.

METHODS: Demographic, tumor-related, clinical, and biochemical variables at diagnosis were analyzed. SIBS (neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio [NLR], platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio [PLR], lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio, and systemic immune-inflammation index) were calculated from baseline laboratory parameters.

RESULTS: Primary tumor sites were the lung (60%), pancreas (10%), thymus (3%), bladder (3%), adrenal gland (3%), and occult origin (20%). Metastatic disease was present in 65% of patients. Survival was markedly heterogeneous, with a median survival of 50.61 days. Tumor resection was associated with improved survival (HR = 0.225), whereas male sex (HR = 2.808), metastatic disease (HR = 15.82), ACTH (HR = 1.002), morning cortisol (HR = 1.023), and late-night cortisol concentrations (HR = 1.027) were associated with increased mortality risk. NLR positively correlated with ACTH (r = 0.575) and morning cortisol (r = 0.658), but none of the evaluated SIBS predicted survival.

CONCLUSIONS: ECS is characterized by a heterogeneous clinical course and poor early survival. Male sex, metastatic disease, and severe hypercortisolism are adverse prognostic factors for overall survival, whereas surgical resection is associated with better outcomes. Hormonal status correlates with inflammatory indices, but the prognostic value of SIBS requires further investigation.

articles.title: Long-term local circulation of an Andes virus lineage in northern Patagonia is linked to the M/V Hondius outbreak.
authors: International Consortium Investigating the M/V Hondius Outbreak
articles.abstract: In 2026, a hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) outbreak caused by Andes virus (ANDV) occurred on a cruise ship. Analyses revealed an unexpected relationship to an outbreak in Argentina in 2018. Retrospective investigation clarified the 2018 outbreak could involve person-to-person transmission and a common ANDV lineage spanned HPS cases from 2018 to 2025 in a geographically defined area in northern Patagonia, without widespread community transmission of ANDV. Route reconstruction for the index cases in the cruise ship outbreak identified geographically plausible exposures to viruses of this lineage in Argentina, but their timing was inconsistent with the expected ANDV incubation period. The infection source for the cruise ship outbreak cannot be resolved with current information, highlighting the need to expand viral surveillance in the ANDV endemic region.

articles.title: Federated, Accessible, Inclusive, and Responsive Virtual Biorepository: Delphi Consensus Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The reemergence of the Zika virus, the novel coronavirus, and new influenza strains highlighted the urgent need for an organized forum to access specimens to advance research, diagnostics, and vaccine development. During the COVID-19 pandemic, gaps in supply chains, communication, and standards between local (federated) and centralized systems cost time and lives. The FAIR-VBS (Federated, Accessible, Inclusive, and Responsive Virtual Biorepository) was proposed to connect communities with samples, address specimen-sharing challenges, and promote inclusion and equity.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to enable equitable contribution, sharing, and access to specimens while addressing the complexities involved. The objective is to build stakeholder consensus on prioritized actions, tools, and responsibilities to establish a functional and practical FAIR-VBS.

METHODS: A Delphi process was conducted online to gather stakeholder input and develop a prioritized action plan for the FAIR-VBS. Respondents were recruited using snowball sampling, and questions were informed by participatory workshops, feedback, outreach efforts, and discussions to identify gaps and best practices. The Delphi process consisted of 2 rounds: an initial ranking informed by stakeholder input and a second round to refine priorities based on the panel feedback. Items were evaluated using a standardized 5-point Likert scale and retained if prioritized by at least 70% of respondents rating an item 4 or higher and no more than 15% rating an item below 2, with descriptive statistics applied. Advisory board discussions supplemented the virtual process to capture nuances, while qualitative data were analyzed using participatory action research methods.

RESULTS: The Delphi process evaluated 34 cumulative items across 2 rounds to identify critical gaps and priorities in biorepository systems. In the first round, 22 out of 30 initial items successfully reached consensus. Panelists organically proposed 4 additional items during the first round; upon evaluation in the second round, 2 of these newly proposed items reached consensus, addressing benefit-sharing challenges (11/15, 73%) and the prioritization of whole blood, plasma, and serum samples (40/42, 95%). Culturally, peripheral blood mononuclear cells were supported as a secondary priority (13/18, 72%). In total, 24 items achieved consensus across both rounds, while 10 items overall did not. Respondents overwhelmingly supported the hybrid FAIR-VBS, which combines federated and centralized systems, offering local convenience with virtual oversight (34/41, 83%). Cost recovery for services was supported by all respondents (43/43, 100%), with a preference for a sliding fee scale to subsidize capacity building in low- and middle-income countries (40/42, 95%).

CONCLUSIONS: Respondents strongly supported the FAIR-VBS to enable equitable access to specimens, services, and benefits. They emphasized the need for clarity on benefit-sharing, regulatory, and ethical frameworks to ensure effective implementation and global inclusivity. A fair and equivalent system to enhance participation and operational continuity is being discussed.

articles.title: A scoping review of naturally occurring Chandipura virus in animal hosts and arthropod vectors.
articles.abstract: Chandipura virus (CHPV), an emerging rhabdovirus endemic to India, causes acute encephalitis, primarily in children. In 2024, India experienced its worst CHPV outbreak in 20 years (245 cases, 33% fatal). Sandflies (family Psychodidae, subfamily Phlebotominae) are considered the primary vectors, but experimental evidence suggests mosquitoes can support infection under laboratory conditions. Animal host species involved in natural transmission remain unknown. We conducted this PRISMA-guided scoping review to identify evidence of natural CHPV infection in animals and arthropods to assess surveillance and emergence potential. Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science and Google Scholar, and three Indian databases (Shodhganga, Krishikosh and CeRA), were searched using predefined terms. Eligible studies included peer-reviewed primary research detecting evidence of CHPV infection (antigen, RNA or antibodies) in arthropods and non-human vertebrate hosts, excluding experimental infection studies. Two reviewers independently screened records, then extracted data on species, location, detection methods and prevalence or seroprevalence. Of 451 screened records (747 total with 296 duplicates removed), 11 met the inclusion criteria. Direct evidence of CHPV infection was reported in phlebotomine sandflies in India, Senegal and Kenya, with low inferred infection prevalence even in outbreak-associated investigations. No evidence was found of natural CHPV infection in wild mosquito or tick populations. Indirect evidence of CHPV exposure (neutralising antibodies) was reported in several livestock species (cattle, buffalo, sheep, goats, pigs), dogs and wild toque macaques, and virus was isolated from a single African hedgehog. In conclusion, direct detection of CHPV in sandflies is consistent with their role as vectors, yet the broader animal host range, their role in virus maintenance and amplification, and the ecological drivers of transmission are incompletely understood. This review highlights the need for integrated One Health surveillance and targeted host-vector studies as globalisation and environmental change promote the spread and redistribution of competent vectors.

articles.title: Singapore grouper iridovirus VP018 exploits FTR86 to promote viral replication through Tollip-mediated degradation of the STING-TBK1 axis.
articles.abstract: Members of the tripartite motif (TRIM) family have been demonstrated to exert crucial roles in immune defense against pathogens. However, functions of the fish-specific TRIM subfamily (FTR), which lacks mammalian orthologues, remains poorly understood. In the current study, we investigated the potential roles of grouper FTR86 (EcFTR86) on innate immune response and its actions during fish virus infection. EcFTR86 was found to localize to lysosomes, and its transcription was significantly up-regulated in grouper spleen cells upon Singapore grouper iridovirus (SGIV) infection. Notably, the exogenous expression of EcFTR86 markedly enhanced SGIV replication, whereas knockdown of endogenous EcFTR86 significantly attenuated viral infection, demonstrating that EcFTR86 functions as a pro-viral factor against virus infection. EcFTR86 negatively regulated type I interferon signaling triggered by STING-TBK1 and interacted with the key molecules of STING-TBKl axis. Mechanistically, EcFTR86 degraded STING or TBK1 via an autophagy-lysosome-dependent pathway. Moreover, autophagic cargo receptor Tollip was identified to interact with EcFTR86, and was involved in EcFTR86-mediated degradation of STING or TBK1. In addition, EcFTR86 was verified to interact with SGIV viral proteins, including VP018 and VP075, whereas only VP018 exploited EcFTR86 to accelerate the degradation effects on STING and TBK1, thereby abrogating the interferon response. Collectively, our findings firstly showed that FTR86 functioned as a negative regulator of interferon response, and was exploited by fish iridoviral proteins to promote viral replication via Tollip-mediated autophagic degradation of the STING-TBK1 axis.

articles.title: Neural integration of acoustic statistics enables mice to detect acoustic targets in noise.
articles.abstract: Sound detection amidst noise presents an important challenge in audition. Many naturally occurring sounds (rain, wind) can be described and predicted only statistically, so-called sound textures. Previous research has demonstrated the human ability to leverage this statistical predictability for sound recognition, but the neural mechanisms remain elusive. We trained mice to detect vocalizations embedded in sound textures with different statistical predictability, while recording and optogenetically modulating the neural activity in the auditory cortex. Mice showed improved performance and neural encoding if they could sample the statistics longer per trial. Textures with more exploitable structure, specifically higher cross-frequency correlations improved behavioral performance as well as neural representation of vocalizations. Activating parvalbumin-positive (PV) interneurons had an asymmetric effect depending on the acoustic context, improving detection and neural encoding of vocalizations for low correlations, and impoverishing them for high cross-frequency correlations. In summary, mice exploit stimulus statistics to improve sound detection in naturalistic background noise, reflected in behavioral performance and neural activity, relying on PV interneurons for temporal integration.

articles.title: Tracking Consensus of Open Multiagent Systems With Lipschitz Nonlinearity and Actuator Attacks.
articles.abstract: This study investigates the tracking consensus problem of a class of open multiagent systems (oMASs) with Lipschitz nonlinearities and actuator attacks. The primary challenges arise from the presence of actuator attacks and nonlinearity terms, as well as the dimensional mismatch in error systems caused by the entry and departure of followers. To address these challenges, a full-order observer is designed to estimate the state of each follower, effectively eliminating the effect of attacks and nonlinear terms on the estimation. Two observer-based resilient controllers, supplemented by a dynamic compensator, are developed to achieve tracking consensus under bounded and unbounded actuator attacks while ensuring that the tracking error remains uniformly ultimately bounded (UUB). Furthermore, a novel additive-bound approach is introduced to tackle the dimensional mismatches in error systems caused by changes in the number of followers, ensuring stability by analyzing the error dynamics before and after switching instants. Finally, numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the theoretical results in maintaining consensus despite changes in the number of followers.

articles.title: Characteristics of EEG Microstate Analysis of Power Grip and Precision Grip Hand Movements from Motor Planning to Execution.
articles.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
articles.abstract: Hand movement is a fundamental daily motor behavior. Precision grip and power grip reflect distinct post-stroke recovery stages and neuroplasticity, making their neural mechanisms critical for motor control and neurorehabilitation. This study employed electroencephalographic (EEG) microstate analysis to investigate neural dynamic characteristics during motor planning and execution stages between precision grip (two-finger pinch, TP) and power grip (hand clenching, HC). High‑density EEG was acquired from 24 healthy participants across TP, HC, and resting states. Separate microstate analyses were conducted using an event-related potentials (ERP)-based approach for planning and an EEG‑based approach for execution. Results showed that nine ERP microstate templates identified during planning shared identical temporal sequences for both grips, with significantly longer duration of the fourth microstate (MS4) in TP than HC. During execution, four canonical microstates (MSA, B, C, and D) were extracted, which are generally associated with auditory processing, visual processing, default-mode network, and executive attention, respectively. Compared with HC, TP induces stronger suppression of MSC, greater activation of MSD, and distinct transition probabilities with enhanced shifts from MSA, MSB and MSC to MSD. Classification accuracy was higher in the execution stage, with Random Forest reaching 72.07% for TP versus rest. These findings indicate that precision and power grip present consistent temporal sequences of microstate templates during planning but undergo task-specific neural regulation during execution. Precision grip requires more extensive planning processing and stronger suppression of non-motor networks. This study reveals the spatiotemporal neural dynamics underlying different grip types, providing potential biomarkers for motor decoding and advancing neurorehabilitation and brain - computer interface applications.

articles.title: Learning Consensus Graph From Cross-Temporal Spectral Embeddings for Incremental Multiview One-Step Discrete Clustering.
articles.journal: IEEE transactions on neural networks and learning systems
articles.abstract: Practical data scenarios usually produce dynamic multiview data, such as user behaviors and sensor signals. Conventional clustering methods have two key defects. First, they need full recomputation for data updates, which reduces computational efficiency. Second, existing incremental methods separate view information fusion from discrete label generation, thus causing continuous error accumulation. To solve the above problems, this article proposes an incremental ultiview discrete spectral clustering (IMDSC) method. IMDSC builds a unified framework to jointly optimize dynamic consensus affinity graph construction, spectral embedding learning, and cluster label prediction, and it can adapt to evolving data and maintain stable clustering performance. Specifically, IMDSC adopts a weighted fusion strategy to build a consensus affinity matrix based on cross-temporal spectral embeddings, and it also preserves the geometric structure of the embedding space via graph regularization. To suppress the embedding space drift in incremental learning, this method introduces an orthogonal rotation matrix. This matrix aligns final spectral embeddings with discrete cluster indicators and eliminates the extra errors brought by the traditional $K$ -means postprocessing step in spectral clustering. Comparative experiments on multiple public benchmark datasets verify that the proposed IMDSC outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both clustering accuracy and computational efficiency.

articles.title: CPCLNet: Advancing Cross-Modal Few-Shot Medical Image Segmentation with Clustering-Inspired Prototype Consistency Learning.
articles.abstract: Cross-modal few-shot medical image segmentation (FSMIS) provides a solution for alleviating annotation scarcity and improving generalization across imaging modalities. However, severe modality discrepancy can disrupt support-query matching, contaminate support-derived foreground and background prototypes, and produce noisy affinity maps, making target-modality segmentation unreliable. To address this problem, we propose CPCLNet, a clustering-inspired prototype consistency learning network for cross-modal FSMIS. CPCLNet formulates cross-modal segmentation as a prototype consistency learning problem and progressively improves feature-space consistency, prototype reliability, and affinity-map coherence. Specifically, a parameter-sharing feature encoder provides a common representation basis across modalities, and a cross-modal distribution alignment module performs episode-specific support-query alignment. A clustering-inspired representative prototype descriptor further suppresses unstable support responses and constructs compact, modality-robust prototypes. Finally, an RWKV-based affinity map prediction module propagates prototype-guided correspondence across long-range spatial contexts with linear complexity. Extensive experiments on three imaging modalities, demonstrate that CPCLNet outperforms existing methods, achieving an average Dice improvement of 3.34 percentage points over the second-best competitor across CT→MRI and CT→PET tasks under both 1-shot and 5-shot settings. Further integration with MedSAM yields consistent improvements, indicating CP-CLNet's complementary potential with foundation models.

articles.title: Clinical-SAM: Agentic Test-Time Adaptation of SAM via Physician-in-the-Loop for Clinical Tumor Segmentation.
articles.abstract: Interactive foundation models such as SAM struggle to generalize across clinical deployment sites. Among existing adaptation strategies, test-time adaptation (TTA) is the most promising, yet current TTA methods trade one problem for another: removing the physician eliminates clinical grounding, while retaining the physician reintroduces a costly annotation burden. In this work, we propose Clinical-SAM, a two-phase agentic physician-in-the-loop TTA framework that teaches a frozen SAM to approximate what a physician would accept - directly and continuously, without requiring spatial annotations. In Phase I (pre-deployment), a self-prompting agent trained via reinforcement learning generates prompts autonomously, eliminating per-case expert spatial input at inference. In Phase II (deployment), the agent policy is refined online by the one signal physicians already produce: a binary accept/reject feedback on each proposed mask. As the binary feedback accumulates across deployed cases, the agent converges toward a policy that produces masks meeting a reference acceptance standard designed to approximate physician judgment, with progressively fewer interactions. We evaluate Clinical-SAM in a pre-clinical setting on six oncological benchmarks spanning CT (colon, pancreas, liver, kidney) and PET (head & neck, lung) tumor segmentation, using agreement with reference-standard segmentations as a proxy for physician acceptance. Clinical-SAM achieves state-of-the-art performance on all six datasets, outperforming fine-tuning, interactive, TTA, and online-learning baselines, while requiring only 3.3 binary judgments per case on average across the six datasets. Our code is available here.

articles.title: Web-Based Isha Kriya Meditation and Breathwork in Long COVID: Mixed Methods Randomized Controlled Pilot Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long COVID affects millions of adults, causing fatigue, dyspnea, cognitive symptoms, and mood disturbances. Effective treatments are limited, and many patients cannot access multidisciplinary rehabilitation because of symptom fluctuation, distance, or specialist shortages. Web-based mind-body interventions may offer accessible, scalable support alongside existing care.

OBJECTIVE: We assessed the feasibility and efficacy of a 3-week web-based yogic breathing and meditation program for long COVID symptoms.

METHODS: In this completed, parallel-group, 6-week waitlist-controlled, mixed methods randomized trial, adults aged 18-70 years with physician-confirmed long COVID were recruited from US clinics and self-referral and randomized 1:1 to immediate intervention or waitlist control, crossing over at week 3. The program included live webinars and video guides for daily self-practice. The primary outcome was adherence, defined as practicing at least 1 of 3 techniques on ≥4 days/week across all 3 active-intervention weeks. Secondary outcomes included perceived stressmood, quality of life, dyspnea, and somatic symptom burden, assessed at baseline, 3 weeks, and 6 weeks. Quantitative outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Semistructured interviews and focus groups underwent conventional content analysis and were integrated with quantitative findings via joint display.

RESULTS: Of 189 randomized participants, 1 was excluded post-randomization for a protocol deviation; 188 (96 intervention, 92 waitlist) began the study. Of these, 124 reached the active intervention period. Among 58 with complete adherence data, 55% met the adherence threshold (60% intervention, 50% waitlist). Secondary analyses included 185 participants with ≥1 assessment. No adverse events were reported. Compared with waitlist control, the intervention group showed greater reductions in total mood disturbance (MD=-10; 95% CI -19 to -1.6; P=.02), negative mood (MD=-7.5; 95% CI -15 to -0.44; P=.04), fatigue (MD=-2.9; 95% CI -4.6 to -1.2; P=.001), MDP immediate perception (MD=-5.5; 95% CI -9.4 to -1.6; P=.007), MDP sensory dimension (MD=-5.1; 95% CI -8.5 to -1.7; P=.003), and somatic symptom burden (MD=-2.0; 95% CI -3.6 to -0.38; P=.02), and greater increases in positive mood (MD=2.9; 95% CI 0.66 to 5.1; P=.01) and vigor (MD=1.7; 95% CI 0.18 to 3.2; P=.03). Stress and quality of life did not differ significantly. Qualitative findings identified medical-system struggles, digital delivery, online support, and practices' effects on resilience and identity. Integration showed convergence for dyspnea and mood, divergence for stress and quality of life, and expansion through themes of medical-system experience, identity, and social connection.

CONCLUSIONS: This web-based yogic breathing and meditation program appears feasible and accessible for people with long COVID. By combining 3 practices in a brief protocol and integrating quantitative and qualitative evidence, this study provides novel insight into both symptom outcomes and dimensions of recovery not captured by standardized measures. Further evaluation should assess longer-term effects and integration into scalable telehealth and virtual rehabilitation pathways.

articles.title: Computed Tomography-Derived Left Atrial Intramyocardial Fat and Low-Voltage Zones in Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Left atrial low-voltage zones (LVZs) are associated with atrial fibrosis and arrhythmia recurrence after atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation and are thought to underlie many recurrences despite durable pulmonary vein isolation. However, noninvasive markers of the arrhythmogenic atrial substrate remain poorly characterized. We sought to investigate the association between computed tomography (CT)-derived left atrial intramyocardial fat (inFAT) and electroanatomically defined LVZs.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this single-center retrospective study, 145 consecutive patients undergoing first-time radiofrequency AF ablation underwent preprocedural dual-source CT and high-density left atrial voltage mapping in sinus rhythm. LVZs were defined as contiguous regions with bipolar voltage < 0.5 mV. ADAS 3D post-processing was used to quantify total inFAT, dense inFAT, and fat-myocardial admixture. LVZs were identified in 51 patients (35.2%). Compared with patients without LVZs, those with LVZs had a higher prevalence of persistent AF (58.8% vs. 17.0%; p < 0.001) and a greater left atrial volume index (LAVi) (74.41 [64.87-99.50] vs. 62.99 [52.78-74.73] mL/m2; p < 0.001). Patients with LVZs also demonstrated larger volumes of total inFAT, dense inFAT, and fat-myocardial admixture, accompanied by lower radiodensity values of total and dense inFAT. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, persistent AF (adjusted odds ratio [OR]: 5.389; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.162-13.433; p < 0.001) and dense inFAT volume (adjusted OR: 3.439; 95% CI: 1.107-10.677; p = 0.033) remained independently associated with the presence of LVZs, whereas LAVi did not. Among the CT-derived fat metrics, only dense inFAT retained an independent association with LVZs after adjustment for clinical covariates.

CONCLUSION: CT-derived dense inFAT was independently associated with left atrial LVZs and may represent a novel noninvasive marker of the arrhythmogenic atrial substrate in AF. Prospective studies are warranted to determine its role in substrate-guided ablation strategies and risk stratification.

articles.title: Use of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Medications and Modified Medication Use Among Adults - United States, 2025.
articles.journal: MMWR. Morbidity and mortality weekly report
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists are medications that help regulate appetite, lower blood glucose levels, and promote weight loss. GLP-1 medications are approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for type 2 diabetes treatment, chronic weight management, and treatment of certain other health conditions. Data from CDC's Rapid Surveys System were used to examine GLP-1 medication use among U.S. adults. During July-August 2025, approximately one in 10 U.S. adults reported taking a GLP-1 medication during the past year. Among GLP-1 users, approximately one in five reported taking a compounded version. Compounded GLP-1 medications are not reviewed by FDA for safety, effectiveness, or quality before they are marketed. Approximately two in five GLP-1 users modified their use of the medication from the way it was prescribed, often citing cost and availability as barriers to prescribed use. Substantial prevalence of GLP-1 medication use highlights the expanded role of these medications in chronic disease pharmacotherapy. Modifications in medication use, particularly among younger adults, reflect, in part, responses to cost- and access-related challenges. Better understanding of real-world medication use, including dose and frequency adjustments, is important because it might have implications for safety and effectiveness.

articles.title: Resuscitation using fresh-frozen plasma is associated with improved contextual fear memory in a non-TBI mouse model of trauma and hemorrhagic shock.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cognitive dysfunction is a consequence of traumatic injury with lasting impacts. Even without direct brain injury, trauma and hemorrhagic shock (T/HS) can cause malperfusion, inflammation, and neuronal injury. Disruption of the endothelial glycocalyx (eGC), a key regulator of vascular homeostasis, contributes to trauma-induced endotheliopathy and may influence secondary neurologic injury. Prior work demonstrated that fresh-frozen plasma (FFP) resuscitation preserves eGC expression and reduces maladaptive vascular repair in a murine T/HS model. This study evaluates post-injury cognition and FFP protection against cognitive impairment compared with lactated Ringer's (LR).

METHODS: Male C57BL/6 mice were randomized to sham procedure or T/HS followed by a volume-driven LR or pressure-directed FFP resuscitation approach. T/HS mice underwent laparotomy, femoral artery cannulation, hemorrhagic shock, pseudofractures via bone homogenate injection, and hindlimb muscle crush injuries. Sham mice received laparotomy and femoral artery cutdown. Four days postsurgery, open field testing assessed locomotion, followed by fear conditioning on days 7 to 8 to assess cognition. Brains were collected to analyze hippocampal glycosaminoglycans hyaluronan, heparan sulfate (HS), and chondroitin sulfate (CS).

RESULTS: Open field testing showed intact locomotion at post-injury day 4 in all groups. On day 8, mice resuscitated with FFP had significantly greater contextual freezing compared with mice resuscitated with LR, consistent with improved hippocampal-dependent contextual memory. Cued fear conditioning did not differ between groups. LR and FFP resuscitation strategies resulted in distinct hippocampal hyaluronan and HS staining patterns, without synthesis gene expression differences. T/HS+LR brains showed increased 4-O-sulfated CS (CS-4S), a neurologically detrimental sulfation pattern, whereas FFP decreased CS-4S and increased CS-6S.

CONCLUSIONS: Goal-directed plasma resuscitation is associated with improved spatial memory and distinct eGC structural remodeling compared with volume-driven crystalloid resuscitation following T/HS. These findings highlight the potential for resuscitation strategy after hemorrhagic shock to influence neurological recovery, even in the absence of direct brain injury.

articles.title: FBXO45-mediated K63 ubiquitination of HYOU1 sustains UPR signaling and promotes chemoresistance in gastric cancer.
articles.abstract: The unfolded protein response (UPR), an evolutionarily conserved protective mechanism, promotes tumor progression and acquired drug resistance, yet how UPR dynamics drive resistance through post-translational regulation remains unclear. Here, we show that acquired chemoresistance in gastric cancer is closely associated with UPR activation and enrichment of heat shock proteins (HSPs). Among them, the endoplasmic reticulum chaperone hypoxia up-regulated 1 (HYOU1) is markedly upregulated during acquired chemoresistance. Immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry identified interactions among HYOU1, FBXO45, and PPM1B. Mechanistically, FBXO45 mediates K63-linked ubiquitination of HYOU1, recruiting additional HSPs under endoplasmic reticulum stress. HYOU1 ubiquitination enhances PPM1B accessibility, which inhibits dephosphorylation of the UPR sensors PERK and IRE1α, thereby sustaining persistent UPR activation. PPM1B functions as a key phosphatase of PERK/IRE1α in acquired resistance. Targeting the FBXO45-HYOU1-PPM1B axis restores drug sensitivity in chemoresistant models. These findings reveal how HSPs hijack the UPR via post-translational modifications to support tumor resistance and provide potential therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Longitudinal dynamics of gut microbiota maturation and its modulators from infancy through childhood.
articles.abstract: Early-life gut microbiota development is closely linked to long-term health. We characterize gut microbiota in 695 Copenhagen Prospective Studies on Asthma in Childhood 2010 (COPSAC2010) children using 16S rRNA gene sequencing of 2,689 fecal samples collected from 1 week to 6 years of age. Gut microbiota development is rapid during the first four years and gradually slows over the subsequent two years. A random forest model predicts microbial age from community composition and defines gut age-centered high- and low-maturity states. High-maturity microbiota exhibits greater alpha diversity, lower beta-dispersion, and maturity-associated network structures, reflecting enhanced community stability. We identify putative taxa with transient, persistent, or enduring associations with maturation. Pets, housing conditions, and maternal antibiotic use at birth show transient associations with maturation, whereas sibling presence and birth season show more sustained associations. 1-year microbiota composition predicts 4-year microbial maturity with modest but non-random performance. Our findings link early-life bacterial colonization and exposures to microbiota development and ecological stability.

articles.title: ZnuB as a targetable vulnerability to combat colistin resistance.
articles.abstract: Plasmid-mediated dissemination of mcr genes has severely compromised colistin efficacy, necessitating adjuvants that restore its antibacterial potency. Despite their essential roles in bacterial survival and virulence, metal ion acquisition systems remain underexplored as therapeutic vulnerabilities. Here, we identify the zinc-uptake gene znuB as a key determinant of colistin sensitivity. znuB deficiency enhances both the bacteriostatic and bactericidal activities of colistin. Mechanistically, znuB deletion upregulates leuO, driving ompS1- and dsbI-mediated membrane damage and oxidative stress upon colistin exposure. Concurrently, znuB loss elevates diacylglycerol levels, inhibiting MCR activity and potentiating colistin efficacy. Furthermore, we identify farrerol and ajmaline as potential inhibitors of both ZnuB and MCR proteins that effectively enhance colistin activity. In murine infection models, combination therapy improves survival and reduces bacterial burdens. Together, these findings demonstrate that targeting zinc homeostasis represents an effective strategy for reversing colistin resistance and combating multidrug-resistant bacterial infections.

articles.title: Molecular Epidemiological Characteristics of Clinical Isolates of CRKP Resistant to Imipenem/Relebactam.
articles.abstract: This study analyzed carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) isolates from a tertiary hospital to determine their level of resistance to imipenem/relebactam (IMR). A total of 174 CRKP clinical isolates collected between January 2023 and June 2024 were categorized, as IMR-sensitive (n = 151) or IMR-resistant (n = 23) based on broth microdilution minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs). No significant differences were found in patient demographics, comorbidities, or length of hospitalization between the two groups. The resistant strains mainly originated from sputum samples (78.3%) and intensive care units. Univariate analysis showed lower resistance to amikacin, cefepime, and tobramycin, higher rmpA detection, and lower blaCTX-M, iutA, and rmpA2 detection in resistant strains (unadjusted p < 0.05); however, none remained significant after FDR correction. Both groups were predominantly ST11, with the predominant capsular types being K64 and K25. These IMR-resistant CRKP strains exhibit multidrug resistance (except to polymyxin and tigecycline) and carry multiple resistance and virulence genes, highlighting the need for enhanced surveillance.

articles.title: From Statistics to Analytics: A Novel Quantum-Based Framework for Traffic Analyses.
articles.abstract: In the evolving landscape of advancements cities are developing rapidly. To meet basic needs people are increasingly using personal vehicles, which increases traffic and the complexity of driving. The primary goal of this research is to ingest, store, and analyze the traffic dataset using a novel technique. While surveying the existing methods it was found that data ingestion and management techniques were quite limited; the existing studies primarily focused on analyzing data using deep network architectures, which require higher computational resources due to their complex architecture. To overcome these gaps we proposed the incremental histogram and quantile partition as quantum approximate optimization algorithm (IHQ-QAOA) technique, which utilizes histogram binning and quantile techniques to ingest data more efficiently with minimal resources. The QAOA technique addresses the clusters by optimizing the cost and identifying the lane change behavior of the vehicles. We extracted insights to analyze traffic patterns using online analytical processing techniques (pivoting, drill-through, slicing, and dicing), which supported the segregation of features from section to lane level, resulting in better data visualization. The proposed techniques are compared with the state-of-the-art using the Next Generation SIMulation (NGSIM) and New Era of Urban Traffic Monitoring with Aerial footage (pNEUMA) datasets, resulting in an average data ingestion efficiency of 75.53%; for lane change analysis, the pNEUMA dataset was tested on a model trained on the NGSIM dataset, and overall accuracies of more than 0.96 were obtained. These achievements show that the suggested approach is reliable and effective for traffic data analysis.

articles.title: C/EBP-β-mediated upregulation of CaV1.2 calcium channel increases arterial constriction in mice with ibrutinib-associated hypertension.
articles.abstract: Ibrutinib, a Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitor, is indicated for treating chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), but hypertension is a common cardiovascular adverse event. Previous studies have linked ibrutinib to cardiac events through dysregulated intracellular calcium handling, but the mechanisms underlying ibrutinib-associated hypertension remain largely unknown. Here, we followed up 225 CLL patients receiving ibrutinib or managed with watch-and-wait strategy, and identified ibrutinib as an independent risk factor for hypertension. In mice, ibrutinib elevated arterial blood pressure (BP) without structural remodeling of small arteries, and it potentiated K+-induced vasoconstriction. In vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), ibrutinib upregulated CaV1.2 channel expression and function, as evidenced by enhanced CaV1.2 currents and K+-triggered-[Ca2+]i elevation. Mechanistically, ibrutinib suppressed casein kinase 2 (CK2)-mediated HSP90β phosphorylation, and stabilized C/EBP-β, which bound to the promoter of Cacna1c gene and drove CaV1.2 transcription. Significantly, C/EBP-β knockdown attenuated ibrutinib-induced CaV1.2 hyperactivity and vasoconstriction. Collectively, these findings reveal a CK2-HSP90β-C/EBP-β-CaV1.2 signaling cascade through which ibrutinib enhances vascular Ca2+ influx and vasoconstriction, thereby elevating arterial BP. Thus, this study nominates C/EBP-β as a therapeutic target for ibrutinib-associated hypertension.

articles.title: Epigenetic regulation of DOT1L methyltransferase activityremodels lipid metabolism to alleviate ferroptosis-induced liver injury.
articles.abstract: Epigenetic modifications contribute to lipid-related disorders by modulating the expression of key genes involved in lipid metabolism. Accumulating evidence suggests that lipid metabolism-mediated ferroptosis drives the progression of metabolic associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and liver injury. However, whether epigenetic mechanisms remodel lipid metabolism to regulate ferroptosis-induced liver damage remains unclear. Here, through pharmacological screening of epigenetics-related compounds and CRISPR-Cas9-based screening targeting epigenetic factors, we identified DOT1 Like Histone Lysine Methyltransferase (DOT1L) as a key sensitizer of hepatocytes to ferroptosis and subsequent liver injury, whereas inhibition of DOT1L reverses the phenomenon. DOT1L loss remodeled the phospholipid landscape by decreasing PUFA-containing phospholipids while increasing monounsaturated and lysophospholipid species. Mechanistically, DOT1L depletion reduced H3K79me1 and H3K79me2 occupancy at the PLA2G7, ALDH3B1, and PLCXD3 loci, particularly across gene-body regions, while increasing promoter-proximal accessibility and expression of these phospholipid-remodeling genes. These genes suppress ferroptosis by reducing the levels of phospholipids containing polyunsaturated fatty acids (PL-PUFAs). Furthermore, we demonstrated that AMPK phosphorylates DOT1L at Ser786, weakens its association with AF9, and suppresses H3K79 methyltransferase activity and ferroptosis sensitivity. Collectively, our findings reveal the AMPK-DOT1L-H3K79 methylation axis as a novel lipid metabolic pathway that regulates ferroptosis and maintains hepatic homeostasis, offering new therapeutic insights for ferroptosis-related liver injury.

articles.title: Phase 2a study of readthrough therapy in nonsense mutation Alport syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alport syndrome (AS), a Mendelian kidney disease, is caused by pathogenic mutations in the X- linked gene COL4A5 and autosomal genes COL4A3, COL4A4 encoding the alpha-chains secreted by podocytes to form the glomerular basement membrane collagen α3α4α5(IV) trimer. Nonsense mutations in autosomal recessive and hemizygous X-linked Alport syndrome (NMAS) introduce premature termination codons and have a particularly poor prognosis, with kidney failure typically occurring by early adulthood. There is substantial unmet need for effective therapy for AS, which has no approved treatments. Exaluren (formerly ELX-02) is a novel eukaryotic ribosome-targeted glycoside that is preferentially taken up by kidney cells and promotes readthrough of premature but not native termination codons, allowing full-length protein production.

METHODS: In this proof-of-mechanism study, three patients (ages 12-18) with autosomal recessive Alport syndrome and a COL4A4 premature termination codon received daily subcutaneous exaluren (0.75 mg/kg) for 8 weeks.

RESULTS: Safety and tolerability assessments (primary endpoint) revealed no new signals. Secondary endpoints assessed by kidney biopsy before and after treatment revealed increased collagen α3(IV), α4(IV) and α5(IV) abundance, physiologically localised collagen α5(IV), and partially improved podocyte morphology in all participants, with changes directionally concordant with increased collagen α3α4(IV) abundance. Proteinuria changes were inconsistent with interpretation limited by intra-patient variability and the short treatment duration; hematuria persisted in all participants.

CONCLUSION: These findings provide first-in-human evidence of exaluren-mediated collagen IV readthrough and justify further trials in Alport syndrome and other nonsense mutation-driven kidney diseases, which often cause early-onset kidney failure.

CLINICALTRIALS: gov Identifier: NCT05448755.

articles.title: Transcriptional regulation of NK cell state by ELF4 links innate immune licensing to kidney fibrosis.
articles.abstract: Fibrosis is a common outcome of chronic tissue injury, yet immune regulators that are conserved across species and translatable to human disease remain poorly defined. By integrating human kidney transcriptomes with multiple murine models of kidney fibrosis, we identified the ETS transcription factor ELF4 as a conserved, immune-enriched regulator associated with disease severity. ELF4 expression was highest in natural killer (NK) cells. Genetic deletion of Elf4, including NK cell-specific ablation, attenuated experimental kidney injury, with reduced inflammation, fibrosis, and loss of renal function. Single-cell and functional analyses showed that ELF4 deficiency disrupts late-stage NK cell maturation and broadly suppresses cytotoxic and interferon-γ (IFNγ) effector programs. Mechanistically, ELF4 directly sustains STAT1 transcription, maintaining a STAT1-TBX21 program required for NK cell maturation and effector competence. Consistent with this framework, NK cell depletion, IFNγ neutralization, or antisense-mediated suppression of Elf4 phenocopied renal protection. Together, these findings identify ELF4 as a transcriptional licensing factor that links NK cell state to kidney injury and highlight innate immune programming as a potential therapeutic entry point in chronic kidney disease.

articles.title: Treatment of Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Review.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Acute ischemic stroke, caused by thrombotic or embolic occlusion of a cervical or cerebral artery, leads to neurologic injury due to sudden disruption of blood flow to the brain. Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of disability and death and accounts for about 85% of strokes in the US.

OBSERVATIONS: Symptoms of acute ischemic stroke vary based on the area of the affected brain. Common presentations include sudden arm or leg weakness, aphasia or slurred speech, sudden loss of balance or coordination, sudden visual difficulties, and/or facial drooping. Patients with suspected stroke should be transported to the nearest emergency department for urgent brain imaging, typically noncontrast computed tomography (CT). Based on 2026 American Heart Association/American Stroke Association (AHA/ASA) guidelines, first-line therapy for patients with acute ischemic stroke presenting within 4.5 hours from symptom onset with disabling symptoms (eg, affecting the ability to perform activities of daily living) is intravenous thrombolysis (tenecteplase or alteplase) in those without intracranial hemorrhage or other contraindications to thrombolysis. The treatment window can be extended to 9 hours-and up to 24 hours in patients with large vessel occlusion (eg, involving the internal carotid artery or proximal middle cerebral artery [M1 segment]) who are unable to receive thrombectomy-based on identification of salvageable tissue using perfusion imaging with CT perfusion or magnetic resonance imaging. In appropriately selected patients with acute ischemic stroke, pooled randomized trial data show an approximately 10% absolute increase in the probability of a better functional outcome with intravenous thrombolysis. Based on 2026 AHA/ASA guidelines, endovascular thrombectomy, which involves clot removal with an intra-arterial mechanical device, is recommended for patients with large vessel occlusion within 6 hours of stroke onset (class 1 recommendation) and is recommended in selected patients with large vessel occlusion within 24 hours of last known well (class 1 recommendation). Endovascular therapy should be performed after intravenous thrombolysis unless patients have contraindications to thrombolytic therapy. Compared with medical management, which includes intravenous thrombolysis when indicated, endovascular thrombectomy produces an approximately 20% absolute increase in functional independence.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Acute ischemic stroke causes substantial disability and mortality. First-line therapy for patients with disabling acute stroke symptoms is intravenous thrombolysis (if no contraindications) within 4.5 hours of stroke onset and up to 24 hours in carefully selected patients not receiving mechanical thrombectomy; for large vessel occlusions, mechanical thrombectomy may be performed up to 24 hours after stroke onset in eligible patients.

articles.title: Effect of magnesium bisglycinate following coronary syndrome in young adults: a retrospective cohort study of self-reported sleep quality, anxiety symptoms, and depressive symptoms.
articles.abstract: Anxiety, depression, and poor sleep are common after acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and adversely affect prognosis, yet treatment options are limited. Oral magnesium bisglycinate improves sleep and mood in non-cardiac populations but has not been studied following ACS. We investigated whether post-discharge magnesium bisglycinate use is associated with improvement in self-reported sleep quality and anxiety and depressive symptom scores. In this single-centre retrospective cohort, 120 patients (68 magnesium, 52 comparator) were followed for three months after ACS. Magnesium bisglycinate (240 mg elemental magnesium daily) was initiated at the first post-discharge visit. The primary outcome was sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, PSQI); anxiety (Beck Anxiety Inventory, BAI) and depression (Beck Depression Inventory, BDI) were secondary outcomes, assessed with serum magnesium at baseline and three months. Baseline characteristics were comparable. At three months, the magnesium group showed greater improvement in self-reported sleep quality (PSQI: 5.2 ± 2.6 vs 7.3 ± 3.1; p < 0.001), anxiety (BAI: 12.1 ± 4.9 vs 15.8 ± 5.3; p < 0.001), and depressive symptoms (BDI: 8.3 ± 4.7 vs 11.2 ± 5.5; p = 0.003), with Cohen's d = 0.57-0.74. Serum magnesium did not differ between groups at either time point (p = 0.55 and p = 0.20), and the associations persisted after multivariable adjustment and in sensitivity models including baseline serum magnesium, renal function, and medications affecting magnesium balance. Post- discharge magnesium bisglycinate use was associated with greater improvement in self-reported sleep, anxiety, and depressive symptom scores following ACS. These hypothesis-generating findings, limited by residual confounding and healthy-user bias, require confirmation in an adequately powered randomized controlled trial.

articles.title: Clinical behaviors of efficient emergency physicians: insights into what they actually do -a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Efficiency in the emergency department is critical for patient care and flow, yet it is a challenging competency to develop and is inconsistently taught in emergency medicine residency programs. This review focused on identifying strategies and behaviors of efficient emergency physicians that can be observed and taught.

METHODS: A scoping review was conducted from January 1, 2015, to July 1, 2025 following the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology, to identify key behaviors of efficient emergency physicians. Medline/PubMed, Embase, Google Scholar, and gray literature were searched using controlled vocabulary, and included all types of methodologies except editorials and commentaries. Data were extracted using a standardized, structured process within the Covidence platform by two independent reviewers.

RESULTS: After screening 6343 articles, 20 articles met full inclusion criteria. A clear and universally accepted definition of emergency department efficiency was not identified. Consequently, the included studies used a heterogeneous range of proxy measures to evaluate efficiency-related outcomes. Although no study directly demonstrated a specific set of strategies that improve efficiency, six major themes emerged. Efficient physicians showed greater effectiveness in communication, targeted investigations, documentation strategies, and clinical teaching skills. In addition, they employed specific cognitive and physical strategies like flow management and movement efficacy. Each theme yielded behaviors that either promoted or impeded efficiency.

CONCLUSION: Although our review identified a limited number of articles linking specific physician behaviors to efficiency metrics, it provides insights into behaviors and strategies that can be taught and observed in emergency physicians. Collectively, the identified strategies suggest that efficiency may largely depend on optimizing the initial patient encounter through communication, clinical reasoning, and shared decision-making. These findings represent the first step in a broader initiative aimed at developing a standardized observational tool to support the development of efficiency in emergency physicians.

articles.title: Sex-based analysis of characteristics, management, and outcomes of patients presenting to the emergency department with syncope.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Syncope is a common emergency department (ED) presentation and can be caused by serious conditions not evident on initial ED evaluation. Research into sex-based differences among ED patients presenting with syncope is lacking. We sought to compare clinical characteristics, management, risk stratification and serious outcomes between male and female ED syncope patients, assess the impact of sex on outcomes after adjusting for comorbidities and Canadian Syncope Risk Score predictors, and evaluate the change in performance of the Canadian Syncope Risk Score with the addition of sex.

METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of the Canadian Syncope Risk Score derivation and validation study cohorts, comparing patient characteristics, ED management and outcomes between male and female patients presenting with syncope, using descriptive statistics and logistic regression models.

RESULTS: Of 9539 total patients, 5190 (54.4%) were female. Male patients were older, had more comorbidities, received more testing in the ED, had longer lengths of stay, were more frequently hospitalized and were more likely to have serious outcomes than females. The association between male sex and serious outcomes persisted after controlling for age, arrival by ambulance, hypertension, diabetes, coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation or flutter, valvular heart disease, and congestive heart failure (OR=1.73, p<0.001) and Canadian Syncope Risk Score predictors (OR =1.45, p=0.005). However, adding sex to the Canadian Syncope Risk Score model did not significantly increase the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (difference = 0.0002, p=0.90).

CONCLUSION: Male ED syncope patients tended to have more risk factors than females, underwent more investigations, and were more likely to have serious outcomes even when controlling for comorbidities. While clinicians should recognize these sex-based differences, they can continue to rely on the Canadian Syncope Risk Score in its current form for risk stratification as incorporating sex did not improve model performance.

articles.title: Creating Consensus: Establishing a Definition of Sports Pharmacy and Its Emerging Role in Sports Medicine.
articles.abstract: Sports pharmacy has become an increasingly recognized specialty within the broader pharmacy profession and serves as a complementary discipline to sport medicine. Yet, the field has lacked a formally established, internationally accepted definition. The absence of standardized terminology has hindered academic integration, interprofessional collaboration, and policy development. This work aimed to establish the first consensus-derived definition of sports pharmacy, accompanied by a responsibility statement to guide future education, certification, and research. In 2024, the US Sports Pharmacy Group (USSPG), comprising pharmacists, academics, anti-doping professionals, student pharmacists, and competitive athletes from diverse US states and international settings, convened a discrete subgroup, the Define Sports Pharmacy Taskforce, to lead the development of a formal definition of sports pharmacy. The taskforce conducted a thematic analysis of existing literature and reviewed 123 open-ended member responses collected between 2022 and 2024. Eight recurring practice themes emerged and informed iterative drafting cycles. Draft definitions were subsequently reviewed by interprofessional stakeholders, including physicians, elite athletes, and anti-doping practitioners. The resulting definition emphasizes medication management, anti-doping advocacy, interprofessional collaboration, athlete-centered ethical care, and the use of therapeutic and pharmacological strategies to optimize performance, support recovery, and protect sports integrity across all levels of physical activity. This consensus-derived framework provides standardized terminology to support the development of educational pathways, establish certification standards, and promote the integration of pharmacists into athlete support teams.

articles.title: Maximal Aerobic Capacity and Aging in Female Masters Athletes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maximal aerobic capacity ( V ˙  O2max) represents the highest rate at which the body can use oxygen during intense exercise and is a key determinant of endurance performance. Although age-related declines in V ˙  O2max have been well documented in male individuals, less is known about this trajectory in female Masters athletes, defined as individuals aged 40 years or older who often engage in lifelong endurance training.

OBJECTIVE: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to quantify cross-sectional age-related differences in directly measured V ˙  O2max among female Masters endurance athletes.

METHODS: PubMed and Web of Science were searched from database inception to 14 May, 2025 for studies reporting directly measured V ˙  O2max in female Masters endurance athletes aged 40 years or older. Eligible exercise modalities included running, cycling, swimming, and large muscle-mass ergometry, with testing conducted under standard environmental conditions. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using a modified Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. Pooled mean V ˙  O2max values were calculated for predefined age groups (40-49, 50-59, 60-69, and 70 years or older) using a random-effects meta-analysis. Meta-regression was used to estimate the relationship between age and V ˙  O2max.

RESULTS: Sixty-nine studies, including 1903 female Masters athletes, met the inclusion criteria. Pooled mean relative V ˙  O2max was 45 mL·kg-1·min-1 (95% confidence interval [CI] 43.0-46.8) in athletes aged 40-49 years, 40 mL·kg-1·min-1 (95% CI 38.5-41.7) in those aged 50-59 years, 35 mL·kg-1·min-1 (95% CI 33.2-37.1) in those aged 60-69 years, and 30 mL·kg-1·min-1 (95% CI 27.2-31.8) in athletes aged 70 years or older. Meta-regression demonstrated that each additional year of age was associated with a 0.57 mL·kg-1·min-1 lower V ˙  O2max (95% CI - 0.70 to - 0.44; P < 0.0001), equivalent to about 11.7% per decade. The association was consistent across testing modalities.

CONCLUSIONS: This systematic review and meta-analysis demonstrates a progressive age-related decrease in directly measured V ˙  O2max among female Masters endurance athletes. Maximal aerobic capacity declines at an average rate of 0.57 mL·kg-1·min-1 per year after age 40 years, corresponding to approximately 11.7% per decade. This decline is evident across endurance sport disciplines and appears consistent with physiological changes associated with aging despite sustained endurance training. These findings provide female-specific reference values and a quantitative framework for future studies on aerobic capacity trajectories in female athletes.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: The protocol was registered on the Open Science Framework (OSF; https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/S2RXZ ).

articles.title: Pathogen-specific salvage of totally implantable ports and the role of antibiotic lock therapy.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Totally implantable venous-access ports (TIPs) are central to cancer therapy, but bloodstream infection (BSI) frequently ends in device loss. Device retention rests on systemic antibiotic therapy, to which antibiotic lock therapy (ALT) can be added, yet the determinants of successful salvage in adults are poorly defined. This study examined which TIP infections can be salvaged.

METHODS: 233 consecutive episodes of TIP-related BSI at a tertiary cancer centre (2017-2020) were analysed retrospectively. The primary outcome was successful TIP salvage: retention of a functioning device with clinical cure. Determinants were assessed by logistic regression and salvage across protocol-defined pathogen categories was tested for trend.

RESULTS: Isolates were Gram-positive in 58%, Gram-negative in 38% and fungal in 4%; 19% polymicrobial. The TIP was salvaged in 68/225 episodes (30%); primary explantation commonest (53%). Salvage fell across the protocol categories: coagulase-negative staphylococci 41%, Gram-negative bacilli/enterococci/other Gram-positives 35%, S. aureus/P. aeruginosa/Candida 2% (P for trend < 0.001). Independent predictors were a high-virulence pathogen (adjusted odds ratio 0.04, 0.01-0.30) and a peripheral arm port (0.29, 0.13-0.65); no comorbidity or severity factor was robustly associated with salvage. ALT, attempted in 79/221 episodes (36%), was not associated with higher salvage among retention attempts (55% vs. 68% with systemic antibiotics alone, odds ratio 0.57, 0.25-1.29).

CONCLUSION: TIP salvage was associated with the infecting organism. The pathogen gradient mirrored guideline-based removal recommendations. About 60% of attempted retentions succeeded, without detectable benefit of ALT. With a pathogen-stratified protocol, salvage can be attempted in selected patients.

articles.title: Risk factors and bacterial epidemiology of recurrent bloodstream infections-a population-based cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Recurrent bloodstream infections (BSI) represent a significant clinical challenge, yet recurrence patterns and predictive factors remain poorly defined. We aimed to identify risk factors for BSI recurrence and characterize its microbiological and temporal patterns.

METHODS: We conducted a population-based retrospective cohort study of all patients with confirmed BSI in 2017 in Skåne, southern Sweden. Recurrent BSI was defined as a positive blood culture within one year of the index BSI, either > 48 h apart for different species or > 14 days for identical species. Patients with recurrent BSI were included along with controls matched on blood culture date who experienced a single BSI and were discharged alive. We performed multivariable logistic regression, analysed species concordance between index and recurrent BSI, and examined time to recurrence by index bacterial group.

RESULTS: Of 3,918 BSI episodes, 416 (10.6%) recurred within one year, with a median time to recurrence of 63 days (IQR 31-151); 60% occurred within 90 days. Independent risk factors included higher Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) (OR 13.9, 95% CI 4.11-50.4 for ≥ 6), immunosuppression (OR 1.96, 1.24-3.12), invasive procedures within the previous 6 months (OR 3.83, 2.12-7.15), undrained infection site at discharge (OR 2.22, 1.08-4.71) and septic shock (OR 4.05, 1.52-11.9).

CONCLUSIONS: Bloodstream infection (BSI) recurrence affects over 10% of patients, most often within three months. Independent risk factors included CCI ≥  6, immunosuppression, recent invasive procedures, undrained infection sites and septic shock. These findings support individualized follow-up in high-risk patients, and further studies should target modifiable risk factors.

articles.title: A Biomimetic gut-on-a-chip Integrated with Multi-Omics Reveal the Mechanism of Listeria monocytogenes Infection Microenvironment-Stimulated In Situ Bacteriocin Production by Lactiplantibacillus paraplantarum RX-8.
articles.abstract: Bacteriocins produced in intestine by lactic acid bacteria (LAB) can suppress pathogens and support homeostasis, offering potential against foodborne bacterial infections. However, complex in vivo intestinal milieu hampers monitoring of bacteriocin production and its regulation during enteric infection. Herein, we developed and first applied a three-dimensional gut-on-a-chip with an intact mucus layer, robust barrier function, and stable immune homeostasis to dynamically examine bacteriocin biosynthesis during infection. Compared with its bacteriocin gene-deletion mutant, L. paraplantarum RX-8 reduced adherent L. monocytogenes by 2.69 lg CFU/mL, preserved mucin and tight-junction integrity, and suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokine release, highlighting the anti-infective role of in situ-produced plantaricin. Although infection modestly reduced L. paraplantarum RX-8 density, it reshaped plnA dynamics, enhanced plnBCD, plaRX, pfs, and luxS transcription, AI-2 activity, and plantaricin RX-8 production 2.25-fold, suggesting coordinated regulation by intraspecies PlnA and interspecies LuxS/AI-2 quorum-sensing (QS) systems. Integrated multi-omics analysis linked this QS-associated phenotype to metabolic, environmental-sensing, and transport reprogramming. Enhanced carbohydrate uptake, pyruvate oxidation, electron transport, and riboflavin metabolism may support ATP generation, redox homeostasis, and stress adaptation.
