Sulfur-containing amino acid metabolism may shift from de novo synthesis toward the activated methyl cycle and AI-2-associated processes, while altered two-component signaling, ABC transport, and SecYEG/YidC-associated export may enhance signal sensing, nutrient acquisition, and plantaricin biosynthesis and secretion. Finally, infection-responsive sRNA0019 was predicted to target plnA and luxS, suggesting a candidate post-transcriptional regulatory layer for both QS systems. These findings provide multilevel insights into bacteriocin biosynthesis during intestinal infection, supporting the efficient application of bacteriocin-producing LAB.

articles.title: Efficacy, Acceptability, and Tolerability of Trazodone in Insomnia Symptoms: A Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Trazodone is widely prescribed off label for insomnia symptoms, but the dose range that best balances efficacy with acceptability and tolerability remains uncertain. This systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis evaluated trazodone for insomnia symptoms, with emphasis on clinically relevant dose selection.

METHODS: We searched Embase, PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library from inception to 17 November 2025, for randomized controlled trials comparing trazodone with placebo or different trazodone doses in patients with insomnia symptoms. Dose-response relationships were evaluated using a one-stage random-effects model with restricted cubic splines. The primary outcome was subjective sleep quality; secondary outcomes were all-cause dropout rate and dropout due to adverse events.

RESULTS: Thirteen randomized controlled trials involving 1366 participants were included. Compared with placebo, trazodone moderately improved subjective sleep quality (Cohen's d = 0.67, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.36-0.98; I2 = 80.86%; p < 0.01). The dose-response curve suggested that efficacy increased at lower doses and approached a plateau around 50 mg/day, although estimates in the higher-dose range were sparse and imprecise. The estimated 50% effective dose was 15.2 mg/day, and the 95% effective dose was 38.2 mg/day, but these estimates should be interpreted as exploratory rather than as precise dose targets. Conventional meta-analysis showed no clear difference in all-cause discontinuation or discontinuation due to adverse events, whereas dose-response analysis suggested a possible dose-related increase in adverse event-related discontinuation.

CONCLUSIONS: Trazodone was associated with short-term improvement in subjective sleep quality among heterogeneous populations with insomnia symptoms. The most observable benefit appears to occur at relatively low doses, while dose escalation may offer limited additional benefit and reduce tolerability. However, interpretation of the findings is limited by considerable clinical heterogeneity, sparse evidence at higher doses, and insufficient data on long-term efficacy and safety.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD420251232065.

articles.title: Humanistic Burden of Sjögren's Disease: A Systematic Review of Treatment Efficacy on Health-Related Quality of Life.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sjögren's disease (SjD) is a chronic autoantibody-driven inflammatory disorder that imposes a significant burden on afflicted patients. SjD is widely underappreciated, underdiagnosed, and undertreated. This may be partly due to the absence of advanced targeted treatments addressing the root cause of the disease. While some drugs are prescribed to help improve symptoms, many patients report inadequate relief, with disease progression and frequent organ damage. This systematic literature review (SLR) assessed the effects of treatments on patients' health-related quality of life (HRQoL). This study was supplemented by a patient focus group to gain additional insight into the humanistic burden of SjD.

METHODS: The SLR was conducted using MEDLINE and Embase (OvidSP) results between January 1, 2014, and February 2, 2026, supplemented with bibliographies, Google Scholar, disease-specific websites, and conference proceedings. Articles were screened specifically for HRQoL outcomes, including patient-reported disease-specific instruments (e.g., EULAR Sjögren's Syndrome Patient-Reported Index [ESSPRI]) and other tools focusing separately on fatigue and ocular/oral dryness. A small patient focus group (N = 4) provided further perspectives on disease burden and management.

RESULTS: Fifty-three records were identified from 44 unique studies related to systemic treatments, including large case series and randomized controlled trials of traditional immunomodulatory or anti-inflammatory agents and newer biological treatments (e.g., rituximab, abatacept, hydroxychloroquine, leflunomide, corticosteroids, iguratimod, dazodalibep, telitacicept). Most systemic treatments provided no meaningful improvements in fatigue or ocular/oral dryness. SjD focus group participants reported persistent, overlapping symptoms, particularly fatigue and cognitive impairment, that limit daily activities. Participants expressed dissatisfaction with current treatments and a strong desire for holistic therapies that address the root cause, improve symptoms, and prevent disease progression.

CONCLUSIONS: Systemic treatments have generally focused on disease activity parameters and have shown limited efficacy in reducing patient-reported symptoms as measured using HRQoL tools in SjD, leaving a significant unmet need for patient-centered holistic therapies.

articles.title: Prescription Coverage Following Initiation of HIV Pre-exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) in a National Cohort of United States Veterans.
articles.abstract: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) is 99% effective in preventing HIV infection when used as prescribed, but barriers to initiation and coverage limit its impact. U.S. military Veterans should have improved access to PrEP through the Veterans Health Administration (VHA). However, limited data suggests that most Veterans who are vulnerable to HIV are not prescribed PrEP, and many do not continue PrEP even when clinically indicated. Our study utilized administrative and pharmacy data from VHA electronic health records (EHR) to identify U.S. Veterans prescribed PrEP between 2021 and 2024 and describe patterns in PrEP initiation and number of days covered by PrEP based on demographic characteristics and social determinants of health over the course of one year. Male Veterans made up 86.6% (n = 12,655) of those prescribed PrEP, and women had significantly fewer days covered by PrEP than men (97 days vs. 205 days, β=-62.0, p < .001). Compared to White, non-Hispanic Veterans (209 average days on PrEP), Hispanic/Latino Veterans had significantly fewer days covered by PrEP (185 average days on PrEP, β=-10.9, p < .001). While increased engagement and integration within the VHA medical system may facilitate PrEP initiation and coverage, disparities persist across sex, race, and other sociodemographic and clinical variables.

articles.title: Lutein Targets TLR4 as a Potential Immunotherapeutic Strategy for Treatment of Doxorubicin-Induced Cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract: Toll-like receptor 4 is an immune receptor associated with inflammatory diseases, including cardiac conditions. Lutein, a natural carotenoid with potent anti-inflammatory effects, protects against coronary heart disease and other cardiovascular issues. We aimed to explore its potential cardioprotective effects against doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy (DIC), focusing on the TLR4/NF-κB and JAK/STAT pathways. We compared its effects with olmesartan, commonly used to manage DIC. This study was performed on five groups of rats: control, doxorubicin (Dox)-treated, lutein-treated, olmesartan-treated, and combination-treated groups. Induction of DIC was performed using Dox (4.5 mg/kg every other day) for ten days. In treatment groups, lutein (50 mg/kg/day) or olmesartan (10 mg/kg/day) was administered for 10 days alongside Dox, while the combination treatment group co-administered lutein (50 mg/kg/day) and olmesartan (10 mg/kg/day) for the same duration alongside Dox. The results indicated that lutein protected cardiomyocytes from Dox-induced histopathological changes, including myocardial fiber disorganization, vascular congestion, and perivascular edema. It decreased the levels of TLR4, NF-κB, p-JAK2, and p-STAT1/3 relative to the Dox group, exhibiting an anti-inflammatory effect through suppression of the TLR4/NF-κB and JAK/STAT pathways. It also had regulatory effects on Akt/mTOR signaling, another pathway linked to TLR4 activation. In comparison to olmesartan, lutein had superior effects on IL-6/JAK2/STAT1/NF-κB and Akt/mTOR levels. Combination treatment also demonstrated cardioprotective effect at histopathological, biochemical, and molecular levels, being more effective than olmesartan on IL-6/NF-κB and Akt/mTOR levels. Moreover, Lutein administration alongside Dox showed anti-inflammatory and cardioprotective effects against DIC, suggesting it as a promising adjunct therapy, either alone or with olmesartan.

articles.title: Endothelin Receptor Antagonists in CKD-Associated Resistant Hypertension: Trial Lessons, Safety Boundaries, and Conditions for Future Clinical Testing.
articles.journal: American journal of cardiovascular drugs : drugs, devices, and other interventions
articles.abstract: Resistant hypertension in chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains a common and difficult-to-treat phenotype after confirmation of true resistance, exclusion of pseudoresistance, and optimization of standard multidrug therapy. Endothelin receptor antagonists (ERAs) have re-entered this space largely through aprocitentan, a dual ETA/ETB receptor antagonist that provides modest but significant blood-pressure lowering in resistant hypertension. However, the clinical interpretation of this class remains constrained by edema/fluid retention, absence of direct comparison with spironolactone, and lack of established hard renal or cardiovascular outcome benefit in CKD-associated resistant hypertension. This Current Opinion reframes the ERA evidence as a set of trial-design lessons rather than as broad class rehabilitation. ASCEND showed that albuminuria reduction is insufficient when exposure and congestion risk are poorly controlled. SONAR demonstrated the value of response and tolerability enrichment. PRECISION clarified the incremental blood-pressure effect of aprocitentan on standardized background therapy, while confirming clinically relevant edema risk. ZENITH-CKD suggests that low-dose ERA strategies combined with SGLT2 inhibition may improve tolerability and testability. The practical implication is a narrow and monitored phenotype: rigorously confirmed resistant hypertension, CKD with residual cardiorenal risk, absence of unstable heart failure or marked natriuretic-peptide elevation, and capacity for close surveillance of weight, edema, renal function, hemoglobin, and albuminuria. At present, aprocitentan should be viewed as a selective add-on option rather than a routine fourth-line default, while future trials should test ERA strategies against contemporary guideline-based comparators and prespecified congestion-risk algorithms.

articles.title: Factors Associated with Vaginal Birth After Cesarean (VBAC): An Analysis of 2019 to 2023 U.S. Birth Certificate Data.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC) is a recommended delivery option for women with a history of one or two cesarean sections. Compared to repeat cesarean deliveries, VBAC is associated with better maternal and infant outcomes. Despite these benefits and national initiatives aimed at reducing unnecessary cesarean deliveries, VBAC rates remain low in the U.S. Research has shown that access to VBAC varies significantly by race, ethnicity, and socioeconomic status. This study aims to examine demographic, socioeconomic, and obstetric factors associated with VBAC in the U.S between 2019 and 2023 and assess whether these associations differ across race groups.

METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted using de-identified U.S. birth certificate data from the National Vital Statistics System (2019-2023). The study sample included 2,580,713 women with one or two prior cesarean deliveries, of whom 420,367 had a vaginal birth after cesarean. Sequential block logistic regression was performed for each year. Race-stratified analyses were conducted using the pooled 2019-2023 data to assess demographic, socioeconomic, and obstetric factors associated with VBAC.

RESULTS: Increased maternal age, Hispanic ethnicity, private insurance, and lower educational attainment were generally associated with lower VBAC odds. Stratified analyses revealed significant within-group differences, including reversals in associations with maternal age and education across some race groups. VBAC rates modestly increased over the study period, though disparities remained.

DISCUSSION: While VBAC is considered a beneficial delivery option, this study shows that it is not equitably utilized. These utilization gaps may point toward opportunities to increase national VBAC rates.

articles.title: Should I pursue a PhD in radiology? Opportunities, pitfalls, and practical strategies.
articles.abstract: Undertaking a PhD in radiology represents a pivotal career choice: one that can open pathways to international mobility, interdisciplinary collaboration, and scientific discovery. This opinion piece examines the opportunities and challenges of pursuing doctoral training in radiology and provides guidance for medical students, radiographers, residents, and practicing radiologists considering this academic path. Yet the process also entails risks: unrealistic goals, inadequate mentorship or institutional support (such as protected time for research, administrative support, and financial resources), and limited genuine motivation can hinder progress and satisfaction. In this expert opinion article, we highlight the natural synergy between clinical radiology and research skills. Beyond advancing academic credentials, a PhD cultivates competencies in statistics, leadership, and teamwork: skills that support careers across academia, healthcare, industry, and policy. We discuss different PhD formats, from monograph-based to publication-based structures, and offer practical advice on project selection, funding strategies, and supervisory relationships. We conclude with an overarching checklist with a compilation of questions to answer the question "Should I pursue a PhD in radiology?." By addressing both pragmatic and personal aspects, including mental well-being, this paper provides a balanced roadmap for (future) imaging professionals aiming to design meaningful and sustainable clinical research careers. KEY POINTS: Question Deciding whether to pursue a doctoral degree in radiology requires navigating complex trade-offs between clinical workloads, personal motivations and diverse program formats. Findings Successful doctoral training relies on aligning personal curiosity with realistic project scoping, accessible methodological support and careful supervisor selection. On the other hand, valuable alternative career paths and potential obstacles should also be considered before taking up the PhD challenge. Critical relevance statement Aligning personal goals, skills, and career planning with the institution's expectations can help (future) imaging professionals transition into sustainable research careers.

articles.title: Real-World Impact of Maralixibat Treatment on Concomitant Medication Use in USA-Based Patients with Alagille Syndrome and Cholestatic Pruritus: A Retrospective Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Alagille syndrome (ALGS) is a rare cholestatic liver disease characterized by severe pruritus, with many patients also experiencing impaired growth, failure to thrive, and fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies. Patients often require multiple antipruritic medications to control pruritus and may also receive nutritional or vitamin supplements to address nutritional deficiencies and improve growth, leading to substantial polypharmacy burden. Maralixibat, a minimally absorbed ileal bile acid transporter inhibitor, is approved for the treatment of cholestatic pruritus in patients with ALGS ≥ 3 months of age in the USA and ≥ 2 months of age in the European Union (EU). This study evaluated real-world concomitant medication usage during long-term maralixibat treatment using pharmacy data from Mirum Access Plus, a single-source specialty pharmacy and education program for patients receiving maralixibat.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted using pharmacy data from the Mirum Access Plus program to evaluate concomitant medication trends for at least 2 years of potential use. Data were extracted on April 30, 2024, and included all patients in the USA who initiated maralixibat by April 1, 2022, and had not discontinued therapy.

RESULTS: This analysis included 178 patients with ALGS who received maralixibat. The median age at maralixibat initiation was 6 years. At the start of maralixibat treatment, patients were taking a median of two antipruritic medications and one nutritional or vitamin supplement. During maralixibat treatment, 43% of patients discontinued ≥ 1 concomitant medication, 21% discontinued ≥ 2 medications, and 8% discontinued ≥ 3 medications.

CONCLUSIONS: These real-world results indicate treatment with maralixibat may reduce polypharmacy burden in patients with ALGS and their caregivers by enabling discontinuation of antipruritic medications and nutritional or vitamin supplements.

articles.title: Modeling the Impact of Monthly Titration of Once-Weekly Insulin Icodec in Insulin-Naive Type 2 Diabetes: Analysis Based on ONWARDS 1 and 3.
articles.journal: Diabetes therapy : research, treatment and education of diabetes and related disorders
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To explore whether monthly titration of once-weekly insulin icodec (icodec) could provide a feasible alternative to the weekly titration utilized in ONWARDS 1 and 3 for insulin-naive individuals with type 2 diabetes (T2D), supporting less-frequent dose adjustments tailored to individual needs.

METHODS: A validated pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic icodec model was adapted using pooled ONWARDS 1 and 3 data to simulate weekly and two different monthly titration scenarios, applying the same initiation dose and self-measured blood glucose (SMBG) target used in the trials. Scenarios 1 and 2 used ± 20 U and ± 50 U adjustments, respectively, informed by the last three fasting SMBG values. Simulations of fasting SMBG, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), icodec dose, and clinically significant (level 2) hypoglycemia were performed over 78 weeks.

RESULTS: At week 78, model-predicted mean (95% range) HbA1c was 7.3% (6.2-9.2%) for scenario 1 and 7.2% (6.0-8.9%) for scenario 2, versus 6.9% (5.9-8.4%) for the weekly titration reference. Model-predicted mean (95% range) prebreakfast SMBG was 7.3 mmol/L (6.0-9.8 mmol/L) and 7.1 mmol/L (5.6-9.3 mmol/L) versus 6.6 mmol/L (5.3-8.3 mmol/L), respectively. Predicted cumulative rates of clinically significant (level 2) hypoglycemia were 0.081 (scenario 1) and 0.15 (scenario 2) events per patient-year of exposure (PYE), both numerically lower than the already low rate predicted for the weekly titration (0.34 events per PYE). These lower predicted rates occurred alongside lower predicted icodec doses.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings support the feasibility of monthly titration of icodec as an alternative to weekly titration for individuals with T2D who require or prefer less-frequent dose adjustments. Prospective clinical evaluation is needed to confirm these model-based findings.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers: NCT04460885 (ONWARDS 1), NCT04795531 (ONWARDS 3).

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Biosimilar Insulin Aspart (Rapilin®) Versus Originator (NovoRapid®) in Type 1 Diabetes: A Multicenter, Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Diabetes therapy : research, treatment and education of diabetes and related disorders
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Data on the biosimilar insulin aspart Rapilin® ("Biosimilar") in patients with T1DM, particularly in children and adolescents, remain scarce. This study compared the real-world efficacy and safety of Biosimilar and the originator insulin aspart NovoRapid® ("Originator") in patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM).

METHODS: Electronic medical records from 34 hospitals in China covering the period from January 1, 2023 to January 31, 2026 served as the data source for this multicenter, retrospective cohort study. A total of 229 patients with T1DM who had been receiving continuous Biosimilar (n = 116) or Originator (n = 113) treatment for ≥ 12 weeks were included. The primary endpoint was the change in glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) from baseline to the last measurement before January 31, 2026. Treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were collected and classified.

RESULTS: Of the 229 included patients, 112 (48.9%) were men. The Biosimilar and the Originator groups had a mean age of 24.88 ± 17.73 years and 30.69 ± 20.84 years, respectively. The Biosimilar and the Originator groups had significant and comparable HbA1c reduction from baseline (adjusted least squares means - 1.90% vs - 1.59%; difference - 0.32%, 95% confidence interval [- 0.94%, 0.31%], P = 0.322). Furthermore, the Biosimilar group showed a marginally significant trend toward a higher HbA1c target (< 7.0%) achievement rate than the Originator group (P = 0.056). Changes in fasting blood glucose, total daily insulin dose, and daily prandial insulin dose were comparable between groups. The incidences of TEAEs (37.1% vs 38.9%), including level 1 to 3 hypoglycemia and diabetic ketoacidosis, were comparable between the Biosimilar and Originator groups. However, patients receiving Biosimilar had significantly lower incidence of injection-site reactions than patients receiving Originator (0.0% vs 5.3%, P = 0.014).

CONCLUSION: Biosimilar showed comparable glycemic control, dose stability, and systemic safety to Originator in a diverse T1DM cohort containing a substantial proportion (50.0%) of pediatric and adolescent patients.

articles.title: Model-Based Economic Evaluations of Interleukin Pathway Inhibitors for Moderate-to-Severe Plaque Psoriasis: A Systematic Review of Model Structures, Assumptions, and Methodological Quality.
articles.journal: Applied health economics and health policy
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To systematically review model-based economic evaluations of interleukin pathway inhibitors for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, with a focus on model structures, key assumptions, parameter sources, economic conclusions, methodological rigor, and reporting completeness.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched from database inception through July 10, 2026, for full model-based economic evaluations in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in which at least one evaluated strategy included an interleukin (IL)-12/23, IL-17, or IL-23 inhibitor. Model architecture, health states, treatment sequences, sources of key parameters, and approaches to uncertainty were extracted a priori, and methodological features were compared through narrative synthesis. Methodological quality and reporting completeness were appraised using the Philips checklist and the Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards 2022 (CHEERS 2022), respectively. Economic findings were synthesized separately for QALY-based cost-utility analyses and Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) response-based cost-effectiveness analyses.

RESULTS: Twenty-six economic evaluations met the inclusion criteria. Thirteen used Markov or state-transition models, five used decision tree-Markov hybrids, two used decision trees, four used cost-effectiveness models without a stated formal architecture, and two used patient-level or other simulation models; 14 explicitly modeled multi-line treatment sequences. Twenty-four evaluations used evidence from randomized controlled trials as effectiveness inputs, and 19 incorporated network meta-analysis or mixed-treatment comparison estimates. Twenty-one conducted formal deterministic sensitivity analyses, with one additional evaluation reporting a limited one-way analysis; 20 conducted probabilistic sensitivity analyses, and 16 reported cost-effectiveness acceptability curves. Only four studies explicitly described tests of model logic, and none systematically compared alternative model structures; subsequent-line effectiveness and patient heterogeneity were also inconsistently addressed. Economically, 16 evaluations were QALY-based cost-utility analyses and 10 were PASI response-based cost-effectiveness analyses. No drug or treatment sequence was consistently optimal across countries; conclusions varied primarily with comparator choice, drug prices, willingness-to-pay thresholds, short-term response rates, and sequencing assumptions.

CONCLUSIONS: Existing models increasingly represent long-term, multi-line treatment pathways, but their treatment of prior treatment history, subsequent-line effectiveness and discontinuation, structural uncertainty, and model validation remains inadequate. Future evaluations should incorporate previous biologic exposure, long-term drug survival, and locally relevant utility and resource-use data, and should explicitly test important alternative model structures. Current economic conclusions are strongly model- and context-dependent; cross-country rankings should not be inferred without accounting for specific prices, thresholds, and treatment sequences. PROSPERO Registration: CRD420261413139.

articles.title: Chronic heavy metal exposure and chronic kidney disease: integrating epidemiology, mechanisms, biomarkers, and interventions.
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects over 800 million people globally. Emerging evidence suggests that chronic heavy metal exposure is a significant yet underappreciated environmental contributor. However, critical uncertainties persist. These include the precise shape of dose-response relationships, whether single-metal guidelines adequately reflect real-world mixtures, and how to translate mechanistic insights into practice. This review synthesizes evidence across epidemiology, mechanisms, biomarkers, and interventions to address these gaps. Large-scale observational studies consistently report associations between cadmium, lead, and arsenic exposure and higher CKD risk and faster eGFR decline. However, causality remains uncertain because most evidence is observational, and reverse causation and residual confounding cannot be ruled out. Dose-response curves often exhibit nonlinear features, including U-shaped and threshold patterns. Several studies have reported interactive or joint associations for metal mixtures at concentrations below some study-specific reference values, although evidence for biological synergism and regulatory inadequacy remains limited. These findings raise concerns that single-metal guidelines may not fully capture mixture effects. Candidate urinary biomarkers such as KIM-1, NGAL, and NAG have been proposed as candidate early markers of tubular injury. However, prospective studies must establish their incremental predictive value, reference ranges, reproducibility, discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility before routine clinical use can be recommended. Translational strategies, including nutritional antagonism, environmental source control, and emerging therapies, show promise in mitigating nephrotoxicity. This review offers three main contributions: a proposed integrative mechanistic framework that treats oxidative stress as one node within a broader network and epigenetic persistence as a hypothesis requiring human validation. A critical synthesis of mixture toxicity that raises the possibility, but not proof, that single-metal standards may not fully capture mixture effects. And a research agenda for evaluating candidate biomarkers as potential early markers, pending prospective validation. Integrating causal inference, mechanistic research, biomarker evaluation, and public health measures may help reduce the burden of metal-related kidney disease and inform potential revisions of environmental safety standards, but current evidence remains insufficient to assert causality or mandate regulatory change.

articles.title: Association between methylmalonic acid and vascular calcification in patients with chronic kidney disease: an observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Methylmalonic acid (MMA) has been regarded as a risk factor for cardiovascular diseases. However, the association between MMA and vascular calcification (VC) in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains unclear.

METHODS: Patients with CKD stage 5 were included and classified into either non-VC, mild VC, or severe VC groups. Restricted cubic splines (RCS) analysis and ordinal logistic regression were performed to examine the relationship between MMA and VC. Moreover, independent external validation was performed based on the NHANES dataset.

RESULTS: A total of 144 patients with CKD were involved, among whom 82.6% had VC. Compared with individuals without VC, serum MMA levels were elevated among those with VC, especially in the severe VC group (P=0.012). RCS analysis revealed an approximately positive linear relationship between MMA and VC (P-nonlinear=0.11). After adjusting for all covariates, each 1 ng/mL increase in serum MMA was associated with 13% higher odds of being in a more severe VC category (OR=1.13, 95%: 1.05-1.22, P=0.001). Additionally, subgroup analyses indicated that the direction of association between MMA and VC was consistent across different age, gender, hypertension, and diabetes groups (P for interaction was 0.77, 0.65, 0.83, and 0.34, respectively). Finally, results were confirmed in the NHANES cohort (n=326).

CONCLUSION: High levels of MMA have a positive association with the risk of VC, particularly severe VC. This study may provide a novel risk marker for VC in patients with CKD.

articles.title: Sclerostin actions in bone and metabolic disease.
articles.abstract: Sclerostin, a 24 kDa glycoprotein secreted primarily by matrix-embedded osteocytes, plays an essential role in the maintenance of bone mass. Sclerostin acts as a suppressor of bone mass accrual through its inhibitory effects on Wnt/β-catenin signaling, which is most dramatically observed in the rare bone overgrowth conditions associated with SOST gene loss of function in humans and laboratory models. In recent years, a second extra-skeletal function for sclerostin has emerged due to its presence in the circulation and the association between serum levels and metabolic indices. Indeed, genetic and pharmacologic inhibition of sclerostin reduces the accumulation of adipose tissue mass and improves insulin sensitivity in mouse models. In this review, we provide an overview of both the basic science and clinical studies that serve as a rationale for the targeting of sclerostin in the treatment of bone loss and describe pre-clinical research focused on sclerostin's actions as a bone-derived endocrine factor that contributes to the skeleton's influence on systemic metabolism and integrative physiology.

articles.title: Assessment of atrioventricular interaction and response to balloon pulmonary angioplasty in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension using cardiac MRI.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate atrioventricular interaction in patients with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) and to determine the effects of balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) on reversible cardiac remodeling assessed by cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective single-center study, 52 patients with CTEPH (mean age: 58 ± 11 years; 34 females) and 35 healthy controls underwent CMR imaging. Twenty-five patients (mean age: 60 ± 12 years; 19 females) who underwent BPA received follow-up CMR at a mean interval of 7 ± 5 months. Cardiac structure, function, myocardial deformation, and epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) were assessed based on cine images.

RESULTS: Compared with controls, patients with CTEPH demonstrated predominant right-sided cardiac involvement, characterized by reduced right ventricular ejection fraction (p < 0.001), marked enlargement of right atrial (RA) and ventricular (RV) volumes, and severely impaired right heart strain (all p < 0.001). Left ventricular systolic function was relatively preserved, with mildly impaired global circumferential strain (p = 0.011) and a trend toward attenuated longitudinal strain (p = 0.055), whereas all left atrial (LA) strain components were markedly impaired (all p < 0.05), indicating altered atrioventricular interaction. Following BPA, the right heart structure, RV function and deformation, and LA conduit strain improved. EAT was comparable between groups and remained unchanged after BPA.

CONCLUSION: CTEPH involves marked right heart systolic dysfunction and early biventricular diastolic abnormalities associated with impaired atrioventricular interaction. BPA could reverse cardiac remodeling by improving right heart structure, function, and partially recovering atrial deformation after pressure relief.

KEY POINTS: Questions Atrioventricular interaction abnormalities and reversible cardiac remodeling in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) after balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) remain insufficiently characterized. Findings CTEPH is associated with impaired right heart strain and altered atrioventricular interaction; BPA improves right heart structure and function and partially recovers atrial deformation. Critical relevance statement Cardiac MRI-derived myocardial deformation and atrial phasic function may reflect alterations in atrioventricular interaction in CTEPH and complement conventional metrics in assessing cardiac remodeling and recovery after BPA.

articles.title: Exploring the potential of herbal nanotechnology for the treatment of urinary tract infections.
articles.abstract: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) continue to pose a substantial clinical challenge due to high recurrence, biofilm-mediated persistence, and the rapid expansion of antimicrobial resistance. The waning effectiveness of conventional antibiotics highlights the urgency for resistance-sparing therapeutic strategies. Recent advances in herbal nanotechnology have enabled the precise nanoengineering of plant-derived phytochemicals, enhancing their stability, bioavailability, and pathogen-specific activity. This review critically appraises nanomaterial-based phytotherapeutic approaches for UTI management, focusing on the mechanistic integration of phytochemical bioactivity with nanoscale delivery systems. Nanomaterials developed from medicinal plants, crude extracts, and isolated phytoconstituents are evaluated for their ability to interfere with uropathogen adhesion, dismantle biofilms, suppress virulence signaling, induce oxidative stress, and regulate host inflammatory responses. Translational barriers, including formulation reproducibility, safety assessment, scalable production, and regulatory compliance, are also examined. By consolidating antimicrobial, antibiofilm, and host-modulatory evidence, this review identifies nano-enabled phytotherapeutic strategies with translational promise as multi-target alternatives to antibiotic-based UTI therapy.

articles.title: Premature immune aging in obesity: a testable framework linking immunosenescence, metaflammation, and multiorgan dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Obesity is a chronic immunometabolic disorder associated with alterations in biological aging pathways and increased risks of type 2 diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, chronic kidney disease, neurodegeneration, and cancer. Obesity and chronological aging share several characteristics, including low-grade inflammation, cellular senescence, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, epigenetic alterations, and immune remodeling. However, these similarities do not necessarily establish accelerated biological immune aging. This review critically evaluates obesity-associated immunosenescence, metaflammation, and multiorgan dysfunction by examining supporting and conflicting findings, alternative explanations, methodological limitations, and therapeutic evidence. Although experimental and observational studies report alterations in lymphocyte differentiation, innate immune function, inflammatory signaling, and selected biological-age markers, these findings are not uniformly observed across immune-cell populations, tissues, or metabolic phenotypes. Metabolically healthy obesity, tissue-dependent epigenetic aging, and differences between human and animal findings challenge the interpretation of obesity as a universal accelerator of immunosenescence. Furthermore, chronological age, cytomegalovirus infection, sex-related differences, adiposity distribution, and metabolic comorbidities complicate attributing immune alterations specifically to obesity. The proposed immunosenescence-metaflammation-multiorgan dysfunction framework therefore remains a testable mechanistic hypothesis rather than an established causal pathway. Although immune-cell phenotypes, epigenetic clocks, inflammatory mediators, and multi-omics signatures may help characterize obesity-associated immune dysfunction, their specificity, longitudinal validity, and clinical utility remain insufficiently established. Nutritional interventions, exercise, bariatric surgery, and pharmacological treatments can improve selected metabolic and inflammatory outcomes, but these improvements do not necessarily demonstrate sustained reversal of biological immune aging. By critically comparing supportive evidence with contradictory observations and unresolved causal relationships, this review identifies the principal limitations of current mechanistic, biomarker, and therapeutic research. Future studies should prioritize longitudinal immune profiling, direct functional assessment, tissue- and sex-specific analyses, causal validation, and controlled interventions incorporating validated immune-aging endpoints to determine whether premature immune aging is a measurable and therapeutically modifiable consequence of obesity.

articles.title: Family Resilience Model-Based Analysis of Factors Influencing Depression Among Parents of Young Children With Neurodevelopmental Disorders in Korea.
articles.journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to analyze the effect of parenting stress perceived by parents of preschool-aged children with neurodevelopmental disorders on depression, using the family resilience model (FRM) and to determine the mediating effect of family protection and the moderating effect of family vulnerability.

METHODS: The participants were 122 mothers with children younger than 7 years diagnosed with neurodevelopmental disorders. Data on general characteristics, parenting stress, family resilience, developmental rehabilitation costs, and depression were collected using self-report questionnaires. Statistical analyses were conducted using SPSS Statistics 26 and Process Macro 4.2.

RESULTS: Parenting stress was found to have a significant effect on depression. Family resilience was identified as a protective factor and mediated the relationship between developmental rehabilitation costs and depression. Additionally, developmental rehabilitation costs moderated the relationship between parenting stress and depression.

CONCLUSION: The findings reveal the relationships among parenting stress, family resilience, and developmental rehabilitation costs in relation to depression among parents of preschool children with neurodevelopmental disorders. Furthermore, the FRM serves as a useful theoretical basis for identifying factors influencing the emotional adaptation of these parents.

articles.title: Treatment Intensity Predicts Target Mastery and Developmental Change in Early Intensive Behavioral Intervention.
articles.journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To examine whether prospectively recorded, delivered one-to-one treatment intensity predicted learning and developmental outcomes in children receiving Early Intensive Behavioral Intervention (EIBI).

METHODS: Thirty-nine autistic children receiving EIBI were followed for 18 months. Delivered treatment hours and mastered treatment targets were recorded weekly. Between-child analyses tested whether each child's average weekly intensity predicted average targets mastered per week and 12-month change in the Learning Accomplishment Profile-Third Edition (LAP-3) developmental index. Descriptive child-week analyses examined associations between weekly intensity and target mastery.

RESULTS: Average intensity predicted average targets mastered per week, accounting for 45.5% of the variance (N = 39, p < .001), and remained predictive after adjustment for baseline chronological age and developmental index. Across 1,970 positive-hour child-weeks, greater weekly intensity was descriptively associated with more mastered targets. Average intensity and average target mastery also predicted 12-month change in LAP-3 developmental index.

CONCLUSION: Higher delivered one-to-one intensity was associated with faster target mastery and greater developmental-index change. Because intensity was not experimentally assigned and weekly observations were nested within children, the findings support prediction rather than causal inference or a universal optimal dose.

articles.title: Precision Neurology in Alzheimer's Disease: Genomics to Drug Optimization for Effective Therapeutic Intervention.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) exhibits high clinical and biological heterogeneity, which complicates the development of one-size-fits-all therapeutic strategies. Standard trial designs can mask subgroup-specific effects, highlighting the need to move towards precision neurology entailing multisystem genomics, biomarkers, and artificial intelligence (AI) integrative signals. The aim of the study is to critically synthesize and evaluate emerging strategies for drug optimization and individual therapeutic algorithms informed by genomic architecture, pharmacogenomics (PGx), and polygenic risk scores (PRS) with the opinion to resolve the controversy and unanswered question. Amplify the convergence into amyloid processing, lipid metabolism, and innate immunity seen from monogenic mutations and over 80 GWAS risk loci. Genotyping of CYP2D6 and CYP2C19 variants permits pharmacogenomic stratifications for the optimization of cholinesterase inhibitor and psychotropic dosing, thereby reducing adverse events. Variants of the alleles APOE ε4 and immune-related factors (e.g., FCGR3A) are significant in predicting the effects of ARIA associated with amyloid on anti-amyloid immunotherapy outcomes. PRS and deep phenotyping (including digital and fluid-based biomarkers) allow for the identification of unique biological endotypes (e.g., tau-dominant vs. vascular-inflammatory) that improve clinical trial enrichment and prognostication. This framework delineates molecular endotypes and translates CYP2D6 or APOE stratification into drug dosing and ARIA risk predictions. These biomarker-driven strategies shift AD management from a passive, reactive therapeutic scheme to an active, personalized one. Utilization of high-dimensional data streams via AI-driven learning health systems converts AD management from a reactive, symptom-based model to that which is proactive and hallmark biomarker-driven precision.

articles.title: Feasibility of High-Intensity Interval Training Before, During, and After Cancer Treatment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To systematically evaluate the feasibility and safety of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) interventions in cancer populations across the cancer care continuum (before, during, and after cancer treatment).

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to 31 December 2025. Studies were included if they enrolled adults with cancer, implemented a HIIT intervention, and reported feasibility outcomes. Recruitment, adherence, and dropout outcomes were calculated as study-specific proportions with 95% confidence intervals and pooled using random-effects models with REML estimation. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 for RCTs and MMAT for non-randomized studies, while certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE.

RESULTS: Twenty-two studies were included, comprising 559 participants in HIIT groups. Pooled recruitment across 20 studies was 0.57 (95% CI: 0.41-0.72), pooled adherence across 21 studies was 0.91 (95% CI: 0.86-0.95), and pooled dropout across 20 studies was 0.11 (95% CI: 0.06-0.16). Recruitment showed considerable heterogeneity, whereas adherence and dropout showed moderate heterogeneity. No statistically significant subgroup differences were observed by study design, intervention setting, treatment phase, or exercise frequency. Adverse events were reported in six studies, with no serious adverse events.

CONCLUSIONS: HIIT appears feasible and safe for individuals with cancer, particularly after enrolment. However, recruitment remains moderate, and findings should be interpreted cautiously due to heterogeneity, risk of bias, and limited certainty of evidence.

articles.title: Critical Role of hnRNP U and NOVA1 in Developing Stage-specific Progression of Metabolic Stress in the Hypothalamus.
articles.abstract: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is a major risk factor for diabetes and cardiovascular disease. The hypothalamus regulates energy homeostasis, and emerging evidence suggests that RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) and alternative splicing (AS) contribute to MetS pathogenesis. In vitro MetS was modelled by TNF-α treatment of hypothalamic GT1-7 cells, while established and chronic in vivo hypothalamic MetS states were generated by feeding mice a high-fat diet (HFD) for 8 and 12 weeks, respectively. NOVA1 and hnRNP U altered the splicing pattern of SNAP 25 and MDM2 genes, respectively, during the stage-specific progression of MetS, where a robust effect of hnRNP U was observed in the db/db mice. Functional knockdown studies were performed in GT1-7 cells to identify the underlying mechanism of hnRNP U. hnRNP U knockdown promoted exon 3 skipping in MDM2, p53 activation, mitochondrial stress, apoptosis, and impaired glucose uptake. This study identifies crucial RBPs and their target genes during the stage-specific progression of MetS, elucidates their roles in regulating mitochondrial stress and apoptosis, and highlights their potential as early therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Association of obstructive sleep apnea with outcomes in hospitalized patients with pneumonia: a retrospective analysis of the nationwide inpatient sample.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) impairs mucociliary defense, reduces ventilatory reserve, promotes systemic inflammation, and predisposes patients to lower respiratory tract infections. Despite biological plausibility, the population-level association of comorbid OSA with pneumonia hospitalization outcomes remains poorly characterized. We aimed to evaluate associations between OSA and clinical outcomes in adults hospitalized with pneumonia using a nationally representative inpatient database.

METHODS: Using the 2018-2020 Nationwide Inpatient Sample (NIS), we conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults (≥ 18 years) hospitalized with a primary diagnosis of pneumonia, stratified by OSA status. Multivariable logistic and linear regression models adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, household income quartile, primary payer, Charlson Comorbidity Index, obesity, hospital type, hospital bed size, and geographic region. P-values were corrected for multiple comparisons (Bonferroni), and E-values were calculated to assess sensitivity to unmeasured confounding.

RESULTS: Among 4,918,328 hospitalizations, 9.2% (n = 450,580) had coexisting OSA. Despite a greater comorbidity burden, OSA was associated with lower in-hospital mortality (3.3% vs. 4.8%; aOR 0.74; 95% CI 0.71-0.77; p < 0.0001), lower sepsis (aOR 0.89; 95% CI 0.87-0.90), and lower septic shock (2.2% vs. 2.7%; aOR 0.80; 95% CI 0.76-0.84). Conversely, OSA was associated with higher acute respiratory failure (48.1% vs. 35.8%; aOR 1.56; 95% CI 1.54-1.59), noninvasive ventilation (NIV) use (14.8% vs. 5.0%; aOR 3.26; 95% CI 3.17-3.34), and acute kidney injury (AKI; 24.1% vs. 22.1%; aOR 1.13; 95% CI 1.11-1.15). Adjusted length of stay was slightly longer (β + 0.11 days; 95% CI 0.07-0.16), while adjusted hospital charges did not differ significantly. All associations except hospital charges remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons; E-values suggested that the sepsis and AKI associations could be explained by relatively weak unmeasured confounding.

CONCLUSIONS: Among adults hospitalized with pneumonia, comorbid OSA was associated with higher rates of acute respiratory failure, NIV use, and AKI, and with lower in-hospital mortality and sepsis. Because of the retrospective administrative design and the lack of data on pneumonia severity, OSA severity, and CPAP use, residual and unmeasured confounding cannot be excluded. These findings are hypothesis-generating, and prospective studies are needed.

articles.title: Effects of Hypoxic Exposure and Training Methods on Wingate Test Performance: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Various forms of altitude/hypoxic exposure and training have been widely implemented in athletes; however, their effects on anaerobic performance remain inconclusive. Therefore, this study aimed to systematically review the effects of acute and chronic hypoxia, and intermittent hypoxic exposure-based training on Wingate Anaerobic Test (WAnT) performance, considering key variables such as differences across protocols and populations.

METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted in three online databases (i.e., PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science). The search was restricted to research articles published in peer-reviewed journals up to July 2025. Each article was read and coded for descriptive variables and WAnT outcomes (i.e., peak power output, mean power output, fatigue index and total work). The risk of bias was assessed using the PEDro scale.

RESULTS: From the 210 studies identified, 43 studies were eligible for this systematic review. Acute protocols were conducted in 16 studies, with 7 reporting 3-8% lower WAnT performance in hypoxia than normoxia, while the remaining studies showed no difference. Chronic protocols were examined in 6 studies, with 4 reporting 2-8% decreased WAnT performance, while 2 observed no change. Seven of 21 intermittent exposure-based training studies reported 3-8% greater improvements in WAnT performance than the corresponding normoxic training.

CONCLUSIONS: Acute hypoxic exposure does not lower WAnT performance unless the exercise is performed under severe hypoxia (FiO2 ~ 0.104) or performed repeatedly. A large hypoxic dose resulting from prolonged (≥30 days) chronic exposure at high altitude would decrease WAnT performance, but not after a shorter training camp at moderate altitude. Intermittent exposure-based training likely benefits WAnT performance when combined with long-duration (≥90 min) exercise but high-intensity interval training itself seems effective in improving anaerobic performance regardless of hypoxic exposure.

articles.title: Cerebellar Intermittent Theta-burst Stimulation Reduces Dual Task Cost in Walking and Balance in Stroke Patients.
articles.abstract: The cerebellum plays a key role in integrating cognitive and motor functions. After stroke, impairments in cognitive-motor dual task (DT) performance increase fall risk and limit functional independence. We aimed to investigate whether cerebellar intermittent theta-burst stimulation (CRB-iTBS) can improve DT performance in patients with subacute ischemic stroke. In this randomized controlled trial, 26 patients with subacute ischemic stroke and lower-limb impairment were assigned to receive CRB-iTBS or sham-iTBS combined with physiotherapy. Stimulation targeted the cerebellar hemisphere contralateral to the lesion. Cognitive task, single-task (ST: standing/walking), and cognitive-motor DT task (counting backward while standing/walking) completion pre- and post-intervention were compared. The primary outcome was the dual-task cost (DTC) of sway area. Secondary outcomes included DTCs for other balance and gait outcome measures, as well as balance and gait performance, electroencephalographic measures, and functional connectivity. CRB-iTBS significantly reduced the DTC for sway area, the primary outcome. DTCs for cadence and double support time were also reduced. Improvements in standing balance and gait performance were observed across ST and DT conditions. During DT walking, CRB-iTBS was associated with increased theta, alpha, and beta power and enhanced global connectivity. Increased frontal theta power correlated with a reduced DTC for cadence. CRB-iTBS improved DT performance, particularly balance as reflected by reduced DTC for sway area, in patients with subacute stroke. Cerebellar neuromodulation may be a promising adjunctive therapy during stroke rehabilitation.

articles.title: Viral Gene Therapy for Danon Disease: From LAMP2 Biology to Clinical Translation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Danon disease is a rare, highly penetrant and morbid X-linked cardioskeletal myopathy caused by loss-of-function variants in the lysosome-associated membrane protein 2 (LAMP2) gene. We review the rationale for LAMP2B gene replacement, the basis for adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9) vector selection, the first-in-human clinical evidence, and immunological barriers that define its therapeutic window.

RECENT FINDINGS: Preclinical models demonstrating restoration of autophagic flux via human LAMP2B gene delivery have provided the basis for clinical translation. The first-in-human phase 1 clinical data highlights the progress of recombinant adeno-associated virus serotype 9 carrying human LAMP2B (AAV9.LAMP2B) gene therapy (RP-A501). Seven male patients received a single intravenous infusion of AAV9.LAMP2B with transient immunomodulation. Myocardial transduction was achieved; LAMP2B protein was detectable by immunohistochemistry, autophagic vacuoles were reduced, left ventricular mass index fell by a median of 23%, cardiac troponin I and natriuretic peptides declined, and functional class improved in all evaluable patients. Toxicity was dose-limiting. Emerging clinical data supports that viral LAMP2B gene therapy is a viable disease-modifying strategy, although from a small cohort, for Danon disease. The long-term durability of transgene expression, patient safety and toxicity profiles with exclusion of affected females remain unresolved. The pivotal single-arm phase 2 study (NCT06092034) is ongoing.

articles.title: Outcomes of anterior gastropexy in minimally invasive hiatal hernia repair: A systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Paraesophageal hernia (PEH) can significantly impact quality of life and may lead to life-threatening complications. Although minimally invasive hernia repair (MISHR) is considered safe, it remains associated with relatively high recurrence rates. This study evaluates anterior gastropexy (AG) during MISHR as a potential operative strategy to reduce recurrence in PEH.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases were searched for studies evaluating AG during MISHR for PEH treatment. The primary outcome was hiatal hernia recurrence (HHR); secondary outcomes included postoperative reflux, postoperative dysphagia, mortality, reoperation, conversion to open surgery, operative time duration in minutes, and hospital stay in days.

RESULTS: A total of 15 studies were included, comprising 931 patients undergoing AG during MISHR. HHR occurred in 13 non-overlapping observational studies including 803 patients, with a pooled recurrence rate of 13.44% (95% CI, 10.09 to 17.68). Post-operative reflux was reported in 6.49% of cases (95% CI, 1.56 to 23.32), while post-operative dysphagia was present in 6.54% (95% CI, 3.71 to 11.27). Pooled mortality was 0.44% (95% CI, 0.04 to 4.21). Reoperation and conversion to open were necessary in 4.71% (95% CI, 2.42 to 8.97) and 1.38% (95% CI, 0.33 to 5.57), respectively.

CONCLUSION: In patients with PEH, HHR after MISHR with AG was estimated descriptively, alongside low rates of mortality, reoperation, and conversion to open surgery in the included cohorts. The only RCT favored AG, and these findings support further comparative studies.

articles.title: Partial loss of NONO function disrupts paraspeckle-like assembly and expands the MRXS34 phenotypic spectrum to a suspected renal medullary tubular disorder.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pathogenic variants in NONO cause X-linked syndromic intellectual developmental disorder 34 (MRXS34; MIM #300967), characterized by neurodevelopmental delay, cardiac defects, and brain malformations. Renal involvement, particularly renal medullary tubular abnormalities, is poorly described in this disorder.

METHODS: Clinical evaluations included echocardiography, cranial magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), renal ultrasonography, and trio-based whole-exome sequencing (WES). We performed functional studies in HEK293T cells transiently transfected with wild-type or mutant NONO expression constructs. We quantified NONO mRNA expression by reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR), protein expression by western blotting, the NONO-SFPQ interaction by co-immunoprecipitation, and subcellular localization by confocal immunofluorescence microscopy.

RESULTS: A 1-month-17-day-old male infant presented with multiple muscular ventricular septal defects, biventricular left ventricular noncompaction cardiomyopathy, corpus callosum dysgenesis, hyperkalemia with markedly elevated aldosterone, and renal ultrasound abnormalities suggestive of a medullary tubular disorder. Trio-WES identified a novel hemizygous frameshift variant, c.671_672del p.(Val224Glyfs*8), in NONO (NM_007363.5). This variant resulted in a 92.6% reduction in NONO mRNA expression relative to wild-type (P < 0.001), consistent with enhanced transcript degradation/NMD, and expression of a truncated protein of approximately 27 kDa at reduced levels (P < 0.01). Co-immunoprecipitation showed that the interaction between mutant NONO and SFPQ was reduced but not completely abolished. Confocal immunofluorescence revealed altered paraspeckle-like foci and reduced SFPQ signal.

CONCLUSIONS: We report a possible association of MRXS34 with a suspected renal medullary tubular disorder, with MSK not excluded, expanding the phenotypic spectrum of NONO-related disorders to include renal medullary/tubular abnormalities. The c.671_672del variant causes partial loss of function through reduced transcript and protein expression, altered subcellular localization, and impaired paraspeckle-like assembly, possibly secondary to impaired NONO-SFPQ heterodimerization. These findings suggest that NONO-related disease should be considered in patients with unexplained renal medullary/tubular anomalies.

articles.title: Effects of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum SG5 on anxiety, insomnia, and gut microbiota composition in college students.
articles.abstract: Accumulating evidence suggests that the gut microbiota can significantly improve psychiatric symptoms such as insomnia and anxiety via the gut‑brain axis. However, current studies on probiotics for improving insomnia and anxiety in college students remain relatively scarce. In this study, Lactiplantibacillus plantarum SG5 was used to evaluate the potential therapeutic effect on insomnia and anxiety in college students by Hamilton Anxiety Scale (HAMA) and Athens Insomnia Scale (AIS). Subsequently, high-throughput sequencing was used to analyze the composition of the gut microbiota after the intervention. The results showed that 113 participants completed the clinical trial, with 56 in the placebo group (MP group) and 57 in the probiotic group (MB group). Compared to the MP, L. plantarum SG5 intervention significantly improved anxiety levels (MP vs. MB = 16.50 vs. 12.00, p = 0.0011) and insomnia severity (MP vs. MB = 11.00 vs. 8.00, p < 0.0001). Gut microbiota analysis after the intervention showed differences in microbiota composition and diversity between the two groups (35 participants per group). Specifically, after L. plantarum SG5 intervention, microbial diversity decreased, while the relative abundance of Bifidobacterium (p < 0.01) and Lactobacillus (p < 0.05) significantly increased. In contrast, the relative abundance of Bacteroides (p < 0.01) and Prevotella (p < 0.05) significantly decreased. These findings provide a possible idea supporting the development of SG5 may as a microbial agent for insomnia and anxiety in clinical settings ( https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=213770 : ChiCTR2400083149, April 16, 2024).

articles.title: Implications of coal fly ash on soil health, food-chain dynamics and public health in india: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Coal fly ash (CFA), a primary solid waste from coal-fired power plants, poses a critical global environmental challenge due to its elevated concentrations of toxic elements. In India, rapid industrialization has driven coal consumption from 612.44 million tons (MT) in 2014-15 to an estimated 1025.3 MT in 2024-25, proportionately escalating CFA generation. This systematic review aims to comprehensively evaluate the multidimensional impacts of CFA on soil health, heavy-metal bioaccumulation in biological systems, and associated public health risks. Utilizing predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, we synthesized data from 34 empirical studies published between 2015 and 2026, retrieved from Google Scholar, Elsevier, and PubMed. Our findings reveal that CFA-influenced soils exhibit significantly higher concentrations of potentially toxic elements with Lead (Pb) and Cadmium (Cd) being the most extensively documented while demonstrating a comparative deficiency in essential macronutrients like nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P). Continuous CFA deposition severely alters soil biological properties, reducing the diversity and abundance of beneficial microbes, plants, nematodes, and earthworms, while promoting the dominance of stress-tolerant microbial communities. Furthermore, soil enzymes such as dehydrogenase, phosphatase, and urease showed significantly diminished activity in affected environments. In agricultural contexts, concentrations of Pb, Cd, and Zn in vegetables grown on CFA-influenced soils frequently exceed the permissible limits established by the WHO and Indian standards. Beyond heavy metals, CFA acts as a potent source of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), harmful gamma radiation, and radionuclides, cumulatively elevating human health consequences, including an identified high risk of cancer near thermal power plants.

articles.title: Mesh fixation versus non-fixation in laparoscopic inguinal hernia repair: absolute burden and clinical relevance of chronic pain - a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Mesh fixation has long been standard practice in laparoscopic inguinal hernia repair (L-IHR), but its necessity remains debated, as fixation devices may contribute to chronic groin pain and increased costs without a clear benefit in mesh stability. While non-fixation is now widely regarded as a safe default, the absolute magnitude and clinical relevance of the pain attributable to fixation remain poorly quantified. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare mesh fixation versus non-fixation in adults undergoing L-IHR and to quantify the absolute burden of chronic pain associated with fixation.

METHODS: A comprehensive online search was conducted across databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane Library) from inception to March 31, 2026. Additionally, a citation reference search was performed to identify further relevant studies. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) exclusively comparing mesh fixation versus non-fixation in adults undergoing L-IHR were included, with no language restrictions. The primary outcomes were chronic pain, postoperative pain, surgical site infection (SSI), seroma formation, and hernia recurrence. Secondary outcomes included time to resume normal activities, length of stay (LOS), operative time (OT), and procedural cost. Meta-analysis was performed using Review Manager (RevMan) version 5.4, and heterogeneity was assessed using I² statistics. Certainty of evidence was assessed with the GRADE approach.

RESULTS: A total of 4,826 records were identified, and 28 RCTs comprising 3,702 patients were included, 16 evaluating the totally extraperitoneal (TEP) and 12 the transabdominal preperitoneal (TAPP) technique. Postoperative pain consistently favored non-fixation at all timepoints in both techniques (TEP: SMD, 0.3 to 0.8; TAPP: SMD, 0.8 to 2.3; all P ≤ 0.04). Chronic pain differed by technique: fixation showed no significant excess in TEP (RR, 1.3; 95% CI, 0.9 to 1.9) but a higher incidence in TAPP (RR, 5.9; 95% CI, 1.6 to 21.7; NNTH, 9); this TAPP estimate was not robust to the exclusion of one or two trials, and no significant excess was observed in trials that assessed chronic pain at six months or later (TEP: RR, 1.4; 95% CI, 0.7 to 2.9; TAPP: RR, 2.0; 95% CI, 0.4 to 9.8). When six-month pain scores were re-expressed on a 0-10 scale, the pooled difference was approximately 0.6 points (95% CI, 0.4 to 0.8), below thresholds of clinical importance proposed for acute and chronic pain, although no threshold has been validated for chronic post-herniorrhaphy pain. No difference was observed in surgical site infection (SSI), seroma formation, or hernia recurrence (all P > 0.05). Return to normal activities favored non-fixation in TAPP (MD, 2.2 days; P < 0.00001), with a borderline effect in TEP that did not reach significance (MD, 0.8 days; P = 0.05). Operative time (OT) was longer with fixation by approximately 4.3 min, with no difference between techniques (MD, 4.3 min; P < 0.0001). Length of stay (LOS) favored non-fixation in TAPP (MD, 0.6 days; P < 0.00001) but not in TEP. Total procedural costs were higher with fixation in all six trials reporting them, with unweighted mean differences of US$542 (range, 303 to 852) in TEP and US$591 (range, 503 to 704) in TAPP, derived from heterogeneous health-care settings. Certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate.

CONCLUSION: In L-IHR, mechanical fixation was associated with greater postoperative pain than non-fixation, with a small pooled difference at six months, while SSI, seroma, and hernia recurrence showed no evidence of a difference between groups, although the estimates for SSI and recurrence were imprecise. An excess of chronic pain with fixation was observed in TAPP but not in TEP; this signal was not robust in sensitivity analyses, and no significant excess was observed in trials that assessed chronic pain at six months or later. Fixation also prolonged OT by a few minutes and added procedural cost, while non-fixation conferred faster recovery and shorter stay in TAPP. Non-fixation remains the approach recommended by current guidelines for most hernia types, with fixation reserved for large medial defects; these data quantify, rather than justify, the pain, time, and cost associated with departing from that default. The certainty of the evidence ranged from very low to moderate.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261419247.

articles.title: Integrated transcriptomic and cistromic analyses reveal associations between mechanotransduction-associated transcription and clock-gene expression in pulmonary arterial hypertension and TEAD-sensitive CRY1/CLOCK responses.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) involves vascular remodeling in an abnormal mechanical environment, but the relationship between mechanotransduction-associated transcription and clock-gene expression remains unclear. We integrated three PAH lung transcriptomic cohorts, donor-level endothelial analyses, vascular cell-state and spatial transcriptomic data, endothelial perturbation transcriptomics, and chromatin-binding data, with validation in human pulmonary artery endothelial cells (HPAECs). In 83 PAH lung samples, restricted maximum likelihood (REML) random-effects pooling showed a positive association between mechanotransduction and clock-related scores (Spearman ρ = 0.393, 95% confidence interval 0.185-0.567; Hartung-Knapp sensitivity P = 0.0279), which weakened when restricted to genes detectable across cohorts. Endothelial pseudobulk data from GSE169471 supported a positive donor-level association (n = 8, ρ = 0.738); the six-donor GSE210248 analysis used different score pairs. Associations varied in direction across vascular cell states, while molecular programs in 217 spatial regions differed by donor and lesion context. In HUVECs, activated YAP/TAZ increased CRY1 and CLOCK expression, with partial attenuation by TEAD-binding-deficient mutants. ChIP-seq identified candidate binding sites near both genes. In HPAECs, a stiffer substrate was associated with higher nuclear YAP/TAZ and CRY1/CLOCK protein levels; construct comparisons and independent TEAD1 knockdown supported TEAD-sensitive expression induction. Beyond prior CRY1 findings, this study provides evidence for CLOCK responses in pulmonary artery endothelium and cell-state heterogeneity. The findings support a candidate regulatory link, not altered circadian function or a causal mechanism of PAH vascular remodeling.

articles.title: Chronic cholestatic liver disease impairs skeletal muscle regeneration: partial modulation by ursodeoxycholic acid of satellite cells and innate immunity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic cholestatic liver disease (CCLD) is associated with skeletal muscle dysfunction, but its effects on muscle regeneration and the response to ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) remain incompletely characterized.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Male C57BL/6 mice received standard chow or a 0.1% 3,5-diethoxycarbonyl-1,4-dihydrocollidine (DDC) diet, with vehicle or UDCA (15 mg/kg/day); tibialis anterior cryoinjury at week 6 was followed by a 12-day recovery (n = 3-6 per group, depending on the assay). We assessed histology, fiber morphometry, embryonic myosin heavy chain (MyHC-emb) staining, flow cytometry, and adult MyHC isoforms. CCLD + UDCA exhibited more histologically altered tissue, more centrally nucleated fibers (both p < 0.0001), and more MyHC-emb⁺ fibers (p = 0.0002) than CCLD at day 12. The Pax7⁺ fraction was greater in CCLD than in controls (18.55% vs. 4.67%; adjusted p = 0.0001) and lower in CCLD + UDCA than in CCLD (4.63%; p = 0.0001), without a change in Myf5/MyoD composition within Pax7⁺ cells. CCLD + UDCA did not differ significantly from CCLD for MHC-II⁺, M1-like, or M2-like macrophage-associated frequencies, whereas the CD11b⁺Ly6G⁺ fraction was higher (p = 0.0043). MyHC-IIB abundance was greater in CCLD + UDCA than in CCLD (p = 0.0436).

CONCLUSIONS: UDCA at 15 mg/kg/day altered selected myogenic and immune marker-defined readouts and MyHC-IIB abundance but did not improve histological indices of post-cryoinjury repair at day 12. A single endpoint cannot distinguish delayed progression, differences in initial injury burden, or persistently incomplete regeneration. These data do not support a clinical recommendation of UDCA for muscle repair.

articles.title: Enhancing the therapeutic efficacy of umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells (UC-MSCs) in wound healing: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells (UC-MSCs) have been shown to improve wound healing. However, multiple challenges directly limit their therapeutic efficacy and clinical applications. Several studies have investigated strategies for modifying UC-MSCs to enhance their therapeutic outcomes in various experimental models. The modified UC-MSCs have been demonstrated to enhance the treatment outcomes. This systematic review evaluates whether modified UC-MSCs enhance wound healing compared with unmodified UC-MSCs, and identifies the modification strategies and underlying mechanisms with improved therapeutic efficacy. Articles on wound healing were searched in the electronic databases SCOPUS, PubMed, and the Cochrane Library. Study quality was assessed using the SYRCLE risk-of-bias tool, and the review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. Of the 52 articles screened, 11 studies fulfilled the criteria and were included in the final analysis. Evidence from the included studies suggests that therapeutic efficacy is significantly improved when UC-MSCs are combined with specific wound-healing materials. However, additional research is warranted to confirm their effectiveness and safety, and to ensure consistent, reproducible results. High-quality randomized controlled trials with low risk of bias are needed to enhance the reliability and clinical applicability of these findings.

articles.title: A systematic review of task-switching in healthy older adults: paradigm manipulations and switch costs.
articles.abstract: It is widely accepted that task-switching performance changes in later-life, but it is currently unclear how differences in measurement accrued over almost one hundred years may be affecting our understanding of task-switching performance differences in young versus older adults. This review investigated the different manipulations used in task-switching paradigms with healthy older adults (age 59-97 years), and the impact of these differences on task-switching performance. A search across four databases resulted in 73 articles meeting the inclusion criteria. We found considerable variability in how task-switching in later-life was operationalised, with increasing complexity in paradigm design over time. Digit tasks were the most common task-switching task, and word-cued switching was the most common switch instruction. Larger switch costs were correlated with complex stimulus features, task environments with less informative cues, and shorter preparation time between trials. Most studies comparing young and older adults have found that task-switching was slower and less accurate in older adults. However, conclusions were limited by substantial under-reporting of non-significant results. Future research with better consistency in reporting is needed to clarify whether paradigm manipulations impact the fundamental goal of accurately capturing the costs of switching when using task-switching paradigms in healthy young and older adults.

articles.title: N-acetylcysteine reduces systemic oxidative stress and inflammation but confers limited organ protection and partial modulation of hepatic ferroptosis and pyroptosis in experimental sepsis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oxidative stress contributes to sepsis-associated organ dysfunction, particularly in hyperinflammatory states. We investigated whether N-acetylcysteine (NAC) attenuates systemic oxidative stress and organ injury and modulates regulated cell death pathways in experimental sepsis.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Female Wistar rats (10 per group) underwent faecal peritonitis with antibiotics, fluids and analgesia. Groups received sham procedures, sepsis without antioxidant treatment, Trolox (50 mg/kg/day)​ or NAC (200 or 400 mg/kg/day). Treatments began 6 h after contamination and continued until 48 h or a humane endpoint. Sepsis induced oxidative and inflammatory disturbances with hepatic and renal injury. NAC improved selected systemic redox indices, reduced circulating cytokines and lowered transaminases and creatinine. Systemic malondialdehyde and thiols were unchanged, while circulating nitrite/nitrate increased at the higher dose. Hepatic glutathione-related measures improved; the higher dose reduced hepatic malondialdehyde, whereas the lower dose increased glutathione peroxidase 4 abundance. Both doses increased acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 and gasdermin D, indicating mixed changes in cell death-associated proteins. Histological injury scores were unchanged, and renal tissue protection was not demonstrated.

CONCLUSIONS: NAC reduced selected systemic oxidative and inflammatory indices without consistent organ or cell-level protection. The hepatic protein findings indicate partial modulation of cell death-associated pathways rather than definitive inhibition.

articles.title: Vitamin D receptor activation alleviates ferroptosis of lens epithelial cells in diabetic cataract by inhibiting NF-κB signaling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic cataract (DC) is a common ocular complication of diabetes recently linked to ferroptosis. Although the vitamin D receptor (VDR) is known to protect against ocular diseases by suppressing ferroptosis, its role in DC remains unclear.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Lens epithelial tissues were collected from patients with age-related cataract and DC. A streptozotocin (STZ)-induced model of DC was established with or without paricalcitol treatment, and an in vitro DC model was established in HLE-B3 cells with VDR overexpression or paricalcitol treatment. Lens epithelial cells (LECs) morphology and mitochondrial ultrastructure were examined by HE staining and TEM, respectively. Blood glucose, body weight, HbA1c, and hemoglobin levels were monitored in animal models, and lens opacity was evaluated. Fe²⁺, MDA, and GSH were measured using commercial assay kits. IF, IHC, Western blot, and RT-qPCR were performed to detect ferroptosis-related proteins and key components of the NF-κB signaling pathway. VDR expression was reduced in lens epithelial tissues of DC patients, with TFR1 upregulation, GPX4/FSP1 downregulation, and mitochondrial shrinkage. Similar changes were observed in STZ‑induced diabetic mice. In vitro, high glucose induced ferroptosis in HLE-B3 cells, as evidenced by TFR1 upregulation, GPX4/FSP1 downregulation, elevated Fe²⁺ and MDA, GSH depletion, and mitochondrial shrinkage. Activation of VDR in vitro and in vivo effectively reversed these changes. Mechanistically, VDR activation inhibited ferroptosis in LECs through suppression of NF-κB activation.

CONCLUSIONS: VDR activation attenuated ferroptosis in LECs of DC by blocking NF-κB signaling, providing both a mechanistic insight and a promising target for future clinical therapies.

articles.title: Diabetes is associated with improved short-term survival in Fournier's Gangrene.
articles.abstract:
