PURPOSE: To evaluate the influence of diabetes mellitus (DM) on short-term and long-term mortality in Fournier's Gangrene (FG) patients following surgical debridement.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of FG patients who underwent surgical debridement at Miriam Hospital between October 2011 and December 2023. Mortality was assessed at 90 days post-debridement and through March 2025. Associations between covariates and mortality were evaluated using Cox regression analysis.

RESULTS: Among our 199 FG patient cohort (83% male, 81% White, median age 58 [IQR: 48, 66]), 135 (68%) were diabetic, with 11 diagnosed on admission. Within 90 days post-debridement, diabetes (HR: 0.20, 95% CI: 0.05-0.80 p = 0.023) and BMI (HR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.87-1.00 p = 0.025) were associated with lower mortality. Over the full study period, age (HR: 1.03, 95% CI: 1.01-1.05 p = 0.011) and Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) (HR: 1.21, 95% CI: 1.06-1.38 p = 0.004) predicted higher mortality while diabetic status and BMI were no longer significant.

CONCLUSION: DM and higher BMI were associated with lower 90-day post-debridement mortality in FG patients, whereas longer-term mortality was independently predicted by age and comorbidity burden rather than diabetes. These associations are hypothesis-generating and warrant prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Dysregulation of redox-inflammatory markers in COVID-19: a multi-parameter analysis with disease severity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Viral infections remain a major global health threat. Viruses manipulate host gene expression, dictating the course of the disease using inflammation-induced oxidative stress. Characterized by uncontrolled reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels and weakened antioxidant defenses, which influence disease severity. SARS-CoV-2 exemplifies this interaction, highlighting the importance of understanding host molecular responses to identify biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

METHODS: The study included infected groups (Severe, Moderate, and Mild) and a control group. Samples were collected using a non-probability stratified sampling approach and were collected early after diagnosis to minimize treatment-related variability: at hospitalization for severe cases, within 12 h of a clinic visit for moderate cases, and within 24 h of RT-PCR confirmation for mild cases. Disease severity classification was based on clinical symptoms and oxygen saturation. This research assesses the intricate interplay between the severity of the viral infection and inflammation-induced redox imbalance using the expression profiles of key antioxidant genes (GPx, Nrf2, SOD2), pro-inflammatory genes (ACE2, NOS2), and an RNA-binding gene (HuR). Total hydroperoxides were measured as an indirect marker of ROS, along with serum Angiotensin II levels and clinical data.

RESULT: The findings demonstrate a coordinated pro-oxidant and inflammatory shift associated with severe COVID-19, characterized by significant dysregulation of redox and inflammatory markers. ROS levels were approximately twofold higher in the severe and moderate groups, while serum Angiotensin II levels were reduced by approximately half in the severe group. Clinical biomarkers were also elevated and correlated with disease severity. Collectively, these findings identify a multi-parameter molecular signature of severe COVID-19 that may help explain disease progression and inform future host-targeted therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: A noninvasive risk stratification prediction model for neuroblastoma through integration of multidimensional clinical indicators.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Current neuroblastoma (NB) risk classification relies partly on tumor tissue-derived information, which may be unavailable in patients who cannot undergo biopsy or surgical resection. Therefore, this study aimed to develop a non-invasive prediction model for NB risk classification by integrating a liquid biopsy biomarker with routinely available clinical indicators. A total of 141 treatment-naïve patients with NB were included and divided into a training cohort (n = 100) and a held-out testing cohort (n = 41). Six pretreatment predictors, including age, sex, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), neuron-specific enolase (NSE), image-defined risk factors (IDRFs), and circulating plasma MYCN amplification status, were incorporated into 11 machine-learning algorithms. Model development and selection were performed exclusively in the training cohort using repeated nested cross-validation with patient-level out-of-fold predictions. Random forest (RF) achieved the best overall performance, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.952 (95% CI, 0.906-0.998), an accuracy of 91%, and a Brier score of 0.079. Decision curve analysis showed positive net benefit across the prespecified threshold range of 15%-50%, while SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis identified IDRFs, NSE, and LDH as the leading contributors to model predictions. After model locking, the RF model retained good discrimination in the held-out testing cohort, with an AUC of 0.890 (95% CI, 0.791-0.989), a sensitivity of 84.2%, and a Brier score of 0.140.

CONCLUSION: These findings support the feasibility of combining circulating MYCN status with routine clinical variables to provide a non-tissue-based approach for assisting NB risk classification.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Current NB risk classification incorporates clinical, imaging, histopathological, and molecular information, some of which requires tumor tissue and may be unavailable before biopsy or surgery.

WHAT IS NEW: • This study developed and independently tested a non-invasive machine-learning model integrating circulating plasma MYCN amplification status with five routinely available clinical indicators, achieving an AUC of 0.952 during nested cross-validation in the training cohort and an AUC of 0.890 in the held-out testing cohort.

articles.title: How similar are siblings with familial Mediterranean fever? A pairwise analysis of clinical concordance.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: This study aimed to evaluate intrafamilial concordance in clinical manifestations, disease severity, and treatment outcomes among affected sibling pairs carrying the same MEFV genotype, and thereby assess whether one sibling's disease course might help inform clinical expectations, monitoring, and individualized management of the other sibling. This retrospective cohort study included 222 patients from 111 affected sibling pairs carrying the same MEFV genotype who were followed at three tertiary pediatric rheumatology centers. Clinical manifestations, laboratory findings, disease severity scores, and treatment characteristics were recorded. Concordance for categorical variables was evaluated using Cohen's kappa (κ) coefficient, and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) were calculated for continuous variables. The median age at diagnosis was 77 months (range 8-214), with a median diagnostic delay of 13 months (range 0-160). The most common clinical manifestations were abdominal pain (79.7%), fever (64.9%), and arthralgia (59.0%). Homozygous M694V was the predominant genotype (45.0%). The median annual attack frequency decreased from 10 (range 0-30) before treatment to 1 (range 0-18) after colchicine therapy. Biologic therapy was required in 14.0% of patients. Concordance between siblings was generally low for most clinical features (κ = 0.095-0.393). Disease severity scores showed slight-to-moderate concordance (ICC = 0.181-0.410). Slight concordance was observed for attack frequency before (ICC = 0.193) and fair concordance after colchicine treatment (ICC = 0.225).

CONCLUSION: Siblings with FMF demonstrated considerable phenotypic variability despite carrying the same MEFV genotype, indicating that the MEFV genotype alone does not fully explain intrafamilial disease expression. Other genetic, epigenetic, environmental, or individual-level factors may be involved; however, their contributions were not directly assessed in this study.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Familial Mediterranean fever shows marked phenotypic variability, even among patients carrying the same MEFV genotype. • Data on the concordance of clinical manifestations, disease severity, and treatment outcomes among affected siblings are limited.

WHAT IS NEW: • In 111 sibling pairs carrying the same MEFV genotype, most clinical manifestations, attack frequencies, disease severity measures, and treatment outcomes showed low concordance. • Pleuritis showed substantial concordance; however, its low frequency and wide confidence interval preclude firm conclusions. Overall, the findings support individualized assessment even among siblings carrying the same MEFV genotype.

articles.title: Surgical outcomes of single-stage posterior debridement combined with titanium mesh cage reconstruction and bone grafting for spinal infection after vertebral augmentation: a multicenter study.
articles.journal: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the surgical outcomes of single-stage posterior debridement combined with titanium mesh cage (TMC) reconstruction and bone grafting in the treatment of spinal infection following percutaneous vertebral augmentation (VA).

METHODS: A multicenter retrospective study was conducted, including patients who underwent surgery for spinal infection after percutaneous VA for osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (OVCF) between January 2018 and December 2023. All patients received single-stage posterior debridement, TMC reconstruction, and bone grafting. Operative duration, intraoperative blood loss, and clinical outcomes-including preoperative, immediate postoperative, and final follow-up visual analogue scale (VAS) scores, Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and local kyphotic Cobb angles-were recorded and analyzed.

RESULTS: A total of 51 patients (17 male, 34 female; mean age: 68.35 ± 6.83 years) were enrolled, of whom 49 completed follow-up and were included in the final analysis; two patients died during follow-up and were treated as missing data. The average interval between VA and revision surgery was 7.51 ± 5.77 months. The preoperative American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) grade was C, D, and E in 2, 40, and 9 patients, respectively. The average operation time was 201.33 ± 84.38 min, with a mean intraoperative blood loss of 900.98 ± 507.99 mL. Pathogens were detected in 31 cases postoperatively. The mean follow-up duration was 19.65 ± 4.56 months. At the final follow-up of the 49 patients, VAS scores, ODI, and local Cobb angles significantly improved compared to preoperative values (P < 0.05). Bony fusion was achieved in 45 of the 49 patients (91.8%), with an average duration of 5.44 ± 1.18 months.

CONCLUSION: Single-stage posterior debridement combined with TMC reconstruction and bone grafting was associated with favorable clinical and radiographic outcomes in patients with spinal infection following percutaneous VA.

articles.title: The double-hit of impaired autoregulation, cardiovascular instability, and the hemodynamic costs of therapeutic hypothermia.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Premature infants and newborns with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) share impaired cerebral autoregulation, so systemic hemodynamic fluctuations may pass directly to the cerebral circulation. This review examines the evidence for a hemodynamic neuroprotection bundle (HNB) paired with inotropic stewardship, with particular attention to late preterm infants with HIE treated with therapeutic hypothermia. Narrative review of mechanistic and observational studies, supplemented by quality improvement reports and randomized trials. Cerebral autoregulation is absent or narrowly functional in many extremely preterm infants and in newborns with HIE, and blood pressure thresholds do not reliably identify hypoperfusion in either group. Therapeutic hypothermia raises systemic and pulmonary vascular resistance and slows the heart, a burden that may be greater in late preterm infants. Vasoactive exposure in the first 72 h was associated with death or brain injury in HIE (OR 3.11, 95% CI 1.39 to 7.0) and with death or severe brain injury in infants born before 29 weeks (adjusted OR 2.9, 95% CI 1.4 to 5.7). A neuroprotection bundle in extremely preterm infants was associated with lower odds of death or severe brain injury (adjusted OR 0.34, 95% CI 0.20 to 0.59), and a neonatal neurocritical care program was associated with lower odds of HIE-related brain injury (adjusted OR 0.30, 95% CI 0.15 to 0.57).

CONCLUSION: An HNB that combines hemodynamic phenotyping with physiologically guided vasoactive therapy, governed by inotropic stewardship, may reduce mortality and brain injury in both populations. Prospective multicenter trials should test the bundle with pre-specified hemodynamic targets.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Impaired cerebral autoregulation leaves the brains of preterm infants and newborns with HIE exposed to blood pressure fluctuations. • Early vasoactive exposure is associated with death or brain injury in both groups.

WHAT IS NEW: • Therapeutic hypothermia adds a hemodynamic load that may offset its neuroprotection in late preterm infants. • A hemodynamic neuroprotection bundle with inotropic stewardship, in which the vasoactive agent is individualized by hemodynamic phenotype rather than by default approach, offers one framework for both populations.

articles.title: Biofilm-responsive nanogels: a closed-loop system for on-demand antimicrobial release for chronic wounds.
articles.abstract: Infections caused by biofilms present one of the major challenges in wound care due to their resistance to antibiotics and their slow healing. Chronic wounds, surgical site infections, and medical device infections are often characterized by biofilm, which forms an extracellular matrix that limits drug diffusion and sustains microorganisms. Nanotechnology has led to the development of nanogels as a novel drug delivery method that improves drug penetration into biofilms and supports sustained drug release. Stimuli-responsive nanogels, which are responsive to physiological changes in the chronic wound environment, including low pH values, enzymatic activities, and excessive production of reactive oxygen species, have shown their effectiveness in solving the problem of the development of bacterial infection. This review provides an overview of the use of biofilms in the physiology of wounds and highlights the significance of nanogels in biofilm-responsive closed-loop system therapy. The use of nanogels as one of the ways to create intelligent systems that can operate like sensors and monitor the wound microenvironment based on its changes and deliver drugs to the wound on demand in response to these changes is considered. Furthermore, recent developments in intelligent wound care systems with respect to patents and clinical trials are critically assessed. However, substantial progress has been made in this area; for moving these systems to clinical settings, further investigation is needed to optimize their sensitivity, therapeutic efficacy, long-term safety, and stability.

articles.title: Group exercise interventions and their impact on patient-reported outcomes in urologic, gynecologic, and breast cancers.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: Patients with urologic, gynecologic, and breast malignancies experience unique treatment-related side effects that can be socially isolating. While group-based exercise can provide social support, its impact on these patients remains unclear. This review aims to examine patient-reported outcomes related to participation in group exercise in these patients.

METHODS: We performed a systematic review of randomized control trials and prospective cohort studies that compared group-based exercise to usual care or individual exercise in patients with a urologic, gynecologic, or breast malignancy and examined patient-reported metrics. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, SPORTDiscus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews were searched between January 2005 and December 2025.

RESULTS: We identified 973 studies and 14 met inclusion criteria. Of the included articles, 9 included breast, 4 included prostate, and 1 included bladder cancer patients, representing 1128 patients. Group exercise was performed in supervised groups or teams of 3-14 participants in a community or hospital facility. Compared to individual exercise, a group exercise intervention showed an improvement in patient-reported quality of life in 1 study where group dynamics were measured.

CONCLUSION: This review was unable to show an advantage in group-based exercise compared to individual exercise with regard to patient-reported quality of life for patients with a breast, prostate, or bladder cancer. However, our study is limited by the absence of measured positive group dynamic in each study. Future investigations will include qualitative and quantitative measures of group dynamic and group cohesion to determine the potentially socially supportive role of group-based exercise interventions.

articles.title: Laser hemorrhoidoplasty vs. stapled hemorrhoidopexy: a meta-analysis of clinical outcomes with considerations in surgical anatomy.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Hemorrhoidal disease is a common colorectal condition affecting millions. Recently, minimally invasive approaches have gained popularity for their faster recovery. However, current literature lacks a comprehensive comparison between these two methods. This systematic review and meta-analysis compares the efficacy and outcomes of stapled hemorrhoidopexy (SH) and laser hemorrhoidoplasty (LH).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus identified studies comparing SH and LH. Patient cohorts were analyzed for recovery, perioperative outcomes, and complications. Meta-analysis was performed using R to calculate pooled Odds Ratios (OR) and Weighted Mean Differences (WMD).

RESULTS: LH demonstrated a significantly shorter mean operative time compared to SH (25.9 vs. 33.0 min; MD = 7.14). The stapled approach was associated with significantly higher rates of postoperative urinary retention (7.7% vs. 3.0%; OR = 1.92), stenosis (4.5% vs. 0%; OR = 9.74), and longer hospital stays (MD = 16.32). No significant differences were observed regarding estimated blood loss (MD = 2.49), return to normal activity, readmission, postoperative bleeding, or overall VAS pain scores at any time point (12 h, 24 h, 1 week, 2 weeks, and 3 months). Subgroup analyses indicated LH yielded significantly lower pain at 3 months in severe cases.

CONCLUSION: LH and SH showed no statistically significant differences across several reported short-term outcomes, including postoperative pain, bleeding, and time to return to normal activities. While LH was associated with shorter operative times, reduced hospital stays, and lower rates of urinary retention and stenosis in the available studies, these findings must be interpreted with caution. Crucially, the true comparative therapeutic efficacy of these techniques remains uncertain. Because relevant variables like symptom resolution, patient-reported outcomes, disease-specific functional outcomes were insufficiently assessed, while recurrence data are limited by heterogeneous and inadequately reported follow-up, this analysis permits conclusions regarding short-term perioperative recovery, but not robust conclusions regarding comparative long-term success and efficacy.

articles.title: Real-world handheld smartphone videos for nystagmus detection in acute vertigo: a feasibility study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate identification of nystagmus is fundamental to the assessment of acute vertigo but remains challenging in emergency department (ED) settings. Although smartphone-based approaches have been proposed as scalable solutions, their feasibility under real-world acquisition conditions remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility of detecting nystagmus from handheld smartphone videos acquired in a real-world ED.

METHODS: A subset of 67 videos from a published handheld smartphone-based acute vertigo dataset was analysed. A salient feature-based eye-tracking algorithm tracked stable ocular and periocular (facial) landmarks across frames. Horizontal displacement signals were extracted, and nystagmus episodes were identified through signal analysis and video verification.

RESULTS: Consistent eye-movement signals were successfully extracted from handheld smartphone recordings acquired during the acute phase of vertigo despite real-world challenges, including variable illumination, camera motion, image instability, and patient-related factors. Nystagmus patterns observed on video were accurately reflected in the corresponding signal traces, including very low-amplitude nystagmus that was barely discernible to the naked eye.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings demonstrate that handheld image acquisition using standard, low-cost smartphones can capture clinically meaningful ocular motor information in real-world emergency care settings. This proof of principle lays the groundwork for the development of more ecologically valid scalable, telehealth-compatible tools for acute vertigo assessment. Further studies are needed to automate detection and validate performance in larger prospective cohorts.

articles.title: RSV bronchiolitis admissions in infants immunized with nirsevimab: a multicenter observational study.
authors: Impact of universal Respiratory Syncytial Virus prophylaxis in Spain Working Group
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Real-world studies have confirmed the high effectiveness of nirsevimab, preventing approximately 80% of RSV bronchiolitis hospitalizations. This study aimed to evaluate the epidemiological and clinical characteristics of RSV bronchiolitis admissions following successful nationwide implementation of nirsevimab. We conducted a retrospective multicenter study across 15 Spanish pediatric emergency departments during the 2024-2025 RSV season. Infants eligible for the RSV prophylaxis, defined as those younger than six months at the start of or during the RSV season, with laboratory-confirmed RSV bronchiolitis requiring hospitalization were included. Patients immunized fewer than seven days before admission or with unknown immunization status were excluded. Epidemiological and clinical data were analyzed according to nirsevimab status, with age-stratified and multivariable analyses performed. Among 366 hospitalized infants with RSV bronchiolitis, 345 were previously healthy. Of these, 165/345 (47.8%) had received nirsevimab. Breakthrough cases were younger than non-breakthrough cases (2.0 months [IQR, 1.1-3.6] vs 5.2 months [IQR, 3.3-6.6]; p < 0.001). Overall, immunized and non-immunized infants showed similar rates of pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admission (26.7% vs 21.1%; p = 0.2) and length of hospital stay (5 days [IQR, 3-7] vs 5 days [IQR, 4-7]; p = 0.6). After age stratification, clinical characteristics and outcomes remained comparable between groups. In multivariable analyses, no statistically significant association was observed between nirsevimab immunization and PICU admission, advanced respiratory support, or length of hospital stay.

CONCLUSIONS: In-hospital outcomes of RSV bronchiolitis admissions did not differ significantly by immunization status. These findings suggest that, once hospitalization is required, nirsevimab may offer limited additional protection against severe disease.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Real-world studies have confirmed the high effectiveness of nirsevimab, preventing approximately 80% of RSV bronchiolitis hospitalizations.

WHAT IS NEW: • In-hospital outcomes of RSV bronchiolitis admissions did not differ significantly by immunization status. These findings suggest that, once hospitalization is required, nirsevimab may offer limited additional protection against severe disease.

articles.title: [Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) : Consensus statement of the DGK, DGTHG, DGAI, DGPTM, DIVI, GRC, DRG, ALKK and DGIIN].
articles.abstract: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) can be considered as a rescue strategy in highly selected patients with refractory cardiac arrest and a potentially reversible cause of cardiac arrest. Both ECPR itself and the subsequent treatment under extracorporeal life support (ECLS) are complex and resource intensive. There is currently no robust evidence for the superiority of ECPR over conventional cardiopulmonary resuscitation. The implementation and maintenance of an effective ECPR program requires clearly structured processes, defined communication channels and robust institutional infrastructure for quality assurance. Ensuring comprehensive and intersectoral quality of care requires the cooperative collaboration of many necessary disciplines. This consensus paper updates the document published in 2018 and defines a common framework of central structural, procedural and clinical requirements.

articles.title: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy associated with obinutuzumab-bendamustine: combination therapy with mirtazapine and immunoglobulin.
articles.abstract: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) is a severe opportunistic infection of the central nervous system resulting from JC virus (JCV) reactivation, often leading to substantial neurological morbidity and mortality. While associated with various immunotherapies, the incidence of PML specifically following obinutuzumab-bendamustine as first-line therapy remains under-reported. We aim to highlight this potent regimen as a trigger for JCV reactivation and evaluate therapeutic strategies. We describe a patient who presented with cognitive decline two years after completing obinutuzumab-bendamustine therapy for follicular lymphoma, accompanied with profound lymphopenia and hypogammaglobulinemia. A diagnosis of PML was established based on deep white matter lesions on brain MRI and a positive cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) polymerase chain reaction for JCV. Treatment consisted of daily mirtazapine together with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) supplementation. At the 2-year follow-up, the patient demonstrated sustained radiological stabilization, cognitive improvement, and undetectable JCV viral load in CSF. Obinutuzumab-bendamustine therapy represents a distinct clinical trigger for PML due to its dual-arm immunosuppressive effects on humoral and cellular immunity. While endogenous cellular immune restoration likely played a primary role in viral clearance, adjunctive mirtazapine and IVIG may represent a feasible supportive strategy, particularly following B-cell-depleting therapy. The therapeutic contribution of this combined regimen requires further investigation.

articles.title: It's All One Trial: a continuous master-protocol framework to accelerate development and confirmation of disease-modifying therapies for type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract: The time required for clinical development and regulatory approval of disease-modifying therapies for type 1 diabetes is the longest of any therapeutic area. Teplizumab, the only product that has received an accelerated approval in the USA for people with stage 3 type 1 diabetes, will require about a decade for its Phase III and confirmatory trial to be completed and full approval to be achieved. This article proposes the 'It's All One Trial' (OT) framework, a single master protocol with one continuously randomised population, one prospective statistical structure, and uninterrupted follow-up spanning early investigation, accelerated approval based on an intermediate endpoint, and later confirmation of durability and clinical benefit. The OT framework is compared with current clinical development practices for treatments aimed at preserving insulin secretion in people with recent-onset type 1 diabetes. Teplizumab's Phase III PROTECT trial and confirmatory βETA PRESERVE trials provide observed and projected timelines for late-stage development. Based on prevailing early clinical development practices and observed and projected timelines of the teplizumab trials, the OT model could reduce total development time by approximately 45 months while increasing use of participant data and reducing the need for repeated enrolment, site activation and study restarts. Implementing the OT model could shorten development timelines, lower capital barriers, conserve scarce clinical trial resources and better honour patient participation by maintaining continuous randomised follow-up, protocol-directed care and a more direct path from early biological effect to durable evidence for practice and regulation.

articles.title: Fetal, placental and amniotic fluid volume across gestation in women with type 1 diabetes: a prospective MRI study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: The aim of this study was to compare fetal, placental and amniotic fluid volumes across gestation by use of MRI in women with type 1 diabetes and women without diabetes.

METHODS: This prospective longitudinal cohort study is part of the FaPDi cohort study. The study included pregnant women with type 1 diabetes and women without diabetes who gave birth at Aalborg University Hospital between November 2020 and April 2023. All participants were invited for MRI scans at 15-20, 26-30 and 34-38 weeks' gestation, from which fetal, placental and amniotic fluid volumes were obtained. The groups were compared across gestation using multiple linear regressions and mixed-effects models.

RESULTS: A total of 63 pregnant women were included in the analysis (25 with type 1 diabetes and 38 without diabetes). In women with type 1 diabetes, the fetal, placental and amniotic volumes were significantly increased at visits 2 and 3. At visit 3, the adjusted differences between groups were 385.9 cm3 (95% CI 140.9, 631.0; p<0.01), 187.8 cm3 (95% CI 35.4, 340.3; p=0.02) and 420.4 cm3 (95% CI 19.5, 821.2; p=0.04) for the fetal, placental and amniotic volumes, respectively. Placental weight to birthweight ratio was increased at delivery among women with type 1 diabetes (p<0.01), but no differences in the intrauterine volume ratios were observed. Maternal HbA1c showed a positive linear correlation with all volumes at visits 2 and 3, with the strongest correlations shown for amniotic fluid volume (R2=0.36).

CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: MRI provides a unique insight into the intrauterine consequences of type 1 diabetes. Pregnancies complicated by type 1 diabetes are characterised by increased fetal, placental and amniotic fluid volumes. The strong association between maternal HbA1c and amniotic fluid volume suggests that amniotic fluid dynamics may provide additional insight into the intrauterine consequences of maternal glucose regulation.

articles.title: Perspectives of rheumatologists on the management of late-onset rheumatoid arthritis: a nationwide cross-sectional survey.
articles.abstract: With population ageing, the number of patients with late-onset rheumatoid arthritis (LORA) is increasing. However, optimal treatment strategies remain unclear. We aimed this study to clarify the current perspectives of rheumatologists regarding the management of LORA. We conducted an anonymous online questionnaire for members of the Japan College of Rheumatology between March and May 2023. The questionnaire consisted of multiple-choice questions about their perspectives on the concept and management of LORA in clinical practice, and on treatment choices based on case vignettes. We aggregated and analysed the responses. A total of 1041 rheumatologists responded to the survey. The most common definition of LORA was '70 years' (n = 392, 38%), followed by '65 years' (n = 287, 28%) and '75 years' (n = 251, 24%). In the management of LORA, 60% (n = 624) of respondents answered that 'safety' is the top priority, followed by 'control of disease activity' (n = 277, 27%). However, most rheumatologists set a treatment goal of 'low disease activity' (n = 545, 52%) rather than 'remission' (n = 330, 32%). The most common response regarding issues when treating LORA was 'comorbidities/complications' (n = 693, 67%), followed by 'adverse events/safety' (n = 620, 60%) and 'cognitive function' (n = 448, 43%). The case vignette revealed that treatment choices for LORA patients are highly variable and affected by many factors, including comorbidities, cognitive function, living environment, activities of daily living, and financial status. This nationwide survey conducted in Japan revealed the challenges rheumatologists face and the diversity of their preferences and perceptions regarding the management of LORA in clinical practice.

articles.title: Early Correlates of High-Risk Lymphatic Subtype on T2-Weighted Pre-fontan Cardiac MRI and Associated Clinical Outcomes.
articles.abstract: Lymphatic dysfunction is a severe complication of the Fontan circulation. Type 3 and 4 lymphatic subtypes identified on T2-weighted cardiac MRI (CMR) are associated with worse Fontan outcomes. Correlates of lymphatic subtype are incompletely described. Of the 171 patients with single ventricle physiology who underwent pre-Fontan CMR with T2-weighting to define lymphatic subtype between 2017 and 2021, 148 had standard-risk lymphatics (subtypes 1, 2, and 3 without pre-Fontan chylous effusions), and 23 had high-risk lymphatics (subtypes 3 with a history of pre-Fontan chylous effusions and 4). The two groups did not differ by demographic, anatomic, or pre-Fontan surgical features. High-risk subtype patients had more pre-fontan hospital days (84 vs. 44, p < 0.001), worse atrioventricular valve regurgitation (AVVR) by echocardiogram, higher aortopulmonary collateral (APC) burden (38% vs. 30%, p = 0.004) and Qp: Qs (1.2 vs. 1.05, p = 0.01) by CMR, and higher left pulmonary artery pressure (11mmHg vs. 10mmHg, p = 0.04) and higher systemic ventricular end diastolic pressure (8mmHg vs. 7mmHg, p = 0.02) by cardiac catheterization. High-risk patients were more frequently deemed to be unsuitable for Fontan palliation (22% vs. 4%, p = < 0.001) while those who did undergo palliation had longer post-Fontan length of stay (14 days vs. 9 days, p = 0.01) and more post-fontan chest tube days (10.5 vs. 7, p = 0.002). This study demonstrates a link between pre-Fontan clinical factors and lymphatic subtype. Further work is needed to understand whether modification of these risk factors might impact lymphatic anatomy.

articles.title: Self-Expandable Harmony Valve Implantation in Supravalvular Pulmonary Position After Senning Procedure: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Transcatheter pulmonary valve implantation has emerged as a minimally invasive therapeutic strategy for the management of right ventricular outflow tract dysfunction, particularly in patients considered unsuitable for repeat surgical intervention. Implantation of the self-expandable Harmony valve represents a therapeutic option for patients with large right ventricular outflow tracts that are unsuitable for balloon-expandable devices. However, significant anatomical variability, particularly in patients following the atrial switch procedure, poses procedural challenges and underscores the importance of meticulous pre-procedural planning. A 44-year-old male with Transposition of the Great Arteries underwent a Senning-Brom procedure in infancy, followed by surgical correction of a baffle leak and pulmonary valve reconstruction at the age of 22. Over time, he developed progressive severe pulmonary regurgitation, confirmed by serial MRI, showing worsening regurgitant fraction (44%) and significant left ventricular (subpulmonic) dilation. The pre-procedural CT screening report for the Harmony valve (TPV25) revealed complex LVOT anatomy, with adequate proximal anchoring but suboptimal distal oversizing. Despite complex anatomy and suboptimal distal oversizing, the procedure was undertaken based on the anatomical dimensions of the main pulmonary artery, favorable proximal anatomy, and a safe distance from the coronary arteries. The procedure was performed via femoral access, and the valve was advanced into the pulmonary artery and deployed in a controlled, stepwise manner at a high level of the bifurcation. Final angiography confirmed stable positioning, optimal anchoring, and complete resolution of pulmonary regurgitation, with preserved coronary flow and no evidence of compression, indicating a successful outcome. This case demonstrates that Harmony valve implantation in a supravalvular pulmonary position is feasible in patients with Transposition of the Great Arteries following atrial switch repair, despite complex anatomy and suboptimal distal oversizing, when the procedure is guided by comprehensive multimodality imaging and adapted implantation strategies.

articles.title: [Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) : Consensus statement of the DGK, DGTHG, DGAI, DGPTM, DIVI, GRC, DRG, ALKK and DGIIN].

articles.title: Fine mapping and breeding application of powdery mildew resistance gene in wheat breeding line N278.
articles.abstract: Powdery mildew, caused by Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici (Bgt), severely impacts wheat production. The deployment of effective resistance genes through marker-assisted selection (MAS) provides an efficient strategy for sustainable management of this disease. In this study, the wheat breeding line N278 showed broad-spectrum resistance to all 24 Bgt isolates at the seedling stage and maintained resistance at the adult-plant stage for five consecutive years. Genetic analysis showed that the resistance was controlled by a single dominant gene, temporarily named PmN278. Bulked segregant RNA-Seq (BSR-Seq) in F2:3 families combined with large-scale molecular marker genotyping of 8,000 F3 individuals delimited the resistance locus to an 882.36 kb interval on chromosome arm 5BL according to Chinese Spring reference genome (v2.1). Sequence alignment and molecular marker detection indicated that the resistance locus identified in N278 corresponds to the previously cloned powdery mildew resistance gene Pm36, which encoded a tandem kinase with a transmembrane domain (WTK7-TM). Gene expression profiling revealed a significant induction of Pm36 transcripts at 48 hours post-inoculation (hpi) with Bgt isolate E09, corresponding to the early stage of fungal infection development in N278. Furthermore, MAS was used to transfer Pm36 into the susceptible commercial cultivar Shixin 828, generating the resistant advanced line NS24. Field evaluation over three consecutive growing seasons showed that NS24 retained stable powdery mildew resistance without obvious negative effects on major agronomic traits. These results validate the effectiveness of Pm36 in an elite Chinese wheat breeding background and provide valuable resources for the deployment of broad-spectrum powdery mildew resistance in wheat improvement.

articles.title: Mortality and Safety in Aesthetic Plastic Surgery: An Italian Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elective aesthetic surgery has grown substantially in Italy, from 262,556 procedures in 2022 to 480,047 in 2024. Despite this, mortality data are scarce and fragmented. International studies confirm low but non-negligible risk, particularly for high-impact procedures such as liposuction and combined surgeries.

OBJECTIVES: To quantify fatal events following elective aesthetic surgery in Italy (2010-2025), characterize patient, procedural, and facility-related factors, compare findings with international data, and propose preliminary safety recommendations.

METHODS: A retrospective review was performed using medico-legal reports, clinical documentation, surgeon interviews, court records, and public archives. All intra- or postoperative deaths following elective aesthetic surgery were included. Data collected included demographics, comorbidities, procedure type, surgical setting, anesthetic management, timing, and cause of death.

RESULTS: Twenty deaths following elective aesthetic surgery in Italy (2010-2025) were identified. Liposuction accounted for 45% of cases ( ≈ 0.02% of total procedures), breast surgery 25% ( ≈ 0.01%), and abdominoplasty 10% ( ≈ 0.004%). Ten procedures (25%) occurred in non-compliant facilities. Leading causes were cardiac arrest or anesthesia-related complications (45%), thromboembolic events (15%), and sepsis/multiorgan failure (20%). Fifty-five percent of deaths occurred days to weeks postoperatively. These findings are consistent with international literature, highlighting high-risk procedures, anesthesia-related complications, and thromboembolism.

CONCLUSIONS: Although rare relative to procedure volume, fatal events are often preventable. Key risk-reduction strategies include rigorous patient selection, structured VTE prophylaxis, anesthetic safety standards, accredited surgical facilities, and structured postoperative follow-up.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE IV: This journal requires that authors assign a level of evidence to each article. For a full descrip tion of these Evidence-Based Medicine ratings, please refer to the Table of Contents or the online Instructions to Authors  www.springer.com/00266 .

articles.title: Underweight and obesity as outcome predictors after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: insights from the DOUBLE-CHOICE trial.
articles.journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: An "obesity paradox" has been described after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), suggesting lower mortality in patients with higher body mass index (BMI) despite greater comorbidity. In contrast, underweight consistently predicts adverse outcomes. Whether these associations reflect a true biological effect or are primarily driven by residual confounding, frailty, and patient selection remains uncertain.

METHODS: This prespecified subgroup analysis included eligible patients from the randomized DOUBLE-CHOICE trial comparing two transcatheter heart valves and two anesthesia strategies (minimalist approach with local anesthesia only vs. standard care with conscious sedation). The primary endpoint was a 30-day composite of all-cause mortality, vascular and bleeding complications, infections requiring antibiotic therapy, and neurologic events. Associations were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, frailty, diabetes, hypertension, chronic kidney disease, and anesthesia strategy.

RESULTS: Among 752 patients (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2, n = 192; BMI < 30 kg/m2, n = 560), obese patients had lower rates of the 30-day primary endpoint (15.2% vs. 27.6%; p < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, obesity remained independently associated with lower risk (adjusted OR 0.48, 95% CI 0.30-0.75; p = 0.002). In contrast, underweight (BMI < 20 kg/m2; n = 23) was associated with a higher incidence of the primary endpoint (55.0% vs. 23.4%; p = 0.003) and remained an independent predictor after adjustment (adjusted OR 3.74, 95% CI 1.30-9.52; p = 0.005).

CONCLUSION: In this randomized TAVI population, obesity was independently associated with favorable 30-day outcomes, whereas underweight identified a small but high-risk subgroup with substantially increased procedural risk. These findings identify underweight as a potential high-risk phenotype requiring further investigation in future studies incorporating more detailed measures of frailty and body composition.

articles.title: Frequency of difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis and associated factors at b/tsDMARD initiation in a tertiary referral center: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory rheumatic disease in which adequate disease control remains challenging in a subset of patients despite the availability of numerous therapeutic agents. In 2021, the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) established the definition of difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis (D2T-RA). To determine the frequency of D2T-RA among RA patients treated with biological or targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (b/tsDMARDs) and to examine factors recorded at b/tsDMARD initiation that were associated with subsequent D2T-RA classification. In this single-center cross-sectional study, D2T-RA status was assessed at an index visit conducted between April and November 2023. D2T-RA status was determined at the index visit using a study-specific operationalization of the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) definition. Treatment-initiation data were collected retrospectively. Clinically selected multivariable models were adjusted for the interval from b/tsDMARD initiation to the index visit. Analyses were repeated after removing the Health Assessment Questionnaire (HAQ) item from the definition. Of the 487 patients included, 181 (37.1%) met the operationalized D2T-RA criteria. None of the factors in the primary model was independently associated with D2T-RA classification. In the model without the 28-joint Disease Activity Score based on erythrocyte sedimentation rate (DAS28-ESR), higher HAQ was associated with D2T-RA (OR 1.56, 95% CI 1.03-2.36; p = 0.036). Removing the HAQ-based item reclassified 23 patients and reduced the frequency to 32.4%. With this outcome, younger age at diagnosis (OR 0.972, 95% CI 0.949-0.996; p = 0.023) and higher body mass index (OR 1.055, 95% CI 1.008-1.103; p = 0.020) were associated with D2T-RA in the primary model. D2T-RA was common in this tertiary cohort of patients receiving b/tsDMARDs. The primary model did not identify an independently associated baseline factor, whereas higher HAQ, younger age at diagnosis, and higher BMI were associated with D2T-RA in additional models. As these associations were not consistent across models, they should be interpreted cautiously..

articles.title: Gastrodin Alleviates Post-Stroke Headache and Neuronal Injury via Activating the PI3K/Akt Pathway.
articles.abstract: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is frequently accompanied by severe neurological deficits and post-stroke headache (PSH). These complications significantly worsen clinical outcomes. Although gastrodin has been reported to exert neuroprotective effects, whether it relieves PSH and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, using a rat model of PSH that exhibits orbital mechanical allodynia and increased facial grooming, we demonstrated that gastrodin dose-dependently alleviated pain-related behaviors, reduced the number of c-Fos-positive neurons in the trigeminal nucleus caudalis, and decreased protein levels of calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) and substance P in the trigeminal ganglion. Mechanistically, gastrodin restored PI3K/Akt pathway activity in the ischemic penumbra, as reflected by increased PI3K and Akt expression and a higher p-Akt/Akt ratio, which was accompanied by reduced cerebral infarct volume, alleviated neuronal pathological damage, and suppressed oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis. All these protective effects were significantly reversed by the PI3K inhibitor LY294002. To validate clinical relevance, we enrolled 80 AIS patients and 50 healthy controls. Peripheral blood PI3K/Akt expression was significantly lower in AIS patients and was correlated with PSH severity and neurological deficits. In conclusion, we revealed that gastrodin exerts dual analgesic and neuroprotective effects by restoring the PI3K/Akt pathway, providing novel insights and experimental support for the treatment of AIS complicated with PSH.

articles.title: Validating sarcopenia definitions in Asian patients with cirrhosis: a first and necessary step to characterizing muscle health.
Reducing Hypothermia Among Intramural Vaginally Born Preterm Neonates Admitted in Neonatal Intensive Care Unit at a Tertiary Care Centre Using Quality Improvement Approach: Authors' Reply.

Fractional Exhaled Nitric Oxide Cut-off Values for Discriminating Asthma Exacerbation and Control in Indian Children with Coexisting Allergic Rhinitis: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study - Correspondence 3.
A pilot study on the impact of Hydroxiram D supplementation on nutritional status and sarcopenia-related parameters.
articles.abstract: Sarcopenia is a frequent and prognostically relevant complication of chronic liver disease. The SARCIRAM pilot trial investigated the effect of Hydroxiram D, a formulation of branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs), β-hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate (HMB), and vitamin D, on nutritional status and sarcopenia-related parameters in patients with compensated cirrhosis due to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). In this single-center, randomized pilot study, adults with compensated MASLD-related cirrhosis (Child-Pugh A) received Hydroxiram D plus standard care or standard care alone for 6 months. The primary outcome was phase angle (PA), while secondary outcomes were appendicular skeletal muscle mass (ASMM)/height², handgrip strength (HGS), and 4-meter walk test (4-mWT). Between-group comparisons used baseline-adjusted models. Post-hoc simulation analyses were used exploratorily to inform the design of future studies. Thirty-two patients were analyzed. After 6 months, the adjusted change in PA was significantly more favorable in the treated group versus controls (+ 0.36° vs. - 0.45°, p = 0.046). Between-group differences in muscle mass, HGS, and gait speed were not statistically significant, although effect estimates directionally favoured the intervention. No treatment-related adverse events were observed. Six months of Hydroxiram D was associated with a more favorable change in PA in patients with compensated MASLD-related cirrhosis, with favorable trends in muscle parameters. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant confirmation in larger, prospectively registered, double-blind trials to confirm efficacy and long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Immunologically optimized Zmp1 peptides reveal a translational serological biomarker platform for tuberculosis diagnosis across disease manifestations.
articles.journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
articles.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) diagnosis remains challenging, particularly for extrapulmonary TB (EPTB), where invasive sampling, low bacillary burden, and limited sensitivity of nucleic acid-based tests in peripheral specimens hinder timely detection. Here, we report an immunology-driven strategy for biomarker discovery and development of a peptide-based serological assay targeting Mycobacterium tuberculosis zinc metalloprotease-1 (Zmp1). Based on the principle that antigenic regions containing overlapping B-cell and CD4⁺T-cell epitopes can promote strong antibody responses through linked recognition and cognate T-cell help, we used an immunoinformatics pipeline to identify two nested immunodominant Zmp1 peptide regions, Mtb-Zp-NT and Mtb-Zp-CT, enriched for overlapping B- and T-cell epitopes.Their diagnostic potential was evaluated using ELISA-based serological assays. A blinded pilot study (N = 137) demonstrated clear discrimination between active TB and TB-recovered individuals. An expanded validation cohort (N = 875), identified from screening approximately 6,086 individuals, included pulmonary TB (PTB), EPTB, TB-recovered individuals, household contacts, non-specific infection/inflammation, and healthy controls. Receiver operating characteristic analyses, supported by DeLong and bootstrap comparisons, demonstrated superior diagnostic performance of the peptide assays compared with Mtb-FL-Zmp1. Mtb-Zp-CT showed the highest accuracy (AUC = 0.93), with > 93% specificity and ~ 76% sensitivity.These findings establish immunologically optimized Zmp1 peptides as promising serological biomarkers for TB, including EPTB. Although further optimization may be required to meet WHO target product profiles, their high specificity supports potential use as an adjunctive diagnostic, particularly for EPTB, and as components of future multi-antigen panels. More broadly, this study demonstrates how mechanistically informed epitope selection can facilitate translation of pathogen-specific immune signatures into minimally invasive diagnostic platforms.

articles.title: Optimal Kidney Protection by Moderate Aggressive Treatment of Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF COMMENTARY: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) has almost never been counted as an important incident endpoint in randomized clinical trials (RCTs) in the prevention of complications and outcomes in essential hypertension but rather included in broader safety assessments. Although target systolic blood pressure (SBP) < 130 and even < 120 mmHg is recommended by some guidelines, it is unclear whether such aggressive treatment has a favorable effect on hypertension-related decline of CKD.

NEW OBSERVATIONS: During the past two decades several RCTs have been performed with patients randomized to more aggressive SBP target vs. SBP target closer to standard treatment. Several large RCTs have targeted and/or otherwise achieved SBP as low as 120 mmHg or maybe even lower in fractions of middle-aged and older high risk essential hypertensive people with major worsening of kidney function. However, other RCTs showed neutral effects or even reduction in kidney endpoints with achieved SBP below 130 mmHg and possible benefit in preventing cardiovascular outcomes though inclusion of soft endpoints in some trials diluted the cardiovascular message. Intensive BP lowering is associated with greater declines in kidney function in all major RCTs investigating target SBP < 120 mmHg. The long-term clinical significance of these changes must be interpreted alongside possible cardiovascular risks. Hence, one should aim at a SBP target < 130 mmHg in middle-aged and older hypertensive patients if the treatment is otherwise well tolerated. The benefits of low SBP targets in patients who develop CKD should be reassessed in the context of new available treatments providing kidney protection such as SGLT2-inhibitors, aldosterone antagonists and GLP1-agonists.

articles.title: A novel partitivirus induces hypovirulence and increases pyraclostrobin sensitivity in the phytopathogenic fungus Lasiodiplodia ziziphi.
articles.abstract: Lasiodiplodia ziziphi causes canker disease in jujube and other woody plants. Its control relies mainly on fungicides. Mycoviruses that cause hypovirulence are an emerging option for the biological control of fungal diseases. In this study, we identified a novel double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) mycovirus, Lasiodiplodia ziziphi partitivirus 1 (LzPV1), from L. ziziphi strain CDZM004. The LzPV1 genome consists of two dsRNA segments. dsRNA1 (1,905 bp) encodes an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), and dsRNA2 (1,773 bp) encodes a capsid protein (CP). The genome is packaged into isometric virions about 32 nm in diameter. Phylogenetic analysis of the RdRp and CP placed LzPV1 in the genus Alphapartitivirus of the family Partitiviridae. LzPV1 was transmitted horizontally through hyphal anastomosis and vertically through conidia. LzPV1 infection reduced the virulence of L. ziziphi, changed its hyphal morphology, and increased fungal sensitivity to the fungicide pyraclostrobin. This is the first mycovirus reported in L. ziziphi and the first partitivirus described in the genus Lasiodiplodia. LzPV1 is a promising biocontrol resource for jujube canker disease.

articles.title: Plasma exosomal microRNA profiling in diabetic foot ulcers: inflammatory and proliferative stages-an observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFU) are chronic, hard-to-heal wounds that drive diabetic lower-limb complications and can ultimately lead to amputation. Exosomal microRNAs (miRNAs) are promising regulators of ulcer repair by modulating inflammation, promoting angiogenesis, enhancing collagen deposition, and facilitating epithelial regeneration. This study profiled plasma exosomal miRNAs across DFU stages to clarify healing mechanisms and identify potential therapeutic targets.

METHODS: Whole-blood samples were collected from patients with uncomplicated type 2 diabetes (DM, n = 6) and patients with DFU (n = 13), including an inflammatory-stage group (DFI, n = 7) and a proliferative-stage group (DFP, n = 6).Plasma exosomes were isolated and characterized by transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis, and Western blotting. Next-generation sequencing was used to compare exosomal miRNA expression between DFU stages and DM, followed by RT-qPCR validation of differentially expressed miRNAs. Bioinformatics analyses were performed to assess involved pathways.

RESULTS: By comparing the plasma exosomal miRNA profiles of patients with DM and DFU, we found that hsa-miR-744-5p, hsa-miR-432-5p, and hsa-miR-1307-3p were upregulated, whereas hsa-miR-15b -5p, hsa-miR-15a-5p and hsa-miR-144-3p were downregulated in DFU versus DM. RT-qPCR validation confirmed the consistent upregulation of only hsa-miR-744-5p and hsa-miR-1307-3p. KEGG enrichment analysis revealed that the dysregulated miRNAs were primarily associated with inflammation- and angiogenesis-related pathways.

CONCLUSIONS: The microRNA profiles of plasma exosomes are associated with healing failure in diabetic foot ulcers, with hsa-miR-744-5p and hsa-miR-1307-3p showing sustained upregulation. This suggests that the inflammation-angiogenesis pathway may be involved, indicating that these plasma exosome miRNAs could serve as potential therapeutic targets for DFU.

articles.title: Rotavirus NSP4 mediates an increase in the pro-inflammatory eicosanoid, prostaglandin E2, during infection.
articles.abstract: Rotavirus (RV) type A is a leading cause of severe infantile gastroenteritis globally. Studies show that prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) levels increase during RV infection, enhancing viral attachment and internalisation. However, the underlying mechanism for the increased PGE2 levels remains unclear. Using a plasmid-based reverse genetics system, we engineered a recombinant RV carrying mutations in the viroporin domain of NSP4 that decreased cytoplasmic calcium (Ca2+) conductivity. This resulted in decreased cytoplasmic phospholipase A2 (cPLA2) activity, the rate-limiting enzyme in PGE2 biosynthesis, and subsequently reduced PGE2 levels and viral yield. These findings are consistent with RV-induced PGE2 production occurring in a NSP4-cyto[Ca²⁺]-cPLA2-dependent manner.

articles.title: Pathogen co-infections and disease complexes in cotton: Environmental drivers, diagnostics and research priorities for disease management.
articles.abstract: Cotton production has long faced multiple-pathogen disease scenarios. These include disease complexes where multiple pathogens are involved, accelerating disease progression, altering symptom expression, and reducing the effectiveness of disease management options. These complexes include cotton root rot, vascular wilt, leaf spot, and boll rot. This Feature Article explores plant-pathogen and pathogen-pathogen interactions in cotton disease complexes and the factors that influence them. It also discusses advances in molecular diagnostics, such as pathogen assemblage profiling, which enables more accurate detection and measurement of co-infections, thereby improving risk evaluation and informing targeted disease management practices. Drawing on evidence from cotton-growing regions worldwide, particular attention is given to the relevance and implications of pathogen co-infection and disease complexes for Australian cotton production systems. Recognizing and managing pathogen co-infections and disease complexes, rather than addressing individual pathogens in isolation, provides a framework for more sustainable cotton production systems and enhances the ability to anticipate and respond to evolving crop health challenges under changing conditions driven by climate change, global trade, and agricultural intensification.

articles.title: Resistome analysis of multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae L-15 harboring blaCTX-M-15 isolated from a diabetic foot ulcer using a low-volume portable broth medium.
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus is one of the most prevalent non-communicable diseases in Indonesia. Diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) infections are among the most severe complications, often leading to bacteremia and mortality. This study aimed to apply a low-volume broth medium supplemented with antibiotics for screening multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria. We used modified low-volume medium for bacterial isolation from diabetic foot ulcers. Bacterial identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed, followed by whole-genome sequencing for resistome analysis. Out of 15 DFU samples, 5 yielded bacteria resistant to amoxicillin and ceftriaxone. Molecular identification using the partial 16S rRNA gene classified these isolates as Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Proteus mirabilis, and Providencia sp. Notably, 5 out of 7 isolates were categorized as MDR due to their resistance to more than three antimicrobial classes. Furthermore, K. pneumoniae L15 exhibited high-level resistance to ceftriaxone with a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of ≥128 µg mL-1. Resistome analysis of K. pneumoniae L15 revealed the presence of aph, blaCTX-M-15, catA2, fosA, qnrS1, sul2, and tetA. Interestingly, blaCTX-M-15 was flanked by mobile genetic elements (MGEs), specifically Tn3 upstream and IS1380 downstream. The blaCTX-M-15 gene structure identified in this study has also been reported in various other Gram-negative bacteria. Detection and analysis of MDR bacterial pathogens in DFU is important for patients care and to decrease spread of MDR pathogens. The blaCTX-M-15 gene in this K. pneumoniae isolate is putatively capable of disseminating to other bacteria via MGEs. Multilocus sequence typing (MLST) determination showed K. pneumoniae L15 in this study belongs to ST14464.

articles.title: Synthetic torpor in the rat protects the heart from ischaemia-reperfusion injury.
articles.abstract: During times of environmental stress, many animals enter torpor: a reversible protective physiological state typically characterised by reductions in core temperature, heart rate, and oxygen consumption. Species that naturally enter this hypothermic and hypometabolic state are tolerant of ischaemia-reperfusion injury. Consequently, there is a growing interest in utilising aspects of torpor for clinical applications such as protection from stroke or myocardial infarction. It is currently unknown, however, whether a torpor-like state is protective in animals that do not naturally enter torpor. Using viral vector-mediated chemogenetic activation of the medial preoptic area of the hypothalamus, we induced synthetic torpor in the rat, a species that does not naturally enter torpor. We demonstrate this state is cardioprotective in an ex vivo ischaemia-reperfusion injury model with an ~40% reduction in infarct size. Synthetic torpor-induced cardioprotection of the normothermic, isolated heart is not dependent on prior hypothermia in vivo. Phosphoproteomic analysis of cardiac tissue indicates that the protective effects of synthetic torpor may be mediated by parallel activation of cell survival and stress tolerance pathways and inhibition of cell death pathways. These findings provide important insights into the mechanisms of organ protective effects of synthetic torpor states with implications for future clinical translation in humans.

articles.title: Enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli, a hound for signals.
articles.abstract: Enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli (EHEC) is a major cause of severe diarrhea worldwide and can produce Shiga toxin, leading to hemolytic uremic syndrome and resulting in high morbidity and mortality. EHEC colonizes the human colon but must overcome multiple barriers before reaching its infection niche. The gut microbiota is known as a first line of defense against pathogen colonization by depleting the microenvironment of nutrients and limiting pathogen expansion. To overcome this limitation, EHEC can sense various signals to identify its infection niche and successfully colonize its host. Here, we review the signals that regulate the locus of enterocyte effacement, or LEE, which encodes EHEC's major virulence factor, a type 3 secretion system (T3SS) that allows EHEC to attach to the host colon epithelium. Over the years, EHEC has been found to sense a variety of signals, from carbon sources to microbiota-derived signals and even host communication factors. These signals are mostly perceived by two-component systems (TCSs) and can regulate LEE expression. Since antibiotics trigger Shiga toxin production, developing anti-virulence approaches to treat EHEC infection is the best alternative. Identifying the signals that regulate LEE expression and the underlying mechanistic pathways can enable new strategies to treat EHEC or enteric pathogens more broadly.

articles.title: Preclinical Characterization of [68Ga]Ga/[177Lu]Lu-PSNT-AB: A Dual-Targeted Agent against PSMA and NTSR1 for Prostate Cancer Theranostics.
articles.abstract: Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) is a key biomarker for prostate cancer (PCa), while neurotensin receptor 1 (NTSR1) is positive in PSMA-negative PCa lesions. For comprehensive diagnosis and therapy of PCa, we synthesized dual-targeted PSNT-AB (combining PSMA-targeted EuK, NTSR1-targeted NT-20.3, albumin-binding 4-p-tolylbutyric acid and DOTA moieties) and prepared [68Ga]Ga/[177Lu]Lu-PSNT-AB. [68Ga]Ga-PSNT-AB possessed high affinity for PSMA-positive LNCaP and moderate affinity for NTSR1-positive PC-3 cells. Probes accumulated time-dependently in relevant cells, and [177Lu]Lu-PSNT-AB exerted potent cytotoxicity. Pharmacokinetics revealed prolonged blood half-lives for both probes. PET imaging revealed persistent [68Ga]Ga-PSNT-AB uptake in LNCaP, 22Rv1 and PC-3 tumors (10.29 ± 0.25% ID/g, 6.61 ± 0.30% ID/g, 3.74 ± 0.12% ID/g at 3 h post-injection). SPECT/CT showed sustained [177Lu]Lu-PSNT-AB retention in LNCaP tumors for at least 24 h. These results demonstrated that [68Ga]Ga/[177Lu]Lu-PSNT-AB are promising dual-targeted probes for PCa diagnosis and therapy, offering a potential strategy for comprehensive and effective precision management of PCa.

articles.title: Discovery of Novel Orally Bioavailable STING Inhibitors with 4,5,6,7-Tetrahydropyrazolo[1,5-a]pyrazine Moiety for STING-Mediated Inflammatory Disorders.
articles.abstract: The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS)-stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling pathway plays a pivotal role in host defense against pathogenic microbes and tumors. However, aberrant activation of this pathway is tightly associated with a wide spectrum of inflammatory and autoimmune disorders, positioning STING inhibition as a promising therapeutic strategy. In this study, we designed and synthesized a series of novel 4,5,6,7-tetrahydropyrazolo[1,5-a]pyrazine derivatives as STING inhibitors. Compound 37 displayed potent STING inhibitory activity and favorable in vivo pharmacokinetic properties and safety. Further studies revealed that 37 blocks STING palmitoylation, thereby suppressing downstream signaling pathway activation. Oral administration of 37 exhibited significant anti-inflammatory effects in 10-carboxymethyl-9-acridanone (CMA)-challenged mice, Trex1-/- mice and cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury (AKI) mice. Collectively, compound 37 represents a novel orally bioavailable STING inhibitor with therapeutic potential against STING-driven inflammatory and autoimmune diseases.

articles.title: Development and Preclinical Evaluation of Six-Transmembrane Epithelial Antigen of Prostate 2 Targeted PET Probes: A Case of Drug Repurposing Based on Molecular Docking.
articles.abstract: Six-transmembrane epithelial antigen of prostate 2 (STEAP2) is overexpressed in prostate cancer, yet no STEAP2-targeted imaging probes exist. Using molecular docking, we screened triptorelin and leuprorelin by radioiodine labeling and identified triptorelin as a high-affinity, selective ligand. To enhance in vivo stability and pharmacokinetics, triptorelin underwent acetylation, PEG extension, and 4-iodophenylbutyric acid conjugation, yielding five DOTA-conjugated analogs radiolabeled with 68Ga. In 22Rv1 xenografts, 68Ga-Trip-5 exhibited moderate but specific tumor uptake (SUVmax 1.8) with favorable tumor-to-background contrast. In vivo stability, biodistribution, pharmacokinetics, and human radiation dosimetry (effective dose 0.00345 mSv/MBq) demonstrated favorable safety. Autoradiography on human prostate cancer specimens showed probe accumulation correlating with endogenous STEAP2 expression. This represents the first STEAP2-targeted PET probe developed via molecular docking-guided drug repurposing. Cellular, biochemical, and imaging data provide supportive evidence of STEAP2-mediated targeting. Preclinical performance supports clinical translation of 68Ga-Trip-5, with definitive target validation.

articles.title: Discovery of Neurolysin Activators with Preclinical Efficacy in an Ischemic Stroke Model.
articles.abstract: The peptidase neurolysin (Nln) is upregulated following ischemic stroke to activate endogenous cerebroprotective mechanisms and has subsequently emerged as a therapeutic target for drug discovery efforts. Overexpression of Nln in a mouse model of ischemic stroke results in significant improvement of stroke outcomes. Herein, we report the discovery of the first non-peptide Nln activators based around a central pyridine-piperazine scaffold that possesses nanomolar potency. This scaffold, exemplified by compounds 7c and 7g, exhibits greater in vitro half-life, blood-brain barrier penetration, mouse brain and mouse plasma stability than previously reported peptidomimetic Nln activators. Compound 7g afforded an in vivo protective effect in the MCAO mouse model of ischemic stroke, significantly reducing infarct volume and brain water content, marking the first report of a small molecule Nln activator with in vivo cerebroprotective effects in a preclinical model.

articles.title: Design and Biological Evaluation of FAP-Man, a Mannosylated FAP-Targeted Radioglycopeptide for Tumor Imaging and Radionuclide Therapy.
articles.abstract: Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) is an attractive target for radiotheranostic development because of its abundant expression in tumor-associated fibroblasts and limited distribution in normal tissues. Here, we developed FAP-Man, a mannosylated FAP-targeted radioglycopeptide based on the FAP-2286 scaffold, to optimize tumor targeting and pharmacokinetic properties. Compared with [68Ga]Ga-FAP-2286, [68Ga]Ga-FAP-Man showed higher tumor uptake in U87MG tumor-bearing mice (16.917 ± 4.986 vs 3.188 ± 0.535 %ID/g at 1 h post-injection) and improved tumor-to-liver contrast. Both [177Lu]Lu-FAP-Man and [225Ac]Ac-FAP-Man significantly inhibited tumor growth compared with PBS-treated controls. Preliminary clinical PET imaging further supported its potential for favorable lesion visualization and lesion-to-background contrast, particularly for hepatic lesions. These findings support further evaluation of FAP-Man as a FAP-targeted radiopharmaceutical candidate.

articles.title: Influence of Fluorine Substitution Pattern in Arylboronic Acid Caps on the Myocardial Perfusion Imaging Properties of Technetium Monocapped Tris(dioxime) Complexes.
articles.abstract: Boronate-based myocardial perfusion tracers represent a promising scaffold for quantitative SPECT myocardial blood flow (MBF) imaging. In this study, five fluorinated 99mTc-labeled boronate derivatives were designed to systematically investigate the influence of fluorine substitution patterns on tracer pharmacokinetics and imaging performance. The fluorination pattern markedly influenced myocardial uptake, hepatic clearance, and overall biodistribution, with 99mTc-2F-HMPBA (99mTc-2F) and 99mTc-3F-HMPBA (99mTc-3F) exhibiting the most favorable profiles. Mechanistic evaluation using isolated heart perfusion demonstrated a high first-pass extraction fraction over a wide range of coronary flow rates, while dynamic SPECT imaging in swine showed tracer-derived K1 values comparable to 13N-NH3 PET-derived MBF. In particular, 99mTc-3F exhibited a more balanced pharmacokinetic profile with improved heart-to-liver contrast. These findings establish fluorine substitution as an effective strategy for tuning the pharmacokinetic behavior of boronate-based myocardial perfusion tracers and identify 99mTc-3F as a promising lead for quantitative SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging.

articles.title: Modular Biomimetic Strategy toward Discovery of Macrocyclic Sulfonamides as SIRT3 Activators against Heart Failure.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) remains a severe global cardiovascular disease with limited targeted therapies. Mitochondrial deacetylase SIRT3 is a promising therapeutic target for HF, yet current SIRT3 agonists suffer from low potency and poor isoform selectivity. Herein, we adopted a modular biomimetic strategy to synthesize a series of macrocyclic sulfonamides and systematically explored their structure-activity relationships. The lead compound 2b (Y0855) exhibited potent SIRT3 agonistic activity (EC50 = 12.6 μM, and Emax = 4.05) and excellent selectivity over SIRT1/2/6. Mechanistically, 2b alleviated cardiomyocyte oxidative stress, cell injury and fibrosis via SIRT3 activation. In a doxorubicin-induced HF mouse model, it markedly restored cardiac function and mitigated myocardial damage. Moreover, 2b possessed improved metabolic stability, making it a valuable lead compound for anti-HF drug development targeting SIRT3.

articles.title: De Novo Design of Multi-Mechanistic AIE Photosensitizer for Broad-Spectrum Bacterial Eradication.
articles.abstract: Antibiotic resistance poses a serious threat to human health. Inspired by the clinical practice of employing drug combinations to achieve combined effects, we hypothesized that integrating multiple mechanisms into a single molecule could address drug-resistant bacterial infections. Based on a propeller-modification strategy and dual alkyl-chain engineering, we de novo designed and synthesized a C2-symmetric propeller-shaped aggregation-induced emission photosensitizer. After iterative screening, the optimized compound MeOTDP-2 exhibits broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, enabling efficient eradication of planktonic bacteria, drug-resistant strains, polymicrobial infections, biofilms, and persister cells, with no cellular invasiveness and negligible cytotoxicity. Mechanistic studies revealed that MeOTDP-2 achieves chemo-photodynamic combined antibacterial therapy by targeting and disrupting bacterial membranes and DNA, alongside light-mediated intracellular reactive oxygen species accumulation. Furthermore, in mouse models of MRSA-induced skin abscess and full-thickness skin wound infection, MeOTDP-2 demonstrated superior therapeutic efficacy to vancomycin. This strategy, integrating dual targeting with multiple mechanisms, offers new promise for overcoming bacterial resistance.

articles.title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Pentacyclic Triterpene Derivatives as Intestinal FXR Antagonists for Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Intestinal farnesoid X receptor (FXR) antagonism has emerged as a strategy to enhance endogenous glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) secretion and improve metabolic control in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Dihydrooleanolic acid methyl ester (DKS26) served as the scaffold for the synthesis of 64 pentacyclic triterpene derivatives modified at the terminal carboxyl group and C-3/C-12 positions. Esterification of the terminal carboxylate emerged as a determinant of FXR antagonism, identifying 4l bearing a tetrazole-containing side chain and C-12 hydroxyl motif. Compound 4l antagonized FXR in a TR-FRET assay (IC50 = 11.79 μM), a fivefold improvement over DKS26. In NCI-H716 cells, 4l reduced NR0B2 (SHP) mRNA expression and markedly stimulated GLP-1 secretion. In HFD/STZ-induced diabetic mice, oral 4l improved glycemia, increased circulating GLP-1 and insulin, and alleviated dyslipidemia and organ injury markers. These findings establish the pentacyclic triterpene scaffold as a platform for FXR antagonism and identify 4l as a lead for further optimization.

articles.title: Enhancing the Specificity of the CAIX-Targeted Radionuclide Probe via the Optimization Cyclic Peptide Cyclization Linker.
articles.abstract: Carbonic anhydrase IX (CAIX) is a key biomarker for clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) PET imaging. The reported probe 68Ga-DPI-4452 strongly targets both hCAIX and hCAII, therefore hindering its clinical applications. This study developed two optimized probes, 68Ga-WF1 and 68Ga-WF2. They have nanomolar affinity for hCAIX but far weaker binding to hCAII compared with that of 68Ga-DPI-4452. In OS-RC-2 tumor-bearing mice, the tumor uptake of 68Ga-WF1 and 68Ga-WF2 was comparable to that of 68Ga-DPI-4452. However, since 68Ga-WF2 exhibited the lowest affinity for mCAII and mCAIX, its gastrointestinal uptake was the lowest. The autoradiography result revealed that three probes strongly bound human ccRCC tissues, while 68Ga-WF1 and 68Ga-WF2 bound far less to digestive tract tissues. Due to the lowest affinity of 68Ga-WF1 for hCAII, it effectively reduces uptake in the human gastrointestinal tract, holding promise for high tumor contrast and low gastrointestinal tract toxicity for ccRCC PET imaging.

articles.title: Discovery of C5-Substituted 2'-Fluorinated Pyrimidine Nucleosides as Potent and Orally Efficacious Anti-HSV Agents.
articles.abstract: Herpes simplex virus (HSV) infections remain a significant global health concern. Through phenotypic screening of a nucleoside-focused library followed by systematic structure-activity relationship (SAR) explorations, we identified C5-substituted 2'-fluorinated pyrimidine nucleosides as promising anti-HSV scaffolds. We found that introducing five-membered heteroaryls at the uracil C5 position significantly enhanced antiviral potency, whereas cytosine and alkynyl derivatives showed limited efficacy. The optimized lead, B10, exhibited potent in vitro inhibition against HSV-1 (EC50 = 0.60 μM) and HSV-2 (EC50 = 7.32 μM) with minimal cytotoxicity. Importantly, B10 demonstrated a highly favorable oral bioavailability of 48.0% in rats. In a murine intranasal HSV-1 infection model, oral administration of B10 significantly improved survival rates, alleviated weight loss, suppressed acute viral replication in the central nervous system, and reduced pulmonary viral titers. These findings highlight the 2'-fluoro-C5-heteroaryl uracil framework as a robust chemotype and establish B10 as an orally efficacious candidate for HSV therapy.

articles.title: A Novel Chemotype of Orally Active SARS-CoV-2 NSP14 Methyltransferase Inhibitors.
articles.abstract: The periodic emergence of human coronaviruses (hCoVs) necessitates direct-acting antivirals targeting underexploited viral proteins with broad-spectrum potential.
