Building on our discovery of TDI-015051, a first-in-class SARS-CoV-2 mRNA cap guanine-N7 methyltransferase (MTase) NSP14 inhibitor whose translational development was limited by metabolic liabilities, we conducted medicinal chemistry optimization of a structurally distinct high-throughput screening hit. We arrived at MAVDA-K-256, a small-molecule inhibitor with improved pharmacological properties compared to TDI-015051. MAVDA-K-256 engaged NSP14 through the formation of a ternary complex with S-adenosyl-l-homocysteine, potently inhibiting its MTase activity and SARS-CoV-2 replication (EC50 = 24.6 nM). MAVDA-K-256 demonstrated broad-spectrum antiviral activity against diverse hCoVs without targeting the host mRNA cap MTase. Its favorable metabolic stability and pharmacokinetic properties enabled twice-daily oral dosing in a murine SARS-CoV-2 infection model, resulting in a five-log reduction in viral lung burden. These findings validate NSP14 inhibition as a promising antiviral strategy and support further preclinical development of MAVDA-K-256.

articles.title: Alpha-Lipoic Acid Derivatives: A Multifunctional Neuroprotective Agent with Potential for Treating Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) is a major public health burden due to its high mortality and disability rates. Neuroinflammation and ferroptosis are two key drivers of IS progression. α-Lipoic acid (ALA) exhibits both anti-ferroptosis and anti-inflammatory activities; however, its anti-ferroptosis efficacy is suboptimal. In this study, we designed and synthesized 23 ALA derivatives. Among them, D14 exhibited the most potent anti-ferroptosis activity, with an EC50 value of 0.00247 μM, an approximately 16,000-fold improvement over ALA, while retaining comparable anti-inflammatory activity (IC50 = 13.6 μM). Mechanistically, D14 scavenged free radicals and activated the Nrf2/GPX4 pathway to restore GSH levels and reduce MDA, Fe2+, and ROS accumulation, thereby inhibiting ferroptosis. D14 also suppressed NF-κB activation by preventing IκBα degradation and p65 phosphorylation, and it reduced IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α secretion. In a rat middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model, D14 reduced cerebral infarct volume and ameliorated neurological deficits, surpassing ALA and the clinically used drug edaravone. Preliminary toxicity evaluation of D14 indicated a favorable safety profile. Overall, D14 is a promising multi-target lead compound for the treatment of IS.

articles.title: HER2-Targeting Affibody Equipped with Albumin-Binding Small Molecules for Radiotheranostics.
articles.abstract: HER2-targeting affibody radioprobes are often limited by rapid systemic clearance and excessive renal accumulation. Herein, we develop a modular chemical strategy to optimize the pharmacokinetic properties of affibodies through conjugation of small-molecule albumin-binding motifs (ABMs). Enabled by our selective S-glycosylation approach, ABMs were introduced via a sugar-based linker, allowing systematic modulation of probe behavior. Evaluation of sugar-modified variants revealed that sugar structure plays a critical role in regulating in vivo distribution, with the GalNAc-modified probe [68Ga]Ga-5c exhibiting favorable tumor-to-background contrast in PET/CT imaging. Further incorporation of ABMs afforded GalNAc-IPBA-functionalized affibody [177Lu]Lu-10a, which achieved an 17-fold extension of circulation half-life, reduced renal accumulation, and maintained efficient tumor targeting. Therapeutically, [177Lu]Lu-10a induced 86.25% tumor growth inhibition with minimal systemic toxicity. This study provides a modular strategy for overcoming pharmacokinetic limitations of affibody-based radiotheranostics.

articles.title: Chimeric Hsp90β-Selective Inhibitors Confer Enhanced Affinity, Selectivity, and Drug-Like Properties.
articles.abstract: The clinical evaluation of 90 kD heat shock protein (Hsp90) inhibitors has been hindered by their detrimental, pan-inhibitory activities. Consequently, the development of Hsp90 isoform-selective inhibitors has been pursued. Although prior compounds have elucidated the roles of Hsp90β in cancer immunotherapy and opioid therapy, their sub-optimal drug-like properties have required extensive optimization campaigns to enhance this scaffold's pharmacological profile. The work presented herein expands upon previous efforts by introducing simultaneous modifications to the "northern" indazolone fragment and "southwestern" appendage to determine whether combinations of the properties at these regions can produce improved Hsp90β-selective inhibitors. These chimeric inhibitors reveal that such modifications can retain Hsp90β affinity/selectivity, while modulating key pharmacokinetic parameters and anticancer activity. Notably, one derivative (8b) also exhibits oral bioavailability and enhances opioid antinociception in a murine model for chronic pain. These findings support the continued development of Hsp90β-selective inhibitors for anticancer therapy, chronic pain management, and other disease indications.

articles.title: Nucleic Acid Aptamers in Bacteriology: Mapping the Landscape, Exploring Bioimaging Applications, Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
articles.abstract: Antibiotic resistance is becoming increasingly widespread, underlining the importance of rapid, accurate identification of bacterial infections for effective diagnostic, clinical, and environmental management. While next-generation sequencing excels at genetic characterization, it falls short in real-time, in situ detection, a critical gap where nucleic acid aptamers emerge as a compelling alternative. These synthetic oligonucleotides enable direct, low-cost, and versatile detection of bacterial targets without requiring DNA extraction or amplification. Their portability supports point-of-care diagnostics, while their molecular precision enables integration into advanced bioimaging platforms for non-invasive, real-time, spatial, and functional monitoring of pathogens in biological environments. This perspective explores the potential of aptamers for bacterial bioimaging, assessing the landscape of bacterial-targeting aptamers, zooming in on aptamer-based bioimaging approaches for bacterial detection, addressing key challenges, and outlining future opportunities, such as real-time dynamic infection imaging and theranostics, polyclonal/multivalent aptamers, multiplex imaging, aptamer-based biosensors, and AI-driven detection.

articles.title: Discovery of Novel GPR119 Agonists with Improved Kinetic Solubility and Drug-like Properties for Type 2 Diabetes Treatment.
articles.abstract: GPR119 is a compelling therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes due to its role in promoting glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide (GIP), and glucose-dependent insulin secretion. This study aimed to develop a series of novel GPR119 agonists with exceptional kinetic solubility over a broad pH range featuring an N-alkyl piperidine head and pyrrolidine 2-carboxamide tail. Among the synthesized compounds, 18f demonstrated potent activity, exhibiting nanomolar potency (EC50 = 12.6 nM) in the hGPR119-cAMP functional assay as well as a 33.3% hypoglycemic effect in an oral glucose tolerance test. A significant enhancement (175.9%) of total GLP-1 levels was observed at 10 mg/kg administration of compound 18f. Further, compound 18f outperformed the antidiabetic effect of sitagliptin as the DPP-4 inhibitor in female Zucker Diabetic Fatty rats. Furthermore, the favorable pharmacokinetic profiles of compound 18f underscore its potential as a promising lead compound for type 2 diabetes treatment.

articles.title: Immune control of lethal Nipah virus infection: the critical role of host macrophages.
articles.abstract: AbstractNipah virus (NiV) is highly pathogenic zoonotic paramyxovirus of Henipavirus genus that causes recurrent human outbreaks in South-East Asia, with a lethality of 40-75%. Immunopathogenesis associated to this emerging virus is still poorly understood and the role of different components of the immune response in the control of infection remains unknown. In contrast to many other mammalian species, wild type mice are resistant to NiV infection, due to an efficient type-I interferon response. We have analysed the role of various immune cell populations in the control of NiV infection and demonstrated the critical role of T lymphocytes but neither B lymphocytes nor NK cells were primordial. In addition, the depletion of phagocytes in mice by injection of clodronate liposomes resulted in dramatical increase of their susceptibility to NiV infection. Moreover, using CD169-DTR transgenic mice we show here that the specific depletion of CD169+ macrophages results in an increased susceptibility of mice to NiV challenge, highlighting the important role of this cell population. Finally, in NiV-infected African green monkeys, which closely resemble severe human Nipah disease, the production of virus-induced type-I and -II interferons was followed with an important increase of CD169+ cells in the blood and lungs, with some of them being NiV-infected. As CD169+ macrophages have been described to play an important role at the crossroads between innate and adaptive immunity in various infections, these results reveal their potentially determining role during NiV infection as well, which may help to better understand this highly lethal infectious disease.

articles.title: Transcatheter Mitral Valve-in-Valve Implantation Despite Left Atrial Appendage Thrombosis: A Challenging Therapeutic Strategy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter mitral valve-in-valve (ViV) implantation is an alternative to redo surgery in high-risk patients with degenerated mitral bioprostheses.

CASE SUMMARY: An elderly woman presented with recurrent acute pulmonary edema due to severe stenosis of a degenerated mitral bioprosthesis. Redo surgery was considered prohibitive (EuroSCORE II: 15%). Transesophageal echocardiography revealed persistent left atrial appendage (LAA) thrombosis despite appropriate anticoagulation, increasing embolic risk. Given severe symptoms and lack of viable alternatives, transseptal mitral ViV implantation was successfully performed using the FLOWer cerebral embolic protection device, without neurological complications and with excellent hemodynamic results.

DISCUSSION: LAA thrombosis is generally considered a relative contraindication to transseptal mitral interventions because of thromboembolic risk. This case highlights the potential role of cerebral embolic protection and individualized heart team decision-making in highly selected patients.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Mitral ViV implantation with cerebral embolic protection may be feasible in selected patients with LAA thrombosis and prohibitive surgical risk.

articles.title: Transbaffle Transcatheter Valve-in-Valve Implantation for Systemic Atrioventricular Bioprosthetic Stenosis in a Patient With Fontan Circulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We report the case of a 29-year-old woman with an atrioventricular canal defect with left ventricular hypoplasia and mitral atresia in the setting of situs inversus and dextrocardia, palliated with Fontan circulation.

CASE SUMMARY: At 21 years of age, she underwent systemic atrioventricular valve replacement with a 33-mm Hancock II bioprosthesis (Medtronic). Eight years later, she developed progressive bioprosthetic stenosis: mean transvalvular gradient of 11 mm Hg with restricted leaflet motion. Given prohibitive surgical risk, transcatheter valve-in-valve (ViV) implantation using a 29-mm Sapien 3 (Edwards Lifesciences) prosthesis was performed via transbaffle access. The procedure resulted in immediate hemodynamic improvement with reduction of the mean gradient.

DISCUSSION: Only a few cases of transbaffle ViV implantation in the systemic atrioventricular position in patients with a Fontan circulation have been reported.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: This case illustrates the feasibility of transbaffle ViV implantation in complex Fontan anatomy and highlights transcatheter therapy as a valuable alternative in high-risk adult congenital heart disease.

articles.title: Leadless Pacing Dyssynchrony and Diastolic Mitral Regurgitation Rescued by Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dual-chamber leadless pacing depends on beat-to-beat implant-to-implant communication; heart failure-related geometric changes may expose limited communication reserve.

CASE SUMMARY: A 92-year-old woman with complete atrioventricular block developed heart failure 9 months after dual-chamber leadless pacemaker implantation, with reduced atrial-to-ventricular (A-to-V) throughput, atrioventricular dissociation, ventricular functional and diastolic mitral regurgitation, and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction. Decongestion was accompanied by shortening of the projected interdevice distance, improvement in A-to-V throughput and atrioventricular synchrony, and disappearance of diastolic mitral regurgitation. Heart failure recurred despite preserved throughput and continued medical therapy. Upgrade to a transvenous dual-chamber pacemaker with left bundle branch area pacing narrowed the QRS and improved left ventricular function and mitral regurgitation.

DISCUSSION: Pacing-induced cardiomyopathy appeared to be the dominant substrate, with dynamic A-to-V limitation as a reversible aggravating factor. Left bundle branch area pacing addressed both atrioventricular and ventricular dyssynchrony.

articles.title: Transinnominate Microaxial Flow Pump Placement in a Patient With Failing Fontan Circulation as Bridge to Transplantation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Impella 5.5 is a temporary microaxial ventricular assist device indicated to unload the left ventricle and support refractory heart failure. Small peripheral arteries and atypical right ventricular anatomy may preclude its use in patients with Fontan circulation.

CASE SUMMARY: We report a 23-year-old man with hypoplastic left heart syndrome palliated to Fontan with refractory heart failure. Impella 5.5 was placed via the innominate artery, providing 4.5 L/min support for 13 days until heart transplantation; he was discharged in good condition.

DISCUSSION: Transinnominate approach enables effective bridge to transplantation despite small peripheral vessels.

NOVELTY: This is the first reported case of Impella 5.5 as a bridge to transplant placed via transinnominate artery in an adult with failing Fontan circulation and a systemic right ventricle.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Impella 5.5 via transinnominate access is feasible in select patients with Fontan circulation and small peripheral vessels and serves as an effective bridge to transplantation.

articles.title: Unraveling Severe Myocardial Dysfunction in Streptococcal Toxic Shock Syndrome: Beyond Septic Shock.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Group A Streptococcus is a clinically important yet underrecognized cause of inflammatory myocardial dysfunction, capable of triggering shock through toxin-mediated injury and inflammation.

CASE SUMMARY: A 19-year-old woman presented with progressive fatigue, severe hypotension, and a purpuric chest rash. Laboratory investigation showed rising troponin, leukocytosis, and lactic acidosis. Echocardiography and right heart catheterization revealed significant biventricular dysfunction. She developed shock requiring mechanical circulatory support with an Impella CP and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. Corticosteroids and intravenous immunoglobulin were initiated empirically for presumed inflammatory myocarditis. Chest wall biopsy grew Group A Streptococcus, supporting the diagnosis of streptococcal toxic shock syndrome (STSS). Ultimately, she recovered cardiac function with mechanical circulatory support and targeted antimicrobial therapy.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights severe, reversible myocardial dysfunction because of STSS.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: STSS can precipitate severe, reversible myocardial dysfunction representing a mixed septic-cardiogenic phenotype that may mimic fulminant myocarditis.

articles.title: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion and Percutaneous Coumadin Ridge Mass Exclusion: Two Targets, One Device.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mobile cardiac masses on the coumadin ridge are rare and carry significant embolic risk, compounded by concurrent atrial fibrillation. Surgical excision may be prohibitive in patients with high bleeding risk.

CASE SUMMARY: A 70-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, a HAS-BLED score of 4, and aversion to anticoagulation was referred for left atrial appendage (LAA) closure. Imaging revealed an incidental 0.56-cm mobile coumadin ridge mass consistent with papillary fibroelastoma. The Amplatzer Amulet was selected for its larger disc geometry to simultaneously occlude the LAA and exclude the mass, with follow-up confirming complete mass exclusion and stability at over 2 years.

DISCUSSION: This is to our knowledge the first reported case of intentional simultaneous LAA occlusion and percutaneous mass exclusion, demonstrating a novel use of device geometry to manage dual embolic risk.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Concurrent LAA and coumadin ridge mass risk can be addressed in a single procedure through deliberate device selection using the Amulet's larger disc.

articles.title: Aortic Dissection After Stage 1 Palliation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric aortic dissection (AD) is rare and usually associated with hypertension or aortopathies. In this case, we present a Stanford type B dissection in an asymptomatic patient with single ventricle heart disease without known genetic aortopathy following stage 1 palliation.

CASE SUMMARY: Dissection was diagnosed on routine catheterization and confirmed on computed tomography angiography. There was no progression, so no surgical intervention was pursued. He underwent stage 2 palliation at age 6 months and continues to do well.

DISCUSSION: AD is rare in pediatrics, especially infants without aortopathy. A single iatrogenic case report after hybrid palliation has been described. Our patient had at least 2 risk factors, aortic coarctation and intermittently elevated blood pressure, that could have predisposed him to dissection.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: AD is rarely seen following the Norwood operation. Stanford type B AD can be safely medically managed in pediatric patients as in the adult guidelines.

articles.title: Pembrolizumab-Associated Myocarditis and Myasthenic Crisis: Discordant Functional and Tissue Recovery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) can cause myocarditis with overlapping neuromuscular toxicity.

CASE SUMMARY: A 77-year-old man developed biopsy-supported ICI myocarditis with biventricular dysfunction (left ventricular ejection fraction: 36%) after 1 pembrolizumab cycle. The course was complicated by seropositive myasthenia gravis (MG) requiring mechanical ventilation and an unexpected nonocclusive saddle pulmonary embolism. Corticosteroid-refractory troponin elevation prompted escalation to abatacept, while prednisone was reduced for worsening myasthenic weakness. Follow-up cardiac magnetic resonance during sepsis showed improved left ventricular ejection fraction of 53%, but myocardial T2 remained elevated with a persistent nonischemic pattern of late gadolinium enhancement. Troponin remained elevated, and ventilator dependence persisted.

DISCUSSION: ICI myocarditis may show improving ventricular systolic function while myocardial tissue abnormalities persist, and coexisting MG may limit corticosteroid use.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Myocarditis and MG may coexist and require multidisciplinary management. Troponin T may remain elevated for months and is not diagnostic of ongoing myocardial inflammation.

articles.title: Antegrade Dissection and Re-Entry for Recanalization of Traumatic Coronary Artery Dissection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traumatic coronary artery dissection (TCAD) is a rare catastrophic complication of blunt chest trauma, often masked by concomitant injuries, posing diagnostic and therapeutic challenges.

CASE SUMMARY: A 20-year-old man with polytrauma after a motorcycle accident developed cardiogenic shock. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) suggested occlusive left anterior descending dissection, confirmed by delayed angiography under extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support. Stingray-based antegrade dissection and re-entry (ADR) with cutting balloon fenestration and drug-coated balloon angioplasty achieved TIMI flow grade 3. Three-month follow-up showed favorable left anterior descending healing and improved cardiac function.

DISCUSSION: CCTA enables early TCAD diagnosis. ADR facilitates guidewire passage, and a stentless strategy is preferable in young polytrauma patients at high bleeding risk.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Maintain suspicion for TCAD after blunt chest trauma, especially with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction features. CCTA aids early diagnosis; ADR-based percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-coated balloon is safe and effective.

articles.title: Navigating a Recanalized RCA CTO Case With Antegrade Dissection and Re-Entry.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe a reproducible, stepwise hybrid approach to a balloon- and microcatheter uncrossable recanalized right coronary artery with a distal chronic total occlusion (CTO) in a postcoronary artery bypass grafting patient with reduced ejection fraction.

KEY STEPS: 1) Dual injections for distal target definition and collateral assessment; 2) Antegrade wiring escalation with recognition of a proximal uncrossable segment; 3) Retrograde right coronary artery collateral wiring attempts; 4) Rotational atherectomy for proximal plaque modification enabling CTO equipment delivery; 5) Stingray-based antegrade dissection and re-entry using a stick-and-swap technique; 6) Intravascular ultrasound confirmation of true-lumen position and landing zones; and 7) Stenting with TIMI flow grade 3 restoration.

POTENTIAL PITFALLS: Failed rotational atherectomy wire delivery can be addressed by applying other lesion-modifying techniques, retrograde externalization, extraplaque plaque modification, or a more proximal subintimal entry for antegrade dissection and re-entry. Failed antegrade dissection and re-entry without a retrograde option may require converting to an investment procedure.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: CTO percutaneous coronary intervention techniques can be performed in non-CTO uncrossable lesions; however, early failure-mode recognition and timely strategy escalation are critical for procedural safety and success.

articles.title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure or Anticoagulation for Atrial Fibrillation: Navigating Heterogeneity in Clinical Evidence: JACC Evidence Review.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
articles.abstract: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has emerged as an alternative to long-term anticoagulation for preventing stroke or systemic embolism in selected patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) based on several randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that collectively enrolled >7,000 participants. In this JACC Evidence Review, we interpret the major RCTs as distinct experiments, clarify what each can and cannot establish, and offer a phenotype-based framework for interpreting the evidence. The most recent RCTs, OPTION, CLOSURE-AF, and CHAMPION-AF, have prompted efforts to pool the evidence into a single summary estimate. However, these trials are not one coherent evidence base; they are distinct clinical experiments that asked different questions. They differ in patient phenotype, comparator, device generation, postprocedure antithrombotic regimen, endpoint construction, and follow-up duration. Study-level meta-analysis of published reports remains methodologically valid for estimating the broad direction of effect of a device class, but when the component trials differ materially in patient phenotype, comparator, and outcome construction, the pooled estimate does not map to a common patient group or treatment decision. Patient eligibility as well as thromboembolic and bleeding risk varied markedly across trials. In addition, device technology has progressed, and comparators have evolved from warfarin to direct oral anticoagulants. Heterogeneity and insufficient details also exist about the antithrombotic therapy regimen in LAAC arms and adjunct antiplatelet therapy in control arms. Methodological issues further complicate interpretation, including the use of bleeding events (ie, the putative ancillary benefit of LAAC compared with anticoagulation) within composite endpoints tested for noninferiority, varying noninferiority margins, analytical approaches that may undermine the interpretation of noninferiority, and exclusion of periprocedural bleeding from primary safety endpoints in some trials. Finally, the standard of care for anticoagulation in AF has evolved, obviating concomitant aspirin use in stable individuals on therapeutic anticoagulation, thereby reducing bleeding risk compared with that of the control arm of LAAC RCTs. For most anticoagulation-eligible patients, anticoagulation remains the preferred first-line strategy. LAAC is a reasonable option when long-term anticoagulation is unsafe or unsustainable provided that procedural risk, adjunct antithrombotic feasibility, surveillance needs, and competing mortality are carefully considered. RCT evidence in this latter population is limited, and RCTs in other populations have features that limit their support for LAAC as an alternative to anticoagulation. Because LAAC and anticoagulation offer different types of risk, aligning the most applicable evidence with patient values through shared decision-making is central to care.

articles.title: Percutaneous Left Atrial Appendage Closure Device Utilization Among Medicare Beneficiaries.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

articles.title: Antihypertensive treatment - achievements and perspectives in Europe by 2026 Italian, Swiss and Norwegian patient care.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of this perspective review paper is to provide a concise overview of selected aspects of contemporary hypertension care in Norway, Switzerland, and Italy; European countries with populations of approximately 5.5, 9, and 61 million inhabitants, respectively. These countries show remarkably similar prevalences of hypertension, as well as comparable proportions of hypertensive patients who are diagnosed, treated, and controlled.

METHODS: Each country has contributed to the development of hypertension management in distinctive ways. This is illustrated by the evolution of hypertension care in the three countries-which advanced hypertension management through different but complementary contributions.

RESULTS: Italy has provided extensive clinical and research expertise, together with sustained engagement in the European Society of Hypertension and in the development of European guidelines. Norway has been strongly involved in the design and conduct of many large clinical trials that helped define the clinical evidence base in the field, and with general practitioners as investigators. Also, the government financed major surveys and epidemiological studies with blood pressure (BP) as a key variable including collecting data for modern risk assessment in old people (SCORE2-Old People). Switzerland, for its part, made important contributions to the development of new antihypertensive drugs, particularly blockers of the renin-angiotensin system and calcium antagonists. Switzerland was also among the first European countries to accept, promote, and reimburse ambulatory blood pressure monitoring performed by general practitioners, already by the late 1980s.

CONCLUSION: We summarize novelties in text boxes besides basic principles, recent clarifications, and important unresolved issues, supported by selected key references.

articles.title: Impact of bronchial thermoplasty on exacerbation rates, quality of life, and healthcare utilization in severe asthma: a systematic review and meta-analysis of long-term outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bronchial thermoplasty (BT) utilizes regulated radiofrequency radiation to diminish airway smooth muscle and enhance asthma management. This study aimed to assess the long-term effects of BT on asthma exacerbation rates, quality of life, healthcare utilization, lung function, and safety in adults with severe asthma.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus through August 2024. Seventeen studies (randomized controlled trials and observational cohorts) with ≥12-month follow-up were included. Outcomes assessed were exacerbations, quality of life, healthcare utilization, lung function, and adverse events. Data were synthesized using random-effects models.

RESULTS: BT was consistently associated with reductions in severe exacerbations and emergency visits. Improvements in asthma-related quality of life were observed and remained evident during long-term follow-up. In contrast, changes in lung function were modest and often not significant. Reported adverse events were generally mild, occurred mainly in the early weeks after the procedure, and no additional long-term safety concerns were identified.

CONCLUSIONS: BT provides sustained clinical benefits in carefully selected severe asthma patients, improving quality of life and reducing exacerbations without long-term safety concerns.

articles.title: Prediction of PD-L1 expression in NSCLC patients based on 18F-FDG PET/CT heterogeneity scores.
articles.journal: The quarterly journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging : official publication of the Italian Association of Nuclear Medicine (AIMN) [and] the International Association of Radiopharmacology (IAR), [and] Section of the Society of...
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aims to explore the role of radiomic features and PET image heterogeneity in predicting PD-L1 expression in NSCLC.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included pathologically confirmed NSCLC patients who underwent pre-treatment 18F-FDG PET/CT and PD-L1 immunohistochemical assessment, PD-L1 positivity was defined as a tumor proportion score (TPS) ≥1%. Metabolic heterogeneity was assessed using the coefficient of variation (COV, SUVsd / SUVmean × 100%), the distance from the hottest voxel to the tumor centroid (NHOC), and the distance from the hottest voxel to the nearest tumor boundary (NHOP). Tumors were semi-automatically segmented using a 40% SUVmax threshold. To capture the most comprehensive peritumoral information, the ROI is expanded by 15 mm. Radiomic features were extracted from intratumoral and 15-mm peritumoral regions on PET and CT images and a model is built with tumor and surrounding features using Gradient Boosting Decision Tree. The model effectiveness is assessed using AUC, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and F1 score.

RESULTS: The study included 96 patients (median age: 64 [59, 70] years), of whom 58 were male. 63 patients were PD-L1 expression positive, while 33 were negative. COV and NHOP was significantly higher in the PD-L1 positive group (Z=-2.688, P=0.007; Z=-3.704, P<0.001), while no significant differences noted in other parameters between the groups (P>0.05 for all). Both COV and NHOP are independent predictors of PD-L1 positivity(P<0.05). The combined radiomics model outperforms the individual radiomics models, with the integrated intratumoral CT, PET, and peritumoral CT radiomics model achieving the highest predictive performance (AUC=0.816). The addition of metabolic heterogeneity parameters (COV and NHOP) further improved discrimination, resulting in all evaluation metrics exceeding 0.8.

CONCLUSIONS: 18F-FDG PET/CT metabolic parameters, especially COV and NHOP, predict PD-L1 expression and improve targeted treatment decision-making.

articles.title: Environmental Tobacco Smoke and Gastric Cancer: Evidence from the Stomach Cancer Pooling (StoP) Project and a Comprehensive Meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Few studies have investigated environmental tobacco smoke (ETS), commonly known as secondhand smoke, and gastric cancer (GC) risk, and the findings have been inconsistent. We conducted a pooled analysis from StoP Project and a comprehensive meta-analysis to evaluate the potential impact of ETS exposure on GC risk.

METHODS: Five case-control studies with ETS information from the StoP project were included (1,560 GC cases and 2,497 controls). Study-specific odds ratios (ORs) and the corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated using unconditional logistic regression models, adjusting for potential confounders. Pooled effect estimates were computed using random-effects models, with heterogeneity assessed using I2 (%) statistics. A comprehensive meta-analysis was conducted including the StoP project and published studies (n=14), with publication bias assed via funnel plot and Egger's test.

RESULTS: Study-specific estimates were heterogeneous, with stronger associations observed among never-smokers. A strong positive association was observed in the Iran study (aOR = 2.38; 95%CI: 1.11, 5.09) among never-smokers. ETS exposure was not associated with GC risk in the pooled StoP analysis. In the comprehensive meta-analysis, the H. pylori-adjusted subgroup showed a positive association (aOR = 1.41; 95% CI: 1.21-1.64). The overall aOR was 1.25 (95% CI: 0.98-1.59, I2 = 69.9%).

CONCLUSIONS: The results support the hypothesis that ETS could be a risk factor for GC, underscoring the importance of targeted preventive measures and public health policies to reduce ETS exposure.

IMPACT: This study provides the most comprehensive evaluation to date of ETS exposure and highlights ETS as a preventable GC risk factor.

articles.title: Hybrid and endovascular repair of aberrant subclavian artery aneurysms and Kommerell diverticulum: single-center experience and long-term outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aberrant subclavian artery (ASA) represents the most frequent congenital anomaly of the aortic arch and may occasionally develop aneurysmal dilation (aASA) at risk of dissection or rupture. Early diagnosis and tailored management are therefore crucial. We report our long-term single-center experience with endovascular and hybrid repair of aASA and Kommerell's diverticulum (KD).

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed all consecutive patients treated for aASA between January 2010 and June 2024 at our tertiary referral center. Primary endpoints were primary technical success, perioperative and late mortality, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Secondary endpoints included symptom evolution, reinterventions, and complications.

RESULTS: Ten patients (5 females, 50%; mean age 62±19 years, range 16-80) were included. Seven (70%) presented with right ASA, and two (20%) with right aortic arch and left ASA. Seven patients (70%) were symptomatic; 43% had acute type B aortic dissection, 14% type A, and 28% descending thoracic aortic aneurysm. Four patients (40%) underwent total endovascular repair, and four (40%) hybrid procedures. Primary technical success was achieved in all cases, with no intraoperative deaths. Perioperative mortality was 10% and late mortality 30%. Complications included type II endoleak, access-site hematoma or infection, and transient upper-limb ischemia. No MACE occurred during the study period.

CONCLUSIONS: Hybrid and endovascular approaches appear to represent safe and effective alternatives to open repair for complex aASA anatomy when performed in experienced referral centers. Given the limited cohort size, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive and hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Real-time Radiation Exposure Monitoring in the Cardiac Catheterization Laboratory Using a Digital RRPD Dosimeter.
articles.abstract: Occupational exposure to ionizing radiation remains an important concern for healthcare professionals working in x-ray-guided interventional environments. Conventional passive dosimetry provides retrospective dose assessment and does not permit immediate modification of operator behavior. We evaluated the feasibility and practical utility of a real-time radiation personal dosimeter (RRPD) during three chronic total occlusion (CTO) percutaneous coronary intervention procedures performed in a cardiac catheterization laboratory. Wearable dosimeters were positioned on the lead aprons of the primary and secondary operators and provided continuous wireless measurements of the dose rate and cumulative radiation exposure. Procedural parameters, including fluoroscopy time, air kerma, dose-area product (DAP), cine acquisition count, and operator dose, were recorded and compared with commonly reported reference ranges for CTO interventions. Radiation exposure increases with procedural complexity. Antegrade CTO procedures demonstrated fluoroscopy time, air kerma, and DAP values below the typical reference ranges, whereas a complex retrograde CTO procedure was associated with higher values consistent with prolonged fluoroscopy. Real-time visualization of radiation peaks was associated with timely operator adjustments without too much clinical interference, including reduced angulation and limitations of cine imaging. The primary operator exposure exceeded the secondary operator exposure in all cases. These findings indicate that real-time personal dosimetry enables continuous exposure monitoring and may support radiation-protective behaviors during high-dose interventional procedures.

articles.title: Hepatitis C, Hearing Loss, and Healthcare Utilization Patterns, a Cross-Sectional Analysis of NHANES Data: 1999-2012.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Hearing loss is a chronic condition in the U.S. with diverse causes, including viral infections, and significantly affects quality of life. Despite the rising incidence of Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, research on its relationship with hearing loss remains limited. Early and consistent interactions with the healthcare system have been shown to improve outcomes in extrahepatic manifestations of HCV and enhance quality of life.

DESIGN: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of HCV history, identified via HCV antibody and RNA testing obtained by the mobile examination center, and hearing loss, measured by pure-tone audiometry, using National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data (1999-2004, 2011-2012) for adults aged 20 to 69. We utilized multivariable logistic regression models to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals, adjusting for important covariates. Results were stratified by degree of healthcare utilization.

RESULTS: Among 6705 participants, hearing loss prevalence was 27.7% in those with HCV versus 12.7% in those without. The adjusted OR for hearing loss in individuals with HCV was 1.81 (95% confidence interval: 1.06, 3.10). Notably, the magnitude of association between HCV history and hearing loss was higher in the low healthcare utilization group than in the high healthcare utilization group (aOR: 2.82 versus 0.72).

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest an association between HCV and hearing loss, with healthcare utilization modifying this relationship. This study fills a gap in the literature and highlights the need for increased clinical monitoring of hearing health in individuals who have had an HCV infection.

articles.title: Wearable electrophysiology monitoring enabled by stretchable porous composite conductors.
articles.abstract: We report a porous AgNWs/PEDOT:PSS composite electrode with uniform conductive networks and cold-welded junctions, fabricated by template-assisted assembly. The porous architecture effectively dissipates stress and accommodates strain, yielding excellent performance at 50% strain and stable performance over 5000 stretching cycles. The electrode enables reliable ECG, EOG, and EMG monitoring.

articles.title: Aflatoxin B1 exposure through peanuts worldwide: national level occurrence and exposure assessment.
articles.journal: Critical reviews in food science and nutrition
articles.abstract: Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is a mycotoxin, or fungal toxin, that contaminates maize, peanuts, and tree nuts grown in warm regions of the world. It causes liver cancer and is synergistic with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection to multiplicatively increase cancer risk. Peanuts (also called groundnuts) are a major source of aflatoxin exposure in many populations worldwide. We conducted a systematic data review to examine the occurrence of AFB1 in peanut food products in 106 nations. We then conducted a dietary exposure assessment based on this occurrence dataset and consumption of peanuts in these nations, to compare trends across the time periods from 1990 to 2024. 22 nations experienced a substantial increase in aflatoxin exposure through peanut consumption, and 22 nations experienced a substantial decrease. Changes in exposure are largely driven by changes in intake levels. Many sub-Saharan African populations have alarmingly high levels of aflatoxin exposure, due to high contamination coupled with high consumption. Detection methods are shown to demonstrate recent improvements in sensitivity. These findings are important given the health risks of high aflatoxin exposure; most notably liver cancer.

articles.title: Almost Half of Very Preterm Infants Were Breastfed at Term Age When Discharged From Home-Based Neonatal Care Following Intensive Care.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To describe breastfeeding practices and outcomes, after discharge and enrolment in neonatal home care, among preterm infants with a gestational age (GA) of less than 32 weeks.

METHOD: A cross-sectional single-centre cohort study of all preterm infants enrolled in neonatal home care in 2020-2024. De-identified data obtained from medical records were analysed using descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: During the 5-year period, a total of 154 preterm infants (median GA 29 + 5 weeks; birth weight 1318 g) were discharged and included in the analyses. The infants were discharged and enrolled in neonatal home care at a median postmenstrual age of 34 + 6 weeks, when a majority (82%) had initiated breastfeeding, and a feeding tube was still in place (81%). Neonatal home care was concluded until a median postmenstrual age of 39 + 1 weeks, at which point 41% were exclusively breastfed, 26% partially breastfed, and 33% exclusively fed by bottle.

CONCLUSION: In this cohort of very preterm infants, the transition from nasogastric feeding tube to oral feeds was feasible during neonatal home care after hospital discharge and resulted in almost half of the infants being exclusively breastfed at term.

articles.title: Glomerular microangiopathy can be associated with nephrotic proteinuria due to both segmental effacement of foot processes and damage to the glomerular endothelial barrier.
articles.abstract: Glomerular microangiopathy (GMA)-caused by etiologies including VEGF inhibition, thrombotic microangiopathy, or malignant hypertension-is frequently linked to nephrotic-range proteinuria. However, the mechanisms of severe proteinuria following glomerular filtration barrier injury remain unclear. We examined how podocyte and glomerular endothelial injury relate to significant proteinuria in GMA. Thirty-seven kidney biopsies were studied, including 10 negative controls (Group 1), 11 GMA cases associated with VEGF inhibition (Group 2), and 16 GMA cases caused by other etiologies (Group 3). Electron microscopy was used to quantify foot process effacement and assess glomerular endothelial injury. To further evaluate endothelial barrier dysfunction, Oil Red O (ORO) staining for lipoprotein deposition and colloidal iron staining for negatively charged proteoglycans were performed. Correlations between ultrastructural changes and proteinuria were analyzed statistically. Nephrotic-range proteinuria was observed in 82% (9/11) of Group 2 and 56% (9/16) of Group 3 cases. In both groups, the severity of proteinuria was significantly associated with the extent of foot process effacement, endothelial edema and detachment, and GBM double-contour formation. ORO staining demonstrated subendothelial lipoprotein accumulation along the GBM in GMA cases but not in controls, consistent with increased glomerular endothelial permeability. In addition, colloidal iron staining was markedly reduced along the GBM in GMA, indicating impaired charge-selective properties of the glomerular filtration barrier. Significant proteinuria in GMA is associated with concurrent podocyte and glomerular endothelial cell injury. Ultrastructural findings, subendothelial lipoprotein accumulation, and reduced GBM proteoglycan staining indicate that endothelial barrier dysfunction, alongside podocyte injury, contributes critically to nephrotic-range proteinuria in GMA.

articles.title: Clinical Utility of Trichomonas vaginalis Reported on Cervical Cytology.
articles.journal: Journal of lower genital tract disease
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Trichomonas vaginalis (T. vaginalis) is the most common nonviral sexually transmitted infection worldwide. Although T. vaginalis may be identified incidentally on cervical cytology, cytology is not considered diagnostic due to historically reported low sensitivity. We evaluated the positive predictive value (PPV) of liquid-based cervical cytology for detecting T. vaginalis and examined subsequent clinical management.

METHODS: All liquid-based cervical cytology specimens reported as positive for T. vaginalis (October 1, 2024, to June 30, 2025) were identified from a large academic hospital laboratory in Southeast Michigan. Residual specimens underwent T. vaginalis-specific nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) to determine PPV. A retrospective review assessed confirmatory testing and treatment within 2 months of the cytology result.

RESULTS: A total of 200 cytology specimens positive for T. vaginalis were included. The mean patient age was 39 years; 81.4% were black or African American. All 200 specimens were confirmed positive by NAAT, yielding a PPV of 100% (95% CI, 98.2%-100%). Follow-up analysis included 132 patients with care documented in the electronic medical record. Of these, 70 had received treatment before cytology results were available and were excluded. Among the remaining 62 patients, only 3 (4.8%) underwent confirmatory testing and 33 (53.2%) received treatment within 2 months.

CONCLUSIONS: Among cytology-positive specimens that underwent confirmatory NAAT, liquid-based cervical cytology had an observed PPV of 100% for T. vaginalis. Despite this high concordance, confirmatory testing was rare and nearly half of patients received no treatment, highlighting missed opportunities for timely management. Increased visibility of T. vaginalis findings within cytology reports may improve treatment and follow-up.

articles.title: National Early Warning Score 2-Guided Sepsis Hour-1 Bundle Care for Adults With Suspected Sepsis in the Emergency Department: A Hybrid Type 1 Effectiveness-Implementation Stepped-Wedge Randomized Controlled Trial Pilot Study (NEWS-1 TRIPS).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To increase the uptake of the Surviving Sepsis Campaign Hour-1 Bundle, we implemented a novel sepsis care model (National Early Warning Score [NEWS]-1 care), in which the Hour-1 Bundle is objectively triggered by a high NEWS-2 (≥ 5). We aimed to determine the feasibility of a full-scale type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation trial of this model.

DESIGN: A pilot type 1 hybrid trial, comprising a stepped-wedge cluster randomized controlled trial and mixed-methods implementation evaluation with staff focus group interviews and an anonymous survey guided by the Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance framework.

SETTING: Four emergency departments in Hong Kong.

PATIENTS: Adult patients of 18 years or older with a clinical diagnosis of infection requiring hospitalization and a NEWS-2 greater than or equal to 5.

INTERVENTIONS: Implementation of the Hour-1 Bundle when NEWS-2 was greater than or equal to 5.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The primary outcome was the feasibility of a full-scale hybrid trial, evaluated based on 14 progression criteria. Preliminary clinical effectiveness and safety were assessed, alongside implementation barriers and facilitators. During the implementation phase, compliance with lactate, blood culture, and antibiotics increased significantly. All progression criteria were met, except for suboptimal overall bundle compliance (56.1%). Exploratory intention-to-treat analysis (standard care group, n = 102; NEWS-1 group, n = 98) showed no significant between-group difference in 30-day all-cause mortality (standard care group, 3.9%; NEWS-1 group, 9.2%; absolute risk difference, 5.3%; 95% CI -1.6% to 12.1%); in-hospital, 90-day all-cause, or sepsis-related mortality; need for mechanical ventilation, renal replacement therapy, intensive care, or surgery; or ventilator-free days and adverse events. Implementation evaluation identified 15 barriers and 13 facilitators.

CONCLUSIONS: The effectiveness of NEWS-1 care remained uncertain, though adverse events were rare. A full-scale hybrid stepped-wedge trial is feasible but requires a much larger sample size. Real-world implementation barriers and facilitators should be considered in sepsis management guidelines.

articles.title: Global Prevalence of Obstetric Causes of Critical Illness in Pregnancy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the prevalence, risks, and outcomes of obstetric causes of critically ill pregnant women admitted to the ICU.

DATA SOURCES: We searched the PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Ovid, and ScienceDirect databases up to May 15, 2026.

STUDY SELECTION: We included studies reporting primary data on critically ill pregnant and postpartum women (up to 48 d post-delivery) admitted to an ICU, with relevant obstetric risk factors and maternal outcomes.

DATA EXTRACTION: Two reviewers independently performed data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment using the adapted Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. The pooled prevalence was estimated using a random-effects model with 95% CIs.

DATA SYNTHESIS: Of the 3,735 total records, 50 studies met the eligibility criteria, encompassing 7,756,232 women receiving obstetric care in tertiary hospitals across 20 countries, with 49,299 ICU admissions. Globally, 1.0% (95% CI, 0.8-1.3%) of pregnant and postpartum women experience critical illness and require admission to an ICU. The frequency varies according to the country's income levels, with the highest in low-income countries (4.1%) and the lowest in high-income countries (0.5%). Notably, 72.3% of ICU admissions were attributed to known obstetric causes, primarily obstetric hemorrhage (23.3%) and hypertension in pregnancy (26.9%). Nearly 33.3% of ICU patients required either respiratory or transfusion support, and the maternal mortality rate among ICU-admitted obstetric women was 8.5%.

CONCLUSIONS: Nearly one in 100 pregnancies require admission to intensive care due to critical illness, and nearly three-quarters of these admissions were due to direct obstetric causes, with high maternal morbidity and mortality. Obstetric hemorrhage and hypertensive disorders account for the majority of ICU admissions. Strengthening obstetric care in resource-limited settings through the expansion and optimization of intensive care services is essential for improving maternal and neonatal outcomes and reducing preventable morbidity and mortality.

articles.title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation in Critically Ill Patients: A Systematic Review of In-Hospital and Post-Discharge Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This systematic review and meta-analysis determines the incidence of new-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF) in critically ill patients, risks of post-discharge systemic thromboembolism, anticoagulation therapy, and the proportion diagnosed with AF post-discharge.

DATA SOURCES: A search of registered databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and CINAHL) was performed from inception to April 20, 2026.

STUDY SELECTION: Eligible studies included critically ill patients (≥ 18 yr old) who developed NOAF during admission to general ICUs or high-dependency units. NOAF was defined as AF in patients without prior history of AF.

DATA EXTRACTION: Data were independently extracted from full-text versions of included studies by nonblinded reviewers.

DATA SYNTHESIS: A Bayesian meta-analysis was conducted on 54 studies (367,896 patients) with a random-effects model using R (Version 4.3.3). Pooled incidence of NOAF in critically ill patients was 10.6% (95% credible interval [CrI], 8.6-12.9%). Absolute risk of post-discharge systemic thromboembolism was 7.1% (95% CrI, 4.5-11.0%), changing to 6.9% (95% CrI, 4.2-11.6%) after age and sex adjustment. Evidence from six studies reports that critically ill patients with NOAF had 1.94 times (95% CrI, 1.23-3.29) higher relative risk of systemic thromboembolism post-discharge than patients without NOAF, rising to 2.01 (95% CrI, 1.54-2.80) with adjustment. Absolute and relative risk are evaluated with follow-up durations ranging from 1.5 months to 5 years, with variable anticoagulation exposure. Anticoagulation rates were low: 32.9% in-hospital (95% CrI, 14.6-57.9%) and 35.9% post-discharge (95% CrI, 19.7-55.9%). On follow-up, 23.9% (95% CrI, 13.9-38.5%) of critically ill patients with NOAF were subsequently diagnosed with AF.

CONCLUSIONS: Our review suggests that NOAF during critical illness is associated with significantly increased risk of post-discharge systemic thromboembolism and subsequent AF diagnosis. However, rates of anticoagulation initiation remain low, highlighting the need for improved risk stratification and targeted strategies post-discharge.

articles.title: Structured Patient and Family-Centered Rounding in the ICU is Associated With Increased Family Confidence in Staff Compassion and Perceived Quality of Information Shared.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Determine whether inviting families to participate in structured, multidisciplinary rounding in the ICU can lead to improved quality of information shared and greater overall confidence in the care delivered to patients.

DESIGN: Pre- and postimplementation observational study based on surveys provided by the Society of Critical Care Medicine-Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute initiative.

SETTING: Academic teaching hospital with 21 medical (closed unit) and 25 surgical (open unit) ICU beds.

SUBJECTS: Family members and care providers of critically ill adults of 18 years and older.

INTERVENTIONS: Families and clinicians were surveyed before and after implementation of a quality initiative to promote greater patient and family-centeredness in daily ICU rounds, using a structured and scripted rounding template. Additional information was gathered regarding provider attitudes toward the incorporation of families in rounds.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: In pre-and postintervention periods, 36 and 28 families were surveyed in the MICU, and 44 and 42 families were surveyed in the SICU, respectively. In pre-and postintervention periods, respectively, 53 and 48 clinicians were surveyed in the MICU, and 46 and 28 clinicians were surveyed in the SICU. Clinician perceptions improved favorably in the MICU, with statistically significant improvements falling under the category of family welcoming, presence, and participation in decision-making; less so in the SICU. Family perceptions improved in almost all parameters in the MICU, with statistical significance achieved in perceived interest in patient needs, control of agitation and pain, and consistency and honesty of information shared. Similar patterns were observed in the SICU but did not reach statistical significance.

CONCLUSIONS: Structured, multi-disciplinary rounding with regular inclusion of family members and bedside nurses was associated with significantly greater family confidence in the quality and honesty of information shared, and an increase in perceived compassion in the care provided by ICU staff. Clinician perceptions regarding family inclusion on rounds were generally positive.

articles.title: The Impact of Hospital Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Volume and Its Distribution Across ICUs on Adult Patients' Outcomes: An Analysis of the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization Registry.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Research from a prior era of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) found that higher hospital ECMO volume was associated with higher survival rates, but it did not examine whether distributing ECMO volume across multiple ICUs affected this relationship.

DESIGN: Retrospective analysis of the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization (ELSO) registry.

SETTING: ECMO centers contributing to the registry.

PATIENTS: Adult patients required ECMO support from 2012 to 2023.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: We analyzed adult patients from the ELSO registry (2012-2023), adjusting for hospital factors and case mix using multivariable hierarchical logistic regression. The main outcome was in-hospital mortality. Hospital experience was measured by the annual number of adult ECMO cases and total ECMO hours. Volume-outcome associations were modeled for all centers and by total adult ICUs per center. We included 115,849 adults on ECMO across 495 hospitals. Model estimates showed small decreases in mortality odds with higher annual case counts (odds ratio [OR], 0.98; 95% CI, 0.97-0.99 per 10-case increase) and ECMO hours (OR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.99-1.00 per 1000 hr increase). Hospitals with one ICU had a median of 10 cases (interquartile interval [IQI], 3-25 cases), while those with four or more ICUs had a median of 50 (IQI, 28-91). Adjusted mortality was higher in centers delivering ECMO across four+ ICUs compared with one ICU (OR, 1.18; 95% CI, 1.06-1.31), the annual case model (OR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.06-1.26), and the annual ECMO hours model. Higher volume was associated with a reduction in the odds of mortality for hospitals with four+ ICUs compared with those with one ICU (OR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.96-1.00 per 10 cases and OR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.99-1.00 per 1000 hr).

CONCLUSIONS: Higher hospital ECMO volume is associated with reduced mortality. Hospitals with more adult ICUs that perform ECMO may experience higher mortality, which may be explained by increased patient complexity and is offset by the higher center volume. More research is needed to better understand the optimum design of ECMO centers.

articles.title: A Telemedicine Intervention for Spontaneous Awakening and Breathing Trials in Small and Large ICUs.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effect of a tele-critical care (TCC) daily audit-and-feedback intervention on spontaneous awakening trial and spontaneous breathing trial protocol compliance.

DESIGN: Pre-post quality improvement study.

SETTING: Single health system composed of 14 hospitals in the Midwestern United States.

PATIENTS: A total of 8909 patients of 18 years or older receiving mechanical ventilation via endotracheal tube for more than 1 calendar day between October 01, 2022 and September 20, 2024.

INTERVENTIONS: Daily in the early afternoon, TCC nurses reviewed mechanically ventilated patients to determine whether a spontaneous awakening trial and spontaneous breathing trial had occurred. They contacted the bedside nurse if no trial had occurred and no weaning exclusion criteria were noted during a manual chart review.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The coprimary outcomes were the proportion of ventilator days during each ventilator episode with documentation of spontaneous awakening trials and spontaneous breathing trials. Linear mixed effects models were used to examine the effect of the intervention on each outcome stratified by ICU size (large ≥ 15 beds or small < 15 beds). Spontaneous awakening trial documentation improved over time throughout the entire period, but the rate of improvement increased significantly after the telemedicine intervention (preintervention slope: 0.2% increase per 30 d; 95% CI, -0.2% to 0.6% and postintervention slope: 1.4% increase per 30 d; 95% CI, 1.0% to 1.9%; p < 0.001 for intervention-time interaction). The telemedicine intervention was associated with a step increase in spontaneous breathing trial documentation in small ICUs (absolute increase, 12.8%; 95% CI, 8.7-16.9%) but not in large ICUs (absolute increase, -0.1%; 95% CI, -1.8% to 1.6%; p = 0.02 for intervention-ICU size interaction).

CONCLUSIONS: The telemedicine intervention was associated with increased spontaneous awakening trials and spontaneous breathing trials selectively in small ICUs. Telemedicine may have promoted practice standardization in small ICUs where exposure to ventilated patients was infrequent. Local ICU characteristics may impact the effectiveness of TCC interventions.

articles.title: A randomized study on migration of the Spectron EF and the Charnley flanged 40 cemented femoral stems: secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial using radiostereometric analysis (RSA) with 10 years' follow-up.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Our primary aim was to compare the 10-year migration of the proximally roughened Spectron EF stem with the Charnley flanged 40 stems in cemented THA. Secondary aims were to assess the influence of polyethylene type on Spectron EF migration, and clinical outcomes.

METHODS: In this randomized trial (NCT00698672), 150 patients (70% women; mean age 70 years) underwent cemented THA with either a Charnley stem (n = 30) or a Spectron EF stem (n = 120, 4 groups with different articulating surfaces). The articulations utilized conventional polyethylene (CPE) or highly crosslinked polyethylene (XLPE) cup liners combined with either cobalt-chromium (CoCr) or Oxinium (OxZr) femoral heads. RSA was performed postoperatively and up to 10 years. Migration was analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Clinical outcome was assessed with the Harris Hip Score (HHS).

RESULTS: After 10 years, 48 patients (14 Charnley, 34 Spectron EF) had evaluable RSA data. Both stems showed posterior translation, subsidence, and retroversion. Retroversion was greater for the Charnley stem than the Spectron EF stem at 3.2° (95% confidence interval [CI] 2.7-3.8) and 1.5° (CI 1.2-1.8), respectively, with a mean difference of 1.7° (CI 1.1- 2.4). The Spectron EF stem had more subsidence at 0.72 mm (CI 0.56-0.88) vs 0.32 mm (CI 0.06-0.57) for the Charnley stem, with a difference of 0.41 mm (CI 0.11-0.71). Spectron EF stems articulating with XLPE had 0.44 mm (CI 0.12-0.76) more subsidence than stems articulating with CPE. HHS improved from 41 (SD 15) to 86 (SD 19) for the Charnley stem and 45 (SD 13) to 86 (SD 15) for the Spectron EF stem with no statistically significant difference between the groups.

CONCLUSION: After 10 years, the Spectron EF stem showed less retroversion, but more subsidence than the Charnley stem, with otherwise similar migration and clinical outcomes. XLPE articulating stems had more subsidence than CPE with the Spectron EF stem.

articles.title: Hepatoduodenal fistula secondary to hepatic hematoma after percutaneous liver biopsy: successful conservative management.
articles.abstract: A 60-year-old woman undergoing evaluation for autoimmune liver disease underwent ultrasound-guided percutaneous liver biopsy. The procedure was complicated by a large hepatic hematoma with active bleeding demonstrated on contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT). Urgent angiography was performed, followed by selective arterial embolization using microcoils, achieving effective hemostasis. Follow-up CT prior to discharge revealed a 9×12cm intraparenchymal hematoma involving segments V-VIII, associated with a 6×2cm extrahepatic component. A routine outpatient CT performed 45 days after embolization demonstrated a reduction in hematoma size, with the presence of intrahepatic gas and imaging findings suggestive of fistulization between the hepatic hematoma and the gastric antrum. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy confirmed the diagnosis of hepatogastric fistula. Despite this finding, the patient remained asymptomatic and clinically stable, with no evidence of infection or gastrointestinal bleeding. After multidisciplinary discussion, and given the absence of clinical repercussion, an individualized conservative approach with high-dose proton pump inhibitors was initiated. Serial radiological follow-up showed progressive reduction of the hematoma and complete resolution of the fistulous tract, confirming the success of non-surgical management. Hepatogastric fistula is an exceptionally rare complication, typically associated with hepatic abscesses or malignancy. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case secondary to hepatic hematoma, successfully managed through an individualized, multidisciplinary, non-surgical strategy.

articles.title: Real world data to improve hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance in cirrhosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Surveillance for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains suboptimal due to poor adherence and limited diagnostic accuracy. We aimed to develop and validate a simple risk score to predict HCC in patients with cirrhosis.

METHODS: A total of 667 patients with cirrhosis were followed for up to 60 months or until HCC development, liver transplantation, or death. A prognostic model was derived using multivariable Cox regression. Discrimination was assessed by Harrell's C-index and time-dependent area under the curve (tAUC), calibration by calibration slope and Brier score, and clinical utility by decision curve analysis. Competing-risk analyses accounted for liver transplantation and death. External validation was performed in 18,856 patients with cirrhosis from the Andalusian Population Health Database.

RESULTS: The A3BS score (age, sex, AST, albumin, and bilirubin) demonstrated good discrimination, with C-index values ranging from 0.73 to 0.76 at 12, 24, 36, and 60 months. Patients in the high-risk group had a substantially higher 60-month cumulative incidence of HCC than those in the low-risk group (32% vs. 9%) and a fourfold increased risk of HCC (sHR 4.0, 95% CI 2.2-7.5; p<0.001). Importantly, patients classified as low risk had a very low probability of developing HCC, with a negative predictive value of 96.5%. Calibration analyses demonstrated good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes and low prediction error, while decision curve analysis confirmed clinical benefit across relevant risk thresholds. External validation confirmed consistent performance (tAUC 0.66 at 36 and 60 months). Predictive performance was particularly favorable in women and individuals younger than 60 years.

CONCLUSIONS: A3BS is a simple five-variable score that provides reliable HCC risk stratification across cirrhosis etiologies and identifies a large subgroup of patients at very low risk of HCC, supporting personalized surveillance strategies and more efficient allocation of healthcare resources.

articles.title: Mechanistic Insights into the Fluorescence Behavior of 2-(2-(1,3-Dioxoisoindolin-2-yl)phenyl)benzothiazole (PHBT) and Its Hydrazine-Induced Products: A DFT/TD-DFT Study.
articles.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. A
articles.abstract: In this study, the fluorescence quenching mechanism of the hydrazine probe 2-(2-(1,3-dioxoisoindolin-2-yl)phenyl)benzothiazole (PHBT) and the distinct luminescence behaviors of its reaction products 2-[2-(2-hydrazinocarbonylbenzamido)-5-methylphenyl]benzothiazole (CHBT), 2-(2-amino-5-methylphenyl)benzothiazole (AMBT), and the AMBT-based derivative 2-(2-acetamido-5-methylphenyl)benzothiazole (ACBT), were systematically investigated via density functional theory/time-dependent DFT (DFT/TD-DFT) calculations. The results indicate that the fluorescence quenching of PHBT arises from a synergistic donor-type photoinduced electron transfer (d-PET) and twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT) mechanism. Upon photoexcitation, the system initially populates a bright LE state (S3), followed by a d-PET process that transfers an electron from the donor to the acceptor, leading to a dark CT state (S1). This CT state subsequently undergoes TICT, ultimately resulting in fluorescence quenching via nonradiative decay. For CHBT, AMBT, and ACBT, excited-state hydrogen bond strengthening was verified through IR and reduced density gradient (RDG) analysis, with the order CHBT > ACBT > AMBT. Potential energy curve scans demonstrate that CHBT and ACBT can undergo ESIPT with low energy barriers (4.20 and 5.54 kcal/mol, respectively), yielding tautomer-form emission. In contrast, AMBT exhibits a higher barrier (8.93 kcal/mol) and remains in the normal form, resulting in normal form-based fluorescence. FMOs and hole-electron analysis further confirm that all three compounds exhibit LE states, and the charge transfer degree (D index) follows CHBT < ACBT < AMBT, which is negatively correlated with the hydrogen bond strengthening trend. This work provides deep insights into the fluorescence switching mechanism and elucidates the electronic and protonic processes governing the luminescence of hydrazine-derived probes.

articles.title: Baseline SGLT2 inhibitor use and documented ascites after a first ascites hospitalization: a retrospective two-center cohort study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) may benefit fluid retention in cirrhosis, but evidence in decompensated patients remains limited. We evaluated the association between SGLT2i and documented ascites during follow-up in patients with cirrhosis and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) after a first episode of ascites.

METHODS: A two-center retrospective cohort study of patients with cirrhosis and T2DM hospitalized for a first episode of ascites between 2017 and 2025 in Spain. Patients were classified according to SGLT2i use before admission. The primary endpoint was the presence of documented ascites at scheduled follow-up assessments after discharge. Secondary outcomes included relevant clinical and biochemical outcomes.

RESULTS: Among 103 patients, 27 (26.2%) received SGLT2i and 76 (73.8%) did not. Median follow-up was 52 weeks [26-104]. SGLT2i users had a lower proportion of documented ascites (13/26 vs 53/66; 50% vs 80.3%; p=0.004). This association persisted after adjustment for potential confounders (aOR 0.23, 95% CI 0.08-0.66; p=0.006), with consistent results in a 6-month sensitivity analysis. No significant differences were observed in hospitalizations for ascites, for overall liver decompensation, LVPs, RA, hepatic encephalopathy, acute kidney injury or survival. Serum creatinine and sodium did not show differences between groups. 5/27 (18.5%) patients discontinued treatment.

CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2i use was associated with a lower proportion of documented ascites after a first episode. Prospective studies are needed to establish their efficacy and safety in decompensated cirrhosis.

articles.title: Cognitive impairment in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease ‒ Clinical evidence, liver-brain mechanisms and research priorities.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most prevalent chronic liver disease worldwide and is increasingly recognized as a multisystem disorder with important extrahepatic manifestations. Among these, cognitive impairment and reduced health-related quality of life (HRQoL) have emerged as clinically relevant but under-recognized findings, although the extent to which cognitive impairment is independently associated with MASLD remains uncertain. This narrative review summarizes current evidence regarding cognitive impairment and HRQoL in MASLD, addressing clinical findings, potential underlying mechanisms, and therapeutic implications. Reported estimates of cognitive impairment vary substantially according to population characteristics, disease stage, and neuropsychological instruments, and should not be interpreted as a general population prevalence. Current evidence is predominantly observational, with some studies showing associations that persist after adjustment for cardiometabolic factors and others finding no independent association. Proposed mechanisms include systemic and neuroinflammation, insulin resistance, oxidative stress, and alterations in the gut-liver-brain axis, although direct human evidence remains limited for several pathways. Lifestyle and metabolic interventions may influence cognitive outcomes, but direct MASLD-specific evidence is limited. Future research should prioritize standardized cognitive assessment, longitudinal validation studies, careful control of confounding, integration of patient-reported outcomes, and prespecified cognitive endpoints in MASLD clinical trials.

articles.title: Host-mediated SUMOylation of pE248R promotes African swine fever virus replication and virulence.
articles.abstract: SUMOylation, the covalent conjugation of small ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO) proteins to lysine residues in target substrates, is an essential post-translational modification in eukaryotes. Recently, microbial manipulation of SUMOylation has emerged as an important virulence strategy for viruses. Here, we demonstrate that African swine fever virus CN/GS/2018 (ASFV CN/GS/2018) pE248R can be conjugated to SUMO1 and provide evidence that prevention of pE248R SUMOylation can block ASFV CN/GS/2018 infection. The E3 SUMO ligase PIAS4 interacts with pE248R via its SUMO interaction motifs (SIMs) and promotes pE248R SUMOylation at its lysine residues at positions 103 and 240. Additionally, PIAS4 can increase the stability of pE248R. Importantly, studies on ASFV CN/GS/2018 pE248R with mutations have shown that the SUMOylation sites, the SIMs, or both are essential for the viral replication cycle in vitro and that mutations in these regions attenuate the virus in swine. Collectively, these findings indicate that ASFV CN/GS/2018 pE248R SUMOylation is critical for ASFV CN/GS/2018 pathogenesis and virulence, thereby providing a potential strategy for ASF vaccine development.IMPORTANCEAfrican swine fever virus (ASFV) poses a devastating threat to the global swine industry, yet effective vaccines and antiviral strategies remain unavailable. While microbial manipulation of host post-translational modifications is a common virulence strategy, how ASFV exploits the host SUMOylation machinery has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate that ASFV CN/GS/2018 pE248R undergoes SUMO1 conjugation mediated by the E3 SUMO ligase PIAS4 via specific SUMO-interacting motifs, which enhances pE248R stability and is essential for the viral replication cycle and virulence in swine. Blocking pE248R SUMOylation at lysine residues 103 and 240 inhibits viral infection, revealing that ASFV CN/GS/2018 hijacks the host SUMOylation system as a critical pathogenesis mechanism. These findings identify a druggable virus-host interaction node and provide a rational target for developing next-generation attenuated ASFV vaccines.

articles.title: Baseline immune transcriptional states predict future HIV-1 acquisition in individuals at risk of sexual infection.
articles.abstract: Natural resistance to HIV-1 acquisition in highly exposed seronegative (HESN) individuals suggests the existence of pre-existing host states associated with reduced susceptibility. However, the baseline molecular determinants of susceptibility remain poorly understood. We analyzed peripheral blood mononuclear cell transcriptomes by RNA sequencing in 104 HIV-1-seronegative men who have sex with men (MSM) at high risk of sexual exposure, including 65 HESN and 39 who subsequently seroconverted. Differential expression, functional enrichment, and spatial genomic clustering analyses were integrated with Elastic Net regularized logistic regression. HESN individuals showed enrichment of sensory receptor (p.adj = 2 × 10⁻¹⁶) and cell-adhesion pathways (p.adj = 9 × 10⁻³), together with non-random genomic clustering (p.adj = 1 × 10⁻⁴) of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) at immune-related loci, including TCR, IGH, KIR, and MHC/HLA regions. In contrast, future seroconverters exhibited increased mRNA metabolism (p.adj = 1.5 × 10⁻¹⁴), immune activation (p.adj = 0.01), and type I interferon signaling (p.adj = 0.02). A 14-gene risk score showed an out-of-fold area under the curve (AUC) of 0.888. Cross-cohort transportability was evaluated in an independent ectocervical RNA-seq data set. Applied without refitting, the signature showed moderate discrimination between long-term HESN and HIV-negative women at high risk of acquisition (AUC = 0.689). The out-of-fold molecular risk score was also associated with time to HIV-1 seroconversion in MSM (log-rank, P = 7.1 × 10⁻¹¹; score × time interaction, P = 0.0086). These findings identify distinct pre-infection transcriptional states associated with HIV-1 acquisition and support partially transportable transcriptional architecture across blood and genital mucosal compartments.IMPORTANCEModeling the baseline transcriptome enables prediction of future HIV-1 acquisition and identifies a transcriptional score associated with time to seroconversion. These findings raise new hypotheses about the biological and genetic mechanisms underlying the HESN phenotype.

articles.title: Infectious bronchitis virus exhibits pan-mucosal tropism and ascends via the cloacal hub to infect the urogenital system.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Infectious bronchitis virus (IBV), a prominent respiratory pathogen of chickens that incurs substantial economic losses to the global poultry industry, exhibits extensive genetic heterogeneity. Highly virulent strains manifest broad multi-organ tropism and elicit severe renal and oviductal lesions. Nevertheless, the precise tissue tropism profiles of different IBV genotypes, as well as their in vivo dissemination routes from respiratory mucosa to distal urogenital tissues, remain incompletely characterized. Here, we systematically elucidated the actual tissue tropism and systemic dissemination routes of IBV using in situ immunofluorescence assays, in vivo fluorescence tracking of a recombinant reporter virus, and an estrogen-induced physiological oviduct model. Our findings reveal that all tested IBV strains exclusively target mucosal epithelial cells. Classical Mass-type and emerging genotype VI strains are limited to respiratory tissues and cranial glands, while virulent QX-like isolates show pan-mucosal tropism across respiratory, lower intestinal, and urogenital tracts. Multi-route challenge and spatiotemporal antigen tracking exclude hematogenous viremia as the spread mechanism. Instead, QX-like IBV colonizes the gut and cloaca, a unique avian anatomical junction, then migrates retrogradely along continuous epithelia to the kidneys and oviducts. This work clarifies tissue tropism of major IBV genotypes and identifies a cloaca-dependent ascending mucosal pathway for urogenital infection of QX-like IBV. These results advance our mechanistic understanding of IBV pathogenesis and support the design of precise disease control and mucosal vaccine strategies.
