IMPORTANCE: Infectious bronchitis virus (IBV), a highly contagious avian gammacoronavirus, causes huge economic losses in global poultry farming. While primarily infecting respiratory mucosa, virulent strains trigger severe renal and reproductive damage. It has long puzzled researchers how respiratory-entry IBV reaches distant urogenital organs. This work delineates IBV's in vivo spread and rules out typical hematogenous dissemination. IBV possesses inherent pan-mucosal tropism restricted to surface epithelia. Virulent strains colonize the cloaca-the avian junction of digestive, urinary, and reproductive tracts-then ascend retrogradely along connected mucosa to kidneys and oviducts. Immature pullets are shielded by sealed oviduct outlets, while mature hens develop severe genital lesions. Resolving this historical dispute, our findings revise IBV pathogenic theories and highlight mucosal immunity as a key target for innovative vaccine design.

articles.title: A viral replication level-dependent continuum of transcriptional and microRNA reprogramming in HIV-1-infected microglia links productive infection to neurocognitive-associated gene networks.
articles.abstract: Microglia are major targets of HIV-1 in the brain. Despite effective antiviral therapy, infected microglia, including those containing a replication-defective provirus, can express viral products that contribute to neuroinflammation, yet how productive infection shapes the host response remains poorly defined. Using single-cell RNA-seq of HIV-1-infected C20 microglia, we stratified cells by HIV-1 splice junction-supporting reads into low- and high-infection groups, resolving a graded rather than binary host transcriptional response. The computational pipeline developed for this quantification is made publicly available. A core set of immune and cell cycle pathways was induced, regardless of infection level, but several programs reversed direction with increasing viral burden: interferon-α/γ and EMT/hypoxia signatures peaked at low infection, while high infection featured suppression of these signatures alongside induction of mTORC1/MYC signaling, ribosome biogenesis, RNA processing, and mitotic activity, with progressive loss of cytoskeletal, motility, and developmental programs. This pattern, except for cell cycle/mitotic signatures, was reproduced in iPSC-derived microglia, supporting its generalizability beyond an immortalized cell line. To identify potential regulatory mechanisms underlying these transcriptional programs, we integrated differentially expressed miRNAs and genes from the low- and high-infection groups, filtered for the canonical inverse miRNA-target relationship, revealing miRNA/mRNA networks enriched for miRNAs previously implicated in HIV-1 replication (e.g., miR-33a-5p and miR-3065-3p) and in neurodegenerative and psychiatric disease (e.g., miR-107 and let-7c-5p). These findings define a productive infection-level continuum in microglial transcription and miRNA reprogramming and identify candidate miRNA-mediated mechanisms, complementary to the canonical Env/Nef/Tat pathway by which HIV-1-infected microglia may contribute to neuroinflammation and neurocognitive impairment in people with HIV-1.IMPORTANCEHIV-1 persists in the brain despite antiviral therapy in part because infected microglia continue to express viral RNA and proteins that promote neuroinflammation, contributing to the cognitive impairment seen in many people with HIV-1. How the level of active viral replication within a microglial cell shapes its response has been unclear since most infection models capture only an averaged, post-replication snapshot rather than the transition from low to advanced infection. By ranking microglia by HIV-1 splice junction-supporting reads, we show that the host transcriptional response is graded rather than binary, and that several pathways, including interferon and growth/proliferative signaling, reverse direction as viral load increases. We further identify a network of HIV-1-dysregulated miRNAs, several previously linked to viral replication or to neurodegenerative and neurocognitive disease, pointing to a mechanism by which infected microglia may influence neuronal health, complementary to the well-studied viral Env, Nef, and Tat proteins.

articles.title: Maternal-fetal health in arboviral diseases: clinical outcomes following prenatal dengue and chikungunya virus infections.
articles.abstract: SUMMARYArthropod-borne viruses (arboviruses) are an increasingly important cause of global infectious disease, yet their effects during pregnancy and early life remain incompletely understood. In the context of declining fertility and birth rates globally, infectious threats to successful pregnancy and neonatal health warrant greater attention. Dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), two of the most prevalent mosquito-borne viruses, are underrecognized contributors to maternal-fetal health. Although these infections rarely result in classical congenital syndromes, accumulating clinical, epidemiological, and experimental evidence indicates that prenatal exposure can impair placental function, drive maternal immune dysregulation, and influence fetal and neonatal immune development. This review summarizes current knowledge on the maternal, placental, and pediatric consequences of DENV and CHIKV infection during pregnancy. We outline the immunological features of the maternal-fetal interface and discuss how pregnancy-associated immune modulation shapes antiviral responses and placental homeostasis. We then review epidemiological and clinical evidence linking prenatal arboviral infection with adverse pregnancy outcomes, neonatal disease, and potential long-term neurodevelopmental effects. Mechanistic insights, including viral immune evasion, placental inflammation, and antibody-mediated immunopathology, are examined. Finally, we discuss clinical considerations for monitoring arboviral-exposed pregnancies and progenies, alongside emerging strategies to reduce maternal infection and improve neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Complications of Distal Femoral Replacement.
articles.journal: The Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons
articles.abstract: Historically, distal femoral arthroplasty was a procedure reserved for salvage oncologic procedures or revision arthroplasty with severe bone loss. More recently, there has been an increase in utilization of distal femoral arthroplasty for patients with native and periprosthetic distal femur fractures. With increased utilization comes an increased incidence of the wide array of complications associated with this procedure, such as prosthetic joint infection, aseptic loosening, patellar instability, extensor mechanism disruption, and periprosthetic fractures. We present the literature on these complications and current management recommendations.

articles.title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Safety of Ventricular Shunt Tap in Suspected Shunt Malfunction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Ventricular shunt tap is used in the evaluation of suspected shunt malfunction and infection, yet concerns regarding diagnostic reliability and infectious complications persist. We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy and safety of shunt tap for identifying proximal and distal shunt obstruction.

METHODS: A retrospective study was performed including all patients undergoing ventricular shunt tap at a single institution. Inclusion criteria were (1) documented procedure note evaluating both proximal and distal function and (2) minimum 30-day follow-up. Operative findings during shunt revision served as the reference standard when surgery was performed. Patients managed nonoperatively without deterioration or shunt revision within 30 days were classified as not having mechanical obstruction.

RESULTS: A total of 213 shunt taps across 94 patients met inclusion criteria. The median age was 30.2 years, and 50 patients (53.2%) were male. The median number of taps per patient was 1.5 (IQR 1-3; maximum 10). For proximal obstruction, shunt tap demonstrated 83.7% sensitivity and 98.8% specificity, with a positive predictive value of 94.7%, negative predictive value of 96.0%, positive likelihood ratio of 71.16, and negative likelihood ratio of 0.16. For distal obstruction, the sensitivity was 77.8% and specificity was 100%, with a positive predictive value of 100%, negative predictive value of 96.9%, positive likelihood ratio infinite, and negative likelihood ratio of 0.22. Opening pressure predicted proximal obstruction (area under the curve 0.839), with an optimal threshold ≤0.5 cmH2O yielding 87.0% sensitivity and 76.9% specificity. Distal runoff predicted distal obstruction (area under the curve 0.924), with an optimal threshold of ≤9.5 cmH2O yielding 100% sensitivity and 88.9% specificity. No shunt tap-related complications, shunt damage, or subsequent infections attributable to the procedure were identified.

CONCLUSION: Ventricular shunt tap is safe and highly informative in evaluating suspected shunt malfunction. Abnormal proximal or distal flow demonstrated excellent specificity, increasing the post-test probability of true mechanical obstruction, while normal flow substantially reduced the likelihood of obstruction. These findings support shunt tap to guide diagnostic and operative decision-making in patients with suspected shunt malfunction.

articles.title: Integrating Virtual Reality and Patient-Specific 3D Models for Staged Craniopagus Twins Separation: Evolution of a Surgical Planning Pipeline Across 3 Consecutive Cases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Craniopagus twins (CPT) represent one of the rarest forms of conjoined twinning, and their surgical separation demands meticulous preoperative planning. We describe the evolution of an integrated surgical planning pipeline combining patient-specific 3-dimensional (3D) printed models, tissue-mimicking materials (TMM), and immersive virtual reality (VR) across 3 consecutive CPT cases at a single institution, and discuss the emerging role of artificial intelligence-driven segmentation as the next translational step.

METHODS: Three CPT cases were managed at the Ribeirão Preto Medical School (University of São Paulo, Brazil). Cases 1 and 2 were completed separations using an incremental prototyping pipeline: computed tomography/MRI-based segmentation, virtual modeling, fused deposition modeling 3D printing with polylactic acid, and silicone rubber or latex covering as TMM. Case 3 continued immersive VR visualization using a Meta Quest 3 headset, enabling the multidisciplinary team to rehearse surgical steps in a simulated operating room.

RESULTS: Thirteen patient-specific models were produced across the 3 cases over approximately 36 months. The pipeline matured progressively: Case 1 established the core workflow; case 2 refined TMM application and skin-surface calculations; cases 2 and 3 integrated VR-based immersive briefings. Separation was achieved in all 3 pairs; in case 3, however, both twins died intraoperatively from hemorrhage and cardiogenic shock with refractory circulatory collapse, despite anatomically accurate planning models. Team feedback indicated that VR enhanced spatial understanding of the shared vascular anatomy and improved preoperative coordination vs flat-screen visualization.

CONCLUSION: The progressive integration of VR into an established 3D printing pipeline represents a meaningful advance in CPT separation planning. Artificial intelligence-driven segmentation tools hold promise for automating the bottleneck step, potentially making this pipeline replicable across institutions with fewer specialized resources.

articles.title: Integration site patterns, clonal expansion, and co-infection effects in HIV reservoirs: a systematic review of studies in people on antiretroviral therapy.
articles.abstract: HIV integrated into specific loci of the host's genome plays a significant role in clonal expansion and the persistence of the HIV reservoir. Certain factors, such as the HIV subtype, co-infections, inflammatory, and immune activation signaling, have been found to influence the integration sites (ISs). This systematic review examines IS patterns, clonal expansion, and the effects of co-infection on HIV reservoirs. A comprehensive search was conducted across four databases. We identified 18 articles published between 2016 and 2025 that met our criteria. We described the methods used for the IS analysis studies, features of the ISs, and their impact on clonal expansion. We also described the effects of cytomegalovirus (CMV), Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB), and influenza virus on the ISs and clonal dynamics. Eleven (61.1%) of the studies were conducted in the USA. Subtypes were mainly HIV-1 B. Ligand-mediated polymerase chain reaction or its variants were the most reported methods. Most HIV integration events occurred within genic regions, with reported proportions ranging from 77.0% to 100.0% of all sites. Most of the ISs were within introns, were in opposite orientation, occurred in cancer-associated genes, and influenced clonal expansion. CMV, MTB, and influenza did not significantly affect IS features but were associated with increased clonality. Expanded HIV-infected cell clones are integrated into genes regulating proliferation and immune signaling. Viral and immune co-factors may influence clonal persistence through other mechanisms. Understanding these will be critical for reservoir-targeted cure strategies.

articles.title: An adaptive multi-scale dilated convolutional neural network for arrhythmia detection.
articles.journal: Computer methods in biomechanics and biomedical engineering
articles.abstract: The rising global incidence of arrhythmia calls for reliable detection methods. Most existing approaches suffer from poor generalization and insufficient feature extraction for long-term electrocardiogram (ECG) signals. This work proposes an adaptive multi-scale dilated convolutional network (AMSDNet). It uses multi-scale dilated convolutions, gated adaptive weight allocation, and spatial attention fusion to capture global ECG features. Validated on Massachusetts Institute of Technology-Beth Israel Hospital Arrhythmia Database (MIT-BIH), the China Physiological Signal Challenge (CPSC) 2018, and the Computing in Cardiology Challenge (CINC) 2017 datasets, our method outperforms state-of-the-art models with average accuracy of 99.7%, 91.8% and 83.7%, respectively.

articles.title: Real-world effects of beremagene geperpavec in epidermolysis bullosa.
articles.journal: Journal of the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology : JEADV
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (DEB) is a severe inherited skin fragility disorder caused by mutations in COL7A1, leading to wounds, inflammation and impaired quality of life. Beremagene geperpavec (B-VEC) is the first approved topical gene therapy delivering functional COL7A1 via a modified HSV-1 vector, enabling local collagen VII expression and improved wound healing.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the real-world, multidimensional long-term outcomes of B-VEC treatment in patients with DEB, including wound healing, systemic inflammation, (auto)-antibody profiles and patient-reported outcomes.

METHODS: In this multicentre observational study, 38 patients with DEB received B-VEC treatment between January 2024 and June 2026. The primary endpoint was the change in wound surface area from baseline during B-VEC treatment. Secondary endpoints included changes in systemic inflammatory and haematological parameters [C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), serum amyloid A (SAA), leucocytes and haemoglobin (Hb)], (auto-)antibody profiles [anti-C7, BP180, BP230 and herpes simplex virus (HSV)-1/2 IgG], body mass index (BMI) and patient-reported outcomes, including pain, pruritus, treatment satisfaction and wound dressing time.

RESULTS: B-VEC treatment was associated with a significant reduction in wound surface area across healing wounds. Patients having persistent wounds exhibited lower BMI and higher leucocyte counts and received systemic biologic therapies less frequently. Anti-BP180, BP230 and HSV-1/2 titres remained stable, while anti-C7 levels increased during treatment. IIF was negative in most patients and did not differ between groups. Systemic inflammation showed a mixed pattern, with reduced leucocyte counts and SAA levels, and slightly increased CRP and IL-6 under treatment. Hb and BMI increased during treatment. Most patients reported high treatment satisfaction and reduction in pain, pruritus and wound dressing time.

CONCLUSIONS: B-VEC therapy provides clinically meaningful improvements in wound healing, patient-reported outcomes and selected systemic parameters in DEB. Treatment response is influenced by host factors such as BMI, systemic inflammation and concomitant therapies. Baseline (auto)-antibody profiles do not appear to predict treatment efficacy. Overall, B-VEC represents a significant advancement in the multidimensional management of DEB in real-world clinical practice.

articles.title: Hyperglycemia promotes maladaptive Dectin-1 signaling and impairs skin antifungal host defense.
articles.abstract: People with chronic hyperglycemia are more susceptible to fungal skin infections, yet the mechanisms behind worse clinical outcomes remain unclear. Using both in vivo and in vitro models, we explored how hyperglycemia affects skin antifungal defenses. Hyperglycemic mice showed increased susceptibility to Candida albicans skin infections, with larger lesions and higher fungal loads at all time points tested. Histology revealed larger abscesses, more extensive myeloid cell infiltration, and poorer control of fungal invasion, all associated with increased chemoattractant production on day 1 post-infection. Glucose reduction with the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist liraglutide reduced lesion size and fungal burden in infected diabetic mice, linking metabolic control to the restoration of innate immune function. Phagocytes and keratinocytes exposed to high glucose exhibited inhibited fungal ingestion. RNA-seq analysis of C. albicans-infected dermal macrophages cultured under high-glucose conditions showed enrichment of genes related to the C-type lectin receptor pathway, including Clec7a (Dectin-1), and also revealed inhibition of downstream signaling pathways required for effective phagocytosis. Pharmacologic blockade or genetic deletion of Dectin-1 restored fungal uptake under high-glucose conditions and improved host defense in vivo. Dectin-1 signaling in hyperglycemia increased prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) production along with increased abundance of microsomal prostaglandin E synthase-1 (mPGES-1). Inhibition of PGE2 synthesis rescued deficient phagocytic function. These findings identify maladaptive innate immune sensing as a key mechanism underlying susceptibility to fungal infection in diabetes and reveal how metabolic stress converts antifungal recognition pathways into drivers of inflammatory dysfunction.

articles.title: Soy foods, isoflavone intake, and diabetic kidney disease: The Fukuoka Diabetes Registry.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/INTRODUCTION: Soy foods are traditional components of the Japanese diet; however, evidence of their association with diabetic kidney disease remains limited. This study examined the association of soy food and isoflavone intake with decreased eGFR and albuminuria in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Overall, 4,922 individuals with type 2 diabetes were enrolled in this cross-sectional analysis. Soy food and isoflavone intakes were assessed using a self-administered diet history questionnaire. Odds ratios for decreased cystatin C-based eGFR (eGFRcys <60 mL/min/1.73 m2) and albuminuria (urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥30 mg/g) were calculated using logistic regression.

RESULTS: Frequent consumption of natto, miso soup, and tofu was associated with lower prevalence of decreased eGFRcys. The multivariable-adjusted odds ratios for the highest vs. lowest frequency categories were 0.49 (95% CI: 0.37, 0.65), 0.63 (0.42, 0.95), and 0.52 (0.30, 0.88), respectively. More frequent natto consumption, but not miso soup or tofu consumption, was inversely associated with albuminuria. Higher isoflavone intake was associated with lower odds of both outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher soy food consumption was associated with a lower prevalence of decreased eGFR, whereas natto and isoflavone intake were also associated with a lower prevalence of albuminuria. Habitual soy intake may be clinically relevant to kidney health.

articles.title: Dynamics of within-host genomic relatedness and emergence of resistance in serial Mycobacterium avium complex isolates during treatment.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Mycobacterium avium complex infections require prolonged multidrug therapy and may develop antimicrobial resistance. We applied whole-genome sequencing (WGS) to assess within-patient genomic relatedness and resistance-associated mutations emerging during therapy. WGS was performed on cultured populations of 30 serial isolates (16 M. avium and 14 Mycobacterium intracellulare) from 13 patients with repeated recovery of the same species. Genomic relatedness was classified by species/subspecies, sequence type (ST), and fastBAPS (FB) clustering. Resistance-associated mutations were assessed in isolates showing susceptible-to-resistant conversion or an increase of at least two dilutions in the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC). Among 13 patients, 10 (76.9%) showed concordant genomic patterns, 2 (15.4%) showed discordant genomic patterns with genetically distinct cultured populations, and 1 (7.7%) showed both concordant and discordant relationships across intervals. Sixteen M. avium cultured populations belonged to four STs (ST112 and ST118, 75.0%) and four FB clusters. Fourteen M. intracellulare cultured populations belonged to four STs, predominantly ST1109 (71.4%). While most cultured populations of the same ST matched the same FB, M. avium ST112 and ST118 and M. intracellulare ST1109 each occurred in two FB clusters. Conversely, three STs (ST112, ST118, and ST1112) of M. avium belonged to the same FB. Among three cases with emergent clarithromycin resistance, rrl mutations (A2058C and A2059G) were identified in two. In one case, an embC-embA intergenic variant showed stepwise increases in variant allele frequency, accompanied by increasing ethambutol MICs. WGS provided two methods for analyzing within-patient genomic relatedness (ST assignment and FB clustering), which were mutually complementary and enabled longitudinal detection of resistance-associated mutations during treatment.

IMPORTANCE: Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary disease often requires prolonged multidrug therapy, during which serial culture-positive isolates may differ in within-patient genomic relatedness and antimicrobial resistance. Distinguishing closely related from genetically distinct isolates and identifying emerging resistance are clinically important but cannot be reliably achieved using conventional species identification or sequence typing alone. In this study, whole-genome sequencing (WGS) of serial M. avium complex isolates enabled high-resolution assessment of within-patient genomic relatedness. WGS also identified emerging resistance-associated mutations, including acquired rrl mutations associated with high-level clarithromycin resistance during macrolide-containing therapy and an embC-embA intergenic variant accompanying increasing ethambutol minimum inhibitory concentrations during ethambutol-containing treatment. These findings support the potential clinical utility of WGS for characterizing genomic relationships among recurrent M. avium complex isolates and detecting emergence of resistance-associated mutations during therapy.

articles.title: Prognostic Impact of Post-Contrast Acute Kidney Injury in Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease Undergoing Endovascular Aortic Repair.
articles.journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-contrast acute kidney injury (PC-AKI) has been regarded as a serious complication after contrast administration, particularly in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). However, the prognostic significance of PC-AKI following endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) remains controversial due to heterogeneity in previous study populations. This study evaluated the association between PC-AKI and longitudinal changes in postoperative renal function and mortality in a well-defined CKD cohort undergoing EVAR.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective study of patients with CKD undergoing elective, primary, and non-complex infrarenal EVAR. Patients were classified according to the presence or absence of PC-AKI. Longitudinal changes in serum creatinine after EVAR, dialysis initiation, all-cause mortality, and the association between contrast volume and PC-AKI were evaluated.

RESULTS: Among 479 EVAR procedures, 164 patients with CKD were included, of whom 17 (10.4%) developed PC-AKI. The linear mixed-effects model showed a significant group-by-time interaction (P < .001). Serum creatinine remained significantly higher in the PC-AKI group than in the non-PC-AKI group at all postoperative time points. However, in the PC-AKI group, model-adjusted mean serum creatinine decreased significantly from 1.75 mg/dL in the postoperative period to 1.46 mg/dL at 12 months with an estimated change of -0.29 mg/dL (95% CI, -0.50 to -0.09; P = .003). No significant differences were observed in dialysis initiation (5.9% vs 0.7%; P = .197) or all-cause mortality (29.4% vs 23.8%; P = .565). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed no significant difference in overall survival between the groups (log-rank P = .246). In the multivariable analysis, contrast volume was not independently associated with PC-AKI (odds ratio [OR], 1.00; 95% CI, 0.98-1.01; P = .845), whereas lower preoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate remained significantly associated with PC-AKI (OR, 1.06 per 1 mL/min/1.73 m2 decrease; 95% CI, 1.01-1.12; P = .018).

CONCLUSION: In this study, PC-AKI may not necessarily be associated with adverse subsequent renal or survival outcomes. In addition, underlying renal vulnerability may be more closely associated with the development of PC-AKI than contrast volume alone. While PC-AKI should not be disregarded, judicious contrast use to ensure appropriate assessment may be reasonable even in patients with CKD.Clinical ImpactPost-contrast acute kidney injury (PC-AKI) occurred in approximately 10% of patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) undergoing elective, primary, non-complex infrarenal endovascular aortic repair (EVAR). Although serum creatinine remained higher in patients with PC-AKI at all postoperative time points, it decreased significantly from the postoperative period to 12 months. No significant differences were observed in dialysis initiation or overall survival between the groups. In addition, contrast volume was not independently associated with PC-AKI, whereas lower preoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate was. These findings suggest that contrast use should not be excessively restricted solely because of concerns regarding PC-AKI, and that judicious contrast use to ensure appropriate assessment may be reasonable even in patients with CKD.

articles.title: Bridging Neurosurgery and Palliative Care: The Unique Role of the Dual-Certified Nurse Practitioner.
articles.journal: Journal of hospice and palliative nursing : JHPN : the official journal of the Hospice and Palliative Nurses Association
articles.abstract: Serious neurological illness and injury are often followed by an unpredictable trajectory of hospitalization and recovery beyond the initial period of stabilization. Patients can experience serious cognitive and functional deficits with looming uncertainty about recovery. Advances in neurosurgical and neurocritical care have increased opportunities for improved outcomes and mortality. Patients with stroke, traumatic brain and spinal cord injury, brain cancer, and progressive neurodegenerative disorders may survive with significant morbidity and ongoing care needs. Neuropalliative care provides a framework to address these concerns through communication, symptom management, and goals of care discussions to ensure alignment of treatment options with patient-centered goals. Despite increasing recognition of these palliative care principles, there is limited integration within neurosurgical practice. Thus, an acute care nurse practitioner (NP) in a neurosurgical subspecialty with additional board certification and expertise in hospice and palliative care plays an important role at the intersection of these disciplines. This article explores the contributions of the dual-certified NP in a neurosurgery subspecialty incorporating palliative care principles into a patient- and caregiver-centric approach for managing serious neurological illness and injury.

articles.title: Pathogen identification and resistance gene expression tests using ASTar remnant bacterial suspension in gram-negative contrived positive blood cultures.
articles.abstract: Rapid pathogen identification, resistance detection, and susceptibility profiling improve antimicrobial prescribing and associated outcomes, but fragmented workflows lead to inefficiencies and are costly. We evaluated a research-use-only (RUO) approach using ASTar remnant bacterial suspension from routine antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) for matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS) pathogen identification and lateral flow assay (LFA)-based detection of targeted resistance mechanisms. Gram-negative bacterial strains from reference and curated resistance collections (CDC1, ARLG2, and ATCC3) (n = 129) were contrived into blood culture bottles and processed in the ASTar System using the ASTar BC G- Kit (Q-linea AB, Sweden). Under RUO conditions, remnant bacterial suspensions were collected ~1-2 h after ASTar run initiation and analyzed using NG Test CTX-M Multi, NG Test CARBA-5, NG Test Acineto-5 RUO, and MALDI-TOF MS. Mean (±SD) remnant suspension volume was 2,722 μL (±300 µL). All samples yielded high-confidence MALDI-TOF MS scores (>2.0), with five initially scoring <2.0 and resolving on repeat testing. LFA results showed full agreement with reference isolates for blaCTX-M positive/negative (32/32) and with 60 or 61 target carbapenemase-positive/negative isolates. Testing of a subset of samples to mimic reflex workflows with ASTar phenotypic results did not affect LFA performance (n = 35; 23 Enterobacterales, 3 Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and 9 Acinetobacter baumannii). Cost savings can be realized versus commercial multiplex PCR. This integrated approach of ~6 h rapid phenotypic AST with same-run identification and resistance detection (1-2 h from instrument start) or reflex testing upon availability of ASTar results may support earlier susceptibility results and offer cost savings to current workflows.IMPORTANCERapid, integrated diagnostic workflows are recommended and essential for improving patient outcomes in bloodstream infections, where delays in pathogen identification and resistance detection can compromise timely antimicrobial therapy. Current workflows often rely on multiple platforms, increasing turnaround time and laboratory burden. Additionally, the clinical impact of rapid diagnostic results is dependent on timely interpretation and implementation within antimicrobial stewardship frameworks, which may involve complex decision algorithms. This study demonstrates that remnant bacterial suspensions generated during routine antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) using the ASTar System can be recovered and utilized for rapid matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry and lateral flow assay-based resistance detection. By enabling pathogen identification and/or resistance detection within ~1-2 h of AST initiation or resistance detection via reflex testing, this approach reduces duplicate sample testing and may enable earlier access to rapid microbiological results.

articles.title: m6A coordinates mumps virus replication and innate immune sensing.
articles.abstract: In this study, we test the hypothesis that N6-methyladenosine (m6A) coordinates a functional trade-off between viral replication and innate immune sensing during mumps virus (MuV) infection. Using single-base resolution GLORI-seq, we identified widespread and non-canonically distributed m6A sites across MuV genomic, antigenomic, and messenger RNAs. Functional analyses revealed that depletion of the m6A methyltransferase METTL3 enhances viral RNA synthesis and nucleocapsid encapsidation in interferon-deficient cells, indicating an intrinsic suppressive role of m6A in viral replication. In contrast, in immune-competent epithelial and dendritic cells, host m6A enhances antiviral signaling, as METTL3 deficiency reduces infection-induced interferon and cytokine responses. Mechanistically, m6A-deficient MuV RNA exhibited increased binding to multiple pattern recognition receptors, including RIG-I-like and toll-like receptors, resulting in enhanced innate immune activation. Additionally, MuV infection extensively remodels the host m6A epitranscriptome in a cell type-dependent manner, with m6A enrichment positively correlating with the expression of immune-related transcripts. Together, these findings demonstrate that m6A acts as a bidirectional regulator during MuV infection by simultaneously restricting viral replication and modulating host immune recognition, providing new insight into epitranscriptomic control of paramyxovirus-host interactions.IMPORTANCEN6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification has emerged as a key regulator of RNA virus infection, yet its role in mumps virus (MuV) remains undefined. Here, we map the single-base resolution m6A landscape of a recombinant MuV and demonstrate that viral m6A restricts genome encapsidation and replication while attenuating innate immune sensing. MuV infection extensively remodels host m6A profiles in epithelial and dendritic cells, preferentially enhancing methylation of innate immune transcripts. Strikingly, m6A-deficient MuV RNA exhibits increased affinity for RIG-I-like and toll-like receptors, eliciting stronger interferon and proinflammatory responses. Our findings identify m6A as a bidirectional regulator of MuV replication and immunity and suggest an epitranscriptomic strategy to optimize live-attenuated vaccine design.

articles.title: Incyclinide exhibits potent antibacterial and anti-biofilm activity against Staphylococcus aureus.
articles.abstract: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and biofilm-associated infections remain major therapeutic challenges. Here, we investigated the antibacterial activity and mechanism of Incyclinide against S. aureus. Incyclinide showed potent activity against 40 clinical isolates, with a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 2 µM for 81.25% of MSSA isolates and 91.66% of MRSA isolates. In representative MSSA and MRSA strains, 1× MIC completely inhibited planktonic growth, while time-kill assays demonstrated concentration-dependent bactericidal activity; at 8× MIC, bacterial counts decreased by 3.2 log10 CFU/mL in NCTC 8325 and 4.3 log10 CFU/mL in USA300 after 24 h. Incyclinide also markedly reduced the biomass of mature, pre-established biofilms. Proteomic profiling of Incyclinide-treated USA300 identified 59 differentially expressed proteins enriched in membrane-related functions. Transmission electron microscopy and fluorescence assays revealed severe cell envelope damage, increased membrane permeability, and membrane depolarization. Exogenous phospholipids antagonized antibacterial activity, with phosphatidylethanolamine and cardiolipin showing stronger effects than phosphatidylglycerol. In addition, resistance induction and whole-genome sequencing identified recurrent clpX mutations; clpX deletion increased the MIC from 2 to 8 µM, whereas complementation restored susceptibility. Molecular docking suggested favorable binding between Incyclinide and ClpX, with a predicted binding energy of -9.4 kcal/mol. Incyclinide also exhibited low hemolytic activity, negligible cytotoxicity toward BEAS-2B and human umbilical vein endothelial cell up to 128 µM, and significant protection in a Galleria mellonella infection model. Collectively, these findings identify Incyclinide as a promising anti-S. aureus agent with potent activity against MRSA and mature biofilms, acting primarily through membrane disruption, with ClpX potentially contributing to susceptibility.IMPORTANCEMethicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and biofilm-associated infections pose significant clinical challenges due to limited therapeutic options. Here, we identify Incyclinide, a tetracycline derivative, as a potent anti-S. aureus agent. It exhibits potent bactericidal activity against clinical MRSA isolates and effectively eradicates mature biofilms. Mechanistically, Incyclinide disrupts membrane integrity, causing depolarization and leakage. Notably, we identify the essential chaperone ClpX as a key molecular determinant of susceptibility through genetic and docking studies. Incyclinide demonstrates a favorable safety profile and superior efficacy compared with vancomycin in a Galleria mellonella infection model. Our findings highlight Incyclinide as a promising candidate featuring a dual membrane-targeting and intracellular mechanism, offering a strategic advantage against drug-resistant and biofilm-embedded pathogens.

articles.title: Early neurological events after carotid revascularization and estimated whole blood viscosity.
articles.journal: Turk gogus kalp damar cerrahisi dergisi
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to investigate the association between preprocedural estimated whole blood viscosity (eWBV) and the 30-day composite outcome of stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA) following carotid revascularization.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 247 patients who underwent elective carotid revascularization between 2020 and 2024, comprising 105 patients who underwent carotid endarterectomy (CEA) and 142 who underwent carotid artery stenting (CAS). eWBV at high and low shear rates was estimated using the de Simone equations based on hematocrit and total plasma protein levels measured within 24 h before the procedure. The associations between eWBV and the primary outcome were assessed using separate logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, diabetes mellitus, symptomatic status, stenosis severity, and procedure type.

RESULTS: Stroke or TIA occurred within 30 days after the procedure in 15 of 247 patients (6.1%), including 6 of 105 patients (5.7%) who underwent CEA and 9 of 142 patients (6.3%) who underwent CAS (p=0.839). After adjustment for the prespecified covariates, the odds ratio for the primary outcome was 25.95 (95% confidence interval [CI], 4.37-154.10) per 1-cP increase in high-shear-rate viscosity and 7.57 (95% CI, 2.52-22.75) per 10-cP increase in low-shear-rate viscosity (both p<0.001).

CONCLUSION: Higher preprocedural eWBV was associated with an increased likelihood of neurological events within 30 days after carotid revascularization. However, given the small number of outcome events and the substantial uncertainty reflected in the wide CIs, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Prospective studies are needed to validate these associations before eWBV can be considered for clinical use.

articles.title: Cis-regulation and natural selection in the evolution of human DNA methylation.
articles.abstract: The vast collection of human-specific traits-such as our unique morphology, cognition, behavior, and diseases-has long been attributed to gene expression divergence between us and our closest living relatives, chimpanzees. Theory suggests that changes to cis-regulatory elements such as promoters and enhancers may drive evolutionary adaptation, and DNA methylation is a key factor in transcriptional cis-regulation. However, we still lack an understanding of (1) how species-specific methylation patterns arise; (2) their downstream effects; and (3) whether they are a common target of natural selection. In this study, we investigated these three questions. By combining a novel hypothesis testing framework with DNA methylation data from six human and chimpanzee cell types, as well as fused interspecies hybrid cells, we disentangled cis- vs. trans-acting methylation divergence across the genome. Across cell types, we found that methylation divergence is primarily driven in cis, which can be linked in some cases to nearby sequence variants such as CpG gains and losses. Although less common, regions with trans-acting methylation divergence were enriched for specific transcription factor (TF) binding motifs, suggesting a role of TFs such as FOXM1 in these differences. Having established these causes of methylation divergence, we then examined the functional consequences of differential methylation. Although methylation lacks a consistent relationship with transcription, we observed that associations between methylation and gene expression are stronger for genes with cis-regulatory divergence. Moreover, we identified lineage-specific selection shaping promoter methylation at the level of entire pathways, including those associated with human-specific traits such as speech, cognition, and susceptibility to infection with hepatitis C. Collectively, our findings provide a mechanistic framework suggesting that DNA methylation may occupy a key position, mediating the effects of both cis- and trans-acting factors on transcriptional networks, including those contributing to human-specific traits.

articles.title: The impact of indoor PM2.5 and PM10 concentrations on allergy and asthma in the Polish Mother and Child Cohort Study (REPRO_PL).
articles.journal: International journal of occupational medicine and environmental health
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Particulate matter (PM) is an important component of air pollution and may contribute to the development or exacerbation of allergic diseases. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the associations between 24-hour indoor PM concentrations and the prevalence of asthma, allergic rhinitis/allergic conjunctivitis, and atopic dermatitis among adolescents participating in the Polish Mother and Child Cohort Study (REPRO_PL).

MATERIAL AND METHODS: Indoor PM2.5 and PM10 concentrations were measured over a 24-hour period using portable air-sampling pumps. Information on adolescent health was obtained from questionnaires and medical records. Additional assessments included spirometry, fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) measurement, and skin prick testing. Unadjusted comparisons and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed for 172 participants with complete data on the analyzed outcome and exposure variables.

RESULTS: Particulate matter 10 showed a positive but statistically non-significant association with asthma (OR = 2.22, 95% CI: 0.88-5.57, p = 0.09). No statistically significant associations were observed between indoor PM2.5 or PM10 concentrations and allergic rhinitis/allergic conjunctivitis or atopic dermatitis.

CONCLUSIONS: Further studies involving larger populations and repeated or longer-term air measurements are needed to clarify the relationship between indoor particulate matter exposure and allergic diseases. Int J Occup Med Environ Health. 2026;39(5).

articles.title: Association of retinal abnormalities and adverse cardiac events in patients with coronary artery disease and type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aim of this study was to evaluate the association of retinal abnormalities and cardiac mortality in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) and type 2 diabetes (DM).

METHODS: The ARTEMIS study is a prospective cohort study of 1,946 patients (68% male; mean age 66.9 ± 8.6 years) diagnosed with CAD. Type 2 DM was diagnosed in 834 patients (43%), and 525 (27%) of them had retinal images available.

RESULTS: During mean follow-up of 8.7 ± 2.2 years, 54 cardiac deaths occurred. From all analyzed retinal abnormalities, diabetic retinopathy (DR) was associated with cardiac death (p = 0.005). DR was independently associated with increased risk of cardiac death (DR 16.2% vs. non-DR 8.4%; hazard ratio [HR] 2.0, 95% CI: 1.0-4.0, p = 0.04) when adjusted with confounding factors. DR was associated with sudden cardiac death (SCD) (DR 8.5% vs. non-DR 3.8%; HR 2.9, 95% CI: 1.1-7.7, p = 0.03) but not with non-sudden cardiac death (DR 7.7% vs. non-DR 4.6%; HR 1.5, 95% CI: 0.6-3.9, p = 0.5). Interestingly, increased hs-TnT, measured in stable phase of CAD, was also associated with DR (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: DR seems to be associated with cardiac death, and more specifically, with SCD in patients with CAD and type 2 DM. DR might be a novel marker of microvascular cardiac disease resulting in ongoing myocardial injury and SCD.

articles.title: International Delphi Consensus on the Use of Near-infrared Spectroscopy for Wound Care and Procedural Decision-making, With Adjunctive Workflow and Time Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) is a point-of-care imaging modality that provides real-time measurement of tissue oxygenation and hemoglobin dynamics. Conventional vascular testing remains an essential component of wound care and limb preservation but evaluates vessel anatomy, blood flow, and other aspects of vascular status that differ from the tissue-level physiological information provided by NIRS. Although the 2 approaches may be complementary, NIRS can independently inform clinical decision-making by providing immediate physiological information at the point of care. This study employed a modified Delphi process to characterize expert perspectives regarding the clinical role, integration, workflow, and value of NIRS across wound care, tissue assessment, and related procedural settings.

METHODS: A modified Delphi process was conducted with a multidisciplinary panel representing diverse specialties, practice settings, and geographic regions. Survey items addressed clinical indications, workflow integration, decision-making impact, operational considerations, and the relationship between NIRS and conventional vascular assessment. Consensus was predefined as ≥80% agreement. A supplementary workflow and time analysis was performed using a subset of experienced users to characterize procedural steps and associated time requirements.

RESULTS: Survey responses generally supported confidence in vascular testing when appropriately selected, performed, and interpreted; however, the Round 1 panel discussion highlighted concerns regarding study selection, interpretation, repeat testing, and variability across testing pathways. Access and timeliness emerged as additional challenges that were consistently identified across both survey responses and the panel discussion. Delays in obtaining clinically meaningful physiological information were reported to contribute to clinically significant consequences, including hospitalization and amputation, particularly in lower-access environments. There was strong agreement that point-of-care NIRS enables earlier recognition of underlying pathophysiology and more timely initiation of appropriate interventions. NIRS was described as integrated across the continuum of care, including initial evaluation, procedural planning, treatment modification, referral support, and longitudinal monitoring. Of the 40 consensus items evaluated by the 18-member panel, 37 (92.5%) met the predefined ≥80% agreement threshold. Overall interrater agreement was very strong (median rWG: 0.92; interquartile range: 0.84 to 1.00). The supplementary workflow and time analysis demonstrated that image acquisition activities were generally efficient, whereas interpretation, documentation, reporting, and care coordination accounted for a substantial proportion of total clinician effort.

CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies a clinically meaningful gap between the availability of diagnostic testing and the timely delivery of actionable physiological information within wound care workflows. Although conventional vascular testing remains essential, clinicians described challenges related to testing pathways, study selection, interpretation, access, timeliness, and integration of physiological information into clinical decision-making. Within this context, NIRS provides point-of-care physiological information and supports longitudinal monitoring of tissue oxygenation throughout treatment. By providing real-time physiological insight, NIRS may facilitate earlier recognition of deteriorating tissue status, support more timely intervention, and help bridge episodic diagnostic assessment with continuous clinical management. More broadly, these findings suggest that the value of emerging diagnostic technologies should be evaluated not only by the information they generate, but also by their ability to deliver actionable data within clinical workflows, support longitudinal monitoring, and account for the clinician effort required to interpret, integrate, document, and act upon physiological findings.

articles.title: Deep Vein Thrombosis Complicated by the Dissemination of Muscular Tuberculosis due to Acupuncture Treatment.
articles.abstract: ObjectivesTo present a rare case of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the right upper extremity caused by muscular tuberculosis (MTB), likely disseminated via acupuncture, and to describe the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges encountered.MethodsThis case report details the clinical presentation, diagnostic workup, and management of a patient with MTB-associated DVT. The patient was treated with standard anti-tuberculosis therapy (rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol) along with anticoagulation therapy (low-molecular-weight heparin and rivaroxaban). Surgical intervention (debridement and drainage) was required due to abscess formation during treatment.ResultsInitially, the patient's DVT had an unclear etiology but was ultimately attributed to MTB. Despite complications including tuberculous abscess formation, combined medical and surgical management led to a successful outcome with resolution of infection and thrombosis.ConclusionsMuscular tuberculosis, though rare, should be considered in cases of unexplained DVT, particularly in patients with risk factors such as invasive procedures (eg, acupuncture). Early diagnosis, combined anti-TB therapy, anticoagulation, and surgical intervention, when necessary, can lead to favorable outcomes.

articles.title: Clonal Hematopoiesis and Cardiovascular and Microvascular Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes: A Retrospective Analysis of the UK Biobank.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) has been associated with cardiovascular disease, but its associations across cardiovascular and microvascular complications in type 2 diabetes remain incompletely characterized.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 17 893 UK Biobank participants with type 2 diabetes, whole-exome sequencing, and no prevalent cardiovascular or microvascular complications. CHIP was defined from the curated UK Biobank call set by ≥1 driver variant with a variant allele fraction ≥2%. Associations with incident outcomes were evaluated using Fine-Gray models with multiple imputation for missing covariates. Driver-gene, clone-size, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses were exploratory.

RESULTS: CHIP was present in 670 participants (3.7%) over a median follow-up of 14.6 years. CHIP was associated with the composite cardiovascular outcome (subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR], 1.19 [95% CI, 1.00-1.42]), with heart failure showing the clearest component association (SHR, 1.43 [95% CI, 1.13-1.81]); acute coronary syndrome and stroke were not significantly associated. CHIP was also associated with the composite microvascular outcome (SHR, 1.34 [95% CI, 1.15-1.56]), broad chronic kidney disease (SHR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.05-1.57]), and retinopathy (SHR, 1.43 [95% CI, 1.15-1.77]) but not neuropathy or strict diabetes-specific nephropathy. Ten-year adjusted risk differences were 1.94% and 3.46% for the cardiovascular and microvascular composites, respectively. Among 2919 proteins, ZBP1 (Z-DNA-binding protein 1) was the only protein retained after false-discovery-rate correction; no metabolite module was associated with CHIP after correction, whereas selected lipoprotein and amino acid/lactate modules were associated with cardiovascular outcomes, particularly heart failure.

CONCLUSIONS: In adults with type 2 diabetes, CHIP was associated with a higher risk of incident microvascular complications and, among cardiovascular outcomes, most consistently with heart failure. Exploratory multiomic findings, including a protein-wide ZBP1 signal and selected metabolic associations with cardiovascular outcomes, provided additional biological context but require independent validation.

articles.title: Sex-Stratified Outcomes in Balloon Angioplasty for Symptomatic Intracranial Artery Stenosis: The BASIS Subgroup Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The BASIS (Balloon Angioplasty for Symptomatic Intracranial Artery Stenosis) trial demonstrated that balloon angioplasty plus aggressive medical management was superior to aggressive medical management alone for symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis. However, whether sex modifies this treatment effect is unknown.

METHODS: This prespecified secondary analysis of the BASIS randomized controlled trial included 501 patients with symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis from 31 Chinese centers (November 2018 to April 2022). Baseline characteristics and outcomes were compared between sexes and across treatment arms within each sex. The primary outcome was stroke or death within 30 days, or ischemic stroke in the qualifying artery territory or revascularization beyond 30 days through 12 months.

RESULTS: Among 501 patients (mean age, 58 years), 158 (31.5%) were women. No significant sex-by-treatment interaction was observed for primary or key secondary outcomes (all P for interaction >0.05). In sex-stratified analyses, balloon angioplasty reduced primary outcome risk versus aggressive medical management in men (2.9% versus 11.1%; hazard ratio [HR]=0.21 [95% CI, 0.07-0.65]; P=0.01). In women, the effect favored balloon angioplasty but was not statistically significant (7.8% versus 18.5%; HR=0.37 [95% CI, 0.14-1.01]; P=0.051).

CONCLUSIONS: No significant interaction between sex and treatment effect was found, suggesting balloon angioplasty's benefit relative to aggressive medical management does not clearly differ by sex. Sex-stratified results showed significant benefit in men and a nonsignificant trend in women, but the study lacked power for definitive interaction testing, so findings are exploratory. Further research is needed to confirm these findings in broader populations.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique Identifier: NCT03703635.

articles.title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices of Quality Management Tools Among Healthcare Workers Before and After Training.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess changes in healthcare workers' (HCWs) knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP) regarding quality management tools (QMTs) before and after training and to explore the effectiveness of the training program in enhancing the application of QMTs in clinical practice.

METHODS: A single-group pretest-posttest interventional study design was adopted, and data were collected through online surveys before the training and 6 months after its completion. The training included 11 hours of theoretical and practical sessions on QMTs such as Find-Organize-Clarify-Understand-Select-Plan-Do-Check-Act (FOCUS-PDCA) and quality management charts. Valid responses from 66 HCWs were analyzed using descriptive statistics and paired t tests.

RESULTS: Significant improvements were observed in HCWs' knowledge (mean score: 50.5-55.2, P < .001), attitudes (38.9-44.5, P < .001), and practices (31.4-36.8, P < .001) posttraining. Notable heterogeneous effects were observed across different QMTs and charts; process- and risk-management-oriented tools achieved substantial improvement, whereas team- and habit-dependent tools showed limited progress.

CONCLUSION: A structured, case-based QMTs training program was associated with improvements in HCWs' knowledge, attitudes, and practices, though gains varied by tools. These findings suggest tool-specific strategies may enhance future QMTs education.

articles.title: Association of physical activity with insulin resistance in shift workers: data from NHANES.
articles.journal: International journal of occupational medicine and environmental health
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the association between shift work patterns and insulin resistance (IR) surrogates, and the potential moderating role of physical activity (PA).

MATERIAL AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study analysed 992 adults from National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2017-2018. Participants were categorized into daytime and variable shift workers. Four IR surrogates were evaluated. Weighted linear regression models adjusted for demographics, anthropometrics, lifestyle, and clinical covariates assessed associations between work schedules, PA, and metabolic outcomes. Sensitivity analyses excluded individuals with diabetes.

RESULTS: Compared to daytime workers, variable shift workers had significantly higher triglycerides, lower high-density lipoprotein-cholesterol (HDL-C), and elevated levels of all IR surrogates. Physical activity was inversely associated with triglyceride-glucose - waist circumference (TyG-WC) and body mass index (TyG-BMI). The most pronounced combined beneficial association was observed for daytime schedules combined with sufficient PA on homeostasis model assessment of IR (HOMA‑IR) and TyG-BMI. However, when stratified, work-related PA correlated positively with these indices, while leisure-time PA exhibited stronger inverse associations; transportation PA showed no association.

CONCLUSIONS: Variable shift work and insufficient PA are associated with adverse metabolic profiles and elevated IR. As a modifiable factor, PA may help mitigate metabolic risk in shift-working populations. Int J Occup Med Environ Health. 2026;39(5).

articles.title: Medication Safety Risks Associated With Inappropriate Use of Non-Crushable Tablets in Enterally Fed Patients: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Hospitalized patients receiving enteral feeding are at high risk of medication administration errors. In clinical practice, non-crushable oral tablets may be inappropriately prescribed, potentially resulting in adverse outcomes. This study examined the association between inappropriate use of non-crushable oral tablets during hospitalization and early post-discharge emergency department (ED) visits among patients receiving enteral feeding.

METHODS: We conducted a nationwide population-based cohort study using a national health insurance claims database in 2020, including 173,476 hospitalized patients receiving enteral feeding. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate the association between inappropriate use of non-crushable tablets and the hazard of the first ED visit during the 3-day post-discharge follow-up period.

RESULTS: Among 173,476 patients, 40.2% were exposed to inappropriate medication use. Exposure was associated with a significantly higher hazard of a first ED visit during the 3-day post-discharge follow-up period (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.954; 95% confidence interval, 1.721-2.217). The association varied significantly across age groups and inpatient departments, with the largest adjusted hazard ratios observed among patients aged <65 years and those treated in hematology and oncology, infectious diseases, and neurosurgery. Selected comorbidities, including hypertension, cerebrovascular accident, and dementia, were also associated with a higher hazard of an early ED visit.

CONCLUSION: Orders for non-crushable tablets among hospitalized patients receiving enteral feeding were common and were associated with a substantially higher hazard of an early post-discharge ED visit. The association varied across age groups and inpatient departments, although these subgroup findings should be interpreted cautiously. These findings highlight an important medication safety concern during transitions of care and support further evaluation of system-level strategies, including prescribing safeguards, clinical decision support, and multidisciplinary medication review, to improve the quality and safety of medication management.

articles.title: Chronic calcified pulmonary artery thrombosis: A rare cause of dyspnea in a young adult.
Acute Kidney Injury Disrupts Cardiac Remodeling via SerpinA3N.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiorenal syndrome type 3 describes cardiac injury triggered by acute kidney injury (AKI). AKI caused by ischemia reperfusion injury represents a model for kidney injury during kidney transplant. It is well known that kidney transplant recipients are at increased risk to develop cardiac fibrosis; however, the molecular mechanisms linking renal injury to myocardial remodeling or cardiac fibrosis remain unclear.

METHODS: Using a C57BL/6J mouse model of ischemia reperfusion injury-AKI, we combined proteomics and RNA seqencing transcriptomics to define early cardiac responses. We validated the proteomics and RNA sequencing data with quantitative polymerase chain reaction, ELISA, cytokine array, and western blotting for profibrotic and injury markers. We assessed SerpinA3N function using a granzyme B activity assay kit and XAV939, an inhibitor of SerpinA3N. Ingenuity pathway analysis further confirmed serine protease activity inhibition and increased expression of cardiac fibrosis-related genes after AKI.

RESULTS: Successful establishment of renal ischemia reperfusion injury causing AKI, followed by significant induction of cardiac injury. AKI significantly upregulated SerpinA3N in the heart while suppressing serine protease (granzyme B) activity. Concomitantly, AKI hearts displayed elevated profibrotic genes (FN1, COL1A1, TGF-β1), mitochondrial dysfunction, and heightened inflammatory signaling. In vitro, inhibition of SerpinA3N with XAV939 restored granzyme B activity, confirming direct suppression by SerpinA3N.

CONCLUSIONS: We conclude that SerpinA3N serves as a key mediator of cardiorenal syndrome type 3 pathogenesis, by inhibiting granzyme B, which promotes profibrotic remodeling in the heart following AKI. Targeting SerpinA3N could be a potential therapeutic approach that restores balanced extracellular matrix turnover and mitigates cardiac fibrosis.

articles.title: Metabolic and Renal Dysfunction Are Associated With Intraplaque Lipid Burden Assessed by Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Intravascular Ultrasound: Insights Into the Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Axis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic framework emphasizes the interrelated contributions of metabolic and renal dysfunction to cardiovascular risk. Whether these disturbances are reflected in coronary plaque composition remains incompletely understood. We evaluated the association of metabolic and renal dysfunction with intraplaque lipid burden using near-infrared spectroscopy intravascular ultrasound.

METHODS: Intraplaque lipid burden was assessed by the maximum lipid core burden index (LCBI) within a 4-mm segment (maxLCBI4mm), and lipid-rich plaque (LRP) was defined as maxLCBI4mm≥324.7. Multivariable linear regression models were constructed with maxLCBI4mm as the dependent variable, and multivariable logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations with LRP.

RESULTS: Among 483 patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention with pre-intervention near-infrared spectroscopy intravascular ultrasound imaging, lower estimated glomerular filtration rate and higher hemoglobin A1c were independently associated with greater intraplaque lipid burden and higher odds of LRP. In analyses standardized per 1 SD, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol showed the strongest association with maxLCBI4mm (β=52.51; 95% CI, 27.49-77.53), followed by estimated glomerular filtration rate (β=33.38; 95% CI, 9.97-56.80) and hemoglobin A1c (β=24.71; 95% CI, 3.71-45.71). Similarly, lower estimated glomerular filtration rate (odds tatio [OR], 1.36; 95% CI, 1.06-1.75) and higher hemoglobin A1c (OR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.05-1.77) were independently associated with LRP. No significant interaction between estimated glomerular filtration rate and hemoglobin A1c was observed.

CONCLUSIONS: Metabolic and renal dysfunction are independently associated with intraplaque lipid burden assessed by near-infrared spectroscopy intravascular ultrasound. These findings provide intracoronary imaging evidence linking the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic framework to plaque-level lipid accumulation.

articles.title: Diet-Driven Modulation of the Gut Microbiome to Enhance Neuroplasticity and Cognitive Recovery After Ischemic Stroke.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract: Cognitive impairment and limited neuroplastic recovery remain major contributors to long-term disability following ischemic stroke. Increasing evidence suggests that stroke-induced disruption of the gut-brain axis, characterized by microbiome dysbiosis and altered microbial metabolite signaling, may influence post-stroke inflammation, synaptic remodeling, and cognitive outcomes. Diet is a key modifiable determinant of gut microbiome composition and metabolic output, yet its role in post-stroke neuroplasticity has not been comprehensively synthesized. This narrative review examines dietary interventions with mechanistic or translational relevance to ischemic stroke recovery, including Mediterranean dietary patterns, ketogenic diets, high-fiber and prebiotic-enriched diets, probiotic and synbiotic supplementation, and intermittent fasting or caloric restriction. We summarize evidence linking diet-induced microbiome modulation to neuroinflammatory regulation, short-chain fatty acid signaling, microglial activity, mitochondrial function, and synaptic plasticity. Shared and diet-specific pathways are discussed, along with current limitations of the evidence base and barriers to clinical translation. Collectively, available data support a biologically plausible role for targeted dietary modulation of the gut microbiome as an adjunctive strategy to enhance cognitive recovery and neuroplasticity after ischemic stroke. Further well-designed clinical studies integrating microbiome profiling, neuroimaging, and cognitive outcomes are needed to define therapeutic potential and guide implementation in stroke rehabilitation. Among these dietary interventions, Mediterranean, high-fiber, and prebiotic-enriched diets currently have the strongest available evidence, while ketogenic and intermittent fasting approaches remain the least supported based on existing clinical and translational evidence.

articles.title: Thirty-Day All-Cause Readmissions After Pregnancy-Associated Hospitalizations With Heart Failure in the United States: Analysis of the Nationwide Readmissions Database.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of pregnancy-related morbidity and mortality in the United States. There is a paucity of data regarding pregnancy-associated heart failure readmissions. This study aims to characterize the 30-day heart failure readmission patterns in pregnancy-associated admissions.

METHODS: The National Readmission Database from 2016 to 2021 was used to identify women aged 13 to 49 with an index hospitalization with heart failure as the primary or secondary diagnosis during a pregnancy-related admission, identified by diagnosis-related group codes and International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) codes. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause readmission. Survey-weighted descriptive analyses and hierarchical multivariable logistic regression were used to characterize readmission patterns and identify independently associated factors.

RESULTS: Among 19 452 eligible index hospitalizations, 2659 were followed by a 30-day readmission; the survey-weighted readmission rate was 13.5%. In the fully adjusted model, Medicare and Medicaid coverage, residence in a small metropolitan area, greater All Patient Refined Diagnosis-Related Group severity, discharge with home health care, and discharge against medical advice were associated with higher odds of readmission. Deficiency anemia, chronic pulmonary disease, diabetes without chronic complications, renal failure, solid tumor without metastasis, and cardiovascular or respiratory disorders complicating pregnancy were also independently associated with increased readmission.

CONCLUSIONS: Approximately 1 in 7 pregnancy-associated hospitalizations complicated by heart failure was followed by a 30-day all-cause readmission. Readmission risk reflected a combination of illness severity, discharge disposition, payer status, geographic location, and selected medical and pregnancy-related comorbidities. These findings support the development and evaluation of individualized, multidisciplinary transitional-care strategies for patients at highest risk.

articles.title: Rationale and Design of a Multicenter, Randomized Controlled Trial: LEAP-Block.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrioventricular block with normal cardiac function is common with right ventricular pacing, which raises risks of pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and symptomatic heart failure in some patients with high pacing burden. Left bundle-branch area pacing demonstrates protective potential to reduce the risk of heart failure on the basis of observational studies. Evidence from a large multicenter randomized controlled trial remains limited.

METHODS: The LEAP-Block (Impact of Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing Versus Right Ventricular Pacing in Atrioventricular Block) study is a prospective multicenter, investigator-initiated randomized controlled trial aiming to verify the hypothesis that left bundle-branch area pacing might have superior impact to right ventricular pacing in reducing the risk of cardiovascular events in patients with atrioventricular block requiring high burden of ventricular pacing and left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50%. A total of 484 patients will be randomized to either left bundle-branch area pacing or right ventricular pacing (1:1). The primary end point is the composite events of all-cause death, heart failure events, and upgrade to biventricular pacing-delivered cardiac resynchronization therapy during at least 24 months of follow-up. Secondary end points include changes in echocardiographic, electrocardiographic, and pacing parameters and device-related complications.

CONCLUSIONS: The LEAP-Block study aims to compare the impact of left bundle-branch area pacing versus conventional right ventricular pacing in patients with atrioventricular block and preserved cardiac function with respect to midterm clinical outcomes. This trial will provide high-quality evidence for the selection of optimal pacing strategies in clinical practice.

REGISTRATION INFORMATION: clinicaltrials.gov. Identifier: NCT04730921.

articles.title: Prediction of Stroke Outcome After Endovascular Thrombectomy From Clinical Characteristics: A Machine Learning Approach.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Predicting outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is challenging. This study aimed to develop a machine learning model to predict outcomes after EVT using only clinical characteristics available shortly after hospital arrival, excluding imaging, laboratory, and angiographic data.

METHODS: We analyzed data from the JSDB (Japan Stroke Data Bank), a multicenter, prospective registry of patients with acute stroke. A total of 4353 patients who underwent EVT between 2016 and 2020 were included, with those from 2016 to 2019 assigned to the derivation cohort and those from 2020 to the validation cohort. The model was developed using 132 routinely collected clinical variables that can be rapidly obtained on patient arrival. Feature selection was performed using the Boruta algorithm, and the model was built using CatBoost. The primary outcome was a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0 to 2 at discharge.

RESULTS: Among 4353 patients treated with EVT, the derivation cohort included 2764 patients and the validation cohort, 1589 patients. In these cohorts, 973 (35.2%) and 547 (34.4%) achieved mRS 0 to 2, respectively. Boruta selected 47 predictors. CatBoost achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.744 (95% CI, 0.710-0.776) in the derivation test set and 0.781 (95% CI, 0.755-0.803) in the validation cohort. Validation areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves were 0.792 (95% CI, 0.765-0.815) for mRS 0 to 1, 0.766 (95% CI, 0.744-0.787) for mRS 0 to 3, and 0.680 (95% CI, 0.631-0.729) for mRS 6.

CONCLUSIONS: Our machine learning model predicted outcomes following EVT using only admission clinical data. This imaging-independent machine learning approach may support early prognostication and facilitate discussions of expected clinical courses.

articles.title: Evaluating the Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Paradox in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypercholesterolemia is an established cardiovascular risk factor. However, studies in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) showed an association between low low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and increased mortality, termed the "LDL-C paradox." This study examined the impact of LDL-C on clinical outcomes in patients with HFrEF and identify distinct hypocholesterolemia subgroups using latent class analysis.

METHODS: Consecutive patients with HFrEF (left ventricular EF <40%) from national registries (2016-2022) were stratified by LDL-C quartiles, with the lowest quartile ≤1.73 mmol/L. Latent class analysis was performed to identify subsets of patients in the lowest quartile. Outcomes included 1-year all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, readmission, and composite end points.

RESULTS: Among 2188 patients, the lowest LDL-C quartile had higher 1-year all-cause mortality than Quartile 2 and 3 (P<0.05) but not Quartile 4, with no intergroup differences in cardiovascular mortality, readmissions, or composite outcomes between groups. Latent class analysis identified 2 hypocholesterolemia subgroups: pathological and nonpathological hypocholesterolemia. The pathological subgroup was older, lower weight, with higher comorbidity burden. Compared with patients with hypercholesterolemia, the pathological hypocholesterolemia subgroup had higher 1-year all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 2.14 [95% CI, 1.17-2.69], P<0.001), cardiovascular mortality (adjusted HR, 1.93 [95% CI, 1.46-2.54], P<0.001), and composite end points (adjusted HR, 1.15 [95% CI, 1.01-1.30], P=0.037), and the subgroup with nonpathological hypocholesterolemia showed comparable outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: A distinct subset of patients with HFrEF with low LDL-C demonstrates different clinical characteristics (older and higher comorbidity burden) and poorer outcomes, potentially elucidating the "LDL-C paradox" cause in patients with HFrEF.

articles.title: Racial and Ethnic Disparities in Postarrest Cardiac Procedures for Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective postarrest care facilitates optimal outcomes for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Relatively little research has evaluated whether there may be racial or ethnic disparities in the workup and management of the patient post arrest.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied out-of-hospital cardiac arrests using the TriNetX research database. We defined out-of-hospital cardiac arrest as any emergency department visit (2013-2024) with a diagnosis of cardiac arrest and included patients who survived to admission. Multivariate adjusted logistic regression was used to compare rates of the following cardiac interventions across race or ethnicity: (1) echocardiography; (2) left heart catheterization; (3) percutaneous coronary intervention; (4) ventricular assist device placement; and (5) automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement.

RESULTS: A total of 58 394 cases of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest met inclusion criteria. Compared with White patients (left heart catheterization: 13.9%, percutaneous coronary intervention: 7.1%, ventricular assist device: 3.0%, automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator: 0.9%), Black patients had lower odds of receiving left heart catheterization (7.2%, adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.60 [95% CI, 0.55-0.64]), percutaneous coronary intervention (2.6%, aOR, 0.47 [95% CI, 0.42-0.53]), ventricular assist device placement (1.6%, aOR, 0.70 [95% CI, 0.60-0.80]), and automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement (0.4%, aOR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.41-0.70]). Hispanic/Latino patients were also less likely to receive left heart catheterization (8.9%, aOR, 0.72 [95% CI, 0.64-0.80]), percutaneous coronary intervention (3.7%, aOR, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.53-0.74]), and automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement (0.4%, aOR, 0.52 [95% CI, 0.33-0.81]).

CONCLUSIONS: Our large multicenter analysis identifies racial or ethnic disparities in postarrest cardiac workup and management. Further research is needed to identify potential causes for these disparities with the hope of developing strategies to address them.

articles.title: Effects of Exercise Preconditioning on Promoting Endogenous Recovery Responses After Ischemic Stroke in Late-Adult Mice.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke causes substantial neurological impairment, and although poststroke rehabilitation can support recovery, neurological deficits often limit the feasibility of exercise in clinical settings. Prestroke exercise has emerged as a potential strategy to enhance resilience to ischemic injury, but most preclinical studies have relied on young adult rodents, in which spontaneous recovery can sometimes obscure clinically meaningful functional effects. However, the impact of exercise preconditioning in later stages of adulthood remains insufficiently characterized.
