Here, we investigated whether a treadmill exercise preconditioning regimen confers neuroprotection and improves recovery-related responses in late-adult mice subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion.

METHODS: Eight-month-old male mice were assigned to sedentary or exercise groups. Following 5 weeks of treadmill running (5 days per week after 1 week of acclimatization), mice underwent 45 minutes of middle cerebral artery occlusion and reperfusion. Behavioral assessments and body-weight monitoring were performed before and after middle cerebral artery occlusion. Infarct volume and cellular responses were evaluated 14 days after stroke.

RESULTS: Fourteen days after stroke, lesion volume was significantly reduced in the exercise group compared with sedentary controls. Exercise preconditioning enhanced neurogenesis, oligodendrogenesis, and CD31-positive vascular responses while suppressing reactive astrocyte activation. Functional improvements were consistently observed across multiple behavioral assays in late-adult mice.

CONCLUSIONS: Preconditioning with treadmill exercise provides neuroprotection against ischemic stroke in late-adult mice by reducing infarct volume and promoting recovery-associated cellular responses. These findings demonstrate that the functional benefits of prestroke exercise extend beyond the young adult stage and support the potential value of regular physical activity as a strategy to mitigate ischemic brain injury later in adulthood.

articles.title: Poorly Controlled Hypertension Alters Coronary Microvascular Contractile Response to Endothelin-1 Before and After Cardiac Surgery.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with chronic hypertension have worse outcomes following on-pump (cardioplegia and cardiopulmonary bypass [CP/CPB]) cardiac surgery. Altered vasomotor function of the coronary microvasculature to ET-1 (endothelin-1) and other agonists may underlie these differences.

METHODS: Heart samples were collected from 85 patients undergoing CP/CPB enrolled in this observational study. Ex vivo coronary microvascular responses to ET-1, adenosine diphosphate, and sodium nitroprusside were assessed using video microscopy. Immunoblotting, immunohistochemistry, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and multiomics approaches were also used.

RESULTS: Coronary microvascular contractile response to ET-1 in patients with uncontrolled hypertension was increased compared with the other 2 cohorts pre- and post-CP/CPB (P<0.05 across ET-1 10-10 to 10-7 mmol/L). Adenosine diphosphate-induced coronary microvascular vasodilation was conversely decreased (P<0.05 for adenosine diphosphate 10-5 and 10-4 mmol/L). Post-CP/CPB microvascular responses to ET-1 and adenosine diphosphate were blunted overall (P<0.05). Antagonism of pro-vasoconstrictive endothelinA receptor diminished contractile response (P<0.05). Transcriptomics and proteomics showed wide regulation of pro-vasoconstrictive pathways. Regression showed that hypertension status and cardiac mass reliably approximated ET-1-induced coronary microvascular contraction (R2 0.95 pre-CP/CPB, R2 0.86 post-CP/CPB), which, in turn, estimated change in ejection fraction pre- and post-CP/CPB (P<0.05). Patients with uncontrolled hypertension had -11% change in EF when compared with the other 2 groups pooled (P<0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Altered coronary microvascular vasomotor function in patients with uncontrolled hypertension may jeopardize myocardial perfusion. Hypertension status and cardiac mass may be used to prognosticate this physiology, which, in turn, estimates change in ejection fraction postoperatively. Perioperative endothelin receptor blockers may benefit patients with uncontrolled hypertension and thus warrant further investigation.

articles.title: Side Effects of Low-Dose Colchicine in Chronic Coronary Disease: A Post Hoc Analysis of the LoDoCo2 Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low-dose colchicine reduces cardiovascular events in patients with chronic coronary disease. However, side effects may compromise compliance and lead to discontinuation of treatment. Therefore, we aimed to assess the incidence of side effects leading to discontinuation of treatment in the LoDoCo2 (Low-Dose Colchicine 2) trial.

METHODS: The LoDoCo2 trial was a randomized controlled trial evaluating colchicine versus placebo in patients with chronic coronary disease. Participants entered a 30-day open-label run-in phase during which all participants received colchicine 0.5 mg once daily, followed by randomization to colchicine or placebo. Tolerability-related side effects leading to treatment discontinuation were evaluated at the end of the 30-day run-in phase and during the randomized phase (median follow-up, 29.5 [interquartile range, 21.6-47.4] months). Cumulative incidence of side effects was presented using Kaplan-Meier curves and compared by treatment arm using Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: During the 30-day run-in phase, 618 of 6519 (9.5%) participants reported side effects. Women had a higher risk of side effects than men during the 30-day run-in phase (odds ratio, 1.53 [95% CI, 1.23-1.89]). After randomization, 114 participants (4.2%) in the colchicine group and 120 (4.4%) in the placebo group discontinued treatment due to side effects (hazard ratio [HR], 0.95 [95% CI, 0.73-1.22]). Gastrointestinal symptoms were most common (colchicine 2.0% versus placebo 1.7%) followed by myalgia (colchicine 1.2% versus placebo 1.6%). No differences in the risk of side effects between colchicine and placebo were seen for any of the subgroups. Women did have a higher risk of reporting side effects compared with men, regardless of assigned treatment (HR, 1.66 [95% CI, 1.22-2.25]).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with chronic coronary disease that tolerated initial treatment with low-dose colchicine, long-term discontinuation due to side effects was uncommon and did not differ between colchicine and placebo.

articles.title: Greenspace Exposure Reduces the Risk of Hypertension: A Large Prospective Cohort Study in Northwestern China.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The effects of greenspace on hypertension remain unconfirmed. This study aimed to validate this by performing a large prospective cohort study in China.

METHODS: PEAHEN-China (Prospective Environment and Health Epidemiological Study in Northwestern China) recruited 5 484 119 adults in 2017 and followed them to 2021. Blood pressure levels and hypertension were measured and defined using recommended standards. Greenspace exposure was estimated using the normalized difference vegetation index and enhanced vegetation index. Cox regression models and generalized estimating equation models were used to assess the associations of greenspace with hypertension incidence and blood pressure levels, respectively. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses were also performed.

RESULTS: During a median 3.21-year follow-up, 1 290 003 new hypertension cases occurred. Living in greener areas was significantly associated with a lower risk of hypertension and lower blood pressure levels. For example, in the adjusted models, compared with the first quartile of normalized difference vegetation index and enhanced vegetation index within a 500-m buffer, the hazard ratios of incident hypertension in the fourth quartile of the 2 metrics were 0.871 (95% CI, 0.861-0.881) and 0.896 (95% CI, 0.885-0.906). In addition, stronger associations of greenspace exposure with hypertension risk and blood pressure levels were observed in younger, male, rural, and less educated participants than their counterparts.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study indicates that neighborhood greenspace may reduce residents' odds of having hypertension, offering robust evidence for developing policies and strategies to mitigate the burden of hypertension.

articles.title: Effects of Transcatheter Tricuspid Edge-to-Edge Repair on Right Heart Dimension and Function.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) has developed as a treatment option for patients experiencing severe tricuspid regurgitation. T-TEER consistently reduces tricuspid regurgitation, but data on subsequent right heart remodeling remain limited. The aim of this study was to evaluate changes in right heart dimension and function after T-TEER using extended echocardiographic follow-up.

METHODS: The study was based on the international EuroTR (European Registry of Transcatheter Repair for Tricuspid Regurgitation), including patients undergoing T-TEER between 2016 and 2024 at 18 European centers. Eligible were patients with available baseline and follow-up (≥90 days postprocedure) echocardiographic assessment.

RESULTS: A total of 699 patients (mean age, 78±8 years; 56% women) were included in the analysis. Echocardiographic follow-up was performed at a median of 407 days (interquartile range, 205-801 days). Right heart dimensions significantly decreased: right ventricular (RV) midventricular diameter from 40.2±8.9 to 37.1±8.4 mm (P<0.001) and end-diastolic area from 28.7±9.0 to 26.2±9.6 cm2 (P<0.001). Procedural success was significantly associated with positive RV remodeling (odds ratio, 1.82 [95% CI, 1.07-3.09]). For RV function, a decline of fractional area change from 37.8%±10.2% to 33.3%±10.1% (P<0.001), and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion from 17.4±4.7 to 16.6±4.7 mm (P<0.001) was observed.

CONCLUSIONS: In the subset of surviving patients with available echocardiographic follow-up, treatment with T-TEER led to favorable long-term changes with reduced RV dimension, associated with procedural success. RV function modestly decreased, likely reflecting normalization after volume unloading.

articles.title: Association Between Stroke Subtype and Outcomes of Edaravone Dexborneol: A Subgroup Analysis of the EXPAND (Effectiveness and Safety of Edaravone Dexborneol in Acute Ischemic Stroke) Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The effectiveness of edaravone dexborneol among acute ischemic stroke subtypes remains unclear. We evaluated its association with clinical outcomes by stroke subtype.

METHODS: This secondary analysis of the prospective EXPAND (Effectiveness and Safety of Edaravone Dexborneol in Acute Ischemic Stroke) study included patients with acute ischemic stroke treated at 72 Chinese stroke centers from December 2022 to October 2023. Patients were classified as having large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) or non-LAA stroke and grouped by edaravone dexborneol use. Primary outcomes were 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores of 0 or 1 and 0 to 2 and ordinal mRS shift. Safety outcomes were 90-day mortality, intracranial hemorrhage, and in-hospital adverse events.

RESULTS: Among 4401 patients, 1061 (24.1%) had LAA and 3340 (75.9%) had non-LAA stroke; the median age was 65 years, and 66.8% were men. Edaravone dexborneol was associated with improved 90-day functional outcomes in the non-LAA group, including higher odds of achieving mRS 0 or 1 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.25 [95% CI, 1.06-1.47]), mRS 0 to 2 (aOR, 1.40 [95% CI, 1.15-1.71]), and a favorable mRS shift (aOR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.12-1.46]; all P<0.05). No significant functional benefit was observed in the LAA group of mRS 0 or 1 (aOR, 0.91; P=0.50), mRS 0 to 2 (aOR, 0.88; P=0.43), or mRS shift (aOR, 0.92; P=0.50). Significant interactions were observed between edaravone dexborneol and stroke subtype (P for interaction=0.03 for mRS 0 or 1, P=0.005 for mRS 0 to 2, and P=0.009 for favorable mRS shift). Safety outcomes were comparable between treatment groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Edaravone dexborneol was associated with improved 90-day functional outcomes in non-LAA but not LAA stroke.

articles.title: Adeno-Associated Virus-Induced Humanized Hypertensive Mouse Model Validates N-Acetylgalactosamine-Conjugated Small Interfering RNA Targeting Angiotensinogen as a Long-Acting Antihypertensive Therapy.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, yet current therapeutic strategies lack sustained efficacy and long-term stability. Our study aimed to construct a humanized rodent model for drugs development especially currently prevalent small interfering RNA medication.

METHODS: A humanized hypertensive mouse model was generated by subcutaneous injection of neonatal mice with adeno-associated viruses encoding hAGT (human angiotensinogen) and hRENIN (human renin). Blood pressure was monitored weekly via tail-cuff plethysmography. Expression of hAGT and hRENIN was assessed by ELISA, Western blot, and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Cardiac function was evaluated by echocardiography at 4 and 6 months postinjection. Hypertension-associated comorbidities were examined through histological analysis and ELISA. A modified N-acetylgalactosamine-conjugated small interfering RNA targeting human hepatic AGT (GalNAc-siAGT) was screened and subcutaneously administered to humanized hypertensive mice, either alone or in combination with valsartan, to evaluate therapeutic efficacy.

RESULTS: The dual adeno-associated virus-induced humanized hypertensive model exhibited a sustained hypertension for 6 months and manifested prevalent comorbidities, including heart failure and kidney disease. This modified GalNAc-siAGT demonstrated significant activity in knocking down hAGT both in vitro and in vivo. Only a single subcutaneous injection of GalNAc-siAGT in humanized hypertensive mice led to a sustained reduction in blood pressure lasting for 2 months, accompanied by cardio- and renoprotective effects. Moreover, combining GalNAc-siAGT with the renin-angiotensin system blocker, valsartan, significantly enhanced therapeutic efficacy.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study validated the antihypertensive therapeutic effect of GalNAc-siAGT in a humanized hypertensive murine model while highlighting the translational potential of this model for clinical drug development.

articles.title: Incidence of Cardiovascular Disease in a Primary Care Population of Young Adults by Disaggregated Race and Ethnicity.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death in the United States, with well-documented racial and ethnic disparities. Data are limited on incidence among patients aged <50 years, particularly within disaggregated Asian and Hispanic subgroups and individuals identifying with multiple racial or ethnic groups. We estimated CVD incidence rates for these groups and assessed whether disparities are explained by other clinical and demographic risk factors.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used Sutter Health Electronic Health Record data (2010-2024) for adults aged 18 to 49 years with at least 2 primary care visits and a 2-year observed baseline period free of CVD. Incident CVD was defined as myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure. We estimated incidence rates, applied age and sex standardization, and fit Cox proportional hazards models adjusting for additional risk factors.

RESULTS: In a cohort of 1 178 551 patients, incidence was 1.14 cases per 1000 person-years (95% CI, 1.12-1.17). After standardization, Pacific Islander individuals (hazard ratio [HR], 2.90 [95% CI, 2.29-3.52]) and non-Hispanic Black individuals (HR, 2.82 [95% CI, 2.58-3.06]) had the highest incidence. Within the Asian group, Filipino individuals had the highest incidence (HR, 1.60 [95% CI, 1.42-1.79]). Hispanic subgroups showed less heterogeneity. Elevated HRs persisted among some groups after adjustment with Cox models.

CONCLUSIONS: Young adult CVD incidence varied across racial and ethnic subgroups. Elevated risk persisted in several groups after adjustment, consistent with the influence of unmeasured social drivers. These findings support collection of granular racial and ethnic data and validation of existing risk prediction tools in young adult subgroups.

articles.title: Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Versus Direct Oral Anticoagulation in High-Risk Patients Undergoing Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion With Watchman FLX.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal antithrombotic therapy after left atrial appendage occlusion remains uncertain.

METHODS: We studied 2817 patients undergoing left atrial appendage occlusion at 8 hospitals from 2016 to 2023 using registry data linked to Medicare claims. Among 2448 Watchman FLX recipients, the primary exposure was time-varying dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) versus pooled direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC)-based therapy. Outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), major bleeding, and device complications. The primary instrumental-variable analysis used operator FLX preference; overlap weighting was secondary and pairwise regimen comparisons exploratory.

RESULTS: DAPT was associated with lower MACE (absolute risk difference [ARD], -1.5% [95% CI, -1.9% to -1.0%]; number needed to treat, 67) and major bleeding (ARD -1.6% [95% CI, -2.0% to -0.9%]; number needed to treat, 63) than pooled DOAC-based therapy, without increased device complications. Overlap-weighted associations with MACE and major bleeding were nonsignificant. In exploratory pairwise analyses, DAPT did not differ significantly from DOAC monotherapy for MACE or major bleeding; lower major bleeding was limited to DAPT versus DOAC plus single antiplatelet therapy (ARD, -0.6% [95% CI, -1.1% to -0.2%]; P=0.008). Most estimated benefit accrued within 6 months.

CONCLUSIONS: DAPT was associated with lower MACE and major bleeding than pooled DOAC-based therapy after Watchman FLX implantation. The safety benefit was concentrated in the comparison with DOAC + single antiplatelet therapy, whereas DAPT and DOAC monotherapy did not clearly differ in either outcome. These findings support randomized trials comparing DAPT with DOAC monotherapy.

articles.title: Associations of Cumulative Wrist Accelerometer-Derived Physical Activity and Proxies of Sedentary Behavior With Early Cardiac Remodeling in Healthy Adolescents.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physical inactivity and sedentary behavior are associated with adverse cardiac remodeling in adults, but evidence in adolescence remains limited. This study examined associations of cumulative accelerometer-derived physical activity and proxies of sedentary behavior during adolescence with early subclinical cardiac features assessed by cardiovascular magnetic resonance.

METHODS: A total of 111 adolescents (55.9% girls) wore a wrist-worn triaxial accelerometer at ages 12, 14, and 16 years to measure physical activity and sedentary behavior proxies. A 3-Tesla cardiovascular magnetic resonance scan was performed at final follow-up to assess cardiac structure and function. Multivariable linear regression models examined associations between cumulative physical activity and sedentary behavior proxies and cardiovascular magnetic resonance-derived metrics.

RESULTS: Daily step counts were positively associated with indexed end-diastolic and end-systolic volumes of the left ventricle (adjusted β per 1000 steps/d, 0.90 mL/m2.7 [95% CI, 0.42-1.37]; 0.36 mL/m2.7 [95% CI, 0.10-0.63], respectively) and the right ventricle (adjusted β per 1000 steps/d, 1.03 mL/m2.7 [95% CI, 0.44-1.61]; 0.44 mL/m2.7 [95% CI, 0.05-0.82], respectively), and with reduced right ventricular longitudinal strain (adjusted β per 1000 steps/d, 0.53% [95% CI, 0.16-0.91]). Greater time spent in sedentary bouts and a higher number of sedentary bouts were associated with increased left atrial active emptying fraction (adjusted β per 100 min/d, 8.21% [95% CI, 0.09-16.34]; adjusted β per 1 bout/d, 1.76% [95% CI, 0.17-3.35], respectively).

CONCLUSIONS: Physical inactivity and sedentary behavior proxies during adolescence were independently associated with early markers of ventricular and atrial remodeling. These findings highlight early cardiac adaptations related to lifestyle behaviors and underscore the importance of promoting active lifestyles from a young age.

articles.title: Association of Stroke Severity With Efficacy of Early Tirofiban Infusion After Intravenous Thrombolysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aims to assess the effects of stroke severity at admission on the efficacy and safety of early tirofiban infusion following intravenous thrombolysis in patients with acute ischemic noncardioembolic stroke using data from the ASSET-IT (Advancing Stroke Safety and Efficacy Through Early Tirofiban Administration After Intravenous Thrombolysis) trial.

METHODS: All 832 patients with acute ischemic noncardioembolic stroke from the ASSET-IT database were included in this exploratory post hoc analysis. The primary efficacy and safety outcomes were an excellent functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score of 0-1 at 90 days) and intracranial hemorrhage.

RESULTS: Among the 832 patients included, the median age was 69 (interquartile range, 59-76) years, 531 (63.8%) were men, 367 (44.1%) had minor stroke (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score <6), and 465 (55.9%) had moderate-to-severe stroke (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score ≥6). There were significant interactions between the primary efficacy and safety outcomes (Pinteraction=0.008, Pinteraction=0.03; respectively). We observed that among patients with NIHSS score ≥6, tirofiban markedly increased odds of achieving an excellent functional outcome (adjusted odds ratio, 2.13 [95% CI, 1.44-3.17]; P<0.001) without significantly increasing the risk of intracranial hemorrhage (adjusted odds ratio, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.37-2.09]; P=0.77). In contrast, no significant benefit was observed in the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score <6 group (adjusted odds ratio, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.64-1.63]; P=0.94) but there was a significant increase in the risk of intracranial hemorrhage (adjusted odds ratio, 6.51 [95% CI, 1.42-62.03]; P=0.01).

CONCLUSIONS: Early tirofiban infusion may be more beneficial for patients with moderate-to-severe stroke treated with intravenous thrombolysis within 4.5 hours of onset, while simultaneously suggesting an increased potential risk of intracranial hemorrhage in minor stroke.

articles.title: Renal Insufficiency and Clinical Outcomes in Acute Ischemic Stroke With Large Infarct: A Prospective Cohort Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to investigate whether renal insufficiency (RI) modifies the effectiveness and safety of endovascular treatment (EVT) in patients with acute ischemic stroke and large infarct in a real-world setting.

METHODS: This study was a post hoc analysis of a prospective multicenter cohort study. RI was defined as an estimated glomerular filtration rate <90 mL/min per 1.73 m2 on admission. Patients were treated with EVT plus standard medical treatment or standard medical treatment alone and were stratified by RI status. The primary effectiveness outcome was favorable outcome (modified Rankin scale 0-3) at 90 days. Safety outcomes included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage and 90-day mortality.

RESULTS: Among 745 patients with acute ischemic stroke and large infarct, 343 (46.0%) had RI and 490 (65.8%) underwent EVT. Compared with standard medical treatment, EVT was associated with improved functional outcomes (modified Rankin scale 0-3) in both the RI (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 2.55 [95% CI, 1.15-5.68], P=0.022) and the non-RI group (adjusted OR 2.65 [95% CI, 1.49-4.73], P=0.001). EVT was also associated with higher risks of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage in both groups (P=0.002 and 0.007, respectively), whereas no significant difference in mortality was observed. Results were consistent in the inverse probability-weighted analyses. No statistically significant interaction was observed between RI status and treatment effect for effectiveness or safety outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with acute ischemic stroke and large infarct, EVT was associated with improved functional outcomes but a higher risk of hemorrhagic complications. We did not find statistically significant evidence of interaction between EVT and RI status for 90-day outcomes.

articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

articles.title: Prognostic Value of Right Ventricular-Pulmonary Artery Coupling in Mitral Valve Surgery and Impact of Concomitant Tricuspid Valve Repair.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic impact of baseline right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling on clinical outcomes following mitral valve surgery with specific consideration of concomitant tricuspid valve repair remains uncertain.

METHODS: A total of 214 patients who underwent mitral valve surgery and presented with moderate tricuspid regurgitation at the index procedure were included. Patients were classified after baseline right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling (impaired versus normal). The primary study end point was a composite outcome of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization. Secondary study end points included all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization.

RESULTS: Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling was observed in 112 patients (52%), while 102 patients (48%) had normal right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling. The rate of concomitant tricuspid valve repair was similar between study groups (50.0% versus 49.0%, P=0.886). Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling was associated with a higher hazard of the composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 2.60, 95% CI 1.32-5.14, P=0.006), heart failure hospitalization (adjusted hazard ratio 3.29, 95% CI 1.27-8.54, P=0.014), and all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 2.25, 95% CI 1.11-4.59, P=0.025) during follow-up. Additionally, concomitant tricuspid valve repair in patients with moderate tricuspid regurgitation was associated with a lower hazard of the composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 0.45, 95% CI 0.26-0.80, P=0.007).

CONCLUSIONS: Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling is a predictor of adverse outcomes after mitral valve surgery. Concomitant tricuspid valve repair for moderate tricuspid regurgitation seems to be associated with improved outcomes.

articles.title: Population Impact of the 2026 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Dyslipidemia Guideline on Lipid-Lowering Therapy Eligibility Among US Adults.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2026 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association dyslipidemia guideline replaces the pooled cohort equations with the atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease component of the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events equations for primary prevention risk estimation and modifies lipid-lowering therapy (LLT) eligibility by lowering the risk-based treatment threshold and expanding diabetes and chronic kidney disease criteria. The population-level impact of this transition is uncertain.

METHODS: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2021 to 2023 participants aged 40 to 75 years without self-reported atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and with available low-density lipoprotein cholesterol. Survey weights were used to generate national estimates. Guideline-supported LLT eligibility was assessed under the 2018 pooled cohort equations-based American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association cholesterol framework and the 2026 Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events-based American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association dyslipidemia framework. Current LLT use was assessed among guideline-supported adults.

RESULTS: The analytic sample included 1662 participants, representing 115.05 million US adults. LLT was supported for 42.82 million adults under the 2018 framework and 42.17 million under the 2026 framework, a net decrease of 0.65 million. Reclassification was substantial: 37.42 million remained supported, 5.40 million lost support, 4.75 million newly gained support, and 67.48 million remained unsupported. Among supported adults, current LLT use was 39.4% under the 2018 framework and 40.5% under the 2026 framework.

CONCLUSIONS: Transition to the 2026 Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events-based framework produced little net change in LLT eligibility but meaningfully changed who was supported for therapy. Persistent undertreatment remains a major implementation gap.

articles.title: High on the Heart? Cannabis Use and Cardiovascular Disease: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract: Cannabis use has increased substantially over the past 2 decades following shifts in public perception, legalization, and medical usage. Although neurological and psychiatric effects are well known, the cardiovascular effects of cannabis exposure are largely understudied. This review evaluates the cardiovascular effects of cannabis use by examining clinical evidence, epidemiological data, and underlying biochemical mechanisms. This review examines cannabis-related cardiovascular conditions, including atherosclerosis, arrhythmias, heart failure, and stroke. The analysis focused on cannabinoid composition, route of administration, frequency of use, and cardiovascular outcomes. Evidence indicates that acute and high Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol/cannabidiol ratio cannabis use is associated with increased risks of various cardiovascular outcomes, especially among younger individuals without cardiovascular risk factors. Given rising use and increasing Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol potency, clinicians must routinely assess cannabis exposure when evaluating cardiovascular disease, especially in younger patients. Future research must prioritize the development of standardized exposure metrics in cannabis-related cardiovascular disease research, thus allowing clinicians and patients to better understand the cardiovascular risks of cannabis use and initiate effective cessation strategies.

articles.title: Risk Stratification and Outcomes of Right Atrial Phasic Function in Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy: A Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advanced arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy is associated with a high risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias (MVA) and end-stage heart failure (HF). However, the prognostic role of right atrial (RA) mechanics, as quantified by cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR), remains largely unexplored.

METHODS: Consecutive patients with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy undergoing CMR between 2014 and 2021 were retrospectively included. Demographics, clinical history, and strain parameters were collected. The primary clinical end points were end-stage HF and MVA.

RESULTS: A total of 316 patients (mean age 38±15 years; 66.1% men) were included. Over a median follow-up of 5.3 years, 49 developed end-stage HF and 103 experienced MVA outcomes. Multivariable Cox and Fine-Gray models showed that impaired RA reservoir strain was an independent predictor of end-stage HF (hazard ratio [HR] 0.92, 95% CI 0.89-0.96, P<0.001) and MVA outcomes (subdistribution hazard ratio (sHR) 0.98, 95% CI 0.96-0.99, P=0.025), with added prognostic value beyond clinical and imaging variables, improving the C-statistic to 0.84 and 0.70, respectively. Kaplan-Meier survival curves indicated that RA reservoir strain <18.6% was associated with higher end-stage HF risk, consistent across subgroups regardless of left ventricular involvement (both log-rank P<0.05). The association between RA reservoir strain <23.0% and MVA was significant in the overall cohort (P<0.001) and in patients without left ventricular involvement (P=0.002), but not in those with left ventricular involvement (P=0.08).

CONCLUSIONS: Lower cardiac magnetic resonance-derived RA reservoir strain was independently associated with end-stage HF and MVA in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy and provided incremental prognostic value beyond conventional risk markers. These findings support RA mechanics as a potential complementary component of multichamber CMR risk assessment, pending external validation.

articles.title: Longitudinal Inflammatory Trajectories and Recurrent Vascular Events After Acute Ischemic Stroke.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inflammation contributes to the pathophysiology of acute ischemic stroke, yet no inflammatory biomarker has been established as a standard prognostic tool. Most prior studies have relied on single baseline measurements, and the prognostic relevance of longitudinal inflammatory changes remains uncertain. We investigated whether baseline levels and longitudinal trajectories of inflammatory burden index (IBI) and hs-CRP (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein) are associated with recurrent stroke and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).

METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 374 patients with acute ischemic stroke were analyzed. IBI was calculated as hs-CRP multiplied by the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio. Serum hs-CRP and leukocyte differentials were measured within 24 hours of admission and at 6 months (±3 months). Baseline hs-CRP was dichotomized at 2 mg/L and IBI at the median baseline value (4.03 mg/L), and longitudinal trajectories were defined as persistent low, increased, decreased, or persistent high based on changes between baseline and follow-up measurements.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 30.5 months, 58 patients (15.5%) experienced recurrent stroke and 69 (18.4%) experienced MACE. Baseline IBI and hs-CRP showed inconsistent associations with these outcomes. In contrast, persistent high IBI was associated with increased risks of recurrent stroke (hazard ratio [HR] 2.46; 95% CI, 1.26-4.78; P=0.008) and MACE (HR 2.42; 95% CI, 1.33-4.43; P=0.004) compared with persistent low IBI. Persistent high hs-CRP was associated with MACE (HR 1.92; 95% CI, 1.08-3.41; P=0.026) but not with recurrent stroke.

CONCLUSIONS: Persistent high IBI trajectories were independently associated with recurrent stroke and MACE, and persistent high hs-CRP trajectories were associated with MACE. Longitudinal assessment of inflammatory biomarkers may provide prognostic information beyond a single baseline measurement after ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Institutional Variation in Electroencephalography Utilization in Neonates With Complex Congenital Heart Disease Across the United States and Its Association With Outcomes.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonates with complex congenital heart disease are at increased risk for perioperative brain injury and seizures. Electroencephalography (EEG) detects clinical and subclinical seizures, but national utilization patterns remain poorly characterized.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Pediatric Health Information System (2016-2025) of neonates ≤28 days with dextro-transposition of the great arteries or single-ventricle physiology undergoing surgical repair or palliation. Mixed-effects logistic regression with hospital as a random effect identified predictors of EEG utilization.

RESULTS: Among 13 202 neonates, 1654 (12.5%) underwent EEG monitoring. EEG monitoring was performed in only 10.8% of neonates with dextro-transposition of the great arteries, 16% of those with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, and 13% of those with non- hypoplastic left heart syndrome single-ventricle lesions. EEG utilization increased from ~6% in 2016 to >14% in 2025, while seizure detection among EEG-monitored patients increased from 13% to ~26% (both P-trend<0.01). Utilization varied substantially across hospitals (0% to >40%), persisting after adjustment for surgical volume. EEG-monitored neonates had higher seizure detection (21.8% versus 5.2%), longer length of stay (33 versus 24 days), and higher hospitalization costs ($344 719 versus $174 865; all P<0.01). In multivariable analysis, EEG utilization was independently associated with seizures (OR ~4), dextro-transposition of the great arteries, and hypoplastic left heart syndrome, but not with cardiac arrest, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, or hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy.

CONCLUSIONS: EEG utilization in neonates with complex congenital heart disease is increasing but remains low and highly variable across US centers. The association of EEG use with higher mortality and costs may reflect confounding by indication or illness severity. Standardized protocols are needed to optimize neurologic monitoring and improve long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Safety and Efficacy of Apixaban Therapy for Coronary Artery Aneurysms After Kawasaki Disease.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anticoagulation combined with aspirin lowers the risk of coronary thrombosis in patients with large/giant coronary artery aneurysms following Kawasaki disease. We aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of apixaban in this high-risk pediatric population and compare it to conventional anticoagulant therapy.

METHODS: In this retrospective study, we described our experience with the use of apixaban in patients with Kawasaki disease with large/giant coronary artery aneurysms. In patients who were previously exposed to conventional anticoagulation, we compared rates of new coronary thrombosis or myocardial infarction (effectiveness) and clinically relevant bleeding (safety) during apixaban versus antecedent conventional therapy. All patients received concomitant antiplatelet agents. Apixaban dosing was guided by weight and anti-Xa chromogenic assays.

RESULTS: Between 2018 and 2025, 28 patients with Kawasaki disease (median age 6.7 years; 75% male) with large/giant coronary artery aneurysms were prescribed apixaban. Of these, 27 (96%) had previously received vitamin K antagonists or low molecular weight heparin. The rates of new coronary thrombosis and new myocardial infarctions were not higher when patients received apixaban versus conventional anticoagulation (0.025 versus 0.041 events per person-year; incidence rate ratio [IRR], 0.61 [95% CI, 0.06-3.3] and 0.013 versus 0.041 events per person-year; IRR, 0.31 [95% CI, 0.01-2.5], respectively). Rates of clinically relevant bleeding were also not higher for apixaban versus conventional therapy (0.038 versus 0.058 events per person-year, IRR, 0.66 [95% CI, 0.11-2.5]).

CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective single-center series of pediatric patients with Kawasaki disease with large/giant coronary artery aneurysms, apixaban combined with antiplatelet therapy was well tolerated and demonstrated no evidence of increased harm relative to conventional anticoagulants. Multicenter research is needed to confirm these findings and define the optimal therapeutic range for apixaban in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Life Expectancy After Incident Ischemic Stroke in a Bi-Ethnic Population: Estimates Over 2005 to 2022.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study measured 5- and 10-year life expectancy after an incident ischemic stroke using a high-quality sample of Mexican Americans and non-Hispanic White patients over a recent period.

METHODS: Data were from the Brain Attack Surveillance in Corpus Christi Project. The sample included 2011 Mexican American and 1262 non-Hispanic White men and women who had an incident ischemic stroke during 2005 to 2022 and were aged 45 years or older at the time of stroke. Participants were followed up to 18 years. Primary outcome was 5- and 10-year life expectancy. Discrete-time logistic regression models were implemented.

RESULTS: Mean age at incident stroke was 69 years. There was no difference in the odds of dying between Mexican Americans and non-Hispanic White men and women after adjustment for age at stroke and sex. Among men, an incident stroke at age 70 years was associated with a 10-year life expectancy of 6.4 years (95% CI: 6.1-6.6) in Mexican Americans and 6.5 years (95% CI: 6.2-6.9) in non-Hispanic White adults. Among women, the analogous 10-year life expectancy was 6.7 years (95% CI: 6.3-6.8) in Mexican Americans and 6.8 years (95% CI: 6.4-7.0) in non-Hispanic White adults. Comparing these estimates to life expectancy at age 70 in the general US population indicates that stroke is associated with a life shortening effect of 2.1 to 2.4 years over 10 years.

CONCLUSIONS: Life expectancy after an ischemic stroke did not differ between Mexican Americans and non-Hispanic White adults. Incident ischemic stroke remains associated with substantial life shortening effects in the recent period.

articles.title: Clinical Observation of Precision Haemodynamic Management Guided by Pulse Index Continuous Cardiac Output in Patients with Septic Cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveThis study aimed to investigate the value of pulse index continuous cardiac output (PICCO) monitoring in assessing the relationship between cardiac function, haemodynamic evolution and prognosis in patients with septic cardiomyopathy (SCM).MethodsSixty patients with SCM were categorised into normal (left ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF] ≥ 50%, n = 21) and reduced (LVEF < 50%, n = 39) cardiac function groups. Haemodynamic parameters (cardiac index [CI], global end-diastolic volume index [GEDVI], systemic vascular resistance index [SVRI], extravascular lung water index and pulmonary vascular permeability index) were dynamically monitored via PICCO at 0, 6, 12, 24, 48 and 72 h. The 21-day mortality was recorded.ResultsThe reduced group was significantly older (62.4 ± 11.9 vs 36.4 ± 8.7 years, P < .001) with higher Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II scores (P = .028) than the normal group. Their CI remained significantly lower than that of the normal group at all time points, reaching a nadir at 24 h (2.46 ± 0.62 vs 3.65 ± 1.03 L/min·m2, P < .001). Unlike the normal group, the reduced group showed a significant GEDVI rebound at 24 h (P ≤ .05). No significant difference in SVRI was found between groups (P > .05). The 28-day cumulative mortality was 38.5% in the reduced group versus 19.0% in the normal group (P = .211).ConclusionPulse index continuous cardiac output monitoring effectively identifies haemodynamic differences across SCM cardiac functions. Patients with reduced LVEF exhibit severe cardiac depression and a 24-h decompensation window. Although mortality differences were not statistically significant in this cohort, PICCO provides vital quantifiable targets for individualised management.

articles.title: The effects of PNF on muscle electrical activity and correlation between sEMG signal and isometric muscle strength in post-stroke patients.
articles.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
articles.abstract: BackgroundObjective assessment of post-stroke muscle strength remains lacking.ObjectiveThis study explored whether Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation (PNF) improves the correlation between surface electromyography (sEMG) and muscle strength to facilitate sEMG-based evaluation in stroke patients.MethodsA crossover-design experiment enrolled 10 post-stroke patients. Baseline isokinetic testing (60°/s knee flexion/extension) determined the affected side's maximum isokinetic extension torque (MET) and angle of peak torque. Two isometric knee extension tasks (separated by a 1-day washout) were performed targeting 40%, 60%, and 80% MET. PNF was randomly applied in only one trial (either the first or second), with the alternate trial serving as control. Rectus femoris sEMG and isometric maximum knee extension torque (ISMET) were recorded.ResultsAt 40% MET, no significant correlation was observed. Without PNF, sEMG root mean square (RMS) and ISMET/body weight (ISMET/BW) showed positive correlations at 60% (r = 0.38, P = 0.095) and negative correlation at 80% MET (r = -0.85, P = 0.003). With PNF, correlations shifted to positive and strengthened with intensity, with significant associations at 60% (r = 0.5, P = 0.014) and 80% MET (r = 0.43, P = 0.044).ConclusionPNF strengthens the correlation between sEMG-derived electrical activity and torque output in post-stroke individuals (notably at moderate-to-high intensities), suggesting its potential for optimizing clinical muscle strength evaluations after central nervous system injury.

articles.title: Molecular Adsorbent Recirculating System Therapy in Severe Amlodipine Overdose: Two Cases and Review of the Literature.
articles.abstract: BackgroundCalcium channel blocker (CCB) overdose is a significant cause of cardiovascular drug overdose-related mortality, with amlodipine emerging as the most frequently implicated agent in serious intoxication. Current management strategies for CCB poisoning include vasopressors, high-dose insulin therapy, and other adjunctive treatments. The unique pharmacodynamic profile of amlodipine can lead to severe and persistent vasoplegic shock that is refractory to conventional therapy. The Molecular Adsorbent Recirculating System (MARS), an albumin dialysis technique capable of removing protein-bound toxins, has been proposed as a potential adjunctive therapy in cases of refractory vasodilatory shock associated with severe amlodipine poisoning.MethodsWe report two cases of severe amlodipine poisoning complicated by refractory vasodilatory shock treated with the Molecular Adsorbent Recirculating System (MARS). A targeted PubMed search was also performed to identify published reports of calcium channel blocker intoxication with severe shock treated with MARS. Only reports describing amlodipine ingestion, either alone or with co-ingested agents, were included.ResultsBoth cases involved severe amlodipine poisoning complicated by refractory vasodilatory shock with multiorgan dysfunction requiring multiple vasopressors, high-dose insulin therapy, mechanical ventilation, and renal replacement therapy. Initiation of MARS was temporally associated with progressive hemodynamic stabilization, including reductions in vasopressor requirements and improvement in lactate levels. In the first case, MARS was successfully continued during prone ventilation for severe acute respiratory distress syndrome. In the second case, persistent cardiopulmonary failure required extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Reinitiation of MARS during ECMO support was associated with improved lactate clearance and reduced vasopressor requirements.ConclusionsSevere amlodipine poisoning can result in profound and persistent vasodilatory shock with multiorgan dysfunction despite multiple conventional and adjunctive therapies. MARS may represent a useful adjunctive therapy in selected cases and can be integrated into complex critical care strategies, including prone ventilation and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.

articles.title: Genetic Spectrum and molecular diagnosis of nystagmus in a spanish paediatric cohort.
articles.abstract: IntroductionNystagmus is a common presenting sign of early onset inherited retinal dystrophies. Identifying a genetic diagnosis for infantile nystagmus syndrome patients is crucial for providing appropriate treatment and genetic counselling. This study aimed to evaluate the genetic findings in paediatric patients with nystagmus assessed between 1st January 2020 and 31st December 2025.MethodsA total of 94 children presenting with nystagmus underwent a detailed ophthalmologic evaluation including electrodiagnostic tests and were referred for genetic testing during the study period. Comprehensive genomic analysis was performed to identify pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants.ResultsOf the 94 patients, 30 (32%) were found to have a pathogenic or likely pathogenic genetic variant. The most frequently implicated genes were PAX6, NDP, TYR, CNGA3, RS1 and FRMD7. These findings reflect the genetic heterogeneity of paediatric nystagmus and underscore the importance of targeted genetic evaluation in affected individuals.ConclusionA significant proportion of children with nystagmus have identifiable genetic causes, with mutations in PAX6, NDP, TYR, CNGA3, RS1 and FRMD7 being the most common in our cohort. Early genetic diagnosis can guide clinical management, inform prognosis, and enable genetic counselling.

articles.title: Response to the Letter to the editor: 'Urban-rural classification and readmission risk estimates in younger adults with ischemic stroke: a secondary analysis'.
Electrical Cardiometry for Non-Invasive Cardiac Output Monitoring in Neonatal and Pediatric Critical Care: A Bayesian Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: ObjectivesTo evaluate the agreement between electrical cardiometry and established reference methods for cardiac output measurement in neonatal and pediatric critical care using Bayesian meta-analysis, while synthesizing evidence on stroke volume bias, prognostic associations, and hemodynamic-guided management.DesignSystematic review and Bayesian hierarchical random-effects meta-analysis conducted according to PRISMA 2020 recommendations.SettingNeonatal and pediatric intensive care units, emergency care settings, and interhospital transport services.Data SourcesMEDLINE via PubMed, Embase, Google Scholar, and ScienceDirect were searched from database inception through March 2026. Reference lists and forward citation tracking were additionally performed to identify eligible studies.Measurements and Main ResultsSix studies including 448 neonates and children met the eligibility criteria. Three method-comparison studies enrolled 223 participants, of which two studies comprising 193 participants and four datasets contributed to the primary Bayesian synthesis. The pooled posterior mean percentage error was 26.9% (95% credible interval [CrI], 24.3%-29.5%), with a 98.3% posterior probability that the true percentage error remained ≤30%. A secondary analysis showed a pooled stroke volume bias of 2.82 mL (95% CrI, 1.71-3.86) and a 99.5% posterior probability that the absolute bias remained <5 mL. Observational evidence associated lower cardiac output with longer mechanical ventilation, while a pilot randomized trial suggested that electrical cardiometry-guided management reduced fluid administration and accelerated vasoactive therapy initiation.ConclusionsPooled evidence indicated a high posterior probability of clinically acceptable agreement between electrical cardiometry and reference methods for cardiac output measurement. Its prognostic and therapeutic value should be confirmed in larger multicenter prospective studies.

articles.title: In vivo biomarkers for limbic-predominant age-related TDP-43 encephalopathy neuropathologic change (LATE-NC): A scoping review of proposed measures.
articles.abstract: BackgroundLimbic-predominant age-related TDP-43 encephalopathy neuropathologic change (LATE-NC) is a common cause of late-life amnestic dementia that mimics Alzheimer's disease but lacks a validated in vivo biomarker.ObjectiveThe authors sought to map the in vivo biomarker candidates for LATE-NC, characterize the type and quality of evidence for each, highlight their validation against postmortem TDP-43 staging and map their performance in both pure LATE-NC and mixed pathology.MethodsFive databases were searched (PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Scopus). Eligible studies investigated in vivo biomarkers for LATE-NC in adults with mean age above 65. Two reviewers independently screened all records; a third adjudicated disagreements. Data were extracted across 24 fields and synthesized narratively.Results43 studies covering structural MRI (19), FDG-PET (8), plasma (7), diffusion MRI (4), multimodal MRI (1), CSF (2), TDP-43 PET (1), and linguistic markers (1) were reviewed. The most replicated signal was medial temporal lobe atrophy and hypometabolism. Several studies framed their candidate as a diagnostic validation against autopsy; yet only three reported formal performance metrics with stated cut-off values. A handful of studies (12%) tested in an independent cohort and the corpus contains only one study from outside North America and Europe (Japan).ConclusionsImaging evidence is well-anchored but mostly exploratory or surrogate validated at this stage. Plasma TDP-43 elevation is consistent but no commercial assay has a validated cut-point. Clinical translation requires external validation, cut-point-anchored diagnostic accuracy, and cohort diversification.

articles.title: Serum 25(OH)D and diabetes risk in adults with prediabetes: evidence, potential mechanisms, and implications.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract: Correcting vitamin D deficiency to reach 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels in the replete range (≥ 20 ng/mL, as defined by the National Academy of Medicine) improves insulin secretion and sensitivity. Emerging evidence indicates that vitamin D may have a more extensive role in reducing risk of type 2 diabetes in selected adults with prediabetes. Specifically, vitamin D supplementation at doses sufficient to achieve 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels ≥ 40 ng/ml appears to confer additional benefit in reducing diabetes risk in subsets of the population with prediabetes. Herein we review evidence that achieving relatively high 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels may lower risk of progression to type 2 diabetes in selected vitamin D-replete adults with prediabetes. We consider potential mechanisms by which this may occur. We also discuss the potential benefits and risks of high-dose vitamin D supplementation across subgroups defined by genetic profile, age, and the presence of additional comorbidities. These findings indicate a potential role for a precision nutrition approach with high-dose vitamin D supplementation to lower risk of type 2 diabetes in adults with prediabetes.

articles.title: An ideal suspect: atrial flutter unmasked by implantable cardioverter defibrillator interrogation.
Determinants and mechanisms of fatigue in older adult patients with stroke: A structural equation modeling approach.
articles.journal: Journal of back and musculoskeletal rehabilitation
articles.abstract: BackgroundThis study aimed to explore the determinants and pathways of fatigue in older adult patients with stroke, drawing upon the theory of unpleasant symptoms, to inform clinical interventions.MethodsA convenience sampling method was used to recruit 234 older adult patients with stroke between July 2024 and January 2025. Data were collected using the Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory, Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, Social Support Rating Scale, and Stroke Specific Quality of Life Scale. Statistical analysis was conducted using R software (version 4.4.3), and a structural equation model was constructed. The mediating effect was evaluated using the Bootstrap method.ResultsFatigue levels were significantly higher in patients with greater anxiety, depression, poorer sleep quality, and higher C-reactive protein (CRP) levels, and in those with lower education level and poorer stroke-specific quality of life (all p < 0.05). The structural equation model demonstrated a good fit (CFI = 1.000, RMSEA = 0.000). Anxiety, depression, and sleep quality were identified as complete mediators between education level, social support, CRP levels, and fatigue. The mediating effect accounted for 70.1 of the total effect, indicating that anxiety, depression, and sleep quality collectively explain most of the association between sociodemographic, psychosocial, and inflammatory factors and fatigue in this population.ConclusionFatigue among older adult patients with stroke is influenced by multiple interrelated factors, with anxiety, depression, and sleep quality acting as key mediators. These findings support routine screening and targeted management of psychological distress and sleep problems to mitigate fatigue during stroke rehabilitation.

articles.title: Data quality and discharge-time readmission risk in diabetes hospitalisations.
articles.journal: Health information management : journal of the Health Information Management Association of Australia
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Electronic health record (EHR) and administrative data are widely reused for readmission modelling, but models may learn from documentation completeness, coding pathways and measurement availability as well as from clinical status.

OBJECTIVE: This study assessed how documentation completeness, administrative fields and interpretable clinical predictors shaped discharge-time 30-day readmission risk stratification among hospitalised patients with diabetes.

METHOD: A retrospective secondary analysis of the public Diabetes 130-US hospitals for years 1999-2008 dataset was conducted. Encounters with death or hospice-related discharge dispositions were excluded. The outcome was 30-day readmission. Four calibrated logistic regression models compared core clinical variables, administrative fields and missingness indicators under a discharge-time prediction frame. Uncertainty was estimated using patient-level clustered bootstrap resampling.

RESULTS: The cohort included 99,343 encounters from 69,990 patient identifiers; 11,314 encounters (11.4%) had 30-day readmission. Weight, maximum glucose serum, A1C result, medical specialty and payer code were missing or not recorded in 96.9%, 94.8%, 83.1%, 48.9% and 39.7% of encounters, respectively. Adding administrative fields increased the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) from 0.640 to 0.667 (ΔAUROC 0.0266, 95% clustered bootstrap confidence interval (CI) 0.0178 to 0.0347). Missingness indicators alone produced little change (ΔAUROC 0.0019, 95% CI -0.0007 to 0.0046). The full model containing administrative fields and missingness indicators showed similar discrimination (AUROC 0.666).

CONCLUSION: The modest performance gain was driven mainly by administrative coding and discharge-pathway variables. EHR readmission studies should define prediction timing, report measurement availability and interpret model performance as a product of clinical data generation as well as clinical risk.Implications for health information management practice:Secondary-use EHR modelling should profile variable availability, establish predictor timing and provenance, test administrative-field contributions and report calibrated performance before local use.

articles.title: NNMT Safeguards Vascular Aging by Modulating an Endothelial LMNA-HSP Stress-Response Axis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: NNMT (nicotinamide N-methyltransferase) is a pivotal metabolic-epigenetic integrator that regulates cellular methylation balance. Although its expression and function exhibit profound, context-dependent heterogeneity in metabolic diseases and cancer, its role within the vascular system, particularly in aging endothelial cells, remains elusive.

METHODS: We examined NNMT expression in a small, pathological, male-only cohort of older versus younger plaque-adjacent human carotid intimal donors, primary mouse aortic endothelial cells, and senescent human umbilical vein endothelial cells. Using endothelial-targeted adeno-associated virus-Tie systems, we assessed the effects of NNMT restoration and knockdown on vasodilation and arterial stiffness in aged mice. Mechanistic insights were obtained through exploratory multiomics integration.

RESULTS: We established that NNMT expression exhibits an exploratory inverse association in a small, pathological, male-only cohort of older versus younger plaque-adjacent human carotid intimal donors, a pattern mirrored by declines observed in primary mouse aortic endothelial cells and senescent human umbilical vein endothelial cells. Functional assays demonstrated that NNMT restoration improves vasodilation and arterial stiffness in aged mice, whereas knockdown exacerbates these deficits. Mechanistically, exploratory multiomics integration, including Cleavage Under Targets and Tagmentation and transcriptomic analyses, suggests that NNMT-associated reduction in histone H3 lysine 27 trimethylation occupancy at the LMNA (lamin A/C) promoter correlates with its transcriptional maintenance, a process influenced by S-adenosylmethionine supplementation. Downstream, we identified that NNMT-induced LMNA stabilization operates in concert with HSF1 (heat shock transcription factor 1) activation and nuclear translocation, a process accompanied by enhanced binding to HSP90 and HSP70 promoters to drive their transcription. Furthermore, we demonstrated that the vascular protective effects of the natural compound Heterophyllin B are mediated, at least in part, by NNMT, as these benefits were partially attenuated after endothelial NNMT knockdown in vivo.

CONCLUSIONS: We identify a protective, age-dependent role for NNMT in vascular endothelium. Our findings reveal that NNMT maintains endothelial homeostasis through coordinated regulation of nuclear LMNA and the downstream HSP (heat shock protein) stress response, highlighting the therapeutic potential of this pathway for addressing age-related endothelial dysfunction.

articles.title: Mapping the Metabolic Penumbra From Standard CT Perfusion: CTP-Derived CMRO2/OEF Estimates Versus CBF/Tmax.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: CT perfusion (CTP) hemodynamic thresholds may overestimate the ischemic core (ghost core) in early presenters. We hypothesized that a metabolic model, defining the core by decreased cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen and penumbra by increased oxygen extraction fraction, estimated from standard CTP, would better predict tissue fate and early neurological outcome.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study (October 2015 to October 2025) included consecutive thrombectomy-treated patients with anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion, admission CTP, and 48±12-hour diffusion-weighted imaging. Predefined relative cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen and oxygen extraction fraction thresholds (metabolic model) were compared with relative cerebral blood flow ≤30% and time-to-maximum (Tmax) ≥6 seconds (hemodynamic model) against diffusion-weighted imaging. Each imaging model (core and penumbra volumes) was added to clinical covariates predicting 48-hour lesion volume (linear regression) and 24-hour and discharge National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (ANCOVA), tested by nested F-tests; imaging models were compared by paired bootstrap of cross-validated R2.

RESULTS: Of 3011 thrombectomy patients, 227 were included (median age, 70 years; 46% male; median onset-to-CTP, 108 minutes; 162 recanalized). Relative cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen ≤30% reduced core overestimation versus relative cerebral blood flow ≤30% (bias, +2.6 versus +20.0 mL; dice, 0.20 versus 0.18; both P<0.001; reproduced in temporal validation), but >10-mL underestimation was more frequent (17% versus 6%). Relative cerebral blood flow error decreased with onset-to-recanalization delay (ρ=-0.30), unlike relative cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (ρ=0.01). In 65 nonrecanalized patients, relative oxygen extraction fraction ≥125% outperformed time-to-maximum on bias (+14.3 versus +19.3 mL; P<0.001) and dice (P=0.002), but not absolute error (P=0.24). The metabolic model better explained 48-hour lesion volume (cross-validated R2, 0.32 versus 0.22; P=0.002). Only the metabolic model improved 24-hour (P=0.004) and discharge (P=0.009) National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score prediction over clinical covariates, outperforming the hemodynamic model at discharge (P=0.04) but not at 24 hours (P=0.21).

CONCLUSIONS: A CTP-derived metabolic model reduced ghost-core misclassification, particularly in early presenters, and better explained 48-hour lesion volume than hemodynamic thresholds, with modest added value for early neurological outcome. Positron emission tomography and external validation are warranted.

articles.title: Diuretic Response in Acute Heart Failure: Prediction vs Direct Measurement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Limited data are available informing the variability and ability to predict diuretic response (DR) longitudinally during decongestion in acute heart failure (AHF).

METHODS: The FASTR pilot trial compared the Reprieve System (n=52) to optimal diuretic therapy control (ODT) (n=44). The ability to longitudinally predict DR, quantified as urine output over the 72-hour intervention, was evaluated in the overall population using baseline characteristics. In the Reprieve arm, directly measured DR during the initial dose finding algorithm was also used to predict longitudinal DR.

RESULTS: Baseline characteristics predicted only 24.7% (p<0.001) of the variance in DR over the course of IV diuretic therapy. As the duration of diuretic therapy increased, DR prediction worsened with no relationship to DR after 18 hours (p≥0.097). Directly measured DR strongly predicted subsequent urine output early (e.g., predicting 84.5% in the variance of the subsequent hour DR, p<0.001). However, this also decreased over time with modest correlation with DR at 24 hours (variance 12.7%; p=0.008) and no correlation after 48 hours (p=0.79). In the Reprieve group, serial DR measurement and diuretic titration occurred in 89% of patients eligible for further diuretic titration resulting in stable therapeutic DR over the study period despite the changes in DR over time.

CONCLUSIONS: Accurately predicting longitudinal DR using baseline characteristics or a single direct measurement of DR is challenging as DR changes rapidly during decongestion. Due to the dynamic nature of DR over therapy, serial assessment and diuretic titration is required to longitudinally achieve therapeutic DR in most AHF patients.

articles.title: Sex-Specific Molecular Patterns Reveal Distinct Age-Associated Arterial Wall Remodeling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease is highly prevalent among elderly patients and often requires revascularization through coronary artery bypass grafting. Women typically undergo coronary artery bypass grafting at older ages than men and experience worse outcomes, disparities that persist even after adjustment for age and clinical variables, suggesting that elderly women face unique biological vulnerabilities not captured by traditional risk factors. This study investigated sex-specific molecular patterns associated with distinct age-associated arterial wall remodeling in patients with coronary artery disease.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, internal thoracic artery specimens were obtained between July 2022 and August 2023 from 135 patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (88 males and 47 females; mean age, 66.3 years). Patients were stratified by age (<65 versus ≥65 years) and sex. Structural remodeling was assessed histologically, and transcriptomic profiles were characterized using whole transcriptome sequencing, followed by pathway-level bioinformatic analyses and targeted quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction validation.

RESULTS: Elderly patients exhibited distinct patterns of intimal hyperplasia: internal thoracic arteries from elderly males showed thicker intimal layers, whereas those from elderly females demonstrated medial thinning, with a significant age-by-sex interaction for medial thickness (P=0.017). Transcriptomic profiling revealed age-associated enrichment of lipid metabolism-related pathways, with upregulation of ADIPOQ, LPL, and FABP4 in elderly patients of both sexes. Divergent molecular patterns were identified beyond this shared age-associated profile. Males showed a proliferative pattern associated with immune suppression and lower EGR1 expression, whereas females exhibited a pattern consistent with impaired structural integrity, accompanied by upregulation of stress-response genes (JUN and JUNB) and reduced expression of the extracellular matrix gene FN1.

CONCLUSIONS: Internal thoracic arteries from elderly patients with coronary artery disease exhibit distinct sex-specific arterial wall remodeling patterns, with immune-suppressed proliferative remodeling in males and stress-associated extracellular matrix vulnerability in females. These findings provide a biological framework for understanding sex differences in age-associated arterial remodeling and may provide context for sex disparities in cardiovascular outcomes.

articles.title: Therapeutically Targetable Th17-Derived miR-721 Drives Autoimmune Myocarditis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocarditis is an inflammatory cardiac disease in which T helper 17 (Th17) cell-driven immune responses contribute to progression toward dilated cardiomyopathy and heart failure. Current therapies mainly rely on corticosteroids but lack specificity, while the role of miR-721, synthesized by Th17 cells, remains largely unexplored in disease pathogenesis.

METHODS: We characterized the presence of mmu-miR-721 and its human homolog hsa-RNA-Chr8:96 in extracellular vesicles secreted by Th17 cells from IL-17 (interleukin-17) eGFP mice with experimental autoimmune myocarditis and from patients with myocarditis. MxCre±Ppargfl/fl mice and luciferase reporter assays were used to validate the target genes of miR-721 and hsa-RNA-Chr8:96, respectively. The functional role of miR-721 in experimental autoimmune myocarditis was investigated using lentiviral vectors overexpression and miRNA sponge molecules for inhibition. Th17 responses and heart inflammation were assessed, and echocardiography was performed after in vivo blockade of mmu-miR-721 in experimental autoimmune myocarditis mice.

RESULTS: Both mmu-miR-721 and hsa-RNA-Chr8:96 were encapsulated in extracellular vesicles and secreted by Th17 cells of mice and patients with myocarditis. Overexpression of mmu-miR-721 in draining lymph node cells from experimental autoimmune myocarditis mice promoted Th17 differentiation via Pparg inhibition and increased RORγt and IL-17 expression. In contrast, no differences in RORγt expression were observed in the absence of Pparg, a target of miR-721, indicating that miR-721 promotes Th17 responses through Pparg repression. In addition, human PPARG was validated as a target gene of hsa-RNA-Chr8:96, as its overexpression in peripheral blood leukocytes downregulated PPARG mRNA levels, suggesting that similar pathways are involved in human pathology. Finally, in vivo blockade of mmu-miR-721 increased Pparg expression, reducing RORγt and IL-17 activation in T cells, leading to decreased leukocyte infiltration in the heart and improved cardiac function thereby ameliorating disease progression.

CONCLUSIONS: miR-721 is released by Th17 cells in extracellular vesicles and promotes Th17 responses during myocarditis through repression of PPARγ, identifying this miRNA as both a mechanistic driver of disease and a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Bilberry (Vaccinium myrtillus L.) extract alleviates insulin resistance in gestational diabetes mellitus by modulating the AKT/LRRFIP1/GLUT4 pathway in skeletal muscle.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is characterized by progressive insulin resistance (IR), with skeletal muscle representing a primary site of this pathology. This study investigated the potential of anthocyanin-rich bilberry (Vaccinium myrtillus L.) extract (VME) to ameliorate skeletal muscle IR in a high-fat diet (HFD) induced rat model of GDM. We integrated proteomics and bioinformatics approaches to elucidate the underlying mechanisms.UHPLC-MS/MS analysis identified cyanidin-3-O-galactoside (C3Gal) as the principal anthocyanin constituent of VME. Daily oral administration of VME (400 mg per kg bw) during pregnancy ameliorated hyperglycemia, IR, and dyslipidemia, and improved oral glucose tolerance in GDM rats. Proteomic analysis of gastrocnemius muscle identified VME associated differentially expressed proteins as candidate targets for further investigation. Gene set enrichment analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis implicated AKT signaling and highlighted Lrrfip1 as a hub gene correlated with HOMA-IR. Cross-species comparison with human type 2 diabetes skeletal muscle transcriptomes (GSE55650, GSE7014) supported target prioritization, with LRRFIP1 showing concordant regulation at both mRNA and protein levels. Molecular docking predicted binding of C3Gal to AKT and LRRFIP1, and a cellular thermal shift assay supported cellular target engagement of C3Gal with these proteins. C3Gal restored p-AKT and GLUT4 levels both in vivo and in palmitate-induced C2C12 myotubes. siRNA mediated knockdown of Lrrfip1 attenuated these effects, whereas pharmacological inhibition of AKT abolished them. Collectively, these findings support LRRFIP1 as a downstream mediator of AKT associated GLUT4 regulation. Together, our data propose LRRFIP1 as a candidate molecular target associated with skeletal muscle IR and support further investigation of VME as a potential dietary intervention for GDM associated IR.

articles.title: Cumulative Genetic Burden Defines a Gradient of Risk in MYBPC3-Related Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: MYBPC3 truncating variants (MYBPC3tv) represent the most common genetic substrate in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, yet carriers show substantial phenotypic variability despite a shared mechanism of haploinsufficiency. The contribution of additional genetic variants to this variability remains incompletely defined.

METHODS: We analyzed 11 991 unrelated hypertrophic cardiomyopathy probands undergoing clinical genetic testing. Analyses focused on MYBPC3tv carriers stratified by additional intermediate-effect variants (IEVs) or second monogenic variants. IEVs were further classified as sarcomeric or nonsarcomeric. All probands were genetically characterized at a single center using standardized sequencing protocols, with uniform ascertainment of IEVs throughout the study period. Primary outcomes included age-related penetrance, maximal left ventricular wall thickness, and major adverse cardiovascular events; independent predictors were assessed by a multivariable Cox regression model.

RESULTS: Among 2767 genotype-positive probands, MYBPC3 accounted for 47.6% of cases, with truncating variants representing 81.9% of MYBPC3-positive individuals. Within MYBPC3tv carriers, additional variants were associated with a stepwise gradient of disease severity. Median age at diagnosis decreased from 48 years in isolated carriers to 42 years in MYBPC3tv+IEV and 28 years in double-monogenic carriers, whereas mean wall thickness increased from 21.3 to 24.1 and 26.3 mm, respectively. In multivariable analyses, cumulative genetic burden remained an independent predictor of major adverse cardiovascular event. Sarcomeric IEV carriers (hazard ratio, 10.3 [95% CI, 2.3-28.7]) and biallelic MYBPC3 carriers (hazard ratio, 23.2 [95% CI, 5.3-115.0]) exhibited the highest risk, although estimates in these subgroups should be interpreted cautiously given the limited number of events. All biallelic MYBPC3 carriers were diagnosed in childhood.

CONCLUSIONS: Cumulative rare variant burden explains a subset of the phenotypic heterogeneity among MYBPC3tv carriers, defining a hierarchical gradient of disease expression. Intermediate-effect alleles and second monogenic variants, particularly biallelic MYBPC3, identify higher-risk subgroups that may benefit from intensified surveillance, individualized management, and guided therapies.

articles.title: Efficacy of Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation in Preventing Poststroke Spasticity: A Sham-Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Poststroke spasticity significantly impairs recovery, yet preventive strategies remain limited. This study evaluated the effectiveness of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) in reducing the development and severity of spasticity in patients with early subacute stroke, offering a possible early intervention.

METHODS: In this double-blind, randomized, sham-controlled trial, 70 patients with early subacute stroke (7-30 days) were randomized to receive 3 sessions of low-frequency (1 Hz, 1000 pulses at 90% resting motor threshold) rTMS over contralesional primary motor cortex (n=35) or sham stimulation (n=35), alongside standard care. The primary outcome was upper-limb spasticity assessed using the modified Modified Ashworth Scale. Secondary outcomes included handgrip strength, muscle power assessed by the Medical Research Council scale, pain assessed by the Visual Analogue Scale, modified Rankin Scale, and Stroke Impact Scale 3.0.

RESULTS: rTMS therapy significantly lowered spasticity scores at 1 and 3 months across all assessed upper-limb joints (P=0.001), improved handgrip strength (P=0.01), and prevented pain (P=0.001). Stroke Impact Scale scores at 1 month showed greater gains in activities of daily living, mobility, hand function, social participation, and recovery in the rTMS group (P=0.001). Functional independence (modified Rankin Scale) was significantly better in the rTMS group (P=0.006) at 3 months. On binary logistic regression, sham stimulation was associated with greater odds of developing spasticity at 1 month (shoulder odds ratio [OR], 8.29 [95% CI, 1.95-35.27], P=0.04; elbow OR, 7.62 [95% CI, 1.69-34.35], P=0.08; wrist OR, 5.18 [95% CI, 1.60-16.78], P=0.06). At 3 months, sham stimulation remained predictive, with higher odds of spasticity at the shoulder (OR, 15.3 [95% CI, 8.26-28.43]), elbow (OR, 13.43 [95% CI, 3.94-45.78]), wrist (OR, 19.9 [95% CI, 4.9-80.96]), and fingers (OR, 26.25 [95% CI, 5.19-132.87], all P=0.001). Minor adverse events like headache and light-headedness were observed in 5 patients.

CONCLUSIONS: Low-frequency rTMS over contralesional primary motor cortex significantly prevented spasticity, improved motor recovery, reduced pain, improved functional outcomes and quality of life in early subacute stroke, supporting its role as a promising adjunctive therapy in early stroke rehabilitation.
