articles.title: Proteomics and Risk of Incident Ischemic Stroke: Meta-Analysis of the ARIC Study and CHS.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke preventive therapies have been slow to emerge due to a limited understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms. We aimed to discover new protein risk factors that are potential etiologic factors and may be candidates for therapeutic intervention.

METHODS: We included ARIC study (Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities) and CHS (Cardiovascular Health Study) participants without prevalent stroke at the time of proteomic profiling (1990-1992 in ARIC and 1992-1993 in CHS). Relative concentrations of proteins in blood were assessed with aptamers (n=4954). Ischemic stroke events were adjudicated through 2019 in ARIC and 2015 in CHS. Study-specific Cox regression adjusting for ischemic stroke risk factors was used to estimate associations between proteins and incident ischemic stroke. Study-specific estimates were combined using fixed-effects meta-analysis. Replication was conducted in 2 independent cohorts (AGES-Reykjavik, UK Biobank). Proteins with a false discovery rate q value <0.05 were considered replicated. Mendelian randomization analyses assessed for potential causal associations between proteins and ischemic stroke.

RESULTS: Median follow-up was 25 and 12 years in ARIC and CHS. 1397 out of 14 139 (10%) participants experienced an ischemic stroke. 44 proteins were significantly associated with ischemic stroke risk (P<1.0×10-5), of which 26 are novel. In 2 independent cohorts, 37 (84%) associations were directionally concordant, and 26 (59%) met criteria for replication. Mendelian randomization analyses suggested MMP12 (matrix metallopeptidase-12) and CNTN1 (contactin-1) may be causally related to ischemic stroke risk. In multivariable Mendelian randomization analyses, higher MMP12 levels had a direct protective effect on ischemic stroke risk, while CNTN1 had a direct harmful effect.

CONCLUSIONS: This proteomic and genomic investigation of ischemic stroke identified novel risk biomarkers and 2 potential etiologic CNTN1 factors that are regulated in response to atherosclerosis and obesity. If future studies confirm our findings, these results may have implications for the development of new preventive therapies.

articles.title: Mosaic ageing: from organ-specific decline to the cause of death.
articles.journal: Philosophical transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series B, Biological sciences
articles.abstract: Ageing is often framed as a systemic, uniform process. However, growing evidence shows that ageing occurs unevenly across cell types, tissues and organs, generating heterogeneous within-individual trajectories. This mosaic perspective highlights the myriad cross-tissue ageing patterns that emerge from interactions among development, the genome and environmental and lifestyle exposures. The way these uneven trajectories play out may determine the emergence of specific ageing-related diseases and ultimately the cause of death. Here, we combine insights from molecular biology, biogerontology and evolutionary ecophysiology to develop an integrative view of mosaic ageing. We first describe the proximate mechanisms underlying organ-specific ageing variation. These mechanisms are moulded through age-specific natural selection, embodying trade-offs between maintenance, function and fitness. We then review tools for quantifying organ-specific ageing, ranging from classical measures such as telomere dynamics to high-resolution approaches including epigenetic, proteomic and multi-omic clocks, single-cell atlases and longitudinal imaging. Finally, we discuss how combining these tools with causal inference methods can help identify drivers of context- and species-dependent senescence and life-history variation and enable organ-targeted biomedical interventions. Overall, this perspective calls for moving beyond systemic models of ageing towards an integrative framework that places heterogeneous organ-specific processes at the centre of ageing research. This article is part of the theme issue 'Developmental circuits in ageing'.

articles.title: Early-life reproductive success predicts lifespan: intrinsic quality, not reproductive trade-offs, explains heterogeneity in a short-lived vertebrate.
articles.journal: Philosophical transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series B, Biological sciences
articles.abstract: Individuals of the same species often display extensive lifespan heterogeneity. However, the factors underlying such heterogeneity remain largely elusive. Here, we examined whether lifespan variation in the naturally short-lived turquoise killifish (Nothobranchius furzeri), an annual teleost with a limited reproductive window, is caused by reproductive trade-offs. To examine the individual covariation in reproduction and lifespan, we focused on males and performed in vitro fertilization using ejaculates collected longitudinally throughout life. We found that lifespan and reproduction do not trade off: early-life reproductive success positively predicts male lifespan and reflects intrinsic quality (IQ). A causal model, where IQ affects both survival and reproduction, recapitulates the empirical patterns. Together, our results show inter-individual variation in IQ explains lifespan heterogeneity in a short-lived vertebrate, challenging the view that reproductive costs drive inter-individual lifespan variation. This article is part of the theme issue 'Developmental circuits in ageing'.

articles.title: Response to Comment on: "Carbon footprint of direct oral anticoagulants in atrial fibrillation and venous thromboembolism".
Prognostic value of right atrial pressure to cardiac output slope in patients undergoing exercise right heart catheterization.
authors: PEX-NET (Pulmonary Haemodynamics during Exercise Network) ERS Clinical Research Collaboration
articles.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of the right atrial pressure to cardiac output relationship (RAP/CO-slope) from rest to end exercise in patients undergoing exercise right heart catheterization for suspected or confirmed pulmonary hypertension (PH).

METHODS: The analysis used data from the retrospective arm of the Pulmonary Hemodynamics during Exercise Network (PEX NET), a multicenter collaboration involving 23 PH centers. Patients were included if resting and exercise measurements were obtained in the same body position and if RAP/CO-slopes were available. Cox proportional hazard models adjusted for age, sex, and hemoglobin were applied. Time dependent ROC curves were used to identify a prognostic cut off.

RESULTS: A total of 856 patients were included (median age 59 years; 67% female), of whom 336 had PH. Over a median follow up of 6.5 years, 114 patients (13%) died. Higher RAP/CO-slopes were independently associated with increased mortality, even after adjusting for established resting and exercise hemodynamics (hazard ratio 1.08, 95%CI: 1.03-1.13, p < 0.001). Among patients with manifest PH at rest, a RAP/CO-slope ≥1.0 mmHg·min·L⁻¹ was linked to a 2.2 fold higher mortality risk (hazard ratio: 2.20; 95% CI: 1.1-4.5; p = 0.032) compared with slopes <1.0 mmHg·min·L⁻¹. In a multivariable model including NT proBNP, 6 minute walking distance, and WHO functional class, the RAP/CO-slope remained the strongest predictor of mortality.

CONCLUSION: The RAP/CO-slope is a strong, independent prognostic marker across a spectrum of RV afterload stress. A RAP/CO slope ≥1 mmHg·min·L⁻¹ was identified as particularly predictive in manifest PH.

articles.title: Combination targeted therapy with Janus kinase inhibition plus biologic agents in refractory JIA: an international multi-centre case series.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe multi-centre real-world experience of combination targeted therapy (CTT) using a Janus kinase inhibitor (JAKi) and biologic in juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA).

METHODS: Paediatric rheumatology centres across the United Kingdom and Republic of Ireland with experience of JAKi-biologic CTT use in JIA were identified. Written patient consent and local approval was obtained.Data on patient characteristics, treatment history, adverse events, and disease activity were collected by retrospective review of medical records. Paired data were analysed using Wilcoxon signed-rank test.

RESULTS: 13 patients with JIA were identified (11 Still's disease/systemic; 1 psoriatic; 1 extended oligoarticular) across nine centres. Historical joint damage (39%) and glucocorticoid toxicity (77%) were common.Median 5 conventional/biologic/targeted synthetic DMARDs (IQR 4-7) were used over a median 66 months (IQR 36-133) before CTT initiation at median age 12 years (IQR 9-14). Tofacitinib-tocilizumab was the most frequent combination.CTT was used briefly as bridging therapy in 2/13, with 11/13 remaining on CTT for ≥12 months, permitting paired analysis at 12 months. A significant reduction in 12-month intravenous methylprednisolone exposure (median 109mg/kg vs. 0mg/kg; p=0.013) and active joint count (median 5 vs. 2 joints; p=0.009) was seen. At last follow-up (median 21.5 months), 6/10 still on CTT had inactive disease, with 8/10 off systemic steroids.No serious infections occurred. Two non-infectious serious adverse events were reported; hip avascular necrosis and pulmonary alveolar proteinosis.

CONCLUSION: JAKi-biologic CTT may have a role in improving disease control in refractory JIA, enabling some reduction in glucocorticoids, with no serious infections reported.

articles.title: Contribution of risk factors to racial/ethnic disparities in tuberculosis among US-born persons.
articles.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: In the United States, tuberculosis (TB) incidence rates are substantially higher among racial/ethnic minorities compared with non-Hispanic White persons. However, few analyses have investigated the mechanisms driving these disparities.

OBJECTIVES: To assess the contribution of geographic factors and individual TB risk factors to racial/ethnic disparities in TB incidence among U.S.-born individuals.

METHODS: We analyzed TB case data for 2012-2019 from the National Tuberculosis Surveillance System, stratified by race/ethnicity, age, sex, and Public Use Microdata Area (PUMA). Age-sex standardized incidence rate ratios (IRRs) were calculated to quantify disparities across racial/ethnic groups. We decomposed these IRRs to quantify the contribution of differences within and between PUMAs to overall disparities. We also estimated the contributions of racial/ethnic differences in the prevalence of established TB risk factors-diagnosed diabetes, current smoking, HIV infection, and excess alcohol use-to TB disparities.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Non-Hispanic American Indian or Alaska Native and non-Hispanic Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander persons had the highest TB incidence rates compared to non-Hispanic White persons (IRR: 15.3 (95% CI: 12.5, 18.6) and 18.1 (12.3, 26.2) respectively). Within-PUMA TB incidence differences accounted for most of the differences in incidence by race/ethnicity, representing 52-96% of total IRRs for each racial/ethnic population. Racial/ethnic differences in the prevalence of individual risk factors had minimal impact on total TB incidence disparities.

CONCLUSIONS: Eliminating racial/ethnic disparities in TB will require more than addressing individual risk factors. Combatting structural or community-level determinants of TB, including treating infection to prevent disease, will be important for accelerating TB elimination.

articles.title: Multiparametric ultrasound characterizes pediatric cystic fibrosis hepatobiliary involvement.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The contemporary European Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition (ESPGHAN)/North American Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition (NASPGHAN) framework broadens the definition of cystic fibrosis hepatobiliary involvement (CFHBI), but the biological interpretation of individual multiparametric ultrasound parameters within this framework remains unclear. We evaluated the biological associations of shear wave elastography (SWE), shear wave dispersion (SWD), and attenuation imaging (ATI) with histopathological phenotypes in children with cystic fibrosis (CF).

METHODS: In this ambispective cohort study, 119 children with CF underwent hepatobiliary assessment, including SWE, SWD, ATI, Doppler ultrasonography, clinical and laboratory evaluation. Histopathological assessment was performed when clinically indicated. CFHBI was classified according to the ESPGHAN/NASPGHAN framework, with the Debray criteria used as a secondary exploratory comparison. Exploratory phenotype-oriented analyses evaluated ultrasound parameters according to corresponding histopathological phenotypes.

RESULTS: Exploratory phenotype-oriented analyses demonstrated significantly higher ATI values in histopathologically defined steatosis (p < 0.001), with good discriminatory performance (AUC 0.813) and an optimal threshold of 0.655 dB/cm/MHz. In contrast, SWE was not associated with histopathologically defined fibrosis (p = 0.151), whereas SWD showed no significant phenotype-specific associations. Secondary exploratory analyses demonstrated significant overall CFHBI discrimination by all three ultrasound parameters, with the highest AUC observed for SWD. The ESPGHAN/NASPGHAN and Debray classifications demonstrated significant disagreement (McNemar p < 0.001), with 22.7% of patients classified as Debray-negative but ESPGHAN/NASPGHAN-positive.

CONCLUSIONS: Multiparametric ultrasound should be interpreted within the contemporary ESPGHAN/NASPGHAN CFHBI framework rather than as a single diagnostic tool for hepatobiliary involvement. The distinct biological associations of SWE, ATI, and SWD support a phenotype-oriented interpretation of individual ultrasound parameters, whereas overall CFHBI discrimination should be interpreted as a secondary exploratory finding requiring prospective multicenter validation.

articles.title: Maternal mean arterial pressure and serum inhibin A as early predictors of hypertensive disorders in low-risk pregnant women attending a University Teaching Hospital in Lagos, Nigeria: A prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluates the role of maternal mean arterial pressure (MAP) and serum inhibin-A level as early predictors of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) among low-risk pregnant women attending a University Teaching Hospital in Lagos, Nigeria.

METHODS: This was a prospective cohort study of 254 consecutively consenting, low-risk, normotensive, and non-proteinuric pregnant women at 13-19 weeks of gestation. Receiver operating characteristics (ROC) curves and validity tests were used to determine the performance of serum levels of inhibin A, MAP, and a combination of both in predicting HDP (gestational hypertension and preeclampsia).

RESULTS: The mean age and parity of the participants was 30.3 ± 4.9 years and 1 (0-2), respectively. The area under the ROC curves of serum inhibin A (0.9981, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.9946-1.000) was higher than for MAP (0.7531, 95% CI 0.6641-0.8421), in predicting the composite endpoint of HDP. The optimum cut-offs for predicting HDP as calculated from Youden's index were 476.8 pg/mL (sensitivity = 100% and specificity = 98.7%) for serum inhibin A and 81.3 mm Hg (sensitivity = 100% and specificity = 50.1%) for MAP. There was no statistically significant difference between the combined predictive ability of inhibin A and MAP compared to that of serum inhibin A alone for predicting HDP (AUC of 0.9984 vs. 09981, P-value = 0.7259.

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrated that serum inhibin A alone and MAP have good and moderate performance, respectively, in predicting HDP in the low-risk cohort of Nigerian pregnant women. The combination of serum inhibin A and MAP has a similar predictive performance as serum inhibin A alone.

articles.title: How to use Quality Improvement to enhance the portfolio for promotion and tenure in Academic Pulmonary, Critical Care and Sleep Medicine.
articles.abstract: Quality Improvement (QI) is a cornerstone for improving patient care and health care systems. However, QI activities are not always recognized within traditional promotion and tenure (P&T) pathways. As a result, faculty with significant QI expertise and impactful contributions may lack clear mechanisms and pathways for academic recognition, promotion, and career advancement. Identifying a clear QI P&T pathway may incentivize faculty to pursue QI as a career. Standardized approaches that translate QI activities into key conventional academic metrics and are documented across multiple domains for P&T are needed to address these gaps. The purpose of this manuscript is to provide a framework for Pulmonary, Critical Care and Sleep Medicine faculty to align QI work with traditional promotion criteria and encourage institutions to recognize the value and scope of QI in P&T considerations. This framework highlights strategies for documenting QI contributions across academic areas such as clinical care, education, research and service and supports faculty considering the value of pursuing an academic career in QI in Pulmonary, Critical Care and Sleep medicine.

articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine

articles.title: Research on the relationship between intelligent diagnosis of diabetes retinopathy and biomarkers based on multimodal data fusion.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: To explore the risk factors of diabetic retinopathy (DR) in type 2 diabetes (T2DM) patients, construct a multimodal deep neural network model based on clinical risk score and fundus image characteristics, and verify the expression changes of key proteins in DR rat models, so as to provide a new method for early diagnosis and grading evaluation of DR.

METHOD: Pathological changes such as increased retinal tissue thickness and disordered cell arrangement were observed, and SPP1, TMEM173, and Circp protein expression were significantly upregulated (p < 0.05).

RESULT: The multimodal deep neural network model that integrates clinical risk scores with fundus imaging features can significantly improve the accuracy and discrimination of DR grading diagnosis, and has good generalisation ability.

CONCLUSION: The DR rat model exhibits significant inflammatory response, oxidative stress, and abnormal angiogenesis, with upregulation of SPP1, TMEM173, and Circp protein expression, which may be involved in the pathogenesis of DR.

articles.title: Beyond Diagnostic Yield: Validating Aspergillosis Criteria in COPD.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine

articles.title: Optimizing Sepsis Time Zero Definitions Through Associations between Antibiotic Timing and Mortality.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Sepsis performance measures require operational definitions of "time zero", but SEP-1's heterogeneous organ dysfunction criteria may not all identify patients vulnerable to harm from antibiotic delays.

OBJECTIVES: To determine which SEP-1 organ dysfunctions identify patients in whom antibiotic delays are associated with increased mortality.

METHODS: We analyzed adults with suspected infection using electronic health record data from 145 U.S. hospitals (2018-2023). We estimated associations between antibiotic timing (1-3 vs. 0-1h and 3-6 vs. 0-3h) and in-hospital mortality for each SEP-1 organ dysfunction criterion, alone and in combination: hypotension, elevated lactate, respiratory failure, renal dysfunction, hyperbilirubinemia, thrombocytopenia, and coagulopathy. We used inverse probability weighting to adjust for baseline and time-varying confounders.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Among 1,849,729 encounters with suspected infection, 624,416 had ≥1 organ dysfunction and received antibiotics within 6h of time zero. Antibiotics at 1-3 vs. 0-1h were associated with higher mortality when time zero was defined by hypotension (aRR 1.07; 95% CI, 1.03-1.10) or lactate ≥4.0mmol/L (aRR 1.10; 1.05-1.15), but not for other dysfunctions alone or in combination. Among patients without hypotension or lactate ≥4.0mmol/L, antibiotics at 3-6 vs. 0-3h were only associated with higher mortality in patients with acute respiratory failure (aRR 1.11; 1.05-1.18).

CONCLUSIONS: Mortality associations with antibiotics beyond 1 hour were most evident when sepsis time zero was defined by hypotension or lactate ≥4.0mmol/L, and with antibiotics beyond 3 hours when defined by acute respiratory failure. These findings could inform refinements to sepsis time zero definitions to better guide antibiotic urgency and performance measurement.

articles.title: [Autoimmune encephalitis is an immune-mediated brain inflammation].
articles.abstract: Autoimmune encephalitis is an immune-mediated CNS inflammation and a common cause of non-infectious encephalitis. Various antibodies involved in the inflammatory process have been identified, which usually correspond to specific clinical phenotypes. LGI1 antibodies are detected in a type of autoimmune encephalitis that involves the limbic system, manifesting as memory disturbances, behavioral changes, dystonic seizures, and autonomic nervous system dysfunction. We describe a case of LGI1 encephalitis with a rare prodromal symptom of cardiac arrhythmia, presenting several weeks before typical neurological symptoms.

articles.title: A Prospective Tandem Colonoscopy Study to Determine Proximal Colon Polyp Miss Rate Among Gastroenterology Trainees.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Existing colonoscopy quality metrics have limited utility for trainees. In particular, the adenoma detection rate may reflect trainer rather than trainee competence. Polyp miss rates may be more objective and feasible metrics of trainee colonoscopy quality. The aim of this study was to assess the proximal colon adenoma miss rate (AMR) and sessile serrated polyp miss rate (SMR) among gastroenterology trainees using a tandem colonoscopy study design.

METHODS: We prospectively recruited adult patients scheduled for screening or surveillance colonoscopy during endoscopy blocks with one of six high-quality trainers. Trainees performed the insertion with attending supervision. The trainee then performed independent withdrawal and inspection of the proximal colon (cecum to splenic flexure), identifying polyps without attending input. Subsequently, the attending performed a second complete inspection of the proximal colon; polyps that were identified on the second pass were considered missed polyps.

RESULTS: In total, 134 patients underwent colonoscopy by 13 gastroenterology trainees over a 17-month period. The overall proximal colon neoplastic (adenoma and serrated) polyp miss rate was 42.6%. Among these, they missed 38.1% of tubular adenomas and 58.9% of sessile serrated polyps in the proximal colon. Approximately 67% of the missed neoplastic polyps were ≤5mm. Trainee AMR and SMR decreased with increasing colonoscopy experience.

CONCLUSIONS: Trainees miss over 40% of proximal colon neoplastic polyps, including the majority of right sided sessile serrated polyps. Measuring polyp miss rates using tandem colonoscopy is a novel and feasible approach to objectively assessing colonoscopy quality among gastroenterology trainees.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of dabigatran in cirrhosis with chronic portal vein thrombosis: A randomized, placebo-controlled double-blind trial (DAB-PVT).
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are emerging options for portal vein thrombosis (PVT) in cirrhosis, though their safety and efficacy remain uncertain. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of dabigatran for PVT recanalization.

METHODS: Eighty-four patients with cirrhosis and PVT were prospectively randomized to receive dabigatran(n=42; 150 mg twice daily) or placebo(n=42) for 12 months. The primary endpoint was complete recanalization(CR) of the portal vein at 12 months. Secondary endpoints included safety, clinical outcomes, and changes in the liver disease severity scores and mortality.

RESULTS: Patients were predominantly male(71.4%), with a mean age of 48.5± 9.1 years and median Child-Turcotte-Pugh(CTP) score of 8(7-8). Medium-to-large varices were present in 60.7%, prior variceal bleeding in 45.2%, and ascites in 54.8%. At 12 months, complete recanalization occurred in 27/42(64.3%) in dabigatran group compared to 9/42(21.4%) in the placebo group(p<0.001). On multivariable Cox regression, dabigatran treatment was independently associated with complete recanalization (adjusted HR, 4.35; 95% CI, 2.03-9.36; P<0.001), along with a more favorable baseline ALBI score (adjusted HR, 2.02; 95% CI, 1.02-4.01; P=0.044). Variceal bleeding episodes were less frequent with dabigatran (3 vs. 12; p = 0.008). Compared with placebo, patients receiving dabigatran showed greater improvement in CTP scores (ΔCTP -0.57 ± 1.17 vs. 0.19 ± 1.17; P=0.004) and ALBI scores (ΔALBI -0.29 ± 0.82 vs. 0.06 ± 0.49; P=0.020). Longitudinal mixed-effects analysis demonstrated significantly different trajectories for CTP and ALBI scores, whereas MELD trajectories were comparable between groups.

CONCLUSION: In patients with Child-Pugh A/B cirrhosis and chronic PVT, dabigatran significantly increased complete portal vein recanalization compared with placebo with fewer bleeding events. The observed differences in clinical events and liver disease severity scores could be considered exploratory requiring evaluation in larger comparative studies.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in Otoscopy for Tympanic Membrane Pathologies: A State-of-the-Art Scoping Review.
articles.journal: The journal of international advanced otology
articles.abstract: This paper aimed to conduct a systematic search within a scoping review framework and provide a critical narrative appraisal of the current literature on artificial intelligence (AI) applications for tympanic membrane (TM) image analysis in the diagnosis of ear infections, with a focus on methodological rigor, dataset characteristics, and clinical applicability. A comprehensive search was performed across various online databases (Scopus, PubMed, Google Scholar, Embase, IEEE Xplore, and SPIE Digital Library) to identify studies published up to June 30, 2024. Studies employing AI for the analysis or classification of TM images in ear disease diagnostics were included. Inclusion and exclusion criteria were predefined. Data extraction covered dataset properties, imaging modalities, AI models, validation strategies, and performance metrics. The level of evidence, potential sources of bias, and methodological rigor were assessed qualitatively. Eighty-three studies met inclusion criteria, encompassing 90 experimental results. Considerable heterogeneity was observed regarding dataset size, image quality, device types, labeling protocols, and AI models. Most studies relied on small, private datasets, limiting model generalizability. While deep learning methods-especially convolutional neural networks-achieved high classification accuracies, methodological limitations included inconsistent data augmentation, imbalanced datasets, and lack of external validation. Few studies employed multidisciplinary teams or standardized protocols. Despite notable advances in AI-driven TM image analysis, direct comparison of studies remains challenging due to substantial heterogeneity and methodological shortcomings. A meta-analysis or systematic review was not performed, as quantitative synthesis would be misleading due to substantial data and labeling heterogeneity, wide methodological diversity, and a widespread lack of external validation across the included studies. Future research should prioritize larger, diverse, and well-annotated datasets, adoption of standardized protocols, and interdisciplinary collaboration to improve the clinical translation and reliability of AI-based diagnostic tools for ear infection management.

articles.title: Effectiveness of digital health interventions for asthma management: an umbrella review protocol.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this review will be to comprehensively synthesize evidence from systematic reviews examining the effectiveness of digital health interventions (DHIs) compared with usual care or non-digital interventions for improving clinical health outcomes in patients with asthma of all ages.

INTRODUCTION: Asthma affects 262 million people worldwide, with a substantial morbidity, mortality, and economic burden. Despite effective treatments, control remains suboptimal due to poor medication adherence and barriers to traditional face-to-face care. DHIs offer various solutions; however, heterogeneous findings across systematic reviews necessitate synthesis to clarify the most effective interventions.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Patients of any age diagnosed with asthma will be included. Eligible interventions will be consumer-focused DHIs (including smartphone applications, telehealth, electronic monitoring devices, web-based platforms, messaging services, and smart inhalers) compared with usual care, non-digital interventions, or other digital modalities. The primary outcome will be asthma control; secondary outcomes will be quality of life, medication adherence and health care utilization. Factors influencing engagement and adverse events will be reported. There will be no language restrictions.

METHODS: This review will follow the JBI methodology for umbrella reviews. Systematic searches will be conducted in MEDLINE (Ovid), Embase (Ovid), Cochrane Library, Epistemonikos, CINAHL Ultimate (EBSCOhost), and JBI Best Practice (Ovid), with PEDro as a supplementary source. Two reviewers will independently conduct study selection, critical appraisal, and data extraction using standardized JBI forms. The findings will be narratively synthesized with tabular summaries, as well as a citation matrix analysis for overlap assessment and visual representations. Certainty of evidence will be rated using GRADE.

SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420251247228 (PROSPERO).

articles.title: Fluorouracil-Associated Coronary Vasospasm and Reversible Cardiomyopathy Mimicking ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction During a First Cycle of FOLFOX: A Case Report.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) is a mainstay chemotherapeutic agent for gastrointestinal malignancies but carries a recognized risk of cardiotoxicity, most often manifesting as coronary vasospasm that can mimic acute myocardial infarction. This report describes the case of a 50-year-old woman with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) due to coronary artery vasospasm during continuous infusion of 5-FU as part of the first round of FOLinic acid (leucovorin), Fluorouracil (5-FU), and OXaliplatin (FOLFOX) chemotherapy for colorectal carcinoma. CASE REPORT A 50-year-old woman with colorectal carcinoma receiving her first cycle of FOLFOX developed severe chest pain during a continuous infusion of 5-FU. Initial emergency department evaluation was reportedly unremarkable, and she was discharged after symptomatic improvement with ketorolac. She returned emergently with recurrent crushing chest pain; a repeat electrocardiogram showed hyperacute T waves and ST-segment elevation, prompting ST-elevation myocardial infarction activation and transfer for emergent catheterization. Coronary angiography revealed no obstructive coronary artery disease. Echocardiography demonstrated a severely reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 30% to 35% with apical akinesis, consistent with 5-FU-induced cardiomyopathy. 5-FU was permanently discontinued, and the patient was treated with vasodilator therapy, with complete resolution of symptoms and normalization of ventricular function on follow-up echocardiography. CONCLUSIONS 5-FU can precipitate life-threatening coronary vasospasm and a fully reversible cardiomyopathy even during a first chemotherapy cycle, in the absence of obstructive coronary artery disease. Early recognition, prompt drug interruption, and a multidisciplinary cardio-oncology approach, including an individualized decision between permanent discontinuation and carefully supervised rechallenge, are essential to guide safe oncologic decision-making.

articles.title: Intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography detection of a mobile echogenic structure at the left atriotomy suture line - A case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) provides real-time anatomical and functional assessment during cardiac surgery and may detect abnormalities that require surgical intervention.

CASE: An 80-year-old woman underwent minimally invasive left atrial myxoma excision combined with a maze procedure under general anesthesia. After weaning from cardiopulmonary bypass, routine TEE revealed a small but highly mobile echogenic structure near the right superior pulmonary vein. The operating surgeon was notified, and external palpation localized the finding to the superior left atriotomy, consistent with a redundant atrial tissue flap protruding through the suture line. Reinforcing sutures were placed to incorporate the flap into the closure and eliminate its protrusion into the left atrium. Repeat TEE confirmed complete disappearance of the lesion. The patient recovered without embolic complications.

CONCLUSIONS: Careful post-bypass TEE examination, including systematic assessment of atriotomy closure sites, may identify potentially embolic mobile echogenic structures and guide surgical management, thereby contributing to perioperative patient safety.

articles.title: Patent Foramen Ovale in Adults With Right-to-Left Shunting: Clinical Significance, Diagnosis, and Contemporary Management.
articles.abstract: During fetal development, the foramen ovale is an important component of normal fetal circulation, allowing oxygenated blood to bypass the nonfunctional fetal lungs and supporting fetal growth and development. After birth, incomplete fusion of the septum primum and septum secundum may result in a persistent patent foramen ovale (PFO), which is present in approximately 25% of adults. Although most individuals remain asymptomatic, PFO has been recognized as an important contributor to paradoxical embolism and cryptogenic ischemic stroke. The clinical significance of PFO depends not only on its presence, but also on patient characteristics and anatomical features that influence the likelihood of right-to-left shunting and embolic events. High-risk morphology characteristics, including a large interatrial communication, elongated tunnel length, and prominent Eustachian valve or Chiari network, are associated with increased embolic potential. Advances in multimodality imaging, particularly contrast transesophageal echocardiography, have improved the diagnosis and anatomical characterization of PFO, while risk stratification tools such as the Risk of Paradoxical Embolism (RoPE) score and the PASCAL classification are important tools when determining whether a PFO is likely to be causally related to ischemic stroke. Treatment options for PFO are also largely related to the risk and morphology of the PFO, with age and risk of recurrent strokes impacting potential treatment options. Closure of PFO may not be recommended in all patients; however, percutaneous closure has become more prevalent in recent years due to its less invasive nature.

articles.title: The Situation-Specific Theory of Caregiver Contributions to Heart Failure Self-Care: An Update.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) self-care remains suboptimal in a large proportion of patients, and informal caregivers play a crucial role in supporting and helping patients to perform self-care behaviors. The Situation-Specific Theory of Caregiver Contributions to Heart Failure Self-Care, originally published in 2018, provided the first theoretical framework describing this process. Eight years after its initial formulation, substantial new empirical evidence, updated clinical guidelines, and advances in nursing knowledge call for a revision of the theory.

OBJECTIVE: To present an updated version of the Situation-Specific Theory of Caregiver Contributions to Heart Failure Self-Care, incorporating new evidence on contributors and mechanisms contributing to outcomes associated with caregiver contributions (CC) to HF self-care.

METHODS: The update followed the integrative approach proposed by Im and Meleis, drawing on 3 sources: the original theory, an integrative literature review of studies published between 2018 and 2026 (N = 17 studies), and the clinical insights and accumulated experience of the research team.

RESULTS: The updated theory introduces a new definition of CC to HF self-care as a dynamic, relational, and context-sensitive dyadic process. New contributors at the caregiver (eg, health status), patient (eg, therapeutic complexity), and dyadic levels (eg, type of relationship) were identified. Caregiver self-efficacy was confirmed as the central mediator of the process. Three new potential moderators were added alongside culture: beliefs, cohabitation, and ability to use technology. Outcomes were expanded to include dyadic-level effects. The theoretical propositions were updated and refined, and a new conceptual framework graphic is presented.

CONCLUSIONS: This updated theory offers a more comprehensive, multilevel, and context-sensitive framework to guide research, clinical practice, and interventions targeting the patient-caregiver dyad in HF.

articles.title: Serologic Guidance for Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Selection and Survival Using the Cosmos Dataset.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a life-support therapy for patients with severe cardiac or respiratory failure. Despite its growing use, evidence-based guidelines for ECMO candidacy remain limited due to small, single-center studies and heterogeneous designs. This study leveraged Epic Cosmos, an electronic health record dataset encompassing over 300 million patient records, to analyze outcomes among 42,210 adults treated with ECMO between January 1, 2019, and February 15, 2026, involving 23,116 (54.8%) venoarterial (VA), 14,632 (34.7%) venovenous (VV), and 4,462 (10.6%) hybrid (VA and VV) cases. Hospital mortality varied from 37% (VV) to 50% (VA). Poisson models by ECMO type for in-hospital mortality adjusted for key demographic and clinical variables showed the admitting diagnosis group had the strongest association with subsequent mortality. Several blood chemistry markers measured within the 24 hours before ECMO initiation were also associated with increased mortality, including elevated lactate, elevated creatinine, and lower pH, though strength of association varied by ECMO type. Our findings support the use of large electronic health record (EHR) datasets for ECMO outcomes research and identify exploratory associations between preinitiation biomarkers and in-hospital mortality that require further validation.

articles.title: A genome-wide association study and genetic risk score for age at diabetes diagnosis support beta-cell dysfunction in young-onset diabetes in Chinese.
authors: Hong Kong Diabetes Biobank Study Group and TRANSCEND Consortium
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We investigated genetic variations driving young age-at-diabetes-diagnosis (ADD) and developed a genetic risk score (GRS) to identify Chinese individuals at risk of young-onset diabetes (YOD with ADD<40).

METHODS: We performed genome-wide association studies (GWAS) for ADD with internal and external replication in 22,611 individuals with type 2 diabetes (T2D, 20% with YOD) and identified Chinese-prioritized loci by conditioning on the polygenic risk score (PRS) of ADD constructed from publicly available datasets. We constructed ADD-GRS using genome-wide independent variants (p<5E-08) and examined its associations with glycemic traits in diabetes and non-diabetes cohorts.

RESULTS: We identified three independent signals at genome-wide significance (P < 5×10-8) mapping to CDKAL1 (rs2206734, β=-0.75 (SE:0.13) per copy of T allele, effect allele frequency (EAF)=0.38, p=2.12E-09), PAX4 (rs61160304, β=-1.01 (SE:0.17) per copy of T allele, EAF=0.19, p=2.51E-09), and KCNQ1 (rs2299620, β=-0.77 (SE:0.14) per copy of G allele, EAF=0.70, p=2.80E-08). The variants at PAX4 and KCNQ1 were independent of the genetic liability estimated by ADD-PRS from Europeans and South Indians. In the diabetes cohort, the ADD-GRS was associated with younger ADD, lower C-peptide, higher HbA1c and pathway-specific T2D-PRS for beta-cell+proinsulin and residual glycemia. Using YOD versus later-onset diabetes as a secondary outcome, LINC02783/PADI1 (rs72895704, OR:1.52 per copy of A allele, EAF=0.02, p=1.93E-06) and TARS2P1 (rs145218437, OR: 1.73 per copy of C allele, EAF=0.02, p=7.57E-08) showed suggestive significance.

CONCLUSIONS: Both known and novel T2D loci contribute to ADD in Chinese people and may be used to detect high risk individuals for early intervention to prevent or delay onset of YOD.

articles.title: Gut microbiome dysbiosis and associated metabolome changes in tuberculosis patients resolve partially post-therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection in the host and subsequent treatment with anti-tuberculosis drugs impact lung pathophysiology and influence the lung and gut microbiome. Elucidating the role of the gut microbiome and its metabolites in the perturbed metabolic and immune functions observed in tuberculosis (TB) might help design corrective prebiotic and probiotic mixtures.

METHODOLOGY: In this study, fecal samples (n = 107) of drug-naïve active TB patients (ATB) and controls (other respiratory disease: NTB and healthy) from the two clinical sites were analyzed for microbiota composition (16S rRNA sequencing), metabolites (GC-TOF-MS), and their correlation. In addition, a longitudinal follow-up study was conducted to understand the dynamics of the microbiota and metabolites during anti-TB treatment in a small cohort (n = 10).

RESULTS: Gut microbiota showed site-specificity; however, an overall reduction in alpha diversity was observed in disease states compared with healthy subjects. Underrepresentation of gut commensals (Faecalibacterium, Ligilactobacillus and Romboustia) and overrepresentation of Thomasclavelia and Clostridioides were observed among active TB patients. The longitudinally followed-up ATB subjects undergoing treatment showed a time-dependent increase in beta-diversity variance. Over time, the beta diversity of follow-up subjects was almost similar to that of healthy controls. Decrease in the abundance of Streptococcus occurred after anti-TB treatment, with higher levels of opportunistic pathogens, such as Escherichia and Stenotrophomonas. Similarly, specific fecal metabolites also returned to pretreatment levels in relative abundance at later time points.

CONCLUSIONS: The gut microbiota of TB patients showed dysbiosis at the time of case presentation and partially resolved upon complete therapeutic interventions. Partial recovery of microbiota observed during treatment is also reflected in the fecal metabolome, indicating the possible use of microbiome and metabolites as adjunct therapeutics in TB.

articles.title: An Analysis of Large Language Model Performance on Hematology Key Feature Questions.
articles.journal: Journal of cancer education : the official journal of the American Association for Cancer Education
articles.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong performance on multiple-choice questions but their ability to independently generate clinical decisions without pre-defined answer choices remains less established. We therefore evaluated LLM performance on post-graduate key feature questions (KFQs), which are designed to assess clinical decision-making at critical points. Thirteen LLMs were assessed in June 2026 using 30 novel hematology KFQs developed and reviewed by two hematologists with training in medical education. Each LLM was then asked to assess each case independently, with context reset between cases. Responses were subsequently evaluated for exact correctness and partial credit. Responses between models were assessed using mixed-effects regression, Cochran's Q test, and Friedman's test. Incorrect responses were classified as knowledge, decision, or comprehension errors and subsequently inter-model analysis was performed. Across 390 responses, exact accuracy ranged from 73.3% to 96.7%. Gemini 3 Flash achieved the highest observed accuracy (29/30; 96.7%; 95% confidence interval, 82.8-99.9%), followed by Gemini 3 Flash Force Thinking and OpenEvidence (both 27/30; 90.0%). DeepSeek V3 had the lowest exact accuracy (22/30; 73.3%). Differences between models were not statistically significant for exact correctness (Cochran's Q = 20.00; p = 0.067) or partial-credit scores (Friedman's χ² = 17.95; p = 0.117). Among 71 incorrect responses, 35 (49.3%) were classified as knowledge errors, 32 (45.1%) as decision errors, and four (5.6%) as comprehension errors. LLMs demonstrated high accuracy on postgraduate-level hematology KFQs, although the limited question bank precludes conclusions about equivalent model performance. Knowledge and decision errors remained common among incorrect responses, supporting evaluation of factual accuracy and clinical judgment alongside aggregate scores. Further research should assess whether learners can recognize model errors and whether LLM assistance improves hematology decision-making.

articles.title: Preparedness of U.S. Gastroenterology Fellows to Implement Contemporary Gastric Cancer Prevention: A Cross- Sectional Survey.
articles.journal: Journal of cancer education : the official journal of the American Association for Cancer Education
articles.abstract: Successful implementation of contemporary gastric cancer prevention depends on gastroenterologists' ability to recognize higher-risk populations, manage Helicobacter pylori infection, identify premalignant gastric lesions, and apply risk-based surveillance. However, the preparedness of U.S. gastroenterology fellows for these responsibilities has not been evaluated nationally. We conducted a national cross-sectional survey (2025-2026) of fellows enrolled in Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education-accredited adult gastroenterology fellowship programs. An anonymous REDCap survey assessed gastric cancer prevention knowledge, educational exposure, confidence, preparedness, and responses to case-based clinical scenarios. Of 191 fellows who initiated the survey, 169 (88%) completed all required items. Only 20% identified all higher-risk populations for gastric cancer, and only 32% selected the correct approximate 5-year U.S. gastric cancer survival rate. Although 97% correctly answered that Helicobacter pylori eradication reduces gastric cancer risk, only 60% recognized the absence of a U.S. Preventive Services Task Force recommendation for gastric cancer screening. Fewer than half reported formal instruction in key prevention domains (30%-46%), only 23% felt prepared to independently manage premalignant gastric lesions, and 81% identified lack of guideline awareness as the principal barrier to early detection. These findings identify important gaps in the preparedness of the future gastroenterology workforce and highlight opportunities to strengthen implementation of evidence-based gastric cancer prevention.

articles.title: Topical 15% trichloroacetic acid versus silver nitrate cauterization in the management of idiopathic childhood epistaxis: a prospective randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: The purpose of the study is to compare the outcomes of trichloroacetic acid (TCA) to silver nitrate chemical cauterization in managing pediatric epistaxis. In this prospective randomized assessor-blinded clinical trial, of 172 randomized patients, 157 pediatric patients with idiopathic anterior epistaxis were divided into 2 groups in a ratio 1:1, where group (A) was treated with silver nitrate 25% after local anesthesia application and group (B) was treated with 15% TCA locally applied to the bleeder. Patients were assessed upon recurrence, pain, and crusting at 1st, 2nd, 4th, and 12th week post-intervention. The incidence of epistaxis was not significantly different between the two groups. Pain was significantly greater in the TCA group (P = 0.008*). Nasal crusting was slightly greater in the TCA group, but the difference was not statistically significant.

CONCLUSION: Although not widely utilized in the management of pediatric epistaxis, TCA is considered an effective chemical cautery agent for the management of childhood epistaxis, with results comparable to those of silver nitrate in terms of recurrence but was slightly worse in terms of pain after intervention.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Number NCT06836791, Date of registration 02/19/2025.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Epistaxis is a very distressing complaint in pediatric otorhinolaryngology. • One of the utilized modalities nowadays that proved efficacy in the management of epistaxis is the chemical cauterization of the prominent vessels in Little's area.

WHAT IS NEW: • This is the first study to compare the efficacy of silver nitrate to TCA in epistaxis treatment. • TCA is considered an effective chemical cautery agent for the management of childhood epistaxis, with results comparable to those of silver nitrate agent.

articles.title: Transoral robotic surgery for head and neck tumours: a critical systematic review of patient selection and outcome reporting.
articles.abstract: Transoral robotic surgery (TORS) is an emerging modality for the minimally invasive resection of head and neck tumours. Despite its introduction approximately 15 years ago, its use has not become widespread in clinical practice. It is hypothesised that both heterogenous patient selection and heterogenous reporting of safety, procedural efficiency,​oncological efficacy, and functional outcomes of TORS compared to alternative treatments has limited effective evidence synthesis and contributed to limited clinical adoption. This review aims to systematically assess patient selection and outcome reporting in the literature and identify areas for improvement. The Medline, Embase and Web of Science databases were searched from inception to June 2025. Articles were included if they reported TORS without neoadjuvant therapy for the management of any tumour in the head and neck, without restriction by subsite, stage, histological type, adjuvant therapy, or reported outcome(s). 1471 studies were identified from searches. After deduplication and screening, 70 studies were included, comprising one randomised controlled trial, 22 non-randomised comparative studies and 47 non-comparative studies. Participant inclusion criteria were generally well-defined according to tumour site and histopathological characteristics. Reporting of all outcomes across safety, oncological, functional and procedural domains was grossly heterogenous. Only six specific outcomes were reported by multiple comparative studies, four of which by the same two studies, which differed in fundamental disease characteristics. This study highlights the need for consistent reporting in TORS-based studies, possibly via a core outcome set, to facilitate robust evidence synthesis of the safety and efficacy of TORS.

articles.title: Producer Perspectives on Extended Producer Responsibility: Incentives and Policy Feasibility in Lebanon.
articles.abstract: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) is promoted as a mechanism to improve post-consumer waste management and circular-economy outcomes. Yet, its feasibility in resource-constrained settings depends on more than formal policy adoption alone. This study aims to develop an empirically informed, producer-centered framework for assessing conditions relevant to the feasibility of EPR implementation in resource-constrained settings, using Lebanon as a case study. Lebanon provides a relevant pre-implementation context because its waste management system faces limited recycling capacity, institutional constraints, and economic uncertainty. The framework organizes five components relevant to implementation feasibility: EPR orientation and conceptual scope, normative responsibility and legitimacy, motivations and the business case for potential adoption, policy-instrument acceptability, and producer perceptions of institutional enabling conditions. Drawing on a nationwide cross-sectional survey of 213 companies (Dec 2024-2025), the study uses descriptive statistics to characterize producer interpretations of EPR, reported motivations for potential adoption, and preferences for incentives and policy instruments. Reported motivations and policy preferences suggest that producer acceptance may depend on economic and institutional support. Mean priority ratings were generally low, although downstream system performance and economic responsibility received higher ratings than broader circular-economy outcomes. The most frequently reported motivations for potential adoption were cost savings, environmental commitment, and reputational benefits. Respondents supported a combination of incentives and obligations, including tax incentives, subsidies, recycling targets, and penalties. The resulting framework integrates these findings into a provisional assessment and hypothesis-generating tool for EPR policy design rather than a validated causal model.

articles.title: Emerging roles of circular RNAs in bovine mastitis and mammary immune regulation: mechanisms, networks and translational potential.
articles.abstract: Bovine mastitis is a complex inflammatory disease. Somatic cell count and bacteriological culture are central to bovine mastitis diagnosis. Complementary molecular measurements could clarify processes underlying persistent mammary injury. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are relatively stable, back-spliced transcripts with context-dependent expression and potential regulatory functions, making them relevant candidates for investigating post-transcriptional control in the bovine mammary gland. This review critically evaluates circRNA evidence in bovine mastitis, with particular emphasis on Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli. It integrates findings from mammary epithelial-cell models, mammary tissue and animal studies, peripheral blood, milk extracellular vesicles and N⁶-methyladenosine-associated circRNA profiling. Available studies report changes in circRNA abundance and modification patterns under mastitis-associated conditions. Candidate circRNAs are associated with inflammatory signalling, epithelial organization, vesicle and phagosome biology, and apoptosis. One functional study also implicates a circRNA in ferroptosis. However, most reported circRNAs are supported only by differential expression, expression validation, host-gene enrichment or predicted circRNA-microRNA-mRNA networks. These findings identify candidate mechanisms but do not establish direct regulation. Functional evidence remains limited, although circPRIM2 and circ_HOMER3 demonstrate that individual circRNAs can modify inflammatory, secretory, apoptotic and ferroptotic phenotypes in bovine mammary epithelial-cell models. Milk extracellular vesicle circRNAs are analytically detectable and infection responsive, but diagnostic sensitivity, pathogen discrimination and added value beyond established tests remain unproven. Progress now depends on coordinate-based nomenclature, full-length isoform resolution, direct interaction and rescue experiments, pathogen-defined animal studies and independent longitudinal cohorts. The immediate priority is therefore to move beyond circRNA catalogues and identify a smaller set of reproducible candidates with validated mechanisms and measurable translational value.

articles.title: Future directions of nanocatalysts in precision medicine: from catalytic therapy to intelligent nanozymes.
articles.abstract: The scope of nanomedicine may be broadened by nanocatalysts, which can actively modulate biochemical reactions in vivo. Of these nanocatalysts, nanozymes (nanomaterials with intrinsic enzyme-like activity) probably have received the most attention. Their activity can catalyze a reaction similar to peroxidase, catalase, oxidase, superoxide dismutase, or glutathione peroxidase, depending on composition, thus generating or scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS) depending on the microenvironment. This review sketches the evolution of this field from first generation iron oxide nanozymes to more recent stimuli-responsive multi-enzyme nanostructures. Moreover, selected experimental studies are examined, starting from in vivo Fenton and Fenton-like chemodynamic therapy and cascade catalysis and oxygen-releasing nanozymes in cancer, to antioxidant, antimicrobial, and immunomodulatory nanozymes in regenerative medicine, neurological, cardiovascular, and infectious disease models, respectively. For every case, the specific nanozyme, the biological model, the proposed mechanism of action, and the primary results are outlined, while the amount of evidence supporting the work is rated. The challenges for translating these systems into the clinic are addressed, such as the selectivity of the catalytic process to the physiological H2O2 concentration, efficiency of biodistribution, availability of long-term safety studies, batch-to-batch consistency, and ambiguity on regulatory pathways. It is speculated which of these issues can be practically solved by machine learning and which are more resistant. Future strategies are envisioned in creating biohybrid, logic-gated nanozymes, omics-guided design, and in vitro autonomous discovery platforms. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable. This study does not involve any clinical trial and does not require trial registration.

articles.title: Does temporomandibular joint disc closed-lock category III require patient stratification into acute and chronic cases?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) intraarticular pain and dysfunction (IPD) due to disc displacement without reduction (DDwoR) often respond to arthrocentesis and arthroscopy. It remains unclear if the duration of symptoms influences the outcomes following arthrocentesis and arthroscopy procedures.

PURPOSE: To measure the association between duration of symptoms in Category III TMJ IPD due to DDwoR and outcome following arthrocentesis or arthroscopy.

STUDY DESIGN, SETTING, AND SAMPLE: A double-blinded randomized clinical trial composed of patients presenting with Category III IPD to the TMJ Consultancy tertiary maxillofacial surgery referral centre in Bhopal, India between March 2024 and March 2025 were screened and enrolled. Patients with prior TMJ surgery, severe degenerative disease and active infection or systemic arthropathy were excluded.

PREDICTOR VARIABLE(S): Duration of symptoms (pain and limitation of mouth opening) categorized as acute (< 8-weeks) or chronic (> 8-weeks) and intervention (arthrocentesis or arthroscopy). The patient allocation followed a randomization into intervention arm.

MAIN OUTCOME VARIABLE(S): The therapeutic effect on pain (visual analogue scale, VAS) and maximal mandibular opening (MMO) measured as vertical incisor distance between 11 and 41. The variables were recorded preoperatively, at 3 weeks and 3 months post-operative.

COVARIATES: Demographics (age, sex), laterality, orthotic use and medical management.

ANALYSES: Normality testing (Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Shapiro-Wilk), intragroup-comparisons (Friedman and Wilcoxon), intergroup-comparisons (Kruskal-Wallis), effect size estimation (Cohen's d), and frequency analysis (chi-square). The significance level was set at P < 0.05.

RESULTS: Eighty subjects with Category III IPD DDwoR were categorized into four groups (n = 20 each): acute-arthrocentesis (AA), acute-arthroscopy (AL), chronic-arthrocentesis (CA), and chronic-arthroscopy (CL). The study subjects consisted of 48(60%) females and 32(40%) males with a mean age 27.9(± 6.5) years (P = 0.9). Baseline VAS for AA 7.75(± 0.85), AL 8.00(± 0.73), (CA 7.00(± 1.12) and CL 7.10(± 1.12). At 3 months VAS reduced to AA 0.35(± 0.81), AL 0.50(± 1.19), CA 1.55(± 2.28) and CL 1.50(± 2.19). A significant reduction of VAS scores observed in all groups from baseline to 3 months (P < 0.0001). Base line MMO (mm) recorded was AA 18.30(± 4.71), AL 18.00(± 5.08), CA 20.35(± 4.27), CL 20.50(± 4.53). MMO at three months post-op improved to AA 31.65(± 3.80) mm, AL 31.65(± 4.04) mm, CA 29.70(± 5.32) mm and CL 29.65(± 5.54) mm. A significant increase in MMO was observed in all groups from baseline to 3 months (P < 0.0001).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Shorter duration of symptoms in Category III IPD DDwoR appears to correlate with improved pain reduction and function with both arthrocentesis and arthroscopy. Acute cases demonstrate superior pain relief, greater functional stability, and absence of relapse, supporting chronological stratification of Category III internal derangement for clinical decision-making.

articles.title: LSS303, characterized as a STING agonist, inhibits porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus replication in vitro.
articles.abstract: Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV) remains a major constraint on global swine production, and no specific antiviral drug is currently available for clinical control. In this study, we evaluated the antiviral activity of a synthetic compound characterized as STING agonist (LSS303) against PRRSV infection in vitro. Cytotoxicity was assessed in Marc-145 cells and PAMs. Antiviral activity was evaluated by reverse-transcription quantitative PCR, western blotting, indirect immunofluorescence, and infectious virus titration. Pretreatment of Marc-145 cells with LSS303 reduced replication of the highly pathogenic PRRSV strain TA-12 in a concentration-dependent manner. At 5 μg/mL, LSS303 also reduced viral replication when applied before, during, or after infection. In PAMs, inhibitory activity was observed against the recombinant PRRSV strains Chah2022 (NADC30-like) and CHjs2022 (NADC34-like). These findings demonstrate cross-strain anti-PRRSV activity of LSS303 in vitro and support its further evaluation as a host-directed antiviral candidate. Whether effective exposure can be achieved in vivo remains to be determined.

articles.title: Nurse-led inferior vena cava assessment using handheld ultrasound within a cardiologist-supported home-care workflow.
articles.abstract: Volume assessment in older adults receiving home-based care is challenging because body weight, edema, and symptoms may be insufficient indicators, particularly in patients with cognitive impairment. We describe a 95-year-old woman with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, severe tricuspid regurgitation, atrial fibrillation, and dementia. Trained visiting nurses acquired standardized inferior vena cava (IVC) images during home visits and shared them with a cardiologist through a secure cloud-based platform. At the initial assessment, the maximum IVC diameter was 19.3 mm and the IVC collapsibility index was 29%; at 3 weeks, these values were 11.0 mm and 54.5%, respectively. Because IVC findings alone cannot establish volume status, they were interpreted alongside weight loss and reduced skin turgor, and oral fluid intake was encouraged based on the overall clinical assessment. Follow-up laboratory data were unavailable, and hydration status could not be objectively confirmed. This case illustrates the feasibility of a cardiologist-supported home-care workflow integrating nurse-performed IVC assessment and remote cardiologist review. Its clinical utility requires further evaluation.

articles.title: GLP-1-based Therapies in MASH: From Metabolic Benefits to an Improvement in Liver Fibrosis.
articles.abstract: The fibrosis stage is the strongest predictor of liver-related outcomes in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), supporting pharmacotherapy for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) with F2-F3 fibrosis. Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists improve MASLD through weight loss and favorable metabolic and anti-inflammatory effects; preclinical studies suggest weight loss-independent signaling mediated by liver sinusoidal endothelial cells. Early trials showed steatohepatitis resolution, but an inconsistent fibrosis improvement. In phase III ESSENCE, weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg significantly increased the proportions of patients achieving "resolution of steatohepatitis with no worsening of liver fibrosis" and a "reduction in liver fibrosis with no worsening of steatohepatitis" at week 72, leading to accelerated approval in the United States and approval in Japan for noncirrhotic MASH with moderate or advanced fibrosis. Non-invasive assessment may support patient selection and monitoring when a biopsy is inappropriate, although response thresholds require validation. This review summarizes the evidence, mechanisms, patient selection, safety, monitoring, and challenges.

articles.title: Impact of a Standardized Emergency Management Protocol for Gastrointestinal Bleeding on Endoscopist Burden: A Pilot Observational Study.
articles.abstract: Objective　The clinical benefits of urgent endoscopy for gastrointestinal bleeding remain controversial. We implemented an original protocol for out-of-hours emergency management of gastrointestinal bleeding to reduce unnecessary urgent endoscopies. We aimed to compare the clinical outcomes during the one-year periods before and after protocol implementation.Methods　In this single-center retrospective study, we included patients admitted for gastrointestinal bleeding after hours from September 2023 to August 2025. The protocol, introduced in September 2024, standardized the assessment of patient condition, criteria for contacting the on-call endoscopist, and the subsequent treatment strategies. The primary endpoint was the proportion of out-of-hours urgent endoscopies. The secondary endpoints were 30-day mortality, on-call endoscopist attendance, additional interventions such as surgery, and rates of rebleeding and blood transfusion.Patients or Materials　A total of 159 patients were analyzed (before protocol implementation, n=73; after protocol implementation, n=86).Results　The proportions of out-of-hours urgent endoscopies (34.2% vs. 17.4%, p=0.02) and on-call endoscopist attendance (53.4% vs. 22.1%, p<0.001) were lower after implementation of the protocol. The 30-day mortality rate did not differ between the periods (0% vs. 1.2%, p>0.99). The rates of rebleeding (8.2% vs. 11.6%, p=0.6) and additional interventions (4.1% vs. 4.7%, p>0.99) did not differ, whereas the rate of blood transfusion was higher after implementation of the protocol (57.5% vs. 75.6%, p=0.02).Conclusion　Standardization of the emergency management of gastrointestinal bleeding was associated with a reduction in out-of-hours urgent endoscopies and on-call endoscopist attendance, without significant differences in mortality, rebleeding, or additional interventions.

articles.title: Real-world characteristics of endovascular treatment for middle cerebral artery M2 segment occlusion in Fukushima Prefecture: a prospective multicenter registry study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The role of endovascular treatment (EVT) in middle cerebral artery M2 segment occlusion remains inconclusive, particularly in rural areas with aging populations. We characterized EVT and medical management (MM) for M2 occlusion in Fukushima Prefecture, Japan, and explored clinical factors associated with outcomes.

METHODS: We analyzed a prospective multicenter acute ischemic stroke registry (July 2020-June 2022; 11 stroke centers). Patients with M2 occlusion were classified into EVT or MM groups; characteristics, workflow metrics, and outcomes were described and referenced against previously reported series.

RESULTS: Among 210 patients, 34 had M2 occlusion (EVT, n=10; MM, n=24). At 90 days, functional independence (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-2) was 40.0% (EVT) and 45.8% (MM); symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage, 0% and 4.2%; mortality, 20.0% and 12.5%; successful reperfusion, 70.0% (EVT). Both groups were older than in previous reports (median 81 years). The EVT group also received rt-PA less often (30.0%) and had longer puncture-to-reperfusion times (81 minutes), whereas the MM group had lower pre-stroke independence (67%) and higher mortality, despite lower severity.

CONCLUSION: Advanced age, delayed reperfusion, and greater pre-stroke dependency distinguished this rural cohort from previous reports and likely account for its outcomes, underscoring the need for locally tailored patient selection for EVT in M2 occlusion.

articles.title: Gestational Age-Associated Pathogen Distributions in Very Preterm Infants With Sepsis.
Case 32-2026: A 50-Year-Old Man with Recurrent Cardiomyopathy.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine

articles.title: Preventing Malaria Infections and Moving toward Malaria Elimination.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract: Malaria continues to be a major health challenge worldwide, causing an estimated 282 million cases of illness and 610,000 deaths in 2024, predominantly among African children. Despite recent stagnation in the progress of malaria prevention, the landscape is undergoing rapid transformation. This review examines current and emerging approaches to preventing malaria infection and supporting malaria elimination, including vector control, transmission-blocking interventions, chemoprevention, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines. Next-generation insecticide-treated nets, expanded use of seasonal malaria chemoprevention, and the introduction of RTS,S/AS01 and R21/Matrix-M vaccines are already reshaping control strategies. Looking ahead, long-acting injectable chemoprevention, transmission-blocking medicines and vaccines, and improved surveillance-driven deployment may further accelerate progress. As funding becomes constrained and decision making shifts increasingly to countries where malaria is endemic, effective malaria prevention will depend on locally tailored, integrated combinations of interventions supported by strong surveillance, regulatory capacity, and national leadership.

articles.title: Prevention of Venous Thromboembolism after Total Hip or Knee Replacement.
authors: PEPPER Trial Investigators and the Steering Committee of the PEPPER Trial
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Studies comparing aspirin with anticoagulants for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty have had conflicting results.

METHODS: In a comparative-effectiveness noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned patients undergoing elective hip or knee arthroplasty to receive aspirin (81 mg twice daily), warfarin (to a target international normalized ratio of 2.0), or rivaroxaban (10 mg daily) for 30 days. The composite primary effectiveness outcome (death from any cause or symptomatic VTE) and primary safety outcome (bleeding, reoperation for wound problems, or myocardial infarction) were evaluated through 6 months in a blinded fashion. The noninferiority margin for the risk difference was 0.69 percentage points.

RESULTS: Among 18,883 participants who had undergone randomization, 15,317 (7214 with hip arthroplasty and 8103 with knee arthroplasty) were included in the primary per-protocol analysis. A primary effectiveness outcome event occurred in 77 of 6090 participants (1.26%) in the aspirin group, in 52 of 4231 (1.23%) in the warfarin group, and in 47 of 4996 (0.94%) in the rivaroxaban group; a primary safety outcome event occurred in 177 (2.91%), 142 (3.36%), and 174 (3.48%), respectively. In pairwise comparisons, 6-month risks of a primary effectiveness outcome event were 1.24% and 0.94% for aspirin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.30 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.20 to 0.81); 1.24% and 1.01% for aspirin versus warfarin (difference, 0.23 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.34 to 0.81); and 1.13% and 1.10% for warfarin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.03 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.57 to 0.63). Risks of a primary safety outcome event were 3.70% and 3.02% for rivaroxaban versus aspirin (difference, 0.68 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.41); 3.65% and 2.88% for warfarin versus aspirin (difference, 0.77 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.58); and 3.59% and 3.61% for rivaroxaban versus warfarin (difference, -0.02 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.89 to 0.85). Intention-to-treat analyses yielded similar results.

CONCLUSIONS: Aspirin prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty was not noninferior to rivaroxaban or warfarin with respect to death or symptomatic VTE. Warfarin and rivaroxaban were not noninferior to aspirin for safety. (Funded by the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute; PEPPER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT02810704.).

articles.title: The skull-meninges-brain axis: a new paradigm for systemic inflammation-driven encephalopathy.
articles.abstract: Despite the significant clinical burden of sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE), current models centering on blood-brain barrier (BBB) damage as the initiating event fail to fully explain the rapid neurocognitive deterioration. This review proposes a paradigm-shifting meningeal sentinel framework that repositions the meninges as the primary immunological gateway in SAE. We integrate three sequential stages - signal sensing, microenvironmental remodeling, and parenchymal propagation - into a unified model in which systemic inflammation is detected by meningeal border-associated immune compartments before overt BBB disruption. Central to this framework are the skull bone marrow-dura mater-brain axis enabling rapid myeloid cell delivery via transcortical channels, meningeal lymphatic dysfunction, and CD4+ T cell suppression, which collectively relay danger signals to the brain. This model reframes BBB breakdown as a downstream amplification event, offering a cohesive explanation for the early cognitive deficits in sepsis and distinguishing SAE from other neuroinflammatory disorders. Importantly, the framework predicts that meningeal-derived mediators enter the cerebrospinal fluid earlier than parenchymal injury markers, opening a window for early diagnosis. Targeting the skull-meninges-brain axis - through modulation of calvarial myelopoiesis, enhancement of lymphatic drainage, or restoration of meningeal T-cell function - offers strategies to prevent irreversible brain damage. This meninges-centered perspective thus advances mechanistic understanding and provides a template for systemic inflammation-driven encephalopathies.

articles.title: Clinical and radiological outcomes of open reduction and internal fixation for Kilfoyle type III pediatric medial humeral condyle fractures: a retrospective single-center study.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric orthopedics. Part B
articles.abstract: Medial humeral condyle fractures are uncommon intra-articular injuries in children and are often overlooked because of delayed trochlear ossification. Delayed diagnosis or inadequate treatment may cause nonunion, malunion, growth disturbance, elbow deformity, and functional limitation. This retrospective single-center study evaluated clinical and radiological outcomes of pediatric medial humeral condyle fractures treated with open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) at a tertiary referral center. Children aged 18 months to 12 years who underwent surgery between March 2016 and February 2022 with at least 2 years of follow-up were included. Fractures were classified using the Kilfoyle classification on radiographs, with computed tomography when the configuration was uncertain. Demographics, injury patterns, surgical details, complications, radiographic union, and elbow range of motion were reviewed from medical records. Seventeen children met the criteria. Mean age was 6.2 years (range: 1.5-12), and all fractures were displaced (Kilfoyle type III). The mean interval from injury to surgery was 1.9 days. Union was achieved in 16 of 17 patients (94.1%). Six patients (35.3%) developed complications: one nonunion requiring revision fixation, one malunion requiring corrective osteotomy, two cases of cubitus varus, and two cases of persistent extension deficit despite physiotherapy. No infection, neurovascular injury, or ulnar nerve palsy occurred. Fifteen patients achieved full flexion, and 13 regained full extension. ORIF provides satisfactory clinical and radiological outcomes for displaced pediatric medial humeral condyle fractures, with a high union rate and acceptable functional recovery. However, complications may occur, particularly in older children. Early diagnosis, accurate anatomical reduction, and long-term follow-up remain essential.

articles.title: Constructing Bimetallic Ruthenium-Nickel Alloy Toward High-Efficiency Selective Hydrogenolysis of Polyethylene Terephthalate Plastic Waste.
articles.abstract: The upcycling of plastic waste into renewable chemicals offers a pathway toward carbon resource recovery and reduced environmental pollution. Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) hydrogenolysis can produce aromatic hydrocarbons, cycloalkanes, or a mixture of both, while achieving selective control over the reaction pathway remains challenging. Herein, we report a TiO2 (P25)-supported bimetallic Ru─Ni alloy catalyst (RuNi/P25) that can directly upgrade PET into cycloalkanes in 84.9% yield with 100% selectivity among the liquid products under mild reaction conditions (230 °C, 1.5 MPa H2). The outstanding performance of RuNi/P25 mainly originates from the electron-rich Ru species, which play a key role in activating hydrogen and C─O bonds. The formation of the RuNi alloy facilitates electron transfer from Ni to Ru, thereby accelerating the hydrogenation rate of the benzene ring and promoting the catalytic activity for converting PET to cycloalkanes. The strategy of constructing a RuNi alloy presented in this work affords a promising approach for the development of highly effective catalysts, which can be applied in the valorization of aromatic plastic wastes and biomass-derived feedstocks.

articles.title: Fluctuation-Driven Chemistry at Aqueous Interfaces and Beyond.
articles.journal: Chemphyschem : a European journal of chemical physics and physical chemistry
articles.abstract: Interfacial electric fields at gas-water, oil-water, and solid-water boundaries are frequently invoked to explain radical formation under ambient conditions. Field strengths of 107-109 V m-1 are often cited as sufficient for this purpose.
