However, the electrostatic work accessible from such fields over molecular distances is substantially smaller than the energies associated with direct one-electron detachment or ionization. This discrepancy raises the question of whether interfacial electric fields directly drive chemistry or modulate an intrinsic property of liquid water. Here we argue that equilibrium interfacial electric fields bias molecular orientation and reaction kinetics but do not constitute a primary energetic input for bond-breaking chemistry. Instead, we propose a fluctuation-driven model in which transient, partially charge-separated configurations of the hydrogen-bond network emerge from cooperative hydrogen-bond fluctuations and can be kinetically selected by solutes (e.g., H+, CO2, formate, DMPO, crown ethers) or catalytic surfaces through electronic coupling, generating charge-transfer pathways involving configurations such as S…(H2O)n -δ or S…(H2O)n +δ, which yield measurable radical products. Interfaces, ions, and weak perturbations reshape the free-energy landscape and alter fluctuation statistics; water autoionization and radical formation can therefore be viewed within a common statistical framework based on fluctuation-accessible electronic configurations.

articles.title: Tracking and Tuning the C1/C2 Pathway: In Situ Spectroscopy and Mechanistic Insights Into Ethylene Glycol Oxidation on Metal-Based Catalysts.
articles.abstract: The electrocatalytic ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR), using ethylene glycol (EG) obtained from hydrolyzed polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste, offers a route for converting this plastic into valuable chemicals. However, steering selectivity between the C1 and C2 pathways remains challenging. This Review focuses on in situ spectroscopy for tracking interfacial reaction dynamics under operating conditions. We summarize how in situ Raman and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy enable real-time identification of adsorbed intermediates and active species, providing mechanistic insights inaccessible to ex situ methods. We then evaluate noble-metal and non-noble-metal catalysts and discuss how their structural characteristics regulate EG adsorption, OH- activation, and intermediate conversion. Particular attention is given to tuning C1/C2 branching to improve activity, selectivity, and poisoning resistance. We further survey EGOR applications in electrolysis systems, including pairing with hydrogen evolution for coproduction of value-added chemicals and hydrogen and coupling with CO2 reduction or organic synthesis to construct energy-efficient electrochemical cells. Ultimately, such mechanistic understanding offers guidance for rational catalyst design and sustainable PET upcycling.

articles.title: Navigating the "Silver Tsunami" in Limb Salvage: Lower Extremity Free Flap Outcomes in Septuagenarians and Octogenarians.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As the United States population ages, an increasing number of elderly patients with chronic lower extremity (LE) wounds require reconstruction. Although prior studies have evaluated flap outcomes in elderly patients undergoing free tissue transfer (FTT), systemic postoperative complications and complication severity remain inadequately characterized. This study compared surgical and systemic complications after LE FTT between elderly and non-elderly patients.

METHODS: A retrospective review of 318 patients undergoing LE FTT between 2011 and 2024 was performed. Patients were stratified into elderly (≥ 70 years) and non-elderly (< 70 years). Baseline characteristics, vascular status, operative variables, 30-day postoperative complications, and long-term outcomes were analyzed. Thirty-day complications were classified as systemic or surgical and graded using the Clavien-Dindo classification. Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analysis were used to evaluate predictors of complications.

RESULTS: Of 318 patients, 54 (17.0%) were elderly. Elderly patients experienced similar rates of any systemic complication (33.3% elderly vs. 22.7% non-elderly, p = 0.099), although acute kidney injury was more common in elderly patients (27.8% vs. 12.9%, p = 0.006). Surgical complications were also similar (33.3% vs. 28.4%, p = 0.469). Overall complication severity did not differ between groups (p = 0.701), and only 1.6% of patients experienced a life-threatening complication. Smoking history (odds ratio [OR] 2.6, p = 0.008) and diabetes (OR 2.7, p = 0.027) independently predicted major complications, while age did not. The Charlson Comorbidity Index outperformed age in predicting both major (area under the curve [AUC] 0.604 vs. 0.539, p = 0.031) and minor complications (AUC 0.647 vs. 0.551, p = 0.011). Septuagenarians and octogenarians did not differ significantly in complications, ambulation, amputation, or mortality.

CONCLUSION: LE FTT is a safe and effective limb salvage option in elderly patients, with no difference in overall systemic or surgical complications. Patient selection and risk assessment for LE FTT should, therefore, be guided by comorbidity burden rather than chronologic age alone.

articles.title: Developmental Differences in Muscle, Tendon, and Cartilage Injuries among Elite Badminton Players.
articles.abstract: This study investigated differences in the characteristics of severe muscle, tendon, and cartilage injuries according to injury timing and post-injury management among elite badminton players. A retrospective interview study was conducted involving 126 badminton players aged 19 to 24 years. A total of 87 severe injury cases reported by 73 athletes were analyzed, with some athletes contributing more than one case. Injuries were classified according to timing into the secondary school group (n=33) and the post-secondary group (n=54). Injury characteristics and post-injury management were compared using chi-square and Fisher's exact tests, with effect sizes. Odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals examined associations with injury timing. Compared with the secondary school group, the post-secondary group had higher odds of lower limb muscle injuries (odds ratio=6.00, 95% confidence interval=1.85-19.47, p=0.003) and smash/stroke-related injuries (odds ratio=5.43, 95% confidence interval=1.15-25.66, p=0.033), whereas the post-secondary group had lower odds of lower limb tendinopathies (odds ratio=0.21, 95% confidence interval=0.08-0.55, p=0.001). These findings suggest that severe injury characteristics may differ according to the timing of injury occurrence, despite no significant between-group differences in post-injury management, and may help inform potential injury prevention priorities based on the observed injury patterns.

articles.title: Prevalence of Persistent Severe Hypertension and Rates of Treatment Among Pregnant Patients in the Prehospital Setting.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) contribute to maternal and fetal morbidity and mortality and require time-sensitive intervention. In April 2025, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), in collaboration with the National Association of EMS Physicians (NAEMSP) and the National Association of EMTs (NAEMT), published new guidelines on the prehospital management of elevated blood pressure in pregnancy. The objective of this study was to determine the prevalence of persistent severe hypertension among pregnant patients encountered by prehospital clinicians, characterize baseline frequency of pre-guideline treatment, and establish a benchmark to inform implementation of these guidelines.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study using the 2024 ESO Data Collaborative public release research dataset (January 1 to December 31, 2024). We identified all 9-1-1 ground EMS scene responses for patients documented as pregnant beyond 20 wk of gestation. We excluded injury-related encounters and patients outside the World Health Organization-defined childbearing age range (15 to 49 years). Consistent with the new guidelines, we defined persistent severe hypertension as at least two documented blood pressure measurements with systolic blood pressure ≥ 160 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure ≥ 110 mmHg. We defined guideline-adherent treatment as administration of both magnesium sulfate (MgSO₄) and an antihypertensive medication (labetalol, hydralazine, or nifedipine).

RESULTS: We identified 39,546 eligible 9-1-1 ground EMS scene responses for patients beyond 20 wk of gestation. The prevalence of persistent severe hypertension was 3.1% (n = 1,234/39,546). Among these patients, 77 (6.2%) received magnesium sulfate only, 19 (1.5%) received an antihypertensive medication only, and 10 (0.8%) received guideline-adherent treatment with both magnesium sulfate and an antihypertensive medication.

CONCLUSIONS: Approximately 1 in 32 pregnant patients beyond 20 wk of gestation encountered by prehospital clinicians had persistent severe hypertension. In the year prior to dissemination of the 2025 ACOG, NAEMSP, and NAEMT-supported guidelines, fewer than 1% received guideline-adherent treatment with both magnesium sulfate and an antihypertensive medication. These findings establish a national benchmark and identify opportunities to improve prehospital care through protocol development, medication availability, clinician education, and implementation of updated guidelines.

articles.title: 7-(Chloroquinolin-4-yl) Sulfanyl Derivatives, Optimization of the Synthesis, In Silico ADMET Profiling Studies, and Evaluation of the Biological Activity Against Leishmania mexicana.
articles.abstract: Leishmaniasis is a parasitic human infection that constitutes a major global health challenge due to limited therapeutic options, toxicity, resistance, and high costs of the drugs approved as therapy. In this study, a group of 7-chloroquinoline derivatives (5-12) was synthesized via an optimized route and evaluated against the human parasite Leishmania mexicana. Compounds were fully characterized and showed favorable in silico ADME/Tox profiles, including high predicted gastrointestinal absorption (>93%), although limited solubility and potential hepatotoxicity were observed for several derivatives. Biological assays demonstrated significant antileishmanial activity. Interestingly, intracellular amastigote assays revealed nanomolar potency and very high selectivity index (SI), with compound 12 exhibiting IC50 = 2.5 nM (SI = 21.030) and compound 9 IC50 = 5.2 nM (SI = 7.384). Mechanistic studies demonstrated concentration-dependent mitochondrial membrane depolarization and acidocalcisome alkalinization. Since these two organelles are both involved in bioenergetics and in parasite intracellular Ca2+ homeostasis, the results support the notion that intracellular Ca2+ disruption is an essential target for different drug actions. Overall, these findings support a multitarget mechanism and position these quinoline derivatives as promising chemical scaffolds for the development of improved antileishmanial strategies.

articles.title: Controlled delivery of ferulic acid via microneedle-administered iron core-graphene shell nanoparticles modulates metabolic response and diabetic neuropathy in mice.
articles.abstract: The clinical application of ferulic acid (FA), a potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant compound, is severely hindered by low bioavailability caused by its poor solubility and rapid metabolism. A synergistic delivery approach was considered to overcome this challenge, specifically 25 ± 5 nm iron-core graphene-shell (Fe@C) nanoparticles, administered via a hollow zeolite microneedle array. A single subcutaneous injection of 6 mg FA/Fe@C in diabetic mice stabilized body weight at 27.3 g (compared to 20 g with daily FA injections) and, over 14 days, significantly improved diabetic neuropathy. This single-dose regimen also reduced blood glucose from 24 mmol L-1 to 21.2 mmol L-1, compared with 15 mmol L-1 in mice receiving daily injections of 50 mg kg-1 FA. The FA/Fe@C not only exhibited therapeutic efficacy, but also a self-protective mechanism. As evidenced by our in vivo safety assessments, the FA actively mitigated the nanoparticle's bioactivity and toxicity. FA/Fe@C resulted in significantly lower renal distress as indicated by BUN, CREA, and UA biomarkers, and reduced oxidative stress (ROS, MDA) in vital organs compared to Fe@C alone. In this research, we demonstrate a rationally designed biomaterial for managing diabetes and its complications.

articles.title: [Posterior periventricular white matter lesions as a clue to the diagnosis of folate deficiency with compound heterozygous MTHFR polymorphisms: a case report].
articles.abstract: An 18-year-old woman presented with a one-month history of persistent dizziness. Brain MRI revealed bilateral periventricular white matter lesions adjacent to the posterior horns of the lateral ventricles. Subsequently, she developed distal paresthesia of the extremities and was admitted for further evaluation. Neurological examination demonstrated abnormal ocular movements in the primary gaze position, horizontal gaze-evoked nystagmus, gait instability, and distal sensory disturbance. There was no antecedent infection, and cerebrospinal fluid analysis was unremarkable. Based on the clinical course and findings, an autoimmune-mediated brainstem-cerebellar disorder was suspected, and high-dose intravenous corticosteroid therapy was administered, resulting in improvement of ocular abnormalities and gait disturbance. Meanwhile, further investigation of the incidental posterior periventricular white matter lesions-considered unrelated to the presenting symptoms-revealed low serum folate levels and compound heterozygous genotype of the MTHFR gene. Vitamin supplementation was initiated accordingly. Notably, the patient's father was also found to have the same MTHFR gene compound heterozygous genotype. This case suggests that bilateral periventricular white matter lesions adjacent to the posterior horns may represent an early radiological marker of folate deficiency associated with MTHFR gene compound heterozygous genotype, even in the absence of overt folate-deficiency symptoms. Recognition of this imaging pattern may facilitate early diagnosis and intervention, potentially preventing future neurological or systemic complications.

articles.title: [Acute management of minor ischemic stroke].
articles.abstract: This review summarizes acute-phase treatment for minor ischemic stroke, focusing on the latest evidence for reperfusion therapy and acute antithrombotic treatment. In patients with large vessel occlusion, the benefit of mechanical thrombectomy is not established and the risk of hemorrhage exists; therefore, indications should be judged carefully for each patient. Intravenous thrombolysis provides limited benefit in non-disabling cases, and dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) can be an option. For minor non-cardioembolic stroke, early DAPT is recommended, and the possible role of adding argatroban is promising, especially for suspected branch atheromatous disease. For cardioembolic stroke, early initiation of a direct oral anticoagulant is desirable in mild cases without a large infarct.

articles.title: [Eltrombopag-associated bilateral internal jugular vein thrombosis presenting with visual impairment and marked intracranial hypertension: a case report].
articles.abstract: We report an 86-year-old man with immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) who developed bilateral internal jugular vein (IJV) thrombosis during treatment with eltrombopag (EPAG). He had experienced multiple cerebral infarctions over several months, but their cause had remained undetermined and warfarin therapy had been continued. Nine days before admission to our hospital, he developed visual impairment, and ophthalmologic evaluation revealed bilateral papilledema. He was admitted for further evaluation. Lumbar puncture demonstrated markedly elevated cerebrospinal fluid opening pressure (53 cm H2O), suggesting intracranial hypertension, and contrast-enhanced MR venography demonstrated bilateral sigmoid sinus thrombosis and bilateral IJV thrombosis. Although early thrombotic changes were retrospectively identifiable on plain MRI obtained at the previous hospital, the diagnosis was delayed because we did not initially recognize the possibility of EPAG-associated thrombosis, and visual impairment persisted despite treatment. In patients receiving EPAG, thrombotic complications should always be considered, and careful assessment of abnormal intraluminal venous signals on plain MRI is important for early diagnosis and therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: Ravulizumab in IgA Nephropathy - Interim Analysis of a Phase 3 Trial.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In patients with IgA nephropathy, complement activation drives glomerular inflammation, which leads to hematuria, proteinuria, and nephron loss. Ravulizumab is a terminal complement inhibitor that prevents formation of C5a and C5b-9.

METHODS: In this phase 3 trial, we enrolled adults with IgA nephropathy who had an estimated glomerular filtration rate of at least 30 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area and proteinuria (24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio [with protein and creatinine both measured in grams] of ≥0.75 or total urinary protein excretion of ≥1.0 g per day), despite standard therapy. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive an intravenous infusion of either ravulizumab or placebo every 8 weeks. In the prespecified interim analysis, the primary efficacy end point was the change from baseline in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at week 34. Safety was also assessed.

RESULTS: In all, 485 patients underwent randomization, with 240 patients assigned to the ravulizumab group and 245 to the placebo group; 352 patients (176 in each group) were included in the interim analysis. In the ravulizumab group, the geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at baseline and at week 34 was 1.56 and 0.83, respectively; in the placebo group, it was 1.60 and 1.48, respectively. At week 34, a significant reduction in the geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio was observed with ravulizumab (-46.6%) as compared with the reduction observed with placebo (-5.6%), corresponding to an adjusted geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio that was 43.4% (99% confidence interval, 30.1 to 54.2) lower with ravulizumab than with placebo (P<0.001). Adverse events occurred in 69.5% of the patients receiving ravulizumab and in 75.8% of those receiving placebo; serious adverse events occurred in 4.6% and 9.0%, respectively. No meningococcal infections or deaths occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: In adults with IgA nephropathy, ravulizumab resulted in a significantly greater reduction in the protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo at week 34. (Funded by Alexion, AstraZeneca Rare Disease Unit; I CAN ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06291376; EU Clinical Trials number, 2023-507851-31-00.).

articles.title: Exploring the design space of SMART RHESINs as a modular nanocapsule platform for functional magnetic nanoparticles.
articles.abstract: Magnetic core/shell nanoparticles (CSNPs) are central to emerging imaging and theranostic concepts, yet translating different magnetic payloads into a common, chemically addressable and functionally expandable architecture remains challenging. SMART RHESIN nanocapsules encapsulate different magnetic nanoparticle (NP) systems within a protective phenolic resin shell and permit structural variation and post-synthetic functionalisation. Here we map the design space of SMART RHESIN phenolic resin hollow nanocapsules across 52 reactions varying monomer choice, CSNP type, loading, co-encapsulation, and polymer additives. The platform incorporates magnetic payloads ranging from lab-synthesised magnetite to commercial iron oxides and cubic NPs, while identifying biogenic magnetosomes as a boundary case for the present synthesis conditions, with the resulting nanocapsule diameter (about 100 to 400 nm) and shell thickness (about 10 to 80 nm) varying systematically with the choice of CSNP system and reaction conditions. Magnetic particle spectroscopy (MPS) indicates reduced viscosity-induced phase shifts for selected representative formulations from this expanded compositional set, phantom MPI demonstrates multi-colour imaging that resolves aqueous and immobilised SR29 signals within a single field of view, and surface carboxylates enable post-synthetic modification, illustrated by 18F-radiolabelling for PET/CT. These findings establish SMART RHESINs as a versatile nanocapsule platform for integrating magnetic NPs with additional optical, radiochemical and future targeting functionalities.

articles.title: Study on the capture and thrombolytic efficacy of magnetic particle clusters under a deeply focused rotating magnetic field.
articles.abstract: Objective. Magnetic particles can serve as carriers for tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) and can be targeted and controllably manipulated under a rotating magnetic field (RMF), providing a potential approach for localized thrombolysis in venous thrombosis. However, current magnetic-control strategies remain limited at larger working distances and under flow conditions because of magnetic-field attenuation, insufficient focusing capability, and blood-flow-induced washout. Therefore, maintaining effective capture and stable motion of magnetic particle clusters (MPCs) remains an important challenge.Approach.To address this issue, we developed a deeply focused rotating magnetic field (DF-RMF) system driven by two synchronously rotating permanent magnets. The system generates a magnetic-field region with an axial dual-peak distribution and centripetal action, thereby promoting MPC accumulation within the target region while maintaining rotational motion. Numerical simulations andin vitroexperiments were conducted to evaluate the magnetic-field characteristics, MPC rotational behavior, capture performance under flow conditions, and thrombolytic efficacy. Experiments were performed in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) and a glycerol-water solution (GWS) with higher blood-relevant viscosity.Main results.Compared with a single-permanent-magnet rotating magnetic field, the DF-RMF provided better particle capture performance at larger working distances. In PBS, particle capture could still be maintained to some extent at a working distance of 5 cm, while particle retention was still observed at a flow velocity of 14 cm s-1and a working distance of 2 cm. Experiments in GWS showed that higher blood-relevant viscosity reduced the long-distance capture capability of the DF-RMF. Finite-element simulations showed that MPC rotation generated localized recirculating flow, velocity gradients, and periodic pressure variations in the surrounding fluid, potentially facilitating tPA transport near the thrombus interface. In the fully occluded thrombus model, the DF-RMF-assisted group achieved complete recanalization, with a thrombus clearance rate approximately five times that of the tPA-only group.Significance.The DF-RMF improved the long-distance capture and anti-washout retention of magnetic particles under flow conditions and enhanced thein vitrothrombolytic effect of tPA, providing a new approach for magnetically assisted thrombolysis.

articles.title: REV-ERBα deficiency exacerbates IL-33-mediated airway inflammation and airway hyperresponsiveness in mice.
articles.abstract: Asthma involves type 2 airway inflammation driven by epithelial-derived interleukin-33 (IL-33), a key mediator of allergic responses. REV-ERBα, a circadian transcriptional repressor, modulates pulmonary inflammation, but its role in IL-33-induced airway pathology remains unclear. Here we investigated IL-33-mediated pulmonary inflammation in wild-type and global Rev-erbα knockout mice exposed intranasally to recombinant IL-33. Loss of REV-ERBα markedly increased recruitment of eosinophils, neutrophils, innate lymphoid cells, and Th2 lymphocytes, exacerbated airway hyperresponsiveness, and elevated chemokines linked to type 2 inflammation. REV-ERBα deficiency also altered circadian clock protein expression, enhanced IL-33/ST2 signaling, and reduced epithelial barrier-associated proteins. These findings indicate that REV-ERBα restrains IL-33-driven airway inflammation and hyperresponsiveness, suggesting circadian mechanisms influence asthma pathogenesis and highlighting REV-ERBα as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Pembrolizumab-Induced Sarcoidosis-Like Immune-Related Adverse Events: A Pooled Analysis of Published Cases and Report of a Novel Manifestation Involving Phosphocalcic Metabolism.
articles.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors such as pembrolizumab can trigger immune-related adverse events, including rare sarcoidosis-like reactions (DISR), whose immunopathogenesis and clinical spectrum remain incompletely defined. We conducted a systematic review of all published cases of pembrolizumab-induced DISR, extracted and descriptively analyzed clinical, laboratory, imaging, and outcome data from 41 patients, and additionally report a 42-year-old woman who developed multiorgan DISR with a previously unreported metabolic complication involving dysregulated calcium homeostasis and ureteral double-J stent calcification. The median age at onset was 65 years, with melanoma as the most frequent underlying malignancy. Lymph nodes, lungs, and skin were the most commonly affected organs, and the median time to onset was 16 weeks, with some cases occurring after treatment discontinuation. ACE levels were elevated in 60% of cases, PET/CT showed increased FDG uptake in 95% of cases, and histologic confirmation was obtained in nearly all patients. Corticosteroids were the most frequent treatment, and 90.5% achieved stable disease or remission. Pembrolizumab-induced DISR is a rare irAE driven by immune dysregulation, and our case expands its clinical spectrum by identifying a novel manifestation of macrophage-mediated calcium dysregulation. Our pooled analysis of all published cases to date contributes to a broader understanding of this underrecognized entity. Early recognition is essential to avoid misdiagnosis of tumor progression, and DISR may serve as a potential biomarker of effective antitumor immune activation.

articles.title: miR-10b-5p targets TGFBR1 to promote keratinocyte-mediated wound healing in diabetic patients and has predictive prognostic value.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic wounds are known for their poor healing outcomes, and microRNAs (miRNAs) have emerged as key regulators of the wound healing process.

AIM: To investigate miR-10b-5p's predictive value in diabetic wound healing and the potential molecular mechanisms underlying its influence on the healing process.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Samples from patients with diabetic wounds were collected and divided into two groups: the good healing group and the delayed healing group. RT-qPCR was used to detect the levels of miR-10b-5p, TGFBR1 and VEGF. A ROC curve was used to evaluate the ability of miR-10b-5p to predict delayed wound healing in diabetic patients. Stimulation of HaCaT cells with 30 mM d-glucose mimics the pathological characteristics of diabetic skin wounds. The proliferation, apoptosis and migration of HaCaT cells were evaluated by CCK-8, flow cytometry and scratch assay. The database prediction, Pearson analysis, and dual luciferase assay demonstrated the targeting relationship between miR-10b-5p and TGFBR1.

RESULTS: In the delayed healing tissues, miR-10b-5p is downregulated while TGFBR1 is upregulated. miR-10b-5p can accurately predict the wound healing outcome of diabetes patients (AUC = 0.910, Sensitivity = 84.70 %, Specificity = 79.30 %). An HG environment inhibited the proliferation and migration of HaCaT cells and induced apoptosis. Overexpression of TGFBR1 reversed the effects of miR-10b-5p overexpression on the proliferation, apoptosis, migration and VEGF expression of HaCaT cells.

CONCLUSION: miR-10b-5p has good predictive value for diabetic wound healing and regulates HaCaT cell-mediated re-epithelialization by targeting TGFBR1.

articles.title: Efonidipine inhibiting CYP4A attenuates palmitate-induced hepatocyte lipotoxicity.
articles.abstract: Efonidipine, a dual L-/T-type calcium channel blocker (CCB), is a clinically established antihypertensive agent with cardiovascular and renoprotective effects. However, whether efonidipine affects CYP4A, a previously established mediator of hepatic lipotoxicity, remains unknown. In the present study, palmitate (PA)-induced steatotic HepG2 and SNU-449 hepatocytes were used to evaluate the hepatoprotective effects of efonidipine and its underlying mechanism. Efonidipine inhibited CYP4A enzyme activity, revealing a previously unrecognized CYP4A inhibitor. It also reduced CYP4A protein expression in PA-treated hepatocytes. This was accompanied by reduced intracellular lipid accumulation and lipogenesis, suppressed oxidative and ER stress, and improved insulin signaling and glucose uptake. These effects were consistently observed in both hepatocyte cell lines. Taken together, these findings suggest that efonidipine may represent a potential repurposing strategy for hepatic lipotoxicity through CYP4A inhibition.

articles.title: ATF4 alleviates doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy by promoting H2S production and antioxidant defense.
articles.abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX) remains a cornerstone in cancer treatment. However, its clinical utilization is significantly hampered by dose-dependent cardiotoxicity. The generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) constitutes the central component of the pathogenesis of DOX-induced cardiotoxicity. Activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4) has been demonstrated to exert a cardioprotective effect and augment cardiac antioxidative capacity in settings of heart failure. To explore the role of ATF4 in DOX-induced cardiomyopathy, cardiac-specific ATF4 conditional heterozygous mice and AAV9 mediated ATF4 overexpression mouse models were utilized. Cardiac function was assessed by echocardiography. The upstream regulator and downstream mediator of ATF4 were evaluated using RNA-seq analysis and further verified using ChIP assay and luciferase reporter assay. ATF4+/- mice exhibited a higher degree of susceptibility to DOX-induced cardiotoxicity in comparison with ATF4flox/flox mice. In contrast, cardiac-specific overexpression of ATF4 by AAV9 confers robust cardioprotection against DOX-induced cardiomyopathy. Mechanistically, we identified the upstream regulator of ATF4 as KLF16. Further, the decrease of ATF4 led to a reduction in cystathionine γ-lyase (CSE) transcription and hydrogen sulfide (H2S) production in the context of DOX-induced cardiotoxicity. ChIP and luciferase reporter assays revealed that ATF4 functioned as the transcription factor of the CSE gene. In contrast, the ectopic expression of ATF4 mitigated oxidative stress and apoptosis in DOX-induced cardiotoxicity, both in vivo and in vitro. The study identified a novel function of ATF4 in opposing oxidative stress in DOX cardiotoxicity through the promotion of CSE transcription. Targeting ATF4 may offer therapeutic benefits for DOX-induced cardiomyopathy.

articles.title: Cultivation strategies for Duddingtonia flagrans: A systematic review and bibliometric analysis.
articles.abstract: Gastrointestinal nematode infections represent one of the primary economic burdens for the global livestock industry. Duddingtonia flagrans (syn. Arthrobotrys flagrans) is the most promising biological control agent for these parasites due to its gastrointestinal-resistant chlamydospores (CL). However, industrial implementation is constrained by the lack of standardized mass-production protocols. This systematic review and bibliometric analysis consolidates evidence on culture media optimization to identify parameters maximizing CL yield, biomass accumulation, and enzymatic activity. Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search across PubMed, SCOPUS, Dimensions, and PATENTSCOPE (1991 to April 2026) yielded 48 eligible documents spanning three decades (1996-2025; 42 articles, 6 patents) generating 58 independent records. Most studies (79.2%) presented a low risk of bias. Research trends from the articles were mapped using Bibliometrix. In plate cultures, polyol supplementation (meso-inositol/mannitol) maximized yields up to 106 CL/cm2. Submerged fermentation exhibited high variability but reached 9.51 × 108 CL/mL in optimized media. Pure solid-state fermentation showed kinetic limitations, peaking at 1.60 × 106 CL/g. Biphasic fermentation combined liquid-phase biomass expansion with solid-phase induction, achieving 2.01 × 108 CL/g within 14 days. High predatory efficacy was reported in studies that assessed functional quality; however, this outcome was not evaluated consistently across cultivation systems. While direct comparisons remain constrained by heterogeneous reporting metrics and the reliance of certain high-yield benchmarks on patent disclosures, current evidence highlights biphasic systems and optimized submerged fermentation as promising platforms for scale-up, effectively mitigating several kinetic constraints of traditional single-phase methods.

articles.title: Targeting neurohormonal signaling cascades in cardiac hypertrophy: Multi-layered anti-hypertrophic paradigm of pyrogallol.
articles.abstract: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy represents a maladaptive response to chronic neurohumoral stimuli mediated by the overlapping renin-angiotensin system (RAS) and sympathetic nervous system (SNS). Continuous stimulation by Angiotensin II (Ang II) and norepinephrine (NE) drives adverse cardiac remodeling, subcellular microdomain remodeling, and embryonic fetal gene re-expression, accelerating progression to heart failure. Recent paradigms highlight the critical role of compartmentalized receptors situated in Golgi membranes in sustaining pro-hypertrophic signaling. Here, we examine the integrated signaling networks activated by Ang II and NE and delineate the multi-layered mechanisms by which the lipophilic polyphenol pyrogallol interrupts these cascades. Lipophilic properties may allow pyrogallol to act across compartments: (1) attenuating plasma membrane GPCR-G protein coupling (AT1R, α1-AR, β1-AR) and second messenger production (IP3, DAG, cAMP); (2) mitigating cytosolic Ca2+ overload and suppressing downstream MAPK signaling (ERK1/2, p38, JNK); (3) disrupting Golgi-localized Epac/PLCε complexes to prevent Protein Kinase D (PKD) phosphorylation; and (4) limiting nuclear translocation of transcription factors associated with embryonic fetal genes (ANP, BNP,β-MHC). Based on these preliminary mechanistic frameworks, pyrogallol represents a candidate molecule warranting further empirical validation as a potential neurohormonal stress brake.

articles.title: Regulatory mechanisms of E3 ubiquitin ligases in cholesterol homeostasis.
articles.abstract: Dysregulated cholesterol homeostasis fundamentally drives atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and related metabolic disorders. Some E3 ubiquitin ligases have emerged as central post-translational nodes that orchestrate cholesterol balance via a sophisticated dual-mode mechanism. Chronologically, they execute rapid, direct ubiquitination and degradation of rate-limiting enzymes (e.g., HMGCR, SQLE), LDL receptors, and cholesterol efflux transporters for acute lipid adaptation, while simultaneously orchestrating slower, transcriptional reprogramming by targeting upstream sensors (e.g., Insigs and LXRs) to reset long-term homeostatic setpoints. This review systematically dissects how distinct classes of E3 ligases-including RING-, HECT-, and RBR-type-coordinately govern cholesterol synthesis, uptake, efflux, and esterification. Furthermore, we discuss the therapeutic prospects of targeting these ligase networks in combating dyslipidemia and its cardiovascular sequelae.

articles.title: Stage-dependent expression of CB1 and CB2 receptors and their vascular effects during the progression of diet-induced atherosclerosis.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the leading cause of global mortality, with ischemic heart disease and stroke representing the most common clinical manifestations. Atherosclerosis, a chronic inflammatory disorder of the arterial wall, constitutes the primary pathological basis of these conditions. Recent studies have implicated the endocannabinoid system (ECS), which includes cannabinoid receptors CB1 and CB2, their endogenous ligands, and metabolic enzymes, in the pathophysiology of atherosclerosis. In the present study, we explored the molecular and functional interactions between the ECS and diet-induced atherosclerosis in Wistar rats. Our results show distinct expression patterns of CB1 and CB2 receptors in the aortic wall, with significant downregulation observed in the advanced stages of atherosclerosis. Functional assays demonstrated stage-dependent vascular responses to selective CB1 and CB2 agonists, indicating that modulation of the ECS influences vascular tone and blood pressure. Additionally, biochemical analysis of endocannabinoids and their catabolic enzymes, including 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG)/monoacylglycerol lipase (MAGL) and anandamide (AEA)/fatty acid amide hydrolase (FAAH), revealed dynamic alterations throughout the course of disease progression. These findings underscore the critical role of the ECS in vascular homeostasis and suggest that cannabinoid-based therapeutic strategies may hold potential for the management of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

articles.title: Complete genome sequence and methylome analysis of Dermacoccus nishinomiyaensis strain 1-2 isolated from sushi.
articles.abstract: Dermacoccus nishinomiyaensis is an actinomycete whose isolation from diverse environments and potential for opportunistic pathogenicity have been documented. Here, we report the complete genome sequence of D. nishinomiyaensis 1-2, isolated from sushi. We provide annotation statistics and insights, such as the antiphage systems arsenal of the strain, including its methylome.

articles.title: ZSP1601 is a non-selective phosphodiesterase inhibitor and a clinical drug candidate for the oral treatment of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a growing global health challenge. Its advanced stage, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), involves complex processes such as metabolic dysregulation, inflammation, and fibrosis. Existing treatments mainly target steatosis but have limited success. Therefore, focusing on inflammation and fibrosis may offer more effective therapeutic options. Phosphodiesterases regulate cAMP/cGMP signaling and are key in MASH-related inflammation and fibrosis. Inhibiting specific PDE subtypes is a promising approach for drug development in MASH. This study presents a comprehensive preclinical pharmacological and pharmacokinetic profile of ZSP1601, a non-selective phosphodiesterase inhibitor currently in clinical trials for MASH. ZSP1601 was developed through structural optimization of pentoxifylline via a three-step chemical synthesis. Molecular docking and enzymatic assays confirmed its role as a non-selective PDE inhibitor. In vitro, ZSP1601 significantly lowered TNF-α levels, showed strong anti-inflammatory effects, and was more effective than pentoxifylline at the same dose. In vivo, ZSP1601 markedly reduced liver NAS scores in the STZ + HFD model and decreased fibrosis in the CDAHFD model in a dose-dependent manner. Consistent with these results, data from liver fibrosis models demonstrated that ZSP1601 significantly alleviated hepatocellular injury and reduced hepatic fibrosis. Pharmacokinetic studies indicated that ZSP1601 has favorable properties in mice, rats, and beagle dogs after single and multiple doses. In summary, ZSP1601, a non-selective PDE inhibitor, presents a promising new treatment for MASH by effectively improving disease outcomes. It is currently being evaluated in a phase II clinical trial.

articles.title: Oxygen Delivery during Cardiopulmonary Bypass and Postoperative Mortality: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oxygen delivery during cardiopulmonary bypass reflects the balance between pump flow, hemoglobin concentration, and arterial oxygenation and is a key determinant of tissue oxygen transport. While inadequate oxygen delivery has been linked to postoperative organ dysfunction, its association with mortality remains unclear.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted including 4,358 adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass at a tertiary center between 2018 and 2024. Time-weighted average indexed oxygen delivery (DO 2i ) was calculated from pump flow, arterial oxygen saturation, hemoglobin concentration, and body surface area. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI), stroke, and intensive care unit and hospital length of stay. Associations were evaluated using multivariable regression models adjusted for demographic, clinical, and procedural factors.

RESULTS: Lower intraoperative DO 2i was associated with higher 30-day mortality. Overall, 75 patients (1.7%) died within 30 days. Each 10-ml · min -1 · m -2 decrease in DO 2i was associated with increased odds of mortality (adjusted odds ratio [OR adj ], 1.16; 95% CI, 1.09 to 1.23; P < 0.001). The adjusted 30-day mortality was 1.69% (95% CI, 1.32 to 2.05%) at the 25th percentile of DO 2i (226.2 ml · min -1 · m -2 ) compared with 0.74% (95% CI 0.41 to 1.07%) at the 75th percentile (295.6 ml · min -1 · m -2 ). Lower DO 2i was also associated with AKI (OR adj , 1.05; 95% CI, 1.03 to 1.07; P < 0.001) and with longer intensive care unit (adjusted incidence rate ratio, 1.02; 95% CI, 1.01 to 1.03; P < 0.001) and hospital length of stay (adjusted incidence rate ratio, 1.01; 95% CI, 1.01-1.02; P < 0.001) but not with stroke (OR adj , 1.00; 95% CI, 0.95 to 1.06; P = 0.877).

CONCLUSIONS: Patients receiving lower intraoperative DO 2i during cardiopulmonary bypass had a higher risk of postoperative mortality, AKI, and prolonged recovery. These findings support the clinical relevance of oxygen delivery during bypass and provide a rationale for future mechanistic and interventional studies.

articles.title: Belowground carbon use in woody plants under experimental warming: uneven evidence for fine-root, root-exudation and mycorrhizal responses.
articles.abstract: How warming changes belowground carbon use in woody plants remains poorly understood. Most experiments measure fine-root, root-exudation and mycorrhizal responses separately, providing limited evidence on how these responses vary together within the same experiment. We synthesized 13 primary publications from 11 independent experiments: 8 field, 1 outdoor pot and 2 controlled experiments. Our synthesis showed no significant increase in fine-root biomass or production. Root respiration, mortality and nitrogen (N) concentration increased, whereas root phosphorus (P) and non-structural carbohydrate concentrations decreased. Root-exudation measurements were reported differently across studies, limiting direct comparisons. Root-exudation responses also varied with nutrient treatment, season and warming duration, while exudate quantity and composition did not always change together. Most mycorrhizal studies measured colonization or infection rather than direct plant-fungal carbon and nutrient exchange. Among the mycorrhizal studies included here, an isotope-based carbon-for-nitrogen ratio proxy varied with N source and sampling time. When multiple belowground responses were measured within the same experiment, concurrent increases in fine-root activity, root exudation and mycorrhizal association occurred only under particular nutrient and temporal conditions and were not a general response to warming. Opposing responses did not demonstrate compensation; no study showed that an increase in one pathway offset a decrease in another in terms of nutrient acquisition or plant performance. Testing whether warming reallocates carbon among fine roots, root exudation, and mycorrhizal fungi will require coordinated measurements of carbon supply, comparable belowground carbon fluxes, plant nutrient acquisition and competing carbon sinks within the same experiment.

articles.title: Letter to the editor: urban-rural classification and readmission risk estimates in younger adults with ischaemic stroke: a secondary analysis.
The rural-urban divide in stroke readmissions: a question of definition, not just geography.
Prasugrel versus Ticagrelor in Acute Coronary Syndromes.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether prasugrel or ticagrelor should be the preferred P2Y12 inhibitor for patients with an acute coronary syndrome is uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a registry-based, open-label, stepped-wedge, cluster-randomized trial in Sweden involving adults who had undergone percutaneous coronary intervention for an acute coronary syndrome. Seven regions, grouped into three clusters, switched from ticagrelor to prasugrel as the default P2Y12 inhibitor in a randomized sequence across four 9-month periods between 2021 and 2024. The primary end point was a composite of death from any cause, fatal or nonfatal myocardial infarction, or fatal or nonfatal stroke through 1 year, as ascertained from national registries. In the intention-to-treat analysis, a mixed model adjusted for cluster and calendar time was used to obtain a policy-level estimate.

RESULTS: A total of 17,095 patients were enrolled; 9444 received care under the default ticagrelor policy, and 7651 received care under the default prasugrel policy. The mean (±SD) age of the patients was 69.8±11.5 years, and 36.8% were at least 75 years old; 27.8% of the patients were female. A total of 39.4% presented with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), 43.7% with non-STEMI, and 16.8% with unstable angina. At 1 year, a primary end-point event had occurred in 11.8% of the patients in the ticagrelor-policy group and in 11.1% of those in the prasugrel-policy group (adjusted odds ratio [prasugrel vs. ticagrelor], 0.90; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.77 to 1.06), and major bleeding had occurred in 4.4% and 4.2%, respectively (adjusted odds ratio, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.64 to 0.99).

CONCLUSIONS: In an unselected population of patients with an acute coronary syndrome who had undergone percutaneous coronary intervention, the risk of ischemic events was not lower with a default prasugrel policy than with a default ticagrelor policy. (Funded by Region Västra Götaland; SWITCH-SWEDEHEART ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05183178.).

articles.title: The Emerging Role of Treatment Policy Implementation Trials in Acute Coronary Syndrome.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine

articles.title: Recent Advances in Camphor-Derived Small-Molecule Organic Fluorescent Probes.
articles.abstract: Camphor, a naturally occurring bicyclic monoterpenoid, has attracted increasing interest as a structural scaffold for the construction of fluorescent probes owing to its rigid framework, facile functionalization, and favorable biocompatibility. In recent years, a variety of camphor-derived fluorescent probes have been developed for the detection of metal ions, reactive biological species, microenvironmental factors, and environmental contaminants. This review summarizes recent advances in camphor-based fluorescent probes reported from 2019 to early 2026. According to their target analytes, these probes are classified into four categories: metal cations, reactive biological species, microenvironmental factors, and environmental contaminants. Their molecular design strategies, synthetic routes, fluorescence sensing mechanisms, and representative analytical applications are systematically discussed. Representative sensing mechanisms, including photoinduced electron transfer (PET), intramolecular charge transfer (ICT), excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT), aggregation-induced emission (AIE), and Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET), are also introduced. Finally, the current challenges and future perspectives for the development of camphor-based fluorescent probes are discussed, including fluorophore design, sensing mechanisms, near-infrared emission, and practical applications in complex biological and environmental systems. This review provides an overview of recent progress in camphor-based fluorescent probes and may serve as a useful reference for future research in this field.

articles.title: Sapablursen for erythrocytosis control in patients with polycythemia vera.
articles.abstract: Polycythemia vera is characterized by erythrocytosis and an increased risk of thrombosis. Sapablursen is an antisense oligonucleotide that suppresses transmembrane serine protease 6, increases hepcidin production, and reduces iron availability for erythropoiesis. IMPRSSION is an ongoing phase 2a, randomized, open-label study in patients with phlebotomy-dependent polycythemia vera. Cohort A (120 or 80 mg) and cohort B (40 mg) received sapablursen subcutaneously once every 4 weeks. The primary efficacy end point was the reduction in phlebotomy frequency from baseline to weeks 17 to 37 in patients who received ≥1 dose. The baseline mean ± standard deviation weekly phlebotomy rate was 0.15 ± 0.07 in cohort A and 0.17 ± 0.07 in cohort B, with reduction by -0.10 (95% confidence interval [CI], -0.13 to -0.07; n = 32; P< .0001) in cohort A and by -0.10 (95% CI, -0.14 to -0.06; n = 17; P = .0001) in cohort B. Sapablursen reduced the median number of phlebotomies from 5.0 at baseline (26 weeks) to 0 in cohort A and 1.5 in cohort B in the efficacy evaluation window (20 weeks). Most adverse events were mild or moderate; anemia and fatigue were most common. The mean change in the myeloproliferative neoplasm-symptom assessment form total symptom score at week 37 was -6.21 points (95% CI, -10.56 to -1.85; P = .0052) in cohort A and -2.71 points in cohort B (95% CI, -8.33 to 2.91; P = .34). Sapablursen reduced phlebotomy need, improved symptoms, and was safe and well tolerated in patients with polycythemia vera. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as NCT05143957.

articles.title: Policy priorities to strengthen specialist heart failure nursing in Europe: findings from a Delphi study.
Risk of recurrence in patients with provoked venous thromboembolism: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) provoked by transient risk factors is generally considered low risk, supporting short-term anticoagulation. However, this paradigm is based on heterogeneous definitions of provoking factors. In this prospective cohort study, we evaluated recurrence risk using the International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis classification of major and minor transient risk factors. Patients with symptomatic deep vein thrombosis and/or pulmonary embolism who completed ≥3 months of anticoagulation were followed after treatment discontinuation. Patients with cancer, major thrombophilia, pregnancy-associated VTE, or indication for extended anticoagulation were excluded. The primary outcome was symptomatic recurrent VTE. Cumulative incidence was estimated by Kaplan-Meier analysis. The study was terminated early due to unexpectedly high recurrence risk among patients with major provoking factors. Between 2019 and 2025, 242 patients were followed for a median of 23.9 months; 72 had major and 170 had minor transient risk factors. Recurrent VTE occurred in 13 patients with major and 7 with minor risk factors. At 24 months, recurrence risk was 9.5% (95% confidence interval [CI], 6.0-14.0) overall and 19.7% (11.0-30.2) after major and 5.0% (2.2-9.5) after minor risk factors. No recurrence occurred in 81 women with hormone-associated VTE; after their exclusion, the recurrence risk among patients with other minor risk factors increased to 9.1% (95% CI, 4.0-17.0). Recurrence after provoked VTE is not uniformly low and varies substantially by the type of transient risk factor. These findings challenge current treatment paradigms and support individualized decisions regarding anticoagulation duration.

articles.title: Urban-rural classification and readmission risk estimates in younger adults with ischaemic stroke: a secondary analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Hospital readmissions following ischaemic stroke remain a serious concern in cardiovascular care, particularly among younger adults whose recovery needs differ from older populations. This study examined predictors of 30-day readmission among stroke survivors aged 19-64 years, with a focus on how different rural-urban classifications influence estimated associations between geography and readmission outcomes.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We conducted a retrospective secondary analysis of hospital discharge data from the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project State Inpatient Databases (2012-15) for six US states. The sample included 85 667 adults aged 19-64 years hospitalized for acute ischaemic stroke. Geographic location was operationalized using multiple rural-urban classifications derived from Urban Influence Codes. Multivariable logistic regression models assessed predictors of planned and unplanned 30-day readmission.Geographic location was not a consistent predictor of readmission across alternative rurality definitions. Living in a large metropolitan area was associated with slightly higher odds of unplanned readmission when compared with other locations (adjusted odds ratio 1.06; 95% CI 1.00-1.12), but this association was not observed when alternative rural-urban classifications were applied. Across models, significant predictors of readmission included age, payer type, length of stay, and number of chronic conditions.

CONCLUSION: Associations between geographic location and stroke readmission outcomes varied depending on how rural-urban classifications were defined. These findings highlight the importance of methodological clarity when interpreting geographic effects in secondary analyses of administrative data and have implications for cardiovascular nurses involved in discharge planning and transitional care for younger stroke survivors.

articles.title: Latent profiles of social isolation and loneliness and their associations with inflammation and clinical outcomes in older patients with heart failure: a prospective longitudinal study.
Structured nurse-administered Delirium Observation Screening Scale detects probable hypoactive delirium missed by clinical intervention criteria in cardiac surgery intensive care unit patients.
Lisocabtagene maraleucel combined with ibrutinib in R/R CLL or SLL: primary results from TRANSCEND CLL 004.
articles.abstract: Patients in the lisocabtagene maraleucel (liso-cel) plus ibrutinib cohort of the phase 1/2, open-label TRANSCEND CLL 004 study had relapsed/refractory (R/R) chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)/small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL) and received liso-cel (50 × 106 [dose level 1 (DL1)] or 100 × 106 [DL2] chimeric antigen receptor-positive T cells) with concurrent ibrutinib from enrollment through 90 days after liso-cel infusion or longer per investigator discretion. Primary end point was complete response/remission (CR)/CR with incomplete marrow recovery (CRi) by investigator assessment. Among 56 patients who received ibrutinib plus liso-cel (DL1, n = 5; DL2, n = 51), median age was 64.5 years (range, 44-77), 98% had high-risk cytogenetics, and median number of prior therapies was 5 (range, 1-13). Median follow-up was 24.8 months (range, 3.1-51.8). At DL2, CR/CRi rate was 45% (95% confidence interval [CI], 31-60), and overall response rate was 86% (95% CI, 74-94). Median duration of response was not reached (NR; 95% CI, 28.7 to NR) for patients with CR/CRi. Median progression-free survival was 31.4 months (95% CI, 20.1 to NR). In DL1 plus DL2, the most common grade ≥3 treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were neutropenia (52%) and anemia (41%). Cytokine release syndrome was reported in 80% of the patients (grade 3, 4%; no grade 4/5), and neurological events were reported in 41% (grade 3/4, 11%; no grade 5). Ibrutinib-related TEAEs were reported in 68% of the patients (grade 3/4, 43%; no grade 5). Liso-cel plus ibrutinib demonstrated notable efficacy in patients with R/R CLL/SLL with predictable and manageable safety. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as NCT03331198 and NCT03435796.

articles.title: Effects of non-pharmacological interventions on post-operative delirium in cardiac surgery patients: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Although non-pharmacological interventions (NPIs) are important for preventing post-operative delirium, their comparative effectiveness in cardiac surgery patients remains unclear. This study aimed to compare different NPIs and identify the most effective strategy using a network meta-analysis (NMA).

METHODS AND RESULTS: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were identified through systematic searches of PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, CNKI, Wanfang Data, and the VIP Database. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool. NMA was conducted using Stata 18.0. Post-operative delirium incidence was summarized as odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and delirium duration as mean differences (MDs) with 95% CIs. A total of 26 RCTs (n = 2913) were included. Overall, NPIs were associated with a reduced incidence of post-operative delirium compared with routine care (OR = 0.42, 95% CI = 0.34-0.50, P < 0.05, I2= 51%). In the NMA, multicomponent therapy (OR = 0.30, 95% CI = 0.19-0.47) and health education (OR = 0.33, 95% CI = 0.12-0.88) significantly reduced delirium incidence. NPIs also shortened delirium duration (MD = -0.96, 95% CI = -1.06 to -0.86, P < 0.05, I2 = 0%), with multicomponent therapy showing the greatest reduction.

CONCLUSION: NPIs reduce the incidence and duration of post-operative delirium in patients undergoing cardiac surgery, with multicomponent therapy combining several non-pharmacological strategies targeting different modifiable risk factors, such as delirium assessment, clinical adjustment, environmental control, and early mobilization, showing the most favourable effects.

REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO: CRD420250655564.

articles.title: Rivaroxaban Then Aspirin vs. Aspirin Alone after Total Hip or Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aspirin after an initial short course of rivaroxaban has been shown to be safe and effective for the prevention of venous thromboembolism after total hip or total knee arthroplasty, but uncertainty remains about the use of aspirin alone.

METHODS: In this multicenter, double-blind, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned patients to receive once-daily thromboprophylaxis with either 81 mg of aspirin or 10 mg of oral rivaroxaban for the first 5 days after total hip or total knee arthroplasty. All the patients then received further thromboprophylaxis with 81 mg of aspirin daily for 9 additional days after knee arthroplasty and for 30 additional days after hip arthroplasty. Patients were followed for 90 days for symptomatic venous thromboembolism, which consisted of either proximal deep-vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism (primary effectiveness outcome), and for bleeding complications (primary safety outcome). The noninferiority margin for aspirin alone as compared with rivaroxaban-aspirin was 0.7 percentage points.

RESULTS: A total of 5429 patients underwent randomization. Venous thromboembolism developed in 13 of 2718 patients (0.48%) in the aspirin-alone group and in 12 of 2647 patients (0.45%) in the rivaroxaban-aspirin group (risk difference, 0.02 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.34 to 0.39; P<0.001 for noninferiority). Major bleeding or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding events occurred in 45 of 2718 patients (1.66%) in the aspirin-alone group and in 54 of 2647 patients (2.04%) in the rivaroxaban-aspirin group (risk difference, -0.38%; 95% CI, -1.11 to 0.34).

CONCLUSIONS: After total hip and total knee arthroplasty, the use of aspirin alone was not inferior to a strategy of using rivaroxaban followed by aspirin for the prevention of symptomatic venous thromboembolism, with no clinically relevant difference in bleeding events. (Funded by the Canadian Institutes of Health Research; EPCAT III ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04075240.).

articles.title: Determinants of risk factor target attainment after myocardial infarction: the Perfect-CR study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: How individual components of cardiac rehabilitation (CR) programmes predict attainment of risk factor targets after myocardial infarction (MI), and their predictive strength relative to patient characteristics, remain unclear. We aimed to identify organizational and patient-level predictors of risk factor target attainment at 1-year post-MI.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Organizational structure and processes followed at all 78 CR centres in Sweden were surveyed and merged with patient-level registry data (n = 6755). Predictors of attaining low-density lipoprotein-cholesterol (LDL-C) and blood pressure (BP) targets and smoking abstinence were identified using orthogonal partial least squares discriminant analysis, generating variables of importance for the projection (VIP) values. Variables with VIP > 0.8 were considered meaningful. The strongest predictors for attaining LDL-C and BP targets included availability of psychosocial management, medication adjustment protocols for nurses, continuity in nurse-patient contact, extended opening hours and adequate facilities, and having a medical director at the CR centre. The strongest patient-level predictors of attaining LDL-C and/or BP targets included low baseline LDL-C and having no history of hypertension, respectively, and the patient having participated in exercise-based CR. For smoking abstinence, the strongest organizational predictors were availability of psychosocial management, having a medical director, prescribing nicotine replacement therapy and varenicline, and self-reported team spirit. Patient-level predictors included having participated in exercise-based CR and group education.

CONCLUSION: We identified multiple CR organizational predictors of attaining key risk factor targets after MI. These results may influence the future design of comprehensive CR programmes.

articles.title: Impact of continuous pharmaceutical care by a collaborative pharmacy team on reducing drug-related problems in coronary heart disease patients: a randomized controlled trial in an integrated healthcare system.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Building upon continuous pharmaceutical care (CPC) models led solely by clinical pharmacists, this study evaluated a collaborative pharmacy team model for reducing drug-related problems (DRPs) in coronary heart disease (CHD) patients during care transitions.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In a randomized controlled trial, 60 hospitalized CHD patients were allocated equally to a CPC group or a usual-care control group. The CPC group received structured pharmaceutical interventions in which clinical pharmacists led hospital care and community pharmacists led post-discharge care during key care transition periods: within 24 h of admission (T0), 24 h pre-discharge (T1), 24-72 h post-discharge (T2), and at 1-month follow-up (T3). Drug-related problems were identified using the Pharmaceutical Care Network Europe classification. Mean DRPs per patient were comparable at T0 (control: 3.03 ± 1.16 vs. CPC: 3.10 ± 1.24; P = 0.827). Subsequently, the CPC group showed significantly fewer DRPs than the control group at T1 (0.17 ± 0.59 vs. 2.13 ± 1.04), T2 (0.03 ± 0.18 vs. 1.97 ± 1.03), and T3 (0.67 ± 0.76 vs. 2.63 ± 1.13) (all P < 0.001). Pharmacist interventions in the CPC group had a high DRP acceptance rate 91.4% (181/198) and a resolution rate 89.1% (106/119). At 1-month follow-up, the CPC group demonstrated superior outcomes compared with the control group: LDL-C goal attainment (63.3 vs. 30.0%, P = 0.010), medication adherence (90.0 vs. 66.7%, P = 0.028), patient satisfaction (Numeric Rating Scale: 9.27 ± 0.52 vs. 8.59 ± 0.52, P < 0.001), and willingness to pay for pharmaceutical services (86.7 vs. 50.0%, P = 0.002).

CONCLUSION: This collaborative pharmacy team model effectively reduced DRPs and improved lipid control and patient-reported outcomes in CHD patients, offering a scalable approach for integrated healthcare systems.

REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: ChiCTR2400086416.

articles.title: Integrating psychological care into atrial fibrillation management: insights from HOPE-AF.
A Potential Adjunctive Role of 7T MRI and Amino Acid PET in Localizing MRI-Occult Functional Pituitary Microadenomas: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Functional pituitary adenomas (FPAs), especially those "MRI-occult" on 1.5T/3T and smaller than 10 mm, present diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, leading to repeated investigations, invasive procedures, and suboptimal outcomes.

PURPOSE: This review examines the potential clinical use and limitations of 7T MRI and amino acid (AA)-PET with tracers like L-[methyl-11C]methionine (MET) or O-(2-[18F]fluoroethyl)-L-tyrosine (FET) for detecting MRI-occult FPAs.

DATA SOURCES: A systematic search of Medline, Embase, and Web of Science was performed up to August 2025, following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines.

STUDY SELECTION: Studies evaluating 7T MRI and AA-PET for MRI-occult PAs were included and independently reviewed by 3 authors.

DATA ANALYSIS: Eighteen studies met inclusion criteria: 4 evaluated the 7T MRI, 8 MET-PET, 3 FET-PET, and 3 hybrid/multitracer approaches.

DATA SYNTHESIS: 7T MRI offers superior spatial resolution, increased signal-to-noise ratio, and improved tissue contrast. AA-PET provides high tumor-to-background contrast, facilitating MRI-occult PAs localization.

LIMITATIONS: Despite these advances, small cohort sizes, heterogeneous protocols, high costs, and limited accessibility limit the current evidence base.

CONCLUSIONS: Ultra-high-field 7T MRI and AA-PET represent emerging complementary imaging techniques for MRI-occult FPAs. Current evidence is preliminary, underscoring the need to standardize protocols, conduct prospective multicenter studies, and assess cost-effectiveness before widespread clinical adoption.

articles.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist Exposure and Long-Term Outcomes in Patients with Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis: A Propensity Score-Matched Real-World Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Asymptomatic carotid stenosis is a prevalent manifestation of atherosclerotic disease and, despite contemporary guideline-directed medical therapy, remains associated with downstream cerebrovascular events and mortality. Given the vascular and cardiometabolic benefits of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1As), we evaluated whether GLP-1A exposure is associated with lower long-term event rates in patients with asymptomatic carotid stenosis.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study used the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Adults (≥18 years) with carotid stenosis (January 1, 2016, to September 30, 2025) were included; patients with prior/baseline cerebrovascular events and those undergoing carotid revascularization within 6 months were excluded to operationalize an asymptomatic cohort. GLP-1A exposure was defined as any GLP-1A use within 6 months after carotid stenosis diagnosis; nonexposed patients served as comparators. Cohorts were propensity score-matched 1:1, and outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: After matching, 30,332 patients were included in each cohort. GLP-1A exposure was associated with lower hazards of ischemic stroke (hazard ratio [HR] 0.63, 0.71, and 0.73 at 1, 3, and 5 years; 5-year cumulative event probability 5.55% versus 6.85%), hemorrhagic stroke (HR 0.63, 0.69, and 0.74; 2.04% versus 2.35%), large vessel occlusion stroke (HR 0.70, 0.77, and 0.81; 2.04% versus 2.27%), and all-cause mortality (HR 0.42, 0.58, and 0.64; 17.11% versus 21.49%). The composite of ischemic stroke or mortality was also lower (HR 0.48, 0.61, and 0.66; 20.88% versus 25.85% at 5 years) in the GLP-1A-exposed cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: In a large real-world cohort with asymptomatic carotid stenosis, GLP-1A exposure was associated with lower hazards of stroke subtypes, large vessel occlusion stroke, and mortality across 1-5 years. These observational findings warrant prospective validation to clarify causality and optimal integration into contemporary medical management.

articles.title: Developing shared decision-making workflow for cardiovascular health: a modified delphi process.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: National guidelines recommend implementing team-based care and shared decision-making (SDM) for improving hypertension control and cardiovascular health. However, best practices for integrating SDM into clinical workflows for health behaviour change and medication management in adults with hypertension and multiple cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk factors remains unclear. The study aimed to develop SDM workflows to inform design of patient decision aids to support health behaviour change and medication management of adults with hypertension and multiple CVD risk factors.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This study used a modified Delphi method with a geographically diverse panel of 18 interprofessional team members. The process included two Rounds of online Delphi surveys between May and October 2024, followed by a virtual panel meeting in November 2024. Consensus was defined as ≥75% of panelists rating items of the SDM workflow as important or very important with each Round of the online Delphi surveys. Of the 18 expert panelists, the majority was female (n = 15, 83.3%) with a mean age of 49.8 years (standard deviation: 12.9). The Delphi process resulted in two SDM workflows to improve health behaviour change and medication management: one with 70 items focused on hypertension control, and another with 75 items addressing the management of multiple CVD risk factors.

CONCLUSION: The study developed two SDM workflows to support hypertension control and CVD risk factor management. These workflows offer a structured approach to integrating SDM into clinical practice and may serve as a guide for designing patient decision aids in cardiovascular health.

articles.title: Reflexology for pain and anxiety in patients undergoing coronary angiography: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The aim of this study was to evaluate the effects of reflexology, a non-pharmacological nursing intervention, on pain and anxiety in patients undergoing coronary angiography.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024607829). A comprehensive literature search was performed in PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane, Clinical Key, and Google Scholar between 15 October 2024 and 15 January 2025, covering studies published from 2000 to 2025. Eight randomized controlled trials and two quasi-experimental studies investigating the effects of reflexology on pain and anxiety in patients undergoing coronary angiography were included. Methodological quality was independently assessed by two reviewers using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (ROB2) and the ROBINS-I tools. Effect sizes were calculated using standardized mean difference (Hedges' g) with 95% confidence intervals for eligible outcomes. A total of 10 studies involving 913 participants were included. Reflexology significantly reduced anxiety levels immediately after the intervention (Hedges' g = -1.78; 95% CI -2.94 to -0.63) and 30 min post-intervention (Hedges' g = -1.16; 95% CI -2.10 to -0.22). Due to heterogeneous pain measurement scales, pooled meta-analysis for pain was not performed. Narrative synthesis indicated reduced pain intensity in the early post-procedural period.

CONCLUSION: Reflexology may be a beneficial and feasible non-pharmacological nurse-led intervention for reducing anxiety and early post-procedural pain in patients undergoing coronary angiography. Integrating reflexology into cardiovascular nursing practice may support symptom management, patient comfort, and psychological well-being as an adjunct to standard cardiac care.

REGISTRATION: PROSPERO: CRD42024607829.

articles.title: Effects of a 2-year randomized controlled trial of parenting centers on caregiver mental health in rural China.
articles.abstract: This study examines how center-based parenting interventions aimed at improving early child development in rural China affect the mental health of caregivers. Data from an analytic sample of 615 caregiver-child dyads (children aged 6 to 24 months, 48.5% girls; data collection: 2015-2017) in a 2-year cluster randomized controlled trial conducted in 100 villages showed that the intervention had no significant effect on caregiver depressive (β = - .047, SE = .079), anxiety (β = .040, SE = .076), or stress (β = .032, SE = .081) symptoms. Subgroup analyses found no significant difference in effects on mental health by prespecified characteristics after adjustment for multiple comparisons, except that the caregivers of children without social-emotional delay at baseline exhibited lower depression scores after the intervention (β = - .205, SE = .097, p = .043). The findings suggest that the center-based parenting intervention focused solely on strengthening parenting skills may be insufficient to improve caregiver mental health over 2 years.

articles.title: Improving children's collective and individual moral reasoning through small-group discussions about narrative fiction.
articles.abstract: This randomized trial tested whether small-group discussions about narrative fiction improve children's collective and individual moral reasoning. The sample consisted of 704 Swiss children (Mage = 10.32, 49.3% girls, 29.8% with a non-Swiss German home language), 159 discussion groups, and 51 teachers across 3 waves in 2022-2023. Data included coded discussions and essays on conflicts between fairness and group loyalty. The intervention enhanced collective reasoning, indicated by increases in student talk, questions, reasons, challenges, and build-ons (RRs = 1.37-8.62) and decreases in unreasoned claims (RR = 0.49). For individual reasoning, children in the intervention group provided more moral justifications (RR = 1.67) but not more group-based justifications and shifted to higher justification levels, including more dual-domain responses (OR = 2.05).

articles.title: The impact of online-offline integrated out-of-hospital education on patients with heart failure: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Poor post-discharge management worsens heart failure (HF) outcomes. Integrated online-offline education (O2O-IOPE) may improve clinical outcomes but remains unquantified. This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to evaluate the effects of O2O-IOPE on the health outcomes of patients with HF.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We searched PubMed, The Cochrane Library, Embase, Web of Science, CNKI, and Wanfang Data from database inception to 18 April 2025, for randomized controlled trials on O2O-IOPE in patients with HF. A total of 13 studies were ultimately included, involving 3216 patients. Quantitative analyses showed that O2O-IOPE can reduce all-cause mortality [risk ratio (RR) = 0.61, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.46 to 0.81, P < 0.01], improve patients' left ventricular ejection fraction [mean difference (MD) = 0.66, 95% CI = 0.11 to 1.21, P = 0.02), quality of life (standardized mean difference, SMD = -0.82, 95% CI = -1.00 to -0.65, P < 0.01), and self-care ability (SMD = 1.81, 95% CI = 0.73 to 2.90, P < 0.01). However, non-significant effects were observed on rehospitalization rate (RR = 0.88, 95% CI = 0.49 to 1.57, P = 0.66), 6-minute walk test (6MWT) (MD = 69.84, 95% CI = -13.76 to 153.43, P = 0.10), or health-related knowledge (SMD = 3.09, 95% CI = -1.55 to 7.72, P = 0.19). Qualitative synthesis suggested potential benefits in the New York Heart Association class, medication adherence, depressive symptoms, and self-efficacy; however, because these findings were each derived from single studies, they should be considered preliminary and not conclusive.

CONCLUSION: The O2O-IOPE framework significantly improves mortality, cardiac function, quality of life, and self-care in patients with HF. Its effectiveness appears to depend more on the quality of integration, particularly active response mechanisms and structured offline components, than on specific digital tools or delivery settings. Future research should focus on optimizing integration strategies and evaluating long-term outcomes across diverse populations.

REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420251101980.

articles.title: ASFNR Current State of Practice in Neuroimaging of Distal Medium Vessel Occlusion Stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Distal medium vessel occlusions (DMVO) constitute approximately 25%-40% of acute ischemic stroke. These potentially disabling strokes remain diagnostically challenging due to vessel caliber, tortuosity, and low sensitivity of standard CT angiography. Multiple recent multicenter randomized controlled trials including Endovascular Therapy Plus Best Medical Treatment Versus BMT Alone for Medium Vessel Occlusion Stroke (DISTAL), Endovascular treatment to improve outcomes for Medium Vessel Occlusions (ESCAPE-MeVO), Evaluation of mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke related to a distal arterial occlusion (DISCOUNT), Endovascular treatment in acute intracranial distal medium vessel occlusion stroke (ORIENTAL-MeVO) and Distal Ischemic Stroke Treatment with Adjustable Low-Profile Stentriever (DISTALS), showed overall heterogenous results of mechanical thrombectomy (MT) over best medical treatment to treat DMVO, with higher symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage rates in the MT arm.

METHODS: Summarize current evidence and provide a "state of practice" guide for radiologists on DMVO detection, workflow standardization, triage, and imaging-based prognostication.

KEY MESSAGE: Optimized CTA (including multiphase), CT Perfusion (territorial Tmax), and MRI DWI/SWI improve diagnostic confidence for DMVO. Certain perfusion parameters indicative of collateral status, for instance, relative cerebral blood volume index and hypoperfusion intensity ratio, have prognostic value. Structured reporting of important positive and negative radiologic findings can guide neurologic triage despite neutral trials. Radiologists play a central role in DMVO diagnosis and prognostication. Standardized imaging workflows are essential in the post-trial landscape.

articles.title: Causal mediation mechanisms underlying early childhood development interventions in rural China.
