articles.abstract: This study examined how early childhood development (ECD) interventions improved children's developmental outcomes in rural China. The three-wave panel data were drawn from a randomized controlled trial with a village-based parenting center intervention conducted between 2016 and 2018. Involving 1,613 children (aged 6-36 months, 52% boys) and their primary caregivers (70% mothers, predominantly Han ethnicity), the causal mediation analysis showed that the parenting center intervention improved children's standardized scores of cognition and language, with the primary caregivers' parenting behaviors (reading books or telling stories with children) playing a significant mediating role. The primary caregivers' parenting behaviors accounted for approximately 17% of the total effect of ECD intervention on children's cognitive outcomes and 29% on language outcomes.

articles.title: In the shadow of crisis: A systematic review and meta-analysis on the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on children's social-emotional skills, behavioral adjustment, and psychological well-being.
articles.abstract: This meta-analysis synthesizes 157 longitudinal studies from 33 countries, involving demographically diverse samples from a wide range of cultural contexts, to examine COVID-19-related changes in social-emotional development, psychological well-being, and behavioral adjustment among children aged 0-12, and the moderating role of political restrictions. Results showed significant declines in children's social-emotional skills and well-being, and increases in behavioral problems in studies comparing pre-pandemic and during-pandemic data. No further declines emerged in studies comparing multiple time points during the pandemic. Political restrictions moderated the effects: Increases in restriction stringency were associated with stronger declines in well-being and greater increases in externalizing problems, whereas higher restriction levels were associated with stronger increases in internalizing problems. These findings underscore the costs of crisis-related disruptions for child development.

articles.title: Improving toddlers' expressive language skills through attachment-based intervention: A randomized controlled trial with low-income, Latine families.
articles.abstract: This study examined the impacts of Attachment and Biobehavioral Catch-up (ABC) on expressive language of Latine toddlers living with their biological parents (N = 173), randomized to home-based Early Head Start supplemented by ABC, or a control group. Mothers' mean age was 30.9 years (SD = 6.5); toddlers (49.7% male) mean age was 13.0 months (SD = 4.1). Compared to controls, children in the ABC group produced significantly higher numbers of utterances and morphemes, types, and tokens, as well as greater mean length of utterances in words and morphemes. An indirect effect of ABC through dyadic mutuality was documented for number of utterances, types, tokens, and morphemes. Findings are considered in the context of the literature on the developmental impacts of parenting interventions.

articles.title: Prevention of depression in patients with atrial fibrillation using an online personalized intervention: the HOPE-AF feasibility study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The overall aim of this study was to examine the feasibility of a personalized online psychological intervention targeting prevention of depression in patients with atrial fibrillation. Specific objectives were to assess acceptability and adherence to the intervention and explore limited efficacy on patient-reported outcomes.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We used a mixed-methods design containing descriptive statistics and ten semi-structured interviews. Participants consisted of 13 women and 15 men and had a mean age of 62 years (range: 26-86). Regarding acceptability, the primary outcome was drop-out, and we found a drop-out rate of 7% among the participating patients (2/28). Completed patients were fully adherent to their personalized planned intervention. For patient-reported outcomes, all mean measures on mental health and health-related quality of life were improved post-intervention. This included depression as measured with the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale. From thematic analysis on the interviews, we generated four themes consisting of meaningful content, communication, technicalities, and personal gain. Overall, patients perceived their personalized intervention relevant for their individual situation, they felt engaged in planning of their intervention and that online treatment allowed a high level of autonomy. Patients felt empowered and experienced that the acquired psychological tools were useful in everyday life with atrial fibrillation.

CONCLUSION: This feasibility study demonstrated a low drop-out rate and high adherence to the intervention. Completion of intervention was associated with potentially improved mental health. The findings support a future randomized controlled trial to evaluate clinical and cost effectiveness of the intervention.

REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT07178691.

articles.title: Remote sophrology in congenital heart disease: the SOPHROCARE randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Despite significant medical advances in recent decades, cardiopulmonary fitness decreases faster in youth with congenital heart disease (CHD) than in healthy peers, resulting in impaired health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and increased cardiovascular risk. Apart from cardiac rehabilitation, non-pharmacological preventive interventions have been scarcely evaluated in this population. Sophrology, a mind-body method involving dynamic relaxation in full awareness, breathing exercises, and imagination, has demonstrated benefits for mental health and well-being. This multicentre randomized controlled trial evaluated the impact of a remote sophrology programme on cardiopulmonary fitness and HRQoL in youth with CHD.

METHODS AND RESULTS: A total of 200 13-to-25-year-old CHD patients were randomly assigned to either the intervention (i.e. eight remote individual sophrology sessions) or the standard of care. The primary outcome was the change in maximum oxygen uptake (VO2max) measured by cardiopulmonary exercise testing from baseline to 12 months. Secondary outcomes included HRQoL and mental health assessments. No significant VO2max group difference was observed [mean difference -0.11; 95% confidence interval (CI) -2.02; 1.79; P = 0.91]. The HRQoL 'Mental Component Summary', 'Mental Health', and 'Vitality' SF-36 scores increased in the young adult intervention subgroup (18-25 years) by 8.98 (95% CI 2.73; 15.23, P < 0.01, effect size 0.84), 14.49 (95% CI 3.17; 25.81, P = 0.01, effect size 0.74), and 15.75 (95% CI 3.97; 27.53, P < 0.01, effect size 0.78) points, respectively.

CONCLUSION: The remote sophrology programme did not improve cardiopulmonary fitness, but significantly enhanced HRQoL in young adults with CHD. Integrating mind-body practices into preventive cardiology programmes should be further evaluated.

REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov: NCT03999320.

articles.title: MR Elastography in Disorders of CSF Dynamics: Current Evidence, Pitfalls, and the Road to Clinical Adoption.
articles.abstract: Disorders of CSF dynamics, including idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus, idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH), and spontaneous intracranial hypotension (SIH), are frequent clinical and imaging phenotypes that overlap with other disease processes. Although conventional MRI remains central for identifying characteristic morphologic features, many imaging findings have variable sensitivity, particularly across disease stages. As a result, current diagnostic pathways and treatment selection are still often reliant on invasive, snapshot-based physiologic tests. MR elastography (MRE) provides a noninvasive, quantitative approach to probe brain viscoelastic properties reflecting tissue microstructure and mechanical strain. These properties are influenced by intracranial pressure volume states within the Monro Kellie constraints, offering a potential "systems level" biomarker of intracranial compliance and CSF venous coupling. This review summarizes the technical foundations of brain MRE relevant to radiologists, including the fundamentals and technical aspects of the technique, and the key sources of measurement variability that influence interpretability and reproducibility. It synthesizes the current clinical evidence supporting MRE for diagnosis, phenotyping, and longitudinal treatment assessment across CSF dynamics disorders, with emphasis on practical integration into contemporary imaging workflows and standardized region of interest reporting. Finally, we highlight the limitations of existing literature and priorities for future research for MRE in this patient population.

articles.title: The Potency of Dual Contrastive Learning Generative Adversarial Network for Reducing Scan Time in PET/CT Imaging with Different Radiotracers of Clinical Importance.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Shortening PET/CT acquisitions without degrading diagnostic or quantitative performance would improve patient comfort and scanner throughput. We evaluated a Dual Contrastive Learning Generative Adversarial Network (DCLGAN) for reconstructing high-quality neuro PET images from reduced time acquisitions across 3 clinically used tracers ([18F] florbetaben [FBB], [18F] FDG, and [18F] N-3-fluoropropyl-2β-carbomethoxy-3β-(4-iodophenyl)-nortropane [FP-CIT]) benchmarking against representative state-of-the-art deep learning models.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this single center retrospective study of symptomatic patients undergoing neuro PET/CT, list mode data from full time acquisitions (20 minutes for FBB; 15 minutes for FDG and FP-CIT) were reconstructed into 3- and 5-minute images. DCLGAN was trained to translate a short time into a full time appearance; raw images and standard 2.5D (U-Net) served as comparators. Image quality was quantified by normalized root mean square error (NRMSE), peak SNR (PSNR), and the structural similarity index (SSIM). Two blinded nuclear medicine physicians graded clinical image quality on a 5-point scale; interreader agreement used the Cohen κ. Quantitative agreement of the standardized uptake value ratio (SUVR) for FBB/FDG and the specific binding ratio (SBR) for FP-CIT between predicted and full time images was assessed with intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) and Bland-Altman analysis.

RESULTS: With DCLGAN at 5 minutes, image quality metrics approached full time performance across tracers: for FBB, NRMSE 0.018, PSNR 34.721 dB, SSIM 0.963; for FP-CIT, NRMSE 0.008, PSNR 41.889 dB, SSIM 0.982; and for FDG, NRMSE 0.013, PSNR 37.502 dB, SSIM 0.986. Mean reader quality scores for 5-minute DCLGAN images were high, 4.48 (FBB), 4.50 (FDG), and 4.55 (FP-CIT), with strong interreader agreement (κ = 0.85, 0.83, and 0.89, respectively). Quantitative agreement with full time scans was excellent: ICCs for 5-minute images were 0.997 (FBB), 0.995 (FDG), and 0.996 (FP-CIT). Bland-Altman analyses showed minimal bias (mean bias: -0.004 for FBB, 0.012 for FDG, -0.029 for FP-CIT) with narrow limits of agreement. Compared with 3-minute reconstructions, 5-minute DCLGAN images demonstrated significantly higher PSNR/SSIM and lower NRMSE (P < .001) while maintaining or improving reader scores and quantitative agreement.

CONCLUSIONS: Across FBB, FDG, and FP-CIT, DCLGAN enabled 5-minute neuro PET acquisitions that appeared to maintain reader rated quality and showed high agreement in SUVR/SBR values with full time scans. These findings suggest that clinically practical scan time reduction may be feasible while maintaining interpretability and quantitative integrity in this cohort.

articles.title: From 'high-risk plaque' to high-value care: measuring vulnerability and managing uncertainty.
Health inequalities across England and their impact on cardiovascular diseases.
Pearls and pitfalls in the diagnosis and management of mitral annular calcification.
articles.abstract: Mitral annular calcification (MAC) is a progressive, degenerative process increasingly recognised for its clinical impact. Beyond being an incidental finding, MAC contributes to mitral valve dysfunction, arrhythmias, systemic embolisation and elevated cardiovascular risk. In developed countries, it has now overtaken rheumatic disease as the leading cause of mitral stenosis. The pathophysiology of MAC involves chronic mechanical stress, pro-inflammatory activation and osteogenic differentiation of valvular cells. Progression is accelerated by age, chronic kidney disease and metabolic derangements. Diagnosing MAC-related valve dysfunction is challenging, as traditional echocardiographic measures often prove unreliable. Multimodality imaging—including 3D echocardiography and cardiac CT—is essential for assessing anatomy, function and procedural feasibility. Importantly, symptoms often reflect combined valvular (eg, aortic stenosis) and myocardial disease (eg, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) phenocopy), necessitating careful haemodynamic evaluation to avoid futile interventions. Management should prioritise medical therapy for symptom control and comorbid HFpEF, reserving interventions for selected patients. Surgical and transcatheter approaches carry high risk and should be undertaken only in specialised centres. Future advances may include tailored devices and therapies targeting calcification pathways.

articles.title: Agreement of ethnicity reporting among patients with cancer with acute coronary syndrome: a national multiregistry analysis.
Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and risk of heart failure: a nationwide cohort study.
Correspondence on 'Colchicine and coronary inflammation: absence of evidence is not evidence of absence' by Aernoud T L Fiolet et al.
18F-FDG PET/CT Findings in a Patient With Uterine Adenomyoma.
articles.abstract: A 50-year-old woman presented to our hospital with lower abdominal pain for 1 week. Pelvic CT revealed a significantly enlarged uterus with multiple nodular and mass lesions. Subsequently, the patient underwent 18F-FDG PET/CT examination.18F-FDG PET/CT revealed multiple nodules and mass lesions in the uterus with intense 18F-FDG uptake. The patient underwent needle biopsy of the uterine lesion. Histopathologic and immunohistochemical findings revealed uterine adenomyoma. This case suggests that uterine adenomyoma with intense FDG uptake is easily misdiagnosed as malignancy, and diagnosis should be confirmed by pathology.

articles.title: Multimodal Point-of-Care Ultrasound Indices and Cardiac Surgery-Associated Acute Kidney Injury: An Exploratory Prospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac Surgery-Associated Acute Kidney Injury (CSA-AKI) remains a common and multifactorial complication. Conventional biomarkers such as Serum Creatinine (SCr) detect injury late. This study explored whether perioperative multimodal Doppler ultrasonography could identify early haemodynamic alterations associated with CSA-AKI.

METHODS: In this prospective, single-centre observational study, adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery at Charlotte Maxeke Johannesburg Academic Hospital underwent serial transthoracic echocardiography and renal Doppler ultrasonography at baseline, on postoperative day 1, and on day 4. Clinical and Doppler-derived parameters were compared between patients who developed CSA-AKI and those who did not. CSA-AKI was defined according to the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. Univariable logistic regression was performed.

RESULTS: Fifty-four patients were included; 21 (39%) developed CSA-AKI. CSA-AKI was associated with higher EuroSCORE II (OR 1.22, 95% CI 1.05-1.50), diabetes mellitus (OR 7.47, 95% CI 2.17-29.3), reduced baseline mitral annular plane systolic excursion (MAPSE) (OR 0.79, 95% CI 0.62-0.96), lower renal End-Diastolic Velocity (EDV) at baseline (OR 0.75, 95% CI 0.59-0.91) and Day 4 (OR 0.70, 95% CI 0.51-0.89), and Day 1 elevated Central Venous Pressure (CVP) (OR 1.19, 95% CI 1.04-1.41). SCr increased, and eGFR declined in the CSA-AKI group by Day 4.

DISCUSSION: The study findings suggest that CSA-AKI was associated with a perioperative haemodynamic profile characterised by lower MAPSE and renal EDV and higher CVP. These unadjusted associations are consistent with impaired longitudinal ventricular function, reduced renal diastolic perfusion, and venous congestion, respectively, but they do not establish causality. Left-ventricular ejection fraction and Renal Resistive Index (RRI) were not statistically associated with CSA-AKI in this cohort. The findings support a hypothesis regarding possible haemodynamic contributors to CSA-AKI that requires confirmation in adequately powered studies.

CONCLUSION: CSA-AKI was associated with lower MAPSE, higher CVP, and reduced renal EDV in univariable analyses. In this observational study, reduced renal EDV may represent a potential haemodynamic marker warranting further investigation; however, no diagnostic threshold or clinical implication can be inferred from these data. Adequately powered prospective studies are required to validate this association and determine its potential clinical utility.

articles.title: Mosaic CDKL5 deficiency drives progressive inhibitory circuit remodelling.
articles.abstract: CDKL5 deficiency disorder predominantly affects heterozygous females, in whom random X-chromosome inactivation generates cellular CDKL5 mosaicism. Although mosaicism is a defining feature of the disease, whether it actively drives disease progression or simply reflects the genetic mode of inheritance remains unknown. Here, we combined age-comparative electrophysiology, quantitative synaptic imaging, transcriptomic profiling and postmortem human brain analyses to determine how mosaic CDKL5 deficiency shapes inhibitory circuit remodeling during disease progression. Heterozygous Cdkl5 female mice exhibited striking age- and region-specific remodeling of inhibitory neurotransmission. Hippocampal inhibition was initially enhanced but progressively declined with age, whereas cortical inhibitory transmission remained preserved at 3 months and increased in middle-aged animals. These functional changes were accompanied by dynamic remodeling of inhibitory presynaptic terminals, persistent disruption of inhibitory synapse organization and reduced hippocampal gephyrin-positive puncta despite preservation of the major inhibitory interneuron populations. At 12 months, heterozygous females also exhibited a higher density of IBA1/CD68 double-positive microglia in both regions compared with age-matched wild-type controls. Importantly, complete Cdkl5 deficiency failed to reproduce the progressive loss of inhibitory presynaptic terminals observed in heterozygous females, indicating that this phenotype is specific to the mosaic condition rather than a simple consequence of complete Cdkl5 loss. Transcriptomic profiling revealed a temporal transition from alterations detected at 3 months in immune-synaptic regulatory pathways to activity-dependent transcriptional programs associated with reduced structural and homeostatic support, consistent with progressive hippocampal circuit reorganization. Exploratory analyses of postmortem cortical tissue from individuals with CDD revealed differences in inhibitory presynaptic labeling between the available young and adult cases, suggesting that inhibitory alterations may also vary with age in human CDD. Together, these findings identify mosaic CDKL5 deficiency as a biologically distinct circuit state characterized by progressive, region-specific inhibitory circuit remodeling and provide a mechanistic framework for disease progression in CDKL5 deficiency disorder.

articles.title: Expanding the genetic landscape of moyamoya angiopathy: insights from 74 trios.
articles.abstract: Moyamoya angiopathy (MMA) is a rare cerebrovascular disorder characterized by progressive stenosis of intracranial arteries and the development of abnormal collateral vessels. While RNF213 is a major susceptibility gene in East Asian populations, the genetic architecture of MMA beyond RNF213, particularly in Europeans, remains largely undefined beyond a few known syndromic causes. We performed whole-exome sequencing on 74 sporadic MMA trios (proband and unaffected parents) of predominantly European ancestry. An additional cohort of 200 probands was screened for gene recurrence. We applied a stringent filtering strategy to identify de novo and rare inherited variants, followed by gene prioritization based on structural modeling, expression data, and biological plausibility. Gene-based burden tests were conducted against large control databases (gnomAD). We identified causative variants in 20 of the 74 probands (27%). Six probands with severe syndromic infant-onset phenotypes harbored de novo variants in the E3 ligase domain of RNF213. Fourteen probands carried a causative copy number variant (n = 3) or a short variant (n = 11) in a known MMA-associated gene (CBL, NF1, PTPN11, DIAPH1, ANO1, JAG1, NOS3, HBB). Beyond these established genes, we identified strong candidate variants in 11 probands from the discovery cohort, involving 11 novel candidate genes. Screening the additional cohort of 200 unrelated MMA probands identified recurrence of the gain-of-function SMAD4 p.Arg496Cys variant, which was de novo in the discovery-cohort proband, linking MMA to dysregulated TGF-β signaling. Other candidate findings included de novo loss-of-function variants in genes regulating epigenetic modulation and RNA splicing (SETD2, HNRNPL, UBAP2L, TOP2B, PRPF40A) and variants affecting vascular stress response (EPAS1, SVEP1, PDCD4). RNF213 was the only gene reaching exome-wide significance in burden testing (P = 2.11 × 10⁻11). This study establishes that MMA in non-East Asian populations is characterized by a strong genetic heterogeneity. These findings expand the molecular landscape of MMA and highlight the utility of trio-based sequencing for uncovering very rare molecular players in this disease. Additional analyses will now be needed to investigate the convergence of MMA pathways.

articles.title: Effectiveness of inpatient psychosomatic rehabilitation in Germany: protocol of a longitudinal study with a waitlist control group.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In Germany, psychosomatic rehabilitation is widely used to improve mental well-being and promote social and occupational participation among individuals with chronic mental and psychosomatic disorders. Although previous studies have reported clinically meaningful improvements following rehabilitation, most have relied on uncontrolled pre-post designs, limiting the strength of the current evidence. The present study exploits the current long waiting times for psychosomatic rehabilitation to form a waitlist control group without influencing the timing of rehabilitation. Overall, the primary objective of our study is to evaluate the short- and medium-term effects of psychosomatic rehabilitation on mental well-being (primary outcome), return to work, and work ability (secondary outcomes). Additional objectives include examining treatment effects in relevant patient subgroups (e.g., diagnostic groups), investigating moderator effects, and analyzing determinants of waiting time until rehabilitation.

METHODS: We will conduct a prospective longitudinal study with a waitlist control group among individuals whose application for inpatient psychosomatic rehabilitation has been approved by the German Pension Insurance agency (Deutsche Rentenversicherung [DRV]). Participants will complete up to 12 online questionnaires at six-week intervals over a period of 16 months. Questionnaire data will be linked with routine data from the DRV rehabilitation statistics database to obtain objective information on rehabilitation and return to work. The effectiveness of psychosomatic rehabilitation will be examined using two complementary analytical approaches: a propensity score-matched waitlist control group comparison to examine the short-term effects of rehabilitation and a discontinuous growth model to examine the medium-term effects of psychosomatic rehabilitation. Both models will also be applied in the subgroup analyses and extended by the relevant interaction terms for the moderator analyses. Determinants of waiting time until rehabilitation will be analyzed using time-to-event models.

DISCUSSION: The study will provide comparatively robust evidence on the effectiveness of psychosomatic rehabilitation in routine care. It may identify patient groups that benefit differently from rehabilitation and factors associated with waiting time until rehabilitation. These findings may inform future efforts to optimize rehabilitation interventions, improve equity in treatment outcomes, and reduce waiting times for psychosomatic rehabilitation.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS): DRKS00038670 (9th December 2025; https://drks.de/search/en/trial/DRKS00038670/details ); WHO UTN: U1111-1332-6419.

articles.title: MicroRNAs in aflatoxin B1-associated hepatocellular carcinogenesis: a scoping review of molecular networks, multiomics evidence, machine learning and translational potentials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is a foodborne hepatocarcinogen, but it remains unclear whether microRNA dysregulation reflects AFB1-associated hepatocarcinogenesis or general hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) biology. This scoping review mapped evidence linking AFB1 exposure, microRNA regulation, molecular mechanisms, multiomics, computational modelling, and machine learning approaches to HCC diagnostics, prognostics, and therapeutics.

METHODS: Peer-reviewed studies published from 2016 to 2026 were identified through Scopus, Embase, PubMed, and Web of Science, supplemented by citation searching, and screened using PRISMA ScR-aligned criteria. The final corpus comprised 104 unique studies classified by AFB1 attribution strength and evidence type across five strata spanning direct human AFB1 HCC microRNA evidence to general HCC contextual evidence.

RESULTS: Experimental mechanistic studies predominated, whereas only one study directly combined measured AFB1 exposure, HCC, and microRNA assessment in humans. The study enrolled 366 HCC cases and 662 controls; circulating miR-4651 provided the strongest exposure-anchored clinical signal, discriminating AFB1-positive HCC with an area under the curve of 0.85, 78.1% sensitivity, and 92.1% specificity. Other studies evaluated exposure-responsive hepatotoxicity, experimental malignant transformation, or rat hepatocarcinogenesis, which cannot be considered interchangeable endpoints. Functionally investigated injury candidates included miR-1679 and miR-124a-3p. Multiomics findings implicated DNA damage, methylation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, inflammation, and metabolic dysregulation, although pathway overlap was heterogeneous and independent functional confirmation was limited. Computational and machine learning studies have expanded network and feature prioritisation, but they have often relied on inferred exposure and limited external validation.

CONCLUSION: Direct human evidence remains scarce, and candidate microRNAs occupy different validation stages. Biological plausibility does not establish clinical readiness; multicentre exposure-anchored validation, harmonised assays and prospective evaluation are required.

articles.title: Serial neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio changes in neonates evaluated for infection: A developmentally contextualized cross-cohort analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Serial neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) changes in neonates may reflect both infection-related processes and rapid postnatal immune adaptation, limiting interpretation based on adult-derived assumptions.

AIMS: To characterize longitudinal NLR changes in neonates evaluated for infection and contextualize relative change against an independent adult infection-related cohort using the same estimand.

STUDY DESIGN: Secondary exploratory longitudinal analysis of two pre-existing clinical cohorts.

SUBJECTS: The source cohorts comprised 65 neonates and 100 adult hospital-admission episodes; at least one valid NLR was available for 62 neonates and 99 adult episodes.

OUTCOME MEASURES: Cohort-specific random-intercept mixed models estimated relative NLR change across three ordered, non-time-harmonized assessments. Cross-cohort effects were expressed as ratios of geometric mean ratios (RoRs).

RESULTS: The analysis included 414 NLR observations. From the first to third assessment, geometric mean ratios were 0.814 (95% CI 0.661-1.003) in neonates and 0.580 (0.487-0.691) in adults; the RoR was 1.403 (1.069-1.842). The global mixed-model test gave p = 0.0433. Robust generalized estimating equations yielded a similar RoR of 1.386 (1.029-1.866) but global p = 0.0901.

CONCLUSIONS: Serial NLR declined less in the neonatal cohort than in the adult comparator, but inference on the overall longitudinal pattern was model-sensitive. The findings support developmentally and clinically contextualized interpretation of neonatal serial NLR and do not identify a causal age effect or diagnostic threshold.

articles.title: Targeting Pseudomonas aeruginosa ventilator-associated pneumonia with a non-antibiotic and biofilm-disrupting live biotherapeutic: preclinical safety and efficacy study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The endotracheal tube (ETT) compromises the host's bronchial defences and facilitates the formation of microbial biofilms and Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP). Although antibiotics remain the cornerstone treatment, their efficacy is often compromised by poor biofilm penetration and the prevalence of multidrug-resistant bacteria. This reveals the need to develop novel non-antibiotic therapeutic strategies. We previously engineered a non-pathogenic strain of the pulmonary bacteria Mycoplasma pneumoniae (CV2) to express anti-biofilm and bactericidal enzymes (VAP platform).

METHODS: We evaluated the safety of an improved version of CV2 (CV8, Mycochassis) in a miniature pig model, and its efficacy with the VAP platform (CV8_VAP) in a piglet model of Pseudomonas aeruginosa-induced VAP. CV8_VAP was administered via intralobe instillation or nebulisation. We assessed the platform's ability to degrade biofilms formed on ETTs in vivo and its impact on the airway microbiota. We evaluated bacterial load in the lungs, inflammatory responses, histopathological and clinical outcomes. Statistics included t-tests, ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis, Mann-Whitney U and mixed-effects rank-based methods.

FINDINGS: VAP platform reduced ETT biofilm thickness and P. aeruginosa load in lungs, with the nebulised route showing enhanced efficacy. Shannon diversity remained statistically comparable across groups in both ETTs and lung tissue. Inflammatory markers in the lung were markedly decreased, suggesting a local immunomodulatory effect. One animal receiving nebulised CV8_VAP died from a suspected anaphylactic-like reaction; no other serious adverse events were attributable to treatment.

INTERPRETATION: These findings suggest CV8_VAP as a promising, non-antibiotic therapeutic strategy for treating VAP caused by P. aeruginosa.

FUNDING: "La Caixa" Foundation, and the European Research Council under the European Union's Horizon 2020 research and innovation program.

articles.title: Ictal 18F-FDG PET/CT Findings in Clinically Silent Seizures Caused by a Frontoethmoidal Nasal Meningoencephalocele.
articles.abstract: A 55-year-old man presented with a 5-year history of drug-resistant epilepsy with monthly clinical seizures. Investigation revealed a left frontoethmoidal nasal meningoencephalocele secondary to osseous fibrous dysplasia. Video-EEG failed to capture scalp epileptiform activity, but a concomitant intranasal electrode recorded frequent, clinically silent electrographic seizures. This continuous intranasal EEG recording during the uptake phase of 18F-FDG PET/CT confirmed eight localized subclinical seizures, each lasting 1-3 minutes. The PET scan demonstrated intense focal hypermetabolism at the herniated tissue tip, matching the electrographic EEG ictal activity. Complete endoscopic endonasal lesionectomy rendered the patient seizure-free for 4 years.

articles.title: Novel Bifunctional PET Tracer 68Ga-DOTA-NI-FAPI-04 PET/CT in Gastrointestinal Tumors: An Exploratory Comparative Study With 18F-FDG.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aims to evaluate the clinical feasibility of 68Ga-nitroimidazole-FAPI (NI-FAPI), targeting both hypoxia and fibroblast activation protein (FAP), in gastrointestinal tumors compared with 18F-FDG PET/CT.

METHODS: Thirty-two patients with gastrointestinal tumors (21 for initial staging, 11 for restaging) underwent both 68Ga-NI-FAPI and 18F-FDG PET/CT within 1 week. Immunohistochemistry for FAP and hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF-1α) was performed. Semiquantitative parameters including SUVmax, TBR, MTV, and total lesion FAP expression/glycolysis (TLF/TLG) were compared. Correlations between SUVmax and primary tumor depth, the short diameter of involved lymph nodes, and liver metastases were analyzed.

RESULTS: Immunohistochemistry confirmed FAP expression on cancer-associated fibroblasts and HIF-1α in tumor cytoplasm. 68Ga-NI-FAPI upgraded initial staging in 2 patients (9.52%). Among recurrent patients, its true positive rate was 100% versus 70% for 18F-FDG. 68Ga-NI-FAPI PET/CT demonstrated higher SUVmax and TBR in primary tumors (14.06±6.26 vs. 10.04±6.53, P=0.005; 12.30±6.80 vs. 6.52±4.38, P<0.001), particularly in signet-ring cell carcinoma (SRCC). It detected more metastases than 18F-FDG (306 vs. 263, P=0.003), with higher SUVmax and TBR in involved lymph nodes, liver metastases, peritoneal metastases, and other distant metastases (all P<0.05). SUVmax of 68Ga-NI-FAPI positively correlated with primary tumor depth (r=0.528, P=0.003), the short diameter of involved lymph nodes (r=0.304, P=0.032), and liver metastases (r=0.349, P=0.040).

CONCLUSION: 68Ga-NI-FAPI exhibits superior diagnostic performance in gastrointestinal tumors compared with 18F-FDG, particularly in staging, SRCC evaluation, and metastasis detection. The positive correlation between tumor size and uptake supports its potential for patient selection in ligand-directed radionuclide therapy, establishing it as an effective theranostic agent for gastrointestinal tumors.

articles.title: A Rare 18F-FDG PET/CT Finding Mimicking Leukemia Cutis in Acute Myeloid Leukemia: Palisaded Neutrophilic Granulomatous Dermatitis.
articles.abstract: Palisaded neutrophilic and granulomatous dermatitis (PNGD) is a rare benign dermatosis typically associated with connective tissue diseases. Its occurrence as a paraneoplastic or reactive phenomenon in hematologic malignancies, particularly acute myeloid leukemia, is exceedingly rare. We present the case of a 65-year-old woman with acute myeloid leukemia who exhibited widespread, intensely hypermetabolic subcutaneous nodules on 18F-FDG PET/CT, strongly mimicking leukemia cutis. Histopathologic examination confirmed PNGD, averting a false-positive interpretation. This case highlights PNGD as a critical diagnostic pitfall in oncologic PET/CT imaging, emphasizing the necessity of histopathologic correlation for hypermetabolic cutaneous lesions to prevent inaccurate upstaging.

articles.title: A Case of Myoepithelioma Mimicking Metastasis on PSMA PET/CT: A Rare Pitfall Evaluated with MRI.
articles.abstract: Myoepithelioma is a rare neoplasm that is usually benign and is most often described in adults. We describe an incidental focus of increased PSMA uptake in the region of the distal phalanx of the great toe in a patient undergoing PSMA PET/CT for initial staging of prostate cancer. While the intense tracer accumulation was initially suspicious for an atypical solitary metastasis, subsequent MRI revealed a well-circumscribed soft tissue lesion. The patient underwent surgical excision, and the diagnosis of myoepithelioma was confirmed. This case highlights that myoepithelioma may represent a rare pitfall in PSMA PET/CT interpretation.

articles.title: Scleroderma in Disguise: Symmetric Girdle-Muscle Uptake on 18F-DCFPyL PET/CT Revealing Inflammatory Myositis.
articles.abstract: Prostate-specific membrane antigen-targeted PET agents are mainly used for prostate cancer; however, uptake in non-prostatic inflammatory tissue can challenge the physician. We report the case of a 75-year-old man referred for characterization of an FDG-avid prostate focus with normal PSA. 18F-DCFPyL PET/CT was performed. Incidental moderate symmetric uptake was found in the pelvic-girdle and paravertebral muscles, without morphologic correlate on CT. Elevated creatine kinase, a late scleroderma-pattern capillaroscopy, and muscle MRI confirmed scleroderma-associated myositis. This case emphasizes that symmetric muscular prostate-specific membrane antigen uptake can reveal active inflammatory myositis.

articles.title: Lung Adenocarcinoma With Extramedullary Hematopoiesis on ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT: A Diagnostic Pitfall in Staging18F-FDG PET/CT.
articles.abstract: A 70-year-old man underwent ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT for evaluation of a pulmonary nodule. He also had a chest wall mass that was initially suspected to represent metastasis. PET/CT images demonstrated that the pulmonary nodule was hypermetabolic, consistent with lung cancer. In contrast, the chest wall mass showed only mild FDG uptake and was interpreted as a benign primary tumor. Pathological examination ultimately confirmed the pulmonary nodule as adenocarcinoma, whereas the chest wall mass was confirmed to be extramedullary hematopoiesis.

articles.title: Giant Endometrioma of the Ovarian Mimicking Malignant Tumor.
articles.abstract: 18F-FDG PET/CT findings of a giant ovarian endometrioma are exceedingly rare. We present a case of a 27-year-old woman with a giant pelvic cystic mass mimicking malignancy. 18F-FDG PET/CT revealed a massive cystic lesion occupying the entire abdominopelvic cavity, with mild internal septations and mild FDG uptake. Despite elevated tumor marker levels, weight loss, and suspicious imaging findings, the final histopathologic diagnosis was bilateral ovarian endometriomas.

articles.title: Intense 18F-FDG Activity in the Urachal Calculus in a Patient With a History of Renal Cell Carcinoma.
articles.abstract: An 81-year-old man presented with new-onset right lumbodorsal pain, four years after radical nephrectomy for right renal cell carcinoma. 18F-FDG PET/CT revealed a high-density focus with intense radioactivity in the midline of the abdomen, corresponding to a urachal calculus. This case highlights the importance of recognizing urachal calculus as a potential false-positive finding in 18F-FDG PET/CT.

articles.title: Physiological Uterine Uptake of 18F-MFBG During Menstruation in a Pediatric Patient With Neuroblastoma.
articles.abstract: An 11-year-old girl with neuroblastoma, enrolled in a clinical trial, underwent 18F-MFBG PET/CT for treatment response evaluation. Imaging showed multiple metastatic lesions. Focal increased radiotracer uptake was also seen in the uterus. Menstrual history confirmed active menstruation, and pelvic ultrasound showed normal uterine morphology and echotexture. This case demonstrates that physiological uterine 18F-MFBG uptake can occur during menstruation-a benign phenomenon that must be recognized to avoid false-positive interpretation of PET/CT findings.

articles.title: Bilateral Renal Metastases From Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma During Immune Maintenance Therapy on 18F-FDG PET/CT.
articles.abstract: Isolated bilateral renal metastasis from esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is extremely rare. We report a 63-year-old man with ESCC treated with neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy and esophagectomy followed by anti-PD-1 maintenance, in whom follow-up 18F-FDG PET/CT demonstrated multiple bilateral renal lesions with intense 18F-FDG uptake. CT-guided biopsy confirmed metastatic squamous cell carcinoma. This case highlights that new isolated renal lesions during cancer immunotherapy should not be assumed to be immune-related nephritis and underscores the value of 18F-FDG PET/CT and biopsy in establishing the diagnosis.

articles.title: Response to Clarification of FAPI PET Response Classification According to PERCIST.
[177Lu]Lu-Prostate-specific Membrane Antigen Radioligand Therapy Combined With a PARP Inhibitor in Treatment-emergent Neuroendocrine Prostate Cancer With Rare Metastases: A New Try.
articles.abstract: A 64-year-old man with treatment-emergent neuroendocrine prostate cancer underwent multitracer PET/CT, which demonstrated low somatostatin receptor expression but marked prostate-specific membrane antigen expression in multiple systemic lesions, including a protruding right abdominal wall metastasis. The patient subsequently received [177Lu]Lu-prostate-specific membrane antigen radioligand therapy combined with olaparib. Follow-up PET/CT showed marked reductions in tracer uptake and tumor burden, accompanied by normalization of the neuron-specific enolase level.

articles.title: Isolated Spermatic Cord Metastasis From Prostate Cancer 6 Years Postradical Prostatectomy Localized by 68Ga-PSMA PET/CT.
articles.abstract: Prostate cancer metastasis to the spermatic cord is exceedingly rare. A 64-year-old man with a history of robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy for high-risk prostate adenocarcinoma (pT3b, Gleason 3+5=9) originating from a PI-RADS 5 lesion in the left prostate hemisphere presented with biochemical recurrence (PSA: 3.77 ng/mL) 6 years postoperatively. Whole-body 68Ga-PSMA PET/CT revealed a solitary, hypermetabolic nodular mass in the contralateral (right) spermatic cord (SUVmax: 23.0), without local or distant metastasis. Surgical excision confirmed metastatic prostatic adenocarcinoma. This case highlights the crucial role of 68Ga-PSMA PET/CT in detecting atypical soft tissue oligometastases and underscores a potential contralateral dissemination mechanism via pelvic vascular collaterals.

articles.title: VEXAS Unraveled: Reversal of Severe Cardiomyopathy in VEXAS With Targeted Immunotherapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vacuoles, E1 enzyme, X-linked, autoinflammatory, somatic (VEXAS) syndrome is an autoinflammatory disorder associated with systemic inflammation. Cardiac involvement is rare (<12%).

CASE SUMMARY: A 72-year-old man with myelodysplastic syndrome presented with sepsis progressing to shock, despite resolution of prior infection and the lack of a new infection. He developed severe nonischemic cardiomyopathy with a left ventricular ejection fraction decline from 65% to 12% with an unremarkable cardiac angiogram, intermittent fevers, and pancytopenia. Genetic testing confirmed VEXAS syndrome. After multidisciplinary discussions, initiation of corticosteroids, interleukin-1 blockade, and Janus kinase inhibition led to recovery of cardiac function to a 54% left ventricular ejection fraction.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights VEXAS syndrome as an under-recognized inflammatory cause of cardiomyopathy. Restored cardiac function, a rarely reported finding, underscores the role of multidisciplinary management and targeted immunomodulatory therapy.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: VEXAS should be considered in older men with refractory systemic inflammation and new cardiomyopathy. Early immunotherapy may reverse cardiac dysfunction.

articles.title: Unraveling Complex Congenital Mitral Valve Anatomy: Beyond the Surgeon's View.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital mitral valve abnormalities exhibit considerable anatomical variability and may be challenging to delineate using conventional echocardiographic views.

CASE SUMMARY: A man in his 50s with mitral regurgitation since childhood presented with exertional dyspnea and severe primary mitral regurgitation. Three-dimensional transesophageal echocardiography revealed extensive prolapse of congenitally connected P2-P3 scallops because of multiple chordal ruptures. A small leaflet-like structure was obscured on the conventional systolic surgeon's view but was identified during diastole and from the left ventricular perspective. Surgical inspection confirmed accessory mitral valve tissue. Mitral valve repair successfully controlled the regurgitation while preserving the accessory tissue.

DISCUSSION: Conventional systolic imaging alone was insufficient to delineate the mitral valve anatomy. Multiphase imaging from complementary perspectives enabled recognition and characterization of the anomalous structure.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Systematic 3-dimensional assessment beyond the conventional systolic surgeon's view may facilitate recognition of otherwise overlooked mitral valve abnormalities.

articles.title: Reconsidering the Management of Middle Ear Myoclonus: A Case Series Presentation and Systematic Review of Surgical Outcomes Following Lysis of the Tensor Tympani and Stapedial Tendons.
articles.journal: Otology & neurotology : official publication of the American Otological Society, American Neurotology Society [and] European Academy of Otology and Neurotology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To present a two patient case series and systematically review clinical characteristics and outcomes of middle ear myoclonus (MEM) and to evaluate whether lysis of the tensor tympani (TT) and/or stapedial tendon (ST) should be considered as an alternative to medical therapy to treat this condition.

DATABASES REVIEWED: MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and Web of Science.

METHODS: Two institutional cases (3 ears) operated on from March through August 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. We then systematically identified English-language studies published before August 2025 and screened them using predefined criteria. Two independent reviewers (C.Z., D.S.) extracted data on demographics, symptom duration, prior medical therapy, surgical procedure (TT and/or ST lysis), technique, laterality, and outcomes. We then used descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: Both patients (3 ears) in the case series achieved complete symptom resolution. Of 756 screened articles, 17 met criteria for full-text review, contributing 70 patients. Combined with the case series, the total cohort comprised 72 patients, of whom 60 (83.3%) had previously tried anticonvulsants, antispasmodics, tranquilizers, sedatives, and/or muscle relaxants, while 12 (16.7%) underwent surgery as initial treatment. Complete symptom resolution occurred in 67 patients (93.1%), partial improvement in 4 (5.5%), and symptom recurrence in 1 (1.4%).

CONCLUSION: TT and/or ST lysis is a safe and effective treatment for MEM with high rates of symptom resolution. Surgical intervention should be considered early in appropriate patients, and patients should be appropriately counseled regarding the high likelihood of complete symptom resolution with surgical intervention.

articles.title: Hemodynamic Challenges After Paraganglioma Resection in Fontan-Palliated Adult With Fontan-Associated Liver Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic hypoxemia in cyanotic congenital heart disease is associated with increased risk of pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma (PPGL), particularly among patients with single-ventricle physiology.

CASE SUMMARY: A 26-year-old man with unbalanced atrioventricular septal defect and extracardiac Fontan palliation, and Fontan-associated liver disease presented with hypertensive crisis, with imaging evidence of PPGL. The patient underwent robotic right adrenalectomy and nodule resection complicated by high-volume chylous ascites for several weeks.

DISCUSSION: Chronic hypoxemia in cyanotic congenital heart disease, particularly univentricular physiology, is a well-established driver of PPGL. Existing guidelines mandate preoperative α-blockade and volume expansion for functional PPGL, but this approach is not tailored to Fontan physiology.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: We present a rare case of operative disruption of retroperitoneal lymphatics superimposed on Fontan-associated systemic venous and lymphatic congestion. Right heart catheterization, cautious α-blockade with volume expansion, and multidisciplinary perioperative management are essential to balance catecholamine blockade against the risks of venous congestion, lymphatic failure, bleeding, and thrombosis.

articles.title: Imaging-Guided Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation in an Adult Patient With Fontan Circulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ventricular arrhythmias are an emerging cause of late morbidity in adults with Fontan circulation, yet catheter ablation strategies in this anatomically complex population remain poorly defined.

CASE SUMMARY: A 25-year-old woman with tricuspid atresia palliated by total cavopulmonary connection presented with sustained ventricular tachycardia. Cardiac magnetic resonance showed circumferential subendocardial fibrosis in the right ventricular outflow tract. Imaging-guided catheter ablation was performed. The cardiac magnetic resonance-defined scar was targeted, abolishing local abnormal ventricular activities. The patient remained arrhythmia-free at the 12-month follow-up.

DISCUSSION: Multimodality imaging facilitated a substrate-based ablation strategy by overcoming the anatomical and hemodynamic constraints inherent to single-ventricle physiology.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Multimodality imaging is essential for ventricular tachycardia substrate characterization in Fontan patients. Right ventricular outflow tract fibrosis may represent the arrhythmogenic substrate even within the rudimentary right ventricle.

articles.title: Challenges of Fontan Completion in Bilateral Bidirectional Glenn: A Patient-Specific Computational Comparison of Conduit Options.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bilateral bidirectional Glenn (BDG) anatomies present a distinct challenge for Fontan completion, with bilateral superior caval inflow creating competitive flow dynamics that impair balanced hepatic flow delivery.

CASE SUMMARY: A 3-year-old with hypoplastic left heart syndrome and bilateral BDG underwent patient-specific computational surgical planning before Fontan completion. Six virtual surgical options, including an extracardiac conduit (ECC) and Y-graft variants with and without bilateral superior vena cava (SVC) bridging, were evaluated, with hepatic flow distribution (HFD) and power loss as primary endpoints.

DISCUSSION: Although its baseline HFD was unbalanced, the ECC demonstrated the most consistent HFD response across simulated physiological states. By contrast, Y-graft performance was highly sensitive to arm placement. Bilateral SVC anastomosis improved HFD but introduced low-velocity stagnant flow, raising concerns for thrombosis.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: In bilateral BDG Fontan planning, computational modeling revealed nonintuitive flow interactions not predictable from anatomy alone. The ECC was selected for surgical robustness, whereas SVC bridging warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Transpulmonary Atrial Pacemaker Implantation in Fontan Circulation With Bilateral Glenn.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with Fontan circulation frequently develop atrial arrhythmias and sinus node dysfunction. Atrial pacing is challenging because conventional transvenous access is limited by complex Fontan anatomy.

CASE SUMMARY: A 20-year-old man with dextroisomerism, bilateral Glenn anastomoses, and Fontan circulation presented with symptomatic sinus node dysfunction and recurrent supraventricular tachycardia. A transpulmonary transvenous approach achieved endocardial atrial lead implantation with excellent pacing parameters. Despite optimized medical therapy, heart failure progressed, and the patient died during transplant evaluation.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights the technical feasibility of transpulmonary endocardial atrial pacing as an alternative to repeat epicardial surgery in selected patients with Fontan circulation. Careful procedural planning, multimodality imaging, and individualized assessment of long-term anticoagulation are important considerations. Despite arrhythmia control, optimized therapy and restoration of atrioventricular synchrony may not prevent heart failure progression, which may be irreversible.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Transpulmonary endocardial atrial pacing is a feasible alternative in carefully selected Patients with Fontan circulation. Sudden cardiac death risk stratification remains limited in this study group.

articles.title: Transvenous Atrial Pacing Via Extracardiac Conduit Fenestration of Fontan Patient With Situs Inversus Totalis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe a stepwise technique for transvenous atrial pacing in a patient with situs inversus totalis and a fenestrated extracardiac (EC) Fontan circulation.

KEY STEPS: Preprocedural caval venography to identify the cavopulmonary anastomoses, EC conduit, and fenestration. A telescopic catheter technique using a 7-F peel-away introducer as the outer sheath, the 5-F pigtail catheter as the inner catheter, and a hydrophilic 0.035-inch guidewire to access the fenestration. Advancement of the 7-F introducer across the fenestration and deployment of an atrial lead in the right atrium.

POTENTIAL PITFALLS: Cavopulmonary anastomoses can be noncoaxial; a femoral snare can help with advancement of the telescopic system. In older Fontan patients, a longer peel-away introducer may be required to reach the EC conduit.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Preprocedural caval venography helps identify the optimal route for lead delivery. A telescopic catheter technique facilitates fenestration access and advancement of the pacing lead.

articles.title: Fontan-Associated Liver Disease: A Novel Strategy to Assess Hepatic Reserve.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evaluating Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD) remains challenging, as elastography reflects passive congestion and standard biochemistry often remains normal. We explore transient hepatic metabolic reserve exhaustion during hemodynamic and dietary stress.

CASE SUMMARY: An asymptomatic 10-year-old boy who had undergone Fontan completion presented for routine evaluation coinciding with an unusually large mixed meal. Dried blood spot amino acid profiling by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry revealed marked hypercitrullinemia (188.9 μmol/L) with elevated ornithine and arginine, whereas shear-wave elastography peaked at 18.1 kPa and systemic ventricular ejection fraction transiently fell to 52%; standard liver biochemistry remained normal. Amino acids normalized within 5 days, with partial recovery of liver stiffness and ejection fraction at 3-month follow-up.

DISCUSSION: Hemodynamic impairment combined with acute dietary stress can transiently exhaust hepatic metabolic reserve before conventional biochemical tests turn abnormal.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Dried blood spot amino acid profiling is a promising noninvasive tool to unmask subclinical metabolic reserve exhaustion in Fontan-associated liver disease when standard liver enzymes are normal.

articles.title: An Acute Coronary Event in a Patient With Fontan Circulation During Pregnancy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is a growing number of adults living with Fontan circulation who are pursuing pregnancy.

CASE SUMMARY: We report a case of a woman with Fontan physiology and pregnancy who had sudden onset chest pain, ST-segment changes, and troponin elevation with coinciding echocardiographic and magnetic resonance imaging changes consistent with myocardial injury from likely paradoxical coronary embolism.

DISCUSSION: Patients with Fontan circulation are at increased thrombotic risk, which is further exacerbated by pregnancy. However, there are limited data regarding appropriate thromboprophylaxis in these patients, especially because there is also a significant bleeding risk.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: This case highlights the complexity of decision-making regarding diagnosis of coronary events in patients with Fontan circulation, as well as challenges determining ideal thromboprophylaxis in these patients during pregnancy.

articles.title: The Fontan Circulation: Lessons Across the Life Span.
Junctional Rhythm Associated With Multilevel Flow Reversal in a Well-Functioning Fontan Detected by 4-Dimensional Flow.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Flow reversal in Fontan circulation is highly associated with Fontan circulatory failure and adverse hemodynamics.

CASE SUMMARY: A 12-year-old boy with hypoplastic left heart syndrome with an extracardiac fenestrated Fontan circuit underwent routine cardiovascular magnetic resonance surveillance. Phase-contrast and 4-dimensional flow imaging demonstrated late-systolic-to-early-diastolic flow reversal throughout the Fontan circuit and across the fenestration. The patient had no Fontan pathway obstruction, significant atrioventricular valve regurgitation, or ventricular dysfunction. Electrocardiography demonstrated a junctional rhythm (JR).

DISCUSSION: JR is common after Fontan palliation and causes atrioventricular dyssynchrony. This case highlights chronic JR as a potential cause of multilevel flow reversal despite otherwise favorable Fontan anatomy and preserved ventricular function, expanding the differential diagnosis of flow reversal in patients with Fontan circulation.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Advanced flow imaging may provide unique mechanistic insights into rhythm-related hemodynamic disturbances and improve the interpretation of Fontan flow patterns.

articles.title: Junctional Rhythm and Atrial Ectopy Presenting as Chronic Abdominal Pain in Fontan Circulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rhythm disturbances may contribute to clinically significant hemodynamic compromise in patients with Fontan circulation, even without overt Fontan failure.

CASE SUMMARY: A 32-year-old woman with double-inlet left ventricle and total cavopulmonary connection presented with years of debilitating abdominal pain resulting in marked functional limitation. Extensive abdominal, hepatic, lymphatic, and cardiac investigations failed to identify a cause. Holter monitoring demonstrated predominant junctional rhythm and frequent atrial ectopy, whereas cardiopulmonary exercise testing revealed heart rate-dependent restoration of sinus rhythm with suppression of atrial ectopy. Invasive assessment showed that temporary atrial pacing suppressed ectopy and improved Fontan hemodynamics. Following AAIR pacemaker implantation, abdominal pain resolved completely and functional capacity improved.

DISCUSSION: This case illustrates that rhythm-related hemodynamic compromise may present with atypical extracardiac symptoms despite reassuring conventional investigations.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Chronic abdominal pain in patients with Fontan circulation may reflect arrhythmia-related hemodynamic compromise despite apparently stable Fontan physiology.

articles.title: Kidney Transplantation in an Adult With a Fontan Circulation: Targeting Renal Perfusion Pressure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dialysis is poorly tolerated in Fontan circulation because of preload-dependent maintenance of cardiac output in the face of passive pulmonary circulation. Evidence that Fontan cardiac output can support kidney-only transplantation remains limited.

CASE SUMMARY: A 24-year-old woman with situs inversus, congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries, pulmonary atresia, and ventricular septal defect palliated with a fenestrated lateral tunnel Fontan developed stage 5 chronic kidney disease from immune-complex glomerulonephritis. Multidisciplinary evaluation supported preemptive kidney-only transplantation based on preserved ventricular function and stable mixed venous oxygen saturation (60%-63%). She remained dialysis-free with excellent 6-month allograft function (creatinine 1.03 mg/dL).

DISCUSSION: Perioperative management targeting renal perfusion pressure (mean arterial pressure minus central venous pressure ≥55-60 mm Hg), maintaining near-baseline Fontan pressures, and using mixed venous oxygen saturation-guided assessment supported immediate graft function.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: In carefully selected patients with Fontan circulation without evidence of Fontan failure, optimization guided by mean arterial pressure minus central venous pressure may enable kidney-only transplantation, avoiding higher-risk heart-kidney transplantation.

articles.title: Ascending Aorta Dilation in the Fontan: To Intervene or Not.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ascending aorta dilation is a known finding in the congenital heart disease population and specifically in patients who have undergone single ventricle palliation.

CASE SUMMARY: We present 3 patients with single ventricle physiology who underwent single ventricle palliations and had severe ascending aorta dilation.

WHY BEYOND THE GUIDELINES: Guidelines for the management of these patients are lacking, and decisions are made on a case-by-case basis.

DISCUSSION: There are case reports of aortic dissection, but true risk remains unknown. Weighing the risks of surgery versus conservative management in patients with single ventricle physiology is challenging.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Surgical intervention on dilated aortas in patients with single ventricle physiology is perilous but possible in the correct circumstances.

articles.title: VA-ECMO Bridge to Transplant in Acute Fontan Circulatory Failure: A Transpulmonary Gradient-Guided Approach to Weaning.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Little is known about strategies for managing adults with Fontan circulation who require temporary mechanical circulatory support.

CASE SUMMARY: A 33-year-old woman with Fontan circulation presented with syncope and was found to have Fontan conduit stenosis with low cardiac output. The patient developed hemodynamic collapse during catheter-based intervention, necessitating veno-arterial extracorporeal circulatory membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) cannulation. She was supported by VA-ECMO and was successfully bridged to heart transplantation after 11 days of support.

DISCUSSION: In a patient with acute Fontan circulatory failure, temporary mechanical support with VA-ECMO and a Fontan-tailored approach to ramp trial and weaning studies ultimately led to informed clinical decision-making and bridge to successful heart transplant.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: VA-ECMO can be used for temporary mechanical circulatory support in acute Fontan failure. Patients with Fontan circulation on VA-ECMO require careful management, with a thoughtful approach to hemodynamics given the circuit's unique physiology.

articles.title: Refractory Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding as an Unusual Manifestation of Fontan Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic venous congestion is an expected consequence of Fontan palliation. In rare cases, hemorrhage arises from congested hemorrhoidal or colonic venous plexuses.

CASE SUMMARY: A 48-year-old man with Fontan palliation presented with massive rectal bleeding causing severe anemia. Colonoscopy and computed tomography angiography excluded malignancy. Repeated mesenteric embolizations provided only transient benefit. As rescue therapy, medical therapy was uptitrated and Fontan fenestration was re-created percutaneously using an atrial flow regulator, preventing further major bleeding at 5 months.

DISCUSSION: As the Fontan population ages, previously underrecognized mechanisms of failure become evident, requiring tailored strategies to restore the "optimal Fontan hemodynamic," the balance between systemic oxygenation and venous congestion being remarkably fragile in advanced Fontan states.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Fontan failure requires individualized, pathophysiology-driven management. Novel medical and interventional treatments may be useful in selected Fontan patients, as a calibrated fenestration may balance oxygenation against venous decompression and improve end-organ stability.

articles.title: Intravascular Lithotripsy to Facilitate Percutaneous Stenting of Obstructed Fontan Circuit.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fontan circuit obstruction generally presents with progressive fatigue or dyspnea on exertion in adulthood with options for management including percutaneous stenting or surgical revision.

CASE SUMMARY: We present the case of a 27-year-old with history of Fontan palliation with Fontan obstruction due to a heavily calcified, obstructive thrombus within the Fontan circuit. We used intravascular lithotripsy to facilitate appropriate stent expansion.

DISCUSSION: Consensus guidelines recommend evaluating adults with Fontan circuits and progressive symptoms with a combination of cardiac catheterization and advanced imaging. However, consensus on management of Fontan circuit obstruction does not exist, and clinical practice varies widely. We present a case that broadens percutaneous management options.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Fontan obstruction presents with progressive dyspnea, and options for management include percutaneous stenting or surgical revision. We present a novel approach to allow stent expansion within a calcified Fontan obstruction using intravascular lithotripsy.

articles.title: Recurrent Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis With Aortic Root Abscess in Fontan Circulation: Navigating a Complex Dilemma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE) in patients with Fontan physiology represents a formidable challenge, with limited data to guide management.

CASE SUMMARY: We report a 30-year-old woman with tricuspid atresia status post-Fontan palliation who previously underwent aortic valve replacement for endocarditis. She presented with recurrent PVE complicated by sepsis, multiorgan failure, and embolic stroke. Echocardiography revealed a 2.2-cm mobile vegetation and aortic root abscess. Following completion of antibiotic therapy and neurological recovery, she underwent a fifth redo sternotomy. A Bentall procedure with reconstruction of the aortomitral curtain was performed using a bioprosthetic valved conduit. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 5 and, at 6-month follow-up, echocardiography demonstrated normal prosthetic valve function.

DISCUSSION: This case illustrates the feasibility and efficacy of complex aortic root surgery in patients with Fontan with recurrent PVE. It underscores the critical importance of multidisciplinary planning, individualized surgical strategy, and optimal timing of intervention to achieve favorable outcomes in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Staged Transcatheter Valve-in-Valve Replacement for Simultaneous Failure of 3 Surgical Bioprosthetic Valves.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe a heart team-driven staged transcatheter strategy for accelerated triple bioprosthetic valve failure in a patient with prohibitive surgical risk.

KEY STEPS: A 78-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus, stage 4 chronic kidney disease, permanent atrial fibrillation, and severe frailty presented with NYHA functional class III heart failure. She had undergone triple surgical bioprosthetic heart valve replacement 8 years earlier. Imaging demonstrated severe aortic, mitral, and tricuspid bioprosthetic valve failure. Given prohibitive surgical risk, a staged transcatheter strategy was selected. Valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement with a 23-mm supra-annular self-expanding valve and bioprosthetic valve fracture was performed first, followed by valve-in-valve (ViV)-transcatheter mitral valve replacement and ViV transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement with 26-mm balloon-expandable valves. All procedures were successful without complications. At 2 months, NYHA functional class improved from III to II, with satisfactory function of all 3 valves.

POTENTIAL PITFALLS: Coronary obstruction, patient-prosthesis mismatch, neo-left ventricular outflow tract obstruction, and hemodynamic intolerance.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Staged triple ViV intervention may provide a feasible alternative to redo surgery. Multimodality imaging and individualized sequencing are critical.

articles.title: Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection of an Anomalous LAD in an Adult With Fontan Palliation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evaluating chest pain in patients with Fontan palliation can be a daunting task given the spectrum of pathology, surgical history, and multisystem involvement.

CASE SUMMARY: A 32-year-old man with double inlet left ventricle status post-Fontan palliation was transferred to our facility with 3 days of chest pain, dyspnea, and a sense of impending doom. An electrocardiogram and troponin trend were consistent with an acute coronary syndrome. Coronary angiography revealed 100% occlusion of the mid-left anterior descending with a linear lucency and intramural hematoma consistent with spontaneous coronary artery dissection type IV. He underwent cutting balloon angioplasty and was discharged on antiplatelet therapy and follow-up imaging to assess for fibromuscular dysplasia.

DISCUSSION: Chest pain is common among patients with congenital heart disease (CHD). Knowledge regarding spontaneous coronary artery dissection in the CHD spectrum is limited. Chest pain differentials for patients with CHD should include evaluation for acquired conditions, particularly as this population ages.

articles.title: Percutaneous Thrombectomy in the Aging Fontan Patient: A New Arrow in the Quiver?
Recalibration of Invasive Hemodynamic Monitoring Devices on Serial Catheterization in Adults With Fontan Circulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There are limited data on long-term accuracy of invasive hemodynamic monitoring (IHM) in patients with nonpulsatile Fontan circulation (FC).

FIRST-IN-HUMAN/EARLY REPORTS SUMMARY: In a retrospective review of 20 patients with FC and CardioMEMS IHM implanted (2015-2025), simultaneous IHM and invasive mean pulmonary artery pressure measurements were available during 6 repeat catheterizations in 6 patients. IHM readings were nearly all lower than invasive measurements, with the absolute difference ranging from 1 to 10 mm Hg.

DISCUSSION/NOVELTY: There are limited reports of recalibration data with IHM, and to our knowledge this is the first report of simultaneous IHM and invasive measurement in adults with FC. IHM accuracy is important with FC as small pressure differences can greatly affect physiology.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: IHM can provide outpatient pulmonary artery pressure measurements in patients with FC. Because we find discrepancy in device measurements in our cohort, we recommend recalibration with each hemodynamic catheterization in this population.

articles.title: Hemoptysis After Fontan Palliation: A 32-Year Single-Center Experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hemoptysis is an uncommon but potentially severe complication after Fontan palliation.

CASE SUMMARY: We retrospectively reviewed 453 patients with Fontan circulation who were evaluated between 1991 and 2023. Thirteen (2.8%) developed hemoptysis, and 9 of those (69%) had recurrent bleeding, accounting for 45 episodes. Twelve patients underwent 28 catheterizations with embolization of 132 aortopulmonary collaterals. Hemoptysis occurred in 3 of 50 patients with right atrial isomerism (6.0%) versus 10 of 403 without it (2.5%; P = 0.164, Fisher exact test). Four patients received inhaled desmopressin with a clinically observed temporary reduction in bleeding. One patient died from massive hemorrhage.

DISCUSSION: Recurrent bleeding and repeated interventions were common, while right atrial isomerism was not significantly associated with hemoptysis.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Hemoptysis after Fontan palliation may recur despite embolization, supporting repeated evaluation and long-term surveillance.

articles.title: Midodrine for Prolonged Pleural Effusions After Total Cavopulmonary Connection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prolonged pleural effusions are a common and frustrating problem after total cavopulmonary connection (TCPC), leading to increased duration of indwelling pleural catheters and prolonged hospital stay. Our center has considered midodrine, a selective alpha-1 receptor agonist with a well-established safety profile, as a potential therapy for post-TCPC effusions.

CASE SUMMARY: We describe our center's experience using midodrine in refractory cases of prolonged pleural effusion following TCPC. Seven patients who had undergone TCPC were prescribed midodrine for the first time at our center within 6 months post-TCPC. In the 3 patients who underwent TCPC at our center, chest tubes were removed a median of 3 days after starting midodrine compared to 11 days in the 4 patients referred for lymphatic intervention.

DISCUSSION: In this single-center experience of patients with prolonged effusions after TCPC, midodrine demonstrated some promise both immediately after TCPC and after lymphatic intervention.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Prolonged pleural effusions remain a challenge in caring for patients after TCPC. Although midodrine shows potential benefit, formal testing of its safety and efficacy on pleural effusion duration is needed.

articles.title: A Successful Fontan Completion for Asplenia Syndrome Complicated by a Hiatal Hernia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hiatal hernia (HH) in patients with a functional single ventricle can increase pulmonary vascular resistance through lung compression and recurrent aspiration.

CASE SUMMARY: A female infant with asplenia, functional single ventricle, and HH presented with lung compression. We prioritized HH repair and gastrostomy placement at 8 months of age, successfully alleviating compression and preventing aspiration. She subsequently underwent a bilateral bidirectional Glenn procedure at 1 year and an extracardiac Fontan procedure at 2 years, demonstrating excellent postoperative hemodynamics.

DISCUSSION: Prioritizing HH repair in patients with single ventricle optimizes pulmonary compliance, providing a safe bridge to Fontan completion when hemodynamically tolerated.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Early surgical intervention for HH optimizes pulmonary hemodynamics, safely bridging patients with single ventricle to Fontan completion.

articles.title: Incidental Hepatocellular Carcinoma on Explant Pathology in Patients With Fontan Circulation After Heart-Liver Transplantation.
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is an increasingly recognized complication of Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD), yet diagnosis remains challenging. We describe 4 patients with Fontan circulation in whom HCC was identified incidentally on explant pathology following combined heart-liver transplantation (CHLT). All patients underwent transplantation for Fontan circulatory failure and had hepatic lesions identified on surveillance imaging that were indeterminate for HCC with normal alpha-fetoprotein levels. Explant pathology revealed well- or moderately differentiated HCC in all cases. Among the 3 patients who survived transplantation, none have experienced recurrence to date. These cases highlight the limitations of current surveillance strategies in a subset of patients with FALD referred for CHLT. Further studies are needed to develop imaging criteria and biomarkers specifically validated for FALD-HCC.

articles.title: Transvenous Atrial Pacing Using Subclavian 3-Dimensional Electroanatomical Mapping in Lateral Tunnel Fontan With Sinus Arrest.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bradyarrhythmias are common late complications after Fontan palliation. Transvenous pacing avoids the high-risk redo sternotomy required for epicardial leads but is technically challenging because of extensive surgical atrial scarring and low-voltage tissue.

CASE SUMMARY: A 39-year-old woman with a lateral tunnel Fontan and severe aortic regurgitation presented with heart failure secondary to bradyarrhythmia and sinus arrest. Using subclavian access, 3-dimensional electroanatomical mapping identified a discrete, viable island of native atrial tissue within an otherwise electrically inert baffle. A transvenous active-fixation pacemaker lead was successfully implanted at this site, restoring stable 1:1 atrioventricular conduction.

DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates that electroanatomical mapping can locate viable atrial tissue and guide lead implantation in complex Fontan atrial substrates. This technique allows for rapid identification of target lead implant sites through a single access point from the pacer pocket.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Three-dimensional mapping enables successful transvenous pacing in highly scarred Fontan atria. This technique allows for mapping and lead placement via the same surgical site.

articles.title: Massive Right Atrial Thrombus After Fontan Palliation Due to Inadequate Atrial Decompression: The Forgotten Chamber.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thromboembolic complications are well recognized after Fontan palliation, typically attributed to low-flow conditions within the pathway. Thrombosis arising from residual native cardiac chambers excluded from the preload circuit is rarely reported.

CASE SUMMARY: A 4-year-old boy with pulmonary atresia and intact ventricular septum underwent pre-Fontan hemodynamic catheterization demonstrating a restrictive atrial septal communication that was balloon dilated, with perceived elimination of the gradient. Ten months after Fontan palliation, he presented with fever and mild respiratory distress and was found to have a giant right atrial thrombus. Imaging suggested profound right atrial stasis because of inadequate atrial decompression. The patient was managed with anticoagulation.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights thrombosis in a native chamber excluded from the preload circuit. Progressive right atrial isolation likely fulfilled Virchow's triad despite an unobstructed Fontan circulation.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Despite exclusion from the preload pathway, definitive atrial decompression is essential when planning a Fontan procedure in patients with pulmonary atresia/intact ventricular septum.

articles.title: Successful Repair of Giant Aortic Aneurysm With Severe Aortic Regurgitation in Fontan Patient.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Progressive aortic root dilation in patients with Fontan circulation requires vigilant monitoring to ensure timely surgical intervention.

CASE SUMMARY: A 41-year-old patient with Fontan circulation (tricuspid atresia, large ventricular septal defect, situs inversus totalis) presented on NYHA functional class II. Echocardiography and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging confirmed severe aortic regurgitation with 8.1-cm ascending aortic aneurysm and impaired function. He underwent a modified Bentall and bilateral Cabrol procedure using 30-mm tube graft, 27-mm mechanical valve, and coronary conduits. Despite a challenging postoperative course requiring temporary intra-aortic balloon pump, he recovered well with improved ventricular function.

DISCUSSION: Aortic root dilation is a recognized late complication in single-ventricle physiology. This is the first report of surgical repair of a giant aortic aneurysm with severe regurgitation and impaired function in mirror-image Fontan anatomy. This case highlights how modified graft techniques overcome extreme surgical constraints.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: A modified Bentall-Cabrol procedure can successfully repair giant aneurysms in Fontan anatomy.

articles.title: Spontaneous Closure of Pulmonary Arteriovenous Fistulas After a Modified Fontan Surgery.
articles.abstract:
