BACKGROUND: This case report discusses a 9-year spontaneous closure of pulmonary arteriovenous fistulas (PAVFs) after a Fontan procedure in a patient with a single ventricle.

CASE SUMMARY: An 18-year-old female patient developed PAVFs after a Glenn procedure in infancy and underwent a total cavopulmonary connection with a 12-mm conduit at age 9. PAVFs remained evident at 1 year of age postoperatively, but multimodal imaging (catheterization, cardiac magnetic resonance, and echocardiography) at 9 years showed complete resolution, with SpO2 96%, mean pulmonary artery pressure 10 to 11 mm Hg, and normal ventricular function.

DISCUSSION: This is the first case of imaging-documented delayed closure of PAVFs up to 9 years following the Fontan procedure, supporting the hepatic factor hypothesis (hepatic venous flow inhibits angiogenesis). The small conduit may have balanced perfusion and thrombosis risk, allowing adaptive flow optimization.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Delayed spontaneous closure of PAVFs can occur years after undergoing a Fontan procedure. Comprehensive multimodal imaging is essential for guiding management in patients with congenital heart disease.

articles.title: Fontan Baffle Failure Signaled by Neurologic Events and Worsening Cyanosis: Transcatheter Vs Surgical Repair.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As the Fontan population ages, follow-up care and attention to quality of life become increasingly complex, requiring a multidisciplinary approach. In this context, cyanosis in patients with an intra-atrial Fontan tunnel may be a signal of structural intracardiac baffle failure associated with clinical deterioration.

CASE SUMMARY: The patients were two 35-year-old adults with fenestrated intra-atrial Fontan circulation in whom neurologic events preceded recognition of worsening desaturation. In the first patient, a focal defect of the inferior caval patch associated with neurologic events, was closed percutaneously with an occluder device. In the second patient, extensive tunnel dehiscence required surgical revision with the creation of a calibrated fenestration.

DISCUSSION: These cases underscore the importance of thoroughly investigating progressive desaturation in patients with Fontan circulation, as identifying and treating the cause is essential to optimize clinical outcomes.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Late Fontan worsening desaturation requires diagnostic investigation. Discriminating focal leak from dehiscence within the tunnel is crucial for treatment strategies.

articles.title: Peritoneal Dialysis for Refractory Ascites in Fontan-Associated Liver Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fontan-associated liver disease and refractory ascites represent advanced systemic failure in patients with Fontan circulation, with limited therapeutic options.

CASE SUMMARY: A 38-year-old woman with tricuspid atresia, after a Fontan procedure, developed progressive Fontan-associated liver disease and recurrent refractory ascites. Imaging showed portal hypertension and cirrhosis, and liver biopsy confirmed advanced congestive hepatopathy with stage V fibrosis. She was not a candidate for transplant or further intervention, so a tunneled peritoneal catheter was placed for palliative drainage.

DISCUSSION: Refractory ascites reflects Fontan failure and a worse prognosis. Conventional therapy is insufficient, and diuretic resistance becomes common. Peritoneal dialysis allows gradual decongestion with reduced hemodynamic stress in preload-dependent circulation. Evidence supports decreased hospital admissions in refractory heart failure, although data in Fontan cases remain limited.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Refractory ascites is a marker for end-stage Fontan failure. Peritoneal ultrafiltration becomes a palliative choice when definitive therapies are not feasible.

articles.title: Leadless Transatrial or Transconduit Pacing in Fontan Circulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epicardial or transvenous pacing strategies may be suboptimal in certain patients with Fontan requiring permanent pacing. Leadless pacing offers an alternative, but experience in complex Fontan anatomy remains limited.

CASE SUMMARY: We report 3 patients with Fontan who underwent transatrial or transconduit leadless pacemaker (LP) implantation. One patient with a lateral tunnel Fontan and sinus node dysfunction underwent successful placement of an AVEIR AR (Abbott) LP in the pulmonary venous atrium. Two patients with Fontan circulation and complete heart block with prior epicardial pacing systems underwent implantation of a Micra AV (Medtronic) LP in the systemic ventricle, with longer follow-up than in prior reports.

CONCLUSIONS: This case series demonstrates leadless pacing in the pulmonary venous, atrial, and systemic ventricular chambers in Fontan circulation, including atrial AVEIR AR implantation and extended follow-up of ventricular Micra AV pacing. These approaches may expand pacing options in selected patients with Fontan when conventional strategies are limited, although long-term outcomes remain unknown.

articles.title: Catheter-Based Selective Pulmonary Artery Digital Subtraction Angiography and Microvascular Reserve Quantification in Fontan Patient.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fontan circulation allows univentricular congenital heart physiology to survive. Pulmonary microvascular images are poorly described in live patients during follow-up.

CASE SUMMARY: A 25-year-old man with a diagnosis of tricuspid atresia status after extracardiac fenestrated Fontan surgery performed at 3 years of age, followed by fenestration device closure a year later, and with a history of hemoptysis at 9 years of age. Follow-up was performed through cardiac catheterization with selective pulmonary artery (PA) digital subtraction angiography (DSA). A decreased percentage of microvascular reserve associated with increased D-dimer suggested in situ thrombosis, and thromboprophylaxis was switched from aspirin to direct oral anticoagulation.

DISCUSSION: We focus on catheter-based PA DSA microvascular reserve percentage, cardiopulmonary exercise test, and D-dimer quantification to generate evidence of in situ microvascular thrombosis.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Catheter-based PA DSA revealing reduced microvascular reserve may identify in situ microvascular thrombosis and offer a novel pathophysiological insight in patients with Fontan circulation during follow-up.

articles.title: Emergency Percutaneous Thromboembolectomy in an Adult With Fontan Circulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thromboembolic complications remain a major source of morbidity in patients with Fontan circulation, particularly in older atriopulmonary connections with atrial arrhythmias.

CASE SUMMARY: A 54-year-old man with tricuspid atresia and Fontan circulation presented with acute hypoxemia and chest pain after diagnosis of a large right atrial thrombus. Imaging confirmed embolization into the pulmonary artery. Considering a future heart transplantation strategy, the multidisciplinary team opted for percutaneous thrombectomy rather than surgery. The procedure resulted in rapid clinical improvement without complications.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights the complexity of thromboembolism management in Fontan patients and illustrates the feasibility of percutaneous thrombectomy as a bridge-to-transplant strategy in selected patients.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Percutaneous thrombectomy may represent an effective option for acute pulmonary embolism in selected Fontan patients.

articles.title: Systemic Atrioventricular Valve Replacement After Fontan Completion: A Multimodality Clinical Case Series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic atrioventricular (AV) valve regurgitation contributes to late Fontan failure. However, physiological changes after systemic AV valve replacement remain poorly characterized, and objective criteria for patient selection and intervention timing remain undefined.

CASE SUMMARY: We reviewed 7 patients after Fontan completion undergoing systemic AV valve replacement, with paired catheterization in all and paired cardiovascular magnetic resonance in 6. Replacement markedly reduced AV valve regurgitation in all patients, with ventricular unloading in evaluable cases and clinical improvement or stabilization. Fontan pressure generally decreased when preoperative central venous pressure was elevated, whereas low-output states, altered loading conditions, collateral flow, and high-output physiology modified the hemodynamic response.

DISCUSSION: Systemic AV valve replacement was associated with favorable hemodynamic and clinical effects, although the pattern and tempo of recovery differed across preoperative physiological stages. These observations suggest that integrated cardiovascular magnetic resonance and catheterization may help characterize disease stage and inform patient selection and intervention timing.

articles.title: Transvenous Coil Implant in a Patient With Lateral Tunnel Fontan: The Route Less Traveled.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ventricular arrhythmias occur in approximately 11% of patients who undergo Fontan palliation. Sudden cardiac death, presumably from ventricular arrhythmia, accounts for approximately 10%-20% of the overall mortality among these patients. Implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) implantation in these patients is challenging because of limited transvenous access to the subpulmonary ventricle.

CASE SUMMARY: A 41-year-old woman who underwent Fontan palliation later developed complete heart block and underwent epicardial pacemaker implantation at the age of 36 years. She developed symptomatic ventricular tachycardia and worsening heart failure with planned heart/lung transplant listing. She was considered to be at prohibitive risk for epicardial defibrillator and failed subcutaneous ICD screening. We describe a transvenous ICD upgrade using a hemiazygos vein coil, inframammary generator, and lead extenders for existing epicardial leads.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights the feasibility of hemiazygos vein coil placement in combination with an inframammary generator pocket in selected patients with Fontan.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: The hemiazygos vein may be a viable option for transvenous coil placement in these patients.

articles.title: Intravascular Lithotripsy in Calcific Fontan Conduit Stenosis: Between a Rock and a Hard Place.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dilation and stenting of stenotic Fontan conduits may be limited by circumferential calcific stenosis. Few options exist for calcium modification in this study group.

CASE SUMMARY: A 29-year-old woman with an extracardiac Fontan was found to have a severely stenotic, circumferentially calcified Fontan conduit (approximately 8 mm). She was brought to the catheterization laboratory for balloon dilation and stent placement. Calcium modification was performed before stenting using intravascular lithotripsy, allowing restoration of the lumen diameter to 20-22 mm. Hemodynamics following lithotripsy and stent placement confirmed the absence of a gradient across her conduit.

DISCUSSION: High-pressure balloons have traditionally been used to facilitate stent expansion in calcified Fontan conduits. However, circumferential calcification may lead to suboptimal results. This case highlights the efficacy of prestent calcium modification with intravascular lithotripsy in a Fontan conduit.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Intravascular lithotripsy may facilitate optimal dilation and stenting in circumferentially calcified Fontan obstruction.

articles.title: Mechanical Hemolysis After Fontan Fenestration Closure: An Unrecognized Complication.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mechanical hemolysis following transcatheter device closure is uncommon and is typically associated with a residual high-velocity shunt. Hemolysis after Fontan fenestration closure has not been previously reported.

CASE SUMMARY: A 7-year-old boy with single-ventricle physiology underwent elective transcatheter Fontan fenestration closure, complicated by hematuria the following day. Laboratory evaluation confirmed nonimmune intravascular hemolysis. Echocardiography demonstrated a well-positioned device without residual shunt but with an atrioventricular valve regurgitant jet directed toward the device. Conservative management was pursued, with biochemical surveillance, folic acid, and iron supplementation. Device removal was not required.

DISCUSSION: Device-related hemolysis is classically attributed to residual shunting. Described herein is hemolysis caused by regurgitant jet collision with a nonendothelialized device. Conservative management is appropriate in stable patients, as given expected resolution with device endothelialization.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Hematuria after Fontan fenestration closure should raise suspicion for mechanical hemolysis, even without residual shunt. Early recognition is essential in Fontan patients and warrants earlier supportive intervention given limited cardiopulmonary reserve.

articles.title: Novel Transvenous Approach for Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator Implantation in a Patient With Fontan Circulation: Trans-Left Pulmonary Artery-Left Atrium.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: After Fontan palliation, direct venous access to the ventricle is eliminated, complicating implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) placement.

FIH/EARLY REPORTS SUMMARY: A 34-year-old status-post lateral tunnel Fontan presented with syncope. He was found to have high-grade atrioventricular block and fractured epicardial leads. He was recommended an ICD with severely depressed single right ventricle function but was not an epicardial candidate because of multiple prior sternotomies and recurrent chest wall abscesses. Despite balloon angioplasty of the transbaffle puncture, a sheath for ICD placement could not be advanced. A trans-left pulmonary artery to left atrial (LPA-LA) puncture was performed at the left pulmonary artery/Fontan conduit junction above the left atrium roof to implant the right ventricle ICD lead.

DISCUSSION: Transpulmonary LPA-LA is a feasible option for ICD lead implantation in patients with Fontan who are not candidates for epicardial leads.

NOVELTY: This is the first report of transpulmonary LPA-LA puncture for ventricular lead placement in Fontan circulation.

articles.title: Cardiac CT in a Criss-Cross Heart With Double-Outlet Right Ventricle Guiding Single-Ventricle Palliation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Criss-cross heart with double-outlet right ventricle (DORV) and dual discordance is a rare phenotype challenging the conventional echocardiographic segmental characterization.

CASE SUMMARY: An infant with prenatally diagnosed complex congenital heart disease had functionally univentricular physiology, severe pulmonary stenosis, and large septal defects. Echocardiography suggested double-inlet left ventricle with transposed great arteries but incompletely defined segmental anatomy and pulmonary arteries. Electrocardiographically gated cardiac computed tomography (CT) angiography established criss-cross atrioventricular relationships with clockwise ventricular rotation, straddling tricuspid valve, DORV from a mildly hypoplastic morphologic right ventricle, severe subpulmonary/pulmonary annular obstruction, confluent pulmonary arteries, single coronary artery pattern, and patent ductus arteriosus, supporting staged single-ventricle palliation.

DISCUSSION: CT provided the segmental and vascular roadmap for staged palliation.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Criss-cross heart with DORV and dual discordance frequently precludes biventricular repair, directing single-ventricle planning. CT is pivotal pre and postoperatively, defining pulmonary artery eligibility for cavopulmonary connection and confirming the substrate for Fontan completion.

articles.title: Lower-Extremity Chronic Venous Disease Interventions in Patients with Fontan: A Single-Center Experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lower-extremity chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) affects >50% of adult patients with Fontan circulation, with 25% having severe CVI. CVI has historically been managed conservatively in patients with Fontan circulation, but this may not adequately control symptoms. Minimally invasive procedures for management of symptomatic CVI are widely performed in the general population and may be appropriate for treatment of patients with Fontan circulation as well.

CASE SUMMARY: We report 5 patients with Fontan circulation with symptomatic CVI who underwent minimally invasive venous procedures targeting CVI.

DISCUSSION: The procedures were performed to manage symptoms that were not adequately controlled with conservative measures and were significantly impacting quality of life. All patients underwent venous ablation, phlebectomy, and/or percutaneous liquid sclerotherapy under general anesthesia, and most were discharged on the same day. Patients reported significant clinical improvement without major complications.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Lower-extremity venous procedures may offer a safe and effective strategy for managing symptomatic CVI in patients with Fontan circulation without major complications.

articles.title: Successful Fontan Completion in a 36-Year-Old: A Durable Glenn.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fontan palliation is commonly completed at 2-4 years, but delays may occur due to medical optimization and, rarely, loss to follow-up.

CASE SUMMARY: A 36-year-old woman with tricuspid atresia status post-bidirectional Glenn presented with significant exercise intolerance and hypoxemia. She had lived over 2 decades with Glenn physiology and successfully carried 2 pregnancies. The patient ultimately underwent fenestrated Fontan completion with significant functional improvement.

DISCUSSION: This case represents an exceptionally prolonged duration of Glenn physiology, demonstrating that this palliation can be highly durable in select patients with favorable anatomy and hemodynamics. Fontan completion in this patient resulted in meaningful functional improvement, though it remains a temporizing measure that carries substantial risks and potential long-term morbidity.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Glenn palliation can be durable in select patients. Fontan completion may meaningfully improve function well beyond the conventional 2-to-4-year age window, and timing should be patient-specific.

articles.title: Recovery of Postpartum Ventricular Dysfunction in a Fontan Patient Treated With Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women with Fontan circulation (FC) are vulnerable to heart failure during pregnancy and postpartum.

CASE SUMMARY: A 25-year-old woman with hypoplastic left heart syndrome palliated to a lateral-tunnel Fontan developed severe systemic right ventricular dysfunction 8 weeks postpartum (fractional area change 24%, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide 5,710 pg/mL) despite preserved function immediately after delivery. Guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) was initiated. Serial imaging demonstrated progressive recovery to baseline ventricular function (fractional area change 39%) by 2 years with marked biomarker improvement and symptom resolution.

BEYOND THE GUIDELINES: Evidence guiding postpartum heart failure management in patients with FC is limited, and there is also limited data on the role of GDMT in FC.

DISCUSSION: Timely initiation of GDMT may facilitate recovery of postpartum systemic ventricular dysfunction in patients with FC.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: This case highlights the potential role of early GDMT initiation in a population lacking disease-specific postpartum management recommendations.

articles.title: Guideline-directed statin therapy and cardiovascular events among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus in South Ethiopia: a case-control study.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) significantly increases cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. Statin therapy is a cornerstone of primary prevention, yet suboptimal prescribing and adherence remain common, particularly in resource-limited settings. Evidence on statin utilization and outcomes in Ethiopian T2DM patients is limited. This study aimed to determine the association between guideline-directed statin therapy and cardiovascular events among T2DM patients at Wolaita Sodo University Comprehensive Specialized Hospital (WSUCSH). A hospital-based case-control study was conducted from April to July 2022 at WSUCSH in South Ethiopia. Cases were T2DM patients aged 40-75 years who developed a first cardiovascular event after T2DM diagnosis. Controls were T2DM patients without CVD, frequency-matched by age (±5 years) and sex. Data were collected through retrospective medical record review and patient interviews using a structured data abstraction form and the Morisky Medication Adherence Scale. Unconditional logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (AOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI), with age and sex included as covariates to account for the frequency-matched design. A p-value <0.05 was considered statistically significant. A total of 196 participants (98 cases and 98 controls) were included. Among cases, stroke (43.9%) and myocardial infarction (35.7%) were the most frequent cardiovascular events. Patients receiving guideline-directed statin therapy had significantly lower odds of CVD events [AOR=0.242, 95% CI: 0.093-0.630, p=0.004]. However, only 13.8% received guideline-concordant therapy, and annual lipid testing was documented in only 4.6%. In this case-control study, guideline-directed statin therapy was associated with lower odds of cardiovascular events among T2DM patients in South Ethiopia. However, the majority of participants did not receive guideline-concordant therapy, highlighting a substantial practice gap. Interventions to improve statin prescribing, adherence, and continuity are urgently needed in this setting.

articles.title: Comparative evaluation of impulse oscillometry and spirometry for the detection of small airway disease in patients with obstructive airway diseases.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Although there is some evidence supporting a correlation between impulse oscillometry (IOS) and spirometry for detecting small airway disease (SAD), in many cases, discordant results are observed. IOS has not yet been established as a standard method for routine pulmonary function assessment in clinical practice. We did this study with the primary objective of diagnosing SAD in patients with obstructive airway diseases (OAD) using IOS and comparing it with spirometry. This cross-sectional, comparative study was conducted from July 2023 to December 2024. Adult patients (≥18 years of age) with diagnosed stable OADs [asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and bronchiectasis] were included in the study (n=118). Maximum expiratory flow 25-75 with a Z score of <-1.64 and resistance at 5 Hz - resistance at 20 Hz (R5-R20) >150% were criteria used for defining small airway obstruction in spirometry and IOS, respectively, and were compared. As secondary outcomes, correlation of severity of SAD across COPD groups, Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) steps using IOS, and comparison of bronchodilatation responsiveness (BDR) were also done. In pre-BDR, IOS and spirometry diagnosed SAD in 94.91% and 82.20% of patients, respectively (p=0.069). There was poor agreement (ĸ=0.155) between these modalities pre-BDR; however, post-BDR, there was fair agreement (ĸ=0.277) between these modalities, and both modalities for the detection of SAD were significantly related (p=0.003). Across various Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease groups, there was no significant difference in the severity of SAD, while across various GINA steps, there was a significant difference in the severity of SAD, especially GINA step 1-2 and step 5. There was poor agreement between these modalities for the BDR test. In conclusion, both modalities performed differently in pre-BDR (discordant) and post-BDR (concordant) settings. For the BDR test, both modalities are not exchangeable. Further research is warranted to determine the optimal setting (pre-BDR vs. post-BDR).

articles.title: Life's Essential 10 and healthspan: implications for cardiovascular prevention.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Quality of care & clinical outcomes

articles.title: Impact of beta-blockers on quality of life in patients with myocardial infarction without heart failure: A prespecified substudy of the DANBLOCK trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Contemporary evidence on the effects of beta-blockers on health-related quality of life (HRQoL) after myocardial infarction (MI) in patients without heart failure is limited, despite widespread use. In this prespecified substudy of the DANBLOCK trial, we aimed to assess whether beta-blocker therapy influences HRQoL after MI in patients with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) >40%.

METHODS: Patients with a recent (≤14 days) MI and LVEF >40% were randomised to open-label beta-blocker therapy or no beta-blocker. HRQoL was assessed at baseline and at three-, 12-, and 24-months using the EQ-5D-5L questionnaire and the EQ visual analogue scale (EQ VAS). The primary endpoints were between-group differences in change from baseline to each follow-up visit estimated by a linear mixed-effects model.

RESULTS: Among 2707 randomised patients, 2681 (99%) completed at least one EQ-5D-5L questionnaire. Median EQ-5D and EQ VAS scores at baseline were 0.95 (Interquartile range [IQR]: 0.87-1.00) and 77 (IQR: 65-87), respectively. Scores remained stable throughout follow-up. No significant between-group differences for EQ-5D index score and EQ VAS score were observed at any time point. At 12 months, mean difference (beta-blocker minus no beta-blocker) in EQ-5D index- and EQ VAS score was -0.001 (95% confidence interval [CI], -0.016 to 0.013, P=0.86) and -1.35 (95% CI, -2.85 to 0.15, P=0.08), respectively. Results were consistent in prespecified subgroups (age, sex, type of MI, and LVEF).

CONCLUSION: Overall, a high HRQoL was observed among post-MI patients. Beta-blocker therapy did not affect HRQoL after MI in patients without heart failure.

articles.title: Temporal Changes in Lipoprotein(a) Following Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined cardiovascular risk factor generally considered stable over an individual's lifetime. Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) may transiently alter Lp(a) concentrations, complicating interpretation. We systematically evaluated temporal changes in Lp(a) following ACS.

METHODS: This PRISMA 2020-guided systematic review searched MEDLINE and Embase from database inception to February 2026. Eligible studies reported serial Lp(a) measurements at two or more time points after index ACS event. Exploratory random-effects meta-analysis of percent change in mean Lp(a) was performed.

RESULTS: Of 3,811 records, 16 studies comprising 1,396 patients met inclusion criteria. Lp(a) demonstrated a dynamic post-ACS trajectory. Using initial post-ACS measurements as the reference, pooled percent change in mean Lp(a) was non-significant at 24 hours post-ACS (+2.5%, 95% CI -6.8 to 11.7; p=0.602). Lp(a) was significantly higher at 7-14 days (+44.0%, 95% CI 4.0-84.1; p=0.031), 1 month (+28.3%, 95% CI 2.7-54.0; p=0.030), and 3-6 months (+22.2%, 95% CI 2.4-42.0; p=0.028). Across two studies, absolute Lp(a) increases >25 nmol/L occurred in 17% and 22% of patients by 3 and 6 months, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Lp(a) is not static post-ACS. Early post-ACS measurements may underestimate long-term concentrations and risk. Repeat measurement weeks to months later is most informative when initial post-ACS Lp(a) values are near clinical decision thresholds or would influence eligibility for emerging Lp(a)-lowering therapies.

articles.title: Fabrication of guggulsterone-E-integrated chitosan-zinc nanohybrids: surface chemical insights, biointerface interactions and multi-target antidiabetic mechanisms.
articles.abstract: The research focuses on evaluating the potential anti-diabetic efficacy of encapsulating guggulsterone-E extract within chitosan-ZnO NPs (Gu@ChZn NPs) through a sustainable production method. UV-vis, FT-IR, FE-SEM, HR-TEM, EDX, XPS, and XRD characterizations were used to identify the physicochemical properties of the Gu@ChZn NPs. The UV-visible absorption peak was noted at 320 nm, and morphological analysis revealed that the particles were mainly spherical with uneven surface characteristics and sizes of 5-45 nm. Based on the biological evaluation, it was found that compared with guggulsterone-E alone, Gu@ChZn NPs had a greater inhibitory effect on selected enzymes such as lipase, α-glucosidase, and α-amylase. Critical genes related to diabetes, including KCNJ11, TCF7L2, IRS-1, HNF1A, HXK4, and ABCC8, were predicted to interact with guggulsterone-E via network pharmacology. Molecular docking analysis revealed substantial binding affinities, with ABCC8 exhibiting the most significant interaction at -9.07 kcal mol-1. The Gu@ChZn NPs exhibit potential as a promising bio-functional nanocomposite with enhanced enzyme inhibitory properties relevant to diabetes-associated metabolic regulation.

articles.title: Regional contributions to historical and future trends of global fungal skin disease burden: A comprehensive analysis of the Global Burden of Disease 2023 study.
articles.abstract: Fungal skin diseases are common and contribute substantially to nonfatal disease burden. Despite their prevalence, these conditions are often overlooked because they are rarely life-threatening. However, the rising prevalence of obesity and diabetes, environmental changes associated with climate change, and the emergence of antifungal-resistant dermatophytes may contribute to increasing future burden. In this study, we analyzed Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 estimates to evaluate fungal skin disease burden, using disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) as the metric for burden across 21 GBD regions. Joinpoint regression was used to characterize temporal trends. Decomposition analyses partitioned changes in DALYs into contributions from population growth, population aging, and epidemiologic change. Future DALYs and age-standardized DALY rates (ASDRs) were projected from 2024-2050 using Bayesian age-period-cohort modeling. Global fungal skin disease DALYs increased from 1.5 million (95% UI, 0.6-3.2 million) in 1990 to 2.0 million (95% UI, 0.8-4.2 million) in 2023 and are projected to reach approximately 2.6 million (95% UI, 1.4-4.4 million) by 2050. Global ASDRs are projected to increase from 26 (95% UI, 10-54) in 2023 to 29 (95% UI, 16-53) per 100,000 population by 2050. We identified regions predicted to contribute to worsening burden, most notably South Asia, which was projected to contribute 45.2% (95% UI, -10.7 to 155.0) of future global DALY increases. Global fungal skin disease burden is projected to increase through 2050, accompanied by worsening ASDRs. Projected regional variation in future burden highlights the need for region-specific prevention, surveillance, and control strategies.

articles.title: GUT-LIVER CROSSTALK: A NOVEL CD226-CD112 INHIBITOR PREVENTS GUT-PRIMED NETOSIS AND ATTENUATES ACUTE LIVER INJURY IN SEPSIS.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We recently identified a novel interaction between intestinal intraepithelial lymphocytes (IELs) and neutrophils via CD226 and CD112. This interaction induces neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation and promotes inflammatory gut-liver crosstalk in sepsis. By mapping the binding site between CD112 and CD226, DPX2 was created to inhibit IEL-induced NET formation. We hypothesize that DPX2 treatment inhibits IEL-mediated NETosis and the subsequent pathologic gut-liver crosstalk.

METHODS: Adult C57BL/6 mice were subjected to sepsis by cecal ligation and puncture (CLP). The treatment group received a 1 μg/g BW i.p. injection of DPX2, while the control group received PBS as vehicle. Liver tissue was evaluated for pro-inflammatory markers, myeloperoxidase (MPO) activity, and TUNEL staining. Serum was analyzed for liver enzyme and cytokine levels. A 7-day survival study was also conducted.

RESULTS: NETs in the portal vein blood and MPO in the liver were increased in septic mice but were significantly reduced by DPX2. Liver tissue levels of inflammatory markers were increased in vehicle-treated septic mice, whereas these parameters were significantly decreased in the DPX2 group. TUNEL staining as well as transaminase levels revealed significant elevations in the vehicle group with significant reduction in hepatocyte injury/death with DPX2. Systemic inflammatory markers were significantly increased in the vehicle group but were significantly decreased in the DPX2 group. Lastly, there was a significant improvement in survival in the DPX2 group compared to the vehicle group.

CONCLUSIONS: Treatment with DPX2 reduces NETosis, acute liver injury, and systemic inflammatory response, leading to improved survival in sepsis.

articles.title: [Tuberculosis continuum: new definitions and clinical implications].
articles.abstract: In 2026, tuberculosis remains a major global public health challenge and the deadliest infectious disease in the world. The concept of the tuberculosis continuum is progressively replacing the traditional distinction between latent tuberculosis infection and tuberculosis disease. It describes Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection as a dynamic spectrum that includes incipient and subclinical stages, which may benefit from early diagnosis and treatment. Interferon-Gamma Release Assays remain the reference tests for screening for tuberculosis infection, although their ability to predict progression to disease is limited. The microbiological diagnosis relies on sputum analysis and rapid molecular assays. This review summarizes current knowledge and emerging diagnostic tools.

articles.title: [Transition from pediatric to adult care in pulmonology].
articles.abstract: The transition from pediatric to adult care for youth with chronic diseases is a major public health issue. This period is marked by significant biological, psychological, and social changes that can foster risk-taking behaviors, poor adherence, and gaps in follow-up care. Data indicate that a structured, gradual, and patient-centered process ensures continuity of care while promoting autonomy and treatment adherence. The attending physician plays a central role in this management, which is typically multidisciplinary. In pulmonology, transition approaches vary depending on the characteristics of the patient and the specific condition; this article illustrates this with four examples in pulmonology: asthma, cystic fibrosis, neuromuscular diseases, and bronchopulmonary dysplasia.

articles.title: [Asthma, air pollution and climate change].
articles.abstract: Asthma is a chronic respiratory disease affecting more than 360 million adults and children worldwide. Outdoor air pollution as well as indoor pollution are major contributors to poor asthma control and may also play a role in disease development. Climate change further exacerbates this burden and influences asthma through additional pathways, including longer pollen seasons, thunderstorm asthma, wildfires, and flooding. Individual protective measures have shown limited effectiveness, whereas reducing exposure at the source through transportation, urban planning, and energy policies remains the most effective strategy. Clinicians have an important role to play, both in educating patients and in advocating for public health measures.

articles.title: Rapid Acquisition of Complex Procedural Skills Using Simulation-Based Mastery Learning: A Multicenter Study in Gastroenterology Fellows.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND STUDY AIMS: Traditional apprenticeship-based procedural training is associated with variable learning outcomes and potential implications for patient safety. We assessed whether a simulation-based mastery learning (SBML) curriculum could enable novice gastroenterology fellows to achieve a predefined mastery benchmark in upper endoscopy.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, quasi-experimental study across six US gastroenterology fellowship programs. Participants were first-year fellows with no prior endoscopy experience assigned to SBML and second-year fellows who had completed 1 year of apprenticeship-based training. The SBML intervention consisted of a 5-day curriculum incorporating deliberate practice with expert coaching and required participants to meet or exceed a minimum passing standard (MPS) before completion. The primary outcome was performance on simulated upper endoscopy, assessed by blinded raters using a 6-point checklist (MPS = 4). Secondary outcomes included knowledge and self-efficacy.

RESULTS: Twenty-six first-year fellows in the SBML group and 15 second-year fellows in the apprenticeship group participated. All 26 (100%) fellows in the SBML group achieved the MPS after 5 days of training, compared with five (33%) of 15 fellows in the apprenticeship group after 1 year (p < 0.001; odds ratio 22.8 [95% CI 3.8-136.0]). Mean checklist scores were higher (4.7 [SD 0.4] vs. 3.2 [0.7]; p < 0.001). Post-training knowledge and self-efficacy were comparable between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: A structured 5-day SBML curriculum enabled novice gastroenterology fellows to achieve mastery-level performance in simulated upper endoscopy. Early competency-based training may accelerate skill acquisition and reduce variability versus apprenticeship.

articles.title: Response to the Letters to the Editor: Bedside Triage by Large Language Models in Acute Pancreatitis.
Conversations That Clear the Air: Supportive Parent-Adolescent Communication and Smoking in a Dyadic Perspective.
articles.abstract: Despite evidence that family communication shapes adolescent health behaviors, few studies have examined the dyadic associations between parents and adolescents. This study investigates supportive parent-adolescent communication and smoking in both generations. Data from a representative sample of 940 parent-adolescent dyads were analyzed using the Actor-Partner Interdependence Model (APIM) with latent constructs. Results revealed significant actor and partner effects for adolescents: both adolescents' and parents' perceptions of supportive communication were associated with lower smoking. For parents, no actor effect emerged, while a marginal partner effect suggested that adolescents' positive perception of communication was related to lower parental smoking. Overall, supportive communication could operate as relational resources associated with reduced smoking, although causal inference is limited by the cross-sectional design. The study integrates two theoretical frameworks (Communication Accommodation Theory and Affection Exchange Theory) as interpretative lenses for the different generational results and overall highlights the utility of dyadic modeling for understanding intergenerational health communication.

articles.title: Association between dietary inflammatory index and high blood pressure in children: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Emerging evidence suggests that the dietary inflammatory index (DII) may influence cardiovascular health in children, but the association between DII and high blood pressure (BP) remains inconsistent. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the association between DII and high BP in children and adolescents.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Wanfang, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure databases were searched from inception to June 12, 2026. Observational studies evaluating the association between DII and high BP in individuals < 18 years were included. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models accounting for the influence of potential heterogeneity.

RESULTS: Six cross-sectional studies comprising 56,741 children and adolescents (nine independent datasets) were included. Overall, a high DII was significantly associated with increased odds of high BP (OR: 1.33, 95% CI: 1.04 to 1.70; p = 0.02), with moderate heterogeneity (I2 = 65%). Leave-one-study-out sensitivity analyses yielded pooled ORs ranging from 1.23 to 1.46. However, the association was no longer statistically significant after excluding certain individual studies, indicating that the pooled finding was sensitive to study exclusion. Subgroup analyses showed no statistically detectable differences across geographic region, mean age, sex, DII cutoff values, BMI adjustment, or study quality (all p for subgroup differences > 0.05). Univariate meta-regression identified study quality (Newcastle-Ottawa Scale score) as the only significant moderator, with higher-quality studies showing a weaker association (coefficient = -0.12, 95% CI: -0.23 to -0.01; p = 0.04).

CONCLUSIONS: Higher dietary inflammatory potential may be associated with increased odds of high BP in children and adolescents. The evidence remains uncertain because all studies were cross-sectional, outcome definitions varied, and study-level sensitivity analyses showed instability.

articles.title: The Diagnostic Dilemma of Acute Vestibular Syndrome: Why HINTS Outperforms Diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging?
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the diagnostic approaches, specifically the comparative accuracy of bedside clinical examinations versus early neuroimaging, in differentiating central from peripheral causes of Acute Vestibular Syndrome (AVS).

METHODS: A comprehensive narrative literature review was conducted utilizing established scientific databases, including PubMed/Medline, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase, covering articles published up to 2024. A structured search strategy was applied using keywords such as "Acute Vestibular Syndrome", "Central vestibular dysfunction", "Peripheral vestibular dysfunction", and "HINTS protocol". Peer-reviewed clinical trials, mechanistic studies, and authoritative guidelines were included to synthesize the current evidence regarding the diagnosis and management of acute vertigo.

RESULTS: The synthesis of the literature reveals that targeted bedside neuro-otological examinations demonstrate superior sensitivity (96.8%) and specificity (98.5%) compared to early "Diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging" in detecting posterior circulation strokes within the initial 48 hours. Early neuroimaging frequently yields false-negative results in up to 14.3% of ischemic events.

CONCLUSION: Accurate differentiation of etiologies in continuous vertigo relies heavily on structured bedside clinical assessments rather than immediate neuroimaging. Implementing these clinical protocols prevents severe neurological sequelae from missed posterior fossa strokes while simultaneously avoiding unnecessary healthcare expenditures for benign peripheral conditions.

articles.title: Welfare-Oriented Non-Invasive Body Surface Temperature Monitoring of Endangered Pangolins via Infrared Thermography and Deep Learning.
articles.journal: Journal of applied animal welfare science : JAAWS
articles.abstract: Pangolin rescue and captive breeding require reliable, animal-welfare-oriented health monitoring. Body surface temperature is an important health indicator, yet invasive measurement may cause stress and infection risks, whereas conventional non-contact systems often compromise accuracy to meet edge-computing constraints. This study develops a non-contact body surface temperature monitoring system integrating a Jetson Orin NX controller, an IPM384 infrared camera, and an SHT35D temperature-humidity sensor for environmental compensation. A lightweight YOLOv8n-PDTW detector is introduced for animal-region localization in infrared images affected by blurred edges and interference from metal food bowls. The model achieves 99.1% precision, 98.4% recall, and an mAP@0.5:0.95 of 88.1%, while reducing model size and computational cost by 38.7% and 37.8%, respectively, compared with YOLOv8n. Embedded deployment enables real-time inference at 23.77 frames/s. Validation against PT100 sensors yields a mean absolute error of 0.234 °C. During 17 days of continuous monitoring, the system captured consistent individual temperature patterns, establishing stable physiological baselines. This efficient, non-contact approach supports pangolin conservation and provides a technical reference for health monitoring in other endangered solitary mammals, although further cross-species validation is required.

articles.title: Successful archetype JC polyomavirus infection in hiPSC-derived neural culture of astrocytes and neurons.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: JC polyomavirus (JCPyV) is the causative agent of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), a fatal neurodegenerative disease in immunocompromised individuals. JCPyV is a strictly human pathogen, and animal models are inappropriate to fully reproduce human disease. PML is often associated with neurotropic JCPyV variants harboring rearrangements within the non-coding regulatory region (NCCR) and VP1 capsid protein gene. However, archetype virus has also been identified in the brain and its association with PML cannot be excluded.

METHODS: To assess the ability of archetype virus to infect neural cells and to explore the cellular effects of JCPyV infection, we performed experimental 35-day infections in neural cell cultures consisting of astrocytes and neurons derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSC).

RESULTS: Archetype JCPyV infection was successfully established in both astrocytes and neurons at comparable rates. Infection in neurons supports our previous observations from brain tissue of PML patients, suggesting that neurons are also true target cells of JCPyV infection. Minor neurotropic variants emerged in the course of infection. RNA sequencing revealed significant regulation of genes implicated in cell cycle, DNA replication and repair, and cell division. The observed remarkable regulation of gene expression was proposedly driven by viral large T antigen, pRb and E2F family transcription factors, with consequent enhancement of JCPyV replication.

CONCLUSIONS: Our neural cell model reproduced many observations from PML brain tissue, suggesting that the model is appropriate to study key cellular events and the pathogenesis of JCPyV in neurodegeneration.

articles.title: Prevalence, Incidence, Clinical Presentation, and Treatment of Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome in Primary Care in the United Kingdom Between 1998 and 2025.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is a multisystemic disorder with a wide range of health consequences. We sought to describe temporal trends in the prevalence and incidence of PMOS and to characterize its clinical presentation, comorbidity burden, and pharmacological management in primary care in the United Kingdom (UK) between 1998 and 2025.

DESIGN: Population-based matched cohort study using primary care records from the UK Clinical Practice Research Datalink.

PATIENTS: Females newly diagnosed with PMOS between the ages of 15 and 49 matched on age, general practice, calendar year of cohort entry, and duration of medical history to population controls without PMOS.

MEASUREMENTS: Annual prevalence and incidence of diagnosed PMOS; baseline prevalence and incidence of cardinal PMOS features and various comorbidities; and pre- and post-cohort entry prevalence of hormonal contraceptive, anti-androgen, ovulation-inducing drug, and metformin use.

RESULTS: The prevalence of diagnosed PMOS increased from < 0.1% in 1998 to 2.0% in 2025, with incidence rising from 0.1 to 3.6 per 1,000 person-years over the same period. Among 125,482 patients with newly diagnosed PMOS matched with an equal number of controls, patients with PMOS had higher baseline prevalence and incidence of cardinal features of PMOS, as well as diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease, sleep apnea, thyroid disorders, endometriosis, uterine fibroids, chronic pain, depression, and anxiety. Use of anti-androgens, ovulation-inducing drugs, and metformin was substantially higher in patients with PMOS, especially in the year following diagnosis.

CONCLUSIONS: PMOS is increasingly diagnosed in UK primary care and is associated with substantial multimorbidity and pharmacotherapy.

articles.title: Specialty-Driven Divergence in Cardiac Imaging (Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography and Single-Photon Emission Computed Tomography) Utilization Following the 2021 Chest Pain Guideline at a Large Military Medical Center.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) received a strong recommendation in the 2021 Chest Pain Guideline as a first-line test for the evaluation of stable chest pain in patients without known coronary artery disease; however, real-world adoption remains variable. Within the Military Health System, imaging decisions directly affect operational readiness. We evaluated changes in the utilization of CCTA versus single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) myocardial perfusion imaging before and after guideline publication at a large military medical center.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 15,772 CCTA or SPECT studies performed for the evaluation of suspected coronary artery disease from 2018 through 2023 at Joint Base San Antonio. Studies were stratified into pre-guideline (on or before October 31, 2021) and post-guideline (on or after November 1, 2021) periods. The primary outcome was imaging modality (CCTA versus SPECT), analyzed by ordering specialty, sex, and age. Chi-square testing, repeat-testing characterization, and generalized estimating equations logistic regression were performed.

RESULTS: Overall, 41.3% of studies were CCTA and 58.7% were SPECT. Among cardiologists, the proportion of CCTA studies increased from 50% to 61% after guideline publication, whereas CCTA use among non-cardiology specialties declined from 36% to 25%, reaching a quarterly nadir of 12.6% in quarter 2 of 2022. Cardiology ordering was the strongest independent predictor of CCTA use (odds ratio 1.90, 95% CI, 1.76-2.05; P < .001). The post-guideline period alone was not independently associated with increased CCTA use (odds ratio 0.98, P = .69). Younger age strongly favored CCTA, and repeat testing most commonly involved SPECT-to-SPECT sequences.

CONCLUSIONS: Publication of the 2021 Chest Pain Guideline was not associated with a uniform increase in CCTA adoption. Provider specialty, rather than the guideline period itself, was the dominant factor associated with modality selection, highlighting the need for targeted education and decision-support interventions to improve evidence-based imaging utilization.

articles.title: Circulation of Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever Virus at the Domestic-Wildlife Interface of the Mnisi Community, Mpumalanga Province, South Africa.
articles.journal: Vector borne and zoonotic diseases (Larchmont, N.Y.)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever (CCHF) is caused by an arthropod-borne virus, Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV), which can infect a wide range of species, including humans, and is endemic in domestic and wild animals in Africa.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Sera were collected from livestock (cattle n = 423, goats n = 167), companion animals (dogs n = 152), and wild animals (impala antelope n = 182) in the Mnisi community (Mpumalanga Province, South Africa), an area characterized by frequent interactions between humans and animals susceptible to CCHFV infection. The presence of CCHFV-specifc antibodies was determined using a commercial double antigen enzyme-immunosorbent assay.

RESULTS: CCHF-specific antibodies were detected in a high proportion of sera from domestic ruminants (72.8% cattle, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 68.3-77.0; 21.6% goats, 95% CI: 15.6-28.6), whereas all sera from impala antelope and dogs tested negative.

CONCLUSIONS: CCHFV seroprevalence in domestic ruminants is high, confirming widespread exposure to CCHFV in the Mnisi community and highlighting the potential risk of transmission to humans, particularly cattle herders.

articles.title: Impatience and Present Bias Do Not Determine Weight Loss in Obesity: Evidence From Lab-in-Field and Survey Data.
articles.abstract: A substantial body of behavioral economics literature links obesity to time preferences, notably impatience-a time-consistent preference for earlier rewards-and present bias-the disproportionate overweighting of immediate payoffs that leads to dynamic inconsistency. Unlike much previous literature, which asks whether time preferences predict weight in broader populations, we examine whether they predict subsequent weight loss among adults who already have overweight or obesity. Using clinically measured outcomes and incentivized preference data from 287 adults with obesity and pre-diabetes enrolled in a 12-month randomized lifestyle-intervention trial, we find that neither impatience nor present bias predicts reductions in body fat or BMI. These findings are robust to alternative measurement strategies and are not explained by the impatience-related attrition that we uncover. To strengthen external validity, we replicate the null relationship using self-reported time preference measures in a nationally representative sample of 7277 adults with overweight or obesity. As baseline impatience meaningfully reduces the likelihood of trial completion, we conclude that impatience affects adherence to medically recommended programs but does not directly impede weight-loss success among those who remain engaged. Interventions targeting impatience or self-control alone may therefore be insufficient to promote weight loss in clinical populations.

articles.title: Exploring the Potential Mechanisms Linking Bisphenol A Exposure to Atrial Fibrillation: An Integrated Multi-Dimensional Analysis from Network Toxicology to In Vivo Validation.
articles.journal: Omics : a journal of integrative biology
articles.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common clinical arrhythmia with complex pathogenesis and limited therapeutic options. The pro-arrhythmic effect of environmental endocrine disruptor bisphenol A (BPA) remains unclear. This study integrated network toxicology, Mendelian randomization (MR), molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, single-cell transcriptomics and in vivo rat experiments to construct a multi-dimensional evidence chain for exploring BPA-mediated AF mechanisms and key intervention targets. We screened 206 shared targets of BPA and AF, which were enriched in endocrine resistance, phosphoinositide 3-kinase-protein kinase B, and lipid-metabolism pathways. Protein-protein interaction and two-sample MR analyses, supported by genetic evidence, suggested cystatin C (CST3) as a potential risk factor for AF, while glutathione S-transferase A1 (GSTA1) and placental growth factor (PGF) served as potential protective factors. Molecular docking confirmed favorable binding activities between BPA and core targets (binding energy < -5.0 kcal/mol), and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations verified stable complex conformations under physiological conditions. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed cell-type-specific expression of target genes: CST3 in immune and stromal cells, GSTA1 in smooth muscle cells and fibroblasts, and PGF predominantly in smooth muscle cells. Further experiments in Sprague-Dawley rats demonstrated that BPA exposure increased AF inducibility, upregulated atrial CST3, down-regulated GSTA1 and PGF, and aggravated atrial fibrosis and inflammatory infiltration. Collectively, BPA may promote AF by interfering with the functions of CST3, GSTA1, and PGF. This study provides evidence for the pro-arrhythmic effects of environmental pollutants and theoretical references for targeted prevention and treatment of AF.

articles.title: Comparison of outcome in patients with idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) following optic nerve sheath fenestration (ONSF) using a medial transconjunctival approach with dural window or superomedial lid-crease incision approach.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study compares outcomes and complications of two common optic nerve sheath fenestration (ONSF) approaches for treating vision loss in idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH).

METHODS: This retrospective comparative study included 71 eyes of 48 patients with IIH who underwent ONSF by two oculoplastic surgeons at the University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center from January 2010 to December 2023. Patients were grouped by surgical approach: Group 1 underwent a superomedial lid-crease incision with fenestration, and Group 2 underwent a medial transconjunctival approach with dural window. Outcomes measured included operative time and changes in visual acuity, visual fields, and color vision within a 180-day postoperative period. Complications were also recorded. Fisher's exact test was used to compare favorable outcome rates between groups. Mean operation time was compared using a simple paired t-test.

RESULTS: Both surgical approaches were successful in preventing progression of vision loss in patients with IIH. Postoperatively, visual acuity was stable or improved in 97% of Group 1 and 85% of Group 2 patients. Both groups showed stability of visual fields and color vision testing. At 6 months, there was no statistically significant difference in outcome between the groups. Furthermore, mean operation time was approximately 30 min shorter in Group 1 compared to Group 2. Both groups had low complication rates.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that the superomedial lid-crease approach with fenestration and the medial transconjunctival approach with dural window for ONSF are both effective in preventing vision loss in patients with IIH, with similarly low side‑effect profiles.

articles.title: Plasmonically Enhanced Microarray Immunoassay for High-Sensitivity Monitoring of Heart Failure.
articles.abstract: Point‑of‑care testing (POCT) demands diagnostic platforms that pair high analytical sensitivity with compact, low‑cost readout hardware, yet fluorescence‑based immunoassays face a fundamental tradeoff between detector cost and detection performance. Plasmonic nanocavities-such as metal-dielectric-metal nanopatch antennas-offer a powerful signal‑amplification strategy by dramatically enhancing fluorophore emission, enabling sensitive fluorescence detection with inexpensive optics. Here, we introduce a plasmonically enhanced fluorescence microarray immunoassay that integrates nanopatch antennas for high‑sensitivity, low‑cost quantification of key heart‑failure biomarkers, NT‑proBNP, NGAL, and galectin‑3, using a custom smartphone‑based detector. The nanopatch antennas yield up to 485‑fold fluorescence enhancement enabling quantitative and multiplexed detection with limits of detection of 0.055, 3.932, and 0.864 ng/mL, respectively. Analysis of NT‑proBNP-positive human samples shows strong correlation with clinically validated assays, demonstrating the potential of this plasmonically enhanced platform to deliver high‑performance heart‑failure biomarker monitoring at low cost in resource‑limited and point‑of‑care settings.

articles.title: Heterogeneous Permissiveness of Chicken Cells and Tissues to Oropouche Viruses.
articles.journal: Vector borne and zoonotic diseases (Larchmont, N.Y.)
articles.abstract: Massive outbreaks of a reassortant Oropouche virus (OROV) spread across Latin America and the Caribbean in 2023-2025. OROV is a reemerging arbovirus belonging to the trisegmented RNA peribunyavirus family. Viral transmission occurs in sylvatic and urban cycles involving humans and other vertebrates with Culicoides biting midges as the main vector in urban settings. Anti-OROV antibodies have been found in domestic and wild birds in Brazilian OROV-endemic areas. However, no studies exist on the permissiveness of OROV in avian models, and the contribution of birds to the OROV spread remains largely unexplored. Our research indicates that chicken embryonic fibroblasts and chicken tissue explants from the liver, heart, and lung are selectively infected by OROV strains isolated by our group in South America, including the novel OROV reassortant. This work contributes to the development of avian models to investigate new determinants in the infection and transmission of an important arbovirus in the Americas.

articles.title: Social and Structural Forces Shaping Reproductive Decision-Making in Hispanic Women with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Qualitative Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) disproportionately affects women of reproductive age, making pregnancy timing and contraception use central to care. Although clinical counseling is vital to reproductive planning, less is known about the sociocultural and structural influences shaping reproductive decision-making among Hispanic women with SLE in the United States. This study explored patient perspectives on multi-level factors influencing reproductive health decision-making.

METHODS: We conducted semi-structured interviews with 30 Hispanic women with SLE recruited from a safety-net rheumatology clinic and a community lupus support organization. Participants were aged 18-45 years, sexually active or considering pregnancy within three years, and fluent in English or Spanish. Interviews were conducted virtually, transcribed, and analyzed using a grounded theory-informed approach, with the Socioecological Model retrospectively applied to guide analysis.

RESULTS: Four major themes aligned with the Socioecological Framework. Reproductive decision-making was shaped by structural stability, including financial security, career readiness, and confidence managing SLE during pregnancy. Culture and religion were present but variably integrated into reproductive health considerations, while partners and family members influenced how risks and decisions were discussed and supported. Participants also relied on informal information networks, including peer experiences and online resources, to interpret reproductive risks and contraception options.

CONCLUSION: Reproductive planning among Hispanic women with SLE is influenced by structural, relational, and informational factors extending beyond the clinical encounter. These findings highlight the need for supportive interventions or resources beyond the clinical encounter, including supportive networks, trusted information, and peer-informed support tailored to young women living with SLE.

articles.title: Diagnostic agreement between ChatGPT-based interpretation of laboratory-generated flow cytometry graphical outputs and hematologist consensus in suspected acute leukemia.
articles.abstract: Accurate, rapid, and standardized interpretation of multiparametric flow cytometry findings is essential for clinical decision-making in patients evaluated for suspected acute leukemia. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of ChatGPT, a general-purpose large language model, in interpreting de-identified, laboratory-generated flow cytometry graphical outputs from patients with suspected acute leukemia and to assess its agreement with the consensus interpretation of two hematologists in terms of diagnostic classification, blast percentage estimation, and hematogone detection. This retrospective observational validation study included 560 patients who underwent bone marrow aspiration and flow cytometric immunophenotyping during their initial diagnostic evaluation for suspected acute leukemia. All included patients were undergoing initial diagnostic evaluation and had neither a previous diagnosis of leukemia nor prior leukemia-directed treatment. The consensus diagnosis established by two hematologists was considered the reference standard. Between May 4 and 15, 2026, de-identified, laboratory-generated PDF images containing flow cytometry dot plots from a three-tube acute leukemia panel comprising 28 antibody-fluorochrome combinations were uploaded directly through the ChatGPT Plus web interface and interpreted using GPT-5.5 (OpenAI). Raw FCS files were not provided. Using the same standardized prompt for each case, the model was asked to estimate the blast percentage, select a single most likely diagnosis from five predefined categories (no pathology, MDS, AML, B-ALL, or T-ALL), and determine the presence or absence of hematogones. The initial response for each case was archived and directly encoded without adjudication. Diagnosis-specific performance was evaluated using one-versus-rest sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, accuracy, and F1-score. Overall agreement between ChatGPT-generated classifications and hematologist consensus was assessed using Cohen's kappa. Pearson's correlation coefficient was used to evaluate the association between blast percentage estimates, whereas Bland-Altman analysis was used to quantify agreement, systematic bias, and 95% limits of agreement. Hematogone detection was evaluated as a binary classification task using sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy. ChatGPT achieved an overall diagnostic accuracy of 78.8% (95% CI, 75.2%-81.9%), with substantial agreement with hematologist consensus (Cohen's κ = 0.712; 95% CI, 0.664-0.757). Diagnosis-specific sensitivity ranged from 69.2% to 87.3%, and PPV ranged from 60.0% to 93.5%. The highest sensitivity was observed for MDS, whereas the highest PPV was observed for no pathology. McNemar's test identified significant systematic differences between ChatGPT and hematologist classifications for no pathology (p = 0.041), AML (p = 0.008), and T-ALL (p = 0.023). Blast percentage estimates were strongly correlated (Pearson's r = 0.818; 95% CI, 0.789-0.844; p< 0.001); however, Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated a mean positive bias of 3.92 percentage points, indicating systematic overestimation by ChatGPT. For hematogone detection, ChatGPT achieved an accuracy of 89.5%, sensitivity of 70.3%, and specificity of 92.4%. ChatGPT-based flow cytometry interpretation showed promise for preliminary diagnostic classification and quality assurance applications. However, expert hematologist validation remains essential, particularly in scenarios associated with high diagnostic consequences, including AML and T-ALL classification, blast percentage estimation, and accurate discrimination of hematogones.

articles.title: The Case of a 59-Year-Old Woman With Acute Right-Sided Weakness and Progressive White Matter Changes.
articles.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology

articles.title: Clinical Utility of Procalcitonin and Its Association With Pathogen Types and Prognosis in Patients With Bloodstream Infection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Procalcitonin (PCT) levels have been reported less frequently in polymicrobial bloodstream infection (BSI). The purpose of this study is to assess the value of serum PCT in early identifying pathogen types isolated from BSI including mixed microorganisms and predicting patient outcomes.

METHODS: Between January 2012 and December 2018, medical records were collected on adult patients with BSI who met the inclusion criteria and underwent PCT testing within 24 h of the onset.

RESULTS: 817 episodes were included in the study. The 30-day mortality rate among patients with polymicrobial BSI was notably elevated compared to those with monomicrobial BSI (50.0% vs. 16.9%, p < 0.001). A notable increase in PCT levels was detected in non-survivors when compared to survivors (6.06 ng/mL vs. 1.23 ng/mL, p < 0.001). Receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC) analysis showed that a PCT level of 3.79 ng/mL yielded a 49.4% sensitivity, a 77.6% specificity, an 83.0% positive predictive value (PPV) and a 40.9% negative predictive value (NPV) for gram-negative or multiple bacteria BSI (the area under the curve 0.642, p = 0.0199). Additionally, the areas under the ROC curve of PCT predicting 30-day mortality was 0.674 (p = 0.0238) with a cut-off value of 1.11 ng/mL, a sensitivity of 79.9%, a specificity of 49.0%, a PPV of 25.9% and a NPV of 91.6%.

CONCLUSIONS: The significant elevation of PCT levels may contribute to early distinguishing gram-negative or polymicrobial BSIs and outcome evaluation with low-to-moderate discriminatory ability, thus optimizing antibiotic treatment regimens and improving the prognosis.

articles.title: An Investigation on the Association Between HIV-1 Integrase and Gene Knock-out.
articles.abstract: Lentivirus-mediated gene therapy has shown promise to provide therapeutic genes for permanent treatment of several diseases. This process relies on integration of the virus genome into that of the host using the virus integrase, which cuts open host DNA for insertion before repair by the cell's non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) pathway. NHEJ can result in insertions or deletions (indel mutations), which may result in genotoxicity. Vector integration is known to activate oncogenes, primarily due to the interaction of the lentivirus vector (LV) genome with genes found near to the site of vector integration. Inactivation of tumor suppressor genes, or gene knockout is also known to occur. In the production of virus particles, genome empty particles are also generated alongside full vector genome containing LV, each still carry the integrase enzyme. Hence, the frequency of genotoxicity associated with NHEJ activity following vector integration or integrase activity alone is difficult to quantify, particularly for gene knock-out. In this study, we used the HPRT locus as a genetic target to investigate gene disruption by genome-containing and empty LV particles to identify the integrase contribution to HPRT mutagenesis. The HPRT gene is large at 35 kb in size and has been used for several mutagenesis studies by carcinogens. It offers forward and reverse selection, where cells with functional HPRT selected for and then cells with inactivated HPRT caused by mutagenesis can be selected to quantify the mutagenic effects of the carcinogen. We firstly used V79 and MRC5 cell lines and primary human T cells derived from healthy donors (male and female) with functional NHEJ DNA repair pathways and AT5BIVA cells with impaired DNA damage repair to follow the cleavage and repair process associated with integrase activity using a fluorescent marker against γH2AX that binds to broken DNA, which is then released after repair. By this analysis, the activity of the virus integrase was also compared for LV with and without virus genome and cells not exposed to virus infection. We next used forward and reverse selection to measure the presence and loss of HPRT activity in infected cells that was observed for genome full and empty LV particles. To further support our findings that integrase activity can cause gene knockout, we expressed HIV-1 integrase in yeast to measure knockout of the CAN-1 gene and found this also occurs. These data show genotoxicity by LV particles is possible even for particles not carrying a therapeutic vector genome and suggest to reduce this potential, empty particles should be removed during LV during manufacture.

articles.title: Letter: Methodological Considerations Regarding "Correlation Between Lp-PLA2 and Platelet Activation in Coronary Artery Disease".
Cardioversion and stroke volume index rather than heart rate alone define haemodynamic success of rate control in septic shock-associated atrial fibrillation.
Dsg2 arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy is accompanied by neocortical synaptic changes in adult mice.
articles.abstract: Heart failure is frequently accompanied by cognitive impairment, yet structural correlates in the brain remain incompletely defined. Here, we assessed whether chronic heart failure is associated with synaptic ultrastructural remodeling in the murine neocortex using a mouse model of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy caused by a point mutation in desmoglein-2 (Dsg2-W2A). Brains from aged adult homozygous Dsg2-W2A mice and age-matched wildtype controls were processed for transmission electron microscopy, and excitatory synapses in layer I of the prefrontal cortex were quantitatively assessed, with comparative analyses in the somatosensory cortex. In the prefrontal cortex, presynaptic terminal area and synaptic vesicle number were reduced in mutant mice, whereas postsynaptic measures were not altered. The prevalence of mitochondria and the spine apparatus within synapses was comparable between genotypes, suggesting no major loss of synapse-associated organelles. Finally, synaptic parameters in the prefrontal cortex did not show a systematic dependence on distance to local blood vessels. Together, these findings indicate moderate region- and compartment-specific synaptic ultrastructural alterations associated with Dsg2 cardiomyopathy and chronic heart failure, with predominant effects on presynaptic terminals.

articles.title: From technique to sensitivity: the transformation of clinical and ethical reasoning in physiotherapy students in the context of chronic neurodegenerative diseases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The evolution of Physiotherapy requires a shift from the biomedical model towards bioethical and humanistic approaches. This study explores how final-year students perceive their professional role when dealing with patients with complex neurodegenerative conditions, where traditional technical success is challenged by the irreversibility of the deterioration.

METHODS: Qualitative research based on interpretative description. Thirty final-year students from the University of Almería (Spain) took part, divided into five working groups. Three training sessions and discussions were held on Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), Alzheimer's disease, stroke and Rett syndrome. The data were analysed using thematic analysis and triangulation by researchers external to the study, with reflexivity ensured through logbooks.

RESULTS: A shift in clinical reasoning was identified, with sensitivity taking precedence over technique. Students redefined therapeutic success in terms of "comfort" and support, valuing "microscopic achievements" such as the preservation of dignity and the alleviation of distress. Of particular note is the ability to adapt ethical principles according to the patient's cognitive integrity (autonomy in ALS versus protection in Alzheimer's) and the integration of the carer as an inseparable part of the therapeutic process.

CONCLUSION: Future physiotherapists perceive humanization and the empathetic interpretation of non-verbal cues as essential therapeutic tools. Unlike previous studies focused on clinical experience, this research explores pre-clinical ethical maturation, offering a unique perspective on the educational foundation and humanistic predisposition of future graduates prior to their immersion in the healthcare system. It is imperative that academic curricula formally integrate competencies in bioethics, palliative care and emotional management to prepare graduates for extreme vulnerability and prevent early professional burnout.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Brain Age Gap from Non-Contrast CT Is Independently Associated with Functional Outcome after Acute Ischemic Stroke.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
articles.abstract: BackgroundOutcomes after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) vary beyond lesion burden and clinical severity, suggesting a role for baseline structural brain vulnerability. We evaluated whether brain age gap (BrainAGE) derived from routine non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) is associated with functional outcome after AIS.MethodsWe analyzed 1,173 AIS patients from a prospective multicenter cohort. A deep learning model estimated brain age from contralesional baseline NCCT to minimize lesion-related confounding. BrainAGE was defined as predicted minus chronological age. The primary outcome was 90-day functional status, assessed using proportional odds regression adjusted for age, sex, baseline stroke severity, early ischemic changes, and reperfusion therapy.ResultsBrainAGE was higher in AIS patients than in controls (+3.1 ± 9.1 years; p<0.001). Higher BrainAGE was associated with worse functional outcome after adjustment for age, sex, and other clinical predictors (POR 1.091 per 5 years; 95% CI 1.023-1.162; p=0.008). BrainAGE improved model fit but modestly improved discrimination.ConclusionsBrainAGE from routine NCCT provided modest incremental prognostic information beyond age and conventional clinical predictors. These findings support CT-based BrainAGE as a marker of brain health complementary to established prognostic factors. Whether BrainAGE improves patient-level risk stratification or clinical decision-making requires independent external validation and prospective evaluation.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Persistent cerebrovascular dysfunction and altered mural cell calcium signaling after sepsis recovery in female mice.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis is associated with long-term cognitive impairment, yet the cerebrovascular mechanisms underlying these deficits remain poorly understood, particularly after clinical recovery. Although cerebral blood flow abnormalities are well documented during acute sepsis, whether microvascular dysfunction persists and how mural cells contribute to these changes remain unknown.

METHODS: We used longitudinal in vivo two-photon imaging in a fecal-induced peritonitis model to examine pericyte calcium signaling, microvascular hemodynamics, vasomotion, and neurovascular coupling before and after sepsis in the same female mice.

RESULTS: Two weeks after sepsis, when mice no longer exhibited clinical signs of illness, both ensheathing and thin-strand pericytes displayed persistently elevated basal Ca2⁺ activity. In the arteriole-capillary transition zone, elevated ensheathing pericyte Ca2⁺ was paradoxically associated with vessel dilation and diminished vasomotor activity. These abnormalities were accompanied by altered red blood cell distribution and attenuated vascular responses during neurovascular coupling.

CONCLUSION: Together, these findings demonstrate that clinically recovered mice exhibit persistent abnormalities in pericyte calcium signaling, microvascular blood flow regulation, and neurovascular coupling-associated vascular responses, identifying pericyte dysfunction as a potential contributor to long-term cerebrovascular impairment after sepsis.

articles.title: Gendered Ethnic Harassment at Work a​nd Impaired Well-Being: The Moderating Effects of Victims' Gendered Ethnic Identity Centrality, Gender, and Ethnic Background.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.abstract: This study examined the effects of gendered ethnic harassment on impaired well-being, and the potential moderating roles of gendered ethnic identity centrality as well as gender and ethnic background.
