An online questionnaire was used to collect data from 275 U.K.-resident workers (50.2% female, 49.8% male; 50.2% ethnically diverse [i.e., Asian, Black, Indian, 'other'], 49.8% White). Aligned with official statistics, ethnically diverse respondents were younger than White respondents. Respondents' age was not controlled for in analyses, in order to allow meaningful comparisons between real groups of people with different ethnic background. Gendered ethnic harassment was associated with higher anxiety and higher depression. Gendered ethnic identity centrality buffered the effects of gendered ethnic harassment on lower job satisfaction and lower life satisfaction, irrespective of gender and ethnic background, and on higher depression in White men. For ethnically diverse women with low gendered ethnic identity centrality, the effect of gendered ethnic harassment on higher anxiety was aggravated. The findings show that contextual factors may help explain inconclusive research evidence about identity centrality's potential buffering role. With view to organisational practice, identity-blind and identity-conscious diversity and inclusion practices must be used simultaneously, in order to increase people's positive well-being and to keep people's negative well-being at a minimum.

articles.title: Cardiovascular disturbances and ward hypotension after major vascular surgery: a single-centre prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Postoperative hypotension can be caused by vasodilation, myocardial dysfunction, severe hypovolemia, and obstruction. We sought to estimate the effects of these causes on the incidence of hypotension after major vascular surgery.

METHODS: We conducted a single-centre prospective cohort study of male and female adult patients undergoing major vascular surgery. We conducted point-of-care ultrasound and sidestream darkfield microscopy imaging to detect vasodilation, myocardial dysfunction, severe hypovolemia, and obstruction. The primary outcome was hypotension (systolic blood pressure < 90 mm Hg or a vasopressor infusion) within 24 hr of surgery.

RESULTS: We recruited 100 patients, of whom 89 had data available for analysis. Hypotension occurred in 20 participants (23%), vasodilation in 30 (34%), and myocardial dysfunction in 11 (12%). Severe hypovolemia and obstruction were not observed. The adjusted marginal risk difference of hypotension was 33% (95% confidence interval [CI], 14% to 53%; P < 0.001) for vasodilation and 41% (95% CI, 3% to 79%; P = 0.03) for myocardial dysfunction. Vasodilation increased the risk of intensive care unit admission by 27% (95% CI, 8% to 45%; P = 0.006) and of requiring a vasopressor infusion by 22% (95% CI, 4% to 39%; P = 0.02).

CONCLUSIONS: Vasodilation and myocardial dysfunction increased the risk of postoperative hypotension, providing insight into the mechanistic development of postoperative hypotension. The absence of severe hypovolemia was surprising. Clinicians should assess for vasodilation and myocardial dysfunction as potential preludes to postoperative hypotension, potentially using point-of-care echocardiography and sidestream darkfield microscopy.

articles.title: Primary Care Engagement and Acute Care Utilization by Interpreter Use in an Urban Resident Clinic: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients who prefer a language other than English (LOE) experience well-documented differences in health care access and quality. How care delivery and utilization differ for those requiring professional interpreter services in resident continuity clinics is not well characterized.

OBJECTIVE: To compare primary care delivery, preventive screening, chronic disease management, and utilization between patients who did and did not require interpreter services.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study using electronic health record data, October 2022 to October 2024. Setting and Participants An urban internal medicine resident continuity clinic in St. Louis, MO, with in-person interpreter services; 14,457 adults, of whom 1058 had documented interpreter use (LOE; > 50 preferred languages) and 13,399 did not (English-proficient). Main Measures Demographics, area-based socioeconomic indicators, comorbidity burden, screening adherence, clinic attendance, emergency department (ED) visits, and hospitalizations. No primary outcome was pre-specified. Key Results LOE patients were older and more often uninsured or Medicaid-insured, yet resided in less-deprived, higher-income areas (median ADI national percentile 71 vs 85) and had lower comorbidity burden. Colorectal, breast, and cervical cancer screening did not differ. Among those with diabetes, glycemic control was worse (A1c < 7%: 49.3% vs 56.8%; difference - 7.5%, 95% CI - 12.9 to - 2.1), as were tetanus vaccination and HIV screening. They had lower no-show rates (14.0% vs 21.0%; difference - 7.1%, 95% CI - 7.9 to - 6.2), more completed visits (mean 4.6 vs 3.9; difference + 0.7, 95% CI 0.5 to 0.9), fewer ED visits (36.2% vs 56.3%; difference - 20.1%, 95% CI - 23.1 to - 17.1), and fewer hospitalizations (26.5% vs 37.3%; difference - 10.8%, 95% CI - 13.6 to - 8.0).

CONCLUSIONS: In this single clinic, LOE patients had greater primary care engagement and lower acute care utilization, with residual gaps in glycemic control and vaccination. These descriptive, hypothesis-generating findings may reflect who reaches care as well as language-access supports and warrant prospective study.

articles.title: Guiding Proton Pump Inhibitor Use Across Common Clinical Settings: A Narrative Review of Guidelines and Expert Consensus.
articles.abstract: The prescription of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) remains high despite well-established indications for their appropriate use. Potential risks associated with long-term PPI use have been frequently reported, including drug-drug interactions, renal disease, dementia, gastrointestinal infections, malignancies, nutritional deficiencies, and cardio-cerebrovascular events. General practitioners are often the primary point of contact for initiating therapy and, importantly, for reassessing the ongoing need for treatment. This review aims to provide practical algorithms for appropriate use across different clinical scenarios, including gastroesophageal reflux, dyspepsia, gastric ulcers, stress ulcer prophylaxis, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug-induced ulcer prophylaxis, and PPI deprescribing strategies. The algorithms were developed based on current clinical practice guidelines and expert opinion, integrating recommendations on indications, duration of therapy, and criteria for deprescribing. This review does not address the role of other concomitant interventions such as surgery, antibiotics, or alternative acid-suppressive therapies. By synthesizing available evidence and existing recommendations into practical clinical decision pathways, this review seeks to support clinicians in optimizing PPI prescribing and reducing inappropriate use.

articles.title: An Interpretable Multimodal Deep Learning Framework Integrating MRI and Clinical Data via Bidirectional Cross-Modal Attention for Improved Cardiac Disease Detection.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases continue to be the primary cause of mortality worldwide; however, precise diagnosis is often limited by dependence on individual data modalities and the unclear nature of traditional deep learning models. In this study, we introduce an explainable multimodal deep learning framework that simultaneously analyzes cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and structured clinical variables through a bidirectional cross-modal attention mechanism that operates on token sequences. The architecture utilizes modality-specific encoders ResNet-50 for imaging and a multilayer perceptron for clinical data interconnected through attention that dynamically aligns complementary information, reducing feature dilution and modal dominance. A multitask objective that includes classification, contrastive alignment (InfoNCE), and regularization further reinforces semantic consistency across modalities. Integrated post hoc explainability modules, such as Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping for spatial localization and SHapley Additive exPlanations for clinical feature attribution, offer transparent decision support. Tested on a cohort of 12,847 patients using fivefold cross-validation, the framework achieved an accuracy of 94.2% and an area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve of 0.97, significantly surpassing unimodal and traditional multimodal baselines (p < 0.01). The explanations generated showed 91% concordance with independent cardiologist evaluations. The findings presented herein were derived through internal five-fold cross-validation conducted at a solitary tertiary care institution, thereby substantiating internal validity while limiting multicenter generalizability; consequently, external validation is requisite for broader applicability. These results demonstrate that attention-driven multimodal fusion, combined with post hoc explainability, provides both strong diagnostic performance and clinically useful transparency, positioning the framework as a promising internally validated approach and a foundation for future external validation.

articles.title: Accounting for hidden wild inputs in conservation substitutes.
articles.journal: Conservation biology : the journal of the Society for Conservation Biology
articles.abstract: Artificial propagation, wildlife farming, ranching, cultivation, and aquaculture support commercial markets and livelihoods, and their products may be promoted as substitutes for wild harvest. However, production labels for these products cannot be used to determine conservation benefit because output may depend on wild inputs. Thus, we developed hidden wild-input (HWI) accounting as a bounded assessment framework. HWIs are wild-derived biological inputs that are important for producing substitutes but also potentially for conservation, and they are underrepresented in labels, statistics, and assessments. Through conceptual analysis and comparison, we identified establishment, maintenance, and scaling production inputs and conducted a counterfactual evaluation to determine the avoided harvest of wild targets, source-population burdens, and other ecological effects, such as wild-input intensity, wild-origin proportion, supplementation frequency, and elasticity. We examined four examples of wild-input use to illustrate the framework: Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) source code Y exposed the gap between production-origin categories and upstream accounting; crocodile ranching showed recurring wild inputs can coexist with conservation gains under regulated management; capture-based European eel (Anguilla anguilla) aquaculture demonstrated production-extraction coupling; and the artificial production of Chinese caterpillar fungus (Ophiocordyceps sinensis) revealed potential commercial dependence when recurring inputs are not reported. Together, the examples showed that source categories cannot be used to quantify upstream burdens, recurring inputs do not indicate conservation failure, and input-output coefficients demonstrate coupling but not net effects. Conservation benefit should be assessed against a credible no-expansion counterfactual by asking whether additional output reduces target harvest, added wild-input burdens remain sustainable, and other ecological effects reverse the gain. Complete biological independence is neither necessary nor sufficient. When input, demographic, and market-substitution data are unavailable, uncertainty should be reported rather than replaced by assumptions based on production labels.

articles.title: Brain MRI Findings of Children with Paroxysmal Sympathetic Hyperactivity Following Severe Traumatic Brain Injury.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: Paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity (PSH) is a clinically significant complication of severe traumatic brain injury (TBI), characterized by episodic sympathetic overactivation and associated with worse clinical outcomes. However, its neuroanatomical basis remains poorly defined, particularly in pediatric populations. This study aimed to identify brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings associated with PSH in children with severe TBI.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of children with severe TBI admitted to a tertiary pediatric intensive care unit. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was systematically reviewed using a predefined region-based approach to evaluate patterns of injury and diffuse axonal injury (DAI) grade. Patients were classified as having PSH based on documented sustained recurrent episodes of sympathetic hyperactivity and physician diagnosis. Neuroanatomical injury patterns were compared between patients with and without PSH. Univariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify independent neuroanatomical predictors of PSH.

RESULTS: A total of 86 children with severe TBI was included, of whom 30 (34.9%) developed PSH. Patients with PSH were older and more frequently injured in motor vehicle collisions. In unadjusted analyses, PSH was associated with deep gray matter and bilateral injury patterns. In multivariable models, basal ganglia injury remained the strongest independent neuroanatomical predictor of PSH (odds ratio 54.8). Grade 3 DAI was also associated with PSH (odds ratio 7.8). After adjustment, PSH remained associated with worse outcomes, including longer intensive care and hospital length of stay, prolonged mechanical ventilation, and higher mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: In children with severe TBI, basal ganglia injury was the strongest independent neuroanatomical correlate of PSH, supporting a central role for deep gray structures in autonomic dysregulation. PSH was associated with worse clinical outcomes, underscoring its substantial clinical burden. MRI-defined injury patterns may help identify patients at increased risk and facilitate earlier targeted management. Prospective studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

articles.title: PKA signaling controls ILC3 homeostasis and IL-23-mediated inflammation in the gut.
articles.abstract: Group 3 innate lymphoid cells (ILC3s) are tissue-protective lymphocytes that are enriched in the healthy gut and depleted in gastrointestinal disorders. Here we created a single-cell atlas to define how ILC3s respond to distinct stimuli, observing that prostaglandin engages protein kinase A (PKA) to upregulate tissue-protective factors. In contrast, the canonical activator interleukin-23 (IL-23) decreased negative regulators of PKA, including PRKAR1A. Lineage-specific Prkar1a deletion reduced ILC3s and increased susceptibility to enteric infection in mice. PRKAR1A was not required in early life but continuously preserved ILC3 homeostasis in adults by restraining PKA activity. Overproduction of IL-23 was sufficient to reduce PRKAR1A in ILC3s and increase PKA signaling that provoked gut inflammation. Finally, ILC3s from the healthy human intestine expressed PRKAR1A, which was downregulated by IL-23 or in inflammatory bowel disease. These results demonstrate that regulated PKA signaling is essential for tissue-protective ILC3s, while IL-23 drives aberrant PKA signaling to elicit intestinal inflammation.

articles.title: MRI-derived synthetic [¹⁸F]FET PET in neuro-oncology: evaluation in glioma grading and differentiation from solitary brain metastasis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: O-(2-[18F]fluoroethyl)-L-tyrosine positron emission tomography ([18F]FET PET) is clinically useful in neuro-oncology but limited by cost and availability. We assessed the clinical utility of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived synthetic [18F]FET PET.

METHODS: A total of 489 patients with histologically confirmed gliomas or brain metastases were retrospectively analyzed. A deep learning model generated synthetic PET images from multimodal MRI in the overall cohort and subgroups. Synthetic PET was evaluated against reference PET for image similarity by peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM), standardized uptake value ratio (SUVR) analysis by Pearson correlation and Bland-Altman analysis, and blinded reader assessment for glioma grading and high-grade glioma (HGG) versus solitary brain metastasis (SBM) differentiation using receiver operating characteristic analysis with area under the curve (AUC).

RESULTS: Synthetic PET showed high similarity to reference PET in the overall, glioma, and metastasis groups (PSNR, 34.7-35.5 dB; SSIM, 0.90-0.96), and SUVR correlations were strong (r = 0.77-0.93, all P < 0.001), with minimal bias and narrow limits of agreement. Compared with MRI alone, MRI with synthetic PET improved glioma grading and HGG-SBM differentiation, increasing AUC from 0.815 to 0.941 and from 0.816 to 0.901 for glioma grading and from 0.731 to 0.871 and from 0.784 to 0.872 for HGG-SBM differentiation across the 2 readers (all P < 0.05). No significant differences were found between MRI with synthetic and reference PET for either task (all P > 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: MRI-derived synthetic [18F]FET PET may enhance glioma grading and HGG-SBM differentiation, providing a PET-like alternative when FET PET is unavailable.

articles.title: Characterization of Major Health Consequences of People Experiencing Homelessness in Chile.
articles.journal: Journal of urban health : bulletin of the New York Academy of Medicine
articles.abstract: People experiencing homelessness face substantial health challenges. However, data on health and causes of death in Latin America are scarce. This study aimed to characterize the health profile of people experiencing homelessness in Chile, describe causes and place of death, estimate survival, and examine factors associated with all-cause mortality, including gender differences. We conducted a retrospective, registry-based study on people experiencing homelessness treated by the Salud Calle Foundation (Santiago, Chile) between 2010 and 2019. It included 751 individuals with a mean age of 48.1 ± 16.9 years, of whom 159 (21.1%) were women. The median duration of homelessness was 12 [IQR 3-75] months. Women were younger (44.1 ± 17.9 vs. 49.2 ± 16.5 years, p < 0.001), experienced homelessness for a shorter duration (12 [2-24] vs 14 [3-96] months; p = 0.010), and had higher rates of schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and infections compared to men. Men had higher rates of substance use, including alcohol, cannabis, cocaine, and cocaine derivatives. During a median follow-up of 64.2 months [IQR, 54.5-98.0], 21.8% of the cohort died, primarily from infections (31.2%), cirrhosis (10.1%), and trauma (8.8%). Over half (54.7%) died unhoused, either on the street or in shelters. Estimated survival rates were 95.7% at 1 year, 88.9% at 3 years, and 85% at 5 years. Multivariate analysis identified older age (HR 1.05) and male gender (HR 2.89) as independent predictors of mortality. Our findings highlight significant health disparities faced by people experiencing homelessness, with a high mortality rate primarily due to infections, cirrhosis, and trauma. They also demonstrate differences in health profiles between men and women, as well as important distinctions in Latin America compared to cohorts from other regions.

articles.title: International multidisciplinary Delphi consensus on advanced practice in non-metastatic upper tract urothelial carcinoma (IMPACT UTUC).
articles.abstract: Non-metastatic upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) is characterized by limited high-level evidence and substantial heterogeneity in clinical practice across diagnosis, staging and treatment, highlighting the need for expert-driven guidance to reduce variability and improve patient outcomes. To address this gap, we conducted the international multidisciplinary Delphi consensus on advanced practice in non-metastatic upper tract urothelial carcinoma (IMPACT UTUC). This two-round, web-based Delphi survey involved 73 international UTUC experts (urologists and medical oncologists) from Europe, the Americas and Asia. A total of 40 statements covering two domains (diagnosis and staging, and treatment) were rated on a 9-point Likert scale, with predefined thresholds for consensus agreement and disagreement. Overall, consensus was achieved for 32 of 40 statements (80%) across both rounds. IMPACT UTUC provides the first structured international Delphi consensus spanning the entire non-metastatic UTUC care pathway, offering pragmatic expert-informed recommendations that could guide current clinical practice and inform the design of future prospective studies.

articles.title: Screening for early-stage type 1 diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is now recognized as an autoimmune disease that evolves through distinct presymptomatic stages, often for years before the onset of hyperglycaemia and the need for insulin therapy. This presymptomatic period creates opportunities for early detection, with the presence of two or more islet autoantibodies (IAbs) defining early-stage, presymptomatic T1DM. Identification of T1DM during this presymptomatic window enables metabolic follow-up and education, thereby reducing the risk of diabetic ketoacidosis at diagnosis while facilitating psychological adaptation, timely access to disease-modifying therapies and participation in clinical trials. Current approaches for identifying early-stage T1DM range from IAb screening of individuals at high risk to screening of the general population, each with distinct advantages and implementation challenges. In this Review, we discuss the rationale for screening, compare screening strategies, examine current implementation initiatives and highlight key clinical, logistical, economic and ethical considerations for large-scale implementation in routine health care. We also consider unresolved challenges, including cost-effectiveness, equitable access to follow-up care and disease-modifying therapies, and harmonization of care pathways, as successful implementation of T1DM screening will ultimately depend not only on scientific advances but also on sustainable integration into health-care systems, marking a shift from reactive treatment towards preventive care.

articles.title: First factor XIa inhibitor nabs FDA approval for stroke prevention.
Increased prevalence of hypertension in paediatric turner syndrome: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract: Girls and women with Turner Syndrome (TS) are known to be at increased risk of aortic dissection, a condition for which hypertension is a modifiable risk factor. Our aim was to determine the frequency of hypertension in girls attending a tertiary paediatric TS clinic and its association with clinical characteristics. Retrospective analysis of clinical data was conducted for girls with TS attending the dedicated paediatric TS clinic at the Royal Hospital for Children Glasgow, between 1976-2023. Blood pressure (BP) was converted to centiles according to age and height. Hypertensive range BPs were defined as BPs ≥ 95th centile and pre-hypertensive range BPs were defined as BPs between the 90th-95th centiles, with measurements on 2 consecutive occasions. 184 girls with TS were included and BP data were available for a total of 172 (93%) with a median (range) age at the time of BP attainment of 12 (4, 18) years. Of these, 38 (22%) had congenital heart disease and 48 (28%) had an existing renal anomaly. The prevalence of hypertensive range BP at clinic within this cohort was 50% (n = 86), with median age of onset at 12 (4, 17) years of age. Pre-hypertensive range BPs were identified in 12 (7%). In total, 14/86 (15%) had ongoing high BP and were prescribed anti-hypertensive treatment. There is an increased prevalence of hypertension within the paediatric TS population compared to the general paediatric population. Early management of blood pressure in this group is likely to reduce cardiovascular disease burden.

articles.title: Oral bacterial lysate treatment for prevention of recurrent wheeze following severe bronchiolitis: protocol for an international multicentre randomised, placebo-controlled trial (BLIPA).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bronchiolitis is a common condition caused by a viral acute lower respiratory infection (ALRI) in infants. Severe bronchiolitis requiring hospitalisation is associated with increased risk of preschool wheeze and school-age asthma. Early exposure to microbial products modulating immune system development may help prevent later wheeze. Thus, this study evaluates whether an oral bacterial lysate after bronchiolitis hospitalisation reduces subsequent wheezing episodes.

METHODS: This international multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial tests bacterial lysate (OM85-BV; Broncho-Vaxom®) in infants after hospitalisation for bronchiolitis. Safety and efficacy will be assessed, and a subset will undergo exploratory mechanistic analyses. For 12-24 months post-discharge, parents/guardians will give one capsule of OM85-BV or placebo daily for 10 consecutive days each month.

RESULTS: The primary endpoint is the number of parent/guardian-reported wheeze episodes 12-months after starting OM85-BV or placebo. Secondary outcomes at 12 or 24-months follow-up include clinical outcomes, parent-proxy quality-of-life scores, incidence of atopy, recurrent wheeze needing asthma medication, wheeze-related hospitalisations, number of ALRI episodes, and mechanistic data on systemic immune pathways and nasopharyngeal and gut microbiota.

CONCLUSIONS: This international multicentre study will determine whether oral OM85-BV given for 10 consecutive days each month for 12-24 months reduces parent/guardian-reported recurrent wheeze episodes post-hospitalisation for bronchiolitis. TRIAL REGISTRATION (4): AZNCTR ACTRN12621001556831 (5/10/2021) and clinicaltrials.gov NCT05064631 (20/08/2020). Prospectively Registered. Approval to use the IMP in this clinical trial was provided by the Australian Government Therapeutic Goods Agency under the clinical trials notification scheme (TGA CTN: CT-2021-CTN-02639-1).

IMPACT: Our study addresses a large unmet clinical need and research gap related to reducing recurrent wheeze in infants post-hospitalisation for bronchiolitis. If our hypothesis is correct, this study may lead to an implementable intervention to improve health outcomes by reducing recurrent wheeze episodes in infants and young children. Reductions in recurrent wheeze might also reduce the incidence of childhood asthma and improve the lung health trajectories of children hospitalised with severe bronchiolitis.

articles.title: Development and validation of an early prediction model for intestinal failure-associated liver disease after enterostomy for necrotizing enterocolitis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Infants undergoing enterostomy for necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) are at high risk of intestinal failure-associated liver disease (IFALD). Early identification of high-risk infants remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and validate an early prediction model for IFALD using routinely available perioperative variables.

STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective study included 388 infants who underwent enterostomy for NEC between November 2019 and November 2024. Clinical, nutritional, and laboratory variables were collected. Boruta and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression were used for feature selection. Logistic regression, LASSO regression, random forest, naïve Bayes, and partial least squares (PLS) models were compared using discrimination, classification metrics, calibration, and decision curve analysis. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) were used to interpret the final model.

RESULTS: Among 388 infants, 103 (26.5%) developed IFALD. The training cohort comprised 273 infants (73 IFALD and 200 non-IFALD), and the validation cohort comprised 115 infants (30 IFALD and 85 non-IFALD). Infants with IFALD had lower gestational age, lower birth weight, shorter residual bowel length, delayed enteral nutrition recovery, and longer parenteral nutrition (PN) dependence. The random forest model showed the best validation performance, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.805 (95% confidence interval, 0.719-0.891), sensitivity of 0.700, specificity of 0.765, and accuracy of 0.748. SHAP analysis identified birth weight, residual bowel length, age at admission, preoperative systemic immune-inflammation index, postoperative platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, and central venous catheter infection as the most important predictors.

CONCLUSIONS: Infants with enterostomy after NEC surgery often need prolonged PN, which increases the risk of IFALD. This study built an early prediction model using routine perioperative data. The random forest model showed good discrimination and high sensitivity, and may help clinicians identify infants who need closer liver monitoring, careful PN management, and infection prevention.

IMPACT: 1. An early six-variable model predicts intestinal failure-associated liver disease after enterostomy for neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis. 2. The model uses birth weight, residual bowel length, age at admission, preoperative systemic immune-inflammation index, postoperative platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, and early central venous catheter infection. 3. Random forest performed best among five evaluated models, with a validation area under the curve of 0.805. 4. This study adds a direct comparison of conventional and machine-learning approaches using routinely available perioperative variables in a comparatively large cohort. 5. After external validation, the model could support early risk stratification, closer liver monitoring, individualized parenteral nutrition management, and catheter-infection prevention.

articles.title: Pharmacological chaperone treatment with Cystadane in aspartylglucosaminuria: an open-label, phase Ib/II trial.
articles.abstract: This phase Ib/II investigator-initiated, open label trial aims to show the safety and efficacy of Cystadane (betaine) in aspartylglucosaminuria, a lysosomal storage disorder characterized by progressive cognitive decline, in Finnish patients homozygous for the Finnish major mutation, aged between 3 and 17 years at study begin (recruited: 25, analyzed: 21). Oral Cystadane efficacy and safety were studied over 48 months. The primary endpoint of the study, reduction of glycoasparagines in the urine, was quantitatively determined using liquid chromatography/mass spectrometry and normalized to urine creatinine. Urine glycoasparagines are significantly reduced upon Cystadane treatment (by 68.6% ±10.8%; p = 0.000), and the study thus meets its primary endpoint. Our data show that Cystadane/betaine efficiently improves the main disease biomarker, and it is safe to use in aspartylglucosaminuria. Further studies should be carried out in a larger patient population over a longer time to demonstrate the effects on disease progression. EudraCT registration number 2017-000645-48.

articles.title: Posterior-lateral basal forebrain cholinergic nuclei hypoconnectivity in the inferior frontal cortex is associated with verbal fluency deficits in schizophrenia.
articles.abstract: Cognitive impairment is a core feature of schizophrenia and remains insufficiently addressed by current treatments. Increasing evidence implicates the cholinergic system, particularly the basal forebrain cholinergic nuclei (BFCN), in cognitive dysfunction. While structural alterations of the BFCN have been reported, alterations in their intrinsic functional connectivity (iFC) remain unclear. The present study examined the iFC of anterior and posterior BFCN subdivisions (aBFCN, pBFCN) in schizophrenia and tested associations with cognitive performance. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging data from the COBRE dataset were analyzed, including 73 healthy controls (HC) and 51 patients with schizophrenia (SCZ). Seed-based connectivity analyses were performed for aBFCN and pBFCN. Group differences were assessed voxel-wise, and group-dependent associations with phonemic verbal fluency (FAS) and processing speed (BACS-SC) were tested using hierarchical regression controlling for age, sex, IQ, and smoking status; verbal learning and memory (HVLT) was examined as a specificity analysis. Exploratory molecular mapping used normative PET-derived neurotransmitter maps, supplemented by spatial-autocorrelation-preserving null models. Distinct connectivity patterns of aBFCN and pBFCN were observed, consistent with previous reports in HC. Compared with HC, SCZ showed reduced pBFCN connectivity with a cluster in the right inferior frontal gyrus (pars opercularis; BA44; p = 0.018, FWE-corrected), whereas no significant differences were observed for aBFCN. The Group × pBFCN-IFG connectivity interaction was significant for FAS (p = 0.014) but not BACS-SC (p = 0.762) or HVLT (p = 0.514). In SCZ, higher pBFCN-IFG connectivity was associated with better FAS performance. Descriptive molecular mapping showed above-average representation of M1 and α4β2 receptor maps as well as several non-cholinergic targets; however, no molecular target showed significant spatial correspondence after spatial-autocorrelation-aware testing and FDR correction. These findings provide evidence for selective pBFCN hypoconnectivity with the right inferior frontal gyrus in schizophrenia. Its association with verbal fluency suggests that disrupted pBFCN connectivity with the inferior frontal cortex may contribute to altered executive control processes involved in verbal fluency in schizophrenia. Together, these findings extend previous evidence of BFCN abnormalities in schizophrenia by demonstrating a systems-level functional alteration of pBFCN-cortical connectivity and its relationship with cognitive performance.

articles.title: The ZmNAC41-ZmABC-ZmCP regulatory module mediates jasmonate-dependent resistance to southern corn rust in maize.
articles.abstract: Plant disease resistance is often governed by complex multigene modules, yet their composition and regulation remain poorly defined. Here, we identify a maize defense module comprising the NAC (NAM, ATAF1/2, and CUC2) transcription factor ZmNAC41, the PADRE domain-containing protein ZmABC, and the cysteine protease ZmCP. This module contributes to resistance to southern corn rust (SCR) caused by Puccinia polysora and is linked to jasmonic acid (JA)-associated defense responses. Upon pathogen infection, ZmNAC41 was rapidly induced and directly activated ZmABC transcription. ZmABC physically interacted with ZmCP. Increased JA accumulation and induction of JA biosynthetic and JA-responsive genes were also observed. Silencing any one of the three genes markedly attenuated JA-associated defense responses and compromised resistance, supporting a functional contribution of all three components to maize defense. Importantly, natural variation analysis identified elite haplotypes carrying favorable alleles of ZmNAC41, ZmABC, and ZmCP, and these allele combinations were significantly associated with enhanced field resistance. Together, our findings reveal a maize defense module that integrates transcriptional regulation and protein interaction and contributes to SCR resistance in association with JA-associated defense responses. These findings provide genetic targets for breeding maize with improved resistance to SCR.

articles.title: [Measuring therapeutic alliance in aphasia therapy: Translation and piloting of the "Aphasia and Stroke Therapeutic Alliance Measure" (A-STAM) questionnaire].
articles.journal: Zeitschrift fur Evidenz, Fortbildung und Qualitat im Gesundheitswesen
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The therapeutic alliance is crucial for the success of speech and language therapy. However, research in this area is still sparse. It is particularly important in aphasia therapy, as communication abilities are closely linked to the development and shaping of the therapeutic alliance. The "Aphasia and Stroke Therapeutic Alliance Measure" (A-STAM) is the first measurement instrument available for assessing this construct. The aim of this study was to translate the patient version into German and to examine its comprehensibility and preliminary reliability.

METHOD: The A-STAM was translated following a multi-step translation procedure informed by established guidelines (forward translations, consensus review, expert panel revision, back translation, and consultation with the original author). Comprehensibility was evaluated in two rounds using cognitive interviews. Adults with chronic aphasia and at most moderately impaired language comprehension were included. Data were analyzed using qualitative content analysis and behavior coding. Reliability (test-retest and split-half) was then examined.

RESULTS: Following comprehensibility testing with five persons with aphasia (PwA), five items were revised by replacing individual terms and reducing linguistic complexity (e.g., simplifying wording). The revised items were deemed to be comprehensible in a second round with five additional PwA. A preliminary evaluation with 22 PwA demonstrated very high split-half reliability (rSB = 0.96) and test-retest reliability (ICC = 0.92).

DISCUSSION: The version translated into German represents the first comprehensible instrument for PwA. The results indicate good comprehensibility and high reliability. However, they should be interpreted with caution due to the limited sample size (n = 22), as methodological guidelines recommend at least 30 heterogeneous participants. Further evaluation with a larger sample (n = 100) is planned.

articles.title: Withholding or continuing glucose-lowering drugs for elective surgery in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: withholding or continuing perioperative metformin. Responses to Br J Anaesth 2026; 137: 1280-1 and Br J Anaesth 2026; 137: 1282-3.
Thrombolysis and thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke: A RAND/UCLA consensus.
authors: Grupo de Trabajo sobre Ictus en la Infancia y la Adolescencia
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The treatment of acute ischemic stroke in the pediatric population involves considerable uncertainty due to the limited evidence on intravenous thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy. The objective was to assess the contribution of different scenario variables to the appropriateness of thrombolysis and thrombectomy in children and adolescents, as an aid to clinical decision-making.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: The RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method was applied. A multidisciplinary panel assessed theoretical clinical scenarios, differentiating two age groups: ≥30 days to 2 years, and >2 to <18 years. The scenarios were rated in two rounds, one of which was face-to-face. Multinomial logistic regression was performed to estimate the contribution of the variables, and CART analysis was used to synthesize the appropriateness criteria in the form of decision trees.

RESULTS: A total of 128 clinical scenarios were assessed per age group. In the multivariable analysis, all the variables contributed significantly. Lesion location contributed most to the fit of the model in patients aged≥30 days to 2 years, as opposed to symptom onset in patients aged>2 to <18 years. The models showed a good overall fit, with Nagelkerke pseudo-R2 values of 0.833 and 0.784, respectively, which allowed summarizing the criteria in the form of decision trees.

CONCLUSIONS: Appropriateness criteria were established to support decision-making regarding thrombolysis and thrombectomy in pediatric ischemic stroke. Lesion location and symptom onset were the variables that contributed most to model fit, depending on the age group. These criteria may support decision-making in contexts of clinical uncertainty, although they cannot replace clinical judgment.

articles.title: Editor Note to "Integrating PET/CT, radiomics and clinical data: An advanced multi-modal approach for lymph node metastasis prediction in prostate cancer" [Comput. Biol. Med. 184, (2025), 109339].
New sites of vulnerability to stop vivax malaria.
articles.abstract: Malaria vaccines based on the PfCSP molecule are now being deployed to prevent infection by the deadly parasite, Plasmodium falciparum. Can we apply the same tricks to stop the second major malaria parasite, Plasmodium vivax? Visweswaren and colleagues studied PvCSP, revealing new sites of vulnerability to target with vaccines.

articles.title: How safe is occupational exposure to cytostatic drugs? Results from environmental and biological monitoring.
articles.journal: Farmacia hospitalaria : organo oficial de expresion cientifica de la Sociedad Espanola de Farmacia Hospitalaria
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Occupational exposure to cytostatic drugs has been associated with acute and chronic toxicity. Despite the publication of guidelines and measures for safety handling, contamination is still reported in most recent studies. The aim of the present work was to assess contamination of cytostatic drugs in a hospital from the North of Spain.

METHODS: Working surfaces from the Pharmacy and the Onco-Hematology services were tested for gemcitabine, dacarbazine, methotrexate, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicinol, doxorubicin, epirubicin, irinotecan, vinorelbine, etoposide, docetaxel and paclitaxel. Urine samples from workers were also analyzed.

RESULTS: Within the Pharmacy service, contamination was detected in 57.6% of the collected samples, with cyclophosphamide and gemcitabine being the most detected compounds. At the Onco-Hematology service, contamination was present in 32.3% of the samples collected from infusion pumps, armchairs and surrounding floors, and in all samples collected from the toilets (all positive for gemcitabine, irinotecan and paclitaxel). Low concentrations (<100 pg/cm2) were detected in ≥76% of the contaminated samples in all the locations, except for the outpatients' area bathrooms, where this value was <40%. In addition, 60.7% of vials, blisters and infusion bags sampled were contaminated. Only 2 of the 82 bracelets worn by workers showed contamination with cyclophosphamide. Finally, all the urine samples were negative.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite the low levels of contamination, it is advisable to carry out monitoring campaigns to maintain workers' awareness and to take corrective actions to minimize occupational exposure.

articles.title: Consensus document on the diagnosis and treatment of metabolic alterations in urinary stone disease.
articles.abstract: Urolithiasis is one of the most prevalent nephro-urological diseases worldwide and entails a significant economic cost for healthcare systems. Metabolic evaluation has become established as an essential tool in the management of patients with a high risk of recurrence, as it enables identification of treatable alterations. This document presents the recommendations of a multidisciplinary group of experts in urology and nephrology for the diagnostic and therapeutic management of metabolic alterations associated with stone disease. A consensus was reached through literature review, with the objective of standardising clinical and metabolic evaluation and optimising the medical treatment of the identified metabolic alterations. The diagnosis should include a complete initial evaluation, including serum and 24 h urine analysis, with specific parameters based on stone composition. The therapeutic recommendations include general measures, such as adequate hydration, restricting sodium and animal protein intake, and targeted pharmacological treatment based on the metabolic alterations identified. Individualisation of therapeutic strategies can reduce the incidence of recurrence, improve quality of life for patients and decrease the need for retreatment. The implementation of these recommendations will enable progress towards precision medicine in stone disease, based on aetiological diagnosis and personalised management.

articles.title: Not all plaque burden is Equal: CACS- versus SIS-derived risk stratification within CAD-RADS categories in mild-to-moderate coronary disease.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess the prognostic value of plaque burden based on CACS and SIS categories over CAD-RADS.

METHODS: In this retrospective, single-center study, 2850 adults who underwent elective CCTA between 2016 and 2020 were screened. A total of 1818 patients were enrolled based on very low-to-intermediate pre-test risk, good image quality (Likert score ≥4), and ≥3 years of follow-up. Clinical data were collected, and CAD-RADS 2.0 with CACS-based plaque burden (CACS-P score) and SIS-based plaque burden (SIS-P score) was quantified. Prediction of 5-point MACE composite outcome (late unplanned coronary revascularization, non-fatal myocardial infarction, hospitalization for heart failure, hospitalization for angina, all-cause mortality) and 2-point MACE composite outcome (non-fatal myocardial infarction and all-cause mortality) was evaluated using survival analysis and multivariable models.

RESULTS: During a median available follow-up of 62 months, 178/1818 patients (9.8%) experienced a 5-point MACE and 96/1818 (5.3%) experienced myocardial infarction/death within the fixed 36-month analysis horizon. Both CAD-RADS severity and plaque burden scores were associated with adverse outcomes. Integration of the CACS-based P-score identified revealed heterogeneity in risk estimates within CAD-RADS categories. For the primary endpoint, CAD-RADS 3/P0 showed HR point estimates of similar magnitude to those observed in CAD-RADS 4-5/P0 and CAD-RADS 4-5/P3-P4 (HR 15.95 [95% CI:3.95-64.36], HR 16.21 [3.23-81.31], and HR 14.13 [5.70-35.01], respectively). For myocardial infarction/death, CAD-RADS 2-3/P0 showed HR point estimates of similar magnitude to those observed in CAD-RADS 4-5/P1-P2. Conversely, SIS-P provided limited additional within category risk stratification.

CONCLUSIONS: CACS-based P score may refine risk stratification in patients with mild-to-moderate stenosis.

articles.title: 2026 iCARDIO Alliance Global Implementation Guidelines on Heart Failure.
articles.abstract: This is the updated 2026 version of the iCARDIO Alliance Global Implementation Guidelines on Heart Failure - originally published in 2025. In these guidelines, we aim to consider inconsistencies in healthcare access, varying infrastructure, resource constraints and diverse local practices as well as practical and political issues that restrict the global applicability of currently available guidelines. There is a need for universal recommendations that address the unique challenges faced by patients and healthcare providers worldwide. Our iCARDIO Alliance Global Implementation Guidelines emphasize the incorporation of novel therapies, while integrating standard of care with the most up-to-date evidence to enable clinicians to optimize patient care. This document is about heart failure (HF), including acute and chronic heart failure, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction as well as HF with improved ejection fraction and cardiomyopathies. Context-specific recommendations tailored to individual patient needs are highlighted providing a thorough evaluation of the risks, benefits, and overall value of each therapy, aiming to establish a standard of care that improves patient outcomes and reduces the burden of hospitalization in this susceptible population. These guidelines provide evidence-based recommendations that represent a group consensus considering the many other published guidelines that have reviewed many of the issues discussed here, but they also make new recommendations where new evidence has recently emerged. Most importantly these guidelines also provide recommendations on a number of issues where re-source limitations may put constraints on the care provided to HF patients. Such "economic adjustment" recommendations aim to provide guidance for situations when "Resources are somewhat limited" or when "Resources are severely limited". Hence, this document presents not only a comprehensive but also concise set of recommendations to guide all aspects of HF management with a unified strategy for the pharmacological, non-pharmacological, invasive and interventional management of this significant global health challenge that is applicable to the needs of healthcare around the globe.

articles.title: Outcomes of Transvenous Lead Extraction for Infectious Versus Non-Infectious Indications.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transvenous lead extraction (TLE) is performed for both infectious and non-infectious cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) indications. Infectious indications are associated with greater systemic illness, whereas non-infectious leads are generally older and more fibrotic. Whether these competing factors differentially influence TLE outcomes remains unclear.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and CENTRAL through October 10, 2026 for studies directly comparing TLE outcomes between infectious and non-infectious indications. Trial registries, conference abstracts, and preprint servers were screened. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included procedural success and complications. Random-effects models were used.

RESULTS: Fifteen observational studies comprising 53,086 patients were included. Infectious indications were associated with higher all-cause mortality (OR 5.61, 95% CI 3.78-8.33; I2 = 82.3%). The association was greater for short-term than long-term mortality (OR 8.57 vs. 2.67; p for interaction < 0.001). Intermediate-term mortality was also higher (OR 3.84, 95% CI 2.50-5.91). Pericardial complications were less frequent with infectious indications (OR 0.71, 95% CI 0.53-0.95). Clinical and complete procedural success and other complications did not differ significantly.

CONCLUSION: Infectious indications were associated with higher mortality, particularly in the short term, whereas procedural success was comparable. Variation in follow-up and infection phenotype likely contributed to heterogeneity.

articles.title: Leadless Versus Transvenous Pacing: Propensity-Matched 12-Month Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leadless pacemakers avoid the subcutaneous pocket and transvenous lead required for conventional pacing, but comparative real-world evidence in patients at high cardiorenal risk remains limited.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of de novo permanent pacemaker recipients between January 2021 and December 2024. The source cohort comprised 150 leadless and 410 transvenous pacemaker recipients. After 1:2 propensity score matching, 150 and 300 patients, respectively, were analyzed. The primary endpoint was the first occurrence of a prespecified 12-month device-related complication composite. A prespecified analysis evaluated patients aged 65 years or older with type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease.

RESULTS: The primary endpoint occurred in 6.7% of leadless and 14.0% of transvenous recipients (risk ratio, 0.48; 95% confidence interval, 0.25-0.92; p = 0.028), an absolute difference of 7.3 percentage points (95% confidence interval, 1.1-12.6). The time-to-event association was similar (hazard ratio, 0.45; 95% confidence interval, 0.23-0.90; p = 0.024) and remained consistent after parsimonious adjustment and competing-risk analysis. The difference was mainly driven by pocket-, lead-, and thoracic access-related events. After pocket- and lead-specific events were excluded, serious complication rates were 5.3% in both groups. Findings in the older diabetes plus chronic kidney disease subgroup were directionally consistent but imprecise.

CONCLUSIONS: The observed advantage of leadless pacing was primarily structural, reflecting avoidance of complications inherent to the transvenous pocket-and-lead system. Non-pocket/non-lead serious complications were similar between groups.

articles.title: Posterior cerebral artery dissection: clinical and angiographic spectrum, management, and outcomes in a retrospective 14-patient case series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Posterior cerebral artery (PCA) dissection is a rare cerebrovascular disorder with heterogeneous clinical and angiographic presentations. Because evidence is largely limited to small case series and individual reports, optimal diagnostic and therapeutic strategies remain uncertain.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 14 patients with angiographically confirmed PCA dissection or dissecting PCA aneurysms identified at a single center between January 2016 and December 2025. Clinical presentation, angiographic characteristics, treatment strategy, procedural complications, and available clinical and vascular imaging follow-up were analyzed.

RESULTS: The median age was 43.5 years (IQR, 33.8-56.3; range, 20-63 years). Hemorrhagic presentation occurred in 8 patients (57.1%), including 6 with subarachnoid hemorrhage (42.9%). Two patients were managed conservatively, 3 underwent conventional stenting alone, 5 underwent flow-diverter treatment, 2 underwent coil embolization without an implanted stent, and 2 underwent conventional stenting combined with coil embolization. Most patients achieved favorable clinical and angiographic outcomes. One patient remained severely disabled (mRS 5), and one patient developed fatal post-procedural subarachnoid hemorrhage after flow-diverter treatment.

CONCLUSIONS: PCA dissection is a rare and clinically heterogeneous condition that may present with hemorrhagic or nonhemorrhagic manifestations. Management should be individualized according to rupture status, lesion morphology, vascular anatomy, collateral circulation, and the feasibility of parent-vessel preservation. Conservative management and different endovascular strategies may be appropriate in selected patients, but the small retrospective nature of available series precludes conclusions regarding superiority of any single treatment approach.

articles.title: One-Year Outcomes of Pulmonary Vein Isolation With a Novel Cryoballoon in Asian Population.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cryoballoon ablations for pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) to treat atrial fibrillation (AF) are well established. The POLAR SMART study was designed to collect prospective real-world data on acute and 12-month safety and effectiveness of the POLARx cryoballoon for de novo PVI.

METHODS: POLAR SMART is a prospective, non-randomized, multicenter study (NCT05282823) with patients enrolled across 19 centers (Japan and South Korea) and followed up to 12 months.

RESULTS: AF ablation was performed in 293 patients, 181 receiving only PVI. In the PVI-only cohort, acute PVI was achieved in 95.0% of patients, and 98.2% of pulmonary veins (PV) with the cryoballoon. Procedure time and fluoroscopy time were 75 ± 25 min and 18.5 ± 11.1 min, respectively. Time to isolation was 42 ± 32 s, with nadir temperature of -56.6 ± 6.9°C. The study met the primary safety endpoint with an event-free rate of 97.3%. The study effectiveness event-free rate at 12 months was 75.6% for entire cohort and 81.1% for PVI-only cohort (POLARx, n = 116; 79.3% and POLARx FIT, n = 65; 84.4%). AF recurrence in PVI-only cohort was 7.2% for POLARx and 6.2% for POLARx FIT. Ablation procedure increased heart rate (HR) significantly for entire cohort (p < 0.001). The optimal HR value at predischarge for 12-month outcome was calculated with 70 bpm (Predicted Probability 0.83). The effect of increased HR remained stable after 12 months for patients ablated with POLARx FIT.

CONCLUSIONS: The POLARx and POLARx FIT cryoballoon systems are safe and effective for PVI in real-world use. POLARx FIT ablation was associated with a sustained HR increase over 12 months.

articles.title: Focused Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Biophysical Mechanisms, Neural Effects, and Clinical Translation.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
articles.abstract: Low-intensity transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS) has emerged as a promising noninvasive neuromodulation technology capable of targeting both cortical and deep brain structures with millimeter-scale spatial precision. Recent advances in ultrasound hardware, acoustic modeling, neuronavigation, and multimodal imaging have accelerated the field from proof-of-concept demonstrations toward mechanistic investigation and early clinical translation. In parallel, growing evidence from animal and human studies has begun to clarify how ultrasound influences neural activity across cellular, circuit, and systems levels. In this review, we synthesize recent progress in understanding the biophysical mechanisms, neurophysiological effects, and network-level consequences of TUS. We discuss insights from optical imaging, electrophysiology, EEG source imaging, and functional MRI, highlighting how these complementary approaches reveal cell-type-specific responses, bidirectional modulation of neural circuits, and distributed changes in functional connectivity beyond the sonicated target. We further examine evidence that functional imaging is evolving from a simple measure of regional activation to a multidimensional biomarker of target engagement, circuit modulation, and treatment response. Despite these advances, important challenges remain. We conclude that TUS is approaching a translational inflection point in which rigorous mechanistic studies, standardized methodologies, and imaging-based biomarkers can establish ultrasound as both a powerful causal neuroscience tool and a clinically viable neuromodulation therapy for disorders involving dysfunctional brain circuits.

articles.title: Learning to Navigate a Changing World: From Brain Systems to Novel Algorithms.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
articles.abstract: Natural organisms navigate a world in constant flux and are frequently confronted with sensory ambiguity and shifting goals. While biological systems can adapt rapidly to navigate in novel and nonstationary environments, this challenge remains a significant hurdle for artificial intelligence. In this review, we examine recent progress in understanding neurobiological systems that allow for adaptive, efficient spatial and abstract navigation in dynamic environments and how these observations have informed new developments for the same behavior in machines. We highlight how predictive learning serves as a unifying framework to describe the organization of neural activity across distributed systems for navigation, including the hippocampal formation, parietal cortex, and higher-order associative structures. Specifically, we explore how such neurobiological systems encode expected future states, dynamic target trajectories, action plans, and internal behavioral strategies. Finally, we contrast the diffuse, inefficient exploration of canonical artificial agents with the structured, efficient control policies for goal-directed navigation observed in natural organisms. By grounding learning in the interplay between action, prediction, and natural behavioral statistics, navigation provides a roadmap for building resilient, neurobiologically inspired continual learning in artificial agents.

articles.title: Maternal Immune Activation and Neurodevelopmental Disorders: A Cross-Species Perspective.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
articles.abstract: Prenatal exposure to infection increases the likelihood of neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). This association is attributed largely to the maternal inflammatory response, maternal immune activation (MIA), rather than to single pathogen. In this review, we discuss the molecular, cellular, and behavioral consequences of MIA and their contribution to NDDs in clinical cohorts and preclinical models across different species. We first trace the pathophysiology linking maternal infection to altered fetal neurodevelopment, describing how diverse immune challenges converge on shared nodes including cytokine signaling, oxidative and nutritional stress, placental dysfunction, and epigenetic modification. We then describe how these perturbations affect neural circuits and behavior, focusing on the disrupted social development. Next, we consider sources of individual variation, including gestational timing, fetal sex, and later-life "second hits," that may contribute to the greater vulnerability. Finally, we discuss the translational implications of this work in terms of maternal cytokine and epigenetic signatures as candidate biomarkers for risk stratification and potential therapeutic approaches.

articles.title: The Neural Correlates of Sickness.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
articles.abstract: The brain protects animals during infection by detecting immune activity, coordinating behavioral and physiological defenses, anticipating potential infectious threats, and limiting excessive inflammation. Collectively termed sickness, these centrally organized responses include changes in body temperature, activity, energy balance, appetite, fluid intake, social behavior, neuroendocrine function, and autonomic output. Rather than constituting a single uniform state, sickness is generated by distributed and partially dissociable neural pathways that translate immune signals into responses appropriate to the nature and stage of an infection. Work presented at a symposium at the 2026 Society for Neuroscience meeting highlights how humoral and cranial sensory pathways detect ongoing immune responses; how social cues, expectations, and prior experience prepare the organism for anticipated threats; and how endocrine and autonomic circuits constrain inflammation and promote recovery. Together, these findings establish the brain as an active regulator of immunity across the full course of illness.

articles.title: MRI ventilation phenotypes of severe asthma.
Squeezing more out of less: blood-flow restriction training in COPD and other conditions, from the clinic to the home.
Bridging basic and clinical research to understand the biological effects of hyperoxia in humans: are we closing the gap?
Thalamic Reticular Nucleus Excitability and Cholinergic Signaling are Disrupted in a Mouse Model of Alzheimer's Disease Neuropathology.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
articles.abstract: The thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN) forms powerful GABAergic connections with thalamic nuclei that regulate sleep, attention, and sensory processing. TRN neurons receive dense cholinergic innervation from the basal forebrain and brainstem, dynamically shaping TRN function across brain states. We previously showed reduced TRN activity and sleep deficits in amyloid precursor protein transgenic mice (APP mice), implicating TRN dysfunction as an early contributor to Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathophysiology. Here, using slice electrophysiology in mice of both sexes, we determined whether changes in intrinsic membrane properties or cholinergic synaptic transmission contribute to TRN hypoactivity in APP mice. We found that TRN neurons located in the inner core and outer shell regions undergo substantial increases in excitability after the first postnatal month. In mature animals, core neurons exhibited higher firing rates and diverse firing patterns, including persistent firing, whereas shell neurons fired at lower rates and displayed more homogeneous firing patterns without persistent activity. Firing diversity in core neurons was mediated in part by low-threshold T-type Ca²⁺ channels. Cholinergic synaptic activation, mediated predominantly by basal forebrain afferents, produced biphasic excitatory-inhibitory postsynaptic responses in both core and shell neurons, with the ratio of postsynaptic excitation and inhibition varying across postsynaptic targets. Overall, cholinergic activation suppressed TRN firing. In APP mice, core neurons showed reduced intrinsic excitability and cholinergic afferents evoked postsynaptic responses with a larger muscarinic receptor-mediated inhibitory component, leading to delayed TRN firing. Together, these findings identify both intrinsic and cholinergic synaptic mechanisms that may contribute to TRN dysfunction during early AD.Significance Statement Alzheimer's disease (AD) is typically diagnosed after cognitive symptoms emerge when treatments are less effective, highlighting the need to understand preclinical disease mechanisms. Cholinergic signaling and slow-wave sleep are disrupted before symptom onset, but the mechanisms underlying these changes remain poorly understood. Because the thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN) receives strong cholinergic input and mediates sleep-related rhythms, it is well positioned to contribute to early AD pathophysiology. We previously found reduced TRN activity and disrupted sleep in an AD mouse model. Here, we show that intrinsic excitability and cholinergic synaptic signaling are altered in TRN neurons during preclinical AD. These changes may contribute to thalamic dysfunction and sleep disturbances, providing a potential circuit mechanism linking early AD pathology to disease progression.

articles.title: The Numb paradox: one protein, multiple isoforms, opposing functions in neurodevelopment, endocytic trafficking, and cancer.
articles.abstract: Numb is a multifunctional adaptor protein that serves as a central regulator of cell fate, linking polarity, signaling, and endocytic trafficking from early development to disease. Initially discovered in Drosophila melanogaster as an intrinsic determinant of asymmetric cell division, Numb's antagonism of Notch signaling has proven to be evolutionarily conserved in mammals, orchestrating the balance between progenitor maintenance and differentiation during neurogenesis. In the mammalian brain, Numb and its paralog, Numb-like (Numbl), integrate polarity cues, receptor trafficking, and transcriptional networks to guide cortical development and maintain neural stem cell homeostasis. Alternative splicing generates multiple Numb isoforms (i.e., p72, p71, p66, and p65) that exhibit distinct structural and functional properties, allowing context-dependent modulation of Notch, p53, and integrin pathways. Isoform-specific expression patterns underlie divergent roles in neurodevelopment, neurite morphogenesis, and tumorigenesis, whereby Numb can act either as a tumor suppressor or as an oncogenic driver. Dysregulated splicing, posttranslational modification, and interaction with RNA-binding proteins such as RBM4, PTBP1, or SRSF9 reprogram Numb's activity across developmental and cancer contexts. Emerging evidence also connects Numb isoform regulation to neurodegenerative processes, including tauopathies and viral neuropathogenesis, as observed in Zika virus infection. Collectively, these findings position Numb as a molecular switch at the crossroads of neurodevelopment, cancer, and degeneration with its isoform diversity providing both mechanistic insight and therapeutic potential for restoring differentiation, restraining oncogenesis, and protecting neuronal integrity.

Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis presenting with acute respiratory failure and reversible lactic acidosis.
articles.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated myocarditis is an uncommon but potentially fatal immune-related adverse event characterised by high morbidity and mortality despite a relatively low incidence. Diagnosis is often challenging because clinical manifestations overlap with more common cardiovascular conditions, including acute coronary syndrome (ACS), heart failure and other forms of treatment-related cardiotoxicity. Early recognition and prompt immunosuppressive therapy are critical to improving outcomes. A man in his 80s with metastatic human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-positive distal oesophageal adenocarcinoma receiving pembrolizumab, trastuzumab and leucovorin, fluorouracil and oxaliplatin (FOLFOX) chemotherapy presented with acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure and marked myocardial injury. Initial evaluation revealed diffuse pulmonary oedema, high-sensitivity troponin elevation (11 374 ng/L, peaking at 34 066 ng/L), elevated lactate (4.4 mmol/L, peaking at 6.0 mmol/L) and mildly reduced left ventricular systolic function. ACS was initially suspected; however, serial electrocardiograms demonstrated no dynamic ischaemic changes, and transthoracic echocardiography showed only mildly reduced ejection fraction. Cardiac MRI revealed focal subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement and myocardial oedema consistent with acute myocarditis. Given the recent pembrolizumab exposure and exclusion of alternative aetiologies, a diagnosis of ICI-associated myocarditis was established. High-dose methylprednisolone (1000 mg daily for 3 days) was initiated approximately 23 hours after presentation, resulting in rapid clinical improvement, resolution of respiratory failure and marked decline in cardiac biomarkers. Notably, serial lactate levels rose following peak troponin elevation and normalised after corticosteroid therapy, closely paralleling clinical recovery. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of ICI-associated myocarditis and underscores the importance of multimodality cardiac evaluation and early corticosteroid therapy. In addition, the temporal association between myocardial injury and reversible lactic acidosis raises the possibility that lactate kinetics may serve as a complementary marker of disease activity in severe ICI-associated myocarditis, a finding that warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Six-year chronic pneumoperitoneum managed conservatively: clinical, ethical and diagnostic considerations.
Diabetic myonecrosis: an under-recognised complication of uncontrolled diabetes.
articles.abstract: Diabetic myonecrosis (DMN) is a rare but serious complication of long-standing, uncontrolled diabetes mellitus. We report a woman in her 60s who presented to the emergency department with a 3-week history of atraumatic subacute right thigh swelling, severe pain and muscle weakness leading to a fall. She had a background of type 2 diabetes mellitus, iron deficiency anaemia and sickle cell trait. Fracture and deep venous thrombosis were excluded. Laboratory investigations showed an elevated C-reactive protein without features of infection and mild elevation of creatine kinase, which is atypical for inflammatory myositis. MRI revealed extensive muscle infarction and oedema in the right thigh consistent with DMN. Optimisation of analgesia was central to functional recovery, while glycaemic control remained an essential component of management given its established association with this complication. Physiotherapy further supported recovery of muscle strength. DMN should be considered in atraumatic limb swelling in patients with long-standing uncontrolled diabetes to facilitate conservative management and avoid unnecessary tests and treatments.

Grading of intrarenal tertiary lymphoid structure-like aggregates and association with early treatment response in proliferative lupus nephritis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Intrarenal tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS)-like lymphoid aggregates have been observed in lupus nephritis (LN), but their clinicopathological relevance and prognostic significance remain incompletely understood. We developed an exploratory histological grading framework for TLS-like lymphoid aggregates and examined its association with early treatment response in proliferative LN.

METHODS: In a single-centre retrospective cohort study of 73 patients with biopsy-proven proliferative LN (International Society of Nephrology/Renal Pathology Society Classes III, IV, III+V and IV+V), TLS-like lymphoid aggregates were graded 0–4 and categorised into three groups (No/Low, Intermediate, High). The primary endpoint was failure to achieve complete remission (CR) at 6 months according to 2021 Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes criteria. The association between TLS-like grade and treatment failure was assessed using multivariable Firth logistic regression.

RESULTS: Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics were comparable across three TLS-like groups. In contrast, higher TLS-like grade was associated with chronic histological damage and interstitial inflammatory infiltration. 6-month CR rates declined from 30.0% for Low-grade and 25.0% for Intermediate-grade to 0% for High TLS-like groups (p=0.033). High TLS-like grade was independently associated with failure to achieve CR (OR 13.519; 95% CI 1.381 to 1822.330; p=0.021) after adjustment for age, sex, estimated glomerular filtration rate, log-transformed proteinuria, pretreatment status and Chronicity Index. Adding TLS-like grade improved discrimination (area under the curve 0.704 vs 0.830). Sensitivity analyses were directionally consistent.

CONCLUSION: High-grade TLS-like aggregates were associated with poorer early treatment response in proliferative LN. TLS-like aggregates may provide complementary information for risk stratification beyond conventional clinical variables in proliferative LN. However, further validation is required before routine implementation.

articles.title: Mosquito vector abundance, spatial distribution and arboviral transmission risk in high-traffic cross-border zones of Tanzania.
articles.abstract: Arboviral diseases remain a major global public health challenge because mosquito vectors continue to expand their geographical range through increasing international travel, urbanization and climate change. This study aimed to assess the abundance, spatial distribution and larval indices of mosquito vectors of medical importance in a cross-border setting. A comprehensive entomological survey, using multiple collection techniques, was conducted between October and November 2024 at high-traffic cross-border zones at Mutukula ground crossing connecting Tanzania and Uganda and Namanga ground crossing connecting Tanzania and Kenya. Adult mosquitoes were collected using BG-Pro traps, CDC light traps and Prokopack aspirators, while larval surveys were conducted through cross-sectional household inspections of potential breeding habitats. Data were summarized using descriptive statistics, and associations between variables were assessed using the Chi-square test or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate. Binomial and Poisson regression models were used to identify factors associated with mosquito abundance and breeding site occurrence, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. A total of 6952 mosquitoes were collected, comprising Culex quinquefasciatus (84.7%, n = 5895), Aedes aegypti (10.0%, n = 689) and Anopheles gambiae s.l. (5.3%, n = 369). Significantly higher abundance of Aedes spp. and Anopheles funestus s.l was recorded in hamlets located within 400 m of the international border (p < 0.0001), whereas Culex quinquefasciatus predominated in hamlets situated beyond 400 m from the border (χ2 = 1938, p < 0.000001). One female Aedes albopictus was detected among the adult Aedes collections, suggesting the potential introduction of this invasive vector. Four of the 10 hamlets surveyed had larval indices exceeding recommended thresholds, indicating an elevated risk of arboviral transmission. This study revealed a high prevalence of Aedes aegypti within the cross-border buffer zone and a broader distribution of Culex species beyond this zone. These findings underscore the urgent need for sustained vector control interventions and strengthened entomological surveillance and control beyond the International Health Regulations (2005) as amended in 2024, which recommended a 400 m buffer zone at points of entry to mitigate the risk of arboviral disease transmission and potential epidemics.

Cohort profile: study design and baseline characteristics of SARS-CoV-2 positive and negative children and youth from the Canadian paediatric outcome improvement through coordination of research networks (POPCORN) COVID-19 prospective cohort study.

Effectiveness and safety of intravenous terlipressin as an add-on treatment for persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn: a study protocol of a multicentre pragmatic randomised controlled trial in China.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN) is a life-threatening condition with severe hypoxaemia and respiratory failure. Approximately 40% of newborns diagnosed with PPHN are hyporeactive to the standard treatment with inhaled nitric oxide (iNO). Effective and safe therapies for PPHN are urgently required. Several case reports have found intravenous injection of terlipressin for PPHN to be a promising therapy to improve the outcomes. Nevertheless, robust evidence from well-designed randomised controlled trials is lacking, and the effectiveness and safety of terlipressin remain uncertain.

METHODS: This open-label, pragmatic randomised controlled trial will be conducted in 15–20 neonatal intensive care units in China. Newborns aged ≤14 days with gestational age ≥34 weeks, birth weight ≥2000 g, oxygenation index (OI) ≥16 and confirmed PPHN are eligible. A total of 218 eligible infants will be enrolled. Infants are randomised 1:1 iNO plus intravenous terlipressin or iNO alone (109 infants per group). The primary outcome is death or use of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Follow-up ends at 28 days after treatment initiation, hospital discharge or death. Secondary outcomes include oxygenation indices, echocardiographic pulmonary pressure, need for additional pulmonary vasodilators, duration of iNO therapy and safety events. Analyses will follow the intention-to-treat principle.

ETHICS AND TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial received approval from the Ethics Committee of West China Second University Hospital. We registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2600122623). The study findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and presentations at academic conferences.

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ChiCTR2600122623.

articles.title: Machine learning-based prediction of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease in Chinese perimenopausal women: a retrospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare the predictive performance of different machine learning (ML) models for non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) in perimenopausal women and to interpret the optimal model using Shapley additive explanations (SHAP).

DESIGN: Retrospective observational study.

SETTING: A health management centre of China.

PARTICIPANTS: A total of 5637 perimenopausal women aged 45–55 years who underwent health examinations were included between February 2022 and August 2023.

METHODS: Physical examination data were collected from perimenopausal women at the Health Management Center of the First Affiliated Hospital of the University of Science and Technology of China. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression was employed for feature selection. Eight ML models were developed with hyperparameter tuning.
