The optimal model was selected based on the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), which was calculated on the training set and was subsequently interpreted.

RESULTS: Among 5637 participants, 1324 (23.5%) were diagnosed with NAFLD. The Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model exhibited the best predictive performance, with an AUC of 0.907 and an accuracy of 0.822 in the validation set. SHAP analysis identified that body mass index, triglycerides, high-density lipoprotein, random blood glucose, alanine aminotransferase, hyperuricaemia, platelet count and albumin were the most influential predictors of NAFLD in this population.

CONCLUSION: The XGBoost model demonstrated superior NAFLD prediction performance compared with other ML methods in the perimenopausal women and might improve health management for this population.

articles.title: Association between psoriatic disease and dyslipidaemia: a chart-based observational study in the United Arab Emirates.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine the association between psoriatic disease and dyslipidaemia in a tertiary hospital setting in the United Arab Emirates.

DESIGN: Chart-based observational study.

SETTING: A tertiary hospital in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.

PARTICIPANTS: Patients aged ≥16 years who underwent lipid testing at a tertiary care centre in Abu Dhabi between 2019 and 2023 were included, regardless of their dyslipidaemia and psoriatic disease status.

PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES: Dyslipidaemia was classified as present or absent using predefined thresholds for triglycerides, total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, non-high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol and sex-specific HDL cholesterol. Among patients with psoriatic disease with dyslipidaemia, the first documented dyslipidaemia identification had to have occurred concurrently or after the recorded onset of psoriatic disease. Those with inherited lipid disorders or taking lipid-altering medications were excluded.

RESULTS: The median age of the 465 eligible patients was 39 years (IQR 29–52 years) and 56% were women. Overall, 47.7% had dyslipidaemia and 25.3% had psoriatic disease. Dyslipidaemia was more common in patients with psoriatic disease than in those without (56.0% vs 44.9%; p=0.038). Unadjusted analysis revealed that psoriatic disease was associated with higher odds of dyslipidaemia (crude OR 1.56; 95% CI 1.03 to 2.40). After adjusting for age, body mass index (BMI) and other covariates, this association weakened and was no longer statistically significant (adjusted OR (aOR) 1.37; 95% CI 0.88 to 2.16). Age ≥40 years, overweight and obesity remained independently associated with dyslipidaemia. Sex-stratified analyses revealed that psoriatic disease was significantly independently associated with dyslipidaemia in men (aOR 2.05; 95% CI 1.08 to 3.99) but not in women.

CONCLUSIONS: In this hospital-based population, the crude prevalence of dyslipidaemia was higher among patients with psoriatic disease; however, this association was attenuated after adjusting for age, BMI and other covariates. An association persisted among men in the sex-stratified analysis. This should be interpreted cautiously, rather than as definitive evidence that sex modifies the association between psoriatic disease and dyslipidaemia. This observed association should be confirmed in larger studies.

articles.title: Exclude or expose in irritable bowel syndrome study: what works for whom and how? Protocol for a randomised controlled trial of internet-delivered FODMAP diet versus exposure-based cognitive behavioural therapy.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a disorder of gut-brain interaction characterised by abdominal pain and altered bowel habits and is associated with reduced quality of life. Although several treatments are effective at the group level, treatment responses vary substantially between individuals, highlighting the need for personalised approaches. This trial investigates moderators and mediators of treatment response to two established IBS interventions to determine for whom treatments are most effective and how they exert their effects.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This parallel-group randomised controlled trial will enrol 235 adults with IBS from community, primary and tertiary care across Australia and the US. Participants will be randomised to a 12 week online fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides and polyols (FODMAP) diet intervention targeting reduction of fermentable carbohydrate intake or an exposure-based cognitive behavioural therapy (E-CBT) programme targeting symptom-related avoidance behaviours, each with therapist support (dietitian or psychologist, respectively). The primary objective is to assess moderators and mediators of treatment response on gastrointestinal symptom severity, measured using the Gastrointestinal Symptom Rating Scale (GSRS-IBS), assessed weekly from baseline to week 12. Pre-specified moderators and mediators include gastrointestinal-specific anxiety and avoidance behaviour and total FODMAP intake; treatment preference will also be examined as a moderator. Treatment expectancy and credibility and therapeutic alliance will be assessed as covariates accounting for non-specific treatment effects. Secondary outcomes, assessed at baseline, post-treatment (12 weeks) and 3- and 6-month post-intervention follow-up, include IBS-specific symptom severity (measured using the IBS-Symptom Severity Scale, IBS-SSS), IBS-related quality of life, eating-related symptoms, psychological symptoms, extraintestinal symptom distress, stool frequency and consistency and gut microbiome composition and function. We will also assess gastrointestinal symptom severity by the GSRS-IBS at 3- and 6-month follow-up to assess maintenance. Linear mixed-effects models will assess treatment effects and moderation. Latent growth curve modelling and time-lagged mixed-effects models will examine mediation.

ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Ethical approval was obtained from the University of Melbourne Human Research Ethics Committee (Project ID: 31186). This manuscript is based on protocol V.4.0 (06–04-26). Recruitment is ongoing. Results will be disseminated via peer-reviewed publications and presentations at scientific meetings.

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT06940596.

articles.title: Effects of henagliflozin proline tablets versus metformin extended-release tablets on body composition in geriatric patients with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus (HABIT-GEMs): study protocol for a multicentre, randomised, open-label trial.
Effect and prognostic value of physical activity for lower-extremity complications of type 2 diabetes across the adult lifespan: a national cohort study using Swedish registers.
Association between daily salt intake and cardiometabolic indicators among employees of a research institute in Beijing, China: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine the associations between daily salt intake (DSI) and a comprehensive panel of cardiometabolic indicators among employees undergoing annual occupational health examinations.

DESIGN: A cross-sectional, single-centre observational study.

SETTING: Annual occupational health examinations at an aerospace research institute in Beijing, China.

PARTICIPANTS: Between May 2025 and July 2025, 2642 participants were enrolled. Each participant provided a fasting morning spot urine sample and written informed consent.

METHODS: Spearman correlation, multivariable linear regression and restricted cubic spline models were used to examine the associations between DSI and cardiometabolic indicators. Model robustness was assessed through stratified analysis and multivariable logistic regression analysis.

RESULTS: After adjusting for confounding factors, DSI showed no significant associations with systolic blood pressure (SBP), diastolic blood pressure (DBP), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) or low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) but exhibited significant negative associations with uric acid (UA), serum creatinine (Cr), triglycerides, fasting plasma glucose and total cholesterol (all p<0.05). Only DBP showed a nonlinear pattern, with an estimated inflection point at a DSI of 8.66 g. In stratified analysis, DSI was inversely associated with UA and Cr across all subgroups while showing no significant association with SBP, DBP, HDL-C or LDL-C. In multivariable logistic regression, higher DSI was associated with lower odds of dyslipidaemia (OR=0.936), impaired fasting glucose (OR=0.832), hyperuricaemia (OR=0.847), higher serum creatinine (OR=0.874) but not hypertension.

CONCLUSIONS: In this occupational cohort, DSI showed either nonsignificant or inverse associations with cardiometabolic indicators after adjustment for confounders. Stratified and multivariable logistic regression analyses showed generally consistent patterns of association.

articles.title: Barriers and facilitators for implementing active surveillance after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy for oesophageal cancer in Dutch hospitals: a qualitative study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To explore barriers and facilitators to implementing active surveillance for patients with a complete clinical response after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) for oesophageal cancer.

DESIGN: A qualitative study using semistructured group interviews. Data were collected and analysed using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR). The CFIR comprised five domains: innovation, outer setting (external healthcare environment), inner setting (hospital organisational context), characteristics of individuals and process of implementation.

SETTING: Six Dutch hospitals participating in the Surgery As Needed for Oesophageal cancer trial.

PARTICIPANTS: 32 medical specialists and nurse practitioners involved in active surveillance and follow-up care.

RESULTS: Barriers related to innovation included the high frequency of surveillance visits and uncertainty regarding the diagnostic value of the first clinical response evaluation (CRE) shortly after nCRT, while optimisation of the protocol (such as refining timing, frequency and criteria for CREs) was a facilitator. Facilitators in the outer setting included ongoing evidence generation through prospective studies. Within the inner setting, barriers involved challenges in coordinating follow-up planning, potential negative financial implications for surgical departments and increased workload for gastroenterology and nuclear medicine teams while existing multidisciplinary collaboration acted as a facilitator. Barriers related to characteristics of individuals included limited endoscopic experience in irradiated tissue, while patient preference for active surveillance and shared decision-making were facilitators.

CONCLUSION: Implementation of active surveillance after nCRT for oesophageal cancer is challenged by organisational complexity and the need for ongoing generation of data on effectiveness of active surveillance. Clear allocation of responsibilities, streamlined surveillance pathways and adequate training are essential to support effective and sustainable adoption in routine clinical practice. Trial registration number (NTR-6803)

articles.title: Longitudinal cohort study of immune-mediated inflammatory diseases within the systems medicine framework of the DREAM Centre: a study protocol.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs) are chronic disorders characterised by dysregulated immune responses affecting multiple organ systems, including the skin, joints and gastrointestinal (GI) tract. Progression across organ systems contributes to clinical heterogeneity and complicates prediction of disease course and treatment response. Systems medicine approaches integrating longitudinal clinical data with molecular profiling provide a framework to address these challenges. The DREAM (Dermatology REsearch Across Multiple disciplines) Centre applies a systems medicine approach to improve the understanding and prediction of disease trajectories and treatment response across IMIDs. The Centre aims to establish the MultiOrgan Systemic Autoimmune Inflammatory Conditions (MOSAIC) cohort as an integrated platform for this research. This protocol describes the first clinical component of MOSAIC, focusing on long-term follow-up of patients with multiorgan IMIDs.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This study is designed as a longitudinal follow-up study of a cohort previously enrolled in a randomised controlled trial at Aarhus University Hospital (2019–2022). The original trial enrolled patients diagnosed with at least two concurrent IMIDs affecting the skin (psoriasis, hidradenitis suppurativa), the joints (psoriatic arthritis and axial spondyloarthritis) or the GI tract (inflammatory bowel disease). All 213 participants will be invited to a single follow-up visit. Assessments include standardised clinical examinations, validated patient-reported outcomes and biological sampling. The primary outcomes are inflammatory disease activity. Secondary outcomes include mental health, quality of life, physical function, work productivity and cardiovascular risk. Exploratory analyses will integrate multiomics data to identify clinical and molecular markers of disease progression and treatment response.

ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The study is approved by the Central Denmark Regional Ethics Committees (1-10-72-185-25). Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, scientific conferences and relevant patient organisations.

articles.title: Fast-track cardiac anaesthesia and early extubation pathway versus usual care for adults undergoing coronary artery bypass graft surgery: a two-centre pilot randomised controlled feasibility trial in Victoria, Australia.
Cluster-level convergence of malaria infection, childhood zero-dose prevalence and health-campaign frequency in sub-Saharan Africa: a Bayesian analysis of 18 countries.
Natural history and risk factors for disease progression in early-stage hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: insights from the SOLENOID cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to understand the natural history of early-stage hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) patients and identify risk factors for disease progression.

BACKGROUND: HCM is a phenotypically heterogeneous disease, characterised by a wide range of clinical outcomes, from asymptomatic to severe heart failure.

METHODS: The predictorS Of cLinical outcomEs iN hypertrOphIc carDiomyopathy (SOLENOID) is an observational, multicentre cohort study conducted across five centres in Europe and the USA. Inclusion criteria were patients with confirmed HCM seen between 2010 and 2022 in New York Heart Association (NYHA) class I. The study’s endpoint was a composite of worsening NYHA class (=N+1) and unplanned cardiovascular hospitalisation, assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Risk factors were identified through univariate analyses at each centre, with results aggregated through meta-analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 961 patients were included, with a median follow-up of 4 years. The mean age was 54±16 years and 29% of the cohort were females. 43% of patients were treated with beta-blockers and 13% had pre-existent atrial fibrillation (AF). Genetic testing revealed mutations primarily in MYBPC3 (30%) and MYH7 (13%) genes. Incidence of the composite endpoint was 26% and 41% at 3 and 5 years, respectively, with NYHA class worsening as the main contributor. The main predictors of the composite endpoint include older age (log-HR=0.33, p<0.05), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (log-HR=1.18, p<0.001), chest pain (log-HR=0.60, p<0.05), fatigue (log-HR=0.73, p<0.01), AF on electrocardiography (log-HR=1.56, p<0.0001), higher N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide levels (log-HR=0.75, p<0.0001), larger left atrial volume index (log-HR=0.29, p=0.04), peak A-wave velocity (log-HR=0.38, p=0.04) and maximal end-diastolic left ventricle wall thickness (log-HR=0.36, p=0.04).

CONCLUSION: Nearly 30% of the early-stage HCM patients experienced disease progression over 3 years, highlighting a medical unmet need. Further research is needed to determine if this population might benefit from intensive monitoring or earlier therapy.

articles.title: Using AI-generated ultra-widefield-like fundus images to assist colour fundus photography in screening for chronic kidney disease: a multicentre cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop a generative artificial intelligence (AI) model that derives ultra-widefield-like (UWF-like) fundus images from conventional colour fundus photographs (CFP) and to assess whether these images improve chronic kidney disease (CKD) screening.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This multicentre cross-sectional diagnostic study included 3776 fundus images from 2056 patients at four centres in China and Japan between 2023 and 2024. The generative model was developed and validated using 1865 images from 1049 patients. CKD screening models were developed using 1750 UWF images and their corresponding UWF-derived CFP-like central crops from 909 patients at Ruijin Hospital with patient-level fivefold cross-validation and externally validated using 161 native CFP images from 98 patients at Jiading Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine. Performance was assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and specificity at fixed sensitivity of 0.80.

RESULTS: In internal validation, AUCs were 0.911 for real UWF images, 0.773 for AI-generated UWF-like images and 0.689 for UWF-derived CFP-like central crops. At fixed sensitivity of 0.80, specificities were 0.879, 0.573 and 0.459, respectively. In external validation, AI-generated UWF-like images outperformed native CFP images, with an AUC of 0.707 versus 0.609 and specificity of 0.458 versus 0.344. Retinal vascular features from AI-generated UWF-like images remained associated with renal function indicators.

CONCLUSION: AI-generated UWF-like images improved CKD screening performance compared with CFP alone. This approach may extend retinal imaging-based CKD screening where UWF imaging is unavailable, but prospective real-world validation is needed before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Prompt sensitivity affects large language model decision-making in aortic stenosis: a real-world study of severity classification, treatment recommendation and exploratory prognostic analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Aortic stenosis (AS) assessment requires integration of discordant echocardiographic and clinical information. The reliability of large language models (LLMs) across prompts and AS phenotypes remains uncertain. This study aimed to compare five LLMs across four prompting strategies for AS severity classification, real-world intervention concordance and exploratory prognostic associations.

METHODS: This retrospective study evaluated five LLMs across four prompting strategies in 1455 patients with AS. Task 1 assessed AS severity classification and Task 2 assessed real-world intervention concordance. Performance was summarised by accuracy, balanced accuracy and macro-F1. Exploratory associations of the best performing Task 2 configuration with all-cause mortality and heart failure progression were examined using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression.

RESULTS: GPT-o1/chain-of-thought (CoT) achieved the highest Task 1 accuracy (97.53%), balanced accuracy (90.93%) and macro-F1 (83.19%). Grok-2/CoT achieved the highest Task 2 concordance (88.32%). Grok-2/CoT recommendations separated heart failure progression-free survival in unadjusted analysis (p=0.006) but not overall survival (p=0.105). After adjustment, recommendation group was not independently associated with mortality (HR 1.41, 95% CI 0.58 to 3.45, p=0.453) or heart failure progression (HR 1.10, 95% CI 0.44 to 2.74, p=0.832).

DISCUSSION: LLM performance varied by model, task and prompt. Apparent prognostic separation observed in unadjusted analysis was not retained after adjustment for clinical characteristics, AS severity and actual intervention.

CONCLUSION: LLMs require prompt standardisation, class-specific evaluation and prospective validation before clinical use.

articles.title: Incidentally detected thrombocytopenia and risk of haematological disease and death in the general population: prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the risk of death, haematological disease, liver disease, and other adverse outcomes in individuals with incidentally detected thrombocytopenia with or without anaemia, and to provide clinically applicable absolute risk estimates supporting evidence based shared decision making.

DESIGN: Prospective cohort study.

SETTING: UK Biobank and an independent Danish replication cohort (from the Copenhagen General Population Study and Danish General Suburban Population Study), with individuals enrolled from December 2006 to October 2010 (UK) or November 2003 to November 2018 (Denmark).

PARTICIPANTS: 485 103 individuals from the general population (380 951 from the UK and 104 152 from Denmark) who attended a health examination, and platelet count, haemoglobin level, leucocyte count, and differential count were measured.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Risk of death from any cause, receiving a diagnosis of haematological disease, and death from haematological disease. Secondary endpoints (UK only) were liver disease, bleeding, non-haematological cancer, thrombosis, and cause specific death.

RESULTS: Isolated thrombocytopenia was detected in 8350 UK individuals (2.2%) and 1408 Danish individuals (1.4%). Median follow-up was 14 years in UK individuals and 11 years in Danish individuals. In both cohorts, the relative risk of death from any cause was increased in isolated mild (platelet count 100-149×109/L) or moderate-severe (platelet count <100×109/L) thrombocytopenia. In the oldest UK individuals aged 65-70 years, the absolute 10 year risk of all cause death was 7% in women with a normal platelet count and haemoglobin level, 10% in women with isolated mild thrombocytopenia, and 14% in women with isolated moderate-severe thrombocytopenia; the corresponding risks for men were 11%, 15%, and 22%, respectively. Although the relative risk of haematological disease and death from haematological disease was increased in isolated mild or moderate-severe thrombocytopenia, all age and sex categories with isolated mild thrombocytopenia had absolute 10 year risks of receiving a diagnosis of haematological disease of ≤4% in UK individuals and ≤7% in Danish individuals, whereas the 10 year risk was ≤2% for individuals with a normal platelet count and haemoglobin level. The absolute risk of death from haematological disease was much lower, and all age and sex categories with isolated mild thrombocytopenia had 10 year risks <1%. The relative risk of non-malignant liver disease, liver cancer, and death from liver disease was increased in UK individuals with isolated thrombocytopenia. The absolute risk was highest for non-malignant liver disease with 10 year risks of <1-2% in individuals with a normal platelet count (depending on age and sex), 2-4% in isolated mild thrombocytopenia, and 3-7% in isolated moderate-severe thrombocytopenia. For most endpoints, risks were generally similar or higher in individuals with thrombocytopenia with anaemia.

CONCLUSIONS: Individuals with isolated mild thrombocytopenia had only a modest absolute risk of haematological disease and death from haematological disease, which may inform shared decision making about haematology referral, investigations, and follow-up.

articles.title: Effect of discontinuing antihypertensives on perioperative hypotension in older patients before non-cardiac surgery: multicentre, randomised, double blind, controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether discontinuing versus continuing angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) on the morning of surgery reduces perioperative hypotension in older patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery.

DESIGN: Multicentre, randomised, double blind, placebo controlled trial.

SETTING: Five tertiary teaching hospitals in China, November 2020 to December 2023.

PARTICIPANTS: 2036 older patients (60-80 years) using ACE inhibitors or ARBs for at least two weeks and scheduled for non-cardiac surgery under general anaesthesia.

INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomised to receive their usual ACE inhibitor or ARB or a placebo in identical capsules on the morning of surgery.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was the incidence of perioperative hypotension (mean blood pressure <65 mm Hg or a ≥30% decrease from baseline requiring treatment). Secondary outcomes included duration of hypotension, requirement for a vasopressor, intraoperative fluid volume, postoperative hypotension, and 30 day complications (neurocognitive disorders, major cardiocerebral events) or mortality.

RESULTS: 2012 patients (mean age 68.8 years; 54.4% male) completed the study: 1004 were included in the antihypertensive group and 1008 in the no antihypertensive group. The incidence of perioperative hypotension was lower in the no antihypertensive group (314/1008, 31.2%) versus antihypertensive group (457/1004, 45.5%): adjusted odds ratio 0.52 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.43 to 0.63); absolute risk difference -14.4% (95% CI -18.5% to -10.1%); P<0.001. The duration of hypotension and requirement for a vasopressor were both reduced in the no antihypertensive group: adjusted mean difference -1.3 minutes (95% CI -1.8 to -0.8 minutes) and 28.5% v 41.1%; adjusted odds ratio 0.54 (95% CI 0.44 to 0.66). Intraoperative fluid volume, postoperative hypotension, 30 day complications, and mortality did not differ significantly between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Discontinuing ACE inhibitors or ARBs on the morning of surgery in older patients with hypertension statistically significantly reduced perioperative hypotension and the requirement for vasopressors without increasing 30 day complications or mortality. This simple strategy provides high certainty evidence for preoperative drug management in this patient population.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2000039376.

articles.title: Recent recommendations for the diagnosis and management of liver cirrhosis and its complications.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Progression of liver cirrhosis is a dynamic transition toward decompensation driven by portal hypertension (PH), while systemic inflammation (SI) mediates organ dysfunction and failure, acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF), and short-term mortality. The recent publication of the Baveno VIII consensus and of harmonized organ failure definitions calls for a reassessment of current concepts and recommendations.

AREAS COVERED: PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science were searched from April 2026 to September 2026 for consensus documents, randomized trials, and large cohort studies on cirrhosis and its complications. Earlier landmark studies were included when they underpinned current recommendations, without any claim to completeness. Noninvasive risk stratification in compensated advanced chronic liver disease, prevention of first decompensation, the clinical phenotypes of decompensation, management of variceal bleeding including preemptive TIPS, ascites, hepatic encephalopathy, renal dysfunction, and ACLF are included together with practical guidance for triage and transfer to expert and transplant centers.

EXPERT OPINION: Management is shifting from reactive treatment of individual complications toward mechanism-based, preemptive care guided by dynamic risk assessment. Harmonized ACLF definitions and biomarkers of systemic inflammation should now enable trials of disease-modifying therapy, the field's largest unmet need.

articles.title: Stressors, Family Functioning, Family Resilience and Family Adaptation in Maintenance Haemodialysis: A Structural Equation Modelling.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This cross-sectional correlational study aimed to develop a structural equation model (SEM) to elucidate the associations among stressors, family functioning, family resilience and family adaptation in maintenance haemodialysis (MHD) patients.

BACKGROUND: The stress burden experienced by patients undergoing MHD has received increasing attention. Stressors may adversely affect family adaptation, making the adaptation process more complex. However, evidence regarding the factors associated with family adaptation among patients undergoing MHD remains limited.

DESIGN: A cross-sectional study.

METHODS: A total of 412 patients with MHD were recruited from December 2023 and July 2024 at three hospitals in Hunan Province. Data on stressors, family functioning, family resilience and family adaptation were collected using the haemodialysis stressor scale, APGAR, Shortened Chinese version of the family resilience assessment scale, and the Chinese version of the family adaptability and cohesion evaluation scales. SEM was employed to test the study's hypotheses. This study was reported in accordance with STROBE guidelines.

RESULTS: The findings revealed that stressors were negatively associated with family functioning, family resilience and family adaptation. Stressors demonstrated an indirect relationship with family adaptation through family functioning and family resilience.

CONCLUSIONS: This study identified the structural relationships among the four variables under investigation. Family functioning and family resilience were found to be potential mediators in the association between stressors and family adaptation.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Stressors are an important concern for patients undergoing MHD. Given the associations observed among stressors, family functioning, family resilience and family adaptation in this study, nephrology nurses may consider both patients' individual needs and their perceptions of family-related factors when assessing adaptation to long-term dialysis, rather than focusing exclusively on individual patient needs. In routine nephrology nursing practice, assessment of stressors and family-related factors may help nurses identify patients who may require additional family-oriented support and facilitate communication with patients and their families. These findings may provide a basis for developing more targeted, evidence-informed approaches to support patients and their families, while further intervention studies are needed to determine the effectiveness of such approaches.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patient or public contribution.

articles.title: Deep Learning-Enabled Magnetic Bead-Capture Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization Enables Multiplex Identification and Digital Counting of Pathogenic Bacteria.
articles.abstract: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are among the most prevalent infectious diseases worldwide. For complicated and antimicrobial-resistant cases, timely diagnosis is critical for guiding targeted therapy and improving patient outcomes. While conventional urine culture suffers from prolonged turnaround times and low positive detection rates, fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) has emerged as a rapid, highly specific alternative. However, its clinical application remains hindered by complicated sample pretreatment, insufficient sensitivity that often requires pre-enrichment by culture, and subjective bias in manual interpretation. To address these bottlenecks, we developed deep learning-enabled magnetic bead-capture fluorescence in situ hybridization (DeepMag-FISH), a culture-free platform that employs artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted digital counting for rapid identification and single-bacterium enumeration of pathogens. We adopted soluble β2-glycoprotein I (sβ2GPI)-coated magnetic beads for efficient pathogen enrichment, and utilized a modular dual-probe labeling strategy for multiplexed hybridization, thus enabling highly specific molecular labeling. Additionally, we integrated this sample processing pipeline with a YOLOv11-based deep learning framework for automatic multiscale feature extraction and precise single-bacterium counting. Validated using spiked urine specimens, DeepMag-FISH clearly differentiated Escherichia coli, Vibrio parahaemolyticus, and Klebsiella pneumoniae with negligible spectral crosstalk. The platform reaches a detection capability of 30 CFU/mL, completing the entire workflow, including all magnetic separation and washing steps, within approximately 3.5 h. By combining magnetic bead-based pathogen enrichment with AI-driven image analysis, this approach mitigates matrix interference and subjective bias in conventional methods, offering a rapid and quantitative approach for pathogen detection in spiked urine samples. Beyond UTI management, DeepMag-FISH may also be explored for potential applications in other fields, such as bloodstream infection diagnosis and food safety monitoring.

articles.title: Acting for High-Quality Cardiovascular Intensive Care in Japan　- The Role of Cardiovascular Intensivists.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society

articles.title: Elevated Lipoprotein(a) Is Associated With Heart Failure in Patients With Peripheral Artery Disease.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic value of lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] in peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains uncertain.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively studied 138 patients with intermittent claudication undergoing endovascular therapy. Patients were classified by Lp(a) level (≥30 vs. <30 mg/dL). The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Elevated Lp(a) was associated with a higher incidence of MACE (31.1% vs. 9.6%; P=0.002), predominantly driven by heart failure. It independently predicted MACE (HR 4.23) and heart failure (HR 5.12), but not cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or stroke.

CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) was associated with heart failure-driven MACE after endovascular therapy in patients with PAD.

articles.title: Multi-model insights into racial and ethnic heterogeneities in early COVID-19 transmission and severity in the U.S.
articles.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic was marked by unequal disease burden across racial and ethnic groups in the US. Using a multi-model ensemble framework, we retrospectively assessed the impact of racial and ethnic heterogeneities in COVID-19 transmission and disease severity on mortality during the winter 2020-2021 surge in California and North Carolina. Models incorporating race and ethnicity projected mortality more accurately than null models, while the ensemble outperformed all individual models on average by weighted interval scores. Eliminating transmission heterogeneities produced larger mortality reductions than eliminating severity differences alone, particularly for Latino populations in California (55% reduction) and Black populations in North Carolina (28% reduction). Reducing severity heterogeneity also lowered mortality, with the greatest benefit among Black populations in both states (21% and 16% reductions in California and North Carolina, respectively). Eliminating both transmission and severity heterogeneity yielded the largest reductions overall, predicting 49-70% lower mortality across racial and ethnic groups in California and 23-40% in North Carolina. Mitigating transmission inequities also produced indirect benefits for non-targeted populations, highlighting the broad impact of reducing disparities in exposure risk and access to protective resources.

articles.title: Oral angiotensin-(1-7) formulation attenuates structural alterations in established emphysema and protects against subsequent allergic airway inflammation.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and asthma can coexist, increasing disease burden and complicating treatment. We investigated whether oral angiotensin-(1-7) [Ang-(1-7)] treatment initiated after emphysema establishment attenuates pulmonary structural alterations and protects against subsequent ovalbumin (OVA)-induced allergic airway inflammation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: C57BL/6 mice were randomly assigned to experimental groups with or without elastase-induced emphysema. Emphysema was induced by three weekly intratracheal instillations of porcine pancreatic elastase. The mice subsequently received an oral formulation of Ang-(1-7) one week later, for four weeks. Treatment was discontinued before the subsequent OVA sensitization and challenge. The groups were sensitized and challenged with either OVA or PBS. Lung morphometry, inflammation, collagen deposition, pulmonary Ang II levels, and gene expression were assessed.

KEY FINDINGS: Elastase caused persistent alveolar enlargement and reduced septal density. Oral Ang-(1-7) attenuated these abnormalities. Treatment reduced elevated pulmonary angiotensin II levels and increased ACE2 mRNA expression in an independent emphysema experiment. OVA induced eosinophilic inflammation, airway remodeling, and increased inflammatory gene expression in emphysematous mice. Following the OVA challenge, previously treated emphysematous mice exhibited reduced pulmonary eosinophilia, inflammatory scores, epithelial thickening, and collagen deposition, alongside improved alveolar morphometry. Ang-(1-7) also decreased the gene expression of CD206, arginase-1, NLRP3, caspase-1, p53, and p16. These protective effects occurred without significant changes in OVA-specific IgE levels.

SIGNIFICANCE: Oral Ang-(1-7) provided structural and anti-inflammatory benefits after establishing emphysema, with protection also evident following an allergic challenge despite treatment withdrawal before sensitization. These findings support prior modulation of the injured pulmonary microenvironment as a promising therapeutic strategy to limit allergic inflammation and airway remodeling in structurally compromised lungs.

articles.title: Closing the GDMT Gap: A Virtual Advanced Practice Provider-Led Heart Failure Medication Titration Program in a Community Health System.
Intrahepatic S100A4⁺ B1 cells are associated with inflammation and fibrosis during Clonorchis sinensis infection.
articles.abstract: Clonorchiasis, caused by Clonorchis sinensis, is a foodborne parasitic disease characterized by persistent hepatobiliary inflammation, progressive liver fibrosis, and an increased risk of cholangiocarcinoma. B cells serve as the core component of humoral immunity, however, the contribution of hepatic B-cell populations to the immunopathology of clonorchiasis remains poorly understood. Here, we show that C. sinensis infection induces a marked accumulation of intrahepatic B cells, among which B1 cells exhibit the most pronounced expansion. Notably, the expanded B1 cells present limited transcriptional signatures associated with antibody production as well as antigen processing and presentation, indicating functions beyond conventional B-cell effector responses. Further analysis identifies a prominent S100A4+ B1-cell population that accumulates significantly after infection and displays transcriptional features linked to cellular stress, immune activation, and inflammatory responses. Spatial quantitative analysis confirms that the abundance of S100A4+ B cells positively correlates with the density of CD11b+ myeloid cells and the α-SMA-positive area in infected liver tissues. Collectively, these findings define S100A4+ B1 cells as a previously underestimated hepatic B-cell population enriched during C. sinensis infection, which is closely associated with hepatic inflammation and liver fibrosis. This study provides novel insights into the cellular immune landscape driving chronic hepatobiliary pathological changes in clonorchiasis.

articles.title: Pragmatic Clinical indicators of Tuberculosis Transmission Risk: a Household Contact Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interrupting TB transmission is a priority in high-burden settings. Identifying highly infectious people with TB may guide targeted interventions.

RESEARCH QUESTION: Can readily available clinical characteristics (eg, lung cavitation, cough duration, modified Bandim TB score) indicate the transmission risk in participants with TB?

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We conducted an observational cohort study in Lima, Peru, enrolling 4,500 index participants. Of the 4,044 people with microbiologically confirmed TB, 3,109 had at least 1 household contact (HHC), yielding 12,767 HHCs. Index participants underwent chest radiograph and TB symptom assessment, from which we derived a modified Bandim TB score. We assessed HHCs for TB infection at baseline and 6 months, and for incident TB disease over 12 months. We analyzed associations between index participant indicators and TB outcomes in HHCs using modified Poisson regression with generalized estimating equations, adjusting for relevant covariates.

RESULTS: Among child HHCs, baseline TB infection risk increased with greater cavitary extent (adjusted trend P = .005) and longer cough duration (adjusted trend P = .002), with similar trends at 6 months. Among cavitation categories, multiple-quadrant involvement was associated with the highest baseline infection risk (adjusted prevalence risk ratio, 1.62; 95% CI, 1.10-2.39), but not with incident disease (adjusted cumulative risk ratio, 1.20; 95% CI, 0.56-2.60). Among cough duration categories, ≥ 56 days showed the highest baseline infection risk (adjusted prevalence risk ratio, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.18-2.13), but not incident disease (adjusted cumulative risk ratio, 1.30; 95% CI, 0.85-1.99). The modified Bandim TB score was not associated with transmission risk.

INTERPRETATION: Our results show that in this large household cohort, cavitary extent on chest radiograph and cough duration in people with TB were associated with increased TB transmission risk and showed dose-response relationships with TB infection. These simple, readily available indicators may help target preventive interventions in high-burden settings; however, associations with incident TB remain uncertain.

articles.title: Associations between temperatures, extreme temperature events, and onset of acute exacerbations of COPD: a time-stratified case-crossover study in China.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-optimal temperatures and extreme temperature events may trigger acute exacerbations of COPD (AECOPD), but most evidence is admission based, potentially misclassifying exposure timing and obscuring susceptible groups.

RESEARCH QUESTION: Are non-optimal temperature and extreme temperature events associated with AECOPD onset, and which patients are most susceptible?

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We used the Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Registry (ACURE) data and assigned residential temperature exposure using ERA5-Land, a reanalysis dataset of European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts. Cold spells (CS) were defined as consecutive days below location-specific low-temperature thresholds, and compound cold spells (CCS) as concurrent daytime and nighttime cold spells. Associations with reported symptom onset were estimated using a time-stratified case-crossover design, conditional logistic regression with distributed lag nonlinear models. Subgroup and cytokine analyses assessed susceptibility and inflammation.

RESULTS: Among 5,634 patients with AECOPD (mean age, 69.4 ± 9.5 years; 78.8% male), lower temperature was associated with higher odds of AECOPD onset, whereas higher temperature was not. The strongest associations occurred for CS lasting ≥3 days and CCS lasting ≥2 days over lag 0-3 days, with ORs of 1.84 (95% CI, 1.22-2.78) and 4.31 (95% CI, 2.07-8.97), respectively. Nearly half had delayed admission within 14 days. Using admission rather than onset dates attenuated estimates by 88.8% for CS and 84.8% for CCS. Associations were stronger among older adults, men, smokers, patients with severe AECOPD in the past year or previously diagnosed COPD, and those using combination inhaler in the preceding year. CS were also associated with higher TNF-α, IL-6, and CXCL-11 concentrations.

INTERPRETATION: Lower temperature and extreme cold events, particularly CCS, were associated with AECOPD onset. Symptom-onset timing may better capture temperature-related associations than admission timing. These findings highlight the need for targeted cold-weather prevention strategies to reduce AECOPD burden.

TRIAL REGISTRY: ClinicalTrials.gov; NO.: NCT02657525.

articles.title: Neurodevelopmental Outcomes in School-Age Children with Down Syndrome: A Comparison of Children with Repaired Complete Atrioventricular Septal Defect and Those without Major Congenital Heart Disease.
authors: Pediatric Heart Network’s CHILD-DS Writing Committee on behalf of the Pediatric Heart Network Investigators
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare neurodevelopmental (ND) and behavioral outcomes in children with Down syndrome (DS) having complete atrioventricular septal defect (CAVSD) repair as infants and those without major congenital heart disease (CHD) requiring surgery and/or annual cardiology follow-up.

STUDY DESIGN: In a multi-center, observational study across North America, 259 children aged 5-12 years with DS (124 CAVSD repair; 135 non-CHD) underwent a standardized ND assessment battery. Co-primary outcomes were cognitive scores through direct child testing of the Stanford Binet Intelligence Scales, 5th Edition (SB-5) and adaptive composite scores from the parent/caregiver-reported Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales, 3rd Edition.

RESULTS: Study groups were comparable across most socio-demographic and medical characteristics; however, the CAVSD group had lower neighborhood socioeconomic status (SES). There was no difference in SB-5 deviation index scores (unadjusted mean ± SD in CAVSD and non-CHD: nonverbal, 41.5 ± 18 vs 43.0 ± 17 and verbal, 37.9 ± 18 vs 38.7 ± 16, respectively). When unadjusted, Adaptive Behavior Composite scores also showed no group difference (CAVSD and non-CHD median (Q1, Q3): 66.5 (57.0, 73.0) vs 69.0 (62.0, 74.0), respectively); however, after adjustment for a priori sociodemographic, baseline neonatal, and medical factors, the CAVSD group scored 3.8 ±1.7 points lower (P=.03). Children with CAVSD were less likely to pass teaching items on the Expressive Vocabulary Test, 3rd Edition, and they had increased social communication challenges on the parent/caregiver-reported Social Communication Questionnaire, Current Version (2.3±1.2, P=.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Among school-age children with DS, those with CAVSD repair showed no difference in cognitive scores compared with children without major CHD, but they had lower adaptive skills and greater social communication challenges. Lower SES in the CAVSD group underscores the need to examine how social drivers of health influence ND outcomes. Findings improve our understanding of ND profiles among children with DS having repaired CAVSD, helping identify those in need of greater ND support.

articles.title: Lipidomic remodeling in a porcine model of acute myocardial infarction-induced cardiogenic shock.
articles.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock following acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is characterized by impaired forward flow and systemic hypoperfusion but remains incompletely understood from a metabolic perspective. While prior studies have focused predominantly on myocardial injury and recovery, the systemic lipidomic response to cardiogenic shock and its relationship to physiological severity remain poorly characterized. We aimed to define cardiac-enriched and systemic lipid remodeling during AMI-induced cardiogenic shock and identify lipid pathways associated with hemodynamic and metabolic dysfunction.

METHODS: Fifteen pigs underwent left anterior descending coronary artery balloon occlusion followed by reperfusion. Nine animals met pre-specified cardiogenic shock criteria (≥30% reduction in cardiac output and arterial lactate >2 mmol/L) and were included for analysis. Serial coronary sinus and mixed venous plasma sampling was performed throughout ischemia and reperfusion. High-throughput lipidomics profiling was integrated with contemporaneous physiological measurements related to cardiogenic shock, including cardiac output, stroke volume, heart rate, and arterial lactate.

RESULTS: AMI-induced cardiogenic shock produced sustained reductions in cardiac output and stroke volume accompanied by progressive lactate accumulation. Multiple plasma lipid classes remodeled dynamically during ischemia-reperfusion, including increases in triglycerides, diglycerides, phosphatidylserines, and acylcarnitines. Lipid remodeling extended beyond cardiac-enriched coronary sinus sampling, with mixed venous plasma demonstrating substantial systemic metabolic adaptation to cardiac dysfunction. Lipid class and species-level analyses identified phosphatidylserines and acylcarnitines as the lipid classes most consistently associated with physiological severity. Phosphatidylserine species tracked worsening lactate accumulation and impaired stroke volume, while acylcarnitines demonstrated strong relationships with lactate and reduced cardiac output. Heart rate demonstrated broader lipidomic associations in coronary sinus plasma than mixed venous blood, supporting compartment-specific cardiac physiological sensitivity.

CONCLUSIONS: AMI-induced cardiogenic shock is associated with coordinated cardiac-enriched and systemic lipid remodeling linked to impaired forward flow and tissue hypoperfusion. Phosphatidylserines and acylcarnitines emerged as candidate pathways associated with cardiogenic shock severity, identifying potential metabolic mechanisms and biomarker targets in acute cardiac failure.

articles.title: Maternal and Neonatal Outcomes Associated with Influenza-Related Hospitalization During Pregnancy: A Population-Based Matched Cohort Study in Suzhou, China, 2018-2024.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physiological and immunological changes render pregnant women susceptible to influenza, leading to increased risks of severe illness and adverse pregnancy outcomes. These outcomes are major causes of perinatal mortality and morbidity, and fetal deaths (including miscarriage and stillbirth) pose a major public health challenge. However, population-based cohort studies on this topic, particularly from China, remain scarce. Therefore, clarifying the association between influenza infection and adverse pregnancy outcomes is critical for optimizing antenatal care and reducing maternal-neonatal risks.

METHODS: We conducted a population-based matched cohort study among pregnant women in Suzhou, China, from October 2018 to September 2024, based on active surveillance of influenza-related acute respiratory or febrile illness (ARFI) hospitalizations. Exposed groups were RT-PCR-confirmed influenza infections among hospitalized ARFI pregnant women, excluding those with delivery outside Jiangsu Province, miscarriage or stillbirth in the current pregnancy, repeated ARFI-related hospitalizations during the same pregnancy, multiple gestations, or already postpartum at ARFI admission. Unexposed groups were selected from the same source population, matched 1:4 by age, last menstrual period, gravidity, and parity, excluding those with any ARFI hospitalization, delivery outside Jiangsu Province, miscarriage or stillbirth in the current pregnancy, or multiple gestation. For preterm birth analysis, we included only exposed women with gestational age 28-37 weeks and their matched controls. For term outcomes (macrosomia, term low birth weight (TLBW), small for gestational age (SGA), large for gestational age (LGA), high-risk infants, frail infants, 1-min Apgar < 7, and neonatal resuscitation), we excluded preterm births and their matched group to avoid confounding. Associations were estimated using generalized estimating equations (GEE) with logit link, clustering by matched-set identifier, and stratified by infection trimester, reporting odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI).

RESULTS: A total of 4,275 pregnant women were enrolled in this study, including 855 in the exposed group and 3,420 in the unexposed group. In the full cohort, influenza-related hospitalization during pregnancy was significantly associated with increased risks of preterm birth (aOR = 1.94, 95% CI: 1.42-2.66), TLBW (aOR = 2.40, 95% CI: 1.08-5.37), LGA (aOR = 1.36, 95% CI: 1.13-1.65), high-risk infants (aOR = 1.96, 95% CI: 1.62-2.38), frail infants (aOR = 1.53, 95% CI: 1.32-1.77), and neonatal resuscitation (aOR = 1.23, 95% CI: 1.08-1.40). For the preterm birth analysis, 2,520 women (504 exposed and 2,016 unexposed) were included. For the term outcomes analysis, 3,975 women (795 exposed and 3,180 unexposed) were included. Influenza-related hospitalization during pregnancy was significantly associated with increased risks of preterm birth (aOR = 3.58, 95% CI: 2.56-5.26), TLBW (aOR = 2.58, 95% CI: 1.13-5.92), LGA (aOR = 1.39, 95% CI: 1.14-1.69), high‑risk infants (aOR = 1.60, 95% CI: 1.29-1.98), frail infants (aOR = 1.47, 95% CI: 1.26-1.71), and neonatal resuscitation (aOR = 1.21, 95% CI: 1.05-1.38). When stratified by trimesters, influenza hospitalization in the first trimester was significantly associated with higher risks of macrosomia (aOR = 3.16, 95% CI: 1.40-7.12) and high‑risk infants (aOR = 2.14, 95% CI: 1.11-4.15), whereas hospitalization in the third trimester was associated with elevated risks of TLBW (aOR = 2.61, 95% CI: 1.09-6.26), LGA (aOR = 1.41, 95% CI: 1.13-1.74), high‑risk infants (aOR = 1.59, 95% CI: 1.26-2.02), frail infants (aOR = 1.58, 95% CI: 1.33-1.87), and neonatal resuscitation (aOR = 1.33, 95% CI: 1.14-1.55).

CONCLUSION: Influenza-related hospitalization during pregnancy was associated with increased risks of adverse perinatal outcomes. However, this association may reflect the combined effects of influenza infection, illness severity, and hospitalization rather than influenza infection alone. Strengthening maternal influenza vaccination, timely antiviral treatment, and surveillance systems remains important to reduce severe influenza and its associated burden.

articles.title: Patterns of Anticoagulant Use in Older Medicare Beneficiaries with Advanced CKD and Newly Diagnosed Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation

articles.title: The Burden of Occult Cerebrovascular Disease in CKD: A Scoping Review.
articles.journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Occult cerebrovascular diseases (OCCD) including extracranial and intracranial atherosclerotic disease (ECAD and ICAD) and cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) are asymptomatic cerebrovascular abnormalities associated with future risk of stroke and dementia. Although chronic kidney disease (CKD) is strongly associated with adverse brain health outcomes, the breadth of evidence regarding OCCD in people with CKD has not been comprehensively characterized. This scoping review summarizes the available literature on OCCD among adults with CKD without clinically overt cerebrovascular disease.

SOURCES OF EVIDENCE: PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched for studies published between January 2000 and July 2025.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Peer-reviewed studies reporting the frequency or characteristics of OCCD manifestations in adults with CKD without a known history of stroke or transient ischemic attack.

CHARTING METHODS: Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data on study characteristics, CKD definitions, neuroimaging modalities, and reported OCCD findings. Methodological quality was assessed using a modified Newcastle-Ottawa Scale.

RESULTS: Forty-six studies comprising 5,153 participants with CKD were included. Study populations varied substantially with respect to CKD stage, dialysis status, study design, and imaging methodology. Two studies evaluating ICAD reported moderate-to-severe intracranial stenosis in approximately one-quarter of participants with CKD. Across studies evaluating ECAD, the frequency of significant extracranial carotid stenosis ranged from approximately 3% in patients with non-dialysis-dependent CKD to 28% among patients receiving dialysis. Thirty-eight studies evaluated manifestations of CSVD, including cerebral microbleeds, silent cerebral infarctions, white matter hyperintensities, and enlarged perivascular spaces. Several studies suggested a greater burden of CSVD manifestations among patients with advanced CKD or dialysis dependence. Reported frequencies varied considerably across studies.

LIMITATIONS: Considerable heterogeneity in study populations, CKD definitions, imaging protocols, and outcome ascertainment methods limited direct comparison across studies.

CONCLUSIONS: Occult cerebrovascular abnormalities are frequently reported across diverse CKD populations, particularly among patients with advanced kidney disease. Variation in the prevalence of abnormalities may reflect differences in CKD severity, participant characteristics, neuroimaging protocols, and outcome definitions. These findings highlight the need for standardized neuroimaging approaches and prospective studies to better characterize the clinical implications of OCCD in CKD.

articles.title: Regulatory T cells in kidney diseases: context-dependent functions and therapeutic potential.
articles.abstract: Kidney diseases, including acute kidney injury (AKI), chronic kidney disease (CKD), IgA nephropathy (IgAN), lupus nephritis (LN), and kidney transplantation, share features of immune dysregulation, persistent inflammation, and progressive fibrosis. Regulatory T cells (Tregs) are central to immune tolerance in the kidney, yet their function is not uniform: it is shaped by developmental origin, disease etiology, disease stage and the metabolic and inflammatory tone of the renal microenvironment. Single-cell and spatially resolved profiling has revealed tissue-resident, activated, dysfunctional, and senescent Treg states in the injured kidney, and has begun to define the renal Treg niche. Building on this evidence, we propose an etiology- and stage-stratified framework in which Tregs protect against acute injury, promote repair, or, under specific conditions, contribute to fibrotic remodeling. This framework rationalizes therapeutic targeting: cytokine and small-molecule Treg expansion (notably low-dose IL-2), Treg-compatible optimization of conventional immunosuppression, adoptive polyclonal and antigen-specific CAR/TCR-Treg therapies, and metabolic or tissue-targeted engineering should be matched to disease etiology and stage. Integrating spatial multi-omics, lineage-stabilizing strategies, and standardized manufacturing and monitoring will be essential to translate Treg-based therapies into precision treatments for kidney diseases.

articles.title: Beyond clinical remission in rheumatoid arthritis: Lessons from hematology and gastroenterology.
articles.abstract: Treat-to-target strategies have substantially improved outcomes in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), yet current remission definitions rely largely on clinical composite criteria and may not fully reflect underlying inflammatory activity. Deep remission is not new in RA, and previous studies have used the term to describe increasingly stringent clinical, imaging, or immunological states. However, these definitions remain heterogeneous, and the clinical significance and actionability of remission depth remain uncertain. Drawing on lessons from chronic myeloid leukemia and inflammatory bowel disease, we reappraise deep remission in RA as a multidimensional concept rather than a new hierarchical treatment target. Clinical remission remains the established treatment target, while imaging and immunological assessments may provide complementary information on residual disease activity. Negative imaging-guided strategy trials do not support treatment escalation solely to achieve imaging normalization, but leave open whether objective phenotyping beyond clinical remission offers broader prognostic and clinical value. We synthesize evidence on whether deep remission assessments provide incremental prognostic or clinically actionable information for structural progression, remission durability, treatment tapering or withdrawal, sustained drug-free remission in selected patients, and cardiovascular outcomes. Deep remission may therefore serve as an aspirational direction for RA care, not as a mandate to normalize every residual abnormality, but as a broader goal of achieving durable, biology-informed control, with the potential to support safer treatment de-escalation in selected patients.

articles.title: Beyond Coronary Artery Disease: Etiologies and Outcomes of the Shark-Fin ECG Pattern: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The shark-fin sign (SFS) is a rare, high-risk electrocardiographic pattern reported in commonly linked with obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD).

OBJECTIVE: To characterize the electrocardiographic patterns, etiologies, and clinical outcomes associated with the SFS.

METHODS: We systematically reviewed PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, and Cochrane from inception through May 20, 2026, including all studies with participant-level data.

RESULTS: Eighty-five papers involving 104 patients were included; 66.3% had non-obstructive etiologies. The obstructive CAD patients were predominantly male (97.1%), while other etiologies were predominantly female (60.8%). Among CAD cases, the left main coronary artery (LMCA)/proximal left anterior descending artery (LAD) was the culprit in 75.0%, and SFS localization matched coronary anatomy in 91.4%. VT/VF and death each occurred in 37.1%, with adverse outcomes confined to those with LMCA/LAD lesions. Among other etiologies, Takotsubo syndrome (TTS, 31.7%), vasospasm (14.4%), myocarditis (6.7 %) and neurologic emergencies (4.8%) were the most frequently reported. VT/VF occurred in 43.4% and 27.5% died. Among patients with TTS, 63.6% experienced VT/VF or death, compared with ventricular arrhythmias in 66% of patients with vasospasm.

CONCLUSION: SFS is a high-risk ECG pattern rather than a diagnosis and warrants urgent etiologic evaluation and cardiac monitoring. Most published data are derived from patients without established CAD. LMCA/LAD disease, TTS, and coronary vasospasm were associated with particularly high-risk hospitalizations. Primary non-cardiac causes should also be considered when clinically suspected.

articles.title: Balloon perforation of a balloon-in-basket pulsed field ablation catheter during pulmonary vein isolation.
Comparative Clinical and Procedural Outcomes Among Three Pulsed Field Ablation Systems for Atrial Fibrillation: A Prospective Real-World Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulsed Field Ablation (PFA) is a non-thermal ablation technology for atrial fibrillation. Several PFA systems are available, with distinct catheter designs and energy delivery protocols. Direct comparisons between PFA systems remain limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study compared the procedural characteristics, safety, and efficacy of three contemporary PFA technologies in routine clinical practice.

METHODS: Consecutive patients undergoing their first pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) using the circular multielectrode array catheter (CMAC)(PulseSelectTM), the variable-loop circular catheter (VLCC)(VaripulseTM) or the lattice-tip catheter (LTC)(AfferaTM) were prospectively included. Freedom from any atrial arrhythmia (AA) was evaluated using 12-lead electrocardiography and 24-hour Holter at 3, 6 and 12 months, followed by routine clinical follow-up.

RESULTS: A total of 198 patients (CMAC:91, VLCC:50, LTC: 57) were included. Acute PVI was achieved in all patients (median age, 68 [61.0, 76.0] years; 127 male (64.1%); 97 paroxysmal (49.0%)). The procedure and ablation times were longest in the LTC group. During a mean follow-up of 352.4±207.2 days, the estimated 12-month freedom from AA recurrence beyond the 8-week blanking period was comparable among the CMAC, VLCC, and LTC groups (76.9%, 71.6%, and 78.8%; log-rank p=0.72). In adjusted multivariable Cox regression, PFA system choice was not associated with AA recurrence (LTC vs. CMAC: HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.39-1.52, p=0.45; VLCC vs. CMAC: HR 1.16, 95% CI 0.58-2.34, p=0.67). One major complication (0.51%, ischemic stroke (CMAC)) occurred.

CONCLUSION: In this prospective real-world study, PVI with the CMAC, VLCC, and LTC showed comparable efficacy and safety outcomes, while procedural profiles differed.

articles.title: Anticoagulation in Subclinical Atrial Fibrillation: An Evidence-Based Framework for Individualized Management.
articles.abstract: The increasing use of wearable monitoring technologies and cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) has led to frequent incidental detection of subclinical atrial fibrillation (SCAF), yet the role of long-term anticoagulation remains uncertain. Growing evidence indicates that SCAF is a separate clinical entity on the continuous spectrum of atrial disease and not just a precursor to clinical disease. We propose that anticoagulation in SCAF should be guided by integrating arrythmia burden, baseline clinical risk and the degree of structural atrial cardiomyopathy in addition to life expectancy and patient preferences. This review synthesizes data from observational studies, randomized clinical trials, and post-hoc analyses to provide a comprehensive and practical framework for individualized anticoagulation, and risk-benefit considerations.

articles.title: Pulsed Field or Cryoballoon Pulmonary Vein Isolation for Atrial Fibrillation in Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) frequently coexist, worsening prognosis. While catheter ablation confers clinical benefits in this high-risk population, comparative data between novel non-thermal pulsed field ablation (PFA) and established cryoballoon ablation (CBA) for AF-therapy in patients with HFrEF are limited.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the efficacy and safety of PFA- with CBA-based pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) in patients with AF and HFrEF (left ventricular ejection fraction ≤40%).

METHODS: This retrospective, international multicenter study included patients with HFrEF undergoing first-time PVI-only procedures between 2018 and 2025. Propensity-score matching (1:1 ratio) was applied to balance baseline characteristics. The primary efficacy endpoint was the first recurrence of any atrial tachyarrhythmia after a 3-month blanking period. Secondary measures included safety events and procedural efficiency.

RESULTS: A total of 700 patients from 12 German and Canadian centers were included, with 420 patients analyzed following propensity-score matching. At 12 months, freedom from atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence with PFA was comparable to CBA (Kaplan-Meier estimates, 65.0% vs. 67.8%; hazard ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.77 to 1.55; P=0.61). No statistically significant differences in observed safety outcomes were detected. PFA significantly improved procedural efficiency with shorter total procedure duration (58±22min vs. 72±22min; P<0.001), left-atrial dwell time (42±16min vs. 52±17min; P<0.001) and lower contrast dye use (0 ml [IQR 0-15] vs. 47 ml [IQR 30-56], P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with AF and HFrEF, PFA-based PVI achieves similar rhythm-control efficacy and safety compared with CBA, while significantly enhancing procedural efficiency.

articles.title: Longevitomics as the Science of the Longevitome: Towards a Unified Systems Science of Healthy Longevity.
articles.abstract: The twenty-first century has transformed longevity research through genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, microbiome science, digital phenotyping and artificial intelligence. Yet healthy longevity remains difficult to explain because its determinants are commonly studied as separate molecular layers, mechanisms or biomarkers. Here, we introduce Longevitomics as an integrative systems framework for understanding, modeling and predicting healthy longevity and define the Longevitome inspired by the Latin expression vita longa (long life) as the dynamic architecture of biological, environmental and behavioral determinants that collectively shape psychosomatic resilience across the life course. We position this proposal in relation to the Hallmarks of Aging, geroscience, biological-age biomarkers, multi-omics and systems medicine. Longevitomics is not intended to replace these established frameworks or to constitute another molecular "ome." Rather, it provides a systems-level framework in which mechanistic hallmarks, multi-omic layers, physiological phenotypes, exposures and adaptive responses can be integrated longitudinally. We further consider how network analysis, causal inference, machine learning and digital-twin approaches may enable reconstruction of individual Longevitome trajectories and support a transition toward predictive and personalized longevity medicine.

articles.title: Hepatic hydrothorax: Time to rethink the treatment paradigm?
From Phenotypes to Metabolotypes: Redefining Small Intestinal Overgrowth Syndromes through the Lens of Microbial Metabolic Signaling and Durable Disease Management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: First described half a century ago as a well-circumscribed malabsorption syndrome in patients with obvious anatomical abnormalities, small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) has evolved into an overused umbrella diagnosis that is used to explain almost any gastrointestinal symptom. This shift has been driven by the widespread availability of breath testing and has resulted in substantial overdiagnosis, inappropriate antibiotic use, and a disconnect between clinical practice and the underlying pathophysiology.

AIM: This review aims to synthesize clinical phenotypic heterogeneity with underlying metabolic signaling networks, thereby proposing a unified framework that reframes SIBO from a purely bacteriological construct to a metabolome-driven signaling disorder.

KEY FINDINGS: Recent evidence has reshaped the clinical landscape into three distinct phenotypes-hydrogen-predominant SIBO, methane-predominant intestinal methanogen overgrowth (IMO), and sulfide-associated intestinal sulfide overproduction (ISO)-each characterized by unique microbial compositions, symptom profiles, and treatment responses. However, gas-based phenotyping captures only the tip of the pathophysiological iceberg. Emerging multi-omics data reveal that underlying metabolic reprogramming-including bile acid remodeling, tryptophan-kynurenine (KYN) pathway dysregulation, and ectopic short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production-defines an endotype that shapes long-term disease trajectories and the spectrum of affected organs, thereby linking SIBO to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), neuropsychiatric disorders, and systemic inflammation.

CONCLUSION: We introduce Small Intestinal Metabolic Overgrowth Syndrome (SIMOS) as the SIBO 2.0 framework, reorienting the therapeutic paradigm from bactericidal eradication toward the restoration of a healthy small intestinal metabolic signaling network-achieved through integrated multimodal strategies comprising antibiotics, prokinetics, dietary interventions, and metabolic modulators.

articles.title: Frailty in older adults hospitalized for decompensated heart failure: prevalence, multidomain assessment and prognostic value.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty is a condition that affects prognosis and quality of life. It is not typically included in the routine assessment on admission for decompensated heart failure (dHF). Our objective was to determine its prevalence and prognosis in people admitted for dHF, with different scales of physical frailty and to evaluate its presence in its other domains.

METHODS: This prospective study analyzed individuals >65 years admitted for dHF grouped according to Fried phenotype. Prevalence and prognosis (mortality or readmission at 1 year) were calculated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression models.

RESULTS: A total of 228 patients were included (mean age 80.8+7.7 years, 52.2% women). Of them, 0.9% were robust, 16.6% were prefrail, and 82.5% were frail. Frail patients were significantly older and more were female (p < 0.001). They had a high prevalence of comorbidity, physical frailty, and nutritional impairment; moderate cognitive impairment; poor quality of life; high fall risk; and a low level of autonomy. During follow-up, 27.2% died and 56.4% were readmitted for dHF. Survival was significantly lower among patients with frailty determined by physical assessment scales and accumulation of deficits (p < 0.001). They had a significantly worse prognosis according to the Fried (HR 1.70, 95%CI 1.03-2.79) and FRAIL (HR 1.48, 95%CI 1.02-2.14) scales.

CONCLUSIONS: Frailty is highly prevalent among individuals admitted for dHF, particularly in the clinical, functional, and psycho-cognitive domains. Despite a multidomain assessment, prognostic value was mainly driven by physical frailty scales. It is necessary to integrate the interdisciplinary assessment of frailty into routine clinical practice.

articles.title: Atherogenic lipoprotein heterogeneity beyond LDL-C in coronary heart disease: small dense LDL cholesterol and an internally validated nomogram.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) reflects the total cholesterol content of LDL particles but does not fully capture particle composition. Small dense LDL cholesterol (sdLDL-C) may provide complementary information on atherogenic lipoprotein heterogeneity beyond conventional LDL-C.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective case-control study included 22,073 hospitalized adults, comprising 17,631 patients with CHD and 4442 non-CHD controls. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, ROC analysis, lower-LDL-C analysis, and LDL-C-sdLDL-C discordance analysis were performed. Associations were additionally examined after adjustment for triglycerides (TG) and non-HDL-C, and large buoyant LDL cholesterol (lbLDL-C) was evaluated. An sdLDL-C-based nomogram was subsequently developed and internally validated.

RESULTS: Patients with CHD had higher sdLDL-C, sdLDL-C/LDL-C ratios, TG, and non-HDL-C, but lower lbLDL-C, whereas between-group differences in LDL-C were small. In Model 3, which included TG, non-HDL-C, and LDL-C, each 1-SD increase in sdLDL-C and the sdLDL-C/LDL-C ratio was associated with higher odds of prevalent CHD (OR 2.37, 95% CI 2.26-2.49, and OR 3.52, 95% CI 3.28-3.76, respectively). lbLDL-C showed an inverse association in its adjusted model (OR 0.39, 95% CI 0.37-0.42). Associations of sdLDL-C and the ratio remained evident among participants with LDL-C < 2.60 mmol/L; those with low LDL-C but high sdLDL-C had higher odds of CHD (OR 6.01, 95% CI 5.29-6.82). Adding sdLDL-C or the ratio to the traditional lipid model increased the apparent AUROC from 0.8159 to 0.8565 or 0.8627, respectively. The eight-variable nomogram achieved a bootstrap-corrected AUROC of 0.879 with a calibration slope of 0.998.

CONCLUSION: sdLDL-C captures atherogenic lipoprotein heterogeneity not fully reflected by LDL-C, with associations persisting after adjustment for TG and non-HDL-C and among participants with lower LDL-C or discordant lipid phenotypes. The sdLDL-C-based nomogram showed good internal discrimination and calibration, although external validation is required.

articles.title: Rationale and Design of the BradycArdia paCemaKer with AV interval modulation for Blood prEssure treAtmenT (BACKBEAT) Pivotal Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrioventricular interval modulation (AVIM) is a novel pacing algorithm incorporated into a dual-chamber cardiac pacemaker that enables treatment of hypertension while simultaneously treating bradyarrhythmias. Prior clinical studies have shown that AVIM reduces 24-hour ambulatory systolic blood pressure (aSBP). The BACKBEAT (BradycArdia paCemaKer with AV interval modulation for Blood prEssure treAtmenT) pivotal trial is designed toassess the safety and efficacy of AVIM in a prospective, randomized controlled trial.

STUDY DESIGN AND OBJECTIVE: BACKBEAT is a global, multicenter, prospective, randomized, double-blinded clinical trial enrolling approximately 316 subjects across up to 130 sites. Eligible participants include patients implanted with, or scheduled to be implanted with, a dual-chamber pacemaker who have uncontrolled hypertension, defined as office systolic blood pressure (oSBP) ≥135 mmHg and aSBP ≥130 mmHg despite stable medical therapy. All eligible subjects will receive AVIM therapy RAMware downloaded to their device and will be randomized to active treatment (AVIM ON) or control (AVIM OFF), in addition to continued medical therapy. The primary efficacy endpoint is the between-group difference in the change of mean 24-hour aSBP from baseline to 3 months post-randomization. The primary safety endpoint is the proportion of subjects in the treatment group free from unanticipated serious adverse device effects at 3 months. Blinding will continue through 12 months to assess longer-term outcomes. At the end of the 12-month blinded phase, subjects may cross over to the alternate group before entering a 2-year follow-up phase.

CONCLUSION: BACKBEAT will provide rigorous evidence regarding the safety and efficacy of AVIM therapy for hypertension in patients with a dual-chamber pacemaker.

articles.title: Natural history and pancreatic cancer risk in PRSS1-associated hereditary pancreatitis: a nationwide cohort.
articles.journal: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hereditary pancreatitis caused by pathogenic variants in the cationic trypsinogen gene is associated with early pancreatic injury and increased pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma risk, but current estimates rely on small historical cohorts. We reassessed the natural history, penetrance, and long-term cancer risk in a nationwide genetically confirmed cohort.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective nationwide cohort study including individuals identified with PRSS1 variants associated with hereditary pancreatitis in France between 1996 and 2025 through the three national reference laboratories. Among 718 identified carriers, 455 had available follow-up. Clinical data were collected using a standardized electronic case report form. Outcomes included pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, diabetes mellitus, and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Standardized incidence and mortality ratios were calculated using national population data.

RESULTS: Median age at symptom onset was 12.5 years (interquartile range, 6.8-24.3), and overall penetrance was 77.6%.
