The cumulative risk of pancreatic exocrine insufficiency reached 27.5% (95% CI, 22.5-32.5) at age 50 years and 36.2% (95% CI, 30.2-42.2) at age 60 years; corresponding estimates for diabetes mellitus were 20.4% (95% CI, 15.2-25.5) and 27.2% (95% CI, 21.1-33.4), respectively. Twenty-two individuals developed pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma at a median age of 63.8 years (interquartile range, 52.3-73.6), with cumulative risk by ages 50 and 60 years of 2.0% (95% CI, 0.2-3.9) and 5.9% (95% CI, 2.3-9.6), respectively. The age- and sex-adjusted standardized incidence ratio for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma was 32.2 (95% CI, 19.4-50.3). Diabetes mellitus was independently associated with an increased risk of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (hazard ratio, 6.8; 95% CI, 2.1-21.2). Overall mortality was higher than in the general population (standardized mortality ratio, 3.2; 95% CI, 2.4-4.3).

CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide cohort with nearly three decades of follow-up, PRSS1-associated hereditary pancreatitis showed high penetrance, early pancreatic insufficiency, and markedly increased pancreatic cancer risk. These findings support lifelong follow-up and pancreatic cancer surveillance strategies that account for increasing risk with age and substantial interindividual variability in age at diagnosis.

articles.title: TIPS for refractory hepatic hydrothorax in patients with cirrhosis: impact of clinical response on survival.
authors: “TIPS for refractory hydrothorax in cirrhosis” study investigators team
articles.journal: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Refractory hydrothorax (RH) significantly impairs quality of life and clinical outcomes in patients with cirrhosis. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) has been suggested as a potential treatment, but evidence is limited. We assessed TIPS effectiveness and impact on survival in patients with RH.

METHODS: Consecutive patients with cirrhosis undergoing TIPS for RH over a 16-year period across 18 European centers were included. Clinical response was assessed up to 12 months after TIPS and was classified as complete (CR: disappearance of symptoms and no further thoracenteses), partial (PR: decrease of symptoms and ≥50% reduction of thoracenteses) or no response (NR: minor or no relief in symptoms and <50% reduction or same/increased number of thoracenteses).

RESULTS: Overall, 147 patients were included. TIPS achieved CR in 88 patients (60%). Mortality rates were 1.54, 5.34, and 11.4 deaths per 100 patient-months in patients with CR, PR, and NR, respectively. Time-dependent cause-specific Cox models showed a significant lower risk of death in CR patients compared with both those with PR (HR = 0.33, 95% CI 0.15-0.73; p = 0.006) and NR (HR = 0.15, 95% CI 0.06-0.37; p < 0.001). At multivariable analysis, CR remained independently associated with improved survival (HR = 0.30, 95% CI 0.14-0.64; p = 0.002).

CONCLUSION: Among patients with cirrhosis and RH selected to undergo TIPS, clinical CR was achieved in a substantial proportion and was independently associated with improved survival.

articles.title: Oral Anticoagulant Choice Across Indications in Cirrhosis: A US Nationwide Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Comparative data on oral anticoagulant safety and efficacy across indications in cirrhosis remain limited. We compared outcomes following direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) versus warfarin initiation in a nationwide US cohort.

METHODS: The primary cohort (Epic Cosmos; 2019-2024) compared propensity score-matched DOAC and warfarin initiators across atrial fibrillation (AF), deep vein thrombosis with or without pulmonary embolism (DVT/PE), and portal vein thrombosis (PVT). Competing-risk regression models evaluated death, liver transplantation (LT), and hemorrhagic and ischemic outcomes. An ancillary cohort (US transplant registry-Medicare linkage; 2021-2022) evaluated INR-driven MELD inflation as a mediator among waitlisted patients.

RESULTS: Among 93,663 initiators in the primary cohort, DOAC versus warfarin initiation in AF was associated with similar mortality and LT rates but lower overall major bleeding and non-gastrointestinal bleeding, including intracranial hemorrhage. In DVT/PE and PVT, DOAC versus warfarin initiation was associated with higher mortality (DVT/PE: sHR 1.21 [95%CI 1.10-1.34]; PVT: sHR 1.43 [1.24-1.65]) and markedly lower LT rates (DVT/PE: sHR 0.25 [0.17-0.38]; PVT: sHR 0.23 [0.17-0.32]); gastrointestinal bleeding was higher with DOACs than warfarin in PVT (sHR 1.26 [1.06-1.50]). Multiple sensitivity analyses corroborated these findings. In the ancillary cohort (n=284), warfarin-associated INR elevation partially mediated LT access differences (percentage mediated: 29%).

CONCLUSIONS: In cirrhosis, DOAC versus warfarin initiation was associated with similar mortality but favorable bleeding outcomes in AF. However, in venous thrombosis, DOAC initiators had higher mortality and lower LT access than warfarin initiators; warfarin-related INR inflation partly explained LT disparities. These findings support indication-specific treatment and reconsideration of INR handling in the US LT allocation system amid increasing DOAC use.

articles.title: Sedating Medications and the Risk of Falls, Hospitalizations, and Hepatic Encephalopathy in Cirrhosis: A Prospective Cohort.
articles.journal: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sedating medications are risky, overused, and may be a modifiable risk factor for adverse events in the general population. Prospective data on the impact of sedating medications in patients with cirrhosis are lacking.

METHODS: In a prospective multicenter cohort, we evaluated associations between sedating medications (gabapentinoids, TCAs, benzodiazepines, anticholinergics, non-benzodiazepine hypnotics, antipsychotics, and opioids), anti-hypertensives, diuretics, and nonselective beta-blockers (NSBBs) with falls, hospitalization, overt hepatic encephalopathy (HE), and death or transplantation. Death and transplantation were treated as competing risks in time-updated Fine-Gray models adjusting for age and sex, MELD-Na and Child class or albumin.

RESULTS: Among 230 participants (mean age 61.8, 60% female, mean MELD-Na 9.9), 40% of patients were on any sedating medications at baseline. The cumulative incidence of falls, hospitalizations, overt HE, and death or transplantation by week 72 were 34%, 35%, 5%, and 9%, respectively. Across adjusted Fine-Gray models, each additional sedating medication was associated with a 30-34% higher hazard of falls (sHR 1.30-1.34) and a 40-48% higher hazard of hospitalization (sHR 1.40-1.48, significant in all adjustment sets); the association with overt HE reached significance only after adjustment for MELD-Na and Child-Pugh class (sHR 1.93, 95% CI 1.03-3.63). Use of ≥2 sedating medications approximately doubled the hazard of falls (sHR 1.86-1.95) and hospitalization (sHR 2.00-2.17) across all adjustment sets. Neither NSBBs nor diuretics were associated with falls or hospitalization CONCLUSION: Sedating medications were associated with increased risk of falls, hospitalization, and overt HE in cirrhosis. Trials of medication review and deprescribing are warranted.

articles.title: Porcine beta defensin 2 alleviates inflammatory responses and oxidative stress induced by enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli K88 associated with the NF-κB/MAPK and Akt/Nrf2 signaling pathways in IPEC-J2 cells.
articles.abstract: Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC) is a major pathogen that causes diarrhea in humans and animals worldwide. Porcine beta defensin 2 (pBD2) is one of the antimicrobial peptides secreted by pigs, exhibiting broad antimicrobial and immunomodulatory activities. However, the effects and underlying mechanisms of pBD2 against ETEC infection remain poorly understood. In this study, porcine intestinal epithelial cells (IPEC-J2) were pretreated with pBD2 before ETEC K88 challenge. The results showed that pBD2 significantly inhibited the ETEC-induced inflammatory responses, as evidenced by the downregulation of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1α, TNF-α, IL-6 and IL-8) and chemokines (Cxcl2 and Ccl20) by 1.76- to 11.04-fold and 1.80- to 4.06-fold at the mRNA and protein levels, respectively (P < 0.05). Concomitantly, pBD2 alleviated oxidative stress, characterized by decreased reactive oxygen species (ROS) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels by 1.93- and 1.27-fold, alongside upregulation of antioxidant enzymes SOD1 and CAT by 5.03- and 3.35- fold (P < 0.05). Mechanistically, pBD2 inhibited the NF-κB/MAPK and modulated Akt/Nrf2 signaling pathways, with fold changes ranging from 1.23- to 3.12-fold (P < 0.05). Furthermore, these anti-inflammatory and antioxidant protective effects were associated with the NF-κB/MAPK and Akt/Nrf2 signaling pathways, as well as the functional interplay between them, as revealed by pharmacological inhibitor assays. Collectively, our findings elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying the protective effects of pBD2 against ETEC infection and provides a theoretical foundation for its potential application as an antimicrobial alternative.

articles.title: Dual roles of MrBeclin1 in autophagy-related gene regulation and antibacterial activity in the giant freshwater prawn Macrobrachium rosenbergii.
articles.abstract: Beclin1 is a multifunctional protein involved in autophagy regulation and antimicrobial defense, yet its roles in the giant freshwater prawn Macrobrachium rosenbergii remain unclear. Here, we cloned and characterized MrBeclin1, which contains a conserved APG6 domain, clusters within the crustacean clade, and is predominantly expressed in hemocytes, with significant upregulation in hepatopancreas and gills upon Aeromonas hydrophila or LPS challenge. Subcellular localization suggested its cytoplasmic distribution. Silencing of MrBeclin1 led to altered expression of autophagy-related genes, reduced antioxidant enzyme activities, elevated lipid peroxidation, and exacerbated histopathological damage following bacterial infection. Furthermore, recombinant MrBeclin1 protein (rMrBeclin1) reduced the growth of A. hydrophila and Citrobacter freundii under the tested in vitro conditions. Overall, these findings indicate that MrBeclin1 participates in the regulation of autophagy-related gene expression and antioxidant defense and exhibits antibacterial activity. This study provides insights into the autophagy-antioxidant immune axis in crustacean innate immunity and a potential molecular target for disease management in M. rosenbergii aquaculture.

articles.title: Prenatal melatonin regulates lung prostanoids expression in newborn sheep exposed to chronic hypoxia.
articles.abstract: Chronic hypoxia during pregnancy disrupts the balance of pulmonary vasoactive agents, altering prostanoid signaling and increasing the contractility of resistance arteries. This leads to elevated pulmonary arterial pressure and vascular resistance, ultimately resulting in pulmonary hypertension of the neonate (PHN). While prenatal melatonin is known to influence vascular tone, its specific impact on the neonatal pulmonary prostanoid system in hypoxic pregnancies remains unclear. This study aimed to determine the effects of third-trimester maternal melatonin administration on the cyclooxygenase and prostanoid pathways, and to evaluate its efficacy in reversing PHN in a high-altitude ovine model. In-vivo and ex-vivo pulmonary vascular function was evaluated in neonatal lambs gestated and born under chronic hypoxia. Furthermore, lung samples from 12-day-old lambs were analyzed using RT-PCR, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. The results demonstrate that prenatal melatonin actively modulates the pulmonary vascular function, and the prostanoids system, altering both the transcriptional and translational expression of specific prostanoids, as well as their spatial localization within pulmonary resistance arteries. However, despite this significant molecular and structural modulation, maternal melatonin treatment failed to reverse or clinically improve PHN in the offspring. These findings highlight the complexity of hypoxia-induced vascular remodeling and suggest that melatonin-driven prostanoid modulation alone is insufficient to overcome PHN, although it can improve some pulmonary function in neonates.

articles.title: Fatty acid profile, atherogenic indices, and cardiac biomarkers in older adults with acute myocardial infarction: Associations with angiographic coronary disease severity.
articles.abstract: This case-control study investigated the relationships between circulating fatty acid (FA) profiles, atherogenic indices, cardiac biomarkers, and coronary artery disease (CAD) severity in acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Plasma FA profile were quantified using gas chromatography in 314 patients with AMI and 422 controls aged ≥60 years. Compared with controls, patients had higher total saturated, monounsaturated, and polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA), including total omega-3 and omega-6 PUFA, whereas linoleic acid and the omega-6/omega-3 ratio were lower. All four atherogenic indices, Castelli risk index-I (CRI-I), CRI-II, atherogenic coefficient, and atherogenic index of plasma (AIP),were independently associated with AMI, with adjusted odds ratios of 1.98, 32.94, 4.00, and 1.79, respectively. Total omega-3 PUFA and CRI-II demonstrated high discriminatory performance, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.904 and 0.910, respectively. Among patients with AMI, total omega-6 PUFA were highest in four-vessel disease, whereas atherogenic indices did not increase consistently with the number of affected vessels. Critical stenosis was associated with higher total saturated fatty acids, palmitic acid, arachidonic acid, and delta-5 desaturase index, alongside lower docosatetraenoic acid and omega-6 elongation index. Multivariable models revealed a novel, independent inverse correlation between AIP and serum angiotensin-converting enzyme activity (partial ρ = -0.169, q = 0.030), whereas CRI-II correlated positively with cardiac troponin I (partial ρ = 0.163, q = 0.038). These findings highlight the interest to introduce FA profiling and atherogenic indices for the biochemical characterization of AMI. Prospective studies are needed to validate these associations and their incremental value for cardiovascular risk stratification.

articles.title: Preoperative Opioid Use Predicts Socioeconomic Vulnerability and Worse Recovery in Elective Total Joint Arthroplasty.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Preoperative opioid prescription may be associated with postoperative outcomes after total joint arthroplasty (TJA). We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients who underwent primary TJA to assess associations between an active preoperative opioid prescription and 90-day complications, lengths of stay (LOS), discharge disposition, one-year patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), and socioeconomic vulnerability.

METHODS: We identified 10,679 patients who underwent primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) or total knee arthroplasty (TKA) from 2018 to 2023. Preoperative opioid use was defined as an active opioid prescription within one month before surgery. This prescription-based definition served as a proxy for opioid exposure and did not confirm that prescriptions were filled or consumed. Outcomes included 90-day complications, LOS, discharge disposition, attainment of substantial clinical benefit (SCB) on PROMs collected from 2021 to 2023, and social vulnerability measured by the Social Vulnerability Index (SVI). Univariate analyses were used to identify candidate variables for multivariable logistic and negative binomial regression models.

RESULTS: Preoperative opioid prescription was identified in 3,935 patients (36.8%). Higher social vulnerability was independently associated with preoperative opioid prescription. In TKA, opioid prescription was independently associated with non-home discharge (odds ratio [OR] 2.07), pulmonary embolism (OR 3.47), longer length of stay (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 1.24), longer procedure duration (IRR 1.05), smaller improvements in the Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score for Joint Replacement (adjusted mean difference -2.44), and lower odds of SCB (OR 0.72). In THA, opioid prescription was independently associated with return to the operating room (OR 6.68), periprosthetic joint infection (OR 3.07), and longer postoperative stay (IRR 1.25).

CONCLUSION: Preoperative opioid prescription was common and was associated with worse outcomes in this TJA cohort. Patients who had a preoperative opioid prescription experienced longer LOS, more frequent non-home discharge, and reduced functional improvement after TKA. Opioid prescription was also correlated with greater socioeconomic vulnerability. Because no intervention was evaluated, these findings identify preoperative opioid prescription and socioeconomic vulnerability as markers of a higher-risk group rather than demonstrating that addressing either one reduces risk.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of the Preoperative Pan-Immune-Inflammation Value for Adverse Outcomes After Hip Arthroplasty for Femoral Neck Fracture: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The pan-immune-inflammation value (PIV) is an emerging systemic inflammatory biomarker, but its prognostic value in patients undergoing hip arthroplasty for femoral neck fracture remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association between preoperative PIV and postoperative adverse outcomes.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included older adults who have femoral neck fractures undergoing hip arthroplasty between June 2024 and May 2026. Preoperative PIV was calculated from routine complete blood count parameters. Multivariable logistic regressions, receiver operating characteristic curve analyses, DeLong tests, restricted cubic spline analyses, and bootstrap validations were performed to evaluate the predictive value of PIV. Nomograms integrating PIV with clinical variables were developed.

RESULTS: Among 594 patients, 38 (6.4%) had postoperative intensive care unit (ICU) admission and 67 (11.3%) developed pulmonary infection. High PIV was independently associated with ICU admission (odds ratio [OR], 6.551; 95% confidence interval [CI], 3.022 to 14.203; P < 0.001) and pulmonary infection (OR, 3.995; 95% CI, 2.202 to 7.248; P < 0.001). Preoperative PIV showed good discrimination for ICU admission (area under the curve [AUC], 0.860; 95% CI, 0.793 to 0.928) and moderate discrimination for pulmonary infection (AUC, 0.690; 95% CI, 0.612 to 0.768). Adding PIV to clinical models improved discrimination for ICU admission (AUC, 0.928) and pulmonary infection (AUC, 0.842).

CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative PIV is independently associated with postoperative ICU admission and pulmonary infection after hip arthroplasty for femoral neck fracture. As a simple and cost-effective biomarker, PIV may facilitate perioperative risk stratification and early identification of high-risk patients.

articles.title: Theraphosid (Tarantula) Bite Envenomation in Humans: A Systematic Review of the Reported Epidemiology.
articles.journal: Toxicon : official journal of the International Society on Toxinology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite the ubiquity of Theraphosidae (tarantulas) in the pet trade, the clinical literature on theraphosid envenomation is heterogeneous, geographically uneven, dominated by selective self-report, and frequently obscured by taxonomic misidentification.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE and supplementary sources were screened against pre-specified criteria for published reports of human theraphosid bites (PRISMA).

RESULTS: Forty-two reports (1889-2026) entered the primary synthesis: 39 were localizable to 17 countries, one did not state the bite country, and two were international hobbyist compilations. Reporting concentrated in South Asia, in captive-keeper bites in Europe and North America, and in Australia. Among Old World species (native to Africa, Asia, and Australasia), African, South Asian, and Southeast Asian lineages were repeatedly associated with intense local pain, delayed generalized muscle cramping, creatine kinase elevation, and, rarely, transient atrial fibrillation, whereas Australian bites caused severe local pain without cramping. New World bites (species native to the Americas) predominantly produced minor local effects, with rare systemic exceptions (suspected anaphylaxis, prolonged cramping, thrombocytopenia). Only 8 of 42 reports had identification by a named arachnologist, zoologist, or institutional laboratory. No validated antivenom and no death attributable to a verified Theraphosidae bite were identified; two deaths attributed to the genus Chilobrachys in a 1997 Indian report lack documented taxonomic and causal confirmation.

CONCLUSIONS: Most reported theraphosid bites were minor, but the literature cannot estimate population-level risk without defined denominators. Some Old World bites were high-acuity events, and the literature has emphasized less heterogeneity in Old World envenomations than exists. Priorities include standardized species identification, prospective registries, and consistent severity reporting.

articles.title: Characteristics and Outcomes of Patients with Atrial Fibrillation Undergoing Peripheral Vascular Interventions.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Atrial fibrillation (Afib) is a common dysrhythmia in patients with peripheral arterial disease (PAD) and can alter antithrombotic management. However, the characteristics and outcomes of patients with Afib undergoing peripheral vascular interventions (PVI) is not well characterized.

METHODS: The Vascular Quality Initiative registry for PVI (2011-2024) was reviewed. The characteristics of patients with Afib were compared to patients without Afib. Perioperative and long-term outcomes were compared including reintervention, major amputation, mortality, and the composite outcome of MALE or mortality (MALE = reintervention or amputation), stratified by indication. Regression analysis was used to determine the independent association of Afib with outcomes.

RESULTS: There were 118,095 patients analyzed (14% with Afib). Patients with Afib were older, more often male, white, and less likely to have history of smoking. Compared with patients without Afib, patients with Afib had higher comorbidities including cerebrovascular disease, coronary artery disease, congestive heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, diabetes mellitus, and hypertension (P<0.001). Preoperatively, Afib patients were more likely to be on anticoagulants (63% vs. 11%; P<0.001), whereas patients without Afib were more likely to be on antiplatelets (80% vs. 68%; P<0.001). Afib patients were more likely to be treated for CLTI (70% vs. 57%; P<0.001). Postoperatively, patients with Afib had significantly higher rates of 30-day mortality in both the claudication (1.0% vs. 0.3%; P<0.001) and CLTI subgroups (4.1% vs. 1.5%; P<0.001). Logistic regression showed that Afib was independently associated with higher odds of 30-day mortality in CLTI (odds ratio = 1.55 [95% CI, 1.33-1.80]; P<0.001). At 18-month follow-up, patients with Afib had significantly higher rates of mortality for claudication (16% vs. 7%; P<0.001, adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) = 1.28 [95% CI, 1.16-1.42]; P<0.001) and CLTI subgroups (40% vs. 22%; P<0.001, aHR = 1.28 [1.23-1.34]; P<0.001). Among patients with CLTI, the composite outcome (MALE or mortality) was significantly higher in patients with Afib (33% vs. 30%; P<0.001), with a trend toward higher risk after adjustment (HR = 1.05 [95% CI, 0.99-1.12]; P=0.094), whereas rates were similar in claudication (14% vs. 15%; P=0.78).

CONCLUSION: Patients with Afib undergoing PVI present with a higher burden of comorbidities, have different antithrombotic medications, and are more likely to be treated for CLTI compared to patients without Afib. Afib was independently associated with a significant increase in perioperative and long-term mortality but did not seem to be associated with limb outcomes.

articles.title: Hybrid Revascularization of Chronic Vertebral Artery Occlusion: A Morphology-Based Classification, Novel Collateral-Channel Techniques, and Mid-Term Patency in a Single-Center Series of 26 Procedures.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic vertebral artery (VA) occlusion encompasses heterogeneous morphologies-de novo atherosclerotic occlusion, in-stent restenosis (ISR), and in-stent occlusion (ISO)-for which no classification-guided revascularization strategy exists. We report the largest single-center series of hybrid revascularization combining VA endarterectomy (VEA) with endovascular techniques, propose a morphology-based classification, and provide the first mid-term patency analysis.

METHODS: Twenty-six consecutive hybrid revascularization procedures performed in 25 patients with chronic VA occlusion between January 2018 and March 2026 were retrospectively analyzed. Lesions were classified as Type I (de novo occlusion), Type II (post-stent ISR), or Type III (post-stent ISO), with a complexity modifier "C" denoting long-segment extension, tortuous/deep origin, or absence of a distal target. Technical success, periprocedural complications, and patency at last imaging follow-up were assessed.

RESULTS: Technical success was 88.5% (23/26) overall, declining across morphological types: 100% in Type I, 88.9% in Type II, and 71.4% in Type III. The C modifier strongly predicted failure (success 50.0% vs. 100% without C; P = 0.008). There was no periprocedural stroke or death; one major cardiac event (3.8%) occurred. At last follow-up (median 34 months; range, 3-96 months), 19 of 23 successfully recanalized arteries (82.6%) remained patent. Mid-term patency was 100% with adjunctive stenting versus 63.6% without (P = 0.037); both reocclusions and one of two restenoses followed stent explantation without re-scaffolding. Novel bailout techniques-VA transposition to the thyrocervical trunk and retrograde revascularization through the ascending cervical artery collateral-rescued three complex anatomies.

CONCLUSIONS: Hybrid revascularization is safe and effective for chronic VA occlusion, with outcomes that depend systematically on lesion morphology. The proposed Type I/II/III classification with the C modifier stratifies technical difficulty and guides strategy selection, while adjunctive stent scaffolding after endarterectomy appears critical for durable patency. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant prospective validation.

articles.title: Acute Zonal Occult Outer Retinopathy: Reappraising a Historical Clinical Concept in the Era of Multimodal Imaging.
articles.journal: Progress in retinal and eye research
articles.abstract: Acute zonal occult outer retinopathy (AZOOR) and the broader "AZOOR complex" have historically encompassed several disorders sharing acute visual symptoms and outer retinal dysfunction. Advances in multimodal imaging have revealed structural abnormalities in many of these presentations, challenging the original concept of an "occult" retinopathy without a visible anatomical correlate. We therefore revisit these concepts in light of modern imaging and current understanding of outer retinal disease. A systematic reassessment of 207 eligible published cases showed that 188 (90.8%) could be assigned a more specific contemporary diagnostic category based on the information available in the original reports. The most frequent assignments were multiple evanescent white dot syndrome (MEWDS), acute outer retinopathy (AOR), and multizonal outer retinopathy and retinal pigment epitheliopathy (MORR). These findings do not establish that the original diagnoses were incorrect or that each contemporary diagnosis represents a biologically independent disease, but show that many presentations historically grouped under AZOOR can now be characterized more specifically. We review the clinical features, multimodal imaging findings, natural history, and management of the principal retinal entities identified through this reassessment. We also examine inherited, toxic, autoimmune, paraneoplastic, post-infectious, and other disorders that may produce similar retinal appearances or provide the underlying clinical or etiological setting for these presentations. Rather than proposing a new disease classification, we suggest a pattern-based diagnostic approach in which OCT and fundus autofluorescence form the core imaging assessment, with additional imaging modalities selected according to the clinical presentation and differential diagnosis. Imaging is used to characterize the predominant pattern and anatomical level of retinal injury and, when possible, to identify a more specific retinal diagnosis; clinical history, systemic evaluation, laboratory testing, electrophysiology, and genetic testing can then guide further investigation of its etiological setting or identify a specific alternative diagnosis. This approach allows patients presenting within the broad clinical spectrum historically associated with AZOOR to be characterized at the most specific level supported by contemporary imaging, while recognizing that the biological relationships among these retinal entities remain incompletely understood.

articles.title: Deep learning-based estimation of multi-tracer PET phenotypes from structural MRI for A/T/N-related analysis and progression prediction in Alzheimer's disease.
articles.abstract: Early identification and staging of Alzheimer's disease (AD) require integrated assessment of amyloid deposition, tau pathology, and neurodegeneration. PET provides spatially resolved in vivo imaging biomarkers, but its routine use is constrained by cost, tracer availability, and radiation exposure, limiting access to complete A/T/N imaging profiles. We propose a conditional flow matching-based framework that estimates SUV-space PET-derived phenotypes related to 18F-FDG, 18F-florbetapir and 18F-flortaucipir from a single T1-weighted MRI scan. To address limitations in SUV-level quantitative fidelity, single-tracer applicability, and external generalization, the framework combines a PET prior network with a time-conditioned velocity network and uses multi-constraint losses to preserve SUV accuracy, regional uptake consistency, and anatomical boundaries. The model was developed using 1,978 paired ADNI MRI-PET records from 991 participants and evaluated in a predefined ADNI test set and an independent hospital PET/MR cohort of 514 participants. In ADNI, voxel-level MAEs were 0.012, 0.034, and 0.021 SUV, with representative ROI Pearson correlations of 0.978, 0.842, and 0.781. In the hospital cohort, corresponding MAEs were 0.014, 0.037, and 0.024 SUV, with ROI correlations of 0.952, 0.803, and 0.834. In OASIS, generated PET-derived features improved CDR stratification and future cognitive decline prediction, increasing AUCs from 0.662 to 0.739 and from 0.569 to 0.643. These findings suggest that the method can provide PET-derived phenotypes related to A/T/N analysis from structural MRI when PET is unavailable, but should not be interpreted as a replacement for molecular PET assessment.

articles.title: Interpregnancy interval and the risk of adverse perinatal outcomes of singleton pregnancies: a retrospective analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.abstract: This retrospective study analyzed 3,568,957 singleton live births from the US National Vital Statistics System (2021-2022) to evaluate adverse perinatal outcomes (preterm birth, low birth weight, small for gestational age) using interpregnancy interval (IPI) as a continuous variable. Departing from conventional categorical classifications, we treated IPI as a continuous monthly variable to precisely delineate the full risk trajectory. Spline smoothing and logistic regression revealed that an IPI of 20 months had the lowest risk. Compared to this nadir, IPI <6 months increased odds by 44% (adjusted odds ratio=1.44, 95% CI 1.40-1.48) and IPI >120 months increased odds by 74% (aOR=1.74, 95% CI 1.70-1.78). Risk and incidence charts were generated for IPI as a continuous measure, including subgroups by prior preterm birth or cesarean section. Our findings confirm that both short and long IPIs are associated with elevated perinatal risks, with 20 months emerging as the optimal interval for subsequent pregnancy planning. These continuous-risk charts offer an evidence-based, practical resource to enhance prenatal counseling and family education.

articles.title: Rational design and research progress of novel mitochondrial uncouplers.
articles.abstract: Mitochondrial uncouplers have been validated as effective therapeutic agents in preclinical models of metabolic dysfunction-associated diseases, including obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), cardiovascular diseases and tumors. In this review, we briefly summarize the biological functions and therapeutic potential of uncouplers, with a primary focus on advances in their chemical-structural optimization. We mainly recapitulate the design optimization strategies and developmental routes of representative scaffolds among protonophore‑type uncouplers, and analyze the design approaches for cutting‑edge protein‑dependent uncouplers. Finally, we provide a critical evaluation of the current dilemmas, research trends and future research directions in the field of uncouplers to provide meaningful references for future investigations.

articles.title: MicroRNA-mediated regulation of brown adipose tissue whitening: molecular mechanisms, pathophysiological implications, and therapeutic opportunities.
articles.abstract: Brown adipose tissue (BAT) is a specialized form of adipose tissue characterized by high mitochondrial density and elevated expression of uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1), which regulates energy homeostasis through non-shivering thermogenesis. Recent studies demonstrate that under pathological conditions such as obesity, aging, chronic inflammation, and metabolic syndrome, BAT gradually loses its thermogenic capacity and exhibits features including enlarged lipid droplets, reduced mitochondrial content, and downregulated thermogenic gene expression-a process termed BAT "whitening." This process is considered a critical pathological basis for obesity-related metabolic disorders. MicroRNAs (miRNAs)-non-coding RNAs approximately 18-24 nucleotides in length-regulate target gene expression at the post-transcriptional level and play pivotal roles in adipocyte differentiation, mitochondrial function, inflammatory responses, and energy metabolism. Accumulating evidence indicates that various miRNAs participate in BAT whitening, influencing brown adipocyte fate and thermogenic capacity by modulating signaling pathways involving PRDM16, PGC-1α, UCP1, AMPK, SIRT1, and TGF-β. This article systematically reviews recent research progress on miRNA-mediated regulation of BAT whitening, focusing on underlying mechanisms related to brown adipogenesis, mitochondrial homeostasis, the inflammatory microenvironment, and exosomal miRNA mediates intercellular communication. Furthermore, it explores the potential of miRNAs as diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets, aiming to provide a theoretical basis for precision interventions in obesity and related metabolic disorders.

articles.title: Impacts of ultra-processed food warning labels on product perceptions and behavioral intentions among Latino adults: A randomized trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ultra-processed foods (UPFs), defined as foods in group 4 of the NOVA classification system, are a key contributor to chronic disease in the United States. Front-of-package warning labels ("warnings") offer a promising strategy to help Americans identify UPFs, increase awareness of their negative health effects, and reduce consumption. However, the effects of UPF warnings, including among Latino adults, remain largely unknown.

STUDY DESIGN: Online randomized trial conducted in 2024.

SETTING/PARTICIPANTS: 4,107 Latino adults (49% limited English proficiency) in the US.

INTERVENTION: Participants viewed one of three labels: a control label displaying a barcode; an intervention identity warning label stating "WARNING: Ultra-processed food"; or an intervention health warning label stating "WARNING: Consuming ultra-processed food and drinks can cause weight gain, which increases the risk of obesity and type 2 diabetes".

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Participants viewed four UPF products each displaying their randomly assigned label. Participants indicated whether the product was UPF (primary outcome) and rated perceived healthfulness of the product, intentions to purchase the product, and perceived message effectiveness (secondary outcomes).

RESULTS: Identity warnings (70% correct) and health warnings (67% correct) led to higher correct identification of UPF than control labels (54%, p<.001), with the identity warning having a larger impact than the health warning (p=.007). Compared to the control label, the identity warning and health warning both elicited lower healthfulness perceptions and purchase intentions (p<.001 for all outcomes) and higher perceived message effectiveness with no significant differences between UPF labels. The impact of the health warning label (vs. the control label) on correct identification of UPF was greater for participants with high education (p=0.012) compared to those with low education, and for participants with limited English proficiency compared to high proficiency (p=0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: UPF warnings may help consumers identify UPFs and influence product perceptions and intentions.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT06296355.

articles.title: Association between antibiotic exposure and markers of disease severity in patients ultimately classified as having viral or non-infectious acute respiratory syndromes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate empirical antibiotic exposure among patients ultimately classified as having viral or non-infectious acute respiratory syndromes.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated consecutive adults hospitalized for acute respiratory syndromes. Final diagnoses were adjudicated as non-infectious, bacterial, viral, or coinfection. The primary analysis focused on patients ultimately classified as viral or non-infectious. Antibiotic exposure during hospitalization was compared according to clinical severity, inflammatory burden, imaging findings, and respiratory support.

RESULTS: A total of 442 patients were included. Final adjudication classified 54 patients as non-infectious, 53 as bacterial, 289 as viral, and 46 as coinfection. Among patients ultimately classified as viral or non-infectious with available antibiotic data, 104/329 patients (31.6%) received antibiotics during hospitalization. Antibiotic-exposed patients had higher NEWS2 scores, lower PaO₂/FiO₂ ratios, higher C-reactive protein and procalcitonin levels. Positive chest radiography findings were more frequent in antibiotic-exposed patients (71% vs 32%), as was escalation of oxygen support (65% vs 38%; p < 0.001 for both).

CONCLUSION: In patients ultimately classified as having viral or non-infectious acute respiratory syndromes, antibiotic exposure was common and appeared associated with physiological severity, inflammatory biomarkers, and radiological abnormalities. These findings support stewardship strategies that help clinicians reassess antibiotics once bacterial infection becomes less likely.

articles.title: Age-specific histological features of severe alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency-associated liver disease (Pi*ZZ genotype) ☆.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver disease in severe alpha-1 antitrypsin (AAT) deficiency (Pi*ZZ genotype) displays a biphasic pattern with peaks in early childhood and later adulthood. The aim was to compare the histological liver phenotype in children and adults with Pi*ZZ genotype.

METHODS: Specimens from 67 Pi*ZZ adults and 48 Pi*ZZ children from six European countries were independently scored by two histopathologists in a blinded fashion. Sequential multiplex immunofluorescence staining (COMET) quantified histological features in a representative adult and pediatric sample.

RESULTS: Pediatric Pi*ZZ samples originated more often from liver transplantation (64.6 vs. 21.2%, p < .001). Compared to adults, children presented a significantly higher fibrosis stage according to METAVIR (4.0 vs. 2.5, p < .001). Liver steatosis was somewhat more prevalent in Pi*ZZ adults, while bile plugs and duct paucity were significantly more common in Pi*ZZ children (bile plugs: 43.8 vs. 10.4%, p < .001; duct paucity 58.3 vs. 1.5%, p < .001) even when adjusted for fibrosis stage. Age-based assessment of pediatric cohort (6-17 years, 1-5 years, < 1 year) revealed that cirrhosis was more common in older age groups than in infants (64.7 vs. 75.0 vs. 30.8%). Youngest children displayed less AAT accumulation and less frequently had larger aggregates, while preschoolers had the highest liver injury markers. >70% of children received ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) and the treated children had a more pronounced fibrosis, cholestasis and duct paucity. Multiplex staining confirmed the loss of mature bile ducts while retaining hepatocyte zonation in pediatric vs adult.

CONCLUSION: Our study reveals unique histological patterns in Pi*ZZ children and adults. It provides basis for further mechanistic studies and may guide selection into clinical trials.

IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD) is an inherited disorder that predisposes to liver disease and can manifest in early childhood as well as late adulthood. Our work systematically compares a large international set of pediatric and adult liver specimen and demonstrates age-specific histological features. Our results should support patient counseling (i.e. in case of late diagnosis of pediatric disease) and management including selection of patients for clinical trials.

articles.title: Effect of two TM6SF2 variants on steatotic liver disease, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: While the TM6SF2 E167K variant is a known driver of steatotic liver disease, the impact of the rarer L156P variant and the cumulative effect of multiple TM6SF2 risk alleles remains undefined.

METHODS: We analyzed 393,742 individuals from the UK Biobank, 239,967 from All of Us, and 113,015 from a Copenhagen Cohort. We assessed MRI-measured proton density fat fraction (PDFF), plasma lipids, alanine transaminase (ALT), cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) as a function of TM6SF2 E167K and L156P genotype combinations. Finally, we tested the associations between other rare missense variants in TM6SF2 and PDFF.

RESULTS: In the UK Biobank, median PDFF increased from 3.0% in non-carriers (EE/LL) to 6.3% in E167K homozygotes (KK/LL), 9.3% in compound heterozygotes (EK/LP), and 20.3% in L156P homozygotes (EE/PP). Compared to non-carriers, cirrhosis risk increased stepwise to odds ratios (ORs) of 3.02 (95% CI: 2.05-4.26) in E167K homozygotes, 4.96 (3.03-7.62) in compound heterozygotes, peaking at 9.96 (2.42-27.1) in L156P homozygotes. A similar pattern was observed for HCC with ORs of 7.81 (5.03-11.55) in E167K homozygotes, 8.63 (4.28-15.4) in compound heterozygotes, and 10.12 (0.57-46.7) in L156P homozygotes. These ORs were mirrored by stepwise decreases in LDL cholesterol and triglycerides. Results were validated in All of Us and the Copenhagen Cohort. A broader screen identified three additional rare TM6SF2 missense variants associated with PDFF (A128V, P216L, and F336C).

CONCLUSIONS: TM6SF2 L156P was associated with increased hepatic fat content and increased risk of cirrhosis and HCC with effect sizes exceeding E167K. The high risk observed in compound heterozygotes suggests a cumulative loss-of-function effect.

IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Although the TM6SF2 E167K variant is a widely studied risk factor for steatotic liver disease (SLD), the clinical impact of the rarer L156P variant, and the combined effect of these two variants have remained uncharacterized. These findings are important for hepatologists, clinical geneticists, and pharmaceutical researchers, as they show that L156P confers an even higher risk of progressive liver disease than E167K, particularly in the homozygous or compound heterozygous states. Practically, these results can guide the design of multi-variant genetic screening panels and help clinicians identify and stratify high-risk patients for early, targeted cirrhosis and HCC surveillance; however, given the rarity of these genotypes and our cohorts' European ancestry, broad clinical guidelines must await further validation in larger, multi-ethnic cohorts.

articles.title: [Acceptability and professional practices of induced abortion between 14 and 16 gestational weeks in France].
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe practices, experiences, and acceptability of induced abortions between 14 and 16 gestational weeks in France.

METHODS: A national cross-sectional study was conducted using an anonymous online self-administered questionnaire from February to April 2025 among professionals involved in abortion care. The questionnaire explored socio-professional characteristics, legislative positions, practices, training, and experience with induced abortion at 14-16 weeks. Analyses included descriptive statistics, univariate comparisons, and multivariate logistic regression to identify factors associated with low comfort (≤ 6/10).

RESULTS: Among 949 opened questionnaires, 704 were analyzed. In 2025, 77 % of respondents supported extending the legal gestational limit. The 14-16 weeks abortion practice group (n = 326) consisted mainly of obstetrician-gynecologists (39.3 %), practicing in university hospitals (53.7 %). Forty-four percent performed exclusively surgical procedures, mainly by dilation and evacuation (60.2%), and 53.7 % performed these procedures less than once per month. Forty-two percent had received no specific training. The main difficulty was the burden of the procedure (30 %), and 15 % had ever felt pressured. Comfort scores were high (median: 8); being aged ≥ 45 years and having a favorable position toward the reform were associated with a lower risk of low comfort.

CONCLUSION: Despite high acceptability, induced abortion between 14 and 16 weeks remains rare, heterogeneous, and concentrated in university hospitals, in a context of insufficient training. Strengthening training could improve practice uniformity and access to care.

articles.title: Metabolic Unloading: How SGLT2i Recalibrate Cell Energetics to Slow CKD Progression.
articles.abstract: Kidney outcome trials demonstrate that sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors consistently slow chronic kidney disease progression; however, the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely defined, as benefits extend beyond glycemic control and hemodynamic effects across diabetic and non-diabetic chronic kidney disease. This review advances a unifying framework in which metabolic unloading of the proximal tubule contributes to renoprotection. The metabolic burden of solute reabsorption places the proximal tubule at the center of renal energetics, predisposing it to hypoxia, mitochondrial stress, and maladaptive injury responses. We synthesize evidence that these agents reduce adenosine triphosphate-dependent transport workload, oxygen consumption and may also reduce megalin-dependent endocytosis, with downstream effects on mitochondrial efficiency, redox balance, and autophagy/mitophagy supported by emerging preclinical data. By mitigating energetic stress, these agents divert tubular cell fate away from maladaptive hypertrophy and fibrosis toward adaptive repair. This framework integrates spatial cortex-medulla vulnerability, reconciles early hemodynamic changes with durable slowing of estimated glomerular filtration rate decline, and explores disease-agnostic benefit. We discuss translational implications including early initiation, identification of high workload phenotypes (hyperfiltration, recovery after acute kidney injury), and deployment of energetics associated biomarkers such as ketones, oxidative stress profiles, and estimated glomerular filtration rate slope. This review positions cellular energetics as an important upstream constraint shaping kidney disease progression, offering a foundation for nephroprotective strategies.

articles.title: From insulin resistance to neurovascular breakdown: mTOR signaling as a convergence point in Alzheimer's disease.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD), the leading cause of dementia, is increasingly recognized as a metabolic disorder characterized by disrupted insulin and insulin-like growth factor-1 signaling in the brain, a concept now referred to as type 3 diabetes. Central to this perspective is the insulin receptor substrate-1/phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B/mechanistic target of rapamycin (IRS-1/PI3K/Akt/mTOR) cascade, which acts as the primary convergence point linking systemic insulin resistance to neurodegeneration. Impaired insulin signaling in astrocytes, neurons, microglia, and cerebral endothelial cells disrupts glucose metabolism, energy production, and amyloid-β (Aβ) clearance, while promoting tau hyperphosphorylation through glycogen synthase kinase-3β activation. Chronic mTOR hyperactivation exacerbates these dysfunctions by suppressing autophagy, impairing insulin sensitivity, and compromising blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity through tight junction disassembly, pericyte loss, and endothelial senescence. These processes collectively establish a self-perpetuating cycle of metabolic dysfunction, protein aggregation, neuroinflammation, and vascular breakdown. Neuron-derived extracellular vesicles have emerged as a promising non-invasive biomarker platform for monitoring central insulin resistance and therapeutic response in real time. Metabolically targeted interventions, including intranasal insulin, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, and mTOR inhibitors such as rapamycin, demonstrate encouraging preclinical and early clinical efficacy in restoring insulin sensitivity, reducing tau and Aβ pathology, and preserving BBB function. However, challenges related to delivery and dosing remain significant barriers to clinical translation. Continued investigation into neurovascular unit and multi-target combination therapies may facilitate the development of effective, biomarker-guided treatments for AD.

articles.title: Physiological responses during high intensity interval training and moderate intensity continuous training in patients attending early cardiac rehabilitation.
articles.journal: Archives of physical medicine and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare the acute ventilatory, haemodynamic, metabolic, and perceptual responses during low-volume high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and time-matched moderate-intensity continuous training (MICT) in early outpatient cardiac rehabilitation (CR) patients with coronary artery disease (CAD).

DESIGN: Single-centre, within-subject, time-matched exercise comparison SETTING: UK outpatient cardiac rehabilitation unit PARTICIPANTS: Eighteen clinically stable CAD patients (15 male, 60.1 ± 9.9 years) attending early outpatient CR; left ventricular ejection fraction > 35%.

INTERVENTIONS: Two exercise sessions per participant: (1) low-volume HIIT (10 × 1-min intervals at 85-90% peak power output (PPO) with 1-min active recovery at 20-25% PPO; total 20-min) and (2) MICT (continuous cycling for 20 min at 40-70% heart rate reserve (HRR)). Sessions were preceded by a 15-minute warm-up and separated by ≥48 h.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Gas exchange (VO₂, VCO₂, VE), heart rate (HR), blood pressure, rate pressure product (RPP), time >90% oxygen uptake reserve (VO₂R), time relative to ventilatory thresholds (VT1/VT2), blood lactate (BLa), energy expenditure and rating of perceived exertion (RPE).

RESULTS: HIIT elicited greater mean VO₂, %VO₂R, time >90% VO₂R, %HRR, RPP and BLa than MICT (all P < 0.003). Participants spent more time above VT2 during HIIT (834 ± 387 vs. 393 ± 465 s; P < 0.0004). RPE was higher during HIIT (13 ± 1 vs. 11 ± 1; P < 0.003).

CONCLUSIONS: Low-volume HIIT elicited greater ventilatory, haemodynamic and metabolic demand than time-matched MICT, alongside higher perceived exertion. These findings demonstrate that low-volume HIIT provides a greater individualised physiological stimulus and may inform personalised HIIT prescription in patients with CAD attending early CR.

articles.title: Association of age at menopause with incident depressive disorders in women: A prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine the association between age at menopause and the subsequent development of depression.

METHODS: This study included 37,754 postmenopausal women from the UK Biobank. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to assess the association between age at menopause and depression risk, and multivariable-adjusted restricted cubic splines (RCS) were used to evaluate the dose-response relationship. Sensitivity analyses evaluated the robustness of the findings.

RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 14.91 ± 3.04 years, 698 participants developed depression. RCS analysis showed a significant linear dose-response relationship between age at menopause and the risk of depressive disorders; each 1-year increase in age at menopause was associated with a 3.5% lower risk of incident depressive disorders (HR = 0.965, 95% CI: 0.947-0.983, P < 0.001). With 50 years as the reference, women who experienced menopause at age 45 years had a 17.3% higher risk (HR = 1.173, 95% CI: 1.031-1.333, P = 0.015), whereas those who experienced menopause at age 55 years had a 20.3% lower risk (HR = 0.797, 95% CI: 0.642-0.989, P = 0.039). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the findings. Stratified analyses showed that the protective association of age at menopause was more pronounced among participants with hypertension, whereas hormone replacement therapy did not significantly modify the association.

CONCLUSIONS: Age at menopause was significantly associated with the risk of new-onset depression in a linear dose-response manner, with a younger age at menopause associated with a higher risk of depressive disorders.

articles.title: Standardized Preoperative Clearance for Elective Spine Surgery Using a Pre-Assessment Surgical Screening Clinic: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND CONTEXT: Elective spine surgery carries meaningful perioperative risk, highlighting the potential value of standardized preoperative optimization pathways. Traditional primary care physician (PCP) clearance can be limited by access barriers and variable workflows, whereas dedicated, anesthesia-led pre-assessment surgical screening (PASS) clinics offer a standardized pathway for preoperative evaluation and optimization.

PURPOSE: To compare surgical cancellation rates and postoperative outcomes among elective spine surgery patients evaluated preoperatively through a PASS clinic versus a PCP.

STUDY DESIGN/SETTING: Single institution, retrospective cohort study using a prospectively maintained institutional database.

PATIENT SAMPLE: Adults aged 18-89 who underwent elective cervical, thoracic, lumbar, or sacral fusion, decompression, discectomy, or arthroplasty after preoperative clearance through either a PCP or the PASS clinic between July 2020 and December 2024 were included. Patients were excluded if they obtained clearance outside of a PCP or the PASS clinic, or their surgery was performed for fracture, infection, or another emergent indication.

OUTCOME MEASURES: Primary outcomes were (1) preoperative surgical cancellations and (2) 90-day pooled complications. Secondary outcomes included discharge disposition, readmissions, ED visits, return to operating room (RTOR), intensive care unit (ICU) transfer, length of stay (LOS), operative time, intraoperative blood transfusions, and pain/opioid outcomes.

METHODS: Surgical cancellations were assessed across all scheduled elective spine surgery cases during the study period. A cancellation event was defined as a scheduled elective spine surgery that did not proceed as planned on the initially assigned operative date. As such, cancellations were analyzed at the scheduled-case level. All cancelled scheduled cases identified during the study period were included, without restriction to a specific interval before the operative date. Cancellations, which were based on the primary documented reason in the medical record, were reviewed and assigned to prespecified categories using a standardized classification framework. Multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses were performed to compare risk-adjusted postoperative outcomes between pathways. A matched-cohort sensitivity analysis was also performed using direct covariate matching, with exact matching on surgeon, sex, smoking status, surgery type, and spinal region.

RESULTS: A total of 4,320 scheduled elective spine surgery cases met inclusion criteria, including 644 PASS and 3,676 PCP cases. Of these, 863 (20.0%) were canceled and 3,457 (80.0%) proceeded to surgery and were included in postoperative outcomes analyses. Cancellation rates were 0.9% (6/644) in the PASS group versus 23.3% (857/3,676) in the PCP group (p < .001). Among completed elective spine surgeries, 638 (18.5%) were PASS and 2,819 (81.5%) were PCP. Unadjusted 90-day complication rates were lower in the PASS group (4.7% vs. 8.0%, p = 0.004). After multivariable adjustment, there were no significant differences in 90-day pooled complication rates (OR: 0.697, 95%CI: 0.460-1.058, p = .090), 30-day (OR: 0.850, 95%CI: 0.504-1.435, p = .543) or 90-day readmissions (OR: 0.841, 95%CI: 0.546-1.295, p = 0.431), RTOR (OR: 1.096, 95%CI: 0.453-2.651, p = .838), 30-day ED visits (OR: 0.973, 95%CI: 0.664-1.427, p = .890), LOS (β: -0.002, 95%CI: -0.144-0.140, p = 0.977), or pain/opioid outcomes (p > .05 for all). In a matched cohort of 1,229 cases (383 PASS, 846 PCP), the 90-day complication rate was lower in the PASS group (4.7% vs 7.9%; OR: 0.573, 95%CI: 0.336-0.979, p = 0.039), with no differences in readmission, RTOR, ED visits, or LOS.

CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center elective spine surgery cohort, preoperative clearance obtained through the anesthesia-led PASS clinic was associated with markedly lower surgical cancellation rates compared to PCP clearance, with no significant differences in risk-adjusted postoperative outcomes. These findings suggest that standardized preoperative screening clinics may substantially reduce surgical cancellations in patients scheduled for elective spine surgery, without evidence of worse postoperative outcomes.

articles.title: Improved glycemic control and lifestyle behaviors with Dexcom continuous glucose monitoring: one-year real-world outcomes from a global registry of people with non-insulin-treated type 2 diabetes in primary care.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Real-world evidence for continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) in non-insulin-treated (NIT) type 2 diabetes (T2D) remains limited. We evaluated one-year Dexcom G7 CGM use in adults with NIT T2D in US primary care.

METHODS: In this non-randomized registry study (NCT06483945), adults with NIT T2D from 10 US primary care sites initiated Dexcom G7 CGM while continuing usual care. Outcomes included 12-month HbA1c change, (primary), CGM use, weight, BMI, and psychosocial and behavioral measures.

RESULTS: Participants (N = 318) were 54% male, 40% non-white, mean age 61 years, and mean BMI 31 kg/m2; 39% had low income. Mean HbA1c decreased by -0.66% at 12 months (95% CI: -0.83% to -0.49%, p < 0.001; n = 171), with similar reductions across age and medication subgroups. Most participants (73.5%) used CGM ≥70% of the time. CGM use was also associated with reduced body weight and BMI (weight, -2.4 kg [95% CI: -3.2, -1.6]; BMI, -0.8 kg/m2 [95% CI: -1.1, -0.5]) and improved diabetes-related distress (2.2 [0.9] to 1.8 [0.8], p < 0.001), dietary patterns, and lifestyle behaviors.

CONCLUSIONS: In real-world primary care, Dexcom G7 CGM use in NIT T2D was associated with improved glycemia, weight, diabetes distress, diet, and lifestyle behaviors, supporting CGM adoption beyond insulin-treated populations.

articles.title: Joint triglyceride-glucose index and single-point insulin sensitivity estimator phenotypes and diabetes outcomes across three populations.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To assess joint triglyceride-glucose index (TyG) and single-point insulin sensitivity estimator (SPISE) phenotypes and their incremental information for diabetes-related outcomes.

METHODS: We analyzed participants without baseline diabetes from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS; n = 4,933) and English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA; wave 6, n = 2,703; wave 4 sensitivity), with the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES; n = 10,080) as secondary cross-sectional evidence. Sample medians and literature-based fixed thresholds defined phenotypes. Adjusted logistic, Cox, and survey-weighted logistic models assessed associations and incremental fit.

RESULTS: High TyG/low SPISE had the largest median-based estimates: CHARLS odds ratio 2.65 (95% confidence interval 2.05-3.45); ELSA hazard ratios 3.57 (2.04-6.25) and 6.41 (3.98-10.33); NHANES odds ratios 6.61 (5.40-8.08) for prevalent diabetes and 4.05 (3.47-4.72) for dysglycemia. Fixed-threshold associations retained the adverse direction. SPISE improved fit beyond TyG, but adding TyG and interaction to SPISE did not improve CHARLS fit (P = 0.251).

CONCLUSIONS: High TyG/low SPISE was associated with diabetes-related outcomes across the three populations. SPISE provided incremental information beyond TyG, with gains varying by comparator and study design.

articles.title: Body composition and blood pressure: Haemodynamic links in young men and women.
articles.abstract: The aim of this study was to explore the sex-specific haemodynamic links between body composition parameters and systolic and diastolic blood pressure (SBP and DBP, respectively) in adults free of cardiovascular disease and not receiving cardiovascular medications. Body mass index (BMI), fat mass (FM), fat-free mass (FFM), SBP and DBP, cardiac output (CO), peripheral vascular resistance (PVR) and aortic pulse wave velocity (PWV) were determined in 235 men and 192 women aged 18-40 years. Multivariable linear regression and single- as well as multiple-mediator models were used to assess haemodynamic mechanisms underlying the associations between body composition and blood pressure. BMI showed positive associations with SBP and DBP in both sexes (P < 0.001 for all). In men, FFM was the main body composition correlate of SBP (P < 0.001), with the positive association driven in part by CO and partially offset by opposing effects through PVR. FM was the dominant body composition correlate of DBP in men and both SBP and DBP in women (P < 0.001 for all), with the positive associations mediated by PVR and PWV in both sexes, and additionally by heart rate in the FM-DBP association in men. Changes in FFM may affect SBP predominantly through CO in young men. Changes in FM may affect DBP in young men and both SBP and DBP in young women, predominantly through vascular mechanisms. These findings provide important insights into sex differences in the physiology of adiposity-related BP changes in young adults and may help inform sex-specific strategies for the management of adiposity-related hypertension.

articles.title: Update on XBP1 in liver pathobiology.
articles.abstract: Chronic liver disease is a major cause of global morbidity and mortality, yet disease-modifying therapies remain scarce. A shared mechanism uniting metabolic, alcohol-associated, viral, drug-induced, cholestatic, and genetic liver injury is endoplasmic reticulum stress and activation of the unfolded protein response. The transcription factor X-box binding protein 1-spliced, a principal output of the inositol-requiring enzyme 1α arm of this response, has emerged as a central determinant of disease pathogenesis. Under endoplasmic reticulum stress, inositol-requiring enzyme 1α splices X-box binding protein 1 messenger RNA to generate the spliced protein, which increases protein folding and degradation capacity and governs hepatic lipogenesis and lipoprotein assembly. A defining feature, however, is its functional dichotomy: typically cytoprotective in hepatocytes but pathogenic in macrophages and stellate cells, and adaptive during transient but maladaptive during unresolved or excessive stress. This dichotomy sans the spectrum of liver diseases and explains, in part, why global manipulation of the pathway has yielded conflicting results and has obstructed targeted drug development. In conclusion, cell-type selectivity is the central translational challenge, preserving protective hepatocyte signaling while restraining it in non-parenchymal cells, which may be addressed through targeted delivery of pharmacologic or genetic therapeutics directed at this pathway in animal models and humans.

articles.title: EBI3-Dependent Pathways Coordinate Regulatory and Effector Immunity During Cutaneous Leishmaniasis.
articles.abstract: Immunoregulatory pathways are critical for maintaining tissue homeostasis during Leishmania braziliensis infection; however, the mechanisms coordinating these responses remain poorly defined. Here, we investigated the role of Epstein-Barr virus-induced gene 3 (EBI3), a shared subunit of IL-27 and IL-35, during cutaneous leishmaniasis. Human lesions showed increased expression of EBI3-associated cytokine subunits, indicating activation of these pathways during infection. Using experimental models, we found that EBI3 deficiency exacerbated lesion development and parasite burden, whereas IL-27 receptor deficiency did not. Loss of EBI3 selectively reduced Foxp3+ regulatory T cell populations and promoted excessive inflammatory responses, including neutrophil accumulation, altered macrophage responses, impaired inducible nitric oxide synthase expression and defective Th1-associated immunity. Consequently, EBI3-deficient mice failed to mount effective antiparasitic responses, leading to enhanced tissue pathology and parasite persistence. Together, our findings identify EBI3 as a central regulator of immune balance and protective immunity during L. braziliensis infection.

articles.title: Helminth infections: from genomic discovery to public health interventions.
articles.abstract: Helminths infect more than a billion people worldwide and cause substantial chronic morbidity, impaired physical and cognitive development in children, and reduced wellbeing and economic productivity, particularly in low-income and middle-income countries. Preventive chemotherapy, sanitation, vector control, and integrated programmes have substantially reduced infection intensity and morbidity in many settings, although sustaining these gains and advancing towards elimination require complementary tools. Advances in genomics, multiomics, and computational biology have added a complementary, data-rich dimension to established parasitology, supporting systematic target identification, improved molecular diagnostics, and new insights into transmission and drug response. In this Review, we examine how these approaches are reshaping the study of helminth infections and the implications of these approaches for diagnosis, treatment, and control. Translating these technological and scientific advances into effective interventions still requires representative data, experimental and field validation, accessible infrastructure, trained personnel, and sustainable implementation, particularly in resource-constrained settings. Ultimately, integrating genomic and molecular discoveries with clinical, epidemiological, and public health strategies within a One Health framework will be central to achieving measurable and sustained improvements in helminth control.

articles.title: Consensus on the definition, components, and grading of composite postoperative pulmonary complication outcomes (PrECiSIOn): insights from an international Delphi expert panel.
articles.abstract: Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) are common after surgery and contribute substantially to morbidity, mortality, and health-care burden, and are frequently used as endpoints in clinical studies. However, absence of standardised definitions and heterogeneity in component selection limit comparability across studies and might bias estimates of treatment effects. The Postoperative Pulmonary Complications-Evaluation for Consensus on Standardised Outcomes (PrECiSIOn) study was an international, mixed-method consensus study using a Delphi process to establish a standardised definition of PPCs, determine severity-based ranking of individual components, and define approaches for their assessment. A multidisciplinary panel of experts in PPCs was recruited and candidate PPC components were identified through a focused literature review, structured into domains, and evaluated across iterative Delphi rounds using a seven-point Likert scale, with consensus predefined as ≥75% agreement. Patient and patient care representative perspectives were incorporated through interviews and surveys, and panellists assigned severity weights to components reaching consensus. Input from 44 panellists and five patients and patient representatives informed the prioritisation of clinically meaningful outcomes. Consensus was achieved on a standardised PPC construct comprising components grouped into four domains: symptoms, diagnoses, therapies, and outcomes. Panellists supported the use of routinely collected clinical data and a standardised in-hospital monitoring approach but did not reach consensus on the optimal follow-up period or need for post-discharge surveillance. Severity-based rank ordering enabled hierarchical organisation of PPC components according to their clinical importance, supporting the development of ordinal composite outcomes that account for differences in severity between individual complications. This international consensus-based framework provides a standardised definition of PPCs incorporating severity-based rank ordering, addresses important limitations of existing composite outcomes, and might facilitate more consistent and clinically meaningful evaluation of perioperative interventions. Further work should focus on external validation, implementation in clinical trial analyses, and assessment of applicability across diverse patient populations and health-care settings.

articles.title: Safety and efficacy of weekly pemvidutide versus placebo for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (IMPACT): 48-week results from a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, phase 2b study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glucagon-GLP-1 dual receptor agonists have shown promise in treating metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). The aim of the IMPACT trial was to assess the effects of one such agent, pemvidutide, in patients with MASH and stage F2 or F3 fibrosis. We previously reported the 24-week primary endpoints of MASH resolution and fibrosis improvement. Here we report the secondary endpoints following 48 weeks of treatment.

METHODS: IMPACT was a 48-week, randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind, phase 2b trial in patients with biopsy-confirmed MASH and fibrosis stage F2 or F3. Patients from 83 sites, including academic and community hospitals and private clinical research clinics, in the USA and Australia were randomly assigned (1:2:2) using an interactive web response system to receive once-weekly subcutaneous pemvidutide (1·2 mg or 1·8 mg), administered without dose titration, or placebo. Patients, investigators, the funder, and all other staff, were masked to treatment assignments throughout the study. The dual primary endpoints of MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis or at least one stage liver fibrosis improvement without worsening of MASH were assessed at week 24. Liver biopsies were not collected at week 48, and only secondary endpoints were assessed at this timepoint. All analyses were conducted in the intention-to-treat population consisting of all randomly assigned patients. The trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05989711) and is complete.

FINDINGS: From July 27, 2023, to Nov 21, 2025, 1557 patients were screened and 212 patients were randomly assigned to pemvidutide 1·2 mg (n=41), pemvidutide 1·8 mg (n=85), or placebo (n=86). Mean age was 53·4 years (SD 12·4), mean BMI was 38·7 kg/m2 (7·8), 123 (58%) patients were female, 89 (42%) were male, and 90 (42%) had type 2 diabetes. At week 48, least-squares mean relative changes in liver fat content were -45·2% (95% CI -56·0 to -34·5; difference from placebo -37·1 percentage points [95% CI -50·6 to -23·5]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group, -54·7% (-62·3 to -47·1; difference from placebo -46·5 percentage points [-57·7 to -35·3]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group, and -8·2% (-16·5 to 0·2) in the placebo group. The least-squares mean absolute change in corrected T1 relaxation time was -124·2 ms (95% CI -157·1 to -91·4; difference from placebo -103·8 [95% CI -143·9 to -63·6]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group, -139·5 ms (-161·7 to -117·3; difference from placebo -119·0 [-151·2 to -86·9]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group, and -20·5 ms (-44·5 to 3·6) in the placebo group. Least-squares mean changes in alanine aminotransferase were -37·8 IU/L (95% CI -44·5 to -31·1; difference from placebo -27·5 [95% CI -35·8 to -19·2]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group and -37·4 IU/L (-42·1 to -32·7; difference from placebo -27·1 [-33·9 to -20·3]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group versus -10·3 IU/L (-15·2 to -5·4) for the placebo group. Least-squares mean changes in enhanced liver fibrosis score were -0·49 (95% CI -0·71 to -0·28; difference from placebo -0·65 [95 % CI -0·92 to -0·38]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group, -0·58 (-0·74 to -0·43; difference from placebo -0·74 [-0·97 to -0·52]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group, and 0·16 (-0·01 to 0·32) for the placebo group. The most frequent pemvidutide-related adverse events were nausea (occurring in nine [22%] of 41 patients in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group, 35 [41%] of 85 patients in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group, and 15 [17%] of 86 patients in the placebo group), diarrhoea (five [12%] in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group, 19 [22%] in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group, and seven [8%] in the placebo group), and constipation (five [12%] in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group, 15 [18%] in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group, and ten [12%] in the placebo group). No severe or serious adverse events were defined as study medication related. Discontinuations due to adverse events occurred in no patients in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group, one (1%) in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group, and three (3%) in the placebo group.

INTERPRETATION: In patients with MASH, 48 weeks of pemvidutide treatment led to significant reductions in non-invasive tests of MASH inflammation and fibrosis, suggesting continued improvement in liver health. These data warrant the continued investigation of pemvidutide in a phase 3 trial.

FUNDING: Altimmune.

articles.title: The fungal phosphate starvation regulator CtPHO4 couples nutrient adaptation to host colonization through the effector NFC1.
articles.abstract: Plant-associated microbes must balance environmental adaptation with virulence and host colonization to survive in fluctuating ecosystems, yet the molecular mechanisms coupling these processes remain poorly understood. Here, we identify the effector NUTRIENT-DEPENDENT FACILITATOR OF COLONIZATION 1 (NFC1) in a conditionally pathogenic Colletotrichum tofieldiae strain, whose expression is tightly regulated by both temperature and phosphate availability. By leveraging plant phosphate starvation response (PSR) mutants and phosphate supplementation, we demonstrate that NFC1 expression is driven by the internal phosphate status of the host. Notably, the fungal PSR regulator CtPHO4 represses NFC1 and colonization during phosphate starvation, while simultaneously activating canonical fungal PSR-related genes. Conversely, under phosphate sufficiency, NFC1 is strongly induced and promotes infection. This host colonization and adaptation machinery is partially conserved in a beneficial C. tofieldiae strain. This study uncovers a molecular link between metabolic adaptation and host colonization, providing a conceptual framework for understanding fungal lifestyle transitions under changing environments.

articles.title: Slow-timescale regulation of dopamine release governs recovery of a motivational drive over days.
articles.abstract: The rise and fall of a motivational state can unfold over many days. We used mouse mating behavior to model how the brain orchestrates such slow-timescale changes in motivation. Male mice become sexually satiated after successful matings, and their motivation to mate recovers over a week. Using deep-brain fluorescence-lifetime imaging in the medial preoptic area (MPOA), we found that tonic dopamine transmission-which regulates mating drive-also declined after mating and gradually re-emerged across several days. Two mechanisms regulated dopamine transmission. First, successful mating transiently reduced the tonic firing of hypothalamic dopamine-releasing neurons, thereby inhibiting dopamine release and mating behavior for 1 to 2 days. Second, these neurons' ability to produce and release dopamine dropped after mating and recovered over the following week, paralleling the recovery of mating drive. Therefore, changes in neuronal firing rate and neurotransmitter composition cooperate to control the early and late phases of motivational dynamics, respectively.

articles.title: Multilayer hydrodynamic modeling of the airway surface liquid reveals impaired transport in HYDIN-related primary ciliary dyskinesia.
articles.abstract: Mucociliary clearance (MCC) is a primary defense mechanism of the respiratory system, driven by the coordinated beating of motile cilia and the nonlinear viscoelastic properties of airway mucus within the airway surface liquid (ASL). Impairment of ciliary function, such as in HYDIN-related primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD), severely compromises mucus transport and leads to chronic respiratory disease. In this study, we developed a three-dimensional, experimentally informed computational model of a representative human nasal ASL segment to quantify MCC efficiency under healthy and HYDIN conditions.
