Ciliary beat patterns were obtained from high-speed video microscopy of cultured nasal epithelial cells and converted into continuous analytical waveforms for numerical implementation. Mucus rheological properties were characterized from the same samples using differential dynamic microscopy: storage and loss moduli were measured, and the shear-rate-dependent viscosity was estimated from the resulting complex viscosity via the Cox-Merz approximation; both were fitted with multimode viscoelastic constitutive models. These experimentally derived kinematic and rheological inputs were integrated into the governing equations of ASL flow to resolve the spatiotemporal velocity field and net mucus transport. The simulations show that healthy cilia generate strong streamwise flow and coherent mucus transport, whereas HYDIN cilia exhibit reduced beat amplitude and impaired recovery-stroke bending, resulting in substantially lower streamwise velocity and an approximately 13-fold reduction in mean ASL transport velocity. Cross-condition simulations indicate that this reduction is predominantly driven by altered ciliary kinematics, while differences in mucus rheology have a comparatively smaller effect. This study provides one of the first fully three-dimensional, experimentally informed computational comparisons of healthy and HYDIN-related MCC. The proposed framework provides a physiologically informed platform for investigating mucociliary dysfunction and may support future studies of inhaled particle transport and drug delivery following incorporation of appropriate particle transport, deposition, and drug-mucus interaction physics.

articles.title: Molecular mimicry arrests the phage packaging AppA-ratus.
articles.abstract: Among characterized phage defenses, those that interfere with phage genome packaging and virion assembly remain comparatively underexplored. Wang et al. show that a small Salmonella Gifsy-1 prophage protein, AppA, disrupts late-stage virion assembly by mimicking the terminase assembly interface and arresting phage DNA packaging, supporting bacterial fitness during intestinal infection.

articles.title: Advancing brain organoids from disease phenotypes to mechanisms and translation across developmental, infectious, and neurodegenerative diseases.
articles.abstract: Diseases of the central nervous system remain among the greatest unmet medical challenges. Human brain organoids provide 3D multicellular systems for investigating neurodevelopmental, infectious, and neurodegenerative diseases in a human cellular context. Considering these distinct disease areas together highlights how organoid studies are moving beyond recapitulating disease phenotypes to define molecular and cellular mechanisms and trajectories: when pathogenic changes emerge, how they evolve, which cell types and states drive or resist disease, and how multicellular interactions shape progression. Integrating human genetics with longitudinal, single-cell, multi-omic, and functional analyses provides access to human-specific processes that are difficult to capture in animal models and enables identification of mechanisms and therapeutic targets anchored in human disease biology. Increasingly, well-characterized organoids offer human new approach methodologies (NAMs) for preclinical therapeutic evaluation. Advances in reproducibility, benchmarking, and appropriate validation will be critical to establishing their predictive value and supporting their use in drug development and regulatory applications.

articles.title: ISX-9 marks the spot for better beta cell differentiation.
articles.abstract: Stem cell-derived islets offer a promising approach to restoring endogenous insulin secretion in type 1 diabetes (T1D). In this issue of Developmental Cell, Zhao, Liang et al. show that ISX-9 expands PDX1+/NKX6-1+ pancreatic progenitors and improves beta-like cell yield and function, while revealing how extracellular matrix signaling regulates progenitor identity.

articles.title: Deletion of SETD7 attenuates systemic inflammation triggered by renal ischemia-reperfusion injury.
articles.abstract: The sudden loss of kidney function within hours to 7 days is called acute kidney injury (AKI), which is mainly caused by ischemia and reperfusion and involves multiple mechanisms, including epigenetic alterations. SETD7 plays a regulatory role in gene expression by methylating histone and non-histone proteins and has been implicated in inflammatory pathways and diabetic nephropathy. However, its deep implications in AKI are still lacking. In this study, we investigated the role of SETD7 in an experimental model of AKI induced by renal ischemia-reperfusion (I/R). Male C57BL/6 wild-type (WT) and global SETD7 knockout (KO) mice were subjected to unilateral renal ischemia followed by 15 days of reperfusion. To assess the model's success, renal function, injury and fibrosis markers, and morphometric parameters were assessed. Next, SETD7 localization and histone methylation were evaluated. The influence of SETD7 knockout on local and systemic inflammatory cytokines was analyzed. Renal ischemia markedly increased the expression of injury and fibrosis markers in the affected kidney by more than 20-fold compared with WT controls: KIM-1, NGAL, vimentin, COL3 and α-SMA (p < 0.05). SETD7 was found in the cytoplasm. The SETD7 knockout animals presented an attenuated systemic inflammatory response (less than 9-fold compared to WT control, p < 0.05), but not a local. Collectively, these findings indicate that SETD7 plays a significant role in modulating systemic inflammation following renal ischemic injury; inhibiting SETD7 expression and function could be a novel therapeutic strategy to control AKI inflammatory stimuli.

articles.title: Interleukin-4 neutralization exacerbates glucose intolerance during streptozotocin-induced diabetogenic window.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated the efficacy of a single-dose streptozotocin (STZ) regimen for inducing type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) in BALB/c mice fed either with standard diet (SD) or high-fat diet (HFD). Protective roles of interleukin-4 (IL-4) during critical diabetogenic window was characterized by temporally monitoring physiological parameters of IL-4-delpleted mice receiving IL-4 monoclonal antibodies (Ab) during STZ-induced disease development period. Long-term effects of IL-4 depletion on metabolic alteration were also monitored for addressing the influences of IL-4 on STZ-induced diabetic development and manifestation. Our data demonstrated that single STZ treatment successfully induced T2DM in both SD- and HFD- mice with intact pancreatic β cell insulin-producing capacity. IL-4 Ab administration resulted in increased fasting blood glucose levels, which was aligned with the timeline of IL-4 depletion, indicating beneficial function of IL-4 in maintaining glucose metabolic efficiency. Notably, transient IL-4 depletion resulted in sustained effects by exacerbating post-onset glucose intolerance. Our findings underscore the vital protective role of IL-4 in preserving metabolic homeostasis during the diabetogenic window. Transient counteracting IL-4 bioactivity facilitates metabolic dysfunction, leading to sustained inferior glucose intolerance. The evidence characterizes and dissects beneficial roles of IL-4 in the diabetogenic window, offering new insights into the anti-diabetic potential of IL-4, as well as the intricate crosstalk among immune responses and metabolic homeostasis. More importantly, the STZ-induced BALB/c model serves as a good platform for evaluating anti-diabetic efficacy, mechanism of pharmacological action and translational potential of structurally identified compounds, especially the protective activity during the pre-onset diabetogenic window.

articles.title: Sociodemographic predictors of postpartum anticoagulant selection in pregnancy-associated venous thromboembolism.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancy-associated venous thromboembolism (VTE) requires anticoagulation into the postpartum period that overlaps with breastfeeding initiation. Low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) and vitamin K antagonists (VKA) are compatible with breastfeeding, whereas direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are currently not recommended. Postpartum anticoagulant selection may be influenced by safety, convenience and access, potentially contributing to racial and socioeconomic inequities in care. We evaluated the impact of race and sociodemographic factors on postpartum anticoagulant selection in a publicly funded healthcare system.

METHODS: This is a population-based cohort study using linked administrative health data in Ontario, Canada. We included Ontario Drug Benefit (ODB) recipients with pregnancy-associated VTE diagnosed between 2012 and 2022 who received ≥1 anticoagulant prescription within 6 months postpartum. Primary outcome was the exclusive receipt of breastfeeding-compatible anticoagulants (LMWH/VKA). Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) were determined to identify factors associated with breastfeeding-compatible anticoagulant use.

RESULTS: Of 113 ODB-eligible individuals with pregnancy-associated VTE, 62.8% received ≥6 weeks of postpartum anticoagulation. During the 6-month postpartum period, 25.7% transitioned to a DOAC. No significant association was observed between race and receipt of breastfeeding-compatible anticoagulation. However, individuals in the most materially deprived neighbourhoods were significantly less likely to receive a breastfeeding-compatible anticoagulant compared with those in less deprived areas (aOR 0.20, 95% CI 0.07-0.58).

CONCLUSIONS: In this population-based cohort, 1 in 4 individuals with pregnancy-associated VTE received a DOAC within 6 months postpartum. Postpartum anticoagulant selection was affected by socioeconomic status. These findings highlight the need to explore structural factors influencing anticoagulant selection to advance equitable postpartum care.

articles.title: Bedside diaphragm ultrasound for early risk stratification in patients with sepsis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between early bedside diaphragmatic ultrasonography findings and clinical outcomes in patients diagnosed with sepsis.

METHODS: This prospective observational study included adult patients who presented to the emergency department with sepsis. Diaphragmatic ultrasonography was performed within the first hour of admission, and diaphragmatic thickness (DT), diaphragmatic thickening fraction (DTF), and diaphragmatic excursion (DE) were measured. Intensive care unit (ICU) admission, invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), need for vasoactive therapy, and mortality were recorded.

RESULTS: A total of 110 patients were included in the study and the in-hospital mortality rate was found to be 21.8%. The mean DE was 3.15 ± 1.31 cm, and the mean DTF was 27.5 ± 13.1%. DD and DA were detected in 30.9% and 26.4% of patients, respectively. ICU admission, IMV, NIMV, vasoactive treatment requirements, and mortality rates were significantly higher in patients with DD or DA (p < 0.01 for all comparisons). Furthermore, SOFA, qSOFA, MEWS, and APACHE II scores were significantly higher in patients with DD and DA.

CONCLUSIONS: In multivariate regression analysis DTF<20% + age + SOFA was independently associated with in-hospital mortality (adjusted (OR: 70.59; 95% CI: 15.27-60.26; p < 0.001).For mortality, DTF<%20 discriminated outcome with an AUC of 0.92 (95% CI 0.86-0.97), DT < 2 mm with an AUC of 0.70 (95% CI: 0.60-0.81), and DE < 2 cm with an AUC of 0.55 (95% CI 0.44-0.65). Bedside diaphragm ultrasound, and DTF in particular, may therefore be a useful adjunct for early risk stratification in emergency department patients with sepsis.

articles.title: Stationary and non-stationary extreme value models for pedestrian-vehicle conflicts incorporating movement type and vehicle conflict speed.
articles.abstract: Pedestrian safety has received growing attention in recent years, and Extreme Value Theory (EVT) has increasingly been applied to estimate rare crash risk using surrogate safety measures. However, EVT-based analyses of pedestrian-vehicle interactions at unsignalized pedestrian crossings remain limited, particularly regarding the influence of movement type and the incorporation of explanatory variables within non-stationary models. This study investigates pedestrian-vehicle interactions at an unsignalized pedestrian crossing using video-based trajectory data and EVT. A total of 164 h of video recordings were processed using TrafxSAFE software to extract trajectories and surrogate safety measures. The final dataset comprised 17,017 pedestrian-arrives-first interactions, which were classified according to the relative approach directions of pedestrians and vehicles. Block Maxima (BM) and Peaks Over Threshold (POT) models were first applied to obtain EVT-based far-tail crash-probability estimates based on Post-Encroachment Time (PET). The BM estimates were conditional on qualifying 10-min blocks containing at least 30 eligible interactions and therefore do not represent arbitrary 10-min periods; this selection limits direct comparability with the POT estimates. For the present dataset, the two approaches produced different crash-probability estimates, and the POT framework was retained for the subsequent movement-specific and non-stationary analyses. Stationary movement-specific POT models showed differences in the fitted PET tail characteristics across pedestrian-vehicle movement types; however, uncertainty in extrapolation towards PET=0 did not support a precise crash-risk ranking among the movement types. Finally, non-stationary POT models incorporating movement type and conflict-point speed as covariates showed that conflict-point speed was associated with the tail behaviour of PET, while the movement-type terms collectively improved model fit beyond conflict-point speed alone. The additive model including both covariates was retained for full-sample interpretation, whereas allowing the association with conflict-point speed to vary across movement types was not supported by the data. At the study site, the findings show how heterogeneity in extreme PET behaviour across movement configurations can be evaluated within a non-stationary POT framework incorporating movement type and conflict-point speed.

articles.title: The IgM- and IgA-enriched immunoglobulin preparation trimodulin suppresses neutrophil extracellular trap formation more effectively in vitro than standard intravenous immunoglobulin.
articles.abstract: Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) represent an important mechanism of defense against pathogens. However, in cases of severe lung infection or sepsis, excessive NET formation has been observed to cause vascular occlusion, inflammation, and tissue damage. Treatment with intravenous immunoglobulins (IVIg), especially those enriched for IgA and IgM, has been shown to improve outcomes in patients with these conditions. We compared trimodulin, a novel polyvalent antibody preparation containing elevated levels of IgM (∼23%) and IgA (∼21%), with standard IVIg to determine their ability to reduce NET formation in vitro. Trimodulin strongly reduced NET formation by neutrophils stimulated with phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA), complexed IgA, or complexed IgG. This effect was accompanied by reduced IL-8 secretion. Standard IVIg showed no significant effect. Dissecting trimodulin into its individual immunoglobulin components revealed that IgM has the strongest capacity to reduce NET formation, followed by IgG. Nevertheless, the combined additive effects of the individual immunoglobulins were less effective than trimodulin, potentially caused by synergistic effects between the three immunoglobulin classes within trimodulin. Together, our data show that trimodulin is a more potent regulator of NET formation than the tested standard IVIg, mainly due to its IgM component. Therefore, trimodulin may be beneficial in conditions involving excessive NET formation.

articles.title: Peripartum echocardiographic findings in preeclampsia and their association with subsequent hypertension.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Preeclampsia, a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy, predisposes women to long-term cardiovascular risk, especially future hypertension. We examined whether peripartum echocardiographic measures were associated with subsequent hypertension among women with preeclampsia without pre-pregnancy chronic hypertension.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective study of 252 women with preeclampsia and 222 normotensive pregnant controls who underwent echocardiography between 20 weeks' gestation and 30 days postpartum within a single integrated health system (2016-2022).

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: Incident hypertension during follow-up (through mid-2023), defined by a new diagnosis of hypertension, systolic blood pressure (BP) >135 mmHg on a recorded visit, diastolic BP >85 mmHg, or initiation of antihypertensive medication. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify echocardiographic and clinical predictors of subsequent hypertension.

RESULTS: Among 474 pregnant women followed for a mean of 2.3 years, 119 of 252 (47.2%) preeclampsia women and 9 of 222 (4.1%) controls met criteria for hypertension. Among women with preeclampsia, 85% had severe features. Eighteen of 26 echocardiographic measures differed significantly between preeclampsia and control groups. In adjusted models limited to women with preeclampsia, both interventricular septal thickness at end-diastole (IVSd) and left ventricular mass index (LVMi) were independently associated with the development of hypertension (IVSd OR = 1.37 per 0.1 cm, p < 0.01; LVMi OR = 1.15 per 10 g/m2, p = 0.04). LVMi greater than 95 g/m2 was associated with a more than threefold higher odds of developing hypertension.

CONCLUSION: Peripartum echocardiography may provide additional insight for identifying women at higher risk for future hypertension, allowing for closer follow-up and early intervention.

articles.title: Nivolumab and total neoadjuvant treatment for locally advanced rectal cancer: results of a phase II trial (CA209-8M4).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: CA209-8M4 is a prospective phase II trial evaluating the addition of nivolumab to total neoadjuvant treatment (TNT) in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients with LARC (T3-4Nany or TanyN1) up to 12 cm from the anal verge received standard chemoradiation (CRT) followed by chemoimmunotherapy (CIMT): six cycles of standard mFOLFOX6 and nivolumab at 240 mg. We defined a novel primary endpoint, combining pathological complete response (pCR) rate among operated patients and long-term (≥12 months) clinical complete response (cCR) rate for those electing watchful waiting, into a composite endpoint of modified pCR (mpCR) rate.

RESULTS: Between April 2019 and March 2024, 29 patients were enrolled, median age 53 years, 72.4% male; 96.6% of tumors were cT3 or cT4, 69.0% cN+, and 96.6% microsatellite stable. Median distance from the anal verge was 7 cm; 51.7% of patients had grade ≥3 adverse events (AEs) during CIMT, including one fatality (mesenteric inflammation), attributed most likely to CRT's unresolved toxicity. Immune-mediated AEs occurred in four patients (13.8%): grade 3 diabetes mellitus (1) and grade 1 hepatitis (3), including one with asymptomatic hyper/hypothyroidism. Twenty-eight patients (96.6%) are assessable for mpCR: 6 of the 15 operated achieved pCR, and 13 were not operated with cCR ≥12 months, leading to a 67.9% mpCR rate. With a median follow-up of 43.5 months (range 25.0-84.1+), all 28 assessable pts are alive with no evidence of disease. The estimated 3-year disease-free survival and 5-year overall survival rates of the entire group are 93% [95% confidence interval (CI) 84-100] and 97% (95% CI 90-100), respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: The addition of nivolumab to standard TNT in LARC seems safe and may enhance its effectiveness, with encouraging mpCR and survival rates. A multicenter randomized trial, further evaluating this strategy, is ongoing.

articles.title: Evaluation of exercise on quality of Life and aerobic capacity in women with heart failure: A systematic review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women with heart failure (HF) present distinct clinical and hormonal characteristics and remain underrepresented in exercise-based randomized trials. Given the reduction in aerobic capacity and quality of life observed in this population, this study aimed to evaluate the effects of exercise training on these outcomes in women with HF.

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Scopus, CINAHL, and LILACS through October 2025. Randomized controlled trials including adult women with HF undergoing structured exercise interventions were selected. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed for peak oxygen uptake (VO₂peak), six-minute walk distance (6MWT), and Minnesota Living with Heart Failure Questionnaire (MLHFQ) scores.

RESULTS: Four randomized trials met the inclusion criteria. Exercise training significantly improved VO₂peak and increased 6MWT distance. However, pooled analysis of MLHFQ did not demonstrate a statistically significant improvement. The certainty of evidence was moderate for VO₂peak and very low for 6MWT and MLHFQ due to risk of bias and imprecision.

CONCLUSION: Exercise training improves aerobic capacity in women with HF with moderate-certainty evidence. Evidence supporting functional capacity and quality-of-life improvements remains highly uncertain. Further adequately powered, women-specific randomized trials are needed.

articles.title: A comparative evaluation of community engagement as a required component of a PharmD education among on-campus and distance pathway students.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate PharmD students' perceptions of a required longitudinal community engagement experience aligned with Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE) Standards 2025, including its contribution to professional identity formation, and to compare perceptions between on-campus and distance pathway students.

METHODS: This descriptive, cross-sectional study evaluated student perceptions of a required longitudinal community engagement experience embedded within the curriculum and aligned with ACPE Standards 2025. Students completed an anonymous, Institutional Review Board-approved 11-item electronic survey consisting of nine Likert-scale items evaluating professional identity formation and personal development (e.g., empathy, communication, leadership, social responsibility), one demographic item identifying instructional pathway, and one optional open-ended question. Descriptive statistics summarized responses and compared outcomes by semester and pathway. Qualitative comments underwent content analysis to contextualize quantitative findings.

RESULTS: Twenty-seven PharmD students completed the survey across three semesters (Fall 2023-Spring 2025). Students reported positive impacts, particularly in self-satisfaction (92.6% agree/strongly agree), leadership and mentorship development (85.2% agree/strongly agree%), social responsibility (92.6% agree/strongly agree), and cultural competence (88.9% agree/strongly agree), with empathy (92.6% agree/strongly agree) and communication skills (88.9% agree/strongly agree) also showing consistent positive responses. While responses were generally favorable across cohorts, distance pathway students reported stronger positive perceptions across most domains compared with on-campus learners.

CONCLUSION: Required longitudinal community engagement was perceived as a meaningful contributor to professional identity formation and workforce readiness across both instructional pathways, supporting sustained integration of community-engaged learning within evolving pharmacy curricula.

articles.title: Practical Management of Multivessel Coronary Artery Disease: Evidence, Controversies, and the Boundaries of Guidelines.
articles.abstract: Multivessel coronary artery disease remains one of the most challenging cardiovascular diseases to manage. Selecting the optimal revascularization strategy requires multidisciplinary Heart Team discussion that incorporates coronary anatomy, clinical risk factors, and patient preferences into the decision-making process. Clinical guidelines provide a valuable framework for standardized, evidence-based care with reduced practice variability. However, many landmark trials enrolled highly selected populations and were conducted before the widespread adoption of contemporary revascularization techniques, including physiologic lesion assessment, intracoronary imaging, and modern arterial grafting strategies. Reflecting a collaborative Heart Team perspective, this state-of-the-art review from the American College of Cardiology Interventional Section Leadership Council and Cardiac Surgery Leadership Council summarizes contemporary evidence, reviews areas of ongoing controversy, and provides practical guidance for managing patients with multivessel coronary artery disease in clinical situations that extend beyond the scope of current guideline recommendations.

articles.title: Using implementation science methods in critical care nursing - part 4: Research approaches.
Liensinine alleviates experimental asthma by attenuating PINK1-associated mitophagy signaling and cellular senescence.
articles.abstract: Toluene diisocyanate (TDI) is a major cause of occupational asthma (OA) with few effective therapies. Dysregulated mitophagy signaling and cellular senescence have been implicated in airway inflammation; however, their roles in TDI-induced asthma remain unclear. The natural alkaloid liensinine (Lie) has been reported to inhibit mitophagy, but its protective potential in asthma remains unexplored. This study investigated whether Lie could alleviate experimental asthma by attenuating PINK1-associated mitophagy signaling and the related cellular senescence. We established mouse and cellular models of TDI-induced asthma. In vivo, mice received intraperitoneal Lie and intranasal adeno-associated virus (AAV) for PINK1 overexpression. In vitro, HBE135-E6E7 cells were exposed to TDI-human serum albumin (TDI-HSA) and transduced with lentivirus for PINK1 overexpression. Lie significantly mitigated airway hyperresponsiveness (AHR), inflammation, and fibrosis. Molecular docking predicted a potential interaction between Lie and PINK1. Lie attenuated TDI-induced PINK1-associated mitophagy signaling, restored mitochondrial function, and reduced senescence. PINK1 overexpression largely reversed the protective effects of Lie on mitochondrial function and attenuated its senescence-reducing effect. In a Transwell co-culture system, pretreatment of TDI-HSA-stimulated HBE135-E6E7 cells with Lie was associated with reduced proliferation, migration, and fibrotic marker expression in MRC-5 cells in the lower chamber, possibly through attenuation of TDI-HSA-induced epithelial injury. Lie pretreatment attenuated PINK1-associated mitophagy signaling and the related cellular senescence in a TDI-induced experimental asthma model.

articles.title: Quassin attenuates secondary brain injury following intracerebral hemorrhage.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) accounts for only 10-15% of all stroke cases, yet it is responsible for up to 70% of stroke-related mortality and long-term disability globally. Quassin, a white, crystalline molecule, is often used in Chinese herbal medicine. Research has shown quassin's neuroprotective properties associated with the inhibition of neuroinflammation in neurological diseases.

METHODS: A total of 120 C57BL/6 male mice were randomly divided into three groups of 40: the Sham group, the ICH + Vehicle group, and the ICH+ Quassin group. ICH was induced in the two experimental groups by injecting collagenase type VII into the basal ganglia. The ICH + quassin group received daily intraperitoneal administration of quassin (1 mg/kg) for three consecutive days. Neurological function was assessed using both the corner test and mNSS. Three days post-ICH, several analyses were conducted: TUNEL staining, Western blot, Evans Blue dye extravasation, and Immunofluorescence/Immunohistochemistry staining were utilized to evaluate molecular targets, blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, and cellular responses.

RESULTS: Quassin treatment significantly improved neurological recovery and exerted a robust protective capacity against acute structural secondary injury, achieving a 72.5% reduction in total lesion volume compared to vehicle controls (p < 0.0001). Quassin markedly suppressed neuroinflammation, as evidenced by a significant decrease in Iba-1+ microglial activation (p < 0.0001) and neutrophil infiltration (p < 0.001). Moreover, quassin treatment was correlated with the downregulation of the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling pathway (p < 0.01) and a notable reduction in pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-α and IL-6. Furthermore, quassin attenuated neuronal apoptosis (p < 0.0001) and preserved BBB structural integrity by suppressing MMP-9 expression (p < 0.01) while upregulating key tight junction proteins, including zonula occludens-1 (p < 0.0001) and Occludin (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Quassin demonstrates significant neuroprotective efficacy in mouse models of ICH by concurrently reducing neuroinflammation, preserving the integrity of the BBB, and mitigating brain cell death.

articles.title: Mitral valve strain and chordal forces as potential diagnostic parameters in pediatric mitral valve disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A challenge in pediatric mitral valve disease is the limited understanding of the biomechanical alterations in valvular dysfunction. This complicates decision-making regarding timing and choice of intervention. Fluid-structure interaction (FSI) simulations offer patient-specific insights into valve biomechanics, unattainable by conventional imaging. This study compared healthy, regurgitant, and surgically repaired pediatric mitral valves to determine whether valve strain and chordal forces differ between groups and whether these measures reflect the biomechanical consequences of disease.

METHODS: A validated FSI framework was applied to assess valve strain and chordal forces in pediatric healthy valves (N = 6) and regurgitant valves (N = 7). Patient-specific geometries were reconstructed from 3D echocardiography, and flow boundary conditions were derived from left ventricular volume data.

RESULTS: Strain analysis revealed statistically significant differences between healthy (6.6% strain) and regurgitant valves (9.8% strain before and 9.0% after surgery), indicating that repair improves but does not normalize strain patterns. Localized high-strain regions were present in regurgitant valves pre- and postoperatively. Regurgitant valves exhibited elevated diastolic chordal forces compared to healthy valves, indicating pathological loading. No statistically significant differences in strain or chordal forces were observed between pre- and postoperative states.

CONCLUSIONS: Valve strain and chordal forces differed between healthy and regurgitant pediatric mitral valves. These biomechanical parameters open the possibility of quantifying mitral valve mechanics and introduce an innovative approach to using valve strain and chordal forces as functional biomarkers, supporting the future clinical integration of patient-specific FSI simulations in the evaluation of pediatric mitral valve disease.

articles.title: Item selection and content validation of the nurse triage quality audit tool (N-TriQAT) in emergency departments: A consensus study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nurse-led triage is a critical process for prioritizing patients in emergency departments. Inaccurate triage decisions may compromise patient safety and system efficiency. Despite use of systems such as the Canadian Triage and Acuity Scale (CTAS), few validated instruments exist to assess nurse-led triage quality, highlighting the need for tools such as the Nurse Triage Quality Audit Tool (N-TriQAT).

OBJECTIVES: To select items and establish the content validity of the N-TriQAT.

METHODS: A structured consensus study based on the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method was conducted, combining two Delphi rounds (electronic) and one virtual face-to-face round. A panel of 32 experts (emergency nurses, physicians, managers, CTAS instructors, and patient partners) was consulted. Experts evaluated and prioritized N-TriQAT items based on relevance and clarity using a nine-point Likert scale and a dichotomous clarity assessment. Median scores and I-CVI were used to determine consensus.

RESULTS: Overall, 73 of 85 items were retained and organized into 11 domains aligned with the triage process. For retained items, I-CVI ranged from 0.45 to 0.97 with median scores from 6 to 9. Rejected items showed lower agreement (I-CVI 0.13-0.73; median 1.7-7). Strong consensus was observed for standardized components (acuity and clinical assessment), including documentation and time-based indicators. Empathy and communication items were less frequently retained, reflecting challenges in operationalization.

CONCLUSION: This study provides a content-validated instrument (N-TriQAT) to assess nurse-led triage quality. Further psychometric evaluation and digital integration may facilitate its implementation in practice, supporting safer and higher-quality emergency care.

articles.title: Advancements in therapeutic targets and drug development for hyperuricemia: Mechanisms, progress, and challenges.
articles.abstract: Hyperuricemia (HUA), characterized by elevated serum uric acid levels, is associated with various comorbidities such as gout, metabolic syndrome, cardiovascular diseases, renal disorders and diabetes, significantly compromising patients' quality of life. The global prevalence of hyperuricemia has increased, with a growing burden reported among younger populations, highlighting the need for effective management strategies. However, current urate-lowering therapies remain limited in variety and efficacy. Long-term urate-lowering therapy is indicated for symptomatic primary hyperuricemia (e.g., gout, tophi, or uric acid nephrolithiasis), whereas its use in asymptomatic cases remains controversial, with recommendations varying across guidelines, particularly for high-risk individuals. Even for patients who meet the treatment criteria, available drugs often prove inadequate, particularly in refractory cases, revealing a critical gap in safe and effective treatment options. To address this challenge, this review narratively outlines the key targets in urate-lowering therapy, including xanthine oxidase for uric acid production, the renal reabsorption transporter URAT1, and serum uric acid regulation, along with their underlying mechanisms. It also summarizes recent advances in urate-lowering agents and compares their pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic profiles. Beyond conventional pharmacological treatments, this review discusses emerging therapeutic strategies, including probiotic-based interventions, small interfering RNA -based therapies, and natural products. Furthermore, recent genetic studies and multi-omics analyses have identified potential therapeutic genes that merit further investigation and could inform the development of future treatments. By synthesizing findings from international research, this review aims to lay the groundwork for the development of innovative therapeutic approaches and advanced pharmacological strategies for hyperuricemia.

articles.title: Frequency of occurrence, signalment, clinicopathologic and imaging findings, and outcomes with nontraumatic spontaneous intracranial hemorrhagic stroke in dogs.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the frequency, clinicopathologic and imaging findings, and outcomes in dogs with spontaneous intra-parenchymal hemorrhagic stroke (sIHS).

ANIMALS: Retrospective study involving 25 dogs.

CLINICAL PRESENTATION: Medical records were reviewed for signalment; neurological, clinicopathologic, and imaging findings; anatomic localization; comorbidities; therapy; and outcome in dogs with sIHS (2010 to 2024). Lesion number, location, and volume were recorded. Outcome was defined as excellent, good, or poor. Frequency was defined out of a contemporaneous population of dogs ≥ 6 years old with an acute presentation of neurological signs.

RESULTS: Affected dogs were older, small- to medium-breed dogs. Dogs often presented for neurological dysfunction reflective of a prosencephalic lesion (19 of 25 dogs) or new-onset seizures (13 of 25 dogs). A single, well-defined hemorrhage within the prosencephalon was commonly observed on MRI. Outcome was frequently excellent. Complete seizure remission was common. Larger lesion volumes were associated with poor outcomes. One dog experienced clinical signs suggestive of an additional sIHS 4 months after the initial stroke. Frequency of sIHS was 25 of 427 dogs (6%) ≥ 6 years old undergoing brain MRI.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: sIHS should be considered in older dogs with an acute onset of prosencephalic dysfunction and/or seizures. Following exclusion of secondary IHS, an excellent long-term outcome may be realized in dogs with sIHS, despite the presence of comorbidities. Short-term anticonvulsant therapy may be necessary. Development of poststroke epilepsy is unlikely. Dogs rarely experience another IHS.

articles.title: MorphSSF: a fast slope-sum adaptive-period dilation algorithm for photoplethysmography beat detection.
articles.abstract: Detecting heartbeats in photoplethysmography (PPG) underlies heart-rate, heart-rate-variability and arrhythmia analysis on wearable and clinical devices, and must be both efficient and accurate. Several accurate benchmark detectors, especially the multi-scale peak-and-trough family (MSPTD/MSPTDfast), rely on costly local-maxima scalograms; we seek a detector that improves the benchmark-wide speed-accuracy trade-off rather than merely accelerating one baseline.Approach: MorphSSF converts each PPG window to a slope-sum function (SSF), estimates the dominant pulse period from a band-limited autocorrelation, and selects candidates as fixed points of a period-matched running-maximum dilation on the SSF. This combines systolic-upstroke enhancement with adaptive period spacing using one-dimensional operations and no scalogram. We evaluate under identical conditions on seven datasets (544 recordings) with benchmark-wide rank tests, detector-specific exclusions and one-to-one matching. Separate fixed-point C and causal MATLAB variants are evaluated.Main results: MorphSSF has the best mean dataset F1 rank. Against MSPTDfast (v2), sensitivity tests favour MorphSSF on five datasets (including a zero median effect on CapnoBase); F1 is higher on MIMIC-test, MIMIC-train and PPG-DaLiA, while positive predictive value (PPV) is lower on WESAD. Both pooled and equal-dataset analyses favour MorphSSF in F1 against all eight baselines. MorphSSF is 3.05-218.18× faster than the eight baselines, including 3.23× faster than MSPTDfast (v2), based on median runtime ratios across recordings. All detectors receive the same prefiltered PPG input, with this shared filtering step excluded from runtime measurements.Significance: Period-adaptive detection on the slope-sum provides an efficient, scalogram-free approach to PPG beat detection.&#xD.

articles.title: Multivariate Searchlight Decoding of Structural Disconnection and Network Features for Predicting Post-Stroke Deficits.
articles.abstract: Lesion-symptom mapping and structural disconnection analyses have advanced our understanding of post-stroke deficits but remain predominantly based on forward inference, limiting identification of regions specifically predictive of behavioral impairment. We developed a multivariate voxelwise searchlight decoding framework for inverse inference integrating probabilistic structural disconnection with network-topological features.Approach. The analysis included 326 stroke patients from the GRECogVASC cohort assessed six months after stroke. For each patient, an age-specific probabilistic structural disconnection map was reconstructed using normative diffusion MRI tractography from 403 healthy controls. Within each voxel-centered searchlight, four features were extracted: disconnection probability, degree, clustering coefficient, and closeness centrality. Support vector machine classifiers were trained within deficit-specific decoding spaces using balanced bootstrap aggregation and majority voting to predict motor, executive, and processing-action-speed impairments. Statistical significance was assessed using 1,000 permutations, retaining voxels that consistently performed above chance across bootstrap iterations. Decoding-derived regions were subsequently assessed for within-cohort individual-level classification. Main results. Initial validation focused on left and right motor impairments, identifying predictive regions primarily within the contralateral precentral gyrus, internal capsule, and corticospinal tract, with mean accuracy ranges of 68.7-77.9%, 66.4-74.6%, and 64.8-71.8%, respectively. At the individual level, decoding-derived masks preserved overall classification performance, with accuracy improvements of up to 2.6% for individual deficits while reducing voxel dimensionality by up to 95.4%. Executive dysfunction and processing-action-speed deficits showed statistically above-chance but lower accuracies (54.5-66.9%). Executive dysfunction involved predominantly left-lateralized frontotemporal regions, whereas processing-action-speed deficits involved distributed fronto-insular, temporal, parietal, visual-association, and commissural pathways.Significance. The multivariate searchlight decoding framework integrating structural disconnection and network topology provides an inverse-inference approach complementary to lesion- and disconnection-symptom mapping for identifying spatially specific predictive patterns after stroke. The strong motor findings provide proof-of-concept support for the approach, whereas the cognitive results support its extension to distributed behavioral domains while underscoring the need for independent replication before neuroanatomical or clinical interpretation (Clinical trial registration: NCT01339195).

articles.title: Workplace exposure characteristics and risk perception of pneumoconiosis among coal mine workers in Mpumalanga Province, South Africa.
articles.journal: Journal of occupational and environmental hygiene
articles.abstract: Pneumoconiosis remains a major occupational health concern among coal mine workers, particularly in high-exposure settings. Understanding both workplace exposure characteristics and workers' risk perception is essential for effective prevention and control strategies. A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted among 239 coal mine workers in Mpumalanga Province, South Africa. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire capturing socio-demographic characteristics, workplace exposure variables, and risk perception of pneumoconiosis using Likert-scale items. A composite exposure index (0 to 3) and a risk perception score (10 to 50) were generated. Descriptive statistics were computed, and associations were assessed using bivariate and multivariable logistic regression as well as ordinal logistic regression models. The majority of participants were male (71.5%) and worked in underground mining (52.3%). High workplace exposure index scores were observed in 78.2% of workers, while 74.9% demonstrated high-risk perception. However, the estimated association between workplace exposure conditions and risk perception was limited (AOR = 0.97; 95% CI: 0.47-1.98), suggesting that workplace exposure characteristics and perceived risk did not necessarily align. Higher age was associated with increased odds of elevated risk perception (AOR = 1.38; 95% CI: 1.04-1.82). Associations for exposure level, sex, and education were comparatively weaker and accompanied by confidence intervals that included the null value. In the ordinal model, female workers had higher odds of elevated risk perception (OR = 1.88; 95% CI: 1.09-3.23). The estimated association between exposure and risk perception was close to null and imprecise (AOR = 0.97; 95% CI: 0.47-1.98). Despite high levels of occupational exposure, risk perception did not consistently align with exposure among coal mine workers. The findings indicate that occupational exposure and risk perception may not always align among coal mine workers, highlighting the need for further research to better understand factors influencing perceptions of pneumoconiosis risk.

articles.title: Titanium dioxide exposure in the Western Australian mining industry: Implications for compliance with current and proposed exposure limits.
articles.journal: Journal of occupational and environmental hygiene
articles.abstract: Titanium dioxide (TiO2) is widely used in mining and industrial processes and is generally considered to have low toxicity; however, inhalation of fine and ultrafine particles has been associated with adverse respiratory effects. Recent proposals to substantially reduce workplace exposure limits (WELs), including a respirable limit of 0.3 mg/m³ for ultrafine/nanoscale particles and 2.4 mg/m³ for fine/pigment-grade particles, have raised questions regarding future industry compliance with the proposed limits. This study analyzed de-identified exposure data sourced from the Western Australia Department of Local Government, Industry Regulation and Safety (LGIRS) Safety Regulatory System (SRS) to evaluate TiO2 exposures in the Western Australian (WA) mining industry. A total of 604 personal inhalable exposure samples collected between 2018 and 2025 were included. Descriptive statistics, exceedance analysis, and temporal trends were assessed against the current WEL of 10 mg/m³ for inhalable TiO2 and the proposed WELs of 0.3 mg/m³ for ultrafine/nanoscale TiO2 and 2.4 mg/m³ for fine/pigmentary-grade TiO2. Exposure levels were consistently low, with most results well below both the current and proposed WELs. Only one sample exceeded the numerical value of the proposed ultrafine/nanoscale limit, while the second-highest value, 0.12 mg/m³, remained below all proposed exposure limits. No samples exceeded the proposed 2.4 mg/m³ respirable WEL, and trends were stable or decreasing over time. Because the samples represented the inhalable fraction, comparison with proposed respirable limits provides conservative evidence of compliance. These findings indicate that the WA mining industry is well positioned to meet more stringent particle-size-specific exposure standards.

articles.title: Healthy Lifestyle Score and the Risk of Cardiovascular Disease, Cancer, and Mortality in an Asian Population: Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Healthy lifestyle behaviors are key modifiable factors for the prevention of chronic diseases and premature mortality. Composite lifestyle scores provide a practical framework for capturing the combined impact of multiple health behaviors, but prospective evidence from multiethnic Asian populations remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study examined the associations between a composite healthy lifestyle score and the risk of cardiovascular diseases, cancer, and all-cause mortality in a multiethnic Asian population.

METHODS: We analyzed prospective data from 9920 participants of the Singapore Multi-Ethnic Cohort who were free of major chronic diseases at baseline. A healthy lifestyle score was constructed from 5 components: BMI, smoking, physical activity, diet quality, and screen time. Scores ranged from 0 to 10, with higher scores reflecting healthier lifestyles. An expanded score, including mental well-being, was examined in a subset. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs were estimated using the Cox proportional hazards model for acute myocardial infarction (AMI), stroke, cancer, and all-cause mortality, adjusting for sociodemographic factors, energy intake, family history of cancer or heart disease, and menopause status.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 14 years, 457 AMI cases, 322 stroke cases, 707 cancer incident cases, and 631 deaths were identified. More favorable lifestyle scores were associated with lower risk of cardiovascular outcomes and mortality, consistent with a dose-response relationship. Compared to participants scoring 8 to 10, those with the lowest score (0-3) had more than 2 times the risk of AMI (HR 2.13, 95% CI 1.47-3.07), stroke (HR 3.21, 95% CI 2.12-4.85), and all-cause mortality (HR 2.01, 95% CI 1.46-2.78). In contrast, no significant associations were observed for cancer incidence. Incorporating mental well-being into the lifestyle score yielded similar results.

CONCLUSIONS: Adherence to a healthy lifestyle was associated with a lower risk of AMI, stroke, and mortality in a multiethnic Asian cohort, highlighting the importance of integrated lifestyle approaches for chronic disease prevention.

articles.title: Anticipated Effects of Using a Poststroke Patient Portal for Stroke Survivors and Carers: Semistructured Interview Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Digital technologies are increasingly incorporated into long-term self-management of health conditions, yet their social impact on stroke survivors and carers remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study explores how stroke survivors and carers view a prototype web-based application ("portal") that allows patients to access and contribute up-to-date information about their health and care poststroke and how this might impact their self-management practices.

METHODS: Through 27 semistructured interviews with 21 stroke survivors and 6 informal carers (performing unpaid care work), we explore the enablers of and barriers to the adoption and use of a portal for stroke survivors. To support discussions, participants were shown images of the portal prototype that displayed various features, including a self-living ability assessment, blood pressure monitoring, and an overview of exemplar personal data.

RESULTS: Four themes were identified to articulate the anticipated effects of the portal: (1) portals as potential tools to empower through enabling survivors and carers to access stroke knowledge and enhance self-management; (2) portals as a method that could offer practical support for recovery management, therefore helping survivors manage their recovery; (3) hesitancy about using a portal, particularly regarding tracking recovery through personal data input; and (4) portals as a method to potentially share information to help keep family, friends, and wider support networks informed about their health and its management. Anticipated experiences also varied by social position. Young stroke survivors, for example, said they would value age-appropriate peer connections, while carers anticipated concerns about additional workload. Participants also felt that family members often lacked understanding of stroke impacts, suggesting that portals could help facilitate better communication about invisible and complex disabilities.

CONCLUSIONS: The anticipated benefits of digital tools for empowering patients need to be weighed against the complexity of people's health and the additional responsibility digital interventions place on carers to communicate for those with severe disabilities. Our findings suggest that for a portal to be effective, it would need to address not only people's medical needs but also their social needs, especially their use of informal care. Further research is needed, including with an implemented portal, to understand the use of portals over extended periods.

articles.title: Horizon-Aware Forecasting of Hypertension Prevalence and Mean Total Cholesterol in Chinese Men: Retrospective Leakage-Controlled Benchmark Study Comparing Statistical, Machine-Learning, and Neural Models.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Forecasts of population-level cardiovascular risk factors can support surveillance and planning, but annual country-level health series are often short. With only 30 or 39 annual values per target, model flexibility can outpace the information available for training, making leakage control, repeated temporal evaluation, and comparison with simple baselines essential.

OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to compare statistical, classical machine-learning, and neural forecasting models for age-standardized prevalence of hypertension (ASPH) and mean total cholesterol (MTC) in Chinese men and to test whether attention or substantially greater neural capacity provides consistent predictive benefit.

METHODS: The authors analyzed 2 officially sourced annual series: ASPH for Chinese men aged 30 to 79 years (1990-2019; 30 observations) and MTC for Chinese men aged 18 years or older (1980-2018; 39 observations). No series was interpolated, extrapolated, imputed, smoothed, spliced, or synthetically extended. Leakage-controlled expanding-window evaluation began after 21 observations and assessed 1-, 2-, and 5-year horizons. Classical machine-learning and neural models used a fixed primary lookback of 3 (L=3), with nested lookback selection disabled; neural models used 10 fixed seeds. Performance was assessed with root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error, mean absolute scaled error, root mean squared scaled error, symmetric mean absolute percentage error, directional accuracy, mean error, median error, diagnostic R², prespecified neural-ablation inference, empirical forecast-interval coverage, and computational-cost reporting.

RESULTS: Statistical models had the lowest RMSE in all 6 target-horizon cells. Autoregressive integrated moving average won for ASPH at h=1 (RMSE 0.000178), h=2 (RMSE 0.000578), and h=5 (RMSE 0.004324), and for MTC at h=1 (RMSE 0.000400) and h=2 (RMSE 0.001479); error-trend-seasonal state space won for MTC at h=5 (0.006991). Classical machine-learning and primary neural models won no cells. Removing attention reduced RMSE in 5 of 6 ablation cells, while the compact architecture had lower RMSE than Original23K in 5 of 6 cells; formal differences were detected for both contrasts at ASPH h=1 and h=2, whereas ASPH h=5 (n=5) was descriptive only. Predictive intervals often undercovered. The benchmark completed all 7242 planned output-producing fits.

CONCLUSIONS: Simple statistical forecasting remained highly competitive in these short, retrospectively estimated annual series. Greater complexity did not ensure better point prediction, and neither attention nor larger capacity conferred a consistent advantage. Point accuracy did not ensure well-calibrated predictive uncertainty; findings were conditional on the 2 targets, target-specific horizons, and small evaluation samples.

articles.title: Cross-Site Stability of Embedding Model Rankings for Known-Item Retrieval From Clinical Notes: Two-Corpus Comparative Evaluation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Retrieval-augmented generation over clinical text depends on the embedding model chosen-a choice that interacts with documentation genre. Cross-site stability of embedding-model rankings has not been evaluated on real electronic health record (EHR) narratives with genre held constant; public benchmarks are predominantly single-source, and multi-institution evaluations compare models and query formulations within tasks rather than ranking stability across institutions.

OBJECTIVE: The aim of the study is to test whether embedding model rankings transfer across 2 institutional EHR corpora, with genre held constant; to examine the contributions of model, site/corpus, and genre and their dependence on scoring; and to test whether the dominant contributor depends on model-panel composition.

METHODS: We compared 13 embedding models on a known-item passage-to-source-document task, each query a deterministic 2-sentence excerpt from its target, in a 2×2 design crossing site/corpus (Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center via MIMIC-IV-Note [Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV Clinical Notes Module] and University of California, San Francisco via ER-Reason) with genre (discharge summary and imaging report). Query sentences were removed from their targets before indexing to prevent verbatim overlap, notes were deduplicated after normalization, models used their recommended pooling, long documents were scored as overlapping chunks by maximum similarity, and cell sizes were matched (N=1235 per cell). Effectiveness was measured by mean reciprocal rank at 10, rank transfer by Kendall τ and selection regret, and variance by factorial decomposition (η2). Transfer, regret, and the contrastive-panel decomposition carry 95% patient-clustered bootstrap intervals.

RESULTS: Among the 8 contrastive models, cross-site Kendall τ was 0.86 (95% CI 0.64-1.00) for discharge and 0.64 (95% CI 0.36-0.86) for imaging. The model×site interaction was small under every scoring choice (η2=0.005-0.029); the site/corpus main effect was negligible under best-chunk scoring (η2=0.000) but scoring-dependent (0.172 under mean-pooling). Cross-site selection regret was 0 for imaging and up to 0.033 for discharge (~10% of the destination's best mean reciprocal rank; intervals 0-0.071). Adding 5 nonretrieval masked-language-model comparators moved the largest term to model (η2=0.874): the dominant-factor question is panel-sensitive, while the qualitative transfer conclusion was unchanged.

CONCLUSIONS: For known-item retrieval from clinical notes at 2 US academic medical centers, embedding-model rankings showed positive cross-site concordance, moderate for imaging and strong for discharge summaries-with intervals wide enough that direction, not magnitude, is the finding. Which factor dominates absolute effectiveness depends on the panel evaluated: primary contrastive-panel scoring favors genre, whereas adding nonretrieval comparators makes model choice dominant; so, claims about major determinants are panel-specific. Cross-site model selection incurred zero to modest performance loss. When documentation genre and retrieval configuration are matched, model-selection results from one institutional EHR corpus may be a useful starting point for another, although local confirmation remains warranted.

articles.title: Classroom Integration of AI-Simulated Patients and Automated Feedback in Doctoral Psychotherapy Training: Longitudinal Mixed Methods Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Psychotherapy education increasingly emphasizes technology-assisted methods that extend deliberate practice beyond human supervision. AI has enabled automated skill assessment and patient simulations, yet few studies have examined how students experience such tools in real-world settings alongside established practice modalities.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to evaluate students' experiences with AI-augmented deliberate practice embedded in an existing psychotherapy course sequence. Secondary aims included identifying implementation barriers, ethical and pedagogical considerations, and factors influencing students' acceptance of AI-assisted learning.

METHODS: Participants were 29 first-year clinical psychology doctoral students in a 2-quarter psychotherapy sequence at an American Psychological Association-accredited program. In the fall course, students completed weekly peer role-plays and could optionally submit transcripts to CARE for AI feedback to supplement peer feedback. In the winter course, students completed required weekly deliberate practice through Skillsetter video vignettes and could optionally practice with CARE's voice-based AI-simulated patients, receiving AI and instructor feedback afterward. Surveys with Likert-type and free-response items were voluntary in the fall and required in the winter; 9 and 25 students completed them, respectively. Analyses included descriptive statistics, matched-pairs testing, and thematic analysis.

RESULTS: In the fall course (n=9), where privacy concerns and survey nonresponse limited data on AI feedback, students rated peer feedback higher than AI feedback on being constructive and helpful (median 3, IQR 3-3 vs median 2, IQR 2-2; P=.02) and recognizing areas to improve (mean 5.22, SD 0.83 vs mean 4.33, SD 0.87; P=.046), citing transcription errors and a narrow focus on empathy while valuing AI's alternative phrasing. In the winter course (n=25), Skillsetter was rated higher than CARE only for learning from mistakes (mean 4.52, SD 2.00 vs mean 3.20, SD 2.04; P=.03); immersion, spontaneous responding, communication beyond words, and alliance building did not differ significantly. Students valued CARE for interactive practice not possible with vignettes but reported undetected vocal pauses (20/25, 80%), insufficient realism (14/25, 56%), and limited emotional expression (13/25, 52%), and raised concerns about AI replacing peer support (22/25, 88%) and peer interaction (20/25, 80%). Asked about AI broadly, students expressed mixed views, citing concerns about supplanted relational dynamics, nonconsensual data use, and generative AI's environmental impacts.

CONCLUSIONS: Embedding AI-augmented deliberate practice into an existing course sequence was feasible, but students' experiences favored established methods: they preferred human over AI feedback and described video vignettes as more realistic than voice-based AI interactions, while valuing AI-simulated patients for interactive practice other modalities could not provide. Implementation barriers included feedback quality, transcription accuracy, and instructor time required to supplement AI feedback. Perceptions of AI's instructional utility appeared contingent on students' trust in the technology, suggesting future deployments should weigh a sample's attitudes toward AI and its value relative to existing training resources.

articles.title: Imaging-Based AI for Predicting Pathological Complete Response in Esophageal Cancer After Neoadjuvant Therapy: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Imaging-based AI may help predict pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant therapy for esophageal cancer. However, an encouraging average diagnostic performance does not establish reliable performance across clinical settings or justify treatment decisions without further validation.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to assess the predictive performance of imaging-based AI across neoadjuvant strategies, distinguish internal from external validation, and examine limitations affecting interpretation.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched through August 7, 2026. Eligible English-language studies evaluated imaging-based AI against pathological assessment of pCR. PROBAST+AI (Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool plus Artificial Intelligence) assessed study quality and risk of bias; GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) assessed certainty for sensitivity, specificity, and diagnostic odds ratio (DOR). Bivariate random-effects models synthesized validation groups separately. CIs described uncertainty in average performance, whereas 95% prediction intervals (PIs) described true performance in a similar new study.

RESULTS: Thirty-three studies contributed 27 internal-validation datasets with 1891 patients and 16 external-validation datasets with 777 patients. Ten publications contributed to both groups. The sum was 2668 validation observations; the unique patient count across datasets and publications could not be verified. Internal sensitivity was 0.77 (95% CI 0.72-0.81; PI 0.57-0.89), specificity 0.82 (95% CI 0.78-0.86; PI 0.60-0.93); DOR, 15.49 (95% CI 11.16-21.50); and area under the curve (AUC), 0.86 (95% CI 0.83-0.89). External sensitivity was 0.73 (95% CI 0.61-0.81; PI 0.34-0.93), specificity 0.83 (95% CI 0.73-0.90; PI 0.36-0.98), DOR 12.93 (95% CI 7.25-23.07), and AUC 0.84 (95% CI 0.79-0.89). DOR PIs were 5.40-44.44 and 2.40-69.62, respectively. Thirty-two studies were conducted in China, and 12 had high validation risk of bias. All GRADE-assessed outcomes had very low certainty. Selecting the first eligible imaging model reported in each article instead of the highest-AUC model showed modest decreases in average performance across 16 internal and 10 external datasets; incomplete alternative-model reporting limited interpretation. Single study algorithm estimates were reported descriptively, without ranking algorithms or interpreting their CIs as evidence of between study consistency or generalizability.

CONCLUSIONS: By combining multiple neoadjuvant strategies and separating validation stages, this review extends earlier neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (NCRT)-focused syntheses and identifies priorities for further model evaluation. Imaging-based AI may support response assessment, but wide PIs, risk of bias, and very low evidence certainty preclude routine clinical adoption without prospective, geographically diverse validation. Future studies should evaluate prespecified models in independent populations, report clinically relevant decision thresholds, and assess calibration and patient outcomes. Until such evidence is available, these models should be considered investigational adjuncts to response assessment and should not independently guide organ preservation or omission of surgery after neoadjuvant treatment.

articles.title: Identifying Metabolic Pathways That Drive Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Protocol for a Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a disorder characterized by hyperglycemia that is first recognized during pregnancy due to a mismatch between placental insulin production and increased maternal need, exacerbating insulin resistance. Few studies have systematically examined the metabolic markers and pathways underlying GDM from diagnosis through the postnatal period, including placental metabolic changes through metabolomics studies.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the metabolite profiles identified through metabolomics, as well as the associated pathways responsible for hyperglycemia during pregnancy and the postpartum period, in mothers with GDM compared with mothers without diabetes during pregnancy.

METHODS: We plan to recruit an equal number of patients with GDM and age- and BMI-matched mothers without GDM. Anthropometric data are collected at the first visit. Samples are collected at 3 time points: serum or plasma samples at the time of GDM diagnosis or at the first visit after diagnosis (24-28 weeks of gestation), placental and cord blood samples during delivery, and postnatal serum samples 4 to 12 weeks after delivery. Macroscopic and microscopic features of the placenta will be noted, and a histological score will be derived. Using liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS) with an untargeted approach, metabolite profiles will be identified in serum samples collected at diagnosis and postpartum, cord blood samples, and placental samples from both groups. The raw mass spectrometry (MS) data will be analyzed using the company-provided MS operator software. After data normalization, univariate analyses will be performed. Subsequently, all statistical analyses will be performed using MetaboAnalyst. Through these analyses, differences in the metabolite profiles and their pathways between mothers with and without GDM across pregnancy, starting from the diagnosis of GDM, will be identified. Data will be analyzed using R software. Clinical and demographic data will be presented as percentages, means, or medians, as appropriate. Logistic regression will be performed to assess the association between biomarkers and the placental histological score.

RESULTS: Ethics approval for the study was obtained from the Christian Medical College Vellore Ethics Committee, along with an institutional research grant in January 2025 and an Endocrine Society of Tamil Nadu grant in May 2026. Recruitment for the study began in June 2025 and was completed by June 2026; as of January 2026, a total of 35 patients had been recruited. The analysis of the samples using LC-MS, along with further statistical analysis, is expected to be completed in the first half of 2027.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings from this study will provide insight into the metabolites or biomarkers, as well as the metabolic pathways involved, in the pathogenesis of GDM across the life course of mothers, compared with those of normoglycemic mothers, and will offer potential insight into the role of the placenta in GDM.

articles.title: Safety and Effectiveness of Motherwort Injection for Hemostasis and Menstrual Regulation: Protocol for a Prospective, Observational, Multicenter Real-World Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Motherwort injection (MI) is a traditional Chinese medicine injection widely used for hemostasis and menstrual regulation in obstetrics and gynecology. Although clinical trials and systematic reviews have demonstrated its effectiveness for specific indications, comprehensive real-world evidence (RWE) regarding its safety, effectiveness, and use patterns across diverse clinical settings remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of MI in routine clinical practice and to generate RWE to support its rational use in women receiving treatment for approved obstetric and gynecological indications.

METHODS: This prospective, observational, multicenter real-world registry study plans to enroll 20,000 patients receiving MI for approved obstetric and gynecological indications in routine clinical practice in China. Treatment decisions, including whether to use MI and the dose and duration of treatment, as well as the use of concomitant medications, are made independently by treating physicians. Safety outcomes include the occurrence, type, severity, and incidence of adverse events and adverse drug reactions (ADRs). Effectiveness outcomes are assessed according to the clinical indication and include perioperative bleeding, postpartum hemorrhage, postabortion bleeding and menstrual resumption, uterine involution, menstrual regulation, and treatment satisfaction. Descriptive statistics will be used to characterize patient characteristics, MI use, and safety and effectiveness outcomes. Prespecified subgroup analyses will examine heterogeneity across major clinical groups. An exploratory nested case-control analysis with 1:4 matching and conditional logistic regression will be used to investigate factors associated with the occurrence of ADRs.

RESULTS: This study has received funding and obtained ethics approval in March 2024 (approval P24003-PJ03). Participant recruitment began on March 31, 2026. By September 2026, a total of 774 participants had been enrolled and included in the study database. The protocol specifies a target sample size of 20,000 participants, with data collection, monitoring, and quality control being conducted according to standardized study procedures. Data analysis has not yet commenced, and the study findings are expected to be published in October 2027.

CONCLUSIONS: This study will provide large-scale RWE regarding the safety and effectiveness of MI in obstetric and gynecological practice. The findings are expected to support postmarketing safety surveillance, optimize clinical decision-making, and contribute to the evidence-based evaluation of traditional Chinese medicine injections.

articles.title: Withdrawal-related calls to a statewide poison control center: a ten-year review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Poison control centers are commonly utilized by the public and healthcare providers following potentially harmful substance exposures. Less frequently, poison control centers are contacted regarding substance withdrawal. This study characterizes a decade of withdrawal-related calls to a statewide poison control center and explores their potential value in identifying emerging public health concerns.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective review of all calls to a statewide poison control center from 2015-2024 that were classified as "withdrawal" for reason of call. Variables assessed included year of call, patient demographics, substance(s) involved, disposition, and medical outcome. Medical outcomes were categorized using National Poison Data System® definitions as minor, moderate, or major. Descriptive statistics were performed.

RESULTS: During the study period, 198 withdrawal-related calls were identified, averaging approximately 20 annually. Most calls originated from hospitals (58.1%), while 36.9% came from private residences. The most frequently implicated substances were tianeptine (24.2%), opioids (20.7%), and benzodiazepines (14.1%). Tianeptine first appeared in 2019 and contributed substantially to an increase in withdrawal-related calls beginning in 2020. The median patient age was 35 years, and 53.0% were male. Overall, 37.4% of cases resulted in at least a moderate medical outcome (34.8% moderate, 2.5% major). Tianeptine accounted for the largest proportion of moderate or major outcomes, followed by opioids, benzodiazepines, gamma-hydroxybutyrate, antidepressants, and phenibut. Sixty-three patients (31.8%) required hospital admission, including 36 (18.2%) admitted to an intensive care unit; tianeptine was associated with 27.8% of ICU admissions. No deaths were documented.

DISCUSSION: This ten-year review demonstrates that withdrawal-related calls represent a small but clinically important component of PCC utilization. Although PCCs are traditionally associated with the management of acute toxic exposures, our findings highlight their broader role in providing consultation for substance withdrawal syndromes and their value as a real-time toxicovigilance resource. An important finding of this study was the changing pattern of substances associated with withdrawal over time.

CONCLUSION: Poison control center utilization extends beyond substance exposure and includes management of substance withdrawal. Withdrawal-related calls may provide valuable surveillance data regarding emerging substance use trends and public health concerns, particularly involving tianeptine and opioids.

articles.title: 120° Widefield SS-OCTA Assessment of Retinal and Choroidal Vascular Changes After Panretinal Photocoagulation in Severe NPDR.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate retinal and choroidal blood vascular changes before and after panretinal photocoagulation (PRP) in severe non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR) patients using widefield swept-source optical coherence tomography angiography (SS-OCTA) covering 120° fundus.

METHODS: A prospective longitudinal study enrolled 55 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and severe non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR), contributing 95 eyes scheduled for PRP, which was administered in four weekly sessions. SS-OCTA scanning (6 mm × 6 mm and 24 mm × 20 mm mode) was performed pre- and 3 months post-PRP. Quantitative parameters included foveal avascular zone (FAZ) size and vessel density (VD) of superficial retinal vessels (SRV), deep retinal vessels (DRV), choriocapillaris (CC), and large and medium choroidal vessels (LMVC).

RESULTS: Compared to pre-PRP values, significant reductions in VD were observed in the DRV (p < .0001) and CC layers (p < .0001) at 3 months after PRP. Reductions in VD were also observed in the SRV and LMVC layers (p = .02, p = .0118, respectively) before and 3 months after PRP. FAZ size and logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) remained unchanged before and 3 months after PRP. FAZ size was positively correlated with BCVA at both pre-PRP and 3-month post-PRP assessments.

CONCLUSION: Widefield SS-OCTA demonstrates that PRP in severe NPDR induces layer-specific microvascular reductions, most pronounced in the deep retina and CC, concurrent with reduced VD of LMVC layer, while preserving central macular structure and function at 3 months after PRP.

articles.title: Characterization of a variable friction shoe for foot drop and pilot test with stroke patients.
articles.journal: Assistive technology : the official journal of RESNA
articles.abstract: Foot drop increases the risk of inadvertent ground contact during the swing phase of gait, which often leads to trips and falls. This study presents the design, characterization, and pilot trial of a variable friction (VF) shoe designed to reduce this risk by providing low friction during inadvertent ground contact and high-friction during stance and toe-off. Characterization results from bench-top testing demonstrated a consistent, load-dependent increase in coefficient of friction (CoF) across multiple surfaces that were maintained over year-long simulated wear. A healthy human-subject trial demonstrated reduced frictional scuff forces and trip events for the VF shoe versus conventional footwear. Three post-stroke patients completed an AB crossover take-home pilot trial where patients wore (A) the VF shoes for 2-weeks and (B) an ankle foot orthosis (AFO) with normal sneakers for 2-weeks. Pilot results showed promise: after the period wearing VF shoes, all subjects increased their 6-minute walk test (6MWT) distance and their 10 meter walk test (10MWT) speed. Results were mixed after the AFO arm. Together, these findings demonstrate the VF shoe's load-dependent frictional behavior, mechanical durability, and preliminary clinical feasibility, supporting its potential as a strategy to mitigate slip‑ and trip-related risk in individuals with foot drop.

articles.title: Meteorological factors, environmental allergen exposure, and individual susceptibility in thunderstorm asthma: a meta-analysis.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thunderstorm asthma is a rare but severe public health issue characterized by sudden asthma outbreaks linked to thunderstorms.

OBJECTIVE: Assess the associations between meteorological factors, environmental allergen exposure and individual susceptibility with thunderstorm asthma risk.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science for studies published up to March 2025. Random-effects models were used to analysis, with subgroup analyses by study type and geographical location. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 statistics, publication bias was evaluated via funnel plots and Egger's test. Sensitivity analyses tested the robustness of findings.

RESULTS: Research were classified into three categories: meteorological factors, environmental allergen exposure, and individual susceptibility factors. Meteorological factors were associated with a modest elevation (OR = 1.20, 95% CI: 1.05-1.37, I2 = 88.1%), with more pronounced effects observed in Europe (OR = 1.26, 95% CI: 1.17-1.37) and Asia (OR = 1.42, 95% CI: 1.04-1.93).
