Exposure to environmental allergens demonstrated a significant association with increased risk (OR = 6.32, 95% CI: 3.16-12.64, I2 = 53.4%), with the strongest effect noted in Oceania (OR = 6.99, 95% CI: 2.35-20.80). In contrast, individual susceptibility factors exhibited a weaker association (OR = 1.59, 95% CI: 0.84-2.98, I2 = 78.9%). Sensitivity analyses corroborated the robustness of these findings.

CONCLUSION: Environmental allergen exposure poses the greatest risk for thunderstorm asthma, followed by meteorological factors, with regional variations. These findings highlight the need for targeted public health strategies in high-risk regions.

articles.title: Green development of Cefuroxime-Loaded Chitosan Nanoparticle Microneedles using citric acid crosslinker: A New Approach for targeted Ocular Infection.
articles.abstract: This study aims to develop chitosan nanoparticles containing cefuroxime sodium, a BCS class 3 drug, which was encapsulated into the nanoparticles using a gelation method and then loaded into dissolving microneedles (DMNs) to enable ocular drug delivery. The nanoparticle formula contained chitosan, citric acid, cefuroxime sodium, and Pluronic F127 at a ratio of (1:1:1:0.05) and exhibited a particle size of 509.97 ± 0.47 nm, and entrapment efficiency (EE%) of 44.94%. The DMNs, prepared by the casting method, was fabricated from carboxymethyl cellulose sodium, sucrose, and polyvinylpyrrolidone, exhibited excellent mechanical strength. The nanoparticle-loaded DMNs successfully penetrated the corneal layer, with a cumulative drug delivery of 75.32 µg/cm2, which was significantly higher than that of DMNs loaded with conventional cefuroxime sodium. The nanoparticle formulation and the conventional cefuroxime sodium formulation had the same minimum inhibitory concentration of 0.90 µg/mL against Staphylococcus aureus, indicating that the pharmacological action was conserved. Additionally, compared to the conventional cefuroxime sodium (2.88 ± 0.05 cm), the nanoparticle formulation showed a noticeably broader inhibitory zone (3.48 ± 0.05 cm), suggesting an increase in antibacterial diffusion. In conclusion, the fabricated DMNs demonstrated sufficient mechanical strength to effectively penetrate the cornea and dissolve rapidly, which highlights their potential as a promising strategy for ocular drug delivery.

articles.title: Engineered Peptide Nanoparticle Targeting Both Bacterial Load Reduction and Bone Repair for the Treatment of Bone Infections.
articles.abstract: Bone infection is a common and serious complication in orthopedic surgery. Conventional antibiotic strategies frequently induce antibiotic resistance, leading to the persistence of bone infections. In this study, an engineered peptide nanoparticle named C8-IK21 was designed based on the coiled-coil motif. Specifically, C8-IK21 effectively targeted bacterial cell membranes, further exacerbating bacterial death through lipid peroxidation. At safe doses, local administration of C8-IK21 demonstrated high efficacy in treating S. aureus-infected cortical bone defects in mice. No detectable resistance emerged under the tested experimental conditions. Additionally, C8-IK21 exhibited anti-inflammatory activity. Furthermore, C8-IK21 could enter cells by binding to ADAM9, activating the ERK signaling pathway to regulate osteoblast differentiation. Meanwhile, C8-IK21 reduced the expression of ITGB1 via ADAM9, thereby inhibiting osteoclast differentiation and function. Moreover, the pro-osteogenic effect of C8-IK21 was validated in organoids. In conclusion, C8-IK21 represents a promising therapeutic approach for the treatment of refractory bacterial infections and bone homeostasis disorders.

articles.title: Swimming motility and type IV pili modulate phagocytosis by shaping physical interactions between Pseudomonas aeruginosa and macrophages.
articles.abstract: During chronic lung infections, Pseudomonas aeruginosa diversifies under selection from antibiotics, metabolic constraints, and host defenses. Macrophages are key sentinels of the innate immune system and play a central role in clearing airway pathogens. Yet, how they process heterogeneous bacterial populations remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate how P. aeruginosa evades phagocytosis under conditions that resemble chronic infection. We use an attenuated mutant lacking a functional type III secretion system (T3SS), which reduces macrophage killing, allowing us to isolate determinants of bacterial susceptibility to phagocytosis. Using transposon insertion sequencing (Tn-seq), we identify bacterial fitness factors under phagocytic selection. Our screen reveals that disruption of genes involved in swimming and twitching motility reduces uptake by macrophages. We find that defects in flagellar and type IV pili (T4P) function interfere with the physical interactions between bacteria and macrophages. Live-cell imaging shows that motility-deficient bacteria exhibit reduced surface accumulation and unstable attachment to macrophages, limiting their internalization. Clinical isolates with reduced swimming or twitching motility display similarly impaired uptake. We also test the influence of bacterial motility on macrophage survival by restoring T3SS activity in flagellar and T4P mutants. In the PAO1 background, most motility mutants retained the ability to kill macrophages indicating that cytotoxicity dominates bacteria-macrophage competition in the presence of a functional T3SS. However, the non-flagellated, hyper-piliated ΔfliCΔpilT mutant showed a surprisingly attenuated killing, which may reflect reduced bacterial encounters with macrophages, impaired engagement of cytotoxic effectors, or both. Together, our results show that swimming motility and type IV pili shape physical interactions between P. aeruginosa and macrophages, thereby influencing phagocytic uptake.

articles.title: Methotrexate use in ectopic pregnancy with baseline transaminase elevation.
articles.abstract: Ectopic pregnancy is a common complication in early pregnancy and remains a leading cause of first-trimester maternal morbidity (0.5 deaths per 100,000 live births). In hemodynamically stable patients, methotrexate is widely used as a fertility-preserving alternative to surgery. However, clinically significant hepatic disease is considered an absolute contraindication for methotrexate therapy. Current guidelines lack clarity concerning the management of patients with elevated liver enzymes, particularly those with metabolic risk factors such as polycystic ovary syndrome and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease, which are growing presentations in reproductive-aged women. We present a case of a tubal ectopic pregnancy managed with reduced-dose methotrexate in the setting of elevated liver enzymes, not seen previously in literature, followed by surgical intervention after medical management failure.

articles.title: The pore-forming protein APOL7C ruptures Leishmania major-containing parasitophorous vacuoles in dendritic cells to promote IL-12 production and the induction of T helper type 1 immunity.
articles.abstract: Classical dendritic cells (cDCs) are required for the efficient priming of T helper type 1 (Th1) immunity against Leishmania major infections in mice. They do so by producing large quantities of IL-12 in response to L. major infection. IL-12 in turn supports the generation of protective CD4+ Th1 cells. However, the mechanism(s) by which L. major instigates robust IL-12 production by cDCs has not been addressed. Here we show that expression of a pore-forming protein called APOL7C is induced in cDCs by L. major infection. APOL7C is expressed in the cytosol of host cells and, remarkably, upon infection is recruited to L. major parasitophorous vacuoles (PVs) where it induces PV rupture. PV rupture leads to the exposure of L. major-derived pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) to cytosolic pattern recognition receptors (PRRs). Cytosolic PRR signaling then drives IL-12 production by cDCs. Consequently, L. major challenge of APOL7C-deficient mice results in reduced numbers of IL-12 producing cDCs as well as a diminished Th1 response. In sum, our data indicate the presence of pore-forming proteins in the cytosol of cDCs that interfere with the intracellular niche of Leishmania to modulate immunity to these parasites.

articles.title: Baloxavir and molnupiravir protect against severe influenza A(H5N1) infection in immunosuppressed hamsters.
articles.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) viruses continue to expand their geographic and host range, raising concerns about zoonotic transmission and pandemic preparedness. Immunocompromised individuals often develop severe and prolonged disease, yet evidence guiding antiviral therapy remains limited. Here, we characterized the pathogenesis and assessed direct-contact transmission of an influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b genotype D1.1 virus recently isolated from a human case in British Columbia, Canada, in cyclophosphamide-immunosuppressed hamsters, with normal hamsters included for comparison of infection outcomes and viral shedding kinetics. We also evaluated the antiviral efficacy of oseltamivir (20 mg/kg twice daily for 5 days), baloxavir (50 mg/kg, 2 doses), and molnupiravir (50 or 200 mg/kg twice daily) as monotherapies or in combination (oseltamivir with low-dose molnupiravir) in immunosuppressed hamsters. While normal hamsters showed no mortality and achieved viral clearance, infection in immunosuppressed hamsters caused severe disease characterized by prolonged viral replication, neuroinvasion, and 75% mortality, with no direct-contact transmission detected. In the antiviral efficacy experiment, placebo-treated hamsters exhibited 50% mortality. Baloxavir resulted in 100% survival, shortened viral shedding, reduced viral replication and pulmonary inflammatory responses, and prevented neuroinvasion. High-dose molnupiravir also prevented mortality and achieved viral clearance in lung and brain tissues. Combination therapy resulted in 75% survival and similarly achieved viral clearance in both tissues, with reduced morbidity compared with oseltamivir and low-dose molnupiravir monotherapies. Oseltamivir resulted in 75% survival but failed to prevent severe clinical signs or reduce tissue viral titers, whereas low-dose molnupiravir showed outcomes comparable to placebo. These findings demonstrate the high pathogenicity of a human A(H5N1) isolate in immunosuppressed hamsters, support baloxavir as an effective therapeutic option, and identify molnupiravir-based regimens as promising strategies for severe influenza A(H5N1) infection.

articles.title: Cardiopulmonary exercise testing and health-related quality of life in children with idiopathic or heritable pulmonary arterial hypertension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive disease causing elevated pulmonary vascular resistance, right ventricular (RV) failure, and premature death. Idiopathic and heritable PAH impair functional capacity and health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) assesses exercise limitation and disease severity, yet its relationship with HRQoL has not been investigated in pediatric PAH.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: A retrospective multicenter study across three French tertiary pediatric cardiology centers was conducted (June 2023-April 2025). Children with idiopathic or heritable PAH who underwent CPET and completed the Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory (PedsQL 4.0) were included. Key CPET parameters were analyzed, and associations to HRQoL scores assessed via Spearman correlation.

RESULTS: Among 19 children (median age 11 years, median follow-up 32 months), exercise capacity was reduced (peak VO2 29 ml/kg/min; 74.5% predicted; Z-score -2.9), with ventilatory inefficiency (VE/VCO₂ slope 40). QoL scores were lower than normative values. No significant correlation was found between CPET parameters and HRQoL scores.

CONCLUSION: Children with idiopathic or heritable PAH present exercise limitation and impaired HRQoL, though CPET parameters were not correlated with HRQoL scores, reflecting limited statistical power. Larger studies are needed to clarify this relationship.

articles.title: Selective activation of macrophage innate signaling pathways and inflammatory responses to Orientia tsutsugamushi Karp and Gilliam strains.
articles.abstract: Orientia tsutsugamushi (Ot) is an obligate intracellular bacterium that can cause scrub typhus, an emerging but severely neglected disease with high mortality rates. Ot Karp and Gilliam strains account for most reported cases in Southeast Asia. Our group has reported that Karp-infected outbred and inbred mice exhibit more severe disease outcomes than their Gilliam-infected counterparts, likely due to their excessive inflammation and tissue injury. Macrophages (MΦs) are the main immune cell target for Ot and play a key role in host defense against infection; they are also key players in immune modulation and cytokine/chemokine production. However, it remains unclear as to how MΦ-Ot interactions impact disease outcomes. In this study, we focused on RNA-seq from C57BL/6 mouse-derived MΦs to reveal Ot infection- and strain-related immune signatures. While Ot infection modulated several common canonical pathways/genes, we identified unique pathway/gene signatures that were highly selective for Karp or Gilliam strain, respectively. Karp infection uniquely upregulated proinflammatory signaling and pattern recognition receptors, involving C-type lectin receptors (CLRs), including Mincle/Clec4e and Dectin-2/Clec4n. In contrast, Gilliam infection enhanced MΦ proliferation and DNA replication, and Gilliam strain grew better in M0-like MΦs than Karp strain. In IFN𝛾-primed (M1-like) MΦs; however, Karp exhibited significantly greater resistance against host killing than Gilliam, suggesting its superior ability to evade host immune responses. Overall, Karp strain preferentially upregulated CLRs and activated type 1-skewed inflammatory responses, but it is also relatively resistant to IFN𝛾-mediated killing. This study provides new insights into potential mechanisms underlying Ot strain-associated immune responses and disease outcomes.

articles.title: Serum ferritin kinetics and ferritin-derived ratios in hospitalised adults with dengue: A prospective serial biomarker study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dengue causes major morbidity and mortality across India, where early identification of patients progressing to dengue shock syndrome or severe hepatitis remains an unmet need. Serum ferritin reflects macrophage activation, but its serial kinetics and ferritin-derived composite indices have not been rigorously evaluated in adult Indian populations. We characterised serial ferritin kinetics and evaluated two ferritin-derived ratios: the Ferritin-to-Platelet Ratio (FPR) and the Ferritin/ALT Ratio (FLR).

METHODOLOGY: This prospective observational study enrolled 100 adult WHO 2009-confirmed dengue patients at SMIMER, Surat (June 2020-November 2021). Serum ferritin was measured by sandwich ELISA on hospital Days 1, 3 and 5 and was also analysed by day of illness; platelet count and transaminases were the lowest and highest values recorded during the stay, and outcomes were recorded if present at any time between admission and discharge. Severity was classified as non-severe (n = 68) or severe (n = 32). Non-circular endpoints-shock/DSS (n = 22), severe thrombocytopenia <20,000/μL (n = 28), and severe hepatitis AST/ALT ≥ 1,000 IU/L (n = 18)-were the primary outcomes for diagnostic accuracy. FPR and FLR were pre-specified composite indices and were compared with their component tests by paired DeLong tests.

PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: Ferritin showed a rise-peak-fall trajectory across hospital days, peaking on Day 3 (mean 955 ± 177 ng/ml; Friedman p < 10-16); by day of illness it rose from a median of 700 ng/ml (illness days ≤3) to 950 ng/ml (days 6-7) and then plateaued. FPR Day 1 separated the severity groups with AUC 0.704 (95% CI 0.579-0.830); severe patients showed five-fold higher median FPR than non-severe patients (39.0 vs 7.5; p = 0.001). Against shock/DSS, FPR Day 1 had AUC 0.801 (95% CI 0.688-0.898), no higher than platelet count alone (AUC 0.784; DeLong p = 0.41). FLR Day 1 discriminated severe hepatitis with AUC 0.995 (95% CI 0.988-1.000), no higher than ALT alone (AUC 1.000; DeLong p = 0.23), the variable that defines this outcome. Against non-circular outcomes, Ferritin Day 1 discriminated shock/DSS with AUC 0.789 and severe thrombocytopenia with AUC 0.727. The ferritin-platelet inverse correlation was demographic-independent (partial Spearman rho=-0.392; p < 0.001). Ferritin offered no incremental benefit over platelet count alone (NRI = 0.143; IDI = 0.000).

CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: Serum ferritin rose from admission to hospital Day 3 and was higher in patients with shock and severe thrombocytopenia. The Ferritin-to-Platelet Ratio and the Ferritin/ALT Ratio are low-cost, but neither discriminated better than the routine test it contains (platelet count or ALT). Because platelet count and transaminases entered the ratios as the lowest and highest values of the admission, and outcomes were recorded over the whole stay, both ratios are markers of disease severity rather than predictors of later shock or severe hepatitis. Prospective multi-centre studies with laboratory values and outcomes timed from admission are needed to test any predictive role.

articles.title: Cystic fibrosis: remarkable success but still not at the finish line.
articles.abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is an autosomal recessive, multisystem disease caused by variants in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene which leads to absent or decreased function of the CFTR protein and its regulation of ion flow through the epithelial cell channels. These channels are present in epithelial cells in multiple organs, and abnormal flow of chloride, bicarbonate, and sodium accounts for the bronchiectasis, malabsorption, diabetes, urolithiasis, liver disease, and infertility commonly seen in these patients. The development of compounds, referred to as highly effective modulators classified as potentiators and correctors, augment CFTR's role in the function of these ion channels and consequently have dramatically improved the life expectancy and quality of life in these patients. With the introduction of these modulators and earlier identification of the CF patient through newborn screening, median predicted survival is now 66 years of age; and there has been a marked decrease in the number of exacerbations, hospitalizations, and need for lung transplantation as well as a marked improvement in nutritional markers and fertility. Continued attention to and appreciation of a multidisciplinary approach, screening for complications, and further development of therapies for those individuals who do not benefit from the modulators are essential to further improve the outcomes of these patients. CF exemplifies and highlights the transformative potential of precision medicine but also illustrates the need to continue our efforts to develop a cure and further therapies to help those 8% who do not presently qualify for the modulators available today.

articles.title: Immune-inflammatory indices and a serum surrogate composite score of blood-brain barrier injury in acute ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic inflammation is linked to blood-brain barrier (BBB) breakdown in acute ischemic stroke (AIS), but the association between peripheral immune-inflammatory indices and BBB permeability remains unclear.

METHODS: We enrolled 286 AIS patients within 24 h of onset. Five indices (NLR, PLR, LMR, SII, SIRI) were calculated from admission samples. A serum surrogate score integrating MMP-9, S100B, and BDNF (not calibrated against DCE-MRI or CSF albumin quotient) indicated BBB injury.

RESULTS: All five indices correlated significantly with the surrogate score after Bonferroni correction (all adjusted p < 0.01). In adjusted regression, SII (β = 0.452, p < 0.001) and NLR (β = 0.387, p < 0.001) were independent correlates. SII had the highest adjusted AUC (0.768; 95% CI 0.711-0.819), indicating moderate discrimination for high surrogate-defined BBB injury. The SII-score association was stronger in patients with NIHSS ≥ 8 (P~interaction~=0.024), with a similar non-significant trend for infarct volume ≥15 mL (P~interaction~=0.067). SII correlated positively with MMP-9 (r = 0.402, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: SII and NLR are independently associated with a serum surrogate score of BBB injury in AIS. SII shows moderate discrimination and may aid early risk stratification, pending validation against gold-standard measures. The SII-MMP-9 correlation suggests shared inflammatory pathways warranting further study.

articles.title: "Kokobe" and "gwasi": Perceptions of leprosy in French Guiana.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leprosy remains endemic in French Guiana (FG), one of the last European territories with autochthonous cases. Despite its historical and sociocultural particularities, no study has specifically explored local perceptions of leprosy in this multicultural context. This study aimed to describe how patients with leprosy from different cultural backgrounds in FG hold alternative explanatory models and practices, and to explore cultural representations of leprosy among members of Western French Guiana (WFG) Maroon communities.

METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: A qualitative study was conducted between April and September 2025. Semi-structured interviews were held with 20 patients across FG health centres and 37 community members in WFG villages linked to the former Acarouany leprosarium. Recruitment continued until thematic saturation was reached, and interviews were subsequently analysed using thematic analysis Patients and WFG members from Maroon communities used culturally specific terms to refer to the disease, kokobe and gwasi, referring respectively to deformities and skin patches, associated with the disease. Spiritual explanations (taboo transgression, curse) predominated among Maroon and Haitian participants, whereas bacterial causation was rarely mentioned. Confusion with diabetes was common. Local plant-based remedies were widely used but did not compromise adherence to multidrug therapy, which was perceived as effective. While most patients in FG reported good social integration, some of them mentioned discriminatory attitudesamong close relatives and in broader social contexts and public services. However, significant family and/or community support was reported in most of the interviews.

CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: Leprosy in FG remains embedded in complex cultural representations that influence disclosure, diagnosis, and care pathways. Strengthening culturally sensitive communication, increasing awareness among health professionals, clarifying person-to-person transmission, and taking local practices into account could help improving adherence and understanding between health workers and patients.

articles.title: MicroRNA-based point-of-care diagnostics for emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases: from biomarker discovery to clinical implementation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are increasingly investigated as host-response biomarkers for infectious diseases, but translation from differential-expression studies to clinically deployable diagnostics remains limited.

AREAS COVERED: This review evaluates the diagnostic and translational potential of miRNAs across malaria, dengue, chikungunya, Zika virus infection, Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever, Japanese encephalitis and Nipah virus disease. Unlike prior reviews focused mainly on biomarker discovery or detection technologies, it provides a cross-disease translational perspective linking miRNA signatures with analytical and clinical validation, point-of-care development, clinical implementation, economic considerations and deployment in resource-limited settings.

EXPERT OPINION: The next phase of miRNA diagnostics should prioritize reproducible multi-miRNA signatures, standardized pre-analytical workflows and prospective multicentre validation rather than continued biomarker discovery alone. Clinical adoption will depend on integrating these signatures into affordable sample-to-answer platforms and demonstrating that results improve defined clinical decisions under real-world conditions.

articles.title: Acute Ethylene Glycol Poisoning Following Accidental Mineral Oil Ingestion With Severe Metabolic Acidosis, Acute Kidney Injury, Respiratory Failure, and Delayed Neurological Sequelae: A Case Report.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Ethylene glycol poisoning is uncommon but life-threatening. Early manifestations can mimic ethanol intoxication, while delayed recognition can lead to severe acid-base, renal, cardiopulmonary, and neurological complications. This report describes the case of a 57-year-old man who unintentionally ingested mineral oil containing ethylene glycol and presented with coma, a high anion gap metabolic acidosis, acute kidney injury, respiratory failure, and delayed neurological abnormalities. CASE REPORT A 57-year-old Han Chinese man developed dizziness, vomiting, wheezing, drowsiness, ataxia, dysarthria, and coma within 12 hours of accidental ingestion of mineral oil containing ethylene glycol. On admission, the Glasgow Coma Scale score was 3, and he had severe metabolic acidosis (pH 7.0, bicarbonate 2.70 mmol/L, anion gap 30.0 mmol/L), hyperkalemia, hypocalcemia, acute kidney injury, and respiratory failure. The blood ethylene glycol concentration was 456.8 μg/mL, and gastric contents were positive. Treatment included intubation, mechanical ventilation, ethanol therapy, correction of acidosis and electrolyte disturbances, organ support, and early bedside blood purification followed by continuous venovenous hemodialysis. Ethylene glycol was undetectable on day 5, and he was extubated on day 14. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) on day 19 showed a recent right periventricular infarct, chronic lacunar infarcts, white-matter demyelination, and microhemorrhages. He was transferred to the general ward on day 24 and discharged on day 30. At the 1-month follow-up, serum creatinine levels had returned to normal and neurological symptoms had improved. CONCLUSIONS Severe ethylene glycol poisoning should be suspected in patients with coma, vomiting, high anion gap metabolic acidosis, renal dysfunction, and a history of possible toxic alcohol exposure. Early antidotal therapy, extracorporeal treatment, serial toxicological, renal, respiratory, and neurological assessments and follow-up are essential.

articles.title: The Second Shift: Supporting Career Transitions for Experienced Nurses.
articles.journal: Journal for nurses in professional development
articles.abstract: Mixed-acuity units are increasingly replacing individualized intermediate and intensive care environments. Although this shift offers benefits, it poses unique challenges for experienced intermediate care nurses (RNs) transitioning to intensive care unit (ICU)-level responsibilities. To support this transition, nursing professional development practitioners at an academic medical center designed and implemented ICU Bootcamp. Using a theory-based approach, this educational intervention aimed to mitigate transition shock and close knowledge and skills gaps among intermediate RNs moving into mixed-acuity settings.

articles.title: Genetic determinants of direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) response: evidence, limitations and barriers to clinical implementation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) offer predictable pharmacokinetics and simplified dosing compared with warfarin, yet clinically important inter-individual variability in drug exposure, efficacy and safety persists. Pharmacogenomics can help explain this variability and advance precision anticoagulation.

AREAS COVERED: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on genetic determinants of the pharmacokinetics and clinical outcomes of dabigatran, rivaroxaban, apixaban and edoxaban, identified by searching PubMed, Embase and Web of Science from inception to May 2026. Evidence from candidate-gene studies, genome-wide association studies, systematic reviews and meta-analyses was synthesized and the magnitude of reported genetic effects were compared the non-genetic determinants of exposure. Variants in CYP3A4, CYP3A5, CES1, ABCB1 and ABCG2 have been investigated for their potential effects on DOAC disposition and response. CES1 variants, particularly rs2244613, rs8192935 and rs71647871, may influence dabigatran exposure, while transporter variants may affect absorption and elimination. CYP3A4/5 and ABCG2 variation has also been associated with altered rivaroxaban and apixaban pharmacokinetics. Evidence for edoxaban, including SLCO1B1 variation, remains limited.

EXPERT OPINION: Pharmacogenomics represents a promising component of individualized DOAC therapy, but routine clinical implementation is in progress. Prospective genotype-guided studies, validated polygenic and clinical-genetic scores, therapeutic concentration thresholds and diverse multiethnic validation are needed before pharmacogenomic testing can reliably inform DOAC selection and dosing.

articles.title: DRLCI: Dual-view Representation Learning Framework for Predicting Drug-Gene Interactions via Causal Intervention.
articles.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
articles.abstract: Investigating drug-gene interactions is essential for advancing personalized medicine and therapeutic innovation. In recent years, Graph Neural Network-based approaches have demonstrated significant potential for this task by utilizing diverse strategies, such as subgraph extraction and hypergraph modeling. However, these associative paradigms remain confined to observational statistics, primarily identifying superficial correlations rather than underlying causal mechanisms. Drug-gene prediction tasks are frequently hindered by hard negative samples acting as confounders, which lead existing methods to overweight biologically irrelevant nodes and introduce substantial noise. Moreover, relying solely on a single topological view restricts the prediction framework to a closed loop of established connections, impeding the discovery of novel interaction patterns. Addressing these deficiencies, we propose a dual-view representation learning framework. Initially, Relation-Aware graph convolution adaptively quantifies the differentiated contributions of neighboring nodes via an attention mechanism to capture key interaction patterns. To refine this procedure, we incorporate a causal intervention mask and a causally-debiased contrastive loss into the feature extraction stage, thereby optimizing the representation space and suppressing confounding effects. Finally, external medical prior knowledge is integrated into the prediction pipeline through a textual modality governed by a gated fusion mechanism. Comprehensive benchmark evaluations demonstrate that our framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on the DrugBank and DGIdb datasets.

articles.title: Graph-Based Minimally Supervised Risk Stratification for Prognosis Prediction in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
articles.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
articles.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is associated with poor outcomes, with 5-year survival after hospitalisation as low as 35-40%. Despite its growing prevalence, effective treatments remain limited. A major barrier to therapeutic success is the substantial biological and clinical heterogeneity within HFpEF, suggesting that distinct patient profiles may require different management strategies. This study investigates whether graph-based machine learning methods can identify distinct patient clusters within the HFpEF population and assess their relationships with clinical characteristics and outcomes. We analysed a multimodal dataset of 133 symptomatic HFpEF patients, comprising more than 240 K attributes derived from comprehensive cardiovascular assessment. These included cardiac MRI, echocardiography, circulating biomarkers of fibro-inflammation, and high-resolution proteomics. Five conventional unsupervised clustering methods were first applied but failed to produce clinically coherent groups, largely due to the complexity and multimodality of the data. To address this, we implemented a minimally supervised Graph Neural Network (GNN) that incorporated limited label information while modelling relationships between patients. This approach produced five clusters with potential clinical relevance. Importantly, cluster membership remained significantly associated with survival after adjustment for established clinical risk factors, including age, sex, BNP levels, symptom burden, and kidney function. Internal validation yielded an accuracy of 0.706 and an $F1$-score of 0.613, indicating reasonably consistent performance and suggesting that graph structure may aid generalisation and class-wise prognostic prediction. Overall, the findings show that minimally supervised graph-based learning can more effectively capture the underlying structure of multimodal HFpEF data than traditional methods. Visualisation and cluster quality metrics further support the effectiveness of the GNN approach.

articles.title: Alternaria leaf spot-induced phyllosphere microbiota and metabolite interact to combat leaf spot disease.
articles.abstract: Pathogen-mediated induced resistance (IR) and beneficial microbe-mediated IR are key for plant survival during pathogen attack, yet how these two forms of IR interact remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that foliar pathogen-triggered induced resistance (IR) orchestrates the assembly of a specific phyllosphere microbiota that can activate IR. Pathogen-triggered IR caused plant flavonol accumulation, which in turn enriched Aureimonas spp., especially the native A. phyllosphaerae Leaf1, in the phyllosphere endophytic microbiota near infection sites. Genetically impairing the capacity of Leaf1 to utilize flavonols reduced its proliferation during pathogen infection. Moreover, Leaf1 protected plants against leaf disease by activating IR and extended the protective range of pathogen-mediated IR. Importantly, pathogen-mediated IR-induced mobilization of native microbiota represented a common yet underrated component of plant resistance to foliar disease. These findings reveal a plant defense "relay" mechanism, whereby pathogen-mediated IR reassembles a specific microbiota that in turn activates IR to jointly combat further pathogen infection.

articles.title: Platelet VEGFR3 suppresses activation and thrombosis through p190A-mediated inhibition of RhoA signaling.
articles.abstract: Vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 3 (VEGFR3) is a key regulator of lymphangiogenesis, but its role in platelets remains undefined. Here, we identify VEGFR3 as an intrinsic inhibitory regulator of platelet function. Using PF4-Cre-mediated conditional deletion, pharmacological inhibition, and biochemical analyses, we show that VEGFR3 deficiency enhances platelet activation, aggregation, secretion, cytoskeletal remodeling, thrombosis, and myocardial injury. Mechanistically, VEGFR3 interacts with the Rho GTPase regulator p190A to limit RhoA activation and Ezrin/Radixin/Moesin phosphorylation, thereby restraining platelet activation. In patients with myocardial infarction, reduced platelet VEGFR3 expression is associated with increased platelet reactivity and greater coronary lesion severity. These findings uncover a previously unrecognized VEGFR3/p190A/RhoA signaling axis that restrains platelet activation and thrombosis and highlight its potential therapeutic relevance in thrombotic disorders.

articles.title: Naringin improves hepatic redox homeostasis and attenuates NF-κB-associated inflammation in high-fat diet-fed and streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the antihyperglycaemic, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory effects of naringin in high-fat diet (HFD)-fed and low-dose streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic rats.

METHODS: Naringin and glibenclamide were administered for 45 days following diabetes mellitus (DM) induction. Blood glucose levels, plasma insulin levels, insulin tolerance, hepatic lipid peroxidation, antioxidant defences, inflammatory markers, and liver and pancreatic histopathology were evaluated.

RESULTS: HFD-fed and STZ-induced diabetic rats exhibited hyperglycaemia, reduced insulin levels, increased lipid peroxidation, impaired antioxidant defences, and elevated expression of NF-κB p65, TNF-α, and IL-6. Naringin treatment significantly reduced blood glucose levels and increased plasma insulin levels. It also reduced lipid peroxidation, improved enzymatic and non-enzymatic antioxidant defences, and attenuated inflammatory marker expression at both the mRNA and protein levels. Histopathological analysis further revealed improvements in hepatic and pancreatic tissue architecture.

CONCLUSION: Naringin ameliorated hyperglycaemia, hepatic oxidative stress, and NF-κB-associated inflammation in HFD-fed and STZ-induced diabetic rats. These findings suggest that naringin may protect against DM-associated hepatic complications, warranting further investigation into its therapeutic potential and clinical relevance.

articles.title: SPROUT Guidelines for Molecular Profiling for Children with Solid Tumors: A Consensus Recommendation from the American Association for Cancer Research.
articles.journal: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Molecular diagnostics are standard of care for most adults with solid malignancies, but implementation in pediatric solid tumors remains inconsistent. The SPROUT (Somatic Profiling for Pediatric Cancer Refining our Understanding and Treatment) Molecular Guidelines Working Group was convened to develop molecular testing guidelines for pediatric solid tumors.

EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN: A structured literature review was performed using Covidence to identify relevant clinical studies evaluating molecular diagnostics in pediatric solid tumors. The literature and collective clinical experience of the multidisciplinary working group were used to develop consensus recommendations for molecular profiling at diagnosis and at relapse or recurrence.

RESULTS: Of 361 manuscripts screened, 41 studies were included for data extraction. Based on the available evidence and expert consensus, recommendations were developed for the use and timing of DNA and RNA next-generation sequencing and methylation profiling across pediatric solid tumors.

CONCLUSIONS: The SPROUT Molecular Guidelines provide a framework for standardized implementation of molecular diagnostics in pediatric solid tumors. Broad adoption of these recommendations may improve diagnostic precision, reduce variability in molecular testing, and increase opportunities for biomarker-directed therapy and clinical trial enrollment for children with cancer.

articles.title: Digital Health Interventions for Pregnancy- and Childbirth-Related Posttraumatic Stress Disorder Symptoms in Postpartum Women: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancy- or childbirth-related traumatic experiences may lead to posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms during the postpartum period, adversely affecting women and their families. Digital health interventions may improve access to psychological support; however, evidence of their effectiveness for pregnancy- and childbirth-related posttraumatic stress disorder (PCR-PTSD) symptoms remains limited and has not been systematically synthesized.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of digital health interventions on PCR-PTSD symptoms in postpartum women, with depressive and anxiety symptoms as secondary outcomes.

METHODS: We searched 7 English-language and 4 Chinese-language databases from inception through April 30, 2026, to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating digital health interventions in women who had experienced pregnancy- or childbirth-related traumatic events and were assessed for PTSD symptoms during the postpartum period. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Effect estimates were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp adjustments and reported as standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% CIs. Statistical heterogeneity, 95% prediction intervals (PIs), subgroup effects, and the robustness of pooled estimates were also examined.

RESULTS: A total of 10 RCTs involving 1026 participants were included. Of these, 9 trials (809 participants) reported PTSD symptom outcomes immediately after the intervention, and 6 trials (413 participants) reported outcomes at follow-up. Digital health interventions were associated with lower PTSD symptom severity immediately after the intervention (SMD -0.59, 95% CI -0.98 to -0.19, 95% PI -1.72 to 0.54; P=.01), with substantial heterogeneity (I²=79.86%). However, the pooled effect was not statistically significant at the longest available follow-up (SMD -0.36, 95% CI -1 to 0.27, 95% PI -2.03 to 1.31; P=.20). All 95% PIs crossed the null. No statistically significant subgroup differences were observed by PTSD-related eligibility requirements, delivery modality, intervention duration, or trauma context. A statistically significant subgroup difference was observed by health care provider involvement (Q=14.46; P<.001); however, this exploratory finding should be interpreted cautiously. Sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the pooled effect on PTSD symptoms immediately after the intervention.

CONCLUSIONS: Digital health interventions may be associated with short-term reductions in PTSD, depressive, and anxiety symptoms among women with pregnancy- or childbirth-related trauma. However, substantial heterogeneity and PIs crossing the null limit confidence in these effects. Further well-designed trials with clinically interpretable outcomes and longer follow-up are needed.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261290528; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261290528.

articles.title: Home-Based, Digitally Assisted Dyadic Tai Chi Intervention for Patients With Chronic Heart Failure and Their Caregivers: Development of an Intervention and Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic heart failure (CHF) imposes a dual and dynamically interrelated burden on patients and family caregivers, whose health and illness management behaviors are interdependent. Exercise interventions that actively engage the patient-caregiver dyad as the unit of rehabilitation in the home setting remain underdeveloped.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop a home-based, digitally assisted, dyadic tai chi (HDTC) intervention and evaluate its feasibility, acceptability, safety, and preliminary effects among dyads of patients with CHF and their caregivers.

METHODS: This sequential, multiphase study comprised intervention development followed by a single-center, assessor-blinded, parallel-group pilot randomized controlled trial. Phase 1 integrated literature review, theoretical frameworks, and stakeholder focus group interviews to develop and refine the HDTC intervention. In phase 2, eligible adults with CHF (aged 18-75 years; New York Heart Association class I-III) and their primary caregivers were recruited from a tertiary medical center in Qingdao, China, from October 14 to November 12, 2024, and followed for 12 weeks. Forty dyads were allocated 1:1 to the 12-week HDTC intervention plus usual care or usual care alone (n=20 per group). Outcome assessors and the data analyst were blinded to group allocation. Feasibility, acceptability, and safety were the primary focus of the pilot trial. Patient, caregiver, and dyadic health outcomes were preliminarily explored at baseline and 4 and 12 weeks. All 40 randomized dyads were included in the intention-to-treat analyses.

RESULTS: The HDTC intervention comprised an online educational seminar, nurse-led dyadic coaching, preliminary face-to-face tai chi training, and supervised HDTC practice. The recruitment rate was 83.3% (40/48), mean session attendance was 73.7% (SD 8.6%), and 70% (14/20) of participants achieved high adherence rate (≥75% attendance). All intervention dyads rated the intervention as acceptable. No intervention-related adverse events were identified. Exploratory generalized estimating equation analyses suggested greater improvements from baseline to 12 weeks in the intervention group than in the control group in functional capacity (β=38.858; P=.001), together with greater reductions in Minnesota Living With Heart Failure Questionnaire scores (β=-1.850; P=.002), sedentary time (β=-1.025; P=.01), and fear of activity (β=-6.550; P=.01). Caregiver burden also decreased (β=-4.350; P<.001), while mutuality improved more for both patients (β=10.508; P<.001) and caregivers (β=6.450; P<.001).

CONCLUSIONS: The HDTC intervention was feasible and acceptable, with preliminary improvements across patient, caregiver, and dyadic outcomes. By integrating shared patient-caregiver participation with digitally supported home-based tai chi, the HDTC intervention extends patient-centered rehabilitation toward a dyad-oriented model. If confirmed in a fully powered trial, this approach may offer a practical strategy for expanding home-based cardiac rehabilitation.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06876441; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06876441.

articles.title: Advancements in biosensor-integrated biomedical devices for early detection of metabolic disorders: a comprehensive review.
articles.abstract: Lifestyle, genetic, and environmental influences are implicated in metabolic disorders, an emerging global health concern, including diabetes mellitus, dyslipidaemia, obesity, and hyperuricemia. The success of disease treatment and the prevention of long-term complications depend on the early identification and ongoing monitoring of metabolic markers. Even though these are accurate, traditional approaches for diagnosis are invasive, labor-intensive, and not amenable to real-time monitoring. By enabling the rapid, sensitive, and minimally invasive detection of biomarkers such as glucose, insulin, lipids, and uric acid, recent developments in biosensor-integrated biomedical technology have revolutionized metabolic diagnostics. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the various forms of biosensors, including electrochemical, optical, piezoelectric, and nanobiosensors, and their classification, mechanisms, and detection principles. High-performance materials such as graphene, carbon nanotubes, and metallic nanoparticles have been incorporated to significantly enhance biosensor performance, and microfluidic lab-on-a-chip systems have facilitated the convenience of collecting non-invasive samples of interstitial fluid, perspiration, or saliva. To ensure the analytical precision and clinical reliability of biosensor responses, validation methods based on bioinformatics and High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC) are highlighted. In addition, continuous monitoring, predictive medicine, and tailored healthcare management have been enabled by the incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and the Internet of Things (IoT) in wearable and intelligent biomedical devices. Widespread clinical translation is hindered by challenges like sensor drift, biofouling, calibration variability, and regulatory constraints, although tremendous progress has been achieved. Future biosensor technology will be developed towards anticipatory, patient-focused, precision-based management of metabolic disorders by synergistic implementation of nanotechnology, AI-enabled analytics, and telemedicine.

RETRACTION: Prognosis and Determinants of Pregnancy Outcome among Patients with Post-Hepatitis Liver Cirrhosis.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract: S.M. Rasheed, A.M. Abdel Monem, A.H. Abd Ellah, and M.S. Abdel Fateh, "Prognosis and Determinants of Pregnancy Outcome among Patients with Post-Hepatitis Liver Cirrhosis," International Journal of Gynecology & Obstetrics 121, no. 3(2013): 247-251, 10.1016/j.ijgo.2012.12.020. The above article, published online on 19 March 2013 in Wiley Online Library (onlinelibrary.wiley.com), has been retracted by agreement between the journal Editor-in-Chief, Michael Geary; and John Wiley & Sons Ltd. UK. Concerns were raised by a third party regarding the distribution of women with liver cirrhosis between Tables 1 and 3 in the study, as they and the Child-Pugh scores all differ between these tables when the numbers should remain the same. The publisher asked the authors to clarify these inconsistencies and provide the raw data for the study. The authors did not provide the requested data but responded to the concerns. Upon review of their response, the editorial team and publisher did not feel it explained these serious concerns adequately. Subsequently, further concerns were identified, including irreproducible odds ratios, lack of a reference category, and contradictions between the confidence intervals and p-values in the tables. In addition, the journal sought a clinical opinion from an expert in the area who felt that some of the clinical findings and outcome were not consistent with the typical clinical course of the condition. As a result, the data and conclusions are considered unreliable, and therefore the article must be retracted.

articles.title: First and Subsequent Major Cardiovascular Events With Oral Semaglutide in High-Risk Type 2 Diabetes: A Secondary Analysis of the SOUL Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: In the Semaglutide Cardiovascular Outcomes Trial (SOUL), oral semaglutide reduced the risk of a first 3-point major adverse cardiovascular event (3-P MACE; including nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, and cardiovascular [CV] death). Total event analyses, assessing both first and subsequent events, can contribute to a better understanding of the impact of interventions on the total burden of disease; however, the effects of oral semaglutide on subsequent events are unknown.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of oral semaglutide vs placebo on total 3-P MACE.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a prespecified secondary analysis of the double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven, phase 3b SOUL randomized clinical trial, conducted from June 2019 to September 2024 with a median (IQR) follow-up of 49.5 (44.0-54.9) months at 444 centers in 33 countries. Participants had type 2 diabetes and atherosclerotic CV disease and/or chronic kidney disease. Data were analyzed from December 2024 to August 2025.

INTERVENTIONS: Once-daily oral semaglutide (maximal dose 14 mg) or placebo, in addition standard of care.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Occurrence of total (first and subsequent) 3-P MACE.

RESULTS: Overall, 9650 participants (median [IQR] age, 66.0 [61.0-72.0] years; 6860 [71.1%] male) were randomized 1:1. In the oral semaglutide group, fewer first and subsequent 3-P MACE occurred (683 total; 579 first and 104 subsequent events) compared with placebo (791 total; 668 first and 123 subsequent events) (mean ratio, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.76-0.97; P = .01). For the end point of 3-P MACE plus non-CV death, there were 138 fewer total events with oral semaglutide (910 events) compared with placebo (1048 events) (mean ratio, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.79-0.95; P = .004). As previously reported, adverse events led to treatment discontinuation in 749 (15.5%) and 559 (11.6%) participants receiving oral semaglutide and placebo, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Oral semaglutide reduced the risk of first plus subsequent 3-P MACE vs placebo, highlighting the benefit of oral semaglutide in reducing the total burden of clinical morbidity and mortality in this high-risk population.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03914326.

articles.title: Assessment of Coronary Inflammatory Risk From Noncontrast Cardiac Computed Tomography.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Individuals with low or minimal coronary artery calcification (CAC) are considered at low cardiovascular risk, but a substantial absolute number of cardiovascular events occur in this population; assessment of coronary inflammation using the fat attenuation index (FAI) score may identify residual inflammatory risk beyond CAC score.

OBJECTIVE: To assess whether coronary inflammation measured on coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) or noncontrast cardiac CT (NCCT) identifies individuals at high cardiovascular risk independent of CAC burden.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this cohort study, a novel artificial intelligence algorithm for measuring FAI score on NCCT was trained and tested in an independent, multicenter, longitudinal cohort of consecutive individuals undergoing clinically indicated CCTA and NCCT for CAC score between 2010 and 2021, with median (IQR) follow-up of 6.7 (4.6-10.0) years. Data were analyzed from January 2010 to March 2024.

EXPOSURE: Agatston CAC score and coronary inflammation from both CCTA (CCTA FAI score, established biomarker) and NCCT (NC FAI score, novel biomarker).

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was cardiovascular (CV) mortality; the secondary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), comprising myocardial infarction, new-onset heart failure, or CV death.

RESULTS: The derivation cohort included 6818 individuals (median [IQR] age, 61 [51-71] years; 3543 female participants [52.0%]), and the external validation clinical outcomes cohort included 19 110 individuals (median [IQR] age, 56.0 [48.0-64.0] years; 9289 female participants [48.6%]). During follow-up, 536 CV deaths and 1727 MACE occurred. FAI scores independently stratified CV mortality risk across CAC score categories, with the strongest associations among individuals with CAC score of 0. Adding CCTA FAI score or NC FAI score to CAC score significantly improved risk discrimination (area under the curve increased from 0.76 to 0.81 and 0.80, respectively; P < .001), reclassification (net reclassification index), and net benefit across all risk thresholds. Among 89 CV deaths in individuals with CAC score of 0 and 138 CV deaths with CAC score of 1 through 99, 44.9% and 44.2% had NC FAI score above the 75th percentile, respectively. Among individuals with CAC score of 0, CV mortality rates increased from 1.4 to 4.0 per 1000 person-years for those with NC FAI score above the 75th percentile, and MACE rates increased from 5.9 to 13.3 per 1000 person-years.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Per the results of this cohort study, NC FAI score provides prognostic performance comparable to CCTA FAI score and improves cardiovascular risk prediction and reclassification beyond CAC score. Elevated FAI score, derived from either CCTA or NCCT, should be interpreted as a risk-enhancing factor that may prompt intensification of established, evidence-based preventive measures and may serve as a potential future gatekeeper for the use of targeted anti-inflammatory treatments.

Fusion of deep and handcrafted features from multi-modal ultrasound data for multi-task liver disease diagnosis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Chronic liver diseases, including fibrosis, inflammation, and steatosis, often coexist and challenge accurate diagnosis. Current approaches either carry procedural risks or fail to provide comprehensive early assessment. This study aims to develop a non-invasive, multimodal ultrasound-based framework for simultaneous grading of all three conditions.

METHODS: Our method integrates deep semantic features from deep learning networks with handcrafted features from quantitative ultrasound techniques, capturing complementary information from B-mode images, shear wave elastography, and radio-frequency data. Deep features can reveal discriminable and robust high-dimension non-linear relationships, while handcrafted features can capture ultrasonic characteristics related to the three diseases. These features are fused via a lightweight neural network to predict the probability of different grades of the three diseases, with liver biopsy results serving as the reference standard. The proposed method is evaluated on a cohort of 142 patients with chronic hepatitis B.

RESULTS: The proposed method achieves AUCs of 0.86, 0.85, 0.89, and 0.93 for fibrosis staging of ≥ F1, ≥ F2, ≥ F3, and F4, respectively; 0.87 and 0.95 for inflammation grading of ≥ A2 and A3, respectively; and 0.83 and 0.93 for steatosis grading of ≥ S1 and ≥ S2, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: The proposed method outperforms existing methods and demonstrates robust performance in both early and advanced disease stages. This multi-task framework has potential as a clinically actionable tool for comprehensive liver disease assessment and decision support.

articles.title: Life-course social mobility and depressive symptoms among older adults: evidence from the Longitudinal Ageing Study in India.
articles.abstract: Evidence linking socioeconomic mobility to depressive symptoms in older adults in low- and middle-income countries is limited. We examined childhood-to-adulthood socioeconomic position (SEP) mobility in India. The primary cross-sectional analysis used complete-case data from 30,358 adults aged ≥ 60 years in the Longitudinal Ageing Study in India Wave 1. Childhood SEP was recalled; adulthood SEP reflected per capita consumption expenditure. Mobility was classified as consistently high, upward, downward, or consistently low. Depressive symptoms were defined by a score ≥ 4 on the 10-item Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D-10), rather than clinically diagnosed depressive disorders. Survey-weighted logistic models incorporated covariates and state fixed effects. Multiple imputation using 30 imputations involving 31,915 participants assessed missing data sensitivity. Weighted depressive symptom prevalence was 30.1%. Compared with consistently high SEP, upward mobility (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.18, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.02-1.35), downward mobility (aOR 1.37, 95% CI 1.18-1.59), and consistently low SEP (aOR 1.31, 95% CI 1.11-1.55) were associated with higher odds. Compared with no high-SEP stages, high SEP at both stages, but not one stage, was associated with lower odds (aOR 0.76, 95% CI 0.64-0.90). In the imputation sensitivity analysis, the upward-mobility estimate was 1.17 (95% CI 0.999-1.360), while downward mobility and consistently low SEP remained associated. Downward mobility and persistent low SEP were consistently associated with depressive symptoms. Evidence for upward mobility was less robust, and the cumulative pattern primarily reflected sustained high SEP. These findings may inform mental health assessment; the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes and influencing factors of breast reconstruction after mastectomy in breast cancer patients: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: To systematically analyze postoperative complications, cosmetic satisfaction, and long‑term oncologic outcomes of different post‑mastectomy breast reconstruction modalities and identify associated risk factors. A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 327 breast‑cancer patients (autologous flap = 182, implant‑based = 145) undergoing immediate or delayed breast reconstruction between October 2018 and November 2024. Eligible patients had a minimum of 12‑month complete oncologic follow‑up. Baseline clinicopathological features, 3‑month perioperative complications, 12‑month composite cosmetic‑satisfaction scores, disease‑free survival (DFS), and overall survival (OS) were compared between groups. Subgroup analyses were performed stratified by reconstruction timing (immediate versus delayed). Multivariate Cox proportional‑hazards regression was applied for exploratory identification of factors associated with reconstruction‑related complications. Given that adverse events were captured within a fixed 3‑month postoperative window, the Cox model violates some time‑to‑event assumptions; results should be interpreted only as observational associations rather than definitive causal risk estimates. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS 26.0. The median follow‑up duration was 61.3 months. The overall 3‑month complication rate was 14.37% (47/327). The autologous‑flap group exhibited a higher rate of reconstructive‑flap partial necrosis (8.24% vs. 0.00%, P < 0.05), whereas the implant‑based group demonstrated a higher capsular‑contracture rate (7.59% vs. 2.75%, P < 0.05). Capsular contracture within the autologous‑flap cohort occurred exclusively among patients receiving secondary implant‑augmented autologous reconstruction. The immediate‑reconstruction subgroup showed a lower crude overall complication rate compared with delayed reconstruction (10.12% vs. 18.87%, P = 0.019). This comparison is substantially confounded by higher pre‑reconstruction radiotherapy exposure in delayed‑reconstruction patients. Autologous‑flap reconstruction yielded higher composite cosmetic‑satisfaction scores (8.12 ± 1.05 vs. 7.23 ± 1.21, P < 0.001). This 10‑point composite surgeon‑patient rating is non‑validated and cannot substitute validated patient‑reported‑outcome instruments such as the BREAST‑Q. Five‑year DFS (87.91% vs. 88.28%, P = 0.892) and OS (92.31% vs. 93.10%, P = 0.785) were comparable across groups. Exploratory multivariate Cox regression indicated that advanced age, higher TNM stage, positive axillary‑lymph‑node metastasis, and postoperative radiotherapy were associated with elevated complication risk. Tumor molecular subtype showed no significant correlation with reconstruction‑related complications or long‑term oncologic survival (P > 0.05). Within this single‑center retrospective cohort, autologous‑flap and implant‑based breast reconstruction demonstrated comparable long‑term oncologic survival. Reconstructive surgery does not alter oncologic mastectomy resection margins; survival comparisons reflect real‑world observational associations and cannot prove causal oncologic equivalence. Autologous‑flap reconstruction was associated with superior composite cosmetic scores at the expense of higher partial reconstructive‑flap necrosis risk. Implant‑based reconstruction carried higher capsular‑contracture risk, particularly in patients receiving chest‑wall radiotherapy. The apparent protective effect of immediate reconstruction on crude complication rates is heavily confounded by baseline patient‑tumor‑treatment characteristics. Individualized reconstructive planning should integrate oncologic features, adjuvant‑therapy schedules, donor‑site conditions, device‑related considerations, and patient preferences. Important inherent limitations of retrospective observational design preclude causal inference from these findings.EBM level: III.

articles.title: Piperonylpiperazine potentiates netilmicin activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms via RhlI-mediated quorum sensing disruption.
articles.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms are inherently tolerant to conventional antibiotics, leading to persistent biocontamination and difficult-to-treat infections. Natural adjuvants that restore antibiotic potency represent a feasible strategy to tackle biofilm-associated resistance. This study presents the first evidence that piperonylpiperazine (Pip), a natural compound derived from pepper, significantly potentiates netilmicin efficacy against planktonic P. aeruginosa PAO1 and substantially improves the clearance of biofilms formed on polystyrene and stainless steel surfaces. A lettuce infection model further confirmed that co-treatment efficiently restrains P. aeruginosa invasive infection. Mechanistically, integrated proteomic profiling, microscale thermophoresis (MST), and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) analyses verified that Pip directly binds to the Lys164 and Asp35 residues of the RhlI protein. This interaction blocks the Rhl quorum sensing signaling cascade and triggers intracellular oxidative damage, which disrupts bacterial membrane architecture and increases membrane permeability. The altered membrane property facilitates netilmicin penetration into bacterial cells, thereby improving bacterial susceptibility and biofilm eradication efficiency. Furthermore, gene knockout and site-directed mutagenesis assays revealed that rhlI deletion or mutation of the Lys164 and Asp35 residues markedly enhances netilmicin sensitivity. These original findings explicitly link the Rhl quorum sensing system to aminoglycoside resistance, providing a novel mechanistic insight for developing natural quorum sensing inhibitors as promising antibiotic adjuvants.

articles.title: Management of Staple‑Line Leaks after Laparoscopic Sleeve Gastrectomy: Efficacy of Double Pigtail Stenting and a Practical Algorithm for Early and Late Leaks.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Staple-line leak (SLL) remains one of the most severe complications following laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG). Although endoscopic internal drainage using double pigtail stents (DPS) has emerged as an effective minimally invasive treatment, evidence comparing its efficacy according to leak timing remains limited. The aim of this study was to evaluate the clinical outcomes of DPS for the management of SLL after LSG and compare treatment success between early and late leaks.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients referred to a tertiary bariatric referral center with confirmed SLL following LSG. Patients were categorized into early (< 7 days) and late (≥ 7 days) leak groups. All patients underwent multidisciplinary management consisting of resuscitation, nutritional support, antibiotics, radiologic assessment, and endoscopic evaluation. DPS was used whenever technically feasible for internal drainage. Primary outcome was successful leak closure without the need for definitive reconstructive surgery. Secondary outcomes included additional interventions, hospital stay, intensive care unit (ICU) stay, and mortality.

RESULTS: Fifty patients with SLL were included (26 early leaks and 24 late leaks). Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics were comparable between groups. DPS placement was attempted in 41 patients. Leak resolution following DPS was significantly higher in late leaks than early leaks (80.0% vs. 52.4%, P = 0.031). Early leaks more frequently required radiologic drainage (84.6% vs. 54.2%, P = 0.030) and surgical intervention (80.8% vs. 25.0%, P = 0.001). The need for definitive reconstructive surgery was also significantly greater in early leaks (53.8% vs. 25.0%, P = 0.048). Length of hospital stay, ICU stay, and mortality did not differ significantly between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Double pigtail stenting is an effective minimally invasive treatment for staple-line leaks after LSG, particularly in patients with late leaks, where high rates of leak resolution can be achieved while avoiding major revisional surgery. Early leaks remain more challenging and frequently require multimodal management combining endoscopic, radiologic, and surgical approaches. Treatment strategies should therefore be individualized according to leak timing within a multidisciplinary bariatric program.

articles.title: Postoperative Tumor-Informed Circulating Tumor DNA Status for Molecular Residual Disease Detection After Curative-Intent Resection of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) frequently recurs after curative-intent resection, and conventional imaging and CA19-9 have limited sensitivity for detecting molecular residual disease (MRD). Tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) may identify postoperative MRD, although the evidence is limited and heterogeneous.

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Embase were searched from inception to July 9, 2026, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Eligible studies compared postoperative tumor-informed ctDNA-positive and ctDNA-negative patients after curative-intent treatment of pancreatic cancer for recurrence, survival, or lead time outcomes. Random-effects models were used to pool risk ratios (RRs) and hazard ratios (HRs). Heterogeneity, leave-one-out sensitivity, prespecified subgroups, ROBINS-I risk of bias, and GRADE certainty were assessed.

RESULTS: Five observational cohorts contributed 237 patients to the radiological recurrence comparison (84 ctDNA-positive and 153 ctDNA-negative). Postoperative ctDNA positivity was associated with increased radiological recurrence (RR 2.50; 95% CI 1.90-3.28; I²=20%), poorer disease-free survival (HR 8.11; 95% CI 3.51-18.73; I²=45%), and poorer overall survival (HR 5.15; 95% CI 2.67-9.94; I²=0%). The direction of the associations persisted in the reported leave-one-out assessments. Recurrence risk was higher in both the early-MRD/landmark and surveillance subgroups, with no statistically significant subgroup difference (P = 0.17).

CONCLUSION: Postoperative tumor-informed ctDNA positivity was associated with an increased recurrence risk and inferior survival after curative-intent PDAC treatment, although a negative result did not reliably exclude residual disease. Prospective interventional studies are needed before ctDNA-guided surveillance or treatment modifications can be recommended for routine practice.

articles.title: Serum Soluble Programmed Death Ligand-1 (sPD-L1) as a Diagnostic Marker in Neonatal Sepsis: Authors' Reply-3.
Claims-defined adrenal insufficiency, hypothyroidism, and type 1 diabetes after immune checkpoint inhibitor initiation in patients with triple-negative breast cancer in Japan.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence of treated adrenal insufficiency, hypothyroidism, and type 1 diabetes after immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) treatment for triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) has not been fully characterized in real-world clinical practice in Japan.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the JMDC claims database, which includes employees of Japanese companies and their dependents. Patients aged 18-74 years with TNBC who received atezolizumab or pembrolizumab between January 2005 and June 2025 were included. Early-stage and advanced TNBC were identified based on the treatment regimen at ICI initiation. We examined the incidence rates and time to onset of claims-defined adrenal insufficiency, hypothyroidism, and type 1 diabetes separately in the two cohorts.

RESULTS: The study included 569 patients with early-stage TNBC (median age, 50.8 years) and 254 with advanced TNBC (median age, 52.8 years). In early-stage TNBC, the incidence rates (95% CIs) of adrenal insufficiency and hypothyroidism were 5.6 (4.0-7.8) and 12.7 (10.0-16.0) cases/100 person-years (PY), respectively. The median times to onset (IQRs) were 124 (86-215) and 117 (89-196) days, respectively. In advanced TNBC, the incidence rates (95% CIs) of adrenal insufficiency and hypothyroidism were 1.4 (0.53-3.8) and 9.2 (6.1-13.8) cases/100 PY, respectively. The median time to onset of hypothyroidism was 84 (63-105) days. Type 1 diabetes was rare.

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides real-world estimates of claims-defined endocrine outcomes after ICI initiation separately in patients with early-stage and advanced TNBC in Japan.

articles.title: Prevalence, associated factors, and outcomes of Clostridioides difficile infection across gastrointestinal cancer subtypes: a US nationwide analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence, associated factors, and clinical and healthcare impact of Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) among hospitalized adults with gastrointestinal (GI) cancer.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of the National Inpatient Sample (2018-2023). Adult hospitalizations with active GI cancer were stratified by CDI status. Survey-weighted multivariable regression identified factors associated with CDI and associations with in-hospital mortality, mechanical ventilation, vasopressor use, renal replacement therapy (RRT), length of stay (LOS), and hospital charges.

RESULTS: Among 3,572,119 weighted GI cancer hospitalizations, 48,900 (1.37%; 95% CI, 1.34-1.40) involved CDI. Prevalence declined from 1.63% in 2018 to 1.22% in 2023. Inflammatory bowel disease was most strongly associated with CDI (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.47; 95% CI, 2.15-2.85), followed by chronic kidney disease (aOR, 1.61; 95% CI, 1.52-1.71) and solid organ transplantation (aOR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.15-1.98). Anal cancer had the highest CDI prevalence (2.32%). CDI was associated with higher in-hospital mortality (aOR, 1.34; 95% CI, 1.23-1.46), mechanical ventilation (aOR, 1.87; 95% CI, 1.71-2.05), vasopressor use (aOR, 1.84; 95% CI, 1.61-2.10), and RRT (aOR, 2.27; 95% CI, 2.01-2.56). CDI was associated with 65% longer LOS (LOS ratio, 1.65; 95% CI, 1.61-1.69) and 40% higher charges (charge ratio, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.35-1.45).

CONCLUSION: CDI occurred in approximately 1 in 73 GI cancer hospitalizations and was associated with higher mortality, organ-support requirements, and healthcare utilization. These findings highlight the clinical burden of CDI in this population and support the need for further studies evaluating prevention and early recognition strategies.

articles.title: Demystifying Autoimmune/Autoinflammatory Lung Disease.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Lung diseases in systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARD) and autoinflammatory diseases may be the initial manifestation of underlying immune dysregulation and are significant contributors of morbidity and mortality in these conditions. This review describes the spectrum of lung diseases across SARD and autoinflammatory diagnoses, summarizing the key distinguishing features within these disorders.

RECENT FINDINGS: SARDs and autoinflammatory diseases may involve the airways, lung parenchyma, pleura, and pulmonary vasculature. Bronchiolar disorders such as bronchiectasis and bronchiolitis may complicate many different SARDs leading to chronic mucus production, pulmonary infection, and recurrent exacerbations. Diffuse parenchymal involvement most commonly presents as interstitial lung disease (ILD) which can involve SARDs such as rheumatoid arthritis, Sjogren's syndrome, and mixed connective tissue disease as well as inborn errors of immunity including monogenic autoinflammatory disorders and interferonopathies. Pleural involvement may manifest as serositis or pleural effusions and chronic involvement may lead to complications such as pleural thickening and lung entrapment. Pulmonary hypertension may develop due to the underlying disorder, such as in systemic sclerosis, but may also develop as a complication of advanced lung disease. Early recognition and treatment of pulmonary involvement in SARD and autoinflammatory diseases is key and emerging therapies beyond anti-inflammatory therapy may be required in the treatment of these conditions. Early recognition and treatment of pulmonary involvement in SARD and autoinflammatory diseases is key and emerging therapies beyond anti-inflammatory therapy may be required in the treatment of these conditions.

articles.title: Fur-regulated MntH mediates metal homeostasis and immune evasion in Yersinia pseudotuberculosis.
articles.abstract: During infection, host nutritional immunity restricts bacterial access to essential transition metals, in part through calprotectin (CP), a host metal-binding protein that sequesters manganese (Mn) and iron (Fe). However, whether the MntH transporter enables Yersinia pseudotuberculosis (Yptb) strain YPIII to withstand this CP-mediated metal restriction remains unclear. To address this question, we characterized the regulation and function of MntH in Yptb YPIII using molecular, genetic, physiological, and mouse-infection approaches. We found that MntH is a conserved member of the natural resistance-associated macrophage protein (Nramp) family whose expression is directly repressed by the ferric uptake regulator (Fur). Deletion of mntH reduced intracellular Mn and Fe accumulation, impaired bacterial growth under metal-limited conditions, and increased sensitivity to peroxide- and hydroxyl radical (HR)-associated stresses. In vitro, deletion of mntH impaired bacterial growth under CP-imposed metal restriction, and this defect was rescued by supplementation with Mn or Fe. In orally infected mice, the ΔmntH mutant yielded lower bacterial burdens in the feces and cecum, reduced competitive fitness, and milder cecal inflammation and liver damage than the wild-type strain. Notably, Yptb infection elevated cecal CP expression and depleted fecal Mn and Fe, whereas mntH expression was induced during infection, supporting a role for MntH in countering host-imposed metal limitation. Collectively, these findings establish Fur-regulated MntH as a key determinant of metal homeostasis, stress tolerance, and intestinal fitness in Yptb and provide insight into how this pathogen adapts to host nutritional limitation.

articles.title: Closing the Gap: The Role of the Advanced Practice Provider (APP) In IBD Clinic.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Gastroenterology faces a widening gap between rising IBD prevalence and a shrinking specialist workforce, leaving many patients without timely access to care. Advanced practice providers (APPs) now make up a significant portion of the GI workforce. This review looks at how APPs can be integrated into IBD practice and what that integration requires to succeed.

RECENT FINDINGS: APPs can meaningfully contribute to much of the IBD care continuum: new consultations, urgent visits, monitoring response to therapy, preventive health screening, chronic care management, and clinical research support. Successful integration depends on clearly defined scope of practice, structured onboarding and ongoing education, and supportive physician champions. Common obstacles include productivity-based pay structures that undervalue non-visit care, lack of structured education/training, inconsistent state scope-of-practice laws, and physician hesitancy. With defined roles, adequate training, and physician support, APPs are well positioned to expand IBD care capacity, improve access, and support long-term practice sustainability amid growing workforce demands.

articles.title: Preoperative inflammatory-nutritional vulnerability and early recovery burden after durable LVAD implantation: the Naples Prognostic Score.
articles.journal: Journal of artificial organs : the official journal of the Japanese Society for Artificial Organs
articles.abstract: We examined whether the preoperative Naples Prognostic Score (NPS) is associated with early recovery after durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation while accounting for death before discharge.
