This retrospective single-center study included 354 patients who underwent implantation during 2015-2026 and had complete NPS measurements: NPS 0-2, n = 102; NPS 3-4, n = 252. The primary outcome was hospital length of stay (LOS) among patients discharged alive. Clinical models included INTERMACS profiles; echocardiographic and hemodynamic covariates were added separately and together. Competing-risk analyses included all patients, with death before discharge as the competing event. Sparse binary outcomes were analyzed using parsimonious Firth logistic regression. Among 301 patients discharged alive, hospital LOS was 18.0 days with high NPS versus 14.0 days with low/intermediate NPS (p = 0.008). The adjusted geometric-mean ratio was 1.15 (95% CI 1.01-1.30) in the clinical/INTERMACS model and 1.14 (0.99-1.31) in the combined model. In all 354 patients, the 30-day cumulative incidence of live discharge was 72.2% versus 84.3%; clinical and combined subdistribution hazard ratios were 0.77 (0.60-0.99) and 0.79 (0.61-1.03). There were 41 deaths within 30 days; the parsimonious adjusted odds ratio was 2.82 (1.19-8.03). Transfusion associations diminished after hemoglobin adjustment. High NPS was associated with longer hospitalization among patients discharged alive and a lower cumulative incidence of live discharge. After combined echocardiographic and hemodynamic adjustment, confidence intervals for hospital LOS and live discharge included the null. NPS may characterize preoperative illness associated with recovery burden; its incremental predictive value and role in treatment decisions require further study.

articles.title: Gut microbiome in leukemia: emerging insights, mechanistic and clinical implications.
articles.abstract: Leukemia is a hematological malignancy that arises from complex interactions among environmental factors, immune dysregulation, and genetic mutations. The Human Microbiome Project has contributed to understanding the potential role of the gut microbiome in the health of patients with leukemia, and its impact on leukemia development, progression, and response to therapies. This review summarizes how the gut microbiome and its constituent microorganisms may influence development and the new therapeutic approaches against leukemia. Recent findings indicate that microorganisms might influence leukemia through multiple mechanisms, including chronic inflammation, homeostasis disruption, and genomic instability. Dysbiosis of the gut microbiome might increase the risk of infection, impair response to immunotherapy and chemotherapy and increase the risk of clinical complications. Probiotics, postbiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) have emerged as promising microbiome-modulating approaches. Despite the abundance of emerging data suggesting potential therapeutic benefits, most studies remain small and preliminary. Integrating gut microbiome science into medical practice may open up new and potentially more effective therapeutic avenues for managing leukemia.

articles.title: Polyamine Dysregulation in Metabolic Dysfunction-associated Steatotic Liver Disease: a Systematic Review of Human Observational Evidence.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most prevalent chronic liver disease worldwide and is closely associated with obesity, insulin resistance, and increased cardiovascular risk. Polyamines have emerged as potential regulators of metabolic and inflammatory pathways implicated in MASLD. We aimed to systematically evaluate the association between polyamines and MASLD severity and related hepatic and metabolic outcomes in human observational studies.

APPROACH AND RESULTS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science and Scopus were searched from inception to April 2026 (PROSPERO registration CRD420261540945). Observational studies assessing polyamine levels or polyamine-related pathways in relation to MASLD and related hepatic or metabolic outcomes were included. Study selection, data extraction, and risk of bias assessment (Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, NOS) were performed independently. A qualitative synthesis was undertaken. Nine studies were included, comprising more than 1,400 participants across clinical cohorts, together with transcriptomic analyses based on publicly available datasets; NOS scores ranged from 6 to 9. Increased hepatic putrescine, together with upregulation of ornithine decarboxylase, was associated with greater histological disease severity and hepatocellular injury in one study. In contrast, lower spermidine levels in circulating and fecal samples were associated with greater disease severity in some studies. Alterations in polyamine-related molecular pathways, including the eukaryotic initiation factor 5​A hypusination pathway, and changes in microbially derived polyamines were also associated with disease severity. Findings varied across studies, with differences in biological matrices, analytical approaches, and disease assessment methods potentially contributing to the observed heterogeneity.

CONCLUSIONS: Distinct alterations in polyamine profiles, particularly increased putrescine and reduced spermidine in specific biological matrices, were associated with MASLD-related disease severity in some observational studies. However, none of the included studies established diagnostic performance using measures such as area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, predefined cut-offs, or external validation. Therefore, polyamines should currently be considered promising candidate molecular biomarkers requiring prospective validation rather than established biomarkers of MASLD severity. The available evidence remains observational and heterogeneous, precluding definitive causal inferences and limiting conclusions regarding clinical utility. Prospective, longitudinal, and multicenter studies using standardized analytical methods, predefined thresholds, and appropriate internal and external validation are required to determine whether polyamine measurements provide incremental value beyond established non-invasive tools.

articles.title: Local Control Options for Metastatic Disease in Sarcoma.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To review the current evidence on local treatment strategies for oligometastatic soft tissue sarcoma at pulmonary and extrapulmonary sites, and evaluate their impact on oncological outcomes.

RECENT FINDINGS: Pulmonary metastasectomy remains the most established local treatment, with 5-year survival rates of 20-58%. Complete (R0) resection, a longer disease-free interval, and fewer metastases are associated with improved outcomes. Stereotactic radiotherapy achieves high local control rates with low toxicity, and a recent systematic review reported survival outcomes comparable to surgery. Image-guided thermal ablation also achieves high local control rates for lung metastases of 1 cm or smaller and offers a minimally invasive option for extrapulmonary metastases. For all modalities, current data are derived predominantly from retrospective studies, and direct comparisons are lacking. Local treatment offers promising outcomes for carefully selected patients with oligometastatic soft tissue sarcoma. Surgery, stereotactic radiotherapy, and thermal ablation should be considered complementary options, selected within a multidisciplinary tumor board according to lesion size, number, and location. Prospective studies are needed to define optimal patient selection and determine the comparative effectiveness of these modalities.

articles.title: The unseen risk: a systematic review of the incidence, management, and outcomes of the trigeminocardiac reflex in skull-base surgery.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study synthesizes contemporary evidence on the trigeminocardiac reflex (TCR) during skull-base and adjacent neurosurgical procedures, with emphasis on operative corridors, triggers, hemodynamic phenotypes, management, and the limits of current outcome evidence.

METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, we systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase through September 15, 2024. Eligible reports described intraoperative TCR or closely related trigeminal autonomic responses during skull-base surgery or adjacent procedures and reported event features, management, or outcomes.

RESULTS: Twenty-eight studies including 329 patients met inclusion criteria. Reported TCR events clustered in microvascular decompression for trigeminal neuralgia (n=168; 51.1%), CPA/posterior fossa or anterior skull-base tumor surgery (n=71; 21.6%), transsphenoidal pituitary procedures (n=47; 14.3%), and percutaneous trigeminal procedures (n=35; 10.6%). Immediate cessation of the provoking maneuver was the cornerstone of management, with anticholinergics, vasoactive agents, or temporary pacing required only in selected severe or recurrent cases. No TCR-attributable mortality was reported. However, evidence regarding long-term functional outcomes remains limited, inconsistently reported, and largely dependent on historical vestibular schwannoma and pituitary cohorts. A procedure-specific synthesis identifies high-risk maneuvers, preventive considerations, and escalation options for each operative corridor.

CONCLUSIONS: TCR should be anticipated during trigeminal manipulation across skull-base surgical corridors and managed initially by immediate cessation or modification of the provoking stimulus, with pharmacologic or resuscitative escalation reserved for persistent or severe events. Although the available evidence supports a procedure-specific approach to prevention and preparedness, heterogeneous definitions, retrospective designs, and incomplete denominators preclude reliable incidence estimates or validated management recommendations.

articles.title: Effects on Sleep Quality and Bioelectrical Parameters of Cellular Health After Administration of a Plant Protein Supplement Combined with Ashwagandha and Rhodiola: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: Plant foods for human nutrition (Dordrecht, Netherlands)
articles.abstract: Sleep disturbances affect a significant portion of the global population, impacting health and quality of life. While plant-based proteins and adaptogens such as ashwagandha and rhodiola have shown individual benefits, their combined effects remain poorly understood. This study evaluated whether a nutritional intervention combining plant protein with ashwagandha-rhodiola could improve sleep quality in middle-aged adults. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial was conducted with 100 participants aged 35-70 years, assigned to VERUM (n=50) or PLACEBO (n=50) groups. The VERUM group received plant protein (27 g/day: pea, rice, hemp isolate) plus adaptogen tablets (Rhodiola rosea 300 mg + Withania somnifera KSM-66® 500 mg) for 30 days. Sleep quality was assessed using the validated Sleep Quality Questionnaire (SQQ) completed daily. Phase angle was measured by bioimpedance (BIA-TELELAB) pre- and post-intervention. Data were analyzed using longitudinal mixed models and non-parametric tests. Seventy-seven participants completed bioimpedance analysis (VERUM group; n= 38, PLACEBO group n=39; mean age 47.8±8.2 years), and sixty-one completed sleep assessments (VERUM group n=32; PLACEBO group n=29). The VERUM group showed highly significant improvements: sleep difficulty reduced by 56% (p<0.001, d=0.91), daytime sleepiness decreased by 60% (p<0.001, d=0.85), and total sleep score improved by 58% (p<0.001, d=0.96), representing a 3.7-fold greater improvement than placebo. Phase angle changes were minimal in both groups. No adverse events were reported. The combination of plant protein with ashwagandha-rhodiola for 30 days produces substantial, clinically relevant improvements in sleep quality with an excellent safety profile, with statistically greater improvements compared to placebo.

articles.title: Phycoerythrin attenuates Pseudomonas aeruginosa - induced pathogenesis, oxidative stress and intestinal dysfunction in Caenorhabditis elegans.
articles.abstract: Cyanobacterial phycobiliprotein, is widely known for its antioxidant, cytoprotective and antimicrobial agent. Using the Caenorhabditis elegans model (C. elegans), we evaluated the lifespan and intestinal integrity along with the oxidative and stress signalling pathways. In the present study, the protective role of phycoerythrin (PE) treatment was evaluated against Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PA), well known pathogen posing risk to both environment and organism. Crude PE extracted from Haplosiphon sp. was purified using ammonium sulphate precipitation and ion-exchange chromatography and was characterized using SDS-PAGE and UV-Visible Spectroscopy, yielding purified PE with an A553/A280 purity ratio of 5.5. Further, the antioxidant potential of PE was demonstrated using in-vitro DPPH (2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl) (IC50 = 26.86 µg/mL) showing 74.3% radical scavenging activity along with ferrous ion chelation. PE treatment increased the mean lifespan of PA-infected worms in a concentration-dependent manner, from 10.4 days in the infected group to 11.8, 13.0, and 13.44 days following treatment with 100, 200, and 500 µg/mL PE, respectively. Consistent with this protective effect, PE treatment reduced intestinal bacterial burden and increased the infection-induced expression of SOD-3, HSP-16.2, SEK-1, PMK-1, SKN-1, and LYS-7, genes associated with oxidative, stress-responsive signalling, and antimicrobial host responses. Together with the observed reduction in intracellular ROS and protection of intestinal barrier integrity, these findings suggest that PE enhances host resistance to PA infection by supporting oxidative stress defence and host protective responses. Overall, PE represents a promising natural bioactive phycobiliprotein for further investigation against bacterial infection and infection-associated oxidative and intestinal stress.

articles.title: Conservative versus surgical management of traumatic acute subdural hematoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute subdural hematoma is among the most severe forms of traumatic brain injury, associated with high mortality and significant neurological morbidity. Optimal management-surgical versus conservative-remains uncertain, particularly in patients whose clinical and radiological presentation does not clearly meet established surgical thresholds. No prior meta-analysis has directly compared these strategies in the broader adult population (> 18 years).

METHODS: Four electronic databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library) were searched from inception to February 2026. Studies were included if they involved adult patients with CT/MRI-confirmed traumatic aSDH comparing surgical (craniotomy or craniectomy) versus conservative management and reporting at least one relevant clinical or radiological outcome. Pooled estimates were calculated using random-effects models.

RESULTS: Eleven studies encompassing 3,792 patients (2,507 male) were included. Surgical patients (n = 1,029) presented with significantly lower admission GCS scores (MD - 1.93; 95% CI [- 3.35, - 0.52]; p = 0.007), greater hematoma thickness (MD + 3.56 mm; p = 0.0009), and larger midline shift (MD + 4.83 mm; p < 0.00001) compared to conservatively managed patients (n = 2,763). Despite a higher crude mortality in the surgical group (25.9% vs. 11.6%), pooled analysis revealed no statistically significant difference in overall mortality (RR 1.36; 95% CI [0.74, 2.50]; p = 0.32). Surgical patients had significantly longer hospital stays (MD + 6.77 days; p = 0.003).

CONCLUSION: No statistically significant difference in mortality was observed between surgically and conservatively managed patients; however, the substantially greater baseline severity of surgically managed patients, together with the absence of patient-level adjustment, means that these observational data are insufficient to determine whether surgery reduces, increases, or has no effect on mortality. Substantial heterogeneity and absence of randomized data underscore the need for prospective trials targeting patients with intermediate clinical presentations.

articles.title: Measles-like hypermutation of a Newcastle disease virus drives fatal encephalitis during BCMA × CD3 T-cell-redirecting immunotherapy.
articles.abstract: Newcastle disease virus (NDV or AOaV-1) is an avian paramyxovirus that typically causes only mild, self-limiting disease in humans. Here, we report fatal neuroinvasive AOaV-1 infection in a patient with multiple myeloma receiving maintenance therapy with teclistamab, daratumumab, and lenalidomide following frontline teclistamab-based treatment and autologous stem cell transplantation. Following rapidly progressive brainstem-cerebellar encephalitis and negative conventional microbiological testing, unbiased metagenomic RNA sequencing of a cerebellar biopsy identified AOaV-1 at high intraparenchymal abundance. Viral genome analysis revealed striking A-to-G and U-to-C substitutions selectively concentrated in the matrix gene, consistent with ADAR-mediated RNA editing. Long-read sequencing resolved two genetically distinct, independently hypermutated CNS haplotypes. Post-mortem analysis demonstrated widespread dissemination and continued viral diversification in multiple brain regions, whereas a peripheral urine sample contained a minimally mutated putative ancestral lineage. These findings support peripheral infection followed by CNS seeding and compartmentalized within-host evolution. The selective matrix-gene hypermutation closely parallels persistent measles virus infection in subacute sclerosing panencephalitis, revealing a shared mechanism of paramyxovirus adaptation to the CNS. Profound immunotherapy-associated immune dysfunction may thus create niches enabling normally low-pathogenic zoonotic viruses to persist, evolve, and acquire severe neurovirulence.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of middle meningeal artery embolisation for chronic subdural haematoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
articles.abstract: Chronic subdural haematoma (cSDH) frequently recurs following standard treatment. Middle meningeal artery embolisation (MMAE) may reduce recurrence by decreasing perfusion of the vascularised subdural membranes. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of MMAE versus standard management. This PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO: CRD420261325584) searched PubMed, Ovid (MEDLINE and Embase), Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library from inception to 28 September 2026. Randomised controlled trials comparing MMAE-based treatment with standard management in adults with radiologically confirmed cSDH were included. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. The primary outcome was study-defined treatment failure. Twelve randomised controlled trials (n = 2,429; 1,202 MMAE; 1,227 control) were included in the primary analysis. Treatment failure occurred in 9.1% versus 18.3%, respectively. MMAE reduced treatment failure (RR 0.52, 95% CI 0.39-0.69), corresponding to an absolute risk reduction of approximately 8.8% and an NNT of approximately 12. In subgroup analyses, benefit was observed in both surgery-only comparator trials (RR 0.41, 95% CI 0.23-0.76) and mixed surgical/conservative comparator trials (RR 0.55, 95% CI 0.37-0.81), with no significant subgroup difference (p = 0.317). MMAE also reduced reoperation/surgical rescue (RR 0.40, 95% CI 0.31-0.52). All-cause mortality (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.37-1.43) and severe adverse events (RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.60-1.16) did not differ significantly between groups. Certainty was moderate for treatment failure and reoperation/surgical rescue and low for mortality and severe adverse events. MMAE-based treatment reduces treatment failure in cSDH, with no statistically significant difference in mortality or severe adverse events. Further well-powered randomised trials using standardised efficacy and safety outcomes are needed to define the optimal role of MMAE in cSDH management.

articles.title: Source-to-sink hydrochemical dynamics and contaminant risks in the transboundary Syr Darya River basin.
articles.abstract: The Syr Darya River Basin is a major transboundary freshwater system in Central Asia facing increasing pressure from climate change, agricultural intensification, mining, industrial development, and urbanization. This study provides a systematic review and quantitative hydrochemical synthesis of published literature addressing water and sediment quality across the basin between 2000 and 2026. A PRISMA-based search identified 1073 records, of which 24 studies containing primary quantitative datasets were retained. Following harmonization, 123 site-specific water observations from 19 studies were integrated into a basin-wide hydrochemical database and evaluated across four operational sectors: Upper Sector, Uzbek-Tajik Sector, Middle Sector, and Small Aral Sea. document a clear downstream hydrochemical evolution from low-mineralized Ca-HCO3 waters in the Upper Sector (TDS 281-302 mg L-1) to increasingly mineralized Ca-Mg-SO4-Cl and Na-SO4 waters in downstream reaches, where TDS frequently exceeds 1000 mg L-1. Salinization emerges as the dominant basin-scale water-quality issue, driven by irrigation return flows, collector-drainage water recirculation, shallow saline groundwater, and strong evaporative losses. Contaminant enrichment is concentrated within specific industrial and mining corridors, particularly in the Chirchik-Akhangaran system, the Angren-Almalyk district, the Shardara Reservoir, and the Small Aral Sea. Arsenic, cadmium, lead, and uranium are the most frequently reported inorganic contaminants of concern, while sediments function as long-term reservoirs for trace elements and persistent organic pollutants. The review highlights major monitoring gaps and supports the need for harmonized transboundary monitoring and integrated basin-scale water-quality management.

articles.title: Comparison of cone beam computed tomography measurements obtained after manual and AI-assisted head positioning and reconstruction.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare measurements obtained from cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) exams by radiologists following manual head positioning and panoramic curve tracing with those obtained after artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted positioning adjustments performed prior to measurement.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Twenty-five CBCT exams presenting edentulous sites corresponding to missing mandibular first molars were selected. Five examiners performed measurements of bone height and width after manual head positioning adjustments and panoramic curve tracing (manual method). Subsequently, the same exams were processed using TomoNav software, which automatically performed volume alignment and generated the panoramic curve and cross-sectional images. The examiners then repeated the measurements (AI-assisted method). Measurements obtained from both approaches were summarized using descriptive statistics and compared using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), paired t-test, and Bland-Altman analysis (p˂0.05).

RESULTS: Excellent inter-examiner reproducibility was observed for both height and width measurements, with ICC values of 0.94 for height and 0.81 and 0.85 for width using the manual and AI-assisted methods, respectively. Significant differences were identified for left-side height, total height, right-side width, and total width (p < 0.05). However, the mean biases were low and overall agreement between methods was excellent, with ICC values equal or greater than 0.89.

CONCLUSION: Measurements obtained with the AI-assisted method for volume repositioning and generation of panoramic and cross-sectional images were comparable to those obtained using a conventional method.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: AI facilitates CBCT implant-planning preprocessing without compromising measurement reproducibility.

articles.title: Symmetry in acute stroke imaging: a diagnostic pitfall.

Differential effects of pea protein isolate, pea protein concentrate, and whey protein isolate supplementation on gut microbiota and metabolic markers in healthy adults: a 3-arm parallel randomised intervention.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: As origin and quality of dietary protein are key modulators of gut microbiota and host metabolism, characterising health effects of different proteins is increasingly important given the need to shift towards more plant-based protein sources for environmental sustainability. Yet, direct comparisons across protein sources and food matrices in humans remain limited. This randomised, double-blind, 3-arm parallel, dietary intervention study examined the effects of four-week pea protein concentrate (PPC), pea protein isolate (PPI) or whey protein isolate (WPI) supplementation (0.5 g/kg body mass/day) on gut microbiota composition in healthy adults as the main outcome.

METHODS: Faecal samples and lifestyle questionnaires were collected weekly, with fasting blood and 24-h urine samples obtained at baseline, mid- and post-intervention. Proteins were compared using two contrasts - PPC vs. PPI and PPI vs. WPI - investigating differences between plant and animal-based proteins as well as between plant-based proteins with different matrixes.

RESULTS: Supplementation of PPC and PPI significantly reduced α-diversity and increased β-diversity, partly modulated by BMI. At species level, relative abundances of Anaerobutyricum hallii and Bifidobacterium longum increased significantly in subjects consuming PPC. A similar result was observed for Lactobacillus crispatus and Limosilactobacillus frumenti in subjects consuming PPI.

CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that different dietary proteins selectively modulate beneficial gut microbial species, highlighting the importance of investigating individual responses to dietary interventions. Further studies are needed to verify how compositional changes translate into changes in microbial functionality.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study is registered at www.

CLINICALTRIALS: gov as NCT05611138 (November 02, 2022).

articles.title: Maternal fish or n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid intake during pregnancy and risk of impaired kidney function at 6 years of age: the Japan environment and children's study.
authors: Japan Environment and Children’s Study Group
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Chronic kidney disease in children causes kidney failure and growth impairment, making its prevention an urgent clinical and public health priority. Experimental animal studies have suggested that maternal intake of n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) during pregnancy may have kidney-protective effects in offspring; however, evidence in humans remains limited. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the association between maternal fish or n-3 PUFA intake during pregnancy and kidney dysfunction in children.

METHODS: We analyzed data from the Japan Environment and Children's Study, a nationwide prospective birth cohort. A total of 2,679 mother-child pairs were included. Kidney dysfunction was defined as an estimated glomerular filtration rate < 90 mL/min/1.73 m² at 6 years of age. Maternal fish or n-3 PUFA intake during pregnancy was categorized into quintiles. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to estimate the associations.

RESULTS: At 6 years of age, 262 children (9.8%) had decreased kidney function. In the adjusted model, maternal fish intake in the highest quintile was associated with a significantly lower risk of kidney dysfunction compared with the lowest quintile (odds ratio, 0.63; 95% confidence interval, 0.41-0.99). Maternal n-3 PUFA intake showed a similar trend, although the association was not statistically significant.

CONCLUSION: Higher maternal fish intake during pregnancy was associated with a reduced risk of kidney dysfunction in offspring, whereas maternal n-3 PUFA intake showed no significant association. These findings suggest that higher maternal fish intake during pregnancy may be associated with a lower risk of impaired kidney function in children.

articles.title: Real-world performance of pelvic MRI and abdominopelvic CT for nodal staging in higher-risk prostate cancer and the incremental clinical value of CT.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Conventional imaging with pelvic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and abdominopelvic computed tomography (CT) is still used for the staging of prostate cancer (PCa), particularly when molecular imaging is unavailable. mpMRI is currently recommended before prostate biopsy. We evaluated the agreement between MRI and CT for nodal and distant staging, their diagnostic accuracy against surgical nodal staging, and the real-world clinical utility of CT when pelvic MRI is already available.

METHODS: Among consecutive prostate biopsies, we retrieved patients with unfavorable intermediate- or high-risk PCa who underwent both pelvic MRI and abdominopelvic CT (and bone scan). Agreement for nodal staging was assessed using Cohen's κ. Diagnostic performance was evaluated in patients undergoing radical prostatectomy with pelvic lymph node dissection, using final pathology as the reference standard. The clinical yield of CT was assessed post hoc, considering nodal or metastatic reclassification or urgent non-PCa-related findings.

KEY FINDINGS AND LIMITATIONS: We included 323 consecutive patients. MRI and CT identified cN1 disease in 6.8% and 8.1% of cases, respectively, and showed moderate agreement for pelvic nodal staging (κ = 0.51), with higher agreement in non-surgical patients. Both modalities demonstrated very low sensitivity for nodal metastases (≤ 20%) compared with pathology, with area under the curve (AUC) < 0.60. In the subgroup of patients who also had molecular imaging available (n = 82) PSMA PET/CT showed superior performance (AUC = 0.86). In a post-hoc exploratory analysis, CT provided oncologically relevant information not detected by mpMRI in 11.0% of patients (number needed to scan [NNS] = 9.2). Considering also urgent non PCa-related findings, 14.1% of CT scans yielded potentially clinically relevant information and the NNS decreased to 7. Limitations include the retrospective design and the lack of centralized imaging review.

INTERVENTION: Imaging strategies were evaluated observationally.

CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: Pelvic MRI and CT show moderate agreement for nodal staging but poor diagnostic accuracy. Although the incremental value of CT beyond pelvic MRI is limited, CT may occasionally provide additional clinically relevant information when PSMA PET/CT is unavailable or not readily accessible.

articles.title: Is there an association between awake and sleep bruxism? : a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To systematically review and meta-analyze the association between sleep bruxism (SB) and awake bruxism (AB) in children and adults.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Observational studies evaluating the association between SB and AB were included. Studies were classified as direct or indirect evidence and according to diagnostic certainty as subject-, clinically-, and device-based. Random effects meta-analyses were performed using odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals.

RESULTS: Forty-nine studies were included. Most were cross sectional (n = 41), followed by case control studies (n = 6) and cohort studies (n = 2). Twenty-four studies were classified as direct evidence and twenty-five as indirect evidence. Most studies assessed subject-based bruxism (n = 35), followed by clinically-based bruxism (n = 10), mixed diagnostic criteria (n = 3), and device-based bruxism (n = 1). The overall meta-analysis included 8970 participants in the SB group and 25,730 in the AB group, showing a significant association between both conditions (OR = 3.74; 95% CI: 2.47; 5.67). The association remained significant in adults, children, direct studies, indirect studies, and studies assessing subject-based or clinically-based bruxism. Heterogeneity was high across all analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence indicates a significant positive association between sleep bruxism and awake bruxism. However, the predominance of cross-sectional designs, self-reported diagnostic methods, and high heterogeneity limits causal interpretation.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: SB and AB should not be assessed as completely isolated clinical findings. This meta-analysis shows that individuals with SB have higher odds of presenting AB. Therefore, when one circadian manifestation is identified, clinicians should actively investigate the other, particularly in patients with temporomandibular disorders, orofacial pain, sleep complaints, or stress related symptoms.

articles.title: National incidence and predictors of in-hospital venous thromboembolism after inpatient lumbar fusion, 2016-2022.
articles.journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To estimate the national incidence of in-hospital VTE recorded during the index lumbar fusion admission and identify independent comorbidity predictors.

METHODS: Adult (≥ 18 years) inpatient admissions undergoing lumbar fusion were identified in the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) from 2016 to 2022 using ICD-10-PCS procedure codes. The primary outcome was in-hospital VTE during the index admission. Characteristics were compared between VTE and non-VTE admissions, and multivariable survey-weighted logistic regression evaluated independent predictors. Significance was set at the P < 0.05 level.

RESULTS: Across 631,165 weighted inpatient lumbar fusion admissions, in-hospital VTE incidence was 0.6%. VTE admissions were older (age distribution, P < 0.001), more frequently male (P = 0.003), and more often involved multilevel fusion (78.5% vs. 74.2%, P = 0.007). On multivariable analysis, the largest adjusted associations were observed for other neurologic disorders (OR 3.76, 95% CI 2.93-4.83, P < 0.001), coagulopathy (OR 3.70, 95% CI 2.89-4.75, P < 0.001), weight loss (OR 3.57, 95% CI 2.35-5.42, P < 0.001), pulmonary circulation disorders (OR 2.78, 95% CI 1.82-4.23, P < 0.001), and paralysis (OR 2.78, 95% CI 2.09-3.71, P < 0.001). Additional predictors included solid tumor without metastasis (OR 1.97, P = 0.022), cerebrovascular disease (OR 1.90, P = 0.003), peripheral vascular disease (OR 1.58, P = 0.002), obesity (OR 1.75, P < 0.001), seizure disorders (OR 1.74, P = 0.016), congestive heart failure (OR 1.71, P < 0.001), and deficiency anemia (OR 1.64, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: In-hospital VTE recorded during the index lumbar fusion admission was uncommon but concentrated among patients with distinct high-risk comorbidity profiles. These findings support risk-stratified inpatient surveillance and prevention strategies during hospitalization.

articles.title: Comprehensive multi-organ and body composition phenotyping identifies metabolic signatures associated with incident type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To derive a multi-organ imaging biomarker panel from whole-body MRI and evaluate its predictive value for incident type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), including the role of intermuscular adipose tissue (IMAT) in reconciling discrepancies between muscle volume and metabolic risk.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analyzed 46,129 UK Biobank participants without diabetes at the time of imaging. Organ volume indices and fat fractions were extracted from Dixon MRI through automated segmentation. Associations between muscle volume indices, fat fractions, and handgrip strength were evaluated, and IMAT was graded in strength-matched participants. Independent imaging biomarkers were identified using adjusted Cox models, and a deep learning model was trained. Added value relative to the Leicester risk assessment score was evaluated using decision curve analysis.

RESULTS: During follow-up, 600 participants developed T2DM. Eight biomarkers independently predicted incident T2DM, including liver volume index (hazard ratio (HR), 1.28; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.19-1.38), pancreas fat fraction (HR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.10-1.28), and gluteus fat fraction (HR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.08-1.27). Gluteal IMAT grades were higher in weak-for-volume participants than in strength-matched controls (median, 2.0 vs 1.0; p = 0.02). The deep learning model achieved a concordance index of 0.814 (95% CI, 0.797-0.832) and, when applied sequentially with clinical criteria, reduced false-positive classifications by 43.0% while preserving 97.3% of true positives.

CONCLUSION: Whole-body MRI-derived multi-organ biomarkers independently predicted incident T2DM and enhanced risk stratification beyond an established clinical risk score. Muscle fat fraction may better reflect metabolic risk than muscle volume in IMAT-rich regions.

KEY POINTS: Question Clinical risk scores miss the multi-organ pathophysiology of type 2 diabetes; does whole-body MRI organ size and fat quantification improve prediction of incident diabetes? Findings Eight MRI-derived biomarkers independently predicted incident type 2 diabetes; a deep learning model using whole-body MRI biomarkers reached a concordance index of 0.814. Clinical relevance Automated whole-body MRI biomarkers capture multi-organ metabolic signatures beyond conventional risk scoring. Applied after clinical screening, they remove 43.0% of false-positive classifications while preserving 97.3% of true positives.

articles.title: Physiology-adapted cardiac CT angiography during veno-arterial ECMO in neonatal and pediatric postoperative congenital heart disease: feasibility and clinical impact.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac computed tomographic angiography (CCTA) provides high-resolution anatomical assessment in cases of congenital heart disease (CHD). This is crucial in patients supported by veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO), since the fundamental alteration of systemic hemodynamics and contrast transit kinetics makes conventional CT acquisition strategies unreliable.

OBJECTIVE: We evaluated the feasibility, diagnostic yield, and clinical impact of a structured CCTA protocol adapted to ECMO-dependent physiology in postoperative neonatal and pediatric CHD patients.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort study (2013-2022) included all consecutive postoperative neonatal and pediatric patients with CHD who underwent clinically indicated CCTA while supported by VA-ECMO subsequent to cardiac surgery. Contrast administration route and scan timing were individualized according to ECMO circuit flow characteristics and clinical indication.

RESULTS: Twenty-six CCTA examinations were performed in 25 patients ranging in age from 3 days to 14.8 years (median age 133 days; median weight 5.1 kg). Contrast was administered via the arterial ECMO limb in 15 cases and intravenously with controlled ECMO flow modulation in 11. In 18 of the 26 examinations (69%), the examination revealed a pathology. CCTA provided anatomical information beyond echocardiography in 22 of 26 cases (85%) and directly informed a surgical or catheter-based intervention in 14 cases (54%), with procedural confirmation in all. No transport-related or CT-related adverse events occurred.

CONCLUSION: When acquisition protocols are adapted to ECMO-dependent hemodynamics, CCTA is feasible and diagnostically consequential in neonatal and pediatric patients supported by VA-ECMO after congenital cardiac surgery. A physiology-guided strategy enables consistent vascular enhancement and frequently identifies clinically actionable findings not detected by echocardiography which can directly inform therapeutic decision-making in this critically ill population.

articles.title: Association between data-driven diabetes subtypes and kidney, cardiovascular, and all-cause mortality outcomes in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Data-driven clustering has identified reproducible diabetes subtypes with distinct metabolic profiles and complication risks. However, their incremental prognostic value and clinical utility beyond conventional risk assessment remain uncertain. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate associations between diabetes subtypes and long-term clinical outcomes in adults.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through February 25, 2026, with an updated targeted literature search and citation/reference screening performed through August 2026. Observational cohort studies classifying adults with diabetes using data-driven clustering and reporting longitudinal kidney, cardiovascular, or mortality outcomes were included. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled study-reported hazard ratios (HRs), and narrative synthesis was conducted when pooling was not possible due to differences in comparator subtype, outcome definitions, or clustering frameworks.

RESULTS: Thirty-four eligible study reports were included; 12 contributed to quantitative synthesis and 22 were synthesized narratively. Because several reports drew on overlapping source cohorts, a unique review-wide participant total was not calculated. Compared with mild age-related diabetes (MARD), severe insulin-resistant diabetes (SIRD) demonstrated the strongest associations with kidney outcomes, including CKD stage ≥3 (HR 1.84; 95% CI 1.53-2.20), advanced CKD (HR 2.34; 95% CI 1.84-2.99), ESKD (HR 3.83; 95% CI 2.47-5.93), and incident macroalbuminuria (HR 2.08; 95% CI 1.39-3.12). Severe insulin-deficient diabetes (SIDD) was also associated with increased kidney risk. Cardiovascular associations were more heterogeneous, although SIDD was associated with increased cardiovascular mortality compared with mild obesity-related diabetes (MOD) (HR 1.89; 95% CI 1.37-2.62). In an exploratory two-study analysis using MOD as the reference subtype, both SIRD (HR 2.05; 95% CI 1.46-2.87) and SIDD (HR 2.04; 95% CI 1.25-3.32) were associated with increased all-cause mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: Data-driven diabetes subtypes are associated with differences in kidney, cardiovascular, and mortality risk, with the most consistent associations observed for SIRD and kidney outcomes. Whether subtype classification improves prediction or clinical decision-making beyond conventional risk factors remains uncertain.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420261299731.

articles.title: Myosteatosis: the missing ectopic fat depot in diabetes and metabolic disease.
Undiagnosed poor sleep quality is common among older adults with type 2 diabetes and is associated with impaired quality of life and depressive symptoms.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Although diabetes is linked to sleep disorders that can reduce quality of life (QOL) and increase depression risk, these conditions are still rarely assessed in clinical practice. This study aimed to evaluate sleep quality in older adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and its association with QOL and depressive symptoms.

METHODS: 151 individuals with T2D aged > 60 years without known sleep disorders underwent a review of clinical history and therapy, biochemical exams, and assessment of Pittsburgh Sleep Quality index (PSQI), World Health Organization QOL Bref (WHOQOL-BREF) scale, and Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS). The population was then split into: Good Sleepers (PSQI ≤ 5) and Poor Sleepers (PSQI > 5).

RESULTS: The prevalence of low sleep quality was 63.6%. Poor Sleepers showed numerically comparable age, sex, body mass index, diabetes duration, and glycaemic control with Good Sleepers. However, Poor Sleepers showed lower scores in the physical health and psychological health domains of WHOQOL-BREF. After adjusting for confounders, PSQI score was associated with CVD (β = 0.26, P = 0.008) and diabetes duration (β = 0.24, P = 0.022). Furthermore, the scores in the physical health (β=-0.35) as well as the psychological health (β =-0.31) domains of the WHOQOL-BREF and the GDS (β = 0.24) were all independently associated with PSQI score (all P < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: In our population of older adults with T2D, poor sleep quality was highly prevalent and associated with poor quality of life and depressive symptoms. Thus, sleep quality assessment should be carefully considered in clinical practice, especially in people with long diabetes duration and complications.

articles.title: T1 mapping-based heterogeneity analysis of Gd-EOB-DTPA-enhanced MRI in cirrhotic nodules: biological basis, emerging evidence, and future perspectives.
articles.abstract: Liver cirrhosis is a major risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and accurate risk stratification of cirrhotic nodules remains a clinical challenge. During hepatocarcinogenesis, regenerative and dysplastic nodules undergo heterogeneous alterations in hepatocyte function, transporter expression, vascular architecture, and tissue composition. However, conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) assessment of intranodular signal heterogeneity largely relies on subjective visual interpretation and lacks standardized and reproducible quantitative biomarkers. Gadoxetic acid disodium (Gd-EOB-DTPA)-enhanced MRI provides functional information during the hepatobiliary phase by reflecting hepatocyte-specific uptake mediated by organic anion transporting polypeptides. Impaired transporter expression during malignant transformation is associated with reduced contrast uptake and may contribute to spatially heterogeneous contrast distribution. Quantitative T1 mapping enables voxel-wise measurement of absolute T1 relaxation times, thereby providing an objective and quantitative approach to tissue characterization. However, most existing studies have primarily focused on mean T1 values or global reduction rates, while intranodular spatial heterogeneity remains insufficiently explored. MRI-based heterogeneity analysis may complement conventional mean-value analysis by capturing regional variations within lesions. However, direct evidence on T1 mapping-derived heterogeneity in cirrhotic nodules remains limited, and its incremental value over mean T1 values for reflecting hepatocellular function or early malignant transformation has not been established. Quantitative heterogeneity descriptors, including standard deviation, coefficient of variation, histogram-based parameters, and texture features, can objectively characterize the magnitude and distribution of spatial T1 variation and provide a quantitative framework for assessing intralesional heterogeneity. This review summarizes the biological rationale, technical principles, and emerging evidence regarding Gd-EOB-DTPA-enhanced T1 mapping for the assessment of intranodular heterogeneity. It further discusses its potential role in malignant transformation risk stratification of cirrhotic nodules, current limitations, and future directions for clinical translation.

articles.title: Experimental evidence for cross-supergroup host switching in photosynthetic symbiosis between Mayorella viridis and Paramecium bursaria.
articles.abstract: Photosynthetic symbioses between unicellular eukaryotes and intracellular green algae (zoochlorellae) are widespread among protists and have evolved repeatedly during eukaryotic evolution. Molecular phylogenetic studies have suggested that host switching has contributed to the present distribution of zoochlorellae, but direct experimental evidence has remained scarce. Here, we examined whether zoochlorellae can be transmitted between the amoeba Mayorella viridis and the ciliate Paramecium bursaria using cross-infection experiments with isolated symbiotic algae and co-culture experiments with intact host cells. Intracellular establishment of zoochlorellae was achieved in all combinations examined. Phylogenetic analyses further demonstrated that Mayorella-associated zoochlorellae belong to multiple evolutionary lineages, supporting repeated acquisition of symbionts during evolution. Transmission electron microscopy revealed that the perialgal vacuole membrane was closely apposed to host tubular endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria, forming membrane associations consistent with putative contact sites. These findings provide experimental evidence for host switching between distantly related protozoan hosts and suggest that conserved host-symbiont interactions may facilitate the establishment and maintenance of photosynthetic symbiosis.

articles.title: [Disaster medicine in undergraduate medical education in Germany: curricular integration, relevance of learning objectives and barriers to implementation : A nationwide survey of faculty leads for multidisciplinary course 8].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous nationwide surveys demonstrated a heterogeneous implementation of disaster medicine education across German medical faculties. This study aimed to provide an updated assessment from the perspective of the teaching personnel responsible for multidisciplinary course 8 (QB 8), including predefined learning objectives, teaching formats and implementation barriers.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: A nationwide quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among QB 8 faculty leads at the 35 medical faculties affiliated with the German Medical Faculty Association at the time of data collection. Data were collected from 1-31 October 2025 using a standardized REDCap® (Research Electronic Data Capture) online questionnaire. Complete questionnaires were analyzed descriptively. Item-specific subpopulations were reflected in the predefined questionnaire routing.

RESULTS: Overall, 23 out of 35 questionnaires were completed (65.7%). Disaster medicine was taught at 18 out of 23 faculties (78.3%) and was mandatory in QB 8 at 10/23 (43.5%). Anesthesiology and intensive care medicine were involved at 16/18 faculties (88.9%). Foundations and strategies of care during mass casualty incidents were rated highly/very highly relevant by 19/20 respondents (95.0%); triage, differentiation between individual and disaster-adapted care and ethical/legal conflicts each by 18/20 (90.0%). The most frequent barriers were insufficient funding/resources (15/20; 75.0%), low curricular priority (11/20; 55.0%) and insufficient integration into mandatory teaching (10/20; 50.0%). Simulations (17/20; 85.0%) and case-based seminars with realistic scenarios (14/20; 70.0%) were most frequently considered particularly suitable.

DISCUSSION: Disaster medicine education is widely implemented among the participating faculties but remains heterogeneous regarding mandatory curricular implementation. The findings support the necessity for an expert consensus on priority learning objectives and further evaluation of competency-based teaching formats that are feasible within undergraduate medical curricula.

articles.title: [German Society of Cardiology position paper-how to treat patients with electrical storm: executive summary].
articles.abstract: Electrical storm (ES), defined as at least three sustained episodes of ventricular arrhythmia within 24 h, is a life-threatening state of electrical and frequently hemodynamic instability associated with a high risk of mortality. Recurrent ventricular arrhythmias indicate prognostically relevant disease progression even before overt ES develops. Accordingly, ES often represents the culmination of a continuum of increasing electrical instability that should ideally be prevented or interrupted at an early stage. Characterization of the underlying arrhythmogenic substrate, arrhythmogenic triggers, and the arrhythmia itself, together with assessment of the overall hemodynamic status, forms the basis for risk stratification, diagnostic evaluation, and targeted treatment of ES. For the first time, the German Cardiac Society (DGK) position paper integrates these three dimensions-substrate, trigger, and arrhythmia (STA)-into the STA triad. Most episodes of ES occur in patients with structural heart disease, particularly ischemic or nonischemic cardiomyopathy with advanced heart failure; primary electrical or inherited arrhythmia syndromes are less common. The NHII-MED (neuroendocrine dysfunction, heart failure/hemodynamics, ischemia/coronary pathology, inflammation/infection, medication/metabolic factors, electrolyte imbalances, drugs/alcohol) framework was introduced to facilitate systematic trigger identification and management. Core components of specialized acute treatment include correction of reversible causes, device management including implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) reprogramming, antiarrhythmic drug therapy, sedation, catheter ablation, autonomic modulation, optimization of treatment for the underlying cardiac disease, and, when required, mechanical circulatory support. The overarching therapeutic objective is to prevent further ventricular arrhythmias and repetitive ICD therapies. This executive summary of the DGK position paper addresses the associated clinical challenges and contemporary management options.

articles.title: [Patient Positioning During Trauma and Orthopedic Surgeries : Risks, responsibilities and practical recommendations].
articles.abstract: The correct positioning of patients in the operating theatre is an essential prerequisite for safe and successful operative interventions in orthopedic and trauma surgery. Operational positioning is often complex and associated with substantial risks. Position-related complications range from skin and soft tissue pressure injuries and musculoskeletal damage to peripheral nerve injuries up to rare but severe events such as postoperative visual loss. Prolonged operative time, obesity, diabetes mellitus and extreme joint positions are major risk factors. In Germany, patient positioning is a joint medical responsibility (surgeon, anesthetist) but primarily assigned to the surgeon with shared responsibility involving anesthesia and operating room personnel. A check by the surgeon and anesthesia at the beginning of the operation is necessary. Standardized checklists, adequate padding, limitation of extreme joint positions and regular intraoperative reassessment are key preventive measures. As positioning-related injuries are considered largely preventable, thorough documentation is of major medicolegal importance. This review provides a state-of-the-art overview of risks, responsibilities and evidence-based recommendations for safe patient positioning in orthopedic and trauma surgery.

articles.title: Engineering defect-rich CeO₂-Pd nanozyme and investigating their ROS mediated antibacterial action.
articles.abstract: Uncontrolled antibiotic use increases bacterial resistance and poses threat to infectious disease management. It led to exploring nanotechnology-based antibacterial alternatives like nanozymes (Nz) which exhibit intrinsic enzyme-like catalytic action. Cerium oxide (CeO2) Nz and its composites have shown immense antibacterial potential due to their multi-enzymatic character. Nevertheless, their antibacterial potential may be enhanced through engineering CeO2 Nz that promotes bacterial adhesion along with enhanced localized-ROS generation precisely at the bacteria-nanozyme interface. Localized stress improves bactericidal efficiency at biologically safe H2O2 concentrations, addressing limitations associated with poor targeting and inefficient ROS utilization. In this context, the current study reports the engineering of defect rich CeO2-Pd Nz for enhanced ROS generation and antibacterial efficacy against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus through Pd loading. The pro-oxidative potential of the Nz was evaluated through colorimetric assays, and radical quencher/enhancer-based fluorescence assays. In vitro antibacterial efficacy of Nz was assessed using spread-plate method, live/dead staining, and biofilm studies. Loading Pd in CeO2 enhanced the oxygen vacancies and defects which consequently amplified its intrinsic peroxidase activity leading to high ROS generation. The engineered Nz demonstrated potent ROS mediated antibacterial activity against both E. coli and S. aureus. The presence of defective sites and surface roughness probably enhanced Nz-bacteria interaction and localized ROS generation which can also be observed through FE-SEM images. This close association induced oxidative stress in bacteria, leading to cell death. Furthermore, the nanozymes exhibited significant antibiofilm activity, effectively suppressing biofilm formation. The synthesized Pd loaded CeO2 Nz was highly selective in its antibacterial action and completely non-toxic toward L6 mammalian cells. The, synthesized Nz therefore, has potential to be used as a safe therapeutics for treating bacterial infections which can be explored in futuristic studies.

articles.title: Focused transesophageal echocardiography in cardiac arrest: promise, limits, and perspective.

articles.title: Voluntariness of same-day versus advance consent in low-risk clinical research: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The solicitation of same-day consent for participation in clinical research is commonly prohibited by research ethics boards because of concerns about limited decision-making time and patient vulnerability. However, these concerns lack empirical support and restrict both research efforts and patient participation opportunities, particularly in medical specialties such as emergency medicine, critical care, and anesthesiology, in which clinicians and patients interact for the first time on the day of a procedure. We aimed to assess the voluntariness of research consent solicited on the day of surgery compared with consent obtained in advance.

METHODS: We performed a prospective, noninferiority randomized controlled trial examining the voluntariness of informed consent to participate in a low-risk clinical research trial at Women's College Hospital in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. The trial design included active deception (invitation to participate in a fabricated research trial) to capture authentic measurements of participants' perceptions of any perceived coercion.

RESULTS: We randomized 114 patients scheduled to undergo anterior cruciate ligament repair for recruitment into a fabricated low-risk perioperative research trial at one of two time points: at a virtual preanesthesia clinic appointment in advance of the day of surgery, or on the day of surgery. Regardless of their decision, all participants received the (same) standard of care. Overall, 71/114 patients (62%) either consented to participate in the fabricated trial or declined participation but consented to a feedback session during which perceptions of coercion were assessed. Greater participation was observed among patients approached on the day of surgery (fabricated trial, 26/58 [45%]; feedback session only, 18/58 [31%]) than in advance (fabricated trial, 17/56 [30%]; feedback session only, 10/56 [18%]). Perceived coercion, measured using two validated psychometric instruments, did not differ between patients recruited on the day of surgery and those recruited in advance. A subset of patients in each group reported modest perceptions of undue influence, but regardless of recruitment time point, these patients demonstrated their agency to decline participation.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that restrictive same-day consent policies, when based on concerns regarding undue influence, may represent a structural barrier to participation in low-risk trials that lacks empirical justification.

STUDY REGISTRATIONS: 1) Open Science Framework ( 46twc ); first submitted 17 March 2023; 2) ClinicalTrials.gov ( NCT07380035 ); first submitted 16 January 2026.

articles.title: Toxocara Cati as a Target for Feline IgA.
articles.abstract: Toxocara cati is a common intestinal parasite of cats globally. On the mucous membranes, the host's immune system defends itself against​ invading pathogens, such as parasites, with immunoglobulin A (IgA) among other mechanisms. The precise role of IgA in T. cati infections is not yet understood.We determined the total IgA levels from serum (n = 8) and feces (n = 10) of T. cati -infected cats before and after anthelmintic treatment with a commercial ELISA. These results were compared with IgA levels of nonparasitic cats (serum n = 8, feces n = 6). We also visualized the binding of feline IgA to​ adult T. cati worms with immunohistochemistry and analyzed the IgA-reactive antigens with Western blot. Five antigenic bands were further analyzed with mass spectrometry.We found no consistency between total IgA levels in serum or feces and T. cati infection. In immunohistochemistry, the intestines, reproductive tracts, excretory canals, and muscle cell bodies of T. cati were the most immunoreactive parts when processed with either Toxocara-positive cat sera or pathogen-free cat serum. When comparing T. cati -infected and pathogen-free cat serum as IgA source in Western blot, most bands showed nonspecific IgA immunoreactivity independent of the host's Toxocara status. In mass spectrometry, the most prevalent proteins in the selected antigenic bands were two uncharacterized proteins, intermediate filament proteins, endoplasmin, paramyosin, actins, and glutamate dehydrogenase. The combined findings of this study suggest that IgA has mainly nonspecific actions against T. cati.

articles.title: Outcome of children with IgA vasculitis with nephritis treated with oral immunosuppressive treatment in combination with steroids.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: IgA vasculitis nephritis (IgAVN) determines long-term kidney prognosis in pediatric IgA vasculitis (IgAV). While corticosteroids (CS) remain standard therapy, the benefit of additional immunosuppressive therapy (IS) remains uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective study of children with biopsy-proven IgAVN treated with CS and IS in 14 French pediatric nephrology centers between 2000 and 2019. Outcomes were compared with a 1:1 matched cohort treated with CS alone, matched for age, proteinuria, eGFR, and histological severity. The primary endpoint was kidney remission, defined as urine protein-to-creatinine ratio <30 mg/mmol and eGFR >90 mL/min/1.73 m².

RESULTS: Fifty-one children (median age 8.5 years) received IS in addition to CS. After a median follow-up of 4.7 years, 30 (59%) achieved remission and 41% had persistent kidney disease. Proteinuria decreased rapidly after IS initiation. In the matched analysis (33 IS + CS vs. 33 CS-only), remission rates were similar (70% vs. 66%, p = 0.79). Older age and delayed initiation of IS were associated with a lower likelihood of remission. Although IS induced a rapid reduction in proteinuria, no significant difference in long-term remission was observed between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: In this pediatric IgAVN cohort, no significant difference in long-term kidney remission was observed between children treated with IS + CS and those treated with CS alone. Given the limited sample size, these findings should be interpreted with caution. Prospective pediatric studies are needed to define the optimal role and timing of IS in IgAVN.

articles.title: Secondary healthcare utilisation in children and young people following kidney transplant: a 10-year retrospective analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hospital admissions are common following paediatric kidney transplantation (PKT), yet national data describing patterns of healthcare utilisation and associated factors are limited.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using UK Renal Registry data linked to hospital episode statistics for patients aged ≤25 years receiving a first kidney transplant in England and Wales between 2012 and 2022. Secondary healthcare utilisation within the first post-transplant year was assessed, including elective and emergency admissions and inpatient days. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with emergency admission.

RESULTS: Among 2004 transplant recipients, 92% experienced at least one hospital admission in the first year, including 64% with ≥1 emergency admission. Emergency admissions (n = 3868) exceeded elective admissions (n = 1596) and were associated with longer length of stay. Younger age (OR per year increase 0.94, 95% CI 0.93-0.96) and female sex (OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.07-1.60) were independently associated with emergency admission. Compared with congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT), glomerular disease (OR 0.59, 95% CI 0.45-0.78) and hereditary nephropathies (OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.49-0.92) were associated with lower odds of emergency admission. Infection was the leading cause of admission (592 patients; median 4 months post-transplant). No independent associations were observed for ethnicity, socioeconomic deprivation, donor type, or preemptive transplantation.

CONCLUSIONS: Hospital utilisation in the first year after PKT remains substantial and is largely driven by emergency presentations, particularly among younger children and those with CAKUT. No independent ethnic or socioeconomic disparities were observed, supporting structured post-transplant care within a universal healthcare system.

articles.title: Collaborative decision-making among pediatric nephrology providers: a qualitative study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Collaborative decision-making involves supporting patients and families in making values-aligned healthcare decisions and may facilitate youth self-management. Very little is known about this process in pediatrics, especially about the roles providers play. This qualitative study aimed to address this gap by interviewing multidisciplinary pediatric nephrology providers to understand their roles in collaborative decision-making, barriers encountered, and strategies to address these challenges.

METHODS: This qualitative study was part of a larger investigation involving pediatric nephrology patients and caregivers. Multidisciplinary pediatric nephrology providers were recruited from two academic children's hospitals in the United States if their patient enrolled in the larger study. Providers completed qualitative interviews to share perspectives on collaborative decision-making.

RESULTS: Multidisciplinary pediatric nephrology providers (N = 17) described their roles in collaborative decision-making as guiding patients and families through complex medical decisions, initiating and facilitating collaborative decision-making discussions, and incorporating patient and family factors to tailor these discussions. However, providers encountered barriers in the process, particularly eliciting values, due to limited clinic time, challenges with relationship-building, and concern about patient burden, misaligned patient-provider values, and poor patient outcomes. Some providers described instances of avoiding collaborative decision-making. Strategies to overcome barriers focused on listening and communicating during decisional conflict.

CONCLUSIONS: Providers aimed to support collaborative decision-making but encountered numerous barriers, including with eliciting patient values and, at times, described hesitance to engage in collaborative decision-making. Providers may benefit from more support to engage in collaborative decision-making, elicit values, and navigate challenging discussions.

articles.title: Impact of posterior vitreous detachment on clinical outcomes in eyes with branch retinal vein occlusion.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate posterior vitreous detachment (PVD) status in eyes with branch retinal vein occlusion (BRVO) and its relationship to structural and treatment outcomes.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of eyes with treatment-naïve BRVO diagnosed within one year of onset from 2009 through 2021, with at least one year of follow-up. Eyes were stratified by PVD status on optical coherence tomography at presentation. Outcomes included cystoid macular edema (CME) prevalence, central subfield thickness (CST), and number of intravitreal injections.

RESULTS: Of 88 eyes, 33 (37.5%) had complete PVD and 55 (62.5%) did not. Patients with complete PVD were older (median 75 vs 67 years; p=0.02) and had a lower prevalence of hypertension (66.7% vs 89.1%; p=0.01). At one year, CME was less frequent in eyes with complete PVD (65.6% vs 88.9%; p=0.01), after adjustments for hypertension, baseline CME, and CST. Eyes with complete PVD had lower median CST (277.5 vs 301.0 μm; p=0.045) and required fewer median injections (4.0 vs 7.0; p=0.01) at one year, after adjustments for baseline CME and CST, but not hypertension. A significant interaction between baseline CST and PVD status was observed for one-year injection burden (p=0.03), with complete PVD associated with fewer injections at lower CST, but more injections at higher CST.

CONCLUSION: In eyes with BRVO, complete PVD at presentation was associated with lower one-year CME prevalence, CST, and injection burden. The relationship between PVD status and injection burden varied by baseline CST, suggesting PVD status and CST may provide complementary information regarding treatment burden.

articles.title: Adult esophageal duplication preoperatively diagnosed by endoscopic ultrasonography and treated with thoracoscopic resection: a case report.
articles.abstract: Esophageal duplication is a rare congenital foregut-derived anomaly that is usually diagnosed during childhood. Adult cases are uncommon and are often discovered incidentally. Because imaging findings frequently resemble those of other mediastinal or esophageal submucosal tumors, establishing a definitive preoperative diagnosis remains challenging. Here, we report an adult case of esophageal duplication that was diagnosed preoperatively using endoscopic ultrasonography and successfully treated with minimally invasive thoracoscopic resection, with emphasis on its characteristic imaging features.A 69-year-old man was incidentally found to have a cystic lesion in the lower esophagus during follow-up for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Computed tomography revealed a well-demarcated mass measuring approximately 50 mm. Endoscopic ultrasonography demonstrated an intramural cystic lesion with homogeneous hypoechoic contents that was continuous with the muscularis propria. Notably, the muscular layer of the cyst was continuous with that of the native esophagus, forming a characteristic Y-shaped configuration, a finding considered typical of esophageal duplication. On the basis of these endoscopic ultrasonography findings, a preoperative diagnosis of esophageal duplication was established. Thoracoscopic excision of the duplication cyst was successfully performed with preservation of the native esophagus. Histopathological examination revealed a cyst lined with ciliated columnar epithelium and a two-layered smooth muscle wall, confirming the diagnosis. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient remains free of recurrence.This case highlights characteristic endoscopic ultrasonography findings, particularly Y-shaped muscular continuity, that enabled accurate preoperative diagnosis and differentiation from other mediastinal and subepithelial lesions, and demonstrates that thoracoscopic resection is a safe and minimally invasive treatment option for adult esophageal duplication.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of selective orexin 2 receptor agonists in narcolepsy type 1: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Selective orexin 2 receptor (OX2R) agonists target the orexin deficiency underlying narcolepsy type 1, but their efficacy and safety across compounds have not been quantitatively synthesized.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane library from inception through September 10, 2026, for randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of oral OX2R agonists in narcolepsy type 1.The primary outcomes were Maintenance of Wakefulness Test sleep latency, Epworth Sleepiness Scale score, and weekly cataplexy rate. Safety analyses included all double-blind active regimens. Adjusted mean differences and incidence rate ratios were pooled using inverse-variance random-effects models with restricted maximum-likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals. Evidence certainty was assessed using GRADE.

RESULTS: Five trials randomized 550 participants and evaluated TAK-994, oveporexton, or alixorexton over 6-12 weeks; the primary efficacy synthesis included 337 participants. Compared with placebo, OX2R agonists increased Maintenance of Wakefulness Test sleep latency by 22.7 min (95% CI 16.8-28.7; 95% prediction interval, 8.0-37.4; I2 = 74.4%; low-certainty evidence), reduced epworth sleepiness scale scores (mean difference, - 9.8 points; 95% CI - 10.9 to - 8.8; I2 = 0%; moderate-certainty evidence), and reduced weekly cataplexy rates by 69% (incidence rate ratio, 0.31; 95% CI 0.23-0.41; I2 = 0%; moderate-certainty evidence). Urinary frequency, insomnia, urinary urgency, and salivary hypersecretion were more frequent with treatment. The TAK-994 program was terminated after hepatotoxicity.

CONCLUSIONS: Short-term OX2R agonist therapy improved wakefulness, sleepiness, and cataplexy in narcolepsy type 1. Limited trials, substantial MWT heterogeneity, and short follow-up constrain class-wide and long-term safety conclusions.

articles.title: Prevalence, Clinical Characteristics, and Hemodynamic Impact of Coronary Artery-Ventricular Microfistulas in Patients with Fontan Circulation.
articles.abstract: Coronary artery-ventricular microfistulas (CAMFs), which are defined as diffuse communications between dilated coronary arteries and the main ventricle, are poorly understood in Fontan circulation. We evaluated their prevalence, clinical features, and longitudinal hemodynamics. We retrospectively reviewed 167 Fontan patients undergoing cardiac catheterization between 2005 and 2025. Excluded were sinusoidal communications in PA/IVS, LV fistulas in HLHS, or solitary focal fistulas. Clinical, surgical, and serial hemodynamic parameters, such as the subendocardial viability ratio (SEVR) and aortic regurgitation (AR) index, were assessed. CAMFs were identified in 6 of the 153 eligible Fontan patients (prevalence: 3.9%). Polysplenia was more frequent in the CAMFs group (33% vs. 5%, ). At initial diagnosis, systemic cardiac index (median 3.3 L/min/m2 [range, 2.2-3.9 L/min/m2]) and ejection fraction (median 52% [range, 44%-65%]) were preserved. Notably, resting SEVR (median 91% [range, 85%-156%]) and AR index (median 54% [range, 44%-59%]) remained stable and well-compensated over a decade of follow-up. Late morbidities included protein-losing enteropathy (17%), pulmonary arteriovenous fistulas (17%), esophageal varices (17%), and death (17%). CAMFs occur in 3.9% of Fontan patients and correlate with polysplenia. Although resting SEVR and AR index remain well-compensated over mid-term follow-up, their impact on long-term outcomes beyond two decades post-Fontan remains uncertain. Careful long-term monitoring is necessary for late extra-cardiac complications and hemodynamic changes.
