The proposed six-phenotype classification provides a simple, admission-available bedside tool for early risk stratification and may inform individualized nutritional and metabolic management in critical care.

articles.title: Revisiting ringworm: an update on the epidemiology, taxonomy, and diagnosis of dermatophytes.
articles.abstract: Dermatophytes are fungi that invade keratin-containing tissues, causing superficial infections in hair, skin, and nails. Dermatophytosis is the most common fungal infection worldwide. The epidemiology of dermatophytes has undergone significant changes in recent decades, as have the tools available to diagnose and identify these pathogens. Here, we review the current epidemiology of dermatophytes, including the emergence of novel lineages, describe recent changes in taxonomy with the use of molecular approaches, and discuss the status of available diagnostic tools for dermatophytosis, with a focus on newer technologies.

articles.title: COVID-19 Is Not an Independent Risk Factor for Post-Intensive Care Syndrome: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundPost-intensive care syndrome (PICS) affects many ICU survivors, leading to persistent physical, cognitive, and mental health issues. The COVID-19 pandemic raised concerns about whether SARS-CoV-2 infection increases PICS risk. This study aimed to evaluate whether COVID-19 is an independent risk factor for PICS and to identify other contributing factors.MethodsThis retrospective cohort included 92 patients treated for respiratory failure in three ICUs at Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin between July 2020 and September 2021. Patients were divided into COVID-19 (n = 49) and non-COVID-19 (n = 43) groups. At three months post-discharge, outpatient assessments consisted of demographic data, ICU-related variables, and evaluations of physical (handgrip dynamometry, Timed Up and Go test), cognitive (Mini-Cog, Animal Naming Test), and psychological health (PHQ-4). PICS was defined as at least one abnormal test; severity was graded by the number of affected domains. Logistic and ordinal regression analyses assessed whether COVID-19 was independently associated with PICS prevalence and severity.ResultsPICS was present in 71.4% of COVID-19 and 62.8% of non-COVID survivors (p = 0.378). Multivariable analysis showed no significant association between COVID-19 and PICS or its severity (OR = 1.46; 95% CI 0.50-4.23; p = 0.486; and OR = 1.09; 95% CI 0.45-2.68; p = 0.845, respectively).ConclusionsCOVID-19 was not independently associated with PICS in ICU survivors. Both groups experience high rates of long-term impairments, highlighting the importance of rehabilitation and follow-up care for all ICU survivors.

articles.title: A core genome multilocus sequence typing scheme for Bacteroides fragilis: insights into population structure and genomic epidemiology.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Bacteroides fragilis strains are important members of the human gut microbiota and represent major opportunistic pathogens responsible for a wide range of anaerobic infections. Their clinical relevance is reinforced by diverse antimicrobial resistance mechanisms and a complex population structure comprising two major phylogenetic lineages, Division I and Division II. Although whole-genome sequencing is increasingly used for bacterial surveillance, no standardized core genome multilocus sequence typing (cgMLST) scheme is available for B. fragilis, limiting high-resolution and comparable genomic analyses. In this study, we developed a cgMLST scheme comprising 2,342 highly conserved loci applicable across both Divisions. The scheme was developed from 433 publicly available genomes with diverse geographic origins, sample types, and isolation periods. It was subsequently evaluated using 118 newly sequenced infection-associated isolates from France not included in scheme development. Clustering analysis identified an accurate single-linkage threshold of 400 allelic mismatches, providing balanced resolution for population structure analyses and high concordance with core genome phylogeny and classical MLST sequence types. Well-defined clusters were identified within both Divisions, with genetic profiles indicative of long-standing evolutionary divergence. These clusters showed no clear association with geographic origin, isolation source, or sampling period. Notably, some clusters were enriched in nim-positive and multidrug-resistant (MDR) isolates, including one in particular that emerged as a genetically divergent MDR-associated lineage within Division II. This cgMLST scheme provides a standardized and high-resolution framework for B. fragilis genotyping. Its implementation in the publicly accessible BIGSdb-Pasteur platform (https://bigsdb.pasteur.fr/) will support global genomic surveillance and future epidemiological studies.

IMPORTANCE: Bacteroides fragilis strains hold a position of relevance within the human gut microbiota, as they represent a major cause of severe anaerobic infections. Defining genotypes is essential for tracking infections and monitoring the emergence and spread of antimicrobial resistance. In this study, we developed a core genome multilocus sequence typing scheme for B. fragilis and applied it to a large collection of isolates from diverse origins. Our results reveal a structured population with well-defined and genetically conserved clusters across both Divisions, consistent with a long-standing population structure. Notably, several clusters were enriched in antimicrobial resistance determinants and multidrug-resistant isolates. This study also provides an easy-to-use resource for global surveillance and future epidemiological investigations of this clinically important pathogen.

articles.title: Measurement-Informed and Fluid-Sparing Cardiovascular Resuscitation Strategies in Pediatric Septic Shock: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: BackgroundPediatric septic shock resuscitation requires restoration of tissue perfusion while avoiding unnecessary fluid accumulation. The available comparative evidence includes both measurement-informed cardiovascular strategies and protocolized early vasoactive/fluid-sparing strategies, which differ substantially in mechanism and implementation.MethodsWe conducted a prospectively registered systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis of pediatric septic shock. To address clinical heterogeneity, interventions were classified post hoc, without changing eligibility criteria or outcomes, as measurement-informed technology-enabled strategies, structured early vasoactive/fluid-sparing strategies, or a hybrid phenotype-informed strategy. Randomized and nonrandomized evidence were analyzed separately. Random-effects models used restricted maximum likelihood; Wald 95% confidence intervals were primary and Hartung-Knapp intervals were examined for every pooled outcome. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I, and certainty using GRADE.ResultsSix comparative studies involving 422 children met eligibility criteria, including five randomized controlled trials and one prospective comparative study. The exploratory mortality synthesis across randomized strategies showed no statistically detectable difference (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.60-1.28; very-low-certainty evidence); the measurement-informed subgroup yielded RR 0.77 (95% CI 0.46-1.27). Two small randomized trials of measurement-informed resuscitation suggested lower total fluid administration during the first 24 h (MD -11.47 mL/kg, 95% CI -16.88 to -6.05; moderate-certainty evidence). Evidence for acute kidney injury was very uncertain (RR 0.48, 95% CI 0.15-1.57). Other outcomes were synthesized narratively because definitions, time points, or estimands were not sufficiently comparable.ConclusionsThe pediatric evidence base comprises mechanistically distinct cardiovascular resuscitation strategies rather than a single uniform intervention. Exploratory mortality pooling does not establish benefit or equivalence. Two small measurement-informed trials suggest lower 24-h fluid administration, but whether this process-level effect improves patient-centered outcomes remains uncertain. Future trials should prospectively link measured physiological variables or protocolized treatment rules to standardized clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Targeting sterylglucosidase 1 attenuates virulence and enables immune protection against Candida albicans.
articles.abstract: Sterylglucosidases are fungus-specific enzymes that regulate ergosterol 3-β-D-glucoside (Erg-SG) homeostasis and represent promising targets for antifungal intervention. Previous studies demonstrated that sterylglucosidases from Cryptococcus neoformans and Aspergillus fumigatus contribute to fungal virulence, and that deletion of these enzymes elicits protective immunity. However, whether sterylglucosidase-mediated pathways similarly influence Candida albicans pathogenicity remains unknown. Here, we identified C. albicans Sgl1 as a bona fide sterylglucosidase that selectively hydrolyzes Erg-SG but not fungal glucosylceramide. Deletion of SGL1 resulted in marked Erg-SG accumulation without altering glucosylceramide levels, confirming its conserved role in sterylglucoside homeostasis. Although the Δsgl1 mutant displayed largely preserved growth, morphogenesis, and stress adaptation, it exhibited impaired biofilm formation. Biochemical characterization, inhibitor profiling, and structural analyses revealed marked species-specific inhibitor susceptibility among fungal sterylglucosidases despite highly conserved overall architecture and catalytic machinery. Structural modeling and docking studies identified differences in ligand positioning and active-site interactions that likely contribute to these divergent pharmacological responses. Functionally, loss of SGL1 significantly attenuated virulence in a murine model of systemic candidiasis. Importantly, vaccination with heat-killed Δsgl1 cells conferred 70% protection against lethal systemic challenge and markedly reduced kidney fungal burden, providing the first evidence that sterylglucosidase-dependent vaccination can induce protective immunity against a non-pulmonary fungal infection. Collectively, these findings establish C. albicans Sgl1 as a conserved regulator of sterylglucoside homeostasis, fungal pathogenicity, and host protection, and identify fungal sterylglucosidases as promising targets for antifungal drug and immunotherapy development.IMPORTANCEFungal infections are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, yet effective immunotherapies and novel antifungal targets remain limited. Candida albicans is a major cause of invasive and mucosal fungal disease, highlighting the need for new therapeutic strategies. Here, we identify the fungus-specific sterylglucosidase Sgl1 as a conserved regulator of ergosterol 3-β-D-glucoside homeostasis and a critical determinant of C. albicans pathogenicity. We further demonstrate that fungal sterylglucosidases exhibit distinct species-specific pharmacological responses despite conserved structural frameworks, revealing opportunities for rational antifungal drug design. Importantly, deletion of SGL1 attenuated virulence and enabled protective vaccination against lethal systemic candidiasis, providing the first evidence that targeting sterylglucoside metabolism can elicit protective immunity against a non-pulmonary fungal pathogen. Together, these findings identify Candida albicans Sgl1 as a promising target for antifungal drug and immunotherapy development.

articles.title: Broad use of feline APN by alphacoronaviruses implicates cats in cross-species transmission.
articles.abstract: Coronaviruses continue to pose a global public health threat, and the increasing frequency of zoonotic spillover events highlights the crucial role of animal hosts in cross-species transmission. As companion animals, cats warrant attention for their potential involvement in coronavirus cross-species spread. Here, we show that feline aminopeptidase N (fAPN) functions as a shared receptor utilized by multiple alphacoronaviruses (α-CoVs), including human coronavirus 229E (HCoV-229E), transmissible gastroenteritis virus, and type-II feline infectious peritonitis virus, to mediate entry into feline cells. Structural and functional analyses reveal that distinct viruses engage fAPN through alternative binding sites, enabling multimodal receptor recognition, and demonstrating notable receptor compatibility. Animal challenge experiments further indicate that HCoV-229E showed detectable viral RNA and infectious virus in the feline respiratory tract, with no apparent clinical signs. Together, these findings establish fAPN as a shared receptor for diverse α-CoVs and reveal a molecular basis for receptor compatibility across viral lineages, providing insight into the determinants of coronavirus host range and cross-species transmission.IMPORTANCEZoonotic coronaviruses repeatedly threaten human health, yet the rules governing their ability to cross species remain incompletely understood. Cats live in close contact with humans and may act as hidden hosts for coronaviruses, but the molecular basis supporting cross-species infection in these animals is unclear. This study demonstrates that feline aminopeptidase N (fAPN) serves as a common receptor for several alphacoronaviruses (α-CoVs), including human coronavirus 229E (HCoV-229E), transmissible gastroenteritis virus, and type-II feline infectious peritonitis virus. These viruses recognize fAPN through distinct binding sites, highlighting the flexibility of receptor recognition. Additionally, HCoV-229E inoculation resulted in detectable viral RNA in the respiratory tract of cats, without apparent clinical signs. These results help explain why α-CoVs can move across host barriers and suggest that cats should be considered when assessing coronavirus spillover risks at the human-animal interface.

articles.title: Decreasing peptide deformylase activity is a beneficial strategy for increasing formaldehyde resistance in Methylobacterium extorquens.
articles.abstract: Formaldehyde is a highly toxic metabolite that can cause extensive damage to DNA and proteins, and strategies to mitigate formaldehyde toxicity are poorly understood. Methylotrophic bacteria, such as Methylobacterium extorquens, thrive on one-carbon compounds as sole sources of carbon and energy. These organisms are excellent models for discovering formaldehyde stress response systems because formaldehyde is an obligate intermediate in their central carbon metabolism. Here, we characterize an evolved def allele (defevo) that increases formaldehyde resistance in M. extorquens. The def gene encodes peptide deformylase (PDF, EC:3.5.1.88), an enzyme that contributes to protein processing by removing the formyl group from N-formylmethionine (fMet) on nascent peptides. The defevo allele has a single missense mutation that decreases PDF activity both in vitro and in vivo. Transcriptomic analysis of the defevo strain indicates that there are pleiotropic effects of this mutation and a differential response to formaldehyde stress. We investigate possible mechanisms for the defevo mutant's increased resistance to formaldehyde, including mitigation of formaldehyde-induced protein stress, and altered membrane physiology. We find that the defevo allele selectively alleviates exogenous, but not endogenous, formaldehyde stress, and identify a trade-off in heat shock resistance. This study reports the first observation of lowered PDF activity benefiting a cellular physiological phenotype. Our work indicates that altered protein metabolism can mitigate the toxic effects of formaldehyde and further our understanding of the strategies that protect cells from formaldehyde-induced damage.IMPORTANCEFormaldehyde is a toxic chemical that can damage essential molecules inside of cells, yet all organisms inevitably produce it during normal metabolism. Despite its ubiquity, our understanding of strategies for how cells navigate formaldehyde toxicity is incomplete. This study focuses on Methylobacterium extorquens, which naturally generates high levels of formaldehyde as part of its growth on simple carbon compounds. We show herein that a single genetic change that slows the processing of newly synthesized proteins during translation can unexpectedly improve the bacterium's ability to resist formaldehyde stress. Further, we show that this single change has numerous effects on the cell, many of which may contribute to formaldehyde resistance.

articles.title: When one size does not fit all: evaluating urine culture stewardship strategies for high-risk pediatric patients.
articles.abstract: Reflex urine culture protocols reduce inappropriate antibiotic use in adults but remain understudied in high-risk pediatric populations, including hematology/oncology and neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) patients. In this study, we evaluated the predictive value of urinalysis (UA) parameters for urine culture positivity within a quaternary care pediatric medical setting. We performed a retrospective analysis of 99,348 urine samples collected between January 2016 and January 2025. Among these, 20,019 paired UA-urine culture specimens were available, including 15,410 (77.7%) clean-catch and 4,609 (22.3%) in/out catheter specimens. UA markers assessed included leukocyte esterase (LE), nitrite, white blood cells, and microscopic bacteria. Across all specimens, the absence of UA markers (LE ≥ trace or nitrite positivity) demonstrated a negative predictive value (NPV) of 98.2% and sensitivity of 89.0% for a positive urine culture (≥10⁵ CFU/mL for clean-catch, and ≥5 × 10⁴ CFU/mL for in/out catheter specimens). The addition of microscopic parameters did not improve diagnostic accuracy. In hematology/oncology patients (n = 1,344), sensitivity was significantly reduced compared with the overall cohort (74.7% vs 89.0%, P < 0.05). Among neutropenic patients (n = 497), NPV remained high (98.7%), but sensitivity declined to 50.0% (P = 0.06). Overall, 1.8% of neutropenic patients with positive cultures had negative UA results, many of whom had prior antibiotic exposure. Implementation of a UA-based reflex protocol would have reduced urine culture orders by 65.3%. Negative UA reliably excluded urine culture positivity in most pediatric patients, supporting reflex culture protocols. However, reduced sensitivity in neutropenic hematology/oncology and NICU patients suggests such protocols are inappropriate for these groups.IMPORTANCERetrospective analysis of over 20,000 pediatric urine specimens demonstrated that screening urinalysis using leukocyte esterase or nitrite reliably predicted a negative urine culture, achieving a 98.2% negative predictive value. Furthermore, the addition of microscopic white blood cell counts did not improve overall diagnostic accuracy compared with automated urinalysis parameters alone. Implementing a urinalysis-based reflex algorithm would safely reduce unnecessary urine cultures by 65.3%, optimizing diagnostic stewardship and laboratory workflows. However, diagnostic sensitivity was significantly compromised in high-risk pediatric cohorts, including hematology/oncology, neutropenic, and neonatal intensive care unit patients. These findings demonstrate that while urinalysis reflex protocols are highly effective for general pediatric populations, diagnostic stewardship algorithms must account for host immune status to avoid missing true urinary tract infections in high-risk patients.

articles.title: A 68Ga-Substituted Keggin Phosphotungstate as an Intrinsically Radiolabeled Inorganic PET Tracer for Cell Tracking.
articles.abstract: Polyoxometalates (POMs) offer unique physicochemical properties for radiopharmaceutical design, yet their integration with clinically relevant radionuclides remains largely unexplored. Here we report the isolation and comprehensive solid-state and solution characterization of the gallium-substituted Keggin phosphotungstate cesium salt, Cs4[Ga(H2O)PW11O39]·8H2O (CsGaPW11), including single-crystal and powder X-ray diffraction, multinuclear NMR (31P, 71Ga, 183W), IR spectroscopy, ESI-MS, elemental analysis, and TGA. The radiolabeled analogue Cs68GaPW11 (45-55 MBq, >96% radiochemical purity) was synthesized in under 60 min, dictated by the 68 min half-life of 68Ga, and retained full structural integrity after radioactive decay. In CHO-K1 cells, Cs68GaPW11 shows higher cellular uptake than 68GaCl3 and 68Ga-oxine, with radioactivity progressively shifting from the cell membrane to the intracellular compartment over 60 min. Together with low cytotoxicity (>90% viability at 100 µM), these findings identify the membrane-permeable Keggin anion as a viable inorganic platform for PET cell tracking.

articles.title: The BspC surface adhesin and gastrointestinal fungal colonization enhance group B streptococcal neonatal infection.
articles.abstract: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) colonizes the gastrointestinal (GI) and female reproductive tracts of up to 30% of healthy adults, but during pregnancy can be transmitted to the newborn, causing neonatal sepsis, pneumonia, and meningitis. Neonatal GI colonization is an important precursor to invasive disease, yet the mechanisms governing GBS intestinal persistence and dissemination are still being elucidated. Given the predominance of hypervirulent sequence type 17 (ST-17) strains in neonatal invasive disease, we hypothesized that the ST-17-associated surface adhesin BspC contributes to gastrointestinal colonization and infection. Using a neonatal mouse model, we found that pups infected with wild-type GBS exhibited increased mortality and significantly higher bacterial burdens in the intestine, blood, spleen, and brain compared with pups infected with a ΔbspC mutant. We also observed that BspC promoted adherence to a 2D organoid model of the human infant colon and Caco-2 intestinal epithelial cells through its variable domain. Building on previous findings that Candida albicans interacts with BspC, we found that C. albicans enhanced GBS intestinal epithelial adherence in a BspC-dependent manner, and coinfection increased intestinal GBS burden and brain dissemination in neonatal mice. Finally, analysis of published human neonatal fecal microbiome data sets revealed higher GBS abundance in infants colonized with C. albicans or other Candida species. Together, these findings identify BspC as a key mediator of GBS intestinal colonization and invasive disease and suggest that fungal colonization of the neonatal GI promotes GBS pathogenesis.IMPORTANCEGroup B Streptococcus (GBS) is a leading cause of neonatal infection, which can result in fatality or long-term neurological morbidity in survivors. Intestinal colonization is an important precursor to invasive disease, yet the factors that promote GBS persistence in the neonatal gastrointestinal tract remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify the GBS surface adhesin BspC as a mediator of intestinal epithelial adherence, gastrointestinal colonization, and systemic dissemination. We further demonstrate that the common fungal pathobiont Candida albicans enhances GBS intestinal adherence and infection. Consistent with our experimental findings, analysis of human infant microbiome data sets revealed greater GBS abundance in infants colonized with Candida species. These findings identify BspC as a key mediator of this process and suggest that fungal colonization can enhance GBS disease.

articles.title: Durable and Additive Disease Control at 52 Weeks With Ixekizumab Plus Tirzepatide Versus Ixekizumab Alone in Adults With Psoriatic Arthritis and Obesity or Overweight: Additional Results From a Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Obesity or overweight occurs in 72% to 82% of individuals with psoriatic arthritis (PsA). Previous data revealed greater disease control with concomitant ixekizumab (IXE) and tirzepatide (TZP) versus IXE alone in adults with active PsA and obesity or overweight with at least one weight-related comorbidity at the week 36 primary end point. The objective of this report is to evaluate the effect of IXE+TZP versus IXE on psoriatic disease control and safety measures up to week 52.

METHODS: TOGETHER-PsA (ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT06588296) is a phase 3b, randomized, open-label, assessor-blinded 52-week trial. Participants were randomized 1:1 to IXE+TZP or IXE using US-approved doses. Week 52 outcomes were prespecified, non-multiplicity-controlled, and exploratory. Outcomes included 50% improvement in American College of Rheumatology response criteria (ACR50) and rheumatologic, dermatologic, patient-reported, metabolic, and safety outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 271 participants were randomized (IXE+TZP, n = 138; IXE, n = 133). The proportion achieving the primary outcome of simultaneous ACR50 and ≥10% weight reduction continued to increase from week 36 through week 52 for IXE+TZP (39.2%) versus IXE (1.7%) (Δ37.5%; P < 0.001). ACR50 continued to diverge after week 36, with a clinically meaningful difference at week 52 for IXE+TZP (43.7%) versus IXE (15.7%) (Δ 28.0%; P < 0.001). IXE+TZP demonstrated significant improvements in ACR20, minimal disease activity, Disease Activity Index for Psoriatic Arthritis, patient-reported outcomes, and metabolic outcomes versus IXE alone. Safety profiles were consistent with previous studies for each drug.

CONCLUSION: Comprehensive improvements in disease activity, including ACR50, quality of life, weight, and metabolic outcomes, continued through week 52 and were greater with IXE+TZP than IXE alone, with no new safety concerns. These findings support concomitant IXE+TZP in patients with active PsA and immunometabolic disease.

articles.title: Electrochemiluminescence as a Transformative Diagnostic Tool for SARS-CoV-2 Variant Detection: Implications for Future Pandemic Preparedness.
articles.abstract: Over the past two decades, the three major betacoronavirus outbreaks, SARS-CoV (2002), MERS-CoV (2012), and SARS-CoV-2 (2019), have resulted in millions of infections and deaths globally. SARS-CoV-2 has displayed rapid mutations, enhancing its transmissibility, immune evasion, and resistance to existing vaccines and diagnostics. For these reasons, it has been named the most notorious viral outbreak in modern history. Due to the ever-mutating Spike (S) protein, key interactions with bioreceptors have been disrupted, making conventional detection methods more challenging. To minimize viral spread and improve diagnostic accuracy, innovative biosensing technologies are critical. As such, electrochemiluminescence (ECL) offers a powerful biosensing platform for SARS-CoV-2 variant detection by combining the high sensitivity of optical detection with electrochemistry. Its advantages include culture-independent detection, low background noise, a broad dynamic range, and the ability to detect low viral concentrations. Recent advances in multiple disciplines, such as novel luminophore development, nanotechnology, lab-on-a-chip miniaturization, and AI-driven machine learning, have further enhanced its diagnostic powers. Furthermore, smartphone-integrated ECL platforms enable rapid, point-of-care testing, improving disease surveillance and outbreak response. By uniting AI with ECL biosensing, the diagnostic system can refine variant classification and predict emerging mutations, making ECL a promising candidate for the next generation of pandemic diagnostics. Despite the many advantages, there is limited research that has explored ECL for SARS-CoV-2 variant detection, which is addressed in this review. This review highlights ECL's potential to become a gold-standard technique for detecting rapidly evolving pathogens, offering a robust and accessible solution for future infectious disease monitoring.

articles.title: Development and external validation of machine learning models for predicting glucose trajectories after continuous intravenous insulin therapy in hyperglycemic crises.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Predicting short-term blood glucose changes after initiation of continuous intravenous insulin infusion (CII) in hyperglycemic crises remains challenging because glucose trajectories are influenced by both patient-specific metabolic severity and dynamically adjusted treatment. This study aimed to develop and externally validate machine learning models for estimating retest glucose levels and glucose-lowering responses after CII initiation.

METHODS: We analyzed 574 post-CII blood glucose measurements from 191 patients with hyperglycemic crises across five Japanese institutions. An independent external validation cohort included 29 patients from another institution. Two complementary models were developed using gradient-boosted decision tree algorithms: a direct retest glucose prediction model and a ΔGlu treatment-response model. We evaluated model performance using internal validation, patient-level fivefold cross-validation, and external validation. ΔGlu was defined as the decrease in blood glucose between two consecutive reassessment points.

RESULTS: The eight-feature direct retest glucose model showed stable predictive performance in internal validation (R2 = 0.853, MAE = 76.9 mg/dL, RMSE = 106.0 mg/dL), patient-level fivefold cross-validation (R2 = 0.803 ± 0.080), and external validation (R2 = 0.802, MAE = 78.0 mg/dL, RMSE = 101.0 mg/dL). Although the eight-feature ΔGlu treatment-response model showed moderate internal performance, its external generalizability for ΔGlu prediction was limited.

CONCLUSIONS: The direct retest glucose model showed stable performance across internal and external validation, whereas ΔGlu itself was more difficult to generalize across institutions. These complementary models may support objective monitoring of short-term glucose trajectories during CII for hyperglycemic crises, although further prospective validation is warranted.

articles.title: Aviation Medicine and Cardiovascular Assessment of Aircrew: A European Society of Cardiology-Aligned Review of Integrating International Civil Aviation Organization, European Union Aviation Safety Agency, Federal Aviation Administration, and Turkish Directorate General of Civil Aviation Aeromedical Standards.
articles.abstract: Aeromedical certification is based on a safety-first principle: a pilot or other aircrew member must not have a medical disorder that creates an unacceptable risk of sudden or subtle incapacitation during flight. Cardiovascular disease remains one of the most important determinants of flight fitness, as it may impair consciousness, judgment, rhythm stability, exercise capacity, and hemodynamic reserve. Modern aeromedical decision-making therefore requires the integration of aviation law, operational risk, contemporary cardiology guidelines, advanced imaging, biomarkers, and long-term surveillance. The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Annex 1 provides the global licensing framework; the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) Part-MED, together with its Acceptable Means of Compliance and Guidance Material, defines detailed operational standards in Europe; and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) employs a protocol- and special issuance-based system for many cardiovascular and metabolic disorders. This review summarizes the aeromedical assessment of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic and acute coronary syndromes, heart failure, cardiomy-opathies, arrhythmias and conduction disorders, pacemakers and implantable cardiac devices, valvular heart disease, aortic disease, congenital heart disease, venous throm-boembolism, cardiovascular pharmacotherapy, and major respiratory conditions rel-evant to flight certification. The manuscript is aligned with current European Society of Cardiology cardiovascular guidance and with the operational aeromedical principles applied by ICAO, EASA, FAA, and the Turkish Directorate General of Civil Aviation. In general, preserved ventricular function, absence of significant symptoms, low thrombo-embolic and arrhythmic risk, stable treatment, and adequate exercise capacity support certification or restricted certification. In contrast, uncontrolled hypertension, unstable diabetes, significant residual myocardial ischemia, reduced ejection fraction, malignant ventricular arrhythmias, implantable defibrillator therapy, severe valvular disease, significant aortic pathology, major congenital hemodynamic lesions, or poorly controlled sleep apnea usually preclude certification. Final decisions remain individualized and depend on license class, operational role, treatment burden, surveillance data, and the judgment of the aeromedical authority.

articles.title: Oral Care of Post-Stroke Dysphagia Patients: A Cross-Sectional Survey of Neurological Nurses' Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Most post-stroke dysphagia (PSD) patients suffer from compromised oral health, which necessitates standardised oral care delivered by nurses. This study aimed to evaluate neurological nurses' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) related to oral care for PSD patients and explore associated influencing factors.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was performed from September to November 2024 with convenience sampling across Southwest China. Data were gathered via an online questionnaire consisting of two parts: demographic characteristics and a self-developed KAP scale tailored for neurological nurses responsible for oral care of PSD patients. Univariate correlation analysis and multiple linear regression analysis were applied to identify predictors of KAP scores.

RESULTS: In total, 337 valid questionnaires were retrieved and analysed, corresponding to an effective response rate of 92%. Around 70.92% (n = 239) of participating nurses had never received targeted training on oral care for PSD patients. The mean total KAP score for neurological nurses regarding oral care for PSD patients was 121.45 ± 18.15, with scores for knowledge, attitudes, and practices being 53.98 ± 10.96, 43.75 ± 7.14, and 23.82 ± 6.50, respectively. Multiple linear regression demonstrated that hospital level, educational attainment, years of neurological nursing experience, and prior specialised training were significant predictors of KAP total scores (P 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Neurological nurses had deficiencies in all three KAP dimensions for PSD oral care. Standardised targeted training programmes should be developed to improve nurses' professional oral care competence.

articles.title: Periodontitis and Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Evidence for a Potential Biological Link.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the potential association between gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and periodontitis (PD) and to explore possible biological mechanisms underlying this link.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In the first part of this study, a two-sample Mendelian randomisation (MR) analysis was conducted to evaluate the potential effect of PD on the risk of GDM, and vice versa. In the second part, transcriptomic data and network-based bioinformatics analyses were integrated, including differential expression analysis and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network construction, to screen for common differentially expressed genes and significantly enriched biological pathways. In the third part, a simplified in vitro β-cell challenge system was established using the human pancreatic β-cell line EndoC-βH1. Cells were exposed to high-glucose and progesterone conditions with or without Porphyromonas gingivalis to examine inflammatory and oxidative stress responses. Differences in the expression of MR-genes, inflammatory cytokines, and reactive oxidative species were evaluated. All analyses were performed using R version 4.2.2 (R CoreTeam, Vienna, Austria).

RESULTS: The forward MR analysis showed evidence consistent with a modest positive association of genetically predicted PD with GDM risk (OR = 1.14, P = 0.006), whereas the reverse analysis did not provide evidence for an association of genetically predicted GDM with PD risk (OR = 1.08, P = 0.222). Sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the MR results. Transcriptomic bioinformatic analyses identified multiple key genes that were dysregulated in both PD and GDM, including inflammatory mediators (IL1RN and TGFB1) and metabolic regulators (AKT1, NOS3, and TCF7L2). Functional enrichment revealed that the overlapping genes were mainly involved in critical biological processes like apoptotic signalling, cell adhesion, and inflammatory responses. The PPI network suggested a synergistic role of PD and GDM in inflammation and metabolic regulation. Compared with the GDM model, β-cells in the GDM+PD model exhibited significantly enhanced inflammatory responses and oxidative stress. Additionally, the MR-genes showed significant expression changes in the GDM+PD model: HSPBAP1, APBA1, and SHC4 were upregulated, whereas CDH1, NDUFAF6, and DGKB were downregulated.

CONCLUSION: These findings provide evidence consistent with a potential biological link between PD and GDM, in which periodontal infection-related inflammatory responses and oxidative stress may aggravate β-cell stress under GDM-like conditions.

articles.title: Intrarenal Pressure Monitoring and Control Strategies Using Suction in Flexible Ureteroscopy: An EAU Endourology Systematic Review of Technologies and Clinical Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Intrarenal pressure (IRP) is a key physiological parameter during retrograde intrarenal surgery (RIRS), and elevated IRP has been linked to postoperative infectious and renal complications. Multiple technologies have been developed to monitor and control IRP during RIRS. We aimed to systematically evaluate pressure-monitoring and pressure-control technologies used during RIRS, including suction irrigation pressure autoregulating systems (SIPS), pressure-monitoring systems, and flexible and navigable suction ureteral access sheaths (FANS), with a primary focus on their IRP control performance and a descriptive assessment of reported perioperative outcomes.

METHODS: This systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261298652). MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched on November 1, 2025. Randomized and non-randomized studies evaluating pressure-sensing, suction-assisted, or SIPS-based technologies during RIRS were included. Primary outcomes were intraoperative IRP metrics. Secondary outcomes included fever, sepsis, stone-free rate (SFR), operative time, and secondary intervention. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, ROBINS-I, and the JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Case Series, as appropriate, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE.

RESULTS: We included 11 studies comprising 786 patients for clinical analysis. Across studies, reported IRP profiles varied by pressure-monitoring or pressure-control technology and procedural protocol. Studies evaluating active pressure-control systems reported low intraoperative IRP, whereas pressure-monitoring studies showed substantial variability in IRP during conventional ureteroscopy. Studies evaluating pressure-monitoring FANS reported controlled IRP profiles alongside higher irrigation flow rates and, in some comparisons, shorter operative times. Use of an 11/13F ureteral access sheath, compared with a 13/15F sheath, was associated with a higher likelihood of elevated intraoperative IRP (≥30 mmHg) (OR: 12.5). Across individual studies, reported postoperative fever rates ranged from 0% to 5%, sepsis rates from 0% to 3%, and stone-free rates for stones ≤2 cm from 87.5% to 95.8%; these outcomes were assessed descriptively. Heterogeneity in study design and pressure-reporting methods precluded meta-analysis.

CONCLUSION: Available studies suggest that pressure-monitoring and pressure-control technologies may improve intrarenal pressure management during RIRS. However, current evidence is limited by methodological heterogeneity and the predominance of non-randomized studies. Large multicenter randomized trials with standardized pressure metrics and clinically meaningful endpoints are required to determine whether improved IRP control translates into better perioperative outcomes.

articles.title: Intracellular α1A-adrenergic receptor regulation of cAMP production by an inside-out mitogen-activated protein kinase signalling pathway in cardiac myocytes.
articles.abstract: Sympathetic stimulation produces beneficial changes in cardiac function through β-adrenergic receptor (βAR) production of cAMP and subsequent alteration of electrical and mechanical activity. Long-term activation of cAMP production also contributes to cardiac remodelling and detrimental changes associated with heart failure. However, sympathetic responses are mediated by the endogenous neurotransmitter norepinephrine (NE), which is also a potent α1-adrenergic receptor (α1AR) agonist, and α1AR activation can produce significant effects on the heart as well. What is less clear is how α1- and β-adrenergic responses interact with one another. Previous studies have demonstrated that α1AR activation can inhibit β-adrenergic regulation of the electrical and mechanical activity of cardiac myocytes, although the signalling mechanisms involved were not previously known. In the present study, we used fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET)-based biosensors in adult rat ventricular myocytes to demonstrate that this cross-talk effect involves the inhibition of cAMP production by intracellular α1A-adrenergic receptors (α1AARs) acting on βARs found on the plasma membrane. Furthermore, we established that this inside-out signalling mechanism involves a mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway that uncouples βARs from downstream signalling in a G protein-coupled receptor kinase (GRK)/arrestin-dependent manner. These results reveal a novel, non-canonical signalling mechanism contributing to α1AR responses in the heart, and that this effect limits βAR production of cAMP by NE. This mechanism may contribute to the cardioprotective effect previously ascribed to α1AAR activation. These findings also clearly demonstrate the importance of considering the contributions of α1 and βARs together when studying the influence of the sympathetic nervous system on the heart. KEY POINTS: Acute sympathetic stimulation produces beneficial changes in cardiac function through the release of norepinephrine (NE), activation of β-adrenergic receptors (βARs) and subsequent production of cAMP. However, long-term sympathetic stimulation of the same signalling pathway contributes to the development of heart failure and cardiac arrhythmias. NE also activates α1-adrenergic receptors (α1ARs), which have been linked to a cardioprotective effect involving a mechanism not well defined. The present study demonstrates that the activation of intracellular α1A-adrenergic receptors (α1AARs) reduces cAMP production by βARs found on the cell surface. This 'inside-out' signalling mechanism acts through a mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway to enhance β-arrestin-mediated uncoupling of βARs from downstream signalling. By limiting excessive cAMP production, α1AAR signalling may help protect the heart during prolonged sympathetic stimulation, highlighting the importance of considering the effects of α1- and βAR signalling together when studying sympathetic responses in the heart.

articles.title: Evaluation of point-of-care testing (POCT) for blood-borne infections in forensic autopsy specimens.
articles.abstract: Lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA)-based point-of-care testing (POCT) for viral antigen and antibody detection enables rapid screening for blood-borne viral infections and may be particularly valuable in forensic autopsy settings, where incomplete antemortem medical histories and invasive procedures increase the risk of occupational exposure. However, its performance in postmortem specimens remains unclear. We evaluated the applicability of LFIA-based POCT for detecting human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and hepatitis B virus (HBV) in autopsy specimens, focusing on postmortem decomposition and the use of solid organ tissues as alternatives to blood. A total of 309 cases were analyzed using LFIA and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) across blood, liver, and spleen specimens. Agreement was assessed using overall, positive, and negative percent agreement and Cohen's kappa coefficient (κ). Positivity rates were compared by specimen type and decomposition status. LFIA agreement with qPCR varied by marker and specimen type, with substantial agreement for HIV and HCV antibody detection in blood and lower agreement in liver and spleen. Fresh specimens generally demonstrated higher LFIA positivity rates than decomposed specimens. Among specimens meeting predefined qPCR positivity criteria, LFIA-positive specimens tended to exhibit higher viral loads than LFIA-negative specimens, reaching statistical significance for HBV in liver, with similar but non-significant trends for blood HBV and liver HCV. LFIA-based POCT may serve as a preliminary screening tool in postmortem settings, particularly when blood is available. Nevertheless, negative results do not exclude infection-especially with low viral loads or advanced decomposition-and should be confirmed by molecular testing.IMPORTANCEForensic personnel performing autopsies face significant occupational risks from exposure to blood-borne viruses, including human immunodeficiency virus, hepatitis B virus, and hepatitis C virus. Unlike clinical settings, forensic autopsies frequently involve bodies with unknown infection histories, making rapid infection screening essential for personnel safety. Lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA)-based point-of-care testing (POCT) for viral antigen and antibody detection offers a rapid, infrastructure-free screening option; however, its performance in postmortem specimens has not been systematically evaluated. This study suggests that rapid immunochromatographic POCT may serve as a preliminary screening tool in forensic autopsy settings, particularly when blood specimens are available. However, a negative result does not exclude infection, especially in cases with low viral load or advanced decomposition, and confirmatory molecular testing remains necessary. These findings provide practical guidance for forensic professionals on appropriate specimen selection and interpretation of LFIA results, ultimately supporting safer autopsy practices.

articles.title: Gentamicin treatment in a murine infection model suggests extracellular Orientia tsutsugamushi contributes to systemic dissemination.
articles.abstract: Orientia tsutsugamushi, an obligate intracellular bacterial pathogen, infects multiple cell types and disseminates via the blood and lymphatic system to affect various organs in human and other mammalian hosts. This bacterium replicates exclusively within living cells; however, it also exists transiently in a metabolically inactive extracellular form. While infected leukocytes are known contributors to the systemic spread of the bacterium, the role of the inactive extracellular form in dissemination has been unclear. In this study, we demonstrate that extracellular bacteria are present in the cell-free plasma fraction of infected human and murine blood. Furthermore, treatment with gentamicin, a membrane-impermeable antibiotic, significantly reduces systemic bacterial growth in a murine infection model. These findings suggest a potential role for the extracellular form of the bacterium in the spread of infection and raise the possibility of exploring the use of gentamicin to augment conventional antibiotic therapy during scrub typhus infection.

articles.title: A dual-action combination therapy targeting bacteria and host immunity against bacterial infections.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: The escalating crisis of antimicrobial resistance, coupled with a stagnant novel antibiotic discovery pipeline, underscores the urgent need for innovative strategies to combat bacterial infections. The development of antibiotic adjuvants that increase the efficacy of existing drugs represents a critical approach for addressing this challenge. We demonstrate that combining the conventional antibiotic azithromycin with the quorum-sensing inhibitor norharmane exerts potent antibacterial effects through both direct bactericidal activity and host immune activation. This combination not only disrupts bacterial structural integrity but also promotes macrophage polarization toward the M1-type phenotype and upregulates the expression of the important mediator, Muc5b, through activation of the IL-17 signaling pathway, ultimately enhancing mucosal immune defense and tissue repair functions. This regimen shows potent antibacterial efficacy against a range of pathogens in vitro and in vivo, along with a favorable safety profile. These findings highlight a promising combinatorial therapeutic strategy against the growing threat of antibiotic resistance.

IMPORTANCE: Antibiotic resistance has become one of the most urgent threats to global public health, yet the development of new antibiotics has slowed dramatically. In this study, we propose a promising alternative strategy that combines azithromycin with a small-molecule compound capable of inhibiting bacterial quorum sensing. This combination not only kills bacteria more effectively than the antibiotic alone but also harnesses the body's own immune system to fight infection. Its mechanisms of action include disrupting bacterial structure, promoting the polarization of macrophages toward the M1-type phenotype, and enhancing bactericidal capacity by activating the IL-17 signaling pathway to stimulate the production of the Muc5b protein. Our findings suggest that this dual-pronged approach could help revitalize existing antibiotics, offering a practical pathway to combat drug-resistant infections.

articles.title: Clinical Guidance for Disease-Modifying Immunotherapy in Children and Adolescents With New-Onset (Stage 3) Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: The 2026 U.S. approval of teplizumab, for children and adolescents aged 8-17 years with recently diagnosed stage 3 type 1 diabetes, changes the first weeks after diagnosis. Clinicians must treat hyperglycemia and teach lifelong care skills while considering whether to preserve residual β-cell function. Teplizumab is the current clinical exemplar, although the implementation challenges extend beyond one agent. This article addresses who should lead care, how to approach eligibility and timing, how to assess β-cell reserve and infection risk, how to sequence treatment with diabetic ketoacidosis recovery and early education, and how to monitor treatment safely. Teplizumab-specific recommendations are identified, with broader principles framed for adaptation across health systems.

articles.title: Distinct cell-type-specific gene expression programs associated with persistence versus clearance of arterivirus infection.
articles.abstract: This study aims to identify cellular markers correlated to persistent viral infection by a comprehensive comparison of blood immune transcriptomes and cell composition from acute and long-term stages of infection using a porcine arterivirus as the model. We applied single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to characterize blood mononuclear cells collected at 14 (acute) and 84 (long-term) days post-infection (DPI) with porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV). Pigs were grouped as persistently infected (PI, n = 5 at 14 DPI; n = 10 at 84 DPI) or virus-extinct (VE, n = 2) phenotypes based on detection of viral RNA in blood collected weekly and tissue samples collected at either 14 or 84 DPI. Monocytes emerged as the primary cellular drivers of infection outcome, with divergence driven mainly by cell-type-specific transcriptional programs rather than differences in immune cell compositions. At 14 DPI, genes expressed at higher levels in monocytes from VE pigs, which were enriched for activation of antiviral and interferon responses, and subsequently transitioned toward a homeostatic profile by 84 DPI. In contrast, monocytes from PI pigs were characterized by metabolic dysregulation at 14 DPI, followed by a chronic inflammation profile at 84 DPI. Temporal analysis revealed the "when and how" rather than the intensity of immune activation as a critical determinant of outcome, with PI pigs failing to mount early, effective antiviral responses. Collectively, these findings identified early monocyte transcriptional programs associated with PRRSV persistence, offering a potential application in the selection of biomarkers for disease surveillance and outbreak management in swine production.IMPORTANCEPersistent viral infection remains a critical challenge in human health, as well as livestock disease management, yet the viral-host immune mechanisms that determine whether infection resolves or persists remain poorly understood. This study used a swine arterivirus persistent infection model system along with advanced single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology to address a broad biological significance question-how circulating immune cell-type-specific transcriptional programs at early stages of infection determine long-term viral outcomes in the host. This work generated the first scRNA-seq data set for porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV) persistent infection and provides a framework for mining cell-type-resolved blood transcriptomes, which could assist in developing therapeutic strategies to manipulate host immune responses toward viral extinction pathways during infection.

articles.title: Functional Mitochondrial States in Heart Failure: Mechanistic Hypotheses and Therapeutic Testing.
articles.abstract:
SIGNIFICANCE: Mitochondrial function links myocardial energy demand to substrate metabolism, calcium handling, redox regulation, and tissue repair. These processes vary within heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, creating opportunities for mechanistic phenotyping across conventional clinical categories.

RECENT ADVANCES: Human myocardial metabolomics and proteomics reveal heterogeneous metabolic remodeling, while experimental cardiac studies connect organelle dynamics, quality control, contact sites, and immune-cell metabolism to functional adaptation and injury. Contrasting substrate and intervention findings emphasize the importance of direction, cellular origin, and physiological context.

CRITICAL ISSUES: Eight interacting modules organize the measurement space. Five illustrative configurations connect energetic and substrate abnormalities, calcium-transfer defects, and downstream injury or immune activity to research questions. They represent different biological levels and have not been jointly derived or validated in human cohorts. Ferroptotic execution and inflammation require separate measurements; their coupling in human HF remains a hypothesis.

FUTURE DIRECTIONS: We propose a worked research rule, a concrete exploratory biomarker panel, and a validation pathway incorporating tissue provenance, temporal behavior, and randomized treatment interactions. Adequate target engagement without cardiac or clinical benefit can challenge therapeutic relevance or patient selection. Clinical application requires reproducible human measurements that improve treatment decisions and outcomes; validated individual assignment is currently unavailable. Antioxid. Redox Signal. 00, 000-000.

articles.title: Acute intermittent carotid body stimulations induce long-term facilitation of respiratory-cardiovascular coupling in rats.
articles.abstract: Hypertension, the leading modifiable risk factor for global mortality, is driven in >50% of cases by neurogenic mechanisms linked to heightened sympathetic nerve activity (SNA). A hallmark of neurogenic hypertension is the exacerbation of respiratory-modulated SNA (RespSNA) and resulting blood pressure Traube-Hering (TH) waves, which emerges during the prehypertensive period and contributes to disease development. Carotid bodies (CBs), the peripheral chemoreceptors involved in the hypoxic response, are hyperactive in hypertensive patients and animal models. Their chronic intermittent stimulation, as seen in obstructive sleep apnoea, promotes hypertension characterised by exacerbated RespSNA and TH waves. Yet, their causal role in initiating these changes remains unclear. Here, we investigated whether acute intermittent CB stimulations could directly enhance RespSNA, TH waves and blood pressure from a physiological baseline, using the in situ working heart-brainstem preparation in rats. Four brief CB stimulations with sodium cyanide, mimicking acute intermittent hypoxia, were sufficient to induce a prolonged (>20 min) increase in both inspiratory and late expiratory RespSNA bursts, TH waves and perfusion pressure, with these effects being prevented by carotid sinus denervation. These changes were accompanied by a reconfiguration of central respiratory and cardiovascular control, including elevated respiratory heart rate variability and enhanced respiratory drive targeting upper airway and abdominal muscles. Our findings demonstrate that acute intermittent CB activation triggers sustained RespSNA and elevation of TH waves, supporting its potential role in development of hypertension. Our data also suggest that CBs play a key role in initiating this respiratory-cardiovascular plasticity and that central mechanisms might contribute to its long-term maintenance. KEY POINTS: Carotid body (CB) overactivity is implicated in sympathetic excitation and development of hypertension, but its direct role in initiating respiratory-cardiovascular dysfunction remains unresolved. We tested whether brief, repeated CB stimulations could trigger lasting changes in breathing and blood pressure control from a physiological baseline. In rats, only four stimulations induced a persistent increase in respiratory-modulated sympathetic activity, elevating blood pressure fluctuations (Traube-Hering waves) and mean blood pressure. These effects, prevented by carotid sinus denervation, were linked to enhanced respiratory-cardiovascular coupling and altered upper airway and abdominal motor control. Our findings reveal that short-term CB activation can induce long-term facilitation of respiratory-cardiovascular coupling, relevant to both physiological adaptations and hypertension pathogenesis.

articles.title: Comparing Length of Argatroban Use Among Patients Managed With Warfarin Versus Apixaban or Rivaroxaban for the Treatment of Suspected Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is limited available data directly comparing warfarin versus direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) for the treatment of acute or suspected heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT). In addition, there are no studies assessing the difference in duration of parenteral anticoagulation when switched to a DOAC versus warfarin in this setting.

OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study is to determine if transitioning to rivaroxaban or apixaban versus warfarin is associated with a shorter duration of argatroban administration.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective chart review included adults with suspected or acute HIT treated with argatroban and transitioned directly to warfarin, apixaban, or rivaroxaban. The primary outcome was duration of argatroban therapy. Secondary outcomes included hospital length of stay, bleeding events, new or recurrent thrombosis, and survival to discharge.

RESULTS: Seventeen patients in the apixaban and rivaroxaban group and 27 patients in the warfarin group were included. Patients transitioned to apixaban or rivaroxaban had a significantly shorter duration of argatroban infusion compared with the warfarin group (3.8 days vs 11.2 days, respectively [P < .001]). Although hospital length of stay was numerically shorter with DOACs, the difference was not statistically significant.

CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: In this study, transitioning to apixaban or rivaroxaban from argatroban for suspected or acute HIT was associated with a shorter duration of argatroban infusion. Application of this data may help reduce the duration of argatroban infusion for those with suspected or acute HIT being transitioned to oral anticoagulation.

articles.title: Experiences of Peer Navigators Implementing an Equity-Focused Intervention to Improve COVID-19 Testing and Vaccination Among Spanish-Speaking Latines in the U.S. South.
articles.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic disproportionately affected Latine communities in the United States, with Spanish-speaking Latine populations having higher rates of infection, hospitalization, and mortality. Our community-based participatory research partnership developed and in 2023 implemented and evaluated Nuestra Comunidad Saludable (Our Healthy Community), a Spanish-language intervention designed to increase COVID-19 testing and vaccination through community-based peer navigation and mHealth. After follow-up data collection, individual in-depth interviews were conducted in Spanish in 2024 with 10 community-based peer navigators, known as Navegantes, to understand their experiences implementing the intervention. Themes were identified through constant comparison. All Navegantes were native Spanish speakers, with a mean age of 45.7 (SD = 12.6, range: 21-66), and immigrated from seven Latin American countries. Fifteen themes emerged within four domains: (1) Navegante Engagement (e.g., Navegantes were highly committed to the intervention); (2) Training and Support (e.g., Activity Logs offered Navegantes "cues to action" and structure for tracking and reporting intervention activities); (3) Implementation Experiences (e.g., Navegantes were able to tailor and personalize COVID-19 messaging to meet the unique needs of each member of their social networks); and (4) Future Directions (e.g., an intervention like Nuestra Comunidad Saludable could be implemented to address other health issues within Latine communities). Interviews identified important learnings about Navegantes' experiences implementing the Nuestra Comunidad Saludable intervention. They also revealed valuable insights into the COVID-19 pandemic, barriers to accessing resources, and Latine community health needs and priorities that warrant future exploration and intervention.

articles.title: Regimens of vitamin D supplementation for women during pregnancy.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Vitamin D deficiency is common in pregnancy and has been associated with adverse health outcomes for the mother and infant, including pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, preterm birth, and low birthweight. The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends a vitamin D intake of 200 international units (IU) per day during pregnancy. Vitamin D supplementation is recommended for women with suspected vitamin D deficiency, but it is not universally recommended. The effects of different doses (regimens) of vitamin D during pregnancy have not been established. This is an update of a Cochrane review first published in 2019, which concluded that vitamin D supplementation (at any dose) may have little or no beneficial effects on maternal or neonatal outcomes.

OBJECTIVES: To assess the effects of different doses of vitamin D supplementation (alone or in combination with calcium or other micronutrients) during pregnancy: more than 600 IU/day versus up to 600 IU/day, and 4000 IU/day or more versus less than 4000 IU/day.

SEARCH METHODS: We searched the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), ClinicalTrials.gov, the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform, and relevant databases in April 2026.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised trials evaluating the effects of different vitamin D regimens during pregnancy on maternal and infant health outcomes. Trials of pregnant women with pre-existing conditions or multiple pregnancies were excluded.

OUTCOMES: The critical maternal outcomes were pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, and any adverse events. The critical infant outcomes were preterm birth and low birthweight.

RISK OF BIAS: We used the Cochrane RoB 1 tool to independently assess the risk of bias in included studies.

SYNTHESIS METHODS: Two review authors independently assessed study eligibility and extracted data from included studies. We conducted fixed-effect meta-analyses in RevMan where it was reasonable to assume that studies were estimating the same underlying treatment effect. If substantial heterogeneity was detected, we conducted random-effects meta-analyses, using the Mantel-Haenszel method for dichotomous outcomes and inverse-variance method for continuous outcomes. We used the GRADE approach to assess the certainty of the evidence.

INCLUDED STUDIES: This review update included 25 studies with 7008 pregnant women. The included studies were conducted in 14 countries between 2004 and 2024. We excluded 29 studies, identified 23 ongoing studies, and listed 21 studies as awaiting classification.

SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: The overall risk of bias of the 25 included studies was mixed. The certainty of the evidence was low for most critical outcomes due to serious risk of bias and imprecision in the results. Vitamin D at a dose of more than 600 IU/day versus up to 600 IU/day, alone or in combination with other micronutrients (19 studies, 5141 women) Vitamin D supplementation during pregnancy at doses of more than 600 IU/day, compared with up to 600 IU/day, may make little or no difference to the risk of pre-eclampsia (risk ratio (RR) 0.90, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.65 to 1.25; 8 studies, 2629 women; low-certainty evidence), gestational diabetes (RR 0.85, 95% CI 0.52 to 1.40; 6 studies, 2373 women; low-certainty evidence), preterm birth (RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.78 to 1.32; 7 studies, 3411 women; low-certainty evidence), or low birthweight (RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.71 to 1.14; 6 studies, 2090 women; low-certainty evidence). Vitamin D at a dose of 4000 IU/day or more versus less than 4000 IU/day, alone or in combination with other micronutrients (14 studies, 4954 women) Vitamin D supplementation during pregnancy at doses of 4000 IU/day or more, compared with less than 4000 IU/day, may make little or no difference to the risk of pre-eclampsia (RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.65 to 1.25; 5 studies, 2456 women; low-certainty evidence), gestational diabetes (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.55 to 1.35; 5 studies, 2420 women; low-certainty evidence), or preterm birth (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.79 to 1.19; 7 studies, 3409 women; low-certainty evidence), and probably makes little or no difference to the risk of low birthweight (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.76 to 1.21; 3 studies, 1637 women; moderate-certainty evidence). Adverse events in both comparisons Reporting of adverse events (e.g. hypercalcaemia, hypervitaminosis D) was heterogeneous across studies. Few adverse events were reported, and we observed no differences between groups (low-certainty to moderate-certainty evidence).

AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: Vitamin D supplementation during pregnancy at higher versus lower doses may make little or no difference to the risk of pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, preterm birth, or low birthweight. Future research should prioritise adequately powered trials with harmonised study designs that include more women from under-represented regions and focus on a consistently defined set of maternal and infant health outcomes. Additionally, trials should include longer follow-up to assess infant and child health outcomes beyond birth.

FUNDING: This Cochrane review had no dedicated funding.

REGISTRATION: The previous version of this review was published in 2019 (DOI 10.1002/14651858.CD013446). The original protocol for this review was registered with PROSPERO (https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42018103763).

articles.title: Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) for treating advanced epithelial ovarian cancer.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Ovarian cancer is the eighth most common cancer in women worldwide. Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) is the most common type; three-quarters of cases present with advanced disease (stage III or IV). Treatment consists of combinations of surgery and chemotherapy. Although initial responses to chemotherapy are good, most women with advanced disease relapse. Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) prevent cancer cells from repairing DNA damage, especially in those with breast cancer susceptibility gene (BRCA) mutations (BRCA-mutant), thereby offering a different mechanism of action for anticancer treatment compared to conventional chemotherapy. This is an update to a review first published in 2010 and previously updated in 2015 and 2022.

OBJECTIVES: To assess the benefits and harms of poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) versus placebo or other anti-cancer treatments for women with newly diagnosed or recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC).

SEARCH METHODS: We identified randomised controlled trials (RCTs) by searching the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials MEDLINE, and Embase up to 2 December 2025.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included trials randomising women with EOC to PARPi versus no treatment/placebo, PARPi versus conventional chemotherapy, or PARPi together with conventional chemotherapy versus conventional chemotherapy alone.

OUTCOMES: We extracted data on overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS), severe adverse events, and quality of life.

RISK OF BIAS: We used the Cochrane tool RoB 1 to assess the risk of bias in the included studies.

SYNTHESIS METHODS: We conducted meta-analyses using the random-effects model to calculate hazard ratios (HR), risk ratios (RR), mean differences (MD), and 95% confidence intervals (CI). We assessed the certainty of evidence using GRADE.

INCLUDED STUDIES: We identified 10 new studies. We included a total of 24 studies (8961 participants) in this 2026 version of the review: eight (4801 participants) with newly-diagnosed, advanced EOC and 16 (4160 participants) with recurrent EOC.

SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: The studies evaluated different PARPi against various comparators. Below we present four key comparisons. Most participants had BRCA mutations, either in their tumour (sBRCA-mutant) and/or germline (gBRCA-mutant), or homologous recombination deficiencies (HRD) in their tumours. Newly diagnosed EOC PARPi versus placebo maintenance after chemotherapy PARPi maintenance treatment after chemotherapy may increase overall survival (OS) (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.58 to 1.10; I² = 70%; 5 studies, 2852 participants; low-certainty evidence), but data are confounded by subsequent treatments, including increased use of PARPi in those in the placebo arms following relapse. PARPi maintenance results in a large improvement in progression-free survival (PFS), irrespective of PARPi type (HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.41 to 0.64; I² = 77%; 7 studies, 3618 participants; high-certainty evidence). PARPi maintenance may result in a slight reduction in quality of life (MD -1.06, 95% CI -3.52 to 1.40; I² = 92%; 3 studies, 1505 participants; low-certainty evidence), but this reduction may not be clinically meaningful. PARPi maintenance results in a large increase in the risk of any severe adverse event (grade 3 or higher; RR 2.66, 95% CI 1.66 to 4.27; I² = 91%; 7 studies, 3648 participants; high-certainty evidence). Recurrent, platinum-sensitive EOC PARPi versus placebo maintenance after chemotherapy PARPi maintenance probably increases OS slightly (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.75 to 1.04; I² = 26%; 5 studies, 1797 participants; moderate-certainty evidence) and results in a large increase in PFS compared to placebo (HR 0.34, 95% CI 0.28 to 0.40; I² = 24%; 6 studies, 2194 participants; high-certainty evidence). PARPi maintenance probably results in little to no difference in quality of life measured using the European Quality of Life 5-dimensions questionnaire Health Utility Index score (MD 0.02, 95% CI -0.01 to 0.05; 1 study, 339 participants; moderate-certainty evidence) or the TOI score (FACT-O questionnaire; MD -0.03, 95% CI -2.16 to 2.10; 1 study, 279 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). However, there is probably a substantially increased risk of any severe adverse event (grade 3 or higher) (RR 3.03, 95% CI 2.11 to 4.36; I² = 61%; 6 studies, 2181 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). PARPi monotherapy versus chemotherapy PARPi monotherapy probably results in little to no difference in OS compared with chemotherapy (HR 1.14, 95% CI 0.95 to 1.37; I² = 0%; 4 studies, 832 participants; moderate-certainty evidence); we are very uncertain about the effect on PFS (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.62 to 1.23; I² = 58%; 5 studies, 969 participants; very low-certainty evidence). PARPi monotherapy may result in little to no difference in quality of life compared with chemotherapy (FACT-O; MD 1.20, 95% CI -1.76 to 4.16; 1 study, 229 participants; low-certainty evidence; global EORTC QLQ-C30 score; MD 0.20, 95% CI -1.79 to 2.19; 1 study, 291 participants; very low-certainty evidence), but may increase the risk of any severe adverse event (grade 3 or higher) (RR 1.30, 95% CI 0.92 to 1.83; I² = 70%; 2 studies, 599 participants; low-certainty evidence). Recurrent, platinum-resistant EOC PARPi monotherapy versus chemotherapy Compared with chemotherapy, PARPi monotherapy reduces OS (HR 1.36, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.65; I² = 54%; 3 studies, 371 participants; high-certainty evidence) and may have little to no effect on PFS (HR 1.07, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.27; I² = 0%; 3 studies, 371 participants; low-certainty evidence). No quality of life data were available, but PARPi may result in little to no difference in the risk of any severe adverse event (grade 3 or higher) compared to chemotherapy (RR 1.16, 95% CI 0.79 to 1.70; 1 study, 100 participants; low-certainty evidence).

AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: PARPi maintenance treatment in women with first-line and platinum-sensitive recurrent disease improves progression-free survival (PFS) considerably, although it has less effect on overall survival (OS) and the OS results are less certain. PARPi maintenance increases severe adverse events, at times when women would otherwise not be on treatment, although quality of life may not be greatly impacted. The use of PARPi in other contexts did not lead to improved outcomes, especially in platinum-resistant recurrent disease. Adverse events and patient-reported outcomes were often poorly reported, which is a concern as this information is crucial for patient decision-making.

FUNDING: No dedicated funding REGISTRATION: Protocol (2009) DOI: 10.1002/14651858.CD007929 Review (2010) DOI:10.1002/14651858.CD007929.pub2 Update (2015) DOI: 10.1002/14651858.CD007929.pub3 Update (2022) DOI: 10.1002/14651858.CD007929.pub4.

articles.title: Analytical Validation of β-Hydroxybutyrate Quantification in Feline Serum with the BT3500 Analyzer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quantitative measurement of serum β-hydroxybutyrate (β-OHB) is essential for detecting and monitoring ketosis and ketoacidosis in diabetic cats, particularly in the era of sodium-glucose cotransporter two (SGLT2) inhibitors, where euglycemic ketoacidosis may occur. The BT3500 analyzer has not been analytically validated for β-OHB quantification in feline serum.

OBJECTIVES: Analytically validate the Randox Ranbut enzymatic β-OHB assay on feline serum using the BT3500 chemistry analyzer, including evaluation of sample stability under refrigerated and frozen storage conditions.

METHODS: Residual feline serum samples and pooled sera were used to assess intra-assay and inter-assay precision, spike-recovery accuracy across five concentration increments, linearity under serial dilution, and analytical sensitivity (LoB, LoD, LoQ). Short-term stability was evaluated at 4°C for 7 days and long-term stability at -20°C at predefined time points up to 360 days.

RESULTS: Intra-assay coefficient of variation (CV%) ranged from 1.68% to 14.48% and inter-assay CV% from 3.08% to 10.20%, with higher imprecision at low concentrations. Recoveries ranged from 110% to 122% (mean 114% ± 4%). Linearity was excellent (slope 1.012; R2 ≥ 0.9998). LoB, LoD, and LoQ were 0.044, 0.091, and 0.150 mmol/L, respectively. β-OHB was stable at 4°C up to 6 days and at -20°C up to 180 days, while decreases exceeding the acceptance limit were observed at 360 days.

CONCLUSIONS: The Randox β-OHB assay on the BT3500 demonstrated acceptable analytical performance in feline serum and is suitable for routine clinical use; frozen storage beyond 180 days may impact result accuracy.

articles.title: Association Between Hemoglobin Concentration and Metabolic Syndrome in a Japanese Population.
articles.abstract: Hemoglobin (Hb) concentration has been associated with metabolic abnormalities, but its relationship with metabolic syndrome (MetS) remains incompletely characterized. We examined these associations in a Japanese health checkup population. This cross-sectional study included 17,567 adults (10,175 men and 7392 women) examined between 2007 and 2024. MetS was defined according to the Japanese criteria. MetS analyses included 10,169 men and 7389 women after excluding nine participants with missing medication data. Sex-stratified regression, sensitivity, restricted cubic spline, and exploratory receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed. MetS was present in 1973 men (19.4%) and 310 women (4.2%). Higher Hb quartiles were generally accompanied by less favorable metabolic profiles. In adjusted linear models, Hb was positively associated with homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), triglycerides, fasting plasma glucose, waist circumference, and body mass index in both sexes; the largest standardized association was with HOMA-IR (men, β = 0.264; women, β = 0.150). In the principal confounder-adjusted logistic model, the odds ratios for MetS per 1 g/dL higher Hb were 1.441 in men and 1.668 in women. Associations remained significant in all sensitivity analyses. Restricted cubic splines indicated significant nonlinearity in both sexes. The areas under the curve for Hb alone were 0.579 in men and 0.676 in women. Higher Hb levels were associated with prevalent MetS and adverse metabolic parameters in both sexes. Hb may provide ancillary metabolic information but is insufficient for standalone MetS screening. The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.

articles.title: In-field crop disease surveillance: from phenotypes to molecules.
articles.abstract: Climate change and increasing ecological complexity intensify crop diseases, causing severe yield losses and threatening global food security. Timely and accurate in-field surveillance is essential for early warning and effective management of crop diseases. Advances in sensing technologies, flexible electronics, and synthetic biology are transforming crop disease surveillance from phenotypes to molecules. In this review, we first summarize major crop pathogens and pests as well as their associated disease biomarkers.
