We then examine field-deployable molecular detection approaches, including point-of-need assays, drone-equipped platforms, wearable devices, and sentinel plants, which enable in-field, real-time, broad-scale, and long-term surveillance of crop infection. We assess their technological readiness and applications in early crop infection detection, field pathogen survey, pesticide application instruction, and investigations of crop stress responses. Finally, we discuss the prospects of miniaturized, high-throughput analytical devices and the Internet of Things, as well as the challenges of translating in-field surveillance technologies into agricultural applications that will reshape crop disease management.

articles.title: Using Bayesian Evidence to Estimate District-Wise Tuberculosis Incidence Rates, Missed Cases and Fraction of Treated Cases in Bangladesh.
articles.journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
articles.abstract: Undetected and untreated tuberculosis (TB) remains a serious public health challenge, which increases mortality and transmission within households and communities. This study estimates district-wise TB incidence rates, missed cases, and the fraction of treated cases in Bangladesh using a Bayesian approach. By integrating data from national TB notifications, TB-related mortality, prevalence surveys, and auxiliary sources in Bangladesh, we developed an analytical model that estimates district-level TB burden from 2008 to 2017. We used a Bayesian modelling approach, treating incidence as a hidden event inferred from other components. We included predictor variables in the analysis at two points in the model-incidence and fraction notified. Here, we estimate the number of missing TB cases across districts, allowing us to identify areas with high proportions of untreated cases. Our findings revealed notable spatial and temporal variation, with some districts showing consistently higher predicted incidence rates and others exhibiting lower detection or treatment coverage. However, treatment coverage showed clear regional disparities, with poorer districts recording substantially lower fractions of treated cases compared to wealthier districts. These findings highlight the need for policymakers to prioritise equitable resource allocation to mitigate the burden of TB in Bangladesh.

articles.title: Validation to NANDA-I of the Nursing Diagnosis Ineffective Community Process Based on Community Assessment, Intervention and Empowerment Model (MAIEC): A Focus Group Consensus Study.
articles.abstract: PurposeThis study aimed to evaluate the content validity of the proposed nursing diagnosis 'Ineffective Community Process' for potential integration into the NANDA-I taxonomy, using the MAIEC model as its theoretical framework.ObjectiveTo evaluate expert consensus regarding the content validity of the diagnostic label, definition, diagnostic dimensions, defining characteristics, related factors, populations at risk, and taxonomic placement.MethodsA constructivist mixed-methods design was applied. A focus group of seven Brazilian nurses (n = 7) with expertise in Community or Public Health Nursing and experience with standardized nursing classifications participated in the diagnostic validation process and were asked to assess agreement with respect to the diagnostic framework. Consensus was assessed using the Tastle & Wierman Consensus Index (IC), and qualitative contributions were incorporated to refine semantic clarity and conceptual alignment.ResultsHigh consensus (IC = 0.8113) was achieved for the diagnostic label Ineffective Community Process, its definition, and the three diagnostic dimensions (Community Leadership, Community Participation, and Community Coping). All defining characteristics across dimensions reached high consensus (IC = 0.8113). Four related factors-low community participation, low literacy, vulnerable socioeconomic conditions, and absence of community leaders-also demonstrated high consensus, while "non-democratic community policies" showed moderate agreement. All indicators of the Portuguese version of the Community Empowerment Assessment Rating Scale (EAVeC) with scores < 3 were validated as criteria for populations at risk.ConclusionFindings provide evidence supporting the content validity of the proposed nursing diagnosis "Ineffective Community Process" and its diagnostic components. The results contribute to the development of community-focused nursing diagnoses and provide a foundation for future international consensus and clinical validation studies.Implications for nursing practice: The proposed nursing diagnosis "Ineffective Community Process" may strengthen nurses' ability to systematically assess and document community-level diagnoses using standardized language. Its potential integration into NANDA-I may enhance visibility of community nursing work, guide targeted interventions to increase community empowerment, and support epidemiological surveillance and outcome evaluation in public health and community settings.

articles.title: Consensus-Based Recommendations for the Management of Deep and Extremely Deep Carious Lesions and Vital Pulp Treatment in Permanent Teeth: A National Delphi Study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To develop consensus-based recommendations for general dental practitioners on deep and extremely deep carious lesions (CLs) and vital pulp treatment (VPT) in mature and immature permanent teeth.

METHODOLOGY: A national modified Delphi study was conducted with a purposively selected expert panel. Twenty-nine statements developed from international guidance were assessed through three anonymous online rounds using a 10-point agreement scale. Free-text justification for scores below 7 informed revision or merging. Positive consensus was predefined as a median score ≥ 7 with an interquartile range (IQR) ≤ 2; statements with greater dispersion could also be accepted when > 90% of experts scored them ≥ 7. Statements remaining uncertain after Round 3 were discussed at an online meeting and anonymously re-rated by the full panel.

RESULTS: Of 34 experts invited, 22 enrolled and completed every rating stage; no item-level data were missing. Five statements reached consensus in Round 1, 10 in Round 2, and six in Round 3. Four merging procedures reduced the 29 initial statements to 24 final statements. The remaining three reached consensus after the meeting and post-meeting rating; none was rejected. Final median scores ranged from 7 to 10, IQRs from 0 to 2, and proportions of scores ≥ 7 from 59.1% to 100%. The recommendations support comprehensive and graded pulpal assessment, selective carious tissue removal for deep CLs when pulp exposure should be avoided, management of extremely deep CLs according to root maturity, and consideration of VPT after pulp exposure and in selected cases of severe pulpitis. They also address asepsis, biomaterial selection, definitive restoration and follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: This national Delphi study produced 24 consensus-based recommendations and a clinical decision-support pathway for managing deep and extremely deep CLs in permanent teeth. The framework may complement existing evidence-based guidance; however, its acceptability, feasibility, transferability, and impact on clinical and patient-reported outcomes require external evaluation.

articles.title: Outcomes of extended septal myectomy for hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy in an Asian cohort.
articles.abstract: BackgroundHypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) is a complex cardiac disorder often treated with septal myectomy, the gold-standard surgical intervention that improves symptoms and survival. Long-term outcome data with paired echocardiographic follow-up from the Indian subcontinent remain limited.MethodsThis was a retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients undergoing extended septal myectomy for HOCM at a single tertiary referral centre between 2014 and 2024, analysed from a prospectively maintained clinical registry. Demographic, clinical, echocardiographic, operative and follow-up data were analysed. Survival was estimated by the Kaplan-Meier method.ResultsA total of 399 patients underwent extended septal myectomy (mean age 41.2 ± 16.5 years; 282/399, 70.7% male; 46/399, 11.5% aged under 18 years). Septal hypertrophy was mainly mid-septal (255/399, 63.9%), with basal (110/399, 27.6%) and apical (34/399, 8.5%) involvement. Myectomy was isolated in 247/399 patients (61.9%) and combined with a concomitant procedure in 152/399 (38.1%); 15/399 patients (3.8%) had undergone a prior cardiac intervention, including alcohol septal ablation in 1/399 (0.3%) and previous cardiac surgery in 9/399 (2.3%). In-hospital mortality was 6/399 (1.5%). Mean follow-up was 5.4 ± 3.1 years, and median follow-up was 5.9 years (interquartile range 2.5-6.7); vital status was complete for all patients. Survival was 98.1% (95% CI 96.7-99.5) at 5 years and 95.9% (95% CI 92.7-99.0) at 10 years.ConclusionsExtended septal myectomy provides excellent structural, functional, and survival outcomes, comparable to leading centres. It should remain the preferred surgical treatment for symptomatic HOCM.

articles.title: Invasive Monitoring in Acute Liver Failure.
articles.abstract: Acute liver failure (ALF) is a rapidly progressive condition marked by severe hepatic dysfunction, coagulopathy, and high short-term mortality driven largely by cerebral edema and circulatory collapse. Because neurological deterioration and hemodynamic instability can evolve unpredictably and interact dynamically, continuous physiologic monitoring is central to management. Invasive intracranial pressure (ICP) monitoring provides the most direct assessment of intracranial dynamics and supports cerebral perfusion pressure-oriented therapy; however, its routine use remains controversial due to limited outcome data and substantial hemorrhagic risk in the setting of severe coagulopathy. Current evidence, largely observational, favors a selective approach to ICP monitoring in patients with advanced encephalopathy or rapidly worsening neurological status, particularly in experienced centers. Noninvasive adjuncts, including optic nerve sheath ultrasound, transcranial Doppler, and electroencephalography, offer complementary information but do not replace direct ICP measurement. Hemodynamic monitoring, anchored by continuous arterial pressure measurement and central venous access, is indispensable for maintaining systemic perfusion and protecting cerebral blood flow. Advanced cardiac output monitoring and echocardiography further enable individualized fluid and vasopressor strategies. Overall, a multimodal, physiology-driven monitoring framework that integrates neurological and circulatory assessment is essential to optimize outcomes in ALF.

articles.title: White Matter and Normal-Appearing White Matter in Low-Disability Patients With Multiple Sclerosis: A Diffusion Tensor MRI Study.
articles.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) is sensitive to white matter (WM) microstructural alterations in multiple sclerosis (MS), but duration-defined "early MS" cohorts may be clinically heterogeneous.

PURPOSE: To investigate diffusion alterations in WM and normal-appearing white matter (NAWM) in low-disability MS versus healthy controls (HC).

STUDY TYPE: Retrospective cross-sectional case-control study.

POPULATION: 20 patients with MS (Expanded Disability Status Scale ≤ 3.5; ambulatory without assistance) and 20 age- and sex-matched HC.

SEQUENCE: 3.0 T; 3D T1-weighted and FLAIR sequences and a single-shot spin-echo echo-planar sequence with 60 diffusion directions (b = 1000 s/mm2) and nine b0 volumes.

ASSESSMENT: Tract-Based Spatial Statistics (TBSS) assessed fractional anisotropy (FA), axial diffusivity (AD), radial diffusivity (RD), and mean diffusivity (MD) in conventional WM and lesion-masked NAWM. DeepLesionBrain (volBrain) automatically segmented WM lesions; a neuroradiologist with 10 years of experience reviewed and corrected segmentations when necessary.

STATISTICAL TEST: FMRIB Software Library (FSL) randomize using 10,000 permutations, threshold-free cluster enhancement, and family-wise error correction (p < 0.01). Permutation Analysis of Linear Models (PALM) used two-sided inference and FWE correction across diffusion metrics and directions.

RESULTS: Standard TBSS showed lower FA in the right anterior corona radiata (ACR) and posterior thalamic radiation (PTR), and higher RD in the corpus callosum genu, in MS versus HC. NAWM-restricted TBSS showed lower FA in the corpus callosum genu, right PTR, and right tapetum, and higher RD in bilateral ACR, right posterior corona radiata, and an unclassified region. In randomized, AD and MD were nonsignificant (minimum corrected p = 0.0118 and 0.0103 in standard TBSS; p = 0.0103 and 0.0107 in NAWM, respectively). Under PALM across-metric correction, no metric remained significant: standard TBSS, FA p = 0.0861, AD p = 0.1273, RD p = 0.0271, MD p = 0.0177; NAWM, FA p = 0.0807, AD p = 0.1225, RD p = 0.0282, MD p = 0.0197.

CONCLUSION: Functionally defined low-disability MS shows focal WM and NAWM microstructural alterations, predominantly reflected by reduced FA and increased RD.

EVIDENCE LEVEL: 4.

TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 1.

articles.title: Comparative Efficacy of Sugammadex Versus Neostigmine for Neuromuscular Blockade Reversal in a Population of Neonatal Intensive Care Patients.
The impact of mild fundal pressure during vacuum extraction on labor and perinatal outcome.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Failed vacuum extraction (VE) is associated with increased adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Mild fundal pressure (MFP) is sometimes applied during VE to assist vaginal delivery and to potentially lower the VE failure rate. We aimed to determine whether the addition of MFP during VE reduces failure rates and its impact on perinatal outcomes.

METHODS: This was a retrospective study at a single tertiary medical center (January 2022 to March 2024). All term singleton VEs were included and stratified by whether or not MFP was applied. MFP was added at the physician's discretion when initial traction was insufficient to achieve adequate fetal descent. The primary outcome was the rate of failed VE and subsequent cesarean delivery. Secondary outcomes included composite maternal adverse events (obstetric anal sphincter injury, shoulder dystocia, postpartum hemorrhage, or hemoglobin drop ≥3 g/dL) and composite neonatal adverse events (neonatal intensive care unit admission, Apgar score <7 at 5 min, umbilical artery pH <7.1, or birth trauma).

RESULTS: Of 2015 VEs, 555 (27.5%) included MFP. Extraction failed in 0.2% with MFP versus 2.2% without (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.08; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.01-0.61, P = 0.014). Composite maternal outcomes were similar between the groups (19.5% vs. 18.3%; aOR 1.02; 95% CI 0.79-1.32). No difference in composite neonatal outcome was observed (15.7% vs. 12.9%; aOR 1.28; 95% CI 0.97-1.69).

CONCLUSION: The application of MFP during VE was associated with reduced failure of operative vaginal delivery without significantly increased maternal or neonatal morbidity.

articles.title: Case Volumes and Outcomes of Early-Career Operators Performing TAVR in the United States.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Operator experience is a key determinant of outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, whether early-career operators achieve comparable results to more experienced peers is unknown. Herein, we evaluate case volumes, patient risk profiles, and 30-day outcomes of early-career versus non-early-career operators performing TAVR in the United States.

METHODS: Using the Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapies Registry, we identified isolated TAVR procedures from October 2011 through March 2024. Early-career status was defined as ≤5 years in independent practice (based on board certification or first TAVR date); non-early-career status was >5 years. Multivariable hierarchical models adjusted for patient-, procedural-, operator-, and site-level factors, including annualized institutional TAVR volume, while accounting for clustering of procedures within operators and operators within sites. Primary outcomes were 30-day mortality and a composite of death, stroke, major bleeding, stage III acute kidney injury, or moderate-to-severe paravalvular leak.

RESULTS: A total of 634 723 TAVR procedures were performed by 3126 operators across 847 sites, including 90 376 (14.2%) by early-career operators. Median annualized lifetime volume was lower for early-career operators (13 [interquartile range, 5-31] versus 19 [interquartile range, 7-42] cases per year; P<0.001). After adjustment, 30-day mortality was similar between early-career and non-early-career operators (2.38% versus 2.44%; risk ratio, 0.97 [95% CI, 0.92-1.01]; P=0.293), whereas the composite end point was lower among early-career operators (11.19% versus 11.77%; risk ratio, 0.95 [95% CI, 0.93-0.98]; P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: In a national TAVR registry, early-career operators performed fewer cases but achieved similar 30-day mortality and a modestly lower adjusted composite event rate relative to more experienced peers. These findings suggest that within the structured, team-based environment of contemporary TAVR programs, early-career status alone is not associated with inferior procedural outcomes and should not be viewed as a barrier to independent practice.

articles.title: Transcatheter Mitral Cerclage Ventriculoplasty: 5-Year Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter mitral cerclage ventriculoplasty places a circumferential tensioning loop around the base of the left ventricle to reduce mitral annular dimensions and reshape ventricular geometry in patients with functional mitral regurgitation and heart failure. Early experience demonstrated reductions in mitral regurgitation and improvements in heart failure symptoms.

METHODS: The National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute Division of Intramural Research Transcatheter Mitral Cerclage Ventriculoplasty Early Feasibility Study was an investigator-initiated, prospective, multicenter study. Between 1 and 5 years, vital status, serious adverse events, routine clinical documentation, and site-reported transthoracic echocardiography findings were collected.

RESULTS: Nineteen procedures were attempted in 18 participants (63% heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, 37% heart failure with preserved ejection fraction). Median age was 73 years, and 63% were female. Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year survival was 57%. One participant underwent left ventricular assist device implantation after 2 years, and 1 participant underwent mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair after 3 years; none underwent heart transplantation. The study was suspended after complete heart block developed in 6 participants, including 4 requiring new cardiac implantable electronic devices. Among participants with available follow-up echocardiography, site-reported imaging demonstrated mitral regurgitation reduction and improved left ventricular ejection fraction through 5 years. Symptomatic improvement was most apparent during the first year and attenuated thereafter.

CONCLUSIONS: Cerclage ventriculoplasty was associated with mitral regurgitation reduction and improved ventricular function among participants with available long-term follow-up. Symptomatic benefit was greatest during the first year and diminished thereafter, suggesting that favorable remodeling may not fully offset progression of the underlying cardiomyopathy.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT03929913.

articles.title: Motion-Informed Neural Network Towards Diastolic Mechanics in Takotsubo Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The pathophysiology of Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) remains perplexing. We developed a motion-informed neural network (MiNN-Echo) using echocardiograms to elucidate the diastolic mechanics of TTS.

METHODS: We trained and validated MiNN-Echo, a deep convolutional neural network (2D+t) echocardiographic prediction model using multi-vendor echocardiograms from 1142 patients (596 TTS and 546 anterior myocardial infarction) in a multi-institutional cohort. A total of 68 expert echocardiographic readers performed human interpretation. The network's dual-branch architecture independently learns spatial and temporal features, using 2-dimensional image frames for spatial representation and segmentation, and optical flow with sinusoidal phase encoding for temporal dynamics. The MiNN-Echo model integrates static cardiac anatomic changes with motion details from 2-dimensional echocardiographic videos to produce interpretable disease predictions.

RESULTS: The MiNN-Echo model achieved an area under the curve of 0.77, compared with 0.69 among human readers in differentiating TTS from acute myocardial infarction. Myocardial motion features during diastole contributed more (≈71%) to the differential diagnosis than those during systole. Compared with patients with acute myocardial infarction, TTS patients showed increased isovolumic relaxation time (112.5 [interquartile range (IQR), 68.75-165.94] ms versus 87.5 [IQR, 54.17-140] ms, P<0.001; 28% versus 19% of diastolic time, P<0.001), decreased passive ventricular filling (before atrial contraction) time (176.04 [IQR, 114.2-248.12] ms versus 258.62 [IQR, 199.89-331.9] ms, P<0.001; 44% versus 54% of diastolic time, P<0.001), and a different mitral-annulus motion trajectory: lower pixel-wise myocardial displacement in the isovolumic relaxation (0.35 [IQR, 0.26-0.47] versus 0.38 [IQR, 0.28-0.51]; P=0.006), passive (0.45 [IQR, 0.33-0.58] versus 0.50 [IQR, 0.38-0.68]; P<0.001), and active ventricular filling (0.43 [IQR, 0.32-0.56] versus 0.48 [IQR, 0.35-0.63]; P=0.001) phases, and altered rotation angles (away from the horizontal A-V plane) in the passive ventricular filling phase (-70.19 [IQR, -89.62 to -41.33] versus -60.34 [IQR, -87.07 to -30.84]; P=0.020).

CONCLUSIONS: MiNN-Echo in echocardiograms elucidates unique myocardial relaxation kinematics to characterize TTS-associated diastolic mechanics.

articles.title: Glycyrrhetinic acid alleviates LPS-induced acute lung injury and is associated with modulation of Keap1-Nrf2 signaling and ferroptosis.
articles.abstract: Glycyrrhetinic acid, a substance extracted from licorice, has several pharmacological activities, such as anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects and antiviral properties. Acute lung injury (ALI) represents a significant contributor to morbidity and mortality associated with respiratory disorders, marked by the presence of lung edema, interstitial neutrophilic infiltration, and dysfunction of intravascular and endothelial barriers, ultimately leading to respiratory failure. The present study aimed to investigate the effects of glycyrrhetinic acid on LPS-induced ALI. Glycyrrhetinic acid pretreatment significantly attenuated LPS-induced pulmonary edema, inflammatory cell infiltration, and alveolar wall thickening, while reducing proinflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β) in BALF and serum. The transcriptomics analysis predicted that the ferroptosis pathways might be involved in the underlying mechanism of glycyrrhetinic acid against ALI, with validation experiments demonstrating glycyrrhetinic acid-mediated restoration of ferroptosis markers. Mechanistically, glycyrrhetinic acid suppressed Keap1 expression and activated Nrf2, enhancing antioxidant responses and inhibiting lipid peroxidation. These findings suggest that glycyrrhetinic acid may modulate inflammation and ferroptosis, with Keap1-Nrf2 signaling potentially contributing to its protective effects. The study suggests that targeting ferroptosis may represent a potential strategy for ALI management, with glycyrrhetinic acid emerging as a promising pharmacological candidate.

articles.title: Disease perception, quality of life and mental health among Chinese patients with transplant-eligible newly diagnosed multiple myeloma following treatment: a cross-sectional survey study.
articles.abstract: Aim: This study evaluated disease perception, health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and mental health among Chinese patients with transplant-eligible newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (NDMM) after treatment in Chinese tertiary hospital settings. Materials & methods: This cross-sectional survey enrolled patients after the treatments for NDMM in two Chinese tertiary hospitals between January and June 2025. This survey study collected disease perception, HRQoL assessment using the EuroQol 5-Dimension 5-Level (EQ-5D-5L) instrument and psychological assessment using the 9-item Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) for depression and the 7-item Generalized Anxiety Disorder scale (GAD-7) for anxiety. Patients were categorized according to treatment pathway (autologous stem cell transplantation [ASCT] vs non-ASCT) for exploratory descriptive comparisons. Multivariable regression analyses were used to explore any factors associated with HRQoL and psychological outcomes. Results: The cohort had a mean age of 57.2 years; 39.6% were male. Pathological fractures (54.7%) and hypertension (35.8%) were common in these surveyed patients. Knowledge gaps existed regarding the negative impact of MM on renal impairment and anemia. The mean EQ-5D utility score was 0.849; anemia was negatively associated with EQ-5D utility score (coefficient, -0.253; 95% CI: -0.444 to -0.062; p = 0.011). Regarding psychological outcomes, the mean GAD-7 anxiety score and PHQ-9 depression score were 4.7 and 3.1, respectively. Progressive disease was significantly associated with higher anxiety (GAD-7: coefficient, 7.963; 95% CI: 3.804 to 12.122; p < 0.001) and depression (PHQ-9: coefficient, 3.358; 95% CI: 1.091 to 5.624; p = 0.005). Conclusion: HRQoL was generally preserved in treated Chinese patients with NDMM, but anemia was linked to poorer HRQoL and progressive disease to greater anxiety and depression, supporting targeted education and psychosocial care.

articles.title: XR serious games for phantom limb pain, neurofunctional recovery, and prosthetic adoption: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To synthesize evidence on Extended Reality (XR) serious games for Phantom Limb Pain (PLP), neurofunctional recovery, embodiment, and adoption following amputation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore were searched up to January 2026. Eligible studies included adults with limb amputation who received XR serious game interventions and reported rehabilitation or user-experience outcomes. Quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Evidence certainty was rated using GRADE across 5 outcome domains.

RESULTS: 24 studies met the inclusion criteria. XR interventions showed consistent PLP reduction, with AR-based phantom motor execution systems reporting the largest effect sizes (d = 0.9-1.3) and preliminary evidence of reversal of cortical reorganization. VR exergames improved gait and balance in 2 RCTs. Immersive VR and EMG systems indicated improved object manipulation, performance time, and motor control. Neurofunctional and embodiment outcomes provided mechanistically plausible evidence regarding cortical activity, embodiment, and physiological adaptation.

CONCLUSIONS: XR serious games show preliminary benefit in reducing phantom limb pain, improving functional mobility, supporting prosthesis control, and enhancing embodiment after amputation. Evidence linking XR-mediated sensorimotor feedback to cortical adaptation remains exploratory but is supported by neurofunctional findings. Usability and engagement outcomes were positive, although real-world implementation and scalability remain under-researched.

articles.title: Wolbachia facilitates the reproduction of a parthenogenetic ladybird.
articles.abstract: Wolbachia is a bacterial endosymbiont that is primarily transmitted from mother to offspring. As a result of the increased transmission by females, strains that favour the production of female offspring, such as by inducing parthenogenesis, are selected for. Here, we assess the role of Wolbachia in recently discovered parthenogenetic populations of the ladybird Nephus voeltzkowi by treating females with an antibiotic. Our results demonstrate that the treatment decreases Wolbachia load, subsequently reducing egg production and development among parthenogenetic females, while having no effect on sexual females. Wolbachia load and reproduction then rebound when the treatment is removed. This suggests that the Wolbachia infection is necessary for successful reproduction in the parthenogenetic females, and it may play a two-part role by facilitating egg laying and late embryo development. The co-occurrence of Wolbachia infection and parthenogenesis in N. voeltzkowi, as well as Wolbachia's effect on host reproduction, makes this a likely candidate for Wolbachia-induced parthenogenesis outside of haplo-diploids. Understanding how Wolbachia impacts diverse insect reproductive systems can shed light on the extent to which these bacteria can affect hosts for their own gain.

articles.title: Predictors of Preterm Delivery in the COVID-19 Era: A Retrospective Cohort Study of a Large, Integrated HealthSystem.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Preterm delivery is the leading cause of perinatal mortality and long-term neonatal morbidity in the United States, and rates are rising. Research has shown that COVID-19 infection may increase the possibility of preterm delivery. However, these studies disproportionately focus on third trimester and iatrogenic cases, often overlooking risk across the entire pregnancy or without adjusting for prior preterm delivery and sociodemographic factors. To address these gaps, the authors investigated the association between COVID-19 at any point in pregnancy and preterm delivery while exploring other predictors of preterm delivery.

METHODS: The authors conducted a retrospective cohort study of members pregnant between March 2020 and March 2021, comparing odds of preterm delivery for those with and without COVID-19. Using logistic regression and χ2 tests, the authors explored associations between preterm delivery and other sociodemographic and clinical characteristics. Data were abstracted from electronic medical records.

RESULTS: Of 14,250 participants, 994 (7%) experienced COVID-19 infection during pregnancy. Overall, 1313 (9%) had preterm delivery. In univariate logistic regression analyses, those with COVID-19 were more likely to be < 35 years old, Hispanic or Black, non-English-speaking, obese, and multiparous. COVID-19 infection during pregnancy was associated with increased odds of preterm delivery in the authors' unadjusted model but not in the multivariable adjusted model. Being ≥ 35 years old, Hispanic, Black, nulliparous, hypertensive, immunocompromised, or having a prior preterm delivery or gestational or chronic diabetes were significantly associated with higher odds of preterm delivery in the authors' multivariable model.

CONCLUSION: COVID-19 infection throughout pregnancy was not associated with increased odds of preterm delivery. Racial disparities and other key covariates like history of preterm delivery may confound the reported increase in preterm delivery.

articles.title: MobiDB in 2027: machine-actionable access to intrinsic protein disorder knowledge.
articles.abstract: MobiDB (https://mobidb.org) integrates structural and functional annotations for intrinsically disordered proteins and regions across UniProtKB. The 2027 release strengthens semantic consistency, programmatic access, and reproducible reuse. A refined controlled vocabulary groups features in a hierarchical way and distinguishes evidence classes and types annotation sources as providers, methods, or aggregation rules. A new versioned REST API, along with a developed MCP server, enables scripts, workflows, and tool-using artificial intelligence systems to retrieve and combine evidence-bearing records through documented operations. The redesigned website applies the same vocabulary to protein entries, documentation, and cross-proteome statistics. Additional developments include standardized Nextflow production workflows, updated RING Protein Data Bank interaction processing, integration of Motif Map of the Proteome and Linear Motif mediated Protein-Protein Interaction Database annotations, and a release-aware catalogue of static datasets for large-scale analysis. Following the recent increase in reference proteomes in UniProtKB, MobiDB now provides a more representative estimate of long-disorder with a median residue coverage of 12.3% in eukaryotes, 1.9% in archaea, 1.7% in bacteria, and 3.4% in viruses; and protein prevalence of 48.7%, 11.9%, 11.2%, and 25.0%, respectively. Together, these developments make disorder knowledge easier to discover, relate to function, and reuse with explicit provenance.

articles.title: Recognition and management of delirium superimposed on dementia in older adults.
articles.abstract: Delirium superimposed on dementia (DSD) - where an individual with pre-existing dementia develops delirium - poses significant diagnostic challenges due to the symptom overlap between delirium and dementia. It is essential, however, that nurses and other healthcare professionals can accurately identify DSD, as delirium is a medical emergency and misattributing symptoms of delirium to dementia can result in extended hospital stay and increased morbidity and mortality. It is often a family member's or carer's report of an acute alteration in the person's cognition, function or behaviour that alerts healthcare professionals to potential delirium in a person with dementia. This article provides an overview of dementia, delirium and DSD, discusses the important role of family carers in identifying early signs of delirium in a person with dementia, and explores the use of evidence-based delirium screening tools. The article outlines implications for nursing practice and includes a composite case study illustrating some of the issues discussed.

articles.title: [Research advances on the role of extracellular matrix alterations in the occurrence and progression of diabetic retinopathy].
articles.journal: [Zhonghua yan ke za zhi] Chinese journal of ophthalmology
articles.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is the most common microvascular complication of diabetes mellitus and seriously endangers patients' visual function. As a core structural component of the retinal microenvironment, the extracellular matrix (ECM) participates in the occurrence and progression of DR via regulating cell proliferation, migration, apoptosis and other mechanisms. However, the systematic understanding of its mechanisms in DR remains quite limited. This review systematically summarizes the structural and functional characteristics, pathological changes, signaling regulatory pathways and therapeutic advances of ECM in DR. Combined with the latest progress in artificial intelligence and multi-omics technologies, it prospects the application prospects of ECM-targeted intervention strategies. This article aims to deepen the understanding of ECM function in DR and provide new theoretical basis and intervention targets for the clinical prevention and precision treatment of DR.

articles.title: [Modifiable risk factors and diabetic retinopathy: a Mendelian randomization analysis].
articles.journal: [Zhonghua yan ke za zhi] Chinese journal of ophthalmology
articles.abstract: Objective: To investigate the causal relationships of body mass index (BMI), smoking, alcohol and coffee consumption, sleep, physical activity, and educational attainment with diabetic retinopathy (DR) and its subtypes. Methods: We conducted a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) study. Genetic instruments were selected from seven large-scale European-descent genome-wide association studies. Summary-level statistics for three DR phenotypes were obtained from the FinnGen consortium. The inverse-variance weighted method was used as the main MR analysis, with weighted median, MR-Egger regression, maximum likelihood, and MR-PRESSO models used for sensitivity analyses to assess the robustness of the findings. The MR study was conducted from September to November 2024. Results: A total of 14 584 patients with DR and 202 082 control participants were included. For analyses of DR subtypes, 2 026 patients with non-proliferative DR and 204 208 control participants, as well as 8 681 patients with proliferative DR and 204 208 control participants, were included. Higher genetically predicted BMI was intensively and independently associated with increased risk of DR and subtypes. The odds ratio (OR) was 1.26 [95% confidence interval (CI): 1.16-1.37, P<0.001] of overall DR, 1.68 (95%CI, 1.38-2.06, P<0.001) of non-proliferative DR, and 1.41 (95%CI, 1.27-1.56, P<0.001) of proliferative DR for 1-SD increase in BMI. Increased coffee consumption was associated with a higher risk of overall DR (OR=1.23; 95%CI, 1.04-1.45, P=0.015), non-proliferative DR (OR=1.72; 95%CI, 1.17-2.53, P=0.006), and proliferative DR (OR=1.33; 95%CI, 1.08-1.63, P=0.007). In addition, genetically predicted educational attainment was inversely associated with non-proliferative DR (OR=0.70; 95%CI, 0.55-0.90, P=0.005). Insufficient evidence was found to support the causal association of smoking, alcohol consumption, sleep, and physical activity with DR (all P>0.05). Conclusions: Based on MR analysis of European populations, higher BMI, increased coffee intake, and lower educational attainment are risk factors for DR.

articles.title: [Modified surgical techniques for macular holes: evolution and introspection].
articles.journal: [Zhonghua yan ke za zhi] Chinese journal of ophthalmology
articles.abstract: Macular hole surgery has evolved from the initial simple pars plana vitrectomy to procedures in which peeling of the internal limiting membrane (ILM) over the macular surface constitutes the core technique. In recent years, an increasing number of modified techniques have continued to emerge, including ILM flap inversion, ILM flap insertion, and transplantation of various biological materials. However, issues such as the unclear surgical indications of these modified techniques have prompted the academic community to reflect on the diversification of macular hole surgical approaches. Based on a systematic review of the rationale behind the evolution of macular hole surgical techniques, this article offers a critical appraisal of the advantages and disadvantages of each technique and advocates a precise surgical strategy guided by evidence-based medicine. The aim is to uphold the fundamental principles of minimally invasive surgery in clinical practice and to achieve optimal visual function improvement with minimal surgical trauma.

articles.title: The lymphatic system: the new target for effective decongestion in decompensated heart failure?
Primary Synovial Sarcoma of the Thyroid Gland Presenting With Early Pulmonary Metastasis: Diagnostic Pathway, SS18 Gene Fusion Confirmation, and Clinical Course.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Primary synovial sarcoma of the thyroid gland (PSST) is an exceptionally rare and aggressive neoplasm. Twenty-one cases have been reported in the literature to date, making this the 22nd reported occurrence. This report presents the case of a 47-year-old woman with PSST confirmed by SS18 gene fusion on fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), who subsequently developed pulmonary metastasis and doxorubicin-induced congestive heart failure, illustrating the aggressive clinical course of this entity. CASE REPORT We report the case of a 47-year-old woman presenting with dysphagia and a left-sided neck mass. Initial FNA was non-diagnostic; repeat FNA raised concern for a spindle cell neoplasm. Left hemithyroidectomy was performed with negative margins, and SS18 gene fusion was confirmed by FISH, establishing the diagnosis of PSST. Following multidisciplinary review, adjuvant chemotherapy was deferred and neck radiation was administered. Pulmonary metastasis was discovered 6 months postoperatively. The patient received eribulin mesylate and subsequent palliative doxorubicin, and her case was complicated by doxorubicin-induced congestive heart failure. She subsequently developed progressive systemic metastatic disease, including brain and bone involvement, and died of the disease 65 months after initial presentation. CONCLUSIONS This case demonstrates that SS18 FISH confirmation is essential when FNA is non-diagnostic for a thyroid spindle cell mass. Despite negative margins and adjuvant radiation, early pulmonary metastasis and ultimately fatal systemic metastatic disease to the brain and bone occurred, underscoring the aggressive clinical course of PSST. Doxorubicin-induced cardiac toxicity further illustrates the systemic therapy burden. BCL-2-directed strategies remain investigational. Complete surgical resection with negative margins is the cornerstone of management.

articles.title: Optimizing AI-Derived CAC Volume Thresholds on Non-Gated Chest CT for Detection of Actionable Coronary Artery Calcium: A Validation Against Agatston Scoring and Radiologist Reporting.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) visually estimated on non-electrocardiogram (ECG)-gated chest CTs is reported inconsistently, limiting identification of high-risk individuals. Although automated AI-derived CAC scoring offers the potential to standardize reporting and improve reliability, this method warrants rigorous validation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Three hundred thirty-two patients (59% female, median age 62) who underwent a non-gated chest CT within 1-year of a dedicated cardiac CT with Agatston's CAC score (CACscore) were identified between 2016 and 2022. AI-Rad Companion (Siemens) was used to compute CAC volume (AI-CACvol). AI-CACvol performance was compared with radiologists' qualitative CAC reports (H-CACqual) using optimized thresholds for identifying actionable CAC. Model performance was further validated in a postimplementation population.

RESULTS: Median AI-CACvol was 20.3 mm³ (IQR 0-188.65), strongly correlated with CACscore (Spearman ρ=0.91, 95% CI: 0.88-0.94); median 31.55 Agatston Units (AU), IQR: 0 to 250). Agreement with CACscore was higher for AI-CACvol versus H-CACqual (weighted kappa 0.88, 95% CI: 0.84, 0.91; vs. 0.85, 95% CI: 0.82, 0.88; P=0.022). At a cutoff of 70 mm³, AI-CACvol demonstrated superior sensitivity compared with H-CACqual for detecting CAC≥100 AU, with greater sensitivity (95% vs. 75%) and comparable specificity (92% vs. 94%). In a validation cohort of 39 patients (64% female, median age 67 y), median CACscore was 43 AU (IQR 0-215) and median AI-CACvol 29.7 mm³ (IQR: 0 to 219.4). The same 70 mm³ cutoff achieved 100% sensitivity and 88% specificity for CAC≥100 AU (n=13).

CONCLUSION: AI-derived CAC volume from non-gated chest CTs correlates strongly with reference CAC scores, showing high sensitivity at actionable thresholds. This supports potential opportunistic screening, though impact on outcomes requires study.

articles.title: Can Patients Self-Acquire Diagnostic Quality Electrocardiograms for Acute Coronary Syndrome?: A Feasibility Study of Remote Cardiac Monitoring and Symptom Reporting.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS), one of the leading causes of death in the United States, requires rapid evaluation, diagnosis, and therapy initiation to reduce morbidity and mortality. Delayed care-seeking remains the primary reason that patients with ACS fail to receive timely treatment. Remote cardiac monitoring may supplement individuals' symptom appraisal and reduce delays. However, ACS patients' ability to remotely self-acquire an electrocardiogram (ECG) is unknown.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether hospitalized patients with suspected ACS can acquire a derived 12-lead (L) ECG using a KardiaMobile 6L remote cardiac monitoring device.

METHODS: Participants were hospitalized patients aged >21 years at high risk for ischemic events (ACS diagnosis with a History, ECG, Age, Risk factors, and Troponin score >3, ie, moderate to high risk for cardiac event) who owned an iPhone. Research assistants trained participants to use mobile applications to (1) acquire an ECG at least once daily during their hospitalization and (2) document symptoms using the ACS Symptom Checklist. A cardiologist blinded to clinical data compared ischemic markers (eg, ST-elevation, ST-depression, and T-wave inversion) on KardiaMobile 6L derived 12L ECGs with hospital-based 12L ECGs.

RESULTS: We enrolled 30 participants (mean age 64.2 ± 11.2 years, 30.0% female, 73.3% White). All participants acquired at least 1 remote cardiac device ECG. A cardiologist classified 88.9% as clean and interpretable; the remainder were noisy but interpretable. Ischemic markers were present on both patient-acquired and hospital-based ECGs. All participants submitted at least 1 Symptom Checklist.

CONCLUSIONS: Hospitalized patients with suspected ACS can self-acquire a 6L ECG and self-report symptoms, and derived 12L ECGs can detect signs of ischemia (eg, ST-elevation). Future studies should examine ECG acquisition and transmission from home and remote evaluation for early ischemia detection and response.

articles.title: Predicting and Mitigating Maternal Risk.
articles.abstract: Rates of maternal cardiac events are increasing, highlighting the importance of identifying people with higher risks of pregnancy. Pregnancy imposes hemodynamic and hormonal changes, which can lead to heart failure, arrhythmias, and other cardiac complications. This review provides an overview of assessing cardiac risks of pregnancy in people with pre-existing acquired and congenital heart disease.

articles.title: Targeting Systemic Immune Dysregulation in Cardiovascular Disease: From Mechanisms to Precision Therapeutic Strategies.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality despite advances in conventional pharmacological therapy. Persistent inflammation and immune dysregulation contribute to residual cardiovascular risk, disease heterogeneity, and variable therapeutic responses. Increasing evidence links cardiovascular injury to systemic immune and immunometabolic disturbances arising from the kidney, liver, brain, hematopoietic and lymphoid organs, gut, and adipose tissue. This review summarizes how systemic immune disturbances contribute to cardiovascular remodeling through altered immune-cell activation, impaired inflammatory resolution, metabolic stress, and pathological immune memory. We discuss the contributions of kidney-, liver-, neuroimmune-, gut-adipose-, and hematopoietic-associated abnormalities to major cardiovascular phenotypes, including heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, cardiorenal syndrome, metabolic cardiomyopathy, and aging-associated cardiovascular disease. These systemic abnormalities converge on common cardiovascular effector mechanisms, including endothelial dysfunction, inflammatory-cell recruitment, macrophage activation, fibroblast remodeling, extracellular matrix deposition, and cardiomyocyte dysfunction. We further examine emerging pharmacological strategies targeting systemic immune dysregulation, including cytokine inhibition, inflammasome modulation, metabolic interventions, and therapies targeting maladaptive immune memory. Although several approaches have demonstrated clinical benefit, effective translation requires identification of biologically defined patient subgroups, reliable biomarkers, and appropriate assessment of therapeutic response and safety. Integrating immune profiling with cardiovascular pharmacotherapy may facilitate a transition from nonspecific anti-inflammatory approaches toward precision modulation of pathological immune networks.

articles.title: GLP-1/GLP-1R signalling in infectious diseases: basic biology, immunometabolic mechanisms, and therapeutic translation.
articles.abstract: Infectious diseases remain a major global health burden, and metabolic disorders such as diabetes and obesity further increase susceptibility to infection and adverse outcomes. These intersecting metabolic and infectious risks have prompted growing interest in the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)/GLP-1 receptor (GLP-1R) axis beyond its established role in glycaemic regulation. GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) modulate systemic metabolism, neuroimmune signalling, vascular and epithelial homeostasis, and inflammatory responses. Whether their infection-related effects arise from direct immune-cell GLP-1R signalling, improved pathogen control, or indirect host protection remains unresolved. This narrative review critically evaluates GLP-1/GLP-1R signalling in infection. It distinguishes live-pathogen models from endotoxin and sterile-injury models, host resistance from host tolerance, and direct receptor-dependent actions from indirect systemic effects. It also differentiates chronic pre-infection exposure from treatment initiated after infection onset. Across selected preclinical models, GLP-1RAs more consistently attenuate inflammation and tissue injury while preserving organ function, whereas their effects on pathogen burden and clearance remain variable. Receptor-specific evidence for immune-cell-intrinsic GLP-1R signalling remains limited, and many reported immune phenotypes may instead reflect metabolic improvement, neuroimmune regulation, or barrier protection. Human evidence is derived mainly from observational studies and secondary analyses of chronic GLP-1RA exposure, with limited evidence from trials initiating treatment during acute infection. Future translation will require cell-specific receptor validation, live-pathogen models with post-infection treatment, parallel assessment of pathogen control and host protection, clinically relevant standard-of-care comparators, and infection-specific safety evaluation. GLP-1RAs are therefore best regarded as candidate host-directed adjuncts. Current evidence does not establish them as direct anti-infective therapies.

articles.title: Conventional Preoperative Prediction of MASLD-Compatible Histologic Abnormality, Fibrosis, and Higher-Grade Steatohepatitis, and Exploratory Machine-Learning Classification of MASH Severity in Patients Undergoing Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is highly prevalent in patients with severe obesity undergoing metabolic/bariatric surgery. Noninvasive preoperative stratification of histologic liver abnormalities remains incomplete. We evaluated conventional regression models and a separate exploratory machine-learning analysis of MASH grade 1 versus grades 2/3.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort included patients undergoing Roux-en-Y gastric bypass between March 2000 and March 2025. Of 1,350 surgical patients, 745 underwent intraoperative wedge liver biopsy and 375 had complete data for conventional modeling. Conventional endpoints were MASLD-compatible histologic abnormality, any documented fibrosis, and higher-grade steatohepatitis, defined as biopsy-reported grades 2/3. The machine-learning analysis included 284 patients with steatohepatitis and used routine preoperative variables, ultrasound-reported steatosis, NFS, the AST/ALT ratio, and FIB-4. Model development used RandomizedSearchCV and repeated stratified cross-validation within the training set, followed by training-based threshold selection and held-out test evaluation.

RESULTS: BMI and triglycerides were associated with MASLD-compatible histologic abnormality, BMI with any fibrosis, and age, BMI, triglycerides, and AST with higher-grade steatohepatitis. The latter conventional model had an apparent AUC of 0.737 and a mean cross-validated AUC of 0.692. L2-penalized logistic regression had the highest machine-learning test ROC-AUC point estimate (0.730; 95% CI, 0.585-0.864), with sensitivity 0.739 for MASH grades 2/3 at a threshold of 0.49. Test Brier score was 0.242; calibration was unsatisfactory (ECE 0.203; calibration slope 13.469), and decision-curve findings remained exploratory.

CONCLUSION: Routine preoperative information showed moderate discrimination for selected histologic outcomes. Both the conventional score and the machine-learning severity classifier require further validation before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Hospitalization Data for a Severe Acute Exacerbation of COPD as Predictors for Persistent Hypercapnia at 3 Months After Discharge.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study's purpose was to develop a prognostication model to predict persistent hypercapnia 3 months after discharge in patients hospitalized for COPD exacerbation and hypercapnia.

METHODS: We developed the prediction model using a training data set comprising of participants in the RESCUE trial who received no ventilation support at home. We externally validated the model with a retrospective cohort. We calculated the rate of persistent hypercapnia 3 months post hospitalization according to the inpatient PaCO2. We also built regression models that included age and prior hospitalizations and calculated Area Under Curve (AUC).

RESULTS: Our training cohort consisted of 69 participants. Among participants with baseline PaCO2 levels between 45 and 52mmHg, 59% had persistent hypercapnia at 3 months. It increased to 73.1% with PaCO2 between 53 and 60mmHg and 100% with greater than 60 mmHg (P < 0.001). Our regression model showed that for each one mmHg increase in baseline PaCO2 the 3-month PaCO2 increased by 0.41. The AUC was 0.779 (95%CI of 0.667 to 0.891).

CONCLUSION: The last inpatient PaCO2 measurement may help predict persistent hypercapnia 3 months after discharge.

articles.title: Temporal Cascade of Post-Stroke Cognitive Impairment: Metabolic-Mitochondrial Crosstalk.
articles.abstract: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is a common and highly disabling complication of stroke. Current research on its molecular mechanisms has largely focused on neuroinflammatory cascades and blood-brain barrier disruption caused by microglial polarization, while the role of cellular metabolism remains underexplored. Metabolic reprogramming is a coordinated network-level adjustment of carbohydrate, lipid, and amino acid metabolism, and has recently become a research hotspot in neurological diseases, particularly centered on phenotypic switching of microglia following metabolic reprogramming. As the center of cellular energy metabolism, mitochondria are closely linked to normal cellular bioenergetics through biogenesis, motility, and quality control; disruption of any of these links after brain injury is intimately associated with neuronal activity. In this review, we adopt a metabolism-oriented perspective to explore the changes in the brain microenvironment after metabolic reprogramming, connect the critical role of mitochondrial dysfunction in disease development, and deeply analyze the core positions of both in the pathogenesis of PSCI, presenting the complex regulatory network linking metabolic disturbances and mitochondrial dysfunction, as described in the Graphical Abstract. Furthermore, we discuss the future prospects of emerging technologies such as mitochondrial transplantation and stem cell therapy, aiming to translate theoretical advances into clinical applications for PSCI.

articles.title: Comparison of rapid portable devices and laboratory methods to assess the blood chemistry of farmed adult common snook (Centropomus undecimalis).
articles.abstract: The application of clinical biochemistry for health monitoring in marine fish aquaculture remains limited, partly due to the lack of validated analytical protocols and species-specific reference values. This study evaluated the agreement between portable devices (PD) (Accutrend Plus analyzer and protein refractometer) and conventional laboratory methods (clinical diagnostic kits) for quantifying glucose, lactate, cholesterol, triacylglycerols, and total protein in the blood of common snook, Centropomus undecimalis. Thirty-six captive-bred adults (mean body weight: 2.35 ± 0.28 kg and a Fulton index of 0.887 ± 0.036) were sampled. Passing-Bablok regression detected proportional bias for lactate (slope 0.684, 95% CI 0.46-0.92), triacylglycerols (slope 0.594, 95% CI 0.38-0.81), and total protein (slope 0.245, 95% CI 0.13-0.38), with lactate and total protein also showing constant bias; glucose and cholesterol did not deviate from the line of identity. Bland-Altman analysis showed a small mean bias only for lactate (0.024 mg/mL, 6.2%; 95% LoA - 0.010 to 0.058 mg/mL). Glucose showed a moderate though systematic difference (17.2%), whereas cholesterol (- 40.9%), triacylglycerols (35.3%), and particularly total protein (- 55.0%; 95% LoA - 65.88 to - 1.04 mg/mL) showed large systematic differences with LoA that excluded zero. The greatest discrepancy was observed between protein measurement techniques; the refractometer has a lower detection limit that differs considerably from laboratory assessment; therefore, it is not recommended for determining physiological condition. The analysis indicates that portable devices and laboratory techniques yield different absolute results and cannot be used interchangeably. Nevertheless, portable devices offer potential utility for establishing farm-specific baseline levels and identifying elevated lactate or glucose levels associated with stress. The measured blood biochemical values provide a baseline for captive adult common snook and indicate that point-of-care diagnostic devices may serve as practical tools for routine health monitoring of C. undecimalis in the field.

articles.title: Optimizing rheumatology referral in patients with psoriasis: a community-based pilot study of four screening questionnaires within a collaborative dermatology-rheumatology pathway.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Musculoskeletal symptoms in patients with psoriasis may indicate psoriatic arthritis (PsA) or other rheumatic diseases requiring specialist assessment. Screening questionnaires may facilitate referral from dermatology to rheumatology, but their performance within collaborative community pathways remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: To compare four psoriasis screening questionnaires for PsA and inflammatory arthritis (IA) within a community dermatology-rheumatology referral pathway and assess operational feasibility.

METHODS: Fifty adults with dermatologist-confirmed psoriasis, no prior PsA, and no systemic psoriasis therapy were prospectively recruited to a cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy pilot study. PEST, EARP, PASE, and ToPAS II were completed before blinded rheumatological assessment. Sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, 95% confidence intervals, and Youden index were calculated for PsA and IA using complete-case denominators.

RESULTS: IA was identified in 13/50 participants (26.0%), including 10 with PsA (20.0%); OA and FMS occurred in 56.0% and 8.0%. Screen-positive rates ranged from 36.0% (PASE) to 64.0% (EARP). ToPAS II had the highest observed Youden index for IA (0.408; sensitivity 76.9%, specificity 63.9%) and PsA (0.290; 70.0%, 59.0%). Alternative or coexisting diagnoses were common among screen-positive participants.

CONCLUSIONS: The pathway was operationally feasible within the two participating practices and identified previously unrecognized inflammatory rheumatic disease. ToPAS II showed the highest observed sensitivity-specificity balance, but small case numbers preclude definitive ranking. Alternative diagnoses among screen-positive participants support use of these questionnaires as triage instruments rather than diagnostic tests for PsA. Key Points • A community dermatology-rheumatology referral pathway was feasible in routine practice. • Rheumatological assessment identified inflammatory arthritis in 26% of participants. • In this pilot cohort, ToPAS II showed the highest observed sensitivity-specificity balance for inflammatoryarthritis and PsA, although definitive ranking was not possible. • Screening questionnaires should guide rheumatology referral rather than diagnose PsA alone.

articles.title: Perioperative neurocognitive outcomes after robot-assisted pelvic surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of reported proportions, comparative risk and prognostic factors.
articles.abstract: Delirium and cognitive decline may complicate recovery after robot-assisted pelvic surgery, but their frequency and relationship to positioning remain uncertain. We assessed reported proportions, comparative surgical risk and prognostic factors. PubMed, CENTRAL, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, ClinicalTrials.gov and WHO ICTRP were searched through 4 August 2026. Eligible adult robotic pelvic studies reported objective cognitive testing or delirium. Two reviewers performed original screening, extraction and question-specific bias appraisal. Post hoc logit random-effects meta-analyses summarized prospective cohorts using restricted maximum likelihood and modified Hartung-Knapp intervals in R. Twenty-six reports represented 25 studies. Five cognitive cohorts (356 participants) yielded 29.0% (95% confidence interval [CI] 20.2-39.8%); excluding Beck yielded 31.8% (20.7-45.4%). Three delirium cohorts (245 participants) yielded a descriptive model summary of 10.3% (2.2-37.0%). Individual delirium proportions were 8/82 (9.8%; exact 95% CI 4.3-18.3%), 4/80 (5.0%; 1.4-12.3%) and 14/83 (16.9%; 9.5-26.7%). The approximate 95% prediction interval from the delirium meta-analysis was very wide (<0.1-99.8%). The same-procedure prostatectomy comparison yielded an unadjusted risk ratio of 1.06 (0.73-1.55) for early cognitive decline. Comparative evidence was of low or very low certainty. Definitions, surveillance and selection limited interpretation; Trendelenburg-duration findings were inconsistent. These proportions describe selected study-defined outcomes. They do not establish attributable robotic or positioning risk, a safe exposure threshold, or benefit from horizontal breaks. Standardized prospective measurement is needed.

articles.title: Integrated multivariate and ecological risk assessment of trace metals in tropical coastal sediments: insights from the Kalpakkam coast, India.
articles.abstract: Surface sediments from the Kalpakkam coast (southeast India) were investigated to evaluate trace metal distribution, contamination status, and ecological risk within a northeast monsoon-dominated tropical coastal system. Ninety-six samples collected seasonally during 2019-2021 were analyzed for grain size, total organic carbon (TOC), and trace metals (Cr, Mn, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn, Pb, Cd, Fe, Al). Sediments were predominantly sandy (mean 88.8%) with moderate TOC (1.45 ± 0.66%). Chromium (280.6 ± 143.5 ppm) and Ni (47.1 ± 15.4 ppm) showed relatively high concentrations, whereas Cu, Zn, and Pb remained low. Cadmium occurred at low absolute concentrations (0.91 ± 0.88 ppm) but displayed notable enrichment. PCA, supported by parallel analysis, identified two dominant geochemical assemblages: a Cr-Ni-Co detrital suite and a Fe-Mn-Zn-Cu-Pb association, which together accounted for 57.81% of the total variance. Significant seasonal variation (p < 0.001) reflected monsoon-driven sediment redistribution. Although Cd showed weak loadings on both retained principal components, it exhibited disproportionate enrichment and ecological weighting. Pollution indices indicated enrichment for Cr (mean EF 10.70) and particularly Cd (mean EF 14.74), whereas the mean Pollution Load Index (0.40) suggested the absence of widespread multi-metal contamination. The Potential Ecological Risk Index (mean: 150.89) indicated a moderate ecological risk; however, sensitivity analysis excluding Cd resulted in a lower PERI (14.86). The mean ERM quotient (0.31) suggested ~ 21% probability of adverse biological effects. Overall, trace metal distributions are mainly controlled by lithogenic inputs and sediment texture, with Cd representing the primary ecological concern.

articles.title: Plasma p-tau217 as a biomarker mapping cognitive impairment in Alzheimer's disease.
authors: CHARM study group; Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Plasma p-tau217 is a well-established biomarker of Alzheimer disease (AD) pathology, but its relationship with cognitive status and longitudinal cognitive change remains less well characterized. We investigated the clinical relevance of plasma p-tau217 as a blood-based biological correlate of cognitive status and change in AD.

METHODS: We included 1147 participants from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) with available plasma biomarkers and amyloid-β (Aβ) status determined by amyloid PET or cerebrospinal fluid Aβ42. Cross-sectional associations between plasma p-tau217 and cognitive performance were evaluated across clinical stages and by Aβ status. Longitudinal associations between baseline plasma p-tau217 and subsequent cognitive change, as well as between changes in p-tau217 and changes in cognition, were assessed using linear mixed-effects models and correlation analyses. Baseline to last follow-up change correlations and separated within-person from between-person associations were also analyzed.

RESULTS: Plasma p-tau217 were higher at more advanced clinical stages, particularly among Aβ+ participants. In the Aβ positive group, higher p-tau217 was associated with poorer baseline MMSE, CDR-SB, and ADAS-Cog13 scores (partial ρ = -0.46, 0.52, and 0.55, respectively). Higher baseline p-tau217 was associated with greater subsequent worsening on all three measures at nominal P < 0.05. Increases in p-tau217 were associated with concurrent worsening in ADAS-Cog13 and CDR-SB (P = 0.001 and P = 0.011, respectively, but not MMSE. Exploratory analyses identified a within-person association between p-tau217 increases and ADAS-Cog13 worsening. Associations were less consistent among Aβ- participants.

CONCLUSION: Plasma p-tau217 was associated with cognitive impairment and longitudinal cognitive change, particularly among Aβ+ participants. These findings support plasma p-tau217 as a potential blood-based biological correlate of cognitive status and longitudinal cognitive change in AD.

articles.title: Adolescent Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Can Be the First Clue to Multisystem Mitochondrial Disease.
articles.abstract: Up to 40% of children with mitochondrial disease develop hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) during their disease course, but HCM is almost never the first presenting manifestation. When it is, the underlying mitochondrial disorder is easily missed: the cardiomyopathy is managed in isolation, and extracardiac findings that emerge later may be dismissed as unrelated. We describe an adolescent whose severe HCM was the first major manifestation of clinicopathologically confirmed multisystem mitochondrial disease with a phenotype consistent with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy. Her cardiomyopathy was managed in isolation for over a year before optic atrophy, primary ovarian insufficiency, osteopenia, and exercise intolerance were ultimately recognized as part of a single mitochondrial process. Endomyocardial and skeletal muscle biopsy confirmed mitochondrial pathology. The diagnosis directly changed management: cofactor supplementation was initiated, her visual acuity stabilized on idebenone, and perioperative planning for transplantation was adapted to prevent catabolic decompensation. Her cardiac disease progressed to heart failure requiring transplantation at age 16 years, but she remains clinically stable with preserved graft function more than 15 years later. This case challenges the assumption that mitochondrial disease should enter the differential only after neurologic dysfunction appears. General pediatricians, who see the whole child longitudinally, are uniquely positioned to recognize when dysfunction in other high-energy tissues points toward a unifying mitochondrial diagnosis in a child with cardiomyopathy.

articles.title: Increased frequency of dislocation following total hip arthroplasty for trauma : an age- and sex-matched cohort study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The purpose of this study was to compare surgical techniques and postoperative outcomes in an age- and sex-matched cohort of patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty (THA) for neck of femur fracture (#NOF) and for osteoarthritis (OA).

METHODS: A single-centre, consecutive series of patients at minimum one-year follow-up following THA for #NOF were compared with a 1:1 age- and sex-matched cohort of patients following THA for osteoarthritis from the same institution. The primary outcome measure was frequency of dislocation at one year postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included rates of all-cause revision, infection, periprosthetic fracture, and mortality at one year and medium-term postoperatively. Cox regression compared medium-term outcomes between groups, accounting for unequal follow-up duration.

RESULTS: A total of 722 patients were included, with 361 in each group. BMI was greater in the OA group (28.9 kg/m2 vs 24.7 kg/m2; p < 0.001). Sex, age, American Society of Anesthesiologists grade, and comorbidity profile did not differ between groups (p > 0.247). Overall, 151 patients (41.8%) in the #NOF group received dual-mobility implants, compared with eight (2.2%) in the OA group (p < 0.001). Femoral offset was similar between groups (42.6 mm and 42.7 mm, p = 0.892). Dislocation rates were greater in the #NOF group than the OA group at one-year (4.4% vs 1.1%; p = 0.011) and by final follow-up. The one-year rates of periprosthetic fracture, all-cause revision, and mortality were similar between groups (p > 0.340), although risk of mortality was greater by final follow-up after THA for #NOF (hazard ratio 1.577; p = 0.033).

CONCLUSION: Despite the more frequent use of dual-mobility implants in THA for #NOF than OA and the otherwise comparable patient demographics and implants used, the risk of early dislocation after THA for #NOF was four times greater than in an age- and sex-matched elective THA cohort. Early postoperative complication rates were otherwise comparable between the groups.

articles.title: Magnitude and durability of RSV-specific immune responses three years after hospitalization for RSV-associated acute respiratory illness among adults ≥50 years.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Understanding immune responses to RSV natural infection in older adults could help inform the need for vaccination, as neutralizing antibodies correlate with protection in this high-risk population.

METHODS: Adults ≥50 years of age hospitalized with acute respiratory illness were prospectively enrolled (September 2018─March 2020) at two Atlanta, Georgia hospitals. Nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal swabs were analyzed, and standard-of-care RSV results were recorded. Follow-up visits occurred in early convalescence (V2), at start of the next respiratory season (SS2), and 2- and 3-years post-infection. Sera were analyzed for RSV-binding IgG by enzyme immunoassay and RSV-A2 and -B1 by neutralization assays. Antibody decay was measured by linear regression of log2-transformed titers. PBMCs were analyzed for T-cell responses by intracellular cytokine staining.

RESULTS: Nineteen RSV-positive and 11 RSV-negative participants were eligible for analysis. For RSV-positive participants, RSV IgG and neutralizing antibodies peaked in early convalescence, and gradually waned through 3-year follow-up. RSV IgG titers declined by -0.08 log2 per month, while RSV-A and -B neutralizing antibody titers declined by -0.05log2 per month and were statistically equivalent to RSV-negative participants by the SS2 visit. For RSV-negative participants, minimal changes in antibody titers were observed over time. No significant differences were seen in RSV-specific T cell responses from SS2 to 2- and 3-year follow-up among either group.

CONCLUSIONS: RSV binding and neutralizing antibodies were transiently elevated following natural infection in older adults but waned to levels similar to RSV-negative participants by the next season's start. Vaccines that counter waning immunity are needed in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Occupational cardiology: the next step in cardiovascular prevention.
Improving Patient Health Literacy in Hypertension and Diabetes: A Quality Improvement Project in Primary Care.
articles.journal: American journal of medical quality : the official journal of the American College of Medical Quality
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic diseases such as hypertension and diabetes require active patient participation in daily management. Limited health literacy contributes to poor adherence to medications, lifestyle recommendations, and monitoring practices, ultimately increasing the risk of complications. This project evaluated whether brief, targeted educational videos could improve patient knowledge and self-management skills in a primary care population.

METHODS: We conducted a quality improvement project involving 109 patients diagnosed with hypertension or diabetes at a primary care clinic. Educational videos covered 5 domains: blood pressure measurement; complications of uncontrolled hypertension; dietary approaches to stop hypertension diet; blood glucose monitoring; and complications of diabetes. Patients viewed the 2- to 3-minute videos via QR code on their own smartphones, or on a clinic phone, while waiting in the exam room. Participants completed the same questionnaire immediately before and after viewing. Changes in knowledge were analyzed using McNemar's exact test for paired responses.

RESULTS: Significant improvements were observed postintervention. In diabetes: knowledge of tools needed for glucose testing (79%-100%, P = 0.016), timing of glucose checks (36%-94%, P < 0.001), hypoglycemia management (61%-91%, P = 0.006), and awareness of nephropathy, neuropathy, and low-density lipoprotein control (P < 0.05). In hypertension: improvement in premeasurement behaviors (50%-83%, P = 0.002), interpretation of systolic/diastolic readings (23%-70%, P < 0.001), and consistent monitoring importance (63%-97%, P = 0.002). Lifestyle-related knowledge (diet, exercise) improved but did not reach statistical significance.

CONCLUSIONS: Brief, QR code-delivered educational videos viewed during in-visit wait time were associated with substantial short-term gains in patient comprehension of critical self-management concepts. This low-cost, adaptable model is feasible in routine primary care.

articles.title: Elevated serum IL-33 and VEGF levels in preschool children with recurrent wheezing.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract: Objectıve: Recurrent wheezing (RW) is a common respiratory condition in preschool children and is associated with an increased risk of subsequent asthma development. Interleukin (IL)-33 and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) are involved in airway inflammation and remodeling, but their role in preschool RW remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate serum IL-33 and VEGF levels and investigate their diagnostic and prognostic value in children with RW.Methods: A total of 132 children were enrolled, including 83 children with RW and 49 healthy controls. Serum IL-33 and VEGF levels were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Children with RW were reevaluated after three years for asthma development.Results: Serum IL-33 and VEGF levels were significantly higher in children with RW than in controls (both p < 0.001). ROC analysis showed good discriminatory performance for IL-33 (AUC: 0.763, 95% CI: 0.679-0.839) and VEGF (AUC: 0.794, 95% CI: 0.714-0.872). During follow-up, 54 of 83 children (65.1%) developed asthma. Multivariable logistic regression identified elevated VEGF levels, food allergy, and a family history of asthma as independent predictors of asthma development. Each 10 pg/mL increase in VEGF was associated with a 19% increase in asthma risk (adjusted OR: 1.19, 95% CI: 1.05-1.35; p = 0.006).Conclusions: Serum IL-33 and VEGF levels are elevated in preschool children with RW. Elevated VEGF levels independently predict subsequent asthma development, suggesting that VEGF may serve as a noninvasive biomarker for identifying children at increased risk of future asthma.

articles.title: Beyond blood: a narrative review of advancements in saliva-based diagnostics.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Human whole saliva is an accessible, noninvasive biofluid reflecting systemic and oral physiology, offering a viable alternative to invasive venipuncture and its associated pre-analytical vulnerabilities (e.g. ex vivo glycolysis).

AREAS COVERED: This narrative review synthesizes salivary biomarkers across major clinical domains, focusing on glycemic control (glucose, 1,5-anhydroglucitol, α2-macroglobulin), cardiovascular risk indices (cTnI, hs-CRP, sAA), critical care and sepsis surveillance (IL-10, acute-phase proteins), endocrinology (free steroid hormones), infectious diseases (HIV, HCV, SARS-CoV-2), oncological liquid biopsy (exosomal miRNAs, ctDNA), and neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer's disease (Aβ42, p-tau181, lactoferrin). Analytical modalities-ranging from high-sensitivity immunoassays to wearable electrochemical biosensors and mass spectrometry-are critically evaluated. Furthermore, this review delineates regulatory-cleared diagnostic platforms (FDA PMA/510(k), EUA, CE-IVD, and SAMHSA-certified panels for viral antibodies, late-night salivary cortisol, and toxicology) from emerging discovery-phase panels.

EXPERT OPINION: Widespread clinical translation remains constrained by unstandardized collection protocols, oral matrix interference, and a lack of normative reference intervals. Transitioning salivary testing into mainstream diagnostics requires three priorities: (1) universal sampling standardization incorporating flow-rate normalization, (2) engineering matrix-matched biosensors tailored for sub-picomolar detection, and (3) rigorous multicenter prospective trials to validate definitive clinical cutoffs, dynamic blood-saliva correlation kinetics, and digital point-of-care integration.

articles.title: Creation and verification of an interpretable machine learning model for forecasting in-hospital results in Cardiorenal syndrome patients in critical condition.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with cardiorenal syndrome (CRS) in the intensive care unit (ICU) have high mortality. Although mortality prediction models exist for specific CRS subtypes, models encompassing all CRS subtypes remain lacking.

METHODS: We used MIMIC-IV (v2.2; n = 6,668) for model development and eICU-CRD (v2.0; n = 3,602) for external validation. In patients who stayed in the ICU for at least 24 hours, predictors, including early treatments, were collected during the first 24 hours to predict in-hospital mortality.
