After 1:1 random undersampling, we compared 11 machine learning algorithms and used SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to select and interpret features.  .

RESULTS: The artificial neural network (ANN) performed best. The final model contained six variables: acute kidney injury (AKI) stage, age, mechanical ventilation, vasopressor use, β-blocker use, and angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor/angiotensin receptor blocker use. The area under the curve (AUC) was 0.810 (95% CI: 0.757-0.860) in internal validation and 0.704 (95% CI: 0.682-0.726) in external validation.

CONCLUSIONS: This interpretable model, available as a web calculator, may help identify high-risk CRS patients 24 hours after ICU admission, although its external performance was moderate. .

articles.title: Emerging pharmacotherapeutic options for adult asthma.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Current biologics have transformed asthma management; however, incomplete responses in some patients with type 2-high disease and the absence of approved targeted therapies for type 2-low asthma highlight the need for novel treatment strategies summarized in this review.

AREAS COVERED: This review examines literature gathered from searches of PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov and conference abstracts from 2014 to the present for listings of approved biologics and investigational therapies across the severe asthma treatment landscape. This review includes clinical trials, preclinical studies, and guideline recommendations to evaluate established and emerging approaches, including next-generation anti-IgE, anti-IL-5/IL-5R, anti-IL-4/IL-13, and anti-TSLP therapies, together with novel targets that are in early-stage clinical trials such as IL-33/ST2, mast cell pathways, and transcription factor inhibitors.

EXPERT OPINION: There is a shift from single-cytokine blockade toward broader modulation of airway inflammation through multi-specific antibodies and intracellular signaling targets. Major unmet needs remain in type 2-low asthma, where no biologic is specifically approved for this endotype. Future progress will depend on improved biomarker-guided patient stratification and the development of therapies capable of achieving individualized, mechanism-driven disease modification.

articles.title: Cell-type-specific FGF23 signalling in chronic kidney disease-associated cardiovascular injury.
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) produces a distinctive cardiovascular phenotype that traditional risk factors cannot fully explain. Fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) rises early in CKD, whereas renal and circulating α-Klotho decline; this imbalance weakens canonical FGFR1c-α-Klotho signalling and permits maladaptive receptor engagement in cardiovascular tissues. The present review synthesises current evidence on cell-type-specific FGF23 signalling in CKD, focusing on receptor topology, intracellular signalling cascades, and therapeutic implications. In vascular endothelial cells, excess FGF23 promotes oxidative stress, depletes nitric oxide, and impairs endothelial function, partly through FGFR1-PLCγ2-NOX2-dependent generation of reactive oxygen species. In vascular smooth muscle cells, FGF23 intersects with MEK-ERK signalling and phosphate sensing, although medial calcification is driven predominantly by phosphate retention and α-Klotho deficiency rather than by FGF23 alone. In cardiomyocytes, α-Klotho-independent FGFR4 signalling activates the PLCγ-calcineurin-NFAT axis, promoting left ventricular hypertrophy, calcium-handling abnormalities, and arrhythmogenic vulnerability. FGF23 also contributes to cardiac fibroblast activation and extracellular-matrix remodelling. A parallel, largely FGF23-independent calcium-sensing receptor-calcium-organelle stress pathway may additionally amplify mitochondrial injury, cGAS-STING signalling, and inflammasome-mediated cell death within the CKD-mineral bone disorder (CKD-MBD) milieu. Emerging experimental evidence that skeletal muscle can generate FGF23 during phosphate stress broadens the traditional bone-centred model of CKD-MBD. Calciprotein particles are additionally implicated as an extracellular signal coupling mineral loading to FGF23 secretion, and prognostic data from naturally occurring feline CKD support a conserved clinical relevance across species. Current therapies lower FGF23 only indirectly, through phosphate, parathyroid hormone, iron, and kidney-protective pathways, and dedicated cardiovascular outcome trials targeting the FGF23-α-Klotho axis are still lacking.

articles.title: Mechanistic understanding of the role of the lung-brain axis in the pathogenesis of PM2.5-induced Alzheimer's disease.
articles.abstract: Air pollution, particularly fine particulate matter (PM2.5), has emerged as an important yet under-recognised environmental contributor to cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease (AD) across the life course. Although epidemiological studies consistently associate long-term PM2.5 exposure with impaired cognition, from reduced neurodevelopmental performance in children to accelerated neurodegeneration in older adults, the biological mechanisms linking inhaled particles to AD-related brain pathology remain incompletely defined. In the present review, we synthesise current epidemiological and experimental evidence to position the lung-brain axis as a central mechanistic framework through which PM2.5 may influence brain aging and AD pathogenesis. Rather than acting solely through direct particle entry into the brain, PM2.5-induced pulmonary injury initiates systemic signalling cascades, including inflammatory mediators, oxidative stress, blood-brain barrier disruption, and extracellular vesicle-mediated intercellular communication, which together propagate disease signals from the lung to the brain. We further examine how these pathways intersect with core AD-related processes, including amyloid-β accumulation, tau pathology, impaired protein clearance, maladaptive microglial responses, and autophagy-lysosomal dysfunction. We also discuss important modifiers of susceptibility and heterogeneity in reported associations, including pollutant composition, co-exposure to other air pollutants, sex, APOE genotype, and epigenetic reprogramming. Overall, the present review proposes an integrated multi-organ model of PM2.5 neurotoxicity that aligns environmental exposure with key mechanisms of AD pathogenesis and highlights priorities for strengthening causal inference and future translational research.

articles.title: Classifying physician-diagnosed childhood asthma status using explainable machine learning: NHANES 2007-2016.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and internally evaluate explainable machine-learning classifiers for physician-diagnosed childhood asthma status and assess the incremental value of five complete-blood-count (CBC)-derived inflammatory indices beyond gender, race, age, family history of asthma, poverty income ratio (PIR), and body mass index (BMI).

METHODS: NHANES 2007-2016 data from 6,437 children aged 2-14 years were split into training (n = 4,505) and held-out test (n = 1,932) sets. Six machine-learning algorithms were compared using PR-AUC as the primary selection metric. Calibration and the classification threshold were derived from training out-of-fold predictions. The final model was evaluated in the held-out test set. KernelSHAP assessed feature contributions, and repeated nested cross-validation evaluated the incremental value of the five CBC-derived indices.

RESULTS: Among 6,437 children, 784 (12.2%) had physician-diagnosed asthma. SVM achieved the highest mean PR-AUC (0.294) during training-set repeated cross-validation and ranked first in all 10 repeats. In the held-out test set, ROC-AUC was 0.743 (95% CI, 0.708-0.778) and PR-AUC was 0.312 (95% CI, 0.268-0.370). At the training-derived threshold of 0.081, sensitivity was 0.672, specificity 0.740, and Brier score 0.097. Family history of asthma had the largest mean absolute SHAP value (0.089). Adding the five CBC-derived indices changed mean PR-AUC from 0.2944 to 0.2956 (paired difference +0.0012; SD 0.0049).

CONCLUSION: The SVM showed moderate discrimination for physician-diagnosed childhood asthma status. CBC-derived inflammatory indices provided no clear incremental improvement beyond gender, race, age, family history, PIR, and BMI. External validation is required before clinical use.

articles.title: Tick tock: how the body's circadian clock keeps cardiometabolic rhythm in check.
articles.abstract: The circadian clock orchestrates the internal timing of numerous physiological processes through an approximately 24-h cycle. It comprises a hypothalamic central clock, which responds to light cues and entrains peripheral clocks within individual cells and organs that, depending on the tissue, regulate gene expression across diverse biological functions in a tissue-specific manner. Peripheral clocks are also entrained by feeding and exercise-related cues, enabling their synchronization with feeding rhythm and physiology. Together, these clocks maintain a complex molecular network essential for metabolic homeostasis. Disruption of circadian rhythms, driven by genetic, environmental, or behavioral factors, is increasingly recognized as a major contributor to cardiometabolic disorders. Modern lifestyles, including shift work, irregular sleep, prolonged exposure to artificial light at night, jet lag, and erratic eating schedules, misalign circadian clocks with environmental cues, contributing to disruption of circadian rhythms or chronodisruption. This misalignment alters hormonal regulation, promotes systemic inflammation, and impairs metabolic balance, thereby increasing the risk of cardiovascular disease, obesity, type 2 diabetes, and related complications. The present review examines the mechanistic roles of core circadian clock genes in cardiometabolic health, highlighting their regulation of physiological processes in peripheral organs such as the heart, liver, and adipose tissue. We further discuss how circadian clock disruption accelerates disease onset and progression and explore emerging therapeutic strategies, including pharmacological modulation of the molecular circadian clock components and personalized chronotherapy. These approaches offer promising avenues to restore circadian alignment and mitigate cardiometabolic risk.

articles.title: Cardiometabolic benefits of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and dual agonists: from obesity and diabetes to heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) accounts for over half of all heart failure hospitalizations and is increasing in prevalence, largely driven by obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and the dual GLP-1/GIP agonist, tirzepatide, have been shown to be safe and effective medications in the treatment of T2DM and obesity, as well as in obesity-related HFpEF.

AREAS COVERED: This review summarizes the pathophysiology of obesity-related HFpEF, mechanisms by which GLP-1 RAs and tirzepatide may improve symptoms and outcomes, and summarize evidence from recent randomized controlled and observational trials across the disease spectrum in which they have been studied. Therapeutic implications and future research directions are also discussed. A structured literature search was performed using PubMed/MEDLINE and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) up to August 2025.

EXPERT OPINION: GLP-1 receptor agonists and tirzepatide represent a promising therapeutic advance for obesity-related HFpEF. Benefits are likely mediated through weight‑loss‑dependent and weight-loss‑independent mechanisms. Important uncertainties remain regarding their role in non-obese HFpEF, optimal patient selection, and their safety in HFrEF.

articles.title: Coupled oxidative and adsorptive desulfurization of fuel using molybdenum-modified carbon derived from PET waste.
articles.abstract: Environmental pollution caused by (SO) x emissions from the combustion of sulfur-containing fuels remains a significant challenge. Oxidation-coupled adsorptive desulfurization is a promising alternative technique to remove aromatic sulfur compounds from fuel. In this study, we developed a bifunctional material for coupled adsorptive and oxidative desulfurization by upcycling PET plastic bottles into a highly functional carbonaceous material via microwave-assisted KOH activation followed by impregnation with molybdenum. The high surface area and porous structure of carbonised PET, together with the metal impregnation, enhance the desulfurization capacity. The adsorbent material was characterised using FT-IR, BET, XRF, TGA, SEM-EDX, XRD, and XPS analysis. The maximum adsorption capacity of the material was found to be 63.76 mg g-1, with a surface area of 254.93 m2 g-1. The overall removal process was thermodynamically favourable and endothermic, and the kinetic data was best described by pseudo-second-order kinetics. The adsorbent was stable up to four cycles after regeneration. The developed cost-effective adsorbent demonstrated effective coupled oxidative-adsorptive desulfurization of real diesel while supporting sustainable management of PET waste.

articles.title: Baseline gradient, valve morphology and left ventricular recovery and survival after TAVR in reduced-ejection-fraction aortic stenosis: a retrospective cohort study.
VAPA-dependent lipid transport at ER-lamellar body contact sites promotes human lung surfactant formation.
articles.abstract: Vesicle-associated membrane protein-associated proteins (VAPs) establish membrane contact sites (MCS) between the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and other organelles through interactions with FFAT-containing proteins, coordinating lipid synthesis, transfer, and metabolism. Their tissue-specific functions remain poorly understood. We report a patient with a homozygous nonsense variant in VAPA (p.(Glu12∗)), presenting with profound global developmental delay and progressive surfactant dysfunction leading to cholesterol pneumonitis and pulmonary fibrosis. Alternative translation initiation partially bypasses the premature stop codon, producing an N-terminally truncated VAPA protein with impaired FFAT binding capacity and disrupted lamellar body (LB) formation in human alveolar type 2 cells. We identify the pulmonary disease-associated ATP-binding cassette transporter A3 (ABCA3), a regulator of surfactant lipid accumulation, as a VAPA interactor. VAPA-ABCA3 interaction facilitates lipid exchange at previously uncharacterized ER-LB MCSs, a function lost upon VAPA truncation. Our findings establish VAPA-dependent MCS dysfunction as a mechanism of syndromic lung disease and define a pathway for surfactant lipid trafficking.

articles.title: Correction: Intermediate knowledge enhanced the performance of the amide coupling yield prediction model.
articles.abstract: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.1039/D5SC03364K.].

articles.title: Measured, not labeled: un-analyzable input versus misclassification in single-lead wearable ECG.
articles.abstract: Objective. Wearable single-lead ECG has expanded arrhythmia screening, but many recordings are inconclusive, and each corpus defines that word differently. We ask how much deployment error is un-analyzable input rather than misclassification when analyzability is measured with one instrument.Approach. We evaluate three diagnostic databases in-domain and leave-dataset-out under a strict loss counting windows carrying each corpus's inconclusive label as errors unless deferred. We score analyzability with an unsupervised morphological criterion calibrated against three experts on free-living ECG. Reference unreadability is sparse and imbalanced: only seven of 15 subjects contain an unreadable window and one supplies 88% of all unreadable windows. Thresholded sensitivity and every prevalence or true-share correction are therefore exploratory.Main results. The criterion flags almost all expert-unreadable windows but only subsets of the windows labeled inconclusive by their corpora: an inconclusive rate measures convention as much as signal. At, criterion-positive windows are 8.1%, 56.7% and 69.6% of the strict proxy loss on Holter, handheld and patch. The true-share point intervals lie below 50% on handheld and above it on patch, but joint calibration-and-sampling envelopes span 50% on both and still do at the Youden threshold 0.60. On handheld, the calibration-only envelope is more than twice as wide as the corpus-sampling-only envelope. Gate-versus-confidence ordering changes with the accounting and corpus; no general selective-risk advantage of the gate is established.Significance. Corpus labels, criterion flags and latent expert unreadability must not be conflated. A gate can win by predicting a labeling convention, and this retrospective study validates neither transfer to smartwatch dry electrodes nor improvement in patient outcomes. Measure the inconclusive rate with a stated criterion on the raw signal; do not inherit it from a corpus label.

articles.title: New sulfonamide derivatives as HDAC inhibitors and apoptosis inducers: design, synthesis, in silico study and anticancer evaluation.
articles.abstract: Cancer statistics indicate that more research is required to combat such a global fatal disease. In an attempt to develop an effective anticancer scaffold, we designed and synthesized new sulfonamide derivatives for potential histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibition. The new derivatives showed antiproliferative activity against three cancer cell lines: HepG-2 (hepatoma), A549 (lung carcinoma), and MCF-7 (breast carcinoma). The most sensitive cancer cell line to the new derivatives was MCF-7, followed by A549 then HepG-2. Compound 10 emerged as the most effective candidate, especially against MCF-7, where it showed an IC50 of 13.56 ± 1.36 µM. Meanwhile, it had an IC50 of 20.03 ± 2.17 and 34.71 ± 4.62 µM against A549 and HepG-2 cells, respectively. Interestingly, molecule 10 exhibited a markedly higher in vitro selectivity toward the tested cancer cell lines than the reference drug 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), with selectivity indices of 8.74 ± 0.88, 5.92 ± 0.74, and 3.41 ± 0.39 against MCF-7, A549, and HepG-2 cells, respectively, compared with 1.59 ± 0.13, 1.16 ± 0.09, and 1.67 ± 0.14 for 5-FU, respectively. These findings indicate greater in vitro selectivity of compound 10 toward the tested cancer cells relative to the normal WI-38 cell line; however, they should not be interpreted as evidence of superior overall safety compared with 5-FU. Furthermore, 10 caused inhibition to HDAC especially HDAC-2, showing an IC50 of 2.27 ± 0.07 µM, in comparison to the reference molecule entinostat (IC50 of 1.21 ± 0.04 µM). The Annexin V-FITC/PI assay indicated that apoptosis was the predominant mode of cell death caused by compound 10. Compound 10 caused an approximately 15-fold increase in the total number of apoptotic MCF-7 cells relative to untreated control cells. Meanwhile, compound 10 increased the expression levels of apoptotic markers p53, and the protein levels of caspase-9 in MCF-7 cells. Whereas it decreased the expression levels of Bcl-2 and VEGF. The docking data that revealed insights into the binding pattern of compound 10 to HDAC-2, were consistent with the biological data. Finally, this study suggests that compound 10 may serve as a lead molecule for further optimization toward new anticancer drugs.

articles.title: Comparative plaque- and liquid-based phage susceptibility testing of Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates in a cystic fibrosis randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract: The optimal phage susceptibility testing (PST) method is unclear. Here, two PST methods were compared using Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates recovered from patients with cystic fibrosis enrolled in a placebo-controlled clinical trial of a single intravenous dose of a four-phage cocktail (WRAIR-PAM-CF1). In total, 508 P. aeruginosa sputum isolates were evaluated, including isolates collected before or after phage or placebo treatment, isolates from the same trial participants over time, and isolates of different colony morphologies from the same participants at the same time point. Susceptibility to phages PaWRA01Φ11, PaWRA01Φ39, PaWRA02Φ83, and PaWRA02Φ87 and a cocktail of all four phages was assessed using a plaque assay (PA) and a Biolog Omnilog-based liquid assay (LA) with the same bacterial inoculum. A total of 170/508 isolates (33%) and 195/508 isolates (38%) were identified as susceptible to the cocktail by PA and LA, respectively. Among the susceptible isolates, 169/170 (99%; PA) and 187/195 (96%; LA) also tested susceptible to at least one of the four phages in the cocktail. Susceptible percent agreement between the PA and LA ranged from 76% to 100% and non-susceptible percent agreement ranged from 89% to 100% for all phages studied and the cocktail. Phage PaWRA02Φ83 demonstrated the greatest individual activity, with 164/508 (32%) and 188/508 (37%) isolates testing susceptible by PA and LA, respectively. The four-phage cocktail provided numerically broader coverage of P. aeruginosa (i.e., had the highest susceptibility rate) than did any single phage. There was high concordance between PST results by PA and LA.IMPORTANCEStandardization of phage susceptibility testing (PST) methods is essential to support phage therapy trials and any future clinical implementation. There are no standardized PST methods or interpretive criteria for PST. In this study, PST was performed by a plaque assay and a Biolog Omnilog-based liquid assay on Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates recovered from cystic fibrosis patients enrolled in a clinical trial. Susceptibility of 508 isolates to four phages and a cocktail of all four was evaluated. There was high concordance between susceptibility assessed by plaque and liquid assays and numerically broader coverage of P. aeruginosa by the cocktail compared to any single phage. This manuscript should be of interest to those performing PST.

articles.title: Clinical significance of different Histoplasma genotypes in human histoplasmosis: insights from a multicenter study from Québec comparing North American (NAm2) with Latin American (LAmA) isolates.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Histoplasmosis is recognized as endemic in Québec; however, no molecular epidemiological studies have been conducted to date. The clinical significance of identifying Histoplasma capsulatum genotypes remains unclear. We performed a retrospective multicenter study of 67 culture-confirmed histoplasmosis cases from four major academic hospitals in Québec between 1988 and 2014. Multi-locus sequence typing (MLST) was performed on isolates, and clinical data were analyzed for genotype-specific associations with demographics, clinical presentations, and outcomes. Most isolates belonged to either the North American clade 2 (48.1%) or Latin American clade A (39.2%), highlighting both endemic and imported disease patterns in Québec. A novel NAm2 sequence type (ST81) was identified, which was unique to Québec and accounted for 61% of the NAm2 isolates, but was not associated with significantly different clinical outcomes compared with other NAm2 strains. In multivariate analysis, disseminated disease was independently associated with immunosuppression (OR 14.18, P = 0.001), male sex (OR 6.01, P = 0.035), and LAmA genotype (OR 5.02, P = 0.031). Severe outcomes (intensive care unit admission, intubation, death, or amphotericin B use) were associated with immunosuppression (OR 4.48, P = 0.023), with a non-significant trend with LAmA infections (OR 3.06, P = 0.069). This first molecular characterization of histoplasmosis infections in Québec suggests a dual epidemiology, with locally acquired NAm2 and LAmA infections more often associated with travel or origin from endemic regions outside Québec. Host factors were associated with disease severity, while the potential contribution of fungal genotype requires further study. These findings highlight the value of molecular characterization for understanding the epidemiology of histoplasmosis in endemic settings.

IMPORTANCE: Histoplasmosis is an important dimorphic fungal infection in North America. Although Québec is a recognized endemic region, its molecular epidemiology has not been previously characterized, and the clinical relevance of different Histoplasma genotypes remains uncertain. In this multicenter study, we performed multi-locus sequence typing with detailed clinical data from 67 culture-confirmed cases diagnosed between 1988 and 2014. This represents the first molecular characterization of clinical Histoplasma isolates from Québec and the largest Canadian cohort examining the association between molecular genotypes, clinical presentation, and outcomes. We identified both North American NAm2 (Histoplasma ohiense) and imported Latin American LAmA (Histoplasma suramericanum) lineages, suggestive of a combination of locally acquired and travel-associated infections. We also identified a novel NAm2 sequence type (ST81) that appears unique to Québec, suggesting possible regional circulation. The LAmA genotype was associated with disseminated histoplasmosis, whereas immunosuppression was the principal predictor of severe outcomes. Overall, host factors were associated with disease severity, while the potential contribution of fungal genotype warrants further study. These findings highlight the value of molecular characterization for understanding the epidemiology of histoplasmosis in endemic settings.

articles.title: 3D network carbon nanotube film supported FeCoNiCrMn high-entropy alloy nanoparticles for integrated adsorption and detoxification of sulfur mustard simulant.
articles.abstract: Carbon nanotube (CNT) films with interconnected three-dimensional (3D) networks are ideal porous scaffolds for high-entropy alloy (HEA) immobilization, enabling integrated adsorption and detoxification of chemical warfare agents. Herein, FeCoNiCrMn HEA nanoparticles (50-150 nm) were uniformly anchored on 3D CNT film networks via ultrafast carbothermal shock (CTs) within 55 ms. The obtained FeCoNiCrMn@CNTs show a single-phase face-centered cubic structure with near-equiatomic composition and multivalent metal sites. At 25 °C and 50% RH, the composite delivers a high equilibrium adsorption capacity of 636 mg g-1 for 2-chloroethyl ethyl sulfide (2-CEES) vapor, a sulfur mustard simulant. A 98.5% degradation efficiency is reached within 12 h via a tandem redox pathway: reductive dechlorination of 2-CEES to hydroxyethyl ethyl sulfide followed by partial C-S bond oxidation, with C-S cleavage as the rate-limiting step. This work provides an ultrafast strategy to construct HEA/carbon nanotube composites and highlights their potential as advanced carbon-based materials for chemical warfare agent detoxification.

articles.title: Stereoselectivity of photoinduced interaction of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug S-ketoprofen with (L/D)-Trp-Leu-Pro-Phe peptide in solution studied by NMR, CIDNP and molecular dynamics simulation.
articles.abstract: The stereoselectivity of chiral drug interactions with enzymatic active sites and cellular receptors is a subject of significant scientific interest. This interest is driven, firstly, by the pronounced differences in the therapeutic activity of drug enantiomers and, secondly, by the emerging role of amino acid chiral inversion in peptides associated with pathologies such as Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and type II diabetes. To probe the fundamental steps of such biomolecular interactions, electron transfer (ET) serves as a well-defined elementary chemical process. Prior investigations of photoinduced ET in chiral donor-acceptor dyads, incorporating (S)-ketoprofen and (L/D)-tryptophan, have revealed stereoselective and spin-selective phenomena. Extending this work, the present study examines the interaction of (S)-ketoprofen with the L- and D-enantiomers of tryptophan within the tetrapeptide tryptophan-leucine-proline-phenylalanine (WLPF), in homogeneous non-aqueous solutions. Utilizing NMR spectroscopy, chemically induced dynamic nuclear polarization (CIDNP) to detect transient paramagnetic intermediates, and molecular modeling, we have demonstrated that (S)-ketoprofen exhibits stereoselective interaction with the peptide epimers. Furthermore, it was shown that the D-epimer of the peptide has a greater tendency to aggregation than the L-epimer. The stereoselective light-induced formation of the ketoprofen ketyl radicals provides a plausible mechanistic basis for ketoprofen's phototoxic side effects.

articles.title: Ab initio diabatic potential energy matrix for the lowest-lying singlet states of HCN responsible for collisional excitation/quenching of CN(X2Σ+/A2Π) with H.
articles.abstract: In hyperthermal chemistry, electronically excited cyano radicals (CN) are considered as a key radiative source in the shock boundary layer in front of supersonic (re)entry vehicles. To correctly model radiative heating in such extreme environments, it is necessary to understand collisional excitation and quenching rates. Although quenching of CN(A2Π) to CN(X2Σ+) with various collision partners has been investigated experimentally, a quantitative understanding of the nonadiabatic transitions in such electronically inelastic scattering has not been achieved. In this work, a full-dimensional diabatic potential energy matrix (DPEM) for the three lowest-lying singlet A' states of HCN, namely the 1 1A', 2 1A', and 3 1A' states, is developed based on multi-reference configuration interaction calculations. The DPEM provides valuable insights into the quenching/excitation of CN(X2Σ+/A2Π) via collisions with H in the singlet manifold.

articles.title: Base composition reflects RNA polymerase II displacement.
articles.abstract: RNA polymerase II (Pol II) transcribes all protein-coding and many non-protein-coding genes in the genome. Pol II transcription termination is crucial for RNA maturation and, when disrupted, can lead to altered RNA processing and RNA export. Termination involves two intertwined processes: RNA cleavage and Pol II release from the DNA (displacement). Despite its importance, the exact mechanisms underlying Pol II displacement from the DNA remain poorly understood. Moreover, under certain cellular stress conditions, there is a partial failure of cleavage, leading to a shift of the position of displacement further downstream, a phenomenon known as readthrough transcription. We present a systematic analysis of Pol II termination across cell types and species and provide novel insights into the mechanism of displacement. Using a probabilistic mixture model to quantify Pol II dynamics across entire gene bodies from nascent RNA sequencing data, we find that genes fall into two classes defined by conserved base composition patterns near the displacement site. Both classes share a T-rich region upstream of displacement, and one class additionally carries a GC-rich region surrounding displacement. We find that GC-rich predisplacement regions have more accessible chromatin and higher levels of phospho-threonine 4 on the CTD of Pol II. Additionally, we find that displacement at genes with only the upstream T-rich pattern are more likely to be affected by perturbations that alter displacement, including heat shock, viral infection, kinase inhibition, and arsenic treatment. Thus, our work identifies two types of Pol II displacement regions, which are differentially affected by perturbations of cellular homeostasis.

articles.title: Integrative computational simulations uncover the conformational activation pathway of AKT1 kinase.
articles.abstract: The AKT1 kinase, a central node in the PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling axis, governs critical cellular processes, including survival and proliferation, and its dysregulation drives cancer, diabetes, and neurodegeneration. While structural studies have resolved static snapshots of AKT1's inactive and active states, the dynamic mechanisms orchestrating its activation, particularly the coupling of phosphorylation-induced signals to catalytic competency, remain poorly resolved. This knowledge gap hinders the development of targeted therapies addressing AKT1's pathological hyperactivation. Using integrative computational approaches, we characterize the hierarchical conformational transitions enabling AKT1 activation at atomic resolution. Microsecond-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and nudged elastic band (NEB) pathway analyses reveal that phosphorylation at T308 initiates a metastable "pre-active" state, destabilizing autoinhibitory interactions at the PH-kinase interface. This triggers potential structural rearrangements: (1) A-loop opening exposes the hydrophobic motif for regulatory phosphorylation, (2) αC-helix rotation establishes the Lys179-Glu198 catalytic salt bridge, and (3) DFG motif flipping enables Asp292-Mg2+ coordination, completing the active site assembly. By mapping the energy landscape of AKT1 activation, this work bridges static structural data with dynamic mechanistic insights, offering a framework for therapeutic intervention against AKT1-driven pathologies.

articles.title: Prefrontal Ensembles Represent Freezing of Conspecifics.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
articles.abstract: Social buffering is a process in which the presence of other members of the same species (conspecifics) decreases stress reactions during threat exposure. In parallel, prior reports showed that groups of individuals display synchronous actions in nonthreatening situations. However, it is unknown if individuals also synchronize actions when facing threats. Prior studies showed social buffering of freezing in pairs of subjects. We now expand these findings and show social buffering of freezing during exposure to a predator and a shock grid in mice of both sexes in a larger group of four conspecifics. Furthermore, mice also displayed synchronized freezing. The presence of freezing synchrony suggests the existence of a neural representation of conspecific freezing. We reasoned that this encoding might be in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), as this region has been implicated in social behaviors and freezing. Strikingly, mPFC neural activity represented the average level of freezing across conspecifics. mPFC ensembles displayed differential encoding of self and conspecific freezing, and during predator exposure the mPFC encoded the number of conspecifics freezing and conspecific freezing bout duration. These data show, for the first time, neural representation of conspecific freezing and suggest that the mPFC may coordinate behavioral responses to threat across conspecifics.

articles.title: Akkermansia muciniphila attenuates macrophage efferocytosis to enhance anti-PD-1 efficacy in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer.
articles.abstract: Approximately 85% of colorectal cancers (CRCs) are microsatellite stable (MSS) and thus exhibit intrinsic resistance to anti-programmed death-1 (PD-1) therapy. In this study, we demonstrate that oral administration of Akkermansia muciniphila (Akk) suppresses tumorigenesis and reprograms the tumor microenvironment in MSS CRC mouse models. Akk attenuates macrophage efferocytosis through the TLR2/NF-κB pathway, an effect that leads to the accumulation of apoptotic cancer cells, which activates the cGAS-STING pathway and potentiates type I interferon production. This immunostimulatory cascade activates effector CD8+ T cells and enhances the response to anti-PD-1 therapy. We conducted a phase 1 trial (NCT06865521) combining Akk probiotics with PD-1 antibody in patients with metastatic MSS CRC after ≥1 prior line of therapy. The combination therapy was safe and achieved an objective response rate of 19%, with responders exhibiting enhanced antitumor immunity. Our multilevel investigation provides a promising strategy to overcome immunotherapy resistance in MSS CRC through targeted modulation of the gut microbiome.

articles.title: Sex-specific adaptations in placental mitochondrial biogenesis and function in babies born with critical congenital heart disease.
articles.abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is the leading cause of birth defects; most critical CHD (cCHD) newborns will develop neurodevelopmental disorders. Abnormal placental development may be involved, as genetics explains only 30% of sporadic CHD cases. Growing evidence suggests that placental dysfunction may result in heart and brain defects, as it shares a common early development. We hypothesized that newborns with cCHD exhibit sex-specific alterations in placental mitochondrial biogenesis and function, which may affect the fetal growth trajectory. Term placenta and paired umbilical cord (UC) blood were collected at birth from cCHD (n = 16) and matched control (n = 20) neonates. Mitochondrial lipid complex (phosphatidic acid (PA), phosphatidylglycerol (PG), and cardiolipin (CL)), acylcarnitine metabolites, and organic acids were determined in placenta by LC-MS/MS. Gene expressions of enzymes involved in mitochondrial biogenesis, dynamics, and lipid pathways were measured in the placenta by RT-qPCR. Placental protein expressions of β-oxidation and OXPHOS were determined by western blot. Mitochondrial dynamics were reduced in cCHD placentas, particularly in male infants. Long-chain acylcarnitine (LC-acar) metabolites decreased in female cCHD placentas and increased in males, while they increased in both sexes in UC plasma. Malonate levels increased in cCHD placentas, affecting the TCA cycle. CL de novo synthesis was dysregulated in the cCHD placentas, though CL concentrations were similar in both groups. The cCHD placenta may compensate for cardiac defects in a potential sex-dependent manner, leading to an accumulation of LC-acar in the UC plasma. Placental mitochondrial adaptation to metabolic needs may have cardioprotective and neuroprotective effects.

articles.title: Mechanism-specific acute silent ischaemic lesions and ischaemic periprocedural stroke after PTAS for severe symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis.
Impact of Trimetazidine on Echocardiographic Indices and Clinical Outcomes in Ischemic Cardiomyopathy: An Updated Meta-Analysis of Clinical Trials.
articles.abstract: Ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) is a major cause of chronic heart failure with impaired left ventricular (LV) function. This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate trimetazidine's effect in patients with ICM compared to standard therapy alone. A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, ProQuest, SAGE, EBSCO Host, Wiley, Science Direct, Springer link, Clinicaltrials.gov , EMBASE, WHO ICTRP databases until November 2024. Clinical trials assessing trimetazidine versus standard therapy in ICM were included. Data were analyzed using a random-effects model to calculate mean differences (MD) and relative risk (RR), with heterogeneity evaluated using the I 2 statistic. Twelve studies met the inclusion criteria. Trimetazidine significantly improved left ventricular ejection fraction (MD 6.35, 95% CI: 4.63- 8.07, p < 0.05, I2 = 69%), reduced LV end-systolic diameter (MD -4.51, 95% CI: -6.21- -2.81, p < 0.05, I2 = 56%), LV end-diastolic diameter (MD -3.13, 95% CI: -6.07- -0.18, p < 0.05, I2 = 86%), and LV end-systolic volume (MD -14.20, 95% CI: -21.19- -7.21, p < 0.05, I2 = 72%). There was no significant difference in left ventricular end-diastolic volume. Exercise capacity improved with a mean increase of 83.64 meters in the 6-minute walking test (MD 83.64, 95% CI: 22.88- 144.41, p < 0.05, I2 = 96%). NYHA class also improved (MD -0.80, 95% CI: -1.48- -0.12, p <0.05, I2 = 97%). Trimetazidine significantly reduced nitrate consumption (MD -2.76, 95% CI -3.84 to -1.68; I 2 = 95%), while its effect on anginal episodes was not significant (MD -1.52, 95% CI -4.49 to 1.46; I 2 = 99%) but became significant after excluding a study with an imputed standard deviation. Trimetazidine as an adjunct to standard therapy may improve cardiac function and exercise capacity in ischemic cardiomyopathy patients. The findings of this meta-analysis must be interpreted with caution due to high heterogeneity in some outcomes. Further large-scale trials are warranted to assess long-term outcomes such as mortality and hospitalization.

articles.title: Association of caregiver burden with the healthcare use and outcomes of older patients attending the ED.
Medical management of major incidents and mass casualty events during military operations: a consensus statement.
Multimodality Imaging-Guided Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation in a Hypoplastic Right Ventricle After Glenn Palliation.
articles.abstract: Adults with single-ventricle physiology increasingly survive into adulthood and may develop complex ventricular arrhythmias. A 44-year-old man with severe right ventricular hypoplasia and previous bidirectional Glenn palliation presented with sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia. Transthoracic and intracardiac echocardiography, computed tomography, and high-density electroanatomic mapping were combined to reconstruct the right-sided anatomy and to characterize the arrhythmogenic substrate. Intracardiac echocardiographic contours were merged with the electroanatomic map to build the geometry of the rudimentary right ventricle, in which extensive low-voltage areas were identified, with the latest and most fragmented late potentials confined to the anterior right ventricular outflow tract. Programmed stimulation did not induce ventricular tachycardia; however, pace mapping within the late-potential region reproduced the clinical QRS morphology with a stimulus-to-QRS interval of 153 milliseconds. Ablation was therefore guided by substrate homogenization, and a postablation high-density remap confirmed abolition of all late potentials. A subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was implanted before discharge.

articles.title: Novel Lung Perfusion Technique Quantifying Preferential Pulmonary Blood Flow in Fontan Patient With Scimitar Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with Fontan physiology have increased pulmonary perfusion heterogeneity compared with patients with normal hearts.

CASE SUMMARY: A 9-year-old girl with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, Scimitar syndrome, and unilateral right pulmonary vein stenosis underwent stent placement to relieve compression of the reimplanted right pulmonary vein after Fontan completion. Serial upper extremity lung perfusion scans demonstrated decreased right lung pulmonary blood flow despite cardiac catheterization demonstrating no in-stent stenosis and normal Fontan pressures. Pulmonary blood flow quantification was performed via separate upper (superior vena cava) and lower extremity (inferior vena cava) radioisotope injections staggered 2 days apart. The total differential pulmonary perfusion determined via this technique was 69.5% to the left lung and 30.5% to the right lung with significant contribution of right lung perfusion via the inferior vena cava.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: This case highlights the strengths and limitations of radioisotope imaging and provides a unique approach to more accurately evaluate pulmonary perfusion patterns in these complex patients.

articles.title: Peripheral microbial metabolites as indicators of gut microbiome disruption: systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Gut microbiome disruption is often characterized by the loss of obligately anaerobic bacteria, which may lead to altered production of microbial metabolites that can be detected peripherally. The application of widely used sequencing-based microbiome analyses to clinical settings is limited by cost, turnaround time, and challenges with patients with very low stool output. Since some products of strictly bacterial metabolism are detectable in blood, peripheral metabolites may provide a rapid and scalable indicator of gut microbiome composition and function. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies reporting circulating microbial metabolites and gut microbiome composition to evaluate whether peripheral microbial metabolites could identify gut microbiome perturbation. Candidate metabolites were identified systematically across an independent set of studies reporting metabolite-microbiome associations, enabling the assessment of reproducibility across disease states and cohorts. We performed a meta-analysis of 19 human cohorts comprising 3,242 participants with paired blood metabolite and stool microbiome data. Anaerobe depletion (obligate anaerobe relative abundance <0.70) was associated with decreased plasma concentration of products of anaerobic microbial metabolism. Combinations of metabolites distinguished individuals with anaerobe-depleted microbiomes from those without. Circulating metabolite levels distinguished between cases and controls with similar performance as gut microbiome composition across a range of health/disease states and changed markedly within patients experiencing gut anaerobe depletion after antibiotic exposure. Circulating microbial metabolites are potentially informative indicators of gut microbiome disruption and may serve as a rapid and scalable method for patient stratification in clinical trials or acute care settings.IMPORTANCECirculating microbial metabolites represent a practical and scalable approach to detecting significant gut microbiome disruption, particularly the loss of obligate anaerobes. Our findings suggest that metabolites capture compositional consequences of microbiome collapse, with performance comparable to direct microbiome profiling in distinguishing disease states. Enabling diagnostic enrichment and real-time monitoring of microbiome injury (e.g., during antibiotic use or critical illness) has potential implications for both clinical care and research, including the selection of patients for investigation of microbiome-targeted therapies. With further validation, circulating metabolites could provide an accessible surrogate for gut microbiome composition in settings where sequencing is impractical.

articles.title: Ten-eleven translocation 3 activates the TGF-β-like ligand Scube3 to promote renal fibrosis: mechanism and translational potential.
articles.abstract: Resident renal fibroblasts are a predominant source for myofibroblasts that produce ECM to contribute to renal fibrosis in the course of chronic kidney disease (CKD). The mechanism whereby fibroblast-myofibroblast transition (FMyT) is driven remains incompletely understood. In the present study, we investigated the involvement of ten-eleven translocation 3 (TET3) in regulating FMyT and renal fibrosis focusing on the regulatory mechanism and translational potential. We report that TET3 deletion in primary renal fibroblasts dampened myofibroblast transition in response to pro-fibrogenic stimuli. Consistently, conditional deletion of TET3 in quiescent fibroblasts (driven by the Col1a2-Cre) or in myofibroblasts (driven by the Postn-Cre) equally attenuated renal fibrosis in mice. Integrated transcriptomic analysis combining RNA-seq and CUT&Tag-seq uncovered signal peptide CUB-EGF-like domain-containing protein 3 (Scube3) as a novel downstream target for TET3. Co-culture assay confirmed that Scube3 mediated intercellular crosstalk and promoted fibroblast activation in an autocrine/paracrine manner. Importantly, myofibroblast-specific Scube3 depletion significantly ameliorated renal fibrosis in mice. Finally, a small-molecule TET3 degrader Bobcat339 suppressed FMyT in vitro and mitigated renal fibrosis in vivo. Our data support a role for TET3 in renal fibrosis and provide proof-of-concept that targeting the TET3-Scube3 axis may yield novel therapeutic solutions for treating CKD.

articles.title: Unveiling and regulating heterogeneous Li+ transport in 3D scaffolds: a gradient electrodeposition strategy toward ultralight and stable Li metal anodes.
articles.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) current collectors are widely explored to suppress lithium dendrite growth in Li metal anodes, particularly under high-current-density operation. Nevertheless, a fundamental mechanistic understanding of Li electrodeposition within such complex 3D architectures remains markedly incomplete. Herein, using a 3D Cu mesh as a model system, we demonstrate that intrinsic heterogeneity in Li+ transport within 3D architectures promotes localized ion-flux amplification, triggering preferential deposition and dendritic nucleation. Guided by this insight, a gradient-descending electrodeposition is proposed to regulate ion flux distribution, enabling dense, uniform, and strongly adherent bulk-like Li deposition. To mitigate the gravimetric penalty associated with conventional metallic scaffolds, an ultralight PET@Cu 3D current collector is further engineered via polymer metallization, achieving an areal mass reduction of 59.2% relative to the Cu mesh while retaining sufficient electrical conductivity and mechanical robustness. When integrated with the gradient deposition strategy, the resulting PET@Cu@G-Li anodes paired with NMC811 cathodes exhibit high-rate capability and exceptional cycling stability, retaining 90.82% of their initial capacity after 600 cycles at 3C. This work elucidates the critical role of mass-transport heterogeneity in Li electrodeposition within 3D frameworks and offers a practical anode design paradigm that reconciles high power density with high gravimetric energy density in Li metal batteries.

articles.title: Anesthetic Challenges in an Adult With Single-Ventricle Physiology and Incomplete Cavopulmonary Palliation Undergoing Noncardiac Interventions.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with single-ventricle physiology may present with complex forms rendering Fontan palliation impossible.

CASE SUMMARY: After multidisciplinary discussion, a 57-year-old man with a history of a right Glenn shunt and a left nonfunctional modified Blalock-Taussig shunt and left aortopulmonary collaterals for pulmonary atresia, hypoplastic right heart and discontinuous pulmonary arteries, required general anesthesia for noncardiac procedures. Intraoperatively, pulmonary blood flow was maintained by avoiding any increase in pulmonary vascular resistance and any reduction in cavopulmonary venous return on the right side and by maintaining systemic blood pressure and adequate cardiac output on the left side.

DISCUSSION: Although the long-term survival of patients with single-ventricle physiology without Fontan palliation is described, there is little known about their anesthetic management.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: The intraoperative management of patients not palliated with the Fontan must be tailored to the existing anatomy and physiology and carried out in collaboration with congenital cardiac anesthesiologists.

articles.title: Diagnostic contribution of anaerobic bottles in pediatric blood cultures: experience at a tertiary children's hospital.
articles.abstract: Routine use of anaerobic bottles in pediatric blood cultures remains controversial because diagnostic yield must be balanced against limited sampling volume. We retrospectively analyzed paired pediatric aerobic-anaerobic blood cultures collected from patients younger than 18 years at a tertiary children's hospital from January 2020 through December 2024. Accession-defined paired sets received within 15 min were grouped into culture episodes; episodes containing at least two paired sets comprised the primary cohort. Among 24,485 multi-set episodes from 8,658 patients, 999 (4.1%) were positive, and 387 (1.6%) were potential-contaminant episodes. Confirmed anaerobic-bottle contribution was observed in 208 positive episodes (20.8%), comprising additional organism recovery in 159 (15.9%) and detection more than 4 h earlier in 49 (4.9%); the absolute added yield was 8.5 per 1,000 episodes. Obligate anaerobes were identified in 11 positive episodes, whereas the majority of the contribution came from facultative organisms, particularly Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, and viridans group streptococci. Contribution was highest in the emergency room (28.2%) and neonatal intensive care unit (25.0%). Compared with the general ward, adjusted odds were higher in the emergency room (adjusted odds ratio, 1.83; 95% confidence interval, 1.23 to 2.73) and lower in the hemato-oncology ward (0.43; 0.21 to 0.85). Contribution was 21.8% among children younger than 4 years. The overall median within-accession time-to-positivity difference (anaerobic minus Peds Plus/F) was small (-0.17 h), although selected organisms showed earlier anaerobic detection. Anaerobic bottles provided complementary diagnostic information in approximately one-fifth of positive pediatric blood culture episodes, mainly through additional recovery rather than uniformly earlier detection.IMPORTANCEChildren often have only a small amount of blood available for culture, making the choice of culture bottles important. In this hospital-wide study, anaerobic bottles added diagnostic information in about one-fifth of positive pediatric blood culture episodes, mainly by recovering organisms that were not found in the paired pediatric aerobic bottle. Most of this benefit involved common bloodstream pathogens that can grow with or without oxygen, including Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, rather than rare obligate anaerobes. A similar overall contribution proportion was observed among children younger than 4 years. However, the pediatric aerobic bottle recovered more organisms overall in direct paired comparisons. These findings support viewing the two bottle types as complementary and emphasize that pediatric blood culture practice should balance adequate total blood volume with thoughtful allocation between bottle types.

articles.title: Junctional Rhythm as Reversible Driver of Fontan Failure: Recovery With Multimodal Therapy Including Atrial Pacing.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In Fontan circulation, pulmonary blood flow depends on low atrial pressure and preserved atrioventricular (AV) synchrony. AV dyssynchrony as a driver of Fontan failure and Fontan-associated liver disease remains under-recognized.

CASE SUMMARY: A 17-year-old boy with Fontan failure, Fontan-associated liver disease, portal hypertension, and effusions had elevated Fontan pressures despite subaortic obstruction relief and Fontan tunnel stenting. Invasive pressure tracings identified junctional rhythm with AV dyssynchrony. Epicardial atrial pacing, preserving AV conduction and avoiding ventricular pacing, normalized Fontan pressures with clinical improvement and a reduction in liver stiffness.

DISCUSSION: In patients with failing Fontan circulation and junctional rhythm, restoring AV synchrony by atrial pacing may reverse Fontan hypertension and improve end-organ congestion.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Junctional rhythm should be considered a reversible contributor to elevated Fontan pressures before attributing failure to anatomy. Atrial pacing, when AV conduction is intact, can improve Fontan hemodynamics and hepatic congestion while avoiding ventricular pacing.

articles.title: Diagnostic challenges in Mycobacterium abscessus pulmonary disease, particularly in patients with cystic fibrosis: toward an integrated precision framework.
articles.abstract: Mycobacterium abscessus has emerged as one of the most formidable pathogens affecting people with cystic fibrosis (pwCF), driven by intrinsic antimicrobial resistance, complex taxonomy, and substantial diagnostic uncertainty. Despite major technological advances, establishing a diagnosis of pulmonary disease remains challenging, as traditional culture-based workflows are constrained by limited sensitivity, prolonged turnaround times. However, recent progress in proteomic and genomic technologies has markedly improved organism detection and taxonomic resolution. This review examines the contemporary diagnostic architecture for M. abscessus pulmonary infection in pwCF, identifying persistent gaps, and proposes a precision-oriented framework in which culture, proteomics, genomics, and host-response biomarkers converge to support earlier and more individualized clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Determinant Factors From Transvaginal Ultrasonography for the Intervention of Retained Products of Conception: A Retrospective Analysis of 61 Cases.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to retrospectively analyze the determining factors for intervention in patients with retained products of conception (RPOC).

METHODS: We included 61 patients diagnosed with RPOC at our institute from January 2018 to May 2024. Interventions were performed for postpartum hemorrhage in 18 patients (intervention group), while the remaining 43 patients were observed until spontaneous resolution occurred (non-intervention group). The maximal dimension of RPOC (size) and blood flow were assessed using transvaginal ultrasonography before the intervention (median, 23.5 days postpartum) in the intervention group and at the 1-month check-up in the non-intervention group. Color Doppler profiles were evaluated for the degree of vascularity using the Gutenberg classification (types 0 to 3). A logistic regression analysis was used to compare the background and ultrasonographic findings of the maximal dimension of RPOC and Gutenberg classification with the requirement for intervention.

RESULTS: The multivariate analysis showed significant differences in the maximal dimension of RPOC (P=0.002) and the Gutenberg classification (P=0.005). The receiver operating characteristics curve for predicting the requirement for intervention, based on the maximal dimension of RPOC and the Gutenberg classification, showed a cut-off of 41 mm and type 1, with areas under the curve of 0.86 (95% confidence interval, 0.75-0.98) and 0.80 (0.69-0.90), respectively. Using a simple prediction model (the maximal dimension of RPOC [mm]×0.1+ [Gutenberg classification] ×2) with a cut-off value of 7.3, the prediction showed a higher area under the curve (0.94, 0.89-0.99) than individual parameters.

CONCLUSION: The combination of the maximal dimension of RPOC and the blood flow profile according to the Gutenberg classification effectively predicts the requirement for intervention.

articles.title: A commensal-derived sugar protects against obesity by regulating immunometabolism.
articles.abstract: Obesity is a worsening global epidemic that is partially regulated by the microbiota through unknown factors. We discovered a human commensal bacterium, Clostridium immunis, which prevents and treats obesity in mice by secreting a phosphocholine-modified exopolysaccharide. Loss- and gain-of-function bacterial mutants involving the phosphocholine biosynthesis locus (licABC) revealed that the phosphocholine moiety is required to protect against metabolic disease. This C. immunis exopolysaccharide decreases small-intestinal and visceral fat levels of IL-22, which increases metabolic activity specifically in visceral adipose tissue; C. immunis lacks activity against obesity when IL-22 or group 3 innate lymphoid cells, predominant secretors of IL-22, are absent. Importantly, phosphocholine biosynthesis genes are less abundant in humans with obesity or hypertriglyceridemia, suggesting conserved functions of bacterial phosphocholine. These results define a bacterial molecule-and its key structural motif-that provides immunometabolic control of obesity. More broadly, they highlight a clinically translatable strategy to reduce visceral fat.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics of Patients With Fontan Circulation and Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia: A Case Series From the SV-ONE Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a rare genetic disorder associated with chronic respiratory disease. In single-ventricle palliation, pulmonary blood flow is driven in part by inspiratory effort and is critically dependent on low pulmonary vascular resistance. The coexistence of PCD and Fontan physiology is uncommon, and outcomes remain poorly defined.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective case series of patients with Fontan physiology and reported PCD within the multi-institutional Single-Ventricle Outcomes Network registry.

RESULTS: Among 1,535 patients with Fontan, only 5 had reported PCD. Median age at Fontan completion was 3 years, with a median follow-up of 7 years. Following Fontan, 2 patients developed chylous pleural effusions. No patient developed plastic bronchitis or protein-losing enteropathy.

CONCLUSIONS: In this case series, Fontan completion was only achieved in a small cohort of patients with reported PCD. These findings emphasize the need for multidisciplinary collaboration to appropriately describe, address, and manage multiorgan comorbidities.

articles.title: Overcoming Social and Financial Barriers to Guideline-Directed Fontan Care.
articles.abstract:
TOPIC: Adults with Fontan circulation require lifelong specialized care, yet social and financial barriers frequently interfere with implementation of guideline-directed management. Advanced practice providers (APPs) practicing in adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) programs are uniquely positioned to identify these barriers through longitudinal relationships and coordinate multidisciplinary interventions that preserve continuity of care.

DISCUSSION SUMMARY: An adult with Fontan circulation developed recurrent atrial fibrillation during prolonged insurance instability, resulting in medication rationing and delayed surveillance. Through routine clinic visits and scheduled longitudinal follow-up, the ACHD APP recognized that interrupted care reflected barriers to access rather than nonadherence. Coordination with electrophysiology, social work, legal advocacy, medication assistance programs, and ACHD physicians allowed the care team to individualize the timing of interventions while preserving guideline-directed management and continuity of specialty care.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Adults with Fontan circulation often require multidisciplinary solutions to overcome barriers to care. The ACHD APP can serve as the clinical hub that identifies barriers, coordinates resources, and helps sustain guideline-directed management.

articles.title: Management and Outcomes of Acute Coronary Syndrome during and after the COVID-19 Pandemic in Kurume City: A Multicenter Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic on acute coronary syndrome (ACS) care has varied widely across regions. Data from stable regional healthcare systems remain limited, particularly regarding potential delayed effects after the acute pandemic phase.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, population-based observational study of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)-treated ACS in Kurume City, Japan, across three periods: pre-pandemic (2019), pandemic (2020-2021), and post-restriction (2022). PCI data were collected from all four PCI-capable hospitals in the region. The primary endpoint was in-hospital mortality among ACS patients. Secondary endpoints included ACS subtype distribution and use of mechanical circulatory support (MCS).

RESULTS: A total of 4,694 PCI procedures were performed between 2019 and 2022, including 1,692 for ACS. Annual PCI volume and the proportion performed for ACS (34.1%-38.6%) remained stable. The proportion of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction was higher in 2020 and remained elevated in 2022 compared with 2019 (p=0.015). In-hospital mortality among ACS patients was comparable during the pandemic years but increased significantly in 2022 (7.4% vs 2.3%-4.0%; p=0.0006), even after excluding post-cardiac arrest syndrome. Rates of MCS use did not differ significantly across years. Emergency medical transport times increased modestly.

CONCLUSION: In this regional healthcare system, the COVID-19 pandemic did not substantially disrupt emergent coronary revascularization or worsen short-term outcomes of PCI-treated ACS during the acute phase. However, in-hospital mortality increased in the post-restriction period, suggesting delayed cardiovascular consequences of the pandemic.

articles.title: Pilot Study Investigating the Safety and Efficacy of Metallic Stent Insertion for Ileocolonic Anastomotic Strictures Related to Crohn's Disease: A Study Protocol.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Lower gastrointestinal tract stenoses are commonly treated with surgery or endoscopic balloon dilation. We conducted a clinical trial to investigate a novel endoscopic treatment called radial incision and cutting (RIC). Although RIC has demonstrated a high technical success rate and has been shown to improve subjective symptoms, the relatively high rate of delayed bleeding in cases of ileocolonic anastomotic strictures due to Crohn's disease (CD) can be problematic. Herein, we report the design of a prospective, single-center, single-arm, exploratory pilot study to evaluate safety and feasibility of self-expandable metallic stent (SEMS) placement as an alternative dilation strategy for ileocolonic anastomotic strictures in CD, particularly in patients in whom delayed bleeding after RIC has been a clinical concern.

METHODS: The major inclusion criteria include age 18-80 years, ileocolonic anastomotic strictures after surgery for CD, and a history of endoscopic balloon dilation or RIC for such strictures. We will employ a SEMS designed for malignant biliary stenosis and conduct SEMS placement in five participants. The primary outcome is the safety of SEMS placement, assessed by determining the frequency of adverse events of special interest, including delayed bleeding and perforation. The secondary outcomes include the technical success rate of SEMS placement, procedure duration, improvement in subjective symptoms, SEMS migration rate, success rate of SEMS removal 1 week after placement, and duration of hospitalization. Subjective symptom improvement is evaluated using the visual analog scale, and long-term results are analyzed using descriptive statistics, Student's t-test, and Kaplan-Meier curves.

CONCLUSION: This exploratory study provides useful information regarding the safety of SEMS placement for ileocolonic anastomotic strictures due to CD, which may contribute to further investigation.

articles.title: From pressure to prognosis: establishing a common language for portal hypertension in advanced chronic liver disease.
Warfarin-Aspirin Therapy in Congenitally Corrected Transposition of the Great Arteries After Lateral Tunnel Fontan.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fontan circulation carries high risk of thromboembolic complications, and optimal anticoagulation strategies in pediatric patients remain controversial.

CASE SUMMARY: A 13-year-old adolescent boy with dextrocardia, congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries, ventricular septal defect, and pulmonary stenosis underwent staged surgical palliation including a bidirectional Glenn shunt followed by the lateral tunnel Fontan procedure. Postoperative echocardiography demonstrated a functioning Fontan circulation with reduced right ventricular systolic dysfunction and mild-to-moderate tricuspid regurgitation. The patient developed postoperative tachycardia (heart rate ∼150 beats/min), for which oral digoxin was initiated during hospitalization. Given the prothrombotic nature of Fontan physiology, long-term anticoagulation with warfarin, along with aspirin, was commenced, and over time, no thromboembolic events occurred during 6-month follow-up.

DISCUSSION: Patients with systemic right ventricles and Fontan physiology represent a high-risk subgroup for thrombosis. Individualized anticoagulation strategies are essential.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Warfarin, along with aspirin, can be safely implemented in selected patients with high-risk Fontan.

articles.title: Correction to: Educational level, mediators, and risk of atrial fibrillation by sex in The Tromsø Study 1994-2016.
Global trends in key modifiable cardiovascular risk factors: a joinpoint analysis across WHO regions (1990-2022).
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To examine temporal trends and quantify changes in prevalence of major cardiovascular disease risk factors (hypertension, tobacco use, elevated cholesterol, diabetes mellitus, and insufficient physical activity) across World Health Organization (WHO) regions.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Analysis of WHO Global Health Observatory, a global database compiling health indicators from over 190 countries. Prevalence (%) estimates were extracted for key modifiable Cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk factors from 1990 to 2022. Joinpoint regression analyses were conducted to calculate the annual percentage change (APC) for each segment identified to have a change in trend and the average annual percentage change (AAPC) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) across the entire time trend. Global trends in CVD risk factors showed mixed patterns. Hypertension prevalence declined in most regions, with the greatest reduction in Europe (AAPC = -1.54, 95% CI: -1.55, -1.53), whilst the Western Pacific showed a slight increase (AAPC = 0.10, 95% CI: 0.08, 0.12). Tobacco use decreased across all regions, most markedly in South-East Asia (AAPC = -3.50, 95% CI: -3.56, -3.43), from 54.1% to 26.6%. Total cholesterol declined modestly in several regions, but increased slightly in the Western Pacific (AAPC = 0.25, 95% CI: 0.07, 0.43). Diabetes prevalence increased across all regions, highest in the Eastern Mediterranean (AAPC = 2.58, 95% CI: 2.57, 2.59) and lowest in Africa (AAPC = 1.58, 95% CI: 1.55, 1.61). Insufficient physical activity also increased in five regions, Africa being the only exception (AAPC = -1.10, 95% CI: -1.19, -1.01).

CONCLUSION: Global trends in CVD risk factors show improvements in hypertension, tobacco use, and cholesterol, but worsening diabetes and insufficient physical activity, highlighting the need for region-specific strategies that drive sustainable, system-level change in modifiable risks.

articles.title: Comprehensive Cardiac Assessment and Assisted Reproductive Technology Considerations in a Long-Lost Patient With Fontan Circulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women with Fontan physiology (modified World Health Organization class III-IV) increasingly pursue pregnancy while assisted reproductive technology in this physiology adds additional hemodynamic and thrombotic risks.

CASE SUMMARY: A 29-year-old woman with tricuspid atresia palliated by a 22-mm extracardiac Fontan, lost to cardiology follow-up since age 15, was referred by her reproductive endocrinology and infertility specialist before assisted reproductive technology. Right heart catheterization, cardiac magnetic resonance, ambulatory monitoring, stress echocardiography, and laboratory testing showed a well-compensated Fontan without high-risk features. Prophylactic enoxaparin was started with ovarian stimulation and held briefly for oocyte retrieval; a comprehensive pregnancy heart team managed her care and followed her closely.

DISCUSSION: The case illustrates failed pediatric-to-adult transition, Fontan-specific preconception evaluation before assisted reproduction, and the importance of a multidisciplinary pregnancy team.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Women with Fontan physiology considering pregnancy, with and without assisted reproductive technology, warrant preconception pregnancy heart team evaluation and individualized thromboprophylaxis; lapse in transition is a modifiable driver of late presentation.

articles.title: Effect of dietary counselling on educational disparities in cardiometabolic health from childhood to adulthood.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: We examined whether parental education was associated with long-term cardiometabolic health and whether the effectiveness of a dietary counselling intervention differed by parental education level, hypothesizing greater effectiveness among highly educated families.

METHODS AND RESULTS: The study comprised 839 participants from the Special Turku Coronary Risk Factor Intervention Project (STRIP), in which the intervention group (n = 417) received individualized dietary counselling during 20 years, while the control group (n = 422) received routine care. Parental education was categorized as low, average, or high at study baseline. Outcomes were assessed repeatedly over 26 years and included dietary intakes, adiposity and metabolic regulation, lipid profile, and blood pressure (BP). Mixed-effects regression models tested the main effects of education and education-by-intervention interactions on outcome trajectories. Higher parental education was associated with higher intake of dietary fibre and lower intake of saturated fatty acids throughout adolescence and early adulthood, as well as with more favourable body mass index (22.5 vs. 24.2 kg/m2 in the high vs. low education groups), homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (1.6 vs. 1.8, respectively), and HDL cholesterol levels (1.4 vs. 1.3 mmol/L) in adulthood. No significant associations were observed for other lipid outcomes or BP. No consistent education-by-intervention interactions were observed for the dietary and cardiometabolic trajectories (interaction P-values > 0.05, except isolated findings for dietary cholesterol and systolic BP). Sensitivity analyses with parental occupational status replicated these findings.

CONCLUSION: Contrary to the study hypothesis, this study suggests no differential effects of the intervention across educational groups.

REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT00223600, https://www.clinicaltrials.gov.

articles.title: Loneliness, unhealthy lifestyle, and incident cardiometabolic disease among middle-aged and older adults across 33 countries: a multicohort study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Loneliness is common in ageing population, we aim to identify the association between loneliness and cardiometabolic disease (CMD) across diverse settings, particularly cardiometabolic multimorbidity, and investigate whether unhealthy lifestyles and socioeconomic status (SES) help explain or amplify their relationships.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Data were obtained from six cohort studies across 33 countries, including the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA), Health and Retirement Study (HRS), Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE), Korean Longitudinal Study of Aging (KLoSA), and Mexican Health and Aging Study (MHAS). Eligible participants were aged 45 years or older. We applied time-varying Cox mixed-effects regression models to evaluate the association between loneliness and incident cardiometabolic diseases. The mediation role of unhealthy lifestyles and the joint effects of socioeconomic status, unhealthy lifestyles, and loneliness on incident cardiometabolic disease outcomes were also explored. Among 81 978 participants, with a median follow-up of 5 years, 15 750 participants developed CMD. Loneliness was associated with higher risk of any CMD (aHR 1.23, [95% CI: 1.20, 1.26]), with a stronger association for multimorbidity (aHR 1.48, [95% CI: 1.37, 1.60]) than for single CMD (aHR 1.18, [95% CI: 1.15, 1.22]). Unhealthy lifestyles mediated 5.19% (95% CI: 3.06, 7.64) of the association with any CMD. Individuals experiencing a combination of low SES, multiple unhealthy lifestyle factors, and loneliness demonstrated the greatest cardiometabolic disease risk (adjusted HR: 1.89, [95% CI: 1.76, 2.02]).

CONCLUSION: Building on prior evidence that has largely come from single-cohort studies, our findings highlighted loneliness as a global risk factor in predicting the incident CMD, particularly cardiometabolic multimorbidity. The highest risk was observed among socioeconomically disadvantaged individuals with multiple unhealthy lifestyles. These findings underscore the needs to address the combined risk of socioeconomic disadvantage, loneliness, and unhealthy lifestyle in multicomponent health interventions.

articles.title: Rapid strengthening and reversal of hippocampal-neocortical interplay mediates human memory formation.
articles.abstract: Classical theories of systems consolidation highlight the importance of hippocampal-neocortical interplay for long-term memory formation. However, how this interaction evolves during multiple days of learning remains unclear. Using day-by-day multisite intracranial electrophysiology, we examined human subjects performing a repeated picture-learning task. From day 1 today 2, the ripple rates during picture learning and free recall significantly increased in the hippocampus and neocortex, which correlated with behavioral memory performance. These enhancements persisted throughout the remaining task days. Notably, from day 2 onward, the ripple coupling between the neocortex and hippocampus not only strengthened, but the temporal sequence of these coupled ripples also reversed-from hippocampus leading to neocortex leading. This rapid strengthening and reversal of hippocampal-neocortical information flow on the second day represents a key signature of human memory formation.

articles.title: Fontan Procedure-Associated Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Complications of a Lifesaving Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fontan surgery is lifesaving for infants with single-ventricle physiology by creating a venocaval bypass tract with the pulmonary arteries; it allows the functioning single ventricle to be used for the systemic circulation. It has been hypothesized that long-standing Fontan circulation increases the risk of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).

CASE SUMMARY: A 34-year-old man with tricuspid atresia type 1A after having undergone Fontan surgery 30 years prior presented with a parietal-occipital hematoma after multiple falls, requiring emergent drainage. Computed tomography of the abdomen revealed diffuse metastatic lesions with significantly elevated alpha-fetoprotein levels, concerning for HCC. He was discharged to inpatient hospice care.

DISCUSSION: The association between Fontan physiology and HCC highlights the importance of early screening of complications to prevent future morbidity and mortality.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: This case offers insight on the importance of monitoring for systemic complications of Fontan patients, and it underscores the need for multidisciplinary collaboration and for a standardized screening protocol.

articles.title: Vascular divide: how the portal milieu shapes neutrophil activation and remote organ damage.
Chronic kidney disease in cirrhosis: a study of inpatients from a global perspective.
Transcatheter Management of Native Aortic Root Thrombus After Fontan Palliation in a Pediatric Patient With COVID-19.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary native aortic root thrombus is a rare complication after single-ventricle palliation.

CASE SUMMARY: We describe a case of a pediatric patient with a single ventricle who developed a native aortic root thrombus and coronary artery thrombi after undergoing Fontan palliation and following COVID-19 infection. This report describes the transcatheter techniques employed to manage the thrombi, as well as the management of an unexpected complication involving thrombus embolization to the left common iliac artery.
