DISCUSSION: Native aortic root thrombus and coronary artery thrombi in single-ventricle patients are potentially fatal events that require urgent intervention. Transcatheter procedures for thrombus resolution are inherently high risk and demand meticulous risk-reduction strategies.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Risk of thrombotic complications may be higher in Fontan patients with COVID-19 infection. Timely use of high-risk procedural strategies in a single-ventricle patient with intracardiac and coronary artery thrombosis may be necessary to avoid lethal complications.

articles.title: Tryptophan depletion generates hyper-reactive portal neutrophils in alcoholic liver disease.
Strategic Multidisciplinary Management of Aortic Dissection in Fontan Survivors: From Emergency Rescue to Proactive Prevention.
Multidisciplinary Treatment for a Fontan Patient With Acute Aortic Dissection and Left Coronary Artery Occlusion.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute aortic dissection complicated by coronary malperfusion is a life-threatening emergency. Although aortic root degeneration is a well-recognized complication in adults with congenital heart disease, aortic dissection causing external compression of the left main coronary artery is rare and requires prompt intervention.

CASE SUMMARY: A 36-year-old man with a surgical history of Fontan palliation presented with severe chest pain. He was diagnosed with acute aortic dissection with coronary occlusion by coronary angiography and computed tomography. A staged multidisciplinary strategy was undertaken: emergent percutaneous coronary intervention with left main trunk stent placement, followed by surgical aortic root replacement with a mechanical valve. The patient was discharged uneventfully.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights progressive aortopathy after Fontan palliation and the importance of multidisciplinary management.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Multidisciplinary management is effective to treat acute aortic dissection complicated by coronary occlusion in complex patients with multiple prior surgeries for congenital heart disease.

articles.title: Stage-dependent gut microbiome and functional signatures across the liver disease spectrum: an integrative multicohort study.
Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation in a Fontan Patient With Myelodysplastic Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adults with single-ventricle congenital heart disease with Fontan palliation can present with associated hematologic malignancies, with complex care implications.

CASE SUMMARY: We present the case of a 23-year-old woman with univentricular heart disease after Fontan palliation with myelodysplastic syndrome who underwent allogenic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT).

DISCUSSION: Fontan circulation leads to a delicate physiology that is susceptible to notable hemodynamic imbalances in a variety of clinical scenarios. HSCT is associated with significant hemodynamic sequelae and carries a significant risk of infection, fluid overload, and medication toxicity that may be potentiated by Fontan physiology.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: We recommend a multidisciplinary approach for decision-making and management with appropriate risk mitigation strategies for patients with Fontan physiology undergoing chemotherapy and HSCT.

articles.title: Steatosis grade and cardiometabolic burden as determinants of hepatocellular carcinoma risk after hepatitis C cure in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
The promise and pitfalls of psychosocial data in cardiovascular prevention: reply to Taha Bhatti.
Strengthening methodological approaches, co-design, and interdisciplinary collaborations for cardiovascular disease and stroke prevention interventions.
The promise and pitfalls of psychosocial data in cardiovascular prevention.
Educational level, mediators, and risk of atrial fibrillation by sex in The Tromsø Study 1994-2016.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To study the association between socioeconomic position (SEP), indicated by educational level, and incident atrial fibrillation (AF), and the role of lifestyle and cardiovascular risk factors as potential mediators in the causal pathway.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Using education as indicator for SEP, we examined the association with AF and the mediation by body mass index, hypertension, smoking, alcohol, and physical activity. Our sample included 25 796 adult women and men from a population-based cohort study with median follow-up of 22 years (1994-2016). Total effect, natural direct effect (not through mediators), and natural indirect effect (through mediators) hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using a counterfactual-based natural-effects model. Total effect of education on AF was small, and only significant for women with upper secondary as compared with primary education (19% lower hazard, 95% confidence interval 4%, 32%). All natural direct effect HRs were non-significant but suggesting increased risk by higher educational level. Compared with women with primary education, natural indirect effect hazard was 11% (4%, 17%) lower in women with upper secondary education, 18% (7%, 28%) lower in women with university/college education <4 years and 25% (12%, 34%) lower in women with university/college ≥4 years. In men, however, natural indirect effect did not differ between the levels of education.

CONCLUSION: We found protective indirect effect of education on AF through lifestyle and cardiovascular risk factors in women, but not in men. The direct effect in both women and men indicated increased risk by higher education, although non-significant.

articles.title: Cardiovascular disease and stroke prevention educational-behavioural programmes for culturally and/or linguistically diverse communities: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To identify the types of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and stroke prevention educational-behavioural programmes for people from culturally and/or linguistically diverse (CALD) backgrounds and investigate their effect on CVD risk factors and disease knowledge.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Four electronic databases were searched from inception to September 2023. Mean difference (MD) and standardized MD was calculated using random effects model, and heterogeneity were assessed using the I2 statistic. Studies that were not included in the meta-analysis were narratively described. The Cochrane Risk of Bias tool and Joana Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal checklist were used to assess the quality of the included studies. Sixteen studies originating from USA and UK (4 RCTs and 12 quasi-experimental pre-post studies) with n = 2331 participants (mean age 57.2 years, 50% women) were included. The programmes were multi-component, 15 of which were culturally adapted and 1 was co-designed. Most were delivered face-to-face in groups. In contrast to the results among the pre-post studies, the pooled analysis showed that educational-behavioural programmes may have little to no effect on SBP (MD 1.18 mmHg, 95% CI -2.42 to 4.79) and HbA1c (MD -0.29%, 95% CI -0.89 to 0.32). The results for LDL cholesterol, BMI, physical activity and dietary intake were also mixed except for CVD or stroke knowledge which demonstrated statistically significant improvements after the intervention.

CONCLUSION: The effect of educational-behavioural programmes on CVD risk factors is inconclusive but may improve CVD or stroke knowledge. Co-designing programmes underpinned by behaviour change theories/techniques with stakeholders and target CALD communities may enhance their potential impact. Future studies should use more rigorous study design i.e. RCTs, valid and reliable outcome measures to reduce inherent bias and strengthen the evidence base for the effectiveness of these programmes.

articles.title: Socio-economic status, cardiovascular risk factors, and coronary atherosclerosis: a SCOT-HEART trial analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To investigate the relationship between socio-economic status, plaque burden on coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA), management, and outcomes.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In a post-hoc analysis of a multi-centre randomized control trial, we assessed associations between socio-economic status and qualitative (stenosis and adverse plaque characteristics) and quantitative (total plaque, calcified plaque, non-calcified, and low attenuation) CCTA plaque features and examined the interaction of socio-economic status on cardiovascular outcomes. Socio-economic status was available in 3948 participants of whom 1989 were randomized to CCTA and 1629 scans were suitable and available for quantitative plaque analysis. Within these 1629 participants, 15% were from the lowest socio-economic quintile and 25% from the highest socio-economic quintile. Participants in the most deprived socio-economic group were younger, had lower cardiovascular risk, and were less likely to have severe stenosis or multi-vessel disease. After adjustment for cardiovascular risk factors, there was no difference in quantitative plaque burden between socio-economic groups. After a median of 4.75 years of follow-up, CCTA-guided management was associated with similar changes in medical therapy, similar reductions in the risk of coronary heart disease death, or non-fatal myocardial infarction in low and high socio-economic groups, with no difference between the base and interaction models (P = 0.35).

CONCLUSION: Socio-economic status is not an independent predictor of coronary artery disease severity; rather, the association is mostly determined by modifiable risk factors. Preventive therapies, guided by CCTA, achieve similar benefits in both low and high socio-economic status individuals.

articles.title: Ticagrelor in the Emergency Treatment of Acute Coronary Syndromes: A Comprehensive Clinical Review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVE: Acute Coronary Syndromes (ACS) - encompassing STEMI and NSTEACS - remain among the foremost causes of cardiovascular mortality worldwide. Ticagrelor, the first reversibly binding, direct-acting oral P2Y12 antagonist, has demonstrated superior efficacy over clopidogrel in landmark trials and carries a Class I recommendation in current international guidelines. This review provides a comprehensive, evidence-based appraisal of ticagrelor's pharmacology, clinical efficacy, safety, and decision- making guidance in the emergency management of ACS.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Web of Science were searched from January 2005 to May 2026. A narrative synthesis prioritised meta-analyses, systematic reviews, and randomised controlled trials, including PLATO, ISAR-REACT 5, TWILIGHT, TICO, PEGASUS-TIMI 54, and GLOBAL LEADERS, alongside the 2023 ESC and 2025 ACC/AHA guidelines.

RESULTS: Ticagrelor significantly reduced cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, and stroke versus clopidogrel (HR 0.84; p < 0.001) with a concomitant all-cause mortality benefit. Ticagrelor monotherapy after short dual antiplatelet therapy reduced major bleeding without increasing ischaemic events. Extended ticagrelor (60 mg twice daily) beyond 12 months reduced recurrent events in high-risk post-myocardial infarction patients. Plaque erosion pathobiology and neutrophil extracellular trap attenuation identify contexts in which ticagrelor may confer additional benefit.

DISCUSSION: Regimen selection requires integrating the culprit lesion phenotype, a two-axis ischaemichaemorrhagic risk framework, and an assessment of contraindications, drug interactions, and special populations, including elderly patients, those with renal impairment, and those requiring oral anticoagulation.

CONCLUSION: Ticagrelor offers potent, reversible platelet inhibition with a favourable efficacy-safety balance across the ACS spectrum. Individualised, phenotype-guided therapy optimises outcomes and minimises harm.

articles.title: Beta-Amino Alcohols as Key Frameworks in Drug Discovery: A Review of Medicinal Applications and Biological Profiles.
articles.abstract: Beta-Amino alcohols, as pivotal frameworks in organic and medicinal chemistry, play a prominent role in drug design and development. This comprehensive review evaluates the therapeutic potential of β-amino alcohols, highlighting their significance in the management of a broad spectrum of human pathologies, including cancer, bacterial infections, malaria, and viral diseases. Furthermore, the efficacy of these molecules in cardiovascular, respiratory, and ocular disorders is assessed. Alongside their therapeutic applications, the epoxide ring-opening process, the primary and most established synthetic pathway for constructing β-amino alcohol cores, is critically discussed and integrated with structure activity relationship (SAR) insights to demonstrate how specific chemical modifications dictate pharmacological potency. The consolidated findings reveal that β-amino alcohols exert their therapeutic effects through diverse molecular mechanisms. These pathways encompass the suppression of malignant cell proliferation, potent bactericidal activity against resistant Staphylococcus aureus strains, inhibition of Plasmodium species in malaria, targeting the main protease (Mpro) of SARS-CoV-2 for COVID-19 therapeutics, and functioning as dual-binding cholinesterase inhibitors for Alzheimer's disease management. Additionally, these derivatives have been reported to modulate adrenergic receptors, highlighting their potential relevance to cardiovascular, respiratory, and ocular therapeutic research, including conditions such as hypertension, asthma, and glaucoma. Overall, this review provides an up-to-date analysis of β-amino alcohol-based therapeutic applications and offers a new perspective on the potential role of these compounds in modern medicinal chemistry, which may contribute to the rational design of novel drug candidates.

articles.title: Functionalization of Carbon Nanotubes with 5‑Phenylvaleryl, Pentadecanoyl, and Adipoyl Chloride: Synthesis and Spectroscopic Surface Analysis Toward Biomarker Sensing.
articles.abstract: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) were covalently modified with aromatic (5-phenylvaleryl, 5PC), long-chain aliphatic (pentadecanoyl, PDC), and oxygen-rich/carboxylated (adipoyl, ACC) chemistries to create a tunable surface interface for detecting volatile and semivolatile chemical biomarkers. Following oxidative activation, 3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane (APTES) amination, and acyl-chloride coupling, successful attachment and differentiation of linker classes were evaluated using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS), and C KLL Auger analysis. Distinct spectroscopic fingerprints corresponding to aromatic, aliphatic, and oxygenated functionalities were resolved despite the intrinsically carbon-rich substrate. These orthogonal signatures provide a compact quality-control strategy for CNT functionalization and establish a framework for correlating surface chemistry with predicted analyte interactions, including aromatic interactions, nonpolar adsorption, and acid-base or hydrogen-bond pairing. This surface chemistry palette is intended to enable flexible CNT-based sensor arrays for noninvasive monitoring of clinically relevant biomarkers, including ketones associated with diabetes, nitrogen-containing species linked to chronic kidney disease, and volatile compounds implicated in preictal seizure states. Sensor-level performance was not evaluated in the present study and is the subject of ongoing device work.

articles.title: Agnuside from Vitex negundo L. Attenuates Hepatocellular Lipid Accumulation: Association with the AMPK/SREBP1/FASN/HMGCR/PPARα/UCP2 Signaling Network.
articles.abstract: Vitex negundo L. (VN) is a medicinal plant known for its anti-inflammatory and hepatoprotective properties, commonly used as a vegetable in northeastern Indian communities. However, its role in treating nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is still underexplored. This study evaluates the therapeutic potential of VN and its bioactive compounds in reducing lipid accumulation in CC1 hepatocytes. A crude extract of VN and its n-butanol fraction (VNBU) were tested on palmitate-induced CC1 hepatocytes to evaluate lipid accumulation. Key compounds Agnuside, 5-hydroxy-3,6,7,3́,4́-pentamethoxyflavone, and Vitexilactone were isolated. Agnuside's effects on lipogenesis, cholesterol accumulation, and fatty acid oxidation were assessed using biochemical assays and Western blot analysis. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations were conducted to explore its interactions with 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase (HMGCR). Agnuside treatment was associated with reduced lipid accumulation by modulating Adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK), HMGCR, Sterol regulatory element-binding transcription factor 1 (SREBP1), Fatty acid synthase (FASN), Peroxisome Proliferator-activated receptors (PPARα), and uncoupling protein (UCP2), suggesting a favorable shift in lipid metabolism. Computational studies indicated that Agnuside binds stably to HMGCR, similar to statins. In summary, these findings suggest that VN and Agnuside exert protective effects in hepatocytes, accompanied by favorable shifts in lipid metabolism markers. Further studies are needed to confirm the causal role of this signaling network.

articles.title: Computationally steered toehold engineering accelerates primer exchange reaction for rapid detection of congenital heart disease-associated miRNAs.
articles.abstract: Isothermal nucleic acid amplification, including the primer exchange reaction (PER), provides a promising basis for molecular diagnostics with potential for point-of-care testing (POCT). However, its clinical translation is severely bottlenecked by prolonged reaction times (typically >4 h) originating from the intrinsic nucleation barrier during initial target recognition. Here, we propose a synergistic computational-experimental paradigm to accelerate PER kinetics by rationally modulating the target-recognition toehold length. By employing oxDNA coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations and NUPACK thermodynamic computations, we systematically decode the free-energy landscape of target-probe interactions. Both theoretical modeling and experimental validation consistently reveal that a precisely extended 15-nucleotide (nt) recognition toehold facilitates initial target recognition and promotes subsequent strand displacement, thereby accelerating the initiation of the PER process. Operating via a programmable dGTP-depleted enzymatic cascade, this precision molecular engineering yields a 75% temporal reduction, compressing PER amplification time to a mere 60 min. The toehold-engineered amplification platform achieves an analytical limit of detection of approximately 662 fM, demonstrating its capability for low-concentration target detection. The observed differences in fluorescence responses among the clinical groups suggest the feasibility of applying the platform to CHD-associated circulating miRNA profiling. We further evaluated the accelerated PER platform by separately detecting three CHD-associated miRNAs (miR-146a-5p, miR-122-5p, and miR-548am-3p) in clinical serum samples and combining their fluorescence responses for exploratory analysis. Preliminary differences were observed among the clinically defined groups. This study establishes a thermodynamically steered kinetic acceleration strategy for dynamic DNA reactions, offering a rapid, reliable, and clinically actionable avenue for early disease screening.

articles.title: Implementation of a National Synthetic Data Infrastructure for Privacy-Preserving Analytical Workflows in the Czech National Health Information System: Development and Evaluation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Demand for health data to support research, innovation, and evidence-based policymaking is increasing, but access to patient-level data is constrained by privacy and data protection requirements. To address this challenge, the Czech Republic developed a national synthetic data infrastructure within the National Health Information System (NHIS). The infrastructure aims to support privacy-preserving secondary use of health data by enabling the development and validation of analytical workflows without providing direct access to operational patient-level databases.

OBJECTIVE: This study describes the design, implementation, governance framework, and operational evaluation of the Czech NHIS synthetic data infrastructure as a national platform for privacy-preserving secondary use of health data and for the development of reproducible analytical workflows. The system strongly supports the continuing relevance and importance of national infrastructures during the transition to full European Health Data Space (EHDS) implementation.

METHODS: The infrastructure was implemented using selected nationwide registries, including reimbursement, cancer, reproductive health, and mortality databases. Synthetic datasets were generated using registry-specific rule-based procedures designed to preserve database structures, variable formats, and selected longitudinal relationships while preventing reconstruction of real patient records. Researchers developed and tested SQL-based analytical workflows within the synthetic environment, whereas execution on primary NHIS databases and disclosure control review were performed exclusively by authorized personnel. The implementation was evaluated using predefined operational indicators, including user adoption, request volume, processing outcomes, transparency measures, and privacy-related incidents.

UNLABELLED: The infrastructure enables the development and validation of SQL-based analytical workflows without direct access to primary patient-level data. Synthetic datasets representing approximately 0.04% to 0.26% of the selected NHIS registries were created while maintaining schema compatibility and selected analytical relationships. Between the platform's public launch and July 23, 2026, a total of 170 users registered, 199 requests were submitted, and 184 requests have been processed (173 with data delivery). A total of 41 (20.6%) requests included consent to share SQL scripts, thereby supporting public transparency and reproducibility. Practical implementation was demonstrated through operational use cases in oncology, nephrology, cardiology, and vaccination research. No privacy-related incidents were reported during the evaluation period.

CONCLUSIONS: The Czech NHIS synthetic data infrastructure demonstrates that privacy-preserving secondary use of national health data can be implemented through a General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)-aligned governance framework that combines synthetic data, controlled execution on operational databases, disclosure-risk assessment, and transparent analytical workflows. Rather than serving as a statistically valid surrogate for inferential research, the infrastructure supports the reproducible development of workflows and the secure preparation of population-level analyses. As a fully operational national implementation aligned with the principles of the EHDS, the platform may provide a reference model for other countries developing privacy-preserving health data ecosystems.

articles.title: Invisible exposure, visible harm: air pollution and the global burden of cardiovascular disease.
articles.journal: Genes and environment : the official journal of the Japanese Environmental Mutagen Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Air pollution is a major modifiable environmental risk factor for cardiovascular disease (CVD). In the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 study, air pollution was the second-leading risk factor for death worldwide, accounting for an estimated 8.1 million deaths from all causes in 2021, and particulate matter (PM) pollution (ambient plus household) was associated with approximately 4.5 million cardiovascular deaths.

MAIN BODY: This narrative review, based on a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science, summarizes evidence on the sources of the main pollutants (fine particulate matter [PM₂.₅], coarse particulate matter [PM₁₀], ultrafine particles [PM₀.₁/UFP], nitrogen dioxide [NO₂], sulfur dioxide [SO₂], ozone [O₃] and carbon monoxide [CO]); the global burden of pollution-attributable CVD; epidemiological evidence from major cohort and multi-city studies; biological mechanisms, distinguishing those supported by human data from those derived mainly from cell and animal models; the associations with specific cardiovascular phenotypes (ischemic heart disease, stroke, hypertension, heart failure, arrhythmia and vascular disease); susceptible populations; transcriptomic, proteomic, lipidomic, epigenetic and microRNA findings; and preventive strategies graded by strength of evidence. Observational studies consistently associate short- and long-term exposure to PM₂.₅ with cardiovascular events and mortality, and controlled-exposure, quasi-experimental and mechanistic studies support a causal interpretation for PM₂.₅. Evidence for individual gaseous pollutants is less consistent, and most multi-omics findings remain exploratory.

CONCLUSION: PM₂.₅ should be regarded as a cardiovascular risk factor in clinical and public-health practice. Key uncertainties include the shape of the exposure-response relationship at very low concentrations, the relative toxicity of particle components, and whether reducing individual exposure lowers hard cardiovascular outcomes. Priorities include prospective multi-omics studies with clinical endpoints in low- and middle-income countries, causal-inference designs, and trials testing exposure-reduction and targeted therapeutic strategies in highly exposed populations.

articles.title: Development of a test matrix for assessing basic calculation skills in nursing and midwifery education: a Delphi study on content validation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pharmaceutical calculations are essential in nursing and midwifery practice, yet errors remain a major cause of preventable harm. Studies indicate high error rates among both professionals and students, often linked to inadequate calculation skills. Despite the recognised importance of entry-level calculation skills, higher education institutions lack validated tools to assess these competencies at programme entry, limiting timely remediation and potentially compromising medication safety.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and content-validate a test matrix for a basic calculation skills test in Flanders (Belgium) nursing and midwifery education, providing a framework for standardised assessment and remediation.

METHOD: A draft test matrix was developed through literature review, analysis of nursing and midwifery curricula, and official primary education mathematics standards. It was structured into five domains, covering 12 learning objectives and 27 learning content items, each linked to a specific cognition level and weighting factor. Content validity was assessed in a two-round Delphi study with a multidisciplinary expert panel. Data from online questionnaires were analysed using CVIs, descriptive statistics, and a thematic review of open-ended responses to achieve consensus and refine the matrix.

RESULTS: Delphi round I included 24 experts, followed by 17 in round II. Their feedback led to the removal of one learning content item and the revision of two weighting factors. After these two rounds, full consensus was reached on all test matrix items, resulting in 5 domains, 12 learning objectives, and 26 learning content items.

CONCLUSION: The study resulted in a content-validated test matrix comprising 12 learning objectives and 26 learning content items. Each learning content item was assigned a weighting factor and linked to a corresponding level of cognition, defined according to Bloom's taxonomy. This framework may provide a foundation for diagnostic testing in nursing and midwifery education programmes.

articles.title: Zone-specific lymph node metastasis prediction model in clinical stage I-II non-small cell lung cancer: a supplementary analysis of JCOG1413.
articles.journal: European journal of surgical oncology : the journal of the European Society of Surgical Oncology and the British Association of Surgical Oncology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal extent of lymph node dissection in early-stage non-small cell lung cancer remains unclear. We aimed to develop zone-specific lymph node metastasis prediction models for clinical stage I-II non-small cell lung cancer using data from the Japan Clinical Oncology Group (JCOG) 1413, a randomized phase III trial comparing lobe-specific and systematic lymph node dissection.

METHODS: The analysis included 1699 eligible cases out of 1711 patients from 44 institutions in JCOG1413. Leave-one-out cross-validation was used to evaluate the prediction algorithm, and multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of metastasis for constructing nomograms. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves with concordance statistics and calibration curves with calibration slope.

RESULTS: We developed models for four zones: upper (including the aortopulmonary zone) (n = 1416), subcarinal (n = 1170), hilar (n = 1662), and peripheral (n = 1662). Common independent predictors included histology, maximum standardized uptake on positron emission tomography, and, particularly for mediastinal zones, primary tumor lobe location. The subcarinal zone showed the best performance, with a concordance statistic of 0.7902 and a calibration slope of 1.0762. Across all zones, calibration slopes remained close to 1.0, and negative predictive values ranged from 96.6% to 99.4%.

CONCLUSIONS: Zone-specific prediction models demonstrated moderate discrimination and well-calibrated estimates of lymph-node metastasis risk, with the highest performance observed in the subcarinal zone. These models could support risk stratification and facilitate individualized intraoperative nodal assessment to inform clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Finerenone ameliorates diabetic cardiomyopathy by modulating inflammation through the FoxO3a/Acod1/MAPK axis.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and its complications
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is one of the leading causes of death among people with diabetes. However, potential treatment strategies for DCM are limited. As another complication of diabetes, finerenone has been shown to alleviate Diabetic Kidney Disease (DKD), but its ability to improve DCM remains unclear.

METHODS: A mouse model of DCM was established using a high-fat diet (HFD) combined with low-dose streptozotocin (STZ). We assessed biomarkers such as body weight, blood glucose, and blood lipids in the mice, and evaluated cardiac function via echocardiography. Histochemical staining was employed to evaluate myocardial tissue structure and the degree of fibrosis, and Western blot analysis was used to detect myocardial protein expression. We investigated the underlying molecular mechanisms through transcriptomic analysis. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) was used to measure Acod1 levels in serum samples from patients with DCM.

RESULTS: Following finerenone administration, DCM mice exhibited alleviated abnormal weight gain (p < 0.01), improved glucose tolerance (p < 0.01), and improvements in lipid metabolism: TG (DCM from 2.49 ± 0.3 to FIN-H 0.59 ± 0.1 mmol/L, mean difference[MD]: -1.9, p < 0.01), TC (DCM from 3.90 ± 0.97 to FIN-H 2.03 ± 0.8 mmol/L, MD: -1.87, p < 0.01), LDL-C (DCM from 1.35 ± 0.14 to FIN-H 0.45 ± 0.15 mmol/L, MD: -0.9, p < 0.01), and HDL-C (DCM from 0.32 ± 0.04 to FIN-H 0.52 ± 0.07 mmol/L, MD: +0.2, p < 0.01). Cardiac function improved significantly: LVEF (DCM from 48.49 ± 7.58% to FIN-H 61.96 ± 7.67%, MD: +13.47%, p < 0.05), FS (DCM from 22.65 ± 6.00% to FIN-H 32.8 ± 4.73%, MD: +10.15%, p < 0.05), and E/e'(DCM from 33.91 ± 5.01 to FIN-H 26.17 ± 3.19, MD: -7.74, p < 0.01). Inflammatory markers decreased: CRP (DCM from 1.12 ± 0.20 to FIN-H 0.65 ± 0.21 mg/L, MD: -0.47, p < 0.01) and IL-6 (DCM from 4.97 ± 2.40 to FIN-H 1.91 ± 0.32 pg/mL, MD: -3.06, p < 0.01). Histological analysis showed reduced myocardial fibrosis (collagen volume fraction: DCM from 0.53 ± 0.09% to FIN-H 0.23 ± 0.10%, MD: -0.30%, p < 0.01). Transcriptomic analysis confirmed elevated Acod1 expression in DCM mouse hearts (p < 0.01), and serum Acod1 levels were significantly lower in patients with DCM (29.93 ± 8.84 ng/mL) compared with healthy controls (37.34 ± 9.88 ng/mL, MD: 7.44, p < 0.01).

CONCLUSION: In summary, finerenone treatment was associated with improved metabolic parameters, reduced myocardial injury markers, reduced inflammation, attenuated myocardial fibrosis, and improved cardiac function in mice with DCM. Notably, finerenone administration also correlated with modulated expression of Acod1 and proteins within the FoxO3a/Acod1/MAPK pathway.

articles.title: Effect of Aficamten in Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy With Comorbidities: Obesity, Hypertension, and Diabetes: SEQUOIA-HCM Substudy.

Systemic Microvascular Endothelial Dysfunction in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction and Type 2 Diabetes: A Pooled Analysis of GLADIATOR-HFpEF, IRON-HFpEF, EMPA-MVD, Hoorn Diabetes Care System, and Healthy Controls.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder featuring microvascular dysfunction and metabolic comorbidities such as type 2 diabetes (T2D). However, the extent to which systemic microvascular abnormalities reflect HFpEF or coexisting T2D remains incompletely understood.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to characterize systemic microvascular dysfunction in patients with HFpEF and to evaluate the contribution of comorbid T2D.

METHODS: Systemic microvascular function, defined as flow responses expressed as cutaneous vascular conductance, was assessed using laser speckle contrast analysis with iontophoresis of acetylcholine, insulin, and sodium nitroprusside. Analysis adjusted for age and sex were performed across healthy controls (n = 23), T2D (n = 138), HFpEF without T2D (n = 63), and HFpEF with T2D (n = 27).

RESULTS: Insulin-mediated microvascular perfusion was reduced in participants with T2D (-0.30 arbitrary perfusion units [APU]/mm Hg; P < 0.001) and in HFpEF with T2D (-0.32 APU/mm Hg; P = 0.004) compared with controls, whereas responses in HFpEF without T2D were not different from controls. Perfusion responses to sodium nitroprusside were reduced in T2D and HFpEF with T2D, while responses to acetylcholine were preserved. No statistically detectable interaction between HFpEF and T2D was observed. Sex did not modify the relationship between HFpEF and microvascular dysfunction, but exploratory sex-stratified analyses showed reduced insulin-mediated microvascular perfusion in T2D (mean difference: -0.30 APU/mm Hg; P = 0.020) and HFpEF + T2D (mean difference: -0.51 APU/mm Hg; P = 0.002) compared with controls.

CONCLUSIONS: Systemic microvascular dysfunction, particularly impaired insulin-mediated vasodilation, was observed in HFpEF. The observed abnormalities were predominantly present in participants with comorbid type 2 diabetes.

articles.title: Acupuncture after surgery of soft tissue tumors of the extremities: postoperative pain and feasibility: a prospective trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Acute pain management following resection of soft tissue tumors (STTs) of the extremities is primarily based on pharmacological interventions. However, current guidelines emphasize the role of complementary non-pharmacological approaches, such as acupuncture. This prospective pilot study aimed to evaluate the feasibility and potential effects of acupuncture following STT surgery of the extremities. Furthermore, this study represents the first to systematically assess the postoperative pain trajectory in this patient population.

METHODS: In this prospective, single-arm, single-centre study, 25 patients undergoing surgical resection of STTs of the extremities received acupuncture on postoperative day (POD) 1. Pain intensity was recorded at predefined time points using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) and the Brief Pain Inventory (BPI).

RESULTS: Participants had a mean age of 60.7 years. Most tumors were malignant, located in the lower extremities, with a median size of 13.1 cm. Postoperative pain at rest was minimal, with a mean NRS score of 1.2 (± 1.2) on POD 1 and below 0.5 (± 0.8) from POD 2 onward. The pain severity index of the BPI declined significantly after POD 1, reaching its lowest level at POD 3. Acupuncture was administered on POD 1. Placement of needles at the "optimal position" was feasible in 8 of 25 patients. The median length of hospital stay was four days. Wound complications occurred in eleven patients, but none were attributable to acupuncture. No other serious adverse events were observed.

CONCLUSION: Acupuncture was feasible, safe, and well accepted in this postoperative setting. Pain levels and opioid requirements remained low throughout the postoperative period. Further controlled studies are warranted to assess efficacy and to refine patient selection and acupuncture techniques in this setting.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS, DRKS00032703) registeres on 18.09.2023.

articles.title: Metformin Induces Persistent DNMT1-Associated DNA-Protein Cross-Links under Glucose Deprivation.
articles.abstract: Metformin, a widely prescribed biguanide for the treatment of type 2 diabetes, is known to exhibit selective cytotoxicity under glucose-deprived conditions that mimic the metabolic environment of poorly vascularized solid tumors. We previously demonstrated, using chicken DT40 cells, that metformin induces DNA-protein cross-links (DPCs) under glucose deprivation. However, the molecular identity of these DPCs and their biological significance in human cells have remained unclear. In the present study, we investigated the nature of metformin-induced DNA damage under metabolic stress conditions using human lymphoblastoid TK6 cells. Metformin induced marked cytotoxicity and chromosome fragmentation under glucose-deprived conditions. Genetic analyses revealed marked hypersensitivity of SPRTN-deficient cells, whereas cells deficient in TDP1, TDP2, or both TDP1 and TDP2 exhibited only modest increases in sensitivity. FITC-based quantification demonstrated that metformin increased the overall DPC burden under both glucose-supplemented and glucose-deprived conditions. In contrast, DNA methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1)-associated DPCs were preferentially detected under glucose deprivation, whereas Topoisomerase I- or Topoisomerase II-associated DPCs were not substantially induced. Furthermore, DNA-associated DNMT1 showed increased levels and prolonged persistence following metformin treatment in sprtn/tdp1/tdp2 triple mutant cells. These findings suggest that the biological consequences of metformin-induced DPCs cannot be explained by their overall abundance alone and may also be related to differences in their molecular composition under glucose-deprived conditions.

articles.title: Right Heart Dysfunction in Valvular Heart Disease: Epidemiology, Prognosis, and Management Considerations.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
articles.abstract: Right ventricular (RV) dysfunction is an important determinant of clinical outcomes across a wide range of cardiovascular pathologies. As the prevalence of valvular heart disease (VHD) increases with the aging population, the intersection between RV function and VHD will become all the more relevant for proper risk assessment, treatment selection, and prognostication. Even though RV dysfunction may not always be attributed to VHD, we aim to give clinicians, researchers, and regulators a deep understanding of how patients with VHD should be evaluated for RV dysfunction and treated when RV dysfunction coexists with VHD. We begin with a discussion of the epidemiology and diagnostic evaluation of RV dysfunction in patients with a variety of VHD subgroups, including right-side (ie, associated with the tricuspid valve) and left-side (ie, associated with the mitral and aortic valves) VHD. Attention is also given in that section to contemporary methods and evolving techniques for identifying and phenotyping different forms of RV dysfunction in patients with VHD. No single imaging test practically or comprehensively captures all degrees and forms of RV dysfunction in patients with VHD; therefore, the discussion emphasizes integrating evidence from different imaging modalities and hemodynamic assessments. The second component of the review discusses how RV dysfunction affects therapeutic options, including medical, transcatheter, and surgical therapies for VHD. The focus of the discussion is on the interplay between RV dysfunction in patients with right-side VHD, namely tricuspid regurgitation (TR). Unlike left-side VHD, where RV dysfunction is a marker of overall disease severity but does not necessarily indicate futility or nonresponse to therapy, right-side VHD and TR-associated RV dysfunction identifies a subset of patients where intervention may precipitate even worse RV function. The nuances of these interactions between ventricular and valvular function are the emphasis of this section, and we aim to provide a framework for understanding RV function in the context of these different forms of VHD. Finally, the review concludes with an eye to the future, discussing the ways in which RV dysfunction can be identified and managed with the use of novel techniques. This discussion is increasingly relevant as RV dysfunction and VHD frequently coexist, and accurate identification is critical to matching the right treatment for the right patient.

articles.title: Upcycling recycled PET into a conductive electrode for a molecularly imprinted polymer based electrochemical sensor for 17β-estradiol detection.
articles.abstract: The upcycling of plastic waste into advanced materials has emerged as a promising strategy across various technologies, including the development of next-generation sensors. This sustainable approach promotes green technological development. In this work, we transformed recycled polyethylene terephthalate (rPET) into a functional conductive electrode substrate for a molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) based electrochemical sensor for the detection of 17β-estradiol (E2). The latter also serves as a relevant model compound as a pollutant to study the sensor's applicability in complex matrices. The MIP-based sensor was fabricated by the electropolymerization of an o-phenylenediamine (o-PD) monomer in the presence of E2 template molecules and gold(iii) chloride trihydrate onto gold-coated rPET substrates. The physical properties of MIP films were characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), atomic force microscopy, contact angle measurement, cyclic voltammetry, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. The binding of E2 molecules to the MIP surface hindered electron transfer of the redox probes, resulting in a concentration-dependent suppression of the electrochemical current measured by square wave voltammetry. The sensor showed high affinity for E2 molecules with a dissociation constant (K d) of 11.2 nM over a linear detection range of E2 concentrations (0.5-500 nM), and a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.18 and 0.41 nM in PBS and in wastewater samples without any complex pretreatment steps, respectively. This developed MIP-based sensor demonstrated the potential of alternative sensors for real-world environmental monitoring of trace endocrine disruptors, while successfully converting rPET into valuable technological products offers a practical roadmap to accelerate the development of sustainable and circular electronics.

articles.title: Elevated Serum Growth Differentiation Factor 15 Levels Predict Poor Prognosis in Patients With Aortic Stenosis Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) reducing cardiovascular events in elderly patients with aortic stenosis (AS), the mortality rate is still high. Growth differentiation factor (GDF) 15 is reportedly a useful prognostic marker for clinical outcomes in the field of cardiovascular diseases, but it is still unclear if elevated serum GDF15 levels predict poor prognosis in patients with severe AS who undergo TAVI.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We measured the pre- and postoperative serum concentrations of GDF15 in 148 patients. The primary and secondary endpoints were all-cause death and a composite event including cardiovascular death, heart failure rehospitalization, stroke, and adverse bleeding event, respectively. There were 30 all-cause deaths and 21 composite events during a median follow-up period of 1,023 days. Both pre- and postoperative serum GDF15 levels were significantly increased with advancing Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score. Multivariate Cox proportional hazards analysis revealed that preoperative serum GDF15 level was independently associated with the primary and secondary endpoints, and the postoperative serum GDF15 level was independently associated with the primary endpoint after adjustment for confounding risk factors. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis for the primary endpoint showed a comparable area under the curve for the pre- and postoperative serum GDF15 levels.

CONCLUSIONS: Both the pre- and postoperative GDF15 concentration could be a feasible marker for clinical outcomes in Japanese patients undergoing TAVI.

articles.title: CORRIGENDUM: Discontinuation of Tafamidis in Wild-Type Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy Patients.

articles.title: Association Between Coronary Inflammatory Burden and Cardiac Dysfunction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure is not only a mechanical impairment but also involves inflammation. This study investigated the association between quantitatively assessed coronary inflammation and cardiac dysfunction, and whether this relationship varied by coronary artery stenosis status.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We studied 627 patients without prior coronary artery disease (CAD) who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography and transthoracic echocardiography. Coronary inflammation was quantified using the perivascular fat attenuation index (FAI) in the proximal segments of the 3 major epicardial coronary arteries. An inflamed artery was defined as a vessel-specific FAI >75th percentile, and patients were categorized by the number of inflamed arteries (0-3). Cardiac dysfunction was defined as either systolic dysfunction (left ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF] <50%) or diastolic dysfunction (LVEF ≥50% with ≥3 abnormal guideline-based criteria). Compared with none, adjusted odds ratios (ORs) for cardiac dysfunction were 1.39 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.70-2.78) for 1, 2.63 (95% CI 1.28-5.42) for 2, and 6.50 (95% CI 3.13-13.45) for 3 inflamed arteries. Associations were consistent in patients without obstructive CAD, with adjusted ORs for cardiac dysfunction of 1.44 (95% CI 0.66-3.16), 2.67 (95% CI 1.18-6.07), and 3.85 (95% CI 1.57-9.48), respectively. Vessel-specific analyses demonstrated similar findings.

CONCLUSIONS: Greater coronary inflammatory burden was dose-dependently associated with cardiac dysfunction, even in the absence of significant coronary stenosis.

articles.title: Early Direct Oral Anticoagulant Initiation After Intracranial Hemorrhage Among Japanese Patients With Nonvalvular Atrial Fibrillation: SAFE-ICH Registry 12-Month Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Understanding the effects of early direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) (re)initiation after intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) in atrial fibrillation is crucial. Previous 30-day outcomes in the SAFE-ICH Registry showed acceptable ischemic/hemorrhagic risks; therefore, we evaluated the 12-month outcomes.

METHODS AND RESULTS: The SAFE-ICH Registry, a prospective, observational cohort study conducted at 32 hospitals in Japan, included 240 patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) who experienced ICH and in whom DOAC therapy was (re)initiated ≤14 days after ICH. Short-term (≤30 days) and long-term (≤12 months) ischemic/hemorrhagic outcomes were investigated. Data were collected through clinical assessments, imaging or telephone interviews over 12 months. The 12-month composite outcome incidence (symptomatic ICH, any stroke, all-cause death) was 22.5% (29.1/100 person-years). The secondary outcome incidence was 6.3% (7.9/100 person-years) for symptomatic ICH, 6.7% (8.4/100 person-years) for any stroke (ischemic: 2.9% [3.6/100 person-years]; hemorrhagic: 3.8% [4.6/100 person-years]), and 14.2% (17.3/100 person-years) for all-cause death. The major bleeding incidence was 6.7% (8.4/100 person-years). Hemorrhagic stroke first appeared approximately 3 months after DOAC (re)initiation, and by month 10, its rate was comparable to that of ischemic stroke. Most deaths were due to aspiration pneumonia.

CONCLUSIONS: Early DOAC (re)initiation after ICH in NVAF was associated with a numerically higher long-term hemorrhagic than ischemic stroke risk. These risks warrant careful consideration when determining the optimal DOAC duration and timing after ICH.

articles.title: Fasting Management Time and Dysphagia in Patients With Acute Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Because dysphagia is an important complication associated with poor prognosis in patients with acute heart failure (AHF), we examined the association between fasting management time and dysphagia at discharge.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively analyzed 644 patients without pre-admission dysphagia hospitalized for AHF, grouped by fasting management time (<48 vs. ≥48 h). After propensity score matching, 121 pairs were identified. In conditional logistic regression, oral intake resumption at <48 h was associated with lower odds of dysphagia at discharge than at ≥48 h (odds ratio 0.19, 95% confidence interval 0.10-0.38, P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Shorter fasting management time was associated with lower odds of dysphagia at discharge.

articles.title: Association of Mean Left Atrial Pressure With Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes in Patients Undergoing Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation: Subanalysis of the Shinshu Catheter Ablation (Shinshu-AB) Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association of invasively measured mean left atrial pressure (LAP) during catheter ablation (CA) for atrial fibrillation (AF) with clinical characteristics and outcomes remains unclear.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We analyzed the data of 480 patients from the Shinshu Catheter Ablation Registry who underwent CA for AF (median age, 69 years; 146 women [30.4%]; 207 patients [43.1%] with persistent AF). Patients were categorized by mean LAP as normal (<12 mmHg; n=318 [66.3%]), mildly elevated (12 to <15 mmHg; n=78 [16.3%]), or elevated (≥15 mmHg; n=84 [17.5%]). Study endpoints were early AF recurrence within the 8-week blanking period, late AF recurrence, and composite adverse clinical events (heart failure hospitalization, symptomatic stroke, or all-cause death) during the 1-year follow-up after CA. Patients in the higher LAP groups had a higher prevalence of obesity and persistent AF, and a larger left atrial volume index. Early AF recurrence differed significantly across the LAP groups and was highest in the elevated LAP group (log-rank P=0.017). After multivariable adjustment, early AF recurrence risk increased across the LAP groups (hazard ratio per-category increase, 1.41; 95% confidence interval, 1.04-1.90; P for trend=0.028). In contrast, late AF recurrence and composite adverse clinical events did not differ significantly across the LAP groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Mean LAP during CA for AF was associated with AF-related clinical characteristics and early AF recurrence.

articles.title: Stepwise Scoring Models for Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Weaning in Patients With Cardiogenic Shock.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Predictors of successful venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) weaning have been reported, but their integration into sequential reassessment remains unclear.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively analyzed 48 adults with cardiogenic shock receiving VA-ECMO. Exploratory stepwise models were constructed using variables available at ECMO initiation, 24, and 48 h. The 48-h model included female sex, pulse pressure, EtCO2, levels of lactate, and creatinine.

CONCLUSIONS: Exploratory stepwise models using routinely available variables may provide a framework for sequential VA-ECMO weaning assessment. External validation is required.

articles.title: Prevalence and Prognostic Impact of Sarcopenic Dysphagia in Older Patients With Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dysphagia is common in older patients with heart failure (HF), but evidence regarding sarcopenic dysphagia remains limited. The purpose of this retrospective study was to clarify the prevalence of sarcopenic dysphagia and its relationship with swallowing-related measures and prognosis in older patients with HF.

METHODS AND RESULTS: The study group included patients aged ≥65 years admitted with HF between June 2021 and December 2023. Patients were classified into 3 groups using the diagnostic algorithm for sarcopenic dysphagia at discharge: robust (without sarcopenia), sarcopenia (with sarcopenia only), and sarcopenic dysphagia (with sarcopenia and dysphagia). Outcomes were swallowing-related measures (maximal tongue pressure, geniohyoid muscle area, and geniohyoid muscle echogenicity) and a 1-year composite outcome (all-cause death or HF-related readmission). Of 524 screened patients, 363 were analyzed (median age 83 years [Q1-Q3: 78-90 years], 46.6% women); 61 patients were robust (16.8%), 215 had sarcopenia (59.2%), and 87 had sarcopenic dysphagia (24.0%). In the analysis of covariance, swallowing-related measures were poorer in the sarcopenic dysphagia group compared with the robust group (P<0.05). In the Cox regression analysis compared with robust, sarcopenia was not statistically significantly associated with prognosis, but sarcopenic dysphagia was associated with a higher risk (hazard ratio 2.53, 95% confidence interval 1.30-4.90, P=0.006).

CONCLUSIONS: Sarcopenic dysphagia affected 24.0% of patients with HF, and was associated with poorer swallowing-related measures and prognosis.

articles.title: Left Ventricular Torsion Derived From Cardiac Cine Magnetic Resonance: Interventricular Interaction of Transcatheter Pulmonary Valve Implantation for Pulmonary Regurgitation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: After tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) repair, pulmonary regurgitation (PR) frequently leads to right ventricular (RV) dilation and heart failure. Transcatheter pulmonary valve implantation (TPVI) reduces RV volume, but its impact on left ventricular (LV) function remains unclear. We hypothesized that LV torsion is a more sensitive indicator than LV ejection fraction (LVEF) and evaluated longitudinal changes in torsion using 3D cardiac cine magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) before and after TPVI.

METHODS AND RESULTS: 30 patients with PR (25 with TOF, 4 with pulmonary artery stenosis, and 1 with double-outlet right ventricle; mean age, 42 years) underwent MRI before, 3 months, and 12 months after TPVI. LV time-torsion curves were derived from short-axis cine images using feature-tracking analysis. Torsion, biventricular function, and the PR fraction (PRF) were assessed. Torsion increased progressively (0.82±0.42 vs. 0.98±0.48 vs. 1.18±0.55 degrees/cm; all P<0.01), whereas LVEF showed no significant change (52.1±11.0% vs. 53.7±9.3% vs. 55.3±9.9%). RV end-diastolic volume index and PRF were significantly reduced at 12 months.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite unchanged LVEF, torsion improved after TPVI, reflecting LVEF-independent LV pump function and interventricular interaction.

articles.title: Study Protocol for a Participant- and Evaluator-Blinded, Randomized Controlled Trial of the Effect and Feasibility of REHA-Glasses for Gait Rehabilitation in Individuals With Acute Stroke Lateropulsion.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Individuals with post-stroke lateropulsion are unable to shift their body weight to the non-paralytic side and consequently lean toward the paralytic side, thereby lengthening the rehabilitation process and hindering independent walking. We developed REHA-glasses, a device that allows the wearer to rotate the perceived visual field in accordance with their incorrect perception of verticality, thereby adjusting their posture to an upright position. No clinical practice guidelines exist for the rehabilitation of patients with post-stroke lateropulsion.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This will be a single-center, exploratory participant- and evaluator-blinded randomized controlled clinical trial (jRCT1052250005). Individuals with acute stroke admitted to hospital within 48 h of onset will be recruited. Participants will be allocated randomly to 2 groups: wearing REHA-glasses during gait rehabilitation or wearing sham REHA-glasses that do not modulate visual input. A total of 5 gait rehabilitation sessions with REHA-glasses will be completed. Outcome measures will be collected at 3 time points: baseline, post-intervention, and 90 (±14) days after stroke onset. The primary outcome is the proportion of participants who improve by ≥1 point in the Functional Ambulation Categories from baseline to post-intervention.

CONCLUSIONS: This will be the first trial to investigate the effect and feasibility of REHA-glasses for independent walking in individuals with acute stroke lateropulsion.

articles.title: Prognostic Implications of Clinically Attributed Left Atrial Enlargement Subtypes in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial enlargement (LAE) is common in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), but its prognostic significance may vary according to the clinical drivers of atrial remodeling. We examined whether prognostic factors differ by clinically attributed LAE subtype in patients undergoing TAVI with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF).

METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively analyzed 317 consecutive patients with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis (AS) undergoing TAVI who had preserved LVEF and LAE. Patients were classified as AS-associated LAE (no atrial fibrillation [AF] and <moderate mitral regurgitation [MR]) or AF/MR-associated LAE (AF and/or ≥moderate MR). The primary endpoint was all-cause death. During a median follow-up of 2.7 years, 69 patients (21.8%) died. The all-cause mortality rate was higher in the AF/MR-associated group than in the AS-associated LAE group (30.7% vs. 19.0%; log-rank P<0.01), but this association was attenuated after adjustment for eGFR, log-BNP, and LAVI. In the AS-associated LAE group, higher log-BNP (hazard ratio (HR) 1.45, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.06-1.98), higher E/e' (HR 1.03, 95% CI 1.01-1.06), and lower TAPSE (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.81-0.99) predicted death. In the AF/MR-associated LAE group, lower eGFR (HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.93-1.00) and higher log-BNP (HR 1.98, 95% CI 1.09-3.59) predicted death after adjustment for age. Interactions were significant for eGFR and E/e'.

CONCLUSIONS: Prognostic markers after TAVI differ by clinically attributed LAE subtype, supporting subtype-informed risk stratification.

articles.title: Discontinuous Intrarenal Venous Flow Pattern With Low Cardiac Index as a Predictor of Poor Prognosis in Patients With Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intrarenal venous flow (IRVF) patterns assessed by Doppler ultrasonography enable non-invasive assessment of renal venous congestion in patients with heart failure (HF). IRVF patterns have also attracted attention as markers of cardiorenal interactions, but their prognostic significance relative to invasive hemodynamics remains unclear.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively analyzed 253 consecutive patients hospitalized for HF who underwent Swan-Ganz catheterization, echocardiography, and IRVF within 24 h of catheterization; 184 patients had a continuous and 69 had a discontinuous IRVF pattern. The endpoint was a composite of HF rehospitalization and cardiac death within 1 year. During follow-up, 22 composite events occurred. The incidence of the composite endpoint was significantly higher among patients with a discontinuous than continuous IRVF pattern (Gray's test, P<0.001). On multivariable Fine-Gray analysis, a discontinuous IRVF pattern was independently associated with the composite endpoint (hazard ratio 5.21; 95% confidence interval 1.81-15.0; P<0.001). In subgroup analyses stratified by median cardiac index and fractional excretion of urea nitrogen (FEUN), a discontinuous IRVF pattern was associated with significantly higher event rates only in the groups with a lower cardiac index (<2.33 L·min-1·m-2) or lower FEUN (<38.1%; P<0.05 for both).

CONCLUSIONS: A discontinuous IRVF pattern could be used as an independent predictor of poor prognosis in HF, particularly in patients with a low cardiac index. Combined assessment of IRVF with hemodynamic and renal markers may enhance clinical risk stratification.

articles.title: Trends in the Prescribed Doses of Loop Diuretics in Patients With Heart Failure Prescribed Dapagliflozin or Empagliflozin in Japan: An Interrupted Time Series Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors and loop diuretics have beneficial diuretic effects in patients with heart failure but may increase the risk of excessive water loss. Therefore, clinical guidelines recommend adjustment of loop diuretic doses when these agents are used concomitantly. However, real-world evidence regarding changes in loop diuretic dosing is limited. This study evaluated changes in prescribed doses of oral loop diuretics in patients with heart failure receiving dapagliflozin or empagliflozin before and after publication of the JCS/JHFS 2021 Guideline Focused Update on Diagnosis and Treatment of Acute and Chronic Heart Failure.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Changes in prescribed dose trends were evaluated using monthly aggregated prescription data obtained from the Medical Data Vision database (Medical Data Vision, Inc., Tokyo, Japan). After publication of the guideline, statistically significant decreases were observed in the empagliflozin-prescribed group for azosemide (-0.1756 mg/month; P=0.0360), furosemide (-0.2180 mg/month; P=0.0485), and torsemide (-0.0387 mg/month; P=0.0378), and in the dapagliflozin-prescribed group for azosemide (-0.8221 mg/month; P=0.0260). The study period for dapagliflozin was too short to provide adequate statistical power.

CONCLUSIONS: The publication of the JCS/JHFS 2021 guideline was associated with decreases in prescribed doses of oral loop diuretics. Dose reduction of oral loop diuretics may be considered in patients receiving concomitant SGLT2 inhibitors in clinical practice.

articles.title: Coronary Thrombosis Detected by Intravascular Ultrasound During Bleomycin, Etoposide, and Cisplatin Chemotherapy.
Early Vericiguat Initiation After First Hospitalization for Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Multicenter Observational Study From the VERIFY-HF Registry and Institutional Cohorts.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hospitalization for the first episode of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) represents an important opportunity to initiate evidence-based therapies. In this study, we aimed to clarify the role of vericiguat after first hospitalization for HFrEF in routine clinical practice.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included patients with HFrEF at their first hospitalization between June 2021 and September 2023 identified from the nationwide Verifying Characteristics and Outcomes in Heart Failure Patients Treated with Vericiguat registry (vericiguat group, n=104) and 2 institutional databases (control group, n=206) (mean age, 67 years; 71% male). The primary endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death or HF rehospitalization within 1 year. In inverse probability of treatment weighting-adjusted Cox models, vericiguat use was associated with a lower risk of the primary endpoint, compared with controls (hazard ratio, 0.26; 95% confidence interval, 0.08-0.81). Sensitivity analysis using alternative weighting methods and a doubly robust model yielded consistent results.

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world Japanese cohort of patients at first hospitalization for HFrEF, vericiguat initiation during index hospitalization was associated with a lower risk of cardiovascular death or HF rehospitalization after discharge. The observed association was directionally consistent with previous trials and pooled analyses, suggesting a potential benefit for this intermediate real-world population.

articles.title: Residual Risk Despite High Short Physical Performance Battery Scores in Older Patients With Heart Failure: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic value of the Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB), which is widely used to assess physical function and prognostic risk in patients with heart failure (HF), is unclear in patients with high SPPB scores. In this study we evaluated whether sarcopenia-related factors defined by the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia in 2019 provided additional prognostic value in this population.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective multicenter cohort study of the J-Proof HF registry included 3,044 patients aged ≥65 years with a discharge SPPB score ≥10. Impairments in handgrip strength, five-times chair stand test, and calf circumference were aggregated into a composite physical function score (range, 0-3). The primary outcome was the composite of all-cause death or rehospitalization for HF within 1 year, which occurred in 25.0% of the cohort. The composite outcome risk increased in a stepwise manner with each additional impaired domain (adjusted hazard ratio per 1-point increase, 1.245; 95% confidence interval 1.132-1.370; P<0.001). The fully adjusted model showed acceptable discrimination (Harrell's C-index=0.694). Each domain independently demonstrated a similar magnitude of association with the outcome.

CONCLUSIONS: Even among older patients with HF and preserved physical performance (SPPB ≥10), accumulation of sarcopenia-related impairments was associated with an increased risk of adverse outcomes. Supplementing the SPPB with simple functional assessments may improve risk stratification in clinical practice.

articles.title: Association Between High-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Efflux Capacity and Renal Function in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The cholesterol efflux capacity (CEC) of high-density lipoprotein (HDL) (HDL-CEC) is inversely associated with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is frequently complicated by chronic kidney disease (CKD), usually associated with increased homocysteine (Hcy), and these conditions are likely to be involved in HDL dysfunction. However, the relationship between HDL-CEC and CKD, as well as Hcy levels in patients with T2DM remains unclear.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This cross-sectional study involved 138 patients with T2DM. CEC was measured using a stable-isotope method with J774 macrophage-like cells and apolipoprotein B-depleted serum. Multiple regression analysis showed that sex (β=0.278; P=0.005), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR; β=0.232; P=0.038), and HDL cholesterol (HDL-C; β=0.197; P=0.030) were independently associated with CEC.

CONCLUSIONS: Sex, eGFR, and HDL-C were independently associated with HDL-CEC in patients with T2DM. These findings suggest that impaired renal function may be related to impaired HDL function in this population, although causal relationships cannot be inferred from this cross-sectional analysis.

articles.title: Whole-Exome Sequencing in Patients With Apical Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: An Exploratory Analysis of Rare Variant Burden and Apical Aneurysm.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Apical aneurysm complicates apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (ApHCM), but its genetic determinants remain unclear.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Whole-exome sequencing (WES) was performed in 72 Japanese patients with ApHCM, including 8 with apical aneurysms. Rare-variant burden was evaluated in core HCM genes, extended cardiomyopathy genes, and candidate remodeling pathways. No prespecified gene set was significantly enriched in aneurysm cases. ALPK3 missense variants were identified only in non-aneurysm cases.

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory cohort, WES did not detect a clear rare coding variant burden signal associated with apical aneurysm.

articles.title: Postoperative Mortality and Risk Factors in Adults With Congenital Heart Disease Undergoing Cardiovascular Surgery: Insights From the Japanese Registry Data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) are prone to complications and usually require surgical intervention, but the surgical risk factors remain poorly defined.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We analyzed data from April 2013 to March 2023 in the nationwide Japanese Registry of All Cardiac and Vascular Disease-Diagnostic Procedure Combination (JROAD-DPC) to assess postoperative cardiac death and its predictors. This study included ACHD patients aged ≥18 years who underwent cardiovascular surgery, and the primary outcome was in-hospital death. A total of 10,535 patients (median age 53 [interquartile range 36-68] years; 50.4% female) were classified into mild (n=6,831), moderate (n=2,388), and severe (n=1,316) complexity groups. Among the 146 in-hospital deaths (1.4%), the highest mortality rate was observed in patients with severe complexity (2.4%). Multivariable analysis showed that age (hazard ratio [HR] 1.15), severe complexity (HR 1.77), renal disease (HR 1.74), pulmonary hypertension requiring medications (HR 2.01), chromosome abnormality (HR 6.22), and high-risk surgery (Fontan surgery or coronary artery bypass grafting) (HR 1.67) were significantly associated with increased in-hospital deaths. Subgroup analyses showed that age, renal disease, and high-risk surgery were prognostic factors in the mild group. Age was not significant in the moderate or severe groups.

CONCLUSIONS: The in-hospital mortality rate after cardiovascular surgery in ACHD was low overall but increased with disease complexity, supporting the need for disease complexity-based, individualized risk assessments in surgical planning.

articles.title: Troponin I Surveillance to Risk-Stratify Early Events After Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Initiation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Troponin surveillance may facilitate early detection of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated myocarditis, but mild elevations and baseline abnormalities complicate interpretation. We assessed early post-ICI troponin I (TnI) dynamics and the performance characteristics of clinically applicable peak TnI thresholds within 3 months of ICI initiation.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We analyzed 281 participants from a cardio-oncology surveillance program. TnI was measured at predefined intervals. Using peak TnI levels within 3 months, we evaluated the performance characteristics of candidate TnI thresholds for identifying adjudicated clinically significant TnI elevation associated with clinically meaningful conditions (e.g., ICI-associated myocarditis) at cut-offs of 50, 100, and 500 pg/mL. Eleven (3.9%) patients had elevated baseline TnI. Within 3 months, clinically significant TnI elevation occurred in 5 (1.8%) patients: ICI-associated myocarditis (n=2); immune-related myositis (n=1); pulmonary embolism (n=1); and seizures (n=1). A 50 pg/mL cut-off yielded 100% sensitivity, 96.0% specificity, 31.3% positive predictive value, and 100% negative predictive value. A 100 pg/mL cut-off demonstrated 100% sensitivity, 99.6% specificity, 83.3% positive predictive value, and 100% negative predictive value. A 500 pg/mL cut-off yielded 40.0% sensitivity and 100% specificity.

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory study, a peak TnI threshold of 100 pg/mL within 3 months identified all clinically significant events with high specificity. This threshold may serve as a pragmatic trigger for expedited evaluation of myocarditis and alternative etiologies.

articles.title: Screening Tools for Pediatric Palliative Care Activation in the PICU: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the performance of two pediatric palliative care screening tools, Pediatric Palliative Screening Scale (PaPaS) scale and Pediatric Intensive Care-Pediatric Palliative Care Screen (PIPPS) score, in critically ill children who died in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) and to assess their ability to distinguish patients with a palliative care trajectory.

DESIGN: Retrospective, single-center observational study.

SETTING: Nine-bed multidisciplinary PICU in a tertiary pediatric referral hospital.

PATIENTS: Children aged 28 days to 18 years who died in the PICU without prior palliative care activation.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Thirty patients were included: 20 with palliative care involvement and 10 without. PIPPS was positive in all patients with palliative care needs at admission, while PaPaS showed variable scores. PIPPS demonstrated higher sensitivity (1.00 vs. 0.95), specificity (0.75 vs. 0.67), and negative predictive value (1.00 vs. 0.89).

CONCLUSIONS: Both tools showed high sensitivity, but PIPPS appeared promising and feasible as an early bedside screening instrument in the PICU. However, prospective multicenter validation is required before PIPPS can be considered a validated tool for early PPC activation.

articles.title: [Mechanism of endothelial cell-derived S100A11 in promoting radiation-induced cardiac fibrosis in C57BL/6 mice].
articles.abstract: Objective: To investigate the role and mechanism of cardiac endothelial cell-derived S100A11 in promoting radiotherapy-induced cardiac fibrosis in C57BL/6 mice. Methods: Eight 6-week-old female C57BL/6 mice were randomly divided into a control group (n=4) and a radiotherapy group (n=4) using a random number table. The control group received no intervention, while the radiotherapy group received a single high-dose irradiation of 16 Gy to the left thorax to establish a mouse model of cardiac injury. At 12 weeks after radiotherapy, echocardiography was performed to measure left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), left ventricular fractional shortening (LVFS), and left ventricular internal dimension at end-systole (LVIDs). Western blotting was used to detect the expression of collagen type Ⅰ (COL Ⅰ) and alpha-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) in mouse cardiac tissue. The mouse cardiac endothelial cell line MCEC were divided into a control group and a radiotherapy group (medium was replaced after endothelial cell adherence, followed by radiotherapy and continued culture for 24 h before sample collection). The supernatants from the control and radiotherapy endothelial cell groups were mixed with complete medium at a 1∶1 ratio and used to culture primary cardiac fibroblasts extracted from C57BL/6 mouse cardiac tissue. These fibroblasts were divided into a control group and a treatment group. Western blotting was used to detect COL Ⅰ and α-SMA protein expression and a scratch assay was used to assess cell migration ability. Endothelial cells were divided into a control group and a radiotherapy group. Western blotting, quantitative real-time PCR, and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) were used to detect the expression and secretion of S100 calcium-binding protein A11 (S100A11) in endothelial cells. Small interfering RNA (siRNA) was used to knock down S100A11 gene expression in endothelial cells. Two siRNAs targeting S100A11 and a siRNA negative control group were separately transfected into endothelial cells. Western blotting was used to verify whether S100A11 expression in endothelial cells was successfully knocked down. The S100A11-knockdown endothelial cells were then subjected to radiotherapy and divided into a control group, siRNA-1 group, and siRNA-2 group. The sample collection method and the method for co-culturing primary fibroblasts were the same as described above, with groups designated as control, siRNA-1, and siRNA-2. Western blotting was used to detect COL Ⅰ and α-SMA protein expression. Primary fibroblasts were treated with recombinant S100A11 protein (100 ng/ml) for 24 h, and Western blotting and immunofluorescence were used to detect COL Ⅰ and α-SMA expression. Transcriptome sequencing was used to detect gene expression changes in primary fibroblasts treated with recombinant S100A11 protein for 24 h. Small interfering RNA (siRNA) was used to knock down integrin subunit beta-like 1 (ITGBL1) gene expression in primary fibroblasts. Two siRNAs targeting ITGBL1 (siRNA-1 and siRNA-2) (i.e., the siRNA group) and a siRNA negative control (si-NC) group were separately transfected into primary fibroblasts. Western blotting was used to verify knockdown of ITGBL1 expression in primary fibroblasts. Primary fibroblasts with ITGBL1 knockdown were cultured with recombinant S100A11 protein for 24 h, and Western blotting and immunofluorescence were used to detect COLⅠ and α-SMA protein expression. Results: Compared with the control group, echocardiography showed that LVEF and LVFS were lower in the radiotherapy group (both P<0.001), and COL Ⅰ and α-SMA protein expression levels in cardiac tissue were higher in the radiotherapy group (both P<0.001). Perivascular fibrotic tissue in the hearts of irradiated mice was increased than that of the control group (all P<0.05). The mRNA, protein, and supernatant protein expression of S100A11 in endothelial cells were higher in the radiotherapy group than in the control group (all P<0.001). The supernatant from radiotherapy-treated endothelial cells increased and α-SMA protein expression in primary fibroblasts compared with the control group (all P<0.05). In S100A11-knockdown endothelial cells subjected to radiotherapy, COL Ⅰ and α-SMA protein expression in primary fibroblasts in the siRNA groups were lower than in the control group (all P<0.05). Recombinant S100A11 protein increased COL Ⅰ and α-SMA protein expression in primary fibroblasts compared with the control group (all P<0.05). Transcriptome sequencing indicated that ITGBL1 gene expression levels were higher in primary fibroblasts treated with recombinant S100A11 protein than in the control group. After ITGBL1 knockdown, S100A11 promoted COL Ⅰ and α-SMA protein expression in primary fibroblasts were lower than in the control group (P<0.05). Conclusions: After radiotherapy, S100A11 expression and secretion are increased in cardiac endothelial cells. This effect can further activate cardiac fibroblasts in C57BL/6 mice and promote the development and progression of cardiac fibrosis.

articles.title: [Expert consensus on light therapy for the treatment of insomnia disorder (2026 edition)].
