authors: Sleep Disorders Rehabilitation Professional Committee of Chinese Association of Rehabilitation Medicine
Community and Primary Care Working Committee of Chinese Sleep Research Society
articles.abstract: Insomnia disorder is a common sleep disorder characterized by a high prevalence and a tendency toward chronicity, which may significantly affect patients' daytime functioning and quality of life. As a non-pharmacological physical intervention, light therapy may improve certain insomnia symptoms by modulating circadian phase and alertness, and has shown potential clinical value in patients with insomnia disorder, including those with circadian rhythm disturbances and selected comorbidities. However, existing studies remain limited by small sample sizes, substantial heterogeneity among study populations, inconsistent intervention parameters, and relatively short follow-up periods. Standardized application across different populations and clinical settings still lacks unified guidance. Based on this, the Chinese Sleep Research Society, the Sleep Disorders Rehabilitation Professional Committee of Chinese Association of Rehabilitation Medicine, and the Community and Primary Care Working Committee of Chinese Sleep Research Society, jointly organized a multidisciplinary expert panel to develop the Expert consensus on light therapy for the treatment of insomnia disorder (2026 edition). The consensus was developed based on the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. It systematically summarizes the mechanisms of action, clinical indications, treatment parameters, efficacy assessment, combination therapy, contraindications, and management of adverse events related to light therapy, and provides corresponding recommendations for special populations, including pregnant and postpartum women, elderly people, and adolescents. A total of 27 recommendations were formulated to provide systematic, standardized evidence-based guidance for the clinical application of light therapy in the treatment of insomnia disorder.

articles.title: [Expert consensus on the application of energy metabolism monitoring in nutritional support therapy (2026 edition)].
authors: China International Exchange and Promotive Association for Medical and Health Care Clinical Nutrition Health Branch
Chinese Society of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition
Chinese Nutrition Society Branch of Clinical Nutrition
articles.abstract: Energy metabolism is the foundation for sustaining life activities. Accurate measurement of energy expenditure is crucial for formulating individualized nutritional support therapy. This consensus was jointly initiated by the China International Exchange and Promotive Association for Medical and Health Care Clinical Nutrition Health Branch, Chinese Society of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition, and the Chinese Nutrition Society Branch of Clinical Nutrition. A multidisciplinary team of experts systematically reviewed the evidence on the application of indirect calorimetry (IC) in energy metabolism monitoring based on the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) system. This consensus proposes 11 clinical questions and 15 recommendations covering clinical scenarios including critically ill patients, obesity and metabolic diseases, chronic diseases (cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, renal, respiratory and hepatic diseases), malignant tumors, burns and trauma, as well as special populations (pregnant and lactating women, neonates). The consensus emphasizes that IC serves as an important reference method for assessing resting energy expenditure. In critically ill and burn or trauma patients, IC helps more accurately determine individual energy requirements and reduce the risks of underfeeding or overfeeding. In patients with chronic diseases, obesity, malignant tumors, pregnancy, and neonates, IC is mainly used to improve the individualization of energy requirement assessment; its impact on clinical endpoints (such as mortality and length of stay) remains to be confirmed by further high-quality studies. It also suggests alternative methods that when IC is unavailable. This consensus aims to provide evidence-based guidance for clinicians to apply indirect calorimetry rationally and standardly, thereby promoting precision in nutritional support therapy.

articles.title: [Exploration of efficacy and safety of breakthrough hemolysis and clonal intervention strategies in treating patients with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria].
articles.abstract: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH) is an acquired clonal disorder of hematopoietic stem cells, characterized by complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis, bone marrow failure, and thrombosis. In the era of complement inhibitors, the clinical outcomes of patients with PNH have markedly improved. However, breakthrough hemolysis (BTH) has emerged as an important clinical challenge affecting treatment efficacy. Current management strategies mainly rely on dose adjustment or switching of complement inhibitors, but these approaches have limited capacity to modify the underlying clonal nature of the disease. In recent years, increasing attention has been directed toward research on strategies aimed at modulating PNH clone burden. This article systematically reviews the therapeutic advances in complement inhibitors for PNH, with a focus on the pathogenesis and stratified management strategies of BTH. On this basis, it further explores the long-term persistence and dynamic evolutionary characteristics of PNH clones, and analyzes the impact of clone burden on treatment decision-making and long-term prognosis. In addition, combined with the previous clinical experience of our team, it discusses the theoretical basis for cytoreductive therapy combined with hematopoietic growth factors as a supplementary strategy for clone-targeted intervention, so as to provide new insights for the individualized treatment of PNH.

articles.title: [Clinical implementation pathway and standardized measures for the "five prescriptions" in the treatment of adult obesity in China].
articles.abstract: The prevalence of overweight and obesity continues to increase globally. Obesity is a chronic, relapsing disease and a major risk factor for cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, obstructive sleep apnea, and several malignancies. Drawing on current guidelines, expert consensus statements, systematic reviews, and pivotal randomized trials, this article proposes an integrated framework of five prescriptions for Chinese adults with obesity: nutrition, exercise, mental health and behavioral care, smoking cessation and alcohol restriction, and pharmacotherapy. Implementation begins with comprehensive assessment and risk stratification. Nutrition and exercise form the foundation, while mental health and behavioral support connect the interventions, sleep is managed through a stratified pathway. Smoking cessation and alcohol restriction support long-term risk reduction, and pharmacotherapy provides evidence-based intensification for eligible patients. This framework translates complex, long-term, relapse-prone obesity care into a standardized pathway that is assessable, prescribable, actionable, monitorable, iterative, and sustainable.

articles.title: Bedaquiline Experience in Treatment Refractory Nontuberculous Mycobacterial Lung Disease, a Retrospective Study at Two Referral Centers.
articles.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The treatment of NTM pulmonary disease is hindered by scarce therapeutic options. Bedaquiline is a diarylquinoline with activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis and a variety of pathogenic nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) that could help fill this unmet need, but clinical data are needed to support its use.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed the use of bedaquiline in patients with NTM pulmonary disease from National Jewish Health and the University of Texas Health Science Center Tyler between the years of 2013 and 2022.

RESULTS: Eighty-seven patients were included in the study. Most patients were female (66/87, 75.8%) and the mean age was 55 years. 54% had cavitary lung disease. People with cystic fibrosis made up 26.4% of the cohort. There were 46 patients with Mycobacterium avium complex, 36 patients with Mycobacterium abscessus and five patients with other mycobacterial infections. 64% of isolates had macrolide resistance, either inducible or mutational, 31% had amikacin resistance (MIC ≥ 64 𝜇g/ml) and 21.8% had both macrolide and amikacin resistance. The mean duration of antibiotic use prior to the initiation of bedaquiline was 32.8 months (0-165 months). The most common indication for bedaquiline use was treatment failure related to intolerance or resistance to antibiotics. Mean duration of bedaquiline use was 20 months (range 1-134 mos.). Bedaquiline was well tolerated: only 10% (9/87) of patients required discontinuation of treatment related to side effects of whom 4 reported adverse events related to bedaquiline, one with a rash, one with nausea and two with transaminase elevation. None of the patients discontinued therapy related to QTc prolongation. Ten patients had to discontinue bedaquiline due to lack of insurance coverage, although the mean exposure to bedaquiline in this group was 18 months (2-43 mo.) Once on bedaquiline, 46% had sputum cultures convert to negative (defined as two negative cultures over three months) and 40% were able to discontinue all therapy with 12 months of negative cultures.

CONCLUSION: In this cohort of treatment experienced patients with drug resistance or intolerance, bedaquiline was well-tolerated and led to cure in 40% of patients.

articles.title: Targeting inflammation during chronic heat stress improved intramuscular heat shock protein 70, myoblast differentiation, and muscle growth in finishing lambs.
articles.abstract: Chronic heat stress induces systemic inflammation and impairs growth performance in feedlot livestock. We sought to determine if anti-inflammatory interventions could improve muscle growth and efficiency in heat-stressed finishing lambs. Commercial wethers (40.8 ± 0.7 kg) were fed under heat stress (40 °C) and administered 0.15 mg/kg injectable dexamethasone every 72 h (n = 11), 1200 mg oral fish oil twice daily (n = 11), or no intervention (n = 11). Pair-fed controls were housed under thermoneutral conditions (19 °C, n = 12). Lambs were necropsied after 30 d. Heat stress-induced inflammation was characterized by greater (P < 0.05) circulating (i.e., extracellular) heat shock protein 70 (HSP70) and TNFα that followed a modest, transient increase (P < 0.05) in circulating cortisol. Heat stress also reduced (P < 0.05) circulating eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and skeletal muscle (i.e., intracellular) HSP70, which are anti-inflammatory. Daily fish oil partially or fully resolved (P < 0.05) heat stress effects on TNFα, cortisol, EPA, and intramuscular HSP70, but not circulating HSP70. Dexamethasone partially or fully resolved (P < 0.05) heat stress effects on cortisol, EPA, and intramuscular HSP70 but did not resolve TNFα and further worsened (P < 0.05) circulating HSP70. Heat stress-induced insulin resistance was indicated by greater (P < 0.05) circulating insulin and IGF-1 that was resolved (P < 0.05) by fish oil but not dexamethasone. Final bodyweights, average daily gain, and gain-to-feed ratios indicative of growth efficiency were reduced (P < 0.05) by heat stress but recovered (P < 0.05) by fish oil and dexamethasone. Live-animal estimates of ribeye area and fat-free muscle mass were reduced (P < 0.05) by heat stress, as was actual mass for 4 of 6 individual muscles weighed at necropsy. Poor muscle growth in heat-stressed lambs was facilitated in part by reductions (P < 0.05) in total (i.e., pax7+) and tended reductions (P < 0.10) in differentiated (i.e., myogenin+) myoblast populations. Differentiated (but not total) myoblasts tended to be recovered (P < 0.10) by fish oil and dexamethasone interventions, resulting in full or partial recovery of several muscle growth indicators. These findings show that induction of systemic inflammation contributes substantially to impaired muscle growth and efficiency in heat-stressed feedlot lambs. As such, inflammation is a feasible mechanistic target for improving outcomes of heat stress with anti-inflammatory bioactive nutrients.

articles.title: Extracellular Vesicles Shed from Senescent Neonatal Pulmonary Microvascular Endothelial Cells Contribute to Pulmonary Vascular Remodeling.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology
articles.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are critical mediators of intercellular communication but their role in bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) complicated by pulmonary hypertension (BPD-PH) is unclear. Here we test the hypothesis that hyperoxia induces neonatal pulmonary microvascular endothelial cell (PMEC) senescence and that EVs shed from these cells potentiate pulmonary vascular remodeling. Newborn PMECs exposed to 75% O2 had increased expression of senescence markers and young adult rats exposed to neonatal hyperoxia showed increased p16, p21 and p53 expression in pulmonary endothelial cells. In vivo, EVs isolated from the supernatant of senescent PMECs (senescent EVs) induced pulmonary vascular remodelling and PH in newborn rats. miRNA (miR) sequencing revealed 31 differentially expressed miRs in senescent EVs as compared to control EVs. Top upregulated miRs included miR-421, miR-4508, and miR-3960. Senescent EVs differentially regulated 271 genes in the lungs of newborn rats. The most downregulated gene was myocyte enhancer binding factor-2 (MEF2C), a known miR-421 target, involved in smooth cell plasticity. To further interrogate the mechanisms by which senescent EVs induce vascular remodelling, pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMs) were incubated with control and senescent EVs, and smooth muscle cell phenotype was assessed. Senescent EVs down-regulated MEF2C and induced a synthetic PASM phenotype. EV uptake inhibition and miR-421 antagomir partially restored MEF2C expression and attenuated these changes. Together, these findings demonstrate that hyperoxia induces PMEC senescence and EVs shed from these senescent cells deliver a miR-421-MEF2C signal that potentiates pulmonary vascular remodelling. Strategies targeting this axis may have important implications for the treatment of BPD-PH.

articles.title: Long-Term Outcomes After Coronary Absorb BVS Implantation Guided by Intravascular Imaging.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery implantation of the absorb bioresorbable vascular scaffold (BVS) without intravascular imaging (IVI) guidance resulted in greater adverse events compared with metallic drug-eluting stents during 3-year follow-up.

AIMS: We assessed the 10-year outcomes of BVS implanted with routine use of IVI guidance.

METHODS: Between November 2014 and October 2016, 100 consecutive patients in whom the operator elected to implant a BVS were treated with 190 BVS devices in 171 lesions at a single center in Brazil. IVI was performed before and after BVS implantation in all patients. Clinical follow-up was complete in all patients (no losses to follow-up) for at least 8.8 years.

RESULTS: Median follow-up was 9.5 years (25th percentile 9.2, 75th percentile 10.1), range 8.8-10.8 years. Through the latest follow-up, no patient experienced a cardiac death or definite scaffold thrombosis, and only one patient had a target-vessel MI (TVMI). Major adverse cardiac events (the composite of all-cause death, any MI, or any revascularization) occurred in 29 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimated 10-year rate 29.4%); target vessel failure (TVF) (the composite of cardiac death, TVMI, or ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization) occurred in 15 patients (10-year rate 15.0%); and target lesion failure (the composite of cardiac death, TVMI, or ischemia-driven target-lesion revascularization) occurred in 10 patients (10-year rate 10.0%). In the landmark analysis, TVF between 3 and 10 years occurred in 7 patients (7.6%).

CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center, non-randomized observational study, the long-term outcomes of BVS implantation in simple and complex coronary lesions with routine IVI guidance were favorable. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in adequately powered randomized studies.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Outcomes in Semaglutide Versus Tirzepatide Users With Obesity and Atherosclerotic Disease: A Target Trial Emulation.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Semaglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist, is approved for cardiovascular risk reduction in individuals with overweight or obesity and cardiovascular disease. Whether tirzepatide, a dual GLP-1 and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor agonist, has similar cardiovascular benefits remains unknown. The objective was to compare the effectiveness of semaglutide versus tirzepatide on the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in individuals with overweight or obesity and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) without diabetes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This active comparator, new user study emulated a trial using national claims data from Komodo Health. Eligible individuals had a history of ASCVD and, within 1 year prior to initiation: BMI ≥ 27 with a diagnosis of overweight or obesity, continuous insurance coverage and no diabetes or contraindications. Prior GLP-1 receptor agonist or obesity medication users were excluded. The primary outcome was a composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, hospitalization for heart failure or unstable angina, coronary revascularization and mortality (revised 5-point MACE). Secondary outcomes included revised 3-point MACE and individual endpoints. Hazard ratios were estimated using Cox models with inverse probability weighting.

RESULTS: There was a non-significant difference in risk of revised 5-point MACE (HR = 1.21, 95% CI: 0.99-1.51) or secondary outcomes between semaglutide and tirzepatide. Sensitivity analyses showed directionally consistent point estimates for revised 5-point MACE but highlighted sensitivity to decisions surrounding early events, off-label use, analytic approach and outcome definition.

CONCLUSIONS: Among adults with overweight or obesity and ASCVD without diabetes, there was no significant difference in cardiovascular risk between semaglutide and tirzepatide.

articles.title: Association Between Orforglipron and Blood Pressure in Adults With Obesity With or Without Type 2 Diabetes: Post Hoc Analyses From ATTAIN-1 and ATTAIN-2 Trials.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This post hoc analysis assessed the association between orforglipron and blood pressure in adults with obesity or overweight without (ATTAIN-1) and with Type 2 diabetes (T2D; ATTAIN-2).

METHODS: This study included ATTAIN-1 and ATTAIN-2 participants randomized to receive orforglipron (pooled doses) or placebo. A mixed model of repeated measures was used to assess changes in blood pressure across baseline subgroups at Week 72. The association between weight change and systolic blood pressure (SBP) was evaluated by exploratory mediation analysis. Blood-pressure-related adverse events were also reported.

RESULTS: Exploratory subgroup analyses reflected reductions in SBP across all baseline subgroups with no clear evidence of heterogeneity in ATTAIN-1 and ATTAIN-2 (all interaction p > 0.10). Reductions in diastolic blood pressure (DBP) were observed across most of the baseline subgroups in ATTAIN-1, while a greater reduction in DBP was observed among participants with baseline DBP ≥ 80 mmHg compared with those who had baseline DBP < 80 mmHg in ATTAIN-2 (interaction p = 0.002). At Week 72, numerically greater proportions of orforglipron-treated participants achieved study-visit-office normal blood pressure than placebo in ATTAIN-1 and -2. Mediation analysis suggests that 58.3% and 80.8% of the reduction in SBP was estimated to be mediated by orforglipron-induced weight reduction in ATTAIN-1 and -2, respectively (p < 0.001). Low blood pressure-related adverse events were uncommon but more frequent with orforglipron treatment than with placebo, and were mostly mild to moderate in severity.

CONCLUSION: In these post hoc analyses of ATTAIN-1 and -2, reductions in SBP were broadly consistent across baseline subgroups, with no clear evidence of heterogeneity. The changes were estimated to be largely mediated by weight loss, and potential weight-independent effects on blood pressure require further evaluation.

articles.title: Comprehensive Thyroid Assessment in a Prospective Japanese Cohort: A Cross-Sectional Baseline Analysis of Thyroid Function, Autoimmunity, and Ultrasonographic Findings.
articles.journal: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thyroid diseases can be evaluated using multiple modalities, including thyroid function tests, thyroid autoantibodies, ultrasonography, and 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography (FDG-PET). However, comprehensive data integrating these modalities in large cohorts remain limited. We aimed to characterize the prevalence and patterns of abnormal findings on thyroid examinations in a medical checkup setting.

METHODS: This was a cross-sectional baseline analysis of a prospective cohort of adults who underwent their initial comprehensive medical checkups between April 1, 2016, and December 31, 2021, at the Preemptive Medicine and Lifestyle Disease Research Center, Kyoto University Hospital. All participants underwent thyroid function tests, ultrasonography, and FDG-PET; anti-thyroperoxidase antibody (TPOAb) titers were measured in a subset.

RESULTS: Among 4407 participants without known thyroid disease (2643 males and 1764 females), the prevalence of thyroid dysfunction, increased blood flow on ultrasonography, diffuse thyroid FDG uptake, and thyroid nodules was 5.8%, 2.5%, 3.4%, and 39.7%, respectively; all were more frequent in females. Among 2420 participants with TPOAb measurements, TPOAb positivity was 7.2%. On the Roche Elecsys platform, TPOAb titers ≥128 IU/mL were associated with concurrent thyroid dysfunction, increased blood flow, and diffuse thyroid FDG uptake. Multivariate analyses identified age, sex, and thyroid volume as major determinants of thyroid function. Using data from 1840 participants without any thyroid abnormalities, we established sex-specific reference ranges for thyroid dimensions and found their correlations with age and body size.

CONCLUSIONS: This analysis provides epidemiological and physiological insights into thyroid health by integrating findings from thyroid function tests, ultrasonography, FDG-PET, and TPOAb measurements. Notably, higher TPOAb titers were associated with concurrent thyroid dysfunction and abnormalities, and age, sex, and thyroid volume were identified as major determinants of thyroid function. The rigorously defined healthy cohort enabled the establishment of sex-specific reference ranges for thyroid dimensions and confirmed associations between thyroid size, age, and body size. This study provides valuable evidence from a Japanese population, for which data have been limited to date. Furthermore, the present study highlights the associations among abnormal findings, relationships within thyroid physiology, and the concurrent associations of high-titer TPOAb with thyroid dysfunction and abnormalities.

articles.title: Microbiome and immune development in preterm infants receiving powdered human milk-based fortification from the PUFFIN trial.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the impact of powdered human milk-based fortification (PHMF) compared to powdered bovine milk-based fortification on gut microbiome and inflammation in preterm infants.

METHODS: Mechanistic study within randomised controlled trial in infants <32 weeks gestation or <1500 g birthweight, only receiving human milk and fully enterally fed without previous fortification, in two UK neonatal intensive care units (NICU). Stool and urine at recruitment (D0), weekly until day 21 (D21) and discharge. Microbiota (stool) and secretory immunoglobulin A (sIgA)/IgA (stool and urine) were evaluated at all time points and immune related proteins (IRP) (stool) at day 7 (D7) and D21.

RESULTS: Twenty-eight patients (14 per arm; median gestation 27.18 ± 2.42 weeks) participated. One hundred and twenty-nine stools and 109 urines were collected. Analysis of gut microbiota (111 stools), sIgA (113 stools and 108 urines), and IRPs (52 stools) was performed. Fortifier type did not significantly impact stool alpha or beta diversity or specific taxa and explained <5% of variance at any time point, with site being most influential (14.7% at day 14 [D14], p = 0.04; 25.7% at D21, p = 0.007). Stool but not urine sIgA was higher in PHMF recipients. Whilst fortifier type was not associated with IRPs from D7 to D21, NICU site impacted IRPs.

CONCLUSIONS: Fortifier type did not have a large impact on microbiota or IRPs but stool sIgA was higher in PHMF recipients. An association between NICU site and other outcomes was observed.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: The Preterm milk fortification in neonates (PUFFIN) study was prospectively registered ISRCTN 22484792.

articles.title: Na+/H+ Exchanger Isoform 1 Regulates Apoptosis Susceptibility in Pulmonary Arterial Smooth Muscle from the Sugen/Hypoxia model of Pulmonary Hypertension.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Lung cellular and molecular physiology
articles.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is characterized by vascular remodeling driven in part by apoptosis-resistant pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs). Na+/H+ exchanger isoform 1 (NHE1) regulates intracellular pH and plasma membrane cytoskeleton anchoring, but the role of NHE1 in PASMC apoptosis remains unclear. PASMCs were isolated from distal pulmonary arteries from control and Sugen/Hypoxia (SuHx) rats, a model of PH. NHE activity was measured via the ammonium pulse technique, protein via immunoblot, and apoptosis via Hoechst staining, Caspase-Glo® 3/7 Assay System and Annexin V/ propidium iodide immunofluorescence. NHE activity and NHE1 surface expression were increased in SuHx PASMCs compared to controls. Despite increased endoplasmic reticulum stress at baseline, SuHx PASMCs were resistant to apoptosis following hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) challenge. Inhibition of NHE activity with ethyl-isopropyl amiloride (EIPA) and NHE1 silencing with siRNA restored apoptosis in SuHx PASMCs. Conversely, NHE1 overexpression in control PASMCs conferred apoptosis resistance. Expression of mutant NHE1 constructs lacking ion translocation or ezrin binding also reduced H2O2-induced apoptosis. Mechanistically, H2O2 increased p38 phosphorylation (p-p38) in PASMCs from control, but not SuHx, rats, indicating impaired activation of this pro-apoptotic pathway. NHE1 suppression via EIPA or siRNA restored p-p38 in SuHx PASMCs, while overexpression of NHE1 (wild-type or mutants) suppressed p-p38 following apoptotic stimulation. Inhibition of p-p38 with SB203580 prevented the pro-apoptotic effect of EIPA, validating a role for p-p38 signaling in NHE1-mediated apoptosis resistance in SuHx PASMCs. These findings identify NHE1 as necessary and sufficient for PASMC apoptosis resistance in PH, by a mechanism involving suppression of p-p38.

articles.title: Quantifying contractile muscle fatigue during exercise in COPD using surface electromyography: from physiological rationale to clinical application.
Liver transplantation in congenital disorders of glycosylation: A systematic review.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To synthesize patient-level evidence on indications, immunosuppression, outcomes, and residual extrahepatic disease after liver transplantation (LTx) in congenital disorders of glycosylation (CDG).

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE was searched from inception to July 5, 2026, supplemented by backward and forward citation searching. Two reviewers independently screened records and full-text reports, linked duplicate patient descriptions, extracted data, and appraised reporting quality. Case reports and series providing individual-level LTx data were eligible. Owing to clinical heterogeneity, results were synthesized descriptively.

RESULTS: The searches yielded 42 records (PubMed/MEDLINE, n = 33; citation searching, n = 9). After removal of eight duplicate records, 34 unique records were screened; 25 were excluded by title and abstract. Nine full-text reports were assessed and all met the eligibility criteria. These publications described at least 12 distinct recipients with ATP6AP1-CDG (n = 5), PMM2-CDG (n = 2), CCDC115-CDG (n = 2), MPI-CDG (n = 1), COG6-CDG (n = 1), or ATP6AP2-CDG (n = 1). Age at first LTx ranged from 7 months to 28 years. Ten of 12 recipients (83.3%) were alive with a functioning graft at the latest reported assessment, although formal actuarial patient and graft survival could not be calculated. Successful LTx generally corrected hepatic synthetic dysfunction and liver-derived glycoprotein abnormalities, but immune, neurological, and pancreatic manifestations persisted.

CONCLUSIONS: LTx can rescue severe hepatic disease and provide liver-specific metabolic correction in selected CDG, but it should not be considered a systemic cure. Candidate selection and immunosuppression require multidisciplinary, genotype-informed assessment. Prospective standardized reporting is needed.

articles.title: Closed-Needle Abdominal Micro-Suction Fat Embolization for Distal Coronary Perforation.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Distal coronary artery perforation (CAP) during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is traditionally managed with embolic coils or autologous fat. However, fat embolization can be technically demanding due to complex tissue harvesting and delivery. We describe a closed-needle lower abdominal micro-suction technique enabling rapid percutaneous harvesting and direct microcatheter delivery of an autologous fat suspension without benchtop processing. An 18-gauge angiographic needle attached to a syringe pre-loaded with 2-3 mL of a 1:1 contrast-saline mixture is inserted into lower abdominal subcutaneous tissue under continuous manual negative pressure, aspirating 1-2 mL of fat-containing tissue fragments within ~10 s (total final volume ~3.5-5 mL). The resulting radiopaque suspension is delivered directly through a microcatheter using an inverted-syringe technique via small, incremental hand boluses of 0.25-0.5 mL until complete sealing is achieved. Descriptive histology confirmed mature adipose tissue fragments admixed with blood, fibrin, and clot. The technique was successfully deployed in two consecutive patients with Ellis type II and III distal CAP. Immediate angiographic sealing was achieved in both cases without open tissue processing or syringe-to-syringe transfer. At 6-month follow-up, both patients remained clinically stable without recurrent pericardial effusion or target-vessel failure. Closed-needle abdominal micro-suction is a rapid, low-resource, zero-transfer bailout technique for autologous fat embolization in high-acuity distal CAPs.

articles.title: Intranasal Pathogenesis-Adaptive Nanotherapeutics Reinstate Regenerative Competence for Post-Stroke Neural Repair.
articles.abstract: Poststroke neurorehabilitation is limited by the poor regenerative capacity of adult neurons. Although neural stem cells (NSCs) can generate new neurons, their reparative potential is constrained by inefficient delivery to cerebral lesions and a hostile regenerative niche. Here, analysis of a single-nucleus transcriptomic dataset revealed pronounced dysfunction and intercellular crosstalk among neurons, microglia, and NSCs, highlighting redox imbalance and impaired nitric oxide (NO) signaling as potential therapeutic targets. Guided by these findings, we develop FCeO2@GLp, a pathogenesis-adaptive nanotherapeutic integrating reactive oxygen species scavenging, NO replenishment and immune modulation within cerebral ischemic microenvironment. Following intranasal administration, FCeO2@GLp actively adheres to the olfactory epithelium (OE), reaches infarcted brain regions, releases cerium oxide (CeO2) nanozyme, fingolimod, and a NO donor in response to local acidity. This coordinated strategy alleviates oxidative stress, reprograms microglia, protects neurons, and enhances NSC proliferation and neuronal differentiation. Consequently, FCeO2@GLp effectively reduces infarct volume and cerebral edema during the acute phase, and improves long-term neurological function and survival, establishing a lesion-responsive strategy for poststroke neural repair.

articles.title: Electrical Storm Triggered by Conus Branch Occlusion During Elective Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Very Severe Aortic Stenosis: Rescue With Balloon Aortic Valvuloplasty Under Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: We report a case of very severe aortic stenosis (AS) in which side-branch occlusion during elective percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) precipitated life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias and hemodynamic collapse. The patient was a 72-year-old man with very severe AS who was scheduled to undergo a valve intervention. Preprocedural coronary angiography revealed a significant, newly developed stenosis in the right coronary artery, and an elective PCI was performed prior to valve treatment. Following intravascular lithotripsy and drug-eluting stent implantation, occlusion of the conus branch occurred, triggering recurrent ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation. Despite initiation of venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and intra-aortic balloon pump support, the patient's hemodynamic status did not improve. Because excessive afterload due to very severe AS was considered the principal pathophysiological mechanism, emergency balloon aortic valvuloplasty was performed. This resulted in rapid hemodynamic stabilization and complete resolution of ventricular arrhythmias. This case illustrates that even a minor side-branch occlusion during PCI can lead to catastrophic outcomes in patients with very severe AS. Furthermore, it highlights that mechanical circulatory support alone may be insufficient, and that prompt relief of valvular obstruction is essential. Careful consideration of the indications and sequence of coronary intervention through discussions with a heart team is warranted for patients with very severe AS.

articles.title: Structural Damage of Coronary Microcatheters During Chronic Total Occlusion Percutaneous Coronary Interventions: The Prospective Multicenter Cross Registry.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary microcatheters are essential in chronic total occlusion (CTO) percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), but their structural failure has mainly been described through passive surveillance.

AIMS: We aimed to determine the incidence, predictors, and procedural impact of microcatheter structural damage during contemporary CTO PCI.

METHODS: The prospective multicentre CROSS registry included 2137 CTO PCI procedures performed at high-volume centers between 2024 and 2025. Suspected damaged microcatheters underwent centralized assessment and were classified as grade 1 (superficial deformation), grade 2 (significant deformation without complete fracture), or grade 3 (complete fracture).

RESULTS: Structural damage occurred in 109 procedures (5.1%); 58.7%, 5.5%, and 35.8% were grade 1, 2, and 3, respectively. Independent predictors of structural microcatheter damage were moderate-to-severe calcification (adjusted OR, 1.93; 95% CI, 1.27-2.94), retrograde approach (adjusted OR, 1.71; 95% CI, 1.10-2.67), moderate-to-severe tortuosity (adjusted OR, 1.61; 95% CI, 1.04-2.50), and longer procedure duration (adjusted OR per 30-min increase, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.06-1.30). Structural damage was associated with increased periprocedural complications (25.7% vs. 7.7%; OR: 4.12, 95% CI: 2.60-6.52; p < 0.0001) and failed CTO PCI (11.0% vs. 3.1%; OR: 3.86, 95% CI: 2.01-7.39; p < 0.0001).

CONCLUSIONS: Structural microcatheter damage occurred in approximately 1 in 20 CTO PCIs and was associated with anatomical complexity, demanding procedural circumstances, and substantially worse procedural outcomes.

articles.title: Development and Validation of a Meal Detection-Based Tool for User Behavior and Meal Management Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Management of the timing and frequency of meal announcements remains a key determinant of postprandial glycemic control in hybrid automated insulin delivery (AID) systems. Tools that translate routine device data into clinically interpretable insights on meal management behavior for individual patients and broader cohorts remain limited. These tools can potentially provide clinicians and users objective data to formulate personalized meal-related recommendations to safely improve outcomes.

METHODS: We developed a framework to quantify meal management behavior from routine AID data. The framework combines a meal detection model and a behavioral classification module that categorizes events as on-time, late, or missed based on temporal relationship between detected meals and carbohydrate entries. The meal detection model was trained on data from adults with type 1 diabetes using MiniMed 780G system (NCT04479826) and evaluated in a validation cohort of 157 individuals with type 1 diabetes using advanced hybrid closed-loop (AHCL) (NCT03959423) system.

RESULTS: Meal events detection accuracy reached 96.9% in the validation cohort, with precision ≥89.6%, recall ≥93.9%, and area under the curve = 0.996. Application of the tool to the validation cohort showed that a higher proportion of on-time announcements correlated with higher time in range (TIR) (ρ = 0.375, q < 0.001) and lower hyperglycemia. Each 10% increase in on-time announcements corresponded to a 2.66% increase in TIR. Increasing delay of late announcements was associated with worse postprandial glycemic outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: This framework enables insights into meal announcement patterns that may support patient counseling, clinical decision support, and large-scale analyses in AHCL systems.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT04479826, NCT03959423.

articles.title: Introduction to the Special Theme Issue: Artificial Intelligence in Rheumatology Research, Education & Practice.
AREG/EGFR Signalling Primes Macrophage Pyroptosis Through an Autocrine Ccl2-Driven Amplification Loop.
articles.abstract: Amphiregulin (AREG) is an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) ligand that has been implicated in inflammatory responses, but its direct role in priming macrophage pyroptosis remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that AREG primes bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) for ATP-induced pyroptosis through an autocrine Ccl2-dependent positive-feedback loop that requires sustained NF-κB activation. RNA-sequencing and functional clustering analyses revealed that AREG and LPS induce both convergent metabolic reprogramming and divergent transcriptional programs in macrophages. Notably, the chemokine signalling pathway was uniquely enriched in AREG-treated cells, with marked upregulation of Ccl2, Cxcl1, Cxcl3 and Cxcl16. Mechanistically, AREG induced Ccl2 secretion in an EGFR-dependent manner. Pharmacological inhibition (mNOX-E36) or antibody-mediated neutralisation of Ccl2 dose-dependently suppressed Caspase1/GSDMD cleavage and IL-1β/IL-18 release, and attenuated NF-κB p65 phosphorylation and IκBα degradation during AREG plus ATP stimulation. Consistently, siRNA-mediated Ccl2 knockdown phenocopied these effects, confirming that autocrine Ccl2 signalling sustains NF-κB activation to drive AREG-primed pyroptosis. Collectively, these findings identify a previously unrecognised AREG/EGFR/Ccl2/NF-κB axis that primes macrophages for pyroptosis, highlighting Ccl2 as a potential therapeutic target in sepsis and other inflammatory diseases driven by this amplification loop.

articles.title: Construction of a Dicyanomethylene-4H-pyran-N,N'-Diphenyl-dihydrodibenzo[a,c]phenazine Conjugate for the Ratiometric Imaging of Lipid Droplets.
articles.abstract: The aberrant accumulation of lipid droplets (LDs) is a hallmark of a variety of human diseases including the metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. Here, we constructed a new fluorescent probe (DCM-DPAC-OMe) based on the conjugation between dicyanomethylene-4H-pyran (DCM) and an N,N'-diphenyl-dihydrodibenzo[a,c]phenazine (DPAC) derivative as a single-molecule ratiometric imaging agent for LDs. Interestingly, the introduction of the electron-withdrawing DCM group completely reverses the dual-emission pattern of DPAC. This mechanistic reversal was studied by theoretical and fluorescence-based analyses. The probe was used for the imaging of LDs in live cells exhibiting a ratiometric red-to-blue fluorescence emission shift when dissolved by in situ generated intracellular LDs.

articles.title: Single-Cell ICP-MS Quantification of Intracellular Chromium and Cell-Surface TNFR2 for Assessing Cr(III/VI)-Induced Lung Epithelial Injury and COPD-Relevant Responses.
articles.abstract: An integrated platform combining droplet microfluidics, lanthanide labeling, and inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) was proposed to quantify intracellular heavy metal and cell-surface protein at single-cell resolution. The workflow performs parallel measurements on homologous single-cell subsets to establish statistical correlations between metal accumulation and functional protein responses. Using tumor necrosis factor receptor 2 (TNFR2) as a model protein, we investigated the effects of atmospheric particulate matter-associated heavy metals on human lung epithelial cells (BEAS-2B). Several heavy metals trigger TNFR2 upregulation, with Cr(VI) exerting the most pronounced effect. The Cr(VI)-induced increase in TNFR2 expression was associated with elevated TNF-α release, higher intracellular ROS, and reduced SOD activity but did not correlate directly with intracellular Cr accumulation, likely due to distinct cellular uptake mechanisms between Cr(III) and Cr(VI). High-concentration Cr(III) exposure, however, led to intracellular Cr enrichment and provoked inflammatory responses. Integration of differential gene expression, TNF-α release, and TNFR2 expression support TNFR2 as a potential indicator of metal-induced oxidative stress, epithelial injury, and COPD-relevant inflammatory responses. This single-cell dual-parameter approach provides a new strategy for linking metal uptake to functional protein responses in environmental toxicology.

articles.title: A Minimally Invasive Diagnostic Platform Compatible with Tissue and Serum Analysis for Early Detection of Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease.
articles.abstract: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), one of the most prevalent chronic liver diseases, initially manifests as simple hepatic steatosis. Without timely intervention, it can progress to cirrhosis and ultimately hepatocellular carcinoma. Early diagnosis and intervention are therefore essential for slowing disease progression and reducing the risk of complications. However, effective minimally invasive methods for the early diagnosis of NAFLD remain limited in clinical practice, posing substantial challenges to large-scale screening. Emerging evidence indicates that during NAFLD progression, the mitochondrial membrane potential in hepatocytes gradually declines, accompanied by increasing spatial disorganization and pronounced alterations in the polarity of the mitochondrial microenvironment. Inspired by these findings, we developed a mitochondria-targeted, polarity-sensitive near-infrared fluorescent diagnostic system for the early detection of NAFLD. A series of probes (BS-X) were designed and synthesized based on a hemicyanine-triphenylamine fluorescent scaffold. Through comprehensive evaluation combining in vitro experiments and theoretical calculations, BS-1 was identified as the optimal probe, exhibiting excellent photophysical properties, low cytotoxicity, and high sensitivity to polarity variations. BS-1 efficiently targeted mitochondria (R = 0.89) and enabled real-time monitoring of dynamic changes in mitochondrial microenvironmental polarity. Notably, BS-1 enabled the detection of distinct disease-associated signals in both liver tissue and serum samples from NAFLD mice as early as one week after disease induction, achieving synchronous detection in hepatic tissue and serum and providing a novel molecular diagnostic tool for the early diagnosis of NAFLD.

articles.title: Isotope-Coded Click Chemistry-Enabled Enrichment for Reliable Profiling and Quantification of Carboxyl Metabolites.
articles.abstract: Carboxyl-containing metabolites are involved in diverse biological processes and are closely associated with metabolic diseases. However, their sensitive and reliable profiling by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) remains challenging because of low endogenous abundance, inefficient electrospray ionization, and substantial interference from complex biological matrices. Here, we developed a click chemistry-enabled enrichment (CCEE) strategy that integrates isotope-coded derivatization with chemoselective enrichment for sensitive and selective profiling and quantification of carboxyl-containing metabolites in biological samples. CCEE markedly improved detection sensitivity and chromatographic performance while effectively reducing matrix interference. The method also exhibited good linearity, reproducibility, and quantitative accuracy. Application of CCEE to human serum enabled broad profiling of the carboxyl submetabolome and revealed metabolic alterations associated with metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD). Targeted absolute quantification of representative metabolites further validated the observed alterations. Notably, serum bilirubin levels were significantly lower in individuals with MAFLD and strongly correlated with multiple clinical indicators. Overall, CCEE provides a sensitive and selective strategy for profiling and quantifying the carboxyl submetabolome, facilitating the investigation of metabolic dysregulation and the discovery of candidate biomarkers for metabolic diseases.

articles.title: Zeolite Nanoreactor Boosted Early Diagnosis of Acute Kidney Injury through a Multifunctional Biosensing Platform.
articles.abstract: Urinalysis plays a crucial role in the early clinical diagnosis of acute kidney injury (AKI). However, early-stage biomarker concentrations are at relatively low levels, and existing methods are limited by single-mode signal output, resulting in insufficient detection accuracy for early diagnosis. To address this, a zeolite nanoreactor-assisted electrochemiluminescence (ECL) and colorimetric sensing platform is developed for kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1) detection, a well-established urinary biomarker of AKI, with high sensitivity and specificity. After specific capture of KIM-1 by the antibody, the zeolite nanoreactor served as a high-capacity porous carrier for Ru(Bpy)32+ or horseradish peroxidase, which provides a nanoconfined environment to enhance ECL and colorimetric reactions, respectively. The multifunctional biosensing platform achieves dual signal output via ECL and colorimetric reactions, ranging from 0.01 pg mL-1 to 100 pg mL-1. The detection limits of KIM-1 via ECL and colorimetric analysis are 7.4 fg mL-1 and 1.0 fg mL-1, respectively. To further validate its application in a complicated environment, urine samples from drug-induced AKI mice were analyzed. The results show that both ECL and colorimetric analysis enable AKI diagnosis 6 h after drug induction, demonstrating the potential for non-invasive diagnosis in the early stages of AKI.

articles.title: LNA Blocker-Enhanced Multiplex Chip-Based Digital PCR for Ultrasensitive Quantification of Liver-Specific DNA Methylation in Plasma.
articles.abstract: Sensitive and selective quantification of rare methylated DNA in plasma remains a major analytical challenge. For methylation targets located in CpG-sparse regions, bisulfite conversion produces only subtle sequence differences between methylated and unmethylated alleles, thereby hindering selective amplification. Here, we report a blocker-enhanced multiplex chip-based digital PCR (cdPCR) strategy for the absolute quantification of liver-specific DNA methylation in plasma. The assay incorporates Locked Nucleic Acid (LNA)-modified blockers to selectively suppress unmethylated background templates, thereby enhancing single-base mismatch discrimination after bisulfite conversion. Seven liver-specific methylation sites within TBX15 were selected and organized into two quadruplex cdPCR panels together with an internal reference gene, enabling multiplex partition-level quantification. The platform achieved a limit of detection of 1 copy/μL, a limit of quantification of 0.2% methylation fraction, and excellent linearity over 1-10,000 copies/μL. In the primary cohort and independent external cohorts comprising 815 plasma samples, the resulting methylation profiles were used to develop diagnostic models using extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) and logistic regression. The XGBoost model distinguished hepatocellular carcinoma from cirrhosis with an AUC of 0.881 in the test set and retained strong performance in early-stage and seronegative disease, outperforming alpha-fetoprotein and des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin. Additional disease-control and pan-cancer cohorts supported the specificity of the methylation-based models. These results demonstrate that coupling LNA-mediated background suppression with chip-based digital partitioning enables selective and sensitive plasma methylation analysis and provides a practical analytical framework for low-abundance nucleic acid detection.

articles.title: Metabolic Bariatric Surgery Leads to Similar Benefits for Diabetes Management and Glycaemia in Remitters and Non-Remitters.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Metabolic bariatric surgery (MBS), for example, Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) can lead to diabetes remission. However, this crude dichotomous outcome fails to fully capture post-operative improvements in glycaemia and reduced medication burden in people who do not remit. The objectives of this research were to investigate predictors of diabetes remission in a multiethnic cohort and to detail post-operative improvements in glycaemia and diabetes management.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Prospective observational study of a discovery cohort comprising 67 adults with obesity and Type 2 diabetes, undergoing a standardised RYGB in the United Kingdom or Singapore. Diabetes remission at 12-15 months was the primary outcome. An adjusted HbA1c was calculated using measured HbA1c and the doses/types of diabetes medications to estimate HbA1c without medication. Findings were validated by retrospective clinical audit of a separate UK cohort of 195 individuals undergoing RYGB.

RESULTS: Diabetes remission was predicted by diabetes duration, measures of treatment intensity and resulting glycaemia (expressed as adjusted HbA1c) and post-prandial insulin secretion. Both remitters and non-remitters in the discovery cohort showed similar improvements in adjusted HbA1c (-38.2 ± 17.5 mmol/mol vs. -39.5 ± 15.5 mmol/mol, respectively, p = 0.739), a finding confirmed in the validation cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: While those who do not experience post-MBS remission have a longer diabetes duration and higher baseline adjusted HbA1c, they benefit similarly from improvements in glycaemia and de-escalation of treatment as those who remit. We suggest that the likelihood of diabetes remission, as assessed by scoring systems, should not be used as a criterion to recommend MBS to patients.

articles.title: The transition from childhood to adulthood in diabetes care: A qualitative evidence synthesis.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To systematically review and synthesise findings from qualitative studies regarding the transition process and transfer from paediatric to adult diabetes care, including perceived strengths and limitations of transition practices. Synthesising qualitative evidence from key stakeholders offers an opportunity to better understand how transition readiness is experienced, how it may influence engagement and outcomes, and why transition programs vary in effectiveness across settings.

METHODS: Qualitative evidence synthesis was completed of the diabetes transition process with articles published in English between 2018 and 2023, which is in line with our previously published quantitative systematic review. Studies were systematically identified and screened by searching six databases and PRISMA criteria were used. Search terms included the following MESH headings and keywords: (type 1 diabetes OR type 2 diabetes OR diabetes mellitus) AND (transfer to adult care OR transition to adult care OR transition readiness). Risk of bias and quality assessments were performed using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme. Both the strengths of weaknesses of each transition programme were extracted, as well as data integration across studies using a thematic synthesis approach.

RESULTS: In total, 15 publications were included of which two-thirds were from North America. Data were obtained from patients, parents/caregivers and healthcare professionals, using semi-structured interviews, surveys and focus groups, covering the full transition period. Three key themes were identified: (1) Expectation of greater autonomy/independence for the person with diabetes (PWD), (2) Loss of paediatric provider and insecurity about new healthcare provider (HCP), and (3) Lack of formal preparation for the transition from paediatrics to adult care. Perceived strengths and weaknesses of the different transition programmes underscore the need for a proactive approach, supporting a smooth transfer and facilitating the young person's independence and self-management capacity.

CONCLUSIONS: This systematic review of qualitative studies highlights the need to address the unique challenges of adolescents and young adults when transferred from paediatric to adult diabetes care and improve quality transition programmes. A smooth transition process demands a personalised approach from HCPs and system-level coordination across care teams is essential for supporting successful engagement within adult diabetes care.

articles.title: Effects of umbilical cord milking versus delayed cord clamping on cerebral oxygenation and ductus arteriosus closure in preterm infants: RCT.
articles.abstract: BackgroundDelayed cord clamping (DCC) and umbilical cord milking (UCM) are placental transfusion techniques that improve oxygen delivery and cardiac output. UCM enhances cerebral oxygenation without delaying resuscitation. Functional closure of the ductus arteriosus (DA) usually occurs within 48 hours after birth in full-term infants, with a high incidence of persistent DA in premature infants.ObjectiveTo investigate the effects of UCM and DCC on functional ductus arteriosus closure and cerebral tissue oxygenation.MethodsThis randomized controlled clinical trial included 100 preterm infants who were allocated to either the UCM group (n = 50) or the DCC group (n = 50). crSO2 and cfTOE were measured after resuscitation and at 12, 24, and 48 hours of life. Echocardiography was performed at 6, 12, 18, 24, and 48 hours of life to assess functional DA closure.ResultsRepeated-measures analysis showed no statistically significant between-group differences in changes in crSO2 (P = 0.194), cfTOE (P = 0.140), or functional DA closure (P = 0.372).ConclusionUCM and 60-second DCC showed no statistically significant differences in cerebral tissue oxygenation improvement or functional ductus arteriosus closure during the first 48 hours of life.

articles.title: Oops! I Cut It Again: Modulatory Proteolysis in Metabolic Health and Disease.
articles.journal: Obesity reviews : an official journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
articles.abstract: Proteolysis is an irreversible posttranslational modification that modulates protein stability, localization, interactions, and function. There are four intracellular proteolytic systems (calpains, caspases, ubiquitin-proteasome system, and lysosomes) and several extracellular proteases (metalloproteases and serine proteases). In this work, we review the diverse effects of proteolysis on the physiology of tissues vital for metabolic homeostasis as well as the contribution of proteolytic systems to the development of metabolic diseases. Proteolytic systems regulate processes essential for maintaining metabolic homeostasis, including insulin secretion, insulin sensitivity and glucose uptake, adipose tissue physiology, muscle mass, and lipid metabolism in the liver. Concordantly, dysregulation of these systems contributes to the development of metabolic diseases, such as metabolic syndrome, insulin resistance, obesity, sarcopenia, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, acting both as causal and aggravating factors.

articles.title: The road ahead for stem cell therapies in type 1 diabetes.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Type 1 diabetes results from autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing pancreatic β-cells. Although exogenous insulin remains the standard treatment, it does not restore physiological glucose regulation. Differentiation of human pluripotent stem cells into β-cells offers a scalable alternative to cadaveric islet transplantation and has progressed rapidly over the past decade, resulting in nine clinical trials at various stages of completion. Despite this progress, durable graft function remains constrained by two major challenges: the absence of key islet microenvironment components, such as vasculature, extracellular matrix and supporting cell types and continued vulnerability to autoimmune and alloimmune rejection.

METHODS & RESULTS: This review considers emerging technological approaches to overcome these barriers. Bioengineered niches, including multilineage organoids, functionalized hydrogels, decellularized matrices and bioprinting, aim to recreate the native islet microenvironment, while synthetic biology approaches, such as hypoimmune gene editing, CRISPR-based transcriptional control and stimulus-responsive survival circuits, seek to enhance grafts' resilience. Computational and single-cell approaches, including gene regulatory network analysis and digital twin frameworks, are beginning to provide predictive tools for benchmarking differentiation quality and forecasting graft outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Together, these complementary strategies, potentially tailored to individual patients, represent a realistic path towards safer, more effective and durable β-cell replacement therapies for type 1 diabetes.

articles.title: Smoking cessation duration and risk of acute myocardial infarction: A nationwide cohort study in Korea.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: While smoking cessation reduces cardiovascular risk, the precise timeline and temporal dynamics of risk reduction using granular time intervals remain poorly characterized. We aimed to estimate the association between smoking cessation duration and cardiovascular risk using 2-year intervals in a large Asian cohort.

DESIGN: Population-based retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: South Korea, using the nationwide National Health Insurance Service database (2002-2023).

PARTICIPANTS: 1 349 545 adults without prior acute myocardial infarction (AMI) or AMI requiring percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) who underwent at least four biennial health examinations, comprising 1 059 469 never smokers, 60 927 quitters and 229 149 current smokers.

MEASUREMENTS: Smoking status was classified from repeated self-reported examinations; quitters were grouped by cessation duration in 2-year intervals up to ≥8 years. Outcomes were incident AMI and AMI requiring PCI, over a mean follow-up of 10.6 years. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for demographic, clinical and lifestyle covariates including pack-years, with current smokers and never smokers as reference groups.

RESULTS: Using current smokers as reference, adjusted HRs decreased progressively with longer cessation duration. Statistically significant risk reduction was evident within 2-3 years [AMI: HR = 0.475, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.403-0.559; AMI requiring PCI: HR = 0.437, 95% CI = 0.359-0.532]. Quitters who maintained cessation for ≥8 years achieved risk levels comparable to never smokers (AMI: HR = 0.396, 95% CI = 0.284-0.552 vs. HR = 0.407, 95% CI = 0.386-0.429; AMI requiring PCI: HR = 0.321, 95% CI = 0.209-0.493 vs. HR = 0.366, 95% CI = 0.343-0.389).

SUMMARY: In a nationwide Korean cohort, the risk of acute myocardial infarction or acute myocardial infarction requiring percutaneous coronary intervention declined progressively with longer smoking cessation; after 8 or more years of sustained abstinence, risk was no longer distinguishable from that of never-smokers.

articles.title: Discrete choice experiments on preferences for financial incentives and nudges in health promotion and disease prevention: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Financial incentives and nudges are increasingly used to promote preventive activities, but little is known about individuals' preferences for their design characteristics or how these characteristics are valued relative to other components of preventive interventions. We conducted a systematic review of discrete choice experiments (DCEs) examining preferences for financial incentives and nudges in health promotion and disease prevention.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus for DCEs published between January 2000 and May 2025 and conducted in upper-middle- and high-income countries. Eligible studies examined health-promotion or disease prevention interventions and included at least one financial incentive- or nudge-related attribute. Data were extracted at the DCE level, adherence to methodologically good research practices was assessed using the International Society for Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research (ISPOR) checklist. We tabulated attribute frequencies and how often attributes ranked first by behavioral target. Relative attribute importance was extracted or calculated as each attribute's range of level coefficients divided by the sum of attribute ranges within each DCE. Pairwise comparison matrices summarized the proportion of within-DCE comparisons in which financial incentive or nudge attributes outranked other attributes.

RESULTS: Fifty-two studies, corresponding to 64 DCEs, were included. Financial incentive attributes accounted for 91 of the 300 identified attributes (30%) and were included in 47 DCEs (77%); nudge attributes accounted for 30 attributes (10%) and were included in 18 DCEs (30%). Preferences for financial incentive- and nudge-related attributes varied across preventive contexts. Financial incentives were more likely to rank highly in determining individual preferences when compared with intervention delivery and administration characteristics, but less so when outcome or cost attributes were included. Magnitude and delivery form emerged as the most salient financial incentive dimensions in terms of relative attribute importance. Most studies were of moderate-to-high quality and commonly used fractional factorial designs, four to six attributes, blocking, and mixed logit models.

CONCLUSIONS: Preferences for financial incentives and nudges are context-dependent and strongly shaped by intervention design. These findings can inform their incorporation into health promotion and disease prevention programs.

articles.title: Assessing caesarean sections using the Robson ten-group classification system: a record-based audit in a tertiary hospital in Bangladesh.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Caesarean section (CS) rates are rising globally, especially in low- and middle-income countries like Bangladesh, yet the factors driving this increase remain debated. In this context, the Robson 10-group classification system stratifies women undergoing delivery into mutually exclusive, clinically relevant obstetric groups based on five obstetric characteristics, enabling standardized comparison of CS rates. This study aimed to classify and analyze CS cases of a tertiary care hospital using the Robson 10-group classification.

METHODS: A retrospective record-based descriptive audit was conducted at the Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, Dhaka, from January to June 2023. Data were collected from hospital records, and CS cases were classified using the Robson 10-group classification system. Descriptive statistics summarized maternal characteristics, pregnancy-related factors, and indications of CS.

RESULTS: Among 1,949 deliveries, 1,269 (65%) were CS, with 1,266 included in the final analysis. The mean maternal age was 26.5 (SD 5.2) years, and 41% were nulliparous. Most pregnancies were singleton (98.5%), term (82%), and cephalic in presentation (89%). The largest contributor to CS was Group 5 (previous CS with a singleton cephalic pregnancy at term), accounting for 37% of cases, followed by Group 10 (preterm singleton cephalic pregnancies) at 14%. Nulliparous women with spontaneous labor (Group 1) contributed 11%, while induced labor or pre-labor CS (Group 2) made up 13.6%. The most common indications for CS were previous CS (43%), fetal distress (26%), and failure of labor to progress (19%).

CONCLUSION: We observed a high CS rate, with previous CS being the largest contributor. Fetal distress and labor dystocia were commonly recorded indications, including among term cephalic groups, highlighting areas that warrant further prospective clinical audit.

articles.title: Considerations on external validation, potential data leakage, and model selection in a PET/CT-based radiomics model predicting residual disease in ovarian cancer.
articles.abstract: Ye et al. recently reported that a PET/CT-based radiomics model incorporating clinical variables and using a support vector machine classifier outperformed conventional scoring systems in predicting complete cytoreduction in ovarian cancer (J Ovarian Res 2026). We appreciate this valuable contribution and wish to raise three points for consideration. First, although the validation cohort was held out from model development, it shares institution and scanner platform with part of the training set. The Siemens platform, which contributed 103 of 153 training patients, was not represented in the validation cohort. The results may therefore primarily reflect reproducibility on the GE platform, and broader cross-center or cross-scanner generalizability may warrant further evaluation. Second, SMOTE oversampling and mRMR feature selection are described as applied to the entire training cohort before nested cross-validation; if this reflects the actual workflow, fold-level data leakage could be a consideration. Third, selecting the SVM from seven models using identical cross-validation estimates and reporting the maximum could, in principle, introduce some optimistic selection bias. These points are offered in the hope of further strengthening the evidence base for broader multicenter use.

articles.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Echocardiography has evolved substantially since its introduction in 1954. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers transformative potential for image acquisition, quantification, interpretation, and reporting. Despite growing research interest, a comprehensive evaluation of the historical trends and evolution of AI in echocardiography is lacking. The study aimed to conduct a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of the global research landscape in this field.

METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted using the Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection databases for publications on AI in echocardiography from inception through November 10, 2025; no language filter was applied. Data analysis was performed using Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Access, and IBM SPSS Statistics. In addition, bibliometric mapping and data visualization were conducted.

RESULTS: Overall, 2682 publications received 35,083 citations (mean, 13.08 citations per publication), spanning 1984-2025. Original articles, conference papers, and review articles accounted for 87.4% and 98.5% of total publications and citations, respectively. Publication output remained limited until approximately 2015, rose gradually thereafter, and accelerated markedly after 2018, with similar output in 2024 and 2025. The United States led in both publication volume and total citations, followed by China and the United Kingdom. The United States also had the highest collaboration link strength, and seven of the top 10 institutions were in North America (six in the United States and one in Canada). Mayo Clinic ranked first, with 142 publications and 3604 citations, and had the earliest first indexed publication among the top institutions (1992). The journal JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging ranked first in both total citations (1,911) and citations per publication (36.75). "Echocardiography," "deep learning," "artificial intelligence," and "machine learning" were the most frequently used terms. The thematic evolution showed continuity of algorithmic-centric themes (1984-2019) with emerging clinically oriented themes (2020-2025).

CONCLUSIONS: This comprehensive bibliometric analysis highlights the rapid expansion of AI research in echocardiography, characterized by an accelerating publication output and emerging clinically oriented research topics. These findings reflect growing research interest in integrating AI into echocardiographic practice and highlight the need for future research prioritizing multicenter validation, clinical translation, and equitable real-world implementation.

articles.title: Outcomes and safety of intravenous thrombolysis in minor ischaemic stroke: a real-world retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The benefit-risk profile of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) in minor ischaemic stroke remains controversial. We evaluated real-world outcomes and safety of IVT in a centre with a liberal thrombolysis policy.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of consecutive adult patients treated with IVT for suspected acute ischaemic stroke with admission NIHSS 0-5 at Stavanger University Hospital between 2008 and 2023. A liberal thrombolysis policy was defined as a treatment threshold that does not exclude patients on the basis of a low NIHSS score or apparently non-disabling symptoms alone. Patients were stratified into NIHSS 0-2 and NIHSS 3-5 subgroups. Outcomes included favourable early neurological status, defined as NIHSS 0-1 within 24 h, functional independence at 90 days (mRS 0-2), poor outcome (mRS 3-6), stroke mimic diagnosis, and symptomatic intracranial haemorrhage (sICH). Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed in confirmed stroke cases, excluding stroke mimics.

RESULTS: Among 2,008 IVT-treated patients, 1270 (63%) had admission NIHSS 0-5: 744 (59%) had NIHSS 0-2 and 526 (41%) had NIHSS 3-5. Stroke mimics accounted for 335 cases (26%) and were more frequent in the NIHSS 0-2 group than in the NIHSS 3-5 group (29% versus 23%; p = 0.041). Among patients with available 90-day mRS, 602/697 (86%) achieved functional independence, with higher rates in the NIHSS 0-2 group than in the NIHSS 3-5 group (93% vs. 76%; p < 0.001). sICH occurred in four patients (< 1%), with no events among stroke mimics. In adjusted analyses restricted to confirmed stroke cases, NIHSS 0-2 was associated with higher odds of favourable early neurological status and functional independence compared with NIHSS 3-5.

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort from a centre with a liberal thrombolysis policy, IVT-treated patients with minor stroke symptoms had favourable functional outcomes and very low complication rates of sICH. The contribution of this cohort lies in describing what a liberal thrombolysis policy produces in unselected routine practice, as opposed to the narrowly defined populations enrolled in randomised trials. These findings provide clinically relevant safety data, but they cannot demonstrate efficacy and should be interpreted descriptively in the absence of an untreated comparator group.

articles.title: Analgesic and clinical side effects of paracetamol and meloxicam in female dogs after elective ovariectomy or ovariohysterectomy - randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This prospective, randomized, blinded, controlled clinical trial aimed at comparing the analgesic and antihyperalgesic effect of paracetamol and meloxicam following elective ovariectomy or ovariohysterectomy in healthy female dogs. In addition, it aimed at evaluating gastrointestinal side effects up to 48 h after surgery. Standardised anaesthesia protocol was utilised in all dogs and, at the end of the surgery, either meloxicam (0.2 mg/kg, Group M, n = 15 dogs) or paracetamol (10 mg/kg, Group P, n = 15 dogs) was administered intravenously. Pain was evaluated at 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 h after the administration of either paracetamol or meloxicam using short form of Glasgow composite pain scale (GCPS-SF). Rescue analgesia with intravenous methadone (0.2 mg/kg) was administered in case of ≥ 6 over 24 points. The success rate of each treatment was calculated based on the need of rescue analgesia within 6 h after surgery. Subsequently, the success rate was assessed for non-inferiority between treatments. The non-inferiority margin was set as -33%. Mechanical nociceptive thresholds and sensitivity to Von Frey filaments were tested at 2, 4 and 6 h after the administration either paracetamol or meloxicam. Once discharged, animals were remotely evaluated through a standardized questionnaire.

RESULTS: Rescue analgesia was administered at the hospital during the 6-hour post-operative period in a total of 15 dogs without difference between groups (p = 0.358). The success rate for analgesia was (9/15) 60% and (6/15) 40% in group M and P, respectively. The lower limit of the 95% CI of the difference for success rate (-55%, 15.5%) was lower than the margin set for non-inferiority (-33%) and therefore the non-inferiority of the group P versus group M was not confirmed. Mechanical sensitivity increased in both group after surgery. Mild self-limiting gastrointestinal side effects were detected in both groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Dogs receiving paracetamol needed more rescue analgesia than dogs receiving meloxicam in the post-operative period. The rate of success with both drugs was lower than expected. Frequent assessment of pain is mandatory to ensure efficient analgesia also beyond the first post-operative day and future studies are warranted to validate methods for out-of-hospital pain assessment.

articles.title: Impact of early versus delayed mobilization after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair in small and medium-sized tears: a prospective randomized study.
articles.journal: Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare early versus delayed mobilization following arthroscopic single-row knotless rotator cuff repair for small and medium-sized tears, performed in the beach-chair position without the use of an abduction sling.

METHODS: A prospective randomized study was conducted on 70 patients aged 20-70 years with small and medium-sized full-thickness supraspinatus tears repaired using single-row knotless suture anchors (one or two depending on tear size). Patients were assigned to early mobilization (EPM, n = 35) or delayed mobilization (DPM, n = 35). Outcomes were assessed using range of motion (ROM), pain (VAS), Constant-Murley and UCLA scores, and MRI tendon integrity at 12 months.

RESULTS: EPM patients showed faster ROM recovery at 3 months (mean 130° vs. 115°; p = 0.02), but one re-tear (2.8%) occurred in this group compared to DPM, where no re-tears occurred. At 12 months, both groups achieved comparable functional and pain outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Early mobilization accelerates short-term ROM recovery, whereas both early and delayed protocols result in comparable functional and pain outcomes by 12 months. Given the limited number of retear events and the absence of a prespecified tear size subgroup analysis, no definitive recommendation can be made regarding a differential mobilization strategy according to tear size.

articles.title: Hearing assistance technologies and social health among individuals with care and support needs: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hearing loss can affect communication, social interaction, participation, and the maintenance of social relationships, particularly among individuals who require care or support in everyday life. Hearing assistance technologies (HATs) may facilitate communication, but their relationship with the multiple dimensions of social health remains insufficiently understood. A multidimensional social-health framework encompassing Capacity, Independence, Social Participation, Structure, Function, and Appraisal provides a basis for examining these relationships beyond individual hearing outcomes. This scoping review aimed to map the existing evidence on HATs in relation to social health among individuals with care and support needs.

METHODS: This scoping review followed the PRISMA-ScR guidelines and the methodological framework proposed by Arksey and O'Malley and further refined by Levac. PubMed, CINAHL, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, Ovid MEDLINE, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore were searched. Studies were eligible if they included individuals aged ≥ 18 years with care and support needs and examined HATs in relation to findings relevant to social health. Data were charted and synthesised descriptively, and findings were organised according to the six domains of the multidimensional social-health framework, comprising Capacity, Independence, Social Participation, Structure, Function, and Appraisal.

RESULTS: The searches identified 1,145 records, of which 21 studies met the inclusion criteria. The included samples were predominantly older.
