Findings were most frequently mapped to the Appraisal and Social Participation domains, whereas Structure and Function were comparatively underrepresented. Intervention findings included improvements in communication-related outcomes and reductions in hearing-related participation restrictions, whereas findings for loneliness, relationship satisfaction, social-network characteristics, and broader social engagement were less consistent. Qualitative findings highlighted stigma and perceived social judgement, with the social acceptability of hearing technologies also described in relation to everyday interaction and technology use.

CONCLUSIONS: Evidence on HATs in relation to social health among individuals with care and support needs remains heterogeneous and uneven across social-health domains. Limited attention to the structural and functional dimensions of social relationships highlights the need for more comprehensive assessment of social health in hearing-care research. Future studies should adopt longitudinal, network-sensitive, and culturally responsive approaches and consider the interpersonal, environmental, and care contexts in which HATs are used.

articles.title: Elevated circulating activin A is associated with disease severity in advanced steatotic liver disease (SLD).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) is a major contributor to the global burden of chronic liver disease and is linked to liver fibrosis. Emerging evidence implicates activin A in this process, but its role remains unclear due to conflicting findings. This cross-sectional study examines circulating levels of activin A and its endogenous inhibitor follistatin in individuals with metabolic dysfunction and evaluates their associations with clinical indicators of steatosis and fibrosis.

METHODS: Plasma activin A and follistatin were measured with ELISA in 309 participants with type 2 diabetes (T2D) with or without SLD and in 97 participants with SLD-related cirrhosis. Hepatic fat was assessed using 1H-MRS-PDFF or MRI-PDFF, or if unavailable, controlled attenuation parameter (CAP). Liver stiffness was measured with vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE).

RESULTS: In the diabetes cohort, participants with steatosis and fibrosis had higher activin A concentrations than participants with neither steatosis nor fibrosis (0.400 ng/mL vs. 0.285 ng/mL, P = 0.036). In the cirrhosis cohort, activin A correlated strongly with liver stiffness (ρ = 0.696, P < 0.001). Participants with VCTE suggestive of compensated advanced chronic liver disease (cACLD) and clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) exhibited significantly higher activin A concentrations than participants without (0.546 vs. 0.307 ng/mL, P < 0.001 and 0.624 vs. 0.396 ng/mL, P < 0.001, respectively). In this study, neither follistatin nor the activin A-to-follistatin ratio​ was associated with steatosis or fibrosis.

CONCLUSIONS: Activin A was associated with liver stiffness and was higher in participants with SLD-related cirrhosis.

articles.title: Knowledge and Self-Reported Practice Gaps in Nurses' Application of Vacuum-Assisted Wound Closure Therapy: A Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
AIM(S): To assess nurses' knowledge and self-reported practices regarding the clinical application of vacuum-assisted wound closure therapy and to examine the relationship between knowledge and self-reported practice.

DESIGN: Multicountry descriptive-analytical cross-sectional survey.

METHODS: A multicountry cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 1814 bedside nurses working in medical, surgical, intensive care, emergency, outpatient and operating-room settings in Palestine, Iraq, Saudi Arabia and Egypt. Participants completed a 37-item knowledge questionnaire and a 23-item self-reported practice checklist. Satisfactory classifications were defined at ≥ 75% (knowledge ≥ 28/37; self-reported practice ≥ 18/23). Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and hierarchical multiple linear regression were used. Workplace/country was modelled as a fixed categorical predictor; hospital-level clustering could not be modelled because hospital identifiers were unavailable.

RESULTS: Among 1814 nurses, none of the knowledge-domain scores reached the prespecified 75% benchmark; precautions (44.5%) and total knowledge (44.0%) were lowest. Overall, 79.4% were classified below the practice benchmark. Knowledge correlated positively with self-reported practice (r = 0.512, p < 0.001). In the adjusted practice model, higher knowledge (B = 0.129, 95% CI 0.105 to 0.153) and previous training (B = 1.077, 95% CI 0.687 to 1.467) were associated with higher practice scores. The practice model had high explained variance (R2 = 0.7858), and the large workplace coefficients require cautious interpretation because hospital-level clustering was not modelled.

CONCLUSION: Substantial gaps in knowledge and self-reported guideline-based practice were identified among nurses using vacuum-assisted wound closure therapy, particularly in safety-related decision-making and the consistent completion of recommended care steps. These findings reflect self-reported behaviour and should not be interpreted as direct observations of clinical practice or patient outcomes.

IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: Standardized guideline-driven education, competency assessment, and refresher training should be considered, with emphasis on indications and contraindications, precautions, device troubleshooting, monitoring and documentation. Future evaluations should verify practice using objective methods and assess patient-level outcomes before inferring effects on safety or wound healing.

IMPACT: What problem did the study address? Variation and gaps in nurses' knowledge and self-reported guideline-based practice when using vacuum-assisted wound closure therapy; the study did not directly measure patient safety or healing outcomes. What were the main findings? No knowledge domain reached the study-specific 75% benchmark; 79.4% of nurses were classified below the practice benchmark, and knowledge was moderately correlated with self-reported practice (r = 0.512, p < 0.001). Higher knowledge and previous training were independently associated with higher self-reported practice scores, although large workplace effects require cautious contextual interpretation. Where and on whom will the research have an impact? The findings inform nurse educators, clinical leaders and wound care services in hospitals using vacuum-assisted wound closure therapy across the Middle East and North Africa clinical settings.

REPORTING METHOD: This study followed the Enhancing Quality and Transparency of Health Research network guidance and used the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology checklist for cross-sectional studies.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Patients, service users, caregivers and members of the public were not involved in the design, conduct, analysis, interpretation, or manuscript preparation because the research focused on nurses' knowledge and self-reported clinical practices.

articles.title: Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage and myositis complicating eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis: a case report and narrative review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is an uncommon antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis characterized by asthma, eosinophilia, and multisystem involvement. Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage and myositis are both infrequent manifestations of EGPA, and their co-occurrence in the same patient has rarely been reported.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 46-year-old man with adult-onset asthma, chronic sinusitis, and marked peripheral eosinophilia was diagnosed with EGPA in 2015. Over six years of follow-up, he had recurrent pulmonary relapses with migratory infiltrates and developed gastrointestinal involvement, nondilated cardiomyopathy, coronary artery disease, myositis, and diffuse alveolar hemorrhage; he was positive for myeloperoxidase (MPO)-ANCA. Disease activity persisted despite high-dose glucocorticoids, azathioprine, cyclophosphamide, and mycophenolate mofetil. Because the disease was severe, organ-threatening, and predominantly vasculitic, an anti-interleukin-5 agent was not chosen for remission induction; instead, rituximab was started and induced sustained remission.

CONCLUSION: This case illustrates that refractory, MPO-ANCA-positive EGPA may respond to B-cell depletion with rituximab. The randomized REOVAS trial did not show rituximab to be superior to conventional remission-induction therapy; however, it was not designed to establish equivalence with cyclophosphamide in severe disease, and the optimal strategy for severe refractory disease remains undefined. ANCA status, together with the pattern and severity of organ involvement, may help individualize treatment in this setting.

articles.title: The roles of ROCK1 and ROCK2 in cardiopulmonary and fibrotic disease: considerations for pan-ROCK inhibition as a therapeutic approach.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Rho-associated protein kinase (ROCK) isoforms, ROCK1 and ROCK2, are central regulators of cellular functions fundamental to the pathogenesis of cardiopulmonary and fibrotic diseases. Evidence from animal and cellular models demonstrates ROCK signaling attenuation exerts potent effects on the dysregulated hyperproliferative, fibrotic, and contractile cellular components of the vascular wall and lung parenchyma. These aberrant cellular processes are central to the pathobiology of diverse cardiopulmonary diseases, including pulmonary hypertension and interstitial lung disease, where effective treatment options remain limited. Both pan-ROCK and ROCK2-selective inhibitors are approved for various diseases. The ongoing development of more potent or isoform-selective ROCK inhibitors across emerging indications highlights an unrealized potential.

AREAS COVERED: The roles of ROCK1 and ROCK2 in tissue remodeling, inflammatory recruitment, and dysfunction in multiple cell types. Searches utilized keywords: 'pulmonary hypertension' or 'cardiopulmonary fibrosis' AND variations on 'ROCK inhibitor' and hand searching of key publications.

EXPERT OPINION: Evidence suggests that pan-ROCK inhibitors may have certain advantages over ROCK2-selective agents for complex cardiopulmonary and fibrotic diseases, as each isoform plays distinct, non-redundant roles in fibrosis and inflammation. Concerns about hypotension as a dose-limiting side effect unique to pan-ROCK inhibition versus ROCK2 inhibition are increasingly unsupported by clinical data.

articles.title: The efficacy of add on cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) to symptomatic patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction on sacubitril/valsartan treatment as regards left ventricle reverse remodeling and functional improvement.
articles.journal: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) represents a substantial worldwide healthcare burden, with nearly 26 million people affected. CRT is widely recommended for HFrEF patients with QRS duration > 150 msec, but its role in those with QRS duration of 130-149 msec remains debated. The objective was to evaluate whether adding CRT improves LV reverse remodeling and functional status in symptomatic HFrEF patients receiving maximally tolerated sacubitril/valsartan with QRS duration of 130-149 msec.

METHODS: This study included 100 patients with HFrEF (≤ 35%) treated with maximally tolerated sacubitril/valsartan and having LBBB morphology with QRS duration of 130-149 msec. Patients were classified into two groups: those receiving CRT and those maintained on medical therapy without CRT. Clinical status, QRS duration, and echocardiographic findings were reassessed after 6 months and compared between groups.

RESULTS: At 6 months, NYHA class improvement occurred more frequently with CRT than without CRT (37 vs. 20 patients, P = 0.004). The decline in end-systolic volume was greater in the CRT group (mean change, 11.42 ± 7.30 vs. 3.54 ± 6.41, P < 0.001). Ejection fraction also showed greater improvement with CRT (mean change, 4.24 ± 3.17 vs. 1.30 ± 2.35, P < 0.001). Hospitalization occurred less frequently in the CRT group (46% vs. 70%, P = 0.03). No deaths were observed in either group throughout follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: In symptomatic HFrEF patients receiving maximally tolerated sacubitril/valsartan with QRS duration of 130-149 msec, adjunctive CRT was associated with greater LV reverse remodeling, improved functional status, and fewer hospitalizations.

articles.title: Genetically predicted lipoprotein(a), first and recurrent venous thromboembolism, and coagulation proteins: evidence against causal relationships.
articles.abstract: Lipoprotein(a) exhibits in vitro antifibrinolytic properties, though it remains uncertain whether this translates into an effect on thromboembolic disease risk. We applied Mendelian randomization (MR) to evaluate the relationship between genetically predicted lipoprotein(a) levels, venous thromboembolism (VTE), and circulating coagulation protein levels. We instrumented lipoprotein(a) using two genetic variants (rs10455872 and rs3798220) that explain 36% of circulating lipoprotein(a) variance. The primary outcomes were first (81,190 cases) and recurrent VTE (1,775 cases). Comparator outcomes included coronary artery disease (181,522 cases) and calcific aortic stenosis (13,765 cases). We performed MR analyses to estimate the association of a genetically predicted 100 nmol/L increase in lipoprotein(a) with each outcome. In exploratory analyses, we tested associations with levels of 35 coagulation proteins in the UK Biobank (n = 46,218) and deCODE (n = 35,559) cohorts. Genetically predicted lipoprotein(a) was associated with a small reduction in risk of first VTE (odds ratio [OR] 0.98, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.96-0.99, P = 0.002), though this was not supported by colocalization (posterior=12%), suggesting that the MR association was driven by genetic confounding. There was no association with recurrent VTE (hazard ratio 1.03, 95% CI 0.91-1.16, P = 0.68). In contrast, genetically predicted lipoprotein(a) was strongly associated with increased risk of coronary artery disease (OR 1.31, 95% CI 1.29-1.33) and calcific aortic stenosis (OR 1.35, 95% CI 1.30-1.40). After multiple testing correction, genetically predicted lipoprotein(a) had no significant association with any coagulation proteins. Human genetic evidence does not support a clinically meaningful role for lipoprotein(a) in VTE risk. These findings support targeting of lipoprotein(a)-lowering therapies toward atherosclerotic and valvular diseases rather than thromboembolic indications.

articles.title: Safety and clinical outcomes of intravenous thrombolysis in stroke mimics compared with acute ischemic stroke: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) is the cornerstone of hyperacute care for acute ischemic stroke (AIS); however, increasingly compressed door-to-needle times mean some stroke mimics (SM) receive thrombolysis. We compared safety, mortality, functional, and disposition outcomes of IVT in SM versus confirmed AIS and assessed whether baseline neurological deficit severity modified these outcomes. We searched five databases up to June 2026 for IVT outcomes in adult SM versus AIS. We assessed risk of bias using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB-2) tool. We pooled 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using fixed- or random-effects models in R, with subgroup analyses by baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score (≤ 7 versus > 7). Twenty-seven cohort studies and one RCT were included, involving approximately 285,000 patients. Compared with AIS, SM had significantly lower odds of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (OR 0.18; 95% CI 0.12-0.27), any intracranial hemorrhage (OR 0.12; 0.07-0.22), in-hospital mortality (OR 0.24; 0.06-0.94), and 3-month mortality (OR 0.24; 0.15-0.39). SM were also more likely to achieve functional independence (mRS 0-1) at discharge (OR 12.04) and 3 months (OR 3.50) and to be discharged home (OR 3.46), with shorter hospital stays (MD - 1.96 days). The hemorrhage reduction was greatest among milder deficits (NIHSS ≤ 7). IVT in stroke mimics carries substantially lower hemorrhagic and mortality risk and better functional outcomes than in AIS, reflecting the benign nature of mimics rather than a treatment effect. Diagnostic uncertainty should not delay or withhold IVT in otherwise eligible patients.

articles.title: Oral anticoagulation with or without antiplatelet therapy for secondary stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation and atherosclerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Patients with ischemic stroke (IS), atrial fibrillation (AF), and atherosclerosis have an increased risk of recurrent ischemic events. Addition of antiplatelet therapy (APT) to oral anticoagulant therapy (OAC) may offer additional protection against these events, at the cost of an increased risk of bleeding. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of combined antithrombotic therapy versus OAC alone in this population. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception through September 2026 for randomized controlled trials and observational studies comparing OAC plus APT versus OAC alone in adults with IS, AF, and atherosclerosis. Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and ROBINS-I. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251164174). Seven studies (4 retrospective, 2 prospective, 1 randomized trial; n= 9,924) were included. Combined therapy was not associated with a reduction in vascular composite outcome (HR 1.10, 95% CI 0.61-1.96), recurrent IS (HR 1.03, 95% CI 0.91-1.16), major bleeding (HR 1.17, 95% CI 0.86-1.59), or all-cause mortality (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.60-1.36). In the subgroup with intracranial or extracranial atherosclerosis, combined therapy showed no significant difference in vascular composite risk (HR 1.67, 95% CI 0.83-3.33). Combined antithrombotic therapy with OAC plus APT was not associated with a reduction in recurrent IS, vascular composite outcome, major bleeding, or all-cause mortality in patients with IS, AF, and atherosclerosis. In patients with intracranial or extracranial atherosclerosis, combined therapy was not associated with a significant difference in the risk of the vascular composite outcome. These findings suggest that the addition of APT to OAC should be approached with caution in this population, and may be best reserved for select clinical contexts.

articles.title: Sex-specific serum metabolomic signatures of chronic kidney failure: a machine learning and interaction analysis based on the UK biobank.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether circulating metabolites are associated with chronic kidney failure (CKF) differently in men and women remains poorly characterized, and metabolomic studies of kidney outcomes have rarely accounted for the dominant influence of renal filtration itself on the circulating metabolome. We aimed to delineate sex-specific serum metabolomic signatures of CKF under a design that separates feature selection from statistical inference and explicitly adjusts for renal function.

METHODS: We analyzed nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) metabolomic profiles from 365,422 UK Biobank participants (199,540 women, 165,882 men). Sex-stratified LightGBM models with SHAP interpretation were fitted exclusively in a random 50% discovery partition; all association estimates were derived in the independent held-out 50% validation partition using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, Townsend deprivation index, ethnicity, fasting status, obesity, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and baseline serum creatinine, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction across 39 sex × metabolite interaction tests. Serum creatinine was excluded from all predictive models to avoid outcome-predictor leakage.

RESULTS: The metabolome provided statistically significant, but clinically modest incremental discrimination over clinical covariates (ΔAUC 0.037 [95% CI 0.031-0.043] in men and 0.026 [0.021-0.031] in women; continuous net reclassification improvement not significant). After creatinine adjustment, seven sex × metabolite interactions remained significant. The cholesteryl-ester fraction of small LDL particles was inversely associated with CKF in both sexes, but more strongly in men (OR per 1-SD 0.79 [0.77-0.81] vs 0.85 [0.83-0.87]; interaction FDR = 4.6×10⁻5), with a concordant pattern for medium LDL (FDR = 2.2×10⁻4); formal sex × spline tests confirmed steeper inverse dose-responses in men. In contrast, the apparently male-specific associations of isoleucine, alanine, and 3-hydroxybutyrate observed in unadjusted models were fully attenuated after creatinine adjustment, indicating confounding by renal filtration. Shared core metabolites were enriched for amino-acid, ketone-body, and glycolysis-related groups in both sexes (all FDR < 0.005).

CONCLUSIONS: Sex differences in the CKF serum metabolome are concentrated in lipoprotein cholesteryl-ester composition and remain robust after renal-function adjustment, whereas amino-acid signatures largely reflect filtration-related confounding. Adjustment for baseline renal function is indispensable in metabolomic studies of kidney outcomes.

articles.title: Utilisation patterns and exploratory short-term outcomes of drug-coated balloon versus drug-eluting stent in percutaneous coronary intervention: a single-centre observational cohort study.
articles.journal: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Drug-coated balloons (DCBs) are an established alternative to drug-eluting stents (DESs) for selected coronary lesions, offering the potential advantages of a stent-free strategy while avoiding permanent metallic implantation. This study compared real-world utilisation patterns, clinical outcomes, and patient-reported outcomes following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with DCBs and DESs.

METHODS: This single-centre retrospective cohort study with prospective follow-up included 214 consecutive patients who underwent PCI with either a DCB (n = 64) or DES (n = 150) between January 2023 and March 2026. Baseline demographic, angiographic, procedural, and clinical characteristics were compared. Patient-reported outcomes were assessed at follow-up using a questionnaire adapted from the domains of the Seattle Angina Questionnaire. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify independent factors associated with DCB utilisation.

RESULTS: The study included 214 patients (mean age 56.55 ± 11.49 years), of whom 72.9% were male. Clinical presentation differed significantly between groups (p = 0.042), the ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) group more frequently underwent DES (46.0% vs. 29.7%), whereas non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) (37.5% vs. 30.7%) and Unstable Angina​ (UA) (15.6% vs. 6.0%) were more common in the DCB group. DCBs were preferentially used in patients with previous coronary revascularization, ISR, small-vessel disease and elective PCI, whereas DESs were more commonly used for acute PCI, total occlusive lesions, and lesions with calcification or thrombus (all p < 0.05). Previous coronary revascularization was associated with increased odds of DCB use, while acute PCI was associated with reduced odds of DCB use compared with elective PCI. No significant differences were observed between groups in mortality at 1, 3, or 6 months, other early clinical outcomes, or patient-reported outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: DCBs were preferentially used in specific clinical and anatomical settings while demonstrating low observed rates of short-term clinical events and no statistically significant between-group differences in patient-reported outcomes. Despite differences in lesion complexity and treatment selection, no significant differences in early outcomes were observed compared with DES. These findings describe contemporary real-world DCB utilisation in a Sri Lankan PCI centre and provide a basis for further multicentre evaluation.

articles.title: Effect of orofacial myofunctional therapy with auto-monitoring on the apnea-hypopnea index in patients with mild-to-moderate obstructive sleep apnea: a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Orofacial myofunctional therapy (OMT) is a promising treatment for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but protocols vary and outcomes are inconsistent. The primary aim was to evaluate the effect of a standardized OMT protocol on changes in apnea-hypopnea index (AHI). Secondary aims were to analyze associations between OMT adherence and change in objective and self-reported outcomes.

METHODS: Treatment-naive adults with mild-to-moderate OSA were randomized in a multicenter trial to 12 weeks of OMT or a waitlist control group. Three nights of polysomnography were completed before and after the intervention. Adherence was registered electronically. The primary outcome was change in AHI. Pre-defined secondary outcomes were changes in desaturation measures and in the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) score. Intention-to-treat analyses were performed using linear mixed-effects models, whereas per-protocol analyses were based on analysis of covariance.

RESULTS: A total of 104 participants (mean age 47.1 ± 12.2 years) were included. Intention-to-treat analysis included 104 participants (52 treatment, 52 waitlist) and showed no significant effect of OMT on AHI. Difference in AHI change between groups was 0.6 (95% CI -3.3 to 4.5; P = .774). Overall mean adherence across all days and participants was 64.6% (95% CI 61.0 to 76.8). Higher adherence was not associated with significantly greater reduction in AHI (β = -0.1, 95% CI -0.2 to 0.1; P = .353). No change was detected in pre-defined secondary outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Twelve weeks of standardized OMT had no significant effect on AHI, desaturation measures or ESS score in treatment-naive patients newly diagnosed with OSA.

CURRENT KNOWLEDGE/STUDY RATIONALE: Orofacial myofunctional therapy (OMT) is increasingly considered a non-invasive treatment for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but existing evidence is heterogeneous and often limited by methodological shortcomings. We therefore conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effects of a standardized OMT protocol in adults newly diagnosed with mild-to-moderate OSA.

STUDY IMPACT: The intervention did not improve pre-defined OSA outcomes, highlighting the importance of rigorous trials even when results are negative. These findings help refine the evidence base for OMT in adults with OSA while supporting continued investigation of alternative protocols and populations stratified by endo- or phenotyping.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Registry: ClinicalTrials.gov, Identifier: NCT06079073, URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06079073 , First submission: 2023-08-23.

articles.title: A Problem in Breast Cancer Interventional Clinical Trials Funded by the National Institutes of Health (NIH) and other US Federal Agencies.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breast cancer (BCa) is the second leading cause of cancer-related death among women in the United States (US), yet declines in mortality have not been equally experienced across racial and ethnic groups. Although Black women have a 5% lower incidence rate than White women, their mortality rate is 38% higher. This disparity represents a persistent inequity in US cancer outcomes. BCa outcomes are profoundly influenced by type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D) and obesity, often operating syndemically and adversely impacting prognosis. Despite biological and clinical relevance, federally funded BCa clinical trials seldom adequately account for these metabolic comorbidities.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 90 completed, female-only BCa interventional clinical trials funded by the NIH and other US federal agencies that were registered on ClinicalTrials.gov as of July 25, 2023. Trials were evaluated for explicit or implicit inclusion of T2D and obesity in eligibility criteria using expert pharmacologic review, FDA-labeled and off-label drug indication analysis, and AI-assisted keyword and context recognition to identify direct or indirect metabolic references.

RESULTS: The study examined 354 conditions across 90 trials. Ten (10) trials explicitly addressed T2D, and only two (2) trials directly addressed obesity. Eight (8) trials indirectly referenced diabetes through glucose-based or metabolic exclusion criteria, and six (6) trials indirectly addressed obesity. Among trials using drugs or behavioral interventions with known metabolic effects, T2D and obesity were rarely considered. Only 3 of these trials addressed both comorbidities and 74.4% did not address either condition.

DISCUSSION: These findings reveal a persistent disconnect between the biological relevance of metabolic comorbidities and their consideration in clinical trial design, reflecting a reductionist paradigm that overlooks real-world patient complexity, especially for women disproportionately affected by T2D and obesity.

CONCLUSION: Federally funded BCa trials in this study were predominantly reductionist in design, with limited consideration of the syndemic interplay between metabolic and oncologic health. Future funding should prioritize trial designs that integrate diabetes, obesity, and metabolic diversity into eligibility, stratification, and analytic frameworks to enhance pathways for implementation, generalizability, and equity in BCa research.

articles.title: Comorbidity vortex in the childhood obesity-metabolic disease continuum.
Category and Modifier Accuracy in a Five-Model Evaluation of Large Language Model Extraction of CAD-RADS 2.0 from Coronary CT Angiography Reports.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: This study evaluates large language model (LLM) extraction of Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS) categories from coronary CT angiography (CCTA) reports using a guideline-derived specification and examines instruction-related improvement, repeatability, and the limitations of extracting plaque and ischemia modifiers alongside the category. Five LLM platforms (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, and Copilot) processed 400 deidentified CCTA report entries under unprompted, specified, and repeated-specified conditions. The primary outcome was exact category agreement with a report-derived consensus reference under the specification (n = 400). Secondary outcomes included three-component agreement (n = 396), modifier accuracy, instruction-related changes, and repeatability. Inference used report-text cluster bootstrap and paired or permutation tests with Holm adjustment. For the primary outcome, category accuracy under the specification was 92.8-95.5% (371-382/400); secondary outcomes included run-to-run category agreement of 97.5-98.8%, whereas three-component accuracy was 59.3-81.6% (235-323/396). Among assigned references, plaque accuracy was 79.2-94.0% (236-280/298) and ischemia accuracy 45.1-90.3% (79-158/175). The specification improved category accuracy in four of five models and three-component, plaque, and ischemia accuracy in all five. Models did not differ significantly in category accuracy (Cochran Q = 8.73; adjusted p = 0.077) but differed in three-component accuracy (Q = 116.48; adjusted p < 0.001). Category extraction was accurate under the specification, with improvement in most models and high repeatability. Joint evaluation of category, plaque, and ischemia revealed limitations in modifier extraction. External and prospective validation is needed to develop a reliable clinical tool and establish its value in routine practice.

articles.title: Opportunistic abdominal aortic calcification assessment on spine radiographs in women with longstanding rheumatoid arthritis: linking cardiovascular burden and femoral neck bone loss.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) and osteoporosis are major comorbidities in rheumatoid arthritis (RA). We assessed abdominal aortic calcification (AAC) opportunistically on spine radiographs and examined its associations with CVD, estimated cardiovascular risk, bone mineral density (BMD), and fragility fractures in women with longstanding RA.

METHOD: This cross-sectional study included 196 consecutive women with longstanding RA followed at a tertiary hospital. All underwent dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry and conventional spine radiography. AAC was graded using the Kauppila score (KS) and categorized as absent, mild-to-moderate (KS 1-6), or extended (KS > 6). Multivariable models evaluated factors associated with AAC and overt CVD.

RESULTS: Participants had a mean age of 62.8 ± 9.6 years and median RA duration of 21 years. AAC was present in 48 women (24.5%), including extended AAC in 25 (12.7%). Overt CVD was documented in 32 participants (16.3%). Extended AAC was independently associated with hypertension (OR 8.57, 95% CI 1.10-67.02), longer RA duration (OR 1.05 per year, 95% CI 1.004-1.09), and lower femoral neck T-score (OR 0.57, 95% CI 0.35-0.95). AAC of any severity was associated with overt CVD (OR 2.89, 95% CI 1.26-6.63).

CONCLUSIONS: AAC detected on routine spine radiographs was common among women with longstanding RA and was associated with cardiovascular burden and lower femoral neck BMD. Opportunistic AAC assessment may complement cardiovascular and skeletal risk evaluation in RA. Larger cohorts are needed to confirm these exploratory associations, and prospective studies are needed to establish predictive value.

articles.title: Interval Between Injury and Surgery Influences Knee Biomechanics During Walking in Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstructed Patients: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) is commonly performed to restore anatomical and functional knee stability. Although altered walking biomechanics have been observed post-ACLR, previous studies have not consistently accounted for the interval between injury and surgery.

OBJECTIVE: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to determine whether walking-related knee biomechanical alterations following ACLR are transient or persist over time, and whether the timing of surgery influences these alterations.

METHODS: Five electronic databases (Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, Physiotherapy Evidence Database [PEDro], and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials [CENTRAL]) were systematically searched from inception through August 2026. Studies comparing walking biomechanics between patients who underwent ACLR and healthy controls and reporting the interval between anterior cruciate ligament injury and reconstructive surgery were included. Biomechanical outcomes during the stance phase of walking were extracted and stratified according to the interval between injury and surgery: short term (0 to < 6 months), mid-term (6 to < 12 months), and long term (≥ 12 months). Standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals were calculated using a random-effects model. Study quality was assessed using a modified Downs and Black checklist.

RESULTS: Of the 3522 identified records, 16 studies involving male and female participants aged 18-55 years met the inclusion criteria. The mean methodological quality score was 65%, indicating an overall moderate level of methodological quality. Compared with healthy controls, ACLR participants demonstrated lower peak knee flexion angle (SMD = - 0.33, 95% confidence interval [CI] - 0.64 to - 0.02, p = 0.03, I2 = 57%), peak knee adduction angle (SMD = - 0.47, 95% CI - 0.92 to - 0.01, p = 0.04, I2 = 66%), and peak knee flexion moment (SMD = - 0.64, 95% CI - 1.05 to - 0.23, p = 0.002, I2 = 76%). In subgroup analyses, the long-term group (≥ 12 months between injury and surgery) demonstrated lower peak knee flexion angle (SMD = - 0.27, 95% CI - 0.54 to - 0.00, p = 0.05, I2 = 8%) and peak knee flexion moment (SMD = - 1.97, 95% CI - 3.77 to - 0.17, p = 0.03, I2 = 88%). The short-term group (0 to < 6 months) demonstrated lower peak knee adduction angle (SMD = - 0.79, 95% CI - 1.18 to - 0.40, p < 0.0001, I2 = 19%) and peak knee extension moment (SMD = - 0.55, 95% CI - 0.93 to - 0.18, p = 0.004, I2 = 50%).

CONCLUSIONS: The interval between anterior cruciate ligament injury and ACLR was associated with differences in postoperative walking biomechanics. Delayed reconstruction (≥ 12 months) is associated with persistent sagittal plane deficits, which may reflect chronic neuromuscular adaptations or preoperative joint degeneration. In contrast, early surgery (within 6 months after anterior cruciate ligament injury) was associated with fewer long-term sagittal-plane deficits, although temporary frontal-plane asymmetries and extension deficits may persist during the early postoperative period and may improve with rehabilitation. These findings underscore the importance of considering the timing of ACLR when planning surgery and postoperative rehabilitation to support walking recovery.

articles.title: Association of dietary fiber intake with stroke history and characterization of a stroke related five gene immune signature: an exploratory study.
articles.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dietary fiber intake has been associated with cerebrovascular health, motivating investigation of its relationship with inflammation and stroke-related immune expression.

METHODS: We combined NHANES population analyses with whole blood microarray and single-cell transcriptomic analyses to examine dietary associations and characterize a stroke-related gene signature. NHANES analyses included 34,928 adults from 2005 to 2018, including 1,348 with self-reported stroke history. Associations were examined using fully adjusted survey-weighted logistic regression, with a sensitivity analysis using two-day mean intake. Candidate genes were selected using GSE16561 and external gene resources, followed by LASSO selection and external validation in 46 GSE58294 participants. Single-cell analysis included 91,176 cells from three paired donors.

RESULTS: Each unit increase in ln(fiber intake + 0.1) was associated with an odds ratio of 0.755 (95% confidence interval 0.663 to 0.861) for stroke history. Analysis of two-day mean intake showed a consistent association, with an odds ratio of 0.601 (0.499 to 0.723). Higher fiber intake was also associated with lower NLR, MLR, SIRI, and CRP levels. Of 15 candidate genes, LASSO retained CD163, PAK1, FOS, PTGS2, and HDAC4. The model achieved an external area under the curve of 0.964 (0.916 to 1.000). Single-cell analysis localized CD163, PAK1, and PTGS2 predominantly to monocytes and conventional dendritic cells. FOS showed broad expression, whereas HDAC4 was relatively enriched in naive CD4 T cells.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify inverse associations of dietary fiber intake with stroke history and systemic inflammatory markers, together with a discriminative five-gene blood signature and its cellular distribution, providing directions for further investigation of nutritional and immune processes in stroke.

articles.title: Spatial transcriptomics tumor microenvironment determinants of tyrosine kinase inhibitor response in renal cell carcinoma: results from a phase 2 clinical trial.
articles.abstract: Metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) exhibits heterogeneous clinical outcomes, and limited biomarkers are available to predict response to targeted therapies. This study evaluated cell compartment-specific transcriptional biomarkers predicting clinical response to the tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) sunitinib. In this phase 2 clinical trial (NCT00715442), 46 patients with metastatic ccRCC received sunitinib pre- and post-cytoreductive nephrectomy, with a primary endpoint of time-to-progression (TTP) and secondary endpoints of overall survival (OS) and sunitinib toxicity. To investigate spatial dynamics of therapeutic response to sunitinib, we applied whole-transcriptome digital spatial profiling (DSP) to tumor tissue from responders and non-responders. For 46 trial patients, median TTP was 8.2 months (95% CI: 6.1-19.3) and OS 36.3 months (95% CI: 19.7-70.5). Responders displayed a tumor microenvironment enriched in pro-inflammatory/immunostimulatory programs, while non-responders displayed enrichment of immunosuppressive programs with elevated PD-L1 expression in myeloid cells and exhausted CD8 + T-cell signatures. Sunitinib resistance mechanisms involving VEGF-dependent and independent angiogenic pathways were identified, revealing potential therapeutic targets. DSP-based machine learning models showed strong prognostic and predictive performance in sunitinib-treated patients in an external JAVELIN Renal 101 cohort, but attenuated performance in the avelumab plus axitinib cohort, indicating treatment-context specificity. Our findings highlight immune regulation as a key determinant of sunitinib response in metastatic ccRCC. Spatial profiling revealed potentially targetable mechanisms of TKI resistance involving SPP1-associated myeloid programs, CD8 + T-cell exhaustion, and angiogenic signaling, highlighting interactions between angiogenesis, lipid metabolism, and tumor immunity as determinants of therapeutic outcome.

articles.title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Dialysis Patients: Insights from a Nationwide Registry Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trans-radial intervention (TRI) has become the standard of care for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). However, in patients on dialysis, trans-femoral intervention (TFI) remains predominant to preserve upper-limb vessels for arteriovenous fistula despite heightened hemorrhagic risk. This study aimed to compare TRI and TFI in dialysis patients undergoing PCI.

METHODS: We used the National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI Registry to compare patients on dialysis who underwent PCIs with TRI versus TFI from January 2018 to June 2025. An instrumental variable analysis with the institutional proportion of TRI use was performed to assess the risk of access-site bleeding and other peri-procedural outcomes.

RESULTS: Among 137,702 dialysis patients who underwent PCI, 28.3% of patients underwent TRI (n=38,901), while 71.7% patients underwent TFI (n=98,801). TRI was associated with a lower risk of bleeding at the access site (adjusted risk difference [aRD]: -0.35%; 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.56% to -0.15%). Overall bleeding (aRD: -1.38%; 95% CI: -1.89% to -0.87%), access-site hematoma (aRD: -0.86%; 95% CI: -1.13% to -0.60%), myocardial infarction (aRD: -0.21%; 95% CI: -0.39% to -0.03%), and mortality (aRD: -1.07%; 95% CI: -1.64% to -0.51%) were also less frequently observed in TRI. Conversely, TRI was associated with a higher risk of stroke (aRD: 0.23%; 95% CI: 0.001% to 0.45%), driven primarily by ischemic stroke.

CONCLUSIONS: TRI was associated with a lower risk of bleeding events, but the effect size was modest. The higher observed stroke risk highlights a potential ischemic trade-off and warrants further study.

articles.title: Subcutaneous abscessation: An atypical presentation of Rhodococcus equi infection in a group of foals.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Integumentary manifestations of Rhodococcus equi infection in foals are infrequently reported in the literature. Subcutaneous abscessation as the primary clinical presentation in temporally clustered cases of foal rhodococcosis in an equine farm has not, to the authors' knowledge, been previously described.

OBJECTIVES: To describe an outbreak of R. equi infection where foals presented with subcutaneous abscessation as the primary clinical sign.

STUDY DESIGN: Clinical case series.

CLINICAL SUMMARY: Three Thoroughbred foals aged 6-11 weeks developed subcutaneous abscesses over a 3-week period in July 2024, out of a cohort of 11 foals. Thoracic ultrasound examination was performed on all foals on the farm, and 6/11 (54%) had evidence of subclinical pneumonia. No foals other than the three cases with subcutaneous abscesses were clinically affected. Purulent aspirates from abscesses in two foals were subjected to microbiological diagnosis and yielded a pure culture of R. equi. Two of the three clinically affected foals received 4 weeks of systemic antimicrobial treatment, and all abscesses resolved. Whole-genome sequencing of one isolate demonstrated near identity to a previous UK isolate associated with pulmonary rhodococcosis, and did not reveal genetic features that could explain the atypical presentation.

MAIN LIMITATIONS: Financial constraints on the farm precluded microbiological confirmation of diagnosis in the third foal. Sequencing of a single isolate precluded assessment of strain relatedness within the outbreak.

CONCLUSIONS: R. equi infection should be considered in foals presenting with subcutaneous abscesses, even in the absence of overt respiratory signs. Exposure-related factors likely contributed to this presentation, and the possibility of a transcutaneous route of entry should be considered.

articles.title: [18F]fluorodeoxyglucose-PET in Therapeutic Decision-Making and Theranostics of Breast Cancer.
articles.abstract: [18F]fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG)-PET/CT informs decisions at almost every point in breast cancer care. It establishes the extent of disease at diagnosis and so determines whether treatment is delivered with curative or palliative intent. This review examines the biology that underlies FDG uptake and explains why uptake varies so markedly between molecular subtypes. It also sets out the evidence supporting FDG-PET/CT in staging and in therapeutic decision-making across chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, HER2-directed treatment, immunotherapy, and radiotherapy planning, before turning to the complimentary role of 18F-FDG PET/CT with theranostic agents.

articles.title: 18F-Florquinitau PET for imaging tau pathology in Alzheimer's disease.
Prevalence of Neck Pain and Its Correlation with Self-Perceived Voice Handicap in Female Patients with Fibromyalgia.
articles.journal: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the prevalence of neck pain and its correlation with self-perceived voice handicap in female patients with fibromyalgia (FM) STUDY DESIGN: Cross-sectional METHODS: Consecutive patients aged 18 to 65 years with a diagnosis of FM were recruited from the Rheumatology Clinic of a tertiary referral center between June 30, 2026, and July 30, 2026. Another cohort, frequency-matched by age and with no history of FM or chronic pain conditions, was recruited as a control group. Informed consent was obtained from all participants. The primary outcome measure was the severity of neck pain and its correlation with self-perceived voice handicap. Neck pain was assessed using the Neck Disability Index (NDI) questionnaire and the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for neck pain, whereas the self-perceived voice handicap was assessed using the Voice Handicap Index-10 (VHI-10) questionnaire and the VAS for hoarseness.

RESULTS: Fifty patients with FM and 50 controls were included in the study. All patients were female. The mean age of the FM group was 44.38 ± 11.98 years, and the mean age of the control group was 47.86 ± 15.56 years. The mean NDI and VAS scores for neck pain were significantly higher in the FM group compared to controls (P < 0.001). There was a significant difference in the mean VHI-10 and VAS scores for hoarseness between the two groups (P = 0.002 and P = 0.011, respectively). The NDI score was moderately correlated with the VHI-10 score (r = 0.498) and the VAS for hoarseness (r = 0.494). Similarly, there was a moderate and positive correlation between the VAS score for neck pain and the VHI-10 (P = 0.467), and the VAS score for hoarseness (r = 0.454).

CONCLUSION: This study showed that FM was a strong independent predictor of higher NDI and VAS scores for neck pain. There was a significant difference in the mean VHI-10 and VAS score for hoarseness between the study group and controls, and a moderate and positive correlation between neck pain and patient-reported voice measures.

articles.title: Re: 'Hepatitis delta in Spain: a nationwide prospective characterization of active infection and liver disease severity' by Alberola et al.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases

articles.title: Bacteriophage associated liver injury in a person with cystic fibrosis and prior liver transplantation.
articles.journal: Journal of cystic fibrosis : official journal of the European Cystic Fibrosis Society
articles.abstract: A 27-year-old man with cystic fibrosis, prior liver transplantation for advanced cystic fibrosis related liver disease, tacrolimus immunosuppression, multidrug resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection, recurrent drug induced liver injury, and intolerance to elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor underwent matched bacteriophage therapy. Intravenous phages were administered at 109 plaque forming units per dose and nebulised phages at 5 × 109 plaque forming units per dose twice daily. Within two days, marked elevations in alanine transaminase, aspartate transaminase, alkaline phosphatase, and gamma glutamyl transferase developed, prompting treatment cessation. Peak alanine transaminase reached 494 U/L and alkaline phosphatase 527 U/L were observed, while bilirubin and coagulation parameters remained normal. Extensive investigation, including magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography and medication review, identified no alternative cause. Rechallenge with nebulised phage therapy alone resulted in recurrent liver enzyme elevation after eight days, again resolving following discontinuation. Temporal correlation was demonstrated between liver function test abnormalities and detection of phage DNA in serum and sputum. No bacteriophage neutralisation, bacterial DNAaemia, development of phage resistance, or significant bacterial genomic change was observed. Despite early cessation, lung function improved over the subsequent six months.

articles.title: Real-world clinical practice with inclisiran for secondary prevention after ischemic stroke.
Disseminated gonococcal infection, HIV infection and complement deficiency: A case report.
Neonatal bilirubin neurotoxicity: An emergency response framework from referral to follow-up.
articles.abstract: A neonate with a total serum bilirubin at or approaching the exchange transfusion threshold represents a life-threatening neurologic emergency that demands a coordinated, time-critical response. The 2022 American Academy of Pediatrics clinical practice guideline revision formally defines an escalation-of-care threshold at 2 mg/dL below the exchange transfusion threshold to trigger prompt, aggressive therapeutic interventions. However, the vast majority of extreme hyperbilirubinemia cases undergo triage in low-resource or community settings, such as outpatient pediatric clinics, general emergency departments, or level I/II nurseries. These settings often lack the specialized capabilities required to perform an emergency exchange transfusion. Consequently, clinical outcomes and long-term neurodevelopmental prognoses depend on rapid recognition of transfer criteria, immediate initiation of temporizing management at the referring site, and stabilization during transport. This review has been developed at an academic level IV neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) and translates AAP guidelines into an actionable, role-specific protocol for referring clinicians, transport teams, receiving NICU staff, and institutional quality bodies. Emphasis is placed on immediate treatment at first clinical contact, specifically continuous intensive phototherapy and intravenous hydration within minutes rather than delaying until arrival at a higher-level center, alongside parallel exchange transfusion preparation, standardized neurologic assessment, proactive family counseling, and institutional follow-up.

articles.title: Patient-reported disability has insufficient clinical accuracy for predicting physical function in survivors of critical illness: a secondary analysis of a cluster-randomised trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-ICU care often misses patients unable to attend in-person clinic visits. Remote assessments of physical function might increase access to ICU aftercare. We investigated whether patient-reported disability predicts handgrip strength (HGS) and the 2-Minute Walk Test (2MWT) distance with sufficient clinical accuracy.

METHODS: This secondary analysis of the stepped-wedge cluster-randomised Enhanced Recovery after Intensive Care trial included patients from 10 German ICU clusters who completed the WHO Disability Assessment Schedule (WHODAS) 2.0 plus either HGS, the 2MWT, or both, 6 months after ICU discharge. Relationships between WHODAS 2.0, HGS, and 2MWT were analysed using scatter plots, correlation coefficients, linear regressions, and Bland-Altman plots. Predictions of HGS and the 2MWT were compared with the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) for both measures.

RESULTS: Of 1463 enrolled patients, 620 were analysed. The median WHODAS 2.0 sum score was 11 (Q1, Q3: 3, 22). The median HGS, expressed as a percentage of the expected value (%exp), was 70.6%exp (Q1, Q3: 54.4, 85.6), and the median 2MWT distance was 73.7%exp (Q1, Q3: 61.5, 85.8). The 2MWT was not completed by 59% of patients. Higher disability was moderately correlated with lower HGS (Spearman %exp: -0.41) and shorter 2MWT distance (Spearman %exp: -0.47). In multivariable regression models, the WHODAS 2.0 sum score predicted HGS in kg (β: -0.27 [95% CI: -0.33 to -0.22]; P<0.001) and 2MWT distance in m (β: -1.94 [95% CI: -2.37 to -1.51]; P<0.001), but the limits of agreement exceeded the MCIDs.

CONCLUSIONS: With increasing disability, HGS and 2MWT performance declined, although correlations were moderate and uncertainty of predictions exceeded MCIDs of both instruments. Remote WHODAS 2.0 assessments cannot replace in-person physical function testing.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT03671447.

articles.title: Low-Dose PCCT-Based Liver Volume Perfusion CT with Phase-Specific Reconstruction Optimization for Morphologic.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Volume perfusion CT (VPCT) of the liver provides functional information but is associated with increased radiation exposure and often requires additional multiphasic CT acquisitions. Photon-counting CT (PCCT) may enable low-dose one-stop imaging by generating diagnostic morphological images directly from perfusion datasets. To evaluate the image quality of single-phase and fused noncontrast and contrast-enhanced images generated from photon-counting CT (PCCT)-based liver dynamic volume perfusion CT (VPCT) for liver morphologic assessment.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective study, 62 patients with liver disease underwent true noncontrast PCCT, liver VPCT, and low-dose delayed-phase imaging. Single-time-point noncontrast, arterial-phase, and portal venous-phase images were reconstructed from the VPCT dataset using virtual monoenergetic image (VMI, 40-70 keV) and Threshold 3D (T3D) reconstruction. Fused T3D images were generated from multiphase perfusion data. Image quality was evaluated using signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), subjective image-quality scores. Radiation dose was recorded.

RESULTS: The one-stop imaging protocol yielded a lower effective dose than the simulated conventional four-phase protocol combined with perfusion imaging (25.9 ± 6.7 mSv vs 31.9 ± 8.5 mSv, P < 0.05). Compared with true noncontrast images, fused noncontrast images showed higher SNR (8.6 ± 3.0 vs 7.0 ± 1.9) and CNR (1.5 ± 1.2 vs 1.0 ± 0.8) (P < 0.05). Although subjective image-quality scores for perfusion-derived noncontrast images were lower than those for true noncontrast images, all remained diagnostically acceptable (score ≥ 3). In the arterial phase, fused images showed the lowest image noise (7.5 ± 2.7 HU), while 40-keV VMI provided the highest CNR (70.4 ± 24.0). In the portal venous phase, fused images achieved the lowest noise (8.8 ± 2.8 HU) while maintaining relatively high CNR (10.4 ± 7.8). Except for 40-keV and 50-keV portal venous-phase images, all reconstructed arterial- and portal venous-phase images achieved diagnostically acceptable subjective scores (≥3).

CONCLUSION: PCCT-based liver VPCT one-stop imaging reduces radiation exposure while providing diagnostically acceptable morphologic images. The optimal reconstruction of noncontrast and contrast-enhanced images varies by imaging phase, supporting a phase-specific image optimization strategy for liver morphologic assessment.

articles.title: Transcriptomic Determinants of Response to Biologic Therapy in Severe Asthma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with severe uncontrolled asthma (SUA) and a T2 eosinophilic phenotype exhibit variable response to biologic therapy (BT). Currently, accurate biomarkers predicting this response are lacking. We aimed to explore whether microRNA (miRNA) and messenger RNA (mRNA) profiles in bronchial biopsies (BB) may help identify patients achieving a complete clinical response after 6 months of BT.

AIMS: To explore whether BB miRNA and mRNA profiles may be associated with clinical response to BT in SUA population.

METHODS: Thirty-four consecutive SUA patients with a T2 high phenotype were characterized and underwent bronchoscopy with BB before initiating anti-IL-5/5R BT. Clinical response was evaluated 6 months later. Both, miRNA and mRNA were extracted from BB, and their expression profiles were analyzed via microarrays. Gene Ontology and KEGG pathway analyses were performed to understand the biological functions and signaling pathways involved.

RESULTS: After BT, 64% showed complete clinical response, 18% patients were non-responders, and 18% obtained a partial response. Comparing non-responders vs. responders showed 35 differentially expressed mRNAs, and 8 miRNAs in BB samples. Integrated analysis of miRNA and mRNA data suggested that three key genes (FOXO1, ZBTB16 and OLFML3) may be involved in asthma pathogenesis.

CONCLUSIONS: Expression patterns between responders and non-responders to BT appeared to differ in BB of SUA patients, highlighting the involvement of multiple pathways related to airway inflammation and airway remodeling. Our results provide preliminary evidence suggesting that FOXO1, ZBTB16 and OLFML3 might be involved in the biological response to anti-IL-5/5R therapy.

articles.title: Educational inequalities and obesity: Independent and lifestyle-mediated associations in a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Educational inequalities in cardiometabolic health are well established, but the role of obesity as an effect modifier remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether obesity modifies the association between educational level and cardiometabolic risk.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study including 3108 working-age adults undergoing occupational health assessments was conducted. Educational level was classified into higher, intermediate, and primary/no formal education. Obesity was defined as BMI≥30kg/m2. Cardiometabolic outcomes included metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), insulin resistance, atherogenic risk, and metabolic syndrome. Multivariable logistic regression models and interaction analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Lower educational attainment was associated with higher prevalence of obesity and adverse cardiometabolic outcomes. Participants with primary or no education showed higher odds of obesity (OR 1.61; 95% CI 1.18-2.21). No statistically significant interaction was observed between educational level and obesity for any cardiometabolic outcome.

CONCLUSIONS: Lower educational attainment was associated with a worse cardiometabolic profile, but obesity did not substantially modify this relationship.

articles.title: Comb-Like EEG Pattern as an Early Diagnostic Clue in Maple Syrup Urine Disease (MSUD): A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
articles.abstract: Maple syrup urine disease (MSUD) is a life-threatening inborn error of amino acid metabolism that often presents in the neonatal period with nonspecific symptoms such as poor feeding, lethargy, and seizures. Although newborn screening (NBS) enables early identification, false-negative results and delays in reporting may lead to missed or delayed diagnosis, resulting in severe neurologic injury. A characteristic EEG finding, the "comb-like rhythm," consisting of central- or frontocentral-predominant, sharply contoured 4-7 Hz theta bursts has been reported in MSUD. However, its diagnostic utility has not been systematically evaluated. Therefore, we aimed to investigate the comb-like rhythm as a diagnostic clue for MSUD. A systematic literature search was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines using MEDLINE and Embase databases up to May 18, 2026. Studies evaluating EEG findings in individuals with MSUD were included. Data on clinical presentation, biochemical findings, brain imaging, and EEG features were extracted and synthesized qualitatively. In addition, two neonatal cases from our institution were included. Associations of the comb-like EEG rhythm with patient age at EEG (neonatal vs. non-neonatal) and plasma leucine concentrations were evaluated using Fisher's exact test and the Mann-Whitney U test. A total of 113 records were screened, and 18 studies were included, comprising 24 symptomatic cases including our two patients. Abnormal EEG findings were reported in 21 of 24 (88%). A comb-like pattern was exclusively observed in neonates with acute metabolic crisis (13/15 neonates [86.7%] vs. 0/9 non-neonates [0%], p < 0.0001). The comb-like rhythm was associated with higher plasma leucine concentrations (median, 3545 vs. 1782 μmol/L, p = 0.0033). The pattern often diminished or resolved following treatment or clinical stabilization. In our two patients, the comb-like rhythm contributed to raising diagnostic suspicion despite initially normal NBS results. The comb-like rhythm may serve as an adjunctive EEG marker that raises suspicion for acute MSUD, given its strong association with neonatal metabolic crisis and severe hyperleucinemia. Further studies are needed to clarify its pathophysiological basis and determine the clinical utility of EEG in MSUD crisis.

articles.title: Dust Storm-Associated Pediatric Allergic Morbidity in Primary Care in Chicago, Illinois.
articles.abstract: We examined the effect of a rare Midwestern dust storm on pediatric allergic morbidity in a Chicago, Illinois primary care setting. As climate and land-use changes expand the geographic range of dust storm activity, primary care clinicians will increasingly encounter environmentally triggered asthma and allergy exacerbations. We performed a retrospective analysis of daily clinic visits before and after the May 16, 2025 dust storm and observed an increase in allergy-related visits, with a significant increase in the first 3 days after the storm. Visit diagnoses included eczema, asthma/reactive airway disease, allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, allergic dermatitis, and seasonal allergies. By focusing on primary care rather than emergency department visits, this work highlights the broader burden of dust-related allergic morbidity in the pediatric population. These findings underscore the need for primary care preparedness and community-level mitigation strategies as extreme weather events become more frequent.

articles.title: Association of Early Palliative Care with End-of-Life Care Quality and Nonbeneficial Treatments in Taiwan: A Nationwide Population-Based Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early palliative care has been associated with reduced aggressive care near the end of life (EOL), particularly among patients with cancer. However, evidence regarding the association between early palliative care and potentially nonbeneficial treatments near the EOL remains limited, particularly among patients with noncancer terminal illnesses and in real-world clinical practice.

OBJECTIVES: To examine the association between early palliative care, EOL care quality indicators, and nonbeneficial treatments among terminally ill cancer and noncancer patients under a universal health insurance system.

METHODS: This retrospective population-based study used Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database to identify adults who received palliative care within one year before death in 2019. Early palliative care was defined as initiation of any palliative care service more than 90 days before death. Outcomes included indicators of EOL care quality and nonbeneficial treatments within the last 30 days of life. Multivariable logistic and linear regression models were used to adjust for demographic characteristics, comorbidities, and terminal diagnoses.

RESULTS: Among 46,343 decedents, 17.2% received early palliative care. Early palliative care was associated with lower odds of aggressive EOL care, including more than one emergency department visit, more than one hospitalization, a hospital stay exceeding 14 days, intensive care unit admission, in-hospital death, use of an endotracheal tube, ventilator support, and cardiopulmonary resuscitation. Early palliative care was also associated with reduced use of nonbeneficial treatments, including blood transfusion and tube feeding or intravenous nutrition.

CONCLUSION: In a nationwide cohort, early palliative care was associated with improved EOL care quality and reduced use of nonbeneficial treatments among terminally ill patients. These findings underscore the clinical importance of earlier palliative care involvement in supporting patient-centered decision making near the EOL and reducing potentially nonbeneficial interventions.

articles.title: Worsening epigastric pain after contact with pet dogs with diarrhoea.
Descriptive Epidemiology in Cancer Research: A Coordinate System for Cancer Science.
articles.abstract: Descriptive epidemiology characterizes the distribution of cancer in populations. Its indicators are neither self-explanatory as facts nor sufficient grounds for causal narratives. Cancer registries, vital statistics, and follow-up systems make incidence, mortality, survival, and prevalence observable, but these measures depend on how cases, deaths, and populations are defined and recorded. We propose an interpretive coordinate system that locates cancer patterns by person, place, time, complementary indicators, and the processes generating these indicators. This framework characterizes burden, identifies unusual patterns and inequalities, and generates and constrains hypotheses. It examines whether population patterns are compatible with changes in diagnosis, screening, treatment, or policy. It does not by itself establish causation, reveal mechanisms, or estimate intervention effects. Here, we clarify what the principal indicators describe, how they are constructed, and how common overinterpretations can be avoided. We present principles and examples from gastric, thyroid, colorectal, and lung cancer to distinguish observed patterns from competing interpretations, identify additional information needed, and clarify which conclusions remain unjustified. Particular attention is given to denominators, age structure, age-period-cohort interpretation, bias, and the assumptions required for comparison and modeling. The aim is to enable cancer researchers to use descriptive epidemiology as a disciplined framework for interpreting population patterns rather than as background statistics or a substitute for causal inference.

Implementing an integrated inpatient-community rehabilitation pathway for adults hospitalised with acute exacerbations of COPD: a quality improvement study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hospitalisation for acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) is associated with functional decline through acute illness, inactivity, deconditioning and loss of independence, while delayed rehabilitation and fragmented postdischarge care can disrupt recovery. We evaluated a physiotherapy-led integrated inpatient-to-community rehabilitation pathway designed to improve recovery timing and continuity.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective quality improvement initiative with retrospective quantitative evaluation of routinely collected process and patient-level outcome data. The Accelerated Respiratory Care (ARC) programme combined enhanced inpatient rehabilitation with an 8-week community pathway and was refined through three Plan–Do–Study–Act cycles. Consecutive eligible AECOPD admissions were screened. Functional and patient-reported outcomes were assessed at admission, discharge and 8 weeks. Admission to 8-week changes among participants with paired data were analysed using paired t-tests; process measures were examined using chronological run charts.

RESULTS: Of 310 AECOPD admissions, 81 enrolled and 47 provided complete admission to 8-week follow-up. Mean time to ARC initiation was 2.9 days. Functional performance improved (1-minute sit-to-stand +5.9 repetitions, 95% CI 4.2 to 7.6; Short Physical Performance Battery +2.3 points, 95% CI 1.6 to 3.0), exceeding published minimal clinically important differences. St George’s Respiratory Questionnaire Total improved by 6.5 points (95% CI −11.1 to −1.9); Symptoms and Impact improved significantly, while Activity did not. Multiple Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System-29 domains also improved significantly. No exercise-related adverse events occurred. Run charts showed non-random variation, including late increasing trends in community contacts and total programme exposure.

CONCLUSION: ARC was feasible within routine care and associated with clinically meaningful improvements in functional and patient-reported outcomes among participants with complete follow-up. The pathway may provide a model for improving rehabilitative continuity after AECOPD, with the longer-term potential to reduce avoidable hospital use. Its effects on length of stay, readmissions and costs remain unestablished and require controlled evaluation. Sustained delivery is likely to require dedicated inpatient and community workforce capacity.

articles.title: Improving junior personnel engagement in military health research: a PPIE workshop.
SeekRBP: Leveraging Sequence-Structure Integration with Reinforcement Learning for Receptor-Binding Protein Identification.
articles.abstract:
MOTIVATION: Receptor-binding proteins (RBPs) initiate viral infection and determine host specificity, serving as key targets for phage engineering and therapy. However, the identification of RBPs is complicated by their extreme sequence divergence, which often renders traditional homology-based alignment methods ineffective. While machine learning offers a promising alternative, such approaches struggle with severe class imbalance and the difficulty of selecting informative negative samples from heterogeneous tail proteins. Existing methods often fail to balance learning from these "hard negatives" while maintaining generalization.

RESULTS: We present SeekRBP, a sequence-structure framework that models negative sampling as a sequential decision-making problem. By employing a multi-armed bandit strategy, SeekRBP dynamically prioritizes informative non-RBP sequences based on real-time training feedback, complemented by a multimodal fusion of protein language and structural embeddings. Benchmarking demonstrates that SeekRBP consistently outperforms static sampling strategies. Furthermore, a case study on Vibrio phages validates that SeekRBP effectively identifies RBPs to improve host prediction, highlighting its potential for large-scale annotation and synthetic biology applications.

AVAILABILITY: The source code of SeekRBP is available via: https://github.com/Saillxl/SeekRBP.

articles.title: Estimated Pulse Wave Velocity, Immediate Antihypertensive Treatment, and Clinical Outcomes After Acute Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether estimated pulse wave velocity (ePWV) influences the effect of early antihypertensive treatment in acute ischemic stroke remains unclear.

METHODS: This study was a post hoc analysis of the China Antihypertensive Trial in Acute Ischemic Stroke conducted in 2009-2013. ePWV was calculated using age and mean blood pressure on admission. The primary outcome was a composite of death or major disability at 14 days or hospital discharge and 3 months after stroke. We examined the association between ePWV and the primary outcome and tested for the interaction between ePWV and early blood pressure-lowering treatment.

RESULTS: Among the 4058 and 3975 participants included in the 14-day or hospital discharge and 3-month analyses, respectively, 1364 (33.6%) and 1001 (25.2%) experienced the composite outcome of death or major disability. The multivariable-adjusted risk ratios (95% CIs) for the highest (≥12.7 m/s) versus lowest ePWV tertile (<11.1 m/s) were 1.23 (1.06-1.43) for the composite outcome of death or major disability and 2.87 (1.10-5.39) for death at 14 days or hospital discharge (P for trend<0.05). At 3 months, the adjusted risk ratios (95% CIs) were 1.41 (1.17-1.70), 3.91 (2.02-7.57), and 2.33 (1.33-4.07) for the composite outcome of death or major disability, death, and vascular events, respectively. There were no significant differences in clinical outcomes between the early antihypertensive treatment and control groups across ePWV tertiles.

CONCLUSIONS: : Higher ePWV was associated with worse clinical outcomes after acute ischemic stroke, and ePWV did not modify the effect of early antihypertensive treatment.

REGISTRATION: -URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT01840072.

Retrospective trend analysis of schistosomiasis, a neglected tropical infection in Ghana.
Newly Reported Major Diagnoses and Subsequent Self-Reported Hypertension Treatment Status in Korean Adults Aged 50 Years or Older.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between a newly reported major diagnosis and subsequent self-reported hypertension-treatment status remains uncertain.

METHODS: We analyzed seven overlapping periods of three visits approximately 2 years apart in the Korean Longitudinal Study of Ageing (2006-2008-2010 through 2018-2020-2022). Eligibility required age ≥50 years, physician-diagnosed hypertension at Visit 1, and reported antihypertensive medication use or hypertension treatment at Visits 1 and 2. Newly reported diabetes, cancer, stroke, heart disease, or chronic lung disease was assessed at Visit 2. The Visit 3 outcome was a report of no current hypertension treatment, including no antihypertensive medication use. Modified-Poisson regression used participant-clustered standard errors. The adjusted absolute risk difference was defined as the standardized probability with a newly reported diagnosis minus that without one.

RESULTS: Among 13,579 observation periods from 3,581 participants, 932 included a newly reported diagnosis. Adjusted probabilities of no reported treatment were 7.5% with and 8.4% without a newly reported diagnosis. The adjusted risk ratio for not receiving treatment for hypertension, including antihypertensive medication, associated with a newly reported diagnosis was 0.89 (95% confidence interval 0.71-1.13); the adjusted absolute risk difference (newly reported diagnosis minus no newly reported diagnosis) was -0.90 percentage points (95% confidence interval -2.66 to 0.85).

CONCLUSIONS: A newly reported major diagnosis was not associated with self-reported antihypertensive medication use or hypertension treatment approximately 2 years later.

articles.title: Obstetric Critical Care Training in Pulmonary and Critical Care Fellowship: A Survey of Fellows and Program Directors.
Comparative Analysis of Visual Emphysema Detection with Low Attenuation Area Quantification: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To systematically review CT-based LAA% for emphysema quantification, explore the application of percentage low attenuation area (LAA% below -950HU), in comparison with visual emphysema scoring.

METHODS: Following PRISMA-DTA guidelines, searches were conducted (01-01-1972 to 01-04-2026) in PubMed, Embase®, and Web of Science databases to identify English-language studies of adults ≥18 years with CT-quantified emphysema. Two independent readers screened titles, abstracts and full texts against predefined inclusion/exclusion criteria. Studies comparing LAA%-quantified emphysema with visual scores were included.

RESULTS: 737 studies were reviewed, 5 (0.7%) met the eligibility criteria. These studies originated from Asia, Europe and the United States. LAA% cut-off values for emphysema varied: two studies used a 6% threshold, one used 5%, another used 1.5%, and one applied ordinal severity thresholds from 1% to 25%. Visual classification also differed, with three studies using the Fleischner Society system, one using a modified 3-point score, and another using the Goddard classification. Agreement between visual assessment and LAA%-based quantification was generally poor, with reported kappa values of 0.22 (n = 1,221), -0.06 (n = 200), and 0.48 (n = 98). Two studies further reported agreement based on sensitivity (86.8% and 58.0%) and specificity (84.2% and 39.0%).

CONCLUSIONS: Based on limited evidence, substantial heterogeneity exists between visual assessment and LAA% quantification in emphysema. Discordance between visual and quantitative CT assessment likely reflects differences in diagnostic criteria and technical characteristics, highlighting the need for standardized reporting and methodology.

ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This systematic review provides a comprehensive comparison of visual scoring and LAA% metrics. It demonstrates limited agreement and substantial methodological heterogeneity of CT assessment of emphysema.

articles.title: Patient choice and uptake of Home-based rehabilitation with Health coaching versus Center-based pulmonary rehabilitation after a COPD-related hospitalization.
articles.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Adherence to center-based pulmonary rehabilitation after a COPD-related hospitalization-which improves all outcomes, including survival-is only 3%. Home-based programs have been proposed as a more feasible option, but they are not systematically offered, and patient preference is unknown.
