OBJECTIVES AND METHODS: This pragmatic randomized trial involving patients with COPD recently hospitalized for a COPD exacerbation, originally aimed to investigate the comparative effect two arms: The choice of a facilitated referral to a center-based outpatient pulmonary rehabilitation program or a home-based program versus a home-based program on adherence to post-hospitalization rehabilitation and disease-specific QoL measured by the Chronic Respiratory Questionnaire. The trial aimed to investigate the patient's preference of home vs center-based rehabilitation in individuals randomized to the choice arm. Daily steps were measured by Actigraph ®.The asynchronous home-based program included weekly health coaching and daily monitoring of daily steps, symptoms, and a 20-minute daily flexibility-balance exercise routine.

RESULTS: Of 1,906 patients approached, 294 (15%) were randomized and agreed to the rehabilitation options offered by the study arms (uptake); of those, 56% completed the 12-week intervention (adherence). Of the 145 randomized to the choice arm, only one patient chose center-based PR; therefore, both groups received the same intervention, and results are presented as a one-group (before-after) analysis. Compared with baseline, the home intervention significantly improved (p < 0.01) physical and emotional QoL (Chronic Respiratory Questionnaire) and increased daily steps beyond the minimal clinically important difference. Trajectory models adjusted for age, FEV1%, and mMRC (breathlessness) confirmed sustained improvements in QoL at 6 and 12 months from baseline.

CONCLUSIONS: When offered a choice of rehabilitation setting after a COPD-related hospital admission for an exacerbation, home-based rehabilitation is patients' preferred option. Sustained quality-of-life improvements in 1 year may represent an opportunity to regain well-being and/or deliver primary palliative care. Our results may have important implications for clinical practice.

articles.title: Stopping GLP-1 treatment could double risk of heart attack, stroke, or death, study finds.
DTC1225, a novel benzothiazole-based compound, ameliorates MASLD by restoring metabolic-redox homeostasis and promoting hepatic lipid remodeling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a highly prevalent chronic liver disorder for which effective pharmacotherapies remain limited. Autophagy is a fundamental intracellular degradation and recycling process that maintains hepatic homeostasis by regulating lipid metabolism and mitigating lipid-induced cellular stress, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target for MASLD.

APPROACH AND RESULTS: Through an in vitro reporter-based screening of a chemical compound library, DTC1225, a novel benzothiazole-derived compound was identified as an autophagy activator that inhibited mTORC1 signaling, promoted transcription factor EB nuclear translocation, activated the autophagy-lysosome pathway, and enhanced autophagic flux. Functionally, DTC1225 reduced lipid droplet accumulation in steatotic HepG2 cells and differentiated 3 T3-L1 adipocytes, accompanied by alterations in autophagy-related markers and gene expression, and attenuation of MASLD-associated cellular injury. In a 4-month fructose, palmitate, and cholesterol diet-induced mouse model of MASLD, DTC1225 alleviated hepatic injury, modulated autophagic machinery, improved lipid metabolic profiles, restored redox homeostasis, and attenuated early-stage hepatic fibrosis. Hepatic lipidomics analysis further revealed that DTC1225 induced selective structural lipid remodeling, shifting the lipidome toward longer-chain and more unsaturated species, with a preferential enrichment of n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids-containing lipids, which may contribute to attenuated lipotoxicity and modulation of membrane fluidity.

CONCLUSIONS: DTC1225 ameliorates MASLD-associated hepatic pathology through multifaceted mechanisms involving coordinated modulation of autophagy-related pathways, lipid metabolism, and redox homeostasis, accompanied by favorable hepatic lipid remodeling. These findings provide a critical rationale for further development of DTC1225 as an innovative therapeutic candidate for MASLD and its associated complications.

articles.title: Microglial, migrasomes promote high-fat diet-induced neurotoxicity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic metabolic abnormalities are established drivers of cognitive decline, traditionally attributed to secondary sequelae of cerebrovascular dysfunction. However, cellular events linking early metabolic stress to subsequent neuronal injury and neurodegenerative processes remain poorly defined.

RESULTS: Here, we demonstrate that high-fat diet (HFD) triggers microglia to release pathogenic migrasomes (long-lived organelle-like vesicles) that promote neuronal injury, during an early phase of metabolic stress, before the emergence of overt dyslipidemia, hyperglycemia, and vascular pathology. We found that HFD feeding remodels the lipid environment of myelin-rich white matter and disrupts myelin homeostasis. Upon phagocytosis of this altered myelin, microglia generate migrasomes enriched with the neurotoxic alarmin S100A9. The pathogenicity of these vesicles was supported by complementary gain- and loss-of-function studies: intracerebral injection of HFD-induced microglial migrasomes was sufficient to impair cognition and induce neuronal injury in healthy mice, whereas Tspan9 conditional knockout in Cx3cr1-CreERT2 mice markedly reduced migrasome formation and thereby attenuated HFD-induced neurotoxicity. Mechanistically, we show that S100A9 is sorted into migrasomes post-myelin phagocytosis and is a critical mediator for their neurotoxic effects.

CONCLUSIONS: These results uncover a metabolic-myelin-migrasome axis as a critical driver of neuronal injury and cognitive decline, identifying the blockade of microglial migrasome biogenesis as a potential therapeutic strategy for metabolism-associated neurological dysfunction.

articles.title: Multi-omics analyses of HFpEF progression and regression reveals multi-organ-specific metabolic dysregulation and impaired inflammation resolution.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a complex cardiometabolic syndrome with limited effective therapies. Given its heterogeneity, whether withdrawal of cardiometabolic stress reverses HFpEF-associated inflammatory, metabolic, and molecular remodeling remains unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To characterize multi-organ metabolic, molecular, and bioactive-lipid remodeling in an obesity-hypertension HFpEF model and determine the extent of recovery during an 8-week combined high-fat diet withdrawal and L-NAME cessation protocol using parallel multi-omics profiling.

METHODS: HFpEF was induced in C57BL/6 mice using a high-fat diet plus nitric oxide synthase inhibition(H + L). A regression cohort(R-H + L) underwent simultaneous return to standard chow and L-NAME cessation for 8 weeks. Multi-omics profiling included targeted and untargeted lipidomics, cardiac transcriptomics, metabolomics, fecal microbiome, and plasma short-chain fatty acid analyses, with detailed assessment of the left ventricle.

RESULTS: H + L mice developed an obesity-hypertension HFpEF phenotype characterized by predominant diastolic dysfunction, concentric remodeling, hypertension, and increased fat mass. The combined regression of H + L protocol attenuated these phenotypic abnormalities but did not restore all measures to control levels. H + L was associated with multi-organ remodeling marked by altered arachidonic acid-derived oxylipid pathways, depletion of triacylglycerols and phospholipids, and enrichment of diacylglycerols and lysophospholipids, consistent with altered resolution-related lipid signaling. Cardiac transcriptomics revealed changes in immune, circadian, vascular, and mitochondrial gene programs, whereas metabolomics revealed altered energy, arginine, and redox metabolism. H + L was also associated with reduced microbial diversity and altered short-chain fatty acids, particularly acetate and propionate. Within the 8-week recovery window, partial reprogramming occurred, but differences remained in lipid signaling, metabolic stress responses, and microbiome-associated measures.

CONCLUSIONS: The HFD/L-NAME model is accompanied by extensive multi-organ metabolic and molecular remodeling. Combined withdrawal of HFD/L-NAME attenuates the HFpEF phenotype however did not fully normalize molecular profiles within the 8-week recovery period. Persistent lipid-remodeling and metabolic dysregulation may represent potential therapeutic targets thus warrants pathway specific investigation.

articles.title: Inhibition of p38γ attenuates liver fibrosis progression by alleviating metabolic reprogramming.
articles.abstract: Liver fibrosis, a consequence of chronic liver disease, commonly advances to cirrhosis and HCC without intervention. P38γ, a member of the four p38 mitogen-activated protein kinases (p38 MAPKs) isoforms, was involved in inflammation across several diseases, yet its impact on the activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) during liver fibrosis remains elusive. Here, we demonstrated that the expression of p38γ was notably higher in fibrotic livers of humans and mice as well as activated LX-2 cells. P38γ knockout could significantly decrease the severity of liver fibrosis, as demonstrated by the attenuated proportion of activated HSCs in the liver and epithelial-mesenchymal transformation and immune cell infiltration. Knockdown of p38γ could block proliferation and phenotypic transformation of activated HSCs in TGF-β1-induced LX-2 cells. Interestingly, knockdown of p38γ could reduce glycolytic flux and TCA cycle, accumulation of glycolytic intermediates and PPP metabolites and enhanced PPP cycling. However, metabolomic analysis results showed that the levels of metabolites were decreased in cultured LX-2 cells after lentivirus-p38γ treatment. Mechanistically, p38γ bound directly to the pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) through its kinase domain, and facilitated the phosphorylation and nuclear movement of PKM2, along with suppressed PKM2 ubiquitination to enhance PKM2-mediated glycolysis, resulting in intracellular lactate accumulation. Elevated lactate levels enhance histone lactylation marks, thereby promoting HSCs phenotypic transformation. Activating PKM2 pharmacologically with DASA-58 partially reversed the glycolysis and activation of HSCs mediated by p38γ. In the absence of available p38γ inhibitors, we conducted high-throughput virtual screening and discovered Crocin I as a new p38γ inhibitor. Therapeutic administration of Crocin I improved liver fibrosis pathologies in mice with optimal safety. An exploratory clinical observation in ten patients suggested a trend toward reduced liver fibrosis after XHHZGP treatment. In conclusion, p38γ promotes the progression of liver fibrosis by inducing phenotypic transformation of activated HSCs based on the intracellular PKM2 reprogramming function of activated HSCs.

articles.title: Defining Clinical Complexity Phenotypes in Atrial Fibrillation: Does It Change Care for Clinicians and Individual Patients?
Harnessing Lung-Kidney Crosstalk: A Novel Ex Vivo Platform for Donor Lung Rehabilitation.
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The lack of perfusate metabolic homeostasis during ex vivo lung perfusion (EVLP) may impair lung physiology or stability and limit the application of advanced donor lung therapies. There is evidence that additional organ support during EVLP can improve graft preservation and transplant outcomes. We hypothesized that incorporation of a kidney into an EVLP circuit would maintain perfusate homeostasis and improve lung preservation and metabolic activity.

METHODS: A novel circuit was developed to allow simultaneous normothermic perfusion of lungs and kidney in parallel. Donor pig lungs underwent 12 hours of cellular EVLP (EVLP, n=5) or combined cellular ex vivo lung-kidney perfusion (EVLKP, n=5). Lung function was assessed hourly and inflammatory cytokines, edema formation, hemolysis, histologic injury, and kidney performance were evaluated.

RESULTS: Simultaneous lung and kidney perfusion achieved target pulmonary and renal perfusion parameters with stable hemodynamics. EVLKP demonstrated trends of higher compliance, lower inspiratory pressure and pulmonary vascular resistance. Perfusate lactate concentration in EVLKP was markedly lower (P<0.0001), glucose concentrations were higher (P=0.0102), and pH shifted towards physiologic levels (P=0.0009) compared to EVLP. Oxygenation capacity was comparable between groups. Kidney perfusion remained stable throughout EVLKP.

CONCLUSIONS: Combined ex vivo lung-kidney perfusion is safe and feasible in a large-animal model for prolonged lung perfusion. EVLKP improved perfusate homeostasis compared with EVLP alone, which is associated with trends of improvement in lung physiologic parameters. These findings suggest that kidney-derived metabolic and biological support may provide benefits beyond perfusate filtration and highlight the potential importance of organ-organ crosstalk during ex vivo perfusion.

articles.title: Early-Life Cadmium Exposure Primes Diet-Induced Hepatic Lipotoxicity via SIRT1-Mediated Reprogramming of Mitochondrial Oxidative Metabolism in Rats.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects over 30% of adults and nearly 13% of children globally, with mitochondrial dysfunction central to its pathogenesis. Cadmium (Cd), a widespread environmental contaminant, accumulates in the liver through chronic dietary exposure. While recent studies have associated hepatic Cd accumulation with MASLD, it remains unclear whether early Cd exposure increases susceptibility to subsequent HFD-induced MASLD, and if so, through what mechanisms. To address this, rats were subjected to early Cd (4 weeks, 2 mg/kg feed), followed by a 6-week HFD (15% lard) or control diet. These in vivo findings were validated in vitro using rat BRL-3A hepatocytes exposed to Cd and palmitic acid (PA). Data revealed that early Cd did not act as an inducer, but rather as a potent exacerbator, markedly worsening HFD-evoked MASLD and PA-induced lipotoxicity. Mechanistically, this aggravation stemmed from Cd-driven reprogramming of mitochondrial oxidative metabolism, orchestrated by transcription factor EB (TFEB) inhibition. TFEB was identified from MASLD transcriptomic data as a direct transcriptional activator of FUNDC1. TFEB downregulation consequently impaired FUNDC1-dependent mitophagy, rewired mitochondrial oxidative metabolism, and promoted hepatic lipotoxicity. Upstream analysis integrating transcriptomic and protein-protein interaction networks identified SIRT1 as a critical node, whose Cd-evoked repression led to TFEB hyperacetylation and transcriptional inactivation, thereby compromising FUNDC1 transactivation. Rescue experiments confirmed that restoring SIRT1 reversed these defects and alleviated lipotoxicity. Collectively, early Cd reprograms mitochondrial oxidative metabolism via the SIRT1/TFEB/FUNDC1 cascade to exacerbate HFD-evoked lipotoxicity, highlighting this axis as a therapeutic target and underscoring the environmental-dietary interplay in MASLD.

articles.title: Isosilybin ameliorates chronic stress induced metabolic syndrome.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. General subjects
articles.abstract: Chronic stress contributes to the development of metabolic syndrome through disturbances in glucose metabolism, lipid homeostasis, and neuroendocrine regulation, thereby increasing the risk of cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes. Isosilybin, a bioactive flavonolignan derived from Silybum marianum (milk thistle), has demonstrated therapeutic potential in various metabolic disorders. However, its effects on chronic stress induced metabolic syndrome and its effects on SIRT6 and PGC-1α expression under chronic stress conditions remain unclear. The present study investigated the effects of isosilybin in a rat model of chronic unpredictable stress induced metabolic syndrome. A total of 24 rats were randomly allocated into four experimental groups (n = 6 per group). Fasting blood sugar levels, systolic blood pressure, lipid markers, and insulin resistance were evaluated. SIRT6 (sirtuin 6), c-Jun (transcription factor Jun), and PGC-1α (peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1 alpha) expression levels were also assessed in the pancreatic and liver tissues. During the final two weeks (weeks 7-8) of the eight week CUS protocol, rats received isosilybin (10 mg/kg/day, orally) while CUS exposure was continued. Isosilybin treatment markedly improved metabolic disturbances. Significant reductions were observed in all metabolic parameters compared with untreated stressed rats. Molecular analyses demonstrated partial restoration of SIRT6 expression together with normalisation of stress-induced alterations in c-Jun immunoreactivity and PGC-1α mRNA expression in hepatic and pancreatic tissues. The findings suggest that isosilybin attenuates chronic stress-induced metabolic syndrome by improving key metabolic parameters and is associated with changes in Sirt6 expression and PGC-1α mRNA levels.

articles.title: Metformin for the treatment of chronic liver disease: Mechanistic rationale, translational evidence, and repurposing opportunities.
articles.abstract: Chronic liver disease (CLD) is characterized by progressive hepatocellular injury, metabolic dysfunction, inflammation, fibrogenesis, and an increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Despite advances in understanding CLD pathogenesis, effective therapies targeting multiple disease-driving pathways remain limited. Metformin, a biguanide widely used to treat type 2 diabetes, has emerged as a candidate for drug repurposing because of its pleiotropic metabolic and immunomodulatory effects. This narrative review examines the mechanistic rationale, translational evidence, and clinical implications of metformin in treating CLD. Experimental studies indicate that metformin modulates AMP-activated protein kinase-dependent and -independent pathways involved in hepatic lipid metabolism, mitochondrial bioenergetics, oxidative stress, autophagy, immunometabolic signaling, hepatic stellate cell activation, and hepatocarcinogenesis. In preclinical models, these effects have been associated with reduced steatosis, inflammatory injury, fibrogenesis, and tumor-promoting signaling. Epidemiological and clinical studies also suggest that metformin use is associated with improved survival in selected patients with cirrhosis and a lower risk of HCC in individuals with diabetes. Although mechanistic, experimental, and epidemiological evidence is encouraging, randomized clinical studies have not consistently shown histological improvement in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis, and clinical findings remain heterogeneous across disease stages and etiologies. Limitations include the gap between mechanistic and clinical evidence, uncertainty regarding the relevance of proposed mechanisms, the context-dependent nature of metformin signaling, and the inherent limitations of observational studies. Overall, metformin is a biologically plausible therapeutic candidate for CLD, but its future clinical role will depend on integrating mechanistic insights with rigorous translational and clinical research to identify patients most likely to benefit.

articles.title: Short-term risk of herpes zoster following acute pyelonephritis vs. lower urinary tract infection: a propensity score-matched cohort study: Short title: Acute pyelonephritis and herpes zoster.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate a possible association among 50-to-80-year-olds between acute pyelonephritis (APN) as compared to with lower urinary tract infection (LUTI) and subsequent herpes zoster (HZ).

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX network. Participants aged 50-84 years with APN were compared with those with LUTI. Propensity score matching was performed using baseline characteristics. After a 1-month lag period, the primary outcome was a new diagnosis of herpes zoster during 6 months of follow-up. Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Age-stratified analyses and sensitivity analyses using 3-month and 9-month follow-up periods were performed.

RESULTS: After 1:1 propensity score matching, each cohort initially comprised 102,084 participants. Following application of the 1-month lag period, the primary outcome analysis included 101,949 participants with APN and 102,040 participants with LUTI. During the 6-month follow-up, herpes zoster occurred in 299 participants with APN and 141 with LUTI, corresponding to crude event proportions of 0.29% and 0.14%, respectively. Compared with LUTI, APN was associated with an increased risk of herpes zoster (HR, 2.13; 95% CI, 1.75-2.61). This association was observed among participants aged 50-64 years (HR, 1.74; 95% CI, 1.32-2.29) and 65-84 years (HR, 2.40; 95% CI, 1.81-3.18) alike. Sensitivity analyses using 3-month and 9-month follow-up periods yielded consistent findings.

CONCLUSION: Among adults aged 50-84 years during a 6-month follow-up period, APN was associated with a higher short-term risk of subsequent herpes zoster than LUTI.

articles.title: CRISPR, mRNA, and Beyond: Nucleic Acid Therapeutics in Allergy and Immunology.
articles.journal: Annals of allergy, asthma & immunology : official publication of the American College of Allergy, Asthma, & Immunology
articles.abstract: The management of allergic and immunologic diseases has long centered on symptom management rather than disease modification. Conventional pharmacotherapy controls manifestations of the immune dysregulation but does little to treat the underlying cause. Newer monoclonal and small molecule therapies target downstream effectors of the type 2 inflammatory cascade, and allergen immunotherapy, while disease-modifying, requires years of administration for effect. Nucleic acid therapies represent a different approach that intervenes at the level of genetic information itself, at the DNA, RNA, or protein-production step. This includes mRNA treatments that direct cells to produce therapeutic proteins or modify allergen-specific immune responses; antisense oligonucleotides and small interfering RNAs that selectively silence disease genes; adeno-associated viral vectors for sustained gene delivery; and CRISPR-based systems that permanently edit the genome. Several technologies have advanced to clinical proof of concept including a CRISPR gene-editing therapy (lonvoguran ziclumeran) that reduced hereditary angioedema attacks by 87% compared with placebo in a randomized controlled trial. An inhaled DNAzyme targeting the intracellular transcription factor GATA3 attenuated allergen-induced late asthmatic responses by 34% in humans, and CD19 CAR-T cell therapy induced drug-free remission in severe autoimmune disease. As of 2025, 24 oligonucleotide therapeutics have received FDA approval, including donidalorsen, the first RNA-targeted prophylactic therapy approved for hereditary angioedema. This review examines each therapeutic technology, its mechanism and delivery strategy, and the evidence relevant to allergic and immunologic disease. Persistent challenges, including delivery beyond the liver, immune responses to viral vectors, and the need for long-term safety data, are addressed alongside a proposed integration with existing treatment paradigms.

articles.title: Distal Humerus Nonunion Following Failed Internal Fixation: How do the Outcomes of Internal Fixation and Total Elbow Arthroplasty Compare?
articles.journal: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Distal humerus nonunions are difficult to treat. The supracondylar ostectomy and shortening (S.O.S.) technique, which combines humeral shortening, parallel plating, and bone grafting, maximizes the success of internal fixation. The purpose of this study was to compare the outcomes of the S.O.S. technique with the outcomes of total elbow arthroplasty (TEA) for distal humerus nonunions.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective review identified 25 distal humerus nonunions treated with the S.O.S. procedure and 45 TEA's performed specifically for distal humerus nonunion at a single institution between 1995 and 2019. All elbows had undergone at least 1 prior fixation attempt. The S.O.S. cohort had a younger mean age and less common intra-articular nonunion compared to the TEA cohort. Sex, mean number of prior surgeries, history of open fracture, and history of infection were similar between groups. Outcomes included complications, reoperations, range of motion, and Mayo Elbow Performance Scores (MEPS).

RESULTS: In the SOS cohort, 2 elbows were lost to follow-up, 21 elbows achieved union, and 2 elbows failed to heal and subsequently underwent conversion to a TEA. Complications occurred in 9 elbows (36%) following S.O.S. compared to 18 elbows (40%) following TEA (OR 0.8, p=0.7). The rates of all-cause reoperation were 48% (12 elbows) after S.O.S vs 27% (12) after TEA (OR 2.5, p=0.08). The S.O.S. cohort had a 100° mean flexion-extension arc compared to 115° for TEA (p=0.06) with similar mean pronation-supination arcs (S.O.S. 155° vs TEA 145°, p=0.2). MEPS scores were similar between groups (S.O.S 79 points, TEA 82 points, p=0.6). When stratifying by location of nonunion, elbows with intra-articular nonunion undergoing S.O.S had a 75% reoperation rate compared to 35% for extra-articular nonunions (OR 5.5, p=0.08). Intra-articular nonunions achieved higher MEPS with TEA compared to S.O.S. (85 vs. 51 points, p<0.01) while extra-articular nonunions achieved higher MEPS with S.O.S. compared to TEA (90 vs 65 points, p=0.01).

CONCLUSION: Despite achieving a high union rate, the S.O.S. procedure presented similar results compared to TEA in terms of MEPS, motion, complications, and reoperations. Elbows with an intra-articular nonunion had better outcomes with TEA while elbows with an extra-articular nonunion fared better with the S.O.S.

articles.title: No Difference in Revision Risk for Uncemented Humeral Stems Compared to Cemented Humeral Stems in Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty for Proximal Humerus Fracture: A Registry-Based Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reverse total shoulder arthroplasty (rTSA) is an effective treatment option for complex proximal humerus fractures (PHF). Humeral stems are commonly cemented in patients with poor bone quality, increased comminution and/or older age to provide rotational stability for stem fixation. Recently, the use of uncemented stems has gained popularity due to newer, more stable designs. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to evaluate whether there were any differences in uncemented versus cemented stems with respect to revision risk.

METHODS: Data from a US-based integrated healthcare system's Shoulder Arthroplasty Registry was utilized to conduct a cohort study. Adult patients with primary rTSA for PHF from 2011-2024 were included. The exposure of interest was humeral stem fixation, classified as uncemented versus cemented. Crude cumulative revision incidence was calculated as one minus the Kaplan-Meier estimate at 5-years follow-up. Propensity score-weighted Cox proportional hazard regression was used to evaluate the risk for all-cause revision. Propensity score weights were calculated prior to outcome evaluation using multivariable logistic regression and included age, sex, body mass index, race/ethnicity, diabetes status, smoking status, American Society of Anesthesiologist's classification, operative year, and operative time.

RESULTS: The cohort comprised 1,415 rTSA; 450 with uncemented stems and 965 with cemented stems. At 5-years follow-up, the crude revision probability was 3.9% for uncemented stems and 3.2% for cemented stems. After propensity score weighting, no difference was observed in all-cause revision for uncemented versus cemented stems (hazard ratio [HR]=1.20, 95% confidence interval [CI]=0.61-2.37, p=0.60). Further, no differences were observed in risk for revision for dislocation (HR=1.06, 95% CI=0.38-2.98, p=0.91) or infection (HR=1.52, 95% CI=0.48-4.82, p=0.48).

CONCLUSIONS: Overall, our observational registry-based cohort study found no difference in revision risk when comparing uncemented to cemented stems for the use of rTSA in PHF. However, we still recommend surgeons consider cemented stem fixation on a case-by-case basis in patients with complex fractures, poor bone quality, and metabolic conditions affecting bone density.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, Retrospective Cohort Comparison using Large Database, Treatment Study.

articles.title: Early-onset Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors: Distinct and Age-Related Metabolic Profiles.
articles.abstract: Early-onset pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (EO-PanNETs) exhibit distinct clinical features, but their metabolic profiles and age-related associations remain poorly understood. This study included 641 patients with PanNETs from four tertiary centers in China. EO-PanNETs were defined as PanNETs diagnosed before 50 years. 1,282 hospital-based nonmalignant controls were matched 1:2 by age and sex. Conditional logistic regression and Cox models were used to assess associations with PanNET occurrence and survival outcomes, respectively. Age-related effect modification was assessed using exposure-by-age interaction terms, with age modeled continuously using restricted cubic splines (RCS) in sensitivity analyses. Compared with late-onset cases, EO-PanNETs exhibited a higher prevalence of reduced high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (29.2% vs 17.8%, P < 0.001). Although the overall prevalence of diabetes was similar between EO-PanNETs and LO-PanNETs, the proportion of new-onset cases among patients with diabetes was higher in EO-PanNETs(71.4% vs. 44.8%, P = 0.018). In case-control analyses using matched nonmalignant controls as reference, alcohol intake (OR, 1.77 vs. 0.79; P interaction = 0.008), diabetes mellitus (OR, 9.72 vs. 3.34; P interaction = 0.048) and elevated triglycerides (OR, 1.75 vs. 1.01; P interaction = 0.023) showed stronger associations with PanNET occurrence in younger individuals. EO-PanNETs also exhibited better overall survival and progression-free survival than LO-PanNETs. RCS analyses further identified age-related differences in the associations of alcohol intake and overweight with PanNET occurrence. These findings highlight age-related differences in the associations of metabolic factors with PanNETs, providing new insights into age-related metabolic heterogeneity in this rare disease.

articles.title: Age-associated alterations in morphometry, intra-cortical canals, lacunar architecture, and mineral density in Type 2 diabetes: Implications for vertebral bone fragility in ZDF rats.
articles.abstract: Type 2 Diabetes (T2D) is associated with elevated bone fracture risk despite normal or higher bone mineral density (BMD), yet the mechanisms underlying vertebral fragility remain poorly understood. We investigated age-related changes in (1) growth, (2) microarchitecture, (3) microporosity (4) mineralization and (5) mechanical properties of vertebral bone from control and diabetic male ZDF rats at 12-weeks and 46 weeks of age. We report that vertebral growth and microarchitecture were compromised in diabetic rats at late-stage diabetes (46-weeks), as compared to control rats, evident from lower vertebral height and depth, thin cortical bone, and deteriorated trabecular architecture. While control rats maintained stable mineral density distribution with ageing, diabetic rats exhibited increased heterogeneity in cortical and trabecular bone in late-stage diabetes, despite unaffected mean BMD. In central cortical bone, diabetic rats had accelerated loss of intra-cortical canals as compared to controls with an unaffected age-driven lacunae density. In the central trabecular bone, T2D induced enlarged lacunae and altered mineral density distribution at early-stage diabetes (12 weeks), while as disease progressed, lacunae became rounder whilst maintaining lacunar density. Furthermore, age-matched differences in peri-lacunar mineralization were not found between control and diabetic rats. These multifactorial changes may contribute to the reduced failure load of vertebral body in diabetic rats (35% lower than age-matched control rats) at 46-weeks of age. Our findings underscore that fracture risk assessment and therapeutic strategies must look beyond BMD in T2D patients.

articles.title: Footprints, fingerprints, and the coronary culprit in MINOCA.

Smoking, recent physical activity and diagnosed cardiometabolic conditions in lifetime bipolar-spectrum disorder: A nationally representative comparison with lifetime major depressive episode without bipolar disorder.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease contributes substantially to premature mortality in bipolar disorder, making modifiable health behaviours important clinical targets. We analyzed the 2022 Canadian Mental Health and Access to Care Survey, including 294 respondents with lifetime bipolar-spectrum disorder derived from the Composite International Diagnostic Interview (CIDI; bipolar I, bipolar II, or algorithm-positive hypomania without bipolar I/II classification) and 938 with lifetime major depressive episode (MDE) without bipolar-spectrum disorder. Survey-weighted regression with 1000 bootstrap replicate weights estimated sociodemographically standardized prevalences and means. Bipolar-spectrum disorder was associated with higher scores on the six-item Kessler Psychological Distress Scale (K6; range 0-24; mean difference 1.32 points; 95% CI 0.34 to 2.29) and more sleep problems (prevalence difference 8.47 percentage points; 95% CI 0.43 to 16.52). Current smoking estimates were also higher (26.8% vs 19.3%; difference 7.49 percentage points; 95% CI -0.29 to 15.28), with a larger difference under the strict bipolar I/II definition after full sociodemographic adjustment. In the broad bipolar-spectrum comparison, smoking, distress, and sleep differences were attenuated and were not nominally significant after additional clinical adjustment. Recent activity was associated with higher positive mental health scores in both groups, while a differential association by diagnosis was not established. No group difference was detected in recent activity or diagnosed cardiometabolic conditions. The cross-sectional, self-reported design precludes causal inference. These results support integrated care addressing smoking, sleep, cardiometabolic assessment, and individualized physical activity.

articles.title: Trait impulsivity, nonsuicidal self-injury, and suicide-related indicators in adolescents with first-episode, treatment-naive depression: a cross-sectional mixed graphical model analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trait impulsivity is multidimensional, and passive suicidal ideation (PSI), active suicidal ideation (ASI), nonsuicidal self-injury (NSSI), and lifetime suicide attempt (SA) history are related but distinct constructs.

METHODS: A single-clinic cross-sectional study enrolled 518 adolescents with first-episode depression who were treatment-naive for any mental disorder. We estimated a nine-node mixed graphical model using LASSO with 10-fold cross-validation. The model estimated conditional associations among depressive and anxiety symptoms, three Barratt Impulsiveness Scale-11 (BIS-11) dimensions, PSI, ASI, past-month NSSI, and lifetime SA history.

RESULTS: The PSI-ASI edge had the largest estimated weight within the self-harm and suicide-related domain (w = 0.58). Motor impulsivity (Mot) was conditionally associated with anxiety symptoms, past-month NSSI (w = 0.23), and lifetime SA history (w = 0.15). Mot had the highest observed one-step bridge expected influence (0.71). Past-month NSSI and lifetime SA history were directly associated (w = 0.16); both were adjacent to PSI, ASI, non-planning impulsivity, and Mot. CS coefficients were 0.36 (EI) and 0.52 (BEI).

LIMITATIONS: Cross-sectional design precludes causal inference. The single-site sample limits generalizability; single-item measures and nonaligned reference periods constrain interpretation of NSSI-SA patterns.

CONCLUSIONS: Motor impulsivity showed a broader cross-domain association pattern than the other BIS-11 dimensions, whereas past-month NSSI and lifetime SA history were conditionally related but not interchangeable. These findings support dimension-specific assessment of impulsivity and separate clinical inquiry into past-month NSSI and lifetime SA history. Evaluating the temporal and clinical relevance of these findings requires longitudinal studies with aligned measurement windows.

articles.title: High free sugar dietary pattern, not high fiber-low energy density pattern, predicts increased bipolar disorder risk: Evidence from 124,191 participants.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Bipolar disorder (BD) is associated with high morbidity and premature mortality. Diet is potentially modifiable, but prospective evidence is limited. We aimed to derive nutrient-driven dietary patterns using reduced rank regression (RRR) and examine their prospective associations with incident BD.

METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, we analyzed UK Biobank data from 124,191 adults without a diagnosis of BD at baseline who completed at least two 24-h dietary recalls. BD diagnoses (ICD-10 F31.0-F31.9) were obtained from hospital and death registries. RRR derived dietary patterns maximising explained variation in four prespecified nutrient response variables: energy density, saturated fat, free sugars, and fiber density. Cox proportional hazards models estimated associations with incident BD. Restricted cubic splines tested non-linearity; heterogeneity and sensitivity analyses assessed robustness.

RESULTS: Two patterns were identified: high fiber density-low energy density (HFbD-LED) and high free sugars (HFS), explaining 42.3% and 19.4% of the total variation across the four nutrient response variables, respectively. During follow-up, 192 BD cases occurred. The HFS pattern was associated with higher BD risk (per 1-SD: HR 1.34, 95% CI 1.12-1.61), with an approximately linear dose-response. HFbD-LED showed no clear monotonic association in primary Cox models. Results were consistent across strata of polygenic risk, physical activity, and biological age acceleration, and in sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: A nutrient-driven dietary pattern characterized by high free sugars was prospectively associated with increased BD risk, supporting further investigation of reducing free sugars as a potential prevention target; causal inference requires confirmation in interventional studies.

articles.title: Associations between circadian-related behaviors and light exposure and depressive and anxiety symptoms among college students: A cross-sectional study of 10, 630 students from 4 universities.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depression and anxiety are highly prevalent among Chinese college students, whose circadian systems face chronotype-schedule mismatch, altered light exposure, and pervasive screen use; the joint associations of these factors with symptoms remain unclear.

METHODS: In a cross-sectional survey of 10,630 students from four Chinese universities, chronotype (rMEQ-5), social jetlag, daytime sunlight exposure, nighttime artificial light exposure (ALAN), and pre-sleep phone use were self-reported; depressive and anxiety symptoms were assessed with the PHQ-9 and GAD-7. Analyses comprised school fixed-effects linear regression with multiple imputation (m = 10), restricted cubic splines, latent profile analysis, and isotemporal substitution models.

RESULTS: In fully adjusted single-exposure models, evening chronotype (β = 2.06, 95% CI 1.76-2.35), social jetlag (0.30/h), ALAN (0.22/SD), and pre-sleep phone use (0.33/30 min) were associated with higher PHQ-9 scores, and daytime sunlight (-0.11 per h/d) with lower scores (all P < 0.05); GAD-7 associations were directionally consistent at half the magnitude. Chronotype associations were nonlinear and concentrated in the evening range; the daylight association attenuated beyond ≈2.5 h/d. A long pre-sleep phone plus high social jetlag class scored 0.74 and 0.40 points higher than the high-daylight class.

LIMITATIONS: The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference; exposures were self-reported.

CONCLUSIONS: Evening chronotype, social jetlag, nighttime light exposure, and pre-sleep screen use were associated with higher, and daytime sunlight with lower, symptom scores; the long pre-sleep phone plus high social jetlag class showed the highest scores; swapping 30 min of pre-sleep phone use for sunlight or sleep was associated with lower PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scores, warranting prospective confirmation.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary Delphi Consensus on the Current Management and Future Outlook for the Treatment of Chronic Graft-versus-Host Disease in Spain.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) is one of the most common complications of allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation, affecting 30-70% of all patients. The present study was conducted to provide a consensus view of the current management and approach to cGVHD in clinical practice in Spain.

METHODS: A study with Delphi methodology was carried out involving two rounds of individual assessments by a multidisciplinary panel of 44 experts corresponding to different professional profiles and geographical settings.

RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: In general, heterogeneity was observed between centres in the diagnosis and management of cGVHD, with differences in the process and times of referral or protocol compliance. Although some centres had multidisciplinary teams with reference personnel, there is still room for improvement to establish an optimal and standardized approach. The experts agreed that the creation of a national consensus, as well as continuous training of the professionals, better patient information, and the availability of biomarkers would be key to improving early diagnosis and patient follow-up. With the current treatments, a complete response to therapy is not usually achieved, and a partial response does not always guarantee stability of symptoms. In addition to efficacy, the experts highlighted toxicity reduction, convenience of dosing, and improved quality of life as key factors in choosing treatment. Most of the experts stated that they follow the recommendations of the NIH consensus for the evaluation of response.

articles.title: The Clinical Spectrum and Diagnostic Challenge of Abdominal Pain in Takayasu Arteritis: A Case-Based Review.
articles.abstract: Takayasu arteritis (TA) is a large-vessel vasculitis predominantly affecting the aorta and its primary branches. It is rare in children, and it poses significant diagnostic challenges, including high risks of misdiagnosis and treatment delay. We report the case of a 13-year-old female patient whose sole initial manifestation was abdominal pain. Over a short disease course of two weeks, aside from persistently and markedly elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate, she had no other typical symptoms of vasculitis. Initially evaluated by gastroenterology, she underwent a complex diagnostic process that ultimately led to imaging confirmation. To gain a deeper insight into this clinical presentation, we conducted a narrative review of existing relevant case reports alongside our present case. A targeted search of the PubMed and Scopus databases was performed, followed by descriptive summarization and analysis of the clinical features of the included cases. Both the present case and the literature review indicate that the clinical manifestations of TA are highly heterogeneous, and TA can be particularly insidious as the cause of abdominal pain. Clinicians should remain vigilant for the possibility of TA and actively consider it in patients with unexplained abdominal pain and persistently abnormal inflammatory markers, even in the absence of typical vascular symptoms. This also underscores the value of non-specific inflammatory markers as screening tools and the importance of multidisciplinary collaboration in identifying such rare diseases.

articles.title: Patterns of Physical Activity Across BMI Categories in Urban Children with Asthma.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Urban children with asthma engage in less physical activity (PA) than their peers. The relationships between levels of PA, sedentary behavior, and asthma control across the weight continuum has not been sufficiently studied. Our main objectives were to examine, in urban children with asthma: 1) how patterns of activity (sedentary time [ST], light PA [LPA], and moderate-to-vigorous PA [MVPA]) varied according to body mass index (BMI) status, and 2) whether ST decreased as MVPA time increased.

METHODS: Urban children (n = 142) ages 7-9 years with persistent asthma and varying weight status completed a 4-week study of asthma and PA. Asthma control was assessed via Asthma Control Test (ACT) scores, and PA was measured via accelerometry. We used dynamic factor analysis within a Structural Equation Modeling framework.

RESULTS: There were no significant differences in time spent in different types of PA based on BMI. Across weight categories, youth who spent more time in MVPA spent more time in LPA, and healthy weight youth who spent more time in MVPA also spent less time in ST (p = 0.02). Youth with OW/OB and better asthma control spent less time in LPA (p = 0.02).

CONCLUSION: Among urban children with asthma, there are different patterns of PA according to BMI status and level of asthma control. Interventions need to encourage engagement in all levels of activity, not just MVPA, and tailor strategies to optimize PA levels in the context of asthma control in this population.

articles.title: Finding the weak spot: a new approach to locate unstable sites prone to conduction block in heterogeneous cardiac tissue.
articles.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology
articles.abstract: Safe and stable action potential propagation is crucial for the proper function of the heart. Altered propagation safety can lead to slow conduction and conduction block, the key ingredients of reentrant and potentially life-threatening arrhythmias. Hence, it is important to develop metrics to quantify the stability of conduction. The previously proposed safety factor, useful in computer simulations, is difficult to determine in real cardiac tissue. We hypothesized that unstable conduction, potentially prone to block, is sensitive to small perturbations of pacing and tested this in co-cultured strands of homozygous connexin 43 knock-out and heterozygous knock-out or wild-type murine ventricular cardiomyocytes grown on microelectrode arrays, and in corresponding computer simulations. The tissues were stimulated at a progressively increasing rate in the presence vs absence of stochastic or alternating variations of pacing cycle length. Variations of conduction times between adjacent electrodes were analyzed using principal components analysis. In 18 out of 19 cultured strands and in 10 out of 10 simulations, our approach correctly identified and predicted the location at which conduction block ultimately occurred already hundreds of beats and tens of seconds in advance. Interestingly, prediction was already possible in the absence of pacing variations, albeit with lower reliability. Finally, the site of slowest conduction was not necessarily the site of block. By permitting to identify sites of unstable conduction most prone to block occurs, our work may find translational applications in clinical cardiac electrophysiology during mapping and ablation procedures and open new avenues to explore innovative markers of conduction stability.

articles.title: Impairment of LEM-domain function in LEMD2-associated cardiomyopathy.
articles.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology
articles.abstract: LEMD2 is an inner nuclear membrane protein that interacts with LMNA and contributes to nuclear membrane integrity and chromatin organization. Pathogenic LEMD2 variants are associated with progressive cardiomyopathy, but the relationship between Lemd2 protein abundance and disease severity remains unclear. Using computational modeling, we designed a Lemd2 in-frame deletion (p.Glu8_Leu9del, ΔE8_L9) within the LEM domain, predicted to alter its conformation, and generated knock-in (KI) mouse by CRISPR/Cas9. Western blot analysis demonstrated that the ΔE8_L9 deletion was associated with a near-complete loss of Lemd2 protein. Findings were considered alongside those previously reported for the Lemd2 p.L13R KI model, which retains ~68% of Lemd2 protein, to describe the cardiac phenotype and nuclear phenotypes associated with two distinct LEM-domain mutations. ΔE8_L9 homozygous mice exhibited postnatal growth retardation and rapidly progressive dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) with systolic dysfunction and myocardial fibrosis by postnatal day 21 (P21), whereas the reported p.L13R model exhibited later-onset DCM. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) revealed dense intranuclear chromatin aggregates and peripheral heterochromatin accumulation in cardiomyocytes. Bulk RNA sequencing identified downregulation of DNA replication- and DNA repair-related pathways at P1.5 and upregulation of mechanical stress-, senescence-, and immune response-related pathways at P21. Consistently, ΔE8_L9 hearts exhibited increased γ-H2AX-positive DNA damage and a numerically lower percentage of Ki-67-positive cardiomyocytes. The ΔE8_L9 model is associated with marked Lemd2 protein reduction, nuclear membrane abnormalities, altered chromatin architecture, DNA damage, and early-onset DCM.

articles.title: Chronic Topical Water-Soluble Cannabidiol Formulation Reduces Intraocular Pressure and Corneal Mechanical Sensitivity in DBA/2J Mice.
articles.abstract: Glaucoma is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disease and a leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. Although elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) is the main modifiable risk factor, current therapies often fail to fully prevent disease progression and may cause ocular discomfort. Cannabidiol (CBD) has attracted increasing interest due to its anti-inflammatory, analgesic and vasoregulatory properties, yet its ocular effects remain controversial, partly due to formulation-dependent limitations and short-term administration paradigms. We evaluated a novel water-soluble topical CBD formulation in a spontaneous murine model of glaucoma (DBA/2J mice), using CD-1 mice as a non-glaucomatous comparator strain. IOP, tear production, corneal mechanical sensitivity and body weight were assessed longitudinally in conscious animals following acute and chronic CBD administration (once or twice daily). Contralateral untreated eyes were analyzed to investigate potential systemic or bilateral effects. Following an initial transient IOP increase, topical CBD progressively induced a significant and sustained reduction of IOP in the treated eyes of DBA/2J mice, particularly during chronic twice-daily administration. IOP changes in contralateral eyes were smaller and inconsistent, supporting a predominantly local ocular effect. CBD also increased corneal touch threshold in DBA/2J mice, indicating reduced corneal mechanical sensitivity, with effects persisting after treatment withdrawal. Tear production and body weight were not significantly affected in either strain, suggesting good ocular and systemic tolerability. Overall, chronic topical administration of a water-soluble CBD formulation lowered IOP and modulated corneal sensitivity in a strain-dependent manner. These findings support CBD as a potential adjunctive therapeutic strategy targeting both ocular hypertension and sensory dysfunction.

articles.title: β-Amyrin,an active compound of Bryophyllum pinnatum,alleviates alcoholic liver disease by regulating AKT1 expression and enhancing antioxidant defense.
articles.abstract: Bryophyllum pinnatum (L. f.) Oken (BP), a traditional hepatoprotective herb, has demonstrated therapeutic potential in managing liver disorders. However, the specific bioactive compounds of BP and its mechanisms against alcoholic liver disease (ALD) remain unclear. In this study, the bioactive compounds of BP were screened by database mining and their targets were predicted. A compound-target-disease network was constructed to identify core targets, followed by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation to validate the binding of β-Amyrin with AKT1. The hepatoprotective efficacy and mechanism were finally verified in ethanol-exposed HepG2 cells. A database screening process has identified four bioactive compounds (β-Amyrin, Astragalin, α-Amyrin and Bryophyllin A). Network pharmacology analyses revealed 138 common targets, primarily associated with lipid metabolism, hepatitis B and C, and the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, and core targets included AKT1, CCND1, EGFR, HIF1A and SRC. Notably, in vitro experiments using ethanol-exposed HepG2 cells demonstrated that β-Amyrin significantly reduced transaminase (ALT, AST), total cholesterol (TC) and triglyceride (TG). Additionally, β-Amyrin enhanced antioxidant defense (SOD, CAT, GSH) and suppressed malondialdehyde (MDA) accumulation. Furthermore, β-Amyrin alleviated intracellular lipid accumulation as evidenced by Oil Red O staining. Mechanistically, β-Amyrin restored the expression of total AKT1 and its phosphorylation level (p-AKT1), which could be abolished by AKT1-specific inhibitor MK2206. This is the first study to identify β-Amyrin as the key bioactive compound of BP against ALD, and these findings provide compelling evidence for BP's potential as a therapeutic strategy for ALD.

articles.title: Elucidating lysosomal dysfunction in cardiac fibrosis progression: Molecular understanding and pharmacological targeting strategies.
articles.abstract: Cardiac fibrosis is a critical pathological condition characterized by an excessive accumulation of extracellular matrix components resulting from persistent cellular stress, inflammation, oxidative stress, and organelle dysfunction. These insoluble fibers form a 3D matrix that is evident in numerous heart-related conditions, including myocardial infarction, heart failure, cardiomyopathies, and hypertension. Cardiomyocytes, unlike fibroblasts and endothelial cells, are post-mitotic and rely heavily on cellular quality-control systems to sustain their workload. Lysosomes, a single-lipid-bilayered membrane-bound organelle, are one of the important organelles that maintain cellular homeostasis by degrading and recycling cellular debris. Autophagy is one of the catabolic processes that is heavily reliant on lysosomes to form autolysosomes, which help degrade and recycle cellular components, proteins, and lipids, and maintain cellular homeostasis. Recently, lysosomal dysfunction has been found to play a critical contributing role in modulating cardiac fibrosis. The involvement of lysosomal dysfunction in mediating cardiac fibrosis progression involves several intriguing mechanisms that regulate lysosomal integrity, including V-ATPase, transcription factor EB (TFEB), lysosomal-associated membrane protein-2 (LAMP-2), cathepsin B, and chaperone-mediated autophagy, among others. The subsequent review, therefore, demonstrates the role of lysosomes in physiological and pathological heart conditions, with a particular emphasis on cardiac fibrosis, the central mechanism underlying the most aggressive stages of cardiac disease. The correlation between lysosomal dysfunction and cardiac fibrosis, as well as the interconnections and cellular pathways linking them, is discussed, along with emerging preclinical and clinical investigations that could be pursued to elucidate the role of lysosomal dysfunction in cardiac fibrosis progression.

articles.title: Beyond ACE2 downregulation: daphnetin as a multi-target agent for COVID-19 and rheumatic comorbidities.
articles.abstract: The continuous emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants (e.g., JN.1, KP.3) and the significantly elevated risk of severe COVID-19 in patients with rheumatic autoimmune diseases highlight an urgent unmet clinical need for dual-targeted therapeutics. Daphnetin (7,8-dihydroxycoumarin), a natural coumarin compound with a long history of clinical use in China, prevents SARS-CoV-2 infection by downregulating the viral entry receptor ACE2 through inhibition of HIF-1α and JAK2/STAT3 signaling. This review synthesizes the pleiotropic pharmacological mechanisms of daphnetin, including anti-inflammatory (NF-κB, JAK/STAT, NLRP3), antioxidant (Nrf2/Keap1), immunomodulatory (Th17/Treg balance), and mitochondrial protective pathways. These pathways are critically involved in the pathogenesis of both severe COVID-19 and rheumatic diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). We propose that daphnetin represents a novel "one agent, dual protection" strategy: it not only blocks viral entry by reducing ACE2 but also mitigates the hyperinflammatory and oxidative stress states that exacerbate both COVID-19 severity and rheumatic disease activity. Given its established safety, oral activity, and low cost, daphnetin is a promising candidate for clinical translation in high-risk comorbid populations. Key unresolved questions and future research directions are also discussed.

articles.title: HSPB1 in Dorsal Hippocampal Astrocytes Contributes to Stress-Induced Reinstatement of Methamphetamine Conditioned Place Preference.
articles.abstract: Methamphetamine (MA) addiction is a chronic neuropsychiatric disorder characterized by compulsive drug-seeking behavior and a high relapse risk driven by the persistent retrieval of reward-associated memories. Although astrocytes are increasingly recognized as important modulators of drug-associated behaviors and reward memories, their contributions to MA-associated contextual memory remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the role of dorsal hippocampal CA1 (dCA1) astrocytes in a stress-induced reinstatement model of MA conditioned place preference (CPP) in female mice. Reinstatement of MA CPP elevated expression of astrocytic markers GFAP and S100β and enhanced Ca2+ signals in dCA1 astrocytes. Chemogenetic inhibition of dCA1 astrocytes significantly attenuated CPP reinstatement. Proteomic profiling of hippocampal tissue revealed heat shock protein beta-1 (HSPB1) as a differentially expressed protein during reinstatement. Subsequent immunohistochemical and immunofluorescence analyses revealed increased HSPB1 immunoreactivity in the dCA1 and its predominant colocalization with GFAP-positive astrocytes. Notably, pharmacological inhibition of HSPB1 using the J2 inhibitor, or GFAP-promoter-driven HSPB1 knockdown robustly suppressed stress-induced reinstatement of MA CPP. These findings reveal that HSPB1 in dCA1 astrocytes contributes to stress-induced reinstatement of MA-associated contextual preference.

articles.title: Neuronal and mitochondrial phenotypes in iPSC-derived bipolar disorder models with and without a family history of mitochondrial disease.
articles.abstract: Psychiatric disorders frequently accompany primary mitochondrial diseases (PMDs), suggesting shared biological pathways between mitochondrial function and psychiatric vulnerability. In this exploratory study, we investigated whether bipolar disorder (BD) occurring in the context of a family history of primary mitochondrial disease is associated with differences in neuronal and mitochondrial phenotypes. We generated induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), neural progenitor cells (NPCs), and cortical neurons (CNs) from three non-psychiatric controls, three individuals with BD without a family history of mitochondrial disease, and three individuals with BD who did not themselves have mitochondrial disease but had relatives with clinically diagnosed mitochondrial (BD-FHMD). Our primary endpoints were distinguished network activity and cytosolic and mitochondrial Ca2+ dynamics, complemented by measurements of mitochondrial and cellular function and metabolomic profiles across differentiation. Across neurodifferentiation, we assessed neuronal network activity, calcium dynamics, mitochondrial and cellular health, and metabolomic signatures. BD neurons exhibited sustained hyperexcitability with increased firing and burst activity. In contrast, BD-FHMD neurons showed lower network activity with enhanced cytosolic calcium responses and prolonged mitochondrial calcium transients. BD-FHMD also exhibited stage-dependent mitochondrial alterations, while BD and BD-FHMD showed distinct developmental metabolic signatures. Together, these findings identify two distinct mitochondrial-associated phenotypes within BD. BD is characterized by a hyperexcitable neuronal phenotype associated with altered developmental metabolic programming, whereas BD-FHMD exhibits calcium dysregulation and altered mitochondrial developmental trajectories consistent with increased bioenergetic vulnerability. These findings suggest that BD occurring in the context of a family history of primary mitochondrial disease may be characterized by a distinct pattern of neuronal and mitochondrial dysfunction. Replication in larger, independently characterized cohorts will be important to determine whether this family-history-defined phenotype can contribute to biologically informed subtyping and therapeutic approaches in BD.

articles.title: Sepsis in Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell Therapy: A Six-Year Nationwide Analysis of Clinical Outcomes and Healthcare Resource Utilization in Hospitalizations for Hematologic Malignancies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients receiving chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy are at increased risk for infection and sepsis due to malignancy-related immune dysfunction, lymphodepleting chemotherapy, and immunosuppression used to treat CAR T-cell toxicities; however, nationally representative estimates of sepsis burden and economic impact remain limited.

OBJECTIVES: This study uses nationally representative U.S. data to evaluate patient characteristics, clinical outcomes, and healthcare utilization associated with sepsis among hospitalizations involving CAR T-cell therapy.

STUDY DESIGN: Adult hospitalizations for acute lymphoblastic leukemia, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, or multiple myeloma in which CAR T-cell therapy was administered between 2017 and 2022 were identified from the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) and stratified by sepsis status. After excluding records with missing covariates, survey-weighted analyses were performed to generate nationally representative estimates. Multivariable regression models were used to evaluate differences in mortality and secondary outcomes, with statistical significance defined as a two-sided p value < 0.05.

RESULTS: Among 10,450 weighted CAR T-cell therapy hospitalizations, 645 (6.2%) were complicated by sepsis. In-hospital mortality was significantly higher in hospitalizations with sepsis (28.7% vs 1.1%; adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 33.96; 95% confidence interval [CI] 18.67-61.75). Sepsis was independently associated with higher odds of acute kidney injury (aOR 4.31), respiratory failure (aOR 11.85), acute hepatic failure (aOR 44.42), and septic shock (aOR 411.05), along with greater use of renal replacement therapy, mechanical ventilation, and vasopressors. Thrombohemorrhagic events were more frequent among hospitalizations with sepsis, including disseminated intravascular coagulation (aOR 9.30), acute venous thromboembolism (aOR 2.95), acute coronary syndrome (aOR 27.63), acute ischemic stroke (aOR 7.53), gastrointestinal hemorrhage (aOR 6.47), and intracranial hemorrhage (aOR 4.84), as well as increased need for cryoprecipitate and fresh frozen plasma transfusion (aOR 2.70). Sepsis was also associated with longer hospital stay (adjusted incidence rate ratio [aIRR] 1.96) and higher hospitalization charges (adjusted charge ratio [aCR] 1.22).

CONCLUSIONS: Sepsis was documented in approximately 6% of CAR T-cell hospitalizations and was associated with higher in-hospital mortality, organ dysfunction, critical-care utilization, longer hospitalization, and higher hospitalization charges. These findings highlight the substantial clinical and healthcare burden associated with sepsis in this population.

articles.title: Decoding Type 2 Asthma Heterogeneity: Cluster Analysis of Australasian Severe Asthma Network.
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Variable clinical remission rates on biologics may reflect heterogeneity within type 2 (T2) asthma, but such heterogeneity remains largely unexplored.

OBJECTIVES: To identify clinically distinct T2 asthma subtypes using multidimensional profiling and hierarchical clustering.

METHODS: All T2 participants (n=764) were from the Australasian Severe Asthma Network, identified by elevated eosinophil levels, elevated FeNO, or allergic sensitization. Baseline clinical and inflammatory data were integrated to identify potential clusters in the training set using hierarchical clustering, followed by prospective assessment of exacerbation over 12 months. A random forest classifier was internally cross-validated and applied to a held-out validation set to assess profile consistency.

RESULTS: Three subtypes emerged as: Cluster 1 (n=241, 45.0%) represented a female-predominant, well-controlled allergic subtype; Cluster 2 (n=110, 20.6%) constituted older T2 asthma patients with overlapping non-T2 features, including increased sputum neutrophil counts, fixed airflow limitation, and multiple comorbidities, with higher severe exacerbation rates (incidence rate ratios [IRR]=2.54, P=0.025) and emergency visit rates (IRR=5.06, P=0.040); and Cluster 3 (n=184, 34.4%) showed multiple elevated T2 biomarkers, poor symptom control and increased severe exacerbation (IRR=2.49, P=0.007) and hospitalization risk (IRR=3.28, P=0.009). The classifier showed 83.6% agreement with the original cluster assignments (κ=0.738), with post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC, age, and BMI as leading discriminators.

CONCLUSIONS: T2 asthma encompasses distinct subtypes with prognostic and therapeutic implications. Our findings support a precision medicine approach for these subtypes: Cluster 3 patients may warrant early assessment for biologic therapy when eligible, while Cluster 2 may benefit from integrated strategies addressing non-T2 traits.

articles.title: Obesity and the heart: "Dangerous Liaisons".
articles.journal: Revista portuguesa de cardiologia : orgao oficial da Sociedade Portuguesa de Cardiologia = Portuguese journal of cardiology : an official journal of the Portuguese Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract: Obesity is the epidemic of the 21st century, with a high impact on global health, and on cardiovascular health in particular, being simultaneously an independent cardiovascular risk factor and being in the etiopathogenesis of other risk factors, namely diabetes. The development of new drugs with proven efficacy in its treatment, such as GLP1 agonists, and dual GLP1 and GIP agonists, with a significant impact on cardiovascular, renal, and other diseases, constitutes a true revolution in the treatment of patients with obesity and cardiovascular disease (CVD). The emergence of the new concept of cardio-renal-metabolic syndrome, in which the presence of excess and/or dysfunctional adipose tissue translates into a set of pathophysiological mechanisms that lead to the development of cardiac, renal, and metabolic diseases, is relatively recent. However, it reflects an increasingly present reality in obese patients, where the coexistence of these pathologies represents a significant worsening of the prognosis and greater difficulty in their management. Given the challenges in prevention, diagnosis, and treatment that patients with adiposopathy and CVD represent, it is clearly beneficial that their approach be carried out by multidisciplinary teams in order to effectively respond to the multiple challenges that this pathology currently presents.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of Tafamidis-treated ATTR-CM patients in a real-world cohort: Comparison with the results of pivotal trials.
articles.journal: Revista portuguesa de cardiologia : orgao oficial da Sociedade Portuguesa de Cardiologia = Portuguese journal of cardiology : an official journal of the Portuguese Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is a progressive and life-threatening disease that leads to heart failure and increased mortality. Pivotal clinical trials - ATTR-ACT, ATTRibute-CM and HELIOS-B - have provided robust evidence supporting the efficacy of TTR stabilizers (Tafamidis and Acoramidis) and the TTR-synthesis inhibitor Vutrisiran in reducing mortality and cardiovascular events. This study aims to compare the clinical characteristics and cardiovascular outcomes of a real-world Portuguese cohort of patients with ATTR-CM treated with tafamidis to those reported in pivotal clinical trials.

METHODS: Single-center, observational study including consecutive patients with ATTR-CM treated with tafamidis 61 mg once a day. Clinical, laboratory, and echocardiographic data were collected and compared with published results from the ATTR-ACT, ATTRibute-CM, and HELIOS-B trials. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality at 24 months, assessed by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis. Secondary outcomes included cardiovascular-related hospitalizations and quality of life, assessed by KCCQ-OS during follow-up, both of which were compared across studies.

RESULTS: A total of 89 patients were included (76 males; 39 with hereditary ATTR-CM and 50 with wild-type ATTR-CM). The Portuguese real-world cohort was older than the ATTR-ACT and HELIOS-B study populations (mean age 78.6 vs. 74.5 vs. 77.0 years, respectively; p<0.001) and exhibited better functional capacity as assessed by New York Heart Association class compared to ATTR-ACT, ATTRibute-CM and HELIOS-B (New York Heart Association (NYHA) I: 30 vs. 9 vs. 12 vs. 15%, respectively; p<0.001). Echocardiography showed higher LVEF (55 vs. 48%, p<0.001) and better GLS (-15 vs -9%, p<0.001) compared with ATTR-ACT. NT-proBNP levels were comparable across cohorts (2639 vs. 2996 vs. 2946 vs. 2021 pg/mL, respectively; p>0.05). Hereditary ATTR was significantly more prevalent in the Portuguese cohort (44%) compared to ATTR-ACT (24%), ATTRibute-CM (10%), and HELIOS-B (11%; p<0.001), reflecting the endemic p.Val50Met mutation in Portugal. Over a follow-up of 27.4 ± 19.3 months, seven patients (7.9%) experienced heart failure hospitalizations and five patients (5.4%) died, including three cardiovascular deaths, corresponding to an annualized cardiovascular-related hospitalization rate of 0.034 events per patient-year. The 24-month all-cause mortality of 5.6% was considerably lower than reported in ATTR-ACT (24.2%), ATTRibute-CM (15.9%), and HELIOS-B (11.4%). However, KCCQ-OS scores were lower than in ATTRibute-CM and HELIOS-B (both p<0.001), likely reflecting comorbidities, and neurological involvement in hereditary cases.

CONCLUSIONS: Patients receiving tafamidis 61 mg for ATTR-CM in this real-world cohort were older, had a higher prevalence of hereditary ATTR, and demonstrated better baseline functional capacity compared to those enrolled in pivotal clinical trials. These observational data provide valuable real-world evidence complementing clinical trials, supporting the use, and safety of tafamidis in this Portuguese cohort.

articles.title: "Rotations in Other Specialties During Neurosurgical Training in Africa: A Multi-country Cross-Sectional Study".
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rotations in specialties outside neurosurgery contribute to the development of multidisciplinary competencies during neurosurgical training. However, the experiences and perceptions of African neurosurgical trainees and specialists regarding these rotations remain insufficiently documented.

OBJECTIVE: To describe respondents' self-reported experiences and perceptions regarding the type, timing, duration, and educational value of rotations in other specialties during neurosurgical training.

METHODS: A multicounty, descriptive cross-sectional electronic survey recruited neurosurgery residents and qualified neurosurgeons trained in Africa through professional networks using non-probability convenience sampling from April 30 to August 30, 2026. A structured questionnaire, pilot-tested among 10 senior neurosurgeons trained outside Africa and excluded from the study, assessed specialty rotations, international training exposure, perceived educational benefits, and curricular gaps. Quantitative data were summarized using descriptive statistics, while free-text responses were descriptively categorized by one investigator and summarized using frequencies and percentages.

RESULTS: 97 participants from 19 African countries were included, comprising 49 residents (50.5%) and 48 qualified neurosurgeons (49.5%). Overall, 86 (88.7%) had undertaken rotations outside neurosurgery. The most frequently reported rotations were General surgery (n=67) and neurology (n=62). Rotations were most reported during the first three years of training. 36 participants (37.1%) reported international rotations.

CONCLUSION: Among surveyed African neurosurgery residents and qualified neurosurgeons, rotations in other specialties were commonly reported and generally perceived as educationally valuable. These findings may inform future discussions and the development of competency-based neurosurgical training curricula adapted to different African contexts but should not be interpreted as representative of all African training programs.

articles.title: Risk Factors for Surgical Site Infection Following Thoracolumbar Instrumentation: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study of 797 Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical site infection (SSI) following thoracolumbar instrumentation is a serious complication associated with revision surgery, prolonged hospitalization, extended antibiotic therapy, and increased healthcare costs. This study aimed to determine SSI incidence and identify independent risk factors for its development.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults who underwent thoracolumbar instrumentation between 2016 and 2022 and had at least 1 year of follow-up. Patients operated on for primary spinal infection were excluded. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and operative variables were analyzed. Univariable analyses were followed by multivariable Firth-penalized logistic regression.

RESULTS: The cohort included 797 patients with a median age of 60 years (IQR, 49-67); 503 (63%) were female. During the overall follow-up period, 33 of 797 patients (4.1%) developed deep SSI, including 31 of 797 (3.9%) within 1 year and 27 of 797 (3.4%) within 90 days. Among the 31 patients with deep SSI within 1 year, the median time from surgery to diagnosis was 28 days (IQR, 18-49). In the prespecified core multivariable models, the number of instrumented vertebrae was consistently associated with higher odds of both 1-year SSI (adjusted OR, 1.50 per additional vertebra; 95% CI, 1.20-1.87; p<0.001) and 90-day SSI (adjusted OR, 1.45 per additional vertebra; 95% CI, 1.15-1.84; p=0.002). Elevated preoperative CRP and platelet count were independently associated with 1-year SSI in sensitivity analyses, whereas BMI and operative time were not.

CONCLUSION: Deep SSI occurred in 3.9% of patients within 1 year after thoracolumbar instrumentation, with most infections diagnosed within 90 days. Longer instrumentation constructs were consistently associated with higher adjusted odds of SSI across both observation windows. Elevated preoperative CRP and platelet count showed additional associations with 1-year SSI in separate sensitivity analyses; these exploratory findings require independent validation.

articles.title: Fully endoscopic microvascular decompression for trigeminal neuralgia accompanied by intraosseous subarcuate loops.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The presence of vascular variations often renders microvascular decompression (MVD) more technically demanding and increases the risk. This study aims to describe a rare variant and report our initial experience in safely MVD via fully endoscopic techniques without drilling the petrous bone.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 356 patients with trigeminal neuralgia (TN) who underwent fully endoscopic MVD between 2010 and 2025 and identified six patients with intraosseous subarcuate loop (SL). Patient data (age, sex), clinical characteristics (symptoms, visual analog scale [VAS] pain score), radiological images, surgical records, and intraoperative videos were analyzed.

RESULTS: Six patients (1.7%) with SL arising from lateral pontine segment of the anterior inferior cerebellum arterial (AICA) and embedded in the petrous bone were identified. Using a 30° endoscope, MVD was successfully performed without drilling the petrous bone to mobilize the loop. There was no endoscope-related mortality. Transient facial numbness occurred in one patient and resolved spontaneously one month after surgery. No postoperative hematoma, infarction, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak, or intracranial infection occurred. All patients experienced immediate pain relief postoperatively. During follow-up, no recurrence was recorded.

CONCLUSIONS: Fully endoscopic techniques without drilling petrous bone are feasible to perform MVD in patients with intraosseous SL. Accurate diagnosis of such variation may favor surgical decision-making to reduce the risk of vascular injury.

articles.title: Urinary Catheter Management on Leaving the Operating Theatre After Elective Colonic Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of gastrointestinal surgery : official journal of the Society for Surgery of the Alimentary Tract
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether patients undergoing elective colonic resection need to keep a urinary catheter when leaving the operating theatre remains uncertain.

METHODS: We searched MEDLINE/PubMed and Cochrane CENTRAL (7 September 2026) and Embase (15 October 2026) for studies reporting urinary retention or urinary tract infection (UTI) by catheter status on leaving theatre after elective colonic surgery. Patients were grouped as Group B (catheter kept) or Group A (no catheter), the latter divided into A1 (never catheterized) and A2 (catheter removed before leaving theatre). Comparative studies were pooled with the Mantel-Haenszel method, with a Peto odds ratio (OR) sensitivity analysis. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and ROBINS-I, and certainty with GRADE.

RESULTS: Six studies met inclusion criteria (2000-2025; n = 845).
