Retention was 4.3% (12/276) in Group A/A2 versus 1.6% (4/246) in Group B (risk ratio [RR] 3.04, 95% CI 0.96-9.62; Peto OR 2.80, 95% CI 1.02-7.69). Retention was 10.7% (16/150) in A1 versus 2.7% (2/73) in A2 (RR 3.50, 95% CI 0.78-15.72; Peto OR 2.66, 95% CI 0.92-7.72). UTI occurred in ≤5.5% of cohorts. All comparative studies were at serious or high risk of bias, and certainty of evidence was very low.

CONCLUSION: Leaving theatre without a catheter appears feasible in selected patients, with low UTI rates, but retention may be more frequent and the evidence is of very low certainty. It cannot establish non-inferiority. Adequately powered randomized trials with standardized outcome definitions are needed.

articles.title: Association of metoprolol with temporal changes in SIRT1, oxidative stress, and inflammatory biomarkers.
articles.abstract: There is a paucity of studies on the effect of beta-blocker on sirtuins (SIRT1)-mediated inflammation and oxidative stress in ischemic stroke. We report the effect of metoprolol on the temporal kinetics of SIRT1-mediated oxidative stress markers [catalase (CAT), glutathione peroxidase (GPx), malondialdehyde (MDA), and reactive oxygen species (ROS)], proinflammatory cytokines (TNFα and IL1β), and their association with outcomes. This was a sub-analysis of our earlier study on effect of beta-blocker in acute stroke. Forty-eight patients within 3-days of ischemic stroke were included. Their demographic characteristics, risk factors for stroke, GCS/NIHSS score, hematological and biochemical parameters, electrocardiogram, echocardiography, and cranial-MRI findings were noted. SIRT1, TNFα, and IL1β mRNA fold-changes were measured by using real-time PCR, and GPx, CAT, MDA, and ROS were measured by using a spectrophotometer. These biomarkers were also measured in 59 healthy-controls. The outcome was defined at 1 and 3-months using the modified Rankin Scale. Twenty-eight patients received metoprolol, and 20 received amlodipine. There is a gradual reduction in TNFα, IL1β, ROS, and MDA and an increase in CAT level in both groups; however, more marked in the metoprolol group. On day 15, the metoprolol group had a comparable level of SIRT1, TNFα, IL1β, and CAT to those with the healthy controls. Metoprolol in acute ischemic stroke helps in upregulating SIRT1 and CAT and downregulating TNFα and IL1β; however, the overall p-value for treatment-by-time interaction was insignificant. The patients in the metoprolol group had a better outcome at 3-months. A large study is needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Impact of pfhrp2/pfhrp3 Gene Deletions on the Diagnostic Performance of HRP2-Based Rapid Diagnostic Tests for Plasmodium falciparum in sub-Saharan Africa: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Histidine-rich protein 2 (HRP2)-based rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) are widely used for the diagnosis of Plasmodium falciparum malaria in sub-Saharan Africa. However, deletions of the pfhrp2 and pfhrp3 genes threaten the accuracy of these tests by causing false-negative results. This study systematically reviewed and synthesized available evidence on the prevalence of pfhrp2, pfhrp3, and dual pfhrp2/pfhrp3 gene deletions and their implications for HRP2-based RDT performance in sub-Saharan Africa. A systematic review and meta-analysis were registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261443503) and were conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Four electronic databases were searched for studies published between January 2015 and June 2026. Random-effects meta-analysis was used to estimate pooled prevalence, while heterogeneity was assessed using Cochran's Q, τ², and I² statistics. Twenty-seven studies met the inclusion criteria. The pooled prevalence of pfhrp2, pfhrp3, and dual pfhrp2/pfhrp3 gene deletions was 3.64% (95% CI: 1.86%-7.01%), 1.63% (95% CI: 0.54%-4.79%), and 1.94% (95% CI: 0.90%-4.14%), respectively. High between-study heterogeneity was observed across all analyses (I² > 91%), reflecting considerable geographical and methodological variability. Diagnostic accuracy analysis demonstrated that HRP2-based RDTs maintained high overall sensitivity and specificity but exhibited reduced sensitivity in settings where pfhrp2 and/or pfhrp3 deletions were prevalent, resulting in false-negative diagnoses and compromised detection of P. falciparum infections. While most studies reported low deletion frequencies, localized hotspots with substantially higher prevalence highlighted areas at greater risk of diagnostic failure. pfhrp2, pfhrp3, and dual gene deletions remain relatively uncommon across sub-Saharan Africa but exhibit marked geographical variation. Their presence can reduce the diagnostic performance of HRP2-based RDTs, underscoring the need for continuous molecular surveillance, routine monitoring of RDT performance, and the adoption of complementary diagnostic strategies in areas with increasing deletion prevalence.

articles.title: MiR-223 and miR-323 as biomarkers of inflammatory and neuropsychiatric alterations in long COVID with chronic viral hepatitis.
articles.abstract: Long COVID involves persistent physical, mental, and functional symptoms following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Its biological mechanisms remain poorly understood, particularly with chronic viral hepatitis. This study investigated associations between microRNA (miRNA) expression and mental and physical health outcomes in individuals with Long COVID, considering chronic hepatitis B or C. This cross-sectional study included 80 individuals divided into four groups (n = 20 each): Long COVID, chronic viral hepatitis, Long COVID with hepatitis, and controls. Depression, anxiety, quality of life, fatigue, and functional status were assessed using validated scales, including the Post-COVID Functional Status Scale. Expression of miR-122, miR-143, miR-223, and miR-323 was quantified by RT-qPCR. Associations were evaluated using non-parametric tests and correlation analyses. MiR-143, miR-223, and miR-323 were significantly upregulated in individuals with Long COVID and hepatitis. MiRNA expression was associated with mental and physical health outcomes, particularly through a positive correlation between miR-323 expression and anxiety levels in individuals with Long COVID and hepatitis. MiR-223 was the only miRNA significantly overexpressed in this group compared with all other groups, suggesting its potential as a biomarker of coexisting conditions. Depression and anxiety affected up to 75% and 50% of individuals in the Long COVID groups, respectively (p < 0.05).These findings suggest that circulating miRNAs, particularly miR-223, miR-143, and miR-323, are associated with Long COVID in the presence of chronic viral hepatitis and may serve as biomarkers of disease burden and clinical heterogeneity.

articles.title: Encapsulation of oligogalacturonides in chitosan-based nanocarriers enhances elicitor-induced plant immunity and disease resistance.
articles.abstract: Plant defense elicitors offer an environmentally friendly alternative to conventional crop protection strategies. Oligogalacturonides are pectin-derived damage-associated molecular patterns that activate plant defense responses and represent promising tools for sustainable crop protection. Despite their potential for crop protection, the practical use of oligogalacturonides remains limited by poor stability, low persistence, and suboptimal delivery to plant tissues. In this study, biodegradable chitosan-based nanoparticles were developed as carriers for the oligogalacturonides delivery. Optimization of the chitosan:oligogalacturonide ratio yielded a nanoparticle formulation combining high oligogalacturonide encapsulation efficiency with favourable physicochemical properties. In vitro assay revealed pH-dependent oligogalacturonide recovery, with greater recovery under mildly acidic conditions and a time-dependent enrichment of biologically relevant intermediate-chain oligomers. Biological assays in Arabidopsis thaliana demonstrated that oligogalacturonides encapsulation enhanced multiple defense responses, including defense-related gene expression, callose accumulation, and hydrogen peroxide production. Furthermore, chitosan-based oligogalacturonide nanoparticles pretreatment strengthened defense responses following Botrytis cinerea infection and significantly reduced disease symptoms. These findings highlight the potential of chitosan-based nanocarriers to enhance oligogalacturonides elicitor efficacy and improve protection against fungal pathogens, supporting their application in sustainable plant protection.

articles.title: Genomic insights into the diversification of the planthopper genus Megamelus in southern South America.
articles.abstract: Understanding the processes that shape diversification remains a central challenge in evolutionary biology. The planthopper genus Megamelus (Delphacidae) provides an attractive system for studying these processes because its species are associated with diverse aquatic and riparian host plants and are of applied importance in the biological control of invasive aquatic weeds. However, phylogenetic relationships within the genus remain poorly resolved. Here, we used genome-wide single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) data generated using nextRAD, a reduced-representation sequencing approach, to reconstruct species relationships and test for introgression among eight of the nine currently described South American Megamelus species sampled across the Río de la Plata basin, together with two additional North American species. Phylogenomic analyses consistently recovered all species as well-supported monophyletic lineages, although relationships among several species differed across analytical approaches, indicating localized phylogenetic discordance. Phylogenetic network inference and D-statistics detected signatures of historical introgression involving multiple lineages, including gene flow between M. scutellaris and the ancestor of M. electrae and M. iphigeniae. These results suggest that both incomplete lineage sorting (ILS) and historical introgression have contributed to the evolutionary history of Megamelus. Ancestral state reconstruction identified Pontederiaceae as the most likely ancestral host family, whereas associations with other host families appear to have evolved independently in different species. The lack of correspondence between phylogenetic relationships and present-day geographic distributions further suggests historical dispersal took place between North and South America. Together, our results provide the first genome-wide phylogenetic framework for Megamelus and establish a foundation for future studies of host specialization, diversification, and the evolution of biological control agents.

articles.title: Alcoholic cardiomyopathy: Metabolic stress, inflammation, epigenetic reprogramming, and therapeutic strategies.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
articles.abstract: Alcoholic cardiomyopathy (ACM) is a major form of non-ischaemic dilated cardiomyopathy characterized by ventricular dilation and impaired systolic function following chronic alcohol exposure. Despite partial reversibility with prolonged abstinence, ACM remains an important cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, while the molecular mechanisms driving disease initiation and progression are incompletely understood. Emerging evidence indicates that ACM is not solely a consequence of direct ethanol toxicity, but rather a complex disorder involving interconnected metabolic, inflammatory, immune, and epigenetic pathways. In this review, we summarize current advances in the pathophysiology of ACM and propose an integrated immunometabolic framework underlying disease progression. Chronic alcohol exposure induces oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, calcium mishandling, and endoplasmic reticulum stress, leading to cardiomyocyte injury and impaired cellular energetics. These disturbances activate pro-inflammatory signaling pathways, including NF-κB and the NLRP3 inflammasome, promoting cytokine production and inflammatory forms of programmed cell death such as pyroptosis. Concurrently, accumulating evidence implicates immune dysregulation as a central contributor to adverse remodeling, characterized by altered T-cell polarization, macrophage phenotypic switching, and dysregulated immune checkpoint signaling that sustain chronic inflammation and fibrosis. In parallel, alcohol-induced epigenetic and post-transcriptional mechanisms, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, and microRNA-mediated regulation, establish persistent transcriptional reprogramming that links transient metabolic stress to long-term alterations in cardiomyocyte function and myocardial structure. Collectively, these pathways form a self-reinforcing network of metabolic injury, immune activation, and maladaptive remodeling that drives ACM progression. A more integrated understanding of these mechanisms identifies oxidative stress, inflammasome activation, immune imbalance, and epigenetic reprogramming as interconnected and potentially targetable processes. Therapeutic strategies combining alcohol abstinence with mechanism-based interventions targeting these pathways may provide new opportunities for precision treatment of ACM.

articles.title: Sonostandard: Sonication for implant-associated infections: A Swiss consensus protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sonication of explanted implants has improved microbiological detection in implant-associated infections. However, large inter-laboratory variability in sonication protocols limits comparability and clinical interpretability. A national consensus-driven initiative was launched to standardize the diagnostic sonication process, using current Swiss practice and the published evidence as a foundation.

METHODS: An evidence-informed structured consensus process was conducted, including a national protocol survey and a scoping review of published sonication workflows. An online consensus meeting followed, with structured item-by-item discussion and a single round of anonymous voting per item (consensus: ≥80% agreement among valid votes).

RESULTS: Twenty-one laboratories participated; four without sonication and one duplicate response was identified. Consensus was reached in 8 of 9 domains: sonication frequency (40 kHz, 100%), intensity (100% device output, 100%), temperature (room temperature, 100%), duration (1 min, 90.5%), fluid (Ringer's solution, 95.5%), pre- and post-sonication vortexing (30 s each, 94.4%), processing within 6 h (87.5%), culture media panel (aerobic blood agar 93.8%, chocolate agar +5% CO₂ 100%, thioglycolate broth 100%, anaerobic Schaedler agar 93.3%), incubation (14 days, 84.6%), and quantitative reporting (CFU/mL, 100%). Neither volume standardization proposal reached consensus: weight-based volume achieved 33.3% and minimum volume rule 43.8%, reflecting ongoing feasibility and implementation concerns.

CONCLUSION: A national consensus protocol was developed to harmonize sonication-based implant microbiology processing across key technical, handling, culture, incubation, and reporting domains, while volume standardization remained open due to operational constraints. This framework is intended to facilitate inter-laboratory comparability, with future work focused on implementation evaluation and evidence-based interpretive thresholds.

articles.title: Moderate-intensity statin and ezetimibe combination therapy versus high-intensity statin on coronary atherosclerotic plaque.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effect of moderate-intensity statin and ezetimibe is known to be non-inferior to high-intensity statin in prevention of adverse clinical events in patients with coronary atherosclerotic disease. However, data regarding regression of coronary atherosclerotic plaque remains limited.

METHODS: In this randomized, non-inferiority trial, patients with intermediate coronary artery stenosis were randomly assigned 1:1 to either moderate-intensity rosuvastatin (10 mg) with ezetimibe or high-intensity rosuvastatin (20 mg) group. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) was performed at baseline and after 12 months or longer to quantify the coronary plaque response. Primary end point was absolute changes in percent atheroma volume (PAV) between baseline and follow-up IVUS, and non-inferiority margin was as 2.5%. Secondary end point was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), which was a composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, and unplanned repeat revascularization.

RESULTS: A total of 280 patients underwent randomization. Follow-up IVUS showed absolute changes in PAV were - 1.286 ± 3.704% and - 1.302 ± 3.586%, respectively for moderate-intensity rosuvastatin and ezetimibe group and high-intensity rosuvastatin group. Mean difference between 2 groups (0.017%; 95% confidence interval: -0.957% to 0.991%) did not exceed noninferiority margin (non-inferiority p < 0.001). Both groups showed acceptable side effect profiles without group differences.

CONCLUSION: Compared with high-intensity rosuvastatin monotherapy, moderate-intensity rosuvastatin and ezetimibe was non-inferior regarding regression of coronary atherosclerotic plaque (Supported by Hanmi Pharmaceutical co., ltd; ROSUZET-IVUS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03169985).

articles.title: Development of a risk prediction model for acute urinary retention after interventional procedures incorporating perioperative nursing-related factors.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: We aimed to develop and internally evaluate a risk prediction model for postoperative acute urinary retention (AUR) that incorporates perioperative nursing-related factors, and to assess its potential clinical utility.

METHODS: This study adopted a retrospective design and enrolled patients receiving relevant interventional procedures, with the presence of postoperative AUR as the outcome. Baseline characteristics, surgery-related factors and perioperative nursing-related variables [preoperative Self-rating Anxiety Scale (SAS) score, privacy protection level, and postoperative pain numerical rating scale (NRS) score] were acquired. Variable screening was completed through Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO)-logistic regression. A multivariate Logistic regression model was constructed and compared with random forest and XGBoost models using five-fold stratified cross-validation. Model performance was evaluated through discrimination and calibration analyses, while decision curve analysis (DCA) was used to assess potential clinical utility.

RESULTS: A total of 320 patients were included, of whom 48 (15.0%) developed AUR. The final Logistic regression model included age, history of benign prostatic hyperplasia, preoperative SAS score, privacy protection level, and postoperative pain NRS score. The model achieved an out-of-fold AUC of 0.954 (95% CI: 0.928-0.976), compared with 0.936 for the random forest model and 0.924 for the XGBoost model. Decision curve analysis showed that the Logistic regression model provided the highest net benefit across the evaluated threshold probability range of 0.05 to 0.30.

CONCLUSION: The prediction model incorporating perioperative nursing-related factors demonstrated good discrimination in internal cross-validation and potential value for postoperative AUR risk stratification. These findings may support postoperative voiding assessment and individualized perioperative nursing management.

articles.title: 3β-trans-CLD alleviates metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) via modulating the IDO1/Nrf2/SREBP1/SCD1 axis in vitro.
articles.abstract: Approved pharmacotherapies for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remain limited, and targeted therapies with high efficacy and favorable safety profiles are urgently needed. Leptopus lolonum is rich in triterpenoids and has hepatoprotective activity; however, its systematic studies are lacking. The aim of this study was to systematically evaluate the therapeutic potential and underlying mechanisms of triterpenoids, especially compound 3β-trans-CLD, in MASLD. To evaluate the efficacy of 3β-trans-CLD, free fatty acid (FFA)-induced HepG2 and L02 hepatocyte models were established. Lipid accumulation, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses were assessed, and transcriptomic profiling was conducted. Rescue experiments were performed using IDO1 and Nrf2 inhibitors to dissect the underlying mechanism. Treatment with 3β-trans-CLD restored mitochondrial membrane potential (JC-1 staining), diminished superoxide anion levels (DHE staining), and attenuated lipid accumulation, as reflected by decreased Oil Red O staining and lower TG and TC contents. Correspondingly, 3β-trans-CLD downregulated key lipogenic regulators FXR, SREBP1, and FASN and concurrently activated the Nrf2-Keap1-HO-1 antioxidant axis. Furthermore, 3β-trans-CLD significantly suppressed the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α and IL-1β) and inhibited NF-κB and IκBα phosphorylation in FFA-induced HepG2 and L02 cells. Transcriptomic profiling identified a marked reduction in IDO1, PCSK9, and SCD expression, all of which displayed strong negative correlations with hepatocellular TG and TC levels. Mechanistically, these results demonstrated that 3β-trans-CLD counteracted MASLD-driven pathological alterations through coordinated regulation of the IDO1/Nrf2/SREBP1/SCD1 signaling cascade. These findings suggest that 3β-trans-CLD counteracts MASLD-driven pathological changes by coordinately regulating the IDO1/Nrf2/SREBP1/SCD1 signaling cascade in vitro.

articles.title: Natural compounds targeting noncanonical Inflammasomes: Molecular mechanisms and pharmacological potential.
articles.abstract: The noncanonical inflammasomes, mediated by murine caspase-11 and its human orthologues caspase-4 and caspase-5, are central components of innate immunity that detect cytosolic lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and initiate gasdermin D (GSDMD)-dependent pyroptosis and inflammatory responses. Although indispensable for host defense against Gram-negative bacterial infection, dysregulated activation of this pathway contributes to the pathogenesis of a broad spectrum of inflammatory diseases, highlighting the noncanonical inflammasomes as attractive therapeutic targets. Increasing evidence indicates that natural compounds modulate noncanonical inflammasome signaling; however, their mechanisms of action and translational potential have not been comprehensively evaluated. Here, we provide a comprehensive overview of the molecular mechanisms governing noncanonical inflammasome activation and of natural compounds, including phenolic compounds, terpenoids, alkaloids, and polysaccharides, that target this pathway. These compounds suppress noncanonical inflammasome signaling through diverse yet convergent mechanisms, including inhibition of cytosolic LPS sensing, modulation of upstream regulatory pathways, suppression of caspase-4/11 noncanonical inflammasome activation, attenuation of GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis, and regulation of oxidative stress and cellular homeostasis. These mechanisms confer protection against diverse experimental inflammatory diseases, supporting the therapeutic potential of natural compounds for the prevention and treatment of noncanonical inflammasome-driven human disorders. We further discuss current challenges, including limited validation in human caspase-4/5 systems, unresolved molecular targets, and translational barriers, and highlight future research directions to facilitate the development of mechanism-based therapeutics targeting the noncanonical inflammasomes.

articles.title: Senescence induces clonal failure of hepatocyte plasticity and reshapes regenerative lineages.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Telomere dysregulation is a central driver of cellular senescence and chronic liver disease. Yet how physiological telomeric attrition, rather than uniform telomere loss, leads to hepatic functional decline remains unclear. We therefore investigate how resolvable telomere dysfunction reshapes liver regeneration.

METHODS: An adeno-associated virus (AAV)-CRISPR-based strategy was developed to induce resolvable telomeric breaks in mouse hepatocytes while preserving endogenous telomere maintenance. Clonal dynamics, lineage tracing, and single-nucleus transcriptomic profiling were used to characterize senescent hepatocyte behavior during chronic liver injury. Human cirrhotic liver samples were analyzed to assess the relationship between hepatocyte telomere length and intermediate cellular states. An in vivo CRISPR screen identified regulators of hepatocyte plasticity under telomere stress.

RESULTS: Telomere-induced senescence did not substantially impair hepatocyte survival or basal metabolic function, but induced a clonal imbalance shaped by telomerase expression. Lineage tracing and single-nucleus transcriptomics demonstrated that senescent hepatocytes exhibited impaired hepatocyte-to-ductal metaplasia during chronic injury, with limited entry into the dedifferentiated state and failure to fully activate the ductal program. This incomplete transition disrupted epithelial composition and exacerbated the ductular reaction. Analyses of human cirrhotic livers revealed an association between preserved telomere integrity and bipotent hepatocyte states. Furthermore, the in vivo CRISPR screen identified regulators of hepatocyte dedifferentiation under telomere stress.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify senescence as a barrier to hepatobiliary clonal balance rather than a direct trigger of hepatocyte loss. Telomere dysfunction thereby promotes pathological epithelial remodeling during chronic liver injury.

IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Telomere shortening is a common feature of chronic liver disease, but how it functionally contributes to regenerative failure remains incompletely understood. Our study shows that telomere dysfunction does not simply compromise hepatocyte survival or basal metabolic capacity. Instead, senescence acts as a clonal and lineage-selective constraint that limits hepatocyte plasticity and alters which cells contribute to regeneration. These findings provide a mechanistic link between telomere attrition, loss of regenerative diversity, and progressive liver dysfunction, and suggest that preservation of hepatocyte plasticity may be an important determinant of regenerative capacity in chronic liver disease.

articles.title: Intermolecular disulfide bond formation promotes Hsp42 higher-order assembly and shapes client selection in yeast.
articles.abstract: Cellular redox homeostasis plays a critical role in regulating protein function, including chaperone activity, through reversible oxidation of cysteine and methionine residues. Previously, we found that budding yeast cells experiencing redox imbalance due to inactivated thioredoxin reductase (trr1Δ) activate the heat shock response and induce hyperaccumulation of the small heat shock protein/sequestrase Hsp42 with misfolded proteins. Building on that finding, this study identified cysteine 127 (C127) within Hsp42 as a redox-active residue that becomes oxidized in trr1Δ cells, upon treatment with the powerful oxidant hydrogen peroxide, or by exposure to the cysteine crosslinker divinyl sulfone (DVSF). In trr1Δ cells, C127 oxidation promoted intermolecular disulfide bond formation and contributed to Hsp42 homo-oligomerization. We show that stable oligomerization requires both the prion-like domain (PrLD) and C127 oxidation. While Hsp42-GFP formed prominent persistent foci in trr1Δ cells, replacement of C127 with non-thiol reactive serine decreased foci formation. Furthermore, the C127S mutation diminished Hsp42 oligomerization and sedimentability. Immunoprecipitation coupled with mass spectrometry analysis revealed that Hsp42 in trr1Δ cells preferentially associated with mitochondrial precursor proteins accumulated in the cytoplasm, as well as oxidation-reduction enzymes. The observed client selectivity was altered by the C127S mutation that diversified the spectrum of Hsp42-associated proteins. Collectively, these findings identify Cys127 as a redox-active switch that regulates Hsp42 assembly, foci formation, stability, and client specificity in response to oxidative stress.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence for sepsis prediction: A review of real-world clinical implementation.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) tools have the potential to significantly improve sepsis care by analysing numerous variables in a timely and cost-effective manner. With appropriate training and fine-tuning, AI systems can support dynamic sepsis risk prediction and may facilitate more individualised clinical assessment and management. However, their generalisability across settings and effectiveness in improving patient outcomes remain to be determined.

OBJECTIVES: This narrative review draws on contemporary literature to describe the clinical implementation of AI sepsis prediction tools, their impact on patient outcomes and sepsis process measures, and the key socio-technical barriers and solutions for translating these tools into clinically reliable and scalable systems to improve sepsis care.

SOURCES: PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus and IEEE were searched for studies on the clinical implementation of AI sepsis prediction tools. We included studies published 2019-2026 that describe or evaluate model impact on patient outcomes or process measures.

CONTENT: Implementation studies show mixed results at improving patient outcomes such as mortality and length of stay, but adoption of AI tools has shown improvements in process measures such as time to antibiotic administration. In addition to the indeterminate clinical impact, the generalisability and scalability of AI sepsis tools have been limited due to several other factors, including heterogeneity of data, alert fatigue, insufficient clinician trust, ethical concerns, algorithmic bias, and uncertainty for clinicians around how to interpret and respond to model generated predictions. We also report a minimum outcome set that future implementation studies should pre-specify and report on.

IMPLICATIONS: Successful integration into clinical practice requires a comprehensive implementation strategy that shifts the research and design focus from improving model accuracy to one that prioritizes real-world evaluation, human-centred design and addresses workflow, training and equity concerns.

articles.title: One patient, two glucose profiles: arm-dependent continuous glucose monitoring discordance in hemiplegia.
Patient Focus: Real Talk: An explanation of "Qualitative Analysis of Patient-Physician discussions about the Benefits and Tradeoffs of Heart Failure Medications".
Clinical effects of istaroxime in acute heart failure and cardiogenic shock: A patient-level pooled analysis of four phase II randomized clinical trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Istaroxime is an inotropic and lusitropic agent tested in acute heart failure (AHF) or AHF-related cardiogenic shock (AHF-CS). We aimed to assess its efficacy and concy in a pooled analysis of all randomized trials performed to date.

METHODS: Patient-level data from four phase II randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials were pooled. The effects of istaroxime 0.5-1.0 µg/kg/min for up to 48 hours vs. placebo on hemodynamics, cardiac function, and clinical outcomes were assessed.

RESULTS: A total of 284 patients were included (n=200 AHF, n=84 AHF-CS). Compared with placebo, istaroxime increased systolic blood pressure through 6 hours (least square [LS] mean difference in the area under the change from baseline curve 28.9 mmHg*h, 95% CI 18.1 to 39.8 mmHg*h) and through 24 hours (LS mean difference 121.4 mmHg*h, 95% CI 63.9 to 179.0 mmHg*h). Reductions in heart rate, body weight, pulmonary capillary wedge pressure and echocardiographic E/e' ratio, and an increase in echocardiographic stroke work index and stroke volume were observed with istaroxime, with a numerically greater improvement in invasive cardiac output and creatinine. Numerically, dyspnea and quality of life were improved, and length of index hospitalization, worsening HF and death were lower with istaroxime. Serious adverse events were similar between the istaroxime and placebo arms.

CONCLUSIONS: In this patient-level pooled analysis, istaroxime 0.5-1.0 µg/kg/min was associated with improvement in SBP and hemodynamic and echocardiographic measurements of cardiac performance, without tachycardia or serious safety concerns. These findings support a phase III program to investigate the impact of istaroxime administration on outcomes.

articles.title: Prenatal per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances exposure and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: fetal sex-specific associations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental chemicals associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, however their role in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to characterize the fetal sex-specific PFAS mixture associations with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.

METHODS: Using data from 217 pregnant individuals from a prospective cohort study, we examined associations between maternal serum concentrations of 12 PFAS and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (gestational hypertension and preeclampsia) using weighted quantile sum regression stratified by fetal sex.

RESULTS: The PFAS mixture, which included 8 of the 12 assessed PFAS that met detection criteria, was not associated with odds of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (OR [95% CI]: 1.06 [0.73,1.53]) in the overall analysis sample. However, in pregnant persons carrying a male fetus, the PFAS mixture was marginally associated with higher odds of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (OR [95% CI]: 1.55 [0.88, 2.73]). In contrast, pregnant individuals carrying a female fetus exhibited negative associations between PFAS mixture and the odds of HDP (OR [95% CI]: 0.34 [0.16, 0.74]). Additionally, individual PFAS congeners contributed differently to each mixture model, with the highest contributions from PFNA and PFOS to the male mixture model whereas PFHxS and MeFOSAA contributed the highest weights to the female mixture model.

CONCLUSION: We found that PFAS associations with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy may differ by fetal sex, which may be an important source of heterogeneity in studies of environmental exposures and adverse pregnancy outcomes.

articles.title: Hospitalizations due to infections in children after high prenatal exposure to perfluoroalkyl substances from contaminated drinking water in Ronneby, Sweden.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prenatal exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) may affect immune development, but evidence on childhood infections requiring hospitalization after high exposure is limited. We examined whether prenatal PFAS exposure from contaminated drinking water was associated with infection-related hospitalizations up to age seven.

METHODS: We conducted a population-based birth cohort study of children born in Blekinge County, Sweden, between 2000 and 2013. Children were followed through national registers from birth until their seventh birthday, death, or emigration. Maternal residential history was linked to water distribution records to classify prenatal PFAS exposure from drinking water. Infection-related hospitalizations were identified using ICD-10 discharge diagnostic codes from the Swedish National Patient Register. We estimated associations using Cox regression with the Andersen-Gill extension for recurrent events.

RESULTS: The study included 21,409 children, of whom 20,137 had complete covariate data. A total of 3,264 infection-related hospitalization events occurred during follow-up. Compared with background exposure, very high prenatal PFAS exposure was associated with an increased rate of hospitalization for upper respiratory tract infections (adjusted hazard ratio 1.80; 95% confidence interval 1.03-3.15). Elevated estimates were also observed for ear, nose, and throat infections, other viral infections, and urinary tract infections, but confidence intervals included the null.

CONCLUSIONS: Very high prenatal PFAS exposure was associated with increased hospitalization for upper respiratory tract infections in childhood, although potential effects of prenatal exposure could not be fully separated from correlated postnatal exposures. These results add to previous evidence from primary care in the Ronneby population and suggest that high early-life PFAS exposure may affect immune function.

articles.title: A930024E05Rik is a hypoxia-upregulated lncRNA that facilitates atrial fibrosis by sponging let-7 miRNAs to modulate collagen expression in cardiomyocytes.
articles.abstract: Hypoxia-induced atrial fibrosis plays a central role in the development and progression of atrial fibrillation (AF), yet the involvement of long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) in this process is not fully defined. This study aimed to identify hypoxia-responsive lncRNAs and investigate their functional roles in hypoxia-mediated fibrotic remodeling. Transcriptomic profiling of HL-1 atrial cardiomyocytes under hypoxic conditions, followed by bioinformatic prediction and molecular validation, including luciferase reporter assays, RNA pull-down, RNA immunoprecipitation, and gain- and loss-of-function analyses, were performed to delineate the downstream effects. Among lncRNA candidates, A930024E05Rik was markedly upregulated by hypoxia and inversely associated with let-7 miRNA expression. Further analyses demonstrated that A930024E05Rik physically interacts with let-7a and let-7e, is enriched in let-7-dependent gene-silencing machinery, and modulates the expression of collagen genes, COL1A1 and COL3A1. Functional assessments demonstrated that A930024E05Rik enhances collagen production by alleviating let-7-mediated repression, as evidenced by reciprocal effects of gene silencing and overexpression. In conclusion, these findings support a competing endogenous RNA mechanism in which A930024E05Rik modulates let-7 miRNA availability to control collagen expression in hypoxic cardiomyocytes, highlighting potential avenues for the application of this A930024E05Rik-let-7 regulatory axis on AF management.

articles.title: Hepatic Erbin loss promotes CCl4-induced liver fibrosis by potentiating the TGF-β/Smad signaling in hepatocytes.
articles.abstract: Hepatocytes comprise the bulk of the organ parenchyma and are vulnerable to various kinds of insults. As a consequence, the injured hepatocytes trigger the progression of liver fibrosis by releasing the profibrotic factors. However, the exact mechanisms involved in the fate regulation of hepatocytes during liver fibrogenesis remain far from clear. Erbin is a cytoplasmic protein that is widely expressed in the epithelial cells at a wide range of tissues. In the present study, we found that Erbin was markedly decreased in hepatocytes in the murine models of CCl4-induced liver fibrosis, as well as in the biopsies of liver cirrhosis patients. Ectopic expression of Erbin protected the mice from CCl4-induced hepatocellular injury and liver fibrosis, whereas knockdown of Erbin aggravated the severity of CCl4-induced liver injury and fibrosis in mice. The mechanistic study showed that overexpression of Erbin suppressed the potential of TGF-β/Smad signaling in hepatocytes by hindering the nuclear translocation of pSmad2. In contrast, inhibiting Erbin potentiated TGF-β/Smad signal transduction. Finally, the pathological significance of Erbin in liver fibrosis was associated with its protective effects against the concomitant apoptosis of hepatocytes in the progression of liver fibrosis. In summary, our observations identify an important regulatory mechanism of TGF-β/Smad signaling in hepatocytes during the progression of liver fibrosis, and, thus, suggest a potential strategy for therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: Postoperative Antibiotic Prophylaxis After Primary Total Joint Arthroplasty: Current Evidence and Future Directions.
articles.abstract: Systemic antibiotic prophylaxis is an important aspect of surgical site and periprosthetic infection prevention in primary total hip and knee arthroplasty. However, the optimal protocol for antibiotic prophylaxis remains controversial. While some guidelines recommend one preoperative dose of antibiotic only, others continue to support up to 24 hours of coverage, and the role of extended oral antibiotic prophylaxis (EOAP) in high-risk patients remains uncertain. Although several guidelines are available, current practice remains heterogeneous, reflecting both variability among recommendations and the lack of a validated decision-making framework to identify patients at risk and the role that extended postoperative antibiotics could possibly play in prevention of infection in this cohort. There remains a substantial need for prospective multicenter studies to establish reproducible risk-stratification models and support a more standardized approach across orthopaedic societies. This narrative review summarizes the current guidelines and available evidence regarding postoperative antibiotic prophylaxis after primary total joint arthroplasty (TJA).

articles.title: Antibacterial, antibiofilm, mucus penetration properties and pulmonary biocompatibility of inhalable spray-dried levofloxacin-ambroxol composite microparticles.
articles.journal: European journal of pharmaceutics and biopharmaceutics : official journal of Arbeitsgemeinschaft fur Pharmazeutische Verfahrenstechnik e.V
articles.abstract: This study evaluated the antibacterial and biofilm-disruption activities of spray-dried levofloxacin (LVX) and ambroxol (AMB) composite dry powder inhaler (DPI) formulations against laboratory and clinical strains of P. aeruginosa and a clinical S. aureus strain. Cytotoxicity and pro-inflammatory activity of the formulations were investigated in THP-1 derived macrophages, healthy and COPD bronchial epithelial cells (HBE), and mucus penetration using an artificial mucus model. Spray dried LVX retained antibacterial activity against PA14 (MIC50 0.075-0.099 µg/mL versus 0.076 µg/mL for free LVX), whereas free AMB showed no antibacterial activity. Formulations containing higher AMB proportions, exhibited greater antibacterial activity than free LVX against AUST-02 and 2.1. The developed formulations also enhanced biofilm disruption against PA14 and AUST-02. AMB improved penetration of spray-dried LVX, particularly with F4 (LVX:AMB 1:1 with 5 % leucine) showing statistically significant (p < 0.05) penetration enhancement compared to free LVX (60.8 % and 82.8 % in 2 h) at 16 µg/mL. All formulations maintained high cell viability (>83 %) in THP-1 macrophages, while no significant cytotoxicity or increase in IL-8 production was observed. Overall, the prepared composite antibiotic microparticles demonstrated superior antibacterial activity against the tested clinical strains, enhanced biofilm disruption and LVX mucus penetration, while preserving pulmonary biocompatibility in the tested cell models.

articles.title: RSP1141, a reversible non-covalent BTK inhibitor, suppresses GPVI-mediated platelet activation.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The glycoprotein VI (GPVI)-Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) axis drives collagen-induced platelet activation and arterial thrombosis. Approved BTK inhibitors act irreversibly on Cys481, raising concerns over off-target kinase inhibition, C481S resistance, and bleeding. We aimed to identify a non-covalent, reversible BTK inhibitor with antiplatelet activity and to define quantitatively its selectivity within the platelet GPVI cascade.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Fifty-five imidazo[4,5-b]pyridine derivatives were screened using a BTK enzymatic assay and CRP-XL-induced aggregation of washed human platelets. The lead compound, RSP1141, was characterized by concentration-response immunoblotting of GPVI signaling nodes, Ca2+ mobilization, functional assays, drug washout, 370-kinase profiling, C481S enzymatic assay, molecular docking, and a murine FeCl₃-induced arterial thrombosis and tail-bleeding model.

KEY FINDINGS: RSP1141 inhibited BTK (IC₅₀ 27.9 nM) and CRP-XL-induced aggregation (IC₅₀ 173.6 nM). In intact platelets, RSP1141 inhibited BTK-pY223 (IC₅₀ 0.316 μM) and PLCγ2-pY753 (0.325 μM) at essentially identical concentrations, whereas SYK-pY525/526 (2.88 μM) and Src-family kinase-pY416 (3.96 μM) required 9.1- and 12.5-fold higher concentrations. Downstream PKC, Ca2+, granule secretion, integrin, and spreading responses were suppressed. RSP1141 retained activity against C481S BTK (IC₅₀ 141 nM), docking predicted no covalent Cys481 engagement, and platelet aggregation and BTK-PLCγ2 signaling recovered after washout. In mice, oral RSP1141 delayed FeCl₃-induced carotid occlusion at 10 mg/kg, whereas tail bleeding time was not detectably prolonged.

SIGNIFICANCE: RSP1141 engages the BTK-PLCγ2 node with approximately 10-fold cellular selectivity over proximal GPVI kinases, inhibits reversibly, and is antithrombotic in vivo without detectable bleeding prolongation, providing a mechanistically differentiated antiplatelet lead.

articles.title: Electroencephalography neurophysiology alterations in association with Aβ and tau pathology across the symptomatic stages of Alzheimer's disease continuum: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Amyloid-β (Aβ) and tau deposition drive Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, how these proteinopathies are linked to macroscopic neural activity alterations measured by electroencephalography (EEG) in symptomatic AD remains inadequately characterized. This study aims to investigate the associations between Aβ, tau, EEG neurophysiology, and cognition.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study of 73 MCI and AD participants, who underwent resting-state EEG, Aβ-PET, and tau-PET. EEG source analysis was performed to extract regional spectral power. Linear mixed-effects models were used to examine the associations of regional Aβ (quantified by SUVR), tau (binary classification), with EEG features, controlling for age, sex and education. Ordinary least squares (OLS) regression was applied to investigate the relationships of EEG spectral power and global Aβ burden with cognitive performance.

RESULTS: Elevated Aβ burden was associated with distinct regional spectral alterations. Specifically, higher Aβ SUVR was significantly correlated with increased theta power and decreased beta power in a subset of cortical regions. Tau positivity did not modulate the amyloid-theta association in any region, but attenuated the amyloid-beta association in a small set of parietal regions.

CONCLUSIONS: We identified a localized pattern of Aβ-related neurophysiological dysfunction across the symptomatic stages of AD continuum, characterized by theta increases and beta decreases, supporting a robust association between Aβ burden and cortical neural slowing. The findings highlight the value of source-localized EEG power as a sensitive indicator of Aβ-associated network dysfunction in AD and underscore the potential of source-localized EEG as a complementary, non-invasive biomarker for assessing pathological burden and informing diagnostic strategies in AD.

articles.title: Mechanism of Sini Decoction and its self-assembled component in improving Doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
ETHOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Sini decoction (SND) is a typical Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) prescription composed of Aconitum carmichaelii Debx, Zingiberis Rhizoma, and Glycyrrhizae Radix et Rhizoma Praeparate cum Melle, used to treat cardiomyopathy in TCM clinical trials. Recent studies have shown that the active ingredients of SND can form self-assembled complexes during decoction, whose bioactivity differs from that of the monomeric compound. However, current research on the active ingredients of SND has not yet included these self-assembled components, and the mechanism by which SND exerts its effects on doxorubicin (Dox)-induced cardiomyopathy remains unclear.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the underlying mechanisms by which SND and its self-assembled component (SAC) improve Dox-induced cardiomyopathy in mice. The complete isolation of the self-assembled complex component from SND was achieved for the first time, and its activity and mechanism were explored, providing a new perspective for revealing the substance basis of TCM prescriptions.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: SAC and the unassembled component (SMC) were separated from SND by ultrafiltration, and UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS was used to qualitatively analyze their chemical components. Based on the main components of SAC, Benzoylmesaconine-glycyrrhizic acid complex (GBMA) was prepared under simulated decoction conditions of SND. A mouse model of cardiomyopathy was established by intraperitoneal injection of Dox, followed by oral administration of SND, SAC, SMC, and GBMA, to evaluate improvements in cardiac systolic function across treatment groups. The effects of SND and its components on cardiac systolic function were evaluated to reveal the differences in their medicinal effects. The mechanisms by which SND and SAC improve cardiomyopathy were systematically investigated using Seahorse energy metabolism analysis, autophagic flux analysis, and Western blotting, with a focus on the interconnected organelles, mitochondria, and autophagosomes.

RESULTS: A total of 173 compounds were identified in SAC. Among them, molecules with lower hydrophilicity tend to self-assemble in the decoction, while molecules with a molecular weight less than 300 Da participate less in self-assembly. SND, SAC, and GBMA significantly improved abnormal cardiac systolic function in Dox-induced cardiomyopathy mice, while SMC had no such effects. SAC and GBMA inhibited Dox-induced excessive mitophagy by downregulating BNIP3 and MFN2 expression, thereby protecting mitochondria and cardiomyocyte nuclei. SND, SAC, and GBMA all alleviated mitochondrial functional impairment in the cardiomyopathy model. They could trigger energy metabolism reprogramming (reducing the expression of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex subunits PDC-E2 and PDC-E3, and increasing the expression of OXPHOS-CI and OXPHOS-CIV) to optimize mitochondrial energy supply efficiency. SMC could downregulate CII expression in OXPHOS and exert some mitochondrial protective effects, but failed to significantly improve mitochondrial functional impairment.

CONCLUSIONS: SND and SAC administration improve Dox-induced cardiomyopathy. They could protect mitochondria and cardiomyocyte nuclei through optimizing mitochondrial energy metabolism efficiency and inhibiting autophagy, while the specific active constituents and their absorption routes remain to be determined. This study elucidates the molecular mechanism by which the adminstration of SAC in SND improves Dox-induced cardiomyopathy, providing new scientific evidence for the combined clinical application of SND and Dox. It also offers a new approach to the research of the substance basis of TCM prescriptions, namely, focusing on the self-assembled substances present in the decoction, rather than assuming the active components are small molecules, to accurately reveal the overall effects of TCM prescriptions and the scientific connotation of their compatibility. It should be noted that the current findings are based on a single batch of SND, and further validation using multiple batches is required to confirm the consistency of the observed effects.

articles.title: Zhenwu Decoction improves myocardial energy metabolism and mitochondrial integrity in pressure overload-induced heart failure partly through AMP-activated protein kinase signaling.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Zhenwu Decoction (ZWD), recorded in the Shang Han Lun, is traditionally used for yang deficiency with fluid retention, a pattern relevant to congestion and impaired cardiac function. Its mitochondrial mechanism in pressure-overload heart failure remains unclear.

AIM OF THE STUDY: To evaluate the cardioprotective effects of ZWD and the contribution of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)-related signaling.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Male C57BL/6J mice subjected to transverse aortic constriction received low-, medium-, or high-dose ZWD (4.32, 8.64, or 17.28 g/kg/day, respectively) or the positive control captopril. Cardiac function, remodeling, oxidative stress, energy metabolites, mitochondrial ultrastructure, transcriptomics, and metabolomics were assessed. In angiotensin II-injured H9c2 cardiomyoblasts, small interfering RNA-mediated AMPK silencing was used to assess pathway dependence.

RESULTS: ZWD improved systolic function and reduced ventricular dilation, injury biomarkers, collagen accumulation, and oxidative imbalance, with the most evident effects at the high dose. It increased adenosine triphosphate and acetyl-coenzyme A, reduced adenosine diphosphate and adenosine monophosphate, and preserved mitochondrial ultrastructure. These changes were accompanied by increased AMPK phosphorylation and sirtuin 1 abundance and reduced dynamin-related protein 1 phosphorylation. Multi-omics analyses identified treatment-associated changes in energy-related pathways. AMPK silencing attenuated, but did not completely abolish, the mitochondrial and metabolic effects of ZWD.

CONCLUSIONS: ZWD ameliorated pressure-overload cardiac dysfunction and improved myocardial energy homeostasis and mitochondrial integrity. AMPK silencing partially attenuated the cellular response, supporting AMPK involvement in these protective effects, alongside increased sirtuin 1 abundance and reduced dynamin-related protein 1 phosphorylation.

articles.title: Protein language model-assisted engineering of a high-performance polyethylene terephthalate hydrolase for enhanced biorecycling.
articles.abstract: Biorecycling of post-consumer polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste represents a sustainable route toward a circular plastics economy. However, enzymatic PET depolymerization remains constrained by the accumulation of the intermediate mono(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (MHET). Here, we propose an in situ alkaline conversion strategy that couples PET depolymerization with MHET conversion to terephthalic acid (TPA). Using a protein language model (PLM)-assisted semi-rational design, we engineered IsPETase variants with enhanced activity under moderate-temperature alkaline conditions. The optimized variant, IsPETaseM8, exhibited a 914.1-fold higher activity compared with the parent enzyme at pH 10 and 50 °C. At a PET loading of 10% (w/w), IsPETaseM8 achieved near-complete PET depolymerization within 24 h at 50 °C, accompanied by continuous conversion of MHET and direct TPA production in the bioreactor. Kinetic and structural analyses revealed that the improved performance arises from enhanced stability and an expanded substrate-binding pocket. Overall, this work establishes an efficient moderate-temperature alkaline PET biorecycling strategy as a complementary alternative to conventional high-temperature enzymatic systems.

articles.title: SADS-CoV nucleocapsid protein inhibits type III interferon production through the TUFM-HDAC10-IRF3 axis to promote viral infection.
articles.abstract: Swine acute diarrhea syndrome coronavirus (SADS-CoV) is a newly identified swine coronavirus with potential cross-species transmission risk. While the ability of SADS-CoV to antagonize host innate immunity has been demonstrated, the underlying signaling pathways remain elusive. Here, we report the identification of the SADS-CoV nucleocapsid (N) protein as a suppressor of type III interferon (IFN-λ). Furthermore, we found that N interacts with TUFM (Tu translation elongation factor, mitochondrial)-which then recruits histone deacetylase 10 (HDAC10)-and HDAC10 subsequently binds to interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3). This cascade inhibits IRF3's nuclear translocation, suppressing Poly(I:C)-induced IFN-λ expression and thereby enhancing SADS-CoV replication. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of HDAC10 with Quisinostat protects piglets against SADS-CoV infection in vivo. These findings reveal how SADS-CoV suppresses innate immunity and provide a valuable clue for developing effective drugs to control SADS-CoV infection.

articles.title: Tumor-mimicking brain parenchymal granuloma with molecular detection of Mycobacterium xenopi by metagenomic sequencing and targeted PCR: a case report.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract: Central nervous system infection caused by Mycobacterium xenopi is exceptionally rare and may mimic intracranial neoplasia. A 60-year-old woman with poorly controlled diabetes presented with progressive headache and left homonymous hemianopia. Magnetic resonance imaging showed an irregularly enhancing right occipital mass-like lesion with marked edema and tumor-like magnetic resonance spectroscopy. Stereotactic biopsy demonstrated chronic granulomatous inflammation without neoplasia; periodic acid-Schiff, Gomori methenamine silver, and acid-fast stains were negative. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing of sterile, unfixed lesional brain tissue detected 2,347 species-specific reads assigned to M. xenopi, with a negative laboratory control. Targeted mycobacterial PCR performed during the diagnostic work-up on remaining biopsy-derived brain tissue was also reported positive for M. xenopi, providing concordant molecular support. Because tissue was limited, no separate specimen was submitted for culture or susceptibility testing. The patient received oral rifampicin, ethambutol, clarithromycin, and moxifloxacin. Headache resolved within 2 weeks, bedside visual-field assessment suggested partial improvement, and available records documented treatment for more than 6 months without clinically apparent adverse events. One-year non-contrast computed tomography showed right occipital encephalomalacic evolution without an obvious persistent mass-like lesion or mass effect. This case highlights the value of tissue-based molecular testing in tumor-mimicking central nervous system granulomas when conventional staining is nondiagnostic, while underscoring the continuing importance of culture, susceptibility testing, and prolonged objective follow-up.

articles.title: Evolving management of upper extremity pseudoaneurysms: Role of observation and nonsurgical management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While the natural history and treatment algorithm of femoral pseudoaneurysms has been well established, the management of Upper Extremity Pseudoaneurysm (UEPSA) is not clearly defined. We sought to evaluate our 30-year experience and management strategies of this pathology.

METHODS: We reviewed 93 patients that were identified utilizing ICD9/10 codes from an initial 384 patients with the diagnosis of aneurysm of the upper extremity from 1992 to 2023. Patients with UEPSA secondary to iatrogenic arterial interrogation were analyzed by duplex based follow-up until successful thrombosis or subsequent intervention was performed. Dialysis access pseudoaneurysms or trauma related UEPSAs were excluded for analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 93 patients were identified with a UEPSA (39 brachial, 43 radial, 6 axillary, 5 ulnar arteries); 12 additional patients were identified who had only a patent neck at the time of formal vascular laboratory imaging and were excluded from treatment strategy analysis (11 radial, 1 brachial). The mean time between iatrogenic event and vascular surgery evaluation was 22 days. Fifty-nine (63.4%) underwent surgical repair, 27 (29.0%) received conservative management, and 7 (7.5%) underwent thrombin injection. Of the 93 treatment group patients that were analyzed, separated into sizes, patients with pseudoaneurysms less than 2cm there were a total of 21/93 (22.5%) patients managed conservatively, and 16/93 (17.2%) patients managed surgically; in contrast for those with greater than 2cm UEPSAs, 6/93 (6.5%) patients were managed conservatively, 43/93 (46.2%) were managed surgically, and 7/93 (7.5%) with thrombin injection. Comparing the first 15 years of the study period there were 27 iatrogenic UEPSAs noted with only 3/27 (11.1%) managed conservatively, while after 2010 there were 66 iatrogenic pseudoaneurysms with 24/66 (36.4%) managed conservatively. Of the UEPSAs managed conservatively, only 3/24 (12.5%) failed conservative management and were recommended to pursue intervention.

CONCLUSIONS: Upper extremity pseudoaneurysms with significant symptomatic hematomas, suspected infection, and/or nerve related symptoms should undergo surgical exploration and repair. A consideration for conservative management of small pseudoaneurysms <2cm without the above presentation, observation and surveillance may be considered with more than 90% achieving successful spontaneous thrombosis.

articles.title: PREVALENCE AND CHARACTERISTICS OF CEMENTAL TEAR: A RETROSPECTIVE CROSS-SECTIONAL CONE-BEAM COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY STUDY.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The aim of this study was to determine the prevalence of cemental tear (CeT) on high-resolution cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) images and to assess its distribution according to selected demographic and clinical variables.

METHODS: This retrospective observational study included CBCT examinations acquired between 2022 and 2025. Cases were identified by searching the radiology report database for "cemental tear" and related terms and were subsequently confirmed by image reassessment. In addition, 2,500 cases initially classified as negative were reassessed to identify potentially missed cases. Age, sex, tooth group, root location, endodontic treatment, alveolar bone loss, and hypercementosis were evaluated using descriptive statistics and Fisher's exact test (p < 0.05).

RESULTS: A total of 30,865 examinations from individual patients were selected. CeT was identified in 114 patients, involving 123 teeth, with an overall prevalence of 0.37%. Most cases occurred in older patients, with a mean age of 63.2 ± 13.5 years. Maxillary central incisors were the most frequently affected teeth (46.34%), and the middle root third was the most common location (39.02%). Significant associations were found between the affected root third and the degree of alveolar bone loss and between tooth group and the affected root third (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: CeT was uncommon in the Brazilian study population and most frequently involved maxillary central incisors and the middle root third. Recognition of this pattern may raise suspicion of CeT in the presence of localized, persistent periodontal defects and support differential diagnosis and clinical management.

articles.title: Fenestrated-Branched Endovascular versus Open Surgical Repair for Elective Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study compared outcomes between patients undergoing elective open surgical repair (OSR) and fenestrated branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR) for thoraco-abdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs) through a systematic review and meta-analysis.

DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane.

REVIEW METHODS: A total of 5 980 articles were screened following the PRISMA protocol. Primary endpoints were thirty day or in hospital major adverse events (MAEs) and mortality, and late all cause mortality. Secondary endpoints were thirty day or in hospital permanent paraplegia, stroke, bowel ischaemia, and new onset dialysis, as well as late re-interventions. A DerSimonian-Laird random effects model was employed to calculate risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for binary endpoints. Significance was defined as a p value of . Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I and evidence certainty with GRADE.

RESULTS: A total of 1 567 patients from five retrospective observational comparative studies were included. FBEVAR was used to treat TAAA in 824 patients (52.6%). Thirty day MAEs (RR 0.51, 95% CI 0.34 - 0.78; p = .002; I2 = 77.0%), mortality (RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.37 - 0.97; p = .040; I2 = 29.0%), and dialysis (RR 0.18, 95% CI 0.06 - 0.54; p = .002; I2 = 80.0%) were significantly less frequent among patients undergoing FBEVAR. Conversely, late aortic related re-interventions were significantly more common in the elective FBEVAR cohort (RR 1.80, 95% CI 1.04 - 3.13; p = .040; I2 = 18.0%). No statistically significant differences were observed between groups in thirty day or in hospital permanent paraplegia (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.51 - 1.91; p = .96; I2 = 39.0%), bowel ischaemia (RR 0.46, 95% CI 0.09 - 2.33; p = .35; I2 = 81.0%), and stroke (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.37 - 2.06; p = .76; I2 = 0.0%), or late mortality (RR 1.29, 95% CI 0.87 - 1.92; p = .20; I2 = 57.0%). According to GRADE, certainty of evidence was low to very low across outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Elective FBEVAR was associated with a significantly lower incidence of thirty day MAEs, mortality, and acute kidney injury requiring dialysis compared with OSR. In contrast, elective OSR was associated with a significantly lower incidence of late aortic related re-interventions, whereas overall re-intervention rates were similar between groups.

articles.title: Neurochemical signatures of morphometric network reorganization in Duchenne muscular dystrophy: Links to cognition and behavior.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is associated with neurocognitive behavior problems and regional morphometric abnormalities, yet large-scale brain network reorganization and its molecular correlations remain unclear. Here, we explored whether remodeling of the individual-level morphological similarity network (MSN) in DMD aligns with specific neurotransmitter systems and associates with cognitive, behavioral, and motor performance.

METHODS: We studied 111 boys with DMD and 80 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (HCs). Individual MSNs were derived from T1-weighted MRI. Global and nodal graph-theoretical metrics were compared between groups, and network-based statistics (NBS) were used to identify altered subnetworks. Spatial correlations linked altered MSN maps to normative PET/SPECT neurotransmitter maps, and Spearman correlations related MSN alterations and neurochemical indices to clinical measures.

RESULTS: The global small-world organization of MSNs was preserved. However, boys with DMD showed increased degree centrality (DC) in the bilateral hippocampus and left cerebellar lobule 3, and decreased DC in the right cerebellar lobule 7b. NBS identified a cerebellar-frontotemporal-subcortical morphological circuit characterized by reduced morphological similarity. MSN alterations showed significant spatial associations with dopaminergic, serotonergic, GABAergic, glutamatergic, cholinergic, and endocannabinoid systems, and the strength of these associations and network disruption were associated with poorer cognitive, motor, and behavioral performance.

CONCLUSIONS: Children with DMD exhibit MSN remodeling centered on a cerebellar-frontotemporal-subcortical morphological circuit that is neurochemically coupled to specific neurotransmitter systems and linked to cognitive, behavioral, and motor deficits. This study elucidates potential neurochemical mechanisms underlying neurobehavioral abnormalities in DMD and may provide biological insights to inform the development of neuromodulation-based therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Timing of cervical-length screening before 24 weeks in twin pregnancy: balancing detection of a short cervix against diagnostic delay.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology

articles.title: Evolving paradigms in mechanical circulatory support and heart transplantation.
articles.abstract: Advanced heart failure management is increasingly defined by the interactions between evolving donor utilization and preservation strategies, mechanical circulatory support (MCS) technologies, and organ allocation frameworks. Heart donation after circulatory death has significantly expanded transplant availability in recent years, while advances in allograft preservation and ex vivo perfusion continue to challenge traditional constraints on ischemic time and donor selection. At the same time, modern temporary MCS platforms have demonstrated the feasibility of more prolonged support, enabling greater utilization of direct bridge-to-transplant pathways within allocation systems that prioritize temporary over durable support. Meanwhile, improvements in durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) technology have progressively shifted their utilization toward destination therapy. Amid this dynamic therapeutic landscape, we sought to review current trends in donor utilization, preservation, mechanical support, and organ allocation. In doing so, we also evaluate how their intersection is reshaping contemporary treatment algorithms, resource stewardship, and pathways toward definitive heart replacement therapy.

articles.title: Feasibility of measuring adenosine triphosphate (ATP), CD39L1, and adenosine in the airways of patients with chronic cough.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extracellular adenosine triphosphate contributes to cough hypersensitivity through purinergic signalling, but airway purinergic biomarkers have not been well characterized in chronic cough.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility of measuring sputum adenosine triphosphate, adenosine, and CD39L1 and their relationship with cough outcomes.

METHODS: In a prospective observational study, 100 adults with chronic cough were classified as chronic cough secondary to asthma or non-asthmatic eosinophilic bronchitis (n = 45) or refractory chronic cough (n = 55) and received guideline-based treatment. Induced sputum was collected before and after treatment. Biomarkers were quantified using bioluminescence and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays and compared with 24-h cough frequency, cough-specific quality of life, and cough severity.

RESULTS: Baseline biomarker concentrations were similar between groups. In refractory chronic cough, lower sputum adenosine triphosphate and higher CD39L1 were associated with worse patient-reported cough outcomes, whereas no associations were observed in chronic cough secondary to asthma or non-asthmatic eosinophilic bronchitis. Sputum adenosine triphosphate decreased following treatment in the overall cohort and in chronic cough secondary to asthma or non-asthmatic eosinophilic bronchitis, while adenosine and CD39L1 remained unchanged. Changes in biomarkers were not associated with clinical improvement.

CONCLUSION: Purinergic biomarkers can be measured in induced sputum. Lower adenosine triphosphate and higher CD39L1 were associated with worse cough outcomes in refractory chronic cough.

CLINICAL IMPLICATION: Measurement of airway purinergic biomarkers may help identify neuronal dysfunction and support the development of targeted therapies for refractory chronic cough.

CLINICALTRIALS GOV ID: NCT04758351.

CAPSULE SUMMARY: Sputum purinergic biomarkers can be measured in chronic cough and may identify neuronal dysfunction, supporting their potential as treatable traits and biomarkers for targeted therapies.

articles.title: Author Correction to "Changes in Hypertension Prevalence and Control in Canada After the COVID-19 Pandemic: Insights From the Canadian Health Measures Survey Cycle 7." Canadian Journal of Cardiology Volume 42, Issue 10, October 2026, Pages 2456-2463. DOI: 10.1016/j.cjca.2026.04.013.
Longitudinal Changes in Physical Performance with Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Coronary Artery Disease.
articles.journal: Experimental and clinical endocrinology & diabetes : official journal, German Society of Endocrinology [and] German Diabetes Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physical performance provides valuable insights into metabolic and cardiovascular health, particularly regarding metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and coronary artery disease (CAD).

OBJECTIVE: This study examined the relationship between longitudinal changes in physical performance, assessed using the Timed Up and Go (TUG) test, and indicators of MASLD, CAD, and body fat distribution over time.

METHODS: This 3-year longitudinal prospective cohort study included 1,096 older adults. Participants underwent baseline and follow-up assessments. Based on TUG results, participants were categorized into four groups: Normal→Normal (Group 1), Impaired→Normal (Group 2), Normal→Impaired (Group 3), and Impaired→Impaired (Group 4). MASLD indicators (Fibrosis-4 index [FIB-4], MASLD liver fat score, and hepatic steatosis index [HSI]), CAD indicators (coronary artery calcium [CAC] and coronary artery volume [CAV] scores), and body fat distribution (L3 cross-sectional visceral fat area [L3VFA], L3 cross-sectional subcutaneous fat area [L3SFA], and visceral-to-subcutaneous fat ratio [VSR]) were also analyzed.

RESULTS: At baseline, groups with impaired TUG exhibited worse MASLD, CAD, and fat distribution profiles. Longitudinally, within-group analyses revealed distinct trajectories based on TUG changes over 3 years. For MASLD, the FIB-4 index significantly increased in participants whose TUG declined from normal to impaired (Group 3) or remained persistently impaired (Group 4)(p<0.05). For CAD, CAC and CAV scores increased significantly across all four groups (p<0.001). Regarding fat distribution, subcutaneous fat (L3SFA) significantly increased in Groups 3 and 4. Additionally, the proportion of individuals with high visceral fat (VFA ≥160 cm²) increased in these impaired groups, whereas it decreased in those who maintained or improved to a normal TUG (Groups 1 and 2).

CONCLUSION: Baseline TUG impairment and within-group longitudinal TUG deterioration were associated with adverse MASLD, CAD, and fat distribution profiles. While causal relationships cannot be established, TUG performance may serve as a functional marker reflecting metabolic and cardiovascular health status in older adults.

articles.title: Comparing artificial intelligence and clinical team discharge predictions to actual patient discharges in two neonatal intensive care units.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: When patients are admitted to the hospital, clinical care teams must enter an expected discharge date (CT-EDD) into the electronic health record (EHR). This is often challenging for neonates admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) due to extended lengths of stay. Pieces, a generative artificial intelligence (AI) program, uses EHR data and machine learning (ML) algorithms to predicted discharge dates (AI-PDD) for patients anticipated to discharge home in the next 5 days.

OBJECTIVE: To compare CT-EDD and AI-PDD for patients at a level 3 (L3) delivery NICU and level 4 (L4) referral NICU with actual discharge dates.

METHODS: Retrospective chart review from Sept 1, 2024 to December 31, 2024 including all NICU patients discharged home. Patients who were transferred or who died before discharge were excluded. The CT-EDD and AI-PDD were recorded starting with the date of discharge and up to six days prior, for up to 7 total days. Days with missing CT-EDD or AI-PDD were excluded. Differences between CT-EDD/AI-PDD and actual discharge date were evaluated.

RESULTS: At the L3 delivery NICU, the CT-EDD demonstrated better accuracy compared to the AI-PDD for each of the 6 days preceding discharge and the day of discharge (p<0.001). The CT-EDD performed better than the AI-PDD for 61.1% of total patient days and 69.4% of patients. Conversely, at the L4 referral NICU, the AI-PDD demonstrated better accuracy compared to the CT-EDD for each of the 6 days preceding discharge (p<0.001). The AI-PDD performed better than the CT-EDD for 61.8% of total patient days and 62.6% of patients.

CONCLUSION: AI-PDD was more accurate than CT-EDD in a L4 referral NICU setting but underperformed in a L3 delivery NICU setting. Additional studies are warranted to evaluate factors that may contribute to these differences.

articles.title: Phase I Trial of Liquid Nitrogen Spray Cryotherapy concurrent with neoadjuvant chemoradiation for Locally Advanced Esophageal Cancer: Dose Escalation and Long-Term Overall Survival.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spray cryotherapy (LNSC) is hypothesized to increase effectiveness of neoadjuvant chemoradiation (CRT). We aimed to determine safety of multiple cryotherapy sessions prior to and concurrent with CRT in locally advanced esophageal cancer.

METHODS: "3+3" phase 1 dose frequency escalation trial. Primary outcome was safety; secondary outcomes were Quality of Life (QoL) complete clinical response (cCR), survival, and immunogenic cell death (change in serum HMGB1).

RESULTS: There was no treatment related grade 2 or 3 adverse events when LNSC was administered before or concurrent with CRT (n =13). Maximum Tolerated Dose was 3 sessions (2 prior to CRT, 1 during CRT). Mean QoL score improved from 37 at baseline to 31, 29, and 34 after the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd sessions (p-value 0.002, 0.004, and 0.4 respectively). CR with LNSC + CRT occurred in 70%. Over median follow-up of 36 months, overall survival was 40%. 38% showed >25% decrease in HMGB1 within 30 days.

DISCUSSION: No patient experienced dose limiting toxicity. LNSC was safely administered during CRT, improved QoL and high cCR rates were observed. These results support proceeding with a phase 2 trial.

articles.title: Excessive Intrapancreatic Fat Deposition and the Potential Therapeutic Role of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Experimental and clinical endocrinology & diabetes : official journal, German Society of Endocrinology [and] German Diabetes Association
articles.abstract: Excessive intrapancreatic fat deposition, also called non-alcoholic fatty pancreas disease, is marked by abnormal fat accumulation in pancreatic tissue and inked to metabolic syndrome, obesity, insulin resistance, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Despite its clinical importance, intrapancreatic fat deposition lacks standardized diagnostic criteria and is often underdiagnosed. This systematic review explores the pathogenesis, diagnostic challenges, and clinical relevance of intrapancreatic fat deposition, with particular attention to the therapeutic potential of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists. A literature search of PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar, supplemented by a post-review verification search, identified six studies (two preclinical and four clinical studies) meeting pre-specified eligibility criteria for original data on a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist intervention with a pancreatic fat outcome, following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidance; several sources considered during full-text review are reclassified as secondary literature or as not evaluating a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist and are cited instead as background.
