Preclinical evidence indicates that liraglutide and semaglutide can attenuate pancreatic endoplasmic reticulum stress, islet-cell apoptosis, and lipid dysregulation in diet-induced obesity models. Clinical evidence is mixed: a retrospective study reported a significant reduction in pancreatic fat with liraglutide in patients with intrapancreatic fat deposition, whereas randomised trials of liraglutide, exenatide, and dulaglutide have not consistently shown a significant between-group reduction, and direct pancreatic fat outcome data for semaglutide in humans are lacking. A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials across glucose-lowering drug classes reported a significant pooled reduction in intrapancreatic fat deposition with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, providing independent, quantitative support for a class effect. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists are already established to confer benefits beyond glycaemic control and pancreatic fat, including cardiovascular, renal, and broader weight-related metabolic benefits; their potential role in intrapancreatic fat deposition is one facet of this wider profile rather than a distinct "dual-purpose" mechanism. Given small samples, heterogeneous imaging, and inability to separate pancreas-specific effects from hepatic and visceral fat reductions, evidence suggests an unconfirmed role for glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists in intrapancreatic fat deposition. Prospective powered trials with standardised imaging and hepatic/visceral fat measurements are needed before clinical practice.

articles.title: [Public Health as an Elective in the Final Clinical Year in Baden-Württemberg, Germany: Results of a Mixed-Methods Study on Elective Evaluation and Development of an Evaluation Instrument].
articles.journal: Gesundheitswesen (Bundesverband der Arzte des Offentlichen Gesundheitsdienstes (Germany))
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In light of global challenges such as pandemics, social inequality, antibiotic resistance, and climate change, public health perspectives are becoming increasingly important in medical care. However, medical education remains predominantly focused on individual patient care. Content related to public health and practical insights into public health services (PHS) have so far been incorporated into the curriculum only to a limited extent. Since November 2023, it has been possible to take a public health elective at six pilot teaching local public health authorities (LHA) in Baden-Württemberg, Germany. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the implementation of this public health elective.

METHODS: Using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design, qualitative individual interviews were conducted with students and supervisors from six pilot LHA. Based on these findings, a questionnaire instrument for the long-term evaluation of the public health elective was developed and piloted. Five students and five staff members from LHA were interviewed. Eight of the 14 students participated in the survey.

RESULTS: The public health elective was rated positively overall by both students and supervisors. The students surveyed highlighted the structured orientation, the dedicated supervision, and the flexibility in rotation planning and working hours. All students reported gaining a good overview of LHA activities. Six out of eight students gave the highest grade, and all will recommend it to others. Practical competencies were acquired primarily in the Child and Adolescent Health Service, the HIV/STI service, and in infection control. Criticisms included the logbook, which was perceived as too extensive and not very practice-oriented, as well as the cross-site organization of the public health elective support classes.

DISCUSSION: The results suggest that the public health elective can help raise awareness of PHS and help medical students with their career planning. Given the global challenges, the public health elective can help incorporate public health perspectives into medical education and provide hands-on experience in this field. Furthermore, there are indications that the introduction of the public health elective may also stimulate organizational development within LHA. Due to the small sample size and potential selection bias, generalizability of findings is limited.

articles.title: Endothelial Contributions to Venous Thrombus Resolution.
articles.abstract: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is an obstructive vascular condition with an incidence of ~1 in 1000 adults per year. Complications of DVT include post-thrombotic syndrome, which is debilitating and painful, and pulmonary embolism, which is life-threatening. Current treatments for DVT are associated with increased risks of bleeding, infection, or re-thrombosis, and fail to accelerate natural venous thrombus resolution. Venous thrombus resolution occurs through a process of organization that involves thrombus retraction away from the vein, fibrinolysis of the thrombus, and the formation of vascular channels within and around the thrombus. Endothelial cell (EC)-lined vascular channels are present in rodent and human resolving thrombi. Rodent models of DVT show that thrombus neovascularization occurs as early as 3-4 days after thrombus induction and increases progressively thereafter throughout thrombus resolution. The extent to which thrombus neovascularization contributes to its resolution, as well as the source of the ECs that vascularize the resolving thrombus, are unclear. Circumstantial evidence suggests that neovascularization is driven by resident ECs that ingress into the resolving thrombus, while circulating endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs) promote neovascularization in a paracrine manner. Resident ECs and EPCs also contribute to thrombus fibrinolysis. The aim of this review is to describe the role of ECs and EPCs in DVT resolution, and the potential of promoting thrombus endothelialization and vascularization for the treatment of DVT. We will also outline knowledge gaps in the understanding of EC/EPC-mediated contributions to DVT resolution. The promotion of EC-mediated thrombus resolution represents a novel therapeutic strategy for DVT.

articles.title: Pantothenate metabolic alterations in PROS1 mutation carriers and the antithrombotic effects of pantethine.
articles.abstract: Background Patients carrying PROS1 mutations are at increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, metabolic alterations linked to PROS1 mutations and their thrombotic contribution remain unclear. Objectives This study aimed to identify metabolic changes in PROS1‑mutation patients through integrated multi‑omics analyses, and to investigate the role of pantothenate derivatives in thrombosis using in vivo and in vitro models. Methods Serum metabolomics, siRNA‑mediated PROS1 knockdown in THLE‑2 cells, murine thrombosis models, and endothelial cell functional assays were employed. Results Patients with PROS1 mutations exhibited significantly reduced serum levels of pantothenate derivatives, particularly pantetheine. siRNA‑mediated PROS1 knockdown in THLE‑2 cells recapitulated this metabolic disturbance. In vivo, pantethine supplementation attenuated thrombus formation and platelet activation in murine models, accompanied by reduced serum levels of vWF and ICAM‑1, and increased TFPI. In vitro, pantethine pretreatment suppressed NF‑κB phosphorylation and reduced endothelial reactive oxygen species, counteracting IL‑1β‑induced procoagulant phenotype, leading to downregulation of vWF and ICAM‑1 and upregulation of TFPI and THBD. Furthermore, pantethine‑conditioned endothelial cells reduced responsiveness of co‑incubated platelets, including attenuated spreading, aggregation, and activation. These findings associate PROS1 mutation‑driven metabolic alterations with thrombotic risk, and suggest a metabolic‑endothelial‑platelet mode of interaction. Conclusions This study demonstrates that patients with PROS1 mutations exhibit reduced circulating pantothenate derivatives, and that pantethine attenuates murine thrombosis and modulates endothelial and platelet function in vitro. These findings identify a metabolic‑endothelial‑platelet association in Protein S deficiency. Whether PROS1 mutations directly cause pantothenate metabolic disturbance, and whether this disturbance mediates thrombosis, require testing in PROS1‑deficient in vivo models.

articles.title: Safety, tolerability, and efficacy of bepranemab in people living with prodromal-to-mild Alzheimer's disease: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tau aggregation is a defining feature of the pathophysiology of Alzheimer's disease and an appealing therapeutic target, yet tau-directed antibodies tested to date-primarily targeting N-terminal epitopes-have failed to slow tau progression or cognitive decline. Bepranemab targets the tau mid-region, predicted in cell-based assays to more effectively block neuron-to-neuron tau spread than anti-tau antibodies targeting the N-terminus. We aimed to investigate the safety and efficacy of bepranemab in slowing progression of tau pathology and clinical decline in people with prodromal-to-mild Alzheimer's disease.

METHODS: This double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial recruited participants across 101 outpatient sites in Europe (eight countries), Canada, and the USA. Participants (aged 50-80 years) with prodromal-to-mild Alzheimer's disease were randomly assigned 1:1:1 (using an interactive response system) to intravenous bepranemab 45 mg/kg, bepranemab 90 mg/kg, or placebo (every 4 weeks for 76 weeks), stratified by diagnosis, apolipoprotein E ɛ4 carrier status, and symptomatic treatment use. The primary endpoint was change from baseline to week 80 in Clinical Dementia Rating Scale-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) total score. Efficacy was assessed in the full analysis set (ie, all randomly assigned participants who received at least a partial dose of trial medication and had at least one valid post-baseline clinic visit and efficacy assessment). Safety was assessed in all randomly assigned participants who received at least a partial dose of the trial medication. No imputation was done for missing data. The trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04867616) and is complete.

FINDINGS: Between Aug 24, 2021, and Oct 25, 2022, 466 participants were randomly assigned to bepranemab 45 mg/kg (n=154), bepranemab 90 mg/kg (n=155), or placebo (n=157) at 85 sites. Median age was 72·0 years (IQR 66·0-76·0), 259 (56%) were female, and 207 (44%) were male. In total, 460 participants were included in the full analysis set: bepranemab 45 mg/kg (n=152), bepranemab 90 mg/kg (n=152), and placebo (n=156). Least-squares mean CDR-SB total score change from baseline to week 80 was 2·15 in the bepranemab 90 mg/kg group and 1·85 in the bepranemab 45 mg/kg group versus 1·81 in the placebo group, with differences versus placebo of 0·34 (95% CI -0·09 to 0·78, p=0·12; 80% CI 0·06 to 0·63) for the bepranemab 90 mg/kg group and 0·04 (-0·40 to 0·47, p=0·87; -0·25 to 0·32) for the bepranemab 45 mg/kg group. Frequency of treatment-emergent adverse events with bepranemab was similar to the placebo group (139 [91%] with bepranemab 45 mg/kg, 140 [91%] with bepranemab 90 mg/kg, and 142 [90%] with placebo); no treatment-related neuroinflammatory safety signals were identified clinically or on brain MRI scans. There were adverse events leading to death in four (1%) participants in the combined bepranemab groups and six (4%) in the placebo group; none were considered related to the trial treatment.

INTERPRETATION: Treatment with bepranemab was associated with an acceptable safety profile. However, the primary endpoint was not met. Hypothesis-generating differences favouring bepranemab in tau PET and 14-item Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive Subscale should be tested prospectively in trials powered for tau PET outcomes and stratified by baseline tau burden and apolipoprotein E ɛ4 status.

FUNDING: UCB.

articles.title: Reframing disease elimination: an update from the Lancet Commission on chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with increasing global burden driven by population growth and ageing, persistent harmful exposures, and substantial health inequities. The Lancet Commission on COPD articulated an ambitious vision for disease elimination with prevention, early detection, and intervention. This Review revisits that vision, assesses progress since 2022, and calls for a broader commitment to lifelong lung health as an update of the Commission. Across seven sections, this Review advances a unified framework integrating the biology of lung development and ageing, precision medicine, patient-centred outcomes, and regulatory reform. COPD is not a single, uniform disease; rather, a biologically complex condition shaped by genetic, developmental, environmental, infectious, and behavioural factors across the entire life course. Effective prevention and care should therefore move beyond the detection and treatment of late physiological impairment toward earlier disease recognition, biological stratification, and interventions to preserve lung health, reduce symptoms, and prevent morbidity and premature mortality. The Review charts a path from reactive, late-stage management toward proactive, equitable, precision-based prevention and care. The central premise is unequivocal: the global burden of COPD can be substantially reduced. Success should be measured not only by gains in lung function and survival but also by improvements in daily functioning, quality of life, and wellbeing. In this expanded vision, COPD is no longer viewed solely as a chronic disease to be managed but as a preventable and modifiable condition within a broader commitment to lifelong lung health.

articles.title: Maternal and perinatal outcomes in pregnant women with Lassa fever: analysis from the LASCOPE prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lassa fever, a viral haemorrhagic fever endemic in west Africa, is usually described as associated with severe maternal and perinatal outcomes. Previous studies reported maternal mortality of 33% (whereas overall mortality is about 14% in Nigeria for patients admitted to hospital) and fetal mortality is up to 60%. However, most evidence derives from small case series with substantial limitations. We aimed to assess maternal death and perinatal outcomes in a prospective cohort study with standardised medical care protocols.

METHODS: We analysed data from the LASCOPE cohort from the Federal Medical Centre Owo, Nigeria, which included all patients with PCR-confirmed Lassa fever. In this analysis, non-pregnant women of childbearing age (15-45 years) were compared with pregnant women, defined as having an ongoing pregnancy during Lassa fever. The primary maternal outcome was all-cause mortality 28 days after admission and the primary pregnancy outcome was fetal death. Mortality at 28 days was compared using Kaplan-Meier estimates and a Cox proportional-hazards model, the cumulative incidence of fetal death was estimated with livebirth as a competing event, and the association between gestational age at symptom onset and fetal death was assessed by logistic regression.

FINDINGS: Between April 4, 2018, and Feb 18, 2023, of 1006 patients in the LASCOPE cohort admitted with PCR-confirmed Lassa fever, 703 were excluded for not being of childbearing age, and 303 were women of childbearing age, of whom 45 were pregnant. The median age of pregnant women was 28 years (IQR 24-32). The 28-day mortality was comparable between pregnant and non-pregnant women (four [9%; 95% CI 2-21] of 45 vs 19 [7%; 95% CI 4-11] of 258; hazard ratio 1·19 [95% CI 0·41-3·50]; log-rank p=0·75). Fetal case-fatality rate was 60% (27 of 45), with higher risk of fetal death if infection occurred early in the pregnancy (100% for the first trimester, 82% for the second trimester, and 25% for the third trimester). Each additional week of gestation at symptom onset was associated with a reduction in the odds of fetal death (odds ratio 0·77 [95% CI 0·61-0·90]). Among 15 liveborn infants, three (20%) died within 30 days.

INTERPRETATION: Although the fetal prognosis was poor, as previously reported, maternal fatality was lower than previously indicated, potentially reflecting improved supportive care and patient monitoring. These findings suggest that maternal mortality might be lower than historically reported, while confirming the urgent need for specific therapeutic interventions to improve fetal outcomes.

FUNDING: INSERM/REACTing; the African Coalition for Epidemic Research, Response and Training consortium; the University of Oxford; the UK Department for International Development; the Wellcome Trust; the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs; the Agence Nationale de Recherches sur le SIDA et les hépatites virales; and the French National Research Institute for Sustainable Development.

articles.title: Mechanical thrombectomy outcomes in childhood stroke.
Incidence and predictors of suboptimal functional outcomes despite successful reperfusion in paediatric stroke: a cohort study from the Save ChildS Pro registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Successful vessel reperfusion with persistent clinical deficit occurs in 40-60% of adults undergoing mechanical thrombectomy but has never been characterised in childhood stroke. We aimed to determine the incidence and predictors of so-called futile recanalisation, in which the occluded artery is reopened but the patient does not recover good function, in paediatric mechanical thrombectomy for acute ischaemic stroke.

METHODS: We retrospectively analysed prospectively collected data from the Save ChildS Pro registry, an international, multicentre, observational registry that included children aged 28 days to 18 years presenting with acute ischaemic stroke across 45 centres in 12 countries between Jan 1, 2020, and Aug 31, 2023. Patients who underwent endovascular thrombectomy and had successful recanalisation (expanded Treatment in Cerebral Infarction [eTICI] grade ≥2b) were included. The primary outcome was suboptimal functional outcome despite successful recanalisation, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score greater than 2 at 90 days, on a scale from 0 (no symptoms) to 6 (death) on which 0-2 denotes functional independence; three additional thresholds (mRS score >1, Pediatric Stroke Outcome Measure [PSOM] >1·0, and PSOM >0·5) were analysed as sensitivity analyses. Adjusted associations between candidate predictors (age, baseline Pediatric National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [PedNIHSS] score, baseline Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score [ASPECTS], and final eTICI grade) and each outcome were estimated using Firth-penalised multivariable logistic regression. Save ChildS Pro is registered with the German Clinical Trials Registry (DRKS00018960).

FINDINGS: 101 patients (54 [53%] males and 47 [47%] females; median age 11·0 years [IQR 6·0-15·0]) had successful recanalisation with 90-day follow-up and comprised the analytical cohort. A suboptimal outcome (mRS score >2) occurred in 18 (18%) of 101 patients. On Firth-adjusted multivariable analysis, lower final eTICI grade was significantly associated with suboptimal outcome (adjusted OR 0·44 [95% CI 0·23-0·84], p=0·012), and younger age was associated in the same direction (0·87 [0·78-0·97] per year, p=0·0098); baseline PedNIHSS score and baseline ASPECTS were not independently associated with a suboptimal outcome. Findings were directionally consistent across the three sensitivity thresholds.

INTERPRETATION: In this analysis, 18% of children with successful recanalisation had a suboptimal functional outcome at 90 days, markedly lower than the proportion reported in adults (40-60%). Lower recanalisation quality and younger age were independently associated with suboptimal outcome, whereas baseline PedNIHSS score and ASPECTS had limited prognostic value. These findings highlight the need for longer-term studies and challenge the direct translation of adult prognostic frameworks to paediatric stroke, supporting age-specific approaches. Given the limited event count, these findings should be considered exploratory and require external validation.

FUNDING: None.

articles.title: Obstructive sleep apnoea: an overlooked challenge in the current NHS Strategy.
articles.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) is common, frequently symptomatic, and closely associated with conditions already prioritised by the UK National Health Service (NHS), including obesity, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, cardiovascular disease, and stroke. Previous estimates suggest that approximately 8 million UK adults aged 30-69 years could have OSA, although the proportion remaining undiagnosed is uncertain. Evidence supports treatment benefits for daytime sleepiness, symptom burden, quality of life, driving safety, and blood pressure in some patients, but not a consistent reduction in major cardiovascular events. UK data indicate long diagnostic waits, regional variation, and gaps in follow-up. A proportionate NHS response should prioritise targeted case-finding within existing chronic-disease pathways, access to validated home-based diagnostics, specialist capacity for complex disease, and sustained treatment support. Implementation should be phased and evaluated prospectively for clinical outcomes, equity, workforce requirements, affordability, and budget impact.

articles.title: Stillbirth Risk with Class II and III Obesity.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We sought to analyze the rates of stillbirth at recommended gestational age epochs based on body mass index (BMI) at first prenatal visit.

STUDY DESIGN: A total of 79,148 births with optimal dating, BMI at first prenatal visit, and absence of maternal complications (chronic hypertension, pregestational diabetes) or fetal complications (aneuploidy, major fetal malformations, fetal growth restriction) were identified from January 2013 to September 2024. Of these, 33,108 (42%) delivered ≥ 34 weeks with a BMI classified as normal, class II, or class III obesity. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) were calculated due to differences in age, race/ethnicity, and parity.

RESULTS: Among patients with class II obesity, no difference in stillbirth was observed compared with normal weight individuals at either early term (370/7 -386/7 weeks) or term (≥ 39 weeks), with aHRs of 2.19 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.67-7.17) and 0.86 (95% CI 0.17-4.34), respectively. Neither were differences found in stillbirth risk for patients with class III obesity compared with normal weight individuals in the late preterm (340/7 -366/7 weeks), early term, or term gestational ages with aHRs of 0.78 (95% CI 0.17-3.57), 2.44 (95% CI 0.61-9.84), and 2.81 (95% CI 0.7-11.28), respectively.

CONCLUSION: Based on our results, the utility of antepartum surveillance for the prevention of stillbirth in patients with class II or III obesity may be of limited benefit.

KEY POINTS: · There is no significant increased risk of stillbirth in class II obesity at term.. · The utility of antepartum surveillance may be of limited benefit.. · No significant increased risk of stillbirth in class III obesity beginning at preterm gestation has been found..

articles.title: Intravascular Lithotripsy in the Treatment of Heavily Calcified Femoropopliteal Arterial Occlusive Disease.
articles.journal: RoFo : Fortschritte auf dem Gebiete der Rontgenstrahlen und der Nuklearmedizin
articles.abstract:
ABSTRACT: Severely calcified lesions of the femoropopliteal segment have always presented very complex conditions for endovascular therapy of peripheral arterial disease (PAD). In particular, the rigidity and instability of the heavily calcified vessel wall result in a limited initial lumen gain after angioplasty, frequent recoil, early restenosis, and an increased rate of reinterventions. In this context, intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is increasingly becoming the focus of interest. By using low-energy shock waves, both superficial and deep intimal and medial calcifications are selectively micro-fractured. This leads to improved vessel compliance and enables effective angioplasty. At low inflation pressures of 4-6 atm, the barotrauma acting on the vessel wall during IVL is overall reduced. Randomized clinical studies demonstrate a higher technical success rate of IVL compared to PTA plus DCB-PTA, with a lower complication rate and significantly better 1- and 2-year patency. IVL can be used both as a stand-alone therapy and for vessel preparation in combination with DCBPTA, and also presents an alternative therapy to atherectomy, cutting, scoring, and high-pressure balloon angioplasty. This review focuses on the methodological description of the IVL with the Shockwave system in the femoropopliteal segment, considering both technical and clinical success data.

KEY POINTS: · IVL enables effective vessel preparation in severe calcified femoropopliteal lesions.. · IVL works with low inflation pressures thereby reducing barotrauma, dissections, and bail-out stenting.. · Patency rates of IVL plus DCB are superior to conventional angioplasty plus DCB..

CITATION FORMAT: · Hölting MS, Bekker I, Stehr A et al. Intravascular Lithotripsy in the Treatment of Heavily Calcified Femoropopliteal Arterial Occlusive Disease. Rofo 2026; DOI 10.1055/a-2907-7766.

articles.title: Updated Recommendations of the German Radiological Society and the German Professional Association of Radiologists on Prostate MRI in the Context of the New S3 Guideline on Prostate Cancer.
articles.journal: RoFo : Fortschritte auf dem Gebiete der Rontgenstrahlen und der Nuklearmedizin
articles.abstract:
ABSTRACT: This article provides an update of the 2021 recommendations of the German Radiological Society (DRG) and the German Professional Association of Radiologists (BDR) on prostate MRI in accordance with the German S3 guideline on prostate cancer (version 8.1, published August 2025). The recommendations define the "current quality standards" for prostate MRI referenced in the S3 guideline and provide detailed guidance on patient history requirements, scheduling and preparation, and current indications for prostate MRI. Newly added sections cover the recommended imaging protocol, applications of artificial intelligence, and requirements for quality and structured reporting. MRI-guided (in-bore) prostate biopsy, including laboratory workup, management of anticoagulation, and antibiotic prophylaxis, is also discussed in detail.

KEY POINTS: · Update of the DRG/BDR recommendations regarding prostate MRI in accordance with the new S3 guideline on prostate cancer (version 8.1, 2025).. · Definition of the "current quality standards" for prostate MRI referenced in the S3 guideline.. · New guidelines regarding indications, applications of artificial intelligence, quality/structured reporting requirements.. · Detailed discussion of MRI-guided (in-bore) prostate biopsy..

CITATION FORMAT: · Franiel T, Asbach P, Beyersdorff D et al. Updated Recommendations of the German Radiological Society and the German Professional Association of Radiologists on Prostate MRI in the Context of the New S3 Guideline on Prostate Cancer. Rofo 2026; DOI 10.1055/a-2979-8879.

articles.title: Microbiome-antibiotic-immune interactions influence mortality in preterm infant gut microbiota-humanized gnotobiotic mice.
articles.abstract: Infants born preterm are treated with antibiotics when bacterial infection is suspected. Antibiotics disrupt the gut microbiota, leading to unfavorable immune and infectious consequences. However, the impact of specific antibiotics on gut microbial and immune responses is largely unknown. We develop a humanized gnotobiotic mouse model where we gavage preterm infant stool into germ-free dams. We treat microbiota-humanized pups with subcutaneous antibiotics with probenecid to model empiric sepsis treatment regimens. Pups humanized with microbiota including ampicillin-resistant Enterobacteriaceae die during ampicillin with probenecid treatment with increased gut permeability and systemic microbial spread. Conversely, pups with microbiota containing gelatinase-expressing Enterococcus faecalis die during meropenem with probenecid treatment with increased gut E. faecalis and systemic immune dysregulation. Gut E. faecalis, especially strains containing gelE and fsr, increase in human preterm infant gut microbiomes after meropenem. These data raise concerns about the unintended consequences of antibiotic treatment and provide a framework for understanding microbiome-antibiotic-immune interplay.

articles.title: Geographic disparities and aging-related burden in reperfusion service output for acute ischemic stroke in China: A national sample spatial analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite expanding stroke centers, regional disparities and population aging challenge acute ischemic stroke (AIS) care in China. We aimed to map the spatial distribution of AIS reperfusion therapy and identify aging-related service mismatch.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study analyzed hospital-level data from 2,522 mainland Chinese hospitals participating in the Survey of National Stroke Telemedicine Treatment Project. Spatial analysis was used to assess service output distribution. Multilevel mixed-effects logistic regression evaluated factors associated with treatment efficiency. A four-quadrant matrix compared regional aging rates with observed thrombolysis volume to identify high-aging-burden, low-service-output mismatch.

FINDINGS: Thrombolysis output showed an east-to-west gradient that became more pronounced after adjusting for aging population. Compared with secondary and below hospitals, tertiary hospitals had a higher monthly thrombolysis volume (10 [5-16] versus 4 [2-8]) and shorter door-to-needle time (DNT) (43 [36-50] versus 48 [41-56]). Core service mismatch, defined by high aging and low output, was concentrated in county-and-below hospitals, which accounted for 70.9% of the total area. Aging rate was associated with achieving a median DNT of ≤60 min (absolute probability difference (%), 2.85; 95% confidence interval, 0.97-4.73; p = 0.003, per 10% increase). Exploratory analysis suggested that larger aging populations were associated with greater thrombolysis volume, which was, in turn, associated with shorter DNT.

CONCLUSION: Geographic disparities and service output mismatch persisted within China's AIS care network. Given the dual associations between population aging and reperfusion therapy service, capacity building in basic hospitals and demographic-based resource allocation may help align services with regional needs.

FUNDING: This work was supported by the Beijing Natural Science Foundation.

articles.title: A CONSTANS-like transcriptional co-activator couples ethylene signaling to jasmonate biosynthesis and is targeted by a fungal effector.
articles.abstract: Ethylene and jasmonate synergistically regulate immunity against necrotrophic pathogens, but how ethylene signaling promotes jasmonate biosynthesis remains unclear. Here, we show that the apple CONSTANS-like (COL) protein MdCOL4 functions as a transcriptional co-activator that couples ethylene signaling to jasmonate biosynthesis during disease resistance. The ethylene-responsive transcription factor MdERF098 directly activates the jasmonate biosynthetic genes MdOPR2 and MdOPR3. MdCOL4 physically associates with MdERF098 and enhances its DNA-binding activity, thereby promoting MdOPR2/3 transcription, jasmonate accumulation, and resistance to apple Valsa canker, a destructive trunk disease caused by Valsa mali, a necrotrophic fungal pathogen. We further identify a fungal effector from V. mali, Vm11039, that translocates into the host nucleus and binds MdCOL4 with higher affinity than MdERF098, competitively disrupting the MdCOL4-MdERF098 complex. This interference attenuates jasmonate biosynthesis and promotes pathogen infection. Together, our findings uncover a transcriptional co-activation mechanism that couples ethylene signaling to jasmonate biosynthesis and establish transcriptional co-activator complexes as vulnerable regulatory hubs targeted by pathogen effectors to suppress hormone-mediated immunity, thereby providing a potential target for engineering resistance against necrotrophic diseases.

articles.title: Plasmodium falciparum Hsp90 supports DNA replication.
articles.abstract: Plasmodium falciparum heat shock protein 90 (PfHsp90) is an attractive antimalarial target, but the molecular pathways dependent on its activity remain poorly understood. Here, we use two chemically distinct Hsp90 inhibitors, geldanamycin and XL888, to profile the PfHsp90-dependent proteome during the blood stage. We identify 131 proteins reduced in abundance following both treatments, 40% of which co-immunoprecipitate with PfHsp90. DNA replication emerges as the most enriched pathway, and PfHsp90 inhibition reduces parasite DNA content and nascent DNA synthesis during blood- and liver-stage development. Combining Hsp90 inhibition with inhibitors of DNA replication further produces synergistic antiparasitic activity. Together, these findings establish a functional connection between PfHsp90 and parasite DNA replication and define a network of conserved and Plasmodium-specific proteins dependent on Hsp90 activity.

articles.title: Pilot study of neurotransmission cognitive therapy using ultra-low-frequency vibration waves in children with cerebral palsy-associated spastic dysarthria.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neurotransmission Cognitive Therapy (NCT) proposes that targeted low-frequency mechanical vibration may modulate sensorimotor pathways involved in speech motor control. However, clinical evidence in pediatric neurodevelopmental speech disorders remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: This pilot study evaluated the feasibility, safety, and preliminary effects of NCT in children with cerebral palsy (CP) presenting with spastic dysarthria.

METHODS: A prospective single-arm pre-post pilot design was conducted involving 12 children (mean age 6.2 ± 1.3 years). The intervention consisted of targeted low-frequency vibration therapy delivered over a six-month period with an initial intensive phase followed by reduced-frequency sessions. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and post-intervention using the Dysarthria Profile and the Urdu Articulation and Phonology Assessment Test (TAAPU). Caregiver-reported outcomes were collected using a structured questionnaire, and safety was monitored throughout the study period.

RESULTS: Improvements were observed in speech motor function and phonological performance following the intervention period. The total Dysarthria Profile score increased from 51.87 to 63.87 (p = .005). TAAPU analyses indicated reductions in selected phonological error patterns, with statistically significant changes in most comparisons (p < .05). Caregiver reports suggested perceived improvements in speech intelligibility and communicative participation. No serious adverse events were reported.

CONCLUSION: NCT was feasible and well tolerated in this pilot cohort. Although improvements in speech-related measures were observed, the single-arm design limits causal inference. These findings provide preliminary evidence supporting further investigation through larger, controlled clinical trials to evaluate efficacy and underlying mechanisms.

articles.title: Caffeine and micro-nanoplastics synergistically reduce host tolerance to parasitic infection.
articles.abstract: Risk assessments of micro-nanoplastics (MNPs) and co-occurring contaminants require understanding how chemical interactions shape animal welfare under parasitism, a key regulator of life history traits. We quantified the chemical stability of caffeine (CAFF) and its adsorption to polystyrene (PS) MNPs and investigated how infection with the ectoparasite Gyrodactylus turnbulli interacts with PS MNPs (0.05 mg L⁻¹) and CAFF (10 or 60 µg L⁻¹) in the guppy host (Poecilia reticulata). Caffeine exhibited a half-life of 17 days in freshwater and 24 days in distilled water, with effective concentration (3 and 9 μg L⁻¹) lower than nominal levels (10 and 60 µg L⁻¹). PS MNPs adsorbed up to 7.5% of a high concentration of caffeine (0.1 mg mL⁻¹) after 18 h exposure indicating negligible adsorption at the tested biological exposure levels. Exposure to single stressors (PS or CAFF) reduced parasite burdens relative to infected fish without chemical exposure, although PS prolonged infection duration. In contrast, combined exposure (PS+CAFF) increased parasite burdens, indicating impaired host resistance. Parasite activity increased significantly at PS + CAFF60 μg L⁻¹ suggesting direct stimulant effects or altered host skin or mucus properties. Host mortality responses to caffeine were non-monotonic: the CAFF 10 μg L⁻¹ treatment significantly increased mortality, whereas the CAFF 60 μg L⁻¹ treatment did not. Notably, combined exposure to both contaminants produced synergistic and non-additive increases in mortality of uninfected fish, and more pronounced effects in infected individuals. Overall, PS MNPs and caffeine act synergistically to increase mortality and reduce resistance to infection. Importantly, inclusion of parasitism alters toxicity outcomes beyond predictions based solely on abiotic stressors.

articles.title: BPA exposure from gestation through the post-weaning period increases susceptibility to allergic airway inflammation in female mouse offspring: Association with reduced mTOR phosphorylation, enhanced autophagy, and Foxp3 promoter methylation.
articles.abstract: Early-life exposure to bisphenol A (BPA), a ubiquitous endocrine disruptor, is associated with increased asthma susceptibility in offspring, yet the mechanisms remain poorly characterized. We examined whether BPA exposure spanning gestation, lactation, and the post-weaning period is associated with allergic airway inflammation in female offspring in relation to mTOR signaling, autophagy, and Foxp3 methylation. Dams received BPA (0.1 µg/mL in drinking water, ~25 µg/kg BW/day) from gestational day 6 to weaning; female offspring continued BPA or vehicle post-weaning and were assigned to control, BPA, ovalbumin (OVA), and BPA+OVA groups before OVA sensitization and challenge. Airway hyperresponsiveness, lung histopathology, BALF inflammation and Th2 cytokines, serum OVA-specific IgE, splenic Tregs, LC3/p62 and mTOR signaling, and Foxp3 methylation were assessed. BPA alone was associated with moderate asthma-like phenotypes approaching those induced by OVA; co-exposure produced the most severe phenotypes, with stepwise control-to-BPA+OVA trends in mucus, LC3 (increasing), and p62 (decreasing). BPA was associated with reduced mTOR phosphorylation (Ser2448) accompanied by PI3K/Akt inhibition and AMPK/TSC1/2 activation, increased Foxp3 methylation, and reduced splenic Tregs, most pronounced under co-exposure. Thus, BPA exposure from gestation through the post-weaning period is associated with exacerbated allergic airway inflammation in female offspring, accompanied by mTOR suppression, enhanced autophagy, Foxp3 hypermethylation, and Treg reduction; interventional studies are needed to establish causality.

articles.title: Patient and occupational dosimetry in fluoroscopy-guided interventions in Spain: Progress made, gaps remaining.
articles.journal: Physica medica : PM : an international journal devoted to the applications of physics to medicine and biology : official journal of the Italian Association of Biomedical Physics (AIFB)
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to assess the current status of patient and occupational dosimetry practices in Spain and identify areas for improvement in relation to European and international recommendations.

METHODS: Two nationwide surveys were conducted by a joint SEFM-SEPR working group, targeting medical physicists at centres performing fluoroscopy-guided interventional procedures. Key topics included DRLs, DMS, occupational radiation protection, certification, and training. Descriptive statistics were used to analyse the responses.

RESULTS: A total of 38 responses were analysed for patient dosimetry and 32 for occupational radiation protection, with broad geographical representation. Most centres reported access to basic dosimetric data; however, 32 % lacked a dedicated DMS. Although 55 % of respondents reported using DRLs, routine application and physician involvement were limited. Patient dose calculations were performed in 58 % of centres but were mainly not recorded. In occupational radiation protection, the availability of personal protective equipment and eye lens dosimetry was high (97 %), while real-time dosimetry systems were implemented in 44 % of centres and not consistently quality-controlled. Variability was also observed in advanced certification, with only 22 % of centres meeting the requirements for second-level certification, and continuing education remained inconsistent.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite clear progress in recent years, significant variability persists in interventional dosimetry practices across Spanish centres. Wider implementation of DMS, stronger integration of DRLs into clinical workflows, and sustained investment in training and education are required to achieve harmonised and optimised radiation protection in line with European and international guidelines.

articles.title: Computed tomography-based sex determination using osseous and pneumatic components of the temporal bone in a Japanese population.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The temporal bone, particularly its petrous portion, is highly dense and resilient, preserving its morphology under extreme conditions. This study aimed to three-dimensionally measure the volume of bone and air of the temporal bone using computed tomography (CT) and to develop an objective, high-accuracy sex estimation model for a contemporary Japanese population.

METHODS: CT images of 120 Japanese adults (57 male, 63 female) were analyzed. Utilizing three-dimensional reconstructed images, the bone volume and air volume were measured. The predictive performance was assessed using classification accuracy and the area under the curve (AUC) from receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis.

RESULTS: Descriptive statistics demonstrated significant sexual dimorphism in both bone volume and air volume across bilateral sides, with males exhibiting significantly larger values than females. In the binary logistic regression analysis, models incorporating specific morphometric parameters provided stable discriminant functions.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate substantial sexual dimorphism in the temporal bone morphology of modern Japanese individuals. In particular, the logistic regression models combining the inner air cell pneumatization and the outer bone volume-both of which are highly resistant to postmortem changes-offer an objective and reliable method for sex estimation. This approach serves as a practical and useful screening tool in forensic practice and disaster victim identification (DVI) scenarios where the pelvis or other cranial structures are unavailable.

articles.title: Upstream behavioural and biological contributions to socioeconomic disparities in cardiovascular disease.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the relative contributions of smoking and adiposity phenotypes to the association between socioeconomic status (SES) and prevalent cardiovascular disease (CVD).

STUDY DESIGN: Cross-sectional observational study.

METHODS: We analysed 4772 adults from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) with available socioeconomic, anthropometric, controlled attenuation parameter (CAP), and cardiovascular data. SES was defined using the poverty income ratio (high/low), with continuous SES examined in sensitivity analyses. Prevalent CVD comprised self-reported myocardial infarction, coronary heart disease, or heart failure. Primary mediators included smoking, body mass index, waist circumference, waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), and CAP. Counterfactual mediation analyses with 1000 bootstrap simulations were adjusted for age, sex, and ethnicity.

RESULTS: The cohort comprised 1683 individuals with low SES and 3089 with high SES. Low SES was associated with higher smoking prevalence (24.0% vs 9.6%) and CVD prevalence (13% vs 8.6%; both p < 0.001). Higher SES was associated with lower odds of prevalent CVD (OR 0.80, 95% CI 0.75-0.85; p < 0.001), with attenuation after adjustment for behavioural, adiposity, and cardiometabolic factors (OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.81-0.94; p < 0.001). Smoking demonstrated the largest mediated proportion, accounting for 19.9% of the SES-CVD association (95% CI 7.3-34.2). Among adiposity measures, WHtR demonstrated the largest contribution (10.4%), exceeding waist circumference (5.0%), body mass index (4.6%), and CAP (1.4%).

CONCLUSIONS: Smoking and central adiposity represent important pathways underlying socioeconomic disparities in prevalent CVD. Smoking demonstrated the largest mediated proportion, while WHtR was the strongest adiposity-related mediator. These findings highlight potentially modifiable behavioural and adiposity-related pathways alongside broader socioeconomic determinants of cardiovascular health.

articles.title: Early-stage inhibition of HIV-1 subtypes A, B, and C gag- protease chimeras by Penicillium chrysogenum P03MB2 metabolites and activity against cell-to-cell spread.
articles.abstract: Despite the success of antiretroviral therapy, human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) cell-to-cell spread remains a major barrier to viral eradication. This study evaluated the antiviral activity of secondary metabolite fractions derived from Penicillium chrysogenum P03MB2 against cell-free HIV-1 infection of patient-derived Gag-protease chimeric viruses representing HIV-1 subtypes A, B, and C, and investigated its impact on cell-to-cell spread. Crude fungal extracts from oat-grown cultures were fractionated using mixed-mode cation exchange (MCX) solid-phase extraction. Cytotoxicity was assessed in TZM-bl cells by MTT assay, antiviral activity was evaluated using a luciferase reporter assay. In silico molecular docking explored predicted interactions between five identified metabolites, including Cytochalasin J, and entry-associated targets (CCR5, CXCR4, and gp120). Cell- to cell transmission was assessed using Jurkat co-culture assays and flow cytometry. The 45% MCX Oats fraction emerged as the most active candidate exhibiting low cytotoxicity (CC₅₀ > 300 µg/mL) and potent antiviral activity across all chimeric variants (IC₅₀: 0.221-1.007 µg/mL; Selectivity Indices: 271-1235). Time-of-addition analysis indicated that maximal inhibition during the early infection stages. Molecular docking identified favourable predicted binding compatibility for Cytochalasin J against CCR5 (reaching -10.9 kcal/mol), CXCR4, and gp120 targets, sharing predicted interacting residues with reference drugs. Furthermore, the fraction significantly reduces newly infected target cells in the cell-to-cell transmission model compared to untreated controls. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that 45% MCX Oats fraction exhibits potent antiviral activity against cross-clade antiviral activity against HIV-1 Gag-Pro chimeras and limits viral transmission in vitro, supporting further bioassay-guided isolation of its active constituents.

articles.title: Association of hypertension with cognitive function in Turkish hypertensive patients: A cross-sectional study.
Displayed CTDIvolume accuracy in ultra-low-dose CT: Limitations of current IEC criteria and a proposal for new constancy benchmarks.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Rapid adoption of ultra-low-dose CT protocols (∼1-2 mGy) used in paediatric cardiac CT examinations challenges current quality control (QC). The IEC 61223-3-5 constancy criterion for CTDIvol display accuracy ("±20% or ±1 mGy") permits up to ±100% relative error at 1.0 mGy, undermining patient dose management and early detection of equipment anomalies. This study evaluates ultra-low-dose display accuracy and proposes revised QC benchmarks.

METHODS: CTDIvol accuracy was evaluated across two state-of-the-art CT systems using a cylindrical polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) phantom with a 32 cm-diameter and a 15 cm-length and a calibrated semiconductor detector. Measurements ranged from 10 to 0.5 mGy (120, 100, and 80 kV), utilizing synchronized and asynchronous rotational exposure methods to ensure geometric reproducibility.

RESULTS: Measured doses remained within a ±20% relative tolerance across a tested range from 0.5 mGy to 10.3 mGy, proving precise control is achievable in the ultra-low-dose range. However, system-specific discrepancies were identified, with manufacturers showing distinct overestimation or underestimation tendencies. Crucially, applying the ±1 mGy absolute tolerance below 5.0 mGy permitted exponentially increasing relative errors, effectively nullifying fundamental QC objectives.

CONCLUSION: The ±1 mGy absolute constancy criterion loses effectiveness in the ultra-low-dose regime, creating a critical latent risk for undetected equipment degradation. International QC standards urgently require revision to ensure reliable dose monitoring.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: We propose establishing a "low-dose boundary value" at 5.0 mGy. Above this threshold, the existing ±1 mGy criterion applies; below it, a uniform ±20% relative tolerance is strictly enforced. This provides a robust, backward-compatible QC framework for low-dose CT, highlighting the need to recognize manufacturer-dependent display uncertainties during protocol optimization.

articles.title: When representations compete: Teacher cognition and instructional tensions in dual numeral systems.
articles.abstract: The coexistence of Arabic-Indic (٠-٩) and Western Arabic (0-9) numeral systems creates representational complexity that teachers must navigate in educational settings. This study explores how mathematics teachers interpret and respond to this complexity, with particular attention to cognitive, instructional, and sociocultural considerations in the Saudi context. A convergent mixed-methods design was employed involving 207 mathematics teachers. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, while qualitative responses were examined through thematic analysis. Findings revealed variation in teachers' awareness of dual numeral systems, ranging from informed and contextualized understandings to more fragmented interpretations. Participants described several factors that they perceived as increasing cognitive demands for learners, including symbolic confusion, representational duplication, directional processing, and inconsistencies between instructional and assessment contexts. At the same time, some educators emphasized potential benefits related to cognitive flexibility and adaptation to diverse learning environments. Integrating quantitative and qualitative findings suggests that teachers differ not only in how they evaluate dual numeral systems but also in how they interpret their cognitive, instructional, and cultural significance. Interpreted through the lens of Cognitive Load Theory, the findings suggest that representational directionality and contextual misalignment may be perceived as factors that contribute to cognitive demands in environments involving multiple symbolic systems. The study highlights the role of teacher cognition in shaping how representational complexity is understood and managed in classroom practice.

articles.title: Machine Learning Reveals Prognostic Value of Medical History in Suspected Coronary Artery Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Risk stratification in suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) relies on clinical history and imaging, but longitudinal medical history may provide additional prognostic information.

OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated whether machine learning models using 10-year historical registry data improves prediction of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) beyond demographics and stress perfusion cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) in patients with suspected CAD.

METHODS: A total of 2,159 patients (65 ± 12 years, 44% women) undergoing stress perfusion CMR were included. Models used demographics, CMR findings, and registry diagnoses and procedures from the prior 10 years. MACE was defined as cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or coronary intervention. Random Forest models were used for binary prediction, and Random Survival Forests (RSF) and penalized Ridge Cox regression for time-to-event analysis.

RESULTS: During 2.7 ± 0.9 years of follow-up, 212 patients (9.8%) experienced MACE. For binary prediction, the area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.66 (95% CI: 0.62-0.69) using demographics and 0.72 (95% CI: 0.68-0.75; P = 0.001) after adding historical registry data. The full model achieved an AUROC of 0.82 (95% CI: 0.79-0.85) and outperformed the demographics-plus-CMR model (AUROC: 0.81; 95% CI: 0.78-0.84; ΔAUROC: 0.014; 95% CI: 0.002-0.027; P = 0.029). In time-to-event analysis, RSF and Cox regression performed similarly using demographics and CMR (concordance index [C-index] 0.80 for both; P = 0.546). After including registry data RSF achieved a C-index of 0.81 (P = 0.144), and Cox performance decreased to C-index 0.77 (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with suspected CAD, machine learning models using 10-year historical registry data have the potential to improve prognostic risk prediction beyond demographics and stress perfusion CMR.

articles.title: Advanced Age in Acute Myocardial Infarction-Related Cardiogenic Shock by Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Status.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains a leading cause of in-hospital mortality in acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Although advanced age is associated with worse outcomes, associations across out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) strata remain incompletely characterized.

OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to evaluate the association between octogenarian status and in-hospital mortality in patients with AMI-related CS (AMI-CS) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and to examine this association in analyses stratified by OHCA status.

METHODS: We analyzed patients with AMI-CS enrolled in the multicenter Kanagawa-ACuTe cardIoVascular rEgistry who underwent PCI. Octogenarian status (≥80 years) was the primary exposure. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate associations with in-hospital mortality, with additional analyses stratified by OHCA status.

RESULTS: Among 658 patients, 177 (26.9%) were octogenarians, and 279 (42.4%) died during hospitalization. Octogenarian status was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR: 2.14; 95% CI: 1.32-3.48; P = 0.002). In stratified analyses, octogenarian status was associated with higher mortality among patients without OHCA, whereas no statistically significant association was observed among those with OHCA. The interaction between octogenarian status and OHCA was not statistically significant (P for interaction = 0.422). Higher heart rate, unmeasurable heart rate, higher serum creatinine, and lower serum albumin were independently associated with mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with AMI-CS undergoing PCI, octogenarian status was independently associated with in-hospital mortality. Although estimates differed numerically across OHCA strata, the interaction was not statistically significant, precluding a conclusion that the association differed according to OHCA status. These stratified findings should therefore be regarded as hypothesis-generating. Chronological age should be considered within a comprehensive clinical assessment rather than in isolation.

articles.title: Geninthiocin promotes RIG-I-mediated anti-RNA viral signaling responses.
articles.abstract: RIG-I, the core RNA sensor of RIG-I-mediated type I IFNs (IFN-I) signaling, induces the innate antiviral response through recognizing RNA viruses. Upon RNA virus infection, RIG-I undergoes autophagic degradation to attenuate host innate immune response for immune evasion. Thus, we sought to discovery the lead compounds that promote RIG-I protein stability to enhance host antiviral ability. Natural compounds have a rich history for contributing to new therapeutic candidates. Up to now, there is rarely reported that natural compounds enhance RIG-I to clear RNA virus. By screening a natural compound library, we identified that Geninthiocin, a natural thiopeptide from a marine Streptomyces, potentiates RIG-I-IFN-I signaling to enhance IFN-I and antiviral ISGs expression through inhibiting RIG-I autophagic degradation. Both in human and murine cells, Geninthiocin promoted RIG-I-mediated IFN-I and antiviral ISGs expression upon Influenza A virus PR8 (IAV) infection or RNA mimics Poly(I:C) stimulation. In vivo, we observed that Geninthiocin significantly suppressed IAV PR8 induced death and enhance the expression of IFN-I and antiviral ISGs in C57BL/6 J mice. By performing molecular docking and biotin pull down assay, we observed that Geninthiocin interacted with RIG-I. Further, Geninthiocin repressed RIG-I autophagic degradation to positively regulate RIG-I-IFN-I signaling response. Together, we reveal the novel function of Geninthiocin in anti-RNA viral innate immune response by enhancing RIG-I-IFN-I signaling activation, which provides new insight in developing therapeutic strategy for IAVs or other RNA viral infectious diseases.

articles.title: Clinical value of video monitoring in seizure classification and medication decision-making: A questionnaire-based study in outpatients with epilepsy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical value of ictal video monitoring in refining seizure classification and guiding antiseizure medication (ASM) decisions in outpatients with epilepsy, and to examine the concordance between eyewitness descriptions and objective video evidence.

METHODS: In this questionnaire-based, single-center study, 525 patients with epilepsy who attended the neurology outpatient clinic of West China Hospital, Sichuan University, between July and September 2025 were enrolled. A self-designed questionnaire was used to collect demographic information, medication history, seizure types, eyewitness descriptions, ictal video recordings, and diagnostic classifications before and after video review. Patients with ictal videos were grouped by recording modality: mobile phone recording, surveillance footage, and video-EEG (VEEG) monitoring. Initial classification was performed without video; a second classification was then performed with video when available. Classifications were independently reviewed once by an experienced epilepsy-specialist neurologist, with final adjudication by a senior physician in cases of disagreement.Categorical variables were compared using the χ2 test or Fisher's exact test when expected frequencies were < 5, with two-sided P < 0.05 considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: Ictal video recordings were available for 159 of 525 patients (30.3 %). Among the 159 patients with complete pre- and post-video diagnostic records, diagnostic revision occurred in 32 patients (20.1 %). The most common revision pathway was bilateral tonic-clonic seizure of unknown onset (BTC) to focal-to-bilateral tonic-clonic seizure (FBTC), accounting for 46.9 % (15/32) of all revisions. A determinate final seizure classification (focal or generalized) was more frequent in patients with ictal videos than in those without (96/159 [60.4 %] vs 121/366 [33.1 %], P < 0.001). ASM regimens were changed based on video evidence in 19/159 patients (11.9 %), and 16 patients required subsequent readjustment. Diagnostic revision rates were 15.2 % (19/125) for mobile phone recordings, 36.8 % (7/19) for surveillance footage, and 40.0 % (6/15) for VEEG monitoring. Diagnostic revision was significantly associated with ASM regimen changes (χ2 = 4.22, P = 0.040). An eyewitness was present at consultation for 512/525 patients (97.5 %), and the diagnostic concordance rate between eyewitness descriptions and video evidence was 89.9 %.

CONCLUSION: Ictal video recording was associated with clinically meaningful revision of seizure classification and influenced ASM decisions in outpatients with epilepsy, with higher diagnostic yield observed for more professional recording modalities. Video evidence may help correct classification bias arising from reliance on verbal history, particularly in identifying focal onset.

articles.title: National burden and mortality patterns of adult brain compression in the United States: a two-decade analysis (1999-2023) using CDC WONDER data.
articles.journal: Journal of the National Medical Association
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Brain compression is caused by diverse groups of conditions and is a fatal neurological emergency. Despite advances in neurocritical care, outcomes remain poor. Our study aims to examine the national, demographic, and regional trends in brain compression-related mortality in the adult U.S. population from 1999 to 2023 using the CDC WONDER database.

METHODOLOGY: Our study analyzed the mortality due to brain compression in the U.S. from 1999 to 2023, using the CDC WONDER database (ICD-10 code G93.5). Data was stratified by ten-year age groups, sex, census region, race, and urbanization. AAMR per 100,000 was calculated based on the 2000 U.S. standard population. Join point regression was employed to determine the APCs and 95% CI.

RESULTS: Between 1999 and 2023, 103,151 brain compression-related deaths were recorded. The overall AAMR increased from 1.38 in 1999 to 1.53 in 2023 (AAPC=0.57, 95% CI: 0.23-0.91, p < 0.05). Males maintained higher AAMR than females (1.33 vs. 1.12). NH Blacks demonstrated the highest AAMR (2.02), while NH Whites exhibited the lowest (1.08). The highest CMR was observed in individuals aged ≥85 years. The West exhibited the highest AAMR (1.54), and nonmetropolitan areas experienced higher mortality rates than metropolitan regions (1.36 vs. 1.15). Sensitivity analysis excluding 2020 and 2021 demonstrated no significant changes in the overall mortality trends (p > 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Brain compression-related mortality has increased over time, with disproportionately higher mortality among males, older adults, NH Blacks, and residents of nonmetropolitan areas, highlighting the need for targeted and equitable neurocritical care interventions.

articles.title: Two pathways to pressure injury in the mechanically ventilated patient.
[Therapeutic Intensity Level Scale: Development and Use for Clinical Decision-Making in a University Hospital].
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and implement a therapeutic intensity level (NIT-Mar) scale in a hospital consortium and evaluate its use.

METHODS: Adaptation of a therapeutic intensity scale through an expert panel and subsequent evaluation based on a retrospective observational study in patients who died from SARS-CoV-2 infection between March and June 2020 in a university hospital consortium. The following were analyzed: clinical characteristics, use and change of the scale, consensus in decision-making, and concordance between the assigned therapeutic intensity level and the therapeutic measures applied.

RESULTS: A total of 210 patients were included, with 74.8% assigned a NIT. No significant differences were found in age, gender, or comorbidities between patients with and without NIT. Decision-making consensus was achieved in 87.9% of cases, mainly among professionals (77%) and families (72.6%), but only in 12.7% with the patient. In 49.7% of cases, the NIT was modified during hospitalization. Concordance between the assigned NIT and applied treatments was 85.3%.

CONCLUSION: The NIT-Mar scale was widely used from its implementation, facilitating decision-making in high-demand healthcare settings. Its flexibility allowed adjustments in therapeutic intensity according to patient evolution. This tool can improve communication between teams, care planning and patient safety.

articles.title: Recent advances in the molecular pathogenesis of Epstein-Barr virus-associated nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is a major etiologic factor in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). Although persistent latent EBV infection has traditionally been viewed as central to NPC carcinogenesis, recent evidence has broadened our understanding of the dynamic interactions between EBV and host cells. Host genetic and epigenetic alterations may precede EBV infection, establishing a cellular environment permissive for viral persistence. Within this permissive context, latent EBV gene products activate oncogenic signaling, with their effects further reinforced by genomic instability and epigenetic reprogramming. This evolving evidence has also challenged the conventional view that EBV in NPC is predominantly restricted to a latent state. Abortive or partial lytic infection may coexist with latency and contribute to malignant phenotypes, while emerging evidence indicates that productive viral replication can occur in a subset of NPC cells and clinical tumors. In parallel, advances in genomic, epigenomic, single-cell, and spatial technologies have uncovered additional mechanisms, including EBNA1-mediated chromosomal instability, EBV-induced three-dimensional chromatin reorganization, and intricate interactions between EBV-infected tumor cells and the immune microenvironment. Collectively, these findings support a dynamic model in which host susceptibility, evolving EBV infection states, and subsequent genomic, epigenomic, and immune remodeling interact to shape NPC development and progression. This review synthesizes recent advances in the molecular pathogenesis of EBV-associated NPC, with particular emphasis on epigenetic reprogramming and the emerging contribution of EBV lytic infection.

articles.title: Ultrasound assessment of the optic nerve sheath diameter in adult patients with suspected intracranial hypertension: A scoping review.
articles.journal: Australian critical care : official journal of the Confederation of Australian Critical Care Nurses
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to map how the ultrasound measurement of the optic nerve sheath diameter is performed in adults with suspected intracranial hypertension.

METHODS: This scoping review was conducted in accordance with the JBI Collaboration and reported following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for scoping review guidelines. Two independent reviewers searched PubMed, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL), Latin American and Caribbean Health Sciences Literature (LILACS), Nursing Database (BDENF), Cochrane Library, Scopus, Embase, Livivo, Web of Science Core Collection, and the CAPES thesis and dissertation repository. Grey literature included Google Scholar.

RESULTS: Of the 2019 records identified, 239 were included. Optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) ultrasonography is primarily performed in adults with suspected or at risk of intracranial hypertension, particularly critically ill, neurocritical care, emergency, and trauma patients. Across the included studies, patients were assessed in the supine position, with their eyes closed, using a high-frequency linear transducer in B-mode. The optic nerve is most consistently measured 3 mm posterior to the globe. The included studies showed variability in ONSD cut-off values suggestive of increased intracranial pressure. Lower thresholds, particularly >5.0 mm, showed high sensitivity (99%) but lower specificity (73%), whereas values between 5.6 and 6.3 mm tended to provide greater specificity. Studies assessing diagnostic performance reported favourable results for ONSD ultrasonography; however, heterogeneity in cut-off values, populations, reference standards, and measurement techniques precludes the definition of a universally accepted threshold.

CONCLUSION: ONSD is a viable, noninvasive approach for assessing suspected intracranial hypertension; it most commonly employs a high-frequency linear transducer in B-mode. The optic nerve is most consistently measured 3 mm posterior to the globe. However, variability in measurement techniques and cut-off values highlights the need for greater standardisation. Furthermore, the limited number of studies addressing the role of nursing indicates a knowledge gap that must be bridged to integrate ONSD ultrasound into nursing practice. OSF REGISTRATION: https://osf.io/m4ej9/.

articles.title: Comparison of artifact elimination strategies during postprocessing for the numerical assessment of localized low frequency magnetic field exposure of the hand.
articles.abstract: Numerical computations of induced electric field strength Eiinside the human body are prone to so-called "staircasing errors", i.e., physically incorrect local enhancements of the computed Eiate such numerical artifacts, ICNIRP suggested in their 2010 guidelines to use the 99thpercentile of the distribution of the 2 x 2 x 2 mm3at the edges of the cubical cells. Similar artifacts can occur due to imperfections in the anatomical body models used. In order to elimin averaged induced electric field strength Ei,avg for comparison with the basic restrictions instead of the maximum computed Ei,avgvalue. However, this suggestion was based on very early computational studies using anatomical body models with relatively low spatial resolution. Moreover, a 99thpercentile-based assessment of Ei,avgappears generally questionable in case of highly localized exposure scenarios, where large fractions of the body remain almost unexposed, and therefore true local hot spots of Ei,avg that should be considered may be excluded from the analysis, simply because the exposed tissue fraction is less than 1 % of the total body volume. Although this problem has been repeatedly pointed out by several research groups in the past, the 99thpercentile-based assessment unfortunately spread out as a "general rule" into some guidelines for exposure assessment. Consequently, the compliance of many devices on the market with exposure limits can be questioned. In this paper we are quantifying the potential underestimation of exposure when using the 99thpercentile-based Ei,avg for several representative scenarios of a highly localized magnetic field exposure of the hand using a state-of-the-art anatomical body model. Besides comparing the 99thpercentile-based Ei,avg values with values obtained when using higher percentiles, we also compare with Ei,avgvalues obtained by applying a statistics-based outlier elimination method proposed by Arduino et al. (2020). Our results clearly demonstrate the inappropriateness of the 99th percentile-based assessment, as it may lead to underestimations of the actual induced Ei,avgby more than a factor of 100, depending on the exposure scenario. In contrast, the statistics-based artifact elimination strategy proves to be a reasonable and robust method for estimating the actual value Ei,avg for highly localized magnetic field exposure of the hand.

articles.title: Reliability and Validity of the Chinese Version of the Ocular Pain Assessment Survey (OPAS-C).
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Our study aimed to investigate the reliability and validity of a translated Chinese version of the Ocular Pain Assessment Survey (OPAS-C) across different cohorts of ocular surface diseases.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 175 participants, comprising 40 healthy controls, 38 patients with dry eye disease (DED), 46 patients with neuropathic corneal pain (NCP), and 51 patients with diabetes mellitus (DM). The OPAS-C scores were compared between the cohorts for each subscale. The internal consistency was assessed using the Cronbach alpha coefficients, and factor validity was assessed using exploratory factor analysis (EFA).

RESULTS: The NCP cohort had higher scores than other cohorts for most subscales, while the DM cohort consistently had the lowest scores for all subscales (all P < 0.05). All subscales of the OPAS-C demonstrated good to excellent reliability for all cohorts, specifically core ocular pain subscales such as ocular pain intensity (past 2 weeks and 24 hours), interference with quality of life, aggravating and associated factors (Cronbach alpha coefficients: 0.715-0.990). EFA revealed a 3-factor model with all questions loading strongly onto the model (factor loading values: 0.447-1.131). Factor 1 (ocular pain and related symptoms subscale) showed excellent reliability (Cronbach alpha coefficient: 0.974), while factor 2 (aggravating and associated factors subscale) and factor 3 (nonocular subscale) showed very good reliability (Cronbach alpha coefficient: 0.882 and 0.871, respectively).

CONCLUSIONS: The OPAS-C is thus a reliable and valid tool in evaluating ocular pain symptoms across diverse patient cohorts, offering a culturally adapted assessment by bridging linguistic barriers.

articles.title: Wearable IMU analysis and semi-supervised recognition of hemiparetic gait states and phases.
articles.abstract: Wearable inertial measurement units (IMUs) can extend gait assessment beyond motion-analysis labora-tories, but rehabilitation applications require interpretable measures and reliable event timing. This sin-gle-center proof-of-concept pilot study developed a wearable framework for post-stroke gait assessment, gait-event detection and phase recognition. Eight participants with post-stroke hemiparesis and eight healthy controls completed walking trials instrumented with seven IMUs, Vicon motion capture, and em-bedded AMTI force platforms. Vicon-derived kinematics, spatiotemporal measures, and bilateral sym-metry characterized the deficits represented in the wearable signals. The affected side showed reduced knee flexion and ankle plantarflexion, shorter spatial progression, and greater reliance on double support. Heel- and toe-marker trajectories generated labels independently of the ankle-IMU inputs, while vertical ground-reaction-force thresholds verified heel-strike (HS) and toe-off (TO). Only bilateral ankle signals were supplied to the classifiers; the seven-sensor setup supported labeling and sensor-location comparison. A target-contralateral lightweight convolutional neural network (TC-LCNN) classified healthy, unaffect-ed-side, and affected-side gait. A semi-supervised gradient-reversal Transformer-BiLSTM (SSGR-TBiLSTM) recognized background, HS, full-foot contact (FF), heel-off (HO), and TO, using weak-to-strong consistency learning, confidence-filtered pseudo-labeling, and gradient reversal to exploit unannotated recordings and reduce participant-dependent variation. Under participant-independent eight-fold validation, TC-LCNN achieved 99.66% ± 0.36% accuracy and 99.71% ± 0.31% macro-F1 with 16.93 K parameters and 0.145 M MACs per window. Under eight-fold leave-one-subject-out validation, SSGR-TBiLSTM achieved left- and right-side macro-F1 scores of 93.50% ± 0.98% and 92.40% ± 0.59%, respectively. Event-level precision, recall, and F1 were 97.90%, 97.40%, and 97.65%; 95.40% and 99.00% of timing errors were within ±50 and ±100 ms. Mean absolute errors were 15-19 ms for HS, 17-23 ms for TO, and 33-41 ms for FF and HO. These preliminary within-cohort findings demonstrate label-efficient gait-state modeling and more precise HS/TO timing, while supporting multicenter and closed-loop valida-tion before phase-triggered clinical use.

articles.title: EEPD1 Deficiency Drives Diabetic Kidney Disease Progression via Amplified Genotoxic Stress and Downregulation of EHHADH.
articles.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD), a major microvascular complication of diabetes, is characterized by oxidative stress and chronic inflammation that collectively promote cellular DNA damage and tubular injury. Although these pathological mechanisms are well recognized, the contribution of DNA repair enzymes to DKD progression remains largely unexplored. Here, we identify endonuclease/exonuclease/phosphatase family domain-containing 1 (EEPD1), a key DNA damage response enzyme, as a novel renoprotective factor in DKD. We found that EEPD1 protein abundance was significantly reduced in the kidneys of high-fat diet/streptozotocin (HFD/STZ)-induced diabetic mice and db/db mice (two widely used murine models of DKD) and in human proximal tubular epithelial cells (HK-2) exposed to high glucose. Genetic ablation of Eepd1 in mice exacerbated renal injury, fibrosis, and dysfunction in both HFD/STZ-induced and HFD-induced diabetic models. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses revealed that Eepd1 deficiency promoted DNA damage accumulation, inflammatory activation, and metabolic dysregulation, particularly through suppression of the peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation (FAO) enzyme EHHADH, at both mRNA and protein levels. Integrated transcriptional analyses and functional validation further identified PPARα as a critical transcriptional mediator linking EEPD1 to EHHADH regulation. Mechanistically, EEPD1 deficiency reduced PPARα expression, whereas PPARα depletion impaired EEPD1-dependent activation of EHHADH expression and promoter activity. Collectively, our findings identify an EEPD1-PPARα-EHHADH regulatory axis that connects DNA repair with peroxisomal metabolic homeostasis and establishes EEPD1 as a potential therapeutic target for DKD.

articles.title: Host resistance and pathogen aggressiveness vary along an elevation gradient in a wild plant-pathogen interaction.
articles.journal: Evolution; international journal of organic evolution
articles.abstract: Diversity in host resistance and pathogen virulence is ubiquitous in nature, determines infection outcomes, provides the raw material for antagonistic (co)evolution, and is fundamental to epidemiological dynamics. Yet empirical data on spatiotemporal variation of host and pathogen abundances together with measures of host resistance and pathogen virulence are rare. To address this gap, we surveyed host abundance and pathogen prevalence in four populations of a plant host and its specialist fungal pathogens along an elevation gradient. Using one of the pathogen species, we experimentally tested whether host resistance, pathogen virulence and aggressiveness vary among the study populations. Our measurements of infection success and severity across several hundred plant-pathogen pairs showed significant variation in both host resistance and pathogen aggressiveness among the populations, with resistance decreasing and aggressiveness increasing with elevation. Further, the high-elevation pathogen population produced the most severe infection on their local host population, whereas the low-elevation pathogen population produced the least severe infections on their local host populations. Our results reveal contrasting patterns between pathogen prevalence and key host and pathogen traits among populations along an environmental gradient, highlighting that shifts in pathogen distributions may reshape epidemiological and evolutionary dynamics between hosts and pathogens.

articles.title: Burden of pruritus in older non-dialysis CKD stage 4-5 patients: 7-year follow-up of the EQUAL study.
