authors: on be half of the EQUAL study investigators
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: Chronic Kidney Disease-associated Pruritus (CKD-aP) is among the top 10 most prevalent and burdensome symptoms in kidney failure, but little is known in CKD stage 4-5 patients. Therefore, the aim of this study is to investigate the prevalence, incidence, and burden of pruritus in older non-dialysis (ND) CKD stage 4-5 patients.

METHODS: The European Quality (EQUAL) study is a prospective, multicenter study involving patients aged ≥ 65 years with an incident drop in eGFR to ≤20 ml/min/1.73m2. Pruritus presence and burden were assessed every 3-6 months between March 2012 and May 2022, using the Dialysis Symptom Index with a five-point Likert scale. High burden was defined as a score 4-5. Cumulative incidence of pruritus was estimated with the cumulative incidence function.

RESULTS: We included 1 380 patients who completed at baseline the pruritus question (yes/no). Patients were observed for a maximum of 7 years. At baseline, 66% were men, mean(SD) for age was 76(7) years, for eGFR 17(5) ml/min/1.73m2, for serum phosphate 1.3(0.3) mmol/L, 41% had diabetes, and 47% had cardiovascular disease. At baseline, 53% reported having pruritus, and 26% experienced a high burden. During 7-years of follow-up, the average proportion of patients with pruritus was 55%, with a mean burden score of 2.8 (95%CI: 2.8 to 2.9). Pruritus status was dynamic, with > 10% of patients alternating between presence and absence every six months. Among those initially without pruritus, the 7-year cumulative incidence was 43% (95%CI: 39 to 47%).

CONCLUSIONS: Pruritus affected approximately 55% of older patients with ND-CKD stage 4-5, with one in four reporting a high symptom burden. Pruritus status was dynamic over time. These findings highlight the need for greater awareness among healthcare professionals and underscore the importance of timely recognition and management of pruritus, with the potential to improve patients' quality of life.

articles.title: Racial and Ethnic Differences in the Incidence of Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis Across the Age Spectrum.
articles.abstract: Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) is an inflammatory myeloid neoplasia with an annual incidence of 5 cases per million children <15 and 1-2 cases per million adults ≥18. Pediatric LCH incidence is known to vary by race/ethnicity; less is known among adults. Therefore, we sought to compare LCH incidence by race/ethnicity in the United States (US) across the age spectrum using data from the US Cancer Statistics (USCS) database. LCH incidence data (2010-2022) were obtained from the USCS database and stratified by age at diagnosis and race/ethnicity. Age was defined as childhood (0-14 years), adolescent/young adult (AYA; 15-39 years), and adult (40+ years); race/ethnicity as non-Hispanic White (NHW), non-Hispanic Black, non-Hispanic Asian/Pacific Islander, non-Hispanic American Indian/Alaska Native, and Hispanic. Age-adjusted incidence rate-ratios (IRRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using SEER*Stat. A total of 4,080 childhood, 1,399 AYA, and 1,819 adult incident cases with LCH were identified in the USCS database. Hispanic children experienced significantly higher LCH IRRs compared to NHW children (IRRHispanic_children_0to14=1.16, 95% CI: 1.08-1.24), while Hispanic AYAs and adults exhibited significantly lower IRRs compared to NHWs AYAs and adults (IRRHispanic_AYAs_15to39=0.74, 95% CI: 0.64-0.85; IRRHispanic_adults_40+=0.54, 95% CI: 0.45-0.65). A sub-analysis among childhood cases demonstrated the strongest effects were among Hispanic children aged 1-4 and 5-9 compared to NHW children (IRRHispanic_children_1to4=1.35, 95% CI: 1.20-1.51; IRRHispanic_children_5to9=1.16, 95% CI: 1.01-1.33). Hispanic children, particularly those 1-9 years, experience the highest incidence of LCH; a trend not observed in Hispanic AYAs and adults. These findings suggest differences in LCH etiology across the age spectrum.

articles.title: Immunosuppression Does Not Appear to Affect Echinococcal Cyst Viability as Confirmed by Immunoblotting Test: A Case Report in a Lung Transplant Patient.
articles.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.abstract: A 61-year-old Italian woman was diagnosed with a CE4 echinococcal cyst in the seventh hepatic segment. The cyst was managed conservatively ("watch and wait") as per WHO guidelines. Serology for Echinococcus granulosus (ELISA) was negative. Five years later, in September 2025, the patient underwent bilateral lung transplant for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Induction with basiliximab, steroids, and treatment with tacrolimus and mycophenolic acid was started. Serology for E. granulosus (ELISA, rapid test [RT], and immunoblotting [IB]) remained negative, and the patient was managed expectantly. Serology with ELISA, RT, and IB remained negative at 0, 1, 3, and 6 months posttransplant. The cyst remained unchanged at all time points. Although anecdotal, this finding supports the hypothesis that unlike alveolar echinococcosis, immunosuppression has no effect on the viability of E. granulosus cysts. This has important clinical consequences. The American Society of Transplantation suggests treating patients for cystic echinococcosis before transplantation, and for adequate candidates, it recommends surgical removal with perioperative albendazole, an approach not supported by the literature. The need for treatment or surgical management of cystic echinococcosis in immunocompromised patients should be reconsidered.

articles.title: Clinical Manifestations and Diagnostic Challenges of Human Taeniasis in a Low-Prevalence Setting: An Eight-Case Series from South Korea, 2019-2025.
articles.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.abstract: In South Korea, a low-prevalence setting for taeniasis, the clinical recognition of this infection remains challenging. Eight patients diagnosed with taeniasis at Chosun University Hospital between January 2019 and July 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. Clinical characteristics, exposure history, and results from stool microscopy, serologic testing, and molecular analyses, including multiplex polymerase chain reaction and 18S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) sequencing, were analyzed to evaluate clinical presentation and diagnostic performance in routine clinical practice. Clinical manifestations were generally mild and nonspecific, and most patients sought medical attention only after spontaneously passing proglottids. A history of consuming raw or undercooked beef was the most common route of exposure. Conventional diagnostic methods, including stool microscopy and serological testing, had limited utility, with stool microscopy successfully used to detect Taenia eggs in only two of six tested patients. Additional molecular analyses in the present study, including multiplex polymerase chain reaction and 18S rRNA sequencing, improved diagnostic confirmation and provided supportive phylogenetic evidence for species relatedness within the genus Taenia, including clustering of seven isolates near Taenia saginata reference sequences and one isolate near Taenia asiatica reference sequences. However, these approaches still lacked sufficient resolution for reliable species-level differentiation. These findings highlight that in low-prevalence settings, the major diagnostic challenge is no longer detecting taeniasis itself but reliably differentiating species, particularly excluding Taenia solium, which may affect decisions regarding further evaluation for cysticercosis or neurocysticercosis.

articles.title: IDF Diabetes Atlas 11th edition 2025: European prevalence and projections of CKD in patients with diabetes for 2050.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association

articles.title: Prevalence of anti-HCV and incidence rate of HCV seroconversion in a large multiregional health check-up population in China: a cross-sectional and longitudinal study of 1.6 million adults.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: China carries one of the heaviest burdens of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection worldwide. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of anti-HCV and incidence rate of HCV seroconversion in a large health check-up population in China.

METHODS: This cross-sectional, and longitudinal study used data from the Meinian health check-up database, covering participants from all 31 provinces of mainland China between 2017 and 2023. Serological samples were tested for anti-HCV using ELISA. The weighted prevalence of anti-HCV and the incidence rate of HCV seroconversion were calculated. Poisson regression was used to identify risk factors for HCV seroconversion.

RESULTS: A total of 1,610,735 participants were included in the analysis of anti-HCV prevalence. The prevalence of anti-HCV in the study population was 0.89% (95% CI, 0.77%-1.01%), with significantly higher prevalence found in females and elderly individuals. Geographically, the prevalence was significantly higher in Central and West China compared to East China. Individuals with abnormal liver function or liver fibrosis, abnormal thyroid function or antibodies, diabetes, and impaired kidney function had significantly higher prevalence. The analysis of HCV seroconversion included 179,447 participants, showing an incidence rate of 0.72 per 1,000 person-years during a median follow-up of 1.5 years. Risk factors for HCV seroconversion included older age, as well as living in Central or West China, border regions, areas with low GDP per capita, and areas with high anti-HCV prevalence.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study reveals significant anti-HCV seroprevalence burden and ongoing risk of HCV transmission in a large health check-up population in China, highlighting the urgent need for systematic screening and enhanced prevention efforts to control HCV transmission.

articles.title: Isavuconazole in the management of central nervous system fungal infections: Parenchymal penetration and clinical performance.
articles.abstract: Invasive fungal infections (IFIs) involving the central nervous system (CNS) represent a critical challenge, with mortality of 50% or more in cerebral aspergillosis, mucormycosis, fusariosis and cryptococcal meningitis, and pharmacokinetic (PK) access restricted by the blood-brain barrier (BBB). This review analyzes the clinical performance and parenchymal penetration of isavuconazole (ISA), a second-generation triazole. ISA exhibits linear PK, a cyclodextrin-free intravenous formulation, and high tissue affinity, favored by moderate lipophilicity (experimental logP 2.56) and in vitro inhibition of P-glycoprotein and breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) efflux transporters. Experimental evidence from animal models shows brain-to-plasma ratios of 0.42 to 1.8, indicating efficient BBB crossing. Human biopsy data show a fundamental PK dichotomy. While cerebrospinal fluid concentrations are restricted (about 1% of plasma), levels in fungal abscesses and inflamed parenchyma reach up to 5.11 mg/L, exceeding the minimum inhibitory concentration reported for Aspergillus fumigatus in those cases. Clinically, ISA was associated with a response in 70% of first-line (n = 10) and 73% of salvage-treated patients (n = 30) with cerebral aspergillosis, and 82% of 28 patients with CNS-only coccidioidomycosis improved or stabilized. Meta-analyses suggest fewer drug-related adverse events and, in randomized subgroups, fewer hepatobiliary events compared with voriconazole, although moderate cytochrome P450 3A4 inhibition warrants monitoring of calcineurin and mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) inhibitors in transplant recipients. ISA is a strategic option for high-complexity CNS-involving IFIs, serving as a therapeutic alternative in salvage and prolonged-maintenance settings, though first-line use in CNS infection awaits confirmation from randomized trials.

articles.title: Factors Affecting Health-Related Quality of Life in Children and Adolescents With Disorders of Sex Development at a Thai Hospital.
articles.abstract: BackgroundChildren and adolescents with disorders of sex development (DSD) face complex medical and psychosocial challenges, yet data on health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in Thailand remain limited. This study examined HRQoL, depression, and anxiety among Thai youth with DSD and identified factors associated with HRQoL.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted among 47 patients aged 8-18 years attending a pediatric endocrine clinic in Bangkok (November 2022-May 2023). Participants completed the Thai versions of the PedsQL™ 4.0, CDI, CES-D, and SCARED. Independent t-tests, one-way ANOVA, and Pearson correlation were used.ResultsThe mean age was 13.2 ± 3.2 years. The HRQoL score was high (M = 87.6, SD = 9.9). Anxiety and depression were present in 17.0% and 8.6% of participants, respectively. Higher depression (CES-D: r = -.63, p < .001) and anxiety (SCARED: r = -.41, p < .001) were associated with lower HRQoL. Participants with psychiatric comorbidity had lower HRQoL (mean difference = -14.7, p = .001). HRQoL did not differ by clinical characteristics.ConclusionsPsychological factors, rather than medical history, are the strongest correlates of HRQoL, supporting routine mental health screening and integrated care in DSD management.

articles.title: [Isolated persistent left superior vena cava: a rare presentation].
articles.abstract: Anomalies of systemic venous return represent rare congenital malformations, accounting for approximately 2% of all such cases. The occurrence of congenital heart disease patients exhibiting an isolated persistent left superior vena cava has been observed at a frequency of 0.07 to 0.13%. Due to their rarity, these anomalies are frequently associated with chromosomal abnormalities. These forms may manifest in isolation or in conjunction with other congenital heart conditions. The following report details a case of a patient two-year-old.

articles.title: Improving Mental Health Support for Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Mothers Through a Universal Screening Quality-Improvement Initiative.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To improve early perinatal mood and anxiety disorder screening for neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) mothers and facilitate timely referral to mental health services through the integration of a dedicated mental health clinician at our level 3 NICU.

METHODS: A multidisciplinary team convened to address barriers to universal maternal mental health screening in our NICU. Key drivers were identified, focusing on appropriate screening tools, availability of a mental health clinician, and a robust referral process should a mother screen positive. The primary outcome measure was percentage of referrals made for mothers who screened positive for perinatal mood and anxiety disorders. The process measure was percentage of mothers screened. Clinical characteristics were compared between mothers who screened positive and those who screened negative to ensure that any disparities identified were addressed in real time.

RESULTS: Since implementation of our universal screening program, 95.0% of mothers in our NICU have been screened for perinatal mood and anxiety disorders (an increase from 29.5%). Of those, 59.9% required referral for additional psychosocial support (an increase from 25.3%). Mothers who screened positive were more likely to be Black non-Hispanic (P<.001), and mothers who screened negative were more likely to be White non-Hispanic (P=.021). No differences were identified in delivery mode or breastfeeding at discharge.

CONCLUSION: A dedicated NICU mental health clinician, with multidisciplinary buy-in, may allow the successful implementation and maintenance of a universal perinatal mood and anxiety disorder screening and referral program.

articles.title: Association Between Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes and Postpartum Contraceptive Method Selection and Use.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether adverse pregnancy outcomes are associated with self-reported postpartum contraceptive use and method selection.

METHODS: We performed a secondary data analysis of data from the Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (phase 8 cohort, 2016-2022). The exposures of interest were adverse pregnancy outcomes, including maternal hypertension, diabetes, preterm birth, prolonged infant hospitalization, and infant death. Contraceptive methods were grouped into four categories: permanent contraception, long-acting reversible contraception, prescription-start methods (patch, ring, pill, or injectable), and patient-start methods (condoms, natural family planning, withdrawal, or abstinence) based on the level of clinical engagement required. We employed multivariable logistic regression to examine the association between adverse pregnancy outcomes and postpartum contraceptive use. Among postpartum contraceptive users, we used multinomial logistic regression to analyze whether adverse pregnancy outcomes influenced method selection.

RESULTS: In this analysis of 222,412 individuals, 32.7% of the study sample experienced at least one adverse pregnancy outcome and 77.4% of the sample reported using contraception. In weighted models, experiencing three or more adverse pregnancy outcomes was associated with lower odds of postpartum contraception usage (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.89; 95% CI, 0.82-0.97). Patients who experienced infant death had lower odds of using any postpartum contraception than those who did not (aOR 0.39; 95% CI, 0.33-0.46). We observed no association between experiencing preterm birth, prolonged infant hospitalization, gestational diabetes, or hypertension and postpartum contraceptive use. Among postpartum contraceptive users, experiencing at least one adverse pregnancy outcome was associated with a higher likelihood of using permanent contraception relative to patient-start methods.

CONCLUSION: Experiencing an increasing number of adverse pregnancy outcomes was associated with lower odds of postpartum contraceptive use. Adverse pregnancy outcomes were associated with permanent contraception use. Patient-centered contraceptive counseling and shared decision making to support patients in identifying and actualizing their postpartum reproductive goals are necessary in the wake of adverse pregnancy outcomes.

articles.title: [Right coronary artery to right atrium fistula treated by percutaneous closure].
articles.abstract: Coronary fistulas are rare congenital anomalies defined by an abnormal communication between a coronary artery and a cardiac chamber or great vessel. We report the case of a 5-year-old male patient (17 kg) referred for cardiac catheterization due to echocardiographic suspicion of patent ductus arteriosus. Coronary angiography revealed a fistula originating from the right coronary artery with direct drainage into the right atrium. Percutaneous closure was successfully performed using a COMED PDA 4/6 device. Post-procedural angiography showed complete occlusion without residual shunt. This case highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic role of cardiac catheterization in congenital coronary anomalies.

articles.title: The debated dilemma of the best choice among primary cardiovascular prevention guidelines.
International Cross-Age Consensus Guideline on Measurable Residual Disease Assessment in Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.
articles.abstract: Measurable residual disease (MRD) assessment is central to risk stratification, response evaluation, and relapse detection in acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). However, substantial global variability in its methodology and implementation persists. Differences in sampling strategies, detection methods, reporting thresholds, and interpretation criteria hinder cross-trial comparability and clinical standardization. To address this, an international expert panel representing major pediatric and adult study groups and reference laboratories developed consensus recommendations, using a structured current-practices survey followed by a multi-round Delphi process. Consensus was achieved on 38 of 41 statements. Recommendations span three domains: pre-analytical requirements, technical and nomenclature standards, and MRD-based remission and relapse definitions. Bone marrow was endorsed as the reference specimen for MRD assessment, and MRD was prioritized over cytomorphology in cases of discordance. Principles for risk- and actionability-guided late MRD monitoring, confirmation of MRD reappearance, and MRD-informed relapse assessment were also defined. Among the key technical consensus statements, a standardized MRD assay nomenclature was adopted. Areas without consensus-namely, anticoagulant choice for PCR-based MRD, interpretation of isolated BCR::ABL1 reconversion, and the exclusive use of MRD to define remission-highlight ongoing biological and clinical complexity. This guideline, applicable across all ages, provides a practical framework to standardize MRD assessment in ALL and support MRD-guided clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Nuclear Receptor Nur77 Orchestrates Hematopoietic Lineage Commitment to Avert Anemia in Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Anemia is a prevalent but poorly understood complication of diabetes mellitus. Here, we identify orphan nuclear receptor Nur77 as a critical suppressor of diabetic anemia. Nur77 expression was downregulated in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) from diabetic patients with anemia. In multiple diabetic mouse models, knockout of Nur77 induced anemia, a phenotype recapitulated by bone marrow transplantation. Mechanistically, Nur77 functioned as a transcriptional repressor in HSPCs, whose deficiency, together with diabetes-associated epigenetic modifications, enhanced chromatin accessibility and expression of genes involved in myeloid leukocyte differentiation. Consequently, this led to myeloid leukocyte-biased differentiation of HSPCs at the expense of erythroid lineage. Pharmacological upregulation of Nur77 with its agonist cytosporone B (Csn-B) effectively prevented anemia in diabetic mice. Clinically, Nur77 levels in HSPCs of diabetic patient negatively correlated with anemia occurrence. Collectively, our findings reveal a novel Nur77-mediated pathway in diabetic anemia pathogenesis and propose Nur77 as a new therapeutic target.

articles.title: [Atrial myxoma with endocarditis-like clinical presentation and neurological event].
articles.abstract: Cardiac myxomas are benign tumors that typically arise in the left atrium and account for 50% of all primary cardiac tumors. They can induce symptoms by obstructing blood flow, causing embolism, or producing general systemic symptoms. Cardiac myxomas derive from multipotent mesenchymal cells, which develop into a gelatinous mass. These tumors are usually solitary and pedunculated, often attached to the atrial septum via a stalk. Because cardiac myxomas pose a significant risk of life-threatening complications, such as embolism, heart failure, or sudden death, timely and effective care and treatment are essential. We present the case of a 16-year-old patient diagnosed with cardiac myxoma by histopathology. She presented clinically with cutaneous involvement consistent with systemic embolism secondary to suspected infective endocarditis. She was referred to a tertiary care center for diagnostic evaluation and to rule out rheumatological conditions such as lupus.

articles.title: [Myocardial fibrosis and ventricular tachycardia in myotonic dystrophy type 1].
articles.abstract: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 is a neuromuscular disorder associated with an increased risk of arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death, for which risk stratification remains a clinical challenge. We report the case of a 45-year-old woman with genetically confirmed myotonic dystrophy type 1 who presented with palpitations and dyspnea. Electrocardiography revealed sinus bradycardia and first-degree atrioventricular block, while Holter monitoring demonstrated a high burden of premature ventricular complexes and episodes of both non-sustained and sustained ventricular tachycardia. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging showed late gadolinium enhancement involving 29% of the left ventricular mass, with a non-ischemic intramyocardial and subepicardial pattern consistent with extensive myocardial fibrosis. Based on the overall arrhythmic risk profile, an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was implanted for primary prevention. During follow-up, no syncope, ventricular arrhythmias, or device therapies were documented. This case highlights the value of a multimodal approach to optimize arrhythmic risk stratification and guide individualized management.

articles.title: Climate, Air Quality, and Emergency Department Use in Northern Germany: Protocol for a Multicenter Register Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Climate change threatens population health through temperature extremes, air pollution, and altered infectious disease patterns. Emergency departments (EDs) are sensitive indicators of climate-related health impacts; however, comprehensive multicenter investigations integrating meteorological factors, air quality, and infectious disease surveillance across different health care provision levels remain scarce in Germany, particularly in maritime climate regions.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to characterize the impact of meteorological factors, air quality, and infectious disease dynamics on ED presentations across multiple health care facilities and care provision levels in northern Germany over an 11-year period.

METHODS: This retrospective, multicenter, observational study will examine ED presentations across 4 facilities representing different care provision levels in the greater Lübeck area and southeastern Schleswig-Holstein, Germany, from January 2014 to December 2024. Clinical data, including ICD (International Classification of Diseases)-coded diagnoses, patient demographics, and temporal information, will be linked with meteorological data from the German Weather Service, air quality measurements from state environmental monitoring, and infectious disease surveillance from the Robert Koch Institute. The primary outcomes will be daily ED visits overall and stratified by disease category (cardiovascular, respiratory, psychiatric, infectious, renal, neurological, and surgical/traumatic). Distributed lag nonlinear models within a generalized additive modeling framework will be used to characterize temperature-health relationships, accounting for delayed and nonlinear effects, and adjusted for temporal trends, seasonality, and infectious disease incidence. Subgroup analyses will examine vulnerable populations by age, sex, and socioeconomic status.

RESULTS: Project planning and conceptualization began in June 2024, and ethical approval was granted in July 2025. Following approval, clinical data were transferred sequentially across participating sites in July 2025, August 2025, and October 2025. Data from 3 of the 4 participating hospitals have been successfully received, while the final outstanding dataset is expected in the second half of 2026. Meteorological data collection was completed in October 2025 and air quality data in January 2026. While preliminary descriptive statistical analyses have already commenced, inferential statistics will be performed once data collection is fully completed.

CONCLUSIONS: This multicenter study will provide systematic evidence on climate-sensitive ED utilization in a maritime climate region of northern Germany. By integrating clinical, meteorological, air quality, and infectious disease data across 4 hospitals of varying care complexity, the study is well positioned to characterize nonlinear and delayed health effects of temperature extremes across a broad spectrum of acute conditions. Results are expected to inform regional health care capacity planning, early warning systems, and public health preparedness, while contributing to the broader evidence base on climate and health.

articles.title: Osteomyelitis Following Infrabrow Orbitotomy for Clinoid Meningioma Resection.
articles.abstract: The transorbital neuro-endoscopic surgical (TONES) approach to resection of tumors involving the superior orbit and skull base describes a minimally invasive technique that avoids larger craniofacial exposure. Described advantages include reduced brain retraction when compared to more extensive cranial approaches, decreased operative time, faster postoperative recovery, and improved cosmetic outcomes. Reported adverse outcomes of this approach include supraorbital nerve injury, eyebrow alopecia, visible scarring, and postoperative soft tissue infection. We describe the case of a patient who underwent infrabrow orbitotomy for a clinoid meningioma and developed orbital osteomyelitis postoperatively. To the best of our knowledge, osteomyelitis of the frontal bone following infrabrow transorbital craniotomy has not been previously reported.

articles.title: Berta, an Open-Source, Modular AI Scribe for Clinical Documentation: Implementation Report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical documentation is a major contributor to physician workload and burnout, particularly in high-acuity settings such as emergency departments. Ambient AI scribes have emerged as a response, but commercial products cost US $99 to more than US $600 per physician per month, operate as opaque systems, and often process data on vendor-controlled infrastructure. These characteristics limit organizational control over data sovereignty, quality improvement, and clinical workflows and create barriers to adoption in resource-constrained settings.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to develop an open-source, modular AI scribe platform that could be deployed entirely within institutional infrastructure, and to evaluate its real-world use across a provincial health system.

METHODS: We developed Berta, an open-source, modular platform that pairs a Next.js front end and a FastAPI back end with configurable automatic speech recognition and large language model components. A closed-source implementation developed in parallel with Berta was deployed at Alberta Health Services (AHS), Canada's largest provincially integrated health system at the time of implementation, and operated within AHS's existing Snowflake AI Data Cloud infrastructure. All clinical audio and text remained within the secure AHS environment. Use and session metadata were automatically recorded during routine clinical use by emergency physicians across AHS between November 2024 and July 2025, and physicians were emailed an optional survey. Operating costs were estimated from Snowflake service consumption over the same period.

UNLABELLED: During the 9-month study period, 197 emergency physicians registered at 105 urban and rural facilities used the system, generating 21,548 clinical sessions and more than 2700 hours of audio. Monthly session volume grew from 675 sessions in November 2024 to 5463 in July 2025. Mean recorded session length was 7.6 minutes, and 42% (82/197) of users customized at least 1 documentation template. Operating costs averaged less than US $30 per physician per month, representing a 70% to 95% reduction in cost compared with commercial subscription prices; this comparison excludes personnel costs for development and maintenance. Survey respondents (69-73 per item) rated user-friendliness as good (median 5, IQR 4-6), reported a median time saving of 16 to 30 (IQR 0-15 to 46-60) minutes per shift, and rated documentation quality the lowest. After the pilot, access was opened to other departments, and by September 30, 2026, approximately 2000 users had registered.

CONCLUSIONS: An in-house AI scribe can be deployed at provincial scale within existing health system infrastructure at a fraction of the operating cost of commercial alternatives while preserving data sovereignty and institutional control. The full cost of ownership and documentation quality require further evaluation. By releasing Berta publicly, we provide a reproducible foundation that health systems can adapt to evaluate and deploy AI documentation technology within their own secure environments.

articles.title: Behavioral Interactions Shaping the Use of a Mobile Health Intervention for Diabetic Foot Self-Care Among People With Diabetes and Caregivers: COM-B and TDF Qualitative Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mobile health (mHealth) interventions show promise for supporting diabetic foot self-care; however, sustained engagement remains a challenge, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. While educational strategies are commonly used to address diabetic foot ulcers, they often fail to translate knowledge into long-term self-care. Understanding behavioral mechanisms underlying mHealth use, including the role of caregivers, is critical for improving implementation and effectiveness.

OBJECTIVE: This study explored how behavioral interactions between people with diabetes and caregivers shape the use of an mHealth app for diabetic foot self-care.

METHODS: This qualitative explanatory study was embedded within a parent study of an mHealth app for diabetic foot care that was conducted in primary care settings in Peru. It used the COM-B (capability, opportunity, motivation-behavior) model and the Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF) to identify mechanisms relevant for intervention design and scale-up. Semistructured interviews were conducted with people with diabetes and caregivers about their experiences related to accessing the app. Data were analyzed using deductive and inductive thematic analysis informed by the COM-B and TDF.

RESULTS: In total, 14 people with diabetes (median age 54 y, 8 women and 6 men) and 10 caregivers (median age 28.5 y, all women) were interviewed. The app use depended on varying interactions between COM-B domains, while other behavioral determinants aligned with a single domain. Across domains, interactions between people with diabetes and caregivers also affected the app use. For example, caregivers often compensated for physical capability limitations through foot positioning or environmental adjustments. Environmental context and resources, including internet access, lighting, and device compatibility, affected the app use for all participants. Motivation for all participants was largely driven by beliefs about the app's preventive value, although reassurance from health professionals and altruism also emerged.

CONCLUSIONS: The app use often depended on collaboration between people with diabetes and caregivers as a dyad, rather than on independent users. This highlights the need to design digital interventions around caregiver demographics, competing responsibilities, and the additional responsibilities an app may introduce. Participants' preference for individual follow-up suggests that nonphysician health personnel and other human support may help maintain continuity and reassurance alongside digital monitoring. Although the app was an early prototype intended for algorithmic training, participant experiences provided insight into real-world usability and contextual barriers for future app development.

articles.title: Retrospective Mexican experience in the transcatheter closure of atrial septal defects using different devices.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Over the past decades, significant advancements and innovations have occurred in the field of percutaneous atrial septal defect (ASD) closure using transcatheter-based devices. The Amplatzer septal occluder has been widely used since its Food and Drug Administration approval in 2001. Studies have shown its high success rate in closing ASDs. Since then, many other devices have been developed and used with high technical success and closure rates, with low rates of serious adverse events and device-related complications. When compared to surgery, percutaneous closure provides a less invasive approach with quicker recovery and reduced physical and psychological impact.

OBJECTIVES: To demonstrate the effectiveness of using different devices for transcatheter ASD closure, emphasizing the success and complications obtained in our patients.

METHODS: Patients with congenital ASDs who underwent transcatheter closure using different devices were included. The primary endpoint was to determine the efficacy and safety of these devices and to determine the incidence of complications at follow-up. Two hundred and eighty-seven patients underwent ASD closure at a median age of 6 years (7 months-70 years).

RESULTS: Only minor complications occurred during catheterization. After a follow-up of 90 ± 67.7 months (up to 96 months), the closure rate was 98.6%, and the absence of atrioventricular block was 100%.

CONCLUSIONS: Transcatheter ASD closure using percutaneous devices has proven to be safe and effective in most cases. However, careful patient selection and follow-up are necessary to minimize complications and ensure optimal outcomes.

articles.title: Pooled prevalence of infectious diseases among first responders in the prehospital setting: A systematic review with meta-analysis by occupation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: First responders often work in unpredictable, uncontrolled environments, where exposure to infected patients and contaminated environments heighten the risk of communicable disease transmission. Their higher infection prevalence compared with the general population has driven the implementation of personal protective equipment, vaccination requirements, safety protocols, and infection prevention education. The aim of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to estimate the pooled prevalence of infections among first responders in the prehospital workers including paramedics, emergency medical technicians, patient transport staff, firefighters, police, and police officers.

METHODS: Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science and PUBMED/Medline were systematically searched. Pooled prevalence estimates were calculated using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation, with Freeman-Tukey double-arcsine transformation and back-transformation to the original prevalence scale. Heterogeneity was assessed using I², τ², and 95% prediction intervals. Meta-regression was used to examine potential sources of between-study heterogeneity, and small-study effects and potential publication bias were assessed using funnel plots and Egger's regression test. Risk of bias was investigated using the AXIS tool.

RESULTS: Following the initial search, 34,874 articles were identified, of which 88 were full-text screened. Of these, 22 studies representing 19,188 first responders were included in this systematic review. The pooled prevalences of hepatitis B and C were 6.2% (95% CI 4.5%-8.2%) and 1.8% (95% CI 0.9%-2.9%), respectively. Around 4% (95% CI 2.6%- 5.9%) of the first responders had MRSA colonisation. Current or past infection with COVID-19 among non-vaccinated first responders was 13.6% (95% CI 4.8%- 25.9%), which reduced to 7.3% (95% CI 3.6%- 12%) after exclusion of studies with high risk of bias. Of the known study characteristics, geographic region significantly contributed to heterogeneity, explaining 36.7% of between-study variance, p = 0.039.

CONCLUSIONS: Infectious disease prevalence varied across pathogens, occupations, and geographical settings among first responders. These findings should be interpreted in light of substantial heterogeneity and limitations in the available evidence but may help inform infection prevention, occupational health policy, vaccination strategies, and future research in first responder services.

articles.title: Patient selection for leadless atrioventricular synchronous pacing: clinical and echocardiographic predictors of sustained device-derived AV synchrony with Micra AV.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Micra AV leadless pacemaker allows atrioventricular synchronous pacing through accelerometer-based sensing of atrial mechanical activity (A4 amplitude). However, determinants of sustained atrioventricular synchrony (AVS) in real-world conditions remain poorly defined.

OBJECTIVE: To identify clinical and echocardiographic predictors of device-derived AVS 1 year after Micra AV implantation, and to assess the association between 1-year AVS and baseline A4 amplitude, and predictors of A4 amplitude.

METHODS: In patients undergoing Micra AV implantation, baseline clinical and echocardiographic data were collected. One-year AVS was evaluated in patients with ≥80% ventricular pacing using a device-derived index reflecting atrial mechanical sensing. Predictors were identified using MI-LASSO and stepwise regression with bootstrap validation.

RESULTS: 94 patients were included; high-degree AV block was the primary pacing indication (N = 88). At 1 year, 38 patients had ≥80% ventricular pacing; median AM-VP% was 82.9% (IQR 73.8-87.8) and AVS index was 83.1% (IQR 77.0-87.7). Predictors of device-derived 1-year AVS included older age, higher left atrial reservoir strain rate, lower right atrial volume index, and lower E/e'. For AVS, R2 was 0.80 (MI-LASSO) and 0.55 (stepwise). One-year AVS was strongly associated with baseline A4 amplitude (p < 0.001). Predictors of A4 amplitude included hypertension, absence of prior cardiac surgery, higher TAPSE, higher left atrial reservoir strain and preserved left atrial conduit strain rate.

CONCLUSIONS: Clinical and echocardiographic characteristics may help identify patients most likely to achieve sustained atrioventricular coupling with Micra AV. Markers of preserved atrial function, limited atrial remodelling, and lower filling pressures may further refine patient selection.

articles.title: Prehospital Whole Blood Resuscitation in Pediatric Patients: A San Antonio Cohort Descriptive.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The objective of this study is to describe the demographic, clinical, and prehospital care characteristics of pediatric patients receiving whole blood (WB) resuscitation by San Antonio Fire Department (SAFD).

METHODS: We conducted an observational retrospective cohort study to evaluate pediatric patients who received prehospital low-titer group O positive WB transfusion through the SAFD prehospital blood program between October 2018 and June 2025. The objective was to characterize patient demographics, injury patterns, resuscitative interventions, shock physiology, and outcomes among pediatric recipients in a mature civilian emergency medical services WB program.

RESULTS: Of 1703 WB transfusions, 73 (4.3%) were pediatric. Most patients were male (76%), age range 1-17 years old with a mode of 17 years, adolescents represented 78%. Trauma accounted for 96% of cases, firearm injury (74%); all penetrating (84%), blunt (12%), with the remainder classified as medical/unknown. Vascular access was intravenous (73%), intraosseous (26%). Tranexamic acid was co-administered in 39%; 12% received ceftriaxone. When analyzed using age-adjusted Shock Index Pediatric Age-Adjusted (SIPA) thresholds (>1.2 for 1-6 years, >1.0 for 7-12 years, and >0.9 for 13-17 years), based on the initial available prehospital heart rate and systolic blood pressure, 45% of patients had an elevated SIPA, 22% had a normal SIPA, 20% were pulseless and therefore could not undergo SIPA calculation, and 14% lacked sufficient vital-sign data for classification. Survival was 50%; died 39%, and unknown outcomes 11%. Mean delta shock index values were most negative in toddlers (1-4 years) -0.97 ± 1.29, followed by children (5-11 years) -0.76 ± 1.07 and adolescents (12-17 years) -0.16 ± 0.46, indicating a greater physiologic response to resuscitation among younger pediatric patients.

CONCLUSIONS: Pediatric WB recipients were predominantly adolescent males who sustained penetrating trauma and presented with moderate-to-severe shock. Younger age groups had larger descriptive decreases in shock index during the prehospital encounter; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small subgroup sizes and observational design.

articles.title: Neuroendocrine activation in the pathophysiology of Chagas cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract: Chagas disease is a zoonosis affecting 6 million people across 21 countries in Central and South America. Chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy represents the most severe form of organ involvement in the disease, characterized by a high incidence of arrhythmias, stroke, thromboembolic events, heart failure, and sudden cardiac death. Decades of research have focused on persistent parasitism, parasite-induced autoimmune processes, and inflammatory responses to Trypanosoma cruzi as potential mechanisms contributing to the degeneration of cardiac myofibers. In recent years, neuroendocrine imbalances involving the sympathetic nervous system, the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, and central T-cell tolerance in the thymus have been proposed as significant contributors to the pathophysiology. The roles of pituitary hormones, the pineal hormone, adipose tissue, and testosterone have also been emphasized. Thymic atrophy, mediated through caspase-dependent mechanisms, along with the aberrant migration of immature and autoreactive T cells into peripheral lymphoid tissues and the myocardium, are central features that likely act concurrently or synergistically with the already known mechanisms to drive the progression of the disease to its advanced stages. mecanismos dependientes de caspasas, junto con la migración aberrante de células T inmaduras y autorreactivas hacia los tejidos linfoides periféricos y el miocardio, constituye un conjunto de procesos que probablemente actúan de forma concurrente o sinérgica con los mecanismos ya conocidos, impulsando así la progresión de la enfermedad hacia sus etapas avanzadas.

articles.title: Tricuspid inflow E-wave velocity for the assessment of severe or greater tricuspid regurgitation: derivation and external validation of threshold values.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Current guidelines include tricuspid inflow E-wave (>100 cm/s by pulsed-wave Doppler) as a semiquantitative criterion for diagnosing severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR), despite limited supporting evidence. We assessed its diagnostic performance for identifying severe or greater TR, deriving and externally validating practical thresholds.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Tricuspid inflow E-wave velocity was measured by pulsed-wave Doppler in consecutive patients with at least mild TR between December 2024 and February 2026. Among 178 patients (77±13 years, 65% women), TR was mild in 44, moderate in 61, severe in 44, massive in 15, and torrential in 14. Mean tricuspid E-wave velocity was 56±16 cm/s and increased with TR severity: 47±8, 50±10, 62±16, 67±13, and 77±21 cm/s for mild, moderate, severe, massive, and torrential TR. Only three patients had E-wave velocity >100 cm/s (one with severe and two with torrential TR). Using multiparametric echocardiographic grading as the reference standard, the >100 cm/s threshold showed 5.5% sensitivity, 100% specificity, and kappa 0.25 for severe or greater TR. As a continuous variable, E-wave velocity discriminated severe or greater TR with an AUC of 0.81. A lower threshold of 52 cm/s yielded 81% sensitivity and 67% specificity, whereas 47 cm/s provided 90% sensitivity and 43% specificity. External validation resulted in 94% sensitivity and 47% specificity.

CONCLUSION: The guideline-recommended threshold of >100 cm/s is highly insensitive for detecting severe or greater TR. Lower cut-offs, particularly 47 cm/s, may be useful for screening to trigger a comprehensive multiparametric assessment.

articles.title: Chronic kidney disease in heart failure: results from an Ecuadorian registry.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Heart failure (HF) frequently coexists with chronic kidney disease (CKD), a combination that is associated with worse outcomes. Data from Ecuador remain limited. We estimated the prevalence of CKD among patients with HF and described prognostic impact according to left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF).

METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted using a single-center HF registry in Ecuador. CKD was defined as an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) < 60 mL/min/1.73m2. HF was categorized by LVEF into reduced (HF with reduced ejection fraction [HFrEF], ≤ 40%), mildly reduced (HF with mildly reduced ejection fraction [HFmrEF], 41-49%), and preserved (HF with preserved ejection fraction [HFpEF], ≥ 50%). The median follow-up was 2.28 years.

RESULTS: Among 706 patients (age 69.9 ± 13.3 years; 31.4% women), 50.3% had an eGFR ≥ 60, 33.1% had an eGFR of 30-59, and 16.6% had an eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m2. CKD prevalence was 57.8% in HFrEF, 41.8% in HFmrEF, and 53.5% in HFpEF (p = 0.003). CKD patients were older and had higher rates of hypertension (HT), atrial fibrillation, and cerebrovascular disease, with higher NT-proBNP levels, larger diastolic diameters, lower LVEF, more tricuspid regurgitation, and pulmonary HT (all p < 0.05). CKD was associated with increased all-cause mortality (49.3 vs. 26.8%), cardiovascular mortality (28.8 vs. 11.8%), all-cause hospitalizations (47.6 vs. 25.9%), and HF hospitalizations (22.2 vs. 11.0%). Predictors of mortality were LVEF ≤ 40% (Hazard ratio [HR] 1.5, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.1-2.2; p = 0.048), moderate/severe tricuspid regurgitation (HR 1.6, 95% CI 1.1-2.2; p = 0.008), and prior HF hospitalization (HR 2.2, 95% CI 1.6-3.1; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: CKD was highly prevalent among patients with HF, particularly among those with LVEF < 50%. Its presence was associated with a more adverse clinical and echocardiographic profile, as well as higher hospitalization, all-cause mortality, and cardiovascular mortality.

articles.title: Mind the Gap: Reframing Global Stroke Prevention Through the Hypertension Care Cascade.

Early ambulatory re-evaluation and follow-up of patients admitted in the acute cardiac care unit - Practical aspects on ambulatory follow-up of acute care patients: acute coronary syndromes, heart failure, ventricular arrhythmias, atrial arrhythmias, conductance disorders, myocarditis, pericarditis, other acute cardiac settings A Clinical Consensus Statement of the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care of the ESC.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
articles.abstract: Early, structured ambulatory follow-up after hospitalization for acute cardiac events remains a key unmet need in cardiovascular care. This clinical consensus statement of the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care of the ESC provides pragmatic, condition-specific guidance on post discharge management and (early) ambulatory re-evaluation for patients admitted to an acute cardiac care unit. It complements existing disease-oriented guidelines by focusing on the vulnerable transition from hospital to home rather than on acute in-hospital treatment. The document first defines key concepts and outlines general principles regarding timing, content, and organization of the first post-discharge contacts, including risk stratification, medication reconciliation, symptom assessment, evaluation of psychosocial status and comorbidities, patient and family education, and integration of cardiac rehabilitation. In practice, the consensus statement discusses the patient's path after discharge: how should the follow-up team look like, when should the first and subsequent visits be planned, what should be done at each contact, and how can multidisciplinary teams and hybrid (in-person plus remote) models be implemented according to local resources. Supplementary material highlights major evidence gaps, including the optimal timing and intensity of follow-up, the composition of ambulatory teams, the role of telemonitoring and digital health, and the needs of vulnerable populations. Overall, this consensus aims to support clinicians in designing structured, individualized, and scalable ambulatory pathways after acute cardiac care.

articles.title: Participatory Development of a Digital Self-Management Intervention for Intensive Care Recovery: Multimethod Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite promising developments in eHealth, a critical gap remains in understanding how to design and implement digital self-management interventions that effectively align with users' needs and the complex context of recovery after treatment in the intensive care unit (ICU).

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and iteratively refine a digital self-management intervention for post-intensive care recovery and to explore related user experiences and usability among individuals with lived ICU experience.

METHODS: A multimethod participatory development process was used including individuals with lived ICU experience (both survivors and family members) and health care professionals involved in ICU recovery. Between April 2022 and July 2026, guided by the Center for eHealth Research and Disease Management Roadmap consisting of 5 phases, data were collected through inspiration sessions and feedback rounds, individual interviews, usability testing, and pilot use, with qualitative data analyzed thematically and quantitative data analyzed descriptively. Findings from each phase informed the subsequent development steps and were revisited when necessary. The study focused on the specification and iterative refinement of the intervention's core components based on identified values and contextual requirements, complemented by preliminary indicators of usability and descriptive usage metrics.

RESULTS: Through stakeholder engagement, key functionalities were defined, including structured recovery information, easy 24-7 access, and guidance in navigating care. Two digital self-management modules, the ICU-RecoveryPointer for ICU survivors and the ICU-FamilyCoach for family members, were developed comprising (1) structured information aligned with the different phases of ICU recovery, (2) concise information tiles with layered content for more in-depth background information, (3) patient-reported e-monitoring features, (4) tailored suggestions addressing recovery challenges and emotional processing, (5) an e-diary with a timeline summary function, and (6) a comprehensive content library. During the pilot phase, the ICU-RecoveryPointer reached 33 linked accounts, with 27 users logging in at least once, whereas the ICU-FamilyCoach reached 66 accounts, with 90 monthly unique-user observations. Usage was primarily concentrated on the information tiles, suggesting that users mainly accessed the informational content within the modules.

CONCLUSIONS: Two digital self-management modules were designed through a participatory and iterative development process, supporting individuals with lived ICU experience during the recovery trajectory. Preliminary user experiences and usage data provided initial insights into usability and engagement, while also highlighting the need for further evaluation before broader implementation.

articles.title: Development of a continuous-wave, fluorescence-based two-color O2 temperature and concentration diagnostic.
articles.abstract: Spatially resolved measurements of temperature and molecular oxygen concentration are needed to understand hypersonic phenomena such as vibrational relaxation, dissociation, and recombination. To address this need, the present work develops and demonstrates a two-color, fluorescence-based diagnostic capable of measuring both of these key quantities in repeated experiments. The diagnostic leverages a narrow-linewidth, continuous-wave laser source to probe the Schumann-Runge bands of O2 near 225 nm behind reflected shock waves. Measured absorption cross-sections and normalized fluorescence signals show good agreement with computational models, exhibiting an average discrepancy of 10.1% and 6.9% for absorption and fluorescence, respectively. Demonstration measurements show good agreement with expected post-shock conditions and exhibit average 2σ temperature and O2 number density uncertainties as low as 8.5% and 5.4%, respectively.

articles.title: Low Muscle Mechanical Power, Worse Clinical Outcomes? A Cohort of Patients on Hemodialysis.
articles.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: In older adults, low muscle mechanical power is an independent predictor of adverse clinical outcomes. In patients with chronic kidney disease, this has not yet been explored. In this study, we hypothesized that low muscle mechanical power is independently associated with increased risks of all-cause mortality and hospitalization in patients on hemodialysis.

METHODS: This study is a secondary analysis of the SARC-HD cohort, which enrolled patients from 19 dialysis centers across Brazil. Adults undergoing hemodialysis were assessed at baseline for relative muscle mechanical power using the five times sit-to-stand test (5-STSrel). Low relative muscle mechanical power was defined based on sex- and age-specific lowest tertiles (p33) of STSrel values (W⋅kg -1) whithin our cohort. All-cause mortality and hospitalizations were collected through a 24-month follow-up period. Cox proportional hazards regression was modeled, with adjustment for clinically relevant confounders.

RESULTS: A total of 922 adults on hemodialysis were included (48.6% ≥60 years and 61.5% males), with 12.8% mortality and 35.4% hospitalization rates. Low muscle mechanical power was associated with an increased risk of all-cause mortality, with an adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) of 1.67 (95% CI: 1.15 - 2.41), but it was not associated with hospitalization (aHR=1.08, 95% CI: 0.87-1.36). In a subgroup analysis of age, the all-cause mortality outcome was significant in patients ≥ 60 years, with an aHR of 2.19 (95% CI: 1.41-3.40), but not in young (aHR=1.02, 95% CI: 0.50-2.10).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients on hemodialysis, low muscle mechanical power was strongly associated with a greater mortality risk, particularly among older patients. These findings position low muscle mechanical power as a clinically and potentially relevant aging-related condition.

articles.title: Routine Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Versus Conservative Management in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: Coronary artery disease commonly coexists with severe aortic stenosis in transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) candidates, yet optimal revascularization remains debated. We meta-analyzed randomized controlled trials comparing routine percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) before or concomitant with TAVI versus conservative management. Major databases were searched through May 2026. Random-effects models calculated risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and evidence certainty was evaluated via the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation. Three randomized controlled trials (1156 patients; PCI: n = 579, conservative: n = 577) were included. Routine PCI was not associated with significant reductions in all-cause mortality (RR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.70-1.15; P = 0.40), cardiac death (RR, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.51-1.08; P = 0.12), myocardial infarction (RR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.45-1.64; P = 0.64), stroke (RR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.48-1.03; P = 0.07), or hospitalization (RR, 1.07; 95% CI, 0.87-1.32; P = 0.52). However, PCI significantly increased major bleeding (RR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.06-2.34; P = 0.02) and any bleeding (RR, 1.77; 95% CI, 1.27-2.48; P = 0.0008), while reducing urgent and repeat revascularization. In conclusion, routine PCI before or concomitant with TAVI reduces subsequent revascularization without conferring survival or ischemic benefit, while increasing bleeding complications. Given the moderate-to-low certainty of evidence, limited cumulative sample size, and clinical heterogeneity across trials, these findings warrant cautious interpretation and favor an individualized, Heart Team-guided revascularization strategy over routine PCI.

articles.title: Operationalizing Cardiac Xenotransplantation: An Administrative Playbook.
articles.abstract: As the field of xenotransplantation advances, institutions must navigate a complex landscape of nonclinical challenges to ensure safe and ethical implementation. This article presents a detailed account of the planning and execution of the first 2 human cardiac xenotransplants performed at the University of Maryland School of Medicine and Medical Center. Beyond the surgical innovation, these procedures required extensive coordination across regulatory, ethical, financial, legal, administrative, and operational domains. Drawing from institutional experience-including after-action analyses and interdisciplinary collaboration-we outline key strategies for Food and Drug Administration authorization, staff education, infection control, financial structuring, and communications planning. We also explore ethical considerations in patient selection and consent, emphasizing transparency, autonomy, and public health safeguards. This article serves as a practical guide for institutions preparing to undertake xenotransplantation, offering insights into the infrastructure and foresight necessary to support this transformative but complex medical advance.

articles.title: Impact of Removing the Mandatory Sobriety Period on Waitlist and Posttransplant Outcomes of Patients With and Without Alcohol-associated Liver Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This single-center study assessed the impact of eliminating the mandatory 6-mo sobriety requirement on waitlist and post-liver transplant (LT) outcomes among patients with and without alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD).

METHODS: Adult patients listed for LT from 2010 to 2023 and followed through 2025 were analyzed. Era 1 (<2018) required ≥6 mo of sobriety, whereas era 2 (≥2018) did not. Competing risk models compared waitlist outcomes across eras. Post-LT survival was compared across eras, followed by a subgroup analysis of era 2 ALD recipients stratified by pre-LT sobriety duration.

RESULTS: ALD listings increased (26% versus 42%), whereas non-ALD declined in era 2 (74% versus 58%). In era 2, listed ALD candidates had a higher likelihood of transplant (hazard ratio, 1.90; P < 0.001), lower likelihood of death/deterioration (hazard ratio, 0.48; P = 0.03), and shorter listing-to-LT time (204 versus 98 d; P = 0.004), whereas non-ALD likelihood of transplant, death/deterioration, and time-to-LT were unchanged. One-year post-LT survival was similar across eras, whereas 3- and 5-y survival were higher in era 2 (83% versus 91%; P = 0.01), driven by improved ALD survival with unchanged non-ALD survival. In a subgroup analysis of era 2 ALD transplant recipients, the <6-mo sobriety group had higher transplant Model of End-stage Liver Disease scores (34 versus 28; P < 0.001) lower unadjusted 1-y survival (88% versus 97%; P = 0.04) but similar survival after adjustment for Model of End-stage Liver Disease score (P = 0.29) compared with the 6-mo sobriety group. Recidivism, rejection, and nonadherence rates were similar between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Liberalization of sobriety policy improved access to LT and long-term survival for ALD patients without compromising non-ALD outcomes.

articles.title: Congenital syphilis requiring VA-ECMO: A case report.
articles.abstract: Congenital syphilis (CS) is a severe infection with a rising global incidence and potentially life-threatening neonatal outcomes. We present a late preterm infant exhibiting respiratory distress, hepatosplenomegaly, and systemic inflammation. Diagnosed with congenital syphilis at 12 hours of life, targeted antimicrobial was promptly initiated. Despite maximal medical management, her clinical course rapidly deteriorated into refractory shock, severe pulmonary hypertension, and multiple organ dysfunction. This necessitated venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO). The infant underwent 7 days of VA-ECMO, 19 days of renal replacement therapy and 23 days of mechanical ventilation before successfully discharging with multidisciplinary follow-up. This case underscores the devastating potential of re-emerging congenital syphilis. It also highlights VA-ECMO as a viable rescue therapy for refractory neonatal shock, emphasizing the critical need for early referral to specialized centers.

articles.title: SNAT2-mediated amino acid import maintains osmotic balance to restrain macrophage metabolic reprogramming and inflammasome activation.
articles.abstract: Macrophages undergo metabolic reprogramming during inflammatory responses to microbial infection, in part because of activation of the transcription factor HIF-1α (hypoxia-inducible factor 1α). Here, we identified regulators of HIF-1α-dependent gene expression during immune activation induced by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and during the hypoxic response using genome-wide CRISPR screens in cultured mouse macrophages. The small neutral amino acid transporter SNAT2 (encoded by Slc38a2) was a key inhibitor of HIF-1α activation and metabolic reprogramming in cultured and bone marrow-derived mouse macrophages in response to LPS but not to hypoxia. Inflammatory stimulation increased SNAT2 protein abundance and dynamically expanded intracellular amino acid pools in a largely SNAT2-dependent manner. Consistent with the role of intracellular amino acids as osmolytes, SNAT2 deficiency resulted in osmotic imbalance and aberrant activation of NFAT5, a central transcriptional regulator of osmotic stress responses. In turn, NFAT5 promoted nitric oxide- and HIF-1α-dependent metabolic reprogramming and augmented NLRP3 inflammasome activation under hyperosmotic conditions. Supplementation with organic osmolytes mitigated both the excessive metabolic reprogramming and hyperosmotic inflammasome activation in SNAT2-deficient macrophages. Consistent with the heightened inflammatory phenotype in vitro, myeloid-specific deletion of SNAT2 reduced bacterial burden in mice infected with Listeria monocytogenes. Together, these findings identify SNAT2 as a negative feedback regulator that restrains macrophage metabolic reprogramming and inflammatory activation by maintaining amino acid availability that supports osmotic homeostasis.

articles.title: Heterogeneous transfusion risk linked to variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease in a non-human primate model.
articles.abstract: Among the 178 cases of variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (v-CJD) in the UK, three were reported between 2003 and 2007 to be linked to a probable transmission through blood transfusion. With no further primary or iatrogenic cases observed worldwide since 2016, several countries are lifting - or have already lifted - deferrals for blood donors who have lived in the UK or, more broadly, Europe, to reduce the threat of supply shortages. However, the high prevalence of silent infection according to abnormal PrP in lymphoid tissues (potentially 100 times higher than for clinical cases in the UK) remains a concern in assessing the potential iatrogenic risk associated with long-term silent carriers for a disease whose incubation periods can extend over decades. In the present study, after experimental intravenous contamination of cynomolgus macaques with v-CJD prions, a relevant model of the human disease, we observed a highly heterogeneous intra- and inter-individual distribution of apparent peripheral prion replication in lymphoid organs that appears to correspond largely to the prion load in blood, the highest levels of which are detectable by amplification-based detection assay. In addition, several primates have developed unexpected incomplete prion phenotypes that escape diagnosis by current conventional techniques and could be intravenously transmitted to mice in the absence of a functional immune system. The peculiar prion strains associated with these atypical phenotypes would involve peripheral mechanisms independent of the immune system, different from those of v-CJD. According to our observations, conventional lymphoid organ prevalence studies may underestimate the true extent of healthy v-CJD carriers, and blood transmission risk assessment should not be based on epidemiological data alone.

articles.title: Public-Facing Visibility of Social Determinants of Health Content in Speech-Language Pathology Graduate Programs: A National Curriculum Review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Social determinants of health (SDoH) shape communication, swallowing, feeding, developmental, educational, and health outcomes across the lifespan. As speech-language pathologists (SLPs) increasingly serve individuals, families, and communities affected by social and structural conditions, graduate education represents an important point of professional preparation. However, limited evidence describes whether SDoH-related content is visible in public-facing speech-language pathology graduate curricula.

METHOD: This descriptive, cross-sectional curriculum review examined publicly available materials from 291 Council on Academic Accreditation-accredited speech-language pathology graduate programs in the United States. Program websites, graduate catalogs, course listings, course titles, course descriptions, and program descriptions were reviewed for SDoH-related language. SDoH visibility was coded across three public-facing locations: course titles, course descriptions, and program descriptions. Descriptive statistics summarized overall visibility, visibility patterns, explicit versus indirectly suggested SDoH language, course type, school or college housing, and geographic distribution.

RESULTS: Public-facing evidence of SDoH content was limited across accredited speech-language pathology graduate programs. Of the 291 programs reviewed, 45 included SDoH-related content in at least one public-facing location, while most programs had no identifiable SDoH content in the reviewed materials. When SDoH content was visible, it appeared most often in course descriptions, followed by course titles and program descriptions. Only a small number of programs demonstrated visibility across all three reviewed locations. Among programs with SDoH content, course type varied, with SDoH-related content appearing more often in required coursework than elective coursework; for some programs, course type could not be determined from public-facing materials.

CONCLUSIONS: Findings suggest that SDoH-related preparation is not consistently visible in public-facing speech-language pathology graduate curriculum materials. Although some programs explicitly or indirectly reference SDoH-related concepts, visibility varies by curricular location, specificity of language, and course type. Greater transparency and intentional integration of SDoH content may strengthen alignment between graduate education, ethical and professional responsibilities, accreditation expectations, and the needs of diverse communities served by SLPs.

SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL: https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.34930578.

articles.title: Modulation of Fe3+ homeostasis by African Swine Fever virus facilitates its efficient replication in Ornithodoros lahorensis and pigs.
articles.abstract: African swine fever virus (ASFV) can be transmitted through direct contact and, in specific ecological settings, by Ornithodoros spp. soft ticks. However, the cellular mechanisms that support ASFV replication in both porcine host and tick vector remain poorly understood. Iron is essential for cellular metabolism and viral replication, but excessive labile iron can induce oxidative stress and ferroptosis-like morphological changes in mitochondria. Whether and how ASFV exploits intracellular Fe3+ homeostasis to sustain its replication has not been fully defined. In this study, proteomic analysis of ASFV-infected PAM (pig) and OME/CTVM24 (derived from Ornithodoros moubata) cells revealed a marked reduction in ferritin/FTH1 abundance, suggesting that ASFV infection alters intracellular iron storage and availability. Further analyses showed that ASFV dynamically regulated labile Fe3+ levels during infection. At the early stage, ASFV promoted NCOA4-associated ferritin turnover, increased labile Fe3+ release, enhanced mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum contact, and induced ferroptosis-like changes in mitochondrial morphology. At later stages, ASFV restrained excessive iron-associated damage, thereby maintaining an intracellular environment compatible with continued viral replication. Pharmacological depletion of labile iron with deferoxamine mesylate markedly suppressed ASFV replication in both porcine and tick-derived cells, indicating that controlled Fe3+ availability is required for efficient viral propagation. Mechanistically, the ASFV-encoded protein pA151R interacted with NCOA4 and promoted autophagic degradation of FTH1 in a manner dependent on its intact LC3-interacting region motif. pA151R also impaired mitochondrial outer membrane integrity and disrupted MDA5-MAVS/VISA signaling. Deletion of A151R impaired the ability of ASFV to modulate Fe3+ homeostasis and significantly reduced viral replication. ASFV infection increased serum iron levels in pigs and caused abnormal iron redistribution and depletion in splenic tissues in vivo. Similar iron depletion and transient ferroptosis-like morphological changes in mitochondria were observed in the salivary glands of ASFV-infected O. lahorensis. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that ASFV exploits Fe3+ homeostasis through a pA151R-NCOA4-FTH1-dependent mechanism to support replication in host and vector cells. This study provides new insights into ASFV metabolic regulation and identifies iron homeostasis and pA151R-mediated ferritinophagy as potential targets for strategies aimed at limiting ASFV replication and tick-associated transmission.

articles.title: Timing of Anticoagulant Initiation After Moderate-Severe and Severe Acute Ischemic Strokes (TAMSS).
articles.abstract: Background: Optimal timing for initiating anticoagulation after acute ischemic stroke remains uncertain, requiring a balance between thromboembolic prevention and minimizing the risk of hemorrhagic transformation. Aims: To compare the safety and efficacy of early versus late anticoagulation initiation after acute ischemic stroke. Methods: Retrospective chart review at a tertiary medical center evaluating early (≤7 days from stroke onset) or late (>7 days from stroke onset) anticoagulation initiation for adults admitted to the Neurological Critical Care Unit between January 1, 2019 and June 1, 2024 with an indication for anticoagulation and a diagnosis of moderate-severe or severe acute ischemic stroke. Results: Primary outcome was a composite of major extracranial bleeding and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 30 days of anticoagulation initiation. Of 356 patients screened, 143 met inclusion criteria; 91 (64%) received early and 52 (36%) received late anticoagulation. Baseline demographics were similar between the cohorts. Primary 30-day outcome occurred in 12% (11/91) of the early and 10% (5/52) of the late cohort (P = 0.78). No differences were observed in bleeding events, recurrent stroke, embolism, or mortality at 30 or 90 days. On multivariable analysis, P2Y12 inhibitor use was associated with increased risk of the primary outcome (OR 5.241, 95% CI 1.295-21.206, P = 0.02). Conclusions and Relevance: Early anticoagulation after ischemic stroke was not associated with higher bleeding risk and may reduce hospital stay, suggesting that early initiation may be safe. Larger prospective studies are needed to determine optimal timing of anticoagulation.

articles.title: Does the Timing of Surgical Debridement Affect Outcomes in Septic Arthritis of the Native Hip and Knee? A Propensity-weighted Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Septic arthritis of the native hip and knee can cause irreversible cartilage damage and systemic illness. Because operative debridement provides source control, delaying it may permit infection to progress, potentially increasing the need for repeat surgery and the risk of death; however, evidence examining these associations remains limited.

QUESTIONS/PURPOSES: Is delayed debridement associated with increased risk of (1) repeat debridement or (2) 1-year mortality in septic arthritis of the native hip and/or knee?

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the Florida State Inpatient Database, a statewide, all-payer database that records procedures by hospital day and includes longitudinal patient identifiers. Between October 2015 and December 2022, we identified 3587 adult admissions involving septic arthritis of the native hip (n = 1014) or knee (n = 2573) treated with surgical debridement. We excluded 1% (42 of 3587) of admitted patients in whom the first debridement occurred after hospital day 10, leaving 99% (3545 of 3587) for analysis (hip n = 1001; knee n = 2544). No included outcome or covariate data were missing. In the screened hip and knee cohorts, the mean ± SD ages were 55 ± 17 years and 60 ± 16 years, respectively, and 46% (462 of 1014) and 34% (879 of 2573) were female. Debridement occurred on hospital days 0 to 1 in 51% (506 of 1001) of hip admissions and 59% (1510 of 2544) of knee admissions; the remaining 49% (495 of 1001) and 41% (1034 of 2544), respectively, underwent debridement on day 2 or later. Stabilized inverse probability-of-treatment weighting was used to balance measured baseline covariates. Weighted log-binomial regression was used to estimate adjusted relative risks (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Among patients with septic knee arthritis, debridement on day 2 or later was associated with a higher risk of repeat debridement than debridement on days 0 to 1 (13% [133 of 1034] versus 5% [72 of 1510], adjusted RR 2.40 [95% CI 1.81 to 3.19]; p < 0.001). One-year mortality also was higher after debridement on day 2 or later (11% [118 of 1034] versus 6% [88 of 1510], adjusted RR 1.54 [95% CI 1.17 to 2.02]; p = 0.002). Among patients with septic hip arthritis, repeat debridement was no different between those treated on day 2 or later and those treated on days 0 to 1 (11% [55 of 495] versus 7% [37 of 506], adjusted RR 1.43 [95% CI 0.95 to 2.15]; p = 0.09). One-year mortality also was no different between the hip timing groups (9% [43 of 495] versus 7% [35 of 506], adjusted RR 1.19 [95% CI 0.77 to 1.85]; p = 0.44).

CONCLUSION: Surgeons should prioritize prompt debridement of septic knee arthritis, and hospitals should implement coordinated pathways to avoid preventable delays. No timing-specific recommendation can be made for septic hip arthritis based on our findings. Larger multicenter studies with granular data on presentation, diagnostic aspiration, antibiotic administration, and debridement are needed to clarify whether debridement timing influences outcomes in septic hip arthritis and to distinguish preventable delays from those related to diagnostic uncertainty or the management of medical comorbidities.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, therapeutic study.

articles.title: Effects of Benralizumab on Clinical Outcomes and Small Airway Function in Patients with Severe Eosinophilic Asthma: A Real-World Study.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
