articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the real-world efficacy and safety of benralizumab in Chinese patients with severe eosinophilic asthma (SEA), focusing on small airway dysfunction.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analyzed SEA patients treated with benralizumab for ≥6 months. Outcomes included ACQ-5 scores, blood eosinophils, IgE, FeNO, spirometry, functional electrical impedance tomography (fEIT), and adverse events. ROC curve analysis identified baseline predictors of clinical remission.

RESULTS: Among 24 patients, blood eosinophils were virtually eliminated by week 4. At 6 months, patients showed significantly reduced IgE and FeNO, alongside improved FEV1, PEF, and MEF25-75 (P < 0.05). fEIT sensitively detected regional pulmonary ventilation improvements. Overall, 79.2% of patients achieved clinical remission at 6 months. Baseline eosinophil counts were significantly higher in remitters and strongly predicted clinical remission (AUC = 0.845; optimal cut-off: 460 cells/μL). Treatment was well-tolerated, with only one mild fever reported.

CONCLUSION: Benralizumab significantly improves asthma control, global lung function, and regional small airway ventilation in Chinese SEA patients. Baseline blood eosinophils serve as a robust biomarker to predict clinical remission and guide precision patient selection.Trial registration: ChiCTR2600121928.

articles.title: Distinct temporal patterns of liver immune responses to pathogenic and non-pathogenic Entamoeba histolytica clones.
articles.abstract: Entamoeba histolytica is a protozoan parasite that can cause severe liver disease known as amoebic liver abscess. However, only a subset of infected individuals develops invasive disease, indicating that host-parasite interactions are critical determinants of disease outcome. In this study, we investigated the clone-specific modulation of hepatic immune responses using non-pathogenic A1np and pathogenic B2p E. histolytica clones. Time-resolved transcriptome analyses (6, 12, 24 hours post-infection) in a murine model revealed distinct immune trajectories. Both clones activated innate immune pathways early after infection, but their responses differed markedly in magnitude and composition. A1np infection induced a rapid and controlled inflammatory response associated with antimicrobial activity and resolution-promoting signalling. In contrast, B2p infection triggered a stronger and more complex immune response characterised by pronounced cytokine and chemokine expression, activation of stress and redox pathways, and tissue remodelling processes. The B2p induced response exhibited features of excessive immune activation, accompanied by the upregulation of counter-regulation genes such as Ackr2. These findings indicate that liver pathology is not solely determined by parasite presence, but rather may also be influenced by the nature and regulation of the host immune response. Overall, the observed differences between A1np and B2p infections suggest that parasite-specific properties shape hepatic immune activation and may influence disease progression.

articles.title: evaluation of the performance of rapid diagnostic tests in point-of-care conditions for serological diagnosis of chagas disease in pregnant women in Colombia.
articles.abstract: Between 2022 and 2024, the National Institute of Health of Colombia and DNDi conducted a performance evaluation study on rapid diagnostic tests under point-of-care conditions for the serological detection of T. cruzi infection in Colombia. The main objective was to assess the performance of four rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) under point-of-care conditions compared to Colombia's official serological diagnostic algorithm based on enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). To achieve this, the performance of each RDT and combined algorithms (parallel and serial configurations) was determined. This was a prospective, observational, and analytical diagnostic study involving 771 pregnant women residing in Colombia. Whole blood samples were collected for rapid tests and serum for reference tests under standardized protocols. All participants were enrolled within the framework of the implementation of the Comprehensive Health Care Route and the Maternal-Perinatal Route of the Ministry of Health, and clinical and laboratory follow-up was guaranteed for all newborns and their mothers. Key findings revealed that the evaluated tests (STAT PAK, ADBIO, BIOLINE, and WL Check Chagas) achieved point estimates of sensitivity ranging from 88.6% to 97.5% and specificity from 98.1% to 100%. STAT PAK showed the best individual performance, and combined algorithms demonstrated promising results. Modeling of the simultaneous (parallel) use of rapid diagnostic tests yielded point estimates of sensitivity between 92.4% and 98.7% and specificity between 97.5% and 99.6%. In turn, serial models, in which a rapid test is initially applied and, if the result is positive, a second test is performed, achieved point estimates of sensitivity between 86.1% and 96.2% and specificity between 99.7% and 100%. Based on the results of this study, RDTs may be considered a valuable tool for screening T. cruzi infection in pregnant women. Selected combinations of RDTs, modeled mathematically from individual RDT results rather than prospectively implemented as diagnostic workflows, showed promising diagnostic performance. The use of RDTs for screening, combined with locally validated simplified confirmation strategies, could significantly improve access to timely diagnosis in rural and remote areas. Furthermore, it could substantially contribute to the widespread implementation of initiatives aimed at universal screening of pregnant women for Chagas disease in Colombia, thereby improving the control of mother-to-child transmission.

articles.title: Spatio-temporal clustering of dengue in Valle del Cauca, Colombia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dengue is endemic in Colombia's Valle del Cauca region. The precise timing and spatial scale of seasonal dengue transmission necessary for effective reactive interventions at the sub-municipal level across the 42 municipalities of Valle del Cauca remain unclear. This study aimed to identify spatio-temporal dengue clusters in Valle del Cauca.

METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: A retrospective observational study was conducted using individual laboratory-confirmed dengue cases, including residential geolocation and consultation dates, reported by healthcare providers to the Sistema Nacional de Vigilancia en Salud Pública (SIVIGILA) in 2022. Residence was utilized as the probable site of infection. Spatio-temporal clustering was analyzed using Kulldorff's space-time scan statistic to identify statistically significant dengue clusters. Results were mapped using R. As a second aim, the association between clinical and demographic characteristics and dengue hospitalization was evaluated. Of 3,964 dengue cases reported in Valle del Cauca in 2022, 2,232 (56%) were laboratory-confirmed. Of these, 1,973 occurred in the defined areas of the nine municipalities included in the spatio-temporal analysis of this study. We identified 28 clusters at the sub-municipal level, with radii of 0-0.98 km, lasting 1-6 months and containing 10-114 cases. Twenty-six clusters (92.9%) spanned both warm-dry and cool-wet seasons, and clusters accounted for 32.0% of spatially analyzed cases. 960 patients were hospitalized. Lower socioeconomic status (OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.07-1.57), enrollment in the state-subsidized insurance scheme (OR 1.74, 95% CI 1.41-2.15) compared with the contributory scheme, and age ≥ 70 years compared to ages 20-29 years (OR 2.47, 95% CI 1.51-4.04) were associated with higher odds of hospitalization.

CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: This study identified dengue clusters at the sub-municipal level with the potential to inform reactive dengue control interventions and demonstrated a disproportionate impact on socioeconomically disadvantaged populations and the elderly in Valle del Cauca, Colombia.

articles.title: Lymphatic filariasis risk prediction models: A systematic review of modelling approaches, predictors, validation practices, and methodological quality.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Risk prediction models are increasingly used to support Lymphatic filariasis (LF) surveillance, identification of residual transmission foci, and elimination planning. However, their methodological quality, validation practices, and translational capacity have not been systematically evaluated.

METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: To address this gap, we conducted a systematic review following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines to characterise the methodological approaches, predictor domains, validation practices, model performance assessment, and risk of bias of published LF risk prediction models. The review was not prospectively registered. Studies developing statistical, Bayesian spatial, ecological niche, machine learning (ML), or hybrid models to estimate LF prevalence, infection status, or transmission risk were included. Data were extracted using the Checklist for Critical Appraisal and Data Extraction for Systematic Reviews of Prediction Modelling Studies (CHARMS), and risk of bias was assessed using the Prediction model Risk Of Bias ASsessment Tool (PROBAST). Twenty-six studies published between 2000 and 2025 were included. Most studies were conducted in Africa and India and relied on spatially aggregated epidemiological and environmental data. Climatic (73.1%) and environmental (76.9%) predictors predominated and frequently co-occurred, whereas socio-demographic (57.7%), programmatic (7.7%), and vector-related (7.7%) variables were less consistently incorporated. Bayesian and spatial models were mostly aligned with expert-driven predictor selection and internal validation, whereas ML and hybrid modelling approaches aligned with algorithm-based predictor selection and cross-validation. Despite increasing methodological diversification, external validation (15.4%) and calibration assessment (7.7%) were rarely reported. All studies were assessed as having high or unclear risk of bias in the analysis domain.

CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: LF risk prediction modelling is methodologically diverse but remains predominantly reliant on internal validation. Limited external validation and calibration assessment constrain generalisability and reliability of published models. Improving external validation, calibration assessment, methodological transparency, and reporting standards will be essential for developing robust prediction models capable of supporting elimination verification and post-elimination surveillance.

articles.title: Contrasting vascular phenotypes of fatal Bothrops envenoming: Hemorrhagic (Bothrops atrox) versus thrombotic (Bothrops lanceolatus).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Envenomation by Bothrops species produces mainly consumption coagulopathy and hemorrhage, and exceptionally thrombosis which is characteristic of few species. These vascular complications are driven by distinct venom toxin repertoires. In the Neotropics, Bothrops atrox typically induces hemorrhagic vasculopathy through SVMP‑mediated endothelial disruption and venom‑induced consumptive coagulopathy (VICC), whereas Bothrops lanceolatus triggers a probable thromboinflammatory syndrome characterized by diffuse arterial and venous thromboses. Comparative clinical descriptions of these divergent vascular phenotypes remain scarce.

METHODOLOGY AND PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: We report two fatal events illustrating the contrasting vascular tropisms of these species. A patient bitten by B. atrox in French Guiana developed profound VICC, followed by massive intracerebral hemorrhage. Histopathology revealed SVMP-compatible endothelial disruption with perivascular erythrocyte extravasation. In Martinique, a patient bitten by B. lanceolatus presented early coagulation disorders, multifocal cerebral infarctions, myocardial ischemia, and multiorgan failure. Thrombus‑formation kinetics (T‑TAS) showed a time-dependent impairment of thrombus formation. These cases highlight the species‑specific vascular signatures of Bothrops envenoming: SVMP‑driven hemorrhagic vasculopathy for B. atrox and probable immunothrombotic vasculopathy for B. lanceolatus. Delayed presentation contributed to irreversible vascular injury in both patients. Advanced imaging, coagulation phenotyping, and histopathology are essential for delineating the underlying mechanisms involved.

CONCLUSIONS: These two fatal cases illustrate a distinct pathophysiological profile of B. lanceolatus envenoming, characterized by thrombotic complications, contrasting with the predominantly hemorrhagic phenotype typically observed in Bothrops envenoming. Early antivenom administration is critical to prevent catastrophic complications.

articles.title: PhagoCyt enables isolation of Salmonella-containing phagosomes and mapping of host and bacteria remodelling of the intracellular niche.
articles.abstract: Macrophages engulf pathogens into dynamic phagosomes, which many bacteria manipulate for survival. However, isolating pure pathogen-containing phagosomes remains challenging. Here, we developed a novel flow cytometry-based isolation and ultrasensitive proteomics approach to analyse phagosomal and bacterial proteomes from macrophages infected with wild-type (WT) Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium (STM) or a ΔphoP mutant at 30 min and 4 hours post-infection. Our approach provides higher throughput, requires lower cell numbers and quantifies more proteins than previous techniques. Our data reveals key host-pathogen interactions, showing induction of PhoP-dependent virulence factors and novel putative proteins that shape STM's intracellular niche. Moreover, our data indicates that bacteria-containing phagosomes recruit mitochondrial membrane for production of reactive oxygen species. These findings provide new insights into Salmonella's manipulation of phagosomal maturation and intracellular niche formation.

articles.title: High seroprevalence and risk factors for Toxoplasma gondii infection in Iquitos: A city in the Peruvian Amazon.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Toxoplasmosis, caused by the intracellular parasite Toxoplasma gondii, is a globally distributed infection with particularly high prevalence in tropical regions. Despite its high endemicity, population-based epidemiological data for the urban Amazon are scarce. This study aimed to determine the seroprevalence of T. gondii and identify sociodemographic and behavioral factors associated with T. gondii infection in the urban population of Iquitos, the largest city in the Peruvian Amazon.

METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: A cross-sectional study was conducted between July 11 and August 10, 2024. Serum samples were collected from 382 adults across four urban districts of Iquitos and tested using an in-house ELISA (sensitivity 98%, specificity 100%) for T. gondii-specific IgG antibodies. All 358 IgG-seropositive participants were tested for IgM antibodies. Bivariate and multivariable Poisson regression analyses with robust variance were performed to identify factors associated with seropositivity. The overall IgG seroprevalence was 93.7% (358/382; 95% CI: 90.8-95.9%), and IgM seroprevalence was 1.7% (6/358; 95% CI: 0.62-3.6%) among IgG-positive individuals. In multivariable analysis, age above 60 years (adjusted prevalence ratio [aPR]: 1.10; 95% CI: 1.04-1.17; p = 0.002), and monthly family income in the 372-593 USD bracket (aPR: 1.07; 95% CI: 1.01-1.15; p = 0.035) were independently associated with IgG seropositivity. Additionally, peri-urban/rural residence (aPR: 1.04; 95% CI: 1.01-1.08; p = 0.025) and use of river or rainwater as a drinking water source (aPR: 1.08; 95% CI: 1.02-1.14; p = 0.010) were independently associated with seropositivity, whereas living in brick/cement housing was negatively associated with seropositivity compared with wooden housing (aPR: 0.95; 95% CI: 0.91-0.99; p = 0.037), suggesting waterborne transmission and structural poverty as key environmental drivers of infection in this setting.

CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: This study documents near-universal exposure to T. gondii in the urban population of Iquitos, underscoring toxoplasmosis as a major public health concern in the Peruvian Amazon. Age, income level, and peri-urban/rural residence were independent predictors of seropositivity. These findings support the prioritization of surveillance and prevention strategies targeting older adults and lower-income households in peri-urban areas, alongside environmental sanitation improvements.

articles.title: The Influencing Factors and Their Mechanisms of Retirement Planning for Middle-Aged and Older Adults: Explanation of the Mediating Effect of Subjective Life Expectancy.
articles.journal: Journal of applied gerontology : the official journal of the Southern Gerontological Society
articles.abstract: Global population aging and delayed retirement policies make understanding retirement planning essential. Using 2020 CHARLS data (n = 7,163; aged 45-64), this study found that only 35.3% of participants had a retirement plan (mean horizon: 8.5 years). Chronic diseases such as diabetes and memory disorders reduced retirement planning intentions by lowering subjective life expectancy (SLE). Notably, non-agricultural employment was associated with a higher likelihood of retirement planning partly through higher SLE. Although non-agricultural workers tended to anticipate earlier retirement, their higher SLE was indirectly associated with later planned retirement. SLE may also be a relevant psychological indicator of retirement planning in other aging societies, although cross-national validation is needed.

articles.title: Current evidence of real-world experience with resmetirom in clinical practice in the United States: a targeted literature review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease is the most common chronic liver disease globally and progresses to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) in up to 30% of individuals. In 2024, the thyroid hormone receptor β agonist resmetirom became the first pharmacotherapy to receive accelerated conditional US approval for adults with MASH and moderate to advanced fibrosis (consistent with F2 to F3), for use in conjunction with diet modification and regular exercise.

AREAS COVERED: A targeted literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, and Europe PMC, to identify reports published in English through 31 March 2026. Congress repositories were manually searched through 30 June 2026.

EXPERT OPINION: Early real world data on resmetirom in the US are encouraging, with signals supporting the efficacy findings reported in the phase 3 MAESTRO-NASH trial. Clinical practice is shifting toward noninvasive testing for patient identification and monitoring. The MASH landscape is transitioning from being limited to lifestyle modifications to the availability of pharmacotherapy; real world use of resmetirom suggests a shift toward use of a liver-directed therapy to manage MASH.

articles.title: Eltrombopag in the treatment of immune thrombocytopenia secondary to SLE: A double-edged sword.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the efficacy and safety of eltrombopag in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)-associated immune thrombocytopenia, with a particular focus on thrombotic risk.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective cohort study of 23 patients with SLE-associated thrombocytopenia treated with eltrombopag. Baseline clinical characteristics, treatment patterns, and outcomes were collected. The primary outcomes were sustained platelet response (≥50 ×109/L at last follow-up) and occurrence of thrombotic events. Exploratory analyses assessed associations between antiphospholipid antibody (aPL) status and thrombosis.ResultsThe mean age was 33.7 ± 12.3 years, and 65.2% were female. aPL positivity was present in 52.2% of patients. A sustained platelet response was achieved in 65.2% of patients, and 21.7% were successfully weaned off corticosteroids. Thrombotic events occurred in 8 patients (34.8%), with arterial events accounting for 50% of cases. The median time to thrombosis was 5.5 months. Thrombosis occurred across a range of platelet counts and was not consistently associated with thrombocytosis. A higher proportion of thrombotic events was observed in aPL-positive patients (41.7% vs 27.3%), although this did not reach statistical significance (OR 1.90, 95% CI 0.33-11.01, p = 0.667).ConclusionEltrombopag was associated with platelet response in this cohort. Thrombosis was numerically more common in aPL-positive patients, but the small sample and imprecise estimate preclude conclusions about its independent contribution. Without a comparator group, whether these events reflect eltrombopag, the prothrombotic milieu of SLE and aPL antibodies, or their interaction cannot be determined.

articles.title: Temperature-dependent Pathogenicity and Host-associated Dominance Patterns of Colletotrichum spp. Causing Apple Bitter Rot in Korea.
articles.abstract: Apple bitter rot has intensified across Korea, yet the ecological processes shaping Colletotrichum populations in orchard landscapes remain unclear. We surveyed symptomatic apple fruits from four major production provinces during 2020-2023 and characterized 783 Colletotrichum isolates using ITS-GAPDH screening, morphology, and multilocus phylogenetics of 24 representative isolates. Multilocus analysis confirmed seven Colletotrichum species, while ITS-GAPDH sequence groups corresponding to C. siamense and C. fructicola predominated among apple-derived isolates and five additional groups occurred at lower frequencies. Surveys of orchard-adjacent black locust and walnut yielded 40 isolates from each host and revealed distinct host-associated patterns. Temperature assays were designed to evaluate fungal performance under favorable and supra-optimal conditions (20-40°C), rather than the complete thermal response curve. Responses were generally high at 20-30°C and declined at higher temperatures. Upper thermal 50% reduction temperatures (UT50) ranged from 29.66 to 36.58°C depending on species and trait, and no measurable mycelial growth occurred at 40°C. Fruit inoculation assays showed isolate- and cultivar-dependent variation in aggressiveness, with lesion development greatest at 20-30°C, reduced at 35°C, and absent at 40°C. Cross-infection tests with 27 isolates demonstrated bidirectional pathogenicity among apple, walnut, and black locust. Together, these results link host-associated community structure with species- and trait-specific upper thermal responses and highlight the potential contribution of surrounding woody hosts to bitter rot epidemiology.

articles.title: Contemporary Outcomes of Catheter Ablation of Long-Standing Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advances in mapping and ablation have improved the safety and efficacy of catheter-based ablation (CA) of atrial fibrillation (AF). Patients with long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation (LSPAF) historically have poor ablation outcomes; however, they are underrepresented in contemporary reports.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate ablation approaches and long-term rhythm control following contemporary catheter ablation for LSPAF.

METHODS: A single-center, retrospective analysis of patients undergoing CA for LSPAF between 2021 and 2025 was performed. Demographic and procedural characteristics were analyzed; 1-year arrhythmia free survival and atrial arrhythmia burden were assessed.

RESULTS: Ninety-five patients (median age 68 years [IQR, 63-73]; 80% male; median BMI 32.4 kg/m2 [IQR, 28.6-35.6]; median ejection fraction 55% [IQR, 49%-60%]; 37% with prior CA) were followed for a median of 20.2 months (IQR, 10.2-29.7). Radiofrequency ablation alone was used in 74 patients (78%), pulsed-field ablation alone in 13 (14%), and both in 8 (8%). Pulmonary veins were isolated in all patients, 88 (93%) underwent additional left atrial ablation, including linear ablation in 88 (93%), posterior wall isolation or ablation in 72 (76%), vein of Marshall ethanol infusion or ablation in 25 (26%), coronary sinus ablation in 24 (25%), and cavotricuspid isthmus ablation in 23 (24%). Fourteen of 92 post-blanking evaluable patients (15.2%) were receiving a class I or III antiarrhythmic drug at last follow-up. Among 57 patients with adequate post-blanking follow-up after a first AF ablation (of 60 first-ablation patients overall), 1-year arrhythmia-free survival was 39.3% (95% CI, 27.8%-55.4%). Among all patients and after allowing repeat procedures, 1-year arrhythmia-free survival was 53.5% (95% CI, 43.3%-66.1%). Among patients with continuous monitoring, median arrhythmia burden decreased from 90.1% (IQR, 21.1%-99.4%) before ablation to 0.0% (IQR, 0.0%-3.8%) at 6 months and 0.0% (IQR, 0.0%-20.0%) at 12 months.

CONCLUSION: In this contemporary cohort of patients undergoing CA for LSPAF, 1-year arrhythmia-free survival was 53.5% when repeat procedures were allowed. Among patients with implanted cardiac devices, arrhythmia burden was markedly reduced after ablation and may complement conventional time-to-first-recurrence endpoints.

articles.title: Predictors of Spasticity in First-Ever Stroke Patients.
articles.journal: Annals of Indian Academy of Neurology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Post-stroke spasticity is a common and disabling complication that hinders functional recovery. The aim of this study was to identify admission variables associated with the development of spasticity in patients with first-ever stroke.

METHODS: This prospective observational study enrolled consecutive adults with clinically and radiologically confirmed ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke within 7 days of onset, from July 2019 to September 2020. Baseline demographic, clinical, and radiological data were collected. The primary outcome was spasticity at 3 months, defined as a Modified Ashworth Scale score of 1 or higher in at least one affected joint.

RESULTS: Of 160 eligible patients, 149 completed follow-up and were analyzed. Spasticity developed in 106 patients (71.14%) at 3 months. In multivariable logistic regression, only the admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score was strongly associated with an increased risk of spasticity at 3 months (adjusted odds ratio: 2.17, 95% confidence interval: 1.53-3.07).

CONCLUSIONS: Simple bedside markers available during acute stroke management may help identify patients at high risk of developing spasticity. The initial stroke severity is the strongest predictor of subsequent spasticity.

articles.title: Diagnostic Utility of Kappa Free Light Chain Index in Patients with Multiple Sclerosis in India: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.journal: Annals of Indian Academy of Neurology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) kappa free light chains (KFLCs) are emerging biomarkers of intrathecal immunoglobulin synthesis in multiple sclerosis (MS) and have been included as supportive markers in the 2024 McDonald criteria. However, data from the Indian subcontinent remain limited. The study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of the KFLC index for MS and examine its association with laboratory and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) biomarkers.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, adults (≥18 years) with MS, inflammatory controls (neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease, seronegative optic neuritis), and non-inflammatory controls (idiopathic intracranial hypertension, normal pressure hydrocephalus) were enrolled. KFLC was measured in paired CSF and serum, and the KFLC index was calculated. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and associations with oligoclonal bands (OCBs), IgG index, disability (EDSS), and MRI biomarkers: central vein sign (CVS) and paramagnetic rim lesions (PRL) were evaluated.

RESULTS: Forty patients were included (22 MS, 12 inflammatory controls, 6 non-inflammatory controls) over six months. KFLC index was higher in MS (median 24 [interquartile range 9-54]) than in inflammatory (4 [3-10]) and non-inflammatory controls (6 [4-7]) ( P < 0.001). ROC analysis showed good performance (area under the curve [AUC] 0.855); a cutoff of 7.40 yielded 86.4% sensitivity and 72.2% specificity. KFLC positivity demonstrated moderate concordance with OCBs (κ = 0.55). KFLC index was significantly higher in patients with CVS and PRL but showed no correlation with IgG index or EDSS.

CONCLUSIONS: KFLC index shows good diagnostic performance for MS and correlates with MRI biomarkers, supporting its clinical utility in the Indian setting.

articles.title: Sertraline Administration to Prevent Intradialytic Hypotension: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Crossover Study (SLATAN Study).
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Intradialytic hypotension (IDH) is common during hemodialysis and is associated with adverse outcomes. Although sertraline may improve autonomic dysfunction, which contributes to the pathogenesis of IDH, its efficacy in preventing IDH remains uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial in maintenance hemodialysis patients with IDH in ≥25% of sessions. Participants received sertraline or placebo for 4 weeks, followed by a 4-week washout before crossover (total 12 weeks). Sertraline was initiated at 50 mg/day for 1 week and increased to 100 mg/day for weeks 2-4. Primary outcome was the incidence of IDH. Secondary outcomes included IDH incidence stratified by diabetes status, symptomatic IDH, therapeutic interventions, intradialytic blood pressure changes, and adverse events.

RESULTS: Thirty-seven patients were enrolled (mean age 64.0 years; 49% male; median dialysis vintage 24 months). In the intention-to-treat analysis, sertraline significantly reduced IDH episodes compared with placebo (2.5 vs 4.2 episodes per patient, p for treatment effect<0.001, period effect=0.607, sequence effect=0.577). Among diabetic patients, IDH incidence was lower with sertraline (2.5 vs 4.3 episodes per patient, p<0.001), whereas no difference was observed in non-diabetic patients. Sertraline also reduced symptomatic IDH (0.5% vs. 1.4%, p=0.036) and therapeutic interventions (5.2 vs. 8.4 events, p=0.001). Systolic blood pressure and mean arterial pressure at 1- and 3-hours during dialysis were significantly higher with sertraline. Adverse events were comparable.

CONCLUSIONS: In maintenance hemodialysis patients with frequent IDH, sertraline significantly reduced IDH episodes, particularly among those with diabetes, decreased symptomatic events and rescue interventions, and improved intradialytic hemodynamic stability.

articles.title: Early ventricular function assessed by speckle-tracking echocardiography (STE) in extremely preterm infants.
articles.abstract: ObjectivesTo evaluate the relationship between early speckle-tracking echocardiography (STE)-derived longitudinal strain and conventional measures of ventricular systolic function in extremely preterm infants and assess their association with mortality before hospital discharge.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included inborn infants born at less than 29 weeks of gestation admitted to a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit between October 2023 and December 2025. Standardised targeted neonatal echocardiography was performed within 72 hours of birth. Left ventricular (LV) and right ventricular (RV) longitudinal strain and conventional measures of ventricular function were evaluated in relation to mortality. Each measure was entered separately into multivariable models adjusted for gestational age and 5-min Apgar score, with bootstrap internal validation.ResultsAmong 144 infants, 32 (22.2%) died before hospital discharge. Infants who died had less negative LV and RV longitudinal strain and lower conventional measures of LV and RV systolic function than survivors (all p < 0.001). LV strain correlated strongly with LV ejection fraction (r = -0.811) and fractional shortening (r = -0.868), while RV strain correlated strongly with RV fractional area change (r = -0.898) and RV output (r = -0.780) (all p < 0.001). All evaluated echocardiographic measures showed high apparent discrimination for mortality (AUC 0.910 to 0.955; all p < 0.001), without significant differences between strain and conventional measures, and remained associated with mortality after adjustment (optimism-corrected c-statistics 0.915 to 0.964).ConclusionsSTE-derived longitudinal strain was closely associated with conventional measures of ventricular systolic function, while both deformation-based and conventional measures were associated with mortality; these exploratory findings require external validation. STE may provide a complementary component of early neonatal haemodynamic assessment in extremely preterm infants.

articles.title: Not all endothelium is equal: regional and sex-dependent roles of DDAH1 in regulating endothelial function.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.abstract: Asymmetrical dimethylarginine (ADMA), an endogenous inhibitor of nitric oxide synthases (NOS), is primarily metabolized by dimethylarginine dimethylaminohydrolases (DDAH1 and 2). This study used endothelial-specific DDAH1 knockout (DDAH1En-/-) mice to test whether reduced endothelial DDAH1 activity impairs cerebral endothelial function and worsens outcomes after cerebral ischaemia-reperfusion. Using male and female, DDAH1En-/- and control (DDAH1fl/fl) mice, we assessed vasoreactivity of middle cerebral (MCA), common carotid (CCA), and systemic arteries (thoracic aortae and first-order mesenteric arteries) ex vivo; and quantified CCA expression of genes associated with vascular smooth muscle (VSM) contractility. ADMA concentrations, and mRNA expression of protein arginine methyltransferases (PRMT), and DDAH were quantified in human cerebral (hCMEC/D3) and aortic (HAEC) endothelial cells. Outcomes following transient MCA occlusion (tMCAo) were also evaluated in male mice. In male DDAH1En-/- mice, NO-dependent vasodilator responses in MCA and CCA were significantly impaired compared to controls, while responses in systemic arteries were unaffected. Vasoconstrictor responses were paradoxically reduced in CCA from male DDAH1En-/- mice in association with altered expression of genes involved in VSM contractility. In contrast to males, vasoreactivity was unaltered in MCA and CCA from female DDAH1En-/- mice. Both PRMT1 and DDAH mRNA expression were higher in hCMEC/D3 compared with HAEC cells, in association with no change in ADMA concentrations. Lastly, in male DDAH1En-/- mice, infarct volumes and functional outcomes post-tMCAo were comparable with controls. These findings underscore a role for endothelial DDAH1 in maintaining endothelial function in cerebral arteries from male but not female mice. However, endothelial DDAH1 does not influence stroke outcomes.

articles.title: Neonatal Morbidity Across the Fetal Growth Spectrum in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is linked to fetal overgrowth and, less commonly, fetal growth restriction (FGR). Few studies have examined neonatal outcomes across the full birthweight spectrum while incorporating antenatal Doppler findings. We evaluated the association between birthweight/Doppler-defined growth category and neonatal outcomes in singleton GDM pregnancies.

METHOD: In a retrospective cohort (2011-2024) of singleton GDM pregnancies delivering at ≥32 weeks, growth categories were assigned after delivery using Hadlock birthweight percentiles and antenatal Doppler findings from the last ultrasound within 14 days of delivery. FGR was defined as birthweight <3rd percentile or 3rd-<10th percentile with an abnormal Doppler criterion; SGA was 3rd-<10th percentile without an abnormal available Doppler criterion. The primary outcome was a composite of arterial cord pH <7.1, 5-minute Apgar <7, neonatal hospital stay >2 days, or phototherapy. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for maternal and obstetric factors.

RESULTS: Among 2,099 pregnancies, 7.7% were FGR, 7.5% SGA, 71.8% AGA, and 13.0% LGA. Composite morbidity occurred in 50% of FGR, 40.7% LGA, 29.3% SGA, and 29.1% AGA (p<0.001). FGR (aOR 1.97, 95% CI 1.32-2.92) and LGA (aOR 1.36, 95% CI 1.00-1.85) predicted increased morbidity; SGA did not. The FGR association persisted at term (aOR 1.72, 95% CI 1.10-2.68).

CONCLUSION: In GDM, FGR and LGA were associated with greater neonatal morbidity. SGA without an abnormal available Doppler criterion was not associated with increased morbidity compared with AGA. These findings support prospective evaluation of Doppler-based risk stratification among small fetuses.

articles.title: Changes in self-related cognitive processes and depressive symptom severity following a single, moderate dose of psilocybin in depressed patients.
articles.journal: Philosophical transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series B, Biological sciences
articles.abstract: Psychedelic-assisted therapy, particularly with psilocybin, is increasingly proposed as a treatment for major depressive disorder, yet the neural and psychological mechanisms underlying its effects remain under investigation. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial, individuals diagnosed with major depressive disorder received a single, moderate dose of psilocybin (0.215 mg kg-1) or placebo, with the same psychological support. We analysed N = 37 individuals with major depressive disorder undergoing assessments of depressive symptoms (Beck's depression inventory and Montgomery-Åsberg depression rating scale), self-concept (Frankfurt self-concept scale) and neural markers of self-referential processing using an fMRI-based task. Compared with placebo, the psilocybin group exhibited significant reductions in depressive symptoms and a significant increase in positive self-concept two weeks after substance administration. Changes in self-concept were significantly correlated with decreased depressive scores. Neuroimaging revealed psilocybin-associated modulation of caudate activation during externally oriented attention after two weeks, contrasting with placebo-induced caudate changes during self-referential processing. These findings extend prior evidence linking psychedelics to changes in self-referential processing and self-concept and demonstrate that such changes occur concurrently with reductions in depressive symptoms. Future research should aim to replicate and extend these results and refine therapy protocols targeting self-processing and self-concept in psychedelic-assisted therapy in major depressive disorder. This article is part of the discussion meeting issue 'From being to identity: analysis and synthesis of the self'.

articles.title: All-in-One Mitochondria-Targeted Iron-Based MOF "Nanomissiles" for Synergistically Potentiated Tumor Ferroptosis, Dual Phototherapy, and Chemotherapy.
articles.abstract: Pronounced heterogeneity and adaptability of tumors inherently curtail monotherapeutic efficacy, necessitating rationally integrated multimodal regimens that enable precise intervention, overcome resistance, and eradicate heterogeneous cell populations within the complex tumor microenvironment (TME). All-in-one mitochondria-targeted "nanomissiles" were created by emodin (Em)-Fe3+-gated, doxorubicin (DOX)-loaded PCN-600(FeIII) (denoted as DOX@ME) nanoparticles for synergistic multimodal tumor therapy integrating ferroptosis, photodynamic therapy (PDT), mild photothermal therapy (MPTT), and chemotherapy. DOX@ME achieved on-demand release of DOX in response to the TME [such as low pH, glutathione (GSH), hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), and adenosine-5'-triphosphate (ATP)] and near-infrared laser, via the disassembly of the Em-Fe3+ gating films and/or the degradation of the PCN-600(FeIII) nanocarriers. Under both 660 and 808 nm laser irradiation, DOX@ME effectively triggered apoptosis via chemotherapy, PDT, and MPTT while robustly accelerating reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, GSH depletion, glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) downregulation, and lipid peroxide (LPO) accumulation to enhance ferroptosis. Moreover, DOX@ME could alleviate thermotolerance by depleting intracellular ATP and downregulating protective heat shock protein 70 to boost the curative efficacy of MPTT. DOX@ME exhibited excellent antitumor efficacy and good biocompatibility and biosafety in A549 tumor-bearing nude mice. Collectively, DOX@ME demonstrates robust clinical translational potential for precision cancer therapy.

articles.title: Three-in-One Injectable Hydrogel Orchestrating Host-Bacteria Targeting, Retention, and Autophagy for Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus-Infected Mastitis Therapy.
articles.abstract: MRSA mastitis is clinically refractory and characterized by progressive inflammation driven by intracellular bacteria that form persistent niches in mammary epithelial cells and macrophages to evade antimicrobial clearance. Conventional antibiotics, particularly β-lactams, are widely used but suffer from poor intracellular accumulation, failing to reach these reservoirs. Even nanocarrier-based strategies struggle to achieve efficient endosomal escape and precise intracellular targeting. Herein, we report a fibronectin-functionalized, fluorinated PLGA nanoparticle encapsulating amoxicillin and sulbactam (Fn-F-PLGA@A/S) engineered with a 2.5% (w/w) fluorinated core for efficient endosomal escape. The fibronectin decoration enables sequential targeting of both host integrins and bacterial fibronectin-binding proteins (FnBPs). Fn-F-PLGA@A/S achieved efficient intracellular delivery, clearing 90% of intracellular MRSA in macrophages and epithelial cells within 4 h in vitro. To prolong mammary retention, Fn-F-PLGA@A/S was loaded into a thermosensitive hydrogel. In a murine MRSA mastitis model, a single intramammary dose of the gel formulation achieved >90% bacterial reduction, attenuated TNF-α and IL-6, and preserved alveolar architecture and tight junctions. Proteomic analysis revealed upregulation of AMPK-mediated autophagy, suggesting that beyond direct antibiotic action, the potent intracellular clearance achieved by Fn-F-PLGA may involve the engagement of host autophagic machinery, potentially facilitating the sequestration of MRSA within degradative compartments. Collectively, by integrating sequential targeting, sustained local retention, and autophagic engagement, this platform provides a robust strategy to address the key limitations of conventional antibiotics against intracellular pathogens in refractory infections.

articles.title: In Vivo Comparison of Algorithms Estimating Left Ventricular Stroke Work From LVAD-Derived Pump Parameters.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate assessment of cardiac work during left ventricular assist device (LVAD) therapy is essential for patient management, device explantation timing, and adaptive control algorithm development. While invasive pressure-volume methods provide accurate work and contractility assessment, their clinical applicability is limited. Non-invasive algorithms utilizing inherent pump parameters offer a promising alternative, yet no systematic comparison exists.

METHODS: Six non-invasive algorithms for estimating stroke work (SW) were compared in 22 healthy German Landrace pigs (48.9 ± 2.6 kg) with a Deltastream DP3 LVAD: maximal LVAD flow derivative, motor power-LV pressure relationship, pressure head-flow relationship, systolic fraction of pressure-flow area, and total/pulsatile components of pump current and flow. After isoflurane-induced heart failure, four interventions were performed: preload reduction (inferior vena cava occlusion, n = 105), afterload increase (aortic balloon occlusion, n = 97), dobutamine infusion (n = 21), and speed ramps (n = 14). Linear multilevel modeling revealed significant main effects for algorithm (χ2 = 582.38), intervention type (χ2 = 73.77), and their interaction (χ2 = 324.80; all p < 0.001), explaining 54.04% of variability.

RESULTS: The pressure head-flow algorithm demonstrated consistently high correlations across interventions, though requiring semi-invasive pressure measurements. The pump flow area algorithm performed robustly during preload, afterload, and speed ramps but failed to capture SW changes during dobutamine. The systolic fraction algorithm achieved the highest correlations during dobutamine but frequently failed mathematical optimization, limiting applicability.

CONCLUSION: No single algorithm performed optimally across all conditions, necessitating context-specific selection. Pronounced inter-individual variability underscores the importance of patient-specific factors. These findings provide the first systematic comparison of non-invasive SW algorithms during LVAD therapy, offering guidance for algorithm selection.

articles.title: HIV-resistant CD19/HIV-targeted dual CAR T cells control HIV replication and B cell lymphoma concurrently in humanized mice.
articles.abstract: Infusion of CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells (CARTs) can result in robust CART expansion, long-term CART persistence, and durable remissions in B cell malignancies. We hypothesized that leveraging this expansion and persistence could enable sustained HIV control by engineering IL-18 secreting CD19 CARTs to co-express an HIV-specific CAR and a signaling-deficient C34-CXCR4 HIV fusion inhibitor (C34-CXCR4*), thereby generating HIV-resistant CD19/HIV dual CARTs. These CD19/HIV dual CARTs functioned as well as single CAR expressing CARTs toward a single target indicating no loss of activity occurred by co-expressing the CARs in the same cell. In a humanized mouse model of leukemia infused with CD4 T cells from a person with HIV (PWH), autologous CD19/HIV dual CARTs achieved tumor eradication comparable to that of CD19-only CARTs, demonstrating preserved antitumor efficacy. Notably, a CD19.BBζ-IL-18 CAR combined with a CD4.28ζ-C34-CXCR4* HIV-specific CAR exhibited enhanced T cell expansion and persistence and superior HIV and tumor control. Together, these findings identify CD19/HIV dual CARTs as a promising strategy to maintain a robust population of HIV-specific CARTs to control viral rebound, while simultaneously treating B cell malignancies, advancing CART based approaches toward durable HIV remission.

articles.title: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation with Vitaflow prosthesis in Latin America.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robust long-term data on the performance and durability of novel transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) valve designs, especially in Latin America, are lacking and warrant further investigation.

OBJECTIVES: To provide a 1 year follow-up data regarding a novel TAVI device.

METHODS: A retrospective, multicenter cohort study was conducted in Latin America of patients with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis treated with the Vitaflow prosthesis from June 2022 to June 2023. The clinical endpoints were all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, vascular and bleeding complications, permanent pacemaker implantation (PPM), and heart failure admission. Echocardiographic outcomes were the transvalvular gradient and paravalvular leak at 1 year of follow-up.

RESULTS: A total of 46 consecutive patients were included. The mean age of the patients was 80.9 ± 6.13 years; 50% were men, the mean STS score was 4.64 ± 2.67, and 60.8% were in NYHA class III/IV. The most used valve size was the 27 mm (47.1%). All-cause death at 1-year follow-up occurred in 4 patients (8.7%), of which 3 were cardiovascular (6.5%). There were 2 strokes, 1 vascular event, 2 major bleeding events, 4 new PPMs, and no myocardial infarctions or heart failure admissions. The 1-year mean transvalvular gradient was 7 ± 4 mmHg, and 3 patients (6.4%) had moderate paravalvular leak, with no severe leaks.

CONCLUSIONS: In a Latin American population, the Vitaflow TAVI valve has proved good safety and efficacy outcomes at 12 months of follow-up in the treatment of patients with severe aortic stenosis.

articles.title: A Disease Trajectory Representation Framework With Risk-Aware Pseudotime Analysis for Electronic Health Records: Application to Heart Failure Risk Stratification.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure develops through complex longitudinal interactions among multiple chronic diseases, making longitudinal disease trajectories an important source of clinical information. Longitudinal disease trajectories contain rich structural information that reflects disease evolution and comorbidity interactions. However, this information is often lost when electronic health record (EHR) data are summarized using conventional pooling strategies or sparse International Classification of Diseases (ICD) representations.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop an interpretable trajectory representation that preserves structural characteristics of longitudinal disease evolution for heart failure risk stratification using EHRs.

METHODS: Longitudinal ICD trajectories were represented using Node2Vec embeddings and summarized with information gain (IG)-weighted geometric features, including historical means, directional shifts, dispersion, and deviation relative to high-risk disease representations. The resulting maximum IG-weighted deviation geometric (mIGwDG) representation was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation against conventional embedding aggregation strategies, sparse ICD one-hot encoding, and a long short-term memory (LSTM) model. To facilitate interpretation of longitudinal disease evolution, we further developed a risk-aware pseudotime framework to organize patient trajectories along a model-inferred risk continuum and used a framework combining IG with the positive pointwise mutual information (PPMI) framework to characterize clinically relevant comorbidity patterns.

RESULTS: The proposed framework achieved an out-of-fold (OOF) area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.667 and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.888, outperforming conventional embedding aggregation methods. Compared with sparse ICD one-hot encoding, the proposed framework reduced feature dimensionality by approximately 75% while maintaining comparable predictive performance. Combining mIGwDG with sparse ICD one-hot features further improved both logistic regression (LR) and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), suggesting that the proposed representation captures complementary longitudinal disease trajectory information. In addition, the risk-aware pseudotime framework organized heterogeneous patient trajectories along a model-inferred risk continuum, while IG×PPMI analysis highlighted clinically relevant comorbidity patterns that supported the interpretation of longitudinal disease organization.

CONCLUSIONS: The proposed framework provides a compact and interpretable representation of longitudinal disease trajectories while maintaining comparable predictive performance. By combining geometric trajectory characterization with risk-aware pseudotime visualization, the framework facilitates the representation of longitudinal EHRs, the visualization of disease evolution, and risk stratification.

articles.title: TAVR in anomalous origin of the right coronary artery with interarterial course and acute takeoff angle.
articles.abstract: Anomalous aortic origin of the coronary arteries (AAOCA) is an infrequent finding that may increase the risk of coronary obstruction during transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). We report the case of an 80-year-old woman with severe aortic stenosis and anomalous origin of the right coronary artery (RCA) from the left coronary sinus, with an interarterial course and an acute takeoff angle. Preprocedural coronary angiography showed ostioproximal occlusion. Intravascular ultrasound demonstrated approximately 80% extrinsic compression, and coronary physiologic assessment confirmed hemodynamically significant ischemia. Given the high risk of myocardial ischemia during TAVR, the RCA was treated with drug-eluting stents before valve implantation. Subsequently, transfemoral TAVR with a self-expandable valve was performed successfully, with preserved coronary patency and no complications. At 4-year follow-up, the patient remained asymptomatic, with a normally functioning prosthetic valve and no hospital readmissions. This case underscores the importance of detailed preprocedural imaging, coronary physiology assessment, and individualized planning to minimize the risk of coronary obstruction in patients with high-risk AAOCA undergoing TAVR.

articles.title: German wine and respiration: Remarks on the discovery, properties and significance of the Bötzinger complex.
articles.abstract: The Bötzinger complex (BötC) comprises a distinct bilateral group of interneurons that are active during the expiratory phase of the respiratory cycle, located in the rostral medulla ventral to the compact formation of the nucleus ambiguus. It was named after the bottles of wine served at the conference dinner of an international meeting held in Germany in 1980, where the first electrophysiological data describing these neurons were presented. In cats, BötC neurons predominantly exhibit an augmenting (E-Aug) firing pattern, whereas in rats E-Aug and E-Dec (decrementing expiratory) patterns are observed. Both subtypes issue axons that often extensively arborise on both sides of the medulla, forming inhibitory glycinergic and/or GABAergic synapses with inspiratory neurons of the dorsal and ventral respiratory groups. Additionally, E-Aug neurons project to the spinal cord and inhibit phrenic motoneurons. These properties contrast with those of another group of bulbospinal expiratory neurons in the caudal medulla, which do not issue medullary axon collaterals and are excitatory. BötC neurons regulate the interval during which inspiratory neurons remain silent and contribute to synchronisation of respiratory activity across both sides of the lower brainstem. Recent in vivo, reduced-preparation and in silico studies indicate that they also contribute to respiratory rhythmogenesis through mutual inhibitory synaptic interactions with the pre-Bötzinger complex. This review provides the history of the discovery and naming of the BötC and a detailed discussion of the properties of BötC neurons, including their location, morphology, afferent and efferent axonal projections, synaptic connectivity and functional role.

articles.title: The Influence of Protein on Beverage Hydration Efficacy: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Beverage composition can dictate effectiveness of hydration and rehydration by influencing several physiological processes, including gastric emptying rate, intestinal absorption and oncotic pressure. While the benefits of solutes such as carbohydrates and electrolytes are well established in hydration beverages, research into the efficacy of protein inclusion remains sparse.

OBJECTIVE: The aim was to evaluate the effects of protein-containing beverages on hydration and rehydration, in terms of fluid retention, cumulative urine, net fluid balance (NFB) and plasma volume (PV) change, when compared with a control beverage.

METHODS: The systematic review was pre-registered (Open Science Framework) and conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library and Web of Science were searched from inception to February 2026 for human trials (≥ 18 years) researching hydration or rehydration following hypohydration or euhydration. To be eligible, beverages contained ≥ 2 g/L protein and reported at least one hydration outcome. Random-effects meta-analyses was performed using standardised mean differences (SMD).

RESULTS: Overall, 16 studies were included in this review (205 participants; 17.1% female, euhydrated: n = 2, hypohydrated: n = 14). Mean protein content in the studies was 23.7 ± 9.9 g/L. Meta-analysis performed on the rehydration studies revealed greater fluid retention (SMD 0.66, 95% CI 0.39-0.93, P < 0.00001, Z = 4.85, medium effect), reduced cumulative urine output (SMD - 0.71, 95% CI - 0.99 to - 0.43, P < 0.00001, Z = 4.93, medium effect), as well as increased NFB (SMD 0.58, 95% CI 0.30-0.85, P < 0.0001, Z = 4.10, medium effect) and augmented PV change (SMD 0.29, 95% CI 0.03-0.55, P = 0.03, Z = 2.19, small effect) following ingestion of protein.

CONCLUSIONS: Protein-containing beverages confer an advantage over a control beverage on hydration metrics. These findings support protein as a potentially beneficial addition to rehydration strategies, however, there was a lack of female participants (17.1%), as well as plant-based beverages, limiting the generalisability of findings to female athletes, as well as those with diets devoid of lactose products.

articles.title: An exploration of whole-blood transcriptomic alterations associated with obesity in the absence of overt metabolic disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity poses significant health risks including metabolic complications, cardiovascular disease, and cancer. However, a subgroup of individuals with obesity do not meet diagnostic criteria for overt cardiometabolic disease. These individuals are often described as having obesity without clinically manifest metabolic complications. Despite this apparent clinical profile, obesity may still be associated with systemic alterations in gene expression and molecular pathways.

METHODS: In this exploratory study, we conducted a comprehensive transcriptomic analysis of whole blood samples from individuals with obesity without overt metabolic abnormalities (OBO) and lean healthy controls (LHC) to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and pathway-level differences. Unsupervised dimensionality reduction was used to visualize global transcriptional patterns between groups.

RESULTS: Differential expression analysis revealed 106 upregulated and 322 downregulated genes in OBO, with the de-ubiquitinase USP17 family and snoRNAs among the most significantly altered. Pathway enrichment analysis identified 33 differentially enriched pathways, predominantly showing lower inferred enrichment of immune-related and DNA damage/repair-associated gene sets in OBO compared with LHC.

CONCLUSIONS: These exploratory findings demonstrate that obesity, even in the absence of overt metabolic disease, is associated with distinct whole-blood transcriptomic signatures. The results provide a hypothesis-generating framework for understanding early systemic molecular alterations associated with obesity.

articles.title: Integrated biochemical and immune markers as predictors of renal function decline in chronic kidney disease: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early prediction of renal function decline in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) is crucial for improving prognosis.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the predictive value of comprehensive biochemical and immunological markers for rapid decline in renal function in CKD patients.

METHOD: This retrospective cohort study included 196 stage 3-4 CKD patients (98 rapid decliners, eGFR loss ≥5 mL/min/1.73m2/year; 98 stable) from a county‑level hospital (2022-2026). Main markers: creatinine (Cr), urea nitrogen (BUN), cystatin C (Cys‑C), β2‑microglobulin (β2‑MG), and retinol‑binding protein (RBP). Secondary markers: parathyroid hormone, antinuclear antibody, anti‑neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA), immunoglobulins (IgG/A/M), and complements C3/C4. Multivariable Cox regression including age, sex, baseline eGFR, proteinuria, and comorbidities as covariates identified independent predictors. Bootstrap internal validation assessed model performance.

RESULT: Cys‑C, β2‑MG, and RBP were significantly higher in rapid decliners (all p<0.01). Cys‑C (HR=2.86, 95% CI 1.52-5.38) and β2‑MG (HR=2.13, 95% CI 1.23-3.69) were independent predictors. Complement C3 was lower (0.89 vs. 1.12 g/L, p=0.01) and ANCA positivity was higher (22.2% vs. 5.6%, p=0.03) in rapid decliners. The Cys‑C+β2‑MG model yielded an AUC of 0.86 (95% CI 0.80-0.92); adding C3 and ANCA increased AUC to 0.89. Bootstrap validation showed an optimism‑corrected AUC of 0.874 (shrinkage factor 0.94).

CONCLUSION: Cys-C, β2-MG, complement C3, and ANCA can serve as effective predictive markers for rapid renal function decline in CKD patients. Combined detection is helpful for early identification of high-risk individuals.

articles.title: Associations of plasma biomarkers and amyloid positron emission tomography with regional tau burden in Alzheimer's disease.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) and plasma biomarkers are clinically established; however, their topographical relationship with regional tau burden remains unclear. We investigated whether amyloid PET and plasma biomarkers are associated with regional tau pathology, measured using second-generation tracer florzolotau (18F) PET, across the Alzheimer's disease (AD) continuum.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study enrolled participants who underwent biomarker assessment between September 2018 and May 2022. The primary outcome was the voxel-wise spatial correlation of florzolotau (18F) standardised uptake value ratio with amyloid PET centiloid and plasma biomarkers, assessed using age- and sex-adjusted whole-brain and region-of-interest (ROI) linear regression analyses, including multivariate models adjusted for amyloid PET centiloid.

RESULTS: The study included 92 individuals (mean age, 71 [standard deviation, 8.8] years; 46 men), comprising 40 amyloid-negative healthy controls, 10 patients with preclinical AD, 21 with mild cognitive impairment due to AD, and 21 with AD dementia. In initial analyses, regional tau uptake correlated widely with plasma amyloid-beta 42/40 (Aβ42/40) ratio, p-tau, and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP). However, following multivariate adjustment for global amyloid burden, correlations for Aβ42/40 and GFAP were completely abolished. In contrast, plasma p-tau217, p-tau181, and neurofilament light chain (NfL) maintained significant amyloid-independent correlations with temporoparietal tau uptake, with p-tau217 uniquely retaining robust and extensive associations across the cortex.

CONCLUSION: Plasma p-tau217 is strongly associated with the spatial distribution and severity of tau burden independent of global amyloid burden. Measuring plasma p-tau217 holds significant potential for patient stratification and monitoring in the era of disease-modifying therapies.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: UMIN Clinical Trials Registry (UMIN000032027), registered 31 March 2018, prospectively registered (URL https//center6.umin.ac.jp/cgiopenbin/ctr_e/ctr_view.cgi? recptno=UMIN000032027). Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (jRCTs031180225), prospectively registered (URL https//jrct.niph.go.jp/enlatestdetail/jRCTs031180225).

articles.title: Target-oriented contrast enhancement strategies for pediatric cardiac CT angiography in congenital heart disease: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) often requires precise anatomical assessment from the neonatal and infant periods. Although echocardiography remains the first-line imaging modality, cardiac computed tomography angiography (CTA) plays an important complementary role in evaluating complex cardiovascular anatomy, coronary artery origin anomalies, great vessel abnormalities, and postoperative anatomy. However, contrast enhancement behavior in neonates and infants differs substantially from that in adults because of low body weight, high heart rate, small-caliber veins, limited circulating blood volume, and short circulation time. In addition, disease-specific flow patterns such as right-to-left shunting, Glenn circulation, Fontan circulation, and surgically altered pathways further modify contrast arrival, mixing, and washout. This narrative review summarizes practical strategies for optimizing contrast enhancement in pediatric cardiac CTA for CHD. Key considerations include iodine dose, contrast concentration, injection rate, injection duration, venous access, saline flush, timing method, and CT technology. The available literature suggests that contrast protocol design should be individualized according to body size, circulation pattern, target anatomy, and scanner performance. In normal neonatal and infant circulation, reproducible enhancement may be supported by body-weight-based iodine dosing, low-kV imaging, diluted contrast material, and stable low-flow injection. In abnormal circulation, particularly Glenn and Fontan physiology, protocol design should additionally consider access-site selection, delayed arrival, heterogeneous mixing, and bolus shaping tailored to the hemodynamic setting. Because the current evidence base remains heterogeneous and is largely derived from single-center studies, the protocol ranges summarized in this review should be interpreted as a practical framework rather than as formal guideline-level recommendations.

articles.title: Circulating Tumour DNA (ctDNA) as an Emerging Biomarker of Response in Early-Phase Oncology Drug Development: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) analysis is increasingly integrated into early-phase oncology trials. However, its role as a pharmacodynamic biomarker of treatment response, particularly its association with radiological response, remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to systematically evaluate the association between longitudinal ctDNA kinetics and radiological response according to Response Evaluation Criteria for Solid Tumors (RECIST) Version 1.1 in early-phase oncology trials.

METHODS: A systematic literature search identified early-phase trials published from 2015 onwards that assessed correlations between ctDNA changes and RECIST radiological outcomes in adults receiving investigational anti-cancer therapy for solid tumours.

RESULTS: Thirty-five studies were included, comprising 2962 treated patients. Significant heterogeneity was observed in ctDNA methodology between trials. Across studies, changes in longitudinal ctDNA were largely aligned with RECIST radiological outcomes. Across 18 cohorts with reconstructable 2 × 2 tables, molecular response was strongly associated with RECIST response (unadjusted odds ratio 7.24; 95% confidence interval 4.87-10.76). However, discordant responses between ctDNA dynamics and radiological outcomes were observed, highlighting the complexity of interpreting ctDNA changes during treatment.

CONCLUSIONS: Longitudinal ctDNA monitoring in early-phase oncology trials demonstrates potential as a complementary pharmacodynamic biomarker of treatment response. Its broad, yet incomplete alignment with conventional efficacy outcomes suggests that ctDNA may provide early biological signal of treatment activity that may help predict clinical benefit. Significant methodological heterogeneity was observed. Future studies should prioritise methodological standardisation and prospective validation of ctDNA kinetics with efficacy outcomes.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD420251064392.

articles.title: Machine learning prediction of electronic-portal-imaging-device-based in vivo dosimetry results using plan complexity metrics, machine output and gamma passing rate: a feasibility study.
articles.journal: Physical and engineering sciences in medicine
articles.abstract: In vivo dosimetry (IVD) is essential for verifying treatment accuracy and current methods only identify discrepancies after delivery. Predicting IVD results beforehand offers proactive risk anticipation. This study aimed to develop a machine learning (ML) model for predicting electronic-portal-imaging-device (EPID)-based IVD results. Input predictors included volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) plan complexity metrics, gamma passing rate (GPRs) from EPID-based patient-specific quality assurance (PSQA), and daily machine output quality assurance (QA) data for each treatment fraction. Seventeen VMAT plan complexity metrics were calculated from DICOM-RT files, and GPRs were obtained from forty head and neck cancer patients. The IVD results, a set of point-dose deviations between reconstructed and planned dose distributions, served as the input response. An ensemble-bagged-tree regression model was used to develop the prediction model. Model performance was evaluated using root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and R-squared. Spearman's rank correlation assessed relationships between predictors and responses. In the test set, the model achieved RMSE of 2.9%, MAE of 2.1%, and R-squared of 0.80. Correlations between EPID-based IVD results and plan complexity, GPRs of PSQA, and machine output QA metrics were weak, while the ML model showed strong predictive accuracy, closely matching predicted and measured IVD results. This study demonstrates the feasibility of combining ML with EPID-based IVD point-dose data. If further developed, this approach could provide fraction-by-fraction IVD estimates in clinics without dedicated IVD software and enable early detection of potential errors, enhancing IVD process.

articles.title: A Longitudinal Retrospective 5-Year Registry Study of the Health Care Chaplains' Work in Finland: Impact of a Large Health Care Services Reform.
articles.abstract: Spirituality and spiritual care are essential parts of patients' well-being and health care. Health care chaplains (HCP) are recognized experts in spiritual issues. The work of chaplains may be subject to cultural and structural changes in the societies. However, very little long-term data are available on the HCPs work or how reforms of health care services influence health care chaplaincy. This study aims to find out how the workloads of HCPs evolved during 2021-2025 and explore the observed differences before and after the 2023 health care reform. The study is based on public registry data of health care chaplains' actual work from the Evangelical Lutheran Church of Finland before (2021-2022) and after (2023-2025) the implementation of a large national health care services reform. All chaplains are obliged to report their daily activities on a weekly basis anonymously to the registry. Information about hospitals, patients and regional populations was collected from annual national statistics. Data concerning chaplains' work were grouped into primary categories defined by the context. The total number of chaplains was 103 and 0,04 per 1000 patients on average during the 5 years, mostly located in the capital area. Chaplains' most prominent tasks were discussions with patients about their health and illness-related issues, life crises and daily life events, while the religious rituals occurred substantially less frequently. The Finnish chaplains met a total of 324,244 persons at different encounters during the years. The number of patients in the age group of 29-64 years increased significantly during the observation period, and the number of conversations about life crises, grieving, death and daily life became more prevalent after the health care reform. It was found that, for the most part, chaplains' tasks did not change and that they were paid only by the Finnish Lutheran Church. In summary, the Finnish Evangelical Lutheran Church pays the health care chaplaincy for all Finnish hospitals, and the pastoral conversations may reflect the instability of health care services reform in the country.

articles.title: Feasibility of robotic-assisted surgery for nutcracker syndrome: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Nutcracker syndrome (NCS) results from compression of the left renal vein, and refractory symptoms require surgical reconstruction. Robotic platforms provide magnified three-dimensional vision and articulated instruments that are theoretically advantageous for vascular dissection and anastomosis within the confined retroperitoneal space. However, the available evidence consists almost entirely of small single-arm case series, and whether robotic-assisted surgery represents a feasible treatment option for NCS has not been established quantitatively; previous systematic reviews were descriptive only, without quantitative pooling of proportional outcomes or stratification by reconstructive technique and age. To evaluate the feasibility of robotic-assisted surgery for NCS in terms of technical completion, conversion to open surgery, perioperative safety, postoperative recovery and symptom relief, and to explore whether heterogeneity was explained by reconstructive technique, age or sample size. Four electronic databases-PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL (Cochrane Library) and the Web of Science Core Collection-were searched from inception to 1 October 2026, and the reference lists of the retrieved articles and of earlier reviews on this topic were screened by hand. Eligible reports were original studies of robot-assisted NCS surgery from which quantitative data could be obtained, provided the series comprised at least three patients; studies of non-robotic procedures, non-NCS cohorts, asymptomatic nutcracker phenomenon, stent implantation by the endovascular route alone, narrative reviews, conference proceedings, single-patient reports and duplicate cohorts were not considered. Screening and data collection were carried out independently by two investigators, and study quality was appraised with the JBI checklist designed for case series. Stata 17.0 was used for the single-arm proportional meta-analyses: individual proportions underwent Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation before being combined under a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model, with the summary estimates then expressed on the original scale, while continuous variables were harmonised to mean ± SD following Wan et al. and Shi et al. Cochran's Q test and the I-squared statistic were used to quantify heterogeneity. Subgroup comparisons were restricted to outcomes with substantial heterogeneity and were interpreted as exploratory analyses of study-level variation rather than as tests of independent effects. Ten studies comprising 140 patients were included (China, 4; USA, 4; France, 2; 9 retrospective and 1 prospective). Reconstructive techniques were left renal vein (LRV) transposition (5 studies, 45 patients), extravascular renal vein stent placement (3 studies, 29 patients) and renal autotransplantation (2 studies, 66 patients). Completion and conversion status could be ascertained in 111 patients from eight studies: 110 (99.1%) completed the planned reconstruction robotically and 1 (0.9%) was converted to open surgery; status was not reported for 29 patients in two studies and these patients were not counted as zero events. The pooled symptom improvement rate was 96% (95% CI 85%-100%; I-squared = 46.66%; 6 studies, 87 patients) and the complete symptom resolution rate 69% (95% CI 34%-96%; I-squared = 77.83%; 4 studies, 35 patients). The pooled incidence of Clavien-Dindo < 3 complications was 17% (95% CI 5%-33%; I-squared = 60.86%) and that of Clavien-Dindo >= 3 complications was 5.5% (95% CI 2.3%-9.8%; I-squared = 0%; 8 studies, 6 events); lymphorrhea/chylous ascites occurred in 15% (95% CI 0%-43%; I-squared = 79.16%) and postoperative reintervention in 3% (95% CI 0%-10%; I-squared = 0%). Pooled operating time was 204.52 min (95% CI 157.47-251.57 min; I-squared = 99.1%), estimated blood loss 54.21 mL (95% CI 37.56-70.86 mL; I-squared = 96.2%) and postoperative length of stay 2.72 days (95% CI 1.60-3.85 days; I-squared = 96.2%). Exploratory technique-stratified analyses suggested lower estimated blood loss, shorter operating time and shorter length of stay after extravascular stent placement than after LRV transposition or renal autotransplantation; however, several strata contained only one or two studies and these differences are descriptive rather than evidence of comparative superiority. Robotic-assisted surgery for NCS was associated with a high rate of technical completion among patients with ascertainable status, favourable symptom improvement and a low frequency of major complications. The apparent ordering of perioperative burden across techniques is consistent with differences in procedural invasiveness but may also reflect confounding by indication, centre effects and case selection. Owing to the single-arm design, short and inconsistent follow-up, absent patency data and very low certainty, these findings should be regarded as a pooled feasibility benchmark rather than as evidence of comparative effectiveness.

articles.title: Timing Is Everything: Reservoir Dynamics and Immune Correlates in Perinatally Acquired HIV-1 Across the Lifespan.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review synthesizes the past 5 years of research on individuals with perinatally acquired HIV-1 (PHIV) with a focus on evaluating the proviral reservoir landscape and associated immunological correlates.

RECENT FINDINGS: We found that the age at the time of study shapes the questions being addressed and insights gained from infancy through adulthood in PHIV cohorts where ART timing shapes immune development and reservoir establishment. In infants and newborns, there has been more frequent antiretroviral therapy interruption (ATI) studies, with and without immunotherapy (e.g., bNAbs), aiming to replicate Mississippi Baby-like control in early-treated infants with small reservoirs. In long-term suppressed adolescents and adults with PHIV, work increasingly focuses on characterization of the long-lived HIV-1 reservoir and defining immunological correlates of smaller, less diverse reservoirs in order to predict post-treatment control. Understanding perinatal HIV-1 infection by life stage is essential for guiding future intervention and cure research.

articles.title: Hematologic changes under [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE PRRT in GEP-NETs: a long-term longitudinal cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) with [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE is increasingly applied for advanced gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NETs). This study aimed to characterize the development of hematologic parameters under PRRT in a large single-center cohort. We retrospectively analyzed 178 patients with GEP-NETs treated with [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE at a university hospital (2012-2023). Hemoglobin (Hb), white blood cell count (WBC), and platelet count (PLT) were assessed at baseline, after 2 cycles (FU1), after 4 cycles (FU2), during post-therapy follow-up (FU3), and at the last available timepoint (FU4). Patients with deteriorating blood values during or after therapy were categorized according to CTCAE v6.0. The occurrence of myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) within the period from completion of the initial PRRT to initiation of salvage chemotherapy or PRRT was investigated.

RESULTS: Baseline mean values were Hb, 13.6 ± 1.6 g/dL; WBC, 6.9 ± 2.0 × 10⁹/L; and PLT, 256 ± 92 × 10⁹/L. A significant decline in those hematological parameters was observed at FU1 and FU2 (p < 0.01).
