Between FU2 and FU3, values recovered significantly (p < 0.001), with no further relevant change at FU4 for Hb and PLT, while WBC increased significantly compared to FU3. At last follow-up (FU4), all parameters remained significantly below baseline (all p < 0.001), but exhibited final values in a normal laboratory range (Hb, 12.4 ± 1.9 g/dL; WBC, 6.3 ± 2.6 × 10⁹/L; and PLT, 216 ± 78 × 10⁹/L). Based on CTCAE v6.0, only 4 patients (2%) developed grade 3 hematological adverse events and no grade 4 adverse event was observed. After completing four cycles of PRRT, 2 patients (1.3%) developed MDS according to the WHO criteria. Patients with chemotherapy prior to PRRT (n = 30) had lower baseline WBC and showed smaller on-treatment declines, but were the only subgroup without Hb recovery from the nadir (median change FU2 to FU4, - 0.35 vs. +0.35 g/dL; adjusted p = 0.017).

CONCLUSION: PRRT with [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE induces a mild short to midterm decline in hematologic parameters, which is followed by a significant increase during long-term follow-up, eventually returning to values within the laboratory reference range. Serious adverse events or MDS are very rare, supporting long-term overall hematologic safety.

articles.title: Association between weight loss and changes in body composition during inpatient multidisciplinary care for patients with chronic kidney disease.
The oral-kidney axis in IgA nephropathy: cnm-positive Streptococcus mutans as a microbial trigger.
articles.abstract: IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is the most common primary glomerulonephritis worldwide and a major cause of chronic kidney disease. IgAN is characterized by mesangial deposition of immune complexes containing galactose-deficient IgA1. Although the multi-hit hypothesis provides a framework for disease pathogenesis, the environmental factors that initiate aberrant mucosal immune responses remain incompletely understood. Recent studies have highlighted the role of mucosal microbiota in disease development. Among potential microbial triggers, oral bacteria have attracted attention because the oral cavity is continuously exposed to microbial antigens and closely linked to mucosal immunity. Collagen-binding Streptococcus mutans expressing the Cnm protein (cnm-positive S. mutans) has been implicated in several systemic diseases and is increasingly associated with IgAN. Clinical and experimental evidence suggests that these bacteria may contribute to pathogenic IgA responses and immune complex formation. In this review, we summarize current knowledge regarding mucosal immunity in IgAN and discuss emerging evidence linking oral microorganisms, particularly cnm-positive S. mutans, to disease pathogenesis. We discuss the emerging concept of an oral-kidney axis in IgAN, in which cnm-positive S. mutans may represent a potential microbial contributor, and consider the therapeutic implications of oral microbial control.

articles.title: Changes in kidney function during dotinurad treatment for hyperuricemia: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hyperuricemia and chronic kidney disease (CKD) are bidirectionally linked; however, studies have shown that urate-lowering therapy with xanthine oxidoreductase inhibitors is largely neutral in regards to renal outcomes. Dotinurad, a selective urate reabsorption inhibitor (SURI) that inhibits URAT1 without impacting ABCG2, OAT1, and OAT3, may exert distinct renal effects; however, clinical evidence regarding its renal impact is dispersed across small studies. In this systematic review, we described changes in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) during dotinurad treatment given for hyperuricemia.

METHODS: We systematically searched the PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, Ichushi-Web, and J-STAGE databases from inception to May 2026 for studies evaluating dotinurad and eGFR. Eligible studies were synthesized descriptively owing to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity.

RESULTS: Sixteen studies encompassing 1323 dotinurad-treated patients (1 randomized trial, 4 nonrandomized comparative studies, and 11 single-arm before-after studies) presented 24 study-level eGFR estimates (baseline mean eGFR approximately 20-100 mL/min/1.73 m2; follow-up 12-52 weeks). Across these studies, eGFR showed no significant decline, remaining generally stable or slightly increasing. In the five comparative studies, between-group differences (dotinurad minus comparator) ranged from +0.5 to +3.5 mL/min/1.73 m2 (or per year for slopes), with 95% confidence intervals including zero in four.

CONCLUSIONS: In the available short-term studies, eGFR generally remained stable during dotinurad treatment in patients with hyperuricemia, including those with CKD. Between-group estimates from five comparative studies were generally imprecise and did not provide consistent evidence of a treatment-related improvement in kidney function. Further randomized trials with prespecified renal end points are warranted.

articles.title: Hypertension and Blood Pressure Dysregulation in Cancer Survivors: Mechanisms, Management, and Future Directions.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review examines the epidemiology, mechanisms, and management of hypertension in patients with cancer, emphasizing treatment-related hypertension, autonomic dysfunction, blood pressure lability, and evolving blood pressure targets in cardio-oncology.

RECENT FINDINGS: Among cancer survivors both during and after their cancer treatment, hypertension is highly prevalent and is associated with increased cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) inhibitors are one of the most common causes of cancer treatment-induced hypertension, although other cancer treatments also contribute. Emerging evidence highlights the coexistence of orthostatic hypotension and hypertension, likely related to autonomic dysfunction, arterial stiffening, baroreflex impairment, and endothelial dysfunction related to cancer and its treatment. Medical management, intensive blood pressure control, and cardio-oncology rehabilitation may improve blood pressure control while mitigating adverse outcomes. Current hypertension management in cancer survivors largely follows general population guidelines despite the unique pathophysiology of cancer and its therapies. Future research should establish cancer-specific blood pressure targets, optimize antihypertensive strategies, and further investigate management of blood pressure lability, autonomic dysfunction, and cardio-oncology rehabilitation.

articles.title: Risk Prediction for Heart Failure in Patients with Cancer: Current Models and Future Directions.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Cancer survivors have an elevated risk for developing heart failure due to prior chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and other overlapping co-morbid conditions. With the advancement in cancer treatment, there is an increasing number of survivors who are at an even higher risk of developing heart failure. There is a growing need for heart failure specific risk prediction models in this population to facilitate early diagnosis and timely management. This review aims to summarize most recent findings on heart failure risk prediction among patients with history of cancer.

RECENT FINDINGS: Current risk prediction models focus on heart failure risk at the time of cancer treatment and shortly thereafter. There is limited data on heart failure risk among long term survivors.

articles.title: A Data-Mining Study of the Safety of the 20-Valent Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccine in Adults in the Vaccine Safety Datalink.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A 20-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV20) was approved for adults by the US Food and Drug Administration in 2021. We conducted a data-mining signal-identification analysis to assess possible adverse events after vaccination.

METHODS: We included individuals aged ≥ 19 years from ten Vaccine Safety Datalink sites who received PCV20 between June 2021 and October 2024 and had continuous medical coverage from ≥ 400 days before through 84 days after vaccination. Using a self-controlled design, incident diagnoses from inpatient and emergency department encounters were assessed for statistical clustering during post-vaccination risk windows within the tree-like structure of International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Clinical Modification diagnosis codes. Two analyses using tree-based scan statistics were conducted: conditional tree-temporal, with moving risk and control windows of varying lengths within an 84-day period; and conditional Bernoulli, with pre-specified risk and control windows of 1-21 and 43-84 days post-vaccination, respectively. A statistically significant cluster was defined as a p-value < 0.01.

RESULTS: We identified 1,042,847 PCV20 vaccinees. In the tree-temporal analysis, statistically significant clusters included codes for non-specific adverse effects of a vaccine or other medical product, within 7 days post-vaccination (p-value range: 0.0001-0.0059); fever, 1-2 days post-vaccination (p-value range: 0.0001-0.0004); cellulitis of the left upper limb, days 2-5 (p-value 0.0001); and hemorrhoids or perianal venous thrombosis, days 42-63 (p-value 0.0045). We also detected statistically significant clusters for non-specific adverse effects from vaccines via the Bernoulli analysis within 21 days post-vaccination (p-value range: 0.0001-0.0069). We reviewed individual-level data from a sample of patients in the cluster for hemorrhoids; hemorrhoids appeared to be either present before vaccination or found during routine colonoscopy.

CONCLUSIONS: This untargeted scan for potential adverse events following PCV20 vaccination did not identify clusters of diagnoses representing new, serious safety concerns, though there was low power to detect an association with rare outcomes. The identified clusters were known vaccination-associated events in pre-licensure randomized controlled trials and prior observational analyses or unlikely to be associated with the vaccine.

articles.title: Pharmacovigilance of Maternal Vaccines in Africa: An Analysis of Reporting Patterns from VigiBase®, 2010-2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal immunisation is an effective strategy for reducing morbidity and mortality in pregnant women and neonates, yet it requires close safety monitoring, but safety surveillance capacity in Africa has historically been limited. The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic provided an unprecedented opportunity to evaluate Africa's capacity for maternal vaccine pharmacovigilance and assess whether pandemic-era gains could be sustained.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize maternal vaccine safety reporting from Africa in VigiBase® (2010-2024), compare reporting patterns for COVID-19 and non-COVID vaccines, and identify priorities for strengthening maternal immunization safety surveillance METHODS: A retrospective descriptive analysis of individual case safety reports submitted by African countries to VigiBase®, the World Health Organization global pharmacovigilance database, was conducted for January 2010 to December 2024. Reports were identified using the Uppsala Monitoring Centre pregnancy algorithm and classified according to the Brighton Collaboration Global Alignment of Immunisation Safety Assessment in Pregnancy adverse events following the maternal immunisation framework. Descriptive statistics and chi-square tests were used to compare COVID-19 and non-COVID vaccine reporting patterns, and a Mann-Whitney U test was used to compare pre-pandemic and pandemic annual reporting volumes.

RESULTS: Africa contributed 817 of 44,316 global maternal vaccine safety reports (1.84%), submitted by 33 of 55 African countries. Of these, 573 (70.1%) were associated with COVID-19 vaccines and 244 (29.9%) with non-COVID-19 vaccines. Annual reporting increased markedly during the pandemic period (median 183.0 vs 4.5 reports/year; Mann-Whitney U  test = 0.0, p = 0.004, effect size r = 0.785), with Africa's global share rising from 0.49 to 2.48%. A total of 1619 adverse events were recorded across 817 reports. Adverse events following maternal immunisation category distributions differed significantly between vaccine types (χ2 = 200.6, df = 5, p < 0.001): COVID-19 vaccines were predominantly associated with maternal systemic events (36.9%) and unclassifiable reports (36.1%), whereas non-COVID vaccines generated proportionally more pregnancy outcome-specific events (25.3%) and fetal adverse events (8.1%). Physicians submitted the most reports but had the highest unclassifiable rate (52.3%), significantly exceeding all other reporter groups (χ2 = 125.0, df = 4, p < 0.001). Consumer reporting rose from one pre-pandemic report to 82 reports during 2021-24.

CONCLUSIONS: The COVID-19 pandemic catalysed a substantial expansion in maternal vaccine pharmacovigilance in Africa, demonstrating the continent's capacity to scale up surveillance rapidly. However, persistent gaps in data completeness and uneven country participation highlight the need for sustained embedded surveillance as new maternal vaccines targeting respiratory syncytial virus and group B Streptococcus are introduced.

articles.title: Comment on: "Population Pharmacokinetics of Intravenous Vitamin C in Adults with Sepsis: A Sub-Study of the LOVIT Trial".
Preferences of Patients with Type 1 Diabetes for Glucose Monitoring Devices: Results from a Discrete Choice Experiment in the UK and Canada.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Regular self-monitoring of glucose levels is integral to diabetes management to achieve glycaemic control and reduce the risk of acute and long-term complications. Wearable glucose monitoring devices provide more comprehensive information on glucose fluctuations than traditional finger-prick testing. However, access restrictions contribute to inequalities in adoption. This study elicited the preferences of patients with type 1 diabetes in the UK and Canada for attributes of glucose monitoring devices.

METHODS: An online discrete choice experiment was conducted among adults (aged ≥ 18 years) with type 1 diabetes. Respondents chose between standard finger-prick testing (usual care) and two hypothetical glucose monitoring devices described using six attributes: convenience of monitoring, time lag, level of information, alarm to signal low and high glucose levels, glycated haemoglobin level and time in range, and an out-of-pocket monthly cost. Responses were analysed using a mixed logit model, and marginal willingness to pay was calculated. A pooled model using country interaction terms was used to formally compare preferences across countries.

RESULTS: The discrete choice experiment was completed by 112 UK and 102 Canadian respondents. Across countries, respondents preferred devices offering convenience, alarm capabilities, real-time glucose readings and more comprehensive glucose information. Preferences were broadly consistent across countries, with only preferences for alarm functionality differing significantly. However, substantial preference heterogeneity was observed within both countries, indicating variation in the device characteristics valued by individuals.

CONCLUSIONS: Overall, the discrete choice experiment results indicate that adults with type 1 diabetes preferred characteristics relating to the newer glucose monitoring devices. Substantial variation in individual preferences suggests that access to a range of glucose monitoring devices may be important to accommodate differences in the characteristics patients value.

articles.title: Robotic pancreatic enucleation versus laparoscopic pancreatic enucleation: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Pancreatic enucleation (PE) is an operation that spares pancreatic parenchyma and thereby preserves glandular function, and it is now widely favoured for benign and low-grade malignant pancreatic neoplasms. Whether adding robotic assistance brings benefit beyond the standard laparoscopic route, however, remains an open question. This meta-analysis therefore contrasted robotic pancreatic enucleation (RPE) with laparoscopic pancreatic enucleation (LPE) with respect to perioperative efficacy and safety. Records of cohort studies that contrasted RPE with LPE were retrieved from the Cochrane Library, PubMed, the Wanfang, Embase and China National Knowledge Infrastructure, covering each database from inception to 1 September 2026. Two investigators working in duplicate screened the records, extracted the data and rated methodological quality with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). R 4.5.3 with the meta package was used for pooling; mean differences (MDs) and risk ratios (RRs) were presented with their 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Publication-bias and sensitivity analyses were omitted because fewer than 10 eligible studies were available. Five studies met the eligibility criteria (each scoring NOS ≥ 7) and together enrolled 272 patients, 144 in the LPE arm and 128 in the RPE arm. Operation time (MD 0.20, 95% CI - 38.98 to 39.39, P = 0.99), intraoperative blood loss (MD 14.60, 95% CI - 3.39 to 32.58, P = 0.11), postoperative pancreatic fistula (risk ratio [RR] 1.21, 95% CI 0.89-1.64, P = 0.23), postoperative bleeding (RR 0.43, 95% CI 0.06-2.97, P = 0.39), and major complications (RR 1.28, 95% CI 0.54-3.00, P = 0.58) did not differ significantly between groups. Postoperative hospital stay was statistically shorter in the RPE group (MD 1.22, 95% CI 0.29-2.16, P = 0.01); however, this finding should be interpreted cautiously and does not, by itself, establish a clinically meaningful recovery advantage. The available evidence is insufficient to demonstrate a clear overall difference between robotic and laparoscopic pancreatic enucleation in perioperative efficacy or safety. Although postoperative hospital stay was shorter in the RPE group in the pooled analysis, the small observational evidence base and potential residual confounding preclude a firm conclusion that robotic surgery provides a recovery advantage. Larger, well-designed prospective multicentre studies are needed.

articles.title: Comparison of alignment in patients with buccally displaced maxillary canines using T-loop mechanics and continuous arch mechanics: a randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the efficiency and effects of T-loop mechanics (TLM) and continuous arch mechanics (CAM) for alignment of maxillary anterior teeth in patients with buccally displaced canines (BDC).

SUBJECTS AND METHODS: In this parallel, two-arm randomized clinical trial, 26 patients with unilateral or bilateral BDC were randomly allocated to TLM and CAM groups. In the TLM group, canines were initially retracted using T-loops, whereas in the CAM group, initial distal movement of the canine was performed using elastomeric chains on a continuous 0.014-inch nickel-titanium (NiTi) archwire without full engagement. After sufficient distal movement in the TLM group and once full canine engagement was achieved in the CAM group, alignment and leveling in both groups were completed sequentially using 0.014-, 0.016-, and 0.018-inch round NiTi archwires. Study models and radiographs were obtained at baseline (T0) and after alignment (T1). The primary outcome was the rate of alignment. Secondary outcomes included anchorage loss, canine tipping, rotation, and intercanine width. Independent t-tests and generalized estimating equation (GEE) models were used for analysis.

RESULTS: The rate of alignment did not differ significantly between the two treatment groups (P = 0.114). GEE model analysis showed significant changes over time for anchorage loss, canine tipping, and rotation in both groups (P < 0.001). The main effect of mechanics and the mechanics × time interaction was not statistically significant (P > 0.05). Intercanine width did not differ significantly between groups (P = 0.378).

CONCLUSIONS: Within the limitations of this clinical trial, both mechanics demonstrated effective alignment of buccally displaced canines with no statistically significant differences between groups; however, the wide confidence intervals preclude any conclusion of equivalence or clinical interchangeability.

articles.title: Association of GLP-1 receptor agonist use with mortality and healthcare utilization in patients with vascular dementia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Patients with vascular dementia (VD) have high mortality and frequent acute care use, and no treatment has been shown to improve these outcomes. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are associated with a lower incidence of dementia and with cardiovascular benefit in type 2 diabetes, but their association with clinical outcomes in patients with established VD is unknown.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study using a national database identified patients with VD from 2016 to 2025. Patients receiving GLP-1RAs within one month of diagnosis were propensity-score matched with non-users (n = 613 per group). Primary outcome was mortality at 1, 3, and 5 years; secondary outcomes included hospitalizations and emergency visits.

RESULTS: GLP-1RA use was associated with lower risk of mortality at 1 year (8.7% vs. 15.9%; HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.34-0.71), 3 years (23.3% vs. 33.8%; HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.44-0.76), and 5 years (34.4% vs. 54.3%; HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.41-0.69) (all p < 0.001). In addition, GLP-1RA use was associated with lower risk of inpatient admissions and emergency visits.

CONCLUSION: GLP-1RA use in patients with VD was associated with lower risk of mortality and healthcare utilization. These beneficial associations warrant prospective randomized trials.

articles.title: Heatwaves in HF: From risk to clinical action.
articles.abstract: Extreme heat represents an important clinical challenge for patients with cardiovascular disease (CVD). Individuals with heart failure (HF) may be particularly vulnerable because heat dissipation requires cutaneous vasodilation, increased skin blood flow, and sweating, whereas HF may limit cardiovascular reserve and increase susceptibility to hypotension, renal dysfunction, and electrolyte disturbances. Risk is further amplified by advanced age, chronic kidney disease (CKD), frailty, cognitive impairment, limited access to cooling, and the use of medications that influence volume status, blood pressure (BP), or thermoregulation. Observational evidence links high ambient temperatures with cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, and recent HF-specific data support an association between short-term heat exposure and increased mortality. However, evidence directly guiding the clinical management of chronic HF during heatwaves remains limited. No randomized controlled trial (RCT) has established whether or how guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) should be modified solely in response to hot weather. This focused narrative review proposes a cautious, phenotype-driven approach. Local heat alerts should prompt anticipatory risk assessment, patient education, and temporary intensification of surveillance, whereas treatment changes should be determined by the interaction between symptoms, congestion, BP, weight, oral intake, urine output, renal function, and electrolytes rather than ambient temperature alone. Telemonitoring may provide an enabling infrastructure for this strategy, although heat-alert-triggered remote management has not been prospectively validated. Extreme heat should therefore prompt increased clinical vigilance rather than automatic medication withdrawal. Prospective studies are needed to validate heat-specific monitoring pathways, hydration strategies, and medication-review protocols in chronic HF.

articles.title: Comparative Efficacy of Novel Non-steroidal Topical Therapies for Atopic Dermatitis: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Despite the availability of several non-steroidal topical therapies for atopic dermatitis (AD), their comparative speed of clinical response remains unclear. This meta-analysis compared the efficacy of novel non-steroidal topical therapies for AD.

METHODS: Four databases were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating topical difamilast 1% twice daily (BID), tapinarof 1% once daily (QD), ruxolitinib 1.5% BID, roflumilast 0.05% or 0.15% QD in patients with AD. Outcomes included Investigator's Global Assessment Treatment Success (IGA-TS) and 50%, 75% and 90% improvement in Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI-50, EASI-75 and EASI-90) at weeks 1, 2, 4 and 8. Frequentist random-effects network meta-analyses estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), primarily comprising indirect comparisons between non-steroidal topicals using a common vehicle comparator.

RESULTS: Twenty-two RCTs (5843 participants) were included. Ruxolitinib demonstrated the highest odds of IGA-TS versus vehicle at week 2 (OR 8.94; 95% CI 5.28-15.12), 4 (OR 9.03; 95% CI 6.27-13.01) and 8 (OR 9.03; 95% CI 6.52-12.50), along with EASI-75 and EASI-90. Difamilast demonstrated favourable EASI-75 (OR 5.34; 95% CI 3.51-8.12) and EASI-90 (OR 6.71; 95% CI 3.79-11.89) responses versus vehicle at week 4; later data were unavailable.

CONCLUSIONS: Efficacy profiles varied across novel non-steroidal topical therapies, with ruxolitinib demonstrating the strongest and most consistent relative efficacy estimates. Response magnitude and timing remain important considerations when selecting topical AD treatments.

articles.title: The Camelid Advantage in Modern Medicine: Exploring The Unique Properties of Camel Lactoferrin.
articles.abstract: Milk is a primary food product recommended for people of every age. It contains numerous beneficial proteins. The concentration of these proteins varies among mammals. Among various sources, camel milk lactoferrin (cLF) has emerged as a subject of particular interest, owing to its unique structural and functional characteristics. Lactoferrin (LF) is a multifunctional glycoprotein as well as a member of the transferrin family. It has gained considerable attention in scientific literature due to its extensive array of health-promoting properties, which include antibacterial, antiviral, immunomodulatory, and anticancer activities. The iron-binding domain of LF is highly conserved across different species, reflecting its essential role in the protein's biological function. However, comparative structural analyses have revealed certain variations in the iron-binding mechanisms of cLF, distinguishing it from other members of the transferrin family. Specifically, cLF exhibits properties that are characteristic of both transferrin and LF, providing a valuable model for understanding the complex mechanisms of iron binding and transport. The unique structural features of cLF make it an ideal subject for in-depth studies aimed at elucidating the molecular determinants of its biological activities. These characteristics underscore the importance of cLF as a critical protein in the context of health and disease. This review aims to provide a comprehensive examination of the structural and functional distinctiveness of cLF, focusing particularly on its role in modern medicine. Notably, the review explores the therapeutic potential of cLF in the management of diabetes, cancer, viral, and bacterial infections, highlighting its emerging applications in clinical settings and its promise as a novel therapeutic agent.

articles.title: Effects of Bacterial-Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Rodent Models of Obesity, Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Insulin Resistance/type 2 Diabetes. A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Obesity, metabolic-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and insulin resistance/type II diabetes (IR/T2D) share gut microbiota dysbiosis as an etiological factor. Bacteria-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as a promising strategy to modulate gut microbiota composition. To systematically review preclinical in vivo evidence on the effects of bacterial-derived EVs in obesity, MASLD and IR/T2D in rats and mice. Following PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO registration CRD420261293767), a systematic search was conducted in PubMed/Medline, Web of Science, Scopus and EMBASE® from inception until January 2026 for controlled in vivo studies in mice and rats. Nine studies met inclusion criteria, all of which were conducted in dietary mice models; no eligible rat studies, or genetically-induced models were identified. EVs administration generally reduced body and adipose tissue weight, hepatic lipid accumulation, improved glycaemic control, and modulated gut microbiota composition. Bacterial EVs show promise for preventing and treating obesity-related metabolic disorders, although evidence remains limited and heterogeneous.

articles.title: Probiotic Pediococcus pentosaceus NQ0729 Attenuates ETEC-Induced Rumen Epithelial Injury in Yak Calves.
articles.abstract: Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC) infection is an important cause of gastrointestinal injury in young animals. However, whether probiotic strains isolated from naturally fermented yak yogurt can protect rumen epithelial health in ETEC-challenged yak calves remains unclear. This study investigated the effects of Pediococcus pentosaceus NQ0729 isolated from naturally fermented yak yogurt on ETEC-induced rumen epithelial injury and explored its associations with the rumen microbiota and microbiota-associated metabolites. ETEC challenge increased the serum IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α, IFN-γ, MDA, and ROS levels and decreased the IL-10, SOD, CAT, GSH-Px, and T-AOC levels (P < 0.05). P. pentosaceus NQ0729 pretreatment attenuated these inflammatory and oxidative stress responses (P < 0.05). ETEC challenge also caused rumen epithelial morphological damage, increased epithelial apoptosis, and reduced the expression of epithelial barrier-related markers, including ZO-1, Occludin, and Claudin-4, as well as the mucin-related marker MUC2 (P < 0.05). These alterations were partially attenuated by P. pentosaceus NQ0729 pretreatment (P < 0.05). In addition, P. pentosaceus NQ0729 reduced the activation of TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB-related inflammatory signaling and enhanced Nrf2-associated antioxidant defense in rumen tissues (P < 0.05). 16 S rRNA gene sequencing and untargeted metabolomics revealed that P. pentosaceus NQ0729 altered the rumen microbial composition and ruminal metabolite profile. Integrated analysis further revealed significant associations among differential rumen genera, microbiota-associated metabolites, and host inflammatory, oxidative stress, antioxidant, and barrier-related indices (P < 0.05). P. pentosaceus NQ0729 alleviated ETEC-induced rumen epithelial injury in yak calves, which was accompanied by reduced inflammation and oxidative stress, improved epithelial barrier-related markers, and changes in the rumen microbiota and microbiota-associated metabolites. These findings suggest that P. pentosaceus NQ0729 may protect rumen epithelial homeostasis, with its protective effects accompanied by changes in the rumen microbiota and microbiota-associated metabolites and by significant associations among microbial, metabolic, and host barrier-related features.

articles.title: Invisible gallbladder: an unusual imaging finding of emphysematous cholecystitis.
articles.abstract: A 59 year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus presented to our emergency department with a 7 day history of intermittent fever and right upper quadrant pain. On examination, he was febrile, tachycardic, tachypneic, and hypotensive. An abdominal computed tomography scan revealed the location of the gallbladder was filled with air and an absent gallbladder wall contour. Emphysematous cholecystitis with perforation was initially suspected. However, imaging revealed no pneumoperitoneum or direct evidence of gallbladder perforation. Cholangiography revealed the gallbladder and biliary tract were patent. An unusual imaging presentation of emphysematous cholecystitis resulting in an invisible gallbladder wall rather than gallbladder perforation was finally diagnosed. The patient had a major abdominal surgery 3 weeks prior to admission. Consequently, he initially underwent percutaneous transhepatic gallbladder drainage. The patient improved significantly after 2 weeks of antibiotics and 4 weeks of percutaneous transhepatic gallbladder drainage; therefore, elective cholecystectomy was deferred. No recurrence of emphysematous cholecystitis after 2 years. This report aims to raise awareness among clinicians regarding the unique imaging feature, diagnostic methods, and management strategies for emphysematous cholecystitis, with the ultimate goal of improving patient outcomes.

articles.title: Interleukin-6, soluble interleukin-6 receptor, and outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: an exploratory biomarker substudy of a prospective multicenter cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe aortic stenosis can be treated with transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Identifying clinical and laboratory factors that predict clinical outcomes after TAVI may facilitate more informed decision-making. We aimed to assess the incidence of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) within 12 months after TAVI and long-term survival according to baseline interleukin-6 (IL-6) and soluble interleukin-6 receptor (sIL-6R) levels.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this biomarker substudy of a prospective multicenter cohort, we evaluated clinical outcomes after TAVI according to baseline IL-6 signal and sIL-6R concentration. We included only patients with an available baseline stored plasma sample. Patients were stratified into high and low IL-6 and sIL-6R groups. Two primary end points were analyzed: (i) 12-month MACCE, and (ii) long-term overall survival. Secondary end points included the individual components of MACCE. Stored baseline plasma was available for measurements in 62 patients who underwent TAVI between December 2018 and September 2021 across three clinical sites. Patients with high IL-6 had a higher 12-month MACCE risk in age- and sex-adjusted Firth penalized Cox regression analysis (HR 3.31; 95%CI 1.02-11.04, P = 0.0458) but not in unadjusted analysis (log-rank P = 0.07). The association was not robust to alternative cutoffs and the age- and sex-adjusted continuous analysis of IL-6 also did not show a statistically significant association (hazard ratio per 1-SD increase, 1.52, 95% CI, 0.86 to 2.46, P = 0.13). No significant associations were observed in the primary models between IL-6 and long-term overall survival or between sIL-6R and either primary end point.

CONCLUSIONS: High IL-6 signal at baseline may be associated with increased 12-month MACCE risk after TAVI, although this finding was sensitive to IL-6 categorization and was not statistically significant in continuous analysis. Baseline sIL-6R concentration was not significantly associated with the analyzed clinical outcomes. These findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: A Validated Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy Claims-Based Coding Algorithm: ValidATTR-US.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Lack of a validated United States (US) claims-based method for identifying transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) limits the reliability and comparability of real-world evidence. We developed and validated a US claims-based coding algorithm (ValidATTR-US) to identify patients with ATTR-CM.

METHODS: ValidATTR-US was developed by optimizing previously published algorithms using International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes and refining them using the STAnford Research Repository (STARR, claims/electronic health record-linked database; N = 61,908) to define the index cohort (n = 694). The Stanford ATTR-CM Patient Registry (N = 634) served as the validation cohort for cross-referencing the index cohort. Index cohort inclusion criteria were age ≥ 60 years at diagnosis and ≥ 2 ATTR-CM diagnosis codes (ICD-10-CM, E85.[0, 1, 2, 4, 82]) on separate days and ≥ 2 cardiac-related codes or ≥ 1 tafamidis claim. Exclusion criteria were multiple myeloma (C90), light chain amyloidosis (E85.81), hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (Z94.84), and organ-limited amyloidosis (E85.4) when co-occurring with cerebral amyloid angiopathy (I68.0), end-stage renal disease (N18.6), or skin disorders (L99). Performance metrics included accuracy ({true positives [TPs] + true negatives [TNs]}/total sample), specificity (TNs/{TNs + false positives [FPs]}), and sensitivity (TPs/{TPs + false negatives [FNs]}).

RESULTS: Accuracy was 99.51% (95% confidence interval [CI] 99.45-99.56%), specificity 99.70% (99.65-99.74%), and sensitivity 80.76% (77.47-83.76%) for detecting patients with ATTR-CM (TP, n = 512; TN, n = 61,092; FP, n = 182; FN, n = 122). Individual ICD-10-CM codes were strongly predictive of ATTR-CM case status (area under the curve [AUC] 0.84) and genotype classification (AUC 0.88).

CONCLUSION: ValidATTR-US is the first US claims-based ATTR-CM coding algorithm validated against a clinically confirmed ATTR-CM registry. Broader application may improve identification of patients with ATTR-CM in real-world datasets and help characterize prevalence and treatment patterns. Graphical abstract available for this article.

articles.title: Haplotype diversity and informativeness of three QDPR-Linked SNPs for family-based linkage analysis in an Iranian study sample.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Deficiency of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4), an essential cofactor in several enzymatic reactions, can result in hyperphenylalaninemia (HPA). Defects in several genes involved in BH4 metabolism can cause BH4 deficiency, including QDPR which encodes quinoid dihydropteridine reductase. The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the informativeness of three single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) markers linked to the QDPR gene for family-based linkage analysis.

METHODS AND RESULTS: The study cohort comprised 41 individuals, including 10 unrelated nuclear families (20 parents and 10 affected offspring) and 11 unrelated individuals without metabolic disease. Using genomic databases, three potentially informative SNP markers linked to the QDPR locus were selected. Conventional PCR products were subjected to Sanger sequencing to identify samples with confirmed genotypes for use as controls. The samples were subsequently genotyped using amplification refractory mutation system PCR (ARMS-PCR), and SNP haplotypes were reconstructed for nine families. Analysis of the three selected markers (rs1496750, rs731437, and rs16896868) showed observed heterozygosity values of 57.1%, 51.9%, and 50.0%, respectively, based on genotypes from all 20 parents and the unrelated individuals with available results for each marker. Individually, they were informative for allele transmission from at least one parent in 7, 8, and 7 families, respectively; together, they permitted transmission to be tracked from both parents in eight families.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide preliminary data on the informativeness of QDPR-linked SNP markers in the studied Iranian sample. Larger family-based studies are needed to assess potential diagnostic utility and recombination involving the flanking markers.

articles.title: Cardiac sarcoidosis or myocarditis: a diagnostic dilemma involving a multimodality multidisciplinary approach.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: Cardiac sarcoidosis and myocarditis both can share histopathological and clinical features, making a distinct diagnosis challenging. Myocarditis is presently regarded as a distinct entity with solely cardiac manifestation, a rapidly progressive clinical course, and a poorer prognosis, whereas cardiac sarcoidosis is a systemic disorder with slower disease progression. However, both conditions can present similarly, often manifesting with high-degree atrioventricular block, ventricular tachyarrhythmias, and heart failure. Despite the use of multimodality imaging, endomyocardial biopsy, and a multidisciplinary team approach, which is considered the current gold standard, making a definitive diagnosis remains challenging. This case report underscores that a non-diagnostic biopsy does not exclude cardiac sarcoidosis in a middle-aged female presenting with unexplained syncope, ventricular ectopy, regional wall motion abnormalities, and non-ischaemic late gadolinium enhancement, highlighting the critical role of a multimodality, multidisciplinary approach to guide early, tailored management.

articles.title: Progress in multimodal imaging assessment of the correlation between perivascular adipose tissue and atherosclerosis.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of death and disability worldwide. Adipose tissue dysfunction is a key driver, and perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) exerts location‑specific effects on the cardiovascular system. This review focuses on PVAT in atherosclerosis, with particular attention to pericoronary PVAT, epicardial adipose tissue (EAT), carotid PVAT, and peri-aortic adipose tissue (PAAT). PVAT homeostasis relies on UCP1‑mediated thermogenesis for metabolic modulation and on paracrine signaling via adiponectin and apelin. Under aging, obesity, or diabetes, PVAT switches from an anti‑inflammatory to a pro‑inflammatory phenotype, accelerating plaque formation through bidirectional inflammatory crosstalk. For clinical assessment, this review highlights progress in multimodal imaging technologies, including CT fat attenuation index, MRI water‑lipid separation, PET/CT, and echocardiography, for noninvasive quantification of PVAT density, composition, and metabolic activity, and compares their advantages and limitations. This review further discusses artificial intelligence (AI)-driven radiomic and radiotranscriptomic approaches that extend PVAT assessment beyond conventional single-parameter metrics. We systematically review the research progress of these techniques in evaluating dynamic PVAT changes and their correlation with atherosclerosis, aiming to clarify the intrinsic correlation between imaging‑derived PVAT functional status and AS development.

articles.title: A flap with its own blood supply: robot-assisted appendiceal ureteroplasty for complex ureteral strictures-a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Long or obliterative strictures of the upper and middle ureter are difficult to reconstruct. Ileal ureter substitution and renal autotransplantation remain established solutions, but carry procedure-specific morbidity, including bowel anastomosis and metabolic disturbance with ileal substitution and vascular complications with autotransplantation. We conducted a systematic review and single-arm proportional meta-analysis to estimate the success and safety of robot-assisted appendiceal ureteroplasty (RAU). In line with PRISMA 2020, PubMed/MEDLINE, Europe PMC, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched up to 10 October 2026 for studies describing RAU outcomes in adults with complex strictures, and data were combined with random-effects models. Four studies (63 patients) were included. Urolithiasis or its endoscopic treatment was the leading cause of stricture (52.4%), and 76.2% of repairs used an appendiceal onlay flap. Pooled surgical success at the latest available follow-up was 95.1% (95% confidence interval [CI] 85.3-98.5%). Complications of any grade occurred in 11 of 63 patients (pooled 17.5%, 95% CI 9.9-28.8%), mostly postoperative urinary tract infections (7/63; pooled 11.1%), whereas Clavien-Dindo grade III-V events occurred in 3.0% (95% CI 0.5-15.4%). The pooled rate of recurrent stricture was 3.3%, and global renal function (creatinine or eGFR) remained stable in most reported patients, although function of the reconstructed kidney was rarely assessed. Mean operative time was 238.8 min (95% CI 106.2-371.4), blood loss 56.7 mL (95% CI 17.9-95.6), and hospital stay 3.4 days (95% CI 1.5-5.3), with wide variation between centres. Published series of selected adults with right-sided strictures treated in experienced centres report high short- to intermediate-term success with RAU; its comparative safety, broader feasibility and long-term durability remain uncertain, and larger prospective series with longer follow-up are required.

articles.title: Rising demand for intensive care in pediatric pancreatitis without an increase of case numbers or disease severity: a 16-year retrospective single-center cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Between May 2024 and November 2025 eight children with pancreatitis were treated at our pediatric intensive care unit, seven of them because of the pancreatitis itself. We reviewed all pediatric pancreatitis admissions to our center from 2010 to 2025 in order to clarify whether a trend of case numbers, etiology or severity explains this clustering.

METHODS: All inpatients under 18 years with an ICD-10 code K85-K87 were identified by a search of our central clinical controlling and reviewed based on the INSPPIRE definitions. An episode required lipase or amylase at least three times the contemporaneous upper limit of normal or diagnostic imaging, together with a compatible presentation. Exclusion criteria included, among others, conditions involving exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, such as cystic fibrosis, or patients on follow-up visits. Severity was graded according to the NASPGHAN classification.

RESULTS: Of 184 identified admissions, 59 patients met the inclusion criteria: 44 acute, 7 acute recurrent and 8 chronic pancreatitis. Median age was 12 years (IQR 8-16), median stay 7 days (IQR 3-12). Biliary disease and inflammatory bowel disease were the most frequent etiologies with 10 patients each, followed by trauma and genetic variants with 7 each; 4 remained unexplained. The index episode was mild in 26 patients, moderately severe in 25, severe in 5 and could not be graded in 3. 15 patients were treated at an intensive care unit, in 9 of them the pancreatitis was the leading reason. 7 of these 9 admissions occurred in 2024-2025, one each in 2011 and 2014 and none in the nine years in between. The annual number of treated patients did not increase (10 in 2024-2025 versus 49 before), and the proportion of severe disease did not either (1/10 versus 4/49).

CONCLUSIONS: Case numbers and severity distribution remained stable over 16 years while the need for intensive care rose markedly in the last two years. Referral of complicated cases after advanced pediatric endoscopy became available locally in 2020 and a lower admission threshold are more plausible explanations than a change of the disease. A perceived local increase of severe pediatric pancreatitis should be checked against the complete case series of the center before it is reported as an epidemiological observation.

articles.title: Cannula exchange for refractory cannula infections during Berlin Heart EXCOR support: a case report.
articles.journal: Journal of artificial organs : the official journal of the Japanese Society for Artificial Organs
articles.abstract: Infection of the cannulae during Berlin Heart EXCOR (BHE) support is a serious complication, with refractory infections often necessitating surgical intervention to prevent their progression to mediastinitis. However, the treatment options for such infections are limited. We report the case of a 4-year-old girl with truncus arteriosus who developed severe heart failure after palliative right ventricular outflow tract reconstruction and aortic valve replacement. The patient successfully underwent a combined surgical procedure consisting of ventricular septal defect and aortic valve closure, redo right ventricular outflow tract reconstruction, and BHE implantation. However, at 10 months after BHE implantation, the outflow cannula exit site was infected by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis. Gallium-67 scintigraphy revealed tracer uptake along the abdominal outflow cannula tract without mediastinal extension. Because the prior aortic valve closure prevented temporary BHE explantation, surgical cannula exchange was performed together with mediastinal irrigation, omental flap transposition, and negative-pressure wound therapy. The infection resolved completely and no recurrent infection was observed during the 1-year follow-up period. In conclusion, cannula exchange combined with omental flap transposition is an effective surgical option for treating refractory cannula infections during BHE support when device explantation is not feasible.

articles.title: Effect of pelvic floor reconstruction on postoperative urinary continence after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Urinary incontinence after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) remains a common and burdensome complication. Whether pelvic floor reconstruction (PR) helps restore continence is still debated. We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science from database inception to October 8, 2026, for controlled studies comparing PR with no reconstruction (nPR) during RARP. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I² statistic. Publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots, Begg's, and Egger's tests. The certainty of evidence was rated using the GRADE approach. Twenty-two studies (5 RCTs and 17 non-RCTs) with 6425 patients (4134 PR and 2291 nPR) were included. At postoperative weeks 1, 2, 4, 12, 24, and 52, continence rates were significantly higher in the PR group than in the nPR group (pooled ORs ranged from 2.58 at 24 weeks to 2.82 at 12 weeks; all 95% CIs excluded 1). Significant heterogeneity was found at all time points except week 2 (I² = 74.3%-87.5%); the 2-week analysis showed minimal heterogeneity (I² = 0.0%). No obvious publication bias was detected. The GRADE assessment indicated that the certainty of evidence was moderate at 2 weeks and low at all other time points, primarily due to the predominance of observational studies and high heterogeneity. Pelvic floor reconstruction during RARP may improve early urinary continence recovery. However, given the low certainty of evidence, considerable heterogeneity, and the predominance of observational data, the magnitude and durability of this benefit remain uncertain. PR should be considered a reasonable option rather than a standardized intraoperative adjunct. Further high-quality, multicenter RCTs with uniform endpoints are warranted.

articles.title: Evaluation of the acceleration of orthodontic movements by applying low-level laser therapy. A randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Adult orthodontic treatment is often prolonged due to biological factors. This randomized split-mouth clinical trial evaluated the effects of low-level laser therapy (LLLT) on orthodontic tooth movement in adults by assessing osteocalcin (OC) and N-telopeptide (NTx) levels as biomarkers of bone remodeling, together with the rate of canine distalization.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Thirty adults (18-35 years) requiring extraction of the maxillary first premolars and canine distalization were included. LLLT (980 nm, 1000 mW, 15 s/point) was applied to selected hemiarches immediately after appliance activation and every two weeks for four months. Gingival crevicular fluid samples were collected before, and 14 days after activation to determine OC and NTx concentrations by ELISA. Canine distalization was measured monthly over four months.

RESULTS: Laser-treated hemiarches showed a significant increase in OC levels compared with baseline (mean difference 0.251 ng/mL, p < 0.0001), whereas changes in control hemiarches were not significant. NTx concentrations also increased significantly following orthodontic activation and were higher in laser-treated than control hemiarches (1.374 ± 0.400 vs. 1.169 ± 0.325 ng/mL, p < 0.0001). After four months, canine distalization was significantly greater in laser-treated hemiarches (4.95 ± 0.64 mm) than in controls (3.79 ± 0.56 mm, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: LLLT enhanced bone remodeling by stimulating both bone formation and resorption, resulting in accelerated orthodontic tooth movement.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These findings support LLLT as a promising adjunctive approach for reducing treatment time and contribute to the evidence needed to optimize laser-assisted orthodontic protocols.

articles.title: Circulating DKK3 is associated with insulin resistance and inflammatory cytokines across normal glucose tolerance, impaired glucose tolerance and type 2 diabetes mellitus: an exploratory cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) involves insulin resistance, inflammation, and hyperglycemia. Dickkopf-related protein 3 (DKK3) has been proposed as a metabolic biomarker, but its role in glucose homeostasis remains unclear. We thus investigated circulating DKK3 levels across normal glucose tolerance (NGT), impaired glucose tolerance (IGT), and T2DM, and its associations with adiposity, insulin resistance, and systemic inflammation.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study of 674 participants (221 NGT, 208 IGT, and 245 newly diagnosed T2DM), we measured anthropometric factors and metabolic parameters, as well as serum levels of DKK3, inflammatory cytokines, and adiponectin. The clinical significance of circulating DKK3 was evaluated through correlation analysis, multivariate regression, logistic regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Dynamic DKK3 responses during oral glucose tolerance testing (OGTT) were also assessed.

RESULTS: Circulating DKK3 rose stepwise from NGT to IGT to T2DM. It correlated positively with adiposity indices (BMI and waist circumference), glycemic parameters (fasting and post-load glucose, HbA1c, fasting insulin, and HOMA-IR), lipid profiles (triglycerides and free fatty acids), and pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-18), whereas it was negatively correlated with HDL cholesterol and adiponectin. Elevated circulating DKK3 remained independently associated with IGT and T2DM after confounder adjustment. Circulating DKK3 showed moderate apparent discrimination for IGT (AUC = 0.682) and high apparent discrimination for T2DM (AUC = 0.906) within this study cohort. As these estimates were derived and evaluated in the same cohort, they are exploratory and potentially optimistically biased. Prospective validation in independent external cohorts is therefore required before clinical translation. During OGTT, circulating DKK3 levels peaked at 30 min, with greater excursions in IGT and T2DM than in NGT.

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory cross-sectional study, circulating DKK3 was associated with progressive metabolic deterioration across NGT, IGT and T2DM, but these findings require prospective external validation and do not establish diagnostic, predictive or causal utility.

articles.title: Colposcopic magnified scanning-assisted CO2 laser treatment (CMSLT) for vaginal high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (VaHSIL): A single-center prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: To evaluate the feasibility of Colposcopic Magnified Scanning Laser Treatments (CMSLT), divided into laser excision (CMSLE) and vaporization (CMSLV), using a scanner-assisted CO2 laser as a singular outpatient therapeutic modality for patients affected by vaginal high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (vaHSIL). vaginal high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (vaHSIL) is a rare condition associated with persistent high-risk HPV infection, carrying a concrete potential for progression into invasive carcinoma. Due to diagnostic complexities and the rarity of the disease, its optimal clinical management and treatment standardization remain controversial. This prospective non-randomized cohort study was conducted between January 2022 and June 2024 on 63 patients with histologically confirmed vaHSIL. Based on the 2011 IFCPC colposcopic terminology, patients were assigned to either the CMSLV group (n = 22) or the CMSLE group (n = 41). The outpatient protocol utilized a laser system implemented with a computerized surgical scanner-assisted micromanipulator. The two-year follow-up included semi-annual screenings with HPV testing, cytology, and colposcopy. Follow-up adherence was high, with a dropout rate limited to 11.3%. The cumulative recurrence risk for vaHSIL was 14.5%, with no statistically significant difference between the two modalities, although the CMSLE group showed a higher 2-year disease-free survival rate (70% vs. 57%). The progression rate to invasive carcinoma was 1.6% 1 cases in the CMSLE cohort), revealing a 2.4% rate of occult cancer missed at initial colposcopic assignment. Only one major complication occurred (vaginal perforation, 1.6% in a post-hysterectomy patient), with no minor complications or long-term sequelae (dyspareunia or pain) reported. CMSLT may represent feasible approach since it happened to be safe, effective and associated with patient compliance. The precision of the scanner-assisted technology minimizes thermal damage and the risk of undertreating occult cancer, allowing for tailored and efficient therapy.

articles.title: Bibliometric analysis of nanotechnology research in acute kidney injury and emerging trends.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study aimed to systematically characterize the global research landscape, knowledge structure, and thematic evolution of nanotechnology research in acute kidney injury (AKI) using bibliometric and visualization approaches.

MATERIALS & METHODS: Publications were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection for the period up to December 31, 2025. After eligibility and relevance screening, 705 publications were included. CiteSpace, VOSviewer, Bibliometrix, and GraphPad Prism were used to analyze publication trends, contributions of countries, institutions, authors, and journals, collaboration and co-citation networks, highly cited references, and keyword patterns.

RESULTS: Publication output increased substantially over the study period, particularly in recent years. China contributed the largest number of publications, followed by the United States, while institutional output was concentrated predominantly in China. Collaboration networks demonstrated extensive but uneven connections across countries and institutions. Journal of Controlled Release was the most productive journal, whereas Kidney International was the most highly co-cited journal. The most frequent keywords were "acute kidney injury," "nanoparticles," and "oxidative stress." Temporal analyses showed a gradual evolution from broad experimental and imaging-related applications toward greater emphasis on oxidative stress, reactive oxygen species, therapeutic delivery, and mechanism-oriented nanotechnology. Ferroptosis also appeared among the more recent trend topics.

CONCLUSION: Nanotechnology research in AKI has expanded into an increasingly interdisciplinary field integrating nephrology, materials science, nanomedicine, and drug-delivery research. Current themes emphasize oxidative injury, targeted delivery, and increasingly mechanism-oriented nanoplatforms. Future research should prioritize rigorous evaluation of targeting performance, pharmacokinetics, biosafety, reproducibility, and translational feasibility to determine the clinical value of emerging nanotechnology strategies for AKI.

articles.title: Proton pump inhibitors in antithrombotic therapy: gastroprotection, drug interactions, and clinical management.
articles.abstract: Antithrombotic therapy is central to the prevention of thromboembolic and ischaemic events in patients with coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, and after percutaneous coronary intervention, but is accompanied by an increased risk of gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB). Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) can reduce upper GIB, although their optimal use across different antithrombotic regimens, potential drug interactions, and inability to prevent lower GIB remain clinically relevant concerns. This structured narrative review examines PPI co-therapy in patients receiving antiplatelet agents, oral anticoagulants, or combined antithrombotic treatment. MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to August 2026, supplemented by contemporary cardiology and gastroenterology guidelines. Randomized trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and large observational studies were prioritized. Evidence indicates that PPIs provide clinically meaningful protection against acid-related upper GIB, particularly in high-risk patients receiving aspirin-containing regimens, dual antiplatelet therapy, or intensified antithrombotic therapy, whereas evidence in isolated oral anticoagulation remains predominantly observational. PPI co-therapy should therefore be targeted according to gastrointestinal bleeding risk and antithrombotic intensity, with periodic reassessment as treatment changes, rather than used as universal gastrointestinal protection. KEY POINTS: • Proton pump inhibitors can reduce the risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding in patients receiving antithrombotic therapy, but their benefit is greatest in patients with additional gastrointestinal bleeding risk factors • Their use should therefore be individualized according to gastrointestinal risk and the intensity of antithrombotic treatment rather than prescribed routinely to all patients • The need for gastroprotection should be reassessed whenever the antithrombotic regimen or the patient's bleeding risk changes.

articles.title: The effect of listening to Qur'an on quality of life and sleep quality in breast cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: To investigate the effect of listening to Qur'an on quality of life and sleep quality in women undergoing chemotherapy for breast cancer. This randomized controlled trial used an open-label design at the participant level, with blinded statistical analysis. Participants were assigned using block randomization to either a Qur'an listening group (QLG) or a control group (CG). During each chemotherapy session, the QLG listened through headphones to a standardized recording of Surah Yasin played on a music player and repeated until the chemotherapy session was completed. The intervention was administered once every 21 days for a total of four sessions, while the CG received standard care only. Data were collected at four time points (T1-T4) using a Breast Cancer Patient Information Form, the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire-Core 30 (EORTC QLQ-C30), Version 3.0, and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Analyses were performed using SPSS 26. Significant Group × Time interactions were observed for several EORTC QLQ-C30 functional and symptom domains after adjustment for multiple comparisons. Global quality of life also showed a significant Group × Time interaction (p = 0.008), indicating different patterns of change between the QLG and CG across the four measurement points. Between-group differences in global quality of life were significant at T2 and T3. For sleep quality, the Group × Time interaction for PSQI total scores was significant after Holm correction (p < 0.001), and PSQI scores were significantly lower in the QLG than in the CG at T4 (p < 0.001). Qur'an listening during chemotherapy was associated with changes in patient-reported quality of life and sleep quality among women with breast cancer. Given the study limitations, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and require confirmation in larger randomized controlled trials.Trial registrationNCT06893770.

articles.title: Robotics in endoscopic spine surgery: a scoping review of clinical applications, workflow integration, and patient outcomes.
articles.abstract: Robotic and endoscopic technologies are increasingly being combined in spine surgery, yet the clinical literature remains fragmented across procedures, platforms, and robotic functions. We conducted a scoping review to map clinical applications of robot-assisted endoscopic spine surgery, describe how robotic systems are incorporated into endoscopic workflows, and summarize the technical, perioperative, and patient-centered outcomes reported to date. PubMed and Scopus were searched through September 2026. Human clinical reports were eligible when endoscopy constituted part of the operative visualization or working approach and a robotic system directly assisted the same spinal procedure. Study selection was reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Of 374 records identified, 122 duplicates were removed and 252 records were screened. Sixty-six reports were sought, 13 were not retrieved, 53 full texts were assessed, and 24 studies were included. The evidence comprised 11 comparative studies, four uncontrolled clinical series, and nine case-based or technical clinical reports. Applications ranged from discectomy and decompression to interbody fusion, pars repair, infection, trauma, and thoracic or craniovertebral procedures. Robots were used for trajectory planning, localization, percutaneous access, guidewire or pedicle screw placement, drilling, endoscope stabilization, and interbody instrumentation. Comparative studies most often showed gains in fluoroscopy use, access efficiency, or instrumentation accuracy; patient-reported outcomes were usually similar between groups. Robotic-endoscopic integration is clinically feasible across an expanding range of spinal procedures, but its patient-level value remains incompletely defined.

articles.title: Carbonyl stress as the missing molecular link between diabetes and neurodegeneration: a unified mechanistic framework for type 3 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus is associated with an increased risk of cognitive dysfunction and neurodegenerative changes, contributing to the emerging concept of "Type 3 Diabetes," characterized by impaired cerebral insulin signaling and altered brain glucose metabolism. However, the metabolic processes connecting systemic metabolic dysfunction with cerebral insulin resistance remain incompletely understood. This review examines carbonyl stress, particularly methylglyoxal and other reactive dicarbonyls, as potential links between dysregulated glucose metabolism and impaired cerebral insulin signaling. We evaluate MGO generation and glyoxalase-mediated detoxification, evidence linking carbonyl stress with insulin-signaling abnormalities and interactions among AGE-RAGE signaling, oxidative stress and neuroinflammation. Particular emphasis is placed on distinguishing evidence from peripheral insulin-responsive tissues, vascular compartments and neuronal models, given the limited direct in vivo evidence establishing MGO as a cause of cerebral insulin resistance. The review further considers potential consequences for neuronal metabolism, synaptic function, and neurodegenerative vulnerability, alongside emerging therapeutic strategies targeting carbonyl metabolism and related pathways, including intranasal nanocarrier-mediated delivery. Overall, carbonyl stress represents a biologically plausible but not yet established molecular link between diabetes-associated metabolic dysfunction and neurodegenerative vulnerability, warranting brain-specific studies to determine its causal and therapeutic relevance.

articles.title: Diagnostic yield and early outcomes of radical prostatectomy without prior histopathologic diagnosis: a single-arm systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the pathological, oncological, and functional outcomes of radical prostatectomy (RP) performed without prior histopathologic confirmation of prostate cancer in patients with a high clinical suspicion of clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa).

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Google Scholar, and Cochrane databases for studies evaluating biopsy-free RP. Adult men with a high clinical suspicion of csPCa based on multiparametric MRI and/or PSMA-PET with elevated PSA or PSA density were included. A single-arm random-effects meta-analysis was performed to estimate the pooled proportions of csPCa, benign pathology, overtreatment, and positive surgical margins (PSM).

RESULTS: Eleven studies comprising 648 patients were included, csPCa was identified in 94.2% of patients (95% CI, 88.4-97.2), whereas benign pathology occurred in only 0.3%. The pooled overtreatment rate was 5.7%, and PSM was observed in 25.4% of cases. Study-level subgroup analysis suggested a higher diagnostic yield in biopsy-naïve cohorts than in cohorts including patients with a previous negative biopsy (95% vs. 80%; p = 0.005), with no significant differences according to imaging modality or surgical approach. Functional outcomes suggested favorable early urinary continence and erectile function recovery; however, heterogeneous and incomplete reporting precluded quantitative synthesis, and these findings were based on descriptive data only. Overall risk of bias was serious, primarily because of verification bias arising from participant selection.

CONCLUSIONS: Biopsy-free RP is a promising imaging-driven strategy for highly selected patients with a high probability of csPCa, demonstrating a high pathological yield of clinically significant disease and a very low observed rate of benign surgery. However, the PSM rate of 25.4% remains a concern, particularly given the absence of a comparator arm. Until further prospective studies confirm these findings, this approach should be reserved for carefully selected patients at high-volume centers following multidisciplinary evaluation and counseling.

articles.title: Physiological prehabilitation for patients undergoing cellular therapy in multiple myeloma and lymphoma: a systematic review.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate physiological prehabilitation for adults with multiple myeloma or lymphoma undergoing cellular or immune-based therapies and to describe intervention characteristics and programme duration.

BACKGROUND: Fatigue, physical deconditioning, and muscle weakness can compromise treatment readiness and quality of life (QoL). Evidence on exercise begun before these therapies remains limited.

METHODS: Six databases were searched from inception to 4 September 2026. Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) and quasi-experimental studies were eligible if exercise began before stem cell transplantation, chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy, or bispecific T-cell engager (BiTE) therapy and assessed physical function plus muscle strength, QoL, or fatigue. Joanna Briggs Institute tools informed methodological appraisal. Findings were synthesised narratively by outcome, alongside exercise characteristics and duration.

RESULTS: Twelve studies (501 participants), comprising three pilot RCTs and nine quasi-experimental studies, were included. Ten evaluated transplantation and two CAR-T therapy; none evaluated BiTE therapy. Aerobic plus resistance or strength exercise predominated, and nine programmes reported a central or protocol duration within 4-8 weeks. Physical function and lower-limb performance findings were generally favourable; handgrip strength, QoL, and fatigue findings were mixed. Heterogeneous methods and predominantly uncontrolled designs limited interpretation.

CONCLUSIONS: Physiological prehabilitation shows preliminary promise for functional preparation before treatment. Aerobic and resistance exercise and the commonly reported programme durations warrant comparative evaluation.

IMPLICATIONS: Adequately powered, therapy-specific RCTs should standardise exercise reporting, assess clinically meaningful outcomes, and evaluate safety and sustained recovery after treatment.

articles.title: Effect of oral vitamin D₃₃ supplementation on salivary vitamin D levels and orthodontic treatment duration: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effect of systemic oral vitamin D₃ supplementation on salivary vitamin D₃ levels during different phases of orthodontic treatment and on the overall orthodontic treatment duration in adolescents undergoing fixed orthodontic treatment.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A randomized controlled trial was conducted among 52 adolescents (13-18 years) with Angle's Class I malocclusion requiring extraction of all four first premolars. Participants were randomly allocated into two groups: Group 1 (control; n = 26) received no vitamin D₃ supplementation, while Group 2 (supplementation; n = 26) received oral vitamin D₃ (60,000 IU every 20 days). Allocation concealment was achieved using the Sequentially Numbered Opaque Sealed Envelope (SNOSE) method. Unstimulated saliva samples were collected at three treatment phases: T1 (archwire insertion), T2 (extraction space closure), and T3 (debonding). Salivary vitamin D₃ concentrations were quantified using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Overall orthodontic treatment duration was recorded from initial archwire placement to appliance debonding. Statistical analysis was performed using independent samples t-tests, with statistical significance set at p ≤ 0.05.

RESULTS: Baseline salivary vitamin D₃ levels were comparable between the two groups. Participants receiving vitamin D₃ supplementation demonstrated significantly higher salivary vitamin D₃ concentrations during extraction space closure (44.39 ± 5.22 ng/mL vs. 38.19 ± 8.65 ng/mL; p = 0.003) and at debonding (48.31 ± 4.86 ng/mL vs. 39.91 ± 8.04 ng/mL; p < 0.001) compared with the control group. The supplementation group also demonstrated a significantly shorter overall orthodontic treatment duration (17.81 ± 1.12 months) than the control group (19.50 ± 1.35 months), corresponding to a mean reduction of 1.69 months (approximately 51 days; p < 0.001). No significant gender-related differences in salivary vitamin D₃ levels were observed.

CONCLUSION: Oral vitamin D₃ supplementation was associated with higher salivary vitamin D₃ levels during key phases of orthodontic treatment and a significant reduction in overall treatment duration. Salivary monitoring of vitamin D₃ may have potential as a useful non-invasive biomarker to guide targeted supplementation strategies aimed at improving orthodontic treatment efficiency, however, further studies are required to establish its clinical utility in guiding supplementation.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Vitamin D₃ supplementation may represent a simple, minimally invasive adjunctive strategy for improving orthodontic treatment efficiency. Monitoring salivary vitamin D₃ levels offers a practical, non-invasive method for assessing vitamin D status, particularly in children and adolescents undergoing prolonged orthodontic treatment. However, supplementation should be individualized and guided by clinical assessment, and further studies are required before routine clinical implementation.

articles.title: First report of Stemphylium eturmiunum causing leaf spot on Eucalyptus tricarpa in Australian native vegetation.
articles.abstract: Eucalyptus spp. dominate Australia's most environmentally and economically significant ecosystems due to their ecological resilience (through post-fire epicormic regeneration), and widespread occurrence in remnant vegetation adjacent to agricultural crops, where they can influence disease dynamics and biosecurity risk (Keane et al. 2000). In March 2025, leaves from epicormic growth of two mature Eucalyptus tricarpa trees exhibiting concolorous 35 mm2 (15% leaf area) asymmetrical brown, sunken necrotic lesions with dark margins were collected from native vegetation near Anglesea, Victoria (38°22'27" S, 144°14'43" E). Approximately 10% of epicormic leaves of adjacent E. tricarpa within a 100 m radius of the site displayed similar lesions. The leaves were surface sterilized (80% ethanol) and sections from lesion margins were cultured (25°C, one week). Hyphal tips were subcultured onto Potato Dextrose Agar (PDA). One lesion yielded three morphologically distinct isolates, including Alternaria sp., Allelochaeta sp., and Stemphylium sp., the second lesion yielded a further two distinct isolates, including Readeriella sp., and Neofusiccocum eucalypticola. All species isolated are known Eucalyptus pathogens (Crous et al. 2018; Keane et al. 2000), except Stemphylium sp. (UOM26001), which was examined further. This genus comprises important agricultural pathogens but are unknown from Australian native vegetation (Vaghefi et al. 2020). Two week-old PDA cultures had pale salmon mycelium and brown sporulation rings. Microscopic examination revealed hyaline few-septate hyphae, and mid-brown vertically and transversely 2-4-septate globose conidia 23.6 ± 3.38 x 17.6 ± 2.59 µm (21.0 - 30.9 x 12.3 - 22.8 µm), n=16, consistent with Stemphylium spp. (Simmons 2001). DNA was extracted via a modified Qiagen Plant MiniKit protocol (Vaghefi et al. 2024), and PCR and Sanger sequencing was performed for the internal transcribed spacer region and intervening 5.8S (ITS), calmodulin and gapdh with primers ITS1/ITS4 (White et al. 1990), caldf1/caldr2 (Carbone and Kohn 1999), and Gpd1/Gpd2 (Berbee et al. 1999). Sequences were deposited in GenBank as PZ054204 (ITS), PZ055902 (cal), PZ055903 (gapdh). BLAST showed all sequences were identical to Stemphylium eturmiunum reference sequences, including ex-holotype (CBS 109845). Multi-locus phylogenetic analysis was performed using RaxML v8.2.11 and MrBayes v3.2.6 (GTR model and 10 000 bootstrap replicates). UOM26001 clustered with S. eturmiunum isolates, with bootstrap and posterior probability values of 96 and 1.00, respectively. To assess pathogenicity, detached leaf assays were conducted due to constraints in sourcing whole trees for representative in planta assays, and biosecurity restrictions for trials external to a laboratory space. Therefore, following a standard method for Eucalyptus spp. bioassays (Alcova et al. 2026) sprigs of E. tricarpa epicormic growth each had 2 leaves surface sterilized (1% NaClO) and inoculated with 1 mm2 plugs of one week old UOM26001 via wounding (abrasions with sterile scalpel) (n = 6) and non-wounding (n = 6) methods. Negative controls (n = 6) were sterilized, wounded, and inoculated with clean PDA. Sprigs were placed in water and incubated for two weeks (12 - 20°C, 90% humidity, 12hr photoperiod), pathogenicity assays were repeated 3 times, for a total of 6 replicates of each inoculation method, including the control. After 14 days, 3/6 wounded, and 2/6 non-wounded inoculated leaves displayed pale brown necrotic lesions, similar but not identical to the original lesion due to the field symptoms being caused by a disease complex rather than UOM26001 alone. Negative controls were symptom free. Sections from lesion margins were plated onto PDA and incubated for one week at 25°C. Colonies re-isolated from all inoculated symptomatic leaf lesions were identified as S. eturmiunum based on culture and conidia morphology, confirming pathogenicity.
