Stemphylium eturmiunum is known in Australia and globally as a pathogen of agricultural crops (Vaghefi et al. 2020), but this is the first report on native Eastern Australian vegetation, and on E. tricarpa globally. This suggests S. eturmiunum may threaten post-fire regeneration of native trees by destroying new photosynthetic surfaces. And while this report cannot fully confirm significance for E. tricarpa due to only a single isolate being recovered, the detection in native vegetation expands the host range of S. eturmiunum, indicating E. tricarpa remnant vegetation could act as a pathogen reservoir, facilitating crop infection in Australian agricultural settings.

articles.title: Outcomes with Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis versus Mechanical Thrombectomy for Patients with Intermediate/High Risk Pulmonary Embolism: A Meta-Analysis of 24,090 Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Randomized trials comparing the outcomes with catheter-directed medical thrombolysis (CDT) versus mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for patients with intermediate/high risk pulmonary embolism (PE) are limited. This meta-analysis aimed to assess the clinical outcomes after CDT versus MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE.

METHODS: Eligible studies compared CDT and MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE underwent catheter-based therapies were retrieved from a comprehensive literature search for PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL through June 2026. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, major bleeding, and the length of intensive care unit (ICU) stay. Summary estimates were analyzed using a random effects model.

RESULTS: A total of 18 studies (24,090 intermediate/high risk patients) were eligible for the analysis. CDT was associated with longer length of intensive care unit (ICU) stay (mean difference: 1.01 days, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.87-1.15) compared with MT. While there was no statistical difference between the two groups regarding the risk of all-cause mortality (risk ratio [RR] 0.88, 95% CI 0.76-1.01, p = 0.068) and major bleeding (RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.74-1.55, p = 0.705). Similarly, the incidence of other clinical outcomes; all-cause readmission, PE-related readmission, blood transfusion rates, length of hospital stay, cardiac arrest, and stroke, were similar between the two groups.

CONCLUSION: Among patients with intermediate/high risk PE treated with catheter-based therapies, there was no difference regarding the clinical outcomes between CDT and MT, but CDT was associated with a longer ICU stay. Larger, well designed randomized trials are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: [Multimodal prevention and risk reduction of cardiovascular diseases with focus on obesity and diabetes].
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of death worldwide. Obesity and diabetes mellitus are among the most important modifiable cardiovascular risk factors, promoting the development of atherosclerosis through chronic inflammation, insulin resistance, dyslipidemia and vascular injury. Effective prevention focuses on lifestyle interventions, including dietary optimization and regular physical activity, supported by digital health applications where appropriate. If conservative measures are insufficient, pharmacotherapy, such as sodium-glucose transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors and incretin-based drugs as well as metabolic surgery, should be considered according to the clinical indications. In addition, optimal blood pressure and lipid control are essential. Long-term cardiovascular risk reduction requires an individualized, interdisciplinary prevention strategy integrating medical, behavioral and societal interventions.

articles.title: Pathological Characteristics and Mechanisms of Sepsis-Induced Testicular Dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Sepsis, a serious life-threatening systemic inflammatory disease, has not received enough attention for the testicular dysfunction it causes. The testis is not only a reproductive organ, but also an important endocrine gland that secretes testosterone and other sex hormones. This study aimed to systematically investigate the persistent damage caused by sepsis to testicular function and to explore the underlying mechanisms, with a focus on macrophages. Clinical observations were performed in sepsis patients, and animal experiments were conducted using the cecal ligation and puncture model. Macrophage depletion experiments were further performed to confirm the mechanistic role of macrophages. Clinical observations showed significant low testosterone levels in patients during both acute and recovery phases. In mice, testicular tissue damage and spermatogenic dysfunction occurred at 24 hours post-cecal ligation and puncture and persisted through day 14. Mechanistic studies revealed that sepsis triggers oxidative stress injury by inducing testicular macrophages proliferation and promoting excessive release of pro-inflammatory factors and reactive oxygen species. Macrophage depletion largely abolished sepsis-induced testicular injury. In conclusion, sepsis causes persistent testicular injury through macrophage-associated inflammatory and oxidative stress responses. These findings elucidate the pathogenesis of sepsis-induced testicular injury and identify potential therapeutic targets for improving reproductive-endocrine function and overall prognosis in sepsis patients.

articles.title: The role of antimicrobial polypeptides in predicting urinary tract infection: UTILISE study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGOUND: Urinary tract infection (UTI) is among the most common serious bacterial infections in childhood. Antimicrobial polypeptides (AMPs) are key effector molecules of the innate immune system and play a crucial role in protecting against infections. The aim of the study was to assess serum and urinary levels of AMPs to determine their ability to distinguish UTI from non-UTI infection, contamination, asymptomatic bacteriuria and healthy control groups.

METHODS: A total of 520 children between ages 0 and 18 years old with UTI, asymptomatic bacteriuria, contamination, non-UTI infections and healthy controls were participated from 37 pediatric nephrology centers. In all groups, pre-treatment blood and urine samples were obtained before the initiation of antibiotics at the admission. In the UTI group, post-treatment samples were also collected after treatment. Serum and urine levels of cathelicidin, defensin-α, defensin-β, hepcidin, lactoferrin, ribonuclease 7 (RNase7), and secretory leukocyte protease inhibitor were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) technique.

RESULTS: Urinary cathelicidin and β-defensin-2 levels were significantly higher in children with UTI than in all comparator groups (all adjusted p < 0.001). Urinary cathelicidin and β-defensin-2 levels decreased significantly after treatment. Other AMPs did not reliably distinguish UTI from contamination, asymptomatic bacteriuria, or non-UTI infections. ROC analysis showed moderate diagnostic performance for urinary cathelicidin (AUC 0.714) and β-defensin-2 (AUC 0.766). Combining both biomarkers increased specificity (85.4%) but reduced sensitivity (67.5%).

CONCLUSION: Urinary cathelicidin and β-defensin-2 were the most promising biomarkers for pediatric UTI, demonstrating moderate discriminatory ability. Although insufficient as standalone diagnostic tests, they may serve as useful adjunctive tools to improve diagnostic confidence in children with suspected UTI.

articles.title: Patent ductus arteriosus and neonatal acute kidney injury-a comparative analysis of treatment strategies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the impact of ductal treatment timing, treatment modality and cumulative ductal exposure on the incidence of acute kidney injury (AKI) in very preterm infants with patent ductus arteriosus (PDA). Additionally, to determine whether high-risk PDA phenotype is independently associated with AKI after adjustment for confounding variables, and to assess whether the initial medical agent for ductal closure is associated with post-treatment AKI.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of 184 infants born under 29 weeks' gestation admitted to a tertiary neonatal unit between 2020-2023. PDA severity was stratified using the El-Khuffash PDA score (high risk ≥5). AKI was defined using the modified neonatal KDIGO criteria. Time-anchored outcomes were used to address AKI temporality. Multivariable bias-reduced logistic regression was performed to control for gestational age, condition at birth, gender and small-for-gestational-age status.

RESULTS: Median gestational age was 26.6 weeks with a median birth weight of 863 g. AKI occurred in 28/175 infants (16%) with 20/28 (71%) occurring by day of life fourteen. AKI incidence was 19.6% in the high-risk, refractory to medical treatment infants, 21.8% in the high-risk responsive to medical treatment infants and 8.7% in low-risk infants. Among high-risk treated infants, post-treatment AKI occurred in 17.1% with no discrepancy between paracetamol-first (14.7%) and ibuprofen-first (18.3%) strategies (adjusted OR 1.63, 0.49-5.48).

CONCLUSION: In this cohort of premature infants with PDA, AKI was common in crude analyses. Among high-risk treated infants, ibuprofen-first treatment strategy was not associated with increased post-treatment AKI, though estimates were imprecise and confounding by indication remains likely.

articles.title: Cortical morphometric similarity alterations and molecular correlates in acute ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Ischemic stroke is associated with distributed cortical structural alterations, but the molecular context of acute-stage morphometric similarity (MS) changes remains unclear. This study aimed to characterize MS alterations in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and examine their spatial transcriptomic correlates using the Allen Human Brain Atlas.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional case-control study, 36 patients with first-ever AIS involving the unilateral basal ganglia and/or corona radiata and 36 healthy controls (HCs) were included. Patients were enrolled within 7 days after symptom onset, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was performed in the acute stage. Whole-brain MS networks were derived from multiple cortical morphometric features. Group differences in regional MS were assessed with adjustment for age, sex, education, and infarction volume. Spatial associations between MS alterations and gene expression were examined using partial least squares regression with post-mortem transcriptomic data from the Allen Human Brain Atlas (AHBA). Correlations between regional MS values and plasma metal concentrations were examined in patients with AIS.

RESULTS: AIS patients exhibited regionally heterogeneous MS alterations, with increased MS mainly in the lateral occipital, lingual, postcentral, and pericalcarine cortices, and decreased MS mainly in the superior frontal, precuneus, and superior temporal regions. Imaging-transcriptomic integration showed that these spatial MS changes were associated with gene expression profiles related to neuronal viability, transcriptional co-regulation, and cellular stress-related pathways. After permutation testing and false discovery rate (FDR) correction, significant associations were identified between right precuneus MS and plasma lead (Pb) and cesium (Cs) levels.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify region-specific MS alterations in AIS and provide spatial transcriptomic context for early post-stroke structural changes.

articles.title: Susceptibility-weighted imaging findings in subacute sclerosing panencephalitis: subcortical paramagnetic rim and deep gray matter changes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder caused by persistent measles virus infection. Conventional MRI plays a key role in diagnosis and staging; however, susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) findings in SSPE have not been systematically characterized, particularly with respect to their relationship to disease burden and neurodegeneration. With this study we aim to evaluate SWI changes in SSPE, with emphasis on the Subcortical Paramagnetic Rim (SPR) and deep gray matter mineralization, and to assess their association with parenchymal disease burden and cerebral atrophy.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 126 patients with confirmed SSPE who underwent MRI including SWI. T2/FLAIR hyperintensities were assessed across predefined supratentorial and infratentorial parenchymal regions. A composite total parenchymal disease burden score was calculated. Cerebral atrophy and deep gray matter mineralization were evaluated using semi-quantitative visual grading systems. SWI was also assessed for the presence of a SPR. Associations between susceptibility findings, parenchymal disease burden, cerebral atrophy, and clinical parameters were analyzed using non-parametric statistical methods.

RESULTS: SPR was identified in 14 of 128 MRI studies (10.9%), most commonly involving the parietal lobes. Patients with the rim had significantly longer symptom duration, higher disease stage, greater parenchymal disease burden, higher atrophy scores, and higher deep gray matter mineralization scores compared with patients without the rim (p < 0.01). Deep gray matter mineralization scores showed significant positive correlations with both global parenchymal disease burden and cerebral atrophy (Spearman's ρ, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: SPR and deep gray matter mineralization, are associated with increasing parenchymal disease burden and atrophy. These findings likely represent imaging markers of disease chronicity and provide complementary information to conventional MRI, particularly in the evaluation of chronic encephalitis in measles-endemic regions.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of oliceridine versus remifentanil for analgesia in mechanically ventilated critically ill adults (CO-ROAM): a multicenter, assessor-blinded, non-inferiority randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Remifentanil provides effective analgesia during invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), but its utility is limited by opioid-related adverse events. Oliceridine, a G protein-biased μ-opioid receptor agonist, may decouple analgesia from these effects, but lacks evidence in critically ill patients.

METHODS: This multicentre, assessor- and patient-blinded, non-inferiority randomised controlled trial was conducted across 19 intensive care units (ICUs) in China. Adults receiving IMV were randomised 1:1 to oliceridine or remifentanil, titrated to a Critical-Care Pain Observation Tool score below 3. The primary endpoint was time in target analgesic range (TTR; non-inferiority margin -10%).

RESULTS: Of 307 randomised patients, 304 comprised the modified intention-to-treat population (151 oliceridine, 153 remifentanil). Median TTR was 96.0% versus 92.3% (absolute difference 3.7%, 95% CI -0.3-5.7%). Oliceridine was associated with fewer mild-to-moderate adverse drug reactions (ADRs), occurring at 15.9 versus 22.2 events per 100 patient-days (IRR 0.72, 95% CI 0.52-1.00, P = 0.049), and a lower rate of respiratory depression during the study period (0% vs. 4.6%, P = 0.015). Post-extubation respiratory depression (0% vs. 7.9%, P = 0.005) and analgesic-sedation costs were both lower with oliceridine. IMV duration, ICU stay, and 28-day mortality did not differ. Subgroup analyses identified a nominal ADR benefit in patients with Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II > 17 and a larger nominal TTR difference in those without acute respiratory distress syndrome.

CONCLUSION: Oliceridine provides non-inferior analgesia to remifentanil with a more favourable respiratory safety profile and lower costs in critically ill adults.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06454292 (registered June 11, 2024).

articles.title: Molecular mapping of the stem rust resistance gene rpg8 in barley.
articles.abstract: Barley can be attacked by both the wheat stem rust pathogen (Puccinia graminis f. sp. tritici) and the rye stem rust pathogen (P. graminis f. sp. secalis) in the northern Great Plains region. The stem rust resistance of the landrace Black Hull-less was first described in response to an isolate of P. graminis f. sp. secalis. This resistance is conferred by a single recessive gene (designated as rpgBH), whose chromosomal position has not been determined. The objective of this investigation was to map this resistance gene on the barley genome and determine the resistance spectrum of Black Hull-less to a diverse panel of both domestic and foreign P. graminis isolates. To map rpgBH, a cross was made between Black Hull-less and the susceptible cultivar Steptoe. Phenotypic evaluations of the resulting F2 population to P. graminis f. sp. secalis isolate A20MN04-2 confirmed the recessive gene action of rpgBH. Genotyping data based on a 3K genotyping platform positioned the gene to the short arm of chromosome 6H. Since rpgBH maps to a genomic position different from all previously described stem rust resistance genes in barley, it was given the new locus designation of rpg8. In seedling assays made against a diverse panel of P. graminis isolates, Black Hull-less exhibited low infection types (from 1 to 23-) to P. graminis f. sp. tritici races MCCFC, QCCJB, HKHJC, TTKSK, TTKTT, TTRTF, and JRCQC and P. graminis f. sp. secalis isolates A20MN04-2 and 92-MN-90, but mostly high infection types (3-2 to 3-3) to P. graminis f. sp. tritici races TTTTF, TKTTF, and TTRTF. Although further evaluations should be made to confirm the adult plant resistance of Black Hull-less in the field, rpg8 may enhance and broaden stem rust resistance in barley.

articles.title: Ciguatoxins alter RyR2 gating, intracellular Ca²⁺ handling and cardiac function in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes and rats.
articles.abstract: Ciguatoxins (CTXs) cause ciguatera, a seafood-borne intoxication frequently associated with cardiovascular manifestations, but the underlying cardiac mechanisms remain poorly understood. We investigated the effects of purified CTX-1B and CTX-3 C in human induced pluripotent stem-cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs), porcine cardiac ryanodine receptor type 2 (RyR2) channels, and rats. In hiPSC-CMs, CTX-1B and CTX-3 C (0.3-5 nM) rapidly increased diastolic intracellular Ca²⁺ and altered spontaneous Ca²⁺ transients. At 5 nM, CTXs increased transient frequency, reduced transient amplitude, impaired contractile performance, and disrupted sarcomeric organisation. In planar lipid bilayers, CTX-1B (1 nM) prolonged RyR2 openings under resting cytosolic Ca²⁺ conditions and remodelled channel gating after activation with ATP (25 µM). Molecular docking predicted a CTX-1B interaction region within the RyR2 transmembrane domain, close to ligand-sensitive regulatory elements, supporting state-dependent modulation of channel gating. Cardiac sheets exposed to CTX showed reduced spontaneous field-potential activity and contraction. In rats, intravenous CTX-1B administration (0.13 ng/g bodyweight) caused bradycardia, premature atrial and ventricular contractions, atrioventricular conduction abnormalities, and atrial flutter. Echocardiography revealed impaired myocardial deformation and relaxation despite preserved ejection fraction. These findings identify altered RyR2 gating and intracellular Ca²⁺ dysregulation as plausible complementary contributors to CTX cardiotoxicity and extend the established mechanism based on persistent voltage-gated Na⁺-channel activation. Combined disruption of sarcolemmal excitability and intracellular Ca²⁺ release could explain the acute electrical and mechanical cardiac abnormalities associated with ciguatera.

articles.title: [Importance of ventricular extrasystole coupling intervals for risk stratification].
articles.abstract: The importance of measuring the coupling intervals of ventricular extrasystoles is discussed, with practical diagnostic, prognostic and therapeutic application in various clinical situations: risk stratification of malignant ventricular arrhythmia and sudden death in cases with short and long coupling interval of ventricular extrasystoles; diagnosis of a variety of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia with repercussions in the therapeutic decision to be made; risk stratification of ventricular tachycardia of the right ventricular outflow tract, benign and malignant forms; localization of the origin of ventricular extrasystoles and risk stratification of sudden death in ischemic heart disease and heart failure.

articles.title: Rethinking the comprehensive management of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM).
articles.journal: Netherlands heart journal : monthly journal of the Netherlands Society of Cardiology and the Netherlands Heart Foundation

articles.title: Arrhythmia management in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.
articles.journal: Netherlands heart journal : monthly journal of the Netherlands Society of Cardiology and the Netherlands Heart Foundation
articles.abstract: Arrhythmias are common in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) and contribute substantially to morbidity at all disease stages. The arrhythmogenic substrate-reflecting diffuse amyloid infiltration, atrial myopathy, autonomic dysfunction, and conduction system involvement-differs fundamentally from that in other cardiomyopathies. Prospective rhythm monitoring reveals a burden substantially higher than previously recognised and predominantly asymptomatic, with bradyarrhythmias and atrial fibrillation (AF) dominating and sustained ventricular arrhythmias remaining rare.This review examines key aspects of arrhythmia management in ATTR-CM. Conduction system disease is frequently encountered, and pacing strategies-including conduction system pacing-are discussed in the context of progressive infiltrative disease. We address the rationale for lifelong anticoagulation in AF irrespective of CHA2DS2-VA-score, and emerging considerations for anticoagulation in selected sinus rhythm patients with impaired atrial function. Rhythm control strategies are reviewed in light of extensive atrial substrate, high AF recurrence rates, and the absence of randomised trial data. The role of implantable cardioverter-defibrillators is examined, with emphasis on the lack of proven survival benefit for primary prevention. Finally, we explore disease-modifying therapies and their potential to attenuate the arrhythmogenic substrate. Overall, structured surveillance, rhythm control, and individualised device decisions form the cornerstones of modern arrhythmia management in ATTR-CM.

articles.title: Transforming cardiac amyloidosis care: navigating the evolving diagnostic and therapeutic landscape.
articles.journal: Netherlands heart journal : monthly journal of the Netherlands Society of Cardiology and the Netherlands Heart Foundation
articles.abstract: Amyloidosis comprises a group of systemic disorders caused by extracellular deposition of misfolded precursor proteins, leading to progressive organ dysfunction. Cardiac amyloidosis, particularly transthyretin-related amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) has transitioned from a rare and underdiagnosed condition to a treatable disease, driven by major advances in diagnostic imaging, increased disease awareness, and the approval of disease-modifying therapies. These therapies target transthyretin (TTR) stabilization and amyloid production or deposition and have led to an evolving therapeutic landscape. As therapeutic efficacy is greatest in earlier disease stages, timely recognition is crucial. Effective management of ATTR-CM requires structured screening of high-risk populations, multidisciplinary collaboration, and longitudinal follow-up. This review provides a practical, clinician-focused framework that addresses clinical presentation and "red flags" to facilitate early detection. It offers a comprehensive overview of the diagnostic pathway, including (AI-enabled) electrocardiography analysis, (non-)invasive imaging modalities, biomarkers, and genetic testing. Additionally, emerging therapeutic strategies are discussed, encompassing supportive heart failure management, amyloid-specific treatments such as TTR stabilizers and gene silencers, and novel approaches including fibril depletion and gene-editing therapies. As the therapeutic paradigm shifts from disease stabilization toward potential reversal, early diagnosis and personalized treatment strategies are essential to improve prognosis and quality of life in patients with cardiac amyloidosis.

articles.title: Cardiac amyloidosis: the role of multimodality imaging.
articles.journal: Netherlands heart journal : monthly journal of the Netherlands Society of Cardiology and the Netherlands Heart Foundation
articles.abstract: Cardiac amyloidosis is an increasingly recognized cause of heart failure, driven by advances in diagnostic techniques and the emergence of disease-modifying therapies. Early and accurate diagnosis is essential as timely treatment influences prognosis. Although endomyocardial biopsy remains the reference standard, non-invasive imaging has become central to the diagnostic pathway and disease evaluation.This review summarizes the contemporary role of multimodality imaging in cardiac amyloidosis. Echocardiography remains the first-line imaging modality and can provide important diagnostic clues, including increased ventricular wall thickness and apical sparing on strain analyses. CMR enables detailed tissue characterization, allowing non-invasive assessment of myocardial amyloid burden and disease progression. Bone scintigraphy has revolutionized the diagnosis of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy by enabling a reliable non-biopsy diagnosis after exclusion of light-chain amyloidosis. Emerging PET tracers may further improve early detection, quantification of amyloid burden, and monitoring of treatment response.The integration of multimodality imaging has fundamentally changed the diagnostic and therapeutic landscape of cardiac amyloidosis, facilitating earlier recognition, improved risk stratification, and longitudinal disease monitoring. As novel therapies continue to emerge, advanced imaging techniques are expected to play an increasingly important role in personalized management and evaluation of therapeutic response.

articles.title: GLP-1 receptor agonists for people with type 2 diabetes and peripheral artery disease: reducing uncertainty in clinical practice.
articles.abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) may be the most frequent first manifestation of cardiovascular disease (CVD) in type 2 diabetes (T2D). Management of PAD in T2D aims to improve symptoms and lower the high risk of major adverse cardiovascular (MACE) and limb (MALE) events. Drugs commonly used are lipid-lowering and antihypertensive medicines, antithrombotic and antihyperglycemic agents. The ADA recommends both GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2i) as the first-line therapy to reduce the cardio-renal risk in people with T2D, including those with PAD. Meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) show that semaglutide is better than placebo in reducing by 30% PAD events in people with T2D (with or without PAD at baseline), although no RCT was designed to investigate PAD-related hard outcomes as a primary endpoint; however, both liraglutide and semaglutide may increase walking distance by approximately 25-30 m at six months in people with T2D and PAD. Cohort studies also confirm that GLP-1RA use is better than non-use in reducing by 28% the risk of MALE in individuals with T2D and PAD, although their retrospective design might introduce residual confounding and under-ascertainment of outcomes. Dedicated RCTs will obtain more direct evidence for the promising lower limb benefits of GLP-1RAs, but the scientific outlook of specific RCTs on hard limb events is empty. In the meantime, clinicians should choose a GLP-1RA of proven efficacy in subjects with T2D and PAD to improve their cardio-nephro-metabolic outlook, as well as their walking capacity, limited at present to liraglutide and semaglutide.

articles.title: Larval exposure to insecticides increases adult susceptibility to bluetongue virus in Culicoides sonorensis Wirth and Jones (Diptera: Ceratopogonidae).
articles.abstract: Culicoides biting midges develop in organically enriched habitats, such as livestock wastewater, which can accumulate pesticide residues from livestock treatments. In some instances, larval development sites are directly targeted with insecticides for vector control. These environmental stressors can affect larval survival and gene expression patterns that govern development and long-term fitness, such as altered immune function. This overlap in gene pathways reflects the integration of detoxification in immunity as a response to both chemical stress and pathogenic threats. As a result, detoxifying pesticides at sublethal levels may developmentally compromise insect vectors, making them more vulnerable to infections in later life stages. In this study, larvae of Culicoides sonorensis Wirth and Jones, a major North American bluetongue virus (BTV) vector, were exposed to the lethal concentration for 10% of the test population (LC₁₀) of three distinct classes of insecticides (permethrin, yeast microencapsulated (YME) fluralaner, or methoprene) while controls received equal amounts of solvent (ethanol or water). Survivors were reared to adulthood and offered defibrinated sheep blood spiked with BTV at three days post-emergence. Engorged females were held for up to 14 days post-infection. At 1, 3, 7, 10, and 14 days post-infection, up to 10 females per treatment group were sampled to test for BTV infection and dissemination using RT-qPCR. Infection and dissemination rates, as well as viral titers as quantified by qPCR, were compared across time points and treatments to evaluate whether sublethal pesticide exposure of larvae alters vector competence of adults for BTV. Exposure to three different pesticides resulted in significantly increased BTV titers, particularly at 7 days post-infection (YME fluralaner and methoprene) and 14 days post-infection (permethrin). Infection and dissemination rates at 7 days post-infection were also significantly higher in midges exposed to YME fluralaner and methoprene. Midges exposed to permethrin had significantly higher dissemination rates at 14 days post-infection. Implications of changes in infection dynamics are discussed.

articles.title: Brain connectivity using functional MRI as a potential biomarker of cognitive dysfunction in type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type-2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a major risk factor classically linked to cognitive impairment. While altered brain connectivity has been observed in individuals with diabetes, the specific neural patterns distinguishing cognitive impairment in diabetics from non-diabetics remain unclear.

AIMS: To compare resting-state functional connectivity patterns between persons with T2DM with mild cognitive impairment (T2DM-MCI) and persons without T2DM but with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), using resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI).

METHODS: Cross-sectional study of 56 patients, from 61 to 85 years old, divided into 2 groups: MCI (29 patients) and T2DM-MCI (27 patients). All participants underwent neuropsychological assessment (Mini-Mental State Examination [MMSE] and Montreal Cognitive Assessment [MoCA]); rs-fMRI was performed on a subset: MCI (27 patients), T2DM-MCI (24 patients). Group differences in resting-state functional connectivity were analyzed using independent component analysis (ICA) implemented in the FSL software package.

RESULTS: Patients with T2DM-MCI showed significantly increased functional connectivity within the left visual and left sensorimotor networks compared to those with MCI only (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Findings suggest T2DM may contribute to altered functional brain connectivity in persons with T2DM with MCI, highlighting the potential of resting-state fMRI as a non-invasive biomarker for detecting diabetes-related functional brain alterations.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

articles.title: Serum Galectin-3 Levels and Aortic Dimensions in Children with Bicuspid Aortic Valve.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to compare serum galectin-3 levels between children with bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) and healthy controls and to investigate the association between galectin-3 levels and aortic dimensions in children with BAV. This prospective, single-center, cross-sectional, controlled study included 47 children with echocardiographically confirmed BAV and 43 healthy controls. Echocardiographic aortic dimensions and corresponding Z-scores, anthropometric measurements, and serum galectin-3 levels were assessed. Aortic dilation was defined as an ascending aorta Z-score > 2. Age, body mass index, and cardiac function were similar between groups, whereas sex distribution differed significantly. Ascending aorta diameter and Z-score were significantly greater in the BAV group than in controls (27.94 ± 5.56 vs. 21.52 ± 2.53 mm, p < 0.001; 2.34 ± 1.54 vs. 0.31 ± 0.72, p < 0.001). Aortic dilation was present in 28 (59.6%) BAV patients. Serum galectin-3 levels did not differ between BAV patients and controls [8.70 (7.03-11.38) vs. 8.05 (6.10-13.15) ng/mL, p = 0.566]. No significant correlation was found between galectin-3 levels and aortic dimensions or Z-scores. Galectin-3 levels were also similar in BAV patients with and without aortic dilation [8.80 (6.58-12.30) vs. 8.15 (6.30-10.95) ng/mL, p = 0.537]. Serum galectin-3 levels were not associated with aortic dimensions or aortic dilation in children with BAV. Longitudinal studies incorporating serial assessment of aortic dimensions and complementary markers of aortic disease are warranted.

articles.title: Long Term Outcomes of Pediatric Patients After Catheter Ablation for Possible Arrhythmia Induced Cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract: Arrhythmia induced cardiomyopathy (AiCM) is reversible, and catheter ablation has become the standard treatment for most arrhythmias. However, as the diagnosis of AiCM can be made only in retrospect, management is often challenging. A single center retrospective study included patients who had ablation for presumed AiCM after January 2011 to assess the outcomes of ablation, and the final diagnosis. 22 patients (11 female) were included in the study with the following distribution of arrhythmias: Atrial Ectopic Tachycardia (AET) = 8, Permanent Junctional Reciprocating Tachycardia (PJRT) = 6, Ventricular Tachycardia = 3, Premature Ventricular Contraction = 1, Atrial Flutter = 1, Atrioventricular Reciprocating Tachycardia = 1. There were two patients where an EP study did not show a specific arrhythmia substrate and the patients proceeded in the transplantation pathway. Of the 20 patients with confirmed tachycardia, four (20%) had complete normalization of function with+ medical management. The remaining 16 patients (80%) achieved no or partial functional recovery, with ablation playing even more important role in these patients. One AET patient showed no recovery of function despite successful ablation, consequently requiring heart transplant due to later confirmed gene-positive cardiomyopathy. Overall, 19 patients (95%) showed normal cardiac function at the end of study period with diagnosis of AiCM. There was one significant complication with AV block due to RF ablation on ECMO in a newborn with PJRT. While medical management can achieve functional recovery in some pediatric AiCM cases, most patients will require catheter ablation with 88% success rate. However, once functional recovery is achieved, long term outcome is excellent. Very rarely ventricular function will not recover despite successful ablation as genetic cardiomyopathies can present with secondary arrhythmia.

articles.title: A Keratin and Polyacrylamide Dual Network Hydrogel Based on Dynamic Coordination between Polydopamine and Mg2+ for Infected Wound Repair.
articles.abstract: Exogenous bacterial infection severely impairs skin wound repair and creates a complex therapeutic challenge that requires simultaneous infection control, oxidative stress regulation, and tissue regeneration. In this study, a PAM/HK/PDANP-Mg2+ multifunctional hydrogel (HPPM) was developed as a cascade therapeutic dressing for infected wounds. In this system, polyacrylamide (PAM) provided a flexible covalently cross-linked framework. Hydrolyzed keratin (HK) offered bioactive and cytocompatible interfaces. Polydopamine nanoparticles (PDANPs) endowed the hydrogel with adhesiveness, photothermal antibacterial activity, and radical scavenging capacity. Coordination between Mg2+ and PDA, together with intermolecular hydrogen bonding, contributed to reversible physical cross-linking within the PAM framework. The optimized HPPM (0.012) hydrogel exhibited a porous structure, high swelling ratio (∼1277%), strong adhesion properties (31.00 kPa), and large tensile elongation (∼560%). Under 808 nm near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, HPPM achieved mild photothermal heating and over 99% antibacterial efficiency against Escherichia coli (E. coli) and Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus). It also showed favorable antioxidant activity, cytocompatibility, and pro-migratory effects. In an S. aureus-infected rat wound model, HPPM (0.012) + NIR accelerated wound closure, reduced inflammation, enhanced collagen deposition and re-epithelialization, and regulated IL-10/TNF-α expression. These results suggest that HPPM promotes infected wound healing through dynamic coordination-driven cascade remodeling of the infected wound microenvironment.

articles.title: Treatment strategies for primary intraosseous squamous cell carcinoma of the solid type in the mandible: a single-centre retrospective analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Primary intraosseous squamous cell carcinoma (PIOSCC) of the mandible is a rare malignancy, and evidence regarding optimal management remains limited. This retrospective study aimed to evaluate clinical outcomes, explore potential clinicopathological associations, and assess the diagnostic performance of imaging modalities in patients with solid-type PIOSCC treated at a single centre.

METHODS: Fifteen consecutive patients with solid-type PIOSCC of the mandible were retrospectively reviewed. Clinical variables, including peri-mandibular muscle infiltration and surgical margin status, imaging findings from computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance (MR) imaging, and fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (FDG-PET/CT), treatment modalities, and survival outcomes were analysed. Overall and disease-specific survival were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis.

RESULTS: The 5-year disease-specific survival rate was 72.2%. For contextual reference, the corresponding 5-year disease-specific survival rate in surgically treated lower gingival squamous cell carcinoma during the same period was 75.5%. Infiltration of the peri-mandibular muscle, combined with close surgical margins, may be associated with poorer clinical outcomes. Among the various imaging modalities, fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) showed the strongest correlation with the pathological maximum tumour diameter in this exploratory analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: This retrospective single-centre analysis suggests that peri-mandibular muscle infiltration and surgical margin status may be associated with prognosis in patients with solid-type PIOSCC of the mandible. FDG-PET may provide complementary information for tumour assessment. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: First detection and biological characterization of African eggplant mosaic virus, an aphid, transmissible potyvirus infecting tomato in Switzerland.
articles.abstract: In 2025, tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) plants exhibiting irregular fruit marbling and spotting were observed at three production sites in Ticino, Switzerland. Transmission electron microscopy, generic potyvirus RT-PCR followed by Sanger sequencing, and subsequent High-throughput sequencing confirmation identified the causal agent as African eggplant mosaic virus (AEMV; Potyvirus melongenae), marking its first detection outside of Africa and its first natural occurrence on tomato. The Swiss isolates represent a highly divergent AEMV strain, sharing only 77.5% full-genome nucleotide identity with the Tanzanian reference isolate. While the P1 region showed extreme hypervariability (51% nt identity), the coat protein (83% nt and 92% aa identities) firmly supported its taxonomic assignment to AEMV. This high sequence divergence suggests toward a long-standing, previously unsampled cryptic reservoir. Biological assays demonstrated efficient transmission by the aphid Myzus persicae and confirmed that while mature plants exhibit only fruit symptoms, early infection of young plantlets leads to severe growth retardation. RT-qPCR analysis showed a significant correlation between viral load and fruit symptom expression. Epidemiological tracing linked all three Swiss outbreaks to a single nursery, suggesting a point-source introduction through infected plantlets. A targeted survey of 81 tomato samples collected in 2024, across 12 Swiss cantons yielded no additional positives, indicating the outbreak is currently localized. To support surveillance, species-specific RT-qPCR diagnostic assays were developed. This study provides a blueprint for the rapid characterization, risk assessment, and containment of emerging plant viruses introduced through international trade, and supplies the diagnostic tools and epidemiological framework needed to manage this virus in the European tomato sector.

articles.title: Hospital cost structures and resource utilisation across representative treatment pathways relevant to complex orthopaedic infection care: a nationwide DRG-based analysis in Germany.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Implant-associated orthopaedic infections require prolonged inpatient treatment, repeated surgery and multidisciplinary care, yet nationwide evidence on how hospital resources are distributed across clinically distinct treatment pathways is limited. This study characterised hospital-side case costs, resource utilisation and aggregate expenditure across representative German diagnosis-related groups (DRGs) relevant to complex orthopaedic infection care.

METHODS: Publicly available 2024 data from the German Institute for the Hospital Remuneration System (InEK) were analysed. Twelve representative DRGs were selected a priori from official definitions and diagnostic/procedural profiles and grouped into six treatment pathways. The InEK cost matrix reflects standardised hospital-side resource costs from participating calculation hospitals and does not represent actual DRG reimbursement. National case frequencies, length of stay and mean case costs were analysed using frequency-weighted pathway estimates, while pathway-level cost composition was calculated from aggregate component expenditure.

RESULTS: The included DRGs represented 36,212 hospitalisations and €305.2 million in aggregate annual hospital-side expenditure represented by the selected DRGs. Mean hospital-side costs ranged from €5,859 to €22,495 per case. Ward care accounted for approximately 34-69% of pathway expenditure; operating theatre services contributed up to 39% in revision arthroplasty. Geriatric rehabilitation generated the largest aggregate expenditure (€119.0 million; 39.0%) because of high case volume, whereas complex vacuum-assisted wound care had the highest per-case cost but only 2.9% of aggregate expenditure. At the aggregated DRG level, mean length of stay was associated with mean case cost (Pearson r = 0.87, 95% CI 0.60-0.96; P < 0.001); leave-one-out correlations ranged from r = 0.79 to r = 0.96.

CONCLUSION: Resource requirements differ markedly across representative DRG pathways relevant to complex orthopaedic infection care. Because the selected DRGs are not infection-exclusive, the reported expenditure should not be interpreted as the national economic burden of implant-associated orthopaedic infection. The findings may inform hospital resource planning and future cost-revenue analyses.

articles.title: Development and Validation of an Extended NEMA Body Phantom to Detect 18F-FDG Heterogeneous Distribution in Texture Analysis.
articles.abstract: We evaluated heterogeneous 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) distribution using texture features and an extended National Electrical Manufacturers Association (NEMA) phantom. Homogeneous and heterogeneous distribution was represented by spheres without or with acrylic beads (5-mm diameter). We reconstructed PET images acquired for 10 min using the Q.clear algorithm and controlled statistical noise by adjusting β values. We calculated maximum (SUVmax) and mean (SUVmean) standardized uptake values and coefficients of variation (COV), then evaluated 22 established texture features to determine homogeneity and heterogeneity. Heterogeneous and homogeneous 18F-FDG distribution was visualized using spherical phantoms with and without beads. The SUVmax and SUVmean were underestimated by ~ 45% in heterogeneous compared with homogeneous 18F-FDG distribution. As the β value increased, the COV for the phantoms with and without beads decreased and eventually became equivalent. When the spherical phantoms with or without beads were imaged using a β value of 100, eight textural features were associated with texture heterogeneity, and six features were associated with texture homogeneity. We extended a NEMA phantom by inserting spheres containing beads to represent heterogeneous 18F-FDG distribution. Robust texture features were determined using the phantom to detect 18F-FDG homogeneity and heterogeneity.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Psychological Interventions for Smoking Cessation Targeting Diabetes Mellitus: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Nicotine & tobacco research : official journal of the Society for Research on Nicotine and Tobacco
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tobacco cessation is a public health priority. However, long-term outcomes remain limited, partly due to insufficient adaptation of interventions to chronic conditions, such as diabetes mellitus (DM), a leading cause of chronic disability worldwide. Evidence regarding the clinical impact of smoking cessation treatments in people with DM remains inconsistent. The objective of this study was to examine the effectiveness of psychological smoking cessation interventions for individuals with type 1 and type 2 DM.

METHODS: A search for scientific studies was conducted in four databases (PubMed, Web of Science, SCOPUS, and PsycINFO), resulting in the selection of 12 studies following PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO, ID: CRD42024531545).

RESULTS: Overall, 83.3% of the interventions incorporated diabetes-adapted components. Programs frequently achieved short-term reductions in cigarette consumption, although complete long-term abstinence was less frequent. Only a minority of studies demonstrated statistically significant higher abstinence rates in the intervention groups than in the control groups, ranging from 31.3% to 70.6% at 6 months and 20.0% to 38.8% at 12 months. The most favorable outcomes occurred in group-based, multicomponent programs for type 2 DM combining diabetes-specific psychoeducation, motivational strategies, and optional pharmacotherapy.

CONCLUSIONS: Due to a moderate-to-high risk of bias across studies, evidence regarding the effectiveness of psychological smoking cessation interventions for individuals with DM remains limited. Further research is needed to identify factors that influence smoking cessation outcomes in patients with DM. The integration of evidence-based programs and interventions tailored to diabetes-related needs, associated comorbidities, and gender-specific factors are essential to address these challenges.

articles.title: A Case Report of Severe Leptospirosis After a Rat Bite in an Urban Setting.
articles.abstract: A 21-year-old healthy male presented with a sepsis syndrome approximately 17 days after a wild urban rat bite. In the emergency room, he was initiated on piperacillin-tazobactam, and after receipt of the first dose, he developed worsening tachycardia, rigors, and hypoxia, followed by hypotension. Given the rodent exposure, the medical team suspected leptospirosis and attributed his decline to a Jarisch-Herxheimer (JH) reaction. A BioFire Global Fever Special Pathogens Panel was obtained the morning after admission and was positive for Leptospira DNA. A CDC lipL32 nucleic acid amplification test from admission was also positive, as was the microscopic agglutination testing (MAT) at 5 weeks. Notably, admission IgM and MAT results were negative. The patient received a 7-day course of ceftriaxone with resolution of most of his symptoms. Leptospirosis is a zoonotic infection typically acquired via exposure to water contaminated with the urine of infected animals, most commonly rodents. This case of severe leptospirosis contributes to the growing literature on leptospirosis occurring in association with rat bites and demonstrates that clinical suspicion combined with nucleic acid testing early in the disease course can enable rapid diagnosis.

articles.title: Cerebrovascular mechanisms of stroke severity in offspring from pre-eclamptic pregnancy.
articles.abstract: Offspring from pre-eclamptic pregnancies face elevated ischaemic stroke risk throughout life, yet the mechanisms linking adverse intrauterine exposure to adult cerebrovascular vulnerability remain unknown. Distal leptomeningeal anastomoses (LMAs), which develop during late gestation are key determinants of stroke severity and represent a plausible target of prenatal programming. Here, we show that experimental preeclampsia (ePE) in rats establishes a persistent cerebrovascular structural and transcriptional phenotype in adult offspring. Following transient middle cerebral artery occlusion, ePE-exposed males exhibited increased infarct volume, oedema, enhanced perfusion deficit and smaller LMA diameters relative to normal pregnant offspring, and 83% had microvascular stasis after stroke. Female offspring were protected from stroke-induced brain injury despite sharing a similar transcriptional landscape. RNA sequencing and DNA methylation profiling revealed differentially expressed genes and discrete differentially methylated regions enriched for vascular development and VEGF-Notch signalling in ePE offspring. These findings support the possibility of a developmental origin of cerebrovascular stroke risk, implicating gestational programming of cerebrovascular gene expression as a sex modulated determinant of adult stroke outcome and a potential target for early intervention. KEY POINTS: Offspring born from pre-eclamptic pregnancies have a greater lifetime risk and death from ischaemic stroke, but why this occurs is unknown. Pial collaterals form during the late gestational period and are a key determinant of stroke severity. Using a rat model, we showed that compared to normal pregnancy, male offspring from pre-eclamptic pregnancies had smaller diameter pial collaterals which was associated with decreased collateral recruitment during ischaemic stroke and worsened stroke outcome. RNA analysis revealed altered expression of genes related to blood vessel development and function in adult offspring. These findings suggest that preeclampsia leads to lasting changes in cerebrovascular structure and gene expression which is associated with increased stroke severity in male offspring suggesting a potential window for early intervention.

articles.title: Practice changing trials: focus on prevention, heart failure, interventional cardiology, and rehabilitation.
Transient Cognitive Vulnerability After Hypoglycemia in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes: Evidence From Continuous Glucose Monitoring and Cognitive Ecologic Momentary Assessment.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Adults with type 1 diabetes experience short-term changes in cognitive performance after glycemic events; however, the duration of such cognitive effects remains unclear. We examined whether hypoglycemic and hyperglycemic events and rapid glucose changes were associated with changes in processing speed or sustained attention in adults with type 1 diabetes and whether these associations varied by time since the event.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Participants (N = 190) completed 15 days of smartphone-based ecologic momentary assessment (EMA; 3 prompts/day) paired with continuous glucose monitoring. Cognitive performance (median reaction time and accuracy) was tested using digit symbol matching (DSM) and gradual-onset continuous performance testing (GCPT; sustained attention) by TestMyBrain (processing speed). Glycemic exposures were defined as hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia lasting ≥15 min and rapid (5-min) increases or decreases in glucose >15 mg/dL, occurring during nonoverlapping intervals: 0-1, 1-2, and 2-3 h before EMA. Multilevel models estimated associations between glycemic exposures and cognitive performance, adjusting for age, EMA count, and interruptions.

RESULTS: Hypoglycemic events occurring within 0-1 h of EMA were associated with slower reaction time and poorer performance on DSM and GCPT. No associations were observed for events occurring 1-2 or 2-3 h before EMA. Hyperglycemic events and rapid glucose increases or decreases were not associated with cognition across most outcomes or time windows.

CONCLUSIONS: Hypoglycemia was associated with a transient period of cognitive vulnerability largely confined to the hour after an event, with little evidence of delayed effects. Findings support avoiding or exercising caution during cognitively demanding tasks for up to an hour after a hypoglycemic event.

articles.title: Cotransplantation With Human AAT-MSCs Enhances Human Islet Graft Survival in Humanized Mice by Modulating B- and T-Cell Responses.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Immune-mediated rejection remains a major barrier to long-term success of islet/stem cell-derived islet transplantation for type 1 diabetes. We evaluated whether cotransplantation of human islets with human α-1 antitrypsin-overexpressing mesenchymal stromal/stem cells (AAT-MSCs) improves islet graft survival by modulating human immune responses in a humanized diabetic mouse model. Humanized NOD/SCID/IL2Rγ-/- (NSG) mice were generated by irradiation and transfer of human CD34+ hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells, resulting in stable T- and B-cell reconstitution. Diabetes was induced by multiple doses of low-dose streptozotocin (STZ), after which mice received intrahepatic transplants of human islets alone or together with AAT-MSCs and were monitored for 100 days. Cotransplantation with AAT-MSCs markedly improved glycemic control, prolonged graft survival, and reduced the risk of rejection. These beneficial effects were associated with lower serum IgM levels, which inversely correlated with graft rejection, and with expansion of regulatory B cells (Bregs), followed by durable suppression of T helper 1, T helper 17, and cytotoxic T cell responses. Cotransplant grafts showed improved insulin preservation and enrichment of interleukin (IL) 10+ cells within islets. In vitro, AAT-MSCs promoted Breg differentiation, shifted cytokine production toward IL-10 over IL-6, and attenuated activated B cell-mediated cytotoxicity against human islets. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that AAT-MSC cotransplantation promotes immune tolerance and human islet graft function, supporting its translational potential to reduce reliance on systemic immunosuppression in the clinic.

ARTICLE HIGHLIGHTS: Immune-mediated rejection limits the long-term success of islet and stem cell-derived islet transplantation in type 1 diabetes, and strategies that protect the graft without systemic immunosuppression are needed. We asked whether cotransplanting human islets with α-1 antitrypsin-overexpressing mesenchymal stromal/stem cells (AAT-MSCs) improves graft outcomes in humanized mice, and how human immune responses are affected. AAT-MSC cotransplantation improved glycemic control, prolonged graft survival, and shifted immune responses toward a more regulatory, less inflammatory profile. These findings support further development of AAT-MSCs as an adjunct to reduce reliance on systemic immunosuppression in islet transplantation.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of prehospital capillary high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I in patients with acute chest pain: the prospective multicenter VALIDATE study.
articles.journal: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) plays a central role in the diagnosis and management of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), including rule-out and rule-in strategies in the emergency department. Extending hs-cTnI testing to the prehospital setting could accelerate patient orientation and clinical decision-making, but the diagnostic performance of prehospital capillary hs-cTnI remains insufficiently studied.

OBJECTIVE: The study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of prehospital capillary hs-cTnI for the diagnosis of NSTEMI at hospital discharge.

DESIGN: The study is a prospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy study with blinded index test results.

SETTINGS AND PARTICIPANTS: Four French emergency medical service systems with 10 mobile intensive care units. Adult patients presenting with acute chest pain were included.

INDEX TEST: Prehospital hs-cTnI measurement using a point-of-care device (Atellica VTLi) on capillary samples. Treating clinicians were blinded to hs-cTnI results.

OUTCOME MEASURES AND ANALYSIS: The primary outcome was the diagnostic performance of capillary hs-cTnI for the diagnosis of NSTEMI at hospital discharge. Diagnostic performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Clinically relevant thresholds were defined a priori based on predefined safety criteria.

MAIN RESULTS: Among 659 patients included in the primary analysis, 71 (10.8%) had NSTEMI. Prehospital capillary hs-cTnI demonstrated good diagnostic performance [area under the curve (AUC) = 0.83, 95% CI = 0.78-0.88]. A rule-out threshold of <2.2 ng/L, evaluated according to prespecified performance criteria, identified 7.1% of patients, with a negative predictive value of 1.00 (95% CI = 0.92-1.00). A rule-in threshold of >43.6 ng/L identified 6.5% of patients, with a positive predictive value of 0.65 (95% CI = 0.51-0.79). In the predefined sensitivity analysis, venous hs-cTnI showed similar diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.84, 95% CI = 0.79-0.89).

CONCLUSION: Prehospital capillary hs-cTnI showed good diagnostic performance for NSTEMI, although feasibility in routine practice was challenged by unavailable or uninterpretable measurements. Further external validation is warranted before implementation in prehospital diagnostic pathways.

articles.title: Risk of Venous Thromboembolism After Lumbar Spine Interbody Fusion: A Propensity-Matched Cohort Study.
articles.journal: The Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a feared complication after spine surgery, with limited data comparing approach-specific risk factors after lumbar interbody fusion. This study compared the rate of VTE complications after transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion (TLIF) and anterior lumbar interbody fusion (ALIF).

METHODS: A multi-institutional electronic medical record database was queried for patients aged older than 18 years undergoing single-level or multilevel TLIF and ALIF between 2004 and 2024. Patients were evenly divided into single-level (n = 9,618) and multilevel (n = 1,774) TLIF and ALIF cohorts. Propensity score matching (1:1) was conducted using demographics, comorbidities, and anticoagulation use. Odds ratios (95% confidence intervals) of VTE and postoperative bleeding complications were calculated at 30, 60, and 90 days.

RESULTS: Compared with single-level TLIF, single-level ALIF was associated with higher odds of VTE events at 30 days (OR: 2.0, 95% CI, 1.4 to 2.9; P < 0.001), 60 days (OR: 1.8, 95% CI, 1.3 to 2.5; P < 0.001), and 90 days (OR: 1.7, 95% CI, 1.3 to 2.4; P < 0.001). Multilevel ALIF was also associated with higher odds of VTE events at 30 days (OR: 2.7, 95% CI: 1.2 to 5.1; P = 0.015), 60 days (OR: 2.0, 95% CI, 1.2 to 3.4; P = 0.010), and 90 days (OR: 1.9, 95% CI, 1.1 to 3.2; P = 0.015) when compared with multilevel TLIF. No significant differences were observed in postoperative bleeding complications between single-level and multilevel TLIF and ALIF cohorts at all study intervals (P > 0.05).

DISCUSSION: ALIF was associated with increased VTE complications, with no differences in postoperative bleeding complications when compared with TLIF. These findings suggest that surgical approach should be considered in perioperative VTE risk stratification and patient counseling after lumbar interbody fusion surgery, highlighting the need for future prospective studies evaluating approach-specific VTE prevention strategies.

articles.title: Multiphase Cardiac CT for Integrated Planning of Mitral Valve Repair: Coronaries and Cannulation Strategies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Degenerative mitral regurgitation (DMR) is the leading cause of primary mitral regurgitation (MR) and is increasingly managed with minimally invasive and robotic-assisted repair. Preoperative planning increasingly relies on computed tomography (CT).

CASE SUMMARIES: Here, we describe a case series of 3 patients with severe degenerative mitral regurgitation who underwent mitral valve repair (2 robotic-assisted, 1 conventional) after CT evaluation. CT findings directly influenced repair feasibility, cannulation site, and operative approach.

DISCUSSION: Preoperative imaging is essential, but current planning relies on multiple studies, including echocardiography and invasive angiography. Electrocardiographically gated, multiphase cardiac CT offers a comprehensive alternative by simultaneously assessing leaflet morphology, annular calcification, coronary artery course, vascular access, and left atrial appendage thrombus.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: We show that a standardized CT protocol can consolidate preoperative planning and optimize patient-specific surgical strategies in mitral valve repair.

articles.title: True Left-Ventricular Aneurysm After Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation: The Role of Imaging in a Rare Complication.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular (LV) pseudoaneurysm is an uncommon but recognized complication of ventricular tachycardia (VT) ablation. In contrast, true LV aneurysm has been reported only rarely.

CASE SUMMARY: Transthoracic echocardiogram, supported by cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging, initially suggested an LV pseudoaneurysm in a patient after VT ablation. During evaluation for percutaneous closure, left ventriculogram and 3-dimensional transesophageal echocardiogram revealed more complex anatomy, prompting referral for surgical repair. Intraoperative findings confirmed a true LV aneurysm.

DISCUSSION: True LV aneurysm may represent a rare complication of deep radiofrequency energy delivery during catheter ablation resulting in myocardial injury. Because differentiating true aneurysms from pseudoaneurysms can be challenging, a multimodality imaging approach may improve anatomical characterization, guide management, and enhance understanding of the underlying mechanism.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Multimodality imaging can improve anatomical characterization and procedural planning in patients with the rare complication of true left aneurysm after catheter ablation.

articles.title: Rethinking Authorship in Large Multicenter Clinical Trials: A Heart Failure Collaboratory Framework for Recognition of Site-Based Investigators.
Safety and Efficacy of Omecamtiv Mecarbil by QRS Duration and Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy in GALACTIC-HF.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prolonged QRS duration portends worse outcomes in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). In GALACTIC-HF, omecamtiv mecarbil (OM) reduced the primary composite endpoint of first heart failure (HF) event or cardiovascular death.

OBJECTIVES: The objectives of this study were to evaluate whether QRS duration and the presence of cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) modify the treatment effect of OM.

METHODS: GALACTIC-HF enrolled patients with symptomatic HF, HFrEF (≤35%), and elevated natriuretic peptides. Baseline QRS duration was available in 8,089 of 8,232 participants (98.0%), who were classified into 3 groups: QRS duration <120 ms without CRT (n = 3,724), QRS duration ≥120 ms without CRT (n = 3,225), and CRT regardless of QRS duration (n = 1,140). The authors assessed whether the effect of OM on the primary composite endpoint, first HF hospitalization, cardiovascular death, and all-cause death differed across these groups.

RESULTS: Patients with QRS ≥120 ms without CRT and those with CRT were older, had lower EF, worse health status, and higher N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels than those with QRS <120 ms without CRT. When modeled as a continuous variable, baseline QRS duration was associated with clinical outcomes among patients without CRT but not among those with CRT. Among patients with QRS ≥120 ms without CRT, OM appeared to confer less benefit for the primary composite endpoint (Pinteraction = 0.072), for cardiovascular death (Pinteraction = 0.003), and for all-cause death (Pinteraction = 0.009). In contrast, among patients treated with CRT, OM was beneficial regardless of QRS duration.

CONCLUSIONS: In GALACTIC-HF, OM appeared less effective in patients with prolonged QRS duration who did not have CRT, whereas it remained beneficial in CRT-treated patients. (Global Approach to Lowering Adverse Cardiac Outcomes Through Improving Contractility in Heart Failure [GALACTIC-HF]; NCT02929329).

articles.title: Molecular Insights into a Precursor-Chlorine Trade-Off Governing Divergent Formation Pathways of PCDD/Fs and Emerging Cl-PAHs in Waste Cocombustion of Cellulose, PET, and PVC.
articles.abstract: Co-combustion of industrial and municipal solid waste (ISW/MSW) is widely practiced, yet PCDD/Fs and emerging chlorinated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (Cl-PAHs) formation under mixed-feedstock conditions remains poorly understood. Here, cellulose, polyethylene terephthalate (PET), and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) were combusted individually and cocombusted with MSW to elucidate how feedstock chemistry regulates chlorinated pollutant formation. Comprehensive mass-spectrometric profiling of target pollutants, aromatic precursors, and the top 50 combustion intermediates, combined with DFT calculations, revealed a precursor-chlorine trade-off governing pollutant formation. PET preferentially generated oxygenated aromatic intermediates, particularly dibenzofuran; PVC supplied the most PAHs and reactive chlorine, and cellulose primarily contributed carbon skeletons. Accordingly, two distinct pathways were proposed: dibenzofuran-centered, chlorination-limited formation of PCDD/Fs and stepwise aromatic growth followed by site-selective chlorination of Cl-PAHs. The higher HOMO energies of two representative PAHs, anthracene and phenanthrene, relative to dibenzofuran indicated their greater susceptibility to electrophilic chlorination. Consequently, Cl-PAHs exceeded PCDD/Fs by 1-3 orders of magnitude and accounted for 83.4% of estimated TEQ. Increasing chlorine availability alleviated the kinetic constraint on dibenzofuran chlorination, causing an approximately 42-fold increase in PCDD/F emissions at 20% PVC blending. These findings establish a molecular basis for feedstock-chemistry-guided management and broaden emission-control priorities from regulated PCDD/Fs to emerging Cl-PAHs.

articles.title: Influence of Urban Form, Weather and Population on Outdoor Airborne Infection Risk: Implications in Greater London for SARS-CoV-2.
articles.abstract: Although airborne infectious disease transmission outdoors is possible, particularly in densely built urban areas with limited ventilation, the role of urban morphology and neighborhood climate heterogeneity in modulating the risk remains poorly quantified. We couple an urban climate model (SUEWS) and a modified Wells-Riley framework to develop a transferable neighborhood-scale approach for mapping outdoor airborne infection risk across morphologically diverse neighborhoods, factoring in urban form, population distribution and meteorologically driven viral infectivity decay. We demonstrate this framework by applying it to SARS-CoV-2 in Greater London. Considering outdoor urban ventilation alone, estimated risk follows a diurnal cycle and peaks at night. Including population distribution, daytime risk in busy commercial centers is up to 7.23 times higher than nighttime. Infectivity decay from ultraviolet B (UVB) exposure reduces risk by 35-45% in less dense areas and up to 99% in high built-density neighborhoods. Despite this mitigation, the highest risks persist in high-rise, high-workplace-density districts (e.g., City of London and Westminster), while lower-rise areas (e.g., Lambeth and Croydon) exhibit reductions exceeding 90%. For SARS-CoV-2, these findings demonstrate strong intraurban heterogeneity in outdoor airborne infection risk in Greater London. More broadly, the transferable framework supports high-resolution mapping to inform targeted, place-based public health interventions.

articles.title: Mechanistic Understanding of Breath-Borne Bacterial Inactivation Kinetics in Oxidant-Rich and Natural Air.
articles.abstract: Bioaerosols play a central role in respiratory infection transmission, but how atmospheric oxidants affect their viability, especially in human respiratory fluids, remains unexplored. Here, we investigated the inactivation of five bacterial species with distinct cell envelope architectures (Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Bacillus subtilis, Staphylococcus aureus, and Mycobacterium smegmatis) suspended in human exhaled breath condensate (EBC) droplets exposed to gas-phase hydroxyl radicals (•OH) produced by ultraviolet irradiation of H2O2. Compared with the other three exposure conditions, the •OH-generating (H2O2+UV) treatment caused the greatest viability loss, with 4-h survival ranging from 24.3% (E. coli) to 63.0% (M. smegmatis). Gram-negative bacteria were sensitive to both H2O2 and •OH, whereas Gram-positive species resisted H2O2 but were inactivated by •OH. M. smegmatis showed the highest tolerance. Inactivation accelerated in smaller droplets, and the size-dependent kinetics were characterized using Weibull and first-order models incorporating surface-area-to-volume ratio. Morphological, biochemical, and metabolomic analyses indicated that the observed inactivation differences were associated with bacterial envelope types and surface characteristics. •OH preferentially degrades outer membrane glycolipids in Gram-negative bacteria and oxidizes cytoplasmic membrane lipids in Gram-positive bacteria, while all species shared a core signature of nucleic acid oxidative damage. These findings provide a molecular understanding of bacterial inactivation kinetics in human EBC droplets and may inform the assessment of bioaerosol transmission risks.

articles.title: Echocardiographic Stratification of Diuretic Response via TAPSE-Pulmonary Artery Systolic Pressure Integration in Decompensated Heart Failure.
articles.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Right ventricular (RV) function is a key determinant of prognosis in heart failure (HF). Although echocardiographic parameters such as tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE) and pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP) are widely used, their interpretation in isolation has limitations, and the relationship between right ventricular-pulmonary arterial (RV-PA) coupling and diuretic response remains insufficiently defined. We hypothesized that a composite TAPSE-PASP (TP) score would better reflect RV-PA coupling and be associated with the natriuretic response. This study aimed to evaluate the association between the TP score and diuretic response, as assessed by spot urinary sodium.

METHOD: This retrospective, single-center study included 81 hospitalized patients with HF. Standard transthoracic echocardiography was performed to measure TAPSE, PASP, and derived indices. A TP score was created using quartile-based categorization. Diuretic response was assessed by spot urinary sodium. Patients were classified as good or poor responders using a threshold of 50 mEq/L.

RESULTS: Poor responders had lower spot urinary sodium levels (28.1 +- 11.3 vs. 95.5 +- 24.1 mmol/L, P < 0.001) and a higher prevalence of worsening renal function (69% vs. 23%, P < 0.001). Individual measures (TAPSE/PASP and TAPSE × PASP) were not significantly associated with diuretic response, whereas the TP score showed a weak but significant correlation with urinary sodium (r = 0.248, P = 0.03). Lower TP scores were associated with impaired RV function markers and a lower natriuretic response.

CONCLUSION: The TP score integrates RV systolic performance and pulmonary vascular load and demonstrated a weak but significant association with diuretic response in patients with HF. Given the retrospective design and lack of external validation, these findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Inflammatory and Combined Indices Outperform Metabolic Indices in Predicting One-Year MACE in NSTEMI with Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Patients with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) carry a high residual cardiovascular risk that is inadequately captured by conventional risk scores. We aimed to compare the prognostic value of ten composite blood-based indices from metabolic, inflammatory, combined, and nutritional categories for one-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in this population.

METHOD: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 557 consecutive NSTEMI patients with T2DM who underwent coronary angiography were enrolled. Ten indices were calculated from admission blood samples: TyG, AIP, and METS-IR as metabolic indices; SIRI, PIV, and NLR as inflammatory indices; CTI and CAR as combined indices; and PNI and HALP as nutritional indices. Discrimination was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis with DeLong comparison, independent predictors were identified by multivariate logistic regression, and survival separation was evaluated by Kaplan-Meier analysis.

RESULTS: One-year MACE occurred in 118 patients (21.2%). Inflammatory indices outperformed metabolic indices in ROC analysis (SIRI AUC 0.764 vs. TyG 0.638; P < 0.001). In multivariate regression, CTI (OR 2.446; 95% CI 1.746-3.427; P < 0.001), SIRI (OR 1.242; 95% CI 1.088-1.417; P = 0.001), and PNI (OR 0.918; 95% CI 0.884-0.954; P < 0.001) remained independent predictors alongside left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), SYNTAX score, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Pure metabolic indices lost significance after CTI entered the model. SIRI yielded the widest Kaplan-Meier survival separation (29.5 percentage points; P < 0.001). CTI remained significant across all subgroups, whereas SIRI lost independence in patients with reduced ejection fraction.

CONCLUSION: In NSTEMI patients with T2DM, CTI, SIRI, and PNI independently predict one-year MACE based on routine admission blood tests. Inflammatory and combined indices outperform pure metabolic surrogates, supporting a shift toward multidimensional risk stratification in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Design and Validation of a Custom-Made Electrocardiogram Machine for Low-Cost, High-Fidelity Cardiac Monitoring.
articles.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Electrocardiography (ECG) is an essential diagnostic tool in cardiovascular medicine; however, access remains limited in low-resource settings because of cost and infrastructure requirements. This study aimed to develop and preliminarily validate a low-cost, custom-made ECG device capable of real-time cardiac monitoring and arrhythmia detection.

METHOD: A portable ECG system incorporating a low-noise analog front-end, microcontroller-based digital processing, and Bluetooth-enabled wireless transmission was designed. Preliminary validation was performed using simultaneous recordings from one healthy volunteer and three patients with documented cardiac arrhythmias, and the results were compared with those of a commercial ECG system in terms of signal quality and rhythm interpretation.

RESULTS: The custom-made device provided stable real-time ECG recordings with satisfactory signal fidelity and low noise levels. Comparative analysis demonstrated encouraging agreement with the commercial ECG system in waveform morphology and arrhythmia identification. Wireless data transmission was reliable throughout the recordings.

CONCLUSION: This pilot proof-of-concept study demonstrates the technical feasibility of a low-cost, custom-made ECG system for real-time rhythm monitoring and preliminary detection of selected cardiac arrhythmias. The device showed satisfactory signal fidelity and agreement with a commercial ECG system in a small validation cohort. Larger prospective studies are required to establish diagnostic accuracy, reproducibility, and clinical generalizability.

articles.title: Can High Triglyceride-Glucose Index Predict Major Cardiovascular Events in Patients with Coronary Bifurcation Lesions Undergoing a Double-Stent Strategy?
articles.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Coronary artery bifurcation lesions (CBLs) represent a complex form of coronary artery disease (CAD) and are associated with an unfavorable long-term prognosis. The triglyceride-glucose index (TyGi) has been shown to provide valuable prognostic information regarding the risk of major cardiovascular events (MACEs) in patients with CAD. This study aimed to determine whether an elevated TyGi could predict MACEs, including target lesion revascularization (TLR), myocardial infarction (MI), and all-cause mortality, over a five-year follow-up period in patients with CBLs undergoing a double-stent strategy.

METHOD: This study included 552 patients who underwent a double-stent strategy between January 2010 and December 2020.

RESULTS: Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified an optimal TyGi cut-off value of 9.2877. Patients were subsequently divided into a low-TyGi group (Group 1) and a high-TyGi group (Group 2). During the five-year follow-up period, the incidence of MACEs was recorded.
