Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated a higher incidence of MACEs in Group 2 than in Group 1 (P = 0.008). In multivariate Cox regression analysis (CRA), ejection fraction, presence of a complex bifurcation lesion, TyGi, and SYNTAX score (Synergy Between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention With Taxus and Cardiac Surgery) were predictors of MACEs (P < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: An elevated TyGi may serve as a useful predictor of MACEs in patients with bifurcation lesions undergoing a double-stent strategy.

articles.title: Surface Defect Engineering via Polyaromatic Cluster Evolution for Efficient Microwave-Driven Carbothermal Shock Synthesis of Nanoparticles.
articles.journal: Langmuir : the ACS journal of surfaces and colloids
articles.abstract: Microwave-driven carbothermal shock (CTS) synthesis has attracted considerable attention as an ultrafast route for nanomaterial production. However, controlling nanoparticle nucleation and growth during the extremely short microwave irradiation period remains challenging. Although defect-rich carbon materials have frequently been employed in microwave-driven CTS synthesis, the influence of a separately introduced defect-containing surface layer on nanoparticle formation remains insufficiently understood. In this study, carbon cloth (CC) was coated with a polyacrylonitrile (PAN) solution and thermally oxidized at 200-400 °C to modify the surface carbon structure through the evolution of PAN-derived polyaromatic clusters prior to microwave irradiation. Raman spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy indicated that increasing the oxidation temperature promoted the formation of larger and more ordered polyaromatic domains, accompanied by changes in the surface defect characteristics. These structural variations were associated with distinct Cu nanoparticle sizes and distributions following CTS synthesis. Among the investigated oxidation temperatures, the PAN-coated CC treated at 300 °C produced the smallest and most uniformly dispersed Cu nanoparticles, with an average diameter of 58 ± 25 nm. These findings suggest that controlling the structural evolution of PAN-derived surface carbon layers can provide a practical approach for regulating nanoparticle size and dispersion during microwave-driven CTS synthesis.

articles.title: ZEB1-Driven GLS1 Transcription Promotes Macrophage Glutamine Metabolism in PAH.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The transcriptional mechanisms governing macrophage glutamine metabolism in pulmonary arterial hypertension remain incompletely understood. We investigated the role of ZEB1 (zinc finger E-box-binding homeobox 1)-mediated transcriptional regulation in macrophage metabolic reprogramming and the development of pulmonary arterial hypertension.

METHODS: Clinical samples and multiomics data sets were analyzed to characterize ZEB1 expression in pulmonary arterial hypertension. Myeloid-specific ZEB1 conditional knockout mice were subjected to hypoxia-induced pulmonary hypertension. Transcriptomic sequencing, metabolomic profiling, chromatin immunoprecipitation-quantitative polymerase chain reaction, dual-luciferase reporter assays, and coimmunoprecipitation were integrated to define ZEB1-dependent molecular, metabolic, and inflammatory programs in pulmonary and bone marrow-derived macrophages. Therapeutic potential was further evaluated using pharmacological interventions and adenoviral ZEB1 silencing in monocrotaline-induced pulmonary hypertension in rats.

RESULTS: ZEB1 was upregulated in pulmonary arterial hypertension and enriched in recruited disease-associated macrophages. Myeloid-specific ZEB1 deletion attenuated macrophage inflammation, pulmonary vascular remodeling, and right ventricular dysfunction. Mechanistically, ZEB1 bound the GLS (glutaminase) promoter and recruited BRD4 (bromodomain-containing protein 4), enhancing histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation at the GLS promoter and promoting GLS transcription and glutamine metabolic reprogramming. Restoration of GLS partially reversed the metabolic and inflammatory effects of ZEB1 deficiency. Pharmacological targeting of ZEB1, combined BRD4 and GLS inhibition, and adenoviral ZEB1 silencing ameliorated experimental pulmonary hypertension.

CONCLUSIONS: ZEB1 promotes macrophage glutamine metabolic reprogramming by recruiting BRD4 and enhancing histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation-dependent GLS transcription. This ZEB1-driven metabolic program promotes macrophage inflammation and pulmonary vascular remodeling, identifying the ZEB1-BRD4-GLS regulatory axis as a potential therapeutic target in pulmonary arterial hypertension.

articles.title: HuR Inhibition Attenuates Hypertension and Fibrosis in Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Upregulation of the RNA-binding protein HuR (human antigen R) has been reported in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), but its pathogenic role remains incompletely understood. We hypothesized that HuR promotes renal and vascular injury in hypertensive CKD and that pharmacological inhibition of HuR attenuates disease progression. We therefore investigated the role of HuR in deoxycorticosterone acetate (DOCA) plus Ang II (angiotensin II)-induced CKD and evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of the HuR inhibitor, KH3 .

METHODS: Male mice underwent uninephrectomy followed by DOCA+Ang II infusion with 1% NaCl in drinking water and were treated with KH3 or vehicle for 3 weeks. Control mice received saline without DOCA or Ang II.

RESULTS: DOCA+Ang II markedly increased HuR expression in circulating exosomes and kidney tissues, which was attenuated by KH3 treatment. KH3 reduced albuminuria, improved renal function, and attenuated kidney hypertrophy, glomerular, and tubulointerstitial fibrosis. These renoprotective effects were associated with reduced podocyte and tubular injury, decreased macrophage infiltration, and suppression of NF-κB (nuclear factor-kappa B) p65, Nox2 (NADPH oxidase 2), AKT (protein kinase B) phosphorylation, TGFβ1 (transforming growth factor β1), and Wisp1 (WNT1-inducible signaling pathway protein 1) signaling. KH3 also partially lowered arterial blood pressure in DOCA+Ang II-treated mice. Further studies in vascular smooth muscle cells and mesenteric resistance arteries suggested that HuR inhibition may suppress vascular profibrotic signaling associated with SGLT2 (sodium-glucose cotransporter 2).

CONCLUSIONS: HuR is upregulated in renal and vascular tissues in DOCA+Ang II-induced CKD and contributes to renal inflammation, oxidative stress, fibrosis, and vascular dysfunction. Pharmacological inhibition of HuR attenuates renal and vascular injury, supporting HuR as a promising therapeutic target for CKD.

articles.title: Piezo1 Responsiveness in Muscle Afferents and Mechanoreflex in Diabetic Rats.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abnormal mechanoreflex function from skeletal muscle significantly contributes to the heightened circulatory response during exercise in type 2 diabetes (T2DM). However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We hypothesized that the abnormal cardiovascular responses in T2DM are mediated by mechanoreflex-induced exaggerations resulting from enhanced Piezo1-mediated mechanosensitivity of muscle afferents.

METHODS: T2DM rats (Sprague-Dawley rats) were given a high-fat diet in combination with a low dose of streptozotocin. Using an in vivo decerebrated rat model and an ex vivo single-fiber recording preparation, we measured muscle mechanoreflex responses, mechanosensitivity of muscle afferents, and Piezo1-mediated responses. Piezo1 protein levels in the membrane fraction were detected by Western blotting in human embryonic kidney 293 (HEK293) cells.

RESULTS: Blood pressure and sympathetic nerve activity responses to mechanoreflex activation, as well as group IV muscle afferent firing to mechanical stimulation and the Piezo1 agonist (Yoda1), were significantly greater in T2DM rats. More importantly, Piezo1 agonist-induced blood pressure changes and group IV afferent firing were significantly potentiated by administration of lipopolysaccharide, a gut-derived inflammatory endotoxin. Furthermore, lipopolysaccharide significantly increased Piezo1 protein in the cell membrane, which was attenuated by a PKA (protein kinase A) inhibitor.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that activation of the lipopolysaccharide-Piezo1 pathway may contribute to enhanced responsiveness of group IV muscle afferents and may be associated with exaggerated circulatory responses to muscle mechanoreflex activation in T2DM.

articles.title: Extravascular Renal Denervation for Resistant Hypertension: First-in-Human Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catheter-based intravascular renal denervation produces modest, variable blood pressure reductions, partly because renal sympathetic nerves lie at variable depths within the periarterial adventitia and because accessory or early branching arteries are inaccessible to intraluminal catheters. We developed an extravascular renal denervation system (HyperQure) delivering circumferential radiofrequency energy from outside the artery and assessed its safety and efficacy. Here, we report the primary 3-month outcomes.

METHODS: This prospective, multicenter, single-arm, first-in-human pilot trial enrolled 10 patients with resistant hypertension (office blood pressure ≥140/90 mm Hg and daytime ambulatory systolic blood pressure [SBP] ≥135 mm Hg despite ≥3 antihypertensive agents) across 7 Korean centers. All underwent bilateral extravascular renal denervation on stable antihypertensive regimens. The primary end point was 3-month change in 24-hour ambulatory SBP; safety outcomes were assessed through 3 months.

RESULTS: All 10 patients (median age, 52.5 years; 7 men) completed follow-up. Seven patients (70%) had accessory or early branching arteries <3 mm typically ineligible for intravascular renal denervation; all were successfully ablated. Median 24-hour ambulatory SBP decreased by 25.0 mm Hg (P=0.008) and median office SBP by 39.5 mm Hg (P=0.002). Seven of 10 (70%) achieved office SBP <140 mm Hg despite a reduction in median antihypertensive burden from 6.0 to 4.5 agents. No major or procedure-related adverse events occurred; follow-up computed tomography angiography showed no vascular complications and renal function was preserved.

CONCLUSIONS: Extravascular renal denervation using the HyperQure renal denervation System warrants evaluation in a larger controlled trial, particularly in patients with complex renal arterial anatomy.

articles.title: A diabetic microenvironment targeted nano-hydrogel loaded with quercetin and EGF for integrated synergistic bacteriostasis and proliferation-promoting diabetic infected wound repair.
articles.abstract: The diabetic wound microenvironment is characterized by high levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS), persistent inflammation, and high susceptibility to infection, greatly hindering the therapeutic efficacy of traditional treatments. In this study, a multifunctional hydrogel (PPS/QR-EGF-Gel) incorporating ROS-responsive quercetin nanoparticles (PPS/QR) and epidermal growth factor (EGF) was developed to accelerate the repair of diabetic infected wounds. The synthesized hydrogel was designed with a dual-action mechanism: in response to the high-ROS environment, the PPS nanoparticles undergo cleavage, which not only releases quercetin (QR) to exert its broad-spectrum antibacterial, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory effects, but also generates nanoparticle fragments that help maintain the bioactivity of the co-delivered EGF. This preservation of EGF's activity significantly enhances its synergistic action with QR, robustly promoting cell proliferation, migration, and angiogenesis. As verified by in vitro experiments, the PPS/QR-EGF-Gel significantly inhibited pathogens including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA, with a bactericidal rate of 81.3-85.4%), decreased ROS levels, and accelerated the proliferation and migration of HaCaT cells and human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). In a diabetic rat model, the hydrogel apparently improved the wound closure rate, reduced the levels of inflammatory factors, and enhanced collagen deposition and angiogenesis. Moreover, proteomics analysis revealed that its superior combined therapeutic effects were achieved by suppressing the NF-κB inflammatory pathway and activating the EGFR/PI3K/AKT/VEGF pathway. This study provides a purification-repair integrated intelligent treatment strategy for diabetic infected wounds, demonstrating both clinical translation potential and broad applicability.

articles.title: Growth Hormone Stimulation Testing in Childhood: Diagnostic Pathways and Discordant Results in a Tertiary Centre Cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Growth hormone stimulation tests (GHSTs) are central to the diagnosis of growth hormone deficiency (GHD) despite recognised limitations. Two failed GHSTs are recommended to confirm GHD; however, a single failed test may be considered sufficient in selected cases. This study aimed to describe GHST practice in a tertiary paediatric endocrine centre, to determine how often an initial subthreshold GHST was not followed by a final diagnosis of GHD and to assess the diagnostic performance of IGF-I, IGFBP-3 and the IGF-I/IGFBP-3 molar ratio.

DESIGN: Retrospective observational study.

PATIENTS: Seventy-three children who underwent GHST for suspected GHD at a tertiary Irish paediatric endocrinology centre.

MEASUREMENTS: Clinical, biochemical and radiological data were reviewed, including height, BMI, height velocity, IGF-I, IGFBP-3, bone age and GHST results.

RESULTS: GHD was diagnosed in 34 children (47%) and excluded in 39 (53%). Of 47 children with a first peak GH below 7 µg/L, GHD was subsequently excluded in 13, an apparent false-positive rate of 27.7% (95% CI 16.9-41.8). Six of the 13 had a severely subthreshold initial response (peak GH < 3 µg/L). Discordant results were clustered in peripubertal children. IGF-I had poor sensitivity and specificity (45.5% and 50.0%, respectively); IGFBP-3 had low sensitivity but high specificity (9.1% and 100%, respectively). The IGF-I/IGFBP-3 molar ratio did not differ between diagnostic groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Approximately one in four children with a subthreshold first GHST was not ultimately diagnosed with GHD. These findings support the need for repeat testing before initiating treatment in children without independent evidence of pituitary disease.

articles.title: Spontaneous Resolution of Post-Myocardial Infarction Intramyocardial Dissecting Hematoma: A Case Report.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Intramyocardial dissecting hematoma (IDH) is a rare mechanical complication following acute myocardial infarction, characterized by blood accumulation within myocardial layers without complete rupture. Clinical outcomes are highly variable, ranging from spontaneous resolution to death. The optimal management strategy remains unclear, particularly regarding the role of conservative versus surgical approaches in hemodynamically stable patients. A 79-year-old male presented 1 month after anterior myocardial infarction treated with percutaneous coronary intervention. Echocardiography revealed a large (70 × 80 mm) heterogeneous mass with scattered echolucent spaces occupying more than half of the left ventricular cavity, originating from the akinetic apex and extending along the interventricular septum. Unlike typical thrombus, no communication with ventricular cavities or color Doppler flow was detected. Cardiac computed tomography revealed a hypodense, non-enhancing lesion (91 × 70 mm), raising the possibility of an intramyocardial hematoma. Despite the massive intracardiac mass, the patient remained hemodynamically stable. Serial echocardiographic monitoring over 2 weeks documented progressive hematoma reduction without additional medical intervention, anticoagulation, or surgical management. Complete resolution of the hematoma occurred without progression to ventricular septal rupture or free wall rupture. Spontaneous resolution of post-myocardial infarction IDH can occur in hemodynamically stable patients without surgical intervention. Serial echocardiographic monitoring is essential for detecting spontaneous regression and guiding management decisions. This case highlights the potential role of conservative management with close imaging surveillance and suggests that conservative management may represent an alternative to surgery in selected patients, particularly those who are hemodynamically stable.

articles.title: Bacterial adaptation is associated with tryptophan metabolism and persistence of nontypeable Haemophilus influenzae.
articles.abstract: Bacterial adaptation to the nutritional environment of the host is critical for infection. We hypothesize that responses to nutrient stress through microevolution enhance invasion, intracellular bacterial community (IBC) formation, and persistence of nontypeable Haemophilus influenzae (NTHI). We previously identified a mutant that arose during prolonged nutrient deprivation and exhibited in vitro persistence and increased IBC formation during experimental otitis media (OM). A single mutation in the gene encoding cyclic AMP phosphodiesterase reprioritizes NTHI metabolism during biofilm growth in this evolved strain with a significant increase in all proteins involved in tryptophan biosynthesis. Given the importance of tryptophan and tryptophan metabolites in host immunity and bacterial virulence, we evaluated the contribution of tryptophan biosynthesis and import on NTHI pathogenesis. Through mutational analyses, NTHI viability in vitro is dependent on tryptophan biosynthesis but independent of tryptophan import. We also observed decreased persistence of IBCs in the absence of tryptophan biosynthesis. In an experimental model of OM, both tryptophan biosynthesis and import mutant strains demonstrated increased fitness compared to the parental strain. The NTHI trp operon has a distinct organization from Escherichia coli and contains an ortholog of ydfG, an NADP-dependent 3-hydroxyl acid dehydrogenase, that contributes to oxidative stress resistance. This ydfG ortholog exhibits greater frequency in mucosal-associated NTHI strains, as compared with commensal or invasive strains. Understanding the underlying mechanisms that NTHI use to respond and survive within the host environment, particularly tryptophan biosynthesis, will inform the development of therapeutics to attenuate current NTHI infections and limit recurrent episodes of OM.IMPORTANCEBacteria exquisitely adapt to environmental cues to survive and, in some cases, cause disease. We observed that bacteria starved for heme-iron evolve to increase the expression of tryptophan biosynthesis genes. We determined that loss of tryptophan biosynthesis decreased intracellular bacterial survival. In an experimental model of middle ear infection, both tryptophan biosynthesis and import mutant strains demonstrated increased fitness compared to the parental strain. We determined that the organization of tryptophan biosynthesis and transport genes is distinct and contains a gene that encodes a protein that contributes to oxidative stress resistance. This gene exhibits greater frequency in mucosal-associated NTHI strains, as compared with commensal or invasive strains. These data reveal coordination of tryptophan metabolism with oxidative stress resistance for bacterial persistence.

articles.title: Coronary Plaque Phenotypes According to Physiological Disease Severity and Pullback Pressure Gradient.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary pressure pullback characterizes both the overall physiological severity and longitudinal distribution of coronary artery disease. However, the respective relationships of physiological disease severity and longitudinal disease distribution with local and vessel-wide plaque phenotypes remain incompletely understood.

AIMS: To investigate the relationships of physiological disease severity and longitudinal disease distribution with coronary plaque characteristics assessed by optical coherence tomography (OCT).

METHODS: We studied 216 patients with left anterior descending coronary artery disease who underwent OCT and angiography-based physiological assessment. Quantitative flow ratio (QFR) represented overall physiological disease severity, whereas the pullback pressure gradient (PPG) index characterized longitudinal disease distribution. Associations with local OCT characteristics and whole-vessel burden of plaque features were assessed using regression models, with physiological indices standardized per 1 SD increase.

RESULTS: Median QFR and PPG were 0.88 [0.73-0.95] and 0.76 [0.69-0.83], respectively. Lower QFR was strongly associated with greater maximum lipid arc (β per 1 SD increase, -39.16°; 95% CI, -52.01 to -26.31; p < 0.001). PPG was not associated with maximum lipid arc in univariable analysis (β, -9.18°; p = 0.19). After accounting for QFR, however, higher PPG was associated with greater lipid arc index (β, 112.26 °·mm; p = 0.012) and smaller minimum lumen area (β, -0.42 mm2; p = 0.011), with a similar association observed for maximum lipid arc (β, 16.60°; p = 0.045). Conversely, lower PPG was associated with greater whole-vessel counts of adverse plaque features in unadjusted analyses, but these associations were attenuated after accounting for QFR.

CONCLUSIONS: At comparable physiological disease severity, a more focal physiological pattern was associated with greater local lipid concentration and lumen compromise, whereas a more diffuse pattern was associated with greater whole-vessel counts of plaque features in unadjusted analyses. These findings suggest that physiological disease severity and longitudinal disease distribution provide complementary information on the spatial phenotype of coronary atherosclerosis.

articles.title: Enterobacter cloacae prevalence in fracture-related infections of the lower leg: a 7-year single centre retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Fracture-related infection (FRI) is a complication of trauma surgery. While FRI treatment guidelines are based on prosthetic joint infection data, we hypothesized that the presence of Gram-negative bacteria like Enterobacter cloacae might be underestimated in FRI. Our primary aim was to identify the prevalence of pathogens in FRI of the lower leg. A second aim was to explore factors associated with the presence of Enterobacter cloacae.

METHODOLOGY: Patients with an FRI of the lower leg between 1 January 2016 and 31 December 2022 were included. We performed a descriptive statistical analysis, and a multivariable logistic regression to examine associations between the outcome (presence/absence of Enterobacter cloacae) and selected covariates.

RESULTS: A total of 81 patients were included. The most frequent pathogens were Enterobacter cloacae (n = 42, 52%) and Staphylococcus aureus (n = 18, 22%). Enterobacter cloacae were the most cultured bacteria in monobacterial (n = 23/51, 45%) and polybacterial infections (n = 19/30, 63%). Fractures treated without external fixators (OR = 0.13, 95% CI [0.03-0.45], p < 0.001) and patients with higher BMI (OR = 0.86, 95% CI [0.76-0.96], p = 0.012) were significantly associated with a reduced odds of having an Enterobacter infection, while controlling for age, sex and open versus closed fracture.

CONCLUSION: A high prevalence of Enterobacter cloacae was observed in culture-positive FRI of the lower leg. Patients without external fixators and with higher BMI showed reduced odds of having an Enterobacter infection. This elevated prevalence emphasizes that this pathogen may warrant broader clinical attention. Our findings highlight the need for large prospective multicentric studies.

articles.title: What Cochlear Implantation with Attempted Hearing Preservation in Widened Vestibular Aqueduct Adds to Understanding About the Etiology and Pathogenesis of Hearing Loss: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: The journal of international advanced otology
articles.abstract: Widened vestibular aqueduct (WVA) is the commonest congenital inner-ear malformation associated with childhood sensorineural hearing loss. Proposed pathophysiological mechanisms include abnormal endolymph-perilymph pressure regulation, hyperproteinaceous perilymph and impaired ionic homeostasis, particularly in SLC26A4-related disease. These vulnerabilities have raised concerns about the feasibility of hearing preservation cochlear implantation (HPCI). The study aims to evaluate HPCI outcomes in children with WVA and identify prognostic factors that may clarify underlying pathophysiology. A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses-compliant systematic review (PROSPERO CRD420251128410) of MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Library, and CINAHL from inception to November 2025 identified studies reporting pre- and postoperative unaided thresholds in WVA cochlear implant recipients. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data. Heterogeneity in outcome definitions required narrative synthesis. Five observational studies including 58 WVA patients (228 total across all cohorts) met inclusion criteria. Hearing preservation ranged from 20%-83% using a variation of outcome criteria. Studies reported improved outcomes with round-window insertion, soft-surgery techniques, and lateral-wall electrodes. In the largest regression analysis, WVA independently predicted poorer preservation. SLC26A4-related WVA did not preclude preservation, and several cohorts reported small postoperative low-frequency threshold changes (<20 dB) despite universal perilymph leakage and varied sealing methods. No study quantified perilymph flow or assessed postoperative vertigo. Hearing preservation cochlear implantation in WVA is feasible, though outcomes vary. Evidence suggests deterioration may relate more to intrinsic abnormalities in cochlear pressure regulation and epithelial physiology, and to potential suction-related trauma, than to perilymph loss alone. Standardized audiometric reporting and integrated anatomical and genetic phenotyping are needed to refine prognostication for children born with WVA.

articles.title: Population pharmacokinetic analysis of lamivudine (3TC) in HIV-exposed neonates and pediatric participants living with HIV-1 from the IMPAACT 2019 and PETITE studies.
articles.abstract: Lamivudine is a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor widely used in combination antiretroviral therapy for the treatment of human immunodeficiency virus infection. Accurate dose selection in neonates and young children remains challenging because of rapid developmental changes in renal clearance. We updated an existing pediatric population pharmacokinetic (PopPK) model, previously developed using data from 210 participants across five studies, by incorporating a maturation function and integrating pharmacokinetic data from two additional studies, IMPAACT 2019 (n = 55) and PETITE (n = 24, all neonates), for a total of 289 participants aged 0.0137 (~5 days) to 19.1 years. Unlike the prior model, which did not include a maturation function, the refined PopPK model incorporates a sigmoid Emax maturation function on clearance (postmenstrual age at which clearance reaches 50% of its mature [adult] value (TM50) 51.4 weeks postmenstrual age; Hill coefficient 4.81), reflecting developmental immaturity of clearance mechanisms in early life. The PopPK model retained a one-compartment structure with first-order absorption and linear elimination. Estimation of allometric exponents for body weight further improved model fit, and inter-individual and inter-occasion variability were included in clearance, volume, and absorption rate constant. Model performance was assessed using standard goodness-of-fit diagnostics and visual predictive checks, which demonstrated good agreement between observed and model-predicted concentrations across the pediatric age and weight range. In conclusion, incorporation of a maturation function on clearance successfully extended the pediatric lamivudine PopPK model to term neonates and infants, with parameter estimates remaining consistent with the original model, supporting model-informed dose selection in this understudied population.

articles.title: Strain-level variation in Proteus mirabilis chondroitin sulfate degradation kinetics and regulation by urea.
articles.abstract: To establish infection, uropathogens must overcome several host defenses, including the glycosaminoglycan (GAG) layer coating the apical surface of the bladder urothelium. GAGs are thought to protect against urinary tract infections (UTIs) by acting as a barrier to uropathogen adherence. However, the ability of uropathogens to degrade and utilize GAGs, and the contribution of these activities toward UTI progression, are largely unknown. We previously discovered that Proteus mirabilis, a common cause of catheter-associated UTI (CAUTI), degrades the GAG chondroitin sulfate (CS). In this study, we sought to define the kinetics and regulation of CS degradation by diverse urinary P. mirabilis strains. We found variation in CS degradation kinetics between P. mirabilis strains and media types. CS degradation in one isolate, Pm123, was repressed by urea, and this repression was dependent on P. mirabilis urease activity. Complementation of the Pm123 endolyase into urea-insensitive HI4320 resulted in a urea-sensitive CS degradation phenotype, suggesting functional differences between the Pm123 and HI4320 endolyases. Sequence alignment and structural modeling identified two unique mutations within the Pm123 endolyase that may contribute to urea sensitivity. Finally, unlike urea-insensitive P. mirabilis strains, loss of CS lyase activity had no effect on Pm123 virulence in a mouse CAUTI model. Our results suggest that the kinetics and regulation of CS degradation differ between P. mirabilis strains, and regulation by urea in some strains may reduce the contribution of CS degradation to urovirulence during murine CAUTI.

articles.title: SSR42 enhances the hemolytic capacity of Staphylococcus aureus by stabilizing the hla mRNA.
articles.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus utilizes a complex regulatory network to precisely control a vast array of virulence factors and facilitate infection. One such regulator, the long regulatory RNA SSR42, is emerging as a key modulator of virulence factor abundance and pathogenesis. Previous work has shown that a primary role for SSR42 is controlling hemolytic behavior through the positive regulation of alpha-toxin (hla/Hla). Herein, we confirm that loss of SSR42 limits hemolytic capacity due to reduced Hla production. Others have suggested that this occurs through the SaeRS two-component system; however, using epistasis experiments, we reveal that SSR42 and SaeRS function independently to control Hla activity. Using a two-plasmid system optimized to detect regulatory RNA-mediated control in gram-positive bacteria, we demonstrate that SSR42 directly enhances Hla production through the hla 5' untranslated region. Using interaction prediction and targeted mutagenesis, we identify a discrete site upstream of the hla ribosome-binding site that is required for SSR42 binding and hemolytic activity. Transcriptional arrest experiments further show that SSR42 stabilizes the hla mRNA, increasing its half-life, and promoting downstream toxin production. Finally, electrophoretic mobility shift assays confirm a specific interaction between SSR42 and the hla 5' UTR. Collectively, these findings establish SSR42 as a major post-transcriptional regulator of S. aureus virulence and reveal a novel RNA-mediated mechanism that promotes alpha-toxin production through stabilization of the hla transcript.

articles.title: TREM2 drives monocyte-derived macrophage responses to Cryptococcus neoformans.
articles.abstract: Cryptococcus neoformans is an opportunistic fungus that can cause pulmonary and central nervous system infections after entry into the lungs. We previously established that signaling through the adapter protein DAP12 inhibits the antifungal response of monocyte-derived macrophages and worsens the survival of mice after C. neoformans infection. However, the molecular mechanisms by which DAP12 signaling is initiated during cryptococcosis remain inadequately characterized. In this study, we identify triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) as a DAP12-associated receptor that is induced on murine monocytes and interstitial macrophages in the lungs in response to C. neoformans infection. TREM2 subsequently represses fungal uptake and M1 polarization by monocyte-derived macrophages. Using an in vitro binding assay, we find that both murine and human TREM2 can directly bind to C. neoformans and that the absence of the cryptococcal cell wall antigen β-1,6-glucan disrupts these interactions. Overall, our findings suggest that the TREM2-DAP12 pathway plays an important inhibitory role in the host immune response to cryptococcal infection by impeding macrophage activation and phagocytosis of fungal cells. We also establish TREM2 as a receptor involved in direct fungal sensing of C. neoformans.

articles.title: Multiplicative Error Analysis: A Scale-Invariant View of TDDFT Two-Photon Absorption Benchmarks.
articles.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation
articles.abstract: Two-photon absorption (2PA) strengths span several orders of magnitude, yet time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) benchmark studies have commonly relied on raw-scale mean absolute errors and linear regression statistics. Such statistics can be dominated by the most intense transitions and do not distinguish systematic multiplicative bias, typical fold error, dynamic range reproduction, and rank preservation. Here, published TDDFT 2PA benchmarks based on coupled-cluster references are reanalyzed by using a scale-invariant, multiplicative framework. For the most widely used benchmark set [J. Chem.Theory Comput. 2022, 18, 1046], it is shown that the five strongest transitions, representing only approximately 10% of the data, account for up to 65.5% of the total raw absolute error. Consequently, raw-scale metrics assign disproportionate weight to a small number of intense transitions and may obscure method performance across the remainder of the intensity range. Across several benchmark sets, the analysis further reveals that similar raw-scale errors can arise from qualitatively different error structures. The multiplicative analysis goes beyond previously recognized qualitative trends by resolving them into directly comparable and interpretable components. These results demonstrate that neither individual raw-scale metrics nor their combinations provide a sufficient basis for identifying a reliable or generally recommended functional, and they support a multidimensional, scale-invariant assessment of 2PA benchmarks. The same framework may also be useful for other properties for which multiplicative errors provide a more appropriate description than additive deviations such as oscillator strengths, kinetic and radiative rate constants, and equilibrium constants.

articles.title: Role of Pancreatic Shear Wave Elastography in Children with Type 1 Diabetes: A Comparative and Correlative Study with Clinical and Laboratory Parameters.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate pancreatic stiffness in children with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) using two-dimensional shear wave elastography (2D-SWE), compare findings with age‑matched controls, and assess associations with pancreatic size, clinical parameters, and disease duration.

METHODS: Seventy‑six children (38 T1DM, 38 controls) aged 5-18 years underwent standardized pancreatic ultrasound with SWE of the head, body, and tail. Three readings per region were averaged. Pancreatic dimensions, fasting blood sugar (FBS), HbA1c, and clinical details were recorded. Group comparisons and correlation analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Children with T1DM showed significantly higher stiffness than controls across all regions (p < 0.001). Mean SWE increased with disease duration: recent‑onset 3.11 ± 1.02 kPa, intermediate 4.72 ± 0.88 kPa, long‑standing 6.29 ± 0.81 kPa; controls 2.85 ± 0.31 kPa. Pancreatic size was smaller in diabetics, with progressive reduction correlating with chronicity. SWE showed a strong positive correlation with disease duration (ρ = 0.823, p < 0.001) and an inverse correlation with pancreatic size. No meaningful association was seen between SWE and HbA1c or FBS. ROC analysis demonstrated good discriminatory performance of pancreatic SWE for differentiating children with T1DM from healthy controls.

CONCLUSIONS: Pancreatic stiffness is increased in children with T1DM and rises progressively with disease duration while pancreatic size declines. SWE reflects long‑term structural change rather than short‑term glycaemic status.

ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This study demonstrates that pancreatic SWE provides quantitative measures of pancreatic stiffness and helps elucidate its associations with pancreatic size and disease duration in children with T1DM.

articles.title: A Multidimensional Framework of Noncommunicable Disease Determinants among Adult Primary Healthcare Patients in Saudi Arabia: Evidence from the PaRIS Survey.
articles.journal: International journal for quality in health care : journal of the International Society for Quality in Health Care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) are a growing public health challenge in Saudi Arabia, placing increasing demands on primary healthcare (PHC). Using OECD Patient-Reported Indicator Survey (PaRIS) data, this study examined NCD prevalence and associated sociodemographic, behavioral, psychosocial, and health-system determinants among adult PHC patients.

METHODS: This cross-sectional analysis included 15,376 adults aged ≥18 years with at least one PHC visit in the six months preceding sampling. Participants self-reported NCDs, health behaviors, psychosocial factors, and healthcare experiences. Weighted prevalence estimates were calculated, and multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with having at least one NCD, reporting adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Most PHC patients reported at least one NCD. Arthritis or ongoing back/joint problems, diabetes, and hypertension were the most prevalent conditions. NCD prevalence was higher among older adults, individuals with lower educational attainment, and those who were overweight or obese. Difficulty understanding health information was associated with higher odds of NCD. In adjusted models, lower self-efficacy, lower perceived care quality, and access barriers were associated with lower odds of NCD.

CONCLUSIONS: NCDs among Saudi PHC patients reflect intersecting individual, psychosocial, and health-system factors. Patient-reported indicators can inform person-centered PHC and Vision 2030 health system transformation.

articles.title: Additional pulmonary blood flow strategy at bidirectional Glenn: impact on pulmonary artery growth and long-term Fontan outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Management of additional pulmonary blood (APBF) flow during staged palliation toward Fontan completion remains debated, however it may influence long-term outcomes. To assess whether APBF promotes pulmonary artery (PA) growth before Fontan completion and whether different APBF strategies correlate with distinct long-term outcomes.

METHODS: A retrospective single-center study was conducted on 205 patients undergoing Fontan completion between 1989 and 2024. Of these, 98 had APBF (83 antegrade APBF, 15 persistent mBT-shunt). Long-term outcomes included survival and freedom from PA stenting.

RESULTS: Pre-Fontan PA diameters were larger in patients with APBF than in those without APBF: LPA 10.70 ± 3.76 mm vs 8.80 ± 3.43 mm (p < 0.0001) and RPA 12.18 ± 3.65 mm vs 10.99 ± 3.65 mm (p = 0.032). Within the APBF group, antegrade flow was associated with larger PA diameters than persistent mBT-shunt: LPA 11.12 ± 3.70 mm vs 9.01 ± 3.51 mm (p < 0.0001) and RPA 12.56 ± 3.67 mm vs 11.12 ± 3.59 mm (p = 0.009). Overall survival was higher in patients with APBF at 20 years (97.5% [95% CI, 83.6%-99.6%] vs 88.2% [95% CI, 75.9%-94.4%], p = 0.032). Freedom from PA stenting at 10 years was 98% (95% CI, 81.7%-96.1%) in patients without APBF, 95% (95% CI, 86.3%-98.5%) in those with antegrade APBF, and 78% (95% CI, 45.9%-92.3%) in those with persistent mBT-shunts.

CONCLUSIONS: APBF appears to promote PA growth without increasing pulmonary pressures, but both APBF strategies may be associated with branch PA stenosis, with different timing according to flow type.

articles.title: A conserved CusR-dependent regulatory pathway couples copper homeostasis with oxidative stress resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae.
articles.abstract: Host-derived copper toxicity is a central antimicrobial strategy that restricts bacterial survival during infection, yet how pathogens integrate copper detoxification with oxidative stress resistance remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify the response regulator CusR as a pivotal coordinator of copper homeostasis and oxidative stress defense in Klebsiella pneumoniae. Loss of cusR results in profound defects in copper tolerance, marked intracellular copper accumulation, and hypersensitivity to hydrogen peroxide, accompanied by elevated intracellular reactive oxygen species. Mechanistically, CusR directly activates the cusCFBA copper efflux operon through promoter binding, whereas regulation of the copA transporter occurs independently of CusR. Importantly, a conserved aspartate residue (D56) within CusR is essential for its activity; both plasmid-based and chromosomal substitution of this residue abolish copper efflux regulation, disrupt copper homeostasis, and exacerbate oxidative stress susceptibility. Comparative sequence analysis further demonstrates that this residue is highly conserved across diverse bacterial species, underscoring its evolutionary importance in copper-responsive signaling. Collectively, our findings reveal a conserved Asp-dependent CusR-CusCFBA regulatory axis that couples copper detoxification to oxidative stress resistance, enabling bacterial adaptation to host-imposed copper stress.IMPORTANCECopper intoxication is an important host-mediated antimicrobial strategy that challenges bacterial pathogens during infection. Although copper resistance systems have been extensively studied, how bacteria coordinate copper detoxification with protection against oxidative stress remains poorly understood. In this study, we identify the response regulator CusR as a key factor linking copper homeostasis and oxidative stress resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae. We demonstrate that CusR directly controls the cusCFBA copper efflux system through promoter binding and that a conserved aspartate residue is essential for this regulatory function. Loss of CusR disrupts copper balance, increases reactive oxygen species accumulation, and reduces bacterial resistance to oxidative stress. These findings reveal a conserved regulatory mechanism that integrates metal stress adaptation with oxidative stress defense, providing new insights into how bacterial pathogens survive under host-imposed environmental pressures.

articles.title: Comment on "Effect of High Dose N-Acetyl Cysteine Supplementation on Markers of Oxidative Stress and Insulin Resistance in Non-Diabetic Patients With Metabolic Dysfunction Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Randomized Controlled Trial".
Intraspecies competition reveals branched-chain amino acid homeostasis as a targetable metabolic vulnerability in uropathogenic E. coli.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are among the most prevalent bacterial infections worldwide, with ~50% of women experiencing at least one UTI in their lifetime. Uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC) is the causative agent of ~80% of UTIs. In contrast, asymptomatic bacteriuria E. coli 83972 (ABU 83972) colonizes the human urinary bladder without causing symptoms and inflammation. Deliberate colonization with ABU 83972 reduced UTI incidence in patients with voiding disorders. However, the mechanisms by which ABU 83972 outcompetes uropathogens in the urinary tract remain poorly understood and are the focus of this report. We performed comparative metabolomics to identify metabolites that promoted the fitness of ABU 83972 in human urine compared to UPEC strain CFT073. Competition assays were conducted between ABU 83972 and UPEC CFT073 in human urine supplemented with select metabolites that were differentially abundant in metabolome profiling. There was a significant reduction in the fitness of ABU 83972 when supplemented with branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) such as leucine and isoleucine in a dose-dependent manner. Further, we identified that BrnQ, a low-affinity BCAA importer, is the main determinant of fitness advantage of ABU 83972 over UPEC. Using isogenic mutants, genetic complementation, amino acid analysis, cell culture, chemical inhibition of BCAA biosynthesis, and mouse models of UTI, we demonstrate that BCAA homeostasis represents a unique nutritional vulnerability in UPEC that could be targeted with chemical inhibitors. In summary, our study highlights that intraspecies competition between commensal and pathogenic strains could be used to detect novel fitness mechanisms and metabolic bottlenecks.

IMPORTANCE: Millions of people suffer from urinary tract infection (UTI) globally, and uropathogenic E. coli is the main cause of UTI. A urinary probiotic strain of E. coli has been used clinically to prevent UTI in some high-risk groups for recurrent UTI for more than 25 years. However, the mechanism of competition between the probiotic and pathogenic strains is not clear. We demonstrate that competition for specific amino acids is critical for the probiotic to compete against the pathogen. Our study identifies specific amino acid import and biosynthetic processes as targets for controlling UPEC growth during UTI.

articles.title: A convergent proline biosynthetic step couples cell wall integrity to virulence in Cryptococcus neoformans.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Metabolic adaptation is essential for the pathogenicity of the opportunistic fungus Cryptococcus neoformans. Although amino acid biosynthesis pathways are critical fitness determinants in fungal pathogens, the physiological contributions of proline biosynthesis remain incompletely understood, with most studies focusing on proline catabolism. Here, we characterized the proline biosynthetic enzymes Pro1, Pro2, and Pro3 in C. neoformans. Proline is produced by two routes that converge on Δ1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate (P5C): a de novo pathway from glutamate via Pro1 and Pro2, and an arginine-derived bypass via Car1 and Car2-both requiring Pro3 for the final reduction of P5C to proline. Although all biosynthetic mutants were strictly auxotrophic for proline, their requirements for virulence differed markedly: in a murine infection model, pro1Δ and pro2Δ mutants retained full virulence, whereas pro3Δ exhibited significantly attenuated virulence accompanied by growth defects and impaired cell wall integrity. Genetic disruption of P5C-generating routes partially restored distinct pro3Δ phenotypes, with PRO2 deletion alleviating delayed growth, and combined PRO2 and CAR2 deletion partially restoring cell size, while cell wall defects remained unresolved. This dissociation indicates that growth requires proper balance of P5C-generating metabolic flux, whereas cell wall integrity depends on a distinct mechanism that is not resolved by blocking P5C production. Together, these findings identify Pro3 as a metabolic gatekeeper coupling proline biosynthesis to cell wall homeostasis, establishing the biosynthetic branch of proline metabolism as a previously unappreciated determinant of fungal pathobiology.

IMPORTANCE: Cryptococcus neoformans is a leading cause of fungal meningitis worldwide, causing life-threatening infections primarily in immunocompromised individuals. To survive within the human host, this pathogen must synthesize essential nutrients through de novo biosynthesis when host-derived supplies are limited. Although proline catabolism has been studied extensively in fungal pathogens, the physiological roles of individual proline biosynthetic enzymes in human fungal pathogens remain incompletely understood. Here, we show that the terminal enzyme Pro3, but not the upstream enzymes Pro1 and Pro2, is selectively required for full virulence in a murine model. Pro3 supports pathobiological fitness by promoting growth under host-relevant conditions and maintaining cell wall integrity. These findings highlight the importance of proline biosynthesis beyond nutrient production and link this pathway to growth, cell wall integrity, and virulence in C. neoformans.

articles.title: Association of A Body Shape Index, But Not Body Mass Index, with Seated Arterial Stiffness Evaluated by Innovative Cardio-Ankle Vascular Index.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A Body Shape Index (ABSI) reflects abdominal adiposity independent of body size. Although the cardio-ankle vascular index (CAVI) is linked to ABSI, whether this association extends to innovative CAVI (iCAVI) remains unclear. We developed iCAVI, an arterial stiffness index measured from the aortic valve to the right brachial artery in the seated position and examined its association with ABSI.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 117 individuals undergoing cardiovascular risk assessment. iCAVI, ABSI, body mass index (BMI), and waist circumference (WC) were evaluated. Associations were assessed using Spearman's correlation and multivariable analyses adjusting for age and sex-adjusted analyses, with further adjustment for hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, and coronary artery disease. Adjusted iCAVI values across anthropometric tertiles were compared.

RESULTS: iCAVI was positively correlated with ABSI (ρ = 0.233, 95% CI [0.048, 0.402], p = 0.012), but not with WC (ρ = -0.054, 95% CI [-0.238, 0.134], p = 0.563) or BMI (ρ = -0.162, 95% CI [-0.339, 0.026], p = 0.081). Age- and sex-adjusted iCAVI increased across ABSI tertiles (2.79, 2.96, and 3.14; p for trend = 0.045). The linear contrast estimate was 0.25 (95% CI [0.01, 0.49]) and remained similar after further adjustment for hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, and coronary artery disease (0.23, 95% CI [-0.02, 0.48]; p for trend = 0.067).

CONCLUSIONS: ABSI was positively associated with iCAVI, whereas BMI and WC were not, suggesting that ABSI may capture aspects of body shape associated with arterial stiffness that are not reflected by conventional anthropometric indices.

articles.title: A novel interprofessional experience caring for post-intensive care and long COVID patients: the optimal clinic experience.
articles.abstract: This short report describes the development of an interprofessional ambulatory care clinic with an interprofessional education program at an academic medical center providing comprehensive care to patients previously hospitalized in the intensive care unit (ICU) or with COVID-19 from May 2020 to May 2026. The OPTIMAL Clinic (lOng COVID/PosT-Icu MultidisciplinAry cLinic) was created during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, with limited staff and temporary funding. Our team consisted of clinical pharmacy and physician trainees, nurse practitioners, occupational therapists, physical therapists, pharmacists, physicians, and social workers, who collaborated strategically and synergistically to optimize patient care. Across repeated evaluations, the clinic model was associated with increased preventive care and financial sustainability, and decreased emergency department visits and unplanned hospitalizations. Our interprofessional education program achieved high ratings from trainees in preceptor support, onboarding, clinical activities, and interprofessional education. Our OPTIMAL clinic exemplifies a model for interprofessional care and education for the support of complex patients after ICU or COVID-19 hospitalizations.

articles.title: Comparative genomics of the skin microbiome and associated isolates of patients undergoing mastectomy with immediate breast reconstruction.
articles.abstract: Mastectomy with immediate breast implant reconstruction (IBIR) is an increasingly common component of breast cancer treatment; however, these procedures carry a substantial risk of surgical site infections (SSIs) and noninfectious wound complications (NIWCs). We hypothesized that the local skin microbiota may contribute to the development of post-operative complications, in part by serving as a reservoir for pathobionts, such as Staphylococcus epidermidis and Cutibacterium acnes. We collected skin and intraoperative samples from 60 patients undergoing mastectomy with IBIR. To evaluate longitudinal shifts in community composition, we performed 16S rRNA gene sequencing of 151 breast and axilla skin swabs collected at pre- and post-operative time points. Using a comprehensive culture approach, we recovered diverse cultivable organisms and selected 232 S. epidermidis and 130 C. acnes isolates from skin swabs, implant swabs, and seroma fluid for whole-genome sequencing and comparative genomic analysis. We observed perturbations to community structure in the breast and axilla following mastectomy. These shifts were characterized by a significant and persistent depletion of Corynebacterium spp., which did not resolve in patients who subsequently developed an SSI. We also uncovered outcome-specific genomic signatures in S. epidermidis isolates, which may offer mechanistic insight into the role of this species in SSI and NIWC development. Importantly, we also identified genomic signatures detectable prior to mastectomy and infection diagnosis that may offer clinical utility toward predicting post-operative complications. Together, these findings illustrate the importance of the skin microbiome in SSI and NIWC development following mastectomy with IBIR.IMPORTANCEAn improved understanding of the relationship between surgical sites and adjacent resident skin microbiota can help identify which patients are at increased risk for developing surgical site infections and noninfectious wound complications. By characterizing bacterial communities before mastectomy with immediate breast reconstruction and during subsequent healing, we sought to evaluate how changes in community composition may contribute to the development of post-operative complications. We also performed in-depth genomic analyses of Staphylococcus epidermidis and Cutibacterium acnes isolates recovered from patients to identify genetic components that may determine whether an isolate protects or predisposes patients toward development of post-operative complications. Last, we identified genomic signatures detectable prior to surgery and infection diagnosis that are correlated with patient outcome, which may serve as informative biomarkers to inform patient care.

articles.title: Bridging microbiology and public health through simulation-based learning.
articles.abstract: Within our synchronous, online global health-focused upper-level microbiology course, we find that students struggle to translate learning to real-world applications. For example, consider the recent measles outbreaks and major events such as the COVID-19 pandemic, which prompt many questions about how basic microbiological information is used by public health professionals. To address these points, we created a simulation-based curriculum that places students in an action role during an infectious disease outbreak. Our stand-alone curriculum walks through a historical measles outbreak that introduces outbreak investigation, community communication, and how these depend on microbiological knowledge. By using breakout groups, students have an opportunity to decide classifications, public messaging, and intervention metrics. We provide students with an outbreak investigation reference worksheet and interweave breakout rooms with didactic vignettes covering background information while revealing actual responses to outbreaks in conjunction with data obtained by responding scientists. Students synthesize material and apply it in real-time, allowing them to exercise critical thinking. Pilot testing in a small, upper-division, virtual classroom suggests that this curriculum has strong potential for increasing mastery of learning objectives and bolstering the relevance of microbiology and public health to popular media.

articles.title: An antibiotic-treated mouse model reveals the progression of intestinal botulism.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Intestinal botulism, including infant botulism and adult intestinal toxemia botulism, is a life-threatening disease caused by intestinal infection with Clostridium botulinum (Cb) spores. Infants are particularly susceptible to Cb infection because of their immature gut microbiota, whereas healthy adults are generally protected by gut microbiota-mediated colonization resistance. Thus, immature gut microbiota or gut dysbiosis is thought to permit Cb colonization. However, the mechanisms underlying colonization resistance and disease progression remain poorly characterized. Here, using adult mice with antibiotic-induced dysbiosis, we established a model for studying Cb infection and characterized intestinal colonization, bacterial expansion, botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) accumulation, and disease progression during intestinal botulism. Intestinal botulism developed in antibiotic-treated mice after intragastric administration of strain 62A spores, whereas untreated adult mice showed no symptoms. In antibiotic-treated mice, Cb expanded over time in fecal samples, followed by accumulation of serotype A BoNT (BoNT/A), which correlated with the progression of botulism symptoms. Cb growth and BoNT/A accumulation occurred mainly in the cecum and colon, but not in the small intestine. Furthermore, this mouse model was applicable to the analysis of intestinal botulism caused by other Cb strains, including 7I03-H, Okra, and Osaka05. Taken together, our findings clarify key aspects of intestinal botulism pathogenesis. This mouse model may provide a useful platform for elucidating the mechanisms underlying intestinal botulism, including infant botulism, and for developing novel therapeutic strategies.

IMPORTANCE: Botulism is a life-threatening disease caused by botulinum neurotoxin, one of the most powerful toxins known. In intestinal botulism, Clostridium botulinum spores enter the intestine, grow there, and release toxin inside the body. However, the detailed process by which intestinal botulism develops remains poorly understood. In this study, we established a mouse model that allows the progression of intestinal botulism to be examined over time. Using this model, we showed that bacterial growth in the intestine, accumulation of biologically active toxins, and worsening of symptoms are closely linked. We also identified the cecum and colon as the main sites of bacterial colonization and toxin accumulation. This model can be used to analyze multiple C. botulinum strains with different characteristics and provides a useful tool for understanding how intestinal botulism develops and for guiding future preventive and therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: BK virus-neutralizing antibodies converge on a shared site of vulnerability on VP1.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: BK virus is a human polyomavirus that infects approximately 80% of adults and establishes lifelong latency. Although primary infection is typically asymptomatic, viral reactivation in kidney transplant recipients can cause BK virus-associated nephropathy, leading to graft dysfunction and rejection. Despite the clinical severity of viral reactivation, antiviral treatment options remain limited. Notably, high serum titers of BK virus-neutralizing antibodies are associated with reduced BK virus DNAemia in kidney transplant recipients, suggesting an important role for humoral immunity in controlling viral replication. Here, we curated a comprehensive database of human antibodies targeting the major capsid protein VP1 by integrating previously reported sequences with newly generated data. Sequence analysis revealed only limited convergence among these antibodies. Nevertheless, functional and biochemical characterization showed that most neutralizing antibodies compete for overlapping epitopes, indicating convergence on a common antigenic site within the receptor-binding cleft of VP1. Together, these findings define an immunodominant site of vulnerability on the BK virus capsid and provide a mechanistic basis for the rational design of vaccines and antibody-based therapies.

IMPORTANCE: BK virus (BKV) reactivation is a common complication in kidney transplant recipients, yet no approved antivirals are currently available. The standard of care consists of reducing immunosuppressive therapy, which carries an inherent risk of graft rejection. Antibodies represent promising therapeutic agents for the prevention and treatment of viral infections, particularly when effective vaccines are unavailable. Elucidating the dominant mechanisms of antibody-mediated protection is crucial for guiding the design and optimization of antibody-based therapies. In this study, we identify novel potent neutralizing antibodies against BKV, compare them with previously reported monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), and demonstrate that they compete for binding. Our findings show that most neutralizing mAbs converge on the receptor-binding cleft of VP1, identifying this region as both a major site of vulnerability and a hotspot for immune-driven viral escape, with important implications for therapeutic design.

articles.title: Pathogenic mechanisms of Echovirus 18-induced encephalitis in a novel hFcRn transgenic mouse model.
articles.abstract: Echovirus 18 (E18) poses an escalating neurological threat in children, with its complex pathogenesis impeded by the absence of robust animal models for comprehensive mechanistic investigation. This study establishes an E18-induced viral encephalitis (VE) model in 7-day-old human neonatal Fc receptor (hFcRn) transgenic mice. After intracranial inoculation with 4.0  ×  106  PFU of E18, mice developed marked signs of infection, characterized by progressive weight loss, motor impairment, elevated viral loads in the brain, and histopathological evidence of VE, ultimately resulting in approximately 75% mortality. The E18-infected mouse brains were accompanied by lymphocytic and granulocytic infiltration, neuronal shrinkage, and focal hemorrhage, with magnetic resonance imaging revealing prominent signal abnormalities in the subarachnoid space and periventricular regions. Interestingly, although all cell types of the brain can serve as carriers of the virus at the single-cell level, E18 exhibits distinct cellular tropism by preferentially targeting astrocytes and microglia rather than neurons and neurofilaments. Additionally, E18 infection orchestrates a complex and adaptive immune response, with dynamic changes among astrocytic subtypes reflecting the evolution of this immune response. Overall, this study successfully establishes a disease model that enhances our understanding of E18-induced encephalitis and provides a valuable platform for evaluating therapeutic interventions and developing vaccines.IMPORTANCEE18 represents an important pathogen in infectious diseases, with potential neurological complications that warrant further investigation. However, due to ethical and technical limitations, its neuropathological mechanisms have long remained unexplored. This study presents a novel encephalitis model using 7-day-old hFcRnTg mice. The integration of MRI, histopathology, and multi-omics analysis elucidated the molecular mechanisms of viral neural invasion, offering critical insights into pediatric viral encephalitis and potential therapeutic strategies. This animal model provides a valuable platform for understanding E18-induced encephalitis mechanisms and evaluating potential therapeutics and vaccines.

articles.title: Perceived learning needs for interprofessional education in diabetes care: a qualitative study of practising primary healthcare professionals.
articles.abstract: Healthcare systems must shift from siloed uniprofessional education toward interprofessional collaborative care to meet the demands of an aging population and rising global diabetes prevalence. Interprofessional education (IPE)-emphasizing understanding of team roles, effective communication, and mutual respect-is increasingly essential for collaborative care. However, IPE as continuing professional development for practising professionals, as opposed to students, remains underdeveloped, with limited understanding of their learning needs. This qualitative study, a secondary analysis of a study on IPE in primary care, explored the learning needs of healthcare professionals. It focuses on diabetes as an exemplar of chronic disease where management is distributed across multiple professions. Using semi-structured interviews with 20 participants from multiple professions, thematic analysis identified four areas of perceived learning needs: greater understanding of interprofessional roles to support collaboration; trust, respect, and effective communication to enhance teamwork; gaps in diabetes care, including prevention, lifestyle and dietary counseling, pharmacology, management of complex cases, and psychosocial challenges; and a preference for interactive formats, such as case-based discussions and journal clubs. These findings highlight the value of engaging healthcare professionals in identifying educational needs, which is crucial for developing relevant, authentic, and participatory IPE curricula for diabetes care.

articles.title: Perioperative Outcomes in Stage 1 Palliated Infants Undergoing Noncardiac Procedures: A Comparison by Shunt Type.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interstage infants with single-ventricle (SV) physiology following Stage I palliation represent a high-risk population for noncardiac procedures requiring anesthesia. Data comparing perioperative outcomes by shunt type remain limited.

AIMS: Describe anesthetic management, perioperative complications, and postoperative outcomes in interstage SV infants undergoing noncardiac interventions and compare outcomes between right ventricle-to-pulmonary artery (Sano) and modified Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt (mBTTS) patients.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center cohort study of interstage SV infants with Stage I palliation undergoing noncardiac surgery or nonsurgical procedures requiring anesthesia between 2015 and 2023. Outcomes were stratified by shunt type.

RESULTS: A total of 208 noncardiac interventions in 120 interstage SV infants were analyzed; 136 (65.4%) encounters in 86 Sano patients and 72 (34.6%) encounters in 34 mBTTS patients. Compared with mBTTS infants, Sano patients underwent interventions at a younger age (57 [IQR 40-83] vs. 105 [59-278] days, p < 0.001) and lower weight (3.6 [3.0-4.1] vs. 4.8 [3.4-7.3] kg, p < 0.001). mBTTS procedures had higher rates of ventricular dysfunction (34.3% vs. 12.7%, p < 0.001), chromosomal abnormalities (63.9% vs. 19.1%, p < 0.001), gastrointestinal comorbidities (87.5% vs. 72.1%, p = 0.014), and hematologic comorbidities (41.7% vs. 22.8%, p = 0.006). Hemodynamic instability requiring vasoactive support was the most common perioperative complication and occurred similarly between groups (31.9% mBTTS vs. 31.6% Sano, p = 0.962). There were no perioperative cardiac arrests. Rates of postoperative escalation of care (2.9%), reintubation (3.0% vs. 2.9%, p = 0.999), readmission (16.2% vs. 16.9%, p = 0.999), and 30-day mortality (2.3% vs. 2.9%, p = 0.999) were low and comparable between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite the high-risk physiology of interstage SV patients, perioperative outcomes were comparable between Sano and mBTTS cohorts. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and should not imply low procedural risk. Favorable outcomes likely reflect careful patient selection, multidisciplinary perioperative care, and specialized institutional expertise.

articles.title: Orientia tsutsugamushi genotypes associated with severe scrub typhus in South India.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Orientia tsutsugamushi is an obligate intracellular bacterium with a complex genome, causing mite-borne scrub typhus in many parts of Asia. We determined O. tsutsugamushi genotypes in chigger mites, small mammal hosts and human fever cases to explore genotype-specific virulence.

METHODS: We enrolled scrub typhus patients from two hospitals in Tamil Nadu, India. Chigger mites were collected from small mammals trapped in 25 rural villages located within the catchment areas of the hospitals. Samples underwent screening for Orientia with real-time PCR followed by nested PCR of the partial tsa56 gene and Sanger sequencing. Phylogenetic trees were used to group sequences into clades, labelled according to the nearest reference genotypes.

RESULTS: We determined 138 tsa56 sequences from 1165 blood samples from human fever cases, 63 sequences from 762 chigger pools, and 58 sequences from 874 small mammals. Sequences were grouped into nine genotypes. The two most common genotypes in chiggers and small mammals were never found in human scrub typhus cases, while genotypes common in humans were rare in chiggers. There was a positive relationship between the human-to-chigger genotype prevalence ratio and the genotype-specific proportions of human infections that were severe (r= 0.87, p= 0.011). Two genotypes, labelled Kato-Vellore and TA763-Vellore, caused 72% of infections involving shock and all five observed deaths. The genotype-specific risk of shock was closely associated with the prevalence of eschar skin lesions (r= 0.84, p= 0.017).

CONCLUSION: O. tsutsugamushi genotypes differed strongly between chiggers and human fever patients and showed marked variation in clinical severity.

articles.title: Development and Validation of EPIC-US: A Reference Model for COPD Policy Evaluation in the United States.
articles.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: The large and growing burden of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) requires evidence-based policies to improve patient outcomes and reduce healthcare costs. We developed the Evaluation Platform in COPD in the U.S. (EPIC-US), a whole-disease model of COPD capable of evaluating interventions across all stages of disease progression within a single policy platform.

OBJECTIVES: The objectives were to develop EPIC-US by adapting a model version developed for Canada (EPIC) and internally and externally validate EPIC-US to an independent clinical cohort.

METHODS: EPIC-US is a stochastic discrete-event simulation model of COPD for U.S. individuals aged ≥40 years. It simulates COPD progression based on individualized trajectories of lung function decline and exacerbations. We matched population size to U.S. census projections for 2015-2060. All-cause mortality was taken from U.S. life tables. Historical and projected trends in tobacco smoking prevalence were aligned with 2018 and 2023 National Health Interview Survey (NHIS) results, while COPD prevalence was informed by National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) data. We used clinical trials, meta-analyses and U.S. administrative data to inform the rate and severity of exacerbations. We externally validated moderate exacerbations and severe exacerbations using the U.S. sub-sample of the NOVEL observational longiTudinal studY (NOVELTY).

RESULTS: EPIC-US simulated outputs closely matched module-specific internal validation targets. The predicted population size of ≥ 40-year-olds was within 1-2% of U.S. Census projections. Predicted mean COPD prevalence (8.1% for ages 40-59 years; 14.4% for ages 60-79 years), and smoking prevalence in 2018 (12.9%) and 2023 (10.1%) were within 0.1-0.4% of NHIS and NHANES estimates. In 2016, EPIC-US predicted 560 hospitalizations for COPD per 100,000 person-years, consistent with the observed rate of 510 hospitalizations. In external validation, severe exacerbations rates in EPIC-US (0.039; 95% CI 0.035-0.043 per patient-year) were comparable to NOVELTY (0.022 per patient-year, 95% CI 0.008-0.065). EPIC-US replicated differences in exacerbation rate across classes of inhaled therapies. However, EPIC-US overpredicted the rate of moderate exacerbations relative to NOVELTY.

CONCLUSION: EPIC-US is the first multi-purpose, whole-disease model of COPD in the U.S., providing a policy-ready platform for simulating both the clinical and economic burden of the disease.

articles.title: Local complications of peripheral intravenous vasopressor use with phentolamine as an antidote: a retrospective review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prior studies have indicated that peripheral administration of vasopressors, particularly norepinephrine, can be considered safe, with local complications occurring in 0% to 1.8% of patients. Our study further explored the local skin complications from peripheral vasopressor administration treated with phentolamine in a large health care system.

METHODS: A retrospective chart review was performed on patients who received phentolamine for effects of local infiltration of pressors. Data were collected for demographics, vasopressor dose and duration of use, phentolamine dose and time after extravasation until administration, peripheral intravenous characteristics, as well as outcomes such as length of stay and mortality. Data on patients who did and did not require central venous catheter placement postextravasation were compared.

RESULTS: Of 92 patients with infiltrated vasopressor intravenous access who required phentolamine, the mean age was 69, with 65% being female and a mean body mass index of 28 kg/m2. The most common sites of intravenous access were the antecubital fossa (33%) and forearm (27%). Mean number of hours prior to extravasation of peripheral vasopressors requiring phentolamine administration was 21 hours. Mean number of minutes prior to phentolamine administration after extravasation was 131 minutes. Seventy-six percent of patients did not any have significant ischemic tissue injury with extravasation, and 24% of patients had only minor bruising and erythema. Two significant reactions occurred, including deep vein thrombosis and local skin necrosis. Fifty-two percent of patients required a subsequent central venous line placement. The mean length of stay was 5.4 days in the intensive care unit and 11.8 days in the hospital, and in-patient mortality was 17%.

CONCLUSION: In our large cohort of patients with extravasation from peripheral vasopressors managed with local phentolamine administration, severe tissue skin or soft tissue injury was rare.

articles.title: Increased Adoption of Robot-Assisted Appendectomy Without Improved Outcomes and Lower Modeled Value.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Surgeons
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robot-assisted appendectomy use is increasing despite uncertain clinical benefit and economic value relative to laparoscopy. We evaluated comparative outcomes, operative efficiency, and modeled value.

STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults undergoing intended minimally invasive appendectomy for appendicitis using 2022-2024 ACS NSQIP data. Robotic utilization was assessed among 140,148 patients. Clinical outcomes were compared using 1:2 propensity-score matching. The primary endpoint combined unplanned conversion to open surgery, postoperative transfusion, organ-space surgical-site infection, and reoperation. Surgical costs were simulated using literature-derived inputs; value incorporated risk-adjusted outcomes and simulated costs.

RESULTS: Robotic utilization increased from 0.7% in 2022 to 2.7% in 2024. Among 2,257 robot-assisted and 4,514 matched laparoscopic cases, the primary composite occurred in 5.5% versus 5.3% (OR 1.06; 95% CI 0.85-1.32; P=.61). Robot-assisted appendectomy required 15.48 additional operative minutes (95% CI 13.66-17.31; P<.001), without significant differences in readmission, mortality, or length of stay. Median simulated costs were $4,526 versus $2,416. Laparoscopic-to-robotic modeled value ratios ranged from 1.53 to 1.80. Even assuming no incremental robotic procedural-cost premium, laparoscopy retained higher modeled value for the primary composite (ratio 1.31; 95% CI 1.09-1.54). Exploratory analyses of complicated appendicitis and BMI ≥40 kg/m² identified no significant clinical advantage with robotics.

CONCLUSIONS: Robot-assisted appendectomy utilization increased nearly fourfold without an observed improvement in short-term outcomes. Longer operative time, higher simulated costs, and lower modeled value persisted across sensitivity analyses, supporting continued scrutiny of robotic adoption for an operation effectively performed laparoscopically.

articles.title: Propolis Supplementation in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects 38% of adults globally, with limited pharmacotherapy. Propolis, a bee-derived compound with diverse biological activities, has emerged as a potential adjunct therapy. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effects of propolis supplementation on hepatic steatosis, metabolic parameters, and liver function in adults with MASLD. We searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library from inception to December 2025 without language or publication-status restrictions and included randomized controlled trials comparing propolis with placebo or dietary counseling in adults with MASLD or nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias with the Cochrane ROB 2.0 tool. Meta-analyses used random-effects models. Publication bias was assessed with Doi plots and the Luis Furuya-Kanamori (LFK) index, and certainty of evidence with the GRADE approach. Four trials (n = 178) of Iranian poplar-type propolis were included. Propolis was associated with significant improvement in hepatic steatosis (three trials, n = 156; RR: 2.41; 95% CI: 1.59-3.66; p < 0.001; I2 = 0%) and modestly reduced fasting glucose (MD: -3.80 mg/dL; p = 0.018). No significant effects were observed on insulin sensitivity indices, lipid profiles, anthropometric measures, or liver enzymes. No publication asymmetry was detected (LFK index = 0.82). Exploratory single-study CYP2E1 and TRPV4 signals were non-significant for propolis monotherapy versus control and confounded by exercise co-intervention. In a small number of short-term trials, propolis supplementation was associated with improvement in ultrasound-assessed hepatic steatosis, with low heterogeneity.
