However, limited trials, small samples, restriction to Iranian propolis, absence of histological endpoints, and single-study mechanistic findings position this as hypothesis-generating research. GRADE certainty was very low to low, underscoring the need for larger, well-designed trials.

articles.title: In Memoriam: Regino "Regy" Gonzalez-Peralta, MD (1959-2026).
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition

articles.title: Epoxy-Functionalized Polysilsesquioxane Coatings for Rear-Side Impact Protection of Thin Functional Ceramics.
articles.abstract: High-performance protective coatings capable of preventing catastrophic impact fracture of thin brittle inorganic substrates are urgently demanded for next-generation 5G/6G consumer electronics; however rational design strategies that simultaneously retain pristine surface aesthetics and achieve prominent shock resistance are still lacking. Herein, a rigid epoxy-functionalized polysilsesquioxane hybrid resin is synthesized, followed by cross-linking with various amine curing agents through a high-efficiency synchronous thermal-moisture dual-curing route. The optimized EGSI coating crosslinked by isophorone diamine (IPDA) achieves a pencil scratch hardness of 9H and a nanoindentation modulus of 2.66 GPa. Viscoelastic characterization confirms a distinctive filler-free self-reinforcement effect originating from the siloxane skeleton; the glass transition becomes indistinct, and the optimized coating preserved ∼40% of its initial glassy storage modulus, corresponding to a remarkably high rubbery plateau modulus of ∼750 MPa up to 300 °C. Ball-drop impact tests support the effectiveness of the proposed rigid backing structural constraint mechanism. When coated on the rear face of 300 μm structural ceramic sheets, the EGSI layer elevates the maximum crack-free nominal drop energy to 63.9 mJ, representing a 233% enhancement compared with bare ceramics. Different from conventional front-side energy-absorbing coatings, this noninvasive rear-side reinforcement scheme avoids damaging the decorative exterior of ceramic components and enables low-cost upgrading of ordinary sintered ceramics to high shock-resistant grade. This study establishes a design approach for the tested systems and coating configuration optimization methodology for reinforcing brittle substrates, showing great application prospects in smartphone ceramic back covers, ultrathin glass panels, and other electronic protective components.

articles.title: Adoption of ESC Guideline-Directed Heart Failure Pharmacotherapy and Outcomes: A Nationwide Claims-Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The actual European heart failure (HF) guidelines recommend the combination of four drugs as a standard therapy (angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor (ACEI)/angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB)/angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI); beta-blocker (BB); mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA); sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT-2i)) in patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). We investigated the current use of this combined treatment in comparison to partly using these drugs in routine data with respect to outcomes of mortality and readmission.

METHODS: We included anonymized data from all patients who were insured with Germany's largest health insurer and had a claims record for hospitalization (2021-2023, follow-up in 2024) with a primary hospital diagnosis of HF. The use of different combinations of the four drug classes and their association with mortality and readmission within 91-365 days following the index stay were analysed (n = 307,755). Data were adjusted for a large set of potential confounders including age, sex, and comorbidities. In addition, the frequency of different 2-, 3-, and 4-drug heart failure medications was assessed from 2019 to 2023.

RESULTS: In 2019 the dominant combination of drugs was ACEI/ARB and BB in nearly 37.84% of all cases. By 2023, the dominating combination was ACEI/ARB/ARNI, BB and SGLT-2i with or without an additional MRA (40.85%). The complete four-pillar therapy was prescribed in 21.81% of cases, while the old combination of ACEI/ARB and BB declined to 21.07%. Outcomes were assessed in 307,755 cases. In total, 55,985 of 298,535 (18.8%) included HF patients died 91-365 days after hospital discharge. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models indicated a significantly lower mortality risk when patients had a combined treatment of all four drugs compared to a two-drug therapy (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.86-0.92). The four-drug therapy was more effective with respect to mortality compared to the three-drug combination with an MRA (0.85, 95% CI 0.82-0.89). The comparison with a three-drug combination including an SGLT-2i performed equally (0.99, CI 0.95-1.03). Female sex was an independent negative predictor of four-drug therapy prescription after multivariable adjustment (AOR 0.62, 95% CI 0.60-0.63).

CONCLUSIONS: Our study suggests that the comprehensive four-drug therapy for heart failure is increasingly implemented in routine care and is independently associated with lower mortality and readmission rates. A three-drug combination including an SGLT-2i may be equivalent in selected cases. Female sex is associated with a lower likelihood of four-drug therapy prescription. These hypothesis-generating results underscore the necessity of investigating sex-specific clinical phenotypes and prescribing patterns in heart failure populations.

articles.title: Acute aortic syndrome rule-out criteria: development and external validation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Acute aortic syndrome (AAS) is a rare but catastrophic event, presenting with non-specific symptoms that mimic common conditions, and carries a mortality approaching 80% when missed. Current clinical tools, including the Aortic Dissection Detection Risk Score (ADD-RS) and its refinement, the simplified AORTA score, achieve high sensitivity when combined with D-dimer but fail to identify a population at sufficiently low risk to safely avoid further testing. To address this gap, the Acute Aortic Syndrome Rule-Out Criteria (ARC) were developed and validated, a pragmatic bedside tool designed to safely exclude AAS in low-risk patients without additional testing.

METHODS: A retrospective multistep derivation and validation study was conducted. The derivation cohort included patients with confirmed AAS from the International Registry of Acute Aortic Dissection (IRAD). Starting from existing scores, candidate predictors were identified from the IRAD dataset and sequentially added to achieve sensitivity ≥ 99%. External validation was performed in patients with suspected AAS across three prospective multicentre cohorts (ADvISED, PROFUNDUS, and DAShED). Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using sensitivity and specificity with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: The final seven-variable ARC included age >60 years, abrupt onset pain, severe pain, hypotension/shock, neurological deficit, pulse deficit, and known aortic disease. Patients were classified as positive if any ARC variable was present and negative only if all variables were absent. In the derivation cohort, ARC achieved a sensitivity of 99.2% (95% CI 99.1-99.3). In the ADvISED/PROFUNDUS cohort (4598 patients, 10.2% AAS prevalence), sensitivity was 100% (95% CI 99.2-100) with specificity 23.7% (95% CI 22.4-25.0). In the DAShED cohort (5346 patients, 0.3% prevalence), sensitivity was 100% (95% CI 76.8-100) and specificity 36.4% (95% CI 35.1-37.7), ruling out 36.3% of patients without missing any AAS cases.

CONCLUSIONS: ARC is an externally validated, pragmatic clinical rule demonstrating high diagnostic sensitivity in a large external validation cohort. When incorporated into existing diagnostic pathways, ARC has the potential to reduce unnecessary testing while maintaining diagnostic performance. Further prospective validation is required to confirm its clinical utility.

articles.title: Disparities in RSV Hospitalisations Among Children Under 2 Years in NSW, Australia.
articles.journal: Journal of paediatrics and child health
articles.abstract:
AIM: To estimate RSV hospitalisation rates among children ≤ 2 years in New South Wales (NSW), Australia over two decades; to examine how rates varied by age, prematurity and selected co-morbidities and to describe temporal, seasonal and geographic patterns in RSV hospitalisation across NSW.

METHODS: RSV hospitalisation rates were calculated using linked population data for all children ≤ 2 years in NSW from 2002 to 2020 (n = 1 770 628). Infant and maternal factors were analysed as covariates using a univariate log-binomial model to determine RSV admission risk between groups. Geographical distributions were visualised using heatmaps according to location at birth.

RESULTS: The overall RSV hospitalisation rate during 2004-2020 was 11.2 per 1000 child-years (95% CI 11.1-11.4) while during the contemporary pre-pandemic period of 2016-2019, the rate was 15.4 (15.1-15.7). Compared to children born term without comorbidities (8.41 admissions per child-years at risk [7.96-8.88]), rates of RSV hospitalisations were significantly higher among premature children (23.8 [23.2-24.5]) and children with any co-morbidities (48.2 [46.1-50.4]). Children with primary immunodeficiency (8.12 [6.78-9.72]), bronchopulmonary dysplasia (6.54 [6.06-7.06]), Down syndrome (5.10 [4.38-5.93]) and congenital heart disease (3.70 [3.53-3.88]) had persistently elevated hospitalisation rates into the second year of life. Hospitalisation rates were higher in Greater Sydney and subtropical northeastern coastal NSW where RSV activity began earlier and was less seasonally defined than temperate regions.

CONCLUSIONS: Strategies to protect premature children and those with comorbidities against RSV are warranted up to 2 years of age given the persistently elevated RSV risk. Regional RSV epidemiology should be considered when developing immunisation strategies.

articles.title: Management of recurrent left atrial leiomyosarcoma.
articles.journal: Turk gogus kalp damar cerrahisi dergisi
articles.abstract: Primary cardiac leiomyosarcoma is an extremely rare malignancy often misdiagnosed as benign atrial myxoma. A 55-year-old male presented with syncope from a recurrent left atrial mass, eight months after initial resection for a presumed myxoma at another center. Redo median sternotomy and macroscopic tumor resection confirmed leiomyosarcoma with R1 margins. Despite adjuvant ifosfamide, mesna, doxorubicin chemotherapy, early cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated local recurrence. A third surgical resection was performed, combined with left atrial cryoablation and mitral annuloplasty. At 6-month follow-up, the patient remains alive without recurrence or metastasis. Aggressive repeated resections with local cryoablation may provide viable disease control in recurrent cardiac leiomyosarcoma.

articles.title: CABG in uncontrolled thyrotoxicosis complicated by thyroid storm: A case report.
articles.journal: Turk gogus kalp damar cerrahisi dergisi
articles.abstract: Cardiac surgery in patients with active thyrotoxicosis carries substantially increased perioperative risks. We report a case of urgent coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in a 43-year-old man with severe biochemical thyrotoxicosis and critical left main coronary artery disease who presented with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. Urgent off-pump CABG was performed with intra-aortic balloon pump support. Within 48 hours of surgery, the patient developed a thyroid storm characterized by fever (40 °C), tachycardia (140-180 beats/min), encephalopathy, and jaundice. The condition was successfully treated with anti-thyroid drugs and intravenous hydrocortisone. The patient recovered fully and was euthyroid at follow-up. Early recognition and prompt multidrug treatment of postoperative thyroid storm are life-saving.

articles.title: Philtrum Fasciocutaneous Advancement Flap for Columellar Reconstruction in Revision Rhinoseptoplasty.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the anatomical suitability of the philtrum fasciocutaneous advancement flap (PFCAF) for columellar reconstruction and its clinical applicability in revision rhinoseptoplasty and nasal reconstruction.

METHODS: A descriptive study was conducted, comprising two components: (i) an anatomical analysis of 115 healthy adults to determine the feasibility of the philtrum as a donor site based on craniofacial measurements, and (ii) a clinical study of eight patients who underwent columellar reconstruction using a PFCAF. Sex-based differences were analyzed. To explore a potential dual benefit (reconstruction plus aesthetic improvement), residual philtrum length after hypothetical advancement was estimated, considering 11-13 mm in women and 13-15 mm in men as aesthetically favorable.

RESULTS: Mean philtrum length was greater in men than in women (16.27 ± 3.9 mm vs. 14.84 ± 2.86 mm; p < 0.05). In 91.9% of individuals, philtrum area exceeded the combined area required to reconstruct the columellar and footplate polygons (p < 0.05). Based on anatomical simulations, approximately 25% of subjects would be expected to remain within the predefined aesthetic range after advancement. Clinically, all eight PFCAF procedures were completed in a single stage with no flap necrosis, infection, or dehiscence and with satisfactory restoration of columellar coverage and projection.

CONCLUSION: PFCAF is a versatile and reliable single-stage option for columellar reconstruction in revision rhinoseptoplasty. Anatomical data support broad applicability, and the clinical series demonstrates safety and effective restoration of columellar coverage; careful preoperative assessment is required to optimize functional and aesthetic outcomes.

articles.title: Is cardiac arrest still a binary clinical diagnosis? Toward electro-mechanical-hemodynamic phenotyping in the era of point-of-care ultrasound.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac arrest (CA) remains operationally recognized through clinical signs of absent effective circulation and classified primarily by electrical rhythm. Point-of-care ultrasound (PoCUS) challenges this rhythm-pulse paradigm by directly revealing cardiac mechanical activity and, with Doppler, circulatory flow, exposing physiologically distinct states concealed within current CA categories.

METHODS: This physiology-based conceptual manuscript proposes an integrated electro-mechanical-hemodynamic framework for CA and translates it into PoCUS-consistent phenotyping, portraying CA presentations (CA phenotypes) as pathophysiological states that may transition from one to another along a spontaneous or treatment-modified continuum.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: The framework distinguishes three principal phenotypes: shockable CA (ventricular fibrillation/pulseless ventricular tachycardia); zero-flow CA, encompassing Asystole and PEA without organized ventricular contraction (S-PEA) or with agonal mechanical activity (A-PEA); and severe low-flow CA (C-PEA), in which organized ventricular contraction persists despite absent palpable pulse, and may generate residual circulation. PoCUS can define mechanical states, identify reversible causes, contextualize diagnostic findings, reveal occult shockable activity, and track phenotype transitions. Doppler and invasive arterial-pressure monitoring further characterize spontaneous flow and pressure and may support phenotype-informed treatment.

CONCLUSIONS: Electro-mechanical-hemodynamic phenotyping extends established ALS classification by providing a standardized physiological language for distinct CA states, enabling more homogeneous research populations, phenotype-specific resuscitation research, and rigorous evaluation of PoCUS-informed management. Taken together, these physiological distinctions provide a rationale for reconsidering how cardiac arrest is characterized and how PoCUS-derived information could inform future research, evidence reviews, and resuscitation recommendations.

articles.title: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease with Caroli-like hepatic cystic lesions: A genetically confirmed family case series.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To describe a genetically confirmed family case series of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) presenting with hepatic cystic lesions that mimicked Caroli disease and to highlight the diagnostic value of integrating imaging findings with molecular genetic testing.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A 36-year-old man with multiple hepatic and renal cysts and a positive family history of cystic kidney disease underwent comprehensive clinical evaluation, laboratory testing, abdominal ultrasonography, abdominal magnetic resonance imaging, and whole-exome sequencing. Clinical and genetic findings were assessed in affected family members.

RESULTS: Imaging demonstrated multiple hepatic cystic lesions with features suggestive of Caroli disease, together with bilateral renal cysts. Whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous pathogenic PKD2 variant (c.2407C>T, p.Arg803*; rs778235410) in all affected family members, confirming the diagnosis of ADPKD type 2. The coexistence of polycystic liver disease and Caroli-like biliary abnormalities created a diagnostic challenge. Integration of family history, imaging findings, and genetic testing enabled accurate diagnosis and appropriate clinical management.

CONCLUSION: ADPKD associated with pathogenic PKD2 variants may present with hepatic cystic lesions that resemble Caroli disease. This case series underscores the importance of combining imaging studies with genetic testing in the differential diagnosis of hereditary cystic hepatobiliary disorders and supports the role of molecular diagnostics in guiding clinical management and genetic counseling.

articles.title: TyG index and progression of diabetic kidney disease in type 2 diabetes: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the independent association between the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and diabetic kidney disease (DKD) progression in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective study included a NHANES cohort (2003 - 2020, n = 4,086) and a clinical cohort (n = 535, median follow-up 36 months). Weighted logistic regression, Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, and ROC curves were used.

RESULTS: In the NHANES cohort, each 1-unit increase in the TyG index was associated with a 56.4% higher risk of prevalent DKD (OR = 1.56, 95% CI: 1.06 - 2.31). A linear positive association and a threshold of 8.19 were identified; above this, risk increased significantly (OR = 1.82). The association was significant in males (OR = 1.61) but not females. In the clinical cohort, a high TyG index (≥ 8.19) independently predicted DKD progression (HR = 1.53, 95% CI: 1.01 - 2.30). Kaplan-Meier curves showed significant differences across TyG groups (log-rank p < 0.001). The AUC for predicting progression was 0.71 (95% CI: 0.68 - 0.74). Sex-stratified analysis confirmed significance only in males (HR = 1.85).

CONCLUSION: The TyG index shows a significant overall association with DKD progression, with a threshold effect at 8.19. Sex-stratified analysis revealed that this association was statistically significant only in male patients. These findings suggest that the TyG index may serve as a convenient and cost-effective early risk predictor for DKD, particularly in male diabetic patients. The observed sex heterogeneity warrants further investigation into the potential role of hormonal factors.

articles.title: Field Emission Enhancement in Graphene/Cu Cathodes Through Laser-Shock-Induced Modulation of Geometry and Work Function.
articles.abstract: Cold cathodes enable compact, low-power vacuum microelectronics with rapid activation. Graphene/metal cathodes offer a flexible, conductive platform, but efficient field emission requires local field concentration to coincide with reduced tunneling barriers while avoiding transfer contamination. Laser shock microforming converts graphene/Cu foils into flexible cathodes in one step without transfer while modulating the local work function. High-curvature protrusions and gradients in graphene disorder, strain, Cu microstructure, surface chemistry, and graphene/Cu coupling create spatial variations in the local emission barrier. In individual monolayer graphene/Cu protrusions, these changes produce local work function contrasts reaching 0.12 eV and align lower barriers with highly curved regions. This spatial alignment enhances field emission, yielding a turn-on field of 4.9 V µm-1, an emission current density of 2.2 mA cm-2, stable emission over 32 h, and durability after 3000 bending cycles. This work extends laser shock processing from geometric shaping to coupled structural and electronic barrier control in graphene/metal cold cathodes, providing a route that can be scaled over large areas for flexible vacuum electronics.

articles.title: The emerging oral-heart failure axis: Mechanistic plausibility, bidirectionality, and the limits of causal evidence. A state-of-the-art review.
articles.journal: Advances in clinical and experimental medicine : official organ Wroclaw Medical University
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a systemic, multiorgan syndrome in which inflammation, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, metabolic abnormalities, and frailty contribute to disease progression. Periodontitis may represent an additional extracardiac source of inflammatory and microbial exposure, whereas HF itself may promote deterioration of oral health through frailty, malnutrition, impaired self-care, and reduced access to dental treatment. This state-of-the-art review evaluates the emerging oral-HF axis, focusing on systemic inflammation, oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction, endothelial and coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD), and myocardial fibrosis and remodeling. Epidemiological studies support associations between adverse oral-health indicators and HF, particularly tooth loss and edentulism, but findings for periodontitis are less consistent and remain vulnerable to residual confounding, reverse causation, and heterogeneous exposure definitions. Experimental studies provide biological plausibility for inflammatory, oxidative, endothelial, and fibrotic pathways, yet direct human evidence linking periodontal inflammatory burden to CMD, myocardial remodeling, or HF progression remains limited. Mendelian randomization does not currently support a direct causal effect of periodontitis on HF, and periodontal treatment has not been shown to reduce HF hospitalization or mortality. The oral-HF axis should therefore be regarded as a biologically plausible, bidirectional framework in which periodontitis may act as a disease modifier rather than an established independent cause of HF.

articles.title: Single-port thoracoscopic complex vs simple lung segmentectomy: Comparative outcomes and feasibility.
articles.journal: Advances in clinical and experimental medicine : official organ Wroclaw Medical University
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complex lung segmentectomy, although effective for early-stage lung cancer, is less widely adopted because of its technical complexity.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare perioperative outcomes, quality of life (QoL), and survival between complex and simple lung segmentectomy performed using single-port thoracoscopy to determine its clinical feasibility.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective analysis screened 218 patients; after exclusions, 210 patients underwent complex (n = 100) or simple (n = 110) segmentectomy at Zhanjiang Central Hospital. Propensity score matching resulted in 92 patients per group. Single-port thoracoscopic surgery was performed, and perioperative outcomes, complications, QoL assessed using the 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36), and survival evaluated using Kaplan-Meier curves were analyzed. Statistical analyses were performed using t-tests, χ2 tests, and log-rank tests (p < 0.05).

RESULTS: Complex segmentectomy was associated with longer operative time, greater postoperative drainage, and longer hospital stays (p < 0.001). Cough (60.87% vs 32.61%; p = 0.007) and air leakage (54.35% vs 19.57%; p < 0.001) were more common in the complex group. No significant differences were observed in postoperative lung function, other complications, such as infection or arrhythmia, or QoL at 6 months (p = 0.071). Survival curves showed comparable prognosis (p = 0.860).

CONCLUSIONS: Despite increased perioperative demands, complex lung segmentectomy achieves lung function, QoL, and survival outcomes similar to those of simple segmentectomy, supporting its role in the treatment of early-stage lung cancer. These findings support its broader application in specialized settings and may inform optimized surgical approaches.

articles.title: Caregiving Challenges Across the Treatment and Recovery Trajectory of Patients Undergoing Oesophageal Cancer Surgery: A Longitudinal Qualitative Study Guided by the Timing It Right Framework.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To explore caregiving challenges experienced by family caregivers of patients undergoing oesophageal cancer surgery across different stages of the treatment and recovery trajectory and how these challenges evolve over time.

DESIGN: A longitudinal qualitative study guided by the timing it right framework.

METHODS: Guided by the Timing It Right Framework, this descriptive qualitative study used semi-structured interviews with 17 primary family caregivers of patients undergoing oesophageal cancer surgery. Data were analysed using thematic analysis.

RESULTS: Caregiving challenges varied across stages and evolved dynamically. Five stage-specific patterns were identified: admission and treatment-planning, emotional shock, disclosure challenges, and treatment decision-making difficulties; preoperative, concerns about surgical tolerance, psychological burden, and surgical safety; postoperative, difficulties meeting care needs, limited caregiving knowledge and skills, and physical and psychosocial strain; hospital-to-home transition, difficulties obtaining care knowledge, nutritional management challenges, and difficulties responding to negative emotions and social withdrawal; and longer-term adjustment, increasing time commitment, financial pressure, fear of recurrence, and anticipatory grief.

CONCLUSION: Caregiving challenges change throughout the disease trajectory. Nurses should provide continuous, stage-specific support that addresses caregivers' evolving informational, practical, psychological, and social needs.

IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: Stage-specific assessment, education, and support may help nurses address caregivers' changing needs during cancer treatment and recovery.

IMPACT: This study highlights the stage-specific and dynamic nature of caregiving challenges across the oesophageal cancer treatment and recovery trajectory.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patient or public involvement.

articles.title: Blood cell aggregation as a hemorheological marker of long-term clinical outcome after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with coronary artery disease.
articles.abstract: BackgroundWe evaluated serial blood cell aggregation changes after PCI in CAD patients and their 12-month outcomes.MethodsWe prospectively enrolled 120 elective PCI CAD patients and 50 frequency-matched controls. Blood was collected pre-PCI, on Days 3, 8, and Month 3. Erythrocyte aggregation index (EAI) was assessed by TAS-plus aggregometry. Patients were grouped into Group I (favorable, n = 106) and Group II (repeat PCI, n = 14).ResultsCAD patients showed higher baseline EAI (0.43 ± 0.06vs.0.29 ± 0.04, p < 0.001), fibrinogen (4.1 ± 0.6vs.2.9 ± 0.4 g/L, p < 0.001), and leukocyte aggregation (32.4 ± 5.8%vs.21.4 ± 4.2%, p < 0.001) than controls. Linear mixed-effects modeling revealed a significant group-by-time interaction for EAI (F(3, 354) = 5.12, p = 0.002). Over 3 months, Group I showed progressive EAI normalization (0.42 ± 0.05 to 0.31 ± 0.03, p < 0.001), whereas Group II maintained elevated EAI (0.46 ± 0.07 to 0.44 ± 0.06, p = 0.245). Leukocyte aggregation increased transiently at Day 3 in both CAD groups (39.8 ± 6.7%vs.40.1 ± 6.5%) and returned to baseline by Month 3 (31.8 ± 5.4% vs. 32.1 ± 5.5%, p = 0.842), showing no persistent between-group differences in this cohort. ADP-induced platelet aggregation was significantly suppressed post-PCI at Day 3 (50.2 ± 7.6%vs.50.7 ± 7.4%, p < 0.001) without between-group differences.ConclusionsPersistent erythrocyte hyperaggregation post-PCI is associated with recurrent ischemia and repeat revascularization and may represent a potential biomarker for clinical risk stratification, pending validation in larger, multicenter prospective studies.

articles.title: Feasibility and Preliminary Effects of Oropharyngeal Alignment Exercise on Swallowing Function in Neurological Disorders with Restricted Mouth Opening: A Pilot Study.
articles.abstract: PurposeThis single-arm pilot study evaluated the feasibility and tolerability of an oropharyngeal alignment exercise (OAE) protocol and explored preliminary changes in swallowing and mouth-opening capacity in individuals with neurological disorders presenting with dysphagia and restricted mouth opening.MethodsOf 12 individuals screened, nine participants (seven with stroke, one with Parkinson's disease, one with cerebellar granule cell neuropathy) completed three phases of eight sessions each: baseline, intervention, and follow-up. OAE, targeting head and neck alignment and postural correction, was delivered twice weekly for four weeks alongside routine rehabilitation. Feasibility was assessed by recruitment, retention, adherence, and safety. Outcomes included maximum mouth opening (MMO), the Mann Assessment of Swallowing Ability (MASA), the Gugging Swallowing Screen (GUSS), and the Penetration-Aspiration Scale (PAS) from videofluoroscopy. Changes were examined using participant-specific baseline ±2SD bands and group-level non-parametric tests.ResultsRecruitment was 75.0%, retention and supervised-session attendance were 100%, caregiver-reported home-exercise adherence was complete during intervention, and no adverse events occurred. Most participants showed intervention- and follow-up-phase values exceeding their baseline ±2SD bands. MMO increased by 6-13 mm, exceeding the reported minimal detectable change in most participants. MMO, MASA, and GUSS showed statistically significant phase-related changes (p < 0.05; Kendall's W = 0.70-0.97), as did PAS, with the largest effect for semisolid boluses.ConclusionsOAE was feasible and well tolerated alongside routine rehabilitation. Preliminary phase-related changes were observed, warranting further evaluation in larger controlled trials with diagnostically homogeneous samples to determine the clinical relevance of OAE in neurological dysphagia.

articles.title: Relationships between physical effort, cognitive workload, and musculoskeletal symptom burden in lean manufacturing environments: Evidence from Moroccan industrial organizations.
articles.abstract: BackgroundMusculoskeletal symptoms remain an occupational health concern in manufacturing, where physical and cognitive demands may coexist. In Lean manufacturing environments, evidence regarding their associations with musculoskeletal symptom burden remains limited.ObjectiveThis study examined the relationships between perceived physical effort, cognitive workload, and musculoskeletal symptom burden among employees working in Moroccan industrial organizations implementing Lean manufacturing practices.MethodsA cross-sectional survey was conducted among 150 employees from Moroccan industrial organizations implementing Lean manufacturing practices. Musculoskeletal symptoms were assessed using the Standardized Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire, perceived physical effort using the Borg Category-Ratio Scale (CR10), and cognitive workload using an adapted NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX). Musculoskeletal symptom burden was defined as the number of body regions with reported symptoms during the previous 12 months. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, multivariable Poisson regression adjusted for sex, age group, industry, occupational position, and seniority were performed, along with complementary group comparisons.ResultsPerceived physical effort was independently associated with musculoskeletal symptom burden, whereas no statistically significant independent association was detected for cognitive workload. Musculoskeletal symptom burden differed across occupational positions. Industry-related findings were less consistent across analyses, while no statistically significant association or group differences were observed according to seniority.ConclusionsPerceived physical effort showed a consistent association with musculoskeletal symptom burden in the investigated Lean manufacturing environments, whereas the association with cognitive workload was not statistically significant. The findings support the relevance of considering physical workload and occupational context when evaluating musculoskeletal health and integrating ergonomic considerations into Lean continuous improvement activities.

articles.title: Efficient estimation of average causal effect with mismeasured exposures.
articles.abstract: Exposure mismeasurement is commonly seen in causal inference based on observational data. Recent evidence suggests that 35%-61% of medical studies using diagnostic tools report non-negligible exposure mismeasurement. For example, in the Global Enteric Multicenter Study, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISA)-based rotavirus detection showed substantial discordance with polymerase chain reaction-based TaqMan Array Card (TAC) testing: 20.1% of ELISA-negative cases tested TAC-positive, whereas 19.5% of ELISA-positive cases tested TAC-negative. The existing methods handling exposure measurement error usually require that the mismeasurement distribution is known or can be estimated from a subset of study subjects with validated exposure statuses. This condition, however, is often violated when the mismeasurement mechanism is complex. In this article, we develop a novel method for estimating average causal effect using samples with exposures subject to misclassification and limited validation subsamples with correctly ascertained exposures. Our method does not require making any modeling assumptions about exposure mismeasurement. We establish some large-sample properties for the proposed method, based on which statistical inference can be easily carried out. The superiority of our proposed estimator is illustrated through extensive simulation studies. Our proposed estimator is shown to achieve a 39%-53% reduction in variance over the estimator relying solely on validation data in our simulation situations. In the application to the Global Enteric Multicenter Study, the proposed method reveals a substantial adjustment of pathogen-specific diarrhea associations that were previously distorted by inaccurate diagnoses.

articles.title: An Evidence-Based Framework for Designing Operating Rooms: Integrating Indoor Environmental Quality, Clinical Outcomes, and Energy Performance.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveThis study proposes an evidence-based design (EBD) framework for operating rooms (ORs) that integrates indoor environmental quality (IEQ), clinical outcomes, and energy performance into a unified, digitally enabled approach.BackgroundHospitals are among the most energy-intensive building types, requiring strict environmental control to support infection prevention, patient safety, and clinical performance. However, in practice, IEQ and energy efficiency are often addressed separately, resulting in suboptimal environmental conditions and increased health risks, including healthcare-associated infections (HAIs). ORs are complex environments where aligning environmental, technical, and clinical requirements is critical.MethodsThe methodology is grounded in EBD principles and integrates architectural, engineering, epidemiological, and clinical perspectives within a lifecycle-oriented decision-making framework. It follows the engineering design model proposed by Morris Asimow, structuring the process across the building lifecycle and focusing on the early design phases (Phases 1-3), when decisions have the greatest impact on performance, safety, and long-term operational efficiency.ResultsA smart OR model was developed that integrates a cyber-physical IEQ control system with a multisensor network for real-time monitoring and adaptive regulation. The closed-loop system dynamically adjusts environmental conditions to user needs, enabling simultaneous control of different microclimatic zones. Simulation results indicate that individualized control can improve patient thermoregulation by reducing heat loss while maintaining acceptable conditions for surgical staff and supporting energy efficiency.ConclusionsThe findings indicate that integrating user-centered IEQ control with cyber-physical systems can support adaptive, high-performance ORs that better align patient needs, staff comfort, and energy efficiency, while promoting safer and effective care delivery.

articles.title: Changing Epidemiology and Healthcare-Seeking Patterns of Chronic Wounds Over Two Decades: A Community-Based Comparative Study from India.
articles.journal: The international journal of lower extremity wounds
articles.abstract: BackgroundChronic wounds represent a significant public health challenge because of their prolonged healing time, associated morbidity, impaired quality of life, and substantial healthcare costs. Despite the growing burden of chronic wounds in low- and middle-income countries, longitudinal community-based data evaluating temporal changes in wound epidemiology remain limited in India. This study aimed to compare the prevalence, epidemiological profile, and healthcare-seeking behaviour associated with chronic wounds in two communities of Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh, over a 20-year period.Materials & MethodsA community-based cross-sectional observational study was conducted between June 2022 and December 2023 in the Sunderpur and Kandwa communities of Varanasi district, Uttar Pradesh, India. A total of 10,003 individuals were surveyed using a pretested semi-structured questionnaire and clinical examination. Demographic characteristics, wound aetiology, anatomical distribution, associated comorbidities, and healthcare-seeking behaviour were recorded. Findings were compared with those of a community-based epidemiological study conducted in the same communities in 2003 (n = 6917). Statistical analyses were performed using descriptive and comparative methods, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant.ResultsNineteen individuals were identified with chronic wounds, yielding an overall prevalence of 1.89 per 1000 population. Urban and rural prevalence rates were 1.57 and 2.64 per 1000 population, respectively. This represented a significant decline compared with the prevalence reported in 2003 (15.03 per 1000 population; p < 0.00001). Compared with 2003, the pattern of wound onset shifted from predominantly traumatic (82.7%) to predominantly spontaneous presentations (84.2%). Lower extremity wounds constituted the majority of cases (89.4%). Diabetic foot ulcers and neglected traumatic wounds were the leading aetiologies, each accounting for 36.8% of chronic wounds. Comorbidities were present in 57.9% of patients, with type 2 diabetes mellitus being the most common (47.4%). A marked change in healthcare-seeking behaviour was observed over the study period, with public-sector healthcare utilization increasing from 37.5% to 68.4%, while reliance on home remedies declined from 50.0% to 5.3%.ConclusionsA substantial reduction in the prevalence of chronic wounds was observed in the studied communities over the past two decades. Chronic wounds continue to predominantly affect the lower extremities and remain closely associated with diabetes mellitus and neglected traumatic injuries. The observed shift toward formal healthcare-seeking behaviour may indicate improved healthcare accessibility and greater awareness regarding wound management within the community. Larger multicentric studies are warranted to confirm these findings and further characterize evolving wound epidemiology in India.

articles.title: Distinct Gut Microbial and Metabolic Biomarkers Related to Atrial Fibrillation in Low-Risk Patients.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology

articles.title: A blended approach design to teaching interprofessional conflict and disagreement management for pre-licensure healthcare students from six different professions.
articles.abstract: Interprofessional conflict is a significant barrier to effective teamwork in healthcare. For pre-licensure healthcare students, conflict is a common part of their clinical experiences. They display different conflict management styles depending on their profession or background. However, opportunities to develop conflict-management skills remain limited. We designed a large-scale blended course to teach pre-licensure healthcare students from six professions about interprofessional conflict management in Lausanne, Switzerland. The course combined pre-class modules with face-to-face simulation-based activities. In December 2024, the first edition of the course was delivered to 621 pre-licensure healthcare students, under the guidance of 31 trained facilitators. Post-course satisfaction was assessed through an online questionnaire (n = 316; response rate: 51%). Quantitative data (n = 315) were analyzed using descriptive statistics, and qualitative data were analyzed using thematic analysis. Qualitative data (n = 280) highlighted that respondents appreciated constructive exposure to interprofessional conflict; group dynamics, and collaboration in a safe learning environment; effective communication through reflective practice; and the transfer of learning to real-life practice. Qualitative feedback highlighted areas for improvement (n = 175), such as reducing the cognitive load. This evaluation indicated that a blended approach to interprofessional conflict management training is feasible and well-received. Future research should assess the impact of this course on interprofessional competencies.

articles.title: Association of medication burden and potential drug-drug interactions with acute kidney injury among critically ill patients receiving anticancer therapy at a tertiary care centre.
articles.journal: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners
articles.abstract: BackgroundCritically ill patients with cancer are exposed to many drugs, including anticancer agents, antimicrobials and supportive medications, which increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and potential drug-drug interactions (pDDIs). The contribution of medication burden and pDDIs to acute kidney injury (AKI) in this population is not well characterised.ObjectiveTo assess the association of medication burden and pDDIs with AKI among critically ill patients receiving anticancer therapy.MethodsThis retrospective observational study was conducted in the intensive care units (ICUs) of a tertiary care centre from August 2025 to September 2026. Adults with malignancy who received anticancer therapy within 30 days before or during ICU stay were included. AKI was defined and staged by KDIGO criteria. Medication burden (total drugs and nephrotoxic drugs) and pDDIs (screened using a standard interaction database) were recorded. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of AKI.ResultsOf 210 patients, 86 (41.0%) developed AKI. Patients with AKI had a higher median number of drugs (11 vs 8, p < 0.001) and pDDIs (6 vs 3, p < 0.001). Independent predictors of AKI were ≥10 distinct drugs (aOR 2.62; 95% CI 1.32-5.18), at least one nephrotoxicity-related pDDI (aOR 2.87; 95% CI 1.43-5.76), APACHE II score (aOR 1.09 per point), pre-existing CKD, sepsis, and cisplatin exposure. In-hospital mortality was higher with AKI (39.5% vs 21.8%, p = 0.007).ConclusionHigh medication burden and nephrotoxicity-related pDDIs were independently associated with AKI in critically ill cancer patients. Routine pharmacist-led medication review and renal-focused interaction screening may help reduce preventable kidney injury.

articles.title: Impact of Opioid Exposure on the Coronary Microvasculature in ANOCA: A Coronary Microvascular Disease Registry Analysis.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Angina with non-obstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA) accounts for up to 50% of patients undergoing angiography for chest pain, with many cases due to coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD). Opioids are often prescribed to patients for multiple indications, and their effects on coronary microcirculation are unclear.

AIMS: To investigate the association between opioid exposure and coronary microvascular dysfunction in patients with ANOCA, focusing on differences in CMD prevalence, CFR, IMR, and MRR between opioid users and non-users, and whether opioid exposure independently predicts impaired microvascular vasodilatory function.

METHODS: A total of 367 ANOCA patients from the Coronary Microvascular Disease Registry (NCT05960474) who underwent invasive coronary function testing (August 2021 to March 2025) were analyzed. CMD was defined by coronary flow reserve (CFR) < 2.5 and index of microcirculatory resistance (IMR) ≥ 25; microvascular resistance reserve (MRR) < 3.0 indicated impaired vasodilatory capacity. All indices were measured by bolus thermodilution. Opioid exposure during the 12 months preceding testing was obtained from the electronic health record and Surescripts database. Patients were categorized as opioid users (≥ 1 prescription > 3 days) or non-users, and stratified as short-term (< 90 days) or long-term (≥ 90 days). The primary outcome was the comparison of CMD prevalence and physiologic parameters (CFR, IMR, MRR) between exposure groups. Because groups differed at baseline, unadjusted comparisons were descriptive; the primary interpretation used a multivariable model of log-transformed MRR adjusted for hypertension, hemoglobin, and chronic kidney disease.

RESULTS: Opioid users had more hypertension, chronic kidney disease, and CCS class IV angina, and lower hemoglobin (12.38 ± 1.60 vs. 13.32 ± 1.58 g/dL; all p < 0.05). CMD prevalence was numerically higher among opioid users (19/55; 34.5%) versus non-users (85/312; 27.2%), but not significantly (p = 0.27). Mean CFR was lower in opioid users (2.84 ± 1.65 vs. 3.32 ± 1.80; p = 0.06), suggesting a trend toward impaired coronary flow. In unadjusted analysis, mean MRR was lower in opioid users (3.27 ± 1.78 vs. 4.02 ± 2.32; p = 0.01). Mean of IMR was similar between groups (18.51 ± 10.58 vs. 18.60 ± 12.24; p = 0.96). After adjustment, the MRR difference was no longer significant (β = -0.11 on the log scale, an estimated 10.5% lower MRR; 95% CI -0.30 to 0.08; p = 0.25); hemoglobin was the only independent correlate (p = 0.011).

CONCLUSIONS: In ANOCA, opioid users represented a distinct clinical phenotype with greater comorbidity, lower hemoglobin, and more severe angina. Their lower unadjusted MRR did not persist after adjustment, and CMD prevalence, CFR, and IMR were similar between groups, suggesting that opioid exposure marks a more complex clinical state rather than independently impairing microvascular vasodilatory function. Residual confounding cannot be excluded, and these exploratory findings require confirmation in larger studies.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Coronary Microvascular Disease Registry, clinicaltrials.gov, NCT05960474.

articles.title: CDKN1A Mediates Regulated Cell Death in Osteoblasts and Exacerbates Periapical Bone Destruction in Apical Periodontitis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Apical periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory bone-destructive disease driven by intracanal microbial infection and host immune-inflammatory responses. Periapical bone destruction arises not only from excessive osteoclastic resorption but also from osteoblast dysfunction and dysregulated regulated cell death (RCD). CDKN1A (p21) is a canonical cell-cycle regulator implicated in multiple RCD programs, yet its role in osteoblast injury and apical periodontitis pathogenesis remains undefined.

METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing (ScRNA) was used to profile osteoblast subpopulations and RCD-related gene expression in human periapical lesions. Porphyromonas gingivalis infection models were established in MG63 and MC3T3-E1 osteoblasts, and DIA proteomics and western blot were used to evaluate RCD-related proteins. The effects of CDKN1A, a disease-associated hub gene screened out in DIA proteomics, on RCD-related proteins were further examined by western blot. Lentiviral silencing and AAV-mediated overexpression were performed in vitro and in rat apical periodontitis models. Bone destruction, RCD activation and osteogenic capacity were assessed by micro-CT, histomorphology and multiplex immunofluorescence.

RESULTS: ScRNA data of apical periodontitis showed that osteoblasts in apical lesions exhibited enhanced apoptosis and pyroptosis and reduced ferroptosis. Single-bacteria P. gingivalis infection markedly upregulated CDKN1A, which promoted osteoblast apoptosis and pyroptosis while suppressing necroptosis and ferroptosis. In vivo, CDKN1A expression increased with disease progression and was negatively correlated with the osteogenic marker OPN. CDKN1A overexpression aggravated bone destruction, whereas its knockdown significantly attenuated bone loss and restored osteogenic activity.

CONCLUSION: CDKN1A acts as a critical regulator that mediates RCD of osteoblasts, impairs osteogenesis and exacerbates periapical bone destruction in apical periodontitis. Targeting CDKN1A-mediated RCD represents a promising therapeutic strategy to limit bone destruction and promote repair in apical periodontitis.

articles.title: Factors Associated With Escalation to Additional Treatment After Percutaneous Catheter Drainage of Symptomatic Pelvic and Inguinal Lymphoceles Following Oncologic Surgery.
articles.journal: Journal of medical imaging and radiation oncology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To identify early post-drainage factors associated with escalation to additional treatment for postoperative symptomatic pelvic and inguinal lymphoceles.

METHODS: This single-centre retrospective study included lymphoceles treated with percutaneous drainage between 2014 and 2024 after oncologic surgery. Lesions were classified into drainage-only and additional treatment groups; escalation was decided at the physicians' discretion without a standardized protocol. Only drainage volumes before initiation of additional treatment were analysed. Associations with escalation were assessed using generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs) with patient ID as a random effect.

RESULTS: Of 61 lesions in 45 patients, 40 were managed with drainage alone, whereas 21 underwent additional treatment (sclerotherapy, n = 19; intranodal embolization, n = 2) at a median of 10 days after drainage. Median Day 2 drainage volume was higher in the additional treatment group (320 vs. 50 mL, p = 0.002). In the multivariable GLMM, Day 2 drainage volume was associated with escalation (odds ratio per 100 mL increase, 1.62; 95% confidence interval, 1.14-2.30; p = 0.008), whereas absence of infection was not. This association remained significant in a secondary analysis adjusted for CT-derived lymphocele volume. Persistent high-output drainage or insufficient reduction in drainage volume was the documented reason for additional treatment in 20 of 21 lesions.

CONCLUSION: Higher Day 2 drainage volume, measured before additional treatment, was associated with subsequent escalation. Although this association may partly reflect physician decision-making, Day 2 drainage volume may help identify lesions warranting closer monitoring and earlier reassessment of the treatment strategy.

articles.title: Chameleon-like afterglow carbon dots for spatiotemporal theranostics of periodontitis by visualizing and reversing calcium overload.
articles.abstract: Periodontitis is the leading cause of tooth loss in adults and is characterized by a pathological cycle of persistent bacterial infection, excessive inflammation, intracellular calcium (Ca2+) dyshomeostasis, and mitochondrial dysfunction. Current clinical diagnostic approaches primarily rely on structural assessments, which fail to capture the dynamic progression of local inflammatory activity. Herein, we developed a "chameleon-like" room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) nanoplatform (CDs@B&A) encapsulated within a biocompatible GelMA hydrogel for integrated theranostic management of periodontitis. Composed of carbon dots, the Ca2+ chelator BAPTA, and the natural antimicrobial agent allicin, this platform exhibits dual fluorescence/phosphorescence emission, a high quantum yield (30.67%), and preferential accumulation at mitochondria-associated endoplasmic reticulum membranes (MAMs). Therapeutically, CDs@B&A functions as an intracellular Ca2+ regulator by buffering excessive Ca2+ accumulation and suppressing pathological STIM1-mPTP and MAPK/NF-κB signaling activation. Meanwhile, the incorporation of allicin provides effective antibacterial activity, while the restoration of Ca2+ homeostasis contributes to mitochondrial recovery and reactivation of osteogenic differentiation in periodontal cells. Benefiting from Ca2+-dependent dynamic quenching of RTP afterglow, CDs@B&A enables non-invasive optical monitoring of inflammatory microenvironmental changes in real time. In vivo animal evaluations confirm that this smart platform significantly promotes alveolar bone regeneration while reflecting microenvironmental pathological dynamics, providing a highly promising optical-therapeutic strategy for the clinical management of inflammatory bone disorders.

articles.title: When Stakeholder Consensus Diverges From Patient Preferences: Selecting Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs) for Kidney Replacement Therapy.
articles.journal: Hemodialysis international. International Symposium on Home Hemodialysis
articles.abstract: The selection of patient-reported outcome measures for kidney replacement therapy requires more than achieving an overall numerical majority among stakeholders. This editorial examines methodological issues arising from a modified Delphi study that selected the EQ-5D-5L and IPOS-Renal for implementation in a kidney registry. Although the final combination exceeded the predefined consensus threshold among participants who voted, it did not receive support from most consumers with lived experience, who predominantly preferred combinations including the KDQOL-36. This divergence illustrates how pooled voting can understate stakeholder-specific differences when one stakeholder group numerically predominates. Additional considerations include the treatment of abstentions and missing votes, the use of open voting after anonymous Delphi rounds, changes in panel participation across rounds, and the distinction between selecting outcome domains and selecting measurement instruments. Replication in other settings should therefore include transparent denominator rules, stakeholder-specific consensus reporting, meaningful patient participation, anonymous final voting, and local assessment of linguistic validity, cultural relevance, accessibility, respondent burden, and clinical actionability. Patient-centered measurement requires patients to meaningfully influence what is measured, how it is assessed, and how results inform care.

articles.title: Leveraging Mendelian Randomisation for Causal Inference in Endodontics.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endodontic diseases have been linked to many potential risk factors and systemic conditions. However, observational associations may reflect sources of bias such as confounding and reverse causality. Mendelian randomisation (MR) can strengthen causal inference, although its assumptions require scrutiny.

OBJECTIVES: To provide an overview of MR in endodontic research and synthesise evidence specifically on causal relationships of endodontic diseases.

METHOD: PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science and Scopus were searched to May 2026. The narrative component established MR's conceptual and analytical framework, including core assumptions, MR designs, data sources, instrument selection, estimators, diagnostics, implementation and appraisal of MR evidence. Original MR studies involving endodontic diseases were identified and compared by phenotype, data source, direction, estimates, replication and assumption support.

RESULTS: The narrative part of the review mapped MR from formulation of a causal question and basic principles to credibility assessment, emphasising the distinction between statistical robustness and biological validity when interpreting causal claims. The systematic search identified 10 studies (2023-2025). Rheumatoid arthritis liability showed the most consistent positive association with endodontic outcomes, but effects were biologically non-specific and unreplicated. Other systemic exposures were mainly null, heterogeneous, borderline or unreplicated; evidence that endodontic disease causes systemic outcomes was limited to isolated findings, including a single lacunar-stroke analysis. Core assumption appraisal showed that instrument relevance was generally well supported from a solely statistical perspective, with most studies using genome-wide instrument selection, reporting strength metrics and drawing on large GWAS datasets. Independence was also addressed in many analyses through ancestry matching, linkage disequilibrium control and confounder screening. The principal limitation concerned exclusion restriction: shared biological pathways and broad pulp and periapical phenotypes often weakened biological specificity and plausibility, while absent colocalisation, relaxed or sparse instrument selection and limited replication left horizontal pleiotropy unresolved.

CONCLUSION: MR offers a valuable framework for generating and testing causal hypotheses in endodontics, but current evidence does not definitively establish broad causal effects between endodontic disease and systemic health. Progress depends on biologically justified instrument selection, larger and more diverse GWAS, clinically validated phenotypes, independent replication, colocalisation, advanced MR designs, triangulation with non-genetic evidence and transparent reporting.

articles.title: A scoping review of autoethnographic approaches in medical education research.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Autoethnography has emerged as a qualitative approach that integrates personal experience with cultural and professional analysis. Although its use is increasing in medical education, the scope, purposes, and methodological characteristics of this literature have not been comprehensively mapped.

METHODS: We conducted a scoping review following the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews and Arksey and O'Malley's framework as developed in Joanna Briggs Institute guidance. Five databases (MEDLINE, Embase, Anthropological Index Online, ERIC, and PsycINFO) were searched from inception to 1 January 2026. Eligible studies explicitly employed autoethnographic approaches and involved medical students, physicians, or medical educators. Data were extracted using an AI-assisted workflow and synthesized descriptively.

RESULTS: Fifty-three studies were included. Publications increased markedly after 2020. Most originated from North America and the United Kingdom. Collaborative autoethnography was the most common approach (51%), followed by solo applications and autoethnography embedded in broader studies. Study purposes were grouped into six categories, including exploration of cultural and social contexts, professional identity formation, and curriculum development. Reflective writing was the predominant data source (81%), often combined with interviews, group processes, and observational methods. Ethical considerations commonly addressed institutional approval, consent, and anonymity, whereas relational ethics were less frequently discussed. Collectively, these features suggest autoethnography is being adapted as a practical and pedagogical tool rather than applied as a fully specified research methodology. Based on these findings, we developed a conceptual process model of how lived experience becomes knowledge through autoethnography in medical education.

DISCUSSION: Autoethnography is a rapidly expanding and methodologically diverse approach in medical education research. Beyond illuminating lived experience, it may also function as a pedagogical and transformative practice. These predominantly North American and UK findings should be interpreted accordingly. Greater clarity in methodological reporting and increased attention to relational ethics are needed to support its rigorous and responsible application.[Box: see text].

articles.title: Anti-drug antibody titer may guide neutralizing antibody testing.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate neutralizing antibodies (NAb) against insulin icodec and explore whether an anti-drug antibody (ADA) titer threshold can guide clinically meaningful NAb testing.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: A cell-based insulin icodec NAb assay was developed and applied to follow-up samples collected after 6 weeks of drug wash-out from two treat-to-target trials in insulin-naïve patients with type 2 diabetes. ADA status and titers, NAb status, efficacy, and safety outcomes were evaluated.

RESULTS: Of 355 follow-up samples, 270 (76%) were ADA positive and 35 (9.9%) were NAb positive. Neither ADA nor NAb status was associated with safety or efficacy concerns. The rate of NAb positivity increased with ADA titer. A titer threshold of 200 improved reliability and interpretability and reduced the number of samples requiring NAb testing by 68%. A higher threshold would be required during active treatment because of residual drug interference.

CONCLUSIONS: ADA and NAb were not associated with detrimental efficacy or safety effects. Integrating ADA titers with clinical outcomes is more informative than stand-alone in-vitro NAb testing. When NAb testing is required, an appropriate ADA titer threshold should guide sample selection.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov IDs NCT03751657 and NCT04795531.

articles.title: Identification of key indicators of colorectal cancer risk in patients with diabetes mellitus using machine learning and Mendelian randomization.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Previous studies have indicated that diabetes mellitus may increase the risk of colorectal cancer (CRC), yet the precise associationremains unclear. To identify critical clinical predictors of CRC risk in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) using machinelearning (ML) and to subsequently evaluate their causal relationship with CRC via Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: A retrospective cohort design was adopted, analyzing clinical records from patients with T2DM and CRC and from those with T2DM alone. Significant predictors were determined using univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses. Four MLmodels were developed, with essential indicators defined by the overlap of top-ranked clinical variables and risk factors. Mendelian randomizationanalysis was then applied to assess causality between the key indicators (exposures) and CRC (outcome), supplemented bysensitivity tests and Steiger analysis. Reverse MR analysis was conducted to examine potential reverse causality between CRC (exposure)and the identified indicators (outcomes).

RESULTS: Univariate and multivariate Cox regression revealed that age [p < 0.05, hazard ratio (HR) = 1.041, 95% confidence interval(CI) = 1.022-1.062] and hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c, p < 0.05, HR = 1.176, 95% CI = 1.094-1.264) were significant risk factors. Logistic regressionwas ultimately identified as the most suitable model, from which two key indicators (age and HbA1c) were derived. Mendelianrandomization analysis demonstrated a causal effect of HbA1c on CRC, confirming HbA1c as a risk factor [odds ratio (OR) = 1.14, 95%CI = 1.01-1.28, p = 0.0336]. Sensitivity analyses and Steiger testing supported the robustness and directionality of these findings. Notably,reverse MR analysis indicated no significant causal effect of CRC on HbA1c [p inverse variance weighted = 0.07853).

CONCLUSIONS: Age and HbA1c were identified as pivotal indicators, with HbA1c exhibiting a unidirectional causal association with CRC, thereby offering insights for potential therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Off-Pump versus On-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting in Prefrail and Frail Patients: 30-Day and 1-Year Outcomes From the FRAGILE Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty is associated with worse outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). However, the comparative effectiveness of off-pump CABG (OPCAB) versus on-pump CABG (ONCAB) in prefrail and frail patients remains uncertain.

METHODS: This multicenter, randomized, open-label trial enrolled patients ≥60 years of age classified as prefrail or frail, randomized 1:1, between January 2018 and December 2024. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of death, myocardial infarction, stroke, renal failure, acute respiratory distress syndrome, or reoperation for bleeding. Secondary outcomes included ventilation time, intensive care unit and hospital stay, transfusion requirements, completeness of revascularization, surgical wound infection at 30 days, and neurocognitive function preoperatively and at 1 year. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle; relative risks with 95% CIs were estimated.

RESULTS: A total of 508 patients were included (OPCAB, n=258; ONCAB, n=250; median age, 68 years [interquartile range, 65.0-73]; 30.5% female). The primary composite outcome occurred in 28 patients receiving OPCAB (10.9%) and 40 patients receiving ONCAB (16.0%; relative risk, 1.47 [95% CI, 0.94-2.31]; P=0.09). Surgical wound infection was more frequent with ONCAB (20 [8.0%] versus 9 [3.5%]; P=0.04). No significant differences were observed in neurocognitive or quality of life outcomes at 1 year. Estimated 1-year survival probabilities were 96.1% and 92.8% in the OPCAB and ONCAB groups, respectively (P=0.099).

CONCLUSION: In prefrail and frail patients undergoing CABG, OPCAB and ONCAB resulted in similar rates of the primary composite outcome. No significant differences between OPCAB and ONCAB were found in neurocognitive outcomes.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02338947.

articles.title: Generation of Human Cardiomyocytes With Adult-Like Metabolism by a Chemically Defined Medium for Mitochondrial Disease Modeling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC cardiomyocytes) as a model for cardiac disease have become increasingly important, bolstered by the Food and Drug Administration's initiative to promote novel alternative methods for biomedical research. A key limitation of metabolically immature iPSC cardiomyocytes is their limited ability to accurately recapitulate mitochondria-dependent pathologies, such as Friedreich ataxia-associated cardiomyopathy. Adult cardiomyocytes are characterized by a high density of interfibrillar mitochondria, abundant respiratory complexes (I-V) that form supercomplexes, and efficient utilization of fatty acids to drive mitochondrial respiration. These unique metabolic structures and functions are largely missing in iPSC cardiomyocytes. Further, whether iPSC cardiomyocytes can efficiently utilize fatty acids for respiration in the presence of glucose, a unique adult feature, remains unclear.

METHODS: We developed a chemically defined, 11-component maturation medium (MM11) designed using a bioinformatics-guided strategy that identified high-fidelity transcriptional markers of adult cardiac metabolic maturity. Human iPSC cardiomyocytes were treated with MM11 for 2 weeks and evaluated at the molecular, structural, and functional levels, with an emphasis on mitochondrial maturity. We benchmarked our results with isolated primary adult human cardiomyocytes. Last, we tested whether this method could enable us to more accurately model Friedreich ataxia cardiomyopathy.

RESULTS: MM11 treatment increased expression of metabolic pathways, including mitochondrial respiration and fatty acid metabolism, at the transcript and protein levels. Ultrastructural analyses revealed the formation of interfibrillar mitochondria and mitochondrial respiratory supercomplexes, a feature never shown in previous reports. Functionally, MM11-treated iPSC cardiomyocytes exhibited substantially increased oxidative phosphorylation and a metabolic preference for fatty acid utilization in the presence of physiologic substrates, as determined by oxygen consumption assays and 13C isotope tracing.

CONCLUSIONS: MM11 promotes robust metabolic maturation of human iPSC cardiomyocytes, enabling sophisticated mitochondrial architecture and substrate utilization. These metabolically matured cardiomyocytes more faithfully model mitochondria-dependent cardiac pathologies, including ischemia-reperfusion injury and Friedreich ataxia cardiomyopathy, improving the use of iPSC cardiomyocytes for mechanistic studies of human heart disease.

articles.title: Concordance Between Subjective and Actigraphy-Measured Sleep and Factors Associated With Discrepancies in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: The relationship between sleep and glucose metabolism underscores the importance of evaluating sleep, especially given the high prevalence of sleep disturbances in individuals with Type 2 diabetes (T2D). Objective sleep measurements like actigraphy may not always align with subjective assessments, such as the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Although discrepancies between objectively measured sleep and subjectively measured sleep have been highlighted in healthy populations and other clinical populations, the relationship has not been well studied in individuals with T2D. We aimed to assess the discrepancies and correlations between actigraphy-measured and self-reported sleep parameters in individuals with T2D, and to identify demographic, psychological, and clinical factors contributing to these discrepancies. Adults (n = 134) with T2D wore actigraphy devices for 14 days and completed study surveys assessing subjective sleep (PSQI), demographics, and psychological and clinical factors. Findings indicated significant discrepancies in total sleep time (TST) and sleep efficiency between the two measurement methods, with self-reported TST being higher. Discrepancy levels varied by sex, depressive symptoms, and perceived stress. After adjusting for covariates, sex and depressive symptoms remained significant factors of greater discrepancies in TST and sleep efficiency. Age, marital status, housing stability, and sleep quality were also associated with discrepancies in sleep efficiency. Employment status and housing stability were factors associated with discrepancies in sleep midpoint. Discrepancies between subjective and objective sleep assessments suggest that integrating both methods could provide a more comprehensive understanding of sleep health. The findings also emphasize the need to consider individual psychological and demographic factors when interpreting sleep measurements.

articles.title: Identification of a unique Env protein mutation associated with ALV-J-induced hemangioma.
articles.journal: Avian pathology : journal of the W.V.P.A
articles.abstract: AbstractALV-J is a retrovirus which can induce diverse tumors in chickens. In this study, ALV-J was identified as the causative agent of both hemangioma and lymphocyte-like tumors in Chinese indigenous layer hens. Microscopic analysis revealed significant vascular endothelial cell hyperplasia across multiple tissues. Viral isolation and sequencing identified unique insertion mutations in the env gene and the 3'UTR. The env insertion was found it enhances viral replication in vascular endothelial cells. Furthermore, infection with the mutant virus led to significant upregulation of vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A) and vascular endothelial growth receptor subtype 2 (VEGFR-2) expression. Collectively, these findings provide important insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying the enhanced pathogenicity of ALV-J.

articles.title: Betel-Quid Exposure and Site-Specific Prognostic Patterns in Oral Cavity Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Betel-quid chewing is a risk factor for oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC), but its associations with tumour subsite and depth-of-invasion (DOI) related prognosis remain unclear. We examined site-specific associations and exposure-stratified DOI thresholds for disease-specific survival (DSS).

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 454 patients from southern Thailand. Tumour-subsite associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression. Exploratory DSS thresholds were derived among surgically treated patients using maximally selected log-rank statistics and evaluated with an exposure-stratified Cox model.

RESULTS: Of 454 patients, 154 (33.9%) were betel chewers. Exposure was associated with tumours of the buccal mucosa (adjusted odds ratio, 5.43), lip (3.96), retromolar trigone (3.28) and gingiva (3.13), relative to oral tongue tumours. Exploratory DOI thresholds were 7 mm in chewers (log-rank p = 0.006) and 15 mm in non-chewers (p < 0.001). After adjustment, DOI > 7 mm remained associated with poorer DSS in chewers (hazard ratio, 3.55; 95% confidence interval, 1.32-9.52; p = 0.012), whereas the association for DOI > 15 mm in non-chewers was attenuated (hazard ratio, 1.56; 95% confidence interval, 0.97-2.53; p = 0.069).

CONCLUSIONS: Betel-quid exposure was associated with OCSCC at quid-contact subsites. Chewers showed a lower exploratory DOI threshold for DSS than non-chewers.

articles.title: PlantPAN 5.0: updated database for integrating multiomics evidence and exploring multilayered transcriptional regulatory networks in plants.
articles.abstract: Plant Promoter Analysis Navigator (PlantPAN) 5.0 (https://plantpan.itps.ncku.edu.tw/) is an integrated multiomics resource for investigating plant cis-regulatory elements and transcriptional regulatory networks. This release expands genome annotations and promoter sequences to 240 species and provides 71 040 transcription factor (TF) annotations and 7762 nonredundant binding matrices. Its companion database, PCBase 3.0, substantially expands ChIP-seq data and newly incorporates ATAC-seq, bisulfite-sequencing, and four Hi-C-based chromatin interaction datasets for Arabidopsis thaliana. The new Differential Analysis function enables comparison of TF binding, chromatin accessibility, and DNA methylation across conditions. The redesigned Promoter Analysis interface provides TF family-level statistics, with a Pattern Overview panel integrating TF-binding site (TFBS) densities, plant DNA large language model-predicted open-chromatin regions, CpG-rich regions, and tandem repeats. Two new modules are introduced: (i) Transcriptome Regulatory Analysis and Coexpression, where candidate regulatory TFs and shared cis-elements in gene sets are prioritized through differential expression and coexpression analysis, and (ii) Interaction Topology Analysis for Chromatin and TFs, where chromatin interaction regions are integrated to reveal potentially coregulated genes and their shared TFs and predicted TFBSs. A Dockerized package enables large-scale local promoter analyses, with data privacy. Therefore, PlantPAN 5.0 is a comprehensive framework for discovering plant transcriptional regulatory mechanisms.

articles.title: Comment on: "Oral Leukoplakia Microbiome Predicts the Degree of Dysplasia and Is Shaped by Smoking and Tooth Loss".
Early oral anti-inflammatory diet for nutritional management in patients with mild acute pancreatitis: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Acute pancreatitis is a hypermetabolic inflammatory disease prone to negative nitrogen balance, making nutritional management critical. Early oral feeding in mild cases can reduce dysbiosis, inflammation, and nutritional risks, but specific guidance is lacking. Anti-inflammatory diets reduce inflammation and modulate gut microbiota, yet have not been applied in mild acute pancreatitis. Therefore, this study aims to develop an early oral anti-inflammatory diet protocol for mild cases and evaluate its safety and efficacy. A randomized controlled trial was conducted. Patients with acute pancreatitis hospitalized in the Department of Gastroenterology of a tertiary hospital in Mianyang, Sichuan Province from December 2024 to December 2025 were enrolled and randomly assigned to an intervention group or a control group (n = 34 each). The control group received conventional dietary management, while the intervention group received an anti-inflammatory diet protocol. Generalized estimating equation models and repeated-measures ANOVA were used to assess safety and efficacy. Safety: No significant differences were observed between groups in the incidence of abdominal pain or bloating; however, the intervention group had a significantly lower incidence of loose stools (P = 0.007). Serum lipase, amylase, and triglycerides showed no significant between-group differences (P = 0.793, 0.665, and 0.314, respectively). Efficacy: The intervention group had lower 2-hour postprandial glucose (P = 0.045). High-sensitivity C-reactive protein was significantly lower in the intervention group (P = 0.013). The intervention group showed smaller decreases in albumin, body weight, and prealbumin (all P < 0.05), as well as smaller changes in muscle mass and fat mass. Mean hospital stay was significantly shorter in the intervention group (P = 0.016), and the 30-day readmission rate was significantly lower (P = 0.039). Significant differences in microbial species were found between the two groups, with enrichment of beneficial bacteria such as Veillonella and Bifidobacterium in the intervention group, and enrichment of Corynebacteriaceae in the control group. The early oral anti-inflammatory diet protocol is safe and effective for patients with mild acute pancreatitis and can serve as a reference for clinical nutritional management. It effectively reduces inflammation, improves nutritional reserves, and helps maintain gut microbiota stability. Furthermore, it lowers the 30-day readmission rate, shortens hospital stay, and reduces the economic burden on patients. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2400094056 (https://www.chictr.org.cn/index.html).
