articles.title: Retraction of: Dapagliflozin preserves kidney function and reduces albuminuria in children with chronic kidney disease.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association

articles.title: Stage-Adaptive Bilayer Hydrogel Coordinates Photodynamic Antibacterial Therapy with Engineered Extracellular Vesicle-Mediated Immunomodulation in Infected Diabetic Wounds.
articles.abstract: During the early phase of treatment, infected diabetic wounds require rapid bacterial control, whereas subsequent healing benefits from relief of persistent oxidative stress and inflammation, resulting in distinct and partly opposing redox demands over time. We therefore developed a stage-adaptive bilayer hydrogel that separates photodynamic antibacterial therapy from engineered small extracellular vesicle (sEV) delivery. The wound-contacting layer contains chlorin e6 (Ce6), while the ROS-responsive upper layer scavenges ROS and retains miR-146a-enriched sEVs carrying a human CD64-recognition module. The bilayer architecture limited premature release of sEV-associated particles during photodynamic treatment but allowed substantial release thereafter, with key vesicle-associated features preserved after irradiation. In human macrophages, engineered sEVs increased intracellular miR-146a, reduced IRAK1 abundance and NF-κB p65 phosphorylation, decreased CD86, and increased CD206. These effects were partly weakened by CD64 blockade. In infected diabetic wounds, Bil-Gel@miR-sEVs reduced bacterial burden and oxidative stress, suppressed IRAK1/NF-κB-associated inflammatory signaling, shifted macrophage-associated markers toward a repair-associated pattern, and improved epithelial, vascular, and matrix reconstruction. This bilayer design therefore links early infection control with later immunoregulation and tissue repair within one biomaterial.

articles.title: Autism Diagnoses Before and After Pregnancy: A Retrospective Population-Based Cohort Study in Ontario, Canada.
articles.journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
articles.abstract: Few studies have examined the reproductive health of autistic girls and women. We undertook a descriptive retrospective population-based cohort study in Ontario, Canada, 2004 to 2023. Among first pregnancies, we (a) estimated the proportion occurring in autistic individuals, (b) examined the distribution of autism diagnoses before, during and after pregnancy and (c) described the preconception characteristics of childbearing autistic individuals based on timing of diagnosis. Autism was identified using a validated algorithm before, during and after pregnancy, the latter until 2024. Preconception socio-demographic and clinical characteristics were compared in each autism diagnosis timing group with nonautistic individuals using descriptive statistics. There were 1,148,470 first pregnancies, of which 1,086 (0.09%) were to autistic individuals. Among autistic individuals, 64.3% had their first diagnosis recorded before conception, 3.3% during pregnancy and 32.4% after delivery. Compared with nonautistic individuals, autistic individuals, regardless of the timing of diagnosis, were younger and more likely to live in low-income neighbourhoods, be long-term Canadian residents and experience co-occurring conditions, violence and high health care use preconception, with the highest rates of these factors among those with pre-pregnancy autism diagnoses. Findings show the importance of addressing preconception health needs of autistic individuals, including those awaiting a diagnosis, and autism training for health care providers.Lay AbstractMost autism research is focused on boys and men. We know less about autistic girls and women, including how many experience pregnancy and what their pregnancy-related needs are. We looked at how many first pregnancies occurred among autistic people, and how many people are diagnosed as autistic before, during and after pregnancy. We also looked at the demographic, social and health characteristics of autistic people before pregnancy, based on when they got their autism diagnosis. To do this, we studied all first pregnancies that happened in Ontario, Canada between 2004 and 2023. We identified autism diagnoses in health care records before, during and after individuals' pregnancies, up until 2024. We then described autistic and nonautistic people according to their age, neighbourhood-level income, rurality, immigration status, co-occurring conditions (like diabetes and depression), violence and health care access before their pregnancy. We found 1,148,470 first pregnancies in Ontario from 2004 to 2023; of these pregnancies, 1,086 (0.09%) were to autistic people. Among autistic people, 698 (64.3%) got their autism diagnosis before pregnancy, 36 (3.3%) during pregnancy and 352 (32.4%) after delivery. Compared with nonautistic people, autistic people were younger, more likely to live in low-income neighbourhoods and more likely to have lived in Canada long-term. They also had more co-occurring conditions; were more likely to experience violence; and used more health care services, including hospital services, before pregnancy. People who were diagnosed as autistic before pregnancy had even more co-occurring conditions, violence and health care use than people who were diagnosed as autistic after pregnancy. Our study shows that it is important to support the pre-pregnancy health of autistic people, including those who are waiting for a diagnosis. Our study also shows that health care providers need training to understand the needs of autistic girls and women.

articles.title: Good Boy: The GB Virus and the Symbiotic Possibilities of Infectious Disease Research.
articles.abstract: The history of the GB virus, nicknamed 'good boy' for the reported benefits it provides to human health, generates new insights into the political and economic conditions that lead to symbiotic relations with viruses. First identified in the context of hepatitis research in the mid-1990s, involving the molecular analysis of blood samples collected during viral surveillance in West Africa and 1960s hepatitis research in Chicago, GB virus infection was associated with slower rates of disease progression among people living with HIV. Contextualizing the GB virus alongside broader developments in 1990s bloodborne virus research, including advances in molecular biology, biotech interest in diagnostics, and biosecurity, this article foregrounds how one virus came to be considered symbiotic under specific conditions. By the early 2000s, biomedical researchers speculated that the GB virus might be useful as a kind of 'biovaccination', particularly in parts of Africa where access to effective HIV prevention and therapy was limited and which were considered a 'hotspot' for zoonotic viruses. As a viral stowaway with unexpected benefits for its hosts, the history of the GB virus represents a symbiotic perspective on the political and economic arrangements that usually define viruses as pathogens in infectious disease research.

articles.title: Toxicity and effectiveness of low-dose and conventional-dose co-trimoxazole for treatment of Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia in Christchurch, New Zealand: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP) is an opportunistic infection which primarily affects immunocompromised individuals. The recommended dose of co-trimoxazole for treatment of PJP is 15-20 mg/kg/day of the trimethoprim component based on an underpowered 1975 study in 20 children with cancer. While this dose is effective, a lower dose may be sufficient and cause less toxicity.

METHOD: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients treated for 'proven' or 'probable' PJP at Christchurch Public Hospital, New Zealand between January 2018 and November 2023. We compared treatment limiting adverse drug reactions (ADR) and 30-day all-cause mortality in patients initiated on a conventional dose of co-trimoxazole (≥12.5 mg/kg/day) versus those initiated on a low dose of co-trimoxazole (<12.5 mg/kg/day).

RESULTS: A total of 148 patients with a positive Pneumocystis jirovecii PCR or immunofluorescence result were treated with co-trimoxazole of whom 139 were categorised as having 'proven' or 'probable' PJP (36 low-dose (25.9%), 103 conventional-dose (74.1%)). A higher proportion of patients receiving conventional-dose co-trimoxazole required a treatment alteration due to an ADR (43.7%, 45/103) than patients receiving low-dose co-trimoxazole (16.7%, 6/36). There was no statistically significant difference in 30-day all-cause mortality between the low- and conventional-dose groups (adjusted hazard ratio for low- versus conventional-dose = 0.76, 95% confidence interval 0.29-1.98, p = 0.57).

CONCLUSIONS: In this comparatively large retrospective cohort, low-dose co-trimoxazole was associated with fewer treatment-limiting ADRs without an observed increase in mortality. These findings add to the growing body of observational evidence supporting the use of lower co-trimoxazole doses for the treatment of PJP.

articles.title: Early Chidamide Maintenance After Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation in High-Risk Myeloid Malignancies: A Prospective Cohort With Time-Dependent External-Control Analysis.
articles.abstract: Chidamide is an oral histone deacetylase inhibitor whose use as early maintenance after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) remains insufficiently defined. This prospective single-center Phase 1/2 cohort included all 47 patients enrolled and treated by March 31, 2026. The Phase 2 primary endpoint was 2-year leukemia-free survival (LFS). An exploratory observational comparison used 23 platform-compatible historical comparators, time-dependent maintenance exposure, and propensity-score overlap weighting. Both cohorts received chidamide-containing conditioning. No formal multiplicity adjustment was applied. Treated-cohort 2-year LFS was 78.6% (95% confidence interval [CI], 63.9%-87.9%). In the main weighted model, maintenance exposure was associated with lower hazards of death (hazard ratio [HR], 0.29; 95% CI, 0.09-0.96) and relapse or death (HR, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.09-0.63). LFS associations were more consistent across sensitivity analyses; overall survival was less stable in landmark analyses. Graft-versus-host disease-free/relapse-free survival remained inconclusive. Maintenance began a median of 16 days after HSCT; 45 of 47 patients reached 20 mg twice weekly, and 35 completed 365 days. Grade 3-4 treatment-emergent adverse events were documented in 37 patients, predominantly cytopenias. One patient died during maintenance from infection with transplant-associated thrombotic microangiopathy; the relationship to chidamide was not determined. Relapse, non-relapse mortality, and lymphocyte subset recovery were descriptive. Maintenance was deliverable with active dose management. Trail Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05682755.

articles.title: Angio-invasive mucormycosis mimicking an aortic dissection in a patient with chronic febrile aplasia.
The Cost of Control in Cardiometabolic Prevention: Insights from Sleep and Circadian Disruption.
Phenotyping of Exercise Response in FORMs of Arrhythmogenic CardioMyopathy: PERFORM-ACM.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.abstract: Patients with arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM) are advised to perform no more than moderate-intensity exercise, but whether such exercise acutely alters hemodynamic, electrophysiological, or cardiac biomarker profiles is unknown. We investigated whether moderate-intensity isometric, resistance, or aerobic exercise induces exercise pulmonary hypertension (exPH, mean pulmonary artery pressure to cardiac output slope >3 mmHg/L/min), troponin T elevation, or changes in late potentials (LP) in definitive or probable ACM. Twenty patients (13 definitive, 7 probable ACM; age 42.2 ± 10.7 years) underwent exercise right heart catheterization during isometric handgrip (HG) and bicep curl (BC) (1 minute each at 70% of maximal voluntary contraction), followed by 2 × 20 minutes of supine cycling (CYC) at the first ventilatory threshold. Central hemodynamics and cardiac biomarkers were measured during each condition, and high-density right ventricular electroanatomical mapping was performed before and after exercise. exPH did not occur in either group (all <3 mmHg/L/min), whereas troponin T rose progressively without group differences (p=0.880). LP within the "arrhythmogenic triangle" decreased in probable (mean change -1.95 ± 1.59%) but increased in definitive ACM (mean change 2.72 ± 2.16%, p<0.001). In conclusion, moderate-intensity HG, BC, and CYC exercise were not associated with exPH in probable or definitive ACM. Despite similar hemodynamic and biomarker responses, post-exercise LP diverged between groups, decreasing in probable but increasing in definitive ACM. This observation warrants validation in larger cohorts with better control for baseline substrate and longitudinal clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Estradiol via GPER Maintains Protection Against Arterial Stiffening During Midlife Hypertension in a Mouse Model of Menopause.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.abstract: Endogenous estradiol is associated with cardiovascular protection, but whether menopausal hormone therapy provides protection in aging women with underlying cardiometabolic disease is still not known. Our previous work has shown that the membrane-bound G protein-coupled estrogen receptor (GPER) plays a crucial role in estradiol's protective vascular effects by promoting vasodilation, attenuating oxidative stress, and reducing arterial stiffness. In the current study, we designed a midlife mouse model of menopause with induced hypertension to more closely mimic the conditions of postmenopausal women in randomized clinical trials. We hypothesized that estradiol's vascular protection would be reduced in the presence of cardiovascular disease, especially when the disease was established before menopause, and that vascular GPER plays a role in the response. Middle-aged female C57Bl/6J mice, wildtype and global GPER knockout mice, and smooth muscle-specific GPER knockout mice were ovariectomized at 46 weeks of age and infused with Ang II to induce hypertension in combination with either estradiol or vehicle treatment. Estradiol did not significantly impact blood pressure but reduced arterial stiffness independent of the timing of hypertension. Either global or smooth muscle cell GPER deletion abrogated estradiol's protection from arterial stiffening. These studies are important for determining whether cardiovascular status should be a factor when considering menopausal hormone therapy and underscores GPER as an important mediator of estradiol's protective vascular effects, particularly with regards to arterial stiffness.

articles.title: Volcanic ash in the airways: compositional controls on inflammation, immune modulation, and infection risk.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: More than one billion people live within 100 km of an active volcano, yet the respiratory hazard of ash resists generalization. Bulk composition modulates eruption parameters, therefore respirability, and determines the availability of crystalline silica and labile metals in basaltic ash.

AREAS COVERED: We review the health-pertinent properties of volcanic ash, consistently reported symptoms of acute exposure, and the thin, confounded evidence for chronic disease, where co-exposure to volcanic gases and aerosols impairs attribution. We develop an underexplored possibility: volcanic environments increase the risk of environmentally acquired lung infection via ash fomites carrying viable bacteria, innate defense impairment, including iron-dependent nutritional immunity, and selection for pathogen metal-resistance systems in metal-rich volcanic environments. Nontuberculous mycobacterial lung disease in Hawai'i and an exploratory country-level comparison of epidemiology metrics with volcanism test whether the disease axis is visible in existing data.

EXPERT OPINION: Volcanic ash hazards are eruption-specific and crystalline silica and labile metals are joined by a scarcely tested third. That is, environmentally acquired bacterial lung infections are higher in 'volcanic' countries and account for a greater share of respiratory infections; both outcomes are ecological and hypothesis-generating. The infectious disease pathway and health effects of chronic exposure remain the least constrained assessment element.

articles.title: Coupled Molecular Crowding and Spatial Confinement Enable Reversible Sensing of Dissolved Chlorine Dioxide.
articles.abstract: Reversible fluorescence sensing of chlorine dioxide (ClO2) is challenging because its strong oxidizing character commonly drives irreversible probe conversion. Here, we show that a porous polymer microenvironment can activate reversible ClO2 sensing in a luminogen that is essentially unresponsive in homogeneous solution. A tripodal o-carborane luminogen, Ph-3Na, was designed to combine molecular crowding with efficient charge-transfer and aggregation-induced emission, affording a 577-fold aggregation-induced fluorescence enhancement and an aggregate-state quantum yield of 47.6%. Immobilization of Ph-3Na within cross-linked porous polystyrene generated a bright sensing material that undergoes pronounced fluorescence attenuation upon exposure to dissolved ClO2 without detectable bulk analyte consumption. Time-resolved fluorescence measurements reveal a shortened excited-state lifetime upon ClO2 exposure, supporting a dynamic-quenching contribution, while calculated frontier-orbital alignment is consistent with a possible photoinduced electron transfer (PET) pathway. The material responds within 45 s over 0.31-20 mg L-1 and retains reversible switching over 150 cycles. Integration into a flow-through device further enables quantitative ClO2 monitoring in environmental and food-disinfection samples. These results establish spatial confinement as a means to promote analyte access and activate reversible PET-based fluorescence sensing beyond conventional molecular probe design.

articles.title: Phase 1b breast cancer prevention clinical trial of 9cUAB30 administered prior to surgical resection.
articles.abstract: We performed a phase Ib clinical trial in participants with breast carcinoma evaluating the effects of the novel rexinoid 9cUAB30 orally for 14-28 days prior to surgical resection. Twenty-seven female volunteers (mean±S.D. age 63±10 years) newly diagnosed with breast cancer awaiting surgery as their initial treatment received 9cUAB30 once daily (240 mg for first 5 participants and 160 mg for the subsequent 22 participants) for 13-25 days. Comparison of breast tissue proliferation (Ki-67) at baseline and end of study revealed no significant change with results similar to participant-matched historical control samples. Secondary analysis of tissue apoptosis (Cleaved Caspase 3) observed an increase from baseline to end of study but when compared to changes exhibited by matched to historical controls, no difference was observed. Exploratory analysis of participant tissue samples by nCounter molecular profiling observed increased cytokine and decreased proliferation marker gene expression. Assessment of circulating dendritic cells demonstrated an increase in type 1 monocytic and a decrease in type 2 plasmacytic cells. 9cUAB30 plasma concentrations day of surgery were 349 ± 204 ng/ml (range 66-873). Most participants had grade 1-2 adverse events with the most common being hypertension, headache and gastrointestinal- and skin-related symptoms. Laboratory analysis observed a small but significant increase in total and LDL serum cholesterol (p<0.001). In this phase Ib clinical trial, 9cUAB30 was well tolerated with mild rexinoid-related side effects, no measurable effect upon breast tissue proliferation but encouraging exploratory effects on gene expression and circulating immune effector cells at relatively high daily rexinoid dosing.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/computed tomography in primary tumor localization and its impact on management in patients with metastases of unknown origin: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Metastases of unknown origin (MUO) remain a diagnostic challenge, with identification of the primary tumor closely tied to treatment planning and survival. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) in detecting the primary tumor in MUO patients.

METHOD: This cross-sectional study included 73 patients with MUO who underwent 18F-FDG PET/CT at the Department of Clinical Oncology and Nuclear Medicine, Assiut University Hospitals, between November 2023 and December 2025. PET/CT findings were correlated with histopathological or clinical-radiological follow-up to classify results as true/false positive/negative.

RESULT: Median age was 64 years (37 males, 36 females). PET/CT suggested a primary tumor site in 76.7% (56/73) of patients. PET/CT correctly localized the primary in 50 patients (true positive), was falsely positive in 6, falsely negative in 2, and correctly excluded a detectable primary in 15 (true negative). Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and accuracy were 96.15, 71.4, 89.3, 88.2, and ~89%, respectively. Lung was the most common identified primary (20%), followed by lymphoma and ovarian cancer (10% each). PET/CT altered tumor, node, metastasis staging or diagnosis in 10 patients (13.7%): 3 (4.1%) were upstaged to M1b, 2 (2.7%) were downstaged to M0, and 5 (6.8%) were reclassified as nonmalignant based on PET/CT findings.

CONCLUSION: 18F-FDG PET/CT is a high-yield, single-step imaging tool for evaluating MUO, showing a primary tumor detection rate and diagnostic accuracy favorable relative to previously published series, and significantly influencing clinical management strategies. Given the modest sample size and heterogeneous reference standard, these findings should be regarded as preliminary pending validation in larger, multicenter cohorts.

articles.title: Oliceridine vs Sufentanil Combined With Ondansetron for Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting and QTc Interval in Hysteroscopic Surgery: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Study.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) is common after hysteroscopic surgery, and opioid use can raise concerns regarding cardiac safety. This prospective study aimed to compare the effects of oliceridine plus ondansetron versus sufentanil plus ondansetron on 24-hour PONV incidence and perioperative changes in the corrected QT interval (QTc) in patients undergoing non-intubated hysteroscopy under general anesthesia. MATERIAL AND METHODS In this randomized, double-blind, controlled study, 62 patients undergoing hysteroscopic surgery under general anesthesia were analyzed. Patients received propofol 2 mg/kg with either oliceridine 0.039 mg/kg plus ondansetron 4 mg (O group) or sufentanil 0.1 μg/kg plus ondansetron 4 mg (S group). The primary endpoint was 24-hour PONV. Secondary endpoints included emergence time, post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) pain scores, and change in QTc from baseline (ΔQTc) measured by 5-lead electrocardiography at predefined time points. RESULTS PONV incidence within 24 h did not differ significantly between groups (0% vs 3.2%, P>0.05). Time to anesthesia emergence was comparable between groups (P=0.960). Numerical rating scale scores at PACU discharge were also comparable (P=0.186). Repeated-measures ANOVA showed a significant time effect for ΔQTc (P=0.001), but no significant group effect (P=0.076) or group×time interaction (P=0.171). CONCLUSIONS Oliceridine plus ondansetron did not significantly reduce 24-hour PONV compared with sufentanil plus ondansetron, and this finding should be interpreted cautiously because of limited statistical power. Perioperative ΔQTc changes were minimal and similar between groups, with no clinically significant QTc prolongation.

articles.title: Arterial-to-End-Tidal CO₂ Gradient Direction as a Differential Diagnostic Clue During Sudden Hypercapnia in Thoracoscopic Surgery with Capnothorax: A Report of 2 Cases.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND During minimally invasive thoracic surgery with intrathoracic carbon dioxide (CO₂) insufflation, an abrupt rise in end-tidal CO₂ (EtCO₂) alone cannot distinguish true hypercapnia from artifactual or exogenous CO₂ contamination. We report 2 contrasting cases in which the direction of the arterial-to-end-tidal CO₂ gradient, Δ(PaCO₂-EtCO₂), guided differential diagnosis. CASE REPORT Case 1: A 62-year-old man undergoing robot-assisted right lower lobectomy developed an abrupt EtCO₂ rise from 40 to 130 mm Hg immediately after CO2 insufflation, with severe hypotension and bradycardia. Arterial blood gas (ABG) analysis showed pH 6.79, PaCO2 228.0 mm Hg, and Δ(PaCO₂-EtCO₂) +98.0 mm Hg, suggesting a possible contribution of low cardiac output to the widened gradient. Insufflation was stopped, 2-lung ventilation resumed, and surgery completed without re-insufflation. Case 2: A 77-year-old man undergoing thoracoscopic subtotal esophagectomy developed an EtCO₂ rise from 54 to 99 mm Hg while hemodynamically stable. After excluding circuit and sampling-line artifacts, ABG analysis showed pH 7.21, PaCO₂ 72.5 mm Hg, and Δ(PaCO₂-EtCO₂) -26.5 mm Hg, suggesting exogenous CO₂ contamination of expiratory gas rather than systemic retention alone. Surgical exploration confirmed a partial injury to the left main bronchus. CONCLUSIONS During abrupt EtCO₂ surges under 1-lung ventilation with capnothorax, the direction of Δ(PaCO₂-EtCO₂) on prompt ABG analysis may help prioritize the differential diagnosis between systemic retention and exogenous contamination, provided hemodynamics and circuit integrity are concurrently assessed. A markedly positive gradient during shock may indicate systemic CO₂ loading with reduced pulmonary perfusion, whereas a negative gradient after artifact exclusion suggests pleuro-airway communication or peri-device leakage. This hypothesis-generating approach remains unvalidated as a standalone diagnostic tool.

articles.title: Sacubitril/valsartan for radiation-induced heart disease in children: preclinical and clinical findings.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Radiation-induced heart disease (RIHD) is a life-threatening sequela for cancer survivors. A proactive preventive strategy is urgently needed but remains elusive, particularly for the vulnerable paediatric population where prospective data are scarce. To address this gap, this study aimed to evaluate the prophylactic efficacy of sacubitril/valsartan against RIHD in children through a comprehensive translational research pipeline.

METHODS: A prospective observational study was first conducted in 40 paediatric solid tumour patients, comparing cardiac function before and 1 week after radiotherapy, with 80 healthy controls. A juvenile rat RIHD model was then established, in which the efficacy of sacubitril/valsartan was assessed and validated through longitudinal echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, histopathology, bulk RNA-seq, and single-nucleus RNA-seq. Finally, a prospective clinical cohort (n = 15 sacubitril/valsartan, n = 15 control) was conducted in paediatric patients post-radiotherapy, with a 12-month follow-up for efficacy and safety.

RESULTS: In paediatric patients, radiotherapy significantly impaired biventricular function, notably reducing left ventricular global longitudinal strain, and mean heart radiation dose was significantly correlated with cardiac function impairment. In juvenile rats, sacubitril/valsartan attenuated pathological ventricular wall thickening, myocardial fibrosis, diastolic dysfunction, and perfusion deficits. Mechanistically, it mitigated endothelial cell damage and immune cell activation, promoted a macrophage phenotypic shift from M1 to M2, suppressed fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition, and broadly attenuated pro-fibrotic and inflammatory cell-cell communication. In the clinical cohort, sacubitril/valsartan significantly improved left ventricular global longitudinal strain and aortic compliance vs controls, with a favourable safety profile.

CONCLUSIONS: This first-in-kind translational study demonstrates that early prophylaxis with sacubitril/valsartan is a feasible and effective strategy to mitigate radiation-induced cardiotoxicity in children. These findings, underpinned by multi-modal validation from bench to bedside, challenge the reactive management paradigm in paediatric cardio-oncology and establish a foundational evidence base for a new standard of proactive heart care in childhood cancer survivors.

articles.title: Incremental yield of genetic retesting in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Modern genetic testing in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) includes newly described HCM-associated genes and full intronic regions of certain classic sarcomeric genes. This study evaluated genetic retesting in HCM patients with a prior negative test and identified predictors of a positive result to guide retesting.

METHODS: This multicentre study included patients with HCM who previously had negative next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based genetic testing at four centres. Subjects were retested using an updated NGS-based HCM panel.

RESULTS: Of 508 retested HCM patients (median age 70 years; 66.9% male; median maximal left ventricular wall thickness 18 mm; median interval from initial genetic test 6.6 years), 46 (9%) had 48 HCM-related variants: 14 in new HCM-associated genes, 3 in deep intronic MYBPC3 regions, 18 intermediate-effect variants, and 13 (8 reclassified) in classic HCM-associated genes. In multivariable analysis, the presence of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) [odds ratio (OR) 3.52; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.38-10.25], the Mayo HCM score (OR 1.46 per 1 point increase; 95% CI 1.08-2.01), and the Toronto HCM score (OR 1.18 per 1 point increase; 95% CI 1.08-1.30) were independent predictors of detecting HCM-related variants at retesting. The diagnostic yields in patients with LGE and a high Toronto score (≥13 points), and with LGE and a high Mayo score (≥4 points), were 80% and 50%, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with HCM and prior negative genetic testing, retesting identified HCM-related variants in 9% of individuals, allowing counselling and risk stratification. Late gadolinium enhancement, combined with the Mayo and Toronto scores, may be used to guide which patients should be prioritized for genetic retesting.

articles.title: Urinary Incontinence, Obesity, Quality of Life, and Loneliness in Older Adults: An Observational Study.
articles.journal: Journal of wound, ostomy, and continence nursing : official publication of The Wound, Ostomy and Continence Nurses Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to examine the prevalence of urinary incontinence (UI) in older adults; the association between UI and obesity; and, among participants with UI, the associations between obesity and UI-related quality of life and loneliness.

DESIGN: Cross-sectional, descriptive, correlational observational study.

SUBJECTS AND SETTING: This study was conducted with 301 older adults living in a province in the Northern Black Sea.

METHODS: Self-reported UI was measured by an investigator-developed questionnaire. Urinary incontinence-specific quality of life was measured using the Incontinence Quality of Life Scale, and loneliness was measured using the Loneliness in the Elderly Scale. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, simple logistic regression, and independent samples t-tests.

RESULTS: The prevalence of UI was 47.20% (n = 142), and 34.60% (n = 104) of participants were obese. Participants who were obese had significantly greater odds of having UI than those who were not obese (OR = 2.16, 95% confidence interval: 1.33-3.50, P = .002). Among participants with UI, obesity status was not significantly associated with Incontinence Quality of Life Scale or Loneliness in the Elderly Scale scores.

CONCLUSION: Approximately half of the older adults in this study experienced UI. Obesity increased the likelihood of reporting UI. Among those with UI, there were no significant associations between obesity and UI-related quality of life or loneliness.

articles.title: Congenital Heart Block: Pathophysiology, Diagnosis, and Management.
articles.abstract: Congenital heart block (CHB) is a rare but potentially life-threatening form of conduction disease that manifests in utero or shortly after birth, resulting from disruption of the normal electrical conduction pathway between the atria and ventricles. The severity of CHB varies depending on the degree of atrioventricular conduction impairment, ranging from first-degree atrioventricular block, characterized by prolonged conduction, to complete third-degree block, in which atrial and ventricular activity are entirely dissociated and function independently. The most common etiology is passive transplacental transfer of maternal anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB autoantibodies, most frequently in the setting of maternal systemic lupus erythematosus or Sjögren syndrome, even when the mother is clinically asymptomatic. Less commonly, CHB arises in association with structural congenital heart disease, most notably left atrial isomerism and corrected transposition of the great arteries. The clinical spectrum ranges from an incidental prenatal finding to fetal hydrops and in utero death, with third-degree CHB carrying a perinatal mortality rate of approximately 15-30%. This review integrates current evidence on the pathophysiology, maternal autoimmune contributions, diagnostic approach, and management strategies for CHB, with an emphasis on the emerging roles of fetal surveillance, pharmacologic interventions, and postnatal pacing.

articles.title: Revisiting lipid droplets in plant virus infection: scarcity of data, abundance of questions.
The role of global longitudinal strain change in the assessment of early cardiotoxicity in patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors: a prospective pilot study of 30 patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) improve survival in various malignancies but may cause immune-mediated cardiotoxicity. Because left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) typically declines late, more sensitive markers are needed for early detection of subclinical myocardial injury. This study investigated the association between changes in global longitudinal strain (GLS) and early cardiotoxicity in patients receiving ICIs.

METHODS: In this prospective, single-center pilot study, 30 consecutive adult patients scheduled for ICI therapy were enrolled. Serial transthoracic echocardiography was performed at baseline, 6 to 8 weeks, and 12 weeks to measure LVEF using the biplane Simpson method and GLS using 2D speckle-tracking echocardiography. Cardiotoxicity was defined as a ≥ 10% absolute reduction in LVEF to < 50% and/or new-onset heart failure, suspected myocarditis, clinically significant arrhythmia, or major cardiovascular events. A relative GLS reduction ≥ 15% was considered indicative of subclinical dysfunction.

RESULTS: During a mean 12-week follow-up, cardiotoxicity occurred in six patients (20.0%). In affected patients, GLS significantly deteriorated early (from - 18.2% ± 2.5% to - 14.1% ± 2.8%, P < 0.001), preceding any significant decline in LVEF. Patients without cardiotoxicity showed stable GLS and LVEF values. A ≥ 15% GLS reduction was associated with cardiotoxicity and showed exploratory discriminatory ability, with 83.3% sensitivity and 91.7% specificity (area under the curve, 0.86; 95% confidence interval, 0.72-0.97).

CONCLUSIONS: Early GLS deterioration was associated with cardiotoxicity despite relatively preserved LVEF. Given the temporal overlap between GLS assessment and cardiotoxicity events in several patients, these findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary management of disseminated tuberculosis with tuberculous meningitis and active hepatitis B in a critically ill pregnant woman in the third trimester: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tuberculous meningitis (TBM) in pregnancy is rare but life-threatening, with substantial maternal and fetal risks. Third-trimester disseminated tuberculosis involving the central nervous system with concurrent active hepatitis B infection has scarcely been reported, particularly among remote pastoral populations with limited healthcare access. This report highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges of this triple comorbidity and underscores the value of multidisciplinary team (MDT) management in such complex scenarios.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 24-year-old pastoralist at 30 weeks of gestation presented with headache, vomiting, fever, and nuchal rigidity. Cerebrospinal fluidanalysis confirmed TBM, and chest computed tomography revealed diffuse miliary nodules suggestive of hematogenous disseminated tuberculosis. Serology was positive for hepatitis B surface antigen, e-antigen, and core antibody, indicating active viral replication. Given life-threatening intracranial hypertension [intracranial pressure (ICP) > 330 mmH2O] in late pregnancy, osmotic agents were withheld for fetal safety, and lumbar cisternal drainage was performed. An MDT comprising respiratory medicine, obstetrics, hepatology, pharmacy, and critical care nursing specialties was assembled. Anti-tuberculosis therapy was intensified to isoniazid, rifampicin, linezolid, and moxifloxacin; ethambutol was discontinued due to fetal optic neuritis, and tenofovir was added for hepatitis B management. Following stabilization, the patient was transferred to a higher-level facility at 35 weeks of gestation and underwent cesarean section at 36 weeks, delivering a live preterm female infant (2320 g, 1-min Apgar score of 8). Both mother and neonate were discharged without complications on December 1, 2025.

CONCLUSIONS: This case demonstrates that early recognition, individualized anti-tuberculosis regimens, and coordinated multidisciplinary collaboration are critical for achieving favorable outcomes in pregnant patients with disseminated tuberculosis complicated by TBM and concurrent hepatitis B infection. The successful management relied on integrated critical care and a multidisciplinary approach, which proved effective even in resource-limited pastoral settings.

articles.title: A comprehensive simulation study evaluating the predictive performance of Cox proportional hazards model and machine learning methods for time-to-event data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Many data-driven risk prediction models have been developed for analyzing time-to-event data. However, choosing the most suitable model for accurate predictions in a specific medical application remains a challenge. Simulation enables effective comparison on the basis of equal-sized datasets. This study provided a comprehensive and fair comparison of the overall survival prediction performance of machine learning models and the traditional Cox proportional hazards model, using both simulated and real datasets.

METHODS: Machine learning models included random survival forests, eXtreme Gradient Boosting, and deep neural networks (DeepSurv). We evaluated the performance of the models using the C-index and the Integrated Brier Score. The evaluation was performed under different data-generating mechanisms, such as varying sample sizes, censoring proportions, the addition of noise variables, and in the presence of different types of model misspecification.

RESULTS: All the models showed improved predictive performance with increasing sample sizes. However, their performance declined as the proportion of censoring increased. An increase in noise variables reduced prediction accuracy across all models, regardless of dataset size. Tree-based models demonstrated promising predictive performance compared to the Cox proportional hazards model and DeepSurv in the presence of misspecification and a large number of noise variables. The Cox proportional hazards model performed well with larger sample sizes and fewer noise variables. It also performed well when the model was correctly specified or had only minor misspecification.

CONCLUSIONS: Appropriate model for a specific medical application should be motivated by the research question and the underlying data structure.

articles.title: Regulation and implications of adipocyte lipolysis in musculoskeletal tissues.
articles.abstract: The musculoskeletal (MSK) system contains several unique adipose tissue depots with an emerging role in health and disease. This includes bone marrow adipose tissues (BMAT), intramuscular and epimuscular adipose tissues (IMAT/EMAT), and adipose tissues in joints and around tendons. Adipocytes within these depots are differentially sensitive to lipolytic stimuli which provides clues as to how, and when, local lipolysis participates in MSK health and global metabolism. This review covers known mechanisms regulating lipolysis in each of the MSK adipose depots while emphasizing commonalities and exploring unique features and potential consequences. For each depot, we evaluate its known basal and stimulated lipolytic responses, particularly in response to adrenergic stimuli, caloric restriction, and exercise. We further synthesize findings across fields including endocrinology, cancer biology, food science, and exercise metabolism. Overall, this review emphasizes the broad importance of lipolysis in MSK adipocytes across species and conditions and highlights translational challenges and opportunities. We also highlight ongoing and future work toward understanding how the mechanisms and consequences of lipolysis in adipocytes of the MSK system can contribute to our ability to promote and maintain health throughout the lifespan.

articles.title: Clinical role, biomechanical aspects, and barriers to the use of hip protectors in fracture prevention: insights from an Italian Delphi consensus panel.
articles.abstract: Hip fractures represent a major cause of morbidity, disability and mortality among older adults. Endocrinologists, bone experts and health authorities are called to all possible efforts in order to prevent osteoporosis, sarcopenia and falls, which are all causal factors of hip fractures due to their huge impact on quality of life, short- and long-term prognosis and direct and indirect costs for health systems worldwide. Hip protectors were proposed as a non-pharmacological intervention to reduce the impact forces transmitted to the proximal femur during falls. However, their clinical use remains limited, and uncertainty persists on their indications, efficacy, and implementation in routine practice. The aim of this study was to explore expert consensus on the clinical role, indications and barriers to the use of hip protectors in older adults at risk of falls. A modified Delphi consensus study organized by Glucocorticoid Induced Osteoporosis Skeletal Endocrinology Group (GIOSEG) involved a multidisciplinary panel of Italian experts in the management of osteoporosis, fragility fractures, and fall prevention. The Delphi process consisted of two rounds of anonymous surveys in which participants rated a series of statements using a six-point Likert scale. The questionnaire covered four domains, including relevance of falls into hip fractures, clinical role of hip protectors, barriers to their use, current gaps and future perspectives. Thirty-five experts participated in the first round and thirty-three completed the second round. Consensus was reached on several key aspects of hip fracture prevention. Hip protectors were recognized as a potentially useful adjunctive intervention, particularly in older adults at very high risk of falls and fractures. Patients' adherence and device acceptability were identified as major determinants of effectiveness, while poor patients' acceptance, limited clinician awareness and lack of reimbursement were recognized as major barriers to implementation. This Italian Delphi consensus highlights the potential role of hip protectors as part of a comprehensive strategy for hip fracture prevention in high-risk older adults.

articles.title: Preoperative BMI and Five-Year Proportional Weight-Loss Maintenance After Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) produces substantial weight loss, but long-term proportional maintenance varies. We examined whether preoperative body mass index (BMI) category was associated with change in percentage total weight loss (%TWL) between 12 and 60 months after primary RYGB.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adults with preoperative BMI ≥ 35 kg/m² who underwent primary RYGB between January 2016 and March 2021 and had weight data at 12 and 60 months. Of 456 eligible patients, 113 (24.8%) lacked 12- or 60-month data and were lost to follow-up (343 analyzed). The primary outcome was Δ%TWL12-60 (60-month minus 12-month %TWL), analyzed by linear regression before and after adjustment for age, sex, preoperative type 2 diabetes, and 12-month %TWL.

RESULTS: Among 343 patients, mean Δ%TWL12-60 was - 3.2, - 5.9, and - 5.4% points across ascending BMI categories. Adjusted differences versus BMI 35-<40 kg/m² were - 2.09 points for BMI 40-<45 kg/m² (95% CI, - 4.62 to 0.44) and - 1.57 points for BMI ≥ 45 kg/m² (95% CI, - 4.18 to 1.03; global P=.268). At 60 months, mean %TWL was 28.7%, 28.3%, and 28.9%, whereas mean BMI was 27.2, 30.4, and 33.6 kg/m².

CONCLUSION: Preoperative BMI category was not clearly associated with %TWL change from 12 to 60 months after RYGB, although the confidence intervals included between-category differences of several percentage points. Similar 5-year %TWL coexisted with substantially different attained BMI values; both measures may therefore provide complementary anthropometric information.

articles.title: Metabolic response during neuromuscular electrical stimulation in critically ill patients with deep sedation: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) is a potential strategy to counteract skeletal muscle atrophy in critically ill patients unable to engage in early mobilization. However, it is difficult to confirm whether the exercise load applied by NMES is sufficient to elicit a physiological effect in patients under sedation or with impaired consciousness, as the appropriate stimulus intensity and exercise load of NMES are generally assessed using subjective responses. This study aimed to evaluate changes in energy expenditure during NMES in sedated, mechanically ventilated patients using indirect calorimetry.

METHODS: This single-center observational study included 22 mechanically ventilated patients under deep sedation in the intensive care unit (ICU). Energy expenditure was measured using indirect calorimetry during NMES sessions. The primary outcome was the difference in energy expenditure before and during NMES. Multivariable linear regression analysis was performed to calculate the adjusted mean difference in energy expenditure. A clinically meaningful increase in energy expenditure attributable to NMES was predefined as 150 kcal/day, which was assumed based on an increase in energy expenditure when sitting on the edge of the bed.

RESULTS: In total, 26 NMES sessions involving 22 participants were included in the analysis. The mean energy expenditure was 1,137 ± 170 kcal/day pre-NMES and 1,350 ± 228 kcal/day during NMES. The adjusted increase in energy expenditure during NMES was 213.8 kcal/day (95% confidence interval, 137.1-290.3). This increase reached statistical significance when tested against the predefined threshold of 150 kcal/day (P = 0.02).

CONCLUSIONS: The exercise load provided by NMES could be objectively assessed by measuring increases in energy expenditure. Although a statistically significant increase in energy expenditure was observed during NMES compared to pre-NMES levels, the magnitude of this increase was minimal. Further research is needed to determine whether NMES protocols that enhance energy expenditure are associated with muscle mass preservation, strength maintenance, and the prevention of ICU-acquired weakness.

articles.title: Serum Soluble Programmed Death Ligand-1 (sPD-L1) as a Diagnostic Marker in Neonatal Sepsis: Correspondence-3.
Reducing Hypothermia Among Intramural Vaginally Born Preterm Neonates Admitted in Neonatal Intensive Care Unit at a Tertiary Care Centre Using Quality Improvement Approach: Correspondence.
Multidisciplinary forensic evaluation of fatal non-traumatic rectus sheath hematoma associated with acute pulmonary thromboembolism and salicylate exposure: A case report.
articles.abstract: Rectus sheath hematoma is an uncommon cause of severe hemorrhage and may present a diagnostic challenge in forensic practice, particularly when the hemorrhage extends from the abdominal wall into the pelvic extraperitoneal space. We report the case of a 71-year-old woman who was found dead at home. Postmortem computed tomography demonstrated a hyperdense lesion extending from the lower abdominal wall into the pelvic cavity. Autopsy revealed a massive hematoma extending from the rectus sheath through the extraperitoneal space into the lesser pelvis, without external evidence of trunk trauma. The total hemorrhage volume was estimated to approach 1000 mL. Additional findings included deep vein thrombosis extending from the inferior vena cava to the left common iliac vein and fresh pulmonary thromboemboli in the lobar branches of both lungs. Histopathological examination demonstrated partial organization of the deep vein thrombosis, whereas the pulmonary thromboemboli were relatively fresh, consistent with an acute terminal event. Toxicological analysis detected salicylic acid at a therapeutic level, and an over-the-counter medication containing acetylsalicylic acid was found at the scene. Taken together, the findings were considered most consistent with fatal non-traumatic rectus sheath hematoma, likely triggered by severe cough in the setting of acute pulmonary thromboembolism and possibly exacerbated by impaired hemostasis associated with salicylate exposure. This case highlights the importance of integrating postmortem computed tomography, conventional autopsy, histopathology, and toxicology in the evaluation of extensive truncal hemorrhage and in the differentiation of non-traumatic from traumatic bleeding in forensic casework.

articles.title: The tachyzoite-bradyzoite transition in Toxoplasma gondii: molecular regulation, host adaptation, and therapeutic opportunities.
articles.abstract: Toxoplasma gondii is a globally prevalent zoonotic apicomplexan parasite. Its reversible transition between fast-replicating tachyzoites and dormant, cyst-encased bradyzoites underpins latent infection, disease recurrence and poor therapeutic outcomes. Immunocompetent hosts usually show no symptoms after primary infection, whereas bradyzoite reactivation in immunocompromised people causes fatal cerebral toxoplasmosis; congenital infection and neuropsychiatric complications also greatly increase the disease burden. Conventional drugs only act on tachyzoites and cannot eliminate metabolically inactive bradyzoites shielded by cyst walls. This review outlines the morphological, metabolic and molecular differences between the two stages, and summarizes diverse triggers for stage conversion including environmental stress, host immune pressure and parasite-intrinsic programs. We also elaborate multi-layered regulatory mechanisms, host adaptation and immune evasion strategies. Moreover, we discuss promising therapeutic targets, advanced research models, current limitations and future research priorities. Unravelling stage conversion mechanisms will facilitate the development of curative treatments for chronic toxoplasmosis.

articles.title: Towards normalization of cognitive function and psychiatric morbidity in patients with neurological symptoms post COVID-19: a longitudinal study.
articles.journal: European archives of psychiatry and clinical neuroscience
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Few studies of cognitive impairment in COVID-19 convalescents have assessed patients longitudinally. The aim of this study was to examine the course of performance-based cognitive functions from 6 (T1) to 12 (T2) months after COVID-19 in patients compared with healthy controls, and to investigate the effect of psychiatric diagnosis and fatigue on cognitive function trajectories.

METHODS: Eighty-one patients with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection reporting neurological symptoms were assessed at T1 and 67 patients at T2 with neuropsychological assessment and a semi-structured psychiatric interview. Fatigue was assessed using the Giessener Beschwerdebogen questionnaire (GBB). Sixty-one, confirmed SARS-CoV-2 antibody negative, healthy controls underwent neuropsychological assessment and completed GBB.

RESULTS: At T1, patients performed significantly (p < 0.001 to 0.031) worse across the different cognitive domains, except for verbal fluency, than healthy controls. At T2, there were no significant differences between the two groups in either cognitive domain. Patients improved significantly from T1 to T2 on 7 of 8 domain scores (p < 0.001 to 0.033) and fatigue scores (p = 0.003). The frequency of psychiatric disorders decreased from 40% to 21%. Having a psychiatric diagnosis at T2 and/or delirium during acute COVID-19 significantly predicted a less favourable cognitive function course.

CONCLUSION: These results suggest cognitive function, psychiatric morbidity and fatigue improve one year after COVID-19. Patients with ongoing psychiatric disorder and/or sequela following COVID-19-related delirium may constitute a vulnerable subgroup for non-improvement of cognitive function and should be specifically targeted for rehabilitation and treatment.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was registered the 09th of October 2020 at clinicaltrials.gov (NCT04576351).

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of apixaban versus rivaroxaban in acute venous thromboembolism: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Apixaban and rivaroxaban are used direct oral anticoagulants for acute venous thromboembolism (VTE), but their comparative efficacy and safety remain uncertain. We compared outcomes with apixaban versus rivaroxaban in adults with acute VTE.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception to April 2026 for comparative studies in adults with acute VTE. Random-effects meta-analyses generated risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs); heterogeneity was assessed using I2, and certainty using GRADE.

RESULTS: Thirteen studies involving 233,569 participants were included. Most evidence came from observational studies, with only one randomized clinical trial contributing to the evidence base. Apixaban showed a non-significant reduction in recurrent VTE (10 studies; 203,462 participants; RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.64-1.05). Recurrent DVT was lower with apixaban (2 studies; 37,941 participants; RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.79-0.98), whereas recurrent PE (3 studies; 45,561 participants; RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.09-6.53) and all-cause mortality (6 studies; 149,742 participants; RR 0.99, 95% CI 0.79-1.23) did not differ significantly. Apixaban was associated with lower major bleeding (13 studies; 221,840 participants; RR 0.75, 95% CI 0.57-0.99), CRNMB (5 studies; 29,530 participants; RR 0.63, 95% CI 0.53-0.75), and gastrointestinal bleeding (4 studies; 56,160 participants; RR 0.68, 95% CI 0.62-0.75). Intracranial bleeding was not significantly different (3 studies; 55,470 participants; RR 0.71, 95% CI 0.24-2.13). Certainty ranged from low to very low.

CONCLUSIONS: Apixaban and rivaroxaban showed broadly comparable efficacy, while apixaban may offer a more favorable bleeding profile. Findings should be interpreted cautiously because of heterogeneity, observational evidence, and low-to-very-low certainty.

articles.title: Phenylbutyrate improves recognition memory and increases dendritic spines in the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus in hypertensive female rats.
articles.abstract: Hypertension and aging are two major global health challenges. They frequently coexist, presenting with aging-related neuronal alterations which are exacerbated under hypertensive conditions. In the present study, we utilized female, 12-month-old spontaneously hypertensive (SH) rats as a translational animal model of combined hypertension and aging. Phenylbutyrate (PB), a compound with reported anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective properties was evaluated for its effects on recognition memory and dendritic architecture. PB treatment significantly improved both short- and long-term recognition memory, as assessed by the novel object recognition test. At the structural level, PB increased dendritic spine density in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) and in multiple subregions of the dorsal hippocampus, including CA1, CA3, and the dentate gyrus. Moreover, PB selectively enhanced the proportion of mature spine phenotypes, increasing mushroom and bifurcated spines in the PFC and hippocampal subregions examined. Together, these findings indicate that PB mitigates recognition memory decline and preserves dendritic spine density and morphology in cortico-hippocampal circuits in this animal model. Our results support PB as a potential therapeutic strategy for neurocognitive dysfunction associated with the comorbidity of hypertension and aging.

articles.title: Rheumatoid factor positivity in ANCA-negative eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis: cardiac mimicry, mononeuritis multiplex, and long-term outcome in a case-based systematic review.
articles.abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is a rare small- to medium-vessel vasculitis characterized by asthma, eosinophilia, and multisystem involvement. Diagnosis is challenging in ANCA-negative disease, particularly when misleading serology is present. We describe a 42-year-old woman with long-standing asthma and a rheumatoid factor (RF) of 322 IU/mL, who initially presented with myocardial infarction-like cardiac involvement with non-obstructive coronary arteries. Over the subsequent seven months, progressive eosinophilia, chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis, and mononeuritis multiplex emerged. ANCA-negative EGPA was diagnosed after connective tissue disease, infection, malignancy, and other causes of hypereosinophilia were excluded. She was treated with prednisolone and azathioprine and subsequently remained off immunosuppressive therapy for more than nine years without reported relapse. On later clinical reassessment, she remained stable apart from mild residual neuropathic symptoms. We also conducted a case-based review following the CABARET standards, searching PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science up to 15 August 2026. We identified 38 published cases of ANCA-negative, RF-positive EGPA, 36 of them without pre-existing rheumatoid arthritis. In these 36, the median age was 53 years and 69% were female. Peripheral neuropathy was reported in 72% and cardiac involvement in 47%; with both occurring in 25%; two patients died of cardiac causes. Among 12 cases with sufficient data to standardize RF relative to the assay upper limit of normal, 75% had RF levels > 3 × ULN. Reporting was often incomplete: both MPO- and PR3-ANCA were documented in only 42% of cases and anti-CCP in 11%. No included published case reported prolonged treatment-free remission, although follow-up and treatment status were incompletely reported in several cases. Based on these gaps, the authors propose a reporting checklist for future EGPA case reports. RF positivity, even at high titer, should not dissuade clinicians from considering EGPA when asthma, eosinophilia, ENT disease, neuropathy, or other compatible manifestations are present.

articles.title: The dual role of protein glycosylation in HBV infection: facilitating viral pathogenesis and shaping host defense.
articles.abstract: Hepatitis B is the most prevalent chronic viral infection worldwide, posing a serious threat to global public health. Protein glycosylation, a critical post-translational modification, regulates diverse physiological processes. Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is associated with altered glycosylation of both viral and host proteins, which influences viral entry, immune evasion and disease progression, while HBV infection remodels host glycosylation. Given the sensitivity of glycosylation patterns to pathological perturbations, it is particularly relevant to examine how HBV exploits host glycosylation machinery to facilitate viral persistence and pathogenesis. This review is organised around a dual-role framework: one arm covers the proviral functions of glycosylation (viral entry, envelope protein folding, processing, assembly and secretion, persistence, immune escape and disease progression), the other the host-protective functions of the same pathways (glycosylation-dependent restriction factors, glycan-dependent ER quality control and ERAD, cellular stress responses and immune regulation). This exploration provides insights into the glycan-dependent mechanisms underlying HBV infection and their implications for developing novel diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Fatal polysubstance intoxications involving inhalation of nitazene analogues: identification of fluetonitazepyne and 5-methyl etodesnitazene.
articles.abstract: The illicit opioid market has undergone notable diversification, with 2-benzylbenzimidazoles (nitazenes) representing an increasingly prevalent class of non-fentanyl synthetic opioids. These compounds challenge forensic toxicology through marked µ-opioid receptor potency and rapid structural evolution, often undetected by routine immunoassay screening. We report two fatal polysubstance intoxications involving inhalation of nitazene analogues via vaping devices, identified in biological matrices. GC-MS-based identification was corroborated by untargeted LC-HRMS screening with in silico data mining and confirmed against certified reference standards.Case 1 involved a 40-year-old male found deceased after an estimated 2-3 days without contact. Fluetonitazepyne was quantified at 0.58 ng/mL in peripheral blood alongside ethanol (0.55 g/kg), supra-therapeutic citalopram (340 ng/mL), sub-therapeutic lithium, and cannabinoid metabolites, concordant with a recovered vaping vial containing the same nitazene. Death could not be established with certainty; based on toxicological findings, it was most likely acute fluetonitazepyne intoxication in the presence of central nervous system (CNS) depressants. Case 2 concerned a 22-year-old male with a witnessed cardiorespiratory arrest following inhalation from a vaping device confirmed to contain 5-methyl etodesnitazene. Despite bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), naloxone administration (1.6 mg), and intensive care, he died from acute anoxic encephalopathy approximately 24 h later. Ante mortem peripheral blood confirmed 5-methyl etodesnitazene at 3.3 ng/mL alongside barbital at toxic concentrations (39 mg/L).Concurrent CNS depressant exposure potentiated fatal respiratory depression, more clearly established in Case 2. These cases document the lethal potential of emerging nitazene analogues and the value of untargeted HRMS-based screening in the absence of certified reference standards.

articles.title: Association of coronary artery calcium with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after catheter ablation according to atrial fibrillation type.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) reflects systemic atherosclerosis and inflammation and may contribute to atrial remodeling. Although CAC has been associated with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF), whether this association differs according to AF type remains unclear.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively analyzed 202 consecutive patients who underwent first-time catheter ablation for AF and had coronary computed tomography between October 2019 and August 2024. CAC was quantified using the Agatston score. The primary outcome was atrial arrhythmia recurrence beyond a 90-day blanking period. Patients were stratified by AF type, and associations were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Branch-specific CAC was also evaluated in exploratory analyses. During a median follow-up of 617 days (IQR, 457-808), atrial arrhythmia recurrence occurred in 19 of 96 patients with paroxysmal AF (PAF; 19.8%) and 39 of 106 patients with non-PAF (36.8%). In the overall cohort, CAC ≥100 was associated with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after adjustment for age, sex, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and left atrial volume index (adjusted HR, 2.03; 95% CI, 1.07-3.86; P=0.031). In age- and sex-adjusted analyses stratified by AF type, CAC ≥100 was associated with a higher risk of recurrence in patients with PAF (adjusted HR, 5.59; 95% CI, 2.05-15.27; P<0.001), whereas no significant association was observed in patients with non-PAF (adjusted HR, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.56-2.52; P=0.647). The interaction between CAC ≥100 and AF type was statistically significant in the age- and sex-adjusted model (P for interaction=0.011) and remained significant in the expanded clinically adjusted model including hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and left atrial volume index (P for interaction=0.005).

CONCLUSIONS: CAC ≥100 was associated with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after AF ablation, and this association may differ according to AF type, with a stronger association observed in patients with PAF. Subgroup and interaction analyses were exploratory and limited by the small number of recurrence events. CAC may provide useful information for post-ablation recurrence risk stratification, although these findings require validation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Pulmonary artery to ascending aorta ratio on pre-procedural computed tomography and pulmonary hypertension after transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
articles.abstract: To investigate whether pre-transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) computed tomography (CT)-derived anatomical metrics are associated with post-TAVR pulmonary hypertension (PH) with elevated pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR). In this post-hoc analysis of a prospective single-center registry (Invasive PPM Registry; UMIN-CTR: 000054628), 97 patients undergoing TAVR with complete CT, echocardiography, and invasive hemodynamics were evaluated. Prespecified CT metrics included main, left and right pulmonary artery diameters, right ventricle/left ventricle ratio (RV/LV), right ventricular outflow tract wall thickness, septal deviation, and the pulmonary artery-to-ascending aorta ratio (P​A:​AA). The primary endpoint was post-TAVR PH with elevated PVR (mean pulmonary artery pressure > 20 mmHg and PVR > 2 Wood units). Incremental value beyond right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP) was assessed. PH with elevated PVR occurred in 21 (21.6%) patients. Diastolic PA:​AA showed the best discrimination, although this was modest (AUC 0.664, 95% CI 0.526-0.798), other metrics performed less well (AUCs 0.46-0.60). At the Youden-optimal threshold of ≥ 0.90, sensitivity was 61.9%, specificity 72.4%, positive predictive value 38.2% and negative predictive value 87.3%. RVSP discriminated poorly (AUC 0.558); adding PA:​AA(d) improved discrimination (AUC 0.710; ΔAUC 0.152), model fit (p = 0.015), risk separation (IDI 0.066; p = 0.020) and reclassification (category-free NRI 0.690; p = 0.024). PA:​AA(d) correlated modestly with post-procedural mPAP (Spearman ρ = 0.247; p = 0.015). In this exploratory analysis, a larger pre-TAVR diastolic PA:AA ratio was associated with post-TAVR PH with elevated PVR and improved discrimination when combined with echocardiographic RV​SP.Trial registration: This study was registered with the University Hospital Medical Information Network Clinical Trial Registry and accepted by the International Committee of Medical Journal ​Editors (UMIN ID: 000054628).

articles.title: Current diagnostic clinical examinations for cardiomyopathies: a nationwide survey of cardiologists in Japan.
authors: research group for the investigative study of the diagnosis, clinical application of genomic information in idiopathic cardiomyopathy, Ministry of Health, Labour, Welfare Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research on Intractable Diseases
articles.abstract: Idiopathic cardiomyopathies-including dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), restrictive cardiomyopathy (RCM), and arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC)-are diagnosed after excluding secondary cardiomyopathies caused by systemic diseases or specific etiologies. Although current guidelines recommend several diagnostic examinations to aid in this differentiation, the extent to which these tests are used in routine clinical practice and their associated factors remain unclear. We conducted a nationwide web-based questionnaire survey among physicians of the Japanese Circulation Society. An invitation was sent by email to 25,258 physicians, and responses were collected anonymously between January 10 and February 28, 2024. The questionnaire assessed respondents' characteristics and whether they would perform diagnostic examinations for each cardiomyopathy using a five-point Likert scale. Responses were categorized into two groups ("always/frequently" vs. "sometimes/rarely/never"), and multivariable nominal logistic regression analysis was performed to examine associations between respondent characteristics and reported routine use of diagnostic tests. Adjusted trends were also assessed for clinical experience and hospital bed categories. Among 1103 (4.4%) respondents, the frequency of diagnostic examinations varied by cardiomyopathy type. A high proportion of respondents (95%) reported that they would perform coronary evaluations in DCM, whereas this proportion was approximately 80% for other idiopathic cardiomyopathies. In contrast, the proportion of respondents reporting frequent use of examinations relevant to the differential diagnosis of secondary cardiomyopathies, such as endomyocardial biopsy (EMB), cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and nuclear imaging, was generally low. Multivariable analysis showed that institutional and physician-related factors were associated with reported testing patterns. Respondents working at larger hospitals more frequently reported routine use of most examinations, and those with fewer years of clinical experience more often reported that they would perform MRI in DCM and EMB and MRI in HCM. In addition, respondents reporting less frequent EMB use in DCM also reported less frequent use of MRI and 67Ga scintigraphy/18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography. In Japan, the proportion of physicians reporting that they would routinely perform several examinations relevant to the differential diagnosis of secondary cardiomyopathies was low, and these responses were associated with physician and institutional characteristics.

articles.title: Mitochondrial antiviral signalling protein (MAVS) in cardiovascular diseases (CVD): a novel pharmacological target.
articles.abstract: Mitochondrial antiviral signalling protein (MAVS), also known as interferon-β (IFN-β) promoter stimulator 1 (IPS-1), virus-induced signalling adaptor (VISA), and CARD adaptor inducing IFN-β (CARDIF), has emerged as a regulatory node linking mitochondrial stress, innate immune signalling, and cardiovascular disease (CVD) pathogenesis. In the cardiovascular system, MAVS is activated not only by viral RNA sensors such as retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I) and melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5 (MDA5), but also by endogenous danger signals. This activation promotes transcription of NLR family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) and pro-inflammatory cytokines, and facilitates NLRP3 inflammasome assembly and cytokine maturation, processes implicated in myocardial inflammation, remodelling, and dysfunction in conditions such as myocardial hypertrophy, atherosclerosis, and cardiomyopathy. Beyond inflammasome activation, MAVS intersects with multiple cell death and homeostatic pathways relevant to CVD, including apoptosis, autophagy, and, potentially, ferroptosis. Preclinical studies show that genetic ablation of MAVS, or pharmacological interventions that limit mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS), mitochondrial double-stranded RNA (mtdsRNA) release, or downstream innate immune signalling, can attenuate MAVS-associated inflammation, oxidative stress, and metabolic remodelling, thereby slowing disease progression in experimental cardiovascular models. MAVS, however, also performs essential protective functions, particularly in antiviral defence and maintenance of cardiac homeostasis, underscoring the need for context-specific, cell-type-restricted, or pathway-selective modulation rather than indiscriminate inhibition. Collectively, these findings position MAVS as a promising therapeutic target in CVD, warranting further investigation into MAVS-associated signalling pathways and their modulation in cardiovascular contexts.

articles.title: Health and economic impacts of achieving WHO air quality targets in 136 Low- and Middle-Income countries.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ambient air pollution is a leading global health risk and disproportionately affects populations of Low- and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs). In 2021, WHO revised its Air Quality Guidelines (AQG), lowering recommended annual limits for fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and nitrogen dioxide (NO2). We estimated the potential health and economic impacts of achieving WHO Interim Target 3 (IT3) and AQG concentrations across LMICs.

METHODS: We conducted a quantitative health impact assessment across 136 LMICs using gridded population data, high-resolution global PM2.5 and NO2 concentration estimates, and country-level Global Burden of Disease 2021 mortality and incidence rates. Published concentration-response functions were applied at ∼ 1 km x 1 km resolution to estimate one-year changes in mortality and disease incidence under IT3 (PM2.5; 15, NO2; 20 μg/m3) and AQG (PM2.5; 5, NO2; 10 μg/m3) counterfactual scenarios. Outcomes were all-cause and cause-specific mortality (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease [COPD], ischaemic heart disease [IHD], and stroke) and disease incidence (COPD, dementia, IHD, and stroke). Mortality changes were valued using country-adjusted value of a statistical life (VSL, Int$ PPP-adjusted 2021). Direct medical and productivity-related costs associated with incidence changes were estimated using a cost-of-illness (COI) framework. Uncertainty intervals (UI) reflect uncertainty in concentration-response functions only and likely underestimate uncertainty if all sources were propagated in the estimates.

RESULTS: Estimated health impact of attaining WHO IT3 and AQG concentrations for PM2.5 was 16.04% reduction (6.58 million, UI: 4.7-8.3 million) and 22.97% reduction (9.43 million, UI: 6.8-11.7million) in annual mortality, respectively. Corresponding VSL-based estimates of annual mortality reductions were Int$5.5 trillion (7.0% of aggregate LMIC GDP) and Int$8.4 trillion (10.7% of GDP), respectively. For NO2, estimated reductions in mortality were approximately 1.06% (435,000, UI: 268,000-594,000) and 2.79% (1.1 million; UI: 706,000-1.6 million), yielding gains of Int$0.6 trillion (0.7% of GDP) and Int$1.5 trillion (1.9% of GDP), for IT3 and AQG scenarios, respectively. Disease-specific mortality reductions were most prominent for IHD and stroke in Asia and Africa. Under the PM2.5 AQG scenario, an estimated 2.82 million (2.2-3.4) COPD, 1.10 million (0.3-1.7) dementia, 7.3 million (3.3-10.4) IHD, and 2.3 million (1.8-2.7) stroke reductions in annual incidence was projected. Associated reductions in direct medical and productivity-related costs were greatest for IHD, COPD, and stroke. NO2-related morbidity reductions were smaller across all outcomes. All health impact estimates are potential reductions relative to current disease burden and reflect postponed all-cause mortality, or the avoidance of disease-specific mortality or incidence, within a single year. Effects for each exposure-outcome pair should be interpreted independently and not summed. Estimates should be interpreted considering data limitations, modelling assumptions, the one-year counterfactual design and the incomplete propagation of uncertainty beyond the CRFs.

DISCUSSION: Achieving both WHO IT3 and AQG values in LMICs could yield substantial reductions in mortality and disease incidence, particularly for cardiovascular and respiratory conditions, alongside large, monetised welfare gains from reduced mortality risk. These findings quantify the potential societal benefit of air quality improvements and support accelerated action toward meeting WHO guideline levels in regions bearing the highest pollution burden.

articles.title: Doxycycline and Risk for Pregnancy Loss : A Multi-database, Multi-indication Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Doxycycline is commonly prescribed to reproductive-aged women, but evidence about safety during pregnancy is limited.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the risk for pregnancy loss after doxycycline exposure in the first trimester.

DESIGN: Retrospective active-comparator cohort study.

SETTING: Merative MarketScan commercial (2005-2021) and Medicaid (1999-2019) claims data.

PARTICIPANTS: Pregnancies ending in loss or live birth among women aged 12 to 55 years.

INTERVENTION: 3 cohorts of pregnancies with first-trimester oral doxycycline or comparator antibiotic prescription fills and concomitant diagnoses of respiratory tract infection (RTI) or acne.

MEASUREMENTS: Pregnancy loss was evaluated using validated algorithms. Doxycycline-exposed pregnancies were matched on propensity score and gestational age to comparator pregnancies (exposed to amoxicillin or a macrolide for RTI or topical clindamycin for acne). Adjusted risk differences and adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) were estimated via binomial and modified Poisson regression separately for each database and comparison.

RESULTS: The study included 218 234 pregnant participants with RTI (110 254 in MarketScan, 107 980 in Medicaid) and 6636 with acne (4719 in MarketScan, 1917 in Medicaid). Among those with RTI, doxycycline use was associated with an increased risk for pregnancy loss compared with amoxicillin use (MarketScan aRR, 1.54 [95% CI, 1.41 to 1.68]; Medicaid aRR, 1.40 [CI, 1.28 to 1.53]).
