Results were similar for the comparison with macrolides (MarketScan aRR, 1.39 [CI, 1.28 to 1.51]; Medicaid aRR, 1.36 [CI, 1.25 to 1.48]). Among patients with acne, the comparison with topical clindamycin was statistically significant in MarketScan (aRR, 1.49 [CI, 1.26 to 1.76]) but not Medicaid (aRR, 1.03 [CI, 0.80 to 1.33]). Among cohorts with statistically significant aRRs, risk differences ranged between 7 and 11 percentage points.

LIMITATION: Residual confounding and exposure or outcome misclassification are possible, and congenital malformations were not evaluated.

CONCLUSION: Doxycycline use for RTI or acne during early pregnancy was associated with an increased risk for pregnancy loss. Clinicians may use this information to weigh risks and benefits when prescribing doxycycline to reproductive-aged women.

PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Cardiac Complications following Creation of Arteriovenous Access in Medicare Beneficiaries with ESKD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) and grafts (AVGs) are the preferred long-term hemodialysis access for the majority of patients, but produce hemodynamic changes that contribute to cardiac complications including heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, and atrial arrhythmia. This cohort study leverages nationwide claims data to examine adverse cardiac events associated with AVGs and AVFs among patients with ESKD.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using 100% Medicare fee-for-service claims to identify adults with ESKD undergoing AVF or AVG creation from 2017-2024. The primary outcome was hospitalization for a composite adverse cardiac event (heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, or atrial fibrillation or flutter) within 1 year. Secondary outcomes included the composite outcome through 5 years, its individual components, all-cause hospitalization, and flow-reduction procedures. Cumulative incidence functions were estimated using Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models. Independent variable analyses were conducted for the primary outcome.

RESULTS: We identified 210,002 accesses (mean age 66.3 years; 43% female) including 147,709 (70%) AVFs and 62,293 (30%) AVGs. AVG recipients had a greater burden of baseline comorbidity and cardiovascular disease. Through 1 year, the cumulative incidence of hospitalization for an adverse cardiac event was 40% (AVF 39%, AVG 44%, P < .001), constituting 61% of all-cause hospitalizations. Heart failure predominated (AVF 33%, AVG 37%, P < .001), followed by atrial fibrillation or flutter (AVF 19%, AVG 21%, P < .001), and pulmonary hypertension (AVF 8%, AVG 9%, P < .001). Older age (≥ 50 years), AVG creation, pre-existing pulmonary hypertension, and atrial arrhythmia were independently associated with a higher hazard of the primary outcome (P < .05).

CONCLUSIONS: The high rate of hospitalization for adverse cardiac events in the first year after arteriovenous access creation supports consideration of strategies (e.g., lower-flow forearm access, flow-volume surveillance) to mitigate the hemodynamic consequences of long-term arteriovenous access.

articles.title: The beneficial impact of a lifestyle modification program on childhood obesity: a comparative study of demographic, anthropometric, and social factors over a decade.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Juvenile obesity is a major risk factor for the development of type 2 diabetes. KiCK is a 1-year outpatient pediatric obesity therapy program at the AUF DER BULT Children's and Youth Hospital. In addition to multiprofessional obesity training, clinical and laboratory data are collected at the beginning and end of the program, and a standardized 6-min walking test (6MWT) is carried out.

METHODS: BMI, laboratory parameters, daily media usage time, and the data of the 6-MWT of the program participants in the years 2009-2012 ("A"), 2012-2015 ("B"), and 2018-2019 ("C") were recorded, and the differences between the three groups were analyzed.

RESULTS: Group A included n=64 children (mean age 12.0; 40.6 % female), group B included n=104 children (mean age 11.7; 55.8 % female), and group C included n=131 children (mean age 11.9; 58 % female). BMI-SDS improved constantly in all three groups (A: 2.4 vs. 2.3 (p=0.009); B: 2.4 vs. 2.2 (p=0.003); C: 2.4 vs. 2.1 (p=0.001)). Obesity therapy significantly improved the walking distance in group B in the 6-MWT (B: 574 m vs. 621 m (p=<0.001)).

CONCLUSIONS: The significant improvement in BMI-SDS over decades shows the constant program's contribution to improved weight outcomes in children and adolescents during the periods studied.

articles.title: Prognostic impact of the Mehran 2 risk score on 1-year mortality after acute coronary syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Mehran 2 score was developed to predict contrast-associated acute kidney injury after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Its prognostic value beyond renal complications remains uncertain. We evaluated the association of preprocedural (model 1) and postprocedural (model 2) Mehran 2 scores with renal outcomes and 1-year mortality in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS).

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 1025 patients with ACS undergoing PCI. Both scores were calculated and categorized into four risk groups. The primary outcome was 1-year all-cause mortality, while secondary outcomes included contrast-induced nephropathy (CIN) and dialysis requirement. Prognostic performance was assessed using multivariable logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic analysis, and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis.

RESULTS: CIN occurred in 105 patients (10.2%), dialysis was required in 21 (2.0%), and 102 (10.0%) died within 1 year. All outcomes increased progressively across Mehran 2 risk categories (P < 0.001). Both scores were independently associated with 1-year mortality [model 1: adjusted odds ratio (OR): 1.59, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.37-1.84; model 2: adjusted OR: 1.60, 95% CI: 1.41-1.83; both P < 0.001]. The area under the curves (AUCs) for mortality were 0.794 and 0.806, respectively, with a modest improvement for model 2 (ΔAUC: 0.012; P = 0.049). Higher scores were associated with significantly lower 365-day survival (log-rank P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Both Mehran 2 models were associated with renal complications and 1-year mortality in patients with ACS undergoing PCI. The preprocedural model may facilitate early cardiorenal risk stratification, whereas the postprocedural model provides only modest incremental discrimination. Further validation against established mortality risk scores is needed.

articles.title: Prior Authorization Outcomes for Advanced Dermatologic Therapies in a Centralized Coordination Model: A Postimplementation Descriptive Analysis.
articles.journal: American journal of medical quality : the official journal of the American College of Medical Quality
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advanced systemic dermatologic therapies (ASDTs) have transformed dermatologic care but remain subject to prior authorization (PA) requirements that delay treatment initiation and impose administrative burdens. To address these barriers, the Mount Sinai Health System established the Biologics Treatment Center (BTC) in 2018 to centralize PA management and patient education.

OBJECTIVE: Assess PA approval rates, turnaround times, and patterns across medications and therapeutic categories within the BTC.

METHODS: Following Standards for Quality Improvement Reporting Excellence guidelines, we conducted a quality improvement analysis of PA requests for ASDTs managed by the BTC. Using de-identified specialty pharmacy data from Shields Health Solutions, we examined PA submissions between June 2020 and December 2021. Descriptive statistics summarized PA status and turnaround time (mean, median, and interquartile range) overall and by medication and therapeutic category.

RESULTS: Of 2,183 PA requests, 73.0% were initially approved, increasing to 87.3% after appeals. The median PA turnaround time was 1 day (interquartile range [IQR]: 0-3) overall. Median turnaround times were 1 day (IQR: 0-3) for approved requests, 2 days (IQR: 0-4.25) for appealed and overturned cases, 1 day (IQR: 0-4) for appealed and upheld cases, and 2 days (IQR: 0-6) for denials without appeal. Approval rates varied substantially by medication, ranging from 97.4% for adalimumab to 30.8% for tildrakizumab.

CONCLUSIONS: This analysis describes PA outcomes for ASDTs within a centralized coordination model, including approval rates, turnaround times, and variability across medications. These findings provide insight into operational performance and highlight areas for further investigation into factors influencing PA outcomes.

articles.title: Asthma prevalence and influenza and COVID-19 vaccination coverage among children aged ≤17 years with asthma.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Children with asthma are at increased risk for complications from respiratory infectious diseases. This study assessed asthma prevalence and influenza and COVID-19 vaccination coverage among children with asthma.

METHODS: Data from the 2024 National Health Interview Survey (NHIS) were analyzed to assess asthma prevalence and influenza and COVID-19 vaccination coverage by asthma status among children.

RESULTS: Current asthma prevalence was 6.5% among children aged ≤17 years. Prevalence was higher among children aged 5-12 years (8.2%) and 13-17 years (7.8%) compared with those aged <5 years (2.2%). Influenza and COVID-19 vaccination coverage among children with current asthma were 54.1% and 50.9%, respectively. Asthma prevalence and vaccination coverage varied by demographic and access-to-care characteristics.

CONCLUSION: Asthma prevalence was higher among older children, males, and non-Hispanic Black children. Influenza and COVID-19 vaccination coverage among children with asthma remained low. Tailored strategies are needed to reduce the asthma burden and improve vaccination coverage in populations with lower uptake.

articles.title: Predicting key viral mutations from within-host deep sequencing data.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Rapid SARS-CoV-2 evolution drives continuous epidemic waves, harming vaccine protection and exerting heavy burden to population health. Predicting virus evolution holds the key for current and future medical countermeasures against infectious diseases by allowing well-matching vaccines and timely epidemic response. However, due to its high genetic diversity, fast transmissibility and evolutionary rate, accurate and timely prediction of SARS-CoV-2 evolution remains a challenge. To address this, we developed a computational framework, Beth-2, to predict key mutations of SARS-CoV-2 through analyzing within-host viral genome deep sequencing data. We leveraged the early fitness signals of variants exhibited within-host and their fitness pattern between-host to infer the emerging mutations with fitness potential. In retrospective data validation, 98.6% of the key SARS-CoV-2 mutations on receptor binding domain could be detected by our model with a median lead time of 9 mo before they reached predominance at population level. Among the 26 prospectively predicted mutations, 69% of them exhibited significantly enhanced transmissibility and five showed significant immune escape from plasma of subjects who received COVID-19 mRNA vaccine collected 6 mo after the prediction time. The mutations predicted by Beth-2 that are functionally enhanced include F456L, the defining mutation of multiple current circulating lineages, including KP.3, NB.1.8.1, and XFG. The model captures mutations of high fitness potential under the natural immune environment of host and is applicable to other pathogens. The framework can be implemented along with the existing genome surveillance network and offers an efficient and effective instrument for vaccine preparation and epidemic response.

articles.title: Normalized Raman imaging for studies of tissue physiology of the kidney.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Conventional histology relies on fixation, embedding, sectioning, and staining methods that distort cellular architecture, extract lipids, and introduce variability, limiting reproducibility. We present a pipeline for automated histopathology in the mouse kidney using normalized stimulated Raman imaging (NoRI) that enables quantitative, label-free protein and lipid measurements at high spatial resolution. NoRI computationally corrects protein, lipid, and water Raman signals, allowing quantitative biomass measurements while preserving tissue architecture, facilitating analysis by convolutional neural networks (CNN) for quantitative, morphological feature extraction. Applied to mouse kidney, CNN analysis of NoRI images was able to accurately classify tubule types (F1=0.93; harmonic mean of precision and recall against immunofluorescence-defined labels), anatomical regions (F1 = 0.91), and biological sex (F1 = 0.97), revealing greater cytoplasmic lipid (+6.5 to 7.3 mg/mL; P ≤ 0.028) and nuclear protein (+26.3 mg/mL; P ≤ 0.001) in female tubules. Using acute kidney injury (AKI) in mice as a disease model to test our histopathology pipeline combining NoRI and CNNs, we captured dynamic lipid and protein organization and quantified brush border remodeling and lipid droplet changes over 25 d postinjury. Spatial lipid quantification was central for feature classification in AKI (F1 = 0.99). Quantitative NoRI images also significantly outperformed equivalent raw stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) images in distinguishing early time points (24 to 48 h) of ischemia-reperfusion injury [F1 = 0.99 (NoRI) vs. 0.84 (SRS); P < 0.0001], demonstrating the improvement of NoRI over conventional SRS imaging. These results establish our pipeline, which combines NoRI imaging with advanced CNN analyses, as a reproducible, quantitative method for histopathology and feature discovery.

articles.title: Trust as a hidden driver of epidemic-relevant behavior: Institution- and behavior-specific associations across 20 national survey waves.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Compartmental models of infectious disease transmission make assumptions about human behaviors. Specifically, they parameterize interactions across population groups, assumed to have distinct epidemiologically relevant behavioral patterns, primarily through contact matrices stratified by demographic variables such as age, gender, or socioeconomic status. Although such demographic characteristics are readily measurable, they may inadequately capture the social and psychological forces that govern protective behaviors. Drawing on 20 waves of a national survey conducted throughout the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, we show that institutional trust-particularly trust in public health agencies, physicians, and hospitals-is a dominant predictor of protective behavior adoption. For mask wearing during periods of strongest pandemic activity, institutional trust explains more behavioral difference across population groups than age, income, education, and partisan affiliation combined. In unadjusted analyses, the difference in protective behavior adoption between individuals with the highest and lowest trust in the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) was four- to six-fold larger than the corresponding differences by age, income, or education, and exceeded the difference between Democratic and Republican respondents. This association was institutionally specific (the relationship attenuates for trust in banks), and behaviorally specific (trust in the CDC is associated with protective behaviors but not visiting a doctor). The latter suggests that trust modifies voluntary compliance with public health recommendations rather than healthcare access or use. These findings identify institutional trust as a candidate stratifying variable for models of behavior-coupled transmission dynamics, and as a measurable target for public health surveillance.

articles.title: [Impact of tumor necrosis factor superfamily member 4 gene polymorphisms on the risk of Crohn's disease and clinical efficacy of ustekinumab].
articles.journal: Zhonghua yi xue yi chuan xue za zhi = Zhonghua yixue yichuanxue zazhi = Chinese journal of medical genetics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the impact of tumor necrosis factor superfamily member 4 (TNFSF4) gene polymorphisms on the risk and clinicopathological features of Crohn's disease (CD), as well as the clinical efficacy of ustekinumab (UST).

METHODS: A total of 296 patients with CD diagnosed at the Department of Gastroenterology, The Second Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University between January 2018 and August 2025, and 532 healthy controls were selected. Genotypes of TNFSF4 (rs3850641 and rs45454293) were detected using multiplex polymerase chain reaction-ligase detection reaction technique. According to the Montreal Classification Criteria of Crohn's disease, the patients were divided into subgroups. The degree of clinical activity and intestinal inflammation degree of CD patients were evaluated by the Crohn's disease activity index (CDAI) and Simplified Crohn's disease endoscopic score (SES-CD), respectively. Unconditional Logistic regression model was used to analyze the distribution of TNFSF4 gene polymorphisms between the CD group and health control group, as well as between different subgroups of CD patients. Among them, a total of 247 cases receiving the routine UST therapy were divided into clinical response group (CDAI decreased by ≥ 100 points compared to week 0 or CDAI < 150 points) and clinical non-response group based on the changes in CDAI at week 8. They were also divided into mucosal healing group (SES-CD ≤ 2 points or no mucosal ulcer) and non-mucosal healing group based on the changes in SES-CD at week 34. Univariate Logistic regression was used to analyze the influencing factors for the clinical response and mucosal healing. Furthermore, unconditional Logistic regression was applied to assess the effect of TNFSF4 gene variants on the clinical response and mucosal healing. Generalized estimating equations were employed to analyze the effect of TNFSF4 gene polymorphisms on the longitudinal changes of efficacy outcomes. Bonferroni correction was applied for multiple comparisons.

RESULTS: The variant genotype (AG+GG) and variant allele (G) of rs3850641 in the CD group were more frequent than those in the control group (38.18% vs. 29.32%, P = 0.011, adjusted P = 0.022; 21.45% vs. 16.45%, P = 0.015, adjusted P = 0.030). The same conclusion was also drawn for the variant genotype (CT+TT) and variant allele (T) of rs45454293 (35.81% vs. 27.26%, P = 0.012, adjusted P = 0.024; 19.59% vs. 14.76%, P = 0.014, adjusted P = 0.028). Although the homozygous variant genotype (TT) of rs45454293 was more frequent among patients with stricturing or penetrating CD compared with those with non-stricturing, non-penetrating CD (5.93% vs. 1.24%, P = 0.041), the adjusted P value was over 0.05 after Bonferroni multiple correction. At week 8 of the UST therapy, the homozygous variant genotype (GG) of rs3850641 in the response group was less prevalent compared with the non-response group (1.69% vs. 11.59%, P = 0.004, adjusted P = 0.008). Similar result was obtained for the homozygous variant genotype (TT) of rs45454293 (1.69% vs. 10.14%, P = 0.008, adjusted P = 0.016). At week 34, the homozygous variant genotype (GG) of rs3850641 in the mucosal healing group was less common compared with the mucosal non-healing group (1.27% vs. 10.11%, P = 0.015, adjusted P = 0.030).

CONCLUSION: The rs3850641 and rs45454293 variants may not only increase the risk of CD, but also reduce the early clinical response rate of the UST therapy. The rs3850641 variant may also lower the late mucosal healing rate of the UST therapy.

articles.title: [Genetic analysis of a child with Frontometaphyseal dysplasia 1 due to variant of FLNA gene and literature review].
articles.journal: Zhonghua yi xue yi chuan xue za zhi = Zhonghua yixue yichuanxue zazhi = Chinese journal of medical genetics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the clinical characteristics and genetic etiology of a child with Frontometaphyseal dysplasia 1 (FMD1) due to variant of FLNA gene.

METHODS: A child who presented at the Department of Endocrinology, the Third Xiangya Hospital of Central South University in July 2025 with a 6-year history of prominent supraorbital ridges was selected as study subject. Clinical data of the child were collected. Peripheral venous blood samples were collected from the child and his parents for the extraction of genomic DNA. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) was carried out, and candidate variant was validated by Sanger sequencing. Pathogenicity of the variant was rated based on guidelines from the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG). Structure of the mutant protein was predicted using AlphaFold and PyMOL software. Literature retrieval was performed using Chinese and English keywords "FLNA gene" and "frontometaphyseal dysplasia". The clinical manifestations and inheritance patterns of previously reported cases with the variant were analyzed. This study was approved by the Ethics Committee of the hospital (Ethics No.: 25971).

RESULTS: The child exhibited multiple skeletal deformities including prominent supraorbital ridges, micrognathia, hearing loss, scoliosis, long bone curvature, broad and flat deformities of the thumbs and great toes, and joint contractures. Additionally, he was complicated with congenital urinary tract obstruction. WES revealed that he has harbored a hemizygous missense variant c.3557C>T (p.Ser1186Leu) in exon 22 of the FLNA gene, which showed a strong correlation with his clinical phenotype. Sanger sequencing confirmed this variant to be de novo in origin. Based on the ACMG guidelines, the FLNA c.3557C>T (p.Ser1186Leu) variant was classified as pathogenic (PS4_Moderate+PM2_Supporting+PM6+PP1_Strong+PP2+PP3). Protein structural modeling suggested that this variant could reduce local hydrogen bonds, which may weaken local anchoring force. Literature review has retrieved 8 articles (1 in Chinese) related to FMD1 due to the FLNA c.3557C>T variant. Together with the present case, a total of 14 patients (13 males and 1 female) were included. All patients showed obvious supraorbital hyperplasia (100.0%). Other common manifestations included wrist/distal joint contracture (14 cases), micrognathia (10 cases), scoliosis (10 cases), and spatulate thumbs/toes (9 cases). Other manifestations included hearing loss (8 cases), permanent tooth agenesis (8 cases), long bone bowing (8 cases), hypertelorism (8 cases). Urinary tract malformations (3 cases) and cardiovascular malformations (2 cases) were relatively rare. Analysis of the inheritance pattern showed that 2 of the 14 patients carried de novo variants, and the remaining 12 patients were from 9 families, with their mothers as heterozygous carriers (one mosaic).

CONCLUSION: This study has diagnosed a child with FMD1 due to a hemizygous c.3557C>T (p.Ser1186Leu) missense variant of the FLNA gene, which expanded the mutational spectrum of FMD1.

articles.title: USP46 restrains K63-linked polyubiquitination-dependent aggregation and activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome in lupus nephritis.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: The activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome necessitates its aggregation within the dispersed trans-Golgi network (dTGN) and subsequent transport from the dTGN to the microtubule organizing center (MTOC), a process facilitated by HDAC6. However, the regulatory mechanisms governing the formation of NLRP3 aggregates remain insufficiently understood. In this study, we demonstrate that proteasome impairment induces polyubiquitination and aggregation of NLRP3 at the MTOC. We demonstrate ubiquitin-specific protease 46 (USP46) as a key factor that recognizes NLRP3 as a substrate and restricts nondegradative K63-linked polyubiquitination at lysine residue K930, thereby preventing excessive aggregation, transport to the MTOC, and inflammasome activation. Furthermore, myeloid-specific knockout of USP46 exacerbates renal injury and inflammation in both lipopolysaccharide-induced-induced endotoxic shock and pristane-induced lupus nephritis models. Our findings provide insights into the regulatory mechanisms underlying the aggresomal activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome.

articles.title: Entropic tightening of knots in granular chains under vibration.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Knots are common in long chains, from DNA and proteins to everyday strings, yet direct observation of knot dynamics is difficult. Using granular chains on vibrating platforms, we directly visualize knot dynamics and find that knot cores spontaneously tighten, a behavior observed across different knot types. We quantitatively explain spontaneous knot tightening using knot-tube theory: segments confined within the knot core experience entropic loss and tend to escape the core to gain conformational entropy. Although driven granular chains are not in thermodynamic equilibrium, their steady-state knot-size statistics are approximately captured by equilibrium statistical mechanics and Monte Carlo simulations. Analyses of state-transition probabilities and time-reversal asymmetry suggest a weak violation of detailed balance when the granular dynamics are projected onto the knot-size coordinate. Finally, we discuss the possible relevance of knot tightening to topoisomerase-mediated DNA unknotting.

articles.title: Dynamic virulence decomposition disentangles host and pathogen contributions over the course of infection.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Decomposing virulence into host and pathogen effects is key to understanding how virulence is generated during infection, and how host and pathogen contributions evolve over time. Conventional virulence decomposition is, however, not designed to quantify how these contributions vary throughout an infection. Building on conventional virulence decomposition, we developed a dynamic framework that integrates disease space analysis to quantify these changing contributions. We applied this framework to existing data from house finches (Haemorhous mexicanus) experimentally infected with the emerging bacterial pathogen, Mycoplasma gallisepticum, examining two biologically meaningful infection phases: an early phase dominated by innate immune responses and a later phase in which the adaptive immune response is fully activated. Our analyses revealed that virulence components evolved differently across infection phases, with pathogen exploitation, per-parasite-pathogenicity (PPP), and host resistance each exhibiting distinct trajectories. These findings corroborated several known evolutionary patterns, while also revealing the evolution of increased PPP in this system. In contrast, the apparent evolution of host tolerance inferred from aggregated peak measurements was not supported by phase-specific analyses, demonstrating that aggregated and phase-specific measures can provide different mechanistic insights into virulence. By linking conventional virulence decomposition with disease space analysis, our dynamic virulence decomposition framework provides a general approach for quantifying how host and pathogen processes shape virulence over the course of infection.

articles.title: Comprehensive classification of HCN1 variants linked to neurodevelopmental disorders with and without epilepsy.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated 1 (HCN1) channels mediate the cationic Ih current, a fundamental regulator of neuronal excitability and synaptic integration, and are predominantly expressed in the cortex and hippocampus. Although HCN1 variants have been increasingly identified in patients with epilepsy, from milder forms to developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEE), genotype-phenotype correlations remain poorly defined. Here, we used patch-clamp electrophysiology and confocal imaging in HEK293 cells to functionally characterize 43 HCN1 variants identified in patients with neurodevelopmental disorders, with or without epilepsy. Based on biophysical properties, we established a classification system comprising four distinct functional classes: I) low or no current; II) hyperpolarizing shift in voltage dependence; III) depolarizing shift in voltage dependence; and IV) generation of an instantaneous current. The molecular basis for this classification was further interpreted using available cryo-EM structures of HCN1. Integration with clinical data from 50 patients revealed a striking correlation between functional class and clinical presentation. Loss-of-function variants prevailed among individuals with milder phenotypes or without epilepsy, with the latter distinctively clustering within the channel selectivity filter. In contrast, gain-of-function and mixed variants were predominantly associated with DEE. Finally, we demonstrate that allosteric modulators, including peptides NB6 and TRIP8bnano and the small molecule J&J12e, effectively normalize channel function across three of the four classes in vitro. These findings establish a biophysical framework for interpreting HCN1 variants, demonstrating that the direction of channel dysfunction is a major determinant of epilepsy risk and severity, and providing a conceptual foundation for future class-based precision medicine approaches.

articles.title: Core effectors of the Fusarium pan-effectome contribute to host specificity.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Fusarium fungi cause economically important diseases of cereal crops, including Fusarium head blight, ear blight, and root rot. Central to these interactions are secreted effector proteins that manipulate host biology to promote infection. In turn, plants have evolved to recognize effector activity to activate immune responses and restrict disease. Despite their importance, the diversity, conservation, and evolution of Fusarium effectors remain poorly understood. Here, we present the Fusarium sambucinum Species complex Effector Compendium (FUSEC), a sequence-defined pan-effectome constructed from 188 high-quality genomes representing 27 species. FUSEC comprises 4,057 sequence-defined effector families, including a conserved soft-core repertoire of 235 families present in at least 95% of isolates. Structure-guided comparisons reorganized these conserved families into 184 structure-defined groups, revealing relationships that extend beyond sequence similarity and identifying similarities to numerous experimentally characterized fungal (a)virulence factors. Despite their broad conservation, soft-core families exhibited substantial within-family sequence diversity, and analyses of diversifying selection identified 44 candidate families undergoing adaptive evolution. Functional screening revealed that the majority of these candidates altered wheat immune responses, and CRISPR-Cas9-mediated gene deletions in Fusarium graminearum demonstrated that multiple conserved effectors contribute to cultivar-dependent Fusarium head blight severity.

articles.title: Hypothalamic lncRNA Synage prevents age-related sperm quality decline by suppressing A-type potassium currents in GnRH neurons.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Age-related decline in male fertility, including diminished sperm quality, poses significant risks to offspring health and is exacerbated by modern trends toward delayed parenthood. Focusing on the hypothalamus-pituitary-testis axis, which governs hormonal control of male reproduction, we identified Synage, a long noncoding RNA expressed in the hypothalamic medial preoptic area (mPOA). We found that Synage expression in gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) neurons decreases with age, correlating with reduced sperm quality and male fertility. mPOA-targeted Synage_B (brain-specific isoform) supplementation increases serum testosterone and improves sperm count and progressive motility in 12-mo-old mice. Conversely, conditional deletion of Synage in GnRH neurons in young mice reduces GnRH neuron firing, decreases serum LH and testosterone levels, impaires sperm quality, and reduces male fertility. Mechanistically, Synage interacts with the heat shock protein HSPA8 and stabilizes the HSPA8-KCHIP4 interaction. Synage loss increases KCHIP4 abundance and its association with the Kv4.2 channel, promoting Kv4.2 membrane recruitment and enhancing A-type potassium currents (IA), thereby reducing GnRH neuronal excitability. Consistent with this model, GnRH neurons from 12-mo-old mice also exhibit reduced excitability. Together, these findings support a role for age-dependent Synage loss in reproductive decline, at least in part through dysregulation of the HSPA8-KCHIP4-Kv4.2 pathway and reduced GnRH neuron excitability. These findings identify Synage as a candidate regulator of reproductive aging and motivate further investigation of its translational potential.

articles.title: The diagnosis of iron deficiency: progress toward consensus.
Correction for Borowiec et al., Mutations at the BLK locus linked to maturity onset diabetes of the young and β-cell dysfunction.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

articles.title: Correction for Tsang et al., Cyclin D1 overexpression supports stable EBV infection in nasopharyngeal epithelial cells.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

articles.title: TLR7-independent control of retroviral infection.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Development of effective immune responses against any pathogen requires efficient activation of the innate immune system followed by induction of an appropriate adaptive immune response using specific signaling pathways tailored to each infection. The sole innate immune receptor implicated in the induction of adaptive immunity to retroviral infection is Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7). We have found that germinal center responses, neutralizing antibody production, and clearance of murine leukemia virus (MLV) infection in BALB.J and C57BL/6N (B6N) mice occurs in the absence of TLR7 signaling. This suggests that a previously unknown alternative sensing pathway exists for the activation of protective immune responses upon retroviral infection. Genetic crosses indicate that the ability to control retroviral infection in the absence of TLR7 signaling is determined by the same recessive mechanism in both B6N and BALB.J mice, suggesting that TLR7-independent responses do not result from a gain-of-function of an alternative pattern recognition receptor. Additionally, we observed that TLR7-deficient BALB.J mice produce neutralizing antibodies against mouse mammary tumor virus (MMTV) infection, indicating that this alternative sensing pathway is active against retroviruses of multiple genera. Finally, we determined that the alternative sensing pathway is also independent of both MyD88 and STING signaling. The ability of mice of two genetic backgrounds to control retroviral infection in the absence of TLR7 signaling provides a valuable tool for the identification of an additional mechanism of retrovirus control. The dissection of this pathway has the potential to alter our understanding of the requirements for the stimulation of antigen-specific neutralizing immunity.

articles.title: CD8+ regulatory T cells limit immunopathology but impair viral clearance in Hantaan virus infection.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: In hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) caused by Hantaan virus (HTNV), virus-specific CD8+ T cells mediate both viral clearance and immunopathology. Here, we characterized a CD8+ regulatory T cell (Treg) subset restricted by HLA-E (and its murine ortholog Qa-1) in HFRS patients and in a murine HTNV infection model. CD8+ Tregs (CD122+Eomes+CD49dloKIR+), a subset substantially enriched for HLA-E-restricted T cells, were significantly reduced in peripheral blood of HFRS patients and displayed a terminally differentiated profile with elevated expression of KLRG-1, NKG2A, CTLA-4, and Fas-L, correlating with disease severity. Two HTNV glycoprotein-derived nonapeptides that bound Qa-1 were identified. Following immunization with the identified HTNV peptides and subsequent HTNV challenge, wild-type (WT) mice showed attenuated renal immunopathology, whereas D227K knock-in mice (with disrupted Qa-1-CD8/TCR interaction) showed enhanced viral clearance in the spleen and kidney but exacerbated renal immunopathology. Mechanistically, Qa-1-restricted CD8+ Tregs from WT mice suppressed effector CD8+ T cell proliferation in a peptide-specific, CD8/TCR-dependent manner via enhanced TGF-β secretion. Strikingly, D227K mutation dichotomously reshaped Treg phenotype: bulk polyclonal CD8+ Tregs displayed compensatory upregulation of inhibitory receptors (NKG2A, CTLA-4, PD-1) and TGF-β, whereas epitope-specific CD8+ Tregs showed impaired antigen-specific suppressive function and attenuated TGF-β production. Collectively, these findings indicate that HLA-E/Qa-1-restricted CD8+ Tregs can restrain immunopathology during HTNV infection, potentially at the cost of delayed viral elimination. Modulation of this axis may provide insights for therapeutic strategies in HFRS and related viral hemorrhagic fevers.

articles.title: Transcranial magnetic stimulation to the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex modulates single-neuron activity in humans.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) to the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) is an established treatment for depression, yet the fundamental question of how cortical stimulation influences single neurons in deep brain circuits critical for mood regulation remains unanswered. Using a rare opportunity to record from intracranial microelectrodes while TMS was delivered in four neurosurgical patients, we evaluated the responses of 185 single neurons. Artifact cleaning enabled single-neuron spikes to be resolved as early as 8 ms after stimulation. We found that single-pulse TMS to the left dlPFC elicited time-locked firing responses in 46% of neurons (26% facilitated only, 19% suppressed only, 1% both). These responses occurred within deep bilateral cortical and subcortical structures, including the putamen and thalamus. Single-pulse TMS tended to facilitate spiking in striato-thalamic putative inhibitory neurons from ~8 ms, peaking at ~80 to 100 ms, and decaying until ~600 ms. In contrast, putative excitatory neurons and limbic areas were suppressed with a slower time course lasting to ~1,000 ms. TMS-evoked potentials recorded from intracranial depth macroelectrodes to quantify network activity revealed that the modulation of responsive neurons was positively correlated with cortico-striato-thalamic network activity and anticorrelated with limbic network activity in one participant with sufficient network and unit sampling. These results suggest that dlPFC TMS recruits a high percentage of neurons spanning cortical and subcortical brain regions bilaterally. The recruitment pattern selectively involves increasing the firing rate of inhibitory neurons in executive control networks while suppressing limbic excitatory drive, providing a candidate cellular mechanism for how cortical stimulation modulates distributed brain networks.

articles.title: Targeting the Microbiome to Treat Alcohol Use Disorder and Liver Disease.
articles.abstract: Alcohol use disorder and alcohol-associated liver disease represent a global health burden, yet treatment options remain limited. Emerging evidence has shown the intestinal microbiome to be a mediator of alcohol-associated organ injury, establishing gut dysbiosis, intestinal barrier dysfunction, and aberrant microbial metabolite production as drivers of disease. The gut-liver-brain axis provides a mechanistic framework in which microbial products and signals fuel hepatic inflammation, steatosis, fibrosis, and neuroinflammation that drive alcohol consumption. This review discusses current evidence on how chronic alcohol exposure shapes microbial communities, disrupts the gut epithelium, and alters innate immune and metabolic circuits in the liver and the brain. We examine how microbiome-targeted interventions, such as probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation, non-absorbable antibiotics, and short-chain fatty acid supplementation, can act on mechanistic targets along this axis. Finally, we highlight knowledge gaps, including the roles of causal microbial taxa, sex differences in gut-immune-brain signaling, and windows of reversibility that must be further investigated and understood to translate microbial modulation into effective therapies. In conclusion, this review summarizes the current literature on targeting the microbiome and the gut-liver-brain axis as a treatment approach, with a focus on the mechanisms within this axis and the interventions that target them.

articles.title: Beyond CYP2C19: the lysosome-CMA-SORT1-CES1 axis as a potential regulator of clopidogrel response.
articles.abstract: Interindividual variability in clopidogrel response remains a significant limitation of antiplatelet therapy, particularly in patients with acute coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention. Cytochrome P450 2C19 is a major determinant of clopidogrel bioactivation but accounts for only part of the variability in platelet inhibition, suggesting additional hepatic regulatory mechanisms. The main competing hydrolytic pathway is mediated by carboxylesterase 1 (CES1), which converts most absorbed clopidogrel into inactive metabolites. However, CES1 activity cannot be inferred from protein abundance alone, as active-metabolite formation also depends on catalytic function, intracellular localization, isoform composition, substrate accessibility and residual CYP capacity. Recent evidence indicates that intracellular trafficking and lysosomal degradation can regulate hepatic CES1 abundance. Sortilin 1 (SORT1) may facilitate CES1 lysosomal targeting, while a cytosolic pool of SORT1 has been reported to undergo chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA)-associated turnover involving HSPA8 and LAMP2A. These relationships were observed in hepatic cell systems and mouse models of lipid metabolism, but not in humans treated with clopidogrel, and thus they support a mechanistic hypothesis rather than an established pharmacological pathway. This review synthesizes recent evidence on clopidogrel metabolism, CES1 regulation, lysosomal trafficking, CMA, and platelet P2Y12 signaling. We suggest that the lysosome-CMA-SORT1-CES1 axis may contribute to the heterogeneity of clopidogrel response by shifting the balance between hydrolytic inactivation and oxidative bioactivation. Although the individual molecular relationships are supported across different experimental models, their integration as a determinant of human clopidogrel response remains untested. Before the proposed axis can be considered clinically or pharmacologically established, direct causal validation is required.

articles.title: Growth factor VEGF-B sustains intestinal Tfh cell stemness to restrict Taurinivorans outgrowth and microbiota-driven obesity.
articles.abstract: Autocrine signaling through vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-1 (VEGFR-1) reprograms T cell metabolism upon TCR stimulation. We found that mice bearing conditional deletion of Flt1 (encoding VEGFR-1) in T cells developed spontaneous obesity with advancing age. Analyses of lymphoid and metabolic tissues identified a VEGFR-1+ T follicular helper (Tfh) population in Peyer's patches and mesenteric lymph nodes. Flt1 deletion impaired Tfh fitness and reduced secretory IgA in the gut, resulting in unrestricted expansion of the pathobiont Taurinivorans. Taurinivorans overgrowth depleted host taurine, which drove obesity via suppressed adipocyte lipolysis and thermogenesis. Mechanistically, a VEGFR-1-AKT signaling axis promoted Tfh cell stemness by limiting p53-mediated senescence. This Tfh-microbiota-obesity pathway was also observed in diet-induced obese mice and in humans. Oral administration of IgA reduced Taurinivorans and alleviated adiposity, highlighting the therapeutic potential of this axis. Tfh cell senescence impairs IgA production, disrupting gut microbial homeostasis, with consequences to host metabolic disease.

articles.title: Chitosan-hyaluronic acid nanoparticles with time-dependent mucoadhesive and mucus penetrating behaviour to overcome pathological lung mucus.
articles.abstract: Bacterial infections are a major complication in pulmonary diseases such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), aggravated by multidrug-resistant bacteria and the presence of pathological mucus that limits antibiotics efficacy. To address this challenge, drug-free chitosan/hyaluronic acid (CS/HA) nanoparticles were developed through a one-step ionic gelation method. By modulating the CS/HA ratio and HA molecular weight, stable, spherical nanoparticles with sizes ranging from 75 to 210 nm and positive ζ-potentials between +22 and +34 mV were obtained. FTIR confirmed electrostatic stabilization. The nanoparticles exhibited a unique time-dependent behavior: initial adherence to pathological mucus for local retention, followed by a hydration-driven surface rearrangement enabling mucus barrier penetration. This sequential mucoadhesive-to-mucus-penetrating transition is reported for the first time for a drug-free carbohydrate network. Biological assays demonstrated excellent biocompatibility with healthy and diseased human lung fibroblasts (HLF, HLF COPD and A549), alongside significant antioxidant activity. Moreover, the nanoparticles exerted dose-dependent, intrinsic antimicrobial effects against major respiratory pathogens, including Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Overall, by engineering a dynamically adaptive interface, this work crucially resolves the historical trade-off between mucosal retention and diffusion, establishing a promising nanotherapeutic strategy for combating multidrug-resistant pulmonary infections directly at the mucus site.

articles.title: [Efficacy and safety of domestic semaglutide injection in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately controlled with metformin: a multicenter, randomized, controlled phase 3 equivalence clinical trial].
articles.abstract: Objective: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of domestic semaglutide injection in the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) inadequately controlled with metformin. Methods: This multicenter, randomized, positive-controlled phase 3 equivalence clinical trial enrolled patients with T2DM from 39 research centers in China between March 13, 2024, and April 9, 2025. Central randomization was performed using interactive response technology, and the subjects were stratified according to their glycated hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) levels (<8.5% and ≥8.5%) and randomly divided into an experimental group (domestic semaglutide injection) and a control group (original semaglutide injection) at a ratio of 1∶1. The primary endpoint was the change from baseline in HbA1c at week 32, with an equivalent threshold of ±0.4%. The key secondary endpoints included HbA1c change from baseline at week 20, the proportion of patients with HbA1c<7.0% or HbA1c≤6.5% at 20 and 32 weeks, and the evaluation of safety. Efficacy endpoints were analyzed in the full analysis set (FAS), and safety endpoints were analyzed in the safety set (SS). Changes from baseline in HbA1c were analyzed using a mixed model for repeated measures; the proportions of subjects with HbA1c<7.0% or HbA1c≤6.5% were compared using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel χ2 test; and safety endpoints were analyzed using Fisher's exact test. Results: Both the FAS and SS included 481 patients, with 241 in the experimental group and 240 in the control group. After 32 weeks of treatment, the least squares mean (LSM) (95%CI) changes from baseline in HbA1c were -1.80% (-1.93%--1.68%) in the experimental group and -1.85% (-1.98%--1.72%) in the control group, with a difference of 0.05% (-0.13%-0.23%)(both one-sided P<0.001). Similarly, equivalence was demonstrated at week 20, with an intergroup difference (95%CI) of 0.08% (-0.10%-0.26%) for the change from baseline in HbA1c (both one-sided P<0.001). The proportions of patients achieving HbA1c<7.0% or HbA1c≤6.5% showed no statistically significant differences between the two groups. The incidence of overall adverse events was comparable between the two groups [85.06% (205/241) vs 83.33% (200/240)], and the incidences of drug-related hypoglycemic events were 0.41% (1/241) and 2.50% (6/240), respectively, with no statistically significant differences (both P>0.05). Conclusions: In patients with T2DM inadequately controlled by metformin, domestic semaglutide injection demonstrated glucose-lowering efficacy equivalent to original semaglutide injection over the 32-week short-term period, with generally similar overall safety profiles between the two groups.

articles.title: Orofacial Strength in a Typically Developing Pediatric Population: A Comparison of the Iowa Oral Performance Instrument and Tongueometer.
articles.journal: Journal of speech, language, and hearing research : JSLHR
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pressure-based assessments of tongue strength are becoming increasingly common in dysphagia management. However, whether different manometric devices produce comparable measurements for the same tasks, particularly in pediatric populations, remains insufficiently clarified. The purposes of this study were to establish age- and sex-specific reference values for tongue, buccal, and lip strength in a pediatric population using the Iowa Oral Performance Instrument (IOPI) and the Tongueometer (TO) and to systematically examine the effects of device, age, and sex on these measurements, as well as the level of agreement between the two devices.

METHOD: A total of 330 typically developing children and adolescents aged 8-18 years were included. For all participants, anterior and posterior tongue strength, buccal strength, and lip (interlabial) strength were measured using both the IOPI and TO. Device, age, and sex effects were examined using mixed factorial analyses of variance. Age- and sex-specific reference ranges for both devices were reported using descriptive statistics. The agreement between devices was assessed using Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) and Bland-Altman plots, while the relationship between devices was assessed using linear regression analysis.

RESULTS: Across all parameters, the TO consistently produced lower pressure values than the IOPI. Additionally, the correlation between all measurements obtained with both devices was moderate to strong. Lin's CCC values indicated poor agreement for all measurements, and Bland-Altman analyses demonstrated systematic bias between devices. Age had a strong main effect on tongue, lip, and buccal strength measurements obtained from both devices, whereas sex effects were generally limited and observed for buccal and lip strength measured.

CONCLUSIONS: The IOPI and TO systematically produce different pressure values in pediatric populations and should not be used interchangeably. Accordingly, this study provides age- and sex-specific reference values for both devices to support device-specific interpretation of tongue and orofacial strength measurements in children and adolescents. The results also indicate that age is a stronger determinant of tongue and orofacial strength during childhood and adolescence than sex.

articles.title: Letter to Editor: Prehospital Antibiotics and 28-Day Mortality in Sepsis: Where Does the Adjusted Benefit Come from?
A New Web-Based Word-Picture Matching Test Reveals Psycholinguistic Effects on Word-Level Reading and Auditory Comprehension in Aphasia.
articles.journal: Journal of speech, language, and hearing research : JSLHR
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Word reading comprehension deficits, often measured by word-to-picture matching (WtPM) tasks, are common in aphasia and alexia. To specify the nature of comprehension deficits, WtPM tasks should manipulate psycholinguistic features, have matched written and auditory versions, and provide normed scores measuring speed and accuracy. Here we present a novel web-based WtPM task that meets those needs. We use it to assess word comprehension deficits in left-hemisphere stroke survivors (LHSS).

METHOD: We examined scores for the novel auditory and written WtPM task in a normative sample (n = 62) and an LHSS sample (n = 63). Mixed-effects models examined accuracy and response time in both groups, and an analysis of variance compared efficiency between the groups. Correlations compared written WtPM performance and item difficulty to auditory WtPM, written lexical decision, and oral reading. A k-means clustering analysis examined deficit patterns in the LHSS group.

RESULTS: WtPM performance was modulated by modality, frequency, and regularity and was impaired in the LHSS group. Written WtPM performance and item difficulty were correlated with auditory WtPM and written lexical decision in both groups and with oral reading in the LHSS group. Over half of the LHSS sample had frank deficits on at least one WtPM task. Comprehension deficits in individual LHSS were often modulated by input modality, word frequency, and regularity.

CONCLUSIONS: We present a clinically accessible WtPM task that captures individual patterns of word comprehension impairment in both written and auditory modalities. The use of efficiency scores allows for the assessment of mild impairments that are missed by ceiling effects on currently available tasks. Input modality, frequency, and regularity affect word comprehension as measured by WtPM. Individual stroke survivors present with different combinations of these effects, which may help to identify specific deficits and spared abilities that can guide reading comprehension treatment.

SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL: https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.33968839.

articles.title: Child Neurology: Neonatal Management of Tyrosine Hydroxylase Deficiency: How Early Is Early Enough?
articles.abstract: Tyrosine hydroxylase deficiency is a rare, treatable, autosomal recessive disorder of monoamine neurotransmitter biosynthesis that typically presents in infancy or early childhood. Despite potential benefits of presymptomatic treatment with levodopa/carbidopa, prenatal or neonatal diagnosis remains extremely rare. We report 2 preterm neonates from unrelated families, both with known family history of tyrosine hydroxylase deficiency. After early diagnosis, levodopa/carbidopa therapy was initiated during the neonatal period. This proactive approach proved feasible and well tolerated, leading to early normalization of subtle motor abnormalities. These cases highlight the importance of early genetic diagnosis of this rare condition and the feasibility of levodopa/carbidopa treatment in neonates.

articles.title: Recanalization and Recurrent Stroke After Cervical Artery Dissection: Developing Appropriate Clinical Guidance?
Recanalization After Acute Cervical Artery Dissection: A Multicenter International Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The rates and factors associated with complete recanalization after cervical artery dissection (CeAD) have not been comprehensively quantified in large cohorts. We sought to determine the 6-month rate of complete recanalization in CeAD, clinical and imaging factors associated with recanalization, and risk of recurrent ischemic stroke based on recanalization status.

METHODS: This was a planned subanalysis of the Antithrombotic Treatment for Stroke Prevention in Cervical Artery Dissection study, a multicenter retrospective cohort including patients with imaging-confirmed CeAD diagnosed between January 2015 and June 2022 at 63 sites worldwide. For this analysis, we included 1,095 patients with single-vessel CeAD causing stenosis at presentation who had available follow-up vascular imaging at 6 months after CeAD. The primary outcome was complete recanalization within 6 months after CeAD. Clinical and imaging variables, as well as recurrent stroke, were compared between patients with and those without complete recanalization. Factors independently associated with complete recanalization were identified using multivariable logistic regression. Time to complete recanalization was analyzed using an accelerated failure time Weibull model.

RESULTS: Among 1,095 included patients (median age 45 years; 46.7% female), 634 (57.9%) achieved complete recanalization by 6 months. In multivariable analysis, each additional year of age was associated with lower odds of complete recanalization (odds ratio [OR] 0.97 per year; 95% CI 0.96-0.98; p < 0.001). Diabetes (OR 0.46; 95% CI 0.27-0.81; p = 0.006), active smoking (OR 0.69; 95% CI 0.50-0.95; p = 0.025), and complete occlusion at presentation (OR 0.44; 95% CI 0.32-0.59; p < 0.001) were independently associated with lower odds of complete recanalization. Complete occlusion at presentation was associated with both longer time to, and lower rates of, complete recanalization. We observed no effect of antithrombotic regimen (antiplatelet therapy vs anticoagulation) on complete recanalization. Incomplete recanalization was associated with a nonsignificant numerically higher proportion of recurrent stroke (5.4% vs 3.5%; p = 0.064).

DISCUSSION: Almost 60% of patients with CeAD achieved complete vessel recanalization by 6 months. Older age, diabetes, smoking, and complete occlusion at presentation were independently associated with incomplete recanalization. Further study is required to determine whether these findings may help guide tailored imaging surveillance and secondary prevention strategies.

articles.title: Associations of Antibodies Against Several Infections With Alzheimer Disease Neuropathology: A Prospective Cohort Study Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Associations of common infections with Alzheimer disease (AD) risk have been reported. A hypothesized mechanism for these is cerebral β-amyloid (Aβ) aggregation as a defense to infection. We studied whether serologic measures of several infections in the UK population are associated with measures of AD neuropathology.

METHODS: This prospective association study used data from the 1946 British birth cohort. Circulating antibodies against 14 pathogens, measured at age 60-64 years, were modelled as pathogen serostatus (indicating lifetime exposure to an agent), pathogen burden indices (measuring cumulative exposure to 2+ pathogens), and seroreactivity tertiles (indicating recent immunologic activity against pathogens). Associations of these were tested with plasma phosphorylated tau at threonine 217 (p-tau217) (primary outcome) and Aβ status (secondary outcome), measured with PET scans, at ages 69-71 years. Modelling used multivariable quantile and logistic regression. Model 1 adjusted for sex and ages at serology and outcome assessment, and models 2 and 3 additionally adjusted for APOE ε4 carriage and education, respectively. We also tested for interactions in associations by APOE ε4 carriage, education, and sex, and for interactions between herpes simplex virus 1 exposure with cytomegalovirus (CMV) and varicella zoster virus (VZV) exposure.

RESULTS: A total of 1,356 and 424 individuals had complete data for p-tau217 and Aβ-PET analyses, respectively. Mean age at p-tau217 was 69.9 years (SD 0.7), and 51.3% of participants were female. Median p-tau217 was 0.30 pg/mL (interquartile range 0.21-0.44). 28.3% had Aβ-positive scans. No notable associations were observed for serology measures with either outcome in main models, except for an unexpected association of herpes simplex virus 2 seropositivity with lower p-tau217 at the 75th quantile (-0.07 pg/mL in seropositive individuals; 95% CI -0.10 to -0.03). Odds of Aβ-PET positivity may have been higher for individuals seropositive for Epstein-Barr virus (odds ratio [OR] 2.84; 95% CI 0.95-8.52) and Toxoplasma gondii (OR 1.69; 95% CI 0.94-3.05). There were also potential interactions in p-tau217 associations by APOE ε4 carriage (for Helicobacter pylori and CMV) and educational attainment (for H pylori).

DISCUSSION: These findings do not imply associations between exposures to many common infections and AD neuropathologies. The possibility of pathogen interactions with APOE ε4 carriage and education in relation to AD neuropathology warrants further study.

articles.title: Infection as a Contributor to Dementia: The Plot Thickens.
Recommendations for the Management of Spontaneous Intracranial Hypotension With Spinal Longitudinal Epidural CSF Collection: A Delphi Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Spontaneous intracranial hypotension (SIH) results from spinal CSF leakage. Epidural blood patch (EBP) is an important first-line treatment. However, pre-EBP, intra-EBP, and post-EBP practice varies widely owing to limited consensus guidance. We aimed to develop expert consensus statements to support clinical decision-making in SIH management, including peri-EBP practices, focusing on patients with spinal longitudinal epidural CSF collection (SLEC) before definitive leak type classification.

METHODS: An international multidisciplinary Delphi process was conducted between January 2024 and July 2025, involving experts in neurology, neurosurgery, radiology, and anesthesiology. Consensus was defined a priori as ≥70% agreement for strong agreement, 60%-69% for partial agreement, and <60% for no consensus, based on a 5-point Likert scale in round 3. Responses were collected anonymously using an online survey platform, with summarized feedback from the previous round provided between rounds.

RESULTS: Fourteen experts were invited, with 10, 9, and 9 participants in rounds 1, 2, and 3, respectively. Before EBP, bed rest was recommended for recent-onset SIH with severe orthostatic headache (88.9%); other conservative methods such as abdominal binder and hydration were considered not mandatory (90%). Semitargeted EBP was recommended as initial management for patients with extradural CSF collections (70%). Dynamic CT myelography was preferred for localization (70%). Post-EBP care was variable, particularly in bed rest duration, with most recommendations (70%) exceeding 12 hours. Definitions of clinical remission (80%) and radiologic remission (90%) were established. Radiologic follow-up after clinical remission was recommended (78%). No consensus was reached on follow-up strategies for persistent symptoms, although "doing nothing" was not recommended. No consensus was reached for persistent extradural CSF despite clinical remission, requiring an individualized approach. Light activity after EBP was recommended within a few days (70%). No consensus was reached on the optimal number of EBPs before invasive leak localization or surgical intervention.

DISCUSSION: This Delphi study outlines expert recommendations and uncertainties for SIH management, including peri-EBP practices. This study incorporated the initial management strategy for patients in whom leak-type classification was incomplete. However, the treatment section primarily focused on the SLEC-positive setting and presumed ventral dural tears; lateral dural tears and CSF-venous fistulas warrant future consensus development.

articles.title: Bibliometrics and Thematic Content of the Papers Published in Neurology Over the Past 75 Years.
Incidence and Post-Stroke Survival in the Normandy Stroke Population-Based Study (2017-2022): Impact of Time-Based Versus Tissue-Based Definitions.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The 11th edition of the International Classification of Diseases (ICD-11) incorporates a tissue-based definition of stroke and may alter estimates of incidence and outcomes. We assessed whether transitioning from a time-based to a tissue-based definition introduces age-dependent changes in stroke incidence and post-stroke survival.

METHODS: The Normandy Stroke Study is a population-based study using multiple overlapping sources to identify stroke cases in Caen-Normandy-Metropole, France. Events occurring between May 15, 2017, and December 31, 2022, were classified using time-based (symptoms ≥24 hours) and tissue-based definitions (symptoms ≥24 hours or <24 hours with neuroimaging evidence of ischemic injury).

RESULTS: Among 3,826 first-ever strokes meeting the tissue-based definition, median (IQR) age was 76 (64-85) years, and 1,932 (50.5%) were female. The age-standardized incidence rate of stroke (95% CI) was 161 (156-166) per 100,000 person-years (ESP2013), including 132 (128-137) for ischemic or undetermined stroke, 22 (20-24) for intracerebral hemorrhage, and 7 (6-8) for subarachnoid hemorrhage. Three-year mortality was 36.4% (95% CI 34.9-38.0). Compared with the time-based definition, the tissue-based definition increased stroke incidence by 6.5% and reduced 3-year mortality by 3.9%. The impact of the tissue-based definition on stroke incidence was greater at younger ages (all strokes: younger than 55 years = +8.5%; 55 years or older = +6.0%; ischemic stroke: younger than 55 years = +12.5%; 55 years or older = +7.3%).

DISCUSSION: Adoption of a tissue-based definition modestly increased stroke incidence and post-stroke survival, with greater impacts at younger ages. Implementation of ICD-11 may introduce age-related differences in temporal trends, highlighting the importance of consistent definitions in stroke surveillance.

articles.title: FDA Approves a Second Weekly Basal Insulin Option for Type 2 Diabetes.
Intracerebral Hemorrhage Expansion in Late Presenters: Proposed Target Expansion Criteria.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The benefit of therapies targeting hematoma expansion (HE) in acute intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is highly time dependent and greatest within the first 2 hours after onset. We aimed to develop imaging-based "target expansion criteria" to identify late presenters (2-12 hours from onset/last seen well) who remain at high risk of HE. To achieve this goal, a practical risk score (target expansion score) was developed.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, international, retrospective cohort study. To mirror a clinical trial population, we excluded patients with brainstem ICH, anticoagulation, and baseline ICH volume >100 mL. The primary outcome was HE (>33%/6 mL). The following imaging predictors of HE were analyzed: high ultra-early hematoma growth (uHG) (baseline volume/onset to imaging time >10 mL/h), hypodensities on noncontrast CT (NCCT), and spot sign on CT angiography (CTA). The study population was randomly divided into development and validation cohorts, and a weighted score was derived from estimates from multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Overall, 492 patients were included: 345 (70.1%) in the development and 147 (29.9%) in the validation cohort. A 4-point score was created, based on independent predictors of HE (high uHG: 1 point, NCCT hypodensities: 1 point, and CTA spot sign: 2 points). The score showed good discrimination in the development and validation cohorts (area under the curve [AUC] 0.77, 95% CI 0.71-0.83, and AUC 0.79, 95% CI 0.71-0.87, respectively). We observed a nonlinear increase in the frequency of HE and mean absolute hematoma growth with higher scores: 9.8% and 0.9 mL (score 0), 17.1% and 3.9 mL (score 1), 48.3% and 11.5 mL (score 2), 70.8% and 13.0 mL (score 3), and 87.5% and 26.9 mL (score 4). These findings were confirmed in the validation cohort. A dichotomized score greater than or equal to 2 predicted HE with 0.61 sensitivity and 0.85 specificity in the development cohort and 0.64 sensitivity with 0.84 specificity in the validation cohort.

DISCUSSION: Imaging-based target expansion criteria, defined as a target expansion score ≥2, identified late-presenting patients with ICH at high risk of HE. These findings might inform future trials targeting HE and increase the pool of eligible patients.

articles.title: The Rural Hospital Crisis Is a Neurologic Crisis: Advancing Equity in Neurology.
See One.
Ecological drivers of Clostridioides difficile disease severity.
articles.abstract: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a common cause of antibiotic-associated diarrhea and arises from disruption of the resident microbiota in the gastrointestinal tract. Despite being a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, CDI presents as a wide spectrum of clinical manifestations, ranging from completely asymptomatic infection to severe and fulminant colitis. Recent research has revealed that CDI disease severity is influenced by the complex ecosystem of the gut, involving interactions between C. difficile, the host, and the resident gut microbiota. This review will summarize the current state of the field in understanding how the balance of interactions in the gut alters CDI disease severity using clinical data and mouse models of infection. In addition, external factors influencing these interactions, such as diet and pharmaceutical drugs, will be discussed. Ultimately, a comprehensive understanding of the ecological factors influencing patient outcome will be critical for the design of novel therapeutics for primary and recurrent CDI.

articles.title: Efficient colonic colonization by Campylobacter jejuni requires the heme receptor ChuA.
articles.abstract: Previous research demonstrated that Campylobacter jejuni encodes a heme utilization system that facilitates heme-dependent growth under iron-limiting conditions, and that transcription of this system is induced during human infection. Despite these observations, it remained unknown whether the heme transport system is required for colonization and disease in a susceptible host. To address this, we created individual non-polar deletion mutants of each component of the heme transport system and examined their ability to promote heme-dependent growth and iron uptake. From this work, we found that only the heme receptor, ChuA, was required for heme-dependent growth and iron acquisition, which supports the earlier work of another group. Furthermore, we examined whether intestinal colonization, immune activation, and pathology were altered during infection with these mutants. After establishing that elevated heme and chuABCD expression occur during C. jejuni infection of IL-10-/- mice, we found that a mutant of the heme receptor, ChuA, exhibited significantly reduced colonization of the colon. In addition, we found that neutrophil and circulating monocyte recruitment were significantly reduced in the colon during infection with the ChuA mutant, but that populations of self-maintaining tissue macrophages remained high. Loss of ChuA reduced colonic colonization and was accompanied by diminished innate immune cell recruitment and intestinal pathology. Together, these findings identify ChuA-dependent heme acquisition as a key determinant of efficient colonic colonization and the associated inflammatory disease.

articles.title: Coming Full Circle in Transcatheter Mitral Valve Intervention in MAC: Lessons From the ENCIRCLE Registry.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

articles.title: Transseptal Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement for Mitral Annular Calcification: ENCIRCLE MAC Registry 1-Year Outcomes.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with symptomatic mitral valve dysfunction (MVD) and mitral annular calcification (MAC) represent one of the most challenging populations in structural heart disease. Advanced age, multiple comorbidities, extensive annular calcification, and unfavorable anatomy often preclude surgical mitral valve replacement or transcatheter repair, leaving many patients with limited treatment options. Whether fully percutaneous transseptal transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) can provide a meaningful treatment pathway for patients with MAC-related MVD remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to evaluate 1-year clinical, echocardiographic, and patient-centered outcomes after transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system in patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD.

METHODS: The ENCIRCLE (SAPIEN M3 System Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement Via Transseptal Access) trial MAC Registry is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study that enrolled symptomatic patients with MAC-related MVD, including ≥ moderate to severe mitral regurgitation (MR), severe mitral stenosis, or combined moderate MR with at least moderate mitral stenosis, who were considered unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair. The primary endpoint was a nonhierarchical composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization (HFH) at 1 year.

RESULTS: Among 364 screened patients, TVMR was attempted in 100, and the valve was implanted in 93. Mean age was 76.1 ± 9.2 years, 51.0% were male, 73.0% were in NYHA functional class III/IV, and mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score for mitral valve replacement was 8.4% ± 4.9%. At 1 year, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of all-cause mortality or HFH was 33.6% (95% CI: 25.0%-44.1%), with 21.1% all-cause mortality and 19.4% HFH. Disabling stroke occurred in 5.1%, clinically significant left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in 4.8%, valve thrombosis in 2.3%, hemolysis requiring transfusion or mitral valve reintervention in 9.2%, and mitral valve re-intervention in 11.4%. Among implanted patients, MR ≤1+ was achieved in 98.5% at 1 year. Improvements in NYHA functional class, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score, and 6-minute walk distance were sustained through 1 year.

CONCLUSIONS: In carefully selected patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair, transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system was associated with sustained MR reduction and meaningful improvements in symptoms and quality of life through 1 year. These findings support consideration of transseptal TMVR as a treatment pathway for selected patients with MAC-related MVD.

articles.title: Disease Control in Generalized Myasthenia Gravis: Consensus Definition, Evolution, and Patient Characterization.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) is a chronic fluctuating neuromuscular disease. Some patients keep experiencing symptoms or adverse events (AEs) despite tailored therapeutic schemes. The aim of this study was to characterize adequately controlled gMG and describe patients' evolution and outcomes, including estimated direct health costs in a universal health care system.

METHODS: Spanish expert neurologists developed a definition of adequately controlled gMG using Delphi methodology. This was applied to an existing cohort of patients recently diagnosed with gMG during 1998-2020 in a Spanish referral neuromuscular diseases' unit. Control status, clinical outcomes, AEs, and health care resource utilization (HCRU) were described biennially.

RESULTS: We assessed 220 patients diagnosed with gMG (54.5% women; mean age at onset of 58 years; 84% anti-AChR, 6% anti-MuSK, 10% seronegative). Adequately controlled gMG was defined as achieving Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America Post-Intervention Status classification of clinical stable remission, pharmacologic remission, or minimal manifestations stable for a year; having an MG-ADL score ≤2; experiencing no clinical exacerbations during the last year requiring a change in immunosuppressive therapy or rescue therapy; and having no or mild AE to therapies (100% of experts in agreement or total agreement). The proportion adequately controlled (AC) patients increased from 62.0% at 2 years after first visit to 81.9% after 8 years of follow-up. 47.3% of patients remained AC in every observation, and 17.7% remained not adequately controlled (NC) in every observation. No features were significantly associated with adequate control. AE-related drug interruption rates were higher in NC patients (ranging from 50% to 100% during the study). The mean cost per patient/year ranged from 2,718.6€ in the first biennial period to 843.1€ in the last biennial period for AC patients and from 10,190.1€ to 5,827.4€ for NC patients.

DISCUSSION: Based on the new gMG control consensus definition, almost 1 in 5 patients do not reach disease control even after 8 years of evolution. Those patients lacked specific clinical features, underscoring the unpredictability of the gMG course. Burden of AE-related drug interruptions, HCRU, and costs per patients/year were higher among those patients NC. However, our study is unicentric and included patients from a referral unit, with a possible overrepresentation of NC patients.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary Approach to Antiplatelet Management in Coronary Syndromes: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
authors: American Heart Association Clinical Pharmacology Committee of the Council of Clinical Cardiology; Council on Cardiovascular and Stroke Nursing; Council on Cardiovascular Surgery and Anesthesia; and Council on Genomic and Precision Medicine
articles.abstract: Antiplatelet therapy is a cornerstone of care for patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease, yet its optimal use requires careful balancing of thrombotic risk reduction with bleeding complications. Since the mid-2000s, advances in stent technology, antiplatelet pharmacotherapy, procedural technique, and risk stratification tools have led to increasingly individualized approaches to antiplatelet management. Current guidelines and evidence emphasize tailoring agent selection, intensity, and duration of therapy according to patient-, procedure-, and disease-specific factors rather than a uniform strategy. However, the growing complexity of evidence, frequent care transitions, social determinants of health, and variability in patient characteristics have increased the risk of inappropriate prescribing, nonadherence, and adverse outcomes.
