Fields aligned along the traditional reaction axis impart only modest differential stabilization (0.5-1.0 kcal·mol-1), insufficient to reverse E/Z ratios except in nearly degenerate cases, whereas molecular-axis alignment boosts this difference to over 2 kcal·mol-1, reliably inverting selectivity by maximizing dipole overlap. To bridge theory and experiment, we have applied the gold-thiolate anchoring in our model, harnessing substrate polarization to amplify transition-state stabilization from roughly 5 kcal·mol-1 in the free system to over 20 kcal·mol-1 at higher field strengths. We further show, via isotropic field ensembles weighted by Boltzmann and von Mises-Fisher statistics, that even nonoriented fields can impose a stereochemical bias of at most 2.5 kcal·mol-1 through dipole torque. These findings establish dipole orientation as a quantitative predictor of EEF-mediated stereocontrol and provide concrete blueprints for deploying "invisible catalysts" in flow reactors, surface-confined assemblies, and microreactor platforms for reagent-free, on-demand synthesis of stereochemically defined molecules.

articles.title: Outcomes in the BETAMI-DANBLOCK trial compared with a Norwegian nationwide myocardial infarction population.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: In patients with myocardial infarction (MI), no heart failure, and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≥ 40%, the combined BETAMI-DANBLOCK trial showed that beta-blockers reduced the risk of all-cause mortality or major adverse cardiovascular events. This study evaluated the representativeness of the trial.

METHODS: Participants in BETAMI (n = 2867) and DANBLOCK (n = 2707) were compared with a cohort of revascularized MI patients with LVEF ≥40%, and no heart failure from the Norwegian Myocardial Infarction Registry (the NORMI cohort)(n = 20 804). Baseline characteristics were evaluated, and absolute risks of all-cause mortality and/or MI were estimated. A transportability analysis was conducted by weighting the BETAMI-DANBLOCK population according to the NORMI cohort.

RESULTS: Median age was 66 years (interquartile range [IQR]: 57-74) in the NORMI cohort and 63 years (IQR: 55-70) in BETAMI and DANBLOCK. Patients in the NORMI cohort had a higher prevalence of diabetes, previous coronary artery disease, and LVEF 40-49%, compared with trial participants. At 3-year follow-up, the absolute risk of all-cause mortality or MI was 12.0% in the NORMI cohort, 7.7% in BETAMI, and 7.8% in DANBLOCK. Corresponding risks of MI were 6.3%, 5.6%, and 4.3%, respectively. The treatment effects of beta-blockers were similar when the trial population was weighted according to the characteristics of the NORMI cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: Compared with the NORMI cohort, participants in BETAMI and DANBLOCK were younger, had a lower proportion of certain comorbidities, and experienced a lower risk of all-cause mortality and MI. Despite these differences, the effect of beta-blockers remained consistent when the trial population was weighted according to the NORMI cohort.

articles.title: Viral respiratory tract infections in heart failure: the FINEARTS-HF trial.
A nurse-coordinated intervention programme vs standard of care after an acute coronary syndrome: the ALLEPRE trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: There is a lack of long-term outcome data supporting the role of nurses in cardiovascular (CV) risk management. The ALLEPRE [ALLiance for sEcondary PREvention after an acute coronary syndrome (ACS)] trial was a pragmatic, randomized, multicentre, interventional trial comparing the efficacy of a nurse-coordinated prevention program (NCPP) with standard of care (SOC).

METHODS: The NCPP patients attended nine individual educational sessions over four years at which a centrally trained nurse provided counselling aimed at identifying CV risk factors and encouraging healthier lifestyles and medication adherence; the SOC patients followed the standard practices of their hospitals. The trial's primary endpoint was the composite of CV death, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), and non-fatal stroke (MACE).

RESULTS: A total of 2057 ACS patients were randomized 1:1 to the NCCP (n=1031) or SOC group (n=1026). In comparison with SOC, the NCPP significantly reduced MACE [16.2% vs 22.6%; hazard ratio (HR) 0.70; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.57-0.85; P-value <0.001], a benefit mainly driven by a reduction in non-fatal MI (9.3% vs 15.2%; HR 0.60; 95% CI 0.46-0.77; P-value=0.0001). The occurrence of the pre-specified secondary outcome of MACE plus ischaemia-driven revascularization was significantly reduced (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.64-0.92; P-value= 0.005). Exercise frequency (P<0.0001), body weight control (P=0.003), and medication adherence (P<0.001) improved more in the NCPP group.

CONCLUSIONS: The NCPP significantly reduced long-term MACE, improved physical activity, body weight control, and pharmacotherapy adherence in post-hospitalization ACS patients. Including an NCPP in healthcare provision may contribute to the successful implementation of secondary prevention strategies.

articles.title: Cardiovascular outcomes of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists: A systematic review.
articles.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To identify and evaluate cardiovascular outcome trials for glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP1RAs) in various patient populations, including those with or without type 2 diabetes (T2D).

SUMMARY: A systematic search of MEDLINE identified 12 cardiovascular outcome-based randomized controlled trials: 10 in patients with T2D, one in patients with overweight/obesity and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) but not T2D, and one in patients with obesity and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Most trials had a low risk of bias. The GLP1RA was administered as a weekly subcutaneous injection in 8 trials, and 2 trials used once-daily oral semaglutide. Follow-up ranged from 1.2 to 5.4 years. GLP1RA therapy showed a consistent reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with T2D. The effect on cardiovascular and all-cause death was less certain. Individually, only liraglutide demonstrated a reduction in MACE, cardiovascular death, and all-cause death. In patients with overweight/obesity and ASCVD (but without T2D), weekly subcutaneous semaglutide lowered the risk of MACE but not cardiovascular death. In patients with obesity and HFpEF (with or without T2D), tirzepatide lowered the occurrence of the composite endpoint of adverse heart failure events and cardiovascular death. Discontinuation of GLP1RA therapy due to gastrointestinal adverse events was common across the trials.

CONCLUSION: These data support the use of GLP1RAs to lower MACE in patients with T2D. A cardiovascular benefit with GLP1RA therapy was also observed in 2 additional patient populations: those with overweight/obesity and ASCVD but without T2D and those with obesity and HFpEF with or without T2D.

articles.title: Left bundle branch area vs biventricular pacing for cardiac resynchronization therapy: the LEFT-BUNDLE-CRT trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Conduction system pacing has emerged as an alternative to biventricular pacing (BiVP) for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). The left-bundle CRT trial evaluated whether left-bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is non-inferior to BiVP in patients eligible for CRT.

METHODS: The left-bundle CRT trial was a multi-centre, randomized, investigator-initiated, and non-inferiority study. Patients with guideline-based CRT indications and left-bundle branch block per Strauss criteria were randomized to BiVP-CRT or LBBAP-CRT. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients with a positive CRT response at 6-months, defined as either an improved clinical composite score (CCS) or a ≥15% reduction in left ventricular end-systolic volume. The non-inferiority margin was the lower bound of the 95% confidence interval (CI) and was set at 10%. Patients were followed for 12-months; secondary endpoints included echocardiographic, clinical, and quality-of-life outcomes.

RESULTS: The baseline characteristics of the 176 patients randomized to BiVP-CRT (n=84) or LBBAP-CRT (n=92) were similar, except for a wider intrinsic QRS in the LBBAP group: median 172 ms [IQR 158-184] vs. 165 ms [152-180]; P=0.04. Crossovers occurred in 26 patients (14.9%). In the intention-to-treat analysis, the primary endpoint was achieved in 94.6% of BiVP-CRT and 89.7% of LBBAP-CRT patients (RR 0.95; 95% CI 0.88-1.02), not meeting non-inferiority. CCS improved in 77% and 68% of patients randomized to BiVP-CRT and LBBAP-CRT, respectively and 85% and 79% had a ≥15% reduction in left ventricular end-systolic volume. Rates of adverse events and heart failure hospitalization were similar between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: In CRT candidates with typical LBBB, LBBAP-CRT was not shown to be non-inferior to BiVP-CRT. Both strategies yielded high response rates and similar clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Perioperative dapagliflozin in diabetic patients undergoing cardiac surgery: the DAPA-CS trial.
Sex differences in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: the FINE-HEART pooled analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: While the prevalence, drivers, and impact of cardiometabolic risk factors are known to differ between women and men, less is known about sex differences in the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome.

METHODS: In this prespecified analysis, individual participant-level data were pooled from two trials of chronic kidney disease and type 2 diabetes (FIDELIO-DKD and FIGARO-DKD) and a trial of heart failure (HF) with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction (FINEARTS-HF). The risk of first HF hospitalization, cardiovascular death, major adverse cardiovascular events, kidney composite outcome, and all-cause death, was compared between men and women using adjusted Cox regression models. Treatment effect heterogeneity in response to finerenone was evaluated using interaction analyses.

RESULTS: Of the 18 991 participants in FINE-HEART, 6664 (35%) were women. Compared with men, women were slightly older (69 vs 67 years) and had a lower median urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (183 vs 337 mg/g). Women were more likely to have Stage 4 CKM syndrome but less likely to receive medical therapies commonly indicated for the management of CKM conditions at baseline, such as aspirin, statins, renin-angiotensin system inhibitors, sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors, and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists. During a median follow-up of 2.9 years, both women and men had similarly high rates of HF hospitalization or cardiovascular death (4.8 vs 3.9 per 100 patient-years, adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0.97, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.89-1.06, P = .52) but lower risk of all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.76-0.91, P < .001) compared with men. There was no evidence of treatment heterogeneity by sex with finerenone in reducing cardiovascular, kidney, and mortality outcomes (all Pinteraction >.05).

CONCLUSIONS: In this pooled analysis of individuals with advanced CKM syndrome, women had a higher burden of multimorbidity and were less likely to receive commonly indicated CKM therapies than men. Finerenone conferred consistent benefits in women and men, reinforcing its use while underscoring persistent sex-based treatment disparities in CKM care.

REGISTRATION: PROSPERO identifier: CRD42024570467.

articles.title: E2F3 Transcriptionally Induces YWHAE to Activate Hepatic Stellate Cells and Drives Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease Progression.
articles.journal: The Tohoku journal of experimental medicine
articles.abstract: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a progressive liver disorder characterized by excessive hepatic lipid accumulation and fibrosis. This study explores the molecular mechanism by which E2F transcription factor 3 (E2F3) transcriptionally activates 14-3-3 protein epsilon (YWHAE), promoting hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation and contributing to NAFLD progression. Mice fed with a high-fat diet showed significantly elevated YWHAE expression in liver tissues. YWHAE knockdown mitigated hepatic steatosis, reduced lipid deposition, and attenuated fibrosis, as confirmed by histological staining and Western blot analysis of fibrosis and lipogenesis markers. Additionally, an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay indicated reduced serum levels of liver injury markers in YWHAE-deficient mice. In vitro, YWHAE knockdown in HSCs suppressed cell viability, migration, and activation, as assessed by cell counting kit-8, scratch assay, immunofluorescence, and reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Mechanistically, chromatin immunoprecipitation and luciferase reporter assays demonstrated that E2F3 bound to and enhanced YWHAE promoter activity, increasing its transcription. Furthermore, E2F3-mediated YWHAE activation promoted HSC activation and exacerbated NAFLD progression in vivo. These findings suggest that the E2F3-YWHAE axis may serve as a potential target for NAFLD treatment.

articles.title: Exploring ambulatory care pharmacists' beliefs and confidence in managing diabetes in perinatal women: A qualitative study guided by the Theory of Planned Behavior.
articles.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe ambulatory care pharmacists' beliefs and confidence in managing diabetes in perinatal women through guided interviews based on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB).

METHODS: This qualitative study consisted of a web-based presurvey and semistructured virtual interviews with ambulatory care pharmacists practicing at a federally qualified health center (FQHC) system to elicit salient beliefs about managing diabetes in perinatal women using the following TPB constructs: behavioral beliefs (BB), normative beliefs (NB), and control beliefs (CB). Descriptive statistics were conducted for quantitative data. Interviews were transcribed and analyzed by 2 independent researchers.

RESULTS: The pharmacist participants (N = 8) were all female and predominantly white (62.5%) and 35 to 44 years of age (87.5%). The majority (87.5%) were board certified in ambulatory care pharmacy, with 6 or more years of experience (75%). When the pharmacists were asked to rate the frequency of their involvement in managing diabetes in perinatal women in current or previous practice settings on a 5-point Likert scale (1 = never, 2 = rarely, 3 = sometimes, 4 = often, 5 = always), the mean (SD) score was 2.9 (1.1). When the pharmacists were asked to rate their confidence in their ability to manage diabetes in perinatal populations on a different Likert scale, the mean (SD) score of 3.8 (1.0) indicated a moderate level of confidence. Thirteen salient beliefs emerged (BB, n = 5; NB, n = 4; CB, n = 4), and pharmacists had positive BB, positive NB, and negative CB toward managing diabetes in perinatal women. "Improved patient outcomes" was the most prevalent BB. For NB, all participants expressed that patients would be in support of pharmacists managing their diabetes in pregnancy. For CB, restrictive collaborative practice agreements emerged as the most salient barrier.

CONCLUSION: Pharmacists who participated in this study were not routinely involved in perinatal diabetes management despite being moderately confident in their ability to provide such services, having positive BB, and believing their patients would be supportive. Pharmacists had negative CB, and future interventions can focus on addressing these barriers.

articles.title: Malakoplakia beyond the bladder: Clinicopathologic characterization of genitourinary involvement at uncommon sites.
articles.abstract: Malakoplakia is a chronic granulomatous condition, presenting as a plaque-like lesion affecting the urinary bladder in immunocompromised patients. Extravesical involvement within the genitourinary tract is even rarer and may mimic malignancy on imaging, posing diagnostic challenges. Here we present a case series of unsuspected extravesical malakoplakia in biopsies and resections performed for various clinical reasons. A retrospective analysis of our database from 2022 to 2025 retrieved seven cases of extravesical malakoplakia. The cohort included 7 specimens from 6 patients (3 males, 3 females; age range 40-67 years). Five of the 6 patients had a history of kidney transplantation, of which 1 was a resection of the transplanted kidney performed for graft failure and intolerance secondary to recurrent urinary tract infections. All transplant patients presented with acute kidney injury. The 2 remaining specimens were from a 63-year-old male with muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma and presented with left epididymorchitis suspicious for abscess. A subsequent orchiectomy revealed malakoplakia, and cystoprostatectomy showed known high-grade invasive urothelial carcinoma in the bladder and malakoplakia in the prostate. All specimens demonstrated sheets of von Hansemann cells with characteristic Michaelis-Gutmann bodies (MGB). The diagnosis of Malakoplakia was crucial in opting for conservative management such as modification of immunosuppression and prolonged antibiotic therapy. Malakoplakia remains a histopathologic diagnosis that is often unsuspected clinically, especially in extravesical sites. In this limited institutional case series, it was incidentally identified and demonstrates the diagnostic value of recognizing this entity to guide appropriate management, especially in immunocompromised patients.

articles.title: Molecular signatures associated with reduced renal function in aortic regurgitation and aortic stenosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) accelerates aortic valve (AV) disease, yet the molecular pathways linking declining renal function to aortic regurgitation (AR) and aortic stenosis (AS) remain poorly defined. We aimed to characterize AV phenotype-specific molecular signatures associated with reduced renal function.

METHODS: We performed an observational cross-sectional study using targeted proteomic profiling (Olink) in human AV from patients with AR or AS, stratified by renal function (eGFR≥60 vs < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2). Pathway enrichment analyses were performed using exploratory candidate proteins. Candidate molecular signatures were subsequently examined in independent cohorts (AR: n = 215; AS: n = 325) across renal function categories using histology, immunohistochemistry, ELISA, and qPCR.

RESULTS: Reduced renal function was associated with distinct molecular patterns in AR and AS. In AR, exploratory proteomic profiling suggested enrichment of neutrophil degranulation, chemotaxis/adhesion and thrombo-inflammatory signaling pathways. Tissue characterization showed progressive extracellular matrix remodeling, collagen maturation, increased neutrophil markers (NGAL, MPO) and upregulation of pro-inflammatory (IL6, IL-8, IL-32, IL-33, CCL-2, TNF-α, RANTES), pro-adhesive (ICAM-1) and pro-thrombotic mediators (PAI-1) across renal function categories. In AS, exploratory proteomics suggested matrix disassembly and osteogenic signatures, while tissue characterization showed greater valvular calcification (BMP-2, -4, -9), collagen degradation (COL1, MMP-1, -3, TIMP-1) and inflammatory infiltration with declining renal function. Shared candidate proteins showed opposite regulation in AR and AS.

CONCLUSIONS: Reduced renal function is associated with distinct, phenotype-specific patterns of AV remodeling-predominantly thrombo-inflammatory in AR and osteogenic-matrix-disruptive in AS- indicating heterogeneous molecular responses across the two major forms of aortic valve disease.

articles.title: Determination of the Discordance Rate Between the CKD-EPI eGFRcr-cys Equation and Measured 8-Hour Urinary Creatinine Clearance.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology (CKD-EPI) estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) equations are recommended over Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance, but preference compared to measured urinary creatinine clearance (mCrCL) is less certain. Both eGFR and mCrCL have unique advantages and limitations. Serum creatinine (SCr) and cystatin C (cysC) based eGFR (eGFRcr-cys) and 8-hour measured urinary creatinine clearance (mCrCL8) have yet to be compared in acutely ill patients.

OBJECTIVE: The primary objective of this study was to determine the discordance rate between eGFRcr-cys and mCrCL8 estimations of kidney function in hospitalized patients. Discordance rate was defined as the overall percentage of patients in which there was a 30% or greater difference between eGFRcr-cys and mCrCL8.

METHODS: This was a single-center, retrospective, observational cohort study of adults admitted between 1/1/2023 and 8/31/2025 with SCr and cysC ordered within 72-hours of mCrCL8. Data was collected via chart review; eGFRcr-cys was adjusted for individual patient body surface area to mL/min for mCrCL8 comparison. Demographic data was analyzed via descriptive statistics. Statistical analysis was performed by Fisher's exact test for nominal data, T-test for normally distributed data and Mann-Whitney U test for non-normally distributed data.

RESULTS: The study included 74 patients (95.9% critically ill, 47.3% female; median age 50 [34.5-67.5] years) with a median SCr 0.60 [0.43-1.05] mg/dL and cysC 1.29 [0.96-2.31] mg/L. Median eGFRcr-cys was 75.1 [49.3-117.4] mL/min and mCrCL8 was 94.8 [43.6-160.9] mL/min. The discordance rate was 59.5%. Discordance was oftentimes resultant from mCrCL8 being higher than eGFRcr-cys (63.6% of the discordant cases).

CONCLUSION: The eGFRcr-cys was discordant with mCrCL8 in 59.5% of predominately ICU patients. Discordance was usually a result of mCrCL8 estimating higher than eGFRcr-cys. Additional studies are needed to definitively discern clinical scenarios where 1 type of kidney function estimation approach is preferred over another.

articles.title: Computerised cognitive training combined with nutritional counseling in mild cognitive impairment - results of a 2 × 2 factorial randomized controlled trial (BrainFit-nutrition study).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Computerized cognitive training (CCT) and nutritional interventions may improve cognitive functioning in individuals with mild cognitive impairment (MCI). This study investigated whether a combination of CCT and online nutritional counseling can improve global cognition in individuals with MCI. We also evaluated differences between MCI-specified and active control versions of the interventions.

METHODS: In this 2 × 2 factorial randomized controlled trial (BrainFit-Nutrition study), conducted fully remotely, participants in Germany with a psychometric diagnosis of MCI (age 60+) were randomized into four groups (Intention to treat, n = 270). For each intervention, one MCI specified and one active control version were developed (cognition: individualized CCT (iCCT) vs. basic CCT (bCCT); nutrition: whole-food plant-based nutrition (WFPB) vs. German Nutrition Society (DGE)). At baseline and after six months, cognitive functioning was assessed with the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA; primary outcome: change after six months). A mixed-model ANCOVA (t0-t6, complete case strategy (CC), n = 228) was applied for the main analysis.

RESULTS: All four groups achieved a significant improvement of approximately 2 points on the MoCA after six months. Estimated marginal means varied from M = 2.44 (iCCTxDGE) to M = 1.77 (iCCTxWFPB), notably without significant group differences. The 2 × 2 mixed ANCOVA revealed a significant main effect of time (F = 3.96, p = 0.048, partial η2 = 0.018). The specific content of the respective modalities being compared (iCCT vs. bCCT; WFPB vs. DGE-oriented counseling) did not appear to make a relevant group difference with regard to the primary outcome. After 6 months, 55% of all participants reached non-MCI values on the MoCA.

CONCLUSION: The results of this study suggest, that in people with MCI, notable improvement in global cognition can be achieved in a six-months intervention period. When CCT is combined with digital nutritional counseling, the form of intervention - whether elaborate or basic - apparently did not modify the outcome; rather, this data set suggests that it is worthwhile to proactively undertake something in both domains. Future clinical studies in mixed-methods-designs, including usual-care comparators, basic science study modules, qualitative aspects and health economic variables are warranted to gain a better understanding of mechanisms, sustainability of effects, clinical relevance, and cost-effectiveness.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ISRCTN10560738; registered 11/23/2021.

articles.title: Liver cancer incidence trends in younger versus older adults over time: an analysis of population-based cancer registry data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver cancer epidemiology is evolving, yet age-specific patterns remain poorly characterized. We aimed to assess variation in age-specific liver cancer incidence trends based on population-based cancer registry data.

METHODS: We extracted annual liver cancer incidence (1978-2017) for 47 countries from Cancer Incidence in Five Continents Plus. Age-standardized incidence rates (ASRs) were compared over time and over the most recent decade for three age-groups (15-49, 50-69, 70 +) using Estimated Annual Percentage Change (EAPC) in 38 populations.

FINDINGS: From 1978-2017, ASRs declined in high-incidence countries in Eastern and South-Eastern Asia but increased in low-incidence countries across Northern America, Australia/New Zealand, and Northern Europe. During 2008-2017, ASRs among younger adults (15-49) declined in 11 of 38 male populations (EAPC -10.0% in France) and in females in the Republic of Korea (-3.7%) and China (-2.6%). In older adults (50-69 and 70 +), ASRs declined in high-incidence countries (Republic of Korea, Japan, China) during 2008-2017, while increasing in 15 male populations and 11 female populations (age 50-69) and in 12 male populations and 10 female populations (age 70 +), mostly in Northern and Western Europe and Northern America. Overall, trends in hepatocellular carcinoma and cholangiocarcinoma were heterogeneous across countries, with interpretation limited by substantial variation in histologically unspecified cases.

INTERPRETATION: Rising liver cancer rates among older adults in historically low-incidence countries might suggest a shift from infectious to noncommunicable causes. In contrast, declines in younger adults in historically high-incidence countries may signal the positive impact of hepatitis and aflatoxin control. Strengthened, targeted prevention remains essential to prevent liver cancer globally.

articles.title: Design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel Nav1.2 inhibitors as antiepileptic agents.
articles.abstract: Voltage-gated sodium channel Nav1.2 is a validated target for anticonvulsant therapy, yet Nav1.2 inhibitors remain scarce. To explore the unexplored N-4 position of the [1,2,4]triazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine scaffold, we designed and synthesized two series of novel derivatives bearing diverse substituents at this position. Their Nav1.2 inhibitory activities were evaluated using FLIPR membrane potential and whole-cell patch-clamp assays, while their anticonvulsant efficacy and neurotoxicity were assessed in MES/ sc-PTZ seizure models and rotarod test, respectively. Structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis revealed that hydrophobic volume complementarity, rather than aromaticity, is the primary driver of Nav1.2 potency. Compound 3b, bearing a simple n-butyl group at N-4, emerged as the most promising lead, exhibiting moderate Nav1.2 inhibition (88.9% at 30 μM; FLIPR IC50 = 11.55 μM; patch-clamp IC50 = 7.62 μM for the inactivated state) and exceptional in vivo efficacy (ED50 = 9.17 mg/kg, TD50 > 813.40 mg/kg, PI >88.70) in the sc-PTZ model. Compound 3y also demonstrated moderate Nav1.2 inhibition (69.8%, IC50 = 12.19 μM) and potent anticonvulsant activity (ED50 = 13.7 mg/kg, PI >23.1). Patch-clamp electrophysiology confirmed that 3b and 3y inhibit the inactivated state of Nav1.2 (IC50 = 7.62 μM and 8.31 μM, respectively) with negligible effect on the resting state. Molecular docking and MD simulations revealed that 3b binds within the Nav1.2 pore via hydrogen bonds, π-π stacking, and hydrophobic contacts. Tissue distribution studies demonstrated efficient blood-brain barrier penetration (brain-to-plasma ratio of 1.65 at 1 h post-dose). Although 3b showed limited stability in human and rat liver microsomes (T1/2 = 12.20 and 10.65 min, respectively), its potent in vivo efficacy and exceptionally high protective index support its continued optimization and preclinical development as a promising candidate for epilepsy therapy.

articles.title: Predictive value of Lung Ultrasound Score for CPAP failure and mechanical ventilation among preterm neonates: a retrospective single-centre cohort study in Jordan.
Cognitive Behavioural Therapy to Optimize Post-Operative Fracture Recovery (COPE): a randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: CMAJ : Canadian Medical Association journal = journal de l'Association medicale canadienne
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent pain after extremity fracture requiring surgical repair is common and associated with long-term morbidity. We sought to determine whether app-based cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) reduces persistent postsurgical pain after fracture repair.

METHODS: We performed a randomized controlled trial of adults from 11 American and Canadian hospitals with an extremity fracture treated with internal fixation. We allocated participants 1:1 to an app-based CBT program or usual care, and followed them at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months post-fracture. Our primary outcome was moderate-to-severe persistent post-surgical pain. We constructed a mixed-effects log-binomial model to explore the effect of CBT versus usual care on moderate-to-severe persistent post-surgical pain over 12 months postfracture.

RESULTS: We randomized 1009 participants to app-based CBT (n = 506) or usual care (n = 503). The mean age of participants was 44.5 years, and 129 (12.8%) presented with an open fracture. Adherence to CBT was modest, with 237/506 patients (46.8%) completing all 7 modules. App-based CBT, compared with usual care, did not reduce the risk of persistent postsurgical pain over 12 months postfracture (30.8% v. 30.3%, adjusted relative risk 1.02, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.89 to 1.16). The 365-day probability of returning to leisure activities without restrictions was 29.0% in the intervention group and 22.4% in the control group (hazard ratio 1.33, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.77). The other secondary outcomes showed no significant differences between treatments.

INTERPRETATION: Among adults with an operatively managed extremity fracture, app-based CBT did not reduce the risk of persistent postsurgical pain over 12 months. Future research is warranted to develop more effective CBT approaches for adults with extremity fractures and to evaluate alternative supportive interventions that may be more acceptable to patients with fracture.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04274530.

articles.title: Risk Factors for Gout Flares After Urate-Lowering Therapy: A Nationwide Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gout is an inflammatory arthritis caused by the monosodium urate crystal deposition in joints, with some patients experiencing recurrent flares. This study compared the clinical characteristics of patients who experienced gout flares with those who did not.

METHODS: Data were analyzed from the Urate Lowering TheRApy in Gout registry, including adults aged ≥ 18 years who met the 2015 American College of Rheumatology/European League Against Rheumatism gout classification criteria. Patients were designated into flare or no-flare groups based on the occurrence of at least one gout flare within the first 6 months.

RESULTS: Among 327 patients, 29.0% experienced at least one gout flare within 6 months. Compared with the no-flare group, patients with flares had higher gout impact scale (P = 0.019) and EuroQoL 5-Dimension 3-Level scores (P = 0.012), and more frequent bone erosion (P < 0.001), and tophi (P = 0.031). Multivariate logistic regression showed that radiographic bone erosion (P = 0.013) and poorer quality of life (gout impact scale, P = 0.037; EuroQoL 5-Dimension 3-Level scores, P = 0.014) were independently associated with increased gout flare risk. Fewer patients in the flare group achieved target serum urate levels at 6 months (P = 0.006).

CONCLUSION: Impaired quality of life, and radiographic evidence of bone erosion were identified as independent risk factors for gout flare in this prospective cohort study. These findings highlight the importance of comprehensive clinical assessment to identify high-risk patients for future flares and optimize individualized management strategies.

articles.title: Elevated Risk of Bladder Cancer Associated With Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in Elderly Korean Men: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) is one of the major metabolic disorders associated with various extrahepatic malignancies. Although growing evidence suggests a link between SLD and bladder cancer, the precise nature of this relationship remains unclear. The goal of our study was to explore the relationship between SLD subtypes and the risk of bladder cancer in elderly Korean men.

METHODS: This nationwide population-based cohort study utilized data from South Korean men aged 65 years and older, collected from 2009 to 2010. The subdistribution hazard ratios (SHRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were evaluated using the Fine and Gray regression model, with all-cause mortality considered as a competing event. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was applied to the SLD and non-SLD groups to create a pseudo-population, enabling a more unbiased evaluation. Overall, the bladder cancer incidence was compared across the SLD and non-SLD groups.

RESULTS: Among 89,903 Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) participants, 1,048 bladder cancer cases were identified, compared to 935 in 84,111 non-SLD participants after IPTW (1.17% vs. 1.11%). In MASLD with increased alcohol intake (MetALD) group, 456 cases were found among 61,709 individuals, versus 578 in 51,765 non-SLD participants (0.74% vs. 1.12%). In this cohort, MASLD revealed an association with a greater risk of bladder cancer (aHR, 1.11; 95% CI, 1.01-1.21; P = 0.027), whereas MetALD showed a decreased risk (aHR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.59-0.76; P < 0.001). The risk was more pronounced in individuals aged < 75 years and in those who engaged in moderate-to-vigorous physical activity.

CONCLUSION: MASLD was associated with an increased risk of bladder cancer, and this association remained significant among never smokers after excluding cases within 3 years.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes of Community-Onset and Hospital-Onset Sepsis Patients: The Korean Nationwide Sepsis Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis is a major global health concern with high morbidity and mortality. To address this burden in Korea, the Korean Sepsis Alliance established a nationwide registry to characterize community-onset and hospital-onset sepsis, to identify risk factors for mortality, and to assess the association between sepsis bundle compliance and mortality.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, prospective cohort study including adult patients with sepsis or septic shock enrolled in the Korean Sepsis Alliance registry from September 2019 to December 2023. A total of 17,246 patients from 15 geographically diverse tertiary or university-affiliated hospitals were included. Sepsis was defined according to the Sepsis-3 criteria. Clinical characteristics, infection sites, microbiological profiles, compliance with sepsis bundles, and outcomes were compared between patients with community-onset sepsis and hospital-onset sepsis. Multivariable Cox regression analysis was performed to identify factors independently associated with 28-day mortality.

RESULTS: Among the 17,246 enrolled patients, 14,600 (84.7%) had community-onset sepsis and 2,646 (15.3%) had hospital-onset sepsis. The incidence of sepsis in the whole cohort was 322.80 per 100,000, including 722.21 per 100,000 for community-onset sepsis and 79.68 per 100,000 for hospital-onset sepsis. Overall hospital mortality was 29.9%, with a higher rate observed in hospital-onset sepsis (36.9%) than in community-onset sepsis (28.7%, P < 0.001). Patients with hospital-onset sepsis had multiple comorbidities, greater sepsis severity, and infections caused by multi-drug-resistant organisms. Pulmonary infections were the most frequent source in both groups. Independent risk factors for 28-day mortality included hospital-onset sepsis, advanced age, poor performance status, comorbidities, septic shock, bloodstream infection, higher Sequential Organ Failure Assessment scores, and respiratory or systemic infections without an identifiable source. Compliance of the 1-, 3-, and 6-hour sepsis bundles was significantly associated with reduced 28-day mortality in both groups.

CONCLUSION: This study presents the first nationwide data on the epidemiology of community-onset and hospital-onset sepsis in Korea. Compliance with time-based sepsis bundles was associated with lower mortality. These findings underscore the need for standardized sepsis care and government policies to enhance early recognition and timely management of sepsis in Korea.

articles.title: Untargeted Metabolomic Analysis of Acute Kidney Injury After Maze-Inclusive Cardiac Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The maze procedure is considered as the standard surgical treatment for atrial fibrillation and might be an independent risk factor for postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI). This study aimed to investigate the metabolic alterations associated with AKI following maze-inclusive cardiac surgery using untargeted metabolomics.

METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 50 patients who underwent the maze procedure with concomitant cardiac surgery. AKI was diagnosed as an absolute increase in serum creatinine level of ≥ 0.3 mg/dL from baseline within 48 hours, or a ≥ 50% increase in serum creatinine within 7 days after surgery. Plasma samples were collected in operation and 24 hours after surgery, and untargeted metabolomic analysis was performed. Differential metabolites were identified and subjected to pathway enrichment analysis. Clinical variables and related metabolites were analyzed to elucidate relationship with AKI.

RESULTS: The concomitant surgeries were valve surgeries in 37 patients, followed by coronary artery (8 patients), and aorta (5 patients). Postoperative AKI occurred in 23 patients (46%). Metabolomic profiling revealed upregulation of tryptophan metabolism in AKI patients, with five candidate metabolites implicated. Among them, kynurenic acid exhibited the most significant metabolite associated with AKI, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.93. Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified kynurenic acid as independent possible predictors of AKI.

CONCLUSION: Tryptophan metabolism is significantly upregulated in patients with AKI after maze-inclusive cardiac surgery. Kynurenic acid presumed in this study represents as candidate metabolite of postoperative AKI, providing an opportunity to gain insight into the underlying pathophysiology through further targeted metabolomics.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Research Information Service Identifier: KCT0011192.

articles.title: FGF2-engineered extracellular vesicles loaded in an ECM-mimetic hydrogel promote wound healing and attenuate scar formation via immunomodulation and enhanced neurovascular responses.
articles.abstract: Impaired wound healing in diabetes is primarily driven by persistent inflammation and neurovascular dysfunction, frequently leading to aberrant tissue remodeling and pathological scarring. Extracellular vesicles of adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (ADSC-EVs) have therapeutic potential but limited tissue-specific efficacy. Fibroblast growth factor 2 (FGF2) promotes angiogenesis and nerve repair but suffers from a short half-life that limits its clinical application. Given the low endogenous expression of FGF2 in ADSCs and its short half-life in vivo, here, we engineered FGF2-functionalized EVs (EV-FGF2) by lentiviral transduction of ADSCs and incorporated them into a click chemistry-crosslinked recombinant collagen/hyaluronic acid hydrogel (CH/EV-FGF2) to enable sustained release and extracellular matrix-mimetic support. In vitro, EV-FGF2 promoted macrophage polarization toward a reparative M2 phenotype, enhanced angiogenesis and axonal outgrowth. In vivo, the CH/EV-FGF2 hydrogel accelerated wound closure in a diabetic mouse wound model, attenuated early inflammation, increased vascular (CD31) and neuronal (βIII-tubulin/Tuj1) markers, promoted neurovascular-associated responses, and attenuated scar formation in a rabbit ear model. In conclusion, this study developed an engineered EV-FGF2 hydrogel system that addresses multiple pathological aspects of diabetic wounds, offering a promising cell-free therapeutic strategy for tissue repair.

articles.title: A sequentially verified dual-lock near-infrared fluorescent probe for imaging lysosomal H2O2/microviscosity dynamics during radiotherapy and STING agonist sensitization.
articles.abstract: Low-dose fractionated radiotherapy is widely used to limit normal tissue damage, yet repeated low-dose irradiation can remodel the tumour microenvironment in ways that impair antitumour immunity and reduce radioimmunotherapy efficacy. Importantly, this immunological outcome coincides with dynamic inflammatory reprogramming at cellular and subcellular levels. Inflammatory status thus provides a mechanistic link between radiotherapy-induced microenvironmental changes and treatment efficacy, but real-time tools to track these fluctuations are still scarce. Here we present Lyso-SCMU-H2O2, a lysosome-targeted near-infrared fluorescent probe for high-fidelity imaging of therapy-related inflammatory dynamics via a dual-lock AND logic gate responsive to H2O2 and microviscosity. In this design, H2O2-induced boronate cleavage relieves photoinduced electron transfer (PeT) quenching, and high viscosity subsequently inhibits twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT) decay, enabling excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT) to produce a large-Stokes-shift NIR signal. This ordered dual validation reduces false positives and improves signal clarity in complex biological settings. Spectroscopic and cellular assays confirmed the stringent dual-lock mechanism, precise lysosomal localisation, and strong response to endogenous inflammatory activation. Using this platform, we observed that repeated 2 Gy irradiation progressively weakened lysosomal inflammatory signalling, and after five fractions, tumour-cell survival increased significantly. In contrast, adding the STING agonist MSA-2 restored the inflammatory fluorescence response and markedly enhanced antitumour efficacy both in vitro and in vivo. These results establish Lyso-SCMU-H2O2 as a high-contrast molecular imaging tool for linking radiotherapy-induced inflammatory remodelling to immune-related outcomes and for guiding more effective radioimmunotherapy strategies.

articles.title: Portal and hepatic vein thrombosis in Philadelphia-negative myeloproliferative neoplasms: Insights from the National Inpatient Sample.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Philadelphia-negative myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) are strongly associated with splanchnic vein thrombosis (SVT), but population-level data describing portal and hepatic vein thrombosis across MPN subtypes and associated hepatic morbidity are limited.

METHODS: We analyzed adult hospitalizations involving polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia or primary myelofibrosis in the 2016-2022 National Inpatient Sample. Portal or hepatic vein thrombosis was required among the first three diagnosis positions, with an any-position sensitivity analysis. Survey-weighted comparisons and multivariable logistic regression evaluated inpatient outcomes; hepatic comparisons were repeated after excluding hospitalizations with coded cirrhosis.

RESULTS: Among 181,818 unweighted MPN hospitalizations, 1217 (0.67%) had qualifying SVT. SVT hospitalizations involved younger patients and proportionally more polycythemia vera. Portal hypertension (30.3% vs. 0.8%) and esophageal varices (21.4% vs. 0.4%) were more frequent with SVT. Among hospitalizations without coded cirrhosis, the corresponding survey-weighted proportions were 20.2% versus 0.33% and 12.7% versus 0.15%. No statistically significant association with in-hospital mortality was detected using the first-three-diagnosis definition (aOR 1.02, 95% CI 0.68-1.54); the any-position analysis yielded an OR of 1.38 (95% CI 1.01-1.90).

CONCLUSIONS: Hepatic and portal-hypertensive morbidity represents a substantial component of the clinical burden associated with MPN-related SVT, even in the absence of coded cirrhosis. These findings underscore the importance of recognizing hepatic complications in the management of MPN-associated SVT.

articles.title: Colorectal Cancer Incidence in the US Versus Canada, Among Individuals Aged 45 to 49 Years, Following US Expansion of Screening Eligibility.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine the differences in colorectal cancer (CRC) incidence between the US and Canada, among individuals aged 45 to 49 years, following expansion of screening eligibility in the US.

METHODS: This is an ecological analysis based on publicly available data for CRC incidence in the US and Canada. US data were based on the US Cancer Statistics Public Use Research Database, while the Canadian data were based on Statistics Canada tables (which represented all Canadian jurisdictions except for Nova Scotia). Descriptive analyses for cancer incidence rates per 100,000 among individuals aged 45 to 49 years were performed for Canada versus the US, with stratification performed for age group, sex, and subsite. Subsequently, a difference-in-differences (DiD) analysis was performed to further examine the differences between the US and Canada.

RESULTS: Colorectal cancer rates per 100,000 (2016 to 2023) for individuals aged 45 to 49 years increased in Canada from 30.6 (2016) to 34 (2023), while in the US, rates increased from 34.9 (2016) to 53.1 (2023). For the US data, when calculating the percentage of localized disease out of all patients with known stages, this increased from 28.5% in 2016 to 40.8% in 2023. Furthermore, comparing US versus Canadian data and using pre- versus postexpansion policy means in both countries, DiD was 12.85 (95% CI: 10.13-15.57, P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Expansion of CRC screening eligibility in the US was associated with a significant increase in reported CRC incidence in the US versus Canada, among individuals 45 to 49 years old, which was principally driven by increasing rates of localized-stage diagnoses.

articles.title: Letter to the Editor Regarding "Prophylactic Subcutaneous Heparin Is Not Associated With Increased Rates of Hematoma, Pulmonary Embolism, or Deep Vein Thrombosis Following Lumbar Fusion".
Remote patient management reduces liver-related hospitalizations in patients with acutely decompensated cirrhosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with decompensated cirrhosis experience frequent hospitalizations, yet evidence supporting remote post-discharge care remains limited. This study assessed the impact of cirrhosis-specific Remote Patient Management (CiRPM) program following hospitalization for acutely decompensated (AD) cirrhosis.

METHODS: Adults hospitalized for AD cirrhosis were included in a three-cohort observational study comparing CiRPM (2021-2024) with contemporary (C-control) and historical controls (H-control, 2018-2019). CiRPM enabled vital-sign and symptom transmission with 24/7 virtual nursing support. Subgroup analyses were conducted by disease etiology, CLIF-C AD score, and decompensation type. IPTW was used to adjust for confounding, and time-to-event outcomes were analyzed using Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: Among 430 patients (156 CiRPM, 152 H-control, 122 C-control), mean age was 59 years, 65% had alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD), CLIF-C AD score of 56. CiRPM was associated with lower 90-day liver-related readmissions versus C-control (39% vs. 58%; HR 0.57, p=0.01) and a similar trend versus H-control (39% vs. 52%; HR 0.67, p=0.07). Associations were stronger among patients with CLIF-C AD ≥60 (HR 0.43 vs. H-control, p=0.005; HR 0.51 vs. C-control, p=0.02). Among ALD patients, fewer fluid-related readmissions (OR 0.40 and 0.37; both p<0.001) and recurrent hospitalizations (OR 0.51; p=0.001 and p=0.002) were observed in the CiRPM group. In non-ALD patients, hepatic encephalopathy readmissions were lower (OR 0.29, p=0.004; OR 0.36, p=0.02). Mortality did not differ across groups.

CONCLUSION: CiRPM enrollment was associated with fewer liver-related hospitalizations, particularly among patients with ALD and CLIF-C AD ≥60, supporting targeted remote management as a scalable post-discharge strategy for this high-risk population.

articles.title: FAST Performance Changes After a Training Sequence Including Augmented Reality Guidance Among Paramedic Students.
articles.journal: Simulation in healthcare : journal of the Society for Simulation in Healthcare
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Point-of-care ultrasound is an essential diagnostic tool in emergency medicine. Among its applications, Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma (FAST) is a rapid imaging method used in initial trauma evaluation. Augmented reality (AR) may provide visual guidance during procedural learning. This study examined changes in FAST performance following a short-term training sequence that included AR-assisted guidance among paramedic students.

METHODS: An interventional study was conducted with 18 undergraduate paramedic students who participated in a two-hour program consisting of a 60-minute lecture and a 60-minute hands-on session. Each participant performed four FAST examinations: 2 conventional and 2 AR-assisted. The primary outcome was total FAST performance time; secondary outcomes were the time for each view and the Quality of Ultrasound Imaging and Competence score, including the Task-Specific Checklist and Global Rating Scale.

RESULTS: The median total FAST time was significantly reduced after the training sequence (difference: 263.5 s; 95% CI: 177-352.5; P<0.001). Significant time reductions were observed in the pericardial, Morison's pouch, and perisplenic views, but not in the Douglas pouch view. Both Task-Specific Checklist and Global Rating Scale scores improved significantly (both P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Improvements in procedural efficiency and technical performance were observed after a short training sequence that included AR-assisted guidance for FAST among paramedic students. Given the fixed examination sequence and absence of a parallel control group, these findings should be interpreted cautiously.

articles.title: Concurrent tropical pulmonary eosinophilia and allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis in asthma: a prospective observational study from a filariasis-endemic region.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Tropical pulmonary eosinophilia (TPE) and allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA) share cough, wheeze, eosinophilia, and marked immunoglobulin (Ig) E elevation and may coexist in patients with asthma in filariasis-endemic settings. We prospectively characterized this overlap phenotype at a tertiary respiratory center in eastern India. Eligible patients older than 10 years had a documented prior physician diagnosis of asthma and, at presentation, an absolute eosinophil count (AEC) >1000 cells/µL and total IgE >1000 IU/mL; all underwent evaluation for both TPE and ABPA. These laboratory thresholds were study-entry criteria and were not substituted for disease-specific diagnostic definitions. TPE attribution required a compatible clinic-serological profile and a study-defined post-diethylcarbamazine (DEC) haematological response of at least 50% reduction in AEC. For the present analysis, ABPA was classified according to the revised 2024 International Society for Human and Animal Mycology criteria using prospectively collected clinical, immunological, and imaging variables. In TPE-compatible patients, DEC was given before ABPA-directed therapy to preserve interpretation of the eosinophilic response. Among 312 prospectively evaluated patients, 132 met the study definitions for TPE-ABPA overlap, 77 for TPE alone, and 103 for ABPA alone.  In the overlap cohort, mean age was 36.2±15.9 years; median baseline AEC was 6071 cells/µL [interquartile range (IQR) 3793-11,000] and median total IgE was 7641 IU/mL (IQR 4525-13,621). Aspergillus fumigatus-specific IgE and IgG were positive in all 132; the filarial antigen was positive in 128 (97.0%), and there was qualitative filarial IgG in all 132.  The dominant recorded high-resolution computed tomography pattern was normal in 73 (55.3%), while bronchiectasis was recorded in 42 (31.8%). All overlap patients received DEC and fulfilled the study-defined ≥50% AEC response criterion. ABPA-directed treatment comprised systemic corticosteroids alone in 71 (53.8%), itraconazole alone in 41 (31.1%), and both in 20 (15.2%). Concurrent TPE and ABPA should be considered in endemic regions when asthma is accompanied by disproportionate eosinophilia and IgE elevation; recognition of one eosinophilic disorder should not prematurely terminate evaluation for the other.

articles.title: Machine Learning Models for Glycemic Prediction in Type 1 and Type 2 Diabetes: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Machine learning models are increasingly used for glycemic event prediction and continuous glucose forecasting, but targets, populations, horizons, validation, and uncertainty reporting remain heterogeneous.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate machine learning models for glycemic prediction in type 1, type 2, and mixed diabetes populations while distinguishing the full evidence map from the quantitatively analyzable subset.

METHODS: We searched 9 English- and Chinese-language databases from inception to April 12, 2026, for studies predicting future glycemic events or glucose values in people with diabetes. Continuous forecasting and binary event prediction were analyzed separately. Root-mean-square error (RMSE) was the principal continuous end point; mean absolute error was supportive. Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was synthesized using a Bayesian random-effects model because analyzable 2×2 data were sparse. Two reviewers (HY and DA) independently applied PROBAST (Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool) to 19 quantitative-source reports (28 assessment units).

RESULTS: We identified 787 records, assessed 310 full texts, and included 299 reports representing 270 studies; 19 reports contributed to quantitative synthesis. The review included 128 type 1, 26 type 2, 78 mixed, and 38 unclear-diabetes-type studies. Pooled RMSE was 1.18 mmol/L (95% CI 1.01-1.34; 37 effects), supportive mean absolute error was 0.90 mmol/L (95% CI 0.78-1.02; 20 effects), and Bayesian pooled area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.926 (95% credible interval 0.877-0.957). Supportive sensitivity and specificity were 0.77 and 0.80. Of 28 PROBAST units, 24 were high risk, 2 unclear, and 2 low. Post hoc exploratory within-report analysis estimated an RMSE increase of 0.481 mmol/L per additional 30 minutes (95% CI 0.213-0.749), but overlap sensitivity reduced certainty. In the 270-study clinical readiness audit, external validation occurred in 4.0% (10/251), prospective evaluation in 0.7% (2/270), calibration in 4.8% (13/270), decision-curve or net-benefit analysis in 2.6% (7/270), and implementation or human-factors evaluation in 2.6% (7/270).

CONCLUSIONS: Glycemic prediction studies show forecasting and discrimination signals, but heterogeneity, high risk of bias, incomplete uncertainty reporting, and limited external and prospective validation preclude deployable benchmarks. Pooled estimates should be viewed as summaries of analyzable literature. Future studies need transparent horizon, threshold, calibration, validation, uncertainty, and implementation reporting.

articles.title: Aggregation induced emission based fluorescent and colorimetric sensor for selective detection of Fe2+: experimental and computational insights with real-time applications.
articles.abstract: A highly responsive fluorescent and colorimetric sensor (N 2,N 6-bis(4-(phenylamino)phenyl)pyridine-2,6-dicarboxamide) DPD has been developed for the selective detection of Fe2+ ions. DPD was readily synthesized through a nucleophilic substitution reaction and characterized through spectroscopic techniques. Sensor DPD displayed aggregation-induced emission (AIE) accompanied by an increase in fluorescence intensity with a bathochromic shift. The aggregation behavior of DPD was further examined by dynamic light scattering analysis (DLS). Among the different metal ions investigated, DPD showed a distinct and highly selective response toward Fe2+, resulting in substantial fluorescence quenching due to photo-induced electron transfer (PET) and the paramagnetic behaviour of Fe2+. The interaction of DPD with Fe2+ was investigated by fluorescence and UV/visible spectroscopy, FTIR spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, and 1H NMR titration and cyclic voltammetry which collectively provide the evidence of DPD@Fe2+ interaction. Theoretical calculations, including frontier molecular orbital analysis and QTAIM analysis, were performed to support the experimental findings. Sensor DPD was successfully employed for the colorimetric detection of Fe2+ in the solid phase and in real potato samples. Furthermore, the sensor was evaluated for the detection of acidic vapors.

articles.title: When the Filter Becomes the Source: POCUS Detection of Inferior Vena Cava Filter Thrombosis Extending Into the Right Atrium.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Inferior vena cava (IVC) filters are used to prevent pulmonary embolism in patients with venous thromboembolism when anticoagulation is contraindicated. Although uncommon, filter thrombosis can result in thrombus propagation and potentially life-threatening embolic complications. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) provides a rapid bedside assessment of the heart, lungs, and may facilitate the prompt recognition of unexpected thromboembolic complications.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 43-year-old man with hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage was admitted to the intensive care unit requiring mechanical ventilation and vasopressor support. Six days after admission, he developed sudden severe hypoxemia, tachycardia, and hypotension requiring reinitiation of norepinephrine. POCUS demonstrated bilateral anterior A-lines, left femoral and popliteal deep vein thrombosis, and preserved right ventricular (RV) function without echocardiographic evidence of RV strain. Catheter-based pulmonary angiography confirmed subocclusive thrombosis involving segmental branches of the right middle and lower lobes, which was treated with mechanical thromboaspiration, followed by IVC filter placement because anticoagulation was initially contraindicated. Four days later, he developed a new episode of acute hypoxemia despite remaining hemodynamically stable. Repeat POCUS demonstrated a large mobile thrombus in transit within the right atrium. Subcostal longitudinal imaging of the IVC demonstrated a large elongated thrombus attached to the IVC filter, with a freely mobile portion extending into the right atrium. Urgent mechanical thrombectomy and IVC filter replacement were performed. The new filter was positioned approximately 2 cm below the confluence of the hepatic veins with the inferior vena cava. Approximately 24 h later, follow-up POCUS showed no evidence of new thrombus formation. More than 2 weeks after admission, following a follow-up brain CT showing no significant progression of the intracerebral hemorrhage, anticoagulation with enoxaparin was initiated and progressively increased to a full therapeutic dose.

CONCLUSION: This case highlights the value of POCUS for the prompt bedside recognition of an established and potentially life-threatening complication of IVC filter placement. Systematic bedside cardiac and venous ultrasound may identify thrombus propagation into the right atrium even in the absence of RV dilation or echocardiographic evidence of RV strain, facilitating timely endovascular intervention.

articles.title: Reimagining COPD treatment: are biologics the next frontier?
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality with persistent symptom burden and frequent exacerbations despite optimized inhaled therapy. Growing recognition of disease heterogeneity such as a distinct type-2/eosinophilic endotype as well as advances in biologic agents motivate reassessment of monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) as targeted treatments.

AREAS COVERED: This narrative review summarizes evidence from Phase 2 and 3 studies for mAbs in COPD, grouping agents by molecular targets (IL-1β, IL-4/IL-4 Rα/IL-13, IL-5/IL-5 Rα, IL-8, IL-17, IL-33/ST2/RAGE/EGFR, TSLP, TNF-α). A literature search of MEDLINE and ClinicalTrials.gov was conducted to identify relevant clinical studies of biologic therapies for COPD, with the search updated through November 2025. Trials of canakinumab, dupilumab, mepolizumab, benralizumab, ABX-IL8, CNTO 6785, astegolimab, itepekimab, tozorakimab, tezepelumab, and earlier neutrophil-directed therapies are reviewed, with emphasis on biomarker-guided enrichment, primary and key secondary outcomes, subgroup signals, and safety profiles.

EXPERT OPINION: Broad anti-inflammatory approaches have largely failed in unselected COPD populations. By contrast, biologics targeting type-2 inflammation or upstream epithelial alarmins show benefit in biomarker-defined subgroups. Future success depends on precise endotype definition, validated biomarkers, and trials designed for enriched populations; careful risk-benefit assessment and real-world validation are essential before designing future clinical trials.

articles.title: Accessing Emergency Surgery: Perceptions of the Challenges, Gaps, and Training by ACVECC Community-Associated Veterinarians.
articles.journal: Journal of veterinary emergency and critical care (San Antonio, Tex. : 2001)
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether there is a shortage of surgical specialists available to clients and pets treated by American College of Veterinary Emergency and Critical Care (ACVECC) diplomate practitioners in clinical practice; to explore the surgical training during ACVECC residency programs; and to explore whether ACVECC diplomates and associated respondents are interested in a formalized emergency surgical certificate program in emergency surgery.

DESIGN: A survey comprising 22 items for identifying respondents' demographics, surgical training experience, and current practice was distributed via email to all diplomates, residency-trained non-diplomates, and current residents on the ACVECC listserv. Respondents were also asked about their interest in the creation of an emergency surgery certificate.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Three hundred individuals responded to the survey, the vast majority in small animal (SA) practice. Thirty-four percent of SA respondents do not have 24-h access to surgical specialists despite their hospital being open 24 h a day. While some practices have ACVECC diplomates or emergency clinicians available to perform out-of-hours surgery, 8% of all respondents have no out-of-hours surgical capability. More than half the respondents (169/300 [56%]) completed their residency surgical requirement in an observational role without any primary cutting responsibility, and most respondents (178/289 [62%]) supported the formation of a structured emergency surgical certificate through ACVECC.

CONCLUSIONS: There is a relative shortage of out-of-hours emergency surgeons within SA emergency practices. Further study and discussion are warranted to better define the necessity and viability of solutions to mitigate this shortage.

articles.title: [Work ability of economically active individuals at risk of old-age poverty].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Population aging contributes to the shrinking of the labor supply. A characteristic feature of the Polish pension system, rarely observed internationally, is the growing number of individuals receiving a pension despite a very short period of social security contributions. This results in an increase in the number of people receiving low pension benefits and an elevated risk of poverty among retirees. One way to mitigate this phenomenon is to extend economic activity, which, however, requires adapting working conditions to the capabilities of older employees. In this context, work ability is of key importance. The aim of this study was to assess the work ability of economically active individuals at risk of pension poverty, with particular emphasis on their capacity to continue working.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: Work ability was measured using the Work Ability Index (WAI). The data come from a nationwide computer-assisted personal interviewing survey conducted among pre-retirement age individuals at risk of pension poverty. The analysis was limited to economically active respondents (N = 704). Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, one- and two-way analysis of variance, t-test, and χ2 test.

RESULTS: The research shows that the average WAI score among people at risk of pension poverty is 33.6 pts. For half of the respondents, this score does not exceed 35 pts. This indicates that this group's work ability is moderate. Just under 1 in 3 people report a good work ability, while virtually no one reports an excellent one. Work ability is significantly linked to the type of the workload, the propensity to continue working and the possibility of achieving the required contribution period. The lowest WAI scores are observed among blue-collar workers who do not intend to work beyond retirement age.

CONCLUSIONS: The limited work ability of people at risk of pension poverty may constitute a significant barrier to both continuing economic activity and achieving the required contribution period, particularly for those furthest from meeting this condition. Therefore, measures relating to age management are of significant importance, especially those aimed at improving workplace ergonomics and supporting mental health. Med Pr Work Health Saf. 2026;77(5).

articles.title: Therapeutic Targeting of the Cancer Microbiome and Metabolome: Ongoing Trials and Future Directions for the Surgical Oncologist.
articles.abstract: The role of the human microbiome in cancer development, progression, and response to therapy has moved from correlative curiosity to demonstrated impact on tumor biology. This represents a critical factor for surgical oncologists as they not only resect these tumors, but also direct perioperative antimicrobial exposure and increasingly co-manage neoadjuvant and surveillance pathways in which microbial state may predict and modify response. This review summarizes the basis for therapeutic modulation of the cancer microbiome and metabolome in a contemporary clinical-trial landscape across four broad strategies: additive (fecal microbiota transplantation, defined consortia, and live biotherapeutic products), subtractive (targeted antimicrobials), dietary and metabolome-directed interventions, and engineered or next-generation platforms. Particular attention is given to subtractive approaches in colon and rectal cancer and to the underexplored perioperative interface between the microbiome and surgical outcomes such as anastomotic leak. We outline the principal methodological and translational obstacles, including low-biomass contamination, causal inference, unintended antibiotic effects, and product standardization. Looking ahead, we propose roles for surgeons across the care continuum, from biospecimen stewardship and trial referral to integration of microbiome and circulating tumor DNA signals in surveillance.

articles.title: Reducing Patient Radiation Skin Dose in Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Using a Dedicated Protocol: A Single-Center Experience.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) expose patients and operators to ionizing radiation, posing risks of deterministic effects such as skin injury and stochastic effects including malignancy. Although real-time dosimetry and dose alerts have been associated with radiation-dose reductions in prior reports, the level of patient radiation reduction associated with implementing a formal, multifaceted radiation reduction program has not previously been reported in a high-volume catheterization laboratory.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of a substantial radiation dose level (SRDL) protocol on patient radiation exposure during PCI.

METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 19,249 PCI procedures at a tertiary center from July 2012 to December 2021. Patients were stratified into a pre-protocol cohort (Phase 1: 17,332 procedures) and a post-protocol cohort (Phase 2: 1917 procedures following implementation in November 2019). The SRDL protocol included real-time radiation monitoring, alert thresholds at 5 Gy air kerma, and structured follow-up for high-dose cases. Study outcomes included air kerma (Ka,r) dose-area product (DAP), contrast volume, and fluoroscopy time.

RESULTS: The study cohort (mean age 66.3 years; 28.5% female) demonstrated significant reductions in radiation exposure after implementing the protocol. Median air kerma declined from 2.6 to 2.0 Gy (23% reduction; p < 0.0001), and median DAP decreased from 158 to 125 Gy·cm2 (20.8% reduction; p < 0.0001). Contrast volume was reduced by 15 mL (11.1% reduction; p < 0.0001), while fluoroscopy time remained unchanged (18.1 vs. 18.3 min; p = 0.094). Despite increased procedural complexity in Phase 2 (multivessel PCI: 69.5% vs. 65.2%; p < 0.001), radiation reduction remained significant.

CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of an SRDL protocol was associated with significant reductions in patient radiation exposure during PCI without increasing procedure time, supporting its use as a safety intervention in high-volume catheterization laboratories.

articles.title: Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping and R2* of Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury Relates to Reactive Oxygen Species Activity.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Iron deposition following ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) plays a catalytic role in reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, contributing to myocardial injury and subsequent heart failure. There is a need for noninvasive imaging methods that quantify iron deposition and ROS activity post-IRI. We aimed to evaluate the relationship between myocardial iron content, measured by quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) and R2*, and ROS activity using PET.

METHODS: IRI was induced in eight swine by percutaneous coronary artery occlusion. Three to seven days post-infarction, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging was performed to acquire multi-echo gradient echo images to reconstruct QSM and R2* maps. ROS activity was quantified using a ROS-activated radiotracer [18F]ROStrace and corrected for myocardial blood flow.

RESULTS: Magnetic susceptibility and R2* were significantly elevated in hemorrhagic myocardial regions compared to remote myocardium (susceptibility: 0.07 ± 0.08 vs. -0.03 ± 0.05 ppm, p value = 0.02; R2*: 43.9 ± 5.0 vs. 23.6 ± 5.6 Hz, p value = 0.0003). Infarct ROS activity was significantly higher than in remote regions (0.15 ± 0.04 vs. 0.11 ± 0.04 mL/g, p value = 0.0009). A moderate and positive correlation was found across R2*, susceptibility and ROS activity, with the strongest association between R2* and ROS activity (bootstrapped ρ = 0.59, p value = 0.073; uncorrected ρ = 0.65, p value = 0.02).

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates a moderate association between iron-sensitive MRI biomarkers in the myocardium and ROS activity in IRI. These findings suggest a relationship between iron-related tissue changes and ROS and highlight R2* and QSM as important imaging biomarkers, potentially aiding in the evaluation of therapeutic targets for treatment of myocardial reperfusion injury.

articles.title: Metabolic Vulnerability Despite Normal BMI: From Adverse Body Composition to Ectopic Fat and Organ Dysfunction.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract: BMI remains the most widely used measure for defining overweight and obesity; however, it does not adequately capture body fat distribution, skeletal muscle mass and quality, adipose tissue function, or ectopic fat accumulation. Consequently, individuals with a normal BMI may exhibit substantial metabolic abnormalities, whereas some individuals with obesity remain relatively metabolically healthy. These observations challenge the assumption that BMI reliably reflects metabolic health and highlight the concept of metabolic vulnerability despite normal body weight. This narrative review examines the biological basis of this metabolic vulnerability and evaluates the evidence supporting a shift from BMI-centered assessment toward body composition-based phenotyping. We discuss the interrelated roles of impaired adipose tissue expandability and function, visceral adiposity, chronic low-grade inflammation, adipose tissue fibrosis, skeletal muscle dysfunction, and ectopic lipid deposition in the development of insulin resistance and organ-specific metabolic dysfunction. Particular emphasis is placed on adipose tissue dysfunction as a potential unifying mechanism underlying metabolic heterogeneity among individuals with similar BMI. The review further examines adverse body composition across normal-weight metabolic phenotypes, including normal-weight obesity (NWO), metabolically unhealthy normal weight (MUNW), lean prediabetes, lean T2DM, lean MASLD, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and chronic kidney disease. Excess visceral adiposity, unfavorable fat-to-lean mass distribution, impaired skeletal muscle quality, and ectopic fat accumulation in the liver, pancreas, heart, skeletal muscle, and other organs may contribute to metabolic risk independently of BMI. We also summarize advances in body composition and ectopic fat assessment, including dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), computed tomography (CT), bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA), and artificial intelligence-assisted imaging, together with emerging therapeutic strategies focused on reducing visceral and ectopic fat, preserving skeletal muscle, and restoring metabolic tissue function rather than pursuing weight loss alone. Moving beyond BMI toward integrated assessment of body composition, adipose tissue biology, and ectopic fat distribution may improve recognition of metabolic vulnerability, facilitate earlier identification of individuals at increased cardiometabolic risk, and support more precise prevention and treatment strategies.

articles.title: The PIC-Police that Protect the Kidney.
Study of Visceral Adiposity Index and Free Androgen Index in Indian Women With PCOS: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: PCOS is a complex endocrine disorder associated with metabolic and hormonal dysregulation. The visceral adiposity index (VAI) and free androgen index (FAI) have emerged as predictive markers for PCOS. This study aims to evaluate the role of VAI and FAI from the aspect of metabolic and hormonal imbalance in PCOS women from urban and rural areas of India.

STUDY DESIGN AND SUBJECTS: Women within the reproductive age of 18-40 years from both rural and urban areas of India were recruited in the study between November 2018 and July 2022 for this cross-sectional study. 12,100 women were approached to participate in the study, of whom 8993 subjects were enroled. After clinical examination and all investigations according to the protocol, 795 were PCOS cases, while 2475 were non-PCOS cases as per Rotterdam criteria. The PCOS group was segregated according to obesity.

MEASUREMENTS: Hormonal profile and ovarian morphology were evaluated along with anthropometric parameters. VAI, FAI, and Lipid Accumulation Product (LAP) were calculated based on biochemical parameters.

RESULTS: VAI and FAI were significantly elevated in PCOS compared to non-PCOS. VAI, FAI, and LAP were significantly increased in obese PCOS. VAI, independent of BMI, was significantly associated with the Ferriman Gallaway (FG) score, FBG, fasting insulin, and LAP, whereas FAI was associated with BMI and LAP.

CONCLUSION: The study underscores that VAI may serve as the surrogate marker of PCOS, independent of obesity.

articles.title: The Rural and Urban Texas Midwifery Workforce: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Survey.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Texas faces a critical shortage of maternity care clinicians in its rural communities, where nearly half of rural counties are maternity care deserts. This study aimed to characterize and compare rural and urban midwives across several domains and identify workforce and health care policy strategies to strengthen Texas's rural maternity workforce.

METHODS: We conducted a secondary, comparative, cross-sectional analysis using 2 parallel web-based surveys in 2025 among rural and urban licensed midwives (LMs), certified professional midwives (CPMs), and certified nurse-midwives (CNMs) practicing in Texas. Harmonized items across instruments allowed pooled comparisons of rural and urban participants. We used descriptive statistics and bivariate analyses to assess differences.

RESULTS: Among practicing midwives (LMs/CPMs and CNMs) in Texas, 228 completed the survey and were eligible for the study. Compared with urban midwives (n = 184), rural midwives (n = 44) were more often self-employed, reported lower incomes, were less likely to have liability insurance, and reported more barriers to physician consultation. Rural midwives were also less likely to offer the option for a vaginal birth after cesarean but reported greater physiologic birth support and legislative engagement. Among CNMs, prescriptive authority was significantly less common in rural areas.

DISCUSSION: Despite workforce and practice barriers, rural Texas midwives demonstrate a strong commitment to physiologic birth and policy advocacy.
