Strengthening the integration of rural midwives into the health care systems through consultation and liability support as well as policy reform is essential to sustaining and expanding the Texas midwifery workforce.

articles.title: Association between anticholinergic burden and geriatric outcomes in older adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Older adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) frequently require multiple medications with anticholinergic and sedative properties for the management of diabetes-related complications and comorbidities, and diabetes itself predisposes patients to geriatric syndromes - making this population particularly vulnerable to the cumulative effects of anticholinergic burden.

AIMS: This study aimed to determine the association between anticholinergic burden and geriatric syndromes in T2DM.

METHODS: This retrospective study analysed comprehensive geriatric assessments of 715 T2DM outpatients from November 2018 to August 2024. Anticholinergic and sedative drug burden was evaluated using the Drug Burden Index, Anticholinergic Cognitive Burden Scale and Anticholinergic Risk Scale.

RESULTS: Among the patients with T2DM (80.63 ± 7.3; 70.3% female), 309 had no anticholinergic burden, 320 had low burden and 86 had high burden. After adjustment for dementia, Parkinson disease and HbA1c, high anticholinergic burden was significantly associated with lower scores on the Barthel Index (P = 0.003; adjusted β = -10.22), Mini Nutritional Assessment (P = 0.005; adjusted β = -1.84), Mini-Mental State Examination (P = 0.001; adjusted β = -2.59) and the Tinetti test (P = 0.006; adjusted β = -2.11), as well as higher Timed Up and Go scores (P = 0.001; adjusted β = 5.13) and an increased risk of sarcopenia (P = 0.031; adjusted odds ratios = 1.83).

CONCLUSION: Anticholinergic medication exposure is observed in more than half of older adults with T2DM. Increased anticholinergic burden is an independent risk factor for sarcopenia, malnutrition and gait, and cognitive and functional decline in older T2DM patients. The use of anticholinergic drugs in older patients with T2DM should be carefully evaluated and strategies to minimise exposure implemented.

articles.title: Routine Fetal Cardiac Screening Versus Screening Fetal Echocardiography: Reconsidering the Distinction.
articles.journal: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine

articles.title: Reverse Balloon Anchoring for Retrieval of an Entrapped Side-Branch Balloon During the Jailed Balloon Technique.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: The jailed balloon technique (JBT) is an effective strategy for side branch (SB) protection during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for coronary bifurcation lesions; however, jailed balloon entrapment is a rare but serious complication. We report the case of a man in his 70s who was successfully resuscitated after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest due to ventricular fibrillation and underwent emergency PCI for a right coronary artery bifurcation lesion. A drug-eluting stent was deployed from the mid right coronary artery to the posterior descending branch using JBT. The jailed SB balloon became entrapped and could not be retrieved despite repeated inflation and deflation, traction, and rotational torque. Further traction resulted in deep engagement of the guiding catheter and an accordion phenomenon of the right coronary artery, raising concern about vascular injury. A balloon was therefore inflated within the stented main vessel, and forward pressure was applied to its shaft to provide counterforce against traction on the entrapped SB balloon. Using this technique, which we termed the "reverse balloon anchoring technique," the entrapped balloon was successfully retrieved without apparent device damage. Final angiography and intravascular ultrasound demonstrated preserved SB flow and adequate stent apposition. The reverse balloon anchoring technique may represent a useful bailout option for jailed balloon entrapment when conventional retrieval maneuvers fail.

articles.title: Structural and mechanistic insights for calpain drug development.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Calpains are Ca2+-activated cysteine proteases with broad roles in cell signaling, cytoskeletal remodeling, cell survival, differentiation, and tissue homeostasis. Calpain activity is implicated in multiple facets of human physiology, and its dysregulation has been reported in numerous pathologies. Yet, therapeutic targeting of calpains has been limited by challenges in achieving calpain-specific inhibition, owing to their complex biology and substrate diversity.

AREAS COVERED: This review covers structural-, molecular- and cell-biology, disease associations, and recent intellectual property activity relevant to calpain drug development. Structural aspects include the domain architecture of classical and non-classical calpains, ancillary domains, calpastatin-mediated inhibition, homo- and heterodimerization, and emerging structural models. Calpains are considered in the broader landscape of cysteine proteases to highlight likely off-target liabilities. Disease- and pathology-focused sections discuss calpain-mediated signaling in neurodegeneration, muscular dystrophy, ocular disease, diabetes, endometriosis, cardiovascular pathology, fibrosis, and cancer. Strategies for calpain modulation are overviewed, including active-site, calpastatin-mimetic, and allosteric inhibitors, gene therapy, and RNA-based approaches.

EXPERT OPINION: A shift beyond pan-calpain inhibition toward isoform-selective drug discovery, improved biomarkers, and accumulating structural insights offers new opportunities. Developing calpain-specific and isoform-selective therapeutics remains an exciting unmet opportunity in cancer, neurodegeneration, retinopathy, muscular dystrophy, and other diseases.

articles.title: Long-Term Prognostic Value of Angiography-Derived Quantitative Flow Ratio and Radial Wall Strain in Untreated Intermediate Coronary Stenoses: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quantitative flow ratio (QFR) measures angiography-derived coronary physiology, whereas radial wall strain (RWS) characterizes cyclic lumen deformation. We investigated their complementary long-term prognostic information in untreated intermediate coronary stenoses and assessed the internal validity of their combined prediction model.

AIMS: We investigated the complementary long-term prognostic information of QFR and RWS in untreated intermediate coronary stenoses, and assessed the internal validity of their combined prediction model.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 236 patients with 236 untreated index vessels and 50%-90% diameter stenosis. QFR and maximum RWS (RWSmax) were calculated offline and were unavailable to treating clinicians. Target vessel failure (TVF) comprised cardiac death, target vessel-related myocardial infarction, or ischemia-driven target vessel revascularization (TVR). Prespecified Cox models used multiple imputation, and four nested models underwent 1000-bootstrap validation with repeat imputation and fitting. Fixed 3-year analyses, calibration, and sensitivity analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Over a median potential follow-up of 66.8 months, 55 patients experienced TVF, including 40 TVR events. TVF occurred in 37/108 patients (34.3%) with RWSmax > 12% and 18/128 (14.1%) with RWSmax ≤12%. In the primary model, the adjusted hazard ratio was 1.14 (95% CI: 1.06-1.23; p = 0.001) per 1% increase in RWSmax and 1.34 (95% CI: 1.08-1.67; p = 0.010) per 0.05 decrease in QFR. The combined model had an apparent C-index of 0.733 and an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.704, compared with 0.597 for the clinical model. Its corrected 3-year AUC was 0.733, and its corrected calibration slope was 0.90.

CONCLUSIONS: Joint assessment of coronary physiology and wall strain provided incremental long-term prognostic information beyond clinical and angiographic characteristics in untreated intermediate lesions. Lower QFR and higher RWSmax were independently associated with TVF, and each added prognostic information beyond the other. The signal predominantly concerned subsequent revascularization. External validation is needed before clinical application.

articles.title: Functional Outcomes After Total Ankle Replacement: A Forgotten Joint Score-12 Analysis With Up to 10-Year Follow-up.
articles.abstract: BackgroundTotal ankle replacement (TAR) offers pain relief and preservation of motion in patients with end-stage ankle arthritis. The Forgotten Joint Score-12 (FJS-12) is a validated patient-reported outcome measure (PROM) designed to assess joint awareness, but data in TAR remain limited.MethodsA retrospective study of all TARs performed at our institution between 2014 and 2023 was conducted. Patients with a minimum of 2 years of follow-up were contacted by telephone, and the FJS-12 was administered. Mean follow-up was 4.83 ± 2.48 years (range 2-10). Demographics, surgical details, and complications were recorded. Statistical analyses explored factors associated with FJS-12 scores. At the end of FJS-12 administration, patients graded their satisfaction on a 4-point Likert scale.ResultsOf 102 ankles screened, 81 patients were eligible (mean age 69.7 years; mean body mass index [BMI] 31.3). Female sex (P = .008), right-sided TAR (P = .004), and additional tendo-Achilles lengthening (P = .004) were associated with lower FJS-12 scores. Scores declined at 3 years post-surgery (P = .011). Other factors, including BMI, smoking, and hypertension, had no significant impact. Based on the score distribution and satisfaction analysis, the Patient Acceptable Symptom State (PASS) threshold corresponded to an FJS-12 of 43, and the forgotten-joint threshold to 85.ConclusionTotal ankle replacement provided favorable short- to mid-term functional outcomes, as measured by the FJS-12. The FJS-12 is a sensitive PROM that detects subtle differences in patient-reported outcomes and may be a useful adjunct in routine TAR follow-up. We propose preliminary TAR-specific PASS and forgotten-joint thresholds that closely match those reported for knee replacement and are lower than those for hip replacement. These thresholds provide clinically meaningful benchmarks for patient satisfaction and should be validated in larger, prospective, multicentre cohorts.Level of Evidence:Level III, retrospective cohort study.

articles.title: Letter to the Editor Regarding "Atrial Fibrillation Ablation Outcomes by Hospital Academic Status" By Shabbir et al.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

articles.title: A Breathable Nanomesh-Textile Electrode Interface for Integrated Multimodal Monitoring.
articles.abstract: Long-term wearable electrophysiology requires electrodes that are skin-conformal, breathable, mechanically stable, and reliably connected to electronics. Existing dry electrodes address parts of this challenge, but the interface between soft electrodes and wearable electronics remains a major source of motion artifacts, open-circuit failure, and poor long-term usability. Here, we introduce a duo-electrode interface that separates the functions of skin contact and electronic interconnection. An electrospun nanomesh serves as a tattoo electrode that conforms intimately to the skin, while a compressible conductive taffeta-foam fabric electrode embedded in a garment provides stable electrical coupling to textile-routed electronics. This architecture preserves the advantages of skin-conformal electrodes while avoiding fragile connections to electronics. We integrate the interface into a bodysuit and eyemask platform for multimodal monitoring of ECG, EMG, EOG, and body position using a centralized electronics module. The system maintains reliable signal acquisition under body motion and muscle activation, with performance comparable to or better than that of commercial hydrogel electrodes. By bridging breathable electrodes with textile-based routing, the proposed duo-electrode strategy establishes a practical method for scalable, comfortable, and long-duration wearable bioelectronic monitoring. This approach may be broadly useful for remote healthcare, rehabilitation, sleep studies, human-machine interfaces, and personalized physiological sensing.

articles.title: Carrier-Free Activatable Nanomodulators for Cuproptosis-Augmented Photoimmunotherapy of Colorectal Cancer.
articles.abstract: Photoimmunotherapy (PIT) has emerged as a promising modality for colorectal cancer (CRC) treatment, yet it often suffers from limited response rates and immune escape. We herein report a carrier-free, tumor-specific nanomodulator (IRP@Cu-R) for near-infrared second window (NIR-II) fluorescence imaging-guided cuproptosis-augmented PIT of CRC. IRP@Cu-R is prepared by co-assembly of IRP@Cu, which is synthesized by linking a NIR-II fluorophore (IR820) with a photosensitizer (PPa) through Cu2+-chelated DTPA, and a boronic ester-masked immune adjuvant (R848-PB) without additional nanocarrier. The drug loading contents for PPa and R848-PB are as high as 21.1% and 17.8%, respectively. With Cu2+ coordinated, both NIR-II fluorescence and photodynamic activity are quenched via photoinduced electron transfer (PeT). Upon exposure to endogenous hydrogen sulfide (H2S), Cu2+ is converted to CuS, thereby restoring both activities. The released Cu2+ is reduced to Cu+ by glutathione (GSH), depleting antioxidants and inducing cuproptosis via lipoylated protein aggregation. Together with PDT, this process enhances immunogenic cell death. Meanwhile, excess H2O2 cleaves the boronic ester bond of R848-PB to release R848. These processes promote dendritic cell maturation, thereby eliciting potent systemic antitumor immunity against primary, distant and metastatic tumors. Thus, this study provides a generalizable carrier-free strategy for integrating activatable NIR-II fluorescence imaging with cuproptosis-augmented photoimmunotherapy.

articles.title: Simultaneous Aortic and Mitral Valve-in-Valve Replacement Using Balloon-Expandable MyVal Valves With Bioprosthetic Valve Fracture.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement and mitral valve replacement have proved to be a viable alternative to redo surgery in patients who have bioprosthetic valve dysfunction. There is a large subgroup of patients who undergo double valve replacement with bioprosthetic valves, especially in patients with rheumatic heart disease. Failure of these bioprosthetic valves would require a transcatheter management strategy. Transcatheter double valve replacement (TDVR) in these complex cases would require careful evaluation and planning of valve sizing, aortomitral interactions, access, and residual gradients. A 73-year-old man with rheumatic heart disease and prior double bioprosthetic valve replacement in 2014 presented with New York Heart Association class (NYHA) III dyspnea and exertional pre-syncope. He had severe stenosis of a 19 mm Perimount Magna aortic bioprosthesis and a 27 mm Perimount Magna mitral bioprosthesis, with pulmonary hypertension. Computed tomography demonstrated suitable anatomy for transcatheter valve-in-valve treatment. He underwent successful TDVR with a 20 mm MyVal balloon-expandable in the aortic position, followed by a post-implantation valve fracture, and a 27.5 mm MyVal transseptally in the mitral position. The final mean gradients were 15 mmHg across the aortic valve and 6 mmHg across the mitral valve at discharge. At 1-year follow-up, the patient remained clinically well without an increase in valve gradients. Simultaneous transcatheter aortic and mitral valve-in-valve replacement can be performed successfully in selected high-risk patients after meticulous multimodality planning. In patients with a small surgical aortic bioprosthesis, intentional bioprosthetic valve fracture may be an important adjunct to optimize post-implantation hemodynamics. This report highlights the complexity of procedural planning for bioprosthetic valve fracture in a small aortic valve, ensuring optimal hemodynamics and the safety and durability of the Myval transcatheter heart valve in challenging and complex procedures like TDVR.

articles.title: Inter-Rater Reliability of the Hemodialysis Acuity Tool for Assessing Patient Care Acuity (the HAT Study).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In Australian hemodialysis settings, the absence of a validated, localized tool to measure patient acuity has resulted in allocation based on hemodialysis chairs availability rather than objective assessment. To address this gap, the Hemodialysis Acuity Tool (HAT) was developed to evaluate patient acuity and determine suitability for specific hemodialysis locations.

AIM: This study aims to assess the inter-rater reliability of the HAT to support hemodialysis nurses in assessing patient care acuity and identifying optimal hemodialysis setting for adults receiving hemodialysis.

METHODS: A prospective observational study examined the use of HAT by hemodialysis nurses to assess patient care acuity. Inter-rater reliability was tested by comparing scores assigned by different hemodialysis nurses. Statistical analysis was performed using descriptive statistics and intraclass correlation coefficient.

RESULTS: Intraclass correlation coefficient indicated moderate to good inter-rater reliability for the categories of physical and psychosocial and the overall total patient scores, though no correlation was found in the hemodialysis category or comorbidity at month 6.

CONCLUSION: The HAT demonstrates potential as a reliable tool for determining patient suitability for specific hemodialysis locations and identifying candidates for home hemodialysis or additional support. Its use can facilitate safe allocation of patients to units equipped with appropriate resources, improving care delivery and supporting workforce planning.

articles.title: DL-HYKIDRECNET: IOT-Enabled Hybrid Deep Convolutional-Recurrent Model for Early Detection of Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a chronic and life-threatening disorder that requires early diagnosis and proper management to prevent severe complications. However, missing and imbalanced clinical data, complex nonlinear relationships, and limited generalization across heterogeneous patient records pose challenges to reliable CKD classification.

AIMS: This study aims to develop a deep learning-based CKD classification framework that addresses these challenges through systematic preprocessing and nonlinear feature learning.

METHODS: The proposed framework uses the publicly available Kaggle CKD dataset containing structured clinical features. The preprocessing stage involves mean imputation for missing values, categorical encoding, MinMax normalization for feature scaling, and the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) to address class imbalance. The processed data are subsequently passed through deep feature learning layers to capture complex nonlinear relationships among clinical variables. The extracted high-level representations are fed into a fully connected dense classification layer with a sigmoid activation function to generate probability scores for binary CKD prediction.

RESULTS: The proposed model achieved an accuracy of 98.8%, precision of 96.8%, recall of 100%, and F1-score of 98.4% on the CKD dataset, demonstrating strong classification performance and consistent behavior across the evaluated data partitions.

CONCLUSIONS: The experimental findings indicate the potential of the proposed framework for effective CKD classification. However, its evaluation is limited to retrospective clinical data and does not establish prospective or external clinical validity. Therefore, the framework represents a research-oriented classification approach with potential for future clinical decision-support applications rather than a clinically validated diagnostic system.

articles.title: External Validation of the UK-BCIS CHIP Score to Predict 1-Year Outcomes in Patients Undergoing IVL-Assisted PCI: Insights From the International BENELUX-IVL Registry.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The United Kingdom-British Cardiovascular Intervention Society complex high-risk indicated percutaneous coronary intervention (UK-BCIS CHIP) score was developed to identify patient- and procedural factors to predict short-term adverse outcomes in patients undergoing high risk percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The performance of the UK-BCIS CHIP score in a patient population treated with intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) for severe coronary calcification remains unknown.

AIMS: To evaluate the prognostic performance of the UK-BCIS CHIP score in patients undergoing IVL-assisted PCI for severe coronary calcification, and to assess procedural and 1-year clinical outcomes across CHIP score categories.

METHODS: This international, multicenter, prospective study included consecutive patients undergoing IVL-assisted PCI between May 2019 and December 2025 from the BENELUX-IVL registry. Patients were stratified according to UK-BCIS CHIP score categories (0, 1-2, 3-4, and ≥ 5). The primary endpoint was 1-year major adverse cardiac events (MACE), defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or clinically driven target vessel revascularization. Secondary endpoints included all-cause mortality, procedural outcomes, and periprocedural complications. Discrimination of the UK-BCIS CHIP score was assessed using the AUC for in-hospital events and the Harrell's C-index for 1-year outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 911 patients were included. Higher UK-BCIS CHIP scores were associated with increased clinical comorbidity, lesion complexity, and procedural intensity. Procedural, device, and technical success rates were comparable across UK-BCIS CHIP score categories (85.1%, 94.4%, and 85.7% overall; p = 0.850, p = 0.813, and p = 0.781, respectively). Complications requiring intervention occurred in 5.5% of patients and did not differ significantly across CHIP score categories (p = 0.347). The 1-year cumulative incidence of MACE, accounting for all-cause death as a competing risk, did not differ significantly across UK-BCIS CHIP score categories (Gray's test p = 0.53).

CONCLUSION: In IVL-assisted PCI, the UK-BCIS CHIP score effectively identifies patients with increased clinical and procedural complexity but shows limited discrimination for mid-term ischemic outcomes. IVL-assisted PCI is safe and effective across the full spectrum of CHIP risk, while long-term prognosis appears primarily driven by underlying comorbidity burden.

articles.title: Unavoidable Stent Extension Into the Bridged Segment During Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Myocardial Bridging: A Focused Review of Mechanisms, Pitfalls, and Treatment Strategies.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Myocardial bridging (MB) is usually managed medically, and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is generally avoided for isolated bridging. In clinical practice, however, stent extension into a bridged segment may be difficult to avoid when proximal left anterior descending (LAD) disease reaches the bridge entrance, LAD chronic total occlusion obscures distal bridge involvement, diffuse disease leaves no bridge-free landing region, or bailout coverage is required for edge dissection or procedural instability. Once implanted within the bridge, a stent is exposed to repetitive extrinsic compression, caliber mismatch, dynamic deformation, and abnormal local shear, creating a substrate for restenosis, deformation, fracture, perforation, and target lesion failure. This focused review addresses unavoidable bridged-segment stenting as a distinct PCI scenario rather than as a general review of myocardial bridging. We summarize lesion-bridge patterns, anatomic and physiologic mechanisms, the role of coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA), intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)/optical coherence tomography (OCT), and invasive physiology in procedural planning, and practical strategies to minimize metal burden and optimize stent-edge placement. We also examine drug-coated balloons, surgical unroofing, coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in selected anatomy, and emerging bioadaptor technology, while explicitly distinguishing established clinical evidence from limited observational data and hypothesis-generating concepts.

articles.title: Interdisciplinary Care to Tackle Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: An Asia-Pacific Perspective.
Intravascular Ultrasound Catheter Entrapment Caused by Extensive Twisting in the Left Main Coronary Artery: A Challenging Retrieval.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: We report a rare case of intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) catheter entrapment in which extensive twisting of the catheter shaft prevented retrieval. In this phenomenon, termed "catheter suicide," the mechanical IVUS catheter twisted within the left main coronary artery (LMCA) and formed complex loops. Initial removal attempts were unsuccessful, and, during these bailout attempts, the imaging core of the IVUS catheter was found to be severed in its proximal portion. Subsequent imaging of another vessel confirmed extensive twisting, with associated iatrogenic dissection, as the cause of entrapment. Ex vivo experiments reproduced this rotational torque-driven complication. The twist was eventually released incidentally when the IVUS catheter was advanced further, and a larger guiding catheter was used, thereby facilitating safe retrieval. Subsequently, a stent was placed to treat the LMCA dissection, achieving thrombolysis in myocardial infarction (TIMI) grade 3 flow, and the patient was discharged without complications. This case illustrates a severe complication specific to mechanical IVUS systems and emphasizes the importance of prevention and early surgical consultation.

articles.title: Internal Mammary Artery Bypass Graft Dissection Mimicking Atherosclerotic Stenosis: Optical Coherence Tomography to Guide Stent Deferral.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Angiographic narrowing of a left internal mammary artery (LIMA) bypass graft does not always reflect atherosclerotic progression. Chronic or spontaneous LIMA graft dissection may be identified using optical coherence tomography (OCT). A patient with severe multivessel coronary disease and a history of coronary stenting and triple coronary artery bypass grafting presented with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction. Coronary angiography demonstrated critical left main-left circumflex disease, extensive left anterior descending artery in-stent restenosis, an occluded venous graft, and eccentric mid-LIMA narrowing. Urgent native-vessel revascularization restored Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) grade 3 flow and relieved the patient's symptoms. During staged LIMA assessment 6 days later, OCT was performed using a Dragonfly OpStar imaging catheter. OCT identified the entry of a longitudinal intimal flap separating the true and false lumens over a long segment, without significant atherosclerosis in the imaged segment. The operators interpreted this "double-barrel" configuration as a nonobstructive dissection of presumed chronicity. Preserved LIMA flow and clinical stability supported stent deferral; the patient remained asymptomatic and with preserved ejection fraction at the 2-month follow-up visit. This report offers important lessons for interventionalists: intravascular imaging can distinguish dissection from apparent atherosclerotic stenosis and significantly drive further management. Inadvertent false-lumen stenting could expand the false channel, compress the true lumen, and compromise graft perfusion. OCT clearly elucidated lesion morphology and supported clinical restraint; however, it did not independently establish dissection age or an exact mechanism of dissection.

articles.title: Step-by-Step Approach to the Wire-Impenetrable Chronic Total Occlusion Proximal Cap.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Wire-impenetrable chronic total occlusion (CTO) proximal caps cannot be penetrated with conventional guidewire escalation. They are often associated with severe calcification and proximal cap ambiguity. Wire-impenetrable proximal caps can be approached using a "go through" or a "go around" strategy. "Go through" involves using penetrative guidewires or other plaque-modifying equipment, such as laser and electrocautery-assisted re-entry (e-CART). The "go around" approach involves getting into the extraplaque space, through which the CTO is traversed in either the antegrade or the retrograde direction, followed by re-entry into the true lumen. Strong guide-catheter support is required for both the "go through" and "go around" approaches. We discuss the approach to wire-impenetrable CTO proximal caps, propose a step-by-step treatment algorithm, and address potential challenges and their troubleshooting.

articles.title: Diabetes, Devices, and Daily Life: Understanding Situations of Mobile Media Use in Chronic Disease Self-Management.
articles.abstract: Over the past 30 years, mobile media have fundamentally transformed our media landscape, including health behaviors such as the self-management of diabetes, which affects about 1 in 10 people in Germany. However, empirical evidence on mobile media use in chronic disease self-management remains inconclusive: most studies focus on single devices and apps rather than broader mobile media ecosystems. Furthermore, they do not account for situational contexts that can shape access to and perceptions of media use. Using a framework structuring the use of metamedia considering situational contexts, we explored mobile media use in diabetes self-management via experience sampling across six waves (June to November 2025) among 102 patients, yielding 4,139 self-management situations involving mobile media. Multilevel latent class analysis identified four situation types that vary by devices used, self-management domains, and physical and social contexts. Further analyses revealed significant differences across the situation types in perceived importance, AI use, injunctive norms, and triggers. Moreover, we identified seven person-level types that differ in self-management behavior but not significantly in sociodemographic or health-related characteristics. Findings underscore the role of mobile media, particularly smartphones, in diabetes self-management, but also highlight their unexploited potential, as situations rarely extend beyond functional routine self-management (e.g., symptom documentation).

articles.title: Incidence rate and factors associated with periprocedural hypoxia during bedside intravitreal ranibizumab injection for retinopathy of prematurity: a multicenter retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy has become an established treatment for type 1 retinopathy of prematurity (ROP). However, evidence regarding intraprocedural hypoxia during bedside intravitreal injection remains limited. This study evaluated the incidence, severity, and predictors of hypoxia during intravitreal ranibizumab injection for treatment-requiring ROP.

METHODS: This retrospective multicenter observational study included premature infants with treatment-requiring ROP who underwent bedside intravitreal ranibizumab injection under topical anesthesia between July 2020 and June 2026 in neonatal intensive care units across the Al Qassim region, Saudi Arabia. Continuous pulse oximetry was used during the procedure and for 30 min afterward. Hypoxia was classified as mild (oxygen saturation 85-89%), moderate (80-84%), or severe (< 80%). Demographic, perinatal, maternal, and ophthalmic variables were analyzed. Logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with hypoxia.

RESULTS: Seventy-four premature infants out of 1430 were included. The mean gestational age was 27.5 ± 2.2 weeks, the mean birth weight was 986.8 ± 265.8 g, and the mean postmenstrual age at treatment was 36.6 ± 2.2 weeks. Hypoxia occurred in 12 infants (16.2%; 95% CI, 8.7-26.6%), including 10 (13.5%) with mild hypoxia and 2 (2.7%) with moderate hypoxia; no episodes of severe hypoxia were observed. Lower gestational age (OR 0.51, 95% CI 0.35-0.76; P = 0.001), lower birth weight (OR 0.991 per gram increase, 95% CI 0.984-0.997; P = 0.004), and longer duration of oxygen therapy (OR 1.35, 95% CI 1.03-1.77; P = 0.028) were associated with hypoxia in univariate analysis. After adjustment, birth weight remained the principal predictor of increasing hypoxia severity. At follow-up, regression of ROP was achieved in 60 infants (81.1%), while 4 (5.4%) required repeat ranibizumab injection and 10 (13.5%) underwent adjunctive laser photocoagulation.

CONCLUSIONS: Bedside intravitreal ranibizumab injection under topical anesthesia was associated with a low incidence of transient hypoxia, and no severe oxygen desaturation events occurred. Lower birth weight and lower gestational age were associated with an increased risk of hypoxia. These findings support the short-term cardiorespiratory safety of bedside ranibizumab injection in premature infants while emphasizing the importance of continuous physiological monitoring, particularly in extremely low-birth-weight infants.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: NCT07701759 obtained on July 8, 2026.

articles.title: Impact of Guideline-Directed Medication Titration Velocity in Patients With Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated whether shorter time to achieving targeted guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) was associated with greater improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). GDMT reduces morbidity and mortality in HFrEF. It is unclear whether the speed of achieving target doses influences improvement in LVEF or related outcomes. This retrospective study included new HFrEF patients seen in a heart failure clinic between January 1st, 2021 and January 1st, 2023 that met study criteria. The primary outcome was improvement in LVEF. Secondary outcomes included reduction in mitral valve regurgitation (MVR) severity and differences in LVEF improvement by provider type. Titration velocity was defined as time from first heart failure visit to attainment of target or maximally tolerated GDMT doses. Eighty-seven patients were included in the study (mean age 61 years; 64.4% male; 58.6% white). After GDMT titration, 90.8% demonstrated improvement in LVEF. Mean time to full GDMT titration was 146.6 days (<6 months). Mean LVEF improvement was 19.5% (<3 months), 19.1% (3-6 months), 21.0% (6-9 months), and 17.3% (>9 months), with no significant difference among groups (P = 0.823). No significant differences were observed in MVR reduction (P = 0.523) or LVEF improvement by provider type (P = 0.703). GDMT titration velocity was not associated with significant differences in LVEF improvement. These findings support individualized GDMT optimization rather than emphasizing rapid dose escalation and suggest potential benefits of longer therapy duration allowing additional time for specialty evaluation and avoiding premature device implantation.

articles.title: PVT1 inhibition alleviates cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury and is associated with stroke diagnosis and severity via MyD88-mediated inflammatory signaling.
articles.journal: In vitro cellular & developmental biology. Animal
articles.abstract: Cerebral ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury is a major cause of neurological disability. This study investigated the role of lncRNA PVT1 in I/R-induced cerebral injury and its clinical relevance. MCAO/reperfusion mouse and OGD/R neuronal cell models were established. Neurological function, infarct volume, brain edema, and neuronal apoptosis were assessed. For clinical validation, 50 acute ischemic stroke patients and 50 healthy controls were enrolled. Serum PVT1/miR-187-3p were measured by qRT-PCR; plasma MyD88 and inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-18) by ELISA. Machine learning (Random Forest) and correlation analyses were performed to evaluate diagnostic utility and relationships with clinical severity (NIHSS score, infarct volume). PVT1 was significantly upregulated under I/R both in vivo and in vitro. Clinically, AIS patients showed markedly elevated PVT1 (3.92 vs. 1.02, p < 0.0001) and reduced miR-187-3p (0.42 vs. 1.01, p < 0.0001), with increased MyD88 and inflammatory cytokines (all p < 0.001). The Random Forest model achieved AUC = 0.92, with PVT1 as the top predictor. PVT1 correlated positively with MyD88 (r = 0.68, p < 0.001) and NIHSS score (r = 0.61, p < 0.001). PVT1 silencing in MCAO mice significantly improved neurological function, reduced infarct volume and brain edema, and attenuated neuronal apoptosis (all p < 0.01). Mechanistically, PVT1 sponged miR-187-3p to derepress MyD88/TLR4 signaling, which was reversed by miR-187-3p restoration. In vivo rescue experiments confirmed that miR-187-3p antagomir reversed the protective effects of PVT1 silencing across multiple endpoints. PVT1 inhibition protects against cerebral I/R injury by restoring miR-187-3p and blocking the MyD88/TLR4 pathway. PVT1 and its downstream axis are associated with stroke diagnosis and severity, and represent promising therapeutic targets and diagnostic biomarkers for ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Resistin is a new player in murine hippocampal neuronal cells: expression and action on cell metabolic activity, proliferation, cell cycle, and expression of selected proliferative and apoptosis genes in HT-22 cells.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Resistin, initially identified as an adipocyte-derived hormone, is associated with obesity, insulin resistance, and diabetes. However, its role in hippocampal neuronal cells remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the effects of resistin on neuronal hippocampal cell function.

METHODS: Expression of Retn and its receptors (Ror1, Cap1, and Tlr4) was analysed in mouse hippocampal HT-22 cells using RT-qPCR. The effects of resistin (0.1, 1, and 10 ng/ml) on metabolic activity (alamarBlue), proliferation (BrdU), cell cycle distribution and apoptosis (Annexin V/PI flow cytometry) were evaluated. Expression of apoptosis- (Bax, Bcl2, caspases-3, -8, -9, and p53) and proliferation-related markers (cyclins A2, B1, D1, and E1) was assessed using RT-qPCR and Western blotting. Activation of ERK1/2 pathway and the involvement of ERK1/2 and TLR4 signalling in resistin action were examined using pharmacological inhibitors.

RESULTS: HT-22 cells expressed resistin and all three investigated receptors. Resistin decreased cellular metabolic activity at 7 h but increased it at 24 h. It stimulated cell proliferation at both time points and altered the cell cycle distribution after 24 h. At a 1 ng/ml, resistin reduced Ccne1 transcript levels and modulated the levels of cyclins and apoptosis-related markers examined. Moreover, resistin decreased the Bax/Bcl2 ratio at both the mRNA and protein levels after 24 h as well as increased ERK1/2 phosphorylation at 5 h. Pharmacological inhibition of ERK1/2 pathway indicated the involvement of ERK1/2 signalling in the resistin-mediated regulation of metabolic activity and proliferation, while TLR4 signalling was involved in the regulation of Casp3 expression and cell proliferation in HT-22 cells.

CONCLUSION: Resistin may act as a novel regulator of hippocampal neuronal cell function.

articles.title: ASO Visual Abstract: Recommendations for the Multimodal Management of Malignant Bowel Obstructions: Results of a North American Multidisciplinary Delphi Consensus.
Independent and joint associations of social determinants of health and circadian syndrome with serum testosterone in adult males.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To examine the association of a multidomain social determinants of health (SDoH) score with serum testosterone and to determine whether circadian syndrome (CircS) modifies this association in adult men.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 5,089 men from NHANES 2011-2016. Survey-weighted linear regression evaluated associations of an eight-component cumulative SDoH score and individual components with testosterone. Interaction terms assessed effect modification by CircS. Sensitivity analyses included a six-component score excluding marital and housing status.

RESULTS: In the fully adjusted model, each one-unit higher SDoH score was associated with 6.46 ng/dL higher testosterone (95% CI 3.81-9.10; P < 0.001), with a positive association across categories. Five component-specific associations were significant, not being married or living with a partner having the largest point estimate and housing tenure being another notable association. Excluding marital and housing status attenuated the association, but the six-component score remained significant (β = 4.97, 95% CI 1.72-8.23; P = 0.003). CircS modified the association (P for interaction = 0.010): it was positive in men without CircS (β = 7.94, 95% CI 5.12-10.76; P < 0.001) but not significant in men with CircS (β = -1.12, 95% CI - 7.59-5.35; P = 0.735). Multiple imputation and other sensitivity analyses supported the primary finding.

CONCLUSION: Higher SDoH scores were associated with higher testosterone, with heterogeneous component-specific associations and attenuation in the presence of CircS. The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.

articles.title: Availability-Aware Prediction of CCTA Findings Using Opportunistic Low-Dose CT and Routine Health-Check Data.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: Laboratory and history data are inconsistently available in health-check records, complicating prediction from combined clinical and imaging inputs. We evaluated an availability-aware ensemble for predicting coronary CT angiography (CCTA) findings in 864 participants, including 221 with Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS) category ≥ 3. Models used eight clinical and 31 low-dose CT (LDCT) inputs, with optional laboratory and history variables. Six learner families underwent fivefold outer and fivefold inner validation; preprocessing, model selection, and cross-fitted sigmoid calibration were confined to outer training data. Calibrated adaptive top-3 aggregation achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.808, average precision of 0.622, and Brier score of 0.14152. Compared with selection of one compatible model, the AUROC difference was + 0.0193 (conditional 95% confidence interval 0.0029-0.0358) and the Brier difference was - 0.01174 (- 0.01723 to - 0.00621). Comparisons with the expanded-pool imputation baseline and common-feature ensembles were inconclusive. Matched analyses supported adding laboratory variables to single-model selection; history increments were uncertain. At threshold 0.15, 29/221 positive cases were missed (13.1%; 95% Wilson interval 9.3-18.2%). Human reviewers considered the proxy measurements acceptable in all 864 analyzed participants. Aggregation improved AUROC and Brier score relative to compatible single-model selection in this cohort. Its additional value over simpler ensembles and its suitability for clinical triage require external and prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Feasibility of Simulated Low-Dose CT with Deep Learning Denoising for Lymphoma PET/CT Imaging: A Clinical Study on Lesion Detection, Staging, and Therapy Response.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: [18F]FDG PET/CT is central to lymphoma staging and treatment-response assessment, but repeated examinations increase cumulative radiation exposure, largely from the CT component. This retrospective study included 152 patients with 211 whole-body PET/CT scans and evaluated whether deep learning-denoised simulated low-dose CT can preserve diagnostic performance. A single-scan cohort of 108 patients was used exclusively for model development, while an independent follow-up cohort of 44 patients (103 examinations) was reserved for quantitative evaluation and a fully crossed multi-reader, multi-case study. Simulated low-dose CT images ranging from 2/3 to 1/8 of the standard dose were reviewed, and the 1/4-dose level was selected as the lowest clinically acceptable level. A denoising model was trained using paired standard-dose CT (SDCT) and simulated low-dose CT at 1/4 of the standard dose (SLDCT) images. Six nuclear medicine physicians evaluated three imaging conditions: PET/CT with SDCT, PET/CT with SLDCT, and PET/CT with denoised SLDCT (D-SLDCT), for image quality, lesion detectability, staging, and treatment response. D-SLDCT significantly improved quantitative image quality compared with SLDCT (all p < 0.0001) and increased subjective image-quality scores (4.11 ± 0.46 vs 3.00 ± 0.00). Staging accuracy was lower under the SLDCT condition than under the SDCT condition (MAE, 1.50 ± 0.27 vs 1.40 ± 0.20; p = 0.0011), whereas the D-SLDCT condition did not differ significantly from the SDCT condition (MAE, 1.44 ± 0.22; p = 0.47). Differences were more pronounced in patients with BMI ≥ 24 kg/m2 and among junior readers. Lesion detectability and treatment-response assessment did not differ significantly across conditions, while within-reader lesion-detection agreement with the SDCT condition improved after denoising (κ = 0.72 vs 0.67). The D-SLDCT condition preserved diagnostic performance, supporting radiation-conscious lymphoma PET/CT. This study was registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR) on February 14, 2026 (registration number: ChiCTR2600119037).

articles.title: Comprehensive geriatric assessment and frailty in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy: toward more individualized and appropriate care.
articles.journal: Netherlands heart journal : monthly journal of the Netherlands Society of Cardiology and the Netherlands Heart Foundation
articles.abstract: Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), once considered a rare disease, is now an increasingly recognized cause of heart failure. This rise in diagnoses is driven by increased awareness, the availability of non-invasive diagnostics, and the introduction of disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) in an aging population. Available DMTs are costly and may require 12 to 18 months before clinical benefit becomes apparent, making careful assessment of expected treatment benefit essential. Because ATTR-CM predominantly affects older adults, frailty, multimorbidity, and competing health risks are common. Frailty is associated with poorer outcomes and reduced quality of life, yet is not captured by current prognostic staging systems, which primarily reflect cardiac disease severity. Frailty assessment may complement cardiac evaluation by supporting personalized DMT decision-making and identifying modifiable vulnerabilities for targeted interventions. This narrative review integrates cardiology and geriatric perspectives to examine the role of Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment, including frailty assessment, in ATTR-CM. Evidence on frailty prevalence, prognostic significance, and the concept of a disease-specific frailty phenotype is summarized. The role and key components of the CGA are outlined. Additionally, a multidisciplinary care pathway incorporating CGA into clinical practice is proposed to support personalized DMT decisions and targeted interventions.

articles.title: Glycemic control is differentially related to spontaneous cortical activity in patients on the Alzheimer's disease spectrum.
articles.abstract: Diabetes is a major risk factor for developing cognitive impairment and studies have shown that poor glycemic control can increase this risk, but the neural mechanisms are poorly understood. Many studies have linked altered spontaneous cortical activity during the resting-state to Alzheimer's disease and other neurological conditions associated with cognitive impairment. Herein, we examine whether the strength of spontaneous activity during the resting-state is differentially related to glycemic control in 37 biomarker-positive participants on the Alzheimer's disease spectrum (ADS) and 43 cognitively normal aging adults. All participants completed resting-state magnetoencephalography (MEG), a blood draw to derive their level of glycemic control (i.e., A1C), and comprehensive neuropsychological assessment. Spontaneous activity was imaged in each of the canonical frequency bands (e.g., alpha) and probed for group differences in the relationship between neural activity and glycemic control. We found significant interactions between A1C and disease status (ADS vs. control) in the delta and alpha bands (p <  0.001). Specifically, delta power decreased with increasing A1C in the ADS group across a broad area of frontotemporal and inferior parietal cortices, while spontaneous alpha decreased with higher A1C in the control group across inferior frontal and temporal cortex. Importantly, delta activity in the superior frontal cortices mediated the effect of A1C on attention performance in the ADS group. In sum, these data suggest that the impact of glycemic dysregulation on spontaneous cortical activity may differ in those on the ADS compared with cognitively normal controls and that spontaneous delta may be critical for attention function.

articles.title: Blood Metal Concentrations and Heart Failure: Stratified Associations by Smoking Status and Selenium Levels with Mendelian Randomization.
articles.abstract: Chronic heavy metal exposure is ubiquitous, yet its association with heart failure (HF) remains unclear. Cross-sectional studies on nutritional biomarkers are susceptible to co-exposure confounding and non-linearity. We analyzed 15,996 U.S. adults from NHANES 2015-2023 using survey-weighted logistic regression, mutual adjustment models, restricted cubic splines (RCS), and two mixture models (qgcomp and WQS). To distinguish observational correlations from causal effects, two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) was performed for selenium. Cadmium was consistently associated with higher HF odds across all observational models (OR per 2-fold = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.08-1.45), and WQS identified it as the major positive contributor (72.6% weight). Crucially, the inverse selenium-HF association (OR per 2-fold = 0.40) remained robust after mutual adjustment for cadmium and all other metals (OR = 0.39, 95% CI: 0.20-0.76), indicating it is not explained by co-exposure confounding. However, MR provided no evidence of a direct causal protective effect (IVW OR = 1.01, 95% CI: 0.99-1.03). While the multiplicative interaction was not statistically significant (P = 0.154), the cadmium association was prominent in the low-selenium stratum (OR = 1.45) but not observed in the high-selenium stratum (OR = 0.94). Furthermore, the cadmium association was stronger among current and former smokers (P for interaction < 0.001). Cadmium is the metal most consistently associated with prevalent HF, and this association is modified by smoking status and selenium levels. The inverse selenium-HF association is robust to co-exposure confounding but lacks genetic causal support, suggesting it is not a direct cardioprotective effect. Future studies with better cumulative exposure biomarkers are needed to establish cadmium causality.

articles.title: Eutectic Mixture as a Novel Approach to Improve Compression Properties of Metformin Hydrochloride.
articles.abstract: Metformin hydrochloride (MET), an antidiabetic medication, possesses poor compression properties and severe elastic recovery, hindering its formulation via direct compaction. This study engineered MET eutectic mixture and cocrystals using freeze-drying and evaluated them for overcoming these compression liabilities and minimizing punch sticking propensity. Niacinamide (NI), a flexible carboxamide micronutrient beneficial in diabetes management, was evaluated alongside D-Mannitol (MAN), a brittle polyol benchmark excipient, at 1:1 and 1:2 molar ratios. Solid-state characterization (PXRD, FTIR, DSC and TGA) confirmed that both adjuvants yield a eutectic mixture at a 1:1 ratio and a distinct cocrystal phase at a 1:2 ratio. Morphologically, the MET-NI systems exhibited unique layered microstructures. Mechanical profile assessment showed that MET-NI eutectic mixture and cocrystals drastically improved MET plasticity, showing significantly reduced yield pressure via Heckel analysis compared to their corresponding physical mixtures. Consequently, the MET-NI systems displayed enhanced compactibility and tabletability, producing mechanically stable tablets at high drug-coformer loadings (99.5% w/w). Conversely, the MET-MAN formulations exhibited dominant brittle deformation, resulting in severe tablet lamination and capping at compaction pressures exceeding 150 MPa. Furthermore, punch sticking assessment revealed that the enhanced internal tablet strength (API:coformer - API:coformer bonding interaction) of MET-NI eutectics and cocrystals reduced punch sticking mass up to 10-fold compared to the physical mixture. This work demonstrates that particle engineering, particularly utilizing eutectic mixture approach via freeze-drying with flexible carboxamides like niacinamide, presents a highly viable approach for modifying the micromechanical properties of problematic drugs to facilitate seamless large-scale direct compaction manufacturing.

articles.title: Evening amber-lensed glasses in combination with a prescribed wake time advance circadian timing in adolescents with delayed sleep-wake phase disorder.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: We tested whether wearing amber glasses during evening hours and a stable wake time advances circadian and sleep timing of adolescent patients with delayed sleep-wake phase disorder (DSWPD).

METHODS: Adolescents (14.3-18.1 years; n = 36 randomized) with DSWPD completed a 3-week study. Dim light melatonin onset (DLMO) was measured after 1 week of habitual sleep/wake. During the next 2 weeks, participants were randomized to one of two groups: the treatment group wore amber-lensed glasses, and a control group wore clear-lensed glasses nightly, starting 7 h before midpoint of baseline sleep, and ending at self-selected bedtime or for 7 h, whichever was shorter. Treatment group participants were additionally instructed to wake at their average baseline school-day wake time (± 15 min). Final DLMO was measured at the end.

RESULTS: The treatment group advanced 40 ± 84 min and the control group delayed - 29 ± 50 min [t(26) = - 2.63, p = .01]. Despite circadian phase changes, weeknight sleep onset and duration remained stable with the amber glasses + stable wake intervention. Weekday wake-up time did not differ between groups; however, the Treatment group woke earlier on weekends during the glasses weeks compared to the Control group [t(25) = 4.13, p < .001], resulting in more stable sleep times across the week.

CONCLUSION: Amber glasses in the evening with fixed wake times shifted circadian phase earlier among adolescents with DSWPD. Although sleep onset did not advance, sleep timing was more consistent across the week. This strategy represents a readily implemented cost-effective intervention to advance the circadian clock and reduce social jet lag in a difficult-to-treat young patient group. Additional directives may be needed to effect other sleep-related outcomes. Current knowledge/study rationale Adolescent patients with DSWPD are at high risk for deleterious sleep-related outcomes. Feasible and effective treatment interventions are sparse.

STUDY IMPACT: Amber glasses timed strategically in the evening with a fixed wake time was associated with circadian phase advances and reduced sleep variability. This intervention is cost-effective and readily implemented. Since physiological changes did not translate into changes in additional sleep/wake behaviors, however, future treatment approaches need to be further refined and delineated.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Registry: ClinicalTrials.gov, Title: Glasses for Adolescent Delayed Sleep-Wake Phase Disorder, Identifier: NCT04378933, URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04378933.

articles.title: Impact of nipple-areola complex micropigmentation on quality of life, body image, and sexuality among women after mastectomy: a mixed-methods study.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate changes in quality of life, body image, and sexual well-being following nipple-areola complex micropigmentation in women who had undergone mastectomy and breast reconstruction.

METHODS: A mixed-methods study with a pre-post, analytical, longitudinal, and prospective design was conducted in a final sample of 18 women who had undergone mastectomy and subsequent breast reconstruction. Quantitative data were collected using validated quality-of-life questionnaires administered before and after micropigmentation. Qualitative data were collected using a structured questionnaire with 13 open-ended questions and analysed using thematic analysis.

RESULTS: Significant pre-post changes were observed in global health status, emotional functioning, and body image, together with changes in sexuality-related dimensions. Qualitative findings described improvements in body perception, emotional well-being, confidence, and comfort in intimate and social contexts. Participants also identified informational, geographical, economic, and emotional barriers to accessing the procedure.

CONCLUSION: Quantitative and qualitative findings showed convergent changes in quality of life, body image, emotional well-being, and sexual well-being following nipple-areola complex micropigmentation. However, the uncontrolled single-group pre-post design does not allow causal inference. Further comparative studies with larger samples, longer follow-up, and greater population diversity are needed to strengthen the evidence regarding the effectiveness and longer-term impact of nipple-areola complex micropigmentation.

articles.title: Operative versus nonoperative management of olecranon fractures in older adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Displaced olecranon fractures in the frail geriatric patient represent a therapeutic challenge, involving the decision between operating to achieve anatomical reduction of the articular surface or not operating due to the high risks associated with poor bone quality and failure of mechanical fixation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane were systematically searched for studies published from inception through February 2026 comparing tension band wiring, plate fixation, or cerclage wiring with nonoperative treatment for displaced olecranon fractures in geriatric patients. Risk ratio (RR) was used to evaluate binary outcomes, and standard mean difference (SMD) for continuous outcomes, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Of 459 articles, eight studies were included. A total of 723 older adults were included. Most patients had Mayo type IIA or IIB fractures. Tension band wiring was the most frequently performed surgical technique, followed by plate fixation and cerclage wiring. Operative treatment was associated with a lower risk of radiographic nonunion (RR 0.19; 95% CI 0.04, 0.8) but increased the risk of overall complications (RR 3.21; 95% CI 1.63, 6.35) and reoperation (RR 4.85; 95% CI 1.72, 13.65) compared to nonoperative treatment. Physical function showed a non-significant trend toward improvement with operative treatment (SMD -0.29; 95% CI -0.72, 0.14). At final follow-up, pain intensity was low and comparable between the two treatment groups across the majority of studies. Approximately half of the reoperation excess comprised elective or symptomatic implant removal, and the overall certainty of the evidence is low.

CONCLUSION: In older adults with displaced olecranon fractures, operative management was associated with a reduced risk of radiographic nonunion and with a higher risk of complications and reoperation compared to nonoperative management.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III Systematic Review/MetaAnalysis Treatment Study.

articles.title: A comparison of outcomes of scrotal vs non-scrotal inguinal hernia repairs in men: an ACHQC analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Scrotal hernias can be technically challenging to the surgeon; however, outcomes are not well studied compared to other types of inguinal hernias. The purpose of this project is to compare outcomes of scrotal vs non-scrotal inguinal hernia repairs utilizing a large hernia registry.

METHODS: The ACHQ database was queried from inception until 12/31/2023 and include all elective hernia repairs in men with scrotal, lateral, or medial defects. Using propensity scoring, operative details as well as post-operative outcomes were compared between scrotal and non-scrotal hernia cohorts. Primary outcome measures were 30-day complication and re-operation rates with secondary outcomes being 30-day SSO/SSI and recurrence rate. Descriptive statistics were generated and comparisons of outcome measures based on type of hernia defects were performed.

RESULTS: A total of 13,764 patients met inclusion criteria, and after propensity matching was performed, a total of 4.532 patients were matched including 1662 scrotal hernia and 2870 non-scrotal hernia. Scrotal hernias were associated with significantly longer operative times and higher rates of partial or total excision of the ilioinguinal nerve intraoperatively. In terms of 30-day outcomes, scrotal hernias were associated with longer hospital stays, more readmissions, as well as higher rates of surgical site occurrence (SSO), SSO/SSI, as well as SSO/SSI requiring procedural intervention. Scrotal hernias were associated with higher one and two year recurrence rates but there was no significant difference in recurrence rates at years 3-5.

CONCLUSION: Although scrotal hernias have some worse outcomes in regard to several measures overall outcomes are comparable to non-scrotal hernias. Surgeons should be aware of the higher rate of SSO's and hernia recurrences at 1 and 2 years in scrotal hernias.

articles.title: Ketogenic diet ameliorates diabetic kidney disease but promotes renal lipid and calcium deposition.
articles.abstract: The ketogenic diet (KD) is widely used for weight loss and the treatment of type 2 diabetes (T2D), yet its impact on diabetic kidney disease (DKD) remains unclear. Here, we show that KD induces weight loss, normalizes hyperglycemia, and promotes sustained ketosis, leading to improved structural and functional features of DKD in a mouse model of T2D, effects not fully recapitulated by exogenous ketone supplementation. Despite these improvements, KD promotes ectopic lipid accumulation and calcium deposition within the kidney. Mechanistically, KD lowers circulating lipids while increasing the circulating abundance of ApoB48-containing intestinal triglyceride-rich lipoproteins and enhancing renal lipid processing, fatty acid uptake, and triglyceride synthesis. In parallel, KD induces hypercalciuria and renal calcification through increased intestinal calcium absorption, driven by activation of the renal-intestinal vitamin D axis, but independent of bone resorption. Together, these findings demonstrate that KD confers renoprotective effects while inducing metabolic adaptations that may compromise renal health.

articles.title: Genomic and multi-omic insights into the heterogeneity of diabetic kidney disease.
articles.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a leading cause of kidney failure and excess morbidity and mortality. Once regarded as a uniform microvascular complication of chronic hyperglycaemia, DKD is now recognized as a biologically and clinically heterogeneous condition. Not all chronic kidney disease in individuals with diabetes can be attributed to diabetes, and distinguishing DKD from non-diabetic kidney disease (non-DKD) is essential for appropriate management. Multiple interacting pathways, including hyperglycaemia, haemodynamic stress, dyslipidaemia, obesity, inflammation and ancestry-specific genetic risk, drive diverse patterns of kidney injury and clinical trajectories. Conventional classification based on glomerular filtration rate or albuminuria alone fails to capture this complexity. Emerging multi-omics approaches are reshaping our understanding of DKD by identifying genomic, epigenomic, proteomic and metabolomic signatures that stratify risk, elucidate mechanisms and inform therapeutic response. Integration of these molecular layers with polygenic scores, data-driven clustering and single-cell kidney atlases is beginning to define disease endotypes and guide precision-medicine strategies. Large-scale collaborative efforts that combine deep phenotyping, biobanking and advanced analytics are accelerating the translation of molecular heterogeneity into actionable biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Despite ongoing challenges - including the need for validation, equitable representation and clinical implementation - omics-driven precision approaches offer the potential to transform DKD management by reducing residual risk and enabling more effective, precision interventions.

articles.title: Family experiences with genetic/genomic testing in the pediatric intensive care unit.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Genetic testing is increasingly utilized in neonatal and pediatric intensive care units (NICUs and PICUs, respectively) for diagnosis and management. Despite this, research on family experiences and genetic testing is limited, especially in the PICU. Our previous NICU study emphasized the importance of communication in conveying test results. Similar to the NICU, PICU settings raise parental stress and uncertainty. We aimed to identify considerations to increase empowerment for parents undergoing genetic testing in the PICU and compare our results to previous NICU findings. The following mixed-methods study, conducted at BC Children's Hospital in Vancouver, British Columbia, included a demographic and validated empowerment survey (EMPATHIC-38) and semi-structured interviews with caregivers of children who underwent genetic testing in the PICU. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Interviews were analyzed using an interpretive description framework and thematic analysis. Transcripts were coded by two independent coders, and themes were finalized. Eleven semi-structured interviews and 12 empowerment surveys were completed. The organization (Mean = 5.79/6.00 ± 0.16) and professional attitude (Mean = 5.77/6.00 ± 0.17) domains scored the highest. The lowest-scoring domain was parental participation (Mean = 5.43/6.00 ± 0.15), measuring healthcare professionals' attitudes toward parental engagement in care. Identified themes included: preferences for different formats for receiving results, considerations for different languages, understandable language, impact on extended family members, funding for testing, and long-term clinical management.

CONCLUSION: In contrast to the NICU, PICU parents showed greater consideration for extended family members and long-term management, with a clear preference for educational materials. Parents in both ICUs identified the need for a clear explanation of uninformative and positive results.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Despite the growing implementation of genetic testing for critically ill children, the evaluation of caregivers' experiences for those undergoing this process is limited, particularly in the PICU. • Factors affecting parental empowerment for caregivers in the PICU environment are critical to tailor family-centred care.

WHAT IS NEW: • PICU-specific considerations for navigating challenges between healthcare professionals and families were identified, which are in contrast to previous findings in the NICU. • To increase caregivers' empowerment, both genetic and nongenetic healthcare professionals should work together with caregivers to navigate various aspects of genetic testing, including funding, timeline, potential diagnoses, long-term clinical management, and implications for extended family members.

articles.title: Pertuzumab in HER2-positive breast cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: HER2-positive breast cancer is a distinct subtype associated with less favorable outcomes without targeted therapy. Dual HER2 blockade with pertuzumab and trastuzumab has shown improved efficacy compared to single-agent approaches, but results across studies remain variable. This meta-analysis aims to evaluate the overall efficacy and safety of pertuzumab-based regimens.

METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library was conducted to identify relevant RCTs. The quality of trials was assessed using the ROB-2 tool, and the certainty of the evidence was assessed using the GRADE tool. Data were synthesized using R.

RESULTS: This study included 8 RCTs with 8367 patients. Pertuzumab-based regimens were associated with improved overall survival. In the locally advanced or metastatic setting, a pronounced benefit was observed (HR = 0.71, 95% CI 0.65-0.77). However, in the neoadjuvant or adjuvant setting, the pooled hazard ratio (HR = 0.81, 95% CI 0.22-3.04), which was not significant. Progression-free survival (HR 0.74; 95% CI 0.67-0.83) was improved compared with the control group. In terms of safety, there was no significant difference in the incidence of any adverse events (risk ratio (RR) = 1.01; 95% CI 0.99-1.02) or grade ≥ 3 adverse events (RR 0.99; 95% CI 0.86-1.13) between the experimental and control groups.

CONCLUSION: Pertuzumab-based dual HER2 blockade is associated with significant improvements in overall survival and progression-free survival in patients with metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer. Importantly, these survival benefits are not accompanied by a significant increase in overall or severe adverse events, supporting its favorable efficacy-safety profile across clinical settings.

articles.title: Dose-dense neoadjuvant bi-weekly nab-paclitaxel followed by epirubicin-cyclophosphamide versus bi-weekly docetaxel followed by epirubicin-cyclophosphamide in patients with HR+/HER2- early breast cancer: a multicentre, randomised, phase III trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dose-dense adjuvant chemotherapy prolongs survival in breast cancer and has been translated into neoadjuvant settings. Although weekly nanoparticle albumin-bound (nab)-paclitaxel yields superior pathological complete response (pCR) rates relative to solvent-based paclitaxel, data supporting its incorporation into a dose-dense neoadjuvant regimen-particularly for hormone receptor positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 negative (HR+/HER2-) tumours-remain limited. This trial therefore evaluated whether a bi-weekly dose-dense nab-paclitaxel schedule improves the proportion of residual cancer burden (RCB) 0/Ⅰ compared with a comparable dose-dense docetaxel regimen, each followed by dose-dense epirubicin plus cyclophosphamide.

METHODS: This was a multicentre, randomised, phase III trial done at three hospitals in China. HR⁺/HER2⁻ patients (cT1-3/N0-1/M0) were randomised 1:1 using dynamic allocation with Pocock minimisation on Ki-67 and TNM stage. The experimental arm received nab-paclitaxel 260 mg/m² intravenously on day 1 every two weeks for four cycles; the control arm received docetaxel 100 mg/m² on the identical schedule. Both cohorts subsequently received epirubicin 90 mg/m² plus cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² intravenously on day 1 every two weeks for four cycles. Primary endpoints were RCB 0/Ⅰ rate; secondary endpoints encompassed disease free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and safety.

RESULTS: Between December 2019 and December 2020, 388 patients (194 per arm) were enrolled. The nab-paclitaxel arm attained an RCB 0/Ⅰ rate of 20.1% (95% CI 14.41-26.72), significantly exceeding the docetaxel arm's 11.34% (95% CI 6.92-15.81; χ²=5.62, P = 0.018). pCR was achieved in 15.98% (95% CI 10.81-21.16) of the nab-paclitaxel group versus 10.31% (95% CI 6.01-14.60) of the docetaxel group (χ²=2.73, P = 0.098). Multivariate analysis confirmed a statistically significant favourable impact of nab-paclitaxel on RCB 0/Ⅰ. Five-year DFS was comparable (90.21% vs. 87.11%; HR: 1.14, 95% CI 0.64-2.05; P = 0.656), as was five-year OS (96.34% vs. 95.31%; HR: 0.64, 95% CI 0.29-1.42; P = 0.274), indicating no significant survival disparity. Grade 3/4 adverse event incidence was similar (30% vs. 38%). The most frequent all-grade toxicities (neutropenia, nausea, myalgia) occurred at comparable rates; however, grade 3/4 peripheral sensory neuropathy was observed exclusively in the nab-paclitaxel cohort. No treatment-related mortality was reported.

CONCLUSIONS: A bi-weekly dose-dense nab-paclitaxel regimen followed by dose-dense epirubicin-cyclophosphamide constitutes a feasible and efficacious neoadjuvant strategy for early stage HR+/HER2- breast cancer, delivering a higher RCB 0/Ⅰ rate without compromising overall safety. The increased incidence of high-grade peripheral neuropathy mandates vigilant monitoring, yet the regimen represents a valuable addition to contemporary neoadjuvant options.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT04182568, Date of registration: 2019-08-21.

articles.title: Clinical recommendations for the inpatient management of lower respiratory tract infections in children and adolescents with severe neurological impairment in Germany-2026 Update.
articles.abstract: Children and adolescents with severe neurological impairment (SNI) require specialized care due to their complex medical needs. These patients often experience severe, recurrent lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs). These infections, of both viral and bacterial etiology, pose a significant risk to these patients, often resulting in respiratory insufficiency and long-term impairments. Based on expert consensus and newly available data, we have updated the previous 2024 clinical recommendations on the management of LRTIs in children and adolescents with SNI in Germany. This update now also addresses multidrug-resistant organism colonization, respiratory support, discharge planning, and prophylactic strategies. The recommendations emphasize comprehensive multidisciplinary care, antimicrobial stewardship, and a stepwise, risk-stratified approach to antibiotic therapy. Initial treatment should involve symptomatic care, including hydration, antipyretics, oxygen therapy, secretion management, and respiratory as well as cough support. In suspected bacterial LRTIs, antibiotic treatment (ABT) should be guided by clinical severity, previous microbiological findings, and treatment response, with an aminopenicillin plus a beta-lactamase inhibitor recommended for community-acquired LRTIs and piperacillin-tazobactam reserved for selected high-risk patients. Ongoing management includes regular reassessment, adjustment of ABT based on pathogen identification, and optimization of supportive care.Conclusion: The updated recommendations provide a practical, multidisciplinary framework for the inpatient management of LRTIs in children and adolescents with SNI, combining optimized supportive care with antimicrobial stewardship and a stepwise, risk-stratified approach to antibiotic treatment. What is Known: • Children and adolescents with severe neurological impairment are particularly affected by severe and recurrent lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI) • The indication and choice of antibiotic therapy for bacterial LRTI is often difficult because there are no evidence-based treatment recommendations for this heterogeneous but vulnerable patient population • The frequent overuse of broad-spectrum or reserve antibiotics in this patient population increases selection pressure for multidrug-resistant pathogens What is New: • Compared with the 2024 recommendations, this update provides more detailed guidance on secretion management and respiratory and cough support, introduces explicit discharge criteria, and expands decision-making for patients colonized with multidrug-resistant organisms. The antibiotic strategy has been further specified regarding broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy, while preventive recommendations have been expanded and updated.

articles.title: High-frequency jet ventilation.
articles.abstract: High-frequency jet ventilation (HFJV) is a ventilation mode that has been available to treat neonatal respiratory failure for more than 35 years. Compared to high-frequency oscillatory ventilation, HFJV can support ventilation with relatively lower mean airway pressures and longer passive expiration. As such, HFJV is often used to treat complex respiratory conditions such as pulmonary hypoplasia, severe pulmonary interstitial emphysema, congenital lung diseases and heterogenous lung states (such as evolving chronic lung disease), in addition to rescue therapy for primary respiratory failure. Common to all these conditions is the need to match ventilator settings to the pathophysiological mechanical and end-expiratory needs. There is renewed interest in HFJV as a potential lung protective modality, especially in the most developmentally immature lungs. The aim of this review is to provide a clinical practice summary of HFJV and the application in different lung conditions. IMPACT: High-frequency jet ventilation is most often used in complex neonatal lung conditions such as pulmonary hypoplasia, interstitial emphysema, the most developmentally immature lungs and gas trapping. High-frequency jet ventilation offers theoretical advantages in these conditions compared to other modalities but safe and effective application also requires greater understanding of mode of action.
