This review aims to provide clinicians with a practical summary of HFJV, specifically an approach to setting HFJV parameters in clinical practice, important clinical considerations and future research priorities to address critical knowledge gaps.

articles.title: Long-term fatigue dimensions in the Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory (MFI) up to five years after radiotherapy and their trajectories in men diagnosed with non-metastatic prostate cancer in the international REQUITE study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fatigue is a common, multidimensional symptom in cancer patients. Little is known about fatigue dimensions and their trajectories in prostate cancer (PCa).

METHODS: Using the Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory (MFI), 1097 men treated with radiotherapy for non-metastatic PCa (2014-2016) prospectively reported fatigue up to five years later. Prevalent fatigue was defined as scores ≥75th percentile in men aged ≥60 years in a German general population sample. Pre-radiotherapy patient characteristics were examined for their associations with general fatigue, physical fatigue, mental fatigue, reduced activity, and reduced motivation two years later using logistic regression models. Fatigue trajectories up to two years post-radiotherapy were explored using latent class growth analysis and multinomial regression.

RESULTS: About 72% (785/1097) of patients reported being fatigued for at least one dimension in the MFI from before the start of radiotherapy up to five years later, with 45% (367/816) being fatigued two years post-radiotherapy. Pre-radiotherapy fatigue level (OR: 4.7-9.0), depression (OR: 2.5), diabetes (OR: 1.8-2.2), hypertension (OR: 1.6-1.8), and BMI (OR: 1.8-2.2) were statistically significant predictors of long-term fatigue two years post-radiotherapy across dimensions. Depression, BMI, and pelvic radiotherapy were associated with experiencing a high fatigue trajectory.

CONCLUSIONS: Early fatigue assessments, in addition to self-reported comorbidities and BMI, showed additional benefits beyond symptom detection by providing prognostic value for poorer long-term fatigue outcomes. Multidimensional fatigue assessments could guide tailored symptom management strategies, targeting specific dimensions to address associated impairments in quality of life and functioning.

articles.title: Metabolic Messengers: endotrophin.
articles.abstract: Endotrophin (ETP), a C-terminal cleavage fragment of the collagen VI α3 chain, has emerged as a key mediator of fibroinflammation and a clinically relevant biomarker of disease progression. Accumulating evidence from both preclinical models and human studies implicates elevated ETP levels as a driver of tissue remodelling, metabolic dysfunction, inflammation and fibrosis across multiple organ systems. Increased ETP has been linked to obesity-associated adipose tissue dysfunction, steatotic liver disease, breast cancer progression, chronic kidney disease and cardiovascular disease, underscoring its broad pathological relevance. The convergence of mechanistic and clinical data positions ETP as a promising therapeutic target across a range of diseases linked by common ETP-driven dysfunction. Here we synthesize current knowledge of ETP's regulation and functions, critically evaluate its role in diverse disease contexts and outline key unanswered questions and emerging strategies for therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: A DiRECT route to type 2 diabetes mellitus remission.

Clinical outcomes associated with angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors versus mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist initiation in patients with hypertension without heart failure: a propensity score-matched study.
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract: Angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors (ARNIs) and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) lower blood pressure, but evidence directly comparing their clinical outcomes in patients with hypertension without heart failure is limited. We compared long-term outcomes associated with ARNI versus MRA initiation in this population. Adults with essential hypertension without heart failure were included if they had documented use of an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor or angiotensin II receptor blocker plus at least one additional antihypertensive drug class. Patients receiving sacubitril or spironolactone or eplerenone after a 1-year washout period were assigned to the ARNI and MRA cohorts, respectively. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes were a composite of acute myocardial infarction and stroke, acute kidney injury (AKI), acute myocardial infarction, and stroke. Outcomes were assessed for up to 1095 days. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 11,832 patients were included in each group. During follow-up, the rates of all-cause mortality in the ARNI and the MRA groups were 7.6% (894 patients) and 10.2% (1 201 patients), respectively. The ARNI group compared to MRA group was associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality, stroke, and AKI, whereas no significant differences were observed in the composite cardiovascular outcome or acute myocardial infarction. Mean systolic blood pressure was modestly lower in the ARNI group, while diastolic blood pressure and the most recently recorded estimated glomerular filtration rate were similar between groups. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective studies.

articles.title: Winter awakening routine for attenuating the morning blood pressure surge.
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular events cluster in the early morning and peak in winter, when the morning blood pressure surge is accentuated by cold. The Japanese Society of Hypertension has identified the winter morning as a critical window in which cold stress, awakening-related sympathetic activation, physical activity, and arising from bed converge, and has recommended gentle activity such as light stretching and deep breathing on waking, without specifying its content. For a national public broadcaster, under the Society's supervision, we designed a 2-minute routine to be performed in bed after awakening: five slow, deep breaths combined with a whole-body stretch, slow rolling from side to side, ankle circles and ankle pumps, followed by sitting up in stages on the bed and five shoulder-blade lifts combined with slow, deep breathing and gentle neck extension before standing. We describe the physiological rationale for each element, drawing on evidence that the morning rise in blood pressure is related mainly to arising rather than awakening, that slow breathing enhances baroreflex sensitivity, that neck posture modulates carotid sinus input, that the blood pressure response to physical activity predicts the morning surge and is heightened in winter and older age, and that orthostatic hypertension is linked to the surge. The routine is intended to make the rise from the sleep trough to the standing morning blood pressure slower and smoother, and thereby to lower the morning peak. Future studies using ambulatory blood pressure monitoring on winter mornings are needed to test whether the routine attenuates the morning surge.

articles.title: Toward patient-centered blood pressure monitoring: validation of a novel low-pressure and rapid oscillometric method according to the ISO 81060-2:2018/Amd1:2020/Amd2:2024 standard.
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract: Out-of-office blood pressure (BP) measurement is central to contemporary hypertension management. However, conventional oscillometric BP monitors often require substantial cuff inflation, potentially causing discomfort, sleep disturbance, and reduced adherence to repeated BP measurement. We developed a novel low-pressure and rapid oscillometric method designed to reduce the cuff pressure and measurement duration while maintaining accuracy. Here, we evaluated the novel automated upper-arm BP monitor incorporating this method (i.e., the Omron HEM-7290T) according to the ISO 81060-2:2018/Amd1:2020/Amd2:2024 standard. The device was assessed in 85 adults using the ISO same-arm sequential measurement protocol. Reference BP values were obtained by simultaneous auscultation. The device's performance was evaluated according to Criteria 1 and 2 of the ISO standard. For Criterion 1, the mean device-observer differences were 0.5  ±  7.09 mmHg for systolic BP (SBP) and 0.6  ±  5.50 mmHg for diastolic BP (DBP). For Criterion 2, the standard deviations of the subject-level mean differences were 5.79 mmHg for SBP and 5.05 mmHg for DBP. All results fulfilled the ISO 81060-2:2018/Amd1:2020/Amd2:2024 validation requirements across the required BP and arm circumference distributions. The Omron HEM-7290T successfully fulfilled ISO validation requirements in adults with 20- to 45-cm arm circumferences. These findings demonstrate that a low-pressure and rapid oscillometric method can achieve international-standard accuracy while potentially reducing the measurement burden. This study provides the clinical validation of a patient-centered BP monitoring technology designed to improve comfort without compromising performance, with potential applications in home BP monitoring, nocturnal BP assessment, and digital hypertension management.

articles.title: B-type natriuretic peptide and subsequent kidney function decline in the general population with preserved kidney function.
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract: Elevated B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) concentrations reflect cardiac stress and are associated with adverse kidney outcomes in patients with established chronic kidney disease (CKD). However, whether modest elevations in BNP are associated with subsequent deterioration in kidney function among individuals with preserved kidney function remains unclear. We investigated 15,071 Japanese adults with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m² and without overt cardiac disease who participated in annual health check-ups. Plasma BNP was measured at baseline, and the primary renal outcome was the first occurrence of an eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m². Median baseline BNP was 8.6 pg/mL (6.9 in men and 11.4 in women). During a median follow-up of 2154 days (95,368 person-years), 2824 participants reached the primary renal outcome (29.6 per 1000 person-years). Event rates increased across sex-specific BNP quartiles (24.0, 26.8, 29.7, and 40.1 per 1000 person-years from the first to fourth quartiles, respectively). After adjustment for established risk factors and baseline serum creatinine, higher baseline BNP remained significantly associated with the primary renal outcome (HR for the fourth vs. first quartile, 1.659; 95% CI, 1.473-1.868). Higher baseline BNP was also associated with a more negative annual eGFR slope. In a sensitivity analysis incorporating dipstick proteinuria, the association remained significant. Higher baseline BNP is therefore associated with subsequent deterioration in kidney function among individuals with preserved baseline eGFR.

articles.title: Cause of death in preterm infants-the black hole of scientific reports on outcomes and prognostication a narrative perspective.
articles.journal: Journal of perinatology : official journal of the California Perinatal Association
articles.abstract: Accurate determination of a cause of death (COD) is fundamental for neonatal quality assessment, parental counseling, and epidemiologic surveillance. Declining autopsy rates raise concerns about the reliability of assigned CODs. Misclassification of COD distorts mortality statistics, hinders understanding of preventable conditions, and limits opportunities for system-level improvement. This narrative review examines literature on infant COD determination and discusses discrepancies between clinically assigned and autopsy-confirmed CODs. Studies show that a substantial proportion of infants were misdiagnosed prior to autopsy. We supplement this with original data from the neonatal unit at Uppsala University Children's Hospital in Sweden, illustrating discordance between clinically assigned and autopsy-confirmed COD and highlighting subgroups where autopsy proved valuable. Furthermore, we discuss declining autopsy rates and their implications for medicine, families, and quality assessment. Understanding CODs in infants is essential for advancing neonatology. Despite advances in diagnostic technology, autopsy remains the gold standard for determining COD and identifying missed diagnoses.

articles.title: Noninvasive assessments for identifying peripheral artery disease described within guidelines, consensus, and best practice statements: A rapid systematic review.
articles.abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects approximately 4% of adults and is associated with lower-limb pain, reduced function, ulceration, amputation, and an increased likelihood of cardiovascular events. Noninvasive vascular testing methods are essential for accurate diagnosis to enable clinicians to deliver appropriate management. Clinical guidelines, consensus statements, and best practice documents are commonly used to guide practice. The quality of these documents, how well they specify the populations requiring screening, assessment, and the most appropriate noninvasive tests to use when diagnosing PAD is currently unclear. This rapid systematic review identified 37 national and international guidelines, consensus statements, or best practice documents that included information on noninvasive assessments for PAD diagnosis published up to 2025. The quality of these documents was assessed using the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research and Evaluation Instrument 2 or Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) appraisal checklist for textual evidence (policy/consensus guidelines), and scores varied substantially, with contemporary documents generally yielding higher scores. Common reasons for lower scores were a lack of systematic methods used to derive recommendations and inadequate engagement with key stakeholders, such as end-users. Within the documents, signs and symptoms of PAD consistently listed as indicators for further vascular assessment were intermittent claudication, rest pain, gangrene, and nonhealing wounds. Other prompts for vascular assessments were traditional cardiovascular risk factors, with some newer guidelines highlighting additional risk factors such as end-stage renal disease, First Nations ancestry, and lack of physical activity. There was varying guidance on the use and interpretation of the tests. Many documents did not consider the changes in diagnostic performance that occur in noninvasive tests in people with diabetes or renal disease. Some newer documents included clinical assessment pathways, which were considered beneficial in simplifying the assessment and interpretation process for clinicians. Although some high-quality documents with strong evidence-based recommendations were identified, there was a gap in comprehensive guidance that could be applied in a variety of settings and patient cohorts. Therefore, the development of an evidence-based, co-designed comprehensive guidance document for noninvasive vascular assessment is warranted.

articles.title: Chronic preoperative benzodiazepine use and perioperative outcomes: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Expert clinical guidelines discourage routine benzodiazepine premedication in older adults because of associations with adverse postoperative outcomes, including delirium and prolonged length of stay. However, these recommendations primarily address acute administration, whereas chronic preoperative benzodiazepine use for non-surgical indications remains incompletely understood, and the relevant evidence has not been comprehensively synthesised. This scoping review characterised the literature on chronic preoperative benzodiazepine use and perioperative outcomes by mapping study characteristics, definitions of chronic use, and associated outcome domains and trends.

METHODS: Published and grey literature were searched across MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, Scopus, and thesis databases. Screening and full-text review were performed independently in duplicate. Eligible studies included adults undergoing surgery with chronic preoperative benzodiazepine use and excluded studies in which benzodiazepines were administered exclusively within 24 h of surgery. This scoping review was preregistered with the Open Science Framework (10.17605/OSF.IO/573JG).

RESULTS: A total of 130 studies were included. Most were observational cohorts (n=109, 83.8%) and examined benzodiazepines as a secondary variable (n=100, 77.0%). Definitions of chronic use were heterogeneous, ranging from 1 month to >1 yr before surgery; duration was not systematically defined in 62 studies (47.7%). Postoperative opioid use (n=53, 40.8%) and delirium or cognitive impairment (n=19, 14.6%) were the most frequently examined outcome domains, with most studies reporting adverse associations with chronic preoperative benzodiazepine use.

CONCLUSIONS: Chronic preoperative benzodiazepine use is an inconsistently defined but clinically relevant perioperative exposure. As this scoping review did not include a risk-of-bias assessment, its findings map the evidence but cannot support causal inference. Standardised definitions and prospective studies are needed to inform perioperative medication optimisation.

articles.title: Knowledge, Perspectives, and Experiences of Women in Kuwait Regarding GLP-1/GIP-Based Medications for Weight Management: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: GLP-1 receptor agonists and dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists are increasingly used for obesity and type 2 diabetes, alongside growing public and social-media attention. Understanding how women perceive these medications and obtain medication-related information may help healthcare professionals support informed and appropriate use.

METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among women aged ≥18 years living in Kuwait from March to June 2026. The questionnaire assessed medication awareness and knowledge, information sources, attitudes, medication-use experiences, and factors influencing treatment decisions. Previous/current users were compared with participants who had never used the medications or were considering future use using appropriate bivariate statistical tests. Multivariable logistic regression was used for selected information-source and perception outcomes, adjusting for age, BMI, and weight-management intention. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05.

FINDINGS: Among 445 participants, 132 (29.7%) reported previous/current GLP-1/GIP-based medication use. Awareness was highest for tirzepatide (88.6%) and semaglutide (73.4%), although understanding of medication mechanisms and adverse effects varied. Social media was the most frequently reported information source overall (56.0%); however, previous/current users were substantially more likely than never/considering users to report healthcare professionals as an information source (57.6% vs 10.2%, P < 0.001) and less likely to report social media (38.6% vs 63.3%, P < 0.001). Previous/current users were also less likely to perceive that medication risks outweighed benefits (24.2% vs 59.4%, P < 0.001). These differences persisted after adjustment for age, BMI, and weight-management intention.

IMPLICATIONS: Despite high awareness of GLP-1/GIP-based medications among women in Kuwait, understanding, information sources, and perceptions varied according to medication-use status. Differences in information sources and safety perceptions highlight an opportunity for healthcare professionals to provide accessible, evidence-based medication information and support informed treatment decisions.

Nipah virus in Asia: A persistent zoonotic threat.
articles.journal: Journal of microbiology, immunology, and infection = Wei mian yu gan ran za zhi
articles.abstract: We conducted a narrative review of the literature on Nipah virus (NiV) in Asia indexed in PubMed through August 31, 2026. NiV is a highly pathogenic zoonotic paramyxovirus with pandemic potential, causing recurrent outbreaks in South and Southeast Asia since 1998, with reported case-fatality rates of approximately 40-75%. Recent outbreaks in Bangladesh and India between January 2025 and June 2026 underscore the continued public health threat posed by this emerging pathogen. Two genetically and epidemiologically distinct strains exist: NiV-Malaysia (NiV-M) and NiV-Bangladesh (NiV-B). Clinical manifestations range from asymptomatic infection to rapidly progressive encephalitis, sometimes accompanied by areflexia, segmental myoclonus, and brainstem dysfunction. Respiratory involvement, including acute respiratory distress syndrome, has been prominent in NiV-B outbreaks. Diagnosis relies on reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) and serological testing; magnetic resonance imaging may reveal multiple brain lesions, predominantly involving the subcortical white matter. No licensed vaccines or specific antivirals exist. Treatment remains supportive. In vitro findings and studies in animal models have identified potential therapeutic candidates, including the monoclonal antibody m102.4 and remdesivir. However, evidence of efficacy in non-human primates does not establish clinical benefit in humans, and the effectiveness of these interventions in patients remains uncertain. Prevention strategies focus on reducing bat-human contact, behavior change interventions, and strict infection control in healthcare settings. The absence of licensed medical countermeasures and the potential for pandemic spread necessitate urgent acceleration of vaccine and antiviral programs alongside strengthened One Health approaches to prevent spillover events.

articles.title: Hepatobiliary infections following hepatic tumor ablation in patients with prior biliary interventions: A propensity-matched analysis using the real-world global databank.
articles.journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/PURPOSE: Hepatobiliary infections seriously complicate outcomes following liver tumor ablation. However, their association with prior hepatobiliary interventions remains inconclusive. This study aims to evaluate the impact of prior hepatobiliary interventions on the risk of hepatobiliary infections following liver tumor ablation.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX Research Network (2000-2025). Patients who underwent hepatic tumor ablation were identified and stratified according to prior ERCP or hepatobiliary surgery. The prevalence and risk factors of post-ablation hepatobiliary infections between patients, specifically focusing on liver abscesses and cholangitis were compared. Pre-specified subgroup analysis was performed, including age, cancer type, status of cirrhosis, and peri-procedural antibiotics.

RESULTS: Of 14,307 enrolled patients, 632 well-paired patients were analyzed after propensity score matching (n = 316 in each group). Analytic results demonstrated that prior hepatobiliary interventions (including surgery and ERCP) significantly increased the risk of hepatobiliary infection (Hazard ratio: 3.50, 95% confidence interval: 2.40 - 5.11). This elevated risk persisted across all subgroups, regardless of age, cancer type, or cirrhosis status. Periprocedural antibiotics administration did not reduce infectious complications.

CONCLUSION: Patients with prior hepatobiliary interventions had an increased risk of hepatobiliary infection after hepatic tumor ablation. Strategies to prevent infection in these patients are warranted.

articles.title: Are conventional prognostic scores applicable to mild-to-moderate volume intracerebral hemorrhage?
articles.journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Admission hematoma volume is a powerful imaging marker for predicting outcomes in intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). However, the applicability of conventional ICH prognostic scores in specific ICH subtypes, particularly in patients with mild-to-moderate volume ICH, remains unclear. Therefore, we developed a novel nomogram model to directly quantify the risk of early mortality in patients with mild-to-moderate volume ICH and compared its performance with existing conventional ICH scores (oICH, mICH-A, mICH-B, and ICH-GS).

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed data from 681 patients with mild-to-moderate volume ICH treated at our institution. Baseline demographic information, clinical characteristics, and outcomes were collected. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and stepwise logistic regression analysis were used to screen for risk factors associated with early mortality and to construct the prediction model, which was visualized using a nomogram. The model's predictive performance was compared with four conventional ICH scores and was internally validated using 10-fold cross-validation combined with bootstrap resampling.

RESULTS: Of the 681 patients, 71 (10.4%) experienced early mortality during hospitalization. LASSO and stepwise logistic regression analyses identified four independent predictors: admission Glasgow Coma Scale score, hematoma volume, hematoma expansion, and ventricular enlargement. The nomogram demonstrated good calibration (mean absolute error = 0.011) and achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.895. The four conventional ICH scores yielded AUCs of 0.801, 0.859, 0.857, and 0.811, respectively. Decision curve analysis demonstrated that the nomogram provided net clinical benefit across a range of threshold probabilities.

CONCLUSION: We developed a nomogram for predicting early mortality in patients with mild-to-moderate volume ICH based on four readily available variables. The conventional ICH scores may remain useful for rough risk assessment in this population.

articles.title: Risk-stratified treatment of type 1 autoimmune pancreatitis: A narrative review positioning rituximab and inebilizumab.
articles.abstract: Most patients with type 1 autoimmune pancreatitis, the pancreatic manifestation of IgG4-related disease, relapse within a decade of glucocorticoid cessation; the disease causes pancreatic exocrine failure, diabetes, and biliary strictures. Glucocorticoids suppress circulating plasmablasts but spare the memory B-cell compartment from which relapse appears to arise; B-cell depletion targets it. Rituximab, off-label for over a decade, is supported by observational cohorts and a meta-analysis; inebilizumab is the first targeted therapy licensed for IgG4-related disease, based on one randomised trial. This narrative review separates two decisions. First, who is likely to need B-cell depletion: any single risk feature, defined by consensus (multiorgan disease, IgG4 more than twice the upper limit of normal [ULN], diffuse pancreatic swelling) or by a quantified relapse hazard (IgG4 >4 × ULN, IgE >380 kIU/L, eosinophilia, proximal biliary strictures), may prompt depletion at diagnosis; patients without risk features may enter a time-limited glucocorticoid trial ending with a prognostic serum IgG4 measurement. Second, which agent: rituximab is the proposed default, and inebilizumab the on-label option. Whether more, or more extreme, quantified relapse predictors favour inebilizumab over rituximab is an untested hypothesis. No head-to-head trial exists, and the inebilizumab trial reported no subgroup analysis for type 1 autoimmune pancreatitis.

articles.title: Mitral annular calcification.
articles.abstract: Mitral annular calcification (MAC) is a chronic, progressive, and degenerative process characterized by calcium deposition along the mitral annulus. This leads to stiffening and distortion of normal mitral annular architecture and ultimately MAC-related valvular dysfunction, which can manifest as mitral stenosis, mitral regurgitation, or mixed valvular disease. Due to its anatomic complexity, transcatheter and surgical interventions for MAC carry significant procedural challenges. As such, multi-modality imaging and multi-disciplinary heart team discussions are critical in MAC evaluation and procedural planning. This review summarizes the epidemiology and pathophysiology of MAC, highlights the critical role of multimodality imaging in the evaluation and procedural planning of MAC, and reviews established transcatheter mitral valve procedures and surgical options for managing MAC, MAC-related valvular dysfunction, and potential complications.

Cold septic shock: recognising the low-output phenotype.
articles.abstract: Septic shock is commonly taught as a warm, vasodilated state, but the cold, low-output phenotype, in which the underlying process is still sepsis but cardiac output is low and vascular resistance high, is under-recognised. Escalating vasopressors alone in these patients support the blood pressure while leaving the low output untreated. I describe how I separate low from high cardiac output shock at the bedside using peripheries, pulse pressure and central venous oxygen saturation and where cold septic shock and its mechanisms sit within this framework. The phenotype is recognised at the bedside, whereas identifying the underlying mechanism usually requires echocardiography. The central principle is to treat the haemodynamic phenotype, not the label.

Bicuspid Aortic Stenosis: Is it Time to Refine Our Classification Before We Randomize?
Development of a Quantitative Contrast CT-Based TAVR-Risk Score to Reliably Predict Deformation in Bicuspid Aortic Valves.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) calcification affects clinical outcomes by causing transcatheter heart valve (THV) deformation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, a computed tomography (CT)-based scoring system for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation has not been established.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to develop a cardiac CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients with BAV who underwent TAVR using contemporary balloon-expandable valves between January 2016 and December 2024 and who had preprocedural and postprocedural CT imaging. The BAV TAVR-risk score integrated calcification severity and distribution across valve leaflets, raphe, annulus, and left ventricular outflow tract, quantified using a fixed HU-850 threshold of detection on contrast-enhanced CT scans. Score thresholds were derived by receiver operating curve analysis with Youden index optimization. Patients were categorized into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk score groups.

RESULTS: Among 321 patients (median follow-up: 1,825 days; Q1-Q3: 765-1,825 days), 56 (17.4%) were classified into the high-risk score group. Both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV occurred in 49 of the 321 patients (15.3%) and were predominantly observed in the high-risk score group. However, in the low-risk score group, 149 of 155 patients (96.1%) demonstrated no underexpansion or eccentricity of the THV. A high BAV TAVR-risk score independently predicted both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV (OR: 89.13; 95% CI: 35.02-226.83; P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: This CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score provides a systematic method to precisely quantify BAV severity which reliably predicts THV deformation for BAV patients with contemporary balloon-expandable valves and may help guide decision-making in this challenging population.

articles.title: Transcatheter vs Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement for Isolated Native Aortic Regurgitation: National Propensity-Matched Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is well established for aortic stenosis, while its application for isolated native aortic regurgitation (AR) was previously off label and technically challenging. Comparative data between TAVR and surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) are limited.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare patient characteristics and outcomes of off-label TAVR vs SAVR among patients with isolated native AR.

METHODS: Using the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Medicare Provider Analysis and Review database, patients ≥65 years of age who underwent TAVR or SAVR for isolated native AR (2017-2023) were identified. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed to evaluate short- and long-term outcomes. Fine-Gray models accounted for death as a competing risk, reported as subdistribution HRs (SHRs).

RESULTS: Among 9,859 patients, 1,742 propensity score-matched pairs were included, with balanced baseline characteristics (mean age 75.8 years vs 75.7 years; female sex 517 of 1,742 [29.7%] vs 528 of 1,742 [30.3%]). In the matched cohort, TAVR was associated with shorter hospitalization (OR: 0.33; 95% CI: 0.28-0.39; P < 0.001) and lower in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.39-1.00; P = 0.048) but higher 30-day pacemaker implantation (OR: 1.73; 95% CI: 1.33-2.25; P < 0.001). Through 5 years (median follow-up 2.58 years), TAVR was associated with increased repeat aortic valve replacement (SHR: 2.04; 95% CI: 1.13-3.66) but similar all-cause mortality (HR: 1.14; 95% CI: 0.98-1.31) and heart failure-related readmission (SHR: 1.09; 95% CI: 0.98-1.21) between treatment strategies.

CONCLUSIONS: In this analysis, TAVR was associated with shorter hospitalization and comparable 5-year survival as SAVR, although pacemaker and long-term reinterventions rates were higher.

articles.title: Paravalvular Regurgitation After TAVR in Low-Flow, Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis: How Much Is Too Much?
Prognostic Impact of Paravalvular Regurgitation in Patients With Severe Low-Flow, Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis Undergoing TAVR.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Paravalvular regurgitation (PVR) is a frequent complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and may influence clinical outcomes in patients with high-gradient aortic stenosis. However, its prognostic relevance in patients with low-flow, low-gradient aortic stenosis (LFLG-AS) undergoing TAVR remains incompletely elucidated.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the prognostic significance of PVR severity in patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR with current-generation prostheses.

METHODS: This multicenter registry-based cohort study included consecutive patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR from January 2019 to December 2024 at 17 high-volume Italian centers. PVR severity was classified using a 5-class grading scheme and stratified as <2+ (none/trace or mild) or ≥2+ (mild-moderate or worse) based on separation of Kaplan-Meier curves for the primary outcome. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death and heart failure hospitalization up to 2 years. Propensity score-weighted Cox regression was used to estimate the independent impact of PVR severity on clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 1,358 patients were included. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed lower event-free survival among patients with ≥2+ PVR at discharge compared with those with <2+ PVR. After propensity score weighting, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with a higher risk of the primary endpoint (adjusted HR: 3.77; 95% CI: 2.88-4.95), as well as higher risks of all-cause death, mainly cardiovascular, and heart failure hospitalization. These findings were consistent across both classical and paradoxical LFLG-AS phenotypes.

CONCLUSIONS: In this large, real-world study of patients with LFLG-AS treated with current-generation TAVR devices, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with worse clinical outcomes after discharge, regardless of LFLG-AS subtype.

articles.title: Tailoring Early Interventional Approach in Asymptomatic Aortic Stenosis: When Might Early AVR Be Too Late?
Prevalence and Consequences of Guideline-Directed Indications for Aortic Valve Replacement in the EARLY TAVR Trial.
authors: EARLY TAVR Trial Executive Committee and Study Investigators
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The current American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association valvular heart disease guidelines were published before several recent trials that provide greater support for early intervention in patients with asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis (AS).

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to investigate the prevalence and clinical impact of American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Class II recommendations for AVR in the EARLY TAVR trial.

METHODS: The EARLY TAVR trial randomized patients with asymptomatic severe AS to transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance (CS) with conversion to TAVR based on development of ACC/AHA Class I indications. Patients in the intention-to-treat cohort were stratified by presence of a Class II indication for AVR at randomization. The primary endpoint of the present analysis was the composite of all-cause death, stroke, or heart failure hospitalization. Interaction tests were performed to assess whether the treatment effect differed by level of guideline recommendation. Timing of conversion to AVR in the CS group according to the presence/absence of Class II indications was also assessed.

RESULTS: Of the 901 patients randomized to TAVR (N = 445) and CS (N = 446), 636 (70.6%) patients had no guideline recommendation, and 265 (29.4%) had at least1 1 Class II recommendation for AVR at the time of randomization. At a median follow-up of 3.8 years, patients with a Class II indication for AVR experienced higher rates of the primary endpoint (Class II: 24.5% vs no recommendation: 14.5%; HR = 1.78; 95% CI: 1.30-2.44; P < 0.001) and were more likely to have acute valve syndrome at the time of conversion. Compared with CS, the relative benefit of early TAVR on the primary endpoint was similar regardless of the presence or absence of a Class II guideline recommendation (HR = 0.62; 95% CI: 0.37-1.02 vs 0.61; 95% CI: 0.40-0.92; Pinteraction = 0.96).

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients in the EARLY TAVR trial, Class II indications for AVR were present in almost one-third of patients at baseline. The benefit of early TAVR was consistent regardless of the presence or absence of Class II indications. These findings support the strategy of early TAVR over CS in asymptomatic patients with severe AS, independent of guideline indications.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03042104; Unique Identifier: NCT03042104.

articles.title: Prosthesis-Patient Mismatch After TAVR: The Durability of Clinical Benefit.
Prosthesis-Patient Mismatch and Patient-Centered Outcomes After TAVR.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement has been widely studied for its association with clinical outcomes, but its effect on patient-reported health status remains less defined.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the association between PPM severity and health status through 3-year follow-up after transcatheter aortic valve replacement.

METHODS: This post hoc analysis of the SCOPE I (Safety and Efficacy of the ACURATE Neo/TF Compared to the SAPIEN 3 Bioprosthesis) randomized trial categorized patients according to PPM severity using Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 criteria. Endpoints included survival and patient-reported health status, with an integrated outcome defined as being alive with good health status (Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score ≥75 without a decline of >10 points from baseline).

RESULTS: Among 662 patients, moderate and severe PPM occurred in 184 (27.8%) and 69 (10.4%), respectively. All-cause mortality at 1 and 3 years was 7.0% and 20.5%, with no differences across PPM categories. Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score was similar through 1 year but lower at 3 years in patients with severe vs no PPM (median 71.1 vs 83.9; P = 0.027). Fewer patients with severe PPM were alive with good health status at 3 years (30.6% vs 49.4%; P = 0.021). In multivariable analysis, severe PPM was associated with a lower likelihood of the integrated outcome (OR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.27-0.96; P = 0.036), but this association was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for 30-day mitral regurgitation (OR: 0.59; 95% CI: 0.30-1.15; P = 0.121).

CONCLUSIONS: Among survivors, severe PPM was associated with a lower likelihood of good health status at 3 years. This association was attenuated after accounting for 30-day residual mitral regurgitation, suggesting a possible contributory role. Given the post hoc design, the findings are hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Staging Cardiac Damage in Aortic Stenosis: A Better Map, But Not Yet a Compass.
Cardiac Damage and Clinical Outcomes in Symptomatic Severe Aortic Stenosis Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The extent of cardiac damage in patients with aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with worse clinical outcomes.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to investigate the clinical impact of cardiac damage using the updated criteria incorporating the echocardiographic probability of pulmonary hypertension.

METHODS: This post hoc subanalysis of LANDMARK trial, which randomized 768 patients with severe AS to the Myval transcatheter heart valve (THV) series or to contemporary THVs (Sapien and Evolut series), used updated cardiac damage classification: stage 0, no cardiac damage; stage 1, left ventricular damage; stage 2, left atrial or mitral valve damage; stage 3, pulmonary artery or tricuspid valve damage; and stage 4, right ventricular damage. The impact of cumulative cardiac damage, defined as meeting all criteria for stages 1 to 4, was also assessed. The primary endpoint was 1-year all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: Cardiac damage stages were assessed in 596 patients (stage 0, n = 36; stage 1, n = 88; stage 2, n = 284; stage 3, n = 84; stage 4, n = 104), with a mean age of 80.2 (5.7) years and a mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons score of 3.3% (2.4%). One-year mortality was 0%, 1.1%, 4.7%, 7.2%, and 20.4% in stages 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4, respectively (log-rank P < 0.001). The area under the curve for predicting 1-year mortality was 0.739. Patients with cumulative cardiac damage had the highest mortality (23.6%). In the multivariable analysis, stage 4 was independently associated with higher 1-year mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: The updated cardiac damage staging stratified 1-year mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement, highlighting the importance of comprehensive echocardiographic assessment in severe AS. (LANDMARK Trial: a Randomised Controlled Trial of Myval THV [LANDMARK]; NCT04275726).

articles.title: Seasonal Differences in Postoperative Hypocalcemia Following Total Thyroidectomy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether seasonal differences contribute to the development of post-thyroidectomy hypocalcemia.

METHODS: A total of 8731 patients who underwent total thyroidectomy between December 1, 2022, and November 20, 2023, were identified. Patients were grouped into seasonal cohorts based on the meteorological definition of seasons (Winter: December-February; Spring: March-May; Summer: June-August; Fall: September-November). Cohorts were controlled for age, sex, and race. Those with a history of calcium or vitamin D supplementation, chronic kidney disease, or related comorbidities were excluded. Hypocalcemia was defined as serum levels less than 8.5 mg/dL. PTH, vitamin D, and phosphorous levels were also assessed.

RESULTS: When comparing the spring cohort to the winter cohort (n = 1911), the risk of hypocalcemia was 18.7% versus 15.5%, respectively (p < 0.01). No significant differences in hypocalcemia risk were observed between other seasonal groups. Differences in levels of 25-Hydroxy-vitamin D, PTH, and phosphorus were also not significant between groups.

CONCLUSION: Seasonal variation was observed in laboratory-defined hypocalcemia following total thyroidectomy, with patients undergoing surgery in the spring demonstrating a higher risk compared with those undergoing surgery in the winter. These findings challenge the hypothesis that postoperative hypocalcemia risk is highest during colder months because of reduced sun exposure and suggest that seasonal influences on postoperative calcium homeostasis may be more complex than vitamin D status alone. Further prospective studies with standardized perioperative calcium, vitamin D, and PTH measurements are warranted to clarify the mechanisms underlying these seasonal differences.

Transradial access in patients with Raynaud's phenomenon: when 'radial-first' requires nuance.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To review and synthesise evidence concerning transradial procedures in patients with Raynaud’s phenomenon and propose a phenotype-based framework for optimised, safe vascular access-site selection.

DESIGN AND APPROACH: This narrative, mechanism-based and hypothesis-generating clinical viewpoint combines limited direct clinical evidence in Raynaud’s phenomenon with indirect evidence from transradial and rheumatological literature concerning radial artery occlusion (RAO), arterial injury, spasm and vascular biology of Raynaud’s phenomenon. The proposed framework represents expert clinical interpretation rather than a validated algorithm or guideline recommendation.

MAIN ARGUMENT AND EVIDENCE SUMMARY: Transradial access is the default strategy for coronary angiography and percutaneous coronary intervention because it is associated with reductions in bleeding and vascular complications compared with femoral access and its use is increasing in vascular interventional radiology. However, it is not biologically neutral and is associated with varying degrees of radial artery spasm, endothelial injury and RAO, all of which may plausibly be more frequent in patients with Raynaud’s phenomenon. Raynaud’s phenomenon is not a single disease. Primary Raynaud’s is largely functional and will usually permit transradial access when careful spasm and occlusion-mitigation strategies are implemented. Secondary Raynaud’s, particularly when associated with autoimmune vasculopathies, may involve structural arterial disease and impaired vascular reserve leading to compromised circulation in the hand, making radial-related access-site injury potentially more consequential. Direct outcome data in this population remain limited, and the absence of evidence of harm should not be interpreted as evidence of safety. A pragmatic phenotype-guided approach is proposed, incorporating detailed clinical review and procedural modification.

CONCLUSION: Radial-first practice should remain the standard for most patients. Raynaud’s phenomenon is not currently established as a formal contraindication to transradial access. However, selected patients with secondary Raynaud’s and features suggesting structural vasculopathy or impaired hand vascular reserve may warrant individualised access-site assessment. The proposed framework is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective validation.

articles.title: Risk-stratified effectiveness of direct oral anticoagulants versus vitamin K antagonists in thrombotic antiphospholipid syndrome: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare the effectiveness and safety of rivaroxaban versus warfarin in antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) and assess baseline risk-stratified treatment effects.

METHODS: Patients with thrombotic APS were treated with either rivaroxaban or warfarin and followed for recurrent thrombosis and major bleeding. Inverse probability of treatment weighting balanced baseline characteristics. HRs and 95% CIs were estimated using Cox models; prespecified subgroup analyses assessed effect modification.

RESULTS: Among 413 patients with thrombotic APS, 89 (21.5%) received rivaroxaban, and 324 (78.5%) received warfarin. Median follow-up was 25.1 months (IQR, 8.5–44.4). Total follow-up was 198.5 patient-years for the rivaroxaban group and 833.1 patient-years for the VKA group. Recurrent thrombosis occurred in six rivaroxaban-treated patients (6.7%; 3.02/100 patient-years) and 26 warfarin-treated patients (8.0%; 3.12/100 patient-years). In weighted analyses, rivaroxaban was not associated with a significantly different risk of recurrent thrombosis (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.27 to 1.75; p=0.44) or major bleeding (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.15 to 3.03; p=0.61). The association between anticoagulant treatment and recurrent thrombosis differed significantly by triple-positive aPL status (P for interaction=0.007). Among triple-positive patients (n=199), rivaroxaban was associated with a higher risk of recurrent thrombosis than VKA (HR 3.65, 95% CI 1.10 to 12.13). In non-triple-positive patients (n=214), rivaroxaban showed a trend toward a lower risk of recurrent thrombosis (HR 0.16, 95% CI 0.02 to 1.17; p=0.071). Among 89 rivaroxaban-treated patients, no recurrent thrombotic events were observed in those with prior arterial thrombosis (0/22), and these patients more frequently received concomitant single antiplatelet therapy (72.7% vs 11.9%; p<0.001) and statins (36.4% vs 7.5%; p=0.002).

CONCLUSION: In this prospective cohort, no statistically significant differences in recurrent thrombosis or major bleeding were observed between rivaroxaban and warfarin. The treatment-by-triple-positivity interaction suggests that the comparative effectiveness of anticoagulants may differ according to aPL profile.

articles.title: Associations of clinical frailty and the triglyceride-glucose index with major adverse cardiovascular events in older adults with acute coronary syndrome in southern Vietnam: a prospective multicentre cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine the associations of clinical frailty and the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, individually and jointly, with 12-month major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in older adults with acute coronary syndrome (ACS).

DESIGN: Prospective cohort study.

SETTING: Two tertiary hospitals in southern Vietnam.

PARTICIPANTS: Adults aged ≥60 years admitted with ACS who underwent coronary angiography and had obstructive coronary artery disease, defined as ≥50% stenosis in at least one coronary artery. Of 447 patients enrolled, 433 were discharged alive and 401 were included in the 12-month post-discharge analysis.

PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was 12-month post-discharge MACE, defined as a composite of all-cause death, recurrent myocardial infarction, stroke, hospitalisation for heart failure and hospitalisation for unstable angina. Frailty was defined as a Clinical Frailty Scale score≥5, and high TyG was defined using the cohort median.

RESULTS: Among 401 participants, 135 experienced MACE. Event proportions were 21.4%, 36.8%, 24.6% and 62.5% in the non-frailty/low-TyG, non-frailty/high-TyG, frailty/low-TyG and frailty/high-TyG groups, respectively. High TyG was associated with 12-month MACE after multivariable adjustment (adjusted HR 1.91, 95% CI 1.30 to 2.80, p<0.001), whereas the association with frailty alone was attenuated (adjusted HR 1.46, 95% CI 0.95 to 2.25, p=0.080). Compared with the non-frailty/low-TyG group, the frailty/high-TyG group had an adjusted HR of 2.78 (95% CI 1.58 to 4.88, p<0.001). The multiplicative interaction between frailty and high TyG was not statistically significant (p=0.331).

CONCLUSIONS: In older adults with ACS, high TyG remained associated with 12-month MACE after multivariable adjustment, whereas the association with frailty alone was attenuated. Patients with both frailty and high TyG had the highest observed event proportion and the largest adjusted HR relative to the non-frailty/low-TyG group. These findings suggest that combined assessment of frailty and TyG may provide complementary information for post-ACS risk assessment.

The global extent of polypharmacy in neonatal intensive care: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Pharmaceutical treatment in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) is challenging, with neonates often receiving multiple drugs during hospitalization. Given their physiological immaturity, polypharmacy raises concerns about potential adverse effects, drug-drug interactions and the risk of supratherapeutic or subtherapeutic treatment. However, the extent and patterns of drug utilization in NICUs remain underexplored. Accordingly, this study aims to systematically summarise existing literature on polypharmacy in NICUs worldwide.

METHODS: This systematic review, registered in PROSPERO, adhered to PRISMA guidelines. A structured search in EMBASE, Medline and CINAHL identified NICU drug utilization studies (2014-2024). Study selection followed a two-step screening process using the PICO framework. Two reviewers independently screened articles, extracted data and assessed quality with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale.

RESULTS: We included 40 studies across 17 countries, with India and Brazil most frequently represented. Cohorts varied widely, with sample sizes ranging from 41 to 799 016. Polypharmacy was prevalent, particularly among preterm neonates. Commonly prescribed drugs were anti-infectives, respiratory agents and gastrointestinal/metabolic medications. Methodological inconsistencies and variability in medication classification complicated accurate quantification of polypharmacy.

CONCLUSIONS: This review highlights the widespread use of polypharmacy in NICUs globally, yet few studies comprehensively assess the full scope and impact of polypharmacy. The lack of detailed data on drug indications, dosages, treatment duration and adverse effects limits the ability to evaluate the safety and clinical consequences of polypharmacy. Data collection resulting in standardized methodologies are essential to advancing neonatal pharmacotherapy ensuring safer medication use in this vulnerable population.

Diabetes Type and Perinatal Adverse Outcomes Among Women in Pregnancy and Neonates in Japan: A Cohort Study Using a Large-Scale Database.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To compare maternal and neonatal outcomes across gestational diabetes, preexisting diabetes, overt diabetes in pregnancy and normoglycaemia in Japan.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using the JMDC claims database, we conducted a retrospective cohort study of mother-neonate pairs from 2015 to 2024. Maternal glycaemic status was classified as normoglycaemia, gestational diabetes, preexisting diabetes or overt diabetes in pregnancy using diagnoses, prescriptions, procedures and timing. Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for maternal pre-eclampsia/eclampsia and severe neonatal complications (neonatal death, foetal distress or neonatal intensive care unit admission).

RESULTS: Among 244 402 neonates from 205 594 mothers, gestational diabetes, preexisting diabetes and overt diabetes were identified in 20 116 (8.2%), 3287 (1.3%) and 901 (0.4%), respectively. Compared with normoglycaemia, gestational diabetes, preexisting diabetes and overt diabetes were associated with higher risks of maternal pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, with aORs of 1.34 (95% CI: 1.21-1.48), 1.96 (1.64-2.33) and 1.89 (1.35-2.64), respectively. Corresponding aORs for severe neonatal complications were 1.45 (1.38-1.52), 1.95 (1.77-2.15) and 2.55 (2.14-3.03), respectively. Compared directly with preexisting diabetes, overt diabetes was associated with higher odds of severe neonatal complications (aOR: 1.31; 95% CI: 1.07-1.59), with no statistically significant difference detected in maternal pre-eclampsia/eclampsia (aOR: 0.96; 95% CI: 0.67-1.40).

CONCLUSIONS: Maternal and neonatal risks varied by hyperglycaemic status. Overt diabetes was associated with a higher risk of severe neonatal complications than preexisting diabetes, with no statistically significant difference detected in maternal pre-eclampsia/eclampsia. Further validation using longitudinal data around pregnancy is warranted.

articles.title: Two-Year Trajectories of DIAL2-Predicted Cardiovascular Risk After Initiation of Semaglutide, Empagliflozin or Their Combination: The DIAL-STEP Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To describe observed clinical changes and trajectories of DIAL2-predicted cardiovascular risk during 24 months of oral semaglutide, empagliflozin or combination treatment.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 332 adults without prior cardiovascular disease (semaglutide, 139; empagliflozin, 106; combination, 87). The primary endpoint was the investigator-defined HIGH category (calculated 1-year risk ≥ 3%); continuous risk was secondary. Generalized estimating equations and linear mixed models assessed trajectories. Sensitivity models added baseline age, sex and their time interactions or baseline predicted risk. Age-fixed and Shapley calculations were exploratory.

RESULTS: Paired 24-month changes included HbA1c -1.13 percentage points (95% CI: -1.27 to -1.00), systolic blood pressure -7.64 mmHg (-9.48 to -5.79), total cholesterol -20.28 mg/dL (-23.84 to -16.73) and weight -3.91 kg (-4.40 to -3.41). Standard DIAL2 was valid for 329, 327 and 325 participants across visits. HIGH prevalence was 24.6%, 23.2% and 23.7%, without a time-by-treatment interaction (p = 0.731). The continuous-risk interaction was significant (p = 0.002; demographic-time-adjusted p = 0.006). In 324 complete cases, standard predicted risk changed from 2.172% to 2.052% (relative change -5.5%); holding age fixed yielded 1.777% at 24 months (-18.2%). These relative changes concern calculated probabilities.

CONCLUSIONS: Glycaemia and several other measured risk factors improved during follow-up. Categorical DIAL2 status remained broadly stable, while continuous estimates varied with risk-factor changes and chronological age. Repeated DIAL2 and its explanatory decompositions do not establish fewer cardiovascular events or superiority of a treatment strategy.

articles.title: Global Trends and Exposure Profiling of Early-Onset Type 2 Diabetes: An Ecological Analysis Using Machine Learning.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early-onset Type 2 diabetes (EOT2D) is an increasing global health concern. We examined global trends in EOT2D incidence and identified robust population-level exposure correlates.

METHODS: Using the data from the GBD 2021, we analysed EOT2D incidence among individuals aged 15-39 years across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2021. Temporal trends were assessed using estimated annual percentage change. Candidate exposures were evaluated using Elastic Net, Random Forest and XGBoost with temporally separated training, validation and test periods. Country-level bootstrap resampling, robust rank aggregation (RRA) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analyses assessed stability and cross-model consensus. Selected exposures were further examined using year fixed-effects and two-way fixed-effects (TWFE) models. Composite exposure indices were constructed to characterize geographic patterns of joint exposure.

RESULTS: EOT2D incidence increased globally, with persistently high rates in Pacific Island countries and rapid increases in Egypt, Greenland and Afghanistan. XGBoost showed the best out-of-time predictive performance. High body mass index and diet low in whole grains were the only cross-model consensus predictive exposures retained by RRA after multiple-testing correction and consistently ranked highest across models and temporal periods. In the year fixed-effects model, both exposures were positively associated with EOT2D incidence. After adjustment for country fixed effects, high body mass index remained significant. Composite exposure indices showed marked geographic heterogeneity but broadly similar patterns across weighting strategies.

CONCLUSIONS: EOT2D incidence is rising globally. Population adiposity showed the most consistent association across analytical approaches, while the association with EOT2D incidence of low whole-grain intake was more context dependent.

articles.title: Persistent Gaps in Semaglutide and Tirzepatide Prescribing Among Adults With Class III Obesity Without Type 2 Diabetes.

Diabetic Ketoacidosis: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) remains a major cause of diabetes-related morbidity and mortality worldwide, yet evidence on its management and clinical outcomes across healthcare settings remains limited. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the precipitants, management and outcomes of adult DKA.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, MEDLINE, CINAHL and ERIC from 2000 to April 2026 for studies reporting precipitating factors, management and outcomes among adults (≥ 16 years) with DKA. Articles that did not report all three were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data and assessed risk of bias. Descriptive synthesis was performed for demographic, biochemical, management and outcome variables. A random-effects meta-analysis estimated summary in-hospital all-cause mortality. This review was registered with PROSPERO (ID: CRD42025641665). https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42025641665.

RESULTS: Nineteen studies met the inclusion criteria, of which 15 studies comprising 1278 DKA episodes contributed to the descriptive synthesis and nine studies including 724 participants to the mortality meta-analysis. Most episodes were classified as moderate or severe DKA. Preadmission glycaemic control was frequently suboptimal. Missed or inadequate diabetes medication was the commonest precipitant (42.2%), followed by infection (28.6%) and newly diagnosed diabetes (11.2%). Substantial regional variation was observed in guideline use, insulin and fluid administration, intensive care admission and treatment-related complications. The in-hospital mortality summary estimate was 2.17% (95% CI, 0.93%-4.99%).

CONCLUSION: Medication omission and infection remain the dominant precipitants of adult DKA worldwide. Marked variation in management practices and outcomes persists across healthcare systems, suggesting inconsistent implementation of DKA care pathways.

articles.title: Birthweight and Glucose Tolerance Status Are Associated With Organ Sizes in Older Adults.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Low birthweight is a risk factor of Type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Organ size is related to organ function and disease, but few studies have examined cardiometabolic organ sizes in relation to birthweight and glucose tolerance. This longitudinal follow-up study investigated whether organ size varied by birthweight and/or glycaemic status in an elderly population.

METHODS AND MATERIALS: 1212 participants aged 53-83 years from the Danish Inter99 20-year follow-up study, with original midwife birthweight records, underwent computed tomography imaging. Linear regression was used to examine associations between birthweight and organ sizes, and differences in organ sizes across normoglycaemic, prediabetes and diabetes groups.

RESULTS: After adjustment for sex, age, birth year, preterm birth and body surface area, a 1 kg lower birthweight was associated with a 2.0% (95% CI: 0.1%, 3.9%) lower kidney volume and a 3.8% (95% CI: 1.2%, 6.5%) lower lung volume, and with a 3.9% (95% CI: 0.3%, 7.5%) larger adrenal gland volume. Further adjustment for subcutaneous and visceral adipose tissue attenuated the lung association. Compared with normoglycaemic participants, individuals with prediabetes and/or diabetes showed larger liver, kidney and adrenal gland volumes, whereas pancreas volume was smaller, adjusted for birthweight and body size.

CONCLUSION: Lower birthweight was associated with smaller kidneys, and to some extent lungs, and with larger adrenal glands, whereas diabetes and prediabetes were associated with larger kidney, liver and adrenal glands, and with lower pancreas volumes. Further studies are needed to understand the clinical and/or physiological implications of these findings.

articles.title: Development and Validation of 10-Year Prediction Models for Cardiovascular, Kidney and Metabolic Events Among Chinese Patients With Prediabetes in Hong Kong.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Risk stratification can support frontline doctors and patients by enabling care and empowering early prevention of cardiovascular, kidney and metabolic disease. We aimed to develop and validate 10-year prediction models for seven major clinical events and mortality among Chinese patients with prediabetes in Hong Kong.

METHODS: This population-based, retrospective cohort study identified 129 834 adults with prediabetes in 2012 and followed them through 2022. Backward stepwise Cox regression was used to develop an office-based non-laboratory model and three extended models with laboratory results, transformations, interactions and medications. Outcomes included cardiovascular disease (CVD), hypertension, Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), chronic kidney disease (CKD), CVD subtypes and all-cause mortality. Four survival machine learning (ML) models were used for comparison. For each outcome, two models for haemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) and fasting plasma glucose (FPG) were developed. Model performance was assessed by discrimination, calibration and decision curve analysis.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 10.4 years, 19.4% of patients developed CVD. Key predictors included age, sex, smoking status, Charlson comorbidity index, body mass index, systolic blood pressure, lipid profiles, estimated glomerular filtration rate and medications. Our Cox models demonstrated moderate-to-good discrimination: CVD (C-index 0.702), hypertension (0.697), T2DM (0.704), CKD (0.790), mortality (0.816) and CVD subtypes (range: 0.673-0.830), with adequate calibration and positive net benefits. Four selected ML approaches showed comparable performance. HbA1c- and FPG-based models showed comparable performance.

CONCLUSIONS: We developed interpretable prediction models for clinically actionable events among Chinese patients with prediabetes in Hong Kong to inform clinical strategies and resource allocation.

articles.title: Effectiveness of GLP-1 RAs and SGLT-2is for Weight Loss and Glycaemic Control: An Observational Emulation of a Target Trial.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2is) are both recommended as second-line treatments for individuals with Type 2 diabetes and obesity, but long-term head-to-head randomized trials in this population are lacking, necessitating a real-world evaluation of their relative benefits in weight loss and glycaemic control.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using observational data from Clalit's medical records, separate target trials were emulated comparing three GLP-1 RAs (liraglutide, dulaglutide and semaglutide) with SGLT-2is in individuals with Type 2 diabetes and obesity. The main outcomes were absolute changes in body weight and HbA1c during follow-up (up to 5 years for liraglutide/dulaglutide and 3 years for semaglutide). We used inverse-probability weighting to adjust for potential confounders.

RESULTS: We identified 4296, 11 159 and 5041 eligible individuals initiating liraglutide, dulaglutide and semaglutide, respectively. Long-term weight loss was similar (6.4-7.3 kg at 5 years) for liraglutide and dulaglutide compared with SGLT-2is; weight loss for semaglutide was 2.6 kg (95% CI: 1.2-4.0) greater than for SGLT-2is at 18 months. At 18 months, HbA1c reductions were 0.4% (95% CI: 0.3-0.5), 0.7% (95% CI: 0.6-0.8) and 0.6% (95% CI: 0.5-0.8) greater for liraglutide, dulaglutide and semaglutide than SGLT-2is, respectively; this advantage was maintained throughout follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: We estimated that, compared with SGLT-2is, liraglutide and dulaglutide provided superior glycaemic control and similar weight reduction over 5 years, and that semaglutide produced greater short-term reductions in both outcomes. Our analyses benchmark the results of short-term randomized trials and extend the evidence to longer periods.

articles.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Use in Patients With Prior Psychotropic Treatment: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Psychotropic medications are frequently associated with weight gain and metabolic syndrome. While GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have generated interest for managing these adverse effects, their current uses in psychiatric populations have to be described. This study aims to describe the real-world patterns of GLP-1RA initiation and persistence among psychotropic users in France.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using the French National Health Data System, we identified prevalent users of psychotropic medications who initiated GLP-1RAs between 2017 and 2023. Patients were characterized by their indication for GLP-1RA treatment (Type 2 diabetes mellitus [T2DM], obesity or neither) and the class of psychotropic medication dispensed. One-year trajectories of monthly GLP-1RA dispensings were analysed using group-based trajectory modelling.

RESULTS: In this nationwide cohort of 102 709 patients initiating GLP-1RAs after psychotropic use, almost all patients were identified with T2DM (95%). Anxiolytics/hypnotics (> 66%), antidepressants (> 56%) and antipsychotics (> 15%) were the most frequently dispensed psychotropics. Less than 5% of patients lacked a clear indication for GLP-1RA. The predominant trajectory was high persistence with GLP-1RA treatment over 1 year (> 60%). Early disruption presented the lowest proportion of T2DM (80%) and the highest use of antiemetic drugs (8%).

CONCLUSIONS: In France, GLP-1RA use among psychotropic users remained primarily in T2DM, regardless of psychotropic class. Off-label use for psychotropic-induced weight gain appeared very limited. High persistence rates were notable, given the challenges of treatment adherence in mental health populations. These findings suggested a predominantly persistent use of GLP-1RAs within labelled indications in the psychiatric population.

articles.title: Improving blood transfusion safety in Somalia beyond infectious disease screening.

Safety, Accuracy, Empathy, Information Quality, and Readability of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Health Advice Generated by 6 Large Language Models: Cross-Sectional Comparative Evaluation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for health information, but chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)-related questions often involve safety-sensitive decisions, including treatment escalation, oxygen therapy, and exacerbation management. Because generative outputs may vary across repeated prompts, response stability is also relevant to comparative evaluation.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to compare 6 public-facing LLM chatbots in answering COPD-related public health questions across safety, accuracy, empathy, information quality, source transparency, readability, and 2-round response stability.

METHODS: We developed a 55-question English COPD question bank from an initial 108-question pool using web-based retrieval, Google Trends, PubMed-informed topic review, patient education resources, and expert screening. Six public-facing chatbot products were evaluated in a primary first round and a post hoc independent second round, added after first-round data collection, using the same 55 questions. Visible model/mode labels are provided in the supplementary materials. Five blinded raters assessed manually scored outcomes against a Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) 2026-centered reference standard, and 6 readability indices were calculated. The primary cross-model analysis used the first round; the second round was analyzed as a matched retest sensitivity analysis. Stability was assessed using exact agreement and Cohen κ for safety, quadratic-weighted κ for ordinal ratings, and absolute-agreement single-measure intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) for continuous scores and readability indices; 95% CIs used question-level bootstrap resampling.

RESULTS: The first round yielded 330 responses. Unsafe responses occurred in every model: ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, and DeepSeek each generated 4 unsafe responses (7.3%); Qwen generated 5 (9.1%); and Doubao generated 6 (10.9%). The overall safety comparison was not statistically significant (Cochran Q=1.909, df=5; P=.86); this finding should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalent safety. Accuracy, empathy, information-quality measures, source-transparency scores, and readability indices differed significantly across models. Across 330 matched question-model pairs, safety classifications agreed in 97.3% of pairs (κ=0.821, 95% CI 0.543-0.979); accuracy and empathy showed weighted κ values of 0.872 and 0.856, respectively; DISCERN (an instrument for judging the quality of written consumer health information on treatment choices) and adapted Ensuring Quality Information for Patients (EQIP) showed ICCs of 0.954 and 0.925. Most readability indices also showed high overall 2-round stability, although model-specific variability remained. Nine safety classifications changed across the 2 rounds (5 from safe to unsafe and 4 from unsafe to safe).

CONCLUSIONS: In this standardized single-turn COPD question set, model performance differed across several evaluated outcomes, whereas the first-round safety test neither established a between-model difference nor demonstrated equivalence. All 6 models produced potentially unsafe advice, and 9 safety classifications changed between rounds conducted several months apart despite high pooled agreement. These findings support cautious use of LLMs for supplementary COPD education, with clinician oversight for individualized treatment decisions and ongoing reassessment as public-facing systems change.

articles.title: The Effects of Vegetarian Diets on Blood Pressure: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
articles.journal: Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a global health issue, and a vegetarian diet has been represented as a key factor in blood pressure reduction by various observational studies and randomized clinical trials (RCTs).

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the impact of vegetarian diets on systolic blood pressure (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) in adults.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 20 RCTs were performed. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were used to search for eligible RCTs up to July 7, 2025, in accordance with the PRISMA reporting guidelines and the search was rerun on March 10, 2026. Studies that compared blood pressure in adults aged 18 years or older who followed vegetarian diets devoid of meat and fish to those who followed control diets were included. Non-clinical trials were excluded. Random-effects models were used to pool data, subgroup analyses were conducted based on intervention duration and health status. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Collaboration tool, and the certainty of evidence was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach.

RESULTS: The pooled analysis of 21 effect sizes from 20 trials including 1,399 participants did not demonstrate a significant reduction in SBP (WMD: -1.08 mmHg; 95% CI: -2.58 to 0.41) or DBP (WMD: -0.35 mmHg; 95% CI: -1.47 to 0.77) with vegetarian diets consumption. Moderate heterogeneity was observed (I2 = 63.9% for SBP; 71.9% for DBP). Subgroup analysis based on trial duration or type 2 diabetes status did not alter the results. The risk of bias for most studies was unclear or low, and the certainty of evidence was rated moderate for both SBP and DBP because of inconsistency.

CONCLUSIONS: There is inadequate evidence to conclude that vegetarian diets significantly reduce SBP or DBP in adults. Further well-designed, long-term randomized controlled trials with robust adherence monitoring are necessary to elucidate the role of vegetarian diets in managing blood pressure.

articles.title: Upper body posture affects three-dimensional scapula orientation: Clinically applicable models may quantify patient-specific scapula orientation in an upright standing patient.
articles.journal: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Scapulothoracic orientation is a key determinant of shoulder function and influences implant positioning and clinical outcomes in shoulder arthroplasty. However, current preoperative planning relies on supine CT scans, which does not represent the patient's upright scapular orientation. Clinically viable methods to quantify upright scapula orientation are lacking. The aim of this study was to quantify upper-body posture obtained from simple lateral photographs. We hypothesized that these photographs can be used to predict three-dimensional (3D) scapular orientation in an upright position.

METHODS: A database of 123 lateral photographs was used in this study to extract clinical assessment parameters (CAPs): forward head posture (FHP), forward shoulder posture (FSP), thoracic kyphosis index (TKI), and forward elbow-humerus ratio (EHF). A validated 3D skeletal upper-body model was used to simulate nine sagittal posture variations, generating corresponding scapular orientations: internal rotation (SIR), anterior tilt (SAT), and upward rotation (SUR). Each CAP was correlated with the 3D model outputs. Weighted correlation models were developed to predict continuous upright scapular orientations for each patient photograph. Unsupervised hierarchical clustering (Ward's method) identified objective upper body posture subgroups.

RESULTS: All CAPs demonstrated normal distributions. Clustering revealed three distinct sagittal posture groups. Strong correlations were found between CAPs and scapular orientation in the 3D model, particularly between TKI and all scapular angles (R2 ≥ 0.94). Applying these correlations enabled continuous prediction of upright scapular orientation in all subjects. Predicted SIR, SAT, and SUR differed significantly between posture clusters (P < .001), demonstrating the method's sensitivity to postural variation.

CONCLUSION: Upper body posture in the standing position correlates with upright scapular orientation. Quantifying posture through simple lateral photographs and applying prediction models provides a clinically feasible method to estimate patient-specific upright scapula orientation. This posture-informed approach offers a practical adjunct to supine CT-based preoperative planning and may improve accuracy in implant positioning and range-of-motion simulation.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Basic Science Study, Computational Modeling.

articles.title: Is Exercising During Dialysis Enough? Rethinking Approaches to be Physically Active.
articles.journal: Journal of renal nutrition : the official journal of the Council on Renal Nutrition of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract:
