OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether participation in intradialytic exercise programs is independently associated with meeting weekly physical activity recommendations.

METHODS: This was a secondary cross-sectional analysis of the XXX multicenter cohort that included patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis. Participation in intradialytic exercise programs was evaluated through weekly frequency (none, 1-2 times/week, ≥3 times/week). Physical activity was evaluated through the International Physical Activity Questionnaire (short-version). Patients were classified as physically active if they met the weekly recommendations of the 2020 World Health Organization guidelines. Poisson regression models with robust variance were fitted to estimate prevalence ratios for meeting physical activity recommendations, using the non-participation group as the reference.

RESULTS: A total of 932 patients were included (61% male; mean age 58±15 years). Overall, 65% did not participate in intradialytic exercise, 21% participated 1-2 times/week, and 15% ≥3 times/week. In crude analyses, participation in intradialytic exercise 1-2 times/week was associated with a 30% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.55-0.88) lower prevalence of meeting weekly physical activity recommendations compared with no participation, whereas participation ≥3 times/week was not associated. These associations were attenuated and no longer statistically significant after adjustment for confounders, although participation ≥3 times/week showed a borderline positive association with meeting physical activity recommendations (PR=1.24, 95%CI: 1.00-1.54).

CONCLUSION: Participation in intradialytic exercise programs, as currently delivered, was not independently associated with meeting weekly physical activity recommendations. Patient characteristics and contextual factors may play a more prominent role in shaping physical activity behavior than participation in intradialytic exercise alone, particularly when exercise routine is limited to lower weekly frequencies.

articles.title: Can Outpatient Total Knee Arthroplasty Be Performed at a Complex, Academic, Quaternary Referral Center?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Outpatient (same-day discharge) primary total knee arthroplasties (TKAs) have been recently popularized, but results from academic medical centers remain limited. Outpatient surgery shifts perioperative responsibilities to the surgeon. Meanwhile, surgeon reimbursements continue to decrease. We retrospectively evaluated 90-day rates of emergency room (ER) visits, reoperations, revisions, and incoming/outgoing postoperative patient touches associated with outpatient TKAs at our complex, academic, quaternary referral center.

METHODS: At our institution, 1,787 outpatient primary TKAs were performed between 2019 and 2024 in 1,552 unique patients. The mean age was 65 years, 51% were women, the mean body mass index (BMI) was 33, the mean American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) score was 2.4, and the mean Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) was 1.5 (range, 0 to 10). Medical comorbidities, ER visits, reoperations, revisions, and postoperative touches within 90 days after TKA were collected. Univariate logistic regression analyses were completed.

RESULTS: The rates of ER visits, reoperations, and revisions within 90 days of surgery were 8.5, 3.1, and 0.7%, respectively. Knees averaged nine postoperative touches, and total touches increased from 61 in 2019 to greater than 5,800 in 2024. The most common first-time ER visit reason was a medical issue unrelated to surgery (35%), followed by evaluation for venous thromboembolism (VTE; 29%). The actual VTE incidence was 0.6%. The most common reoperation was manipulation under anesthesia (MUA; incidence 1.5%). The 90-day periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) incidence was 0.7%, and all cases required reoperation or revision. Older age and increasing ASA score were significantly associated with risk of ER visits (odds ratio [OR] 1.2; P = 0.01 and OR 1.8; P < 0.001, respectively). Increasing CCI was significantly associated with risk of ER visits (OR 1.2; P = 0.001), revisions (OR 1.5; P = 0.001), and PJI (OR 1.3; P = 0.02).

CONCLUSIONS: We found a high rate of ER visits within 90 days after outpatient TKAs, with nearly 40% unattributable to surgery. Increasing age and comorbidities were associated with increased ER visit risk, and comorbidities also increased revision and PJI risk. Knees averaged nine non-clinic postoperative touches.

articles.title: Can All Knees Be Restored? Reproduction of Pre-Arthritic Coronal Alignment and Aseptic Revision Risk by Preoperative Phenotype: An Exploratory Stratified Competing-Risks Analysis With a Targeted Bayesian Sub-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Personalized alignment in total knee arthroplasty (TKA) aims to restore pre-arthritic coronal anatomy. We tested whether restoration was associated with aseptic revision and whether any association varied by preoperative phenotype.

METHODS: We analyzed 1,566 primary TKAs in 1,286 patients (2010 to 2024) with national registry linkage and a median follow-up of 7.1 years (range, 0.02 to 15.8). There were four prespecified restoration definitions tested: arithmetic hip-knee-ankle (aHKA) angle within ± 2° (reference), exact Coronal Plane Alignment of the Knee (CPAK) match, joint-line obliquity within ± 3°, and full restoration. Multivariable Fine-Gray models treated death as a competing event, and phenotype interactions were tested formally. A Bayesian model estimated risk in the zero-event near-neutral subgroup.

RESULTS: There were 67 aseptic revisions. None of the definitions was significantly associated with aseptic revision (aHKA subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR] 0.66, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.38 to 1.14; exact CPAK match sHR 0.60, 95% CI 0.26 to 1.41). Point estimates favored restoration in near-neutral, but not off-neutral phenotypes, although no interaction test was significant (all P ≥ 0.15). Among 55 fully restored near-neutral knees, none of which were revised, the Bayesian five-year incidence was 0.44% (95% credible interval, 0 to 4.79). Retaining infection revisions as a competing event changed no estimate by more than 0.01.

CONCLUSIONS: Restoration of pre-arthritic coronal alignment was not significantly associated with aseptic revision. A more favorable association in near-neutral knees was suggested but not confirmed by interaction testing. These hypothesis-generating findings require external validation.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, prognostic study.

articles.title: Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty for Septic Versus Aseptic Loosening: A Minimum 20-Year Comparative Study of Survivorship, Functional Outcomes, and Failure Predictors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although several studies have compared outcomes after septic and aseptic revision total knee arthroplasty (TKA), evidence describing survivorship beyond 20 years remains limited. This study compared the minimum 20-year clinical outcomes, implant survivorship, complications, and predictors of failure following revision TKA performed for septic and aseptic loosening.

METHODS: A retrospective comparative study was performed on 912 revision TKAs performed by a single surgeon. The cohort consisted of 292 knees that underwent revision for septic loosening and 620 knees revised for aseptic loosening. All patients were followed for a minimum of 20 years. Clinical and radiographic outcomes were evaluated. Kaplan-Meier survivorship analysis was performed, and multivariable Cox regression analysis was used to identify independent predictors of failure.

RESULTS: Both groups demonstrated significant postoperative improvement in Knee Society Scores (KSS). However, patients undergoing revision for septic loosening achieved lower final KSS (82 versus 88 points; P = 0.005) and function scores (61 versus 78 points; P = 0.003) than those undergoing revision for aseptic loosening. Re-revision was required in 74 knees (25.3%) in the septic group compared with 70 knees (11.4%) in the aseptic group. Recurrent infection occurred in 13.0% and 2.9% of knees, respectively. Kaplan-Meier survivorship at 25 years, with re-revision for any reason as the endpoint, was significantly lower after revision for septic loosening than after aseptic loosening (74.7% versus 88.6%; log-rank, P = 0.004). Septic revision TKA was the strongest independent predictor of failure (hazard ratio [HR], 2.41; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.74-3.34; P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Revision TKA provided durable long-term reconstruction for both septic and aseptic loosening. Nevertheless, revision for septic loosening remained associated with inferior functional outcomes, increased complications, higher re-revision and reinfection rates, and significantly reduced implant survivorship over more than two decades of follow-up.

articles.title: The Prognostic Implication of Preoperative Troponin Elevation at Hospital Admission in Hip Fracture Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The purpose of our study was to evaluate the prognostic significance of preoperative troponin elevation in patients who have hip fractures.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) or observational studies published up to December 2025 comparing patients who have elevated cardiac troponin levels at hospital admission with those presenting normal troponin levels in patients who have hip fractures. Risk ratios (RR) were used to evaluate binary outcomes and mean differences (MD) for continuous endpoints, with 95% confidence intervals (CI).

RESULTS: A total of five studies comprising 2,148 patients who had hip fractures were included. The group with normal troponin at admission had significantly lower overall mortality compared to the group with elevated troponin (RR 2.11; 95% CI 1.63 to 2.74; P < 0.01). In a subgroup analysis, mortality at one month (RR 3.65; 95% CI 1.59 to 8.39; P < 0.01) and three months (RR 1.98; 95% CI 1.51 to 2.60; P < 0.01) was also significantly lower in patients with normal troponin at hospital admission. However, there were no significant differences between groups for arrhythmia, congestive heart failure, or lengths of hospital stay.

CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative elevation of cardiac troponin at hospital admission was consistently associated with an increased risk of mortality, supported by low to moderate-certainty evidence. These findings support the potential role of admission troponin as an accessible prognostic biomarker for early risk stratification in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Total Hip Arthroplasty versus Hemiarthroplasty for Displaced Fragility Femoral Neck Fractures in Older Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Mortality, Reoperation, and Surgical Complications.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Femoral neck fractures in the elderly are managed surgically, most often with either a total hip arthroplasty (THA) or hemiarthroplasty. The purpose of this meta-analysis was to compare the risk of: (1) mortality; (2) revision; and (3) surgical complications of those who undergo THA or hemiarthroplasty for fragility femoral neck fractures.

METHODS: A thorough review of four electronic databases (PubMed, CINAHL plus, EMBASE, and SCOPUS) was performed for all articles pertaining to this topic from 2016 to 2026. A total of 31 studies were included. Mortality was evaluated at 1-month and 1-year. All other surgical complications were stratified based on short-term (≤ two years) and long-term outcomes (greater than two years). The final cohort consisted of 114,064 THAs and 443,016 hemiarthroplasties. The THA cohort was younger (-0.62 years; P = 0.0001), and the hemiarthroplasty cohort had more women (74.1 versus 70.5%; P = 0.0001).

RESULTS: A THA was associated with lower 1-year mortality (random relative risk (RR), 0.79; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.65 to 0.97; P = 0.02) without heterogeneity (P = 0.11; I2 = 40%) or publication bias (P = 0.77). The cohort undergoing THA had a higher risk of instability in long-term (random RR, 1.84; 95% CI, 1.66 to 2.04; P = 0.0001) without heterogeneity (P = 0.41; I2 = 2%) or publication bias (P = 0.31).

DISCUSSION: Those who undergo THA for fragility femoral neck fractures may have a decreased risk of 1-year mortality while having an increased risk of postoperative instability. Our study was unable to determine a difference in the risk of 1-month mortality, revision, periprosthetic joint infection, and periprosthetic fractures between the cohorts. Future studies should evaluate the role of surgery- and patient-specific variables in outcomes following hemiarthroplasty and THA for femoral neck fracture.

articles.title: Age-dependent molecular and neuroimaging changes following social defeat stress in adolescent and adult rats.
articles.abstract: Social stressors are associated with psychiatric disorders in humans, and social defeat stress (SDS) is widely used to model adverse social experiences in rodents. Previous research has demonstrated that social defeat stress induces different behavioral and biological changes at different developmental stages, but research on its neurological effects has been limited. We aimed to investigate the effects of social defeat stress on neural function in adolescence and adulthood using behavioral tests, positron emission tomography (PET), and immunoassays in separate groups of adolescent and adult rats. The results showed that social defeat stress reduced body weight gain and increased corticosterone secretion in both adolescent and adult rats. In terms of behavior, social defeat stress also decreased social interaction time and increased immobility time at both developmental stages. In the PET analysis, the adolescent and adult defeat groups did not show significant changes in glucose metabolism or targeting gamma-aminobutyric acid type A and serotonin 1A receptors. However, social defeat stress induced a marked increase in [18F]FPEB uptake, a PET measure targeting metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGluR5), in the amygdala and hippocampus of adolescent, but not adult rats. The findings indicate that social defeat stress can induce similar physiological and behavioral changes in adolescence and adulthood but distinct neuroimaging responses, particularly in mGluR5 system. These findings enhance our understanding of the neurobiological effects of social stress across developmental stages.

articles.title: Late-onset filtering bleb complications: A review.
articles.abstract: Late-onset filtering bleb dysfunction remains an important determinant of long-term outcomes following glaucoma filtration surgery. Although trabeculectomy provides sustained intraocular pressure (IOP) reduction, progressive changes in bleb architecture and wound healing can result in filtration failure, hypotony, leakage, ocular discomfort, and sight-threatening infection. This review examines the clinical characteristics, underlying mechanisms, assessment, prevention, and management of late-onset bleb complications, with emphasis on individualized, mechanism-directed care. Standardized bleb grading systems facilitate documentation of morphology and longitudinal assessment. Anterior segment optical coherence tomography and ultrasound biomicroscopy complement clinical examination by delineating bleb architecture and identifying potential sites of outflow obstruction, while optical coherence tomography angiography offers an evolving approach to evaluating bleb vascularity. Elevated IOP may arise from internal ostial obstruction, scleral flap adhesion, subconjunctival fibrosis, or encapsulation. Management depends on the site and extent of dysfunction and includes medical therapy, laser intervention, antifibrotic-augmented needling, and surgical revision. Conversely, excessive filtration and compromised conjunctival integrity may cause persistent hypotony, bleb leakage, and hypotony-related structural changes. Treatment ranges from selected conservative measures to compression sutures, conjunctival advancement, and tissue grafting, according to the underlying defect and associated complications. Bleb-related infection requires urgent recognition and treatment, with management determined by the extent of intraocular involvement. Related complications following glaucoma drainage device implantation, nonpenetrating surgery, and subconjunctival microstent procedures are also considered. Successful long-term care requires balancing adequate aqueous drainage against the risks of overfiltration, tissue fragility, and infection. Lifelong surveillance, patient education, and timely intervention remain central to preserving visual function. Future advances in quantitative imaging, targeted wound modulation, and safer filtration strategies may improve the durability and safety of bleb-dependent glaucoma surgery.

articles.title: Examining the associations between commonly prescribed medications and depressive disorders in very old adults- an exploratory study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depressive disorders are a serious concern in very old adults (85+), as the prevalence of depressive disorders seems to increase with age. However, research on the association between commonly prescribed medications and depressive disorders among the oldest old is lacking, hindering proper risk assessment and medication management. The aim of this exploratory study was to investigate the associations between depressive disorders and prescribed medications in very old adults.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study utilized data from the GERDA study, with 2012 participants categorized as depressed (n = 680) or non-depressed (n = 1332) based on assessments during home-visits and evaluated by an experienced geriatrician. Medication use, medical conditions and demographic characteristics were compared between depressed/non-depressed participants using descriptive statistics, t-tests, and chi-square tests. Logistic regression analyses were conducted to explore the relationships between depression, relevant medical conditions and specific medications.

RESULTS: The results revealed 17 medications with significantly different usage rates between depressed and non-depressed individuals. After adjustments for confounding factors, Proton Pump Inhibitors, H2 receptor antagonists and agents lowering serum lipid levels (inversely associated) showed associations with depressive disorders.

CONCLUSIONS: Healthcare professionals should exercise caution in prescribing medications for very old adults, considering the potential associations between medications and depressive disorders. Further research is needed to better understand the relationship between depressive disorders and medication use in this demographic, as this knowledge may improve clinical guidelines for medication use in very old adults.

articles.title: Long-Term Adherence and Outcomes in Ambulatory Heart Failure Patients Using the Cordella Pulmonary Artery Sensor System.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) patient adherence and clinician response times are central to the effectiveness of hemodynamic-guided management using implantable pulmonary artery sensors. We analyzed the relationship of both with clinical outcomes through 2 years in the PROACTIVE-HF study.

METHODS AND RESULTS: To determine if patient adherence and clinician response times were linked to clinical outcomes, we calculated the incidence of heart failure events (HFEs), including HF hospitalizations (HFH), in patients with adherence above or below the median and in clinician response time above or below the median, over 2 years using Poisson regression. Over 2 years of follow-up in the PROACTIVE-HF trial (N=456), patients transmitted data a median of 6.3 days per week and clinicians responded within a median of 1.7 days. Low-adherence patients had more HFH than high-adherence patients (0.71[CI:0.6-0.83] vs 0.55 [CI:0.46-0.66], p=0.04). This association was attenuated and no longer significant after adjustment for baseline differences between groups (adjusted IRR 0.83; 95% CI 0.64-1.09; P=0.19). Low clinician compliance was associated with more HFH than high clinician compliance (0.72 [CI: 0.61-0.84] vs 0.54 [CI: 0.45-0.65], p=0.02).

CONCLUSIONS: In this 2-year analysis from the PROACTIVE-HF trial, both lower patient adherence and lower clinician response times were associated with more HFHs, although these findings were attenuated when adjusting for baseline differences. These findings reinforce that patient engagement with their clinical data along with responsive clinicians is fundamental to the success of remote HF management.

articles.title: Occurrence, potential sources, and microbial associations of microplastics in the Puzhehei Lake watershed, a karst region of Southwest China.
articles.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are emerging contaminants of global concern, yet their potential sources, distribution across environmental media, and associations with sediment microbial communities in karst lake watersheds remain poorly understood. This study investigated the occurrence, potential sources, multimedia distribution, and microbial associations of MPs across surface water, groundwater, and sediments in a representative karst region of Puzhehei Lake watershed in southwestern China. The results indicate that MPs were widely detected in all environmental media, with average abundances of 21.26 items L-1, 31.25 items L-1, and 4415.32 items kg-1 in surface water, groundwater, and sediments, respectively. Although groundwater exhibited a higher mean MP abundance than surface water, the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.225). MPs were predominantly fragments (55.79%-58.21%) and dark-colored particles (black, gray, and brown), with particle sizes mainly concentrated at ≤0.05 mm. The major polymer types identified were polystyrene (PS), polypropylene (PP), and polyethylene terephthalate (PET). Positive matrix factorization (PMF) analyzed three factors tentatively associated with agricultural activities (40.65%), tourism (34.00%), and domestic activities (25.35%), respectively. Further analyses suggested potential associations among the MP characteristics, sediment bacterial communities and predicted nitrogen-cycling functional groups. Although several correlations involving MP morphology, color, and particle size were nominally significant, none remained statistically significant after false discovery rate correction. These findings provide preliminary insights into the potential relationships between MPs and sediment microbial communities in karst environments. However, these microbial associations should be regarded as exploratory and hypothesis-generating because of unmeasured environmental covariates and the possibility of residual spatial confounding. This study provides insights into the potential sources and environmental distribution of MPs and offers a basis for pollution management in ecologically vulnerable regions.

articles.title: Temporal Transportability and Component Deconstruction of a Multipollutant Air Quality Health Index: Health Information Beyond the Composite Score.
articles.abstract: Health-oriented air-quality indices condense multiple pollutants into a single metric, yet their temporal transportability is rarely evaluated independently. We evaluated the Bangkok Air Quality Health Index (AQHI) without recalibration from 2021 to 2024 (1,461 days; 26 postcodes; 23 hospitals) and compared it with a PM2.5-based Air Quality Index (AQI). Negative binomial models assessed index-morbidity associations across short-term exposure windows; additional analyses examined threshold discordance, pollutant contributions, PM10-related cardiovascular associations, particle-gas interactions, falsification, and out-of-time prediction. Whole-score associations were outcome- and period-dependent, and the AQHI did not consistently improve model fit relative to the AQI. Among AQI-Moderate days, AQHI ≥7 did not distinguish higher same-day restricted morbidity, but MA0-1 analyses showed concordant positive patterns for total and cardiovascular morbidity that were not multiplicity-robust. PMcoarse (PM10-PM2.5) remained positively associated with cardiovascular morbidity after nonlinear PM2.5 and gaseous adjustment (MA0-1 incidence rate ratio 1.175, 95% CI 1.076-1.283). O3 showed no stable independent positive association; its interaction with PMcoarse for respiratory outcomes, particularly asthma, was directionally positive but exploratory and not multiplicity-robust, whereas SO2 showed no consistent positive association. On discordant AQI ≤100/AQHI ≥7 days, removing the O3 contribution reduced the AQHI below 7 in all cases. Neither whole-score index consistently improved out-of-time prediction. These findings indicate limited incremental information from the composite AQHI, while identifying selected component-specific and short-window morbidity signals. The AQHI may therefore be useful as a multipollutant contextual indicator to inform precautionary health communication, rather than as a stand-alone morbidity-warning threshold or a superior predictor of morbidity, particularly when the PM2.5-based AQI remains Moderate.

articles.title: H3K9 lactylation transcriptionally activates EHMT2 to drive pulmonary arterial hypertension via PPARγ repression.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is characterized by excessive proliferation and migration of pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs), yet how hypoxia-associated metabolic reprogramming contributes to pulmonary vascular remodeling remains unclear. Here, we show that hypoxia elevates intracellular lactate in PASMCs, promoting HBO1 (lysine acetyltransferase 7/KAT7)-catalyzed H3K9 lactylation (H3K9la) at the EHMT2 promoter and enhancing EHMT2 transcription. Smooth muscle cell-specific Ehmt2 deletion attenuates pulmonary vascular remodeling and right ventricular hypertrophy in SU5416/hypoxia (SuHx) mice and suppresses PASMC proliferation and migration. Conversely, EHMT2 overexpression promotes these phenotypes and mediates lactate-induced PASMC dysfunction. RNA sequencing of pulmonary arteries from Ehmt2-deficient mice identifies PPARγ repression as a downstream mechanism. EHMT2 inhibits PPARγ nuclear translocation, whereas rosiglitazone ameliorates EHMT2-induced PASMC dysfunction. Moreover, administration of lactate exacerbates SuHx-induced PAH in an EHMT2-dependent manner. Collectively, these findings identify a lactate-H3K9la-EHMT2-PPARγ axis linking hypoxia-induced metabolic reprogramming to pulmonary vascular remodeling and PAH progression.

articles.title: Sinomenine prevents monocrotaline-induced pulmonary arterial hypertension by inhibiting osteopontin-mediated PASMC phenotypic switching.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a life-threatening disease driven by progressive pulmonary vascular remodeling, and aberrant phenotypic transition of pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs) serves as the core pathological driver of disease deterioration. Sinomenine (SIN), a structurally defined isoquinoline alkaloid isolated from Sinomenium acutum (Thunb.) Rehder & E.H.Wilson, exhibits anti-inflammatory, vascular-protective, and anti-remodeling activities. Nevertheless, the exact molecular mechanism by which SIN regulates PASMC dysfunction to prevent PAH remains unclear. In vivo, SIN administration significantly attenuated MCT-induced PAH, right ventricular hypertrophy and pulmonary vascular remodeling in rats. In vitro, SIN effectively suppressed platelet-derived growth factor-BB (PDGF-BB)-triggered proliferation, migration and phenotypic switching of PASMCs. RNA-sequencing coupled with KEGG enrichment analysis further identified the ECM-receptor interaction pathway as the key signaling cascade dysregulated by MCT, with osteopontin (OPN) validated as the central functional target of SIN. OPN overexpression recapitulated the pro-remodeling effects of PDGF-BB in PASMCs, and such abnormal phenotypes were prevented by SIN. Molecular docking and cellular thermal shift assay demonstrated that SIN binds to NF-κB, a transcription factor of OPN, and suppresses PDGF-BB-induced NF-κB activation. This study uncovers a novel mechanism of SIN against PAH and highlights OPN as a critical mediator of its protective effects.

articles.title: Sofalcone, a mucoprotective drug, inhibits platelet activation and arterial thrombosis.
articles.abstract: Gastrointestinal injury remains a major limitation of aspirin-based antiplatelet therapy. Sofalcone is a clinically used mucoprotective drug with an established safety profile, but its effects on platelet function remain unclear. This study aims to evaluate the antiplatelet effects of sofalcone and elucidate its underlying mechanisms. In human platelets, sofalcone inhibited platelet adhesion on collagen and suppressed aggregation and secretion induced by U46619, collagen, and arachidonic acid. It converted ADP-induced irreversible aggregation into a reversible response while minimally affecting thrombin-induced aggregation or coagulation parameters. Sofalcone did not alter TXA2 production or activate cyclic AMP or cyclic GMP signaling. Instead, it produced rightward shifts in U46619 concentration-response curves and attenuated TP receptor-mediated Ca2+ mobilization in platelets and TP-expressing HEK293T cells. Docking analysis suggested interaction with the TP receptor binding pocket. Notably, a long half-life major metabolite of sofalcone displayed slightly greater antiplatelet potency. Under whole blood flow conditions, sofalcone and its metabolite reduced thrombus formation on collagen-coated microfluidic chamber surfaces. Combination treatment with sofalcone and either aspirin or ticagrelor further enhanced the inhibition of platelet aggregation and thrombus formation. In mice, intraperitoneal or oral sofalcone prevented FeCl3-induced arterial thrombosis without prolonging tail bleeding time. Together, these findings support the potential repurposing of sofalcone as an alternative or adjunctive antiplatelet therapy, particularly in settings where gastrointestinal protection is clinically desirable.

articles.title: Targeting PLAGL2 in hepatocellular carcinoma and metabolic liver injury: molecular mechanisms and pharmacological opportunities.
articles.abstract: PLAGL2 is a C2H2 zinc-finger transcription factor increasingly recognized as a potential pharmacological target in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and metabolic-inflammatory liver disease. Although PLAGL2 has traditionally been studied as an oncogenic regulator, recent evidence links it to therapeutically relevant adaptive programs in HCC, including the PLAGL2-EGFR-HIF-1/2α signaling loop, non-coding RNA-mediated PLAGL2/HIF-1α regulation, C-MET/STAT3-associated survival signaling, macrophage recruitment, extracellular matrix remodeling and resistance to targeted therapies. In parallel, hepatocyte-specific Plagl2 deficiency has been shown to alleviate metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) by limiting MYD88-licensed inflammasome activation, pyroptotic signaling and IL-1β-associated macrophage activation. These findings suggest that PLAGL2 may operate at the interface of hepatocyte stress, inflammatory remodeling and tumor adaptation. Recent development of PLAGL2-directed small molecules, including compounds that suppress PLAGL2 transcriptional activity or target its DNA-binding domain, further raises the possibility that this transcription factor is pharmacologically approachable. This review critically evaluates PLAGL2 as an emerging therapeutic candidate in liver disease, focusing on hypoxia-linked signaling, inflammasome activation, extracellular matrix remodeling, therapeutic resistance and early pharmacological targeting strategies. We also discuss the attractive but still unproven hypothesis that PLAGL2 contributes to the MASH-HCC continuum.

articles.title: Prostaglandin-Endoperoxide Synthase 1 Regulatory Variants Link Aspirin-Treated Cardiovascular Outcomes to Multicellular Cyclooxygenase-1 Expression and Activity Beyond Platelet-Derived Cyclooxygenase-1 Inhibition.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 1 (PTGS1) encodes cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1). Aspirin inhibits platelet COX-1/thromboxane A2 (TXA2)-dependent aggregation to prevent major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). However, relationships of low aspirin response, namely laboratory aspirin resistance (LAR) and MACE, with PTGS1 variants remain uncertain.

METHODS: In total, 486 cardiovascular patients, 454 on mono-antiplatelet therapy (MAPT), 32 on dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT, aspirin plus clopidogrel), had complete data including COX-1-specific platelet function and median 4.75-year follow-up. MACE comprised acute myocardial infarction, acute stroke, and ischemia-driven revascularization. Eighteen bioinformatically annotated PTGS1 regulatory variants were genotyped.

RESULTS: Smoking and clopidogrel exposure significantly modified LAR. Kaplan-Meier analysis linked LAR to higher crude MACE odds in MAPT and MAPT+DAPT groups (log-rank P < 0.05). Genetic analyses clarified gene-LAR, gene-MACE, gene-LAR-MACE interrelationships. Promoter rs1330344 showed lower LAR odds, with unchanged MACE odds, consistent with mild COX-1 modulation. Intronic rs7866582 conferred higher MACE odds alone, consistent with leukocyte COX-1/proinflammatory prostaglandin elevation. 3'-untranslated region (3'-UTR) rs10306190 exhibited marginally higher LAR odds yet lower MACE odds, consistent with variant-mediated COX-1 upregulation and marked vascular COX-1/PGI2 elevation counteracting residual TXA2 under aspirin. 3'-UTR rs10306196 displayed higher MACE odds alone, consistent with marked vascular COX-1/PGI2 reduction (nominal Firth P < 0.05, except for rs10306190-LAR). However, after multiple testing correction, no significant associations were observed (all BH-FDR Q > 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: LAR and PTGS1 variants lack population-level value for MACE prediction. This study links aspirin-treated MACE to multicellular COX-1 actions beyond platelets.

articles.title: Restoring Myocardial Sodium-Calcium Homeostasis: A Central Mechanism of Empagliflozin in Heart Failure.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) remains a major global health challenge, with high morbidity, frequent hospitalization, and substantial mortality despite major advances in guideline-directed therapy. Landmark EMPEROR-Reduced and EMPEROR-Preserved trials established empagliflozin, a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i), as an effective therapy across the spectrum of HF, independent of diabetes status. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying its cardioprotective effects remain incompletely understood. Growing experimental and translational evidences suggest that restoration of myocardial sodium (Na+) and calcium (Ca2+) homeostasis represents a key mechanism. In failing cardiomyocytes, intracellular Na+ and Ca2+ overload, leading to impaired excitation-contraction coupling, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, electrical instability, and adverse ventricular remodeling. Empagliflozin appears to interrupt this pathological cascade by limiting pathological Na+ entry, attenuating late sodium current (INa-L) and sodium-hydrogen exchanger 1 (NHE1) activity, modulating Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) signaling, improving Na+-Ca2+ exchanger (NCX)-mediated Ca2+ handling, and preserving mitochondrial ion homeostasis. This review summarizes current evidence linking empagliflozin to myocardial Na+-Ca2+ homeostasis, discusses the integration of ion-handling mechanisms with its established clinical benefits, highlights unresolved mechanistic controversies, and outlines priorities for future basic and translational research.

articles.title: KLHDC3-mediated degradation of transcriptional repressor SCAND1 is regulated by Hsp90.
articles.abstract: The ubiquitin-proteasome system and the stress response pathway are highly integrated in order to maintain proteostasis. C-degron E3 ligase substrate adapters recognize certain proteotoxic substrates, although their integration with the cellular stress response has not been previously investigated. Here, we evaluate the C-degron E3 ligases KLHDC3 and APPBP2 for their substrates and pathway dependencies with chemical inhibitors. KLHDC3 and APPBP2 downregulated SCAN-domain containing transcriptional regulators SCAND1 and ZSCAN18, respectively. A bioactive compound screen in reporter cell lines revealed inhibition of KLHDC3 by a panel of Hsp90 inhibitors. KLHDC3 post-translationally downregulated SCAND1 across multiple cell lines, leading to changes in cell viability in endometrial cancer cell lines. SCAND1 overexpression in MFE-296 cells repressed gene targets that drive proliferation and immune responses. This work reveals a mechanism where constitutive post-translational suppression of a transcription factor is released on Hsp90 inhibition, establishing C-degron E3 ligases and their substrates as mediators of the cellular stress response and expanding the known functions and proteostasis implications of a C-degron E3 ligase.

articles.title: Complex antennal modifications of silkworm N-glycans as potential baculovirus ligands.
articles.abstract: The domesticated silkworm Bombyx mori evolved from a wild species almost 5000 years ago and is the basis for sericulture practised especially in some Asian countries, while silkworm cell lines as well as silkworm larvae are used in biotechnology. Silkworms are affected by a number of viral pathogens, including baculoviruses; thus, molecular mechanisms of viral infection are of interest in sericulture and virology. As any eukaryotes, many silkworm proteins are N-glycosylated. In this study, the N-glycomes of B. mori larvae, including strains either susceptible or resistant to a silkworm virus, were examined using an LC-MS/MS approach which revealed not only which proteins are N-glycosylated, but indicated that the N-glycomes contain novel glucuronylated, xylosylated and phosphorylcholine-modified glycans, including examples with masses of over 3000 Da due to extended antennae, in addition to typical oligomannosidic and fucosylated structures. Western blotting and glycoproteomic analyses indicate that specific glycoproteins are modified with phosphorylcholine, whereby this epitope is also recognised by human C-reactive protein and other innate immune proteins when the natural glycans were printed in a microarray format. Binding data indicate that N-glycans and phosphorylcholine may play a role in recognition of silkworm proteins by the B. mori nucleopolyhedrosis virus. Our data not only demonstrate the complexity of the silkworm N-glycome, unsurpassed by other insects studied thus far, but indicate the challenges facing glycoengineering to refine the use of insect systems as biotechnological factories for therapeutic proteins.

articles.title: Letter to the Editor: "Dissociation between Airflow and Lung Volume Responses following Triple Therapy Device Switching in Asthma-COPD Overlap".
articles.journal: The American journal of the medical sciences
articles.abstract: We critically examine Yamada and Nakaizumi's report on device switching in asthma-COPD overlap. Major limitations include a retrospective, unbalanced design (23 vs. 10) with significantly different follow‑up intervals unadjusted in analysis, and a small sample lacking power calculation. The inference of lung deflation from inspiratory and vital capacity changes is unsupported without direct total lung capacity or functional residual capacity measurements; these indices are effort‑dependent and highly variable. Moreover, the observed COPD Assessment Test score changes do not reach the minimal clinically important difference, and the comparison confounds device type with drug formulation, while adherence and technique were not assessed. We conclude that these findings are hypothesis‑generating only, and prospective, randomised, formulation‑matched studies with robust physiological endpoints are required before clinical application.

articles.title: Imported melioidosis with septic shock in a short-term visitor from Cambodia to Japan: a case report and literature review of imported cases in Japan.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract: Melioidosis is a potentially fatal infectious disease caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei, a soil-dwelling Gram-negative bacterium endemic to Southeast Asia and northern Australia; however, it remains a rare imported disease in Japan. Here, we report a case of melioidosis in a 70-year-old Cambodian man who developed septic shock during a short-term visit to Japan. We also performed a literature review of all reported cases of imported melioidosis in Japan. The patient presented with a three-day history of abdominal pain and diarrhea. He was immunocompromised and was receiving prednisolone and tocilizumab for adult-onset Still's disease. Blood cultures obtained on admission revealed Gram-negative rods. The organism was initially identified as Burkholderia thailandensis by MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry but was later confirmed to be B. pseudomallei at the reference laboratory. The patient developed septic shock but recovered with intensive supportive care and antimicrobial therapy consisting of meropenem and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. This case and our literature review highlight that, even in non-endemic countries, melioidosis should be included in the differential diagnosis in patients with a history of travel to, or residence in, endemic regions, and that prompt diagnosis and timely initiation of appropriate treatment are essential.

articles.title: KDM4B-PTX3-mediated dendritic cell senescence drives severe asthma and predicts biologic non-response.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Severe asthma is driven by uncharacterized Type 2-independent pathways, with 30-50% biologic non-response and no approved disease-modifying therapies for airway remodeling. The histone demethylase KDM4B and inflammatory mediator pentraxin 3 (PTX3) link to fibrotic lung disease, but their reciprocal regulatory circuit in dendritic cell (DC) senescence and severe asthma pathogenesis remain undefined. We previously reported unidirectional KDM4B-dependent PTX3 upregulation; here we define a fully validated bidirectional KDM4B-PTX3 positive feedback loop that sustains cDC2 senescence.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate if a bidirectional epigenetically regulated KDM4B-PTX3 positive feedback loop in CD1c⁺ cDC2 senescence is a conserved Type 2-independent pathway driving severe asthma, and a viable therapeutic target and predictive biomarker.

METHODS: In a discovery cohort (n = 226), plasma PTX3 was quantified and linked to outcomes. scRNA-seq mapped its cellular origin, while ChIP/ATAC-seq, in vitro assays, and HDM/PM2.5 mouse models delineated KDM4B-PTX3-driven DC senescence. A reverse PTX3 → KDM4B feedback loop was validated via recombinant stimulation, neutralization, and NF-κB inhibition. Inhaled KDM4B inhibitor QC6352 was evaluated for efficacy, with full formulation specs, lung/plasma PK, isoform selectivity, and extended 4-week post-treatment toxicology. A 5-gene PTX3-senescence signature was developed and validated in fully independent cohorts, with performance assessed by DeLong AUC, calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA).

RESULTS: Plasma PTX3 was elevated in severe asthma, correlating with impaired lung function and exacerbations; CD1c⁺ cDC2 were the primary source. DC-specific Ptx3 knockout murine experiments confirm lung cDC2 drive ∼61% of circulating plasma PTX3 levels during chronic airway inflammation, resolving ambiguity regarding systemic PTX3's cellular origin. KDM4B epigenetically regulated PTX3 via H3K9me3 demethylation, forming a feedback loop conserved across triggers. Recombinant PTX3 induces NF-κB-dependent KDM4B transcription, completing the bidirectional regulatory circuit; PTX3 neutralization ablates HDM-driven KDM4B upregulation ex vivo. Senescent DCs drove remodeling via SASP; DC-specific Ptx3 deficiency attenuated collagen deposition and smooth muscle thickening. TIM4⁺ senescent DCs impaired tolerance via phosphatidylserine (PS) sequestration, acting as a soluble PS sink that deprives DC-Treg synapses of PS required for downstream TGF-β/SMAD tolerogenic signaling rather than via primary efferocytosis defects, reducing Treg induction from 11.8% to 4.7%. Inhaled KDM4 inhibitor QC6352 reversed senescence/remodeling with 4-week durability and a favorable safety profile; QC6352 exhibits 28-41-fold enzymatic selectivity across KDM4 isoforms, and KDM4B re-expression genetic rescue confirms all in vivo phenotypes are on-target. The signature predicted non-response, outperforming eosinophils and FeNO; combination yielded AUC = 0.89.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings establish the bidirectional KDM4B-PTX3-DC senescence axis as a Type 2-independent driver of severe asthma, resolving prior limitations of unidirectional mechanistic data, ambiguous cohort independence, and undervalidated drug selectivity/safety claims. Inhaled KDM4B inhibition is a promising disease-modifying therapy, and the PTX3-senescence signature enables personalized biologic selection for non-responding patients.

articles.title: Effects of exercise preconditioning on neuroinflammatory and neuroprotective markers in animal models of stroke: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Currently, mounting evidence suggests that exercise preconditioning beneficially modulates the neuroimmune responses following stroke. However, meta-analysis of preclinical studies specifically addressing this topic remain limited. This study aims to conduct a comprehensive analysis of preclinical literature investigating the effects of exercise preconditioning on neuroimmune responses in animal models of stroke. The objective is to provide a theoretical foundation and scientific rationale for applying exercise training in stroke prevention.

METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, CNKI, Wanfang, and VIP were searched from inception to 20 July 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that examined the effect of exercise preconditioning on neuroimmune responses after stroke in animal models. Effect sizes were pooled with a random-effects model and reported as standardized mean differences (SMD).

RESULTS: A total of 24 studies were included in this systematic review. Meta-analysis revealed that in post-stroke brain tissue, exercise-pretreated animals exhibited significantly reduced levels of ionized calcium binding adapter molecule 1 (Iba1) [SMD = -2.85, 95% confidence interval (CI) (-4.66, -1.03)], interleukin (IL)-1β [SMD = -3.86, 95% CI (-5.73, -1.99)], IL-6 [SMD = -1.55, 95% CI (-2.98, -0.12)], inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) [SMD = -6.18, 95% CI (-8.37, -3.99)], toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) [SMD = -3.70, 95% CI (-5.28, -2.12)], nuclear transcription factor-κB (NF-κB) [SMD = -3.37, 95% CI (-4.59, -2.16)], Cysteine-dependent Aspartate-specific Protease-1 (Caspase-1) [SMD = -2.42, 95% CI (-3.70, -1.15)], and NLR family, pyrin domain containing protein 3 (NLRP3) [SMD = -2.77, 95% CI (-4.00, -1.53)] compared to non-exercising animals, while levels of IL-10 [SMD = 6.63, 95% CI (1.50, 11.75)], tyrosine kinase receptor B (TrkB) [SMD = 4.30, 95% CI (3.14, 5.46)], and neuronal nuclei antigen (NeuN) [SMD = 8.52, 95% CI (5.61, 11.44)] were significantly elevated. In serum, levels of tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) [SMD = -4.50, 95% CI (-7.66, -1.34)] and IL-1β [SMD = -2.41, 95% CI (-3.49, -1.32)] were significantly reduced. No significant differences were observed in other neuroimmune responses.

CONCLUSION: Exercise preconditioning appears to exert beneficial effects on neuroinflammatory and neuroprotective markers after experimental stroke. Nevertheless, the certainty of the evidence is limited by small sample sizes, substantial heterogeneity, unclear risk of bias across multiple domains, potential small-study effects, and the predominance of young male animals. Therefore, these findings should be interpreted with caution and require confirmation in rigorously designed preclinical studies.

articles.title: The association of physical activity and sedentary behaviour with the development and progression of microvascular complications in type 1 and type 2 diabetes: A systematic review of cohort studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic retinopathy, nephropathy and neuropathy substantially impair quality of life. This review synthesised longitudinal evidence on physical activity (PA), sedentary behaviour (SB), and the development or progression of these microvascular complications in adults with type 1 (T1D) or type 2 diabetes (T2D) METHODS: Seven databases were searched from inception, with a supplementary update conducted on 30 October 2026 for prospective or retrospective cohort studies comparing PA or SB levels in relation to eligible retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy or severe neuropathy-related foot outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed with the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Exposures (ROBINS-E) tool, and findings were synthesised narratively.

RESULTS: Twelve studies (nine prospective and three retrospective) were included. Reported sample sizes summed to 2.55 million, although overlapping cohorts meant that participants were not necessarily unique. One South Korean registry contributed 2,495,031 participants, approximately 98 % of this total, so the aggregate sample was dominated by one national population. Evidence on SB was restricted to one cohort of 175 participants with established diabetic peripheral neuropathy, in which greater sedentary time was associated with higher odds of first diabetic foot ulcer (OR 2.95, 95 % CI 1.45-6.44). Higher PA was associated with lower risk of several renal and neuropathic outcomes, predominantly in T2D; retinopathy findings varied.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher PA was associated with some favourable longitudinal microvascular outcomes, mainly in T2D, but residual confounding, self-reported exposures and heterogeneous outcomes limit interpretation. Evidence on SB was restricted to one small cohort and cannot establish its association with incident microvascular complications.

articles.title: Global spatial distribution and risk factor profiles of Co-occurring type 2 diabetes and ischemic heart disease across 204 countries and territories.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) and ischemic heart disease (IHD) interact reciprocally and contribute to massive global multimorbidity burden. This study aimed to map global T2D-IHD co-occurrence patterns and quantify key risk factors to support targeted integrated prevention.

METHODS: We extracted incidence data of T2D and IHD and exposure data of 58 risk factors for adults aged ≥ 25 years across 204 countries and territories in 2021 GBD. SHAP machine learning and negative binomial regression were applied to screen independent risk factors, and population-attributable fractions (PAFs) and a composite risk index were calculated to evaluate attributable disease burden.

RESULTS: Among 204 countries and territories, 36.27% were consistent, 32.84% T2D-dominant and 30.88% IHD-dominant. Six key risk factors were identified, including two shared metabolic risks (high body mass index, kidney dysfunction), one T2D-specific (high fasting plasma glucose), and three IHD-specific risks (low temperature, high systolic blood pressure, diet low in whole grains). Collectively, cumulative exposure to the three T2D-related factors explained 22.98% of global T2D cases, while the five IHD-related factors explained 56.22% of global IHD cases. The combined PAF of these six risk factors exceeded 70% T2D and IHD cases in consistent regions. In addition, high-risk exposure areas of these factors spatially overlapped greatly with T2D and IHD hotspots.

CONCLUSION: Global T2D-IHD co-occurrence showed obvious spatial heterogeneity driven by modifiable shared and disease-specific risks. Combined interventions for common risks plus regionally targeted strategies for unique hazards are essential to alleviate their combined global health burden.

articles.title: Characterization of EHV-1 viral genes at the respiratory tract using a tracheal explant culture model.
articles.abstract: Equine herpesvirus 1 is the cause of respiratory disease, abortions, and equine herpesvirus myeloencephalopathy (EHM) in horse populations worldwide. Current vaccines do not prevent EHM. Several viral genes have been implicated in systemic dissemination and viral transfer to the CNS, but their roles during early respiratory events remain unclear. This study employed an equine tracheal explant culture model to characterize the role of selected EHV-1 genes in viral replication, infectivity, and innate immune activation during early respiratory infection. Tracheal explants were collected from respiratory healthy horses and inoculated with EHV-1 Ab4 WT or EHV-1 Ab4 recombinant viruses containing deletions or substitutions in genes involved in neuropathogenesis. Viral infection was evaluated using complementary approaches including immunohistochemistry, quantitative PCR, TCID₅₀ assays, and RT-qPCR analysis of innate immune genes. Deletion of ORF1 resulted in increased viral antigen detection, elevated viral DNA levels, enhanced production of infectious virus, and induction of innate immune markers (TLR3, IRF7, IRF9, CXCL9, CXCL10, CCL2, IL-6) supporting the role of ORF1 in modulating epithelial immune responses during early infection. Deletion of ORF2 increased antigen detection and showed limited regulation of chemokines (CXCL9, CCL5). Deletion of the gI-gE heterodimer reduced infectious virus production despite limited effects on viral genome presence, while increasing the expression of TLR3, IRF7, and CXCL9, highlighting its importance in cell-cell spread at the respiratory epithelium. Additionally, gB4, gD4, and the N752 variant exhibited WT-like replication with only subtle immune effects. Collectively, these findings provide insight into viral determinants that shape early epithelial infection and may influence downstream disease outcomes.

articles.title: Clinicobacteriological profile, Mortality Predictors and Antimicrobial Resistance in Necrotising Soft Tissue Infections: A prospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Necrotising soft tissue infections (NSTIs) are rapidly progressive infections requiring prompt diagnosis and management. This study assessed predictors of mortality, microbiological spectrum, antimicrobial resistance patterns, and differences between polymicrobial and monomicrobial NSTIs in a prospective manner.

METHODS: This study enrolled patients aged 15 years or older with clinically suspected NSTIs who presented between March 2022 and February 2023. Clinical, laboratory, surgical, and outcome data were collected. Tissue and pus samples were processed for aerobic and anaerobic cultures. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed according to CLSI guidelines. Mortality-associated factors were analysed using univariate analysis, binary logistic regression, and survival analysis.

RESULTS: Eighty-seven patients were included, predominantly male (87.3%), with a median age of 47.5 years. Extremities were most commonly affected. The mortality rate of this cohort was 25.3%. Polymicrobial infections predominated (49.4%), while monomicrobial NSTIs were associated with higher mortality (p = 0.022). Gram-negative organisms, particularly Acinetobacter baumannii and Escherichia coli, were the most frequent pathogens. Obligate anaerobes were significantly associated with polymicrobial infections. Chronic liver disease (p = 0.003) and systemic toxicity (p = 0.018) independently predicted mortality, whereas higher haemoglobin levels were protective. High antimicrobial resistance was observed, including carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii and Enterobacterales. Among the anaerobes, resistance to clindamycin and cefoxitin, along with reduced susceptibility to metronidazole, was reported.

CONCLUSION: NSTIs remain associated with substantial mortality, especially in monomicrobial infections due to multidrug-resistant Gram-negative pathogens. Early recognition, prompt surgery, and region-specific empirical antimicrobial therapy are crucial for improving outcomes.

articles.title: Plasma extracellular vesicle proteomic signatures are associated with immunothrombosis and homeostatic dysregulation in septic shock.
articles.abstract: Sepsis and septic shock are life-threatening conditions involving severe immune, coagulation, and organ dysfunction. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) circulate during systemic inflammation and carry molecular cargo reflecting pathophysiology; however, differences in plasma EV proteomic profiles between sepsis and septic shock remain incompletely characterized. In this exploratory cross-sectional study, we characterized SEC-enriched plasma EV preparations from patients with sepsis (n = 7), septic shock (n = 7), and healthy controls (n = 7) using label-free shotgun proteomics. Differential proteomic, functional enrichment, and protein-protein interaction analyses revealed distinct molecular patterns and biological networks across clinical groups. Proteins differing between patients and healthy controls were enriched in innate immune responses, neutrophil degranulation, complement/coagulation pathways, and cell adhesion. Furthermore, direct comparison between sepsis and septic shock highlighted specific patterns in the septic shock group related to homeostatic processes, biological regulation, and tissue remodeling. Overall, our findings indicate that plasma EV-enriched preparations exhibit distinct proteomic patterns associated with sepsis and septic shock, including proteins mapping to immune, coagulation, and homeostasis-related processes. These results provide an exploratory proteomic framework for investigating EV-associated molecular changes between clinical groups, while functional studies and validation in larger cohorts will be required to determine their biological and clinical relevance. SIGNIFICANCE: Sepsis is a heterogeneous clinical syndrome in which the molecular changes associated with increasing disease severity remain incompletely characterized. In this exploratory study, we used label-free shotgun proteomics to characterize Size Exclusion Chromatography-enriched plasma extracellular vesicle preparations from healthy controls and patients with sepsis or septic shock. The analysis identified group-associated protein patterns and biological processes related to innate immunity, neutrophil responses, complement, coagulation, and homeostatic regulation. Rather than establishing a functional role for EVs in these processes, our findings show that EV-associated proteomic profiles contain molecular information associated with clinical disease severity. These results provide candidate molecular patterns and biological hypotheses for validation in larger independent cohorts and for subsequent functional investigation.

articles.title: Clinical Consensus Guidelines on Antibiotic Prescribing Practices for Infants with Gastroschisis Utilizing Modified Delphi Methodology.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastroschisis is the most common congenital abdominal wall defect in newborns and common surgical diagnosis for which antibiotics are prescribed in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). Multiple studies demonstrate early and prolonged antibiotic exposure, despite evidence of overuse resulting in delayed initiation of feedings, later full feedings, and blood stream infection. The purpose was to develop expert consensus on evidence-driven clinical guidelines for microbiologic screening and antibiotic usage in neonates with simple gastroschisis.

METHODS: The Children's Hospitals Neonatal Consortium (CHNC) Gastroschisis Focus Group utilized a modified Delphi method to develop clinical consensus guidelines (CCG). Committee leaders drafted 10 recommendations after literature review and group discussion. Each recommendation was sent to focus group members via REDCap survey tool and members scored responses on a 5-point Likert scale.

RESULTS: In the first survey, there were 23 respondents and 7/10 recommendations received a mean score >80%, meeting the criteria for consensus. Following review of results and comments, the remaining statements were edited and sent out for the second round survey where all achieved consensus. Themes included the practice of screening for infection at birth by blood culture, and antibiotic use practices at the time of birth and abdominal wall closure. These included risk stratification for infection, spectrum of antibiotic therapies utilized, length of therapy, and timing of antibiotic administration.

CONCLUSION: We present a consensus evidence-based framework for antibiotic use and stewardship practices in infants with simple gastroschisis, which will be important as many centers lack standardized guidelines in this population.

articles.title: A preliminary characterization of humoral markers and immune gene expression of rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) subjected to emerging Lactococcus petauri infection.
articles.abstract: Lactococcus petauri is an emerging causative agent of lactococcosis in farmed rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) yet host immune responses to this pathogen remain entirely uncharacterized. This study provides a preliminary description of innate immune dynamics following intraperitoneal challenge with 100 CFU/fish of L. petauri strain TURK72 in two genetically selected trout lines, resistant (R) and susceptible (S) to lactococcosis, differentiated by a single nucleotide polymorphism (C>T) at position 140 of the mhc-iiβ gene. No mortality or clinical signs were observed, suggesting the development of a possible subclinical infection model. Leukocyte differential counts, five selected non-specific humoral immune parameters, and RT-qPCR expression of 12 immune-related genes (il-8, mhc-ii, saa, ptx, cox-2, cath-1, cath-2, hepcidin, c3, c5, casp3, casp8) were assessed in head kidney and spleen at 1 and 7 days post-infection (dpi). Among the humoral parameters, only serum lysozyme activity differed significantly, increasing from ∼1,000 U/mL at 1 dpi to ∼2,500-2,700 U/mL at 7 dpi. Gene expression analysis revealed significant time-dependent changes, predominantly in the head kidney at 1 dpi (il-8, mhc-ii, saa, ptx, hepcidin, c5) and in the spleen at 7 dpi (casp3, casp8). These results represent initial immune reference for L. petauri-challenged rainbow trout and highlight areas requiring further investigation.

articles.title: Efficacy of chitosan-supported biofilm vaccine against Vibrio parahaemolyticus in Penaeus vannamei.
articles.abstract: Pacific white-leg shrimp, Penaeus vannamei, were immunized by immersion with formalin-inactivated biofilm (BF) and free-cell (FC) preparations of Vibrio parahaemolyticus at 106 CFU/mL for 30 days and evaluated for immune responses, biochemical changes, and disease resistance. Biofilm production was optimized using chitosan particles (10 mg/mL) in tryptone soy broth supplemented with 2% NaCl for 72 h, as confirmed by crystal violet staining, viable bacterial enumeration, and FE-SEM. The optimized biofilm was subsequently used to formulate the inactivated BF vaccine. Following challenge with V. parahaemolyticus (106 CFU/mL), the BF vaccine provided significantly higher protection, with an RPS of 57.15%, compared with FC vaccine group (42.87%). The BF group also exhibited significantly higher total haemocyte count at 72 h post-infection (hpi). Vaccination modulated key innate immune and antioxidant responses, including respiratory burst activity, superoxide dismutase, prophenoloxidase, and catalase activities. In addition, vaccinated shrimp showed improved biochemical profiles, with lower SGOT and SGPT activities and higher total protein, albumin, and globulin levels compared with controls. Overall, the chitosan-supported biofilm vaccine enhanced immunogenicity, improved physiological condition, and conferred greater protection against V. parahaemolyticus infection than the free-cell vaccine. These findings highlight its potential as an immersion-based vaccination strategy for sustainable disease management in P. vannamei aquaculture.

articles.title: Mycetoma in the United States: A Clinical Review.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology
articles.abstract: Mycetoma is a neglected chronic granulomatous infection of the skin and subcutaneous tissue caused by filamentous bacteria (actinomycetoma) or fungi (eumycetoma). Although classically associated with tropical and subtropical regions, cases have been reported in the United States and the disease is underrecognized, leading to misdiagnosis and delayed treatment. This clinical review synthesizes United States-focused evidence on mycetoma epidemiology, risk factors, clinical presentation, diagnostic evaluation, and management. In the United States, mycetoma may be acquired abroad or locally, particularly in warmer regions, and reported demographic patterns differ from endemic areas, with cases often affecting older and urban populations. Clinically, it usually presents as a slowly progressive, painless subcutaneous nodule with draining sinuses and grain-containing discharge. Accurate distinction between actinomycetoma and eumycetoma is essential for appropriate treatment. Diagnosis relies on early collection of grains and deep tissue for histopathology and culture, with bedside microscopy as an adjunct, and imaging to define disease extent and bone involvement. Actinomycetoma is managed with prolonged antibiotics and is often cured without surgery, whereas eumycetoma typically requires long-term antifungal therapy plus surgical excision, with higher recurrence risk and rates of amputation.

articles.title: The Contribution of WWEIA, NHANES Nutrient Data to the Nutrition Evidence Base: Analytic Applications and Health Outcomes, 2013-2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A 2025 scoping review by Kogan, et al. quantified the use of What We Eat in America (WWEIA), National Health and Examination Survey (NHANES) nutrient data in the scientific literature. However, it did not explore study characteristics, such as health outcomes or types of analyses.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize health outcomes and study types found in the publications reporting WWEIA, NHANES nutrients identified in the 2025 scoping review, and to identify nutrients most frequently reported by health outcome and study type.

METHODS: Employed a human-supervised artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted workflow to extract additional data from publications identified in the 2025 scoping review. The workflow consisted of five phases: (1) prompt development, (2) data extraction and standardization, (3) data validation, (4) data cleaning and analysis, and (5) narrative description of the results.

RESULTS: Of the 2,200 peer-reviewed publications reporting WWEIA, NHANES nutrients between 2013-2023, association analyses were most common (79%), followed by surveillance (30%), dietary index (27%), and adequacy (11%) studies. Among the 1,753 studies classified as association or mortality analyses, approximately 85% (n=1,496) reported at least one health outcome. Within diet-related health outcome categories, cardiovascular disease was the most frequently reported (18% of publications), followed by obesity/weight loss (10%), diabetes/insulin resistance (9%), bone health (4%), and cancer (4%). Nutrients most frequently reported across health outcomes and study types included energy, protein, carbohydrate, total fat, dietary fiber, total saturated fatty acids, total monounsaturated fatty acids, total polyunsaturated fatty acids, and sodium.

CONCLUSIONS: WWEIA, NHANES nutrient data are used across a range of analytic applications and health outcomes, with distinct nutrient-reporting patterns observed within these contexts. Consideration of these empirical patterns, together with Dietary Reference Intakes, Dietary Guidelines for Americans, and nutrition labeling requirements, may help inform priorities for maintaining high-quality nutrient profile data in national dietary surveillance and research.

articles.title: Association of Adult and Pediatric Cardiac Surgery Volumes with Outcomes of the Ross Procedure in Adults.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is growing interest in application of the Ross procedure for treatment of aortic valve disease; however, utilization is restricted to specialized centers. The present study evaluated the differential association of adult aortic valve surgery and pediatric cardiac surgery volumes on outcomes of adults undergoing the Ross operation.

METHODS: The 2016-2022 Nationwide Readmissions Database was queried to identify all adults undergoing the Ross procedure. Hospitals were categorized as pediatric high-volume centers (pHVC, ≥75th percentile pediatric cardiac surgery volume), adult high-volume centers (aHVC, ≥75th percentile aortic valve replacement/repair volume among non-pHVC), and low-volume centers (LVC). Major adverse events (MAE) were defined as a composite of mortality, stroke, prolonged ventilation, acute renal failure, pulmonary embolism, cardiac arrest, and reoperation.

RESULTS: Among 1,212 adults undergoing the Ross operation, 37.7% were treated at pHVC, 56.7% at aHVC, and 5.6% at LVC. National utilization increased from 63 cases in 2016 to 385 in 2022, with the number of performing centers rising from 14 to 37. Patients at LVC experienced the highest rates of MAE (42.1% vs aHVC 8.8% vs pHVC 3.8%, p<0.001). After risk adjustment, care at LVC was associated with a 7.7-fold increase in odds of MAE compared to pHVC (95% CI 3.0-19.7, p<0.001). Outcomes at aHVC and pHVC were comparable, although aHVC had higher rates of reoperation (4.5% vs 0.6%, p<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Adults undergoing the Ross operation at LVC face worse outcomes compared to aHVC and pHVC. These findings support selective referral strategies and regionalization of care.

articles.title: Surgical Timing and Physiology-Specific Outcomes in Congenital Heart Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In low- and middle-income countries, most children with congenital heart disease reach the operating room after the guideline-recommended window has closed. Existing analyses grade delay by chronological age or a binary early/late split and report outcomes in aggregate, not by physiology.

METHODS: All 12,190 consecutive pediatric congenital heart operations at a single Indian tertiary center (2020-2025) were graded against national guidelines using a lesion-normalized Guideline Deviation Score, from G0 (timely) to G4 (critically delayed). Logistic regression and restricted cubic splines assessed operative mortality, morbidity, and resource utilization overall and within seven pre-specified physiological subgroups.

RESULTS: Of 10,187 gradable operations, 73.7% were delayed and 34.8% critically delayed. Operative mortality was 2.1% (adjusted OR per grade, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.81-0.96]; P = .004). Fontan-stage palliation was the only subgroup with progressive morbidity increase (64% at guideline age, 85% at grade 3; P = .002), inflecting near age 12 years. Left-to-right shunt lesions showed forward morbidity accumulation (adjusted OR, 1.05 [1.01-1.09]; P = .03). Resource utilization rose with delay overall (adjusted OR, 1.04 [1.01-1.07]; P = .01) and in left-to-right shunt and transposition physiology, but fell in cyanotic and Fontan-stage groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Three in four children missed their guideline window. Operative mortality did not rise with delay, which reflects case-mix confounding rather than evidence that delay is safe, since the youngest and sickest children are operated first. Morbidity rose with delay in Fontan-stage and left-to-right shunt physiology. Physiology-specific grading supports surgical decision-making when a child presents late.

articles.title: An NCG mouse model of Hantaan virus reveals systemic infection and organ-specific cellular tropism.
articles.abstract: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) caused by Hantaan virus (HTNV) is primarily endemic across Eurasia, posing a severe threat of renal failure and mortality. The mechanisms of HTNV infection remain poorly understood, largely due to the lack of susceptible animal models. In this study, we established a systemic HTNV infection mouse model using highly immunodeficient NCG mice. Following viral inoculation, we assessed viral loads via quantitative RT-PCR and mapped cellular tropism and co-localization of HTNV with potential receptors using immunofluorescence staining. While histopathological lesions were subclinical, HTNV-infected NCG mice exhibited robust viremia and sustained viral replication across multiple organs, including the kidney, lung, spleen, reproductive organs, and liver. HTNV exhibited distinct organ-specific cellular tropism in vivo, predominantly targeting fibroblasts and interstitial cells of the renal collecting duct in the kidney, alveolar epithelial cells and macrophages in the lung, and broadly infecting multiple cell populations in the brain and ovary. Co-localization analyses indicated HTNV infection might be associated with distinct entry receptors across target organs: potentially ITGB1 and gC1qR in specific renal cells, and ITGB1 and ITGB2 in pulmonary AT1 cells and macrophages, respectively. These findings demonstrate that NCG mouse is a valuable in vivo model for studying HTNV replication and systemic dissemination.

articles.title: PROphylactic use of closed incision negative Pressure wound thERapy for VASCular surgery groin incisions: recommendations from an international expert-based consensus (PROPER-VASC).
authors: PROPER-VASC Study Collaborators, PROPER-VASC Study Collaborators (all individually citable on Pubmed)
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to obtain experts' consensus and define recommendations regarding best clinical practices on the use of prophylactic close incision negative wound pressure therapy (ciNPWT) in patients undergoing groin incisions in vascular surgery METHODS: A modified Delphi consensus methodology was employed over three rounds, involving a panel of 20 experts, by using a four point likert scale. Statements that reached consensus at the first round were submitted to a second round, unmodified. Statements that failed the first round were adapted and proposed to the second and third rounds of judgment. Agreement and consistency derived from the three rounds were used to develop recommendations on the prophylactic use of ciNPWT on groin incisions after vascular operations.

RESULTS: After three rounds, 3 statements were rejected, and 20 recommendations were made. Six received a Grade B consensus, and fourteen statements reached a Grade A consensus. Experts agree on the potential of ciNPWT in reducing superficial groin SSI in patients with high-risk features, which should consequently be treated with such technology routinely, contrary to standard-risk patients who would not benefit as much from ciNPWT dressings. Practical recommendations that reached consensus included the use of ciNPWT as soon as possible after surgery, possibly already in the operating theater, and devices should stay in place for 5-7 days.

CONCLUSIONS: Inguinal ciNPWT should be used in patients at increased risk of SSI and wound dehiscence after vascular interventions to prevent superficial infections. Individualized risk assessment should be performed for each patient to guide decision-making and practical instructions for device management should be provided.

articles.title: Comparative 30-Day Outcomes of Lower Extremity Bypass versus Endovascular Revascularization for Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia in Octogenarians.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Endovascular revascularization is often favored for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) in octogenarians because of lower morbidity, but whether it achieves comparable limb salvage is unclear. We also compared bypass using single-segment saphenous vein (SSSV) versus alternative conduits.

METHODS: Octogenarians (≥80 years) undergoing nonemergent lower extremity endovascular revascularization or infrainguinal bypass for CLTI were identified from the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) databases (2011-2022). Multivariable logistic regression compared 30-day outcomes between endovascular and bypass procedures and between SSSV and non-SSSV conduits.

RESULTS: Among 5,715 octogenarians, 2,614 underwent bypass and 3,101 endovascular intervention. Bypass had higher major adverse cardiac events (MACE; 6.39% vs 3.35%; adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.42; P = .01), sepsis (4.09% vs 2.00%; aOR, 1.94; P < .01), and length of stay >7 days (59.1% vs 28.9%; aOR, 2.39; P < .01), but lower 30-day major amputation (3.14% vs 3.58%; aOR, 0.64; P < .01), with no difference in mortality (5.85% vs 4.29%; P = .06). Among bypass patients, SSSV (n = 1,737) more often had operative time >4 hours (42.8% vs 30.4%; aOR, 1.83; P < .01) and more wound complications (17.8% vs 13.4%; aOR, 1.45; P < .01) than non-SSSV conduits, without a significant increase in mortality or MACE.

CONCLUSIONS: In octogenarians with CLTI, bypass was associated with greater perioperative morbidity but lower 30-day major amputation; selection bias and short follow-up limit inference. SSSV was associated with more >4-hour operations and more wound complications, without significantly higher mortality.

articles.title: Addressing Healthcare-Associated Infection Risks Through SEIPS Model-Driven System Optimization: A Six-year Longitudinal Study.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) are preventable patient safety events that threaten healthcare quality. Conventional infection prevention and control (IPC) strategies often focus on individual compliance while neglecting systemic vulnerabilities in HAI management work system. This study evaluated whether the Systems Engineering Initiative for Patient Safety (SEIPS) model-driven intervention could sustainably reduce HAI-related safety risks.

METHODS: A 6-year longitudinal prospective study was conducted in a tertiary general hospital in Wuhan, China. In late 2018, HAI management work system was comprehensively analyzed using the SEIPS framework across five dimensions: person, tools and technology, environment, task, and organization. From 2019 to 2024, targeted interventions were implemented, and periodic monitoring, evaluation and optimization were conducted.

RESULTS: From 2018 to 2024, the incidence episode rate of HAIs decreased from 1.68% to 0.58% (χ² = 1666.4, P < .001). The incidence episode rate of multidrug-resistant organism infection declined from 0.204% to 0.068% (χ² = 209.6, P < .001), and surgical site infection decreased from 0.18% to 0.10% (χ² = 21.6, P < .001). Device-associated infections also declined, including ventilator-associated pneumonia from 8.69‰ to 0.79‰, central line-associated bloodstream infection from 0.09‰ to 0.02‰, and catheter-associated urinary tract infection from 0.78‰ to 0.06‰.
