Hand hygiene compliance improved from 66.45% to 80.84% (χ² = 145.1, P < .001).

CONCLUSIONS: The SEIPS model-driven intervention was associated with sustained improvements in HAI safety indicators and staff safety behavior, supporting its value as a systematic framework for IPC performance improvement. The SEIPS framework could help healthcare institutions shift from compliance-centered IPC to system-level comprehensive intervention.

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of National Guidelines for the Diagnosis of Tuberculosis Infection in Europe.
authors: 3rd European Reference Laboratory Network for Tuberculosis (ERLTB-Net-3)
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diagnosis and preventive treatment of tuberculosis (TB) infection (TBI) are essential for TB prevention and elimination in the European Union/European Economic Area (EU/EEA). However, implementation of global recommendations into national guidelines and routine practice varies across the area. This study aimed to characterise current practices and assess alignment and gaps in national TBI diagnostic guidelines among European countries within the ECDC third European Reference Laboratory Network for Tuberculosis (ERLTB-Net-3).

METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was distributed to all ERLTB-Net-3 member countries in July 2025. The survey assessed: (i) national guideline characteristics; (ii) screening indications; (iii) diagnostic practices; (iv) organisational aspects; and (v) quality assurance and monitoring.

RESULTS: Of 30 ERLTB-Net-3 member countries, 24 (80%) responded. Most reported national guidelines aligned with WHO recommendations. Tuberculin skin test and interferon-gamma release assays were widely used, although testing strategies and organisational approaches varied. Few reported external quality assessment and systematic monitoring of TBI diagnosis and treatment was limited.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite recognition of TBI diagnosis as a priority for TB elimination in EU/EEA, substantial variation in diagnostic practices persists across the region. Greater alignment and harmonisation of diagnostic strategies, alongside strengthened quality assurance and surveillance systems, could advance TB elimination in the region.

articles.title: Mpox hospitalizations and HIV-associated immunosuppression at a single center in China: clinical characteristics, treatment, and outcomes.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe clinical features, HIV co-infection, immune status, treatment, and outcomes among hospitalized mpox patients in China.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 59 PCR-confirmed mpox hospitalizations involving 58 patients admitted from 29 June 2023 to 8 December 2025. Variables were summarized descriptively, with exploratory subgroup comparisons by HIV status and CD4 category, including an analysis restricted to patients with HIV.

RESULTS: All hospitalizations occurred in male patients; median age was 34 years and median hospital stay was 10 days. MSM exposure was recorded in 51/59 hospitalizations (86.4%), anogenital pain in 49/55 (89.1%), perianal rash in 48/59 (81.4%), and perianal ulceration or proctitis in 47/59 (79.7%). HIV infection was documented in 39/59 hospitalizations (66.1%). Among 46 records with available CD4 counts, 12 (26.1%) had CD4 <200 cells/µL; 11 involved patients with HIV and one involved an HIV-negative patient. Among HIV-positive records with available CD4 counts, the median hospital stay was longer in the CD4 <200 cells/µL group than in the CD4 ≥200 cells/µL group (15 vs 8 days; P=0.002). Complications occurred in 14/59 hospitalizations (23.7%). One patient died during hospitalization at the study hospital; another death at a different hospital after discharge was identified through follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: Hospitalized mpox was characterized by MSM exposure, anogenital disease, HIV co-infection, and immunosuppression. Among patients with HIV, lower available CD4 counts were associated with longer hospital stays, whereas differences in complications and in-hospital mortality remained uncertain.

articles.title: Choline attenuates lipopolysaccharide-induced neuroinflammation in the BV-2 microglial cell line via the α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor/nuclear factor kappa-B signaling pathway.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the potential mechanisms by which choline (CHO) attenuates lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced neuroinflammatory responses in BV-2 microglial cells through network pharmacology-based prediction and in vitro experiments. These neuroinflammatory responses are implicated in the pathophysiology of sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE).

METHODS: Putative CHO targets were retrieved from PubChem, the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database (CTD), and SwissTargetPrediction, while SAE-associated genes were sourced from OMIM and GeneCards. Overlapping targets from both datasets were subjected to protein-protein interaction (PPI) network construction, along with Gene Ontology (GO) functional annotation and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway enrichment, to identify core candidate genes and key signaling cascades. The predicted outcomes were subsequently verified by in vitro experiments, including cell viability assays, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), immunofluorescence, quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR), and Western blot.

RESULTS: An intersection of 672 SAE-associated genes and 109 CHO-responsive genes yielded 24 common targets. Among them, TNF, IL10, IL6, MMP9, and IL1B were identified as potential hub therapeutic targets. KEGG enrichment analysis revealed the involvement of multiple pathways, with the nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κB) cascade being particularly notable. In cell-based assays, CHO administration reduced the levels of pro-inflammatory mediators (TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6) and concurrently increased those of anti-inflammatory markers (IL-4, IL-10, and CD206). Furthermore, CHO elevated α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (α7nAChR) expression while suppressing IκBα and NF-κB p65 phosphorylation. Treatment with the α7nAChR antagonist methyllycaconitine citrate (MLA) reversed these effects.

CONCLUSIONS: CHO may inhibit microglial neuroinflammation and promote anti-inflammatory polarization, potentially via the α7nAChR/NF-κB signaling pathway.

articles.title: Changing Patterns of Extrapulmonary Tuberculosis Over 60 Years in a Brazilian University Hospital.
articles.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a serious public health problem worldwide. Extrapulmonary TB results from hematogenous dissemination or the extension of the infection to an adjacent organ by contiguity. This retrospective observational study analyzed TB admissions included in a historical institutional grouping comprising extrapulmonary presentations, miliary TB, and combined pulmonary and lymph node TB at a Brazilian university referral hospital between 1965 and 2024. Demographic, clinical, HIV co-infection, and outcome data were extracted from a prospectively maintained institutional database. Patients were compared between the pre-1990 and post-1990 periods using Pearson's χ² test to evaluate temporal changes in epidemiological characteristics. Among 15,601 hospitalizations, 792 admissions involved a diagnosis of TB, including 306 (38.6%) in the historical study group comprising extrapulmonary presentations, miliary TB, and combined pulmonary and lymph node TB. Meningoencephalitic tuberculosis was the most frequent presentation (44.4%) and showed the highest case fatality rate (30.1%), predominantly affecting young children. Among admissions in the historical study group, the proportion of meningoencephalitic TB was lower after 1990 (73.5% versus 22.4%; p<0.001), whereas the proportions of lymph node, pleural, and combined pulmonary and lymph node TB were higher. By decade, meningoencephalitic TB decreased from 51 cases (15.06 per 1,000 departmental admissions) in 1965-1974 to 3 cases (1.26 per 1,000) in 2015-2024. In the unadjusted comparison, in-hospital case fatality was 34.8% before 1990 and 5.7% thereafter (p<0.001). Within meningoencephalitic TB, case fatality was 36.1% (35/97) before 1990 and 15.4% (6/39) thereafter. These findings describe changes in the clinical distribution and admission-based frequency of TB presentations within a single department. Changes in referral, admission practices, and diagnostic capacity may have contributed, precluding inference about population incidence or attribution to specific causes.

articles.title: Post-approval study preliminary 1-month outcomes of the first 100 patients treated with an off-the-shelf multibranch aortic device.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To report the preliminary 1-month outcomes from the post-approval study of the first 100 patients treated with the GORE® EXCLUDER® Thoracoabdominal Branch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE).

METHODS: This multicenter, nonrandomized, prospective study of the TAMBE aortic component included endovascular repair of an aortic disease involving the visceral vessels. Demographics, core-lab adjudicated imaging characteristics, perioperative metrics, and postoperative 1-month outcomes are reported.

RESULTS: The first 100 patients treated were 30% female, 81% white, and the median was age 74 years. Anatomic classifications included 48 patients (49.0%) with Extent I-IV thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA), 21 (21.4%) with pararenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA), 12 (12.2%) with juxtarenal AAA, and 17 patients with post dissection pathology (n=11) or 'other' (n=6). Enrollment and treatment of 45.0% of the patients were at sites without prior TAMBE device experience. Prior aortic surgery was noted in 48.0% of patients treated. For patients with Extent I-III TAAA (n=22), staging of the TAMBE procedure was planned with initial proximal thoracic endovascular aortic repair in 7 patients (31.8%). Median aneurysm diameter was 6.2 cm. The GORE® VIABAHN® VBX Balloon Expandable Endoprosthesis was used in all patients, with additional use of a VIABAHN® self-expanding stent in six patients. Intentional non-use of one or more portals (with planned plug occlusion) was a strategy used in 15 (15.0%) patients. Median procedure time was 280 minutes, and median length of stay was four days with 83 patients (83.8%) discharged to home. Branch target vessel technical success rate was 98.9% (average of 1.39 stents into the celiac, 1.44 superior mesenteric artery, 1.62 right renal, and 1.59 left renal per portal). Three patients (3.0%) died, all were procedure related. Major adverse events in 8 patients (8.1%, 3 had ≥1 event) included 1 (1.0%) respiratory failure, 4 (4.0%) permanent paraplegia, 4 (4.0%) renal function decline, and 1 (1.0%) bowel ischemia. No patient experienced a major stroke, aneurysm rupture, or myocardial infarction. A total of eight Type 1c or Type IIIa/IIIc endoleaks were detected in 6 (6.1%) patients. No conversion to open-surgical repair, rupture, or device migration/integrity issues were reported.

CONCLUSIONS: The preliminary analysis of the FDA-mandated post-approval study 1-month outcomes in this prospective multicenter cohort treated with the TAMBE device demonstrates applicability to more extensive thoracoabdominal pathology with similar outcomes to the pivotal trial. Distinct findings for the TAMBE device in the real-world include successful treatment of post-dissection aneurysms, increased staging strategies for spinal cord protection with low paraplegia rates, and rapid adoption by many sites that did not participate in the pivotal trial.

CLINICALTRIALS: GOV: NCT06578741.

articles.title: Platelet NLRP3 signaling promotes thromboinflammation and organ injury in sepsis.
articles.journal: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis is characterized by dysregulated host responses to infection, leading to microvascular thrombosis, organ dysfunction, and death. Although NLRP3 regulates platelet activation and arterial thrombosis, its role in sepsis-associated thromboinflammation remains unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To investigate the contribution of platelet NLRP3 to microvascular thrombosis, inflammation, and organ injury during sepsis.

RESULTS: Pulmonary IL-1β increased during sepsis and colocalized with platelets. Platelet NLRP3 deficiency attenuated pulmonary IL-1β elevation, whereas adoptive transfer of wild-type, but not NLRP3-deficient, platelets increased pulmonary IL-1β in NLRP3-deficient recipients. Platelet NLRP3 deficiency improved survival, reduced pulmonary and hepatic microvascular thrombosis, and attenuated organ injury. Furthermore, NLRP3 deficiency reduced platelet activation, phosphatidylserine exposure, platelet-neutrophil interactions, inflammatory cell accumulation, neutrophil extracellular trap formation, and inflammatory cytokine levels. Importantly, reduced platelet activation, phosphatidylserine exposure, and platelet-neutrophil interactions were evident at 6 hours after cecal ligation and puncture, before detectable differences in bacterial burden. Septic plasma induced platelet NLRP3 activation and IL-1β maturation through TLR4/MyD88-sensitive signaling. IL-1β neutralization attenuated septic plasma-induced platelet activation, phosphatidylserine exposure, and platelet-neutrophil interactions, whereas recombinant IL-1β restored these responses in NLRP3-deficient platelets.

CONCLUSIONS: Platelet NLRP3 contributes to pulmonary IL-1β responses and promotes thromboinflammation during experimental sepsis. Its deficiency reduces microvascular thrombosis and organ injury while improving survival, suggesting platelet NLRP3 as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Beyond neurones: cardiac involvement in motor neurone disease.
articles.abstract: Motor neurone disease (MND) is a fatal neurodegenerative disorder defined by the progressive loss of upper and lower motor neurones. This degeneration leads to muscle wasting and weakness, most prominently affecting the upper and lower limbs, the bulbar musculature responsible for speech and swallowing, as well as the respiratory muscles (Feldman et al., 2022). As the disease advances, affected individuals experience profound functional decline, loss of independence, and ultimately respiratory failure, which remains the leading cause of death (Kiernan et al., 2021). Despite advances in understanding the molecular and cellular mechanisms of MND, effective disease‑modifying treatments are limited and there is no cure. Management therefore focuses largely on symptomatic treatment and multidisciplinary supportive care to maintain quality of life (Simon et al., 2015). The long-standing view of MND as a disease confined to the motor system is increasingly being challenged. Emerging evidence from human and rodent studies suggests that other organ systems, such as the heart, may also be affected, raising the possibility that cardiac involvement is a clinically relevant but under‑recognised feature of the disease.

articles.title: Induction immunosuppression in kidney transplant recipients treated with early corticosteroid cessation: A propensity score case-matched analysis.
articles.journal: American journal of transplantation : official journal of the American Society of Transplantation and the American Society of Transplant Surgeons
articles.abstract: Early corticosteroid cessation is recommended for low immune risk kidney transplant recipients, but the optimal induction immunosuppression is uncertain. We compared the outcomes of 4,770 first kidney only transplant recipients in the U.S. between 2010 and 2022 treated with tacrolimus and mycophenolate without corticosteroids induced with interleukin-2 receptor antagonists (IL-2Ra) to a matched cohort induced with anti-thymocyte globulin rabbit ( Thymoglobulin.) Only 13% of patients treated with early corticosteroid cessation were induced with IL-2Ra and these patients were more likely to be older and have diabetes. After 1:1 matching, patients treated with IL-2Ra had a higher adjusted risk of allograft loss from any cause (Hazard Ratio (HR) = 1.20, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.12 to 1.29), death with allograft function (HR = 1.20, 95% CI 1.10 to 1.31), and allograft loss with death as a competing risk (sub hazard ratio SHR = 1.20, 95% CI 1.04 to 1.38). We conclude that IL-2RA induction is selectively used in older, sicker patients but is associated with a higher risk of transplant failure compared to matched patients treated with Thymoglobulin. The findings highlight the need for prospective trials to define optimal induction in patients who may benefit most for early corticosteroid cessation.

articles.title: Combined Rituximab and Daratumumab Induces Remission in Refractory Post-Transplant Crescentic IgA Nephropathy.
articles.journal: American journal of transplantation : official journal of the American Society of Transplantation and the American Society of Transplant Surgeons
articles.abstract: Recurrent crescentic IgA nephropathy (IgAN) after kidney transplantation is rare, aggressive, and often refractory to standard immunosuppression. We report a 17-year-old recipient with biopsy-confirmed recurrent crescentic IgAN two years after transplantation despite corticosteroids and targeted-release budesonide. Rescue therapy comprised one rituximab infusion with daratumumab, followed by four daratumumab infusions. Proteinuria decreased from 5.21 to 0.06 g/g, serum albumin normalized, and allograft function remained stable through day 482 after the first rescue infusion. Longitudinal CyTOF and flow cytometry showed sustained peripheral B-cell depletion and transient NK-cell reductions. One mild upper respiratory infection occurred. Sequential biopsies showed resolution of the active cellular crescent, although mesangial IgA staining and electron-dense deposits persisted. These clinical, histologic, and immune changes were temporally associated with combined CD20- and CD38-targeted therapy. This single case cannot establish efficacy, distinguish the contributions of rituximab and daratumumab, or exclude effects of preceding and supportive treatments, but supports further study of this rescue approach.

articles.title: Which patients with possible endocarditis should be treated as if the diagnosis were definite? An international modified Delphi study.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To identify which combinations or numbers of diagnostic criteria in possible infective endocarditis (IE) are associated with the decision to treat as IE, that is, to give a full course of endocarditis antibiotic treatment.

METHODS: In a two-round modified Delphi study, international IE experts rated 47 standardised vignettes covering possible IE, of which 39 formed the basis of the main analysis. On a nine-point Likert scale, they indicated whether they would treat the patient as if he or she had IE. Consensus in favour required ≥70% of ratings at 7-9 and ≤15% at 1-3; consensus against was defined symmetrically. Associations with criteria were explored by modified Poisson regression.

RESULTS: Of 137 experts, 103 completed round 1 (84 [83%] from Europe; 71 [69%] infectious disease specialists) and 98 of 102 round 2. Consensus was reached for 24 of 39 vignettes (62%): in favour of treating as IE in 22 (56%) and against in 2 (5%). Consensus in favour rose with accumulating criteria: 33% with minor criteria only, 45% with one major and one minor, and 74% with one major and two minor. Fifteen vignettes (38%) reached no consensus. In an exploratory model, consensus in favour was most strongly associated with typical (adjusted risk ratio [aRR] 12.40, 95% CI 2.11-72.93) and consistent (aRR 8.27, 1.17-58.54) major microbiological criteria and with major imaging criteria (aRR 7.37, 1.62-33.51). The criteria associated with consensus differed by valve type: imaging in native-valve and microbiological in bioprosthetic-valve vignettes.

CONCLUSIONS: Expert consensus on treating possible IE as IE was reached in 62% of scenarios, almost exclusively in favour of treatment, and was most strongly associated with major criteria. These findings describe current expert views under uncertainty and do not establish the clinical benefit of treating possible IE as definite.

articles.title: Transvenous Lead Extraction Using the PISA Approach: A Decade of Experience from a National Referral Centre.
articles.journal: Revista portuguesa de cardiologia : orgao oficial da Sociedade Portuguesa de Cardiologia = Portuguese journal of cardiology : an official journal of the Portuguese Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: The widespread implantation of cardiovascular implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) has led to a growing demand for safe and effective transvenous lead extraction (TLE), particularly concerning device-related infection, venous occlusions and lead dysfunction. As procedural complexity increases, so does the importance of adopting reliable and adaptable extraction strategies. We present a comprehensive, single referral centre experience using the PISA technique - a rotational sheath-based approach - to perform transvenous lead extraction over a 10-year period.

METHODS: This retrospective study included all patients undergoing TLE at a national referral centre between February 2013 and December 2024. Extractions were initially performed using simple traction as the first-line approach, and in all cases where simple traction was unsuccessful, the PISA approach for lead extraction was employed. Clinical and radiological success, complications, and mortality were analyzed.

RESULTS: A total of 283 patients underwent extraction of 530 leads, with a median lead dwell time of 96 months (IQR: 48-144). The majority of devices were pacemakers (62.9%), followed by cardiac resynchronisation devices (20.2%) and transvenous implanted cardioverter defibrillators (15.9%). Infection was the predominant indication (74.6%). The majority of procedures were performed via a superior approach. Clinical success was achieved in 97.5% of cases, whereas complete radiological success was achieved in 92.9% of patients. Major complications were observed in 2.8% of the procedures. In-hospital mortality rate was 3.9%, with only one death (0.4%) related to a major complication (not intra-procedure). During a median follow-up of 39 months (IQR: 17-74), all-cause mortality was 22.3%. Of these deaths, 3.9% occurred during the index hospitalization for TLE, 6.4% within the first year post-procedure, and 12.0% beyond the first year. Rehospitalisations due to cardiovascular or non-cardiovascular causes were observed in 19.8% of patients throughout the follow-up period.

CONCLUSION: TLE extraction with the PISA technique is a high effective methodology, with favourable complication and mortality rates in patients with CIED. The implementation of structured peri-procedural protocols and a growing team experience may contribute to support a high-successfully programme.

articles.title: Exome-wide characterization of genetic diversity and population-specific functional variants in indigenous tribal populations of India.
articles.journal: Journal of genetics and genomics = Yi chuan xue bao
articles.abstract: India harbors over 4600 endogamous ethnolinguistic groups shaped by multiple waves of migration, long-term isolation, and social stratification. Odisha, an eastern state of India, is home to 62 indigenous tribal groups, many of which remain genetically understudied. We perform high-coverage whole-exome sequencing of 13 tribal groups (n = 515) from Odisha, collectively termed OdiTribe. We identify 625,596 single-nucleotide variants (SNVs), of which 37.02% are rare, and 5.54% (n = 34,667) are unreported non-singletons (AC > 1). Population genetic analyses reveal that the OdiTribe populations broadly overlap with Austroasiatic- and Dravidian-speaking tribal populations, while also exhibiting heterogeneity across subgroups. Outgroup f3 statistics reveal high shared drift between Bonda and the Nicobarese. Approximately 43% of the individuals show elevated inbreeding coefficients (≥0.0156), and 14.17% carry ROH segments >8 Mb, indicative of recent consanguinity. Functional annotation identifies pathogenic variants in HBB, HBD, BTD, and BRCA2 genes, as well as multiple homozygous high-confidence predicted loss-of-function (HC-pLoF) variants across the dataset. Our study provides exome-wide insights into genetic diversity, endogamy, and population-specific variants of potential clinical relevance among endogamous indigenous tribal populations, underscoring the importance of including isolated and underrepresented groups in population and medical genetics research.

articles.title: Shared management of patients with concomitant rheumatological disease and neoplasia: A collaborative Delphi consensus by the Italian Association of Medical Oncology and the Italian Society of Rheumatology.
authors: “Rheumatologic-Oncologic Multidisciplinary Assessment - Rh.O.M.A.” SIR Study Group
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The increasing intersection between rheumatological and oncological diseases-particularly in the context of immunostimulatory cancer therapies-poses significant clinical challenges. Immunotherapy may induce new-onset autoimmune or rheumatologic manifestations, while immunosuppressive anti-rheumatic therapies may impact cancer risk and outcomes. However, solid epidemiological data and guidelines on how to manage such scenarios are lacking. This project aimed to develop expert-based guidance to support decision-making in patients with concurrent rheumatological and oncological disease or immune-related adverse events due to oncological therapies.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A modified Delphi process was conducted based on anonymity, iterative feedback, and multidisciplinary involvement. After a narrative review (54 articles, 2000-2025), three key assumptions and two sets of consensus statements were developed: Section A (7 statements) and Section B (4 statements). An expert panel of 18 clinicians (14 rheumatologists and 4 oncologists), supported by 2 methodologists, rated each statement on a 1-10 scale. Rated each statement on a 1-10 scale. Statements with lower agreement were revised and re-evaluated in in one or more additional rounds.. Voting was anonymous. Agreement was defined as >70% of experts rating a statement ≥7.5.

RESULTS: All statements reached consensus, in most cases after two rounds, and one (A4) after a third round following a substantial re-formulation.. One assumption was eliminated and three statements revised. Final agreement was reached on two assumptions and 11 statements. Experts emphasized individualized cancer risk assessment in patients on csDMARDs or bDMARDs, and early rheumatological evaluation in cancer patients with immune-related adverse events. Though robust cause-effect data are lacking, expert clinical experience may support preliminary recommendations.

CONCLUSIONS: This consensus provides structured, clinically grounded guidance for managing key challenges at the intersection of oncology and rheumatology.

articles.title: Is atherosclerosis an autoimmune disease?
articles.abstract: Atherosclerosis was traditionally viewed as a lipid-storage disorder driven by dyslipidemia and vascular injury. However, accumulating evidence indicates that immune mechanisms are central to disease initiation, progression, and plaque destabilization. Oxidized low-density lipoprotein (oxLDL) and related oxidation-specific epitopes (OSEs), ApoB100 peptides as well as newly identified autoantigens function as modified self-antigens that trigger both innate and adaptive immune responses, linking metabolic stress to chronic vascular inflammation. Innate immune activation is sustained through trained immunity, whereby monocytes and macrophages undergo long-lasting epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming that promotes a persistent pro-inflammatory phenotype. Additional contributors include dendritic cell-mediated antigen presentation, activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome and interleukin-1β signaling pathway, and type I interferon responses, all of which amplify vascular inflammation and plaque progression. Clinical benefits observed with anti-inflammatory therapies targeting these pathways provide evidence for their pathogenic relevance. Adaptive immune responses are characterized by the presence of antigen-experienced T and B lymphocytes within atherosclerotic lesions. oxLDL- and apolipoprotein B (ApoB)-reactive T cells contribute to disease progression through loss of immune tolerance and predominance of pro-inflammatory T helper 1 responses, whereas regulatory T cells exert protective effects. CD8 cytotoxic T cells as well as B cell subsets contribute to the formation of atherosclerotic plaque. Humoral responses against oxLDL generate both atheroprotective and pro-inflammatory antibodies, depending on their specificity and functional properties. Emerging evidence of tertiary lymphoid structures within the arterial wall further supports local antigen-driven immune activation. The accelerated development of atherosclerosis in systemic autoimmune diseases highlights important mechanistic overlap between systemic autoimmunity and vascular pathology. Nevertheless, immune activation in atherosclerosis remains largely initiated by lipid accumulation and vascular injury rather than a primary breakdown of systemic immune tolerance. Atherosclerosis does not appear to require a primary, generalized breakdown of systemic self-tolerance. Nevertheless, ApoB-reactive CD4+ T cells can lose regulatory features during disease progression, indicating impaired antigen-specific immune regulation. Whether, and to what extent, the local arterial environment drives this change remains to be established. Collectively, current evidence supports the concept that atherosclerosis is a chronic immune-mediated inflammatory disease with prominent autoimmune features, providing a rationale for the development of targeted immunomodulatory therapies.

articles.title: Rheumatic fever: At the interface of autoimmunity and autoinflammation - An overlap hypothesis.
articles.abstract: Autoinflammatory diseases (AIDs) are disorders of innate immunity characterised by recurrent febrile episodes, systemic inflammation and markedly elevated inflammatory markers. In their classical definition, these diseases occur without pathogenic autoantibodies or antigen-specific autoreactive T and B cells. Many systemic AIDs (SAIDs) involve organs, including the pericardium. Acute rheumatic fever (ARF) is an immune-mediated complication of group A Streptococcus (GAS) infection and remains a global health concern, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Patients with ARF experience inflammatory episodes involving fever, arthralgia, arthritis, chorea, cutaneous features, cardiac complications, all underpinned by a pronounced systemic inflammatory response. Recurrent episodes following further GAS exposure can contribute to rheumatic heart disease (RHD), its chronic valvular sequela. Genetic susceptibility and GAS exposure contribute to disease development. Molecular mimicry is a major proposed mechanism, involving cross-reactive antibodies and T cells that recognise both microbial and host antigens, including cardiac myosin, laminin and tropomyosin. However, recurrent GAS-triggered episodes of ARF are characterised by marked systemic inflammation, raising the possibility that innate immune mechanisms contribute to inflammatory amplification and disease severity. We therefore propose that rheumatic fever (RF) may lie at the interface between autoimmunity and autoinflammation, with established autoimmune mechanisms potentially complemented by dysregulated innate immune responses. This autoimmune-autoinflammatory overlap remains a hypothesis that requires validation through functional immunological studies, particularly those investigating inflammasome pathways.

articles.title: Development and evaluation of inhalable imipenem dry powder for treating pulmonary P. aeruginosa infection.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary infections caused by P. aeruginosa (PA) remain a major clinical challenge due to biofilm formation, intrinsic resistance, and limited antibiotic penetration into lung tissues following systemic administration. Imipenem (IPM), a broad-spectrum carbapenem, requires high intravenous doses (500 mg every 6 h with cilastatin) to achieve therapeutic lung levels, leading to frequent dosing and systemic toxicity. Pulmonary delivery via dry powder for inhalation (DPI) offers a targeted alternative. However, formulation development is hindered by the chemical instability, specifically its susceptibility to thermal and hydrolytic degradation in the amorphous state. In this study, a high-dose, chemically stable IPM dry powder for inhalation (IPM-DPI) was developed by co-spray-drying IPM with L-leucine. The optimized 50:50 (w/w) IPM: L-leucine powder exhibited an initial IPM potency of ∼94% and low residual moisture content (<2% w/w). Differential scanning calorimetry and powder X-ray diffraction of IPM-DPI confirmed amorphous IPM and semi-crystalline L-leucine, while Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy suggested intermolecular interactions between IPM and L-leucine. The IPM-DPI demonstrated excellent aerosolization, achieving fine particle fractions of ∼67% (Orbital™ DPI) and ∼53% (RS01® DPI), with a mass median aerodynamic diameter of 2.4-3.2 µm and retained antimicrobial potency (minimum inhibitory concentration of 0.125-0.25 µg/mL). IPM-DPI maintained >95% of its initial IPM potency after 6 months at -20 °C, demonstrating improved stability associated with intermolecular interactions between leucine and IMP, with the semi-crystalline leucine phase forming a matrix around IMP molecules within the particle core. Overall, the developed IPM-DPI enables localized pulmonary delivery of imipenem, potentially eliminating the need for cilastatin and reducing systemic toxicity associated with parenteral therapy.

articles.title: House dust mite sublingual immunotherapy and rhinitis-related quality of life in biologic-controlled severe asthma: A propensity score-matched real-world study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether house dust mite sublingual immunotherapy (HDM-SLIT) provides additional clinical benefits in patients with severe asthma already controlled by biologic therapy remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effects of add-on HDM-SLIT on rhinitis-related and asthma-related outcomes in patients with biologic-controlled severe asthma and allergic rhinitis.

METHODS: In this propensity score-matched real-world study, 86 patients with severe asthma and allergic rhinitis were analyzed after 1:1 matching of patients receiving HDM-SLIT with those receiving biologic therapy or continuing biologic therapy alone (43 patients per group). Changes in Rhinoconjunctivitis Quality of Life Questionnaire (RQLQ), Asthma Quality of Life Questionnaire (AQLQ), Asthma Control Questionnaire (ACQ)-6, lung function, type 2 biomarkers, and airway structural parameters by quantitative computed tomography were evaluated over 12 months. Covariate-adjusted analyses and a sensitivity analysis restricted to patients receiving dupilumab were performed.

RESULTS: RQLQ showed greater improvement with HDM-SLIT than with control (standardized mean differences [SMD] 1.545, 95% CI 0.910-2.180; p <0.001), and this finding remained significant in covariate-adjusted and dupilumab-restricted sensitivity analyses. AQLQ also improved with HDM-SLIT (SMD 0.673, 95% CI 0.097-1.250; p = 0.036). ACQ-6, FEV1% predicted, and percentage of airway wall area relative to total area (WA/Ao%) showed nominally greater improvements in the primary analyses (p = 0.023, 0.039, and 0.038, respectively). but these findings were not statistically significant after additional covariate adjustment.

CONCLUSION: In patients with biologic-controlled severe asthma with allergic rhinitis, the most consistent benefit associated with add-on HDM-SLIT was improvement in rhinitis-related quality of life.

articles.title: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and major cardiovascular events: Hospital resource use, survival and predictors of death in a retrospective cohort from the Brazilian private healthcare system.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brazilian data on the course of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) after a myocardial infarction or stroke are scarce.

OBJECTIVES: To estimate the association of myocardial infarction or stroke with death and hospital resource use in patients with COPD in a Brazilian private healthcare network.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort of patients aged 40 years or older with a COPD-specific ICD-10 code (J41 to J44) and a spirometry report, followed from the date both criteria were met. Myocardial infarction or stroke was a time-varying exposure: patients with a history at entry were exposed from entry, and those with a first event during follow-up were exposed from the event. Cox models with the time-varying exposure and negative binomial regression were used.

RESULTS: The 1257 patients were followed for 1368 person-years; 63 had a history of myocardial infarction or stroke at entry and 41 had a first event during follow-up. Sixty-two died, 3.8 per 100 person-years in unexposed and 15.4 in exposed person-time (adjusted HR 3.81; 95% CI 2.00 to 7.27; p < 0.001), with the highest hazard in the first 90 days after an incident event (HR 4.26). Exposed person-time had more hospital admissions (IRR 2.69; 95% CI 1.85 to 3.92) and intensive care unit admissions (IRR 3.77; 95% CI 2.25 to 6.33).

CONCLUSION: In patients with COPD, myocardial infarction or stroke was followed by a near fourfold increase in the hazard of death and a threefold increase in hospital admissions.

articles.title: Recurrence After Primary Lumbar Discectomy: Rate, Reoperation, and Risk Factors in A Single-Center Cohort Over A 10-Year Study Period.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Recurrent lumbar disc herniation after primary discectomy is a clinically important complication whose temporal pattern, revision surgical profile, and associated comorbidities remain incompletely characterized in long-term cohorts. We aimed to define the rate and timing of reoperation-confirmed recurrence, characterize the revision profile, and examine associated risk factors.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 432 consecutive patients who underwent primary lumbar discectomy between January 2015 and December 2024, with a median follow-up of 85 months (interquartile range 50-103). Recurrence was defined as reoperation-confirmed, same-level ipsilateral reherniation after an initial pain-free interval. Follow-up status and external reoperations were verified through the national electronic health record system up to the study end date (6 March 2026), with no loss to follow-up. Associations were examined using multivariable logistic regression (with Firth penalization) and Cox proportional hazards modeling.

RESULTS: Reoperation-confirmed recurrence occurred in 28 patients (6.5%); this represents the reoperation-confirmed recurrence rate rather than the overall incidence of recurrent herniation, since conservatively managed recurrences were not counted. Recurrence was predominantly late, with 68% of events beyond the first postoperative year (median 18.5 months). At reoperation, 21 patients (75%) required instrumented posterolateral fusion for objective segmental instability, with a mean segmental translation of 4.2 ± 1.1 mm and a mean angulation of 12.2° ± 2.1° on dynamic flexion-extension radiographs, both exceeding the predefined instability thresholds. The remaining 7 patients (25%) underwent revision discectomy alone. No second recurrence occurred over a median post-revision follow-up of 61.5 months. In the primary logistic model, hypertension was associated with recurrence (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 3.42, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.04-11.21; p = 0.043), whereas the association of diabetes mellitus was of similar magnitude but did not reach statistical significance (OR 3.17, 95% CI 0.97-10.35; p = 0.056). Diabetes mellitus reached significance only in the secondary Firth penalized and time-to-event analyses. Active smoking was not associated with recurrence (OR 0.64; p = 0.321). Given the limited number of events (n = 28), these findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory; in particular, the study was not powered to overturn existing evidence linking smoking with recurrence, and the 10-year survival estimate is exploratory given few patients at risk beyond 5 years.

CONCLUSION: In this 10-year single-center cohort, reoperation-confirmed recurrence occurred in 6.5% of patients and was predominantly late (median 18.5 months), indicating that postoperative surveillance should extend beyond the first year. Three quarters of revisions required instrumented fusion for objective instability. No second recurrence was observed. Hypertension was associated with recurrence in the primary analysis, whereas the association of diabetes mellitus did not reach significance in the primary model and was supported only by secondary analyses. Both comorbidities should be investigated further in adequately powered multicenter studies.

articles.title: Fever Without Source in Well-Appearing Neonates and Young Infants ≤ 60 Days of Age.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There are only a few evidence-based clinical practice guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of febrile (rectal body temperature ≥ 38°C) neonates/young infants aged > 7 and ≤ 60 days who are in good general condition (well-appearing) and in whom no clinical source of infection can be identified (fever without source, FWS). The approach in clinical practice is correspondingly heterogeneous, resulting in excessive exposure to invasive diagnostics, hospital admissions, and broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy.

METHODS: Critical discussion of published studies and a comprehensive literature search conducted by an expert group of the GERMAN SOCIETY FOR PAEDIATRIC INFECTIOUS DISEASES: followed by step-by-step consensus on clinical algorithms adjusted to the German healthcare system.

RESULTS: The consensus discussion was informed by data from 124 studies published since the release of the US clinical practice guideline of the American Academy of Pediatrics in 2021 or adding evidence relevant to the guideline. Newborns with FWS (8th to 28th day of life) should be admitted to a paediatric hospital. A blood culture and a clean-catch or catheter urine sample must be taken. Regardless of viral co-infections or laboratory signs of inflammation, a lumbar puncture and an empiric antibiotic therapy for neonatal sepsis should be seriously considered for these children. In febrile young infants > 28 and ≤ 60 days of age (well-appearing with FWS), a blood culture and a clean-catch or catheter urine sample should also be taken. However, a stepwise approach is indicated when deciding on hospitalization, lumbar puncture, and antibiotic therapy. The absolute neutrophil count, C-reactive protein, procalcitonin, and laboratory signs suggesting viral infections are considered in the algorithm. Under certain safety conditions, outpatient care without antibiotic therapy is possible in individual cases, and clinicians should engage parents in shared decision-making whenever there is more than one recommended option.

CONCLUSION: The risk-based approach proposed here for well-appearing infants > 7 and ≤ 60 days of age with FWS has the potential to avoid unnecessary lumbar punctures, antibiotic therapy, and hospital admissions without neglecting the increased risk of invasive bacterial infections in this age group. However, a prospective multicentre evaluation in the German healthcare system is warranted.

articles.title: Pituitary Stalk Interruption Syndrome in Adulthood: Diagnostic Recognition, Clinical Spectrum, and Long-Term Follow-Up.
articles.journal: Hormone and metabolic research = Hormon- und Stoffwechselforschung = Hormones et metabolisme
articles.abstract: Pituitary stalk interruption syndrome is usually diagnosed during childhood, and data on outcomes in adulthood are limited. This retrospective, single-center study evaluated the diagnostic history, endocrine phenotype, and clinical outcomes of 14 adults with radiologically confirmed pituitary stalk interruption syndrome. The cohort comprised eight men and six women, with a mean age of 28.8±6.4 years and a mean documented follow-up at our center of 5.6±3.2 years. Hypopituitarism was diagnosed during childhood in 12 patients and during adulthood in 2 patients. Thirteen patients had deficiencies of all four anterior pituitary hormone axes, whereas one patient had growth hormone and gonadotropic deficiencies with preserved corticotropic and thyrotropic functions. In six patients diagnosed during childhood, pituitary stalk interruption syndrome was recognized only after later reassessment of pituitary imaging. Eleven patients received growth hormone treatment during childhood, and 13 of 14 patients reached their calculated target height. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and dyslipidemia were each present in 10 patients. Four patients had bone mineral density below the expected range for age. One female patient achieved a live birth following in vitro fertilization. In this real-world cohort, the skeletal and metabolic findings observed despite generally favorable growth outcomes support the need for lifelong endocrine follow-up.

articles.title: Cardiovascular outcomes with survodutide in adults with obesity at increased cardiovascular risk (SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Survodutide, a glucagon receptor and GLP-1 receptor dual agonist, improved markers of cardiometabolic health in people with obesity, but cardiovascular safety for this new class remains to be established.

METHODS: SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT was a global, phase 3, randomised, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled, multicentre, event-driven, cardiovascular safety trial conducted at 524 clinical sites in 34 countries. We included participants aged 18 years or older with a BMI of 27 kg/m2 or greater and established cardiovascular disease or at least two obesity complications or risk factors for cardiovascular disease; participants with chronic kidney disease were eligible if they also had a BMI of 30 kg/m2 or greater. Participants were randomly assigned by interactive response technology (1:1:1) to once-weekly subcutaneous survodutide (up-titrated to 3·6 mg or 6·0 mg) or placebo. The primary endpoint was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, non-fatal stroke, non-fatal myocardial infarction, ischaemia-related coronary revascularisation, or heart failure event (targeting 189 primary endpoint events). We assessed the non-inferiority of pooled survodutide compared with placebo with a margin of 1·65 for the upper limit of the two-sided 95% CI of the hazard ratio (HR). Efficacy and safety analyses included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of survodutide or placebo. The primary analysis was performed according to the treatment-regimen estimand, which assessed treatment effects regardless of any early discontinuation of survodutide or placebo, temporary stop, the use of protocol-prohibited obesity medications, or a prolonged dose-escalation period. This completed trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06077864.

FINDINGS: From Nov 20, 2023, to Nov 8, 2024, we screened 7753 participants, of whom 5530 (71·3%) participants were recruited and randomly assigned to treatment. 23 (0·4%) participants were not treated; 1836 (33·3%) of 5507 participants received survodutide 3·6 mg, 1835 (33·3%) received 6·0 mg, and 1836 (33·3%) received placebo; 2194 (39·8%) were female, 3313 (60·2%) were male, and 4332 (78·7%) were White. Median time in study was 22·0 months (IQR 20·1-23·7). 1029 (56·0%) in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, 1039 (56·6%) in the survodutide 6·0 mg group, and 1083 (59·0%) in the placebo group remained on treatment until study closeout. The primary endpoint occurred in 136 (3·7%) of 3671 participants in the survodutide group and in 76 (4·1%) 1836 participants in the placebo group (HR 0·89 [95% CI 0·67-1·18; p<0·0001 for non-inferiority). Adverse events occurred in 1708 (93·0%) of 1836 participants with survodutide 3·6 mg, 1708 (93·1%) of 1835 with survodutide 6·0 mg, and 1571 (85·6%) of 1836 with placebo. Gastrointestinal adverse events were more frequent with survodutide than in the placebo group (nausea occurred in 882 [48·0%] of 1836 participants in the 3·6 mg group and 900 [49·0%] of 1835 in the 6·0 mg group vs 223 [12·1%] of 1836 in the placebo group, and vomiting occurred in 582 [31·7%] participants in the 3·6 mg group and 623 [34·0%] in the 6·0 mg group vs 89 [4·8%] in the placebo group). Gastrointestinal adverse events leading to treatment discontinuations occurred in 354 (19·3%) participants in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, 381 (20·8%) in the survodutide 6·0 mg, and 34 (1·9%) in the placebo group. Serious adverse events occurred at similar rates across treatment groups (413 [22·5%] in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, 381 [20·8%] in the survodutide 6·0 mg, and 439 [23·9%] in the placebo group). Fatal adverse events were similar across treatment groups (16 [0·9%] in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, 16 [0·9%] in the survodutide 6·0 mg, and 11 [0·6%] in the placebo group) and were primarily due to cardiac disorders (six [0·3%] in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, seven [0·4%] in the survodutide 6·0 mg, and six [0·3%] in the placebo group).

INTERPRETATION: In participants with obesity with established cardiovascular disease or chronic kidney disease or at increased risk of cardiovascular disease, survodutide was not associated with increased risk for the primary composite endpoint of death from cardiovascular causes, non-fatal stroke, non-fatal myocardial infarction, ischaemia-related coronary revascularisation, or heart failure event compared with placebo. This cardiovascular safety trial provides clinicians with reassuring data that treatment with survodutide, a novel glucagon receptor-GLP-1 receptor dual agonist, is not associated with increased cardiovascular risk.

FUNDING: Boehringer Ingelheim.

articles.title: Naegleria fowleri in a warming world: epidemiology, genotypic distribution, management challenges, and priorities for public health action.
articles.abstract: Naegleria fowleri causes primary amoebic meningoencephalitis, a fatal infection with profound implications for global health burden and water safety. Rising global temperatures and ageing water infrastructure are expanding the ecological range of this pathogen, increasing exposure risk in both high-income and resource-constrained settings. The infection mainly occurs through contact with warm freshwater and brackish waters and inhalation of cyst-laden dust; however, surveillance systems remain fragmented and under-resourced, particularly in low-income and middle-income countries. Diagnosis is often delayed or made post-mortem, and survival is exceedingly rare. In this Review, we synthesised the current knowledge on global epidemiology, genotypic distribution, and environmental drivers of N fowleri emergence and identified key gaps in monitoring, water treatment, and governance. We propose that climate-resilient water safety strategies, integrated surveillance, and cross-sectoral collaboration are urgently needed to mitigate the risk of Nfowleri exposure and to minimise future cases of primary amoebic meningoencephalitis. Strengthening global health systems to address this emerging threat will require coordinated investment, policy innovation, and research to close knowledge gaps and protect clinically vulnerable populations.

articles.title: Reconstructing developmental and disease progression with sample-level embeddings.
articles.abstract: Single-cell genomics is transformative for characterizing cellular heterogeneity, but many biological questions require comparing samples rather than individual cells. Typical analyses compare "case" and "control" groups, ignoring sample-level variation within them. Here, we present scSLIDE (single-cell sample-level inference using density estimation), a framework that transforms each sample's single-cell data into a compact profile describing where its cells are distributed in high-dimensional space. By comparing these density profiles, scSLIDE calculates embeddings to characterize variation across samples. We implement scSLIDE in version 6 of our Seurat package and apply it to COVID-19 infection, Alzheimer's disease, and zebrafish embryogenesis. scSLIDE reveals patient subgroups, reconstructs disease trajectories, and identifies coordinated cellular programs across samples. We discover separable axes of infection and severity, a trajectory of Alzheimer's progression, and embryonic "pseudostages" that vary across and within time points. Our results demonstrate how case-control analyses collapse rich biological variation into binary labels and how sample-level embedding represents a powerful analytical alternative.

articles.title: The Association of Body Weight, Composition, and Anthropometric Indices of Obesity with the Presence of Diabetic Neuropathy in People with Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Observational Studies.
articles.journal: Obesity reviews : an official journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Obesity has been identified as an independent risk factor for the development of diabetic neuropathy in type 2 diabetes (T2D). However, the relationship of individual parameters relating obesity with diabetic neuropathy is poorly understood. We evaluated these relationships in this systematic review and meta-analysis.

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase were searched from 1980 to July 5, 2025, for observational studies comparing anthropometric measures, including body weight, visceral fat (%), body mass index (BMI), waist circumference (WC), and waist-to-hip ratio (WHR), between individuals with and without diabetic neuropathy. Mean differences (MDs), odds ratios (ORs), and hazard ratios (HRs) were pooled using random-effects models. Subgroup and meta-regression analyses explored sources of heterogeneity by neuropathy type, geographic region, study design, diabetes duration, and HbA1c.

RESULTS: Higher BMI was significantly associated with diabetic neuropathy (OR = 1.09; 95% CI: 1.02 to 1.16; MD = 0.55; 95% CI: 0.22 to 0.89). Central obesity was associated with neuropathy risk (WC MD = 2.05 cm; 95% CI: 1.15 to 2.94; HR = 1.25; 95% CI: 1.04 to 1.51; WHR MD = 0.01; 95% CI: 0.00 to 0.01). Associations were more evident for peripheral neuropathy than for autonomic neuropathy. Diabetes duration and HbA1c may contribute to the heterogeneity between studies.

CONCLUSION: BMI and WC were consistently, albeit modestly, associated with diabetic neuropathy in individuals with T2D, whereas the difference in WHR was small and inconsistent across neuropathy subtypes. No significant differences were observed in either body weight or visceral fat between individuals with and without diabetic neuropathy.

articles.title: Challenges and Improvement Strategies to Increase Staff Vaccination Coverage in Long-Term Care.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Keeping staff in post-acute and long-term care (PALTC) settings up to date on adult vaccinations is important to protect them and reduce the spread of vaccine-preventable illness to residents. This quality improvement (QI) project aimed to increase vaccination coverage among PALTC staff while exploring improvement strategies tailored to this setting.

DESIGN: QI project conducted in 2, 12-month cohorts between 2022 and 2024.

SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: QI teams from 15 skilled nursing facilities and 6 assisted living facilities across 9 states participated in the QI project. QI teams included staff and administrators working at the facility and corporate level in roles such as medical directors, directors/assistant directors of nursing, and infection preventionists.

METHODS: QI teams implemented vaccination strategies, reported monthly staff vaccination coverage for 3 vaccines (COVID-19, influenza, and hepatitis B), received monthly technical assistance, and met quarterly with other facilities to share lessons learned. We report staff vaccination coverage at baseline and end point by vaccine, highlight common challenges across participating facilities, and provide examples of facilities' QI strategies.

RESULTS: Most facilities did not improve staff vaccination coverage. Only 1 of 16 facilities with complete COVID-19 coverage data (6%) showed a modest improvement over time, 7 of 15 facilities with complete influenza coverage data (47%) maintained or improved coverage, and 4 of 6 facilities with complete hepatitis B coverage data (67%) showed improvement. Facilities focused their QI efforts on making vaccination convenient, respecting staff autonomy, and engaging staff in dialog but were challenged by staffing shortages, limited data infrastructure, and vaccine hesitancy. Facilities found it especially difficult to gather and report immunization data for staff; in some cases, low coverage reflected missing data.

CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Improving PALTC staff vaccination coverage nationally will require addressing data gaps, making vaccination convenient and affordable for staff, and addressing vaccine hesitancy through respectful dialog.

articles.title: Long-term effects of driver feedback on harsh braking behavior: insights from survival models.
articles.abstract: This study investigates the long-term effects of smartphone-based driver feedback on harsh braking behavior using a large-scale naturalistic driving dataset. The overall naturalistic driving dataset comprised 24,904 trips from 31 drivers across all experimental phases, of which 2220 post-feedback trips were used to investigate relapse after feedback withdrawal. The analysis compares behavior across baseline, feedback and post-feedback periods to assess both immediate and sustained effects of feedback interventions. Descriptive statistics and non-parametric tests indicate a significant reduction in harsh braking events during the feedback phase, confirming the short-term effectiveness of feedback in improving driving behavior. However, a noticeable relapse is observed following the removal of feedback, suggesting challenges in maintaining behavioral improvements over time. To further explore the persistence of these effects, survival analysis techniques were applied, including Kaplan-Meier estimators, Cox Proportional Hazards models with frailty, Weibull Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) models with clustered heterogeneity and Random Survival Forests (RSF). The Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrates a gradual decline in the probability of remaining free from a first relapse during the post-feedback phase, reaching approximately 40.3 % by the 150-trip mark. Key predictors of relapse include driver age, vehicle engine capacity and trip duration, with older drivers exhibiting more stable behavior over time. In terms of model performance, the Weibull AFT model provided the most suitable balance between interpretability and predictive accuracy, while the RSF model provided a flexible, non-parametric, data-driven approach capable of accommodating complex non-linear relationships and interactions among predictors. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of continuous or reinforced feedback mechanisms to sustain safer driving behavior and provide a methodological framework for assessing long-term behavioral dynamics using survival analysis.

articles.title: Fumarate hydratase attenuates HDM/LPS-induced asthmatic airway inflammation by inhibiting Drp1-mediated mitochondrial fission in airway epithelial cells.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitochondrial structural and functional dysfunction in airway epithelial cells is recognized as a central driver in the progression of severe asthma. However, the current understanding of the mechanisms underlying damage to the mitochondria remains insufficient, and effective therapeutic strategies for its repair are lacking. Fumarate hydratase (FH) is a pivotal metabolic enzyme in the tricarboxylic acid cycle. It exhibits anti-inflammatory and tissue-repairing effects in immune-related diseases, but its contribution to asthma has not been previously reported.

METHODS: We examined the role of FH in severe asthma utilizing human transcriptomic datasets and in vitro (airway epithelial cells) and in vivo (mouse) models induced by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) in combination with house dust mites (HDM), in conjunction with FH overexpression and pharmacological inhibition interventions. Mitochondrial function, mitochondrial dynamics, and inflammatory responses were assessed, together with Drp1 overexpression rescue and NRF2 inhibition experiments.

RESULTS: Analysis of human severe asthma datasets, together with HDM/LPS-induced cellular and mouse models, consistently revealed reduced FH expression. Restoration of FH expression improved mitochondrial function, suppressed Drp1-associated mitochondrial fission, and reduced airway inflammation, whereas Drp1 overexpression partially reversed the mitochondrial protective effects of FH. FH also reduced Keap1 expression, promoted NRF2 nuclear translocation and HO-1 expression, and NRF2 inhibition attenuated the anti-inflammatory effects of FH.

CONCLUSION: These findings identify FH as a previously unrecognized metabolic regulator with protective effects in airway inflammation and support a role for mitochondrial fission-fusion dynamics in FH-mediated protection of airway epithelial cells.

articles.title: Cognitive load of healthcare professionals in the intensive care unit: A bibliometric analysis from 2016 to 2025.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To identify research hotspots, major contributors, and developmental trends in studies on cognitive load among ICU healthcare professionals.

METHOD: A bibliometric analysis was conducted on data retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection, covering scholarly publications from January 1, 2016, to December 31, 2025. CiteSpace software was used to visualize and analyze countries, institutions, cited journals, and keywords.

RESULTS: A total of 169 articles were included. The annual publication output showed a steady upward trend over the decade, rising from 7 publications in 2016 to 34 in 2025. Notably, 82 articles (48.5% of the total) were published between 2023 and 2025. The United States ranked first in contributions (63 publications, 37.28%). Capital Medical University in China was the most productive institution (6 publications, 3.55%). The most frequently cited journal was Critical Care Medicine (75 citations). Research hotspots centered on three thematic directions: workload and mental demand among ICU nursing staff, psychological outcomes and occupational well-being, and clinical assessment and patient-centered management. Emerging trends included psychological well-being promotion and risk prevention related to cognitive load.

CONCLUSIONS: Research on cognitive load in ICU healthcare professionals has grown substantially, with increasing attention to nursing workload, mental health, and patient safety.

articles.title: Health-related quality of life after intensive care: a longitudinal cohort study using item-level network analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine relationships between individual SF-36 items at 3 and 12 months after intensive care unit (ICU) discharge using network analysis with conventional health-related quality of life (HRQoL) scores as complementary context.

METHODS: This single-center longitudinal cohort study included adult ICU survivors admitted between March 2011 and December 2021 who completed the 36-item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36) at 3 and 12 months. Item-level Gaussian graphical models were estimated and compared using a paired-sample Network Comparison Test. Conventional SF-36 scores were described over time and compared with French population reference values.

RESULTS: Overall, 479 ICU survivors completed both assessments. Bodily Pain item 2 (BP2), assessing pain interference with normal work, ranked among the three items with the highest node strength at both assessments and was associated with the Social Functioning item 1 (SF1). Network structure (M = 0.178, p = 0.14) and global strength (S = 0.032, p = 0.90) did not differ significantly between 3 and 12 months. Seven of the 319 descriptively retained edges had unadjusted p values below 0.005. HRQoL remained below French reference values at 12 months particularly in physical and role-related domains, despite partial improvement.

CONCLUSIONS: Item-level network analysis provided a complementary perspective on SF-36 responses by describing relationships between individual HRQoL items alongside the extent of impairment captured by conventional scores. Its implications for follow-up and rehabilitation remain hypothesis-generating.

IMPLICATIONS FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE: Conventional HRQoL scores alone may not fully capture how symptoms and functional dimensions are interconnected. Combining score-based assessment with network information may support a more comprehensive evaluation of recovery after critical illness.

articles.title: SPARC: Sectorized Partial-Angle Reconstruction Based Motion Correction Method for Multi-Phase CCTA.
articles.abstract: Multi-phase Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography (CCTA) provides a clear visualization of coronary arteries, offering comprehensive and reliable imaging support for the clinical diagnosis of coronary artery disease. However, traditional motion correction reconstruction algorithms lack reconstruction robustness despite their interpretability, while deep learning reconstruction methods achieve high imaging quality at the expense of interpretability and anatomical reliability in clinical CCTA practice. This study aims to simultaneously achieve interpretable and robust multi-phase coronary reconstruction.Approach. We propose a motion trajectory estimation and motion correction framework termed sectorized partial-angle reconstruction-based motion correction (SPARC) for CCTA. The proposed framework integrates sectorized partial-angle reconstructions, a spatio-temporal cascaded network for coronary centerline extraction, and a phase-accumulated fuzzy C-means clustering algorithm for motion trajectory estimation. These components work together to minimize motion estimation errors and enhance the quality of motion-corrected reconstruction.Main results. Experimental results from both simulations and clinical studies demonstrate that SPARC achieves superior reconstruction performance compared with existing methods. SPARC effectively reduces coronary motion artifacts and restores clear vessel structures while preserving reconstruction fidelity, achieving the best scores on all metrics.Significance. By preserving both interpretability and anatomical reliability while effectively reducing motion artifacts, SPARC provides a clinically deployable solution for motion-corrected multi-phase CCTA, supporting more reliable imaging for coronary artery disease diagnosis.

articles.title: Sampling-free Monte Carlo dropout approximation for single-pass uncertainty quantification in deep learning-based PET reconstructions.
articles.abstract: Medical image reconstructions using deep learning (DL) can rapidly generate high-quality images from degraded measurements, but their clinical adoption remains challenging, largely due to the lack of fast and reliable methods to quantify aleatoric (data-driven) and epistemic (model-driven) uncertainties on a per-prediction basis. We aim to develop a computationally efficient approach for estimating both uncertainties at the voxel level in DL-based image reconstruction within a single inference run.Approach: We present a moment propagation-based framework that analytically approximates the conventional, multi-realization Monte Carlo (MC) dropout by propagating feature-map means and marginal variances through network layers, followed by a pre-calibrated correction table to compensate for covariance effects omitted in the approximation. This enables joint estimation of reconstruction, aleatoric uncertainty and epistemic uncertainty in a single forward pass. The proposed framework was implemented on top of FastPET -- a network model synthesizing PET reconstructions from time-of-flight histo-images -- and evaluated in a patient pilot study of 26 total-body PET/CT acquisitions (16 [18F]-FDG and 10 [18F]-PSMA cases).Main Results: Proposed method achieved relatively strong agreement with the 50-pass MC approach, with absolute differences <0.5% for reconstruction, <4.2% for aleatoric uncertainty and <9.8% for epistemic uncertainty, along with narrow spreads across patients and tracer types, while reducing computation time by ~40-fold. In a complementary proof-of-concept low-count experiment, regional tracer uptake confidence intervals (CIs, derived from propagated uncertainties) widened with increased noise level, and reference uptakes consistently fell close to CI boundaries, indicating the proposed method could provide roughly calibrated uncertainty magnitudes reflecting quantitative prediction errors.Significance: The proposed approach provides a sampling-free and relatively accurate approximation to the multi-pass MC-based uncertainty estimation in the histo-image-based DL PET reconstruction framework. Per-prediction uncertainty quantification enables direct assessment of AI confidence and potentially supports more reliable and informed decision-making.

articles.title: Influence of Aging and Wave-Current on Microplastic Transport in Estuarine Environments.
articles.abstract: Estuaries are critical transition zones for microplastics (MPs) migrating from rivers to the ocean and are recognized as hotspots for MP accumulation. However, the transport and deposition of MPs under the combined action of waves and currents in these environments remain poorly understood. Here, this study investigated the behavior of three MP types (PA, PVC, and PET) using laboratory flume experiments. Fenton oxidation was used to simulate aging over 0-15 days, and high-speed imaging (50 fps) was utilized to capture particle trajectories and instantaneous velocities under both current-only and combined wave-current conditions. Under current-only conditions, the horizontal transport distance decreased in the order PA > PVC > PET, i.e., opposite to the order of particle density (PA < PVC < PET). The denser PET particles settled more rapidly, shortening the time available for horizontal advection, whereas the lower-density PA particles remained in suspension longer and were thus transported farther. Fenton aging markedly enhanced the transport capacity of settling MPs. In contrast, the addition of wave transformed particle trajectories from nearly linear settling to cycloidal or spiral patterns, significantly suppressing horizontal transport. A dimensional-analysis-based semi-empirical model confirmed that wave parameters dominated MP transport. This study reveals a "wave-induced interception effect" in estuaries, whereby strong wave dynamics suppress the horizontal transport of settling MPs and largely mask the effect of aging on their transport. These findings offer new insights for predicting the fate of aged MPs in estuarine environments.

articles.title: External hydrocephalus in adult neurocritical patients.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: External hydrocephalus (EH) in adults is an underrecognized clinical entity characterized by CSF circulatory failure and progressive subarachnoid space (SAS) dilation under high intracranial pressure (ICP). Data regarding its incidence, pathophysiology, and management in adult neurocritical care are sparse.

OBJECTIVE: To describe the incidence, risk factors and outcome of EH in adult neurocritical patients.

METHODS: Prospective study of patients with moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury (msTBI) or spontaneous subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) admitted to intensive care unit (ICU). Three subgroups ere defined: 1) radiological EH: dilated SAS between two successive CT scans; 2) radiological EH in the context of intracranial hypertension (IH): suspected o confirmed elevated ICP; and 3) radiological EH and invasively documented elevated ICP.

RESULTS: A total of 128 patients were included (78 msTBI, 50 SAH). The incidence of radiological EH was 20.3 % (26.9 % in msTBI and 10 % in SAH), while the incidence of radiological EH in the context of IH was 7.8 % (10.3 % in msTBI vs. 4 % in SAH). The median time to EH onset was 4.5. Radiological EH in the context of IH was significantly associated with younger age, refractory intracranial hypertension, surgical intervention, decompressive craniectomy, and prolonged ICU stay. Intracranial hypertension due to EH required external lumbar drainage in 70 %.

CONCLUSIONS: The first prospective study on EH adult neurocritical patients is presented. EH presents as a not uncommon and complex driver of secondary neurological deterioration and prolonged hospital resource utilization in adult neurocritical care. Diagnosis requires a high index of suspicion based on clinical and radiological findings. It is associated with refractory intracranial hypertension, generally requiring an external lumbar drainage.

articles.title: CMRCUNet: a cross-modal calibration U-Net for acute ischaemic stroke lesion segmentation from multi-sequence MRI.
articles.abstract: Acute ischaemic stroke is a major cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide, and rapid delineation of infarct lesions on brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is important for supporting time-sensitive treatment decisions. Multi-sequence MRI, including diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps, and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR), provides complementary information for characterising acute ischaemic lesions. However, many deep learning approaches process these modalities using shared encoders and direct skip connections, which may limit modality-specific feature learning and remain challenged by the severe foreground-background imbalance characteristic of stroke lesion segmentation.Method: We propose CMRCUNet, a multimodal segmentation framework that combines modality-specific residual encoders, a Cross-Modal Calibration (CMC) module, and an attention-gated decoder. The modality-specific encoders independently learn sequence-dependent representations from DWI, ADC, and FLAIR, while the CMC module performs adaptive, input-dependent weighting of modality-specific features at multiple resolution levels before decoder fusion. Focal Tversky Loss is used to address severe lesion-background imbalance. The framework is evaluated in both 2D and 2.5D configurations; the 2.5D configuration incorporates neighbouring axial slices to provide limited through-plane contextual information while retaining two-dimensional convolutional operations. Test-time augmentation (TTA) is additionally evaluated to improve inference robustness.Results: CMRCUNet was evaluated on the ISLES 2022 dataset using a patient-level evaluation protocol with an independent 37-patient test cohort. The 2.5D configuration combined with TTA achieved a Dice similarity coefficient of 0.792 ± 0.142, sensitivity of 0.854 ± 0.132, specificity of 0.996 ± 0.012, and a 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) of 8.21 ± 8.70 mm.Conclusion: CMRCUNet provides a multimodal framework that integrates modality-specific feature extraction, adaptive cross-modal calibration, attention-gated decoding, and limited inter-slice contextual information for acute ischaemic stroke lesion segmentation. The results support further investigation of adaptive cross-modal calibration, particularly through external multi-centre validation.

articles.title: Morphology-dependent Fe3O4 nanozymes with NIR-enhanced peroxidase-like activity for antibacterial wound therapy.
articles.abstract: Bacterial infection severely impairs wound repair, and antibiotic-based treatment is increasingly challenged by antimicrobial resistance. Herein, Fe3O4 nanozymes with octahedral, spherical, and cubic morphologies were synthesized and systematically compared for peroxidase-like activity, photothermal performance, and antibacterial efficacy. Despite their comparable sizes and good dispersibility, the three nanozymes exhibited distinct morphology-dependent catalytic activities. Octahedral Fe3O4 nanoparticles (O-IONP) showed the highest POD-like activity, strongest hydroxyl radical generation, lowest apparent Michaelis constant toward TMB, and highest maximum reaction velocity. The catalytic activity of Fe3O4 nanozymes increased with temperature and reached an optimum near 55 oC, indicating the feasibility of photothermalenhanced catalysis. Under 808 nm near-infrared irradiation, O-IONP displayed the most efficient photothermal response and reached a temperature favourable for POD-like catalysis. In vitro, O-IONP combined with NIR reduced Escherichia coli viability to approximately 2% and caused severe bacterial membrane deformation, collapse, and rupture, while maintaining acceptable cytocompatibility toward macrophages. In an E. coli-infected wound model, O-IONP with NIR significantly accelerated wound closure, reducing the wound remaining ratio to approximately 13% on day 10. This work demonstrates a simple morphology-engineered Fe3O4 nanozyme platform for photothermal-catalytic antibacterial therapy and infected wound healing.

articles.title: SARS-CoV-2 variants and cardiovascular complications - Implications for surveillance and vaccination: A narrative review.
articles.abstract: COVID-19, caused by SARS-CoV-2, is linked to both acute and lasting cardiovascular complications. This review synthesizes 165 studies from MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library to summarize cardiovascular outcomes, underlying mechanisms, and implications for variant surveillance and vaccination. Clinical evidence reveals increased risks of arrhythmias, ischemic and inflammatory heart disease, heart failure, cerebrovascular events, and thromboembolic disorders even after the acute phase, including in non-hospitalized patients. These risks are higher following more severe infections. Proposed mechanisms include direct viral injury, endothelial dysfunction, complement activation, dysregulated inflammation and coagulation, and disruption of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system. Experimental studies show spike mutations alter viral entry and antibody escape, though their impact on cardiovascular outcomes is still unclear.
