Vaccination is associated with fewer cardiovascular events and post-acute sequelae, despite offering incomplete protection. Ongoing genomic surveillance, vaccination efforts, and cardiovascular follow-up are crucial to inform preventive strategies and manage the long-term cardiovascular burden of SARS-CoV-2 infection.

articles.title: Bow hunter's syndrome presenting with embolism in an older patient treated with C1-2 posterior fixation using intraoperative digital subtraction angiography: illustrative case.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bow hunter's syndrome (BHS) is a rare cause of vertebrobasilar insufficiency (VBI) or artery-to-artery embolism resulting from vertebral artery (VA) occlusion during head rotation due to cervical instability. VBI predominates, whereas embolic BHS is rare.

OBSERVATIONS: A 77-year-old man presented with recurrent posterior circulation ischemic strokes. A cardiac embolism was initially suspected, and a brief episode of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF) was detected via an insertable cardiac monitor. However, wall irregularity was noted in the left VA at the C1-2 level, together with atlantoaxial subluxation associated with os odontoideum. Dynamic digital subtraction angiography (DSA) with head rotation demonstrated left VA occlusion at C1-2 in the right rotational flexion position, with distal flow maintained via collateral circulation. The patient was diagnosed with a cerebral embolism due to BHS. Given the recurrent strokes, atlantoaxial fixation was performed, and intraoperative DSA confirmed a cervical alignment preserving VA flow. No recurrence occurred during postoperative follow-up.

LESSONS: BHS should be considered in the differential diagnosis of infarction confined to the posterior circulation, even in older patients with AF. C1-2 posterior fixation effectively prevents recurrent infarction, and intraoperative DSA is useful for determining a cervical alignment that preserves VA blood flow. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26750.

articles.title: CNS metastatic renal cell carcinoma radiologically mimicking nerve sheath tumors: illustrative cases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) shows unpredictable, often delayed metastatic behavior, and CNS involvement carries significant morbidity. Rare metastases to cranial and spinal nerves can masquerade as benign nerve sheath tumors, causing misdiagnosis and treatment delays. Recognizing distinguishing features is essential to guide management.

OBSERVATIONS: The authors present the cases of 3 patients with pathologically confirmed clear cell RCC metastatic to neural structures, presenting 6-9 years after nephrectomy. The sites included the cervical dorsal root ganglion, cerebellomedullary angle involving lower cranial nerves, and cerebellopontine angle mimicking trigeminal schwannoma. Initial MRI showed well-circumscribed, homogeneously enhancing masses with smooth margins and bony remodeling, favoring nerve sheath tumors. Closer review revealed atypical features including arterial spin labeling hyperperfusion, a susceptibility-weighted hemosiderin rim, vasogenic edema, and interval growth. PET/CT and biopsy confirmed metastatic disease. Management was individualized with radiosurgery, resection, and systemic therapy, achieving durable local control.

LESSONS: Patients with prior RCC warrant a high index of suspicion for metastasis even when imaging suggests a benign nerve sheath tumor. Advanced MRI and PET/CT help identify features atypical for schwannoma and locate the safest biopsy site. When feasible, pathological diagnosis should precede definitive local therapy to inform radiosurgical dose, surgical planning, systemic therapy, and prognosis. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26518.

articles.title: Viability of Public Statistics-Based Synthetic Personas in Small-Area Public Health Surveillance: Sociodemographic Benchmark Consistency Study Using Korea Community Health Survey and Korean Statistical Information Service Data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Synthetic population and persona datasets can provide artificial individual-level records without exposing personal data. However, for surveillance use, they must preserve the joint profiles that define vulnerable groups, not only marginal distributions.

OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated whether a public statistics-based Korean synthetic persona dataset is consistent with Korea Community Health Survey (CHS) and Korean Statistical Information Service (KOSIS) benchmarks for auxiliary small-area public health surveillance.

METHODS: We compared 1,000,000 synthetic persona rows with 1,156,122 adult respondents from the 2021-2025 CHS and selected KOSIS municipal indicators. Core variables were age group, sex, marital status, living-alone status, and education; province or municipal area replaced marital status in the regional profiles. Economic activity and occupation were treated as sensitivity domains. We compared marginal and joint distributions using percentage-point differences and total variation distance (TVD) and quantified CHS sampling uncertainty using 500-replicate stratified cluster percentile bootstrap intervals and compared high-dimensional TVD with CHS split-half references. Sparse-cell, KOSIS correlation, and regional composition-standardized analyses assessed robustness and potential downstream use.

RESULTS: Persona rows were close to CHS for sex (TVD<0.001, 95% bootstrap percentile interval 0.000-0.001), province (TVD 0.006, bootstrap percentile interval 0.005-0.006), living-alone status (TVD 0.008, bootstrap percentile interval 0.007-0.009), and age group (TVD 0.013, bootstrap percentile interval 0.012-0.014). Differences were larger for marital status (TVD 0.039, bootstrap percentile interval 0.038-0.040) and education (TVD 0.059, bootstrap percentile interval 0.058-0.061). The national core profile had a TVD of 0.106 (bootstrap percentile interval 0.105-0.107), compared with a CHS split-half median of 0.009 (2.5th-97.5th percentile 0.008-0.011). The municipal profile had an observed TVD of 0.117, a bootstrap mean of 0.122 (95% bootstrap percentile interval 0.120-0.123), and a split-half median of 0.082 (2.5th-97.5th percentile 0.080-0.084). After restriction to CHS cells with n≥100, the municipal TVD decreased to 0.091. At the municipal level, CHS- and persona-composition standardized unmet health care rates differed by a mean of 0.109 percentage points (Pearson r=0.567), but standardization with national profile-specific probabilities did not reproduce observed local CHS rates (Pearson r=0.004 for persona composition). The conditional KOSIS living-alone comparison was modest (Pearson r=0.547).

CONCLUSIONS: The synthetic persona data showed close agreement for several basic demographic margins but less consistent agreement for high-dimensional sociodemographic profiles. They may support composition-based scenario development and dashboard prototyping but should not be used as stand-alone sources for local surveillance or health-outcome inference without additional calibration and validation.

articles.title: Paired vagus nerve stimulation therapy for posterior circulation ischemic strokes: illustrative cases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While the global disability burden due to stroke remains substantial, the emergence of novel neurorestorative therapies offers new opportunities for poststroke recovery. Vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) paired with upper extremity (UE) rehabilitation (paired VNS) is an FDA-approved therapy shown to improve UE impairment and reduce motor deficits in patients with chronic stroke. However, published evidence describing its use in posterior circulation strokes is limited.

OBSERVATIONS: This case series presents 4 patients with persistent UE impairment following posterior fossa strokes who underwent implantation and treatment with paired VNS months to years after their cerebrovascular event. Functional improvements were observed in all cases, including gains in Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity or Wolf Motor Function Test scores. All patients also reported improved functional use of the affected limb during daily activities and improvements in their quality of life.

LESSONS: These cases suggest that paired VNS therapy may support meaningful functional recovery following posterior fossa stroke, even years after the initial event. Improvements were observed in both objective motor outcomes and patient-reported function and quality of life. These observations expand the clinical experience with paired VNS in a stroke subpopulation associated with significant long-term disability, and contribute to addressing a gap in the literature. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26535.

articles.title: Intracranial Aneurysm Complicated by Common Carotid Artery Infarction Following FDS Procedure.
articles.abstract: Flow-diverter stents (FDS) are widely used in the endovascular reconstruction of large, wide-necked intracranial aneurysms; their mechanism of action primarily involves altering the hemodynamics within the aneurysm to promote thrombus formation. They represent a highly promising device for the treatment of intracranial aneurysms. When treating aneurysms located in the anterior circulation, key branches may be covered by the flow-diverter stent. The incidence of occlusion in these branches has been reported in the literature; moreover, even when branch occlusion occurs, associated neurological deficits are extremely rare. However, postoperative occlusion of the common carotid artery following flow-diverter stent placement is also extremely rare in clinical practice. This paper reports a case of a patient who developed left common carotid artery occlusion following the implantation of a fine-mesh stent. One year after the placement of a Surpass Evovle Flow Diverter System fine-mesh stent, the patient presented with symptoms such as impaired limb movement during a follow-up examination. Cranial MRI revealed a left frontoparietal cerebral infarction. Following treatment with enteric-coated aspirin tablets, the patient's symptoms improved, and they were discharged. The aim of this study is to analyze the mechanism of occurrence and the management process by combining intraoperative, postoperative imaging, and follow-up data, while reviewing the relevant literature to explore the risk factors, clinical characteristics, and prevention and treatment strategies for this complication.

articles.title: Intraoral Rhomboid-Designed Philtral Dimpleplasty Combined With the Muscle-Roll Flap Technique: A Clinical Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the surgical technique, efficacy, and complications of intraoral rhombus-designed philtral dimple plasty with muscle-roll flap for cosmetic philtral dimple reconstruction.

METHODS: A retrospective study included 47 women with congenital philtral dimple flattening and hypoplastic philtral ridges. Surgery was performed through a small midline upper labial vestibular incision. Dissection extended to the deep reticular dermis. The superficial orbicularis oris was selectively resected, while part of the deep layer was preserved as a mechanical anchor. After rhombus-shaped aesthetic planning, redundant superficial muscle was rolled bilaterally to reconstruct the philtral ridges. Deep dermis was anchored at multiple points into the deep orbicularis oris, and mucosa was closed in layers. Postoperative static and dynamic lip morphology and complications were recorded; patient satisfaction was assessed on a 4-point scale.

RESULTS: All patients completed long-term follow-up. Stable philtral dimples and natural-looking philtral ridges were achieved in 42 patients (89.4%), with improved upper-lip projection, vermilion eversion, and no dynamic distortion. Mild dimple shallowing occurred in 5 patients (10.6%) without loss of philtral architecture. Two cases had delayed mucosal healing, resolving with local oral care. No cases of severe infection, salivary cyst formation, or persistent lip numbness were observed. Patient satisfaction: 35 patients reported being "very satisfied," 9 "satisfied," and 3 "fair."

CONCLUSIONS: This new technique simultaneously reconstructs the philtral dimple and ridges. The key to success lies in precise identification of the muscular layer, preservation of the deep orbicularis oris anchoring structures, and meticulous handling of the submucosal labial glands.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV-therapeutic study.

articles.title: Revising Terminology and Phenotype Definitions for AI-Based Decision Support in Fluid Therapy: Call for Consensus.
articles.abstract: Intravenous fluid therapy is a cornerstone of optimizing body hydration, circulation, and perfusion, yet its rational implementation is limited by inconsistent clinical terminology. As fluid therapy moves toward AI-empowered clinical decision support systems (AI-CDSS), there is a critical need for high-quality, verified training data. The reliability of these systems is currently threatened by misleading data resulting from ambiguous definitions and the interchangeable use of nonsynonymous terms, such as "dehydration" and "hypovolemia." This multidisciplinary panel-of-experts opinion article intends to start a discussion by identifying the key drawbacks in current terminology and proposes solutions, including a shift toward adequacy-based phenotypes and categorizing blood and water volumes as "insufficient," "optimal," or "excessive" rather than relying on context-sensitive quantitative measures such as "low," "normal," or "high." Illustrative scenarios are used to show how inconsistent terminology and static quantitative labels could mislead an AI-CDSS. The proposed phenotype matrix is designed to provide a structured, systematic description of fluid requirements for specific clinical objectives that can be integrated into clinical algorithms and machine learning databases. An example of a fluid requirement assessment algorithm is used for exploring its applicability in AI training. The proposed terminology and phenotype matrix are provisional: they represent the opinion of a multidisciplinary expert panel and have not undergone formal consensus, clinical validation, or testing within an AI system. Broad consensus-building initiatives will follow.

articles.title: The commercial trade in exotic pets has had little impact on wild populations of reptiles and amphibians.
articles.journal: Conservation biology : the journal of the Society for Conservation Biology
articles.abstract: The commercial trade in exotic pets has raised concerns about population-level impacts from collection in the wild; however, proponents of the trade claim that such concerns are unfounded. To resolve this debate, more information is needed on the volume of the pet trade, the species involved, their conservation status in the wild, and the relative numbers of wild-caught versus captive-bred animals. To examine these issues for reptiles and amphibians, we assembled and analyzed data on >255,000 specimens over a 16-year period from the pricelists of a major commercial supplier in the United States and >85,000 specimens over a 6-year period from suppliers in Europe. A small number of species dominated: 31% of listings included 22 species (14 snakes, four lizards, three frogs, and one turtle were all listed >2000 times). Of the 27 most commonly listed taxa, all were rated by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) as least concern, except for two python species where collection for the pet trade is likely to be a minor threat compared with habitat destruction. The proportion of all listings that were described as captive-bred rather than wild-caught was approximately 34% and increased over time. There was no overlap between species that were in high demand for the pet trade versus for their meat and skins. We concluded that the major risks to reptiles and amphibians from the pet trade do not involve the unsustainable harvest of wild animals, but there are animal welfare issues and threats related to the spread of disease to wild populations and ecological and genetic impacts of released pets. Over the period that we surveyed, the numbers and types of reptiles and amphibians offered for sale by the U.S. and U.K. suppliers were unlikely to have imperiled populations of most species that were traded.

articles.title: Monoclonal Gammopathy of Neurologic Significance: A Practical Framework for Diagnosis and Management.
articles.abstract: Monoclonal gammopathy of neurologic significance (MGNS) refers to peripheral neuropathies that are attributable to a monoclonal immunoglobulin produced by an underlying clonal plasma cell population or B-cell population in the absence of multiple myeloma, amyloid light chain amyloidosis, or polyneuropathy, organomegaly, endocrinopathy, monoclonal protein, skin changes syndrome. Because the prevalence of both monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) and peripheral neuropathy increases with age, their coexistence is frequently incidental. However, population-based studies demonstrate a significantly higher risk of neuropathy among patients with MGUS compared with matched controls. Establishing causality requires careful clinical phenotyping, correlation with electrodiagnostic studies, and systematic exclusion of alternative and potentially life-threatening causes that require urgent intervention. This review presents a practical, stepwise diagnostic and therapeutic framework for MGNS, emphasizing multidisciplinary collaboration between hematology and neurology. The approach is illustrated through two representative clinical scenarios: IgM MGUS with anti-myelin-associated glycoprotein (anti-MAG) neuropathy and non-IgM MGUS with chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) or its variants. Treatment approaches differ fundamentally between these subtypes. B-cell-directed therapy with rituximab is the most commonly used first-line treatment for IgM anti-MAG neuropathy, whereas non-IgM MGNS with CIDP is managed with immunomodulatory strategies including intravenous immunoglobulin, corticosteroids, and plasmapheresis. We also discuss novel therapeutics, including Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors and complement-directed therapies. This framework provides clinicians with a structured approach to assess causal likelihood, stratify patients by neuropathy subtype, and guide evidence-based treatment decisions across the MGNS spectrum.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes of Multidisciplinary Remote Patient Monitoring for Patients With Poorly Controlled Type 2 Diabetes: Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multidisciplinary remote patient monitoring (RPM) programs may support diabetes management by enabling ongoing glucose monitoring and timely treatment adjustments between clinical encounters. Evidence describing real-world implementation of RPM programs for diabetes in high-risk populations remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated clinical outcomes of a multidisciplinary RPM program for patients with uncontrolled type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).

METHODS: Adults with T2DM, hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) >7%, and insulin therapy who enrolled in an RPM program at the University of Mississippi Medical Center between July 2020 and December 2022 were included. Patients received a Bluetooth-enabled glucometer and structured follow-up from nurses and pharmacists operating under a collaborative practice agreement. A propensity score-matched control group receiving usual outpatient care was identified. The primary outcome was the change in HbA1c from baseline to follow-up. Secondary outcomes included acute care use and RPM engagement, including program completion.

RESULTS: Among 109 RPM participants, mean HbA1c decreased from 10.79% (SD 2.35%) to 8.85% (-1.94 percentage points). In the matched cohort of 95 RPM and 95 control patients, HbA1c decreased by 1.97 versus 1.71 percentage points, respectively (between-group difference: -0.27, 95% CI -1.01 to 0.47; P=.48). Among matched RPM participants, program completers (n=19) had greater HbA1c reductions than noncompleters (n=76; -3.41 vs -1.61 percentage points; P=.01). Acute care use occurred in 13.7% of RPM participants versus 24.2% of matched controls; rates were 23.4 versus 24.2 per 100 person-years, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Substantial improvements in glycemic control were observed among patients with uncontrolled T2DM enrolled in a multidisciplinary RPM program. Greater HbA1c reductions were observed among program completers, although this exploratory finding may reflect response-related selection because program completion required achievement of the program's glycemic target. Further study is needed to determine the comparative effectiveness of RPM and strategies to sustain patient engagement.

articles.title: Caregiver Perceptions of Blood Glucose Monitoring in Children and Adolescents Living With Type 1 Diabetes in Kyrgyzstan, Mali, Tanzania, and Peru: Qualitative Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Caregivers play an important role in caring for children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes. Controlling blood glucose levels is an essential part of diabetes management. Previous studies in low- and middle-income countries have found that tools for measuring blood glucose are unavailable and unaffordable. However, very little is known about the perceptions of caregivers in low- and middle-income countries with regard to the important element of self-monitoring of blood glucose in type 1 diabetes and emerging technologies and their suitability for these contexts.

OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to explore caregivers' perceptions of how self-monitoring of blood glucose impacts everyday life. For the purpose of this study, the term "caregiver" refers to either a parent or an adult responsible for assisting with the management of type 1 diabetes in a child/adolescent.

METHODS: This qualitative descriptive study involved 24 interviews with caregivers identified through a mix of purposive and snowball sampling. Interviews were carried out based on common themes from an interview guide. This study was part of a larger study conducted in Kyrgyzstan, Mali, Peru, and Tanzania. Interviews were analyzed using thematic analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 24 interviews were conducted, with over 80% of caregivers being female. The tools used raised issues related to blood glucose meters, such as finger pricks, follow-up, and affordability. Whereas for continuous glucose monitors, issues of acceptability, accessibility, and affordability of these devices were mentioned by the interviewees. Interviewees also highlighted different disruptions to daily life due to type 1 diabetes, such as nutrition, school, and the need to access medical care. Across settings, caregivers described substantial psychological burden linked to repeated finger pricks, financial strain, and challenges managing diabetes during school and nighttime periods.

CONCLUSIONS: Caregivers' perspectives on blood glucose monitoring highlighted the psychological and financial burden that weighs on them. Technological solutions, such as continuous glucose monitors, make it possible to alleviate certain obstacles related to the use of blood glucose meters and strips, but given their high cost, this can increase the financial burden.

articles.title: Association of eHealth Literacy With Cognitive Function, Frailty, and Functional Status in Hospitalized Geriatric Patients: Cross-Sectional Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The rapid growth of digital health technologies has highlighted the importance of eHealth literacy, which is crucial for navigating health information and tools such as telemedicine and eHealth records. However, older adults often have reservations about digital technologies and face barriers due to cognitive, sensory, and motor impairments, which hinder their ability to effectively use digital health applications. Despite its relevance, research on eHealth literacy in older populations is limited, with a particular gap in understanding how self-assessments of eHealth literacy correlate with health characteristics.

OBJECTIVE: The study seeks to explore eHealth literacy among hospitalized geriatric patients in Germany. The main objective is to evaluate the eHealth literacy level within this particular group and identify the clinical and sociodemographic factors that may influence it.

METHODS: Data from this observational study were analyzed to explore characteristics influencing eHealth literacy in hospitalized geriatric patients. The study included patients aged 60 or older in the Department of Geriatric Medicine at Marien Hospital Herne and enrolled in the standardized early rehabilitation pathway. eHealth literacy was measured using the German version of the eHealth Literacy Scale (GR-eHEALS), a self-assessment tool. Sociodemographic and clinical data, including cognitive function (Montreal Cognitive Assessment [MoCA]), frailty (Clinical Frailty Scale [CFS]), and depression (Depression in Old Age Scale [DIA-S]), were collected. Statistical analyses involved descriptive statistics, t tests, chi-square tests, and regression analyses to examine the relationship between eHealth literacy and various factors. Sociodemographic and clinical data, including cognitive function (MoCA), frailty (CFS), and depression (DIA-S), were collected.

RESULTS: A total of 244 participants (aged 60-97, mean 77.2, SD 6.9 years) were included in the analysis. Participants generally reported an eHealth literacy, with higher scores in "information seeking" (mean 3.64, SD 0.84) compared to "information appraisal" (mean 3.32, SD 0.80). Significant differences in eHealth literacy were observed by age, with older participants scoring lower on both subscales. Frailty was significantly associated with critical appraisal of online health information (B=-1.372, 95% CI -2.554 to -0.189), suggesting that individuals who are frail struggle more with evaluating health information. No significant associations were found with other sociodemographic variables, including MoCA scores, education, or gender.

CONCLUSIONS: While the findings suggest a positive self-reported ability to engage with digital health tools, the selective sample and reliance on self-assessment limit the accuracy of these results. It also emphasizes the need for tailored interventions to support older adults in improving their eHealth literacy, particularly those with higher levels of frailty. Further research, including longitudinal studies and objective assessments, is essential to better understand and address the digital health needs of the geriatric population.

articles.title: Living donor-domino liver transplantation for maple syrup urine disease: surgical and metabolic outcomes.
articles.journal: Liver transplantation : official publication of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the International Liver Transplantation Society
articles.abstract: This study evaluates the feasibility and safety of combining living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) with domino liver transplantation (DLT) for maple syrup urine disease (MSUD). MSUD causes neurological impairment due to branched-chain amino acid accumulation (BCAA). Liver transplantation restores metabolic homeostasis via branched-chain ketoacid dehydrogenase (BCKDH) present in the donor graft. MSUD livers can be reused as domino liver grafts (DLG) since enzyme deficiency in DLG is supplied by production in other recipient's tissues. From October 2012 to September 2025 live donors (LD), MSUD patients and DLG recipients were enrolled for DLT and followed for at least 1 year after transplantation. Plasma BCAA levels in MSUD patients at 3 time points (pretransplantation, early [1-90 d], and late [>90-365 d] posttransplantation) were compared with age-matched pediatric controls without metabolic disorders. Surgical and metabolic outcomes were monitored up to 1-year post-transplantation. Among 32 LDLT for MSUD, 27 (84.4%) grafts were reused. Patient/graft survival was 93.8% for MSUD recipients and 96.3%/85.2% for DLG recipients, respectively. Late hepatic artery thrombosis occurred in 3.1% of MSUD patients and 7.4% of DLG recipients. Primary factors for DLG disposal were double arteries and younger MSUD patients, related to small arterial caliber. No increased risk related to DLG donation was demonstrated. Combining LDLT and DLT expands the donor pool for pediatric patients while ensuring safety in MSUD treatment, with microsurgical arterial reconstruction supporting DLG reuse. Higher graft-to-recipient weight ratio (GRWR) was associated with better early metabolic control, but this association was not significant after adjustment for age, suggesting that the apparent contribution of graft size to early metabolic adaptation may be age-related.

articles.title: Renin Kinetics and Hemodynamic Response During Treatment of Vasoplegic Shock With Angiotensin II (TENSINTEST): Protocol for a Multicenter Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Shock is a life-threatening condition that can lead to multiorgan failure and death. Vasopressors are needed for the treatment of vasoplegic (distributive) shock. Angiotensin II (AT II) is a novel vasopressor. Approximately two-thirds of patients respond to AT II, and one-third do not. AT II is part of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS). Renin is the limiting enzyme of the RAAS, and among other mechanisms, its concentration is regulated by AT II concentration through a negative feedback loop. It might be an indicator of response to AT II therapy.

OBJECTIVE: We designed a study with a primary objective of developing and standardizing an AT II stress test, which could help predict the responsiveness to AT II in patients with distributive shock, regardless of its origin.

METHODS: This is an investigator-initiated, multicenter observational clinical study of renin kinetics before and 6 hours after starting an infusion of AT II in patients with vasoplegic shock and adequate fluid resuscitation who are severely ill. Prior to AT II, patients will receive an infusion of norepinephrine base of 0.3 mcg per kilogram per minute or higher, and vasopressin of 0.03 IU per minute according to institutional protocol. Blood samples for serum renin determination will be obtained immediately prior to and after 6 hours of AT II infusion. We hypothesize that patients who demonstrate a negative trend in relative renin ratio (defined as renin plasma concentration at baseline or at 6 hours after treatment with AT II divided by upper normal concentration of plasma renin [50 mU/L]) will have a greater number of 28-day organ failure-free days (days without vasopressors, mechanical ventilation, or renal replacement therapy). The primary analysis will assess the association between early renin reduction and organ failure-free days using an adjusted proportional odds ordinal regression model.

RESULTS: The research was funded in December 2024. After obtaining ethics approval in July 2025, data collection started on August 1, 2025. As of July 2026, a total of 70 patients had been enrolled. Data collection is expected to be completed in 2027, after which the results will be analyzed and published.

CONCLUSIONS: The goal of our study is to determine whether renin 0-6 h kinetics (difference between renin levels before and 6 hours after starting an AT II infusion) are associated with clinical outcomes in patients who require AT II. Our study could contribute to the development of a more individualized approach to vasopressor therapy and avoidance of inappropriate use of AT II in patients who are not responders, allowing earlier discontinuation of AT II and consideration of alternative therapies.

articles.title: Association of Fenofibrate Add-on Therapy with Postoperative Diabetic Retinal Outcomes After Cataract Surgery in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To examine whether preoperative fenofibrate-plus-statin exposure was associated with postoperative diabetic macular edema (DME)-related and proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR)-related composites compared with statin exposure alone.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Adults with type 2 diabetes undergoing cataract surgery who received fenofibrate plus statin therapy were matched 1:1 with those receiving statin therapy alone. The co-primary outcomes were a DME-related composite, defined by a DME diagnosis or intravitreal injection, and a PDR-related composite comprising PDR, panretinal photocoagulation, or vitreous hemorrhage. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) over cumulative 1- to 5-year horizons. Sensitivity analyses evaluated 6-month outcomes, recent preoperative fenofibrate exposure, a laboratory-complete cohort, and Nd:YAG capsulotomy.

RESULTS: Matching yielded 2,521 pairs. After outcome-specific exclusions, the DME-related composite analysis included 2,292 exposed and 2,327 comparator patients. Fenofibrate-plus-statin exposure was associated with a lower hazard of the DME-related composite at every horizon, including 1 year (HR, 0.486 [95% confidence interval [CI], 0.324-0.728], P < 0.001) and 5 years (HR, 0.678 [95% CI, 0.515-0.892], P = 0.005). For the PDR-related composite, the 95% CI excluded 1.0 only at 2 years (HR, 0.605 [95% CI, 0.397-0.922], P = 0.018). Sensitivity analyses using a recent-exposure definition and a laboratory-complete cohort generally supported the DME-related composite finding, whereas Nd:YAG capsulotomy hazards were similar between groups.

CONCLUSION: Preoperative fenofibrate-plus-statin exposure was associated with a lower hazard of the postoperative DME-related composite, while findings for the PDR-related composite were inconclusive. Prospective validation is needed.

articles.title: Effects of advanced practice nurse-driven sedation weaning and early extubation after cardiac surgery amid health care disruption in South Korea.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Association of Nurse Practitioners
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease has reached unprecedented levels, leading to a substantial increases in the number of cardiac surgeries. Despite the life-saving efforts of surgery, complications remain, including pulmonary complications, which can lead to death. To mitigate these complications, early extubation has emerged as an evidence-based practice for patients undergoing cardiac surgery. The physician shortages that occurred after the mass resignation of physician trainees in South Korea disrupted postoperative care provided in intensive care units (ICU) and impeded early extubation. Our institution accordingly expanded the advanced practice nurses' (APNs) scope of practice to include performing extubation when deemed clinically appropriate after cardiac surgery. This practice change led APNs to develop and implement a sedation weaning and early extubation protocol.

PURPOSE: To evaluate the effects of an APN-driven protocol implemented in the cardiac ICU.

METHODOLOGY: This retrospective study compared two group outcomes: preimplementation and postimplementation groups.

RESULTS: This study revealed differences in health outcomes between the two groups of patients. Beneficial health outcomes were achieved due to this protocol in the opioid use and ventilator time of patients with low grade of heart failure in the postprotocol group, which were 16.7% lesser and 17.0% shorter than those in the preprotocol group.

CONCLUSION: This APN-driven protocol proves its effectiveness without causing compromised health outcomes during a health care crisis in South Korea.

IMPLICATIONS: This protocol incorporating nursing staff autonomy for both sedation and extubation can be implemented and tested for its usefulness for instances where gaps of care occur such as during physician shortages.

articles.title: Non-Prostate Cancer-Related Factors That Influence Serum Prostate-Specific Antigen: A Narrative Review of 45 Non-Malignant PSA Modifiers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To consolidate into a single review more than forty non-cancer-related factors that have been found to elevate or reduce prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels in the peer-reviewed literature, emphasizing their contribution to false-positive and false-negative clinical interpretations.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A narrative literature review was conducted using PubMed, focusing on human studies describing benign physiologic, infectious, inflammatory, iatrogenic, hormonal, pharmacologic, and laboratory-related factors that influence PSA values. The review emphasizes contemporary studies but incorporates earlier foundational literature where relevant.

RESULTS: Forty-five non-cancer-related factors were identified that influence PSA values through biologic, mechanical, pharmacologic, or analytic mechanisms. Thirty factors were associated with transient or persistent PSA elevation, whereas fifteen were associated with PSA reduction. Some factors varied substantially in the strength, magnitude, and consistency of reported PSA effects across studies. PSA elevations were reported in association with prostatic inflammation or infection, urinary retention, ejaculation, non-instrumental prostatic physical stimulation, urologic instrumentation, and systemic inflammatory conditions. PSA reductions were observed with medications including 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, statins, thiazide diuretics, metformin, and certain lifestyle factors. Inter-assay and inter-laboratory variability alone has been reported to result in PSA differences exceeding 20%. Tables summarizing the approximate magnitude and duration of PSA change for each modifier were developed, along with a patient questionnaire intended to support, not replace, clinician judgment.

CONCLUSION: PSA interpretation must incorporate awareness of more than forty influencers that can alter PSA independent of any malignancy. Accounting for these PSA level-altering variables can improve PSA test result specificity and enhance confidence in prostate cancer risk assessment. Use of a structured patient questionnaire, a thorough consideration of benign factors that can alter PSA, repeat testing when transient factors are present, and consistent blood assay methodology can reduce unnecessary imaging, unneeded biopsies, and missed malignancies.

articles.title: Leading at night: The learned role of the nocturnal intensivist adult-gerontology acute care nurse practitioner.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Association of Nurse Practitioners
articles.abstract: Nighttime intensive care unit (ICU) practice requires timely clinical decision making, interdisciplinary coordination, and rapid response to patient deterioration despite reduced access to many daytime resources. Adult-gerontology acute care nurse practitioners (AG-ACNPs) are increasingly integrated into critical care staffing models to provide continuous bedside presence and support high-acuity patient management. This article describes an autonomous nocturnal ICU model in which AG-ACNPs function as primary overnight providers while maintaining physician collaboration and escalation pathways. The model is discussed across medical and cardiovascular ICU settings to highlight differences in patient populations, clinical reasoning, procedural expectations, and specialty-specific competencies. Shared themes include advanced assessment, crisis management, procedural readiness, communication, advocacy, and leadership in resource-limited nighttime environments. The article also examines clinical, operational, and professional implications of AG-ACNP-led nocturnal practice, including the need for structured onboarding, competency validation, mentorship, specialty-specific education, and institutional support. As patient complexity, physician workforce shortages, and ICU demands continue to increase, autonomous AG-ACNP staffing models may help sustain safe, timely, and coordinated critical care delivery overnight. Clear role expectations, collaboration, and ongoing professional development are essential to supporting AG-ACNPs practicing at this level of responsibility.

articles.title: North Carolina nurse practitioner perspectives on physician supervisory requirements: Regulation and reality.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Association of Nurse Practitioners
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nurse practitioners (NPs) improve health care access and provide high-quality care, yet 11 U.S. states continue to require physician supervision. Little is known about how statutory supervision functions in routine practice.

PURPOSE: To describe NPs' experiences with physician supervision in North Carolina and examine associations between supervisory relationship characteristics and perceived benefit of supervision.

METHODOLOGY: A descriptive, correlational survey was conducted among NPs practicing in NC. A researcher-developed electronic survey assessed demographics, supervisory characteristics, and perceptions of physician supervision. Descriptive statistics summarized responses, and chi-square analyses examined associations between supervisory characteristics and perceived supervision benefit.

RESULTS: A total of 1,486 NPs participated. Supervisory relationships varied considerably. Nearly half (44.6%) rarely or never practiced at the same site as their supervising physician, 64.9% never participated in shared patient visits, and 45.2% reported no physician review of plans of care or clinical documentation. Overall, 59.8% disagreed that having a supervising physician was beneficial to practicing effectively. Greater clinical interaction, including shared practice location, real-time consultation, physician review of plans of care, shared patient visits, and shared patient panels, was significantly associated with greater perceived benefit of supervision (all p < .001). More experienced NPs were less likely to perceive supervision as beneficial.

CONCLUSIONS: Statutory physician supervision often occurs with limited direct clinical interaction. Perceived value appears associated with meaningful clinical collaboration rather than supervisory requirements.

IMPLICATIONS: These findings provide empirical evidence to inform policy discussions and suggest models emphasizing collaboration rather than mandatory supervisory agreements may better reflect contemporary NP practice.

articles.title: Protecting the Vulnerable Phase in Newly Diagnosed Heart Failure.
Adverse Event Profiles of Leadless Pacemaker Systems Reported to the FDA MAUDE Database (2021-2026).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leadless pacemakers represent a major advance in cardiac rhythm management. The Micra Transcatheter Pacing System (Medtronic) and Aveir Leadless Pacemaker (Abbott) are distinct leadless pacing platforms with different device architectures and implantation mechanics. The FDA Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience (MAUDE) database provides a real-world source of post-market adverse event reports.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize adverse event profiles of contemporary leadless pacing systems using structured MAUDE data from January 2021 to January 2026, and to assess temporal trends, device problem-patient problem relationships, the timing and reported mechanisms of adverse events and deaths, and generational differences within the Micra platform.

METHODS: Adverse event reports for Micra and Aveir were extracted from the FDA MAUDE database. Records with event dates before January 1, 2021, were excluded. Reports were deduplicated using a structured multi-step process. Analyses were restricted to structured MAUDE fields, including event type, device-problem codes, patient-problem codes, brand name, and dates. Report narratives were additionally analyzed by rule-based text classification with manual validation to clarify ambiguous FDA codes, event timing, and reported mechanisms of death. Each device platform was analyzed independently using descriptive statistics with 95% Wilson confidence intervals.

RESULTS: A total of 14 064 unique reports were included (9973 Micra; 4091 Aveir). Among Micra reports, 7.9% were deaths, 41.1% injuries, and 51.0% malfunctions; high capture threshold (23.7%) was the most frequent device problem, and pericardial effusion (9.0%), cardiac perforation (7.9%), and cardiac tamponade (7.3%) were the leading clinical patient problems. Among Aveir reports, 4.3% were deaths, 32.4% injuries, and 63.3% malfunctions. The leading Aveir device problems were stretching/deformation of the fixation helix (FDA code "Stretched"; 18.3%)-97.7% intra-procedural and 87.2% without clinical consequence-and device dislodgement (18.0%). The code "Embolism/Embolus" (14.0%) denoted device embolization in 97.5% of Aveir reports and was more frequent for the atrial than the ventricular device (20.6% vs. 13.2%, p < 0.001), without decline over time. No clinical signs or symptoms were reported in 64.2% of Micra and 58.5% of Aveir reports. Events were intra-procedural in 45.3% of Micra and 66.4% of Aveir reports, and perforation/effusion/tamponade was the leading reported mechanism of death (51.4% and 67.2%, respectively). Newer-generation Micra devices showed lower reported death proportions than earlier models.

CONCLUSIONS: Leadless pacemaker systems show distinct reported adverse event patterns in real-world post-market surveillance. Micra was characterized mainly by perforation-related complications, whereas Aveir was characterized by fixation-helix damage, dislodgement with device embolization-particularly of the atrial device-and separation-related events. For operators, these findings underscore the importance of device-specific implantation technique, procedural experience, and ongoing learning curve effects in leadless pacing.

articles.title: A Diagnostic Pitfall on 18F-FDG PET/CT: Transient Vertebral FDG Uptake During Immunotherapy.
articles.abstract: An 80-year-old man with poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma underwent 18F-FDG PET/CT for initial staging and treatment response assessment following pembrolizumab therapy. Follow-up PET/CT demonstrated a new FDG-avid focus within the T3 vertebral body without a corresponding CT abnormality. Subsequent contrast-enhanced MRI revealed no structural correlate at the site of uptake. A repeat PET/CT performed 3 months later showed complete resolution of the vertebral lesion without additional treatment. The imaging findings favored transient immune-related inflammatory uptake or a pseudoprogression-like phenomenon rather than true osseous metastasis.

articles.title: Sustained 177Lu-FAPI-2286 Retention in Graves' Orbitopathy.
articles.abstract: A 39-year-old man suffering from Graves' ophthalmopathy, which was resistant to steroids (with a clinical activity score of 5/7 and a moderate-severe EUGOGO grade), had a 68Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT scan. This scan showed strong bilateral FAPI activity in the extraocular muscles, especially in the inferior recti, even though his visual acuity remained normal. A later low-dose 177Lu-FAPI-2286 retention study confirmed that the radiotracer stayed selectively within the recti. This example suggests that fibroblast activation protein-targeted theranostics could be a new way to image and possibly treat Graves' orbitopathy.

articles.title: Reverse PSMA Theranostic Discordance: Reproducible ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 Uptake in Skeletal Metastases Inconspicuous on Serial ¹⁸F-PSMA-1007 PET/CT.
articles.abstract: 18F-PSMA-1007 PET/CT is widely used for selecting patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) for 177Lu-PSMA radioligand therapy. We present a striking case in which multiple skeletal metastases demonstrated intense, reproducible ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 uptake on post-therapy scintigraphy across all three treatment cycles, yet remained occult or only minimally avid on serial ¹⁸F-PSMA-1007 PET/CT. SPECT/CT confirmed anatomic lesion localization, excluding artifact. This case of "reverse theranostic discordance" challenges the assumption that diagnostic PSMA PET faithfully represents the full target landscape for radioligand therapy. Systematic SPECT/CT review after treatment cycles may reveal therapeutically relevant disease invisible to pretherapy PET.

articles.title: Explainable machine learning reveals topological control of vacancy energetics in 2D carbon.
articles.abstract: Vacancy defects strongly influence the structural and energetic behavior of two-dimensional carbon materials, yet their energetic description remains challenging due to the interplay between local reconstruction and network topology. In this work, we combine atomistic simulations, topological descriptors, and machine learning to investigate vacancy energetics in graphene and phagraphene. A dataset of defective structures was generated across vacancy concentrations from 2% to 24% and characterized using physically grounded descriptors, including ring statistics. Increasing vacancy concentration induces a progressive reorganization of the carbon network, with a reduction of hexagonal rings and the emergence of non-hexagonal motifs. This effect is more pronounced in graphene, while phagraphene exhibits a more distributed response due to its intrinsic topological diversity. Machine learning models achieve high predictive accuracy, with graphene displaying a structured and near-linear descriptor-energy relationship, whereas phagraphene requires more flexible models. SHAP analysis identifies the vacancy count as the dominant contributor to the predictions, with ring-based topology acting as a secondary but systematic correction. A reduced model based on nvac and the topological descriptor (R5 - R6) captures the main energetic trends, and the comparison between graphene and phagraphene shows that the weight of this topological correction depends strongly on the underlying lattice. These results establish a direct link between topology, structural disorder, and vacancy energetics in two-dimensional carbon systems.

articles.title: Renal Metastasis From Follicular Thyroid Carcinoma: Concordant FDG and Radioiodine Avidity.
articles.abstract: A 54-year-old man with back pain showed lytic vertebral lesions on MRI. 18F-FDG PET/CT revealed an FDG-avid thyroid primary, skeletal metastases, and a relatively low FDG-avid right renal lesion. Thyroid histopathology confirmed follicular carcinoma. Post-thyroidectomy radioiodine scan demonstrated intense uptake in both skeletal and renal lesions. Biopsy from the renal lesion confirmed renal metastasis. Renal involvement in differentiated thyroid cancer is rare and may demonstrate concordant FDG and radioiodine avidity.

articles.title: Deep Sedation in Single-Shot Pulmonary Vein Isolation: A Head-to-Head Look at Two Pulsed Field Versus Cryoballoon Ablation Approaches.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Deep sedation (DS) is routinely used during single-shot pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) to optimize patient comfort and procedural stability. However, data on sedative requirements and procedural tolerance of pulsed field ablation (PFA) under DS compared with thermal technologies remain limited.

METHODS: In this single-center study, consecutive patients underwent PVI with cryoballoon (CB), PFA using a pentaspline catheter (PC) or the balloon-in-basket catheter (BC). All procedures were performed under DS with midazolam, fentanyl, and propofol, administered by electrophysiology staff without anaesthesiologist supervision. Propensity score matching (1:1:1) was applied for age, sex, body mass index, and hypertension. Procedural characteristics, sedative/analgesic requirements, and complications were analyzed.

RESULTS: Acute PVI without major complications was achieved in all 156 enrolled patients. PC procedures were associated with higher body-weight- and time-adjusted requirements for propofol (CB: 0.10 ± 0.04 mg/kg/min; PC: 0.15 ± 0.04 mg/kg/min; BC: 0.11 ± 0.03 mg/kg/min; p < 0.001) despite the lowest total dose of propofol used (CB: 440 ± 144 mg; PC: 348± 80 mg; BC: 433 ± 160 mg; p = 0.00). Procedural times (CB: 47.5 [40-60] min, PC: 29 [25-35] min, BC: 47.5 [40-56] min, p < 0.001) and fluoroscopy times (CB: 9.5 [6.3-13.6] min; PC: 6.2 [4.4-9] min; BC: 7.2 [6.1-11.2] min, p = 0.001) were shortest in the PC group. Sedation-related hemodynamic stability was comparable across all cohorts.

CONCLUSIONS: The novel BC demonstrated excellent feasibility under DS, with reduced normalized sedative requirements compared with the PC and a safety profile comparable to CB ablation. These findings suggest that optimized waveform design and field homogeneity may enable safe and comfortable PVI under DS without the need for general anesthesia.

articles.title: Intrathyroidal Parathyroid Adenoma Mimicking a Thyroid Nodule on Ultrasound: Localized by 18F-Choline PET/CT.
articles.abstract: We report the 18F-Choline PET/CT findings of an intrathyroidal parathyroid adenoma (IPA) in a 30-year-old woman with primary hyperparathyroidism. Cervical ultrasound showed no parathyroid abnormality but revealed a hypoechoic nodule within the left thyroid lobe, initially misdiagnosed as a thyroid nodule. 18F-Choline PET/CT demonstrated intense focal uptake in the lesion, precisely localized to the intrathyroidal region. Postoperative pathology confirmed an IPA. This case highlights the value of 18F-Choline PET/CT in accurately localizing an IPA misdiagnosed as a thyroid nodule on ultrasound, thereby avoiding unnecessary fine-needle aspiration and thyroid surgery.

articles.title: 68Ga‑PSMA PET/CT Facilitates Identification of a Rare Rectal Metastasis From Prostate Cancer.
articles.abstract: An 86-year-old man underwent radical prostatectomy for prostate adenocarcinoma (T3aN0M0) 5 years ago. He presented with recurrent constipation for 5 months. Pelvic MRI raised suspicion of rectal cancer. Serum prostate specific antigen (PSA) was mildly elevated (9.610 ng/mL). PET/CT revealed thickened rectal walls with no significant hypermetabolism on 18F‑FDG imaging, but marked radiotracer uptake on 68Ga‑PSMA imaging (SUVmax = 22.4). Final pathology confirmed metastatic prostate cancer to the rectum. For patients with a history of prostate cancer presenting with rectal occupying lesions, metastatic disease should be included in the differential diagnosis.

articles.title: 18F-FAPI PET/CT and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance for Cardiac Fibrotic Process in End-stage Renal Disease: A Pilot Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: End-stage renal disease (ESRD) increases the risk of myocardial fibrosis. This study aimed to detect cardiac fibroblast activation and fibrosis in ESRD using 18F-labeled fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET/CT and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR).

PATIENTS AND METHODS: This prospective clinical trial (NCT07107919) enrolled 33 ESRD patients who underwent 18F-FAPI PET/CT, with 19 patients undergoing CMR. Myocardial FAPI activity was quantified. Cardiac function [left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF), left atrial ejection fraction (LAEF)] and tissue parameters [native T1, extracellular volume (ECV), late gadolinium enhancement (LGE)] were assessed by CMR. Spearman correlation analysis assessed correlations between 18F-FAPI uptake and CMR parameters.

RESULTS: A total of 75.76% (25/33) of ESRD patients showed myocardial FAPI uptake, significantly higher than the controls (P < 0.05). 18F-FAPI-42 PET identified more segments with evidence of fibroblast activation than CMR-late gadolinium enhancement detected fibrosis (82 vs. 71). Compared with FAPI-negative patients, FAPI-positive patients had increased native-T1, decreased LVEF, LAEF and RVEF (P < 0.05). FAPI-positive segments showed higher native-T1 and extracellular volume % than FAPI-negative segments (P < 0.05). FAPI activity correlated with LVEF, RVEF, LAEF and native-T1. Higher myocardial FAPI uptake was associated with lower LVEF and longer dialysis duration.

CONCLUSIONS: 18F-FAPI PET enables in vivo detection of cardiac fibroblast activation in ESRD and correlates with functional and tissue parameters by CMR. FAPI uptake may serve as an imaging biomarker for cardiac remodeling. Further studies are warranted to clarify the role of 18F-FAPI PET in evaluating the efficacy of anti-fibrotic treatment and in assisting cardiac risk stratification in ESRD patients.

articles.title: Dual-tracer 18F-FDG and 18F-PSMA PET/CT Findings in Metastatic Scrotal Extramammary Paget Disease Initially Suspected as Prostate Cancer.
articles.abstract: We present dual-tracer 18F-FDG and 18F-PSMA (prostate-specific membrane antigen) PET/CT findings in a 75-year-old man with prior scrotal extramammary Paget disease who developed diffuse bone and lymph node lesions. L1 vertebral biopsy initially favored metastatic prostatic acinar adenocarcinoma, but serum prostate-specific antigen was 0.567 ng/mL and prostate biopsies were benign. PET/CT showed intense FDG and PSMA uptake in widespread osseous and nodal lesions, whereas the prostate showed no focal FDG uptake or abnormal PSMA uptake. This discordant imaging pattern, together with clinical and pathologic correlation, supported metastatic scrotal extramammary Paget disease rather than prostate cancer.

articles.title: Cross-platform Comparison of Quantitative Florbetapir Amyloid PET Using MIMneuro and Neurophet SCALE PET.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quantitative amyloid PET is increasingly used in clinical practice, but the interchangeability of quantification software remains uncertain. We compared quantitative amyloid PET measurements, diagnostic performance, and platform-specific thresholds between two FDA-cleared software packages, MIMneuro and Neurophet SCALE PET, using clinical Florbetapir 18F-PET/CT.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 95 consecutive patients who underwent Florbetapir 18F-PET/CT were independently analyzed using MIMneuro and Neurophet SCALE PET. Quantitative measures included standardized uptake value ratios (SUVRs) and global Centiloid values. Cross-platform agreement was evaluated using Pearson correlation, Bland-Altman analysis, and Cohen κ statistics. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was used to determine platform-specific thresholds for predicting visual amyloid positivity.

RESULTS: Regional SUVRs showed moderate correlations (r = 0.414 to 0.674; all P < 0.001), with the strongest correlation observed for global Centiloid values (r = 0.684). Neurophet yielded significantly higher global SUVR values than MIMneuro (mean bias, -0.20; P < 0.001), whereas the difference in Centiloid values was not significant. The optimal thresholds for predicting visual amyloid positivity were 1.10 versus 1.40 for global SUVR and 20.7 versus 34.4 for global Centiloids for MIMneuro and Neurophet, respectively. Cross-platform agreement was moderate using SUVR (κ = 0.42) and improved with Centiloids (κ = 0.60).

CONCLUSIONS: Although MIMneuro and Neurophet SCALE PET showed moderate agreement, their quantitative measurements were not directly interchangeable at clinically relevant thresholds. These findings suggest that platform-specific quantitative thresholds may be needed when amyloid PET is used for clinical interpretation, longitudinal follow-up, or selection of patients for antiamyloid therapy.

articles.title: Intense 18F-FDG Uptake in Isolated Splenic Rosai-Dorfman Disease.
articles.abstract: A 66-year-old woman with left upper abdominal pain had a solitary splenic mass nearly inconspicuous on unenhanced CT but progressively enhancing, although hypoattenuating relative to adjacent splenic parenchyma, on contrast-enhanced CT. 18F-FDG PET/CT showed intense uptake (SUVmax, 15.1) without additional suspicious hypermetabolic foci within the imaged field of view. CT suggested a potentially malignant splenic neoplasm, with lymphoma among the preoperative considerations. Splenectomy confirmed Rosai-Dorfman disease. No recurrence was identified on CT at 10 months. This case illustrates the broad differential diagnosis of solitary FDG-avid splenic masses.

articles.title: Clinically Occult Cecal Metastasis From Prostate Adenocarcinoma Detected by 18F-PSMA Positron Emission Tomography at Biochemical Recurrence: A Rare Finding.
articles.abstract: We present a patient with biochemical recurrence after salvage radiation and combined androgen deprivation therapy with abiraterone who underwent 18F-PSMA PET/CT for a rapidly rising prostate-specific antigen (PSA). The scan revealed an intense prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-avid focus in the cecum without an apparent CT correlate. Colonoscopy identified a smooth, 2 cm nonobstructing cecal mass, and biopsy confirmed metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma by morphology and immunohistochemistry. This case demonstrates 18F-PSMA PET/CT detection at a low PSA level of a clinically occult metastatic lesion involving the cecum, an exceptionally rare site for prostate cancer spread. Colonoscopy and biopsy confirmation of atypical PSMA-avid gastrointestinal lesions remain essential, as physiologic colonic uptake, PSMA-avid diverticula, and PSMA-expressing primary colorectal cancers are well-documented mimickers.

articles.title: Postrenal Acute Kidney Injury After Forced Diuresis During 68Ga-PSMA PET/CT.
articles.abstract: For active surveillance assessment, 68Ga-PSMA PET/CT was performed in a 73-year-old man with Gleason 3+3 prostate adenocarcinoma. PET/CT showed a markedly enlarged prostate indenting the bladder base, with focal midline activity suggestive of prostatic urethral urinary retention. Intravenous furosemide was administered before 120-minute delayed imaging, which showed complete resolution of the activity and excluded pathologic uptake. After discharge, he developed urinary urgency and incomplete emptying, progressing to lower abdominal and pelvic pain with elevated creatinine. Postrenal acute kidney injury from acute urinary retention was diagnosed. Catheterization and inpatient monitoring normalized renal function, highlighting an underrecognized risk of forced diuresis.

articles.title: Clarification of FAPI PET Response Classification According to PERCIST.
Physics-Informed Implicit Neural Representations in Biomedical Tomography: Principles, Applications, and Reliability.
articles.abstract: Biomedical tomography reconstructs spatially and temporally varying images or biophysical fields from indirect measurements governed by acquisition physics. Physics-informed implicit neural representations (INRs) parameterize these unknowns as coordinate-conditioned neural fields, optionally incorporating physical states, and estimate their parameters through measurement consistency. Despite growing adoption, the specific contributions of INRs are often conflated with those of forward modeling, continuous representation, and neural priors, obscuring when they offer substantive advantages. This review adopts a representation-physics-inference perspective to clarify the role of INRs relative to conventional voxel, basis, and other neural parameterizations. We examine how coordinate and state conditioning provide a direct interface to the forward model, while shared network parameters couple reconstruction updates across queried locations and states. Starting from scan-specific INR reconstruction, we identify three limitations: insufficient measurement information, modeling uncertainty, and the computational burden. Corresponding advances are organized into prior-enhanced reconstruction, joint estimation of target fields and physical variables, and scalable or amortized inference. Using representative examples from CT, MRI, ultrasound, photoacoustic imaging, PET, and optical tomography, we assess how these strategies affect reconstruction bias, identifiability, quantitative reliability, and computational efficiency. We distinguish essential, enabling, or merely incidental INR roles according to their coupling with acquisition physics. This perspective clarifies the opportunities and limitations of physics-informed INRs and identifies forward-model fidelity, solution identifiability, scalable inference, and independent quantitative and clinical validation as development priorities.

articles.title: Reimagining Dental Education: Consensus Recommendations for Innovation, Technology Integration, and Practice Transformation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: With advances in technology, artificial intelligence (AI), and evolving practice landscapes, dental schools are at a critical juncture to develop the next generation of technology-adept and practice-ready oral health professionals. Major challenges include limited technology literacy and integration, and the need to prepare new graduates to thrive within a rapidly evolving practice environment.

OBJECTIVE: To develop consensus recommendations on how dental education can integrate technology and innovation, and prepare the next generation to be practice ready in a myriad of practice settings.

CONSENSUS PROCESS: At the 2026 Reimagining Dental Education Summit held at Harvard University, eight academic and organization leaders, including two working group Co-Chairs and a Summit Scholar, reviewed evidence and participated in three future-back facilitated discussion sessions. Consensus required unanimous agreement by all working group members and recommendations were proposed and refined through a final report-out process.

RECOMMENDATIONS: To address technology and AI implementation, the working group recommended: (1) creation of an AI and technology curriculum across all levels of dental education, (2) creation of a dedicated leadership role to develop integration strategies for AI and emerging technologies, and (3) deployment of AI to improve institutional effectiveness, faculty calibration, patient care, and student learning. To address practice readiness, the working group recommended: (1) development of pathways to reduce time toward obtaining a dental degree, (2) creation of pathways to enhance practice readiness through external clinical experiences, (3) creation of additional postgraduate residency opportunities with incentives.

CONCLUSIONS: Dental education is positioned to further prepare graduates to embrace evolving practice realities through a solutions-oriented skill set that includes AI-literacy, innovation, integration of emerging technologies, and real-world clinical experience. Coordinated action across institutions and sectors is essential to translating these recommendations into practice and to make a meaningful impact on society.

articles.title: Polygenic Risk Scores for Kidney Function Decline in Japanese Population-Based Cohorts: A Validation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Large-scale genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified hundreds of genetic loci associated with kidney function. However, most polygenic risk score models for kidney function were developed in European populations, limiting their accuracy in non-European groups. This study aimed to validate the clinical utility of polygenic risk scores for kidney function decline in the Japanese general population.

METHODS: We analyzed the Shika resident cohort cross-sectional and the Toshiba worker cohort prospectively to construct polygenic risk score models based on GWAS data from Japanese populations incorporating 344,577 and 352,151 genetic variants, respectively. The primary outcome was kidney function decline, defined as eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2. With adjustments for traditional risk factors, multivariate logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess associations between the polygenic risk score and kidney function decline.

RESULTS: In the Shika resident cohort (n = 895, mean age 62 years), 157 participants (18%) had eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2; each standard deviation (SD) increase in the polygenic risk score conferred 55% higher odds (OR 1.55, 95% CI 1.28-1.89). In the Toshiba worker cohort (n = 6,769, mean age 40 years), 1,593 participants (24%) developed eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2 over median 8.3-year follow-up; each SD increase in the polygenic risk score was associated with 16% higher risk (HR 1.16, 95% CI 1.10-1.22). Adding the polygenic risk score to clinical models was associated with improved integrated discrimination in both cohorts, but the overall improvement in predictive ability was limited.

CONCLUSIONS: The polygenic risk score was independently associated with kidney function decline beyond established risk factors and was associated with modestly improved risk prediction accuracy in Japanese populations, supporting its potential utility for personalized chronic kidney disease management.

articles.title: Reducing Low-Value Care Through the Smarter Care Virginia Initiative.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Low-value care costs more than $100 billion annually and remains pervasive despite decades of evidence documenting its clinical and financial harms. While several US states have begun discouraging its use, the feasibility of such statewide interventions in partnership with large health systems remains unknown.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effectiveness of a clinician-led, multistakeholder, statewide initiative to reduce low-value care in the Commonwealth of Virginia.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This quality improvement study used a difference-in-differences analyses comparing low-value service changes among patients attributed to 6 health systems vs 12 control systems in the Commonwealth of Virginia preintervention (January 1 to December 31, 2019) vs postintervention (January 1 to December 31, 2022). Any patient eligible to receive 1 or more of the 9 measured low-value services in the 18 health systems evaluated were included. Data were analyzed between December 1, 2023, and September 1, 2026.

EXPOSURE: The intervention, Smarter Care Virginia, included health system financial support, clinician education, and quarterly peer-comparison performance scorecards.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the percentage of patients receiving any of 9 selected low-value services: (1-3) preoperative laboratory, imaging, and cardiac testing; (4-5) electrocardiogram/cardiac screening and cardiac stress testing; (6-7) diagnostic imaging and opioids for acute back pain; (8) advanced diagnostic eye imaging; and (9) peripherally inserted central catheter lines for patients with chronic kidney disease. Secondary outcomes included adverse events (eg, myocardial infarction-related hospitalization) and per-capita spending on the 9 low-value services.

RESULTS: A total of 17 223 clinicians (7222 in the intervention group and 10 001 in the control group) and 4.5 million patients (approximately 68% of Virginia's adult population) were identified. In 2019, 10.5% of patients in the intervention group and 10.7% of patients in the control group received 1 or more low-value services; in 2021 to 2022, rates declined to 8.5% and 9.1%, respectively. The intervention was associated with 10.4% fewer patients receiving 1 or more low-value services (absolute reduction, -1.1 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.1 to -0.1 percentage points; P = .04). There was no statistically significant change in adverse events (0.03%; 95% CI, -0.02% to 0.03%; P = .84) or spending on the 9 low-value services ($0.33; 95% CI, -$3.43 to $4.11).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this quality improvement study, a statewide, clinician-led initiative was associated with a small but statistically significant reduction in low-value care delivery without evidence of harm. Achieving larger reductions may require combining such health system-driven efforts with additional strategies, such as payment reform and physician and hospital accountability, that discourage the use of low-value care.

articles.title: Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index is Associated with Renal Interstitial Inflammation and Renal Outcomes in Patients Undergoing Native Kidney Biopsy.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) is an established index for assessing nutritional risk and is associated with adverse outcomes in chronic kidney disease; however, its relationship with renal histopathological findings remains unclear. We investigated the associations of GNRI with renal pathological findings and renal outcomes in patients undergoing native kidney biopsy.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study was a secondary analysis of a previously established cohort of 503 native kidney biopsy patients with evaluable renal medullary tissue. After excluding patients with nephrotic-range proteinuria, tubulointerstitial nephritis, antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis, anti-glomerular basement membrane disease, and polyarteritis nodosa, 308 patients were analyzed. Patients were stratified by median GNRI, and the primary outcome was a composite of a ≥40% decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate or initiation of renal replacement therapy. Associations were evaluated using multivariable linear regression and Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 2.4 years, 62 patients (20.1%) reached the renal outcome. Lower GNRI was independently associated with older age, greater proteinuria, and greater cortical interstitial inflammatory cell infiltration, but not with cortical interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy (IFTA). In addition, lower GNRI was independently associated with adverse renal outcomes (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 1.90; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.10-3.29), and the association persisted after adjustment for cortical IFTA (HR, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.08-3.23). Addition of GNRI improved C-index from 0.673 to 0.698 and significantly improved model fit beyond established clinical factors and cortical IFTA (likelihood ratio test, P = 0.024).

CONCLUSION: In patients undergoing kidney biopsy, lower GNRI was associated with renal interstitial inflammation rather than chronic fibrosis and was independently associated with adverse renal outcomes.

articles.title: GLP-1/Glucagon Receptor Dual Agonists for Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis and Steatotic Liver Disease (MASH/MASLD): A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a progressive liver disease with high unmet therapeutic need. GLP-1/glucagon dual receptor agonists are an emerging drug class, but no meta-analysis has evaluated it exclusively.

METHODS: In this registered systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD420261325731), we searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, and Google Scholar through January 2026 for placebo-controlled randomized trials of GLP-1/glucagon dual agonists in adults with MASH or MASLD. Four trials (survodutide, pemvidutide, cotadutide; n=673) were pooled with DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models; Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment was a sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: Dual agonists increased MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis (RR 2.98, 95% CI 2.09-4.24; k=2). A borderline, exploratory signal for fibrosis improvement was observed (RR 1.38, 95% CI 1.01-1.88; p=0.044; k=2); neither trial was individually significant. Relative liver fat fell by 46.24% (95% CI -55.24 to -37.24), and ≥30% liver fat reduction was more frequent (RR 4.39, 95% CI 2.97-6.49). ALT (MD -20.38 IU/L, 95% CI -33.00 to -7.75), AST (MD -18.80 IU/L), body weight (MD -4.36%) and systolic blood pressure (MD -5.22 mmHg) decreased; the ELF reduction was not retained in sensitivity analyses. Nausea (RR 2.90), vomiting (RR 9.58) and diarrhea (RR 1.90) were more frequent; serious adverse events were not (RR 1.06). Split-placebo analyses were consistent.

CONCLUSIONS: Dual agonists were associated with a higher likelihood of MASH resolution, a borderline exploratory fibrosis signal, and reductions in liver fat, liver enzymes, weight and systolic blood pressure, with more gastrointestinal adverse events. These early-phase findings support continued Phase 3 evaluation.

articles.title: Myocardial Responses to Eplontersen in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: The CARDIO-TTRansform CMR study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transthyretin-lowering therapies target the underlying cause of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), but their effects on myocardial amyloid burden and cardiac remodelling remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated the myocardial effects of sustained transthyretin suppression with eplontersen using serial multiparametric cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR).

METHODS: This CMR study was a pre-specified, international, prospective study embedded within the randomized, placebo-controlled phase 3 CARDIO-TTRansform trial. Participants underwent CMR at baseline and planned assessments at weeks 25, 49, 97, and 140. The primary imaging analysis evaluated longitudinal changes in CMR parameters using mixed models for repeated measures. Myocardial amyloid regression and progression were defined as ≥5 percentage-point decreases and increases in extracellular volume (ECV), respectively. All other patients were considered stable.

RESULTS: We enrolled 120 participants with baseline and ≥1 follow-up CMR assessment (eplontersen, n=58; placebo, n=62; mean age, 76.7±6.5 years; 95% male; baseline stabilizer, 12.5%). At week 140 eplontersen resulted in lower ECV, compared with placebo (least-squares mean difference [95% CI], -6.7 percentage points [ -8.7 to -4.7]; P<0.001) and lower native T1 ( -25.9ms [-41.7 to -10.2 ]; P=0.002) and left ventricular mass (-19.1g [-28.0 to -10.2]; P<0.001). Eplontersen also increased left ventricular ejection fraction (+5.1% [1.8-8.3]; P=0.002), right ventricular ejection fraction (+4.6% [0.6-8.7]; P=0.03), and left ventricular global longitudinal, circumferential, and radial strain and right ventricular longitudinal strain (all P<0.05), compared to placebo. At week-140, myocardial amyloid regression occurred in 12.5% receiving eplontersen versus 0% receiving placebo, whereas progression occurred in 12.5% versus 76%, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Sustained transthyretin suppression with eplontersen resulted in substantially lower myocardial ECV and favorable changes in cardiac structure, biventricular systolic function, and myocardial deformation compared with placebo in a cohort of patients mostly not on background stabilizer at baseline. These findings provide randomized evidence that lowering circulating transthyretin modifies myocardial disease progression in ATTR-CM and support serial multiparametric CMR for characterizing myocardial treatment response.

articles.title: From Glycemic Control to Obesity Management: A 20-year Systematic Evidence Map of GLP-1 Trials and Their Relevance to Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based therapeutics have evolved from glucose-lowering agents into a major component of obesity care, with increasing relevance to metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS). However, the long-term evolution of the randomized trial ecosystem across the full incretin-agonist spectrum has not been systematically mapped. We conducted a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review, evidence map, and bibliometric analysis of randomized controlled trials evaluating GLP-1-based therapeutics, including selective GLP-1 receptor agonists and GLP-1-based co-/tri-agonists. ClinicalTrials.gov, PubMed/MEDLINE, and Scopus were searched for trials registered and/or published between July 1, 2005, and June 30, 2025.
