After deduplication and eligibility assessment, 517 unique randomized trials were included. Trial activity was more than threefold higher in the recent era, with 393 trials (76.0%) initiated during 2016-June 2025 compared with 124 trials (24.0%) during July 2005-2015. Early development was predominantly diabetes-centered, whereas the later era showed marked expansion into obesity and weight-management, cardiovascular and cardiorenal outcomes, and other emerging indications. Across the mapped corpus, later-phase and larger-enrollment studies became increasingly prominent, reflecting maturation into broader and more pragmatic cardiometabolic development programs. Bibliometric patterns paralleled these shifts, showing a mature diabetes-centered literature and a rapidly expanding obesity evidence community. Over two decades, GLP-1-based therapeutics have transitioned into a broad obesity and cardiometabolic trial ecosystem. These trends are increasingly relevant to bariatric surgeons, particularly in relation to preoperative optimization, postoperative adjunctive therapy, and recurrent weight gain after MBS, and highlight the need for more durable, comparative, and post-bariatric randomized trials.

articles.title: Investigating the Effect of Synbiotic Supplementation on Inflammatory Indices in Critically Ill Septic Children: a Triple Blind Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is a major global health challenge associated with high mortality and long-term disabilities, with gut microbiota playing an important role in its pathophysiology. Probiotics and synbiotics may help restore microbial balance and modulate the inflammatory response. This study aimed to assess whether synbiotic supplementation could reduce inflammatory biomarkers and improve clinical outcomes in children with sepsis admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit compared with placebo. Fifty-four patients with sepsis were randomly assigned to receive either a synbiotic supplement (KidiLact) or a placebo. Participants consumed two sachets daily for 4-7 days. The study evaluated inflammatory markers, including interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), C-reactive protein (CRP), and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), as well as clinical outcomes and mortality. After the intervention, the synbiotic group had significantly lower CRP (p = 0.004), IL-6 (p < 0.001), and TNF-α (p < 0.001) levels than the placebo group. IL-6 and TNF-α decreased by 92.57% and 39.63%, respectively, in the synbiotic group, with statistically significant differences compared with placebo (IL-6: p < 0.001; TNF-α: p < 0.001). No statistically significant differences were observed between groups in clinical outcomes, including length of hospitalization, duration of PICU stay, duration of mechanical ventilation, duration of antibiotic therapy, or mortality. Daily administration of two sachets of the synbiotic supplement for 4-7 days may improve inflammatory biomarkers in children with sepsis admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit. However, no statistically significant differences in clinical outcomes or mortality were detected. Larger and adequately powered studies are needed to determine whether synbiotic supplementation improves clinical outcomes in this population. IRCT, IRCT20230523058266N1 Registered 30 October 2023, https://irct.behdasht.gov.ir/trial/71397 .

articles.title: SGLT2 Inhibitors in Anthracycline-Related Cardiac Dysfunction: Critical Evidence Appraisal and State-Specific Pharmacotherapeutic Positioning.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) improve cardiorenal outcomes, but their role in anthracycline-related cardiac dysfunction (ARCD) beyond established indications is uncertain. We appraised mechanistic and clinical evidence across pre-exposure prophylaxis (State A); an isolated surveillance abnormality or mild asymptomatic cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD), both with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (State B); and symptomatic CTRCD/heart failure irrespective of ejection fraction or asymptomatic moderate/severe CTRCD (State C).

METHODS: This critical narrative review used structured searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Europe PMC, Web of Science Core Collection, and ClinicalTrials.gov, supplemented by an Embase search during revision. Peer-reviewed literature through 15 August 2026 and registry status through 22 August 2026 were assessed by clinical state, evidentiary directness, endpoint relevance, and validity threats.

RESULTS: Human evidence was predominantly retrospective, and SGLT2i use usually reflected conventional indications. Small prospective nonrandomized studies focused on imaging or biomarkers. Favorable associations remain vulnerable to residual confounding, treatment selection, competing cancer mortality, exposure-timing bias, and source-cohort overlap. No peer-reviewed randomized between-group efficacy report was available by the literature cutoff. Experimental studies support biological plausibility but not direct myocardial target engagement, a uniform class effect, preserved anticancer activity, or clinical benefit.

CONCLUSION: State C warrants phenotype-appropriate guideline-based care, including SGLT2i when indicated; an incremental ARCD-specific benefit remains unproven. Without another indication, initiation in States A and B remains investigational. HFA-ICOS may guide surveillance and trial enrichment but is not a prescribing trigger.

articles.title: Community-associated clostridioides difficile infection from the One Health Approach perspective.
articles.abstract: Community-associated Clostridioides difficile infection (CA-CDI) has been defined as the presence of CDI on an outpatient basis or within 48 h of hospitalization in a patient not having been discharged from a healthcare facility during the previous 12 weeks. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the prevalence of CA-CDI in 2023 has surpassed healthcare-associated CDI (HA-CDI). Based upon the alarmingly increasing rates of CA-CDI, there is an urgent need for preventive measures as well as improved and widely implemented surveillance systems in order to contain this spread. The purpose of this review is to elaborate upon the intricate interplay between humans, animals and the soil, as reservoirs of Clostridioides difficile. In this regard, the One Health Approach will shed light upon this complex interconnection. Finally, within this framework, the prudent administration of antimicrobial agents as well as the potential role of machine learning will be pointed out.

articles.title: Bacterial co-infection in patients hospitalized with respiratory syncytial virus and influenza a infection: a retrospective observational cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare the prevalence, microbiological characteristics, and clinical impact of bacterial co-infection in adults hospitalized with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) or influenza A infection.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed RSV or influenza A infection in Central Denmark. Bacterial co-infection was identified using bacterial culturing and urinary antigen testing. Poisson regression was used to estimate risk ratios for bacterial co-infection, and Cox proportional hazards regression was used to evaluate associations between bacterial co-infection and adverse clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: Among 4,537 patients, 1,394 had RSV infection and 3,143 had influenza A infection. Among patients undergoing microbiological testing, bacterial co-infection was identified in 187/611 (30.6%) RSV-infected patients and 298/947 (31.5%) influenza A-infected patients (p = 0.72). Among all patients bacterial co-infection was identified in 187/1,394 (13.4%) RSV infected patients and 298/3,143 (9.5%) influenza A infected patients (p < 0.01) Haemophilus influenzae was the most common pathogen in both groups, followed by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Moraxella catarrhalis and Staphylococcus aureus. Bacterial co-infection was associated with increased ICU admission and mortality among influenza A infected patients, whereas estimates were lower in RSV.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing microbiological testing, bacterial co-infection was identified at similar rates in patients hospitalized with RSV and influenza A infection. The most frequently isolated bacteria in both viral groups were bacterial species harboring genes for beta-lactamase production. These findings support consideration of tailoring the empirical antibiotic therapy to cover pathogens with beta-lactamase production when bacterial co-infection is suspected in RSV and influenza A infected patients. Bacterial co-infection was associated with poorer clinical outcomes in Influenza A than RSV.

articles.title: Family screening and genetic testing in transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis : Changing (not only) variant transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis.
articles.journal: Netherlands heart journal : monthly journal of the Netherlands Society of Cardiology and the Netherlands Heart Foundation
articles.abstract: With increasing awareness of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) as a cause of heart failure and the availability of disease-modifying therapies, the importance of early diagnosis has grown. Consequently, greater emphasis has been placed on genetic testing and family screening to identify individuals with variant transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTRv) who are at risk of developing ATTRv cardiomyopathy (ATTRv-CM). To identify individuals with a genetic predisposition to the disease, all individuals with ATTR-CM should undergo genetic testing with subsequent cascade genetic testing in relatives when a genetic variant is identified. In asymptomatic pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) transthyretin (TTR) variant carriers, structured follow-up is recommended to enable early diagnosis, allowing timely initiation of treatment. Additionally, systematic family screening protocols may also help identify and detect ATTR-CM in general, including wild-type ATTR-CM.In conclusion, this narrative review provides clinicians with an overview of how to manage patients with ATTRv-CM and their families. Indeed, comprehensive genetic and cascade screening strategies are essential for early identification and optimal management of ATTR-CM. Future perspectives include refinement of risk stratification, optimization of diagnostic and screening pathways, improved timing of treatment initiation, and addressing health inequalities to ensure equitable access to care.

articles.title: Redefining Research Priorities for Youth and Family Behavioral Health in the United States: Results from an Expert Consensus Process.
articles.journal: Administration and policy in mental health
articles.abstract: Decision-makers in U.S. public behavioral health systems need reliable evidence on effective policies and practices to effectively navigate a landscape characterized by resource constraints and workforce challenges. To identify the highest priority information needs and research priorities of the youth behavioral health field, we engaged 60 research producers and researcher users in an expert consensus process that included two phases: (1) a pre-summit survey and (2) an in-person summit that included a Nominal Group Process (NGP). Participants included academic researchers, state behavioral health and Medicaid decision-makers, youth and family advocacy leaders, federal funders, and providers from 22 states. Results of the survey identified workforce development (41% of respondents), return on investment analysis (33%), and cross-system collaboration (33%) as top priorities. During the expert summit, participants reviewed survey results, discussed priority information needs, and engaged in an NGP that generated and ranked 191 recommendations. Highest-ranked information needs included evidence-based policy and financing options for cross-system interventions (16 votes), peer support best practices (16 votes), and rapid service scaling methodologies (15 votes). Research users were more likely than research producers to prioritize research on specific populations, including young children, youth with intellectual/developmental disorders, and transition-aged youth. Both groups prioritized research on effective financing strategies, cross-system collaboration, and workforce development. Results provide a research agenda for the U.S. youth behavioral health field that prioritizes expansion of the knowledge base on effective system and policy strategies and greater collaboration between researcher producers and research users to meet real-world information needs.

articles.title: Land Use Affects Spirometra mansoni Infection in Red Fox in Hokkaido, Japan.
articles.abstract: The spatial heterogeneity of parasite distribution is driven by factors such as land use and climate. However, the factors driving the transmission and persistence of many zoonotic parasites remain poorly understood. This study focused on the infection status of Spirometra mansoni, a zoonotic endoparasite of the red fox (Vulpes vulpes schrencki) in Hokkaido, the northernmost island of Japan. We surveyed the prevalence of S. mansoni in 251 red foxes. We investigated the association between the presence of S. mansoni infection in red foxes and land-use and climatic factors in the areas surrounding collection sites using generalized linear mixed model. We found 6.37% prevalence of S. mansoni in red foxes throughout Hokkaido with a heterogeneous distribution. Furthermore, we found that the presence of S. mansoni was positively associated with a land-use gradient characterized by greater freshwater and paddy fields coverage and less other open lands coverage. In contrast, no significant effects of climate were observed. This result suggests an association between land use and transmission of S. mansoni in red foxes, the definitive host of the parasite, in Hokkaido, Japan. The effect of land use may be mediated by the abundance of intermediate hosts, including aquatic organisms, such as frogs and copepods. This highlights the importance of better land-use policies worldwide that consider their impact on zoonotic diseases.

articles.title: Authors' reply regarding "Dynamics of infection, vaccination and excess mortality during the COVID-19 pandemic among older individuals-a nationwide analysis".
Testing bias and the absence of clinical diagnostic criteria: considerations on infection definition in the COVID-19 excess mortality study by Koster and colleagues.
Molecular Diagnostics and Clinicopathologic Spectrum of Kinase Fusion-Positive Spindle Cell Neoplasms of the Oral and Maxillofacial Region: A Systematic Review and Pooled Patient-Level Analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To characterize the clinicopathologic and molecular spectrum of kinase fusion-positive spindle cell neoplasms arising in the oral and maxillofacial region and to evaluate the patient-level contribution of molecular testing to diagnosis, classification, and therapeutic stratification.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception through July 31, 2026, supplemented by Google Scholar screening, reference checking, and citation tracking. Eligible reports described primary oral or maxillofacial spindle cell neoplasms harboring oncogenic kinase fusions or rearrangements. Overlapping publications were reconciled through patient-level deduplication. Clinicopathologic, immunophenotypic, molecular, diagnostic, treatment, and outcome data were synthesized descriptively. Molecular evidence was categorized into three prespecified tiers, and methodological quality was assessed using design-appropriate Joanna Briggs Institute tools.

RESULTS: Fifteen eligible reports contained 22 report-level tumor occurrences, which were reduced to 15 unique patients after deduplication. Median age was 8 years (range, neonatal period-65 years), and 9 patients (60.0%) were pediatric. Tumors involved oral/superficial mucosal-perioral sites in nine patients, deep maxillofacial soft tissues in three, and intraosseous sites in three. Alterations involved NTRK1 or NTRK3 in 10/15 patients (66.7%), RAF1 in 3/15 (20.0%), and MET and BRAF in one each. A partner-defined fusion was identified in 11/15 tumors; 11 were classified as Tier A, three as Tier B, and one as Tier C. A specific diagnostic or therapeutic contribution of molecular testing could be reconstructed in 7/15 patients, most often involving diagnostic refinement/reclassification or diagnostic establishment. Molecularly matched kinase inhibition was documented in two patients; one LMNA::NTRK1-positive maxillary tumor showed a rapid and durable response to larotrectinib.

CONCLUSIONS: Oral and maxillofacial kinase fusion-positive spindle cell neoplasms form a rare, morphologically and immunophenotypically heterogeneous spectrum extending beyond NTRK alterations. Integrated molecular testing can refine difficult diagnoses and, in selected patients, identify actionable kinase drivers. However, the small and molecularly selected evidence base precludes population prevalence estimates or comparative conclusions regarding treatment effects.

articles.title: From Dysbiosis to Vascular Disease: the Gut Microbiota in Type 2 Diabetes and Atherosclerosis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) are closely linked chronic disorders and leading causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Increasing evidence identifies the gut microbiota (GM), including its microbial genes and metabolites, as potential modifiers of these processes. This narrative review summarizes mechanistic, translational, and clinical evidence linking GM dysbiosis with T2D and atherosclerosis and evaluates microbiota-directed therapeutic strategies.

RECENT FINDINGS: Converging mechanistic, translational, and clinical evidence supports GM dysbiosis as a plausible shared contributor to T2D and atherosclerosis through interconnected pathways involving impaired intestinal barrier integrity and metabolic endotoxemia, TLR4/NF-κB- and inflammasome-mediated inflammation, and microbial metabolites, including short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), bile acids (BAs), trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), phenylacetylglutamine (PAGln), and tryptophan-derived indoles. These pathways can influence glucose and lipid metabolism, insulin signaling, immune activation, endothelial function, and vascular inflammation, providing a biological framework linking dysglycemia with increased cardiovascular risk and supporting the GM as a potential therapeutic target. However, the field remains limited by predominantly observational and confounded human data, incomplete causal evidence, and heterogeneous responses to microbiota-directed interventions. Dietary modification, prebiotics, probiotics, synbiotics, next-generation probiotics and postbiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation, and microbiota-modulating antidiabetic therapies have shown signals of benefit on metabolic or vascular surrogate endpoints, but evidence for durable clinical benefit remains limited and inconsistent across strains, populations, and study designs. Future progress in GM manipulation to improve cardiometabolic outcomes will require function-focused, causally grounded research and adequately powered, outcome-driven clinical trials incorporating GM-guided patient stratification. Until such evidence is available, the GM should be viewed as a biologically compelling and promising, but not yet clinically actionable, link between metabolic and atherosclerotic disease.

articles.title: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists for VEGF-pathway inhibitor-associated hypertension and proteinuria: biological rationale, clinical evidence, and a hypothesis-generating framework.
articles.abstract: In this narrative review, we integrate mechanistic, clinical, and cardiorenal evidence relevant to mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) in vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-pathway inhibitor-associated hypertension and proteinuria. VEGF-pathway inhibition can cause systemic endothelial dysfunction, altered nitric oxide and endothelin signaling, and heterogeneous glomerular injury, including thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) with VEGF-ligand blockade and podocytopathy with some VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors. Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) blockade, dihydropyridine calcium-channel blockers, careful blood pressure control, quantitative proteinuria assessment, and recognition of structural kidney injury remain the established management foundation. MR blockade is biologically attractive because it can lower blood pressure and proteinuria and modulate inflammatory, vascular, and glomerular pathways; however, most supporting evidence is extrapolated from resistant hypertension and chronic kidney disease. Direct oncology evidence is limited to small, nonrandomized datasets and remains hypothesis-generating. Accordingly, MRAs should not be positioned as a preferred third-line antihypertensive class or as established prophylaxis for VEGF-pathway inhibitor-associated renal toxicity. They may be considered as a phenotype-selected option when hypertension and non-nephrotic proteinuria coexist, conventional diuretic escalation is clinically unattractive, product-specific kidney function and potassium criteria are met, and close monitoring is feasible. Prospective oncology studies using kidney-function, structural, and treatment-continuity endpoints are required before routine adoption can be recommended.

articles.title: Physical Performance After Acute Myocardial Infarction: Gait, Frailty, and Cardiovascular Prognosis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Physical performance and frailty have emerged as potential markers of physiological reserve and cardiovascular vulnerability after acute myocardial infarction (AMI). This review examines the prognostic significance of gait speed, lower-extremity physical performance, frailty, and sarcopenia after AMI and acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and discusses their underlying pathophysiological mechanisms and clinical implications.

RECENT FINDINGS: Slow gait speed, impaired Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) scores, and frailty are associated with mortality, rehospitalization, heart failure, and adverse cardiovascular events after AMI or ACS. Gait speed and SPPB may provide incremental prognostic information beyond conventional cardiovascular risk assessment and established risk scores. These associations may reflect an interconnected cardiac-vascular-muscle axis involving reduced cardiac reserve, vascular dysfunction, impaired skeletal muscle perfusion, sarcopenia, and physical deconditioning. Importantly, emerging evidence suggests that targeted cardiac rehabilitation may improve gait speed, muscle strength, and overall physical performance in vulnerable patients. Physical performance represents a clinically relevant and potentially modifiable dimension of post-AMI cardiovascular vulnerability. Incorporating gait speed, SPPB, and frailty assessment into conventional risk stratification may improve patient phenotyping and identify individuals requiring more intensive rehabilitation and follow-up. Further prospective studies are needed to standardize assessment strategies and determine whether improving physical performance translates into better cardiovascular outcomes.

articles.title: Neurological and Medical Complications in Brain Tumor Patients. 2026 Update.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Patients with brain tumors have a plethora of potential complications that arise from both the tumor and its therapeutic management. These complicate clinical management and produce morbidity and occasionally mortality. In this review we discuss the most common neurological and medical complications that include tumor-related epilepsy, vasogenic edema, infection, thromboembolism, endocrine abnormalities and cognitive impairment and its management. This review is an update to the 2020 article by Schiff and Alyahya.

RECENT FINDINGS: IDH mutant gliomas cause neuronal hyperexcitability via D-2 -hydroxyglutarate production; use of IDH inhibitors may lower the rate of seizures in this patient population. Pneumocystis prophylaxis with antibiotics has been traditionally recommended with radiation and concurrent temozolomide chemotherapy but newer data suggest no difference in hospitalization or survival. Podoplanin produced by tumor cell releases into the circulation, often via extracellular vesicles, activates platelets and may contribute to venous thrombus formation. Direct oral Anticoagulants (DOACs) are the treatment of choice for venous thromboembolism, with high quality of evidence and a strong recommendation in cancer-associated thrombosis. Though brain tumor patients were underrepresented in clinical trials, retrospective studies support its safety in this population. Brain tumor patients are prone to complications arising from both the tumor and the treatment strategies. Management requires a multidisciplinary strategy with supportive medications including antiseizure medications, corticosteroids, anticoagulants for thromboembolism, and neurocognitive rehabilitation. Early recognition and timely intervention can reduce the morbidity associated with these complications leading to better patient outcomes.

articles.title: Integrative Network Pharmacology and Transcriptomic Analysis Prioritizes CCR1 and C5AR1 as Candidate Thromboinflammatory Targets Shared by Panax notoginseng Saponins and Stroke-Relevant Drugs in Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract: Thromboinflammation is a central pathological process contributing to secondary brain injury after ischemic stroke (IS). Panax notoginseng saponins (PNS) exert pleiotropic anti-inflammatory, antithrombotic, and vascular effects, but the molecular convergence between PNS-associated pharmacology and stroke-relevant conventional agents remains incompletely characterized. We integrated network pharmacology, bulk transcriptomic datasets, single-cell RNA sequencing, regulatory-network analysis, and structure-based molecular docking to prioritize candidate targets shared by PNS and an exploratory screening panel of 16 stroke-relevant pharmacological agents. Predicted drug and PNS targets were intersected with IS-associated differentially expressed genes (DEGs), followed by network analysis, independent cross-dataset expression assessment, gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA), transcription-factor (TF) prediction with co-expression analysis, myeloid-cell sub-clustering, and GNINA docking. The screening framework yielded 79 shared predicted pharmacological targets and 10 disease-associated candidates: ITK, CDK2, C5AR1, VDR, S1PR2, KIF11, CCR1, FAP, PRKCD, and MAOA. CCR1 and C5AR1 were prioritized because they combined high network connectivity with consistent disease-associated expression across the analyzed datasets and strong links to thromboinflammatory pathways. BATF2 and SPI1 expression positively correlated with both C5AR1 and CCR1 in GSE56267. Myeloid sub-clustering further showed that C5ar1 was broadly distributed across stroke-associated microglial and monocyte/macrophage states, whereas Ccr1 was more restricted to activated inflammatory and infiltrating myeloid populations. GNINA docking of all fourteen network-defined receptor-ligand systems identified five complexes with docking affinity scores between - 8.06 and - 10.94 kcal/mol (ginsenosides Rd and Re at CCR1; notoginsenoside R1, ginsenoside Rg1, and ginsenoside Rd at C5AR1). Collectively, these analyses prioritize CCR1 and C5AR1 as convergent candidate thromboinflammatory nodes shared by PNS-associated and stroke-relevant pharmacological target spaces. The findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish pharmacological synergy, direct receptor coupling, or causal therapeutic mechanisms.

articles.title: Safety, recovery, and hospital resource use after robot-assisted pheochromocytoma resection in a 48-hour short-stay pathway: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: To compare perioperative safety, early recovery, and resource use between a short-stay pathway and conventional inpatient care for robot-assisted pheochromocytoma resection. This single-center retrospective cohort included 110 patients who underwent robot-assisted pheochromocytoma resection: 47 managed in a short-stay pathway with discharge planned within 48 h of hospital admission and 63 managed with conventional inpatient care during the same period. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of Clavien-Dindo grade II or higher complications, unplanned intensive care, emergency attendance, readmission, reoperation, or death. Secondary outcomes included intraoperative hemodynamic instability, postoperative hypotension and hypoglycemia, pain, opioid consumption, Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15), length of stay, costs, pathway completion, and patient satisfaction. Welch t tests and Fisher exact tests were used for unadjusted comparisons, and absolute risk differences (RDs) and mean differences are reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Exploratory linear models with heteroscedasticity-robust standard errors adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, ASA class, tumor size, and duration of alpha blockade; sensitivity analyses additionally adjusted for surgeon, surgical approach, secretory phenotype, and hypertension. Baseline, comorbidity, endocrine, and operative characteristics were similar between groups (all standardized mean differences < 0.30). The 30-day composite safety outcome occurred in 1 of 47 short-stay patients (2.1%) and 1 of 63 conventional inpatients (1.6%; RD 0.5% points, 95% CI -6.6 to 9.6; P = 1.000). Intraoperative hemodynamic instability was also similar (83.0% vs. 87.3%; P = 0.590), as were persistent postoperative hypotension (8.5% vs. 7.9%) and postoperative hypoglycemia (8.5% vs. 7.9%). The planned 48-hour discharge target was achieved in 44 of 47 patients (93.6%). Compared with conventional care, the short-stay pathway had lower 24-hour pain scores (mean 1.8 vs. 2.4), total inpatient opioid exposure (8.7 vs. 17.7 mg morphine milligram equivalents), postoperative stay (44.2 vs. 105.1 h), total stay (49.2 vs. 476.4 h), and total in-hospital cost (CNY 49,858 vs. CNY 64,802), with higher 24-hour QoR-15 (119.7 vs. 107.9) and satisfaction (9.2 vs. 8.2); these differences remained significant after Holm correction and were consistent in fully adjusted sensitivity analyses. Among selected patients undergoing robot-assisted pheochromocytoma resection, the short-stay pathway was associated with similar observed perioperative safety outcomes, faster recovery, shorter hospitalization, lower in-hospital costs, and higher patient satisfaction than conventional inpatient care. Because only two composite events occurred and the 95% CI of the risk difference was wide, these findings provide preliminary evidence of feasibility rather than proof of equivalent safety, and support prospective validation.

articles.title: RNA interference targeting host physiological pathways enhances Beauveria bassiana efficacy against the tomato red spider mite Tetranychus evansi.
articles.abstract: The tomato red spider mite Tetranychus evansi is a major pest of Solanaceous crops and is increasingly difficult to control due to rapid development of resistance to acaricides. Entomopathogenic fungi such as Beauveria bassiana provide environmentally compatible alternatives, but their relatively slow action and variable efficacy limit field performance. This study investigated whether RNA interference (RNAi)-mediated disruption of key physiological pathways in T. evansi could enhance fungal pathogenicity. Spray bioassays revealed stage-specific susceptibility to B. bassiana strain HGS-1, with adult females being the most susceptible stage; however, mortality reached only 54% after 9 days at 1 × 109 spores/mL. To identify molecular targets, genes associated with housekeeping, immune, and cuticle-related functions were screened using RNAi. The result showed that silencing of genes TeATP, TeRPL13, TeRPS18, TeMyd88, TePGRP, TeCPR25, TeHex1, and TeHex2 significantly induced death of adult mites. The fungal infection​ following RNAi showed​ that silencing of these genes increased mitesusceptibility​ to B. bassiana. Co-application of dsRNA and B. bassiana further enhanced control efficacy. In particular, dsTeRPL13 and dsTeNox increased cumulative mortality by 18-19%, while dsTeCHS and dsTeHex1 reduced median lethal time, indicating faster disease progression. These results demonstrate that RNAi-mediated targeting of host physiological pathways can improve the performance of fungal biocontrol. By weakening metabolic capacity, immune defense, and cuticle integrity, this approach offers a promising, biosafe strategy for managing spider mites and addressing acaricide resistance within integrated pest management (IPM) programs.

articles.title: Climate-resilient tourism in Türkiye's Mediterranean and Aegean: an integrated tourism climate index and physiologically equivalent temperature assessment.
articles.abstract: Tourism in the Mediterranean and Aegean regions of Türkiye is highly vulnerable to global warming, primarily due to intensifying physiological heat stress and shifting seasonal thermal regimes. While macro-climatic indicators like the Tourism Climate Index (TCI) are widely used to assess destination suitability, they often fail to capture actual human biometeorological experiences, particularly extreme heat stress under future climate scenarios. To address this limitation, this study integrates the TCI and Physiologically Equivalent Temperature (PET) to evaluate baseline (1990-2020) and future (2070-2100, SSP5-8.5 scenario) outdoor thermal comfort across distinct elevation gradients. A high-resolution GIS-based spatial-temporal framework was applied to map monthly comfort classes. The results show a clear transition from cold-dominated to heat-stressed thermal regimes across the study area. Future projections indicate a significant warming trend; while Ideal TCI conditions increase by up to 40% in spring, summer suitability declines by over 50%. Crucially, PET analysis indicates a 55% expansion of Hot and Very Hot conditions by 2100, revealing a strong spatial divergence along the elevation gradient: low-elevation coastal areas may retain acceptable TCI scores yet experience severe physiological heat stress, whereas mid- and high-elevation zones maintain comparatively favorable summer thermal conditions. Consequently, tourism suitability shifts toward spring and autumn and toward higher elevations during summer, highlighting elevation as an important spatial control on future thermal comfort. This dual-index assessment demonstrates that human thermal perception must guide climate-adaptive tourism planning. The findings emphasize the necessity of altitudinal and seasonal diversification, alongside climate-sensitive design, to ensure human thermal resilience in the Eastern Mediterranean.

articles.title: From Birth to Burden: A Comprehensive Analysis of Health and Nutrition Inequities among Tribal Populations in India.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tribal populations in India, constituting 8.6% of the population, face disproportionate health and nutrition challenges compared with other groups. These inequities begin before birth, persist throughout the life course, and reflect structural marginalisation and unmet health needs.

OBJECTIVE: This study provides a comprehensive analysis of health and nutrition inequities among tribal populations in India, with particular focus on maternal and child health, nutritional status, and the burden of communicable and non-communicable diseases. The study compares key health and nutrition indicators between tribal and non-tribal populations to quantify and contextualise the magnitude of disparities experienced by tribal communities and to identify priority areas for improving health equity.

METHODS: Data for this study were obtained from the Report of the Expert Committee on Tribal Health, which compiles evidence from nationally representative sources, including the Census of India, National Family Health Survey (NFHS), and National Sample Survey Office (NSSO). The report provides comprehensive information on mortality, nutritional status, disease burden, and healthcare access among tribal and non-tribal populations. These data were extracted and analysed to describe the health and nutrition profile of tribal populations and to compare key indicators with the non-tribal population as a reference group. The comparative analysis was used to quantify and contextualise the magnitude and patterns of health and nutrition inequities experienced by tribal populations in India.

RESULTS: The findings reveal substantial socioeconomic and health disparities among Scheduled Tribes (STs) in India. Despite more favourable sex ratios, ST populations experienced higher school dropout rates and greater dependence on agriculture. These disadvantages were compounded by poor living conditions, with nearly half of tribal households practising open defecation and lacking access to improved sanitation and clean cooking fuel. Although infant and under-five mortality rates declined by more than 60%, substantial gaps relative to non-tribal populations remained. Nutritional deprivation persisted, with high burdens of malnutrition and anaemia. Hypertension prevalence was particularly high in Odisha (51.0%) and Kerala (40.5%), highlighting the growing burden of non-communicable diseases. While tuberculosis control improved over time, disparities in treatment access between the public and private sectors remained.

CONCLUSIONS: ST populations in India continue to face substantial health, nutritional, and socioeconomic disadvantages. Although progress has been achieved in several health indicators, significant gaps in maternal and child health, nutrition, and non-communicable diseases persist, particularly among women and children, highlighting the unequal distribution of health gains. These persistent disparities, along with marked inter-state variations, underscore the need for sustained, targeted, and equity-focused interventions to improve tribal health outcomes.

articles.title: Erdosteine Enhances Tobramycin Activity Against a Tobramycin-Resistant Clinical Isolate and PAO1 Reference Strain of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic respiratory infections caused by pathogens including Pseudomonas aeruginosa (P. aeruginosa) pose a major therapeutic challenge in patients with pulmonary diseases such as cystic fibrosis (CF) and non-CF bronchiectasis, where treatment efficacy is limited by the formation of biofilms, the emergence of multidrug resistant pathogens and a shortage of new and effective antibiotic classes. One approach to address this problem involves the use of "antibiotic enhancers", which are compounds that potentiate the activity of existing antibiotics without possessing direct antimicrobial effects of their own. The mucoactive thiol-based prodrug erdosteine, currently approved for the treatment of acute and chronic respiratory diseases, has been reported to exhibit anti-adhesive activity against respiratory pathogens, suggesting a clinically relevant contribution to the prevention of bacterial colonisation. Furthermore, in addition to reported anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, erdosteine has demonstrated the ability to potentiate the activity of various antimicrobial drugs. However, to date, whether erdosteine can enhance the activity of tobramycin, an antibiotic widely used to treat pathogens in the respiratory tract, has not been investigated. In this study, we investigated the ability of MET-1, the primary active metabolite of erdosteine, to enhance the activity of tobramycin against P. aeruginosa strains using a panel of both in vitro and in vivo assays.

METHODS: The activity of both mono- and combination therapies was measured in planktonic P. aeruginosa (strains RP73 & PAO1) using in vitro microdilution assays including chequerboard analysis and time-kill assays, whilst activity against biofilms were analysed using microtiter plate assays with readouts including total biomass, metabolic activity, and bacterial enumeration. Combination therapy of 40 mg/kg tobramycin and 100 mg/kg erdosteine was also assessed in vivo using a murine model of chronic pulmonary infection induced by P. aeruginosa.

RESULTS: 10 mg/L MET-1 significantly enhanced the antimicrobial activity of tobramycin in planktonic cultures of RP73 at 24 h and PAO1 at 4 h, leading to a greater than 2 log10 reduction in bacterial numbers compared to tobramycin monotherapy, despite MET-1 demonstrating no intrinsic bactericidal activity. In mature biofilms, MET-1 substantially enhanced tobramycin activity, reducing the biomass-derived IC₅₀ by approximately 18-fold in RP73 and 13-fold in PAO1. Finally, combination therapy of 40 mg/kg tobramycin and 100 mg/kg erdosteine was associated with a lower pulmonary bacterial burden in a murine model of chronic pulmonary infection.

CONCLUSIONS: Our in vitro and in vivo studies highlight the ability of erdosteine to potentiate the activity of tobramycin suggesting that erdosteine has the potential to reduce the burden of long-term antimicrobial therapies in patients with chronic respiratory infections and thus improve clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Echocardiographic cardiac structural Z-scores in children with severe malaria: a cross-sectional study in Southeast Nigeria.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe malaria is associated with cardiovascular alterations resulting from chronic anaemia, increased cardiac output, and myocardial stress. Echocardiographic Z-scores provide standardized assessment of cardiac dimensions and function in children, but data from African populations remain limited.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate echocardiographic Z-scores of cardiac structure and function among children with severe malaria and compare findings with healthy controls.

METHODS: This comparative cross-sectional study involved children with severe malaria and age-matched healthy controls. Echocardiographic measurements of cardiac valve dimensions and functional parameters were obtained and converted to Z-scores indexed to body surface area. Comparisons were also made between children with severe malarial anaemia (SMA) and those with other forms of severe malaria. Correlations between cardiac parameters and age were assessed.

RESULTS: Cardiac valve dimension Z-scores were comparable between subjects and controls (p > 0.05). However, ejection fraction was significantly lower in children with severe malaria compared with controls (65.5 ± 13.1 vs. 69.0 ± 9.8; p = 0.03). Among subjects, children with SMA had significantly lower left ventricular posterior wall diameter, interventricular septal thickness, and left ventricular internal diameter in systole compared with other severe malaria phenotypes (p < 0.05). Significant positive correlations existed between age and most Z scores of cardiac valve dimensions as well as selected functional parameters.

CONCLUSION: Children with severe malaria demonstrate preserved cardiac valve dimensions but reduced systolic function. Severe malarial anaemia is associated with alterations in selected cardiac functional parameters, underscoring the importance of echocardiographic evaluation in affected children.

articles.title: Clinical presentation, management strategies, and mortality outcomes in idiopathic aortitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Idiopathic Aortitis (IA) is defined as inflammation of the aortic wall, in the absence of a systemic disease or an infection. Most cases are found incidentally during repair of thoracic aortic aneurysms. Given the rarity of the disease, data on IA diagnosis and treatment are limited and derived mainly from small observational studies. This study aims to comprehensive and up-to-date synthesis of the available evidence on IA.

METHODS: Literature search of the PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases was performed in late September 2025. Data regarding patients' medical history, presentations, complications, diagnostic investigations, management and outcomes were obtained.

RESULTS: A total of 58 studies were included, comprising data from 79 patients with idiopathic aortitis. The mean age was 46 ± 20 years, with a slight male predominance of 53%. Weight loss was the most frequently reported symptom (58%). Regarding management, 44% underwent exclusive surgical treatment, 31% received mixed therapy, and 25% were managed medically. Corticosteroids were utilized in 51% of cases. The overall mortality rate was 20%. Significant predictors of mortality included a younger age at presentation (18 vs. 48 years, P < 0.001) and descending aorta involvement (P = 0.005). Conversely, corticosteroid administration (P = 0.002) and clinical surveillance (P < 0.001) were significantly associated with survival.

CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis highlights idiopathic aortitis as a severe condition with significant mortality whereas the administration of corticosteroids and clinical surveillance are strongly associated with survival, our findings emphasize the need for standardized, evidence-based management protocols and prospective multicenter studies to optimize patient outcomes.

articles.title: Mid to long-term effect of balloon pulmonary valvuloplasty on right ventricle function: a three-dimensional echocardiographic study.
articles.journal: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV) remodelling may persist after balloon pulmonary valvuloplasty (BPV) for isolated valvular pulmonary stenosis (PVS). Three-dimensional echocardiography (3DE) enables global RV volumetric assessment beyond conventional 2D indices.

METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study included 200 pediatric patients (≤ 18 years) with isolated PVS who underwent successful BPV (post-procedural peak gradient < 36 mmHg) at least 1 year before evaluation. All patients had clinical assessment, ECG, standard 2D/Doppler echocardiography (TAPSE, S', FAC), and ECG-gated 3DE RV quantification to derive RV end-diastolic and end-systolic volume indices and right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF). Patients were classified into 2 groups; group 1 had normal RVEF (≥ 45%) and group 2 had impaired RVEF (< 45%).

RESULTS: RVEF was normal in 71% (n = 142) and impaired in 29% (n = 58). Group 2 was associated with; older age at assessment (median 120 vs. 72 months, p < 0.001), later intervention (median age at BPV 24 vs. 3 months, p < 0.001), and longer time since BPV (96 vs. 68 months, p = 0.004). it also showed association with higher pre-dilatation peak gradients (97.24 ± 26.47 vs. 83.8 ± 24.61 mmHg, p = 0.017) and higher post-dilatation gradients (30.97 ± 9.81 vs. 23.56 ± 8.59 mmHg, p < 0.001). Group 2 also had lower conventional RV function indices: S' 12.64 ± 3.22 vs. 15.01 ± 1.09 cm/s, TAPSE 16.28 ± 2.75 vs. 19.21 ± 1.72 mm, and FAC 39.86 ± 5.21 vs. 49.8 ± 2.62% (all p < 0.001). by using 3DE interrogation, group 2 showed higher RVEDV index (62.0 ± 11.06 vs. 43.14 ± 11.44, p < 0.001) and RVESV index (34.41 ± 8.24 vs. 22.76 ± 6.65, p < 0.001) .

CONCLUSIONS: At ≥ 1 year after successful BPV, nearly one-third of children showed impaired 3DE-derived RVEF, associated with older age at intervention, higher residual gradients, and RV dilatation, patients with RV impairment were underestimated when assessed by 2D vs. 3D echo, supporting the role of 3DE in long-term surveillance.

articles.title: Rare genetic variants in leber hereditary optic neuropathy: molecular mechanisms, diagnosis, and emerging therapies.
articles.abstract: Hereditary optic neuropathies, such as Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON), remain a focus of active research. Diagnostic challenges and severe clinical consequences often result in atypical presentations, creating significant obstacles for neuro-ophthalmology. The field has garnered increased attention due to advances in molecular biology and genetic engineering. Pathogenic variants in mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and nuclear DNA disrupt oxidative phosphorylation, reduce adenosine triphosphate production, and increase reactive oxygen species generation, to which retinal ganglion cells are particularly vulnerable. Rare genetic variants have been identified in LHON and related mitochondrial disorders, including mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, lactic acidosis, and stroke-like episodes and Leigh syndrome. Phenotypic heterogeneity, variable heteroplasmy levels, and limited sensitivity of targeted genetic testing complicate the detection and interpretation of rare variants. As a result, comprehensive next-generation sequencing is increasingly necessary for accurate molecular diagnosis and timely treatment initiation. Recent therapeutic interventions include genotype-specific approaches, such as adeno-associated virus serotype 2-mediated allotopic expression, and genotype-independent therapies, such as idebenone. Diagnostic standards for mitochondrial optic neuropathies have shifted from focusing solely on the three primary pathogenic mtDNA variants to a broader molecular diagnostic framework. Future research should prioritize mtDNA sequencing in cases with inconclusive diagnoses using conventional methods, incorporate mitochondrial and nuclear genomics, and leverage artificial intelligence-based approaches. Accurate identification and classification of rare variants, together with a deeper understanding of their phenotypic consequences, will facilitate the development of individualized therapeutic strategies to prevent further visual decline. This review outlines potential directions for multifaceted treatment strategies in patients with rare LHON-associated variants and critically evaluates current evidence regarding the clinical significance of rare mitochondrial and nuclear genetic variants in LHON and related mitochondrial optic neuropathies.

articles.title: The spectrum of amyloid cardiovascular disease.
articles.abstract: Cardiac amyloidosis, historically characterized as a restrictive cardiomyopathy, is now understood as a multi-compartmental disorder. Atrial amyloid infiltration-whether ANP-derived isolated atrial amyloidosis secondary to atrial stretch, or primary atrial ATTR infiltration-produces an atrial cardiomyopathy that frequently manifests as atrial fibrillation and a thrombogenic substrate even in sinus rhythm. Cardiac amyloidosis exhibits a high prevalence in heart failure, particularly among elderly patients presenting with preserved ejection fraction. Furthermore, TTR amyloid frequently coexists with degenerative aortic stenosis, and amyloid deposits are also found in the coronary microcirculation and the aorta. Given the current availability of efficacious treatments for amyloidosis, the recognition of these diverse clinical manifestations is paramount for achieving accurate diagnosis, appropriate risk stratification, and timely therapeutic intervention to enhance cardiovascular outcomes. This review frames amyloid cardiovascular disease as a multisystem process affecting the myocardium, atria, valves, and vasculature-often with extracardiac red flags-rather than solely as an infiltrative ventricular cardiomyopathy. Actionable implications currently concentrate on ventricular ATTR/AL cardiomyopathy and concomitant aortic stenosis; coronary and aortic medial deposits remain mechanistically important research targets rather than independently treatable lesions.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of the cladribine, idarubicin, and cytarabine regimen for treating acute myeloid leukemia: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This research sought to provide exploratory evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of the cladribine, idarubicin, and cytarabine (CIA) regimen for acute myeloid leukemia (AML).

EVIDENCE ACQUISITION: PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Embase databases were retrieved up to September 9, 2025. Meta-analysis was implemented utilizing R (version 4.5.1).

RESULTS: All efficacy endpoints were analyzed and reported separately by disease status. In newly diagnosed (ND) AML, pooled estimates were: complete remission (CR), 72.7% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 66.4%-79.0%); complete remission with incomplete hematologic recovery (CRi), 7.1% (95% CI: 3.7%-10.6%); overall response rate (ORR), 80.4% (95% CI: 76.8%-84.0%); 1-year overall survival (OS), 60.5% (95% CI: 53.5%-67.5%); and 2-year OS, 65.5% (95% CI: 33.4%-97.5%). For relapsed/refractory (R/R) AML, only CR could be quantitatively pooled (pooled estimate 37.1%, 95% CI: 7.5%-66.6%), albeit with limited statistical power. CRi, ORR, and OS were not pooled owing to insufficient studies; available data are described narratively. The pooled safety estimates were: rash/skin reaction 34.3% (95% CI: 0.0%-85.0%), severe infection in ND AML 59.5% (25.2%-93.8%), severe bleeding in ND AML 5.9% (2.8%-9.0%), and 28-day all-cause mortality 6.1% (1.1%-11.2%).

CONCLUSIONS: Results indicate promising remission in ND AML, particularly low- to intermediate-risk cases. In contrast, efficacy is limited in R/R AML. Severe infections remain a major safety concern. Given the small number of studies and single-arm pooling, findings should be interpreted with caution. Future research should prioritize larger well-defined R/R AML cohorts, standardized CIA dosing regimens, and head-to-head randomized controlled trials against contemporary standard-of-care regimens (e.g., 7 + 3 plus gemtuzumab ozogamicin, CPX-351, and venetoclax-based combinations). Further exploration of CIA combined with molecular targeted agents (e.g., FLT3/IDH inhibitors) and standardized reporting of long-term endpoints including event-free survival and relapse-free survival are warranted.

articles.title: Short-term outcomes of the hinotori versus da Vinci robotic surgical systems in colorectal cancer surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Direct comparative evidence on the hinotori and da Vinci robotic systems in colorectal cancer surgery remains limited. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to compare their short-term perioperative outcomes. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies directly comparing hinotori with da Vinci robotic surgery in patients with colorectal cancer. Study-level data were pooled using random-effects models, with mean differences (MDs) for continuous outcomes and odds ratios (ORs) for dichotomous outcomes, each with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Five retrospective propensity-score-matched studies involving 462 patients (hinotori, n = 204; da Vinci, n = 258) were included. Operative time (MD 30.57 min, 95% CI 17.51-43.64; I² = 0%) and console time (MD 30.72 min, 95% CI 17.29-44.16; I² = 42%) were significantly longer with hinotori, whereas length of hospital stay was significantly shorter (MD - 1.58 days, 95% CI - 2.92 to - 0.24; I² = 63%). No statistically significant differences were detected for estimated blood loss (MD 3.42 mL, 95% CI - 6.98 to 13.82; I² = 66%) or for postoperative complications (grade I-II: OR 0.78, 95% CI 0.36-1.69; grade III-IV: OR 0.54, 95% CI 0.16-1.76; overall: OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.37-1.46). In this meta-analysis of propensity-score-matched studies, hinotori was associated with longer operative and console times and a shorter hospital stay than da Vinci, whereas no statistically significant difference was detected in blood loss or postoperative complications. Because clinically important differences in safety could not be excluded and residual confounding could not be ruled out, these findings should be regarded as preliminary; larger prospective comparative studies are warranted.

articles.title: Differential Ecotoxicity of Marine Litter Components: Identification of Typologies with Higher Hazard Potential.
articles.journal: Archives of environmental contamination and toxicology
articles.abstract: Marine litter was sampled on beaches from the Baltic (Germany), the NE Atlantic (Galicia) and the Mediterranean (Morocco, Tunisia, Egypt, Italy) coasts according to standard procedures, and occasionally from the NE Atlantic seafloor by trawling. Collected items were associated to OSPAR and JRC typologies. The ecotoxicity of specific types of marine litter was assessed by measuring the inhibition of Paracentrotus lividus embryo-larval development caused by their leachates. Cigarette butts exhibited the highest toxicity consistently across all sampling sites, followed in decreasing order by foam, fisheries related items, and strings. The food-related items: plastic caps, metal caps and PET water bottles, showed the lowest ecotoxicity. Overall, the results indicate substantial differences in the ecotoxicological hazard of marine litter typologies under standardized laboratory conditions, with cigarette butts showing the highest hazard potential among the categories tested.

articles.title: Association of HTR3A and COMT polymorphisms with electroacupuncture response for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting in breast cancer: a secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Preliminary findings indicate that electroacupuncture (EA) reduces chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV), yet individual responses vary. This study aimed to explore associations between selected single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and complete protection (CP) against CINV and to conduct an exploratory evaluation of their predictive value.

METHODS: This exploratory analysis was based on a randomized controlled trial (RCT) of EA (NCT05275569). Three candidate SNPs in HTR3A and COMT were genotyped by Sanger sequencing. The primary outcome measure was CP against CINV, defined according to the endpoint of the prospective study. Firth logistic regression was applied to evaluate associations between clinical or genetic variables and CP under additive, dominant and recessive models.

RESULTS: A total of 189 patients with breast cancer (BC) were enrolled, with 96 allocated to true EA group and 93 to sham EA group. The two groups were comparable in clinical variables and genotype distribution, and all three SNPs conformed to Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium (HWE). In the true EA group, CP achievement rates varied by rs909411 genotype: 42.9% (AA), 32.1% (AG), and 62.3% (GG) (P = 0.027). Univariable Firth logistic regression indicated that rs909411 was associated with a higher likelihood of achieving CP under both additive (OR = 2.088, 95% CI: 1.089-4.249, P = 0.026) and recessive models (OR = 3.080, 95% CI: 1.327-7.429, P = 0.009). After Multivariable adjustment, rs909411 remained statistically significant (additive: OR = 2.138, P = 0.027; recessive: OR = 3.241, P = 0.011). rs4633 was associated with a lower likelihood of achieving CP under the recessive model (univariable OR = 0.089, P = 0.035; Multivariable OR = 0.059, P = 0.016). No consistent association was observed for rs4680, and no significant SNP-by-treatment interactions were detected.

CONCLUSION: Exploratory treatment-stratified analyses identified associations of rs909411 and rs4633 with CP within the true EA group.

articles.title: Single-port robotic thoracic surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative outcomes versus multiport robotic surgery and uniportal VATS.
articles.abstract: Single-port robotic-assisted thoracic surgery (SP-RATS) has expanded rapidly, but its comparative effectiveness remains uncertain across platforms and access strategies. We systematically evaluated SP-RATS against multiport robotic-assisted thoracic surgery (MP-RATS) and uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (uVATS). PubMed/MEDLINE, CENTRAL, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov, and supplementary sources were searched through October 5, 2026. Random-effects meta-analyses with modified Knapp-Hartung inference were used for continuous and common binary outcomes, whereas rare events were analyzed using fixed-effect Peto odds ratios. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist, and certainty using GRADE. Sixty reports were included; 23 provided Group A or B comparative data, with one study at critical risk of bias excluded from the primary quantitative synthesis. Compared with MP-RATS, SP-RATS demonstrated broadly similar perioperative outcomes without a consistent disadvantage. Lymph-node yield was nominally lower (MD, - 1.18 nodes; 95% CI, - 2.31 to - 0.05; P = 0.043), but this finding did not persist across sensitivity analyses. Compared with uVATS, SP-RATS was associated with shorter chest-tube duration (MD, - 0.49 days; 95% CI, - 0.85 to - 0.13; P = 0.013), with additional favorable signals in lymph-node yield, chest drainage, and conversion, although these were less consistent across sensitivity analyses. Complications, R0 resection, and mortality did not differ significantly between approaches. Certainty of evidence was low or very low across all pooled outcomes. SP-RATS appears to be a viable minimally invasive alternative, achieving reduced robotic access without an evident trade-off in perioperative safety or immediate oncologic outcomes. Prospective comparative studies are needed to determine whether reduced robotic access provides reproducible clinical benefit.

articles.title: Sequencing trastuzumab deruxtecan and sacituzumab govitecan in metastatic breast cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) and sacituzumab govitecan (SG) are both approved for metastatic breast cancer (mBC), and patients with HER2-low disease are often candidates for both, but the optimal sequence is undefined. This systematic review and meta-analysis compared outcomes of the second antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) by treatment sequence (SG→T-DXd versus T-DXd→SG).

METHODS: Following PRISMA (PROSPERO CRD420251250322), PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL and major oncology conference proceedings were searched through December 2025 for studies of sequential T-DXd and SG in mBC. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival on the second ADC (PFS2). Hazard ratios (HRs) were obtained from patient-level data, published estimates or reconstructed Kaplan-Meier curves and pooled using a random-effects model. Study heterogeneity was assessed using the I² statistic. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed with ROBINS-I and GRADE.

RESULTS: Of 694 records, 17 retrospective studies were included; seven (292 SG→T-DXd and 286 T-DXd→SG patients) contributed to the PFS2 meta-analysis. The pooled HR for T-DXd→SG versus SG→T-DXd was 1.54 (95% CI 0.98-2.40; I²=61%), 1.72 (95% CI 1.23-2.41; I²=10%) after excluding one study, and 1.36 (95% CI 0.89-2.10) with covariate-adjusted estimates. Median PFS2 was 3.3 months with SG→T-DXd and 2.8 months with T-DXd→SG.

CONCLUSION: Point estimates favoured SG→T-DXd, but given very low certainty and likely confounding by tumour subtype, current data do not establish the superiority of either sequence. Prospective, subtype-stratified studies are needed.

articles.title: International Model to Inform the Care of Individuals with a Vertebral Fragility Fracture.
articles.abstract: Vertebral fragility fractures (VFF) are associated with pain, impaired function, and increased fracture risk. Our aim was to develop an internationally applicable model to guide the care of individuals with VFF. The Fragility Fracture Network (FFN) VFF Special Interest Group established the project structure and scope: review existing guidance and adapt recommendations and a visual model; solicit knowledge user feedback; make iterative revisions to the recommendations and visual model based on feedback; and finalize the recommendations. The model adapts recommendations from a published international Delphi consensus and national guidance. Knowledge user feedback was obtained through a survey disseminated via FFN channels across 40 countries. The survey responses informed iterative revision and finalization of the care model. The final VFF care model comprised three domains. 'Pain management' emphasizes structured pain and physical functioning assessment, multimodal pharmacological and non-pharmacological strategies, patient education, and timely referral for specialist review when indicated. The domain 'Improving Physical Functioning' included promoting movement, early mobilization, exercise focused on strength, balance, and back extensor endurance, and behaviour change approaches to support return to physical activities of leisure and daily living. The domain, Fall and Fracture Prevention, integrates falls and fracture risk assessment and prevention. It included nutritional evaluation, optimization of vitamin D and calcium intake, osteoporosis medication initiation, and referral for exercise, home hazard assessment, and specialist input. Cross-cutting components included patient education, behavioural support, and communication to ensure continuity of care. The VFF care model offers a comprehensive framework adaptable to diverse settings and an international perspective. Its multidisciplinary approach addresses gaps in VFF management and includes defined Key Performance Indicators. A multidisciplinary team developed an internationally applicable model to guide the care of individuals with vertebral fragility fracture, with input from knowledge users in 40 countries, with recommendations on pain management, improving physical functioning, and preventing falls and fractures.

articles.title: Transition From Oral to Long-Acting Injectable Preexposure Prophylaxis: Comparative Levels of Cabotegravir, Tenofovir, and Emtricitabine in Plasma and Seminal Fluids.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although oral preexposure prophylaxis (PrEP) with tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF)/emtricitabine (FTC) is highly effective for individuals whose sexual activities place them at high risk for HIV infection, it is limited by adherence. Long-acting injectable cabotegravir (CAB-LAI) offers an alternative, but limited data are available on its distribution in seminal fluid (SF), a key vector for sexual HIV transmission. In this study, the pharmacokinetics of antiretrovirals in the blood plasma (BP) and SF of HIV-negative men who have sex with men during the transition to CAB-LAI were characterized.

METHODS: Forty-four men who have sex with men initiated on CAB-LAI at San Raffaele Hospital (January-May 2025) were enrolled. At baseline (T0), 23 of the participants were on daily TDF/FTC, 18 were on event-driven TDF/FTC, and 3 were PrEP naïve. Oral PrEP users continued TDF/FTC for 7 days after the first injection. BP and SF samples were collected at 0 (T0), 7 (T1), 30 (T2), and 90 (T3) days after injection. The drug levels were quantified using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. HIV testing was performed longitudinally.

RESULTS: At T0, the median TDF levels were 31 ng/mL in BP and 152 ng/mL in SF, whereas the median FTC levels were 79 ng/mL in BP and 676 ng/mL in SF. At T1, both drugs remained detectable in fewer participants, with consistently higher levels in SF. By T2, both drugs had largely decreased in level, with isolated detectable cases, and neither drug was measurable at T3. The median BP CAB concentration was 1844 ng/mL at T1, with 80% of the men exceeding the protective 664 ng/mL threshold. This proportion remained high at T2 (77.3%) and T3 (60.6%). By contrast, the SF CAB concentrations were approximately 100-fold lower.

CONCLUSIONS: Most participants achieved BP-protective CAB levels within 1 week, confirming sustained efficacy. However, CAB was often below the detection limit in SF.

articles.title: Effects of Eplontersen on Cardiac Structure and Function in Patients With Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy: Insights from the CARDIO-TTRansform Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In CARDIO-TTRansform, the TTR (transthyretin) silencer eplontersen did not significantly reduce the primary end point of cardiovascular death and recurrent cardiovascular events in patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy, although treatment effects varied by baseline TTR stabilizer use. Whether eplontersen favorably affects cardiac structure and function is unknown.

METHODS: CARDIO-TTRansform randomized 1432 patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy to eplontersen (45 mg) subcutaneously every 4 weeks or placebo. Echocardiograms were performed at baseline and weeks 61, 97, and 140. Associations of baseline echocardiographic measures with all-cause mortality and the primary end point were evaluated using Cox and semiparametric proportional rates models. Between-group differences at week 140 were analyzed with mixed models for repeated measures.

RESULTS: Among 1426 participants with baseline echocardiograms (mean age, 76±7 years, 91% men, 85% wild type, 57% receiving stabilizers), baseline measures of left ventricular systolic function (LV ejection fraction, global longitudinal strain, stroke volume, myocardial contraction fraction), diastolic function (E wave deceleration time, septal e', average E/e'), and right ventricular function and hemodynamics were independently associated with all-cause mortality or the primary end point. At week 140 (echocardiograms available in 554 patients in the eplontersen group and 506 in the placebo group), eplontersen attenuated increases in mean LV wall thickness (least-squares mean [LSM] difference, -0.24 mm [95% CI, -0.48 to -0.01]) and declines in LV stroke volume (LSM difference, 1.88 mL [95% CI, 0.07-3.69]), myocardial contraction fraction (LSM difference, 0.88% [95% CI, 0.25-1.57]), average E/e' (LSM difference, -0.71 [95% CI, -1.36 to -0.07]), and right ventricular outflow tract velocity-time integral (LSM difference, 0.42 [95% CI, 0.00-0.85]) versus placebo in the overall cohort. Beneficial effects were driven almost exclusively by patients not receiving stabilizers at baseline. No significant treatment effects were observed in patients receiving stabilizers.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy, eplontersen modestly attenuated deterioration in prognostically important measures of LV systolic, diastolic and right ventricular function, primarily among patients not receiving stabilizers at baseline. These findings complement the clinical findings of CARDIO-TTRansform and suggest that TTR silencing may attenuate progression of cardiac dysfunction in TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy.
