articles.title: [Socioeconomic inequalities in breast cancer in Germany: current situation and development over time].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breast cancer is one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality among women in high-income countries. To date, there is little evidence available regarding the role of socioeconomic factors in Germany. This study examines socioeconomic differences and time trends in the incidence, stage at diagnosis and mortality of breast cancer.

METHODS: The study is based on small-area data from cancer registries as well as official statistics on causes of death and population. The data were linked at district level to the German Index of Socioeconomic Deprivation. Missing data on tumour stage were imputed using multiple imputation. Age-standardised incidence and mortality rates by regional socioeconomic deprivation were estimated using multilevel Poisson regressions.

RESULTS: Areas with low levels of deprivation consistently showed higher incidence rates, primarily due to more frequent diagnoses at early stages. In the early 2000s, breast cancer mortality was highest in affluent areas. Due to a sharper decline in these areas, most deprived areas recorded the highest mortality rates from 2008-2010 onwards. The modelled rates thus point to a reversal in the pattern of inequality, with breast cancer mortality becoming increasingly higher in most deprived areas.

DISCUSSION: The temporal development suggests that the emerging reversal of the social gradient in breast cancer mortality cannot be explained primarily by differences in the trends in incidence or stage at diagnosis. Other factors, such as socially determined differences in the prevalence of comorbidities and their risk factors, could play a key role and should be investigated further.

articles.title: [Emergency medicine requirements for the resuscitation room and the resuscitation room team].
articles.abstract: The resuscitation room is the central interface between prehospital emergency medical services (EMS) and in-hospital emergency care for critically ill and severely injured patients. From an EMS perspective, requirements are defined for activation, prenotification, team structure, handover, overload management and feedback. Written activation and allocation criteria are required that are applicable in the prehospital setting and agreed upon by hospitals, emergency dispatch centres and EMS providers. Prenotification must take place through a continuously available, reliable communication channel, be actively acknowledged and enable transparent feedback on capacity. Paramedics must be authorised to activate the resuscitation room independently of the presence of an emergency physician. On arrival, a qualified and operational team with clearly identifiable roles should be available. Handover should be structured and as interruption-free as possible. The exploratory online survey showed that trauma resuscitation care is predominantly guideline-based and more often includes a written minimum staffing requirement. In nontrauma resuscitation care, written activation criteria and binding team structures were less frequently available. Although handovers were mostly standardised, substantial deficits existed in overload and diversion protocols as well as in interprofessional feedback structures involving EMS. These findings indicate a need for coordinated procedures, transparent capacity management and binding quality-assurance measures.

articles.title: Integrating PCR and sequencing for the identification of pathogenic fungi on formalin-fixed tissues: a systematic review toward a pragmatic histomolecular solution.
authors: on behalf the Infectious Diseases Pathology Working Group of the European Society of Pathology (ESP)
articles.journal: Virchows Archiv : an international journal of pathology
articles.abstract: Although histopathology is a gold standard for the diagnosis of invasive fungal infections, the morphological analysis does not provide an accurate genus and/or species identification. Because this specific identification is required for antifungal therapy prescription, the implementation of molecular techniques to identify fungi on formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue in practice is crucial, especially when specimen has not been simultaneously sent to the mycology laboratory. However, such approaches/procedures remain heterogenous. The objective of this systematic review (PROSPERO: CRD420261420594) was to gather data from the literature to support future efforts toward the standardisation of diagnostic practices for fungal identification on FFPE tissue. Among the 1,550 records found on MEDLINE-PubMed and Google Scholar, 57 studies were included. Thirty-two, 27, and 10 studies investigated the use on FFPE tissue of taxon-specific fungal PCR (n = 1421 FFPE samples tested), panfungal PCR followed by Sanger sequencing (n = 1647 FFPE samples tested), and targeted next-generation sequencing/massive parallel sequencing (NGS/MPS) or untargeted metagenomics (n = 408 FFPE samples tested; some studies reported several techniques), respectively. The sensitivity and specificity of the techniques, according to pre-analytical, histopathological, and molecular criteria were reported and discussed. Advantages and limitations of each technique are presented. While taxon-specific fungal PCR are widely available and highly sensitive, sequencing-based techniques have a broader spectrum for identification purpose. Finally, because of the contamination of tissue sections and the presence of fungi belonging to microbiota on samples, the molecular identification should always be correlated to the pathogenic fungi's morphology, to ensure an accurate and reliable integrated histomolecular diagnosis.

articles.title: Persistent systemic hypertension in a child with carbonic anhydrase II deficiency.
articles.abstract: Carbonic anhydrase II (CA II) deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive disorder classically characterized by osteopetrosis, renal tubular acidosis (RTA), and intracranial calcifications. We report a 10-year-old girl with genetically confirmed CA II deficiency who developed acute severe hypertension after previously documented normotension. Blood pressure reached 160/100 mmHg and was accompanied by headache, vomiting, and transient neurological symptoms requiring intravenous antihypertensive therapy. Hypertension persisted beyond the acute episode and was confirmed by ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) despite treatment, requiring long-term antihypertensive therapy. Serial ABPM during follow-up subsequently demonstrated sustained blood pressure control, permitting stepwise dose reduction and eventual discontinuation of amlodipine approximately two years after presentation. Systemic hypertension has not previously been reported in CA II deficiency. This single-patient observation is hypothesis-generating and does not establish a causal relationship.

articles.title: PODIUM renal dysfunction criteria identify children with higher severity of illness than KDIGO acute kidney injury criteria in an observational cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: KDIGO acute kidney injury (AKI) criteria are not specific to children. Pediatric Organ Dysfunction Information Update Mandate (PODIUM) renal dysfunction criteria were developed for children but have not been adopted. PODIUM defines renal dysfunction more strictly than KDIGO and adds fluid overload (FO) as an independent criterion. The impact of these changes on AKI diagnosis has not been evaluated.

METHODS: Retrospective analysis of pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admissions at an academic children's hospital from 06/2022-05/2025. Creatinine, urine output, fluid balance, and weight were extracted in 6-h intervals. Patients were classified by maximum KDIGO AKI stage and PODIUM AKI. Outcomes were mortality, PICU length of stay (LOS), and major adverse kidney events at 30 days (MAKE-30).

RESULTS: In 10,454 patients, 2,602 (25%) met KDIGO AKI criteria: 1,124 (11%) KDIGO 1, 579 (5%) KDIGO 2, and 899 (9%) KDIGO 3. By PODIUM, 1,599 (15%) met criteria. 105 (9%) KDIGO 1 patients and 16 (0.2%) patients without KDIGO AKI met PODIUM criteria; all KDIGO 2/3 met PODIUM. 110/1,599 (7%) of patients with PODIUM AKI met only FO criterion. Outcomes were similar between KDIGO 2/3 and PODIUM AKI (mortality 6-7%, median LOS 7-8.5 days, MAKE-30 12%). Patients meeting PODIUM by FO alone had worse outcomes than KDIGO Stage 1 or No AKI (mortality 4% vs. 1-2%, median LOS 13.8 vs. 1.5-5.5 days), but not different MAKE-30.

CONCLUSIONS: PODIUM criteria capture all KDIGO 2/3 patients while excluding most KDIGO 1 patients. PODIUM criteria appear useful for identifying critically ill children with clinically significant AKI resulting in greater short-term illness severity, while KDIGO criteria capture a larger spectrum of AKI severity.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes and mortality predictors of peritoneal dialysis in critically ill neonates.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peritoneal dialysis (PD) is a commonly used kidney replacement therapy for neonatal acute kidney injury (AKI), yet data on outcomes and mortality predictors remain limited. This study evaluated the clinical outcomes, complications, and mortality predictors of PD in neonates with AKI.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included neonates who underwent PD in a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit between 2018 and 2023. Clinical characteristics, PD indications, complications, and outcomes were analysed. Survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis, and independent mortality predictors were identified using multivariable Cox regression.

RESULTS: Eighty-one neonates underwent PD. Fifty-eight percent were preterm, with a median gestational age of 36 weeks and a mean birth weight of 2449.8 ± 1000.4 g. The most common indications for PD were azotemia (71.6%) and oligoanuria (48.1%). Median PD duration was 6 days, and overall mortality was 74.1%. Median survival time after catheter insertion was 8 days. Dialysate leakage was the most frequent complication (14.7%). Independent predictors of mortality were hydrops fetalis (HR 15.26, p < 0.001), inborn metabolic disorders (HR 6.82, p < 0.001), fluid overload (HR 4.43, p = 0.039), and perinatal asphyxia (HR 2.73, p = 0.024). PD was associated with significant improvements in acid-base and electrolyte parameters.

CONCLUSIONS: Mortality remains high among neonates requiring PD. Hydrops fetalis, metabolic disorders, fluid overload, and perinatal asphyxia were independently associated with death. Early recognition of these high-risk features may improve risk stratification and clinical management.

articles.title: Proximal complement inhibition with pegcetacoplan in recurrent C3 glomerulopathy after pediatric kidney transplantation: a case report.
articles.abstract: C3 glomerulopathy (C3G) is a rare complement-mediated kidney disease caused by dysregulation of the alternative pathway, often leading to progressive kidney failure and high post-transplant recurrence rates. Treatment options for recurrent disease are limited, though complement inhibitors have emerged as targeted therapies. A 9-year-old girl presented with edema, hypertension, hematuria, and low C3 levels. Kidney biopsy showed dense deposit disease. Despite corticosteroids and mycophenolate mofetil, she rapidly progressed to kidney failure requiring dialysis. After kidney transplantation, early recurrence occurred within 2 months. Treatment with renin-angiotensin system blockade and the C5 inhibitor ravulizumab led to transient improvement followed by relapse. Therapy was switched to pegcetacoplan. Early improvement was noticed within 2 weeks, and normal kidney function with no hematuria or proteinuria at 6 months. This case highlights the aggressive nature of pediatric C3G after kidney transplantation and suggests that proximal complement inhibition may improve disease control and graft outcomes.

articles.title: Pediatric living-donor kidney transplantation in infants and low-weight children: what have we learned so far?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kidney transplantation (KTx) in low-weight (LW) children is technically demanding due to the size mismatch between adult-sized kidneys and small recipients. We evaluated the impact of recipient weight on surgical morbidity, perioperative recovery, and long-term graft outcomes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We analyzed 156 consecutive living-donor pediatric KTx between 2018 and 2025. Recipients were divided into three groups by body weight: Group 1 ( < 10 kg), Group 2 (10 to <15 kg), and Group 3 ( ≥ 15 kg). Primary outcomes were postoperative complications and postoperative length of stay. Graft and patient survival were analyzed among the groups.

RESULTS: Recipient weight was found to be the sole independent predictor of overall postoperative complication risk. However, in pre-specified exploratory analyses focusing on major complications, previous abdominal surgery also emerged as a significant risk factor. Recipient weight category and previous abdominal surgery were found to be independent predictors of hospital length of stay. No vascular or graft thrombosis was observed. At 1 year, death-censored graft and patient survival were 98.7% and 99.4%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Recipients weighing <15 kg, particularly the <10 kg group, experienced higher perioperative morbidity but can achieve excellent graft and patient survival with appropriate surgical adaptations and careful perioperative care. These findings support timely KTx at experienced centers rather than delaying transplantation solely to achieve strict weight thresholds.

articles.title: Neonatal kidney injury: diagnosis, management, and long-term kidney health - the perspective of the European Neonatal Nephrology Working Group.
authors: ESPN Working Group and ESPR Special Interest Group neonatal nephrology
articles.abstract: Advances in perinatal and neonatal care have improved the survival of preterm and intrauterine growth-restricted (IUGR) infants, yet these achievements bring underlit challenges, including kidney development and long-term renal health. Because nephrogenesis occurs largely before birth, preterm birth interrupts this process, resulting in reduced and structurally immature nephrons. These infants, as well as those exposed to adverse intrauterine environments such as malnutrition or preeclampsia, are predisposed to kidney vulnerability that extends into later life, increasing their risk for chronic kidney disease (CKD). Paediatric nephrologists and neonatologists from the Neonatal Nephrology Working Group (WG) of the European Society for Paediatric Nephrology (ESPN) and the Special Interest Group of the European Society for Paediatric Research (ESPR) collaborated to synthesize current evidence on risk factors, mechanisms, and management of kidney injury in neonates.Key findings highlight that neonatal acute kidney injury (AKI) remains difficult to diagnose using adult-derived criteria, as creatinine-based definitions fail to account for postnatal adaptation and fluid dynamics. AKI in neonates commonly arises from multifactorial causes (i.e., perinatal asphyxia, sepsis, patent ductus arteriosus, and/or exposure to nephrotoxic drugs) and often manifests through systemic consequences like fluid overload. Management emphasizes fluid and electrolyte optimization, cautious use of nephrotoxic agents, and individualized nutrition to support growth while minimizing metabolic derangements. Emerging neonatal-specific kidney replacement therapy technologies, including miniaturized and continuous circuits, expand therapeutic options but require further evaluation. Follow-up is warranted; nevertheless, current evidence is unable to provide an evidence-based strategy. This evaluation underscores the urgent need for integrative research, neonatal-specific diagnostic criteria, and evidence-based guidelines tailored to this vulnerable population. By bridging neonatology and nephrology, the newly established WG aims to foster multidisciplinary strategies that improve both short- and long-term kidney outcomes in preterm and critically ill newborns.

articles.title: Assessing caregiver knowledge level among families of children with chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is characterised by long-term decline in kidney function. Early detection and treatment may be associated with a delay in the progression of the disease. Increased awareness and knowledge of disease carries great importance. In this cross-sectional study, CKD knowledge level of the caregivers of paediatric patients with CKD was assessed.

METHODS: Caregivers of paediatric patients aged 1-21 years with stage 2-5 CKD who had not started kidney replacement therapy (KRT) and had at least 1-year follow-up were recruited. CKD knowledge levels were assessed using a questionnaire developed based on a review of the literature. Demographic features potentially associated with knowledge level, the impact of knowledge on the patients' prognosis and disease progression were investigated.

RESULTS: A total of 47 paediatric patients with CKD, with a mean age of 14 ± 3.9 years, along with their caregivers, were included. Average follow-up duration was 6.5 years. Mean eGFR at CKD diagnosis was 58.3 mL/min/1.73 m² (Stage 3a), and mean eGFR during study period was 39.5 mL/min/1.73 m² (Stage 3b). Mean score was 64.9 out of 100 on the questionnaire. Caregivers of patients with early-stage CKD (stages 2-3) had higher educational levels (p = 0.048); caregivers of patients diagnosed at advanced-stage CKD and caregivers with healthcare workers in their family demonstrated higher CKD knowledge levels (p = 0.048 and p = 0.020, respectively). Higher caregiver CKD knowledge levels were associated with reduced school absenteeism (p = 0.020) and better school performance (p = 0.008).

CONCLUSION: We believe that targeted educational interventions to improve caregivers' knowledge may contribute to better quality of the patient's life.

articles.title: Sustained hypokalemia and peritonitis rates in children undergoing peritoneal dialysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peritonitis is a major cause of technique failure and morbidity in children receiving peritoneal dialysis (PD). Identifying modifiable risk factors for infection is essential to improving outcomes in pediatric PD patients. Hypokalemia has been associated with peritonitis in adults receiving PD, but this relationship has not been evaluated in children.

METHODS: Forty-six pediatric dialysis centers within the Standardizing Care to Improve Outcomes in Pediatric End-Stage Kidney Disease (SCOPE) Collaborative contributed prospective data of children receiving maintenance PD between April 1, 2016, and July 31, 2024. Patients with three or more months of potassium measurements were included. Sustained hypokalemia was defined as a potassium level of 3.5 mmol/L or lower for at least two out of three consecutive months. Generalized linear models were used to evaluate annualized peritonitis rates between those patients with sustained hypokalemia and those without. Among individuals with sustained hypokalemia, generalized linear models were used for intra-individual comparisons between periods of sustained hypokalemia and periods without.

RESULTS: There were 437 patients (37%) with sustained hypokalemia and 749 without in the cohort. The peritonitis rate during sustained hypokalemia was not different from the rate in those without (rate ratio (RR) 1.07, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.80-1.44). In patients with sustained hypokalemia, the annualized peritonitis rate was similar between months when they had sustained hypokalemia and months without hypokalemia (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.72-1.33).

CONCLUSIONS: Hypokalemia was common among children undergoing PD. However, it was not found to be associated with an increased rate of peritonitis.

articles.title: Infection with Tritrichomonas muris in BALB/c mice: pathogenicity and antibody response.
MRI features of symptomatic progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy: a prospective cohort study using a standardized multisequence 3T MRI protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) is an opportunistic infection of the brain caused by the JC polyomavirus (JCPyV). Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the most sensitive imaging modality for the in vivo detection of PML. However, comprehensive data on imaging findings using standardized multisequence MRI protocols are limited.

OBJECTIVE: To systematically characterize MRI findings of clinically active PML in a large, prospectively collected cohort using a comprehensive and standardized MRI protocol.

METHODS: Eighty patients with active PML underwent standardized 3T brain MRI including 3D T2w-fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR), 3D T1w, T2w, diffusion-weighted (DWI), susceptibility-weighted (SWI) and contrast-enhanced T1w sequences. Lesions were analysed for dissemination, location, morphology, borders, and signal characteristics.

RESULTS: Most patients showed widespread (90%) and bilateral (93%) involvement. The frontal (91%) and parieto-occipital (93%) lobes were most frequently affected, with lesions typically involving the juxtacortical (95%) and deep white matter (99%), but also frequently extending into the cortical grey matter (94%) and deep grey matter (71%). Most patients showed large (> 3 cm, 89%), focal (99%), T2w-hyperintense (100%) and T1w-hypointense (99%) lesions with ill-defined borders (79%). DWI hyperintensity was present in 90% of patients, while hypointense (sub)cortical bands on SWI were detected in 61%. Contrast enhancement was observed in 55% of patients. Additional characteristic imaging features included the punctate pattern (76%) and the shrimp sign (20%).

CONCLUSIONS: PML exhibits characteristic but heterogeneous MRI findings at the patient level, predominantly characterized by widespread white matter involvement with frequent cortical grey matter involvement. DWI and SWI frequently reveal additional characteristic imaging features that may aid in the identification and characterization of PML lesions. Our data support the use of standardized, comprehensive multisequence imaging protocols for consistent detection and phenotyping of PML across diverse immunosuppressive conditions.

articles.title: Preprocedural angiographic difference in cerebral circulation time and clinical outcomes after successful reperfusion for middle cerebral artery occlusion.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate whether the affected-to-contralateral difference in cerebral circulation time (ΔCCT) on preprocedural digital subtraction angiography is associated with early neurological and 90-day functional outcomes after endovascular treatment (EVT) and successful reperfusion.

METHODS: Patients with acute M1 or non-distal M2 middle cerebral artery occlusion who underwent EVT and achieved successful reperfusion (mTICI ≥2b) were retrospectively included. Semi-automatically measured ΔCCT was evaluated in relation to the primary outcome of 24-hour National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) improvement and the exploratory outcomes of early neurological deterioration (END) and a 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score ≥ 3. Models were adjusted for age, sex, baseline NIHSS score, collateral status, and occlusion location.

RESULTS: Among 132 patients, the median ΔCCT was 1.31 s (IQR, 0.97-1.67 s). Each 1-standard-deviation increase in ΔCCT was associated with 3.39 points less 24-hour NIHSS improvement (adjusted β = -3.39, 95% confidence interval [CI] -4.79 to -1.98; P < 0.001), higher odds of END (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 3.11, 95% CI 1.92-5.42; P < 0.001), and higher odds of a 90-day mRS score ≥ 3 (aOR 1.58, 95% CI 1.06-2.41; P = 0.028).

CONCLUSION: Among patients with M1 or non-distal M2 occlusion who achieved successful reperfusion, a longer pre-EVT ΔCCT was associated with less early neurological improvement and, in exploratory analyses, higher odds of END and an unfavorable 90-day outcome. Its generalizability to broader EVT populations requires further evaluation.

articles.title: Guiding Inpatient Glycemic Management with Continuous Glucose Monitoring. A Prospective Nonrandomized Comparative Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Diabetes therapy : research, treatment and education of diabetes and related disorders
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) is a cornerstone of ambulatory diabetes management, and its utility in the inpatient setting remains underexplored. This study evaluated a CGM-guided management strategy against point-of-care capillary blood glucose (CBG) monitoring in adults who were hospitalized with hyperglycemia.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective, nonrandomized comparative cohort study, reported according to the Strengthening the Reporting of OBservational studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) statement, at a national referral center in Mexico City. A total of 338 adult inpatients with hyperglycemia were allocated to either the CGM group (n = 169) or the standard CBG monitoring group(n = 169). The primary outcome was the percentage of glucose readings between 70 and 180 mg/dL, measured with intermittently scanned CGM in the CGM group and with a four-point daily capillary schedule at 06:00, 12:00, 18:00, and 24:00 in the CBG group.

RESULTS: The capillary schedule yielded 6123 of 7024 scheduled measurements (87.2% capture), including 1431 at 24:00. Readings in range averaged 54.9% by CGM and 57.8% by CBG, based on approximately 96 and 4 daily measurements per patient, respectively. CBG at 24:00 was 27.0 mg/dL lower than the same patient daytime mean (95% CI, 20.9-33.0 lower; p < 0.001), with 79.2% of midnight readings in range versus 52.4% during the day. Hypoglycemia was distributed across the whole day, with 19.9% of CBG readings below 70 mg/dL recorded at 24:00, and seven patients had hypoglycemia detected only overnight. Time below 70 mg/dL was 10.5% by CGM and 5.6% by CBG; whereas, below 54 mg/dL was 3.7% and 1.4%, respectively. Mean glucose and the coefficient of variation improved from the first to the second half of hospitalization in both groups.

CONCLUSIONS: The two groups recorded a similar percentage of readings in range, however, the sensor detected hypoglycemia twice as often. One in five capillary readings below 70 mg/dL was recorded at 24:00, and a daytime-only schedule would have missed all of them, as well as the hypoglycemia documented overnight in seven patients.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT05096858. Enrollment began on 13 April 2020 and the record was first posted on 27 October 2021, hence, the study was in part retrospectively registered.

articles.title: Surgical outcomes and functional morbidity after retrosigmoid/retrocondylar and midline suboccipital approaches for foramen magnum meningiomas: a single-arm meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Foramen magnum meningiomas (FMMs) are surgically challenging due to their proximity to the cervicomedullary junction, lower cranial nerves, and vertebrobasilar circulation. Although far-lateral transcondylar approaches are commonly used for ventral lesions, less extensive posterior/posterolateral corridors are increasingly employed. We performed a single-arm meta-analysis to quantify oncologic control and functional morbidity following retrosigmoid/retrocondylar and midline suboccipital approaches for FMMs. A PRISMA-guided systematic review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception through July 2025 (last search 31 July 2025). Eligible studies were original clinical case series with ≥ 5 patients (all eligible series proved retrospective) reporting FMM resection via posterior midline suboccipital or lateral/posterolateral suboccipital corridors, including retrosigmoid/retrocondylar approaches with limited condyle drilling ≤ 1/3 when performed. Studies with nonseparable outcomes from more extensive transcondylar/far-lateral approaches were excluded. Pooled proportions were calculated using a random-effects model with Freeman-Tukey transformation and reported with 95% confidence intervals. Seven retrospective case series from 1997 to 2019 contributing 133 eligible patients were included; one series was restricted to its 34 intradural cases operated through eligible corridors. Weighted mean age was 54.4 years, 75.2% (100/133) were female, and sample-size-weighted mean follow-up was 58 months. Retrosigmoid/retrocondylar corridors were used in 74/133 patients (55.6%) and midline suboccipital craniectomy in 59/133 (44.4%), often with C1 laminectomy. Dedicated retrosigmoid/retrocondylar series included predominantly anterior/anterolateral tumors, whereas midline series included mixed attachments. Formal approach-specific comparisons were limited by heterogeneous reporting. When performed, condyle drilling was generally limited to the posterior one-third; no postoperative craniocervical instability or fusion was reported. Pooled gross total resection was 91% (95% CI: 84-96%; 119/133 patients, 7 studies), recurrence was rare (3/133, 2.3%; pooled 1%, 95% CI: 0-4%), and long-term functional independence was 83% (95% CI: 71-93%; 60/74 patients, 5 studies). New cranial nerve deficits, transient or permanent, occurred in 21% (95% CI: 13-30%; 22/99 patients, 6 studies), cerebrospinal fluid leak in 12% (95% CI: 6-20%; 13/99, 6 studies), and perioperative mortality in 3% (95% CI: 0-9%; 7/133, 7 studies), with two additional late deaths from aspiration pneumonia during follow-up. Taken together, retrosigmoid/retrocondylar and midline suboccipital approaches for FMMs achieve high resection rates, low recurrence, and favorable long-term function, often without extensive condylectomy. These pooled estimates represent a combined figure across two anatomically distinct corridors applied to topographically different tumors (retrosigmoid/retrocondylar routes predominantly for anterior/anterolateral lesions and midline suboccipital exposure predominantly for posterior/posterolateral lesions), and do not imply that the approaches are interchangeable. Cranial nerve morbidity, cerebrospinal fluid leak, and perioperative mortality remain important considerations.

[Correction: Perimenopause and postmenopause: acute diagnostic and therapeutic aspects for the DACH region : Consensus paper of the Austrian Society for Gynecology and Obstetrics (OEGGG), the German Society for Gynecology and Obstetrics (DGGG) and the Swiss Society for Gynecology and Obstetrics (SGGG)].
Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs) for Targeted Drug Delivery: A Review of Design-to-Release Correlations.
articles.journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are crystalline porous materials that consist of adjustable metal nodes and organic linkers. These properties enable MOFs to act as effective vehicles for drug delivery when designed to control the breakdown or opening of the framework upon receiving a trigger, such as a biological or chemical stimulus [1, 2, 3, 4]. Even though the latest advances in research into MOFs have expanded the literature, the published information on the correlation of the factors concerning the design of MOFs (the type of metal node and linker used, the size of the particles, and surface treatment) with the process of the release of drugs has not been conducted to the fullest extent.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to conduct a systematic review of the (i) synthesis and physico-chemical characterization methods applied to the development of stimuli-responsive MOFs used for targeted drug delivery and of the (ii) design-to-release relationships that govern the use of pH, redox, light, temperature, and enzymatic triggers.

METHODS: The review follows PRISMA 2020 [5]. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect were searched for English-language primary research published during 2014-2025. Two reviewers screened records and extracted information on MOF identity, synthesis, characterisation, loading, release and biological outcomes. Complete screening, extraction and appraisal records are unavailable for independent verification. The present synthesis is qualitative; selected numerical observations are attributed to individual studies, without pooled estimates or cross-study regression. pH-, redox-, light-, temperature- and enzyme-responsive systems illustrate the diversity of MOF-based delivery. ZIF-8, MIL-family, UiO-66 and porphyrinic carriers offer different loading and release strategies. Loading capacity, particle size and surface modification influence performance, but comparisons depend on cargo, formulation and assay conditions. The available documentation does not support a pooled release ratio, a BET-loading regression, or a universal size optimum. Animal studies were appraised with SYRCLE [6].

articles.title: A literature scanning and prioritization framework to guide future systematic reviews for world cancer research fund international's global cancer update programme.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The 2018 World Cancer Research Fund (WCRF)/American Institute for Cancer Research Third Expert Report (TER) on diet, adiposity, physical activity, and risk of 19 cancers could be enhanced with new data. A framework is needed to prioritize future systematic reviews.

METHODS: We searched PubMed (January 2019-February 2024) for meta-analyses, pooled analyses, randomized controlled trials (RCTs), Mendelian randomization (MR) studies, and large (> 100,000 participants) cohort studies. We assessed TER findings using conditional power (CP) and fail-safe number (FSN) statistics. We developed an exposure-based prioritization score (PS) by awarding or subtracting points considering the quantity, statistical significance, direction, and novelty of associations.

RESULTS: We compared 366 meta-analyses, 121 pooled analyses, 19 RCTs, 174 MR studies, and 391 cohort studies covering 151 exposures and 28 cancers with 1,371 TER meta-analyses. Based on CP, nonsignificant TER associations likely to become significant with additional evidence included folate and colorectal, waist circumference and lung, total fat and ovarian, tea and ovarian, and red meat and kidney cancers. The FSN indicated that most significant TER associations are unlikely to change with additional evidence. The median PS was 6 (range: - 15 to 163), with top scores observed for anthropometric measurements (PSheight=40 to PSBMI=163), physical activity (PS=100), sedentary behavior (PS=64), alcohol (PS=52), tea (PS=36), dietary fiber (PS=31), milk/dairy (PS=29), micronutrients (PSretinol=27 to PSiron=38), vitamins (PSB12=22 to PSvitD=91), soy (PS=24), isoflavones (PS=23), and sugar-sweetened beverages (PS=22).

CONCLUSION: The prioritization framework can help identify impactful systematic reviews to complement TER conclusions and enhance our understanding of emerging research.

articles.title: Multiorgan [18F]florbetapir PET/CT uptake in multiple myeloma-associated systemic AL amyloidosis: a case report.
articles.abstract: [18F]florbetapir (AV-45) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) is emerging as a tool for noninvasive amyloid imaging. In this case report, we describe [18F]florbetapir PET/CT findings in a 77-year-old male patient with multiple myeloma (MM) and suspected AL amyloidosis. A whole-body PET/CT scan was performed to assess tracer uptake across multiple organs, and the imaging findings were correlated with bone marrow examination and biopsy results. The scan revealed prominent [18F]florbetapir retention in the myocardium, thyroid, lungs, parotid glands, tongue, gastric wall, and various muscle groups. The imaging findings were interpreted alongside hematologic findings and gastrointestinal biopsy evidence in the assessment of systemic AL amyloidosis associated with MM. Our findings suggest that [18F]florbetapir PET/CT may help visualize the distribution of tracer uptake without establishing amyloid deposition at each uptake-positive site. Diagnostic accuracy and clinical utility require evaluation beyond this single case.

articles.title: Pre-operative stereotactic radiosurgery versus intraoperative cesium-131 brachytherapy for resected brain metastases: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pre-operative stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) and intraoperative cesium-131 (Cs-131) brachytherapy are alternatives to post-operative SRS for resected brain metastases (BMs). The randomized phase 3 Radiation One and Done Study (ROADS; NCT04365374) showed improved surgical-bed control with Cs-131 tiles versus post-operative stereotactic radiotherapy, but outcomes relative to pre-operative SRS are undefined.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and ScienceDirect were searched through October 2026 (PRISMA 2020); one further trial was identified by other methods. Twelve-month local control (LC), leptomeningeal disease (LMD), radiation necrosis (RN), and overall survival (OS) were extracted for treatment-naïve BMs. Proportions were pooled with random-effects generalized linear mixed models and compared with a test for subgroup differences; sensitivity analyses included meta-regression, Hartung-Knapp, leave-one-out, follow-up, and fractionation analyses.

RESULTS: Fifteen pre-operative SRS studies (918 patients/940 BMs) and four brachytherapy studies (207 patients/217 BMs) were included. Pooled 12-month LC was 97% (95% CI 90-99) with Cs-131 brachytherapy and 90% (86-93) with pre-operative SRS (test for subgroup differences p = 0.054; meta-regression p = 0.019; Hartung-Knapp p = 0.066); among studies reporting observed counts, LC was 99% vs. 90% (p = 0.009). Within pre-operative SRS, LC was 96% after hypofractionated and 86% after single-fraction treatment (p = 0.005). LMD (9.1% vs. 5.1%) and RN (0.7% vs. 5.2%) did not differ significantly. Median OS was 15.6 months with brachytherapy (range 5.9-42.5; 11.0 months, range 5.9-20.1, excluding the ROADS estimate) and 14.4 months with pre-operative SRS (range 6.3-26.4).

CONCLUSION: Both approaches achieved high LC with low rates of LMD and RN. There was a trend towards higher LC with Cs-131 brachytherapy than with pre-operative SRS (97% vs. 90%; p = 0.054), and significantly so among studies reporting observed counts (99% vs. 90%; p = 0.009). Hypofractionated pre-operative SRS achieved LC similar to that of brachytherapy, suggesting that the difference may reflect single-fraction dose de-escalation rather than an intrinsic advantage of either modality. The two techniques may serve complementary roles, and prospective comparative study is warranted.

REGISTRATION: This review was not registered in PROSPERO.

articles.title: Preprocedural transesophageal echocardiography before cardioversion in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy-associated atrial fibrillation and thromboembolic risk: A follow-up, granular study.
293-Day Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump Support as a Bridge to Transplantation in Refractory Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) is widely used as temporary mechanical circulatory support in patients with refractory heart failure complicated by cardiogenic shock. However, its use is generally limited to short-term therapy because of device-related complications.

CASE SUMMARY: A 57-year-old man with idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy receiving guideline-directed medical therapy and cardiac resynchronization therapy with defibrillation developed cardiogenic shock refractory to inotropic therapy, requiring IABP implantation. Mechanical circulatory support was maintained for 293 days, including 291 days as a bridge to heart transplantation and 2 days after transplantation.

DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates that prolonged IABP support is feasible when combined with transition to a left subclavian approach, serial device replacement, and meticulous multidisciplinary management.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: In carefully selected patients, prolonged IABP support, combined with individualized device management and multidisciplinary care, may provide sustained clinical stabilization and serve as an effective bridge to heart transplantation.

articles.title: Kinetics of Re-differentiation with Short-Course Dabrafenib and Trametinib in Patients with Radioiodine-Refractory Thyroid Cancer.
articles.journal: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: MAPK pathway activation suppresses iodine-handling genes, including sodium-iodide symporter (NIS), contributing to loss of iodine avidity in radioiodine-refractory thyroid cancer. Prior BRAF/ MEK inhibitor re-differentiation trials improved iodine uptake but used empiric 4-6 week treatment. The timing of maximal NIS re-expression remains undefined. We evaluated whether short course dabrafenib plus trametinib restores iodine uptake and provides clinical benefit.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this multicentre phase II trial, patients with progressive metastatic radioiodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma harbouring BRAFV600E or RAS mutations received dabrafenib and trametinib. I-124 PET/CT dosimetry was performed at baseline and after 2 weeks, with repeat imaging at week 4 post therapy if dosimetry criteria was not met. Radioiodine was administered once criteria was met. The primary endpoint was attainment of predicted lesional absorbed dose ≥20 Gy with I-131 activity ≤300 mCi. Secondary endpoints included RECIST response, progression-free survival (PFS), thyroglobulin response, and safety.

RESULTS: Nine of 14 patients (64%) met the dosimetry criteria and received radioiodine; 6 out of 9 (67%) restored iodine uptake within 2 weeks. Among radioiodine-treated patients, best objective response rate within 6 months was 75% by RECIST. Median PFS was 10.8 months. RAS-mutant tumours demonstrated greater lesion regression than BRAFV600E-mutant tumours. Early reduction in stimulated thyroglobulin and preserved FOXE1 nuclear localisation, and higher tumour-to-normal GLIS3 nuclear expression were associated with re-differentiation response.

CONCLUSIONS: Short-course dabrafenib/ trametinib can induce rapid re-differentiation within 2 weeks in a subset of patients with MAPK-driven radioiodine-refractory thyroid cancer, supporting individualized BRAF/MEK inhibition duration rather than empiric prolonged treatment.

articles.title: Multimodal LFIA platform integrating visual readout, smartphone grayscale imaging and surface-enhanced Raman scattering for point-of-care detection of SARS-CoV-2 protein.
articles.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
articles.abstract: Rapid, simple, and sensitive antigen detection remains important for point-of-care screening and respiratory infection surveillance. Conventional lateral flow immunoassays (LFIAs) enable rapid visual testing, but their sensitivity is often limited for low-abundance viral antigens. Herein, we developed a multimodal LFIA platform for SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (N) protein detection in simulated saliva. The platform integrates three complementary readout modes on a single strip: naked-eye visual observation for rapid qualitative screening, smartphone grayscale imaging for digital recording and semi-quantitative comparison of test-line color intensity, and surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) measurement for sensitive spectral quantification. Citrate-capped gold nanoparticles were labeled with 4-mercaptobenzoic acid and conjugated with anti-SARS-CoV-2 N protein detection antibodies to construct Raman-active immunoprobes. The calculated analytical limit of detection (LOD) was 5.2 pg mL-1, whereas 50 pg mL-1 was the lowest experimentally tested concentration that produced a clearly distinguishable SERS response. The lowest experimentally distinguishable concentration for smartphone grayscale analysis was 160 pg mL-1. The naked-eye visual threshold was approximately 200 pg mL-1. In simulated saliva samples, recoveries ranged from 87.70% to 103.70%, with relative standard deviations of 4.8-7.1%. These results demonstrate that the proposed multimodal LFIA strategy preserves the simplicity of conventional strips while enabling digital interpretation and sensitive low-concentration antigen detection in saliva-like matrices.

articles.title: Multifunctional Cross-Linked Micelles for the Treatment of Acute Pneumonia Caused by MDR-KP with Reduced Cytokine Storms and Restored Metabolism and Immune Balance.
articles.abstract: Acute pneumonia caused by multidrug-resistant superbugs such as Klebsiella pneumoniae (MDR-KP) poses a severe public health threat for clinical patients with high mortality rate, where excessive cytokine storms and cellular dysfunction are the leading causes of death. More seriously, these superbugs have evolved specialized biological mechanisms that allow them to persist long-term within macrophages, rendering antibiotics and immunomodulators ineffective. Herein, a smart and multifunctional nanomicelle (NAC151-micelle), composed of colistin-NAD+-crosslinked drug and inhibitor H151, is developed for cooperatively killing of MDR-KP bacteria, alleviating hyperinflammatory cytokine storm, and improving metabolism and immune balance. NAC151-micelles optimized through in vitro bactericidal assays can smartly be responsive to the highly reduced environment within infected macrophages, allowing rapid release of active cargoes, including colistin and NAD+, thereby achieving efficient clearance of extra- and intracellular MDR-KP while improving cellular energy metabolism. Meanwhile, co-loaded H151 can cooperatively downregulate key inflammatory pathways of STING-TBK1-IRF3 and NF-κB p65 phosphorylation in macrophages with NAD+, reducing a cytokine storm. In MDR-KP-induced acute pneumonia infection, following intranasal tracheal administration, we observe a targeted accumulation in lung and significant downregulation of MDR-KP burden, together with drastically decreased cytokine storms with good safety. Furthermore, the immune balance in the lung is also greatly improved; pathological tissue injury is effectively repaired; and notably, functional macrophages are essential mediators of their therapeutic efficacy. Collectively, our study presents a safe and multifunctional therapeutic strategy (NAC151-micelles) for acute pneumonia caused by super-bacteria MDR-KP with rapid bacterial clearance, reduced cytokine storms, and improved metabolism and immune balance.

articles.title: Mycoplasma pneumoniae CARDS toxin hijacks annexin A2 to enhance clathrin-mediated endocytosis and induce a cytopathic effect.
articles.abstract: Mycoplasma pneumoniae is a primary cause of bacterial community-acquired pneumonia. One of its key virulence factors, the community-acquired respiratory distress syndrome (CARDS) toxin, replicates most clinical symptoms of the infection. Although CARDS toxin exhibits multi-receptor binding affinity, the mechanisms governing its cellular entry remain poorly understood. In this study, we characterized the toxin entry pathway mediated by the host protein annexin A2 (AnxA2). Using flow cytometry and biotinylated membrane protein analysis, we demonstrate that CARDS toxin induces a rapid, transient translocation of AnxA2 to the plasma membrane, peaking at 15 min post-exposure. This recruitment occurs via a phosphorylation-independent mechanism, distinguishing it from the Src-dependent recruitment typically observed in other physiological contexts. Co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) of the clathrin heavy chain revealed an enhanced AnxA2-clathrin association that accelerates clathrin-mediated endocytosis of toxin. Endosomal fractionation, immunofluorescence, and co-IP studies confirmed the time-dependent co-localization and physical interaction of CARDS toxin with AnxA2 within early endosomes. Furthermore, CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of AnxA2 in A549 cells demonstrated that this protein is essential for the internalization of CARDS toxin; its absence not only reduces the toxin binding but also effectively impairs the rapid cellular uptake required to trigger the downstream cytopathic effects and vacuolation. These results establish that CARDS toxin modulates host surface remodeling through AnxA2 cell surface translocation to facilitate efficient cellular entry, identifying a rate-limiting step in M. pneumoniae pathogenesis.

articles.title: Deficiency in vitamin B12 biosynthesis and propionate catabolism impairs anaerobic growth of Salmonella Dublin on ethanolamine and 1,2-propanediol.
articles.abstract: Salmonella enterica serovar Dublin is primarily adapted to cattle, and although rarely isolated from humans, infections are often associated with systemically invasive disease. In contrast, the closely related serovar Enteritidis exhibits a broad host range, is highly prevalent in humans, and typically causes self-limiting gastroenteritis. Serovar Typhimurium, which also usually causes localized gastroenteritis, can exploit intestinal compounds such as ethanolamine and 1,2-propanediol to support anaerobic respiration in the inflamed gut, using tetrathionate as an electron acceptor. Genes involved in anaerobic metabolism are frequently degraded in serovars associated with systemic infection. Interestingly, despite its high systemic invasiveness, S. Dublin retains most of these genes, including those required for ethanolamine and 1,2-propanediol utilization. In this study, we compared the growth of S. Dublin and S. Enteritidis clinical isolates under anaerobic conditions with ethanolamine or 1,2-propanediol as sole carbon sources, and their ability to colonize the intestine and trigger inflammation in mice. S. Dublin failed to utilize either compound in minimal medium supplemented with tetrathionate. The defect in ethanolamine catabolism was linked to a deficiency in the cobalamin biosynthesis pathway, as supplementation restored function. In contrast, impairment of 1,2-propanediol metabolism involved not only cobalamin deficiency but also mutations in the propionate degradation pathway. In mice, S. Dublin elicited weaker inflammatory responses and lower intestinal colonization compared to S. Enteritidis. These findings reveal metabolic deficiencies in S. Dublin not predicted by genomic analyses and suggest gene silencing of functions relevant for intestinal colonization but dispensable for systemic growth, representing a possible intermediate stage toward an extraintestinal lifestyle.

articles.title: "Does age during cleft palate closure have an impact on postoperative complications? A randomized trial".
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal timing of cleft palate closure remains debated, balancing potential benefits for speech and hearing against risks of postoperative complications and long-term effects. Current Dutch guidelines recommend closure before 12 months, but some studies suggest earlier repair at 6-8 months may improve functional outcomes.

METHODS: We conducted a randomized cohort study of 82 children with cleft lip and palate or isolated cleft palate, allocated to early (6-8 months) or late (10-12 months) palatal closure. Primary outcomes were intra- and postoperative complications, including bleeding, infection, dehiscence, and oronasal fistula. Secondary outcomes included operative time, hospital stay, and associations between patient characteristics and outcomes.

RESULTS: Eighty patients were analyzed (43 early, 37 late). Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. The mean operative time was shorter in the early group (p = 0.005), while hospital stay was similar. No intraoperative complications or blood transfusions occurred. Postoperative infection was rare (2.3% in the early group vs. 5.4% in the late group). Wound healing problems occurred in 14 patients (32.6%) in the early group and 14 patients (37.8%) in the late group (p = 0.479). Within this category, wound dehiscence was observed in 6 patients (13.9%) in the early group and 4 patients (10.8%) in the late group (p = 0.485). All wounds had spontaneously healed by the 3-month follow-up. During follow-up, fistula formation was observed in 7 patients (16.3%) in the early group and 10 patients (27.0%) in the late group (p = 0.281). Four patients (9.3%) in the early group and three patients (8.1%) in the late group required symptomatic fistula repair before age 3 years (p = 0.350). No significant differences were found between the groups. Subsequently three patients in the early group had fistula surgery combined with VPI surgery at an average age of 56 months and seven patients in the late group at an average of 61 months. Importantly, cleft width was significantly reduced following vomer flap closure (p < 0.001). Moreover, greater initial cleft width independently predicted fistula development (p = 0.048).

CONCLUSION: Early palatal closure at 6-8 months is safe and does not increase short-term complications compared to closure at 10-12 months. Operative time was reduced in the early closure group, and a vomer flap effectively narrowed cleft width. As the initial cleft width prior to surgery was a predictor of fistula formation, reducing width may contribute to improved outcomes. Larger, multicenter studies are needed to confirm safety and assess long-term speech, hearing, and maxillary growth outcomes.

articles.title: Beyond association: pathogenesis models reveal ecological drivers of vaginal dysbiosis.
articles.abstract: Despite its critical importance to health, our understanding of the vaginal microbiome lags far behind other mucosal sites, reflecting both the distinct biology of the human vaginal microenvironment and the historic neglect of women's reproductive health in biomedical research. Recent investment in this area, coupled with the widespread use of high-throughput omics technologies, has greatly expanded our understanding of vaginal microbiota states and their associations with health and disease. However, associative studies that correlate community composition with clinical outcomes are limited in their ability to define causal, modifiable host-microbe relationships that support a protective microbiota. Consequently, broad probiotic strategies based on descriptive findings show limited success in restoring lasting homeostasis in the female reproductive tract. Murine infection models provide tractable systems for identifying evolutionarily conserved physiological processes that influence microbial growth. Here, we highlight studies across pathogenesis fields that leverage murine models to identify ecological factors controlling infection susceptibility in the vaginal microenvironment. Rather than treating pathogen colonization as an endpoint alone, we emphasize how genetically tractable microbes reveal the resources, barriers, and immune responses mediating microbial persistence, ascension, and inflammation. Where possible, we integrate these findings with clinical observations to assess their relevance to human reproductive health. Together, these studies illustrate how imperfect but tractable models reveal causal drivers of vaginal dysbiosis in women and help ground large-scale associative studies in a more clinically relevant way.

articles.title: Predictors of 30-day post endoscopic variceal band ligation bleed: a prospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute esophageal variceal bleeding (AVB) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with cirrhosis. Endoscopic variceal ligation (EVL) is the standard of care for achieving hemostasis; however, post-EVL bleeding remains a serious and potentially fatal complication. Data on reliable predictors of post-EVL rebleeding is heterogeneous. This prospective study aimed to identify the predictors of post-EVL rebleeding in patients undergoing EVL for acute esophageal variceal hemorrhage.

METHODS: This prospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary academic referral center in Southern India over a 12-month period. Patients were enrolled following preset inclusion and exclusion criteria. Standardized medical therapy, in accordance with institutional protocols, was offered to all enrolled patients, and all patients were followed up after discharge. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of 30-day rebleeding after index EVL. Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) score was identified as a significant predictor, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis determined an optimal cut-off value that predicted post-EVL bleeding. Paired analysis was performed to identify the short-term changes in laboratory and endoscopic parameters before and after the endoscopy.

RESULTS: A total of 150 patients were enrolled in the study; alcohol was the predominant etiology for cirrhosis. Thirty-day rebleeding after index EVL occurred in 12 patients (8%). In univariate analysis, platelet count, International Normalized Ratio (INR), total bilirubin, MELD score, and Child-Pugh class were significantly associated with post-index-EVL rebleed. In multivariate analysis, the MELD score was the only independent predictor (adjusted OR, 899; 95% CI, 1.300-2.774; P<0.001). ROC analysis demonstrated predictive performance for MELD with an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.970. A MELD cut-off score of ≥11.5 provided excellent sensitivity and specificity for predicting post-index EVL bleed. Although owing to the heterogeneous nature of the bleed and parsimonious nature of the multiple regression model, these findings are considered exploratory and need external validation. Procedural factors, including timing of endoscopy, number of bands deployed, variceal grade, portal hypertensive gastropathy, and proceduralist experience, were not associated with 30-day rebleeding after index EVL.

CONCLUSIONS: In this prospective single-center cohort, 30-day rebleeding after successful index EVL occurred in 8% of patients. MELD score was the only independent predictor identified in the multivariable model, and a MELD threshold of ≥11.5 showed high discriminatory performance in this derivation cohort. However, the small number of rebleeding events, heterogeneous bleeding sources, and absence of external validation limit the generalizability of this threshold. Larger studies are needed to validate MELD-based risk stratification after EVL. MELD-based risk stratification may help identify patients who require closer post-EVL surveillance. Further large-scale studies are needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: The Post-Sepsis Neutrophil: Lymphocyte Ratio: A Population Signal in Search of Individual Meaning.
Association Between the Neutrophil:Lymphocyte Ratio After Hospitalization for Sepsis and Long-Term Outcomes: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Long-term outcomes after sepsis survival remain poor. No clinical laboratory tests are in use for stratifying long-term risk after sepsis, limiting the development of secondary prevention. The peripheral blood neutrophil:lymphocyte ratio (NLR) reflects innate and adaptive immune cell balance, and may reflect an immune milieu which is associated with long-term risk after sepsis. Accordingly, we evaluated the association between the NLR in the weeks after sepsis hospitalization discharge-a time when patients are routinely seen in post-ICU clinics-and long-term outcomes.

DESIGN: Population-based cohort study.

SETTING: Ontario, Canada, 2010-2020.

PATIENTS: Adults discharged alive from a sepsis hospitalization.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The exposure was the first outpatient NLR-derived from the complete blood count-measured 15-90 days after sepsis discharge. Among 37,250 survivors with available NLR, the median (interquartile range [IQR]) time-to-measurement was 34 days (22-54 d), and the median NLR was 2.7 (1.8-4.2). Within 1 year, 17,732 patients (47.6%) were rehospitalized or died (median [IQR] time-to-event, 82 d [27-185 d]). The frequency of rehospitalization or death increased across increasing NLR quartiles: 34.2%, 41.5%, 50.3%, and 64.4% (ptrend < 0.001). Compared with the lowest quartile, adjusted hazard ratios (95% CI) were 1.24 (1.18-1.29), 1.54 (1.48-1.62), and 2.25 (2.15-2.35) across higher quartiles. For most patients, NLR after sepsis returned to its patient-specific presepsis ambient level, which was itself prognostic.

CONCLUSIONS: Among sepsis survivors, outpatient NLR measured 15-90 days after discharge is strongly associated with 1-year risk of rehospitalization or death. As a simple, widely available biomarker, the NLR may support early postsepsis risk stratification and inform development of secondary prevention strategies.

articles.title: A Multifunctional Chitosan-Based Hydrogel for Sustained Support throughout Wound Healing.
articles.abstract: Effective wound management requires dressings that can maintain a moist environment, prevent infection, mitigate oxidative stress, and accommodate dynamic skin movements. However, conventional hydrogel dressings are often limited by insufficient mechanical flexibility and limited multifunctionality. To overcome these limitations, we designed a multifunctional chitosan-based hydrogel wound dressing through sequential modification with lysine and gallic acid. The incorporation of lysine enhanced the amino group density, which improved the antibacterial efficacy of the CLG hydrogel, while gallic acid introduced potent antioxidant activity and mussel-inspired adhesion capabilities. The CLG hydrogel also demonstrates a high swelling ratio, which enables efficient absorption of wound exudate. In vivo evaluations confirmed accelerated wound closure, enhanced collagen deposition, and stimulated angiogenesis. These properties enable the CLG hydrogel to provide sustained protection and multifunctional support throughout the different phases of wound healing, highlighting its potential for translational applications in advanced wound care.

articles.title: Ensemble-Based Segmental Helical Organization in an Aib-Rich Lipidated Peptide: Biomacromolecular Insights from High-Field NMR.
articles.abstract: Tirzepatide (TZP) is a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist that has demonstrated remarkable therapeutic efficacy for the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. Despite its clinical importance, residue-specific information on its solution conformation remains limited due to its structural complexity, including noncanonical amino acids and a lipidated side chain. In this study, we performed a solution NMR investigation of tirzepatide to establish residue-specific resonance assignments and characterize its conformational properties in an aqueous solution. Backbone and side-chain resonances were assigned using multidimensional NMR spectroscopy, including 1H-15N HMQC, TOCSY, and NOESY experiments. Reliable sequential NOE connectivities were identified for several peptide segments, while ambiguous and unresolved resonances were conservatively excluded from the structural interpretation. The N-terminal Aib2 residue served as an important assignment anchor but did not define a stable terminal structure. In contrast, the Aib13 region exhibited a locally organized backbone environment with a short helical-like conformational tendency, suggesting Aib13-centered local ordering within the peptide chain. Structure calculations based on the 1.2 GHz NMR and CD experiments revealed that tirzepatide does not adopt a single rigid conformation in solution but instead exists as a conformational ensemble composed of locally ordered and flexible regions. These findings provide a residue-specific view of tirzepatide dynamics in solution and offer structural insights into the conformational landscape of this therapeutically important peptide.

articles.title: A Bacterial Extracellular Matrix Protein Forms a Supramolecular Metallogel.
articles.abstract: The microbial extracellular matrix (ECM) is a complex network of self-secreted biopolymers that unite cells in biofilms, providing them with structural integrity and protection from antimicrobials. Made of fibrillar proteins interspersed with polysaccharides, ECM material is often implicitly held responsible for biofilms' hydrogel-like mechanical signature; the exact molecular mechanisms of the ECM assembly and their link to hydrogel formation, however, remain enigmatic. Here, we discover that in the presence of zinc ions, TasA, the major ECM protein of Bacillus subtilis, forms hydrogels that recapitulate the mechanical properties of whole biofilms. Electron and atomic force microscopies as well as small-angle X-ray scattering showed that cross-linking with zinc ions induced a transition in the TasA architecture from one-dimensional fibers to two-dimensional nanosheets. Electron paramagnetic resonance and X-ray diffraction data link this dramatic morphological shift to molecular changes in the coordination environment of zinc ions and protein structure. This study provides the first example and a novel molecular mechanism of supramolecular metallogelation by a native bacterial protein. Bridging between molecular processes, mesoscopic structure, and macroscopic material properties, it not only advances the fundamental understanding of ECM assembly in situ but also establishes artificial ECM-based (metallo-)hydrogels as matrix mimics for bacterial infection studies.

articles.title: Enzyme-Responsive Chemiluminescent Nanofibrous Membranes for Monitoring and Photothermal Therapy of Infected Wounds.
articles.abstract: Rapid detection and effective elimination of wound infection are imperative for wound management. Herein, we designed a chemiluminescence nanofiber membrane (CL-PVA/PLA@PB NCs) that integrates visual diagnosis and on-site photothermal disinfection for enhancing wound healing. The composited nanofiber membrane was fabricated from adamantyl-phenoxy-1,2-dioxetane-modified polyvinyl alcohol (CL-PVA) and polylactic acid (PLA) and loaded with a photothermal agent, Prussian blue nanocubes (PB NCs). Upon interaction with alkaline phosphatase secreted (ALP) by bacteria, strong chemiluminescence from CL-PVA/PLA@PB NCs was observed, allowing us to detect bacteria at the site of infected wounds and evaluate the wound infection status. Furthermore, under near-infrared (NIR) laser irradiation, the excellent photothermal effect induced by PB NCs endowed the membrane with potent antibacterial properties. Meanwhile, in vivo experiments showed that the CL-PVA/PLA@PB NCs with excellent biocompatibility could achieve chemiluminescence-guided photothermal antibacterial therapy, accelerating wound healing. Chemiluminescence-guided photothermal antibacterial therapy based on CL-PVA/PLA@PB NCs provided a new approach for wound monitoring and therapy.

articles.title: SeqSol-FECS: An Integrated Deep Learning and Structural Modeling Framework for Protein Solubility Engineering.
articles.abstract: Escherichia coli is widely used as a workhorse for heterologous protein expression. However, insoluble protein expression is frequently encountered. The mechanisms underlying protein solubility remain incompletely understood, limiting the effectiveness of current protein solubility engineering strategies. Here, SeqSol, a sequence-level solubility prediction model capable of prioritizing single-amino-acid substitutions through WT-mutant rescoring, was developed using 71,425 proteins. SeqSol achieved an accuracy of 75.8% and an AUC of 0.840 on an independent test set and correctly identified experimentally validated solubility-enhancing mutations from diverse proteins. To minimize the risk of activity loss, candidate mutation sites were prioritized according to conformational flexibility, relative solvent accessibility, and evolutionary conservation before solubility engineering. Using only 30 experimentally tested mutations, the resulting SeqSol-FECS framework increased the solubility of two industrial enzymes from 56.18% and 10.53% to over 95%, respectively, while maintaining their specific activities. SeqSol-FECS provides an efficient strategy for enzyme solubility engineering and biomanufacturing applications.

articles.title: Modulating Transthyretin Fibril Stability with D-Retro-Inverso Peptides.
articles.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
articles.abstract: A major cause of heart failure in elderly patients is the deposition of transthyretin (TTR) fibrils. Using molecular dynamics simulations, we explore how the stability of TTR fibrils can be modulated by D-retro-inverso (DRI) peptides, built from D-amino acids with the sequence of the parent peptide switched. We screened a library of peptide candidates generated from aggregation-prone regions in the TTR sequence, including peptides from WALTZ-DB 2.0 database of amyloid peptides, and selected three peptides based on their potential to disrupt interactions in a structurally flexible region of the fibril. Peptides were docked to the surface of the TTR fibril using HADDOCK 2.4, followed by all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate peptide-fibril interactions and their effects on fibril structure. We finally describe a potential mechanism by which one of these peptides, DRI-K6V, perturbs the structural integrity of TTR fibrils, and identify the segment K80-S100 as a potential target for modulating TTR fibril stability. Our results may open the way to the design of peptide drugs targeting established TTR amyloidosis.

articles.title: AI-Driven Discovery Pipeline Identifies Carvedilol as a Novel Partial Agonist of THRβ.
articles.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
articles.abstract: Thyroid hormone receptor beta (THRβ) is a key therapeutic target for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and dyslipidemia, yet the discovery of structurally diverse agonists remains challenging. Here, we developed an AI-driven hierarchical drug discovery framework integrating graph neural network (GNN)-based virtual screening, structure-based modeling, and multilevel biological validation to accelerate THRβ agonist identification. The optimized GNN model outperformed conventional machine-learning approaches and enabled efficient prioritization of active compounds from an in-house library. Subsequent molecular docking and MM/GBSA rescoring identified Carvedilol as a high-confidence candidate. TR-FRET assays confirmed that Carvedilol acts as a partial THRβ agonist with preferential SRC2-2 coactivator recruitment, comparable to Resmetirom. Cellular assays further demonstrated that Carvedilol significantly reduced lipid accumulation and triglyceride levels and upregulated key metabolic regulators, including DIO1, ME1, and LDLR. Molecular dynamics and dcTMD analyses elucidated that Carvedilol is stabilized within the ligand-binding pocket through dominant hydrophobic interactions and specific hydrogen bonds with Thr273 and His435. Overall, this study repurposes Carvedilol as a structurally distinct THRβ agonist and validates an effective AI-guided strategy for nuclear receptor-targeted drug discovery.

articles.title: Functional status of children with myelomeningocele and the burden of their informal caregivers: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the functional performance of children with myelomeningocele undergoing rehabilitation and its association with the perceived burden of their informal caregivers.

METHODS: A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted at a rehabilitation center with eight child-caregiver dyads representing the entire population of children with myelomeningocele receiving care at the institution. Child functionality was assessed using the Pediatric Evaluation of Disability Inventory - Computer Adaptive Test, and caregiver burden was measured using the Informal Caregiver Burden Assessment Questionnaire. Sociodemographic and clinical data were also collected. Descriptive statistics and Pearson correlation analyses were performed between the domains of both instruments.

RESULTS: Caregivers were all mothers, most with low household income and full-time caregiving responsibilities. Most children exhibited functional performance below age expectations in the domains of Mobility, Daily Activities, and Social and Cognitive Skills. Only three participants achieved normative percentiles above 50 in more than one domain. The lowest continuous scores were observed in Responsibility, followed by Daily Activities and Mobility. Financial Burden and Family Support showed the highest mean caregiver burden scores. Strong negative correlations were identified between functional performance and subjective burden domains, indicating that lower functionality was associated with greater emotional burden, stronger reactions to caregiving demands, and lower perceptions of efficacy and control.

CONCLUSIONS: Functional deficits in children with myelomeningocele are associated with increased emotional and practical burden among informal caregivers. These findings highlight the importance of rehabilitation strategies aimed at improving children's functional independence while also incorporating caregiver support as an essential component of care.

articles.title: Ultrasound non-mass lesions of the breast: imaging features, pathologic risk, and interobserver agreement.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the sonographic and clinical characteristics of breast non-mass lesions detected on ultrasound, identify factors associated with increasing pathological risk, and assess interobserver agreement among breast radiologists.

METHODS: This retrospective study included breast ultrasound examinations performed between January 1, 2021, and August 30, 2025. A keyword search in the picture archiving and communication system identified 2,002 examinations potentially describing non-mass findings. After exclusions, 666 potentially eligible lesions were independently evaluated by three breast radiologists. Lesions were classified as non-mass according to a predefined majority rule (≥ 2 of 3 observers) and assessed using a three-level clinical concern score. Final diagnoses were established by histopathology or ≥ 2 years of imaging follow-up. Associations between imaging and clinical variables and pathological categories were evaluated using univariable analyses and multivariable ordinal logistic regression. Interobserver agreement was assessed using kappa statistics and Gwet's AC1.

RESULTS: A total of 610 lesions in 610 patients were classified as non-mass by majority decision. Malignancy was identified in 13 of 610 lesions (2.1%). Interobserver agreement for non-mass classification was high, although agreement estimates differed between Gwet's AC1 (0.80) and Fleiss' kappa (0.24). A clinical concern score of 3 predicted malignancy with a sensitivity of 76.9% (10/13) and specificity of 98.6% (582/590). Multivariable analysis showed that architectural distortion [odds ratio (OR): 8.40; 95% confidence interval (CI): 3.89-18.16; P < 0.001], posterior acoustic shadowing (OR: 4.76; 95% CI: 1.84-12.28; P = 0.001), and vascularity (OR: 2.69; 95% CI: 1.22-5.97; P = 0.015) were independently associated with increasing pathological risk.

CONCLUSION: Most breast non-mass lesions detected on ultrasound are benign; however, architectural distortion, posterior acoustic shadowing, and vascularity are independently associated with increased pathological risk.

CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: Recognizing specific ultrasound features associated with higher pathological risk may help distinguish non-mass lesions requiring more intensive diagnostic evaluation from predominantly benign findings and support more consistent clinical management.

articles.title: Illumination of anguillid herpesvirus 1 transmission in European eels reveals the importance of host developmental stage and agonistic social interactions.
articles.abstract: The European eel has a complex life cycle involving various developmental stages and migrations through marine and freshwater environments. It is critically endangered and therefore a flagship species for conservation efforts. The European eel is also an important fish species in aquaculture. One of the major pathogens contributing to the decline of the European eel is thought to be anguillid herpesvirus 1 (AngHV-1). In this study, we used in vivo bioluminescent imaging to study the ability of AngHV-1 to infect the various developmental stages of the European eel, and to investigate virus transmission between eels. Our results highlight that eels become sensitive to AngHV-1 infection only when they become yellow eels (a freshwater stage prior to maturity), with the gills and the periodontal mucosa acting as the first sites of replication after inoculation by immersion in virus-containing water. Also, multifocal cutaneous bioluminescent signals appeared in grouped eels, but not in isolated eels. These observations suggested that the virus might be transmitted through biting between fish. In support of this hypothesis, experiments based on single artificial bites occurring between infected eels and naïve eels led to the infection of all exposed subjects. The biological relevance of AngHV-1 transmission by biting was further supported by observation of the instability of virion infectivity in water and fish mucus. Our study thus challenges the current paradigm that fish viruses are transmitted mainly via water acting as an abiotic vector. It demonstrates that, as in air, so in water, social interactions matter.IMPORTANCEFish viruses have devastating effects on wildlife and severe economic impact on aquaculture. The current paradigm is that they are transmitted via water acting as an abiotic vector. Here, we used in vivo bioluminescent imaging to study the ability of anguillid herpesvirus 1 (AngHV-1) to infect different developmental stages of European eel and to investigate virus transmission between eels. The major findings were that (i) eels become sensitive to AngHV-1 infection only when they become yellow eels, with the gills and the periodontal mucosa acting as the first sites of replication after inoculation by immersion in virus-containing water; (ii) AngHV-1 is efficiently transmitted between fish through biting, thereby avoiding virion instability in water and mucus. Our study thus challenges the current paradigm that fish viruses are transmitted mainly via water acting as an abiotic and protective vector. It demonstrates that, as in air, so in water, social interactions matter.

articles.title: Beyond executive robotics: harnessing artificial intelligence for data-driven governance in complex urological units.
articles.journal: Archivio italiano di urologia, andrologia : organo ufficiale [di] Societa italiana di ecografia urologica e nefrologica
articles.abstract: Robotic surgery has revolutionized urological procedures by offering high intraoperative precision; however, current platforms operate primarily in an executive dimension, lacking predictive and context-aware capabilities. In the modern healthcare landscape, technology alone cannot resolve systemic bottlenecks such as waiting lists, operating room underutilization, and rising costs. This manuscript explores the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) - including machine learning, deep learning, and predictive analytics - with robotic urology to foster data-driven clinical management.
