By optimizing pre-operative planning, mitigating peri-operative complications (such as acute kidney injury and urosepsis), and automating smart scheduling and bed management, AI elevates complex urological units into predictive organizations. Under the "Human-in-the-Loop" ethical framework, AI acts as a decision support system, empowering the urologist as a hybrid Clinical Manager while restoring time for patient-centered care.

articles.title: The path to recovery: treatment adherence mediates the effect of subjective age on rehabilitation outcomes in older adults.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The current study aimed to test the effect of subjective age on rehabilitation outcomes in older patients following hip osteoporotic fracture or stroke. Additionally, we tested the hypothesis that adherence to therapy mediates the effect of subjective age on outcomes.

METHODS AND MEASURES: Patients (N = 158, mean age = 77.15, age range = 64-98) reported their subjective age during the first week of rehabilitation, physiotherapists reported adherence to therapy throughout rehabilitation, and rehabilitation outcomes (rehabilitation effectiveness) were assessed by a multidisciplinary team of healthcare personnel using the Functional Independence Measure.

RESULTS: As hypothesised, the results revealed that a younger subjective age during the first week of rehabilitation predicted higher rehabilitation effectiveness. Moreover, this effect of subjective age was mediated by higher adherence to the therapeutic protocol during rehabilitation.

CONCLUSION: Our findings highlight the significance of subjective age not just as a predictor of health outcomes but also as an antecedent to coping with health crises, further elucidating the behavioural mechanisms underlying the link between subjective age and rehabilitation effectiveness.

articles.title: Intravenous Thrombolysis in Extracranial Arterial Dissection Stroke: A Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: The Canadian journal of neurological sciences. Le journal canadien des sciences neurologiques
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extracranial arterial dissection (EAD) is a leading non-atherosclerotic cause of ischemic stroke in adults under 45 years of age. Intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) is central to acute stroke care, but its use in EAD remains contentious. We performed an updated meta-analysis of IVT versus conservative therapy in EAD-related stroke.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception through August 2026 per PRISMA 2020 (PROSPERO: CRD420261296521). Co-primary outcomes were excellent (modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0-1) and favorable (mRS 0-2) 90-day recovery; secondary outcomes were symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH), mortality and recurrent stroke.

RESULTS: Five studies met the criteria (11,285 patients; 1,410 IVT, 9,875 non-IVT); no new studies were identified. Crude analyses showed lower odds of excellent recovery (odds ratio (OR) 0.78, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.63-0.97), no difference in favorable recovery (OR 0.86, 95% CI 0.67-1.10) and higher odds of sICH (OR 2.15, 95% CI 1.01-4.56) and mortality (OR 3.38, 95% CI 2.85-4.03) with IVT. Adjusted analyses of the two largest studies showed greater functional independence (OR 1.67, 95% CI 1.23-2.28) and home discharge (OR 1.40, 95% CI 1.01-1.92) with IVT, without excess mortality or hemorrhage.

CONCLUSION: Crude analyses suggested worse outcomes and excess mortality/hemorrhage with IVT; adjusted analyses from the largest datasets showed better functional and discharge outcomes with no safety signal, suggesting confounding by indication rather than causal harm. EAD alone should not preclude IVT in eligible patients.

articles.title: Characterization of herpes B virus isolated from wild cynomolgus macaques and its pathogenic effects in captive hosts.
articles.abstract: Despite the high seroprevalence of herpes B virus (BV) among wild macaques, it remains unclear why BV is rarely transmitted to humans who live alongside macaques in their natural habitats. We investigated disease progression, host immune responses, viral shedding, histopathology, and immunohistochemistry of tissues after BV injection in cynomolgus macaques. BV was isolated from a wild Thai cynomolgus macaque living in southern Thailand and intramuscularly injected into four captive macaques (two males and two females) housed at the Animal Biosafety Level 3 facility. Over 49 days, all macaques remained clinically healthy but showed enlarged lymph nodes. IgM was detected on 9 days post-infection (dpi) and peaked at 13 dpi, while IgG appeared on 11 dpi and peaked at 28 dpi. No viral DNA was detected in oral, urogenital, or rectal swabs throughout the 49 day study period. However, viral DNA was identified in the spleen, sublingual gland, and trigeminal ganglia. Histopathology revealed tissue damage in the spleen and trigeminal ganglion, with BV immunoreactivity in the spleen. Overall, BV injection induces localized lymphoid and immune responses without causing clinical symptoms or viral shedding in natural macaque hosts. This may help explain why natural macaque hosts remain healthy and why human BV infections associated with wild cynomolgus macaques have rarely been documented.IMPORTANCEHerpes B virus (BV) isolated from a wild cynomolgus macaque was inoculated into captive macaques in an experimental setting. BV infection triggers localized lymphoid and immune responses (IgM and IgG) without causing clinical symptoms or viral shedding. Viral DNA was detected in the spleen, sublingual gland, and trigeminal ganglia. These insights improve our understanding of how BV interacts with its natural macaque hosts and shed light on the rare transmission of BV from wild macaques to humans.

articles.title: The pks gene clusters modulate the pathogenicity of Klebsiella pneumoniae by impairing neutrophil extracellular traps.
articles.abstract: The pks gene clusters, crucial virulence-associated gene clusters in Klebsiella pneumoniae (K. pneumoniae), have been verified to exacerbate disease severity in infected hosts. During the early stage of pks-positive K. pneumoniae infection, neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) are produced by neutrophils to capture and eliminate pathogens. However, neutrophils struggle to completely eliminate bacteria via NETs. To confirm the role of the pks gene clusters in infection, we performed a bacterial survival assay to assess neutrophil dysfunction. NET structural damage was confirmed via scanning electron microscopy observation and NET staining. The DNA breakage was verified by γH2AX staining and Western blot. In the mouse sepsis model, immunofluorescent staining and histological analysis were used to verify pathogenic changes induced by the pks gene clusters. Data were analyzed using the Mann-Whitney U test or the Kruskal-Wallis H test. Results showed that the pks gene clusters were associated with DNA damage. The pks gene clusters disrupted the mesh-like structure of NETs, which resulted in NET dysfunction. In vivo, pks-positive K. pneumoniae affected the bactericidal capacity of NETs. In the mouse model, pks-positive Klebsiella pneumoniae is more prone to inducing liver abscess formation. In conclusion, the pks gene clusters impair NET function, reducing NETs' ability to capture and kill bacteria, and increasing the risk of liver abscess formation.IMPORTANCEThis study elucidates the interplay between the pks gene clusters of Klebsiella pneumoniae and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs). Our observations underscore the impact of the pks gene clusters on NETs' functionality, and we further investigate its implications on murine pathogenicity and virulence. These findings offer novel insights into the clinical management of Klebsiella pneumoniae infections.

articles.title: Comparison of robot-assisted gait training and visual feedback balance training on balance and gait outcomes in patients with stroke: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robot-assisted gait training and visual feedback balance training are technology-assisted approaches used to improve balance and mobility after stroke. Although both have demonstrated beneficial effects when incorporated into conventional rehabilitation, direct comparisons between these approaches under comparable treatment conditions remain limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare the effects of RoboGait-based robot-assisted gait training and ProKin-252 visual feedback balance training on balance, mobility, gait, motor recovery, fear of falling, and functional independence after stroke.

METHODS: This randomized, assessor-blinded, parallel-group trial included 50 participants with subacute or chronic stroke (mean age: 63.86 ± 9.06 years). Participants were allocated to RoboGait or ProKin-252 training. Both groups received conventional balance and gait rehabilitation for 40 min, 5 days/week for 4 weeks, with an additional 30-min technology-assisted intervention twice weekly. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and after 4 weeks. The Berg Balance Scale (BBS) was the primary outcome, analyzed using analysis of covariance adjusted for baseline BBS.

RESULTS: Balance scores improved significantly in both groups (p < .001), with mean increases of 4.44 ± 1.71 points in the RoboGait group and 5.92 ± 1.91 points in the ProKin group. Adjusted post-treatment BBS favored ProKin, with a between-group difference of 1.43 points (95% CI, 0.37-2.49; p = .009). ProKin also produced greater improvements in fear of falling (p = .004) and forward-backward postural sway (p = .027). Functional mobility, gait speed, lower-extremity motor recovery, functional ambulation, and functional independence improved significantly in both groups without significant between-group differences.

CONCLUSION: Both groups demonstrated improvements in balance and functional outcomes. ProKin produced a statistically greater improvement in BBS and additional advantages in fear of falling and forward-backward postural sway; however, the adjusted BBS difference was modest, with no significant between-group differences in gait or broader functional outcomes.

articles.title: Comprehensive profiling of genotype-specific dengue antibody responses using a newly developed single-round infectious particle panel.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Neutralizing antibodies provide critical protection against dengue virus (DENV) infections. However, under certain conditions, antibodies can also enhance infection and contribute to severe disease through antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE). ADE can occur through extrinsic mechanisms, in which antibody-opsonized virions engage with Fcγ receptors (FcγRs) on target cells to facilitate increased viral entry, while intrinsic mechanisms have been proposed in which FcγR-mediated uptake triggers intracellular pathways that promote viral replication. The extensive genetic diversity of DENV further complicates the evaluation of antibody functionality, as antibodies may exhibit distinct neutralizing and enhancing activities against different viral genotypes. Here, we developed a single-round infectious particle (SRIP) panel representing 17 DENV genotypes across all four DENV serotypes. This genotype-inclusive platform enables assessment of antibody-mediated neutralization and FcγR-dependent enhancement of infection through luciferase reporter quantification. Using this panel, we evaluated antibody responses from DENV-infected individuals, healthy volunteers, and flavivirus-cross-reactive or DENV-specific monoclonal antibodies. Our findings reveal genotype-specific variations in antibody-mediated neutralization and enhancement, emphasizing the complex interplay between antibody responses and DENV genetic diversity. This SRIP panel provides a robust approach for profiling functional antibodies against genetically diverse DENV strains. While the current platform primarily quantifies extrinsic ADE, its single-round infection format and intracellular replicon-based readout provide a foundation for future investigations of intrinsic ADE mechanisms. Overall, this platform offers broad applications for studying dengue immunity, evaluating vaccine-induced antibody responses, and advancing our understanding of antibody-mediated protection and disease enhancement.

IMPORTANCE: Dengue virus (DENV) comprises four serotypes and substantial genetic diversity, which can influence the ability of antibodies to neutralize or enhance infection. However, comparative assessment of antibody functionality across diverse DENV genotypes remains challenging because differences in viral genetic backgrounds can confound functional measurements. We developed a single-round infectious particle (SRIP) panel representing 17 DENV genotypes in which the prM and E structural proteins are varied on a common replicon backbone. This design provides a standardized platform for directly comparing antibody-mediated neutralization and Fcγ receptor-dependent enhancement across genetically diverse DENV strains. By characterizing antibody responses against a broad range of genotypes, the panel can reveal differences in functional antibody activity that may be overlooked when using a limited number of representative strains. The platform is therefore useful for investigating how DENV genetic diversity influences antibody-mediated protection and extrinsic antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE), as well as for evaluating the breadth of antibody responses induced by infection or vaccination. Although the current platform primarily quantifies extrinsic ADE, its single-round infection format and quantitative intracellular reporter readout provide a foundation for future studies investigating intrinsic ADE in more physiologically relevant immune cell models. This genotype-inclusive panel offers a practical approach for standardized functional profiling of dengue antibodies and may facilitate improved evaluation of vaccine-induced immunity and antibody responses across the genetic diversity of DENV.

articles.title: Draft genome sequences of two Stenotrophomonas muris isolates, CBAS 1154 and CBAS 1234, recovered from patients with ICU-acquired ventilator-associated sepsis.
authors: Ribeiro Gomes de Queiroz Crespo I
articles.abstract: We report the high-quality draft genome sequences of two clinical Stenotrophomonas muris isolates recovered from the lower respiratory tract of intensive care unit patients with ventilator-associated sepsis in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Based on our review of the available literature, we found no previous records of this species from Brazil.

articles.title: Does incremental inspiratory muscle training provide additional benefits over minimal‑load training for respiratory muscle strength, diaphragm thickness, and diaphragmatic excursion in patients with pre‑dialysis chronic kidney disease? A randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare the effects of incremental-load inspiratory muscle training (IMT) versus fixed minimal-load IMT on respiratory muscle strength, diaphragm thickness, and excursion in patients with non-dialysis chronic kidney disease (CKD).

METHODS: In this randomized, controlled, blinded clinical trial, patients with CKD stages G3a-G5 were allocated to incremental-load IMT, with progressive loading up to 60% of maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP), or fixed minimal-load IMT at 5 cmH2O. Both interventions were performed daily for 8 weeks. Respiratory muscle strength was assessed by manovacuometry, while diaphragm thickness, excursion, and thickening fraction were evaluated using ultrasonography before and after the intervention.

RESULTS: Inspiratory and expiratory muscle strength increased in both groups, with no significant between-group differences in MIP (adjusted mean difference [AMD] = 32.97 cmH2O, 95% CI: -4.44 to 12.37; p = .344) or maximal expiratory pressure (AMD = 1.52 cmH2O, 95% CI: -6.81 to 9.85; p = .712). Diaphragm thickness and excursion also increased within both groups, without significant between-group differences (thickness: AMD = 0.10 mm, 95% CI: -0.17 to 0.37; p = .461; excursion: AMD = 0.22 mm, 95% CI: -0.46 to 0.90; p = .514). No significant between-group difference was observed in diaphragm thickening fraction (AMD = 6.74% points, 95% CI: -3.03 to 16.51; p = .170).

CONCLUSION: In patients with pre-dialysis chronic kidney disease, 8 weeks of progressive-load inspiratory muscle training did not result in additional benefits over fixed minimal-load training in respiratory muscle strength, diaphragmatic thickness, or excursion. Although both groups showed improvements, these findings suggest that progressive loading may not confer superior short-term benefits in this population. Larger, adequately powered trials are warranted to clarify the effects of training intensity and determine the optimal inspiratory muscle training protocol.

articles.title: Clinical Spectrum of epilepsy in children at a tertiary pediatric neurology center: Unaddressed methodological limitations.
articles.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape

articles.title: Virus-specific impacts on honey bee flight performance are mediated by the octopamine pathway.
articles.abstract: High annual honey bee colony losses are associated with environmental and biological stressors, including virus infections. In insects, the octopamine (OA) pathway orchestrates the 'fight-or-flight' response, regulating energy mobilization, temperature, and flight. We determined that sacbrood virus (SBV) infections induce expression of an OA receptor and enhance honey flight performance, whereas deformed wing virus (DWV) infections reduce flight performance, but how viruses interface with this pathway remained unknown. To elucidate the relationships between the OA response, virus infection, and flight, honey bees were infected with SBV or DWV and exposed to OA, epinastine (EP) - an OA receptor antagonist, or both OA and EP; flight and gene expression were assessed. Pharmacologic manipulation revealed that OA supplementation rescued flight deficits in DWV-infected bees, but diminished performance in SBV-infected bees, while blocking OA receptors altered these effects. Transcriptome analyses indicated that SBV infections, and DWV infection with OA treatment, activated honey bee metabolic pathways, and that SBV-infected bees had greater expression of genes involved in OA synthesis, unless treated with OA. These results provide mechanistic insight for virus-specific impacts on honey bee flight, which may have consequences for foraging efficiency, colony health, and virus transmission.

articles.title: Highly Processed Food Consumption, Maternal Sociodemographic Variables, and Pregnancy Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal diet quality during pregnancy is an important modifiable, yet often overlooked, factor in pregnancy outcomes for both the pregnant individual and their baby. Dietary patterns in the United States are often linked to sociodemographic factors and include a significant proportion of highly processed foods (HPF), known contributors to adverse health outcomes. However, these relationships are poorly understood in pregnant populations.

OBJECTIVES: The objectives of this retrospective observational study were to use Dietary Screener Questionnaire (DSQ) data to (a) explore the consumption of common HPFs during pregnancy, and (b) examine the relationships between HPF consumption and sociodemographic factors and maternal pregnancy outcomes.

METHODS: We collected sociodemographic information, pregnancy outcomes, and DSQs capturing dietary intake during the previous 30 days from women who delivered their infants at a large metropolitan hospital in Boston, Massachusetts, between January 2019 and August 2021. We calculated descriptive statistics for sociodemographic, pregnancy outcome, and HPF intake data. We used separate linear regression models to examine associations between total HPF consumption and sociodemographic and pregnancy outcome variables; we further examined significant relationships with multivariable regression.

RESULTS: Ninety-six women participated (most were White), privately insured, and not Hispanic/Latina. Women in this cohort consumed HPFs an average of 1.91 times each day. There was a trend towards lower total HPF consumption among Black/African American and Asian participants compared to White participants. Total HPF consumption was significantly lower among former smokers compared to those without a history of smoking and among participants diagnosed with gestational diabetes compared to those without diabetes. Conversely, participants with chronic hypertension consumed more HPFs than those without a hypertensive disorder. No other significant interactions were noted.

DISCUSSION: Future research is needed to assess the relationships between HPF consumption, sociodemographic factors, and health outcomes across diverse populations of pregnant individuals. Obstetric clinicians, particularly nurses, should consider expanding pregnancy nutrition counseling to include methods such as a DSQ to reduce HPF intake.

articles.title: Between Paris, Berlin, Moscow, and Warsaw: four Polish physicians in the transnational making of modern neurology.
articles.journal: Journal of the history of the neurosciences
articles.abstract: Modern neurology emerged through the circulation of clinicians, methods, concepts, and institutional models across nineteenth- and early twentieth-century Europe. This historical narrative review examines Józef Babiński (1857-1932), Edward Flatau (1868-1932), Józef Brudziński (1874-1917), and Władysław Sterling (1877-1943) as four selected case studies in that process. Drawing on published primary texts, contemporary accounts, biographical scholarship, and modern historiography, we argue that their contributions are better understood as products of transnational scientific networks than as isolated national achievements. Babiński transformed bedside neurological semiology in Paris and extended it from the plantar response to cerebellar signs and anosognosia. Flatau combined medical training in Moscow with neuroanatomical work in Berlin before helping to build neurological research and clinical institutions in Warsaw. Brudziński joined pediatrics, bedside examination, experimental physiology, hospital organization, and university building. Sterling, trained in Warsaw, Berlin, Munich, and Paris, contributed with Flatau to the early conceptual history of torsion dystonia and heredity. Their careers also reveal how partitions, migration, institutional settings, war, and political violence shaped scientific opportunity and historical memory. The uneven persistence of their eponyms illustrates how neurological credit can preserve individual names while obscuring collaborative and transnational origins.

articles.title: Relationship Between Post-Operative Complications and Length of Stay in Patients Requiring Free Flap Reconstruction of the Head and Neck.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reconstructive with free flap procedures are often required following ablative removal of pathologies from the head and neck. The Clavien-Dindo Classification (CDC) system is widely used to grade complication severity; however, there are limited studies examining the relationship between complications and length of stay (LOS) in this cohort.

PURPOSE: To evaluate the association between complication severity and both hospital and intensive care unit (ICU) LOS in patients undergoing head and neck free flap reconstruction.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 994 patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Complications were graded using the CDC system. LOS was analysed using generalised linear models with a Gamma distribution and log-link. Kruskal-Wallis tests were used for supplementary analysis.

RESULTS: Complications occurred in 54.5% of patients. Higher CDC grades were significantly associated with longer ICU (p < 0.001) and hospital LOS (p < 0.001). CDC Grades II, IIIb and IVa were independently associated with prolonged ICU LOS. All CDC grades were associated with increased hospital LOS.

CONCLUSION: This study provides outcome data linking complication severity to ICU and hospital LOS. The CDC, while advantageous, fails to separate significant negative outcomes, such as free flap failure from a more simple return to theatre. Modifications may further improve distinction in complications and effect on overall hospital stay.

articles.title: The importance of the kinetic-chain base in the forehand stroke of (sub)elite wheelchair and able-bodied tennis players.
articles.abstract: In overhead sports, generating high movement velocities relies on a solid base of support that facilitates efficient energy transfer through the kinetic chain. This mechanism is also likely fundamental to forehand performance in tennis. Therefore, this study examined how the kinetic-chain base influences forehand performance (ball speed, ball spin rate, and ball bounce accuracy) in (sub-)elite wheelchair and able-bodied tennis players. Fifteen able-bodied (mean age 23.2 ± 5.9 years) and 15 wheelchair tennis players (mean age 25.0 ± 7.5 years), participated in this experimental study. Participants performed forehands from different starting positions to induce variability in peak angular velocities (PAVs) along body segments of the kinetic chain. On-court performance outcomes were assessed using a multi-camera tracking system. Pelvis/wheelchair and trunk PAVs, measured with inertial measurement units, were entered as predictors of forehand performance in regression analyses using generalised estimated equations. A one-radian-per-second increase in pelvis/wheelchair and trunk PAV resulted in a significant increase in ball speed (0.5 m·s-1 and 0.2-0.7 m·s-1, respectively), independent of ball bounce accuracy. No significant associations were observed between pelvis/wheelchair or trunk PAV and ball spin rate.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Microvasculature- and Layer-Resolved Neurovascular Signatures of Peri-Infarct Depolarizations Revealed by Functional Ultrasound Imaging.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
articles.abstract: Peri-infarct depolarizations (PIDs) critically influence neurovascular dysfunction and lesion expansion after ischemic stroke, yet their hemodynamic signatures across cortical layers and vascular compartments remain poorly defined. Using functional ultrasound (fUS), a technique based on ultrafast Doppler imaging that enables high-sensitivity and high-resolution mapping of individual vessels, we characterized the spatiotemporal dynamics of cerebral blood volume (CBV) during PIDs in rats subjected to photothrombotic ischemia. PIDs arose at the ischemic core and propagated through the ipsi-lesional cortex, exhibiting a characteristic sequence of hypoperfusion, peak hyperemia, and post-depolarization depression. Analysis of penetrating arterioles and venules revealed marked hemispheric differences, while comparable CBV modulation between arterioles and venules was observed within the infarcted hemisphere. Laminar profiling further demonstrated that deeper cortical layers displayed greater hyperemic responses and more pronounced CBV depression than superficial layers during PID. Together, these findings establish functional ultrasound as a powerful in vivo approach for resolving microvascular and laminar hemodynamic dynamics during PIDs and for defining PID-associated CBV signatures that reflect early neurovascular dysfunction in acute ischemic stroke.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Infection, Inflammation, and the Second Hit Hypothesis in Moyamoya Disease: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a progressive cerebrovascular disorder with significant morbidity. RNF213 is the primary susceptibility gene, but its low penetrance suggests a "second hit" (e.g., infection/inflammation) is required for clinical onset. This review synthesizes evidence on RNF213's immunological functions and downstream cascades driving MMD arteriopathy, identifying translational opportunities and knowledge gaps.

METHODS: We performed a narrative synthesis of peer-reviewed literature (PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, up to 2026) on RNF213 biology, immune-inflammatory signaling, endothelial dysfunction, angiogenesis, and animal models, constructing a mechanistic framework linking genetics to environmental triggers.

RESULTS: RNF213 modulates interferon and NF-κB pathways. MMD arteriopathy results from endothelial dysfunction, aberrant angiogenesis, and chronic perivascular inflammation, converging on smooth muscle proliferation and stenosis. Translational tools-circulating biomarkers and immunomodulators-show preliminary promise but remain exploratory.

CONCLUSION: Evidence supports an immune-mediated two-hit model, but the spatiotemporal sequence from peripheral triggers to focal intracranial disease is unresolved. Major limitations include lacking robust animal models and prospective biomarker validation. Future research should prioritize longitudinal multi-omics, patient-derived iPSC models, and validated biomarker cohorts to enable precision medicine.

articles.title: Persistent infection is associated with divergent evolution of T cell repertoires.
articles.abstract: In chronic infection, T cell clones recognizing the same epitope are variably expanded, with some clones evolving to become dominant, while others are lost. Clonal expansion and changes in the repertoire reflect both T cell receptor-intrinsic (TCR-intrinsic) and -extrinsic factors, yet the individuality of TCR repertoires makes it difficult to disentangle how TCR sequence shapes clonal behaviors. To address this, we exploited the observation that TCRs can be grouped into clusters based on sequence similarity. Using complementarity-determining region 3β (CDR3β) sequencing data derived from lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus-specific CD8+ T cells from mice infected early and late in the course of chronic infection, we identified CDR3β clusters ubiquitously shared by all mice. The pattern of CDR3β cluster abundance was highly similar between mice at the early time point in both self-limiting and persistent infection models. Over the course of chronic infection, the pattern of cluster abundance diverged between mice and dominant clones emerged that did not share sequence similarity between mice. This repertoire divergence was not observed in self-limiting infection, where the pattern of cluster abundance established early in infection was stable between mice beyond resolution of infection. In chronic infection, the repertoires of stem-like and exhausted antigen-specific T cells remained similar over time within individual mice, suggesting clonal selection acts on the stem-like pool. Our findings suggest that antigen-specific CD8+ T cell clones expanded early in infection have CDR3β motifs that are shared between mice, supporting a role for TCR structural properties in determining the repertoire structure. Divergent patterns of repertoire composition later in chronic infection suggest that these shared CDR3β motifs are less important in patterning the repertoire than during the initial response and there is greater complexity in factors that sculpt the repertoire over the course of persistent antigen exposure.

articles.title: Genomic, single-cell, and functional profiling of the CD48-CD244 axis and NK cell dysfunction in multiple myeloma.
articles.abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) orchestrates immune evasion by subverting natural killer (NK) cell function. CD48, one of the most abundant NK ligands on MM cells, paradoxically enhances NK cell activation yet is associated with high-risk cytogenetics and poor patient survival. We integrated multiomics (bulk and single-cell RNA-seq, assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing [ATAC-seq], chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing [ChIP-seq]), genome-wide CRISPR knockout/activation screens, and machine learning to dissect CD48 regulation and function. In human MM and Vκ*MYC mouse scRNA-seq datasets, NK cells exhibit stepwise increases in inflammatory and exhaustion signatures and loss of cytotoxic potential as disease progresses. In vitro coculture assays show that CD48 overexpression on MM enhances NK cell cytokine secretion, whereas chronic exposure leads to ex vivo NK dysfunction. In vivo, CD48-overexpressing Vκ*MYC tumors progress more slowly and extend host survival, while NK cell depletion accelerates disease. These findings support a context-dependent role for CD48, potentiating acute NK responses while coexisting with chronic NK exhaustion, and suggest strategies to modulate CD48 for therapeutic benefit.

articles.title: Early nutrition impacts later setmelanotide treatment of obesity in mice.
articles.abstract: Unhealthy nutrition in early life can reduce response to a weight loss drug in adult obesity.

articles.title: Carbon monoxide exposure and the risk of cardiac arrhythmia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: International journal of environmental health research
articles.abstract: Although carbon monoxide (CO) exposure is associated with cardiovascular diseases, its relationship with cardiac arrhythmias remains unclear. This meta-analysis evaluated the association between CO exposure and arrhythmia risk in the general population and patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs). PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Embase were searched from inception to June 2025. English-language studies investigating CO exposure and arrhythmias or ventricular arrhythmias were included. Adjusted estimates were pooled as odds ratios (ORs) or hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using random-effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic, and study quality was evaluated using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Seventeen studies were included: seven involving the general population and ten involving ICD patients. In the general population, CO exposure was significantly associated with increased arrhythmia risk (OR: 1.07; 95% CI: 1.02-1.13; p = 0.01; HR: 1.25; 95% CI: 1.01-1.53; p = 0.04). However, no significant association was observed in ICD patients for arrhythmias (OR: 1.02; 95% CI: 0.99-1.02; p = 0.20) or ventricular arrhythmias (OR: 1.03; 95% CI: 0.99-1.06; p = 0.18). These findings suggest that CO exposure increases arrhythmia risk in the general population, whereas no significant association was identified in ICD patients.

articles.title: Contemporary pharmacotherapeutic options for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) is driven by both proximal thromboembolic obstruction and microvasculopathy. While pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) and balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) are effective for selected patients, pharmacotherapy is indispensable in the contemporary era. This review provides an updated overview of medical therapy within a multimodal treatment paradigm.

AREAS COVERED: This review examines lifelong anticoagulation, including comparative evidence for vitamin K antagonists and direct oral anticoagulants, and the efficacy and safety of approved and off-label PH-targeted therapies for inoperable CTEPH or persistent/recurrent PH after PEA. Riociguat, phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitors, endothelin receptor antagonists, treprostinil, and selexipag are reviewed, together with combination therapy, pharmacotherapy before and after PEA or BPA, and assessment of treatment response.

EXPERT OPINION: Riociguat has the strongest evidence for symptomatic inoperable CTEPH or persistent/recurrent PH after PEA; subcutaneous treprostinil may benefit selected patients with severe disease. PH-targeted therapy should not delay PEA referral. Anatomical inoperability, procedural risk, limited specialist access, and informed refusal require different responses. After intervention, decisions to continue medication should consider residual disease, symptoms, right ventricular function, and exercise limitation, not resting hemodynamics alone. Comparative studies should determine who benefits from medication before BPA and when it can safely be withdrawn.

articles.title: Altered effective connectivity during cognitive distancing in cognitive behavioral therapy nonresponders with depression.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Approximately half of individuals with major depressive disorder (MDD) do not respond to cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT). Cognitive distancing is a reappraisal tactic central to CBT, and neural responses during reappraisal have been linked to psychotherapy outcome. We examined whether pretreatment effective connectivity during cognitive distancing was associated with CBT response in adults with MDD.

METHODS: Seventy-seven outpatients with MDD (31 women) completed fMRI during a distancing task before 25 CBT sessions as part of the SPeED trial, which included a pre-CBT phase of exercise or waiting list. Dynamic causal modeling estimated effective connectivity within a 10-region network. Group differences were assessed with parametric empirical Bayes, and predictive utility was evaluated with leave-one-out cross-validation.

RESULTS: Responders (n = 39) showed greater relative modulation along a dorsomedial-to-ventrolateral prefrontal-to-superior frontal/pre-supplementary motor area cascade during distancing, whereas nonresponders exhibited greater relative modulation of amygdala-to-ventrolateral prefrontal cortex connectivity. Nonresponders showed decreased dorsolateral prefrontal self-inhibition during negative picture processing, consistent with heightened local excitability. Distancing-related effects exceeded 99% posterior probability and predicted treatment response in cross-validation (r = .21-.31, p < .05).

CONCLUSIONS: Effective connectivity during distancing robustly differentiated responders from nonresponders, with nonresponders showing weaker intra-prefrontal control and stronger amygdala-to-prefrontal influence. These neural patterns contribute to insight into CBT nonresponse and suggest a mechanism associated with lowered symptom improvement through cognitive interventions. However, incremental predictive value beyond baseline clinical measures was modest. If replicated prospectively, such measures may contribute to multimodal prediction models and adjunctive treatment strategies.

CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION NAME: Neurobiological correlates and mechanisms of the augmentation of psychotherapy with endurance exercise in mild to moderate depression - SPeED, http://apps.who.int/trialsearch/Trial2.aspx?TrialID=DRKS00008869, DRKS00008869.

articles.title: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors and risk of self-harm in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: an active comparator, new user cohort study in two independent cohorts.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) has twice the self-harm risk of the general population, the role of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT-2i) is unclear; this study aimed to assess whether SGLT-2i use is linked to lower self-harm risk in T2DM.

METHODS: Through the Shenzhen Public Health Data Platform, we constructed two cohorts (SGLT-2i vs. dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors [DPP-4i], and SGLT-2i vs. glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists [GLP-1RA]) via a target trial emulation framework. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using overlapping weighting Cox regression models.

RESULTS: The SGLT-2i versus DPP-4i cohort included 85,789 SGLT-2i users and 53,810 DPP-4i users. After a median follow-up of 1.85 years (interquartile range: 0.91-2.70), 567 (0.66%) cases of self-harm occurred in the SGLT-2i group and 567 (1.05%) in the DPP-4i group. After overlapping weighting, SGLT-2i was associated with a lower risk of self-harm compared with DPP-4i (HR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.76-0.98), and this result was consistent across various sensitivity analyses. In the SGLT-2i (n = 130,330) versus GLP-1RA (n = 5,126) cohort, a lower risk of self-harm (HR: 0.76, 95% CI: 0.59-0.99) was associated with SGLT-2i compared with GLP-1RA. However, in some sensitivity analyses, no statistically significant difference was observed between SGLT-2i and GLP-1RA users.

CONCLUSIONS: SGLT-2i use is associated with a lower risk of self-harm compared with DPP-4i and GLP-1RA. These findings provide supportive evidence for the safety of SGLT-2i and highlight their potential role in the mental health management of T2DM patients.

articles.title: Co-existent autoimmune diseases in people with multiple sclerosis and a review on choice of immunotherapy.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Coexisting autoimmune diseases in multiple sclerosis (MS) may influence disease-modifying therapy (DMT) choice, but Indian data remains limited. This study aims to determine the prevalence of co-existent autoimmune disorders in Indian MS patients and assess their impact on DMT selection.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: This multicentre, cross-sectional observational study included 355 adults with MS evaluated across five Indian neuroimmunology clinics between 2016 and 2026. Comorbidity prevalence was compared against general-population estimates, and DMT utilization was compared between patients with and without autoimmune comorbidities.

RESULTS: Fifty-nine patients (16.6%) had an autoimmune disorder, with hypothyroidism (5.9%), rheumatoid arthritis (RA; 2.0%), and type 1 diabetes mellitus (1.4%) being the most common. Prevalences of RA (2.0% vs 0.49%; p = 0.002) and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD; 0.8% vs 0.02%; p < 0.001) were significantly higher than population estimates. Comorbidities shifted treatment: Rituximab use was lower in the comorbidity group (49.2% vs 69.3%; p = 0.003); dimethyl fumarate (22.0% vs 1.4%; p < 0.001) and azathioprine (5.1% vs 0.7%; p = 0.004) were prescribed more frequently.

CONCLUSIONS: Autoimmune comorbidity occurred in about 1/6 Indian MS patients, with excess RA and IBD relative to population prevalence and an associated shift in DMT selection.

articles.title: Stroke Triggered by Respiratory Viruses: Ecological Study of Temporal and Spatiotemporal Associations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infections have been linked as short-term triggers for stroke, but the extent of their contribution is unclear. We examined population-level temporal and spatiotemporal associations between common respiratory viruses and stroke in an ecological study in Victoria, Australia.

METHODS: The statewide Victorian Admitted Episodes data set, covering all hospital admissions for stroke between June 2010 and December 2022, was analyzed against statewide representative data from SnotWatch respiratory polymerase chain reaction tests. Population size, climate, and air pollution data sets for the same period were treated as population-level confounders. Time-series analysis was used to model weekly stroke events and respiratory virus levels (% of polymerase chain reaction tests positive for each pathogen), and attributable fractions were computed using distributed lag nonlinear modeling. To examine spatiotemporal variation, the weekly association by Statistical Area Level 2 was modeled using a Bayesian Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation.

RESULTS: We analyzed 153 730 stroke events (61% ischemic, 25% hemorrhagic, and 14% unspecified) and 6 180 896 respiratory specimens. In the time-series analysis, higher weekly levels of specific respiratory viruses were associated with increased rates of stroke after controlling for confounders. Our model estimated that the fractions of strokes attributed to enterovirus and human metapneumovirus 4.6% (95% CI, 2.5-6.6) and 1.3% (95% CI, 0.3-2.3), respectively, which rose during peak viral weeks. The attributable fractions differed between ischemic stroke (human metapneumovirus 3.7%) and hemorrhagic stroke (enterovirus, 5.8%; parainfluenza, 3.2%). Spatiotemporal analysis revealed greater effect sizes in areas potentially associated with agricultural/industrial activity, as well as in outer-urban areas, based on the regionality of the Statistical Area Level 2 of usual patient residence.

CONCLUSIONS: At the population level, there were clear, observable time- and space-time-related associations between respiratory virus activity and stroke. People living in higher-risk areas during peak respiratory virus periods may be more susceptible to acute stroke. This warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Endothelial KLK8 Promotes Diabetic Nephropathy via a LIFR Dependent Mechanism.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The molecular pathways in endothelial cells (ECs) in diabetic nephropathy (DN), a primary microvascular complication of diabetes, remain unclear. Tissue KLKs (kallikrein-related peptidases) participate in pathophysiological processes in ECs. We aimed to explore the roles of endothelial KLKs in DN and define the underlying mechanisms.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Renal KLK8 was the most highly upregulated KLK in streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice and cultured glomerular ECs (GECs) upon high glucose treatment. C57/BL6 background global (Klk8-/-) and endothelial Klk8 knockout (Klk8ΔEC) mice, as well as DBA/2J mice with endothelial Klk8 knockdown, displayed improved albuminuria, mesangial matrix expansion, and glomerulosclerosis caused by streptozotocin compared with the corresponding wild-type mice. Single-cell RNA sequencing showed that many pathways linked to DN in ECs, mesangial cells, and tubule cells were reversed in Klk8ΔEC mice. Endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition caused by streptozotocin was extensively improved in Klk8ΔEC mice, which was confirmed in Cdh5CreERT2+/--mT/mG+/- mice with endothelial Klk8 knockdown. Proteome coupled with other approaches revealed that KLK8 cleaved SDC4 (syndecan-4), which contributed to the loss of glycocalyx integrity in GECs during DN progress. Lifr was one of the key genes in ECs and mesangial cells regulated by endothelial Klk8 during DN progress. Endothelial KLK8 upregulated LIFR (leukemia inhibitory factor receptor) expression through PLC (phospholipase C)/ERK (extracellular signal-regulated kinase)/RUNX1 (runt-related transcription factor)1 pathways, and upregulated LIFR contributed to high glucose-induced GEC dysfunction and MC activation. Knockdown of Lifr ameliorated hallmark features of DN and improved endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition and SDC4 expression in the glomeruli of diabetic mice. LIFR was upregulated in GECs and mesangial cells in patients with DN. Circulatory LIF (leukemia inhibitory factor), KLK8 and soluble SDC4 levels were increased in patients with DN, and KLK8 level was positively correlated with LIF, soluble SDC4 and creatinine levels.

CONCLUSIONS: Endothelial KLK8 promotes GEC dysfunction and abnormal crosstalk with mesangial cells through a LIFR-dependent signaling in DN, which immediately highlights therapeutic targets for DN.

articles.title: Cost-Shifting for Cardiovascular Hospitalizations Between Medicare Advantage and the Veterans Health Administration System.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality among US veterans, many receiving cardiovascular care across both the Veterans Health Administration (VA) and non-VA hospitals, driven in part by the growth of Medicare Advantage (MA) enrollment. With both systems federally financed, overlapping payment responsibilities raise concern for duplicative federal spending on inpatient CVD care.

METHODS: We conducted a national, cross-sectional study using 2021 linked MA and VA data to identify CVD hospitalizations defined using diagnosis-related groups among MA-enrolled veterans with VA benefits. Each CVD-related hospitalization (eg, heart failure exacerbation) was categorized by source of payment: MA-paid community hospital care, VA-paid community hospital care, or VA-direct care at VA hospitals. High-veteran plans were defined as ≥20% veteran enrollment. Multinomial logistic regressions were used to evaluate associations between high-veteran MA plan enrollment and payment source, adjusting for patient characteristics and state fixed effects. Analyses were stratified by admission complexity and elective status.

RESULTS: Sample included 76 722 MA-enrolled veterans (mean [SD] age, 78.0 [8.8] years, 97.9% male), of which 10 366 (13.5%) were in high-veteran MA plans, and 66 356 (86.5%) were in high-veteran MA plans. Veterans in high-veteran MA plans were less likely to have MA-paid community hospitalizations than those in low-veteran MA plans (43.2% versus 69.2%; -26.1 percentage-points [95% CI, -27.1 to -25.1]) but more likely to have VA-paid community care (28.1% versus 16.0%; +12.2 percentage-points [95% CI, 11.3-13.0]) and VA-direct care (28.7% versus 14.8%; +13.9 percentage-points [95% CI, 13.0-14.8]). Results were consistent across admission types and medical complexity.

CONCLUSIONS: Veterans enrolled in high-veteran MA plans were more likely to have inpatient CVD care financed by the VA, suggesting that MA plans may be shifting costs despite receiving capitated payments intended for inpatient care. Policy reforms are needed to reduce duplicative federal spending and improve coordination of cardiovascular care.

articles.title: Perceptions of Rheumatologists on Barriers and Enablers to Adoption of Interdisciplinary Models of Care in Rheumatology in Ontario, Canada.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Interdisciplinary models of care, where rheumatologists provide care collaboratively with interdisciplinary healthcare professionals (IHPs), can enhance rheumatology service delivery, yet their adoption remains limited. This study aimed to identify barriers and enablers to adopting an interdisciplinary model of care, as perceived by rheumatologists.

METHODS: We conducted semi-structured interviews with rheumatologists practicing without IHP support in Ontario, Canada. The interview guide was informed by the Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF), an implementation framework used to identify determinants of health-professional behaviour. Content analysis was used to deductively code data to TDF domains and to inductively derive within-domain themes related to factors influencing adoption of interdisciplinary care.

RESULTS: We interviewed 14 rheumatologists. Seven TDF domains were relevant to adoption of interdisciplinary care: Optimism, Beliefs about Capabilities, Beliefs about Consequences, Reinforcement, Environmental Context and Resources, Knowledge, and Skills. Rheumatologists reported optimism that interdisciplinary models would achieve desired outcomes, felt confident in training IHPs, and anticipated benefits for patients and rheumatologists. These factors, together with prior positive experience with interdisciplinary teams, were seen as key enablers of adoption. Barriers included insufficient funding, space constraints, limited availability of trained IHPs, and turnover risk. Most rheumatologists reported gaps in knowledge of IHP training and scope, and limited business skills for recruitment/hiring.

CONCLUSION: This study identified behavioural determinants of rheumatologists' adoption of an interdisciplinary model of care. To overcome barriers and strengthen enablers, sustainable funding, IHP workforce development, practical implementation resources (business guidance and training), and clear blueprints of successful care models including IHP role descriptions, are required.

articles.title: Tracheostomy and Home Invasive Ventilation in Severe Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia: A Scoping Review of Indications, Timing, Outcomes and Transitional Care.
articles.journal: Journal of paediatrics and child health
articles.abstract:
AIM: To map the literature on tracheostomy and home invasive ventilation in infants and children with severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), including indications, timing, respiratory outcomes, comorbidities, complications, growth, neurodevelopment, social determinants and transitional care.

METHODS: We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and CINAHL/EBSCO from inception to 30 June 2026. Search terms combined BPD or chronic lung disease of prematurity with tracheostomy or tracheotomy. Eligible studies included infants or children with BPD who underwent tracheostomy, received chronic invasive ventilation or were discharged on home mechanical ventilation. Conference abstracts without full-text articles, duplicate precursor abstracts, reviews and editorials were excluded from primary synthesis.

RESULTS: Forty-one studies were included. Evidence was mainly retrospective, including cohorts, administrative database studies, multicentre registries and single-centre observational studies. Tracheostomy was generally considered for persistent invasive ventilation, failed extubation, high respiratory support needs, pulmonary hypertension, airway malacia, growth failure, sedation burden or limited developmental progress. Timing varied widely across centres. Pulmonary hypertension was associated with illness severity and mortality risk, although many children receiving home ventilation improved over time. Among survivors, ventilator liberation and decannulation were common but often occurred over several years. Airway complications, readmissions and operative airway interventions were frequent. Evidence also highlighted centre-level variation, racial and social disparities and limited caregiver-centred data.

CONCLUSIONS: Tracheostomy and home invasive ventilation in severe BPD represent a prolonged care trajectory. Future work should define consensus indications, optimise timing, standardise transitional care and prioritise family-centred and equity-focused outcomes.

articles.title: Postbiotics derived from Latilactobacillus curvatus alleviate alcoholic liver injury by reshaping intestinal microbiota and activating the lysozyme-AHR-IL-22 axis.
articles.abstract: Long-term alcohol exposure disrupts gut microbiota and mucosal immune homeostasis, promoting the pathogenesis of alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) via the gut-liver axis. Postbiotic intervention has emerged as a potential strategy for alleviating ALD, yet its protective mechanisms within the impaired intestinal microenvironment remain unclear. This study investigated whether postbiotics derived from Latilactobacillus curvatus can alleviate alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) and explored their active components and underlying mechanisms. In two alcohol-exposed mouse models, heat-killed L. curvatus (HKLC) significantly reduced liver injury, steatosis, oxidative stress, and inflammation, while improving lipid metabolic homeostasis. HKLC also restored intestinal barrier integrity by increasing tight junction protein expression and recovering cecal short-chain fatty acids. Microbiota analysis showed that HKLC remodeled both bacterial and fungal communities, suppressing opportunistic pathogens such as Parasutterella excrementihominis and Candida albicans while enriching beneficial short-chain fatty acid-associated bacteria including Phascolarctobacterium faecium. Fractionation experiments further showed that the cell precipitate fraction was the major active component, reproducing most of the protective effects of whole HKLC. Mechanistically, HKLC and its cell precipitate fraction enhanced intestinal lysozyme and Defa5 expression, reactivated the AHR-IL-22 signaling pathway, and increased downstream antimicrobial peptides. These findings demonstrate that L. curvatus-derived postbiotics alleviate ALD mainly through the gut-liver axis by restoring intestinal homeostasis, reshaping gut microbiota, and activating lysozyme-associated mucosal immune signaling. This study provides experimental evidence supporting postbiotic-based strategies for ALD intervention.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance of MRI, endorectal ultrasound, and FAPI PET/MRI for identifying pathological complete response after short-course radiotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy in locally advanced rectal cancer: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate imaging-based response assessment is essential for proficient mismatch repair (pMMR) locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC). This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of MRI, endorectal ultrasound (ERUS) and 18F-FAPI PET/MRI for identifying pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy (SCRT) followed by chemoimmunotherapy.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 143 patients. Diagnostic performance was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy with 95% confidence intervals. Cohen's κ assessed agreement between imaging-defined complete response (iCR) and pCR. Paired comparisons used Cochran's Q and Holm-adjusted exact McNemar tests.

RESULTS: The pCR rate was 51.0%. MRI (n = 118), ERUS (n = 81), and PET/MRI (n = 25) achieved sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy of 4.76%, 98.18%, and 48.31%; 30.95%, 87.18%, and 58.02%; and 60.0%, 100.0%, and 84.0%, respectively. PET/MRI-assessed imaging complete response showed substantial agreement with pCR (κ = 0.643).

CONCLUSION: Neoadjuvant SCRT followed by chemoimmunotherapy achieved high pCR rates in pMMR LARC. Conventional MRI and ERUS showed limited sensitivity despite relatively high specificity. 18F-FAPI PET/MRI showed potential diagnostic utility in a small subgroup, but its moderate sensitivity and limited sample size warrant further validation. These findings highlight the limitations of imaging alone and the need for comprehensive response assessment.

articles.title: 'Have you a table?': epistemic instability, experimental tabulation, and the presentation of medical statistics in and after the Indian Plague Commission, 1898-9.
articles.abstract: The visualisation of data in tables has been essential to the historical development of epidemiological reasoning. As visual devices, tables have enabled epidemiologists to compare populations and establish multi-factorial association as a hallmark of modern epidemiology. While tables have usually been understood as instruments of ordering, this article argues that, in fin-di-siècle science, tabulation was a site of scientific experimentation and conflict, and that epidemiological standards later crystallised at least in part in response to the use and misuse of tabulation during these years. Drawing from an analysis of the tabulation practices found in the Indian Plague Commission (IPC) of 1898-99 - a landmark study which has not been fully integrated into the history of epidemiology - this article details how tables were introduced as powerful albeit inconsistent tools of epidemiological reasoning. We initially consider the testimony of medical officers in India, who used tables as an experimental tool to test the value of Haffkine's vaccine against plague. For commissioners, by contrast, tables were disruptive, equipped with the power of epistemic transgression. Contrary to the traditional function of tables as instruments of colonial order - useful for facilitating the abstraction and categorisation of colonised populations - tables in the IPC emphasised uncertainty and chance at the heart of epidemiological inquiry. This epistemic instability mattered, as we show, for the scientific community in Britain, where criticism of the IPC report stimulated sweeping debate on the presentation of contingency in medical statistics, advancing the formalisation of British epidemiology over the first decades of the twentieth century.

articles.title: Stratification of Gastric Cancer Based on Methylation Status of Enhancer Regions and Effects on Transcriptional Regulation.
articles.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus-positive gastric cancer (EBV(+) GC) shows extensive DNA hypermethylation in gene promoter regions. DNA methylation induced by EBV infection contributes to carcinogenesis through tumor suppressor gene inactivation. Whereas aberrant DNA methylation in enhancer regions might reportedly contribute to carcinogenesis, its impact has not been fully elucidated. Therefore, we here performed DNA methylome analysis on clinical samples, including GC and normal gastric mucosa, using the Infinium MethylationEPIC BeadChip array to evaluate the epigenome in the enhancer regions. We stratified GC cases into three subclusters using hierarchical clustering analysis based on the methylation status of enhancer regions; EBV(+) GC samples were classified into the most extensively methylated subcluster. We identified genes with promoters unmethylated but enhancers aberrantly methylated in EBV(+) GC. Such methylated genes included Inositol polyphosphate-5-phosphatase A (INPP5A), which is associated with the phosphoinositide 3-kinase/Akt signaling pathway and cell proliferation and survival, and showed lower expression levels in EBV(+) GC compared with normal mucosa and other GC samples. We infected GES1, an immortalized gastric epithelial cell line, with EBV in vitro, and demonstrated the induction of aberrant DNA methylation in the INPP5A enhancer region and the downregulation of its expression. These findings indicate that EBV(+) GC exhibits a specific DNA hypermethylation phenotype in enhancer regions, and EBV infection in gastric cells could induce aberrant DNA methylation in enhancer regions, involving dysregulation of cancer-related gene expression.

articles.title: Pharmacological treatment of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation-associated thrombotic microangiopathy with focus on the FDA-approved antibody narsoplimab.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Transplantation-associated thrombotic microangiopathy (TA-TMA) is an endothelial injury syndrome after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT), presenting as microangiopathic hemolysis, thrombocytopenia, microvascular thrombosis and multiorgan dysfunction. Dysregulated complement activation is central, rendering complement inhibition a major therapeutic target.

AREAS COVERED: This review summarizes the evolving concepts of the pathogenesis, diagnosis, risk stratification, and therapeutic landscape of TA-TMA, emphasizing complement-directed therapies. We discuss terminal complement inhibition with eculizumab and ravulizumab, proximal and alternative pathway inhibition with pegcetacoplan and iptacopan, and lectin pathway inhibition with narsoplimab as the only drug approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA). We critically appraise narsoplimab with respect to its pivotal trial, expanded access program, and comparative studies with other approaches. Differences in study populations, response definitions, safety ascertainment and regulatory assessments are discussed.

EXPERT OPINION: Narsoplimab represents an important advance as the only FDA-approved treatment for TA-TMA, with consistent responses reported in different studies of high-risk patients and an acceptable safety profile. However, current evidence supporting narsoplimab is limited to single-arm studies. Future studies should employ harmonized diagnostic and response criteria, compare complement-directed strategies, and evaluate biomarker-driven early diagnosis and intervention to prevent severe organ damage that may be fatal.

articles.title: Prevalence of TPMT and NUDT15 pharmacogenomic variants in a diverse germline testing cohort from India.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Thiopurines are cytotoxic antimetabolites used in malignancies and autoimmune conditions, with their clinical use requiring careful monitoring due to the risk of severe myelosuppression driven by the accumulation of active thioguanine nucleotides. This toxicity is largely driven by impaired metabolism of thiopurine metabolites, particularly in individuals with TPMT or NUDT15 variants. The prevalence and spectrum of these pharmacogenomic variants in the Indian population remain incompletely characterized.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We analyzed whole-exome data from 1,742 Indian individuals (including 609 with hematologic conditions) to assess clinically relevant pharmacogenomic variants per CPIC guidelines, identifying TPMT *3C and *3B no-function alleles in 3.10% (n = 54).

RESULTS: The high-risk NUDT15 c.415C >T (*2/*3) variant was identified at an allele frequency of 7.26% (245 carriers; 14.06% of the cohort), including eight homozygotes. Comparative analyses demonstrated pronounced population-specific variation, with several alleles enriched in South Asians but rare or absent in other populations.

CONCLUSION: To our knowledge, this represents the largest pharmacogenomic assessment of TPMT and NUDT15 variants in an Indian cohort to date. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating population-specific genomic data into clinical decision-making frameworks and support the implementation of preemptive TPMT and NUDT15 genotyping prior to initiation of thiopurine therapy in Indian patients.

articles.title: Quantitative fragility of reported association between aspirin use and hepatocellular carcinoma risk in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: Letter to the editor on "Aspirin and hepatocellular carcinoma risk in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: Nationwide cohort study with genetic risk analysis".
A Unique Case of PPP1R12A-Related Urogenital and Brain Malformation Syndrome Phenotypically Overlapping With VACTERL Association, With Additional Literature Review of Previously Described Phenotypes.
articles.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
articles.abstract: PPP1R12A-related urogenital and brain malformation syndrome (UBMS) is a rare genetic disorder caused by pathogenic variants in PPP1R12A, which encodes a regulatory subunit of myosin phosphatase. We report a 46,XY male with a heterozygous de novo pathogenic variant in PPP1R12A, c.2629del (p.S877Pfs*38). He presented with features consistent with UBMS, including bilateral cryptorchidism, Müllerian duct remnants, tracheoesophageal fistula, anal atresia, and global developmental delay. Notably, he exhibited cardiac anomalies and hepatic cirrhosis not previously reported in individuals with PPP1R12A-related UBMS, including bilateral pulmonary artery hypoplasia and mitral valve prolapse; however, a causal relationship between these findings and the PPP1R12A variant has not been established. His presentation also has significant overlap with VACTERL association. This case reinforces the association between PPP1R12A dysfunction and complex urogenital and gastrointestinal malformations while expanding the phenotypic spectrum to include novel cardiac and hepatic findings. Collectively, these findings raise the possibility of an expanded phenotypic spectrum associated with PPP1R12A-related disease, though additional data is needed to determine whether all associated features are attributable to the variant.

articles.title: Association of Immunomodulatory Treatment with Long-Term Visual Outcomes in Behçet Uveitis: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe clinical characteristics and treatment patterns in Behçet disease-associated uveitis at a tertiary center and to explore the association between immunomodulatory treatment (IMT) and long-term visual outcomes.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included adults diagnosed with Behçet disease-associated uveitis/retinal vasculitis. Demographics, anatomical uveitis classification, ocular inflammatory grades, logMAR best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), complications, surgeries, and systemic therapies were extracted from medical records. Overall ocular outcomes were summarized at the affected-eye level. Comparative analyses according to IMT exposure were performed at the patient level using one eye per patient; in bilateral cases, the eye with worse baseline logMAR BCVA was selected. IMT exposure was defined as documented use of antimetabolite therapy, a T-cell inhibitor, or a TNF-α inhibitor during follow-up. Group comparisons and multivariable analyses were exploratory.

RESULTS: Thirty patients were included (66.7% male; mean age 39.5 ± 11.9 years). Panuveitis was the most common anatomical subtype (56.7%). A total of 42 affected eyes were analyzed descriptively. Mean logMAR BCVA changed from 0.613 ± 0.935 at baseline to 0.894 ± 1.158 at final follow-up. Systemic therapy included oral prednisone in 73.3% of patients, antimetabolite therapy in 40.0%, a T-cell inhibitor in 20.0%, and a TNF-α inhibitor in 13.3%. In patient-level analyses, 13 patients had IMT exposure and 17 did not. Final logMAR BCVA was lower in the IMT-exposed group than in the non-exposed group (0.587 ± 0.870 vs. 1.498 ± 1.303, p=0.050). In an exploratory multivariable linear regression model adjusted for baseline logMAR BCVA, age at visit, and panuveitis, IMT exposure was associated with lower final logMAR BCVA (coefficient, -1.192; 95% CI, -2.131 to -0.253; p=0.015).

CONCLUSIONS: In this Korean tertiary-center cohort, Behçet uveitis commonly involved panuveitis with substantial long-term visual morbidity and surgical burden despite systemic therapy. IMT exposure showed a favorable association with final logMAR BCVA in patient-level analyses, although causal inference is limited by the retrospective design and potential confounding. Larger multicenter studies with standardized activity, relapse, and treatment-exposure metrics are warranted.

articles.title: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Reveal the Strength of Mediterranean, DASH, and Plant-Based Diets in Diabesity.
articles.journal: Obesity reviews : an official journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) frequently coexist as diabesity, a condition marked by chronic low-grade inflammation. This systematic review and meta-analysis compared the Mediterranean diet (MedDiet), Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH), and plant-based diets (PBD) on anthropometric, metabolic, and inflammatory outcomes in adults with obesity and/or T2DM.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, and SciELO were searched to June 2025 for randomized controlled trials. The minimum intervention duration of 8 weeks applied exclusively to the meta-analysis, whereas shorter trials could be included in the qualitative synthesis. Study quality was assessed with the Downs & Black scale and certainty of evidence with GRADE. Random-effects meta-analyses estimated mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals.

RESULTS: No dietary pattern significantly reduced body weight or BMI compared with control diets, and DASH trials could not be included in the quantitative synthesis. PBD significantly lowered fasting blood glucose (MD 4.34 mg·dL-1; 95% CI 1.29-7.38), whereas differences in HbA1c and total cholesterol were not significant. Within-group analyses, reported descriptively, showed reductions from baseline in both arms, and inflammatory markers declined in some studies. Most studies were of fair-to-poor quality; comparisons among diets are indirect, and certainty of evidence was low to very low.

CONCLUSION: The MedDiet and PBD may support the management of obesity and/or T2DM, although current evidence does not establish the superiority of any single pattern. Future trials should address long-term adherence, mechanisms, and head-to-head comparisons.

articles.title: Unified Command in Local Public Health: Case Studies of Rabies and Tuberculosis Responses in Douglas County, Nebraska.
articles.abstract: As public health emergencies become more frequent and complex, local health departments must increasingly rely on public-private partnerships and whole-community approaches to respond effectively. The Douglas County Health Department (DCHD), serving Nebraska's most populous county, demonstrates how a local agency can coordinate large-scale responses by implementing a unified command structure with diverse partners. This case study presents 2 concurrent public health emergencies that occurred in late 2023: (1) the detection of raccoon rabies virus variant (RRVV) in a domestic kitten, a pathogen not previously identified in Nebraska, and (2) the largest pediatric tuberculosis (TB) exposure investigated in the county's history. Both incidents required rapid coordination across local, state, and federal agencies, as well as engagement with healthcare systems and community organizations. In each response, DCHD activated a unified command structure to facilitate operational objectives, allocate resources, and coordinate risk communication. The rabies response included enhanced animal surveillance, a trap-vaccinate-release campaign, and the manual distribution of 18,000 oral rabies vaccine baits. No additional human or animal cases of RRVV were identified. The TB response involved identifying 643 exposed individuals, conducting mass testing clinics with local healthcare partners, and rapidly initiating prophylaxis for vulnerable populations. No cases of secondary transmission were identified. These case studies demonstrate how local health departments can lead complex responses by leveraging established partnerships, aligning with National Incident Management System principles, and coordinating unified command operations. Lessons learned from Douglas County's experience offer practical guidance for other jurisdictions preparing for zoonotic and airborne infectious disease threats, especially when internal resources are limited.

articles.title: Modelling indirect protection from typhoid conjugate vaccines in the TyVAC-Bangladesh trial.
articles.abstract: In the TyVAC-Bangladesh cluster-randomized trial, a dose of typhoid conjugate vaccine (TCV) in children aged 9 months to <16 years conferred strong protection against typhoid fever. However, indirect protection among unvaccinated residents was modest and not statistically significanct, raising questions about TCV's effectiveness against Salmonella Typhi transmission and ability to induce herd effects in endemic settings. We hypothesize that this low observed indirect protection could be explained by some combination of transmission across cluster boundaries, limited vaccine protection against infection, and insufficient vaccine coverage. To evaluate these hypotheses, we simulated the trial using a primary transmission dynamic model calibrated against clinical surveillance data, and an alternative model incorporating serological data. Vaccinating 64% of eligible children (the observed trial coverage) induced up to 67% and 54% indirect protection in the primary and alternative models, respectively, depending on the transmissibility of chronic carriers and TCV efficacy against S. Typhi infection. The trial results were consistent with 15% to 85% TCV efficacy against infection in the primary model, and 60% to 90% protection in the alternative model. If adults were vaccinated at the same coverage level as children, we estimate that indirect protection would have increased from 19% to 40%-57%. These findings suggest that TCV confers protection against transmission from acute S. Typhi infections, and that the low indirect protection observed in the TyVAC-Bangladesh trial can be explained by transmission from unvaccinated adults.

articles.title: Clinical consultation: The role of vitamin A in the management of confirmed acute measles infection.
articles.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Although measles was declared eliminated in the United States in 2000, the rate of measles infection in 2026 is the highest in more than 3 decades. This clinical consultation explores the role of vitamin A in the treatment of acute measles infection and the challenges posed with this treatment in pediatric patients due to the limitations in currently available formulations.

SUMMARY: The role of vitamin A in the treatment of acute, confirmed measles infection has been well established and is recommended by major medical organizations, including the World Health Organization and American Academy of Pediatrics. Despite the benefits that vitamin A has demonstrated in past studies, treatment with vitamin A remains difficult due to challenges in administration secondary to the limited formulations currently available in the United States. Multiple options exist to extract liquid vitamin A from capsules, but these methods are cumbersome and possess significant challenges.

CONCLUSION: Vitamin A treatment should be used in patients with acute, confirmed measles infection, after confirming that they are not at risk for drug interactions and have no symptoms of vitamin A toxicity if they were previously treated with vitamin A. A concentrated liquid formulation of vitamin A approved by the US Food and Drug Administration is needed to overcome current obstacles with administration of vitamin A in pediatric patients unable to swallow capsules.

articles.title: A SNP in the MdWRKY11 promoter controls the segregation of Glomerella leaf blotch susceptibility in apple.
articles.abstract: Glomerella leaf blotch (GLB), a severe fungal disease caused by Colletotrichum gloeosporioides, threatens the apple (Malus domestica Borkh.) industry worldwide. The susceptibility of apple to GLB is controlled by a single dominant locus. Although several markers for GLB susceptibility have been developed, the causal genes and their functional variations have not been explored. In this study, we used MapQTL and fine mapping to identify SNP544 C/G in the MdWRKY11 promoter as the major factor underlying the variation in GLB susceptibility in apple. The SNP544 G allele generates a W-box motif that is directly bound by MdWRKY29 and activates MdWRKY11 expression during C. gloeosporioides infection. In turn, MdWRKY11 binds to the MdDMR6.1 promoter and activates its expression, leading to salicylic acid degradation and leaf necrosis. The MdWRKY11 SNP544 G allele was strongly associated with GLB susceptibility, with a prediction accuracy of 96.2% in 767 Malus accessions. In addition to SNP544, we identified nine allelic variations in MdWRKY11 across 29 Malus accessions, with a combined prediction accuracy for GLB susceptibility of 99.6%. These findings shed light on the genetic control of GLB susceptibility in apple and provide an efficient molecular marker for breeding GLB-resistant cultivars.

articles.title: Global Variation in National Tuberculosis Guidelines: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a leading cause of infectious mortality worldwide, with primary care playing a central role in early detection, treatment, and prevention. The World Health Organization (WHO) End TB Strategy provides a global framework for TB control, but its implementation varies across national guidelines.

METHODS: We conducted a scoping review of national and international TB guidelines published between 2015 and 2025. A systematic search of databases and grey literature identified relevant documents. Guidelines were analysed across key domains of TB management, including screening, diagnosis, treatment, preventive therapy, treatment monitoring, and HIV/TB coinfection. Countries were classified as high- or low-incidence settings based on WHO incidence thresholds.
