RESULTS: 76 guideline documents from 34 countries and international organisations were included. Overall, strong alignment with WHO standards was observed for core clinical practices such as diagnosis and treatment regimens. However, substantial variation was identified in case-finding strategies, latent TB infection (LTBI) management, treatment monitoring, and HIV/TB service integration. High-incidence countries prioritised active case finding to reduce transmission, whereas low-incidence countries emphasised targeted screening and preventive therapy.

CONCLUSIONS: While clinical management of TB is broadly standardised, variation in guideline implementation reflects differences in epidemiology and resource availability. Addressing structural barriers and supporting context-specific implementation will be essential to optimise TB control and improve outcomes across diverse settings.

articles.title: Prolonged exposure, eye movement desensitization and reprocessing therapy, and cognitive restructuring versus waiting-list for individuals with PTSD and psychosis (RE.PROCESS): A multicenter, four-arm, assessor-masked, superiority randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence indicates the potential efficacy of trauma-focused therapies for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in psychosis. This is the first randomized controlled trial to evaluate the superiority of Prolonged Exposure (PE), Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing therapy (EMDR), and Cognitive Restructuring (CR) plus treatment as usual, compared to a waiting-list (WL) plus treatment as usual control group.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, assessor-masked, randomized controlled trial in patients with a lifetime schizophrenia spectrum psychotic disorder and PTSD. Participants (N = 162) were randomized (1:1:1:1) to PE, EMDR, CR, or WL and followed up until 6 months post-randomization. Therapy conditions had a maximum of 16 twice-weekly sessions. Primary outcome was researcher-rated PTSD symptom severity (Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5; CAPS-5).

RESULTS: PE, EMDR, and CR significantly reduced PTSD severity compared to WL over time from baseline to 6-month follow-up. At 6-months, adjusted differences and between-group effect sizes on the CAPS-5 were -9.76 (95% CI -16.13,-3.38; p= 0.0029) with d= -0.90 (95% CI -1.36,-0.44) for PE, -11.74 (95% CI -18.04,-5.44; p= 0.0003) with d= -1.04 (95% CI -1.50,-0.58) for EMDR, and -12.72 (95% CI -18.89,-6.55; p= 0.0001) with d= -1.00 (95% CI -1.46,-0.54) for CR. Significant therapy effects were also found for secondary PTSD (-related) outcomes, but not for psychosis.

CONCLUSIONS: In comparison to WL, PE, EMDR, and CR were effective in reducing PTSD symptoms in individuals with PTSD and psychosis, with large effects. Replication in larger samples is needed, although these results support expanding access to trauma therapies in this underserved population.

articles.title: Postoperative prophylactic and delayed oral antibiotics after total shoulder arthroplasty: a multi-institutional database analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the effectiveness and safety of prophylactic and delayed postoperative oral antibiotics following total shoulder arthroplasty (TSA).

METHODS: The TriNetX database was queried for primary TSA patients. Those with prior pathologic fracture, upper extremity malignancy, infection, prosthetic joint infection (PJI), or revision surgery within 6 months were excluded. After 1:1 propensity score matching, two comparisons were performed: (1) prophylactic oral antibiotics within 1 postoperative day versus controls (n=5,891 per cohort) and (2) delayed oral antibiotics on postoperative days 7-30 versus controls (n=3,087 per cohort). Outcomes at 30 and 90 days included acute kidney injury (AKI), emergency department (ED) visits, readmission, PJI, and revision surgery.

RESULTS: At 30 days, prophylactic antibiotics were associated with fewer readmissions (2.78% vs. 3.73%; P=0.004), with no differences in AKI, ED visits, PJI, or revision surgery. At 90 days, they were associated with higher PJI (0.92% vs. 0.48%; P=0.004) and a trend toward lower ED visits (5.25% vs. 6.16%; P=0.032) and readmissions (3.70% vs. 4.67%; P=0.009), but higher revision surgery (1.17% vs. 0.73%; P=0.014). Delayed antibiotics were associated with higher rates of AKI, ED visits, readmissions, and revision surgery at both 30 and 90 days (all P<0.001), as well as higher PJI at 90 days (3.14% vs. 0.42%; P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Although residual confounding cannot be excluded, postoperative prophylactic or delayed oral antibiotics were not associated with reduced PJI or revision surgery and may be associated with antibiotic-related adverse effects. Level of evidence: III.

articles.title: Simultaneous Infection Control and Reconstruction Using Continuous Local Antibiotic Perfusion in Septic Knee With Extensive Soft Tissue Defect: A Case Report.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Continuous local antibiotic perfusion (CLAP) has emerged as a treatment strategy for bone and soft tissue infections; however, its role in septic arthritis with extensive soft tissue defects remains unclear. We report a case of septic knee arthritis with joint exposure after patellar fracture fixation, in which a combined strategy of aggressive source control, CLAP, and early flap reconstruction enabled infection management and soft tissue coverage to proceed concurrently rather than sequentially. CASE REPORT A 69-year-old woman developed methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infection with a 12×8 cm anterior knee soft tissue defect after patellar fracture fixation, presenting 2.5 months after the index surgery. Total patellectomy, extensive debridement, and CLAP were performed. With CLAP maintained throughout, reconstruction with a gastrocnemius muscle flap and split-thickness skin grafting was performed 1 week later, allowing infection management and reconstruction to proceed in parallel. Soft tissue coverage was achieved 17 days after referral, and inflammatory markers normalized within 3 weeks. At the 2-year follow-up, there was no recurrence of infection, and the patient was able to ambulate with full weight-bearing using a knee extension orthosis and a cane. CONCLUSIONS In selected salvage cases, a combined strategy incorporating CLAP and early flap reconstruction may allow infection control and reconstruction to proceed in parallel. The contribution of individual components cannot be isolated from this single case. Although total patellectomy compromised the extensor mechanism, the outcome was clinically acceptable in the context of limb salvage and eradication of infection.

articles.title: Molecular Determinants of Treatment Resistance in Cervical Cancer: A Systematic Review and Integrative Bioinformatic Analysis of Publicly Available Datasets.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: Treatment resistance remains a major challenge in cervical cancer management, particularly among patients undergoing chemoradiotherapy. Despite increasing knowledge of resistance-associated molecular pathways, clinically validated biomarkers capable of predicting treatment outcomes remain limited. This study combined a systematic review of clinical and preclinical studies with an integrative bioinformatic analysis of publicly available transcriptomic datasets. Gene expression profiles from cervical cancer models exposed to chemotherapeutic agents and epigenetic modulators were analyzed to identify treatment-response-associated transcriptional signatures. Candidate genes were subsequently evaluated in clinical datasets comprising normal cervical tissue, cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, and invasive cervical cancer. Functional enrichment analysis, protein-protein interaction network construction, and survival analyses were performed to assess biological relevance. A total of 38 genes demonstrated concordant expression changes across independent treatment conditions. Clinical evaluation revealed progressive dysregulation of several candidates during cervical neoplastic progression and invasive disease development. Functional analyses indicated enrichment of pathways related to extracellular matrix organization, metabolic regulation, and p53-associated signaling. Network analysis identified lumican (LUM) as a candidate gene occupying a relatively high connectivity within the constructed interaction network. No statistically significant association between LUM expression and overall survival was observed. This integrative approach identified reproducible treatment-response-associated transcriptional signatures that may participate in biological processes relevant to therapeutic adaptation in cervical cancer. LUM emerged as a prioritized candidate for future investigation. However, its biological and clinical significance remains exploratory and requires validation in independent treatment-annotated cohorts and functional studies.

articles.title: Everyone Is Welcome: The Role of Community Cafés in Addressing Food Insecurity and Community Connectedness.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Nonprofit organizations such as a community café that use a pay-what-you-can model are emerging as innovative solutions to address food security. The community café is unique in that it can also address social connectedness. This study explored how a community café can address food security and social connectedness.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study used the socioecological model and was conducted from April 2023 to March 2025. Participants included individuals who dined at the café or were enrolled in its culinary apprenticeship program. The data collected included the USDA FSSM, SF-12 Quality of Life, demographic and biometric data (BMI, BP, A1C).

RESULTS: Descriptive and inferential statistics were used to examine relationships among community belonging, physical and mental health, and sociodemographic factors. Higher engagement with the café was associated with more favorable health outcomes. Regression models identified key relationships between café participation, biometric indicators, and quality of life scores.

CONCLUSIONS: Findings from this study provide novel insight into how community café models may influence individual health outcomes and community connectedness. These results support the importance of community cafes in addressing the multifaceted challenges of food insecurity and promoting social connectedness.

articles.title: Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Patients With Pulmonary Hemorrhage.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Severe pulmonary hemorrhage may lead to refractory hypoxemia and/or hemodynamic collapse and cause high mortality. However, the use of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) in this patient population is rare. The aim of this study is to better define and understand this patient population by exploring the baseline characteristics, complications, and outcomes of patients who receive ECMO support due to pulmonary hemorrhage, based on data extracted from the extracorporeal life support organization (ELSO) registry. Between 2003 and 2023, 96 patients received ECMO due to pulmonary hemorrhage. Complications occurred in 54% of the patients, mainly acute kidney injury (AKI) with need for renal replacement therapy (RRT; 28%) and bleeding (pulmonary, gastrointestinal) (15%). Respiratory infections occurred in 37.1% of the patients. The most common diagnostic/therapeutic procedures were computed tomography scans in 9%, bronchoscopy in 41%, surgery in 8%, and apheresis in 6% of the patients. Interventional radiology procedures were performed in only 2% of the patients. Interpretation of these data should be performed cautiously, as underreporting is a known limitation of the ELSO Registry. Forty-seven patients (49%) were weaned from ECMO, and 46 (48%) survived until discharge. Survival and complication rates are comparable to the overall ECMO cohort in the ELSO Registry, which makes ECMO a feasible strategy in this patient population.

articles.title: Employers' Perceptions of Costs & Benefits to Mitigate Against Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) in the Workplace: A Qualitative Study.
articles.journal: Journal of occupational and environmental medicine
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore employers' mitigation strategies against Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19).

METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 28 US employers to understand how the pandemic impacted their business operations, mitigation strategies implemented, and the utility of their emergency preparedness plans.

RESULTS: Employers reported significant operational and financial challenges implementing COVID-19 mitigations including engineering and administrative controls, particularly policies around social distance, remote work, use of personal protective equipment (PPE), and vaccinations. Except for healthcare organizations, most large-sized firms had emergency preparedness plans, but these lacked infectious diseases components. Many small businesses had neither emergency nor infectious disease plans.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study highlighted gaps in emergency preparedness among employers, particularly small businesses. Employee resistance to new policies in future epidemics may be mitigated by ongoing employee engagement and leadership support within a company's existing safety culture.

articles.title: Postmortem pulmonary concentrations of tilmicosin and gamithromycin in cattle with fatal bovine respiratory disease.
articles.abstract: Bovine respiratory disease (BRD) is a health and economic problem in intensive beef production. Antimicrobial (ATM) therapy requires adequate ATM concentrations at the pulmonary infection site. This study determined pulmonary concentrations of tilmicosin (TIL) and gamithromycin (GAM) in cattle that died from BRD under field conditions and characterized the ATM susceptibility of isolates recovered from affected lungs. Lung samples from 41 cattle were analyzed by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. TIL was detected in 56.1% of lungs (0.013-8.811 µg/g; mean 0.956 µg/g; median 0.117 µg/g), and GAM in 24.4% (0.032-2.323 µg/g; mean 0.570 µg/g; median 0.193 µg/g). Detection of TIL and GAM was significantly associated with reported treatment (p<0.001); in animals with documented treatment, TIL and GAM were detected in 90% and 100% of cases, respectively. Concentrations varied widely between animals and were lower than those previously reported in healthy cattle. This may point to altered pulmonary ATM accumulation in advanced BRD; however, the observational design, without a healthy or survivor comparison group or paired plasma measurements, does not allow this explanation to be established. Susceptibility testing of 46 evaluable isolates showed 93.5% and 97.8% susceptibility to TIL and GAM, respectively. Despite this susceptibility, the animals died; the data cannot establish the cause, which may involve disease stage at treatment, timing of diagnosis, irreversible lung injury, pathogen interactions, host factors, or altered pulmonary ATM distribution. The findings emphasize the need to integrate knowledge of pulmonary ATM distribution, early diagnosis, and rational ATM use to improve BRD outcomes.

articles.title: Detection of Strongyloides stercoralis DNA in Urine of Patients with Parasitologically Confirmed Chronic Strongyloidiasis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Strongyloides stercoralis is a neglected soil-transmitted helminth capable of causing chronic infection through autoinfection and life-threatening disease in immunocompromised individuals. Diagnosis remains challenging because stool-based parasitological methods have limited sensitivity, particularly in chronic infections. This study evaluated the detection of S. stercoralis DNA in urine samples from patients with parasitologically confirmed strongyloidiasis.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted from May 2025 to June 2026 on 169 individuals referred to the Strongyloidiasis Laboratory, Tehran University of Medical Sciences. Stool samples were examined by direct smear, formalin-ethyl acetate concentration, and nutrient agar plate culture. Urine samples from stool-positive patients were collected before treatment. DNA extracted from urine sediments was analyzed by conventional PCR targeting the S. stercoralis 18​S rDNA gene. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 27.

RESULTS: A total of 507 stool specimens (three per patient) were examined, and chronic strongyloidiasis was diagnosed in 12 of 169 participants (7.1%; 95% CI 3.7-12.1%). Urine PCR targeting the 18S rDNA gene was positive in 4 of 12 patients with parasitologically confirmed S. stercoralis infection (33.3%; 95% CI 9.9-65.1%), producing the expected 162-bp amplicon. Three of the four PCR-positive patients had diabetes mellitus, although the association was not statistically significant (P = 0.067), likely because of the small sample size.

CONCLUSION: This preliminary study demonstrated the detection of S. stercoralis DNA in urine samples from a subset of parasitologically confirmed patients. However, the small number of positive cases and the absence of a control group preclude the assessment of specificity and overall diagnostic accuracy. Further studies involving larger cohorts, appropriate negative controls, and more sensitive molecular techniques are needed to determine the diagnostic potential of urine-based PCR for strongyloidiasis.

articles.title: Long-term permanent plots in silviculture and forest ecology research: a global systematic review of progress, challenges, and prospects.
articles.abstract: While sampling design and intensity are well-established components of forest inventories, other key permanent sample plots (PSPs) attributes, including plot shape, plot size, spatial arrangement, installation protocols, and remeasurement schedules, and measurement thresholds, have received comparatively less attention in terms of cross-study consistency. Consequently, no widely accepted standard exists for PSPs establishment and monitoring. We acknowledge that these choices must be tailored to research objectives and ecosystem contexts, to improve study comparability, facilitate data exchange, and support broader silvicultural and ecological inference. PSPs are fixed sampling units in which trees are repeatedly measured, tagged, taxonomically identified, and, in some cases, spatially mapped; however, substantial variation persists in plot dimensions, configuration, and inclusion criteria for trees, saplings, and seedlings, limiting dataset integration across regions and ecosystems. Following established systematic review guidelines and employing bibliometric methods, we reviewed 141 peer-reviewed studies published between 2000 and 2024, evaluating 32 variables related to PSP design, establishment, and monitoring. We synthesized global methodological approaches, identified major sources of variation and key knowledge gaps, assessed their implications for cross-study comparability. We also identified aspects of PSPs protocols for which greater consistency in reporting, and documentation are both desirable and feasible, while retaining flexibility to accommodate differences in silvicultural and ecological context, monitoring objectives, and research questions. Based on the evidence compiled, we propose recommendations to strengthen methodological rigor, improve data interoperability, and enhance the global representativeness of long-term forest monitoring efforts.

articles.title: Plasma CAF22, a Biomarker of Neuromuscular Junction Integrity, is Associated with Risk and Earlier Onset of Statin-Associated Muscle Symptoms.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Statin-associated muscle symptoms (SAMS) are a major limitation to effective lipid-lowering therapy. C-terminal agrin fragment 22 (CAF22) is a biomarker of neuromuscular junction degradation, but its role in predicting SAMS remains unclear.

METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 383 adults aged 40-60 years initiating statin therapy were followed for 12 months. Baseline plasma CAF22 was measured prior to statin initiation. Statin intolerance was defined as clinically significant muscle symptoms leading to dose modification, discontinuation, or switching. Logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess associations with the occurrence and timing of statin intolerance, respectively.

RESULTS: Statin intolerance occurred in 17% of participants. Higher baseline CAF22 was associated with increased odds of statin intolerance (adjusted OR: 1.32, 95% CI: 1.08-1.61, p = 0.006) and earlier onset (adjusted HR: 1.38, 95% CI: 1.15-1.63, p < 0.001). The association was consistent across unadjusted and age- and sex-adjusted models. Higher handgrip strength was associated with reduced odds (OR 0.82, 95% CI 0.74-0.97, p = 0.018) and delayed onset (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.66-0.95, p = 0.011) of intolerance. Diabetes mellitus was independently associated with both increased odds and earlier onset, while lipophilic and high-intensity statin use were associated with earlier intolerance. Other demographic and biochemical variables were not significant predictors.

CONCLUSIONS: Baseline CAF22 is independently associated with the risk and timing of statin intolerance. These findings support a role for neuromuscular junction integrity in SAMS and suggest that CAF22 may represent a potential biomarker of vulnerability.

articles.title: Nurse-Led Assessment and Transitional Care in Early Dapagliflozin Initiation for Post-Infarction Heart Failure.
[68Ga] Ga-FAPI positron emission tomography/computed tomography uptake following liver stereotactic body radiation therapy in hepatocellular carcinoma: two case reports.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography have shown high sensitivity for detecting hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI uptake also occurs in benign fibroinflammatory processes, creating a specific challenge for post-treatment surveillance after liver-directed therapies.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report two HCC patients who underwent stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) and subsequently developed FAPI-avid hepatic lesions. In Case 1, a 68-year-old man showed focal FAPI uptake in segment VI following SBRT, which Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) characterised as fibrosis (LI-RADS LR-TR non-viable), with stable tumour markers and no clinical progression. In Case 2, a 77-year-old man exhibited FAPI avidity in the treated lesion, with MRI findings suggestive of post-treatment change. In both cases, the increased FAPI uptake was deemed as false-positive and attributed to post-radiation fibroinflammatory changes.

CONCLUSION: These cases highlight a critical interpretative limitation of [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI PET/CT in post-SBRT HCC surveillance. Fibroblast activation in healing tissues can mimic recurrence; MRI correlation should be done to prevent misdiagnosis. Our report provides novel evidence that SBRT-induced hepatic fibrosis may confound FAPI-based imaging and adds to the evolving understanding of FAPI's performance in surveillance of liver malignancies.

articles.title: Risk factors for the recurrence of chronic subdural hematomas in patients undergoing burr-hole drainage.
articles.abstract: Chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH) is a common neurosurgical disease, particularly in the elderly. The recurrence of cSDH remains a clinical challenge, with several risk factors postulated. Although adjunctive treatments to surgery exist, such as steroids, statins, and middle meningeal artery embolization, the number needed to treat is high, and patient selection remains unclear. This retrospective study aimed to identify risk factors for recurrence after burr hole drainage of cSDH. A single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients undergoing burr-hole drainage for cSDH between February 2012 and May 2023. The primary outcome was surgical recurrence, defined as cSDH recurrence requiring reoperation within six months. Clinical characteristics, preoperative radiological findings, comorbidities and medications, and postoperative findings were assessed as potential risk factors using univariate analysis and, after imputation, multivariable analysis.A total of 766 patients with a recurrence rate of 11.2% (86/766) were included. Significant preoperative risk factors for recurrence included subacute and separated hematoma types (p = 0.02), larger hematoma volume (p = 0.004), greater midline shift (MLS) (p = 0.006), lower Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) (p < 0.001) and higher Markwalder score (p = 0.012). Postoperative findings significantly associated with recurrence were larger cavity volume (p = 0.005), greater MLS (p = 0.01), a higher Markwalder score (p = 0.01) and modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score (p < 0.001) at discharge. After multivariable logistic regression, subacute hematoma age (OR 2.097, p = 0.036), absence of hypertension (OR 1.937, p = 0.012), larger postoperative cavity volume (OR 1.012, p = 0.016), greater postoperative MLS (OR 1.179, p < 0.001), and higher mRS at discharge (OR 1.959, p = 0.002) remained independently associated with recurrence. We found subacute hematoma, larger postoperative subdural cavity volume, higher mRS at discharge, greater postoperative MLS, and the absence of hypertension as factors significantly associated with surgical recurrence within six months.

articles.title: Histoplasma capsulatum Strains from the American Regions Displayed Different Virulence Strategies According to Their Phylogenetic Species.
articles.abstract: Virulence strategies from distinct phylogenetic species of the Histoplasma capsulatum complex have been scarcely documented. Using assays for intracellular replication of H. capsulatum yeasts, induction of cytokine production in yeast-infected human cell-lines (pneumocytes A549 and differentiated macrophages THP-1), and determination of lethal dose 50% (LD 50%) in yeast-infected male BALB/c mice, we characterize virulence strategies of four H. capsulatum strains from the American regions. Yeast replication in human cell-lines expressed by colony-forming units/mL at 2, 6, 24, and 48 h postinfection, supported that EH-315 and 60I strains (NAm 3 and LAm A phylogenetic species, respectively) developed major ability to survive intracellularly. Cytokine production by infected host cell-lines was mainly detectable at 24 and 48 h postinfection. The A549 cells only produced high values for CCL2 and CXCL8 chemokines when infected with EH-315 and 60I strains, whereas the THP-1 cells showed high values for CCL2, CCL5, CXCL8, IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-6 cytokines when infected with each fungal strain tested, highlighting the results for EH-315 and 60I strains. Likewise, LD 50% data showed that the NAm 3 strain (EH-315) was the most lethal. Thus, the obtained findings could differentiate virulence strategies depending on the genotypes of H. capsulatum strains studied.

articles.title: Plasma-derived hyperhomocysteinemia, PGAM5, and oligomeric α-synuclein as a biomarker panel for idiopathic Parkinson's disease.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess a novel panel of plasma biomarkers, comprising homocysteine (HCY), phosphoglycerate mutase 5 (PGAM5), and oligomeric α-synuclein, for the diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD) and to investigate the mechanistic interactions among these biomarkers.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, serum HCY was measured in all 150 patients with PD and 113 healthy controls (HCs), whereas plasma PGAM5 and oligomeric α-synuclein were assayed in subsets (80 PD/78 HC and 67 PD/89 HC, respectively). The diagnostic associated risk factors, and interrelationships of these biomarkers were analyzed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, multivariable logistic regression, and mediation analysis, respectively. Additionally, a diagnostic nomogram was constructed.

RESULTS: Plasma levels of HCY, PGAM5, and oligomeric α-synuclein were significantly elevated in individuals with PD (all P < 0.001). The combined biomarker panel yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.89 for PD diagnosis, which increased to 0.93 when integrated with the rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (RBD) questionnaire score. HCY was an independent risk factor for PD and was associated with male sex, older age, hypertension, longer disease duration, and more severe motor/cognitive deficits (all P < 0.01). Oligomeric α-synuclein mediated 25.72% of the association between HCY and PD (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: This study validates a high-performance plasma biomarker panel for PD, identifies HCY as a risk factor for severe disease progression, and provides clinical evidence that oligomeric α-synuclein mediates the neurotoxic effect of HCY, highlighting a promising therapeutic target.

articles.title: Preventable drivers of acute respiratory infections among under-five children in India's high-risk zones: application of population attributable fractions analyses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute respiratory infections (ARI) remain a major contributor to morbidity and mortality among under-five children in India. Although previous national studies have identified individual-level risk factors, evidence on the spatial distribution of ARI and the burden statistically attributable to selected exposures within hotspot regions remains limited.

METHODS: We analysed data from the 2019-21 National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) Children's Recode file using a two-stage analytical framework. First, district-level ARI hotspots were identified among 221,849 under-five children across 707 districts. Second, analyses were restricted to children residing in hotspot districts (weighted n = 108,470). Survey-weighted prevalence, multivariable logistic regression, and population attributable fraction (PAF) analyses accounted for sampling weights, clustering, and stratification.

FINDINGS: A total of 167 districts were identified as ARI hotspots, predominantly in central and eastern India. The unrestricted national weighted prevalence of ARI in the study dataset was 2.74%, compared with 7.23% (95% CI 7.08-7.39) within hotspot districts. Recent diarrhoeal illness (AOR 4.37, 95% CI 4.01-4.76) and maternal tobacco use (AOR 1.29, 95% CI 1.06-1.57) were independently associated with ARI. The PAF was 19.6% for recent diarrhoea and 0.7% for maternal tobacco use. Rural residence, interpreted as a contextual marker rather than a directly modifiable exposure, had a model-based PAF of 10.2%. The joint counterfactual scenario yielded a PAF of 28.7% (95% CI 20.4-36.1).

CONCLUSIONS: Under-five ARI is geographically concentrated in distinct hotspot districts. Integrated interventions addressing diarrhoeal disease and maternal tobacco exposure, together with improvements in rural child-health services and infrastructure, may reduce ARI burden in these districts. Because rural residence is not itself an intervention, its PAF should be interpreted as a priority-setting indicator of place-based disadvantage rather than as the effect of relocating rural populations.

articles.title: Gerbode defect presenting as an atypical tricuspid regurgitation jet: recognizing the unrecognized.
MUC1 attenuates chronic obstructive pulmonary disease through integrated regulation of pulmonary epithelial cell senescence, transdifferentiation, and inflammatory cascades.
articles.abstract: Impaired pulmonary epithelial cell homeostasis is a key pathogenic feature in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Mucin 1 (MUC1/Muc1) is a membrane-tethered glycoprotein that plays important roles in modulating various disease progression. This study aims to decipher the role and mechanisms of MUC1 in the pathogenesis of COPD. We found functional variants (rs4072037 T > C and rs12411216 C > A) in MUC1 were associated with increased susceptibility to COPD. MUC1-C expression in lung tissues was age-dependent, elevated in adults but decreased in elderly COPD patients. Aged Muc1-deficient mice showed increased cellular senescence in alveolar type II (AT2) epithelial cells and spontaneously developed emphysema. In cigarette smoke (CS)-induced COPD model mice, Muc1 deficiency caused an accelerated decline in lung function, impaired mitochondrial function, enhanced lung inflammation, and impaired AT2-to- alveolar type I (AT1) epithelial cell transdifferentiation. Adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9)-mediated AT2 cell-specific reconstitution of Muc1 ameliorated COPD in association with integrated suppression of pulmonary inflammation and enhancement of AT2 transdifferentiation and mitochondrial function. Mechanistically, we found MUC1 attenuated senescence and associated cell dysfunction, including activation of PINK1/Parkin-dependent mitophagy flux and AMPK/NDUFS4-driven mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming in AT2 cells. In addition, MUC1 modulated CS extract (CSE)-induced human AT2-to-AT1 transdifferentiation through enhancement of β-catenin nuclear translocation. Moreover, overexpression of MUC1 in lung epithelial cells inhibited CS-induced NF-κB activation and inflammatory responses in both in vitro and in vivo. Collectively, this study identified MUC1 as a protective molecule and potential target for COPD, particularly emphysema, via facilitating AT2-to-AT1 cell transdifferentiation, while prohibiting senescence and inflammation.

articles.title: Echocardiography-led multimodal assessment for pulmonary hypertension in a right heart catheterization-referred cohort: incremental value of ECG and natriuretic peptides.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right heart catheterization (RHC) is the reference standard for diagnosing pulmonary hypertension (PH), whereas echocardiography is the primary noninvasive tool for identifying patients who require further evaluation. Whether electrocardiography (ECG) and natriuretic peptides provide incremental diagnostic information beyond echocardiographic assessment in patients referred for RHC remains uncertain.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 130 hospitalized patients with suspected PH who underwent echocardiography, 12-lead ECG, B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) or N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) testing, and RHC during the same admission. PH was defined as mean pulmonary arterial pressure > 20 mmHg on RHC. A temporal validation cohort of 42 consecutive eligible patients was used to evaluate the final model without refitting. To reduce collinearity, the final multimodal model included pulmonary artery systolic pressure estimated by echocardiography (PASP ECHO), ECG positivity, and BNP/NT-proBNP positivity. Model discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, areas under the curve (AUCs) were compared using DeLong's test, calibration was assessed using calibration plots and calibration metrics, and internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling.

RESULTS: Among 130 patients in the derivation cohort, 111 had PH and 19 did not. The final multimodal model showed higher discrimination than PASP ECHO alone in the derivation cohort (AUC 0.825, 95% CI 0.722-0.928 vs. 0.730, 95% CI 0.620-0.841; DeLong P = 0.008). At the Youden threshold, the final model showed high specificity but limited sensitivity, whereas a sensitivity-oriented threshold increased sensitivity at the expense of specificity. Bootstrap internal validation yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.811. In the temporal validation cohort, the final model showed an AUC of 0.792, compared with 0.749 for PASP ECHO alone; this difference was not statistically significant. Bland-Altman analysis showed wide limits of agreement between PASP ECHO and invasive systolic pressure estimates, indicating that echocardiographic and invasive pressure estimates are associated but not interchangeable.

CONCLUSIONS: In this RHC-referred suspected PH cohort, ECG and natriuretic peptide positivity provided complementary information beyond PASP ECHO. However, because of the small sample size, marked class imbalance, and limited subtype characterization, the proposed multimodal approach should be considered exploratory. Larger prospective studies with subtype stratification and external validation are required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: More than meets the lumen: The expanding role of cardiac CT.
Hormones, glycaemia and innate immunity: correlates of NK cell dysfunction in type 2 diabetes.
articles.journal: Hormone molecular biology and clinical investigation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is linked to impaired natural killer (NK) cell function and altered sex hormone homeostasis. We examined the associations of HbA1c, sex hormones and NK-cell subsets with peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) cytotoxicity.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 58 patients with T2DM and 62 metabolically healthy controls were enrolled. PBMC cytotoxicity (specific lysis of K-562-GFP target cells, an NK cell-associated readout) was measured by flow cytometry. Serum estradiol, testosterone and HbA1c were measured, and NK-cell subsets were quantified by flow cytometry. In an exploratory sub-cohort of 16 patients undergoing bariatric surgery, omental adipose tissue (OAT)-derived immune cells were compared with paired PBMCs.

RESULTS: There was a reduction in PBMC cytotoxicity for men with T2DM compared to control men and for women compared to men with T2DM. Multiple regression analysis showed that the cortisol level and PBMC cytotoxicity were inversely correlated (adjusted R2=0.218), while the testosterone level and percentage of CD56+CD16+ NK-cells were positively correlated (adjusted R2=0.218). The OAT-derived cells proved to be more cytotoxic than matched PBMCs (p=0.0005).

CONCLUSIONS: These are theory generating associations. The cross-sectional design and limited number of children in the OAT sub-cohort and the lack of surgical control group in the non-diabetic population limit the ability to make causal inferences and need to be confirmed in future prospective studies.

articles.title: Semaglutide (Wegovy) for secondary cardiovascular prevention in adults with an elevated BMI.
Effect of Infection-Site-Targeted Postural Drainage on Mechanical Ventilation Duration in Intensive Care Unit Patients: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: The journal of nursing research : JNR
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mechanical ventilation (MV) is essential for intensive care unit (ICU) patients with respiratory failure, but prolonged MV increases the risk of complications.

PURPOSE: This study was conducted to evaluate the effect of infection-site-targeted postural drainage, guided by imaging, on patient outcomes compared with conventional care.

METHODS: In this randomized controlled trial, 384 ICU patients requiring MV were assigned to either the personalized-care group (PCG), which received imaging-guided drainage, or the routine-care group (RCG), which received standard positional changes. The primary outcome was MV duration, and secondary outcomes included PaO2/FiO2 (PF) ratios, ICU/hospital length of stay, and 28-day mortality.

RESULTS: The PCG was found to have significantly shorter MV duration (median 7 vs. 9 days, p<.05) and higher PF ratios at critical time points (X2, X4, X5; p<.001). A shorter average ICU stay length was reported for the PCG (12.3 vs. 13.4 days), although the difference was not significant after multivariable adjustment. No between-group difference was observed in terms of 28-day mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: The results indicate that imaging-guided, nursing-led postural drainage effectively improves pulmonary function and shortens MV and ICU lengths of stay without increasing mortality risk, supporting the integration of individualized pulmonary care, potentially enhanced through intelligent technologies, into routine ICU practice.

articles.title: Renal Outcomes With Staged Versus Concomitant PCI and TAVR: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
A sex-specific platelet switch controls anti-tumor immunity in glioblastoma.
articles.abstract: Sex differences in glioblastoma (GBM) outcomes are shaped by biological, hormonal, and immune factors, but the mechanisms driving these disparities remain unclear. We identify platelet protease-activated receptor 4 (PAR4) signaling as a regulator of sex-specific anti-tumor immunity. GBM patients exhibit increased platelet reactivity driven by PAR4. In murine models, pharmacologic or genetic inhibition of PAR4 prolongs survival in females, but not males, and is estrogen dependent, persisting in hormonal females regardless of chromosomal sex. The survival advantage is mediated within the tumor microenvironment through enhanced CD8+ T cell infiltration and function. PAR4-activated platelets suppress CD8+ T cell activity, whereas CD8+ T cell depletion abolishes both tumor-induced platelet reactivity and the PAR4-dependent survival advantage. Mechanistically, PAR4 inhibition enhances CD8+ T cell signaling through interaction with estrogen receptor β (ERβ). These findings demonstrate that platelets are critical regulators of sex-specific anti-tumor immunity and identify PAR4 as a promising therapeutic target in cancer.

articles.title: Cross-database generalization of a single-feature threshold model for congestive heart failure detection from short-term heart rate variability.
articles.abstract: Objective.To evaluate the transferability of interpretable single-feature threshold models across the five evaluated databases for congestive heart failure (CHF) detection from short-term heart rate variability (HRV), and to compare their performance with optimized multi-feature classifiers.Approach.Twenty HRV features from 60 s inter-beat interval windows in five databases were evaluated using leave-one-database-pair-out nested cross-validation with six outer-test sets and their corresponding outer-development sets. Within each outer-development set, directions and thresholds were fitted on inner-train sets, and features were selected according to mean inner-validationF1 score. The selected model was refitted on the complete outer-development set. The most frequently selected feature was further evaluated across the six outer-test sets with separately fitted directions and thresholds. Eight multi-feature classifiers were optimized and evaluated using the same data splits. Performance was assessed using record-balanced window-level metrics and database-stratified recording-level bootstrap confidence intervals.Main results.The short-term detrended fluctuation analysis scaling exponent (f14) was selected most frequently. The f14 threshold model achieved the highest mean test AUC (0.881 ± 0.038),F1 score (0.718 ± 0.079), and sensitivity among the evaluated single-feature and multi-feature models. Among the eight multi-feature classifiers, Random Forest achieved the highest mean test AUC (0.858 ± 0.067).Significance. An interpretable single-feature threshold model showed strong CHF-normal sinus rhythm discrimination in the five evaluated databases. f14 was the strongest candidate in this evaluation, although its thresholds varied across outer-development sets and its clinical specificity requires further validation.

articles.title: 3D-Printed Microneedles for Periodontal and Oral Mucosal Therapy: A Systematic Review of Therapeutic and Fabrication Strategies.
articles.abstract: Microneedles (MNs) technologies have emerged as a promising platform for localized drug delivery in the mouth, offering minimally invasive access to the oral mucosa, including gingival tissues. However, their integration with advanced additive manufacturing remains underexplored, despite the need for high-precision, patient-specific devices that can overcome the limitations of conventional pharmacotherapy. This review analyzes the recent developments in 3D-printed MNs for intraoral drug delivery, focusing on polymeric designs enabled by stereolithography, digital light processing, continuous liquid interface production, and two-photon polymerization. High-resolution vat-photopolymerization systems demonstrate superior spatial resolution and fabrication accuracy, allowing the reproducible production of MNs geometries with optimized tip radii, internal channels, and drug-loading microstructures. MNs-mediated delivery of antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and healing-promoting agents demonstrates potential not only for the management of periodontal inflammation, oral mucosal lesions, and soft-tissue defects but also for preventive interventions in early-stage diseases and for the control of recurrence. Despite these advances, major barriers persist, including limited in vivo validation under dynamic oral conditions, insufficient mechanical assessment under masticatory forces and salivary flow, and a lack of standardized regulatory frameworks for intraoral MNs devices. Overall, the current findings indicate that 3D-printed MNs represent an emerging and highly promising class of localized therapeutic delivery systems for the management of conditions affecting the periodontal tissues and the oral mucosa, with substantial opportunities for technological refinement and clinical translation.

articles.title: Antibiotics and outcomes of cancer immunotherapy: An updated meta-analysis and clinical applications.
articles.abstract: The gut microbiome is a modifiable determinant of response to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI), positioning antibiotic exposure as a critical yet under-recognized risk factor for worse survival outcomes in immuno-oncology. As nearly 30% of ICI-treated patients receive antibiotics and indications of cancer immunotherapy are expanding, this issue represents a global challenge in oncology. Here, we paint an updated and comprehensive landscape of antibiotic exposure in immuno-oncology, provide actionable clinical recommendations, and envision future avenues for improvement. First, we describe the biological mechanisms by which antibiotic-induced dysbiosis contributes to ICI resistance. Next, through an updated meta-analysis of 116 cohorts and 97,850 cancer patients treated with ICI, we found a significant association between antibiotic exposure and survival outcomes (overall survival, hazard ratio [HR]: 1.49, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.34-1.65; progression-free survival, HR: 1.44, 95% CI: 1.31-1.58). Finally, we discuss antibiotics stewardship and microbiome-centered strategies to prevent, diagnose, and/or repair dysbiosis.

articles.title: A one-step LAMP-CRISPR/Cas12a platform targeting lytA and cpsA for rapid parallel identification and virulence stratification of Streptococcus pneumoniae.
articles.abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae (S. pneumoniae, SPN) is the primary pathogen causing community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), purulent meningitis, sepsis, and acute otitis media. Accurate species identification and rapid differentiation of invasive strains are critical for clinical management and infection control. Based on loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) and CRISPR/Cas12a technologies, this study established a parallel dual-target detection platform targeting the S. pneumoniae-specific lytA gene and the capsular polysaccharide synthesis regulatory gene cpsA. A dual-readout mode combining fluorescence detection (FD) and lateral flow test strip (LFTS) was adopted to meet diverse laboratory testing requirements. For each target-specific reaction, LAMP amplification and CRISPR/Cas12a cleavage were sequentially performed in a single closed tube using paraffin-oil stratification to suppress solvent evaporation, effectively preventing aerosol contamination. Range-finding serial-dilution assays revealed that the lowest gDNA concentrations producing positive signals in all three technical replicates reached 1 fg μL-1 (FD) and 10 fg μL-1 (LFTS). This assay specifically distinguished S. pneumoniae from other common clinical pathogens and preliminarily identified encapsulated invasive strains, with 100% sensitivity and specificity consistent with conventional PCR. This LAMP-CRISPR/Cas12a platform, with its closed-tube design, avoids contamination, while FD and LFTS dual readouts cater to diverse testing needs. Featuring high sensitivity, excellent specificity, simplicity, and speed, it provides an innovative and practical solution for the rapid diagnosis of S. pneumoniae and holds great clinical potential.

articles.title: Agricultural waste-derived sweat sensor integrated into wettability-tunable microfluidics for noninvasive metabolic evaluation.
articles.abstract: Wearable sweat patches allow real-time and noninvasive monitoring of metabolism through sweat biomarker analysis. However, challenges related to sweat collection efficiency and the lack of sustainable sweat sensors impede the widespread adoption of sweat analysis. Here, we report the design of a wearable sweat patch integrating an agricultural waste-derived sweat sensor for sensitive sweat uric acid (UA) and glucose (Glu) analysis and surface wettability-controlled microfluidics for efficient sweat collection. We evaluate the performance of the wearable patch for the noninvasive monitoring of UA and Glu in sweat. We also validate the usability of the wearable patch in assessing metabolic status in metabolic disorders including gout and diabetes.

articles.title: Prenatal ambient ozone exposure and risk of offspring congenital heart disease: A three-level meta-analysis.
authors: All authors have read and approved the final manuscript
articles.journal: Journal of the Air & Waste Management Association (1995)
articles.abstract: Prenatal exposure to ambient ozone has been hypothesized to increase the risk of congenital heart defects (CHD) in offspring; however, epidemiological evidence remains inconclusive. To quantitatively synthesize the available evidence on the association between prenatal ambient ozone exposure and the risk of congenital heart defects (CHD) in offspring, and to explore potential effect modifiers through subgroup analyses and meta regression. The PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, Embase and CNKI databases were systemically searched from 1970 until April 2026 to find articles related to offspring CHD and periconceptional ozone exposure. Inverse variance weighted random-effects multilevel models were conducted to pool estimates and stratify associations by heart defect type, country income level, study design, investigation time period, and data source. Dose-response relationships were examined via meta-regression and the heterogeneity and publication bias in relevant studies was also examined. A total of 29 studies comprising 302 effect estimates were identified. The overall pooled odds ratio for the association between prenatal ozone exposure and CHD was 1.032 (95% CI: 1.004-1.060). Stronger associations were observed for transposition of the great arteries (OR = 1.172), conotruncal defects (OR = 1.134), and atrioventricular septal defects (OR = 1.204). The embryonic period was the most susceptible exposure window (OR = 1.064, 95% CI: 1.006-1.126). Stronger effects were found in upper-middle-income countries (OR = 1.039), studies conducted after 2020 (OR = 1.145), and hospital-based data (OR = 1.112). Dose-response analysis suggested a 1% odds increase per 10 μg/m3 ozone increment, though not statistically significant. Considerable heterogeneity was observed. This meta-analysis suggests that prenatal ozone exposure may modestly increase CHD risk. The substantial heterogeneity highlights the need for standardized exposure assessment and further prospective studies.

articles.title: Liquorice flavonoids ameliorate type 2 diabetes mellitus via modulation of the AMPK/mTORC1/AKT signalling network.
articles.abstract: The increasing global burden of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and the limited efficacy of single-target therapies highlight the potential of multi-component interventions. Here, liquorice flavonoids (LF), a multi-component extract from Glycyrrhiza uralensis, were evaluated for their antidiabetic effects and underlying mechanisms in T2DM. LF were prepared and chemically characterised by LC-MS-based profiling and quantitative analysis and their effects were assessed in high-fat, high-sugar diet/streptozotocin (HFD/STZ)-induced diabetic mice and sodium palmitate (SP)-induced insulin resistance (IR) HepG2 cells. LF markedly improved metabolic abnormalities in diabetic mice, as evidenced by reduced fasting glucose levels, improved glucose handling and insulin sensitivity, together with alleviation of dyslipidemia. In IR HepG2 cells, LF promoted glycogen synthesis, suppressed gluconeogenesis and lipogenesis, and enhanced fatty acid oxidation. Mechanistically, LF modulated the AMPK/mTORC1/AKT signalling network, as evidenced by increased AMPK and AKT phosphorylation and reduced mTORC1 activity. Pharmacological inhibition of AMPK with BAY-3827 partially attenuated LF-induced signalling changes, supporting a role for AMPK while suggesting the involvement of additional regulatory mechanisms. Collectively, these results support the potential of LF as a multi-component therapeutic strategy for T2DM and offer mechanistic insight into its beneficial effects on metabolic dysfunction through the AMPK/mTORC1/AKT signalling network.

articles.title: Commercial and Novel Drug-Loaded Coatings with Anticoagulant and/or Antibacterial Functions for Clinical Applications.
articles.abstract: Drug-loaded coatings significantly improve the bioactivities of multiple medical devices. The most widespread applications are assembling anticoagulant coatings on blood-contacting medical devices to enhance blood compatibility and applying antibacterial coatings to prevent device-induced infection. Notably, a vicious cycle between bacterial infection and thrombosis may result in deterioration of condition and even lead to treatment failure. Thrombosis caused by blood incompatibility of medical devices provides niduses for bacterial colonization, whereas bacterial endotoxins accelerate thrombosis by activating platelets. In some situations, the interactional process can also trigger inflammatory responses and calcification processes. Therefore, the demands for anticoagulant and antibacterial are necessary and mutually influenced. This review presents a summary of current commercial drug-loaded anticoagulant coatings and a detailed report on novel drug-loaded coatings with anticoagulant and/or antibacterial effects. We highlight the synthesis and assembly techniques, drug-release duration, and biofunctional behavior of referenced coatings. Based on careful comparison and comprehensive summary of the state-of-the-art literature, this review reveals the difficulties in large-scale production of the emerging coatings and the functional differences compared to the existing commercial coatings, and predicts the general process for manufacturing and commercialization.

articles.title: Current Advances in Antioxidant Nanozymes for Liver Diseases.
articles.abstract: The liver with unique physiological functions is susceptible to oxidative stress (OS) damage from reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, further triggering various liver diseases. Compared with conventional pharmacological and surgical therapies, natural antioxidant enzymes represent promise for liver disease therapy due to high ROS scavenging and low immunogenicity. However, their clinical translation is limited by instability and complex preparation. Antioxidant nanozymes not only mimic natural enzymes, but possess advantages including simple structure, low cost and high stability. They have emerged as ideal therapeutic options for liver diseases by mitigating OS, modulating inflammation, and remodeling the pathological microenvironment. This review innovatively elucidates hepatic OS pathogenesis from a synergistic perspective, integrating indirect (inflammatory pathways) and direct (organelle stress, oxidase activation) ROS generation routes, thereby filling gaps in existing literature. Subsequently, we systematically summarize advances in five representative classes of nanomaterials: metal-, selenium-, carbon-, organic- and metal-organic frameworks (MOF)-based, and emphasize catalytic mechanisms and activity regulation strategies to guide the design of effective, low-toxicity antioxidant nanozymes. Furthermore, this review highlights recent progress of antioxidant nanozymes in typical liver diseases, including drug-induced liver injury, hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury, liver fibrosis, and acute liver failure, alongside clinical translation bottlenecks. Finally, current challenges and future perspectives for antioxidant nanozymes are outlined.

articles.title: Firmonertinib in advanced non-small cell lung cancer with epidermal growth factor receptor P-loop and αC-helix compressing mutations.
articles.abstract: P-loop and αC-helix compressing (PACC) mutations comprise a structurally distinct subgroup of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with limited treatment options. Firmonertinib is a once-daily oral, brain-penetrant, mutant-selective EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor with a unique trifluoroethoxy side chain. Firmonertinib had high anti-proliferative efficacy in EGFR PACC-mutant cells and xenografts. In the phase 1b FURTHER study (NCT05364073), patients with metastatic EGFR PACC-mutant NSCLC randomized to receive first-line firmonertinib 160 mg (n = 25) or 240 mg (n = 22) had confirmed objective response rates (ORRs) of 43% and 68%, median duration of response not reached and 14.6 months, and median progression-free survival of 11.1 and 16.0 months, respectively; treatment-related adverse events led to dose reductions (19% and 24%) and discontinuation (3% and 0%). Intracranial ORR among patients with brain metastases at baseline was 47% (8/17). Results support further study of first-line firmonertinib in patients with EGFR PACC-mutant NSCLC.

articles.title: Micro and nanoscale probes for spatiotemporal cell analysis and manipulation.
articles.abstract: Understanding dynamic cellular processes requires technologies capable of probing living cells with high spatial and temporal precision while preserving viability. Conventional approaches, including bulk omics, microinjection, and electroporation, often provide only static snapshots or induce significant cellular perturbation. Recent advances in micro- and nanoscale probes are enabling minimally invasive intracellular delivery, sampling, sensing, and manipulation with unprecedented precision. This review examines the current state of the art in micro and nanoscale probe technologies, including fluidic force microscopy (FluidFM), nanopipettes, open-space microfluidic probes, and nanoneedle arrays. We discuss how these complementary platforms enable controlled delivery of biomolecules, longitudinal molecular sampling, intracellular electrophysiology, electrochemical sensing, and spatiotemporally resolved analyses from single cells to living tissues. We placed particular emphasis on their ability to overcome the limitations of destructive endpoint assays by facilitating repeated interrogation of the same cell, quantitative molecular delivery, and multimodal measurements with subcellular resolution. Finally, we discuss the remaining engineering challenges, including improving throughput, integrating complementary sensing modalities, and advancing these promising technologies into robust platforms for laboratory studies of cultured cells and tissues.

articles.title: In-Situ Dynamic Chemical Reconstruction Synthesis of Dual-Antioxidants for Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Treatment.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a serious circulatory system disease characterized by redox imbalance, which results from the overexpressed reactive oxygen species (ROS) and inactivated antioxidation defense system. In this work, a dynamic chemical reconstruction strategy has been developed for PAH treatment through the in situ synthesis of antioxidant nanocatalyst MoOy and selenium oxyanions from a molybdenum selenide nanosystem in response to the oxidative microenvironment of PAH. MoOy nanoparticles catalyze the exogenous antioxidation reactions to scavenge ROS efficiently, while the soluble selenium oxyanions upregulate the expression of selenoproteins to reinforce the endogenous antioxidant defense system. These two processes cooperatively alleviate oxidative stress of pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs), thus suppressing their malignant proliferation/migration and finally mitigating pulmonary arterial remodeling for PAH treatment. This work presents a dynamic chemical reconstruction strategy for in situ synthesis of exogenous and endogenous antioxidants, offering a dual-axis antioxidation approach for the treatment of multiple redox imbalance-associated diseases.

articles.title: Hydration-Gated Photoinduced Electron Transfer in BODIPY Dyes.
articles.abstract: Fluorescent probes based on photoinduced electron transfer (PET) are widely used to image intracellular environments. Here we report donor-acceptor dyads based on the BODIPY chromophore in which PET is selectively activated upon hydration. Replacing fluorine groups at boron with triethylene glycol (TEG) chains confers aqueous solubility and modulates the electronic properties of the boron-coordinated core, suppressing PET in polar organic solvents while enabling efficient charge separation in water. This switching arises from hydrogen bonding at the alkoxy oxygens, which strengthens the effective acceptor character of the BODIPY, supported by electrochemistry, transient absorption spectroscopy, and DFT calculations. The mechanism is general across dyads incorporating various aromatic donors and BODIPY substitution patterns. The lead compound, 5-TEG, displays hydration-dependent fluorescence lifetimes spanning a 6 ns range. In fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) of living cells, tumor spheroids, and intestinal organoids, 5-TEG provides high brightness and lifetime contrast, enabling segmentation of subcellular compartments and reporting on microenvironmental differences. These results establish hydration-gated PET as a tunable photophysical mechanism for designing fluorescence probes with lifetime-encoded readouts in complex biological environments.

articles.title: Sustainable Electrosynthesis of Hexamethylenetetramine via Paired Electrolysis of Nitrate and PET Waste.
articles.abstract: Hexamethylenetetramine (HMTA) is a critical organonitrogen compound widely used in the defense, pharmaceutical, and polymer industries. Conventional HMTA production relies on toxic formaldehyde (HCHO) and energy-intensive Haber-Bosch-derived ammonia (NH3) as feedstocks. This study demonstrates a sustainable electrocatalytic approach for the direct synthesis of HMTA via paired electrolysis, using nitrate (NO3 -) and polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste as nitrogen and carbon sources, respectively. With iron-doped nickel phosphide (Fe-Ni2P) as a bifunctional catalyst, the system achieves concurrent cathodic NO3 - reduction to NH3 with a Faradaic efficiency of ∼ 96.0%, and anodic oxidation of PET-derived ethylene glycol to electrophilic *HCHO intermediates. These resulting intermediates subsequently condense with nucleophilic NH3 to form HMTA with ∼75.2% carbon selectivity. Mechanistic studies reveal that Fe doping induces charge redistribution and upshifts the d-band center, thereby facilitating the adsorption and activation of reactants and lowering the energy barrier for *HCHO intermediate formation and desorption-a critical step enabling subsequent C─N coupling. This work establishes a mild and sustainable electrocatalytic route for HMTA synthesis from environmental waste, underscoring the potential of paired electrolysis in valorizing waste into valuable organonitrogen chemicals.

articles.title: Stoichiometric Reduction of Dinitrogen to Hydrazine Upon Protonation of Heterobimetallic Chromium-Aluminum Hydride Complexes.
articles.abstract: The activation of dinitrogen (N2) via heterobimetallic cooperation remains a compelling strategy for N2 functionalization. Herein, we report the synthesis and reactivity of a well-defined chromium-aluminum hydride dinitrogen complex, [(depe)2(H)Cr(μ-N2)AlH2]2 (depe = Et2PCH2CH2PEt2). Crystallographic and spectroscopic analyses reveal substantial N2 reduction driven by a "push-pull" interaction between the electron-rich Cr centers and the electrophilic Al Lewis acid core. Upon stoichiometric protonation with [Ph2NH2]OTf, the highly activated bridging N2 units undergo selective proton-coupled reduction to release hydrazine (N2H4) in up to 97% yield. Crucially, structure-reactivity investigations reveal a clear correlation between the presence of the central Al─H bonds and the selective hydrazine formation. Furthermore, the central aluminum hydrides exhibit high regioselectivity toward silyl electrophiles, enabling the precise construction of fully and partially substituted derivatives; notably, in 5-8 the Cr─N2-Al motif and terminal Cr─H units are retained. Subsequent redox investigations demonstrate that deep chemical reduction induces a core rearrangement into a unique complex, [(depe)2(H)Cr(μ-N2)]2(μ-AlH2)(μ-Li), followed by multimetallic cleavage. These transformations underscore the essential role of the Lewis acidic Al(III) center in maintaining multimetallic structural integrity and sustaining N2 activation. Overall, these findings define a heterobimetallic Cr─Al hydride framework in which the central Al─H motif governs stoichiometric hydrazine release and site-selective hydride functionalization.

articles.title: Mild caloric restriction accelerates atherosclerosis via dysregulated cholesterol homeostasis and lipogenesis in HCHF-fed ApoE-deficient mice.
articles.abstract: Recent ACC/AHA guidelines recommend ≥ 5% weight loss over 6 months to reduce cardiovascular risk in obesity. However, some populations paradoxically exhibit increased cardiovascular disease (CVD) following weight loss. We investigated whether mild food restriction (MfR) accelerates atherogenesis through proatherogenic lipid remodeling. ApoE-deficient mice were fed Chow or a high-cholesterol/high-fat (HCHF) diet for 6 months, with MfR producing 5% lower body-weight gain. Atherosclerotic burden was quantified histologically, and hepatic lipidomes were analyzed by electrospray ionization tandem mass spectrometry (ESI-MS/MS) and compared with plasma lipidomic profiles from patients with CVD. MfR improved insulin sensitivity by lowering blood glucose and triglycerides but increased circulating cholesterol and accelerated atherosclerosis. HCHF-fed mice developed larger, more numerous plaques with increased necrotic core formation, thinner fibrous caps, higher intima/media ratios, and inflammatory cell infiltration. Similar proatherogenic changes occurred in Chow-fed mice subjected to MfR. Mechanistically, MfR increased hepatic free cholesterol and enriched proatherogenic phosphatidylcholine, phosphatidylethanolamine, lysophosphatidylcholine, sphingomyelin, ceramide, and cholesterol ester species, yielding a CERT1 score of 8.1 indicative of cardiovascular risk. These lipid alterations mirrored plasma lipidomic signatures from patients with CVD with diabetes. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that mild caloric restriction is not universally atheroprotective and can accelerate atherosclerosis in hypercholesterolemic states by disrupting cholesterol homeostasis and promoting proatherogenic lipid remodeling.

articles.title: Discovery and Bioinspired Synthesis of Neuroprotective Geranylated Chalcones From Artocarpus communis.
articles.abstract: Two geranylated chalcone oligomers, artocarpusones A (1) and B (2), featuring a highly functionalized 6/5/6/5/6-fused pentacyclic hemiketal, were discovered from the medicinal plant Artocarpus communis, along with six related compounds 3-8. Their structures with absolute configurations were established using comprehensive spectroscopic analyses that were supported by computational calculations. Biosynthetic considerations suggest that 1-7 could be derived from a single precursor 8. Guided by this insight, a bioinspired synthesis of 1-7 was achieved in a total of 7-9 steps from 8. The synthesis is enabled by bioinspired cascade reactions encompassing oxidative rearrangement, Michael additions, hemiketalizations, 6π-electrocyclization, and hetero-Diels-Alder reaction. Notably, congener 2 exhibited anti-ischemic stroke activity both in vitro and in vivo, suggesting its potential as a neuroprotective candidate for further therapeutic evaluation.

articles.title: Loss of ADAMTS9 disrupts ciliogenesis and collagen homeostasis, resulting in nephronophthisis-like polycystic kidneys.
articles.abstract: ADAMTS9 mutations cause the ciliopathies nephronophthisis and Joubert syndrome. Here we demonstrated that deletion of ADAMTS9 in the proximal nephron led to polycystic kidney development in mice. In males, Adamts9 deletion caused kidneys to become highly cystic while remaining small without undergoing enlargement. In contrast, female mice developed cystic kidneys at a slower rate. ADAMTS9 deletion disrupted ciliogenesis through the loss of cleavage of the ciliary transition zone (TZ) protein TMEM67, which led to loss of the MKS/B9 module - a key component of the ciliary gate. Functional analysis of all 8 ciliopathy patient variants of ADAMTS9 identified to date showed that the TMEM67 C-terminus failed to localize to the TZ, thus disrupting a key regulatory mechanism in patient renal ciliogenesis. Modeling ADAMTS9-mediated TMEM67 cleavage using TMEM67 cleavage-deficient mice revealed loss of TZ formation, but not elevated canonical Wnt signaling, as the underlying mechanism driving cystogenesis. Adamts9 deletion led to comparatively intense interstitial collagen deposition, which likely restricted kidney enlargement and resulted in the characteristically small kidney phenotype seen in nephronophthisis. By comparative analysis of 4 interconnected polycystic kidney models, in addition to Pkd1- and Pkd2-deleted kidneys, we identified differential collagen homeostasis as a principal factor determining cystic kidney size and type.

articles.title: Long-term reprogramming of classical monocytes with altered ontogeny mediates enhanced lung injury in sepsis survivors.
articles.abstract: Patients who survive sepsis are predisposed to new hospitalizations for respiratory failure, but the underlying mechanisms are unknown. Using a murine model in which prior sepsis predisposes to enhanced lung injury, we previously discovered that classical monocytes persist in the lungs after long-term recovery from sepsis and exhibit enhanced cytokine expression after secondary challenge with intranasal LPS. Here, we hypothesized that immune reprogramming of post-sepsis monocytes and altered ontogeny predispose to enhanced lung injury. Monocyte depletion and/or adoptive transfer was performed 3 weeks and 3 months after sepsis. Monocytes from post-sepsis mice were necessary and sufficient for enhanced LPS-induced lung injury and promoted neutrophil degranulation. Prior sepsis enhanced JAK/STAT signaling and AP-1 accessibility in monocytes and shifted monocytes toward the neutrophil-like monocyte lineage. Neutrophil-like monocytes demonstrated a proinflammatory phenotype with enhanced IL-1β expression and reduced phagocytic capacity. In human sepsis and/or pneumonia survivors, monocytes were predictive of 90-day mortality and exhibited transcriptional and proteomic neutrophil-like signatures. We conclude that sepsis reprograms monocytes into a proinflammatory phenotype and skews bone marrow progenitors and monocytes toward the neutrophil-like lineage, predisposing them to induce neutrophil degranulation and lung injury.

articles.title: Vorinostat for graft-versus-host disease prevention in pediatric and young adult patients with hematologic malignancies.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUNDThis prospective, single-arm, multicenter phase I/II trial evaluated vorinostat added to standard graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) prophylaxis in pediatric, adolescent, and young adult (AYA) patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) from HLA-matched related, HLA-matched unrelated, and haploidentical donors.METHODSPatients aged 3-39 years received twice-daily vorinostat with tacrolimus/methotrexate after HLA-matched HCT from day -10 to +30, or with posttransplant cyclophosphamide/tacrolimus/mycophenolate mofetil after haploidentical HCT from day +5 to +30. The primary endpoint was cumulative incidence of grade 2-4 acute GVHD by day +100. All outcomes were based on intention-to-treat analysis.RESULTSForty-three patients were enrolled; median age was 19 years, with 74% receiving HLA-matched and 26% haploidentical HCT. The recommended phase II dose was 60 mg/m2 twice daily. No dose-limiting toxicities, unexpected vorinostat-related serious adverse events, or primary graft failures occurred. Median neutrophil and platelet recovery occurred at 14 and 18 days, respectively. Day +100 grade 2-4 and 3-4 acute GVHD were 14% (95% CI, 5.6%-26%) and 4.7% (95% CI, 0.83%-14%), respectively. One-year overall survival was 88.4% (95% CI, 79.3%-98.5%), relapse 14% (95% CI, 5.6%-26%), nonrelapse mortality 4.7% (95% CI, 0.8%-14%), and GVHD-free/relapse-free survival 55.8% (95% CI, 42.8%-72.8%). Correlative studies demonstrated on-target HDAC activity, with increased histone.RESULTSForty-three patients were enrolled; median age was 19 years, with 74% receiving HLA-matched and 26% haploidentical HCT. The recommended phase II dose was 60 mg/m2 twice daily. No dose-limiting toxicities, unexpected vorinostat-related serious adverse events, or primary graft failures occurred. Median neutrophil and platelet recovery occurred at 14 and 18 acetylation and lower proinflammatory cytokines.CONCLUSIONThese findings support randomized evaluation of vorinostat-based GVHD prophylaxis in pediatric and AYA HCT.TRIAL REGISTRYClinicalTrials.gov NCT03842696.FUNDINGNIH grants 1R01CA249211, UG1HL069330, 1K24HL156896, and NHLBI Training Grant T32HL007622-36.

articles.title: Oxygen-Tolerant, Controlled Synthesis of Degradable and Water-Soluble Poly(Vinyl Amide)s via Radical Ring-Opening Copolymerization of Cyclic Dithiothreitol.
articles.abstract: Radical ring-opening polymerization (rROP) has emerged as a powerful strategy for introducing degradable linkages into vinyl polymer backbones. In this study, we report an oxygen-tolerant photoinduced electron/energy transfer reversible addition-fragmentation chain transfer (PET-RAFT) polymerization approach for the synthesis of degradable copolymers from cyclic dithiothreitol (cDTT) and a broad range of technologically relevant N-vinyl monomers, as well as other less activated monomers. This method gives access to well-defined copolymers with predictable molecular weights, low dispersities, and efficient cDTT incorporation. Degradable polymers were accessed using low cDTT feed ratios (2-10 mol%), enabling the preparation of materials with compositions dominated by the parent vinyl monomers while presenting multiple cleavable sites along the backbone. The incorporated cDTT generates disulfide, thioaminal, and vicinal diol functionalities, thereby enabling backbone degradation under reductive, acidic, and oxidative conditions. Despite the low cDTT content employed, which limits the extent of reductive cleavage, periodate-mediated oxidation enabled efficient and rapid backbone degradation. This work expands the scope of cyclic disulfides as comonomers in rROP and provides a practical route to degradable vinyl materials based on widely used N-vinyl species.

articles.title: Cyclooxygenase-2 negatively regulates innate lymphoid cell type 2 differentiation and function during allergic lung inflammation.
articles.abstract: Type 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2) are a population of lineage-negative cells in the lung, gastrointestinal tract, and skin that have emerged as a significant component of type 2 allergic inflammation. The regulation of cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) metabolites is critical to the pathophysiology of many inflammatory disorders, including allergic asthma. While COX-2 regulates Th9 and Th17 cell differentiation and function during allergic lung inflammation, it remains unknown whether COX-2 also regulates ILC2 cell differentiation and function under similar conditions. To address this question, we examined lung ILC2 cells from COX-2+/+ and COX-2-/- mice after ovalbumin-induced (OVA-induced) or Alternaria-induced allergic lung inflammation. ILC2 cells were significantly increased in COX-2-/- lungs compared with COX-2+/+ lungs after OVA exposure in vivo. The increase in ILC2 cells was accompanied by an increase in expression of the cytokines IL-5 and IL-13 and of the transcription factor GATA3. Both genetic disruption and selective inhibition of COX-2 significantly increased ILC2 cell differentiation from isolated common lymphoid progenitor cells (CLP) in vitro. Furthermore, COX-2-derived PGE2 acting via EP2 receptors significantly reduced IL-33 and TSLP expression, and it attenuated ILC2 cell differentiation in vitro and in vivo. Thus, during allergic lung inflammation, COX-2-derived PGE2 signals through the EP2 receptor to negatively regulate lung ILC2 cell differentiation and function.

articles.title: Cell-free hemoglobin upregulates pulmonary endothelial heparanase expression to drive glycocalyx destruction and inflammation in sepsis.
articles.abstract: Both elevated plasma cell-free hemoglobin (CFH) and heparanase-driven endothelial glycocalyx shedding are contributors to microvascular dysfunction and organ injury in sepsis. However, the mechanisms governing heparanase activation, and the potential role of CFH in this process, are not understood. Utilizing patient samples, mice with cecal slurry-induced (CS-induced) peritonitis and elevated CFH, and human lung microvascular endothelial cells (HLMVECs), we tested the hypothesis that CFH upregulates heparanase production to drive endothelial glycocalyx degradation. In human sepsis, elevated circulating CFH was associated with higher heparanase and heparan sulfate levels, which in turn correlated with adverse clinical outcomes. CS+CFH-treated mice had increased plasma heparanase, glycocalyx degradation, and pulmonary and systemic inflammation; endothelial heparanase deletion abrogated these effects. Additionally, in both pulmonary endothelial cells isolated from CS+CFH-treated mice and HLMVECs exposed to CFH and TNF-α, heparanase transcription and active enzyme production were increased. The deleterious effects of CFH were attenuated by acetaminophen, a hemoprotein reductant. In summary, we demonstrate that CFH oxidation stimulates endothelial heparanase expression and activation during sepsis, leading to endothelial glycocalyx degradation, which may disrupt the endothelial barrier and result in organ injury. Our findings highlight the CFH-heparanase axis as a potential therapeutic target for endothelial glycocalyx preservation in sepsis.
