articles.title: Sphingolipid metabolism contributes to sexual dimorphism in COPD pathogenesis.
articles.abstract: Sex-specific mechanisms in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remain poorly defined. Sphingolipids are bioactive mediators that regulate airway epithelial integrity, inflammation, and bronchial smooth muscle tone, and their dysregulation contributes to airway hyperresponsiveness. We tested whether sphingolipid metabolism is regulated by sex in COPD. Lung tissue and paired plasma from female and male never-smoking controls, ever-smoking controls, and individuals with COPD were analyzed for sphingolipid enzyme expression and metabolite levels. Bronchial rings from mice and human bronchial smooth muscle cells (HBSMCs) were exposed to estradiol or cigarette smoke extract (CSE) with and without ceramidase or sphingosine kinase inhibitors. Expression of sphingolipid regulators ASAH1 and ORMDL3 was increased in COPD airways, significantly higher in women, and correlated with airway smooth muscle remodeling. Plasma from women with COPD showed increased sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P), whereas men exhibited higher ceramide levels. Female mice displayed greater CSE-induced bronchial reactivity, attenuated by sphingosine kinase inhibition. In male donor HBSMCs, estradiol increased ASAH1, ORMDL3, S1P, and smooth muscle protein expression and enhanced contractility. CSE further augmented molecular responses in estradiol-treated cells but reduced collagen gel contraction, whereas ceramidase inhibition attenuated estradiol-dependent effects. These findings suggest that estrogen-dependent alterations in sphingolipid metabolism contribute to airway hyperreactivity and remodeling in women with COPD.

articles.title: 5-Year Follow-Up of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement With Self-Expanding Intra-Annular Versus Commercially Available Valves.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long-term outcomes of the self-expanding intra-annular Portico transcatheter aortic valve are not known.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to report the 5-year outcomes of the PORTICO IDE randomized controlled trial.

METHODS: This multicenter trial randomized (1:1) patients with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis at high/extreme surgical risk to transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with the self-expanding intra-annular valve (study valve) or Food and Drug Administration-approved commercially available valves (CAVs; balloon-expandable or self-expanding supra-annular platforms). Assessments of the primary safety endpoint (30 days) and the primary efficacy endpoint (1 year) have been previously reported. Prespecified clinical outcomes and hemodynamic valve parameters are presented through 5 years.

RESULTS: We randomized 750 eligible patients (mean age: 83 years, 52.7% female) to the study valve (n = 381) or CAV (n = 369). Compared with CAV, the study valve showed similar 5-year all-cause mortality or stroke (55.6% vs 51.3%, P = 0.42). Cardiovascular mortality was numerically higher in the study valve group compared with the CAV group (33.4% vs 25.8%; P = 0.06). Naïve permanent pacemaker implantation was higher in the study valve group (36.6%) than the CAV group (20.3%; P < 0.0001) at 5 years. At 5 years, the study valve showed a lower mean transvalvular gradient (7.2 ± 3.0 vs 9.5 ± 6.5 mm Hg, P = 0.008), but similar valve area (1.78 ± 0.45 vs 1.71 ± 0.51 cm2, P = 0.40) compared to CAV.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients at high or extreme surgical risk, TAVR with the self-expanding intra-annular transcatheter heart valve had similar 5-year overall survival, stroke rates, and valve function compared with commercially available valves.

articles.title: Left Bundle-Branch Pacing versus Right Ventricular Pacing for Atrioventricular Block.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular pacing is associated with cardiac dyssynchrony and left ventricular systolic dysfunction. Left bundle-branch pacing preserves left ventricular electrical and mechanical synchrony, but its clinical benefits relative to right ventricular pacing in patients with atrioventricular block remain unclear.

METHODS: In this investigator-initiated, international, open-label, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned patients with atrioventricular block in a 1:1 ratio to receive left bundle-branch pacing or right ventricular pacing. The primary outcome was a composite of death from any cause, hospitalization for heart failure, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy.

RESULTS: A total of 702 patients underwent randomization, with 348 assigned to receive left bundle-branch pacing and 354 to receive right ventricular pacing; 17 patients (6 in the left bundle-branch pacing group and 11 in the right ventricular pacing group) were excluded before device implantation. A total of 685 patients (342 in the left bundle-branch pacing group and 343 in the right ventricular pacing group) were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis. The mean age of the patients was 68.4 years, and 57.5% were men. At the prespecified interim analysis, the data monitoring committee recommended early termination of the trial. At a median follow-up of 35.1 months (interquartile range, 23.6 to 40.7), a primary-outcome event had occurred in 16 patients in the left bundle-branch pacing group and in 35 patients in the right ventricular pacing group (Kaplan-Meier 4-year cumulative incidence, 8.5% and 19.2%, respectively; hazard ratio, 0.41; 95% confidence interval, 0.23 to 0.75; P = 0.003 by a stratified log-rank test). Serious adverse events unrelated to implantation procedures occurred in 39 patients (11.8%) who had received left bundle-branch pacing and in 33 patients (9.3%) who had received right ventricular pacing (P = 0.32).

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with atrioventricular block, left bundle-branch pacing was superior to right ventricular pacing in reducing the risk of a composite of death from any cause, hospitalization for heart failure, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. (Funded by Project on New Technology of Jiangsu Province and others; OptimPacing ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04624763.).

articles.title: Retatrutide Once Weekly in Adults with Knee Osteoarthritis Pain and Obesity.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Retatrutide, an investigational triple agonist of GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon receptors, may be useful for the treatment of painful knee osteoarthritis in persons with obesity.

METHODS: In two phase 3 trials, adults without diabetes who had painful knee osteoarthritis and a body-mass index of at least 27 were randomly assigned to receive once-weekly subcutaneous retatrutide (9 or 12 mg in TRIUMPH-4 and 4, 9, or 12 mg in TRIUMPH-1-OA) or placebo. In TRIUMPH-4, the primary end points were the change in the WOMAC pain score (range, 0 to 10, with higher scores indicating worse pain) and the percent change in body weight at week 68. In TRIUMPH-1-OA, the primary end point was the change in the WOMAC pain score at week 80. For non-pain-related end points, intercurrent events were handled with a treatment-policy strategy. For pain-related end points, a hybrid-treatment estimand was applied, with a hypothetical strategy for intercurrent events that suggested treatment failure and a treatment-policy strategy elsewhere. We also report results for an intention-to-treat (ITT) estimand.

RESULTS: A total of 445 participants underwent randomization in TRIUMPH-4 and 574 in TRIUMPH-1-OA. At 68 weeks, the mean changes in the WOMAC pain score (hybrid-treatment estimand) with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-4 were -3.96 (9 mg) and -3.74 (12 mg), versus -2.12 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -1.83 [95% confidence interval {CI}, -2.37 to -1.30] and -1.61 [95% CI, -2.16 to -1.07], respectively). For the ITT estimand, the corresponding differences from placebo were -1.70 (95% CI, -2.19 to -1.22) and -1.38 (95% CI, -1.91 to -0.85) (P<0.001 for all comparisons). The mean percent changes in body weight with retatrutide were -20.0% (9 mg) and -23.7% (12 mg), versus -4.6% with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -15.4 percentage points [95% CI, -18.7 to -12.1] and -19.2 percentage points [95% CI, -22.4 to -15.9]; P<0.001 for both comparisons). At 80 weeks, the mean changes in the WOMAC pain score (hybrid-treatment estimand) with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-1-OA were -3.22 (4 mg), -3.48 (9 mg), and -3.64 (12 mg), versus -1.87 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -1.35 [95% CI, -1.92 to -0.78], -1.61 [95% CI, -2.20 to -1.02], and -1.77 [95% CI, -2.34 to -1.20], respectively). For the ITT estimand, the corresponding differences from placebo were -0.96 (95% CI, -1.61 to -0.30), -1.41 (95% CI, -2.07 to -0.75), and -1.64 (95% CI, -2.26 to -1.02) (P≤0.005 for all comparisons). In both trials, serious adverse events were more common with retatrutide than with placebo, and the most common adverse events were gastrointestinal.

CONCLUSIONS: In participants with painful knee osteoarthritis and obesity, treatment with retatrutide resulted in significantly greater reductions in both the WOMAC pain score and body weight than placebo. (Funded by Eli Lilly; TRIUMPH-4 and -1 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05931367 and NCT05929066.).

articles.title: Uncertainty-Guided Steering Vector Test-Time Adaptation for the Classification of Breast Ultrasound Images.
articles.abstract: Deep learning models for breast ultrasound classification frequently suffer from performance degradation due to domain shifts caused by differences in imaging equipment, acquisition protocols, and preprocessing across institutions. Although test-time adaptation (TTA) has been proposed to mitigate this problem, conventional gradient-based methods may be unstable in medical imaging settings and can even degrade performance under severe target-domain shifts. We propose Uncertainty-guided Steering Vector Test-Time Adaptation (USV-TTA), a gradient-optimization-free TTA method that performs feature correction at test time without updating model parameters. USV-TTA uses frozen source batch-normalization statistics to estimate target-sample uncertainty and derive steering vectors that represent the direction of domain shift, then corrects high-uncertainty samples by suppressing projections along this direction. USV-TTA was evaluated on 4 external breast ultrasound datasets comprising 6267 images included in the binary benign/malignant evaluation. On the class-imbalanced GDPH dataset, USV-TTA achieved the highest AUROC of 0.813, outperforming the source model and preventing the degradation observed with TENT (0.711). On the heterogeneous AJMC dataset, which included images acquired from 11 ultrasound systems, USV-TTA also achieved the highest AUROC of 0.773. On BrEaST and BUS-BRA, USV-TTA maintained competitive discrimination performance, although DLTTA achieved the highest AUROC on BrEaST and SAR achieved the highest AUROC on BUS-BRA. Across target datasets, USV-TTA reduced expected calibration error in the most challenging domains without incurring the instability observed in several gradient-based TTA methods. These findings suggest that effective and stable test-time adaptation for breast ultrasound classification can be achieved without gradient-based optimization, supporting safer deployment under domain shift.

articles.title: Clinical performance and applicability of prediction models using wearable-derived physiologic signals to anticipate migraine or headache attacks: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated the performance, risk of bias, and clinical applicability of prediction models using wearable-derived or ambulatory physiologic signals to anticipate short-term migraine or headache outcomes in adults.

BACKGROUND: A migraine or headache forecast can support self-management only when it is accurate, calibrated, actionable, and associated with an acceptable false-alarm burden. Wearable devices estimate autonomic, activity, and sleep-related features from surrogate signals, but their clinical readiness has not been systematically evaluated.

METHODS: We reviewed prediction-model studies using objective wearable or ambulatory physiologic signals to anticipate migraine or headache outcomes in adults. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to May 18, 2026. Reporting was structured according to Transparent Reporting of a Multivariable Prediction Model for Individual Prognosis or Diagnosis-Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses, with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 used for study selection. We used Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool/Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool +artificial intelligence-compatible criteria and a task-specific narrative synthesis.

RESULTS: Eight studies were included. Tasks were near-onset detection (20-40 min), night-to-next-day forecasting, and multi-day forecasting. Among comparable models, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve ranged from 0.62 to 0.84. In the largest study (146 adults; 21,550 prediction days), area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.84 (95% confidence interval, 0.82-0.85) for next-day moderate-to-severe headache and 0.76 (95% confidence interval, 0.74-0.77) for a 3-day horizon. Five studies had high analysis-domain risk of bias and three had some concerns. No study reported external validation; calibration was reported once.

CONCLUSION: Wearable-based prediction models remain early proof-of-concept studies, not clinically validated alert systems. Their reported discrimination may partly reflect between-person differences in headache frequency rather than within-person forecasting. External validation, calibration, threshold-specific alert burden, and evidence that acting on forecasts improves outcomes are needed before clinical use.

articles.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists Are Associated With Increased Incidence of Carpal Tunnel and Cubital Tunnel Syndromes: A Matched Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1As) are a novel and increasingly popular drug class for treating diabetes and obesity, which are well-known risk factors for carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) and cubital tunnel syndrome (CuTS). This study aims to assess the impact of GLP-1A medications on the development of these conditions, the effect on intervention, and subsequent complications following treatment.

METHODS: This retrospective matched cohort study utilized data from the TriNetX platform. Patients receiving GLP-1As were matched to a control cohort. The incidence of CTS and CuTS, identified via International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision diagnosis codes, was compared between the GLP-1A and control cohorts. Associated risks were calculated. Patients with an index diagnosis of CTS or CuTS were then stratified into GLP-1A use and non-use groups. Progression to initial intervention was evaluated over 5 years. Finally, outcomes were compared for patients who underwent operative treatment.

RESULTS: A total of 72 521 patients on GLP-1A were matched with a control cohort. The GLP-1A cohort was more likely to be diagnosed with CTS (odds ratio [OR], 1.33; P < .001) and CuTS (OR, 1.34; P < .001). Among patients with CTS or CuTS, the GLP-1A cohort was more likely to receive corticosteroid injection and operative management. There was no difference in postoperative opioid prescription, infection, or electromyography after undergoing carpal or cubital tunnel release between the GLP-1A and control cohorts.

CONCLUSIONS: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist use was associated with an increased risk of developing CTS and CuTS and requiring intervention. Further research is required to elucidate the mechanisms between GLP-1A use and these outcomes.

articles.title: Long-Term Outcomes of Laparoscopic Sleeve Gastrectomy at 10 Years: Weight Loss, Type 2 Diabetes Remission, and Quality of Life.
articles.abstract: Laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) is currently the most frequently performed bariatric procedure worldwide. Although its short- and mid-term efficacy is well established, its long-term durability particularly regarding sustained weight loss, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remission, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and quality of life (QoL) remains debated, and laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (LRYGB) is still considered the gold-standard metabolic procedure.

articles.title: Automated Prediction of Diabetes-Related Foot Ulcer Healing at Initial Assessment.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes-related foot ulcers (DFUs) that fail to heal within the expected trajectory and become chronic are associated with substantial morbidity. The current clinical standard for identifying chronic DFUs relies on a <50% reduction in wound area over 4 weeks. There is a critical need for tools that can predict wound-healing outcomes at first clinical presentation to enable timely, individualised wound management. We have developed and validated TherMUL, an AI device that analyses the texture of thermal images to predict DFU healing.

METHODS: Adults with neuropathic DFUs were recruited from 2 specialist foot clinics in Melbourne, Australia. TherMUL, a software-based device, was used to take thermal images during the initial visit. Texture features were extracted using grey-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) analysis. Wound-healing status at 12 weeks served as the ground-truth label for model training. A support vector machine (SVM) classifier was trained using the images from 44 healed and 24 unhealed DFUs. A separate unseen dataset was used for a preliminary feasibility assessment.

RESULTS: The classifier achieved a mean area under the curve (AUC) of 0.635, with a sensitivity of 75.8% for predicting unhealed DFUs, and a specificity of 53% for identifying healed DFUs. In the preliminary evaluation, 5 of 7 predictions correctly matched the 12-week podiatry outcomes.

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrated early feasibility of using TherMUL to assist clinicians in predicting 12-week DFU healing outcomes at first clinical presentation, with moderate discriminative performance. This non-contact, point-of-care approach has the potential to support earlier identification of DFUs unlikely to heal and enable more timely, targeted wound management strategies.

articles.title: Preventive cardiovascular ultrasound imaging: a strategy for lifelong atherosclerosis control.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Atherosclerosis develops silently over decades before manifesting as myocardial infarction, stroke, or cardiovascular (CV) death. Carotid and femoral ultrasound can identify subclinical atherosclerosis SA), quantify plaque burden, and refine cardiovascular risk assessment beyond traditional risk factors.

AREAS COVERED: This narrative review synthesizes evidence from population-based cohorts, longitudinal studies, clinical trials, and imaging investigations from 1987-2026 identified through PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar. Carotid and femoral plaque prevalence, associated risk factors, vulnerability, natural history, prediction of CV events across the lifespan, serial ultrasound assessment of plaque progression and regression, including responses to lifestyle modification and lipid-lowering therapy are discussed. Comparisons with other imaging modalities and the importance of primordial prevention to reduce cumulative exposure to CV risk factors are addressed.

EXPERT OPINION: Carotid and femoral plaque ultrasound offers a practical, accessible, radiation-free approach to detecting subclinical atherosclerosis and supporting individualized prevention. Plaque assessment may inform risk discussions, reinforce lifestyle changes, and improve adherence to appropriate lipid-lowering therapy. Standardized acquisition, reproducible measurements, and validated thresholds are needed for broader implementation. Prospective trials should establish whether ultrasound-guided prevention improves clinical outcomes. Integrating plaque imaging with sustained risk factor control and primordial prevention may help reduce the lifetime burden of atherosclerotic CV disease.

articles.title: Dental Students' Preparedness for Disability Care: A European Multicentre Study With a Focus on Hearing and Visual Impairments.
articles.journal: European journal of dental education : official journal of the Association for Dental Education in Europe
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Effective communication is essential in dental care. However, patients with hearing or visual impairments encounter barriers that hinder their understanding, expression of concerns, and participation in shared decision-making. Limited evidence is available regarding dental students' preparedness to treat these patient groups across European dental schools. This study examined dental students' self-reported confidence and desire for hands-on experience in treating patients with disabilities, as well as their educational exposure, clinical experience, and attitudes regarding patients with sensory impairments.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A multicentre cross-sectional survey was conducted among dental students in Amsterdam, Bucharest, and Copenhagen using an online questionnaire. The survey included 41 items addressing demographics, prior experience with people with disabilities, educational exposure, confidence, and attitudes towards treating patients with sensory impairments. Data were analysed using descriptive and non-parametric statistics.

RESULTS: The analysis included 146 responding students. Across the three centres, students recognised the importance of special care dentistry, while self-reported confidence was variable and low to moderate in several groups. Educational exposure appeared greater among master's students than bachelor's students; however, confidence levels varied between centres and educational levels. Clinical experience with patients with hearing and visual impairments was limited. Most respondents expressed a desire for hands-on training.

CONCLUSION: Despite recognising the importance of special care dentistry, many students reported limited confidence in treating patients with disabilities, alongside limited practical experience in managing patients with hearing and visual impairments. These findings suggest that more structured educational and clinical opportunities may help strengthen students' preparedness to treat patients with disabilities.

articles.title: Dynamic machine learning models for the early prediction of acute kidney injury following left ventricular assist device implantation: An explainable AI approach.
articles.journal: The International journal of artificial organs
articles.abstract: The risk of developing acute kidney injury (AKI) following left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation is high, making its prediction essential. Current tools are limited by relying on static, preoperative data and "black-box" models. Our aim was to create a transparent prediction tool for AKI that integrates dynamic postoperative laboratory results with explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). In a cohort of 138 LVAD patients, AKI was defined using KDIGO criteria within 7 days post-surgery. We evaluated LASSO, Random Forest, and XGBoost models, using the SMOTE method to manage class imbalance within a stratified 10-fold cross-validation. The LASSO model achieved the best performance with a ROC-AUC of 0.755. SHAP analysis revealed that dynamic postoperative laboratory changes were as important as baseline renal function in predicting AKI. Using risk scores calculated 48 h post-surgery, the model successfully predicted whether day 7 AKI would be "persistent" or "transient." Accurately predicting post-LVAD AKI is feasible using an interpretable machine learning model that tracks dynamic data. This approach can serve as a reliable tool for early risk assessment, enabling physicians to identify high-risk patients earlier and implement proactive interventions.

articles.title: Associations of the Low Arousal Threshold With Arrhythmia Burden and Heart Rate Variability in Obstructive Sleep Apnea Using Polysomnography With 24-h Holter Electrocardiography.
articles.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a widespread condition that increases the risk of arrhythmias. Recently, the role of specific OSA phenotypes, including the low respiratory arousal threshold (ArTH) phenotype, has been largely explored. This study aimed to assess whether the estimated low ArTH in patients with obstructive sleep apnea is significantly associated with arrhythmia burden and alterations in heart rate variability (HRV). Data from adults who underwent full-night video-polysomnography (vPSG) with 24-h 12-lead Holter electrocardiography (ECG) were included. ArTH was estimated noninvasively using the Edwards method. Arrhythmias were scored and counted. HRV was quantified in time, geometric, and frequency domains using ECG across a predefined circadian schedule. The analysis included 166 participants; 134 were classified as low ArTH, and 32 as high ArTH. The low ArTH group had a lower supraventricular arrhythmia burden, including fewer supraventricular premature contractions (SVPC), fewer SVPC pairs, and fewer supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) episodes than the high ArTH group. Daytime HRV differed between the groups, with higher RMSSD in low ArTH and higher LF power. In multivariable analyses, low ArTH remained associated with SVPC and SVPC pairs. Differences in HRV parameters were limited and were largely attenuated after adjustment for clinical confounders. The results suggest the potential importance of the ArTH phenotype as an independent indicator of arrhythmia in patients with OSA. However, the results should be interpreted as exploratory and hypothesis gathering. Further, prospective studies are needed to assess the utility of ArTH in risk stratification.

articles.title: Healthcare professionals' experience with early-stage (stage 1 and 2) type 1 diabetes and readiness for immunotherapies in adults: A UK-based survey.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 1 diabetes progresses through presymptomatic early stages defined by islet autoantibody positivity and glycaemia. Early detection reduces ketoacidosis and facilitates access to disease-modifying therapies. The extent to which autoantibody screening and follow-up have been adopted in UK clinical practice for adults is uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a web-based survey of members of the Association of British Clinical Diabetologists (ABCD), Diabetes Technology Network UK (DTN-UK) and Primary Care Diabetes and Obesity Society (PCDOS) between 12 December 2025 and 2 February 2026.

RESULTS: Of 164 complete responses, 116 (71%) were from doctors, 40 (24%) from nurses and 8 (5%) from other healthcare professionals. The majority were from district general hospitals (n = 91, 56%), followed by tertiary centres (n = 31, 19%), community-based and private specialist diabetes services (n = 14, 9%) and general practice (n = 28, 17%). Thirty-five per cent (11/31) in tertiary centres and 21% (22/105) in other care settings reported experience in managing adults with early-stage T1D. Among these clinicians, HbA1c was the most commonly used follow-up method (73% in tertiary centres and 86% in other settings), while approximately half offered capillary blood glucose and ketone meters and/or continuous glucose monitoring. In general practice, access to islet autoantibody testing was limited, and few had local guidelines for managing stage 1 or 2 T1D. In diabetes specialist practice, autoantibodies to GAD, IA-2 and ZnT8, but not insulin, were the most widely requested islet autoantibody assays. Perceived readiness to implement immunotherapy was low across all settings.

CONCLUSIONS: Early-stage T1D management is evolving within UK clinical practice. Monitoring and management practices broadly align with consensus recommendations. Education, national guidance and clear commissioning frameworks will be essential for successful provision of immunotherapies.

articles.title: The never-asked: Understanding the gap in emotional support for people living with diabetes.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Diabetes distress affects about one-third of adults with diabetes and is associated with poorer health outcomes, yet routine screening by healthcare professionals remains uncommon. This study examined person-reported experiences of emotional health screening across a large Australian sample.

METHODS: Adults with diabetes completed an online cross-sectional survey involving emotional health screening and assessing whether their diabetes healthcare provider had ever asked about their diabetes-related emotional health. Participant characteristics were compared by 'asked' status. A pre-specified multivariable logistic regression identified demographic and clinical predictors of never being asked. Open text responses were analysed using inductive thematic analysis.

RESULTS: Of the 1092 eligible respondents (median age 57 years [IQR 44-67]; n = 676 women [62%]; diabetes duration 10 years [4-21]; n = 274 [25%] with type 1 diabetes; n = 391 [36%] using continuous glucose monitoring [CGM]), most (n = 797; 73%) reported never being asked about their diabetes-related emotional health by their diabetes healthcare provider. Approximately 42% screened positive for diabetes distress (PAID-5 ≥ 8), with similar prevalence irrespective of 'asked' status. CGM use was the strongest predictor of being asked about emotional health, with CGM non-users having nearly double the odds of never being asked (OR = 2.00, 95% CI 1.19-3.33, p = 0.007). Seven qualitative themes emerged, highlighting the emotional burden of diabetes, inconsistent care and participants' desire to be asked about emotional wellbeing.

CONCLUSIONS: Most adults with diabetes in Australia are not asked about their emotional health, despite guideline recommendations. Elevated distress is common yet under-identified. Systemic changes are needed to close this gap.

articles.title: Systemic and Psychological Influences on Pulp Vitality Testing: Implications for Diagnostic Accuracy in Endodontics-A Narrative Review.
articles.journal: Australian endodontic journal : the journal of the Australian Society of Endodontology Inc
articles.abstract: Dental pulp vitality is traditionally assessed using sensibility tests such as thermal and electrical methods, which primarily measure nerve function rather than pulpal blood flow. Other techniques, including pulse oximetry and laser Doppler flowmetry, offer information on tooth blood flow, potentially providing a more appropriate measure of pulp health. This review explores how psychological and systemic health conditions such as anxiety, depression, diabetes and hypertension, as well as factors like aging, hormonal changes, physical activity and bruxism, can affect pulp function and responses during testing. If not carefully considered, these influences may lead to misdiagnoses. While blood flow-related methods may help address these challenges, they are not yet commonly used in clinical practice. The findings emphasize the complexities of assessing pulp vitality in patients with underlying health conditions and suggest that this could improve clinical approaches to pulp testing.

articles.title: Letter to the editor: differential effects of adenotonsillectomy on growth and asthma control in children with obstructive sleep apnea and varying body mass index: a prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery

articles.title: Taste testing: gustometry deciphered - a scoping review.
articles.journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To map and synthesize the protocols and methodological approaches used in chemical gustometry with taste solutions, focusing on taste assessment methods, the solutions and substances employed, concentration ranges and units of measurement, and the procedures used to determine taste thresholds.

METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently and in duplicate by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer. The review followed the PRISMA-ScR guidelines and was prospectively registered on the Open Science Framework.

RESULTS: Of 6,881 records identified, 10 studies met the eligibility criteria, comprising 722 participants across three clinical contexts (oncology/hematology, diabetes mellitus, and otologic disease). The whole-mouth sip-and-spit method and assessment of detection/recognition thresholds were most frequently used. Substantial heterogeneity in methods, tastants, and concentration units limited comparability across studies.

CONCLUSION: Standardization of chemical gustometry protocols remains a challenge given the methodological heterogeneity identified, underscoring the need for greater methodological rigor and consistency in future research to improve reproducibility and cross-study comparability.

articles.title: Hemodynamic effects of semaglutide in individuals with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity: a placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract: The glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist semaglutide improves symptoms in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) through unclear mechanisms. Here, in this double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, we randomly assigned 81 patients (47 women) with HFpEF and obesity to semaglutide (2.4 mg weekly) or placebo for 52 weeks. The primary outcome was the change in invasively measured pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP), a direct measure of cardiac congestion, during low-intensity exercise. Additional mechanistic outcomes included other hemodynamic measures and hemodynamic HFpEF remission (defined as normal PAWP under conditions of both rest and exercise at 52 weeks). At baseline, PAWP was 17.5 ± 4.3 mmHg at rest and 31.7 ± 5.2 mmHg during exercise. After 52 weeks, the mean change in PAWP during exercise was -9.8 (95% confidence interval (CI): -11.3 to -8.2) mmHg with semaglutide and +0.9 (95% CI: -1.3 to 3.0) mmHg with placebo (estimated difference, -10.6 mmHg; 95% CI: -13.3 to -8.0; P < 0.0001). As compared to placebo, semaglutide also decreased resting PAWP (estimated difference, -7.1 mmHg; 95% CI: -9.8 to -4.4; P < 0.0001), and semaglutide-treated patients were more likely to experience hemodynamic remission (53.7% versus 7.4%, odds ratio = 14.1, 95% CI: 3.0-134.6, P < 0.001). The results from this trial indicate that, in patients with HFpEF and obesity, treatment with semaglutide reduced left heart filling pressures during exercise and at rest and was associated with hemodynamic HFpEF remission in over half of treated patients. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05371496 .

articles.title: Editorial for "5.0 T Coronary Magnetic Resonance Angiography in Calcified Coronary Arteries: Diagnostic Performance Compared With Computed Tomography Using Invasive Angiography as Reference".
articles.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI

articles.title: AustrAIHANZ - consensus guidelines on the investigation and management of autoimmune haemolytic anaemia in Australia and New Zealand.
articles.abstract: Autoimmune haemolytic anaemia is a rare immune-mediated disorder leading to accelerated red cell destruction and anaemia. There is considerable clinical heterogeneity, with some patients barely requiring intervention, while others experience fulminant haemolysis and experience mortality rates as high as 30% with severe anaemia and end-organ ischaemia. As there is insufficient high-quality clinical data to guide management, we developed consensus practice statements based on Delphi methodology to provide clinicians with guidelines to approach diagnostic investigations, initiation of therapy, second-line treatment options, supportive care and pregnant patients.

articles.title: Longitudinal Taxonomic and Predicted Functional Gut Microbiome Responses to Tirzepatide and Semaglutide: An Exploratory Secondary Analysis of the OMDOT-1 Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Glucagon-like peptide-1-based therapies improve metabolic outcomes, but longitudinal gut microbiome dynamics remain poorly characterized. We compared taxonomic and predicted functional microbiome responses to tirzepatide and semaglutide in Type 2 diabetes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This exploratory secondary analysis included 36 participants from a randomized controlled trial comparing tirzepatide, semaglutide and conventional treatment. Faecal samples were collected at five time points over 16 weeks and analyzed by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Genus-level features were screened using MaAsLin2, and candidate genera were further evaluated using longitudinal mixed-effects models. Predicted microbial functions were inferred using PICRUSt2 and analyzed using MaAsLin2. Primary analyses were adjusted for baseline body mass index, with exploratory sensitivity analyses additionally adjusted for changes in body weight and haemoglobin A1c.

RESULTS: No significant between-group differences in beta diversity were observed. Alpha diversity increased predominantly in the tirzepatide group, with a significant time-by-treatment interaction versus control. Longitudinal trajectories relative to the control group differed for several genera, including Romboutsia_B, Barnesiella and Ruminococcus_E with both treatments and Vescimonas with tirzepatide (q < 0.05). Across 2106 predicted EC features, longitudinal effects were positively correlated between tirzepatide and semaglutide (67.1% concordant direction; Pearson r = 0.450, p < 0.001). Treatment-versus-control analyses identified predicted functional changes involving energy and carbohydrate metabolism.

CONCLUSIONS: Tirzepatide and semaglutide were associated with partially distinct taxonomic changes, accompanied by broadly similar predicted functional patterns. These longitudinal findings complement, while remaining distinct from, Week-16 shotgun metagenomic endpoint analyses.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (jRCT), jRCT1051240017.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics, Effectiveness and Safety Outcomes in Chinese Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease and Type 2 Diabetes Who Initiated Finerenone: A Retrospective Real-World Cohort Study From the FOUNTAIN Platform.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Finerenone was approved in China in 2022 for adult patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) associated with Type 2 diabetes (T2D). This study aimed to characterize Chinese patients with CKD and T2D who initiated finerenone in routine clinical practice and to evaluate treatment outcomes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study used electronic health records from Tianjin, China, and included adult patients with CKD and T2D who initiated finerenone between January 2023 and December 2024. Baseline characteristics were summarized. Relative changes in urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and serum potassium were assessed. Recorded hyperkalaemia events were evaluated during follow-up. Key outcomes were examined in the overall cohort and across subgroups.

RESULTS: A total of 6537 patients were included (66.4% male; mean age 57.6 years). Of these, 97.0% with baseline UACR and eGFR values were categorized as moderate, high, or very high Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) risk categories. At Month 4, median UACR decreased substantially by 40.7% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 32.2%, 49.1%), the mean eGFR declined slightly by 3.2% (95% CI: 2.4%, 4.0%) and the mean serum potassium increased by 4.6% (95% CI: 3.9%, 5.3%). These trends were generally consistent across subgroups. The incidence rate of hyperkalaemia events was 4.1 per 100 person-years.

CONCLUSIONS: Patients with CKD and T2D who initiated finerenone experienced a substantial reduction in UACR, a slight decrease in eGFR, and were generally well tolerated during follow-up. These findings reinforce the effectiveness and safety of finerenone in Chinese real-world clinical practice.

articles.title: Effects of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists on Hyperuricemia, Serum Uric Acid and Gout: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Hyperuricemia and gout are common but underappreciated comorbidities in Type 2 diabetes (T2D), obesity and chronic kidney disease (CKD). We aimed to quantify the pooled effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 receptor agonists on serum uric acid (SUA), incident gout and hyperuricemia, and to determine whether these effects vary by drug class and are mediated by weight loss.

METHODS: We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL and ClinicalTrials.gov through July 2026 for RCTs of ≥ 12 weeks' duration reporting SUA change, gout flares or hyperuricemia incidence. Random-effects meta-analysis, subgroup and sensitivity analyses and meta-regression were performed. Registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261468511).

RESULTS: Eighteen RCTs (77 942 participants) met inclusion criteria. Incretin-based therapy significantly reduced SUA versus control (weighted mean difference [WMD] -0.44 mg/dL, 95% CI -0.52 to -0.35), reduced incident gout flares (hazard ratio [HR] 0.62, 95% CI 0.53-0.72), and reduced hyperuricemia incidence (odds ratio [OR] 0.61, 95% CI 0.53-0.70). Dual GIP/GLP-1 RA (tirzepatide) produced greater SUA lowering than mono GLP-1 RAs (-0.62 vs. -0.35 mg/dL, p = 0.001). Body-weight loss was a significant moderator of SUA reduction (β = -0.041 mg/dL per kg, p < 0.001), explaining 84.7% of between-trial heterogeneity, with a significant weight-independent intercept (-0.19 mg/dL, p < 0.001). The SUA reduction was robust in all sensitivity analyses, including restriction to placebo-controlled trials. GRADE certainty was high for SUA and moderate for gout flares (owing to small-study effects) and hyperuricemia incidence.

CONCLUSION: Incretin-based therapies were associated with modest reductions in SUA and with a lower incidence of gout flares and hyperuricemia, an effect largely related to weight loss. The clinical relevance of these effects, and the mechanism of any weight-independent component, remains uncertain and warrant confirmation in dedicated trials.

articles.title: Lower Safety Attitudes Are Associated With Greater Rationing of Nursing Care: A Cross-Sectional Study Among Hospital Nurses.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To examine the association between nurses' safety attitudes and rationing of nursing care, and to identify organisational and individual factors associated with the frequency of care rationing.

DESIGN: Cross-sectional, correlational study.

METHODS: Data were collected from 224 registered nurses working in hospital settings in Poland. Three instruments were used: the Perceived Implicit Rationing of Nursing Care Questionnaire, the Safety Attitudes Questionnaire-Short Form (Polish cultural adaptation), and an author-developed questionnaire assessing sociodemographic characteristics and work environment factors. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson's correlation coefficients, and multiple linear regression.

RESULTS: The majority of nurses demonstrated negative safety attitudes, with fewer than one in five participants scoring above the established positive safety attitudes threshold. More positive safety attitudes were associated with lower levels of rationing of nursing care. Education level, hospital referral level, patient age group, and nurse age were identified as factors significantly associated with care rationing. Higher education level, higher hospital referral level, and providing care to adult patients were associated with increased rationing, whereas older age was associated with lower rationing.

CONCLUSION: Rationing of nursing care is associated with nurses' safety attitudes as well as with selected organisational and individual factors. These findings highlight the multifactorial nature of care rationing and underscore the role of safety culture in nursing care delivery.

IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: Strengthening patient safety culture may contribute to reducing omissions in nursing care. Healthcare organisations-particularly those operating in complex, high-acuity settings-should implement strategies that optimise workload distribution and support clinical decision-making. The findings also indicate that nurse age, rather than years of professional experience, may play a role in managing competing care demands, suggesting the potential value of structured mentoring and supervision programmes for less experienced nurses.

REPORTING METHOD: This study adhered to the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) reporting guidelines for cross-sectional studies.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: This study did not include patient or public involvement in its design, conduct, or reporting.

articles.title: Is the Developmental Stage of Grapevine Clusters a Good Predictor of Ontogenic Resistance to Plasmopara viticola?
articles.abstract: Reduction patterns in grapevine berry cluster susceptibility to downy mildew (DM) due to ontogenic resistance were investigated under different viticultural conditions in northern Italy to develop mathematical equations for predicting the infection risk of Plasmopara viticola. Clusters were inoculated with sporangial suspensions of P. viticola at different developmental stages (DS), and disease severity was assessed twice weekly. The best fit was obtained using time-dependent logistic equations in which time was expressed as cluster DS (R2 = 0.876), days after DS65 (full flowering) (R2 = 0.880), or accumulated degree-days (base 0°C) after DS65 (R2 = 0.882), all with a mean absolute error below 9%. The fitted curves consistently showed high susceptibility before and during early flowering, followed by rapid increase in ontogenic resistance after full flowering, sharp decline in susceptibility, and asymptotic approach to complete resistance. The inflection point, representing the fastest decrease in susceptibility, occurred at approximately DS72, 10 days after DS65, or 245 degree-days. Bands were empirically generated so as the Mean Absolute Error for the excluded out-of-band observations remained below the 2% disease severity threshold. Bands were widest during the rapid decline in susceptibility, reflecting variability among viticultural conditions. The DS-based equation, together with the bootstrapping variability in its parameter estimation and experimental error, was used in a Monte Carlo framework to provide a stochastic distribution of the predicted DM severities. Unlike deterministic approaches, which provide a single estimate of susceptibility at a given developmental stage, stochastic approaches produce a range of possible susceptibility levels with associated probabilities.

articles.title: Effects of semaglutide on cardiac structure and function in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity: a pre-specified cardiac magnetic resonance substudy of the CAMEO-SEMA trial.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists improve symptoms in patients with obesity and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). We recently demonstrated that semaglutide reduces exertional pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP) in obesity-related HFpEF, but potential effects of semaglutide on cardiac structure and function that may underlie these hemodynamic improvements remain unclear. In this prespecified cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) substudy of the randomized CAMEO-SEMA trial, 49 participants (33 semaglutide, 16 placebo, 28 female) underwent CMR at baseline and 52 weeks, within 1 day of invasive exercise hemodynamic assessment. The prespecified primary CMR endpoint was change in left atrial (LA) reservoir strain; other prespecified CMR endpoints included LV filling dynamics, which were assessed by early filling rate indexed to end-diastolic volume (eFR/EDV). Compared with placebo, semaglutide improved LA reservoir strain (+5.7% [95% CI, +0.3 to +9.7]; P=0.037) and eFR/EDV (+0.64 s-1 [95% CI, +0.42 to +1.00]; P<0.0001). Improvements in LA reservoir strain and LV filling dynamics were associated with reductions in exercise PAWP (r=-0.46, P<0.001 and r=-0.65, P<0.0001, respectively). With respect to other prespecified CMR endpoints, semaglutide reduced LV mass, restored more physiologic LV geometry, and improved right ventricular function and biventricular myocardial mechanics. The results of this CMR substudy indicate that in patients with obesity-related HFpEF, semaglutide improves LA function and LV diastolic filling dynamics, identifying improvements in myocardial function that may contribute to semaglutide's improvement of hemodynamics. ClinicalTrials.gov number: NCT05371496.

articles.title: On generative artificial intelligence in scientific writing.
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
articles.abstract: Scientific communication - the dissemination of ideas, hypotheses, and discoveries - is fundamental to advancing human knowledge and to ensuring public access to new knowledge as it is generated. Growth in the use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in scientific communication has been explosive, likely driven by high uptake among an adept userbase with demanding schedules, making the efficiency gains attractive. The rapid uptake of AI is creating disruptive changes in the way scientific communication happens, affecting the methods by which abstracts, manuscripts, figures, presentations, and funding proposals are generated, and in many cases impacting the final product. In this perspective piece, we reflect on the rapidly changing landscape of AI use in scientific communication with attention to the potential immediate and long-term risks. The inherent unauthorized secondary use of the data used to train AI models raises questions about credit and plagiarism in academia. Fabricated references have proliferated in the scientific literature resulting from "hallucinations" by AI models. Meanwhile, each use of an AI model comes with an incremental risk to the environment at an already perilous time. More abstractly, AI use in scientific communication risks the process itself becoming iterative, prioritizing summation while diminishing insights that fuel the scientific engine. Finally, the friction that AI models remove from writing may risk removing an essential part of the process of scientific thinking, particularly for the next generation of scientists. While we acknowledge that AI is here to stay, we feel an element of caution is warranted in its implementation, to help preserve science and its dissemination as a fundamentally human endeavor.

articles.title: Identifying Structural Heart Disease and Prioritizing Echocardiography Through Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Tele-ECG: An External Validation of the PROVAR+ Study.
articles.abstract: Structural heart disease (SHD) is underdiagnosed where echocardiography access is limited. We evaluated the role of artificial intelligence-enabled ECG for SHD detection (AI-ECG-SHD) in cardiovascular screening. We prospectively enrolled adults undergoing public-system cardiovascular screening in two Brazilian cities. Participants underwent clinical assessment, digital 12-lead tele-ECG, and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) interpreted by cardiologists. ECG signals were analyzed using a validated AI-ECG-SHD algorithm through an application programming interface. SHD was defined as moderate/severe ventricular dysfunction/hypertrophy, wall-motion abnormalities, moderate/severe valvular disease, congenital heart disease, or pericardial disease. AI-ECG-SHD performance was assessed at a predefined threshold and discrimination compared with a model incorporating clinical variables and major conventional ECG abnormalities. Number needed to screen (NNS) was calculated. Among 3,779 participants (median age 66 years; 56.7% women), 58.7% screened AI-ECG-SHD-positive and 24.2% had TTE-detected SHD. Major ECG abnormalities (OR=3.73), age (OR=1.22/10-years), male sex (OR=1.50), Chagas disease (OR=1.89), coronary disease (OR=3.01), and heart failure (OR=1.33) independently predicted SHD. AI-ECG-SHD probability (each 10% increase) was strongly associated with SHD (OR 1.55, 95%CI 1.51-1.61; p<0.001) and showed superior discrimination versus the conventional model (AUC 0.80, 95%CI 0.78-0.82 vs 0.75, 95%CI 0.74-0.77; p<0.001). AI-ECG-SHD achieved 59.4% accuracy, 87.3% sensitivity, 50.4% specificity, 92.6% negative-predictive value, diagnostic odds ratio 7.00, and NNS 4.7. AI-guided prioritization reduced estimated time to diagnosis of 50% of SHD cases from 407 to 172 days under fixed TTE capacity. In conclusion, AI-ECG-SHD improved SHD detection over conventional prediction and may enable scalable, resource-efficient TTE prioritization in underserved public healthcare systems.

articles.title: Rat hepatitis E virus RNA detection in isolated cases of acute undifferentiated febrile illness without acute hepatitis.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rat hepatitis E virus (ratHEV; Rocahepevirus ratti) is an emerging zoonotic pathogen whose clinical spectrum is predominantly hepatic. Whether ratHEV causes acute undifferentiated febrile illness (AUFI) without acute hepatitis has not been systematically evaluated.

METHODS: This retrospective observational study at a southern Spain tertiary hospital (April 2021-October 2023) evaluated patients tested for Rickettsia spp. and/or Coxiella burnetii. AUFI was defined as community-acquired fever ≥38°C lasting <21 days without localizing features or initial etiology; patients with acute hepatitis were excluded. AUFI cases were compared with contemporaneous febrile patients presenting with a localizing focus. The primary outcome was sequence-confirmed infection. Detections without sequence recovery were classified as probable infections.

RESULTS: Of 1,684 patients assessed, 312 were eligible: 81 with AUFI (median age 53 years [IQR, 37-64]; 54 [66.7%] men) and 231 comparators. Sequence-confirmed ratHEV infection occurred in 1/81 AUFI patients (1.2%; 95% CI, 0.2-6.7) and 0/231 comparators (0%; 95% CI, 0-1.6; P = 0.260). Two additional AUFI patients had detectable ratHEV RNA without sequence recovery. Combining confirmed and probable infections, ratHEV RNA was detected in 3/81 AUFI patients (3.7%; 95% CI, 1.3-10.3; P = 0.017). The confirmed infection presented as a self-limiting febrile illness without liver dysfunction, ratHEV RNA cleared upon fever resolution. The recovered genotype C1 sequence clustered with ratHEV rodent sequences from the same region.

CONCLUSIONS: RatHEV RNA was detected exclusively among AUFI patients. These findings support prospectively evaluating ratHEV as a potential cause of AUFI where the virus circulates in animal reservoirs.

articles.title: Microbiome-Targeted Interventions for Pediatric Asthma and Allergic Diseases: Current and Emerging Approaches.
articles.journal: Annals of allergy, asthma & immunology : official publication of the American College of Allergy, Asthma, & Immunology
articles.abstract: Allergic diseases are among the most common chronic diseases of childhood and remain a major public health challenge. Increasing evidence indicates that the early-life gut microbiome plays a central role in immune maturation, making it an attractive target for allergy prevention. During the first 1000 days of life, interactions between the developing microbiome and the immune system help establish immune tolerance, while disruptions to this process increase the risk of asthma and allergic diseases. Current microbiome-targeted strategies largely focus on optimizing early-life microbial exposures through interventions such as mode of delivery, antibiotic stewardship, breastfeeding, and exposure to diverse environmental microorganisms. These approaches are already incorporated into public health recommendations and promote healthy microbiome development without directly manipulating microbial communities. Newer approaches seek to intervene more precisely through microbial transfer therapies, live biotherapeutic products, prebiotics, postbiotics, and microbial metabolite-based therapies. Although several have shown encouraging preclinical and early clinical results, evidence supporting routine clinical use remains limited. The next generation of microbiome therapeutics is likely to be defined less by changing which microbes are present than by restoring the microbial functions that establish immune tolerance. This conceptual advance is driving the development of increasingly targeted microbiome-based interventions and provides a framework for the next generation of allergy prevention strategies. Translating these mechanistic insights into safe, effective therapies that complement established public health measures represents the next major challenge in preventing asthma and allergic diseases.

articles.title: Sirtuins in Cellular Senescence and Cardiovascular Diseases: From Mechanistic Basis to Activator Development and Translational Perspectives.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of mortality worldwide, and cellular senescence serves as a core driving factor in the pathogenesis and progression of cardiovascular degeneration and related diseases. Sirtuins act as a crucial molecular hub linking cellular senescence to CVDs, and their upregulated activity is closely associated with delayed cellular senescence and preserved normal cardiovascular function; therefore, the research and development of small-molecule Sirtuin-activating compounds (STACs) hold important research value and promising translational potential for CVD intervention. This review systematically elucidates the molecular mechanisms by which various Sirtuin subtypes influence senescence-related processes in CVDs through the regulation of biological events such as DNA damage repair, mitochondrial homeostasis, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses. Furthermore, it comprehensively outlines their roles in major cardiovascular conditions, including hypertension, angiogenesis, atherosclerosis, aortic aneurysm and dissection, and heart failure. Finally, this paper summarizes recent advances in the development of Sirtuin activators and, in light of current challenges such as insufficient specificity and hurdles in clinical translation, provides perspectives on the future development of Sirtuin-targeted therapies for the prevention and treatment of CVDs.

articles.title: The new steatotic liver disease nomenclature identifies different risk trajectories for liver-related complications in compensated patients.
articles.journal: Clinics and research in hepatology and gastroenterology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Recently, a new nomenclature for steatotic liver disease (SLD) defines metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), metabolic dysfunction and alcohol-associated steatotic liver disease (MetALD), and alcohol-related liver disease (ALD), according to alcohol consumption and presence of metabolic risk factors. This study aimed to identify risk factors associated with liver-related events (LREs) in patients with SLD.

METHODS: A single-center study including 335 patients with biopsy-proven SLD was conducted between 2009 and 2021. Patients with other causes of chronic liver disease or prior decompensated liver disease were excluded. The incidence of LREs and associated risk factors were analyzed using a Fine and Gray competing risk model, with non-liver-related death as a competing event.

RESULTS: A total of 335 patients were included with a median follow-up of 3.6 years. Among them, 221 were classified as MASLD, 26 as MetALD, and 88 as ALD. Advanced fibrosis (F3-F4) was observed in 55% of MASLD, 50% of MetALD, and 68% of ALD patients. During follow-up, LREs occurred in 9% of MASLD patients, 19% of MetALD patients, and 30% of ALD patients. Overall mortality was 12% in MASLD, 19% in MetALD, and 21% in ALD. In multivariable analysis, advanced fibrosis, daily alcohol intake, and diabetes were independently associated with LREs.

CONCLUSIONS: Across the SLD spectrum, alcohol consumption and fibrosis stage are major risk factors for liver-related events. Accurate assessment of alcohol intake, although challenging in clinical practice, remains essential to optimize patient care.

articles.title: Improving the Quality of Care in Advanced Prostate Cancer Through Personalised Diagnostic Testing. Outcomes of a Sharing Progress in Cancer Care taskforce conducted under the auspices of the European Association of Urology.
articles.abstract: Timely biomarker assessment is essential to optimise outcomes in prostate cancer (PCa) by enabling the appropriate use of targeted therapies for defined molecular subtypes. Several approved treatments for metastatic castration-resistant PCa, including PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy, immune checkpoint inhibition, and poly(ADP)-ribose polymerase inhibitors (PARPi), require confirmation of specific biomarkers such as PSMA expression, mismatch repair deficiency, or pathogenic variants in homologous recombination repair genes. Targeted agents are also moving into earlier disease stages, further increasing the need for early biomarker testing. Despite rapid therapeutic advances, access to biomarker-informed care remains inconsistent, potentially leading to delayed or missed treatment opportunities. A multidisciplinary task force of experts addressed challenges and solutions related to biomarker implementation for prostate cancer patients, integrating guideline-supported practice, evidence from published/ongoing studies up to June 2026, and their expert opinion. Biomarker implementation is multidisciplinary, with urologists and uro-oncologists having a coordinating role in integrating molecular testing into clinical workflows, from biopsy acquisition and test selection to interpretation and patient communication. Tumour heterogeneity necessitates a biopsy strategy combining targeted and systematic sampling. The possibility of lineage plasticity may warrant repeated sampling. Both germline and somatic testing are critical components of precision care, with potential emerging roles for circulating tumour DNA, digital pathology biomarkers, and advanced imaging such as PSMA PET. Institutional strategies, clinician training, multidisciplinary collaboration, and innovative testing models are required to overcome current barriers to sustainable implementation. Overall, improving the timelines and equity of biomarker-guided decision-making is urgent to fully realise the potential of precision oncology in PCa.

articles.title: Acute Stone-Related Healthcare Utilization Before Definitive Stone Surgery: Variation by Surgical Modality and Sociodemographic Characteristics.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize acute stone-related healthcare utilization during the year before definitive stone surgery and examine variation by surgical modality and sociodemographic characteristics.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Adults (≥ 18 years) undergoing first definitive stone surgery with ureteroscopy, shock wave lithotripsy, or percutaneous nephrolithotomy in Epic Cosmos from 2015 through 2025 were identified. Acute stone event days included unique days involving stone-related emergency department visits or hospitalizations, decompression procedures, or infections during the preceding year. Quasi-Poisson regression evaluated differences by surgical modality and, in separate modality-adjusted models, race, Social Vulnerability Index quartile, and Rural-Urban Commuting Area category.

RESULTS: Among 1,074,341 patients, 79.4% underwent ureteroscopy, 16.5% shock wave lithotripsy, and 4.1% percutaneous nephrolithotomy; 69.6% experienced at least one acute stone event day. Compared with ureteroscopy, expected event counts were higher before percutaneous nephrolithotomy (incidence rate ratio 1.18, 95% confidence interval 1.13-1.22) and lower before shock wave lithotripsy (incidence rate ratio 0.63, 95% confidence interval 0.61-0.65). Compared with White patients, burden was higher among Black patients (incidence rate ratio 1.12, 95% confidence interval 1.09-1.14). Burden increased progressively across Social Vulnerability Index quartiles, reaching 16% higher in the most versus least vulnerable quartile. No meaningful differences occurred by Rural-Urban Commuting Area category.

CONCLUSIONS: Acute stone-related healthcare utilization before definitive surgery was common and varied by surgical modality, race, and neighborhood social vulnerability, but not rurality. These findings identify populations experiencing disproportionate preoperative morbidity and support further evaluation of coordinated pathways from acute presentation to definitive stone care.

articles.title: Temporal distribution of suicide within a day among children and adolescents in Japan, 1995-2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Understanding the temporal distribution of suicidality is essential for timely support and care. However, it remains unclear how suicide deaths among children and adolescents are distributed within a day. We aimed to describe the temporal distribution of suicide death among this population and its variation by sex, school grade, day of the week, month, and calendar year.

METHODS: This nationwide descriptive epidemiologic study used vital statistics (death records) in Japan from 1995 to 2023. Cause and time of death were collected from death records. To estimate the 24-h distribution of suicide death, we used the kernel density estimator for circular data. We further stratified by sex, school grade, day of the week, month, and calendar year to explore variations in the distribution by these factors.

RESULTS: From 1995 to 2023, 9453 children and adolescents died by suicide and had valid information on time of death. The overall distribution showed a bimodal pattern with a primary peak at 18:00-19:00 and a secondary peak at 01:00-02:00. This bimodal pattern was more marked among boys with higher school grades. The evening peaks were consistently observed across weekdays, months, and years, while the evening peak was flatter on weekends.

CONCLUSIONS: Among children and adolescents, the distribution of suicide death showed the bimodal pattern with peaks at 18:00-19:00 and 01:00-02:00 while this distribution varied by demographics and temporal contexts. These findings highlight the importance of designing temporally targeted suicide prevention strategies for children and adolescents.

articles.title: Decoding PilQ: From pathogenicity to vaccine potential against fish Edwardsiellosis.
articles.abstract: Edwardsiella piscicida is an intracellular bacterium causing fish Edwardsiellosis. PilQ is the structural protein of type IV pili and crucial for bacterial virulence. This research aimed to investigate the pathogenic roles and immune protective effects of E. piscicida PilQ. PilQ contains a secretin-N domain and a secretin domain, classified as a member of the secretin protein family, and was located on the external membrane of E. piscicida. The PilQ mutation (TXD1ΔPilQ) significantly reduced bacterial survival under acidic and oxidative conditions, and the motility and biofilm formation of bacteria. Moreover, compared to wild E. piscicida, the PilQ mutation markedly decreased the adhesive and invasive capacity of E. piscicida to peripheral blood leukocytes (PBLs); meanwhile, the TXD1ΔPilQ could boost the reactive oxygen species (ROS) production of PBLs. On the other hand, antibody-mediated PilQ blocking yielded consistent phenotypes with PilQ gene deletion; moreover, the block of PilQ conspicuously suppressed the E. piscicida reproduction in PBLs. Additionally, we observe that recombinant PilQ (rPilQ) could bind to PBLs and activate the PBLs' ROS and acid phosphatase (ACP), and the vaccinated rPilQ could further activate head kidney macrophages (HKMs) vitality, heighten expression levels of immune genes, and boost the fish serum's antibacterial properties via enhancing the production of IgM, resulting in that rPilQ acted as a subunit vaccine against E. piscicida infection. The results provided the first evidence that PilQ is crucial to the E. piscicida virulence and acts as a potential candidate for developing subunit vaccines in teleost.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of obinutuzumab β in patients with active systemic lupus erythematosus: a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: B cells play a central role in the pathogenesis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and are a therapeutic target. We therefore assessed the efficacy and safety of obinutuzumab β, a glycoengineered type II anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody, in patients with active SLE.

METHODS: In this multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial, we enrolled patients who were aged 18-80 years, fulfilled the 2019 European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology-American College of Rheumatology classification criteria for SLE, and had active disease (defined as a Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Disease Activity Index 2000 [SLEDAI-2K] score of 8 or more and positivity for antinuclear antibodies or anti-double stranded DNA antibodies) at 30 tertiary hospitals in China. Participants were randomly allocated 1:1 to receive obinutuzumab β or placebo, stratified by SLEDAI-2K score and 24-h urine protein level. Patients, investigators, and the sponsor were masked to treatment allocation. Patients received intravenous infusions of obinutuzumab β (1000 mg) or placebo on days 1, 15, 169, 183, 365, and 379. All patients maintained their background standard therapy. The primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of patients with an SLE Responder Index (SRI)-4 response at week 12 assessed in all patients who were randomly assigned and received at least one dose of study treatment (ie, the full analysis set). Safety was assessed in all patients who received any study treatment and had at least one post-dose safety assessment (ie, the safety analysis set) over 52 weeks. The study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05796206) and is complete. People with lived experience were not involved as research partners in this study.

FINDINGS: Between May 26, 2023, and July 29, 2024, 171 patients were screened for eligibility. Of these, 123 patients were randomly assigned to receive obinutuzumab β (n=61) or placebo (n=62) and were included in both the full analysis set and safety analysis sets. The mean age was 36·1 years (SD 10·3). 115 (93%) of 123 patients were female, eight (7%) were male, and 117 (95%) were Han Chinese ethnicity. At week 12, 32 (52%) of 61 patients in the obinutuzumab β group and 21 (34%) of 62 in the placebo group had an SRI-4 response (adjusted risk difference 19 percentage points, 95% CI 3-36; p=0·022). Serious adverse events occurred in 12 (20%) patients in the obinutuzumab β group and 14 (23%) in the placebo group. One fatal treatment-emergent adverse event (sepsis) occurred in the placebo group.

INTERPRETATION: Obinutuzumab β plus standard therapy improved SRI-4 response at week 12 in Chinese patients with active SLE, with a generally manageable safety profile over 52 weeks. These phase 2 findings support further evaluation and longer-term safety follow-up.

FUNDING: Beijing Mabworks Biotech.

articles.title: Weight management in people with HIV.
articles.abstract: Excess weight gain in people with HIV is now recognised as a common risk associated with the use of guideline-recommended antiretroviral therapy, such that nearly 50% of people with HIV are living with comorbid obesity. Weight gain and clinical obesity exacerbate cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic health complications in this population and chronic weight management strategies that reduce these risks are now an urgent priority. Behavioural interventions can be offered to improve diet and increase physical activity, including increasing protein intake and promoting regular physical activity. Additionally, there is a growing body of evidence to support the use of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapies in people with HIV, along with a historical literature showing the efficacy of tesamorelin; however, there are sparse data to direct the use of other approved obesity management medicines specific to this population. Finally, bariatric surgical interventions are suggested to be safe and efficacious for those with chronic HIV infection and comorbid obesity. This Series paper identifies a range of key evidence gaps and research priorities for obesity management in people with HIV, including a lack of trials of GLP-1 therapies in people with HIV powered to key clinical outcomes, such as major adverse cardiovascular events and body composition endpoints, implementation science to define models of care, and research on the heterogeneities in clinical outcomes of obesity treatment by sex.

articles.title: Induction of labour vs spontaneous labour onset and maternal and perinatal outcomes and maternal experiences: The Birth Experience Study (BESt).
articles.journal: Women and birth : journal of the Australian College of Midwives
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Induction of labour (IOL) is rising around the world, with little known about consequent outcomes in large cohorts of childbearing women.

AIM: To examine the impact of IOL vs spontaneous labour onset on maternal and perinatal outcomes, as reported by women in a national survey.

DESIGN: A cross-sectional, online, maternal self-report survey, was open in Australia from March-December 2021.

PARTICIPANTS: 7791 women who had a spontaneous onset (n = 5230), or IOL (n = 2561) were included.

ANALYSIS: Labour, birth and postnatal outcomes were classified as binary variables and percentages. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed, controlling for likely confounders.

RESULTS: Compared with spontaneous onset of labour, survey respondents having an IOL were significantly more likely to experience: forceps or vacuum; episiotomy; emergency caesarean; excessive blood loss; physical pain and/or poor or decreased physical health; birth as traumatic; regrets about their birth experience; diagnosis of PTSD; obstetric violence; and less skin-to-skin contact with their babies. Neonatal outcomes following IOL included: significantly higher odds of being distressed during labour; having jaundice; and being given formula when the mother had chosen to breast feed. There was no difference in major perineal injury or pelvic floor outcomes, or admission of the baby to special care nursery or neonatal intensive care.

CONCLUSIONS: IOL was associated with significant negative physical and psychological health impacts for women and babies compared to spontaneous labour onset. There is a need for more research on clinical and psychological impacts of IOL for women, to ensure decision making is informed.

articles.title: Implementation of Single-Pill Combination Therapy Through Team-Based Care for Hypertension Control in Resource-Constrained Settings: A Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Single-pill combination therapy improves medication adherence and hypertension control. However, limited evidence is available on its implementation in routine clinical practice.

OBJECTIVE: To assess the long-term effectiveness, implementation, and sustainability of single-pill combination therapy through team-based care for blood pressure reduction among patients with uncontrolled hypertension in primary care settings in Colombia and Jamaica.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Multicountry, unblinded, pragmatic, cluster randomized clinical trial. Twenty primary care clinics in Jamaica and 20 in Colombia were randomly assigned to either the single-pill combination therapy group or the standard care group. A total of 1706 adults with uncontrolled hypertension were enrolled between February 23, 2023, and September 12, 2024. The final follow-up visit occurred on September 9, 2026.

INTERVENTIONS: In the intervention group (n = 869), a team-based care approach that included physician and nurse training, health coaching, home blood pressure monitoring, and blood pressure audit and feedback was used to implement single-pill combination therapy. Single-pill combinations were purchased locally and provided to patients. In the standard care group (n = 837), patients received monotherapy or polytherapy with guideline-recommended medications covered by health insurance or government programs. The intervention lasted 18 months, with additional follow-up at 24 months.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the between-group difference in change in systolic blood pressure from baseline to 18 months. Three blood pressure measurements were obtained at each of 2 visits at each time point using a standard protocol.

RESULTS: Among the 1706 enrolled participants, at baseline, the mean age was 61.4 years, 69.9% of participants were female, and 98.2% were taking antihypertensive medications. Among the 1574 participants included in the primary analysis, systolic blood pressure decreased by 19.1 mm Hg, from 145.9 mm Hg at baseline to 126.8 mm Hg at 18 months, in the intervention group and by 9.0 mm Hg, from 145.0 mm Hg to 136.1 mm Hg, in the standard care group, with a between-group difference of -10.1 mm Hg (95% CI, -13.3 to -6.9 mm Hg; P < .001). At 18 months, 69.5% of patients in the intervention group and 29.2% in the standard care group achieved systolic blood pressure less than 130 and diastolic blood pressure less than 80 mm Hg. Serious adverse events (death and hospitalization) occurred at similar frequencies in the intervention (7.9%) and standard care (9.9%) groups.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Implementing single-pill combination therapy through team-based care significantly reduced blood pressure over 18 months among adults with uncontrolled hypertension in Colombia and Jamaica. This comprehensive strategy integrating single-pill combination therapy with team-based care could be widely adopted and scaled up for hypertension control, particularly in resource-constrained settings.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05405920.

articles.title: Implementation of Single-Pill Combination Therapy Through Team-Based Care for Hypertension Control in Resource-Constrained Settings: Research Summary.
