Low-Voltage Area Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: Research Summary.
Low-Voltage Area Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: The COAST-AF Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) for persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) has demonstrated modest success rates. Ablation of atrial low-voltage areas (LVA) has shown potential results, but more data are required.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether PVI plus LVA ablation is superior to PVI alone in reducing atrial arrhythmia recurrence in patients with AF.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Single-blind randomized clinical trial in 14 AF ablation centers in Canada. Adults with persistent AF of more than 3 months were enrolled between August 2018 and September 2024 and followed up for 18 to 36 months through April 2026.

INTERVENTION: Patients were randomized to PVI plus LVA ablation or PVI alone.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was atrial arrhythmia recurrence beyond 90 days after a single catheter ablation procedure. Secondary outcomes included repeat ablation for AF, atrial flutter, or atrial tachycardia, emergency visits or hospitalization, arrhythmia recurrence over 18 months, procedure duration, total ablation delivery time, AF burden, and safety outcomes. The primary efficacy analysis was based on the modified intention-to-treat principle for patients who received the intervention.

RESULTS: Among 508 enrolled patients, 253 were randomized to PVI plus LVA ablation and 255 to PVI alone. Mean (SD) age was 65.2 (9.0) years, 386 (76%) were male and 268 (54%) had LVA. After a mean (SD) follow-up of 21 (15) months, 124 (49.4%) randomized to PVI plus LVA and 146 (57.5%) randomized to PVI reached the primary outcome (hazard ratio [HR], 0.82; 95% CI, 0.65-1.04; P = .11). In the prespecified principal subgroup analysis of 268 patients with LVA, arrhythmia recurrence occurred in 68 of 138 patients (49.3%) following PVI plus LVA ablation compared with 90 of 130 patients (69.2%) following PVI alone (HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.66-0.91; P = .002). Arrhythmia recurrence over 18 months (37.0% vs 56.2%; HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.64-0.92) and AF burden were lower after PVI plus LVA ablation in this group. Among patients without LVA, recurrence was similar between ablation groups (56 of 113 [49.6%] vs 51 of 113 [45.1%]; HR, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.90-1.32). Procedure duration and ablation delivery time were longer in the PVI plus LVA ablation group. Safety outcomes were similar between groups.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, among patients with persistent AF, adjunctive LVA ablation did not significantly reduce atrial arrhythmia recurrence in the overall population over a mean 21-month follow-up. A prespecified principal subgroup analysis of patients with LVA suggested that adjunctive LVA ablation was consistent with reduced recurrence of atrial arrhythmias in this group.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, Identifier: NCT03347227.

articles.title: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial of a Digital Health Intervention for Medication Optimization in Heart Failure: The ENGAGE-HF Trial Outcomes.
articles.abstract: Background: Despite clear evidence that guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) significantly reduces mortality and hospitalizations in patients with heart failure (HF) with reduced and mildly reduced ejection fraction, real-world implementation remains suboptimal. Digital health interventions may promote GDMT titration after hospital discharge. Methods: The ENGAGE-HF trial was a multicenter, two-arm, open-label, randomized controlled trial across three academic centers, funded by the AHA Strategically Focused Research Network (SFRN) for Health Technology and Innovation. Patients recently hospitalized with HF, with or without a primary hospital diagnosis of HF, and LVEF <50% receiving suboptimal GDMT were randomized 1:1 to either the ENGAGE-HF app or usual care for 90 days. The ENGAGE-HF intervention consisted of a patient-facing mobile app and a clinician dashboard overseen by study coordinators. The primary outcome was the Medication Optimization Score (MOS, scale 0-100%) at 90 days. Secondary outcomes were individual GDMT therapies and the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score at 90 days. Results: A total of 134 participants were randomized. At 90 days, the adjusted MOS was significantly higher in the ENGAGE-HF group compared to the control group (83.7% vs. 74.0%, p = 0.010). Results remained consistent across multiple sensitivity analyses. Overall prescribing prevalence increased more in the ENGAGE-HF group for MRAs (+15.9 vs. +2.5 percentage points) and SGLT2 inhibitors (+10.9 vs. +2.5 percentage points). Furthermore, the ENGAGE-HF group demonstrated greater increases in achieving target doses for ARNI (+18.8% vs. +6.3%) and beta-blockers (+8.5% vs. +0.6%). KCCQ-23 CSS at 90 days was 75.2 (SE 2.6) in the intervention group versus 72.2 (SE 2.6) in the control group (between-group p = 0.40). Conclusions: ENGAGE-HF, a digital health intervention that integrates remote monitoring, patient engagement, and clinical decision support, significantly improved GDMT optimization at 90 days compared with usual care among patients with HF. Registration: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov Unique Identifier: NCT06750549.

articles.title: Variability of lipoprotein(a) levels in patients with acute myocardial infarction between admission, discharge, and follow-up.
authors: FRENCHIE-Lp(a) Investigators and the French Alliance for Cardiovascular Trials (FACT) investigators network
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Using Lp(a) concentrations measured during stable follow-up as the reference, we aimed to assess the temporal variability of Lp(a) after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and to explore a pragmatic strategy for Lp(a) measurement.

METHODS AND RESULTS: The FRENCHIE-Lp(a) cohort enrolled consecutive adults hospitalized for AMI in 21 centres. Lp(a) mass concentration, measured at admission, hospital discharge, and 3-12 months follow-up, was analysed both as a continuous and predefined categorical variable (≤20, >20-≤50, >50-≤70, >70 mg/dL). Assuming follow-up Lp(a) as the reference, we aimed to identify the threshold values that would allow us to accurately identify patients with Lp(a) > 70mg/dL, the threshold mostly used for patient selection in phase III trials of targeted Lp(a) therapies. A cumulative threshold analysis was performed to identify the Lp(a) value below which the misclassification rate (i.e. % of patients with follow-up Lp(a) > 70 mg/dL) remained <1%. Among 1561 patients (aged 61 ± 12 years; 21.3% women), median Lp(a) was 13 mg/dL at admission and remained stable over time (median difference overtime = 0 mg/dL). However, only 68.5% of patients remained in the same Lp(a) category overtime. In patients with discharge-Lp(a) ≤37 mg/dL (72.5% of the population), only 0.97% had Lp(a) >70 mg/dL at follow-up compared to 39.9% of those with discharge-Lp(a) >37 mg/dL.

CONCLUSION: Although the median Lp(a) level remained stable between admission and follow-up, one-third of AMI patients shifted within Lp(a) categories over time. Pending external validation, an exploratory two-step strategy based on Lp(a) measurement at discharge, followed by repeat testing in patients with Lp(a) >37 mg/dL, showed a misclassification rate below 1% for identifying patients potentially needing intervention.

REGISTRATION: Clinical trial Number: NCT04050956.

articles.title: Thymectomy Extent, Immune Recovery, and Infectious Burden After Neonatal Cardiac Surgery.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal cardiac surgery frequently requires thymectomy, but the consequences of extensive thymic removal remain uncertain.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied 105 neonates undergoing sternotomy (2015-2024), comparing infections and 6-month lymphocyte recovery after partial versus total thymectomy, with Firth regression adjusted for bypass duration and surgical era. Separate cohorts underwent paired plasma biomarker (n=8) and whole-blood RNA sequencing (n=4) analysis before and after thymectomy.

RESULTS: Among 105 neonates, 27 underwent partial and 78 total thymectomy. Multiple infections occurred in 2 of 27 (7%) after partial and 23 of 78 (30%) after total thymectomy (P=0.02); after adjustment for bypass duration and surgical era, the association was not statistically significant (Firth-adjusted odds ratio, 2.99 [95% CI, 0.82-15.85]; P=0.10). Median lymphocyte count decreased after total but increased after partial thymectomy (change, -0.8 versus +0.9×103/μL; P=0.011). Tumor necrosis factor-α decreased in all 8 biomarker participants (unadjusted P=0.0078). RNA sequencing in 4 patients (2 partial, 2 total thymectomy) identified 835 differentially expressed genes; pre-T-cell receptor α decreased in all 4 pairs (log2 fold change, -2.50; adjusted P=6×10-6).

CONCLUSIONS: Total thymectomy was associated with reduced 6-month lymphocyte recovery and higher unadjusted odds of multiple infections. The infection association was not statistically significant after adjustment, and few events (2 of 27 after partial thymectomy) limit precision and cannot exclude a clinically important effect; these findings are hypothesis-generating. Biomarker and transcriptomic findings are exploratory and cannot distinguish thymectomy from surgery, maturation, or postoperative recovery. Prospective studies are underway to evaluate thymic preservation and autologous reimplantation.

articles.title: Effects of Sotatercept on Cardiac Structure and Function in Combined Post- and Precapillary Pulmonary Hypertension in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: Analysis of the CADENCE Study.
[Post-resuscitation care 2025: neurological prognosis of post-cardiac arrest brain injury].
articles.abstract: Post-cardiac arrest brain injury represents a central component of the post-resuscitation syndrome, driven not only by the initial hypoxic-ischemic insult but also by reperfusion injury after the return or start of mechanical circulation. Complex neuronal damage accounts for a substantial proportion of mortality among successfully resuscitated patients, making reliable neurological prognostication a key objective of post-resuscitation care and clinical decision-making. The 2025 European Resuscitation Council guidelines emphasize a structured, multimodal approach to neuroprognostication. Prognosis should not rely on a single parameter; instead, it requires the integrated interpretation of clinical findings, electrophysiological data, neuroimaging results, and circulating biomarkers. This strategy aims to reduce falsely pessimistic predictions, prevent premature withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy, and avoid the unnecessary prolongation of futile intensive care in cases of irreversible brain injury. In the early phase of return of spontaneous circulation, neurological assessment may be confounded by several factors, including residual sedation, neuromuscular blockade, metabolic disturbances, and cardiorespiratory instability. Therefore, accurate prognostication depends on the correction of reversible conditions and stabilization of physiological parameters before definitive conclusions are drawn. Importantly, neurological outcome assessment is inherently time-dependent, and appropriate timing is essential for safe and evidence-based decision-making. Overall, the 2025 recommendations advocate standardized, multidisciplinary, and stepwise neuroprognostication as a cornerstone of post-resuscitation management, prioritizing patient-centered care while minimizing uncertainty and supporting long-term neurological recovery whenever possible. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(45): 1799-1809.

articles.title: [Advanced airway management of patients with preserved circulation in Hungarian emergency departments].
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Advanced airway management of patients with preserved circulation (not in cardiac arrest) is a critical, high-risk procedure in emergency care. Internationally, safety improves through standardized procedures, equipment, documentation, and training.

OBJECTIVE: To map current practice in Hungarian emergency departments regarding who performs the procedure, the degree of regulation, the available drugs and devices, documentation practices, and training.

METHOD: We conducted a cross-sectional online questionnaire survey. Based on the department-head registry of the Hungarian Society of Emergency Medicine, we sent the questionnaire to the heads of all 44 Hungarian emergency departments. Data were collected between May and July 2026 and analyzed using descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: The response rate was 52% (23/44). In 96% of the departments, the procedure was routinely performed by emergency care providers. A written protocol existed in 48% of the departments (mandatory in 17%). Propofol, a depolarizing neuromuscular blocking agent, and a bougie were available in all departments. Non-invasive ventilation was available in 96% of departments, videolaryngoscopes in 74%, and capnographs in 78%; however, only 39% mandated capnography. In 52% of the responding departments, no dedicated procedural documentation was produced, and 57% had no regular topic-specific training.

DISCUSSION: In the responding departments, the procedure was performed predominantly by emergency clinicians, and the basic pharmacological and equipment requirements were largely met. However, organizational safeguards for patient safety - a uniform protocol, mandatory capnography, structured documentation, and regular training - were often lacking, indicating both deviations from international recommendations and clear targets for improvement.

CONCLUSION: In the responding Hungarian emergency departments, the airway management practice for patients with preserved circulation was highly heterogeneous and insufficiently standardized. Priorities for improvement include a uniform protocol, mandatory capnography, structured documentation and a national registry, and regular training. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(45): 1835-1842.

articles.title: A Potential New Therapeutic Option for Exercise Intolerance in Patients with Heart Failure and Preserved Ejection Fraction.
Iron Repletion in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: The IRONMET-HFpEF Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Iron deficiency is present in >50% of patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and is associated with reduced exercise capacity and survival. Whether iron repletion improves exercise capacity as objectively measured by peak oxygen uptake ([Formula: see text]) is unknown. The IRONMET-HFpEF trial (Impact of Intravenous Iron Repletion on Mechanisms of Exercise Intolerance in HFpEF) sought to determine whether ferric derisomaltose (FDI) compared with placebo improves peak [Formula: see text] in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction with iron deficiency.

METHODS: This was a double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial of patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and iron deficiency, defined as ferritin <100 ng/mL or <300 ng/mL with transferrin saturation <20%. Participants were enrolled between December 2021 and April 2026. Single-dose ferric derisomaltose (1000 mg; n=44) or placebo (n=21) was administered once intravenously. The primary end point was the change in peak [Formula: see text] from baseline to 12 weeks with an analysis of covariance model including terms for treatment group, baseline peak [Formula: see text], and sex. Secondary end points included changes in [Formula: see text] at the anaerobic threshold, 6-minute walk test distance, New York Heart Association class, health status assessed by the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary Score, and iron biomarkers at 12 weeks.

RESULTS: Among 65 randomized participants (median age, 68 years [interquartile range, 58-76 years], 72% women, transferrin saturation 16.0±7.4%, ferritin 57.8±48.9 ng/mL), 64 (98.5%) completed the study. The median baseline peak [Formula: see text] was 12.7 mL·kg-1·min-1 (interquartile range, 10.6-15.8 mL·kg-1·min-1) in the FDI group and 12.2 mL·kg-1·min-1 (11.6-14.6 mL·kg-1·min-1) in the placebo group. At 12 weeks, peak [Formula: see text] improved by 1.2 mL·kg-1·min-1 (95% CI, 0.6-1.7) in the FDI group and was unchanged (0.1 mL·kg-1·min-1 [95% CI, -0.7 to 0.9]) in the placebo group (least-squares mean difference, 1.1 mL·kg-1·min-1 [95% CI, 0.2-1.9]; P=0.02). [Formula: see text] at the anaerobic threshold, 6-minute walk test distance, and New York Heart Association class also improved in the FDI compared with the placebo group (all P<0.05), whereas the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary Score did not differ significantly between groups (FDI group, +4.4 [95% CI, -2.4 to 11.2]; P=0.20). FDI increased transferrin saturation (9.4% [95% CI, 4.9%-13.9%]) and ferritin (183 ng/mL [95% CI, 128-238]) compared with the placebo group (PLSMD<0.001 for both). There were no serious adverse events related to FDI administration.

CONCLUSIONS: In the largest trial to date of iron repletion in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction with iron deficiency, FDI improved multiple measures of exercise capacity.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04945707.

articles.title: Early third-trimester maternal cardiac function and morphometry in high-risk pregnancies that subsequently developed fetal growth restriction and/or pre-eclampsia.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate maternal cardiovascular function and cardiac morphology in early third-trimester pregnancies at high risk for fetal growth restriction (FGR) and compare findings between pregnancies that subsequently developed FGR and/or pre-eclampsia (PE) and uncomplicated pregnancies.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study included singleton pregnancies at high risk for FGR referred to the Maternal-Fetal Medicine Department at the Hospital Clinic of Barcelona, Barcelona, Spain, between August 2022 and August 2024, for a routine second-trimester fetal anomaly scan. The patients were assessed between 27 + 0 and 28 + 6 weeks' gestation and were only included in the analysis if they did not have a diagnosis of FGR or PE at the time of evaluation; those who subsequently developed FGR and/or PE were identified during follow-up. Maternal echocardiography was performed to assess cardiac output (CO), stroke volume (SV), systemic vascular resistance (SVR) and structural parameters including left ventricular (LV) wall thickness and chamber volumes. Results were compared between pregnancies that subsequently developed FGR (with or without PE), pregnancies that subsequently developed isolated PE and uncomplicated pregnancies. Multivariable analysis was performed using quantile regression of the medians for CO and SVR, adjusted for body mass index (BMI), with FGR and PE assessed independently.

RESULTS: A total of 948 patients were included in the final analysis, of whom 129 developed FGR and/or PE (including 59 that developed FGR (with or without PE) and 70 that developed isolated PE) and 819 had uncomplicated pregnancies. Median mean arterial pressure (MAP) was higher in the FGR (with or without PE) group (82.0 mmHg) and the isolated-PE group (84.8 mmHg) than in the uncomplicated group (79.7 mmHg; P = 0.027 and P < 0.001, respectively), with the isolated-PE group showing the highest MAP values (isolated PE vs FGR (with or without PE), P = 0.047). Median heart rate was elevated in the isolated-PE group (82.5 bpm) compared with the FGR (with or without PE) group (77.0 bpm; P = 0.03). In the multivariable analysis, FGR and PE were associated independently with lower CO and higher SVR prior to their development. Median SV was reduced in the FGR (with or without PE) group (59.7 mL) and the isolated-PE group (61.1 mL) compared with the uncomplicated group (64.2 mL; P = 0.030 and P = 0.016, respectively). Median BMI-indexed CO was also lower in the FGR (with or without PE) group (0.18 (L/min)/(kg/m2)) and the isolated-PE group (0.17 (L/min)/(kg/m2)) compared with the uncomplicated group (0.19 (L/min)/(kg/m2); P = 0.005 and P = 0.001, respectively). Median SVR was elevated in the FGR (with or without PE) group (1393 dynes × s/cm5) and the isolated-PE group (1339 dynes × s/cm5) compared with the uncomplicated group (1252 dynes × s/cm5; P < 0.001 and P = 0.01, respectively). Compared with the uncomplicated group, the isolated-PE group showed greater median LV myocardial thickness at end diastole (0.50 vs 0.47 cm; P = 0.003), interventricular septal thickness at end diastole (0.92 vs 0.89 cm; P = 0.031), posterior wall thickness at end diastole (0.98 vs 0.94 cm; P = 0.013) and relative wall thickness (0.45 vs 0.42; P = 0.001). Moreover, the FGR (with or without PE) group had a smaller median LV end-diastolic diameter (4.27 cm) compared with the uncomplicated group (4.48 cm; P = 0.003), indicating that preload may be reduced in patients who developed FGR (with or without PE). LV mass indexed for BMI was similar across groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Maternal cardiovascular alterations may precede the development of FGR and PE and differ by phenotype. Pregnancies that subsequently developed FGR and/or PE showed reduced CO, but those that developed FGR reflected lower preload without tachycardia, while those that developed isolated PE showed hypertensive features with a compensatory rise in heart rate. Maternal echocardiography may aid early risk stratification and guide tailored surveillance and therapy in pregnancies at high risk for FGR. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

articles.title: A Pilot Clinical and Experimental Study of Type I Collagen Matrix Implantation Versus Microfracture for Knee Cartilage Defects.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Microfracture is used to treat cartilage defects but may compromise subchondral bone integrity. Type I collagen matrix implantation has emerged as a potential alternative for advanced (Outerbridge III-IV) lesions, although supporting evidence remains limited. This study combined clinical evaluation with an animal model to validate treatment outcomes. The aim was to compare short-term clinical efficacy and cartilage repair quality of Type I collagen matrix implantation versus microfracture and to validate clinical findings in an animal model. MATERIAL AND METHODS This prospective, randomized, exploratory pilot translational study included both animal and clinical experiments. Full-thickness cartilage defects were created in 18 rats and treated with a blank control, microfracture, or Type I collagen implantation. After 12 weeks, gross and histological evaluations (Safranin O/Fast Green staining) were performed. Concurrently, 36 patients with knee cartilage defects were enrolled in a randomized, single-blind trial (collagen group, n=20; microfracture group, n=16) and followed for 12 months. Lysholm, International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC), and Magnetic Resonance Observation of Cartilage Repair Tissue (MOCART) scores were recorded preoperatively (Lysholm and IKDC only) and at 3, 6, and 12 months postoperatively. RESULTS In the animal model, Type I collagen implantation produced superior cartilage and subchondral bone repair compared with the control and microfracture groups. Clinically, both groups showed significant improvement; the collagen group consistently achieved higher functional and MOCART scores (P<0.05). CONCLUSIONS Type I collagen matrix implantation was associated with more favorable cartilage regeneration and better short-term clinical outcomes than microfracture, representing an effective biomaterial-assisted treatment strategy for knee cartilage defects.

articles.title: Risk of red blood cell transfusion in patients with preoperative anemia requiring cardiac surgery.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Preoperative anemia is common and a strong predictor of perioperative red blood cell (RBC) transfusion in cardiac surgical patients. Both anemia and RBC transfusion are independently associated with adverse postoperative outcomes, but their interrelationship is difficult to disentangle because RBC transfusion acts as a mediator rather than a confounder.

AREAS COVERED: This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the relationship between preoperative anemia, RBC transfusion, and postoperative outcomes in cardiac surgery, with particular emphasis on recent advances in causal inference mediation analysis. We discuss outcome-specific mediation patterns, patient characteristics that may modify anemia and transfusion related risk, and implications for perioperative management.

EXPERT OPINION: Mediation analysis provides a valuable framework for distinguishing the direct effects of anemia from RBC transfusion-mediated effects. Current evidence suggests that RBC transfusion mediates a substantial proportion of anemia-associated mortality, whereas direct anemia effects appear more important for renal complications. Future patient blood management should move beyond uniform transfusion thresholds toward individualized strategies that account for patient's risk profile, physiological reserve, intraoperative factors and the outcome-specific balance between the potential benefits of correcting anemia and the risks of RBC transfusion.

articles.title: [Expert consensus on pathological evaluation of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma after neoadjuvant therapy (2026 version)].
authors: Esophageal Cancer Cooperative Group of Cancer Pathology Committee of China Anti-Cancer Association
articles.journal: Zhonghua bing li xue za zhi = Chinese journal of pathology

articles.title: Optimizing colistin dosing in acute-on-chronic liver failure patients with sepsis due to multidrug-resistant Gram-negative pathogens.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) patients with sepsis represent a special population that is highly susceptible to serious infections but remains understudied for antibiotic dose optimization. Colistin, a reserve antibiotic for multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections, is frequently used for management of sepsis in this group of patients. There is an unmet medical need to describe a dosing regimen developed using a population pharmacokinetic approach in this group of patients.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: ACLF patients receiving intravenous colistin were enrolled. Population pharmacokinetic modeling was performed using nonlinear mixed-effects methods, with covariate analysis and bootstrap validation. Monte Carlo simulations were conducted to evaluate the probability of target attainment (PTA) across dosing regimens and renal function strata.

RESULTS: A total of 68 plasma concentrations from eligible patients admitted over 2 years were analyzed. Colistin pharmacokinetics were adequately described by a one-compartment model, with considerable inter-individual variability. Creatinine clearance was found to be a significant covariate for clearance. The probability of target attainment (PTA) for pertinent PK/PD index varied across different dosing regimens and renal function strata.

CONCLUSIONS: Colistin pharmacokinetics in patients with ACLF is highly variable, with creatinine clearance emerging as a significant covariate. We propose a creatinine-clearance-guided dosing regimen based on the findings of the study.

articles.title: Highly specific detection of PET NPs using an amino-functionalized PEC sensor based on a SnS2@MoS2 heterojunction.
articles.abstract: The rapid detection of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) nanoplastics (PET NPs) is hindered by their low concentration, high mobility and lack of a distinguishable interface with other nanoplastics. In this study, we developed an SnS2@MoS2/APTES amino-functionalized photoelectrochemical sensor capable of detecting PET NPs with high specificity. The SnS2@MoS2 heterojunction synthesized via in situ hydrothermal synthesis and the APTES self-assembled amino-functionalized interface enable PET NPs to interact with amino-functionalized interface at multiple sites through oxygen-containing groups such as ester groups, carbonyl oxygen and ether oxygen. The sensor exhibits a detection range of 0.5-800 μg mL-1 for PET NPs, with a detection limit of 0.17 μg mL-1. DFT calculations further indicate that the PET-APTES system exhibits a lower adsorption energy (-1.37 eV) and a more significant interfacial charge rearrangement, demonstrating that the APTES amino siloxane interface exhibits a polymer structural selectivity toward PET. Furthermore, this PEC sensor exhibits good recovery rates (96.04%-102.76%) in practical water samples such as seawater, bottled water and tap water. It provides a new method for interface recognition and signal conversion for the specific PEC detection of PET nanoplastics.

articles.title: Instant CMQT stabilization coupled UHPLC-MS/MS for the quantification of reduced and total forms of cysteine, homocysteine, and glutathione in blood plasma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reduced and total forms of cysteine (Cys), homocysteine (Hcy), and glutathione (GSH) are key players in redox homeostasis, and their dysregulation is linked to diseases such as sepsis. However, accurate quantification of reduced thiols in plasma remains challenging due to rapid air oxidation of native thiols. In this work, a thiol-specific reagent (2-chloro-1-methylquinolinium tetrafluoroborate, CMQT) that reacts rapidly under mild conditions was coupled with UHPLC-MS/MS to develop a method for the simultaneous determination of reduced and total forms of Cys, Hcy, and GSH in plasma samples.

RESULTS: CMQT rapidly stabilizes native thiols in whole blood without inducing hemolysis. The proposed method was validated for linearity, precision, accuracy and sensitivity. Calibration curves showed excellent linearity (R2 > 0.9993). Intra- and inter-day precisions ranged from 0.14% to 7.23%, and accuracy from -5.62% to 4.15%. The limits of detection for the reduced and total forms of Cys, Hcy and GSH ranged from 0.051 to 0.88 μM. The method was successfully applied to a lipopolysaccharide-induced endotoxemia mouse model, revealing that reduced Hcy and reduced GSH may serve as potential biomarkers for early and late oxidative stress, respectively. The method was also validated on human plasma samples, confirming its applicability across species and revealing sex-related thiol differences.

SIGNIFICANCE: The combination of rapid and hemolysis-free thiol stabilization with MS-based structural characterization provides a robust analytical tool for thiol redox studies and could be extended to other biological matrices.

articles.title: An integrated analytical strategy combining UPLC-QTOF-MS-based metabolomics and 16S rRNA sequencing to explore the mechanism of Shenqi Jieyu decoction in coronary heart disease complicated by depression in ApoE-/- mice.
articles.journal: Journal of chromatography. B, Analytical technologies in the biomedical and life sciences
articles.abstract: Coronary heart disease combined with depression (dual-heart disorder) exhibits high morbidity and poor prognosis, lacking safe unified therapeutic agents. Shenqi Jieyu Decoction (SQJY) relieves depressive and cardiovascular symptoms in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) patients, yet its underlying multiple potential mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, an ApoE-/- mouse model of dual-heart disorder was induced via high-fat diet combined with chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS). Behavioral testing, aortic pathological staining, hippocampal neurochemistry, and ultra-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC-QTOF-MS)-based untargeted metabolomics of serum and cecal contents were integrated with 16S rRNA sequencing, establishing an integrated multi-omics workflow to examine the potential modulatory effects of SQJY and to explore its possible mechanism. Behavioral and pathological assays indicated that SQJY alleviated atherosclerosis and depression-like phenotypes, elevated hippocampal 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT), dopamine (DA) and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), and suppressed neuroinflammatory cytokines. 16S sequencing suggested SQJY remodeled dysregulated gut microbiota toward a more balanced profile. Metabolomics identified disturbed sphingolipid and glycerophospholipid metabolism as important metabolic signatures that H-SQJY group corrected more extensively in cecal content (68 of 265 metabolites) than in serum (8 of 103). Phylogenetic Investigation of Communities by Reconstruction of Unobserved States 2 (PICRUSt2)-based prediction of microbial functions was integrated, and Spearman correlation analysis showed significant associations between predicted microbial functions, differential gut microbes and lipid metabolites. Collectively, SQJY showed concurrent potential cardioprotective and antidepressant effects, possibly through restoring gut microbial homeostasis and modulating lipid metabolic disorders. These correlative and predicted findings provide preliminary evidence for the potential application of SQJY in dual-heart disorder.

articles.title: Role of collagen in right ventricular passive anisotropic viscoelasticity with pulmonary hypertension.
articles.journal: Journal of the mechanical behavior of biomedical materials
articles.abstract: Collagen is a structural extracellular protein that contributes to the anisotropic elastic behavior of the right ventricle (RV). It is established that collagen is significantly altered in pulmonary hypertension (PH), including overall content, degree of cross-linking, and fiber alignment. The RV is viscoelastic, though, and how collagen contributes to the overall tissue viscoelastic behavior with PH development remains unknown. Therefore, the aim of this study was to investigate the role of collagen in the anisotropic viscoelasticity of the RV free wall (RVFW) during PH progression. Equibiaxial stress relaxation tests were performed in healthy and PH rat RVFW before and after the enzymatic breakdown of collagen via collagenase. A Fung-type quasilinear viscoelastic constitutive model was then applied to further delineate the changes in RVFW mechanics. We found that collagen degradation significantly reduced RVFW viscosity and elasticity, with stronger effects in the diseased group. The reduction in RVFW elastic behavior was stronger in the longitudinal direction than the circumferential, while the reduction in viscosity was similar between directions in both groups. Constitutive modeling results showed weakened RVFW stiffness after collagenase treatment in both groups, but distinct responses of relaxation strength coefficients between the healthy and diseased groups. In the longitudinal direction, the relaxation strength coefficients were positively correlated with the viscosity to elasticity ratio measured from experimental data in both groups. Our findings demonstrate distinct collagen deposition and morphology between healthy and diseased RVFW, suggesting that RV fibrosis results in unique regulation of RVFW mechanics.

articles.title: First use of a woven allogeneic vascular graft made of cell-assembled extracellular matrix (CAM) as an arteriovenous shunt in sheep: a pilot study.
articles.abstract: Reliable vascular access is vital for patients undergoing hemodialysis. Current arteriovenous shunts (AVS) made of expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) are prone to thrombosis, intimal hyperplasia, and infections. To overcome these limitations, biological Tissue-Engineered Vascular Grafts (TEVGs) were produced by weaving threads made from Cell-Assembled extracellular Matrix (CAM), i.e., extracellular matrix produced by ovine fibroblasts in culture. The woven TEVGs were designed with a 6 mm internal diameter and beveled ends to facilitate use as an AVS. They had a burst pressure (3069 ± 546 mmHg) and a compliance (4.4 ± 0.5%/100 mmHg) closer to those of native blood vessels than ePTFE prostheses. Woven TEVGs were implanted as carotid-jugular AVS in sheep and compared to ePTFE controls in a bilateral model (n = 8 animals). Grafts were easily punctured with 16G hemodialysis needles once at 4 weeks without loss of structural integrity or hemorrhagic complications. Overall TEVGs patency was 100%, while it was 87.5% for ePTFE grafts (n = 8). Histological analysis revealed an inflammatory response that decreased between 4 and 8 weeks. A luminal neotissue was observed at 8 weeks with smooth muscle cells and localized endothelialization. Localized calcification of CAM was observed and appeared to be correlated with high tissue compaction. This proof-of-concept study demonstrates the feasibility of using a completely biological TEVG made from woven CAM as an AVS in an allogeneic large animal model. Future studies are needed to understand and avoid the never-before-observed calcification of the CAM in a large animal model, as well as to determine longer-term outcomes.

articles.title: Assessing Diastolic Function With AI and Echocardiography: From Risk Prediction to Therapeutic Targets.
Integrating polygenic and classical risk factors for cardiovascular risk stratification in a polish primary-care cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) promise improved cardiovascular risk stratification, but most validation derives from UK or Nordic biobanks. The transferability of these scores to Central European populations and their incremental value over classical risk factors in routine care remain unestablished.

OBJECTIVES: To determine whether a coronary PRS derived from external European data transfers to a Polish primary-care population and adds discrimination for prevalent cardiovascular disease beyond classical risk factors.

METHODS: In the nationwide Polish LIPIDOGEN2015 primary-care cohort, we derived PRS for coronary heart disease, myocardial infarction (MI) and stroke from FinnGen data with continuous shrinkage priors and applied them to imputed genotypes. We compared allele frequencies of 1397 unrelated participants with a non-Finnish European (NFE) reference and, in 1328 participants with clinical data, related the PRS to coronary artery disease (CAD), MI and stroke recorded at baseline and to a composite including death during follow-up, with and without classical risk factors or SCORE2.

RESULTS: Allele frequencies correlated with the NFE reference (r = 0.97). Per standard deviation (SD), the coronary PRS was associated with prevalent CAD (odds ratio 1.36, 95% CI 1.11 to 1.67) and the composite endpoint (1.26, 95% CI 1.04 to 1.51), as were two validated genome-wide scores. Adding it to classical risk factors changed the area under the curve (AUC) for the composite endpoint by 0.0017 (95% CI -0.0005 to 0.0076), from 0.860 to 0.861; results with SCORE2 were similar. The study had 80% power for odds ratios per SD of 1.31 (CAD) and 1.27 (composite).

CONCLUSIONS: A coronary PRS derived from external European data retains its association with prevalent CAD without re-derivation in this Polish primary-care cohort but, in this cross-sectional, event-limited sample, adds little discrimination to classical risk factors. Its value for predicting future events in this setting remains to be tested against incident outcomes.

articles.title: Quantification of vortex characteristics and rupture risk assessment in abdominal aortic aneurysms using the liutex method.
articles.abstract: The blood flow of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs) is characterized by complex vortex interactions. Previous studies have found three flow types in AAAs (Type I: multiple vortices; Type II: non-helical single vortex; Type III: helical main flow channel), and Type III has strong correlation with rupture risk. However, flow pattern classification is subjective and qualitative, hindering further improvements in risk prediction. To enhance the predictive value of vortex-based metrics, three-dimensional models of 40 infrarenal AAAs (22 ruptured and 18 unruptured) were reconstructed from preoperative CTA images for computational fluid dynamics analysis. Flow pattern types and two novel quantitative vortex parameters based on Liutex method (volume vortex fraction (vVF) and directional entropy (H)) were compared between the two groups. A multiparametric rupture risk prediction model was constructed. Receiver operating characteristic curves and the area under the curve (AUC) were employed to evaluate predictive performance. Results demonstrated that vVF in the ruptured group was significantly higher (p = 0.02). Type III AAAs exhibited a median vVF of 15.29 %, significantly surpassing those of Types I and II, and a 12.5 % threshold achieved 80 % accuracy in identifying these high-risk patterns. Ruptured cases exhibited higher entropy, facilitating more granular risk stratification. Ultimately, the integrated model combining maximum diameter, flow pattern, and directional entropy achieved an AUC of 0.86 (p < 0.001). By objectively quantifying vortex structures and establishing a multiparametric prediction model, this study significantly enhances the predictive accuracy for AAA rupture, providing a reference for risk evaluation.

articles.title: Interleukin-6 Inhibition with Ziltivekimab for Atherosclerotic Disease.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The inflammatory cytokine interleukin-6 is hypothesized to be a therapeutic target for patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease. Whether neutralizing interleukin-6 levels with ziltivekimab, a monoclonal antibody, reduces the risk of adverse cardiovascular events remains unknown.

METHODS: We conducted a multinational, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving adults with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular inflammation (defined by a high-sensitivity C-reactive protein [CRP] level of ≥2 mg per liter). Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous ziltivekimab (15 mg once monthly) or placebo. The primary efficacy end point was a 3-point major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE). This composite end point included death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke.

RESULTS: A total of 6376 patients were included in the full analysis population: 3184 were assigned to receive ziltivekimab and 3192 to receive placebo. The mean age of the patients was 69.4 years, and 27.5% were women. At 24 months, the between-group difference in the median percent change in the levels of inflammatory biomarkers among patients receiving ziltivekimab as compared with those receiving placebo was -76 percentage points for free interleukin-6 and -64 percentage points for high-sensitivity CRP. During a median follow-up of 33 months, a primary end-point event occurred in 561 patients (17.6%) in the ziltivekimab group and in 565 patients (17.7%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.99; 95% confidence interval, 0.88 to 1.11; P = 0.84). Serious adverse events occurred in 54.6% of the patients in the ziltivekimab group and in 54.8% of those in the placebo group; serious infections occurred in 20.4% and 17.9%, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular inflammation, a strategy of lowering interleukin-6 levels with ziltivekimab did not result in a lower risk of cardiovascular events than placebo. (Funded by Novo Nordisk; ZEUS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05021835.).

articles.title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Lowering in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Uncertainty persists regarding the effects of intensive blood-pressure lowering in patients with type 2 diabetes.

METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted in Brazil, patients with elevated blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, and high cardiovascular risk received intensive therapy targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or standard therapy targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. The primary end point was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure.

RESULTS: Of the 9476 ethnically diverse patients who were enrolled, 4745 were assigned to receive intensive therapy and 4731 to receive standard therapy. The mean (±SD) age was 64.7±8.2 years, and 5871 of the patients (62.0%) were women. The mean systolic blood pressure during follow-up (with exclusion of the first 3 months) was 121.8±10.8 mm Hg in the intensive-therapy group and 135.4±8.2 mm Hg in the standard-therapy group. During a median follow-up of 4.0 years (interquartile range, 3.9 to 4.0), a primary-outcome event occurred in 286 patients (6.0%; 1.65 events per 100 person-years) in the intensive-therapy group and in 315 patients (6.7%; 1.83 events per 100 person-years) in the standard-therapy group (hazard ratio, 0.90; 95% confidence interval, 0.77 to 1.06; P = 0.20). Serious adverse events occurred in 706 patients (14.9%) with intensive therapy and in 693 patients (14.6%) with standard therapy.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with type 2 diabetes, targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg, as compared with less than 140 mm Hg, did not reduce the occurrence of major cardiovascular events. (Funded by Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein and the Brazilian Ministry of Health; OPTIMAL-DIABETES ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04040634.).

articles.title: Discontinuing Statins in Older Adults without Cardiovascular Disease.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether discontinuing statin therapy in older adults with at least two chronic conditions but no known cardiovascular disease affects the time to a first cardiovascular event is not well characterized.

METHODS: We conducted an international, open-label, randomized, controlled trial that enrolled adults at least 70 years of age who were taking statins for primary prevention. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either discontinue or continue statin therapy and other lipid-lowering therapies. The primary outcome was a composite of nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal ischemic stroke, or death from any cause, whichever occurred first. The primary analysis assessed noninferiority on the basis of the between-group difference in restricted mean event-free survival time at 2 years, with a noninferiority margin of -5.2 weeks.

RESULTS: A total of 1880 participants underwent randomization: 938 were assigned to the discontinuation group and 942 to the continuation group. The mean age of the participants was 77.5 years, and 46.9% were women. The between-group difference in the restricted mean event-free survival time at 2 years was -2.0 weeks (95% confidence interval, -3.7 to -0.3; P<0.001 for noninferiority). Over a median follow-up of 103 weeks, 119 participants (12.7%) in the discontinuation group and 87 (9.2%) in the continuation group had a primary-outcome event. At least one serious adverse event occurred in 43.0% of the participants in the discontinuation group and in 39.8% in the continuation group.

CONCLUSIONS: Among older adults with at least two chronic conditions but no known cardiovascular disease, discontinuation of statin therapy was noninferior to continuation with respect to major cardiovascular events or death from any cause at 2 years. (Funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation; STREAM ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05178420.).

articles.title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Control in Patients with Previous Ischemic Stroke.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether intensive blood-pressure control reduces cardiovascular risk after cerebrovascular events remains uncertain.

METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 30 sites in Brazil, we assigned participants with elevated blood pressure and previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack to receive intensive treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or to receive standard treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. The primary outcome was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure.

RESULTS: A total of 4368 participants were enrolled, with 2172 assigned to intensive treatment and 2196 to standard treatment. The mean (±SD) age of the participants was 63.9±11.2 years, and 2093 (47.9%) were women. During the follow-up period, excluding the first 3 months, the mean systolic blood pressure was 122.0±11.5 mm Hg (median, 119.6 mm Hg) in the intensive-treatment group and 135.2±9.7 mm Hg (median, 135.0 mm Hg) in the standard-treatment group, with a between-group mean difference of 13.1 mm Hg (95% confidence interval [CI], 12.5 to 13.8). Over a median follow-up of 3.9 years, a primary-outcome event occurred in 236 participants (10.9%; 3.25 events per 100 person-years) with intensive treatment and in 297 (13.5%; 4.11 events per 100 person-years) with standard treatment (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.94; P = 0.007). The composite renal outcome (sustained reduction of ≥50% in the estimated glomerular filtration rate or progression to end-stage renal disease) was more common with intensive treatment. The overall incidence of serious adverse events was similar in the two groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Among participants with previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack, targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg resulted in a lower incidence of major cardiovascular events than targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. (Funded by Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein and the Brazilian Ministry of Health; OPTIMAL-STROKE ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04036409.).

articles.title: Pelacarsen and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with High Lipoprotein(a).
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pelacarsen, an antisense oligonucleotide, reduces serum levels of lipoprotein(a). However, the effect of pelacarsen on cardiovascular outcomes remains uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted an international, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving patients with preexisting cardiovascular disease and a lipoprotein(a) level of at least 70 mg per deciliter. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous pelacarsen (80 mg) administered monthly or matching placebo. The primary end point was a major adverse cardiovascular event, defined as a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or urgent coronary revascularization.

RESULTS: A total of 8350 patients underwent randomization, with 8322 included in the efficacy analysis; 4157 patients were assigned to receive pelacarsen, and 4165 to receive placebo. The mean age of the patients was 59.7 years, and 27.0% were women. The median lipoprotein(a) level at baseline was 236 nmol per liter. At 12 months, the lipoprotein(a) level was 64.4 nmol per liter in the pelacarsen group and 233.4 nmol per liter in the placebo group. The median follow-up was 4.7 years. A primary end-point event occurred in 511 patients (12.3%) in the pelacarsen group and in 503 (12.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.02, 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.90 to 1.15, P = 0.76). Among patients with a baseline lipoprotein(a) level of at least 90 mg per deciliter, a primary end-point event occurred in 402 of 3266 patients (12.3%) in the pelacarsen group and in 403 of 3274 (12.3%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.87 to 1.15; P = 0.99). Serious adverse events occurred in 1553 of 4166 patients (37.3%) who received pelacarsen and in 1709 of 4154 (41.1%) who received placebo.

CONCLUSIONS: Pelacarsen did not result in a lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events than placebo at a median follow-up of 4.7 years. (Funded by Novartis; Lp[a]HORIZON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04023552.)See also in NEJM Evidence: Extended Analyses of Pelacarsen and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with High Lipoprotein(a).

articles.title: Achieved LDL-C Levels and Clinical Outcomes Following Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with Drug-Coated Balloons for De Novo Coronary Lesions.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with a drug-coated balloon (DCB) is a coronary revascularization strategy; however, the prognostic impact of achieved low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels after intervention remains unclear. In this study, we aimed to understand the association between LDL-C and the clinical outcomes in patients undergoing PCI with DCB.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients who underwent PCI with DCB (April 2019-March 2023) and had available 6-month LDL-C data. The clinical outcomes were assessed using a 6-month landmark approach. Patients were stratified by LDL-C level (＜70, 70-＜100, and ≥ 100 mg/dL). The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and target lesion revascularization (TLR).

RESULTS: Among 320 patients, 47.8% had LDL-C ＜70 mg/dL, 31.6% had 70-＜100 mg/dL, and 20.6% had LDL-C ≥ 100 mg/dL. The cumulative incidence of MACE and TLR was significantly higher with increasing LDL-C levels (log-rank P = 0.006 and P = 0.023, respectively), whereas all-cause mortality and myocardial infarction did not differ significantly. In a multivariate Cox regression analysis, LDL-C ≥ 100 mg/dL independently predicted TLR (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.31; 95% confidence interval, 1.16-4.61; P = 0.02). In an exploratory subgroup analysis, PCSK9 inhibitor use was associated with lower achieved LDL-C levels and reduced rates of MACE and TLR.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing PCI with DCB, higher achieved LDL-C levels, particularly LDL-C ≥ 100 mg/dL, were independently associated with an increased TLR risk, which primarily drove the observed difference in MACE. These findings highlight the importance of optimal LDL-C management following PCI with DCB.

articles.title: Challenges in nuclear emergency preparedness: pharmacists' awareness, knowledge, and willingness to participate in the emergency distribution of stable iodine in Japan.
articles.abstract: The effective implementation of stable iodine (SI) prophylaxis is a critical component of nuclear emergency preparedness; however, the role and readiness of pharmacists, who are key providers of medication guidance, remain unclear. This nationwide survey aimed to assess pharmacists' awareness, knowledge, and willingness to participate in the emergency distribution of stable iodine (EDSI) and to compare those outcomes in prefectures that include areas within 30 km of a nuclear power plant (Zone-included) with those in other prefectures (Zone-excluded). Among 489 pharmacists aware of SI, the Zone-included demonstrated significantly higher awareness of EDSI procedures and priority populations. However, their willingness to cooperate in EDSI was paradoxically lower than that of the Zone-excluded. Only one-third of all respondents understood priority groups for SI prophylaxis, and many expressed concerns about providing accurate medication counseling during emergencies. These findings reveal critical gaps in professional preparedness and highlight the need for targeted education, structured training in nuclear emergency medicine, and institutional frameworks that support pharmacists' roles during nuclear incidents. Strengthening these systems is essential to ensure timely, safe, and effective public protection in future nuclear emergencies.

articles.title: Current Status and Outcomes of Infective Endocarditis in Adults With Congenital Heart Disease in Japan　- A Nationwide JROAD-DPC Analysis.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nationwide data on infective endocarditis (IE) in adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) in Japan are limited.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Using a nationwide Japanese administrative database (2013-2023), we identified 822 ACHD patients (median age 41 years; 32.0% female) hospitalized for IE. In-hospital mortality rate was 4.0%, and cardiac surgery was performed in 38.6%. Older age, severe CHD complexity, and pulmonary hypertension were independently associated with in-hospital death.

CONCLUSIONS: This study clarified the clinical characteristics and outcomes of IE in ACHD in Japan.

articles.title: Pediatric nonmalignant hematology ICU admissions: A 10-year study.
articles.abstract: Nonmalignant hematological disorders in children may lead to severe complications requiring Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) admission. Data regarding critically ill patients with these conditions remain limited. This study assesses disease burden, clinical course, and critical care requirements in this population. We conducted a retrospective observational study of pediatric patients with nonmalignant hematological disorders in a level III PICU between 2016 and 2025. Demographics, diagnoses, admission characteristics, supportive therapies, organ dysfunction, infectious complications, and outcomes were analyzed. During the study period, 146 admissions involving 91 patients accounted for 3.9% of all PICU admissions. Median age at admission was 10 years (IQR 6.2-13.4), and 56% of patients were male. SCD was the most frequent underlying diagnosis (47 patients, 51.6%; 70 admissions, 47.9%), followed by BMF syndromes (20 patients, 22%; 47 admissions; 32,2%), predominantly aplastic anemia (AA). Most admissions were planned (n = 92, 63%). Surgical indications accounted for 45.2% of admissions (n = 66), medical causes for 39.7% (n = 58), and procedure-related for 15.1% (n = 22). Among unplanned medical admissions, septic shock was the leading cause of PICU admission (40.8%), followed by pulmonary complications. Infectious episodes occurred in 40 admissions, with microorganisms isolated in 47.5% of cases. Healthcare-associated infections (HAI) occurred in 16.4% of admissions. Unplanned admissions were associated with longer PICU stays. Overall PICU mortality was 6.2%, exceeding predicted mortality (3.4%), with septic shock the leading cause of death. Nonmalignant hematological disorders represent a substantial PICU burden, particularly among SCD and BMF patients. Unplanned admissions carried higher morbidity and mortality, underscoring the need for vigilant monitoring and timely escalation of care.

articles.title: Economic Evaluation Models of Specialty Disease-Modifying Anti-rheumatic Drugs After Failure of Conventional Therapies: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Decision-analytic models are widely used to evaluate specialty disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs in rheumatoid arthritis, but approaches to modeling uncertainty, validation, and transparency vary. We aimed to synthesize the modeling approaches of published economic evaluations of specialty disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs for adults with rheumatoid arthritis after failure or intolerance of conventional therapies.

METHODS: We searched EMBASE, MEDLINE, and EconLit (up to 30 June 2026) for model-based full economic evaluations published in 2010 or later. Two reviewers screened studies and abstracted model conceptualization, scope, structure, and assumptions; model uncertainty and value-of-information analyses; model validation; and model transparency and potential conflicts of interest.

RESULTS: Forty-four studies met inclusion criteria. State-transition models predominated (22 cohort Markov models and 17 microsimulations), with fewer hybrid decision tree plus Markov models (2) and discrete-event simulations (3). Most studies used payer or health-sector perspectives (31/44) and lifetime horizons (35/44). One-way sensitivity analysis (41/44) and probabilistic sensitivity analysis (40/44) were commonly reported, whereas value-of-information analysis was rare (2/44). Validation reporting largely reflected face validity; technical verification was reported in 5/44 studies and predictive validation in 1/44. No study provided a publicly available executable model, and reporting of data and input accessibility varied.

CONCLUSIONS: Rheumatoid arthritis economic models commonly use state-transition frameworks and functional disability measures to project lifetime costs and health outcomes, but show persistent gaps in uncertainty analysis, validation, and reproducibility. Future models should more systematically test structural and extrapolation assumptions, strengthen validation, and improve documentation and data sharing to support policy and coverage decisions.

articles.title: Molecular Mechanism of Aerobic Exercise Regulating YAP to Improve TAC-Induced Heart Failure.
articles.abstract: The Yes-associated protein (YAP) pathway regulates cardiomyocyte proliferation, apoptosis, and immune homeostasis, with dual cardiac pathophysiological roles: aberrant activation worsens heart failure (HF), while targeted inhibition of YAP restores myocardial health. This study explores how aerobic exercise and Verteporfin intervention mediate YAP signaling to mitigate HF. The study uses a pressure overload-induced HF animal model to evaluate the effects of aerobic exercise, YAP inhibition, and their combination. Aerobic exercise preserved YAP abundance and suppressed phosphorylation-YAP overexpression in TAC-induced heart failure. This improves mitochondrial ultrastructure and cardiac function. YAP inhibition attenuates maladaptive remodeling by modulating macrophage polarization, downregulating M1 and upregulating M2 markers. The combination of aerobic exercise and YAP inhibition synergistically reduces fibrosis, hypertrophy, inflammation, and restores cardiac function. These findings identify YAP as a key target for exercise-mediated cardioprotection, and the potential mechanism may be through protecting mitochondrial integrity and immune homeostasis. This study offers novel insights into exercise-regulated YAP signaling as a therapeutic strategy for pressure overload-induced HF.

articles.title: Association Between Colchicine Use and Clinical Outcomes Post Cardiac Surgery: A Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.journal: American journal of cardiovascular drugs : drugs, devices, and other interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Colchicine has been shown to mitigate inflammation and reduce adverse cardiovascular events. However, evidence from clinical trials has been mixed regarding its efficacy in cardiovascular prevention among patients undergoing cardiac surgery.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to evaluate the association between colchicine use and cardiovascular outcomes in patients undergoing cardiac surgery.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic literature search on various electronic databases for relevant studies from their inception until July 15, 2025. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) with two arms-one with colchicine as an intervention and the other with placebo-in patients undergoing cardiac surgery were included. Risk ratios (RRs) and weighted mean differences (WMDs), along with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), were pooled using a random-effects model. A p value of < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: Nine RCTs with 2005 patients (990 in the colchicine group and 1015 in the placebo group) were included. The mean age was 62.8 years. Pooled analysis demonstrated that compared with placebo, colchicine was significantly associated with a reduction in the risk of postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) (RR 0.70 [95% CI 0.59-0.83], p < 0.001). However, between the groups, there was no statistically significant difference in the risk of all-cause mortality (ACM) (RR 0.81 [95% CI 0.39-1.69], p = 0.57, I2 = 0%), stroke (RR 1.86 [95% CI 0.48-7.12], p = 0.37), and permanent pacemaker implantation (PPM) (RR 1.36 [95% CI 0.08-22.44], p = 0.83). Length of hospital stay, which was exploratory, was significantly shorter in the colchicine group (WMD - 1.16 [95% CI - 1.89 to - 0.44], p < 0.01) compared to placebo.

CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis demonstrates that colchicine appears to reduce the risk of POAF. However, it does not significantly affect the risks in terms of PPM, ACM, or stroke.

REGISTRATION: PROSPERO identifier no. CRD420251117966.

articles.title: Music-based interventions for anxiety and depression in adult cancer patients: an umbrella review of the evidence landscape and methodological quality.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Music-based interventions have been increasingly investigated as complementary approaches for managing anxiety and depression among adults with cancer. However, the growing number of systematic reviews has resulted in heterogeneous conclusions, and the methodological robustness and characteristics of the existing evidence synthesis landscape remain uncertain. This umbrella review aimed to critically appraise the evidence landscape and methodological quality of systematic reviews evaluating music-based interventions for anxiety and depression in adults with cancer.

METHODS: An appraisal-focused umbrella review was conducted. We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, EBSCO, Scopus, Wiley Online Library, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, ProQuest, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang Data, and VIP Database from inception to January 6, 2026. Systematic reviews of randomized controlled trials evaluating music-based interventions for anxiety and/or depression in adults with cancer were eligible for inclusion. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and methodological appraisal. Methodological quality was assessed using A Measurement Tool to Assess Systematic Reviews 2 (AMSTAR 2), risk of bias was evaluated using the Risk Of Bias In Systematic Reviews tool (ROBIS), and overlap among primary studies was quantified using the corrected covered area (CCA). Narrative synthesis was conducted without new meta-analysis or quantitative reanalysis.

RESULTS: Twenty systematic reviews published between 2015 and 2025 were included. All included systematic reviews incorporated quantitative synthesis, including one network meta-analysis. Among the 19 reviews assessed using AMSTAR 2, 17 (89.47%) were rated as having low or critically low confidence in their findings. ROBIS assessment showed that 12 reviews (60%) had a high risk of bias, whereas 5 (25%) were judged as having a low risk of bias. Overlap among primary studies was slight, with CCA values of 5.04% for anxiety and 3.97% for depression. Although most systematic reviews reported beneficial effects of music-based interventions, interpretation of these findings was limited by methodological concerns, risk of bias, and inconsistent reporting of certainty assessments.

CONCLUSION: This umbrella review indicates that music-based interventions may have beneficial effects on anxiety and depression outcomes in adults with cancer; however, confidence in these findings is constrained by limitations in the methodological quality and reporting of existing systematic reviews. Future evidence syntheses should prioritize rigorous methodology, transparent reporting, and improved assessment of evidence certainty to strengthen the evidence base for music-based interventions in cancer care.

articles.title: Correction: Erythrocyte membrane with CLIPPKF as biomimetic nanodecoy traps merozoites and attaches to infected red blood cells to prevent Plasmodium infection.
Human plasma amino acid balance favours HIV-1 replication in primary CD4 T lymphocytes.
articles.abstract: Cellular metabolism supports all viral replication steps, and the metabolic state of infected cells is a key factor influencing viral infections. Human Immunodeficiency virus (HIV) remains latent in resting CD4 T lymphocytes but actively replicates in activated CD4 T cells, in part due to enhanced energy metabolism. Here, using the recently developed Human Plasma-Like Medium (HPLM) that mimics the physiological plasma concentration of metabolites, we investigate how this near-physiologic environment modulates HIV-1 infection in primary CD4 T cells. Compared to the conventional culture medium (RPMI), HPLM enhances HIV-1 infection in CD4 T cells despite similar levels of cellular activation, proliferation and expression of viral receptors. In contrast with previous studies using RPMI, HPLM increases infection while decreasing energy metabolism and affecting other non-energetic metabolic pathways. By adjusting levels of several metabolites in RPMI and HPLM, we uncover that the amino acid balance rather than energy metabolism favours HIV-1 replication in this system. Overall, our study uses near-physiological conditions to better define metabolic dependencies of viral infections and highlights non-energetic metabolism pathways important for HIV-1 infection.

articles.title: Single-nucleus cNMF identifies a six-gene classifier predictive of atrial fibrillation recurrence.
articles.journal: Mammalian genome : official journal of the International Mammalian Genome Society
articles.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) reflects intertwined immune-stromal remodeling, yet compact and generalizable diagnostic markers remain limited. Left-atrial single-nucleus RNA-seq was analyzed using SCTransform, PCA/UMAP, and lineage-aware cNMF (K = 4-8) to define transcriptional programs. Immune-related genes were filtered via ImmPort and analyzed using clusterProfiler, ReactomePA, and Enrichr. A 16-model benchmarking framework integrating stepwise GLM and LASSO identified a six-gene panel (EXT1, ATG7, PTPRC, MERTK, IRAK3, RORA). Immune infiltration was estimated using CIBERSORTx, and clinical outcomes were assessed using Andersen-Gill and Fine-Gray models. Experimental validation included RT-qPCR, siRNA-mediated knockdown, wound-healing, colony formation, and immunofluorescence assays in AF-mimicking atrial fibroblasts. Docking-guided drug screening and gene-drug interaction assays were performed to evaluate therapeutic targeting. Luciferase assays confirmed miRNA regulation. cNMF revealed lineage-restricted programs enriched in TGF-β, interferon-α, and inflammatory signaling, with macrophage and T cell activation as dominant features. The six-gene panel achieved AUROC = 0.583 (AUPRC = 0.627) with consistent external validation. RT-qPCR confirmed upregulation of all genes under AF-like conditions. Functional assays demonstrated that MERTK and IRAK3 regulate fibroblast activation, migration, proliferation, and extracellular matrix deposition, with MERTK exerting the strongest effect. Docking-guided screening identified MK-2461 as a potent inhibitor of fibrotic remodeling, significantly reducing gene expression, wound healing, and α-SMA/collagen accumulation. Lack of additive effects with MERTK knockdown indicated target dependency. hsa-miR-155-5p directly repressed all six genes. Persistent AF showed increased recurrence and progression risk. This integrative framework links immune-stromal remodeling, miRNA regulation, functional fibroblast activation, and therapeutic targeting, identifying MERTK as a key driver and actionable target in AF progression.

articles.title: Healthcare Professionals' Priorities for Guidelines on Deprescribing Antihyperglycemics: A Mixed-Methods Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: For older adults living with frailty and type 2 diabetes, reassessing the appropriateness of medications is important. This may include consideration of deprescribing (reducing or stopping) antihyperglycemic medications. Our deprescribing.org team created a guideline for deprescribing antihyperglycemics in 2017. To inform a guideline update, we conducted a prioritization exercise to ensure our update addresses current healthcare professional (HCP) needs and priorities.

OBJECTIVE: The aim was to establish HCP priorities with regards to the guideline topics, outcomes, and knowledge translation materials included with the 2017 guideline and identify gaps in the content to be added to the update.

METHODS: We conducted a sequential explanatory mixed-methods study between April and June 2025, including a survey open to participants globally, followed by focus groups open to participants in Canada. Quantitative survey data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Qualitative data within the survey and focus group discussions were analyzed using summative content analysis and conventional content analysis, respectively.

RESULTS: All guideline topics proposed in the survey were considered either "extremely important" or "important" by the majority of participants. The outcome considered most critical for decision-making when deprescribing was clinical symptoms of hypoglycemia (91%). As a knowledge translation tool, a decision-support algorithm was considered important or extremely important by 84% of respondents. Qualitative findings highlighted considerations for incorporating novel antihyperglycemic agents into deprescribing decisions, cost implications for the patient, and knowledge translation resources (e.g., reporting templates) to support clear communication between prescribers, and patient education materials.

CONCLUSIONS: The topics and outcomes included in deprescribing.org's 2017 antihyperglycemic deprescribing guideline were all considered important or extremely important by HCPs and therefore we will recommend that these be carried forward into the new guideline. Next steps will include reporting HCP priorities to the guideline panel and updating the systematic review for the guideline.

articles.title: Understanding left atrial pressure: basic physiology, hemodynamics, and current echocardiographic assessment.
articles.abstract: Left atrial pressure (LAP) is a major determinant of pulmonary congestion and a key hemodynamic parameter in patients with heart failure and atrial fibrillation. LAP has traditionally been regarded as a surrogate of left ventricular (LV) filling pressure. However, growing evidence indicates that LAP reflects integrated interactions between left atrial (LA) mechanics, LV diastolic and systolic function, and extrinsic mechanical restraints throughout the cardiac cycle. Understanding the physiological basis of the LAP waveform provides important insights into the LA booster pump, reservoir, and conduit functions, as well as LA-LV interactions. Recent advances in echocardiography have expanded the noninvasive assessment of LAP beyond conventional Doppler indices. Contemporary approaches integrate the values of transmitral flow, mitral annular velocity, pulmonary venous flow, LA volume, and LA reservoir strain to provide a more comprehensive noninvasive assessment of LAP. In particular, LA reservoir strain has emerged as a promising marker of LAP and atrial mechanics. Additionally, exercise stress echocardiography and preload stress testing can reveal occult abnormalities in LAP responses that are not apparent at rest, particularly in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. Abnormal LAP also plays a central role in the pathophysiology of atrial fibrillation, atrial remodeling, and stiff LA physiology. This review summarizes the physiological determinants of LAP, the hemodynamic significance of the LAP waveform, and contemporary echocardiographic approaches for the assessment of LAP, and the impact of extrinsic mechanical restraints on LAP, with particular emphasis on the clinical relevance of LA-LV interactions in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and atrial fibrillation.

articles.title: Timing of Artificial Intelligence vs Human Identification of Cardiac Amyloidosis on Echocardiography.
Validation of Ontario criteria for patients transplanted with hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.journal: HPB : the official journal of the International Hepato Pancreato Biliary Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver transplantation (LT) is a curative treatment option for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with different listing criteria available. Data on expected survival of patients with regard to the Ontario criteria (OC), and predictive performance of its components, is warranted.

METHODS: Within the United Network for Organ Sharing registry, patients with HCC, and complete tumor information at the time of listing were included. Survival analysis, prediction performance (area under the receiving operating curve (AUROC)) for post-transplantation overall survival (OS), and multivariable regression was conducted. Differences of OC compared to the Milan Criteria (MC) were investigated.

RESULTS: The 29,086 patients with HCC having received LT have a median age of 60years(IQR:55,64), 22,303 (77%) male, and a median Model of End-stage Liver Disease score of 10(IQR:8,14). Patients within OC reached a post-transplant 5-year OS of 76%(95%CI:75,76), median OS 13.5years (95%CI:13.2,13.9), and HCC-associated deaths occurred in 8.0% at 5 years. OC's performance for 10-years OS corresponds to an AUROC of 62%(95%CI:61,63). 'Within-MC-beyond-OC' have a higher mortality hazard rate compared to 'within-MC-within-OC' (aHR:1.83; 95%CI:1.60,2.10) - driven by high alpha fetoprotein (AFP) levels.

DISCUSSION: The OC are associated with excellent results. Incorporating AFP appears to improve risk stratification of HCC patients listed for LT.

articles.title: Body composition in octogenarians with chronic kidney disease. Role of gender.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The population with chronic kidney disease (CKD) is undergoing marked ageing, and octogenarian patients represent a growing group with distinctive clinical and functional characteristics. In this context, alterations in fluid status and body composition (BC) limit the usefulness of body mass index, necessitating a more accurate assessment with bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA). The aim of this study was to evaluate gender-related differences in body composition in octogenarian patients with CKD in a prospective observational cohort study with a 14-year longitudinal follow-up of clinical events.

METHODS: A total of 724 patients were included (46.4% women), with a mean age of 84.7 years and a mean estimated glomerular filtration rate of 36.6 ml/min/1.73 m2. Vectorial tetrapolar BIA was used to analyse body composition parameters, hydration status, and bioelectrical variables, while muscle strength was assessed by handgrip dynamometry. In addition, risk of progression to kidney replacement therapy, fracture risk, cardiovascular risk, and age-adjusted comorbidity were evaluated.

RESULTS: The results revealed clinically relevant gender differences.
