Women exhibited lower comorbidity and a lower risk of initiating kidney replacement therapy, but a significantly higher risk of osteoporotic and hip fractures. From a BC perspective, women showed higher adiposity and a greater proportion of ECW, together with lower muscle mass, lower TBW and ICW, and reduced muscle strength. Men presented greater muscle mass and strength but a higher prevalence of dynapenia. Overall sarcopenia was infrequent in the cohort.

CONCLUSION: These findings highlight a marked sexual dimorphism in body composition and functional status among octogenarians with CKD, with important clinical implications for risk stratification and individualized management in this population.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "The attenuation of gut microbiota-derived short-chain fatty acids elevates lipid transportation through suppression of the intestinal HDAC3-H3K27ac-PPAR-γ axis in gestational diabetes mellitus" [The Journal of Nutritional Biochemistry 133 (2024) 109708].
Association of Advanced Age With Functional Recovery After Endovascular Thrombectomy in Patients With Large-core Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Evidence supporting endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for large-core ischemic stroke has expanded, but outcomes in patients aged ≥80 years remain insufficiently characterized. We evaluated outcomes after EVT in this population, with particular attention to prestroke disability-adjusted functional recovery.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with anterior-circulation large vessel occlusion and large-core stroke (Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score 0 to 5 or CT perfusion core volume ≥50 mL) treated with EVT between October 2019 and September 2025. The primary outcome was prestroke disability-adjusted functional recovery, defined as 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) ≤ prestroke mRS + 1.

RESULTS: Among 377 patients, 75 were aged ≥80 years, and 302 were <80 years. Functional recovery occurred in 14.7% and 18.9%, respectively. Age ≥80 years was not significantly associated with functional recovery (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.00; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.45-2.22; p = 0.992). Patients aged ≥80 years had lower odds of mRS 0 to 3 (aOR, 0.41; 95% CI, 0.21-0.79) and higher odds of mortality (aOR, 1.79; 95% CI, 1.01-3.16). Successful reperfusion and hemorrhagic outcomes did not differ significantly between groups. Each 10-year increase in age was associated with lower odds of functional recovery (aOR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.46-0.77).

CONCLUSION: Among selected patients aged ≥80 years with large-core ischemic stroke, successful reperfusion and functional recovery remained achievable after EVT, despite poorer conventional functional outcomes and higher mortality. Advancing age was associated with progressively worse outcomes when modeled continuously. These findings support individualized prognostic assessment after EVT rather than reliance on chronological age alone.

articles.title: Diabetic ketoacidosis associated with the reuse of single-use materials in a patient with type 1 diabetes mellitus treated with an advanced hybrid closed-loop system: A case report.
articles.abstract: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) remains a potentially serious complication in individuals with type 1 diabetes mellitus, even in those treated with continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion systems. We describe the case of a 45-year-old woman using an advanced hybrid closed-loop system who was admitted with an episode of mild DKA in the absence of identifiable precipitating factors. Metabolic correction was performed according to current recommendations, with a favorable clinical course. Subsequent review of continuous glucose monitoring data and insulin delivery records revealed persistent hyperglycemia secondary to malfunction of the infusion device. This was associated with structural deterioration of a reused insulin cartridge designed for single use, in the context of a shortage of original supplies. This case highlights the importance of infusion materials in pump therapy safety, the limitations of automated systems in detecting mechanical failures, and the need for safe alternative strategies in situations of supply disruption.

articles.title: Auditory-Perceptual Voice Evaluation: Validation of the Chilean Spanish Adaptation of the Consensus Auditory-Perceptual Evaluation of Voice (CAPE-V).
articles.journal: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to validate the Chilean Spanish adaptation of CAPE-V and examine its psychometric properties for auditory-perceptual assessment of voice quality in Chilean speakers.

STUDY DESIGN: This was a quantitative, nonexperimental, cross-sectional, descriptive-comparative validation study.

METHODS: The original CAPE-V was adapted to Chilean Spanish through translation, synthesis, back-translation, expert committee review, and pretesting. Sixty-two voice samples were analyzed: 31 normophonic and 31 dysphonic voices. The samples were not matched by sex or age, and laryngological diagnosis and dysphonia severity were not controlled. Four Chilean Spanish-speaking speech-language pathologists with 10 or more years of experience rated all samples using GRBAS and the Chilean Spanish CAPE-V, with a 7-day interval between instruments. Internal consistency, intra-rater reliability, inter-rater reliability, concurrent validity with GRBAS, and construct validity were examined.

RESULTS: The Chilean Spanish CAPE-V showed high internal consistency for overall severity, roughness, strain, breathiness, and loudness, and moderate consistency for pitch. Intra-rater reliability was high for most parameters, except loudness, which was moderate. Inter-rater agreement was excellent for overall severity, roughness, strain, and breathiness, and good for loudness and pitch. Concurrent validity with GRBAS was strong for overall severity/grade and roughness, and moderate for breathiness and strain. Dysphonic voices scored significantly higher than normophonic voices across all CAPE-V parameters.

CONCLUSIONS: The Chilean Spanish CAPE-V is a valid and reliable instrument for auditory-perceptual assessment of dysphonia in Chilean speakers.

articles.title: Air Embolism During Cryoballoon Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation Under Different Respiratory Management Strategies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary air embolism is a rare but potentially fatal complication during catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF). Use of large-bore sheaths, such as those required for balloon-based catheter ablation, in the setting of unstable respiratory control may increase the risk.

METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated consecutive patients who underwent first-time cryoballoon ablation (CBA) for AF from January 2017 to December 2024. Patients were divided into two groups according to respiratory management strategy: adaptive servo-ventilation (ASV, n = 266) and laryngeal mask with mechanical ventilation (LM, n = 225). The incidence of complications was compared, with a primary focus on air embolism.

RESULTS: A total of 491 patients (median age 68 years, 71.3% male) were included. Coronary air embolism occurred in 5 patients (1.9%) in the ASV group and in none of the patients in the LM group (absolute risk difference, 1.9%; 95% CI, -0.1% to 4.3%; p = 0.066). In one patient with coronary air embolism, brain MRI performed on the day of the procedure incidentally revealed an asymptomatic acute cerebral embolic lesion. Other complications included two cases of cardiac tamponade in the ASV group and two cases of transient phrenic nerve palsy in the LM group.

CONCLUSIONS: Coronary air embolism was numerically less frequent in patients undergoing cryoballoon ablation with laryngeal mask ventilation than in those managed with ASV, although the difference did not reach statistical significance. Further prospective studies are warranted to clarify the potential role of respiratory management in procedural safety.

articles.title: Transplacental transfer efficiency and longitudinal dynamics of antibodies against RSV in early childhood: a paired mother-neonate cohort study in southern China.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Maternal antibodies provide early-life protection against severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection but wane rapidly. With the availability of maternal vaccine and half-life extended monoclonal antibodies for infants, understanding transplacental antibody transfer and subsequent antibody dynamics is important for optimising immunisation strategies.

METHODS: We conducted a longitudinal cohort study of 695 mother-neonate pairs in southern China between 2013 and 2021. Serum samples were collected from mothers at delivery and from children at birth, 2, 4, 6, 12, 24, 36 months, and 5-8 years of age. All samples were tested for RSV pre-F IgG antibodies using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. A subset of samples was additionally tested for neutralizing antibodies (nAbs) using a foci reduction neutralization test.

RESULTS: Maternal and cord blood RSV pre-F IgG antibody levels were positively correlated ( = 0.87; P<0.001) with a mean transplacental transfer ratio of 1.44 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.40-1.47). A 10-fold increase in maternal antibody levels was associated with a 6.46-fold increase in cord blood antibody levels, corresponding to a 35% decrease in transplacental transfer ratios. Preterm birth was associated with 17% lower cord blood antibody levels than full-term birth. Maternally derived antibodies declined rapidly after birth, with an estimated half-life of 34.3 days (95% CI, 33.9-34.8); antibody levels reached a nadir at approximately 10 months of age and gradually increased thereafter. RSV pre-F IgG and nAb titers from children were strongly correlated (repeated-measures correlation: = 0.846, P < 0.001), and the correlation persisted after adjustment for age ( = 0.743, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight the importance of addressing lower maternally derived antibody levels in preterm infants, particularly in the context of maternal immunisation. Longitudinal antibody dynamics reveal a distinct period of low antibody levels during infancy that may inform the timing of targeted RSV immunisation strategies.

articles.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors on Asthma Exacerbations.
articles.journal: Annals of allergy, asthma & immunology : official publication of the American College of Allergy, Asthma, & Immunology

articles.title: Characterizing population movement patterns during a Sudan Virus Disease outbreak to adjust response efforts, Uganda, 2022.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: In September 2022, Uganda declared a Sudan virus disease outbreak in Mubende District. The Uganda Ministry of Health sought to characterize population movement patterns to identify areas at heightened transmission risk and guide outbreak response efforts.

METHODS: From September to December 2022, response teams adapted the Population Connectivity Across Borders (PopCAB) method to conduct focus group discussions, key informant interviews, and participatory mapping with case-contacts and community members across three districts. Results characterizing local and cross-border travel routes and reasons for travel were applied to adjust response actions.

RESULTS: Participants identified 69 locations across seven non-contiguous districts, including healthcare facilities, gold mines, schools, and transportation hubs linked to travel for trade, farming, healthcare, and family visits. Ministry of Health response teams used the results to enhance surveillance, risk communication, and infection prevention measures at priority locations including cross-border areas. Surveillance activities adjusted by the PopCAB results directly detected two cases in Kampala and indirectly identified 26 additional cases in newly targeted districts.

CONCLUSIONS: Integrating community-based mobility mapping into contact tracing enabled rapid identification of high-risk areas beyond the outbreak epicenter. Response teams in similar settings can rapidly deploy this approach to generate real-time mobility data, improve resource allocation, and strengthen communicable disease containment efforts.

articles.title: A blinded, non-inferiority randomised clinical trial comparing the efficacy and safety of low-dose methotrexate and ciclosporin for the control of moderate to severe canine atopic dermatitis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Canine atopic dermatitis (cAD) is a chronic, inflammatory skin disease that may require long-term systemic immunomodulatory treatment. Low-dose methotrexate (MTX) is an inexpensive immunomodulator used in human dermatology, but robust veterinary data are lacking.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether weekly subcutaneous low-dose MTX is non-inferior to oral ciclosporin (CsA) in controlling moderate-to-severe cAD.

ANIMALS: Fifty-five client-owned dogs with non-seasonal moderate-to-severe cAD enrolled at nine dermatology centres in France.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Randomised, double-blind, positive-controlled, multicentre non-inferiority trial. Dogs received either subcutaneous MTX (0.15-0.5mg/kg/week) plus oral placebo, or oral CsA (5mg/kg/day, then spaced) plus injectable placebo. The primary endpoint was the percentage reduction in the CADESI-04 lesional score on week 28 (non-inferiority margin 20%). Secondary endpoints included the Pruritus Visual Analogue Scale (PVAS) and CADESI-04 scores, assessed 4-weekly, and drug protocol safety assessments.

RESULTS: Fifty-five dogs were randomised (MTX n=28; CsA n=27). At week 28, mean CADESI-04 reductions were 65.4% (MTX) and 69.5% (CsA), demonstrating non-inferiority. CsA induced faster improvement (weeks 4-12), but efficacy converged by week 20. Gastrointestinal adverse events occurred more frequently with MTX (82%) than with CsA (70%). No consistent haematological, renal or hepatic injury was observed during the study. Two MTX-treated dogs developed severe liver disease during long-term follow-up.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Weekly subcutaneous low-dose MTX provided non-inferior control of lesions and pruritus compared with CsA by week 28. Although slower in onset and associated with more gastrointestinal adverse events, MTX may represent an affordable long-term cAD treatment option, with appropriate hepatic monitoring.

articles.title: Elevated plasma phenylacetylglutamine is independently associated with heart failure: A cross-sectional biomarker study.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract: Phenylacetylglutamine (PAGln), a microbial metabolite generated from dietary phenylalanine, has emerged as a candidate mediator in cardiovascular disease, but whether it holds diagnostic value for heart failure (HF) is unclear. We designed a cross-sectional case-control study at Xiangya Hospital, enrolling 104 participants (65 stable HF patients and 39 non-HF controls), to address this question. Plasma PAGln was quantified by ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS). Concentrations were significantly higher in the HF group than in controls (median 1.7 vs. 1.2 μM, P = 0.001). After multivariable adjustment for age, sex, body mass index, lifestyle factors, comorbidities, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, every 1-SD increase in log-transformed PAGln raised HF odds by 95% (odds ratio [OR] 1.95, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.07-3.56, P = 0.030). The top tertile carried 4.57-fold greater odds than the bottom tertile (OR 4.57, 95% CI 1.08-19.45, P = 0.040). On receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, PAGln achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.658 (95% CI 0.551-0.764) with 46.2% sensitivity and 84.6% specificity. PAGln tracked positively with LDL-C, total cholesterol, and fasting glucose, and inversely with estimated glomerular filtration rate. Notably, the highest PAGln levels were seen in HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), with a significant difference between non-HF and HFrEF subgroups (P = 0.01). Collectively, our results indicate that elevated plasma PAGln is independently linked to HF and may reflect disease severity, supporting its potential as a complementary metabolic biomarker for HF evaluation.

articles.title: CAD PVAT-derived exosomes impair endothelial barrier function through the miR-183-5p/TPM1 axis.
articles.abstract: Crosstalk between perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) and vascular endothelial cells plays an important role in vascular homeostasis and atherosclerosis. However, the contribution of PVAT-derived exosomes to coronary endothelial barrier dysfunction remains incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated the effects of PVAT-derived exosomes obtained from patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) and non-CAD surgical controls on human coronary artery endothelial cells and explored the underlying molecular mechanism. Compared with exosomes from non-CAD controls, CAD PVAT-derived exosomes increased endothelial permeability, disrupted F-actin organization, reduced junctional protein expression, and decreased nitric oxide production and endothelial nitric oxide synthase phosphorylation. miR-183-5p was enriched in CAD PVAT-derived exosomes, and miR-183-5p overexpression reproduced several features of endothelial dysfunction. Dual-luciferase reporter assays identified tropomyosin 1 (TPM1) as a direct target of miR-183-5p. Importantly, inhibition of miR-183-5p attenuated CAD PVAT-exosome-induced endothelial dysfunction, whereas TPM1 overexpression partially reversed the detrimental effects of miR-183-5p. Together, these findings suggest that the miR-183-5p/TPM1 axis contributes to CAD PVAT-exosomes mediated endothelial barrier dysfunction and may represent a potential link between PVAT dysfunction and atherosclerosis.

articles.title: MicroRNA-9-5p targets ELAVL1 to regulate NLRP3 inflammasome activation and cardiomyocyte pyroptosis in diabetic hypoglycemic myocardial injury.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Recurrent hypoglycemia during intensive glycemic control in diabetes is an independent risk factor for cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying its myocardial damage remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the role of post-transcriptional regulatory networks in diabetic recurrent hypoglycemic myocardial injury.

METHODS: Type 2 diabetic mouse models were established using a high-fat diet combined with streptozotocin (STZ) injection, and recurrent hypoglycemia was induced by repeated insulin administration. Integrated mRNA-seq and small RNA-seq were performed to screen differentially expressed genes and microRNAs (miRNAs). Key upstream regulators of the NLR family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome were identified via Pearson correlation analysis combined with predictions from the StarBase, TargetScan, and miRDB databases. Direct binding between miRNA and target gene was verified by dual-luciferase reporter assays. Gain- and loss-of-function experiments were conducted in a diabetic hypoglycemic HL-1 cardiomyocyte model by transfection with miR-9-5p mimics/inhibitor and ELAV-like protein 1 (ELAVL1)-targeting short hairpin RNA (sh-ELAVL1). In vivo intervention and rescue experiments were performed via tail vein injection of miR-9-5p agomir/antagomir and sh-ELAVL1 lentivirus. Myocardial structure and function were evaluated using echocardiography, hematoxylin-eosin (HE) staining, immunofluorescence, and Western blot.

RESULTS: Mice with diabetic recurrent hypoglycemia exhibited significant weight loss (p<0.001) and impaired cardiac function. Transcriptome analysis identified 42 differentially expressed genes between the diabetic (DM) and diabetic hypoglycemic (HDM) groups, with specific enrichment of the NOD-like receptor signaling pathway. Protein levels of NLRP3, cleaved caspase-1 (p20), and the N-terminal fragment of gasdermin D (GSDMD-N, p30) in the myocardium were further significantly upregulated in the HDM group compared with the DM group (p<0.001). Correlation analysis combined with StarBase database screening identified ELAVL1 as the key upstream RNA-binding protein regulating NLRP3 (r=0.82, p<0.001). Small RNA sequencing revealed 16 significantly downregulated miRNAs in the HDM group versus the DM group. Intersection with TargetScan and miRDB predictions of ELAVL1-targeting miRNAs identified miR-9-5p as the sole candidate, which was significantly downregulated in the HDM group (p<0.001). Dual-luciferase reporter assays confirmed direct binding of miR-9-5p to the 3' untranslated region (3'UTR) of ELAVL1 (p<0.001). In vitro, transfection with miR-9-5p mimics significantly reduced the protein levels of ELAVL1, NLRP3, and cleaved caspase-1 (p<0.001), increased cell viability, and decreased lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release (p<0.001). Conversely, miR-9-5p inhibitor promoted these pathological changes, which were fully reversed by sh-ELAVL1 (p<0.001). In vivo, miR-9-5p agomir significantly improved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and left ventricular fractional shortening (LVFS) (both p<0.01), inhibited co-localization of NLRP3 with apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a CARD (ASC), and downregulated the protein levels of GSDMD-N, interleukin-1β (IL-1β), and interleukin-18 (IL-18) (p<0.001). miR-9-5p antagomir exacerbated these injuries, which were effectively reversed by co-administration of sh-ELAVL1 (p<0.001).

CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that miR-9-5p directly targets ELAVL1 to inhibit NLRP3 inflammasome activation and cardiomyocyte pyroptosis, thereby attenuating myocardial injury and improving cardiac function in diabetic recurrent hypoglycemia. The miR-9-5p/ELAVL1/NLRP3 axis may represent a promising therapeutic target for diabetic hypoglycemic myocardial injury, although clinical validation of this axis in patients with diabetes remains to be performed.

articles.title: A Novel Disaccharide 1-Lactulose Ameliorates Acute Liver Injury by Suppressing Oxidative Damage and Promoting Hepatocyte Proliferation.
articles.abstract: Acute liver injury (ALI), arising from diverse etiologies such as drug exposure and viral infection, represents a major global health concern characterized by extensive hepatocyte damage. Protecting injured hepatocytes is a central therapeutic objective, yet clinically available agents that directly target and preserve these cells remain scarce. Here, we synthesized 1-Lactulose, a novel disaccharide, and demonstrated its specific binding to asialoglycoprotein receptor 1 (ASGPR1), a hepatocyte-surface transport receptor, by molecular docking and isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC). In vitro, 1-Lactulose protected AML-12 cells against H2O2- and acetaminophen (APAP) -induced injury, as evidenced by restored cell viability, reduced malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, elevated superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity and glutathione (GSH) content, and enhanced proliferation of damaged hepatocytes. Notably, these protective effects were attenuated by Asgpr1 silencing, suggesting that the protective effect of 1-Lactulose is at least partially dependent on ASGPR1. Treatment with 1-Lactulose consistently attenuated liver injury, suppressed oxidative stress, and promoted hepatocyte proliferation in three mouse models of ALI induced by APAP, CCl4, and ethanol. Mechanistically, 1-Lactulose downregulated Nox4 and upregulated Pdgfra in both AML-12 cells and injured liver tissues, which was associated with attenuated oxidative damage and enhanced hepatocyte proliferation. Collectively, these findings suggest that 1-Lactulose is an ASGPR1-binding hepatoprotective disaccharide that protects against ALI across multiple etiologies through dual modulation of Nox4 and Pdgfra, supporting it as a promising therapeutic candidate for the treatment of ALI.

articles.title: Characterizing White Matter and Structural Brain Network Alterations in Children with Growth Hormone Deficiency Using Diffusion Tensor Imaging.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To characterize white matter microstructure and structural brain network topology in children with growth hormone deficiency (GHD) using diffusion tensor imaging and explore their associations with clinical indicators.

METHODS: A total of 77 short-stature children (GHD = 50, idiopathic short stature [ISS] = 27) and 40 healthy controls (HC) underwent 3D-T1WI and DTI. Nineteen participants were excluded due to poor data quality (10 in the GHD group, 4 in the ISS group, and 5 in the HC group), yielding a final analytical cohort of 40 children with GHD, 23 with ISS, and 35 healthy controls. Tract-Based Spatial Statistics and graph-theoretical analysis were applied to characterize white matter microstructure and network topological properties. Clinical metrics including bone age and pituitary volume were collected.

RESULTS: Children with GHD showed reduced fractional anisotropy together with elevated mean and radial diffusivity relative to controls. Children with ISS showed elevated mean and radial diffusivity without a reduction in fractional anisotropy, and their diffusivity elevations exceeded those observed in the GHD group. Graph-theoretical analysis revealed that the GHD group had significantly higher global efficiency and lower characteristic path length than the HC group, as well as lower clustering coefficient than the ISS group. Rich-club findings were contingent on both the method used to define core nodes and the connection retention thresholds applied to backbone networks. Nodal analysis identified significantly higher betweenness centrality of the left insula in ISS compared with both the GHD and HC groups. Significant associations were observed between white matter microstructural properties, network connectivity, and clinical variables, including age, bone age, and bone age delay.

CONCLUSION: Children with GHD exhibit altered white matter microstructure and global organization of the structural brain network, which differed from the pattern observed in ISS, and these imaging measures were associated with age, bone age, and bone age delay; given the cross-sectional design, causal inference remains unwarranted.

articles.title: Cardiomyocyte-derived ACE2/Ang-(1-7) axis mediates DIZE-induced inhibition of TGF-β signaling to attenuate cardiac fibrosis following myocardial infarction.
articles.abstract: Cardiac fibrosis represents a critical pathological determinant of poor prognosis in coronary artery disease (CAD). Pharmacological activation of the angiotensin-Converting enzyme 2/angiotensin-(1-7) (ACE2/Ang-(1-7)) axis is a promising anti-fibrotic approach for cardiac fibrosis, a condition that currently lacks effective therapies. Diminazene aceturate (DIZE) is recognized as an ACE2 agonist with anti‑fibrotic activity, the molecular mechanism of which has not been fully elucidated. This study demonstrates that the anti-fibrotic effects of DIZE are exerted via a cardiomyocyte-mediated paracrine mechanism, rather than through direct action on fibroblasts. Using a cardiomyocyte-fibroblast co-culture system and transcriptomic analysis, we found that ACE2 activated by DIZE on cardiomyocytes enhances the conversion of Ang II to Ang-(1-7), which subsequently suppresses the pro-fibrotic transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) signaling in adjacent fibroblasts. This effect was partially abrogated by the Ang-(1-7) antagonist A779, confirming Ang-(1-7) as a key paracrine mediator. To exploit this mechanism in vivo, a collagen-binding, low-intensity focused ultrasound (LIFU)-responsive nanoplatform (CNA35-GDP) was developed for specific DIZE delivery. In a rat model of myocardial infarction, LIFU-triggered DIZE release from CNA35-GDP was found to significantly improve cardiac function and attenuate fibrosis. These therapeutic benefits were accompanied by restoration of the ACE2/Ang-(1-7) axis and suppression of TGF-β signaling, thereby validating the proposed mechanism. Collectively, activation of cardiomyocyte-derived ACE2 by DIZE inhibits collagen production in fibroblasts through paracrine Ang-(1-7) and downstream suppression of TGF‑β signaling.

articles.title: GPR146 as a therapeutic target: Linking lipid metabolism with macrophage inflammation in atherosclerosis.
articles.abstract: Atherosclerosis is driven by dyslipidemia and chronic inflammation. GPR146 has emerged as a regulator of cholesterol metabolism; however, whether GPR146 links lipid metabolism with macrophage inflammation during atherosclerosis remains unclear. Apolipoprotein E-deficient (ApoE-/-) mice were fed a high-fat diet for 12 weeks, followed by 4 weeks of intervention with adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated hepatic GPR146 knockdown or rosuvastatin treatment. Atherosclerotic lesions and plaque composition were assessed using Oil Red O staining and immunofluorescence. Lipid profiles, oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL), and inflammatory markers were evaluated using enzymatic assays, ELISA, and qPCR, respectively. In ox-LDL-stimulated THP-1-derived macrophages, GPR146 was silenced to examine lipid accumulation, inflammatory responses, transcriptomic alterations, and the potential involvement of the JAK-STAT signaling pathway. GPR146 expression increased in atherosclerotic lesions, particularly in macrophage-rich regions. Hepatic GPR146 knockdown reduced atherosclerotic lesion burden, circulating total cholesterol and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels, ox-LDL accumulation, and inflammatory activation within plaques. In macrophages, GPR146 silencing suppressed ox-LDL-induced lipid accumulation, accompanied by reduced CD36 expression and decreased foam cell formation. GPR146 silencing also attenuated pro-inflammatory macrophage activation, as evidenced by reduced expression of inflammatory mediators. Transcriptomic analysis implicated JAK-STAT signaling, with reduced JAK2 and STAT3 expression following GPR146 silencing. Pharmacological inhibition of the JAK-STAT signaling partially recapitulated the anti-inflammatory effects associated with GPR146 knockdown. Together, these findings suggest that GPR146 contributes to lipid metabolic regulation and macrophage inflammatory responses during atherosclerosis and may represent a therapeutic target warranting further investigation.

articles.title: The RGS4-Gαq/11 axis in vascular homeostasis: Mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
articles.abstract: Vascular homeostasis, a dynamic equilibrium maintained by the circulatory system, is fundamental to cardiovascular health. Its dysregulation underlies the pathogenesis of major cardiovascular disorders, including hypertension. G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), a versatile family of seven-transmembrane proteins, play a central role in maintaining vascular homeostasis. Upon activation, certain GPCRs couple to Gαq/11 proteins and initiate multiple downstream signaling pathways, thereby regulating vascular tone, structural remodeling, and inflammatory responses. Regulator of G protein signaling 4 (RGS4) functions as a key GTPase-activating protein (GAP) that markedly accelerates GTP hydrolysis by Gαq/11, thereby promoting the timely termination of Gαq/11-mediated signaling. RGS4 therefore plays an important role in maintaining the balance of G protein signaling in the vasculature. Based on the three-dimensional structure of RGS4 (PDB ID: 1AGR), this review systematically delineates the GAP catalytic mechanism of RGS4 and its interactions with downstream effectors, including Gαq/11 and PLCβ. It discusses the pathological role of the RGS4-Gαq/11 signaling axis in major cardiovascular disorders. In addition, from a structural pharmacology perspective, this review surveys the druggable features of RGS4 and reviews previously published in silico docking and molecular dynamics studies of its representative inhibitors, intending to inform potential therapeutic strategies targeting the RGS4-Gαq/11 axis in cardiovascular disease.

articles.title: Frailty Burden in Patients with HFrEF Undergoing Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation: Clinical Outcomes and Readmissions.
articles.journal: The American journal of the medical sciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty is common and has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes across cardiovascular populations. However, its prognostic significance, particularly the impact of graded frailty burden, among patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) undergoing catheter ablation for ventricular tachycardia (VT) remains incompletely characterized.

METHODS: We evaluated the association between frailty burden and in-hospital outcomes among patients with HFrEF undergoing VT ablation using the Nationwide Readmissions Database. Frailty was defined using the validated Johns Hopkins Adjusted Clinical Groups (ACG) frailty indicator. Cumulative frailty burden was quantified as the number of domains (range: 0-10). Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess associations with outcomes, and in-hospital mortality probabilities were estimated across increasing frailty burden.

RESULTS: Among 17,367 hospitalizations for VT ablation in patients with HFrEF, 7.4% were classified as frail. Frailty was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.59; 95% CI, 1.19-2.13; p<0.001), and increased complication rates. Frail patients had higher 30-day (13.6% vs. 9.1%) and 90-day (33.7% vs. 28.1%) readmission rates compared with non-frail patients. Frailty burden demonstrated a graded association with in-hospital mortality, with estimated mortality increasing progressively with each additional frailty domain.

CONCLUSIONS: Frailty is independently associated with worse in-hospital outcomes and higher readmission rates among patients with HFrEF undergoing VT ablation, with a graded increase in risk across increasing frailty domains. These findings suggest that frailty burden may serve as a clinically relevant risk stratification marker in this vulnerable cohort.

articles.title: Reply to: "Letter to the Editor: Dissociation between Airflow and Lung Volume Responses following Triple Therapy Device Switching in Asthma-COPD Overlap".
articles.journal: The American journal of the medical sciences

articles.title: Prevalence of coronary artery disease on coronary CT angiography in asymptomatic, predominantly high-risk Indian adults: A single-centre cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CAD) in South Asians often develops at a younger age and may not be adequately detected by conventional risk stratification or coronary artery calcium scoring (CACS). In this study we assessed the prevalence of CAD in asymptomatic, predominantly physician-referred individuals undergoing coronary CT angiography (CCTA).

METHODS: This single-centre cross-sectional study included 1750 asymptomatic individuals, predominantly physician-referred for cardiovascular risk assessment, who underwent CCTA between 2019 and 2024. Clinical risk factors, Framingham risk score (FRS), and CACS were recorded. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of CAD. Prevalence of CAD in low FRS and CACS was further analysed.

RESULTS: CAD was detected in 1084 individuals (62%), including 787 (45%) with non-obstructive and 297 (17%) with obstructive disease, while coronary calcification (CACS >0) was seen in 957 (54.6%) patients. Increasing FRS scores were associated with increased CAD prevalence (p < 0.001). Increasing CACS was also associated with CAD severity (p < 0.001). On multivariable logistic regression, independent predictors of CAD included age (OR 1.09 per year, 95%CI 1.08-1.11), male sex (OR 2.20, 95%CI 1.55-3.13), diabetes (OR 2.07, 95%CI 1.56-2.76), hypertension (OR 1.47, 95%CI 1.09-1.98), obesity (OR 1.45, 95%CI 1.00-2.10), and elevated LDL/HDL ratio>4 (OR 1.93, 95%CI 1.22-3.04).

CONCLUSION: In this selected cohort of asymptomatic, predominantly high-risk Indian adults referred for CCTA, subclinical coronary atherosclerosis was common, including among individuals with low Framingham risk or zero coronary calcium. Whether detecting such disease with CCTA improves outcomes or is cost-effective requires prospective, outcome-based evaluation.

articles.title: Nutrient-mediated protection against environmental pollutant-induced heart defects: mechanisms and opportunities.
articles.journal: Food and chemical toxicology : an international journal published for the British Industrial Biological Research Association
articles.abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is the most prevalent birth defect worldwide, yet effective prevention strategies remain limited. Accumulating evidence implicates environmental pollutants as significant contributors to abnormalities in cardiac development. The molecular initiating events encompass xenobiotic-receptor-mediated signalling and direct toxicant-biomolecule interactions. These initial events trigger a series of downstream pathogenic cascades that ultimately result in cardiac developmental defects. Nutrients with biological activity and generally favorable safety profiles at recommended dietary intake levels offer considerable potential as preventive agents against pollutant-induced cardiac malformations. Notably, combined nutrient interventions may exert superior synergistic protective effects relative to single-nutrient approaches. This narrative review comprehensively summarizes the molecular initiating events and subsequent pathogenic pathways involved in pollutant-induced cardiac developmental abnormalities. We further critically evaluate the preclinical evidence and signalling targets of nutrients, and propose a scientific framework for the development of precision prenatal nutritional strategies to reduce the burden of environment-related CHD.

articles.title: Optimizing cognitive and behavioural recovery after stroke: clinical integration of dietary supplements with a focus on ω-3 fatty acids.
articles.abstract: Stroke remains a leading cause of long-term disability worldwide, with many survivors experiencing persistent cognitive and behavioural impairments despite advancements in acute management. Post-stroke neurorecovery is often incomplete, contributing to dementia, depression, and reduced quality of life, particularly in low- and middle-income settings where access to advanced rehabilitation and therapeutics is limited. This highlights an urgent need for accessible, adjunctive strategies that can enhance functional recovery. Emerging preclinical evidence indicates that dietary supplements can modulate key biological processes underlying neurorecovery, including neuroplasticity, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial function, and synaptic remodeling. In this narrative review, we examine the role of major classes of nutraceuticals such as omega-3 fatty acids, vitamins, minerals, polyphenols, and amino acids in supporting cognitive and behavioural recovery after stroke with particular emphasis on omega-3 fatty acids, given their central role in neuronal membrane integrity, lipid-mediated signaling, and resolution of inflammation. We integrate mechanistic insights with preclinical and clinical data explicitly highlighting that theoretical models and basic research demonstrate significant promise, while current clinical evidence remains heterogeneous and frequently inconclusive. We discuss how dietary supplementation might be strategically incorporated alongside conventional rehabilitation paradigms including physiotherapycognitive training, and pharmacotherapy. We further highlight emerging concepts such as the gut-brain axis, precision nutrition, and biomarker-guided interventions, which are shaping the future of personalized neurorehabilitation. Ultimately, while dietary supplements offer a promising, cost-effective and accessible adjunctive approach. their current clinical utility is constrained by mixed translational efficacy. Overcoming these limitations will require rigorous patient selection, optimized timing, and shift towards evidence-based personalized, multimodal strategies. This will be essential to fully harness their therapeutic potential in improving cognitive and behavioural outcomes in stroke recovery.

articles.title: Evolution and impact of sarcopenia and myosteatosis in the context of liver transplantation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Sarcopenia and myosteatosis have a well-documented adverse impact on survival in liver cirrhosis patients. This study aimed to assess the prevalence and risk factors associated with muscle impairment before liver transplantation (LT), their evolution after LT, and to determine their prognostic value.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: All cirrhotic patients listed for LT at our center between 2006 and 2010 were included. Sarcopenia and myosteatosis were assessed on transverse L3 CT images at LT listing and at 12 (M12), 60, 120, and 180 months after LT.

RESULTS: The study population consisted of 198 patients, 75.3% of whom were men, and 149 underwent LT. At LT listing, sarcopenia was diagnosed in 45.5% of patients and myosteatosis in 36.5% and 20.1% had both sarcopenia and myosteatosis. One year after LT, 56.1% of patients had persistent sarcopenia and 15.3% had de novo sarcopenia. Sarcopenia significantly improved at M12 post-LT (p=0.034). Post-LT patient survival was 89.2%, 76.3%, and 59.3% at 1, 5, and 10 years respectively. In multivariate analysis, at LT listing, MELD score ≥ 25 (HR: 2.549; p=0.001), sarcopenia (HR: 1.749; p=0.004) and myosteatosis (HR: 1.630; p=0.012) were found to be independent risk factors for overall mortality. The effects of sarcopenia and myosteatosis were additive: overall survival was significantly reduced in patients with both sarcopenia and myosteatosis compared to patients with isolated sarcopenia/myosteatosis (p=0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Sarcopenia and myosteatosis are common in cirrhotic patients listed for LT, persist after LT, and have a major and independent impact on overall mortality.

articles.title: Dose-Related Effects of Chronic Dietary Fructose Consumption on Sperm Functional Quality, Chromatin Packaging, and Testicular Redox Homeostasis in C57BL/6 Mice.
articles.abstract: Chronic consumption of high-fructose diets has been associated with metabolic disturbances, but its effects on male reproductive function and testicular redox homeostasis remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the effects of chronic exposure to different concentrations of dietary fructose on sperm quality, chromatin integrity, oxidative status, metabolic parameters, and cognitive function in male C57BL/6 mice. Mice were randomly assigned to control, 10% fructose (F10%), or 30% fructose (F30%) groups and received the respective solutions in drinking water for 15 consecutive weeks. Body weight, fasting blood glucose, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), adiposity, testicular morphometry, sperm concentration, motility, morphology, chromatin maturity, DNA integrity, intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS), membrane lipid peroxidation, testicular malondialdehyde (MDA), total antioxidant capacity (TAC), fructose content, and spatial working memory were assessed. F30% exposure significantly increased body weight, adiposity, fasting blood glucose, and glycated hemoglobin (P < 0.05). Both F10% and F30% groups showed significantly reduced sperm concentration and progressive motility, increased morphological abnormalities, protamine deficiency, histone retention, DNA denaturation susceptibility, intracellular ROS, and membrane lipid peroxidation (P < 0.05). F30% further increased testicular MDA and fructose levels and decreased TAC (P < 0.05). Spontaneous alternation in the Y-maze was significantly reduced in both fructose groups, whereas exploratory activity decreased only in F30% mice (P < 0.05). Chronic fructose exposure adversely affects sperm function, chromatin integrity, and redox homeostasis even at 10%, while higher exposure intensifies reproductive, metabolic, testicular oxidative, and cognitive alterations.

articles.title: Enterococci as Emerging Pathogens in Infective Endocarditis and Cardiac Device Infections: Future Implications.
articles.abstract: Enterococci are emerging as important pathogens in an era of an aging population with high healthcare and antibiotic exposure, along with an increasing utilization of prosthetic valves, transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), and cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs). Contemporary cohorts place enterococci among the three leading causes of infective endocarditis, with highest risk after TAVR, where enterococci account for 15% to 30% of cases in several registries. Enterococci cause a smaller proportion of CIED infections, but present late with lead or valve involvement. Enterococcus faecalis currently causes majority of enterococcal endocarditis. Its endovascular tropism, adhesion to damaged tissue and prosthetic surfaces, biofilm tolerance, and association with occult infective endocarditis during bacteremia make it the principal cardiac species of concern. Enterococcus faecium represents a distinct future threat. Hospital-adapted lineages combine prolonged intestinal colonization, environmental persistence, mobile resistance elements, ampicillin resistance, frequent vancomycin resistance, and biofilm capacity. Absolute burden may rise because the population-at risk-living with cardiac foreign devices is expanding. Future monitoring therefore requires linked, species-level surveillance that connects bacteremia, imaging, recurrence, resistance, and genomic data.

articles.title: Molecular and functional characterization of interleukin-11b in large yellow croaker (Larimichthys crocea) during pathogen-induced immune responses.
articles.abstract: Interleukin-11 (IL-11) is an important cytokine involved in immune regulation in vertebrates. However, the specific functions of the IL-11b paralog in marine fish, particularly in mucosal responses to parasitic infection, remain poorly understood. In this study, an IL-11b homolog, named LcIL-11b, was identified from large yellow croaker (Larimichthys crocea), and its potential role in pathogen-induced immune responses was investigated. The open reading frame of Lcil-11b was 600 bp, encoding a protein of 199 amino acids with a predicted signal peptide and a conserved IL-11 domain. Multiple sequence alignment and phylogenetic analysis showed that LcIL-11b clustered with teleost IL-11b homologs and was distinct from the previously reported IL-11a homolog in large yellow croaker. Tissue distribution analysis showed that Lcil-11b was constitutively expressed in all examined tissues, with relatively high expression levels in the skin and gill. After Cryptocaryon irritans infection, Lcil-11b was significantly induced in mucosal and immune-related tissues, especially at 24 h post-challenge. In head kidney cell line from large yellow croaker (LYCK), inactivated Vibrio alginolyticus stimulation markedly increased Lcil-11b expression at 72 h. Transcriptome and WGCNA analyses further showed that Lcil-11b was located in an infection-responsive module associated with immune receptor signaling, phagocytosis, endocytosis, chemokine signaling, and epithelial responses. Functional assays showed that LcIL-11b overexpression increased SOD and GSH-Px activities, reduced MDA accumulation and apoptosis under bacterial stimulation, and was accompanied by increased transcript levels of jak1, stat3, and bcl2. These results suggest that LcIL-11b is a pathogen-responsive IL-11b homolog and may participate in immune responses and cellular protection in large yellow croaker.

articles.title: Segment and side specific determinants of carotid atherosclerotic burden: evidence for a distinct left internal carotid artery phenotype.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Carotid atherosclerosis is an important feature in patients with cerebrovascular events, but its determinants may vary across arterial segments and sides. We assessed segment- and side-specific determinants of carotid atherosclerotic burden.

METHODS: We studied 177 patients aged 18-65 years who were hospitalized with acute ischemic stroke or TIA and underwent carotid ultrasonography. Atherosclerotic involvement of bilateral common carotid arteries, carotid bifurcations and internal carotid arteries was assessed using a Burden of Disease (BoD) score. We examined segment-specific associations between BoD, stenosis severity and cardiovascular risk factors.

RESULTS: Plaques were more frequent at the carotid bifurcation and in the internal carotid artery than in the common carotid artery. After Bonferroni correction, age and hypertension were associated with BoD in the carotid bifurcation and internal carotid segments bilaterally; hypertension was also associated with left common carotid BoD (p = 0.003). BMI was associated with right bifurcation and internal carotid BoD (p = 0.007 and p = 0.005), Lp(a) >30 mg/dL with left internal carotid BoD (p = 0.002), and fibrinogen with left common carotid BoD (p = 0.005). The multivariable model for the left internal carotid artery explained the largest proportion of variance (R2 = 0.274), with contributions from hypertension (0.092), Lp(a) >30 mg/dL (0.084), BMI (0.036), fibrinogen (0.035) and atrial fibrillation (0.027). Associations with stenosis severity were less consistent (n = 16-54).

CONCLUSIONS: In this symptomatic cohort, carotid atherosclerotic burden showed segment- and side-specific associations with cardiovascular risk factors. The broader range of associations in the left internal carotid artery is hypothesis-generating and requires confirmation in larger prospective cohorts.

articles.title: Long-term outcomes in dalbavancin-treated patients with vascular graft infection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Data on dalbavancin use in vascular graft infections (VGI) are lacking. We aimed to report our experience of its efficacy and safety.

METHODS: This retrospective monocentric study included patients with VGI, according to MAGIC criteria, who received at least one dalbavancin dose between 01/2021 and 11/2024, followed for at least one year. One-year relapse-free survival and safety were assessed.

RESULTS: Seven patients with a median Charlson's score of 2 (IQR (Bouza et al., 2018; Seltzer et al., 2003; Frazier et al., 2023 [2-4])), median age of 62 years (IQR [61-73]), received a median of two (IQR (Molina et al., 2022; Bouza et al., 2018 [1,2])) dalbavancin injections. Before dalbavancin initiation, patients had received a median of four antibiotic regimens (IQR (Seltzer et al., 2003; Frazier et al., 2023; Turner et al., 2022; Hidalgo-Tenorio et al., 2023 [3-6])) and undergone one surgical procedure (IQR (Molina et al., 2022; Bouza et al., 2018 [1,2])). Partial graft replacement was performed in three patients (42.9%). At one year follow-up, all patients were alive, actively followed, without relapse or adverse event.

CONCLUSION: Dalbavancin showed promising outcomes in a limited subset of Gram-positive pathogen VGI patients.

articles.title: Early circulating cell-free mitochondrial deoxyribonucleic acid and mortality in adults with sepsis: A systematic review and Meta-analysis protocol.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess whether higher circulating cell-free mitochondrial deoxyribonucleic acid concentrations within the first 24 h are associated with higher all-cause mortality at 28-30 days in adults with sepsis.

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched on October 17, 2026. Eligible observational studies will assess early circulating concentrations and prognosis. At least two reviewers will independently select studies, extract data, and assess risk of bias using Quality In Prognosis Studies or the Joanna Briggs Institute analytical cross-sectional tool. Certainty will be assessed using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation. Meta-analysis will require at least three independent studies with compatible estimates for the same outcome. Inverse-variance random-effects models will use restricted maximum likelihood and modified Hartung-Knapp intervals. Association measures, discrimination, and concentration differences will be synthesized separately. When a cohort reports both mortality horizons, 28-day estimates will be preferred; 30-day-only estimates will remain eligible.

EXPECTED RESULTS: The review will characterize associations with mortality and organ dysfunction, discrimination, and additional prognostic information, accounting for baseline severity, clinical setting, and measurement conditions.

CONCLUSIONS: The synthesis will inform further evaluation of this biomarker for risk assessment in sepsis.

articles.title: Rituximab in IgA Nephropathy: The RITA Multicenter Randomized Trial.
articles.journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: B-cell dysregulation contributes to IgA nephropathy (IgAN). Rituximab (RTX) targets CD20-positive B cells, but its efficacy in adults with IgAN receiving stable renin-angiotensin system inhibitor (RASI) therapy remains uncertain. This study sought to evaluate the efficacy and safety of RTX combined with RASI therapy compared with RASI therapy alone.

STUDY DESIGN: Multicenter, randomized, controlled trial.

SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: Chinese adults with biopsy-proven IgAN across 10 centers, with 24-hour urine total protein (UTP) >1 g/day despite ≥3 months RASI therapy, and blood pressure <130/80 mmHg.

INTERVENTIONS: RTX plus RASI versus RASI alone for 12 months OUTCOMES: Primary: 24-hour UTP change at month 12. Secondary continuous: changes in 24-hour UTP at month 6 and in eGFR and serum Gd-IgA1 at month 12. Secondary categorical: ≥50% reduction in 24-hour UTP at months 6 and 12, ≥50% eGFR decline or doubling of serum creatinine, and ESKD.

SAFETY: adverse events, serious adverse events, and infections. Exploratory analyses examined outcomes through month 24.

RESULTS: Among the 106 participants randomized (53 per group), 24-hour UTP change at 12 months was similar between groups (adjusted GMR, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.80-1.36). Median change of 24-hour UTP was -0.21 g/day for RTX and -0.26 g/day for RASI. No statistically significant differences were observed in eGFR (adjusted mean difference, 3.80 mL/min/1.73 m2; 95% CI, -0.47 to 8.06), Gd-IgA1 (adjusted GMR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.87-1.24), or the proportion achieving a ≥50% reduction in 24-hour UTP (15.1% vs 20.8%). Adverse events occurred at similar rates between two groups; no events of ≥50% eGFR decline, doubling of serum creatinine, or ESKD occurred during the 12-month treatment period. These findings were consistent with analyses that included outcome data through month 24.

LIMITATIONS: The follow-up period was relatively short, and only Asian patients were enrolled.

CONCLUSIONS: No additional reduction in proteinuria or preservation of kidney function was observed with the addition of RTX to optimized RASI-based therapy in patients with IgAN.

FUNDING: Grants from government (National Key Research and Development Program, Major International [Regional] Joint Research Program of China, National Natural Science Foundation of China, National Facility for Translational Medicine [Shanghai], Shanghai 'Rising Stars of Medical Talent' Youth Development Program), academic (Shanghai Shenkang Hospital Development Center), and non-profit (International Society of Nephrology) sources.

articles.title: One-Year Comparative Outcomes of Direct Oral Anticoagulants Versus Warfarin In Patients With Left Ventricular Thrombus And High Bleeding Risks.
articles.abstract: Management of left ventricular (LV) thrombus in patients with high bleeding risk presents a therapeutic challenge. Warfarin has been the traditional anticoagulant used for left ventricular thrombus; direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are increasingly used as alternatives. We decided to study whether DOAC offered any advantage over Warfarin in this high-risk group of patients. Using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network, we identified adult patients with LV thrombus and high bleeding-risk conditions (such as prior bleeds, CKD stages 3-5, Peptic ulcer disease) between 2013 and 2023. Patients were stratified into two cohorts: DOAC (n=3,762, matched n=2,208) and Warfarin (n=2,542, matched n=2,208). Outcomes assessed over one year included stroke/transient ischemic attack (TIA), cerebral infarction, mortality, acute gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding, systemic arterial embolism, intracranial hemorrhage (ICH), major bleeding, embolic events, and all-cause hospitalization. Cox regression estimated hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI); p-value <0.05 was considered significant. The mean age was 66.8 ± 14.4 for patients on DOAC and 63.9 ± 15.0 for those on warfarin. After matching, baseline characteristics were well balanced between the two groups. At one year, DOAC use was associated with significantly lower risks of mortality (24.9% vs 29.3%, HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.75-0.94, p=0.003), systemic arterial embolism (1.9% vs 3.1%, HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.39-0.88, p=0.008), intracranial hemorrhage (1.3% vs 2.3%, HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.35-0.90, p=0.016) and all-cause hospitalization was slightly lower with DOACs (72.0% vs 75.5%, HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.83-0.96, p=0.001). No significant differences were observed for Stroke/TIA, cerebral infarction, or major bleeding. In conclusion, in this large propensity-matched cohort of patients with LV thrombus and high bleeding risk, use of DOACs demonstrated superior safety and effectiveness compared to warfarin, with reduced mortality, major bleeding, and thromboembolic complications. These findings support the use of DOACs in this high-risk population, though prospective randomized trials are warranted.

articles.title: Swallowing-Induced Ventricular Tachycardia: Mechanistic Inference and Patient Management Require Caution.
Neuromuscular Determinants of Strength Training Response in COPD: A Multilevel Approach to Understanding Non-Response After Pulmonary Rehabilitation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: COPD is associated with significant lower limb muscle weakness, a predictor of mortality. Pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) incorporating resistance exercises is a key intervention to counteract this impairment. However, 50% of patients fail to improve muscle strength, classifying them as non-responders (NR). To understand this variability, this study aimed to assess all components of the muscle strength production chain before and after PR, and to identify predictors of non-response.

METHODS: 33 COPD patients completed a 4-week inpatient PR program including standardized strength training following ACSM international guidelines. Quadriceps maximal voluntary isometric contraction (QMVIC), rate of force development (RFD), voluntary activation (VAcortical), corticospinal excitability (MEP/Mmax), and contractile properties were assessed before and after PR. Patients with a QMVIC increase < 7.5N·m were classified as NR. Logistic regression analysis was used to identify predictors of non-response.

RESULTS: On average, QMVIC improved (+5.4 N·m; p=0.02), but 60.6% of patients were NR (despite comparable training metrics). Baseline VA was similar between groups. Responders showed a significant increase in VAcortical (p=0.03), while NR exhibited no changes (p=0.78). Corticospinal excitability and peripheral muscle adaptations improved similarly in both groups. RFD was lower in NR both pre and post PR (p<0.01), and was identified as a key predictor of non-response (sensibility: 95%; specificity: 90%).

CONCLUSION: Both groups displayed comparable improvements in corticospinal excitability and peripheral muscle properties; however, only responders showed a significant increase in voluntary activation. Identifying RFD as a predictor of non-response provides a valuable tool for early patient stratification and personalized training strategies.

articles.title: Long term maintenance of patient defined goals following pulmonary rehabilitation in COPD: An observational study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) is a key treatment for patients with COPD. The main challenge in PR is maintaining benefits over the long term. The main objective of this observational study was to evaluate the proportion of patients who maintained at least half of their personal goals, as determined during the PR programme (PRP), at one year.

METHODS: Patients with COPD admitted to a PRP were prospectively included in this observational study. At the end of the PRP, patients were assessed using standard tools (exercise capacity, dyspnea, quality of life …) and developed a written plan for goal maintenance. Patients were then assessed at 6 and 12 months. The primary endpoint was maintenance of the goal(s) determined by the patient at 12 months. The secondary endpoints were the maintenance of the goal(s) at 6 months and the maintained benefits of the PRP at 12 months.

RESULTS: 221 patients were included and 214 analysed. Fifty one percent of the patients maintained at least half of their goals at 12 months and sixty four percent of the patients at 6 months. At 12 months, anxiety was not significantly altered, and the increases in dyspnea and depression, as well as the decrease in exercise capacity and quality of life, were significant but not clinically relevant (except quality of life).

CONCLUSION: after a PRP including a written plan for maintaining goals, half of the patients maintained at least half of their goals at 12 months, without experiencing a clinically relevant decline in PR benefits.

articles.title: Intraoperative desaturation: the anesthesiologist's routine, research's blind spot.
Effects of Lévy Jumps on the Dynamics of a Stochastic HIV Model.
articles.abstract: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) is a severe infectious disease that primarily targets CD4+ lymphocytes, weakens immune function, and increases susceptibility to opportunistic infections. Persistent HIV infection may eventually progress to Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS). In this study, we formulate and analyze a stochastic HIV/AIDS model incorporating Brownian perturbations and finite activity Lévy jumps to describe HIV transmission dynamics under random environmental fluctuations and abrupt epidemic shocks. First, the proposed stochastic system is shown to admit a unique global positive solution for biologically feasible initial conditions. To examine the dynamical behavior of the system, suitable Lyapunov functions are constructed and applied to establish extinction and persistence results for the model. We derive a sufficient condition for almost sure extinction of the HIV-positive classes, and show that when the stochastic threshold satisfies R0s>1 the proportion of aware HIV-positive individuals persists in the mean, with an explicit lower bound. Numerical simulations of the jump-diffusion model, with 100 independent replicates per scenario, support the theoretical findings; in particular, they exhibit noise-induced extinction in a regime where the deterministic model is endemic. A global sensitivity analysis (Latin hypercube sampling with partial rank correlation coefficients) identifies the transmission, education and progression rates as the parameters that most strongly influence R0s. Moreover, the results reveal that stochastic environmental perturbations significantly influence the spread of HIV. In particular, sufficiently large noise intensities may contribute to reducing disease transmission and suppressing epidemic outbreaks within the population.

articles.title: Heart Failure Fellowship Recruiting Is Not a Spectator Sport: Lessons We Learned at a Bootcamp for Potential Trainees.
Electrocardiogram-based artificial intelligence to predict incident heart failure with preserved versus reduced ejection fraction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure is classically divided into two subtypes based on the ejection fraction (EF): HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), each with varying risk mitigation strategies. Electrocardiogram-based artificial intelligence (AI) may facilitate HF subtype-specific risk prediction, to enable tailored prevention.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Based on a previously validated HF prediction architecture, we developed an ECG-based AI model to predict 10-year risk of incident HFrEF (LVEF <50%) versus HFpEF (LVEF ≥50%) (Electrocardiogram to Heart Failure Subtype, "ECG2HF-Subtype"). ECG2HF-Subtype was developed in 98,190 individuals in Massachusetts General Hospital (MGH), and validated in three test sets: MGH, Brigham and Women's Hospital (BWH), and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (BIDMC), among individuals without prior HF. HF was identified using a validated natural language processing model, and subtypes were classified by LVEF proximate to incident HF. Discrimination was quantified using time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and average precision (AP), with comparisons to age and sex, and a multinomial logistic regression classifier including PREVENT-HF variables. In aggregate, models were evaluated in MGH (n=16,739, age 56±17, 54% women), BWH (n=75,195, 56±16, 59%) and BIDMC (n=30,133, 56±17, 54%). ECG2HF-Subtype consistently discriminated incident HFrEF (MGH 10-year AUROC 0.89 [0.86-0.91], 10-year AP: 0.11 [95%CI 0.09-0.15], cumulative incidence 1.73%; BWH: 0.88 [0.87-0.89], 0.13 [0.11-0.14], 2.23% BIDMC: 0.88 [0.86-0.89], 0.14 [0.12-0.17], 2.19%) and HFpEF events (MGH 10-year AUROC 0.83 [0.81-0.85], 10-year AP: 0.10 [95% CI 0.09-0.13], cumulative incidence 3.17%; BWH: 0.79 [0.77-0.80], 0.06 [0.06-0.07], 2.75%), BIDMC: 0.81 [0.80-0.82], 0.10 [0.09-0.12], 3.49%), with consistently greater AUROC versus age and sex. When compared to PREVENT-HF variables, ECG2HF-Subtypes had favorable discrimination of HFrEF (e.g., 10-year AUROC in MGH+BWH 0.86 [0.84-0.88] vs. 0.78 [0.76-0.80]), and modestly lower for HFpEF (10-year AUROC in MGH+BWH 0.78 [0.76-0.80] vs. 0.81 [0.79-0.82]).

CONCLUSIONS: By predicting risk of HFpEF and HFrEF, AI-enabled ECG analysis may enable targeted prevention to reduce HF-related morbidity.

articles.title: Relationship between Prior Bisphosphonate Usage and Foot and Ankle Surgeries in Charcot Foot: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: The Journal of foot and ankle surgery : official publication of the American College of Foot and Ankle Surgeons
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Charcot neuroarthropathy of the foot (CF) is a condition characterized by joint instability and inflammation most commonly seen in patients with uncontrolled diabetes and peripheral neuropathy. Previous research has investigated the use of bisphosphonates against CF, but these studies employed small sample sizes.

PURPOSE: This study aims to identify whether bisphosphonate usage prior to CF diagnosis is associated with different surgery rates compared to non-usage. We hypothesize that prior bisphosphonate usage is associated with fewer lower extremity surgeries compared to non-usage in CF patients.

STUDY DESIGN: Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study METHODS: This study used TriNetX de-identified health records from 64 healthcare organizations and compared patients in two cohorts: CF with and without bisphosphonate treatment approximately six months before diagnosis. Propensity score matching (PSM) accounted for confounding variables. Patient risk ratios, p-values, and 95% confidence intervals were calculated for outcomes at 6 months and 5 years after CF diagnosis. PSM yielded a sample size of 1,409 patients for the 6-month interval and 1,435 patients for the 5-year interval.

RESULTS: Six months after CF diagnosis, patients in the bisphosphonates group had lower rates of arthrodesis and other osseous/soft-tissue surgical procedures compared to CF patients without bisphosphonate treatment. Patients taking bisphosphonates had fewer lower extremity amputation, arthrodesis, and additional osseous/soft-tissue surgical procedures at 5 years.

CONCLUSION: These data suggest that CF patients with prior bisphosphonate use require fewer lower extremity surgeries. These data would be relevant to foot specialists and researchers interested in new possibilities to improve outcomes in CF patients.

articles.title: Extended Clopidogrel Monotherapy versus Dual Antiplatelet Therapy in Acute Coronary Syndrome Patients With and Without Heart Failure: A Prespecified Subgroup Analysis of the OPT-BIRISK Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal extended antiplatelet strategy after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) in patients with heart failure (HF) remains uncertain.

METHODS: In OPT-BIRISK, patients at high ischemic and bleeding risk who completed 9-12 months of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) were randomized to clopidogrel plus placebo or aspirin for 9 months. This analysis compared treatments by recorded HF history. The primary endpoint was Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) types 2, 3, or 5 bleeding; the key secondary endpoint was major adverse cardiac and cerebral events (MACCE).

RESULTS: Of 7,758 patients, 653 (8.4%) had HF history. Without HF, bleeding occurred in 83/3,565 (2.3%) monotherapy recipients and 118/3,540 (3.3%) DAPT recipients (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.53-0.92). With HF, bleeding occurred in 12/308 (3.9%) and 9/345 (2.6%), respectively (HR 1.49, 95% CI 0.63-3.53). MACCE occurred in 90/3,565 (2.5%) versus 120/3,540 (3.4%) patients without HF (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.57-0.98) and 11/308 (3.6%) versus 16/345 (4.6%) patients with HF (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.36-1.66). Interaction P values were 0.1021 for bleeding and 0.9345 for MACCE.

CONCLUSIONS: Extended clopidogrel monotherapy reduced clinically relevant bleeding in patients without a history of HF after PCI for ACS. No statistically significant treatment-by-HF interaction was observed for bleeding or MACCE, although HF-specific treatment effects remain inconclusive because of limited events.

articles.title: Survival Is Not Necessarily Success: The Fontan Paradox.
Phylogenomics reveals putative primarily free-living Parabasalia (Eukaryota: Metamonada) and multiple lifestyle transitions within an important phylum.
articles.abstract: Parabasalia is a diverse group of anaerobic flagellates, containing parasites, commensals, mutualists (e.g., termite symbionts), and free-living species. The best-known representative is Trichomonas vaginalis, which causes a sexually transmitted infection in humans. Despite their importance, the phylogenetic placement of free-living lineages as well as the internal phylogeny of Parabasalia have remained unclear. We sequenced transcriptomes from 17 parabasalian isolates, including eight that are free-living. This nearly doubled the group's genome-scale taxon sampling. State-of-the-art phylogenomic analyses yielded a robustly resolved tree, which is supplemented by a complementary four-gene analysis with broader taxon sampling that shows no conflict with the phylogenomic tree. Three major clades within Parabasalia were recovered, which we consider subphyla: Trichomonada, Tritrichomonada, and Pimpavickaa. While all Tritrichomonada species are endobiotic, several Trichomonada lineages are free-living. The separation between Trichomonada + Tritrichomonada and Pimpavickaa, which includes two exclusively free-living species - Pimpavicka limacoides and Alexandriella bishopae - is the split closest to the root of Parabasalia. Light and transmission electron microscopy confirms that Alexandriella exhibits canonical parabasalian morphology. The tree topology indicates either several reversals to free-living lifestyle within trichomonads or multiple independent origins of endobiotic lifestyle within Parabasalia, highlighting this group's evolutionary plasticity. Putative homologs of BspA- and Pmp-like surface proteins (implicated as Parabasalia virulence factors) are present in pimpavickids, implying their later repurposing for endobiotic and parasitic lifestyles. Analyses of some glycoside hydrolase family proteins suggest their role in the evolutionary ability of parabasalian lineages to switch between lifestyles. A moderate taxonomic revision of Parabasalia is provided.

articles.title: Observation of the therapeutic effect of handheld induction therapy combined with electromyographic biofeedback on post-stroke dysphagia.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical efficacy of handheld induction therapy combined with electromyographic (EMG) biofeedback for post-stroke dysphagia in a real-world setting.

METHODS: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 105 patients with post-stroke dysphagia were enrolled; after multinomial propensity score (GPS) estimation with common support trimming, 96 patients (32 per group) were included in the final analysis: Group A (conventional treatment), Group B (conventional treatment + EMG biofeedback), and Group C (conventional treatment + EMG biofeedback + handheld induction therapy). The efficacy was assessed after 4 weeks by comparing videofluoroscopic swallowing study (VFSS) scores, Modified Mann Assessment of Swallowing Ability (MASA) scores, Functional Oral Intake Scale (FOIS) scores, and overall effective rates among the three groups.

RESULTS: After treatment, Group C had significantly higher VFSS oral-phase, pharyngeal-phase, and aspiration scores than Groups A and B (all P < 0.001), as well as higher MASA scores (85.37 ± 6.54 vs. 73.25 ± 6.24 and 73.31 ± 6.31, respectively; all P < 0.001), and FOIS scores (6.05 ± 0.35 vs. 5.14 ± 0.28 and 5.09 ± 0.31, respectively; all P < 0.001). The total effective rate was highest in Group C (96.88%, 31/32), followed by Group B (84.38%, 27/32) and Group A (71.88%, 23/32), with a significant difference among the three groups (P = 0.025). Adverse reactions did not differ significantly (P = 0.440).

CONCLUSION: Handheld induction therapy combined with EMG biofeedback may effectively improve swallowing function and clinical efficacy in post-stroke dysphagia, with favorable safety; further prospective studies are warranted.

articles.title: Phase 3 clinical development of semaglutide (2015-2026): a comprehensive evidence-based review of trial designs, therapeutic outcomes and global clinical experience.
articles.abstract: Semaglutide, a long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA), has become an important therapeutic agent for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), obesity, and associated cardiometabolic complications. Its prolonged pharmacological activity and availability as subcutaneous and oral formulations have supported extensive clinical development across diverse populations. This review critically evaluates Phase 3, Phase 3a, and Phase 3b clinical trials (CTs) assessing the efficacy, safety and therapeutic utility of semaglutide, with an emphasis on the SUSTAIN, PIONEER, STEP, SELECT, FLOW, SOUL and related programmes. Eligible trials were assessed according to study design, registration, treatment duration, population characteristics, interventions, comparators, primary endpoints, adverse events (AEs) and clinical significance. Collectively, the evidence demonstrates clinically meaningful improvements in glycaemic control and body weight, as well as cardiovascular and renal benefits, in selected populations. Evidence from obesity and post-bariatric studies further supports its expanding therapeutic role beyond conventional glucose management. Gastrointestinal events, particularly nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation, were the predominant adverse effects, while overall tolerability remained consistent with the established GLP-1RA profile. However, differences in populations, treatment duration, comparators and endpoint definitions highlight important evidence gaps. This review synthesises Phase 3 clinical evidence to define the evolving therapeutic position, safety profile and future research priorities for semaglutide.

articles.title: Effectiveness of various balanced electrolyte solutions in the resuscitation of patients with diabetic ketoacidosis: A pairwise meta-analysis and network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: In diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), choice of resuscitative fluid is debated, and superiority of balanced electrolyte solutions (BES) over each other remains unevaluated. This meta-analysis compared the effectiveness of BES with normal saline (NS) (18 studies), while network meta-analysis evaluated various BES (16 studies). PubMed, Cochrane Library, and EMBASE were searched from inception till April 28, 2025. Compared to NS, BES was associated with significantly shorter time to DKA resolution (MD = -4.41 h; 95 %CI = -7.00, -1.82), shorter length of hospital stay (LHS, MD = -0.43 days; 95 %CI = -0.72, -0.14), higher postresuscitation bicarbonate levels (PBL, MD = 1.20 mmol/L; 95 %CI = 0.48,1.92), and lower postresuscitation chloride levels (PCL, MD = -3.31 mmol/L; 95 %CI = -5.32, -1.29), though time to DKA resolution, PBL, and PCL had significant heterogeneity. Compared to NS, Sterofundin (MD = -4.30 h; 95 %CI = -6.14, -2.46; p < 0.0001) and RL (MD = -2.60 h; 95 %CI = -4.13, -1.07; p = 0.0009) had significantly shorter time to DKA resolution. Similarly, LHS was significantly shorter with Sterofundin (MD = -0.67 days; 95 %CI = -1.15, -0.19; p = 0.0066). PBL increased significantly with Plasmalyte (PL, MD = 2.16 mmol/L; 95 %CI = 1.12,3.20; p < 0.0001), and Ringer's lactate (RL, MD = 1.24 mmol/L; 95 %CI = 0.75,1.73; p < 0.0001), while PCL reduced significantly with RL (MD = -6.22 mmol/L; 95 %CI = -6.69, -5.76; p < 0.0001), Sterofundin (MD = -3.60 mmol/L; 95 %CI = -5.10, -2.10; p < 0.0001), and PL (MD = -3.16 mmol/L; 95 %CI = -4.58, -1.73; p < 0.0001). Rate of hyperkalemia (OR = 4.06; 95 %CI = 1.17,14.15) and acute kidney injury (OR = 2.26; 95 %CI = 1.00,5.08) was significantly higher with RL compared to NS. Thus, compared to NS, BES improved PBL and PCL, with faster time to DKA resolution and shorter LHS, but did not consistently improve adverse clinical outcomes. Comparison among BESs is indirect and hypothesis-generating; thus, direct head-to-head trials using patient-related outcomes are required in future trials.

articles.title: Response to comments on "Profile, Predictors, and Outcomes of Multidrug-Resistant Neonatal Sepsis: Insights from a Level III NICU in Kolkata, Eastern India".
Persistent leukopenia masks hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome.
articles.abstract: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) typically comes with fever, facial flushing, rash, thrombocytopenia, acute kidney injury, coagulopathy and leukocytosis. However, atypical manifestations may obscure diagnosis. A 30-year-old man with rodent exposure had high fever, thrombocytopenia, and persistent leukopenia, without overt renal dysfunction despite mild renal involvement in the form of proteinuria.
