Hantaan virus was confirmed by serology and RT-PCR. The patient recovered following ribavirin and supportive management. This case highlights that in HFRS-endemic regions, hantavirus infection should be suspected among patients with unexplained fever, thrombocytopenia, and persistent leukopenia rather than the typical leukocytosis, even without overt renal dysfunction.

articles.title: Cognitive leisure activity and incident dementia among older adults with diabetes: a 5-year prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Exercise and physical activity are modifiable lifestyle factors for cognitive health, but whether cognitive leisure activity is also associated with dementia among older adults with diabetes is unclear. We examined its association with dementia incidence.

METHODS: This 5-year prospective cohort included 779 adults aged ≥65 years with diabetes. Cognitive leisure activity was assessed using the cognitive activity scale and classified as lower (0-7 points) or higher (8-42 points). Incident dementia was identified from health and long-term care insurance records. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), adjusting for relevant baseline factors; a further model also adjusted for moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA). Sensitivity analyses used Fine-Gray models with death as a competing event.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 5.0 years (IQR, 5.0-5.0), 112 participants developed dementia. After multivariable adjustment, higher cognitive leisure activity was associated with a lower hazard of incident dementia (HR, 0.615; 95% CI, 0.414-0.913). After additional adjustment for MVPA, the association remained similar (HR, 0.624; 95% CI, 0.419-0.929). Findings were similar when cognitive leisure activity was modeled continuously. In competing-risk analyses, the subdistribution HR was 0.667 (95% CI, 0.455-0.977) after additional adjustment for MVPA.

CONCLUSION: Among older adults with diabetes, higher cognitive leisure activity was associated with lower 5-year dementia risk after accounting for baseline cognitive function, cardiometabolic factors, and measured physical activity, including walking in sensitivity analyses. Cognitive leisure activity may complement other lifestyle factors supporting cognitive health in this population.

articles.title: Information, Mass, Energy Principles: A biophysical and ecological framework for understanding the brain.
articles.abstract: The brain is a highly complex biological system whose structure, function, and evolution are constrained by material resources and energy availability, as any other natural system. Here, we extend the ecological Information-Mass-Energy (IME) framework (Peñuelas, 2024) to neuroscience. In contrast to purely computational models, we propose that the brain is an information-organizing system constrained by mass availability, energetic expenditure, and thermodynamic efficiency. Through comparative analyses across mammalian species, we identify a superlinear scaling relationship between white and grey matter volumes, alongside a positive association between white matter volume and inhibitory-control performance. This suggests that neural organization contribute to cognitive capacities beyond brain size alone. Integrating these findings with metabolic scaling principles, we propose that brain evolution involves trade-offs between increasing informational complexity and the material and energetic costs required to sustain it. Within this framework, we formulate testable hypotheses concerning how informational organization may scale with neural material and energetic expenditure. Furthermore, we introduce a quantitative disturbance-recovery model that incorporates carrying capacity, recovery rate, and disturbance magnitude and duration, generating testable predictions for neurological conditions such as stroke and neurodegeneration. By combining empirical scaling relationships with a mathematical framework for neural organization, energetic constraints, and resilience, the IME framework offers a novel biophysical and ecological perspective on brain evolution and function. This framework also provides a foundation for investigating energetically sustainable information processing in biological and artificial systems.

articles.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic technologies in cardiovascular development: Implications for congenital heart disease and regenerative medicine.
articles.abstract: Cardiac development constitutes a highly coordinated spatiotemporal process involving the precise regulation of numerous key genes and signaling pathways at specific anatomical sites and developmental stages. How distinct embryonic lineages coordinate with complex spatiotemporal microenvironments through cell fate transitions and the remodeling of developmental niches to regulate cardiac chamber specification, conduction system development, valvulogenesis, and vascular formation remains a fundamental question in understanding cardiovascular development. Elucidating these processes in greater depth is essential for understanding the mechanisms underlying congenital heart disease (CHD) and for advancing cardiac regenerative research. In recent years, advances in single-cell and spatial transcriptomic technologies have overcome traditional research bottlenecks, providing novel perspectives for elucidating cardiovascular cell heterogeneity, lineage relationships, developmental trajectories, and cell-cell interactions. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in the application of single-cell and spatial transcriptomic technologies in cardiovascular development research, focusing on the developmental characteristics of three major tissue compartments, namely the myocardium, endocardium, and epicardium, and further outlines their applications in elucidating the mechanisms of CHD and in the field of cardiac regeneration. In the future, the deep integration of single-cell and spatial transcriptomic technologies with lineage tracing and functional genomics is expected to further elucidate the regulatory mechanisms of cardiovascular development and advance precision diagnostics and regenerative therapeutic strategies for these diseases.

articles.title: Medical Complications of Catatonia and Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Journal of the Academy of Consultation-Liaison Psychiatry
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catatonia and neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) are related neuropsychiatric conditions linked to diverse and potentially life-threatening medical complications; however, no large-scale review of existing literature has described the types and rates of such complications.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to systematically examine documented medical complications associated with catatonia/NMS, delineate their clinical implications, and inform strategies for monitoring and improving patient outcomes.

METHODS: Systematic searches of PubMed and Web of Science were conducted up to February 8, 2025 for articles including patients with catatonia or NMS who experienced medical complications. Reviewers independently performed screening and data extraction. Quality assessment was completed via the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Case data were analyzed using descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: 281 articles (11 observational studies and 270 case reports/series) met inclusion criteria. Eleven observational studies examined medical complications in 2,008 patients with catatonia/NMS; study quality was low in 1, moderate in 6, and high in 4. Across studies, pneumonia occurred in 0-64% of patients, rhabdomyolysis in 0-30%, and deep vein thrombosis/pulmonary embolus (DVT/PE) in 0-25%, with these complications reported in both malignant and non-malignant presentations. Comparative studies identified catatonia as a significant risk factor for specific complications including DVT and rhabdomyolysis. Case reports/series (364 patients; mean age 45.7 years) demonstrated widespread complications including rhabdomyolysis (n=178), renal dysfunction (n=105), respiratory dysfunction (n=78), respiratory infections (n=47), aspiration (n=36), pulmonary emboli and infarcts (n=43), cardiac dysfunction (n=37), and malnutrition (n=63). Overall 23.9% (n=87) of case-reported patients experiencing medical complications from catatonia/NMS died. Within this case-report sample, mortality rates appeared lower among those receiving benzodiazepines (n=26, 16.9% vs n=61, 29.1%) and electroconvulsive therapy (n=6, 7.3% vs. n=81, 28.7) compared to those not receiving such interventions.

CONCLUSIONS: Catatonia/NMS carries high risks for multisystem complications and mortality, including in non-malignant cases and younger patients. Rhabdomyolysis, renal injury, respiratory compromise, and thromboembolism were particularly common. Among case reported patients, numerically lower mortality rates were seen in those who received benzodiazepines or electroconvulsive therapy. Clinicians should recognize strategies that may reduce risk for certain medical complications.

articles.title: Plasma proteomic profiling reveals mediating proteins and preventive targets linking ambient air pollution to type 2 diabetes incidence: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Ambient air pollution has been associated with type 2 diabetes (T2D), but the underlying biological mechanisms remain poorly understood. We included 44,917 participants with 2,911 plasma proteins from a large prospective cohort and followed them for incident T2D. Long-term PM2.5, NO2, NOx, and SO2 exposures were estimated via bilinear interpolation. Cox regressions assessed air pollutant-T2D associations. Elastic net regression identified air pollution-associated proteins and constructed a protein score. Mediation analyses identified top-mediating proteins. Functional and PPI analyses identified hub proteins. Druggability was screened using two drug databases, with binding potential evaluated by molecular docking across seven small-molecule databases. During 13.64 years of follow-up, 3,193 incident T2D cases occurred. Per IQR increase in PM2.5, NO2, NOx, and SO2 was associated with 5%-14% higher T2D risk. We identified 187 proteins mediating the PM2.5-T2D association, 61 for NO2, 66 for NOx, and 14 for SO2. The protein score mediated 31.69% (PM2.5), 18.06% (NO2), 16.81% (NOx), and 19.71% (SO2) of the associations. Functional and PPI analyses revealed these proteins function through cytokine-cytokine receptor interactions, chemokine signaling, leukocyte migration, and inflammation-related pathways. We further identified 13 targeted proteins with approved drugs (4 in DrugBank, 4 in Therapeutic Target Database). Molecular docking indicated 5 have potential small-molecule binders. This study identified potential biological pathways and candidate mediators linking air pollution to T2D, particularly through inflammatory and immune-related pathways mediated by plasma proteins, and identified potential intervention targets, offering opportunities for drug repurposing and precise prevention.

articles.title: Statin Use and Age-related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Disease Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
TOPIC: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between statin use and the prevalence, incidence, and progression of age-related macular degeneration (AMD).

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: AMD is a major cause of vision loss in older adults, many of whom receive statins for cardiovascular prevention.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library through October 2025 for randomized trials and cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies with comparators. We assessed risk of bias with tools appropriate to each design and pooled effect measures separately using random-effects models. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO.

RESULTS: Twenty-eight studies included 1,918,120 participants. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) for the prevalence of any, early, and late AMD were 1.03 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.86-1.24), 1.10 (95% CI, 0.92-1.31), and 0.75 (95% CI, 0.46-1.25), respectively. For incidence of any AMD, the pooled hazard ratio (HR) was 1.04 (95% CI, 0.82-1.31) and the OR was 0.76 (95% CI, 0.43-1.34), with substantial heterogeneity. For neovascular AMD incidence, different study subsets suggested lower hazard (HR, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.60-0.85) and higher risk (risk ratio, 1.31; 95% CI, 1.18-1.44); the OR was inconclusive (0.93; 95% CI, 0.82-1.05). Progression evidence was limited and heterogeneous. Ten of 12 longitudinal nonrandomized studies had serious overall risk of bias.

CONCLUSION: The evidence was of very low certainty and insufficient to establish a protective or harmful effect of statins on AMD. These findings do not support prescribing statins specifically for AMD or discontinuing otherwise indicated therapy.

articles.title: Clinicopathologic characteristics of gastric adenocarcinoma in autoimmune gastritis: Impact of Helicobacter pylori infection and diagnostic implications of multifocal disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autoimmune gastritis (AIG)-associated gastric adenocarcinoma (GC) and the impact of Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) remain incompletely characterized, particularly regarding synchronous multifocal disease.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 826 AIG patients from two centers and identified 93 with GC. Clinicopathological features and H. pylori association were analyzed. Five patients with synchronous multifocal adenocarcinoma (11 lesions) underwent detailed immunophenotypic and molecular profiling.

RESULTS: GC occurred in 11.26% of AIG patients. Tumors predominated in the gastric body (69.7%), were well-differentiated tubular adenocarcinomas (74.7%), and early-stage (90.5%). H. pylori infection was significantly more frequent in GC patients (16.1% vs. 5.2%; OR 3.52, 95% CI 1.88-6.70; P < 0.001). The neoplastic spectrum included multifocal intragastric carcinoma (5 cases), an AFP-producing carcinoma, fundic gland adenocarcinoma, and pyloric gland adenoma with intramucosal carcinoma. The five multifocal cases showed severe corpus atrophy; all 11 lesions were small (median 0.8 cm), flat, differentiated adenocarcinomas confined to mucosa/submucosa. Marked inter-lesional immunophenotypic heterogeneity (MUC2, MUC5AC, MUC6, p53) was observed. One of these cases showed a dMMR phenotype with MLH1/PMS2 loss across all three lesions. No recurrence occurred at median follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: AIG-associated GC shows distinctive body-predominant, well-differentiated, early-stage features. H. pylori infection is associated with a 3.5-fold increased GC risk in this cohort. Multifocal lesions display inter-lesional immunophenotypic heterogeneity consistent with field-related tumorigenesis. The finding of dMMR raises the differential diagnosis of Lynch syndrome and should prompt consideration of germline evaluation.

articles.title: Assessing radiology recommendations on neuroimaging reports for patients with idiopathic intracranial hypertension.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of ophthalmology. Journal canadien d'ophtalmologie
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterise the frequency and nature of radiologists' recommendations in magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography reports for patients with papilledema attributable to idiopathic intracranial hypertension.

DESIGN: Retrospective chart review.

PARTICIPANTS: In total, 146 consecutive patients with papilledema secondary to idiopathic intracranial hypertension were included. They were all ≥18 years of age with optic disc edema and preserved visual function or a visual field defect consistent with papilledema and underwent structural neuroimaging.

METHODS: Electronic medical records were assessed for clinical and imaging characteristics.

RESULTS: In total, 146 patients (131 female and 15 male) were analysed. The mean age was 32.9 ± 10.8 years. Recommendations were provided in 33 reports (22.6%). Lumbar puncture (LP) was the most common recommendation (72.7%), followed by additional imaging (15.2%), and referral to other providers (9%). Of the 67 radiologists who contributed to the 146 reports, 11 (16.4%) recommended LP in at least 1 of their reports. Incidental findings were characterised in 15 (10.3%) reports.

CONCLUSIONS: In this study, radiologists provided recommendations in 22.6% of radiology reports, with LP being the most frequent recommendation. Future studies evaluating the appropriateness and impact of such recommendations are warranted.

articles.title: Cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor in acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (DAPT-SHOCK-AMI): a randomised, double-blind trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) can compromise the administration and absorption of oral P2Y12 inhibitors and carries high ischaemic and mortality risks. This trial assessed whether intravenous cangrelor was non-inferior to crushed oral ticagrelor for short-term clinical outcomes and whether it provided faster and more consistent platelet inhibition in patients with AMI-CS.

METHODS: DAPT-SHOCK-AMI was a double-blind trial conducted at 29 hospitals across five European countries (Czech Republic, France, Germany, Poland, and Slovakia). Patients older than 18 years with AMI-CS were randomly assigned (1:1 ratio, stratified by centre, age, sex, presence or absence of ST-segment elevation, and mechanical ventilation) to cangrelor (30 μg/kg bolus followed by an infusion of 4 μg/kg per min for at least 2 h) or crushed ticagrelor (180 mg loading dose). The primary laboratory endpoint was a platelet reactivity index of less than 50% at the end of primary percutaneous coronary intervention. The primary clinical endpoint was death, myocardial infarction, or ischaemic stroke at 30 days. The primary clinical endpoint was analysed for non-inferiority with a prespecified margin of 1 percentage point among all randomly assigned patients who received study treatment. The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03551964) and EudraCT (2018-002161-19); recruitment and 1-year follow-up are complete, and 5-year follow-up is ongoing.

FINDINGS: Between Aug 1, 2018, and Jan 19, 2024, 605 patients (137 [23%] were female) were randomly assigned to cangrelor (n=298) or ticagrelor (n=307); no surviving patients were lost to the 1-year follow-up. The primary laboratory endpoint was analysed in 56 (19%) patients in the cangrelor group and 68 (22%) in the ticagrelor group, and was achieved in 56 (100%) of 56 patients receiving cangrelor and 15 (22%) of 68 receiving ticagrelor (p<0·0001). The 30-day primary clinical endpoint occurred in 112 (38%) of 298 patients receiving cangrelor and 126 (41%) of 307 receiving ticagrelor; non-inferiority was not demonstrated (difference -4 percentage points [90% CI -10 to 3]; Pnon-inferiority=0·13). Major bleeding at 30 days occurred in 19 (6%) of 298 patients receiving cangrelor and 16 (5%) of 307 receiving ticagrelor.

INTERPRETATION: To our knowledge, this is the first randomised trial to compare P2Y12 inhibitor strategies specifically in patients with AMI-CS. Cangrelor achieved effective platelet inhibition more frequently than crushed ticagrelor at the end of primary percutaneous coronary intervention. Non-inferiority of cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor was not demonstrated for the primary 30-day clinical endpoint. These trial findings can inform future trials of P2Y12 inhibition strategies in patients with AMI-CS.

FUNDING: Czech Republic Ministry of Health, Charles University (Czech Republic), and NextGenerationEU.

articles.title: Amrecibart and cenvacibart for the prevention of catheter-related thrombosis (ROXI-CATH): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs) are often complicated by venous thromboembolism, yet no thromboprophylaxis is approved. Factor XI (FXI) inhibition might prevent catheter-associated venous thromboembolism without increasing bleeding. We evaluated the safety and efficacy of amrecibart and cenvacibart for preventing venous thromboembolism after PICC placement.

METHODS: ROXI-CATH is a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial conducted across 12 hospital centres in Bulgaria, Canada, Israel, Romania, the UK, and the USA. Eligible participants aged 18 years or older undergoing PICC insertion, with the PICC expected to remain for at least 14 days, and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 2 or less were randomly assigned (1:1:1) using a permuted block design and stratified by site and diagnosis of active cancer to receive a single intravenous infusion of amrecibart (300 mg; anti-FXI A2 domain monoclonal antibody), cenvacibart (250 mg; anti-FXI catalytic domain monoclonal antibody), or placebo. Participants, principal investigators, and study site staff were masked to treatment assignment. The primary efficacy outcome was adjudicated venous thromboembolism (symptomatic or asymptomatic PICC-associated deep vein thrombosis or superficial vein thrombosis, or pulmonary embolism, including pulmonary embolism-related death) up to day 14. Ultrasounds were performed on days 7 and 14. The key secondary efficacy outcome was adjudicated thrombosis detected by ultrasound in the upper extremity with the PICC up to day 14. The primary safety outcome was site-reported treatment-emergent adverse events up to the end of the study. The key secondary safety outcomes were adjudicated major and clinically relevant non-major (CRNM) bleeding up to day 14. Efficacy analyses were performed in the full analysis set, which consisted of all randomly assigned participants who received any study drug and with any evaluable post-baseline ultrasound or a confirmed episode of venous thromboembolism. Safety analyses were performed in the safety analysis set, which included all randomly assigned participants who received any study drug (as treated). This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06299111 (completed; these analyses were performed after database lock on May 6, 2026).

FINDINGS: Between Sept 20, 2024, and Dec 19, 2025, 240 participants were screened, and 195 were randomly assigned to amrecibart (n=65), cenvacibart (n=66), or placebo (n=64). One participant in the placebo group who did not receive study treatment and had no evaluable ultrasound was excluded from the full analysis set. The median follow-up time was 100 days (IQR 100-103). The median age was 60 years (49-69), and 89 (46%) of 194 participants were female, 105 (54%) were male, and 192 (99%) were White. Adjudicated venous thromboembolism up to day 14 occured in 13 (20%) of 65 participants in the amrecibart group (odds ratio [OR] 0·37 [90% credible interval 0·18-0·65]), 13 (20%) of 66 participants in the cenvacibart group (0·36 [0·17-0·64]) compared with 27 (43%) of 63 participants in the placebo group. Adjudicated PICC-associated venous thromboembolism up to day 14 occurred in 12 (18%) participants in the amrecibart group (OR 0·30 [95% CI 0·14-0·67]), 13 (20%) participants in the cenvacibart group (0·32 [0·14-0·69]), compared with 27 (43%) participants in the placebo group. Site-reported treatment-emergent adverse events up to day 100 occurred in 45 (69%) participants in the amrecibart group, 42 (64%) participants in the cenvacibart group, and 48 (76%) participants in the placebo group. No participants had major bleeding up to day 14. CRNM bleeding up to day 14 occurred in two (3%) participants in the amrecibart group, two (3%) in the cenvacibart group, and two (3%) in the placebo group. Serious adverse events occurred in nine (14%) participants in the ambrecibart group, six (9%) in the cenvacibart group, and ten (16%) in the placebo group. One (2%) participant in the amrecibart group, four (6%) participants in the cenvacibart group, and two (3%) participants in the placebo group died; these deaths were assessed as not related to treatment by the respective investigators.

INTERPRETATION: A single infusion of amrecibart or cenvacibart reduced the incidence of venous thromboembolism following PICC insertion, suggesting FXI inhibition at the A2 or catalytic domain as a promising prophylactic strategy for contact-mediated thrombosis.

FUNDING: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of anti-tau drugs for Alzheimer's disease: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.journal: The journal of prevention of Alzheimer's disease
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate and compare the effects of different anti-tau drugs on clinical and biological outcomes in patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD).

METHODS: PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Embase databases were searched for identifying randomized, controlled clinical trials from inception to December 2025.

RESULTS: Twelve high-quality studies with 11 drugs were evaluated. Systematic meta-analysis did not demonstrate significant efficacy of anti-tau drugs in preventing cognitive and functional declines or clearance of tau deposition on PET. However, effects in reducing levels of p-tau (SMD=-0.48, 95% CI: -0.73 to -0.22, P < 0.01) and t-tau (SMD=-0.69, 95% CI: -0.94 to -0.45, P < 0.01) in the cerebrospinal fluid were observed. Network analysis revealed that MAPTRx and nicotinamide ranked highest for improving cognitive function, and gosuranemab ranked highest for tau biomarker changes.

CONCLUSION: The current findings highlight the disease-modifying potential of anti-tau therapies for AD, although clinical benefit is limited. The observed reductions in CSF tau biomarkers and the favourable safety profile of current anti-tau therapies suggest promising therapeutic potential for the treatment of AD. However, the clinical value of anti-tau therapies should be confirmed in adequately powered phase III trials with biomarker-enriched populations.

articles.title: Prevalence and prognostic significance of respiratory failure before or at liver transplantation in acute-on-chronic liver failure: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Respiratory failure (RF) is an important organ failure phenotype in acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF), but its prevalence and prognostic significance among liver transplant (LT) recipients remain uncertain. We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Web of Science Core Collection for observational studies through August 17, 2026. Of 33 included study reports, clinically comparable data were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis; other evidence was synthesized narratively. Pooled RF prevalence was 7.5% (95% CI: 2.1%-23.0%) at earlier pretransplant assessment, 13.5% (5.7%-28.5%) among recipients with EASL-CLIF ACLF assessed on the day of LT, and 28.9% (9.7%-60.6%) among recipients with ACLF-3 assessed near LT. A broad analysis of 21 reports yielded 12.9% (9.0%-18.1%; 95% prediction interval: 3.3%-38.9%). Across three independent cohorts, pooled 1-year post-LT survival was 55.3% (20.0%-86.0%) in RF-positive recipients and 82.1% (66.9%-91.2%) in RF-negative recipients. RF-positive recipients had higher 1-year mortality (unadjusted RR = 2.41, 95% CI: 1.50-3.90). One study reported 6-month mortality RRs versus non-ACLF recipients of 2.02 (95% CI: 1.23-3.30) without RF and 6.96 (95% CI: 4.84-10.00) with RF. Overall, RF was consistently associated with higher post-transplant mortality, but adjusted evidence remains insufficient to establish its independent prognostic value. Interpretation should account for RF assessment timing, ACLF severity, concurrent organ failures, and transplant selection practices.

articles.title: Living with mechanical ventilation: A grounded theory study of patients' experiences in the intensive care unit.
articles.journal: Australian critical care : official journal of the Confederation of Australian Critical Care Nurses
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Mechanical ventilation (MV) is an essential life-sustaining intervention in intensive care units (ICU). However, beyond its physiological benefits, patients frequently experience profound physical dependence, communication barriers, and emotional distress. Understanding these experiences is essential to inform person-centred nursing care and humanisation strategies in critical care settings.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to explore the experiences of patients receiving invasive MV, identify the meanings attributed to these experiences, and generate a substantive theory to inform humanised critical care nursing.

METHODS: A qualitative study based on Classical Grounded Theory (Glaser and Strauss) was conducted. Adult patients who received invasive MV for at least 48 h in the ICU at Vall d'Hebron University Hospital (Barcelona, Spain) participated in semistructured interviews. Data were analysed using constant comparative analysis involving open, axial, and selective coding, supported by NVivo 12 software. Guba and Lincoln's criteria were applied to ensure trustworthiness.

FINDINGS: Extreme Vulnerability was identified as the core category explaining patients' experiences. Participants described profound bodily dependence associated with invasive medical devices and immobility, an inability to communicate that generated frustration and helplessness, and emotional isolation during critical illness. Nurses mitigated distress by recognising nonverbal communication, maintaining a therapeutic presence, and providing continuity of care, while family members provided emotional support through their reassuring presence and by helping healthcare professionals interpret participants' nonverbal cues. Following ICU discharge, participants described the transition to the general ward not only as a positive step towards recovery but also as a period of adjustment characterised by uncertainty and reduced perceived continuity and intensity of care.

CONCLUSIONS: Invasive MV was experienced not only as a life-sustaining intervention but also as a period of profound bodily dependence, disrupted communication, and reliance on others during critical illness. These findings highlight the need to integrate technical excellence with person-centred, relational care. By providing a substantive grounded theory of Extreme Vulnerability, this study highlights the central role of critical care nurses in leading person-centred interventions, promoting active family involvement, and humanising intensive care practice throughout the care trajectory.

articles.title: Early recurrence of febrile seizures in the pediatric emergency department: development and internal validation of FSERS, a practical bedside risk score.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Febrile seizures (FS) are common and generally benign. Early recurrence within 24 h does not itself mandate admission or treatment but may prompt reassessment before discharge, particularly when atypical or evolving features raise concern for an alternative acute neurologic diagnosis. We aimed to develop and internally validate a bedside score for early FS recurrence.

METHODS: We included 400 children with confirmed FS presenting to a tertiary pediatric emergency department (PED) between January 2020 and December 2024. Complex-phenotype FS was defined by focal onset or prolonged duration only. Backward stepwise multivariable logistic regression derived a parsimonious model, followed by 1000-iteration bootstrap internal validation.

RESULTS: Early recurrence occurred in 45/400 children (11.2%). Independent predictors were neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR; adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.345), seizure duration (aOR 1.154), C-reactive protein (CRP; aOR 1.187), serum sodium (aOR 0.606), and fever-to-seizure interval (aOR 0.821). The continuous model achieved an apparent area under the curve (AUC) of 0.924 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.897. The derived integer FS Early Recurrence Score (FSERS) had an apparent AUC of 0.905 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.887.

CONCLUSIONS: FSERS integrates five readily available variables into an internally validated estimate of early FS recurrence risk. It is not an admission rule, treatment trigger, or diagnostic model for central nervous system infection or acute encephalopathy, and should complement clinical reassessment and red-flag evaluation. Prospective multicenter external validation is required before score-based changes in observation or disposition are considered.

articles.title: The pathological role of chemokines and chemokine receptors in diabetic vascular disease.
articles.abstract: Diabetic vascular diseases, which include microvascular and macrovascular diseases, are a common complication of diabetes mellitus. Both chemokines and their receptors are involved in the pathophysiological process of diabetic vascular diseases, given their diverse functions. Crucially, when evaluating these chemokine networks, it is essential to distinguish descriptive clinical and bioinformatic biomarker observations from functional causal mechanisms established through in vitro and in vivo interventional studies, as observational concentration changes alone do not inherently demonstrate a direct pathogenic role or identify a therapeutic target. In this review, we examine recent studies and provide an overview of the mechanisms underlying chemokine-mediated signaling in diabetic microvascular and macrovascular diseases. We conclude that while circulating chemokines primarily serve as diagnostic or prognostic biomarkers, specific functional chemokine axes represent viable therapeutic targets for diabetic vascular complications.

articles.title: Circulating interleukin-18 as a severity-associated cytokine in Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mycoplasma pneumoniae causes atypical pneumonia that ranges in severity. Interleukin (IL)-18, a pro-inflammatory cytokine, has been implicated in infection-related inflammation. In this study, we evaluated the association between circulating IL-18 and disease severity in M. pneumoniae pneumonia patients (MPP).

METHODS: The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024606393). The PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, and ScienceDirect databases were searched from inception to September 2025. Studies reporting serum or plasma IL-18 levels in children with MPP were included. Pooled mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated. Subgroup analyses were performed by country and IL-18 detection method. Publication bias was assessed using funnel plots and Egger's test. Study quality and risk of bias were evaluated using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale.

RESULTS: Among the 17 included studies, 11 contributed to the comparison between children with MPP and non-MPP controls. The pooled analysis showed higher circulating IL-18 levels in children with MPP (MD = 178.95 pg/mL, 95% CI [133.28, 224.62]; I2 = 99.4%; p < 0.001). Eight studies contributed to the comparison between severe and non-severe MPP, with higher circulating IL-18 levels observed in severe MPP (MD = 76.86 pg/mL, 95% CI [50.25, 103.47]; I2 = 98.9%; p < 0.001). Subgroup analyses indicated variation by country and detection method, while sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the findings. Funnel-plot asymmetry was observed, although its interpretation was limited by substantial between-study heterogeneity.

CONCLUSIONS: Circulating IL-18 is elevated in MPP and higher in severe disease, supporting its potential as a severity-associated cytokine. However, the substantial heterogeneity among current studies warrants cautious interpretation and further validation of their results.

articles.title: Tear-fluid glial fibrillary acidic protein combined with optic-nerve ultrasonography for non-invasive assessment of cerebral involvement in severe pre-eclampsia: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine whether serum and tear-fluid glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), anti-GFAP autoantibodies, and optic-nerve ultrasonography are associated with disease severity in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, and to explore whether their combination adds to the identification of severe pre-eclampsia.

STUDY DESIGN: This prospective cross-sectional study included 184 pregnant women equally allocated to normotensive pregnancy, gestational hypertension, moderate pre-eclampsia, or severe pre-eclampsia (n = 46/group). Serum GFAP and anti-GFAP autoantibodies were measured in all participants, and tear-fluid GFAP in a predefined subgroup (22/group). Standardized optic-nerve ultrasonography assessed optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD), optic disc height (ODH), optic nerve diameter, and scleral canal diameter. Associations were analysed using non-parametric statistics, Spearman correlation, and receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) analysis.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Between-group differences in biomarkers and ultrasonographic parameters, correlations with disease severity, and discrimination of severe pre-eclampsia by ROC analysis.

RESULTS: Serum GFAP increased only in severe pre-eclampsia, whereas tear-fluid GFAP increased progressively from moderate to severe disease (both P < 0.001). Anti-GFAP autoantibodies peaked in moderate pre-eclampsia. Tear-fluid GFAP correlated strongly with ODH (r = 0.772) and with clinical severity (all P < 0.001). ONSD (AUC 0.984) and ODH (AUC 0.973) were the most accurate individual markers; tear-fluid GFAP (AUC 0.908) outperformed serum GFAP (AUC 0.744).

CONCLUSIONS: Tear-fluid GFAP rises earlier than serum GFAP and tracks ultrasonographic signs of raised intracranial pressure, supporting it as a non-invasive marker of astroglial injury in pre-eclampsia. Optic-nerve ultrasonography provides the strongest discrimination of severe disease. Prospective multicentre studies with neurological outcomes are needed before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Impact of oral diuretic monitoring duration prior to discharge on 30-day heart failure readmission rates.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current guidelines recommend transitioning patients with heart failure (HF) to oral diuretics prior to discharge, yet data guiding the optimal duration of oral diuretic monitoring remains limited. Prior retrospective studies assessed discharge-day oral diuretics or used a 24-hour monitoring cutoff.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate time on oral diuretic prior to discharge and 30-day HF readmission.

METHODS: This single center retrospective study included patients admitted for acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) between 1/2020-9/2022. The primary end-point was 30-day HF readmission. Logistic regression models were used to estimate odds of readmission across varying durations of oral diuretic therapy (<24, 24-47, 48-71, and ≥72 h). Inverse propensity score weights (IPTW) were applied to control for confounder variables. Statistical significance was assessed using 95% confidence intervals (CI).

RESULTS: A total of 466 patients were included (mean age 67.2 + 16.2 years; 56.2% male). IPTW results showed no significant difference in readmission rates for patients on diuretics < 24-hour group compared to 24-47 h (odds ratio (OR) 0.78 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.36, 1.67], 48-71 h (OR 0.78 [CI 0.36, 1.69]), and ≥72 h (OR 0.99 [CI 0.45, 2.15]). There was no significant difference in readmission rates when comparing <24 h versus ≥24 h of oral diuretic therapy (OR 0.85 [CI 0.43, 1.68]).

CONCLUSION: In patients with ADHF, extending oral diuretic monitoring beyond 24 h before discharge was not associated with reduced 30-day HF readmissions. Future studies should investigate the relationship between time on oral diuretics and overall response prior to discharge.

articles.title: Vancomycin presoaking of ligament grafts: State of the Art and graft-specific evidence.
articles.journal: Journal of ISAKOS : joint disorders & orthopaedic sports medicine
articles.abstract: Septic arthritis after ligament reconstruction is uncommon but potentially devastating. Vancomycin graft presoaking was developed as an adjunct to standard systemic prophylaxis and sterile technique to reduce viable Gram-positive contamination before implantation and biofilm maturation. This State-of-the-Art review evaluates its biological rationale, clinical effectiveness, safety, implementation, graft-specific considerations, hypersensitivity, antimicrobial stewardship, geographic variation, cost-effectiveness, and unresolved controversies. A structured narrative search of PubMed was updated through October 11, 2026, supplemented by backward citation screening and targeted review of relevant guidance and evidence syntheses. The clinical evidence remains predominantly observational. Large comparative cohorts and pooled analyses consistently associate vancomycin graft presoaking with lower rates of septic arthritis after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR), with the most direct evidence applying to hamstring autografts. Limited randomized evidence is available but remains underpowered for a rare postoperative infection outcome. Absolute benefit varies with baseline infection risk. Laboratory, animal, and clinical studies have not demonstrated harm within commonly studied short-exposure protocols, although the most direct clinical safety evidence also derives from hamstring autografts. Evidence for bone-patellar tendon-bone grafts, quadriceps tendon grafts, allografts, revision procedures, and non-ACL ligament reconstructions remains substantially more limited or indirect. One uncontrolled 2026 quadriceps tendon series represents an unconfirmed graft-specific safety signal rather than evidence of a contraindication. No alternative graft-presoaking antibiotic currently has a clinical evidence base comparable to vancomycin. Based on the current evidence, vancomycin graft presoaking may be considered as an adjunct to standard systemic prophylaxis in hamstring autograft ACLR within a standardized protocol. It should not replace established infection-prevention measures, and extrapolation to other graft types or reconstruction settings should reflect the directness of the available evidence. Future research should prioritize graft-specific protocol optimization, prospective comparative evidence, antimicrobial-resistance surveillance, and long-term graft and cartilage outcomes.

articles.title: N-terminal 24-amino acid fragment (GI24) of the 36-amino acid peptide PMAP-36 (porcine myeloid antimicrobial peptide 36) exhibits antiviral activity against porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus in vitro.
articles.abstract: Given vaccine strategies provide limited protection against porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV) prevalence and transmission, there is an urgent demand for developing novel antiviral strategies against to combat this pathogen. Antimicrobial peptides are known to possess antiviral activity against viruses. In this study, We screened and identified PMAP-36, a member of linear porcine myeloid antimicrobial peptides (PMAPs) from the porcine cathelicidin family, which exhibits prominent antiviral activity against PRRSV. Furthermore, the N-terminal 24-amino acid fragment (GI24) of the 36-amino acid peptide PMAP-36 serves as the key active region responsible for its antiviral function, as it robustly inhibits both PRRSV attachment and cellular entry. We also show that GI24 exerts anti-inflammatory effects, as it suppresses the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines and the activation of inflammatory signaling pathways induced by both PRRSV and Lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Additionally, we demonstrate that TREM1 is a crucial target gene mediating the anti-inflammatory effects of GI24. Collectively, our data reveal that porcine-derived antimicrobial peptides inhibited PRRSV infection and suppressing pro-infammatory responses. Therefore, porcine cathelicidin-derived antimicrobial peptides represent excellent candidates for the development of potential therapeutic agents against PRRSV infection.

articles.title: PACAP attenuates diabetic neuropathic pain by modulating ERK-PGC1α- associated mitochondrial homeostasis.
articles.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
articles.abstract: Diabetic neuropathic pain is a debilitating complication of diabetes for which disease-modifying therapies remain limited. Pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide (PACAP) has been implicated in neuroprotection and metabolic regulation, but its role in diabetic neuropathic pain remains unclear. Here, we found that patients with diabetic neuropathic pain had reduced serum PACAP-38 levels and elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines compared with patients with diabetes mellitus alone. In streptozotocin-induced diabetic neuropathic pain (DNP) mice, PACAP partially improved body weight recovery but did not markedly reduce fasting hyperglycemia, glucose tolerance or pancreatic islet injury. Importantly, PACAP improved gait performance, attenuated mechanical, thermal, and cold hypersensitivity, and preserved intraepidermal nerve fibers. Transcriptomic and validation analyses showed that diabetic neuropathic pain was associated with endothelial impairment, hypoxia-related signaling, mitochondrial alterations, and redox imbalance in dorsal root ganglia. PACAP treatment partially modulated DNP-related transcriptional changes, including those linked to mitochondrial metabolism, oxidative stress-related processes, and neuronal function. Mechanistically, PACAP increased ERK phosphorylation and PGC1α expression, enhanced mitochondrial biogenesis-related responses, preserved mitochondrial ultrastructure, and improved mitochondrial membrane potential. ERK inhibition with U0126 attenuated PACAP-mediated mitochondrial protection and analgesic effects. These findings suggest that PACAP alleviates DNP through an ERK-PGC1α-associated mechanism that contributes to the restoration of mitochondrial homeostasis in sensory neurons, rather than by substantially correcting systemic hyperglycemia.

articles.title: Long-Term Outcomes After Left Ventricular Assist Device Exchange: Survival Rates and Postoperative Complications.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Some patients require left ventricular assist device (LVAD) exchange because of pump thrombosis, infection, or pump failure. The aim of this study is to compare the long-term survival and postoperative complications between patients who did not require LVAD exchange and patients who required LVAD exchange.

METHODS: We included patients who underwent HeartMate II, HeartWare Ventricular Assist Device and HeartMate 3, LVAD implantation at our institution between December 2008 and November 2019. We compared survival rate and postoperative complications between the cases which did not require LVAD exchange (Group 1) and the cases which required LVAD exchange (Group 2).

RESULTS: There were 333 cases which met our criteria. Group 1 included 296 cases; group 2 included 37 cases. Causes of LVAD exchange were pump thrombosis (n = 22), driveline fracture (n = 6) cases, driveline infection (n = 8), and pump failure (n = 1). There was no statistical difference between groups in cumulative incidence of death 5 y after surgery, or in postoperative gastrointestinal bleeding and neurological complications. The rate of postoperative device-related infection was higher in group 2.

CONCLUSIONS: To the best of our knowledge, this report includes the longest follow-up period comparing patients who required LVAD exchange after surgery to those who did not require LVAD exchange. LVAD exchange can be performed safely without increasing mortality rates, gastrointestinal bleeding, or neurological complications.

articles.title: Construction and Validation of a Predictive Model for Recurrence of Secondary Hyperparathyroidism After Parathyroidectomy.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to develop and validate a nomogram to predict the risk of recurrence after total parathyroidectomy with autotransplantation (tPTX + AT) in patients with secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT).

METHODS: A total of 528 patients with SHPT who underwent initial tPTX + AT at the 960th Hospital of the PLA Joint Logistics Support Force from January 2013 to June 2024 were retrospectively enrolled. Patients were randomly divided into a training cohort (n = 369) and a validation cohort (n = 159) at a 7:3 ratio. Independent risk factors were screened using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression combined with the Cox proportional hazards model, and a nomogram prediction model was constructed accordingly. The model's discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated using the concordance index (C-index), time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis.

RESULTS: The postoperative recurrence rate was 14.39%. Four independent predictive factors were jointly screened: preoperative 25-hydroxyvitamin D, intact parathyroid hormone on the first postoperative day, preoperative serum calcium concentration, and the number of resected parathyroid glands. The C-index was 0.759 in the training cohort and 0.716 in the validation cohort. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for 2-, 4-, and 6-y recurrence in the training cohort were 0.970, 0.804, and 0.745, respectively, and 0.736, 0.705, and 0.736 in the validation cohort, demonstrating acceptable predictive performance of the model. Calibration curves showed good consistency between predicted probabilities and observed outcomes. Decision curve analysis indicated that the model provided clinical net benefit across clinically relevant threshold probabilities.

CONCLUSIONS: This study successfully developed and validated a nomogram prediction model for recurrence after tPTX + AT in patients with SHPT. The model demonstrated acceptable predictive performance and can serve as a valuable individualized risk assessment tool for postoperative management in SHPT patients.

articles.title: A Needs Assessment of Research Methodology Training for Acute Care Surgeons in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Comparative Global Survey.
authors: International Relations Committee of the American Association for the Surgery of Trauma (AAST)
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Most injuries occur in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet the trauma literature largely reflects high-income countries (HICs), and no research-methodology course is tailored to LMIC acute care surgeons or to trauma-specific infrastructure such as injury registries. We surveyed acute care surgeons to inform an American Association for the Surgery of Trauma (AAST) research-methodology curriculum.

METHODS: A voluntary 25-item Research Electronic Data Capture survey developed by the AAST International Relations Committee, covering research experience, infrastructure access, and training priorities, was distributed (January-June 2025) by email and social media to AAST members and partner international trauma organizations. Respondents were classified by World Bank income group and compared using chi-square or Fisher exact tests.

RESULTS: Of 132 respondents, 72 (55%) practiced in HICs and 60 (45%) in LMICs. versus HIC peers, LMIC respondents reported less research experience (73% versus 90%; P = 0.01), fewer publications (38% versus 74%; P < 0.001), and markedly less access to a trauma registry (20% versus 86%), statistical support, and a research coordinator (all P ≤ 0.006). A higher proportion of LMIC respondents selected registry design (52% versus 26%), scientific writing (67% versus 46%), and literature appraisal (47% versus 28%), while HIC respondents favored statistics and retrospective research (P < 0.05); and more likely to agree a mentor would help their research (93% versus 60%; P < 0.001). Course interest was high in both groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Interest in research-methodology training was strong across income settings, but LMIC surgeons reported distinct, infrastructure-linked needs centered on trauma-registry building, scientific writing, foundational skills, and mentorship. Course design should reflect these differences rather than export a high-income model.

articles.title: The association of subjective quality of life with emotion dysregulation and binge-eating pathology in acne vulgaris: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acne vulgaris (AV) imposes psychosocial burden beyond lesion severity, yet the specific psychological profiles it produces remain incompletely characterized.

OBJECTIVE: To examine emotion dysregulation (DER) and binge-eating disorder (BED) psychopathology in AV patients, and evaluate whether subjective quality of life (QoL) mediates the association between objective severity and psychological outcomes.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study enrolled 100 AV patients and 105 matched controls. Objective severity (GAGS), QoL (AQLS), DER (DERS-16), and eating psychopathology (EDE-Q-13/BED subscale) were assessed. Bootstrapped mediation analyses and multivariate regression were performed.

RESULTS: AV patients demonstrated significantly higher DERS-16 (d = 1.82) and BED subscale scores (p = 0.005) than controls. Group membership predicted DERS-16 and EDE-Q-13-BED scores independently of sociodemographic covariates. GAGS severity showed no direct association with DERS-16 or EDE-Q-13. Crucially, AQLS significantly mediated the effect of GAGS on both DERS-16 (β = 2.747, 95% CI [0.164, 5.837]) and EDE-Q-13 (β = 0.336, 95% CI [0.036, 0.836]); these indirect effects remained robust after adjustment for education, occupation, and income.

STUDY LIMITATIONS: Cross-sectional design limits causal inference. Significant sociodemographic differences existed between groups (controlled via regression). Statistical power for GAGS subgroup comparisons was limited. No structured psychiatric interviews were conducted.

CONCLUSIONS: Subjective QoL impairment, rather than objective lesion burden, is associated with significant indirect effects on both emotion dysregulation and affect-driven eating pathology in AV patients. Routine dermatological care should integrate QoL assessment and psychological screening, irrespective of clinical severity.

articles.title: Correction: Time to rethink washout periods in inflammatory bowel disease clinical trials: an international Delphi consensus.
Effect of a nurse-led supported self-care intervention on cardiometabolic outcomes in adults with type 2 diabetes: a quasi-experimental study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Supported self-care interventions are increasingly used in diabetes management; however, evidence regarding their impact on cardiometabolic outcomes in primary care remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: To examine changes in cardiometabolic indicators following a nurse-led supported self-care intervention in adults with type 2 diabetes.

METHODS: A single-group pre-post study derived from a larger quasi-experimental project was conducted between March and November 2023 at a Family Health Unit in Central-West Brazil. Participants received three monthly nurse-led supported self-care consultations and two telephone follow-ups. Clinical and anthropometric measures were assessed at baseline, during the intervention, and post-intervention, whereas HbA1c, triglycerides, TyG, and TyG-WC were assessed at baseline and post-intervention. Data were analyzed using Friedman, Wilcoxon signed-rank, and McNemar tests, as appropriate.

RESULTS: Twenty-nine participants completed follow-up and were included in the final analysis. Significant reductions were observed in waist circumference, systolic blood pressure, TyG, and TyG-WC. No significant change in HbA1c was observed between baseline and post-intervention.

CONCLUSIONS: The nurse-led supported self-care intervention was associated with favorable within-participant changes in selected anthropometric and cardiometabolic measures, particularly those related to central adiposity and cardiovascular risk. However, no significant improvement in HbA1c was observed. Controlled studies are needed to determine whether these changes can be attributed to the intervention.

articles.title: Hepatic ITGBL1 promotes fibrogenesis and ductular remodeling through integrin-dependent latent TGF-β activation.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
articles.abstract: Liver fibrosis is a major determinant of chronic liver disease progression and hepatobiliary remodeling. However, extracellular regulators linking fibrogenesis to pathological biliary responses remain incompletely understood. Integrin beta-like protein 1 (ITGBL1) is an extracellular matrix-associated protein implicated in integrin modulation, but its functional role in chronic liver injury remains unclear. A liver-specific doxycycline (DOX)-inducible zebrafish model was established to evaluate the effects of hepatic ITGBL1 gain-of-function in vivo. Fibrogenic and biliary responses were assessed using histologic, molecular, and genetic approaches. Mechanistic studies tested pathway dependence on itgav and ltbp1 using liver-specific genetic ablation, with cilengitide used as a complementary RGD-integrin pharmacologic perturbation. Hepatocyte-specific ITGBL1 induction triggered progressive hepatic stellate cell activation, extracellular matrix accumulation, and chronic fibrotic remodeling. Sustained ITGBL1 expression further promoted ductular reaction and biliary epithelial expansion during chronic liver injury progression. Genetic disruption of itgav or ltbp1 attenuated SMAD3 activation, collagen deposition, fibrogenic transcriptional programs, and associated histological remodeling; cilengitide independently attenuated fibrogenic readouts. These data support a working model in which hepatic ITGBL1 lies upstream of integrin/LTBP1-dependent latent TGF-β/SMAD3 signaling and provide a mechanistic framework for further resolving the molecular interactions among ITGBL1, ITGAV, and LTBP1 and the αv-integrin heterodimer involved. This pathway may represent a therapeutic target for fibrosis-associated biliary remodeling.

articles.title: Statin-Ezetimibe Combination Therapy versus Statin Monotherapy in Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: A Prespecified Secondary Analysis of the Randomized Ez-PAVE Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In a target-directed low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C)-lowering strategy, the impact of the initial treatment regimen has not been investigated in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. We compared the efficacy and safety of initial statin-ezetimibe combination therapy versus statin monotherapy within intensive or conventional LDL-C-targeting strategies.

METHODS: In this prespecified second randomization of the randomized Ez-PAVE trial (Effects of Ezetimibe Combination Therapy for Patients With Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: Randomized Comparison of LDL Cholesterol Targeting <70 versus <55 mg/dL) conducted at 17 centers in South Korea, a total of 3048 patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease were enrolled between January 2021 and July 2022. Following the first randomization to either an intensive (<55 mg/dL) or conventional (<70 mg/dL) LDL-C-targeting strategy, patients underwent subsequent randomization (initial statin-ezetimibe combination therapy [n=1525] versus statin monotherapy [n=1523]) and were followed up for 3 years. Lipid-lowering therapy was adjusted according to a predefined protocol to achieve LDL-C targets. The primary end point was a 3-year composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, any revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina.

RESULTS: The mean±SD age was 64.4±9.0 years, and 638 patients (20.9%) were female. The incidence of the primary end point did not differ between statin-ezetimibe combination therapy (128 patients [8.5%]) and statin monotherapy (119 patients [7.9%]; hazard ratio, 1.07 [95% CI, 0.83-1.37]; P=0.596). Patients who received statin-ezetimibe combination therapy achieved lower median LDL-C levels during follow-up than those who received statin monotherapy in both the intensive-targeting (53 mg/dL [interquartile range, 45-62 mg/dL] versus 62 mg/dL [interquartile range, 53-74 mg/dL]) and conventional-targeting (63 mg/dL [interquartile range, 55-73 mg/dL] versus 70 mg/dL [interquartile range, 62-81 mg/dL]) strategies. During follow-up, ezetimibe was added to the treatment regimen of 241 patients (34.3%) and 177 patients (24.8%) who initially received statin monotherapy in the intensive- and conventional-targeting strategies, respectively. The treatment effect of intensive-targeting versus conventional-targeting strategies was consistent regardless of therapy regimens without significant heterogeneity (Pinteraction=0.583). The safety end points were similar between the groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Within a target-directed LDL-C-lowering strategy, cardiovascular efficacy and safety did not differ significantly, whether initiated as statin-ezetimibe combination therapy or as statin monotherapy, but combination therapy facilitated achievement of a lower LDL-C target.
