articles.title: Integrated Prenatal Cardiopulmonary Assessment Using Fetal Echocardiography in Isolated Left-Sided Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Prenatal severity assessment in congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) primarily relies on lung-based parameters such as the observed-to-expected lung-to-head ratio (o/eLHR) and liver position; however, these markers do not fully reflect fetal cardiopulmonary adaptation. We investigated the prognostic significance of fetal echocardiographic parameters and integrated these in prenatal prediction models in left-sided CDH.

METHODS: This nationwide multicenter retrospective study included fetuses with prenatally diagnosed isolated left-sided CDH. Gestational age-adjusted Z-scores were generated for fetal cardiac dimensions. Receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed to evaluate prognostic performance for survival.

RESULTS: A total of 363 fetuses were included, with an overall survival rate of 74.9%. Non-survivors demonstrated significantly smaller right pulmonary artery and mitral valve dimensions than survivors. Among fetal echocardiographic parameters, the mitral-to-tricuspid valve ratio (MTR) demonstrated the strongest predictive performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.77. In fetuses evaluated at ≤ 29 weeks' gestation, an exploratory model combining MTR with o/eLHR and liver-up status achieved an apparent AUC of 0.827.

CONCLUSION: Fetal echocardiographic parameters were associated with survival in CDH. Integrated prenatal cardiopulmonary assessment incorporating MTR may provide complementary prognostic information although independent external validation is required.

articles.title: Leveraging AI-ECG Technology for Early Notification and Tracking of AF Development (LATENT): A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Electrocardiographic analysis aided by artificial intelligence (AI) may identify atrial electrical vulnerability during sinus rhythm. The objective of this study was to determine whether AI-enabled ECG (AI-ECG) is effective for detecting atrial fibrillation (AF), atrial flutter (AFl), or prespecified pre-AF atrial findings in a randomized trial.

METHODS: In this single-center, open-label trial, 14 665 adults 40 to 85 years of age without previous AF/AFl were randomized to an AI-ECG-guided strategy or usual care. Participants randomized to AI-ECG who were then identified by AI as having a high-risk sinus-rhythm ECG in the preceding year were offered Holter monitoring for ≤7 days. Each monitored high-risk intervention participant was paired with an age- and sex-matched control selected before control ECGs underwent AI analysis. Matched controls received identical monitoring to reduce ascertainment bias. Reporting cardiologists were blinded to AI results and randomized assignment. The primary outcome was a composite of newly detected AF, AFl, or pre-AF atrial findings within 90 days. Pre-AF atrial findings comprised frequent premature atrial complexes, short runs of premature atrial complexes, or nonsustained AF/AFl.

RESULTS: Among 7337 intervention and 7328 control participants, 84 (1.1%) and 78 (1.1%), respectively, were classified as high risk. Of the 84 high-risk intervention participants, 48 (57.1%) underwent monitoring, as did 48 matched controls. The primary outcome occurred in 54 intervention participants (0.74%) versus 35 control participants (0.48%; odds ratio, 1.54 [95% CI, 1.01-2.37]; P=0.046). Hypothetical reclassification of 1 intervention event to a nonevent changed the primary analysis P value to 0.057. The intervention effect on detection of the primary composite outcome differed by baseline AI-ECG risk (Pinteraction<0.001): 32.1% versus 2.6% among high-risk participants and 0.4% versus 0.5% among low-risk participants. AF/AFl detection (0.3% versus 0.2%) and antiarrhythmic therapy initiation at 180 days (2.3% versus 2.4%) did not differ significantly between the intervention and control groups. Participant-reported monitoring-related adverse events, including skin reactions and discomfort, occurred in 22.9% of monitored intervention participants versus 18.8% of matched controls.

CONCLUSIONS: AI-ECG-guided monitoring resulted in a modest increase in the detection of new AF, AFl, or pre-AF atrial findings. However, these findings were fragile statistically and sensitive to reclassification of 1 event. LATENT (Leveraging AI-ECG Technology for Early Notification and Tracking of AF Development) demonstrates the clinical application of AI-ECG risk stratification to guide targeted rhythm surveillance, providing a foundation for larger trials evaluating its impact on patient outcomes.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT06847932.

articles.title: AI-ECG Atrial Fibrillation Detection: Unlocking Secrets in Sinus Rhythm?
AI-ECG: Gatekeeper-in-Training for Population-level Atrial Fibrillation Screening.

Multimodality Cardiac Imaging Substudy of the DAPT-SHOCK-AMI Randomized Trial: Echocardiographic and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Assessment of Cangrelor versus Crushed Ticagrelor in Cardiogenic Shock Complicating Acute Myocardial Infarction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS), the myocardium sustains a dual injury: ischemia of the culprit territory and global hypoperfusion from low cardiac output. Whether platelet inhibition at reperfusion affects the microcirculation, the infarct, the noninfarcted myocardium, and ventricular function, and over what time course, has not been examined with serial imaging. The prespecified multimodality imaging substudy of the randomized DAPT-SHOCK-AMI trial (intravenous cangrelor versus crushed oral ticagrelor) addressed this question.

METHODS: Patients at prespecified imaging sites underwent serial echocardiography (208 enrolled; evaluable examinations in 175, 120, and 99 patients in the acute phase, at 1 month, and at 1 year) and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR; 93 enrolled; 73, 68, and 63); 81 patients (40 and 41) underwent both modalities. Blinded core laboratories analyzed all studies. The primary imaging endpoint was microvascular obstruction (MVO) on acute CMR, evaluable in 60 patients; secondary endpoints were infarct size, native T1 of the global, infarcted, and remote myocardium, left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction (LVEF), global longitudinal strain (GLS), E/e', and left atrial volume, and their changes. Comparisons between the cangrelor and crushed ticagrelor arms used covariate-adjusted logistic or linear regression; the substudy was not separately powered.

RESULTS: The odds of acute MVO were lower with cangrelor (adjusted odds ratio 0.27 [95% CI 0.08 to 0.98]; P=0.023). Infarct size did not differ between the arms. At 1 year, native T1 of the remote myocardium was lower with cangrelor (adjusted mean 1114 [95% CI 1057 to 1171] versus 1171 [1115 to 1228] ms; P=0.005). Over 1 year, LVEF increased more with cangrelor on echocardiography (37.9% versus 21.7% of the acute value; adjusted P=0.046) and CMR (15.8% versus 2.1%; P=0.027), with greater improvement in GLS, lower E/e', and less left atrial enlargement; no parameter differed between the arms at 1 month.

CONCLUSIONS: In AMI-CS, serial multimodality imaging characterized microvascular, tissue-level, and functional injury over 1 year. Cangrelor was associated with less acute MVO, lower remote native T1, and more complete recovery of LV function than crushed ticagrelor, without a difference in infarct size; these hypothesis-generating findings suggest differences in the microcirculation and non-infarcted myocardial injury but do not establish a treatment mechanism.

articles.title: Can Intravenous Cangrelor Protect the Myocardium in Infarction-related Cardiogenic Shock?
Chaetomorpha linum (O.F.Müller) Kützing 1845 attenuates glucotoxicity via modulation of polyol pathway, oxidative stress and glucose metabolism in adipose tissue.
articles.abstract: Chronic hyperglycaemia in type 2 diabetes drives a self-perpetuating cycle of glucotoxicity. This study investigated the therapeutic potential of extracts from the green seaweed Chaetomorpha linum (O.F.Müller) Kützing, 1845 to mitigate glucotoxicity in rats adipocytes. Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) analysis revealed distinct phytochemical profiles, with the aqueous extract containing isolobinine, kurarinol, rutaevin, and proanthocyanidin-A2, and the ethanol extract containing caryoptin, mesembrinol, 12-deoxyphorbol-13-octadecanoate, and aspulvinone H. Bioactivity assays showed that C. linum extracts reversed glucotoxicity-induced pathologies, restoring glucose uptake (3.9-6.1 mg/g adipose tissue at 240 µg/mL), suppressing polyol pathway enzyme activities (2.7-9.5 µmol/min/mg, at 240 µg/mL), and enhancing antioxidant defense markers. Concurrently, the extracts inhibited key digestive enzymes (26.7-41.0 µmol/min/µL, at 240 µg/mL). Molecular docking supported these findings, with rutaevin showing the high affinity for aldose reductase (-11.7 kcal/mol) and proanthocyanidin-A2 for lipase (-9.9 kcal/mol) and glutathione peroxidase (-7 kcal/mol). These findings highlight C. linum as a promising source of bioactive compounds for diabetes management.

articles.title: Statistical analysis plan for the 'Pharyngeal electrical stimulation for acute stroke dysphagia trial' (PhEAST) (ISRCTN98886991).
articles.abstract: Introduction Post stroke dysphagia is common, associated with poor functional outcome and lacks treatment strategies beyond behaviour therapies delivered by speech & language therapists. Here, we present the statistical analysis plan for the ongoing pharyngeal electrical stimulation for acute stroke dysphagia trial (PhEAST). PES is a candidate treatment for dysphagia present in non-ventilated stroke patients. Methods PhEAST is an investigator-initiated international prospective randomised open-label endpoint-blinded phase-4 superiority trial involving 650 participants with tube-dependent post-stroke dysphagia. Consenting patients are randomised to PES versus no PES given on top of standard care with PES given daily for 6 days. The primary outcome is the dysphagia severity rating scale (DSRS), a measure of swallowing impairment, made at days 14 and 90 and analysed using repeated measures regression. Conclusion We present the statistical analysis plan for the main analyses based on data up to day 90 along with planned secondary analyses including presentation of baseline data, health economics, cognition and extended follow-up to 12 months.

articles.title: Long Term Outcomes After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Patients With Lymphoma: A Propensity-Matched Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with a history of lymphoma may develop significant coronary artery disease (CAD), which may be treated by percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), yet long term outcomes are not well characterized.

METHODS: We reviewed patients with a history of lymphoma undergoing PCI from our institutional PCI database and compared characteristics and outcomes to a cohort without cancer. Long-term mortality and major adverse cardiac events (MACE) (cardiac death, myocardial infarction (MI), target vessel revascularization (TVR)) were assessed.

RESULTS: Of the 11,953 patients identified, 83 (0.7%) had past or current lymphoma. Most had Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) (n=23; 28.8%) or Hodgkin's Lymphoma (HL) (n=22; 27.%), and 31 (37.3%) presented with acute coronary syndrome. Lymphoma patients, as compared to non-lymphoma patients, were similar with respect to age, sex, hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, prior MI, and prior PCI (all p=ns). The 1, 3, and 5-year survival rates were 90.5%, 69.5 %, and 52.5% in lymphoma patients as compared to 88.0%, 77.1%, and 66.7% in propensity matched non-lymphoma controls. Lymphoma was an independent predictor of mortality (OR 1.59; 95% CI 1.07-2.36, p=0.02) after multivariable adjustment. In propensity matched analysis over a median follow up of 4.2 years (IQR 1.28, 7.73), lymphoma was not independently associated with worse survival or MACE.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with CAD undergoing PCI, <1% had previous or active lymphoma. Although lymphoma may appear predictive of mortality in regression models with multivariable adjustment, mortality and MACE rates are similar to propensity matched controls.

articles.title: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A 20-Year Cohort Study of Clinical Features and Transplant-Free Survival.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate prevalence, clinical characteristics, and long-term liver-related outcomes of primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) in patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), focusing on determinants of transplant-free survival.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 2,376 patients with IBD were screened over 20 years, and 30 patients with PSC were identified. A matched IBD control group without PSC (n=90) was included for comparison. Clinical features, biochemical parameters, and liver-related outcomes were analyzed. Transplant-free survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis, and exploratory univariable Cox regression was performed to identify predictors of liver transplantation.

RESULTS: PSC was identified in 1.3% of patients and was more frequently associated with ulcerative colitis. Large-duct PSC accounted for 87% of cases, and cirrhosis was present in 20% at diagnosis. During median follow-up of 60 months, liver transplantation occurred in 27% of patients. Baseline cirrhosis was strongly associated with reduced transplant-free survival (log-rank p=0.002) and increased risk of liver transplantation (HR 6.05, 95% CI 1.49-24.61). Median transplant-free survival was 4 years in cirrhotic patients, whereas it was not reached in non-cirrhotic patients. Biochemical response to ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) was not associated with transplantation or mortality. Compared with controls, PSC-IBD patients more frequently exhibited extensive colitis and backwash ileitis, while treatment exposure and remission rates were similar.

CONCLUSION: PSC is a clinically relevant but uncommon comorbidity in IBD. Baseline cirrhosis emerged as the primary determinant of adverse liver-related outcomes, whereas biochemical response to UDCA was not prognostically informative. These findings suggest that disease stage at diagnosis, rather than biochemical response, should guide risk stratification and clinical decision-making in PSC.

articles.title: Prediction of Subsequent Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure After a 24-Hour Landmark in Cirrhotic Patients With Variceal Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Some cirrhotic patients admitted with variceal upper gastrointestinal bleeding experience clinical deterioration during hospitalization and develop acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF), a critical event strongly associated with short-term mortality. Since ACLF may be reversible in its early stages, risk stratification prior to overt ACLF is clinically important.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study (2015-2025) involving cirrhotic patients admitted for esophagogastric variceal bleeding. A 24-hour landmark analysis was performed among patients who remained ACLF-free during the first 24 hours after admission, with subsequent ACLF before discharge as the primary outcome. Predictors were identified using LASSO and best-subset selection procedures. Logistic regression and random forest models were developed and compared with the available AIMS65 and Glasgow-Blatchford score (GBS) risk categories. Model performance was assessed in terms of discrimination (AUC), calibration (CITL and calibration slope), and clinical utility (decision curve analysis with integrated net benefit). External validation was performed using an independent cohort.

RESULTS: Of 1,787 screened patients, 555 were included in the derivation cohort and 240 in the external validation cohort after application of the 24-hour landmark. Subsequent ACLF occurred in 281 and 114 patients, respectively. Four predictors were retained in the final model: shock index (SI), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), prothrombin time (PT), and total bilirubin (TBil). In the derivation cohort, the AUCs were 0.752 for logistic regression and 0.715 for the random forest model, compared with 0.654 for the AIMS65 categories and 0.699 for the GBS categories. In the validation cohort, the corresponding AUCs were 0.723 and 0.715, compared with 0.668 for the AIMS65 categories and 0.667 for the GBS categories, respectively. Calibration was more stable for logistic regression than for random forest. Decision-curve analyses indicated positive but overlapping net benefits across models, suggesting potential complementary use rather than clear superiority over the benchmark risk categories.

CONCLUSIONS: We developed and externally validated models to estimate the risk of subsequent ACLF after the first 24 hours of hospitalization following variceal UGIB. The logistic regression model demonstrated stable probability calibration and may provide complementary information for post-admission ACLF risk reassessment. Prospective studies are required to evaluate its clinical impact and broader applicability.

articles.title: Initial Diabetes Therapy After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting and Long-Term Outcomes.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is common among patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), but optimal post-CABG glucose-lowering therapy remains uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the OptumLabs Data Warehouse of adults with T2D undergoing isolated CABG from 2012-2024. Follow-up began 30 days after discharge. Glucose-lowering therapy was modeled as a time-varying exposure with patients contributing no-observed-therapy person-time until the first qualifying post-discharge fill. Pairwise comparisons used stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes were heart failure hospitalization, stroke, and repeat coronary revascularization.

RESULTS: Among 19,237 patients, 24.9% had no observed post-discharge therapy, 42.8% received metformin, 22.9% received insulin, and 9.4% received GLP-1RA/SGLT2i therapy. All active therapies were associated with lower mortality compared with no observed therapy, including GLP-1RA/SGLT2i (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.58-0.87), metformin (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.55-0.66), and insulin (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.67-0.84). Among active therapies, metformin was associated with lower mortality than insulin (HR, 0.61 [0.54-0.70]); GLP-1RA/SGLT2i comparisons with metformin and insulin were less precise. Metformin was also associated with lower cumulative incidence of heart failure hospitalization than no observed therapy and insulin, and lower stroke incidence than insulin.

CONCLUSIONS: Observed glucose-lowering therapy initiation after CABG was associated with lower mortality compared with no observed therapy across all active treatment groups. These findings highlight a potential care gap and suggest that proper initiation of diabetes therapy after CABG represents an important opportunity to improve long-term outcomes following surgical revascularization.

articles.title: Long-Term Survival After Initial Invasive or Conservative Management of Stable Coronary Disease in ISCHEMIA-EXTEND.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: It is unknown whether routine invasive management of chronic coronary disease improves long-term survival when added to guideline-directed medical therapy.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the effects of initial invasive and conservative strategies on long-term mortality in patients with chronic coronary disease.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this long-term follow-up study of the International Study of Comparative Health Effectiveness with Medical and Invasive Approaches (ISCHEMIA), an international trial of patients with chronic coronary disease, moderate or severe ischemia, left ventricular ejection fraction of 35% or more, and no left main coronary artery disease, unacceptable angina, or recent acute coronary syndrome, participants were randomized at 320 sites in 37 countries beginning August 2012 and followed up through December 2025. Data were analyzed using the intention-to-treat principle.

INTERVENTION: ISCHEMIA randomized patients to an initial invasive strategy of guideline-directed medical therapy plus coronary angiography and revascularization (when feasible) or an initial conservative strategy with guideline-directed medical therapy alone, with invasive management for failure of medical therapy.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: All-cause, cardiovascular, and noncardiovascular mortality were analyzed using cumulative incidence estimates, Cox and Fine-Gray models, bayesian analysis, and restricted mean survival time.

RESULTS: Among 5179 participants, median age was 64 (IQR, 58-70) years; 23% were female, 42% had diabetes, and median ejection fraction was 60% (IQR, 55%-65%). During 9-year median follow-up (range, 1 day to 13.4 years), 1071 deaths occurred (782 during extended follow-up): 672 cardiovascular, 359 noncardiovascular, and 40 unclassified. All-cause 11-year mortality was not significantly different between groups (25.8% invasive vs 26.9% conservative; estimated difference, -1.0 percentage point [95% CI, -4.2 to 2.1 percentage points]; adjusted hazard ratio [AHR], 0.97 [95% CI, 0.86-1.09]). By bayesian analysis, the posterior probability of more than 1 percentage-point survival benefit to invasive vs conservative was low (18%). Cardiovascular mortality at 11 years was 15.8% in the invasive group vs 17.1% in the conservative group (estimated difference, -1.4 percentage points [95% CI, -4.0 to 1.3 percentage points]; AHR, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.75-1.02]). Noncardiovascular mortality at 11 years was 9.1% in the invasive group vs 8.1% in the conservative group (estimated difference, 1.0 percentage point [95% CI, -0.9 to 2.9 percentage points]; AHR, 1.18 [95% CI, 0.96-1.45]). Eleven-year restricted mean survival was not significantly different (estimated difference, 14 days [95% CI, -41 to 70 days]).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, long-term all-cause mortality in patients with high-risk chronic coronary disease was not significantly different after routine invasive vs initial conservative management.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04894877.

articles.title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention and Long-Term Outcomes in Stable Coronary Artery Disease: Extended Follow-Up of the COURAGE Randomized Trial.
Long-Term Survival After Initial Invasive or Conservative Management of Stable Coronary Disease in Patients With Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease: ISCHEMIA-CKD EXTEND.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In the ISCHEMIA-CKD trial (International Study of Comparative Health Effectiveness With Medical and Invasive Approaches-Chronic Kidney Disease), at a median follow-up of 2.2 years, the primary composite outcome of death or nonfatal myocardial infarction was similar between an initial invasive strategy (INV) compared with an initial conservative strategy (CON) in patients with moderate or severe myocardial ischemia and advanced chronic kidney disease. However, the long-term outcomes comparing the 2 strategies are unknown.

METHODS: Participants in the ISCHEMIA-CKD trial were randomly assigned to either INV, involving coronary angiography and revascularization when feasible, added to guideline-directed medical therapy or to CON with guideline-directed medical therapy alone and invasive procedures reserved for failure of guideline-directed medical therapy. After the active intervention trial phase, long-term vital status follow-up was conducted through participant contact by participating sites and by health record and centralized death database searches. The primary outcome for the extended follow-up phase was all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes were cause-specific mortality, including cardiovascular and noncardiovascular mortality.

RESULTS: Among the 777 participants randomized (388 to INV and 389 to CON), over a median of 8 years of follow-up, vital status retention among survivors was 95%. There was a total of 429 deaths (55%). Cumulative all-cause mortality (57.4% versus 56.8%; adjusted hazard ratio, 1.05 [95% CI, 0.87-1.28]) or cardiovascular mortality (40.3% versus 38.4%; adjusted hazard ratio, 1.06 [95% CI, 0.84-1.34]) at 8 years did not differ between INV and CON. The restricted mean survival time was 1941 days (1834-2047 days) for INV versus 1990 days (1885-2094 days) for CON, with an adjusted estimated difference of -99 days (-245 to 46). The posterior probability of at least a 1 percentage point lower or higher death with INV at the 8-year median follow-up was 28% and 52%, respectively. Similarly, the posterior probability of at least a 1 percentage point lower or higher cardiovascular mortality with INV was 23% and 56%, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with at least moderate ischemia and advanced chronic kidney disease, there was no significant long-term benefit of an initial INV at reducing the risk of all-cause or cardiovascular mortality compared with an initial conservative strategy.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT01985360.

articles.title: Age and Neuroimmune Diseases.
articles.abstract: With the aging population accelerating, age has become a core factor influencing the clinical phenotypes, treatment responses, and prognoses of neuroimmune diseases (NDs), including those affecting the central nervous system (CNS) and peripheral nervous system (PNS). This cross-disease review summarizes the shared and specific age-related characteristics of NDs, focusing on the pathological basis of immunosenescence and neurodegeneration underlying age-related ND progression. We extract the clinical manifestations, immune and neural mechanisms of elderly ND patients, and evaluate the challenges and individualized adjustment principles of therapeutic strategies for this population. We explore the age-related immune dysregulation features between NDs and other systemic autoimmune diseases (e.g., systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), type 1 diabetes (T1D)). This review aims to construct a cross-disease framework for the precision management of NDs in the aging era, identify research gaps and future directions, and emphasize age-adapted intervention strategies for optimizing the prognosis of elderly ND patients.

articles.title: Prophylactic dexamethasone for prevention of opioid-induced nausea and vomiting in cancer patients: a randomised controlled trial (DEX-OINV Trial).
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Opioid-induced nausea and vomiting (OINV) is a common, distressing complication when starting opioids in cancer patients, yet evidence for prophylaxis is limited, and no randomised trial has evaluated dexamethasone in this setting. We assessed whether prophylactic dexamethasone reduces nausea and vomiting following initiation of oral morphine in opioid-naïve cancer patients.

METHODS: In this open-label, randomised controlled trial at a tertiary cancer centre, opioid-naïve adults initiating oral morphine were randomised 1:1 to prophylactic oral dexamethasone or no prophylaxis. Rescue antiemetics were given in both arms. The primary outcome was nausea severity on an 11-point numerical rating scale (NRS) at Days 1, 3 and 5. Secondary outcomes were vomiting episodes and rescue antiemetic use. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle, with multivariable logistic regression adjusting for clinical covariates.

RESULTS: Of 180 patients screened, 150 were randomised (dexamethasone n = 74; control n = 76). Mean nausea severity was lower with dexamethasone at all timepoints (Day 1: 1.36 vs 2.93; Day 5: 0.74 vs 1.53; both p ≤ 0.01), with a number needed to treat of 5 on Day 1 to prevent one episode of clinically meaningful nausea (NRS ≥ 4). The benefit persisted after adjustment (Day 1 aOR 0.38, 95% CI 0.19-0.75). Vomiting episodes were significantly reduced on Day 1. No serious adverse events occurred, and no patient discontinued treatment because of an adverse event.

CONCLUSION: Prophylactic dexamethasone was associated with lower nausea severity during the critical early period of oral morphine initiation and was well tolerated. Dexamethasone is a widely available and inexpensive agent that warrants confirmation in larger multicentre trials.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: CTRI/2026/02/104005, prospectively registered on 16 February 2026.

articles.title: Characterization of N-glycosylation remodeling in cerebrospinal fluid extracellular vesicles in children with purulent meningitis and viral meningitis: an exploratory glycomics study based on MALDI-TOF/TOF-MS.
articles.abstract: To investigate differences in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) N-glycosylation profiles among children with purulent meningitis (PM), viral meningitis (VM), and disease controls (DC). This retrospective exploratory study included six children with PM, three with VM, and three children with leukemia in complete remission without central nervous system infection. CSF-derived extracellular vesicles(CSF-EVs)were characterized by transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis, and Western blotting. N-glycans were released using PNGase F, purified by porous graphitized carbon solid-phase extraction, and analyzed by matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry. Fifteen derived glycan traits were quantified. Group differences were assessed using Kruskal-Wallis tests with pairwise comparisons, and associations with clinical inflammatory markers were evaluated using Spearman correlation. CSF N-glycan profiles showed distinct patterns across the three groups. Hierarchical clustering based on glycan traits separated PM, VM, and DC samples. Compared with DC, both PM and VM showed altered sialylation, but their remodeling patterns differed. PM showed increased highly sialylated glycan traits, whereas VM showed increased disialylation and reduced galactosylation- and core fucosylation-associated traits. Bisecting GlcNAc-related traits were reduced in both infection groups. Total bisecting GlcNAc (B Total) was positively correlated with serum procalcitonin (PCT) levels (r = 0.681, P = 0.015). Pediatric CNS infections were associated with distinct CSF N-glycan remodeling patterns. These findings provide preliminary evidence of infection-associated glycosylation alterations and support further validation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of perioperative dexmedetomidine in nephrectomy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dexmedetomidine is a highly selective α2-adrenergic receptor agonist with sedative, analgesic, and sympatholytic effects. The use of dexmedetomidine during nephrectomy has been investigated in several randomized controlled trials, although the findings remain inconsistent.

AIMS: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluate the efficacy and safety of perioperative dexmedetomidine administration in patients undergoing nephrectomy.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library from inception to November 2025. Randomized controlled trials and observational studies comparing dexmedetomidine versus control in patients undergoing nephrectomy were included. Primary outcomes included acute kidney injury (AKI) incidence, renal replacement therapy, Cystatin C, and serum creatinine. Meta-analysis was performed using RevMan software with random-effects models.

RESULTS: Eight studies (n = 1140) were included. Systemic intravenous dexmedetomidine did not significantly reduce AKI incidence (RR 1.08, 95% CI [0.85, 1.38]) but significantly reduced postoperative pain scores at day 1 (SMD - 0.37, P < 0.01) and day 2 (SMD - 0.27, P = 0.008), and postoperative nausea and vomiting (RR 0.66, 95% CI [0.44, 0.99]). Regional/neuraxial adjuvant use showed superior analgesia and possible renal-protective effects.

CONCLUSION: Dexmedetomidine provides significant analgesic benefits without reducing clinically defined AKI. Its use as a regional adjuvant warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Long COVID: A Modified Delphi Consensus on Definition, Burden, Diagnosis and Management in Southeast Asia.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Long COVID is a heterogeneous post-infectious condition following acute severe acute respiratory syndrome-coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection. Ongoing uncertainty around its definition, burden, diagnosis and management complicates clinical recognition and care in Southeast Asia.

METHODS: A modified Delphi consensus study was conducted with twelve experts from six Southeast Asian countries to develop regional guidance on long COVID. Consensus was predefined as ≥ 80% agreement, corresponding to at least 10 of 12 experts selecting the same response in multiple-choice questions or indicating agreement on Likert-scale questions (e.g. agree/strongly agree, most important/more important, relevant/highly relevant). Questions that reached consensus were removed from the subsequent round, while unresolved questions were revised, consolidated, or expanded. In the final round, a post hoc descriptive category, 'moderate endorsement', was applied to Likert-scale questions that had not reached consensus, with 'important' as the midpoint category of the five-point importance scale ('most important' to 'least important'), to capture responses judged important but falling short of the consensus threshold.

RESULTS: Consensus was reached for all 'definition', 'burden' and 'management' theme questions and most 'diagnosis' questions. Experts defined long COVID as unexplained symptoms persisting for > 3 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection, distinct from post-acute COVID-19, with no minimum severity threshold requirement. Long COVID was recognised as affecting approximately 6%-10% of individuals after SARS-CoV-2 infection, consistent with published WHO and KSID estimates; clinical evaluation and symptom-guided testing were recommended for its diagnosis. Hospitalisation during acute COVID-19 was identified as a risk factor for developing long COVID. The experts recommended multidisciplinary, symptom-directed care, rehabilitation, pacing and follow-up. Vaccination and reinfection prevention were supported as important long COVID risk-reduction strategies, and early antiviral treatment should be considered to prevent severe acute illness and hospitalisation in high-risk individuals. Consensus was not reached on the past medical history required for diagnosis; moderate endorsement was observed for booster status, absence of early antiviral treatment, pre-COVID health assessment and standardised patient-reported outcome tools.

CONCLUSION: This Delphi study provides a practical regional consensus framework for long COVID in Southeast Asia.

articles.title: Contemporary Inhaled Maintenance Therapy Patterns and Treatment Progression for Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) in the United States: Findings from the DUALITY Patient Journey Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Inhaled maintenance therapy (long-acting β2-agonists [LABA], long-acting muscarinic antagonists [LAMA], and inhaled corticosteroids [ICS], used alone or in combination) is the cornerstone of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) management. This study described contemporary real-world COPD treatment patterns in the USA.

METHODS: Retrospective data for patients aged ≥ 40 years with COPD were obtained from Komodo Research Data (01/01/2016-06/30/2024). The index date was January 1, 2022 for patients with a prior COPD diagnosis (i.e., prevalent patients) or the first observed COPD diagnosis for incident patients. Continuous health insurance enrollment was required for ≥ 12 months pre-index (i.e., baseline) and ≥ 6 months post-index, unless death occurred (i.e., follow-up). A claims-based algorithm identified lines of therapy for inhaled maintenance treatments. Treatment patterns were described during follow-up, overall and among subgroups of interest, including at-risk patients (i.e., ≥ 1 severe or ≥ 2 moderate exacerbations during baseline).

RESULTS: A total of 1,421,278 patients with COPD were identified (incident 153,390; prevalent 1,267,888). Over a mean follow-up of 16.6 and 24.7 months, 33.0% and 51.2% of patients with incident or prevalent COPD, respectively, received inhaled maintenance therapy. Dual therapy was the most common treatment class (20.2%, 32.5%), driven by ICS/LABA use, followed by triple therapy (12.5%, 22.5%), and monotherapy (7.6%, 12.0%). Among at-risk patients, only 58.8% received any inhaled maintenance therapy (dual therapy 37.0%, triple therapy 27.8%, monotherapy 13.2%).

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world study, there was unmet need across the COPD journey, evidenced by low uptake of inhaled maintenance therapy, including among those with a history of exacerbations. Maintenance therapy regimens were not fully aligned with Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Diseases recommended treatment, and persistence to triple therapy was limited. Further research is warranted to understand barriers to timely treatment initiation, optimize escalation and persistence, and identify patients with unmet need despite inhaled maintenance therapy.

articles.title: The role of capybaras (Hydrochoerus hydrochaeris) as hosts for hemoplasmas in an urban park of Brazilian Midwest.
articles.abstract: Hemoplasmas (hemotropic mycoplasmas) are Gram-negative bacteria that bind to the surface of red blood cells of mammals and may cause hematological alterations in the infected host, and in urban environments, wildlife species may act as important reservoirs of these agents. The study aimed to evaluate, through molecular analysis, the infection of hemoplasmas in capybaras from the Parque das Nações Indígenas, Campo Grande, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil. Additionally, we evaluated the health status of infected and non-infected capybaras by haematological parameters. The results of PCR assays based on the 16 S rRNA gene confirmed the presence of hemoplasmas in 84.6% (55/65) of the samples. Phylogenetic inferences based on 16 S and 23 S rRNA genes positioned the sequences into the ´Candidatus Mycoplasma haematohydrochoerus´ clade. The findings suggest that the high prevalence, low genetic variability, and unchanged hematological parameters may indicate host tolerance or adaptation to 'Ca. M. haematohydrochoerus' infection.

articles.title: To cradle or not: assessing the use of a lumbar puncture cradle on lumbar puncture success rates.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Neonatal and infant lumbar puncture success rates range from 50 to 80%, while traumatic lumbar punctures are reported in 30-50%. A novel lumbar puncture cradle, SMöLTAP®, designed to standardize seated positioning may improve procedural outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate the first-pass success and traumatic lumbar puncture rates using the cradle compared to the lateral decubitus.

METHODS: This was a single-center cohort study from August 2020-October 2024 in a tertiary pediatric emergency department. Term and corrected preterm infants (≥ 37 weeks, ≤ 3 months) requiring a lumbar puncture were identified through an EPIC report. Unstable infants, those requiring opening pressure, performed under sedation or using ultrasound guidance, and charts with missing documentation were excluded. Lumbar punctures using the cradle were identified first, and a stratified random sampling technique was used to select the non-exposed cohort, in which lumbar punctures were performed in the lateral decubitus position. Chi-square analysis and logistic regression were used to analyze lumbar puncture success rates.

RESULTS: 142 infants were included (mean age 26 days, 57% male). Cradle use was associated with a higher first-pass success rate: 63%, as opposed to 41% in the control lateral decubitus group p = 0.01. It remained significantly associated with first-pass success after a multivariable logistic regression (OR 2.23, 95% CI 1.06-4.68, p = 0.03). Cradle use was associated with fewer traumatic lumbar punctures, 36% versus 59% (p = 0.01), percent difference 23% (95% CI 6.6-37.8). There was no difference in the overall success rate, 80% versus 70%, p = 0.17.

CONCLUSION: The cradle is a promising tool that may improve first-pass success, reduce traumatic lumbar punctures, and provide more precise management of febrile infants requiring a lumbar puncture, thereby reducing clinical diagnostic and management challenges.

articles.title: Emergency medicine: the failed experiment.

Antibacterial and pro-osteointegrative bioactive coatings on titanium implant surfaces for oromaxillofacial applications: a systematic review and bayesian network meta-analysis of preclinical studies.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Numerous preclinical studies have investigated bioactive coatings on titanium implant surfaces to enhance antibacterial and osteointegrative performance in oromaxillofacial applications. However, these studies employ heterogeneous experimental methods and biological outcomes, making it difficult to identify which coating strategies hold the greatest translational potential. This systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis (NMA) aimed to rank titanium coating strategies published over the last five years according to their biological performance, using a quantitative statistical framework.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Nine coating categories of increasing compositional complexity, ranging from single-component (inorganic, organic, peptides/growth factors) to two-component and three-component formulations combining these classes with each other or with antibiotics, were compared across six biological outcomes in preclinical models. Inclusion criteria followed the PICOS framework for studies published between 2020 and 2025. Three databases were searched according to PRISMA 2020 and its NMA extension. Mean difference (MD) was used for outcomes on a common scale; ratio of means (RoM) when measurement units were heterogeneous. Treatment ranking was estimated using the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA). Study reporting quality and data completeness were assessed, and studies with insufficient quantitative data were excluded from the quantitative synthesis.

RESULTS: Of 143 records identified, 59 met the inclusion criteria and 40 contributed to the quantitative synthesis. SUCRA rankings indicated that three-component hybrid coatings incorporating antibiotics achieved the highest antibacterial performance and osseointegration, while inorganic coatings functionalized with peptides or growth factors demonstrated superior osteogenic differentiation. Organic coatings combined with peptides or growth factors showed the greatest cell proliferation.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide the first evidence-based ranking of bioactive coating strategies for titanium implant surfaces, suggesting a potential advantage of multi-component formulations over single-agent approaches across biological outcomes.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The identified compositional complexity gradient may inform the rational design of future multifunctional coatings and help prioritize candidates for further preclinical and translational validation in oromaxillofacial applications.

articles.title: Retinal and choroidal changes on optical coherence tomography in pre-eclampsia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To summarize optical coherence tomography (OCT)-detected retinal and choroidal changes in pre-eclampsia (PE), to support clinicians in interpreting these changes within the clinical context.

METHODS: We systematically searched four databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus) through February 2025 to identify observational studies comparing OCT metrics in PE versus control groups. Pooled mean differences (MD) and standardized mean differences (SMD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using random-effects models. Between-study heterogeneity was quantified with the I2 statistic and its sources explored by meta-regression and by subgroup analysis (PE severity, presence of retinal changes, risk of bias, OCT device, eye-selection method, and country); for each subgroup analysis the residual I2 was compared with the I2 of the corresponding overall analysis. Risk of bias was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) checklist.

RESULTS: Fifteen studies with 854 eyes from women with PE, 631 eyes from women with normal pregnancy (NP), and 245 eyes from non-pregnant controls (NC) were included. Compared with NP, PE was significantly associated with reduced peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer (p-RNFL) thickness (SMD: - 0.13, 95% CI: - 0.20 to - 0.06, P = 0.01, I2 = 0%). No statistically significant differences were observed for subfoveal choroidal thickness (SFCT; pre- and post-partum), nasal and temporal choroidal thickness, or central subfield macular thickness (CSMT) in the primary pooled analyses, most of which demonstrated substantial to considerable heterogeneity (I2 up to 94%). Exploratory subgroup analysis suggested that pathological retinal changes and PE severity partially (I2 reduction = 40%) or fully (I2 reduction = 92%) accounted for heterogeneity in pre-partum SFCT estimates.

CONCLUSION: The p-RNFL thickness is subtly reduced in PE compared to NP, representing subclinical structural change. While primary analyses found no significant choroidal or macular differences, subgroup analyses suggest a potential increase in SFCT in severe PE or in the presence of retinal pathology, warranting further investigation.

articles.title: Effects of nutrition counseling on quality of life in adults with cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Cancer and its treatments can often reduce patients' quality of life (QoL). Nutrition counseling, as a potential adjunctive intervention, may promote dietary behavior change and alleviate treatment-related burdens. However, the existing evidence regarding its effectiveness in improving QoL among adults with cancer remains inconclusive. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of nutrition counseling on QoL in adults with cancer.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Scopus, and the ClinicalTrials.gov registry from inception to August 23, 2026. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials evaluating the effects of nutrition counseling on QoL in adults with cancer. Effect sizes were estimated as standardized mean differences (SMDs) using Hedges' g with small-sample correction and pooled using a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model to obtain summary estimates with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Sensitivity analyses and subgroup analyses were also conducted to assess the robustness of the pooled estimates and explore potential sources of heterogeneity.

RESULTS: A total of 20 trials involving 1,668 participants were included in the review, with 1,301 participants contributing post-intervention QoL data to the meta-analysis. The pooled effect of nutrition counseling on QoL was SMD = 0.71 (95% CI: 0.35-1.07; p < 0.001), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 88.7%; τ² = 0.587). The 95% prediction interval ranged from - 0.94 to 2.36, indicating that the magnitude and consistency of effects may vary across settings. Subgroup analyses showed higher pooled effect estimates in studies conducted in Asia (SMD = 1.42; 95% CI: 0.70-2.15; p < 0.001), developing countries (SMD = 1.57; 95% CI: 0.75-2.38; p < 0.001), and Eastern cultural backgrounds (SMD = 1.42; 95% CI: 0.70-2.15; p < 0.001), and among studies with a mean baseline BMI < 25 kg/m2 (SMD = 0.84; 95% CI: 0.38-1.30; p < 0.001). A post hoc subgroup analysis showed a higher pooled effect estimate among studies with a study-level mean participant age ≥ 65 years (SMD = 1.33; 95% CI: 0.48-2.19; p for subgroup differences = 0.038). The certainty of evidence was rated as very low according to the GRADE approach.

CONCLUSIONS: Nutrition counseling may improve QoL among adults with cancer, but the very low certainty of evidence and substantial heterogeneity limit confidence in the magnitude and consistency of this effect. Future high-quality studies are warranted to confirm these findings and clarify how clinical and contextual factors influence the effectiveness of nutrition counseling. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW​ REGISTRATION: PROSPERO registration no. CRD420251165789.

articles.title: Postoperative Adverse Events Following Concurrent Midurethral Sling and OnabotulinumtoxinA for Mixed Urinary Incontinence.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: For mixed urinary incontinence, concomitant midurethral sling (MUS) and onabotulinumtoxinA (Botox® (BTX-A)) can be considered, but data regarding safety are sparse. Adverse event rates following combined MUS + BTX-A are hypothesized to be similar to those following MUS alone.

METHODS: This was a retrospective matched cohort study comparing adverse events in patients with mixed incontinence undergoing MUS (n = 200) versus combined MUS + BTX-A (n = 100) between January 1, 2011, and March 31, 2024. The primary outcome was culture proven urinary tract infection (UTI) at 3 and 6 months. Secondary outcomes included any UTI (culture proven or empirically treated), urinary retention, and postoperative overactive bladder (OAB) treatment. Logistic regression was used to assess the impact of baseline variables on outcomes.

RESULTS: Patients undergoing concurrent MUS + BTX-A were more likely to have prior stress incontinence surgery, OAB treatment, and postoperative prophylactic antibiotic use. Culture-proven UTI occurred more frequently in the MUS + BTX-A group at 3 months (23.0% vs 12.5%) and 6 months (25.0% vs 15.0%) on unadjusted analysis. After adjustment for measured covariates, the association was attenuated and not statistically significant at 3 months (adjusted OR 1.60, 95% CI 0.78-3.30) or 6 months (adjusted OR 1.47, 95% CI 0.75-2.91). Rates of retention-related events and subsequent OAB treatment were similar between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Concurrent MUS + BTX-A was associated with higher crude of culture-proven UTI, although adjusted analyses did not demonstrate a statistically significant association. Larger studies are needed to better define the safety of concurrent treatment.

articles.title: Pediatric Bow Hunter syndrome: clinical, vascular, and longitudinal findings from a single center and systematic review of the literature.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Bow Hunter syndrome (BHS) is a rare cause of pediatric vertebral artery dissection (VAD) and posterior circulation arterial ischemic stroke (AIS) due to dynamic compression during head rotation. Imaging features, vascular evolution, and outcomes remain poorly defined.

METHODS: We reviewed children with definite or probable BHS diagnosed at a tertiary pediatric center between 2010 and 2026. A systematic review identified published pediatric cases (0-18 years) of definite/probable BHS.

RESULTS: Twelve boys were included (mean age, 7.3 years; mean follow-up, 54.4 months). Posterior circulation AIS occurred in 10/12 (83.3%), with multifocal infarcts of different ages in eight and additional anterior circulation embolic infarcts in three. VAD was bilateral in 6/12 (50%), consistently involving V3. Distal posterior cerebral and/or superior cerebellar artery stenosis or occlusion with collateral networks occurred in 7/12 (58.3%); basilar artery involvement in 4/12. Dynamic vascular imaging demonstrated position-dependent vertebral artery compromise in 9/12 patients (eight by rotational DSA and one by Doppler ultrasound). Craniocervical junction variants were present in 10/12 (83.3%), without flexion-extension instability. Early recurrent AIS occurred in 5/10 despite antithrombotic therapy. Serial imaging showed early vascular evolution followed by stabilization. Two patients underwent surgery; the others were treated conservatively.

CONCLUSIONS: A rotational mechanical mechanism should be considered in children with posterior circulation AIS and V3 abnormalities, particularly when preceded by overlooked prodromal symptoms or minor trauma- and sport-related triggers. Multimodal neurovascular imaging, especially dynamic angiography, is essential for diagnosis, surveillance, and individualized treatment planning aimed at preventing further vascular injury.

articles.title: Impact of [18F]fluoroestradiol PET/CT on clinical management in patients with estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To systematically review the literature and perform a meta-analysis on the proportion of clinical management changes from [18F]fluoroestradiol ([18F]FES) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) in patients with estrogen receptor (ER)-positive breast cancer.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Systematic review and meta-analysis conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. The study protocol was registered in the Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420261373183). MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane databases were searched until March 2026. Studies were selected using criteria based on participant, index test, and target condition framework: patients with ER-positive breast cancer, index test was [18F]FES PET/CT, and target condition was the change in management following [18F]FES PET/CT compared with conventional workup. Pooled proportions of management changes were calculated across the included studies, including subgroup and sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: Ten studies involving 773 patients were included. The pooled proportion of management changes following [18F]FES PET/CT was 38% (95% confidence interval (CI): 31-45%). Subgroup analyses showed the following: 17% (95% CI: 11-27%) for intramodality changes and 10% (95% CI: 5-21%) for intermodality changes; 17% (95% CI: 8-31%) for changes from endocrine therapy (ET) to non-ET and 12% (95% CI: 8-17%) from non-ET to ET; 6% (95% CI: 1-38%) for avoidance of additional workup and 6% (95% CI: 1-34%) prompting additional workup. Even in patients without management change, [18F]FES PET/CT was beneficial in 39% (95% CI: 24-58%) by improving diagnostic certainty and supporting current treatment options.

CONCLUSION: [18F]FES PET/CT impacted management in 38% of patients with ER-positive breast cancer.

KEY POINTS: Question What proportion of patients with estrogen receptor (ER)-positive breast cancer have their clinical management influenced by the results of [18F]fluoroestradiol PET/CT? Findings [18F]fluoroestradiol PET/CT impacted management in 38% of patients with ER-positive breast cancer, including inter-/intramodality changes, switches to/away from endocrine therapy, and additional diagnostic workup avoided/added. Clinical relevance [18F]fluoroestradiol PET/CT had a substantial impact on the management of patients with ER-positive breast cancer.
