Ultrasound-derived fat fraction and shear wave elastography for liver assessment in bariatric surgery candidates: diagnostic performance and longitudinal changes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of ultrasound-derived fat fraction (UDFF) and auto-point shear wave elastography (Auto-pSWE) in bariatric surgery candidates, identify biological variables independently associated with their values and monitor postoperative changes in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) patients.

METHODS: This prospective study enrolled patients who underwent UDFF and Auto-pSWE examinations within 3 days before bariatric surgery (October 2023-February 2025), with intraoperative biopsy as reference. Diagnostic performance of UDFF and Auto-pSWE (which measured shear wave velocity, SWV) were analyzed by receiver operating characteristic analysis. Multivariable generalized linear models identified variables independently associated with UDFF and SWV. Postoperative follow-ups were conducted at 3 and 6 months in MASLD patients.

RESULTS: A total of 237 patients (mean age, 29.42 ± 9.37; 98 men) were included. UDFF showed excellent diagnostic performance for steatosis grades (AUCs: 0.991 for ≥S1, 0.911 for ≥S2, and 0.831 for ≥S3), with steatosis percentage as the strongest independent correlate (partial R2=0.302). SWV exhibited moderate diagnostic performance for significant fibrosis (AUC = 0.752), with fibrosis stages and alanine aminotransferase showing similar independent explanatory power (partial R2=0.067 and 0.063, respectively). In 104 MASLD patients, median UDFF decreased substantially by approximately 80% at 6 months while SWV transiently rose at 3 months before returning to a level comparable to baseline at 6 months.

CONCLUSION: UDFF provides accurate assessment of steatosis and shows potential for postoperative monitoring, whereas Auto-pSWE demonstrates moderate performance for significant fibrosis and transient postoperative changes, supporting its complementary rather than standalone role.

articles.title: Paraphyton cookei as a cause of dermatophytosis in calves.
articles.abstract: Dermatophytosis is a contagious and zoonotic superficial fungal infection affecting various animal species. In cattle production, ringworm has huge sanitary and economic relevance. Although Trichophyton verrucosum is the main etiological agent of bovine dermatophytosis, infections caused by other dermatophyte species may occasionally occur. This study reports an outbreak of dermatophytosis in calves caused by the geophilic dermatophyte Paraphyton cookei in southern Brazil. The outbreak occurred on a beef cattle farm in the state of Rio Grande do Sul during the spring. Of the 360 cattle in the herd, 120 were calves aged 60-90 days, of which 30 exhibited skin lesions characterized by irregular areas of alopecia of varying sizes, accompanied by small crusts and distributed across multiple body regions. Hair and crust samples were collected for mycological examination. Fungal culture produced colonies with macroscopic and microscopic characteristics consistent with P. cookei. The identification was further confirmed by sequencing of the internal transcribed spacer region of rDNA. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of dermatophytosis in calves caused by P. cookei. These findings highlight the importance of considering geophilic dermatophytes in the differential diagnosis of bovine dermatophytosis and reinforce the relevance of laboratory identification methods for accurate etiological diagnosis and epidemiological surveillance.

articles.title: Antibiotic Exposure and Treatment Outcomes in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma and Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Systemic antibiotics may disrupt the gut and oral microbiome, potentially affecting anticancer treatment efficacy. Their prognostic relevance in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), particularly during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based therapy or definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT), remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated associations between systemic antibiotic exposure around treatment initiation and oncologic outcomes.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched from January 2015 to March 28, 2026. Eligible studies included patients with HNSCC or NPC receiving ICI, definitive CRT, or chemo-immunotherapy and reporting overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), or objective response rate (ORR). Random-effects models pooled hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for OS and PFS; ORR was synthesized descriptively. Risk of bias was assessed, as appropriate, using ROBINS-I, ROBINS-E, RoB 2, or the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale.

RESULTS: Eleven studies involving 6,293 patients were included; nine studies (4,507 patients) contributed to survival meta-analyses. Antibiotic exposure was associated with worse OS (HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.52-2.08) and PFS (HR 1.58, 95% CI 1.28-1.96). Associations were consistent in ICI-treated cohorts (OS HR 1.80, 95% CI 1.53-2.13; PFS HR 1.67, 95% CI 1.24-2.25) and CRT cohorts (OS HR 1.73, 95% CI 1.29-2.32; PFS HR 1.53, 95% CI 1.11-2.11). Heterogeneity was low-to-moderate for OS (I2=28.6%) and negligible for PFS (I2=0%). Leave-one-out analyses showed stable OS (HR range 1.76-1.86) and PFS estimates (1.58-1.63). Worse OS was observed for both 30-60-day pre-ICI exposure (HR 2.04, 95% CI 1.43-2.90) and concurrent/peri-treatment exposure (HR 1.74, 95% CI 1.49-2.04). ORR was descriptively lower in antibiotic-exposed patients. Most studies had serious/high risk of bias, primarily due to confounding by indication.

CONCLUSIONS: Systemic antibiotic exposure around treatment initiation is associated with inferior survival and response in HNSCC and NPC. However, predominantly observational evidence and substantial confounding preclude causal inference. Prospective microbiome-informed studies are needed.

articles.title: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 2 in a North Indian endogamous community: clinical and genetic insights from multigenerational families.
articles.abstract: Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 2 (SCA2) is an autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder caused by CAG repeat expansion in the ATXN2 gene. Endogamous populations may exhibit clustering of inherited disorders because of founder effects and restricted gene flow. This study aimed to characterize the clinical and genetic features of SCA2 in multigenerational Banjara families from North India. A total of 141 individuals from 23 multigenerational Banjara families were clinically evaluated. 55 clinically affected individuals and at-risk family members underwent molecular testing for ATXN2 CAG repeat expansions using flanking PCR followed by capillary electrophoresis. Clinical characteristics were summarized using descriptive statistics, and the relationship between CAG repeat length and age at onset was assessed by linear regression. Pathogenic ATXN2 CAG repeat expansions were identified in 39 of the 55 individuals who underwent genetic testing (70.9%), including 32 symptomatic individuals and seven asymptomatic carriers. The expanded alleles ranged from 33 to 48 CAG repeats (mean 41.6 ± 3.3). Gait ataxia was the most common presenting symptom. A significant inverse correlation was observed between CAG repeat length and age at onset (R² = 0.71, P < 0.0001). In this study, we found SCA2 across multiple multigenerational Banjara families from North India. The inverse relationship between ATXN2 CAG repeat length and age at onset was also observed in our cohort. The presence of asymptomatic carriers highlights the importance of early molecular diagnosis, family-based genetic counselling, and targeted screening in high-risk families.

articles.title: Public Participation in U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Advisory Committees: A Qualitative Analysis.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: The FDA frequently solicits public input to inform advisory committee meetings reviewing new drug applications. Although intended to enhance transparency and incorporate patient perspectives, the content of these submissions has not been well described.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize public comments to FDA advisory committee meetings and examine the values and considerations expressed.

DESIGN: Qualitative study using inductive content analysis with an iterative coding framework. Comments were coded by one reviewer and independently double-coded for a random subset; disagreements were resolved through discussion (Light's kappa = 0.81).

SETTING: Public comments associated with FDA advisory committee meetings for five new drug applications reviewed between January 2020 and December 2024.

PARTICIPANTS: A random sample of 600 public comments from the five products with the highest public engagement: (1) sodium phenylbutyrate-taurursodiol for ALS; (2) teplizumab for type 1 diabetes; (3) midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) for PTSD; (4) delandistrogene moxeparvovec for Duchenne muscular dystrophy; and (5) eflornithine tablets for pediatric neuroblastoma.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Stakeholder role, stance regarding drug approval, and thematic content.

RESULTS: Submissions were most commonly from caregivers or immediate family members (31.5%), individuals without disclosed roles (20.0%), friends or extended family (18.5%), and patients (17.2%). Most comments supported approval (90.2%), with few neutral (7.8%) or opposing (1.3%) views. Four themes emerged: (1) experiential considerations; (2) evidentiary considerations, including clinical trial data and personal observations; (3) regulatory and policy considerations, such as urgency of access; and (4) values-based considerations, such as therapeutic hope and autonomy.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Public comments were overwhelmingly supportive of approval, reflecting experiential, evidentiary, policy, and values-based considerations. Strengthening mechanisms for synthesizing public input may enhance transparency and confidence in the FDA regulatory process.

articles.title: GLP-1 receptor agonist use in patients with minor stroke is associated with lower risk of post-stroke dementia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Minor ischemic stroke is associated with increased risks of post-stroke dementia independent of stroke recurrence, yet there are no guideline-recommended therapies targeted at cognitive outcomes. Glucagon-like peptide - 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have been shown to be associated with lower risk of dementia among diabetes patients; however, their effect on cognitive outcomes among minor stroke patients is largely unknown.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used de-identified electronic health record data from the TriNetX US Collaborative Network (2016-2025). Adult patients with minor ischemic stroke (NIHSS ≤ 5 and non-disabling) were included. Patients with prior intracranial hemorrhage, mood disorders, anxiety disorders, cognitive impairment, or dementia were excluded. GLP-1RA use was defined as a prescription prior to or within 3 months of stroke diagnosis. After 1:1 propensity score matching on 75 baseline characteristics, outcomes were assessed over a 5 year follow-up using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: After propensity score matching, 1,425 patients per group were analyzed. Mean age was 60.7 years, with diabetes present in 92.7% and mean HbA1c of 8.7%. GLP-1RA use was associated with a 48% lower hazard of post-stroke dementia (3.4% vs. 7.0%, HR 0.52 [95% CI 0.37-0.74]) and a 31% lower hazard of other neurocognitive complaints (17.2% vs 25.6%, HR 0.69 [95% CI 0.59-0.81]) over 5 years. GLP-1RA use was also associated with reduced mortality (4.4% vs. 8.8%; HR 0.57 [95% CI 0.42-0.77]) and major ischemic stroke (1.5% vs. 2.7%; HR 0.59 [95% CI 0.35-1.01]). No significant difference in intracranial hemorrhage rates was observed.

CONCLUSIONS: Among this cohort of minor ischemic stroke patients mostly with concomitant diabetes, GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly reduced risks of post-stroke dementia and other neurocognitive complaints. These findings support prioritizing GLP-1RA use for diabetic patients who suffered minor ischemic stroke. Prospective trials are warranted to confirm causality and determine optimal implementation.

articles.title: Human‑Scale Lymphatic Modeling to Guide Lymphatic Interventions: Application to a Soft Robotic Assist Device.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The lymphatic system is essential for maintaining tissue-fluid homeostasis. In conditions of elevated venous pressures (e.g., congestive heart failure or congenital single-ventricle heart disease after Fontan palliation), increased capillary filtration and impaired lymphatic drainage disrupt this balance, predisposing patients to lymphatic overload and edema. The lack of human-scale computational models capturing lymphatic pumping and coupled tissue-fluid exchange limits the development of effective interventions.

METHODS: We developed a human-scale lumped-parameter model that combines multi-lymphangion thoracic duct pumping with a Starling-based tissue-fluid balance model, enabling integrated simulation of central lymphatic function and tissue-fluid homeostasis. The framework was used to evaluate surgical and device-based lymphatic interventions. Model predictions were combined with virtual fitting using MR-derived anatomy from three Fontan patients to demonstrate translational applicability and design an extravascular soft robotic lymphatic assist sleeve, whose performance was characterized in hydraulic benchtop experiments.

RESULTS: The model reproduced physiologic thoracic duct flow (~3.1L/day) and predicted interstitial fluid accumulation under venous hypertension (up to ~ 18 mL/min net accumulation). Surgical (lymphatic decompression) and device-based (extravascular sleeve) interventions increased thoracic duct flow and reduced simulated tissue-fluid accumulation (47% and 76.5% reduction, respectively), with the sleeve providing frequency-dependent augmentation. Virtual fitting confirmed anatomical feasibility of device implantation in all three Fontan patients. Benchtop testing demonstrated pressure step-ups from 5.5 to ~ 17 mmHg and flow augmentation from 2.5 to ~ 18 mL/min at actuation frequencies of 20-60 bpm.

CONCLUSION: Our human-scale computational framework offers mechanistic insights into lymphatic dysfunction under elevated venous pressure and provides a platform for the design and evaluation of lymphatic interventions.

articles.title: Age-structured HPV dynamics under randomly switching epidemiological regimes.
articles.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a common sexually transmitted infection whose transmission and disease progression depend strongly on age and are shaped by prevention strategies such as vaccination and screening. Temporal changes in transmission conditions, contact patterns, and healthcare conditions may induce epidemiological regimes that switch over time, making it difficult to characterize long-term transmission and invasion thresholds. We study an age-structured model for HPV transmission in a randomly fluctuating epidemiological environment, where temporal variability in epidemiological conditions is represented by a finite-state continuous-time Markov chain, while vaccination is assumed to remain fixed across regimes. Each regime is governed by a deterministic age-structured system. Using semigroup methods, we characterize the invasion threshold of the randomly switching system, relate it to the reproduction numbers of the regime-specific models, and derive fast- and slow-switching limits. We further establish exponential extinction of the infected population in mean and almost surely when the random reproduction number is below one, while above the threshold we obtain instability of the linearized first-moment dynamics. Our results provide a rigorous mathematical framework for understanding HPV dynamics under temporally varying epidemiological conditions.

articles.title: Mitochondrial translation deficiency limits the cardiac benefit of ketogenic diet in early-onset cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract: Mitochondrial cardiomyopathy is a devastating disorder with no effective treatment. Ketogenic diet (KD) has shown therapeutic benefit in some mitochondrial disease models but failed or caused harm in others, suggesting its efficacy depends on the underlying genetic defect. KD has ameliorated cardiomyopathy in models where the electron transport chain retains structural integrity, yet it has not been tested in a model with a primary defect in mitochondrial translation. We therefore examined KD in heart- and skeletal muscle-specific Dars2 knockout mice (hmKO), a model of fatal early-onset mitochondrial cardiomyopathy caused by loss of mitochondrial aspartyl-tRNA synthetase, which is essential for translation of all 13 mitochondrial DNA-encoded oxidative phosphorylation subunits. Male hmKO mice and wild type littermates received either a ketogenic or normal chow diet from weaning until the humane endpoint. KD induced a partial shift toward cardiac fatty acid metabolism and activated mitochondrial biogenesis signaling. However, these adaptations did not improve survival, cardiac hypertrophy, skeletal muscle atrophy, motor performance, respiratory chain complex abundance, enzyme activities, or cardiac ATP levels. KD reduced antioxidant gene expression, without increasing protein carbonylation, and amplified the mitokine response, with increased GDF15 and FGF21 in the heart and serum. These findings show that substrate availability alone cannot restore cardiac bioenergetics when mitochondrial translation capacity is severely impaired. Instead, mitochondrial translation machinery defines a critical boundary for metabolic interventions in mitochondrial cardiomyopathy. Our results argue that the therapeutic potential of KD in mitochondrial disease is mechanism-dependent and should not be generalized across genetically and bioenergetically distinct forms of mitochondrial cardiomyopathy.

articles.title: EMAIL-HF: Can Digital Strategies Shorten the Path from Scientific Evidence to Clinical Practice in Heart Failure?
articles.abstract: A substantial gap persists between scientific evidence and clinical practice in heart failure (HF). Digital solutions have emerged as promising strategies to accelerate the implementation of evidence-based therapies. This mini-review examines the results of the EMAIL-HF study, a registry-based, randomized, controlled, parallel-group clinical trial conducted in Denmark that included patients aged 20 years or older with a diagnosis of HF irrespective of left ventricular ejection fraction, who were not receiving SGLT2 inhibitors (SGLT2i). Participants were randomized to usual care or a digital strategy consisting of an e-mailed letter with information on SGLT2i, followed by contact with an HF specialist. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients redeeming a prescription for dapagliflozin or empagliflozin within 6 months of randomization and the secondary endpoint was a composite of time to first HF hospitalization or death from any cause. The digital strategy significantly increased SGLT2i initiation within 6 months, although no difference in HF hospitalization or all-cause mortality was observed during the 24-month follow-up. Whether these strategies can translate modest improvements in treatment uptake into sustained, scalable, and cost-effective gains across diverse healthcare systems remains uncertain.

articles.title: Criteria-led discharge in paediatric inpatient care in Switzerland: a quality improvement study of implementation, safety and satisfaction.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Paediatric hospitals have high admission rates and short lengths of stay, leading to a high turnover. The discharge process is challenged by delays and a lack of standardisation. Criteria-led discharge (CLD) has been proposed to overcome these challenges. CLD enables nursing staff to safely discharge patients once predefined clinical criteria are met, reducing reliance on physician review and minimising delays. We introduced CLD on a paediatric ward and evaluated its implementation in a quality improvement study pre- (December 2023-March 2024) and post-implementation (December 2024-March 2025). Outcomes were assessed using retrospective electronic health record data and surveys. The primary outcome was patient safety, measured by 14-day readmission and complication rates. Secondary outcomes included efficiency and patient flow, measured by length of stay, time of day at discharge and discharge delays, as well as patient, caregiver and staff satisfaction. A total of 355 eligible admissions (202 pre-, 153 post-implementation) were included into the analysis in three diagnostic groups: 122 bronchiolitis, 135 pneumonia and 98 asthma. 14-day readmission rates were comparable between CLD (3.2%), standard discharge (SD) (3.4%) and post-implementation SD (4.5%) cohorts. Patient, caregiver and staff satisfaction was high.

CONCLUSIONS: CLD is non-inferior in terms of safety compared to standard discharge. It subjectively improved discharge efficiency and positively impacted workload distribution while maintaining high patient, caregiver and staff satisfaction. CLD is a promising tool to facilitate discharges in paediatrics. Local adaptation and quality control are necessary for successful implementation.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Criteria-led discharge (CLD) increases standardisation, safety and efficiency in discharges from hospital.

WHAT IS NEW: • CLD is a safe method to discharge children from inpatient paediatric wards. • CLD may decrease stress of ward staff and enhance efficiency in paediatric hospitals.

articles.title: Vitamin D status and chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy in patients with cancer: a systematic review with exploratory quantitative synthesis.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is a clinically important toxicity of neurotoxic anticancer therapy. This review evaluated whether serum or plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D) status is associated with CIPN risk or severity in patients with cancer.

METHODS: The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261438011). PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from database inception through 23 June 2026. Eligible English-language human studies reported vitamin D status and CIPN-related outcomes during or after neurotoxic anticancer therapy. Vitamin D measurement timing was coded, risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-E, and adjusted and unadjusted estimates were synthesized separately. Two-study pooled models were prespecified as exploratory.

RESULTS: Fourteen records contributed evidence. Exploratory adjusted pooling for severe CIPN included two studies and showed a common-effect odds ratio (OR) of 1.81 (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.32-2.49; I2 92.4%); the random-effects OR was 2.94 (95% CI 0.63-13.73). Exploratory adjusted pooling for any CIPN included two studies and showed a common-effect OR of 2.76 (95% CI 1.70-4.48; I2 70.5%) and a random-effects OR of 3.36 (95% CI 1.20-9.43). Most evidence had high or very high risk of bias, and the pooled models should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory.

CONCLUSION: Low vitamin D status may be associated with greater CIPN risk or severity, particularly when measured before treatment or at baseline. The evidence remains hypothesis-generating because of small study numbers, heterogeneity, and risk of bias.

articles.title: Cerebral Blood Flow-Derived Myogenic Dynamics Reveal Impaired Postischemic Cerebrovascular Recovery in Experimental Stroke.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Restoration of cerebral blood flow (CBF) after ischemic stroke does not necessarily indicate recovery of cerebrovascular regulation. We tested whether myogenic-band dynamics derived directly from CBF signals provide information beyond mean perfusion during cerebral ischemia and after acute stroke.

METHODS: Transient focal cerebral ischemia was induced in 29 Sprague-Dawley rats using middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion. Bilateral laser-Doppler flowmetry (LDF)-derived CBF signals were decomposed using empirical mode decomposition and Hilbert transform, and myogenic-band activity (0.15-0.4 Hz) was quantified by absolute and relative power. Cross-validated logistic regression models were used to evaluate whether myogenic-band power provided discriminative information beyond mean CBF alone.

RESULTS: Ipsilateral mean CBF fell from 73.5±51.8 p.u. at baseline to 52.2±38.0 p.u. during late ischemia (P=0.0088), then increased to 126.6±91.5 p.u. after 3 hours of reperfusion (P=0.0050 versus baseline). Relative myogenic-band power decreased from 37.43±14.65% to 13.35±7.51% during ischemia (P<0.0001) and remained below baseline after reperfusion (20.74±12.02%, P=0.00033 versus baseline); contralateral relative power was comparatively preserved. Combining mean CBF and myogenic-band power improved discrimination of baseline from late ischemia (AUC, 0.99 versus 0.70 for mean CBF alone) and late reperfusion (AUC, 0.88 versus 0.70).

CONCLUSIONS: Frequency-specific analysis of LDF-derived CBF reveals persistent, lateralized abnormalities in myogenic-band dynamics that are not captured by mean perfusion alone. The persistence of depressed myogenic activity despite restored or elevated mean CBF demonstrates incomplete recovery of frequency-specific oscillatory dynamics after reperfusion. These findings support myogenic-band power as a potential functional measure of persistent postischemic cerebrovascular dysfunction.

articles.title: Corrigendum to 'Lung Cancer Screening in Asia: An Expert Consensus Report' [Journal of Thoracic Oncology Volume 18 Issue 10 (2023) 1303-1322].
articles.journal: Journal of thoracic oncology : official publication of the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer

articles.title: Development and Feasibility of In Situ Simulation for Pressure Injury Prevention in Intensive Care.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop, validate and test in situ simulation scenarios aimed at pressure injury (PI) prevention for nursing professionals working in an intensive care unit (ICU).

DESIGN: A multi-method study is planned across four phases.

METHODS: Conducted at a high-complexity Brazilian university hospital, this four-phase study: (1) development of simulation scenarios and checklists; (2) content validation by 11 experts (CVI/MKC); (3) pilot testing with 12 nursing professionals; and (4) ICU-based educational intervention. Scenarios were grounded in international guidelines and the NLN/Jeffries Simulation Theory. Feasibility was assessed via metrics of acceptability, appropriateness, adoption and fidelity.

RESULTS: Two evidence-based simulation scenarios and checklists were developed for registered nurses and nursing technicians, achieving high content validity among 11 experts. The in situ intervention reached 83% of the unit's nursing staff, demonstrating strong operational feasibility and acceptability. Beyond education, the scenarios served as a diagnostic tool, successfully identifying critical practice gaps, notably in Braden Scale utilization, pressure redistribution and the execution of standardized preventive measures.

CONCLUSION: The scenarios demonstrated satisfactory content validity and proved feasible for use in ICUs. In situ simulation showed potential to support continuing education actions, promote critical reflection on clinical practice and identify gaps in care processes related to PI prevention.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: In situ simulation can contribute to strengthening continuing health education, support the review of care practices and favour the implementation of evidence-based preventive measures for PI prevention in intensive care.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC INVOLVEMENT: No patient or public involvement in the development of this study.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://ensaiosclinicos.gov.br/rg/RBR-4xc2sk8.

articles.title: Extended Analyses of Pelacarsen and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with High Lipoprotein(a).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pelacarsen is an antisense oligonucleotide that reduces serum levels of lipoprotein(a). In a randomized placebo-controlled trial in patients with established cardiovascular disease, pelacarsen did not reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events compared to placebo. We further investigated the association of pelacarsen treatment with cardiovascular outcomes.

METHODS: We report the association of pelacarsen treatment with a primary composite end point of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or urgent coronary revascularization. Analyses included on-treatment, uninterrupted treatment, total primary end point events (first and recurrent events), landmark analyses classified by changes in and achieved lipoprotein(a) at 3 months, and key subgroups including baseline lipoprotein(a), low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (CRP), and time from qualifying event to enrollment.

RESULTS: For participants on treatment, a primary end point occurred in 434 participants (10.4%) randomly assigned to placebo and 380 participants (9.1%) assigned to pelacarsen (hazard ratio, 0.98; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.85 to 1.12). When evaluating participants with uninterrupted treatment, a primary end point event occurred in 167 participants (11.0%) in the pelacarsen group and 204 participants (10.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.89 to 1.34). When evaluating total primary end point events, there were 644 events in the pelacarsen group and 646 events in the placebo group (rate ratio, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.87 to 1.14). In landmark analyses evaluating participants alive and free of the composite end point at 3 months, when compared to placebo there was no association between pelacarsen treatment and the primary end point either in participants with reduction in lipoprotein(a) greater than or equal to the median (170 nmol/l) (hazard ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.92 to 1.29) or in participants who achieved lipoprotein(a) lower than or equal to the median (69.5 nmol/l) (hazard ratio, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.93 to 1.29). There was also no association between pelacarsen treatment and the primary end point in any of the evaluated key subgroups including classification by median baseline lipoprotein(a), LDL cholesterol, high-sensitivity CRP, or time from qualifying cardiovascular disease to enrollment.

CONCLUSIONS: Pelacarsen was not associated with a reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events when evaluated by treatment exposure, changes in or achieved lipoprotein(a) levels at 3 months, considering total events, or within subgroups of baseline lipoprotein(a), LDL cholesterol, or high-sensitivity CRP levels.

articles.title: Pesticides and Hypospadias in Southern Brazil: An Ecological Study.
articles.abstract: Rio Grande do Sul ranks among the Brazilian states with the highest pesticide consumption and one of the highest prevalences of hypospadias, a congenital anomaly often associated with prenatal exposure to endocrine-disrupting chemicals. We assessed the relationship between prenatal pesticide exposure and hypospadias risk through an ecological study of 1 776 670 live births in the state from 2010 to 2022. Using a spatial Bayesian hierarchical model, we examined associations between hypospadias and municipal-level indicators: relative crop area, pesticide sales, and probability of pesticide detection in water samples. The prevalence was 4.69 cases per 10 000 live births, with 10 municipalities at high risk and 15 at low risk. Higher risk was associated with tobacco cultivation. Sales of metaflumizone and Melaleuca alternifolia were associated with increased risk, while detection probabilities of alachlor and DDT showed the largest estimated effects, although these estimates were accompanied by substantial uncertainty. While causal inference is not possible in this ecological design, findings generate hypotheses for future research on prenatal pesticide exposure. Considering other environmental risk factors may further clarify hypospadias etiology. Identifying modifiable determinants is key to guiding interventions and public policies to reduce this condition's burden, particularly in rural areas and agricultural populations.

articles.title: Nocardia seriolae Infection Causes Granulomatous Pathology, High Mortality and Growth Impairment in Cultured Rice Field Eel (Monopterus albus).
articles.abstract: During a recent epidemiological survey of rice field eel (Monopterus albus) aquaculture farms in Jiangxi Province, China, we observed a characteristic presentation of multifocal granulomatous nodules suggestive of nocardial infection. Bacterial isolation yielded light-yellow, pigmented colonies with a granular texture and dry, wrinkled surface. Microscopy revealed branching filamentous rods characteristic of Nocardia, while histopathology demonstrated granulomatous inflammation with severe necrosis. Molecular identification, supported by whole-genome sequencing, confirmed the isolate as Nocardia seriolae, designated strain HZAU2505. Targeted sampling of clinically symptomatic fish across fifteen batches revealed a Nocardia seriolae PCR detection rate of 22.86% (8/35) among diseased animals. Notably, specific PCR surveillance targeting the Nocardia seriolae ITS gene detected Nocardia seriolae DNA in 90.9% (10/11) of frozen feed samples from affected facilities. Disk diffusion screening for aquaculture-approved drugs indicated that strain HZAU2505 was susceptible to doxycycline, neomycin, florfenicol, intermediate susceptible to ciprofloxacin, and resistant to enrofloxacin and penicillin. Complementary broth microdilution assays (CLSI M24) revealed consistent resistance patterns: isolates were susceptible to aminoglycosides (amikacin), tetracyclines (doxycycline), macrolides (clarithromycin), and oxazolidinones (linezolid), showed intermediate susceptibility to quinolones (ciprofloxacin), but exhibited strong resistance to β-lactams (amoxicillin-clavulanate), sulfonamides (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole), and glycopeptides (vancomycin). Experimental infection with 106 CFU/fish of strain HZAU2505 led to 80% cumulative mortality. Infected Monopterus albus displayed perianal lesions, internal white nodules, and clinical signs consistent with natural infections. Bacterial loads reached up to 105 copies/mg sample. Infected fish also exhibited significantly reduced growth, with a 17.7% lower weight gain rate after 21 days compared to controls, alongside markedly elevated total triglyceride (TG) concentrations. This study provides evidence of Nocardia seriolae infection in Monopterus albus, which manifests as severe necrotizing lesions, significant growth impairment, and high mortality. These findings highlight a critical risk to eel aquaculture productivity and disease management.

articles.title: Reversible severe functional decline in an older patient with Alzheimer's dementia: A case report.
articles.journal: Nutrition in clinical practice : official publication of the American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Enteral feeding via percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) is generally discouraged in advanced dementia, because it has not been shown to improve survival, aspiration risk, or functional outcomes. However, these recommendations assume accurate disease staging. Reversible conditions such as metabolic encephalopathy and severe malnutrition may mimic terminal-stage dementia, leading to premature limitation of potentially beneficial nutritional support. This case highlights the importance of individualized reassessment before concluding that enteral feeding is futile.

CASE PRESENTATION: An 85-year-old woman with an 8-year history of Alzheimer dementia developed profound functional decline over 3-4 months, including mutism, inability to ambulate, incontinence, and minimal oral intake. At a routine visit with her primary care clinician (PCC), she was presumed to have progressed to advanced dementia, and no further evaluation was pursued, because current guidelines discourage artificially administered nutrition and hydration in advanced dementia. After transitioning to home-based primary care, her new PCC investigated the unusually rapid decline. Laboratory testing revealed severe hypernatremia (sodium, 158 mmol/L), acute kidney injury, and severe malnutrition (body mass index [BMI], 16.1). She was diagnosed with metabolic encephalopathy superimposed on moderate-stage Alzheimer dementia. Nutritional assessment confirmed severe malnutrition by Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) criteria. Following transdisciplinary evaluation and shared decision-making with the patient's daughter, her designated health care proxy, PEG placement was performed. Nutritional rehabilitation normalized laboratory values, restored BMI to 21-22, and resulted in marked cognitive and functional improvement.

CONCLUSIONS: Severe malnutrition and metabolic derangements may produce a reversible syndrome that mimics advanced dementia. Careful evaluation of reversible contributors to rapid decline is essential before forgoing nutritional support, thus allowing for individualized, goal-concordant decisions and avoiding inappropriate therapeutic nihilism.

articles.title: Implementation of Pharmacogenomics in Pediatric-Focused Institutions Within the Pharmacogenomics Global Research Network.
articles.abstract: Descriptions of how pediatric-focused institutions implement pharmacogenomic testing are scarce, and often not differentiated from adult-focused institutions. We aimed to provide a detailed description of how pediatric-focused institutions across the world implemented pharmacogenomic testing in clinical practice. A survey was distributed to members of the Pharmacogenomics Global Research Network to assess program infrastructure, implementation efforts, genes tested, method of testing, and clinical decision support. The survey was completed by 43 institutions that have implemented pharmacogenomics: 12 pediatric-focused, 10 adult-focused, and 21 institutions serving all ages. All pediatric-focused institutions provide testing for CYP2C19, CYP2C9, CYP2D6, CYP3A5, NUDT15, and TPMT. Psychiatry and hematology/oncology were the specialties most commonly reported as implementing pharmacogenomics at pediatric-focused institutions. Most institutions have clinical decision support incorporated into their electronic health record and a similar number of compensated employees contributing to the program, regardless of age group focus. All pediatric-focused institutions were non-profit and often received programmatic funding from internal sources. A higher proportion of pediatric-focused sites provided patient education (92%) compared to adult-focused (60%) and those caring for all ages (76%). Pediatric-focused institutions interested in implementing or expanding their pharmacogenomic services will encounter many of the same opportunities and considerations as adult institutions. The results of this survey highlight additional unique considerations for pediatric-focused pharmacogenomic implementation and may serve as a roadmap for pediatric institutions interested in implementing or expanding pharmacogenomic services.

articles.title: A Retrospective Study of the Efficacy of Regional Anesthesia in Reducing Donor Site Harvest Pain in Burn Patients.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: Despite advances in burn care, the pain of burn treatment remains unresolved. The creation of donor harvest sites is often unavoidable, and the subsequent pain is difficult to treat. Regional anesthesia for the donor harvest sites can provide effective analgesia, however, there is limited literature regarding its efficacy. The purpose of this study was to assess the use of regional anesthesia for donor harvest site pain. Patients admitted to the burn center from January 1, 2011, to May 15, 2025, with thigh donor site harvest(s) were reviewed for study inclusion. Data collected included demographics, burn variables, hospital course data, and regional anesthesia procedure details. Descriptive statistics were used to determine differences between the block and non-block groups. Of the 524 patients included, 164 (31.3%) had donor site blocks and 360 (68.7%) did not. There were 77 (47%) with single shot blocks and 87 (53%) had indwelling catheters (groin or epidural). The groups were well-matched in their demographics, burn injury data, and hospital variables. The overall oral morphine equivalents (OME) and pain report levels were similar between the block and control groups in all three post-operative periods. However, causal conclusions are limited by this retrospective, heterogenous study. An appropriately protocolized prospective study is planned.

articles.title: A nomogram model for analyzing risk factors of postpartum hemorrhage in twin pregnancies with cesarean section.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The rising prevalence of twin pregnancies and cesarean sections (CS) is a significant risk factor for postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), contributing to increased maternal morbidity and mortality globally. Establishing a reliable risk assessment model for PPH could facilitate timely identification and intervention, thereby improving maternal outcomes. This study aimed to develop an effective nomogram for predicting PPH in twin pregnancies undergoing CS.

METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed data from 1704 women with twin pregnancies who delivered by CS between 2016 and 2022 at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University, China. To identify risk factors for PPH after CS in twin pregnancies, univariate analysis and LASSO (least absolute shrinkage and selection operator) regression were employed. A nomogram was subsequently developed based on the results of binary logistic regression analysis and the Akaike information criterion (AIC). Model validation was performed using bootstrap resampling, with performance assessed through discrimination (receiver operating characteristic curve), calibration (calibration plot and Hosmer-Lemeshow test), and clinical utility (decision cur analysis, DCA).

RESULTS: The nomogram for PPH was created using eight best predictor variables, namely, parity, assisted reproductive technology (ART), preeclampsia (PE), placenta previa, placenta accreta, anemia, the sum of the neonatal birthweight, and general anesthesia, which were all independent risk factors for PPH after CS in twin pregnancies. The nomogram demonstrated strong discrimination and calibration performance, with robust clinical utility as evidenced by area under the curve (AUC) analysis and DCA. Internal verification confirmed the consistency between predicted and actual values.

CONCLUSIONS: Parity, the use of ART, PE, placenta previa, placenta accreta, degree of prenatal anemia, total neonatal birthweight, and the use of general anesthesia are significant risk factors affecting the incidence of postpartum hemorrhage after CS in patients. The prediction model based on the above factors provides an accurate tool for assessing PPH risk, offering potential to guide clinical decision-making and further reduce maternal mortality.

articles.title: Exercise-Related Heart Rate Response Traits and Parkinson's Disease: Genetic Correlation, Gene-Based Analysis, and Bidirectional Mendelian Randomization.
articles.abstract: Background: Recent observational studies suggest that impaired exercise-related heart rate responses may precede the clinical diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD). However, it remains unclear whether this association reflects shared common-variant genetic architecture, bidirectional causal effects, or other mechanisms. Methods: We analyzed genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics for post-exercise heart rate recovery at 50 s (N = 54,137), heart rate increase during exercise (N = 54,137), and PD (N = 482,730). Linkage disequilibrium score regression (LDSC) estimated genetic correlations (rg). Gene-based, gene-set, and gene-property analyses were conducted using Multi-marker Analysis of GenoMic Annotation (MAGMA) via Functional Mapping and Annotation (FUMA). Bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR) was used to assess potential causal effects. Results: LDSC revealed no significant genetic correlation between PD and post-exercise heart rate recovery at 50 s (rg = -0.006, P = 0.903) or heart rate increase during exercise (rg = -0.021, P = 0.694). No overlap was observed between the sets of genes reaching Bonferroni-corrected significance for PD and either exercise-related heart rate response trait. Likewise, no overlap was observed among significant gene sets or tissue-specific enrichment results after FDR or Bonferroni correction. Bidirectional MR analyses did not identify statistically supported associations within the precision of the available data, with a limited number of instruments and wide confidence intervals. Conclusions: These findings do not support strong shared common-variant genetic architecture or statistically supported bidirectional causal associations between PD and exercise-related heart rate response traits. They refine the interpretation of prior observational associations. Other mechanisms cannot be excluded.

articles.title: Burden of Albuminuria in US Adults and its Association with Obesity, Sex and Mortality: A Cross-sectional Analysis of NHANES 2003-2020.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Renal physiology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Albuminuria is an early marker of kidney disease diagnosis, severity and progression. Obesity, a major public health concern in the United States, may contribute to the development of albuminuria; however, the obesity-albuminuria relationship remains incompletely defined. We hypothesized that albuminuria is more prevalent in obese individuals and is associated with poor survival.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of NHANES survey cycles from 2003 to 2020, with linked mortality data through 2016. The study included 59,717 participants aged ≥18 years with available urinary albumin creatinine ratio (uACR) and BMI ≥18 kg/m2. BMI was categorized into normal weight, overweight and obese. Albuminuria was defined as UACR ≥30 mg/g and categorized into three severity grades (mild, moderate, and severe). Logistic regression models were used to assess the association between obesity and albuminuria, and adjustment by sociodemographic and clinical factors was assessed. Survival across albuminuria severity grades was examined.

RESULTS: Among individuals with albuminuria the prevalence of obesity was significantly higher than those without albuminuria (40.2% vs 32.9%; p<0.001). Individuals with albuminuria were relatively older and had higher prevalence of diabetes and hypertension as compared to the no albuminuria group. Obesity was significantly associated with higher odds of albuminuria (OR 1.36; 95% CI 1.23-1.50) when controlling for sociodemographic and clinical factors. We also observed higher odds of albuminuria in individuals who were males (OR 1.58, 95% CI 1.37-1.82), ages 18 to 44 years (OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.26-1.68), and ages 45 to 64 years (OR 1.79, 95% CI 1.49-2.14). The Individuals with albuminuria had poorer survival, with stark decline in a stepwise manner across albuminuria severity grades.

CONCLUSION: Obesity is strongly associated with albuminuria in U.S. adults. Albuminuria is linked to survival disadvantage, underscoring the importance of screening among individuals with obesity and early initiation of nephro-protective therapies in individuals with albuminuria.

articles.title: Housing mice in thermoneutrality causes peripheral tissue-specific changes in the number, identity, and phase of circadian-expressed mRNA transcripts.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology
articles.abstract: Laboratory mice are typically housed at room temperature (20-25°C), well below their thermoneutral zone (about 30°C), imposing chronic mild cold stress that increases metabolic rate by 30-40%. Because circadian and metabolic physiology are highly temperature-sensitive, we tested whether this housing condition reshapes rhythmic gene expression in tissues central to cardiovascular and metabolic health. We hypothesized that mild cold stress suppresses circadian gene expression in peripheral tissues. We performed RNA sequencing on hearts, livers, and diaphragms collected every 4 hours over 48 hours in constant darkness from male mice to identify transcripts with approximately 24-hour rhythms. Thermoneutral housing reorganized the circadian transcriptome tissue-specifically. Out of ∼13000 filtered transcripts, the proportion of rhythmic transcripts (q<0.05) in the heart nearly quadrupled, from 11% (1410) at room temperature to 42% (5282) at thermoneutrality, while the diaphragm rose modestly (6% to 9%; 792 vs. 1153). The liver's overall proportion was unchanged (36% vs. 37%; 4041 vs. 4150), yet more than 30% of rhythmic transcripts were unique between housing conditions. Almost 80% of rhythmic genes in the heart under thermoneutrality show acrophase near the subjective activity/rest transition. Gene ontology analysis revealed coordinated changes in the temporal organization of metabolic pathways in the heart and liver but less pronounced in the diaphragm. These changes occurred without detectable changes in core clock expression, implicating regulators acting downstream of, or parallel to, the clock itself. Because room temperature housing is standard across biomedical research, our findings show that this overlooked variable can distort the circadian transcriptome of tissues central to cardiovascular and metabolic disease, with implications for how mouse studies model human physiology.

articles.title: Association of high-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation with 6-month cognitive outcomes and white matter lesion progression in patients with cerebral small vessel disease and cognitive impairment.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the association of high-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) with 6-month cognitive outcomes and white matter lesion progression in patients with cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) and cognitive impairment.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study design was used. Data from 427 patients with CSVD and cognitive impairment who attended the Department of Neurology of our hospital from January 2022 to December 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Based on treatment documented in the medical records, patients were classified into an rTMS group (n = 228), who had received 10 Hz high-frequency rTMS over the left DLPFC as part of routine clinical care, and a control group (n = 199), who had received conventional pharmacotherapy alone. Both groups received standardized basic CSVD treatment; the rTMS group additionally received rTMS once daily, 5 days per week, for 2 consecutive weeks (10 sessions). Complete baseline and 6-month neuropsychological and MRI records were required for inclusion; therefore, all 427 patients had complete data for the prespecified outcomes and no imputation was required. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in change from baseline in Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score at 6 months (ΔMoCA). Secondary outcomes included changes in MMSE, TMT-A, TMT-B, Rey-Osterrieth Complex Figure delayed recall, MoCA responder rates, imaging outcomes, safety, and exploratory subgroup analyses. A propensity score matching (PSM) sensitivity analysis was performed for ΔMoCA, MoCA responder rates, and WMHV change.

RESULTS: The rTMS group showed significantly greater delta-MoCA than the control group (mean difference [MD] = 1.11, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.56-1.66, p < .001, Cohen d = 0.38). The rTMS group also showed significantly greater improvement in MMSE (MD = 0.87, 95% CI: 0.42-1.32, p < .001, d = 0.37), TMT-B (MD = 14.35 s, 95% CI: 0.86-27.83, p = .037, d = 0.20), and Rey delayed recall (MD = 1.73, 95% CI: 0.55-2.90, p = .004, d = 0.28) compared with the control group. The between-group difference in TMT-A did not reach statistical significance (MD = 4.35 s, 95% CI: -0.37 to 9.08, p = .071), but became significant after ANCOVA adjustment for age, education, and baseline score (p = .001). The rTMS group had significantly higher responder rates than the control group at all three thresholds: delta-MoCA ≥ 1 point (85.1% vs. 70.9%, odds ratio [OR] = 2.35, p < .001), ≥2 points (74.1% vs. 60.3%, OR = 1.89, p = .002), and ≥3 points (61.4% vs. 46.2%, OR = 1.85, p = .002). No statistically significant between-group differences were observed for any imaging parameter (WMHV, FA, ADC, Fazekas grade progression; all p > .05). A PSM sensitivity analysis (195 matched pairs) yielded consistent results for the primary outcome (MD = 1.23, 95% CI: 0.64-1.81, p < .001, d = 0.29). In exploratory subgroup analyses (not prespecified), cognitive severity (interaction p < .001) and diabetes status (interaction p = .014) suggested potential treatment effect modification, with numerically greater benefit in patients with moderate cognitive impairment and those without diabetes. The overall incidence of adverse events did not differ significantly between groups (15.4% vs. 13.6%, p = .602); all events were mild to moderate and transient, and no serious adverse events occurred.

CONCLUSION: In this retrospective cohort study, high-frequency rTMS over the left DLPFC was associated with greater improvement in long-term cognitive function in patients with CSVD and cognitive impairment, particularly in global cognition, executive function, and memory, with a favorable safety profile. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested that cognitive severity and diabetes status may influence treatment outcomes, warranting prospective validation. rTMS did not significantly delay white matter lesion progression; its cognitive benefits may be mediated primarily through enhanced neuroplasticity and functional network reorganization rather than structural lesion modification.

articles.title: Pain Characterization: Presentation Patterns, and Multidimensional Assessment in Women with Advanced Gynecologic Cancer in a Palliative Care Service.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pain in advanced cancer is a complex and multidimensional phenomenon extending beyond intensity to include biological, psychological, and social components. In women with advanced gynecologic malignancies, pain is highly prevalent yet often undercharacterized, particularly in resource-limited settings where disparities in access and delayed integration of palliative care may influence its presentation and management.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize multidimensional pain features and identify distinct descriptive pain patterns in women with advanced gynecologic cancer receiving palliative care.

DESIGN: Observational study.

SETTING/SUBJECTS: Electronic medical records of women aged ≥18 years with advanced gynecologic cancer and documented pain, treated at a tertiary cancer center in Mexico between 2013 and 2023, were reviewed.

MEASUREMENTS: Sociodemographic and clinical variables were collected. Pain assessment included location, intensity, time of onset, and characteristics (somatic, visceral, neuropathic, or mixed). Psychosocial factors, including anxiety and depression, were also evaluated. Descriptive statistics were used to explore multidimensional pain patterns.

RESULTS: A total of 1,015 women were included (median age 56 years; most had≤12 years of education). Cervical and ovarian cancers predominated (43.4% and 32.3%). Pain was mainly pelvic or abdominal (81.0%) and commonly mixed visceral/neuropathic. Median intensity was moderate (4/10), with higher intensity in uterine sarcoma (median 7/10). Nearly half of patients presented anxiety or depression.

CONCLUSIONS: Pain in advanced gynecologic cancer is heterogeneous and multidimensional, with identifiable tumor-type-specific pain patterns that may inform individualized, patient-centered management strategies, particularly in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Factors that influence medical students' residency program selection: a scoping review.
articles.journal: Academic medicine : journal of the Association of American Medical Colleges
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The residency application and match process is a consequential transition in physicians' careers. Although designed to "match" applicants and programs based on mutual preferences, applicants' decisions are influenced by contextual, cultural, and personal factors. Despite its importance, the literature on how applicants evaluate and select residency programs remains fragmented and lacks a unifying conceptual framework. This scoping review synthesizes the literature to map factors influencing residency program selection.

METHOD: The authors searched three databases without date restrictions, with the final search conducted in June 2026. Studies were eligible if published between January 2015 and June 2026 and reported residency selection factors among US or Canadian participants involved in the National Resident Matching Program or Canadian Resident Matching Service. Two reviewers independently screened titles/abstracts and full texts. A standardized tool captured bibliographic details, participant characteristics, methods, and reported selection factors. Data were summarized using descriptive statistics and content analysis. Factors were mapped to the Learning Environment framework, encompassing social, organizational, personal, societal, and physical and virtual space components.

RESULTS: Sixty-five studies published in 41 journals were included. Most studies used surveys (n = 62; 95.4%), typically author-developed. Four studies (6.2%) used interviews. Most included medical students (n = 48; 73.8%), while 25 (38.5%) included residents or fellows reflecting retrospectively. Across studies, 1,237 factors were identified (mean 19.1 per study). Social (n = 317; 25.6%), Organizational (n = 313; 25.3%), personal (n = 305; 24.7%), and societal factors (n = 255; 20.6%) were similarly reported. Physical and Virtual space factors were infrequently reported (n = 30, 2.4%).

CONCLUSIONS: Residency selection reflects applicants' assessments of interrelated learning environment components rather than isolated program attributes. Applying the Learning Environment framework highlights that applicants are selecting not only a training site, but a learning environment where they hope to grow personally and professionally. These findings may inform more intentional program design, recruitment strategies, and applicant decision making.

articles.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape

articles.title: Saphenofemoral junction reconstruction and recurrence after the treatment of superficial venous reflux disease with endovenous ablation methods.
articles.abstract: BackgroundRecurrence of varicosities and reflux-related symptoms after endovenous ablation of the great saphenous vein (GSV) remains common. Standard ablation is delivered 1.5-2 cm distal to the saphenofemoral junction (SFJ), leaving the junctional tributaries and dilated proximal junction untreated, unlike conventional high ligation and stripping. We compared standard endovenous ablation with a technique combining open SFJ reconstruction and endovenous ablation.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed patients treated for symptomatic primary GSV reflux. Group 1 underwent standard endovenous ablation (at our institution or referred from elsewhere). Group 2 underwent open SFJ reconstruction - ligation of the junctional tributaries, division of the saphenous vein, and reduction of the dilated common femoral vein - plus endovenous ablation of the GSV trunk. The protocol was introduced during the study period and applied selectively and non-randomly; patients with a body mass index ≥30 kg/m2, those aged ≥70 years and those with groin skin infection received standard ablation. Beyond a 3-month review, duplex follow-up was not standardised and was performed mainly when symptoms recurred. Symptomatic recurrence, recurrent visible varicosities, duplex recurrence patterns, reintervention and complications were reported separately.ResultsGroup 1 included 115 patients (70 treated at our institution and 45 referred after treatment elsewhere) and Group 2 included 203. Mean age was 54.3 ± 10.9 and 48.7 ± 14.8 years, and 62.6% and 71.9% were female, respectively. Group 1 had a higher body mass index and more diabetes, hypertension and smoking (all P ≤ .003). During follow-up, 18 patients in Group 1 (15.7%) returned with symptomatic recurrence, compared with 7 (3.4%) in Group 2 (p < .001; adjusted OR 0.14, 95% CI 0.05-0.40). No Group 2 patient showed a patent refluxing GSV trunk. In Group 2, six patients (3.0%) had groin wound complications, four managed with wound care and two requiring surgical revision, and one had a minor groin hematoma; one Group 1 patient developed deep vein thrombosis. There was no pulmonary embolism and no mortality.ConclusionsIn this selected, non-randomised cohort, adding open SFJ reconstruction to endovenous GSV ablation was associated with an acceptable complication rate, at the cost of reintroducing groin wound morbidity, and with lower symptomatic recurrence than standard ablation. Given the baseline imbalance, potential referral bias and non-standardised follow-up, these findings show an association rather than a preventive effect. Whether patients at particularly high risk of SFJ/anterior accessory saphenous vein-related recurrence benefit from this approach should be tested prospectively.

articles.title: SV2A PET imaging in Parkinson's disease and atypical parkinsonism: A systematic review of neuroimaging methodologies and regional findings.
articles.abstract: BackgroundReduced presynaptic density, commonly referred to as synaptic loss, is an early and clinically relevant feature of parkinsonian disorders. The development of positron emission tomography (PET) radiotracers targeting synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A (SV2A) has enabled in vivo quantification of synaptic density.ObjectivesThis systematic review examines neuroimaging methodologies and regional SV2A PET findings in Parkinson's disease (PD), progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), corticobasal degeneration (CBD), and multiple system atrophy (MSA).MethodsA systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines, including studies employing validated SV2A PET radiotracers to quantify synaptic density in parkinsonian populations. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies (QUADAS)-2 tool. Substantial methodological heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis; findings were synthesized narratively.ResultsFourteen studies were included. In PD, the substantia nigra was the most affected region, with striatal involvement more prominent in advanced disease (>6 years duration). In PSP and CBD, synaptic loss was widespread, exceeded grey matter atrophy, and correlated with clinical severity and cognitive decline; longitudinal PSP data showed reductions of approximately 3-4% per year in frontal and caudate regions. In MSA, infratentorial involvement (cerebellum, pons, medulla) predominated, enabling diagnostic differentiation with high accuracy (AUC up to 0.99).ConclusionsSV2A PET reveals disease-specific patterns of reduced presynaptic availability, consistent with synaptic loss, across parkinsonian disorders, supporting its potential as a diagnostic and monitoring biomarker. Methodological harmonization and longitudinal multicenter studies are needed to establish clinical utility.

articles.title: David vs supracoronary with non-coronary sinus replacement in acute type A aortic dissection: 5-year outcomes.
articles.abstract: BackgroundAcute aortic dissection complicated by severe aortic regurgitation (AR) requires urgent surgical intervention. The optimal root management strategy remains controversial. This study compared the long-term outcomes of the Tirone David procedure and supracoronary aortic replacement with non-coronary sinus replacement in patients with acute type A dissection.MethodsThis retrospective observational study included 80 consecutive patients with acute aortic dissection type A (AADA) and severe AR who underwent surgery between October 2015 and February 2020 at the University Hospitals, with a 5-year follow-up. Patients were divided into two groups: valve-sparing reimplantation (Tirone David, n=40) and supracoronary repair with non-coronary sinus replacement (n=40). Outcomes included operative data, postoperative complications, mortality, and echocardiographic assessment of AR immediately postoperatively, at 6 months, and at 5 years.ResultsThere were no significant differences in age, cross-clamp time, bypass time, intensive care stay, hospital stay, or early mortality between groups (p>0.05). Immediate postoperative AR occurred significantly more frequently in the supracoronary group (57.5% mild AR) compared with the Tirone David group (5.0% mild AR; p<0.001). At 6 months and 5 years, the incidence of AR remained significantly lower in the Tirone David group (10% and 15%) versus the supracoronary group (65% and 75%, respectively; p<0.001).ConclusionsIn this selected cohort of relatively stable patients with AADA and severe AR, the Tirone David procedure was associated with better long-term aortic valve competence than supracoronary aortic replacement with non-coronary sinus replacement, without an observed increase in major perioperative complications.

articles.title: Knowledge, attitudes, practices, and vaccination gaps related to hepatitis B among adolescents in a hyperendemic, fragile setting: A cross-sectional study from Mogadishu, Somalia.
articles.journal: The International journal of risk & safety in medicine
articles.abstract: BackgroundHepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major public health problem in sub-Saharan Africa, yet evidence on adolescents' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) toward HBV is limited in Somalia. This study assessed HBV-related KAP and associated factors among high school students in Mogadishu.ObjectivesTo assess HBV-related knowledge, attitudes, practices, and vaccination status among high school students in Mogadishu, Somalia, and identify associated factors.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted among 392 high school students using a structured questionnaire. Descriptive statistics summarized KAP levels. Associations between sociodemographic variables and KAP outcomes were examined using chi-square tests and logistic regression.ResultsAlthough 98.0% of students had heard of HBV, 63.0% of participants demonstrated good knowledge of hepatitis B, while 37.0% had poor knowledge. Positive attitudes toward HBV were reported by 27.0% of participants, whereas 73.0% had negative attitudes. Just over half of respondents (52.5%) reported good preventive practices, while 47.5% had poor practices. HBV vaccination coverage was 39.3%. In multivariable analysis, grade level was significantly associated with the KAP domains, although the pattern of association varied across knowledge, attitudes, and practices.ConclusionHigh school students in Mogadishu exhibited substantial gaps in HBV knowledge, negative attitudes, and low vaccination uptake. Educational grade level was a key determinant of HBV-related KAP, highlighting the need for targeted, school-based interventions to strengthen adolescent HBV prevention.

articles.title: Potential for targeting peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma in type 2 diabetes.
'You've got something to look at and something to achieve': Perspectives of adults with type 2 diabetes on professional-mode glucose monitoring. A GP-OSMOTIC nested qualitative study.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Approximately half of adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D) have average glucose levels above the recommended range, increasing the risk of long-term complications. Intermittent (quarterly) use of professional-mode continuous glucose monitoring (Pro-CGM) offers opportunity for greater personalisation of management, collaborative care and targeted education to support behavioural modification. Framed in Self-Determination Theory (SDT), this study aimed to explore how Pro-CGM was experienced by adults with T2D, and to identify potential mechanisms for behaviour change.

METHODS: This qualitative study was nested within a pragmatic, 12-month randomised controlled trial of quarterly Pro-CGM in primary care. Participants were purposively recruited from the intervention group; 22 individuals from six primary care clinics in Victoria, Australia, took part. An abductive analytic approach was adopted, whereby data-driven themes were subsequently interpreted through the SDT framework.

RESULTS: Qualitative analyses identified Pro-CGM monitoring and consultation experiences both satisfied and frustrated individual needs. Impacts on motivation and behaviour change were influenced by the degree to which support needs were met by clinicians and individual differences (e.g. regulatory orientation, preferences). This suggests that more sustained changes in behaviour and longer-term improvements in HbA1c may have occurred if Pro-CGM was implemented in a manner that provided appropriate support for psychological needs.

CONCLUSION: Pro-CGM has the potential to improve engagement in diabetes self management and health outcomes among people with T2D. Consideration of Pro-CGM-related resource needs for people with T2D, including facilitation of clinical support, is required to optimise the engagement with and sustain behavioural change for people with T2D.

articles.title: Impact of a pharmacist-led pharmacogenomic service on test capture rates in oncology: A retrospective pre-post cohort study, 2024-2026.
articles.journal: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners
articles.abstract: BackgroundPharmacogenomic (PGx) testing can support clinical decision-making to reduce toxicity associated with commonly used oncology therapies. However, PGx testing remains underutilized in oncology practice due to lack of personnel to coordinate testing. We evaluated whether the implementation of a pharmacist-led PGx service increased PGx testing among oncology patients.MethodsWe used a retrospective cohort study to compare outcomes from the pre-and post-intervention periods following implementation of a pharmacist-led PGx service within our Duluth oncology clinic, Minnesota-USA. EHR/laboratory data were extracted on adult cancer patients with planned/receiving 5-fluorouracil, capecitabine, or irinotecan between September 1, 2024, and March 31, 2026. The primary outcome was PGx capture, defined as the rate of patients who received PGx testing prior to chemotherapy initiation. Secondary outcomes included tests with actionable results and the proportion leading to therapy modification. Descriptive statistics, Chi-square test, Mann-Whitney U test, and adjusted (age and sex as covariates) logistic regression were used. All analyses were performed using SPSS (IBM 29.0) and RStudio (2025.09.1 + 401) with a statistical significance at ≤0.05.ResultsA total of 184 (N) eligible patients were included, with 107 in the pre-implementation group and 77 in the post-implementation group. PGx test capture rates increased from 25.2% in the pre-implementation group to 53.2% post-implementation (P < 0.001). In adjusted analysis, the post-implementation group remained significantly associated with higher PGx testing (OR = 3.40, 95% CI: (1.82,6.36))ConclusionImplementation of a pharmacist-led PGx workflow substantially increased testing. Integration of pharmacists into oncology PGx services may improve the identification of clinically relevant variants and support medication optimization.

articles.title: Novel ABCA1 mutations in Tangier disease associated with early-onset type 2 diabetes: A case report.
articles.abstract: Tangier disease (TD) is a rare disorder caused by mutations in the ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1) gene with autosomal recessive inheritance and is characterized by extremely low high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) and premature atherosclerosis. Although experimental studies suggest that ABCA1 plays an important role in pancreatic β-cell cholesterol homeostasis, its clinical contribution to diabetes development in humans remains unclear. We report a 69-year-old Japanese man with early-onset type 2 diabetes mellitus, profound hypo-HDL cholesterolemia (HDL-C 5 mg/dL), and severe atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Genetic analysis identified compound heterozygous ABCA1 variants (p.Arg104Cys and the novel p.Asp1706Tyr), both of which were predicted to be potentially pathogenic, although direct functional validation was not performed. Despite a 40-year duration of diabetes, endogenous insulin secretion was partially preserved. This case highlights phenotypic variability in TD and suggests that variant-specific effects on ABCA1 function and polygenic susceptibility may influence diabetes development in humans.

articles.title: Association between impaired cold perception threshold and serum calcium in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between serum calcium levels and cold perception threshold (CPT) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 334 type 2 diabetes mellitus patients from a tertiary hospital endocrinology department (March 2020-November 2024). Clinical, laboratory, and quantitative sensory testing (QST) data were collected. The correlations between serum calcium and cold/heat perception thresholds (CPT/HPT) were assessed using correlation analysis, multiple linear regression, and multivariable fractional polynomial (MFP) modeling.

RESULTS: Among the 334 enrolled patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (146 DM only; 188 with DPN), the DPN group was older and had longer diabetes duration (both P < 0.001). Patients with DPN demonstrated significantly impaired thermal sensation, with lower CPT and higher HPT than the DM group (both P < 0.001). Serum calcium positively correlated with mean CPT in both the total cohort (r = 0.170, P = 0.001) and the DPN subgroup (r = 0.160, P = 0.028), and negatively correlated with mean HPT in the total cohort (r = -0.115, P = 0.031) and the DPN subgroup (r = -0.175, P = 0.017), but not in the DM-only group. A calcium-CPT dose-response relationship was observed.

CONCLUSION: Serum calcium is an independent influencing factor for CPT in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, with a dose-response relationship observed. This finding suggested that in type 2 diabetes mellitus patients with low serum calcium levels, there should be heightened awareness of the risks of impaired cold perception and aggravated neuropathy, thereby enabling earlier risk stratification and personalized management.

articles.title: Streptococcus suis-induced mitophagy via Eno-HSP90AA1 interaction disrupts the blood-brain barrier.
articles.abstract: Streptococcus suis serotype 2 (SS2), a zoonotic pathogen associated with meningitis in humans and pigs, disrupts the blood-brain barrier (BBB) during infection, but underlying mechanisms remain inadequately elucidated. This study demonstrated that SS2 infection induced mitophagy in human brain microvascular endothelial cells (hBMECs), with Eno (Enolase) identified as the key bacterial protein responsible for the activation of PINK1-Parkin pathway. Using Co-immunoprecipitation, mass spectrometry, and confocal microscopy, we identified that Eno interacted with the host molecular chaperone HSP90AA1 via its N-terminal domain, necessitating the integrity of the second α-helix (residues 87-98). The interaction between Eno and HSP90AA1 may promote mitochondrial proteotoxic stress and misfolded protein accumulation, thereby contributing to mitophagy induction, while the loss of mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) alone is insufficient to initiate this process. Importantly, Eno-induced mitophagy did not result in cell death but instead led to the degradation of the tight junction protein claudin-5 (CLDN5), thus compromising BBB integrity. Both in vitro BBB models and in vivo mouse infection studies substantiated the involvement of Eno-induced mitophagy in BBB disruption. These findings reveal a novel mechanism whereby SS2 Eno exploits host HSP90AA1 to activate mitophagy, triggering the degradation of CLDN5 to breach the BBB. This study provides new insights into SS2 pathogenesis and identifies the Eno-HSP90AA1-mitophagy axis as a potential therapeutic target for preventing bacterial meningitis.

articles.title: Radial Artery Pseudoaneurysm With Individualized Non-Operative Management: A 4-Case Series.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Radial artery pseudoaneurysm (RAP) is an uncommon complication of radial arterial access. Although rarely life-threatening, it can cause significant morbidity. With the increasing use of radial access for coronary and endovascular procedures, arterial blood gas sampling, and invasive hemodynamic monitoring, RAP remains a potential access-site complication. Given its rarity, the literature on its management is limited and consists mainly of case reports and small case series. We report 4 cases of iatrogenic RAP with different non-operative management. CASE REPORT Four patients developed RAP following radial arterial access for intra-arterial blood pressure monitoring or coronary angiography. In Case 1, ultrasound-guided compression (UGC) was chosen because of poor collateral hand circulation and concerns for hand ischemia with thrombin injection, resulting in successful thrombosis of the pseudoaneurysm. Cases 2 and 3 underwent ultrasound-guided thrombin injection (UGTI), with Case 3 requiring repeat injection following recanalization. Case 4 had a large, flat-appearing pseudoaneurysm that was unsuitable for direct thrombin injection; balloon-assisted thrombin injection was attempted to preserve the radial artery but was unsuccessful, and a covered stent was deployed for exclusion of the pseudoaneurysm. CONCLUSIONS A range of non-operative approaches can be used in the management of RAP, depending on the clinical and anatomical circumstances.
