UGC and UGTI can achieve successful thrombosis, while endovascular techniques can provide an alternative when initial treatment is unsuccessful or the anatomy is challenging. Further studies are needed to better define the outcomes of these approaches and to establish a standardized treatment algorithm for RAP.

articles.title: Colchicine in chronic coronary artery disease: effects on vascular glucose uptake, inflammation, remodeling and blood pressure.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The mechanisms underlying colchicine's cardiovascular benefits in patients with coronary artery disease remain unclear and warrant further translational investigation.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 111 patients with chronic coronary artery disease and aortic or carotid target-to-background ratio ≥1.6 were assigned to colchicine 0.6 mg daily (n=55) or placebo (n=56) for 24 weeks. Arterial inflammation was assessed using 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) of the ascending aorta. The primary endpoint was the change in mean maximum target-to-background ratio over 24 weeks. Secondary and exploratory objectives included evaluation of systemic inflammatory markers and blood pressure. To support interpretation of the clinical findings, a complementary hypertensive rodent model, the spontaneously hypertensive rat (SHR), was treated with colchicine for 4 weeks to explore vascular and inflammatory pathways potentially influenced by colchicine using immunohistochemistry, myography and proteomics.Colchicine did not reduce aortic FDG uptake compared with placebo (adjusted mean change 0.05 [95% CI -0.02 to 0.12] vs 0.01 [95% CI -0.06 to 0.08]; p=0.38). In secondary and exploratory analyses, colchicine was associated with a reduction in neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (adjusted mean change -0.36 vs -0.08; p=0.033), a trend toward lower high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (adjusted geometric mean percentage change -28.2% vs -5.8%; p=0.060) and attenuation of increases in systolic (adjusted mean change 0.88 mmHg vs. 4.94 mmHg; p=0.046) and diastolic (1.41 mmHg vs. 4.35 mmHg; p=0.048) blood pressure. In SHRs, colchicine had no effect on the aorta but attenuated the progression of hypertension and reduced inflammation and extracellular matrix remodelling in mesenteric resistance arteries, while enhancing vasodilator responses. Reductions in CXCL10, CXCL2, NLRP3 and IL-18 expression were observed in mesenteric arteries from the SHR following colchicine treatment.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings support the hypothesis that vascular effects of colchicine likely extend beyond large conduit arteries, while the specific pathways and relevance to coronary atherosclerosis require further investigation.

articles.title: Fertility rates across generations in twins and singletons: a total population study in Finland.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: Does twin status and zygosity (monozygotic vs dizygotic; same-sex vs opposite-sex) predict fertility outcomes and intergenerational reproductive patterns compared with singletons?

SUMMARY ANSWER: Dizygotic female twins had a modestly higher number of biological children than singletons and monozygotic twins and were more likely to have a twin birth, but we did not observe differences for males or intergenerational differences.

WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Dizygotic twinning is associated with heritable hyperovulation and higher natural fertility but less is known about whether being a twin or zygosity influences reproductive outcomes across generations.

STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION: A population-based longitudinal cohort study using part of the Finnish Twin Cohort and national population registers. Participants included an Anchor Generation composed of monozygotic (MZ; N = 4068), same-sex dizygotic (SSDZ; N = 8890), opposite-sex dizygotic (OSDZ; N = 8474), unknown zygosity (XZ; N = 2320) twins, and singleton controls (N = 1 193 404) born between 1945 and 1957 (total N = 1 217 156; 49.1% female), their mothers, their children, and their grandchildren.

PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS: Fertility outcomes (number of biological children, age at first birth, childlessness, multiple births) were derived from Finnish population registers. Analyses followed a preregistered plan (https://osf.io/qbwv3).

MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: Differences in fertility between singletons and twins were modest and varied by sex and zygosity. Differences were observed generally in the mothers of twins and female twins themselves, with limited differences in the offspring of twins as compared to the offspring of singletons. Twins were slightly older at first birth, had fewer total biological offspring, but were more likely to have a twin birth. Dizygotic twins in particular differed from monozygotic twins and singletons.

LIMITATIONS, REASONS FOR CAUTION: Findings are limited to individuals born in mid-20th-century Finland and thus generalizability to recent populations or non-Nordic contexts may be restricted. Further, analyses are observational, and causal inference is limited due to alternative motivation behind fertility rates like social or cultural reasons.

WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS: These findings suggest that zygosity and sex interact to shape reproductive outcomes, offering insight into genetic and environmental contributions to fertility. They highlight the value of large twin cohorts for studying intergenerational reproductive trends and the representativeness of twins in population-based fertility research.

FUNDING: As a supporting activity to ongoing research projects, funding for this project was provided by the Broad Trauma Initiative at the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard.

DISCLOSURES: The authors declare no conflict of interest.

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: N/A.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Manifestations of Lyme Disease.
articles.abstract: Lyme disease is a tick-borne zoonosis caused by Borrelia burgdorferi that can involve multiple organ systems, including the cardiovascular (CV) system, noted in ~1-10% of untreated patients. This can produce atrioventricular (AV) or bundle branch block, atrial fibrillation, and myopericarditis in the acute phase, and dilated cardiomyopathy in the chronic phase. Myocardial involvement may lead to ventricular tachyarrhythmias and sudden death. AV block is reported in ~90% of cases, and in 30-60% of cases, it may necessitate cardiac pacing, at least temporarily, as most cases of high-degree AV blocks resolve with antibiotic therapy within 1 week. Occasionally, aortic dissection may occur. Although Lyme carditis, in the form of myocarditis, pericarditis, and less often endocarditis, is generally self-limited with early appropriate therapy, there is also the potential for lasting CV sequelae, such as persistent AV block (noted in 90% of cases), dilated cardiomyopathy and heart failure, and the rare occurrence of coronary artery involvement and aneurysmal changes. Patients with Lyme disease should receive oral tetracycline or penicillin, which can decrease the incidence of late-stage disease; however, some patients may fail early treatment. In cases of aseptic meningitis and radiculoneuritis, IV penicillin will be needed. As Lyme disease has now replaced syphilis as the "Great Imitator," physicians should be at vigilance for the disease, especially in endemic areas, and be familiarized with the particular skin rash of erythema chronicum migrans, an expanding skin lesion with the characteristic "bull's-eye" appearance patch with a center of clear skin and a distinct peripheral outer erythematous ring.

articles.title: Mapping and Outcome Implications of Left Atrial Low Voltage Regions as Determined by a Novel 122-electrode Spherical Mapping and Ablation Catheter.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
AIMS: A novel 122-electrode spherical mapping/pulsed field ablation (PFA) device is known to effectively ablate atrial fibrillation (AF). The aim of this study is threshold optimization of LVA for the unique geometry of the Globe electrodes and the prognostic association, to evaluate if the extent of low voltage areas could predict recurrence.

METHODS AND RESULTS: The PULSAR study was an IDE trial of 183 patients undergoing first-time paroxysmal AF ablation with one-year outcomes of any atrial arrhythmia. During this study, a subset of patients (n=82) had detailed pre-ablation voltage maps performed with the catheter. Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) was then performed with PFA. Patients were followed with weekly transtelephonic monitoring, ECG, and Holters at 3, 6, and 12 months. Recurrence was defined as any atrial arrhythmia (AA) > 30 seconds.Receiver operator curve (ROC) analysis revealed that a low voltage threshold of 1.0 mV had the highest value (0.735). The percentage LVA surface area resulting from a threshold of 1.0 mV that predicted AA recurrence was 11.6%. Univariate and multivariate analysis revealed the percentage LVA was the strongest predictor of AA recurrence. The 12-month freedom from AA was 84.6% and 52.9% for subjects under and over the low voltage area threshold respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: A voltage threshold of 1.0 mV is proposed as a threshold for defining LVA using the spherical catheter, but a range of approximately 0.5-1.5 mV yielded similar performance. Increased low voltage area in the pre-ablation atrial map was associated with a higher risk of AA recurrence.

articles.title: Economic comparison of emerging and alternative robotic surgical platforms versus established multiport da Vinci systems in urologic surgery: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: To systematically evaluate the economic evidence comparing emerging robotic surgical platforms with established da Vinci systems in urologic surgery, a systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 and prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261433387). PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for English-language studies published between January 1, 2021 and June 25, 2026. Studies reporting extractable procedure-level or component-specific cost data for emerging robotic platforms were eligible. Comparative studies versus da Vinci systems constituted the primary evidence, while non-comparative economic reports were retained as contextual evidence. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale or Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools. Of 2,577 identified records, 12 studies were included. Evaluated platforms comprised Hugo RAS, Senhance, Sentire C1000, Hinotori, Versius, EDGE MP1000/MP2000, and da Vinci SP. Radical prostatectomy was the most frequently studied procedure. Economic methodologies varied substantially and included time-driven activity-based costing, activity-based costing, hospital-system cost analysis, variable surgical cost analysis, and patient out-of-pocket cost assessment. Hugo RAS and Senhance/Sentire showed lower costs in selected studies or cost components, although longer operating room utilization and implementation-related inefficiencies offset part of these differences in some settings. Da Vinci SP was associated with comparable or higher costs than multiport systems. Evidence for Hinotori, Versius, and EDGE remained limited. No platform demonstrated a consistent overall cost advantage across studies. The economic performance of robotic platforms depends on instrument strategy, operating room efficiency, procedural volume, hospitalization, and local procurement arrangements rather than platform price alone. Standardized prospective multicenter economic evaluations are needed to support procurement and health-technology decisions.

articles.title: Comparative validation of standard screening tools and an exploratory model for detecting obstructive sleep apnea in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVES: Despite representing a highly prevalent comorbidity, standard screening tools for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) lack validation in the hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) population. We sought to prospectively evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of three widely used screening tools against gold-standard polysomnography in an HCM cohort and to explore the potential for a tailored predictive model.

METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, patients with HCM completed the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), Berlin (BQ) and STOP-Bang questionnaires before undergoing inpatient overnight polysomnography.

RESULTS: Of 159 participants (median age 60; 64% male), 90 (57%) had OSA (46% mild, 26% moderate, 28% severe). Standard tools yielded modest performance: STOP-Bang [AUC 0.59 (0.50-0.68), sensitivity 77% (68-86), specificity 40% (28-52)]; ESS [AUC 0.58 (0.49-0.67), sensitivity 24% (15-33), specificity 92% (86-98)]; and Berlin [AUC 0.62 (0.53-0.71), sensitivity 65% (55-75), specificity 57% (45-69)]. In contrast, an exploratory model incorporating age, BMI, and waist-hip ratio showed promising preliminary results [AUC 0.82 (0.74-0.88), sensitivity 60% (48-72), specificity 84% (75-91)].

CONCLUSIONS: This study underscores the high prevalence of OSA in patients with HCM and demonstrates that standard screening tools developed for the general population perform poorly in this cohort, complicating clinical triage when polysomnography is delayed. While the derived exploratory model may represent an improvement in risk stratification, these findings require extensive external validation. Targeted screening strategies tailored to the unique pathophysiology of HCM remain necessary to improve OSA identification and management in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Association of pre-transplant right ventricular function parameters with long-term cardiovascular outcomes following kidney transplantation.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: The hemodynamic effects of end-stage kidney disease and associated pulmonary hypertension may impair right ventricular (RV) function and influence cardiovascular (CV) outcomes after kidney transplantation (KT). We aimed to evaluate the association between pre-transplant echocardiographic RV function parameters, including RV strain, and long-term CV outcomes following KT. In this retrospective cohort study, we included adult KT recipients at a single Midwest academic center from 2015 to 2024 who had adequate-quality pre-transplant echocardiograms and follow-up at our institution. RV function parameters included tricuspid annular systolic velocity (S'), tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), fractional area change (FAC), RV index of myocardial performance (RIMP), and RV free wall strain measured by two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as a composite of CV death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, cerebrovascular accident, heart failure hospitalization, coronary revascularization, or sustained ventricular arrhythmias. Among 371 patients (mean age 53.5 ± 13.1 years; 56% male) followed for a median of 4.9 years (IQR, 3.1-6.4), 79 (21.2%) experienced MACE. On univariable Cox analysis, RIMP and RV strain parameters were associated with MACE, whereas S', TAPSE, and FAC were not. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed lower MACE-free survival in patients with abnormal mid and apical RV strain, whereas the basal and dichotomized average-strain comparisons were not significant. In multivariable models, only average, mid, and apical RV strain remained independently associated with MACE. Pre-transplant RV strain was independently associated with long-term MACE after KT and may aid CV risk stratification. Further studies are needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance feature-tracking strain characterization across phenotypic spectrum of danon disease.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: To characterize atrial and ventricular strain across the phenotypic spectrum of Danon disease (DD) and explore their relationships with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) extent. This retrospective case-control study included 27 DD patients (median age 17 [range 10-50] years; 15 males) and 32 healthy controls. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging was performed at 3-T with cine and LGE. Structural, functional, and LGE parameters were assessed. Kruskal-Wallis H test with Dunn's test and Bonferroni correction was used for intergroup comparisons; Mann-Whitney U or t-test for two-group comparisons; Spearman's correlation; and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis were used. Left atrial (LA) and right atrial (RA) strain were impaired across all DD subgroups versus controls, with LA strain impairment evident even in the hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) subgroup with preserved LVEF. LV global longitudinal strain (LV-GLS) was reduced across all subgroups, whereas global circumferential strain (GCS) and global radial strain (GRS) impairment were confined to hypertrophic and dilated cardiomyopathy (HCM-DCM) and dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) subgroups. Mid-ventricular longitudinal strain was relatively preserved (P = 0.062). LGE extent correlated with GRS (all P < 0.01). Left atrial conduit strain rate (LASRe) demonstrated the best diagnostic performance (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.981; sensitivity 88.9%, specificity 100%). CMR feature-tracking revealed phenotype-specific bi-atrial and biventricular strain abnormalities in DD. Atrial strain impairment was detectable even in HCM with preserved LVEF, suggesting early mechanical dysfunction. LASRe showed promising discrimination and warrants validation. HCM-DCM may represent a possible transitional phenotype; longitudinal validation is required.

articles.title: Written exposure therapy as treatment for comorbid PTSD and SUD: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness, feasibility, and acceptability of Written Exposure Therapy (WET) when it is used as a component in integrated treatment of comorbid PTSD and Substance Use Disorder (SUD). A systematic review and meta-analysis was used to synthesise foundational knowledge regarding WET.

RECENT FINDINGS: Twelve studies were included and analysed in the review. Random-effects meta-analysis of six studies showed large overall pre/post decrease in PTSD severity (Hedges' g = 1.18, 95% CI [0.68, 1.72], p < 0.001). Rate of retention (69.03%) was higher than typically seen in integrated prolonged exposure treatments for PTSD-SUD. The majority of participants and providers found WET feasible and acceptable. A minority of participants found concurrent treatment for both disorders burdensome. Findings suggest that can be an effective component in integrated treatment of PTSD-SUD, owing to its efficacy, brevity, and low-burden of integration. Limitations of the current findings include small samples, lack of comparator groups, and limited information regarding treatment components and change in SUD.

articles.title: Preoperative classification of histopathological growth patterns in colorectal liver metastases using prospective 18 F-FDG PET/CT.
articles.abstract: Colorectal liver metastases (CLM) exhibit distinct histopathological growth patterns (HGPs) at the metastasis-liver interface, clinically relevant for prognosis and potential predictive value. This study investigates the feasibility of using Fluorine-18 Fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomography Computed Tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) to preoperatively classify HGPs in CLM and secondly investigate PET parameters as prognostic markers for overall survival (OS). In a prospective study at Umeå University Hospital (June 2013-December 2017), 78 patients with resectable CLM underwent contrast-enhanced liver MRI and 18F-FDG PET/CT imaging. HGP classification was performed on tissue sections according to 2017 international guidelines. PET features (SUVmean [standardised uptake value], SUVmax, metabolic tumour volume [MTV] and first-order texture metrics) were analysed to distinguish encapsulating (eHGP) from replacement (rHGP) patterns. In pretreated patients, multivariate logistic regression including both metabolic and texture parameters identified significant associations for parameters from the fixed level threshold algorithm (VuePoint Sharp IR) with small odds ratios. Overall, PET parameters showed limited ability to discriminate between eHGP and rHGP. OS was superior with eHGP versus rHGP (log-rank p = 0.045). In chemonaïve patients, SUV-based metrics showed unadjusted exploratory associations with OS after liver surgery, varying by reconstruction/delineation and were not significant after correction for multiple testing. FDG-PET-derived parameters were not reliably associated with HGP and did not support non-invasive HGP prediction in this cohort. eHGP was associated with superior survival, underscoring the value of HGP assessment for prognostication while alternative non-invasive biomarkers remain to be identified.

articles.title: Effects of photobiomodulation therapy on secondary healing of the palatal donor site after free gingival graft harvesting: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated photobiomodulation (PBM) therapy for postoperative pain and secondary wound healing at the palatal donor site after connective tissue harvesting. Following PRISMA guidelines, five databases were searched through 20 October 2025 for randomized controlled trials comparing PBM therapy with appropriate controls. Primary outcomes were postoperative pain (visual analogue scale, VAS) and epithelialization; secondary outcomes were analgesic consumption, remaining wound area, and bleeding. Random-effects meta-analysis was used, risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool and certainty of evidence with GRADE. Nine randomized controlled trials with 299 participants were included. Day-1 pain could not be pooled. No statistically significant difference in postoperative pain was observed at day 3 or day 7, with reductions of approximately 1.2 and 0.4 points on a 0-10 scale. Complete epithelialization at 14 days was more than twice as frequent, with no significant difference at day 21. The remaining wound area at day 7 was smaller by approximately 22 mm². Heterogeneity was moderate for pain and low for healing outcomes. PBM therapy may increase the proportion of palatal donor sites achieving complete epithelialization at 14 days. For postoperative pain the evidence is very uncertain, and no statistically significant reduction was observed at either pooled time point. Most trials carried a high or unclear risk of bias, and treatment protocols were heterogeneous. Larger trials with standardized dosimetry are needed to establish the clinical value of PBM therapy at the palatal donor site.

articles.title: Muscle Lipid Localization Relates to Insulin Sensitivity: Responses to Exercise and Weight Loss Interventions.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract: Subcellular lipid localization in skeletal muscle associates with insulin sensitivity in humans, yet these lipid distributions do not substantially revert after 12 weeks of insulin-sensitizing lifestyle interventions. This suggests interventions may need to occur earlier, before prediabetes or type 2 diabetes develops, or that lipid localization responds rapidly to acute changes in energy balance and physical activity that may not be captured following typical weight loss or exercise training interventions. To address this gap, we assessed the effect of acute and chronic insulin-sensitizing interventions across a spectrum of metabolic health in three separate studies. Individuals with obesity and normal glucose tolerance (NGT, n= 35, 39.4±1.0 yrs, BMI 35.7±0.7) or prediabetes/type 2 diabetes (pre/T2D, n=34, 43.8±1.3 yrs, BMI 35.3±0.7) completed 12-week interventions (combined weight loss plus exercise, weight loss alone, exercise alone, or delayed control). Endurance-trained athletes (n=20, 27.3±1.2 yrs, BMI 22.1±0.4) performed 1.5 hours of acute exercise at 50% or 70% VO2max under fed and/or fasted conditions. Muscle biopsies obtained pre/post intervention or acute exercise were fractionated into sarcolemmal, mitochondrial/ER, cytosolic, and nuclear compartments and analyzed by targeted lipidomics. Triacylglycerols were inversely associated with insulin sensitivity across all compartments. Ceramides showed inverse associations in sarcolemmal, mitochondrial/ER, and nuclear fractions, but a positive association in the cytosol. In contrast, 1,2-DAGs were positively associated with insulin sensitivity in mitochondrial/ER, cytosolic, and nuclear compartments. Neither lifestyle interventions nor acute exercise substantially altered subcellular lipid distribution. Overall, subcellular lipid localization was strongly associated with insulin sensitivity yet changed inconsistently following acute and chronic interventions, regardless of metabolic status. These data suggest that more dramatic changes in weight and fitness, and/or interventions longer than 12 weeks may be required to modify muscle subcellular lipids linked to insulin resistance.

articles.title: Heterogeneity in dosages and treatment conditions forms a blurred picture of the results.
Integrated clinical, biochemical, cardiac imaging, and transcriptional changes under MEK inhibition in complicated Noonan syndrome.
articles.journal: European journal of human genetics : EJHG
articles.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a major contributor to morbidity and mortality in Noonan syndrome (NS), with a high risk of heart failure and arrhythmias. Lymphatic dysplasia represents another clinically significant manifestation often associated with significant morbidity. Emerging evidence suggests that MEK inhibitors may target these severe complications. Seven pediatric patients with molecularly confirmed NS and severe, treatment-refractory HCM and/or lymphatic effusions received oral trametinib treatment under compassionate use. Clinical, biochemical, and echocardiographic parameters were longitudinally assessed to evaluate efficacy and safety. Transcriptomic analysis of RAS/MAPK pathway-related gene expression was performed in a subset of patients at baseline, one week after treatment initiation, and during prolonged therapy. Trametinib treatment was maintained at doses ranging from 0.0075 to 0.033 mg/kg/day for 3-45 months. All patients showed a rapid decrease in NT-proBNP levels, followed by significant reductions in interventricular septal thickness and, when present, left ventricular outflow tract obstruction. In patients with lymphatic dysplasia, trametinib was associated with sustained reduction of pleural effusions and improved respiratory status. Treatment discontinuation led to progressive clinical and biochemical worsening, with improvement after reintroduction, when performed. Transcriptomic analysis demonstrated early modulation of RAS/MAPK pathway signatures in most patients. Adverse events were mild (grade 1), predominantly dermatological, and manageable with dose adjustments. These findings provide additional clinical and molecular evidence supporting trametinib treatment as a targeted therapeutic strategy for cardiac and lymphatic manifestations in NS. Prospective studies are needed to define long-term safety, optimal dosing, and treatment duration of MEK inhibition in NS and other RASopathies.

articles.title: Corrigendum to 'Enhancing spectral interpretability and band selection prior to prediction model development via CAKE' [Talanta 310 (2026) 130168].
The impact of maternal cardiovascular risk factors and diseases on offspring cardiovascular health.
authors: endorsed by the International Lipid Expert Panel (ILEP)
articles.abstract: The increasing number of pregnancies among women at cardiovascular risk or with established cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) has become a major global health concern because of its lasting influence on the health of their offspring. Maternal heart disease, hypertension, diabetes, obesity, and abnormal lipid levels, including also elevated lipoprotein(a), can disturb fetal growth and development, leading to changes in the heart, blood vessels, and metabolism that raise the risk of CVD problems in childhood and later life. The rising age of pregnant women, especially in the developed countries, also increases this risk. These effects result from a combination of inherited traits and alterations in the intrauterine environment, including impaired blood flow, inflammation, oxidative stress, and disrupted nutrient transfer through the placenta. Such disturbances can modify the structure and function of the developing cardiovascular system and contribute to lifelong vulnerability to CVDs. Studies from large populations show that children born to mothers with cardiovascular conditions have about twice the risk of developing CVD compared with those born to healthy mothers. Good maternal health before and during pregnancy, supported by balanced nutrition, regular physical activity, and effective control of blood pressure, lipids, body weight, and blood sugar, is strongly linked to better outcomes for both mother and child. Although current lifestyle interventions in pregnancy have shown promising effects on maternal wellbeing, their influence on the long-term cardiovascular health of the offspring remains uncertain. Strengthening preconception care, well-designed healthcare education, improving cardiovascular screening in women of reproductive age, and promoting heart-healthy habits across the life course are essential to prevent the transfer of cardiovascular risk from one generation to the next.

articles.title: Beyond Steatosis: HIV-Associated Liver Fibrosis and the Limits of Current Screening Algorithms.
Unveiling structural bottlenecks of dynamic disorder in a density-tunable glass former: From strong to fragile regimes.
articles.abstract: Fragility characterizes how rapidly a glass-forming liquid slows down upon supercooling, but whether strong and fragile behaviors arise from the same microscopic relaxation mechanism remains unclear. Here, we address this question using a density-tunable soft-repulsive binary mixture spanning distinct fragility regimes and analyze particle jump dynamics within the framework of dynamic disorder. Across these regimes, we show that increasing fragility is accompanied by progressively broader cage-lifetime distributions and increasingly non-exponential survival probabilities, revealing non-Poisson cage-to-jump statistics governed by fluctuating jump rates and slowly evolving structural variables. To characterize their structural origin, we first identify the neighbor ranks most strongly coupled to jump motion using Kullback-Leibler divergence and Pearson correlation analyses. We then introduce a structural slowness parameter that combines these neighbor-distance fluctuations into a reduced slow coordinate for constructing the slow-fluctuation survival probability. A comparison with the actual survival probability shows that localized neighbor-distance fluctuations control the jump rate in the strong regime, whereas extended neighbor rearrangements become relevant in the intermediate and fragile regimes, increasing the effective dimensionality of the slow-variable space. In the fragile regime, distance-based descriptors alone become insufficient at the lowest temperature, where the Voronoi free volume captures additional cage-volume fluctuations in the rate-controlling slow variable. Point-to-set correlations (PTS) grow with fragility, but the spatial extent of the slow variables exceeds the PTS length. These results reveal how the structural bottleneck for microscopic rate fluctuations evolves across density-tuned fragility regimes, linking dynamic disorder, multidimensional slow variables, and static correlations in glass-forming liquids.

articles.title: Performance of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways in patients with suspected myocardial infarction: a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In patients with suspected myocardial infarction, the 0/1 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 1 h) is recommended in current guidelines for early risk stratification. However, individual trials used different safety outcomes, and efficacy outcomes were inconclusive or not assessed. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of all randomised controlled trials to synthesise the totality of the evidence, assess heterogeneity across trials, and evaluate clinically relevant outcomes using harmonised definitions across trials.

METHODS: In this systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform from inception to July 6, 2026, without language restrictions, for randomised trials comparing the safety and efficacy of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways (blood draws at 0 h and 3 h, ie, standard care). Individual participant data were obtained and outcome definitions were harmonised. The primary analysis used a two-stage random-effects meta-analysis. After receipt of the individual participant data but before data harmonisation or analysis, the primary safety outcome was refined to a composite of all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction within 30 days, from the originally specified composite of all-cause death or any new myocardial infarction. The primary efficacy outcomes were emergency department length of stay and direct discharge from the emergency department. This meta-analysis is registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261383452).

FINDINGS: Our systematic review identified five randomised trials, all of which provided individual participant data. Among these, the definition of the primary safety outcome varied, and in four trials emergency department length of stay was not reported for the whole analysis population. We included 110 933 patient presentations (55 489 managed with the 0/1 h pathway and 55 444 managed with the 0/3 h pathway). Within 30 days, all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction occurred in 446 patient presentations (0·8%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 562 patient presentations (1·0%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled odds ratio [OR] 0·83 [95% CI 0·45-1·53]; I2=62·9%; τ2=0·143). Emergency department length of stay was 314 min (IQR 211-481) in the 0/1 h pathway group versus 308 min (209-453) in the 0/3 h pathway group (random-effects pooled geometric mean ratio 1·03 [95% CI 0·85-1·25]; I2=99·2%; τ2=0·024). Direct discharge from the emergency department occurred in 37 190 patient presentations (67·0%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 36 485 patient presentations (65·8%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled OR 1·31 [95% CI 0·79-2·16]; I2=97·8%; τ2=0·156).

INTERPRETATION: Across the available randomised trials, short-term adverse event rates were low with both pathways, but the pooled safety estimate remained imprecise. On average, earlier cardiac troponin retesting did not reduce emergency department length of stay or clearly increase direct discharge, and substantial between-study heterogeneity indicates that treatment effects might not translate uniformly across health-care systems. For hospitals considering transitioning from a 0/3 h to a 0/1 h pathway, implementation decisions should take broader diagnostic and organisational considerations into account.

FUNDING: Swiss National Science Foundation, Swiss Heart Foundation, University Hospital Basel, University of Basel, and Foundation for Cardiovascular Research Basel.

articles.title: Faster troponin, same time in the emergency department: what is next for acute coronary syndrome assessment?

Ruzaltatug rezetecan versus chemotherapy for EGFR-mutated advanced non-small-cell lung cancer progressing after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy (HERON-Lung01): interim analysis of a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in China.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ruzaltatug rezetecan is a novel HER3-directed antibody-drug conjugate that has shown promising antitumour activity and manageable safety in pretreated EGFR-.mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in a phase 1 trial. We aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of ruzaltatug rezetecan with chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC that had progressed after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy.

METHODS: HERON-Lung01 is a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial conducted at 62 sites in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years, with locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC harbouring an EGFR activating mutation (exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation), and had progressed during or after EGFR-TKI therapy. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive ruzaltatug rezetecan 8·0 mg/kg or chemotherapy comprising pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 plus carboplatin (area under the curve 5) or cisplatin 75 mg/m2 for four cycles, followed by maintenance pemetrexed. All treatments were administered intravenously on day 1 of each 3-week cycle. Block randomisation was stratified by presence of brain metastases, EGFR mutation subtype, and use of a first-line third-generation EGFR-TKI. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS), as assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR), in the intention-to-treat population. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06671379). Recruitment is complete, with the trial ongoing.

FINDINGS: Between Nov 29, 2024, and Jan 29, 2026, 498 patients were randomly assigned to receive ruzaltatug rezetecan (n=250) or chemotherapy (n=248). The median age was 60·0 years (IQR 54·0-68·0); 276 (55%) patients were female and 222 (45%) male. At the prespecified interim PFS analysis, median follow-up was 7·7 months (95% CI 7·1-8·3). BICR-assessed PFS was significantly longer with ruzaltatug rezetecan than with chemotherapy (median 8·3 months vs 5·4 months; hazard ratio 0·47 [95% CI 0·36-0·60]; one-sided p<0·0001). Grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in 101 (41%) of 248 patients receiving ruzaltatug rezetecan and 93 (39%) of 239 patients receiving chemotherapy, most commonly decreased neutrophil count (64 [26%] of 248 patients vs 46 [19%] of 239 patients), decreased white blood cell count (29 [12%] vs 29 [12%]), and anaemia (15 [6%] vs 26 [11%]). TRAEs led to treatment discontinuation in three (1%) patients in the ruzaltatug rezetecan group and three (1%) in the chemotherapy group. One death (unknown cause) in the ruzaltatug rezetecan group was considered by the investigator to be possibly treatment related.

INTERPRETATION: Ruzaltatug rezetecan significantly prolonged PFS compared with chemotherapy, with a manageable safety profile, in EGFR-TKI-resistant, EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC. These data support ruzaltatug rezetecan as a potential treatment option in this setting.

FUNDING: Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals.

articles.title: Incidence and Risk Factors for Invasive Mold Infections in Children During First-Line Chemotherapy for Primary Acute Leukemia: A National Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Invasive mold infections (IMI) are life-threatening complications during treatment for pediatric acute leukemia. Population-based data on IMI incidence, timing, and outcomes during first-line therapy remain limited. We aimed to provide a nationwide epidemiological overview of IMI during first-line treatment of pediatric acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and explore potential treatment-related risk factors.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective nationwide cohort study of all children (<18 years) initiating first-line chemotherapy for AML or ALL in Denmark during 2008-2022. IMIs were classified as proven or probable according to 2020 European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer and the Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium criteria by review of microbiology, imaging, pathology, and chart data. Follow-up covered first-line chemotherapy. Competing risk-adjusted cumulative incidence of IMI was estimated, risk factors were evaluated using Cox regression, and survival after IMI was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method.

RESULTS: Among 621 patients, 43 (6.9%) developed IMI: 14/90 (15.6%) with AML and 29/531 (5.5%) with ALL. In adjusted Cox regression, AML was associated with higher IMI hazard than ALL (HR 5.6, 95% CI, 2.6-12.1), whereas no other prespecified risk factors were independently associated with IMI. Incidence rates were 38.6 per 100 patient-years in AML and 2.7 in ALL. Nearly half of IMIs occurred beyond 90 days after initiation of first-line chemotherapy. Four patients experienced a second distinct IMI episode; Aspergillus species accounted for 37 out of 47 (79%) episodes and non-Aspergillus molds for 10 out of 47 (21%). IMI-associated death occurred in 10 patients (1.6% of the cohort), yielding a case fatality rate of 23% among IMI cases; IMI was present in 43% of all deaths.

CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide cohort, IMI occurred more frequently than reported in many previous pediatric studies, particularly in AML. IMIs were observed throughout first-line therapy, despite antifungal prophylaxis, and were associated with substantial mortality, emphasizing the need for sustained clinical vigilance beyond induction.

articles.title: Real-World Use of Ceftazidime-Avibactam for Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacterales Infections in Children: A 7-Year Cohort from a Latin American Referral Center.
articles.journal: Journal of the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric data on ceftazidime-avibactam (CAZ-AVI) for carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) infections remain limited, particularly in Latin America, where Klebsiella pneumoniae carbapenemase (KPC)-producing organisms are endemic. We describe the clinical characteristics, microbiological profile, and outcomes of children with CRE infections treated with CAZ-AVI at a tertiary referral center in Colombia.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of children younger than 18 years with clinically significant CRE infections treated with CAZ-AVI between January 2018 and June 2025. Clinical, microbiological, treatment, and outcome data were collected. The primary outcome was clinical response at the end of therapy.

RESULTS: Forty-three patients were included (median age, 11 years [IQR, 6-15]); 25 patients (58%) were immunocompromised, 29 (67%) required PICU admission, and 16 (37%) presented with septic shock. K. pneumoniae was the predominant pathogen (33 patients, 77%), and KPC was the most common carbapenemase detected (39 patients, 91%). Clinical improvement within 72 h occurred in 40 patients (93%), with a median time to response of 2 days (IQR, 2-3). Overall, 40 patients (93%) achieved clinical cure. The estimated 30-day survival probability was 95.3% (95% CI, 88.8-100), recurrence occurred in 3 patients (7%), and no treatment-related adverse events were documented.

CONCLUSION: In this real-world pediatric cohort from a KPC-endemic setting, CAZ-AVI was associated with favorable clinical outcomes and good tolerability. These findings support its role as an important therapeutic option for pediatric CRE infections and underscore the importance of mechanism-guided antimicrobial management.

articles.title: Safety and efficacy of the 0/1 h pathway for myocardial infarction in the emergency department: an international, pragmatic, stepped-wedge, cluster-randomised, controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The evaluation of patients with suspected myocardial infarction relies on serial measurements of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin. We aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of implementing the guideline-recommended 0/1 h pathway, compared with a 0/3 h pathway, in hospitals that had not yet adopted the newer strategy.

METHODS: PRESC1SE-MI was an international, pragmatic, stepped-wedge, cluster-randomised, controlled, masked-endpoint trial at 19 hospitals in ten countries. The study included consecutive adults presenting to the emergency department with acute non-traumatic chest discomfort and suspected myocardial infarction. Hospitals using a 0/3 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 3 h) as standard care were randomly allocated to implement the 0/1 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 1 h) after 6 months (early implementation) or 12 months (late implementation). The trial was designed to test the non-inferiority of the 0/1 h pathway for safety and its superiority for efficacy. The non-inferiority margin was set at an odds ratio of 1·3. Analyses were done in the full analysis set. The coprimary safety outcome was a composite of death from any cause or new type 1 myocardial infarction within 30 days, and the coprimary efficacy outcome was emergency department length of stay. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05649384, and is active but no longer enrolling.

FINDINGS: Between Dec 1, 2020, and Dec 31, 2024, 71 983 consecutive patient presentations were screened, of which 67 624 (93·9%) met the eligibility criteria and comprised the full analysis set. Median age was 59 years (IQR 46-73); 29 954 (44·3%) patient presentations were in female patients and 37 670 (55·7%) were in male patients. 13 753 (22·2%) of 62 060 patient presentations with available data were in patients with known coronary artery disease, and 5855 (8·7%) patient presentations had an adjudicated index diagnosis of myocardial infarction. Overall, 36 464 patient presentations were managed with a 0/3 h pathway and 31 160 with the 0/1 h pathway. Death from any cause or new type 1 myocardial infarction occurred in 454 (1·2%) patient presentations in the 0/3 h group and in 341 (1·1%) patient presentations in the 0/1 h group (adjusted odds ratio 0·93 [95% CI 0·77-1·13]; pnon-inferiority=0·0004). The median emergency department length of stay was 309 min (IQR 203-470) in the 0/3 h pathway and 309 min (207-474) in the 0/1 h pathway (ratio of adjusted median times 1·00 [95% CI 0·97-1·02]; two-sided p=0·65).

INTERPRETATION: Implementation of the 0/1 h pathway met the prespecified non-inferiority criterion for the 30-day composite safety outcome but did not shorten emergency department length of stay compared with the 0/3 h pathway. In this setting, implementation of the 0/1 h pathway alone should therefore not be expected to improve emergency department throughput.

FUNDING: Swiss National Science Foundation, Swiss Heart Foundation, University Hospital Basel, University of Basel, Foundation for Cardiovascular Research Basel, Fondazione Ricerca Molinette, Idorsia, and Roche.

articles.title: Generalised eruptive histiocytosis mimicking lymphoma relapse in a patient with previous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
articles.abstract: A 92-year-old man with a history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma treated with chemoradiotherapy, and later with radiotherapy for an isolated cutaneous relapse with complete response, presented with a 1-month history of multiple asymptomatic erythematous-to-violaceous papules and nodules on the face, trunk, and upper limbs. Given his oncological history and previous skin involvement, lymphoma relapse was the leading diagnostic concern, with cutaneous metastases and sarcoidosis also considered. However, skin biopsies showed a non-Langerhans cell histiocytic infiltrate expressing CD45, CD68, and CD163, without CD1a, CD20, PAX5, S100, or Langerin expression. Skin and blood flow cytometry identified no abnormal cell populations, and a PET-CT scan showed no abnormal metabolic activity. Clinicopathological correlation narrowed the differential to group C (cutaneous) histiocytosis, and subsequent spontaneous regression of the lesions over 3 months without treatment supported the diagnosis of generalised eruptive histiocytosis. At 15 months of follow-up, there was no recurrence or evidence of active disease. This case illustrates that cutaneous histiocytoses can mimic several inflammatory and neoplastic conditions, including lymphoma relapse, reinforcing the need to actively resist cognitive bias in people who have had cancer through reflective reassessment, broad differential diagnosis, and biopsy confirmation.

articles.title: Pandemic waves as the outcome of coupled social and disease dynamics: A mathematical modelling study.
articles.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic was strongly shaped by population behavioural responses. As cases surged, populations adopted contact precautions that reduced infection levels. This, in turn encouraged relaxation of control measures and prepared the ground for the next pandemic wave. Standard mathematical models do not account for this interaction between infection dynamics and behaviour. Here, we compare a standard transmission model to a coupled behaviour-disease model. We parameterise the models for 13 European countries, using data on SARS-CoV-2 infection incidence and stringency of control measures. We show how coupling behavioural and disease dynamics improves the ability of mathematical models to explain and predict crucial features of pandemic waves. Our findings demonstrate how behavioural feedback influences not only current transmission patterns but also the timing and magnitude of future pandemic waves. Such models could help decision-makers anticipate population responses to public health interventions, thereby contributing to scenario planning and intervention design.

articles.title: Infection-age structured transmission model highlights the efficacy of case-finding operations.
articles.abstract: Early epidemic control often relies on case-finding operations. To assess their theoretical efficacy, we develop an infection-age structured early growth transmission model that incorporates symptom-based diagnosis, mass screening, and both forward and backward contact tracing. By deriving integral equations for the forward and backward tracing rates and coupling them with a Lotka-Euler-type equation for the early growth rate, we obtain a closed deterministic system. This system enables the computation of early growth rates and reproduction numbers under different case-finding scenarios. Using parameter values calibrated from the 2021 Yangzhou outbreak, the theoretical scenario comparisons show that diagnosis alone provides limited control of early epidemic growth, whereas the integrated case-finding scenario substantially suppresses transmission. The results further show that reducing the effective reproduction number below one requires stronger mass screening and contact tracing when infected individuals generate more secondary infections on average. Together, these findings indicate that the theoretical efficacy of case-finding operations depends jointly on intervention intensity and the effective transmission structure.

articles.title: Angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitors and renal outcomes in patients with heart failure: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitors (ARNi) significantly improve cardiovascular outcomes in patients with heart failure (HF). Their effects on kidney function in this population remain incompletely characterized. A systematic review and meta-analysis were performed to explore the impact of ARNi on renal outcomes.

METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, and PubMed databases were searched for randomized trials comparing ARNi with renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system inhibitors (RAASi) alone. Outcomes included the incidence of worsening renal function, hyperkalaemia, hypotension, >50% decrease in eGFR, end-stage renal disease, rise in serum creatinine >2.5 mg/dl, and acute kidney injury. Risk of bias was assessed using the ROB 2.0 tool.

RESULTS: Fifteen studies with 31 574 individuals were included. Mean age was 67 years and 33% were female. ARNi significantly reduced the incidence of worsening renal function events [relative risk (RR): 0.83, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.71-0.96; P = .01], corresponding to 13 fewer events per 1000 patients. ARNi were also associated with a lower risk of >50% decline in eGFR (RR: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.47-0.78; P < .001) and acute kidney injury events (RR: 0.82, 95% CI: 0.69-0.97; P = .024) compared with RAASi alone. There was no significant difference in the incidence of hyperkalaemia >5.5 mmol/L between groups, while ARNi were associated with a higher incidence of symptomatic hypotension (RR: 1.54, CI 95%: 1.35-1.76; I2 = 69%; P < .001).

CONCLUSIONS: ARNi are associated with a lower risk of adverse renal outcomes compared with RAASi in patients with heart failure. However, this benefit should be interpreted alongside an increased risk of symptomatic hypotension.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of digital health in primary care: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Digital health has rapidly expanded, accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic, and is widely used for consultations, disease management, and efficiency improvements in primary care. While it is considered clinically effective and potentially cost-effective, evidence on economic impact remains limited. Previous reviews have been condition-specific, highlighting the need for a systematic review focused on cost-effectiveness of digital health within primary care.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this systematic review was to summarize and investigate the cost-effectiveness of digital health among adult primary care patients.

METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted using the PICO framework. Studies were included if they involved adult primary care patients (≥18 years), evaluated digital health interventions versus usual care, and reported cost‑effectiveness based on economic evaluations. PubMed, Scopus, and Health Business Elite were searched in January 2025. An updated search was conducted in September 2026. Results were reported in a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) flow diagram. Methodological quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Checklist for Economic Evaluations. A narrative synthesis was performed.

RESULTS: The initial search identified 4,091 records and resulted in 47 included studies. The updated search in September 2026 identified an additional 658 records, of which seven additional studies met the eligibility criteria, resulting in a total of 54 included studies. Most were trial‑based full economic evaluations focusing on digital interventions for depression and anxiety, adopting a healthcare perspective. Overall, digital health interventions were frequently associated with favourable economic outcomes, although results varied by intervention, population, economic evaluation method, and time horizon.

DISCUSSION: This review is innovative in its focus on the cost‑effectiveness of digital health interventions in primary care. Unlike previous reviews, it systematically synthesises trial‑ and model‑based economic evaluations. The review advances the field by clarifying the economic evidence base and has practical implications for decision‑makers considering the implementation of digital health in primary care. The review is limited by rapidly evolving digital health terminology, the exclusion of grey literature, and substantial methodological heterogeneity between trial‑based and model‑based economic evaluations. Potential selection bias related to digital literacy may limit generalisability.

CONCLUSIONS: Digital health in primary care demonstrated favourable economic outcomes across a broad range of clinical areas, with the majority of studies reporting cost-effective results. However, despite this positive pattern, methodological heterogeneity limits comparability between studies. Greater standardization of economic evaluation methods and reporting is therefore needed to strengthen the evidence base and support implementation decisions.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO registration no. CRD42025644904; [https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42025644904].

articles.title: Reply to the letter titled "comment on "effect of combined aerobic and resistance training on kidney health in adults with type 2 diabetes: A randomized controlled trial".
Patient Engagement in a Virtual Cardiac Rehabilitation Platform: Secondary Analysis of the ERA-Nudge Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mobile health interventions have the potential to motivate healthy behaviors. Optimal strategies for engaging patients in cardiac rehabilitation (CR) through mobile health interventions remain unclear.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine patient engagement in a mobile app platform for CR across patient characteristics and by the method of delivery of nudge messages over the 12 weeks of CR.

METHODS: The authors analyzed data from the ERA-Nudge (Enhancing Rehabilitation Adherence Through Optimized Nudge) study, a pragmatic randomized trial conducted at an urban safety-net hospital testing nudges (short messages designed using behavioral economics to elicit behavior change) to enhance CR adherence and log healthy activity. Trial patients were given access to a smartphone-based app. Nudges were initially sent as app notifications. Later in the study, patients received nudges as text messages. We assessed patient characteristics associated with app engagement, and we compared time spent in the CR app among patients receiving nudges as app notifications vs text messages. The trial enrolled patients who could engage with messages in either English or Spanish at an urban safety-net hospital with a qualifying CR diagnosis and a smartphone from May 2019 to May 2023. We describe minutes spent in the app across patient characteristics and by type of nudge delivery, and we compare the 2 approaches using unadjusted and multivariate negative binomial regression over the 12 weeks of CR.

RESULTS: In total, 223 patients received nudges: 74 via app notification and 149 via text message. Overall, patients spent an average of 219 (SD 328) minutes in the app, and 3 (1.3%) patients used the app for zero minutes. Patients receiving only app nudges spent a mean of 167 (SD 365) minutes in the app, and patients receiving text messages and app nudges spent 245 (SD 306) minutes in the app (unadjusted ratio 1.5, 95% CI 1.1-2.0; P=.02). After adjusting for age category, sex, primary language, CR location (hospital vs home), and highest education achieved, Spanish-preferring patients, patients with some college education, and patients receiving text messages spent more time in the app. Patients receiving nudges as text messages and app notifications spent an adjusted ratio of 1.8 (95% CI 1.2-2.5; P=.002) times as many minutes in the app compared to those getting nudges as app notifications.

CONCLUSIONS: Among an urban safety-net population, text message nudges were associated with greater time in the app compared to nudges delivered as app notifications. These findings suggest that text messages may result in greater patient engagement for mobile health interventions.

articles.title: Reducing oil content in fried potato chips is associated with attenuated diet-induced metabolic disturbances: Insights into gut-liver metabolic associations from multi-omics analysis.
articles.abstract: This study investigated metabolic responses to diets containing fried potato chips with different oil contents using an 8-week feeding model in male C57BL/6 J mice. Reduced-oil (22.30% oil) and high-oil (38.22% oil) potato chips were incorporated into experimental diets at 40% (w/w), resulting in dietary fat contents of 11.92% and 18.29% and calculated energy densities of 4.09 and 4.41 kcal/g, respectively. Compared with the high-oil potato-chip group (HFG), the reduced-oil potato-chip group (LFG) exhibited lower final body weight (53.71 ± 3.89 vs. 63.79 ± 4.88 g, respectively), accompanied by less pronounced dyslipidemia, oxidative alterations, and hepatic lipid accumulation. Serum triglyceride concentrations were lower in the LFG (1.28 ± 0.01 vs. 1.79 ± 0.01 mmol/L, respectively), while biochemical and histological findings indicated comparatively attenuated hepatic metabolic disturbances. Gut microbiota profiling, targeted hepatic bile acid analysis, and untargeted hepatic lipidomics revealed distinct microbial and metabolic profiles between the dietary groups. Exploratory multi-omics integration further identified associations among gut microbial composition, hepatic bile acid profiles, and lipidomic features. However, because food intake was measured at the cage level and the diets differed in energy density and overall nutritional composition, the observed metabolic differences cannot be attributed specifically to oil reduction. The multi-omics associations also do not establish causal mechanisms. Collectively, these findings characterize metabolic responses to nutritionally distinct fried-potato-chip-containing diets and provide preliminary evidence supporting further investigation of reduced-oil food-processing strategies.

articles.title: Hospital at home for the acute care of patients with liver disease: a clinical review.
articles.journal: Liver transplantation : official publication of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the International Liver Transplantation Society
articles.abstract: Patients with liver disease experience frequent hospitalizations for complications such as hepatic encephalopathy, ascites, infections, and gastrointestinal bleeding, resulting in substantial healthcare utilization and reduced time spent at home. Hospital at Home (HaH) is an increasingly utilized care model that delivers hospital-level acute care in the patient's home through multidisciplinary care teams, remote monitoring, and home-based diagnostic and therapeutic services. This review summarizes the rationale for considering HaH in liver disease and outlines key program components. We review the existing evidence supporting HaH, including the limited hepatology-specific literature as well as broader data from randomized trials and systematic reviews in related populations. We show early studies in patients with cirrhosis suggest that HaH is feasible and safe in appropriately selected individuals. Furthermore, the broader studies comparing HaH to traditional care have consistently demonstrated comparable or improved clinical and patient-centered outcomes such as mortality, readmission rates, cost of care, patient experience, and caregiver burden. HaH represents a promising patient-centered addition to the continuum of acute care for individuals with advanced liver disease. Broader implementation in hepatology will depend on establishing evidence-based patient selection frameworks, defining disease-specific models of care, and carefully designed studies to better understand the impact of HaH on clinical outcomes, healthcare utilization, equity in access to care as well as patient-reported and caregiver outcomes.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics, treatment, and prognosis of sexual-related rectal foreign bodies: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Rectal foreign bodies (RFBs) inserted for sexual purposes are an increasingly reported surgical emergency, but the evidence remains fragmented across case reports and small series. We systematically reviewed the literature on sexual-related RFBs to characterize clinical features, management strategies, and outcomes.

METHODS: We searched major English- and Chinese-language databases for studies published from January 1, 2000 to July 31, 2026 that reported patients with RFBs related to sexual activity (PROSPERO registration CRD420261467581). Case reports, case series, and cohort studies were eligible. Patient-level pooled proportions with Wilson 95% CIs and random-effects meta-analyses of proportions (Freeman-Tukey transformation, DerSimonian-Laird estimator) across series with 5 or more patients were calculated. Study quality was assessed with Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) checklists and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). Quality thresholds were defined a priori by the authors based on established conventions in the systematic review literature.

RESULTS: Fifty-nine studies (34 case reports, 21 case series, 4 cohort studies) from 22 countries, comprising 376 patients, were included; 40 studies were of high, 17 of moderate, and 2 of low quality. Most patients were male (98.1%), with a mean age of approximately 49 years; autoerotic insertion accounted for 92.5% of cases. Glass objects (20.3%) and sex toys (19.3%) were the most common foreign bodies. Overall, 61.4% of patients presented more than 24 h after insertion and 98.2% had attempted self-removal. Abdominal pain (25.9%) and rectal pain (24.6%) predominated. Transanal extraction was achieved in 73.4% of patients (meta-analytic estimate 71.9%, 95% CI, 60.8-81.9; I2 = 72.5%), laparotomy in 19.2%. Bowel perforation occurred in 4.7% (pooled 3.3%), stoma creation in 7.2% (pooled 5.1%), and mortality was 0.6% (pooled 1.4%, 95% CI, 0.4-3.0; I2 = 0%). Overall retrieval success was 99.7%.

CONCLUSION: Sexual-related RFBs occur predominantly in middle-aged men who present late, often after failed self-removal. Transanal extraction succeeds in most patients; perforation, stoma creation, and death are uncommon. A stepwise, escalation-based management approach is supported by the available evidence.

articles.title: Technical variation and evidence maturity in gender-affirming peritoneal vaginoplasty: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peritoneal vaginoplasty is increasingly being adopted within feminizing genital gender-affirming surgery. However, the way and extent to which peritoneum is used for vaginal lining varies considerably, and the term "peritoneal vaginoplasty" appears to encompass several technically distinct procedures.

AIM: To assess technical variation and surgical indications in gender-affirming peritoneal vaginoplasty, and evaluate evidence maturity through the lens of the Idea, Development, Exploration, Assessment and Long-term study (IDEAL) framework.

METHODS: A systematic search identified studies reporting use of peritoneum in gender-affirming vaginoplasty. Data on surgical characteristics and indications were extracted as primary outcomes and data on evidence maturity as secondary outcomes. Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines were followed, and risk of bias was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute checklists.

OUTCOMES: Primary outcomes were technical characteristics, including flap number, configuration, vascularization, extent of vaginal lining, surgical indication, postoperative management, and reported outcomes. Secondary outcomes included study design, rationale for innovation, prospective registration, informed consent, outcome selection, outcome measures, and IDEAL stage.

RESULTS: Of 1425 screened records, 23 full-text and five video articles were included, representing 14 centers. Techniques were categorized into four groups based on peritoneal flap number, configuration, and vascularization. Substantial heterogeneity was observed in technical characteristics, surgical indications, and postoperative management. Techniques were largely center-specific, and indications ranged from routine use in primary vaginoplasty to genital skin deficiency, patient preference, and secondary reconstruction. No included publication reported prospective registration or referred to a published protocol. Informed consent was reported in six studies. Rationale for innovation, outcome selection, and technical choices was absent or limited. Safety was the predominant outcome, with 22 of 23 full-text studies reporting complications, whereas only three included survey-based patient-reported outcomes. Two studies were most consistent with IDEAL stage 2a. The remaining studies could not be staged.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: Peritoneal vaginoplasty should not be regarded as a single intervention. Technique- and indication-specific evaluation is needed to identify which patients may benefit most from each approach and in whom specific techniques may be inappropriate or contraindicated.

STRENGTHS AND LIMITATIONS: Strengths include the comprehensive technical overview and structured evaluation using IDEAL. Limitations include incomplete reporting, probable participant overlap, and heterogeneity precluding pooled outcome synthesis.

CONCLUSION: Peritoneal vaginoplasty comprises a heterogeneous group of techniques rather than a standardized procedure. Technical variation, differing indications, and heterogeneous outcome reporting preclude clinically meaningful comparison of safety and effectiveness. Prospective, technique- and indication-specific studies are required to determine the clinical role of individual techniques.

articles.title: Perioperative venous thromboembolism prophylaxis during penile prosthesis surgery without routine drain placement: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients undergoing penile prosthesis surgery are at elevated risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE), yet perioperative thromboprophylaxis is not addressed in current urologic guidelines and the safety of subcutaneous heparin (SqH) without drain placement remains unclear. We aim to evaluate the safety and efficacy of perioperative SqH for VTE prevention in penile prosthesis surgery performed without surgical drains.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed all penile prosthesis surgeries performed at a single institution from January 2019 to January 2025 in which no drain was placed. Demographics, comorbidities, Caprini risk scores, VTE risk factors, hematoma incidence, and 90-day postoperative complications were compared between patients who did and did not receive perioperative SqH.

RESULTS: The primary outcome of our study was postoperative VTE, with secondary outcomes including hematoma formation and 90-day complications. Of 524 patients, 85% were classified as high risk for VTE (Caprini ≥ 5). A total of 246 (47%) received perioperative SqH. VTE occurred in 0.7% (2/278) of patients who did not receive SqH, while no VTE was observed in the SqH group. Hematoma rates were similar between groups (SqH 2.0% vs non-SqH 2.2%; P = .920). Caprini scores and most comorbidities were comparable, though smoking (P = .043) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) (P = .025) were more common in the non-SqH cohort.

DISCUSSION: Implementation of VTE prophylaxis with SqH in penile prosthesis patients may reduce the risk of VTE in a high-risk population and is relatively cost effective and simple to implement. The main strength of this study is that it is the largest cohort of penile prosthesis patients receiving SqH to be analyzed. In addition, our patient population is unique in the lack of drain placement postoperatively. The study is limited by its retrospective nature and potential bias in reporting complications. The cohort of patients receiving SqH prophylaxis did not develop a VTE and adverse event rates were similar between groups suggesting a possible protective benefit without increasing postoperative complications.

articles.title: Peptides for male sexual dysfunction: a systematic review of emerging evidence.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sexual dysfunction remains highly prevalent among men and significantly impacts quality of life. Peptides are short chains of amino acids designed to mimic endogenous signaling molecules and modulate a variety of physiological pathways.

AIM: To systematically review the available human evidence evaluating the effects of peptide and peptide-derived therapies on male sexual function, reproductive hormones, and semen parameters.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials, crossover studies, prospective clinical studies, and experimental physiological studies evaluating peptide-based interventions in adult men.

OUTCOMES: Outcomes of interest included erectile function, sexual desire, orgasmic and ejaculatory outcomes, reproductive hormones, semen parameters, and adverse events.

RESULTS: Twelve studies comprising 372 male participants met inclusion criteria. Investigated peptides included melanocortin receptor agonists (PT-141/bremelanotide and Melanotan II), kisspeptin analogues, and oxytocin. Melanocortin receptor agonists demonstrated the most consistent improvements in erectile function, producing significant increases in penile rigidity and erectile duration in healthy men and men with erectile dysfunction, including sildenafil non-responders. Kisspeptin increased gonadotropin secretion, enhanced sexual brain processing, and improved penile tumescence and measures of sexual desire in men with hypoactive sexual desire disorder. Oxytocin showed mixed effects, with potential benefits on orgasm intensity, sexual satisfaction, and partner interaction, but no consistent improvements in erectile function, ejaculation latency, or semen parameters.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: Peptide-based interventions may influence male sexual health through distinct peripheral, central, endocrine, and relational mechanisms, offering potential adjuncts or second-line alternatives for men who have failed or are intolerant of first-line pharmacotherapy.

STRENGTHS AND LIMITATIONS: Strengths include the synthesis of human clinical evidence across multiple peptide classes and principal domains of male sexual function. Overall, studies were limited by small sample sizes, heterogeneous populations, short follow-up durations, and a lack of comparative studies.

CONCLUSION: Melanocortin receptor agonists currently have the strongest evidence for improving erectile outcomes, while kisspeptin represents a promising emerging therapy for sexual desire and reproductive endocrine modulation. However, the evidence base remains limited, and further studies are required before these therapies can be incorporated into routine clinical practice.

Impact of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease on survival after chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy in large B-cell lymphoma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR T-cell) therapy is the standard of care for relapsed/refractory (R/R) large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL). The impact of pre-existing chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) on outcomes of LBCL after CAR-T cell therapy are not well characterized. This study aimed at evaluating the significance of pre-existing COPD on overall survival (OS) in LBCL treated with CAR-T cell therapy.

METHODS: We conducted propensity score-matched cohort study using registry data from TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Patients aged ≥18 years who received CAR T-cell therapy were identified using ICD-10-PCS and CPT codes and stratified by the presence (or absence) of documented diagnosis of COPD (ICD-10-CM: J44.x). Propensity score matching was performed adjusting for age, gender, ethnicity, and race. Primary outcome was OS. Secondary endpoints included hematologic and non-hematologic toxicities.

RESULTS: A total of 173 patients with COPD and 173 without COPD were included. Cohorts were balanced across most baseline characteristics. Axicabtagene ciloleucel was the most commonly administered product in both cohorts. The COPD cohort demonstrated significantly worse median OS (760 vs. 1412 days). The 5-year OS was higher in patients without COPD (HR=0.72 (95%CI=0.52-0.99), p = 0.048).

CONCLUSIONS: COPD is associated with inferior OS following CAR T-cell therapy in R/R LBCL. These results advocate for the integration of COPD status into pre-CAR T-cell risk stratification protocols and for proactive pulmonary optimization, multidisciplinary evaluation, and heightened vigilance in this cohort. Patients with R/R LBCL and concurrent COPD should not be categorically excluded from CAR T-cell therapy.

articles.title: The Role of Health Coaches on a Clinical Research Team: Development & Implementation of a Health Coach-Informed Research Model During User Testing of a Lupus Whole Health Intervention.
articles.abstract: The purpose of this paper is to describe the impact of a health coach-informed research model within an interdisciplinary lupus research team during intervention development and user testing. Health coaches are increasingly integrated into lifestyle medicine interventions for chronic disease management, but their role has largely been described in intervention delivery, with limited research on their integration during development. The Lupus WHEEL (Whole Health Empowerment for Endotypes of Lupus) program, is an interdisciplinary intervention designed for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), adapted from a shared medical appointment model originally developed for type 2 diabetes. Two National Board-Certified Health and Wellness Coaches (NBC-HWC) served as active interdisciplinary research team members across three phases: pre-user testing, during user testing, and post-user testing. Integration was supported by disease-specific clinical immersion, weekly interdisciplinary team meetings, and a coach-developed debrief tool for real-time observations. Throughout the study, coach integration extended beyond intervention delivery to include program refinement, scope-of-practice review, structured debriefing, and shared research team decision-making, resulting in restructured session sequencing, revised goal tracking, and content adjustment based on participant feedback. Notable insights were that earlier integration of health coaches expanded their role beyond delivery, fostered bidirectional learning, and highlighted the value of clinical immersion, offering a replicable framework for lifestyle medicine research teams. Trial Registration: Whole Health Empowerment for Endotypes of Lupus: Improving Quality of Life in SLE (WHEEL). ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT06720584. URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06720584. Unique Protocol ID (IRB): Pro00111699.

articles.title: The Financial Impact of Antivascular Endothelial Growth Factor Drug Durability.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To examine the yearly cost of antivascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy borne by patients and to assess the major contributors to patient cost.

METHODS: A retrospective, cross-sectional cost analysis was conducted of 29 250 insured patients in a single practice receiving anti-VEGF injections over a 21-month period between January 1, 2023, and September 30, 2024. Direct costs to the patient were abstracted, including patient copay and patient-responsible portions of imaging, medication, procedure, and visit costs; medication costs were based on average sales price. Transportation cost and opportunity cost associated with missed work were operationalized to estimate indirect costs, using age-stratified employment rates and median earnings from the United States Bureau of Labor Statistics for both patients and accompanying caregivers.
