RESULTS: The mean (±SD) direct cost per visit was $91.72 ± $22.22. Indirect costs per visit varied by indication, with a mean indirect cost per visit of $97.89 for patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and $164.44 for patients with diabetic macular edema (DME) for a half day of missed work, and $167.98 and $301.09, respectively, for a full day off work. Indirect costs accounted for 45.37% to 74.86% of total patient cost for a half day off, and 58.76% to 84.50% for a full day off. Relative to the baseline of 12 monthly bevacizumab injections received annually (half-day off scenario), the equivalent total patient cost accrued would correspond to a mean annual number of injections of 9.32 and 10.00 for aflibercept 2 mg, 11.09 and 11.35 for aflibercept 8 mg, and 9.05 and 9.78 for faricimab 6 mg in patients with neovascular AMD and patients with DME, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Patient cost is driven more by visit frequency and its associated indirect costs than by drug price. Less frequent dosing with a more durable agent can therefore lower the total cost experienced by patients despite a higher acquisition price.

articles.title: Neutrophil extracellular traps and routine coagulation biomarkers predict pregnancy outcomes in recurrent pregnancy loss.
articles.abstract: Recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) is a complex reproductive disorder involving immune dysregulation, inflammation and coagulation imbalance. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) may provide a mechanistic link between inflammatory activation and thrombosis-related placental dysfunction but their combined predictive value with routine coagulation biomarkers remains insufficiently defined. This single-center prospective study enrolled 350 pregnant women at 6-10 weeks of gestation, including controls, women with successful ongoing pregnancy (SOP), and women with RPL adverse outcomes during follow-up. Candidate biomarkers included NETs, myeloperoxidase-DNA complex, protein S (PS), protein C (PC), antithrombin (AT), D-dimer, and platelet aggregation indicators. After correlation-based screening, five predictors were retained: NETs, PS, PC, AT, and D-dimer. Logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM), k-nearest neighbor (KNN), and decision tree (DT) models were developed and internally validated using five-fold cross-validation. SVM achieved the highest averaged area under the curve (AUC = 0.9420), whereas KNN showed the highest overall accuracy (81.43%). Multivariable regression indicated that elevated NETs and D-dimer were associated with increased risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes, whereas higher PS, PC, and AT were associated with protective effects. These findings suggest that NETs and routine coagulation biomarkers may provide useful information for early risk stratification in RPL. Further multicenter external validation and longer follow-up are required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Static plantar pressure measurements do not predict high-pressure regions during shod walking in diabetic subjects.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Foot ulceration is a serious complication of diabetes and associated with elevated plantar pressures during walking. Custom accommodative insoles are most effective when informed by dynamic pressure data; however, static pressure collection offers a faster and more clinically feasible alternative. The ability of static pressure measurements to predict dynamic high-pressure regions remains unclear and needs investigation.

METHODS: Static in-shoe and static barefoot plantar pressure measurements were compared with dynamic in-shoe pressure data from 31 feet in 18 participants with elevated dynamic in-shoe forefoot pressures. Dynamic high-pressure regions were defined as sensors exceeding 200 kPa. Peak plantar pressure at dynamic high-pressure regions and sensor-level Pearson and Spearman correlations were compared between static and dynamic measurements. Receiver operating characteristic curves were used to determine static pressure thresholds for identifying dynamic high-pressure regions. Dice coefficient, sensitivity, and positive predictive value assessed spatial agreement and classification performance.

FINDINGS: Static peak plantar pressure at dynamic high-pressure regions and sensor-level correlations were higher for static in-shoe than static barefoot comparisons (p < 0.001). Static pressure thresholds were 40.4 kPa for in-shoe and 55.8 kPa for barefoot data, with AUCs of 0.85 and 0.72, respectively. Dice coefficients were 0.31 and 0.27, sensitivity was 0.80 and 0.66, and positive predictive values were 0.22 and 0.19 for static in-shoe and barefoot data.

INTERPRETATION: Static pressure measurements demonstrated an association with dynamic plantar pressure but limited spatial agreement with predicting dynamic high-pressure regions. Static measurements may provide information about dynamic high-pressure regions but should not replace dynamic in-shoe pressure assessment for targeted offloading of insoles.

articles.title: Effect of a simulation-based risk perception intervention on glycemic control in community-dwelling older adults with uncontrolled type 2 diabetes: A quasi-experimental study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study examined the effect of a simulation-based risk perception intervention on glycemic control and diabetes self-care behaviors in community-dwelling older adults with uncontrolled type 2 diabetes.

METHODS: A quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design with repeated measures was conducted in Phetchaburi, Thailand. Sixty-two older adults (aged ≥60 years; HbA1c >7%) were pair-matched on age, sex, education, and diabetes duration, forming 31 matched pairs; one member of each pair was assigned to the experimental or control group by coin toss. The 12-week intervention, grounded in Rothman and Kiviniemi's health risk communication framework, combined individual and group sessions using a blood flow simulation model, motivational interviewing, and biweekly follow-up. Data were analyzed using ANCOVA and mixed-design ANOVA.

RESULTS: After adjusting for baseline HbA1c, the experimental group showed a statistically significant reduction in HbA1c at Week 12 than controls (adjusted means 7.67 vs. 7.97; F(1,59)=75.63, p<.001, partial η²=0.56). A statistically significant time × group interaction was observed for overall self-care behaviors (F(2120)=43.21, p<.001, partial η²=0.41) and all four subdomains.

CONCLUSIONS: A simulation-based risk perception intervention was associated with statistically significant improvements in glycemic control and self-care behaviors among older adults with uncontrolled diabetes, although the HbA1c reduction fell below the minimal clinically important difference. This nurse-assisted approach shows potential for future implementation in community and primary care settings; however, feasibility of delivery by routine primary care nurses amid existing nursing shortages in some localities was not evaluated and warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Development and Validation of a Prediction Model for Recurrent Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The definition of very high risk from the American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology 2018 and 2026 cholesterol guidelines may oversimplify heterogeneity in recurrent atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk.

OBJECTIVES: We developed a prediction model for recurrent ASCVD and compared its performance with the 2018 cholesterol guideline.

METHODS: We used electronic health records from Kaiser Permanente Southern California (KPSC) for model development and the REGARDS (Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke) cohort for external validation. We included adults with a prior ASCVD and followed them for recurrent ASCVD or up to 10 years. We used elastic net regularization for predictor selection and a Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards model for model development. Model performance was evaluated using time-dependent area under the curve, sensitivity, and specificity compared with the 2018 guideline.

RESULTS: Among 70,310 and 5,239 adults from KPSC and REGARDS, 17,344 and 1,185 experienced recurrent ASCVD during the median (Q1, Q3) follow-up of 6.1 (2.5, 10) and 8.3 (4.0, 10) years, respectively. Time-dependent area under the curves were 0.68 (95% CI: 0.66-0.69) in KPSC and 0.67 (95% CI: 0.65-0.69) in REGARDS. Compared with the 2018 guideline, using a 5-year 15% risk threshold, the model classified a similar proportion of patients as high risk and improved sensitivity from 64% (95% CI: 62%-66%) to 73% (95% CI: 71%-75%) in KPSC and from 69% (95% CI: 65%-72%) to 73% (95% CI: 69%-76%) in REGARDS; specificity remained similar in KPSC (51% and 52%) and improved in REGARDS (from 45% to 50%).

CONCLUSIONS: Compared with the 2018 cholesterol guideline, the new model improves identification of individuals at very high risk of recurrent ASCVD, supporting more personalized treatment decisions.

articles.title: Transcatheter Solution to Atypical Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Drainage in a Single Ventricle Patient.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Partial anomalous pulmonary venous drainage (PAPVD) is typically incompatible with single ventricle physiology if left unrepaired before cavopulmonary connection. This report describes a rare anatomical variant and novel interventional solution.

CASE SUMMARY: An 8-month-old female with hypoplastic left heart variant developed profound cyanosis following bidirectional Glenn because of unrepaired PAPVD of the right upper pulmonary vein to the superior vena cava (SVC). Retrospective 3-dimensional reconstruction of the patient's neonatal computed tomography angiogram revealed a small interlobar vessel between the anomalous pulmonary vein and the anatomically normal right lower pulmonary vein. This interlobar vessel's gross dilatation and anatomical features permitted percutaneous device occlusion of the PAPVD connection to the SVC, isolating SVC return to the cavopulmonary circulation while preserving unobstructed pulmonary venous return to the atrium.

DISCUSSION: Surgical and interventional solutions are reviewed in the context of this unusual anatomical variant.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: In the uncommon circumstance of an unrecognized anomalous pulmonary vein with connections to both systemic and pulmonary venous circulations, consideration may be given to interventional occlusion of the PAPVD connection to the systemic vein. Retrospective application of contemporary 3-dimensional reconstruction tools can add great value in delineating complex or unusual anatomy.

articles.title: Left Ventricular Aneurysm Associated With Severe Aortic Regurgitation.
articles.abstract:
IMAGES: Multimodality imaging findings.

CASE SUMMARY: A 53-year-old man presented with exertional chest tightness. Transthoracic echocardiography showed severe aortic regurgitation, left ventricular dilatation, basal inferior wall thinning with paradoxical motion, and an eccentric regurgitant jet impinging on the basal inferior wall. Coronary computed tomography angiography excluded obstructive disease. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance demonstrated an inferior aneurysm with near-transmural late gadolinium enhancement. Four-dimensional flow imaging further characterized the regurgitant jet trajectory, with a localized vortex and elevated wall shear stress. He underwent bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Multimodality imaging demonstrated spatial concordance between eccentric regurgitant flow, regional hemodynamic abnormalities, and myocardial injury.

articles.title: Patient-Specific Physical and Computational Models for Replicating Coronary Stent Deployment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous coronary intervention with balloon angioplasty and stent implantation is standard therapy for coronary artery disease, but accurate prediction of patient-specific procedural outcomes remains challenging.

CASE SUMMARY: Patient-derived imaging data were used to reconstruct three-dimensional coronary models, which were further translated into a three-dimensional-printed physical phantom and a finite element digital twin. The identical stent and balloon were deployed in the phantom; stent deployment was computationally simulated, and both were compared with the clinical optical coherence tomography.

DISCUSSION: Both platforms reproduced key procedural features. The phantom moderately underestimated, and the finite element model overestimated, the clinically observed lumen gain. These proof-of-concept findings support the technical feasibility of building patient-specific artificial twins, but quantitative accuracy will require further model refinement and validation before clinical use.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Patient-specific models offer a means to visualize procedural characteristics and test alternative stent designs or deployment strategies outside the patient.

articles.title: Trends in Care and Outcomes Among Emergency Department Patients With Chest Pain Without Myocardial Infarction.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To characterize trends in hospitalization, downstream care, and outcomes among emergency department (ED) patients with chest pain without acute myocardial infarction (AMI) diagnosis.

METHODS: We analyzed claims data from a large national commercial insurer (2007-2021) and identified ED visits with a principal diagnosis of chest pain. We excluded visits with secondary diagnoses of AMI or other significant cardiopulmonary conditions and those preceded by cardiac testing, coronary procedures, AMI admissions, or chest pain ED visits within 6 months. Usage outcomes included index hospitalization (principal), 7-day cardiac testing, and 30-day coronary revascularization. The principal clinical outcome was 180-day postindex AMI hospitalization. Adjusted annual rates were estimated using generalized estimating equations, and trends were assessed using inverse-variance-weighted linear regression.

RESULTS: We included 773,250 index chest pain ED visits (mean age 54.2 years; 54.3% women). Adjusted hospitalization rates declined from 42.7% to 18.6%, and 7-day noninvasive testing decreased from 26.7% to 9.1%. Revascularization within 30 days declined from 5.8% to 3.6%. Overall, 180-day postindex AMI hospitalization showed no significant temporal trend, ranging from 0.8% to 1.2%. However, a modest increasing trend was observed among patients aged 70 years and older.

CONCLUSION: Among ED patients with chest pain without AMI diagnosis, hospitalization, cardiac testing, and revascularization declined substantially from 2007 to 2021. Overall, downstream AMI hospitalization remained stable, although those in older adults experienced modest rises. Although efforts continue to identify additional low-risk patients for safe discharge, future research should quantify the potential benefits of hospitalization and cardiac testing, particularly for older adults and high-risk patients.

articles.title: A High-Yield Solution to the Emergency Medicine Resident Scholarly Activity Requirement.
Cardiac electrophysiology procedures must be performed exclusively by trained electrophysiologists: A statement from the Heart Rhythm Society and Heart Rhythm Advocates.
articles.abstract: The exponential growth of clinical cardiac electrophysiology (CCEP) as a subspecialty has created an important unresolved question in contemporary cardiovascular medicine: Who is qualified to perform electrophysiology (EP) procedures? As nonelectrophysiologists increasingly perform procedures that require the nuanced expertise of a trained or board-certified CCEP (eg, permanent pacemaker implantation, implantable cardioverter-defibrillator implantation, cardiac resynchronization therapy, and transvenous lead extraction), the consequences for patient safety, procedural outcomes, and health system efficiency have become impossible to ignore. This article presents a comprehensive, evidence-based argument that cardiac EP procedures must be performed exclusively by physicians who have completed accredited fellowship training in CCEP. We draw upon peer-reviewed outcome data, guideline-derived training standards from the Heart Rhythm Society, the American College of Cardiology, and American Heart Association, including the newly published 2026 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association/Heart Rhythm Society Advanced Training Statement on Clinical Cardiac Electrophysiology, as well as registry analyses spanning hundreds of thousands of patients to substantiate our position. The risks associated with suboptimal operator training are not theoretical; they are measurable, costly, and potentially fatal. The evidence presented demonstrates that operator specialization in EP is among the most powerful independent predictors of procedural safety and long-term outcomes and can be as important as institutional volume in many analyses. We call upon hospital credentialing committees, national medical societies, payers, regulatory bodies, and policymakers worldwide to establish and enforce a definitive standard: only trained CCEPs should implant and manage cardiac implantable electronic devices, perform catheter ablation procedures, execute transvenous lead extraction, and conduct formal EP studies.

articles.title: Validation of a prognostic model for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and evaluation of methods to include related data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Prognostic models estimate a patient's individual risk of future health outcomes using clinical and demographic data, supporting treatment planning. Such models are particularly useful for chronic diseases, where predicting disease progression can help guide interventions and improve patient outcomes. In chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), several models have been developed to predict long-term mortality risk. However, these models are often trained on patients diagnosed 10 to 20 years ago, and outcomes may have improved since then. As a result, such models may be miscalibrated by the time they are published, potentially limiting their clinical utility.

METHODS: We aim to validate an existing COPD prognostic model for five-year mortality from the date of diagnosis to explore potential miscalibration over time and across regions. Moreover, we evaluated modelling methods to improve predictive performance in target datasets by incorporating related (ancillary) data while accounting for heterogeneity, including: (i) developing a logistic regression model in the target data, (ii) Intercept Recalibration to update the intercept using the target data, (iii) Logistic Recalibration to update both intercept and calibration slope using the target data, and (iv) Membership-based recalibration that reweights ancillary data using propensity scores. These approaches were assessed using newly collected target datasets, or by leveraging the existing development dataset only.

RESULTS AND CONCLUSION: The existing model demonstrated similar discrimination across the external validation settings, with mean AUC values ranging from 0.79 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.72 to 0.85) to 0.80 (95% CI 0.78 to 0.83). However, mean calibration-in-the-large (CITL) values varied from 0.001 (95% CI -0.25 to 0.34) to 0.46 (95% CI 0.29 to 0.61) in the newly available target data, likely reflecting shifts in baseline risk. Among the methods evaluated for improving prediction by incorporating ancillary data while accounting for heterogeneity, Intercept Recalibration was a simple method that generally reduced CITL to near-zero levels. Importance weighting using propensity scores also provided a potential alternative, although its performance varied across settings. These methods can be applied during development using existing data or after development with newly collected data, and may improve model calibration for the target population.

articles.title: Mechanical limitation of compression depth in a common CPR training manikin.
articles.abstract: Current CPR guidelines recommend a chest compression depth of 5-6 cm. During an in-hospital training project using a widely adopted manikin (Resusci Anne, Laerdal Medical), integrated distance sensors consistently recorded compression depths below this target range.Further mechanical evaluation showed that a depth of 6 cm is not physically achievable with this model; the maximum displacement did not exceed 5.7 cm, even when measurements included chest components as recommended by the manufacturer. Although limited to a single, widely used manikin, these findings highlight the need to reassess calibration and mechanical design to ensure alignment with guideline-based CPR training and accurate performance feedback.

articles.title: Perceptions of Opisthorchis viverrini infection and raw fish consumption among villagers in Champasak Province, Lao PDR: a qualitative study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Opisthorchis viverrini (O. viverrini) infection is a major public health concern in the Greater Mekong Subregion. Lao People's Democratic Republic (Lao PDR) has been reported to have a remarkably higher prevalence. This study aimed to explore local perceptions and practices related to O. viverrini infection and raw fish consumption. We conducted a qualitative study on O. viverrini infection in villages in Champasak Province, Lao PDR.

METHODS: We investigated villagers' perceptions and practices, focusing on the consumption of raw fish dishes. Focus group discussions (FGDs) were carried out in September 2024 and April 2025 in four villages, two in Khong District and two in Mounlapamok District.

RESULTS: A total of 68 participants from four villages participated in 10 FGD sessions. The mean age was 46.5 years (range: 19-73; SD = 11.15), with 26.5% male and 73.5% female. The majority of participants had completed primary school (44.1%) or had some secondary education (33.8%). In total, 94.1% of the participants reported farming as their main occupation. The participants were generally uncertain when asked whether they knew the disease. Some believed that alcohol, lime juice, and other ingredients could kill parasites in raw fish meat. All participants reported having eaten raw fish dishes, except for two elderly women who had stomach problems. The participants said that fish considered suitable for raw fish dishes were those with scales and of larger size. Feeding raw fish to small children was restricted, but there was no clear age standard for when children were permitted to begin eating raw fish dishes. In addition to typical koi pa and larp pa, participants mentioned other raw fish preparations, including pa te (thinly sliced raw fish) and pa chum (raw fish dipped in a hot pot). They also described the use of wasabi as a condiment for raw fish. Sharing food, including raw fish dishes, was described as a common social practice in the community, and refusing such sharing was considered difficult.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that raw fish consumption is shaped by local contexts. Understanding these contexts may help inform the development of culturally appropriate, community-specific interventions.

articles.title: Implementation of home-based Digital Rehabilitation in sub-Saharan Africa: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The need for rehabilitation in sub-Saharan Africa is largely unmet due to challenges such as limited access to rehabilitation, lack of healthcare professionals, high costs, challenging geographical distance and poor health infrastructure. Home-based Digital Rehabilitation may offer an opportunity to overcome some challenges. However, little is known about successful implementation of home-based Digital Rehabilitation in sub-Saharan Africa. We aimed to identify the technologies used and the important factors considered for the implementation of home-based Digital Rehabilitation.

METHODS: We performed a scoping review according to the framework proposed by Arksey and O'Malley, with improvements made by Levac et al. The search strategy was developed on PubMed and translated to Embase, CINAHL, Cochrane, Web of science, IEEE, Science Direct and SpringerLink to identify literature published from 2018 to 2023 conducted in sub-Saharan African countries. We performed a gray literature search to supplement the results. We extracted data on technology and implementation determinants based on the domains of the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research 2.0 (CFIR) and summarized them narratively. In addition, 11 key stakeholders were consulted to explore their experiences with digital technologies and their perspectives on factors relevant to the implementation of home-based Digital Rehabilitation.

RESULTS: We included 25 studies in the final set of papers. Technologies such as applications, web-based programs, videoconferencing, short-message-services, television/radio, social media, and 3-D printers are already utilized for rehabilitation in sub-Saharan Africa. Important implementation determinants were identified in three of five CFIR domains, including intervention effectiveness, relative advantages, costs and the design, client acceptability, the use of implementation frameworks, and appropriate implementation strategies. Barriers to and facilitators of implementation were reported across studies, including the need for sufficient technical infrastructure and ongoing technical support to operate the technology.

CONCLUSION: The results of this study highlight the need to develop and implement sustainable Digital Rehabilitation approaches that consider all domains of the CFIR 2.0, including structural characteristics, religious and cultural factors, local conditions, local policies and legislation, and intervention financing. The implementation of home-based Digital Rehabilitation requires systemic adaptations, such as the development of an appropriate technical infrastructure and reimbursement mechanism, as well as increasing (digital) health literacy in society.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Stakeholders' experiences of the implementation of a multifactorial intervention for safe patient handling and movement: a qualitative explorative and descriptive study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite growing evidence for the effectiveness of safe patient handling and movement (PHM) interventions, there is limited insight into implementation and sustainment in routine healthcare. By focusing on stakeholders directly involved in implementation following a cluster randomised controlled trial (RCT), this study provides insight into the mechanisms through which a safe PHM intervention is enacted in practice and how the implementation processes contribute to implementation.

AIM: To explore stakeholders' experiences of implementing a multifactorial intervention for safe PHM, and to examine the determinants and perceived outcomes influencing its integration and sustained use in clinical practice.

METHODS: A qualitative explorative design was employed, using individual interviews with 25 implementation stakeholders (leaders, external facilitators, and implementation team members). The stakeholders were recruited from a cluster RCT evaluating the effectiveness and implementation of a multifactorial safe PHM intervention in Swedish regional and municipal healthcare units. Data were analysed with qualitative deductive-inductive content analysis using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) as a theoretical framework.

RESULTS: The analysis resulted in five deductive categories corresponding to CFIR constructs (innovation, inner setting, individuals, implementation process, and actual implementation outcomes) and 13 inductively developed categories. Determinants influencing the implementation of a safe PHM practice were described. The implementation outcomes reflected implementation, enactment of the intervention in practice, and conditions for sustained use, manifested through perceived changes in safety culture, work routines, and use of patient handling equipment.

CONCLUSIONS: This study identified key determinants and perceived outcomes influencing the implementation of safe PHM practices. The interdependence between leadership, facilitation, and participants' active engagement with knowledge shaped the implementation process, enabling translation into practice. Outcomes were reflected in the perceived integration of practices into clinical routines and changes in safety culture, indicating implementation. These findings highlight the importance of organisational and social processes in supporting the sustained use of new practices.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study is part of a cluster randomised controlled trial, registered at ClinicalTrials.gov on 2 November 2022 (ref NCT05276180).

articles.title: Distribution of combined p-values for baseline variables in a consecutive sample of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Combined p-values derived from summary statistics of baseline variables in randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are expected to follow a uniform distribution. Extreme values indicate similarity or dissimilarity across randomized groups. To date, investigations have been limited to a small number of clinical fields; here, we assess the distribution of combined p-values in a consecutive sample of RCTs.

METHODS: Based on a PubMed search between February 1 and 18, 2022, 568 RCTs were included. Baseline variables were analysed using Carlisle's method, yielding one combined p-value per RCT. A threshold of combined p-values of p ≤ 0.05 or p ≥ 0.95 was applied. Differences in combined p-value distributions between subgroups were assessed using the two-sample Anderson-Darling (AD) test.

RESULTS: 26.2% (149/568) of the included RCTs had combined p-values of p ≤ 0.05 or p ≥ 0.95, compared with the 10% expected by chance. Of these, 104 RCTs (18.3%) were found in the upper extreme tail of p ≥ 0.95 and 45 RCTs (7.9%) in the lower extreme tail of p ≤ 0.05. Smaller RCTs (N ≤ 100) had more extreme combined p-values than larger RCTs (N > 100) (AD test p = 0.001). RCTs with > 7 baseline variables had more extreme combined p-values than those with ≤ 7 variables (AD test p = 0.004). A sensitivity analysis showed that 20.6% of RCTs still had extreme combined p-values after controlling for reporting errors related to SE and SD. Another sensitivity analysis showed that some extreme results could be explained by assuming high correlations between baseline variables within an RCT.

CONCLUSION: A substantially higher proportion of RCTs in a consecutive sample exhibited extreme similarities or dissimilarities in baseline characteristics across groups than expected by chance (26.2% vs 10%), indicating problems with randomisation. Further investigation into the causes and implications of implausible baseline distributions in RCTs is warranted.

REGISTERED: 2023-03-20 at https://www.researchweb.org/fourol/project/280487.

articles.title: Serum endostatin is selectively reduced in non-steatotic chronic hepatitis C and normalizes after direct-acting antiviral therapy: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endostatin is an endogenous inhibitor of angiogenesis that has been linked to chronic liver disease and proposed as a circulating marker of fibrosis in hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. Although direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) reliably achieve viral eradication and improve liver-related outcomes, their effects on circulating endostatin have remained unknown.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Serum endostatin levels were measured in 92 patients with chronic HCV infection and compared with those in 30 healthy controls. In a longitudinal subgroup of 58 patients, samples were available before treatment, at weeks 4 and 12 of therapy, and at sustained virological response 12 (SVR12). Serum from 85 patients was analyzed at SVR12.

RESULTS: Patients with chronic HCV had significantly lower serum endostatin levels than healthy controls before therapy. This decrease was confined to patients without hepatic steatosis, whereas patients with steatotic liver disease exhibited endostatin levels comparable to those of healthy controls. Endostatin levels were not associated with advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis, as assessed by noninvasive fibrosis scores and ultrasound. In cirrhosis, serum endostatin levels were reduced after excluding patients with a glomerular filtration rate < 90 mL/min who had higher serum endostatin levels. During DAA therapy, serum endostatin increased in patients without steatosis and, by SVR12, reached levels similar to those in patients with steatotic liver disease and healthy controls. Endostatin was positively associated with age. After age adjustment, endostatin positively correlated with albumin, leukocyte and platelet counts, and negatively correlated with the model for end-stage liver disease score, bilirubin, international normalized ratio, glomerular filtration rate, and high-density lipoprotein. Because these variables did not differ between patients with and without steatotic liver disease, the differential regulation of endostatin in chronic HCV is likely driven by additional disease-specific mechanisms.

CONCLUSIONS: This study showed that chronic HCV is associated with reduced serum endostatin levels in patients without steatosis, which normalize after successful DAA therapy. Serum endostatin is not a marker of fibrosis severity in chronic HCV, either before or after viral clearance. Serum endostatin levels are increased in patients with impaired renal function, which is a confounding factor in patients with liver disease. Together, these findings provide preliminary evidence for a previously unrecognized pattern of endostatin dysregulation in chronic HCV that is almost reversed after antiviral cure.

articles.title: Anterior Abdominal Wall Pexy Stitch During Laparoscopic Peritoneal Dialysis Catheter Insertion Improves 1-Year Reoperation Rates.
articles.abstract: BackgroundPeritoneal dialysis (PD) is an increasingly popular renal replacement therapy, but catheter obstruction or migration can compromise patency. Catheter pexy (CP) and omentopexy have been described as prophylactic adjuncts to increase patency but not studied in a large cohort. We hypothesized that prophylactic CP would be associated with decreased one-year PD catheter reoperation.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included patients aged 18-89 who underwent PD catheter insertion at a single tertiary care facility between 2016 and 2023. The primary exposure was CP during PD catheter insertion. The primary outcome was one-year reoperation (removal or revision). Covariates included demographics, obesity classification, comorbidities, and concomitant omentopexy. Propensity-score matching (1:3 nearest neighbor method) analyzed the association of CP with 1-year catheter patency.ResultsOf 524 patients identified, 429 were included in the baseline cohort. Of those, 327 (76.2%) had prophylactic CP and 102 (23.8%) did not. Baseline characteristics were similar, except more frequent concomitant omentopexy in the CP group (36.1% vs 19.6%; P = 0.003). After excluding reoperations due to infection (n = 40) and fibrin plugging (n = 17), unadjusted one-year reoperation rates were lower for the CP group (11.8% vs 20.4%; P = 0.04). Estimated by inverse probability weighted regression adjustment, CP was associated with a 10.2% [95% CI -19.9% to -0.4%] decrease in one-year reoperation.ConclusionThis large cohort study is the first to demonstrate that prophylactic CP improves one-year PD catheter patency. Prospective randomized trials are warranted to establish the benefit of prophylactic CP.

articles.title: Diffusion MRI-Based Fetal Thermometry Using Cerebrospinal Fluid: A Translational Feasibility Study.
articles.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Noninvasive fetal temperature assessment could improve MRI safety monitoring and provide insight into fetal physiology. Diffusion MRI is a potential approach because water diffusivity in free fluids is temperature dependent. However, the applicability of adult-derived diffusivity-temperature calibration to neonatal and fetal CSF remains uncertain.

PURPOSE: To evaluate the feasibility of diffusion MRI for noninvasive estimation of a diffusion-derived proxy of fetal temperature in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

STUDY TYPE: Prospective feasibility study.

POPULATION/SUBJECTS: 11 preterm neonates (postmenstrual age, 30.0-40.6 weeks; 5 male, 6 female) underwent CSF diffusion MRI for translational validation, and 11 fetuses (gestational age, 27.6-37.6 weeks) underwent CSF diffusion MRI for in utero feasibility assessment.

FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 1.5T monopolar spin-echo echo-planar diffusion imaging for neonatal validation; 3T monopolar spin-echo echo-planar diffusion MRI for fetal imaging.

ASSESSMENT: Temperature was derived from CSF apparent diffusion coefficients using an established diffusivity-temperature calibration. Neonatal estimates were compared with pre and postscan axillary temperatures. Monte Carlo simulations evaluated the effects of noise, gradient-amplitude scaling errors, and calibration uncertainty.

STATISTICAL TESTS: Bland-Altman analysis, linear regression, descriptive statistics, Huber M-estimation, and Monte Carlo simulations were performed. Statistical significance for regression analyses was defined as p < 0.05.

RESULTS: Diffusion-derived CSF temperatures agreed with axillary measurements within approximately ±1°C in 11 preterm neonates and showed Bland-Altman biases of 0.41°C and 0.50°C for mean diffusion-derived temperature compared with pre and postscan axillary measurements, respectively. In 11 fetuses, the CSF temperature estimates using the Huber M-estimator were 37.13°C ± 0.41°C (mean ± SD). Monte Carlo simulations revealed a decrease in the temperature SD from about 4.5°C at SNR = 30 to 1.6°C at SNR = 80. Gradient-amplitude scaling errors of ±8% resulted in approximately 6.5°C-7°C absolute temperature bias, which was reduced to ≤ 0.1°C after ideal effective b value correction.

DATA CONCLUSION: Diffusion MRI enables feasible estimation of a diffusion-derived proxy of fetal temperature in CSF.

TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 1.

articles.title: The Scoop on Shots: A Cross-Sectional Survey Describing Where Adults in the United States Obtain Information About Vaccines.
articles.journal: American journal of health promotion : AJHP
articles.abstract: PurposeTo describe which information sources are most frequently used by adults in the United States to obtain information about vaccines, characterize which of these sources are perceived to be the most and least trustworthy, and examine the number of information sources used by various sociodemographic groups, with an emphasis on sex and age.DesignCross-sectional survey with quota sampling.SettingOnline in the United States, March 2025.Sample5152 adults residing in the United States.MeasuresNumber of information sources used to obtain vaccine-related information, the most and least trusted information sources, and self-reported sociodemographic variables.AnalysisDescriptive statistics and Poisson regressions were used to examine associations between the total number of information sources used and sociodemographic characteristics.ResultsSurvey respondents reported using an average of 2.9 sources (range: 0-12). Medical professionals represented the most frequently used and the most trusted source for vaccine-related information, while radio represented the least used information source and social media the least trusted source. The number of information sources used varied according to respondent age, ethnicity, education, and income.ConclusionMedical professionals represent the most used and trusted source for vaccine-related information. The number of information sources used to gather vaccine information varies along sociodemographic lines. Public health practitioners must give these points due consideration when designing communication strategies.

articles.title: Disrupting the Importin-5-Glycoprotein Interaction Attenuates LCMV and Confers Protection Against Lethal Challenge.
articles.journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy
articles.abstract: Karyopherins serve as critical regulators of viral infection through canonical nucleocytoplasmic transport functions, however, their non-canonical roles beyond nuclear trafficking remain poorly understood. Here, employing lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) as a model, we elucidate a previously unrecognized function of importin-5 (IPO5), a β-karyopherin family member, in recognizing the basic amino acid-rich cytoplasmic domain of the viral glycoprotein (GPC), thereby facilitating efficient intracellular trafficking and productive viral release. Disruption of the IPO5-GPC interaction led to compromised viral replication; notably, a recombinant LCMV harboring charge-reversing mutations in the GPC cytoplasmic basic motif (KRR496-498EED) exhibits robust attenuation in vivo while eliciting potent protective immunity against lethal wild-type LCMV challenge in mice, highlighting its promise as a live-attenuated vaccine candidate. Among the enveloped RNA viruses examined in this study, IPO5 impacts the release of viruses possessing glycoprotein cytoplasmic domains enriched in basic residues. Overall, our findings highlight the role of IPO5 to viral infection and demonstrate that disruption of the IPO5-GPC interaction constitutes an attractive strategy for developing live-attenuated vaccines against highly pathogenic arenaviruses.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Associations of the triglyceride/HDL-cholesterol ratio and triglyceride-glucose index with malnutrition risk and other geriatric parameters in older adults: a retrospective cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: Journal of investigative medicine : the official publication of the American Federation for Clinical Research
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate the association of the triglyceride/HDL-cholesterol ratio (THR) and the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index with malnutrition risk and other geriatric parameters among patients attending a geriatric outpatient clinic.

METHODS: A total of 355 patients aged ≥65 years who presented to the geriatric outpatient clinic and completed a comprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA) were retrospectively evaluated in this study. Patients were divided into tertiles according to THR and TyG values. Mini Nutritional Assessment-Short Form (MNA-SF) and CGA parameters were recorded and compared between groups. Malnutrition risk was defined as MNA-SF <12.

RESULTS: The median age of patients was 79 years (59.7% female). Regarding comorbidities, TyG and THR values were higher in the presence of diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease, and malignancy (all p<0.05). In unadjusted analyses, gait speed was positively correlated with both TyG and THR (both p<0.05). Higher THR and TyG values were correlated with higher MNA-SF scores, and MNA-SF score remained associated with both indices in multivariable linear regression analyses. In binary logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, and diabetes, both indices were associated with malnutrition risk (MNA-SF <12; present in 69.6% of patients) and with impaired Timed Up and Go test performance; the association with malnutrition risk persisted after additional adjustment for basic activities of daily living, instrumental activities of daily living, depression, and comorbidity burden, in which higher THR was also associated with higher odds of Clinical Frailty Scale >4. After multiple-testing correction, only the association of THR with malnutrition risk remained significant. THR and TyG had limited discriminative power for malnutrition risk (area under the curve 0.601 [95% CI 0.535-0.667] and 0.592 [95% CI 0.526-0.659], respectively).

CONCLUSION: Within the observed range, higher THR and TyG values were associated with lower malnutrition risk in older outpatients. Because their discriminative power is limited, these indices should not be considered independent screening or diagnostic tools; reverse causality cannot be excluded, and prospective studies are needed.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Effect of inositol supplementation on plasma adipokine levels: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.journal: Journal of investigative medicine : the official publication of the American Federation for Clinical Research
articles.abstract: Evidence suggests that inositol supplementation has anti-obesity, anti-hyperglycemic, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory effects. Therefore, considering that adipokines are therapeutic targets in the management of metabolic diseases due to their involvement in various biological processes, the goal of this meta-analysis was to determine the effect of inositol supplementation on adipokine levels in gestational diabetes, postmenopausal women, polycystic ovary syndrome, and type 2 diabetes. The search process was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov databases from inception to February 2026. A restricted maximum likelihood model with Hartung-Knapp adjustment was conducted to calculate the pooled effect size. The leave-one-out method was employed to determine the impact of each study on the overall effect size. The meta-analysis of seven randomized controlled trials revealed that inositol supplementation has no significant effect on adiponectin (WMD: 2.70 µg/mL, 95% CI: -1.02, 6.41, p = 0.12, I2 = 91%; Figure 3), leptin (WMD: 1.57 ng/mL, 95% CI: -33.28, 36.42, p = 0.66, I2 = 64%; Figure 4) or resistin (WMD: -7.43 ng/mL, 95% CI: -89.30, 74.45, p = 0.45, I2 = 94). Additionally, the sensitivity analysis was robust for adiponectin, while the effect size was sensitive to one study for each leptin and resistin. In conclusion, our results suggest that inositol supplementation has no beneficial effect on circulating adipokine levels.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Air pollution increases cardiometabolic diseases in China: A nationwide longitudinal cohort study.
articles.journal: Journal of investigative medicine : the official publication of the American Federation for Clinical Research
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the associations between long-term exposure to multiple ambient air pollutants (PM1, PM2.5, PM10, O3 and NO2) and the incidence of cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) in middle-aged and older Chinese adults, and to identify potential effect modifiers.

DESIGN: Nationwide longitudinal cohort study.

SETTING: The China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), covering 28 provinces in China.

PARTICIPANTS: A total of 8,725 participants aged 45 years and older from the CHARLS 2011 baseline, free of pre-existing CMM, defined as having two or more of the following four conditions: hypertension, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and stroke, with complete follow-up data through 2020. Participants with only one of these conditions at baseline were retained.

PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was incident CMM. Secondary outcomes included pollutant-specific hazard ratios and effect modification by education level and sleep duration. Sensitivity analyses using multiple imputation were performed to assess the robustness of the associations for all five pollutants.

RESULTS: Long-term exposure to PM1, PM2.5, PM10, O3 and NO2 was significantly associated with an increased risk of incident CMM. Stronger associations were observed among participants with lower educational attainment and shorter sleep duration.

CONCLUSIONS: Long-term exposure to ambient air pollutants is associated with a higher risk of CMM in the Chinese middle-aged and older population. These findings highlight the importance of air quality improvement and targeted public health strategies for socioeconomically disadvantaged and sleep-deprived subgroups.

articles.title: Clinical Spectrum of Young-onset Hypertension: Diverse Etiologies, Target-organ Damage, and Diagnostic Challenges - A Seven-case Series.
articles.abstract: Young-onset hypertension - defined as sustained blood pressure elevation presenting before the age of 40 years - is increasingly encountered in tertiary care settings in India. Unlike hypertension in older adults, it frequently harbors secondary etiologies, presents with severe target-organ damage, and poses considerable diagnostic challenges. This case series illustrates the clinical heterogeneity of the condition and highlights the importance of systematic evaluation in this population. We report seven cases (age range 19-38 years; six males, one female) presenting to a tertiary care teaching hospital. Secondary etiologies included biopsy-proven focal segmental glomerulosclerosis with nephrotic-range proteinuria (Case 1), bilateral ostial renal artery stenosis complicated by heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (Case 2), and hypertension associated with erythrocytosis under evaluation (Case 6). Hypertensive emergency with acute ischemic stroke and hemorrhagic transformation, complicated by hypertensive dilated cardiomyopathy, occurred in Case 7. Essential hypertension was established in Cases 3-5, with end-organ manifestations including hypomagnesemia-induced ventricular premature complexes (Case 4) and hypertensive retinopathy (Case 5). Diagnostic investigations included renal biopsy, renal Doppler ultrasonography, renal angiography, 24-h Holter monitoring, serum erythropoietin assay, and brain magnetic resonance imaging. Individualized antihypertensive regimens were supplemented by disease-specific interventions. Outcomes ranged from clinical stabilization to partial neurological recovery, reflecting the variable prognosis associated with delayed diagnosis and inadequate treatment. Young-onset hypertension is not a uniformly benign or essential condition. Systematic evaluation for secondary causes and comprehensive assessment of target-organ damage are critical, particularly in resource-limited settings where these steps are frequently deferred.

articles.title: Applying the CONSENSUS-LAI virological failure definition in real-world practice: Evidence from the multicentre LAHIV cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Definitions of virological failure (VF) for long-acting cabotegravir plus rilpivirine (CAB+RPV) remain inconsistent across real-world cohorts. The CONSENSUS-LAI Delphi process (September 2025) set a shared plasma threshold of ≥200 copies/mL. We evaluated its impact on VF classification and whether its publication influenced prescriber behaviour.

METHODS: Retrospective analysis of virologically suppressed adults initiating CAB+RPV across 11 centres in Tuscany, Italy. Switches attributed to VF by the treating physician were reclassified as meeting CONSENSUS-LAI plasma criteria or as sub-threshold. Rates were calculated per 100 person-years (PY); switches before and after September 2025 were compared with Fisher's exact test.

RESULTS: Among 297 participants (418 PY), 11 switches were attributed to VF (2.63/100 PY, 95% CI 1.31-4.71). Six (54.5%) met CONSENSUS-LAI plasma criteria (1.44/100 PY, 95% CI 0.53-3.12), five with a single value >1000 copies/mL, one with confirmed values ≥200 copies/mL; 4 were sub-threshold and one was cerebrospinal fluid viral escape with undetectable plasma HIV-1 RNA. Emergent resistance occurred in three cases, all CONSENSUS-LAI-defined failures. No resistance was detected in the two sub-threshold cases tested; all four sub-threshold VF re-suppressed, although two of four were switched to a protease inhibitor-based regimen. Sub-threshold switches were 1/6 before and 3/5 after CONSENSUS-LAI publication (p = 0.24).

CONCLUSIONS: The CONSENSUS-LAI definition nearly halves the VF rate, aligning it with cohorts using a ≥200 copies/mL threshold. Emergent resistance was confined to CONSENSUS-LAI-defined failures, whereas sub-threshold viraemia, without detected resistance, still drove most post-consensus switches, highlighting the challenges of translating consensus recommendations into routine practice.

articles.title: Host plant species modulate whitefly-mediated transmission of tomato leaf curl New Delhi virus and viral effects on vector performance.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tomato leaf curl New Delhi virus (ToLCNDV) is an emerging bipartite Begomovirus primarily transmitted by the whitefly Bemisia tabaci, causing severe yield losses in cucurbit and solanaceous crops. Despite its rapid spread, the differential susceptibility of these crop families and the vector-virus-host interactions driving transmission disparities remain poorly characterized.

RESULTS: Our field surveys revealed widespread ToLCNDV infection, with high prevalence in cucurbits although infection in solanaceous crops was much less frequent. Subsequent vector transmission experiments demonstrated that B. tabaci efficiently acquired ToLCNDV from infected melon, tomato and tobacco plants, and that transmission efficiency and viral accumulation were significantly higher in melon plants. Whitefly host adaptability ranked melon > tomato > tobacco, aligning positively with transmission efficiency. Notably, ToLCNDV infection exerted a graded mutualistic effect on whitefly fitness across different plants: survival and reproduction were significantly enhanced on the non-adaptive host tobacco, reproduction was promoted on the moderately adaptive host tomato, and no significant fitness effects were observed on the highly adaptive host melon.

CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate that differential ToLCNDV transmission on cucurbits versus solanaceous crops is collectively shaped by vector host adaptability, host plant antiviral capacity, and virus-mediated mutualism. Unraveling these mechanisms is crucial for accurately predicting viral epidemic risks and developing effective control strategies. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

articles.title: IgG4-Related Disease: A Diagnostic Dilemma for 20 Years.
articles.abstract: We report a case of IgG4-related disease in a 65-year-old man who remained undiagnosed for two decades. His disease initially manifested as periorbital oedema, followed by right cheek swelling, lymphadenopathy and a widespread pruritic eruption of skin-coloured and pale erythematous papules. IgG4 was only considered after a stroke protocol MRI of the brain demonstrated an incidental finding of characteristic orbital manifestations. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of IgG4-related disease and emphasises the importance of recognising its varied presentations to facilitate early diagnosis and management.

articles.title: Capsular Repair During Hip Arthroscopy for Femoroacetabular Impingement Syndrome Improves Revision Rates and Hip Outcome Score Result but Not Overall Patient-Reported Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
articles.journal: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether capsular repair (CR) after hip arthroscopy for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome provides superior clinical outcomes, functional recovery, and complication profiles compared with nonrepair.

METHODS: Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, a search of PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and MEDLINE identified 5 randomized controlled trials comparing CR with no capsular repair in patients with femoroacetabular impingement. Studies published between 2000 and September 2025 with a follow-up of ≥12 months were included. Data on patient demographics, surgical techniques, postoperative protocols, patient-reported outcome measures, complications, and revision rates were extracted. Standardized mean differences were calculated using random-effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed using Cochran's Q statistics and Higgins' I2.

RESULTS: Five randomized controlled trials (n = 615) met the inclusion criteria: 334 patients in the no capsular repair group and 281 in the CR group. Most patient-reported outcome measures, including the modified Harris Hip Score, the International Hip Outcome Tool-12, and all subscales of the Copenhagen Hip and Groin Outcome Score, showed no significant differences between groups. However, the Hip Outcome Score showed a significant advantage for CR (standardized mean difference = 0.59; P < .001). Revision procedures were more frequent in patients who did not undergo CR (15 vs 8 cases). Heterogeneity was generally low across analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: CR after hip arthroscopy for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome did not show significant advantages over nonrepair in most pooled patient-reported outcome measures, including the modified Harris Hip Score, International Hip Outcome Tool-12, and Hip and Groin Outcome Score subscales. However, CR was associated with superior Hip Outcome Score outcomes and lower rates of revision procedures and conversion to total hip arthroplasty. These differences were observed predominantly in studies including unrepaired T-capsulotomy, whereas studies evaluating only interportal capsulotomy generally reported comparable outcomes between repair and nonrepair.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level II, systematic review and meta-analysis of Level I and II studies.

articles.title: Mechanisms of impaired awareness of hypoglycaemia: Lessons from neuroimaging.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract: Hypoglycaemia is a physiological stress and the body generates symptom and hormonal responses that alert the individual and protect them. Protection from hypoglycaemia requires three layers of defence. Firstly, a physiological counter-regulatory response that is designed to correct glucose through glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis; secondly awareness-the ability to perceive symptoms and attribute them to hypoglycaemia; and thirdly a behavioural and emotional response that serves as motivation to avoid subsequent episodes. Impaired awareness of hypoglycaemia (IAH) affects up to a third of people with type 1 diabetes and increases the risk of severe hypoglycaemia. The traditional model of IAH suggests this is a physiological habituation response caused by recurrent episodes that can be reversed on meticulous avoidance of hypoglycaemia. Recent data, especially from neuroimaging, suggests important roles for regions of the brain involved in salience, attention and interoception, implying a more nuanced view of IAH that may involve deficits in each of these areas. This may explain why simple hypoglycaemia avoidance using technology may not suffice to restore awareness, requiring a more holistic approach that addresses key cognitive barriers.

articles.title: The Use, Environmental Knowledge and Climate Change Attitudes of Australian Nurses and Midwives Regarding Nitrous Oxide.
articles.abstract:
AIM: The aim of this research was to investigate the clinical use of nitrous oxide among Australian nurses and midwives, assess their pharmacological knowledge of the gas, determine their awareness of its environmental effects and evaluate their broader attitudes toward climate change.

BACKGROUND: Balancing clinical efficacy with environmental sustainability is an emerging priority in acute pain management. While nitrous oxide offers rapid, reversible analgesia, its substantial ecological footprint as a greenhouse gas cannot be ignored. Nurses and midwives are well-positioned to drive sustainable analgesic practices, yet their current utilisation and awareness of these environmental impacts require further investigation.

DESIGN: A cross-sectional survey of nurses and midwives practising in Australia.

METHOD: Australian nurses and midwives who have administered nitrous oxide as part of patient management were invited to complete a 62-item survey. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics and qualitative responses were thematically analysed.

RESULTS: Responses from 446 respondents were analysed. Pharmacological knowledge of nitrous oxide was low (median 28.6%), as was awareness of its environmental impact (median 28.6%). Respondents aged 40 and under had lower awareness of nitrous oxide's impact on climate (28.6% vs. 42.9%). Climate change beliefs and intentions were high (both 80.0%). Awareness of nitrous oxide's environmental impact explained 79% of variance in climate change belief (F = 35.211).

CONCLUSION: Administration of nitrous oxide by nurses and midwives in Australia for acute pain management occurs across diverse healthcare settings. However, significant knowledge gaps regarding its pharmacological properties and environmental impact highlight an urgent need for targeted education, clinical guidance and sustainable practice initiatives. Addressing these gaps will empower clinicians to balance patient comfort with environmental stewardship, supporting healthcare delivery that is both high quality and ecologically responsible.

IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: This study highlights a critical gap in knowledge regarding both the pharmacology and environmental impact of nitrous oxide among Australian nurses and midwives. While nitrous oxide remains a valued, safe option for acute pain management, addressing its significant ecological footprint requires bridging this knowledge gap through education, clear clinical guidance and sustainable practice initiatives. Effective pain management must balance patient comfort and clinical safety with environmental stewardship to deliver clinically effective, ecologically responsible care.

IMPACT: This study investigated the clinical utilisation of nitrous oxide for acute pain management among Australian nurses and midwives, while evaluating their pharmacological knowledge and awareness of its environmental implications. Despite strong climate change commitments, nurses and midwives face a significant knowledge-practice gap regarding nitrous oxide, showing limited understanding of both its pharmacology and its severe environmental impact.

REPORTING METHOD: In reporting the results, we have used the Checklist for Reporting of Survey Studies (CROSS).

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patient or public contribution.

articles.title: Multimorbidity patterns and disease co-occurrence networks in older adults with diabetes: A national population-based network analysis.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This study aimed to characterize multimorbidity patterns and disease co-occurrence networks among older adults with diabetes in China.

MATERIALS: This cross-sectional study analysed data from older adults aged ≥65 years with diabetes from the 2018 Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey. Network and hierarchical clustering analyses were used to examine co-occurrence patterns among 17 chronic physical and mental conditions.

RESULTS: A total of 1408 participants with diabetes were included, comprising 593 male participants (42.1%) and 815 female participants (57.9%). Overall, 91.6% of participants had ≥1 additional chronic condition, and 71.3% had ≥2 additional chronic conditions. Hypertension (75.5%), heart disease (36.7%) and affective disorder (33.7%) were the three most common conditions; the hypertension-heart disease combination was the leading comorbidity pair (31.75%). Arthritis ranked highest for strength, closeness and betweenness in the overall network; epilepsy also ranked highly for strength and betweenness, particularly among participants aged ≥75 years and in the central and western regions. Five comorbidity clusters emerged from hierarchical clustering, with centrality profiles differing by age, sex and region.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study indicated that multimorbidity burden was high among people with diabetes aged ≥65 years in China and was characterized by distinct network structures and clustering patterns. Arthritis and epilepsy showed high centrality in the comorbidity network, and network characteristics differed across age, sex and regional groups. These findings suggest that health management for older adults with diabetes should address not only common cardiometabolic conditions but also musculoskeletal, neurological and mental health problems.

articles.title: Efficacy of Virtual Reality Teaching in Pressure Injury Wound Care Education for Nurses: A Quasi-Experimental Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pressure injuries are a common clinical concern that lead to prolonged hospital stays and place a burden on health-care systems and society. They are also a key indicator of nursing care quality. Pressure injury wound care can be taught by integrating 360° virtual reality (VR) technology into instruction. Doing so can address limitations in traditional skills training and enhance learning interactivity.

AIM: To determine the efficacy of 360° VR teaching on nurses' knowledge, clinical skills and self-efficacy in pressure injury wound care.

METHODS: This quasi-experimental study was conducted from December 2023 to February 2024 on 114 nurses from a teaching hospital in central Taiwan. Participants were assigned to either an experimental or a control group through cluster sampling. The experimental group received 360° VR-based instruction, whereas the control group received traditional classroom instruction. Preintervention and postintervention assessments were conducted to measure knowledge, skills and self-efficacy in pressure injury care. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, chi-squared tests, paired t-tests and independent-samples t-tests.

RESULTS: Baseline analysis revealed no significant differences between the experimental and control groups in sex, age or advanced nursing qualifications, except for a significant difference in work unit distribution. After the intervention, although no significant between-group difference was observed in knowledge, the experimental group scored higher in pressure injury wound assessment. The scores for wound care skills and self-efficacy significantly improved, particularly for wound dressing techniques, and cognitive gains positively affected self-efficacy.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings support that implementing 360° VR teaching practices enhances nurses' skills and self-efficacy in pressure injury wound care, particularly for wound dressing techniques, and cognitive gains positively affected self-efficacy.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Flexible 360° desktop VR simulations provide an accessible, low-cost training modality that effectively bridges the gap between theoretical instruction and bedside wound care. By integrating interactive clinical scenarios into hospital-based continuing professional education, this approach significantly enhances nurses' perceived competence in pressure injury wound assessment, dressing techniques and overall clinical self-efficacy.

IMPACT STATEMENT: This study demonstrates that immersive 360° desktop VR significantly outperforms conventional lecture-based teaching in enhancing nurses' perceived procedural proficiency and clinical confidence. Adopting this accessible simulation approach within hospital education drives ongoing clinical competency, directly supporting the delivery of standardized wound care and improved patient safety outcomes.

articles.title: Prostatic granulomatosis with polyangiitis as an uncommon cause of fever of unknown origin: diagnostic pitfalls and a review of reported cases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fever of unknown origin (FUO) represents a significant diagnostic challenge in infectious diseases practice, and granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA), a rare non-infectious cause of FUO, may lead to diagnostic delay when presenting with prostatic involvement. This study aims to present an atypical case of prostatic GPA and to increase clinical awareness through a focused review of reported cases published after the 2017 International ANCA Consensus.

CASE PRESENTATION: We retrospectively reviewed a 2023 case initially diagnosed as urinary tract infection and subsequently identified as GPA after further evaluation.

METHODS: In addition, a targeted literature search was conducted using PubMed, Google Scholar, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase to identify adult cases with biopsy-confirmed prostatic involvement for descriptive analysis.

RESULTS: Our patient presented with refractory prostatitis and FUO and was diagnosed with GPA based on PR3-ANCA positivity and multiorgan biopsies. Overall, 19 cases were analyzed, with a mean age of 52.4 ± 16.7 years. FUO with concomitant lower urinary tract symptoms was present in 27.8% (n = 5), PR3-ANCA positivity in 88.9%, skin involvement in 22.2%, and absence of pulmonary involvement in 33.3%. Renal involvement was less frequent (27.8%) than generally reported in GPA. Prolonged unnecessary antibiotic use before diagnosis occurred in 61.1% of cases, and overall survival was 88.9%.

CONCLUSION: Prostatic GPA may mimic refractory urinary infection and contribute to delayed diagnosis. Awareness of this rare prostatic manifestation is important for early diagnosis and improved prognosis.

articles.title: A Causally Guided Imaging-Informatics Framework for Ranking DXA-Derived Hip Imaging Phenotypes in Hip Fracture Risk Prediction.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) provides multiple hip measurements, but their value for fracture risk stratification is rarely evaluated within an imaging-informatics framework. We developed a causally guided framework to rank DXA-derived hip imaging phenotypes and assess whether ranked phenotypes improve hip fracture prediction. We analyzed 21,098 UK Biobank participants with linked health records, DXA-derived hip measures, and prespecified covariates. Sixteen phenotypes spanning bone mineral content (BMC), bone mineral density (BMD), and T-score across hip-related regions were evaluated. Confounder selection was guided by a prespecified directed acyclic graph (DAG). Backdoor-adjusted average treatment effects (ATEs) were estimated on the absolute risk-difference scale per standard deviation (SD) increase. Effect heterogeneity was evaluated for total femur BMD, and prediction was assessed using clinical variables combined with ATE-ranked phenotypes. Among 21,098 participants, 115 had hip fractures. All 16 phenotypes showed negative backdoor-adjusted ATEs per SD increase. The largest ATEs were observed for total femur BMC and BMD, each with a risk difference of - 0.0047, corresponding to 4.7 fewer hip fractures per 1000 participants per SD higher phenotype value. Conditional effects of total femur BMD were stronger among older participants and those with lower BMI. Clinical variables plus the top 11 ATE-ranked phenotypes achieved higher AUC than FRAX with femoral neck BMD (0.842 vs. 0.709), with higher sensitivity (0.748 vs. 0.443) and similar specificity (0.793 vs. 0.777). DXA-derived hip phenotypes differed in backdoor-adjusted ATEs. This framework may support interpretable phenotype selection for fracture risk stratification.

articles.title: ASO Visual Abstract : Performance of 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT for Diagnosing Tumor Thrombus and Predicting Response to Pembrolizumab and Axitinib in Patients with Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Pilot, Retrospective Study.
"They've Come a Long Way": A Qualitative Study of Hospitalization Experiences for Serious Injection-Related Infections in Boston, MA.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Serious injection-related infections (SIRIs) have risen during the opioid overdose epidemic. SIRIs are morbid, costly, and lead to prolonged hospitalizations. Efforts to link patients to medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD) during SIRI hospitalizations have expanded. Additional understanding about patient experiences during SIRI hospitalizations may guide improving satisfaction with inpatient treatment as well as post-hospital care.

METHODS: To explore experiences in the hospital and with transitions of care, we conducted qualitative interviews of individuals with opioid use disorder (OUD) who had been diagnosed with a SIRI over a three-year period ending in 2022. Participants with a qualifying SIRI were identified and recruited directly from an inpatient hospital service, a harm reduction program or through telephone outreach to individuals previously discharged with a SIRI or enrolled in an outpatient parental antibiotic program. We administered a brief survey and conducted semi-structured interviews. Interviews were transcribed and inductively coded. Key themes were then identified.

RESULTS: Participants (n = 30) were mostly male (19), white (21), housed (20), and had endocarditis (10) or osteomyelitis (9). Four themes emerged. First, participants delayed presentation to the hospital due to concerns about stigma, withdrawal, and pain control. Second, positive experiences in the hospital were shaped by empathy and adequate pain and withdrawal management; negative experiences were related to stigma, withdrawal and pain. Third, in-hospital substance use and patient-directed discharges (PDDs) were driven by withdrawal and conflict with hospital staff. Fourth, efforts to plan discharges were valued, though some participants identified opportunities for improvement, including greater emphasis on consistent protocols and shared decision-making.

CONCLUSION: Individuals with OUD and SIRIs provided four themes of clinical care that can guide efforts to improve hospital experiences and discharge planning for people with SIRIs. MOUD and shared decision-making about treatments are practical approaches to improving care for people with SIRIs.

articles.title: Strangers in Familiar Voices.
COPD Exacerbation in Aboriginal Australians: Examining Ethnic Disparity in AECOPD Guideline Alignment Between Aboriginal and Non-Aboriginal Patients.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbations and hospital admission rates remain high in the Top End of Northern Territory (NT), Australia, particularly among Aboriginal people.

AIMS: To examine the clinical characteristics of patients admitted with acute exacerbations of COPD (AECOPD) and evaluate the alignment of care with the Australian COPD-X guidelines in a regional and remote context.

METHODS: Retrospective study included adult Aboriginal and non-Aboriginal patients aged > 18 years admitted to the Royal Darwin Hospital with a primary diagnosis of AECOPD between June 2022 and June 2023.

RESULTS: A total of 211 hospital admissions were recorded (Aboriginal 140 (41.4% remote air retrievals)) and non-Aboriginal 71) from 140 patients (Aboriginal 89 and non-Aboriginal 51). The median age was 64.1 years (Aboriginal: 56.5 years, non-Aboriginal: 74.5 years), males 51.4%, current smokers 66% (Aboriginal: 69.3%, non-Aboriginal: 59.2%). The most common symptom at presentation was shortness of breath in both groups. The median length of hospital stay was 3.83 in Aboriginal and 4.9 days in non-Aboriginal patients. Recommended interventions, including chest X-rays, sputum microbiology, corticosteroids use, antibiotics, supplemental oxygen, and non-invasive ventilation, were administered appropriately in alignment with COPD-X guidelines. However, discrepancies in guideline recommendations were observed between Aboriginal and non-Aboriginal patients. Notably, among Aboriginal patients' spirometry was recorded in only 55.1%, referral for chest physiotherapy or pulmonary rehabilitation, smoking cessation, vaccination coverage, and home support were low. Post-discharge follow-up care was inadequate, including adherence to treatment recommendations. Further, homelessness was associated with recurrent hospital admissions. These disparities were assessed to be related to geographic and social barriers to healthcare faced by Aboriginal Australians.

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates a substantial burden of AECOPD among patients in the Top End of the NT, including younger age and frequent air retrievals and higher hospital admission rates among Aboriginal patients. Although acute inpatient management was generally consistent with Australian COPD-X guideline recommendations, important gaps were identified in COPD management for long-term outcomes, particularly among Aboriginal patients. These findings may reflect the influence of social determinants of health, limited access to healthcare, and geographic isolation. Future revisions of the COPD guidelines could consider the unique challenges of regional and remote settings to support more equitable, culturally appropriate, and effective COPD management.

articles.title: Assessing kidney function for drug dosing in critical illness.
articles.abstract: Kidney-function assessment supports drug dosing in critical illness but does not directly measure drug clearance. Reduced creatinine generation, fluid shifts and rapidly changing filtration can make creatinine-based estimates misleading, whereas genuinely augmented renal clearance can cause insufficient drug exposure. These processes can coexist. This narrative review distinguishes estimated glomerular filtration rate from estimated or measured creatinine clearance and explains how equation version, body-surface-area indexing and sampling time affect interpretation. It separates the 2021 creatinine, 2012 cystatin C and 2021 creatinine-cystatin C equations of the Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration (CKD-EPI) and considers when each can inform a clinical decision. Cystatin C provides complementary information, not an intensive-care reference standard; timed urinary creatinine clearance is also vulnerable to collection error and changing physiology. We present a resource-adapted assessment framework rather than a validated dosing algorithm. It accommodates delayed cystatin C results, unavailable or unreliable urine collections, non-steady-state kidney function and access to therapeutic drug monitoring. Augmented renal clearance is treated as a continuum, with drug-specific thresholds distinguished from research definitions. Examples involving antibiotics, levetiracetam and gabapentin show why a kidney-function estimate must match the metric used in the relevant label or pharmacokinetic model. The practical objective is a documented, revisable dosing decision that integrates estimated kidney function, drug exposure and the consequences of under- or over-treatment, without assuming that biomarker discordance identifies its own cause.

articles.title: Systematic review of pulmonary and cardiovascular disease among asphalt pavers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asphalt pavers may be exposed to a wide range of potentially hazardous substances, and an annual decline in lung function among asphalt pavers has been reported. Studies reporting a modest increase in lung cancer mortality among asphalt workers have been thoroughly summarized and reviewed.

AIMS: The aim of this paper was to systematically review and meta-analyse mortality from non-malignant pulmonary diseases and cardiovascular disease (CVD) associated with asphalt paving (PROSPERO Nr CRD42022341463).
