METHODS: A librarian conducted a literature search in February 2024. We included human studies, assessed risk of bias, conducted meta-analysis and assessed confidence in effect-estimates using GRADE. We included cohort studies reporting estimates on mortality from non-malignant pulmonary disease and CVD among asphalt pavers compared with referents.

RESULTS: We included 10 cohort studies (3714 to 248 087 participants). Asphalt paving was associated with standardized mortality ratio (SMR) from all causes of 0.94 (95% CI 0.81-1.07), SMR from non-malignant pulmonary disease was 1.19 (95% CI 0.95-1.42), whereas SMR from CVD was 0.88 (95% CI 0.75-1.02).

CONCLUSIONS: Our study gave no support to the hypothesis linking asphalt work to excess mortality from cardiovascular or non-malignant pulmonary disease. The studies were not adequately adjusted for confounders. Healthy worker bias may have affected the results. From the GRADE assessment we are uncertain (very low confidence) about the association between asphalt paving and mortality from cardiovascular or non-malignant pulmonary disease. New studies, especially on non-malignant pulmonary disease with better control of confounding factors are warranted.

articles.title: Pregestational maternal diabetes primes neonatal beta cell dysfunction with structural remodelling, impaired calcium buffering and altered mTORC2-Gαq-PKCα signalling in a pig model.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: Offspring of mothers with diabetes are at increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes, and this predisposition is established during fetal life. The aim of this study was to define the functional, morphological and molecular alterations in neonatal pancreatic islets associated with maternal hyperglycaemia, with a particular focus on beta cells, an area that remains poorly understood. Given its similarity to humans in endocrine pancreas development, the pig was used as a translational animal model.

METHODS: Using genetically diabetic and beta cell reporter pig models, we performed functional assessments of glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in vivo and in situ using fresh pancreatic tissue slices from neonatal piglets born to hyperglycaemic mothers (PHGs) or normoglycaemic mothers (PNGs). Morphological and molecular profiling, including proteomics and single-cell RNA-seq, were performed to elucidate molecular changes reflecting the developmental impact of maternal diabetes on offspring metabolic health, with a particular focus on neonatal beta cells.

RESULTS: PHGs were born hyperglycaemic, hyperinsulinaemic and insulin resistant, exhibiting markedly delayed glucose and insulin response curves following oral glucose administration, with more pronounced effects in male piglets. Elevated basal insulin secretion and an almost blunted glucose responsiveness of pancreatic tissue slices were associated with increased insulin and somatostatin content, expansion of beta (+35%) and delta (+47%) cell populations, and organisation into larger islet clusters. Neonatal PHG islets exhibited a molecular profile consistent with intrinsic beta cell dysfunction that partially overlapped with type 2 diabetes (e.g. RBP4 upregulation), together with alterations in glucose sensing (near absence of GLUT2), nutrient metabolism resembling congenital hyperinsulinism (HADH downregulation), and cytosolic Ca2⁺ homeostasis (near absence of the Ca2⁺ buffer calbindin D28K). In addition to an ATF4-dominated stress signature, a shift towards a distinct PHG beta cell subcluster characterised by low expression of ribosomal genes was observed, with an adaptive early-response-gene-mediated transcriptional reactivity. In contrast to the Gαs-adenylyl cyclase-cAMP-PKA signalling axis that dominated in PNG beta cells, neonatal PHG beta cells displayed distinct alterations in Gαq-PLC-PKCα signalling components, the mTORC2 target PKCα, and CREB1, suggesting a restructured signalling architecture.

CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: Our findings reveal altered islet modelling with a unique beta cell dysfunction profile that partially overlaps with, but differs from, that of type 2 diabetes. A shift towards a beta cell subcluster exhibiting an adaptive early-response-gene-mediated transcriptional reactivity and an ATF4-associated transcriptional stress signature provides insight into molecular alterations associated with fetal exposure to maternal diabetes and may contribute to the increased risk of metabolic disease in offspring.

articles.title: Robust fine-mapping in the presence of linkage disequilibrium mismatch.
articles.abstract: Fine-mapping methods based on summary statistics from genome-wide association studies and linkage disequilibrium (LD) information are widely used to identify potential causal variants. However, LD mismatch between the external LD reference panel and the genome-wide association study population is common and can compromise fine-mapping accuracy. Here we developed Robust SparsePro (RSparsePro), a probabilistic graphical model with an efficient variational inference algorithm, to perform robust fine-mapping in the presence of LD mismatch. In simulation studies with varying degrees of LD mismatch, RSparsePro identified credible sets with consistently higher power and coverage than existing methods. In fine-mapping cis-protein quantitative trait loci and complex trait risk loci, RSparsePro identified credible sets with consistently higher enrichment of variants with potential functional impacts and cross-study and cross-LD-reference-panel replication rates. RSparsePro also identified biologically relevant variants in drug target genes and implicated potential regulatory mechanisms for low-density lipoprotein cholesterol.

articles.title: Blood pressure control assessed by clinic and home blood pressure measurements among hypertensive patients in India: results from the GRAND study.
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract: Hypertension is a prevalent non-communicable disease and a significant cardiovascular risk factor in India, affecting 25% of adults. Among those treated, only 52.5% achieved controlled clinic blood pressure (CBP). We investigated blood pressure (BP) control in India using CBP and home BP (HBP). This multicenter, cross-sectional study across 18 centers in 12 states within 7 regions enrolled hypertensive participants aged 20-70 years receiving antihypertensive medications for ≥3 months who regularly visited their clinic. A background survey and four CBP readings were collected at baseline ("Clinic Visit 1") and Clinic Visit 2. Participants underwent HBP monitoring for seven days. Based on average CBP across the two clinic visits and average HBP, participants were classified as having well-controlled hypertension (CBP < 140/90 mmHg and HBP < 135/85 mmHg), white-coat uncontrolled hypertension (WUCH; CBP ≥ 140/90 mmHg and HBP < 135/85 mmHg), masked uncontrolled hypertension (MUCH; CBP < 140/90 mmHg and HBP ≥ 135/85 mmHg), or sustained uncontrolled hypertension (SUCH; CBP ≥ 140/90 mmHg and HBP ≥ 135/85 mmHg). Among 1920 participants, 1578 with appropriate CBP and HBP readings were analyzed. Of these, 55.9% had well-controlled hypertension, 5.1% had WUCH, 21.8% had MUCH, and 17.2% had SUCH. The proportion classified as controlled was 77.7% using clinic BP alone versus 55.9% using both clinic and home BP, a difference of 21.8 percentage points. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating HBP alongside CBP for comprehensive assessment of BP control and identification of BP control phenotypes. Clinical trial registration: Registered at Clinical Trials Registry-India (CTRI) under CTRI/2023/02/049486 on 06 February 2023.

articles.title: Publisher Correction: Conceptual framework and expert guidance on intrapancreatic fat deposition: the Melbourne consensus.
Intra-arterial tenecteplase for acute basilar artery occlusion with sufficient recanalization after thrombectomy: the INSIST-IT randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract: The clinical effect of adjunctive intra-arterial tenecteplase after successful recanalization in acute basilar artery occlusion (BAO) remains uncertain. In this prospective, randomized, adaptive-enrichment, open label, blinded-end point, multi-center trial, patients with BAO within 24 h of estimated symptom onset who achieved successful reperfusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) were randomized (1:1) to intra-arterial tenecteplase (n = 75) or control (only received standard medical therapy, n = 69). The primary efficacy outcome was independent ambulation (modified Rankin Scale 0-3) at 90 days; the primary safety outcome was symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH). The trial was stopped early due to safety concerns and lack of efficacy per Data Safety and Monitoring Committee recommendation. Among 144 randomized patients, 143 (99.3%) completed follow-up. At 90 days, independent ambulation was achieved in 40.0% of the tenecteplase group versus 50.0% in the control group (OR 0.67; 95% CI 0.34-1.29; P = 0.23). sICH occurred in 6.2% versus 4.8% (OR 1.31; 95% CI 0.28-6.89; P = 0.73). All-cause mortality at 90 days was 41.3% versus 26.5% (OR 1.96; 95% CI 0.97-4.03; P = 0.063). In this prematurely terminated trial, adjunctive intra-arterial tenecteplase did not improve functional outcomes in patients with BAO.

articles.title: Applicability of cognitive decline risk scores in a high socioeconomic preventive medicine cohort.
articles.abstract: BackgroundValidated cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease risk scores (CAIDE, ANU-ADRI, LIBRA, LIBRA2) were developed in general-population cohorts; how they behave in the high-socioeconomic, health-selected populations typical of preventive-medicine programs and over-represented in ageing cohorts is undescribed.ObjectiveLacking a cognitive outcome, we did not test predictive validity but described score distributions, inter-score concordance, the components driving variance, and complementary biological data.MethodsFour scores were computed for 895 participants aged ≥45 years in the Zoī cohort, a self-referred, self-funded preventive-medicine sample. Concordance was assessed by Spearman correlations and, after dichotomization, by pairwise agreement (percentage agreement, Cohen's κ). Principal component analysis identified components accounting for most between-person variance. Complementary data (DEXA body composition, HbA1c, erythrocyte omega-3) were cross-tabulated with score-derived risk categories.ResultsConcordance was moderate (ρ = 0.39-0.60), and dichotomized categories were fairly-to-moderately concordant across families (Cohen's κ 0.33-0.52). Protective variables showed ceiling effects (education ≥10 years, 86%; social/cognitive activity, 100%), leaving cardiovascular factors (BMI, hypertension, coronary heart disease) to account for most variance. Despite 91% having normal BMI (≤30 kg/m2), DEXA-measured fat mass showed a dose-response gradient across all scores (CAIDE 4.36-6.26); HbA1c revealed a glycemic gradient invisible to self-reported diabetes.ConclusionsIn this high-socioeconomic cohort, the scores were moderately concordant and varied almost solely by cardiovascular components, protective factors being saturated. Whether this reflects uniformly low risk or reduced ability to separate individuals cannot be determined without a cognitive outcome. Complementary biological measurements added stratification, supporting augmented risk-assessment tools to be validated against cognitive endpoints.

articles.title: Synchrotron X-ray Data of non-diseased and diabetic Human Pancreas Tissue and Islet Segmentation Model.
articles.abstract: Three-dimensional virtual histology using synchrotron radiation micro-computed tomography enables non-destructive visualization of biological tissue microarchitecture with isotropic resolution. To support quantitative studies of human pancreatic morphology, we provide high-resolution 3D X-ray imaging datasets of 55 pancreatic tissue cores from 32 individuals. The collection comprises histologically non-diseased pancreatic tissue from organ donors and non-neoplastic regions of surgical resection specimens from patients with pancreatic cancer, including subgroups with insulin-dependent diabetes or following neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue cores with a diameter of 1 mm were imaged at 650 nm isotropic voxel size, yielding a mean effective spatial resolution of 1.66 µm. The cohort includes reconstructed volumes, corresponding immunohistochemistry, clinical metadata, expert-validated annotations, and dataset-specific example 2.5D U-Net models for automated segmentation of islets of Langerhans. A representative co-registered section yielded a Dice similarity coefficient of 0.81 and intersection-over-union of 0.67. This openly accessible, FAIR-compliant resource supports quantitative analysis of endocrine, exocrine, ductal, and stromal architecture and provides a reproducible reference framework for three-dimensional virtual histology of human pancreatic tissue and computational benchmarking.

articles.title: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke: the BRETIS-TNK2 trial.
articles.abstract: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during endovascular treatment (EVT) may increase first-pass recanalization and dissolve microcirculatory thrombi, but its efficacy and safety are uncertain. We hypothesised that this strategy would improve functional outcomes versus EVT alone. This phase 3, randomised, adaptive-enrichment, open-label, blinded-endpoint multicentre study aims to evaluate whether intra‑arterial tenecteplase improves clinical outcomes for patients with acute ischemic stroke. Patients with large‑vessel occlusion eligible for EVT within 24 hours of symptom onset were randomly assigned (1:1) to the tenecteplase group receiving intra‑arterial tenecteplase during EVT or the control group receiving EVT alone. The primary endpoint was favorable functional outcome. Of 380 randomised patients (192 in the tenecteplase group and 188 in the control group), primary outcome data were available for 190 and 186 patients, respectively. Favorable 90-day functional outcomes (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) occurred in 40.0% of the tenecteplase group versus 46.8% of the control group (unadjusted odds ratio 0.76, [95% CI 0.50-1.14], P = 0.19). This work suggests intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy did not improve 90-day functional outcomes in this population. (Funded by National Science and Technology Major Project and hospital-initiated grants; ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT05657444).

articles.title: Rescue treatment for medium vessel occlusion by intra-arterial tenecteplase: the RESCUE-TNK randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract: In patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by medium vessel occlusion (MeVO), intra-arterial tenecteplase may offer a targeted strategy to improve recanalization; we hypothesized that intra-arterial tenecteplase would increase successful reperfusion compared with standard care with a comparable safety profile. This phase 2, prospective, randomised, open-label, blinded-endpoint, multicentre study aims to assess the efficacy and safety of intra-arterial tenecteplase for patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by MeVO. Patients with MeVO were randomly (1:1) assigned to receive intra-arterial tenecteplase or standard care. The primary outcome was successful reperfusion of medium vessel occlusion. A total of 80 patients were randomized to either the tenecteplase group (n = 41) or control group (n = 39). Successful reperfusion reached 61.0% (25/41) in the tenecteplase group versus 28.2% (11/39) in the control group (unadjusted odds ratio 3.98, 95% CI 1.56-10.16; P = 0.004). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 24 h was similar between the tenecteplase and control groups. This work suggests that intra-arterial tenecteplase significantly increased the probability of successful reperfusion compared with standard care, with a comparable safety profile in this stroke population. (Funded by Shenyang Science Tech Project and hospital-initiated grants; ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT05657470).

articles.title: Association of pre-stroke blood pressure with functional outcome after stroke. The PRESS study.
articles.abstract: The aim of this study was to analyze the association between the mean of available outpatient blood pressure (BP) measurements recorded during the 12 months preceding stroke and functional outcome at 90 days in patients with stroke, adjusting for other established prognostic factors. This was a prospective, observational study including consecutive adult patients admitted with acute stroke between October 2022 and October 2023. Pre-stroke outpatient BP data were obtained from the shared electronic medical record system of Catalonia. All available outpatient systolic blood pressure (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) measurements recorded during the 12 months preceding stroke onset were collected. A total of 187 patients were included. Sixty patients (32.1%) had a poor functional outcome at 90 days, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) ≥ 3 (>3 in those with a previous mRS = 3). In unadjusted models, mean pre-stroke outpatient SBP and DBP and the outpatient SBP measurement closest to stroke were associated with poor functional outcome at 90 days. In the multivariate analyses adjusted for age, baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, pre-stroke mRS, mean in-hospital SBP or DBP, type of stroke and history of atrial fibrillation, pre-stroke SBP (OR 2.52, 95% CI 1.59-4.01, per 1 SD increase, p < 0.001), and pre-stroke DBP (OR 2.78, 95% CI 1.60-4.84, p < 0.001) were associated with a poor outcome. In conclusion, higher mean outpatient BP levels during the year preceding stroke were independently associated with poor functional outcome at 90 days.

articles.title: [18F]FET PET enables histopathology-validated detection of non-contrast-enhancing glioblastoma.
articles.abstract: Accurate visualization of glioblastoma is essential for guiding biopsy, resection and radiotherapy. Contrast-enhanced MRI is routine in clinical practice, yet it can miss metabolically active tumor outside areas of blood-brain barrier disruption. In a histopathology-validated cohort with 472 tissue samples of 61 patients with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, we show that O-(2-[¹⁸F]fluoroethyl)-L-tyrosine PET ([18F]FET PET) depicts tumor tissue significantly better than contrast-enhanced MRI (CE-MRI), especially in regions that show no enhancement on MRI. [18F]FET PET achieves substantially higher sensitivity for tumor detection (91.2% vs 52.6%) and maintains high reliability in non-enhancing tissue (positive predictive value 98.3%), findings that are consistent across newly diagnosed and recurrent disease and in both cohorts undergoing either resection or biopsy. These results indicate that [18F]FET PET complements MRI by revealing MRI-occult tumor burden. Incorporating amino acid PET into routine planning may therefore improve the accuracy of tumor visualization and, ultimately, patient management.

articles.title: Trajectory and genetic correlation mapping of cross-disease risks following incident type 2 inflammatory diseases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 inflammatory diseases (T2IDs) such as atopic dermatitis (AD), asthma, food allergy, eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE), chronic sinusitis (CS), and others, are immune-mediated conditions that frequently co-occur across organ systems and contribute to substantial disease burden. While the atopic march has long served as a conceptual model for T2ID progression, it remains unclear whether this linear sequence captures the broader comorbidity structure of T2IDs.

METHODS: We systematically analyzed comorbidity patterns across nine T2IDs using two complementary methods: Large-scale real-world data (RWD) from over 129 million electronic health records, genome-wide and local genetic correlation, including three novel (asthma, chronic sinusitis, allergic rhinitis) metanalyses of genome-wide association studies.

RESULTS: Retrospective matched cohort analyses reveal a highly interconnected disease network in which CS emerged as a central node, increasing the risk of multiple other T2IDs across diverse patient populations. AD, food allergy, and vasomotor and allergic rhinitis also show strong cross-disease effects. Subgroup analyses uncover notable age-, sex-, and race-specific disparities. Genetic correlation analyses support shared heritability among many disease pairs, complemented by the temporal ordering of associations present in the RWD. Local genetic correlation position asthma as the central node of the shared polygenic architecture, converging on canonical type 2 inflammatory loci.

CONCLUSIONS: Together, our results highlight that T2ID progression extends beyond the atopic march and is shaped by a complex and heterogeneous network of interactions. This work provides a data-driven framework to guide risk stratification, inform early preventive strategies, and prioritize upstream disease targets within the type 2 inflammatory spectrum.

articles.title: The placental transfer of nirmatrelvir using the ex vivo human placental perfusion model.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Nirmatrelvir is an effective therapeutic option for COVID-19 infection and is often administered after symptom onset in pregnant individuals, but few data are available on the associated fetal exposure. The placental perfusion model evaluates maternal-fetal drug transfer across the human placenta and thus can determine fetal drug exposure. The objective of our study was to quantify the amount of nirmatrelvir transfer across the human placenta using the ex vivo placental perfusion model.

METHODS: In a dual closed-closed perfusion of a single human placenta lobule, nirmatrelvir was added to the maternal circulation at its clinical concentration (2.21 μg/mL) or at 10 times this level (22.1 μg/mL). For each placenta studied, there was a 1-h perfusion control period followed by a 3-h exposure period. Samples of the perfusate were collected throughout the experiment to measure nirmatrelvir concentrations and placental viability markers.

RESULTS: Perfusions conducted with nirmatrelvir at 2.21 μg/mL (n = 4) and 22.1 μg/mL (n = 5) concentrations showed a fetal-maternal concentration ratio (F:M) of 0.34 and 0.42, respectively, at 180 min. F:M was adjusted for nonplacental physiological factors, including binding of albumin and α-1-acid glycoprotein, and ionization. The adjusted F:M ranged from 0.26 to 0.35 for placentas perfused with 2.21 μg/mL and from 0.33 to 0.47 for placentas perfused with 22.1 μg/mL of nirmatrelvir.

CONCLUSIONS: Nirmatrelvir readily crosses the term human placenta in a concentration-dependent manner. These transfer kinetics provide a foundation for future physiologically based pharmacokinetic modelling, supporting the development of personalized nirmatrelvir dosing strategies in pregnancy.

articles.title: Triptonide alleviates sepsis-associated acute lung injury by suppressing the STAT3/HIF-1α-mediated aerobic glycolysis in macrophages.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Sepsis-associated acute lung injury (SA-ALI), represents a major contributor to mortality among septic patients during the early hyperinflammatory phase. Triptonide, a diterpenoids extract from Tripterygium wilfordii Hook f has anticancer and contraceptive effects. However, its potential and mechanism in SA-ALI are largely unknown. This study aims to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy and elucidate underlying mechanisms of triptonide in SA-ALI to identify new clinical strategies.

EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced endotoxemia model or caecal ligation and puncture (CLP) model was used to induce SA-ALI in mice, accompanied by treatment with triptonide, triptolide and 2-methoxyestradiol. Parallel in vitro experiments involved LPS-treated mouse primary macrophages cultured with or without triptonide. Transcriptomic sequencing of macrophages was performed to explore the anti-inflammatory mechanisms of triptonide, which were further substantiated using specific activators, inhibitors and adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated gene targeting.

KEY RESULTS: Our data shows that triptonide effectively inhibits macrophage pro-inflammatory activation, reduces pulmonary inflammation and alleviates SA-ALI pathology (i.e. inflammatory cell infiltration, oedema and cell apoptosis), thereby improving the survival of septic mice. Transcriptomic sequencing combined with metabolic analysis shows that triptonide suppresses aerobic glycolysis in pro-inflammatory macrophages by inhibiting the Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription 3 (STAT3)/Hypoxia inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) axis. Notably, the therapeutic efficacy of triptonide against SA-ALI was abolished in myeloid cell-specific HIF-1α overexpressed mice (LyzM-CreDIO-hif1a mice).

CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Triptonide protects against SA-ALI by suppressing the STAT3/HIF-1α signalling axis, thereby inhibiting aerobic glycolysis-mediated pro-inflammatory macrophage activation, which suggests that triptonide is a promising therapeutic strategy for SA-ALI.

articles.title: Inhaler technique in acute wheezing: Factors associated with adequate knowledge.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess knowledge and skills in the use of spacer devices among children presenting to a pediatric emergency department with an acute exacerbation of wheezing or asthma and among their caregivers, and to identify associated factors.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional descriptive study in 134 children aged 2-15 years with previous spacer use who presented with an acute exacerbation of wheezing or asthma. Eligible patients had either a prior physician diagnosis of asthma or a history of recurrent wheezing (≥3 previous episodes). Knowledge and skills were assessed in caregivers and children capable of using the device independently ("autonomous children") by means of a checklist developed in house based on current guidelines. Performance was classified into four levels according to the percentage of correctly performed items. We conducted logistic regression analyses to identify factors associated with adequate knowledge.

RESULTS: Overall, 63.4% of participants showed a high level of knowledge regarding spacer use. Caregivers demonstrated better performance compared to autonomous children (77.7% vs 30%). Better knowledge was directly associated with younger age and follow-up in pediatric pulmonology department in autonomous children, and inversely associated with age in caregivers. Despite generally favorable results, relevant technique errors were frequent, particularly among autonomous children.

CONCLUSIONS: Most caregivers demonstrated adequate knowledge of spacer use; however, significant errors persist, especially among autonomous children. These findings highlight the need for repeated and structured educational interventions.

articles.title: Transforming Growth Factor Beta/Smad Signaling: A Therapeutic Target of Chinese Herbal Medicine for Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: Transforming growth factor beta/Smad signaling has emerged as a promising therapeutic target for kidney disease. Increasing evidence suggests that Chinese herbal medicine (CHM), including single herbs, bioactive compounds, herb pairs, and multi-herb formulas, modulates this signaling network in acute kidney injury, chronic kidney disease, and transitions of acute kidney injury-to-chronic kidney disease and acute kidney injury-on-chronic kidney disease. Frequently studied herbs include Rheum officinale (rhubarb), Wolfiporia cocos (Fu Ling), Scutellaria baicalensis (HuangQin), Salvia miltiorrhiza (Dan Shen), Astragalus membranaceus (Huang Qi), and Coptis chinensis (Huang Lian). Experimental studies suggest that CHM interventions act at multiple regulatory levels, including Smad3 activation, Smad3/Smad7 balance, post-translational modification, and epigenetic regulation, while also interacting with oxidative stress, ferroptosis, inflammatory signaling, microRNA regulation, gut microbiota, and renal-immune cell crosstalk. Overall, CHM shows promise as a multitarget strategy against transforming growth factor beta 1/Smad-driven kidney fibrosis, but further mechanistic and multicenter clinical trials are needed.

articles.title: [Hypercholesterolemia and lipid profile alterations in Moroccan patients with myocardial infarction: A case-control study].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypercholesterolemia, particularly elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), is a major risk factor for cardiovascular diseases, including myocardial infarction.

AIMS: This study aimed to investigate lipid profile alterations in Moroccan patients with myocardial infarction.

METHODS: This case-control study included 104 patients hospitalized for myocardial infarction at the Ibn Rochd University Hospital Center (mean age: 59±11 years; range: 30-82 years) and 79 apparently healthy controls recruited at the Pasteur Institute of Casablanca (mean age: 48±8 years; range: 23-57 years). Serum total cholesterol (TC), triglycerides (TG), LDL-C, and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) were measured using standardized enzymatic methods.

RESULTS: Patients with myocardial infarction exhibited significantly higher levels of TC, TG, and LDL-C compared with controls, with increases of 17.5% (P<0.001), 78.2% (P<0.001), and 27.7% (P<0.001), respectively. In contrast, HDL-C levels were significantly reduced by 22.2% in patients with myocardial infarction (P<0.001).

CONCLUSION: These findings highlight a strong association between dyslipidemia and myocardial infarction in the Moroccan population, emphasizing the importance of lipid profile monitoring for cardiovascular risk prevention.

articles.title: [Right aortic arch with a true bicarotid trunk and aberrant left subclavian artery in an adult: Value of CT angiography].
articles.abstract: We report a rare right aortic arch variant detected during neurovascular assessment in a 48-year-old woman. Arch-to-vertex computed tomography angiography showed three consecutive branches: a true bicarotid trunk dividing into both common carotid arteries, a separate right subclavian artery, and an aberrant left subclavian artery with a retroesophageal course. Neither a Kommerell diverticulum nor aortic dissection was identified. Focused questioning disclosed chronic dysphagia, without definitive evidence of vascular esophageal compression. No causal relationship with the presenting stroke could be established. This case underscores the value of multiplanar and three-dimensional imaging in distinguishing a true bicarotid trunk from a common brachiocephalic-carotid origin, identifying aberrant subclavian anatomy, and informing cardiovascular and neuroendovascular procedural planning.

articles.title: From tissue adaptation to disease-associated eosinophil states.
articles.abstract: Eosinophils are highly adaptable immune cells whose phenotype and function are shaped by developmental, spatial, temporal, and inflammatory cues. Beyond their classical roles in type 2 immunity, eosinophils participate in chronic inflammation, fibrosis, metabolic disease, infection, and cancer. Here, we review how disease-associated eosinophil states emerge through perturbation of four interconnected determinants: eosinophil development, local tissue environment, tissue residency time, and inflammatory context. We discuss how disease can alter eosinophil development before tissue entry and reshape eosinophil adaptation within tissues, and how these processes may influence therapeutic responses. Together, these observations provide a framework for understanding disease-associated eosinophil diversity and for considering therapeutic strategies that preserve beneficial tissue-associated functions.

Volume status of patients with hyponatremia across the age span - results from a large prospective international study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: Hypotonic hyponatremia is the most common electrolyte disorder in hospitalized adults and becomes increasingly prevalent with age. However, age-related differences in volume status and underlying etiologies remain poorly characterized. We aimed to assess the distribution of volume status and etiologies of hypotonic hyponatremia across the adult age span.

METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of the prospective Hyponatremia Intervention Trial (NCT03557957), including hospitalized adults with chronic moderate-to-severe hypotonic hyponatremia. Patients were stratified into three age groups (<65, 65-79, ≥80 years). Final volume status (hypovolemic, euvolemic, or hypervolemic) was determined at the end of hospitalization based on the complete in-hospital clinical course.

RESULTS: Overall, 1992 patients (F/M 1050/942; median age 73 [63-81] years) were analyzed. Euvolemic hyponatremia (n = 1073) predominated across all age groups and sexes, mainly due to syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis (SIAD; n = 853). In adjusted analyses, patients aged 65-79 years (OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.19-1.88) and ≥80 years (OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.14-1.91) had higher odds of SIAD than patients aged <65 years. Volume status distribution differed across age groups (p = 0.007), driven by a higher prevalence of hypervolemic forms in patients aged ≥80 years; however, the association between age category and volume-status phenotype was attenuated and no longer statistically significant after multivariable adjustment. Hypovolemic hyponatremia (n = 613) was most commonly due to gastrointestinal sodium losses in younger patients, whereas diuretics accounted for nearly 50% of cases in those aged ≥80 years. Among patients with hypervolemic hyponatremia (n = 306), heart failure and liver insufficiency were the leading causes, with heart failure increasing and liver insufficiency decreasing across age groups.

CONCLUSION: Euvolemic hyponatremia was the predominant form across all age groups and was mainly due to SIAD, with both older age groups showing higher adjusted odds of SIAD compared with patients aged <65 years. Age-related differences were observed in the distribution of etiologies within hypovolemic and hypervolemic hyponatremia.

articles.title: Interaction between unhealthy sleep pattern and obesity on cardiometabolic multimorbidity.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Obesity and unhealthy sleep are established risk factors for cardiometabolic multimorbidity, but their joint effect remains unclear. This study aims to investigate their joint effect on cardiometabolic multimorbidity risk by analyzing data from 2 independent cohorts.

METHODS: We analyzed cross-sectional (Fuqing Cohort, N = 34,703) and prospective data (UK Biobank, N = 362,474; 12.3-year median follow-up, 3980 incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity cases). We defined unhealthy sleep (≥3 of 5 traits: late chronotype, sleep <7 or >8 h/day, frequent insomnia symptoms, self-reported snoring, frequent daytime sleepiness), cardiometabolic multimorbidity (≥2 of type 2 diabetes, coronary heart disease, stroke), and obesity (general: BMI ≥25 kg/m²; central: waist circumference ≥80 cm in women, ≥94/90 cm in European/Asian men). The reference group had a sleep score <3 and no corresponding obesity. Logistic and Cox regressions evaluated associations and additive interaction was assessed.

RESULTS: Unhealthy sleep and both obesity types independently increased cardiometabolic multimorbidity risk in both populations. The joint effect was stronger for unhealthy sleep combined with central obesity (FQC adjusted OR = 3.46; UKB adjusted HR = 2.55) than general overweight/obesity (FQC adjusted OR = 2.61; UKB adjusted HR = 2.46). Additive interaction showed stronger effect for unhealthy sleep with central versus general overweight/obesity in Europeans (adjusted RERI: 0.61 vs. 0.32). A similar additive interaction in Asians turned non-significant after covariate adjustment. Insomnia and central obesity showed a significant additive interaction in both cohorts.

CONCLUSIONS: Unhealthy sleep and obesity jointly increase cardiometabolic multimorbidity risk, with central obesity having a stronger additive interaction than general overweight/obesity. Integrated public health strategies targeting sleep and weight are warranted.

articles.title: [Surgery in transition: Impact of the early COVID-19 pandemic on visceral surgery in Germany].
articles.journal: Zeitschrift fur Evidenz, Fortbildung und Qualitat im Gesundheitswesen
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Changes in visceral surgical care in Germany during the early COVID-19 pandemic have not yet been sufficiently described. To date, data on in-hospital mortality and postoperative complications remain limited.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: In this retrospective analysis, anonymized administrative data from the Federal Statistical Office of Germany (Destatis) for the period from 2018 to 2021 were evaluated comparatively, focusing on the most frequently performed visceral surgical procedures nationwide. Demographic characteristics, procedure volumes, length of hospital stay on regular wards and intensive care units, postoperative complications, and in-hospital mortality were analyzed.

RESULTS: A total of approximately 2.1 million procedures were recorded over the 4-year study period. Compared with the pre-pandemic years 2018 and 2019, procedure volumes decreased by approximately 9% in 2020 and 2021, respectively. The average length of stay in the intensive care unit and in hospital decreased during the pandemic. Postoperative complications, including pulmonary embolism, acute kidney injury, sepsis, and peritonitis, increased during the pandemic years compared with the preceding years. Overall in-hospital mortality in visceral surgery increased from 2.43% in 2018 to 2.55% in 2020 and 2.53% in 2021. In particular, in-hospital mortality in colorectal surgery increased from 7.37% in 2019 to 7.95% in 2021, while the mortality among COVID-19-positive patients following colorectal procedures reached 48%. In contrast, mortality rates in esophageal, hepatic, and pancreatic surgery remained largely unchanged.

CONCLUSION: During the COVID-19 pandemic, Germany experienced a substantial reduction in the volume of visceral surgical procedures and hospital length of stay, while postoperative complications and in-hospital mortality increased. A potential causal relationship with SARS-CoV-2 cannot be established based on the available data. These findings emphasize the importance of systematically evaluating the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on surgical care in Germany and of developing evidence-based strategies to maintain surgical capacity and patient safety during future pandemics.

articles.title: Preoperative Prediction of Lymph Node Metastasis in Rectal Cancer Using Multimodal Magnetic Resonance Imaging Radiomics Combined with Clinical Risk Factors.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate the preoperative predictive value of multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) radiomics combined with clinical risk factors for lymph node metastasis in rectal cancer, and to construct and validate an efficient and reproducible preoperative prediction model.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 129 patients with pathologically confirmed rectal cancer who underwent surgery at our hospital between 2017 and 2023. Preoperative pelvic T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (T1CE), and complete clinical data were collected. Three-dimensional regions of interest were manually segmented on the tumors using ITK-SNAP software, and radiomic features were selected via variance filtering and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Patients were randomly divided into a training cohort (n = 90) and an internal validation cohort (n = 39) at a 7:3 ratio. Five Logistic regression prediction models were constructed: single-sequence radiomics, multimodal radiomics, multimodal radiomics combined with clinical risk factors, and clinical factors alone. Using postoperative pathology as the gold standard, the diagnostic performance of each model was evaluated by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy.

RESULTS: The multimodal radiomics combined with clinical risk factors model demonstrated the best predictive performance, with an AUC of 0.885 (95% CI: 0.819-0.937), sensitivity of 85.3%, specificity of 82.1%, and accuracy of 83.6% in the internal validation cohort. Its performance was significantly superior to that of the single-sequence models, the multimodal radiomics model, and the clinical model alone (all P < 0.05). Entropy from T2WI, peak enhancement from T1CE, tumor volume, tumor size, carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) were identified as independent predictors of lymph node metastasis. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis confirmed that the model was well-calibrated and provided substantial net clinical benefit.

CONCLUSION: Integrating multimodal MRI radiomics from T2WI and T1CE with clinical indicators such as CEA and NLR significantly improves the preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis in rectal cancer, demonstrating promising clinical applicability. However, as this was a single-center retrospective study, further multicenter, large-sample external validation is warranted to confirm the stability and generalizability of the model.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of patient-specific PEEK implants in craniomaxillofacial reconstruction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: International journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery
articles.abstract: Polyether ether ketone (PEEK) has emerged as a promising alternative to titanium and autologous bone for craniomaxillofacial (CMF) reconstruction, particularly in patient-specific implant design. However, its clinical performance (aesthetic and functional) across the wide spectrum of CMF indications remains incompletely defined. A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to April 29, 2026. Studies reporting clinical outcomes of patient-specific PEEK implants in adult CMF reconstruction were included. The data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment (JBI tool) were performed by two reviewers independently. Fifteen studies involving 203 patients and 236 patient-specific PEEK implants met the inclusion criteria. Reconstructions addressed cranial, orbital, midface, and mandibular defects following benign and malignant tumour resection, trauma, or infection. The pooled overall complication rate was 20.1%, with most complications being minor and predominantly related to local surgical conditions rather than implant failure. Implant loss occurred in 13 cases (pooled implant loss 6.5%), between 55 days and 2 years postoperatively. Aesthetic outcomes were reported as satisfactory or very satisfactory with a pooled rate of 87.4%. Functional outcomes were generally acceptable, particularly in non-load-bearing reconstructions. The implant loss rate was numerically higher in previously irradiated patients, although this subgroup was very small (7/236 implants). Patient-specific PEEK implants represent a clinically effective alloplastic option for selected CMF reconstructions, providing favourable aesthetic and functional outcomes when appropriate indications and local risk factors are carefully considered.

articles.title: Association of duration of amino acid infusion and renal protection: the less, the better. Response to Br J Anaesth. 2026; 137: 652-3.
Silencing the fire alarm: responding to intraoperative blood pressure targets.
articles.abstract: A meta-analysis in a recent issue of the British Journal of Anaesthesia pools randomised evidence on intraoperative arterial blood pressure targets in nine trials in noncardiac surgery. With a total of 14 658 patients included in the analysis, the authors show that higher mean arterial pressure targets do not reduce 30-day mortality, acute kidney injury, or myocardial injury. These findings reinforce the distinction between low blood pressure as a marker of perioperative vulnerability and low blood pressure as a modifiable therapeutic target. Correcting arterial pressure might normalise a number without removing the underlying physiological vulnerability that drives adverse postoperative outcomes. Therefore, this meta-analysis supports a shift from reflexive increases in blood pressure targets towards attention to the underlying cause of haemodynamic instability.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Targeting HSP90ab1: curcumin and silybin inhibit NNV infection in sea perch (Lateolabrax japonicus) via receptor blockade and immune enhancement" [Fish Shellfish Immunol. 176, (2026), 111508].
Post-discharge healthcare utilization and diabetes care among rural and nonrural adults following hypoglycemic or hyperglycemic crises.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To explore rural-and nonrural differences in healthcare utilization in primary and endocrinology care among adults with diabetes who experienced hypoglycemia or hyperglycemic crises requiring emergency department (ED) or hospital care.

METHODS: This is a retrospective cohort study from a large integrated healthcare system between January 1, 2020, and October 1, 2024. We identified adults (≥18 years) with diabetes who had an ED encounter or hospitalization with a primary diagnosis of hypoglycemic or hyperglycemic (diabetic ketoacidosis or hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state) crisis, subset to those in rural areas (population <20,000) or nonrural areas, and quantified differences in rates of subsequent healthcare utilization with primary care and endocrinology at 30, 60 and 90 days post-discharge.

RESULTS: We identified 1258 individuals experiencing an index hypoglycemic (N = 677: 26.4% rural, 73.6% urban) or hyperglycemic (N = 581: 19.3% rural, 80.1% urban) crisis. Within 30 days of discharge, rural residents had fewer primary care clinician encounters (39.5% vs 49.3%, P = 0.003) and endocrinologist encounters (8.6% vs 16.3%, P = 0.001) than urban residents. Lower encounter rates in rural residents continued at 60 and 90 days.

CONCLUSIONS: Following hypoglycemic and hyperglycemic crises, when timely follow-up is essential, rural residents may be less likely to see primary care or endocrinology clinicians.

articles.title: Valuable Role of 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose-PET/computed Tomography in Therapeutic Decision-Making of Infectious and Inflammatory Disorders.
articles.abstract: 18F-FDG (18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose)-PET/computed tomography (CT) has emerged as a pivotal molecular imaging modality that extends beyond diagnosis to influence therapeutic decision-making in infectious and inflammatory diseases. By detecting increased glucose metabolism in activated inflammatory cells, it enables whole-body visualization of active disease before structural abnormalities become apparent on conventional imaging. Quantitative parameters support reproducible longitudinal monitoring. Its incorporation into international guidelines highlights its growing role in precision-guided management. Emerging technologies, including digital and long axial field-of-view PET/CT, artificial intelligence, radiomics, PET/MR imaging, and pathogen-specific or immune cell-specific tracers, may further enhance diagnostic accuracy and personalized treatment.

articles.title: 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/Computed Tomography in Fever of Unknown Origin: A Comprehensive Clinical Review.
articles.abstract: This article provides a thorough summary of the most recent research on [F]fluorodeoxyglucose PET/computed tomography (CT) in the assessment of fever and inflammation of undetermined origin (FUO/IUO). The pathophysiologic basis of FDG uptake in infection and inflammation, preparation for the scan, pooled diagnostic performances, characteristic uptake patterns for interpretation, its role in prognostication, cost-effectiveness, and imaging pitfalls are all covered. Additionally, a diagnostic approach that uses FDG PET/CT as a preliminary second-line test is suggested. Long axial field-of-view PET/CT, PET/MR imaging, and new pathogen-specific tracers are also highlighted as interesting future possibilities for enhancing diagnostic specificity in FUO/IUO.

articles.title: PCSK9-Targeted Therapy and Kidney Function in Chronic Kidney Disease: A Systematic Review and Narrative Synthesis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) increases cardiovascular risk, but renal impairment, proteinuria, dialysis, and transplantation complicate interpretation of lipid-lowering therapy. This systematic review evaluated renal tolerability, kidney-related clinical and biological evidence, and unresolved renal-outcome gaps for proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9)-targeted therapies in CKD.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception and most recently updated on September 19, 2026; ClinicalTrials.gov was additionally searched on September 19, 2026. Eligible evidence included clinical trials and CKD subgroup analyses, renal-impairment pharmacology, observational cohorts, dialysis and transplant reports, pharmacovigilance, case-based evidence, and kidney-specific experimental studies. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted, and appraised reports. Findings were synthesized narratively without quantitative pooling. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261402376).

FINDINGS: One hundred five reports representing 116 underlying studies were included. Evolocumab, alirocumab, and inclisiran consistently lowered low-density lipoprotein cholesterol without a clear short- to medium-term signal for deterioration in creatinine-based kidney function across the CKD strata studied. Evidence for reduced albuminuria or proteinuria was limited to small uncontrolled studies, and mechanistic findings did not establish clinical evidence of renoprotection. Most renal tolerability evidence came from cardiovascular or lipid-efficacy trials dominated by mild-to-moderate non-dialysis CKD; advanced CKD, dialysis, and kidney transplantation were excluded or sparsely represented.

IMPLICATIONS: Current evidence supports lipid-lowering efficacy in mild-to-moderate non-dialysis CKD but does not establish renoprotection or an antiproteinuric effect. Kidney-centered studies are needed in advanced CKD, dialysis, and transplantation.

articles.title: Cell-type- and subregion-specific basolateral amygdala inputs to ventral CA1-subiculum.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
articles.abstract: The hippocampus is essential for learning and memory and interacts extensively with cortical and subcortical regions. Although the heterogeneity of intrinsic connectivity of hippocampal neurons is well established, the diversity of its extrahippocampal connectivity remains less understood. Such differential connectivity may contribute to functional diversity of hippocampal neurons in specific positions. Ventral CA1 (vCA1) and ventral subiculum (vSub) form strong reciprocal connections with the basolateral amygdala (BLA), a region critical for emotional and social regulation. Consequently, BLA-vCA1-vSub circuits have been implicated in anxiety-related and social behaviors. However, the functional connectivity from BLA to vCA1-vSub at the cellular and circuit levels is underexplored. To address this, we combined viral tracing with Channelrhodopsin-2 (ChR2)-assisted slice electrophysiology to examine BLA projections to vCA1-vSub in mice of either sex. We found that BLA inputs are not uniformly distributed along the transverse axis in vCA1-vSub. Instead, BLA selectively excites pyramidal neurons in distal vCA1-vSub while largely avoiding proximal vCA1 near CA2. BLA terminals strongly excited parvalbumin-expressing interneurons but only weakly recruited a small subset of somatostatin-expressing interneurons, generating robust disynaptic inhibitory synaptic currents in pyramidal neurons. Additionally, the same distal pyramidal neurons that receive BLA excitation also project back to the BLA. These findings reveal that BLA establishes cell-type- and subregion-specific excitatory connections within vCA1-vSub, highlighting a circuit architecture that may underlie functional heterogeneity in ventral hippocampal processing.Significance statement The hippocampus interacts extensively with cortical and subcortical regions, yet how long-range extrahippocampal inputs are organized across hippocampal subregions remains poorly understood. We examined projections from the basolateral amygdala (BLA) to the ventral hippocampus and found that BLA inputs selectively excite pyramidal neurons in distal ventral CA1 and ventral subiculum while largely avoiding proximal ventral CA1. BLA projections preferentially excite parvalbumin-expressing interneurons, provide disynaptic inhibition onto pyramidal neurons, and are reciprocally connected with the same pyramidal neurons in ventral CA1 and subiculum they excite. These findings reveal a highly selective connectivity pattern of amygdala-hippocampal circuits, providing a circuit framework for understanding how emotional information is routed through distinct ventral hippocampal pathways.

articles.title: Uplifting RNA Science in Africa: A Call to Action.
articles.abstract: The 21st century has witnessed the emergence of an entire new class of therapeutic and prophylactic medicines based on RNA. These transformative advances have arisen from decades of fundamental and applied research efforts to understand, exploit, and modify the properties of RNA to improve lives and livelihoods for patients and broader societal stakeholders. However, the contributions of African scientists, businesses and policymakers to the RNA research ecosystem have been minimal. This, despite the opportunities for exploitation of RNA-based medicines in specific health issues endemic to the region, such as the neglected tropical diseases schistosomiasis, lymphatic filariasis and Buruli ulcer, as well as chronic respiratory disorders (asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disorder) that disproportionately impact low and middle countries. Here, we outline some of the challenges faced by the incipient RNA bioscience research community in Africa, which remains hindered by a deficiency of strategic vision and insufficient momentum, an underdeveloped culture of collaboration, and persistent constraints in resources and infrastructure. Overcoming these issues requires a re-imagining of how the global RNA research community and African scholars mobilise resources for co-production of RNA-related knowledge and innovation. Potential solutions include forging equitable partnerships with institutions in the Global North, strengthening local, regional, and transnational collaborative networks in RNA science, and developing grassroots platforms that expand RNA education, research training, and communitywide networking across Africa. Together, these approaches offer a pathway to build sustainable capacity, nurture scientific leadership, and accelerate the growth of the continent's RNA bioscience ecosystem.

articles.title: Venous Outflow Imaging in Acute Ischemic Stroke: An ASFNR State of Practice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous outflow (VO) imaging describes the egress limb of the cerebral collateral circulation and has been associated with outcome in acute ischemic stroke; its added value beyond arterial collaterals and perfusion measures remains uncertain. More than a dozen VO measures have been proposed on CT and MR techniques used in acute stroke, spanning three physical signals: venous opacification, venous transit and venous oxygenation. They differ in what they measure, in evidence maturity and in readiness for reporting.

METHODS: A writing group reviewed the peer-reviewed studies of cerebral venous drainage measures in acute ischemic stroke. The scope is CT and MRI obtained during routine acute stroke evaluation, excluding measures that require catheter angiography or ultrasound. We describe each measure's acquisition, definition, evidence and technical limitations, and propose a reporting framework based on these features.

KEY MESSAGE: VO markers are descriptive prognostic measures, not treatment-selection criteria. The cortical vein opacification score (COVES) has the most mature CTA evidence and may be considered when venous timing is adequate, though meta-analyses support an association rather than a threshold; comprehensive venous outflow (CVO) adds the internal cerebral vein. Prolonged venous transit (PVT) adds a temporal dimension read from perfusion, but remains investigational, as do the composite arterial-venous scores, quantitative venous timing and oxygen extraction fraction mapping. Susceptibility signs index deoxygenation and venous blood volume, not drainage. Reporting should name the technique and describe opacification, transit or oxygenation findings in their own terms. The evidence base is predominantly anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion imaged before thrombectomy.

articles.title: Ultrasound Findings of Clostridium difficile Infection and Its Induced Pseudomembranous Colitis in Children: Review of the Literature With Image Illustration.
articles.abstract: Clostridium difficile (CD) causes various conditions in pediatric patients, ranging from asymptomatic colonization to severe colitis that can progress to pseudomembranous colitis (PMC). Appropriate antibiotic treatment is important to prevent catastrophic outcomes. This review article describes the ultrasound findings of various patterns of CD infection. Bowel wall thickening, bowel internal ring, bowel external ring, and ascites were more frequently detected in cases with CD infection. Furthermore, PMC cases showed marked thickening of the entire colon, mucus-entrapped overlying pseudomembranes, and colonic fluid entrapment within the colonic lumen. The extent of these findings may be attributable to the severity of PMC.

Triple immune impairment in an elderly patient with IgG4-AIP and MGUS complicated by dual severe infections over 3 years: A case report.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Reports of IgG4-related autoimmune pancreatitis (IgG4-AIP) combined with monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) are mostly limited to short-term follow-up and single infectious complications. To date, no published literature has described octogenarian patients with this overlap complicated by 2 severe concurrent opportunistic infections together with 3-year serial immune-biomarker monitoring. Long-term follow-up data regarding multiple opportunistic infections under continuous immunosuppressive therapy remain scarce for this rare clinical entity.

PATIENT CONCERNS: An 82-year-old male patient was diagnosed with IgG4-AIP superimposed by IgGλ-type MGUS. Markedly elevated serum IgG4 (3278.00 μg/mL) and a monoclonal paraprotein level of 2.34 g/L were noted at baseline. Initial combined glucocorticoid-based immunosuppressive therapy partially improved pancreatic lesions. Subsequently, he developed concurrent Staphylococcus hominis bacteremia and active pulmonary tuberculosis.

DIAGNOSES: Three-tier superimposed immune impairment, consisting of chronic IgG4-related inflammation, MGUS-associated clonal plasma-cell dysregulation, and drug-induced lymphopenia, was considered the key driver for the dual life-threatening opportunistic infections.

INTERVENTIONS: Standardized antibacterial and antituberculosis therapeutic regimens were administered to treat the dual infections. Immunosuppressive strategies were adjusted for this high-risk geriatric patient.

OUTCOMES: Complete resolution of infectious lesions was achieved. Over the 36-month longitudinal surveillance period, serum paraprotein remained stable without progression to multiple myeloma, while serum IgG4 concentrations fluctuated independently of MGUS activity. Serial immune profiling confirmed persistent cellular immunodeficiency in this elderly MGUS carrier. This constitutes the first reported octogenarian patient with overlapping IgG4‑AIP and IgGλ‑MGUS suffering from dual severe opportunistic infections following immunosuppressive therapy.

LESSONS: Persistent cellular immunodeficiency substantially elevates the risk of life-threatening opportunistic infections in elderly patients with concomitant IgG4-AIP and MGUS. Cyclophosphamide should be used with extreme caution in this vulnerable geriatric subgroup. Pathogenetic mechanisms, infectious risk factors, and preventive considerations for this rare overlapping immune disorder deserve clinical attention.

articles.title: Effects of opioid-free and opioid-sparing anesthesia on postoperative delirium: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a common neurocognitive condition linked with increased morbidity, long-term cognitive decline, and death. Perioperative opioid exposure may contribute to delirium through sedation, neuroinflammation, and neurotransmitter dysregulation. Opioid-free anesthesia and opioid-sparing anesthesia using agents such as ketamine, esketamine, and dexmedetomidine have emerged as a potential strategy to reduce POD. This meta-analysis evaluated the effects of opioid-free and opioid-sparing anesthetic regimens on POD in adult surgical patients.

METHODS: Embase, PubMed, and Web of Science were searched from inception to April 2026. Randomized controlled trials comparing ketamine-, esketamine-, or dexmedetomidine-based opioid-free and opioid-sparing strategies with placebo, conventional opioid-based anesthesia, or standard care were included. The primary outcome was POD. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effects model.

RESULTS: Forty-one randomized controlled trials involving 7852 patients were analyzed. POD occurred in 488 of 4013 patients receiving opioid-free/opioid-sparing interventions and 633 of 3839 controls. Overall, these strategies significantly reduced the risk of delirium (RR = 0.641, 95% CI: 0.525-0.784; I2 = 52.2%). Subgroup analyses showed reductions with esketamine (RR = 0.745, 95% CI: 0.526-1.053) and dexmedetomidine (RR = 0.612, 95% CI: 0.471-0.796), while ketamine demonstrated a nonsignificant trend toward benefit (RR = 0.598, 95% CI: 0.251-1.423). No significant publication bias was detected.

CONCLUSIONS: Opioid-free and opioid-sparing anesthetic strategies reduce POD in adult surgical patients, with dexmedetomidine and esketamine showing the most consistent benefits. These findings support multimodal opioid-sparing anesthesia for perioperative neurocognitive protection.

articles.title: Computer-assisted Taylor spatial frame for correcting malalignment after unilateral external fixation of tibial fractures.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy of computer-assisted Taylor spatial frame (TSF) for correcting malalignment after unilateral external fixation (UEF) of tibial fractures. This retrospective cohort study included 18 patients with tibial misalignment after UEF between February 2019 and February 2024. Using the TSF technique, X-ray parameters (deformity, frame, and mounting) were entered into software to generate a six-axis correction prescription. Reduction time, number of X-ray exposures, total external fixation duration, clinical fracture healing time, complications, and functional recovery were recorded. The Wilcoxon signed-rank test was used to compare preoperative and final visual analogue scale (VAS) scores because the paired differences were not normally distributed; data are presented as mean (range) or median (interquartile range [IQR]). All 18 patients were followed up for a mean of 14.9 months (range: 12-18 months). Satisfactory reduction was achieved in all cases after TSF adjustment. Mean reduction time was 19.0 minutes (range, 15-24 minutes), and patients received a mean of 1.4 X-ray exposures (range, 1-3). Clinical fracture healing occurred after a mean of 24.0 weeks (range, 21-29 weeks), and total external fixation lasted a mean of 25.2 weeks (range, 22-30 weeks). Johner-Wruhs ratings at final follow-up were excellent in 15 patients and good in 3 (100% excellent/good). Median VAS scores improved from 7 (IQR, 6-8) before surgery to 1 (IQR, 0-2) at final follow-up (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, Z = -3.77, P < .001). Superficial pin tract infections developed in 3 patients (16.7%; 3/18) and were controlled with oral antibiotics and dressing changes. No patient had deep infection, pin loosening, nonunion, or bone exposure. In this small, single-arm retrospective cohort, all 18 patients achieved satisfactory reduction with computer-assisted TSF, and adjustment times were short. No patient underwent secondary open reduction or fixation. These preliminary findings suggest that TSF may serve as a feasible minimally invasive option for correcting early malalignment following UEF of tibial fractures; however, multicenter controlled studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these results.

articles.title: Glucocorticoid therapy for acute interstitial nephritis in a patient with diabetic nephropathy: A case report.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Acute interstitial nephritis (AIN) can cause acute kidney injury. Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a chronic microvascular complication of diabetes. The coexistence of these diseases complicates diagnosis and treatment.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A 41-year-old man with diabetes and hypertension presented with dizziness on 4 January 2025. His renal function was normal 7 months previously, but his sCr was 258 μmol/L immediately before admission and peaked at 299 μmol/L after admission. The patient reported use of an unidentified herbal decoction during the previous month.

DIAGNOSES: A biopsy showed acute tubular injury (70% of tubules), mild tubulitis (<5% of tubules), and interstitial inflammatory infiltration (~10% of cortex), consistent with AIN. The glomerular findings met the 2010 Renal Pathology Society criteria for class IIa DN. There was no infection or systemic autoimmune disease. The herbal decoction was a possible trigger.

INTERVENTIONS: Prednisone was started on 15 January 2025 (0.52 mg/kg/d), followed by tapering and discontinuation. Repaglinide and insulin were used for glycemic control. Dapagliflozin was added at follow-up for glycemic normalization and renoprotection. Hypertension was treated, but no adjustments were required after glucocorticoid initiation.

OUTCOMES: At discharge, the sCr was 194 μmol/L. At the follow-up (March 19, 2026), there were improvements in the sCr, eGFR, blood urea nitrogen, HbA1c, and 24-h urinary protein, and these clinical parameters were about the same at the last follow-up (April 9, 2026). The antidiabetic regimen was continued unchanged, and the most recent HbA1c was 5.6% (March 19, 2026). The patient developed corticosteroid-associated hyperglycemia and insomnia. The hyperglycemia was successfully managed with insulin, and the insomnia improved during corticosteroid tapering. Dapagliflozin was subsequently added for glycemic control and kidney protection. No infection was recorded.

LESSONS: Kidney biopsy should be considered when a patient with diabetes develops acute kidney dysfunction because AIN can coexist with DN. This patient's kidney function improved after initiation of prednisone, but antihypertensive therapy was intensified before prednisone treatment. Glycemic therapy was then modified, and the possible offending herbal decoction was previously discontinued. Although we only examined a single patient with AIN and DN, glucocorticoid therapy may have contributed to the resolution of AIN.

articles.title: Adult-onset Still's disease and sarcopenia-related traits - muscle mass, strength, and function: A bi-directional Mendelian randomization study.
articles.abstract: The causal relationship between adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) and sarcopenia remains unclear. Therefore, we employed Mendelian randomization (MR) to investigate the causal link between these 2 conditions. This study investigated the causal relationships between AOSD (n = 201,947) and sarcopenia-related traits, including low handgrip strength (n = 256,523), left handgrip strength (n = 406,552), right handgrip strength (n = 461,089), appendicular lean mass (ALM, n = 450,243), and walking pace (WP, n = 459,915). In the first stage, AOSD served as the exposure variable, while the sarcopenia-related traits treated as the outcome variables; in the second stage, the roles were reversed. MR analysis employed inverse variance-weighted, weighted median, weighted mode, and MR-Egger methods. Cochran's Q statistic was used to assess heterogeneity, while MR-Egger regression and MR-PRESSO were utilized to evaluate pleiotropy. The robustness of the findings, risk of bias, and causal direction were assessed using leave-one-out analysis, funnel plots, and R2 statistics. AOSD may contribute to reduced muscle mass and strength, but not to impaired muscle function. Genetically predicted AOSD is causally associated with reduced ALM (odds ratio [OR] = 0.971, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.951-0.991; P = .005) and increased risk of low hand grip strength in individuals over 60 (OR = 1.046, 95% CI: 1.001-1.091; P = .048). It also reduces left hand grip strength (OR = 0.984, 95% CI: 0.976-0.992; P < .001), with no significant effect on right hand grip strength (OR = 0.995, 95% CI: 0.987-1.003; P = .240). with no effect on WP is also observed (OR = 0.994, 95% CI: 0.988-1.001; P = .080). Genetically predicted sarcopenia-related traits (ALM and bilateral grip strength) had no robust causal effect on AOSD. While inverse variance-weighted suggested nominally significant associations of reduced grip strength (≥60 years) and slower WP with AOSD, these results were inconsistent across MR methods and warrant cautious interpretation. AOSD leading to a decline in muscle mass, strength However, it does not significantly affect muscle function, whereas most sarcopenia-related traits showed no convincing causal effect on AOSD. Nominally significant associations observed for low hand grip strength in participants over 60 years and WP were not robust across sensitivity analyses and await further validation.

articles.title: Association of SII and SIRI with anxiety and depression severity in patients with acute coronary syndrome: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Emerging evidence indicates that inflammatory mechanisms may play a key role in linking psychological disorders to cardiovascular outcomes. This study aimed to explore the association between anxiety and depression levels and two inflammatory markers, the Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII) and the Systemic Inflammatory Response Index (SIRI), in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS). This retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted on 1498 patients with ACS who underwent coronary angiography (CAG) in Rasht, Iran, between January 2022 and June 2023. SII and SIRI were calculated for all patients. Patients' psychological status regarding anxiety and depression was evaluated using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS). All data analyses were conducted using SPSS version 22. The mean age of the patients was 58.49 ± 11.14 years, with males comprising 57.5% of the sample. Male participants exhibited significantly higher levels of anxiety and depression compared to females (P < .05). Individuals with comorbidities showed significantly lower anxiety scores (P < .05). Anxiety levels varied significantly based on CAG findings (P = .004). In multivariable ordinal logistic regression analyses, neither SII nor SIRI was significantly associated with depression severity (SII: OR = 1.029, 95% CI: 0.70-1.49; SIRI: OR = 1.012, 95% CI: 0.86-1.03) or anxiety severity (SII: OR = 0.906, 95% CI: 0.63-1.29; SIRI: OR = 1.005, 95% CI: 0.98-1.03). Systemic inflammation indices (SII and SIRI) did not show significant associations with anxiety or depression severity in cardiac patients, highlighting their limited utility as psychological predictors.

articles.title: Global burden and trends of subarachnoid hemorrhage in women aged 55 years and older: A repeated cross-sectional analysis of the GBD 2021 study.
articles.abstract: Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is a highly fatal stroke subtype with high mortality and disability. Women aged 55 years and older, approximating the postmenopausal population, carry a substantial share of this burden, yet global estimates for this group remain poorly defined. In this repeated cross-sectional analysis of Global Burden of Disease 2021 data, we examined incidence, prevalence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) among women aged 55 years and older in 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2021. Rates were directly age-standardized to the World Health Organization World Standard Population, and trends were summarized using the estimated annual percentage change from log-linear regression. We decomposed demographic and epidemiological drivers. Socioeconomic inequality was assessed with the concentration index and the slope index of inequality against the sociodemographic index (SDI). Between 1990 and 2021, the absolute number of incident and prevalent cases increased sharply, whereas deaths and DALYs declined slightly, even as age-standardized rates fell (all 4 rate trends declined significantly; estimated annual percentage change for the incidence rate = -1.65, 95% confidence interval = -1.77 to -1.52). The burden increased sharply after age 70. East Asia, particularly China, saw the sharpest declines in incidence and mortality rates, whereas India, Indonesia, and sub-Saharan Africa saw notable increases in absolute case numbers. Demographic shifts, mainly population aging and growth, drove the rising burden. Improvement in high-SDI regions explained little. After age standardization, none of the 4 rates was clearly correlated with SDI. Inequality analyses showed absolute gaps that narrowed for deaths and DALYs but widened slightly for prevalence, with prevalent cases concentrated in higher-SDI countries and deaths and DALYs in lower-SDI countries. The absolute burden of SAH in women aged 55 years and older is increasing because of population aging and socioeconomic disparities. Priorities should include targeted blood pressure screening and control for this age group in primary care, standardized emergency neurosurgical referral pathways, and expanded access to noninvasive neurovascular imaging in low and low-middle SDI regions.

articles.title: Time- and posture-specific management of severe supine hypertension and neurogenic orthostatic hypotension in diabetic autonomic neuropathy: A case report.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Coexistence of neurogenic orthostatic hypotension with supine or nocturnal hypertension creates a therapeutic challenge because treatment of either component may aggravate the other. This case illustrates a clinical management framework based on characterization of the full hemodynamic phenotype, repeated reassessment, and treatment adaptation according to posture and time of day, integrating postural blood pressure (BP) responses, 24-hour BP monitoring, symptoms, functional status, comorbidities, and safety findings.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A 63-year-old man with hypertension and insulin-treated type 2 diabetes presented with orthostatic dizziness and presyncope. Antihypertensive therapy was intensified for elevated seated BP. After intensification, upright tolerance worsened, with recurrent syncope, a rib fracture, and loss of functional independence. Symptoms remained disabling despite antihypertensive withdrawal and nonpharmacological measures.

DIAGNOSES: Supine-to-seated-to-standing assessment showed a BP fall from 197/99 mm Hg supine to 122/81 mm Hg seated and 79/56 mm Hg standing, with presyncope and heart rate increasing from 72 to 86 beats/min. Supine measurements and 24-hour BP monitoring documented severe supine and nocturnal hypertension, reverse dipping, and mean asleep BP 203/107 mm Hg. Autonomic testing demonstrated combined cardiovagal and adrenergic dysfunction, supporting neurogenic orthostatic hypotension due to diabetic autonomic neuropathy.

INTERVENTIONS: Management was tailored to upright and recumbent periods. A removable transdermal nitroglycerin patch was used overnight. Nonpharmacological measures included repeated encouragement to increase fluid intake, but daily intake generally remained below 2 L. Clinical assessment suggested relative volume depletion. Low-dose morning fludrocortisone was introduced cautiously despite severe supine/nocturnal hypertension. After upright tolerance improved, morning lercanidipine was added. Subsequent 24-hour BP monitoring showed a more balanced profile.

OUTCOMES: Orthostatic symptoms and upright tolerance improved. No further syncope or falls occurred, and functional independence improved. Later 24-hour BP monitoring showed reduced nocturnal predominance, with mean awake/asleep BP 164/86 and 165/89 mm Hg, respectively. Mild peripheral edema was managed with intermittent torasemide.

LESSONS: This case illustrates how integrating postural BP responses with 24-hour BP patterns can identify competing hemodynamic phenotypes that may require different management during upright and recumbent periods. Repeated reassessment and individualized treatment adaptation according to the documented BP pattern and clinical context may help balance competing risks of upright hypoperfusion and supine/nocturnal hypertension.

articles.title: Association between serum insulin levels and self-reported walking difficulty among adults with a history of stroke: A cross-sectional study of NHANES 1999-2018.
articles.abstract: Stroke is one of the leading causes of long-term disability worldwide. Walking difficulty is an important functional limitation among adults with a history of stroke. However, the association between serum insulin levels and self-reported walking difficulty in this population remains insufficiently studied. This study analyzed data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999-2018 to evaluate the association between serum insulin levels and self-reported walking difficulty among adults with a self-reported history of stroke. Weighted logistic regression models were used to adjust for confounders. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was conducted to explore potential nonlinear relationships. Sensitivity analyses were performed to assess the robustness of the findings. Subgroup analyses and interaction effect tests were conducted to examine heterogeneity across different populations. A total of 488 adults with a self-reported history of stroke were included in this study, representing 15,92,140 individuals in the US population. In the fully adjusted model, each 1 µU/mL increase in serum insulin level was associated with 5% higher odds of self-reported walking difficulty (OR = 1.05, 95% confidence interval: 1.01-1.09, P = .028).
