Quartile-based analysis showed that higher insulin levels (Q3, Q4) were significantly associated with greater odds of self-reported walking difficulty, with the highest quartile (Q4) showing an OR of 5.10 (95% confidence interval: 1.93-13.48, P = .001). RCS analysis suggested a possible nonlinear association between serum insulin levels and self-reported walking difficulty (P for non-linearity = .032). The associations observed in the sensitivity analyses were in the same direction as those in the primary analysis. Higher serum insulin levels were associated with greater odds of self-reported walking difficulty among adults with a self-reported history of stroke. These findings do not establish causality or a role for insulin in stroke-related motor recovery.

articles.title: The influence of high body mass index on asthma: A study integrating GBD 2021 and Mendelian randomization.
articles.abstract: Elevated body mass index (BMI) represents a significant adjustable risk element for asthma, posing a considerable worldwide health concern. This research was designed to assess the worldwide impact of asthma due to high BMI between 1990 and 2021, forecast patterns through 2050, and use 2-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) to examine whether elevated BMI is genetically associated with asthma risk, in order to guide preventive approaches. The data for this study were obtained from the global burden of disease 2021 study and the integrative epidemiology unit OpenGWAS project. We employed decomposition analysis, Joinpoint regression, and the Bayesian age-period-cohort model to analyze asthma-related mortality and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) by age, sex, and socio-demographic index region. Additionally, a bidirectional 2-sample MR analysis was performed to investigate the association between genetically predicted BMI and asthma risk. From 1990 to 2021, the global age-standardized mortality rate and age-standardized DALY rate for asthma attributable to high BMI declined. In contrast, the absolute number of deaths and DALYs increased by 63.9% and 45.7%, respectively. The most significant decline occurred between 1996 and 2000, while low-middle socio-demographic index regions experienced consistent increases. Projections to 2050 indicate a continued decline in age-standardized mortality rate but a slight increase in age-standardized DALY rate. Notably, females and older adults carried a higher disease burden. The MR analysis identified a positive, genetically supported association between elevated BMI and asthma risk (inverse-variance weighted odds ratio = 1.389, 95% confidence interval: 1.303-1.479). However, substantial heterogeneity across genetic variants suggests that this estimate should be interpreted with caution. The asthma burden related to high BMI is forecast to increase in the coming decades, mainly fueled by population growth, population aging, and socioeconomic inequalities. MR further supports a unidirectional, genetically supported association between higher BMI and asthma risk. These results highlight the critical necessity for implementing focused and fair public health strategies across the globe to tackle elevated BMI and reduce the associated asthma burden.

articles.title: Association between early central venous pressure monitoring and 30-day mortality in critically ill patients with comorbid heart failure and sepsis: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Central venous pressure (CVP) is widely used in the intensive care unit (ICU), but the optimal timing to initiate CVP monitoring remains unclear for patients with comorbid heart failure and sepsis. We explored the association between time to initial CVP measurement and 30-day mortality in this high-risk population. This retrospective cohort study included 9246 critically ill patients with comorbid heart failure and sepsis from the MIMIC-IV database. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis examined the relationship between time to initial CVP measurement and 30-day mortality. Inverse probability of treatment weighting followed by weighted logistic regression was used to assess the association between early CVP monitoring (≤6 hours after ICU admission) and 30-day mortality. A nonlinear J-shaped association emerged, with the lowest risk at 2.89 hours post-admission. Early CVP monitoring was associated with lower 30-day mortality (OR = 0.816, 95% CI: 0.688-0.967, P = .019). A landmark sensitivity analysis comparing no monitoring, early (≤6 hours), intermediate (6-86 hours), and late (>86 hours) monitoring showed a time-dependent relationship: intermediate (OR = 1.396, 95% CI: 1.194-1.632, P < .001) and late monitoring (OR = 3.141, 95% CI: 2.263-4.359, P < .001) were associated with progressively higher mortality. In critically ill patients with comorbid heart failure and sepsis, early CVP monitoring within 6 hours of ICU admission was associated with lower 30-day mortality, while delayed monitoring carried an elevated risk. Early integration of CVP within a multimodal hemodynamic assessment framework may be a prudent approach in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Can the Finnish Diabetes Risk Score (FINDRISC) identify gestational diabetes?: A multicenter cross-sectional study in Türkiye.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a common pregnancy complication with short- and long-term adverse outcomes for mother and child. The Finnish Diabetes Risk Score (FINDRISC) is a simple, validated questionnaire for type 2 diabetes risk, but its ability to identify GDM is not well established. In this multicenter cross-sectional study, 797 pregnant women at 24 to 28 weeks of gestation who attended 3 tertiary hospitals in Istanbul, Türkiye, between June and September 2024 completed the Turkish FINDRISC at the same visit as their routine GDM screening. GDM was diagnosed by the 1-step (75-g oral glucose tolerance test [OGTT]) or two-step (50-g glucose challenge test followed by 100-g OGTT) approach. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analysis were performed. GDM was diagnosed in 104 women (13.0%). The FINDRISC score was higher in women with GDM (median 8 [interquartile range 6-12] vs 7 [4-10]; P = .001); each 1-point increase was associated with 8% higher odds of GDM (OR 1.08; 95% confidence interval, 1.03-1.13). The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.599 (95% confidence interval, 0.542-0.655). At the optimal cutoff (≥8 points), sensitivity was 62.5%, specificity 53.2%, positive predictive value 16.7%, negative predictive value 90.4%, and negative likelihood ratio 0.70; 37.5% of GDM cases scored below this cutoff. A cutoff of ≥4 points yielded 88.5% sensitivity but would have avoided OGTT in only 22.0% of women. In multivariable analysis, age ≥ 35 years (adjusted OR 2.40), body mass index > 30 kg/m2 (adjusted OR 2.88), and non-daily fruit/vegetable intake (adjusted OR 1.70) were independently associated with GDM. When administered at 24 to 28 weeks, FINDRISC showed poor discrimination for concurrently diagnosed GDM. Its negative predictive value largely reflects the low prevalence of GDM, and no cutoff combined acceptable sensitivity with a meaningful reduction in OGTTs. FINDRISC should not replace universal OGTT screening; pregnancy-specific risk models evaluated prospectively in early pregnancy are needed.

articles.title: Prevalence of Dokha use in Arabian countries: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dokha, a form of tobacco smoked using midwakh pipes, is increasingly used in Arabian countries, yet comprehensive prevalence data remain limited. This study aimed to systematically review and meta-analyze the prevalence of Dokha use across Arabian countries, stratified by gender, type of use, and use of specific smoking tools.

METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase for studies published in English from inception to June 2025. Eligible studies reported prevalence estimates of Dokha use among any population subgroup in Arabian countries. Two independent reviewers screened studies, extracted data, and assessed methodological quality using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to estimate pooled prevalence rates for current and lifetime Dokha use among males and females, as well as use of specific Dokha smoking tools. Data were analyzed using Comprehensive Meta-Analysis version 3.0.

RESULTS: Out of 729 studies found, 12 studies were included, encompassing populations from multiple Arabian countries. Current Dokha use among females was extremely low (0.7%, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.1%-4.9%), whereas males exhibited substantially higher current use (14.6%, 95% CI = 7.9%-25.4%). Lifetime use followed similar trends, with a pooled prevalence of 9.1% (95% CI = 3.9%-20.0%) among females and 25.6% (95% CI = 10.8%-49.5%) among males. Use of specific Dokha smoking tools was reported at 7.3% (95% CI = 5.6%-9.4%) for current use and 15.8% (95% CI = 10.0%-24.0%) for lifetime use. Considerable heterogeneity was observed across studies, particularly among male users, reflecting differences in population, geography, and study methodology.

CONCLUSION: Dokha use in Arabian countries demonstrates pronounced gender disparities, with males showing substantially higher prevalence than females, which highlights the need for targeted public health interventions, surveillance, and culturally sensitive tobacco control strategies addressing Dokha use in this region.

articles.title: Association between inpatient aspirin exposure and 28-day mortality in critically ill patients with sepsis-induced coagulopathy: A cohort study.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the association between inpatient aspirin exposure and 28-day mortality in critically ill patients with sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC). We conducted a retrospective cohort study extracting data from the MIMIC-IV v3.1 database (2008-2022). Adult critically ill patients with SIC in the intensive care unit (ICU) were included. The primary outcome was 28-day mortality. Secondary outcomes encompassed mortality (e.g., in-hospital, ICU, 60-day, 90-day, and 1-year) and duration of ICU-free, ventilation-free, or vasopressor-free days within 28 days of admission to the ICU. Multivariable Cox regression, propensity score matching (PSM), inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), overlap weighting (OW), pairwise algorithmic weighting (PA), and doubly robust estimation were employed to control confounders. Robustness of findings was assessed through subgroup and sensitivity analyses. Among 9095 critically ill patients with SIC, 3207 (35.3%) received aspirin during ICU hospitalization. After 1:1 propensity score matching (2069 pairs), inpatient aspirin exposure was independently associated with significantly lower 28-day mortality (hazard ratio [HR] 0.74; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.65-0.85; P < .001). This association remained consistent across multiple analytical methods including IPTW (HR 0.76; 95% CI: 0.70-0.84; P < .001), OW (HR 0.72; 95% CI: 0.61-0.84; P < .001), PA (HR 0.73; 95% CI: 0.61-0.84; P < .001), and doubly robust estimation (HR 0.76; 95% CI: 0.61-0.94; P < .001). Inpatient aspirin exposure was also associated with more favorable secondary clinical outcomes (all P < .001). In critically ill patients with SIC, inpatient aspirin exposure was independently associated with lower 28-day mortality and more favorable clinical outcomes. These findings should be interpreted as an association rather than evidence of a causal therapeutic effect. Prospective randomized studies are warranted to validate these findings.

articles.title: Causal association between gestational diabetes mellitus and peripartum mental disorders: Evidence from two-sample Mendelian randomization.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is associated with multiple maternal and neonatal complications, but its direct causal impact on peripartum mental health remains uncertain. This study used a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) approach to assess whether genetically predicted GDM increases the risk of peripartum mental disorders, including depression, anxiety, and suicidality. Genetic variants associated with GDM were obtained from the FinnGen consortium, and summary data for peripartum mental disorders were derived from genome-wide association studies. Independent single-nucleotide polymorphisms (P < 5 × 10-6, r2 < 0.001) were analyzed using inverse-variance weighted, MR-Egger, and weighted median methods. Heterogeneity, pleiotropy, and causal direction were evaluated using Cochran's Q, the MR-Egger intercept, and Steiger filtering. Nineteen independent single-nucleotide polymorphisms were identified. Inverse-variance weighted analysis indicated a positive causal association between genetically predicted GDM and peripartum mental disorders. The estimated effect was β = 0.048, with a standard error (SE) of 0.014 and P = 8.3 × 10⁻⁴; the odds ratio was 1.049 (95% confidence interval = 1.020-1.0779). The results were consistent in all the sensitivity analyses, with no evidence of heterogeneity or pleiotropy. The MR findings provide genetic evidence supporting a causal link between GDM and peripartum mental disorders. These results underscore the need for integrated clinical management that simultaneously addresses metabolic control and psychological well-being in women diagnosed with GDM.

articles.title: Prognostic value of anti-gp210 antibodies in primary biliary cholangitis: A Systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease characterized by portal inflammation and immune-mediated nonsuppurative destructive cholangitis. Recent studies have shown that anti-gp210 antibodies are associated with the prognosis of PBC. Here, we conducted a pooled analysis of the relationship between anti-gp210 antibodies and the prognosis of PBC patients to identify high-risk patients early and provide individualized interventions.

METHODS: PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Web of Science databases were searched until January 2025. A meta-analysis was undertaken using a fixed-effects model and 95% confidence interval (CI) when no statistically significant heterogeneity existed; otherwise, a random-effects statistical model was used.

RESULTS: A total of 12 records were included in this systematic review and meta-analysis. The results of our meta-analysis showed that anti-gp210 positive PBC patients had a higher incidence of liver failure (relative risk (RR), 6.11; 95% CI, 3.16-11.81) and mortality (RR, 1.92; 95% CI, 1.55-2.37) and a lower ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) response rate (RR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.73-0.89) compared with anti-gp210 negative patients. Moreover, the presence of anti-gp210 antibodies was independently associated with a poor prognosis in patients with PBC (hazard ratios (HR), 4.53; 95% CI, 2.83-7.26). In addition, anti-gp210 positive PBC patients had higher serum gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase (GGT) (mean difference (MD), 53.03; 95% CI, 3.70-102.36), immunoglobulin M (IgM) (MD, 1.29; 95% CI, 0.80-1.78), and immunoglobulin G (IgG) (MD, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.07-2.06) levels and lower albumin (MD, -1.74; 95% CI, -2.80 to - 0.69) levels.

CONCLUSION: In conclusion, PBC patients with positive anti-gp210 have a worse prognosis than those with negative anti-gp210. Incorporating anti-gp210 testing into clinical practice could enhance risk stratification and guide personalized management, ultimately improving outcomes for this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Synchronous hepatocellular carcinoma and nasopharyngeal carcinoma in a patient with chronic hepatitis B: A case report and literature review.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Synchronous double primary cancers involving hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) are exceptionally rare. Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is an established cause of HCC, whereas Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection is the major etiological factor for NPC. We report a patient with synchronous HCC and NPC and review the relevant literature.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A 63-year-old Chinese man with chronic HBV presented with a liver mass detected on routine screening. He reported nasal obstruction.

DIAGNOSES: Contrast-enhanced imaging showed a 46 × 59 mm hepatic lesion with portal vein tumor thrombus and a 41 × 29 mm nasopharyngeal mass with bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy. Biopsies confirmed moderately differentiated HCC and EBV-associated non-keratinizing NPC. Final diagnoses were HCC Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer Stage C (CNLC IIIa, Child-Pugh A) and NPC T3N2M0 Stage III (AJCC 8th edition).

INTERVENTIONS: He received hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC, mFOLFOX) combined with tislelizumab and donafenib; radiotherapy for NPC was deferred after shared decision-making. Entecavir was continued.

OUTCOMES: At 19-month follow-up, both tumors remained controlled; the NPC met radiographic complete response criteria.

LESSONS: Synchronous HCC and EBV-associated NPC were controlled during treatment with a tislelizumab-containing multimodality regimen, and the NPC achieved a radiographic complete response. The contribution of each treatment component cannot be determined from a single case, and definitive radiotherapy remains the standard of care for locoregionally advanced NPC. Multidisciplinary management and close monitoring are essential.

articles.title: A clinicopathological prediction model for remission after transsphenoidal surgery for acromegaly: A retrospective single-center cohort study.
articles.abstract: Transsphenoidal surgery (TSS) is the primary treatment of choice in acromegaly. Previous research on predicting remission after TSS was mainly based on clinical and radiological data, lacking histopathological evaluation. Our aim is to produce a clinicopathological prediction model for remission after TSS in acromegaly, enabling clinicians to better inform patients on expected treatment outcomes. This single-center study involved retrospective data collection in a large tertiary referral center in The Netherlands. One hundred patients in whom TSS was performed as primary therapy between January 2000 and July 2019 were included. Uni- and multivariate regression models were used to identify predictors of early biochemical remission according to the consensus criteria, long-term remission (defined as an age- and sex-normalized Insuline growth like factor 1and the absence of postoperative treatment (radiation therapy, repeat surgery, or medical therapy) at last follow-up, irrespective of residual tumor on postoperative magnetic resonance imaging ), and long-term remission without residual tumor (defined by the same biochemical and treatment criteria with the additional absence of residual tumor on postoperative magnetic resonance imaging ). In univariate logistic regression, a larger tumor volume, a larger maximum tumor diameter, a higher modified Knosp classification grade, the presence of cavernous sinus invasion, and a higher random growth hormone at diagnosis were significantly associated with lower remission rates. Tumor subtype and proliferation markers were not. In multivariate logistic regression, a simple model with only maximum tumor diameter as an independent variable predicted best for early biochemical remission (OR 0.85, 95% CI 0.78-0.93, P < .001, sensitivity 78.9%, specificity 71.8%), long-term remission (OR 0.79, 95% CI 0.70-0.88, P < .001, sensitivity 79.5%, specificity 73.7%), and long-term remission without residual tumor (OR 0.75, 95% CI 0.66-0.86, P < .001, sensitivity 79.4%, specificity 78.0%). Maximum tumor diameter was the best predictor, while histopathological characteristics were not predictive for remission after TSS in acromegaly in this cohort.

articles.title: Comparative efficacy and safety of second- and later-line BRAF-targeted regimens in BRAF V600E-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: BRAF V600E mutations occur in approximately 8 to 12% of metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) cases and define an aggressive phenotype with poor prognosis. While the BEACON CRC trial established encorafenib-based combinations as effective second-line options, direct head-to-head comparisons among available BRAF-targeted regimens are lacking. This network meta-analysis (NMA) compared the relative efficacy and safety of second- and later-line BRAF-targeted regimens in BRAF V600E-mutant mCRC.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception through January 2026. Eligible studies enrolled adult patients with BRAF V600E-mutant mCRC receiving second- or later-line BRAF-targeted therapy and reported time-to-event survival outcomes. A frequentist NMA was conducted under a random-effects model using the netmeta package in R. Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled for progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). Where HRs were unavailable, individual patient data were reconstructed from Kaplan-Meier curves using the Guyot method. Treatment ranking used P-scores, with irinotecan plus cetuximab as the reference comparator.

RESULTS: Four trials enrolling 922 patients across 9 treatment arms were included. All 4 experimental regimens demonstrated significant PFS benefit over irinotecan plus cetuximab. Encorafenib plus cetuximab plus alpelisib ranked highest for PFS (HR 0.33, 95% CI 0.15-0.71; P-score 0.789), followed by encorafenib plus binimetinib plus cetuximab (EBC; HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.29-0.49), encorafenib plus cetuximab (EC; HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.31-0.50), and vemurafenib plus irinotecan plus cetuximab (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.32-0.77). For OS, only EBC (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.39-0.69) and EC (HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.46-0.76) achieved statistically significant benefits. No significant difference was detected between EBC and EC on either endpoint. No between-study heterogeneity was detected (I2 = 0%). In the exploratory safety network, encorafenib plus cetuximab was the only encorafenib-based regimen associated with significantly fewer grade ≥ 3 adverse events than irinotecan plus cetuximab (odds ratio 0.67, 95% CI 0.47-0.96).

CONCLUSION: These findings position encorafenib-based therapy, and encorafenib plus cetuximab in particular, as the reference standard for previously treated BRAF V600E-mutant mCRC, while underscoring that the incremental value of more intensive regimens must be weighed against tolerability and confirmed in adequately powered trials.

articles.title: Bone marrow sarcoidosis in Takayasu arteritis: Case report and literature review.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Takayasu arteritis (TA) is a systemic granulomatous large-vessel vasculitis predominantly involving the aorta and its primary branches. Sarcoidosis is a systemic granulomatous disorder characterized histologically by non-necrotizing epithelioid granulomas, most commonly affecting the lungs. Although the coexistence of TA and sarcoidosis has been documented, bone marrow involvement by sarcoidosis in a patient with concomitant TA has not, to our knowledge, been previously reported.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A 46-year-old woman with a confirmed diagnosis of TA presented with elevated systemic inflammatory markers and diffuse hypermetabolic activity on positron emission tomography (PET). Clinical, radiological, and pathological evaluations were performed.

DIAGNOSES: Bone marrow biopsy revealed multiple non-necrotizing granulomas, supporting bone marrow involvement by sarcoidosis. This overlap of granulomatous conditions was identified in the context of persistent systemic inflammation.

INTERVENTIONS: Mycofenolate Mofetil was replaced by Infliximab therapy.

OUTCOMES: The patient exhibited significant clinical improvement and marked improvement in inflammatory markers with infliximab therapy.

LESSONS: This case highlights the importance of maintaining a broad differential diagnosis in patients with autoimmune or inflammatory diseases who develop new systemic manifestations. Recognizing rare organ involvement in overlapping granulomatous conditions is critical for accurate diagnosis and management.

articles.title: Mechanistic study of ECM phenotype switch in epicardial adipose tissue in atrial fibrillation: A bioinformatics study.
articles.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common cardiac arrhythmia. Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) is closely associated with AF, but its molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate the extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling characteristics of AF-related EAT. Using the publicly available RNA-sequencing dataset GSE135445 (AF: n = 6, sinus rhythm: n = 6), we performed differential expression analysis (DESeq2) on gene-level counts regenerated from the raw sequencing reads, single-gene analysis focusing on ECM gene families, and gene set enrichment analysis. An "ECM phenotype switch" hypothesis was proposed based on the coordinated dysregulation of interstitial and basement membrane collagen genes. Differential expression analysis identified 610 differentially expressed genes. Notably, the basement membrane-specific collagen COL4A4 was significantly upregulated in AF (log2FC = 4.37, Padj = 2.7 × 10-9), accompanied by significant upregulation of COL4A3, whereas interstitial collagen repair genes (COL1A1, COL1A2, COL3A1, and FN1) showed consistent downregulation, defining an "ECM phenotype switch" characterized by suppressed interstitial repair coupled with independent basement membrane deposition; the fibrinolysis inhibitor SERPINE1 (plasminogen activator inhibitor-1) was also markedly upregulated (log2FC = 3.89, Padj = .026). Gene set enrichment analysis implicated ribosome biogenesis and translation dysregulation as a potential associated upstream program (normalized enrichment score = 2.26-3.03 and false discovery rate = 0.012-0.013). AF-related EAT exhibits an ECM phenotype switch characterized by suppressed interstitial collagen repair and independent basement membrane collagen deposition, potentially associated with ribosome biogenesis dysregulation. These hypothesis-generating findings provide a novel framework for understanding EAT-mediated atrial remodeling in AF.

articles.title: Effects of Tai Chi combined with repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation on sleep and emotional outcomes in older adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep problems are common in older adults and are frequently accompanied by emotional symptoms, including depression, anxiety, and stress. Tai Chi and repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) have both been applied as non-pharmacological interventions for sleep and mood regulation. However, evidence regarding the effectiveness of their combined use remains limited.

METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, the Cochrane Library, CINAHL, and Scopus from inception to December 16, 2025, to identify randomized controlled trials. The search strategy combined terms related to Tai Chi, repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation, and randomized controlled trials. Reference lists of relevant articles were also screened to identify additional eligible studies. Pooled mean differences with 95% confidence intervals were generated using RevMan 5.4, with risk of bias and certainty assessed through established tools including GRADE.

RESULTS: Three trials encompassing 211 older adults qualified for analysis. Combined Tai Chi and rTMS was associated with a significant reduction in sleep severity compared with control interventions (SMD = -0.51; 95% CI: -0.90 to -0.12; P = .01; I2 = 43%). Evidence for other sleep-related outcomes and for depression, anxiety, and stress was inconclusive.

CONCLUSION: The available evidence suggests that the combination of Tai Chi and rTMS may improve overall sleep severity; however, this finding should be interpreted cautiously given the small number of trials and sensitivity to individual studies. Evidence for specific sleep parameters and emotional outcomes remains inconclusive. Further well-designed randomized trials are needed to clarify the potential role of this combined intervention in sleep and mood regulation.

articles.title: IgD-λ POEMS syndrome presenting with edema, pulmonary hypertension, and renal impairment: A case report.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Polyneuropathy, organomegaly, endocrinopathy, monoclonal plasma-cell disorder, and skin changes (POEMS) syndrome is a rare multisystem syndrome associated with clonal plasma-cell disorders. The IgD-λ subtype is uncommon, and a low-level monoclonal protein may escape detection by routine electrophoresis and immunofixation electrophoresis (IFE), delaying diagnosis.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A 38-year-old woman was admitted in April 2025 with intermittent bilateral lower-extremity edema for >3 years, elevated serum creatinine for 8 months, and acute worsening over 4 days. She subsequently developed pulmonary hypertension, polyserous effusions, splenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, anemia, thrombocytosis, and renal impairment, and had been diagnosed elsewhere with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension.

DIAGNOSES: Right-heart catheterization confirmed precapillary pulmonary hypertension. Routine serum and urine protein studies, including IFE, were negative. Following multidisciplinary evaluation, nerve-conduction studies showed peripheral neuropathy; serum vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) was elevated; and bone marrow studies demonstrated a clonal plasma-cell population with cytoplasmic λ light-chain restriction. Extended serum IFE, including anti-IgD and anti-IgE antisera, detected a trace, nonquantifiable monoclonal IgD component, establishing IgD-λ POEMS syndrome. Renal biopsy showed POEMS-associated glomerular microangiopathy-like lesions with acute tubular injury.

INTERVENTIONS: The patient received dexamethasone acetate plus lenalidomide and underwent autologous stem-cell transplantation on December 2, 2025.

OUTCOMES: By March 2026, peripheral edema had resolved, pulmonary hypertension was mild on echocardiography, serum creatinine had decreased to 60 μmol/L, and VEGF had normalized.

LESSONS: POEMS syndrome should be considered in patients with unexplained multisystem disease, particularly edema or polyserous effusions accompanied by pulmonary hypertension and renal impairment. Negative routine M-protein testing should not exclude the diagnosis; VEGF testing, bone marrow evaluation, and extended IFE may reveal an occult plasma-cell clone.

articles.title: Joint associations of estimated glucose disposal rate and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein with metabolic syndrome in Korean adults: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Metabolic syndrome (MetS), an important metabolic risk phenotype within the broader cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) framework, is characterized by insulin resistance and chronic low-grade inflammation; however, evidence regarding the joint relationship of these 2 biological dimensions with MetS remains limited. We analyzed cross-sectional data from 20,781 Korean adults aged ≥ 19 years who were enrolled in the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES) 2015-2018. MetS was classified using the National Cholesterol Education Program Adult Treatment Panel III framework with waist circumference thresholds adapted for the Korean/Asian populations. Weighted logistic regression was performed to examine the relationships between estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) and MetS. Potential dose-response patterns were further explored using restricted cubic splines. Joint analyses, interaction analysis, and prespecified subgroup analyses were also performed. MetS was present in 29.4% of participants after weighting. In the fully adjusted model, higher eGDR was associated with lower odds of MetS per unit (OR 0.48, 95% CI: 0.47-0.49), whereas log-transformed hs-CRP showed a positive association with MetS, with higher levels corresponding to greater odds (OR 1.71, 95% CI: 1.64-1.79; both P < .001). Dose-response analyses revealed a decreasing pattern for eGDR and an increasing pattern for hs-CRP in relation to MetS. In joint analyses, progressively higher odds of MetS were observed across exposure categories, with the low-eGDR/high-hs-CRP profile corresponding to the greatest odds of MetS. No significant multiplicative interaction was detected (P for interaction = .064). The association of the joint high-risk profile with MetS was generally consistent across subgroups and appeared stronger among younger participants and those without diabetes. Lower eGDR and higher hs-CRP levels were independently associated with MetS in Korean adults, and the low-eGDR/high-hs-CRP profile was associated with the highest odds of MetS. Their joint assessment may provide complementary information for characterizing adverse metabolic profiles within the broader CKM framework, although prospective studies are needed to determine its predictive value.

articles.title: Bibliometric analysis of septic cardiomyopathy: Current status, research hotspots, and emerging trends (2015-2025).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Septic cardiomyopathy (SCM) represents a life-threatening complication of sepsis. This study provides the first systematic bibliometric analysis and visualization of research in this field during the critical decade following the publication of the "Sepsis-3" definition (2015-2025), highlighting the current status, hotspots, and emerging trends.

METHODS: Publications related to SCM were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection for the period August 2015 to August 2025. After data cleaning, bibliometric and visualization analyses were conducted using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, Scimago Graphica, and Excel/GraphPad Prism.

RESULTS: The annual number of publications has shown exponential growth since the release of the Sepsis-3 guidelines. China has emerged as the global leader in research output, with Wuhan University identified as the leading institution. The knowledge base is anchored in the Sepsis-3 guidelines and seminal reviews on pathophysiology. Research frontiers have evolved from macro-level concepts such as "inflammation" and "oxidative stress" toward more precise molecular targets, including "ferroptosis," "mitophagy," and the "NLRP3 inflammasome," while "machine learning" has begun to penetrate as an emerging methodological approach.

CONCLUSION: Over the past decade, research on SCM has shifted from broad pathophysiological concepts toward specific molecular mechanisms. The resulting knowledge map provides a reference for identifying key literature, influential teams, and emerging research directions. Future studies should link mechanistic findings to clinical phenotypes and evaluate diagnostic and therapeutic strategies using patient-centered outcomes.

articles.title: Risk of retinal vascular occlusion following COVID-19 vaccination: A meta-analysis of nearly 15 million individuals.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Retinal vascular occlusion is a rare ocular condition reported following coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccination. However, the association between vaccination and retinal vascular occlusion remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the frequency and risk of retinal vascular occlusion following COVID-19 vaccination.

METHODS: Four electronic databases were systematically searched through August 2026. Observational studies reporting retinal vascular occlusion after COVID-19 vaccination were included. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to estimate pooled event proportions and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Potentially overlapping study populations were assessed, and study quality was evaluated using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale.

RESULTS: Five studies comprising 14,877,781 reported participants were included. The pooled proportion of retinal vascular occlusion events among vaccinated individuals was 0.02% (95% CI: 0.00%-0.07%; I2 = 99.5%). The overall association between vaccination and retinal vascular occlusion was not statistically significant (RR = 2.12, 95% CI: 0.65-6.90; P = .213), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 96.8%). However, separate analyses showed statistically significant associations for retinal artery occlusion (RR = 2.03, 95% CI: 1.17-3.51) and retinal vein occlusion (RR = 2.26, 95% CI: 2.08-2.47), without a significant difference between subtypes (P = .696). No significant associations between retinal vascular occlusion and vaccine were observed in sex-specific analyses. Among vaccine types, ChAdOx1/AstraZeneca showed a significant association (RR = 2.00, 95% CI: 1.60-2.50), based on a single study, whereas pooled associations for other vaccines were nonsignificant.

CONCLUSION: Retinal vascular occlusion events following COVID-19 vaccination were rare. Although the overall association was not statistically significant, separate arterial and venous analyses showed significant associations. Substantial heterogeneity, potential confounding, and differences in contributing studies limit definitive conclusions. Further research is needed to clarify these findings.

articles.title: Effects and safety of Korean red ginseng on the clinical course of uterine leiomyoma: A double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Korean red ginseng (KRG) is widely used as a dietary supplement, but its effects on uterine leiomyoma growth and reproductive hormones are unclear. We evaluated whether KRG affects leiomyoma growth, routine laboratory indices, or endocrine profiles in premenopausal women with uterine leiomyoma managed expectantly.

METHODS: In this single-center, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial, premenopausal women aged 20 to 45 years with a uterine leiomyoma of 1 to 8 cm suitable for expectant management were allocated 1:1 to KRG 3 g/d or matching placebo for 6 months. Participants, investigators, ultrasonography examiners, and analysts were blinded. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in the 6-month change in maximal diameter of the index leiomyoma on ultrasonography, analyzed by analysis of covariance adjusted for baseline diameter. Secondary outcomes were complete blood count, ferritin, liver enzymes, and reproductive hormones.

RESULTS: Between December 2015 and September 2019, 69 participants were randomized (placebo 34, KRG 35) and 61 completed the 6-month assessment (placebo 30, KRG 31); all 8 noncompletions were losses to follow-up. Maximal diameter increased modestly in both groups, with no significant between-group difference in change (mean difference -0.11 cm; 95% confidence interval: -0.33 to 0.12; P = .34); the upper confidence limit lay below the prespecified target difference of 0.33 cm. There were no significant between-group differences in laboratory changes or in baseline-, age-, and body mass index-adjusted log scale hormone ratios, and the multivariate hormone profile did not differ between groups (Pillai's trace = 0.056; P = .68). In exploratory post hoc analyses, the internal correlation structure among hormone changes was similar in both arms. No treatment-related serious adverse event and no discontinuation for intolerance was documented, although adverse events were ascertained passively.

CONCLUSION: In premenopausal women with uterine leiomyoma managed expectantly, 6 months of KRG supplementation did not meaningfully alter leiomyoma growth, routine laboratory indices, or reproductive hormone homeostasis compared with placebo. Within the constraints of a modest sample size, incomplete characterization of the study product, and passive adverse-event ascertainment, these findings do not establish the safety of KRG, and they support no conclusion regarding nonserious adverse effects.

articles.title: National trends and demographic disparities in mortality involving co-listed chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and substance use disorders among U.S. adults aged ≥65 years: A population-based serial cross-sectional CDC WONDER analysis, 1999 to 2020.
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and substance use disorders (SUDs) frequently coexist, yet national mortality patterns involving both conditions among older adults remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated temporal, demographic, geographic, and substance-specific patterns in U.S. death records co-listing COPD and SUDs among adults aged ≥65 years. We conducted a descriptive serial cross-sectional analysis of Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Wide-ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research multiple cause of death data from 1999 to 2020. Eligible records included deaths among adults aged ≥65 years in which COPD (International Classification of Diseases, 10th revision J41-J44) and SUDs (F10-F19) were both recorded in the Multiple Cause of Death fields. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) were calculated overall and by sex, race/ethnicity, census region, urbanization, and state; age-group analyses used age-specific crude mortality rates. Joinpoint regression estimated annual percent changes and average annual percent changes. Secondary analyses examined individual F10 to F19 categories, with a sensitivity analysis excluding tobacco/nicotine-related disorders (F17). Among 1,524,216 qualifying deaths, the overall AAMR increased from 25.5/100,000 in 1999 to 213.2 in 2020, peaking at 219.0 in 2017. Males had higher pooled AAMRs than females (216.98 vs 132.54). The highest pooled racial/ethnic AAMR occurred among non-Hispanic American Indian or Alaska Native adults (191.99), followed closely by non-Hispanic White adults (188.68). The Midwest had the highest regional AAMR, while nonmetropolitan counties had higher AAMRs than metropolitan counties (232.82 vs 152.03). Tobacco/nicotine-related disorders accounted for the predominant substance-specific burden. Excluding F17 yielded an average annual percent change of 2.19% (95% confidence interval, 1.37-3.02). In the overall F10 to F19 analysis, mortality involving co-listed COPD and SUDs increased markedly during the earlier study period before stabilizing, whereas temporal trajectories differed across individual substance categories. Substantial demographic, geographic, and substance-specific heterogeneity was observed. Findings are descriptive and should not be interpreted causally.

articles.title: Development and pilot feasibility testing of an evidence-based endotracheal tube maintenance protocol for critically ill patients: A delphi consensus study.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to develop and preliminarily pilot-test an evidence-based endotracheal tube (ETT) maintenance protocol for adult critically ill patients in intensive care units. Based on the Population, Intervention, Professional, Outcome, Setting, Type of Evidence framework, an initial protocol draft was constructed via systematic literature synthesis. Two rounds of modified Delphi expert consultations were conducted among a multidisciplinary panel of 12 specialists across 8 tertiary hospitals. Subsequently, a 3-month feasibility pilot involving 10 frontline intensive care unit nurses was implemented to evaluate bedside usability and protocol adherence. Expert questionnaire recovery rates were 100% in both rounds, with an expert authority coefficient (Cr) of 0.896. In Round 2, all retained items achieved acceptable convergence (coefficients of variation ≤ 0.18, mean scores 4.42-5.00), while Kendall W was 0.329 (P < .001). The feasibility pilot demonstrated an overall nursing compliance rate of 88.5% and informed 7 targeted modifications to resolve bedside operational barriers. The finalized protocol comprises pre-procedure governance, intra-procedure interventions (ETT securement, cuff pressure maintenance at 25-30 cm H2O, subglottic drainage, indication-driven suctioning, oral care), and post-procedure emergency response and quality auditing. This study established a standardized, granular, and clinically operable ETT maintenance protocol with robust expert consensus and high bedside usability. It provides a practical framework for critical care nursing, laying the foundation for future multicenter clinical efficacy trials.

articles.title: The application value of two-dimensional speckle tracking imaging technology in evaluating the functions of the left atrium and left atrial appendage in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation: A comparative cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is associated with increased risk of stroke due to left atrial appendage (LAA) thrombus formation. Two-dimensional speckle tracking imaging (2D-STI) may provide valuable insights into left atrial and LAA functional changes associated with thrombus formation. This study aimed to evaluate the functions of the left atrium (LA) and LAA in patients with non-valvular AF by using 2D-STI and explore echocardiographic parameters associated with the presence of LAA thrombus. In this comparative cross-sectional study, consecutive patients with non-valvular AF who were scheduled for radiofrequency ablation were screened. Finally, 68 eligible AF patients and 30 age-matched healthy controls were included. All AF patients underwent preoperative transthoracic echocardiography, transesophageal echocardiography, and two-dimensional speckle tracking imaging, and were classified according to the presence or absence of LAA thrombus detected by transesophageal echocardiography into the thrombus group (n = 32) and the non-thrombus group (n = 36). The healthy controls were included as a reference group for comparison of echocardiographic parameters. The left atrial appendage emptying velocity (LAAEV), left atrial global longitudinal strain (LAGLS), and LAA global longitudinal strain (LAAGLS) were measured and compared between groups. Compared with the control group, AF patients showed significantly reduced LAAEV, LAGLS, and left atrial appendage global longitudinal strain (all P < .05). In AF patients, the thrombus group had significantly lower LAAEV, LAGLS, and left atrial appendage global longitudinal strain compared to the non-thrombus group (all P < .05). Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that LAAEV and left atrial strain during reservoir phase were significantly associated with the presence of LAA thrombus. 2D-STI can quantitatively evaluate the functional changes of the LA and LAA. LAAEV and left atrial strain during reservoir phase may serve as useful echocardiographic markers for assisting clinical evaluation of LAA thrombus.

articles.title: Magnetic resonance neurography-supported L3-L4 radiculitis presenting as refractory peripatellar neuropathic pain in a patient with diabetes: A case report.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Peripatellar pain is usually attributed to local knee disorders. However, proximal neural lesions can also cause pain around the knee. Third and fourth lumbar (L3-L4) radiculitis presenting mainly as peripatellar neuropathic pain is uncommon and may be missed when typical radicular symptoms are absent.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A 75-year-old man with a more than 20-year history of type 2 diabetes presented with severe left peripatellar pain for 10 days. The pain was burning and stabbing and was accompanied by numbness and marked touch-evoked allodynia. The visual analog scale score was 8-9/10, and the Douleur Neuropathique 4 score was 9/10. He had no low back pain, typical radicular pain, motor weakness, or reflex abnormalities.

DIAGNOSES: Knee magnetic resonance imaging showed degenerative changes that did not explain the neuropathic pain phenotype. Lumbar magnetic resonance imaging showed no definite compression of the L3 or L4 nerve roots. Electrodiagnostic testing did not provide level-specific localization. Magnetic resonance neurography showed asymmetric hyperintensity involving the left L3 and L4 proximal neural structures, supporting the diagnosis of L3-L4 radiculitis.

INTERVENTIONS: Neuropathic pain medications and knee-targeted procedures provided inadequate or only transient relief. The patient was subsequently treated with pregabalin, duloxetine, short-term opioid analgesia, and optimization of glycemic control.

OUTCOMES: The pain and allodynia gradually improved within 2 weeks, and analgesic medications were discontinued. At 3 months, the visual analog scale score was 0-3/10 and the Douleur Neuropathique 4 score was 1/10. Touch-evoked allodynia had resolved.

LESSONS: L3-L4 radiculitis may present as refractory peripatellar neuropathic pain without low back pain or typical radicular symptoms. When severe neuropathic pain around the knee cannot be explained by local pathology, a proximal neural lesion should be considered. Magnetic resonance neurography may help identify radiculitis that is not evident on conventional lumbar imaging.

articles.title: Fasting glucose-to-HDL cholesterol ratio and risk of MASLD in nonobese Chinese adults: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is increasingly recognized in nonobese individuals; however, reliable markers for early risk identification remain limited. The fasting glucose-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (FHR) ratio, which reflects integrated glucolipid metabolism, has emerged as a potential indicator. This study aimed to evaluate the association between FHR and the incidence of MASLD in nonobese adults. This retrospective cohort study included 16,173 nonobese Chinese adults (body mass index < 25 kg/m2) from the Wenzhou Health Examination Cohort. Participants without MASLD at baseline were categorized into quartiles according to their FHR levels. Incident MASLD was diagnosed using abdominal ultrasonography during follow-up. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) after adjusting for demographic, clinical, and metabolic factors. Dose-response relationships were assessed using restricted cubic spline models, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to evaluate predictive performance. During follow-up, 2322 participants developed MASLD. Higher FHR levels were significantly associated with an increased risk of MASLD. In the fully adjusted model, each 1-unit increase in FHR was associated with a 22% higher risk of MASLD (HR, 1.22; 95% CI: 1.17-1.27, P < .001). Compared to the lowest quartile, the highest quartile showed a significantly elevated risk (HR: 2.10, 95% CI: 1.78-2.48; P for trend < 0.001). A positive dose-response relationship was also observed. ROC analysis showed that FHR had a moderate predictive ability (AUC, 0.701; 95% CI, 0.690 to 0.713), with an optimal cutoff value of 3.87. Elevated FHR was independently associated with an increased risk of MASLD in nonobese Chinese adults. Thus, FHR may serve as a simple and cost-effective biomarker for early risk stratification in this population.

articles.title: Causal relationship between educational attainment and complications of Type 2 diabetes: Mendelian randomization study.
articles.abstract: Educational attainment (EA) is a critical metric for evaluating individual socioeconomic status, as it significantly impacts mortality rates and the occurrence of various diseases. This study aims to investigate the causal relationship between education and complications associated with type 2 diabetes mellitus, while also examining potential mediating pathways. To assess the causal relationship between EA and specific complications of type 2 diabetes, this study employs univariable Mendelian randomization (UVMR). Throughout this analysis, single nucleotide polymorphisms are utilized as genetic tools, thereby minimizing confounding and bias arising from reverse causation. With each 4.2-year increase in EA, patients with type 2 diabetes exhibit a reduced risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus with neurological complications (DNC) (0.33; 0.20, 0.54), type 2 diabetes with ophthalmic complications (DOC) (0.57; 0.41, 0.80), type 2 diabetes with peripheral circulatory complications (DPCC) (0.60; 0.39, 0.93), and type 2 diabetes with renal complications (DRC) (0.47; 0.32, 0.69). Among the 27 candidate mediators, body mass index, waist circumference, and watching television showed relatively large mediation proportion point estimates for some outcomes. The findings of this study suggest that EA exerts a causally protective effect on DNC, DOC, DPCC, and DRC. The candidate mediating pathways warrant further investigation because their independent contributions have not been established.

articles.title: Association between hemoglobin glycation index and metabolic syndrome in Saudi adolescents: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is a cluster of cardiometabolic risk factors associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The Hemoglobin Glycation Index (HGI), which quantifies the difference between observed glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) and HbA1c predicted from fasting plasma glucose, has been proposed as a metabolic risk marker. However, evidence regarding its association with MetS remains inconsistent, particularly among adolescents. This study examined the associations between HGI and MetS, including sex-stratified patterns, among Saudi adolescents from Riyadh. This cross-sectional study included 2342 Saudi adolescents (893 boys and 1449 girls; mean age, 14.8 ± 1.7 years) recruited from secondary schools in Riyadh between September 2019 and March 2021. Anthropometric measurements, blood pressure, fasting plasma glucose, HbA1c, lipid profile, vitamin D, and selected biochemical markers were assessed. HGI was calculated as the difference between observed and predicted HbA1c, with predicted values derived from a linear regression model using fasting plasma glucose. MetS was defined using established pediatric criteria. Unadjusted binary logistic regression and correlation analyses were performed. MetS was present in 43.3% of participants and was more prevalent in boys than girls (47.1% vs 40.9%). Participants with MetS had higher body mass index, blood pressure, triglycerides, and fasting plasma glucose levels, lower high-density lipoprotein cholesterol and vitamin D levels (all P <.01). HGI was lower in participants with MetS than those without (-0.057 ± 0.60 vs -0.003 ± 0.52, P <.05), with the largest difference observed among girls. In unadjusted logistic regression analyses, higher HGI tertiles were associated with lower odds of MetS compared with the lowest tertile. Correlation analyses revealed different correlation patterns between boys and girls; however, most associations between HGI and clinical or biochemical variables were weak in magnitude. Higher HGI tertiles were inversely associated with MetS in this cross-sectional sample of Saudi adolescents, contrary to patterns commonly reported in adult populations. As these associations were unadjusted and the study was cross-sectional, they should not be interpreted as independent or causal. Longitudinal studies incorporating direct measures of insulin resistance, pubertal status, erythrocyte turnover, and inflammatory markers are needed to clarify the biological basis and directionality of the HGI-MetS association in adolescents.

articles.title: Anterior reconstruction using femoral ring allografts for thoracolumbar infectious spondylitis: Clinical and radiologic outcomes of a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Surgical treatment is required in infectious spondylitis when conservative management fails or vertebral destruction causes instability. Autologous bone graft is considered the gold standard but is limited by donor-site morbidity and availability. Femoral ring allografts are widely used in degenerative conditions, but their role in infectious spondylitis is unclear. This study evaluated the clinical, radiologic, and laboratory outcomes of anterior reconstruction using femoral ring allografts. In this single-center retrospective cohort study, reported in accordance with the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology statement, we reviewed 25 patients who underwent anterior corpectomy and reconstruction using femoral ring allografts followed by posterior instrumentation between December 2011 and September 2023. Clinical outcomes (VAS, Oswestry Disability Index, Frankel grade), laboratory parameters (erythrocyte sedimentation rate, C-reactive protein), and radiologic outcomes (Cobb angle, fusion) were compared preoperatively and at final follow-up. Paired comparisons used the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, with Hodges-Lehmann estimates, distribution-free 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and effect sizes (r). Infection control and complications were analyzed. The mean follow-up was 29.2 ± 23.9 months (range, 12.0-87.2 months). VAS improved from 7.3 ± 1.1 to 1.9 ± 1.0 (Hodges-Lehmann estimate -5.50; 95% CI, -6.00 to -5.00; r  = 0.87) and Oswestry Disability Index from 37.7 ± 5.9 to 10.7 ± 3.5 (-26.50; 95% CI, -29.50 to -23.50; r = 0.87; both P < .001). Neurological function improved significantly (r = 0.76, P < .001). Erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein decreased significantly (both P < .001). Sagittal alignment was corrected with partial loss over time but remained improved at final follow-up (5.55°; 95% CI, 3.40°-8.95°; r = 0.69; P < .001). Fusion was achieved in 92% and infection control in 96%. Complications occurred in 16%. In patients with large anterior column defects not amenable to tricortical iliac autograft, femoral ring allograft reconstruction achieved reliable infection control, a high fusion rate, and satisfactory clinical and radiologic outcomes over a mean follow-up of 29.2 months. Within this period, it appears a reasonable alternative to structural autograft when donor-site morbidity or graft availability is a concern. Longer-term comparative studies are needed to confirm the durability of graft incorporation and to define its role relative to contemporary titanium-based reconstruction.

articles.title: Development and validation of a machine learning model and nomogram for predicting lung metastasis in thymoma: A population-based study.
articles.abstract: The lung is the most frequent site of metastasis in patients with advanced thymoma. As a result, predicting the probability of lung metastasis and survival time has become a key focus in clinical practice. However, accurate prediction models are currently lacking. We collected complete data from 2004 to 2015 in the Surveillance, Epidemiology and End Results (SEER) database. Cox regression analysis was used to evaluate factors associated with the prognosis of thymoma patients. These independent prognostic factors were incorporated into the nomogram prognostic model. We validated the survival model by incorporating prognostic factors using receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration plots, C-index, and decision curve analysis curves. Synthetic minority over-sampling technique statistical methods were used to evaluate the machine learning model most suitable for building a predictive model of lung metastasis. Receiver operating characteristic curves, probability density plots, and confusion matrices were used to evaluate the performance of the prediction model. A total of 1776 thymoma patients were included in this study. Among them, age, sex, World Health Organization classification, Masaoka_Koga_Stage, surgery, chemotherapy, and lung metastasis were independent factors affecting metastasis. The machine learning model built by the gradient boosting machine algorithm performed best through internal data validation. Then, we used the gradient boosting machine algorithm to construct a web predictor of lung metastasis, and completed the construction and verification of the nomogram model. We developed an accessible online prediction tool (https://lung-metastasis---thymoma-ckfrve2aqrqr8tsdwbrqik.streamlit.app/) to evaluate the risk of lung metastasis. In addition, a predictive nomogram model was developed to predict the prognosis of patients with lung metastasis.

articles.title: Comparison of anticoagulation efficacy and safety of different heparin dosages in cardiogenic shock patients supported by intra-aortic balloon pump: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: The study aimed to evaluate whether a half-dose heparin flush strategy during intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) support improves safety compared with the standard-dose strategy in patients with cardiogenic shock (CS). In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 128 CS patients who received IABP support between January 2023 and December 2024 were included. Sixty-eight patients received a standard-dose heparin flush, and 60 received a half-dose flush. The primary endpoints were clinically relevant bleeding (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium 2, 3, or 5) and thrombocytopenia (platelet count < 100 × 109/L). Multivariable logistic regression was conducted, adjusting for dual antiplatelet therapy and renal dysfunction. The incidence of clinically significant bleeding events and thrombocytopenia was significantly lower in the half-dose group than in the standard-dose group (P < .05). Compared with the standard-dose group, the half-dose heparin flush strategy was significantly associated with a lower risk of clinically significant bleeding (odds ratio = 0.15; 95% confidence interval = 0.03-0.68). Among the secondary outcomes, the half-dose group had a significantly lower transfusion requirement than the standard-dose group (P < .001). No significant differences were observed between the 2 groups in activated partial thromboplastin time, activated clotting time, in-hospital mortality, or catheter-related occlusion events. In patients with CS receiving IABP support, the half-dose heparin flush strategy was associated with lower incidences of thrombocytopenia, clinical bleeding, and transfusion requirements. No device-related thrombotic events were observed in either group, suggesting that the half-dose heparin flush strategy may contribute to optimizing anticoagulation management during the peri-support period.

articles.title: Metabolic syndrome and liver fibrosis in nondiabetic MASLD: A cross-sectional double machine learning study.
articles.abstract: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is associated with hepatic fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), but whether this association is causal in nondiabetic MASLD has not been assessed with semiparametric causal methods. We analyzed 1306 nondiabetic adults with MASLD from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2017 to 2020; 959 (73.4%) had prediabetes. The contrast was the supra-threshold MetS phenotype (≥3/5 harmonized components) versus the subthreshold phenotype (0-2/5), estimated as a covariate-standardized stratum contrast. Three co-primary outcomes were prespecified: fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4) ≥ 1.3, age-residualized FIB-4, and age-independent FibroScan ≥ 7.9 kPa. We applied double machine learning, augmented inverse probability weighting, causal forests, and 4 meta-learners, with 20 robustness analyses prespecified and 9 added at peer review. Estimates diverged with the age dependence of the outcome. For FIB-4 the adjusted risk difference was 0.153 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.057-0.250; P = .002; E value = 3.75), or 0.095 (0.050-0.140) under a constant-effect specification; across 10 specifications estimates ranged from 0.078 to 0.163, attenuating to 0.091 (95% CI, -0.018 to 0.201; P = .10) after age residualization and to 0.001 (95% CI, -0.094 to 0.097; P = .98) for FibroScan, whose interval excludes the FIB-4 estimate at equal precision. Age stratification showed no effect below 40, with heterogeneity for FIB-4 (I2 = 72%) and age-residualized FIB-4 (I2 = 73%) but none for FibroScan (I2 = 0%), so the gradient is specific to FIB-4. Shapley decomposition ranked fasting glucose and central obesity highest, but every component's CI included zero, and no component pair showed additive-scale interaction after adjustment. Selection into the MASLD sample was exposure-dependent (40.7% vs 30.7%; P < .001); weighting gave 0.126 (0.003-0.250). The supra-threshold MetS phenotype was associated with a higher prevalence of FIB-4-defined fibrosis risk but not with age-independent elastography. The divergence tracks the outcome measure rather than sample composition: perturbations addressing what FIB-4 measures converge on 0.08 to 0.10, while those addressing sample composition leave it near 0.13 to 0.15. These findings generate hypotheses for confirmatory longitudinal testing rather than definitive causal evidence. They apply to the predominantly prediabetic MASLD population studied here and cannot be extrapolated to metabolically healthy or lean MASLD.

articles.title: Current epidemiological profile and characteristics of traumatic and nontraumatic spinal cord injury in Jinan, China: A two-center retrospective observational study.
articles.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is a highly disabling neurological condition associated with long-term functional impairment and substantial healthcare needs. In Jinan, hospital-based evidence directly comparing traumatic SCI (TSCI) and nontraumatic SCI (NTSCI) within the same regional tertiary-care system remains limited. This study aimed to describe and compare their epidemiological and clinical profiles to inform targeted prevention and hospital-based care planning. We conducted a 2-center, hospital-based retrospective observational study of patients with SCI admitted between 2015 and 2024. Categorical variables were summarized as n (%) and compared between TSCI and NTSCI using Pearson chi-square tests or Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact tests, as appropriate. Because length of stay was markedly right-skewed, it was summarized as median (interquartile range [IQR]) and compared using the Mann-Whitney U test. All comparisons were two-sided and unadjusted. A total of 1334 patients with SCI were included (1134 TSCI and 200 NTSCI). TSCI showed a greater male predominance than NTSCI (78.66% vs 56.50%, P < .001), and age-group distributions also differed (P < .001). Falls (46.03%) and traffic accidents (40.65%) were the leading TSCI mechanisms; electric bicycle-related crashes accounted for the largest share of traffic-related TSCI (191/461, 41.43%). The leading NTSCI etiologies were neoplasm (33.00%), demyelinating disease (20.00%), infectious disease (17.00%), vascular disease (15.50%), and degenerative disease (14.50%). American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale distributions differed between groups (P < .001). Median length of stay was 12 days (IQR = 8-21) for TSCI and 46 days (IQR = 33.75-61) for NTSCI (P < .001). A primary in-hospital complication was recorded in 78.31% of TSCI and 80.00% of NTSCI patients (P = .591); however, the distribution of primary complication categories differed overall (P = .040). Urinary tract infection was more frequent in TSCI (24.78% vs 16.00%, P = .007), whereas pulmonary infection was more frequent in NTSCI (12.26% vs 18.00%, P = .027). Within these 2 tertiary hospitals in Jinan, TSCI and NTSCI showed different demographic, neurological, treatment, hospitalization, and primary complication patterns. TSCI was characterized by prominent fall- and traffic-related injury mechanisms, whereas NTSCI showed heterogeneous etiologies and substantially longer hospitalization. These hospital-based findings support targeted prevention priorities and differentiated clinical care pathways but should not be interpreted as population-level incidence estimates or as independent effects of traumatic versus nontraumatic etiology.

articles.title: The relationship between sirtuin1 gene polymorphism and coronary heart disease: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study systematically assesses the relationship between sirtuin (SIRT)1 gene polymorphisms rs4746720T > C, rs3818292G > A, rs7895833 A > G, and rs7069102C > G with the risk of coronary heart disease (CHD).

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane databases were searched for literature examining the connection between SIRT1 gene polymorphism and CHD. The search time limit was from the establishment of the database to June 15, 2024. Stata 15.0 software was used for data analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 9 articles were included (1839 cases in the case group and 1937 cases in the control group). Meta-analysis showed that the rs4746720 dominant model (TC + TT > CC) [odds ratio = 1.321, 95% confidence interval (1.032-1.692), P = .027] was nominally associated with an increased risk of CHD, although this association did not remain significant after correction for multiple testing (Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted q = 0.176), whereas the rs7069102 dominant model (CC + CG > GG) [odds ratio = 0.278, 95% confidence interval (0.126-0.612), P = .001] was associated with a decreased risk of CHD and remained significant after correction (adjusted q = 0.013). However, the rs7069102C > G, rs7069102CC > GG, rs7069102 CG > GG, rs7069102CC > CG + GG, rs4746720T > C, rs4746720TC > TT, rs7895833 and rs3818292 gene polymorphisms were not associated with the risk of CHD.

CONCLUSION: The rs7069102 CC + CG genotype of SIRT1 may be associated with a reduced risk of CHD, whereas the association between the rs4746720 TC + TT genotype and CHD risk was only nominally significant and did not withstand correction for multiple comparisons. However, limited by the quantity and quality of the included studies, the above conclusions need to be verified by more high-quality studies.

articles.title: Association between pre-stroke anemia and risk of acute kidney injury following ischemic stroke: A multi-institutional retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Although anemia is an established risk factor for acute kidney injury (AKI), its specific impact on post-stroke AKI remains inadequately explored. This study aimed to investigate the association between pre-stroke anemia and the risk of developing AKI after acute ischemic stroke. This retrospective study, using the TriNetX research network database, identified adult patients who experienced their 1st recorded ischemic stroke between January 2010 and December 2023. Patients were categorized based on hemoglobin levels within 3 months pre-stroke: anemia (hemoglobin ≥8.0 and <12.0 g/dL) versus control (hemoglobin ≥12.0 g/dL). After 1:1 propensity score matching, we analyzed the outcomes at 1-year follow-up. The primary endpoint was the development of AKI during the follow-up period. Secondary endpoints comprised all-cause mortality, pneumonia, and intensive care unit admission. After propensity score matching, 61,896 patients were included in each cohort. Patients with pre-stroke anemia had a significantly higher 1-year risk of AKI (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.89, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.83-1.96), mortality (HR: 1.86, 95% CI: 1.80-1.93), pneumonia (HR: 1.76, 95% CI: 1.69-1.84), and intensive care unit admission (HR: 1.60, 95% CI: 1.55-1.65) compared to controls (all P < .001). A graded association was observed between increasing anemia severity and adverse outcomes. The findings remained robust across sensitivity and subgroup analyses. Pre-stroke anemia is associated with an increased risk of post-stroke AKI and other adverse outcomes. However, given the observational nature of this study, future prospective studies are warranted to confirm these findings and elucidate the underlying mechanisms.

articles.title: Association of the triglyceride glucose-waist circumference index with hypertension among US adults: A cross-sectional study from NHANES.
articles.abstract: The triglyceride glucose-weight-adjusted waist index (TyG-WWI), integrating glycolipid metabolism and central obesity, may offer a novel approach to identifying metabolic dysregulation linked to hypertension, yet its association with hypertension among general adults remains inadequately characterized. In this cross-sectional analysis of 2716 adults (aged ≥ 20 years) from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2015 to 2018, hypertension was defined by self-reported physician diagnosis. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses, and exploratory mediation analyses were applied, accounting for the complex survey design with fasting subsample weights. Of 2716 participants, 890 (32.8%) had hypertension. After full adjustment, each unit increase in TyG-WWI was associated with a 2% increase in the odds of hypertension (OR = 1.02, 95% confidence interval: 1.01-1.03, P < .001). A nonlinear dose-response relationship was observed (P for nonlinearity < .05), with risk accelerating at higher TyG-WWI levels; participants in the highest quartile had 72% higher odds than those in the lowest quartile (OR = 1.72, 95% confidence interval: 1.21-2.46; P for trend < .001). Subgroup analyses showed stronger associations in females and in normal-weight individuals. Exploratory mediation analyses suggested that body mass index and uric acid may account for 30.49% and 7.95% of the association, respectively; these estimates are descriptive and should not be interpreted as evidence of biological mediation. Higher TyG-WWI was independently associated with a higher prevalence of self-reported hypertension among United States adults across all body mass index categories. These findings support TyG-WWI as a promising composite marker for hypertension risk stratification; the exploratory mediation estimates warrant confirmation in prospective studies.

articles.title: Risk factors and morbidity characteristics of surgical site infection following ankle fracture ORIF: A comprehensive analysis.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to describe the incidence and microbiological characteristics of surgical site infection (SSI) after open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) of ankle fractures and identify clinical factors associated with SSI. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 248 patients who underwent ankle fracture ORIF between January and December 2023. SSI occurring within 30 postoperative days was identified from available inpatient and postoperative medical records. Demographic, injury-related, laboratory, and perioperative variables were compared between patients with and without SSI. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted associations with SSI. SSI occurred in 32 of 248 patients (12.9%), including 25 superficial and 7 deep infections. Cultured organisms included Escherichia coli (n = 10), Staphylococcus aureus (n = 7), Klebsiella pneumoniae (n = 6), Enterobacter cloacae (n = 5), and Staphylococcus epidermidis (n = 4). In multivariable analysis, open fracture, wound class II-III, and neutrophil percentage > 75% were associated with SSI. Age and body mass index (BMI) also showed positive associations, although the precise unit-specific effect sizes could not be reliably reconstructed from the archived statistical analysis; these comparatively large per-unit estimates should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of SSI events and potential residual confounding. SSI occurred in 12.9% of this single-center ankle fracture cohort. Older age and higher BMI showed associations with SSI, together with open fracture, less-clean operative wounds, and neutrophilia. The magnitude of the age- and BMI-related effects should be interpreted cautiously because their original regression scaling could not be independently reconstructed.

articles.title: Intestinal tuberculosis with multiple intestinal perforations in a 5-month-old infant: The role of metagenomic next-generation sequencing: a case report and literature review.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Intestinal tuberculosis (ITB) is a chronic infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex and is relatively rare in infants. However, severe complications such as intestinal perforation can pose significant clinical challenges. We report the clinical features, diagnosis, and therapeutic management of intestinal perforation caused by ITB in an infant.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A 5-month-old male infant presented with fever and abdominal distension, which progressed to intestinal obstruction and multiple perforations involving the distal ileum and appendiceal region. The clinical presentation was atypical.

DIAGNOSES: The diagnosis was established through surgical exploration and metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS).Conventional investigations, including the tuberculin skin test using purified protein derivative and interferon-gamma release assay, were negative. mNGS of peritoneal drainage fluid detected mycobacterium tuberculosis complex with 2868,520 sequence reads, and Ziehl-Neelsen staining of mesenteric nodule specimens was positive for acid-fast bacilli.

INTERVENTIONS: The infant underwent surgical intervention for the intestinal perforations, followed by the standard four-drug anti-TB regimen (rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol) together with linezolid, imipenem, and amikacin.

OUTCOMES: The infant showed substantial clinical improvement, with weight gain and encouraging developmental progress; although the ileostomy remains in situ, closure is planned after full nutritional recovery. To our knowledge, this is among the youngest reported cases of postnatally acquired primary ITB presenting with multiple intestinal perforations in an infant without a known history of TB exposure.

LESSONS: In infants with severe unexplained intra-abdominal infection and inconclusive conventional TB investigations, mNGS may facilitate the early diagnosis of ITB. Timely surgical intervention combined with anti-TB therapy may improve outcomes in these critically ill patients.

articles.title: Global Proposal for the TNM Staging System for Poorly Differentiated Thyroid Cancer.
authors: International Aggressive Thyroid Cancer Collaborative Group
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Poorly differentiated thyroid cancer (PDTC) lacks a dedicated staging system, requiring use of the eighth version of the American Joint Committee on Cancer and Union for International Cancer Control TNM staging system (TNM-8) for differentiated thyroid cancer despite its distinct biology.

OBJECTIVE: To develop a PDTC-specific staging system.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study analyzed data from the International Aggressive Thyroid Cancer Collaborative Group (IATCCG), including surgically treated patients at 91 centers in 14 countries from January 1984 to January 2026. External validation was performed using patients from the US Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. Data were analyzed from December 2025 to June 2026.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was overall survival. With M1 disease predefined as stage IVB, the schema for stages I-IVA in patients with M0 disease were redefined. All possible TN combinations were fitted into multivariable Cox models, with the lowest Akaike information criterion defining the proposed system.
