Prognostic discrimination was assessed using adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) and C statistics.

RESULTS: Among 1010 patients in the IATCCG cohort, 610 (60.4%) were female, and the median (IQR) age at diagnosis was 58 (46-68) years; median (IQR) follow-up was 41 (15-85) months. Among 170 patients in the SEER cohort, 85 (50.0%) were female, and the median (IQR) age at diagnosis was 61 (49-72) years; median (IQR) follow-up was 92 (42-154) months. In the IATCCG cohort, level VII lymph node metastasis (LNM) was associated with lower 5-year overall survival (45.2%; 95% CI, 33.4-61.2) than level VI (73.2%; 95% CI, 64.4-83.3) or lateral neck LNM (56.7%; 95% CI, 49.4-65.0). Level VII LNM was therefore reclassified from N1a to N1c. The lowest Akaike information criterion configuration among 16 738 candidates defined stages I to IVA as follows: I, T1N0/NX/N1a or T2N0/NX; II, T1N1b/N1c, T2N1a/N1b, or T3N0/NX/N1a; III, T2N1c, T3N1b, or T4aN0/NX/N1a; IVA, T3N1c, T4aN1b/N1c, or T4b any N; and IVB, M1 disease. Compared with TNM-8, stage I disease decreased from 44.4% (448 of 1010) to 24.6% (248 of 1010) and stage IV disease increased from 18.5% (187 of 1010) to 32.4% (327 of 1010) with the proposed system. The proposed staging had a higher C statistic than TNM-8 (0.74 [95% CI, 0.71-0.76] vs 0.71 [95% CI, 0.68-0.74]; difference, 0.03; 95% CI, 0.01-0.04). Corresponding SEER C statistic values were 0.76 (95% CI, 0.71-0.81) vs 0.74 (95% CI, 0.68-0.79), respectively (difference, 0.02; 95% CI, -0.01 to 0.06).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This cohort study found that this PDTC-specific staging system provides improved prognostic stratification reflecting its different biology. These data provide a strong rationale for the potential inclusion of a stand-alone American Joint Committee on Cancer staging system for PDTC.

articles.title: A Teleglaucoma Screening System for Individuals at Risk of Open-Angle Glaucoma: Long-Term Clinical Outcomes and Comparative Cost Analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the clinical effectiveness and economic impact of a teleglaucoma screening program for individuals at increased risk of developing open-angle glaucoma (OAG).

DESIGN: Prospective cohort study with retrospective evaluation of long-term clinical outcomes and comparative cost analysis.

PARTICIPANTS: Consecutive individuals with risk factors for OAG enrolled in a teleglaucoma screening program between 2020 and 2022.

METHODS: A targeted teleglaucoma screening program was implemented within the Donostialdea Integrated Healthcare Organization (Gipuzkoa, Spain). Consecutive individuals with risk factors for OAG were included. The teleglaucoma assessment included best-corrected visual acuity, non-contact tonometry, pachymetry, and peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer optical coherence tomography (pRNFL-OCT), performed by an optometrist and reviewed asynchronously by glaucoma specialists. Findings consistent with glaucoma or suspicious for glaucoma were considered positive screening results, whereas ocular hypertension (OHT) or the absence of abnormalities were considered negative screening results. Clinical effectiveness was evaluated through analysis of glaucoma-related diagnoses recorded using ICD-10 codes during a five-year follow-up period. A comparative cost analysis was conducted from a societal perspective. Patient satisfaction was assessed using the Client Satisfaction Questionnaire (CSQ-8).

MAIN OUTCOMES MEASURES: Agreement between teleglaucoma classifications and glaucoma-related ICD-10 diagnoses recorded during follow-up, diagnostic performance indicators, patient satisfaction, and costs.

RESULTS: A total of 1,112 patients were included (mean age 60.2 years), of whom 63.1% were women. Positive screening results were identified in 8.2% of participants. Overall agreement between the teleglaucoma assessment and follow-up ICD-10 diagnoses was 92.6%, with a mean follow-up of 3.7 ± 0.8 years. Sensitivity was 64.5%, specificity 93.4%, and negative predictive value 98.9%. Patient satisfaction was high, with a mean score of 8.5/10. The economic analysis demonstrated a 50% reduction in total costs compared with conventional care, with a cost per patient of €40.7 versus €81.2.

CONCLUSIONS: The teleglaucoma system demonstrated a high ability to rule out disease among individuals at risk of glaucoma, reduced costs and achieved high patient satisfaction. However, moderate sensitivity and the use of coded clinical records as the reference standard should be considered.

articles.title: Towards Contact-Free Cardiac Magnetic Resonance: Feasibility of Remote Photoplethysmography for Cardiac Triggering and Gating.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) sequences necessitate synchronisation with the cardiac cycle. This is routinely obtained through electrocardiographic (ECG) detection of the R-wave with subsequent triggering or gating of the acquisition, depending on the type of sequence. An accepted alternative is the use of transmissive photoplethysmography using a fingerclip (fPPG) to detect the peripheral pulse wave.

OBJECTIVES: To assess the feasibility of contact-free remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) for CMR triggering/gating.

METHODS: In this prospective study (www.drks.de, DRKS00036686), CMR sequences were triggered/gated by ECG, fPPG and rPPG. The primary endpoint was trigger accuracy, measured by true positive rate (TPR), positive predictive value (PPV), beat detection error rate (BDER) and trigger-latency variability (TLV) in the rPPG and fPPG tracings compared to the ECG tracing. Secondary endpoints were technical success, image quality and quantitative CMR measurements of the acquired CMR sequences. Subsequently, the rPPG algorithm was adjusted to improve pulse wave detection in patients with skin type Fitzpatrick 5-6.

RESULTS: 64 subjects were included. rPPG initially provided comparable measures of trigger accuracy to fPPG, with worse performance in subjects with skin type Fitzpatrick 5-6. Adjusting the rPPG algorithm significantly improved trigger accuracy irrespective of skin type: BDER (%) for fPPG 8.5 (0.9-23.0), for rPPG 7.2 (0.3-49.1) and for the adjusted rPPG 1.3 (0.2-11.2). Image quality with both fPPG and rPPG were comparable to ECG. The differences observed in quantitative CMR measurements between fPPG, rPPG and ECG were in the order of inter-observer-variability.

CONCLUSIONS: Contact-free rPPG is a viable alternative to standard CMR triggering/gating using ECG or fPPG. Adjustment of our algorithm led to excellent trigger accuracy irrespective of skin type.

articles.title: Ectopic Parathyroid Adenoma Mimicking a Vagal Paraganglioma on Somatostatin Receptor PET.
Possible post-infectious sequelae of tick-borne Rickettsia and Ehrlichia infections.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the presence of symptoms and immunological profiles after infection with tick-borne spotted fever rickettsiosis (SFR) or ehrlichiosis.

METHODS: Adults evaluated for acute tick-borne disease completed symptom surveys through 90 days. Cases were classified using standard epidemiological definitions. Participants with alpha-gal sensitization were excluded from the primary analysis. Acute and convalescent cytokine profiles were compared between participants with and without symptoms present at the 90-day timepoint.

RESULTS: Among 71 participants, 37 (52.1%) and 33 (46.5%) met criteria for confirmed or probable ehrlichiosis and SFR, respectively; seven met criteria for both. After excluding 12 participants with alpha-gal sensitization, 15 (50.0%) with ehrlichiosis and 13 (50.0%) with SFR reported at least one moderate or severe symptom at 90 days, compared with one of eight (12.5%) participants classified as not a case. Fatigue and musculoskeletal pain were most common. Participants with symptoms present at 90-days showed higher pro-inflammatory and lower anti-inflammatory cytokine levels, but differences were not statistically significant.

CONCLUSIONS: Post-infectious syndromes after tick-borne disease may not be limited to Lyme disease. These preliminary findings support patient-reported experiences and warrant larger studies to define the prevalence, predictors, pathogenesis, and clinical course of possible persistent symptoms.

articles.title: A 3D Deep Learning Model for Assessing Concomitant Pulmonary Embolism Risk by Integrating Clinical and Computed Tomography Venography Features in Patients with Lower Extremity Deep Venous Thrombosis.
articles.journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to develop and validate a multimodal deep learning (DL) model integrating clinical and computed tomography venography (CTV) features for predicting concomitant acute pulmonary embolism (PE) risk in patients with lower extremity deep venous thrombosis (LEDVT).

METHODS: This multicentre retrospective study enrolled patients with LEDVT undergoing both computed tomography pulmonary angiography and lower extremity CTV. Centre 1 data were used for model training and internal validation, while data from centres 2 and 3 were used for external testing. Clinical models (logistic regression [LR], random forest [RF], support vector machine [SVM], and XGBoost), 3D DL models (VGG-11, VGG-16, ResNet-18, Res2Net-50, and DenseNet-121), and combined models (LR, RF, SVM, and XGBoost) integrating clinical, imaging, and DL features were developed to select the best performer, which was further benchmarked against validated clinical risk scores (Wells score and modified Geneva score).

RESULTS: A total of 348 patients from centre 1 were randomly split into training and internal validation sets, and 127 patients from two independent institutions formed the external testing cohort. The optimal LR clinical, 3D VGG-16 DL, and SVM combined models achieved external testing area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.776, 0.789, and 0.836, respectively. DeLong tests confirmed that the SVM combined model significantly outperformed the LR clinical model and validated clinical scores (all p < .050) on the external testing set, while yielding a comparable AUC to the 3D VGG-16 DL model. Decision curve analysis indicated higher net benefit for the SVM combined model, alongside superior calibration, and positive net reclassification improvement and integrated discrimination improvement values.

CONCLUSION: The SVM combined model integrating clinical, imaging, and DL features demonstrated robust performance, offering a promising tool for predicting concomitant acute PE in patients with LEDVT.

articles.title: Esophageal Manometry is Needed for Accuracy in Selected Patients with Postcapillary Pulmonary Hypertension.
articles.abstract: Both mean pulmonary artery (mPAP) and pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP) are essential determinations in the hemodynamic evaluation of patients undergoing a right heart catheterization. These pressure determinations are traditionally obtained at end-expiration and reflect the intramural pressure relative to the atmospheric pressure, but not the pressure distending the vessel wall which is the transmural pressure. In conditions in which the intrathoracic pressure is elevated, the intravascular pressure may overestimate the transmural pressure. A relatively simple way to estimate the transmural pressure is to measure the esophageal pressure (Pes). We previously shown that in patient with obesity, this correction decreased the number of patients diagnosed with postcapillary PH. Physicians need to consider the measurement of Pes in patients with increased mPAP and PAWP in the context of conditions known to be associated with high intrathoracic pressure and particularly when a potential increase in Pes may alter the management. As with other hemodynamic determinations, it is essential to understand the technique, limitations and potential errors in Pes measurement. Further research is needed to determine whether the measurement of Pes improves clinical decision-making or outcomes.

articles.title: Association of pre-existing sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor therapy with outcomes in cardiogenic shock: a multicentre cohort study.
Sudden Death in Patients with Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Pooled Analysis of Five Randomized Trials.
Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction Reductions During Long-Term Aficamten Treatment in Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Findings From FOREST-HCM.
Anticipatory Cardiac Deceleration Is Related to Cautious Decision-Making after Threat Image Exposure.
articles.abstract: Cautious decision-making can be an adaptive tendency in stressful environments and in certain individuals. We hypothesized that cautious decision-making is supported by anticipatory cardiac deceleration (ACD)- a brief cardiac slowing tied to preparation and action readiness. To test this hypothesis, we examined whether individuals with stronger ACD make more economically cautious choices after exposure to threat-depicting images. Participants (N = 97; 65% women, Mean age = 22.4 years) completed a threat priming decision-making task while electrocardiography was collected. To manipulate emotional contexts, every economic lottery choice was preceded by an affective image depicting a neutral, injury threat, or infection threat scene, and choice trials were presented in three separate blocks - one for each image type. Cardiac deceleration was assessed during 10-s countdown periods before each block. Results indicate that individuals with greater ACD before the infection threat block made more cautious choices after exposure to the infection threat images. This association was strongest when the infection block occurred last in the task sequence, i.e., when that image condition was more predictable. No significant relationships emerged for the other image conditions suggesting that anticipatory deceleration might only relate to behavioral caution in certain threat conditions. Results are consistent with the hypothesis that ACD is an autonomic correlate of preparation that is relevant to human performance and fear/anxiety theories.

articles.title: Ambient fine particulate matter and asthma emergency visits in Lima, Peru: Does Residential Proximity to Major Roads Matter?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Living near major roads may increase the short-term effects of ambient PM2.5 exposure on asthma exacerbations. We evaluated whether residential proximity to major roads modifies the association between ambient PM2.5 and asthma emergency department (ED) visits in Lima, Peru.

METHODS: We analyzed asthma ED visits from 10 public hospitals in Lima (2017-2023) using a time-stratified case-crossover design. We used a high-resolution (1×1 km) multi-source model to assign daily mean PM2.5, temperature, and relative humidity to geocoded residences. We classified residential proximity to major roadways (>75th percentile of traffic volume) by distance thresholds from 100 to 500 m. Using conditional logistic regression with distributed lag non-linear models, we estimated lag-specific and cumulative associations and tested for effect modification.

RESULTS: We included 75,602 asthma ED visits (mean age 16.2 years; 50.7% male) matched to 258,120 control-days. PM2.5 was associated with higher odds of ED visits across lags 0-15 days, with the strongest lag-specific association at lag 0. The exposure-response relationship was steeper at lower PM2.5 concentrations. At lag 0, an increase in PM2.5 from 5 to 15 μg/m3 was associated with 9% higher odds of an ED visit (OR=1.09, 95% CI 1.01-1.16). Cumulative associations over lags 0-15 days were higher among residents living within 400 m of a major roadway (OR=4.02, 95% CI 1.97-8.19) than among those living at ≥400 m (OR=1.66, 95% CI 0.81-3.38; interaction p-value=0.04).

CONCLUSIONS: Short-term increases in ambient PM2.5 were associated with higher odds of asthma ED visits, with a steeper exposure-response relationship at lower concentrations and effects accumulating over the preceding 15 days. Associations were consistently stronger among residents living within pre-specified proximity thresholds to major roadways, supporting a pattern compatible with effect modification.

articles.title: Polymer-specific stimulation of sulfide and methane production by microplastics in sewer biofilm.
articles.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) in wastewater elicit unintended impacts on bio-processes. However, little information is available regarding the response of sewer biofilm to MPs. This work clarifies how three structurally distinct MPs (i.e., polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), and polyamide 6 (PA6)) at 500 μg/L within the reported wastewater range influence sulfide and methane production in sewer biofilm during long-term exposure and after cessation of external MP addition. Results showed all MPs increased the sulfidogenic activity relative to the control, with PVC exhibiting the greatest increase (33.3 ± 1.8%), followed by PA6 (23.7 ± 6.2%) and PET (16.0 ± 2.4%). PET uniquely increased methane production (21.3 ± 3.9%, p < 0.01), while PVC and PA6 showed no significant effect. Critically, these enhanced activities persisted after terminating external MP addition, indicating that the functional effects of long-term MP exposure can extend into the post-dosing phase. Genetically determined EPS restructuring enabled sewer biofilm defense against MPs, with enhanced secretion and hydrophobic component binding forming protective barriers against both MPs and associated chemical stress. The pronounced sulfidogenic response under PVC exposure coincided with increased humic-substance content and electron transport system activity, suggesting that alterations in the extracellular redox environment contributed to sulfate reduction. PET-specific methanogenesis was closely associated with elevated F420 activity and greater acetate-associated metabolic potential. Additionally, microbial community restructuring revealed a substrate-focused adaptation characterized by increased representation of hydrolytic/acidogenic populations and enhanced upstream substrate-processing potential. Collectively, these results indicate that MPs alter sewer sulfur and carbon transformations through polymer-dependent changes across extracellular, microbial, and metabolic levels. This study underscores the pervasive presence of MPs in wastewater as a concealed threat that aggravates corrosion and greenhouse gas emission in sewer systems.

articles.title: The Gut-Liver-Brain-Lung Axis in Alcohol Use Disorder: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Implications.
articles.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a multi-organ disease associated with an increased risk of severe pneumonia and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). While alcohol-related lung disease has often been attributed to ethanol-mediated injury to the alveolar epithelium, new evidence suggests a more broad and integrated model in which pulmonary vulnerability arises as a consequence of dysregulation in the gut-liver-brain axis. This review proposes a framework to explain how chronic alcohol consumption induces dysregulation in the gut-liver-brain axis and subsequently primes the lung for failure when a secondary hit, such as sepsis or infection, occur. Drawing on human observations and mechanistic studies in experimental preclinical models, we outline four candidate pathways that may link alcohol-related gut, hepatic, and neuroimmune changes to pulmonary vulnerability: 1) alcohol induces gut barrier disruption and dysbiosis, leading to the escape of lipopolysaccharides (LPS) into circulation; 2) the liver transitions to an amplifier of inflammation, releasing inflammatory signals into systemic circulation; 3) simultaneously, neuroimmune circuits such as the vagal cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway and the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis are disrupted by chronic alcohol exposure, resulting in delays in resolving inflammatory responses; and 4) the lungs receive these inputs on a background of glutathione depletion and innate immune dysfunction, resulting in an environment that may appear normal at baseline but is primed to fail. Recognizing alcohol-related lung disease as a potential consequence of altered gut-liver-brain signaling in the context of chronic alcohol use could provide a foundation for developing targeted therapeutic strategies for ARDS in individuals with AUD.

articles.title: Early platelet count trajectories and short- and long-term mortality in patients with sepsis: a group-based trajectory modeling study based on the MIMIC-IV database.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Platelet abnormalities are common in sepsis; most studies evaluate single measurements. We characterized early platelet count trajectories during the first 48 h after intensive care unit (ICU) admission and evaluated associations with short- and long-term mortality.

METHODS: Adult Sepsis-3 patients were identified from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database. Group-based trajectory modeling was applied to platelet counts at 12-48 h after ICU admission. Associations with mortality were examined using Kaplan-Meier, multivariable Cox and logistic models, with propensity-matched, multiple-imputation and reclassification analyses and the 48-h landmark analysis as primary; sepsis-induced coagulopathy was scored using International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis (ISTH) criteria.

RESULTS: Among 5,046 ICU stays (4,775 patients), four trajectories were identified: persistently low (n = 1,153; 22.8%), moderate with mild decline (n = 1,847; 36.6%), high with moderate decline (n = 1,516; 30.0%) and very high with marked decline (n = 530; 10.5%). In the primary landmark analysis (n=4,930), adjusted 28-day mortality hazard ratios versus the moderate-with-mild-decline group were 1.66 (95% CI 1.40-1.97), 1.33 (1.12-1.57) and 1.34 (1.07-1.69), consistent at 90 days, 1 year and in whole-cohort and matched analyses. Sepsis-induced coagulopathy affected 82.6% of persistently low patients; trajectory and coagulopathy remained jointly associated with mortality. Trajectory membership improved reclassification over clinical variables (continuous NRI 0.193, 95% CI 0.160-0.281).

CONCLUSIONS: Early platelet trajectories identify four sepsis patient groups with distinct mortality risk. The persistently low association was most robust; the high-but-declining association was attenuated in five-group analyses. Trajectories add information beyond single measurements.

articles.title: Lactate in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: an evidence synthesis and a hypothesis-generating framework for dynamic assessment.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome is staged with measures that capture organ-specific abnormality rather than integrated metabolic reserve under stress. Lactate is a circulating fuel and signal exchanged among every organ the syndrome names. We synthesise the human evidence on lactate handling across adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, kidney, liver and myocardium, and on what resting and dynamic lactate measurement has shown. That evidence contains two negative findings: in ARIC, the association of resting lactate with incident diabetes was lost after adjustment for fasting glucose and insulin, and the only direct comparison with cardiorespiratory fitness in metabolic syndrome found no independent lactate signal. Against this evidence we propose lactate resilience - blood-lactate excursion and recovery relative to standardised external work - as a hypothesis-generating framework only; it is not a biomarker, score, diagnosis or treatment target and does not alter CKM management. The contribution of this framework is not a demonstration of clinical value but a falsifiable specification: prespecified abandonment criteria (redundancy with peak oxygen uptake, ventilatory threshold and measured physical activity) and negative controls (tracking of renal function alone; attenuation after adjustment for glycaemia and fitness) against which the construct can be tested and, if necessary, discarded.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of cavo-tricuspid isthmus ablation using the linear-shaped pulsed field ablation catheter: LINEAR study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cavotricuspid isthmus(CTI) using pulsed field ablation(PFA) is still challenging.

METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 90 consecutive patients with atrial fibrillation(AF) and atrial flutter(AFL), who received CTI ablation using a linear-shaped PulseSelect PFA Loop catheter. Coronary angiography of the right coronary artery was performed before and just after PFA application. During the CTI ablation following PVI, the initial 45 patients did not receive prophylactic nitroglycerin administration (control group), and the latter 45 patients received systemic nitroglycerin administration of 1.5 mg before the applications (NTG group).

RESULTS: All patients achieved an acute line of block using only the PFA catheter, with 91.1% requiring two or fewer applications. Operators performed additional "bonus" applications, resulting in an average of 4.4 ± 1.4 applications per patient. After a mean waiting period of 24.7 min, high-density mapping revealed a re-conduction gap in 20 patients (22.2%). Of these 20 patients with reconduction, four had an epicardial bridge. Coronary artery spasm was observed in 51.1% of the control group. In contrast, prophylactic nitroglycerin administration significantly reduced the incidence of coronary spasm to 15.6% in the NTG group. No severe spasms were observed in the NTG group. Among nine patients who underwent a repeat ablation procedure due to clinical AF recurrence, CTI reconduction was found in five (55.6%).

CONCLUSION: Linear-shaped PulseSelect CTI ablation readily achieves acute block, but early reconduction limits long-term durability despite consolidation applications. Without prophylactic NTG, there is a notable risk of coronary spasm, necessitating its routine use. Additionally, systematic postprocedural follow-up is needed to assess delayed coronary safety.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Ulinastatin in the Treatment of Patients with Sepsis: The ADJUST Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Urinary trypsin inhibitor (ulinastatin, UTI) has shown potential survival benefits in sepsis; however, conclusive clinical evidence is lacking.

RESEARCH QUESTION: In patients with sepsis, does adjunctive ulinastatin, compared with placebo, reduce 28-day all-cause mortality?

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: In this multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, adult ICU patients with sepsis meeting Sepsis-3 criteria within 48 hours of admission were randomized (1:1) to receive intravenous UTI (400,000 IU every 8 hours) or placebo, for up to 10 days in addition to standard care. Randomization was stratified by site and septic shock. The primary endpoint was 28-day all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints included ICU, hospital, and 90-day mortality, and ICU/hospital length of stay.

RESULTS: Of 347 patients randomized, 340 (169 UTI, 171 placebo) received intervention and were included in the safety analysis; after 5 post-intervention withdrawals, 335 (165 UTI, 170 placebo) were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. At 28 days, death had occurred in 39 of 165 patients (23.6%) in the UTI group and in 39 of 170 patients (22.9%) in the placebo group (absolute difference, 0.7% [95% CI -8.4% to 9.7%]; P = .98; hazard ratio 1.03, 95% CI 0.66 to 1.61, P = .90). Secondary outcomes were similar in the two groups. Adverse events occurred in 56.8% (96/169) of UTI and 42.7% (73/171) of placebo patients (absolute difference 14.1%, 95% CI 3.6%-24.6%; P = 0.009).

INTERPRETATION: In patients with sepsis, adjunctive UTI did not reduce mortality compared with placebo. Routine use of UTI for sepsis is not supported by these findings.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov; https://clinicaltrials.gov; NCT02647554.

articles.title: Hippocampal CA2 modulates trace fear conditioning through circuit-specific tuning of CA1 activity.
articles.abstract: Forming associations between temporally separated events depends on pathways linking the CA1, the subiculum (SUB), and the entorhinal cortex. The degree to which this process requires the CA2, which shares extensive connectivity with these regions, remains unknown. Using trace fear conditioning (TFC), in which mice learn to associate a tone and shock separated by a temporal gap, we found that chronic blockade of dorsal CA2 (dCA2) output reduced cue-associated freezing without comparable effects following delay fear conditioning or during contextual fear recall. In contrast, acute inhibition of dCA2→dCA1 projections during either conditioning or recall increased cue-test freezing, whereas inhibition of dCA2→dSUB projections produced no detectable behavioral effect. These manipulations were associated with distinct patterns of hippocampal cFos expression. Fiber photometry showed that dCA2→dCA1 calcium activity exhibited tone-onset modulation during conditioning and late-trace modulation near the time at which shock had occurred during conditioning. Moreover, acute CA2 inhibition during conditioning was associated with persistent tone-onset CA1 modulation during subsequent drug-free recall. Together, these findings identify dCA2 as a contributor to TFC and link dCA2→dCA1 signaling to fear expression and the temporal organization of CA1 activity across learning and recall.

articles.title: Advances in Next-Generation Sequencing and Single-Cell Transcriptomics for Profiling NK Cell Heterogeneity and Functional Diversity in Cancer.
articles.abstract: Natural Killer (NK) cells, as the prototypic member of innate lymphocytes, play a key role in recognizing and killing malignant cells without the need for prior desensitization. NK cell-based therapies have been considered as a promising approach for the treatment of a wide range of hematological and solid malignancies. However, identification and characterization of highly functional populations of NK cells is essential for the advancement of this field. Recent advances in next-generation sequencing (NGS) and single-cell transcriptomics have enabled high-resolution profiling of NK cell diversity at the molecular level. This review explores methods for assessing NK cell function, including chromium-51 release assays, flow cytometry, impedance-based cell analysis systems, microfluidic platforms, bioluminescence imaging, PET, and multiplex imaging systems. Applications of NGS in NK cell research, including KIR receptor genotyping, exome and genome sequencing, and RNA-seq, are also discussed. Herein we examined the impact of NK cell heterogeneity on cancer treatment strategies and personalized therapeutic approaches, and analyzes the challenges and future directions in this field.

articles.title: Physiological impact of reduced anthelmintic intervention in naturally infected Thoroughbred foals: identifying stress indicators of welfare significance.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastrointestinal parasitism is common in pasture-raised foals, yet fecal egg count (FEC) may not reflect its physiological impact. Reduced anthelmintic use therefore requires integrated indicators of health, stress, and resilience.

AIMS/OBJECTIVES: To evaluate associations between FEC, growth, hematology, leukocyte morphology, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), cortisol, and behavior-related observations in naturally infected Thoroughbred foals managed under selective anthelmintic control.

METHODS: Thirty-five foals were followed from birth to 13 months under extensive management in southern Brazil, yielding 348 monthly evaluations. Growth, clinical and behavioral responses, FEC, coproculture, hematology, NLR, serum cortisol, fecal consistency, and anthelmintic efficacy were assessed using nonparametric analyses.

RESULTS: Cyathostomins predominated (84.0%), whereas Strongyloides spp. occurred mainly in summer. FEC ranged from 0 to 2,900 eggs/g and varied markedly among individuals. Body weight and wither height increased progressively, with average daily gain exceeding 1.0 kg/day during the first three months. Hematological values were mostly within reference ranges, and leukocyte abnormalities were infrequent (4.21%) and mild. Mean NLR was 1.56 ± 1.03. Cortisol was lower in treated foals (P < 0.001) but was not associated with FEC. No consistent associations were found between FEC and growth, hematology, leukocyte morphology, NLR, cortisol, or fecal consistency. Fecal egg count reduction was 6.6% after ivermectin plus praziquantel and 83.3% after piperazine.

CONCLUSION: Foals maintained growth and physiological stability despite persistent subclinical parasitism. FEC alone was insufficient to indicate physiological or behavior-related impairment or the need for treatment.

articles.title: SIRT1-mediated deacetylation of HMGB1 suppresses neuroinflammation and cellular senescence to alleviate diabetic peripheral neuropathy.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
articles.abstract: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is a devastating complication of diabetes. While neuroinflammation and cellular senescence are known contributors to DPN pathogenesis, the precise molecular mechanisms linking these processes remain unclear. In this study, we demonstrate that advanced glycation end products (AGEs) promote the nuclear-cytoplasmic translocation of high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1), enhancing its extracellular secretion. This extracellular HMGB1 functions as a damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP), recruiting inflammatory cells and inducing neuroinflammation and cellular senescence in PC12 cells. Consistent with these cellular findings, HMGB1 levels were markedly elevated in STZ-induced DPN mice. Notably, systemic neutralization of HMGB1 effectively suppressed neuroinflammation and senescence, thereby ameliorating DPN. Mechanistically, AGE treatment downregulated Sirtuin 1 (SIRT1), resulting in increased HMGB1 acetylation, which facilitated its nuclear export and extracellular release. Consequently, SIRT1-mediated deacetylation of HMGB1 attenuated neuroinflammation and delayed cellular senescence, playing a pivotal role in alleviating DPN. Our findings unveil the critical role of the SIRT1/HMGB1 deacetylation axis in orchestrating neuroinflammation and cellular senescence, highlighting targeted inhibition of HMGB1 secretion as a promising therapeutic strategy for DPN.

articles.title: Evaluation of phyto-additive mixture on growth performances and immunoprotection against white feces syndrome in Pacific white shrimp, Penaeus vannamei.
articles.abstract: Disease outbreaks like white feces syndrome significantly effecting shrimp farming productivity, and one of the primary challenges is enhancing the innate immune system of shrimp to improve resilience against Vibrio-associated diseases. Phyto-additives provide an eco-friendly approach to sustainable shrimp farming by improving growth, antioxidant defences, modulating immune responses, and strengthening resistance to pathogenic infections, while reducing dependence on synthetic compounds. To address these challenges, this study evaluated a dietary phyto-additive mixture containing crude extracts of Syzygium cumini, Withania somnifera, Curcuma longa, Allium sativum, Argemone mexicana and lemon peel on the growth performance, digestibility, and immune response of Penaeus vannamei against white feces syndrome. 540 juvenile shrimp (1.14 ± 0.05 g) were randomly distributed into six treatment groups in triplicate (30 shrimp/tank). Six experimental diets were formulated by supplementing the basal diet with 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, and 0.5 g 100 g-1 of the phyto-additive mixture, designated as Control, T1, T2, T3, T4, and T5, respectively. The feeding trial was conducted for 60 days, during which the experimental diets were administered three times daily at 10:00, 14:00, and 18:00H. Shrimp fed the T4 diet showed significantly higher final body weight, weight gain, specific growth rate, protein efficiency ratio, nutrient digestibility, and digestive enzyme activities compared to other treatment groups (P < 0.05). In addition, Shrimp fed the T4 diet (1.20 ± 0.08) exhibited a better feed conversion ratio than the control (1.64 ± 0.06) and other treatment groups. However, survival, whole-body proximate composition, and amino acid profile did not differ significantly among groups (P > 0.05). Following a 14-day challenge test, shrimp fed the T4 diet exhibited significantly higher antioxidant enzyme activities and relative mRNA expression of immune-related genes, including LYZ, TLR, and IMD, compared to the other treatments (P < 0.05). These genes strengthen shrimp innate immunity through antibacterial defence (LYZ), pathogen recognition (TLR), and activation of downstream immune responses (IMD). Furthermore, shrimp in the T4 group exhibited significantly lower cumulative mortality (13.33%) than those in the Control group (53.33%) following infection with Vibrio parahaemolyticus and the pathogen associated with White Feces Syndrome. In conclusion, dietary supplementation with 0.4 g 100 g-1 of the phyto-additive mixture significantly enhanced growth performance, nutrient digestibility and resistance against white feces syndrome in P. vannamei by modulating the innate immunity.

articles.title: Proceedings from the 2025 International Consensus Meeting on Orthopedic Infections: Prevention of Periprosthetic Shoulder Infection.
articles.journal: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is an uncommon but serious complication of shoulder arthroplasty. Many preventive practices are also extrapolated from hip and knee arthroplasty despite important differences in microbiology and surgical procedures. Furthermore, prevention is complicated by the importance of Cutibacterium acnes, which resides within the dermis and sebaceous structures and may not be reliably eliminated by conventional skin preparation. This International Consensus Meeting (ICM) aimed to develop evidence-based consensus recommendations for prevention of shoulder PJI.

METHODS: The Shoulder Group of the 2025 ICM on Orthopedic Infections included international shoulder surgeons, infectious disease physicians, and microbiology experts. More than 100 proposed questions were refined to 86, of which 25 addressed prevention. For each question, delegates performed a systematic literature review and developed a proposed recommendation. Evidence and recommendations were presented to the full group, discussed, revised, and voted upon using a modified Delphi process. Delegates voted agree, disagree, or abstain. Degree of consensus and strength of recommendation were assessed separately.

RESULTS: Consensus was achieved for all 25 questions, with 65%-100% agreement. Male sex and clinical or physical evidence of malnutrition were identified as PJI risk factors. Moderate-strength evidence supported avoiding corticosteroid injection within 3 months of shoulder arthroplasty, while evidence regarding hemoglobin A1c >8% was conflicting. Consensus supported individualized perioperative management of disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs, perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis, alcohol-based skin preparation, and avoidance of razor shaving. Evidence was insufficient to determine the effects of testosterone supplementation, diagnostic indication, continuation of antiplatelet therapy before revision, extended oral antibiotic prophylaxis, or antibiotic prophylaxis for dental and other invasive procedures. Evidence was also insufficient to support specific intraoperative interventions for reducing PJI, including intrawound antibiotics, antiseptic irrigation, iodine-impregnated drapes, electrocautery, tranexamic acid, or selection of a particular arthroplasty type.

CONCLUSION: The 2025 ICM identified several strategies applicable to current practice while highlighting substantial gaps in shoulder-specific evidence. Many recommendations remain based on limited or extrapolated evidence. Prospective shoulder-specific studies using clinical PJI as the primary outcome are needed to determine which prevention strategies provide meaningful benefit.

articles.title: Three-hospital study of endoscope protein contamination and microbiome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Over 15 million colonoscopies and 7 million upper-GI endoscopies are performed annually in the United States, requiring reprocessing after each use to reduce infection risk. Methods for endoscope quality control are limited and require rapid turnover and high sensitivity/specificity.

METHODS: Here we explore two novel approaches to measure protein soil on endoscopes: turbulent fluid flow (TFF) extraction and extractionless assay for quick check of endoscope reprocessing (QC-ER). Microbial strains in extracted samples are characterized with Next-gen sequencing and PCR.

RESULTS: Both methods are suitable for clinical use. For TFF, 68 samples across three hospitals had an average pre-cleaning protein mass of 541±342µg and post-cleaning mass of 59±57 µg. For QC-ER, 63 samples across three hospitals had an average pre-cleaning mass of 66±52µg and post-cleaning mass of 28±33µg. None of 60 samples tested positive for microbes after high-level disinfection.

DISCUSSION: In method validation, both high level disinfection exposure and clinical sample matrices interfered with protein quantification by the bicinchoninic acid (BCA) assay. TFF and QC-ER detected soil that remained after simple rinsing. Differences in clinical results for pre-cleaning were likely due to post-procedure protocols. All levels were below consensus thresholds.

PRINCIPAL CONCLUSIONS: The amount of protein on endoscopes in healthcare facilities was quantified by these methods and fell within the expected range, with variations by type and age of endoscope.

articles.title: Acridine Derived Photosensitizers for Fungal Photoinactivation and Their Limited Clinical Applicability.
articles.abstract: This narrative review evaluates what published experiments establish about acridine-derived photosensitizers for fungal photoinactivation, with emphasis on imidazoacridinones and literature published through July 2025. Selected derivatives reduced the number of colony-forming planktonic Candida cells under direct blue-light illumination. Compounds absorbing in the same spectral region produced different colony-count reductions; their activity also varied with cellular accumulation and irradiation conditions. These culture results do not establish efficacy against infection. Blue excitation penetrates tissue poorly, limiting its use against fungi at depth. Host-cell testing of C1330 used a tetrazolium-reduction (MTT) metabolic assay in human keratinocytes. This assay did not determine whether treated cells could still form colonies and cannot establish host safety or selective fungal killing. Claims of cell killing require assessment of colony-forming survival in fungi and colony-forming mammalian cells. Separate acridine-orange studies examined coatings applied to fungi immobilized on quartz and light-triggered release from liposomal films containing triclosan. These surface and release experiments do not establish treatment of infected tissue. Evidence for mature-biofilm killing, sustained fungal control, and preferential fungal injury remains inadequate. The reviewed imidazoacridinones are therefore unlikely to have a useful clinical role on the available evidence: their blue excitation limits tissue penetration, and fungal killing at exposures that preserve host-cell survival has not been demonstrated.

articles.title: From Rotational Activation to Reentry Initiation in Scar-Related Ventricular Tachycardia: Unidirectional Block at a Conducting Gap Along a Fixed Line of Block.
Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Sudden Cardiac Death: Epidemiology, Mechanisms, Risk Stratification, and Prevention.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as the most prevalent chronic metabolic liver disease worldwide. Cardiovascular adverse events have long been the leading cause of death in the MASLD population, far exceeding liver-related mortality. Sudden cardiac death (SCD) represents the most insidious and rapidly progressing extreme clinical phenotype among these cardiovascular complications. However, the relationship between MASLD and SCD has long received insufficient attention. Accumulating evidence from clinical studies indicates that MASLD is associated with elevated sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) risk independent of conventional cardiometabolic risk factors. Notably, while non-invasive clinical proxies of hepatic steatosis (such as the fatty liver index) identify individuals with heightened susceptibility to SCA, advancing liver fibrosis shows the strongest, gradient-dependent association with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, although its relation to SCA or SCD specifically requires confirmation. Sudden death in MASLD may result from primary ventricular arrhythmias or, in advanced cirrhosis, from non-shockable arrest due to hemodynamic, infectious, or metabolic decompensation. Although shared cardiometabolic risk factors account for a substantial portion of this association, proposed mechanisms include insulin resistance-related myocardial energy disturbances, inflammation-associated myocardial and electrophysiological remodeling, cirrhosis-associated circulatory dysfunction, and gut-derived endotoxemia. In clinical practice, non-invasive fibrosis scores, circulating biomarkers, and imaging parameters represent promising candidate risk markers for evaluating electrophysiological vulnerability, though a validated, MASLD-specific SCD risk prediction model remains to be established. Strategies such as lifestyle intervention, metabolic-targeted pharmacotherapy, and intensive management of cardiovascular risk factors may interrupt the progression from MASLD to SCD. This review summarizes the current evidence to inform cardiovascular risk management across the course of MASLD.

articles.title: Ventricular Fibrillation During Pulsed Field Ablation With Dual-Energy Focal Catheters in Patients With Cardiac Implantable Electronic Devices.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Arrhythmia induction during catheter ablation in patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) has been reported, but the risk associated with pulsed field ablation (PFA) remains poorly characterized.

OBJECTIVE: To estimate the procedural incidence of unexpected ventricular fibrillation (VF) during PFA in patients with CIEDs and describe associated clinical and device findings.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center cohort study of consecutive PFA procedures in patients with CIEDs. All procedures were reviewed for unexpected VF.

RESULTS: Among 107 consecutive procedures using PFA energy in patients with CIEDs, 83 were atrial and 24 were ventricular ablations. Unexpected VF occurred in 4 patients (overall incidence 3.7%, 95% CI 1.0% - 9.3%): 1 during left atrial PFA for pulmonary vein isolation and 3 during left ventricular PFA for ventricular tachycardia ablations. VF occurred at ablation sites both near and remote from CIED lead tips. Device electrograms demonstrated prominent ablation artifact with abnormal triggered activity and mode switch behavior. Intra-procedural recordings also demonstrated local capture and R on T mechanisms.

CONCLUSIONS: Unexpected VF during PFA in patients with CIEDs occurred in 3.7% of procedures. These results complement prior adverse-event reports and support systematic pre-, intra-, and post-procedure CIED management, with external defibrillation immediately available, whenever PFA or dual-energy ablation is performed in patients with cardiac devices.

articles.title: Increased Left Ventricular Wall Thickness without Increased Mechanical Dispersion: A Distinguishing Feature of Transthyretin Amyloidosis Cardiomyopathy.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia (LTVA) is infrequent in patients with transthyretin cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) despite severe cardiac dysfunction. We aimed to assess left ventricular mechanical dispersion (LVMD), as a marker of arrhythmia substrate, in ATTR-CM in comparison to other phenotypes with increased left ventricular (LV) wall thickness and in relation to LTVA occurrence.

METHODS: Patients with suspected cardiac amyloidosis (CA) and increased LV wall thickness (septal thickness ≥12 mm) were identified. Patients with other types of CA and obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy were excluded. Data from comprehensive clinical assessments, laboratory tests, echocardiography with speckle tracking, and Tc-99m labeled pyrophosphate scintigraphy (PYP) were retrospectively collected from each patient. Diagnosis of ATTR-CM was established based on current recommendations. Longitudinal follow-up was performed over 5 years for LTVA (ventricular tachycardia and sudden cardiac arrest).

RESULTS: In ATTR-CM group (n=150) lower LV ejection fraction, impaired global longitudinal strain (GLS), higher LV mass index, smaller end-diastolic volume index and higher relative apical sparing (RAS) were observed compared to the non-amyloid LVH group (n=223). Significantly lower mechanical dispersion (LVMD) was a remarkable feature of ATTR-CM, additive to ESC echocardiography parameters for the differential diagnosis (net reclassification improvement: 0.74). Higher LVMD was associated with increased risk of LTVA, whereas ATTR-CM was associated with a lower risk of LTVA. Mediation analysis further supported the mediating role of LVMD in the association between ATTR-CM and LTVA.

CONCLUSION: Lower LVMD seems to be a distinguishing feature of ATTR-CM in association with infrequent LTVA despite severe increased LV wall thickness.

articles.title: Mitochondrial-derived peptide humanin alleviates AKI-to-CKD transition by inhibiting TRIM28-mediated ubiquitination of Suclg1.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) resulting from ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) may subsequently progress to chronic kidney disease (CKD) and eventually end-stage renal disease (ESRD). Humanin, a mitochondria-derived peptide, has been implicated in various physiological and pathological processes and exhibits cytoprotective effects against inflammation, apoptosis, and oxidative stress. Nevertheless, its role in the AKI-to-CKD transition remains poorly understood. This study showed that renal humanin expression was downregulated in a murine IRI model and this reduction was significantly correlated with renal function decline and kidney fibrosis progression. Exogenous supplementation of S14G-humanin (HN) was found to protect against kidney fibrosis induced by IRI. Mechanistically, HN attenuated kidney fibrosis by stabilizing succinate-CoA ligase subunit alpha (Suclg1) by inhibiting tripartite motif-containing protein 28 (TRIM28)-mediated ubiquitination of Suclg1. Inhibition of Suclg1 abolished the renoprotective effects of HN, underscoring the critical role of Suclg1 in the AKI-to-CKD transition. Moreover, HN-mediated upregulation of Suclg1 reduced superoxide dismutase 2 (SOD2) succinylation, linking metabolic reprogramming to mitochondrial dysfunction and fibrotic progression. Collectively, these findings reveal a critical role of humanin in mitigating kidney fibrosis and identify Suclg1 as a promising therapeutic target in the AKI-to-CKD transition.

articles.title: Preliminary Experience with a Standardized Perioperative Protocol for Infection Prevention in Inflatable Penile Prosthesis Surgery.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe a structured, multimodal perioperative protocol for infection prevention in Inflatable penile prosthesis (IPP) surgery and report preliminary outcomes.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed a prospectively maintained single-surgeon database of all IPP procedures performed at two XXXXXX XXXXXX hospitals between January 2017 and December 2025, classified as primary implants, removal and replacement (R/R), or component revisions (CR). Salvage procedures and explantations were excluded. A structured, protocol-driven perioperative antibiotic regimen individualized by procedure type was employed throughout, using a modified no-touch technique, copious antibiotic irrigation, a compressive mummy wrap dressing, and 23-hour inpatient observation. A Jackson-Pratt drain was placed routinely in primary cases and selectively in R/R and revision cases.

RESULTS: Of 487 procedures (406 primary, 58 R/R, 23 CR), one surgical site infection occurred (primary implant patient, 0.25%; 1/406), for an overall rate of 0.21% (1/487); no infections occurred in the R/R or CR groups. The infected case was managed with malleable salvage and later uncomplicated replacement. Mean age was 62.5, 63.4, and 65.2 years for primary, R/R, and revision patients, respectively. Comorbidities in the primary group included hypertension (64.5%), hyperlipidemia (60.3%), diabetes (32.3%), HIV (1.0%), and preoperative S. aureus/MRSA colonization (16.5%).

CONCLUSIONS: A standardized, multimodal perioperative protocol, including MRSA decolonization, chlorhexidine bathing, antimicrobial prophylaxis, no-touch technique, drain usage, and compressive dressing was associated with a very low infection rate across all procedure types, supporting further evaluation of this approach in broader settings.

articles.title: Lifestyle counseling including the DASH diet improves multiple metabolomic profiles.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lifestyle interventions improve cardiometabolic risk factors, but data from randomized trials on their impact on detailed metabolomic profiles remain limited.

OBJECTIVES: Our aim was to evaluate the effects of lifestyle counseling with and without the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet on changes in metabolomic patterns.

METHODS: We analyzed data from 690 adult participants of the randomized PREMIER trial. The trial compared three lifestyle interventions: 'Advice-only', 'Established', and 'Established plus DASH'. Fasting plasma metabolites were quantified by NMR spectroscopy at baseline and 6 months, and principal component (PC) analysis was used to identify metabolomic patterns. Multiple linear regression examined the interventions and changes in BMI and heart rate in relation to changes in PC scores and individual metabolites.

RESULTS: Thirteen PCs representing lipoprotein, triglyceride-rich, amino acid, fatty acid, inflammatory, and ketone-related patterns were identified. Compared with Advice-only, the Established intervention reduced PC4 (β = -0.50, P = 0.04), VLDL cholesterol, and saturated fatty acids. Established plus DASH had broader effects, reducing PC9 (β = -0.33, P = 0.01), PC11 (β = -0.28 P = 0.004), and PC12 (β = -0.23, P = 0.02), increasing omega-3 fatty acids, and lowering branched-chain and aromatic amino acids, lactate, citrate, and GlycA. BMI change was associated with multiple PCs, whereas heart rate change showed fewer independent associations.

CONCLUSIONS: Lifestyle interventions induce coordinated metabolomic changes across lipid, amino acid, and inflammatory pathways. Weight loss appears to be the primary driver, while adding DASH provides broader metabolomic benefits than standard lifestyle counseling.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00000616 (PREMIER: Lifestyle Interventions for Blood Pressure Control - Full Text View - ClinicalTrials.gov).

articles.title: Difficult-to-Treat Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa: Resistance Mechanisms and Susceptibility to the Novel Antipseudomonal β-Lactams.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an intrinsically resistant, opportunistic Gram-negative pathogen and a major cause of healthcare-associated infection, with a marked ability to acquire further resistance during therapy. Multidrug-resistant (MDR), extensively drug-resistant (XDR), and pandrug-resistant (PDR) classifications are widely used but may poorly reflect treatment difficulty, since resistant isolates may remain susceptible to other effective agents. The difficult-to-treat resistance (DTR) framework identifies non-susceptibility to a clinically relevant set of first-line agents and provides a more treatment-focused phenotypic classification; it has been adopted by Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) and by the new Japanese Society of Chemotherapy/Japanese Association for Infectious Diseases (JSC/JAID) guidance, although it remains underrecognized in Japan. Four novel antipseudomonal β-lactams are now available for DTR P. aeruginosa (DTR-P): ceftolozane/tazobactam, ceftazidime/avibactam, imipenem/relebactam, and cefiderocol. The 2026 JSC/JAID guidance incorporates underlying resistance mechanisms into its approach to selecting among these agents. This review examines the evidence linking individual resistance mechanisms to expected in vitro susceptibility, emphasizing the heterogeneity of DTR isolates and the importance of direct susceptibility testing. We also summarize current epidemiology in Japan, where carbapenemase-producing isolates remain uncommon and chromosomal mechanisms predominate, and contrast this with regional differences worldwide. We then examine the practical challenges of mechanism-based antimicrobial selection, including limited access to mechanism testing and the frequent coexistence of resistance mechanisms. Finally, we review clinical outcome evidence for the four agents, noting broadly comparable efficacy across available studies but limited direct comparative evidence and no prospective evidence establishing that mechanism-guided selection improves clinical outcomes over conventional approaches in DTR-P infections.

articles.title: Private Equity Acquisition of U.S. Hospitals Providing Neonatal and Pediatric Care from 2000-2021.
articles.abstract: Private equity (PE) ownership of U.S. adult hospitals is increasing, but the temporal trends and hospital characteristics of PE-owned hospitals providing neonatal or pediatric care remain unknown. We created a retrospective cohort of neonatal- and pediatric-serving U.S. acute care hospitals with 2000-2021 American Hospital Association and Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) data. We determined the exposure, PE hospital ownership, annually with 3 databases: Pitchbook, the PE Stakeholder Project Hospital Tracker, and the CMS change of hospital ownership file. PE ownership of neonatal- and pediatric-serving hospitals has increased, from 11 (0.3%) to 100 (3.5%) hospitals over 2000-2021 while all neonatal- and pediatric-serving hospitals have decreased from 3,618 to 2,737. PE facilities in 2021 were smaller; located in the rural Southeast; had higher operating margins; and provided less neonatal and pediatric intensive care unit care. Overall, there was higher growth in PE-owned neonatal and/or pediatric acute care hospitals in the face of declining numbers of these hospital overall, with unequal geographic distribution.

articles.title: Functional vulnerability of the M1/S1 transitional zone in post-stroke motor deficits in mice.
articles.abstract: Functional outcome after cortical infarction depends not only on lesion volume but also on its anatomical location. However, the functional differences between the primary motor cortex (M1), secondary motor cortex (M2), and primary somatosensory cortex (S1) have rarely been compared within a single task, and the functional significance of the territory between them remains unexplored. In this study, we induced photothrombotic infarctions centered on M1, M2, or S1 in mice and assessed right forelimb movement during a skilled lever-pull task for up to 28 days post-infarction, using DeepLabCut with manual curation. By registering every lesion to the Allen Mouse Brain Common Coordinate Framework, we performed pixel-wise mapping of impairment independent of anatomical boundaries. We found that while lesion volume in M1 correlated with the magnitude of the deficit, M2 lesions failed to induce detectable deficits, and S1-centered lesions produced deficits that did not persist above baseline. Importantly, pixel-wise mapping revealed that infarcts encompassing the M1/S1 transitional zone caused the most severe and persistent deficits. These results demonstrate that coverage of this motor-somatosensory transitional zone, rather than anatomical labeling, is the key determinant of behavioral impairment and its long-term recovery.

articles.title: Hantavirus infection and the boundaries of autoimmunity: Vascular immunopathology, autoimmune-like mimicry, and post-infectious phenomena.
articles.abstract: Orthohantaviruses are rodent-borne RNA viruses causing acute systemic vascular syndromes, principally haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome. Although primarily infectious, hantavirus disease may generate vascular, renal, haematological, and systemic phenotypes that overlap with immune-mediated disorders. This Review critically examines the boundary between infection-driven immunopathology and autoimmunity. Hantavirus infection involves endothelial dysfunction, innate antiviral sensing, interferon responses, cytokine and chemokine amplification, complement activation, immunothrombosis, and adaptive immune responses, whose expression is further influenced by virus-, host-, and tissue-specific factors. These mechanisms contribute to the marked heterogeneity of clinical disease and may reproduce autoimmune-like clinical and laboratory features, but do not, in themselves, establish sustained loss of immune tolerance. Current evidence is substantially stronger for acute infection-associated immunopathology and phenotypic mimicry than for persistent autoreactivity or causally attributable post-infectious autoimmune disease. Reported autoimmune phenomena remain uncommon and predominantly case-based, while longitudinal, antigen-specific, and epidemiological evidence is limited. Persistent or recurrent manifestations after resolution of infection therefore require additional serological, histopathological, or other objective evidence of sustained immune dysregulation. Hantavirus infection thus provides a clinically informative model for distinguishing antiviral immunopathology from autoimmune-like mimicry and rare possible post-infectious autoimmunity, with direct implications for diagnosis and therapeutic restraint. TAKE-HOME MESSAGES.

articles.title: ROS/pH/glucose-responsive hydrogel based on 3-aminophenylboronic acid-modified hyaluronic acid and PVA loaded self-assembled ursolic acid/β-acids nanoparticles accelerates MRSA-infected diabetic wound healing.
articles.abstract: Bacterial infection severely delays the healing of diabetic wounds. Although hydrogels are widely explored as wound dressings, many lack the multi-responsiveness needed to adapt to the dynamic microenvironment of infected wounds. Herein, we designed a nanocomposite hydrogel that integrates antibacterial and antioxidant functions with responsiveness to ROS, pH, and glucose. First, self-assembled spherical nanoparticles (size <200 nm) composed of ursolic acid, β-acids, and Fe3+ were fabricated. These nanoparticles exhibited potent antioxidant and antibacterial properties, and their assembly mechanism was elucidated through experimental methods and molecular simulations. A triple-responsive hydrogel (UAHPHY) was prepared by 3-aminophenylboronic acid grafting hyaluronic acid and subsequently crosslinking with polyvinyl alcohol. Incorporating the nanoparticles into this three-dimensional porous hydrogel preserved their antibacterial and antioxidant bioactivities. The drug-loaded hydrogel maintained high viability of L929 fibroblasts and HUVECs for 72 h, promoted L929 proliferation, enhanced HUVEC-mediated tube formation, and displayed a low hemolytic rate. In an MRSA-infected diabetic wound model, the hydrogel markedly accelerated wound closure over 14 days. RNA-seq analysis revealed that the resulting UAHPHY hydrogel promoted wound healing might by activating the PI3K/AKT as an associated pathway. Collectively, this microenvironment-adaptive functional hydrogel offers an effective therapeutic strategy for treating MRSA-infected diabetic wounds.

articles.title: Recommendations for the Examination, Processing, and Reporting of Non-neoplastic Pericardial Diseases: A Consensus Statement on Pericardial Disease from the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology.
articles.journal: Cardiovascular pathology : the official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Recent advances in the evaluation and management of pericardial diseases highlight the importance of accurate pathologic assessment. Despite these current developments, the handling, processing, and reporting of pericardial specimens have not been formally addressed in recent years. This consensus document is intended to enable the pathologist to evaluate the pericardium as a surgical specimen as well as at postmortem examination, with particular emphasis on standardized gross and microscopic assessment of the pericardium.

METHODS AND RESULTS: An international expert panel comprising volunteer members of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology was convened to develop consensus recommendations. Strong agreement on best practices was achieved through a series of in-person and hybrid virtual meetings. The document outlines recommendations for the handling and processing of surgical pericardial specimens, including appropriate histochemical and immunohistochemical stains and ancillary diagnostic studies. Guidance for the systematic examination of the pericardium at autopsy is also provided. In addition, a nomenclature for common and well-defined pathologic processes is proposed, together with relevant differential diagnoses. The recommended terminology encompasses the predominant inflammatory cell infiltrates and the spectrum of organization from fibrinous pericarditis to established pericardial fibrosis.

CONCLUSION: This consensus document provides a standardized framework for the pathologic evaluation of the pericardium with the goal of improving diagnostic consistency, facilitating communication among clinicians and pathologists, and promoting uniformity in clinical practice and research.

articles.title: Pathology of the parietal pericardium: A consensus statement on pericardial disease from the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology.
articles.journal: Cardiovascular pathology : the official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Pericardial diseases encompass a broad spectrum of infectious, inflammatory, metabolic, traumatic, iatrogenic, and neoplastic disorders occurring in the setting of both localized and systemic conditions. Advances in understanding of the pathogenesis and diagnosis of pericardial disease have been substantial. Despite extensive literature on the clinical aspects of pericardial disease, relatively few studies have focused on its pathologic features.

METHODS AND RESULTS: An international panel from volunteer members of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology conducted a comprehensive review of the literature to develop a consensus document on the recommendations for pathologic evaluation of the parietal pericardium. This first document summarizes our state-of-the-art understanding of the etiological and morphological aspects of pericardial diseases, including pericardial effusions, cardiac tamponade, infectious and non-infectious pericarditis, and constrictive pericarditis, and incorporates updated clinical definitions and diagnostic criteria.

CONCLUSION: This consensus review highlights the role of pathology in the diagnosis of pericardial disease. Future efforts should explore establishing contemporary reference ranges for normal pericardial fluid volume, refining the pathologic characterization of pericarditis, correlating histopathologic findings with advanced cardiac imaging, and elucidating the molecular mechanisms driving the progression of pericardial fibrosis to constrictive disease.

articles.title: Peritoneal Dialysis Prehabilitation: Background and Protocol for the CORE-PD Pilot Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of renal nutrition : the official journal of the Council on Renal Nutrition of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract: Physical function impairment and decline is common for people living with kidney failure and receiving peritoneal dialysis. Consequently, this population experience unfavourable health outcomes including loss of independence, reduced life participation and overall poor quality of life. Physical function is a patient identified research priority with strategies to mitigate decline critical, however, yet to be rigorously explored and moreover, implemented as part of routine care. Prehabilitation refers to a process of improving physical function prior to a surgery or medical treatment and, may represent a novel strategy to prepare people who are due to commence peritoneal dialysis treatment. These interventions typically involve exercise and aim to enhance cardiorespiratory fitness, muscle strength and, foster positive behaviour change. This paper discusses the impact and challenges associated with peritoneal dialysis and physical function decline and, introduces a protocol for how prehabilitation could be implemented for people preparing to commence peritoneal dialysis. The primary aim of this proposed protocol is to explore the feasibility and acceptability of such an intervention, with secondary outcomes focusing on the impact of the intervention on patient identified, high-priority outcomes including life participation, infection and technique survival.

articles.title: Beyond Traditional Approaches: The Rush Rod Construct for Managing Chronic Periprosthetic Joint Infection in Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traditional management strategies for total knee arthroplasty (TKA) periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), such as two-stage arthroplasty with static or dynamic spacers, have limitations. We developed a Rush Rod-reinforced articulating construct intended for use as both a first-stage spacer in two-stage revision and as a definitive 1.5-stage solution. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the construct's infection-free survival and functional outcomes in the management of chronic TKA PJI.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of patients who have a chronic TKA PJI treated with a Rush Rod construct between 2010 and 2023 at a single tertiary referral center. Patients were categorized as planned for two-stage revision or definitive 1.5-stage revision. The primary outcome was re-infection-free survival, analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods. The secondary outcomes included tier-based outcomes as per the Musculoskeletal Infection Society (MSIS) outcome reporting tool (ORT) and postoperative knee range of motion (ROM). There were 40 patients who were included who had a mean age of 66 years and a median follow-up of 39 months (range, 12 to 133).

RESULTS: There were nine patients (22.5%) who retained the Rush Rod construct as a definitive 1.5-stage solution. Overall, 32 patients (80%) remained free of reinfection during follow-up. Using the MSIS ORT, 7.5% of cases failed management due to PJI. Following Rush Rod construct implantation, mean knee flexion exceeded 100°, with preservation of near-full extension, with further improvement observed following second-stage reimplantation. There was one episode of construct dislocation observed.

CONCLUSIONS: The Rush Rod construct provides durable infection control and preserves knee ROM when used as the first stage of a two-stage revision or as a definitive 1.5-stage solution for chronic TKA PJI. A substantial proportion of patients retained the Rush Rod construct as definitive treatment while maintaining satisfactory function. This technique represents a reliable and flexible alternative to traditional spacer strategies.

articles.title: Concurrent Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor and Factor Xa Inhibitor Use Is Associated With Increased Transfusion and Periprosthetic Joint Infection After Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty Despite Tranexamic Acid.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) impair platelet function, and concurrent SSRI and oral anticoagulant use has been associated with major bleeding in medical populations. We evaluated whether preoperative concurrent SSRI and factor Xa (FXa) inhibitor use was associated with higher transfusion and complication rates compared with use of either medication alone after primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) when tranexamic acid (TXA) use was standard.

METHODS: Adult patients who underwent primary THA and received TXA on the day of surgery were identified in a large electronic health records database. The SSRI-only, FXa-only, and concurrent-use cohorts were independently 1:1 propensity-score matched to controls who did not have either exposure. The concurrent-use cohort was also matched directly to the SSRI-only and FXa-only cohorts. The primary outcome was allogeneic red blood cell transfusion. The secondary outcomes were surgical site infection (SSI), venous thromboembolism (VTE), periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), and revision THA at 30, 90, and 365 days.

RESULTS: Compared with matched controls, SSRI-only patients had significantly higher transfusion, PJI, and revision THA rates at all timepoints (30-day transfusion risk ratio [RR] 1.44; 1-year PJI, RR 1.48; 1-year revision, RR 1.84; all P < 0.001). The FXa-only patients did not have higher transfusion or complication rates. Compared with SSRI-only patients, concurrent use was not associated with significantly different rates of any outcome at any timepoint. Compared with FXa-only use, concurrent use was associated with higher transfusion rates at all timepoints and higher PJI and revision rates at 90 days and one year (RR 1.54 to 2.12; all P ≤ 0.026).

CONCLUSION: Preoperative SSRI use was associated with higher transfusion, PJI, and revision THA rates. Concurrent use exceeded FXa-only rates, but not SSRI-only rates, suggesting that SSRI use may be the more important perioperative risk marker. The use of SSRIs should be recognized during preoperative bleeding-risk assessment.

articles.title: Metaphyseal Sleeves for Bone Defects in Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The management of metaphyseal bone defect constitutes a persistent challenge in revision total knee arthroplasty (RTKA). Metaphyseal sleeves achieve fixation through biologic press fit and have been increasingly utilized for managing severe bone defects. While individual series have reported favorable outcomes, an integrated and systematic synthesis of the current evidence remains unavailable.

METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library was conducted from inception through March 30, 2026. Studies were considered eligible if they reported clinical, radiographic, or survivorship outcomes using metaphyseal sleeves in RTKA. Data extracted included patient demographics, implant details, function, survivorship, and radiographic outcomes. All pooled estimates were calculated using random-effects models, and subgroup analyses were performed according to fixation method and duration of follow-up. A total of 41 studies comprising 3,037 knees and 4,774 sleeves were included.

RESULTS: The pooled postoperative Knee Society Score Knee score was 90.9 points (95% confidence interval [CI], 82.6 to 99.3), and the pooled maximal knee flexion was 108.3° (95% CI, 102.2 to 114.5). The rate of all-cause re-revision was 6.5% (95% CI, 4.2 to 9.2), with periprosthetic joint infection identified as the leading cause of failure. Sleeve removal for aseptic loosening occurred in 0.1% (95% CI, 0 to 0.4) of sleeves, and the rate of osseointegration was 99.6% (95% CI, 98.5 to 100). There was no statistically significant difference in sleeve removal for aseptic loosening between uncemented and hybrid fixation or between the ≤ 36 months and greater than 36 months groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Metaphyseal sleeves in RTKA are associated with low rates of aseptic loosening and high rates of radiographic osseointegration, with periprosthetic joint infection remaining the predominant cause of failure. Sleeve survival appears independent of fixation method and is maintained over the duration of follow-up. Further studies with surveillance beyond 10 years and direct comparative investigations between sleeves and alternative metaphyseal fixation methods are warranted.

articles.title: Complications After Primary Total Joint Arthroplasty in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The outcomes after total joint arthroplasty (TJA) for patients who have solid organ transplants (SOT) remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate: 1) overall medical and surgical complication rates, 2) survivorship-free rates from periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) and mortality specifically, and 3) risk factors for complications in SOT recipients undergoing TJA.

METHODS: A retrospective study was performed of all SOT recipients undergoing primary TJA at a single academic institution between 2005 and 2024, with a minimum one-year follow-up. Demographics, surgical characteristics, medical comorbidities, transplant type, and immunosuppressive therapy were recorded. We identified 103 TJAs (69 total hip arthroplasties [THA], 34 total knee arthroplasties [TKA]) in 89 SOT recipients who had a mean follow-up of 4.9 years. The overall complication rate was 26.2% (27 of 103). Logistic regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses were performed. An alpha level of 0.05 denoted significance.

RESULTS: The surgical and medical complication rates were 13.0 and 13.0% after THA, and 5.9 and 20.6% after TKA, respectively. After THA, five-year infection-free and mortality-free survivorships were 97.8 and 92.0%, respectively, with no difference by transplant type (P = 0.40 and P = 0.84, respectively). After TKA, five-year infection-free and mortality-free survivorships were 96.4 and 74.8%, respectively, with no difference by transplant type (P = 0.57 and P = 0.29, respectively). When controlling for confounders, body mass index (Odds Ratio [OR] 0.88, P = 0.02) and history of liver transplant (OR 0.21, P = 0.04) were associated with increased complications.
