CONCLUSION: While overall complication rates were high, SOT recipients demonstrated low PJI rates following TJA when managed with multidisciplinary perioperative care. Only renal transplant recipients developed PJI, demonstrating potentially higher susceptibility in this subgroup. The mortality rates identified are concordant with literature describing general survivorship of patients after SOT and therefore appear to not be affected by undergoing TJA.

articles.title: Constitutional Restoration versus Mechanical Neutral in the Younger Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Pre-Specified Bayesian Competing-Risk Analysis of Alignment Accuracy and Aseptic Revision.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In younger total knee arthroplasty (TKA) patients, revision rather than death dominates competing risks, so any true alignment effect is least likely to be masked. We asked whether deviation from constitutional alignment or from mechanical neutrality more strongly predicts aseptic revision and whether the effect is clinically meaningful.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed TKA patients younger than 65 years who had paired pre- and postoperative long-leg radiographs and minimum two-year follow-up. We used two per-degree exposures to capture the competing philosophies: restoration error (absolute change in arithmetic hip-knee-ankle angle) and neutralization error (absolute postoperative mechanical hip-knee-ankle deviation from 180°). The primary endpoint was aseptic revision, with death and infection as competing events. A pre-specified Bayesian competing-risk model used weakly informative and skeptical priors with posterior-probability inference. Cause-specific and Fine-Gray models and the six-month Oxford Knee Score (OKS) were secondary analyses.

RESULTS: Among 470 TKAs (376 patients) with 26 aseptic revisions, restoration error was uninformative (hazard ratio [HR] 1.00 per degree, 95% credible interval [CrI] 0.90 to 1.10; 52% probability of any harm). Neutralization error was probably harmful (HR 1.08 per degree, CrI 0.93 to 1.22; 87% probability of harm; 50% probability of a clinically meaningful effect [≥ 1.5-fold increase over a 5° error]). The probability that neutralization error mattered more than restoration error was 81% and stable under the skeptical prior. Frequentist cause-specific and Fine-Gray models agreed with these estimates, and neither error was associated with the six-month OKS.

CONCLUSIONS: In younger TKA patients, deviation from mechanical neutral predicted aseptic revision more strongly than deviation from constitutional alignment. Although personalized alignment carried no measurable survivorship penalty at midterm follow-up, the intended target accuracy matters more than the alignment label.

articles.title: Referral Geography, Case Complexity, and Definitive Surgical Strategy in a Regional Specialized Center for Periprosthetic Joint Infection in China.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Specialized models of care for periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) are increasingly advocated, but the relationship between referral geography, complexity at presentation, and definitive surgical management remains incompletely defined. We evaluated whether broader referral geography was associated with greater accumulated prereferral burden, differences in definitive surgical strategy, and treatment outcomes in a regional specialized PJI center in China.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of 492 consecutive patients who underwent surgical treatment for hip or knee PJI between January 2017 and December 2024 at a regional specialized referral center. Referral geography was categorized as Urumqi, other regions within Xinjiang, or outside Xinjiang. Multivariable logistic regression analyses evaluated factors associated with single-stage revision rather than debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention (DAIR), and with infection-related failure rather than infection control. A sensitivity analysis compared patients treated during the COVID-19 period (2020 to 2022) with those treated during the remaining study years.

RESULTS: Broader referral geography was associated with greater accumulated prereferral burden. Median symptom duration increased from 1.3 months in Urumqi to 4.0 months in Xinjiang, excluding Urumqi, and 12.0 months outside Xinjiang (P < 0.001). The prevalence of a sinus tract increased from 15.1 to 35.3% and 51.2%, respectively (P < 0.001), and the proportion of patients who had two or more prior PJI-related procedures increased from 4.7 to 8.3% and 30.0% (P < 0.001). After adjustment for measured clinical factors, patients from Xinjiang excluding Urumqi had greater odds of undergoing single-stage revision than patients from Urumqi (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 2.54; 95% CI [confidence interval], 1.37 to 4.70; P = 0.003), as did patients referred from outside Xinjiang (adjusted OR, 4.06; 95% CI, 1.48 to 11.14; P = 0.006). The referral region was not associated with infection-related failure after adjustment. The overall distribution of treatment outcomes did not differ significantly across referral strata (P = 0.801) or between patients treated during and outside the COVID-19 period (P = 0.863).

CONCLUSION: In this regional specialized PJI center in China, broader referral geography was associated with greater accumulated prereferral burden and greater adjusted odds of undergoing single-stage revision rather than DAIR, but was not associated with infection-related failure. These findings underscore the importance of accounting for referral case mix when evaluating specialized PJI care. The absence of statistically significnt differences in outcomes across referral strata should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence, and the observed associations do not establish the superiority of one surgical strategy over another.

articles.title: Microenvironment of Bone and Joint Infection: Examining the Microenvironment.
articles.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a major complication of arthroplasty, and conventional diagnostic methods for PJI remain limited by suboptimal sensitivity, long turnaround times, high cost, and patient inconvenience, particularly in biofilm-associated and culture-negative infections. Emerging data suggest that the infected joint microenvironment contains host- and pathogen-derived molecular signatures with substantial diagnostic potential. This review evaluates current evidence on microenvironment-related biomarkers in PJI, including host extracellular vesicles, host cell-free nucleic acids (microRNA/cell-free DNA), non-host-derived biomarkers, and sequencing-based pathogen detection techniques. Host-derived biomarkers show favorable discriminatory capability by characterizing inflammatory and immune responses, and metagenomic and sequencing-based technologies improve pathogen identification. Despite encouraging diagnostic performance, widespread clinical implementation remains limited due to a lack of standardization, cost, and limited prospective validation. Future prospective multicenter studies should integrate conventional microbiological methods with molecular and microenvironment-based approaches to improve diagnostic accuracy.

articles.title: Development and Temporal Validation of a Risk Prediction Model for Piperacillin/Tazobactam Induced Thrombocytopenia in Older Patients.
articles.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia (DITP) is a rare but potentially life-threatening adverse drug reaction, with evidence largely limited to case reports. Piperacillin-tazobactam (PTZ) appears to carry a relatively higher risk, particularly in older patients. This study aims to elucidate the clinical characteristics and risk factors associated with piperacillin-tazobactam (PTZ)-induced thrombocytopenia in older patients, to develop and validate a risk prediction model.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, we screened 5,454 older inpatients (≥60 years) treated with PTZ for pulmonary infections at Xiangya Hospital (2020-2022) for model development, with a separate 2024 cohort for temporal validation. After strict exclusion, 258 patients entered the model development phase (202 non-cases and 56 thrombocytopenia cases). Among the 56 cases, 40 were confirmed as PTZ-related and analyzed by multivariate logistic regression to identify independent risk factors, leaving 242 patients in the final development cohort. Model performance was evaluated using the separate temporal validation cohort (n=151) via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.

RESULTS: PTZ-related thrombocytopenia occurred in 16.5% (40/242) of the development cohort. The independent risk factors identified included: baseline platelet count ≤150×10⁹/L (OR=8.065, 95% CI: 3.510-18.530), serum creatinine ≥80 μmol/L (OR=3.925, 95% CI: 1.752-8.797), aspartate aminotransferase ≥30 U/L (OR=3.154, 95% CI: 1.415-7.028), and hemoglobin ≤90 g/L (OR=3.172, 95% CI: 1.319-7.629). The prediction model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.819 (95% CI: 0.753-0.885) in the development set and 0.713 (95% CI: 0.568-0.858) in the temporal validation set.

CONCLUSION: A predictive model incorporating baseline platelet count, serum creatinine, aspartate aminotransferase, and hemoglobin demonstrated good discriminative performance for PTZ-induced thrombocytopenia in older patients, supporting its potential utility for individualized risk stratification.

articles.title: Secondary mitral regurgitation in HFrEF: Predicting reversibility on medical therapy before intervention.
Preoperative high-frequency QRS parameters and left bundle branch area pacing response in non-ischemic left bundle branch block patients: An exploratory study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBP) has become a preferred as a novel strategy for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). High-frequency QRS (HFQRS) analysis can detect subtle ventricular depolarization abnormalities that are not identifiable on standard electrocardiography and may provide novel markers for predicting response to LBBP.

METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 58 consecutive patients with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy and left bundle branch block (LBBB) who underwent guideline-directed LBBP between 2022 and 2025. LBBP response was defined as an absolute increase in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) >10% at 6-month follow-up. Preprocedural HFQRS parameters were quantitatively analyzed, including mean HFQRS amplitude and the high-frequency morphological index (HFMI).

RESULTS: Forty-three patients (74.1%) met the criteria for LBBP response. Responders had significantly lower anterior mean HFQRS amplitude (1.61 ± 0.59 vs. 2.60 ± 1.01 μV, P = 0.002) and higher anterior HFMI (24.7% vs. 16.1%, P = 0.002) than non-responders. Anterior mean amplitude showed the strongest predictive value for LBBP response (AUC = 0.800, 95% CI 0.656-0.944). Patients with lower anterior mean amplitude demonstrated better event-free survival (log-rank P = 0.011). In multivariable analysis, lower anterior mean amplitude independently predicted greater LVEF improvement (β = -0.474, P = 0.003) and was associated with more pronounced reverse remodeling (P = 0.001).

CONCLUSION: In patients with non-ischemic LBBB undergoing LBBP, reduced anterior mean HFQRS amplitude is independently associated with improved ventricular recovery and a higher likelihood of response to resynchronization therapy. HFQRS analysis may provide a useful noninvasive tool for preprocedural risk stratification and patient selection in LBBP.

articles.title: Baseline circulating thrombospondin-1 is associated with recurrence after catheter ablation in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Recurrence after radiofrequency catheter ablation remains common in patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF), and clinically accessible biomarkers for pre-procedural risk stratification are limited. Thrombospondin-1 (TSP-1) is a circulating matricellular protein implicated in inflammatory and profibrotic pathways.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of 211 patients with paroxysmal AF undergoing first-time radiofrequency catheter ablation. Baseline circulating TSP-1 was measured before ablation and analysed primarily as a continuous (log-transformed) variable, with a pre-specified 75th-percentile threshold used for exploratory subgroups. The primary endpoint was AF recurrence after a 3-month blanking period. Multivariable Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, time-dependent discrimination with bootstrap optimism correction, and propensity score matching (sensitivity analysis) were performed.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 700 days, 61 patients (28.9%) experienced AF recurrence. Higher baseline TSP-1 was independently associated with recurrence in the full cohort (adjusted HR per 1-SD of log-TSP-1, 1.54; 95% CI 1.26-1.88; p < 0.001) and persisted after propensity score matching (HR 4.73; 95% CI 2.18-10.29). Adding TSP-1 improved time-dependent discrimination at 700 days (AUC 0.62 to 0.70; optimism-corrected 0.66; Harrell's C 0.627 to 0.705), although reclassification metrics were mixed and the incremental value was exploratory.

CONCLUSION: Elevated baseline circulating TSP-1 was associated with a higher risk of AF recurrence after first-time radiofrequency catheter ablation in patients with paroxysmal AF. These findings support further evaluation of TSP-1 as a candidate biomarker for pre-procedural risk stratification.

articles.title: Cardiovascular risk stratification in patients undergoing liposomal anthracycline: Association with cardiovascular outcomes and overall survival.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elderly patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma and cardiovascular disease are frequently treated with regimens incorporating non-PEGylated liposomal anthracycline to mitigate cardiotoxicity while preserving antitumor efficacy. However, considering their unique pharmacokinetics, validation of a cardiovascular risk stratification tool for these patients is much needed.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients with newly diagnosed non-Hodgkin lymphoma treated with rituximab, cyclophosphamide, non-PEGylated liposomal doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone (R-COMP) between 2014 and 2025. Baseline demographics, cardiovascular history and medications, echocardiographic and laboratory parameters were recorded. Patients were stratified into risk categories according to the Heart Failure Association International Cardio-Oncology Society (HFA-ICOS) score. Outcomes included overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS) and incidence of cardiovascular events defined as asymptomatic left ventricular dysfunction, new-onset or worsening heart failure and acute coronary syndrome.

RESULTS: The cohort consisted of 265 patients [median age 73 years (69-77); 51% males]; 41% were classified as moderate risk, 55% as high risk, and 4% as very high risk. During a median follow-up of 29 months, 38 patients (14%) died. OS and cardiovascular events occurrence significantly differed across the three HFA-ICOS risk categories; in particular, very high-risk patients exhibited substantially higher hazards of mortality (HR 5.8) and cardiovascular events (HR 40.4). Cardioprotective therapy at baseline appears not influence cardiovascular outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: The HFA-ICOS score effectively stratifies mortality and risk of cardiovascular events among patients treated with R-COMP. Despite the limited number of very-high risk patients and the heterogenous, non-randomized cardioprotective strategies at baseline, our findings may provide evidence supporting its integration into practice.

articles.title: Pathovars of Escherichia coli associated with diarrhoea - which, when and how to treat them.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In recent years, nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) have enabled the routine detection of the major intestinal pathogenic Escherichia coli (InPEC) pathovars associated with diarrhoeal disease. These include enteropathogenic E. coli (EPEC), enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC), Shiga toxin-producing E. coli (STEC), enteroaggregative E. coli (EAEC), enteroinvasive E. coli (EIEC), a pathotype closely related to Shigella species. However, the indications for testing and the appropriate therapeutic management of these infections remain insufficiently defined.

OBJECTIVES: This review summaries current knowledge of the major InPEC pathovars to clarify when diagnostic testing is warranted and to define their clinical management, with particular emphasis on the role of antibiotic treatment.

SOURCES: This narrative review draws on relevant studies published over the past 20 years and identified through PubMed searches. Major original studies, reviews, and guidance documents were selected, and their reference lists were examined to identify additional key publications.

CONTENT: EPEC, EAEC, and ETEC generally cause mild-to-moderate watery diarrhoea, although EPEC and EAEC are also frequently detected in asymptomatic individuals. Supportive care, particularly the prevention and treatment of dehydration, is therefore the cornerstone of management. EIEC infections range from mild diarrhoea to severe dysentery-like disease but routine molecular diagnosis cannot distinguish EIEC from Shigella spp.. STEC are the InPEC pathovar of greatest concern in industrialized countries they can cause haemolytic uraemic syndrome (HUS) and death. The risk of HUS depends on both host factors and the strain's virulence profile and may be influenced by exposure to certain antibiotics.

IMPLICATIONS: Routine testing for EPEC, EAEC, and ETEC is rarely warranted. As molecular assays cannot distinguish EIEC from Shigella spp. and routine culture does not reliably identify EIEC, treatment should be guided by disease severity. Antibiotic use in STEC infection remains controversial, and randomized trials are needed to assess whether selected agents or alternative strategies can prevent HUS in high-risk patients.

articles.title: Temperature-Heart Rate Coupling Mismatch Index (THRCI) and Its Association with Early Organ Dysfunction and Mortality in Sepsis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Early sepsis risk stratification remains challenging. We hypothesized that abnormal early coupling between body temperature and heart rate reflects physiologic dysregulation and predicts subsequent organ dysfunction.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: This single-center prospective cohort at Anting Hospital (March 2021 to September 2025) evaluated adults with Sepsis-3-defined sepsis using a 12-hour landmark design. The Temperature-Heart Rate Coupling Mismatch Index (THRCI) combined four predefined features derived from paired bedside temperature and heart rate data during the first 12 hours. The primary endpoint was a ≥2-point increase in Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score from 12 to 48 hours. Secondary endpoints were new vasopressor use and new invasive mechanical ventilation after 12 hours, and 28-day mortality. Patients who died, were discharged, or were transferred to another institution before the landmark were excluded. Adjusted penalized regression and bootstrap internal validation were used.

RESULTS: Of 413 screened patients, 336 were enrolled and 322 analyzed; 108 (33.5%) met the primary endpoint. Each standard-deviation increase in THRCI was nominally associated with higher adjusted odds of SOFA worsening (adjusted odds ratio 2.02, 95% confidence interval 1.12-3.74; p=0.019; false discovery rate-adjusted q=0.06). Adding THRCI increased the apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve from 0.71 to 0.78 (optimism-corrected 0.76). Secondary associations were directionally consistent; none of the four associations remained significant after multiplicity adjustment.

CONCLUSIONS: Early temperature-heart rate coupling mismatch showed a nominal association with near-term SOFA worsening and may provide incremental prognostic information in sepsis. These exploratory findings require external validation.

articles.title: Prevalence, clinical implications and prognostic impact of frailty and other geriatric conditions in patients with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Frailty in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) remains poorly characterized. The aim of this study was to analyze the prevalence and prognostic influence of frailty and other geriatric conditions such as nutritional risk, cognitive status, depression, and dependence in patients with ATTR-CM.

METHODS: We performed an observational, prospective, single-center study of 110 ATTR-CM patients who underwent comprehensive geriatric assessment from October 2024 to April 2025 and were followed up to September 2026. Study endpoints were all-cause death and the combined event of all-cause death or worsening heart failure. Outcomes were assessed by the Kaplan-Meier method and multivariable Cox regression.

RESULTS: The prevalence of frailty, based on 4 different criteria, varied from 32.7% to 62.7%. Dependence, depression, nutritional risk, and cognitive impairment were detected in up to 70.9%, 29.1%, 27.3%, and 15.5% of patients, respectively. Frailty, defined as a Clinical Frailty Scale > 4, a Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe-Frailty Instrument > 2, or a Short Physical Performance Battery < 10, was independently associated with an increased risk of both study outcomes. Dependence (Katz index < 6) and cognitive impairment (Mini Examen Cognitivo score < 23) were also independent predictors of both outcomes. Frailty diagnosis showed incremental prognostic value when added to United Kingdom National Amyloidosis Centre stages.

CONCLUSIONS: Frailty is frequent in patients with ATTR-CM and is associated with impaired clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Left Subclavian Artery Revascularization and Early Neurological Outcomes After Zone 2 TEVAR.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: LSA revascularization is generally favored when intentional LSA coverage is planned during elective zone 2 TEVAR, whereas in urgent settings the decision is individualized according to anatomy, ischemic risk, and clinical urgency. This study evaluated the association between preoperative or concomitant LSA revascularization and early neurological outcomes after zone 2 TEVAR.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 32 patients who underwent zone 2 TEVAR with intentional LSA coverage between January 2018 and December 2024. Patients were classified according to whether LSA revascularization was performed before or concomitantly with TEVAR (Rev+, n=21) or not (Rev-, n=11). The primary endpoint was any 30 day neurological complication, including ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), and spinal cord ischemia (SCI). Major neurological events, defined as stroke or SCI, were additionally evaluated.

RESULTS: Early neurological complications occurred in 4/21 patients (19.0%) in the Rev+ group and 3/11 (27.3%) in the Rev- group (p=.667), corresponding to an absolute risk difference of -8.2 percentage points (95% CI, -39.4 to 23.0) and a risk ratio of 0.70 (95% CI, 0.19-2.58). Major neurological events occurred in 3/21 (14.3%) and 2/11 (18.2%) patients, respectively (p=1.000). Stroke occurred in 3/21 (14.3%) Rev+ patients and 1/11 (9.1%) Rev- patients, while SCI occurred in no Rev+ patients and in 1/11 (9.1%) Rev- patients. LSA revascularization was not significantly associated with the primary endpoint (OR, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.12-3.34; p=.582). Results remained similar after separate adjustment for age, dissection, urgency, coronary artery disease, and chronic kidney disease. Sensitivity analyses using major neurological events as the endpoint and including postoperative LSA revascularization in the exposure definition also yielded similar results.

CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative or concomitant LSA revascularization during zone 2 TEVAR was associated with a numerically lower rate of early neurological complications, although the difference was not statistically significant. Larger studies are needed to better define the association between LSA revascularization and neurological outcomes after zone 2 TEVAR.

articles.title: VOLUME ADJUSTED CALCIUM ANALYSIS OF AORTOILIAC ATHEROSCLEROSIS AS A PREDICTOR OF AMPUTATION FREE SURVIVAL.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES: Pre-operative cross-sectional imaging guides surgical planning in vascular surgery. Despite the relationship between atherosclerotic burden and surgical success, no studies have adjusted atherosclerotic burden according to lumen volume. Given variability in vessel diameter and significance of aortoiliac disease, we developed a volume-adjusted calcium score (VACS) and evaluated its association with patient outcomes.

METHODS: This single-institution retrospective study included 187 patients over nine years who underwent peripheral vascular intervention. Using TeraRecon, calcium and patent lumen volumes were quantified along a contiguous aorto-iliac segment totaling 10 cm generating a VACS. An intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) assessed inter-rater reliability. Patients were stratified into two groups. Primary outcomes were death at one year and amputation-free survival. Secondary outcomes were re-interventions and number of arteries treated.

RESULTS: Intervention type did not differ between the two groups. Patients with higher VACS were more likely older, have CHF, COPD, or hypertension. Patient in the higher VACS group had greater number of arteries treated, subsequent vascular interventions, and one-year all-cause mortality. A Cox-regression model demonstrated a VACSgreater than 0.33 was independently associated with decreased amputation-free survival at one year (HR 2.24, p=0.019).

CONCLUSION: In patients undergoing intervention for aortoiliac occlusive disease, higher VACS was independently associated with worse one-year amputation free survival. Incorporating patent lumen volume into VACS appears to capture a systemic atherosclerotic burden not fully reflected by traditional lesion-specific assessments.

articles.title: Posterior Transverse Plication of Tortuous Internal Carotid Arteries During Carotid Endarterectomy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Excessive tortuosity of the internal carotid artery (ICA) can create a risk of kinking after carotid endarterectomy (CEA) with patch angioplasty. Posterior transverse plication (PTP) shortens and straightens the ICA without arterial transection or resection. This study reviewed our outcomes with PTP followed by patch angioplasty during CEA.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study identified patients who underwent CEA between 2006 and 2023. Patients treated with PTP and patch angioplasty (PTP+P) were compared with a contemporaneous cohort undergoing CEA with Dacron patch closure alone (DP) for the same atherosclerotic carotid disease. Early and long-term outcomes included neurologic events, restenosis, pseudoaneurysm formation, reintervention, and survival.

RESULTS: Of 168 carotid interventions, 116 met inclusion criteria: 16 PTP+P and 100 DP. Patients in the PTP+P cohort were older and had higher rates of chronic renal insufficiency and coronary artery disease. There was no 30-day mortality or postoperative TIA/stroke in either cohort. During follow-up, no ipsilateral ischemic neurologic event occurred, and there was no significant difference in restenosis, pseudoaneurysm formation, reintervention, or overall survival. In adjusted analysis, increasing age was associated with worse survival, while PTP was not.

CONCLUSIONS: In this small series, adding PTP during CEA before patch angioplasty appeared safe for correcting ICA tortuosity. The complication profile was similar to that of patients with straighter ICAs who underwent DP closure alone. A wide patch and intraoperative duplex ultrasound are advisable to prevent and detect technical narrowing at the plication site.

MESHWORDS: Carotid endarterectomy; internal carotid artery tortuosity; posterior transverse plication; patch angioplasty; restenosis.

articles.title: Anthraquinone-enriched fraction of Rheum australe D. Don by Bioassay-guided fractionation and synergistic interaction with tetracycline against Bacterial pathogens.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Rheum australe is an important medicinal herb known as Himalayan rhubarb. Traditionally used in Ayurveda and Tibetan medicine to treat diabetes, diarrhoea, hypertension, obesity, wounds, backache & gastrointestinal diseases.

AIM OF THE STUDY: The current study is focused on studying the antibacterial and synergistic potential of the anthraquinone-enriched fraction of R. australe in combination with conventional antibiotics.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: The extract of R. australe was prepared using 70% ethanol with a Soxhlet apparatus, and Bioassay guided fractionation was done. Broth microdilution methods determined antibacterial and Synergistic activity of crude extracts and subfractions. Phytoconstituents were identified by LC-MS, and molecular docking was done to study the interaction with penicillin-binding protein 3, and docking-predicted potential interacting Phytoconstituents were quantified by HPLC.

RESULTS: The extraction yield of the hydroalcoholic extract was recorded as 40.66 ± 3.05%. The chloroform subfraction showed the strongest antibacterial activity among all the subfractions against MRSA (64 μg/ mL), S. aureus (16 μg/mL) &P. aeruginosa (8 μg/mL) mL, and also the strongest synergistic activity with tetracycline against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) (FICI 0.19-0.5), Staphylococcus aureus (FICI 0.0312-0.125), and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (FICI 0.125-0.375). Six phytoconstituents (piceatannol, chrysophanol, rhein, aloe-emodin, physcion & emodin) were identified by LC-MS. Molecular docking and MD simulation data revealed that among all the phytoconstituents, aloe-emodin, chrysophanol, emodin, & rhein indicated favourable interactions. HPLC analysis showed that these four phytoconstituents were enriched in the chloroform subfraction.

CONCLUSION: The current study suggests that the chloroform subfraction enriched in anthraquinones exhibits strong antibacterial activity and synergistic activity in combination with tetracycline, and the synergistic mechanism of the combination remains to be established.

articles.title: Evaluation of Zebrafish (Danio rerio) as a Potential Experimental Host for Rhinosporidium seeberi Under Laboratory Exposure Conditions.
articles.abstract: Rhinosporidiosis is a chronic granulomatous disease caused by Rhinosporidium seeberi, an aquatic pathogen whose life cycle and host interactions remain poorly understood due to the absence of an in vitro culture system and a reliable experimental animal model. Phylogenetic placement of R. seeberi within the Mesomycetozoea and its strong association with fresh water habitats suggest a possible role for aquatic vertebrates as alternative or intermediate hosts. In this study, we evaluated whether zebrafish (Danio rerio) could serve as a potential experimental host for R. seeberi. Adult zebrafish were exposed to histopathologically, and PCR confirmed human rhinosporidiosis tissue under passive immersion and trauma-enhanced conditions and monitored for up to 90 days post-exposure (dpe). Behavioural activity, feeding, survival, and gross morphology were assessed longitudinally, followed by quantitative behavioural analysis and whole-fish histopathology. Zebrafish exhibited no mortality, signs of infection, behavioural abnormalities, or external lesions throughout the study period. Quantitative locomotor analysis revealed no infection-associated behavioural changes. Histopathological examination of major organs, including gills, liver, muscle, kidney, stomach, heart and brain, revealed no evidence of R. seeberi sporangia, endospores, granulomatous inflammation, or tissue pathology at either 30 or 90 dpe. These findings indicate that R. seeberi has a limited potential to infect zebrafish under laboratory exposure conditions. This study provides the first experimental evidence that zebrafish are unlikely to serve as a model for rhinosporidiosis and underscores the need to explore alternative hosts and experimental approaches to investigate the biology of this uncultivable pathogen.

articles.title: Long Non-Coding RNAs in Tuberculosis: From Pathogenesis to Precision Therapeutics.
articles.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), is among the most prominent causes of global mortality, with the latest records pointing towards approximately 1.3 million deaths in 2023. Despite the worldwide use of the Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine and standard anti-TB drugs, the appearance of multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) strains is on the rise. This trend legitimately demands a shift in our focus toward the host-directed interventions. Recently, long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have emerged as regulators at the interface between the immune and metabolic systems during Mtb infection. They function as molecular regulators that coordinate inflammatory signalling and cellular energy metabolism. This review attempted to provide critical insights into how lncRNAs are regulated during a TB infection. Circulating lncRNAs show clear diagnostic potential, with some signatures outperforming conventional tests in discovery-phase cohorts; however, we also discuss significant implementation barriers in high-burden countries, including ultra-cold-chain logistics for RNA-based platforms. We have highlighted the need for translational development to move from cell lines to primary human cells and clinical cohorts. Unlike prior reviews that majorly catalogue TB-associated lncRNAs, this literature-based study delineates an evidence-level stratification framework and a five-tier translational roadmap to guide clinical development of lncRNA-targeted host-directed therapies.

articles.title: Viral Infections as Gatekeepers of Bacterial Infections in Otitis Media: Immune Mechanisms and Implications for Therapeutic Interventions.
articles.abstract: Otitis media (OM) is a highly prevalent inflammatory disease of the human middle ear and a key contributor to poor health outcomes in young children on a global scale. While bacterial pathogens such as Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and Moraxella catarrhalis are well-recognised contributors to OM, increasing evidence highlights respiratory viruses as critical gatekeepers that predispose the middle ear to bacterial infection. Viral upper respiratory infections initiate mucosal inflammation, disrupt epithelial barrier integrity and mucociliary clearance, and alter host immunological responses. Collectively, these changes create a permissive environment for bacterial colonization, ascension, and persistence within the middle ear. Viral and bacterial coinfections are commonly found and are linked to poorer clinical outcomes, extended inflammation, and increased disease severity. This review synthesises current evidence on the mechanisms by which viruses prime the middle ear for subsequent bacterial infections, with particular emphasis on epithelial dysfunction, receptor modulation, interferon-driven immune responses, and alterations in innate immune training. Furthermore, it discusses the translational implications of viral-bacterial interactions for the development of improved diagnostic, therapeutic, and preventive strategies, including antivirals and vaccines, in the context of polymicrobial disease dynamics. A clear understanding of these interactions is crucial for advancing improved interventions to lower the global burden of OM.

articles.title: Recent Progresses in Immune Cell Therapy for Tuberculosis.
articles.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a leading cause of global mortality. Its prevention and control face major challenges, including a large latent infection reservoir, high transmissibility, complex treatment protocols, rising drug-resistant TB (notably multidrug-resistant TB, MDR-TB), and comorbidities. MDR-TB has severely undermined conventional pharmacotherapy, with suboptimal global treatment success rates. Thus, novel strategies are urgently needed to accelerate elimination of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and shorten treatment duration. Immune cell-based therapies, acting through multiple targeted mechanisms, align well with the complex demands of TB treatment. When integrated with advanced technologies such as genetic engineering and nanotechnology, immunotherapy holds substantial promise for developing novel regimens. This review systematically delineates major immune cell types involved and their mechanisms of action, critically assesses current technical bottlenecks, and explores future innovative directions. It also critically evaluates recent encouraging clinical trials in TB immunotherapy. Collectively, these efforts aim to establish a robust theoretical and practical translational framework, overcome existing limitations, accelerate clinical translation of immune cell-based therapies, provide new options for patients, and advance the field toward personalized and precision medicine.

articles.title: The game-theoretical analysis of multiple Nash equilibria of a cholera epidemic model with non-exponential distributions.
articles.abstract: Cholera continues to persist in regions characterized by inadequate sanitation and poverty, where vaccination and clean water are recommended as primary preventive measures. This study aims to determine the utility maximizing action for individuals in the absence of government intervention, particularly when the age of infection follows some general distributions, including Exponential, Gamma, and Weibull distributions. To this end, we develop a game-theoretical cholera transmission model incorporating age-structure. In this model, individuals evaluate the associated benefits and infection risks to determine whether to vaccinate or use clean water, thereby establishing a payoff function. The findings reveal that imperfect vaccine efficacy results in the existence of multiple Nash equilibria, and the conditions for these equilibria vary depending on the distribution. Numerical simulations further indicate that, under the same mean, smaller variance necessitates higher vaccine efficacy to enable the occurrence of multiple Nash equilibria. Additionally, we examine how relative costs influence strategy selection when both vaccination and clean water are used simultaneously. The results infer that, due to the relatively high cost of clean water, individuals are more inclined to choose vaccination.

articles.title: Interhemispheric structural connectivity alterations and hierarchical connectome gradient reorganization following SARS-CoV-2 infection.
articles.abstract: Neurological sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection extend beyond the acute phase, yet the structural basis of network-level brain changes across disease severity remains poorly understood. We investigated structural brain connectivity and connectome gradient organization in adults with polymerase chain reaction-confirmed coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), stratified into non-hospitalized and hospitalized groups, alongside a comparison group with non-COVID respiratory infection, using 3T diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging. Network-Based Statistics was used to identify subnetworks of altered structural connectivity, and connectome gradients were derived separately for each hemisphere using diffusion map embedding and compared across groups within seven canonical resting-state networks. Network-Based Statistics identified a predominantly interhemispheric subnetwork differing across the three groups, linking left-hemispheric control and salience regions to right hemisphere sensory and association areas, with a related subnetwork distinguishing hospitalized participants from the comparison group. Connectome gradient analysis revealed group-related differences in connectivity-derived embedding positions within sensorimotor and dorsal attention networks, more pronounced among hospitalized participants. These findings suggest that SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with severity-related interhemispheric structural connectivity differences and altered hierarchical connectome organization, particularly within sensorimotor and dorsal attentional systems. Given the cross-sectional design, modest sample size, and absence of behavioral data, these findings should be considered exploratory and do not establish anatomical fiber loss, causal mechanisms, or predictive clinical value; instead, they provide a structural framework to guide future studies of neurological outcomes after COVID-19.

articles.title: Mechanism by which metformin alleviates neuralgia in the spinal cord of diabetic rats.
articles.abstract: Painful diabetic neuropathy (PDN) is a common chronic complication of diabetes mellitus (DM). Metformin is a widely used hypoglycemic drug that exerts anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects. In the present study, we revealed that metformin attenuates mechanical allodynia through the AMPK pathway in the spinal cord of DM rats. Metformin intervention significantly elevated the levels of phosphorylated-AMPK (p-AMPK, the activated form of AMPK) in the L4-6 spinal dorsal horn (SDH) of DM rats. In addition, the inhibition of AMPK activation by Compound C clearly blocked metformin-mediated analgesia. Moreover, AICAR treatment significantly attenuated mechanical allodynia. Additionally, AMPK activation was observed in both neurons and glial cells. Interestingly, metformin intervention reduced the activation levels of microglia and astrocytes in the L4-6 SDH of DM rats, which suggests that AMPK plays a complicated role at the cellular level in the spinal cord. In conclusion, metformin alleviates diabetic mechanical allodynia by activating AMPK signaling in the L4-6 SDH of DM rats, and inhibits microglial and astrocytic activation. These findings support the potential use of metformin in the clinical treatment of PDN.

articles.title: Additively Manufactured Titanium Implants and Customised Meshes: Clinical Evidence in Implant Dentistry, Bone Regeneration and Maxillofacial Rehabilitation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To critically evaluate human clinical evidence on additively manufactured (AM) titanium implants and other devices used in oral and maxillofacial rehabilitation and guided bone regeneration (GBR), focusing on clinical outcomes, complications and long-term predictability.

DATA: Original human clinical investigations involving AM titanium endosseous implants, root-analogue implants, subperiosteal and maxillofacial implants, and customised titanium meshes were eligible, including randomised controlled trials, prospective and retrospective studies, case series and case reports. Studies without clinical outcomes, animal and laboratory investigations, technical reports and reviews were excluded from the primary clinical synthesis.

SOURCES: A structured, indication-specific literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE for studies available up to 22 October 2026, combining terms related to AM, implant design, clinical applications and outcomes. Additional publications were identified through publisher platforms and backward and forward citation tracking.

STUDY SELECTION: Conventional AM endosseous implants demonstrated favourable short- and medium-term outcomes, with survival rates ranging from 94.5% to 100% across selected clinical cohorts. Root-analogue implants showed promising results in anatomically selected patients, although evidence remains limited. Patient-specific subperiosteal and maxillofacial devices enabled rehabilitation in challenging anatomical conditions, but long-term complications, particularly mucosal exposure, infection and reintervention, remained significant concerns. Customised titanium meshes achieved clinically meaningful bone augmentation, although randomised trials demonstrated no consistent superiority over established barriers. Methodological heterogeneity and limited long-term follow-up restricted comparative interpretation.

CONCLUSIONS: AM titanium represents a promising and clinically viable technology, with particularly encouraging evidence supporting conventional endosseous implants. Patient-specific applications expand therapeutic possibilities in complex clinical situations, although controlled long-term investigations are required to establish their predictability and comparative effectiveness.

CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: AM titanium devices offer valuable opportunities for implant rehabilitation, patient-specific reconstruction and guided bone regeneration. Their clinical use should be guided by indication-specific evidence, biological risks, long-term maintenance needs and patient-centred outcomes rather than manufacturing innovation alone.

articles.title: Neutrophil Extracellular Traps Orchestrate Diabetic Podocytopathy Through ROS/NLRP3/Pyroptotic Axis and Gut-Kidney Microbiota Crosstalk.
articles.abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a common microvascular complication of diabetes mellitus (DM). Emerging evidence indicates that neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) contribute significantly to podocyte injury in DN:however, the specific underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study demonstrates that NET biomarkers are elevated in diabetic mice and patients with diabetes and positively correlate with DN severity. Treatment with deoxyribonuclease Ⅰ (DNase I), which degrades NETs, partially prevented podocyte dysfunction and renal injury. Mechanistically, NET formation triggered excessive generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), activating the nuclear factor-κB ( NF-κB) signaling pathway and NOD-like receptor protein 3 ( NLRP3) inflammasome, thereby inducing podocyte pyroptosis. Furthermore, increased gut microbiota dysbiosis,characterized by decreased probiotic diversity and increased pathogenic bacteria, was observed in DN mice. DNase I treatment restored probiotic diversity, highlighting a potential interaction between NETs and gut microbiota in DN progression. Collectively, our findings suggest that NETs critically mediate diabetic podocyte dysfunction through ROS-induced activation of NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated pyroptosis and gut microbiota dysbiosis, underscoring the therapeutic potential of targeting NETs in DN treatment.

articles.title: From NAD+ elevation to clinical benefit: tissue-specific regulation and translational barriers in aging and age-related disease.
articles.abstract: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) decline has been implicated in aging and age-related disease, and precursor supplementation with nicotinamide riboside (NR) or nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) has shown efficacy in preclinical models. Human trials, however, have produced inconsistent functional outcomes, and the sources of this translational gap remain poorly defined. We combined a bibliometric analysis of 3,271 aging-focused NAD+ publications (2004-2025) with a critical synthesis of mechanistic and clinical evidence to localize where and why preclinical findings fail to translate. The bibliometric analysis revealed three structural features of the literature: (i) original research articles dominated the corpus, whereas the document-type classification cannot distinguish preclinical experiments from human observational or interventional studies; (ii) research is siloed across disease domains with limited cross-tissue comparison; and (iii) intervention-oriented keywords (NMN, NR, supplementation, drug delivery) have outpaced empirical clinical validation. Mechanistic synthesis showed that these structural gaps correspond to biological heterogeneity: NAD+ biosynthesis, consumption, redox balance, and subcellular compartmentalization are tissue- and compartment-specific, such that systemic precursor elevation does not uniformly restore functional NAD+ in disease-relevant tissues. Four subcellular pools-nuclear, cytosolic, mitochondrial, and axonal-each possess distinct rate-limiting bottlenecks, and hepatic metabolic reserve introduces an overlooked source of inter-individual variability. Across neurodegeneration, metabolic disease, cardiovascular aging, and sarcopenia, NAD+ dysregulation follows disease-specific mechanisms rather than a universal decline phenotype. We propose a precision-medicine framework that shifts the core question from whether NAD+ can be elevated to whether a defined intervention corrects a specific NAD+ defect in the appropriate tissue and subcellular compartment. This framework provides a structured basis for designing next-generation NAD+-targeted trials with tissue-specific biomarkers and function-oriented endpoints.

articles.title: RESPONSE-ADAPTIVE STEREOTACTIC BODY RADIOTHERAPY BOOST AFTER CONCURRENT CHEMORADIOTHERAPY IN UNRESECTABLE STAGE III NSCLC: A PROSPECTIVE SINGLE-CENTRE COHORT STUDY.
articles.journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to escalate the dose to the residual primary tumor with an adaptive stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) boost after concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CRT) in unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and to explore, within this cohort, whether a higher cumulative dose to the residual primary was associated with better locoregional control (LRC) and whether this translated into a difference in overall survival (OS).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this single-center, prospective, single-arm cohort, 51 patients received concurrent CRT (50 Gy/25 fractions with weekly carboplatin and paclitaxel) followed by an adaptive boost (30 Gy/5 fractions to the residual primary, 10 Gy/5 fractions to residual nodes), without consolidation durvalumab. Doses were summed by deformable registration and reported as EQD2. Response was assessed at 3 months with FDG-PET/CT (PERCIST), and toxicity with CTCAE v5.0. Outcomes estimated by Kaplan-Meier; predictors by Cox regression.

RESULTS: At a median follow-up of 26 months, 2-year OS and LRC were 61.5% and 62.8%. The median PFS and DMFS were 13 and 16 months, and distant metastasis was the dominant failure pattern (41.2%). Cumulative dose below 94.77 Gy (EQD2) to the residual primary independently predicted worse LRC (HR 5.86), and a 3-month locoregional SUVmax ≥4.55 predicted worse LRC (HR 5.04). OS was independently associated with residual nodal volume, 3-month metabolic progression, and subsequent locoregional progression. Grade 3-4 pneumonitis occurred in 7.8%, grade 3 esophagitis in one patient (2%), and hemoptysis in five (9.8%).

CONCLUSION: The SBRT boost achieved encouraging locoregional control, including in bulky and node-advanced disease, without immunotherapy, and higher cumulative dose to the residual primary was associated with better locoregional control. Hemoptysis was the main safety concern and occurred predominantly in patients with pre-existing hemoptysis, supporting careful selection and strict bronchial constraints. Local escalation alone did not overcome the competing risk of distant failure.

articles.title: Comprehensive vaccination guidelines for patients with inborn errors of immunity: A European Society for Immunodeficiencies Consensus.
authors: European Society for Immunodeficiencies Clinical Working Party
articles.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inborn errors of immunity (IEI) encompass over 550 subtypes characterized by impaired immune responses. Individuals with IEI may exhibit suboptimal vaccination immune responses, and some risk severe adverse events following live attenuated vaccines. The International Union of Immunological Societies (IUIS) categorizes IEIs into 10 groups based on most consistently reported phenotypes. Previous vaccination recommendations lack IEI subtype-specific guidance aligned with IUIS classification, limiting clinical utility in daily practice.

OBJECTIVE: To develop comprehensive, tailored vaccination recommendations for distinct IEI subgroups based on specific immune defects, vaccine types, therapeutic regimens, and exposure risks.

METHODS: An expert panel collaborated with the European Society for Immunodeficiencies (ESID) Clinical Working Party to develop evidence-based guidelines, with consensus defined as ≥75% expert agreement on contested recommendations. The guidelines incorporate the IUIS 2024 classification and address individual risk assessment based on IEI subtype, vaccine type, and treatment regimen.

RESULTS: Non-live vaccines are safe for all IEI patients but provide varying protection depending on the underlying disorder. Live attenuated vaccines are contraindicated in many IEI subtypes, though individual assessment may permit exceptions. Influenza and pneumococcal vaccines are strongly recommended given patients' respiratory infections vulnerability. Novel recommendations include tick-borne encephalitis and SARS-CoV-2 vaccines, treatment-specific approaches, and travel advice.

CONCLUSION: These ESID guidelines provide IEI subtype-specific vaccination recommendations, enabling personalized approaches that optimize protection while minimizing adverse event risks.

articles.title: From mortality association to attributable deaths in multidrug-resistant neonatal sepsis.
Prognostic Value of Late Gadolinium Enhancement in Non-Ischemic Dilated Cardiomyopathy: A Prospective Observational Study from India.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (NIDCM) represents a significant cause of heart failure and sudden cardiac death (SCD). Current risk stratification relies heavily on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), which has limitations in predicting adverse outcomes. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) on cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging may provide additional prognostic information.

METHODS: This prospective observational study enrolled 88 consecutive NIDCM patients who underwent CMR imaging at our institution. Patients were followed for a minimum of 6 months and thereafter until a common study closure date, giving a mean follow-up of 337±173 days. The primary endpoint was a composite of major adverse cardiac events (MACE), defined as sudden cardiac death, heart failure death, aborted sudden cardiac death, sustained ventricular tachycardia, and heart failure hospitalization.

RESULTS: LGE was present in 44 patients (50%). The most common pattern was mid-myocardial enhancement (40.9%), followed by a combination of patterns (25.0%) and transmural enhancement (22.7%); the interventricular septum was the most frequently involved segment (81.8%). MACE occurred in 22.7% of LGE-positive patients versus 13.6% of LGE-negative patients. ROC curve analysis identified LGE extent >26% of LV volume as the optimal threshold for predicting MACE (sensitivity 70%, specificity 73.5%, AUC 0.75). Patients with LGE >26% had significantly higher event rates (43.7% vs 10.7%; unadjusted OR 6.48, 95% CI 1.45-28.9; p=0.02).

CONCLUSIONS: Greater LGE extent was associated with adverse cardiac events in NIDCM patients. CMR-based risk stratification may help identify high-risk patients who could benefit from ICD, but external validation in larger cohorts is required before using this threshold clinically.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of the dual SGLT1 and SGLT2 inhibitor JP-2266 in Type 2 Diabetes: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 study (Diabetes Metab J, published online July 29, 2026).
Surgical outcomes of infective endocarditis in children and adults with congenital heart disease.
articles.journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Reports describing surgery for infective endocarditis (IE) in children and adults with congenital heart disease (CHD) are limited. This study aimed to determine the patient characteristics, preoperative conditions, surgical outcomes, and risk factors in this cohort.

METHODS: All children and adults with CHD who underwent surgical treatment for IE between 2001 and 2024 were reviewed. Patient characteristics and surgical procedures were evaluated; survival, recurrent IE, and risk factors were analyzed.

RESULTS: A total of 96 patients underwent surgical treatment for IE, including 52 children and 44 adults with CHD. Underlying CHD included ventricular septal defect in 31 patients, aortic stenosis/insufficiency in 26, and tetralogy of Fallot in 14. The most frequently infected lesion was the aortic valve in 40 patients, and the most frequently detected organism was Staphylococcus species in 34 patients. Vegetation was observed in 65 patients. Median age at surgery was 17.2 (IQR: 11.7-29.4) years. In-hospital mortality was 6.3%, and survival at 5, 10, and 20 years was 90.6, 88.1, and 80.5%, respectively. Freedom from recurrent IE was 96.4% at 20 years. Number of previous operations (hazard ratio (HR): 1.585, p=0.005), gram-negative bacteria (HR: 11.475, p<0.001), emergency operations (HR: 17.988, p=0.001), and longer aortic cross-clamp time (HR: 1.011, p=0.043) were risk factors for mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: In children and adults with CHD, mortality following surgery for IE was low, and recurrent IE was rare. Individualized management based on the patient's preoperative condition and the causative organism appears to be important for improving survival.

articles.title: Aortic Root Abscess in Infective Endocarditis: Prognostic Impact and Outcomes of Patch Repair.
articles.journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Due to discrepancies between guidelines and expert consensus, we examined the perioperative and mid-term outcomes of aortic root abscesses to determine their prognostic significance and optimal surgical management.

METHODS: We completed a single-center retrospective study of patients surgically treated for aortic valve infective endocarditis (AV IE) from 2019 to 2024. We compared outcomes in patients with and without root abscess, and among abscess cases, between patch repair and extended surgery (root reconstruction or replacement). The primary outcome was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE, composite of all-cause death, heart failure (HF) readmission, and stroke). Outcomes were analyzed using Kaplan Meier estimators and Cox proportional hazards.

RESULTS: Among 158 patients (57% with abscess) with a median follow-up of 1.22 years (IQR 0.13-2.53), root abscesses were associated with increased MACCE (adjusted HR 3.15 (1.51-6.59), p=0.002) and HF readmission (SHR 4.54 (1.55-13.30), p=0.006). In patients with aortic root abscess, 62 underwent patch repair and 21 underwent extended surgery. Patch repair was associated with decreased MACCE (adjusted HR 0.34 (0.15-0.74), p=0.006), all-cause mortality (p=0.002), and death at 30 days (13% vs 33%, p=0.035) compared to extended surgery.

CONCLUSIONS: Aortic root abscess was associated with increased MACCE and HF readmissions compared to AV IE without abscess, identifying root abscess as a marker of adverse prognosis and supporting prompt recognition and referral in aortic valve endocarditis. Patch repair for aortic root abscesses is a safe and reasonable approach in patients with suitable anatomy compared to more extensive surgery.

articles.title: Preventive Tirofiban for Early Neurological Deterioration in Acute Ischemic Stroke Without Thrombolysis or Thrombectomy.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: We assessed whether preventive intravenous tirofiban reduces early neurological deterioration (END) in acute ischemic stroke without thrombolysis or thrombectomy, and how population, timing and comparator differences affect interpretation.

METHODS: A focused evidence update included PubMed searching through October 13, 2026, screening of 520 records and citation checks. Randomized and observational evidence were separated. Risk ratios (RRs) were analyzed using restricted maximum-likelihood models, with fixed-effect, Hartung-Knapp, prediction-interval and influence analyses. Abstract-level evidence was evaluated separately where eligibility was uncertain.

RESULTS: Two randomized trials (1,395 participants) yielded discordant END estimates: RR 0.50 (95% CI 0.32-0.77) and 0.91 (0.67-1.22). The exploratory pooled RR was 0.69 (0.38-1.24; I²=79.6%; τ²=0.143), with marked model dependence. Four trials contributed 2,017 observed 90-day modified Rankin Scale 0-1 outcomes: RR 1.12 (1.05-1.19); modified Hartung-Knapp CI 1.01-1.23 and prediction interval 0.98-1.28. Excluding ESCAPIST because of discrepant published counts widened the modified Hartung-Knapp interval to 0.96-1.27. Separately, the BRANT abstract reported RR 1.01 (0.90-1.13); target-population eligibility was unconfirmed. Treatment-by-time interactions and mediation of functional benefit through END prevention were not established.

CONCLUSIONS: Preventive END effects are trial-specific. The functional signal is sensitive to source and model assumptions and does not establish END-mediated benefit. Imaging-guided selection and incremental benefit over optimized oral therapy require direct randomized evaluation, with standardized neurological, functional and bleeding outcomes.

articles.title: Comparing the magnitude of change in memory function following telehealth versus in-person delivery of a group memory skills intervention for survivors of stroke.
articles.abstract: Telehealth could potentially improve memory rehabilitation access post-stroke, but its suitability is underexplored. We aimed to characterize changes in stroke survivors' memory function and memory strategy use after completing a compensatory memory skills group intervention via telehealth, compared to in-person. Our retrospective study drew upon two previous parent studies, and examined change in memory goal attainment, everyday memory failures, and memory strategy use at program completion (T1) and follow-up (T2), relative to baseline. Non-inferiority analyses then compared change among in-person (n = 24) and telehealth (n = 30) participants. Among telehealth participants, repeated-measures ANCOVAs indicated goal attainment at T1 (p < .001, d = 1.08) and T2 (p < .001, d = 1.33), and reduced memory failures by T2 (p = .011, d = -0.58). Internal strategy use increased by T1 (p < .001, d = 0.89) and T2 (p = .003, d = 0.68), but external strategy use did not (pT1 = .079, dT1 = 0.43; pT2 = .319, dT2 = 0.25). While these findings were promising, non-inferiority analyses comparing telehealth and in-person delivery were inconclusive. Further research directly comparing delivery modalities is therefore needed. Offering participants their preferred intervention format in future trials may help further our understanding of how stroke survivors might maximally benefit from memory rehabilitation.

articles.title: Use of Biologics and Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors During Pregnancy in Patients with Systemic Autoimmune Diseases and Cancer.
articles.abstract: Biologics and immune checkpoint inhibitors have transformed the treatment of autoimmune conditions and cancers. However, safety data regarding use during pregnancy are limited. Clinicians are left to weigh the potential benefits of treatment with frequently unknown risks to the pregnant patient and developing fetus. These therapies do not cross the placenta during the first trimester; thus, they are unlikely to cause teratogenicity. Use later in pregnancy has the potential to immunosuppress the neonate, which could lead to infection and inadequate vaccine response. These large molecules are minimally transferred into breastmilk and are mostly compatible with nursing.

articles.title: What's Coming Up Next? The Physiology of Gastroparesis and GLP-1 Agonists.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) is an incretin to regulate glycemia, activates peripheral and central neural pathways to control appetite, and inhibits upper gut transit to reduce food intake. Peptide and nonpeptide GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), as well as a combined GLP-1 and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), agonist are approved for type 2 diabetes, weight reduction, and other indications. GLP-1RA therapy can be complicated by upper gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms, including nausea and vomiting. Delayed gastric emptying secondary to GLP-1RAs may be influenced by drug pharmacokinetics, associated neuropathy, and development of tachyphylaxis with repeated dosing. A theoretical risk of pulmonary aspiration from retained gastric contents is concerning for patients undergoing anesthesia before endoscopy or surgery. Managing upper GI complications of GLP-1RA therapy includes diet modifications, antiemetic medications, and treatments that stimulate gastric emptying. Newer agents in testing include nonpeptide GLP-1RAs and GLP-1RAs acting in concert with GIP, glucagon, or other receptor-mediated pathways.

articles.title: Differential Regulatory Activities of Potassium and Aldosterone in the Distal Nephron: A Resolution to the Aldosterone Paradox.
articles.abstract: Aldosterone has long been viewed as a master regulator of fluid and electrolyte homeostasis, acting through the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) to stimulate electrogenic Na+ transport via the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) in the distal nephron. This primary effect is thought to drive both K+ secretion and Cl- reabsorption; however, the underlying mechanism has remained obscure and the dual regulation has generated an enigma often referred to as the aldosterone paradox. Here we propose a model for regulated K+ secretion centered on local regulation of ENaC in the late distal convoluted tubule and early connecting tubule. In this segment, the MR is constitutively activated by glucocorticoids rather than by aldosterone, and yet ENaC activity and K+ secretion through the renal outer medullary K+ channel (ROMK) are not constitutive but, rather, are highly regulated. The model holds that the key regulatory step for K+ secretion involves a cell-autonomous mechanism through which local interstitial [K+] stimulates mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2)-dependent phosphorylation of the ENaC regulatory serum- and glucocorticoid-induced kinase 1 (SGK1); the K+-sensing kinase augments this phosphorylation by serving as a scaffold to enhance the physical interaction of mTORC2 with SGK1. Aldosterone acts further downstream to stimulate ENaC primarily in the late CNT and cortical collecting duct, in which ROMK apical expression is relatively low and Na+-Cl- reabsorption is favored. This revised paradigm resolves the aldosterone paradox and has important implications for hypertension, potassium disorders, and potentially medical therapies.

articles.title: Community health worker-led home blood pressure monitoring in rural sub-Saharan Africa: a diagnostic accuracy study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Home blood pressure monitoring (HBPM) coordinated by community health workers (CHWs) is a potential strategy to improve hypertension detection in sub-Saharan Africa, yet data on its diagnostic performance in this setting are scarce. We aimed to determine the diagnostic accuracy of CHW-coordinated HBPM in Kenya and The Gambia using daytime ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) as the reference standard.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study, we recruited a random sample of representative age-stratified individuals aged 30 years or older from the general population of two health and demographic surveillance systems in Kilifi, Kenya, and Kiang West, The Gambia. We used the latest enumeration lists of the two health and demographic surveillance systems as sampling frames and performed computer-generated random sampling within five predefined age strata (30-39 years, 40-49 years, 50-59 years, 60-69 years, and ≥70 years). Pregnant women were excluded, and participants were eligible to participate irrespective of previous hypertension status. CHWs trained and provided participants with HBPM devices for self-measurement of blood pressure twice a day, for a minimum of 3 days and a maximum of 7 days. For the reference standard measurement, an ABPM device was fitted by CHWs, and ambulatory blood pressure was measured every 15 min during the day and 30 min at night. We used blood pressure cutoffs derived from the European Society of Hypertension to determine the age-standardised measures of accuracy (sensitivities, specificities, positive predictive values [PPVs] and negative predictive values [NPVs], positive likelihood ratios [LR+] and negative likelihood ratios [LR-] and area under receiver operating characteristic curves) of HBPM among participants who had valid HBPM and ABPM measurements.

FINDINGS: Between Aug 18, 2023, and Dec 13, 2024, from 1452 eligible participants, we included 1279 participants with valid HBPM and ABPM measurements (696 in Kenya and 583 in The Gambia). In 1279 participants, the median age was 54 years (IQR 43-66), 805 (62·9%) were women, and 474 (37·1%) were men. The age-standardised prevalence of hypertension on daytime ABPM was 23·1% (95% CI 19·9-26·2) in Kenya and 27·1% (23·6-30·6) in The Gambia while the respective prevalences on HBPM were 32·5% (29·1-35·8) and 31·2% (27·5-34·9). The age-standardised sensitivities and specificities of HBPM were 82·6% (76·2-89·0) and 82·4% (79·0-85·7) in Kenya and 68·7% (61·3-76·1) and 83·5% (79·7-87·2) in The Gambia. The age-standardised PPVs and NPVs were 58·6% (52·0-65·2) and 94·0% (91·6-96·4) in Kenya and 59·9% (52·5-67·2) and 88·1% (84·8-91·4) in The Gambia, respectively. The age-standardised LR+ and LR- were 4·68 (3·67-5·69) and 0·21 (0·13-0·29) in Kenya and 4·15 (3·09-5·21) and 0·37 (0·28-0·46) in The Gambia, respectively. In both countries, the area under receiver operating characteristic curve for HBPM was above 75%.

INTERPRETATION: HBPM showed moderate-to-high sensitivity and high specificity for detecting hypertension in two rural sub-Saharan African communities. HBPM represents a promising alternative for increasing hypertension awareness in rural sub-Saharan Africa.

FUNDING: The UK National Institute for Health and Care Research, the UK Medical Research Council, and the Wellcome Trust.

articles.title: Post-exercise hypotension is greater after dynamic resistance than isometric exercise.
articles.abstract: Post-exercise hypotension (PEH) is a clinically relevant response to acute exercise and a predictor of blood pressure (BP) adaptations to chronic training. Although both dynamic and isometric resistance exercise (RE) are effective complementary strategies for BP management, their comparative effects on PEH remain unclear. This study (i) compared PEH following dynamic-and isometric-RE matched for exercise characteristics and total workload, and (ii) examined systemic hemodynamics and autonomic function during exercise, as cardiovascular perturbations may influence PEH magnitude. In a crossover-design, ten normotensive-young men completed: dynamic-RE and isometric-RE on bilateral-leg-press (2-min×4-sets, 30% of MVC, with equivalent workload), and non-exercise control. BP was measured at rest and for 90 minutes post-intervention. Systemic hemodynamics and baroreceptor sensitivity (BRS) were assessed during RE. Dynamic-RE elicited significant PEH (approximately -8mmHg) versus isometric-RE and control (p<0.05-0.01), with reductions in systolic-, diastolic-, and mean-BP evident from 40 to 90 min post-exercise. Isometric-RE did not induce PEH. Dynamic-RE produced greater cardiovascular/autonomic responses, including higher heart-rate, stroke-volume, cardiac-output alongside larger reductions in total-peripheral-resistance and BRS. In conclusion, when matched for exercise characteristics, dynamic but not isometric-RE induced a PEH effect. The PEH effect of dynamic-RE may, in part, be related to its larger cardiovascular/autonomic perturbations, potentially promoting greater postexercise vasodilation.

articles.title: Identification and regulation of an ACC1-associated lipogenic metabolon in liver.
articles.abstract: De novo lipogenesis (DNL) plays a pathogenic role in triglyceride (TG) accumulation in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Strategies to reduce hepatic steatosis focus on inhibiting enzymes involved in DNL and TG synthesis. Here, we identify a nutrient-responsive, post-translational regulatory mechanism that enhances DNL in mouse liver models and primary rat hepatocytes. Under anabolic conditions, ACC1 interacts with multiple enzymes in the DNL and TG synthesis pathway, supporting the formation of an ACC1-associated lipogenic metabolon. Immunofluorescence and electron microscopy (EM) reveal that ACC1 and associated lipogenic proteins are enriched in lipid droplet (LD)-associated and mitochondria-LD interface regions. In steatotic livers, ACC1-associated lipogenic protein interactions are increased, consistent with enhanced hepatic lipogenesis in MASLD. These studies identify a post-translational mechanism that promotes the spatial coordination of lipogenic enzymes and facilitates substrate channeling to enhance TG synthesis. Disruption of this lipogenic metabolon may provide a therapeutic approach for treatment of MASLD.

articles.title: Managing Abnormal Uterine Bleeding During Anticoagulant Therapy in Clinical Practice.
articles.abstract: Anticoagulant therapies, including heparins, vitamin K antagonists, and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) such as rivaroxaban, apixaban and dabigatran, are crucial for the treatment and the prevention of venous thromboembolism (VTE). While DOACs offer improved safety profiles, their use, espe-cially in women of reproductive age, increases the risk of abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB), partic-ularly heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB). HMB, defined as blood loss exceeding 80 mL per cycle or causing significant life disruption, is associated with reduced quality of life and substantial economic costs. Women on anticoagulants report higher incidences of HMB, often requiring adjustments in therapy or additional interventions. Management strategies include the referral for a gynecological consultation, the adjustment of hormonal therapy and anticoagulant treatment, the administration of tranexamic acid, and the treatment of iron deficiency. The review underscores the importance of a comprehensive, personalized approach to managing AUB in women on anticoagulants to optimize both anticoagulation effectiveness and patient quality of life.

articles.title: Temporal trend and geographic variation in anticoagulation of patients hospitalized with acute pulmonary embolism: the RIETE registry 2013-2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A recent U.S. study of initial anticoagulation in adults with acute pulmonary embolism (PE) requiring hospitalization found intravenous unfractionated heparin (UFH) use exceeded 50%. Guidelines, however, recommend low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) over UFH for most patients requiring parenteral anticoagulation. Use patterns in other geographic regions are unclear.

METHODS: We analyzed data from RIETE, a prospective multinational registry of consecutive patients with venous thromboembolism. We included adults hospitalized for acute PE from 2013 through 2024 in 273 hospitals across 31 countries. We assessed temporal trend and regional variation in initial anticoagulation. Using multivariable regression, we identified variables independently associated with UFH.

RESULTS: Among 36,210 adults, 83.2% received subcutaneous LMWH, 7.1% UFH, and 6.8% direct oral anticoagulants. LMWH use decreased slightly from 2013 to 2024 (85.8% to 79.2%; unadjusted), while UFH increased (8.9% to 10.4%). Wide geographic variation was observed in overall use of LMWH (37%--95%) and UFH (2%--39%). When adjusted for demographic and clinical covariates, increased weight, recent surgery, recent major bleeding, severe anemia, thrombocytopenia, severe renal dysfunction, abnormal vital signs, and early reperfusion therapy were positively associated, whereas age >80 years, active cancer, chronic lung disease, prior ischemic stroke, and year were negatively associated with UFH. Compared with Spanish hospitals, hospitals in other European countries, the United States, and Asia were independently associated with UFH use.

CONCLUSIONS: Results highlight opportunities for some geographic regions to align anticoagulation practices more closely with evidence-based guidelines recommending LMWH as the preferred parenteral agent in most patients with PE requiring hospitalization.

articles.title: Welcome to Seminars in Thrombosis & Hemostasis 2027.
Predicting Inactive Disease in Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis: A Dynamic Machine Learning Approach.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal management of juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) remains challenging. The ability to predict disease progression in JIA can improve personalized treatment decisions, but few reliable predictors have been identified.

METHODS: Using data from the Childhood Arthritis and Rheumatology Research Alliance (CARRA) Registry (years 2015-2024), we developed machine learning models to predict attainment of inactive disease in children with non-systemic JIA. We compared three structurally distinct algorithms: Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBN), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). Using a dynamic approach, the models predicted at each timepoint whether a child would attain inactive disease approximately six months later, based on the preceding 12 months of data (demographic, clinical, and medication variables), with predictions updated as new visits accrued.

RESULTS: A total of 8,093 participants were included. On an independent test cohort, all 3 models achieved comparable discrimination (AUC 0.76-0.79). Predicted probabilities were well-calibrated (Expected Calibration Error ≤0.03). Disease activity levels in the preceding 12 months, presence of enthesitis and uveitis were the strongest predictors. The dependency structure learned by the DBN indicated that treatment decisions were primarily reactive to disease activity and shaped by JIA category and step-therapy requirements.

CONCLUSIONS: Machine learning approaches can predict attainment of inactive disease over time with moderate discriminative performance, offering potential to support early identification of children with JIA at risk for unfavorable outcomes. The suboptimal care patterns and systems-level barriers identified through our analyses highlight priority targets for quality improvement initiatives and policy interventions to reduce gaps in JIA care.

articles.title: Clinical predictors of lateral meniscal hypermobility and development of the Hypermobile Lateral Meniscus Syndrome Score.
articles.journal: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA
articles.abstract:
