PURPOSE: To identify independent preoperative predictors of arthroscopically confirmed lateral meniscal hypermobility and to develop and internally validate the Hypermobile Lateral Meniscus Syndrome Score (HLMSS).

METHODS: A retrospective diagnostic prediction model study included 482 patients undergoing knee arthroscopy: 156 with lateral meniscal hypermobility, 171 with structural lateral meniscal tears without hypermobility and 155 arthroscopic controls. Lateral meniscal hypermobility was defined arthroscopically as reproducible anterior translation of the posterior horn beyond the midpoint (>50%) of the lateral tibial plateau. Preoperative clinical and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) variables were evaluated as candidate predictors. Independent predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression, and the HLMSS was derived from regression coefficients. Internal validation was performed using 1000 bootstrap resamples. Discrimination, calibration and clinical utility were assessed.

RESULTS: The cohort included 482 patients (mean age, 31.8 ± 9.4 years; 62.4% male). Mean age was 28.9 ± 8.1 years in the hypermobility group, 34.7 ± 10.2 years in the structural tear group, and 31.8 ± 8.7 years in controls; 64.7%, 60.8% and 61.9% were male, respectively. Independent predictors of lateral meniscal hypermobility were intermittent locking (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 4.78), hyperflexion pain (aOR, 4.21), rotational instability sensation (aOR, 3.74), posterolateral pain (aOR, 3.12) and popliteomeniscal fascicle abnormality on MRI (aOR, 2.68). The HLMSS demonstrated an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.91 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.88-0.94) and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.89. At ≥7 points, sensitivity was 86.5% and specificity was 84.8%. In the restricted comparison with structural lateral meniscal tears, the AUC was 0.84 (95% CI, 0.80-0.88).

CONCLUSION: The HLMSS demonstrated good to excellent discrimination for identifying arthroscopically confirmed lateral meniscal hypermobility using preoperative clinical and MRI findings. External validation in consecutive symptomatic populations is required before routine clinical implementation.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, retrospective diagnostic cohort study.

articles.title: Weakening the negative biological activities of recombinant human tumor necrosis factor (hTNF) via immunization with the V91D hTNF derivative induces potent neutralizing antibodies against hTNF in vivo.
articles.abstract: TNF is a critical proinflammatory cytokine involved in both immune responses and autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA). While anti-TNF monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) provide therapeutic benefits for RA, a resultant induction of anti-drug antibodies reduces the treatment efficacy for some RA patients receiving anti-TNF mAbs. In this study, we attempted to overcome this problem by inducing potent neutralizing antibodies in the body via immunization with a TNF derivative that would be biologically less inflammatory - a recombinant human TNF, which is mutant with a valine-to-aspartic acid substitution at position 91 (V91D hTNF). Since immunization with exogenous TNF has the potential to be very harmful for the human body, V91D hTNF was created by replacing the valine at position 91 with aspartic acid. Although the half-maximal concentration (EC50) of V91D hTNF is approximately 10,000 times higher than that of WT hTNF, immunizing mice with V91D hTNF successfully induces anti-TNF Abs with reactivity comparable to those produced by WT hTNF in both soluble and membrane-bound forms. The V91D hTNF Abs neutralize the negative biological activities of WT hTNF both in vitro and in vivo, in a manner similar to that of adalimumab. All mice immunized with V91D hTNF survived in an acute model of hTNF-galactosamine lethal shock. These findings indicate that the rhTNF derivative (V91D hTNF) shows promise for use as a vaccine antigen that will neutralize hTNF and minimize the risk of inflammation posed by WT hTNF. The strategy we propose here could be an alternative antibody-based therapy to treat chronic autoimmune diseases such as RA.

articles.title: Immune-state transition pharmacology in severe infection: From static endotypes to dynamic treatment targets.
articles.abstract: Precision immunotherapy in severe infection has historically targeted static molecular endotypes identified at admission. However, critical illness represents a rapidly moving target where inflammatory tissue damage, myeloid paralysis, lymphocyte depletion, and repair mechanisms evolve asynchronously along divergent trajectories. Consequently, interventions prescribed from an admission snapshot often exert their peak biological effect only after the host's therapeutic priorities have already shifted. Synthesizing contemporary evidence from longitudinal patient cohorts, recent biomarker-guided randomized trials, and critical-illness pharmacokinetics, we introduce an organizing translational framework: immune-state transition pharmacology. Rather than assigning patients to fixed categories, this paradigm treats reproducible, within-patient functional transitions as dynamic therapeutic targets over defined operational intervals. We demonstrate that successful immunomodulation requires decoupling three distinct pharmacological clocks: plasma clearance half-life, receptor occupancy, and functional biological response duration. While prolonged target engagement by long-acting antibodies risks causing fatal immunosuppression during secondary infections, short-acting antagonists provide the temporal agility required to manage fluctuating host states. To operationalize this approach, we outline a pragmatic bedside pathway integrating calibrated serial biomarkers, particularly standardized monocyte human leukocyte antigen-DR, with emerging rapid microfluidics, explicitly accounting for analytical turnaround times and residual drug exposure. We further propose sequential multiple assignment randomized trial designs to rigorously evaluate adaptive decision rules for initiating, switching, or discontinuing immunotherapies based on real-time functional trajectories. Ultimately, by synchronizing therapeutic kinetics with evolving host pathophysiology, immune-state transition pharmacology transforms sepsis management from static snapshot phenotyping into trajectory-matched precision medicine, balancing pathogen eradication with tissue preservation and durable functional recovery.

articles.title: Association between nasogastric tube placement and self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms in patients receiving endovascular thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion: A post-hoc analysis of the ENCHANTED2/MT trial.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-stroke anxiety and depression are common after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for large vessel occlusion (LVO) and impair long-term recovery. Nasogastric tube (NGT) placement marks severe dysphagia and illness, but its association with anxiety or depression remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate whether NGT placement is associated with the presence and severity of 90-day self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms after successful EVT.

METHODS: We performed a post-hoc analysis of the ENCHANTED2/MT multicentre randomized controlled trial, including patients with anterior-circulation LVO who achieved successful reperfusion and had complete 90-day EQ-5D-3 L data. Participants were stratified by in-hospital NGT placement (No-NGT group vs. NGT group). The primary outcome was self-reported anxiety/depression assessed by the EQ-5D-3 L dimension (no, moderate, or extreme symptoms). We explored the association between NGT placement and the proportion and severity of self-reported anxiety/depression using propensity score matching (PSM) and logistic regression, and performed exploratory subgroup analyses.

RESULTS: Of 575 patients, 280(48.7%) received an NGT. Before matching, the proportion reporting self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms was 38.6% in the NGT group versus 15.6% in the no-NGT group (unadjusted OR3.40, 95%CI 2.30-5.09). After adjustment for measured clinical covariates, the association remained significant (adjusted OR2.97, 95%CI 1.93-4.63; ordinal OR3.06, 95%CI 1.99-4.77). After PSM, 175 patients were matched in each group; NGT placement remained associated with higher odds of self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms (37.7% vs 21.1%; OR2.26, 95%CI 1.41-3.65; ordinal OR2.25, 95%CI 1.41-3.63). In exploratory subgroup analyses, the association appeared more pronounced in patients with admission NIHSS ≤ 15 (OR3.83, 95% CI1.82-8.07; P for interaction = 0.049).

CONCLUSION: In this post-hoc analysis, NGT placement was associated with higher odds of self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms.NGT requirement may identify patients who deserve closer psychological assessment.

articles.title: Towards natural behaviour processing for the representation and prediction of digital behaviour.
articles.abstract: Characterising individual differences in behaviour and predicting future behaviour are central goals of psychological science. However, behavioural data are difficult to obtain, and most research relies on nomothetic approaches that aggregate them into summary statistics. This aggregation obscures person-specific patterns that would afford an idiographic understanding of individual behaviour. Pervasive digital technologies (e.g., smartphones, wearables, and computer-mediated systems) now generate fine-grained, temporally ordered records of everyday behaviour, creating unprecedented opportunities to study both systematic inter-individual differences and patterns of intra-individual variation in digital behaviour. Here, we introduce Natural Behaviour Processing (NBP) as a framework for analysing digital behavioural data using sequence modelling approaches adapted from natural language processing. We argue that behaviour shares structural properties with language: both involve a repository of possible actions (vocabulary), systematic patterns governing how elements typically combine (grammar), and context-dependent meaning (semantics). These structural parallels motivate applying sequence-based models, which have revolutionised language processing, to the study of behaviour more broadly. We provide a brief illustrative review of pioneering studies demonstrating that sequential approaches capture person-specific patterns that aggregation loses, across topics including life outcomes, decision making, social media use, consumer behaviour, digital education, and health. We discuss the challenges facing NBP adoption, including the tension between predictive modelling and theoretical understanding, the need for large-scale curated behaviour datasets, and methodological training requirements. By modelling the order and context of everyday actions rather than aggregates, NBP could enable person-specific representations of behaviour that support both individual-level prediction and systematic comparison of individual differences across people.

articles.title: Understanding COVID-19 vaccine concerns among adults with diabetes at federally qualified health centers: a qualitative analysis of open-ended survey responses.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Adults with diabetes mellitus (DM) have higher risks for COVID-19-related morbidity and mortality. This qualitative study analyzed why some adults with DM at federally qualified health centers (FQHCs) declined to receive a COVID-19 vaccine during the COVID-19 pandemic.

METHODS: A COVID-19 outcomes/vaccination uptake survey was administered to adults with type 1 and type 2 DM on insulin therapy at 33 FQHCs from Nov. 2021-Jul. 2022 as part of a larger study. We cross-sectionally and thematically analyzed open-ended responses from participants that explained why they did not receive a COVID-19 vaccine. Responses were coded using the 3 Cs of Vaccine Hesitancy Model (complacency, confidence, and convenience reasons). Responses that did not match the 3 Cs were coded as "other" or "unspecific" reasons for vaccine hesitancy/refusal. Descriptive statistics (n, %, mean, standard deviation [SD]) summarized participant demographics and codes.

RESULTS: Out of 450 survey participants, 80 (17.8%) reported not receiving a COVID-19 vaccine; of those, 67 participants (mean age = 46.6 years [SD ± 15.1], 65.7% female, 49.3% White) reported 80 total reasons for being unvaccinated. Most reflected low confidence (38.8%), such as distrust in vaccines, distrust in the health system and government, and concerns tied to misinformation, or were unspecific (35.0%). Convenience reasons (13.8%) included vaccine inaccessibility, vaccine ineligibility e.g., due to medical contraindications, and dislike of vaccines. Complacency reasons (8.8%) included low perceived susceptibility/threat from COVID-19 and perceived vaccine ineffectiveness. Other reasons (3.8%) included religious beliefs and personal freedom.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that multi-level factors contributed to COVID-19 vaccine hesitancy/refusal among adults with DM at FQHCs. Tailored vaccine education, improved vaccine communications, and multifaceted interventions are needed to address their vaccine concerns.

articles.title: Admission Hyponatremia and its Clinical Correlates in Male Psychiatric Inpatients: A Retrospective Study From Turkey.
articles.journal: International journal of psychiatry in medicine
articles.abstract: ObjectiveHyponatremia is a common electrolyte disturbance in psychiatric patients related to psychogenic polydipsia, psychotropic medications, and medical comorbidities. Data on the prevalence of admission hyponatremia and its independent clinical correlates in psychiatric inpatients remain limited.MethodThis retrospective study included 322 consecutive male psychiatric inpatients hospitalized between June and December 2022. Hyponatremia was defined as serum sodium <135 mEq/L within 24 h of admission. Sociodemographic, clinical, and laboratory data were extracted from electronic medical records. Age and disease duration were entered into a Firth penalized logistic regression model. Sensitivity analyses used alternative sodium cut-offs (<134 and <136 mEq/L), glucose-corrected sodium, and continuous sodium.ResultsHyponatremia was identified in 15 patients (4.7%, 95% CI 2.8-7.5%). Older age, longer disease duration, and a greater number of psychiatric hospitalizations were associated with hyponatremia in univariable analyses. After adjustment for age, disease duration remained associated with hyponatremia (OR = 1.07 per year, 95% CI = 1.02-1.14, P = .006), with similar estimates across alternative sodium cut-off values, but was not associated with continuous sodium. Diabetes mellitus was also associated with hyponatremia univariably, though this should be interpreted with caution given the small number of affected patients and its attenuation after glucose correction.ConclusionsAdmission hyponatremia was identified in 4.7% of male psychiatric inpatients. Disease duration was associated with hyponatremia after adjustment for age, although its contribution cannot be fully separated from that of age. These findings support careful evaluation of abnormal admission serum sodium values. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to confirm these findings and clarify underlying mechanisms.

articles.title: Quantifying multi-lesion detection and localization in whole-body FDG PET/CT with a multimodal foundation model.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo develop a 3D AI framework for detecting and localizing multiple lesions in whole-body FDG PET/CT, and to evaluate whether a pretrained PET/CT foundation model can improve lesion detection performance compared with conventional training from scratch.ApproachThe AutoPET cohort comprised 1,014 studies divided into 700 training, 114 validation, and 200 subject-independent test studies. Tumor masks were converted into 3D bounding boxes. We developed a one-stage 3D lesion detector using a PlainConvUNet backbone to extract multi-scale encoder-decoder features for lesion classification and box regression. To leverage foundation-model representations, the PlainConvUNet backbone was initialized with weights from our previously developed multi-center PET/CT foundation model, pretrained using masked autoencoding, and subsequently fine-tuned for lesion detection. Four configurations were compared: PET+CT trained from scratch, PET only, CT only, and PET+CT initialized from the pretrained PET/CT foundation model. Detection performance was evaluated using free-response receiver operating characteristic (FROC) and alternative FROC (AFROC) analyses, qualitative analysis, and lesion-size-stratified operating curves.Main resultsMultimodal PET+CT consistently outperformed either modality alone across task-based detection metrics, demonstrating the complementary contributions of metabolic and anatomical information. Importantly, initialization from the pretrained PET/CT foundation model further enhanced lesion detection performance compared with training the same PET+CT detector from scratch, increasing absolute FROC sensitivity by 0.034-0.041 across the evaluated 1-4 false-positive-per-scan operating range and improving AFROC AUC by 0.028. Detection performance increased with lesion size, with small lesions remaining the most challenging. The separation between the pretrained and randomly initialized PET+CT configurations was more evident in the smaller-lesion strata, whereas their operating curves increasingly overlapped for larger lesions.SignificanceThis study provides a detection-centered, task-based characterization of multi-lesion analysis in whole-body PET/CT. Multimodal PET+CT improves lesion detection compared with either modality alone, lesion size is a major determinant of detection performance, and initialization from a pretrained PET/CT foundation model provides an additional performance improvement.

articles.title: Coagulopathic manifestations as a primary presentation of canine angiostrongylosis: a retrospective case series.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the clinical presentations, diagnostic findings, and treatment outcomes of 3 dogs with atypical, predominantly coagulopathic manifestations of Angiostrongylus vasorum infection and to highlight the associated diagnostic challenges.

ANIMALS: 3 client-owned dogs presented at a veterinary referral hospital in Flanders, Belgium, between March 2018 and April 2022. Cases were eligible for inclusion if coagulopathic manifestations were a predominant component of the clinical presentation and canine angiostrongylosis diagnosis was confirmed.

CLINICAL PRESENTATION: The 3 included dogs were male and aged 8 months, 1 year, and 5 years. They presented with clinical signs attributed to hemarthrosis, intracranial hemorrhage, or both, with onset and progression varying among patients. Respiratory signs were absent in 1 dog and mild in 2 dogs, and initial diagnostic considerations included primary orthopedic or neurological disease.

RESULTS: All dogs exhibited coagulation abnormalities consistent with consumptive coagulopathy, including thrombocytopenia, prolonged clotting times, and/or increased D-dimer concentrations. Infection with A vasorum was confirmed by serological antigen detection and/or fecal Baermann examination. Imaging findings included joint swelling, intracerebral hemorrhage, and mild interstitial pulmonary changes. Treatment consisted of anthelmintic therapy with adjunctive corticosteroids, and 2 dogs received plasma transfusion. All dogs recovered with resolution of clinical signs and normalization of laboratory abnormalities.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These cases highlight the importance of including canine angiostrongylosis in the differential diagnosis for dogs presenting with unexplained coagulopathy or hemorrhage, even in the absence of respiratory signs, particularly in regions where the parasite is emerging. Early diagnosis and treatment are critical to prevent potentially life-threatening complications.

articles.title: Premedication with medetomidine compared to acepromazine reduces the risk of hypotension and mild acute kidney injury in healthy dogs undergoing gonadectomy surgery: results of a randomized clinical trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare premedication with medetomidine or acepromazine in regard to hypotension and acute kidney injury (AKI) in dogs undergoing elective gonadectomy.

METHODS: This randomized clinical trial included healthy dogs ≥ 6 months of age undergoing gonadectomy in a university teaching hospital. Exclusion criteria were weight < 4 kg, American Society of Anesthesiologists risk > 2, or cardiovascular/renal disease. Premedication consisted of methadone and medetomidine at 0.3 to 5 µg/kg or acepromazine at 0.01 to 0.05 mg/kg IM. Anesthesia was induced with alfaxalone and maintained with isoflurane. Hypotension (mean arterial pressure < 60 mm Hg) frequency, severity, and duration; recovery temperature; and vomiting and pain interventions were compared. Oliguria 24 hours postoperatively was defined as no urination with low-volume bladder. Serum creatinine was measured from blood before and 24 hours after surgery. Acute kidney injury was defined as an increase of > 26.5 µmol/L.

RESULTS: The medetomidine group included 51 dogs and the acepromazine group 43. There were no differences in preoperative characteristics, anesthetic doses, or time. Hypotension was significantly less frequent (51% vs 84%), had a shorter duration (14 ± 20.2 minutes vs 26 ± 24.2 minutes), and was less severe (lowest mean arterial pressure 60.0 ± 14.9 mm Hg vs 51 ± 10.3 mm Hg) following medetomidine. Acute kidney injury was less frequent in the medetomidine group (9.8% vs 20.9%), with no oliguric AKI cases compared to 4 following acepromazine. There were no differences in postoperative hypothermia or treatments for vomiting or pain.

CONCLUSIONS: Premedication with medetomidine results in a lower frequency and duration of hypotension and might reduce the risk of AKI.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: For healthy dogs undergoing elective surgery, premedication with medetomidine is preferable to acepromazine.

articles.title: Evaluation of knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions of interventional radiology among the Jordanian population.
articles.journal: Journal of medical imaging and radiation sciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interventional Radiology (IR) comprises multiple minimally invasive techniques that aid in the diagnosis and treatment of a plethora of conditions. However, some studies worldwide indicate low public awareness, with IR often conflated with Diagnostic Radiology (DR). No prior study has evaluated this knowledge gap in Jordan. This study aims to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions of IR among the Jordanian population.

METHODS: A cross-sectional, questionnaire-based survey was distributed via social media and convenience sampling. The survey, available in both English and Arabic, assessed demographics, awareness, procedural knowledge, and attitudes toward IR. A total of 429 participants were analyzed using R software. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, and multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Slightly over half (52.2%) of participants had heard of IR. Self-assessed knowledge was low (67.6% "Poor/Very poor"), and 73.9% were confused about the difference between IR and DR. While 72.0% preferred IR over surgery in a hypothetical choice, only 44.1% definitively agreed to undergo an IR procedure when advised. Awareness was significantly lower among females and those in non-medical occupations. High rates of misattribution were observed, with only 18.2% correctly identifying MRI as a DR procedure.

CONCLUSION: There is a significant public knowledge gap regarding IR in Jordan, creating an "awareness-preference paradox." Despite a theoretical preference for minimally invasive IR treatments, a lack of concrete knowledge hinders real-world acceptance. Targeted educational initiatives are needed to clarify the role of IR and improve the utilization of these therapeutic options.

PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Interventional radiology uses minimally invasive procedures guided by medical imaging and can offer an alternative to some types of surgery. This study surveyed people in Jordan to understand their knowledge and views of interventional radiology and related imaging services. This study found that awareness and understanding of interventional radiology were generally low, many people confused it with diagnostic imaging, but most said they would prefer a minimally invasive treatment option. This matters because better public education could help people make informed healthcare decisions and improve access to available treatment options.

articles.title: Residential natural outdoor environment and stroke incidence in older adults in Southern Sweden: A register RELOC-AGE cohort study.
articles.journal: International journal of hygiene and environmental health
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, particularly in later life. While prior research suggests that proximity to green spaces may reduce stroke incidence and support post-stroke recovery, the relationship between the natural outdoor environment and stroke incidence remains underexplored. We investigated the associations between the residential natural outdoor environment and stroke incidence among older adults.

METHODS: Utilizing Register RELOC-AGE data, a cohort study was conducted among 259,769 older adults aged 60+ residing in the Scania region, Southern Sweden. Data from Swedish population registers in 2008, and area-aggregated Perceived Sensory Dimension Score (PSD-score) derived from the Scania outdoor environment database (ScOut) were categorised into tertiles (high, intermediate and low) reflecting the natural outdoor environment close to residence. Incident strokes per 100,000 person-years were assessed between 2009 and 2019. Cox proportional hazard (multi-) exposure models adjusted for socioeconomic; demographic and health were used to examine associations between the PSD-score and stroke incidence.

RESULTS: During the 10-year follow-up, 23,509 individuals experienced a stroke. Stroke incidence was the lowest among those with a high PSD-score (overall incidence rate of 668/100,000) compared with those with a low and intermediate PSD-score (incidence of 733/100,000 and 720/100,000, respectively). High PSD-score was associated with a lower hazard of stroke (adjusted HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.89-0.95), also when additionally adjusted for multiple exposures (adjusted HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.92-0.98).

CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that living in more favourable residential natural outdoor environment are protective against stroke, consistent across sexes. Although there was an indication for a protective effect for those living in high PSD-score areas in urban municipalities, interaction analyses indicated statistical uncertainty. These results highlight the potential relevance of natural outdoor environments for age-friendly and public health planning. Future research should investigate the mechanisms underlying these associations and the role of the natural outdoor environment in post-stroke recovery, while also considering stroke severity.

articles.title: Predictors of longer recognition time in acute aortic dissection: a retrospective observational study.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute aortic dissection (AAD) carries a high mortality risk closely tied to diagnostic timeliness. Delays remain prevalent, driven by atypical presentations-particularly in patients without a chief complaint of pain. This study identified predictors of a longer recognition time, as indicated by prolonged door-to-CT times, and developed a cumulative prediction model for patients presenting without pain complaints.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of 197 adult patients diagnosed with AAD at a tertiary emergency department (ED) from 2016 to 2023. Patients were classified as having a shorter (< 74 min) or longer (≥ 74 min; cohort median) door-to-CT completion time. Predictors were identified by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-penalized logistic regression and decision tree analysis. A subgroup analysis characterized pain-complaint-free patients using a stepwise identification algorithm.

RESULTS: A longer door-to-CT time was associated with female sex, older age, and physiological instability. The strongest multivariable predictors were absence of abrupt pain (odds ratio [OR] 2.81, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.47-5.46) and non-severe triage classification (OR 4.70, 95% CI 1.71-15.29). Dyspnea (OR 2.14) and elevated diastolic blood pressure (OR 1.02/mmHg) also independently predicted a longer door-to-CT time. Among pain-complaint-free patients (n = 46), a stepwise combination of mediastinal widening on chest radiography, Charlson Comorbidity Index ≥ 3, and Shock Index > 1.0 was present in all identified cases (cumulative case coverage 46/46; 95% CI 92.3%-100%).

CONCLUSION: This study identifies a high-risk profile for a longer recognition time of AAD, particularly in older female patients and those presenting without sudden pain. For patients unable to report pain, chest radiography, shock index, and comorbidity burden may be considered to help identify atypical presentations warranting urgent evaluation.

articles.title: Exercise-Induced Tricuspid Regurgitation: Clinical Predictors and Hemodynamic Implications.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exercise-induced preload/afterload changes could affect tricuspid regurgitation (TR).

OBJECTIVES: The study aims to assess exercise-induced TR (exTR+), its consequences, and predictors.

METHODS: Consecutive patients underwent exercise cardiac catheterization and three-dimensional echocardiography. ExTR+ was defined as a ≥1 grade increase in TR severity.

RESULTS: ExTR+ occurred in 34% of 132 patients. Patients with exTR+ were older, had more atrial fibrillation, higher natriuretic peptides/heart failure with preserved ejection fraction probability scores, higher filling pressures, and lower cardiac output (P < 0.05). ExTR+ displayed greater right ventricular dilation, right atrial pressure rise, lower cardiac output, and lower oxygen consumption (P < 0.05). Exercise rather than resting TR regurgitant volume was more associated with cardiac output and oxygen consumption. Baseline TR, atrial fibrillation, and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (OR: 1.065, 4.97, and 1.0004 per pg/mL, respectively, P < 0.05) predicted exTR+ (area under the curve: 0.91).

CONCLUSIONS: ExTR+ is frequent, identifies heart failure with preserved ejection fraction-like phenotypes with a maladaptive exercise response, and adds information beyond resting TR.

articles.title: Three-dimensional versus conventional miniplates in the management of mandibular angle fractures: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of cranio-maxillo-facial surgery : official publication of the European Association for Cranio-Maxillo-Facial Surgery
articles.abstract: Mandibular angle fractures are common injuries associated with a relatively high rate of postoperative complications, and their management remains biomechanically challenging. Three-dimensional (3D) miniplates have been introduced as an alternative to conventional two-dimensional (2D) miniplates, with the aim of improving stability; however, their clinical superiority remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare the outcomes of 3D and conventional miniplates in the management of mandibular angle fractures. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and the Cochrane Library was performed up to 15 March 2026, supplemented by manual searches and trial registries. Randomized controlled trials and comparative studies evaluating 3D versus 2D miniplates were included. Data extraction and risk of bias assessment were performed independently by two reviewers using the Cochrane RoB 2 and ROBINS-I tools. Meta-analysis was conducted using a random-effects model, and certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE approach. Eighteen studies were included, comprising 10 randomized controlled trials, 3 prospective studies, and 5 retrospective studies. Pooled analysis demonstrated no statistically significant differences between 3D and 2D miniplates in postoperative infection (log risk ratio -0.93; 95% CI: -2.11 to 0.25), malocclusion (log risk ratio -0.80; 95% CI: -2.04 to 0.45), wound dehiscence (log risk ratio -0.68; 95% CI: -1.72 to 0.37), hardware failure (log risk ratio -1.10; 95% CI: -3.26 to 1.06), or hardware removal (log risk ratio -0.35; 95% CI: -2.32 to 1.61). Operative time also showed no significant difference (mean difference -2.65 min; 95% CI: -7.42 to 2.13), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 81.5%). The certainty of evidence ranged from low to moderate, primarily due to risk of bias and imprecision. Current evidence indicates that 3D miniplates do not confer a significant clinical advantage over conventional miniplates in mandibular angle fractures. Both systems demonstrate comparable outcomes, and treatment choice should be individualized. Further high-quality, adequately powered randomized trials with standardized outcome reporting are required to establish definitive clinical recommendations.

articles.title: How to read a systematic review and meta-analysis critically: Lessons from the lactate-to-albumin ratio in sepsis.
Platelet transfusion practices in the intensive care: To know, to do and not to do.
Individualized mean arterial pressure during cardiac surgery The OPTIPAM Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether targeting an individualized mean arterial pressure (MAP) during cardiac surgery improves outcomes remains uncertain. The balance between improved perfusion and vasopressor-driven blood pressure augmentation is unclear.

METHODS: In this single-blind, multicenter randomized clinical trial conducted in 10 tertiary centers in France, adult patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass were assigned to either individualized MAP management (target within ±10% of preoperative baseline during surgery and for 24 h postoperatively) or standard management (target MAP ≥65 mm Hg). The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, acute kidney injury, or prespecified neurologic complications within 7 days. Safety outcomes included hemorrhagic complications and transfusion requirements.

RESULTS: A total of 172 patients were enrolled before the trial was stopped early by the data and safety monitoring board because of increased bleeding in the individualized group. Mean intraoperative MAP was higher with individualized management (80.6 vs 75.6 mm Hg; P<0.001), despite limited target adherence (33% of intraoperative time) and greater vasopressor use. The primary outcome occurred in 27 of 85 patients (32%) in the individualized group and 25 of 87 (29%) in the standard group (relative risk, 1.1; 95% CI, 0.7 to 1.8; P=0.76). Hemorrhagic complications occurred more frequently in the individualized group (18% vs 3%; P=0.003).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing cardiac surgery, it was not possible to determine whether an individualized MAP strategy reduced major postoperative complications. More bleeding complications were observed in the individualized group. Future studies should further investigate this safety signal when evaluating individualized blood pressure targets.

articles.title: Toward More Reliable Dengue Early Warning: Bridging the Gap Between Theory and Practice.
articles.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.abstract: Dengue continues to expand globally, increasing pressure on health systems across tropical and subtropical regions. Despite advances in surveillance, data availability, and predictive modeling, early warning often remains insufficiently linked to timely public health action. The challenge, therefore, is not prediction alone but translating heterogeneous surveillance information into actionable intelligence. Key determinants, including climate, human mobility, adult female mosquito abundance, vector infection, asymptomatic infection, and population immunity, vary in feasibility, spatial and temporal resolution, and early-warning value. Climate indicators provide important context but may lack local specificity, and symptomatic case surveillance is constrained by underascertainment and reporting delays. Human mobility can improve spatial risk assessment and, in selected settings, forecasting, whereas adult mosquito surveillance provides complementary information on local vector abundance. The authors of the present study propose an Operationally Prioritized Early Warning (OPEW) framework that integrates sentinel surveillance, scale-aware interpretation of complementary signals, feasibility-based prioritization, event-triggered intensification, and explicit links between surveillance thresholds and predefined actions. The OPEW framework is not a validated prediction model but a testable operational framework that prioritizes information according to epidemiological relevance, timeliness, feasibility, and decision value. Prospective evaluation should assess predictive performance, actionable lead time, resource requirements, and public health outcomes against existing approaches.

articles.title: Acute Right Heart Failure Following Left Coronary Myocardial Infarction in Left Ventricular Assist Device-Supported Patients: A Case Series and Mechanistic Insight.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Right heart failure (RHF) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in patients supported with durable left ventricular assist devices (LVADs). While right coronary artery infarction is a recognized cause of acute RHF, the ventricular consequences of left coronary system infarction in LVAD-supported patients are not well characterized. We describe two patients supported with HeartMate III LVADs who developed acute RHF within 24-48 hours after successful revascularization of acute left coronary system occlusions (mid-left anterior descending artery and left main coronary artery). Both had previously stable LVAD function and no evidence of advanced RHF. After revascularization, each developed hypotension, rising central venous pressure, reduced LVAD flows, and echocardiographic evidence of severe right ventricular (RV) dilation and dysfunction with septal shift toward the left ventricle. Hemodynamic deterioration reversed with inotropic support, diuresis, and LVAD speed adjustment, without mechanical RV support. These cases suggest left coronary acute myocardial infarction (AMI) may precipitate acute RHF in LVAD-supported patients through septal ischemia with impaired ventricular interdependence, acute increases in RV afterload, and relative RV ischemia despite patent right coronary arteries. Heightened surveillance and early echocardiographic assessment after left-sided AMI in LVAD recipients may enable prompt recognition and timely intervention.

articles.title: Novel Occupational and Environmental Risk Factors for SARS-CoV-2 Infection Among Coal Miners: Longitudinal Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Miners are essential rural workers who may work in close proximity to others in inadequately ventilated environments and cannot telecommute or work flexible hours, rendering them vulnerable to SARS-CoV-2 transmission. Exposure to particulate air pollution may also be associated with an increased risk of SARS-CoV-2 infection and mortality. Chronic exposure to particulate matter causes overexpression of the alveolar angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 receptor, facilitating SARS-CoV-2 entry into lung epithelial cells.

OBJECTIVE: We tested the hypothesis that coal miners with higher levels of self-reported particulate matter exposure assessed separately for occupational dust, residential wood burning, and shared transportation have a greater risk of SARS-CoV-2 infection than miners with lower exposure.

METHODS: We conducted a longitudinal study from February 2021 to March 2022 involving 169 surface coal miners in New Mexico and 61 in Wyoming. Seropositivity was determined by measuring immunoglobulin G antibodies to the nucleocapsid protein of SARS-CoV-2 in plasma samples at baseline and at 3, 6, and 12 months after study enrollment. Predictor variables were self-reported exposure to occupational dust, wood burning, and shared transportation. The outcome variable was postbaseline incident seropositivity, defined as any new positive antibody result following enrollment during the 12-month study period. We used logistic regression and Firth-penalized likelihood for analysis; the multivariable model used the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator model selection method. Multivariable models were adjusted for sex, race and ethnicity, mine site (state), COVID-19 vaccination status, and baseline (prevalent) seropositivity.

RESULTS: The study included 230 miners-44% (101/230) Hispanic and 13% (29/230) American Indian, mostly men (202/230, 88%), and 73% (169/230) from New Mexico and 27% (61/230) from Wyoming. At baseline, 23% (52/230) of participants reported COVID-19 vaccination; 25% (58/230) reported high baseline dust exposure, 18% (41/230) reported burning wood very often, and 23% (54/230) reported sharing transportation very often. Higher self-reported mining dust exposure was associated with lower odds of incident seroconversion, but the association was not significant after adjustment (adjusted odds ratio 0.42, 95% CI 0.17-1.07; P=.07). No incident seroconversions occurred among participants reporting frequent residential wood burning (0/35, 0%), and wood-burning frequency was not associated with incident seroconversion. Shared transportation frequency was also not associated with incident seroconversion.

CONCLUSIONS: Self-reported occupational dust exposure was not associated with higher odds of incident SARS-CoV-2 seroconversion in miners; point estimates instead suggested lower odds. This unexpected finding most likely reflects unmeasured workplace factors rather than a protective effect of dust; because individual respirator use and work microenvironment data were not collected, no causal inference can be drawn. Our results highlight the need for additional research on how occupational and environmental exposures interact with infectious disease dynamics in essential rural workforces.

articles.title: Trends in the body of literature on selective dorsal rhizotomy: a bibliometric analysis spanning 12 decades.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to report the results of a bibliometric analysis of the 12-decade body of literature on selective dorsal rhizotomy (SDR).

METHODS: The authors queried the Web of Science database for English-language articles relevant to SDR. Article authorship, keywords, and citations were captured with high fidelity and extracted using analyses performed primarily using the Bibliometrix tool in the R statistical package. Reference publication year spectroscopy (RPYS) was used to explore high-impact years with seminal papers advancing the understanding of the SDR technique and applications.

RESULTS: Between 1912 and 2025, the mean annual growth rate of publications on SDR was 0.98%, leading to a comprehensive corpus of 1184 documents (793 articles) from 3747 unique authors. International co-authorship increased over the 12-decade period analyzed, with contemporary analysis demonstrating international collaboration on 20.47% of articles published from 2010 to 2025. The Journal of Neurosurgery, and later the Journal of Neurosurgery: Pediatrics, demonstrated consistent impact, while the journal Developmental Medicine and Child Neurology published the most articles, published articles that were cited most frequently, and published articles that had the highest impact. Early in the publication record, etiologic and technical terms such as pain, stimulation, and gait analysis were prominent. More recently, research focus has shifted toward unified outcome measures, including gross motor function, along with procedure reliability, follow-up, and surgical outcomes. The terms "children," "cerebral palsy," and "spasticity" have remained constant areas of interest measured via keyword analysis. Using RPYS, 31 foundational articles on SDR were identified, with contemporary RPYS articles highlighting cross-discipline discussion and patient selection strategies.

CONCLUSIONS: Interest in SDR increased in the late 1980s and early 1990s, coinciding with advances in cerebral palsy classification and improvements in gross motor function scales. The focus of SDR research demonstrated a shift from technique and etiology to outcomes and cross-disciplinary patient selection. The modern era is characterized by collaborative research that spans international borders and involves neurosurgical patient selection in collaboration with colleagues in rehabilitative fields.

articles.title: Molecular Transmission Clustering and Pretreatment Drug Resistance Among Men Infected With HIV-1 Who Have Sex With Men in Baotou, China: A Cross-Sectional Subgroup Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, men who have sex with men (MSM) have become a high-risk group for HIV transmission due to their complex, secretive sexual relationships, posing challenges to HIV-1 prevention.

OBJECTIVE: We analyzed factors associated with molecular transmission clustering and pretreatment drug resistance (PDR) among newly reported HIV-1-infected MSM in Baotou, China, and to provide locally relevant evidence for targeted public health interventions.

METHODS: We conducted a subgroup cross-sectional molecular epidemiological analysis of all newly reported HIV-1 cases attributed to homosexual transmission in Baotou between January 2022 and December 2024. The sample comprised 213 treatment-naïve MSM, from whom plasma samples were obtained. A 1.3-kb fragment of the HIV-1 pol gene was amplified and sequenced using next-generation sequencing. Inclusion criteria were a newly reported HIV-1 infection, no antiretroviral therapy at the time of this writing, and self-reported same-sex sexual behavior. Primary outcomes were clustering in a genetic distance-based molecular transmission network and the presence of PDR according to the Stanford HIV Drug Resistance Database.

RESULTS: In total, 176 pol gene sequences were successfully obtained, with circulating recombinant form (CRF)-07_BC being the most prevalent subtype, accounting for 56.82% of the total sequences. The molecular transmission network was constructed using a pairwise genetic distance of 1.30%, with 52 of 176 (29.55%) sequences forming 19 clusters within the network. The network exhibited significant assortative mixing by age (ra=0.41; P=.001), marital status (ra=0.408; P=.002), and educational attainment (ra=0.385; P=.001), rather than random mixing. Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that CRF07_BC subtype-infected individuals had a significantly higher risk of clustering (AOR 4.98; 95% CI 1.92-12.94; P<.01). Compared to never-married individuals, divorced or widowed individuals were less likely to have clustered cases (AOR 0.27; 95% CI 0.08-0.92; P<.05). The prevalence of PDR was 6.57% (n=14). Nonnucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor resistance was the most common (n=8, 3.76%), followed by protease inhibitor resistance (n=5, 2.35%), and nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor resistance (n=3, 1.14%). Drug-resistant strains were more frequently detected among individuals infected with the CRF07_BC subtype (χ28=90.44; P<.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Unlike previous studies primarily focused on high-burden southeastern coastal regions of China, we investigated the molecular transmission characteristics of HIV-1 among MSM in the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. Our findings demonstrate that transmission clustering and drug resistance patterns previously observed are also present in northern border areas. This study integrated HIV-1 molecular transmission network analysis with next-generation sequencing technologies to identify key populations involved in local HIV transmission, thereby supporting targeted public health interventions. In addition, surveillance of PDR among high-risk populations may facilitate the development of evidence-based antiretroviral treatment strategies and improve the efficient allocation of limited health care resources.

articles.title: Comparing risk factors for postoperative dysphagia following single- or multilevel anterior cervical spine surgery.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Studies have shown that patients undergoing multilevel cervical operations are at greater risk for postoperative dysphagia compared to those who undergo single-level operations. This study aimed to compare risk factors for postoperative dysphagia in patients undergoing single- versus multilevel anterior cervical surgery.

METHODS: A prospectively collected quality registry was retrospectively reviewed to identify candidates who underwent anterior cervical procedures. Procedures involving 1 disc space were categorized as single level, and procedures involving ≥ 2 consecutive disc spaces were categorized as multilevel. Dysphagia rates were determined using Eating Assessment Tool-10 (EAT-10) scores. Univariate and multivariate analyses were performed to identify significant risk factors for postoperative dysphagia within 12 months of surgery.

RESULTS: Of 1705 patients who met the inclusion criteria, 804 (47.2%) underwent single-level and 901 (52.8%) underwent multilevel procedures. Both groups had similar rates of baseline dysphagia (14% vs 14%, p > 0.9). Multilevel patients had significantly higher rates of dysphagia at 1 month (64% vs 54%, p = 0.001), 3 months (32% vs 25%, p = 0.004), and 12 months (29% vs 21%, p = 0.004) postoperatively. Multivariable regression revealed that for single-level surgery, Black race (OR 2.40, p = 0.021), higher American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class (OR 1.45, p = 0.018), symptom duration for more than 12 months (OR 1.66, p = 0.043), baseline dysphagia (OR 4.53, p < 0.001), diabetes (OR 1.76, p = 0.014), peripheral vascular disease (OR 3.74, p = 0.049), and operations involving C3-4 (OR 2.25, p = 0.004) were independent predictors of postoperative dysphagia within 12 months of surgery. For multilevel procedures, baseline dysphagia (OR 7.31, p < 0.001), diabetes (OR 1.61, p = 0.022), and operations involving C3-4 (OR 1.85, p = 0.011) or C4-5 (OR 1.64, p = 0.010) were independent predictors of postoperative dysphagia, while listhesis (OR 0.63, p = 0.042) was an independent predictor of no postoperative dysphagia.

CONCLUSIONS: Patients undergoing single-level cervical procedures are at lower risk for postoperative dysphagia. Preexisting dysphagia, diabetes, and the inclusion of upper cervical levels independently contribute to dysphagia risk following both single-level and multilevel surgical procedures. Black race, ASA class, prolonged preoperative symptom duration, and peripheral vascular disease are associated with dysphagia risk particularly in single-level procedures, while listhesis predicts lower dysphagia risk specifically in multilevel surgical procedures. These results can aid patient counseling by providing stratified risk factors for postoperative dysphagia.

articles.title: Mobile App for Assisting Patients With Type 1 Diabetes in Insulin Dose Adjustment: Development and Usability Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In resource-limited countries, most patients with type 1 diabetes (T1DM) use basal-bolus insulin therapy. Optimal dosing requires matching insulin to carbohydrate intake, premeal blood glucose levels, and physical activity-a complex process prone to error, particularly for patients with limited health literacy.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and pilot-test a new mobile app designed to adjust bolus insulin doses based on the carbohydrate content of the meal, premeal blood glucose, and physical activity, tailored specifically for Iraqi patients with T1DM.

METHODS: To guide the app's development, a literature search was conducted to identify key features in mobile apps for improving glycemic control in patients with T1DM. Evidence highlighted bolus insulin calculation, blood glucose tracking, and patient education as the most impactful features; consequently, these 3 functionalities were selected as the core components of the app. The scientific content of the app was based mainly on the latest American Diabetes Association guidelines and reviewed by 8 experts to ensure accuracy. After initial app prototype development, a cross-sectional pilot feasibility study was conducted at the Diabetes and Endocrine Center in Basrah, Iraq. A purposive sample of 10 health care professionals (5 endocrinologists, 2 dietitians, 2 clinical pharmacists, and 1 diabetes educator) and 10 patients with T1DM (aged ≥15 y) was recruited. The app was installed on participants' smartphones, and standardized instructions on its functions and usage were provided. After a 10- to 14-day trial period, participants evaluated the usability, satisfaction, and perceived benefits of the app using newly developed and validated 3-point Likert scale questionnaires (one specific to patients and the other to health care professionals), alongside an optional open-ended question for qualitative feedback.

RESULTS: Positive feedback was reported across both groups. A favorable usability rating was expressed by 80% of experts and 90% of patients. Regarding app benefits, 90% of experts and nearly all patients considered it effective for adjusting insulin doses, improving treatment adherence, and reducing hypoglycemia. At least 70% of experts noted provider benefits (reduced workload and improved monitoring). All participants were satisfied and would recommend the app.

CONCLUSIONS: The new app tested in this study demonstrated promising acceptability and usability among patients with T1DM and relevant health care professionals. However, given the small sample size, these findings should be interpreted as preliminary feasibility evidence. A larger, adequately powered clinical trial is warranted to confirm these results and evaluate the app's clinical impact on glycemic outcomes.

articles.title: Evaluating the Performance of Large Language Models in Vascular Surgery Cases: Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude are increasingly used by clinicians, yet their accuracy, safety, and consistency in clinical cases remain poorly defined. Most studies assess LLMs using multiple-choice questions rather than free-response reasoning.

OBJECTIVE: The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the performance and safety of 3 widely used LLMs in realistic vascular surgery scenarios in key domains such as diagnosis, investigation, and multidisciplinary and multimodal management. The secondary objective of this study was to evaluate the safety of the models' outputs.

METHODS: A total of 42 fictitious vascular cases across 5 major pathologies (acute limb ischemia [ALI], aortopathy, chronic limb ischemia, diabetic foot infection, and extracranial cerebrovascular disease) were independently entered into GPT-5, Gemini 2.5, and Claude Sonnet 4.5 using standardized prompts. Each model answered structured questions covering diagnosis, investigation, and management (both operative and nonoperative). Responses were scored out of 20 by a panel using a predefined rubric. Each plan's overall safety was separately assessed. Comparative analyses used 2-tailed t tests, ANOVA, and multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Mean composite scores by model were 86.5% for ChatGPT, 83.5% for Gemini, and 88.0% for Claude, whereas scores by disease were 82.7% for ALI, 83.8% for aortopathy, 85.9% for chronic limb ischemia, 86.1% for diabetic foot infection, and 80.7% for extracranial cerebrovascular disease (P>.05 in each case). Unsafe plans were generated in 11.9%, 23.8%, and 7.1% of cases by ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, respectively. On multivariable analysis, independent predictors of unsafe outputs were lower composite score (odds ratio [OR] 0.471, 95% CI 0.306-0.722; P=.001), higher word count (OR 1.003, 95% CI 1.001-1.005; P=.001), and ALI (OR 20.9, 95% CI 3.79-61.8; P<.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings demonstrate LLMs' promise in managing routine vascular surgery cases. However, their inconsistent safety profiles and ethical limitations preclude unsupervised clinical use. Rigorous specialty-specific validation is essential before they may be integrated into routine practice.

articles.title: Image-Based Consensus Molecular Subtyping Refines Prognostication in Stage II/III Colorectal Cancer: A Retrospective Analysis of the SCOT Trial.
authors: imCMS Consortium; S:CORT Consortium; TransSCOT Consortium
imCMS Consortium, S:CORT Consortium, TransSCOT Consortium
articles.journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Risk stratification in localized colorectal cancer (CRC) remains inadequate. Transcriptome-based classifiers such as consensus molecular subtyping (CMS) improve this, but are challenging to implement. We determined the performance of a novel image-based method for CRC CMS subtyping (imCMS) using routine pathology images from the SCOT trial and investigated association of imCMS subtypes with clinicopathologic and tumor molecular and immune factors, treatment benefit, and survival.

METHODS: We applied a novel imCMS classifier to stage II/III CRCs from the SCOT trial (ISRCTN59757862) which examined 3 versus 6 months of adjuvant oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy following curative-intent surgery. We determined correlates of imCMS subgroups and investigated imCMS prognostic and predictive value for CRC recurrence-free interval, overall survival (OS), and survival after CRC recurrence (SAR) by univariable and multivariable Cox regression.

RESULTS: A total of 2,816 cases were informative for imCMS classification, of which 664 (24%) were imCMS1 (immune), 987 (35%) imCMS2 (canonical), 433 (15%) imCMS3 (metabolic), 653 (23%) imCMS4 (mesenchymal), and 79 (3%) of mixed subtype. Analysis confirmed expected associations of imCMS1 with deficient DNA mismatch repair (dMMR) and imCMS3 with KRAS mutation and revealed substantially lower intraepithelial CD8+ and intrastromal FoxP3+ T-cell infiltrate (CD8IE-FoxP3IS) in imCMS4 tumors. imCMS classification was strongly prognostic independent of clinicopathologic factors, dMMR, and CD8IE-FoxP3IS in multivariable analysis but did not predict differential benefit from chemotherapy duration or regimen. The combination of imCMS with CD8IE-FoxP3IS groups defined CRC subgroups with substantially different recurrence risk. Analysis of OS and SAR revealed notable discordance in imCMS3 and imCMS4 prognostic value before and after relapse.

CONCLUSION: imCMS classification improves CRC prognostication beyond existing tumor factors and is potentially deliverable in clinical practice. imCMS prediction of therapeutic benefit requires further study.

articles.title: Burn resuscitation: does hypertension change the outcome?
Plant potassium channel β-subunits confer antiviral defense via disrupting potyviral 6K2-mediated vesicle maturation and trafficking.
articles.abstract: Potyviruses constitute the largest known group of plant RNA viruses. Their 6K2 protein is an integral membrane protein that induces the formation of vesicular structures, which support viral RNA replication and act as vehicles for intracellular movement. While multiple host proteins are known to regulate either viral replication or movement, it remains largely unclear whether and how a single host protein can coordinately modulate both processes. Here, we identify NbKNB1, a Nicotiana benthamiana homolog of the plant potassium channel β-subunit. Genetic assays demonstrate that NbKNB1 confers antiviral activity against turnip mosaic virus (TuMV). NbKNB1 localizes predominantly to the plasma membrane in healthy cells, but relocalizes to 6K2-induced viral replication complexes during TuMV infection. Biochemical analyses show that NbKNB1 directly interacts with 6K2, disrupting 6K2 self-association and impairing the maturation of 6K2-tagged vesicles. NbKNB1 also competes with the viral cylindrical inclusion (CI) protein for 6K2 binding, thereby inhibiting TuMV cell-to-cell movement. A 6K2-binding-deficient mutant, NbKNB1Δ270-279, fails to restrict both viral replication and intercellular movement, confirming that direct interaction with 6K2 is required for NbKNB1-mediated suppression of TuMV infection. Moreover, NbKNB1 and its maize homolog ZmKZB1 also reduce infection by other potyviruses. Collectively, these findings reveal a novel antiviral strategy in which plant potassium channel β-subunit homologs target the viral 6K2 protein to counteract potyvirus infection, and provide a promising target for antiviral breeding.

articles.title: Parental obesity is associated with altered hematopoiesis and impaired viral immunity in offspring.
articles.abstract: The prevalence of obesity among adults of childbearing age has tripled worldwide since 1975. Obesity during pregnancy has been linked to impaired neonatal immunity and a higher risk of infections in childhood but the causal mechanisms have not been defined. Using a mouse model of diet-induced obesity, we documented impaired antiviral immunity in the offspring of obese mice, corresponding with reduced cell-mediated immune responses. This included lower frequencies of Tbet+ CD4+ T helper 1 cells and a decrease in cytotoxic CD8+ T cells in the lungs of mice infected with respiratory Sendai virus, and confirmed in spleens from mice infected with LCMV. Consistent with impaired cellular immunity, single-cell transcriptomic analysis of bone marrow revealed altered hematopoiesis in these offspring, with evidence of interferon-induced skewing toward myelopoiesis at the expense of lymphocyte development. Our studies provide an in-depth transcriptomic profile of immune cell progenitors in the bone marrow paired with mature innate and adaptive immune cell populations in lymph nodes at single-cell resolution. Results suggest that compromised immune protection from viral infections in the offspring of obese mice stems from altered lymphocyte development that is influenced by inflammatory interferon signaling in bone marrow.

articles.title: Thermoresponsive Adhesive Hydrogel Enabling Dynamic Adhesion Switching for Diabetic Chronic Wound Healing.
articles.abstract: Diabetic chronic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, increased susceptibility to bacterial infection, and impaired tissue regeneration, which collectively hinder wound repair. Hydrogel dressings have emerged as promising candidates for chronic wound management; however, achieving stable tissue adhesion for wound protection while enabling gentle removal during dressing replacement remains challenging. Although stimuli-responsive adhesive hydrogels have been developed to achieve on-demand debonding, their reliance on external chemical triggers and limited adaptability in complex wound environments restrict their further application. Herein, we developed a thermoresponsive multifunctional hydrogel dressing (HG-CT@Al) that integrates dynamic adhesion regulation with wound microenvironment modulation through a one-pot photopolymerization strategy. The NIPAM/AAm/AA copolymer network endowed HG-CT@Al with temperature-responsive adhesion switching, while the chitosan (CS) semi-interpenetrating network and dynamic coordination interactions between tea polyphenols (TP) and Al3+ enhanced structural stability and provided antibacterial and antioxidant functions. By optimizing the network composition, HG-CT@Al maintained strong tissue adhesion at physiological temperature (35 °C, 167.22 N/m) and reduced adhesion strength after mild heating (45 °C, 97.99 N/m), enabling on-demand gentle debonding. Meanwhile, HG-CT@Al exhibited excellent antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. aureus (99.65 and 99.69%, respectively) and strong antioxidant capacity (95.61% DPPH radical-scavenging efficiency). In a full-thickness diabetic wound model, HG-CT@Al significantly accelerated wound closure and promoted re-epithelialization, collagen deposition, angiogenesis, and M2 macrophage early enrichment. This study presents a multifunctional hydrogel strategy integrating temperature-responsive dynamic adhesion regulation and wound microenvironment modulation, providing an effective approach for diabetic chronic wound management.

articles.title: BPR-30901649, An Angiotensinogen-Targeting Small Interfering RNA, Achieves Ultra-Durable Target Silencing and Sustained Blood Pressure Reduction Through 20 Weeks in Hypertensive Non-Human Primates.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension affects over 1.3 billion adults worldwide, and poor adherence to daily oral therapy contributes to inadequate blood pressure (BP) control. We characterized BPR-30901649, a liver-targeted small interfering RNA (siRNA) against angiotensinogen (AGT), hypothesizing that its optimized design would confer greater potency and durability than an advanced clinical-stage AGT siRNA benchmark.

METHODS: BPR-30901649 was selected through in vitro and in vivo screening in HepG2 cells and human AGT (hAGT) transgenic mice. Off-target risk was assessed by RNA sequencing in primary human hepatocytes. Pharmacodynamics were evaluated in hAGT mice after single and repeat subcutaneous (SC) dosing, and in hypertensive cynomolgus monkeys given a single SC dose of 1.5 or 3.0 mg/kg, with serum AGT and systolic BP (SBP) monitored for 20 weeks. Investigational New Drug (IND)-enabling toxicology was conducted in rats and nonhuman primates (NHPs).

RESULTS: RNA sequencing indicated low off-target risk. In hAGT mice, BPR-30901649 produced significantly deeper serum AGT knockdown than the benchmark. In hypertensive NHPs, a single SC injection produced rapid, dose-dependent, and sustained AGT suppression; at week 20, SBP remained reduced by 14.2% (20.3 mm Hg) and 17.3% (25.3 mm Hg) in the low- and high-dose groups, respectively. In repeat-dose toxicology, the no-observed-adverse-effect level was 100 mg/kg in NHPs.

CONCLUSIONS: BPR-30901649 surpassed an advanced clinical-stage AGT siRNA benchmark in vivo and showed a wide preclinical safety margin, supporting its clinical development as a potential twice-yearly therapy for hypertension.

articles.title: Oral Acarbose Inhibits Baseline Salivary Amylase and Blunts Early Postprandial Glycemia: Randomized Cross-Over Study.
articles.abstract: This study investigated whether salivary α-amylase (SAA) inhibition by acarbose affects postprandial blood glucose (BG) in healthy individuals. This single-blinded, placebo-controlled, randomized cross-over trial included 4 conditions: trial 1 (T1), placebo (oligosaccharide); trial 2 (T2), swallowing 50 mg of acarbose; and trials 3 and 4 (T3 and T4), simultaneous intake of starch (150 g of rice) with 50 mg or 100 mg of acarbose, respectively. Fifteen young, healthy women were enrolled. Peak ΔBG occurred at 30 min in both T1 and T2 and at 60 min in T3. ΔBG at 30 min was significantly lower in T3 and T4 than in T2 (both P<.05) without trial order effect, while BG areas under the curve did not differ between T2 and T3. Inhibition of SAA by oral acarbose reduced the early postprandial increase in BG compared with intact SAA activity in healthy individuals.

articles.title: Implementing Effective Infection Prevention and Control in Residential Aged Care Through Communities of Practice: Protocol for a Before-and-After Study (IMMERSE-2).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In Australian residential aged care, infection prevention and control (IPC) Lead nurses (IPC Leads) are a key part of the IPC program. IPC Leads are often the main IPC contacts and provide support to staff to improve IPC and resident outcomes. To enhance their competence and self-efficacy, IPC Leads need to engage in ongoing role development. Connecting with other IPC Leads, learning together, and sharing ideas and resources could also be beneficial. Communities of practice (CoPs) have been shown to improve self-efficacy and job satisfaction by fostering belonging, peer learning, and problem-solving. Drawing on social learning theory, CoPs encourage learning with and from one another to explore and iteratively develop practice. This study draws on the CoP literature and builds on our previous pilot of a CoP for IPC Leads in 1 state of Australia, which found promising impacts on confidence and practice change.

OBJECTIVE: This study will evaluate CoPs for IPC Leads working in Australian residential aged care. Primarily, the study will assess changes in IPC Leads' self-efficacy. It will also explore job satisfaction and IPC practice improvement and assess the acceptability and feasibility of CoPs.

METHODS: We are conducting a before-and-after study using multimethods. We will recruit IPC Leads from across Australia to participate in the CoPs. The CoPs will be implemented over 12 months, with online sessions held monthly for 30 to 60 minutes each. Baseline and 12-month follow-up surveys of IPC Leads' self-efficacy and job satisfaction and audits of IPC practice will be conducted. At the 12-month follow-up, surveys and interviews with IPC Leads will be used to assess the acceptability and feasibility of the CoPs and to explore case examples of IPC Leads facilitating practice change. Researcher notes and costing data collected will be used to further evaluate the feasibility and fidelity of the CoPs. Quantitative data will be summarized descriptively, and an ordinal mixed-effects model with a logit link will be used to assess change in self-efficacy. Interview data will be analyzed using an inductive approach, followed by a deductive approach, based on the Framework Method.

RESULTS: This project was funded in October 2024 and commenced in February 2025. As of April 30, 2026, 97 potential participants had registered their interest in participating, but no participants had been enrolled (ie, consented to participate). Recruitment of IPC Leads began in March 2026. The CoPs are expected to commence in June to July 2026. Data collection will commence in May 2026, and data analysis is expected to be completed by January 2028. Study results are expected to be published in 2028.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings will create new research knowledge in the field of CoPs and knowledge translation in the aged care sector and inform the sustainability and potential for future scale-up of this collaborative social learning approach.

articles.title: Effectiveness of a Multicomponent Digital Therapeutic Program on Inhaled Medication Adherence in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Poor medication adherence is a critical impediment to effective chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) management and remains challenging to track in routine care. Digital therapeutic interventions may improve chronic disease management through remote monitoring and patient education. However, most existing digital interventions focus on individual components of disease management, and evidence from longer-term pragmatic randomized controlled trials evaluating integrated digital therapeutics in routine clinical practice remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a multicomponent digital therapeutic program combining electronic inhaler monitoring (EIM) with behavioral support in improving medication adherence and symptom-related outcomes among patients with COPD prescribed pressurized metered-dose inhalers, and to assess patient engagement and implementation in routine clinical practice.

METHODS: In this prospective, open-label, unblinded, randomized controlled trial, patients with COPD prescribed pressurized metered-dose inhalers were enrolled and randomized in a 2:1 ratio to either the intervention group or the control group. All participants received an EIM device to objectively record inhaler use throughout the 24-week study period. Patients in the intervention group also received personalized medication reminders from the EIM, adherence feedback, educational content, and clinician-supported follow-up through an integrated digital management platform based on EIM-derived data, whereas the control group received usual care. The primary outcome was medication adherence over 24 weeks. Secondary outcomes included exacerbations, COPD symptoms, quality of life, and lung function.

RESULTS: A total of 158 participants were randomized, including 106 in the intervention group and 52 in the control group. The median monitoring coverage was 161.5 (IQR 86.3-168.0) days during the follow-up period. The self-reported adherence measured using the Test of Adherence to Inhalers showed no significant between-group differences at any follow-up time point. However, the electronically monitored adherence was significantly higher in the intervention group than in the control group (59.5% vs 33.1%, P=.009). Adherence declined over time in both groups, decreasing from 85.3% during weeks 0 to 4 to 43.0% during weeks 12 to 24 in the intervention group and from 76.8% to 11.9% in the control group over the same intervals, resulting in a progressively larger between-group difference over follow-up. No significant differences were observed in exacerbations, health-related quality of life, symptom burden, lung function, or mental health outcomes. In an exploratory analysis, a significantly greater proportion of participants in the intervention group achieved the minimal clinically important difference in the COPD Assessment Test score than in the control group (odds ratio 2.21, 95% CI 1.11-4.41; P=.02).

CONCLUSIONS: The multicomponent digital therapeutic program significantly improved objective medication adherence in patients with COPD over 24 weeks. While most clinical outcomes did not differ significantly between groups, the higher proportion of participants achieving a clinically meaningful improvement in the COPD Assessment Test score warrants further investigation.

articles.title: A transcriptional and cellular exploration of obesity and type II diabetes in human adipose tissues.
articles.abstract: Obesity is tightly linked to metabolic disorders such as type II diabetes mellitus (T2D), although a subpopulation of individuals with obesity do not present with these morbidities. The biological factors conferring T2D vulnerability remain incompletely understood. We recruited 58 individuals with obesity with or without a clinical diagnosis of T2D (Ob + T2D and Ob). We profiled paired samples of omental and subcutaneous adipose by single-cell RNA sequencing (n = 10), flow cytometry under basal and stimulated conditions (n = 42), and histology (n = 17). Flow cytometry and chemokine quantification were also performed in paired whole blood. We identified reprogramming of the omental stromal compartment, centered on mesothelial and endothelial cells, alongside contrasting innate T cell and macrophage phenotypes across depots. Mesothelial and IGFBP2+ cells exhibited a fibrotic, epithelial-mesenchymal transition-like phenotype, while omental endothelial cells exhibited a lipid-overload, inflammatory, antigen presentation profile in T2D. Omental and subcutaneous adipose innate T cells exhibited divergent inflammatory profiles between tissues. These findings reveal previously unidentified insights into the pathophysiology of T2D in adipose tissue and identify compensatory networks within the tissues that could be exploited by targeted therapeutics.

articles.title: Mevalonate pathway regulates double-negative regulatory T cell stability in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
articles.abstract: Lipid metabolism dysfunction and immune imbalance are critical pathogenic drivers of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Double-negative regulatory T cells (DNTreg) are important immune regulatory cells that maintain liver immune homeostasis. However, their survival and function are compromised in MASLD. Herein, we found that mevalonate pathway and its rate-limiting enzyme HMG-CoA reductase (HMGCR) were significantly down-regulated in DNTreg from both mice and patients with MASLD, correlating with impaired DNTreg viability and immunosuppressive function. Arachidonic acid is enriched in MASLD liver and inhibits DNTreg HMGCR expression. Geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGPP), a downstream product of HMGCR, mediates RAC1 geranylgeranylation, which facilitates its interaction with mitochondrial CLPX protease, thereby enhancing mitochondrial function and immunoregulatory activity of DNTreg. Adoptive transfer of Pggt1b+/- DNTreg into MASLD mice demonstrated significantly diminished therapeutic efficacy compared with wild-type DNTreg. In conclusion, mevalonate metabolism-mediated geranylgeranylation is essential for the suppressive activity and immune homeostasis of DNTreg in MASLD.

articles.title: Temporal dynamics of antigen-specific T cell expansion in primary SARS-CoV-2 infection.
articles.abstract: Quantifying T cell response during primary infection in humans is crucial for understanding adaptive immunity. Leveraging a controlled human challenge to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, we characterized antigen-specific T cell responses within and across individuals. Notably, individual clones reached similar maximum frequencies despite differences in the timing of their peak expansion. Mathematical modeling within a coarse-grained framework suggested that variability in precursor frequency between different T cell clones could be one mechanism to explain this relationship. Single-cell profiling revealed distinct temporal programs for CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, with CD4+ cells expanding earlier but contracting to a lower frequency. Clones with similar receptors, likely recognizing the same antigen, expanded at similar times. Together, these findings highlight how clone-intrinsic properties such as precursor frequency and CD4/CD8 subset status shape T cell clonal kinetics. These insights provide a quantitative framework for understanding T cell response in humans, with implications for vaccine design.

articles.title: CD8+ T cells induce RIPK1-regulated brain endothelial cell death in cerebral malaria.
articles.abstract: Cerebral malaria (CM) is a potentially lethal complication of Plasmodium falciparum infection characterized by blood-brain barrier disruption and brain hemorrhage. Although immune-mediated endothelial damage is central to CM pathology, the mechanisms linking cytotoxic immune responses to endothelial injury remain unclear.
