Here, we show that CD8+ T cells induce receptor-interacting serine/threonine-protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)-regulated cell death of brain endothelial cells in mouse CM, while RIPK1 phosphorylation is increased in brain endothelial cells in human CM. Using magnetic resonance imaging, three-dimensional tissue-cleared brain imaging, cross-species pathology, endothelial translatomics, immunocerebrovascular interactomics, and genetic association testing, we identify a CD8+ T cell-dependent, RIPK1-centered mouse endothelial cell death program. Combined RIPK1 and caspase inhibition protected cross-presenting endothelial cells from CD8+ T cell-mediated death in vitro. In vivo, brain endothelial-specific genetic inactivation or systemic pharmacological inhibition of RIPK1 kinase activity prolonged survival in mouse CM without altering parasitemia. These findings support RIPK1 inhibition as a promising therapeutic strategy to counter CD8+ T cell-induced endothelial death in CM.

articles.title: Combating drug-resistant Aeromonas veronii: Multiomics revealed the antibacterial mechanism of resveratrol.
articles.abstract: Aeromonas, widely distributed in aquatic ecosystems, is a prevalent fish pathogen and can cause human infections via contaminated aquatic products, polluted water contact, or tainted food consumption. Escalating antibiotic resistance in Aeromonas strains highlights an urgent need for alternative natural antimicrobial agents. This study investigated resveratrol's antibacterial mechanisms against Aeromonas veronii and evaluated its protective efficacy in hybrid sturgeon. Resveratrol exhibited strong activity [minimum inhibitory concentration: 128 microgram per milliliter (μg/ml), minimum bactericidal concentration: 256 μg/ml], disrupting cell wall/membrane integrity, inducing reactive oxygen species accumulation, inhibiting adenosine 5'-triphosphate synthesis, and down-regulating key metabolic pathways via transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses. In the sturgeon infection model, resveratrol-nanoemulsion notably improved survival, reduced tissue bacterial loads, mitigated oxidative stress and inflammation, and restored intestinal barrier function. These findings confirm resveratrol as a promising antibiotic alternative against A. veronii, with nanoemulsion formulation enhancing its therapeutic efficacy.

articles.title: Structure of the Chimalliviridae bacteriophage Goslar reveals host recognition and infection machinery.
articles.abstract: Large-genome bacteriophages (phages) of the Chimalliviridae family have a distinctive life cycle, building compartments inside infected bacterial cells that broadly protect their genomes from host defenses. Here, we use cryo-electron microscopy to determine a structure of the Escherichia coli-infecting Chimalliviridae phage Goslar. We combine manual modeling of 25 structural proteins with AlphaFold structure predictions of an additional three proteins to generate a composite model with 2888 protein chains from 28 different structural proteins, totaling more than 1.4 million amino acid residues. Our structure reveals the architecture of the Goslar capsid, portal, tail, and baseplate, highlighting structural similarities and differences with other tailed phages. Combining our structural data with quantitative mass spectrometry of Goslar virions, we identify several high-copy virion-associated proteins that likely play key roles when injected into host cells upon infection. We also identify a Chimalliviridae-specific family of proteins that form long, flexible filaments anchored at the phage baseplate and which incorporate carbohydrate-binding domains, suggesting a key role in host recognition.

articles.title: Electron competition in azobenzene programs infection-adaptive antibacterial therapy.
articles.abstract: Conventional stimulus-responsive antibacterial systems generally operate through binary trigger-activation mechanisms, making them poorly suited to evolving infection microenvironments and thereby contributing to persistent infection and resistance development. Here, we establish an azobenzene-based kinetic regulatory system in which oxygen gradients commonly present in infected tissues continuously program reaction kinetics through electron competition. Oxygen acts as a competing electron acceptor within the reductive reaction network, partitioning electron transfer between azo reduction and oxygen consumption. Substituent electronic structures further reshape reduction propensity, encoding distinct kinetic behaviors. These electronically programmed kinetics translated into adaptive nanoscale dissociation and drug-release profiles: Electron-rich azobenzenes rapidly disassembled under severe hypoxia, whereas electron-withdrawing structures sustained release under mild hypoxia, generating infection state-adaptive antibacterial outputs. Moreover, the same electronic features governing reduction kinetics also reduced the reactivity and toxicity of reductive metabolites. This work establishes electron competition as a strategy for converting environmental gradients into continuous kinetic outputs for adaptive antibacterial therapy.

articles.title: Reduced apelin expression and atrial fibrosis in postoperative atrial fibrillation following coronary artery bypass grafting.
articles.abstract: The role of apelin in atrial fibrosis linked to postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is not fully understood. This exploratory study investigated apelin's association with POAF-related atrial fibrosis and its impact on profibrotic signaling. The study included 18 patients: six CABG patients with POAF, six CABG patients without POAF, and six patients with congenital heart disease in sinus rhythm (serving as a secondary reference). Left atrial appendage tissue was analyzed histologically and molecularly, and serum apelin levels were measured on postoperative day 2 in CABG patients. Primary neonatal rat atrial fibroblasts were treated with transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1) both with and without apelin, or subjected to apelin silencing. Compared with CABG patients without POAF, the POAF group exhibited lower atrial apelin expression and serum concentrations, increased collagen deposition, elevated TGF-β1 expression, and enhanced phosphorylation of mothers against decapentaplegic homolog 2 (Smad2), while total Smad2 remained unchanged. Experimentally, apelin attenuated TGF-β1-induced fibroblast activation, collagen expression, and Smad2 phosphorylation. Conversely, apelin silencing increased the expression of fibrosis-associated proteins. These preliminary findings suggest a link between reduced apelin and atrial fibrosis, as well as POAF after CABG. They also indicate antifibrotic effects of apelin, potentially mediated through TGF-β1/Smad2 signaling. Further research with larger clinical cohorts and complementary experimental models is necessary to fully elucidate the pathway mediation and clinical significance of these findings.

articles.title: Yellow fever virus infection triggers the assembly of compositionally unique and specialised stress granules.
articles.abstract: The phase separation of biomolecules into stress granules (SGs) allows the cell to tightly regulate translation activity in response to different stimuli, such as oxidative stress, starvation, or the recognition of non-cellular RNA. Recent reports suggest SGs induced during viral infection may act as a crossroad between the cellular stress response and the activation of the innate immune response. Here, we aimed to dissect the role of SGs in the context of yellow fever virus (YFV) infection. We found that YFV infection with both 17D vaccine and Asibi pathogenic strains resulted in translational shut-off and the formation of SGs at 48 hours post infection (hpi), although viral infection was already apparent at 24 hpi. This delay may be coupled to the ability of the YFV capsid to inhibit SG formation through an interaction with the SG scaffolding protein G3BP1. To elucidate the role of YFV-induced SGs during infection, we inhibited SG assembly using a small-molecule inhibitor as well as siRNA-mediated knockdown of SGs and found that while SG formation does not impact viral replication, silencing of SG scaffolding proteins is associated with increased expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISG). Uncovering the proteome of YFV-induced SGs, our compositional analysis revealed a unique composition, distinct from NaAs-induced SGs, which displayed enrichment in mitochondrial proteins. Further functional analysis revealed that YFV infection is associated with mitochondrial damage and dysfunction, which coincides with formation of virus-induced SGs. Together, we propose that YFV-induced SGs may be involved not only in the modulation of cellular homeostasis but also in influencing mitochondrial functions.

articles.title: Nurses' Attitudes and Experiences With Generative AI in Clinical Practice: Qualitative Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The rapid advancement of generative AI (GenAI) holds transformative potential for clinical nursing practice, yet its integration also brings significant risks and uncertainties. Despite growing discourse on AI in health care, frontline nurses' firsthand experiences, perceptions, and practical needs regarding GenAI remain largely under-synthesized in the existing literature.

OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aimed to synthesize qualitative evidence to clarify the core themes related to clinical nurses' perceptions, experiences, obstacles, and requirements when using GenAI in real-world clinical settings.

METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across 10 electronic databases (PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, ProQuest Dissertations and Theses, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, VIP Information, SinoMed, and Wanfang) for records published between January 2018 and June 2026. Eligible studies included qualitative and mixed methods studies involving registered nurses that explored their perceptions and experiences of GenAI in clinical practice. Two independent reviewers (MMW and CYZ) performed study selection, quality appraisal, and data extraction, with disagreements resolved by consensus. Quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklist for Qualitative Research. Extracted data encompassed study characteristics, participant demographics, and GenAI-related contextual factors. Data synthesis followed Thomas and Harden's 3-phase thematic synthesis: initial inductive coding generated descriptive themes, which were subsequently integrated with the Technology Acceptance Model for Artificial Intelligence in Nursing (TAM-AIN) framework to develop higher-order analytical themes. Certainty in the evidence was evaluated using the GRADE-CERQual (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation-Confidence in the Evidence from Reviews of Qualitative Research).

RESULTS: Of the 4350 initially identified records, 13 studies from 6 countries (China: n=6; Saudi Arabia: n=3; United States, Singapore, Australia, and South Korea: n=1 each) met the inclusion criteria, encompassing qualitative data from 234 registered nurses. Three main themes emerged: patterns of nurses' engagement with GenAI (ranging from passive observation to proactive integration), multidimensional perceived threats to adoption (functional, professional, and accountability-related), and the moderating role of organizational readiness, which influenced whether these threats hindered or facilitated GenAI uptake in practice. The GRADE-CERQual assessment showed moderate to high confidence in all findings.

CONCLUSIONS: Nurses' engagement with GenAI ranges from passive observation to proactive integration, accompanied by legitimate concerns about functional reliability, professional role displacement, and accountability ambiguity. The moderating role of organizational readiness further highlights that training, tool optimization, and institutional governance remain critical yet often unmet. These findings necessitate coordinated efforts across workforce development, technological design, and regulatory frameworks. Future research should prioritize the development of clinically validated, context-aware GenAI systems that incorporate human-in-the-loop oversight, ensuring that efficiency gains do not compromise the delivery of compassionate, person-centered care.

articles.title: Is Obesity Severity Associated With Increased Postoperative Morbidity after Minimally Invasive Appendectomy? A 2020-2024 NSQIP Propensity Score-matched Analysis.
articles.abstract: BackgroundObesity may increase morbidity after minimally invasive appendectomy (MIA). We evaluated 30-day outcomes by obesity status and severity.MethodsUsing the 2020-2024 ACS NSQIP Participant Use Files, patients with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2) were compared with those without obesity, and class III obesity (BMI ≥40 kg/m2) with class I-II obesity. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed. Outcomes included mortality, conversion to open surgery, surgical site infection (SSI), organ-related complications, operative time, and length of stay. Sensitivity analyses adjusted for residual comorbidity imbalance using multivariable logistic regression.ResultsAmong 211,221 patients, 78,659 (37.2%) had obesity. PSM yielded 78,567 pairs for the main comparison and 14,203 for the subgroup comparison. Obesity was associated with higher odds of superficial SSI (OR 1.75; 95% CI 1.58-1.94), deep incisional SSI (OR 1.70; 95% CI 1.28-2.26), conversion (OR 1.33; 95% CI 1.06-1.67), and renal insufficiency (OR 1.62; 95% CI 1.32-1.98). Class III vs class I-II obesity was associated with higher odds of superficial SSI (OR 1.80; 95% CI 1.48-2.18), deep incisional SSI (OR 3.09; 95% CI 1.61-5.93), and renal insufficiency (OR 2.23; 95% CI 1.50-3.31). After additional adjustment, incisional SSI associations persisted in both comparisons, whereas conversion and renal insufficiency associations were no longer significant.ConclusionsMIA showed a favorable safety profile in patients with obesity, with low absolute mortality and major complication rates. SSI associations persisted after adjustment, including class III vs class I-II obesity.

articles.title: Digital Health Intervention to Optimize Heart Failure Management After Hospital Discharge in Brazil (OPT-HF): A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Barriers to optimizing guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for heart failure include infrequent clinical visits, clinician inertia, and poor patient knowledge. Digital health interventions (DHIs) may mitigate these barriers, but evidence from low- and middle-income countries is limited. We evaluated whether a DHI would improve GDMT use and other outcomes in Brazil.

METHODS: We enrolled adults admitted for heart failure with ejection fraction <50% and GDMT gaps (≥1 GDMT class not started or ≥2 classes ≤50% target dose) across 5 Brazilian public hospitals from November 2023 to August 2025. Participants were randomized to usual care or the DHI comprising a patient-facing app linked to a provider dashboard, supporting nurse-led remote monitoring, cardiologist teleconsultations, and self-care education. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in mean heart failure GDMT score (0-12) at 90 days. Secondary outcomes included differences in health status, self-care, hospitalization rates, and all-cause mortality. Intention-to-treat analyses used baseline-adjusted linear regression and estimated risk ratios.

RESULTS: Among 154 randomized patients (DHI: 87; usual care: 67), mean age was 65±14 years; 62% were male, 66% were Black, 44% had ≤4 years of education, and 68% were New York Heart Association class III/IV. Primary outcome data were available for 141 participants (91.6%; DHI: 81; usual care: 60). Mean GDMT scores increased from 7.2 in both groups to 10.5 with DHI versus 7.5 with usual care at 90 days (changes: +3.3 versus +0.3 points; adjusted difference, 3.01 [95% CI, 2.30-3.73]; P<0.001). A borderline difference was observed in health status (7.89; P=0.052). Improvements were observed in self-care (β=14.79 [95% CI, 9.78-19.81]; P<0.001). Fewer participants were hospitalized with DHI than usual care (9/87 [10.3%] versus 15/67 [22.4%]; risk ratio, 0.46 [95% CI, 0.21-0.99]; P=0.048), with no statistically significant difference for deaths.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients hospitalized for heart failure in Brazil, a context-adapted DHI improved GDMT use, self-care, and reduced hospitalizations. These findings provide early randomized evidence supporting DHI for GDMT optimization in low-resource settings.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://ensaiosclinicos.gov.br/rg/RBR-10vpf9bm; Unique identifier: U1111-1295-1864.

articles.title: Severe Rosuvastatin-Associated Rhabdomyolysis and Dialysis-Requiring Acute Kidney Injury in an Octogenarian Patient: A Case Report.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Statins are fundamental to dyslipidemia management, but high-potency rosuvastatin can cause myotoxicity in vulnerable older patients. We present a probable case of rosuvastatin-associated rhabdomyolysis causing stage 3 acute kidney injury requiring hemodialysis in an 87-year-old woman with polypharmacy, highlighting clinical management and outcomes. CASE REPORT An octogenarian presented with progressive muscle weakness and inability to ambulate 20 days after starting rosuvastatin (20 mg/day), ezetimibe (10 mg/day), and evogliptin (5 mg/day). Laboratory tests revealed creatine kinase above 4267 U/L, serum creatinine 6.13 mg/dL, blood urea 220 mg/dL, severe hyponatremia (122 mEq/L), bicarbonate 15 mEq/L, and elevated transaminases (AST 419 U/L; ALT 342 U/L). Direct bilirubin (0.2 mg/dL) and gamma-glutamyl transferase (28 U/L) levels were normal, excluding primary hepatocellular or cholestatic liver injury. Urinalysis findings supported myoglobinuria. Refractory oliguria despite aggressive intravenous fluid resuscitation required emergency hemodialysis with sodium correction to prevent osmotic demyelination; rhabdomyolysis prompted rosuvastatin cessation. Concomitant nephrotoxic and renally cleared medications were temporarily withheld. During a 30-day hospital stay with 8 hemodialysis sessions, dialytic support was discontinued on Day 23 (serum creatinine 1.61 mg/dL). After physical rehabilitation, the patient was discharged on Day 30 with full motor strength (MRC grade 5/5). At 3 months, serum creatinine had stabilized (1.40 mg/dL; eGFR 38 mL/min/1.73 m²; creatine kinase 62 U/L) and independent ambulation continued. CONCLUSIONS Statin-associated rhabdomyolysis in older adults can be followed by renal recovery with dialysis independence and functional recovery through early drug cessation, fluid resuscitation, and timely dialytic support. Formal Naranjo assessment (score 5) classified the reaction as "probable," highlighting the multifactorial risks of geriatric polypharmacy.

articles.title: SECNet: Differentiable Mask-Driven Spatiotemporal Learning for Video-Based Spontaneous Echo Contrast Severity Detection.
articles.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
articles.abstract: Spontaneous Echo Contrast (SEC), characterized by smoke-like dynamic echogenicity in trans esophageal echocardiography (TEE), serves as a critical imaging biomarker for assessing thromboembolic risk. However, current diagnostic approaches depend on manual interpretation or regression-based algorithms, which are labor-intensive, prone to inconsistency, and limited in generalizability. To address these challenges, we propose SECNet, an end-to-end deep learning framework for auto mated SEC detection in TEE videos. SECNet incorporates two key components: (1) a region-of-interest segmentation module that accurately localizes SEC-prone cardiac structures while suppressing surrounding noise; and (2) a spa tiotemporal feature extraction module that captures both temporal dynamics and spatial distribution of SEC. These modules are linked through a novel differentiable mask guided bridging mechanism that enables joint optimization of localization and representation learning. Trained on a clinical dataset of 1,106 annotated TEE videos, SECNet achieves 93.7% accuracy and a 90.0% F1-score, outper forming the compared methods by 3.1-23.3 percentage points in accuracy. An auxiliary experiment on EchoNet Dynamic further demonstrates the applicability of the architecture to a related echocardiographic video-analysis task. This study supports standardized and reproducible SEC assessment to assist thromboembolic risk evaluation in clinical workflows.

articles.title: Context-Aware Graph Causality Inference for Few-Shot Molecular Property Prediction.
articles.journal: IEEE transactions on computational biology and bioinformatics
articles.abstract: Molecular property prediction is becoming one of the major applications of graph learning in Web-based services, e.g., online protein structure prediction and drug discovery. A key challenge arises in few-shot scenarios, where only a few labeled molecules are available for predicting unseen properties. Recently, several studies have used in-context learning to capture relationships among molecules and properties, but they face two limitations: (1) exploiting prior knowledge of functional groups that are causally linked to properties and (2) identifying key substructures directly correlated with properties. We propose CaMol, a context-aware graph causality inference framework, to address these challenges by using a causal inference perspective, assuming that each molecule consists of a latent causal structure that determines a specific property. First, we introduce a context graph that encodes chemical knowledge by linking functional groups, molecules, and properties to guide the discovery of causal substructures. Second, we propose a learnable atom soft-masking strategy to disentangle causal substructures from confounding ones. Third, we introduce a chemically grounded augmented distribution intervener that holds the learned property-relevant representation $C$ fixed while varying complementary functional-group representations sampled from other molecular contexts. This mechanism reduces dependence on context-specific correlations and promotes intervention-robust prediction. Experiments on diverse molecular datasets showed that CaMol achieved superior accuracy and sample efficiency in few-shot tasks, showing its generalizability to unseen properties. Also, the discovered causal substructures were strongly aligned with chemical knowledge about functional groups, supporting the model interpretability.

articles.title: Atorvastatin inhibits PASMC proliferation in pulmonary hypertension via the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3/IL-1β pathway.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a progressive disorder leading to right heart failure. This study explored how atorvastatin (ATO) alleviates PH using a multidisciplinary approach. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and dynamics analysis were employed to identify ATO targets. A PH rat model was established via monocrotaline (40 mg/kg) subcutaneous injection, and animals were divided into CT, PH, and ATO (10 mg/kg/day) groups. Hemodynamics, histopathology, and immunofluorescence were evaluated. In vitro, pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs) were exposed to PDGF-BB (20 ng/ml) with or without ATO (10-8 M). Cell proliferation was measured by CCK-8 and PCNA expression, and key proteins in the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3/IL-1β pathway were analyzed via western blot. siRNA-NLRP3 was used to verify NLRP3's role in PASMCs proliferation. Network pharmacology identified 277 common targets, with KEGG analysis linking ATO to the NF-κB signaling pathway. Docking showed strong binding affinity between ATO and TLR4 (-6.3 kCal/mol) through non-covalent interactions with ASN464 and PHE487. In vivo, ATO reduced right ventricular systolic pressure, right ventricular hypertrophy and pulmonary artery thickening. Immunofluorescence confirmed NLRP3 co-localization with α-SMA+ PASMCs. ATO downregulated TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3/IL-1β protein expression in PH rats' lungs and PASMCs, and suppressed PDGF-BB-induced PASMCs proliferation via the pathway inhibition. Direct knockdown of NLRP3 reduced both PDGF-BB-induced and non-PDGF-BB-induced proliferation of PASMCs, and ATO primarily inhibited PASMCs proliferation through NLRP3. These findings demonstrate that ATO directly targets TLR4 to inhibit NF-κB/NLRP3/IL-1β signaling, thereby reducing PASMCs proliferation and suppressing PH progression.

articles.title: Micropeptides: challenges and opportunities in cardiovascular pharmacology.
articles.abstract: Micropeptides are small proteins that generally comprise fewer than 100 amino acids and are translated from short or noncanonical open reading frames. They were long overlooked, but their role is being actively explored as biologically active regulators with potential pharmacological relevance. Advances in ribosome profiling, proteogenomics, peptidomics, and computational modelling have enabled the identification and characterization of a substantially larger repertoire of micropeptides. Yet, it is important to focus on rigorous validation of endogenous translation, molecular targets, concentration-dependent activity, and peptide-specific effects. In particular, cardiovascular micropeptides can regulate myocardial calcium handling and contractility, exemplified by DWORF, which activates sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase 2a and has shown therapeutic potential in multiple preclinical models of cardiomyopathy and heart failure. Other candidates, including mitoregulin, mitolamban, BRAWNIN, IAMP, SPAAR, and MFRLP, have been linked to distinct aspects of mitochondrial bioenergetics, inflammatory signalling, ischemia-reperfusion injury, angiogenesis, vascular smooth-muscle phenotypic switching, and arterial remodeling. Collectively, these findings suggest that micropeptides may provide novel therapeutic targets or pharmacological tools across several cardiovascular conditions, including heart failure, ischemia-reperfusion injury, and vascular remodeling. However, clinical translation will require advances in tissue-specific delivery, control of expression and stoichiometry, pharmacokinetic characterization, safety assessment, biomarker development, and demonstration of reproducible effectiveness in human-relevant and large-animal models before evaluation in clinical trials.

articles.title: Reproductive Health in Monogenic Kidney Disease: Practical Guidance for Fertility, Genetic Counseling, and Pregnancy Care.
articles.journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN
articles.abstract: Monogenic kidney diseases, including autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), Alport spectrum disorders, Fabry disease, and monogenic podocytopathies presenting as focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), increasingly affect people of reproductive age. Reproductive care extends beyond pregnancy to fertility, menstrual and sexual health, contraception, assisted reproduction, inheritance counseling, and long-term shared decision-making. This review uses these four disease groups to illustrate distinct counseling challenges arising from autosomal dominant, X-linked, autosomal recessive, and genetically heterogenous inheritance, including the underrecognized disease burden in heterozygous women with X-linked Alport syndrome or Fabry's disease. Across diseases, adverse maternal and fetal outcomes are driven primarily by reduced kidney function, chronic hypertension, proteinuria, prior preeclampsia and major extrarenal disease, whereas genotype, inheritance pattern, and syndromic features further shape counseling and reproductive genetic decisions. Preconception counseling should integrate maternal risk stratification; discontinuation or planned transition of fetotoxic agents, such as renin-angiotensin system inhibitors, tolvaptan, SGLT2 inhibitors, mycophenolate, and migalastat; and genetic counseling that addresses recurrence risk, cascade testing, and reproductive options, including prenatal diagnosis and preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic disorders (PGT-M). During pregnancy, close co-management by nephrology, maternal-fetal medicine, and genetics is essential to control blood pressure, provide low-dose aspirin prophylaxis, monitor kidney function and proteinuria, distinguish preeclampsia from progressive glomerular disease, and anticipate disease-specific complications such as cyst infection, intracranial aneurysm, nephrotic syndrome, and cardiac arrhythmia. Postpartum care should include medication re-optimization, breastfeeding counseling, kidney and cardiovascular surveillance, and revisiting contraception and future reproductive goals. Reproductive decision-making should be nondirective and centered on patient values, access to care, and tolerance for uncertainty. Evidence remains limited, largely retrospective, and enriched for milder disease, particularly regarding fertility outcomes, male reproductive implications, the reproductive safety of emerging targeted therapies, and genotype-specific pregnancy risk, underscoring the need for prospective multicenter studies.

articles.title: suPAR Is Associated with Progressive Albuminuria in Type 1 Diabetes: Findings from the PERL Trial.
articles.journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Soluble urokinase plasminogen activator receptor (suPAR) is an immune-derived glycoprotein implicated in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and glomerulopathy. suPAR predicts CKD progression, but whether it is associated with longitudinal albuminuria worsening, including in patients without established albuminuria, is untested in diabetic kidney disease (DKD). We examined this in type 1 diabetes using albumin excretion rate (AER) trajectory.

DESIGN, SETTING, PARTICIPANTS, MEASUREMENTS: Post hoc analysis of 506 participants with a single baseline suPAR measurement from the PERL trial, a 3-year multicenter randomized controlled trial in type 1 diabetes with early-to-moderate DKD. Linear mixed models estimated suPAR's association with AER and iohexol-measured glomerular filtration rate (iGFR) trajectories. Structural equation modeling assessed whether albuminuria level accounted for the association between suPAR and iGFR decline.

RESULTS: Mean age was 51 years, 34% female, diabetes duration 35 years, iGFR 68 mL/min/1.73 m2, median AER 44 μg/min, and median suPAR 3.43 ng/mL. Each suPAR doubling was associated with 11.6% per year additional AER increase (P<0.001), with a dose-response across quartiles and robust to sensitivity analyses. Time-lagged analysis confirmed the association with subsequent AER worsening (P=0.004). Among 125 eGFR-decline qualifiers (predominantly normoalbuminuric), higher suPAR was associated with accelerated AER worsening (+13.1%/yr per doubling, P=0.005; +11.7%/yr in the 101 normoalbuminuric), although none crossed the proteinuria threshold. suPAR was also associated with AER category progression (HR 1.61, P=0.002) and ≥40% eGFR loss (HR 1.86, P=0.01). suPAR was not independently associated with GFR slope (total effect P=0.49); its association with lower GFR was accounted for by albuminuria level (indirect effect -0.59 mL/min/yr per doubling, P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: suPAR was independently associated with progressive albuminuria worsening in type 1 diabetes with DKD, including accelerated worsening among normoalbuminuric patients. These associations are consistent with suPAR marking active podocyte injury and support its evaluation for early risk stratification.

articles.title: CD8+ T cells and humoral immunity may mitigate the effects of antibody-dependent enhancement: implications for dengue vaccine design.
articles.abstract: Dengue vaccine development is complicated by antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE)-a phenomenon in which antibodies paradoxically boost viral growth. Signals of immune-mediated enhancement were observed in the CYD-TDV (Dengvaxia) vaccine trials, but have not yet been reported for trials of TAK-003 (Qdenga). To better understand how prior immunity influences dengue infection outcomes, we developed a mechanistic within-host model of acute dengue infection dynamics that incorporates ADE as well as humoral and CD8+ T-cell immunity. Model simulations illustrate a potentially very important difference between enhancement by antibody, enhancement by humoral immunity, and enhanced severity of secondary infection. Model results also suggest that recipients of CYD-TDV may have been more likely to experience immune-mediated enhancement because of its yellow fever virus backbone and corresponding lack of dengue-specific CD8+ T-cell epitopes. The model provides a possible explanation for differences in reported outcomes of dengue vaccine trials and suggests incorporating DENV backbones from all four serotypes as a potentially promising way forward in the design of future dengue vaccines.IMPORTANCEVaccines are typically designed to elicit humoral (antibody-mediated) immunity, and antibody titers are commonly used as correlates of protection. Because CD8+ T-cell responses are more challenging to measure, they are not typically used as correlates of protection and have received comparatively less attention. For viruses such as dengue, where antibodies may increase viral replication and thus the risk of severe disease through antibody-dependent enhancement, it is necessary to understand how humoral and cellular immunity interact during infection. Our model suggests that low antibody levels can enhance viral replication but that this effect can be mitigated by humoral and CD8+ T-cell immunity. This result offers a hypothesis to explain the observed differences in outcomes between the CYD-TDV and TAK-003 trials and suggests that evaluating CD8+ T-cell responses alongside antibody titers may be important for designing and assessing the safety and efficacy of future dengue vaccines.

articles.title: A Methodology for Calculating Casualties from Nuclear Explosions.
articles.abstract: Recent threats by Russian politicians to attack NATO countries with nuclear weapons provide an impetus to develop a well-defined framework for assessing the potential human impacts of such a conflict. Here we propose a new methodology for computing the potential casualties and fatalities from a nuclear explosion over a populated area. Considerable information is available regarding human responses to explosive shock waves, ionizing nuclear radiation, and intense heat radiance, compiled from medical studies and wartime experiences. In the case of nuclear weapons, the main effects of blast overpressure, initial neutron and gamma ray fluxes, and thermal radiation are readily calculated as a function of distance from a detonation point once the energy yield and height of burst are specified. Combining information on nuclear weapon effects and human responses to such effects, a new probabilistic model is developed to estimate the rates of morbidity and mortality in a nuclear attack. Furthermore, possible hazards to the immediate survivors due to mass fires ignited by weapon bursts are addressed. Among the data utilized to validate our casualty model are observations from the Hiroshima and Nagasaki nuclear bombings. Extrapolations of possible outcomes to much larger modern strategic nuclear weapons are also illustrated.

articles.title: Semilunar nucleus neurons are highly excitable and potentiated by group I mGluRs to drive descending excitation to the mouse MNTB.
articles.abstract: Medial nucleus of the trapezoid body (MNTB) neurons receive one of the largest synapses in the mammalian brain, the calyx of Held; however, multiple studies reported additional non-calyceal excitatory inputs of largely unresolved origin to MNTB neurons. Most recently, the semilunar nucleus (SLN) was identified as a potential source of such non-calyceal input in the rat. To elucidate the function of this novel pathway, we investigated the connectivity and physiology of the mouse SLN, with particular focus on neuromodulation by group I metabotropic glutamate receptors (mGluRs). Viral tracing not only confirmed the SLN-MNTB pathway in mice, but also revealed that MNTB-projecting SLN neurons received their input from the ipsilateral auditory cortex. Physiological characterization of SLN neurons using whole-cell patch-clamp recordings showed that SLN neurons, unlike most other auditory brainstem neurons, were intrinsically highly excitable. Electrical stimulation of the fibre tracts located dorsal to the SLN, evoked small, slow AMPA receptor-mediated EPSCs in SLN neurons that readily summated temporally. Immunolabeling revealed a heterogeneous expression of mGluR1 and mGluR5 across SLN neurons. A subpopulation of SLN neurons exhibited spontaneous action potential firing at resting membrane potential. Pharmacological activation of group I mGluRs further increased spontaneous firing of SLN neurons. Probing for functional connectivity between SLN and the ipsilateral MNTB, fibre tracts dorsal and lateral to the MNTB were stimulated, eliciting primarily non-calyceal AMPA receptor-mediated EPSCs in MNTB neurons. These findings suggest that SLN output may provide a glutamatergic tonic drive to MNTB neurons, potentially modulating their temporal processing. KEY POINTS: MNTB receives a descending input from the ipsilateral auditory cortex via SLN. SLN neurons are highly excitable during development and into maturation, with a subset exhibiting spontaneous firing at resting membrane potential. Descending glutamatergic input to SLN is small and slow, and shows consistent temporal summation. Group I mGluRs further enhance spontaneous firing of SLN neurons and both mGluR1 and mGluR5 are expressed in the SLN. Descending ipsilateral projections to MNTB neurons primarily drive glutamatergic, non-calyceal inputs.

articles.title: Firearm Injury Prevention Bystander Intervention for Adolescents in Shooting Sports: A Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Firearm injury is the leading cause of death for adolescents in the US. Few adolescent firearm injury prevention interventions exist that center partnership with firearm-owning communities.

OBJECTIVE: To measure the impact of the Guardians 4 Health shooting sports firearm injury prevention bystander intervention among youth in 4-H Shooting Sports (4HSS).

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This parallel cluster randomized clinical trial enrolled youth in the US at 4HSS clubs with 6 or more adolescents and the ability to use video conferencing technology. Sites were enrolled from June 2022 to July 2024; they were block randomized and stratified by rurality and state-level child access prevention laws. Intervention sites received the shooting sports firearm injury prevention curriculum, and wait-listed control sites continued standard 4-H programming. Outcome data were collected by survey and aggregated across 5 hypothetical scenarios at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months. Analyses followed intention-to-treat principles. Complete-case analyses used linear mixed models adjusting for baseline and randomization variables; multilevel multiple imputations were adjusted for baseline covariates.

INTERVENTION: A 3-session novel adolescent firearm injury prevention bystander intervention curriculum, previously developed in conjunction with 4HSS.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was behavioral intention to use bystander intervention. Secondary outcomes were knowledge, subjective norms, attitudes, and perceived behavioral control.

RESULTS: A total of 61 sites from 28 states were randomized (32 to intervention and 29 to control); 50 sites (intervention, 26 sites of 250 youth; control, 24 sites of 174 youth) completed baseline data collection. Of 424 participants, the median (IQR) age was 14 (13-16) years; 226 were male (53.3%). Among 333 participants with nonmissing family firearm ownership data, 291 reported ownership (87.4%). Linear mixed-model analyses showed a small difference in behavioral intention between groups at 3 months (Β = 0.10; 95% CI, 0.003-0.19) but not at 6 months; multiple imputation results were similar. Significant positive intervention effects on firearm injury risk knowledge were observed at both time points in both analyses and on perceived behavioral control at 3 months.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this nationwide cluster randomized clinical trial of a codeveloped adolescent firearm injury bystander intervention curriculum demonstrated a small short-term positive effect on intention to use bystander interventions and a durable effect on firearm injury risk knowledge. Findings support partnership between shooting sports organizations and public health researchers and the value of the firearm injury prevention bystander intervention within 4HSS. Consideration of boosters and larger-scale evaluation is warranted.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04804189.

articles.title: SGLT2 Inhibitors, Potassium Binders, Pregnancy After Kidney Donation, and More From Kidney Week.
Metabolic and biochemical predictors of glycemic response after bariatric surgery: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bariatric and metabolic surgery is one of the most effective treatments for severe obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), promoting metabolic changes beyond weight loss. However, the biochemical determinants of postoperative glycemic response remain incompletely understood.

METHODS: A scoping review was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus were searched for studies published between 2016 and 2025 evaluating metabolic and biochemical variables associated with glycemic outcomes after bariatric surgery.

RESULTS: Twenty-two studies were included, comprising eight randomized controlled trials and fourteen cohort studies. Bariatric surgery was consistently associated with reductions in HbA1c and significant rates of T2DM remission. Improvements in insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), beta-cell function, and incretin response-particularly GLP-1-were associated with better outcomes. Reductions in inflammatory markers, including IL-6, IFN-γ, and TNF-α, were also reported.

CONCLUSION: Glycemic improvement after bariatric surgery is associated with complex metabolic interactions involving insulin sensitivity, incretin modulation, and inflammatory changes. These findings support the role of bariatric and metabolic surgery as a metabolic and immunometabolic intervention, although the descriptive design of a scoping review precludes causal inference.

articles.title: Mesenchymal Stromal Cell-Derived Secretome for Diabetic Foot Ulcers: Therapeutic Potential, Challenges in Clinical Translation, and Future Directions.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) represent one of the most challenging chronic complications of diabetes mellitus, developing in approximately 15 to 25% of affected individuals over their lifetime and imposing a substantial burden on healthcare systems worldwide. Even with coordinated, multidisciplinary wound management strategies, a substantial proportion of these ulcers fail to heal in a timely manner, predisposing patients to secondary infection, lower-limb amputation, and elevated mortality risk. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) have long been investigated as a regenerative treatment option given their reparative capacity; however, translating live-cell therapy into routine practice has been hindered by limited post-transplantation cell viability, inefficient tissue engraftment, and the practical difficulties of large-scale cell manufacturing. As an alternative, attention has shifted toward the MSC-derived secretome a complex mixture of extracellular vesicles, cytokines, chemokines, trophic factors, and microRNAs which appears to preserve much of the parent cells regenerative and immune-modulating activity without the drawbacks associated with administering live cells.

METHODS: In this review, we examine the biological composition and mechanistic actions of the MSC secretome as they relate to DFU repair, focusing specifically on strategies for topical application.

RESULTS: Evidence from preclinical diabetic wound models points to accelerated wound closure, stimulation of new blood vessel formation, remodeling of the extracellular matrix, and dampening of persistent inflammatory activity following secretome treatment. Findings from early clinical trials have likewise been encouraging, with rates of complete wound closure ranging from 62 to 100% across two limited studies enrolling between 10 and 110 participants, with outcomes varying according to the cellular origin of the secretome, the route by which it was delivered, and differences in study design. Several barriers still limit clinical adoption. GMP-compliant production protocols have not been harmonized across manufacturers. Batches vary from one production run to the next. No validated assay yet exists to measure biological potency. Long-term safety data remain limited, and questions about the appropriate dose are still unresolved. Looking ahead, engineered or modified secretome formulations, combination therapies, and smart wound-monitoring devices may help improve outcomes further.

CONCLUSION: Current evidence supports the MSC secretome as a promising, cell-free option for DFU management. Its place in standard clinical care will depend on large, multicenter randomized controlled trials and on establishing consistent, standardized manufacturing practices.

articles.title: Pre-pregnancy maternal steatotic liver disease and offspring neurodevelopmental disorders: a nationwide cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/PURPOSE: Maternal metabolic health before pregnancy is increasingly linked to offspring neurodevelopment, but metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), the most common chronic liver disease worldwide, has not been examined in this context. We investigated whether maternal steatotic liver disease (SLD) phenotypes identified before pregnancy are associated with offspring neurodevelopmental disorders.

METHODS: In this nationwide Korean cohort of 778,401 mother-child pairs, maternal pre-pregnancy phenotypes (no SLD, MASLD, and alcohol-involved SLD) were defined using the fatty liver index (FLI), cardiometabolic criteria, alcohol intake, and diagnostic codes. Offspring were followed through 2022 for registration-confirmed intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and for claims-based attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Cox regression estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with and without adjustment for body mass index (BMI), diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidemia in addition to other covariates.

RESULTS: Without this adjustment, MASLD was associated with intellectual disability (HR 1.72, 95% CI 1.52-1.96), ASD (1.42, 1.22-1.66), and ADHD (1.22, 1.15-1.30). After this adjustment, HRs were 1.05 (0.89-1.24), 1.18 (0.98-1.44), and 1.09 (1.01-1.17), respectively. The ADHD estimate was smaller when at least two separate claims were required (1.06, 0.98-1.15). Estimates for alcohol-involved SLD were imprecise.

CONCLUSION: Pre-pregnancy MASLD was associated with higher risks of offspring neurodevelopmental disorders in analyses without adjustment for maternal BMI and metabolic conditions. These associations were substantially attenuated after adjustment; a modest ADHD association remained only under the least stringent claims-based definition and should be interpreted with caution. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant confirmation with pregnancy-specific exposure assessment and sibling-comparison designs.

articles.title: Real-World Toxicity and Outcomes of KEYNOTE-522-Style Neoadjuvant Pembrolizumab for Triple-Negative Breast Cancer in Australia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Following the KEYNOTE-522 trial, neoadjuvant pembrolizumab with chemotherapy (chemo-IO) became the standard of care in Australia for patients with triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). In KEYNOTE-522, patients achieved significantly higher pathological complete response (pCR) at the cost of more immune-related adverse events (irAEs). The objective of this study was to collect real-world data on the use of neoadjuvant pembrolizumab in patients with TNBC to identify patterns of irAEs and outcomes.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Retrospective data were collected across three tertiary hospitals in Melbourne, Australia, for all patients diagnosed with TNBC who commenced neoadjuvant pembrolizumab combined with chemotherapy from December 2022 until August 2024. Data were collected until October 30, 2025, and included baseline demographics, neoadjuvant treatment and irAEs, breast surgery, and pCR rates, and were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Kaplan-Meier estimates.

RESULTS: Fifty-four female patients received neoadjuvant chemo-IO (median age = 52 years, median follow-up = 26 months). Three patients had a history of autoimmune disease. 69% had nodal involvement at diagnosis. 65% of patients experienced at least one irAE, most commonly thyroid dysfunction (28%), adrenal dysfunction (20%), colitis (9%), and arthralgias (9%). 43% of those with irAEs were hospitalized, 9% required intensive care, and 51% have ongoing sequelae. The median time to onset of irAE was 84 days (22-505 days). 50% achieved pCR. There was no difference in pCR between those who experienced an irAE and those who did not (p = 0.081).

CONCLUSION: Real-world data show a higher proportion of irAEs associated with neoadjuvant pembrolizumab in TNBC than the original KEYNOTE-522 study, with a notable proportion leading to hospitalization. This information can be used to guide shared decision-making.

articles.title: Changes in left atrial reservoir function and their association with exercise capacity after outpatient cardiac rehabilitation in early-stage heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) improves exercise capacity in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Nonetheless, changes in left atrial (LA) mechanics after outpatient CR and the link between changes in LA function and exercise capacity in early-stage HFpEF remain unclear. Therefore, we aimed to examine changes in LA reservoir function after outpatient CR and its association with exercise capacity in early-stage HFpEF.

METHODS: Echocardiography and cardiopulmonary exercise testing were performed pre- and post-CR in 21 patients with early-stage HFpEF without prior HF hospitalization (median age: 80 years; median HFA-PEFF score: 4). Exercise capacity was assessed by peak oxygen uptake (VO2). Left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LV-GLS) and LA reservoir strain (LASr) were derived using speckle-tracking echocardiography. Early diastolic mitral inflow velocity to mitral annular velocity (E/e') ratio was measured. LA stiffness index was calculated as the ratio of E/e' to LASr.

RESULTS: Peak VO2 (13.3 ± 3.7 to 15.0 ± 3.8 mL/kg/min, p < 0.001) and LASr (20.4 ± 7.3 to 24.2 ± 6.9%, p = 0.002) significantly increased after outpatient CR. The peak VO2 change rate correlated with the LASr and LA stiffness index change rates (r = 0.62, p = 0.003; r = - 0.53, p = 0.017, respectively), but not with the LV-GLS change rate (r = 0.08, p = 0.735). LASr change rate continued to be associated with the peak VO2 change rate after multivariable adjustment in exploratory models.

CONCLUSIONS: In early-stage HFpEF, LA reservoir function increased after outpatient CR, and changes in LA reservoir function were independently associated with changes in exercise capacity.

articles.title: Correction: Translating Guidelines into Practice: Implementation of NT-proBNP Testing for Early Heart Failure Detection in Diabetes, a Narrative Review.
The metabolic role of prolactin in pregnancy.
articles.abstract: Prolactin has evolved from being viewed solely as a lactogenic hormone to being recognized as a key regulator of maternal metabolic adaptation during pregnancy.However, clinical studies have reported apparently conflicting associations between circulating prolactin and gestational diabetes, maternal adiposity and metabolic health, limiting its clinical interpretation despite compelling experimental evidence for its metabolic effects.Experimental models demonstrate that prolactin receptor (Prlr) signalling regulates pregnancy-induced β-cell expansion and insulin secretion, adipose tissue remodelling and maternal energy allocation, while also contributing to the endocrine network governing calcium homeostasis and skeletal adaptation. By contrast, human studies show heterogeneous relationships between circulating prolactin and glucose homeostasis, gestational diabetes, adiposity and lipid metabolism, with limited evidence linking physiological prolactin concentrations to maternal bone remodelling.These discrepancies may partly reflect dynamic changes in prolactin across gestation and differences in maternal metabolic phenotype. Accounting for gestational timing and metabolic context may therefore improve the interpretation of circulating prolactin and help define its contribution to maternal metabolic adaptation across pregnancy and lactation.

articles.title: Dropped Out Before They Ever Competed: A Population-Wide Registry Analysis of Relative Age Effects in Norwegian Track and Field from Age 10 to 25.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Relative age effects (RAEs), the overrepresentation of children born early in the selection year among participants in age-graded sport, shape who enters organised youth sport and who remains in it. The dominant theoretical account locates the generation of RAEs in adolescent talent-selection cycles, predicting amplification through adolescence. If selection instead occurs before children enter organised sport, participation-level inequities would need to be addressed at the entry stage rather than at adolescent talent identification. I tested this prediction using population-wide registry data 2011-2026 from the Norwegian Athletics Federation (87 624 athletes; 1 395 788 performances; the entire competing cohort), comparing birth-quarter distributions across ages 10-25 against monthly birth counts from Statistics Norway. Logistic regression with sex × age interaction tested for adolescent amplification; Manski-style bounds quantified the influence of athletes appearing briefly without a recorded birth date (61% at ages 10-12; overwhelmingly short-career early leavers).

RESULTS: At age 10, the youngest registered competition age, Q1 comprised 28.3% and Q4 19.7% of competitors, against population baselines of 24.6% and 22.9% (   χ 2 = 79.9  , p < 10 - 15    , Cohen's w = 0.10  ). The Q1/Q4 ratio of 1.44 showed no upward age trend through 25 (range 1.36-1.75), and restricting the analysis to ages 13-25, where birth-date coverage is 89-99%, gave the same conclusion. Logistic regression did not support the cumulative-advantage prediction in females (  β age  = - 0.007  , p = 0.46  ), showing only a mild curvilinear elevation in males peaking at age 18-19 ( p = 1.0 × 10 - 5    for the sex × age interaction). First-year retention from age 10 was nearly identical across quarters (Q1-Q4 gap 2-3 pp), confirming the skew was not produced by differential dropout within the registry. Findings were robust to exclusion of the COVID-19 pandemic years.

CONCLUSIONS: In a population-wide individual sport without team selection, the birth-quarter skew is established by age 10 and stable through senior level. This pattern is inconsistent with the cumulative-advantage prediction and points to pre-entry selection. I hypothesise that mastery experience through measurable personal progress retains surviving athletes, a feature less available in team-sport contexts. These findings support directing, and evaluating, efforts to reduce relative-age-related participation inequities at the sport-entry transition rather than only at adolescent talent-identification stages; testing this account in other individual sports and countries is a priority.

articles.title: MRI-based virtual radiographs of the pelvis for assessment of acetabular morphology.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We generated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based virtual radiographs (VRs) from hips with/without intra-articular contrast and compared them with conventional anteroposterior pelvic radiographs (CR) regarding measurement bias, interobserver and intraobserver agreement, and diagnosis of acetabular deformities; we also assessed hip deformity prevalence on VR in asymptomatic participants.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective study of 50 patients (100 hips; mean age 34 years) with femoroacetabular impingement or hip dysplasia undergoing CR and unilateral magnetic resonance arthrography. Additionally, 53 asymptomatic participants underwent noncontrast MRI. Segmentation of the osseous pelvis was performed on T1-weighted volume interpolated breathhold examination (VIBE) Dixon MRI using 3D nnU-Net, pseudo-computed tomography generation, and cone-beam projection to generate VR. Acetabular coverage (lateral center edge angle (LCE), acetabular index (AI), anterior/posterior coverage, extrusion index (EI)), and acetabular version were compared between CR and VR. Interobserver agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and κ statistics; bias with Bland-Altman analysis.

RESULTS: Interobserver agreement for VR ranged from moderate to almost perfect (ICC/κ 0.60-0.94), except for the AI. LCE showed no significant bias with ( - 0.2° ± 2.5, p = 0.663) or without contrast ( - 0.2° ± 2.2, p = 0.530). Systematic differences occurred for AI, EI, anterior/posterior coverage, and ischial spine sign; 57-75% of discrepancies were within CR interobserver variation. Diagnostic classification showed substantial agreement between CR and VR (κ = 0.62), comparable to CR interobserver agreement (κ = 0.70). In asymptomatic participants, 13% had acetabular dysplasia, 68% normal coverage, and 19% overcoverage.

CONCLUSION: MRI-based VR provides acetabular morphology assessment comparable to CR and enables radiation-free evaluation in symptomatic patients and asymptomatic populations.

KEY POINTS: Question Can MRI-based virtual radiographs reproduce conventional radiographic measurements of acetabular morphology, enabling radiation-free two-dimensional assessment in symptomatic patients and asymptomatic populations? Findings The lateral center-edge angle showed no significant bias between virtual and conventional radiographs; diagnostic classification of acetabular deformities agreed substantially (κ = 0.62), comparable to conventional radiograph interobserver agreement. Relevance Statement MRI-derived virtual radiographs can provide acetabular measurements comparable to conventional radiographs without ionizing radiation, supporting integration into three-dimensional surgical planning and enabling assessment in young patients and population-based cohorts where repeated radiographs are undesirable.

articles.title: Mycological and molecular confirmation of Trichophyton benhamiae infection in a Guinea pig.
articles.abstract: Trichophyton benhamiae is an emerging zoonotic dermatophyte of increasing clinical and epidemiological importance. This study reports a case of T. benhamiae infection in a pet guinea pig, identified from a skin scraping obtained from a lesion and submitted to our laboratory for diagnostic investigation. The clinical specimen was cultured using standard mycological methods, and the resulting isolate was evaluated based on its macroscopic and microscopic characteristics and by matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS) analysis. MALDI-TOF MS matched the isolate to the database reference entry designated "Microsporum audouinii_canis" with a score of 2.093. For definitive species identification, the internal transcribed spacer (ITS) region was amplified using the ITS1 and ITS4 primers, and the resulting amplicon was sequenced and compared with GenBank data. Sequence analysis revealed 99.64% sequence identity to T. benhamiae. Complete clinical resolution was achieved following approximately three weeks of treatment with topical ketoconazole cream, with no recurrence during the four-month follow-up period. At the four-month follow-up, direct KOH examination and fungal culture of samples collected from the previously affected site were negative. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of a culturally and molecularly confirmed T. benhamiae infection in a pet guinea pig in Türkiye.

articles.title: Volume status as a potential state-dependent modifier of obstructive sleep apnea severity in chronic kidney disease and dialysis: a narrative review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This narrative review examines whether volume status may act as an underrecognized, state-dependent modifier of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and dialysis-dependent kidney failure. The main question was which links between extracellular volume, rostral fluid shift, and OSA are supported by empirical studies, and which implications for assessment and treatment remain hypothesis-generating.

METHODS: Evidence was synthesized from thematic searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to May 1, 2026, supplemented by reference-list review. An integrative narrative approach used purposive study selection and qualitative interpretation rather than systematic screening, pooled analysis, or formal risk-of-bias assessment.

RESULTS: Sleep apnea is common in CKD and end-stage kidney disease, particularly when objective testing is used. Small physiological and imaging studies, mainly in hemodialysis patients, associate fluid overload and regional fluid measures with sleep apnea severity. Responses to fluid removal are heterogeneous, and some intervention studies include both obstructive and central events. These findings do not establish a reproducible volume-sensitive OSA phenotype. Effects on sleep-study timing, positive airway pressure (PAP) requirements, residual events, drug-induced sleep endoscopy, and upper-airway intervention outcomes remain unestablished.

CONCLUSION: Volume status is a plausible state-dependent modifier of OSA severity in selected patients, supported predominantly by small dialysis studies. Distinguishing systemic from regional fluid and transient measurement states from reproducible patient characteristics provides a framework for testable hypotheses. Current evidence does not justify changes to sleep-study scheduling, PAP management, or upper-airway treatment selection.

articles.title: Pharmacological Management of Atrial Fibrillation Across the Heart Failure Ejection Fraction Spectrum: Rate Control, Rhythm Control, and Beyond.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To summarise the contemporary pharmacological management of atrial fibrillation (AF) in heart failure (HF), focusing on rate and rhythm control and upstream therapies across the ejection fraction spectrum.

RECENT FINDINGS: Rate control remains a cornerstone of AF management, particularly in permanent AF or haemodynamically fragile patients, with beta-blockers, digoxin, and non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers selected according to ejection fraction phenotype. Concurrently, increasing evidence supports early rhythm-control strategies because of their prognostic benefits in HF populations, with current guidelines reinforcing a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF)-guided approach to antiarrhythmic drug selection. Beyond conventional drugs, HF guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) is emerging as an important upstream pharmacological strategy for modulation of the arrhythmogenic substrate. AF management in HF requires an integrated, phenotype-oriented approach combining symptom control, thromboembolic prevention, and optimisation of GDMT. LVEF remains a key determinant of pharmacological safety and therapeutic selection, whereas haemodynamic status primarily guides acute management decisions.

articles.title: Digital Health Interventions in Cardiovascular Prevention: Medication Adherence, Risk Factor Management, and Patient Engagement.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Blood pressure (BP) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) are leading cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk factors yet remain suboptimally controlled. Digital health technologies may help bridge the gap between guideline recommendations and improved cardiovascular (CV) outcomes. We review digital health interventions for hypertension and dyslipidemia management.

RECENT FINDINGS: Mobile health (mHealth) interventions, including Corrie, LINKED-BP, Hello Heart, and Mass General Brigham platforms, demonstrate meaningful improvements in BP and LDL-C, particularly when paired with clinical support. In contrast, low-intensity text messaging alone produces modest or inconsistent benefits. Electronic Health Record (EHR)-based alerts can support therapy intensification but require thoughtful integration and clinician co-design. Artificial Intelligence (AI) may identify nonadherence and automate prescription refills, although further study is needed. Equitable implementation among high-risk and underserved populations remains essential. Digital health can promote treatment adherence, patient activation, earlier intervention, and access to care, with potential to improve CVD prevention at scale.

articles.title: Impact of Particulate Matter Exposure on Neurological Health in Older Adults: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This systematic review evaluates the current epidemiological evidence on the relationship between particulate matter (PM) exposure and neurological health in older adults, with particular attention to cognitive decline and neurodegenerative disease.

RECENT FINDINGS: A PRISMA-guided systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect was conducted through January 2026. Twenty-one observational studies met the inclusion criteria. The most frequently studied outcomes were cognitive performance and decline and cognitive impairment, including mild cognitive impairment (MCI), with several studies reporting adverse associations, particularly for long-term PM2.5 exposure. Evidence for dementia and Alzheimer's disease was also provided by several large cohort studies, although findings varied across exposure metrics and clinical endpoints. In contrast, evidence for Parkinson's disease-related hospitalizations, cerebral amyloid burden, retinal neurodegeneration, mental disorder-related hospital admissions, and individual PM constituents was more limited and was often based on one or a few studies. Findings concerning specific PM constituents were heterogeneous and should therefore be considered exploratory. The available evidence suggests an association between PM exposure and adverse neurological health in older adults, with the most substantial evidence concerning long-term PM2.5 exposure and cognitive outcomes. However, the strength and certainty of the evidence vary considerably across pollutants and neurological endpoints. Heterogeneity in study design, exposure assessment, and outcome definitions should be considered when interpreting the overall findings.

articles.title: Heart Regeneration: Endogenous and Exogenous Mechanisms and Their Significance for Cyanotic Congenital Heart Disease.
articles.abstract: Myocardial remodeling and the limited regenerative capacity of mammalian cardiomyocytes constitute major barriers to heart failure therapy. Current therapies cannot reliably restore lost cardiomyocytes, and advanced heart failure may ultimately require mechanical circulatory support or transplatation. This review synthesizes recent advances in endogenous cardiac regeneration mechanisms, focusing on three key regulatory pathways: intracellular signaling, extracellular matrix (ECM) interactions, and exogenous cell-based therapies. We examine strategies to enhance the reprogramming of non-cardiomyocytes into functional cardiomyocytes, leveraging insights from regeneration-competent animal models including zebrafish and neonatal mice. Additionally, we explore the emerging role of hypoxia as a pro-regenerative signal, particularly in the context of cyanotic congenital heart disease (CCHD) such as tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) and pulmonary atresia (PA) with intact ventricular septum or ventricular septal defects. While stem cell technologies and intrinsic cardiomyocyte proliferative mechanisms have shown preclinical promise, clinical translation remains fraught with challenges. This review aims to provide a comprehensive, integrated perspective on endogenous regeneration pathways and their therapeutic potential to transform heart failure management. We further emphasize the unique therapeutic value of these regenerative mechanisms in CCHD: chronic hypoxia triggers hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α)-mediated metabolic reprogramming and cell-cycle regulation, which paradoxically activates pro-regenerative signaling and establishes a transient myocardial regenerative window. This window can be harnessed via early neonatal surgical intervention to facilitate myocardial repair.

articles.title: Short- and long-term effects of dapagliflozin as an adjunct to insulin therapy in diabetic dogs: a pilot study.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated adjunctive dapagliflozin therapy in insulin-treated diabetic dogs to assess short- and long-term glycemic, clinical, and laboratory outcomes in dogs with naturally occurring diabetes mellitus. Six diabetic dogs received a compounded liquid oral dapagliflozin (CLODapa) formulation (0.088 ± 0.013 mg/kg once daily) in addition to ongoing insulin therapy for 100 days. We monitored continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) before and after treatment initiation, and serially assessed clinical, biochemical, and urinary parameters. Short-term dapagliflozin administration significantly reduced mean interstitial glucose, glucose nadir and peak values, and increased time within the target glucose range (60-250 mg/dL), while decreasing time above range. Glycemic variability increased, although time spent < 60 mg/dL and clinical hypoglycemia did not increase; however, CLODapa's initial dosage was reduced in four dogs due to concerns about hypoglycemia, increased in one, and left unchanged in another. Long-term treatment was associated with reductions in fructosamine, systolic blood pressure, alanine aminotransferase, aspartate aminotransferase, alkaline phosphatase, and cholesterol concentrations. No evidence of diabetic ketoacidosis, urinary tract infection, electrolyte imbalance, or acid-base disturbance was detected. Unintentional weight loss was documented in three patients and required a ~ 25% increase in food intake. Adjunctive dapagliflozin showed promise in improving glycemic control in diabetic dogs despite posing a risk of hypoglycemia, supporting further investigation of SGLT2 inhibition in canine diabetology.

articles.title: Effects of intradermal lymphocyte therapy in patients with recurrent pregnancy loss: secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial investigating purinergic signaling, inflammation, and cellular energy status.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL), a multifactorial and complex reproductive disorder, is diagnosed when there are two or more documented back-to-back failed pregnancies. Intradermal lymphocyte therapy (ILT) emerged as a promising intervention, aiming to modulate the intricate immunological milieu implicated in RPL. This study was designed to assess the effects of ILT on pregnancy and live birth rate and also provide insight into potential immunometabolic mechanisms underlying the clinical efficacy of lymphocyte therapy in RPL.

METHODS: The study included 100 patients with RPL, who received ILT (treated group, n = 50) or routine treatment (untreated group, n = 50), as well as 30 healthy women with a history of successful pregnancy as a control group. Low-dose ILT (Three injections of 20 × 10^6 PBMCs) was administered according to a standardized protocol, and flow cytometric analysis of CD39 and CD73 expression, ELISA measurement for serum levels of TNF-α, TGF-β, IL-1, and IL-10, as well as intracellular ATP and AMP using commercially available enzymatic colorimetric assay kits, were conducted.

RESULTS: Pregnancy and live birth rate were significantly higher in the treated group compared with the untreated group (p < 0.001). In patients with successful pregnancy, across all measured cytokines (TNF-α, TGF-β, IL-1, and IL-10), as well as ATP/AMP ratio and CD39⁺CD73⁺ cell frequency, treated patients exhibited significant pre- to post-treatment changes, whereas routine treatment patients showed no statistically meaningful differences. After treatment, between-group differences were statistically significant across all measured outcomes, although the level of statistical significance varied across outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Low-dose ILT may be associated with improved successful pregnancy and live birth rates in RPL patients. These clinical outcomes coincided with changes in purinergic signaling, inflammatory cytokines, and cellular energy status; however, formal mediation cannot be inferred from the present analysis.

articles.title: Evaluation of anti-obesity effects of ethanolic extract of Hydrocotyle sibthorpioides and its phytosomal formulation in high-fat diet-induced obesity in Wistar rats.
articles.abstract: Obesity is a chronic metabolic disorder characterised by dyslipidemia, hyperglycemia, oxidative stress, inflammation and organ dysfunction. The anti-obesity drugs available are effective but adverse effects often limit their long-term use. Hydrocotyle sibthorpioides is a medicinal plant rich in flavonoid and phenolic compounds, with reported antioxidant and metabolic regulatory properties. The present study was aimed at investigating the anti-obesity potential of ethanolic extract of Hydrocotyle sibthorpioides (EEHS) and its phytosomal formulation in a high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity model. EEHS was characterised by phytochemical screening, thin-layer chromatography and determination of total phenolic and flavonoid contents. Obese male Wistar rats induced by HFD were treated with EEHS (100-400 mg/kg), EEHS phytosomes (400 mg/kg) or orlistat (25 mg/kg) for seven weeks. Physiological, biochemical, and histopathological parameters were assessed. EEHS exhibited significant anti-obesity effects in a dose-dependent manner, with the phytosomal formulation being the most significant efficacy. Treatment resulted in marked improvement in body weight, fasting blood glucose, lipid profile, liver enzyme levels, liver lipid accumulation, total body fat, TNF-α, antioxidant status and organ weights. Histopathological analysis confirmed reduced hepatic and vascular damage, inflammatory cell infiltration and adipocyte hypertrophy. The phytosomal formulation showed effects similar to those of orlistat and was more effective than the traditional extract. EEHS, especially as a phytosomal preparation, exhibited a potent anti-obesity effect. It ameliorated metabolic, inflammatory, oxidative, and histopathological alterations associated with HFD-induced obesity. The present findings suggest that EEHS may be a promising natural approach for the management of obesity.

articles.title: Identification of bacterial communities and tick-borne pathogens in the fowl ticks (Argas persicus) from Almaty Oblast, Turkistan Oblast, and Shymkent City of Kazakhstan.
articles.abstract: Argas persicus (the fowl tick) is native to Central Asia. In this study, a total of 671 soft ticks were collected from chickens in three sampling sites (Bakanas District, Almaty Oblast; Sayram District, Turkistan Oblast; Shymkent City), Kazakhstan. A total of 16 tick pools (10 ticks per pool) were used for 16 S rRNA gene-based microbiome profiling by sequencing the V3-V4 region. Subsequently, seven genetic markers were amplified for molecular detection of Anaplasma, Rickettsia and Coxiella. Alpha and beta diversity analyses revealed that A. persicus ticks in Bakanas District had the highest microbial richness and diversity, while the ticks in Shymkent City and Sayram District exhibited highly similar microbial community compositions. The microbiome was predominated by Proteobacteria, specifically the genera Rickettsia and Coxiella, especially in Sayram District and Shymkent City, and the relative abundance of the top 30 bacterial components differed among sampling sites. Three pathogens including unclassified Anaplasma sp., Rickettsia hoogstraalii and Coxiella burnetii were detected for the first time in A. persicus ticks in Kazakhstan. The unclassified Anaplasma sp. was prevalent in ticks associated with domestic poultry and migratory birds, while Rickettsia hoogstraalii tended to parasitize seabird-related ticks with high prevalence. In addition, Coxiella burnetii infection prevalence was higher in pastoral areas than in urban areas, and birds act as secondary transmission vectors. These findings reveal that tick-borne pathogens harbored by avian soft ticks deserve close attention, especially in Central Asia.

articles.title: Resolving clinical Dilemmas in Hyperkalemia management for chronic heart failure: Current and emerging roles of sodium zirconium cyclosilicate.
articles.abstract: Hyperkalemia, commonly defined as a serum potassium concentration > 5.0 mEq/L, is a frequent and clinically important complication in patients with chronic heart failure (HF), particularly those with chronic kidney disease receiving guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT). Its impact extends beyond the electrolyte abnormality itself because recurrent hyperkalemia may lead to underuse, dose reduction, or discontinuation of prognostically important therapy. The risk is not uniform across GDMT classes: mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists carry the greatest direct risk, angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, and angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors also increase risk, whereas sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors may reduce serious hyperkalemia. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC) effectively lowers serum potassium and randomized evidence supports its use to maintain normokalemia and facilitate spironolactone optimization. However, a reduction in mortality or HF hospitalization has not been established. Emerging observational data suggest additional potential roles in supporting individualized dietary liberalization, improving gastrointestinal tolerability relative to traditional resins, and preventing recurrent hyperkalemia after treatment withdrawal. These findings should be interpreted cautiously because several supporting studies are small, nonrandomized, and potentially affected by residual confounding. Long-term treatment also requires attention to sodium exposure and edema, particularly in patients with HF or advanced kidney disease.
