This review integrates class-specific hyperkalemia risk, practical potassium thresholds, efficacy and safety evidence, comparison with patiromer, health-economic considerations, and remaining evidence gaps to provide a clinically applicable framework for individualized potassium management in HF.

articles.title: Upper post canine dental variation in the late Miocene hominid Hispanopithecus - is H. crusafonti sympatric with H. laietanus at Can Llobateres, Vallès-Penedès Basin, Spain?
articles.abstract: The aim of this paper is to assess variation within the upper premolar and molar samples from the Late Miocene hominid samples of Hispanopithecus to test the single species hypothesis using multivariate statistics. A series of correspondent and hierarchical cluster analyses were generated against 17 teeth from both species of Hispanopithecus. The morphological range (non-metric) of variation in Hispanopithecus crusafonti dental specimens from the Can Ponsic locality is well within the range of the extant hominids. The morphological range observed in H. laietanus from Can Llobateres, however, is shown ​ to be greater than that observed in the four extant hominid species. An upper third premolar specimen, IPS-1792, from Can Llobateres is shown to reflect the H. crusafonti morphotype, which indicates it may be a specimen of this species as opposed to H. laietanus. If this is correct, this indicates that both hominid species were sympatric. The techniques used here also test the serial position of isolated molars, demonstrating that IPS-1814 which has traditionally been considered an M1 is almost certainly an M3, with the same applying to IPS-1771 which has been considered a likely M2 but is also shown to be an M3.

articles.title: Female Fingerprint: Sex-Specific Aspects in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Atrial fibrillation (AF) and heart failure (HF) frequently coexist and represent a major source of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. This review summarizes current evidence on sex-specific differences in epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, prognosis, and treatment in women with AF and HF.

RECENT FINDINGS: Emerging evidence indicates that women with AF and HF constitute a distinct clinical and biological phenotype. Women typically develop AF at older age, more commonly present with hypertension and HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), and report greater symptom burden and impaired quality of life. Sex-specific mechanisms including hormonal influences, atrial fibrosis, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, autonomic dysregulation, and microvascular disease contribute to these differences. Population studies further demonstrate sex-related disparities in HF development and outcomes across AF subtypes. Despite increasing awareness, women remain underrepresented in clinical trials and are less likely to receive rhythm-control strategies, catheter ablation, or device therapy. Recognition of the "female fingerprint" in AF and HF is essential for individualized risk stratification and the advancement of precision cardiovascular medicine.

articles.title: Genetic and phenotypic landscape of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in the MENA region: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is the most common inherited cardiomyopathy, and it is a leading cause of sudden cardiac death (SCD) in young people. Recessive genetic disorders are especially prevalent in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region due to consanguinity, which affects the genetic landscape of hereditary disorders. Here we conducted a systematic review of mutations in patients with HCM in the MENA and report genotype-phenotype associations to provide an evidence base for personalized diagnostic and therapeutic interventions.

METHODS: We systematically searched the PubMed, ProQuest, and Scopus databases from inception until October 2025 to collect all genetic data and phenotypes of patients with HCM in the MENA. Broad search terms were used to capture all relevant literature describing genetic variants associated with HCM in the MENA region including inheritance patterns and genotype-phenotype associations.

RESULTS: The database search returned 448 studies, with 17 meeting inclusion criteria. 14 studies were case series, 2 studies were case reports, and 1 was a case-control study. In 1323 HCM subjects in the MENA, there were 107 genetic variants in 21 genes. The majority of the variants occurred in MYBPC3 and MYH7, consistent with other populations. However, there were also homozygous variants in recessive genes, founder mutations, and novel variants in non-sarcomeric genes in the region, with patients experiencing more severe clinical phenotypes.

CONCLUSION: To our knowledge, this is the first systematic review on genetic variants associated with HCM in the MENA region. The genetic landscape of HCM is complex and unique in the MENA. The underrepresentation of MENA populations in global genomic resources remains a barrier to variant interpretation. Region-specific gene panels may be required to advance the diagnosis of HCM in the region.

articles.title: Atrial fibrosis, atrial fibrillation susceptibility, and molecular remodeling in female goats with cardiac TGF-β1 overexpression.
articles.abstract: Atrial Fibrillation (AF) is the most common cardiac arrhythmia in adult humans. Atrial fibrosis plays a primary role in developing and sustaining this disease phenotype. Specifically, TGF-β1, a potent pro-fibrotic molecule, is implicated in cell turnover, increasing the amount of extracellular matrix in the heart. This increase leads to aberrant electrical signaling and can produce AF. In this study, we hypothesized that TGF-β1 modulates AF susceptibility in TGF-β1 transgenic goats and that genes related to TGF-β1 and AF would be differentially expressed when compared to wild-type (WT) controls. Transgenic (TG) female goats expressing the active form of human TGF-β1 under the control of the cardiac-specific α-myosin heavy chain (α-MHC) promoter and age-matched wild-type female goats were utilized in the study. Pacemakers were implanted in all animals for continuous arrhythmia monitoring and AF inducibility, which was evaluated using five separate 10 s bursts of atrial pacing (200-160 ms). Tissue samples were collected from both atria of TG and WT goats. RNA was extracted, and gene expression analyses were run on a selected panel of genes. Immunohistochemistry was performed on atrial tissue to evaluate for the presence of selected inflammatory markers to elucidate AF substrate in these animals. There was a significant increase in AF inducibility in both frequency and duration in TGF-β1 goats compared to their WT counterparts. There was no significant difference in the number of inflammatory cells tested by immunohistochemistry. Differentially expressed genes between the TG and WT groups were found in several functional categories including AF, apoptosis, extracellular matrix, inflammation, and TGF-β1.These data support the hypothesis that fibrosis is an important modulator of AF susceptibility. More specifically, an overexpression of TGF-β1 significantly increases expression levels of ECM proteins and TGF-β1 signaling modulators, adding to elevated AF risk without altering underlying inflammation.

articles.title: Comparative outcomes of Hugo RAS and Versius surgical systems versus da Vinci in four urological procedures: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Robot-assisted surgery has transformed urological surgery, with the da Vinci Surgical System dominating for over two decades. Following the expiry of key Intuitive patents in 2019, two particular platforms - Medtronic's Hugo™ RAS system and CMR Surgical's Versius® Surgical Robotic System - have gained regulatory approval and entered urological practice. Comparative evidence between these platforms and da Vinci® across urological procedures remains limited. This systematic review follows PRISMA guidelines and a prospectively registered protocol (PROSPERO: CRD420261319741). MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from January 2016 to August 2026. Comparative studies of Hugo™ RAS or Versius® versus da Vinci® in patients undergoing robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP), robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN), pyeloplasty, or radical cystectomy were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I. 19 studies (21 procedural comparisons) involving 2,482 patients were included. In RARP, blood loss and length of stay showed substantially overlapping ranges between platforms, with no consistent direction of effect, though setup and docking times were consistently longer with the newer platforms. Positive surgical margin rates and early continence recovery overlapped widely in RARP. In RAPN, warm ischaemia times differed by five minutes or less across reporting studies, and trifecta rates were within 5 percentage points. The single small pyeloplasty study reported identical median operative times, but provided minimal comparative information. Early comparative evidence has not demonstrated consistent differences in peri-operative, oncological or early functional outcomes between Hugo™ RAS or Versius® and da Vinci® in experienced, high-volume centres. However, the included studies were small, non-randomised and not powered to detect clinically meaningful differences or to demonstrate equivalence. These findings therefore represent an absence of evidence of a difference rather than evidence of comparable effectiveness. Prospective studies including robotic-naïve centres are needed to advance our understanding.

articles.title: Minimally important change of the PROMIS Global Health in older stroke patients: a multicentre prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Interpretation of patient-reported outcome measures (PROM) score changes requires knowledge of the minimally important change (MIC). The Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System Global Health questionnaire (PROMIS-GH), which contains subscales assessing physical and mental health, is increasingly used in post-stroke care. However, the MIC of the PROMIS-GH subscales has not been estimated in patients with ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA). This study aimed to estimate the MIC of PROMIS-GH subscales in older stroke and TIA patients.

METHODS: This Dutch multicentre prospective cohort study included adults aged ≥ 70 years with a recent ischemic stroke or TIA (May 2024-March 2026). The PROMIS-GH was administered at baseline and after 1 month of follow-up. The MIC of the PROMIS-GH subscales was primarily estimated using the predictive modelling approach. Two additional methods, the mean change method and receiver operating characteristic analysis, were performed as secondary analyses.

RESULTS: We included 125 patients. Ninety-five patients with a median age of 78 completed the study. Using predictive modelling, we estimated an MIC of 1.3 points for the global physical health (GPH) subscale. MIC for the global mental health (GMH) subscale could not be estimated.

CONCLUSION: The MIC for the GPH subscale in older patients with ischemic stroke or TIA was small, suggesting that even small score changes may be clinically relevant in this population. No reliable MIC could be estimated for the GMH subscale, highlighting the need for further research.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06495073, registered on 3 July 2024.

articles.title: Gasdermin, inflammatory, and heat-shock gene expression profiles in the naturally aged male mouse brain following propolis and dexpanthenol treatment.
articles.abstract: Aging is accompanied by alterations in inflammatory signaling, regulated cell-death pathways, and cellular stress responses in the brain. This study investigated the effects of propolis and dexpanthenol, administered individually or in combination, on gasdermin-related, inflammatory, and heat-shock gene expression in naturally aged male mice. Thirty-five male CD-1 mice were randomly allocated to five groups (n = 7/group): Young Control, Aged Control, Aged + Propolis, Aged + Dexpanthenol, and Aged + Propolis + Dexpanthenol. Propolis (200 mg/kg/day) and dexpanthenol (500 mg/kg/day) were administered for 14 days. Whole-brain mRNA expression of GSDMD, GSDME, GSDMC, TNF-α, IL-1β, HSP70, and HSP90 was evaluated by quantitative real-time PCR. Natural aging was associated with marked reductions in TNF-α, IL-1β, and HSP70 expression, whereas GSDMD, GSDME, GSDMC, and HSP90 were not significantly altered after correction for multiple comparisons. Propolis reduced GSDME and IL-1β expression while increasing GSDMC relative to aged controls. Dexpanthenol increased GSDMD and HSP70 expression, shifted TNF-α toward the young-control profile, and reduced HSP90 expression. Combined administration produced a distinct transcriptional profile characterized by pronounced increases in GSDMD, TNF-α, IL-1β, and HSP70 relative to aged controls. These findings indicate that propolis and dexpanthenol are associated with distinct, gene-specific transcriptional responses in the naturally aged brain rather than uniform changes across the inflammatory and gasdermin-related genes examined. Because the analyses were restricted to mRNA expression, the observed gasdermin transcriptional changes do not establish functional pyroptosis. The prominent HSP70 response further suggests that cellular stress adaptation and proteostasis may represent important components of these treatment-associated molecular changes.

articles.title: Testing the EQ-HWB-9 with seven-day versus today recall periods in dementia: variability and recall adherence under health fluctuations.
articles.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare a "7-DAY" and "TODAY" recall period of the EQ-HWB-9 in people living with dementia (PlwD) with regard to day-to-day health changes (health fluctuations) and recall period adherence.

METHODS: In this mixed-methods study, PlwD-caregiver dyads from German primary care were randomized to complete the EQ-HWB-9 (self- and proxy-proxy report) using either a "7-day" or "today" recall period over a two-week time period on day 1, day seven and day 14. In addition, caregivers recorded daily health fluctuations over 14 days via a diary. Health fluctuations were examined in relation to EQ-HWB-9 score variability and recall adherence, which was assessed via semi-structured caregiver interviews. Quantitative analyses included recall group comparisons, effect sizes, and variance analyses.

RESULTS: Seventy-four dyads were included (PlwD mean age 77 years; 41.9% female; caregiver mean age 71 years; 71.6% female). Proxy EQ-HWB-9 scores were higher (worse health) than self-reports and higher with the "7-day" versus "today" recall. Caregivers reported at least one health fluctuation in 92% of PlwD; fluctuations occurred in 41% of daily assessments. Greater diary-documented fluctuation was associated with higher EQ-HWB-9 score variability. Recall adherence differed by health fluctuation status: caregivers of PlwD with no to low health fluctuations favored TODAY, whereas those of PlwD with high health fluctuations favored the 7-DAY recall time frame.

CONCLUSIONS: No single recall period appears optimal for all PlwD. Recall period selection should consider individual health fluctuation patterns to improve the performance of HRQoL assessments in dementia.

articles.title: Acute effects of hibiscus tea versus coffee consumption before prolonged sitting on blood pressure and heart rate variability in adults: a randomized crossover trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare acute effects of consuming hibiscus tea and coffee before prolonged uninterrupted sitting on blood pressure (BP) and heart rate variability (HRV) in young, healthy adults.

METHODS: In a randomized crossover trial, participants (n = 24; 24.9 [4.9] years old; 50% women; 54.2% with overweight/obesity) completed two 3-hour prolonged uninterrupted sitting sessions after consuming hibiscus tea or coffee. A Polar H10 heart rate (HR) strap connected to a Polar V800 monitor evaluated HRV indices, including HR, standard deviation of normal R-R intervals (SDNN), root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD), low-frequency power (LF), and high-frequency power (HF). A sphygmomanometer (Welch Allyn Connex) measured systolic (SBP) and diastolic (DBP) BP, and mean arterial pressure (MAP) was calculated. HRV indices were natural log-transformed (ln) due to skewness. Generalized linear mixed models with random effects examined the influence of both beverages on BP and HRV while adjusting for baseline values.

RESULTS: SBP, DBP, and MAP were significantly lower (β = - 4.2, - 3.3, - 3.6 mmHg, respectively), and lnHF (β = 0.3) was significantly higher in the hibiscus tea condition compared with the coffee condition (p < 0.05 for all). No other significant differences were detected for other HRV indices (p > 0.05 for all). Sex- and BMI-stratified analyses suggested potential variation in cardiovascular responses across subgroups, although these findings should be interpreted cautiously as formal interaction tests were not performed.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that hibiscus tea may have potential to favorably modulate cardiovascular responses to prolonged uninterrupted sitting compared with coffee, although further controlled studies are needed to confirm these effects and establish their long-term implications.

articles.title: Associations between biomarkers of vitamin K and cardiovascular disease risk factors: the role of lipids.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Emerging evidence indicates that vitamin K is important not only for its role in blood coagulation activation, but also for cardiovascular health. However, the results are equivocal, and due to the lipophilic nature of vitamin K, adjustment for triglycerides may be important. We investigated the associations between levels of circulating vitamin K vitamers, phylloquinone (PK) and total menaquinones (MK), and dephospho-undercarboxylated matrix Gla protein (dp-ucMGP, a biomarker of functional vitamin K status), with multiple cardiovascular disease risk factors and adjusted for triglycerides.

METHODS: From the population-based Inter99 cohort, 2,195 participants had available fasting blood samples from which dp-ucMGP, PK, and MK-4 to MK-10 were analysed (mean age, ± SD: 68, ± 7 years, 48% female). Cross-sectional associations with cardiovascular disease risk factors were examined per doubling of vitamin K biomarkers using multivariable regression models.

RESULTS: Both PK and total MK were positively associated with hypertriglyceridemia: OR (95%CI) 1.91, (1.69, 2.18) and 13.1, (7.55, 23.4), respectively, but not measures of adiposity and diabetes. However, after triglyceride adjustment, higher PK and total MK were inversely associated with central obesity: 0.86, (0.79, 0.95) and 0.61, (0.37, 0.98), respectively, and diabetes: 0.81, (0.69, 0.95) and 0.33, (0.13, 0.81), respectively. Higher dp-ucMGP was associated with hypertriglyceridemia: 1.50, (1.08, 2.09). After adjustment for triglycerides, higher dp-ucMGP remained associated with central obesity: 2.81, (2.16, 3.70) and obesity: 3.31, (2.50, 4.42).

CONCLUSION: After accounting for triglycerides, both PK and total MK were inversely associated with measures of adiposity and diabetes, suggesting that blood triglyceride levels need to be accounted for when considering circulating vitamin K levels. Higher dp-ucMGP, reflecting reduced vitamin K-dependent MGP carboxylation, was associated with adiposity markers independent of triglycerides.

articles.title: The Transumbilical Breast Augmentation: Safety and Satisfaction in a Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of 13,210 Breasts.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As one of the most commonly performed aesthetic procedures, breast augmentation can be performed through several surgical access routes. Transumbilical breast augmentation (TUBA) offers the advantage of implant placement through a concealed umbilical incision. However, despite its aesthetic appeal, evidence supporting its safety, reproducibility, and clinical outcomes remains limited and heterogeneous.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted in MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science through August 2025. Studies including adult women undergoing TUBA with silicone or saline implants were eligible. Primary endpoints were patient-reported satisfaction and hematoma incidence. Secondary endpoints included capsular contracture, reintervention, infection, seroma, intraoperative bleeding, implant malposition, inadvertent plane placement, implant rupture or deflation, operative time, and other adverse events.

RESULTS: Seventeen studies were included, encompassing 6,605 patients (13,210 breasts), of whom 6,510 underwent TUBA. Patient-reported satisfaction was consistently favorable across studies, with high satisfaction rates. Single-arm meta-analyses demonstrated low pooled incidences of hematoma (0.2%, 95% CI: 0.1-0.5%), capsular contracture (1.7%, 95% CI: 0.9-3.2%), reintervention (2.3%, 95% CI: 1.2-4.4%), infection (0.0%, 95% CI: 0.0-0.7%), and intraoperative bleeding (0.2%, 95% CI: 0.1-0.8%). Other adverse events were infrequent, and operative time clustered around a median of 60 minutes. Overall, risk of bias was predominantly moderate.

CONCLUSION: This study suggested that TUBA resulted in high patient-reported satisfaction and low reported rates of major complications. However, these findings are descriptive and should be interpreted cautiously, because the predominance of retrospective single-arm studies substantially limits causal inference. Moderate risk of bias and short follow-up further preclude definitive conclusions regarding its safety, reproducibility, or equivalence to established approaches.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE IV: This journal requires that authors assign a level of evidence to each article. For a full description of these Evidence-Based Medicine Ratings, please refer to Table of Contents or online Instructions to Authors www.springer.com/00266 .

articles.title: Pediatric renal abscess in the modern imaging era: clinical features, microbiology, management, and renal outcomes.
articles.abstract: Pediatric renal abscess is an uncommon but potentially serious infection that may result in permanent renal injury. Despite advances in imaging, its contemporary clinical features and long-term renal outcomes have not been comprehensively described. We conducted a structured descriptive review of reports published between January 2000 and June 2026 using PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science, identifying 65 articles describing 361 pediatric cases eligible for analysis. Renal abscess occurred across all pediatric age groups, with a slight female predominance. Underlying urinary tract abnormalities were reported in a substantial proportion of cases, although reporting was incomplete; vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) was identified in 33.1% of assessable patients (82/248), most commonly during post-abscess evaluation. Among the 55 patients with available data on the timing of VUR diagnosis, only 9.1% (5/55) had a documented diagnosis prior to abscess onset. A history of prior urinary tract infection was present in 17.8% (38/214) of assessable cases. Clinical presentation was often nonspecific, with fever present in most patients, whereas lower urinary tract symptoms were less common. Pyuria was absent in 30.6% (52/170) of assessable cases. Urine and blood cultures showed limited diagnostic yield, whereas abscess fluid cultures demonstrated high diagnostic yield when performed. Most children were successfully managed with antimicrobial therapy, although approximately one-quarter required drainage procedures. Among patients with reported post-infectious technetium-99m dimercaptosuccinic acid findings, renal cortical scarring was identified in 68.0% (34/50); however, this likely reflects selection bias due to non-uniform imaging practices. Overall, post-infectious imaging abnormalities were reported in a substantial proportion of evaluated patients, although follow-up was inconsistent. These findings suggest that pediatric renal abscess may represent the initial clinically apparent presentation leading to the detection of previously unrecognized VUR. Structured post-infectious evaluation and standardized follow-up may help clarify underlying urinary tract abnormalities and long-term renal outcomes. A higher resolution version of the Graphical abstract is available as Supplementary information.

articles.title: CT and MRI in periprocedural transcatheter mitral valve replacement: expert recommendations by the European Society of Cardiovascular Radiology (ESCR) and the North American Society for Cardiovascular Imaging (NASCI).
articles.abstract: Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) is a minimally invasive treatment option for symptomatic patients with severe mitral valve disease who are at high surgical risk or ineligible for open-heart surgery. The procedure has been associated with improved quality of life and functional status in selected patients and is increasingly recognized as a valuable therapeutic option in the management of complex mitral valve disorders. A multidisciplinary Heart Team is essential to ensure the clinical success of TMVR, and imaging specialists play a central role in the preprocedural assessment for patient and device selection, during the procedure, to guide and monitor the implantation, and after the procedure, for follow-up and for the correct diagnosis of short- or long-term complications. Echocardiography is required for initial diagnosis, for assessment of valve hemodynamics, intraprocedural guidance and monitoring. However, a multimodality approach including CT and/or MRI is frequently needed to correctly manage the phase of preprocedural planning and the diagnosis of complications. This consensus document, developed by a working group of experts from the European Society of Cardiovascular Radiology (ESCR) and the North American Society for Cardiovascular Imaging (NASCI), provides evidence-based recommendations for CT and cardiac MRI acquisition and post-processing in procedural planning and postprocedural evaluation in patients undergoing TMVR. Emphasis is placed on the technical requirements and standardization of imaging protocols, which must account for the heterogeneity of imaging equipment used in clinical settings. The document also outlines recommendations for all necessary preprocedural measures to ensure consistency, accuracy, and effective communication among specialists. KEY POINTS: Question How can CT and MRI acquisition, measurement, and reporting for TMVR be standardized to support accurate procedural planning, device selection, and follow-up? Findings This expert consensus provides recommendations for standardized CT and MRI protocols, key measurements, and structured reporting throughout TMVR planning and follow-up. Clinical relevance CT and MRI assessment may improve patient selection, procedural planning, multidisciplinary communication, and detection of postprocedural complications, supporting safer and more consistent TMVR practice across centers.

articles.title: Anti-plaque effect of a surface pre-reacted glass-ionomer-based prophylactic paste under cariogenic challenge: a randomized in situ study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the anti-plaque effect of a prophylactic paste containing Surface Pre-Reacted Glass-ionomer (S-PRG) fillers under cariogenic challenge using a randomized in situ model.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This randomized, double-blind study involved 18 volunteers; both the participants and the outcome assessor were blinded to the prophylactic agent allocation. The prophylactic agents were the S-PRG-based Pro-Care Gel (Shofu Inc.; test), Herjos (Vigodent; conventional comparator), and pumice and water (negative control). The other factors were cariogenic challenge (presence or absence) and time of plaque accumulation (24 h and 7 days). During 8 days, volunteers wore intraoral appliances with enamel blocks divided into 2 rows (split-mouth design), in one of them a cariogenic challenge was applied (20% sucrose, 8x/day). Prophylaxis was performed at baseline and again after the 24-hour assessment. The three agent phases were separated by 7-day washout periods. Plaque accumulation was evaluated by quantitative digital image analysis of plaque-covered area (mm²) and adapted Simplified Oral Hygiene Index (OHI-S) scores.

RESULTS: Three-way repeated-measures ANOVA showed significant main effects of Time, Cariogenic Challenge, and Prophylactic Agent (all p < 0.001). A significant Time × Prophylactic Agent interaction (p = 0.022) indicated different temporal patterns among agents. Plaque accumulation increased from 24 h to 7 days in all groups, while Pro-Care Gel showed the lowest plaque-covered area at both evaluations; the OHI-S analysis showed the same overall group/time pattern.

CONCLUSIONS: Under the conditions of this short-term in situ study, the tested S-PRG-based prophylactic paste (Pro-Care Gel) resulted in lower stainable plaque accumulation than the tested conventional paste (Herjos) and pumice/water. These findings are specific to the products and outcomes evaluated.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: S-PRG prophylactic paste exhibits a sustained anti-plaque effect, markedly reducing dental plaque accumulation relative to the two comparators during the 7-day evaluation period. This strategy could particularly be effective for high-caries-risk patients, as the material's efficacy is not compromised by frequent sucrose exposure.

articles.title: Pan-Genomic Insights into Bradyrhizobium ottawaense: Highlighting a Strain with Unusual Host-Specific Compatibility.
articles.abstract: Biological nitrogen fixation occupies a paramount position in sustainable agriculture. The present study elucidates the genomic diversity and symbiotic capabilities of Bradyrhizobium ottawaense focusing on the commercial B. ottawaense strain RCAM0104 to decipher the genetic bases of plant-bacterial interactions and the evolutionary adaptability of these microorganisms. Experimental assessments of symbiotic compatibility revealed that RCAM0104 effectively nodulates Arachis hypogaea, Glycine soja, and Vigna unguiculata, but is ineffective on Glycine max. Histological examinations confirmed successful infection processes in most host plants, with the exception of white nodules observed on cultivated soybean. Prediction of type III effectors in the RCAM0104 genome identified effector proteins potentially involved in its promiscuous symbiotic phenotype. These findings highlight the genetic flexibility of B. ottawaense and its capacity to adapt to diverse host plants. The observed host-specific nodulation patterns correlate with specific variations in the accessory genome, suggesting their potential role in determining symbiotic compatibility, potentially through gene transfer from local strains. This research contributes significantly to our understanding of the evolutionary dynamics and ecological plasticity of rhizobia in symbiosis with legumes, providing insights into the mechanisms regulating plant-microbe interactions. Based on these results, we hypothesize an evolutionary trade-off, where a loss of compatibility with one host may have occurred concurrently with the putative acquisition in compatibility with another.

articles.title: [When the lifesaver sparks fear : Anxiety after ICD Implantation].
articles.abstract: Implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) improve survival in patients at risk of life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias. Psychological distress following ICD implantation, however, is often underestimated, although it is common, clinically relevant, and may adversely affect quality of life and prognosis. Meta-analyses report prevalence rates of approximately 23% for anxiety disorders, 15% for depression, and 12% for posttraumatic stress disorder. Major risk factors include ICD shocks, particularly recurrent shocks, negative illness perceptions, poor device acceptance, type D personality, and female sex. In contrast, somatic comorbidities appear to influence psychological adjustment mainly indirectly through symptom burden. Psychosocial constructs such as illness perception, device acceptance, and ICD-related concerns are closely associated with quality of life, depression, and anxiety. Partners and family members may also experience considerable psychological distress, including "shock anxiety." Structured patient education, optimized ICD programming to minimize shocks, and targeted psychosocial and psychotherapeutic interventions may reduce psychological distress. Systematic psychosocial risk assessment and integrated cardiological and psychological care should therefore become an integral part of long-term ICD management to improve patients' psychological adjustment and quality of life.

articles.title: USP18 deubiquitylates TRIM25 to facilitate RIG-I-mediated antiviral innate immune signaling.
articles.abstract: The cytosolic sensor retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I) is essential for initiating antiviral innate immunity, and its activation is tightly regulated by ubiquitination. Although the deubiquitinating enzyme ubiquitin-specific protease 18 (USP18) is known to regulate interferon signaling, its role in the RIG-I pathway remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that USP18 acts as a positive regulator of RIG-I-mediated antiviral responses. We find that USP18 specifically promotes K63-linked ubiquitination of endogenous RIG-I during viral infection, potentiates downstream interferon signaling, and restricts RNA virus replication. Mechanistically, USP18 directly binds to the E3 ligase tripartite motif-containing 25 (TRIM25) and removes its K48-linked ubiquitin chains primarily at lysine 156 (K156), thereby stabilizing the TRIM25 protein. This deubiquitinating activity is essential, as a catalytic mutant (USP18 C64S) binds TRIM25 but fails to stabilize it or enhance RIG-I signaling. Knockdown of TRIM25 abolishes USP18-mediated enhancement of RIG-I ubiquitination and the interferon response, establishing that TRIM25 is required for USP18-mediated enhancement. Our study unveils a novel USP18-TRIM25-RIG-I axis that amplifies antiviral immunity, revealing USP18 as a multifaceted regulator that fine-tunes interferon responses at both the receptor and sensor levels.

articles.title: [Paracentral acute middle maculopathy after transient branch retinal artery occlusion following coronary angiography].
articles.abstract: A 76-year-old woman noticed reduced vision with a central scotoma in her left eye one week after coronary angiography for angina pectoris. Best-corrected visual acuity in the left eye was 0.5. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showed a hyperreflective lesion of the inner nuclear layer inferior to the macula, and paracentral acute middle maculopathy (PAMM) was diagnosed. OCT angiography was unremarkable in the acute phase. Fluorescein angiography revealed delayed arterial perfusion inferior to the macula, consistent with a transient branch retinal artery occlusion. Cardiovascular work-up showed carotid stenosis and dyslipidemia; lipid-lowering therapy was intensified. After 3 months, visual acuity in the left eye was 1.0, but a central scotoma persisted. OCT showed atrophy of the inner nuclear and outer plexiform layers, and OCT angiography showed capillary rarefaction of the deep capillary plexus. PAMM is a rare complication of coronary angiography. In patients with a new central scotoma after cardiac catheterization, PAMM should be considered and a comprehensive cardiovascular work-up initiated.

articles.title: Revisiting the role of sex in stroke risk stratification in atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2024 European Society of Cardiology guidelines introduced the CHA2DS2-VA score, omitting female sex from stroke risk stratification in atrial fibrillation (AF). However, evidence on the relative predictive performance of CHA2DS2-VA versus CHA2DS2-VASc across diverse populations remains inconsistent. We therefore conducted a systematic evaluation of their discrimination and reclassification performance.

METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational cohort studies comparing CHA2DS2-VA and CHA2DS2-VASc for prediction of ischaemic stroke or thromboembolic events in patients with AF. Discrimination was evaluated using the difference in C-statistics (ΔAUC) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), and reclassification using continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI). Pooled estimates were derived using random-effects models.

RESULTS: Seven studies including 250,112 patients were analysed. In the overall population, discriminative performance was comparable between the CHA2DS2-VA and CHA2DS2-VASc scores (ΔAUC 0.00065, 95% CI -0.00288 to 0.00417; IDI 0.00010, 95% CI -0.00063 to 0.00083). Continuous NRI indicated a modest advantage for CHA2DS2-VASc (-0.05615; 95% CI: -0.10350 to -0.00880). Among patients not receiving oral anticoagulation, both discrimination and reclassification were similar between the two scores. Variability in reclassification performance was observed across regions and study periods.

CONCLUSIONS: The CHA2DS2-VA and CHA2DS2-VASc scores showed comparable discrimination for stroke risk prediction in patients with AF when evaluated as continuous scores, although reclassification modestly favoured the CHA2DS2-VASc score. The clinical contribution of female sex to risk prediction appears context-dependent and warrants further evaluation.

articles.title: Machine learning prediction model and influencing factors for low back pain in middle-aged and older adults based on CHARLS cohort data.
articles.journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low back pain (LBP) is a common condition that leads to functional impairment and reduced quality of life in the modern population. Given the complexity of its etiology, this study aims to systematically identify precise risk factors at the population level and establish predictive models to provide a scientific basis for the early prevention of low back pain.

METHODS: Using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) spanning 2011 to 2020, a total of 93,022 middle-aged and older adults were included in the analysis. Feature selection was performed using L1 regularization (LASSO) and recursive feature elimination (RFE). Eight machine learning models including logistic regression, random forest, and LightGBM were constructed and their predictive performances were compared. Model interpretability was assessed using SHAP values.

RESULTS: LASSO and RFE jointly identified 20 core risk features. Among the eight machine learning models, LightGBM demonstrated optimal predictive performance, achieving an AUC of 0.898. SHAP analysis revealed that the co-occurrence of pain in multiple sites, such as "leg pain-knee pain-back pain," constituted the strongest predictor cluster for LBP. Poor self-rated health and depressive symptoms were also identified as significant risk factors.

CONCLUSION: By integrating population-level big data, this study developed a highly accurate and easily interpretable predictive model for low back pain. The findings suggest that comprehensive prevention and treatment strategies for low back pain should focus on the coordinated management of pain in the "back-leg-knee" region, while also taking psychosocial factors into account.

articles.title: Inadvertent intraspinal deployment of an iliac venous stent: a case report of surgical removal and one-year follow-up.
articles.journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Iliac venous stenting is an established treatment for symptomatic iliac venous obstruction and post-thrombotic disease. Although usually safe, malposition of a venous stent into the spinal canal is exceptionally rare and may cause serious neurological injury.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 53 years old woman with chronic left lower-limb swelling and pain caused by iliac venous thrombosis underwent left lower-limb venography, iliac vein balloon dilation, and stent implantation. During deployment she reported left lower-limb pain, which was initially considered procedure-related. On the first postoperative day, she developed severe right buttock pain radiating to the right lower limb, bilateral foot numbness, and reduced bilateral extensor hallucis longus strength. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and Computed Tomography (CT) showed that the metallic stent entered the spinal canal through the left L5/S1 intervertebral foramen, crossed the canal, and reached the right L5/S1 foramen. After 3 weeks of conservative treatment without meaningful recovery, posterior exploration was performed. Because the intraspinal stent segment appeared thrombosed and no active bleeding was identified, the segment was withdrawn, cut, and removed under direct visualization while protecting the dural sac and nerve roots. Internal fixation was not required because the involved L5/S1 segment was a stable lumbosacral transitional level.

CONCLUSIONS: Inadvertent intraspinal deployment of an iliac venous stent is a rare but potentially serious complication. Radicular pain or neurological deficit during or after iliac venous stenting should prompt immediate multiplanar imaging. In this patient, posterior partial removal after multidisciplinary assessment was associated with favorable neurological recovery. Further cases are required to determine the safety and generalizability of this approach.

articles.title: Demographic, comorbidity, and temporal trends in anterior (ALIF) versus posterior (PLIF/TLIF) single-level lumbar interbody fusion: a retrospective analysis from 2015 to 2023.
articles.journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of this study is to characterize national demographic and comorbidity profiles associated with anterior lumbar interbody fusion (ALIF) versus posterior interbody fusion (PLIF/TLIF) and evaluate temporal utilization patterns.

METHODS: Using a commercial insurance database from 2015 to 2023, adults undergoing single-level ALIF or posterior interbody fusion were identified. Univariate tests compared baseline characteristics. Annual utilization trends were estimated with Poisson regression or negative binomial regression if overdispersion was present. Significance was set at P < 0.05.

RESULTS: Among 407,319 patients, 133,323 underwent ALIF and 273,996 underwent posterior interbody fusion. Mean age was higher for posterior interbody fusion (61.8 vs. 59.5 years; P < 0.001), as was mean Elixhauser Comorbidity Index (5.3 ± 3.6 vs. 5.2 ± 3.6; P < 0.001). Sex distribution and rheumatoid arthritis were similar (P > 0.05 for all). Posterior interbody fusion patients more frequently had obesity, diabetes, hypertension, COPD, chronic kidney disease, congestive heart failure, coronary artery disease, osteoporosis, and tobacco use (P < 0.001 for all). ALIF procedures increased at an average annual rate of 6.66% (95% CI, 4.60-8.47; P < 0.001), whereas posterior interbody fusion increased 1.98% per year (95% CI, -0.19-4.19; P = 0.075); the annual growth-rate difference (ALIF - posterior interbody fusion) was 4.68% points (95% CI, 1.71-6.98; P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: In this national sample, posterior interbody fusion was more commonly used in older, more medically complex patients, while both approaches grew over time with faster growth for ALIF and increasing ALIF share. These descriptive patterns outline contemporary selection of anterior versus posterior approaches and motivate outcome-focused, risk-adjusted studies in key subgroups.

articles.title: Clinical pharmacology of antidiabetic drugs: an update.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This review describes the updated pharmacology of antidiabetic drugs and its translation into clinical applications.

METHODS: English language literature published from January 1, 1998 to July 25, 2026 was collected using PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Ovid. Research articles, reviews, and clinical practice guidelines were included for discussion.

RESULTS: Currently, ultra-long-acting basal insulins are emerging, allowing less frequent injections. Glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), tirzepatide, and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) have novel pharmacodynamic properties and clinical evidence of cardiorenal and metabolic benefits, supporting their important roles in individuals with type 2 diabetes (T2D) who have high cardiorenal risk. Because of their effects on weight reduction, GLP-1RAs (semaglutide, liraglutide, and orforglipron) and tirzepatide are approved for the treatment of obesity. Furthermore, SGLT2is (empagliflozin, dapagliflozin, and sotagliflozin) provide cardiorenal benefits, with supporting potential mechanisms, in individuals with heart failure and chronic kidney disease. Conventional oral drugs (e.g., metformin, thiazolidinediones, dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors, sulfonylureas, meglitinides, and α-glucosidase inhibitors) lack sufficient pharmacologic and clinical data on cardiorenal benefits, suggesting their roles as adjunctive therapies. Novel candidates, including triple incretin hormone agonists (acting on GLP-1, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide [GIP], and glucagon receptors), GLP-1RA-GIP antagonism-based therapies, amylin analogues, and new dual SGLT1/2 inhibitors, show promising results for glycemic control and weight loss.

CONCLUSION: Overall, a comprehensive understanding of the pharmacologic characteristics of antidiabetic drugs promotes appropriate drug use for the management of T2D and cardiometabolic diseases and helps avoid undesirable events. Ongoing investigations of novel approaches may contribute to improved patient care in the future.

articles.title: Dynamics of two reaction-diffusion SIS epidemic models with spatio-temporal periodic control strategies.
articles.abstract: In the practice of infectious disease prevention and control, the regional and cyclical interventions (e.g., seasonal sub-regional disinfection, localized lockdowns, or phased vaccination campaigns) are key factors in regulating the dynamic characteristics of disease transmission. In this paper, we investigate the dynamics of two reaction-diffusion susceptible-infected-susceptible (SIS) epidemic models incorporating spatio-temporal periodic control strategies. The models simulate the application of two strategies: one involves establishing local spatial control zones where the disease transmission rate is reduced to zero; the other entails population-wide control (e.g., large-scale vaccination, mask-wearing, or voluntary quarantine) to achieve an overall reduction in the transmission rate. By analyzing the impact of control cycles on disease spread, we find that longer durations and higher proportions of control measures enhance the likelihood of disease eradication, and further derive the critical period value that determines the outbreak and extinction of infectious diseases. In particular, we obtain the optimal and worst positions of the control zone in one-dimensional periodic space. We establish the threshold dynamics of the ordinary differential equation SIS model with multi-stage temporal control and the partial differential equation SIS model with multi-stage population-wide control. Finally, numerical simulations indicate that the optimal control zones should be prioritized for establishment in high-risk areas rather than low-risk areas. These insights may provide theoretical guidance for designing effective disease control policies.

articles.title: Imaging-based epicardial adipose tissue assessment and serum adipokines in postoperative atrial fibrillation after coronary artery bypass grafting.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is a common complication after cardiac surgery. We evaluated the associations of preoperative epicardial adipose tissue thickness (EATT), measured by transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) and multislice computed tomography (MSCT), and circulating adipokines with POAF after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), and compared the imaging methods. This prospective observational cohort included 96 consecutive eligible adults without prior atrial fibrillation who underwent elective isolated CABG. EATT was measured preoperatively by TTE and MSCT, and serum adiponectin, leptin, and resistin concentrations were determined. POAF was recorded during the first postoperative week. POAF occurred in 26 patients (27.1%). EATT measured by both methods was higher in patients who developed POAF. In multivariable analysis, EATT measured by TTE (odds ratio, 2.05; 95% confidence interval, 1.45-2.89; p < 0.001) and age (odds ratio, 1.08; 95% confidence interval, 1.00-1.156; p = 0.040) independently predicted POAF. The area under the curve was 0.818 for TTE (cutoff, 6.55 mm; sensitivity, 73.1%; specificity, 87.1%) and 0.787 for MSCT (cutoff, 6.22 mm; sensitivity, 80.8%; specificity, 75.7%), with no significant difference (p = 0.127). Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of - 0.016 mm. Serum adipokine concentrations were not associated with POAF. Increased EATT and older age independently predicted POAF after isolated CABG. TTE showed performance comparable to MSCT and may provide a practical, radiation-free approach to preoperative EATT assessment. Larger multicenter studies are needed.

articles.title: Effects of angiotensin receptor blockers on aortic growth and clinical events in Marfan syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract: Thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA) is a major cause of aortic dissection and premature mortality in Marfan syndrome. Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) may slow aortic enlargement, but their effects on clinical and imaging outcomes remain uncertain. The aim of the study is to evaluate the effects of ARBs on clinical events and aortic growth in patients with Marfan syndrome. We searched the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Ovid MEDLINE, PubMed, and Web of Science through February 1, 2025. Acute aortic dissection and all-cause mortality were the primary outcomes. Binary outcomes were analyzed using both Mantel-Haenszel common-effect (MH-CE) and inverse-variance random-effects (IV-RE) models. For outcomes with an event incidence below 10% in every contributing study, the MH-CE estimate was emphasized and the IV-RE estimate was treated as a sensitivity analysis. Continuous outcomes were analyzed using IV-RE models. All analyses were conducted with the meta package in R (v4.3.2). Seven randomized controlled trials involving 1522 patients with Marfan syndrome were included in the main analysis. For acute aortic dissection, the MH-CE estimate was RR 0·62 (95% CI 0·24-1·59) and the IV-RE estimate was RR 0·62 (95% CI 0·20-1·92). For all-cause mortality, the corresponding estimates were RR 0·53 (95% CI 0·17-1·64) and RR 0·58 (95% CI 0·16-2·07). Confidence intervals were wide and crossed unity. ARBs were associated with less aortic-root growth measured by MRI (MD - 0·48 mm/year, 95% CI - 0·89 to - 0·08) and by echocardiography over 3 years (MD - 0·51 mm/3 years, 95% CI - 0·85 to - 0·17), whereas annual echocardiographic measurement showed no significant difference (MD - 0·06 mm/year, 95% CI - 0·22 to 0·10). No significant effect was observed on ascending-aortic diameter, aortic Z-score at 3 years, aortic surgery, or serious adverse events. No statistically significant effect modification was detected in exploratory subgroup analyses. In patients with Marfan syndrome, ARB therapy was associated with small reductions in aortic-root growth in selected imaging analyses but did not significantly reduce acute aortic dissection or all-cause mortality. Sparse events, wide confidence intervals, and limited follow-up preclude firm conclusions regarding clinical benefit. Adequately powered, long-term trials with standardized imaging and clinical outcomes are required.

articles.title: Disproportionality analysis of ventricular extrasystoles reported with semaglutide in VigiBase and the FDA Adverse Event Monitoring System.
articles.abstract: Semaglutide is widely used to treat type 2 diabetes and obesity and to reduce cardiovascular risk. However, its association with cardiac rhythm-related adverse-event reporting in routine clinical practice remains incompletely characterized. To investigate cardiovascular and rhythm-related adverse-event reporting associated with semaglutide, with a focus on ventricular extrasystoles, we conducted a disproportionality analysis of individual case safety reports from VigiBase and the FDA Adverse Event Monitoring System (AEMS; formerly the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System [FAERS]). Reports were included when semaglutide was recorded as a suspected drug, according to database-specific criteria. Cardiovascular outcomes were identified using Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities Preferred Terms. Reporting odds ratios (RORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated. A cross-database reporting signal was defined as at least three semaglutide-associated reports and a lower 95% CI bound exceeding 1 in each database. After deduplication and application of the predefined inclusion criteria, 1980 semaglutide-associated cardiovascular reports from VigiBase and 1754 from AEMS were included. Among the screened cardiovascular and rhythm-related preferred terms, ventricular extrasystoles was the only term that met the prespecified signal criterion in both databases. Ventricular extrasystoles, clinically corresponding to premature ventricular contractions, showed disproportionate reporting in VigiBase (ROR 1.77, 95% CI 1.31-2.40) and AEMS (ROR 1.37, 95% CI 1.00-1.88; unrounded lower CI bound > 1). Ventricular extrasystoles showed a consistent disproportionality signal across VigiBase and AEMS. Although spontaneous reporting data cannot establish incidence, causality, or prognostic significance, this finding warrants prospective investigation using systematic electrocardiographic assessment and ambulatory rhythm monitoring.

articles.title: Dual-channel surface-enhanced Raman immunoassay for simultaneous determination of atrial-fibrillation-associated NT-proBNP and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I in artificial serum.
articles.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
articles.abstract: Atrial fibrillation is associated with myocardial wall stress and low-grade injury, yet parallel measurement of N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) generally requires separate immunoassays. We developed a single-chamber, dual-channel surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) immunoassay that combines antibody-functionalised magnetic capture beads with Au@Ag nanotags encoded by 4-mercaptobenzonitrile at 2227 cm-1 and 4-mercaptobenzoic acid at 1077 cm-1. A 9 × 9 full-factorial calibration design spanning 0-10 000 pg per mL NT-proBNP and 0-500 pg per mL hs-cTnI was executed across three independently prepared tag lots. Ten spatial spectra were aggregated at the sample level, preprocessed and quantified by a batch-grouped partial least-squares model. Limits of detection were 6.30 pg mL-1 for NT-proBNP and 0.46 pg mL-1 for hs-cTnI; corresponding limits of quantification were 18.7 and 1.35 pg mL-1. Across matrix lots and concentration levels, recoveries were 93.1-107.8% and total coefficients of variation were 4.8-9.4%. Thirty-six independently prepared, blinded artificial-serum specimens representing four dual-biomarker phenotypes were compared with electrochemiluminescence and chemiluminescent microparticle immunoassays. Under an equal-error-variance assumption, Deming slopes were 0.963 and 1.012, concordance correlation coefficients were 0.9951 and 0.9930, and concentration-quadrant agreement was 35/36. Grouped validation and specimen-level comparison assessed the dual readout without treating spatial spectra as independent replicates. This architecture provides a controlled route to simultaneous cardiac-biomarker measurement in artificial serum.

articles.title: Genomic and probiotic characterization of newly isolated Akkermansia strains from camel and horse feces in alleviating obesity and metabolic dysregulation.
articles.abstract: Accumulating evidence points to Akkermansia muciniphila as a promising candidate to improve obesity-associated metabolic disorders. However, studies on the isolation, identification, and functional validation of Akkermansia strains from the intestines of animals occupying specialized ecological niches (such as camel and horse) remain limited. In this study, we isolated an Akkermansia muciniphila strain Muc_T9 and an Akkermansia massiliensis strain Mas_DA from camel and horse feces, respectively. In vitro assessment revealed divergent probiotic adaptive traits between the two strains, particularly in gastrointestinal stress tolerance. Genomic analysis revealed the presence of genes encoding the functionally related effector proteins P9 and Amuc_1100. In high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mice, supplementing with Muc_T9 and Mas_DA significantly ameliorated HFD-induced obesity, dyslipidemia, glucose intolerance, and alleviated colonic inflammation and histological damage. Notably, divergent expression patterns of key genes involved in lipid metabolism and adipose tissue remodeling suggest potential differences in host metabolic regulatory modes. Furthermore, both strains restored gut microbial diversity and increased the relative abundance of putative short-chain fatty acids (SCFA)-producing bacteria. Collectively, Muc_T9 and Mas_DA effectively alleviate HFD-induced metabolic disturbances, providing a theoretical foundation for preventing obesity and metabolic diseases. However, due to the relatively short intervention period and the limitations of functional predictions, extended intervention combined with multi-omics approaches is warranted to further clarify the strain-specific regulatory mechanisms and sustained effects.

articles.title: Mucus Plugging Across Multiple Chronic Respiratory Diseases: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the prevalence, clinical characteristics, and clinical outcomes of mucus plugging across chronic respiratory diseases.

METHODS: Two authors searched four databases for eligible studies. Prevalence of mucus plugging was pooled and shown as percentage with a 95% confidence intervals (CI). Differences in clinical characteristics were summarized using mean differences or odds ratios, with corresponding 95% CIs. Sensitivity analyses, subgroup analyses and meta-regression were conducted for heterogeneity assessments. Associations between mucus plugging and clinical outcomes were systematically evaluated.

RESULTS: A total of 33 studies was included. Prevalence of mucus plugging in asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and cystic fibrosis reached 63% (95%CI 52%, 74%), 47% (95% CI 38%, 55%) and 63% (95% CI 46%, 81%) respectively. Mucus plugging was associated with higher eosinophil counts and FeNO, and lower FEV₁% and FEV₁/FVC in asthma, as well as higher smoking odds. In COPD, mucus plugging was associated with older age and lower BMI, FEV₁%, FVC% and FEV₁/FVC (all p < 0.05). Meta-regression suggested that eosinophil counts (p < 0.01), FeNO (p = 0.02) and FEV1% (p=0.04) contributed to heterogeneity in asthma, and inhaled corticosteroid (p < 0.01) and FEV1/FVC (p < 0.01) contributed to heterogeneity in COPD. Presence of mucus plugging was also associated with higher risk of acute exacerbation, mortality, prolonged hospital stays and increased hospitalization costs in patients with COPD.

CONCLUSION: Mucus plugging is prevalent in chronic respiratory diseases and associated with distinct clinical characteristics and outcomes. Future research may focus on mucus plugging as a treatable trait to improve prognosis of these patients.

articles.title: Association Between Socioeconomic Status and Dysphagia Among Japanese Adults.
articles.abstract: Socioeconomic status (SES) is a well-established determinant of various health outcomes; however, its association with dysphagia remains poorly understood. We examined the association of household income and educational attainment with the prevalence of dysphagia among community-dwelling Japanese adults. This cross-sectional study included a total of 9,912 adults (4,225 men aged 21-95 years and 5,687 women aged 20-91 years). Dysphagia was assessed using the 10-item Eating Assessment Tool. SES was evaluated by self-reported household income and educational attainment. Logistic regression analysis was performed, stratified by age (younger: <65 years; older: ≥65 years) and sex. Models were adjusted for age, smoking status, alcohol consumption, leisure-time physical activity, living alone, number of medications, toothbrushing frequency, self-reported bilateral posterior occlusal support, hypertension, dyslipidemia, diabetes mellitus, and body mass index. In both sexes, household income was significantly associated with lower odds of dysphagia among participants aged ≥ 65 years, but not among those aged < 65 years. Conversely, an inverse association between educational attainment and the prevalence of dysphagia was consistently observed in men regardless of age, whereas this association was only observed among women aged < 65 years. Higher household income was inversely associated with dysphagia among men and women aged ≥ 65 years. Higher educational attainment was inversely associated with dysphagia among men regardless of age and women aged < 65 years.

articles.title: Independent predictors of 28-day mortality in ICU patients with Acinetobacter baumannii versus Non-Acinetobacter baumannii gram-negative tracheal aspirate isolates.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated independent risk factors affecting 28-day mortality in intensive care unit (ICU) patients with Acinetobacter baumannii versus non-A. baumannii Gram-negative bacilli isolated from tracheal aspirate cultures. Overall, 120 ICU patients (66 males, 54 females; age: 36-94) enrolled between January 2024 and December 2025 were divided into two equal groups: the A. baumannii (n = 60) and the non-A. baumannii (n = 60). Age, sex, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) score, APACHE II score, septic shock rates, and CRP levels were similar between groups (P > 0.05). However, carbapenem resistance (98.3% vs. 56.7%; P < 0.001), mechanical ventilation (MV) requirement (75.0% vs. 53.3%; P = 0.022), and 28-day mortality (63.3% vs. 40.0%; P = 0.018) were significantly higher in the A. baumannii group. ICU length of stay was significantly shorter in the A. baumannii group (16.5 vs. 26.5 days; P = 0.008), due to early-period mortality. Predominant non-A. baumannii pathogens were Klebsiella pneumoniae (51.7%) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (35%). Multivariate logistic regression identified MV requirement (aOR: 4.706, 95% CI: 1.792-12.359, P = 0.002), A. baumannii infection (aOR: 2.512, 95% CI: 1.055-5.983, P = 0.037), and higher CCI score (aOR: 1.523, 95% CI: 1.155-2.007, P = 0.003) as independent predictors of 28-day mortality. A. baumannii isolation from tracheal aspirates and MV requirement are strong independent risk factors for 28-day mortality in ICU patients. High carbapenem resistance restricts therapeutic options and drives early mortality. Early diagnosis, rapid microbiological identification, targeted antimicrobial therapy, and strict infection control practices are paramount to improving survival outcomes in critically ill patients.

articles.title: Post-Pars Plana Vitrectomy Endophthalmitis in Patients with and without Systemic Immunosuppression.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether systemic immunosuppression is associated with endophthalmitis after pars plana vitrectomy (PPV), and whether risk varies by drug class and time window.

METHODS: Retrospective propensity score matched cohort study using TriNetX, a federated network of 72 US healthcare organizations. Exposed adults undergoing PPV used corticosteroids, classic nonbiologic immunosuppressants, targeted small molecule immunomodulators, or biologics for at least 3 months before surgery; controls had none in the prior year. Matching controlled for demographics, comorbidities, and surgical indication. The outcome was endophthalmitis within 365 days, assessed over early (1-42 days), 1-90 day, and later (43-365 day) windows. Cox modeling was secondary.

RESULTS: After matching, 25,997 patients per cohort were analyzed. No class was associated with endophthalmitis during the early window. During the later window, risk was higher for all immunosuppressants (RR 1.74; 95% CI 1.33 to 2.28; P < .0001), corticosteroids (RR 1.81; 95% CI 1.38 to 2.37; P < .0001), and biologics (RR 2.00; 95% CI 1.00 to 4.03; P = .045). In Cox regression, corticosteroids (HR 1.19; 95% CI 1.01 to 1.39; P = .037) and biologics (HR 1.51; 95% CI 1.08 to 2.11; P = .016) remained independent risk factors.

CONCLUSION: Systemic corticosteroid use prior to PPV was associated with late-onset endophthalmitis, with excess risk appearing between 43 and 365 days rather than in the early period. This timing is atypical for surgically acquired infection, and some late events may reflect endogenous or inflammatory disease. Immunosuppressed patients may warrant a longer window of suspicion.

articles.title: Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 Inhibitors and Bullous Pemphigoid: A Danish Nationwide Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Anti-diabetic dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4i) are associated with an increased risk of bullous pemphigoid (BP), but Danish population-based data, including product specific estimates, are lacking.

METHODS: We conducted a nationwide matched case-control study in Denmark of incident BP cases diagnosed between 2007 and 2024. BP cases were matched 1:100 to population controls using risk set sampling based on age, sex, and index date. DPP-4i exposure was defined as at least one redeemed prescription before the index date (ever use) or during the preceding three months (current use). In a specificity analysis, we compared DPP-4i users and users of other type 2 antidiabetics without DPP-4i use with non-users of type 2 diabetes medications. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% CIs were estimated using conditional logistic regression.

RESULTS: We identified 2,497 incident BP cases and 249,700 controls (median age 78 years). DPP-4i exposure was more common among BP cases for both ever use (OR: 3.81, 95% CI: 3.31-4.40) and current use (OR: 5.59, 95% CI: 4.70-6.63). For current use, the highest odds ratios were observed for vildagliptin (OR: 10.82, 95% CI: 6.73-17.41) and linagliptin (OR: 9.86, 95% CI: 7.33-13.25), whereas the estimate for sitagliptin was lower (OR: 2.46, 95% CI: 1.65-3.66). In the specificity analysis, other antidiabetic therapies did not show a similarly increased risk of BP.

CONCLUSION: In the Danish population there was a strong association between DPP-4i use and incident BP. This was most pronounced for vildagliptin and linagliptin while the signal was weaker for sitagliptin.

articles.title: Comparison of PSMA- and CD70-targeted PET/CT in The Diagnosis of Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Retrospective Cohort and Prospective Head-to-head Study.
articles.journal: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Currently, PSMA- and CD70-targeted imaging are the main focuses in the molecular imaging of RCC, but these modalities have not been compared in clinical studies. The primary outcome of this study was to compare the sensitivity of two imaging modalities in diagnosing RCC lesions and explore their diagnostic thresholds. Secondary outcomes included differences in detection rates, variations in tumor uptake, target-to-background ratios, and their practical impact on patient treatment decisions.

EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN: Retrospectively, data were collected from patients with pathologically confirmed RCC who underwent PSMA-targeted ([68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11) or CD70-targeted ([68Ga]Ga-NOTA-RCCB6) PET/CT. Tumor uptake, target-to-background ratio, and lesion detection rates were compared. Another independent prospective study enrolled patients with suspected RCC who underwent both imaging modalities, comparing the sensitivity of the two methods in detecting RCC lesions and investigating diagnostic thresholds.

RESULTS: The retrospective cohort included 128 patients, while the prospective study finally enrolled 36 patients. [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-RCCB6 exhibited higher sensitivity (88.7% vs. 76.1%; P < 0.001) for ccRCC, particularly for pulmonary and hepatic metastases, and exhibited higher SUVmax and TBR at the primary lesion and in pulmonary metastases. The detection rates of [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-RCCB6 and [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 were both limited for nccRCC (68.8% and 63.0%, respectively). [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-RCCB6 improved the extent of lesion detection in 35% (9/26) of patients and affected treatment decisions in 15% (4/26) of patients.

CONCLUSIONS: [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-RCCB6 PET/CT significantly enhanced diagnostic sensitivity for pulmonary and hepatic metastases, facilitating precise staging and treatment decision-making. Therefore, it represents a valuable complement to existing imaging modalities for ccRCC.

articles.title: Molecular determinants of Kingella kingae translocation across polarized respiratory epithelium.
articles.abstract: Kingella kingae is the leading cause of osteoarticular infections in children under 36 months of age. The pathogenesis of K. kingae disease begins with colonization of the oropharynx followed by translocation across the respiratory epithelium, entry into the bloodstream, and dissemination to distant sites. The bacterial factors that facilitate translocation across the respiratory barrier are poorly understood. In this study, we used polarized Calu-3 cells differentiated at an air-liquid interface (ALI) as a model of the respiratory epithelium combined with molecular genetics, barrier integrity measurements, cytotoxicity assays, and RNA sequencing to interrogate the molecular mechanism by which K. kingae breaches the respiratory epithelium. We found that the pore-forming RtxA toxin drives disruption of the epithelial barrier and is a major contributor to translocation. We observed that type IV pili (T4P) also contribute to translocation and mediate a toxin-independent translocation mechanism. Strains lacking both RtxA and T4P were unable to translocate, confirming that at least one or the other of these factors is required for translocation. Transcriptomic profiling of K. kingae identified 512 differentially expressed bacterial genes during infection and suggested a new role for HprK and a novel esterase in the process of translocation. This study establishes that multiple bacterial factors influence K. kingae translocation across the respiratory epithelial barrier and provides insight into important gene expression changes during K. kingae interaction with host cells.

articles.title: When Less is More: A Physiology-Driven Approach to a 17-Hydroxylase Deficiency Case Series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: 17-hydroxylase deficiency (17OHD) is a very rare form of congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) caused by autosomal recessive mutations in the cytochrome P450 family (CYP17A1). Despite low cortisol, adrenal insufficiency does not typically manifest because elevated corticosterone, a weaker glucocorticoid (GC), exerts GC effects. Exogenous GC are the foundation of treatment but can be associated with significant side effects. Published literature regarding management strategies is limited.

CASE PRESENTATIONS: We describe three female adolescents treated for 17OHD with different GC regimens. All patients presented at age 14 with delayed puberty, hypertension, and primary ovarian insufficiency. Patient 1 was initially treated with physiological hydrocortisone divided three times daily (10 mg/m2/d) and spironolactone 100 mg/d, separately and combined, which did not lower her blood pressure (BP). Eventually, a combination of physiological hydrocortisone once daily (8.8 mg/m2/d) and gradual titration to a higher spironolactone dose (100 mg bid) normalized her BP (115/75 mmHg) with no side effects. Patient 2 was treated with dexamethasone 0.25 mg daily for 10 years with poor follow-up and developed multiple complications related to supraphysiological GC use. She was transitioned and successfully treated with hydrocortisone 10 mg every morning and 5 mg every afternoon with a normal BP and potassium for over a year. Patient 3 was treated with cortisone acetate for 2.6 years and then with dexamethasone for about 10 months before discontinuation of GC and transition to spironolactone monotherapy. Her potassium and BP remained normal.

CONCLUSION: In conclusion, 17OHD is a rare form of CAH, with about 500 published cases and limited established management guidance. Our cases highlight the importance of considering the pathophysiology of 17OHD when developing a management plan; a supraphysiological GC therapy may not be necessary to manage the hypertension and hypokalemia. Physiological hydrocortisone dosing lowers but does not normalize DOC production allowing DOC to exert GC effects. Physiological hydrocortisone and/or monotherapy with mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists both mitigate GC-related side effects, avoid adrenal suppression, and minimize risk for adrenal crisis in patients with 17OHD.

articles.title: Flagellin enhances innate immune responses in human airway epithelium during bacterial infection.
articles.abstract: Bacterial pneumonia poses a significant challenge to public health, often leading to antibiotic treatment failure. Enhancing innate immunity represents a promising adjunctive strategy to conventional antibiotic therapy. Bacterial flagellin, a Toll-like receptor 5 (TLR5) agonist, has been shown to stimulate innate immune defenses when delivered via the respiratory route, demonstrating efficacy in both preventing and treating bacterial pneumonia in murine models. This protective effect is primarily mediated through TLR5-driven activation of airway epithelial cells. This study aimed to characterize the immunomodulatory effects of flagellin on human primary respiratory epithelium. Using the MucilAir air-liquid interface model and RNA sequencing, we demonstrated that apical administration of flagellin induced robust immune responses in airway epithelium derived from healthy individuals, as well as patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and cystic fibrosis (CF). TLR5-mediated epithelial signaling triggered key immune-related pathways, including cytokine production, leukocyte chemotaxis, neutrophil recruitment, and antimicrobial defense, with strong commonalities across healthy and diseased airway epithelia. Furthermore, we demonstrated that flagellin effectively activated immune responses during infection of the airway epithelium with the bacteria Pseudomonas aeruginosa or Streptococcus pneumoniae. However, epithelial activation alone was insufficient to directly limit bacterial colonization or replication, highlighting the potential role of epithelial-immune cell interactions in achieving effective bacterial clearance. These findings support TLR5 activation as a promising therapeutic strategy to enhance host defense mechanisms and improve treatment outcomes for bacterial pneumonia in both healthy individuals and patients with COPD or CF.

articles.title: Prolonged Versus Intermittent Piperacillin-Tazobactam Infusion in Critically Ill Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Prolonged infusion of β-lactam antibiotics is recommended for adults with sepsis, but whether this benefit applies specifically to piperacillin-tazobactam remains uncertain. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing prolonged with intermittent infusion of piperacillin-tazobactam in critically ill adults.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials from inception to March 10, 2026. Eligible randomized controlled trials compared prolonged (continuous or extended) with intermittent infusion of piperacillin-tazobactam in critically ill adults. Primary outcomes were clinical cure and all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included intensive care unit length of stay and duration of antibiotic therapy. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to calculate pooled risk ratios for dichotomous outcomes and mean differences for continuous outcomes.

RESULTS: Seven studies comprising 6,080 patients were included. For clinical cure, the pooled estimate favored prolonged infusion (risk ratio 1.23, 95% confidence interval 1.07-1.42, 6 trials, 585 participants; very low-certainty evidence). The effect on 28-day mortality was uncertain (risk ratio 0.47, 95% confidence interval 0.16-1.41, 2 trials, 104 participants; low-certainty evidence). There was no clear difference in 90-day mortality (risk ratio 0.92, 95% confidence interval 0.84-1.01, 2 trials, 5,532 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). BLING III contributed 99.3% of the weight in the analysis. The pooled mean difference in antibiotic treatment duration was -2.47 days (95% confidence interval -3.92 to -1.02, 2 trials, 120 participants; very low-certainty evidence), but the evidence was very uncertain.

CONCLUSION: In this meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials, prolonged infusion of piperacillin-tazobactam may improve clinical cure in critically ill adults, but the evidence is very uncertain. The estimate for 90-day mortality was consistent with the direction of benefit reported for β-lactams overall, but the confidence interval included no effect. These findings are consistent with the class-level evidence but do not independently confirm a mortality benefit specific to piperacillin-tazobactam. The effects on 28-day mortality and antibiotic treatment duration remain uncertain.

articles.title: Relationship between trunk and pelvis coordination strategies and stances during tennis forehand strokes.
articles.abstract: The forehand is the most common groundstroke, yet stance-related pelvis-trunk mechanics during acceleration remain unclear.
