We compared open (OS), semi-open (SES), and square stance (SS) forehands in 25 male competitive tennis players (21.3 ± 2.0 years) performing maximal-effort flat strokes, with three-dimensional kinematics recorded at 200 Hz. Signed peak X-factor, forward momentum, angular-momentum peaks, peak delay, and continuous relative phase (CRP) variability were analysed using repeated-measures ANOVA. Time series of pelvis and trunk angular momentum and CRP were analysed using one-dimensional statistical parametric mapping (SPM1D). Stance affected peak delay, signed peak X-factor, forward momentum, and peak pelvis angular momentum, but not peak trunk angular momentum. Mean signed peak X-factor was negative in OS and SS but positive in SES. OS predominantly showed pelvis-first angular-momentum peaks, whereas SES and SS predominantly showed trunk-first peaks. SS showed the greatest forward momentum. During early acceleration, pelvis and trunk angular momentum were greater in OS and SES than in SS. CRP differed significantly among stances during 14.3%-62.5% of acceleration, with post hoc comparisons indicating greater pelvis phase lead in OS and SES than in SS. These patterns may inform stance-specific biomechanical assessment. Their associations with ball speed and stroke performance remain untested.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in Paediatric Endocrinology: A Narrative Review from the Perspective of Early-career Clinicians and Researchers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) use by early-career paediatric endocrinologists has started without waiting for the training and governance structures to develop. Since early-career physicians and researchers of today hold no pre-AI performance baseline against which to appraise the AI outputs, career stage-specific concerns regarding rapid adoption of AI use in the field have emerged. The goal of this review was to examine AI use in paediatric endocrinology from the early-career perspective.

SUMMARY: A narrative, non-systematic literature review regarding the AI use in paediatric endocrinology across the four professional domains (curricular coverage, clinical practice, teaching, and research) was conducted in January 2026 and updated through July 2026. 57 relevant publications were identified, with level of evidence differing significantly between domains, and inversely with how freely the AI tools are used: from randomised-trials data regarding specific clinical applications like closed-loop insulin delivery and automated bone age assessment, to no published data regarding use of large language models in the research domain. Greatest benefit of automated bone age assessment in the early career stage was reported, while no published studies examining AI use by early-career paediatric endocrinologists were found.

KEY MESSAGES: While being most exposed to unsupervised AI use, early-career physicians are also the least studied group. Having in mind the lack of pre-AI baseline in this population, findings of this review emphasize the potential career stage-dependent risks regarding the AI use, and the need for subspecialty-specific AI competency frameworks.

articles.title: MRI-Based Analysis of Post-HIFU Efficacy in Uterine Adenomyosis and Personalized Treatment Strategies.
articles.abstract: Objectives To evaluate the clinical outcomes of high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) ablation in patients with different subtypes of adenomyosis as classified by preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and to explore the implications for personalized treatment planning. Design A retrospective cohort study. Participants 447 patients with adenomyosis who underwent HIFU treatment were classified according to the Kishi MRI criteria into Type I (intrinsic, n=195), Type II (extrinsic, n=92), Type III (intramural, n=50), and Type IV (full-thickness, n=110). Methods All 447 patients underwent HIFU ablation under standardized procedural protocols.Treatment parameters, non-perfused volume (NPV) ratio, relief of dysmenorrhea (assessed by NRS score), and improvement in menstrual blood volume (assessed by FPS score) were analyzed and compared across subtypes at 3 and 6 months post-treatment. Results Patients with Type IV adenomyosis had significantly larger lesion volumes and required longer treatment durations with higher energy delivery (p<0.001). The NPV ratio was highest in Type I (74.91% ± 28.34%), followed by Type III (70.34% ± 26.12%), both significantly higher than in Type II (60.01% ± 2.9%) and Type IV (65.93% ± 25.41%) (p<0.05). All subtypes demonstrated significant and sustained improvement in both dysmenorrhea and menorrhagia at follow-up (p<0.05). The comprehensive treatment success rate was highest for Type IV at both 3 (21.82%) and 6 months (27.27%). Limitations This study has several limitations. First, the retrospective design inherently introduces selection bias and limits causal inference. Second,long-term follow-up beyond 6 months was not available, precluding assessment of durability of symptom relief and recurrence rates. Conclusions High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) provides effective symptom relief for all MRI-classified subtypes of adenomyosis. Treatment parameters and efficacy, however, vary by subtype. MRI classification is therefore crucial for guiding treatment and anticipating technical challenges. A personalized approach based on subtype may further optimize therapeutic outcomes.

articles.title: Thioxanthone micellar platform for versatile photocatalysis in water via dual energy and electron transfer.
articles.abstract: A thioxanthone-based nonionic surfactant forms micellar nanoreactors enabling versatile aqueous photocatalysis via energy transfer (EnT) and/or photoinduced electron transfer (PET). Without a sacrificial electron donor, it sensitises molecular oxygen for thioether oxidation. Conversely, adding a nickel catalyst and Et3N switches the path to PET, driving C-P couplings in water.

articles.title: Dynamic Transmitral Gradient From Eccentric Aortic Regurgitation Resolved by Valve-in-Valve TAVR.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bioprosthetic aortic valve degeneration can present as isolated regurgitant failure, and an eccentric jet may raise the transmitral gradient, mimicking mitral stenosis.

CASE SUMMARY: An 84-year-old man presented with acute heart failure 12 years after surgical aortic valve replacement. Echocardiography showed a degenerated Trifecta bioprosthesis with an immobile leaflet causing severe eccentric aortic regurgitation, whose jet impinged on the anterior mitral leaflet and produced severe functional mitral stenosis. Given high surgical risk, the heart team performed transfemoral valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement.

DISCUSSION: Trifecta leaflet tear causes regurgitant rather than stenotic failure; an eccentric jet can raise the transmitral gradient independent of the Austin Flint murmur. Valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement eliminated the regurgitation, improved leaflet mobility, and reduced the mean mitral gradient from 17 to 6 mm Hg, with complete symptom resolution.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Eccentric aortic regurgitation can cause a reversible rise in transmitral gradient; treating it can resolve apparent mitral stenosis without mitral intervention.

articles.title: First-in-Human Mechanical Bilateral Iatrogenic Coronary Leaflet Obstruction Risk Nullification (BICORN) for Transcatheter Aortic Valve-in-Valve Replacement.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We describe mechanical leaflet traversal as an alternative to electrosurgical traversal for BICORN during valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement in a patient with unfavorable cardiac orientation and extreme bilateral coronary obstruction risk.

KEY STEPS: The ShortCut device created targeted basal splits in both coronary leaflets. The left coronary cusp split was crossed using a Pilot 100 guidewire (Abbott) and microcatheter with an EBU 3.5 guide catheter (Medtronic) and Agilis steerable introducer (Abbott) support. After balloon dilation, the left coronary cusp was translocated with an 18-mm True Dilatation Balloon (BD). A 20-mm SAPIEN 3 Ultra transcatheter heart valve (Edwards Lifesciences) was then advanced through the right coronary cusp split and deployed within the pre-existing 23-mm SAPIEN 3 valve (Edwards Lifesciences).

POTENTIAL PITFALLS: Mechanical traversal requires precise targeting. Leaflet translocation may cause embolization, severe aortic insufficiency, or hemodynamic compromise, requiring readiness for immediate valve deployment.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Mechanical traversal may facilitate BICORN when cardiac rotation, unfavorable catheter trajectory, neosinus malalignment, eccentric coronary takeoffs, or leaflet fibrocalcification make electrosurgical traversal challenging.

articles.title: Inadvertent Left Ventricular Pacing Through an Unrecognized Sinus Venosus Atrial Septal Defect.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inadvertent left ventricular (LV) lead placement is rare but exposes patients to systemic thromboembolism.

CASE SUMMARY: An 89-year-old man received a dual-chamber pacemaker for atrial fibrillation with paroxysmal complete heart block. Severe right atrial dilatation prevented right ventricular lead placement, and the operator converted to a sheath-delivered "left bundle branch area" approach. Seven months later, imaging unexpectedly showed the lead coursing from the superior vena cava through an unrecognized superior sinus venosus defect into the left atrium, across the mitral valve, into the LV. Transesophageal echocardiography confirmed a 30 × 20 mm superior sinus venosus defect with partial anomalous pulmonary venous return.

DISCUSSION: A paced right bundle branch block pattern is expected during left bundle branch area pacing, and activation-time criteria may be falsely reassuring when the lead paces the LV endocardium directly. Atrial septal defect screening is warranted whenever right-sided dilatation is unexplained.

articles.title: Blue Babies Grown Old: Aspirational Care for an Older Patient With ACHD.

Cost-Minimization and Budget-Impact Analysis of N-Terminal Pro B-Type Natriuretic Peptide Biomarker Assay for the Risk Assessment and Monitoring of Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension in the Australian Healthcare Setting.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) is a biomarker for risk stratification in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Published evidence supports NT-proBNP as a complementary parameter within the multiparameter risk stratification framework recommended by the 2022 European Society of Cardiology/European Respiratory Society guidelines, used alongside transthoracic echocardiography (TTE). This study compares the financial implications of a publicly funded NT-proBNP biomarker assay with a TTE-based approach in patients with PAH from the Australian healthcare perspective.

METHODS: The cost-minimization analysis estimates the annual per-patient cost of risk assessment in PAH. Additionally, a 6-year budget-impact analysis was conducted using an epidemiological approach. The model compared publicly funded NT-proBNP-guided risk assessment in PAH with a reference scenario using TTE alone, with NT-proBNP estimated to replace 1.5 TTE tests per patient annually. Model inputs were derived from Australian public databases and published literature, with costs adjusted to 2025 Australian dollars.

RESULTS: The unit costs for NT-proBNP and TTE tests were $58.50 and $258.70, respectively. The annual per-patient cost with public funding of NT-proBNP was $880.75 compared with $1034.80 without NT-proBNP, leading to a yearly cost saving of $154.05. The budget-impact model estimated 2450 patients with PAH in year 1, increasing to 3619 by year 6. Assuming 90% uptake rate of NT-proBNP testing, the net savings to the Medicare Benefits Schedule ranged from $288 549 in year 1 to $426 190 in year 6 (85% Medicare Benefits Schedule rebate applied).

CONCLUSIONS: Routine NT-proBNP testing for risk assessment and monitoring in PAH could result in considerable cost savings of $2.3 million over 6 years.

articles.title: National registry data on the neonatal outcome of infants born at 22-25 weeks in Germany.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: There are no population-based data on neonatal outcomes of infants born in Germany at 22-25 weeks' gestation. We set out to obtain national data on neonatal outcomes of infants born at 22-25 weeks gestation.

METHODS: We analyzed mandatory quality control data submitted by all neonatal intensive care units on all infants born alive in Germany at 220/7 to 256/7 weeks' gestation and generating a neonatal case who died or were discharged between 1/1/2014 and 31/12/2023, focusing on survival to discharge/transfer and survival without severe complications of prematurity.

RESULTS: The number of live-births totaled 1889 at 22, 3405 at 23, 5193 at 24 weeks, and 5572 at 25 weeks. The proportion of infants offered intensive care at birth increased from 39.9% at 22 to 98.9% at 25 weeks. Across the 10-year study period, this proportion increased from 37.6% (2014-2018) to 42.2% (2019-2023; p=0.04) for infants born at 22 weeks, but did not change at higher gestations. Survival in those offered intensive care at birth ranged from 41.4% at 22 weeks to 84.1% at 25 weeks. Survival without severe complications of prematurity in those offered intensive care increased from 8.0% to 43.0% between 22 and 25 weeks.

CONCLUSIONS: In Germany, ∼40% of infants born alive at 22 weeks were offered intensive care at birth, of whom ∼40% survived. In these survivors, about 20% were discharged without severe neonatal complications. These population-based data may help to counsel parents with imminent birth at 22-23 weeks. The low number of live births at 22 and 23 weeks may reflect withholding of proactive prenatal management. Future studies should also ascertain deaths before labor and during delivery.

articles.title: Lineage tracing of alpha-to-beta cell transition after injection of Wnt pathway-stimulated human multipotent stromal cell-secreted proteins.
articles.abstract: Diabetes is projected to affect >600 million people by 2045. Although life-saving insulin therapy can manage hyperglycemia, exogenous insulin is not a cure for diabetes, and life-expectancy for those affected is reduced by 10-15 years. Regenerative therapies aimed at replenishing functional beta cell mass have gained interest. However, the cellular mechanisms that mediate islet regeneration remain unclear. We have shown that human bone marrow-derived multipotent stromal cells (MSC), licenced by WNT-pathway activation using CHIR99021 (CHIR), secrete factors (CHIR CdM) that promote beta-cell recovery in streptozotocin (STZ)-treated immunodeficient NOD/SCID mice. Here, we investigated whether this regeneration involved alpha-to-beta cell conversion, using a Glucagon-iCre;Rosa26-TdTomato (GcgXTdT) lineage-tracing model. Following hyperglycemia induction with STZ and intrapancreatic injection of CHIR CdM, TdTomato+/insulin+ cells were transiently increased within 4 days of injection, indicating alpha cell plasticity and acquisition of insulin expression. CHIR CdM injection also increased the abundance and proliferation of insulin+ cells at day 28. Additionally, CHIR CdM injection altered infiltrating pancreatic immune cell composition, including increased CD4+ and CD68+ cells. Together, these findings demonstrate that intrapancreatic administration of a single injection of CHIR CdM initiates a regenerative response characterized by alpha-to-beta cell plasticity, insulin+ cell-proliferation, and immune remodeling in immune competent GcgxTdT mice. While additional regenerative stimuli may be required for beta cell maturation to restore glycemic control, understanding the mechanisms by which pancreatic beta cell regeneration is initiated in the presence of immune cells may help inform therapies for the treatment of diabetes.

articles.title: Ventricular arrhythmia-heart failure interaction and mortality in ICD recipients after myocardial infarction.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Ventricular arrhythmia (VA) and heart failure (HF) frequently coexist in patients with ischaemic left ventricular (LV) dysfunction. Whether VA and HF events are bidirectionally associated remains unclear. We investigated their bidirectional relationship and associations with mortality.

METHODS: We analysed 1014 patients from the multicentre WICD-MI study. All received a wearable cardioverter-defibrillator after acute myocardial infarction (MI) and subsequently underwent implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) implantation, with persistent LV ejection fraction ≤35%. Associations between ICD-treated VA, HF-events (HF hospitalization, heart transplantation, or LV assist device implantation), and all-cause mortality were assessed using time-dependent Cox models.

RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 2.6 years post-ICD implantation, VA was independently associated with an increased risk of HF events [aHR = 3.50 (1.66-7.38), P = .001], while HF events similarly preceded subsequent VA [aHR = 2.96 (1.59-5.50), P = .0008]. Both were independently associated with all-cause mortality, with a numerically higher aHR for HF events [aHR = 7.96 (4.71-13.47), P < .0001] than for VA [aHR = 4.43 (2.35-8.36), P < .0001]. Sensitivity analyses suggested that the VA-HF association was strongest for shock-treated arrhythmias. In exploratory analyses, VA was strongly associated with subsequent HF events in subcutaneous ICD recipients [aHR = 15.08 (4.62-49.22), P < .0001] but not in transvenous ICD recipients (P for interaction = .0002).

CONCLUSION: In ICD recipients with persistent LV dysfunction following MI, VA and HF events are bidirectionally associated and independently associated with mortality. The VA-HF association was strongest for shock-treated arrhythmias. These findings highlight the potential value of integrated HF and VA management.

articles.title: Medication Administration Errors by Caregivers of Children with Chronic Illness in Home Settings: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: International journal for quality in health care : journal of the International Society for Quality in Health Care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Home-based medication administration is vital for managing paediatric chronic conditions but is prone to errors that affect patient safety and outcomes. Children suffering from​ chronic conditions such as cancer, diabetes, epilepsy, and sickle cell disease frequently require medication outside hospital settings, necessitating non-professional caregivers to administer and oversee these medications. This systematic review synthesised global evidence on medication administration errors (MAEs) by caregivers in home settings.

METHODS: In accordance with the JBI methodology and PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Scopus for English-language studies published between January 2015 and December 2025. The methodological quality of the studies was evaluated using the JBI critical appraisal checklists, and data were collected using standardized JBI forms and were synthesized narratively.

RESULTS: Out of 25,508 records reviewed, 12 studies met the inclusion criteria. The prevalence of errors, as observed directly, ranged from 30% to 80%, with pharmacist-led assessments identifying a high rate of 89.89%. Dosing errors were the most frequently reported, appearing in six of the 12 studies, followed by errors related to timing and the method or route of administration. Clinical harm was reported in 8-12.8% of the error cases, resulting in preventable hospitalizations and treatment failures due to chronic underdosing. The most consistently noted risk factors were polypharmacy, insufficient health literacy among caregivers, and limited caregiver proficiency in English.

CONCLUSIONS: Medication errors at home are frequent and have significant clinical implications for children with chronic illnesses. To address this, healthcare systems should incorporate structured education for caregivers into discharge plans and enhance access to dosing aids and digital tools, especially in resource-constrained areas such as sub-Saharan Africa.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics of Mediastinal Paragangliomas: A retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Studies focusing on mediastinal paragangliomas are limited. In this study, we describe the clinical, pathological, and genetic characteristics of mediastinal paragangliomas.

METHODS: Clinical data from all patients with extrapericardial mediastinal paragangliomas at a single center were retrospectively analyzed. Germline variants were assessed using next-generation sequencing and Sanger sequencing of blood samples. Patients were grouped according to genetic variants and tumor location, and clinical characteristics were compared.

RESULTS: 22 patients (male:female ratio, 8:14) were included in the study, with a mean age of 41.4 years. Hypertension was present in 16 patients (72.7%), and 13 (59.1%) exhibited typical catecholamine-related symptoms. Tumors were located in the anterior, middle, and posterior mediastinum in 1 (4.5%), 4 (18.2%), and 17 (77.3%) cases, with an average size of 5.3±1.7 cm. Multiple tumors were identified in 6 patients. Catecholamine-producing tumors were observed in 17/21 (81.0%) patients. Surgical resection was performed in 20 (90.9%) patients. No postoperative local recurrences were observed. Metastasis occurred in 2/18 (11.1%) cases. Eleven patients underwent genetic testing; six harbored SDHx mutations. Compared with anterior and middle mediastinal tumors, posterior mediastinal tumors were associated with higher rates of typical symptoms (12/17 vs. 1/5, p = 0.043) and catecholamine-producing function (17/17 vs. 0/4, p < 0.001), as well as higher levels of 24-hour urinary norepinephrine (5.10 × ULN vs. 0.56 × ULN, p = 0.037).

CONCLUSION: Mediastinal paragangliomas are rare and are frequently associated with SDHx variants. Posterior mediastinal tumors are predominantly functional and noradrenergic; recognizing these features may facilitate diagnosis.

articles.title: Effect of Ivermectin on Biosafety and HSP70 Gene Expression in Cyprinus carpio.
articles.abstract: The present study evaluated the biosafety of Ivermectin (IVM) and its effects on haematological, serum- biochemical, immunological, heat shock protein 70 (HSP70) expression in Cyprinus carpio. The median lethal dose (LD50) of IVM was estimated as 8.91 ± 3.46 mg kg⁻¹ body weight. Based on the LD50 study, a biosafety assessment was conducted using single oral doses of IVM at 0 (control), 0.54, 1.00, 2.55, 3.69, and 5.11 IVM mg kg⁻¹ body weight over 21 days. Haemato-physiological, biochemical, immunological and molecular responses were evaluated to access the physiological effects of IVM exposure. Principal component analysis (PCA) revealed clear dose-dependent clustering, while Multivariate analysis of Variance (MANOVA) indicated overall treatment effects measured among the six experimental groups at each respective sampling day (Wilks' λ = 9.21 × 10⁻¹², Pillai's trace = 4.8621, p < 0.001). Key stress determinants includes red blood cell (RBC), white blood cell (WBC), haemoglobin (Hb), packed cell volume (PCV), liver enzymes, nitro blue tetrazolium (NBT) activity, serum lysozyme (LYZ), and HSP70 expression, demonstrated an dose-dependent physiological stress. Fish exposed to ≥ 2.55 IVM mg kg⁻¹ body weight, showed pronounced physiological stress, whereas doses ≤1.00 IVM mg kg⁻¹ body weight, caused minimal alterations. All parameters at 0.54 IVM mg kg⁻¹ body weight, were comparable to the control, identifying this dose as the No Observed Adverse Effect Level (NOAEL), while 1.00 IVM mg kg⁻¹ body weight was designated the Lowest Observed Adverse Effect Level (LOAEL). These findings emphasize the need for cautious use of IVM in aquaculture and provides a basis for defining safe dosage limits of IVM for its application in aquaculture.

articles.title: Demographic variation of viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus among Round Gobies in the St. Lawrence River.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We investigated the demographic dynamics of viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus (VHSV) infections in wild Round Goby Neogobius melanostomus from the nearshore habitats of the upper St. Lawrence River from 2018 to 2022. We examined viral prevalence and titers between Round Goby sexes and age-classes to identify how demography correlates with prevalence and amplification of this pathogen within this host species.

METHODS: Reverse-transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction was used to detect and quantify viral N-gene genetic material in pooled organ (i.e., liver, kidney, spleen) and brain tissues of wild Round Gobies that were collected from the upper St. Lawrence River. Age and sex were assigned to each individual to elucidate how patterns of infection prevalence and amplification vary depending on demography within this host species.

RESULT: Viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus was detected by reverse-transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction in 49.62% of the sampled Round Gobies, with significant variation in prevalence and titers observed across demographic groups. Sex-based VHSV prevalence was 15.87% in females and 55.95% in males, and infected fish of both sexes contained similar median viral titers. Age-based prevalence increased with age, ranging from 14.29% in age-1 fish to 68.35% in age-4 fish, whereas viral titers were highest in age-2 fish and decreased with age thereafter.

CONCLUSION: Round Gobies exhibit a high prevalence (49.62%) of VHSV infections. However, the pathogen is distributed unevenly among demographics within this species. Both sex and age interact with the infection status of an individual.

articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine

articles.title: Development and Validation of a Pre-COPD Score to Predict Incident COPD.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: The ability to predict progression from a pre-disease state in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), pre-COPD, to overt COPD remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: To test the hypothesis that development of COPD can be predicted by characterizing pre-COPD and creating a simple pre-COPD score.

METHODS: We identified individuals without airflow obstruction, defined as pre-bronchodilator (BD) forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1)/forced vital capacity (FVC)≥0.70 and ≥lower limit of normal, from the Copenhagen General Population Study (CGPS)(N = 14,506), Copenhagen City Heart Study (CCHS)(N = 8673), and Genetic Epidemiology for COPD (COPDGene) Study(N = 2982). A pre-COPD score was developed in CGPS by assigning 1 point to each of smoking history≥10 pack-years, active smoking, any respiratory symptom, asthma, and pre-BD FEV1/FVC 0.70-0.75, and 4 points for pre-BD FEV1<80% predicted, indicating presence of Preserved Ratio Impaired Spirometry (PRISm), with external validation in CCHS and COPDGene. Participants were followed for 5-10 years for incident COPD, defined as pre-BD FEV1/FVC<0.70 and FEV1<80% predicted.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: During follow-up, COPD developed in 669 individuals (4.6%) in CGPS, 685 (7.9%) in CCHS, and 367 (12%) in COPDGene. In CGPS, 10-year incidence was 1.5% in the low-risk, 9.3% in the intermediate-risk, 24% in the high-risk, and 42% in the very high-risk category. Corresponding 5-year incidences were 3.7%, 7.3%, 12%, and 25% in CCHS, and 4.1%, 5.3%, 13%, and 31% in COPDGene, respectively. The pre-COPD score demonstrated good discrimination with areas under curve of 0.88 in CGPS, 0.76 in CCHS, and 0.81 in COPDGene. The pre-COPD score was also associated with exacerbations.

CONCLUSIONS: The pre-COPD score is useful in predicting the onset of COPD with clinically relevant discrimination in three cohorts with different risk profiles.

articles.title: High-Risk Vasospastic Angina With Recurrent Ischemic and Arrhythmic Events: A Case Report.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Vasospastic angina can cause myocardial infarction and malignant ventricular arrhythmias, but a persistent coronary occlusion in a patient with established vasospasm creates an acute diagnostic and procedural dilemma. A man with recurrent troponin-positive presentations and prior non-obstructive coronary angiography developed 99% mid-left anterior descending artery narrowing in 2024 that markedly regressed after intracoronary nitrate; ergonovine provocation was subsequently positive. In April 2026, at age 42, he presented with anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction after irregular use of vasodilator therapy. Angiography showed total occlusion of the left anterior descending artery at the previously nitrate-responsive segment. Intracoronary nitrate did not restore flow, and ventricular fibrillation occurred during the procedure. Bailout drug-eluting stent implantation restored flow. A proximal right coronary artery occlusion was also identified during the same procedure and treated with stenting. In June 2026, angiographically confirmed stent thrombosis required repeat percutaneous coronary intervention; an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was subsequently implanted after multidisciplinary review. This case highlights the need to consider superimposed thrombotic or structural mechanisms when coronary occlusion in a patient with established vasospastic angina does not resolve after intracoronary nitrate. Bailout revascularization may be necessary when flow cannot be restored in a hemodynamically unstable patient, but it does not eliminate the underlying vasomotor disorder.

articles.title: Sequential Coronary Obstruction After Native TAVI: Immediate Acute Occlusion and Very Late Stent Compression by Aortic Wall Hematoma.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Coronary obstruction is a rare but catastrophic complication of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) associated with high mortality. While acute and delayed presentations have distinct pathophysiological mechanisms, their occurrence in the same patient is exceedingly rare. We present a unique case of a 91-year-old female who developed acute left main coronary artery (LMCA) obstruction immediately following native TAVI using a balloon-expandable valve, which was successfully treated with bail-out percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Three months later (> 60 days, classified as "Very Late" coronary obstruction), she presented with severe angina and heart failure. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) revealed extrinsic compression of the previously implanted coronary stent caused by a localized aortic wall hematoma. A repeat PCI with a stent-in-stent technique restored coronary flow, leading to complete clinical recovery. This case expands the known mechanical spectrum of very late coronary obstruction according to recent classification frameworks and highlights the vital role of intravascular imaging and multimodality assessment in diagnosis and management.

articles.title: Randomized Evaluation of an Autoimmune Disease Prediction Model - AURA (AUtoimmune Risk Assessment).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: No evidence-based guidance exists for triaging individuals with positive antinuclear antibody (ANA) tests for rheumatology referral. We developed and deployed an interpretable clinical prediction model to predict which individuals with incident positive ANA tests will develop systemic autoimmune disease and evaluated its effect on time to autoimmune disease diagnosis in a 2-year randomized pragmatic study.

METHODS: The model was integrated into the electronic health record (EHR) at a single academic health system. All ANA-positive individuals were randomly assigned 1:1 independently of risk scores. In the intervention group, individuals with high-risk scores were invited for expedited rheumatology evaluation. In the control group, risk scores were calculated but not acted on. All participants received standard of care and could be referred to rheumatology. Chart reviews every 6 months assessed whether patients had undergone rheumatology evaluation and received a diagnosis of autoimmune disease. The primary outcome, time from positive ANA test to diagnosis, was analyzed using a Cox proportional-hazards model. Among individuals evaluated by rheumatology within 6 months of the positive ANA, the proportion diagnosed with an autoimmune disease was compared between study groups.

RESULTS: Of 2385 randomly assigned individuals, 954 were analyzed in the intervention group and 1006 in the control group after postrandomization exclusions. Individuals in the intervention group had a significantly shorter time to autoimmune disease diagnosis from the date of positive ANA (hazard ratio, 1.9; 95% confidence interval, 1.3 to 2.7; P<0.001). Among individuals diagnosed with an autoimmune disease, the median time to diagnosis was 43 days in the intervention group and 138 days in the control group. Among those evaluated by rheumatology within 6 months of a positive ANA test, 23% in the intervention group and 16% in the control group were diagnosed with an autoimmune disease (P=0.07).

CONCLUSIONS: In this randomized pragmatic study, the intervention incorporating the clinical prediction model was associated with a significantly shorter time to autoimmune disease diagnosis. (Funded by the National Institutes of Health and others.).

articles.title: Design is Everything.
articles.abstract: AbstractThe use of risk prediction models to guide clinical decision-making is becoming more common in practice. Evaluating their effectiveness is often done after implementation and without the benefit of an experimental design. Although evaluations based on observational data can yield useful information, they are prone to multiple sources of potential bias. Randomized trials, such as the one conducted by Barnado and colleagues and published in this issue, represent the highest standard of evidence for establishing causal effects of interventions. Their study provides evidence that model-guided referral to early rheumatology evaluation can expedite the diagnosis of autoimmune disease. The study also demonstrates the feasibility of implementing trials in care settings to generate rigorous, real-world assessments of model- and AI-guided clinical workflows on patient-level end points. Using predictive models impacts patient outcomes by prompting a sequence of decisions or interventions. In the AUtoimmune Risk Assessment (AURA) study, for example, risk classification is the first step; the second step is selective referral for expedited rheumatology evaluation. Generating an earlier diagnosis depends on whether the model is flagging the right patients for early referral, and whether early referral itself yields more diagnoses. Building on the contribution of Barnado and colleagues, this Editorial describes a design that can isolate the separate effects of each sequential step of the overall intervention. More generally, it highlights the fundamental importance of trial design for understanding not just whether a model-guided intervention works, but also how.

articles.title: Single-Nucleus Transcriptomics Reveals Cell Type Specific Defence Responses and Identifies AhWRKY40 as a Key Regulator of Peanut Resistance to Sclerotium rolfsii.
articles.abstract: Peanut stem rot caused by Sclerotium rolfsii is a devastating soil borne disease that severely constrains peanut production worldwide. Despite its economic importance, highly resistant peanut cultivars are still largely unavailable, and the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying peanut resistance remain poorly understood. We obtained a total of 29,308 high-quality nuclei, annotated five major cell types, and detected 52,819 expressed genes. Comparative analysis revealed widespread transcriptional reprogramming and a predominance of downregulated genes in response to pathogen infection, accompanied by a substantial reduction in cell abundance across all cell populations. Notably, epidermal cells harboured the highest proportion of disease resistance genes. Pseudotime trajectory analysis further demonstrated that S. rolfsii infection altered cellular transcriptional states and induced cell type specific immune reprogramming. Integrative analyses combining gene coexpression, pseudotime dynamics, virtual knockout, and transgenic validation consistently identified AhWRKY40 as a key regulatory factor associated with disease resistance. Overexpression of AhWRKY40 enhanced resistance to S. rolfsii and was accompanied by increased accumulation of jasmonic acid (JA) and salicylic acid (SA), suggesting its involvement in hormone-mediated defence responses. Collectively, our study provides new insights into the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying peanut resistance to stem rot, identifies AhWRKY40 as a promising candidate gene for disease resistance, and establishes a valuable resource for functional genomics and molecular breeding to improve southern blight resistance in peanut.

articles.title: Successful Management of Infective Native Infrarenal Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Associated With Micrococcus luteus and Streptococcus mitis in a 77-year-Old Man.
articles.abstract: BackgroundInfected native abdominal aortic aneurysm (INAAA) is a rare but life-threatening condition characterized by rapid progression and high mortality.Case SummaryWe report a 77-year-old male with a history of arterial hypertension, ischemic heart disease, and stage IVB hormone-sensitive prostate adenocarcinoma, presenting with lumbar pain and mild inflammatory activation, including leukocytes 8.8 ×10³/µL and C-reactive protein 3.6 mg/dL (normal <0.50 mg/dL). Computed tomography angiography (CTA) demonstrated a 50-mm infrarenal aneurysm, with periaortic inflammatory changes and a periaortic hematoma. A multidisciplinary decision, made 3 hours after admission, favored urgent open surgical repair with resection and in situ reconstruction. Midline laparotomy with debridement and resection of the affected aorta was performed; in situ reconstruction was carried out using a rifampicin soaked bifurcated Dacron graft covered with bovine pericardium with anastomoses to healthy aortic and iliac segments. Intraoperative cultures identified Micrococcus luteus and Streptococcus mitis, rare pathogens in this context. Targeted therapy included intravenous ceftriaxone during hospitalization, followed by oral amoxicillin-clavulanate and doxycycline for seven weeks. Histopathology confirmed chronic granulomatous abscessed inflammation. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient was discharged home on postoperative day 17. At six months, follow-up imaging demonstrated a patent reconstruction without signs of persistent infection.ConclusionThese findings highlight the importance of early recognition, aggressive debridement, and coordinated multidisciplinary management in achieving optimal outcomes in INAAA, particularly when atypical microorganisms complicate diagnosis and therapeutic decision-making.

articles.title: Percutaneous Rescue of Acute Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction After Mitral Valve-In-Valve Replacement.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO) is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR). Mitral valve-in-valve procedures are generally associated with a lower risk of LVOTO because of the predictable geometry provided by the surgical bioprosthesis, yet severe obstruction may still occur and precipitate abrupt hemodynamic collapse.

CASE: A 79-year-old woman with a degenerated 27-mm Carpentier-Edwards Perimount mitral bioprosthesis presented with acute decompensated heart failure due to severe bioprosthetic mitral stenosis. Following multidisciplinary Heart Team evaluation, she was considered not a candidate for redo mitral valve surgery and underwent urgent transseptal valve-in-valve TMVR with a 26-mm balloon-expandable SAPIEN valve.

INTERVENTION: Immediately after valve deployment, severe LVOTO developed, with an invasive peak-to-peak LV-aortic gradient of 120 mmHg. A mechanism-guided percutaneous rescue strategy was undertaken. Correction of the structural component of obstruction reduced the gradient to 60 mmHg. Persistent obstruction suggested a significant dynamic contribution, prompting selective septal branch coil embolization, which further reduced the gradient to 20 mmHg and resulted in immediate hemodynamic stabilization.

CONCLUSION: Severe LVOTO after valve-in-valve TMVR may reflect both structural and dynamic mechanisms. Persistence of significant obstruction after structural correction should prompt consideration of a dynamic component and may guide effective rescue therapy.

articles.title: B-cell activation markers and cancer risk in people with HIV: An integrative case-control and Mendelian randomization analysis.
articles.abstract: Early and continuous antiretroviral therapy (ART) reduces cancer risk in people with HIV (PWH), yet residual risk potentially driven by persistent B-cell activation remains. We used observational and genetic triangulation to evaluate whether baseline B-cell biomarkers are associated with subsequent cancer risk. We conducted: (i) a nested case-control study within the INSIGHT trials (158 cases and 313 matched controls) assessing B-cell biomarkers (sCD23, sCD27, sCD30, CXCL13) in PWH; and (ii) two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) to evaluate likely causal relationships between these proteins and 23 cancer types using general-population genome-wide association studies. Median time from study entry to cancer diagnosis was 2.9 years. In PWH, CXCL13 was associated with overall cancer risk (highest tertile vs. lowest tertile OR 2.36, 95% CI 1.24-4.5), driven by infection-related cancers (N = 82; OR 4.81, 1.76-13.1) and lymphoma (N = 36; OR 9.92, 1.58-62.2). The CXCL13 association remained robust among virally suppressed participants (P = 0.018). sCD30 was also associated with infection-related cancers (OR 2.77, 1.09-7.03). sCD23 showed a linear association with infection-related cancer (OR per SD 1.42, 1.01-2.00), though tertile-based analyses were non-significant. In the general population, MR meta-analyses showed null associations for these biomarkers across 23 cancer types (P > 0.05). Our study links B-cell markers with cancer risk in PWH, identifying CXCL13 as a marker of infection-related cancer risk despite effective ART, highlighting a "residual inflammatory gap" for modern risk stratification. The lack of causal MR signals suggests these proteins are markers of HIV-associated immune activation rather than universal etiological factors for cancer.

articles.title: Cardiometabolic Outcomes in Dahl Salt-Sensitive Rat Pregnancies: Impact of a Maternal Hypertensive High-Fat Diet.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract: Excessive adiposity and chronic hypertension are major risk factors of preeclampsia, a leading hypertensive disorder of pregnancy. Yet, mechanisms underlying the complex interplay between adiposity, chronic hypertension, and preeclampsia remain incompletely understood, partly due to the limited availability of experimental models that capture these interactions. Herein, we explored maternal cardiometabolic adaptations in high-fat diet (HFD)-fed Dahl Salt-Sensitive rats, an established model of HFD-associated chronic hypertension. We hypothesized that HFD-fed dams would display a superimposed preeclampsia-like phenotype compared to control diet (CD)-fed Dahl Salt-Sensitive females. HFD-fed dams exhibited attenuated gestational weight gain, increased ketogenesis, cardiovascular dysfunction and blunted uteroplacental vascular adaptation to pregnancy. HFD feeding was associated with high blood pressure pre-pregnancy and during most of gestation and lactation. Interestingly, however, both groups displayed a drop in blood pressure during late gestation, with lower blood pressure nadir and lower urine protein excretion in HFD-fed dams. Short-term pregnancy outcomes were largely preserved in HFD-fed dams, including litter size, pup viability, and placental efficiency. Long-term, dietary normalization failed to reverse the hypertensive phenotype of HFD-exposed dams, with blood pressure remaining 10-15 mmHg higher than controls for at least 14 weeks post-weaning. In conclusion, HFD-fed Dahl salt-sensitive females developed chronic hypertension and impaired metabolic and cardiovascular adaptations to pregnancy. Yet, neither CD- nor HFD-fed dams exhibited hallmark preeclampsia features, including late-gestation blood pressure rise, proteinuria, and fetal growth restriction. This model therefore provides a valuable platform to investigate adaptive cardiometabolic mechanisms that may attenuate preeclampsia risk in obese and chronic hypertensive patients.

articles.title: Longitudinal trends in vaccination uptake and respiratory infection burden in systemic lupus erythematosus: a population-based cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate longitudinal patterns of vaccination uptake and respiratory infection outcomes among patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) compared with controls and identify factors associated with vaccination uptake.

METHODS: Population-based cohort study using a healthcare organization database. Adult patients with SLE (diagnosed 2010-2023) were identified through a validated registry and matched 1:100 to controls by birth year, sex, and socioeconomic status. Vaccination uptake for influenza, pneumococcal, and COVID-19 vaccines, respiratory infections, hospitalizations, intensive care unit (ICU) admissions, and mortality were evaluated. Temporal trends and factors associated with vaccination uptake were assessed using multivariable models.

RESULTS: The study included 3,692 patients with SLE and 382,753 matched controls (median follow-ups 12.8 and 13.4 years, respectively). Vaccination uptake was higher among patients with SLE than controls (influenza: 77.6% vs. 56.4%; pneumococcal: 55.6% vs. 32.1%; COVID-19: 74.2% vs. 72.0%; all p < 0.01). Patients with SLE experienced higher rates of respiratory hospitalization (34.8% vs. 11.5%), pneumonia hospitalization (23.9% vs. 5.9%), ICU admission (12.8% vs. 2.7%), and all-cause mortality (21.0% vs. 8.5%) (all p < 0.001). Longitudinally, vaccination uptake and respiratory hospitalizations remained consistently higher among patients with SLE. Pneumonia hospitalization rates increased over time in controls but remained stable in SLE (interaction p = 0.020). Older age, more comorbidities, higher socioeconomic status, and exposure to glucocorticoids were independently associated with influenza and pneumococcal vaccination uptake rates in SLE.

CONCLUSION: Patients with SLE demonstrated substantially higher vaccine exposure than controls but experienced elevated respiratory infection rates and severe outcomes. These findings support efforts to optimize infection prevention strategies in SLE.

articles.title: Optimized Hemoglobin Depletion Improves Clinical Proteomics from Dried Blood Spots.
articles.abstract: Equitable access to large sample cohorts for robust, high-throughput proteomics for biomarker discovery is a major barrier to widescale clinical implementation. Dried blood spots (DBS) offer a minimally invasive alternative to venous blood draws, enabling at-home microsampling (<50 μL) for centralized analysis, thus enhancing research participation. This approach is particularly relevant for under-represented groups, including children, the elderly, minority backgrounds and those with long-term health conditions such as chronic kidney disease (CKD), where disease fluctuations may occur outside the clinic, and vein preservation is critical. Proteomic analysis has demonstrated great utility in monitoring disease progression, and for biomarker/therapeutic target discovery. However, liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) of whole blood is hindered by the wide dynamic range and the relatively high-abundance of proteins such as hemoglobin, compromising biomarker discovery. Here, we establish an optimized workflow for protein extraction and hemoglobin depletion from microsamples obtained using DBS, enabling sensitive and high-throughput proteomic analysis. We demonstrate that hemoglobin depletion increases protein identifications by ∼50%, mitigating ion suppression and dynamic range effects, enabling the identification of putative biomarkers from patients with stage 5 CKD on dialysis. We also evaluated a commercial cell-free DBS device which yielded a sample more representative of plasma compared to traditional DBS and enabled greater depletion of hemoglobin compared to traditional DBS with hemoglobin depletion methods. Our findings offer a scalable approach for biomarker discovery, facilitating remote, longitudinal clinical studies.

articles.title: Integrated Lipidomic and Energy Metabolomic Analyses Reveal the Cardioprotective Mechanisms of Meconopsis horridula Alkaloids in Heart Failure.
articles.abstract: Meconopsis horridula Hook. f. & Thomson (MH) is a traditional Tibetan medicinal herb used to promote blood circulation and treat cardiovascular disorders; however, its active constituents and cardioprotective mechanisms in heart failure (HF) remain poorly understood. In this study, liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry was used to characterize the alkaloid profile of MH, and the cardioprotective effects of its alkaloid fraction were evaluated in a doxorubicin-induced rat model of HF. A total of 26 alkaloids were identified. Treatment with MH alkaloids significantly improved cardiac function and attenuated myocardial injury in HF rats. To elucidate the underlying mechanisms, quantitative lipidomics and targeted energy metabolomics analyses were performed. Compared with the model group, MH treatment altered multiple lipid and energy metabolites associated with ether lipid metabolism, glycerophospholipid metabolism, lipid and atherosclerosis, glyoxylate and dicarboxylate metabolism, and the citrate cycle. Integrated pathway analysis identified NADH/ubiquinone oxidoreductase complex assembly factor 6 (NDUFAF6), AMPK, ACC, GLUT4, ACOT1, and ATP2A as key regulatory nodes. Western blot analysis further supported the involvement of these proteins in MH-mediated metabolic remodeling. Collectively, these findings suggest that MH alkaloids alleviate HF by partially restoring dysregulated glucose and lipid metabolism and provide mechanistic insights into their cardioprotective effects.

articles.title: Serum Metabolic Differences Across Glucose Metabolic States Using Untargeted UPLC-HRMS Metabolomics.
articles.abstract: Insulin resistance (IR) and impaired glucose regulation (IGR) involve metabolic disturbances beyond changes in blood glucose. This cross-sectional study applied untargeted UPLC-HRMS metabolomics to serum from 109 participants across normal glucose tolerance (NGT), IR, IGR, and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). An integrated analysis of 457 putatively annotated metabolites combined multivariate statistics, clustering, and machine learning to characterize differences among glycometabolic groups and assess the discriminatory information. Pairwise comparisons respectively identified 60, 42, and 59 differential metabolites for NGT vs IR, IR vs IGR, and IGR vs T2DM, including five shared across all comparisons. LASSO and random forest evaluated fixed differential-metabolite panels through stratified 5-fold cross-validation repeated ten times and 1,000 label permutations. The corresponding pooled AUC ranges were 0.918-0.923, 0.995-0.996, and 0.828-0.950. Because panel selection preceded cross-validation, these estimates describe within-cohort discrimination rather than generalizable predictive performance. Pathway analysis of the union of differential metabolites indicated nominal enrichment of lysine degradation and nicotinate and nicotinamide metabolism. Shared metabolites also showed associations with clinical measures of glucose homeostasis and insulin response. These findings characterize distinct yet partly shared metabolic features across glycometabolic states and provide candidates for targeted confirmation and independent longitudinal validation.

articles.title: Leveraging Urinary Proteomics to Advance Pathophysiologic and Biomarker Perspectives of Chronic Kidney Disease in Cats.
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is one of the most prevalent diseases in feline medicine. Mass spectrometry-based urinary proteomics offers powerful insight into biomarker candidates and disease subtyping in CKD by measuring protein profiles rather than individual proteins. This study aims to measure the urinary proteome to identify protein profiles in cats with and without CKD to gain pathophysiological insights into the disease and more precisely diagnose CKD. Here, we identify 2,219 urinary proteins in the feline urinary proteome. Using univariate biomarker analysis, we show that MMP-7 may be a promising biomarker of CKD in cats. We then demonstrate the power of using protein profiles rather than individual proteins by grouping proteins based on how they trend across disease states. The changes to the global urinary proteomes of individual cats showed three distinct groups of CKD cats with unique protein profiles, suggesting that different pathophysiological mechanisms mediate disease subtypes. We demonstrate that large-scale urinary proteomics may provide a powerful framework for discovering candidate biomarkers that advance the subtyping and mechanistic understanding of feline CKD.

articles.title: Sex-Specific Plasma Proteomic Alterations Underpin Distinct COVID-19 Progression and Post-COVID-19 Condition.
articles.abstract: Sex differences in COVID-19 and its sequelae remain poorly understood, which hinders targeted therapies. We performed plasma proteomic analyses of 69 hospitalized patients with COVID-19 and 30 healthy controls from a prospective Chinese cohort. The UK Biobank and Mount Sinai Biobank were employed for validation and provided insights into the progression mechanisms. Biological and tissue enrichment analyses characterized sex-specific pathways and tissue-enriched proteins. We identified ANXA11, a molecular tether that physically links RNA granules to lysosomal membranes to enable their long-distance transport and local translation, as a protein associated with male-specific susceptibility to SARS-CoV-2 infection. Decreased ANXA11 protein levels were linked to higher risk of infection in males, replicated in the UK Biobank. Sex-specific proteomic alterations revealed distinct biological responses, including glycosylation-related pathways in females and cell adhesion, platelet-leukocyte interactions, and inflammatory responses in males. Sex-specific protein changes were also associated with distinct post-COVID-19 symptom profiles. ANXA11 was identified as a novel protein associated with the male-specific susceptibility to SARS-CoV-2 infection. Sex-specific protein changes revealed distinct mechanistic differences between male and female patients in COVID-19 progression and may explain sex differences in post-COVID-19 conditions.

articles.title: Ubi-SCAPE Enables Deep Exploration of the Poly-Ubiquitylome.
articles.abstract: Post-translational modification with chains of the 76-amino acid protein ubiquitin ("poly-ubiquitylation") confers diverse fates to the targeted protein and non-protein substrates, including degradation, intracellular trafficking, and signal transduction. Despite being one of the most frequent modifications, the complexity of poly-ubiquitin chains adds methodological challenges to their characterization. Trypsin-resistant tandem ubiquitin-binding entities (trTUBEs), engineered from natural ubiquitin-binding domains, can capture intact poly-ubiquitylated material with high cumulative avidity. However, such approaches have suffered from considerable co-eluting contaminants in proteomics applications. Here, we introduce an optimized trTUBE-based method for poly-ubiquitylated proteome purification, drastically depleting non-ubiquitylated protein contaminants and mono-ubiquitylated proteins. The method, termed ubiquitylomics by stringent, cleavable, affinity-based proteome extraction (Ubi-SCAPE), offers a streamlined and reproducible (median R2 > 0.98; CV < 8%) means of characterizing the poly-ubiquitylome. Over 7800 poly-ubiquitylated proteins and 8500 ubiquitin-modified peptides (diGly) were quantified with Ubi-SCAPE at a throughput of 40 samples per day, as well as over 6000 proteins from 100 μg of unstressed cell lysate. Upon acute stress by heat-shock, we identified 2700 proteins and 8000 diGly peptides with increased poly-ubiquitylation, offering similar biological insights as far more material-, labor-, and cost-intensive peptide-based ubiquitin enrichment methods would provide. Ubi-SCAPE therefore provides a simple and effective means of comprehensively quantifying a selectively enriched poly-ubiquitylome.

articles.title: Targeted Analysis of >1500 Plasma Proteoforms via Individual Ion Mass Spectrometry.
articles.abstract: Plasma proteomics has emerged as a powerful approach for interrogating human biology, identifying disease-associated proteomic changes, and advancing precision diagnostics. In recent years, affinity-based plasma proteomics platforms with predefined protein panels, such as Olink and SomaScan, have emerged to complement bottom-up mass spectrometry (BUP). This study leverages a novel mass spectrometry platform to capture targeted proteoform information lost by mainline antibody-, aptamer-, and BUP-driven workflows. The Plasma Proteoform Assay (PPA) uses Individual Ion Mass Spectrometry (I2MS) to resolve mixtures of intact proteins presented by direct injection. Two proteoform panels, PPA 526 and PPA 1514, were defined from human plasma samples obtained from 81 individuals. The panels quantify 526 proteoforms derived from 59 genes and 1,514 proteoforms from 155 genes, respectively. Across both panels, the proportion of targeted proteoforms with CVs below 20% ranged from 59% to 80%. PPA was benchmarked in studies including 9 pooled plasma samples derived from subjects with hepatic cirrhosis (N = 30 individuals) and a cohort of resilient agers carrying a SERPINE1 (PAI-1) mutation (N = 27 individuals). PPA signatures distinguished SERPINE1 mutation carriers from affected individuals and provided sufficient resolution to discriminate among cirrhosis disease stages. In summary, we present PPA 526 and PPA 1514, the first scalable plasma proteoform panels capable of tracking hundreds to thousands of targets in a few minutes per sample.

articles.title: Proximity Labeling: An Empowering Tool for Deciphering Molecular Mechanisms.
articles.abstract: Proximity labeling (PL) has become a widely used approach for studying protein-protein interactions (PPIs) and addressing limitations of conventional techniques in capturing transient, weak interactions, and physiological protein networks within living systems. Over the past decade, core PL enzymes, notably APEX2, BirA* (BioID), and TurboID, have been iteratively engineered, with reported improvements in temporal resolution, targeting specificity, and biocompatibility. This review summarizes how PL technologies have developed and describes the enzymatic properties, catalytic mechanisms, and reported performance trade-offs of the commonly used tools. We then survey applications of PL in neuroscience, cardiology, oncology, and infectious disease, where it has been used to map compartment-specific proteomes and spatiotemporally regulated networks, including neural activity-driven PPIs, tumor microenvironment cross-talk, and host-pathogen interfaces. Many of the resulting candidates await orthogonal validation. We also describe recently reported conditional PL systems with optical, calcium- or oxygen-dependent control. Finally, we discuss open questions and possible directions for PL development, including enzyme-directed evolution, multisignal responsive regulation, cross-omics integration, and translational applications. This review is intended as a practical reference for researchers to support the selection and application of PL platforms in specific experimental contexts from mechanistic studies to the identification of candidate therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Proteomic Signatures of Intracellular Bordetella pertussis in Respiratory Epithelial Cells.
articles.abstract: Bordetella pertussis is a strictly human-adapted pathogen and the etiologic agent of whooping cough, a reemerging respiratory disease. Current vaccines fail to prevent colonization, and emerging evidence indicates that B. pertussis can establish intracellular infections that may contribute to its persistence. Previous studies showed that this pathogen adapts its phenotype and survives within human macrophages by modulating bactericidal responses through pertussis toxin (PT) and adenylate cyclase toxin (CyaA). Here, we analyzed the proteome of B. pertussis after internalization into epithelial cells, another possible host niche. Proteomic adaptations were mainly associated with metabolic adjustments indicative of a decelerated intracellular metabolism. Using mutant strains, we found that neither PT nor CyaA is required for B. pertussis for survival in epithelial cells, which is consistent with the absence of a detectable stress response in intracellular bacteria. Proteins previously identified as required for B. pertussis intracellular survival within macrophages, such as factors involved in the bacterial adaptation to acidic compartments, proved neither induced by the intracellular environment nor required for intracellular survival within epithelial cells. Collectively, the findings suggest that these epithelial cells may represent a more favorable niche than macrophages for bacterial persistence.

articles.title: Metabolomic Changes in Biofilm of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Under Early-Stage Tobramycin Treatment Identified by 2D NMR-Based COLMARq.
articles.abstract: Biofilms are estimated to account for a large proportion of persistent microbial infections and are associated with substantial mortality in hospitals. Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms exhibit higher resistance to antibiotics compared to their planktonic growth form, making them difficult to eradicate and contributing to the mounting global challenge posed by infectious diseases. To gain deeper insights into the metabolic response of biofilms to antibiotic pressure, we conducted a quantitative, untargeted metabolomics analysis using heteronuclear 2D NMR spectroscopy. Biofilms were grown in the presence of sub-inhibitory concentrations of tobramycin, and metabolic alterations were identified and quantified using the COLMARq analysis platform. Our analysis revealed significant metabolic shifts even at low doses of tobramycin with key metabolites such as UDP-glucose increasing and putrescine decreasing. Pathway enrichment analysis highlighted alterations in amino acid biosynthesis, energy metabolism, and stress response pathways. Notably, the accumulation of glutathione disulfide indicates enhanced oxidative stress, while the depletion of β-alanine, succinate, and GABA suggested metabolic shifts linked to biofilm adaptation. These findings provide new insights into the metabolic reprogramming of biofilms under antibiotic treatment and offer perspectives into biofilm behavior in the case of Pseudomonas aeruginosa when exposed to antibiotics from an early stage of infection.

articles.title: Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers in the Blood for Sepsis Diagnosis.
articles.abstract: Early sepsis diagnosis in critically ill patients remains a major unmet need. We employed a multiphase proteomic strategy integrating discovery by data-independent acquisition, targeted verification by parallel reaction monitoring, clinical confirmation with ELISA, and machine learning to identify robust blood biomarkers. In discovery and verification cohorts, three consistently downregulated proteins, α-2-HS-glycoprotein (AHSG), clusterin (CLU), and kallistatin (SERPINA4), were prioritized. A random forest model combining these markers yielded an apparent area under the curve (AUC) of 0.94 in the training cohort. Crucially, in a prospective evaluation of 143 patients with suspected sepsis, representing the true test of generalizability, the model achieved an AUC of 0.87, significantly outperforming PCT and CRP, and correctly classified 73.0% of confirmed sepsis cases as high-risk. This triple-biomarker panel enables rapid, accurate early detection of sepsis and offers a readily translatable diagnostic tool for clinical practice.

articles.title: Association of decreased serum Netrin-1 with inflammatory markers, neurological severity, and 3-month outcome in hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare serum Netrin-1 levels among hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage (HICH) patients, hypertensive patients without cerebrovascular lesions and healthy controls, and analyze its correlations with inflammatory markers, neurological deficit severity and 3-month functional prognosis.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort enrolled 294 participants from September 2021 to September 2022, including 98 HICH patients, 92 uncomplicated primary hypertension patients and 104 healthy subjects. Serum samples were collected within routine clinical time windows, yet the intervals from hemorrhage onset and acute treatments to blood collection were inconsistent. Multiple subgroup, correlation and prognostic analyses were conducted with exact p-values presented; p < 0.01 was set as a strict threshold for primary interpretations.

RESULTS: HICH patients had markedly lower serum Netrin-1 than healthy controls (p < 0.001), with no significant difference versus hypertensive patients (p = 0.083). Netrin-1 was negatively correlated with NIHSS, mRS, IL-6 and CRP, and positively correlated with IL-10. Its concentrations declined progressively with aggravated neurological impairment. Multivariate regression identified low Netrin-1, high NIHSS and brainstem hemorrhage as independent predictors of poor 3-month outcome (GOS 1-3). The internal ROC analysis showed an AUC of 0.896 (95%CI 0.817-0.923).

CONCLUSION: Reduced serum Netrin-1 correlates with severe neurological damage and unfavorable 3-month prognosis in HICH, serving as an independent prognostic indicator after covariate adjustment. Restricted by retrospective single-center design, inconsistent sampling timing, insufficient outcome events and lack of external validation, Netrin-1 is merely an investigational biomarker rather than a validated clinical prognostic assay.

articles.title: Mitochondrial Oxysterol Signaling in Epigenetic Regulation and Therapeutic Development.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract: Oxysterols are oxygenated cholesterol derivatives with receptor-dependent and epigenetic activities. This review examines how mitochondrial cholesterol metabolism and oxysterol sulfation may connect lipid metabolism to DNA methylation and communication between hepatocytes and macrophages. Biochemical studies show that 25-hydroxycholesterol (25HC) and 27-hydroxycholesterol (27HC) activate DNA methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1), whereas their 3-sulfated derivatives inhibit the activities of DNMT1, DNMT3A, and DNMT3B. Cholestenoic acid (CA) has a concentration-dependent effect, activating DNMT1 at lower concentrations and inhibiting it at higher concentrations. In hepatocyte models, these activities are associated with altered promoter CpG methylation and expression of genes involved in lipid metabolism, inflammatory responses, and cell survival. The sulfated CA metabolite, 3β-sulfate-5-cholestenoic acid (3SCA), is secreted by hepatocytes and modifies inflammatory gene expression in macrophages. We propose an oxysterol epigenetic rheostat in which metabolite concentrations and sulfation influence DNMT activities. Published animal studies support protective effects of 25-hydroxycholesterol 3-sulfate in fatty liver disease, endotoxemia, and acetaminophen-induced liver injury. Its clinical formulation, larsucosterol, has shown favorable hepatic and metabolic signals in Phase 1b fatty liver studies and nominally significant mortality reductions in prespecified US Phase 2b alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) analyses. These encouraging findings require confirmation because the overall Phase 2b primary endpoint was not met. Larsucosterol has received Fast Track and Breakthrough Therapy designations from the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for AH and is currently being evaluated in a registrational Phase 3 trial.

articles.title: Sex influences the mosquito virome in a host-specific way.
articles.abstract: Mosquitoes harbor diverse eukaryotic viruses. These viral communities, or viromes, probably influence mosquito physiology, including pathogen transmission. However, the factors shaping the virome remain largely unstudied, limiting our understanding of its role in mosquito biology. Here, we assess the influence of sex on the eukaryotic virome of mosquitoes. Ecological differences between males and females, such as female-specific blood feeding, may lead to differential viral exposure and virome structure. We investigated the influence of sex in sympatric populations of Culex quinquefasciatus and Aedes aegypti, two major human pathogen vectors. A total of 5,743 mosquitoes were collected in various habitats in Burkina Faso (West Africa) over 2 years. Shotgun sequencing of 115 pools revealed 47 viral taxonomic units (VTUs) from 28 viral families. Viromes differed between the two mosquito species, enabling within-species analysis of sex effects. Significant differences in beta diversity were observed between sexes in both species, while alpha diversity differences were significant only in C. quinquefasciatus. Additionally, five indicator viruses, taxonomically diverse and including two novel species, were identified associated with sex. Most indicator VTUs were found in both sexes but with different infection rates. Their low prevalence suggests that sex-based differences are not present in all individuals but are detectable at the population level. Our findings unveil that sex can influence the mosquito virome, and that this effect depends on mosquito species. Moreover, our results provide a first model of the virome structure as a function of sex in two mosquito species of public health significance.IMPORTANCEMosquitoes carry many viruses that do not infect humans but can influence how mosquitoes interact with pathogens that threaten human health. Yet, the factors that shape these viral communities in nature remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated whether male and female mosquitoes differ in the viruses they carry. Sex could affect the virome because males and females have distinct ecological and physiological traits, such as blood feeding in females. We examined the viromes of two major disease vectors, Aedes aegypti and Culex quinquefasciatus, collected in large numbers in Burkina Faso and screened using metagenomics. We found that males and females harbor different viral communities, and that these differences vary between species. These patterns were not driven by sex-specific viruses but by viruses that differed in prevalence between sexes. Our findings show that sex influences mosquito viromes in the field and offer new insight into mosquito-virus interactions.

articles.title: CD6 downregulation from cell surface in human herpesvirus-6A/B-infected T cells.
articles.abstract: Human herpesvirus 6A/B (HHV-6A/B) belongs to the Betaherpesvirinae subfamily and mainly replicates in activated T cells. Although HHV-6B establishes lifelong latency after primary infection and infects nearly all adult humans, its immune evasion strategies in vivo remain incompletely understood. CD6 is a key costimulatory receptor that shapes T-cell activation and communication. Here, we identify CD6 as a previously unrecognized target of HHV-6A/B. Infection triggered internalization of CD6 from the plasma membrane into the cytoplasm and led to its proteasome-dependent degradation. CD6 transcription and maturation through the secretory pathway were unaffected, indicating that downregulation occurs through post-transcriptional mechanisms involving altered endolysosomal trafficking. We further demonstrate that the virus-specific U21-U24 gene cluster is required for CD6 downregulation, as deletion of this cluster abolished CD6 degradation in both T-cell lines and primary cord blood mononuclear cells. These findings reveal a viral strategy that disrupts T-cell surface architecture and suggest a role for CD6 modulation in supporting HHV-6A/B persistence.IMPORTANCEHuman herpesvirus 6B (HHV-6B) infects nearly all individuals early in life and persists lifelong, yet the mechanisms by which it modulates host immunity remain poorly defined. CD6 is a critical costimulatory receptor that shapes T-cell activation and communication within the immune system. Here, we identify CD6 as a previously unrecognized target of HHV-6A/B and demonstrate that infection triggers its internalization and proteasome-dependent degradation. We further show that this process is driven by the virus-specific U21-U24 gene cluster, revealing a dedicated viral strategy for altering host protein trafficking. Because degradation of immune surface molecules is a common mechanism of immune evasion among persistent viruses, our findings provide new insight into how HHV-6A/B remodels T-cell function to support long-term persistence. Understanding this pathway may inform future approaches aimed at preventing or mitigating diseases associated with HHV-6 reactivation.

articles.title: Clinically relevant RSV anti-F antibodies exhibit comparable inhibition of syncytium formation despite marked differences in neutralization potency.
articles.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of lower respiratory tract infections in infants, immunocompromised individuals, and older adults. A hallmark of RSV infection is the formation of multinucleated syncytia through fusion between infected and adjacent uninfected cells. This process is mediated by the RSV fusion protein (RSV F) expressed on infected cells, which interacts with receptors on neighboring cells to drive membrane fusion. Syncytium formation may facilitate cell-to-cell spread while reducing virion exposure to extracellular neutralizing antibodies and immune cells. Clinically used monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) target RSV F and are routinely evaluated using conventional virus neutralization assays. However, their ability to inhibit syncytium formation remains poorly characterized because these assays primarily measure virus-to-cell entry rather than cell-to-cell fusion. Here, we present a quantitative flow cytometry-based assay to measure RSV-induced syncytium formation during infection. Using this assay, we evaluated clinically relevant anti-F mAbs and compared their potency in syncytium inhibition and conventional virus neutralization assays in HEp-2 and A549 cells. Palivizumab, nirsevimab, and clesrovimab inhibited syncytium formation in a dose-dependent manner, with only modest differences in potency. In contrast, nirsevimab and clesrovimab exhibited substantially greater virus neutralization potency than palivizumab. These findings indicate that inhibition of RSV-induced cell-to-cell fusion represents a distinct functional property of anti-F antibodies that is not fully captured by conventional neutralization assays. Our assay provides a quantitative approach to assess syncytium inhibition and highlights the value of complementary functional readouts for evaluating antibodies targeting RSV and other syncytium-forming viruses.IMPORTANCERespiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of respiratory disease in infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. A hallmark of RSV infection is syncytium formation, although its contribution to viral spread and disease pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Increased fusogenicity has been associated with disease severity, and syncytium formation may promote cell-to-cell spread while limiting virion exposure to extracellular neutralizing antibodies. Although RSV fusion (F)-specific monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) are increasingly used for disease prevention, their ability to inhibit syncytium formation remains unexplored, as conventional neutralization assays primarily measure virus-to-cell entry. Here, we describe a quantitative flow cytometry-based assay to measure RSV-induced syncytium formation and evaluate inhibition by clinically relevant anti-F mAbs. Our results indicate that syncytium inhibition represents a distinct functional property of anti-F antibodies that is not fully captured by conventional neutralization assays, highlighting the value of complementary functional readouts for evaluating antibodies targeting RSV and other syncytium-forming viruses.

articles.title: AASLD EXPO: Diagnosis and management of hepatitis delta virus (HDV) infection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: HDV infection represents a rare co-infection or super-infection among persons with HBV infection and is associated with significant morbidity and mortality due to an increased risk of liver events such as hepatic decompensation and HCC.

METHODS: The Expert Practice Opinion (EXPO) document was developed by subject matter experts and commissioned by the AASLD Practice Guidelines Committee to provide timely guidance on the screening, diagnosis, and management of HDV infection. Writing group members performed a targeted literature review and generated EXPO statements which were agreed upon by group consensus.

RESULTS: All individuals who are HBsAg positive should be tested at least once for HDV infection with HDV antibody. HDV antibody positive individuals should undergo HDV RNA testing to confirm active infection. All individuals with chronic HDV should undergo further evaluation including non-invasive fibrosis testing, preferably with elastography. Lab monitoring and HCC surveillance imaging is suggested every 6 months. All adults with chronic HDV viremia and compensated liver disease should be considered candidates for HDV therapy with bulevirtide for chronic virologic suppression, or alternatively bulevirtide plus peg-IFN alfa-2a for individuals without contraindications to peg-IFN and who desire a finite duration regimen. Considerations for patient selection, treatment regimen, monitoring, assessment of response, and care of patients in special populations are summarized in the document.
