articles.title: Bacterial community response to postmortem changes predicts the causes of death and postmortem interval.
articles.abstract: Determining the postmortem interval (PMI) and cause of death (COD) in decomposed remains a major challenge in forensic pathology because morphological and biochemical indicators progressively deteriorate during decomposition. Microbial communities are highly responsive to environmental and physiological changes and may therefore provide complementary forensic information. In this study, we used a murine model to investigate postmortem microbial succession associated with three death-related conditions-ligature strangulation (LS), hemorrhagic shock (HS), and organophosphate poisoning (OP)-across postmortem time points from 2 to 20 days. Swab samples from three skin sites (face, chest, and abdomen) were collected and subjected to 16S rDNA sequencing, and microbial community dynamics were evaluated using bioinformatics and random forest (RF) machine-learning models. Our results revealed distinct COD-associated microbial trajectories. LS carcasses exhibited accelerated morphological decomposition and earlier Proteobacteria dominance, whereas HS showed delayed decomposition-related changes. OP exhibited distinct microbial diversity and succession patterns, particularly during early PMI. Alpha- and beta-diversity analyses indicated that both COD and PMI significantly influenced microbial community structure. RF models showed strong discriminatory performance for COD classification (AUC > 0.95) and PMI classification (AUC 0.88-0.98), with distinct microbial features contributing to the two classification tasks. These findings suggest that physiological conditions associated with different causes of death may contribute to distinct postmortem microbial trajectories, while temporal microbial succession provides informative markers for categorical PMI classification. Collectively, microbiome-based approaches may serve as complementary forensic tools for simultaneous PMI classification and discrimination of death-related conditions.

articles.title: Mapping Cardiovascular Prediction Models in the General Population: Where Are We Now and Where Next?
articles.journal: European heart journal. Quality of care & clinical outcomes
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This scoping review aimed to comprehensively map the landscape of prediction models for predicting cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk in the general population over the past two decades, including model development, validation, updating, and impact assessment.

METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase databases were searched from January 2006 to November 2025 for studies that developed, validated, updated, or assessed the impact of at least one CVD risk prediction model in the general population. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data on general characteristics, justification, methodological characteristics, and reporting characteristics. Findings were summarized descriptively.

RESULTS: We included 322 studies, comprising 220 development studies (yielding 298 models), 94 independent validation or update studies, and eight studies providing nine impact assessments involving seven models. Of the 220 development studies, 90.0% cited at least one existing model; the most frequently cited justification was insufficient predictors (44.4%). Among the 298 models, 86.6% had undergone internal validation, while external validation (43.0%), updating (8.7%), and impact assessment (2.3%) remained low. Reporting completeness varied: 82.3% reported both discrimination and calibration, 49.4% provided full model specification, and 51.1% offered a practical tool. Notably, only 24.3% of models published after 2015 cited the TRIPOD guideline. Only 11.1% were reported to be recommended in clinical guidelines.

CONCLUSION: Despite a substantial increase in CVD prediction model development, critical gaps persist in external validation, reporting transparency, and clinical impact assessment. Future research should prioritize strengthening the evidence base of existing models through rigorous validation, transparent reporting, and implementation research.

articles.title: Heterogeneous treatment effect estimation with instrumental variable methods.
articles.abstract: Instrumental variable (IV) methods are widely used to address unmeasured confounding in observational studies but typically estimate the local average treatment effect (LATE) for compliers. If there exist effect modifying variables that also affect the choice of treatment, the LATE may have limited clinical relevance. To address this limitation, we propose a novel framework for estimating the conditional average treatment effect (CATE) for a categorical treatment variable in the presence of both observed confounding and effect-modifying variables in addition to valid IVs. Building on recent developments in data fusion between randomized trial and observational data, we combine IV estimators with estimators based on covariate adjustment. By making parametric assumptions about the residual unobserved confounding effect, we obtain a consistent estimator of the CATE with relatively high efficiency. In a simulation study with nonlinear effect modification and unobserved confounding, we show that our estimator outperforms competing IV and covariate-adjusted estimators in terms of mean squared error. We further illustrate the applicability of the method, utilizing it to compare tumor necrosis factor alpha inhibitors as the first line biologic treatment of rheumatoid arthritis conditional on age. The analysis illustrates how the proposed method can estimate population-relevant, clinically interpretable treatment effects and suggests smaller differences between treatments among older patients. This work provides a general framework for combining instrumental and confounding information to estimate individualized causal effects when treatment effects are heterogeneous and there are more than two treatment alternatives.

articles.title: Circadian blood pressure dipping patterns, hypertension, and cortisol metabolism across the weight spectrum.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood pressure (BP) exhibits a circadian rhythm with a nocturnal decline, dipping. Alterations in cortisol metabolism have been linked to hypertension and nondipping patterns. This study aimed to examine associations between 24-h BP patterns, hypertension, and cortisol levels.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 426 participants (329 with BMI ≥30 kg/m2; 97 with BMI 18.5-29.9 kg/m2) underwent 24-h ambulatory BP monitoring and assessments of 24-h urinary cortisol/cortisone ratio (F/E ratio), serum corticosteroid-binding globulin, and serum F/E ratio. Dippers were defined by at least 10% nocturnal BP fall; nondippers as less than 10% BP fall; and risers as a nocturnal BP increase.

RESULTS: Participants with BMI 18.5-29.9 kg/m2 (BMI 24.8 ± 2.7 kg/m2) compared to participants with BMI at least 30 kg/m2 (BMI 40.9 ± 6.8 kg/m2), were older (47.6 ± 8.2 vs. 43.9 ± 10.9, P = 0.002), had lower 24-h mean SBP (119 ± 11 vs. 131 ± 12 mmHg, P < 0.001), and were less frequently nondippers (50.5 vs. 66.6%, P = 0.004). No significant difference was observed in cortisol metabolism when comparing nondippers and dippers (sex-stratified). In a multivariable regression analysis, female sex, BMI at least 30 kg/m2, being normotensive, or receiving antihypertensive treatment were all significantly associated with a lower 24-h urinary F/E ratio. Among nondippers with BMI 18.5-29.9 kg/m2, urinary F/E ratio was positively associated with 24-h mean SBP (r = 0.46, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Associations between cortisol biomarkers and BP variation were limited in participants with BMI at least 30 kg/m2, but appeared stronger in individuals with BMI 18.5-29.9 kg/m2 with nondipping BP.

articles.title: Cancer Before Cancer: Measuring the Biological Consequences of the Modern Exposome.
articles.abstract: Cancer is conventionally defined when malignant transformation can be demonstrated, yet carcinogenesis is increasingly understood as a multistep biological process extending from exposure and tissue response through clonal evolution and, in some individuals, clinically apparent malignancy. The modern exposome provides a framework for considering environmental, endogenous, metabolic, infectious, occupational, and social influences that accumulate and interact across the life course. These influences can converge on chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, immune dysregulation, metabolic dysfunction, genomic instability, and epigenetic remodeling. Importantly, these processes are not specific to cancer and may accompany many chronic diseases. Their relevance to carcinogenesis therefore depends on persistence, tissue context, interaction with inherited and acquired susceptibility, and trajectories that favor clonal selection and malignant progression. This review develops a measurement-centered framework for identifying biological states that may precede clinically detectable cancer. The framework integrates quantitative assessment of tissue physiology, longitudinal biomarkers, genetic and epigenetic information, and external and internal exposure measures. It distinguishes transient physiological variation from persistent biological deviation by emphasizing magnitude, duration, reproducibility, and trajectory rather than isolated abnormal measurements. The proposed approach does not define cancer by a pre-malignant measurement or imply deterministic progression. Instead, it identifies a research pathway in which validated quantitative measurements could characterize biological states, support causal investigation, and permit longitudinal evaluation of preventive interventions before overt malignancy. Translation will require rigorous analytical and clinical validation, causal inference, longitudinal outcome studies, assessment of overdiagnosis and clinical benefit, and demonstration that measurement improves outcomes rather than merely increasing detection.

articles.title: Prevalence of low-renin hypertension: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current recommendations support measuring plasma renin and aldosterone in all adults with hypertension to detect primary aldosteronism (PA). However, clinical guidelines do not address individuals with low renin (commonly defined as a direct renin concentration <10 mU/l or plasma renin activity <1 ng/ml/h) who do not meet diagnostic criteria for PA and have normal or low aldosterone concentration, a normal aldosterone-to-renin ratio, and/or adequate suppression of aldosterone following salt loading or captopril challenge. This systematic review aimed to estimate the global prevalence of low-renin hypertension, as emerging evidence suggests this group may benefit from treatment distinct from standard antihypertensive therapy.

METHODS: The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42023467251). MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane databases were searched for studies reporting renin measurements in hypertension. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data, with disagreements resolved by consensus. Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute tool. Pooled prevalence estimates and heterogeneity were calculated using random-intercept logistic regression and I2 statistics.

RESULTS: Of 2745 records identified (1968-2024), 56 studies involving 13 210 participants met inclusion criteria. The pooled prevalence of low-renin hypertension was 32% (95% CI 28-35%; I2 =  94%). Prevalence was higher in studies with >70% Black participants (47% vs. 30%, P = 0.034). In studies with confirmatory testing to exclude PA, the pooled prevalence was 27% (95% CI 25-29%; I2 = 0%).

CONCLUSION: Low-renin hypertension affects a substantial proportion of individuals with hypertension, particularly among Black populations. Further research is necessary to guide optimal management.

articles.title: Missing Baseline Control Data Limit Causal Inference About Caregiver Education for Preventing Hot-Water Burns in Children.
Author's Response: Missing Baseline Control Data Limit Causal Inference About Caregiver Education for Preventing Hot-Water Burns in Children.
Multiparametric cardiomyocyte profiling with single-LED excitation reveals subtype-specific electromechanical coupling in LQTS in vitro.
articles.abstract: Cardiac excitation-contraction coupling (ECC) is an essential and tightly regulated process that links action potentials to intracellular calcium release and mechanical contraction. At the whole-heart level, ECC is captured by integrative evaluation of electrical and mechanical components of the cardiac cycle through parameters termed electromechanical delay (EMD) and electromechanical window (EMW). Alterations in the EMD or EMW reflect impaired electromechanical coupling and have been associated with increased arrhythmic risk across multiple cardiac diseases. However, it is currently unclear whether and how equivalent metrics can be derived and interpreted in vitro or meaningfully applied to patient-specific human disease models. Here, we implement ECC profiling in vitro using a single-LED optical imaging system that enables simultaneous measurements of membrane voltage, intracellular calcium and contractility. This approach allows quantification of individual transients and their temporal relationships. To investigate distinct perturbations of ECC, we applied this platform to human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) representing three mechanistically distinct ECC perturbations: a repolarization defect (LQT2, KCNH2 p.A561V), a calmodulin-associated calcium-handling defect (CALM-LQTS, CALM1 p.F142L) and pharmacological contractile uncoupling by myosin ATPase inhibition (blebbistatin). Cellular analogues of the clinical EMD and EMW were robustly quantifiable and provided mechanistically informative ECC signatures that were not entirely captured by conventional metrics focused on asynchronous individual transient analysis. Pharmacological targeting of the main cardiac ion currents further validated these findings and confirmed the robustness of the ECC quantification. This novel technique provides a basis for more sensitive assessment of disease phenotypes, arrhythmogenic risk and pharmacological effects in human cellular models, supporting the development of new approach methodologies. KEY POINTS: A single-LED optical platform enables fully synchronized, simultaneous measurement of voltage, calcium and contraction in human-induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived cardiomyocytes (CMs) at a high spatial and temporal resolution. In vitro analogues of the clinical electromechanical delay and electromechanical window can be robustly quantified in hiPSC-CM monolayers and behave consistently with their in vivo counterparts under genetic and pharmacological perturbations. Despite comparable APD80 prolongation, LQT2 and CALM-LQTS hiPSC-CMs display divergent electromechanical signatures, demonstrating that integrative ECC metrics resolve mechanistic differences not captured by conventional single-transient analyses. Pharmacological recapitulation of the disease phenotypes further confirmed these observations. In vitro ECC profiling offers a sensitive approach for distinguishing mechanistic perturbations of cardiac function and improving the characterization of arrhythmogenic risk.

articles.title: Rotational thromboelastometry and endothelial-derived extracellular vesicle changes in thrombotic microangiopathy versus other envenoming syndromes following hump-nosed pit viper envenoming.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Thrombotic microangiopathy is an uncommon complication of snakebite with unclear pathophysiology. We explore the mechanisms of venom-induced consumption coagulopathy, thrombotic microangiopathy and acute kidney injury in hump-nosed pit viper bites.

METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted at District General Hospital Horana, Sri Lanka (June 2023 to December 2024). Thirty-five patients were recruited, including: local envenoming alone (20), venom induced consumption coagulopathy (2), thrombotic microangiopathy (5) and acute kidney injury without thrombotic microangiopathy (8). Laboratory tests were performed every 12 hours, and rotational thromboelastometry (delta and platelet) and flow cytometry for extracellular vesicles at the earliest diagnosis of envenoming.

RESULTS: All thrombotic microangiopathy cases developed severe acute kidney injury, with 4/5 requiring dialysis. All eight cases of isolated acute kidney injury had mild kidney dysfunction that resolved. The international normalized ratio was normal in patients with thrombotic microangiopathy and acute kidney injury, however rotational thromboelastometry revealed coagulation abnormalities, including fibrinogen dysfunction despite normal fibrinogen levels, in patients with thrombotic microangiopathy. Isolated acute kidney injury had mild to moderate rotational thromboelastometry abnormalities. Endothelial-derived extracellular vesicles were proportionally highest in the thrombotic microangiopathy (median 12.6%) group. Red cell-derived extracellular vesicles were raised in thrombotic microangiopathy and isolated acute kidney injury groups.

DISCUSSION: Thrombotic microangiopathy and severe acute kidney injury are associated in hump-nosed pit viper envenoming. Rotational thromboelastometry revealed coagulation abnormalities, missed by conventional coagulation testing. Thrombotic microangiopathy in hump-nosed pit viper envenoming was associated with raised endothelial- and red cell-derived extracellular vesicles.

CONCLUSION: Rotational thromboelastometry is more sensitive than conventional coagulation testing for detecting coagulopathy and the associated risk of developing thrombotic microangiopathy and AKI in hump-nosed viper bites. Endothelial injury may be a factor in the pathogenesis of thrombotic microangiopathy in hump-nosed pit viper envenoming.

articles.title: Gender differences in acute poisoning: a 35-year cohort study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Drug overdose is an increasingly common cause of death, more commonly in males. In contrast, women present more commonly to emergency departments with overdose. We therefore aim to investigate gender differences in the characteristics and severity of acute poisoning.

METHODS: Adult (18-64 y) poisoning admissions to a tertiary toxicology service were reviewed (1990-2024), and females were compared to males. Data were extracted from a prospective database, including drug/toxin ingested, clinical effects, treatment, length of stay, intensive care admission and death. Primary outcomes were death, intensive care admission and intubation.

RESULTS: There were 22,316 (75%) deliberate self-poisonings - 14,101 females (63%), 8,178 males and 37 transgender; 2,101 (7%) recreational overdoses - 695 (33%) females and 1,406 (67%) males. Females ingested more paracetamol/analgesics, antidepressants and quetiapine, while males ingested more alcohol, amphetamines and opioids. Median age for deliberate self-poisoning in females (33 years [IQR:24-44 years]) was similar to males (34 years [IQR:25-44 years]). There were 1,268 females (9.0%) admitted to intensive care, compared to 912 males (11.2%), which was significantly different (absolute difference 2.2%;95% CI:1.3-3.0%; P < 0.001). Less females were intubated than males (790 [5.6%] vs 549 [6.7%]; P = 0.001). Inpatient mortality was similar for females (32; 0.2%) and males (24; 0.3%), and no difference in length of stay. More females had hypotension, while more males developed coma and hepatotoxicity. Males were more likely to receive sedation and naloxone. Gender differences were similar for recreational poisoning, except greater mortality in males. Gender remained an independent predictor of intensive care and intubation in a multivariate logistic regression model, with males more likely to be intubated and admitted to intensive care.

DISCUSSION: More males took recreational overdoses, including opioids, and females had more deliberate self-poisoning, with less toxic medications. Female deliberate self-poisoning patients were less commonly intubated and admitted to intensive care. Drug type did not account for the gender difference in outcomes.

CONCLUSION: We found only minor differences between inpatient morbidity and mortality for females compared to males. Males were more likely to be admitted to intensive care and be intubated, mainly due to higher rates of coma.

articles.title: Boerhaave's syndrome complicated by pneumorrhachis and chemical meningitis.
articles.abstract: Boerhaave's syndrome is a life-threatening condition characterised by oesophageal perforation. This report presents a case of Boerhaave's syndrome complicated by pneumorrhachis (air in the spinal canal) and chemical meningitis. A 26-year-old male developed meningism and an agitated delirium following oesophageal rupture, with imaging confirming pneumorrhachis and cerebrospinal fluid analysis consistent with chemical meningitis. Despite a prolonged Intensive Care Unit stay complicated by encephalopathy and severe agitation, the patient made a full neurological recovery with supportive care. This case illustrates a unique pathophysiological progression and underscores the importance of early recognition, exclusion of bacterial meningitis, appropriate prognostication and multidisciplinary management of pneumorrhachis complicating Boerhaave's syndrome.

articles.title: Circulatory effects of intravenous magnesium sulphate in children in the cardiac ICU: insights using high-fidelity physiologic monitoring.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravenous magnesium sulphate is routinely administered in paediatric cardiac ICUs for the correction of hypomagnesemia. Its physiologic effects in critically ill children have not been clearly characterised. We aimed to describe circulatory and oximetric responses following intravenous magnesium sulphate administration.

METHODS: A single-centre retrospective, descriptive cohort study of paediatric cardiac ICU patients aged 1-12 years who received intravenous magnesium sulphate. Temporal responses in physiologic indices were characterised using locally estimated scatterplot smoothing and restricted cubic spline regression adjusted for patient characteristics.

RESULTS: 57 magnesium administrations were analysed. Blood pressure demonstrated early and minor relative declines followed by a progressive increase above baseline. Modelled venous resistance reached a nadir of 7.2% below baseline (95% bootstrap confidence interval -24.77% to 25.19%) and modelled mean circulatory filling pressure reached a nadir of 2.2% below baseline (95% bootstrap confidence interval -10.85% to 8.55%) at 124 minutes. Regional oxygen saturation remained above baseline throughout most of the observation period, reaching a maximum increase of 2.6% (95% bootstrap confidence interval -0.38% to 7.55%) at 480 minutes among 30 administrations with regional oxygen saturation data, while modelled oxygen extraction showed a sustained reduction below baseline.

CONCLUSION: Findings suggest modest, coordinated changes in venous and arterial vascular physiology, with preserved regional oxygenation. Wide confidence intervals indicate uncertainty and heterogeneity in physiologic response patterns. These findings provide novel insight into the temporal circulatory response to magnesium sulphate in critically ill children and support prospective studies to further characterise these responses and establish causal relationships.

articles.title: Healthcare Access, Use, Affordability, and Satisfaction Among Adults With Cardiovascular Conditions After Enrollment in Medicare Advantage Versus Traditional Medicare.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease is highly prevalent among older adults and remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in Medicare. Medicare Advantage (MA)-the managed care alternative to traditional Medicare (TM)-offers adults integrated care and supplemental benefits that may improve outcomes and satisfaction for this high-risk population.

METHODS: We used longitudinal data from the National Health and Retirement Study (2010-2022) and an event-study, difference-in-differences design to compare changes in self-reported measures of health care access, utilization, affordability, and satisfaction among adults with cardiovascular conditions newly enrolling in MA versus TM (exposure) at 65 years. Eligible adults had a self-reported history of hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, heart disease, or stroke.

RESULTS: A total of 3312 adults with cardiovascular conditions newly enrolled in Medicare, 34.3% in MA (mean age, 63.6 years; 60.5% female) and 65.7% in TM (mean age, 63.5 years; 56.5% female). Following enrollment, there were no differential changes in health care access or utilization between MA and TM at any follow-up time point. However, new MA enrollees experienced relative improvements in affordability compared with their TM counterparts, including greater reductions in trouble affording medical care (difference-in-differences estimate -6.6 percentage points [95% CI, -12.0 to -1.3]) and trouble affording prescription medications (difference-in-differences estimate -4.6 pp [95% CI, -9.2 to -0.2]) by the end of follow-up. Satisfaction with care increased in both groups but with larger gains among MA enrollees (difference-in-differences estimate at the end of follow-up +11.3 pp [95% CI, 5.2-17.4]).

CONCLUSIONS: For adults with cardiovascular conditions transitioning into Medicare at 65 years, enrollment in MA was associated with greater improvements in affordability and satisfaction compared with TM. These findings may inform coverage decisions for this high-risk population, though generalizability to older beneficiaries or those with more advanced disease remains uncertain.

articles.title: How Stroke Genetics Is Impacting Clinical Care: Now and the Future.
articles.abstract: The past decade has seen a transformation in our understanding of the genetics of stroke. However, a commonly asked question is how do these advances impact the practicing clinician now, and what are their implications for clinical care in the future? This review outlines the major recent advances in stroke genetics and addresses 4 questions most relevant to the clinician: What do we now know about the genetic architecture of stroke? When and how should genetic testing be used to identify monogenic stroke? How can genetic information be applied to risk stratification and prevention? And what therapeutic implications are emerging from genetic discoveries? It highlights the success of genome-wide association studies in stroke and how these have transformed how we understand the genetic architecture of stroke. An increasing number of monogenic forms of cerebral small vessel disease are being identified, and guidance on when and how to test for them is covered. Polygenic risk scores are gaining increasing attention. How these can be applied, and the challenges in their use are discussed. Lastly, the impact of genomics on stroke therapeutics, whether by identifying new targets, assessing causality using techniques such as Mendelian randomization, or pharmacogenomics, is discussed.

articles.title: Multiomics Integration Reveals a Skeletal Muscle Metabolic Myopathy in Cardiometabolic HFpEF.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Skeletal muscle dysfunction is a major peripheral determinant of exercise intolerance and physical disability in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Metabolic and mitochondrial dysfunction are considered to be key components of skeletal muscle dysfunction, but comprehensive profiling of metabolic pathways has not been conducted. Elucidation of dysregulated metabolic pathways is essential to determine viable targets for the treatment of exercise intolerance in HFpEF.

METHODS: Male ZSF1 Obese rats (HFpEF, n=8) and Wistar Kyoto lean normotensive controls (Control, n=8) were studied at 26 weeks of age. The gastrocnemius was analyzed using bulk RNA sequencing, proteomics, metabolomics, and lipidomics. Differential expression across all omics layers was determined using standard statistical modeling with thresholds of absolute fold‑change >1.5 and FDR <0.05, unless otherwise specified. Additional targeted plasma and skeletal muscle metabolomics and lipidomics were performed in HFpEF and control rats, including analyses of the soleus and the extensor digitorum longus, to validate features associated with predominantly oxidative and glycolytic muscle, respectively.

RESULTS: Pathway-level analysis for RNA sequencing and proteomics revealed significant downregulation of oxidative phosphorylation (natural enrichment score (NES), -2.1; P<0.005), electron transport chain (NES, -2.0; P<0.005), and tricarboxylic acid cycle cycle (-1.8; P<0.05). The most upregulated pathways were PPAR signaling (NES, 2.2; P<0.0001), tryptophan metabolism (NES, 1.8; P<0.005), and amino acid oxidation (NES, 1.8; P<0.005) pathways. Metabolomics revealed an accumulation of tricarboxylic acid cycle cycle intermediate, isocitrate, and phosphate reduction. Branched-chain amino acids were significantly increased, whereas amino acids related to tryptophan metabolism were reduced and shifted towards increased serotonin accumulation. Phospholipid species were differentially regulated with increased palmitoylated phosphatidylcholines but reduced arachidonoyl-phosphatidylcholine species. Phosphatidylethanolamines species (16:0/16:1-18:0/18:2) were increased.

CONCLUSIONS: HFpEF skeletal muscle shows signatures of profound mitochondrial and peroxisomal dysfunction with lipid overload, impaired branched chain amino acid and tryptophan metabolism, and a shift in membrane phospholipid composition, supporting an acquired metabolic myopathy in cardiometabolic HFpEF.

articles.title: Effects of a parenting and unconditional cash transfer intervention on child development and maternal well-being in urban Bangladesh: medium-term follow-up of a cluster randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite extensive evidence that early childhood parenting interventions improve children's development, whether these effects are sustained in the longer term remains uncertain. We measured the medium-term effects of a parenting and cash transfer programme compared to a cash transfer alone on child, parenting, and maternal outcomes.

METHODS: In the original trial, we recruited twenty clusters in Rangpur City Corporation of Bangladesh and randomised them equally to intervention (parenting and unconditional cash, 299 participants) or control groups (unconditional cash transfer only, 300 participants). Participants were mothers of children aged 6-16 months on enrolment. Here, we followed up mother/child dyads five years after the intervention when children were aged 6.2 to 8.4 years. The parenting intervention involved fortnightly home visits by trained facilitators for one year. Funds for the cash transfer were provided by the Government of Bangladesh. The primary child outcome was IQ, while secondary ones included reading and mathematics skills. Parenting outcomes included quality of home stimulation and mothers' childcare knowledge. Maternal outcomes included depressive symptoms, empowerment, violence exposure and quality of life.

RESULTS: Out of the 599 participants enrolled in the initial trial, 555 (92.7%) mother/child dyads participated in this five-year follow-up. We observed no benefits of the combined intervention compared with cash alone for the primary outcome of child IQ (effect size = 0.11; 95% confidence interval = -0.04, 0.27); for the secondary outcomes, we observed benefits for reading, but not for mathematics skills. We also found benefits for home stimulation, mothers' childcare knowledge, depressive symptoms, and empowerment, but none for mothers' violence exposure and quality of life.

CONCLUSIONS: Although we found no benefit for the primary outcome of child IQ, a combined parenting and cash transfer intervention showed medium-term benefits compared to cash transfer alone for children's reading skills, home stimulation, mothers' childcare knowledge, depressive symptoms, and empowerment. However, as these findings are related to secondary outcomes of interest for our study, they should be considered as hypothesis-generating only.

REGISTRATION: clinicaltrials.gov: NCT03753646 (original cluster randomised controlled trial), NCT07432971 (follow-up).

articles.title: Development and evaluation of a subjective measurement of geographical hardness-to-reach: a survey of data collectors in a large-scale cluster randomised trial of azithromycin mass drug administration.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Distance from residence to the nearest health facility is a known predictor of child mortality. However, physical distance alone may not fully capture geographical hardness-to-reach. Subjective assessments from data collectors may offer additional insight into village-level accessibility and its relationship to health outcomes.

METHODS: This was a sub-study of Large-scale Assessment of the Key health-promoting Activities of two New Mass Drug Administration regimens with Azithromycin, a large-scale cluster-randomised trial of mass administration of azithromycin in Mali. We developed a 14-item survey and administered it to 25 data collectors to evaluate village geographical accessibility. We recorded survey completion time and respondent burden assessments to investigate the measurement's feasibility. We assessed convergent validity by correlation between two composite scores derived from survey items and objective measures (distance and travel time to the nearest health facility, the Malian national outreach programme status, and the average monthly rainfall) and predictive validity using under-five mortality as the criterion. Inter-rater reliability was evaluated by intra-cluster correlation coefficients (ICC).

RESULTS: The mean time of completing the survey was three minutes. Survey composite scores reflecting subjective village inaccessibility were associated with higher under-five mortality in the villages: one standard deviation change towards harder access associated with up to 8% higher under-five mortality rate, even after adjusting for distance to the nearest health centre. Internal consistency between the items ranged from moderate to high, with polychoric correlation coefficients ranging from 0.49 (items 'How long does it take for you to get to this village on rainy season' and 'Condition of the roads on non-rainy season') to 0.94 (items 'How hard this village is to reach' and 'How difficult it is for the residents to seek medical care'). Inter-rater reliability for all-item composite score and two-item composite score, was moderate to strong, with the average ICCs being 0.74 and 0.69, respectively). The composite scores showed expected associations with objective accessibility indicators, with Pearson correlation coefficients between all-item composite score and distance to the nearest health facility, average monthly rainfall, and travel time by car being, 0.36 (P < 0.001), 0.22 (P < 0.001), and 0.35 (P < 0.001), respectively. Pearson correlation coefficients between two-item composite score and distance to the nearest health facility, average monthly rainfall, and travel time by car were 0.34 (P < 0.001), 0.22 (P < 0.001), and 0.32 (P < 0.001), respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate acceptable feasibility and reliability, with moderate convergent and predictive validity. This simple survey can serve as a useful tool for evaluating hard-to-reach areas and guiding resource allocation in public health interventions, including mass drug administration campaigns.

REGISTRATION: clinicaltrials.gov: NCT04424511 (parent trial).

articles.title: Heart Failure Presenting With Concurrent Chylothorax and Chylous Ascites Resolved by Revascularization in Ischemic Cardiomyopathy: A Case Report and Review.
Impact of multimodal interventions on β-lactam use in patients with penicillin or cephalosporin allergy.
articles.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the impact of multimodal interventions, including electronic cross-reactivity alert suppression, clinician education, and implementation of a β-lactam allergy guideline, on β-lactam prescribing in hospitalized adults with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy.

METHODS: Single-center, retrospective pre-post study included adults (≥ 18 years) with documented penicillin or cephalosporin allergy. Patients were excluded if they received fewer than two antibiotic doses, died within 48 hours of admission, had allergies to both penicillins and cephalosporins, or received antibiotics solely for surgical prophylaxis. The primary outcome was penicillin or cephalosporin administration. Secondary outcomes included hospital length of stay, allergic reactions, Clostridioides difficile infections, and antimicrobial discontinuation due to adverse reaction.

RESULTS: Among 234 patients included (pre-intervention n = 123; post-intervention n = 111), baseline demographics, Charlson Comorbidity Index, and allergy characteristics were similar between groups. Penicillin or cephalosporin use increased significantly following interventions (65% vs 81%, P = 0.006), while non-β-lactam use decreased (26.8% vs 14.4%, P = 0.020). There were no differences in duration of therapy, frequency of allergic reactions, hospital length of stay, 30-day C. difficile infection rates, or antimicrobial discontinuation rates due to allergy or intolerance.

CONCLUSION: A bundled strategy combining guideline implementation and education with removal of β-lactam cross-reactivity alerts significantly increased penicillin and cephalosporin prescribing among adults with documented penicillin or cephalosporin allergies without increasing allergic reactions or other safety events. These findings support multimodal stewardship approaches to safely optimize β-lactam utilization in hospitalized patients with reported allergies.

articles.title: Early-onset severe dilated cardiomyopathy in a child with COL5A1 and ABCC9 variants: a possible complex genetic contribution.
articles.abstract: We report a 16-month-old boy presenting with progressive respiratory distress and generalised oedema. Chest radiography revealed pulmonary oedema, and echocardiography demonstrated severe left ventricular dilation with markedly reduced systolic function (ejection fraction ∼ 30%). There was no clinical, laboratory, or cardiac magnetic resonance evidence supporting myocarditis. Cardiac MRI demonstrated a non-ischaemic dilated cardiomyopathy phenotype without evidence of myocardial fibrosis. Despite intensive medical therapy, only partial functional recovery was observed. Aetiological evaluation using clinical exome sequencing identified a heterozygous likely pathogenic ABCC9 variant together with a heterozygous COL5A1 variant of uncertain significance. Although the pathogenic contribution of the COL5A1 variant remains uncertain, its coexistence with the ABCC9 variant may have contributed to the unusually early and severe clinical presentation.

articles.title: Causal inference with real-world data in health care research: a scoping review protocol and study within a review protocol.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study will improve the understanding and application of causal inference methods in health care research using real-world data (RWD). It seeks to systematically synthesize existing methods across different data sources, and assess whether large language models (LLMs) can support key steps in review processes.

INTRODUCTION: Randomized controlled trials are considered the gold standard for evaluating treatment effects, as randomization balances confounders and enables causal inference. However, randomized controlled trials are often costly, time-consuming, or ethically infeasible. As a result, RWD, such as electronic health records, medical registries, and health insurance claims, are increasingly used in medical research. Complex methods are necessary to derive causal inference from RWD.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Studies that use RWD, evaluate any type of health outcome as a primary endpoint in order to investigate patient health status, address a causal question related to a treatment or intervention, and estimate a causal effect size related to the causal question will be eligible for inclusion.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase.com, and Web of Science will be searched for articles published in peer-reviewed journals between January 1, 2010, and January 29, 2026. A scoping review will be conducted to identify and categorize causal inference methods applied to RWD, focusing on theoretical frameworks, data requirements, and inferential assumptions in order to develop a taxonomy of methods. The frequency, context of use, and quality of reporting will be systematically assessed. In parallel, a study within a review (SWAR) will evaluate the performance of LLMs for title and abstract screening and full-text data extraction compared with human reviewers.

REVIEW REGISTRATION: OSF https://osf.io/69mcd; SWAR Store (ID 66) https://www.qub.ac.uk/sites/TheNorthernIrelandNetworkforTrialsMethodologyResearch/FileStore/SWARFileStore/SWAR66%20Stella%20Erdmann%20(2025%20AUG%2001%202302).pdf.

articles.title: Sleep-like slow waves in wakefulness index post-stroke behavioural alterations.
articles.abstract: Increases in high-amplitude, low-frequency EEG oscillations during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep serve as markers of neuronal silencing, which disrupts functional connectivity and is associated with a loss of awareness and responsiveness. Cortical slowing likewise occurs during wakefulness, upon sleep deprivation, and accompanies performance deterioration. Recent work has revealed similar oscillations (termed 'sleep-like slow waves') following stroke in brain regions close or connected to a brain lesion, offering a plausible but untested mechanism for stroke-related behavioural impairment. Here, we simultaneously recorded EEG and behavioural performance while 30 unilateral stroke patients (12 left hemisphere, 18 right hemisphere) and 27 age-matched healthy adults completed a computerised perceptual decision-making task. Stroke patients had predominantly middle cerebral artery strokes (n=25), with a small subset of posterior cerebral artery (n=4), and anterior cerebral artery/middle cerebral artery (n=1) lesions. Sleep-like slow waves occurred more frequently in stroke patients relative to healthy controls, with limited spatial specificity when comparing patients with left and right lesion sites (more slow waves ipsilateral of the lesion). Furthermore, there was a significant correlation between slow wave occurrence and the accuracy and speed of perceptual reports in stroke patients, suggesting that variations in the occurrence of slow waves may contribute to cognitive heterogeneity post-stroke. As sleep-like slow waves predict deficits in perceptual decision-making following stroke, they represent a plausible mechanism of post-lesion functional network dysfunction extending beyond the damaged regions, thereby contributing to broader cognitive impairments.

articles.title: Correspondence to letter to the editor on "Evaluating treatment response thresholds for cost-effective treatment in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease".

SGLT2 inhibitor and fibrosis progression in MASLD: Correspondence to letter to the editor on "Comparative risk of fibrosis progression with sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 vs. dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus with low-to-intermediate fibrosis".
Evaluation of ITS copy number variation among Clarireedia jacksonii isolates using single-copy genetic markers cam and hsp60.
articles.abstract: Molecular tools are widely used for plant pathogen detection and quantification. Recent quantitative PCR applications for the turfgrass disease causal agent Clarireedia jacksonii were developed targeting the ITS region and showed potential utility in improved disease management. However, accurate and consistent pathogen quantification is contingent on stable copy numbers of the target genes across populations. In this study, we evaluated the genomic copy number of molecular markers in C. jacksonii using in silico analyses, quantitative PCR, and digital PCR. Calmodulin (cam), elongation factor 1-alpha (ef1α), and minichromosome maintenance protein 7 (mcm7) were consistently identified as single-copy loci, whereas ITS exhibited multiple copies in two out of nine assemblies. Digital PCR confirmed that cam and heat shock protein 60 (hsp60) closely followed theoretical single-copy expectations across a genomic DNA dilution series of C. jacksonii isolate HRS10. In the analysis of 27 C. jacksonii isolates, ITS was consistently detected as a multicopy locus, with copy number estimates ranging from 33 to 48 copies per genome when normalized using cam and from 34 to 52 copies per genome when normalized using hsp60. These results demonstrate that ITS copy number variation among C. jacksonii isolates was consistently observed, independent of the single-copy reference locus used for normalization. Therefore, single-copy genetic markers, such as cam and hsp60, may represent superior choices for accurate and stable estimation of fungal genome equivalents in C. jacksonii.

articles.title: Time to antibiotics and outcomes for children hospitalized with community acquired pneumonia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: It is unclear whether time to antibiotics changes outcomes for hospitalized children with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) and whether observation is safe.

OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to compare outcomes among children with CAP admitted to the hospital who did and who did not receive antibiotics within 4 h of presentation to the Emergency Department.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, retrospective cohort study using data from four hospitals obtained from the Pediatric Health Information System. Children aged 3 months to 18 years, with a chest X-ray, admitted to the hospital from the ED with suspected CAP who received antibiotics were enrolled. Our primary outcome was a composite of escalation of care (escalation in respiratory support, transfer to the intensive care unit, vasopressor use, or chest tube placement). Secondary outcomes were length of stay, duration of oxygen use, and cost of stay. Inverse propensity weighted logistic regression and log gamma regression to evaluate the association of early versus late antibiotics and outcome.

RESULTS: There were 758 children hospitalized with CAP who met inclusion criteria, of which 451 (59%) received antibiotics within 4 h. There was no statistical difference in escalation of care between those who received early versus late antibiotics (3% vs. 2%; odds ratio [OR]: 1.46 [95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.57,3.73]). There were no statistical associations with secondary outcomes.

CONCLUSION: This study provides an opportunity for antibiotic stewardship by showing that more time to observe patients with CAP without antibiotics does not change outcomes. This time may identify patients who will improve without antibiotics, limiting side effects.

articles.title: A natural talent: natural killer cells in nonpathogenic Simian immunodeficiency virus infection.
articles.journal: Current opinion in HIV and AIDS
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: HIV emerged from simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV), which infects African nonhuman primates (NHP). Among these natural hosts of SIV, some species are characterized by lack of progression toward AIDS, despite persistent high viremia. Most recently, natural killer (NK) cells have emerged as an important mechanism by which natural hosts avoid pathogenesis. This review summarizes the findings on NK cells in natural hosts, with a particular focus on recent findings in African green monkeys (AGMs); the discovery of novel functions of NK cells; and lessons learned for the development of an HIV cure.

RECENT FINDINGS: AGMs display strong control of SIV replication in secondary lymphoid organs, unlike humans living with HIV-1. This control is mediated by NK cells and favored through high levels of membrane-bound trans-presentation of interleukin-15 (mbIL-15) by follicular dendritic cells, migration into B cell follicles by IL-6-mediated CXCR5 upregulation, and expansion of terminally differentiated NKG2AlowCD16+ NK cells with increased MHC-E restricted activity and enhanced potential for antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity.

SUMMARY: Study of SIV natural hosts has identified protective immune mechanisms with potential therapeutic applications for HIV cure.

articles.title: Multimodality imaging to enhance substrate characterization for ventricular tachycardia ablation: what's new?
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Image integration is now widely used to delineate the ventricular tachycardia substrate, and the first randomized data have appeared. We review developments of the past 18 months relevant to the practicing ablationist, with attention to what imaging-defined scar represents and how it should be applied at the bedside.

RECENT FINDINGS: Imaging-defined scar has been validated against co-registered whole-heart histology, confirming that most CMR channels correspond to bundles of surviving myocytes. Both commercially available platforms identify compact scar but underestimate nonconfluent scar, particularly in the epicardium. Intramyocardial fat rather than fibrosis alone distinguishes arrhythmogenic channel segments, making computed tomography complementary to cardiac magnetic resonance. The first randomized trial of image integration (InEurHeart) demonstrated that computed tomography-guided ablation shortened procedures without compromising safety. The landscape of image integration continues to evolve. Photon-counting detector computed tomography has entered clinical comparison, and digital twin-guided ablation has reached first clinical use.

SUMMARY: Imaging modality selection should follow aetiology, with intracardiac echocardiography used adjunctively wherever available. Advances in imaging protocols and integration offer novel toolkits for the clinician ablating ventricular tachycardia targets. Future studies should remember to validate image integration against mapped or surmised ventricular tachycardia circuits.

articles.title: Tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair versus transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement - what are the key issues?
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Recent clinical studies of tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) and transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) have provided important insights into patient selection and therapeutic decision-making. This review summarizes the latest evidence and proposes a practical approach to selecting the optimal transcatheter therapy.

RECENT FINDINGS: The therapeutic goal of T-TEER is to achieve mild or less residual tricuspid regurgitation (TR), which is associated with favorable clinical outcomes. The likelihood of achieving this goal depends largely on tricuspid valve anatomy and transesophageal echocardiographic imaging quality. Although T-TEER has an excellent safety profile, its efficacy is limited in patients with unfavorable anatomy. In contrast, TTVR reliably achieves near-complete TR elimination and is an attractive option for patients unsuitable for T-TEER. Appropriate candidates for TTVR should have acceptable anatomical suitability, preserved right ventricular function and pulmonary hemodynamics to tolerate the acute increase in right ventricular afterload, tolerance of long-term anticoagulation, and an acceptable risk of permanent pacemaker implantation.

SUMMARY: Selection between T-TEER and TTVR should be individualized, choosing the therapy that provides the optimal balance of efficacy and safety for each patient.

articles.title: To jail or to extract? Management of patients with transvenous pacing leads undergoing transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Uncertainly exists regarding lead management of patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) who will undergo transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention (TTVI). Using published data describing the impact of TTVI on lead function, this review provides a framework for clinicians when deciding whether transvenous pacing leads should be retained ("jailed") or extracted for patients undergoing TTVI.

RECENT FINDINGS: Among patients with CIEDs who underwent transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement, the incidence of lead malfunction requiring lead revision was ~5%. Most lead abnormalities occurred within 24 h postprocedure but late cases (>3  months) also occurred. The rate of lead malfunction is lower (~1%) for patients who underwent transcatheter edge-to-edge tricuspid repair. Head-to-head comparison between devices is lacking. The presence of transvenous leads did not appear to adversely affect procedural and clinical outcomes of patients undergoing TTVI.

SUMMARY: When clinicians decide on whether lead jailing or extraction should be pursued for patients undergoing TTVI, a personalized approach is required with consideration of the following aspects: the lead's impact on procedural success, the benefits and risks of lead extraction, ongoing and future requirement for pacing and/or defibrillation, and the future risk of extraction if the lead is jailed.

articles.title: Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging in locally advanced prostate cancer: the radiologist's perspective on staging, treatment planning, and response assessment.
articles.abstract: Clinically locally advanced prostate cancer (PCa) is usually defined as cT3-T4 disease with or without regional nodal involvement. Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) is still the reference examination for local T staging because it combines high-resolution anatomic evaluation with functional information from diffusion-weighted imaging and, when performed, dynamic contrast-enhanced imaging. Its main strengths are the depiction of extraprostatic extension, seminal vesicle invasion, apical or bladder-neck involvement, and the delivery of side-specific information that surgeons and radiation oncologists need for planning. Its main limitation is reduced sensitivity for focal microscopic extension and for nodal metastases, for which prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PSMA PET/CT) is more sensitive. In current practice, mpMRI and PSMA PET/CT therefore play complementary rather than competing roles: mpMRI defines the local extent of disease, whereas PSMA PET/CT refines nodal and distant staging. Beyond initial staging, mpMRI also contributes to surgical evaluation, radiotherapy target delineation, adaptive replanning after androgen deprivation therapy, and the detection of recurrence after treatment. Interpretation after hormonal therapy, surgery, or radiotherapy, however, requires awareness of treatment-related signal changes and of the risk of both under- and overcalling recurrence. This narrative review summarizes the radiologist's perspective on how mpMRI should be performed, interpreted, and reported in clinically locally advanced PCa. Particular emphasis is placed on staging, treatment planning, and response assessment within a multimodality imaging pathway.

articles.title: Cessation of oral anticoagulation after atrial fibrillation ablation: who and when?
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The ideal long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC) management strategy for patients who have undergone successful catheter-based atrial fibrillation ablation is not well defined. Over the past 20  years, observational studies suggested that OAC could be safely discontinued for patients with intermediate thromboembolic risk, but randomized trial data were lacking to inform clinical practice.

RECENT FINDINGS: Recently, two randomized clinical trials on this topic have been published: The Optimal Anticoagulation for Enhanced Risk Patients Post-Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation (OCEAN) and Anticoagulation One Year after Ablation of Atrial Fibrillation in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation (ALONE-AF). These trials showed that OAC cessation at 1 year after successful atrial fibrillation ablation was not associated with increased thromboembolic risk for patients with an intermediate stroke risk profile (i.e. CHA2DS2-VASc 1-3 points). In both trials, the annualized rate of thromboembolism was below 1%. Patients with higher thromboembolic risk (i.e. CHA2DS2-VASc ≥4 points or history of stroke/transient ischemic attack) were minimally represented in these trials.

SUMMARY: For patients without high-risk features for thromboembolism, the OCEAN and ALONE-AF trials showed that OAC cessation is a viable option at 1 year after ablation if no atrial fibrillation is documented by routine rhythm monitoring modalities.

articles.title: Saddle pulmonary embolism and heparin-induced thrombocytopenia in acute pancreatitis: a case report.
articles.journal: Blood coagulation & fibrinolysis : an international journal in haemostasis and thrombosis
articles.abstract: Acute pancreatitis causes severe inflammation, predisposing patients to thromboembolism, which can be further complicated by heparin-induced thrombocytopenia and thrombosis (HITT). A 47-year-old diabetic male patient with severe acute pancreatitis developed a massive saddle pulmonary embolism. Low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) treatment triggered a deep vein thrombosis, and a severe platelet drop (28 × 109/l), confirming HITT. Due to a refractory response to fondaparinux, the patient was successfully switched to direct oral anticoagulation with dabigatran etexilate (150 mg twice daily). This led to rapid platelet normalization and clinical stability. When standard parenteral treatments fail in HITT, direct oral anticoagulants like dabigatran offer an effective alternative strategy.

articles.title: Personalized anticoagulation and drug monitoring for pregnancy-associated venous thromboembolism in hereditary type IIa antithrombin deficiency.
articles.journal: Blood coagulation & fibrinolysis : an international journal in haemostasis and thrombosis
articles.abstract: Pregnant women with hereditary type IIa antithrombin deficiency (ATD) are at significantly increased thrombotic risk. We present the case of a woman with four consecutive pregnancy losses due to venous thromboembolism (VTE), subsequently diagnosed with type IIa hereditary ATD. Type IIa ATD is exceptionally rare. The principal therapeutic challenge lies in the absence of established guidelines regarding optimal anticoagulant selection, dosing strategies, and monitoring approaches for such patients, contributing to treatment failure in her first four pregnancies. The patient was referred to our institution before her fifth conception. Preconception intervention began, and we instituted low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) therapy, with dose titration guided by thrombin-antithrombin complex (TAT) and anti-Xa activity levels. This regimen demonstrated safety and efficacy, achieving a maximum nadroparin dose of 10 250 IU twice daily. Under close pharmacotherapeutic monitoring by a clinical pharmacist using this individualized protocol, the patient achieved a successful term delivery and was discharged.

articles.title: Perioperative combined intravenous and intra-articular tranexamic acid does not increase venous thromboembolism risk after total knee arthroplasty in plateau areas: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Blood coagulation & fibrinolysis : an international journal in haemostasis and thrombosis
articles.abstract: After total knee arthroplasty (TKA), rivaroxaban is often used to prevent venous thromboembolism (VTE), while tranexamic acid (TXA) is used to reduce perioperative bleeding. However, plateau hypoxia may affect coagulation. We assessed whether combined intravenous and intra-articular TXA increases VTE risk in plateau TKA patients. This single-center, prospective, randomized, double-blind, pilot controlled trial was conducted at altitude greater than 3500 m. Fifty unilateral TKA patients were randomized to experimental (intravenous + intra-articular TXA) or control (intravenous TXA alone). All received rivaroxaban for 14 days. Primary outcome was new-onset DVT (deep vein thrombosis) or PE (Pulmonary Embolism) at day 3; secondary outcomes included thromboelastography (TEG) and coagulation parameters at 6 h, 1, 2, and 3 days. No VTE occurred in either group. Nonthrombotic ultrasound findings (intermuscular vein dilation with blood stasis) were observed in 9/25 (36%) of the experimental group and 13/25 (52%) of the control group, with no between-group difference (P = 0.254). TEG parameters showed no significant differences, except for a transiently lower D-dimer in the experimental group on day 1 (P < 0.001), though clinical relevance is unclear. Hb and Hct declined less in the experimental group at all time points (P < 0.05), suggesting reduced blood loss. In plateau TKA patients, adding intra-articular TXA to intravenous TXA did not increase short-term VTE risk. These preliminary findings suggest combined TXA with rivaroxaban may be well tolerated in this population.

articles.title: Network disruption in post-stroke depressive symptoms: a Bayesian multicohort study.
articles.abstract: Post-stroke depressive symptoms are common, but studies on the contributions of lesion locations to depression symptoms remain inconsistent. Bayesian statistics offer the possibility to clarify these inconsistencies by providing evidence in favor and against observed associations. We reanalyzed four previously published observational cohorts with 1,864 patients with stroke characterized for depressive symptoms from France, Korea, Germany and the USA. We performed voxel-wise Bayes factor mapping using general linear models. Lesion maps were used to test for associations of post-stroke depressive symptoms with lesion location. Network level associations were tested based on structural disconnection and functional lesion network maps estimated by reference to normative connectome data. Due to a sample size with broad lesion coverage, Bayesian inference was informative in large parts of the brain. Lesion associations were found in clusters in the right hemisphere including cortical (frontal, insular, parietal) and subcortical regions (striatum, amygdala, hippocampus) and adjacent white matter. Evidence of no contribution to post-stroke depressive symptoms was observed in large parts of the left hemisphere. Structural disconnection was linked to depressive symptoms in the bilateral frontal white matter prominently involving the corpus callosum and anterior thalamic radiation. Lesion network mapping revealed evidence of an association of post-stroke depressive symptoms with network connectivity in the left posterior cingulate cortex and precuneus, and less consistently, the bilateral anterior insula, along with widespread absence of associations in other regions. Depressive symptoms were most strongly associated with right frontal lesions and right-dominant structural disconnection in frontal cortico-subcortical circuits.

articles.title: Left Ventricular Free-Wall Injury During Emergency Pericardial Drainage After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention-Related Coronary Perforation.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Coronary perforation during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) can cause pericardial bleeding and shock. Emergency pericardiocentesis may be lifesaving, but persistent bloody drainage after apparently successful coronary sealing creates a diagnostic trap: clinicians may assume ongoing coronary leakage and miss catheter-related injury. We report a safety lesson from this setting. CASE REPORT A 63-year-old woman weighing 37 kg underwent PCI for a severely calcified right coronary artery lesion. Coronary perforation after stenting was sealed with a covered stent. After transfer to the ward, she developed shock and increased apical pericardial effusion. Our treating team performed real-time echocardiography-guided apical pericardiocentesis, draining 200 mL of bloody fluid with transient improvement. Routine catheter-position checks, including agitated saline injection, contrast fluoroscopy through the catheter, pressure-waveform recording, and blood gas or oxygen saturation testing, were not performed or not documented. Drainage remained bloody, with approximately 1000 mL additional output, recurrent hypotension, and a hemoglobin decrease from 102 to 67 g/L. Repeat coronary angiography showed no recurrent extravasation. Fluoroscopy/digital subtraction angiography showed an abnormal catheter trajectory, with the distal tip projected over the aortic region. Computed tomography was not performed because the patient proceeded directly to emergency surgery. Surgical exploration confirmed left ventricular free-wall penetration. The catheter was removed only after pledgeted repair was secured. The patient recovered well. CONCLUSIONS This case emphasizes a safety message rather than a proven intravascular route. After PCI-related perforation, persistent bloody drainage with shock should prompt immediate drain-position reassessment and controlled removal if intracardiac or intravascular malposition is possible.

articles.title: Lean metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
articles.journal: Current opinion in endocrinology, diabetes, and obesity
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Lean metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is increasingly recognized as an important but often overlooked condition. A normal BMI does not necessarily mean a low risk of liver or metabolic disease, making early recognition particularly important.

RECENT FINDINGS: Lean MASLD can develop through a combination of visceral fat, insulin resistance, loss of muscle mass, genetic factors, and changes in the gut-liver axis. Conventional BMI-based assessment can miss those at risk of liver fibrosis and cardiovascular complications. Emerging metabolic and genetic markers may improve early detection and risk assessment.

SUMMARY: Lean MASLD should not be regarded as a benign form of fatty liver disease, as it can still carry significant hepatic and cardiometabolic risks. Management should focus on healthy diet, regular aerobic and resistance exercise, maintaining muscle mass, assessing liver fibrosis, and reducing cardiovascular risk. Further research is needed to develop practical tools for earlier diagnosis and personalized treatment.

articles.title: Thrombotic microangiopathy after kidney transplant: a mechanistic + therapeutic decision tree.
articles.journal: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Posttransplant thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) is classified as de novo or recurrent, with distinct triggers and management implications for kidney transplant recipients. This review provides an etiology-based framework for de novo TMA and the current approach to diagnosis, pretransplant risk assessment, and management of recurrent complement-mediated TMA (atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome).

RECENT FINDINGS: Complement alternative pathway dysregulation underlies both de novo and recurrent posttransplant TMA, with pathogenic variants in complement regulatory proteins-factor H, complement regulatory proteins-factor I, and membrane cofactor protein identified in a substantial minority of affected recipients and increasingly sought as a second hit alongside calcineurin inhibitor exposure, antibody-mediated rejection, infection, and ischemia-reperfusion injury. Eculizumab, and increasingly ravulizumab, have transformed outcomes in complement-mediated disease, with growing evidence supporting pretransplant prophylactic use in high-recurrence-risk genotypes and protocol-based alternatives in lower-risk settings.

SUMMARY: A systematic, etiology-directed approach-addressing reversible triggers, excluding rejection and infection, and reserving complement blockade for complement-mediated or refractory disease-remains central to managing posttransplant TMA, though randomized trial data to guide optimal prophylactic strategy remain limited.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence in dialysis.
articles.journal: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning in dialysis have matured beyond the initial phase of algorithm development. Recent work has shifted toward clinical implementation, evaluation, and governance. During the past year, the first randomized trial of AI-guided dosing in maintenance hemodialysis has been published, a meta-analysis of technology-guided dry-weight adjustment has appeared, and the first professional society framework for the responsible use of AI in kidney care has been released.

RECENT FINDINGS: The Anemia Control Model is now supported by hospitalization outcomes and cost-effectiveness analyses. A randomized trial demonstrated that AI-guided erythropoiesis-stimulating agent dosing achieved outcomes comparable to physician-directed dosing. Technology-guided dry-weight adjustment is supported by a meta-analysis of 21 randomized trials. Machine learning for vascular access is evolving toward preoperative clinical decision support, while peritoneal dialysis is beginning to receive greater attention from the machine learning community. Large language models are entering nephrology along two complementary paths: open generative systems for education and clinical support, and deterministic, protocol-driven frameworks designed for safety-critical bedside applications. At the same time, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has released comprehensive lifecycle guidance for AI-enabled medical devices.

SUMMARY: The major challenge for AI in dialysis is no longer developing accurate prediction models. Instead, success will depend on effective workflow integration, validation across diverse patient populations, ongoing postdeployment monitoring, and demonstrating meaningful improvements in patient outcomes.

articles.title: A practical framework for using GLP-1 RAs, SGLT2i, and MRAs with contemporary immunosuppression in kidney transplant recipients.
articles.journal: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Calcineurin inhibitors (CNIs) remain central to kidney-transplant (KTX) immunosuppression (IS) but contribute to nephrotoxicity and cardiometabolic (CM) complications which negatively affect patient and graft survival. This review presents a practical framework for adding glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA), sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i), and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) to established IS regimens. These agents complement individualized optimization of IS, including CNI-sparing strategies when indicated.

RECENT FINDINGS: Evidence in KTX recipients remains limited, but available studies suggest that these agents may improve glycemic control, weight, blood pressure, proteinuria, and cardiorenal risk without routinely requiring changes to IS choice or dose. Whether these changes improve patient and graft survival remains unproven. GLP-1 RA related gastrointestinal effects may alter oral IS absorption, warranting continued CNI trough monitoring, particularly when significant gastrointestinal symptoms occur after initiation or dose escalation. SGLT2i require assessment of volume status, renal-function, and infection risk. MRAs may compound CNIs associated hyperkalemia and early eGFR decline, requiring close potassium and renal-function monitoring.

SUMMARY: These therapies may extend cardiorenal benefits observed in nontransplant chronic kidney disease to selected KTX recipients. Their use should be individualized, introduced sequentially, and supported by monitoring of graft function, electrolytes, volume status, blood pressure, and IS exposure. Temporary withholding should follow drug-specific perioperative and sick-day guidance, particularly for SGLT2i.

articles.title: Association of Homocysteine With All-Cause and Cardiovascular Mortality in Individuals With Advanced Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome: A Nationwide Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome reflects the overlap of cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and metabolic disorders. The prognostic relevance of homocysteine (Hcy) in advanced CKM syndrome remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of serum Hcy levels with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in adults with advanced CKM syndrome. MATERIAL AND METHODS This prospective cohort study included 3658 adults with advanced CKM syndrome from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999-2006. Hcy was analyzed continuously and by tertiles. The primary analyses used survey-weighted Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). Restricted cubic splines assessed potential nonlinear associations. RESULTS During a mean follow-up of 153.4 months, 2008 all-cause deaths and 686 cardiovascular deaths occurred. After full adjustment, each 1-unit increase in Hcy was associated with higher all-cause mortality (HR 1.01, 95% CI 1.00-1.02; P=0.014), and the highest vs lowest Hcy tertile was associated with increased all-cause mortality (HR 1.43, 95% CI 1.19-1.72; P<0.001). For cardiovascular mortality, associations were directionally positive but not statistically significant after full multivariable adjustment for either continuous Hcy (HR 1.01, 95% CI 1.00-1.02; P=0.053) or the highest vs lowest tertile (HR 1.34, 95% CI 0.96-1.86; P=0.082). Restricted cubic spline analysis suggested nonlinear associations. CONCLUSIONS Higher Hcy was independently associated with increased all-cause mortality in adults with advanced CKM syndrome. The association with cardiovascular mortality was directionally positive but did not reach statistical significance after full multivariable adjustment.

articles.title: Nationwide Survey of Laboratory-Initiated Peripheral Blood Smear Review Practices in Korea: Criteria, Workload, and Reimbursement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral blood (PB) smear review is an essential component of the diagnostic workup for hematological disorders. Laboratory-initiated PB smear reviews (LIRs) are performed based on predefined criteria involving complete blood count (CBC) parameters, analyzer-generated flags, and clinical information. However, nationwide data on LIR practices, workloads, and reimbursements are limited. Therefore, we investigated the status of LIR practices in Korean institutions.

METHODS: A nationwide survey of medical institutions in South Korea was conducted between October and November 2025. Responses covering LIR criteria, analyzer flag utilization, workload, reporting, and reimbursements were collected from 103 institutions. Workload was assessed using case- and time-based approaches.

RESULTS: Among the participating institutions, 94.1% used predefined LIR criteria. Analyzer-generated flags were the most frequently applied criteria (95.8%), followed by CBC (85.4%) and automated differential count (85.4%) parameters. Compared with the 2010 Korean nationwide survey, supplementary criteria for reticulocyte count, clinical information, and delta checks were less frequently used. The numerical thresholds exhibited notable inter-institutional variability. The operational burden was concentrated on technologist-performed workflows, with median monthly times of 4,825 and 575 min for technologists and hematology specialists in large academic centers, respectively. Most institutions (79.4%) did not claim reimbursements for LIRs.

CONCLUSIONS: LIR practices in Korea have evolved toward simpler, analyzer-centered workflows; however, variability persists in terms of review criteria, workload, reporting, and reimbursements. Therefore, updated consensus recommendations and reimbursement policies are required.

articles.title: The Art Behind the Algorithm: Hybrid Ablation and the Need for a Lifetime Strategy in Non-Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract: The management of persistent and long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation remains highly variable in clinical practice, despite increasingly refined guidelines and an expanding ablation armamentarium. Treatment sequencing is frequently driven by local program infrastructure and institutional culture, and hybrid ablation is often deferred until multiple endocardial procedures have failed, by which point progressive atrial remodeling may have already narrowed the therapeutic window. Randomized and registry data support a meaningful role for hybrid ablation earlier in the disease course of selected patients with non-paroxysmal AF, particularly those with enlarged atria, prolonged AF duration, advanced substrate, or failed prior endocardial ablation. Contemporary pulsed-field ablation technology has improved procedural safety and efficiency, yet freedom from recurrence at one year in persistent AF remains substantially lower than in paroxysmal AF across all current energy platforms, reflecting the complexity of atrial substrate over time. This ongoing myocardial remodeling places non-paroxysmal AF closer to a chronic structural cardiac disease than to a discrete procedural target and demands a lifetime management strategy rather than a sequence of isolated procedural decisions. The mindset for other progressive structural cardiac diseases has already moved in this direction-aortic valve stenosis is now managed through a multidisciplinary team that integrates anatomy, timing, procedural durability, and long-term risk across the full patient trajectory. We propose an AF Heart Team framework for non-paroxysmal AF in which catheter-based, hybrid, and surgical strategies are selected according to disease phenotype and lifetime trajectory, with the goal of intervening before advanced remodeling reduces the likelihood of durable rhythm control.

articles.title: Abnormal inferior parietal hub configuration during mindfulness following rumination in remitted depression.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rumination persists in remitted depression (RD) and increases relapse risk. Mindfulness-based strategies may interrupt rumination, but network reorganization during the transition from rumination to mindfulness is poorly understood.
