METHODS: Fifty-one patients with RD and 41 healthy controls (HCs) were recruited and completed a six-state fMRI paradigm (resting state I, negative autobiographical recall, rumination, mindfulness, distraction, and resting state II). We used network-based statistics (NBS) within each state and graph-theoretical analyses across sparsity thresholds. Rumination severity was assessed with the Ruminative Responses Scale (RRS). An exploratory analysis tested rumination to the mindfulness similarity of the left inferior parietal lobule (IPL) connectivity profile.

RESULTS: During mindfulness, RD showed a hyperconnected NBS component linking default mode, dorsal and ventral attention, and frontoparietal and somatomotor networks, anchored in a left IPL hub. A more widespread hyperconnected component was observed during resting state II in RD. Graph theoretical analyses showed that, during mindfulness, RD exhibited reduced degree centrality, betweenness centrality, and nodal efficiency in the left IPL (all FDR-corrected p < 0.05). IPL connectivity profile similarity from rumination to mindfulness was significantly lower in RD compared with HCs. Within RD, IPL degree and nodal efficiency were negatively associated with RRS.

CONCLUSIONS: RD is characterized by an IPL-centered hub configuration during mindfulness following rumination, marked by broad coupling but reduced hub efficiency and reduced rumination-to-mindfulness reconfiguration. Clinically, inefficient hub reconfiguration during mindfulness attempts may index a residual vulnerability and may represent a candidate target for monitoring and intervention.

articles.title: The stroma-vascular compartment: central facilitator of the damage response and repair across organs.
articles.abstract: Tissue injury initiates a complex, multicellular programme whose outcome i.e. functional repair or irreversible fibrosis, is determined by the coordinated activity of the stroma-vascular compartment (SVC). This network of resident fibroblasts, vascular mural cells, endothelial cells and immune populations acts as a gatekeeper of tissue integrity. Following ischaemia, trauma, or mechanical damage, extracellular danger signals are sensed by pattern-recognition receptors and transduced into cell type-specific metabolic and mechanical responses. An initial inflammatory wave clears cellular debris, after which endothelial sprouting and matrix deposition proceed toward scar maturation; a collagen-rich structure whose geometry ultimately governs future perfusion. Epigenetic reprogramming and metabolic rewiring enforce each of these transitions while simultaneously imprinting a memory that skews subsequent responses in the context of ageing, diabetes, chronic inflammation or clonal haematopoiesis. Targeting the SVC, rather than the parenchyma alone, now underpins therapeutic strategies spanning precision senolytics, engineered stromal cell grafts, and biomechanically instructive scaffolds.

articles.title: National support for a healthy checkout policy: a randomised message-framing experiment.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Healthy checkout policies set nutritional standards for store checkouts and have been implemented in three US jurisdictions. We compared four message frames, each describing a different rationale for the policy, on adults' support for a healthy checkout policy.

DESIGN: Participants were randomised to one of four message frames: (1) expanding healthy choices; (2) reducing parental stress by removing unhealthy items from child eye level; (3) improving community and child health; or (4) addressing predatory marketing. We used Poisson regression with robust standard errors to examine policy support by message frame and explore variation in support by socio-demographic characteristics.

SETTING: Online randomised experiment.

PARTICIPANTS: A convenience sample of US adults (analytic N 3978) recruited online via quota-matching to approximate national socio-demographic characteristics.

RESULTS: Overall, most participants (65 %) supported a healthy checkout policy. Support was moderately higher (68 %) when the policy was framed as reducing parental stress than addressing predatory marketing (64 %) or expanding healthy choices (61 %; all p < 0·05). Policy support was also higher when framed as improving community and child health (67 %) than expanding healthy choices (61 %; p < 0·01). In adjusted models, overall policy support was higher among adults with Hispanic ethnicity (68 %); incomes >$35 000 (range 66-70 %); a prediabetes or type 2 diabetes diagnosis (67 %); at least some college education (67 %) and residence in the Northeast US (70 %; all p < 0·05).

CONCLUSIONS: Support for a healthy checkout policy was high, especially when framed around benefits to child health. Adults with certain socio-demographic and clinical characteristics may especially support healthy checkout policies.

articles.title: Association of serum sodium correction rate with clinical outcomes in adults with hypernatremia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal rate of serum sodium correction in adults with hypernatremia remains unclear. We evaluated the association of faster vs. slower correction with mortality and other clinical outcomes.

METHODS: Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched seven databases through November 19, 2025, for studies evaluating serum sodium correction rate and clinical outcomes in adults with hypernatremia. For quantitative synthesis, study-defined faster and slower correction categories were retained, with effect directions harmonized as faster versus slower correction. Odds ratios (ORs) and mean differences were pooled using random-effects models, and risk of bias was assessed using Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions.

RESULTS: Eleven observational studies were included; nine studies (11 comparison units) contributed to the overall mortality meta-analysis. Faster correction was not significantly associated with overall mortality (OR, 0.856; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.546-1.342), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 94.8%) and a wide 95% prediction interval (0.167-4.399). No significant associations were observed for 7-day or 30-day mortality. In exploratory analyses, no significant difference was observed among hypernatremia-onset subgroups, whereas faster correction was associated with higher mortality in intensive care unit (ICU) populations (OR, 1.390; 95% CI, 1.089-1.775; p = 0.008) but not in non-ICU/mixed populations. Neurological complications could not be quantitatively synthesized, and hospital length of stay did not differ significantly.

CONCLUSION: Faster sodium correction was not significantly associated with overall mortality in adults with hypernatremia. However, the observational nature of the available evidence and substantial between-study heterogeneity indicate considerable uncertainty across clinical settings.

articles.title: RNA-Targeted Therapeutics in Cardiovascular Risk Reduction: From Gene Silencing to Precision Cardiology.
articles.abstract: Advances in cardiovascular prevention and treatment have substantially improved patient outcomes. However, residual cardiovascular risk remains a major clinical challenge. Traditional lipid-lowering and antihypertensive therapies, although effective, remain limited by suboptimal adherence, adverse effects, and persistent residual cardiovascular risk. RNA-targeted therapeutics have emerged as a transformative therapeutic paradigm, offering durable and highly specific gene silencing through small interfering RNA and antisense oligonucleotide platforms. This review evaluates the current evidence on RNA-targeted therapeutics for cardiovascular risk reduction, with an emphasis on their mechanisms of action, clinical efficacy, safety, and emerging therapeutic applications. A review was conducted using PubMed, Embase, Scopus, ScienceDirect, the Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov from inception to June 2026. A total of 154 eligible studies were included and narratively synthesized by therapeutic class and molecular target. Inclisiran reduced low-density lipoprotein cholesterol by approximately 50% with twice-yearly dosing, while pooled ORION analyses suggested a reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events. Pelacarsen, olpasiran, and lepodisiran achieved 80-98% reductions in lipoprotein(a), whereas zilebesiran lowered systolic blood pressure by more than 15 mm Hg with sustained effects for up to 24 weeks. Across studies, RNA therapeutics demonstrated favorable safety profiles, with predominantly mild injection-site reactions. Although definitive cardiovascular outcome data remain unavailable for several emerging agents, RNA-targeted therapeutics represent a promising advance in precision cardiovascular medicine by providing durable, mechanism-based therapies capable of addressing important residual cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: Efficacy of Nutritional Intervention in Adult Patients With Heart Failure: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Approximately 50% of heart failure (HF) patients are malnourished, doubling mortality risk; however, interventional evidence remains limited. A previously published meta-analysis found modest weight improvements only in malnourished/cachectic patients (5 studies, n = 275). This review updates the evidence in a broader HF population to evaluate the effect of nutritional interventions on all-cause mortality, hospital readmissions, and body mass index (BMI) in HF, determine whether intervention type moderates effect size, and identify sources of heterogeneity via meta-regression. This PRISMA-compliant, PROSPERO-registered (CRD420261445761) systematic review and meta-analysis searched PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane, and Embase for randomized controlled trials, quasi-randomized, and observational studies evaluating nutritional interventions (supplements, fortification, enteral/parenteral nutrition, counseling, with or without exercise) to increase protein/energy intake in HF, updating a 2021 search. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias (RoB 2.0 for randomized controlled trials; ROBINS-I for observational studies). Random-effects models pooled risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs), with subgroup, meta-regression, and sensitivity analyses. Of 7190 records screened, 23 studies (n = 2240) were included; 18 contributed to meta-analysis. Risk of bias was predominantly low. Nutritional intervention significantly reduced all-cause mortality (RR 0.43, 95% confidence interval: 0.26-0.71, P = 0.001), with no significant effect on readmission or BMI. Exercise capacity improved significantly (6-minute walk distance mean difference 25.01, 95% confidence interval: 5.26-44.76, P = 0.013), while quality of life, creatinine, and B-type natriuretic peptide showed no significant change. Nutritional intervention was associated with reduced mortality and improved exercise capacity in HF, though effects on hospitalization, BMI, and biomarkers were nonsignificant, warranting cautious interpretation.

articles.title: Pin-related complications in robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 15,874 knees.
articles.abstract: This review evaluated the incidence, characteristics, and management of pin-related complications following robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (RA-TKA). MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from January 1, 2010, to April 15, 2026 for studies evaluating pin-related complications following primary RA-TKA. Pooled complication rates were estimated using a random-effects generalized linear mixed model, and a random-effects Mantel-Haenszel meta-analysis compared complication rates between intra-incisional and extra-incisional tracker pin placement. Descriptive analyses summarized pin techniques, complications, and management. Thirty-seven studies comprising 15,874 RA-TKAs were included with a mean age of 65.5 years, body mass index of 30.5 kg/m², and follow-up of 10.7 months. Femoral pins were most commonly placed intra-incisionally (54.9%), whereas tibial pins were most commonly placed extra-incisionally (52.5%). The random-effects pooled pin-related complication rate was 0.47% (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.25-0.90%), compared with a crude rate of 0.89% (142/15,874). Wound complications (n = 93, 0.59%) and fractures (n = 24, 0.15%) were most common. Of the 93 wound complications, 69 (74.2%) occurred at extra-incisional tibial sites. Of 40 pin-related complications with reported management, 70% were managed nonoperatively. Meta-analysis of four studies (5,635 knees) found no significant difference between intra-incisional pin placement (risk ratio [RR] 0.25, 95% CI 0.03-2.06; P = 0.20; I² = 70%). Among RA-TKA pin-related complications with reported management, most were managed nonoperatively. Wound complications were most frequently reported at extra-incisional tibial sites, but comparative evidence did not demonstrate a significant difference between placement strategies. Further comparative studies and standardized reporting are needed to optimize pin safety. PROSPERO ID: CRD420261371245. LOE: IV.

articles.title: Role of Arachidonic Acid Metabolic Dysregulation in Sheep Brain Injury Caused by Coenurus cerebralis Infection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coenurus cerebralis (C. cerebralis) infection is a common parasitic disease in sheep that causes severe neurological damage. However, the underlying metabolic changes triggered by this pathogen in host sheep remain poorly understood. This study aimed to explore the effects of C. cerebralis infection on in vivo metabolic functions in sheep.

METHODS: Broad-targeted blood metabolomics was used to screen differential serum metabolites between C. cerebralis-infected sheep (BE-P group) and healthy sheep (BE-N group). Combined with KEGG enrichment analysis and ELISA assays, we further validated key metabolic molecules and related pathways.

RESULTS: A total of 25 significantly differential metabolites were identified, including 19 upregulated and 6 downregulated metabolites. KEGG enrichment indicated that the arachidonic acid (AA) metabolic pathway was the most significantly dysregulated pathway. ELISA results showed that serum phospholipids (PLs), phospholipase A2 (PLA2), AA, prostaglandin E2 (PGE2), thromboxane B2 (TXB2), 5-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid (5-HETE), leukotriene B4 (LTB4), cysteinyl leukotriene receptor 2 (CysLT2R), and soluble epoxide hydrolase (sEH) were markedly increased, whereas epoxy-eicosatrienoic acids (EETs) were decreased in the BE-P group. C. cerebralis infection disturbed the AA metabolic pathway, with abnormal activation of its downstream cyclooxygenase (COX), lipoxygenase (LOX), and cytochrome P450 (CYP450) branches. These changes were accompanied by neuroinflammation, oxidative stress and microcirculation disturbance, which ultimately disrupted cerebral metabolism. Notably, serum CysLT2R level in the BE-P group was 2.13-fold higher than that in the BE-N group, representing the most prominent difference. CysLT2R may mediate neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier disruption and neuronal injury through the Gαq signaling pathway.

CONCLUSIONS: C. cerebralis infection disturbs the arachidonic acid metabolic pathway and activates its downstream metabolic cascades. CysLT2R is a key altered molecule, which may participate in the brain injury induced by C. cerebralis infection.

articles.title: Efficacy of ablative laser therapy for vulvar lichen sclerosus: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract: To evaluate the efficacy of ablative laser therapy, compared to sham laser or topical corticosteroids, or an alternative laser treatment protocol for improving symptom burden and disease severity in women with vulvar lichen sclerosus (VLS). Systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for RCTs evaluating fractional ablative lasers in adult women with confirmed VLS. Primary outcomes were change in patient-reported symptom burden (visual analog scale [VAS]) and objective disease severity (LS Score, Clinical Scoring System, vulvar-appearance VAS). Mean differences and standardized mean differences were pooled using a random-effects model with restricted maximum-likelihood (REML) estimation of between-study variance and Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman (HKSJ) adjustment of confidence intervals; heterogeneity was assessed with I²; risk of bias was assessed with Cochrane RoB 2.0. Three RCTs (151 patients) evaluating fractional CO2 laser versus sham laser, topical clobetasol propionate 0.05%, or low-dose CO2 laser were included, with follow-up of 18 to 32 weeks. Laser therapy produced a non-significant reduction in VAS total (mean difference, 1.04; 95% CI, -4.71 to 6.79; P=0.52; I²=58%) and LS severity scores (standardized mean difference, -0.27; 95% CI, -1.47 to 0.94; P=0.44; I²=65%). No adverse events were reported. Current evidence from three small, short-duration RCTs does not demonstrate a statistically significant benefit of fractional ablative laser therapy for vulvar lichen sclerosus. Larger, adequately powered trials with standardized outcomes are needed before laser therapy can be recommended as primary or adjunct treatment. PROSPERO CRD420261385742. Not applicable.

articles.title: Work productivity impairment and its associated factors among patients with cancer in Bangladesh: a hospital-based cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: Journal of cancer survivorship : research and practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer imposes substantial physical, psychosocial, and economic burdens on affected individuals, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where out-of-pocket healthcare financing remains dominant. Despite these challenges, evidence on work productivity impairment among patients with cancer in Bangladesh is limited. This study aimed to evaluate work productivity impairment and identify the factors associated with it among cancer patients in Bangladesh.

METHODS: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 300 patients with cancer receiving treatment or follow-up care at two tertiary-level hospitals in Bangladesh: Rajshahi Medical College Hospital and Faridpur Medical College Hospital. Work productivity impairment was assessed using the validated Work Productivity and Activity Impairment (WPAI) questionnaire, with overall work impairment derived from absenteeism and presenteeism scores. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize participants' characteristics and work productivity outcomes, while beta regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with overall work impairment.

RESULTS: The mean absenteeism, presenteeism, and overall work impairment scores were 38.1%, 49.7%, and 63.3%, respectively. Overall, work productivity impairment was substantial, with presenteeism contributing more to productivity loss than absenteeism. Beta regression analysis showed that older age (β = 0.028, p < 0.001), higher levels of occupational physical activity (β = 0.032, p = 0.028), having lung cancer (β = 1.208, p < 0.001), prostate cancer (β = 1.139, p < 0.001), and other cancers comprising skin, liver, laryngeal, hematological, bone, and cervical cancers (β = 0.721, p < 0.001) compared with thyroid cancer, being diagnosed with stage II cancer (β = 0.389, p = 0.011) compared with stage I and a longer duration since diagnosis (β = 0.101, p = 0.012) were significantly associated with greater work impairment. In contrast, higher educational attainment was significantly associated with lower work impairment (β = - 0.039, p = 0.018).

CONCLUSION: Cancer patients in Bangladesh experience substantial work productivity impairment, highlighting a severe dual functional and financial burden. Both clinical and socio-demographic factors significantly influenced productivity loss. The findings underscore the urgent need for affordable cancer care, workplace accommodation policies, and strengthened financial risk protection mechanisms to reduce the economic and occupational consequences of cancer in Bangladesh.

IMPLICATIONS FOR CANCER SURVIVORS: Targeted support can help cancer survivors maintain work productivity, reduce financial hardship, and improve quality of life.

articles.title: Genomic analysis of extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from a dog with a severe episode of self-trauma and urinary tract infection.
articles.abstract: Extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Enterobacterales are emerging pathogens of major importance in veterinary medicine. This study describes the clinical, microbiological, and genomic characteristics of ESBL-producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from a dog with paraparesis and concurrent pyelonephritis, chronic cystitis, and a self-traumatized limb lesion. A 12-year-old mixed-breed female dog underwent repeated antimicrobial therapy during hospitalization. Urine obtained by cystocentesis and wound samples were cultured, and ESBL-producing strains were characterized by antimicrobial susceptibility testing and whole-genome sequence-based analysis. CTX-M-55-producing E. coli sequence type (ST) 457, phylogroup F, O11:H25, and fimH145, was recovered from urine and wound samples, while the wound sample also yielded a CTX-M-15- and SHV-2-producing K. pneumoniae ST39, KL149:OL2α.2. The two closely related E. coli strains differed by 96 single nucleotide polymorphisms, despite sharing the same ST, resistome, plasmid replicons, and virulence profile. ESBL-positive strains carried multiple virulence genes, with the E. coli strains classified as extraintestinal pathogenic E. coli strains. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of ESBL-producing K. pneumoniae ST39 in an animal in Brazil. The co-occurrence of ESBL-producing E. coli ST457 and K. pneumoniae ST39 in the same dog highlights the potential for companion animals to harbor clinically relevant multidrug-resistant lineages and reinforces the need for continuous antimicrobial resistance monitoring and antimicrobial stewardship in this sector.

articles.title: Retraction Note: Inhibition of RBM25 preserves cardiac mitochondrial homeostasis and attenuates ischemic heart failure.
Subsequent epilepsy surgery after SEEG-guided radiofrequency thermocoagulation: Outcomes and prognostic value of treatment response-a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Stereoelectroencephalography-guided radiofrequency thermocoagulation (SEEG-RFTC) is used not only as a minimally invasive treatment for drug-resistant focal epilepsy, but also as an in vivo test of an SEEG-defined epileptogenic network. Whether response to RFTC is associated with the outcome of subsequent surgery remains uncertain. We evaluated seizure outcomes after later resective, disconnective, or ablative surgery and the association between RFTC response and later surgical outcome. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to June 1, 2026. Eligible studies included patients treated with SEEG-RFTC and reporting therapeutic, safety, downstream-treatment, or postsurgical outcomes. Single-arm outcomes were pooled using random-effects logit models. Sparse permanent-complication data were analyzed with a random-intercept logistic model, and responder-versus-nonresponder comparisons with random-effects odds ratios; Hartung-Knapp inference was examined as a small-sample sensitivity analysis. Risk of bias was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute tools, with additional Quality In Prognosis Studies assessment of the three studies contributing to the prognostic meta-analysis. Twenty-nine original clinical studies met the eligibility criteria. Six studies comprising 194 patients reported extractable outcomes after qualifying subsequent resective, disconnective, or ablative epilepsy surgery; 141 patients achieved a favorable seizure outcome. The pooled favorable-outcome proportion was 72.4% (95% confidence interval [CI], 65.6%-78.3%; I2 = 0%). Three studies directly compared responders with nonresponders. Responders had numerically higher odds of favorable later outcome under the conventional random-effects model (odds ratio, 3.86; 95% CI, 0.80-18.57; I2 = 47.1%), but Hartung-Knapp small-sample inference substantially widened the uncertainty (odds ratio, 3.86; 95% CI, 0.19-77.91; P = .193). The pooled proportion proceeding to another epilepsy procedure was 22.0% (95% CI, 11.1%-38.8%), with substantial heterogeneity across clinical pathways (I2 = 84.1%), while permanent neurological complications occurred in 2.7% (95% CI, 1.0%-6.9%). Approximately seven of 10 selected patients had a favorable seizure outcome after subsequent resective, disconnective, or ablative epilepsy surgery following SEEG-RFTC. A positive RFTC response may strengthen confidence in the surgical hypothesis, but current evidence does not establish independent prognostic value. Current evidence does not support using RFTC nonresponse alone to exclude an otherwise appropriate candidate from definitive epilepsy surgery. SEEG-RFTC may therefore serve as a decision-informing component of network-based surgical evaluation rather than solely as a focal ablative treatment.

articles.title: Optimal duration of levetiracetam prophylaxis following supratentorial tumor resection: a multi-study analysis.
articles.abstract: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of short-course (≤ 9 days) versus extended-course levetiracetam (LEV) prophylaxis for preventing seizures in seizure-naïve patients following supratentorial tumor resection. A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted across PubMed, Google Scholar, and the Cochrane Library. Eight studies encompassing nine distinct clinical cohorts (N = 385) were included. Studies were dichotomized into Short-Term (ST: ≤ 9 days) and Extended-Term (ET: > 9 days) groups. Pooled seizure incidence was analyzed using a random-effects model, and a multivariate meta-regression isolated drivers of seizure risk. A temporal crossover analysis mapped medication attrition against marginal prophylactic benefit. The ST group demonstrated a pooled seizure incidence of 2.4% (95% CI: 1.1%-4.6%), significantly below the 12% historical baseline. Conversely, ET cohorts exhibited higher, volatile rates (up to 34.7%), statistically indistinguishable from untreated late-onset benchmarks (20%). Meta-regression identified only treatment duration and tumor type as significant moderators of outcomes (p < 0.05); age, gender, and LEV dosage (1000-3000 mg) had no impact. Safety analysis revealed a day-14 "clinical pivot": early well-tolerated somatic effects transitioned to severe neuropsychiatric toxicity with extended therapy, driving high attrition rate. ST (≤ 9 days) LEV protocol provides maximal prophylactic efficacy with minimal toxicity. Extending prophylaxis beyond this window offers no incremental protection against late-onset seizures but subjects patients to an intolerable neuropsychiatric burden. While prospective control trials are necessary to establish definitive guidelines, our findings indicate that a short term LEV course may offer a highly favorable risk-benefit profile. Extending prophylaxis beyond this timeframe seems to offer minimal additional benefit while markedly elevating the risk of neu​ropsychiatric toxicity, thereby requiring prudent clinical evaluation.

articles.title: Amyloid PET is a cost-effective exam to monitor Donanemab treatment in Alzheimer's disease.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract: Anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies are the first drugs approved as disease targeted therapies for the treatment of early Alzheimer's disease (AD). Donanemab and Lecanemab have shown a reduction of amyloid in amyloid PET scans, with an average of - 55.48 centiloids in the Lecanemab trial and - 88.0 centiloids in the Donanemab trial at 18 months. Despite their efficacy, these treatments are associated with amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA), necessitating regular MRI surveillance and strategies that minimize treatment duration to reduce risk. Economic modeling indicates that amyloid PET at 52 weeks is cost-effective when its cost is below 20.8-23.2% of the price of 78-week Donanemab therapy, translating into substantial savings and reduced adverse-event exposure. Studies with lecanemab are missing. Broader implementation is limited by access, cost, and the need for standardized centiloid quantification. Overall, amyloid PET appears to be a valuable tool for guiding duration-limited Donanemab therapy and may improve safety, efficiency, and resource utilization.

articles.title: Total Small Bowel Length and Limb-length Decision-making in Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery for Asian Populations: An APMBSS 2026 Modified Delphi Expert Consensus Statement.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Total small bowel length (TSBL) varies substantially and may modify the physiological effect of intestinal bypass in metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS). Fixed limb lengths do not account for individual variation and may contribute to suboptimal metabolic effect or excessive malabsorption.

METHODS: The APMBSS 2026 TSBL Consensus Panel used a two-round modified Delphi process. Faculty rated 38 statements across seven domains on a 5-point Likert scale. Thirty-five statements reached consensus in Round 1 and were reaffirmed during faculty review at the congress without repeat scoring; only three were revised and revoted. Consensus required a median score of at least 4 and at least 80% of ratings at 4 or 5; strong consensus required at least 90% agreement.

RESULTS: Forty-one analyzable responses from 15 countries/regions were included in Round 1. Thirty-five statements reached consensus. Three statements were discussed, revised, and revoted; one additional statement reached consensus. Overall, 36 of 38 statements achieved consensus (30 strong, 6 consensus). No final consensus was reached on routine TSBL measurement during standard sleeve gastrectomy or on diminishing metabolic returns beyond a 150-cm biliopancreatic limb in Roux-en-Y gastric bypass.

CONCLUSION: The consensus supports standardized measurement and documentation of TSBL and procedure-specific limb lengths in bypass-based procedures. It does not prescribe a universal limb-length formula, but establishes a framework for interpreting bypass physiology, balancing metabolic efficacy and nutritional safety, and evaluating TSBL-adjusted strategies in Asian registries and prospective studies.

KEY POINTS: • TSBL provides an anatomical denominator for interpreting intestinal bypass. • Standardized TSBL and limb-length documentation was supported by the panel. • No universal TSBL-adjusted limb-length formula was supported. • The panel supported a minimum 300-cm common channel for SADI-S in Asian populations.

articles.title: Spontaneous recanalization of pediatric internal carotid artery dissection during aspirin monotherapy: a retrospective case series.
articles.journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Internal carotid artery (ICA) dissection is an increasingly recognized cause of arterial ischemic stroke (AIS) in children, but optimal management strategies remain uncertain. While anticoagulation or antiplatelet therapy is commonly employed, data on radiographic outcomes and vessel recanalization rates are limited. The objective of this study was to describe the clinical and radiographic outcomes of children with ICA dissection-related AIS who received aspirin monotherapy for secondary prevention.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed five consecutive pediatric patients with acute AIS secondary to ICA dissection treated at our institution between 2018 and 2025. All patients received aspirin monotherapy (3-5 mg/kg/day) initiated at diagnosis. Clinical presentations, neuroimaging findings (MRI/MRA, DSA, vessel wall imaging), laboratory evaluations, and follow-up imaging were analyzed. The primary outcome was angiographic vessel recanalization on follow-up imaging.

RESULTS: Three patients had right-sided and two had left-sided intracranial ICA dissections. Two cases were associated with definite trauma, while three cases were spontaneous. All patients presented with acute hemiparesis, and two presented with seizures. Laboratory findings ruled out the diagnosis of large-vessel vasculitis. Follow-up vascular imaging (MRI/MRA) performed at discharge demonstrated complete recanalization of the affected ICA in all five patients. All patients achieved favorable neurological outcomes with resolution or significant improvement of deficits.

CONCLUSION: This case series demonstrates that aspirin monotherapy may be associated with complete vascular recanalization and favorable clinical outcomes in pediatric ICA dissection, including both traumatic and spontaneous cases. It suggests that complete vessel recanalization may be more common in children than previously recognized.

articles.title: Evaluation of the NORPACS risk score in STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The no-reflow prediction in acute coronary syndrome (NORPACS) risk score was developed to predict the risk of no reflow after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to investigate whether the NORPACS risk score predicts the outcome of patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) treated with primary PCI (pPCI).

METHODS: This retrospective study included 1725 patients. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis revealed 6 as the optimal NORPACS risk score cut-off value. Patients were thus dichotomized into two groups: high (≥ 6) NORPACS risk score (n = 765) and low (< 6) NORPACS risk score (n = 960).

RESULTS: The frequency of in-hospital and all-cause mortality was significantly higher in the high NORPACS risk score group than in the low NORPACS risk score group. Compared with the baseline model, in the full model of binary logistic regression, the NORPACS risk score as both a continuous and a categorical variable emerged as an independent predictor of in-hospital mortality (odds ratio [OR]: 1.61, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.31-1.99, p < 0.001; OR: 4.96, 95% CI: 2.13-11.54, p < 0.001; respectively). Compared with the baseline model, in the full model of multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression analysis, the NORPACS risk score as both a continuous and a categorical variable emerged as an independent predictor of all-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.22, 95% CI: 1.07-1.38, p = 0.004; HR: 1.97, 95% CI: 1.27-3.06, p = 0.003; respectively).

CONCLUSION: The NORPACS risk score can be used for prognostication of patients with STEMI treated with pPCI. It predicts in-hospital and long-term all-cause mortality and may serve as a practical tool for risk stratification in this patient population.

articles.title: Comprehensive meta-QTL analysis uncovers stable loci for fruit traits, morphological development, anthocyanin regulation, and biotic stress resistance in eggplant.
articles.journal: TAG. Theoretical and applied genetics. Theoretische und angewandte Genetik
articles.abstract: Eggplant (Solanum melongena L.) is a crop of significant nutritional value within the Solanaceae family; however, advancements in breeding for fruit quality, stress resilience, and architectural traits are limited due to the quantitative nature of inheritance for these traits. Meta-QTL (MQTL) analysis provides a powerful approach for integrating QTL information from various studies for identifying stable genomic regions. We integrated 620 initial QTLs derived from 23 independent studies that encompass traits related to morphology, fruit characteristics, anthocyanin content, prickles, and resistance to biotic stress. A high-density consensus genetic framework was constructed, onto which 425 QTLs (68.54%) were successfully projected. Meta-analysis identified 97 stable MQTLs across LG1-LG12, with the mean confidence interval decreasing from 10.29 cM for the initial QTLs to 3.42 cM for the MQTLs, corresponding to an approximately threefold reduction in interval width (66.8% narrowing). Candidate gene mining within 40 prioritized MQTLs resulted in the retrieval of 1,440 gene models, which were subsequently refined to 68 high-confidence candidates. This refinement was based on domain architecture, synteny conservation with tomato and potato, ortholog analysis, and expression profiling. Key genomic hubs were identified across several chromosomes, most notably on Chromosome 6, which acts as a multi-trait super-region housing major loci for anthocyanin pigmentation (MQTL6.4_A), morphological traits (MQTL6.3_M), and prickle development (MQTL6.3_P). Other critical intervals include Chromosome 3 (MQTL3.1_Bs) for biotic stress resistance, and Chromosomes 1 and 4 (MQTL1.1_F, MQTL4.3_F) for fruit quality traits. These hotspots are enriched for coordinated, multi-layered regulatory networks and functional modules, including pattern-recognition receptors (e.g., LRR-RLKs), transcriptional regulators (WRKY, MYB), scaffolding proteins, and specialized metabolic and structural enzymes (such as GDSL esterases, laccases, F-box proteins, and SWEET transporters). The significant conservation of synteny with both tomato and potato, along with functional insights from Arabidopsis orthology, underscores the evolutionary stability and functional importance of these co-adapted candidate gene complexes across the Solanaceae. This study represents the first comprehensive MQTL analysis in eggplant, establishing a robust genomic framework for trait improvement, providing key markers and candidate genes to accelerate marker-assisted selection and genomic breeding aimed at developing climate-resilient, high-quality varieties.

articles.title: Sleep duration: a neglected factor in stroke prevention among individuals with dysglycemia.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
AIM: Stroke imposes a staggering and escalating disease burden in China. Individuals with dysglycemia face a markedly elevated risk of incident cerebrovascular events. This study aimed to characterize global and Chinese trends in stroke burden and examine the association between sleep duration and stroke among individuals with dysglycemia, with a particular focus on the potential utility of sleep duration as an behavioral marker for cerebrovascular risk assessment.

METHODS: This study utilized the Global Burden of Disease 2023 database to assess the trends of stroke burden globally and in China(1990-2023). In addition, the study was conducted using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), encompassing participants aged ≥ 45 with baseline dysglycemia and no prior stroke. Sleep duration was obtained from the 2020 survey, while incident stroke status was ascertained across the 2013, 2015, 2018, and 2020 follow-up waves. Stepwise logistic regression models were employed to evaluate the independent association between baseline sleep duration and new-onset stroke. Restricted cubic splines (RCS) with four knots were applied to explore non-linear dose-response relationships. Additionally, subgroup analyses were conducted to identify effect modifications, and receiver operating characteristic curves evaluated the discriminatory performance of the prediction model including sleep factors.

RESULTS: Despite declining global age-standardized rate, the absolute stroke burden in China significantly increased from 1990 to 2023, particularly among males and older adults. In the CHARLS cohort, 7,274 patients with dysglycemia were included in 2011. After a ten-year follow-up, 694 participants (9.54%) developed new strokes. Notably, the sleep duration was significantly longer (9.95 ± 1.74 h hours, P < 0.0001) in the new stroke group. The model after including covariates showed that for every additional hour of sleep, the risk of stroke increased by 22% (OR = 1.22, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.13-1.32). Crucially, RCS analysis uncovered a non-linear inflection point at 7.5-8 h, demonstrating that cerebrovascular risk accelerated rapidly beyond this threshold. The fully adjusted model showed the highest discriminatory performance among the evaluated models, although the overall discrimination remained modest (AUC = 0.666).

CONCLUSIONS: China's absolute stroke burden continued to surge. Sleep duration may serve as an easily obtainable behavioral marker that complements conventional factors in stroke risk assessment among individuals with dysglycemia.A non-linear association was observed, with stroke risk increasing more rapidly beyond approximately 7.5-8 h of sleep. These findings suggest that sleep duration may provide complementary information for identifying metabolically vulnerable individuals at elevated cerebrovascular risk, although further prospective validation is required. By synergizing human epidemiological expertise with data-driven modeling, this study may provide a feasible approach to complement stroke risk stratification in metabolically vulnerable populations.

articles.title: Detection of common neonatal sepsis pathogens using a contemporary pediatric blood culture system.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate recovery and time to positivity (TTP) of neonatal sepsis pathogens at low and ultra-low organism concentrations using a contemporary pediatric automated blood culture system.

STUDY DESIGN: Six common neonatal sepsis pathogens were prepared in a 1:1 mixture of donor whole blood and saline-organism suspension at final concentrations ranging from ≤1 to 10-20 CFU/mL. Aliquots of 0.25-2.0 mL, containing 0.125-1.0 mL donor whole blood, were inoculated into BD BACTEC Peds Plus/F bottles. Recovery and TTP were assessed.

RESULTS: Clinically important neonatal pathogens remained recoverable at very low inocula, including ≤1 CFU/mL. Median TTP ranged from 10 to 12 h for Escherichia coli and Streptococcus agalactiae to 20-26 h for coagulase-negative staphylococci. Increasing organism concentration shortened TTP for E. coli, Haemophilus influenzae, Staphylococcus capitis, and S. agalactiae. Inoculated suspension volume had relatively little effect on TTP among recovered cultures. Recovery improved across larger inoculated suspension volumes, particularly for staphylococcal organisms.

CONCLUSIONS: A contemporary pediatric blood culture system demonstrated excellent recovery of common neonatal sepsis pathogens, including at very low organism concentrations. Larger inoculated suspension volumes primarily improved pathogen recovery rather than substantially faster detection. These findings support optimizing and documenting blood culture specimen volume as part of neonatal diagnostic stewardship.

IMPACT: Common neonatal sepsis pathogens remained recoverable at very low organism concentrations, including ≤1 CFU/mL, using a contemporary pediatric blood culture system. Organism-specific differences in time to positivity were more pronounced than the generally modest effects of organism concentration or inoculated suspension volume. Larger inoculated suspension volumes primarily improved pathogen recovery rather than detection speed. Recovery of staphylococci was reduced at smaller inoculated suspension volumes, particularly at ultra-low organism concentrations. These findings support attention to specimen volume and documentation of the volume obtained as components of neonatal diagnostic and antimicrobial stewardship.

articles.title: Haemodynamic responses to tracheal intubation are context-dependent rather than patient-specific: risk is patient-derived but sympathetic tone-dependent. Comment on Br J Anaesth 2026; 137: 872-4.
Simpler is not always better: Phylodynamic misspecification and deep-learning corrections.
articles.abstract: Phylodynamics bridges the gap between epidemiology and pathogen genetic data. The birth-death (BD) model and its extensions serve to infer the average number of secondary infections Re and the infection duration d from time-scaled pathogen phylogenies. Moreover, more complex models add extra parameters, such as the average length of the incubation period, the proportion of superspreaders in the infected population, or the speed-up in detection after contact-tracing. However, these additional parameters come at an important computational cost: While the simplest, BD, model, has a closed-form solution, its extensions do not and require numerical methods for their likelihood computation. This leads to increased computational times and potential numerical errors. Therefore, the BD model remains the favorite researchers'choice for real dataset analyses, and is often applied even in cases where more complex epidemiological aspects are present. We investigated, using simulations, how model misspecification influences inference of Re and d in the phylodynamic framework. We showed that the use of models not accounting for various epidemiological aspects leads to bias. In particular the simplest, BD, estimator tends to underestimate Re in the presence of super-spreading, incubation or contact-tracing, which might be dangerous from the public health perspective. In contrast, deep-learning-based estimators for complex models, accounting for multiple epidemiological factors, performed well in our simulations both on the data where those factors were present and where they were absent. This motivates the use of complex epidemiologically realistic estimators, whose design has recently become possible thanks to deep learning.

articles.title: Reducing blood transfusion vital signs monitoring frequency in a cancer center: a best practice implementation project.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Frequent vital signs monitoring during blood transfusion is standard practice to detect adverse reactions. However, intensive monitoring has increased nursing workload without clear added benefit for stable patients.

OBJECTIVE: This project aimed to implement an evidence-based, reduced-frequency vital signs protocol for blood transfusions and evaluate monitoring and documentation compliance during blood transfusion administration in an ambulatory cancer center in Singapore.

METHODS: Using JBI's seven-phase Evidence Implementation Framework, the team conducted a baseline audit, identified barriers through JBI's Getting Research into Practice (GRiP) approach, implemented change strategies, and conducted follow-up and sustainment audits over 11 months. Outcomes included compliance with monitoring and patient education. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics (frequencies and percentages).

RESULTS: Baseline compliance with the existing protocol was 0% (n = 30). After implementation, compliance with the reduced-frequency protocol increased to 60% (n = 30) and reached 100% at sustainment (n = 10). Patient education improved from 17% at baseline to 96% post-implementation and 100% at sustainment. No adverse events were reported during the implementation period.

CONCLUSIONS: Implementing an evidence-based reduction in vital signs monitoring frequency for transfusions in an ambulatory cancer setting was practical and improved protocol adherence and patient education. No adverse events were reported during the implementation of surveillance. However, larger prospective evaluations are needed to further assess rare adverse events. The findings support hospital-wide implementation with continued audit and monitoring.

articles.title: Prevention of catheter-associated urinary tract infections in a respiratory care center: a best practice implementation project.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Catheter-associated urinary tract infections (CAUTIs) are among the most common health care-associated infections, contributing to increased morbidity, prolonged hospitalization, and higher health care costs. Patients in respiratory care centers (RCCs) are at increased risk due to prolonged catheterization and high dependency on invasive devices. Despite established guidelines, gaps in adherence and challenges in sustaining recommended catheter management practices remain common.

OBJECTIVE: This project aimed to implement evidence-based practices for CAUTI prevention in patients admitted to an RCC and to support sustainable practice change through structured implementation and ongoing monitoring of clinical indicators.

METHODS: This best practice implementation project was conducted in the RCC of a tertiary medical center in Taiwan using the JBI Evidence Implementation Framework. A baseline audit was undertaken with six evidence-based criteria, followed by identification of barriers and development of targeted strategies using JBI's Getting Research into Practice (GRiP) approach. Implementation strategies included workflow clarification, targeted micro-learning and structured staff education, system-level support such as digital tools for checklist completion, and reinforcement of multidisciplinary collaboration. A follow-up audit was conducted to evaluate changes in compliance.

RESULTS: Baseline compliance varied across criteria, with high compliance in daily hygiene practices but lower compliance in staff education, protocol availability, and multidisciplinary involvement. Following implementation, compliance improved across all six criteria. The most notable improvements were observed in staff education and protocol availability, which increased from 16.67% to 100% and from 58.33% to 100%, respectively. Marked improvement was also observed in multidisciplinary involvement, while moderate improvements were seen in hand hygiene and timely catheter removal. Trends in catheter utilization and CAUTI incidence were monitored with CAUTI incidence remaining low during the extended post-implementation period despite variability in catheter utilization. This supported the sustainability of practice changes.

CONCLUSIONS: A structured, framework-guided implementation approach led to improvements in compliance with evidence-based CAUTI prevention practices in an RCC. Addressing workflow barriers, incorporating system-level support, and strengthening multidisciplinary collaboration were important components of practice change.

articles.title: Improving asthma care: a call for leadership in health, equity and climate.
articles.abstract: Now is the time for a co-ordinated revolution in asthma care in Aotearoa New Zealand. New Zealand can and should accelerate uptake of guideline-based single maintenance and reliever therapy and actively reduce the unnecessary use of therapies based only on short-acting beta agonists. These two actions together will achieve three important goals: reduced avoidable asthma harm, reduced health inequity and reduced healthcare greenhouse gas emissions. Leadership is required from clinicians, manufacturers, policymakers, funders and Pharmac.

articles.title: Women's cardiovascular health in Aotearoa New Zealand: insights from a systematic literature review.
articles.abstract: Heart disease (HD) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality globally, yet it remains understudied, underdiagnosed and undertreated in women. Although attention towards gender equity in heart health has increased, significant knowledge gaps persist in understanding the impact, incidence and experiences of women living with HD in Aotearoa New Zealand. This systematic review identified and synthesised evidence on the heart health of women in Aotearoa New Zealand, focussing on clinical outcomes, awareness of HD and lived experiences. The review followed a registered protocol (PROSPERO: CRD420246000029). Systematic searches of Ovid MEDLINE, PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, ProQuest Health & Medical and ProQuest Dissertations identified studies published between 2000 and 2024. Inclusion/exclusion criteria were defined in PROSPERO and refined in Covidence. Eligible studies were assessed for risk of bias using Joanna Briggs Institute appraisal tools, and data were synthesised using Braun and Clarke's thematic framework. The search identified 61 papers. Key themes included: delayed diagnosis for women and lower likelihood of receiving guideline recommended treatments; pronounced equity gaps for Māori and Pacific women, who face higher premature cardiovascular mortality and barriers to care; the psychological burden of HD and women's experiences of reduced or delayed care; and the essential role of culturally responsive, patient centred models of care in improving outcomes. The literature reveals ongoing gaps in diagnosis, treatment and care for women with HD in Aotearoa New Zealand. Addressing these inequities requires gender specific and culturally grounded strategies to improve cardiovascular outcomes for diverse communities.

articles.title: The health of the New Zealand cardiac sonographer workforce: cardiac sonographer workforce survey.
articles.abstract:
AIM: The aim of this study was to quantify the current state of the cardiac sonographer workforce within Health New Zealand - Te Whatu Ora.

METHODS: In 2024, the Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand surveyed all Health New Zealand - Te Whatu Ora echocardiography departments to collect workforce data on cardiac sonographers. Population data were obtained from Health New Zealand - Te Whatu Ora.

RESULTS: A total of 109 Health New Zealand - Te Whatu Ora-employed cardiac sonographers were identified. Of these, 72 (70%) were female and 71 (70%) trained in New Zealand. Twenty percent were aged over 50 years, with experience ranging from trainees to 45 years in practice. Nationally, there was one cardiac sonographer per 49,000 people, compared with one per 14,000 in Australia. In two of the five districts with the highest proportions of Māori and Pacific people, this ratio exceeded the national average: Northland (1:69,000) and Hawke's Bay (1:62,000). Workforce capacity remained largely unchanged over time, from 1.4 full-time equivalent (FTE) per 100,000 population in 2010 to 1.6 FTE per 100,000 in 2024, while vacancies increased from 3.2 FTE (4.5%) in 2013 to 15.9 FTE (19%) in 2024.

CONCLUSIONS: New Zealand has substantially fewer cardiac sonographers than Australia, with little growth in workforce capacity and a fivefold increase in vacancies since 2013, raising concerns about workforce sustainability and equitable access to echocardiography services.

articles.title: Multiomic Depth in Right Ventricular Failure: Lost in Translation?
Hypertension Drives Piezo1 to Put the Brakes on Cerebral Blood Flow.
Plasma free light chains across chronic kidney disease stages: real-world patterns of kappa, lambda, and κ/λ ratio.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Free immunoglobulin light chains (FLCs) are key biomarkers for plasma cell disorders, but interpretation is complicated in patients with impaired kidney function because reduced renal clearance leads to accumulation of polyclonal FLCs. Although FLC concentrations are known to increase as kidney function declines, data from routine clinical practice remain limited.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 7,921 plasma samples referred for clinical FLC testing between 2021 and 2025 using the Siemens N Latex FLC assay. Free κ and λ concentrations were paired with same-day creatinine measurements, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was calculated. Samples were grouped according to KDIGO eGFR categories. To reduce the influence of overt monoclonal gammopathies, samples with extreme κ/λ ratios (<0.1 or >10) or a documented M-component were excluded. FLC distributions were estimated using non-parametric and bootstrap methods. Analyses were descriptive and performed at the sample level.

RESULTS: Both κ and λ FLC concentrations increased progressively with declining eGFR. Across eGFR categories, κ concentrations increased approximately ten-fold and λ concentrations approximately five-fold from the highest to the lowest kidney function group. The κ/λ ratio remained relatively stable overall, although variability increased and upper percentiles widened at the lowest eGFR levels.

CONCLUSIONS: FLC concentrations are strongly influenced by kidney function, underscoring the importance of interpreting results in the context of eGFR. These real-world findings provide a descriptive overview of FLC distributions across kidney function categories. However, because of the retrospective design, repeated sampling, limited clinical information, and lack of diagnostic validation, the results should be considered exploratory.

articles.title: Resolution Pharmacology: Targeting the Annexin A1-FPR2/ALX Pathway.
articles.journal: Current topics in microbiology and immunology
articles.abstract: Annexin A1 (AnxA1) and its receptor formyl-peptide receptor type 2 (FPR2)-also termed lipoxin A4 receptor (ALX) or FPR2/ALX-are highly effective modulators of several biological phenomena that enable the resolution of acute inflammation. These properties are reflected in non-redundant roles of this pro-resolving protein and its receptor in several preclinical models of disease. Here we reason on the translational opportunity posed by the fundamental science associated with AnxA1/FPR2 and propose potential clinical applications in disease areas where unablated inflammation and dysregulated immune cell activation and recruitment occur. We discuss AnxA1-derived compounds as well as the translational investigations based on FPR2 small-molecule agonists. In summary, we surmise that exploitation of the AnxA1/FPR2 pathway is a viable and amenable approach to establish resolution pharmacology as a new branch formed by innovative therapeutics that mimic endogenous processes of the resolution of inflammation.

articles.title: Distinct phenotypes associated with the same homozygous ENPP1 c.26dup variant.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: ENPP1 pathogenic variants have been associated with a wide phenotypic spectrum, ranging from generalized arterial calcification of infancy to vascular stenoses and autosomal recessive hypophosphatemic rickets.

CASE PRESENTATION: This study presents two cases of cousins who are homozygous for the c.26dup (p.Gly10ArgfsTer67) variant in the ENPP1 gene, but who exhibit distinct clinical features. The first patient developed hypophosphatemic rickets in early childhood. He was subsequently diagnosed with hypertension due to multiple arterial stenoses. In the second case, prenatal monitoring revealed generalized vascular calcification of intrauterine onset. Postnatally, the patient was diagnosed with heart failure, for which medical therapy was initiated, and early parenteral pamidronate was administered. However, the infant died during infancy due to a respiratory infection.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that ENPP1 variants may manifest with heterogeneous phenotypes and modifying factors may influence the variant's clinical expression. Case 1 was previously reported with limited clinical information as part of a national Turkish cohort of patients with autosomal recessive hypophosphatemic rickets type 2 caused by ENPP1 deficiency. However, as the study was a cohort analysis, it did not comprehensively describe the patient's clinical course, cardiovascular involvement, long-term follow-up, or the intrafamilial phenotypic variability observed within the affected family. Our report contributes to a better understanding of this rare genetic disorder's clinical spectrum and to clarifying the genotype-phenotype correlation.

articles.title: Genetic dissection of cell type-specific congenital heart disease variants reveals ETS1 control of vascular smooth muscle cell fate.
articles.abstract: Numerous congenital heart disease (CHD) risk variants lie in cis-regulatory elements, yet the impact of variants in repressed and bivalent chromatin on cell type-specific heart development is unclear. Here, we generated a single-cell multiomic atlas of human cardiac differentiation by jointly profiling H3K27ac, H3K27me3, H3K4me3, and transcriptomes in individual cells, classifying cis-regulatory elements into six chromatin states, enabling prioritization of 610 CHD-associated noncoding variants enriched in lineage- and state-specific regulatory elements, including repressive and bivalent regions. CRISPR knockin of selected variants perturbed nearby gene expression and impaired cardiac differentiation. Dissection of a Polycomb-marked variant near ETS1 (ETS proto-oncogene 1) revealed local H3K27me3 loss, H3K27ac gain, and ETS1 up-regulation, which redirects differentiation toward second-heart-field progenitors with epithelial characteristics at early stages and, ultimately, highly migratory ETS1+ vascular smooth muscle cells. Together, our work establishes a single-cell chromatin-state framework for interpreting noncoding CHD risk variants and uncovers an ETS1-driven program linking Polycomb-deregulated noncoding variation to aberrant vascular smooth muscle fate commitment during human cardiogenesis.

articles.title: Dynamic redox reactivation of platinum sites for long-term glycolate electrosynthesis from polyethylene terephthalate wastes.
articles.abstract: Glycolates are indispensable in the health, chemical and pharmaceutical industries, whereas their mainstream production involve toxic chemicals and harsh operating condition. An alternative route for glycolate production is electrifying ethylene glycol (EG) that originates from polyethylene terephthalate (PET) but suffers from poor durability of active platinum site that tend to deactivate. Herein, we demonstrate a dynamic redox reactivation strategy, which alternates between working potential for oxidizing EG to glycolate and nonworking potential for reviving active platinum sites by the chemical reduction of adsorbed EG, realizing an unprecedented stability for over 3000 hours under average current density of ∼220 milliamperes per square centimeter. Upscaling this approach, the assembled electrolyzer drives a record current of 10 amperes at 1.18 volts for repeatable 40 batches of glycolates electrosynthesis, with each batch converting 48.0 grams of PET to 11.6 grams of glycolates (52.8% yield), 37.7 grams of p-phthalic acid (95.8% yield), 248.7 grams of NaHSO4 (95.2% yield) and ∼11.5 liters of hydrogen, showcasing a considerable revenue of ∼$1072 per ton glycolate.

articles.title: Pancreatic α cells function as MHC class II-dependent antigen-presenting cells in type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is an autoimmune disease characterized by T cell-mediated destruction of pancreatic β cells, in which antigen presentation is essential. Although professional antigen-presenting cells initiate autoreactive T cell responses, whether endocrine cells contribute to antigen presentation within inflamed islets remains unclear. Here, we show that pancreatic α cells acquire major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II (MHC-II)-dependent antigen-presenting capacity during T1D progression. Reanalysis of single-cell RNA sequencing datasets from nonobese diabetic (NOD) mice and human T1D islets revealed progressive up-regulation of MHC-II associated genes in α cells. Immunostaining validated the increased of MHC-II level both in NOD mice and patients with T1D. Mechanistically, inflammatory cytokines activated the Janus kinase-signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK-STAT) pathway in α cells, leading to JAK-STAT-dependent MHC-II induction. Functionally, activated α cells internalized, processed, and presented exogenous antigens, acquired expression of costimulatory molecules, and promoted antigen-specific CD4+ T cell activation. These findings identify pancreatic α cells as nonprofessional antigen-presenting cells and expand the current understanding of antigen presentation in autoimmune diabetes.

articles.title: Allosteric anticoagulation: emerging non-orthosteric inhibitors of factor XI and factor XIa.
HIV: tackling inequalities and sustaining access to care in an era of global health regression.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The global HIV response has entered a critical moment. Tools to prevent and treat HIV are more effective than ever, yet financing cuts, political and policy regression, and persistent inequalities threaten access to these tools. This review examines key developments over the past 18 months, focusing on how inequality is shaping progress in the global HIV response.

RECENT FINDINGS: Progress against HIV remains highly uneven across regions and populations. New infections are increasingly concentrated among key populations - including gay and bisexual men, sex workers, transgender people, and people who inject drugs - and among adolescent girls and young women in some regions, reflecting persistent criminalization, stigma, gender inequality, and economic exclusion. The 2025 global health financing shock has disproportionately disrupted prevention, treatment, community-led services, and monitoring systems, making its full impact difficult to assess. Meanwhile, lenacapavir and other long-acting prevention technologies could transform HIV prevention, but their impact will depend on financing, infrastructure, and whether they reach the populations most likely to benefit.

SUMMARY: Addressing these challenges requires less emphasis on developing new HIV technologies than on ensuring that existing and emerging tools reach the populations who need them most. Sustained progress will require financing, protection of human rights, community leadership, and health systems capable of delivering prevention and treatment to populations most affected by HIV.

articles.title: Deep learning and dual-domain fusion of temporal and spectrotemporal SCG for valvular heart disease classification.
articles.abstract: Heart valve disease (HVD) is a growing cause of cardiovascular morbidity, yet accessible screening tools remain limited. Tri-axial seismocardiogram (SCG) signals capture mechanical signatures of both stenosis and regurgitation, but their non-stationary nature and subtle inter-lesion morphological differences challenge robust classification from a single representation. This study proposes an electrocardiogram (ECG)-free dual-domain deep learning framework that combines a 1D convolutional-recurrent encoder of raw SCG waveforms with a 2D EfficientNet encoder of continuous wavelet transform scalograms, integrating temporal and spectrotemporal representations through feature-level fusion. The framework was evaluated on primary valve lesion classification in 94 patients, with an additional exploratory analysis of multi-valvular, aortic-stenosis-dominant disease. Under patient-level stratified group cross-validation, the fused model achieved the highest mean accuracy (65.3%; 95% CI, 59.8%-70.7%), exceeding both unimodal encoders and the majority-class (35.2%) and covariate-only (39.1%) baselines. The same mean performance ordering was preserved when the image backbone was replaced, although the confidence intervals overlap at this cohort size. Under the segment-level protocol used in prior studies, the framework achieved 99.63% accuracy, with faster training convergence and more compact, separable feature clusters than either unimodal encoder. These findings support the value of combining temporal and spectrotemporal SCG representations and demonstrate its potential for ECG-free HVD classification under patient-independent evaluation.

articles.title: Design and Synthesis of Photoswitchable Conjugated Dithienylethene-Naphthalimide Scaffolds: Applications in Molecular Logic and Anticounterfeiting.
articles.abstract: Modulation of optical properties by multiple stimuli became a valuable tool to design molecular switching devices, logic gates, sensing devices, advanced anti-counterfeiting agents, etc. Herein, a dithienylethene (DTE)-, naphthalimide (NI)-, and aniline-based molecular switch was conceptually designed and synthesized, which showed efficient fluorescence switching by light irradiation, as well as acid/base stimuli. The switching of fluorescence was carried out by modulation of photoinduced electron transfer (PET) and energy transfer mechanisms. Feasibility of the PET process was further corroborated by calculating Gibb's free energy following the Rehm-Weller equation as well as by computational calculations. The molecule showed visible-light (400 nm)-triggered photocyclization, which was further validated by its congeners with various electron-donating as well as electron-withdrawing substituents. The multifunctional fluorescence switching capability of the compound was utilized to develop a complex logic gate, where UV light, visible light, acid, and base were used as external stimuli as input function. The compounds showed a substitution-dependent fluorescence switching ratio, where the 4-benzonitrile-based compound had the highest fluorescence switching ratio among all congeners (4-benzonitrile, phenyl, aniline, and anisole) and was utilized to generate photochromic and fluorescent patterns and write secret code.

articles.title: Switching between semaglutide and tirzepatide in obesity management: an expert-consensus framework for approximate clinical efficacy-matched switching doses.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Currently, there are no available guidelines for switching from semaglutide to tirzepatide, since the mechanisms of action and pharmacokinetics differ, thus posing a challenge for continuous treatment of obesity.

AREAS COVERED: A narrative review of PubMed, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov (to May 2026) evaluated trials and cohorts comparing semaglutide (0.25-7.2 mg) and tirzepatide (2.5-15 mg). We synthesized indirect treatment comparisons to outline dose-response relationships and develop approximate efficacy‑matched switching dose bands.

EXPERT OPINION: Estimation of clinical efficacy-matched switching doses is more practical than mandatory lowest-dose initiation, which naturally risks a 'therapeutic gap' and subsequent weight regain. Until prospective switching trials validate exact conversions, clinicians should utilize the proposed equivalence bands and the five-step clinical decision algorithm to guide seamless transitions, titrating doses every 4-8 weeks based on individual tolerability and metabolic outcomes.

articles.title: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis: From Genetics to Management.
articles.journal: Seminars in respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM) is a rare multisystem disease that exemplifies how sustained investigation can transform both biological understanding and clinical management. LAM is diagnosed almost exclusively in women, typically during the reproductive years, consistent with an important role for hormonal influences in disease activity. The disease is characterized by diffuse cystic lung remodeling that can lead to progressive loss of lung function and, in severe cases, respiratory failure. Once viewed primarily as an unusual smooth muscle-like proliferation, LAM is now considered a low-grade metastasizing neoplasm characterized by heterogeneous disease-cell states that contribute to remodeling of the lung parenchyma and interact dynamically with stromal, lymphatic, immune, metabolic, and hormonal cues. Although the anatomical origin of LAM cells remains debated and continues to be an active area of research, sporadic and tuberous sclerosis complex-associated LAM (S-LAM and TSC-LAM, respectively) share a central molecular mechanism: biallelic inactivation of TSC1 or TSC2, which disrupts the TSC1-TSC2 protein complex and results in constitutive activation of mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1). This mechanistic insight provided the rationale for mTORC1 inhibition with sirolimus, which has transformed disease management by stabilizing lung function and reducing disease burden in many patients. In parallel, serum vascular endothelial growth factor-D has emerged as a clinically useful biomarker supporting noninvasive diagnosis and the assessment of disease burden and treatment response. Yet current therapies are not curative, and LAM cells persist despite mTORC1 inhibition. Continued advances in single-cell biology, genomic studies, hormonal and metabolic regulation, mechanistic dissection of disease-cell states, immune-stromal interactions, and biomarker discovery are now reshaping LAM as a model of precision medicine for rare neoplastic diseases. These efforts may guide rational combination therapies aimed not only at controlling disease progression but also, ultimately, at eliminating persistent LAM cells.

articles.title: The effect of renal denervation on blood pressure in patients with chronic kidney disease (RDN-CKD Study): Results of a multicentre, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled and blinded investigator-initiated trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular ultrasound renal denervation (uRDN) offers the opportunity to modulate sympathetic nervous system activity, thereby lowering blood pressure (BP) and potentially improving or stabilizing renal outcomes.

OBJECTIVE: We hypothesized that in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 3 and uncontrolled hypertension, endovascular ultrasound-based RDN will lower BP after 6 months.

METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled, blinded, clinical trial, investigated the effects of uRDN or sham in patients with CKD stage 3 and uncontrolled hypertension. The primary and secondary endpoints were changes in ambulatory BP (ABP) and office BP at 6 months. The study was prematurely stopped due to slow enrollment.

RESULTS: Twenty subjects (uRDN: N  = 10, sham: N  = 10) completed the 6-month visit. At 6 months, the sham-corrected change from baseline in 24 h systolic ABP was -5.60 mmHg (95% CI -10.7, -0.54 mmHg; P  = 0.170). The sham corrected change from baseline in 24-h diastolic ABP was -5.90 mmHg (95% CI -9.25, -2.55; P  = 0.035) and from baseline daytime ABP -6.85 mmHg (95% CI -10.6, -3.08; P  = 0.030). Sensitivity analysis restricting the analysis to those patients who were fully adherent to medication ( N  = 7 in each group) found a sham-corrected change from baseline 24-h diastolic ABP of -5.71 mmHg (95% CI -9.40, -2.03; P  = 0.053) at 6 months. Based on the composite endpoint of 24 h ABP and office BP for systolic/diastolic BP, a win ratio of 1.71 (95% 1.26-2.34; P  = 0.014) was found for systolic BP and a win ratio of 4.59 (95% CI 2.94-7.16, P  < 0.001) was found for diastolic BP, indicating significant changes in BP following RDN. Estimated glomerular filtration rate remained stable over 6 months, with no difference between the groups. There were no safety signals associated with uRDN.

CONCLUSIONS: This prospective randomized, sham controlled, blinded trial in patients with uncontrolled hypertension and CKD was prematurely stopped, resulted in small number of patients and we did not find a statistically significant effect on systolic BP, whereas a consistent reduction in diastolic BP following uRDN was observed. These data should guide the design of a larger confirmatory trial in patients with CKD.

articles.title: Acute angiotensin type 1 receptor blockade restores intracranial cerebral compliance in renovascular hypertension with high sodium intake.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute intravenous (i.v.) losartan, an angiotensin type 1 receptor (AT1R) antagonist, normalizes elevated mean arterial pressure (MAP) and intracranial pressure (ICP) and improves brain compliance in renovascular hypertensive rats (two-kidney, one-clip; 2K1C). However, central losartan fails to alter blood pressure in 2K1C rats that voluntarily consume hypertonic saline, a normally aversive solution. We therefore tested whether systemic losartan also would reduce blood pressure (BP) in 2K1C rats given ad libitum access to 0.3 M NaCl (2K1C_Na) and examined its effects on ICP and intracranial cerebral compliance (ICC).

METHODS: Male Holtzman rats underwent left renal artery clipping to induce renovascular hypertension. Cardiovascular parameters were recorded in awake or anaesthetized animals, and water and sodium intake, serum (SNa), and cerebrospinal fluid (CSFNa) sodium concentrations were measured.

RESULTS: Hypertensive rats exhibited greater water intake than SHAM_Na, and 2K1C_Na rats consumed large amounts of 0.3 M NaCl. Although SNa and CSFNa did not differ among groups, CSFNa was higher than SNa in 2K1C_Na rats. Intravenous losartan (10 mg/kg of body weight) significantly reduced MAP and ICP in 2K1C rats but not in 2K1C_Na animals. Following hexamethonium (30 mg/kg of body weight), MAP and ICP decreased in both 2K1C_Na and SHAM_Na rats. Notably, losartan improved brain compliance in 2K1C_Na rats despite no significant changes in MAP or ICP.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate that acute AT1R blockade enhances ICC independently of unchanged MAP in renovascular hypertension with high sodium intake, suggesting a potential neuroprotective role of losartan regardless of ICP and MAP levels.

articles.title: History of hypertension is associated with improved survival in patients with nonischemic etiology of heart failure and reduced ejection fraction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension (HTN) is a common comorbidity in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), yet its prognostic significance remains complex.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between HTN and all-cause mortality in patients with HFrEF, stratified by ischemic and nonischemic etiologies.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 11 242 patients with HFrEF treated between January 2009 and October 2025 at a national tertiary referral center. Patients were categorized according to ischemic vs. nonischemic etiology. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models, with multivariable adjustment for baseline characteristics.

RESULTS: HTN was present in 6992 patients (62%), and 6963 (63%) had ischemic heart disease (IHD). During a median follow-up of 5.0 years, 4952 patients (44%) died. Crude mortality was higher among hypertensive patients (46% vs. 41%, P  < 0.001). In univariate analysis, HTN was associated with increased mortality risk (HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.17-1.30, P  < 0.001). However, after multivariable adjustment, HTN was associated with a reduction in mortality (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.87-0.97, P  = 0.004). Stratified analysis demonstrated that this protective association was confined to patients without IHD (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.77-0.92, P  < 0.001), while no significant association was observed in those with IHD (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.92-1.06).

CONCLUSION: In patients with HFrEF, HTN is associated with reduced mortality only in those with nonischemic etiology.

articles.title: Insulin resistance in the adipose tissue is associated with cardiac mortality: the Hiroshima study on glucose metabolism and cardiovascular diseases.
articles.abstract:
