These comprised one prospective study and eight case reports involving 21 patients and 33 titanium implants, 20 of which were diagnosed as titanium hypersensitivity cases based on skin testing, immunological assays, histological or immunohistochemical analysis, or clinical symptoms. In 17 cases, implant removal was required, whereas three were managed by abutment replacement.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite the limited evidence, current data indicate that titanium hypersensitivity is rare but clinically relevant. Titanium micro-particles often originating from early mechanical wear may act as immunological co-factors in susceptible patients, underscoring the need for standardized and sensitive diagnostic protocols to support early and accurate identification.

articles.title: Fulminant myocarditis: outcome predictors in an international cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Fulminant myocarditis (FM) is a complex clinical syndrome characterized by acute myocardial inflammation and cardiogenic shock. Evidence on long-term outcomes, mortality risk factors, and targeted treatment options remains limited.

METHODS: This retrospective analysis included consecutive adult patients admitted for FM between January 2012 and November 2022 at 26 European tertiary centres. According to endomyocardial biopsy (EMB) findings, patients were categorized as lymphocytic (LM), eosinophilic (EM), necrotizing eosinophilic (NEM), and giant-cell myocarditis (GCM) for the main analyses. Patients with inconclusive histopathology and those who did not undergo EMB were analysed separately. Primary outcomes were in-hospital and 1-year mortality. Multivariable logistic regression models were employed as generalized linear models to analyse the association of prespecified risk factors with mortality. Estimated associations are reported as odds ratios, generalized marginal effects, and adjusted prediction plots.

RESULTS: A total of 271 patients [median age 43 years (interquartile range: 33-55 years), 58% male] were included in the analysis, of whom 146 fulfilled histopathologic criteria of LM (n = 99), EM (n = 18), NEM (n = 3), or GCM (n = 26). In the remaining 125 cases, EMB was inconclusive (n = 48) or not performed (n = 77). While there were no significant differences in cardiac arrest rate, admission Simplified Acute Physiology Score (SAPS) II, ventricular function, initial pH, and liver and kidney function parameters between histopathologic subgroups, the use of immunosuppressive medications and need for organ replacement varied. In the overall population, in-hospital and 1-year mortality were 31% and 34%, respectively. The highest 1-year mortality rate was observed among patients with GCM (LM: 25%, EM: 28%, NEM: 33%, GCM: 54%, P = .04). Patients who survived to discharge had an excellent functional outcome and long-term recovery of ventricular function. In total, 17 patients (6%) received a heart transplant during follow-up. Older age, lower pH, and histopathologic diagnosis of GCM were independently associated with in-hospital and 1-year mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: In-hospital mortality among patients with FM remains high. Age, pH, and histopathological findings may serve as prognostic markers to identify high-risk patients and to guide treatment strategies. Long-term outcomes are excellent among those who survive to discharge.

articles.title: Discontinuation of renin-angiotensin system inhibitors before non-cardiac surgery: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The best management approach for renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibitor use before surgery is controversial. Some studies have suggested that continuation could increase the risk of clinically significant peri-operative hypotension and, thus, organ injury. By contrast, others believe that withholding them significantly increases the risk of severe hypertension and heart failure. To determine the most effective strategy, this systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials compared discontinuation vs continuation of RAS inhibitors in patients undergoing non-cardiac and non-vascular surgeries.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) databases were searched for randomized controlled trials that compared discontinuation vs continuation of RAS inhibitors in patients undergoing non-cardiac and non-vascular surgery.

RESULTS: Five randomized controlled trials (n = 10 773 patients; 5388 randomized to discontinuation) were included. Discontinuation of an RAS inhibitor probaby reduced peri-operative hypotension (27.66% vs 34.06%; risk ratio [RR] 0.81, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.73-0.89; moderate certainty). The evidence is very uncertain about effects on peri-operative hypertension (9.46% vs 8.05%; RR 1.38, 95% CI 0.66-2.89; very low certainty). For major clinical outcomes, discontinuation suggested little to no difference in acute kidney injury (10.45% vs 10.69%; RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.66-1.45; low certainty), acute heart failure (5.38% vs 5.32%; RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.76-1.31; low certainty), myocardial infarction (1.22% vs 1.00%; RR 1.19, 95% CI 0.60-2.39; low certainty), stroke (0.42% vs 0.40%; RR 1.04, 95% CI 0.56-1.93; low certainty), and arrhythmias (1.80% vs 1.40%; RR 1.28, 95% CI 0.69-2.38; low certainty).

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that discontinuation of RAS inhibitors is likely to reduce peri-operative hypotension in patients undergoing non-cardiac, non-vascular surgery, but the evidence is very uncertain about effects on peri-operative hypertension and major clinical outcomes.

articles.title: The hypoxia, lactate and lactylation axis in lung disease: A metabolic and epigenetic framework.
articles.abstract: Hypoxia accompanies diverse pulmonary diseases and can promote glycolytic reprogramming and lactate accumulation. Lactate serves as a metabolic fuel and signalling molecule and can supply substrates for protein lysine lactylation. These activities are related but experimentally distinct. Here, we evaluate a hypoxia, lactate and lactylation framework across pulmonary hypertension, lung cancer, pulmonary fibrosis, acute lung injury, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and asthma. We distinguish studies that manipulate oxygen availability and measure downstream metabolic and lactylation responses from those that demonstrate lactate signalling or lactylation without establishing hypoxia as the initiating event. We assess evidence for individual mechanisms according to human validation, biochemical resolution and the specificity of in vivo interventions. This comparison identifies substantial gaps between an observed metabolic sequence and proof that a particular lactylation event mediates disease. We also examine how protein lactylation intersects with RNA-modifying enzymes and DNA-repair machinery, while recognizing that direct nucleic-acid lactylation remains unvalidated. Potential interventions range from lactate production and transport to lactylation regulators, but current agents frequently alter metabolism or other protein acylations. The framework therefore provides a basis for testing how oxygen stress influences pulmonary pathology rather than evidence for a uniformly established causal pathway or a clinically validated therapeutic class.

articles.title: Additional value of optical coherence tomography-fractional flow reserve for the optimization of percutaneous coronary intervention.
articles.journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) optimization remains largely driven by intravascular imaging, potentially leading to overtreatment of functionally irrelevant findings.

OBJECTIVES: To compare the impact of optical coherence tomography (OCT), angiography-derived fractional flow reserve (FFRangio), and the integration of imaging and physiology (OCT-FFR) on post-PCI optimization strategies.

METHODS: Among patients included in the AQVA-I and II trials, we selected those receiving post-PCI OCT (n = 79). Physiology reconstruction based on OCT traces was obtained in 76 OCT runs. One operator, blinded to the post-PCI optimization procedural plan and to final PCI result, planned the procedure according to FFRangio, OCT and OCT-FFR. The primary endpoint was the rate of any additional post-PCI optimization maneuver. Secondary endpoints included type of optimization strategy and pairwise differences between modalities.

RESULTS: Among 79 patients, 76 had complete triplet data. The rate of any additional post-PCI optimization was highest with OCT (33/76, 43.4%), followed by OCT-FFR (26/76, 34.2%) and lowest with FFRangio (5/76, 6.6%) (overall p < 0.001). The overall rate of any additional maneuver was not significantly different between OCT and OCT-FFR (absolute paired difference 2.6%; adjusted p = 0.500). Recommendations for edge dissection stenting, post-dilation for stent underexpansion, and post-dilation for malapposition were identical between OCT and OCT-FFR. In contrast, additional stenting of adjacent segments was reduced with OCT-FFR compared with OCT (4/76 [5.3%] vs 12/76 [15.8%]) and was recommended at the same rate as with FFRangio (4/76 [5.3%]).

CONCLUSIONS: OCT guidance is associated with a higher rate of post-PCI optimization maneuvers compared with FFRangio, reflecting its sensitivity to morphological abnormalities. Integration of functional assessment through OCT-FFR significantly reduces additional stenting in segments defined as 5 mm proximal and distal to the stent edges, while preserving treatment of clinically relevant mechanical complications.

articles.title: Cardiac Cirrhosis Associated With Valvular Heart Disease and Intracardiac Shunting.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac cirrhosis results from chronic hepatic congestion secondary to right-sided heart failure, causing sinusoidal injury and progressive fibrosis. Its presentation can mimic primary hepatic cirrhosis, creating diagnostic uncertainty.

CASE SUMMARY: A 41-year-old woman with mitral valve prolapse presented with abdominal distention, dyspnea, and edema, with hepatojugular reflux and a holosystolic apical murmur. B-type natriuretic peptide was elevated with normal liver enzymes. Imaging suggested cirrhosis with ascites, but echocardiography revealed severe mitral regurgitation and a large secundum atrial septal defect with right-sided enlargement. Right heart catheterization confirmed elevated right-sided pressures with left-to-right shunting. Paracentesis showed a low serum-ascites albumin gradient and high protein. She was started on diuretics and referred for valve repair and atrial septal defect closure.

DISCUSSION: Despite imaging suggesting liver disease, labs, examination, and ascitic fluid analysis directed the diagnosis toward a cardiac etiology. Hepatic dysfunction may reverse after correcting the underlying cardiac cause.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Consider cardiac causes of ascites even when imaging suggests cirrhosis. Work-up should include labs, echocardiography, ascites analysis, and right heart catheterization.

articles.title: Swirling vectors: The myocardial substrate of the precordial swirl pattern in anterior myocardial infarction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The electrocardiogram reflects the vectorial summation of myocardial injury, yet the mechanisms underlying some myocardial infarction (MI) patterns remain uncertain. We hypothesized that the precordial swirl pattern, traditionally attributed to LAD occlusion proximal to the first septal (S1) branch, may instead reflect an interaction between transmural and subendocardial injury.

METHODS: We analyzed 105 prospectively enrolled patients with first anterior ST-elevation MI treated with successful primary percutaneous coronary intervention and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) 3-7 days later. The precordial swirl phenotype was defined as ST elevation in V1-V2 with ST depression in V5 and/or V6. Segmental late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) transmurality, edema, LAD occlusion relative to S1, and continuous lateral ST deviation were analyzed.

RESULTS: Twenty-two patients (21.0%) had the phenotype. Median patient-level mean LGE transmurality was lower (33.3% [30.8-40.6] vs 39.6% [33.3-46.9]; P = 0.008), and the proportion of involved segments with <50% transmural LGE was higher (71.4% [55.6-87.5] vs 55.6% [40.0-66.7]; P = 0.003). Proximal-to-S1 occlusion was similar (36.4% vs 36.6%; P = 1.000). More negative V5-V6 ST deviation correlated with lower LGE transmurality (ρ = 0.310; P = 0.002) but not basal-mid septal LGE burden (ρ = 0.096; P = 0.341). After adjustment for infarct size, sex, and hypertension, the association with the fraction of segments exhibiting ≥50% transmural LGE persisted (β = -10.89 percentage points; P = 0.039).

CONCLUSIONS: Precordial swirl was associated with less transmural LGE, without detectable enrichment for proximal-to-S1 occlusion or greater septal injury, although moderate anatomical differences cannot be excluded. These findings are compatible with a contribution from heterogeneous transmural injury to the surface ST field.

articles.title: Reply to "From Pharmacovigilance to Whole-Person Care: The Urgent Case for Integrating Mental Health into Hepatology".
Reply to correspondence on "Outcomes of oral antidiabetic drugs in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: a nationwide target trial emulation study".
Correspondence to Letter to the Editor on "Disentangling Combustible-Cigarette Cessation From Noncombustible Tobacco Use in Steatotic Liver Disease".

Correspondence to editorial 2 on "Dynamic transitions in steatotic liver disease subtypes and risk of liver-related events: a nationwide cohort study".
Targeting PDGFRβ from radiopharmacy to nuclear medicine: Translational implementation of [68Ga]Ga-ATH001 PET/CT at an academic center.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Positron emission tomography (PET) enables non-invasive whole-body assessment of molecular biomarkers and is particularly valuable for evaluating heterogeneous diseases such as cancer. Platelet-derived growth factor receptor beta (PDGFRβ) is a stromal biomarker expressed on activated pericytes and fibroblasts that contributes to tumour remodelling, vascular regulation and therapeutic resistance. This study describes the translational implementation of the PDGFRβ-targeting PET tracer [68Ga]Ga-ATH001, from GMP-compliant radiopharmaceutical development to its first reported oncology application in patients with liver tumours.

METHODS: A GMP-compliant automated synthesis of [68Ga]Ga-ATH001 was established using a ModularLab PharmTracer synthesizer and validated for clinical use. The tracer was prospectively implemented in the IMAGINE-1 study (EU CT 2025-522290-11-00). PET imaging included dynamic liver acquisition immediately after injection, followed by whole-body PET/CT imaging and delayed liver scans to assess tracer biodistribution, tumour uptake and tracer kinetics.

RESULTS: [68Ga]Ga-ATH001 was successfully translated into clinical production using an automated in-house synthesis process, achieving a decay-corrected radiochemical yield of 51.9 ± 0.7 %, radiochemical purity of 97 %, radiochemical stability of 96.3 ± 0.5 % after 2 h at room temperature and apparent molar activity of 47.2 ± 1.6 GBq/µmol at EOS. Three consecutive production runs assessed reproducibility; a fourth batch served as a microbiological worst-case challenge and was excluded from the assessment. PET/CT imaging in three patients with colorectal liver metastases showed SUVpeak tumour-to-background ratios of 1.5 to 1.8 at 60 min after injection.

CONCLUSION: GMP-compliant production enabled the first reported oncology application of [68Ga]Ga-ATH001 in patients with liver tumours. The ongoing phase 1 IMAGINE-1 study will further evaluate its clinical potential.

EU TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials Information system: CTIS, EU CT 2025-522290-11-00, Registered 29 September 2025, IMAGINE-1 | 2025-522290-11-00 | CTIS.eu.

articles.title: ISLES'24: Final stroke infarct prediction with multimodal imaging and clinical data. Where do we stand?
articles.abstract: Accurate estimation of brain infarction (i.e., irreversibly damaged tissue) is critical for guiding treatment decisions in acute ischemic stroke. Reliable infarct prediction informs key clinical interventions, including the need for patient transfer to comprehensive stroke centers, the potential benefit of additional reperfusion attempts during mechanical thrombectomy, decisions regarding secondary neuroprotective treatments, and, ultimately, prognosis of clinical outcomes. This work introduces the Ischemic Stroke Lesion Segmentation (ISLES) 2024 challenge, which focuses on the prediction of final infarct volumes from pre-interventional acute stroke imaging and clinical data. ISLES'24 provides a comprehensive, multimodal setting where participants can leverage all clinically and practically available data - including full acute CT imaging, sub-acute follow-up MRI, and structured clinical information - across a train set of N=150 cases. On the hidden test set (N=98), the top-performing model, a multimodal nnU-Net-based architecture, achieved a Dice score of 0.285 ± 0.213 and an absolute volume difference of 21.2 ± 37.2 mL, underlining the significant challenges posed by this task and the need for further advances in multimodal learning. This overview of the ISLES'24 challenge offers two primary contributions: first, it provides a standardized, clinically realistic benchmark for post-treatment infarct prediction, built on a comprehensive, open, and multimodal longitudinal stroke imaging dataset; second, it provides insights into the strengths and limitations of current algorithms and delineates key research directions to guide the development of next-generation infarct prediction models.

articles.title: Multivessel Assessment by Angiography-Derived Index of Microcirculatory Resistance in Patients With Nonobstructive Coronary Artery Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current guidelines recommend testing for coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) in the left anterior descending coronary artery, and it is unclear whether multivessel assessment can improve the diagnostic yield and prognostic value of CMD.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic implications of multivessel CMD assessment using angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance (angio-IMR) in patients with nonobstructive coronary artery disease (NOCAD).

METHODS: Angio-IMR was measured in all 3 major coronary arteries in 439 patients with NOCAD. Single-vessel assessment was defined as angio-IMR measurement in the left anterior descending coronary artery only. Multivessel assessment was defined as angio-IMR measurement in all 3 major coronary arteries. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events, comprising a composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and hospitalization for heart failure.

RESULTS: Multivessel assessment identified more patients with CMD than single-vessel assessment (46.7% vs 24.1%; P < 0.001). During a median follow-up period of 4.3 years, an increased number of vessels with CMD was associated with a higher risk for major adverse cardiovascular events after adjustment for diabetes mellitus, smoking, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and history of myocardial infarction (adjusted HR: 1.963 per vessel; 95% CI: 1.513-2.548; P < 0.001). Multivessel assessment showed superior prognostic performance compared with single-vessel assessment when added to a clinical risk factor model (area under the curve: 0.751 vs 0.707; P = 0.034).

CONCLUSIONS: Multivessel assessment by angio-IMR improved the diagnostic yield of CMD and added incremental prognostic information compared with single-vessel assessment in patients with NOCAD.

articles.title: Reinitiation of Optimal Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy After Coronary Bypass Grafting in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction.
Nurses' infection prevention and control observations, compliance with standard precautions, and associated factors: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nurses' infection prevention and control (IPC) practices influence infection transmission, and their observations of others' practices may be associated with their own compliance with standard precautions. This study aimed to describe nurses' IPC observations and standard precautions compliance, examine their relationship, and identify associated characteristics.

METHODS: This descriptive cross-sectional study included 335 nurses from four clinical departments of a city hospital (November 2025-March 2026). Data were collected using the Nurses' Infection Prevention and Control Observation Questionnaire (NIPCOQ; higher scores indicate more frequent observation of poor practices) and the Compliance with Standard Precautions Scale (CSPS-T) and analyzed using non-parametric tests and multiple linear regression with robust standard errors.

RESULTS: Mean NIPCOQ and CSPS-T scores were 27.56 ± 9.89 and 14.16 ± 3.40, respectively, and were moderately and inversely correlated (ρ = -0.323, P < .001). Working in intensive care (vs surgery; B = -3.30, 95% CI -6.49 to -0.58) was associated with less frequent, and 6-10 years of experience (vs 0-5; B = 3.21, 95% CI 0.28 to 6.31) with more frequent, observation of poor practices. High school and associate degree graduates reported higher compliance than bachelor's degree holders. Each model explained about 5% of the variance.

DISCUSSION: Nurses who less frequently observed poor IPC practices reported better compliance, although the direction of this association cannot be determined. Individual characteristics explained little variation; organizational factors such as workload, staffing, and safety culture should be examined in multicenter studies.

articles.title: Effects of Cognitive Orientation to Daily Occupational Performance (CO-OP) Intervention on Executive Functioning for Activities of Daily Living in Patients With Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: Hong Kong journal of occupational therapy : HKJOT
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine the effects of the Cognitive Orientation to Daily Occupational Performance (CO-OP) intervention on executive functioning to promote the performance of activities of daily living in patients with stroke using a randomized controlled trial.

METHODS: Thirty-eight patients with stroke who met the inclusion criteria were randomly assigned to either an experimental (n = 19) or a control (n = 19) group using a computer-generated randomization program. The experimental group received the CO-OP intervention, whereas the control group received conventional occupational therapy. Both interventions were delivered over 12 sessions, 5 times per week, with each session lasting 60 min. The Executive Function Performance Test - Korean version, Canadian Occupational Performance Measure, Performance Quality Rating Scale, Korean version of the Modified Barthel index, and Korean version of the Instrumental Activities of Daily Living Scale were administered for pre- and post-intervention assessments.

RESULTS: Both groups showed significant improvements in executive function, occupational performance, and activities of daily living following the interventions (p < .001). However, when comparing the magnitude of change between the two groups, the experimental group demonstrated significantly greater improvements across all measures (p < .05, p < .01, p < .001). These findings indicate that the CO-OP intervention led to statistically greater enhancement than conventional occupational therapy.

CONCLUSION: This study provides evidence that the CO-OP approach in occupational therapy can effectively improve executive function, occupational performance, and activities of daily living in patients with stroke. Therefore, the CO-OP intervention, as a client-centered and evidence-based approach, may be a valuable therapeutic method in future clinical practice.

articles.title: Preliminary insights into the association between platelet indices and uterine inflammatory status in cyclic mares.
articles.abstract: Endometritis is a major cause of subfertility in mares and is characterized by uterine inflammation and impaired uterine clearance. Platelets contribute to inflammation, immune regulation and tissue remodeling, and platelet (PLT) indices have emerged as readily available biomarkers of inflammatory conditions; however, their association with endometritis in mares remains poorly understood. This study evaluated the relationship between PLT indices and uterine inflammatory status in cyclic mares. Seventeen cyclic mares were classified into healthy (n = 10) and endometritis (n = 7) groups based on cytological evidence of endometrial inflammation and ultrasonographic detection of intrauterine fluid accumulation. Uterine inflammatory status was characterized by endometrial cytology and ultrasonographic findings, including intrauterine fluid accumulation and endometrial edema. PLT indices were measured using an automated hematology analyzer (ADVIA® 2120i), and plasma estradiol (E2) and progesterone (P4) concentrations were determined. Group comparisons were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple testing. Mares with endometritis showed significantly higher PLT count, plateletcrit (PCT), mean platelet volume (MPV), platelet large cell ratio (P-LCR), platelet distribution width (PDW), mean platelet mass (MPM), platelet component distribution width (PCDW) and platelet mass distribution width (PMDW) than healthy mares. All significant differences remained after correction and exhibited large to very large effect sizes. In addition, mares with endometritis showed higher plasma E2 concentrations and lower P4 concentrations than healthy mares. These findings indicate that endometritis is associated with marked alterations in circulating PLT characteristics, particularly in indices related to PLT size, heterogeneity, and mass. PLT indices obtained from routine hematological analyses may represent accessible complementary biomarkers of uterine inflammatory status in mares.

articles.title: A Natural Occluder? Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation With Congenital Absence of the Left Atrial Appendage.
CODA-DTA: A context-guided model for predicting drug-target binding affinity in new compounds and targets.
articles.abstract: Accurate drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction is important for computational drug discovery, yet existing models often show limited generalization ability for new compounds or protein targets that were not included during model training. One important reason is that most DTA methods use the same prediction rule for all compound-target pairs, which is insufficient to capture the diverse and pair-specific nature of molecular interactions. To address this issue, this study proposes CODA-DTA (COntext-Driven Adaptive Drug-Target Affinity), a context-guided prediction model designed to adapt its prediction process to each specific compound-target pair. The proposed model combines a pretrained chemical sequence model, ChemBERTa-2, to represent compounds from SMILES strings, with a pretrained protein sequence model, ESM-2, to represent target amino acid sequences. It further uses a lightweight pair-guided matching module to adjust the compound-target comparison according to the current input pair. Experimental results on the Davis and KIBA datasets demonstrate that CODA-DTA achieves superior performance, particularly under cold-drug and cold-target settings. Component-removal experiments further verify the effectiveness of the proposed context-driven adaptive interaction mechanism and low-rank conditional parameterization. These results suggest that context-driven adaptive interaction learning is an effective strategy for robust cold-start DTA prediction and disease-oriented drug prioritization.

articles.title: Indexed versus non-indexed creatinine clearance for augmented renal clearance: potential implications for drug dosing.
18F-mFBG PET Detects Neuroblastoma Recurrence Prior to 123I-mIBG SPECT.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A high-risk stage M neuroblastoma patient suspected of residual disease in a T3-4 paraspinal soft tissue mass had no evidence of disease on MRI or 123I-mIBG SPECT/CT.

OBSERVATIONS: 18F-mFBG PET/CT performed in a clinical trial showed abnormalities in the upper and lower thoracic spine, lumbar spine, and pelvis. Two months later, the MRI was unchanged, and 123I-mIBG SPECT/CT showed only an equivocal upper thoracic spine focus. 123I-mIBG SPECT/CT and MRI at 4 months post-18F-mFBG showed positive findings in the thoracic spine consistent with neuroblastoma.

CONCLUSIONS: Follow-up confirmed that 18F-mFBG PET/CT identified neuroblastoma at least 2 months prior to 123I-mIBG and MRI.

articles.title: Tinostamustine-nivolumab therapy is associated with antigen-specific cellular and humoral immune responses in heavily pre-treated patients with advanced melanoma.
articles.abstract: ENIgMA is a phase IB trial (NCT03903458; SNCTP000003243) evaluating the safety and preliminary activity of the first-in-class alkylating deacetylase inhibitor tinostamustine in combination with nivolumab (3 mg/kg) in patients with predominantly immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-resistant, advanced melanoma. We conducted this longitudinal immune monitoring study in 15 of the 17 enrolled patients to characterize systemic immunologic changes associated with an immunomodulatory dose of tinostamustine. We have previously demonstrated that combination of tinostamustine with nivolumab was able to induce disease stabilization in 54% and confirmed partial responses in 23% of evaluable patients. Peripheral blood samples collected longitudinally during treatment were analysed by flow cytometry, serum antigen-specific IgG enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), and intracellular cytokine staining following ex vivo peptide stimulation. Longitudinal flow cytometric analyses demonstrated dynamic changes in peripheral immune subsets, including T cells, natural killer (NK) cells and monocytes, suggesting ongoing immune engagement during tinostamustine-nivolumab therapy. In progressors, elevated baseline lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels significantly and inversely correlated with circulating T cell frequencies, indicating distinct immune profiles associated with poor clinical outcome. Antigen-specific adaptive immune responses were detectable despite extensive prior treatment and high tumour burden. CD4+ T cell responses, particularly TNFα-associated responses directed against melanoma-associated antigens, represented the dominant cellular immune activation pattern. Additionally, treatment related increases in melanoma-associated antigen-specific IgG responses were also observed in several patients. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that immunomodulatory doses of tinostamustine in combination with nivolumab are linked with preserved adaptive immune competence and detectable cellular and humoral immune activation in heavily pre-treated patients with advanced melanoma.

articles.title: Electrocardiographic and Echocardiographic Markers of Atrial and Ventricular Remodeling Allow Identification of Cardiac Sarcoidosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac sarcoidosis (CS) is a rare but life-threatening manifestation of systemic sarcoidosis. Although positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging provide high diagnostic accuracy, they are unsuitable for first-line screening. Widely available modalities such as electrocardiography (ECG) and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) focusing only on ventricular abnormalities show limited sensitivity.

OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate whether a combined diagnostic model integrating ECG and TTE parameters, emphasizing atrial and ventricular remodeling, can accurately identify patients with CS.

METHODS: We prospectively included 252 consecutive patients with biopsy-proven sarcoidosis. CS was defined by characteristic findings on PET-CT or cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. A comprehensive set of atrial and ventricular ECG and TTE parameters was analyzed. Diagnostic models were constructed using univariable and multivariable logistic regression, and discriminative performance was assessed.

RESULTS: CS was identified in 37 (14.7%) patients. On ECG, prolonged P-wave duration, prolonged QRS duration, and reduced T-wave amplitude in lead aVR were independently associated with CS. On TTE, increased left atrial volume index, increased left ventricular end-diastolic diameter, and impaired left ventricular global longitudinal strain emerged as significant predictors. ECG- and TTE-based models showed comparable discrimination for CS identification (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve: 0.87 for both). A combined ECG/TTE model, driven primarily by QRS duration, left atrial volume index, and left ventricular global longitudinal strain, achieved the highest diagnostic performance (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve: 0.90).

CONCLUSIONS: An exploratory multimodal, noninvasive approach integrating atrial and ventricular ECG and TTE markers provides high diagnostic accuracy for identifying CS and may serve as a pragmatic screening and triage tool to guide referral for advanced cardiac imaging. Clinical Trial Registration DRKS00031557 on drks.de (German Clinical Trials Register).

articles.title: Conduction System Pacing in Pediatric Patients: Outcomes From a Multicenter International Cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP) may be advantageous in children requiring lifelong ventricular pacing, but long-term durability data are limited.

OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to evaluate the long-term preservation, durability, and safety of CSP in pediatric patients.

METHODS: This international, multicenter, retrospective study included consecutive patients aged ≤18 years undergoing His bundle pacing or left bundle branch area pacing at 9 experienced centers. The primary endpoint was long-term preservation of CSP.

RESULTS: Among 120 patients (mean age 12.6 ± 3.7 years), 68 (56.7%) had congenital atrioventricular block, 41 (34.2%) had congenital heart disease, and 12 (10.0%) underwent CSP for heart failure/cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). Acute CSP implantation, defined as achievement of His bundle pacing, left bundle branch pacing, or left ventricular septal pacing, was successful in 116 patients (96.7%). After a median follow-up of 24 months (Q1-Q3: 10-54 months), electrical lead performance remained stable. Among 101 patients with CSP at implantation and follow-up capture assessment, CSP was preserved in 95 (94.1%). Kaplan-Meier-estimated freedom from loss of CSP was 100.0% at 1 year and 98.2% (95% CI: 94.7%-100.0%) at 2 and 3 years. CSP lead-related complications occurred in 10 patients (8.3%), and reintervention was required in 9 (7.5%). In the CRT subgroup, left ventricular ejection fraction improved from 28.8% ± 9.4% to 46.8% ± 12.0% (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: CSP is a feasible, safe, and durable physiological pacing strategy in children, with excellent long-term CSP preservation and stable electrical performance despite ongoing somatic growth. CSP may also provide effective physiological resynchronization in pediatric patients requiring CRT.

articles.title: Ibrutinib-Induced Effusive Constrictive Pericarditis and Acute Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ibrutinib-associated pericardial disease is uncommon, and inflammatory effusive-constrictive pericarditis is rarely reported.

CASE SUMMARY: A 66-year-old man with recurrent chronic lymphocytic leukemia receiving ibrutinib presented with dyspnea and palpitations. Echocardiography showed a fibrinous circumferential pericardial effusion with constrictive physiology. Simultaneous right and left heart catheterization confirmed ventricular interdependence, and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated diffuse pericardial late gadolinium enhancement consistent with active inflammation. He developed atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. Ibrutinib was discontinued, and anti-inflammatory therapy, rate control, and anticoagulation were initiated. Follow-up imaging showed complete resolution of the effusion and constrictive physiology.

DISCUSSION: Multimodality imaging established the diagnosis and guided conservative management. Complete recovery after ibrutinib withdrawal and anti-inflammatory therapy supports a drug-related inflammatory mechanism and suggests that selected patients may avoid pericardiectomy.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Ibrutinib may rarely cause inflammatory effusive-constrictive pericarditis with atrial fibrillation. Multimodality imaging and multidisciplinary cardio-oncology care are critical for diagnosis and individualized management. Early recognition and medical therapy may reverse constrictive physiology and avoid pericardiectomy.

articles.title: Catastrophic Multivessel Coronary Thrombosis After Discontinuation of Antithrombotic Therapy in Adult-Onset Kawasaki Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kawasaki disease (KD) diagnosis in adulthood is often delayed and can lead to severe coronary sequelae.

CASE SUMMARY: A 23-year-old man who first developed clinical manifestations of KD at age 18 years developed a medium-sized coronary artery aneurysm because of delayed initial treatment. Antithrombotic therapy, including warfarin, was prescribed but later discontinued during follow-up. At age 23 years, he presented with acute myocardial infarction complicated by lethal ventricular arrhythmias requiring mechanical circulatory support. Emergency coronary angiography revealed concurrent thrombotic occlusions of the left anterior descending and right coronary arteries. Emergent percutaneous coronary intervention of both vessels restored coronary flow, resulting in favorable neurologic and clinical recovery.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights that interruption of antithrombotic therapy in patients with KD-related coronary aneurysms may precipitate catastrophic multivessel thrombosis.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Patients with persistent KD-related coronary artery aneurysms require follow-up and antithrombotic therapy tailored to thrombotic risk.

articles.title: Very Late Complete Heart Block After Cardiac Transplantation Presenting as Acute Decompensated Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complete atrioventricular (AV) block is an uncommon late complication after heart transplantation; in the denervated allograft, which depends on rate for output, it may present as heart failure rather than syncope.

CASE SUMMARY: A 61-year-old man developed complete AV block 22 years after biatrial transplantation, presenting with acute decompensated heart failure and preserved ejection fraction. Serial electrocardiograms over 5 years documented stepwise progression to complete AV block. After conventional septal fixation repeatedly failed, left bundle branch area pacing was delivered via the atrial port with a right ventricular backup lead on the ventricular port; symptoms and function improved at 6 months.

DISCUSSION: Very late allograft conduction disease is rarely documented longitudinally and is easily misattributed to rejection; physiological conduction system pacing was feasible despite failed conventional fixation.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Consider conduction disease in long-term transplant recipients presenting with heart failure, and use serial electrocardiographic surveillance to detect its gradual evolution.

articles.title: Leaflet Perforation During Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair: A Stepwise Dual-Device Strategy Leveraging Valve Geometry Modification.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe a stepwise dual-device bailout strategy for posterior leaflet perforation during mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair.

KEY STEPS: After a new high-velocity leaflet-body jet was identified, direct annular-side resealing was infeasible because tissue between the perforation and annular hinge was minimal. A first PASCAL ACE device was implanted lateral to the perforation to eliminate residual lateral mitral regurgitation and shorten the anteroposterior diameter, approximating the basal leaflet segments. A second device was advanced medially with a reduced opening angle to avoid posterior left ventricular wall interference and achieve deep near-annular sealing.

POTENTIAL PITFALLS: Perforation-associated jets may be mistaken for residual coaptation-line mitral regurgitation, and repeated regrasping may fail or worsen leaflet injury when annular-side tissue is insufficient.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: When direct resealing is not feasible, valve geometry modification with a first device may facilitate definitive sealing with a second device.

articles.title: Transcatheter Mitral Paravalvular Leak Closure With a Multifunctional Ventricular Septal Defect Occluder.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Paravalvular leak (PVL) after surgical mitral valve replacement is an uncommon but clinically significant complication. Redo surgery carries a high risk, making transcatheter closure a viable and less invasive alternative.

CASE SUMMARY: We report 2 cases of mitral PVL following prior surgical valve replacement who presented with signs and symptoms of heart failure. After echocardiographic evaluation, a transcatheter approach was undertaken to deploy a Konar-multifunctional (MF) ventricular septal defect (VSD) occluder under fluoroscopic guidance. Following the procedure, both patients showed significant clinical improvement with complete resolution of PVL.

DISCUSSION: This case series emphasizes the feasibility and favorable outcome of transcatheter closure using the Konar-MF VSD occluder, off-label as an alternative to redo surgery in high-risk surgical patients with mitral PVL. Larger studies are warranted to evaluate the safety and efficacy of this off-label approach across a broader patient population.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: New-onset symptoms of heart failure and hemolytic anemia even after years of surgical mitral valve replacement warrant careful and timely evaluation for PVLs. In select high-risk patients who are not ideal candidates for redo surgery, off-label use of the Konar-MF VSD occluder is a feasible alternative for closure of PVLs.

articles.title: Revisiting the Role of Chemotherapy in Advanced Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chemotherapy has been always considered scarcely or completely ineffective in the treatment of metastatic and progressive MTC.

CASE REPORT: We report the case of a 45-year-old man who underwent total thyroidectomy and lymphadenectomy in May 2023 for bilateral MTC with extrathyroidal extension and 2/23 metastatic lymph nodes. Germline and somatic RET genetic analysis were negative. From July 2023 to February 2024 tumour markers progressively increased and a 18F-DOPA PET/CT revealed metastases in the cervical region and mediastinal inlet. Therefore, cabozantinib was started, obtaining a partial response, but after 1 year of treatment disease progression at the cervicomediastinal level was documented, despite dosage increase. Thus, an off-label treatment with lenvatinib was started, achieving a transient stabilization. In October 2025, a further disease progression was diagnosed. The patient started off-label chemotherapy consisting of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) 400 mg/m2 intravenous (IV) bolus, followed by 5-FU 2400 mg/m2 as a 48-hour infusion, combined with dacarbazine 800 mg/m2 IV in 30 minutes, every 14 days for the first month and then every 21 days for the following months. Chemotherapy was very well tolerated. At the last visit, after 17 cycles, tumour markers returned to the normal range (CA 19-9 22.9 kU/L, CEA 2.5 μg/L) and PET/CT scanning showed a complete response.

CONCLUSION: In conclusion, this case shows that, although treatment with multikinase inhibitors is actually the first choice for advanced RET-wild-type MTC, conventional chemotherapy can be effective at least in some patients and should always be considered, especially in case of failure of other approaches.

articles.title: ATTEST 2027: A Framework for AI Transparency Tiered by Evidentiary Stakes.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is now being used across scientific research workflows, from data extraction and code generation to literature synthesis and manuscript drafting. Scientific journals and professional organizations agree that authors should disclose AI assistance. But disclosure that treats all AI use equally with a single generic declaration reveals little about the nature of AI's influence on evidence generation. Polishing grammar carries a different risk than extracting outcomes from clinical notes, classifying pathology, or making causal inference. We propose ATTEST (AI Transparency Tiered by Evidentiary Stakes), a framework that evaluates AI assistance by its consequences. ATTEST classifies AI use into eight broad categories of functions, each scored at one of four risk tiers (Low, Medium, High, Very High). The framework is operationalized by a declaration checklist that authors complete at submission. Within this tiered system, we propose minimum reporting standards by function, cross-cutting requirements, and obligations for reviewers and editors. The goal is to make AI's role in evidence generation transparent to readers, reviewers, and editors so they can evaluate the integrity of scientific findings.

articles.title: Pulmonary Artery Interventional Thrombectomy Stent System: Combined Application of Stent and Negative Pressure Aspiration.
articles.abstract: This protocol describes a pulmonary artery thrombectomy technique that combines stent deployment and negative pressure aspiration to achieve rapid thrombus removal and restore pulmonary arterial perfusion. Prolonged obstruction may lead to right heart dysfunction and hemodynamic instability. The pulmonary artery thrombectomy stent system provides a rapid approach to thrombus removal and restoration of pulmonary perfusion, thereby alleviating respiratory distress and hypoxemia while reducing pulmonary vascular resistance and right ventricular strain. This technique is applicable for patients with intermediate- to high-risk pulmonary embolism, particularly those with contraindications to thrombolysis. Preoperative computed tomography imaging revealed pulmonary artery emboli involving both the left and right pulmonary arteries and their branches. Following thrombectomy using the pulmonary artery interventional thrombectomy stent system, postoperative imaging confirmed complete clearance of the thrombi and full restoration of pulmonary artery blood flow.

articles.title: Clinical Evidence for Adding Chaiqin Chengqi Decoction to Acute Pancreatitis Care: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Trials.
articles.abstract: Chaiqin Chengqi Decoction (CQCQD) is used as an adjunctive treatment for acute pancreatitis, but its clinical benefit remains uncertain because available trials vary in intervention composition, outcome definitions, and methodological quality. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated randomized controlled trials comparing CQCQD plus conventional treatment with the same background regimen without CQCQD or with placebo. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, CNKI, Wanfang Data, and VIP Database were searched from inception through June 10, 2026. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Random-effects models generated risk ratios (RRs) or standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Nineteen trials involving 1,824 participants were included. Study-defined overall response favored adjunctive CQCQD (16 trials; RR = 1.21, 95% CI: 1.16-1.26; I2 = 0%). CQCQD was also associated with lower C-reactive protein (SMD = -2.55, 95% CI: -3.41 to -1.69), interleukin-6 (SMD = -1.76, 95% CI: -2.30 to -1.22), serum amylase (SMD = -2.22, 95% CI: -3.04 to -1.39), and Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II scores (SMD = -2.08, 95% CI: -3.36 to -0.80), and with a higher CD4+/CD8+ ratio (SMD = 1.41, 95% CI: 0.48-2.35). However, heterogeneity was substantial for all continuous outcomes, most trials were at high risk of bias, and GRADE certainty was low or very low. Patient-important outcomes, including mortality, persistent organ failure, major complications, and pain, were inconsistently reported and could not be reliably pooled. Overall, adjunctive CQCQD was associated with favorable short-term response, laboratory, and severity outcomes, but the available evidence does not establish reductions in mortality, persistent organ failure, or major complications. More rigorous multicenter trials using standardized CQCQD formulations and consistent patient-important endpoints are required.

articles.title: Dihydrotanshinone I in Paired Vemurafenib-Sensitive and Resistant A375 Melanoma Cells.
articles.abstract: Acquired resistance limits the response to vemurafenib in melanoma. This study investigated dihydrotanshinone I (DHT) in parental A375 cells and a vemurafenib-resistant derivative (A375R). An exploratory computational workflow combined target prediction, survival associations, tumor-versus-normal expression comparisons, dependency screening, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) Cox regression, and random survival forests. Heat shock protein 90 alpha family class A member 1 (HSP90AA1) and signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) were prioritized for cellular testing. Cellular thermal shift assays showed DHT-associated thermal stabilization, and combined small interfering RNA depletion produced greater phenotypic effects than single-target depletion. Eight drug combinations yielded Chou-Talalay combination indices of 0.520-0.940 in A375R cells. Transcriptional changes and lipid-peroxidation readouts were consistent with altered resistance-associated and oxidative-stress programs. Together, these findings support further investigation of HSP90AA1 and STAT3 in the response of resistant melanoma cells to DHT.

articles.title: Competing Endogenous Ribonucleic Acid Networks in Cervical Cancer: Mechanisms and Clinical Implications.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer (CC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women, with persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) representing its primary etiological factor. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), circular RNAs (circRNAs), and pseudogenes can function as competing endogenous RNAs (ceRNAs) by competing with messenger RNAs (mRNAs) for binding to microRNAs (miRNAs), thereby reducing miRNA-mediated repression of target mRNAs. This review categorizes the ceRNA axes reported in CC as oncogenic or tumor-suppressive and examines their convergence on major signaling pathways, including Wnt/β-catenin, phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/Akt, mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), Hippo, and Notch, together with the strength of the supporting evidence. The roles of these networks in prognosis, resistance to cisplatin and radiotherapy, and responses to bioactive compounds are also evaluated. Most reported axes are supported primarily by cell-line experiments, whereas absolute RNA quantification is frequently unavailable and patient-level validation remains limited. Accordingly, ceRNA networks represent potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets, although additional mechanistic and clinical evidence is required to establish their clinical applicability.

articles.title: Developing and Externally Validating Explainable Machine Learning for Elastography-Defined Steatotic Liver Disease.
articles.abstract: Explainable machine learning is widely applied to non-invasive detection of steatotic liver disease, but published pipelines are rarely tested against a properly specified regression comparator, rarely validated independently, and almost never examined for measurement artifact in the outcome label itself. This protocol addresses those gaps in a form that can be re-executed end-to-end on public data. The procedure uses the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2017 to March 2020 release for development and the August 2021 to August 2023 release as a frozen external validation set. Steps include verification of variable codes against the raw transport-file headers, cohort construction, recoding of skip-pattern missingness prior to multiple imputation, nested cross-validation with tuning confined to training folds, design-weighted performance estimation, paired-bootstrap comparison, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis with stability checks, and ten pre-specified sensitivity analyses. Representative results show that routine clinical data discriminate VCTE-defined steatosis at an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.843 and advanced fibrosis at 0.837, both of which were reproduced in external validation, and that these values greatly exceed those of FIB-4, which discriminated at 0.565. Gradient boosting did not outperform penalized logistic regression for steatosis and showed at most a modest advantage for fibrosis. A probe-selection test built into the protocol revealed that the XL elastography probe reads the controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) 22.9 dB/m higher than the M probe at equivalent body mass index, and that removing this coupling reduced steatosis discrimination from 0.843 to 0.810. The protocol applies to any NHANES prediction question and, with the weighting steps adapted, to other complex-survey datasets. Its distinguishing features are the artifact test, the cross-method explainability check, and full pre-specification of sensitivity analyses.

articles.title: Video-Based Micro-Teaching Protocol for Value Integration in Chinese Pre-Service Teacher Education: A Randomized Controlled Study.
articles.abstract: Integrating ideological-political, moral, and professional values into subject teaching requires pre-service teachers to translate educational principles into observable instructional actions. This randomized controlled study evaluated a value-integrated micro-teaching intervention against an active pedagogical comparison. At Yunnan Normal University, 102 final-year pre-service teachers were randomly assigned to two conditions, with 51 participants per condition. Both conditions followed a four-week sequence of baseline teaching, planning, first recorded teaching, timestamped video review, peer and mentor feedback, revision, and final assessment. The intervention linked selected values to subject objectives and observable actions; the comparison addressed explanation, learner engagement, and formative feedback. The primary outcome was Value-Integrated Teaching Performance, measured using a four-dimension 0-20 rubric. Overall Micro-Teaching Performance was assessed separately using a six-dimension 0-100 rubric. Ninety-six participants provided valid final assessments. Linear mixed-effects models used 198 available baseline and final records and adjusted for school stage and subject domain. The intervention produced greater improvement in Value-Integrated Teaching Performance, with an adjusted between-condition difference in change of 2.17 points (95% confidence interval (CI), 1.18-3.16; p < 0.001). Overall Micro-Teaching Performance also improved more in the intervention condition, with a difference in change of 3.94 points (95% CI, 1.69-6.19; p < 0.001). Complete-case analyses of covariance yielded consistent estimates. The combined value-focused instructional package improved immediate teaching-performance scores within the assessed micro-teaching setting. These findings concern task-specific instructional enactment rather than enduring changes in personal values or professional ethics.

articles.title: Genomic Features and Risk Factors of Carbapenem-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa Bloodstream Infections.
articles.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (CRPA) bloodstream infection is associated with high mortality and limited treatment options. This retrospective cohort study was conducted at a single Chinese hospital from January 2020 to January 2026 and included adult patients with P. aeruginosa bloodstream infection. Clinical data were extracted from the hospital information system, and whole-genome sequencing was performed on 48 CRPA isolates to determine multilocus sequence types, carbapenemase genes, and capsular serotypes. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression were used to identify factors associated with CRPA acquisition. Among 110 patients, 48 (43.6%) had CRPA bloodstream infection. Prior ICU stay within 1 month (adjusted OR = 5.67, 95% CI: 2.81-11.45, p < 0.001) and prior carbapenem exposure within 30 days (adjusted OR = 3.89, 95% CI: 1.92-7.88, p < 0.001) were independent risk factors for CRPA acquisition. ST-3757 was the predominant sequence type (39/48, 81.3%), KPC-2 was the predominant carbapenemase gene (32/48, 66.7%), and O11 was the most frequent serotype (12/48, 25.0%). All ST-3757 isolates shared pairwise average nucleotide identity above 98.5%, and phylogenetic analysis placed them in a single well-supported clade. These findings indicate that prior healthcare exposure and carbapenem use drive CRPA bloodstream infection in this setting and that an ST-3757-O11-KPC-2 lineage is locally epidemic, supporting targeted antimicrobial stewardship and genomic surveillance.

articles.title: A rare homozygous PPP1R15B variant in a child with diabetes, microcephaly, and growth failure.
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus can occur in patients who present with neurodevelopmental and systemic abnormalities, potentially indicating underlying syndromic monogenic forms. Autosomal dominant forms of monogenic diabetes are relatively well characterized compared with recessively inherited forms. Here, we present a case of a 17-year-old male patient with postnatal growth failure, microcephaly, motor and intellectual disability, bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, and insulin-dependent diabetes diagnosed at the age of 9 years, in whom a new homozygous variant in the PPP1R15B gene was identified. This gene plays a regulatory role in the cellular response to endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress. Variants in PPP1R15B can lead to prolonged ER stress, cellular dysfunction, and apoptosis, particularly in pancreatic β cells. To date, only three families with PPP1R15B variants have been reported. Our patient showed unique clinical features, including postnatal growth retardation and early-onset diabetes. This case highlights the importance of investigating monogenic causes in patients with syndromic diabetes and contributes to our understanding of the pathogenic role of ER stress-related mechanisms in such presentations.

articles.title: Cumulative barriers to healthcare access as a marker of health system failure: evidence from a national study of people with diabetes in Brazil.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate healthcare access barriers and their cumulative association with clinical and economic outcomes among Brazilians with diabetes, focusing on the primary care context and health inequalities.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A weighted survey (n = 1843) was conducted in 2024 using a structured questionnaire. The sample was weighted to match the Brazilian National Health Survey, ensuring representativeness of public health system users. A cumulative barrier score (0-8) was analyzed using Poisson regression adjusted for sociodemographic and clinical variables.

RESULTS: The primary barriers identified were difficulty scheduling appointments (47.4%), medication unavailability (42.6%), and lack of supplies (39.4%). The mean barrier score was 4.13 (standard deviation 2.80). A consistent dose-response pattern showed that a higher cumulative barrier burden was associated with increased emergency department visits, higher out-of-pocket expenditures, and a greater prevalence of chronic complications (adjusted prevalence ratio 1.05 per additional barrier; 95% confidence interval 1.04-1.07; p < 0.001). These impacts were more pronounced among low-income individuals and those with type 1 diabetes.

CONCLUSION: Healthcare access barriers are highly prevalent in Brazil and are cumulatively associated with adverse clinical and economic outcomes. This cumulative burden serves as a pragmatic marker for identifying high-risk individuals and informs public health strategies to reduce health inequalities and improve care delivery in primary care settings.

articles.title: Synthesis and preclinical evaluation of a novel 2-[18F]fluoropyridine-bearing rhodamine for myocardial perfusion imaging with PET.
articles.abstract: [18F]Rho6G-DEG-F is a rhodamine-based PET radiotracer for myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) that exhibits excellent first-pass myocardial extraction, persistent cardiac retention, and high heart : liver ratios in rats and pigs. However, in human volunteers, heart : liver contrast was suboptimal. The primary goals of this study were to design an [18F]Rho6G-DEG-F analogue of attenuated lipophilicity for radiolabelling via nucleophilic heteroaromatic 18F-fluorination ([18F]Rho6G-DEG-Py-F; [18F]6), and to evaluate [18F]6 in rats and mice. To that end, precursors bearing 2-nitro- (5) and 2-trimethylammonium triflate (8)- pyridine groups were prepared in overall yields of 48% and 29%, starting from rhodamine 6G; final purification did not require C18 chromatography. Manual standard radiofluorination conditions (TEA[18F]F/TEAHCO3/DMSO/160 °C/20 min) afforded a best decay-corrected radiochemical yield (DC-RCY) of 31% from 5 and 7% from 8. In the latter case, precursor and radiotracer were easily separated by HPLC (molar activity = 33 ± 8 GBq per µmol). Upon translation to an automated synthesizer, [18F]6 was obtained in DC-RCYs of 9.3% and 0.7% from 5 and 8 respectively; best molar activities were 50 and 144 GBq per µmol respectively. [18F]Rho6G-DEG-Py-F exhibited complete stability in rat and mouse serum over 120 min (37 °C). A radiometabolite assay in two rats showed differing metabolic profiles between sexes, but similar % intact tracer at 60 min (32-34%). Micro-PET imaging in rats demonstrated extended myocardial retention (SUV > 1.0 at 120 min), gradual liver washout, and high heart : liver ratios (3.7 in male, 2.5 in female at 120 min); however, similar experiments in mice revealed low heart uptake and rapid metabolism (SUV ∼ 0.3; heart : liver ratio = 1.0 at 120 min).

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of a self-expandable stent-based endobiliary radiofrequency ablation: A preclinical study.
articles.abstract: The temperature-controlled, bipolar self-expandable stent (SES)-based radiofrequency ablation (RFA) system represents a novel endobiliary RFA approach; however, its efficacy and safety must be verified before clinical application. The study aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of SES-RFA in a porcine common bile duct (CBD) model. Ablation ranges were investigated using ex vivo porcine liver according to radiofrequency energy and time. For the in vivo study, radiofrequency parameters were set at 20 W for a 20-mm electrode and 25 W for a 25-mm electrode at 70°C for 120 s. Twelve pigs underwent endoscopic-guided SES-RFA using either electrode (n = 6 each). Animals were randomly euthanized at 24 h or 2 weeks after SES-RFA (n = 3 per group). The RFA-treated CBDs were evaluated using cholangiography, cholangioscopy, hematology, histology, and immunohistochemistry. The SES-RFA system was successfully deployed and retrieved through-the-scope without device failure. All animals survived until the study endpoint without RFA-related adverse events, including ductal perforation, contrast leakage, or hematoma. Hepatobiliary levels of alkaline phosphatase, aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, and gamma-glutamyl transferase were significantly higher at 2 weeks than at 24 h post-SES-RFA (all p< 0.05). Ablation ranges and degree of mucosal damage, including collagen and TUNEL-positive deposition, were significantly increased at 2 weeks than at 24 h (all p< 0.05). The temperature-controlled bipolar SES-RFA system effectively and safely produced circumferential coagulative necrosis without ductal perforation in the porcine CBD. The system may be used for managing unresectable malignant biliary obstruction in anatomically challenging regions where conventional RFA is difficult to use.

articles.title: The decline of respiratory function in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis patients and the role of non-invasive ventilation.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a chronic neurodegenerative disease characterized by a poor prognosis, with an average survival of 3 to 5 years from symptom onset. Respiratory failure is the main cause of death, and non-invasive ventilation (NIV) is a cornerstone in the management of ALS patients. This single-center retrospective study was conducted at Siena University Hospital between 2010 and 2024 to analyze respiratory function parameters in ALS patients undergoing NIV, stratified by disease severity and followed over one year, to assess the relationship between lung function decline and the timing of NIV initiation. A total of 49 patients (29 males, 20 females; mean age 67±12 years) were enrolled, and 31 (63%) received NIV. Clinical and functional parameters, including forced vital capacity (FVC), pCO₂, respiratory symptoms at baseline, and longitudinal measurements of sitting FVC (FVCsit%), supine FVC (FVCsup%), and pCO₂, were collected and analyzed over time. Differences in FVC decline were observed according to the timing of NIV initiation. Among non-severe patients, those starting NIV at T0 showed a 22.5% reduction in FVC over a mean follow-up of 12.8±4.8 months. Patients initiating NIV at T2 exhibited a reported FVCsit decline of 26% (p=0.0488) and a survival of 51.3±50 months from NIV initiation, whereas those starting later (T3-T6) showed a greater decline (FVCsit decline 34%, p=0.0002) and shorter survival duration (15.7±28.6 months). These findings describe differences in respiratory function trajectories and observed survival among patients initiating NIV at different follow-up time points. However, the retrospective design, small sample size, baseline differences between groups, and potential confounding and survival-related selection bias limit causal interpretation. Further studies are needed to clarify the relationship between NIV initiation timing and clinical outcomes in ALS.

articles.title: Outcomes of SGLT2-inhibitor-induced euglycaemic diabetic ketoacidosis in a North Queensland intensive care unit: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Evidence on sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i)-associated euglycaemic diabetic ketoacidosis (EuDKA) in the intensive care unit (ICU) and its comparison with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is limited. This study aims to describe ICU characteristics, management and outcomes of SGLT2i-associated EuDKA, identify predictors of poorer outcomes and compare findings with T1DM-DKA. Single-centre retrospective cohort (2017-2023) of adults admitted to a Northern Queensland ICU. EuDKA was defined by plasma glucose <13.9 mmol/L plus ⩾1 of acidaemia, low bicarbonate, raised anion gap or ketonaemia, in patients with T2DM on SGLT2i. A comparator cohort comprised ICU admissions with T1DM-DKA. Demographics, precipitants, biochemistry, insulin therapy, and outcomes were extracted and analysed with non-parametric tests. Fourteen EuDKA and 31 T1DM-DKA admissions were included. EuDKA patients were older with more frequent comorbidities; First Nations Australians were over-represented. Presenting features were heterogeneous, with overlapping precipitants (commonly caloric restriction/fasting or intercurrent illness). Compared with T1DM-DKA, EuDKA had milder biochemical derangement and lower 24-h insulin dose but required longer insulin therapy and longer ICU length of stay; time to acidosis resolution was similar. In exploratory analyses, end-organ complications in type 2 diabetes were associated with longer ICU stay, while obesity and pre-admission insulin therapy were associated with prolonged acidosis duration. ICU-admitted SGLT2i-associated EuDKA differs clinically and in management from classical T1DM-DKA. Findings highlight diagnostic challenges, potential high-risk subgroups, and the need for prospective, multicentre studies to inform risk-based management in critical care.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of ustekinumab and vedolizumab in very early-onset inflammatory bowel disease: A multicenter study from the pediatric inflammatory bowel disease Porto Group of ESPGHAN.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to assess vedolizumab and ustekinumab efficacy and safety in patients with very-early onset inflammatory bowel disease (VEO-IBD).

METHODS: A retrospective study involving 29 European and North American sites affiliated with the IBD Porto Group of European Society for Paediatric Gastroenterology Hepatology and Nutrition. Clinical and laboratory data were collected from patients with VEO-IBD who commenced vedolizumab or ustekinumab before 6 years of age, between 2014 and 2024.

RESULTS: Ninety-six patients (60.4% females) were included (58 ulcerative colitis, 29 Crohn's disease, and 9 IBD-Unclassified). Median (Q1-Q3) age at diagnosis was 2.3 (0.4-4.2) years, 37 (38.5%) patients were diagnosed at age <2 years old. Thirty-seven (38.5%) patients received ustekinumab, 67 (69.7%) vedolizumab, and 11 (11.5%) both drugs. Median (Q1-Q3) follow-up time was 11 (6-26) and 14 (7-39) months for ustekinumab and vedolizumab, respectively. Eighty (84.2%) patients were previously treated with infliximab, 23 (24.2%) with adalimumab, and 20 (20.8%) with both. The median (Q1-Q3) time from diagnosis to vedolizumab and ustekinumab initiation was 15 (9-26) and 20 (11-36) months, respectively. Ustekinumab-treated patients achieved clinical remission in 24.3%, 51.4%, and 40.5% at end of induction, week 26, and week 52, with steroid-free remission in 18.9%, 45.9%, and 35.3%, respectively. Vedolizumab-treated patients achieved clinical remission in 29%, 47.5%, and 40.3%, with steroid-free clinical remission (SFCR) rates of 10.4%, 43.3%, and 37.3% at the same time points. Infectious adverse events were reported in 3 (8.3%) of ustekinumab-treated and 5 (7.6%) vedolizumab-treated patients, none severe.

CONCLUSIONS: Ustekinumab and vedolizumab demonstrated high therapeutic durability in patients with VEO-IBD; 1-year rates of SFCR were modest.

articles.title: Renal Vein and Inferior Vena Cava Thrombosis in Neonates With Adrenal Hemorrhage: Gray-Scale Clues Beyond Doppler.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal adrenal hemorrhage is usually followed sonographically to document evolution and exclude congenital adrenal masses. In some neonates, it may be the visible suprarenal component of renal vein and/or inferior vena cava thrombosis.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed neonates with sonographic adrenal hemorrhage and concomitant renal vein and/or inferior vena cava thrombosis identified through a 2015-2025 institutional database search. Medical records, radiology reports, ultrasound images, gray-scale and Doppler findings, venous involvement, and follow-up imaging were reviewed.

RESULTS: Eight neonates with sonographic adrenal hemorrhage and concomitant renal vein and/or inferior vena cava thrombosis met inclusion criteria. Adrenal hemorrhage was unilateral, left-sided in six and right-sided in two. During the imaging course, ipsilateral renal gray-scale abnormalities were identified in all neonates, including apparent renal enlargement in six and intrarenal echogenic linear streaks in seven. Inferior vena cava thrombus was visible on gray-scale imaging in all cases. Renal hilar venous flow was detectable in all six neonates evaluated with ipsilateral renal Doppler, despite renal vein thrombosis.

CONCLUSION: In neonates with adrenal hemorrhage, meticulous gray-scale assessment of both kidneys, renal veins, and inferior vena cava, followed by targeted Doppler, may improve recognition of associated venous thrombosis.

articles.title: Percutaneous dilatational tracheostomy in adult intensive care: An ANZICS consensus statement.
articles.abstract: Percutaneous dilatational tracheostomy (PDT) is a commonly performed procedure in intensive care units; However, the high-quality evidence base guiding many aspects of its practice remains limited, resulting in variation across clinicians and institutions. This statement was drafted by a panel of experts, later reviewed by an expert working group comprising representatives from the Australian and New Zealand Intensive Care Society and the College of Intensive Care Medicine, and endorsed by the boards of both organisations. The recommendations presented are based on the best available evidence and, where evidence is scarce, on structured expert consensus. The scope of this statement is confined to PDT in adult intensive care patients. This document reflects current practice at the time of publication and is intended to be a living document, subject to regular review to include emerging evidence and evolving standards of care. In summary, this consensus statement provides evidence-informed, expert-guided recommendations to standardise PDT practice in adult ICUs across Australia and New Zealand, while acknowledging current variability and gaps in the evidence base.

articles.title: APICS 2026: The Asia Pacific Intensive Care Symposium goes to Bali.
Nurse-Led Sepsis Scoring System for Adult Febrile Neutropenia: Protocol for a Two-Phase Clinical Prediction Model Study With Remote Patient Monitoring.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adults with hematological malignancies who develop febrile neutropenia (FN) face elevated risks of sepsis, intensive care admission, and treatment interruptions. Early sepsis detection is challenging, as classical clinical signs are often attenuated or delayed in this population. Current risk stratification tools demonstrate limitations when applied to adults with FN. A tailored, nurse-led scoring system integrating clinical, laboratory, and physiological predictors may enhance early sepsis identification.

OBJECTIVE: This 2-phase study aims to develop and internally validate a nurse-led sepsis risk score for adults with FN in phase I and to temporally validate its performance in phase II. The new score will be compared to the MASCC risk index, CISNE, NEWS2_ and qSOFA at FN onset . The secondary objectives include evaluating associations between risk groups and remote patient monitoring alerts within 24 hours of FN onset, interrater agreement, and bedside feasibility.

METHODS: The study is being conducted in the hematology and bone marrow transplantation department of a tertiary care hospital in Bengaluru, India. Phase I uses a nested matched case-control design within a retrospective cohort of approximately 140 patients with FN. We will analyze clinical, laboratory, and physiological predictors measured at FN onset using multivariable conditional logistic regression, with internal validation via bootstrapping. In Phase II, which utilizes a prospective temporal validation cohort, bedside nurses will calculate the proposed score at FN onset alongside the MASCC, CISNE, NEWS2, and qSOFA scores A substudy will include additional nurses scoring independently to assess interrater agreement and feasibility. Two blinded reviewers will adjudicate phase I outcomes within 14 days of FN onset, while assessors blinded to all scores will adjudicate phase II outcomes within the same time frame. The primary outcome is sepsis within 14 days of FN onset. Phase II evaluates discrimination, calibration, and comparative diagnostic performance.

RESULTS: We obtained ethics approval in April 2025, and the study was registered in June 2025 (CTRI/2025/06/088290). The initial phase I derivation was completed in November 2025, using sepsis within 14 days of FN onset as the primary outcome. A protocol amendment in September 2026 harmonized the outcome window to 14 days, prompting rederivation of the model and superseding the initial analysis. Phase II commenced in December 2025. As of September 2026, enrollment and data collection were ongoing, with study completion anticipated in December 2026. Main results are expected in 2027.

CONCLUSIONS: This protocol evaluates an FN-specific, nurse-led sepsis score integrating clinical and laboratory predictors with contactless physiological measurements. We will examine remote patient monitoring alerts as secondary markers of clinical instability. Validation findings will establish the score's predictive performance and inform future implementation studies.

articles.title: Glutaraldehyde Efficacy Against Cryptocaryon irritans Tomonts, Inducing ROS Generation and DNA Damage and Controlling Cryptocaryoniasis in Larimichthys crocea Factory-Style Aquaculture.
articles.abstract: Cryptocaryon irritans is a pathogenic ciliate that causes cryptocaryoniasis and substantial economic losses in the mariculture industry. This study evaluated antiparasitic effects of glutaraldehyde (GA) against C. irritans tomonts and its therapeutic potential during C. irritans infection in large yellow croaker (Larimichthys crocea). In vitro, screening demonstrated that GA aquatic disinfectant (GA-ad) significantly inhibited tomont development, achieving half lethal concentration (LC50) at 10.23 μL/L for 8 h treatment. Toxicity test showed that three 8 h treatments with GA-ad at 10 times concentration of LC50 (102.3 μL/L) were safe for the fish. Therapeutic application of GA-ad (1 × LC50 = 10.23 μL/L, and 2 × LC50 = 20.46 μL/L) in the treated groups survived L. crocea till 63% and 100% on Day 21 (Relative tomont number, RTN = 0), while in the infected group (untreated) survival rate was 0% by day nine (RTN = 39.48). For the mechanistic study, GA chemical reagent (GA-cr, 10.23 μL/L, Pure GA = 5.12 μL/L) was used which induced oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation in tomonts, as evidenced by increased ROS and MDA level, reduced GSH:GSSG and CAT activity, and increased T-SOD activity. Additionally, the mRNA expression of P21, P53, Nqo1 and Gst were significantly upregulated in GA-cr treated tomonts. Collectively, these findings indicate that GA-cr disrupts redox homeostasis, induces oxidative and DNA damage that ultimately leads to cell cycle arrest in C. irritans. Overall, 20.46 μL/L of GA-ad is highly effective for controlling cryptocaryoniasis in L. crocea aquaculture.

articles.title: Addressing the Oral-Systemic Health Divide by Strengthening Dental Referral Pathways in Primary Care.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: The bidirectional relationship between oral health and systemic health has been widely studied and has important implications for patient care.
