Despite the growing evidence of oral conditions being linked to systemic diseases and other adverse health outcomes such as cardiovascular disease, diabetes and other chronic conditions, and adverse pregnancy outcomes, oral health remains largely excluded from general medical practice.

RATIONALE: This historical and persistent separation limits opportunities for timely intervention and interprofessional management of oral diseases. Factors contributing to this compartmentalization include the historical separation of dental and medical education training, the absence of a straightforward referral system, and lack of infrastructure to effectively guide patients through the referral process.

KEY POINTS: To address these gaps, we recommend three strategies: (1) cross training primary care providers through targeted education in recognizing common oral conditions, assessing clinical urgency, and initiating appropriate referral; (2) leveraging user-friendly health IT referral systems facilitating two-way communication between medical and dental teams while enabling easy tracking and follow-up and (3) redesigning clinic workflows to include designated referral navigators (e.g., care coordinator, dental coordinator) who can address patient barriers to referral completion including appointment scheduling, insurance navigation, follow-up reminders and other logistical challenges.

IMPLICATIONS: With these recommendations, our overarching goal is to strengthen dental referral pathways within primary care settings, ultimately integrating oral health into general practice.

articles.title: Evaluating the effectiveness of the D1 Now intervention to improve outcomes among young adults with type 1 diabetes: Protocol for a cluster randomised controlled trial.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Young adults living with type 1 diabetes (T1D) often experience sub-optimal outcomes due to competing life demands, disruptions in care, reduced clinic attendance, and difficulties in self-management. To improve outcomes among this population, we developed and piloted the D1 Now intervention using a user-centred and theory-informed approach. This protocol describes a cluster randomised controlled trial (RCT) to test the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of the D1 Now intervention.

METHODS: A cluster RCT seeking to recruit 348 young adults (aged 18-25) with type 1 diabetes from 12 hospital diabetes centres in Ireland. Centres will be randomised to receive either standard care or the D1 Now intervention, which includes two components: an agenda-setting tool and a support worker. The primary outcome is the change in HbA1c from baseline to 12-month follow-up. Secondary outcomes include participant-reported psychosocial outcomes, clinical outcomes, self-management outcomes, and healthcare utilisation. We will collect data through blood samples, online participant surveys, and participant records at baseline and 12 months. Additionally, we will conduct a cost-effectiveness evaluation and a mixed-methods process evaluation.

DISCUSSION: We anticipate that the D1 Now intervention will be both effective and cost-effective in improving clinical and psychosocial outcomes for young adults compared to standard care. The findings from the process evaluation will shed light on how the intervention works (or not) and how implementation into health services (if warranted) can be optimised. If effective, D1 Now will offer a sustainable model of care to support engagement and self-management for young adults living with type 1 diabetes.

articles.title: Immersive Virtual Reality Cognitive Stimulation for Delirium Prevention in Older Surgical Intensive Care Unit Patients With Cognitive Impairment: Protocol for a 3-Arm Randomized Pilot Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative delirium is common among older adults after major surgery, especially those with cognitive impairment, and is associated with prolonged hospitalization, functional decline, mortality, and subsequent cognitive deterioration. Nonpharmacologic delirium-prevention strategies are recommended but are difficult to deliver reliably in high-acuity environments because they require repeated staff-intensive interactions, consistent patient engagement, and integration into complex intensive care unit (ICU) workflows.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the feasibility, usability, safety, acceptance, and adherence of ReCognitionVR 2.0, an immersive virtual reality (VR)-based cognitive stimulation intervention designed for older surgical ICU patients with mild-to-moderate cognitive impairment.

METHODS: This is a single-center, 3-arm, parallel-group randomized pilot trial. Ninety adults aged 65 years or older undergoing major surgery with expected postoperative ICU admission and Montreal Cognitive Assessment scores of 15 to 24 will be randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio to ReCognitionVR 2.0 cognitive stimulation, passive VR control exposure, or standard-of-care nurse-led reality orientation. VR sessions will be delivered once daily for up to 20 minutes on postoperative days 1 through 3 when participants are calm and alert. The primary outcomes are feasibility metrics, including recruitment, outcome completion, safety and tolerability, usability, acceptance, and adherence. Secondary outcomes estimate preliminary changes in attention and executive function using the Months Backward Test and NIH Toolbox Flanker Inhibitory Control and Attention Test. Postoperative delirium incidence is an exploratory clinical outcome.

RESULTS: This study was funded in September 2025. Participant recruitment and data collection are currently ongoing. Preliminary data quality assessments and exploratory reviews of the collected data are underway. Formal statistical analyses of the trial outcomes will be conducted after participant enrollment is completed and the study database has been finalized and locked. As of July 29, 2026, we had enrolled 18 participants. Early operational experience informed the refinement of exploratory VR performance metrics and the documentation of protocol deviations. Following an oxygen-connection near miss, we added a preintervention oxygen/readiness checklist as an operational safety safeguard. Enrollment of 90 participants is projected to be completed in 2027 if the current recruitment pace is sustained. Results are expected to be published in winter 2027.

CONCLUSIONS: This protocol will generate data on feasibility, safety, usability, adherence, digital performance, cognitive assessment, and delirium measurement, all needed to optimize ReCognitionVR 2.0 and to design a future multicenter efficacy trial of VR-enabled delirium prevention in critical care.

articles.title: Indications, Techniques, and Outcomes of Meniscus Centralization for Root Tears and Meniscus Transplantation: An International Expert Consensus Statement.
authors: Delphi Consensus Group on Centralization Procedures
articles.journal: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To develop an expert consensus statement on the biomechanics, diagnosis, surgical indications and techniques, rehabilitation protocols, and postoperative outcomes of centralization procedures in meniscus root pathology and meniscal allograft transplantation.

METHODS: A working group generated 39 statements on meniscal centralization from previously published data for evaluation in a 3-round modified Delphi process. A panel of 22 international experts rated each statement on a 5-point Likert scale, and statements were retained, revised, or excluded according to predefined thresholds (≥75% agreement and <20% disagreement). Rounds 1 and 2 included both literature-derived items and open-ended responses, allowing panel members to propose additional statements.

RESULTS: Ultimately, 35 statements were retained, with 100% participation across all rounds. The expert panel reached consensus that centralization may be considered in the setting of root repair and meniscal allograft transplantation to reduce meniscal extrusion (ME), improve joint contact mechanics, potentially enhance root healing, and limit displacement of the repair. The expert panel suggested that the degree of ME may help guide decision-making and that successful outcomes after medial meniscus posterior root repair with centralization may be evaluated by changes in ME and degenerative progression. Medial meniscus posterior root centralization should be considered when ME on magnetic resonance imaging exceeds 3 mm, and lateral centralization should be considered for lateral root tears with concomitant meniscofemoral ligament injury and >3 mm extrusion. Centralization was not recommended in advanced osteoarthritis. Panelists supported its use in symptomatic medial ME with varus deformity in combination with high tibial osteotomy. Transtibial tunnels, suture anchors, and hybrid constructs were all considered acceptable, provided that fixation is individualized to the location of ME and native meniscotibial anatomy and overtightening is avoided. The panel emphasized the need for long-term studies to confirm the durability and joint-protective benefits of centralization.

CONCLUSIONS: The panel supported consideration of meniscal centralization when magnetic resonance imaging shows extrusion greater than 3 mm in medial meniscus posterior root tears and in selected lateral root tears with concomitant meniscofemoral ligament injury and extrusion greater than 3 mm. Its use was discouraged in the setting of advanced osteoarthritis, whereas a combined approach with high tibial osteotomy was supported in patients with symptomatic varus-associated medial ME. No single fixation construct was preferred; transtibial, anchor-based, and hybrid techniques were all considered acceptable. Emphasis was placed on individualized surgical decision-making and on avoiding overconstraint.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level V, expert opinion.

articles.title: Adherence monitoring and intervention using a clinical decision support system in a pediatric gastroenterology clinic.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop and evaluate the implementation, feasibility, and acceptability, and implementation of an electronic health record (EHR)-based clinical decision support (CDS) tool addressing medication adherence, the Adherence Action Plan (A2P), among youth with gastrointestinal (GI) conditions.

METHODS: The A2P was developed, piloted, and implemented over 12 months for all patients seen in the GI Clinic of a Midwestern pediatric tertiary hospital. The A2P program comprised an adherence assessment followed by needs-matched, evidence-based solutions when the assessment indicated poor adherence. EHR analytics of clinical documentation was used to assess weekly provider use of A2P. At the end of the A2P implementation period, providers completed questionnaires assessing feasibility, usability, and perceived impact on clinical practice. Patients and families were surveyed regarding feasibility and perceived impact on medication-taking behaviors.

RESULTS: Among the 1110 encounters in which nonadherence was identified, 47% included documentation of A2P use. Providers documented modifying treatment plans to address adherence concerns in 71.4% of encounters and reviewing evidence-based adherence strategies with families in 78.6%. Most families rated the A2P as feasible and reported improved knowledge and self-efficacy related to medication adherence, with 86% reporting implementation of identified adherence-focused interventions in their home. Provider ratings of the A2P tool indicated moderate feasibility ratings but below-average usability scores.

CONCLUSIONS: The A2P is a promising CDS tool to support GI providers in identifying and addressing medication nonadherence. Future refinement efforts are needed to improve usability and workflow integration and to evaluate the tool's impact on adherence and clinical outcomes in adequately powered studies.

articles.title: Epicardial Fat Thickness in Fetal Growth Restriction: Impact on Neonatal Outcomes and Predictive Value.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is a condition associated with heightened risks of perinatal morbidity and mortality. Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) has been identified as a potential marker for metabolic changes in fetuses, but its role in FGR remains underexplored. This study aimed to assess fetal epicardial fat thickness (EFT) in the third trimester and its correlation with FGR diagnosis and fetal measurements.

METHOD: A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted at a Perinatology Clinic involving 82 pregnant women, including 43 with FGR and 39 controls. FGR diagnosis was based on Delphi criteria. EFT measurements were performed using echocardiography techniques, and statistical analyses were conducted to assess correlations and predictive values. Fetal EFT was measured using ultrasound, and interobserver reliability was assessed using the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC).

RESULTS: In the FGR group, EFT was significantly lower than in controls (p < 0.001). A significant moderate positive correlation was observed between EFT and fetal abdominal circumference (r = 0.363, p = 0.017). ROC analysis identified an EFT cutoff value of ≤ 1.41 mm for discriminating FGR, with 60.5% sensitivity and 92.3% specificity (AUC = 0.802, p < 0.001). In addition, EFT showed significant discriminatory ability for composite adverse neonatal outcomes (AUC = 0.727, p = 0.001).

CONCLUSION: This study highlights the potential clinical significance of fetal EFT thickness in FGR diagnosis and neonatal outcome prediction. EFT measurements offer valuable insights into fetal metabolic status and may aid in early identification of high-risk pregnancies. Further research is warranted to validate these findings and integrate EFT assessments into routine prenatal care for improved perinatal management strategies.

articles.title: Bone-Patellar Tendon-Bone and Quadriceps Tendon Autografts Are More Cost-Effective Than Hamstring Autograft and Allograft for Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction.
articles.journal: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare the cost-effectiveness of bone-patellar tendon-bone (BPTB) autograft, hamstring (HS) autograft, quadriceps tendon (QT) autograft, and allograft anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction using contemporary clinical data and time-driven activity-based costing.

METHODS: A decision-analytic Markov model was constructed to compare 5-year costs and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) for BPTB, HS, QT, and allograft anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction. Probabilities of graft failure, donor-site morbidity, infection, and revision outcomes were derived from contemporary literature. Direct medical costs were obtained from multicenter time-driven activity-based costing data. Model outcomes included costs, QALYs, and the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio. Deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses assessed model robustness across clinically plausible parameter ranges.

RESULTS: QT and BPTB autografts were the highest-value strategies in the model. At a willingness-to-pay threshold of $50,000 per QALY, QT was cost-effective relative to BPTB (incremental cost-effectiveness ratio: $42,905) and showed slightly greater modeled effectiveness; however, BPTB was least costly ($3917 vs $4901) and nearly as effective (4.589 vs 4.612 QALYs). HS autograft and allograft were more costly and less effective in the base-case model. Threshold analyses showed that small changes in operative cost (BPTB decrease of 4.5% or QT increase of 3.7%) or donor-site morbidity (BPTB decrease from 43.0% to 39.9% or QT increase from 2.9% to 7.8%) shifted the preferred strategy from QT to BPTB. In probabilistic sensitivity analyses, QT was preferred in 55.7% of simulations and BPTB was favored in the remaining 44.3%, with QT dominant in 22.4% of simulations.

CONCLUSIONS: QT and BPTB autografts offered the highest value for anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction, with QT slightly more effective and BPTB least costly. HS autograft and allograft were more costly and less effective. Given the sensitivity of these results to surgeon-specific factors, operative costs, and donor-site morbidity, graft selection should remain individualized based on patient goals, clinical considerations, and surgeon expertise rather than cost alone.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, economic and decision analysis.

articles.title: Interagency Communication of Stroke Burden to Inform Health Policy Decision in Indonesia.
articles.abstract: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) threaten population health and fiscal sustainability in low- and middle-income countries. In Indonesia, abundant evidence on stroke coexists with fragmented policy responses, an information-policy paradox. Using stroke as a tracer condition, this study examined how interagency communication shapes collaborative governance among health, finance, and planning institutions. An embedded qualitative case study combined document analysis (n = 47), four focus group discussions (28 participants), and 15 semi-structured interviews with national and subnational stakeholders. Data were coded thematically and mapped to three collaborative governance dimensions: starting conditions, institutional design, and collaborative process. We identified eight communication barriers, including overlapping mandates, fragmented information flows, coordination without follow-through, and divergent institutional frames. Health stakeholders framed stroke as a clinical burden; finance stakeholders framed it as a budgetary risk. Participants' accounts suggest that presenting stroke burden as a shared fiscal concern may help bridge these logics, which we treat as a proposed mechanism rather than a demonstrated condition for policy alignment. The findings informed a Strategic Communication Plan combining stakeholder-specific messaging, coordination routines, shared indicators, and joint accountability; its effects require evaluation. Interagency communication is a necessary but not sufficient component of collaborative governance, operating alongside political, fiscal, and regulatory conditions.

articles.title: Fecal microbiota transplantation and microbiota-based therapeutics in pediatric clinical practice: Current status and emerging indications.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) is a safe and effective treatment for recurrent or refractory Clostridioides difficile infection (rCDI) in children and adults. This review outlines the evidence behind FMT for rCDI, considerations in special pediatric populations, and limitations in current practice due to FMT access for patients under the age of 18.

articles.title: Double Burden: Anxiety Symptoms and Chronic Conditions Compound Poor Health Outcomes Among Survivors of Intimate Partner Violence.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Experiencing intimate partner violence (IPV) is linked to poorer health and wellbeing, yet the interplay between physical and psychological comorbidities remains underexplored. This study evaluates the compounded burden of chronic illness and anxiety on self-perceived health in a national cohort of IPV survivors.

METHODS: Fifteen thousand nine hundred forty-seven participants in the NIH All of Us database with accessible medical records who reported experiencing IPV answered questions from validated questionnaires about anxiety history, perceived overall health, and social satisfaction. Four groups were established: controls, high anxiety and a chronic condition, only high anxiety, and only a chronic condition. Chronic conditions were based on SNOMED codes (e.g., HTN, DM, COPD, and autoimmune conditions). Weighted propensity scores balanced cohorts based on age, sex, education, and race/ethnicity. Proportional odds logistic regressions predicted the odds of reporting negative overall health and social satisfaction based on exposure group.

RESULTS: Compared to controls, IPV survivors with both high anxiety and a chronic condition had greater odds of reporting worse overall health (OR = 3.30, 95% CI [3.01-3.63]) and lower social satisfaction (OR = 2.11, [1.92-2.31]). Those with either high anxiety or a chronic disease, to a lesser degree, reported worse overall health (OR [1.34(1.22-1.48), 2.28(2.03-2.56)] and lower social satisfaction (OR [1.52(1.38-1.66), 1.26(1.12-1.41)].

CONCLUSIONS: Anxiety symptoms and chronic illness are strongly associated with poorer perceived health and social satisfaction among IPV survivors. While each comorbidity negatively impacted perceived health, their combined burden conferred the greatest risk. The data suggest that chronic conditions exert a greater impact on perceived overall health, while anxiety is more strongly linked to lower social satisfaction, indicating benefits for clinical interventions that prioritize physical health for those with chronic illness and psychosocial support for those with anxiety.

articles.title: Family Presence During Invasive Procedures: Perceptions of Registered Nurses in Spain and Ethical Implications for Humanised Care.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To analyse the perceptions of registered nurses in Spain regarding family presence during invasive procedures (FPIP), identifying perceived benefits, barriers to its implementation, and associated sociodemographic variables.

DESIGN: A descriptive, cross-sectional, quantitative study.

METHODS: A nationally representative sample of 1836 registered nurses was obtained using the validated Spanish version of the Questionnaire on Family Presence in Invasive Procedures (QFP-IP). Data were collected anonymously online between November and December 2024. Descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were performed (Student's t, ANOVA, post hoc tests), and the psychometric properties of the scale were examined (Cronbach's α = 0.904; ICC = 0.90).

RESULTS: Overall, nurses showed favourable attitudes towards FPIP, though barriers such as insufficient training, fear of interference, and professional stress persisted. Positive attitudes increased with age, years of experience, and higher educational attainment. Paediatric and geriatric services were the most supportive, whereas intensive care and operating theatre units were more reluctant. Men and those with postgraduate or specialised training expressed greater acceptance.

CONCLUSIONS: FPIP is recognised by Spanish nurses as an ethically relevant and humanising practice that strengthens communication, autonomy, and compassion in care. Organisational and ethical frameworks are needed to ensure its safe and equitable implementation.

IMPACT: This nationwide study offers the first empirical evidence in Spain on FPIP from a nursing perspective. Its findings provide guidance for developing clinical protocols, ethics education, and institutional policies that promote moral agency and family-centred, humanised care.

CONTRIBUTION FROM PATIENTS OR THE PUBLIC: Nurses participated via an online survey and were able to respond to it by accepting the study conditions.

articles.title: Quality without a mandate: An exploratory national survey of perioperative autologous transfusion accreditation barriers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perioperative autologous transfusion, encompassing intraoperative cell salvage (ICS), acute normovolemic hemodilution (ANH), and autologous component production, is integral to patient blood management. Association for the Advancement of Blood and Biotherapies (AABB) has published comprehensive quality standards, yet perioperative accreditation remains profoundly underutilized; fewer than 10 U.S. institutions are currently accredited. No prior study has characterized these barriers.

METHODS: The AABB Perioperative Accreditation Committee administered a six-item electronic survey to AABB members in August-September 2023, addressing services provided, program oversight, quality control (QC), governance, and accreditation barriers. Fifty-seven complete responses were analyzed using descriptive statistics. This study met criteria for Non-Human Subjects Research self-determination.

RESULTS: Seventy percent of respondents (40/57) reported providing perioperative services. Only 60% expressed a positive level of comfort with perioperative program oversight and patient safety; 28% were neutral and 12% were uncomfortable. More than one in four (28%) confirmed the absence of formal QC or did not know whether any was performed. No single discipline dominated governance, and 25% reported fragmented, unclear, or absent oversight. The most frequently cited barrier was that accreditation is not required, endorsed by 53%.

CONCLUSIONS: Perioperative autologous transfusion programs in the United States often operate without the quality oversight applied to every other blood component service. The dominant barrier is not cost or complexity but the absence of external accountability. Existing oversight through The Joint Commission, the College of American Pathologists (CAP), the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), and AABB's Blood Bank and Transfusion Service (BBTS) accreditation does not extend to perioperative operations in any program-specific sense. Practical frameworks exist; adoption requires action from professional societies, hospital leadership, and regulatory bodies.

articles.title: Policy, ethical, and practical considerations of artificial intelligence use in the internal medicine clerkship: results of a survey of clerkship directors.
articles.journal: Academic medicine : journal of the Association of American Medical Colleges
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into medical education is accelerating, yet the policies guiding its use remain unclear. This study aimed to characterize the landscape of AI-related policies in U.S. internal medicine (IM) clerkships and examine clerkship directors' (CDs) perspectives on ethical and practical considerations for student AI use.

METHOD: An annual, nationally representative survey of IM CDs at 141 U.S. allopathic medical schools with membership in a medical education professional association was conducted from September through December 2024. One section included 21 questions on AI use in clerkships, policies about its use, and CDs' perspectives towards students' AI use. Descriptive statistics summarized policy prevalence and perspectives, and qualitative content analysis described free-text responses about policies.

RESULTS: The response rate for the survey section on AI was 80.9% (114/141 schools). Most CDs reported no formal policy on AI use (45/114, 39.5%) or were uncertain about whether one existed (39/114, 34.2%). When policies existed, they required students to obtain explicit permission or supervision for AI use and mandated disclosure when using AI-generated content. CD perceptions of hypothetical student usage of AI varied: 49/114 (42.9%) described AI use for a reflection essay as "cheating" compared with 6/114 (5.2%) for clinical diagnosis (p < 0.001). Most CDs (84/114, 73.7%) reported that they would encourage AI use for at least one clinical skill domain-including differential diagnosis and patient education-but few (7/114, 6.1%) reported that their institution provides firewall-protected AI tools for clinical use.

CONCLUSIONS: Policies guiding AI use in IM clerkships do not yet exist or are not well known by CDs. Policy gaps and varying perspectives on appropriate AI use may create ethical and practical ambiguity for students and their clinical supervisors. Institutions should prioritize developing clear policies and secure infrastructures to support responsible, supervised AI use in medical education.

articles.title: Patience, sociocultural patterns and self-reported caring behaviours among nursing students.
articles.abstract: This study examined whether patience is associated with caring behaviours among nursing students and its relevance to emotion regulation-related processes and professional socialisation. A cross-sectional correlational study was conducted with 861 nursing students. Data were collected using measures of patience and caring behaviours and analysed using descriptive statistics, group comparisons, Pearson correlation analysis and multiple linear regression. Patience was positively associated with caring behaviours (r = 0.365, p < 0.001). Patience scores varied across academic year and socio-cultural characteristics. After adjustment for gender and academic year, patience remained associated with caring behaviour scores. These findings position patience not as a direct measure of emotion regulation or a causal determinant of caring, but as a distinct psychological attribute relevant to maintaining attentive and respectful engagement during demanding care interactions. Longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to clarify its relationship with measured emotion regulation processes and its practical significance for nursing education.

articles.title: Immune-competent organ-on-chip methodologies to study type 1 diabetes.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is a self-driving autoimmune condition leading to the death of insulin-producing β-cells of the pancreas. β-cell-reactive immune cell extravasation into the intra-islet space is fuelled by a cycle of inflammation including immune, vascular and endocrine dysfunction. Since clinical pancreatic biopsy is contraindicated, T1D research relies on static in vitro culture or in vivo models that either cannot fully replicate the dynamic interactions between the three different tissue types or differ greatly from the human disease process.

METHODS: Recent advances in bioengineering have led to the emergence of Organ-on-Chip (OoC) platforms that aim to recapitulate the human diabetic pancreatic environment. Early T1D-relevant OoC-based research focused on the assessment of islet viability. This review turns its attention to the next frontier of vascularised and immune-competent PoC models, which hold promise for the study of the insulitis of T1D and to predict treatment response to novel therapies.

RESULTS: PoC models can incorporate technologies developed for cancer and non-diabetes inflammation applications to inform chip design, vascularisation, immune perfusion and pancreatic component incorporation. An established PoC model can then be utilised for a detailed quantitative and qualitative analysis and functional correlation of the immune, vascular and pancreatic components according to an a priori Context of Use (CoU).

CONCLUSION: The ease of manufacturing, combined with a future possibility of a fully human autologous PoC, could enable high-throughput screening of T1D tissue for underlying causes of patient heterogeneity that, in turn, could inform personalised treatment approaches, prolonged cell therapy survival and novel preventative measures.

articles.title: Classification of brain variants on fetal ultrasound: international Delphi consensus.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop an expert consensus classification and management framework for fetal-brain variants identified on prenatal ultrasound across all trimesters of pregnancy that cannot be categorized confidently as either benign or pathological.

METHODS: A two-round international Delphi survey was conducted among experts in fetal medicine and neurosonography, with survey data collected between September 2025 and March 2026. Forty-eight fetal-brain variants, identified through a scoping literature review of PubMed/MEDLINE from database inception to August 2025, performed between June and August 2025, and illustrated with representative ultrasound images, were evaluated. Brain variants were classified according to clinical significance and recommended management into three predefined categories: 'green' (benign variants requiring no additional investigation or follow-up), 'orange' (requiring neurosonographic follow-up) and 'red' (requiring dedicated neurosonography, fetal-brain magnetic resonance imaging and/or genetic investigations). Consensus was predefined as ≥ 70% agreement. In Round 2, experts confirmed their agreement regarding categorization of variants that had reached consensus in Round 1 and reassessed variants that did not reach initial consensus.

RESULTS: Forty-eight experts from 14 countries participated in Round 1 and 39 (81.3%) completed both rounds. Of the 48 evaluated variants, 35 (72.9%) reached consensus after two rounds: 12 were classified as 'green', seven as 'orange' and 16 as 'red'. Green variants included isolated choroid plexus cysts < 10 mm across all trimesters, regular asymmetry of the choroid plexuses, isolated cavum septations, cavum vergae, cavum velum interpositum, isolated small cavum septi pellucidi with intact corpus callosum and dolichocephaly with normal head circumference and normal brain morphology. Orange variants included isolated enlargement of intracranial translucency with preserved anatomy, large or bilateral choroid plexus cysts, isolated enlargement of subarachnoid spaces without compression and isolated cyst of the cavum septi pellucidi. Red variants included abnormal posterior fossa markers (loss of normal three-space anatomy, increased brainstem-vermis angle, reduced brainstem-occipital bone distance), periventricular cysts associated with adjacent white-matter abnormalities, thickened corpus callosum and distortion of the interhemispheric fissure, among other findings. Thirteen (27.1%) variants failed to reach consensus, highlighting persistent uncertainty in interpreting subtle isolated asymmetries and selected cystic variants.

CONCLUSIONS: This international Delphi consensus proposes an initial expert-derived classification of commonly encountered feta-brain variants on ultrasound. Because the classification has not been validated against postnatal imaging or neurodevelopmental outcomes and reproducibility has not been assessed, prospective evaluation is required before it can be applied in routine practice. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

articles.title: Cholesteatoma Recidivism in Pediatric Versus Adult Patients: Disease Extent and Prognostic Factors.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether pediatric age independently predicts cholesteatoma recidivism beyond anatomical disease extent using the EAONO/JOS and SAMEO-ATO classifications.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of 128 primary cholesteatoma surgeries (128 ears in 126 patients; median follow-up, 5.8 years) was conducted. Etiology, stage, topographical extension (STAM), and surgical category (SAMEO-ATO) were recorded. A data-driven threshold (< 20 years) was identified via maximally selected rank statistics. Predictors were determined by Group Lasso selection and Firth's penalized Cox regression.

RESULTS: Recidivism was identified in 21 of 43 pediatric and 16 of 85 adult ears. The 5-year cumulative risk was 53.9% (95% CI, 34.2%-67.8%) in children versus 19.1% (95% CI, 9.5%-27.7%) in adults (log-rank p < 0.001), driven by early residual disease (p = 0.004) rather than true recurrence (p = 0.058). The sinus tympani (S2) was a site of recidivism in 38.5% of pediatric versus 5.6% of adult cases (p = 0.016). Multivariable analysis identified four independent predictors: pediatric age (hazard ratio [HR] 2.24; 95% CI, 1.09-4.63), supratubal recess involvement (HR 3.41; 95% CI, 1.56-7.45), mastoid extension (HR 2.43; 95% CI, 1.01-5.84), and absence of mastoidectomy relative to canal wall-down technique (HR 8.67; 95% CI, 1.95-38.41).

CONCLUSION: Pediatric age, supratubal recess involvement, mastoid extension, and mastoidectomy omission relative to canal wall-down technique independently predict cholesteatoma recidivism. The predominance of residual over recurrent disease, with a median detection interval of approximately 14 months, supports active 12-18 month postoperative surveillance and long-term clinical follow-up on a risk-stratified basis.

articles.title: Decoding Ewing sarcoma: from EWSR1::FLI1 translocation to advanced diagnostic approaches.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This review discusses Ewing sarcoma and its diagnostic approaches, highlighting emerging high-throughput technologies that address current diagnostic limitations by enabling rapid, accurate, and personalized diagnostic strategies.

AREAS COVERED: Diagnostic approaches for Ewing sarcoma encompass conventional imaging modalities, including X-ray, Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), and Positron Emission Tomography (PET), together with histopathological and molecular techniques such as Immunohistochemistry (IHC), Reverse Transcriptase-Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-PCR), Fluorescence in Situ Hybridization (FISH), as well as advanced modalities like liquid biopsy, Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS), nano-diagnostic methods, and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven analytical tools. Together, these enable earlier and more accurate detection, molecular profiling, personalized medicine, and precision-guided clinical decision-making.

EXPERT OPINION: Emerging diagnostic technologies offer new opportunities to improve the detection and molecular characterization of Ewing sarcoma through earlier diagnosis, comprehensive genomic profiling, and personalized medicine. Although NGS, liquid biopsy, and AI have demonstrated significant potential for precision diagnostics, their clinical implementation remains limited by high costs, restricted accessibility, and the need for standardized protocols and clinical validation. Continued technological refinement, integration into routine practice, and access will help overcome existing barriers, strengthen precision diagnostics, improve patient outcomes, and support personalized medicine.

articles.title: Angiotensin receptor blockers and nontraditional health outcomes: an umbrella review of meta-analyses of randomised controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) are prescribed for cardiovascular and renal protection, but their effects on nontraditional health outcomes remain unclear. With the increasing use of ARBs in diverse populations, clarifying their broader impact has important clinical implications.

METHODS: We conducted an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that assessed ARBs and nontraditional health outcomes. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception to April 2026. Methodological quality was appraised using AMSTAR 2, and certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. Where trial-level data were available, we re-analysed outcomes using random-effects models and evaluated heterogeneity, 95% prediction intervals, and small-study effects.

RESULTS: Fifteen systematic reviews and meta-analyses of RCTs were included, covering 35 unique nontraditional outcomes. Nine outcomes reached nominal statistical significance, but only a few met more stringent credibility criteria. The most credible associations were lower risks of headache and new-onset diabetes, and lower fasting plasma insulin levels with ARB therapy. Associations with migraine severity, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and insulin resistance were suggestive or exploratory because of prediction intervals crossing the null, sparse data, heterogeneity, or limited certainty. No convincing evidence supported associations with oncological, infectious, or transplant-related outcomes. Most included reviews were rated as low or critically low-quality using AMSTAR 2, warranting cautious interpretation.

CONCLUSION: ARBs appear to provide therapeutic benefits beyond traditional indications, particularly in metabolic and neurological domains, without evidence of excess harm. These findings may inform clinical decision-making in patients at risk of diabetes or with comorbid pain conditions.

articles.title: Understanding depression and anxiety symptoms in women with Mayer-Rokitansky‑Küster‑Hauser syndrome (MRKH): Exploring the influence of shame and psychological flexibility.
articles.abstract: Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome (MRKH) is a congenital condition warranting a biopsychosocial perspective and a multidisciplinary approach in research and clinical settings. Previous studies on psychopathological symptoms in women with MRKH have reported mixed results. This study aimed to (1) compare depressive and anxiety symptoms in women with MRKH with published summary statistics from a non-clinical sample, (2) compare chronic illness-related shame in women with MRKH with published statistics from samples with other chronic illnesses, (3) examine differences between women who had and had not completed medical treatment on the study variable, and (4) explore chronic illness-related shame, self-compassion, and psychological flexibility as predictors of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Eighty-one women with a self-reported MRKH diagnosis were recruited through patients' associations and completed online self-report measures assessing depressive and anxiety symptoms, chronic illness-related shame, self-compassion, and psychological flexibility. Women with MRKH revealed higher depression, anxiety, and chronic illness-related shame than reference samples. Participants who had previously undergone medical treatment showed lower levels of depression and anxiety. Chronic illness-related shame predicted both depressive and anxiety symptoms, while psychological flexibility predicted anxiety symptoms specifically. This study emphasizes the relevance of targeting chronic illness-related shame and psychological flexibility when designing psychological interventions for these women.

articles.title: Cost-Effectiveness and Economic Boundaries of Low-Titer Group O Whole Blood in Pediatric Trauma.
articles.abstract: Low-titer group O whole blood (LTOWB) reduces mortality in pediatric trauma when added to component therapy (CT;ie, any protocol based on ratios of isolated blood components). Despite this benefit, no cost-effectiveness analysis has compared the strategies. We built a decision tree comparing LTOWB+CT with CT alone for previously healthy children under 16 requiring massive transfusion. We used a 30-day horizon, a US Level I trauma center perspective, and a willingness to pay threshold of $100,000 per mortality averted. LTOWB+CT averted 2.7 additional deaths per 100 patients and cost $788.32 more per case. The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was $29,571.17 per mortality averted; LTOWB+CT was cost-effective in 58% of iterations. Cost-effectiveness was lost below a willingness to pay of $25,000, above an LTOWB unit cost of $1,566.18, or more than 5.3 LTOWB or 9.1 packed red cell units. Low-titer group O whole blood is a cost-effective addition to pediatric massive transfusions protocols (MTP), but definable economic limits bind its value.

articles.title: Atrial fibrillation care in internal medicine: a multicenter survey of screening, anticoagulation responses, and clinical support needs.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Internal medicine physicians frequently encounter atrial fibrillation (AF) and anticoagulation-related problems before or alongside cardiology input. We described internal medicine residents' and specialists' first-choice method for confirming suspected AF, how often they reported screening for AF in four prespecified risk-enriched patient groups (screening method and interval were not specified), their responses to common anticoagulation scenarios, and their preferences for practical clinical support.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter cross-sectional online survey in nine hospitals in Türkiye. All 549 eligible internal medicine physicians listed on institutional staffing rosters were invited; 327 completed a 34-item questionnaire (response rate 59.6%). Item-level response distributions were the primary outcomes; resident-specialist comparisons were exploratory.

RESULTS: Twelve-lead electrocardiography was selected for diagnostic confirmation by 88.4%. Always/often screening was reported by 19.9%-38.8% of respondents across four prespecified risk-enriched groups: patients aged ≥ 65 years, those with heart failure, those with a history of stroke or transient ischemic attack, and those with diabetes or chronic kidney disease. Fewer than half selected the prespecified reference response in five selected scenarios: stable coronary disease (47.7%), the direct oral anticoagulant-unsuitable option of a mechanical prosthetic valve or moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis (46.5%), apixaban dose reduction (38.5%), minor bleeding (37.9%), and an international normalized ratio outside the target range (34.3%). A practical algorithm was considered useful by 94.5%, structured internal medicine-cardiology collaboration by 86.5%, and 75.5% requested further education.

CONCLUSIONS: Although most respondents selected electrocardiography for AF confirmation, always/often screening was reported by fewer than 40% in each assessed risk-enriched group, and responses to anticoagulation scenarios varied, including among specialists. These findings support prospective evaluation of a locally adapted, internist-led pathway integrating opportunistic screening prompts, a defined initial assessment, and clear criteria for timely cardiology input.

articles.title: A Mitochondrial Autophagy-Synthesis Dynamic Equilibrium Liposome for the Repair of Energy Metabolism in Acute Kidney Injury.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a clinical syndrome primarily attributed to mitochondrial dysfunction, characterized by disrupted mitochondrial balance. Impaired biogenesis leads to insufficient energy supply, while defective autophagy results in the accumulation of damaged mitochondria-both of which exacerbate injury to renal tubular epithelial cells. In this study, we developed melatonin/pioglitazone liposomes (MP@Lip) for AKI therapy via restoration of mitochondrial dynamic balance. When melatonin and pioglitazone was jointly delivered to damaged renal tubules, they activated mitochondrial autophagy and biogenesis, thereby bidirectionally restoring mitochondrial network homeostasis. Mechanistically, AMPK/SIRT3/PGC-1α-related signaling may be involved in the mitochondrial protection of MP@Lip. Upon AMPK phosphorylation, SIRT1/SIRT3 deacetylase activity is upregulated, the ratio of LC3B-II/LC3B-I increases, p62/SQSTM1 decreases, and autophagy is enhanced. PGC-1α enhances transcriptional activity and promotes the expression of mitochondrial biogenic markers (TOM20). This complementary degradation-synthesis loop gradually restores mitochondrial dynamic balance. In vitro experiments confirmed that MP@Lip reduces ROS production and apoptosis while restoring mitochondrial membrane potential. In vivo studies demonstrated improvement in renal function indicators, alleviation of inflammatory responses and histopathological damage, and no systemic toxicity. This strategy shifts AKI treatment from symptomatic support to ameliorating mitochondrial dysfunction, providing a targeted, complementary and relatively safe approach that may be applicable to other mitochondrial functional-related diseases.

articles.title: Nothing about us without us: evaluating the quality of engagement in a patient advisor program.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Patient Advisor Program at Henry Ford Health is an innovative initiative aimed at strengthening patient engagement in research, quality improvement, and clinical care. Patient engagement yields increased relevance of studied topics and builds trust within communities. As such, it is vital to evaluate the quality of patient engagement across research programs. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the quality of engagement for patient advisors (PA) enrolled within the Patient Advisor Program.

METHODS: A cross-sectional survey, sent via REDCap to 578 active and inactive PAs, utilized the Public and Patient Engagement Evaluation Tool-Patient (PPEET) consisting of 19-items, closed- (n = 13) and open-ended (n = 6) items across the core principles of quality engagement: (1) Communication and supports for participation (3 items), (2) Sharing your views and perspectives (4 items), (3) Impacts and influence of the engagement initiative (4 items), and (4) Final thoughts (n = 3). All closed-ended questions were answered on a 5-point Likert scale with anchors from strongly disagree to strongly agree and analyzed using descriptive statistics. Open-ended questions were analyzed using a 3-step qualitative content analysis.

RESULTS: The final dataset of those who completed the PPEET survey included 199 PAs with a mean age of 60.7 years (SD = 15.6). PAs were primarily women (75.6%), and identified as White (64.3%), followed by Black (30.7%). Most PAs had been engaged for 1-3 years (30.7%) and participated in an average of 4.6 research projects (SD = 7.32). Across the 4 PPEET domains, the proportion of participants who agreed or strongly agreed with the items ranged from 62.9% to 92% for communication and supports for participation, 83.9% to 91.5% for sharing your views and perspectives, 79.4% to 83.4% for impacts and influence, and 85.9% to 88.9% for final thoughts PAs commented on areas of improvement (e.g., a broader range of research opportunities/topics), program strengths (e.g., diversity), and program impact (e.g., positive impact on the advisors themselves).

CONCLUSIONS: PAs reported quality engagement experiences in the Patient Advisor Program. Future research is needed to standardize evaluation of patient engagement in research to provide generalizable results.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Correction: Occurrence of antimicrobial-resistant, extended-spectrum beta-lactamase and carbapenemase-producing bacterial isolates from intensive care unit environment in two hospitals of Ethiopia.
Trainings and Recommendations for Physician Firearm Secure Storage Counseling for Suicide Prevention: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Suicide is a public health crisis in the USA. Secure storage of firearms can reduce suicide risk by putting time and distance between a suicidal crisis and access to a firearm. However, physicians often do not provide counseling to patients. This scoping review examines educational interventions that provide physicians and physicians-in-training skills to counsel patients about firearm secure storage.

METHODS: This scoping review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute scoping review methodology and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) format. A literature search was conducted across Medline, Embase, PsycInfo, Cochrane Library, CINAHL Plus with Full Text, and Web of Science and included publications through April 9, 2025. Eligibility criteria included articles that (1) involved trainings on firearm secure storage for suicide prevention or provided commentary on what should be included in potential trainings; (2) had study populations that included physicians; and (3) were available in English.

RESULTS: Forty articles were included: 21 commentaries providing suggestions on physician firearm secure storage counseling education and training and 19 articles involving development and implementation of physician education and training. Training varied and included conversation strategies, facts about suicide, and storage methods and devices. Nineteen articles included study participant details, with emergency medicine (four studies), pediatrics (four studies), and psychiatry (three studies) most included. Most reported increased knowledge relating to firearms, improvements in attitudes and beliefs on importance of speaking with patients about firearm safety, and improvements in confidence and comfort in counseling.

DISCUSSION: This review found limited but promising literature on training physicians to provide firearm secure storage counseling for suicide prevention. Limitations include that only records published in English were included and that, as a scoping review, the quality of individual studies was not assessed. Standardized, evidence-based curricula are needed for broader implementation.

articles.title: Development of a Simplified Multi-Physics Computational Model of the Coronary Microcirculation.
articles.abstract: Coronary blood flow (CBF) is influenced by multiple biophysical factors, including vascular function (vasoconstriction/vasodilation), structural remodeling (vascular wall thickening), tissue mechanical properties (stiffness), cardiac electrophysiology, and dynamic extravascular forces. However, it is difficult to experimentally determine how these biophysical factors interact to regulate CBF. For example, during type 2 diabetes (T2D) reduced vascular wall stiffness due to reduced coronary vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) stiffness, increased wall thickness due to inward hypertrophic remodeling and increased myocardial stiffness may alter CBF. However, the relative importance of these biophysical factors and their direct effect on CBF is not known. Here, we developed a simplified multi-physics computational model of myocardial tissue deformation and intramyocardial blood flow and used this model to investigate how several biophysical factors influence CBF. This model accounts for excitation-contraction coupling, myocardial fiber structure, dynamic myocardial contraction, passive myocardial mechanical properties, and the mechanics of VSMCs in the coronary microvascular walls. Baseline models yielded CBF velocity waveforms that exhibited peak diastolic velocities and waveform morphologies that were comparable to Doppler echocardiography measurements in normal adult humans. Parameter variation studies were conducted to investigate how several biophysical factors alter the morphological properties of the CBF velocity waveform, and results indicate that VSMC and passive myocardial tissue stiffness were the major drivers of CBF. In addition, the flow regulatory properties of VSMCs were found to depend on the degree of myocardial stiffness. This computational framework represents a new way to investigate how coronary-cardiac interactions regulate CBF.

articles.title: Endoscopic dacryocystorhinostomy with versus without silicone intubation in chronic dacryocystitis: a comparative meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dacryocystitis, an inflammation of the lacrimal sac typically caused by nasolacrimal duct obstruction (NLDO), is often treated with endoscopic dacryocystorhinostomy (EN-DCR). Silicone intubation is commonly employed during the procedure to help maintain ostial patency; however, its effectiveness remains debated. This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to determine whether silicone intubation improves surgical outcomes compared with EN-DCR performed without intubation in patients with chronic dacryocystitis (CD).

METHODS: A comprehensive literature search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and CENTRAL identified 19 eligible retrospective and prospective studies involving 1,236 eyes (655 with intubation, 581 without) from inception to June 3, 2025. Studies were eligible if they involved patients with CD undergoing EN-DCR and compared outcomes between procedures performed with or without silicone intubation. Exclusion criteria included ipsilateral rhinitis, case reports, review articles, and studies without a comparative arm. Primary outcomes included surgical success rates, functional success, patency, and complication rates at various follow-up intervals. Risk of bias was assessed using Risk of bias 2 (ROB2) and Newcastle-Ottawa scale (NOS) for observational studies. Statistical analyses were conducted using RStudio (R version 4.6.1). Certainty of evidence was appraised using the GRADE framework, and publication bias was assessed via funnel plot asymmetry and Egger's regression test using RStudio (R version 4.6.1). This meta-analysis was registered in PROSPERO (ID: CRD420251072646).

RESULTS: The overall surgical-success analysis included 1,221 eyes and showed no statistically significant difference between EN-DCR with versus without silicone intubation (OR = 0.83, 95% CI [0.51-1.35], p = 0.46, I2 = 26.5%). Results remained nonsignificant across follow-up subgroups (≤ 3 months: OR = 0.81, 95% CI [0.39-1.68], p = 0.57; approximately 6 months: OR = 1.58, 95% CI [0.78-3.17], p = 0.20; ≥ 12 months: OR = 0.49, 95% CI [0.21-1.16], p = 0.10), with no significant difference between subgroups (p = 0.11). No significant difference was observed in functional success (OR = 0.88, 95% CI [0.52-1.50], p = 0.64) or anatomical success assessed by irrigation (OR 0.99, 95% CI [0.63-1.56], p = 0.96) or endoscopic finding (OR 0.98, 95% CI [0.59-1.63], p = 0.94). Complication rates, including granulation tissue formation (OR = 1.71, p = 0.12), synechiae (OR = 0.95, p = 0.90), post-operative bleeding (OR = 0.65, p = 0.59), and punctal injury (OR = 1.55, p = 0.52), were comparable between groups. Stent expulsion occurred in 3% (95% CI [1-9%]) of intubated eyes. No significant publication bias was detected across all assessed outcomes (Egger's test, all p > 0.05). The overall certainty of evidence ranged from low for primary and anatomical outcomes to very low for complication outcomes per GRADE assessment.

CONCLUSION: In conclusion, the pooled analysis showed no statistically significant difference between EN-DCR with and without silicone intubation. However, the certainty of evidence ranged from low to very low, and the true comparative effect remains uncertain. Further long-term trials are warranted to clarify the indications for silicone intubation in EN-DCR.

articles.title: A Fully Automated Segment-Specific CCTA Plaque Quantification Workflow using Deep Learning.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) remains essential for diagnosing coronary artery disease, while the focus has moved from stenosis to plaque burden. Current workflows either need manual adjustments that limit consistency and efficiency, or they lack segment-specific precision. This study evaluated the effectiveness and reliability of a fully automated deep learning-based plaque quantification method using CCTA. DVPlaque workflow, a fully automated deep learning model, was developed to quantify segment-specific plaque volume. A total of 271 CCTA scans were included. Plaque quantification was performed by the expert and DVPlaque model, respectively. Reliability was measured through interclass correlation coefficient (ICC) analysis and Bland-Altman plots. DVPlaque workflow cost less time than expert measurement (p < 0.0001). Among these segments of major coronary arteries, proximal left ascending artery (LAD) had the highest prevalence of plaque (97.0%). Among these coronary arteries, the volumes of total plaque (TP), calcified plaque (CP), noncalcified plaque (NCP), and low-density NCP were the highest in LAD (all p-values < 0.05). On a per-patient level, the ICCs for TP, CP, and NCP volume were 0.962, 0.985, and 0.932. The corresponding biases and 95% limits of agreement were - 25.39 [ - 261.51, 210.73] mm3, 11.88 [ - 52.78, 76.55] mm3, and - 37.27 [ - 255.88, 181.33] mm3. For TP, CP, and NCP, per-vessel ICCs were all > 0.90, and per-segment ICCs were > 0.90 except for mid-LAD NCP (0.887). DVPlaque scheme was capable of quantifying plaque volume with excellent efficiency. The automated quantification of CP and NCP exhibited strong reliability even on a per-segment level, facilitating clinical application.

articles.title: AI-Based Low-Dose Chest CT Assessment of Coronary Artery Calcification Score: An Analysis of Accuracy-Relating Factors.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: This study evaluates the accuracy of AI-based coronary artery calcium scoring on nongated low-dose chest CT and identifies factors affecting calcium risk classification, using ECG-gated noncontrast cardiac CT as the reference standard. This prospective study included 312 patients with chest pain who underwent ECG-gated noncontrast cardiac CT and additional low-dose chest CT (LDCT). LDCT images were reconstructed using pulmonary and standard kernels. AI software automatically quantified Agatston, mass, volume, and total coronary artery calcium scores (CACSs). Patients were stratified by Agatston-based risk category, heart rate (≤ 65 vs. > 65 bpm), and BMI (< 25 vs. ≥ 25 kg/m2). Agreement, systematic bias, and risk classification performance were assessed using Bland-Altman analysis, ICC analysis, Friedman tests with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons, linear regression, and confusion matrices. Pulmonary kernel LDCT produced Agatston scores comparable to ECG-gated CT, with no significant differences across heart rate, BMI, or calcium severity subgroups. Under this kernel, measurement bias showed weak but significant correlations with heart rate and BMI (r = 0.145 and r = 0.131, respectively; both P < 0.05). Overall, nongated LDCT-derived CACS correlated strongly with reference CACS (r > 0.94). The low heart rate/low-BMI subgroup showed the best risk stratification performance, with 80% accuracy and good agreement (κ = 0.72). AI-assisted CACS assessment on nongated low-dose chest CT may serve as an adjunctive tool for opportunistic coronary artery calcification screening and preliminary cardiovascular risk stratification. Its accuracy may be influenced by reconstruction kernel and calcification burden, whereas heart rate and BMI may not be significant influencing factors.Trial Registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500100073,2 April 2025, the study was retrospectively registered).

articles.title: Cross-Center Stroke Evaluation using Carotid Ultrasound Patterns via Scale-Adaptive Frequency-Enhanced Neural Network.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: Medical imaging datasets vary across institutions due to differences in scanner types, posing challenges for model generalization. To address the issue, this study proposed a scale-adaptive frequency-enhanced neural network (SAFE-Net), which leveraged a DWT-ViT encoder to incorporate frequency-domain features into a transformer-based architecture for cross-center stroke evaluation. The discrete wavelet transform (DWT) decomposed carotid color Doppler (CCD) images into multiresolution frequency sub-bands. The extracted high-resolution (Xh) and low-resolution (Xl) features are concatenated to enhance both local and global feature extraction. Experimental results demonstrated that SAFE-Net achieves the highest accuracy, with 92.5% accuracy on Institution A and 93.75% on Institution B, outperforming other models in stroke evaluation. SAFE-Net maintains cross-center generalization, with an accuracy of 90.73% when trained on Institution A and tested on Institution B, and 89.16% in the reverse setting. Also, the model required 25% fewer parameters and 2.0× fewer FLOPs than conventional models. These findings underscored the effectiveness of SAFE-Net across diverse medical imaging datasets.

articles.title: Effects of chronic care model-based intervention offered to elderly patients with diabetes on medication adherence, self-management, and activities of daily living: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: This study was conducted to reveal the effects of a Chronic Care Model (CCM)-based intervention offered to elderly patients with diabetes on their medication adherence, self-management, and activities of daily living. This randomized controlled study was conducted on diabetic patients; older adults received inpatient treatment in an internal medicine clinic of a state hospital; the patients in the trial group were provided with training using the CCM. The comparisons following the trial revealed that the differences between the group mean values were statistically significant in all variables except the Katz ADL (p < 0.05). The mean MARS score and mean total DSMS score of the trial group were found to be statistically significantly higher than those of the control group (p < 0.001). The study confirmed that CCM-based interventions offered to elderly patients with diabetes were effective on medication adherence and self-management.

articles.title: Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) and Soil-Transmitted Helminth Infection among Children Living in Slums and In Situ Slum Upgradation Housing in Odisha, India.
articles.journal: Journal of urban health : bulletin of the New York Academy of Medicine
articles.abstract: Soil-transmitted helminth (STH) infections are considered neglected tropical diseases. Prior studies have demonstrated that substandard housing conditions and deficiencies in water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) in urban slums significantly contribute to a high prevalence of STH infections among children. This study assessed the difference in WASH practices and STH infections in children aged 3 to 12 living in slums and in situ slum upgradation housing. A cross-sectional study was conducted among urban slum children living in three cities in Odisha, India, using a multi-stage cluster random sampling method. The prevalence of intestinal helminthic parasites-Ascaris lumbricoides (roundworm), Trichuris trichiura (whipworm), Ancylostoma duodenale, and Necator americanus-was assessed in the stool samples using both direct microscopy and the Kato-Katz procedure. The findings showed a significant difference (χ2 = 19.915, p < 0.001) between STH infections in slums (48%) and in situ slum upgradation housing (34%). In slum housing, children aged 10 to 12 had a higher risk (OR 2.154, p = 0.059). The use of community or public toilets was associated with increased risk (OR 2.234, p = 0.106), while shared toilets did not show significant risk (OR 1.455, p = 0.245). City-specific findings indicated that children in Cuttack had a significantly lower risk of STH infection compared to those in Bhubaneswar (OR 0.299, p < 0.001), and similar results were observed for Puri (OR 0.438, p = 0.001). The findings suggest that both age and geographical location significantly influence STH infection risk, highlighting the need for targeted interventions in specific communities focusing on WASH and behavioral determinants.

articles.title: Rapamycin and human longevity among kidney transplant recipients surviving the first year.
articles.abstract: Rapamycin, an mTOR inhibitor, continues to be investigated for hypothesized physiological, disease prevention, and longevity benefits, but few studies have been conducted in humans. Using US national organ transplant registry data, one of the largest real-world datasets examining chronic rapamycin exposure in humans, we compared the Kaplan-Meier survival age distribution of 4885 kidney transplant recipients prescribed rapamycin compared to 6589 recipients not prescribed rapamycin. Recipients were followed a median of 11 years and 6443 died during the study period. Propensity score weighting was used to adjust for exposure group differences in age, BMI, diabetes, and 15 other factors. After adjusting for demographic and clinical differences between groups, the median survival age of 64.6 years in the rapamycin group and 64.3 years in the non-rapamycin group were statistically similar (95% confidence interval for median survival age difference -1.6, 2.0 years). In this large cohort of kidney transplant recipients who were alive with a functioning graft at 1 year post-transplant, we did not observe a meaningful improvement in long-term survival with mTOR inhibition.

articles.title: In silico identification of drug compounds to arabinose-5-phosphate isomerase of Proteus mirabilis to combat its antibiotic resistance using an integrated bioinformatics: subtractive proteomics, molecular docking, MD simulation and DFT studies.
articles.abstract: Proteus mirabilis is a major opportunistic Gram-negative pathogen causing complicated urinary tract infections (UTIs), particularly in catheterized patients. Although several antibiotics, including streptomycin, erythromycin, and sparfloxacin, remain effective against some infections, the growing spread of multidrug-resistant P. mirabilis strains has created an urgent need to identify new therapeutic targets and treatment options. Using a subtractive proteomics approach, this study identified potential therapeutic targets in P. mirabilis. Among the 417 essential pathogen-specific proteins, 11 were identified as druggable, virulence-associated, and antibiotic resistance-related proteins, making them promising novel therapeutic targets against P. mirabilis. Among them, nine are enzymatic proteins involved in crucial biological pathways such as glycan and amino acid biosynthesis, energy metabolism, cellular signaling, and genetic information processing. The protein-protein interactions (PPIs) and hub gene analysis revealed arabinose-5-phosphate isomerase (API) as a primary target; structure-guided virtual screening identified five hits, ferric derisomaltose, hyaluronic acid, acarbose, rutin, and dihydrostreptomycin that exhibit binding affinities ranging from -13.540 to -10.616 kcal/mol with P. mirabilis arabinose-5-phosphate isomerase (PmAPI), suggesting their potential as anti-P. mirabilis agents towards infectious disease control. The density functional theory (DFT) studies and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations interaction analysis on PmAPI with potent hits clearly showed reactivity of the hits and stable binding with PmAPI during the 500-ns MD simulation.

articles.title: Deep learning-based segmentation of the ischemic core and severe hypodensity on noncontrast head CT compared with CT perfusion and diffusion-weighted imaging.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare the spatial overlap, imaging marker agreement, and outcome associations of acute ischemic regions of interest (ROIs) using deep-learning NCCT (DLNCCT) versus manual NCCT, CTP, and DWI-based segmentations.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We trained a deep learning model to segment ischemic ROIs on admission NCCT (DLNCCT). DLNCCT was compared with manual NCCT, CTP (rCBF < 30%/38%), and DWI using the Dice similarity coefficient (mean ± SD), Bland-Altman analysis (mean difference [95% CI]), and concordance correlation coefficient (CCC). For each ROI, we compared NCCT imaging biomarkers: average lesion density (HU); modified net water uptake (mNWU in %); total volume (mL); and hypodense (≤ 26 HU) volume (mL). DLNCCT biomarkers were associated with reversed 90-day ordinal modified Rankin Scale (genOR [95% CI]).

RESULTS: We used 218/762 train/test cases. Dice was 0.30 ± 0.30 between DLNCCT and manual segmentation, 0.22 ± 0.25 between DLNCCT-DWI, and 0.15 ± 0.22/0.21 ± 0.24 between CTP (rCBF < 30%/< 38%)-DWI. DLNCCT-DWI biomarker agreement was -1 HU (95% CI: -7; 6) for average density (CCC: 0.71), 4.9% (95% CI: -7.0; 16.8) for mNWU (CCC: 0.35), -16 mL (95% CI: -108; 76) for total volume (CCC: 0.57), and -4 mL (95% CI: -31; 23) for hypodense lesion volume (CCC: 0.75). Average lesion density (1.11 [95% CI: 1.06; 1.16]) and hypodense volume (0.85 [95% CI: 0.72; 0.99]) were associated with 90-day mRS.

CONCLUSION: Spatial and biomarker agreement between DLNCCT and DWI was suboptimal but comparable to CTP-DWI. Nevertheless, DLNCCT-derived average lesion density and hypodense volume were associated with functional outcomes.

KEY POINTS: Question Deep-learning models segment ischemic tissue on NCCT, but their spatial overlap and accuracy of imaging biomarker assessment relative to DWI and CTP core remain unclear. Findings Deep-learning NCCT segmentation showed good agreement with DWI in measuring hypodense (≤ 26 HU) volumes (- 4 mL [95% CI: -31; 23]; CCC 0.75). Clinical relevance Despite limited spatial overlap, NCCT-derived deep learning biomarkers showed agreement comparable to DWI, with improved performance in patients with poor ASPECTS and collateral scores. Hypodense volume and average lesion density were associated with functional outcome.

articles.title: PRKAG2 Cardiac Syndrome: A Comprehensive Review of Clinical Manifestations, Pathophysiological Mechanisms, and Precision Medicine Frontiers.
articles.abstract: PRKAG2 cardiac syndrome (PCS) is a metabolic storage cardiomyopathy caused by pathogenic variants in the PRKAG2 gene encoding the γ2-subunit of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK). It is defined by left ventricular hypertrophy, ventricular preexcitation and progressive conduction system disease accompanied by early-onset atrial arrhythmias. This review systematically evaluates PCS, outlining its clinical manifestations, genotype-phenotype spectrum, and diagnostic clues that distinguish it from sarcomeric hypertrophy. It explores underlying pathophysiological mechanisms, detailing how chronic AMPK activation drives glycogen accumulation via allosteric G6P activation of glycogen synthase, following a biphasic temporal model from early GLUT4-mediated glucose flooding to late metabolic feedback suppression. It further examines how Akt-mTOR hyperactivation fosters hypertrophy and how activated fasciculoventricular pathways mediate preexcitation. Finally, it reviews current supportive clinical management and highlights emerging precision medicine frontiers-including RNA-based silencing, pharmacological pathway inhibitors, and CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing-that aim to shift PCS care toward targeted disease modification.

articles.title: Hydrothermal catalyst-free saponification of post-consumer colorless PET: response surface methodology approach.
articles.journal: Environmental science and pollution research international
articles.abstract: Hydrothermal catalyst-free alkaline hydrolysis of post-consumer colorless polyethylene terephthalate (PET) was investigated using response surface methodology based on a three-factor Box-Behnken design (BBD). Reaction temperature (135-155 °C), reaction time (2-4 h), and NaOH concentration (2-4 M) were varied in 15 experimental runs, and PET degradation and gravimetric terephthalic acid (TPA) recovery were quantified. PET degradation ranged from 77.98 to 100.00%, while TPA recovery ranged from 68.72 to 91.41%. A maximum PET degradation of 100.00% was observed at 145 °C, 3 h, and 3 M NaOH, whereas the maximum TPA recovery of 91.41% was obtained at 155 °C, 3 h, and 2 M NaOH. Within the fitted PET degradation model, reaction temperature and the temperature-NaOH concentration interaction were statistically significant individual terms; however, the overall PET degradation model was not statistically significant (P = 0.108). The TPA recovery model was also not statistically significant (P = 0.521), indicating limited predictive capability. A selected compromise condition of 155 °C, 3.5 h, and 2 M NaOH was experimentally evaluated in triplicate, yielding complete PET degradation and 86.11 ± 2.45% TPA recovery. An exploratory particle-size assessment showed complete PET degradation for the tested dimensions of 0.5-2.0 cm under this condition. XRD and FTIR supported the identification of the recovered crystalline products as TPA, although quantitative chemical purity was not determined. These findings demonstrate the laboratory-scale feasibility of catalyst-free hydrothermal alkaline hydrolysis of cleaned colorless post-consumer PET within the investigated operating conditions, while identifying limitations in statistical prediction, complete mass balance, product-purity assessment, and scale-up evaluation.

articles.title: Clinical utility and implementation of genomic newborn screening: findings from the SNUseq Baby Project.
articles.journal: European journal of human genetics : EJHG
articles.abstract: Genomic newborn screening (NBS) has emerged as a powerful complement to conventional screening; however, its clinical utility remains to be fully established. We conducted a prospective multicenter pilot study within the Seoul National University Hospital network from November 2025 to February 2026. A panel of 419 genes was curated by a multidisciplinary expert team based on early childhood onset, disease severity, the presence of an asymptomatic window, and the local availability of effective treatments. Genome sequencing was performed on 399 newborns, including six monozygotic twin pairs analyzed as single data points. In addition to 385 inborn neonates, 14 neonates referred because of abnormal conventional NBS results were included. As a result, the screen-positive rate was 1.3% (5/393). Two positive cases with variants in SLC25A15 and MYO15A were missed by conventional NBS, and we also identified three cases harboring pathogenic variants in arrhythmia-associated genes, a category inherently beyond the scope of conventional screening. Among 49 neonates with abnormal conventional NBS results, all were negative on genomic NBS. The median turnaround time from sample collection to final report was 26 days. Genomic NBS demonstrated favorable precision and complementary clinical utility beyond conventional screening. Regular multidisciplinary curation of target genes and long-term longitudinal follow-up are essential for successful clinical implementation.

articles.title: Isoform-resolved sequencing uncovers a hidden code inside RNA methylation changes in heart failure.
Comprehensive m6A landscape from direct RNA sequencing reveals SYNPO2L RNA isoform regulation mechanisms in heart failure.
articles.abstract: Accumulating evidence suggests that epitranscriptomic regulation, particularly the m6A modification, contributes to heart failure progression. However, modification dynamics are not yet mapped and studied at base resolution and transcript isoform level. Here we use Nanopore direct RNA sequencing to profile m6A remodeling at transcriptome-wide and site-specific resolution in a mouse heart failure model. We identify thousands of differentially methylated sites with distinct sequence motifs and associations with RNA regulatory and cardiac function processes. Cross-species comparison reveals conserved m6A regulatory features in mouse and human heart failure. Isoform-resolved analysis further uncovers co/posttranscriptional regulation events involving isoform switching and m6A regulation in the SYNPO2L transcript. Mechanistically, m6A modification, alternative promoter usage and associated regulatory elements collectively explain this observation. Overall, our study provides a comprehensive, high-resolution characterization of m6A landscape and its remodeling in heart failure. Isoform-level regulation exemplifies an underappreciated shaping of RNA expression and modification.

articles.title: Associations of long-term exposure to air pollution with glucose homeostasis biomarkers and diabetes-related comorbidities in people with recent-onset type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
