AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: Air pollution (AP) contributes to diabetes progression and comorbidities, but underlying mechanisms remain unclear, as no observational studies have applied gold-standard phenotyping or distinguished between the effects of type 1 diabetes, type 2 diabetes and diabetes subtypes. We examined whether AP exposure was associated with glucose homeostasis biomarkers and diabetes-related comorbidities in people with recent-onset type 1 diabetes, type 2 diabetes and diabetes subtypes.

METHODS: This cross-sectional analysis is based on data from 1120 participants in the German Diabetes Study (417 with type 1 diabetes and 703 with type 2 diabetes). The glucose homeostasis biomarkers used were HbA1c, insulin sensitivity (clamp-derived M value), insulin secretion (glucagon-stimulated C-peptide6min) and insulin clearance (clamp derived). Diabetes-related comorbidities included CVD risk (SCORE2-Diabetes),  V ˙ O 2 max    as an indicator of cardiorespiratory fitness, albuminuria as a marker of kidney function and the presence of distal sensorimotor polyneuropathy (DSPN). Five-year means of exposure to AP (particulate matter [PM] with diameters of <2.5 μm [PM2.5] and <10 μm [PM10] and nitrogen dioxide [NO2] before baseline at individual residential addresses were examined. Associations between each exposure-outcome pair were estimated per 1 IQR increase in air pollutants using multivariable linear and logistic regression. Two-pollutant analysis, cumulative risk index (CRI) analysis and insulin-treated type 1 diabetes model analysis were performed as sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: Among those with type 1 diabetes, higher PM2.5 was associated with higher HbA1c (exp[β]=1.07 [95% CI 1.03, 1.11]), insulin secretion (exp[β]=1.19 [95% CI 1.03, 1.36]), lower  V ˙ O 2 max    (exp[β]=0.94 [95% CI 0.89, 0.99]) and higher albuminuria (exp[β]=1.72 [95% CI 1.34, 2.20]). Among type 2 diabetes, higher PM2.5 was associated with higher HbA1c (exp[β]=1.04 [95% CI 1.01, 1.06]), lower insulin sensitivity (β=-0.42 [95% CI -0.82, -0.03]), lower insulin secretion (exp[β]=0.94 [95% CI 0.89, 0.99]), lower insulin clearance (exp[β]=0.92 [95% CI 0.87, 0.98]), higher CVD risk (exp[β]=1.07 [95% CI 0.99, 1.16]), lower  V ˙ O 2 max    (exp[β]=0.91 [95% CI 0.88, 0.95]), higher albuminuria (exp[β]=1.71 [95% CI 1.41, 2.08]) and higher odds of DSPN (OR 1.53 [95% CI 1.02, 2.32]). Similar associations were observed for PM10 and NO2. Associations were directionally attenuated in two-pollutant models but remained consistent in CRI and insulin-treated type 1 diabetes analyses. Differences were observed in associations between diabetes subtypes.

CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: Long-term AP exposure was consistently associated with higher HbA1c; reduced whole-body insulin sensitivity, secretion and clearance; and an increased burden of diabetes-related comorbidities in type 2 diabetes. Associations were less consistent in type 1 diabetes. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01055093.

articles.title: [Prolonged mechanical ventilation after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Following coronary bypass surgery, postoperative intensive care plays a central role in the subsequent course of the illness. It is well known that patients with prolonged mechanical ventilation have an increased risk of developing numerous secondary organ complications and consequently have higher morbidity and mortality. The objective of this study was to validate established risk factors for prolonged postoperative mechanical ventilation after isolated coronary bypass surgery in a recent, representative patient collective.

METHODS: In this retrospective, single-center study, all patients who underwent isolated coronary bypass surgery in 2024 and subsequently received interdisciplinary intensive care at the Ulm University Clinic were included.

RESULTS: The 312 patients included in the study were between 45 and 85 years old; 84% (n = 262) were male. The median ventilation time for all patients was 15 h (Q1 = 11 h; Q3 = 21 h), whereby 19.5% (n = 61) required prolonged mechanical ventilation (PMV). In the multiple logistic regression analysis, intraoperative perfusion time (OR = 1.01; 95% CI 1.0-1.02; p = 0.04) and postoperative peak lactate (OR = 1.26; 95% CI 1.12-1.41; p < 0.001) were significant independent risk factors for PMV. The PMV group also had significantly lower oxygenation indices (Horovitz index = paO2/FiO2), more positive fluid balances on the first and cumulatively on the second postoperative day, longer ischemia and surgical times, and higher European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation (EuroSCORE) scores. Hospital mortality was significantly higher at 8.2% (n = 5) in the PMV group than in the non-PMV group at 0.8% (n = 2).

CONCLUSION: A comprehensive risk profile for prolonged mechanical ventilation is an essential component of intensive care risk stratification and treatment planning. It enables a differentiated assessment of severity and complexity of underlying diseases and thereby associated organ dysfunction. Against this backdrop, necessary intensive care interventions can be initiated early and potentially contribute to improve treatment outcomes.

articles.title: TSL-phosphorylated SGS3 shifts RDR6 from terminal nucleotidyltransferase to polymerase activity to promote RNAi and immunity.
articles.abstract: RNA-dependent RNA polymerase 6 (RDR6) and suppressor of gene silencing 3 (SGS3) form small interfering RNA (siRNA) bodies to synthesize double-stranded RNA, triggering RNA interference. Like viral RDRs, RDR6 not only has polymerase action but also has terminal nucleotidyltransferase activity that tails single-stranded RNA templates, causing their degradation. How the dual activities are controlled is unknown. Here we discovered that Arabidopsis Tousled (TSL) predominantly phosphorylates Ser65 and Ser68, located in the intrinsically disordered region of SGS3, to promote RNA interference. SGS3 phosphomimics trigger the formation of liquid-like siRNA bodies but have lower RNA-binding affinity, thereby enhancing RDR6 polymerase activity to synthesize double-stranded RNA for downstream processing by Dicer-like 2/4. Conversely, hypo-phosphorylated SGS3 forms larger and solid-like aggregates that hold RNA templates with stronger affinity, thereby prompting RDR6 terminal nucleotidyltransferase activity. Moreover, viral infection drives SGS3 hypo-phosphorylation and aggregation, suppressing viral siRNA production and host defence. Collectively, stoichiometric phosphorylation of SGS3 switches two distinct activities of RDR6 to tune RNA silencing and host anti-viral immunity.

articles.title: Regulation of the 22-nt antiviral silencing pathway in tomato by two RNA viruses.
articles.abstract: RNA silencing plays a central role in plant antiviral defence, in which viral RNA is processed into small RNAs (sRNAs) that guide Argonaute-mediated cleavage of viral transcripts. Among these, 22-nucleotide (nt) sRNAs are unique in their ability to trigger secondary sRNA production, thereby amplifying transitive silencing. In tomato, this 22-nt antiviral pathway is strongly activated upon virus infection through the upregulation of DCL2b, yet the underlying mechanism has remained unclear. miR6026, generated by DCL2b and targeting DCL2b itself, forms a feedback loop that fine-tunes this response. Here we show that tobacco mosaic virus (TMV) and tomato bushy stunt virus (TBSV) activate DCL2b transcription via the Dof16 transcription factor. Transcription of MIR6026 is also activated by both TMV and TBSV, while viral infection promotes DCL2b relocalization towards the cytoplasm, preventing pri-miR6026 processing into mature miR6026. This redistribution is associated with reduced phosphorylation of DCL2b at Tyr69, which weakens its interaction with importin-α and limits its nuclear localization. Notably, Arabidopsis DCL2 exhibits a similar virus-induced relocalization pattern, highlighting a conserved mechanism that enhances antiviral silencing during infection while minimizing off-target effects on host genes under normal conditions.

articles.title: Avascular necrosis of the femur following COVID-19: an updated systematic review.
articles.journal: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: One of the complications of COVID-19 infection is avascular necrosis of the femoral head. To date, various studies have reported a wide range of osteonecrosis of the femoral head in patients with COVID-19. The previous systematic review included only 14 studies. So, this systematic review aims to update the findings of these studies.

METHODS: Databases such as PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, PsycINFO, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were systematically searched by two independent researchers on April 1st, 2024.

RESULTS: A literature search revealed 1229 records, 161 full-texts were evaluated, and finally, 55 studies remained for systematic review. Fifty-five studies were included in this systematic review. Four studies were cross-sectional studies, six were retrospective studies, and the remaining (45studies) were case reports or case-series studies. Totally, 864 cases were included. Except for 12 studies, 43 studies reported the administration of steroid therapy in included cases. The most common underlying conditions were hypertension, followed by diabetes. In 274 (31.7%) of included cases, AVN was bilateral, and both hips were involved. In some studies, non-surgical treatments-including supplement therapy, anticoagulant therapy, physiotherapy, and hyperbaric oxygen therapy-were administered. Several studies reported symptomatic improvement in patients treated with the core decompression approach. Total hip arthroplasty (THA) was the most commonly used surgical treatment.

CONCLUSIONS: Avascular necrosis of the femoral head in cases that have survived COVID-19 should be considered carefully as early diagnosis helps to preserve the joint and its function.

articles.title: Cardiac and vascular involvement in protein misfolding diseases.
articles.abstract: Protein misfolding diseases impose a substantial and often under-recognized burden on both the heart and vasculature. In this Review, we outline how the failure of proteostasis drives oligomer toxicity, amyloid deposition and inflammation in cardiovascular tissues as well as microvascular injury and thrombosis, which culminate in cardiovascular dysfunction. We define the cardiovascular hallmarks of protein misfolding diseases, focusing on transthyretin amyloidosis and immunoglobulin light chain amyloidosis, and the disease-specific organ tropisms. We examine neurodegenerative proteinopathies affecting the heart-vascular-brain axis, highlighting how amyloid-β and α-synuclein accumulation contribute to dysautonomia, vascular dysfunction and adverse outcomes. We summarize diagnostic pathways and clinical indicators for early diagnosis of cardiovascular involvement in protein misfolding diseases and review established and emerging biomarkers of vascular stress and proteotoxic load. We also map the current therapeutic landscape for protein misfolding diseases, including strategies to reduce the synthesis of precursor proteins or promote the stabilization of mature proteins as well as fibril-directed therapies, and discuss remaining challenges, such as residual cardiovascular risk, that support the development of mechanism-informed therapeutic approaches. Finally, we propose a research roadmap that prioritizes systematic cardiovascular screening in at-risk populations, harmonized methods for vascular phenotyping, biomarker-anchored mechanistic clinical trials across protein misfolding diseases, and artificial intelligence-based approaches and precision medicine frameworks that integrate genotype or distinct protein conformational strain patterns, organ tropism and dynamic proteostasis measures.

articles.title: Kidney stones.
articles.abstract: Kidney stones form as a result of the accumulation of mineral deposits on an organic matrix. They are more common in patients with metabolic and/or anatomical abnormalities that lead to urine supersaturation, have a prevalence of ~10% and recur in ~50% of patients at 5-10 years of follow-up. Known risk factors for kidney stones are obesity and metabolic syndrome, anatomical abnormalities leading to urinary stasis, dietary habits and genetic factors leading to potential dysregulation of urinary calcium, uric acid, oxalate and cystine concentrations. Kidney stones are diagnosed based on imaging, including ultrasonography, radiography and CT. Minimally invasive treatments, including shock wave lithotripsy, ureteroscopy and percutaneous nephrolithotripsy, have largely replaced open surgery in kidney stone management. These modalities can achieve stone clearance, while minimizing complication rates, improving health-related quality of life and enabling a quicker return to daily activities compared to open surgery. Technological advances, such as advanced laser fibres and devices and suction technology, which are used during minimally invasive treatments, are further improving clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Human serum albumin abundance, function and removal in chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract: Human serum albumin, the most abundant protein in human plasma, exerts a multitude of physiological functions that extend beyond its canonical roles in oncotic pressure and solute transport. It acts as a dynamic interface in redox regulation, toxin clearance, immune modulation and pharmacokinetics. In chronic kidney disease, dialysis and transplantation, albumin has diagnostic and therapeutic relevance far surpassing that of a nutritional marker. Emerging insights into the structure-function relationships of albumin, including its binding dynamics, redox isoforms and post-translational modifications, challenge the current paradigm of albumin in chronic kidney disease, which focuses on preserving quantity, and suggest that a shift towards restoring quality might have clinical benefits. Here, we propose two new conceptual frameworks, the 'albumin paradox', which reconsiders albumin removal during dialysis as a potentially therapeutic mechanism, and the 'inflammation-mitigation hypothesis', which positions albumin functionality as a target in extracorporeal immune modulation. Integrating biophysical, pathophysiological and clinical perspectives, we aim to reframe albumin from a merely passive bystander and laboratory parameter to a modifiable determinant of systemic health and disease.

articles.title: Cyber-pirates: the perils of agentic AI for the protection of healthcare data.
articles.journal: Australasian psychiatry : bulletin of Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists
articles.abstract: The recent unauthorised access by AI agents of Australian Medicare Statistics is alarming. This unauthorised access attack, or "hack," has occurred in the context of similar hacks on Hugging Face and RubyGems by swarms of AI agents acting together. AI agentic hacks represent a substantial cyber security threat, both for large and small organisations, and for sensitive data, such as in healthcare records. We provide a succinct update on these events and basic advice on defending healthcare data against hacks by AI agents.

articles.title: Role of C-reactive protein response to antibiotic therapy in children with a ventriculo-peritoneal shunt infection: a retrospective study.
Climate Change Concern, Preventive Hope, and Disaster Literacy: A Descriptive Correlational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Climate change poses serious risks to public health and psychosocial well-being. Understanding the emotional and cognitive factors associated with climate-related behaviors is essential for developing effective public health and nursing interventions.

PURPOSE: The study aimed to determine adults' levels of climate change concern, hope for prevention, and disaster literacy, and to examine the relationships among these variables.

METHODS: This descriptive correlational study was conducted with 615 adults selected through convenience sampling. Data were collected using the Climate Change Worry Scale, the Climate Change Hope Scale, and the Disaster Literacy Scale. Descriptive statistics, Pearson's correlation, and multiple linear regression analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Participants reported moderate levels of concern, hope, and disaster literacy. Positive but weak correlations were found among the three variables (r ≈ 0.23-0.35, p < 0.01). Hope for prevention (β = 0.30, p < 0.001) and climate change worry (β = 0.13, p = 0.001) were positively associated with disaster literacy in multiple linear regression analysis. The model explained 13.1% of the variance in disaster literacy.

CONCLUSIONS: Relationships among climate change concern, hope for prevention, and disaster literacy were statistically significant but weak. Enhancing public knowledge in this area may positively influence individuals' perceptions and emotional responses to climate change.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PUBLIC HEALTH NURSING: Public health nurses familiar with community contexts should take an active role in raising awareness about disaster preparedness and climate-related risks. Community education initiatives should address disaster literacy alongside climate change worry and hope for prevention, and their effects should be evaluated in future intervention studies.

articles.title: One less ouch: Implementation of Continuous Glucose Monitoring in the treatment of pediatric Diabetes Ketoacidosis.
Free latissimus dorsi flap reconstruction for complex skull osteomyelitis and osteoradionecrosis with selective vascularized serratus anterior fascia dural repair: a retrospective series of 13 cases.
articles.journal: International journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery
articles.abstract: Cranial osteomyelitis, osteoradionecrosis, and persistent calvarial bone exposure with dural involvement are severe conditions associated with high morbidity. In irradiated or infected fields, vascularized tissue reconstruction is essential for durable healing. This article reports our experience with free latissimus dorsi (LD) flap reconstruction for complex cranial osteomyelitis, osteoradionecrosis, and calvarial exposure, with use of vascularized serratus anterior fascia for dural repair. A retrospective single-center study included adult patients who underwent microsurgical reconstruction for cranial osteomyelitis, osteoradionecrosis, or exposed skull bone with dural involvement between 2016 and 2026. All patients were reconstructed using a free LD muscle flap; vascularized serratus anterior fascia harvested on the same thoracodorsal pedicle was used when dural repair was required. Primary outcomes were flap survival and infection control. Thirteen patients were included (mean age 60.3 years). Prior radiotherapy was present in 69% and active infection in 92%. Dural involvement occurred in 54% of cases. Cervical vessels were used in 62% of reconstructions. Complete flap failure occurred in three patients (23%), with one successful salvage, resulting in final flap survival of 85%. At a median follow-up of 15.5 months, 62% of patients had stable reconstruction without recurrent infection. Mortality (38%) was mainly related to underlying oncologic or neurological disease. In this high-risk cohort, free LD muscle flap reconstruction provided vascularized soft-tissue coverage for complex infected or irradiated cranial defects. In selected patients with dural involvement, vascularized serratus anterior fascia allowed simultaneous dural repair. These findings support selective use of this chimeric configuration when dural reconstruction is required.

articles.title: Developing content validity of a questionnaire exploring various relationships with one's body in obesity: A Delphi expert consensus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Factors contributing to weight variation, and specifically the perception of one's own body, are major elements to take into account in the obesity clinical pathway. The aim of the study was to develop and test the content validity of a multidimensional self-administered questionnaire exploring body-relatedness.

METHODS: A review guided the development of the questionnaire. Fifty-two dimensions and 261 items were extracted. A Delphi method was then performed with 23 experts and 7 patients suffering from obesity. In the 4-Round Delphi, the group rated their agreement on the utility and the relevance of dimensions and items, respectively. The consensus was reached when 75% of members were in agreement.

RESULTS: Consensus was reached for a 38-dimension and 65-item questionnaire covering 11 domains: (1) body image satisfaction, (2) anxiety about the whole or parts of the body, (3) deviation of logical thinking from reality, (4) socio-cultural influence on appearance, (5) behaviour related to body image, (6) perception of interoceptive signals, (7) perception of health related to body relationships, (8) gap between silhouette perception and reality, (9) reaction to hunger, (10) satisfaction with the sensation generated by touch, and (11) social distances.

CONCLUSIONS: The new clinical tool is multidimensional, the items are specific, easy to understand and to interpret in the clinical care pathway. Through this new tool, we hope to raise professionals' awareness of complex body-related disorders.

articles.title: Analysis of the situation of nurses in diabetes care and therapeutic education in hospital and primary care settings in Spain: a cross-sectional and comparative study (ASENET-es).
authors: Therapeutic Education Group of the Spanish Society of Diabetes
articles.abstract:
AIM: To describe and compare the situation of nurses dedicated to Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support (DSMES) in Spain, in both hospital care (HC) and primary care (PC) settings of the Spanish National Health Care System.

PARTICIPANTS AND METHODS: Observational, descriptive, comparative, and cross-sectional study focused on nurses dedicated to DSMES in the Spanish public health care system. All nurses attending people with diabetes (PwD) in HC and a randomized selection in PC were invited to participate through an online survey. Diabetes training, work setting, type of care, professional role, outcome indicators, and job satisfaction were recorded.

RESULTS: A total of 253 hospitals and 963 primary health centers (PC) participated. A total of 1060 surveys were analyzed (34.53% HC). Greater diabetes training (P < .001), more DSMES programs (P < .001), more group and telehealth interventions (P < .001), and greater development of advanced practice roles (P < .001) were observed in HC than in PC. In HC, programs were mainly focused on type 1 diabetes (74.32% vs 24.35%; P < .001), whereas in PC they focused on type 2 diabetes (58.65% vs 51.64%; P = .029). Technology-based interventions were more developed in HC than in PC (65.69% HC vs 18.10% PC; P < .001).

CONCLUSIONS: This first national study shows that specific diabetes training, use of programs, and development of advanced practice roles are greater among nurses in HC than in PC. Structured program criteria are not met in half of the cases. The health care setting influences nurse training and educational activities.

articles.title: Influenza vaccination in people with diabetes mellitus: Clinical rationale, current evidence, and implementation challenges.
articles.abstract: People with diabetes mellitus (DM) are at increased risk of hospitalisation, complications, and mortality from influenza due to immune dysfunction, metabolic imbalance, and a higher incidence of cardiovascular events. This narrative review, targeted at clinical practice in Spain, summarises recent evidence on diabetes and influenza vaccination and explores barriers to its implementation. Evidence shows that annual vaccination in people with DM reduces hospitalisations, cardiovascular events, and mortality, particularly in those aged ≥ 60 years or with comorbidities; higher-immunogenicity formulations (high-dose or adjuvanted) may provide an additional benefit in these populations. In addition, coadministration with other adult vaccines is feasible. Person-centred recommendations for endocrinology and general practice are proposed to improve suboptimal coverage. Influenza vaccination is cost-effective and may help reduce inappropriate antibiotic use and antimicrobial resistance in this population.

articles.title: [Hypersensitivity reactions to iodinated contrast media].
authors: les membres du groupe FISARD (French Investigators for Skin Adverse Reactions to Drugs) de la Société Française de Dermatologie
articles.abstract: More than 75 million iodinated contrast media (ICM) are injected worldwide each year. These molecules cause hypersensitivity reactions in 0.5% to 3% of cases, causing real harm to patients. Reactions to ICM are classified into two groups according to their onset time. Immediate hypersensitivity reactions (less than 1hour after injection) include a variety of skin, respiratory, digestive or hemodynamic clinical signs. The most serious manifestation is anaphylactic shock. Non-immediate hypersensitivity reactions (between 1hour and 7days after injection) mainly present as a maculopapular rash. Severe forms may be observed, such as DRESS (drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms). The diagnosis and management of patients is based on skin testing. Skin tests confirm the involvement of a suspected ICM and guide the choice of an alternative molecule during a provocation test or a re-exposure. In vitro tests have low sensitivity and are used less frequently. Premedication protocols are controversial and their use is limited. Serious hypersensitivity reactions must be investigated in specialized centers after assessing the risk-benefit ratio for the patient.

articles.title: What's Hot in Coronary Artery Disease? Innovation With Consideration of Scale and Equity.
Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT and Grok Responses to Common Patient Questions about Mitral Regurgitation.
Implementation of an Accelerated Treatment Pathway for Patients with Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contemporary guideline-directed medical therapy for patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) includes four classes of drugs with independent and additive benefits. While current guidelines recommend early initiation and rapid dose titration of quadruple therapy, its effective and safe implementation in real-world clinical practice remains uncertain.

METHOD: A nurse-led clinical pathway was developed to support early in-hospital initiation of quadruple therapy and rapid post-discharge titration for patients admitted with HFrEF. The Accelerated Treatment (ACT) Pathway was introduced for patients admitted under the Cardiology Service at Te Toka Tumai Auckland Hospital, New Zealand. The pathway involves initiating low-dose quadruple therapy before discharge, followed by weekly clinic visits to facilitate individualised drug up-titration over a 4-week period. Follow-up echocardiography was performed after 3 months to re-assess left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) according to usual clinical practice. This report describes the early experience with the ACT Pathway, including drug use, safety outcomes, and changes in LVEF in response to treatment.

RESULTS: Between March 2023 and October 2024, 103 patients proceeded with the planned pathway. The mean age was 57 years, 20% were women, 67% were non-New Zealand European (including 17% Māori and 27% Pacific), 59% had non-ischaemic heart failure, and the median LVEF was 27%. At hospital discharge, quadruple therapy was successfully initiated, with all patients receiving renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) inhibitors, 96% beta blockers, 87% spironolactone, and 55% sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors. The proportion of patients meeting the performance measure (≥50% of the maximum dosage) increased from discharge to 4 weeks as follows: RAAS inhibitors, 31%-82%; and beta blockers, 35%-69% (all p<0.001); and the proportion of patients receiving mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists increased from 87% to 92%. Loop diuretic use decreased: only 40% of patients were still receiving a daily dose of diuretic at 4 weeks. There were no hospital admissions due to hypotension or acute kidney injury. Median LVEF was 27% (interquartile range [IQR] 20-33) during hospitalisation and 43% (IQR 34-50) after 3 months, an overall increase of 13 percentage points (p<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: The implementation of the ACT Pathway successfully achieved its goal of safe, early initiation and rapid titration of quadruple therapy to maximum tolerated doses within 4 weeks in patients admitted with HFrEF in a real-world setting. This pathway has demonstrated the potential for substantial benefits for patients, whānau, and the health care system in a New Zealand context.

articles.title: What's Hot in Heart Failure Management: An Updated Perspective on Guidelines, Populations, and Innovation From the 2026 Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand Annual Scientific Meeting.

Variations in Access to Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Versus Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement by Socioeconomic Factors: A Retrospective Population-Level Study in New South Wales, Australia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite increasing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) activity in Australia in recent years, patient access to TAVI remains limited and is often more complex than access to surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR). The aim of this study was to identify socioeconomic factors associated with the likelihood of receiving TAVI versus SAVR in New South Wales (NSW), Australia.

METHODS: Data from the NSW Admitted Patient Data Collection were used to compare the clinical and socioeconomic profiles of patients aged ≥65 years who underwent either TAVI or SAVR between 1 November 2017 and 28 February 2022. Multiple logistic regression analyses were performed on the overall patient cohort and on subgroups defined by age groups, hospital type and funding type.

RESULTS: The study included 6,493 patients (mean age: 79.1 years, 35.5% female) who underwent aortic valve replacement (SAVR=3,294; TAVI=3,199). The odds of receiving TAVI versus SAVR increased significantly with age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] for patients aged 85 years and older versus those aged 75-84 years: 12.3, 95% CI: 9.99-15.2). Patients from the most disadvantaged socioeconomic areas had lower odds of receiving TAVI than those from the least disadvantaged areas (aOR:0.58, 95% CI: 0.47-0.73). Patients with private health insurance/Department of Veterans Affairs (PHI/DVA) funding were more likely to receive TAVI than SAVR (aOR: 3.29, 95% CI: 2.61-4.14), with this finding consistent across age groups and even more pronounced in patients treated in public hospitals (aOR: 5.82, 95% CI: 4.40-7.70).

CONCLUSIONS: Our study highlights significant variations in TAVI access based on age, socioeconomic status of area of residence, and funding type. These findings underscore the need for policy settings that promote equitable access and ensure that procedural choices for aortic valve replacement reflect clinical needs.

articles.title: Are there differences in the optical properties of subtractively and additively manufactured zirconia restorations? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
STATEMENT OF PROBLEM: Whether additively manufactured (AM) and subtractively manufactured (SM) zirconia differ in optical behavior under staining and aging remains uncertain.

PURPOSE: The purpose of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to evaluate differences in color stability (ΔE), translucency (TP), and translucency change (ΔTP) between AM and SM zirconia after aging.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: An electronic search was conducted across the PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar databases through October 2025. Eligible studies were English-language in vitro investigations directly comparing AM and SM zirconia for ΔE, TP, or ΔTP. The data were pooled using a random-effects model and expressed as weighted mean differences (WMDs) with 95% confidence intervals. Heterogeneity was analyzed using Cochran Q and I² statistics, and publication bias was examined with the Egger test and trim-and-fill correction. Risk of bias was assessed using the RoBDEMAT tool.

RESULTS: From 4218 records, 5 in vitro studies were included. AM zirconia showed lower ΔE (WMD=-0.226; 95% CI: -0.349 to -0.103; P<.001; I²=97.1%), lower TP (WMD=-4.191; 95% CI: -4.958 to -3.423; P<.001; I²=98.0%), and greater ΔTP after aging (WMD=0.887; 95% CI: 0.091 to 1.683; P=.029; I²=97.0%) compared with SM zirconia.

CONCLUSIONS: AM zirconia demonstrated less color alteration, lower initial translucency, and higher translucency variation after aging than SM zirconia. However, these optical differences remained within clinically acceptable thresholds.

articles.title: Deep learning denoising and positron range correction of clinical [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-TOC PET images.
articles.abstract: PET image quality degradation due to positron range effects in high-energy positron-emitting radionuclides such as Gallium-68 (68Ga) can be mitigated by applying positron range correction (PRC). Deep learning (DL) models have been shown to improve image quality by reducing image noise. This study aimed to evaluate a DL model for simultaneous denoising and 68Ga-specific PRC in clinical [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-TOC PET scans. Three different U-Net-based DL models were trained to map reduced-count PET images reconstructed without PRC (25%, 33%, or 50% of acquired counts) to full-count PET images reconstructed with tissue-independent PRC (FC-PRC). The generated reduced-count-enhanced images (RCE-25%, RCE-33%, RCE-50%) were evaluated using the mean standardized uptake value (SUVmean) in liver and lung, noise levels in liver, and maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) of soft tissue lesions. Three experienced nuclear medicine physicians assessed the overall image quality (OIQ), overall diagnostic confidence (ODC), and lesion detectability (sensitivity, specificity, accuracy). Compared to FC-PRC, RCE-33% and RCE-50% exhibited similar noise, whereas RCE-25% showed substantial residual noise. CNR was reduced for RCE-33% (-5.6%, p=0.001) and RCE-25% (-8.0%, p<0.001), but was comparable for RCE-50%. All reduced-count-enhanced images demonstrated lower SUVmax (RCE-25%: -3.8%, p=0.02; RCE-33%: -7.0%, p<0.001; RCE-50%: -5.2%, p<0.001). RCE-33% and RCE-50% achieved non-inferior OIQ and ODC compared to FC-PRC, while RCE-25% demonstrated only non-inferior ODC. All reduced-count-enhanced images showed high sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy (>90%). The proposed DL-based approach achieved comparable noise and image quality down to 50% of counts. Although it did not outperform the reconstruction-based PRC, its benefit lies in simultaneous denoising and PRC in a single step.

articles.title: Acute coronary thrombosis following anabolic-androgenic steroid use in a female athlete: A case report.
articles.abstract: Anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) use has been associated with adverse cardiovascular events, including myocardial infarction. Proposed mechanisms include alterations in hemostasis and fibrinolysis, endothelial dysfunction, and abnormal vascular reactivity, potentially increasing susceptibility to coronary thrombosis. However, establishing a causal relationship in an individual patient requires careful exclusion of alternative etiologies. We report the case of a 45-year-old female fitness coach who presented with acute myocardial infarction following a six-week course of oxandrolone and methenolone in preparation for a bodybuilding competition. She had no conventional cardiovascular risk factors. Electrocardiography showed ST-segment elevation in the inferior leads. Coronary angiography revealed a large non-occlusive thrombus in the mid-right coronary artery with preserved TIMI 3 distal flow and no obstructive coronary artery disease. Optical coherence tomography confirmed a large adherent thrombus without visible intimal rupture. An extensive thrombophilia and autoimmune workup was unremarkable, and no cardiac source of embolism or in-hospital arrhythmia was identified. The temporal relationship with AAS exposure suggested a possible causal link. The patient was managed conservatively with intensive antithrombotic therapy, and follow-up coronary angiography at two months demonstrated complete thrombus resolution. This report highlights the potential association between AAS exposure and acute coronary thrombosis and discusses possible pathophysiological mechanisms, the diagnostic role of intracoronary imaging, and the individualized management of this uncommon presentation.

articles.title: [Evaluation of a citizen conference on patient and citizen advisory boards in general practice research networks - Analysis of participant evaluations and future prospects].
articles.journal: Zeitschrift fur Evidenz, Fortbildung und Qualitat im Gesundheitswesen
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Initiative DESAM-ForNet has created a nationwide infrastructure for patient participation in general medicine by establishing patient/citizen advisory boards. To provide an opportunity for exchange, the Dresden/Frankfurt General Practice Research Network (SaxoForN) organized a citizen conference in 2024. The added value, prerequisites, challenges and prospects of patient participation were discussed during a World Café and a panel discussion. An online survey was used to evaluate the conference program and format, as well as to gather feedback on participants' preferences and expectations regarding the future design of participatory structures.

METHODS: The online questionnaire contained closed and open questions, enabling participants to anonymously evaluate the conference and provide feedback. Quantitative data were evaluated using descriptive statistics, free-text responses were analyzed using content analysis.

RESULTS: 23 of the 28 advisory board members participated in the evaluation. The event and individual program sections achieved average scores ranging from 1.17 to 1.70 on a school grading cale. In their responses participants emphasized the open, appreciative atmosphere, the exchange of ideas in the World Café and the opportunity to network and gain new insights. At the same time, there was a clear desire to continue the exchange and to sustainably institutionalize the work of advisory boards.

DISCUSSION: The evaluation shows that nationwide exchanges between citizen advisory boards are considered highly beneficial in terms of satisfaction with the format, motivation, and networking. At the same time, important areas for structural development were identified.

CONCLUSION: The results highlight the potential of nationwide citizen conferences to promote networking, empowerment and knowledge sharing in general practice research. To ensure the long-term establishment of patient and citizen participation, it is necessary to permanently establish supraregional exchange formats, expand training opportunities for mutual learning, and structurally embed stable funding for the participation infrastructure.

articles.title: Ablation of Twin Atrioventricular Node-Mediated Macroreentrant Tachycardia in a Patient With Complex Heterotaxy Syndrome.
articles.abstract: Twin atrioventricular (AV) nodes constitute a rare and highly complex electrophysiological substrate for tachycardia in heterotaxy syndrome (complex cardiac heart disease). We present the case of an 18-year-old male with right atrial isomerism, asplenia, univentricular physiology, and a Glenn shunt, who presented with a regular wide-QRS tachycardia associated with severe hemodynamic decompensation. High-density electroanatomical mapping identified two distinct His bundle recordings separated by 20.3 mm. Together with two non-preexcited QRS morphologies and different conduction properties, these findings supported suspected twin AV node-mediated macroreentry, with proposed anterograde conduction via the inferior-posterior system and retrograde conduction through the superior-anterior system; complete circuit mapping and entrainment were not possible. Following an initial procedure complicated by pulseless electrical activity clinically attributed to post-cardioversion myocardial stunning, a second electrophysiological study prioritized functional characterization during sinus rhythm and atrial pacing without preablation reinduction of the clinical tachycardia. Selective ablation of the superior-anterior His region preserved AV conduction and was followed by noninducibility of the clinical tachycardia. A separate isthmus-dependent flutter was also ablated. At two months, clinical assessment, ECG, and 24-hour Holter monitoring showed no documented recurrence or new AV block.

articles.title: Differences in the Glucose Management Indicator Between Continuous Glucose Monitoring Systems.
articles.abstract:
AIM: The glucose management indicator (GMI) estimates HbA1c from continuous glucose monitoring (CGM)-derived mean glucose. We assessed whether this relationship differs between contemporary CGM systems.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this observational study, mean sensor glucose was derived from 2 months of CGM data preceding HbA1c measurement in adults with Type 1 diabetes using Dexcom (Dx) G6/G7 (n = 252) or Medtronic Guardian 4/Simplera (GSi) (n = 180). Device-specific GMI equations were derived using linear regression of measured HbA1c on mean sensor glucose and compared with the original GMI equation. For direct comparison of the Dx and GSi GMI equations, these GMI equations were combined, with 95% confidence intervals calculated using the delta method.

RESULTS: The Dx GMI equation yielded statistically significantly lower GMI values compared with the original GMI equation at mean sensor glucose levels < 13.7 mmol/L, with increasing differences at lower glucose levels. Conversely, at mean sensor glucose levels above 8.3 mmol/L, the GSi GMI equation yielded statistically significantly higher GMI values than the original GMI equation, with increasing differences at higher glucose levels. The Dx and GSi device-specific GMI equations yielded statistically significantly different GMI values > 6.7 mmol/L, with increasing differences at higher glucose levels.

CONCLUSIONS: The relationship between mean sensor glucose and HbA1c differed between contemporary CGM systems. This finding suggests that device-specific GMI equations may improve interpretation of glycaemic control in the absence of standardisation across contemporary CGM systems.

articles.title: Metformin and Severe Post-COVID-19 Outcomes Among Individuals With Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: We evaluated the relationship between metformin, one of the most commonly prescribed medications for individuals with diabetes, and COVID-19 sequelae.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We evaluated a retrospective cohort of individuals in the National Clinical Cohort Collaborative with Type 2 diabetes mellitus and COVID-19 who were prescribed metformin or a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor (DPP4i) at least 30 days before the onset of acute COVID-19 between 1 October 2021, and 15 November 2023. We compared the 12-month cumulative incidence of Long COVID diagnosis (ICD-10 U09.9: Post COVID-19 condition, unspecified), probable Long COVID (based on a model-derived phenotype), and mortality between individuals prescribed metformin versus DPP4i. We applied Super Learner and targeted maximum likelihood estimation to obtain risk ratios while adjusting for covariates of interest.

RESULTS: In our sample of 53 332 individuals with Type 2 diabetes and COVID-19, we found that metformin prescription was associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality after COVID-19 (adjusted risk ratio [aRR]: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.51, 0.73). We also observed that metformin users, compared to DPP4i users, had a slightly lower risk of probable Long COVID (aRR: 0.87, 95% CI: 0.81, 0.94) but did not detect a significant relationship with the clinically defined outcome of Long COVID diagnosis (aRR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.68, 1.20).

CONCLUSIONS: These findings support the hypothesis that metformin prescription during acute COVID-19 may be associated with lower mortality among adults with diabetes.

articles.title: Hidden behind the ear: an overlooked clue to prolonged fever.
Expanding the Clinical and Molecular Spectrum of Progressive Familial Intrahepatic Cholestasis Associated With Biallelic Variants in LSR.
articles.abstract: Progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis (PFIC) comprises autosomal recessive disorders causing early-onset cholestasis that may progress to cirrhosis and liver failure. Although more than 13 genes are associated with PFIC, some patients remain genetically undiagnosed. LSR, encoding lipolysis-stimulated lipoprotein receptor, has recently emerged as a candidate gene. LSR contributes to tricellular tight-junction integrity and epithelial barrier function. We report four additional patients from three unrelated families with biallelic LSR variants, expanding the reported clinical and molecular spectrum. Features included intractable pruritus, cholestasis with normal or mildly elevated gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT), progressive hepatic dysfunction and variable extrahepatic findings, including growth failure, neurodevelopmental delay, seizures and microcephaly. Two patients died from end-stage liver disease. Review of published cases suggests a predominantly progressive cholestatic phenotype with variable syndromic features. These findings support consideration of LSR variants in unresolved PFIC and the value of comprehensive genomic testing.

articles.title: Effectiveness and major bleeding complications with venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in category E pulmonary thromboembolism: a multicentre retrospective study.
PDGFRβ-Targeting VHH Tracer Enables Noninvasive PET Imaging of Kidney Fibrosis.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: With a prevalence above 10% worldwide, chronic kidney disease is one of the leading medical burdens. Independent of the underlying cause, kidney fibrosis emerges as the common final endpoint and serves as the most robust predictor of disease progression and long-term prognosis. Fibrosis is driven by extracellular matrix-producing mesenchymal cells, which are characterized by platelet-derived growth factor receptor β (PDGFRβ) expression. PDGFRβ also mediates fibrogenesis in these cells and represents a potential therapeutic target for direct intervention or a potential anchor for selective delivery of antifibrotic drugs. Diagnostic approaches assessing PDGFRβ expression in kidneys are missing. Here, we developed and evaluated a novel tracer using a PDGFRβ-targeting biparatopic variable domain of a heavy-chain-only antibody construct, designated SP02SP26-ABD, for in vivo, noninvasive, molecular imaging of kidney fibrosis. Methods: PDGFRβ expression was assessed in human kidney biopsies and publicly available transcriptomic datasets. In vivo imaging studies were performed in 2 distinct murine models of kidney fibrosis using fluorescence imaging and 89Zr-labeled PET. Specificity and dose dependency were evaluated using a nonspecific control variable domain of a heavy-chain-only antibody construct, R2R2-ABD, and coinjection of increasing amounts of unlabeled SP02SP26-ABD. Ex vivo biodistribution and correlation with histologic and molecular markers of fibrosis were performed. Results: PDGFRβ was increased in fibrotic human kidneys across multiple disease entities, predominantly localized to pericytes and fibroblasts, supporting its relevance as a translational imaging target. In vivo imaging demonstrated significantly higher tracer accumulation in fibrotic compared with nonfibrotic kidneys across both models, whereas tracer accumulation in nonrenal organs was low, with minimal uptake in the spleen. We found no difference between fibrotic and nonfibrotic kidneys when using a nonspecific R2R2-ABD control construct, whereas increasing amounts of unlabeled SP02SP26-ABD led to a dose-dependent decrease in tracer accumulation, consistent with a saturation effect. Tracer signal correlated with PDGFRβ expression, confirming the specificity of the approach. Conclusion: We provide the first proof of concept for noninvasive PET imaging of PDGFRβ-expressing fibrogenic cells in kidney disease, supporting further development of this approach for specific, noninvasive assessment of kidney fibrosis.

articles.title: Clinical Study Protocol for PENTILULA: A Phase 1/2 Study Assessing [177Lu]Lu-Pentixather for Relapsed or Refractory CXCR4-Positive Acute Leukemia.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: C-X-C chemokine receptor type 4 (CXCR4) inhibition may represent a new therapeutic strategy for patients with acute leukemia (AL), not only by increasing chemosensitivity but also by preventing relapse through disruption of residual leukemic cell interactions with the bone marrow niche. Radiolabeled CXCR4 ligands are available for PET imaging ([68Ga]Ga-pentixafor) and radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) ([177Lu]Lu-pentixather/[90Y]Y-pentixather). Early clinical experience with CXCR4-targeted RPT, together with the reported feasibility of CXCR4-targeted PET in acute myeloid leukemia, supports the development of theranostic approaches targeting the CXCR4/C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 12-defined leukemia-initiating cell niche. The objective of this study is to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of a single infusion of [177Lu]Lu-pentixather in patients with relapsed/refractory AL (including both acute myeloid leukemia and acute lymphoblastic leukemia). Methods: PENTILULA is an investigator-initiated, first-in-human, prospective phase 1/2 study based on a standard 3 + 3 dose-escalation design with 5 levels and 3-6 patients per level. Key inclusion criteria include patients with relapsed/refractory AL with CXCR4-positive leukemic cells. The primary endpoint is the incidence and evaluation of dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) and determination of the MTD. DLTs will be assessed 4-6 wk after RPT and include grade 3 or higher nonhematologic toxicity, prolonged grade 4 pancytopenia with hypocellular bone marrow, and excessive renal or hepatic radiation absorbed dose. The MTD is defined as the highest level at which fewer than one third of patients experience a DLT. In a subset of patients, [68Ga]Ga-pentixafor PET/MRI will be performed to explore the predictive value of theranostic PET imaging on CXCR4 expression, dosimetry, and treatment response. Conclusion: This first-in-human clinical study is ongoing, having reached the fifth and final activity level. [177Lu]Lu-pentixather is being used to definitively establish the MTD and preliminary efficacy of this CXCR4-targeted approach in this high-risk population with limited therapeutic options.

articles.title: Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor as a Radiotheranostic Target in Orthotopic Models of Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with a 5-y survival rate of approximately 20%. Although glypican-3-targeted radiotheranostics are under development, a plurality of patients with HCC lack glypican-3 expression, underscoring the need for alternative targetable antigens. Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) is overexpressed in 50%-70% of HCC tumors and represents a clinically validated therapeutic target. Here, we developed and evaluated a panitumumab-based EGFR-targeted radiotheranostic pair, [89Zr]Zr-desferrioxamine-panitumumab ([89Zr]Zr-Pani) for immuno-PET and [225Ac]Ac-Macropa-panitumumab ([225Ac]Ac-Pani) for targeted α-particle therapy, in clinically relevant orthotopic HCC models. Methods: Panitumumab was conjugated with desferrioxamine or Macropa chelators and radiolabeled with 89Zr or 225Ac, respectively. EGFR expression was characterized across a panel of HCC cell lines. Binding affinity, biodistribution, and tumor specificity were assessed in subcutaneous and orthotopic Huh-7 models, with EGFR-mediated targeting confirmed by blocking (200-fold molar excess of unlabeled panitumumab). Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in mice bearing orthotopic Huh-7-Luc+ tumors (n = 6 per group) after a single 9.3 kBq dose of [225Ac]Ac-Pani, with longitudinal monitoring by bioluminescence imaging, [89Zr]Zr-Pani immuno-PET, and blood chemistry. Results: [89Zr]Zr-Pani exhibited high-affinity binding to EGFR (dissociation constant, 0.35 nM) and demonstrated robust tumor accumulation in both subcutaneous Huh-7 (20.6 ± 2.6 %IA/g) and orthotopic Huh-7-Luc+ tumors (19.3 ± 2.0 %IA/g) at 120-192 h postinjection. Biodistribution of [225Ac]Ac-Pani closely mirrored that of [89Zr]Zr-Pani across organs and tumors, with tumor uptake reduced approximately 5-fold by blocking (21.7 ± 1.1 vs. 4.5 ± 0.6 %IA/g; P < 0.0001), confirming EGFR-specific targeting. A single 9.3 kBq administration of [225Ac]Ac-Pani induced substantial early tumor regression and significantly prolonged median survival (70 d) compared with vehicle (28 d) and blocking (35 d) groups (log-rank P < 0.0001), with no clinically meaningful hepatotoxicity or renal toxicity. However, tumor regrowth eventually occurred in all treated mice. Conclusion: [89Zr]Zr-Pani and [225Ac]Ac-Pani represent a radiotheranostic pair that enables EGFR-specific imaging and targeted α-particle therapy in orthotopic HCC models. These findings establish EGFR as a promising radiotheranostic target in HCC, broadening the patient population eligible for image-guided radiopharmaceutical interventions for liver cancer.

articles.title: Descending Necrotizing Mediastinitis After Thyroidectomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thyroidectomy is a commonly performed endocrine procedure with generally low complication rates. Descending necrotizing mediastinitis (DNM) is an exceptionally rare but life-threatening complication resulting from cervical infections that spread into the mediastinum. DNM following thyroid surgery has been reported only rarely.

METHODS: We analyzed retrospectively five patients who developed DNM following thyroid surgery between 2023 and 2025 at two tertiary centers. The patients' demographics, comorbidities, surgical procedures, clinical presentation, imaging, microbiology, treatment, complications, and outcomes were reviewed. The diagnosis was based on clinical and radiological evidence of cervicomediastinal infection, with operative confirmation in the four patients who underwent surgical drainage. A literature review was conducted using PubMed, MEDLINE, and Embase.

RESULTS: The case series included four women and one man (age 35-68, mean 53.8 years). All patients had at least one comorbidity, including obesity, cardiovascular or respiratory disease, immune compromise, and chronic nicotine use. Surgical procedures included total thyroidectomy (n = 3) and hemithyroidectomy (n = 2). Symptoms developed 2-10 days postoperatively, including cervical pain, swelling, fever, dysphagia, dyspnea, tachycardia, and subcutaneous emphysema. Contrast-enhanced (CT) of the neck and chest demonstrated findings consistent with DNM in all patients, with operative confirmation in the four patients requiring surgical drainage. Microbiological analyses identified Streptococcus pyogenes in three patients and Streptococcus pneumoniae in one patient. Concomitant methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) was isolated in one of the patients with S. pyogenes, while an additional patient had a positive rapid Group A Streptococcus test without confirmatory culture. Treatment included cervical drainage (n = 4), thoracic intervention (n = 2), tracheal repair (n = 1), and ICU admission (n = 4). Complications included acute kidney failure, septic shock, pleural/pericardial effusions, pulmonary embolism, and cardiac arrest. All patients survived with hospital stays ranging 7 to 42 days (median 21). Although the acute infectious process resolved in all patients, some required rehabilitation and one experienced long-term disability affecting daily activities and work capacity.

CONCLUSION: DNM after thyroidectomy is rare but potentially life-threatening. Early recognition, contrast-enhanced CT, prompt surgical drainage, and broad-spectrum antibiotics are essential. Awareness of predisposing factors and vigilant postoperative monitoring improves outcomes.

articles.title: Quantitative assessment of synovial inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis using shear wave elastography: a pilot study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the discriminatory performance of shear wave elastography (SWE) for detecting ultrasound-confirmed wrist synovitis in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), derive preliminary diagnostic cut-offs and examine associations between synovial stiffness and ultrasound inflammatory burden.

METHODS: This cross-sectional pilot study included 133 participants: 60 patients with RA and ultrasound-confirmed synovitis, 30 patients with RA without ultrasound-confirmed synovitis, 30 healthy controls and 13 individuals with wrist ganglia. Bilateral radiocarpal and midcarpal recesses were assessed using B-mode ultrasound, power Doppler (PD) and SWE. Ultrasound-confirmed synovitis was prespecified as synovial hypertrophy (SH) grade ≥2, irrespective of PD. Associations between SWE and ultrasound inflammatory burden were assessed using recess-level linear mixed-effects models and participant-level analyses.

RESULTS: Participant-level mean SWE showed high discriminatory performance within this pilot cohort for ultrasound-confirmed synovitis: area under the curve (AUC) 0.998 for kPa, with an optimal cut-off of 19.49 kPa (98.3% sensitivity; 100% specificity) and AUC 0.994 for m/s, with an optimal cut-off of 2.89 m/s (95.0% sensitivity; 100% specificity). Mean SWE was significantly higher in patients with ultrasound-confirmed synovitis than in all other groups (p<0.001). At the recess level, SWE increased progressively with wrist-adapted Global Outcome Measures in Rheumatology (OMERACT)-European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) Synovitis Score, SH and PD grades (all p<0.001). After adjustment for Disease Activity Score in 28 joints using erythrocyte sedimentation rate, age, disease duration, current conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drug use and current biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drug use, wrist-adapted GLOESS mean and PD mean were independently associated with SWE.

CONCLUSION: SWE showed high discriminatory performance for ultrasound-confirmed synovitis within this single-operator pilot cohort and was closely associated with ultrasound inflammatory burden. The preliminary diagnostic cut-offs require independent validation, including assessment of interobserver reproducibility, before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Advances in the management of mitral valve disease: contemporary review for clinicians.
articles.abstract: Mitral valve disease is a major global contributor to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, with its epidemiology shaped by regional characteristics and changing causes. In high income countries, degenerative mitral regurgitation predominates, resulting from ageing populations, although functional mitral regurgitation is increasingly recognised and constitutes an increasing proportion of the burden of mitral regurgitation. In contrast, rheumatic mitral stenosis and regurgitation affect younger patients in low and middle income areas. Advances in multimodality cardiac imaging have enhanced the precision of diagnostic and prognostic evaluation, and periprocedural planning and guidance. Management strategies are evolving, with surgical repair or replacement remaining the standard for eligible patients, supported by minimally invasive approaches and optimal timing and indications. Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair and transcatheter mitral valve replacement are new treatment options for patients at high risk or previously considered to be inoperable. This review summarises the contemporary perspectives of the epidemiology of mitral valve disease, the pathophysiology, diagnostic imaging modalities, and treatments for mitral regurgitation and stenosis, and outlines future directions.

articles.title: Paediatric case mix in UK military non-combatant evacuation and humanitarian operations: a retrospective observational service evaluation.
The Mediator Complex Protein Vmg1 Plays a Central Role in the Regulation of Development and Pathogenicity in the Soil-Borne Pathogen Verticillium dahliae.
articles.abstract: Verticillium dahliae is a soil-borne pathogen that causes vascular wilts in a wide variety of agronomically important crops worldwide. The lack of host specificity and the systemic nature of the infection pose a challenge for the control of this pathogen. Furthermore, V. dahliae produces resistant structures, the microsclerotia, that can remain viable in the soil for long periods of time and are the main source of inoculum for new infections. In this work, using a forward genetic approach and targeted gene deletion we have identified Vmg1, a putative ortholog of the Mediator Complex protein Med15, as a major regulator of morphogenesis and essential for pathogenicity in V. dahliae. Mutants deleted for vmg1 do not sporulate, produce microsclerotia with an aberrant structure, show reduced aerial mycelium formation, and do not induce any Verticillium wilt symptoms. They also exhibit impaired glucose metabolism and altered stress responses. The developmental defects observed in Δvmg1 strains are consistent with their inability to undergo processes that require cell budding. In planta analyses using confocal and scanning electron microscopy show that the Δvmg1 strain goes through the prevascular phase of the infection but remains trapped outside the xylem vessels in the vascular tissue. We propose that as previously shown for the well-characterized Saccharomyces cerevisiae Med15 protein, Vmg1 is a major interaction hub of multiple signaling pathways in V. dahliae. Hence, Vmg1 activity integrates the regulation of developmental processes, stress responses, metabolism and other functions required for V. dahliae to cause disease and successfully complete its life cycle.

Marked reduction in serum uric acid levels after empagliflozin initiation in a patient with heart failure.

Incidence of and household responses to paediatric diarrhoeal disease and acute respiratory infection in Chitwan, Nepal: protocol for a prospective cohort study.
Direct comparison of diagnostic models for pancreatic cancer in patients with new-onset diabetes in the British population.

Intensive care admissions, experiences and outcomes for Indigenous children in Australia, Aotearoa (New Zealand), Canada and the USA: a scoping review protocol.

Which barriers and solutions do (psycho-)medical providers perceive at the interface of acute care, rehabilitation and aftercare of patients with sepsis? An interdisciplinary online focus group study in Germany.
2026 Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) strategy report: executive summary and key changes.
articles.abstract: The Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) Strategy Report provides a comprehensive, annually updated evidence-based approach to asthma diagnosis, assessment, treatment, and prevention across the lifespan. Its central approach is personalized, iterative care based on the Assess-Adjust-Review cycle for both symptom control and reduction of future risk (including severe exacerbations, persistent airflow limitation, and treatment-related harm).GINA emphasizes objective confirmation of diagnosis wherever possible, and regular assessment of lung function, inhaler technique, adherence, multimorbidity, risk factors (including Type-2 biomarkers), and patient goals and preferences. GINA strongly recommends that all adults, adolescents, children and most preschoolers with asthma should receive inhaled corticosteroid (ICS)-containing treatment. GINA recommends against short-acting beta2-agonist (SABA)-only treatment. For adults/adolescents, GINA Track 1 using low-dose ICS-formoterol, an anti-inflammatory reliever (AIR), either as-needed-only (AIR-only) or as maintenance-and-reliever therapy (MART), is preferred because of its substantial reduction in severe exacerbations compared with SABA-based regimens, and its simplicity. Age-specific treatment pathways in children also emphasize ICS-containing therapy and exacerbation prevention.For difficult-to-treat and severe asthma, GINA provides structured guidance, emphasizing diagnostic verification, optimization of modifiable factors, inflammatory phenotyping, biologic therapy selection, and (as for all patients) systemic corticosteroid stewardship. Acute exacerbation care incorporates long-term preventive treatment, including post-discharge reassessment of management and action plan.Key 2026 updates include expanded AIR options for adults and children, revised guidance on severe asthma and selection of biologic treatment, and substantial updates to acute asthma management.GINA integrates evidence-based management with shared decision-making, self-management education, implementation, and global advocacy to reduce preventable asthma morbidity and mortality.

articles.title: Anti-inflammatory effects of inhaled corticosteroids-containing treatment for symptom relief: a randomized crossover trial in asthma.
Thoracic epidural versus paravertebral blockade for reducing chronic post-thoracotomy pain (TOPIC-2): open label, parallel group, superiority, multicentre, randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effectiveness of paravertebral blockade versus thoracic epidural during the perioperative period in reducing chronic post-thoracotomy pain.

DESIGN: Open label, parallel group, superiority, multicentre, randomised controlled trial.

SETTING: 15 thoracic centres in the UK.

PARTICIPANTS: Adult patients undergoing thoracotomy randomised (1:1) to either paravertebral blockade or thoracic epidural using a web based service between January 2019 and September 2023.

INTERVENTIONS: Participants in the paravertebral group received three single-shot paravertebral injections of local anaesthetic before incision followed by placement of a paravertebral catheter. Participants in the epidural group had a thoracic epidural catheter placed and loaded with local anaesthetic before incision.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: The primary outcome was incidence of chronic post-thoracotomy pain at six months after randomisation, defined as a 100 mm visual analogue score greater than or equal to 40 mm (indicating moderate pain) when considering worst chest pain over the past week. Secondary outcomes included acute pain (visual analogue score of 100 mm) and complications.

RESULTS: 770 patients were enrolled, of which 428 (56%) were male (mean (standard deviation, SD) age 66.6 (11.0) years). After 33 exclusions of patients after randomisation who did not proceed to thoracotomy, 737 remained in the modified intention-to-treat population (364 in the paravertebral group, 373 in the epidural group). Six months after randomisation, 59 (22%) of 272 participants in the paravertebral group and 47 (16%) of 292 participants in the epidural group developed chronic post-thoracotomy pain (adjusted risk ratio 1.32 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.93 to 1.86), adjusted risk difference 0.05 (95% CI -0.01 to 0.11), P=0.12). During the acute phase, worst and average pain was greater on day 1 with paravertebral blockade (adjusted mean difference 7.7 mm (95% CI 2.8 to 12.5 mm) and 7.0 mm (95% CI 2.7 to 11.2 mm), respectively), but no different on days 2-3. Hypotension was less common in the paravertebral group than the epidural group (12% v 18%, respectively, adjusted risk ratio 0.66 (95% CI 0.46 to 0.94), adjusted risk difference -0.06 (95% CI -0.11 to -0.01)), as was pruritis (4% v 12%, adjusted risk ratio 0.37 (95% CI 0.21 to 0.64), adjusted risk difference -0.07 (95% CI -0.11 to -0.03)), although more participants in this group experienced urinary retention (12% v 6%, adjusted risk ratio 2.21 (95% CI 1.35 to 3.61), adjusted risk difference 0.05 (95% CI 0.01 to 0.09)), complications were similar otherwise.

CONCLUSIONS: Paravertebral blockade did not reduce chronic post-thoracotomy pain at six month follow-up compared to thoracic epidural. Thoracic epidural provided marginally better acute pain relief one day after the operation, but showed no difference thereafter. Postoperative complications were comparable between groups. The findings support the ongoing use of both techniques.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03677856.

articles.title: Opportunistically Detecting Signs of Hypertension on a Consumer Smartwatch.
articles.abstract: Hypertension is a silent killer, with over half of affected adults unaware of their condition1,2. This lack of awareness is a major concern, as early intervention is critical for preventing major adverse cardiovascular events3,4. Here we show that applying artificial intelligence (AI) to multimodal waveforms (photoplethysmography and accelerometry) recorded using a widely available consumer smartwatch (AI-PPG-ACC-HTN), without any cuff calibration, can detect hypertension with accuracy levels comparable to traditional cuffed blood pressure (BP) devices in the existing clinical framework. We validated AI-PPG-ACC-HTN in a prospective, multicenter study of 196 diverse participants free from known cardiovascular disease and antihypertensive medication against gold-standard 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring. Over seven days of real-world monitoring, AI-PPG-ACC-HTN detected hypertension with a sensitivity of 65.8% (95% CI, 54.0%-76.3%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%), and positive predictive value (PPV) of 80.6% (95% CI, 68.6%-89.6%). In comparison, initial office BP screening achieved a sensitivity of 55.3% (95% CI, 43.4%-66.7%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%) and PPV of 77.8% (95% CI, 64.4%-88.0%). These results highlight an opportunity for consumer smartwatches to facilitate population-level opportunistic hypertension screening by prompting at-risk individuals toward clinical assessment and confirmatory diagnosis using established cuff-based methodologies, offering an accessible tool to address this major public health challenge.

articles.title: Association between the Triglyceride-Glucose Index and Clinical Outcomes in Acute Atherosclerotic Ischaemic Stroke Patients Following Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We aimed to investigate the association between the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and unfavourable clinical outcomes in patients with atherosclerotic acute ischaemic stroke (AIS) undergoing endovascular thrombectomy (EVT).

METHODS: Patients with AIS who underwent EVT between January 2019 and September 2024 were enrolled. The primary outcome was an unfavourable functional outcome at 3 months (modified Rankin Scale score 3-6); secondary outcomes were symptomatic intracerebral haemorrhage (sICH) and all-cause mortality at 3 months. The TyG index was analysed continuously and in quartiles by logistic regression, restricted cubic splines and receiver operating characteristic curves.

RESULTS: Among 670 patients, 269 (40.1%) had an unfavourable functional outcome at 3 months, 91 (13.6%) died at 3 months for all-cause, and 85 (12.7%) developed sICH. Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest TyG quartile was independently associated with unfavourable functional outcome (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.91, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03-3.56) and mortality (aOR 5.15, 95% CI 2.06-12.86). The overall spline association was significant for all endpoints; only mortality was non-linear (P = 0.032), with risk rising above a TyG index of approximately 8.9. Discrimination was modest, with area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.583 for unfavourable functional outcome and 0.612 for mortality. No significant interactions were found across prespecified subgroups, except for blood glucose level.

CONCLUSION: An elevated TyG index is independently associated with 3-month unfavourable functional outcome, mortality and sICH after EVT, and may aid prognostic risk stratification, although further validation is required based on the existing predictive indicators.

articles.title: Cholangitis alters iron-related parameters predominantly in cholangiocarcinoma: a prospective exploratory ERCP-based study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pancreatobiliary tumor serum markers have limited diagnostic utility. Bile has emerged as a promising matrix for biomarker discovery. Acute cholangitis may interfere with biomarker interpretation. This study evaluated the impact of cholangitis on selected tumor biomarkers and on iron metabolism.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: In this prospective study, 117 patients treated with endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) were included, with the following indications for the procedure: choledocholithiasis (n=70), cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) (n=24), and pancreatic cancer (PC) (n=23). Bile samples were obtained during ERCP and analyzed using ECLIA (CA19-9, PIVKA-II, AFP, CEA, ferritin, CA125), colorimetric assays (iron, TIBC), and ELISA (hepcidin). Patients were stratified by diagnosis and by the presence of cholangitis.

RESULTS: Biliary infection did not significantly affect biliary CA19-9, CA125, or PIVKA-II across the analyzed disease groups. The most pronounced changes were observed in iron-related biomarkers, particularly in patients with CCA, who exhibited higher biliary iron, ferritin, and TIBC concentrations in the presence of concomitant cholangitis. Lower biliary hepcidin concentrations were observed only in patients with PC and concomitant cholangitis. However, these associations did not remain statistically significant after false discovery rate (FDR) adjustment.

CONCLUSION: Biliary infection appears to have a limited effect on conventional biliary tumor markers but may influence iron-related biomarkers, particularly in patients with CCA. Although these associations did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons, they suggest that biliary iron metabolism may respond differently to cholangitis than conventional tumor markers. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger, multicenter cohorts.

articles.title: Basiliximab use and early graft dysfunction after liver transplantation: an overlap-weighted multicenter study.
articles.journal: Clinics and research in hepatology and gastroenterology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Basiliximab has been associated with a reduced risk of acute cellular rejection, infection and renal failure in liver transplantation. However, its association with early graft dysfunction (EAD) and EAD-related outcomes remains unclear.

METHODS: A multicenter retrospective cohort was enrolled. Association of basiliximab use with EAD, and EAD-related outcomes (prolonged ICU stay and peri-operative mortality) were evaluated. The treatment effects were estimated using overlap weighting method based on outcome-specific propensity score models incorporating recipient, donor and peri-operative characteristics. Sensitivity analysis was performed after excluding centers with highly imbalanced basiliximab use.

RESULTS: Of 903 eligible recipients, 393 (43.5%) received basiliximab induction. Overlap weighting achieved excellent covariate balance (nearly all absolute standardized mean differences < 0.03). After weighting, EAD incidence was 7.8 percentage points lower with basiliximab (23.3% vs. 31.1%); overlap-weighted logistic regression showed that basiliximab use was associated with significantly lower odds of EAD (OR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.48-0.94; p = 0.02). No significant associations were observed with prolonged ICU stay or peri-operative mortality, and findings remained robust in sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: Basiliximab induction was associated with lower odds of EAD after liver transplantation; however, as confounding by indication cannot be excluded in this observational design, validation in larger prospective studies is warranted.

articles.title: Clinical management of intrusive luxation in primary teeth: A systematic review of treatment approaches and outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This systematic review aimed to evaluate management strategies for intrusive luxation in primary teeth according to the degree of intrusion and to analyze associated clinical and radiographic outcomes.

DATA SOURCES: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, PubMed (MEDLINE), Web of Science, Scopus, Embase, and Library Cochrane were systematically searched for eligible studies published up to July 23, 2026.

STUDY SELECTION: Clinical trials, observational studies, case reports, and case series involving children with intrusive luxation of primary teeth were included. Findings were synthesized qualitatively by study design and management approach. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal checklist.

RESULTS: Among 1,331 identified records, 21 studies were included (nine retrospective studies and 12 case reports). Spontaneous re-eruption was the most frequently reported management approach, with favorable outcomes across different degrees of intrusion, although recovery was slower and less predictable in severe cases. Post-traumatic complications in primary teeth, including pulp necrosis, pathological root resorption, ankylosis, infection, and premature tooth loss, as well as enamel and structural abnormalities in permanent successors, were reported during follow-up. Surgical repositioning and fixation were described in few studies, with variable outcomes and complications. Overall, most studies had a low risk of bias.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports conservative management as the preferred approach for intrusive luxation in primary teeth. Long-term follow-up and prospective studies remain essential to strengthen the evidence and refine treatment recommendations.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Conservative management of intruded primary teeth may minimize unnecessary invasive procedures and preserve the developing permanent dentition. However, long-term follow-up remains essential for early detection of delayed pulpal, periodontal, and developmental complications.

articles.title: SREBP1 inhibition downregulates NR2B-PSD95 interaction in glutamate excitotoxicity following cerebral ischemic reperfusion injury.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1 (SREBP1), a transcription factor has been identified to participate in NMDAR-dependent excitotoxicity in delayed hours especially after 6 h of post ictus ischemia. We have demonstrated that downregulation of SREBP1, NR2B and PSD95 (postsynaptic density protein-95) and subsequent downstream apoptotic proteins reduces ischemic/reperfusion (I/R) injury in an experimental rat model and glutamate exposed cortical culture model.
