METHODS: Male wistar rats were injected vehicle, Ro25-6981 or SREBP1 siRNA for seven days in a row prior to middle cerebral artery occlusion induced I/R injury. The neurological functions and neuronal loss were observed using behavioural paradigms, TTC staining, haematoxylin and eosin and NeuN staining. Further, neuronal survival was assessed by MTT, LDH and Hoechst staining assay in glutamate exposed primary cortical culture I/R model in SREBP1 transfected cells. Expression of nt-SREBP1, NR2B and PSD95 were detected using immunoblotting after 24 h in in-vivo stroke and in-vitro excitotoxicity model. Further, alterations in PTEN, JNK, and Caspase-3 expression were assessed by immunofluorescence staining.

RESULTS: In-vivo and in-vitro experiments showed that SREBP1 inhibition substantially attenuated neuronal cell death in delayed hours of both post ischemic- and glutamate-insult. Further, SREBP1 inhibition restrained excitotoxicity induced activation of NR2B, PSD95, JNK and Caspase-3 proteins.

CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that SREBP1 manipulates NR2B-PSD95 signaling to cause excitotoxic damage followed by ischemic reperfusion injury in the delayed hours.

articles.title: Epidemics by beneficial microorganisms drive evolution.
articles.journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases
articles.abstract: Epidemics of beneficial microorganisms (beneficial to the host) generally go unobserved; a few recent advantageous epidemics have been reported, including an epidemic of corals by a Vibrio species that made them resistant to bleaching and epidemics of stinkbugs by Burkholderia spp. that conferred resistance of the insect to the insecticide fenitrothion. There are similarities and differences between epidemics caused by pathogenic and by beneficial microbes. Both contain genomic islands (GIs) involved in epidemics. GIs of pathogenic bacteria contain virulence genes, such as those encoding specific toxins that damage eukaryotic cells, in addition to fitness genes that assist colonization. GIs of beneficial bacteria lack virulence genes, but contain similar fitness genes. Pathogenic epidemics are detected almost immediately through symptoms and have a finite time, whereas beneficial epidemics mostly go undetected and can persist for long periods, possibly leading to genetic and thus evolutionary changes. The key to epidemics (beneficial or pathogenic) is rapid horizontal transmission of the causative agent from one host to another via contaminated surfaces, water, air, and by direct contact. Vertical transmission can also occur. Pathogenic bacteria elicit an immune response, while beneficial bacteria usually do not, since they are recognized by the host as "self". There are many examples of important evolutionary events that were driven by the acquisition of microbes by animals and plants. However, acquisition of a microbe, leading to evolution, can be considered an epidemic only if the infection spreads rapidly. We suggest that beneficial epidemics can help explain at least the initial steps of punctuated evolution.

articles.title: Forensic Dermatology of Tattoos: Part 3A. Cutaneous Diseases and Infections with Tattoos in a Forensic Setting.
articles.abstract: Forensic dermatology involves the medical and legal assessment of the skin, mucosa, hair, and nails to evaluate injury or death. Tattoos, a form of body modification, play an integral role in forensic dermatology evaluations. Inoculating pigment into the skin creates a tattoo, for which forensic dermatology of tattoos will have been presented in four contributions. The first in the series (Part 1) discusses the epidemiology of tattoos in a forensic setting. The second (Part 2) gives the types of tattoos that can be found in a forensic setting. The current contribution in the series (Part 3) presents various circumstances associated with tattoos in a forensic setting; the first section (Part 3A) focuses on cutaneous diseases and infections and the second section (Part 3B) centers on benign skin lesions and cancers. The fourth contribution in the series (Part 4) discusses the forensic aspects of tattoos. A tattoo-associated cutaneous disease can be localized to affect only the tattoo, or it can become a systemic disorder; in the latter situation, the condition not only appears on the subject's skin, mucosa, nails, or hair but it also can affect the overall health of the person. Inflammatory dermatoses, granulomatous conditions, lymphocytic proliferations, neutrophilic dermatoses, and papulosquamous diseases and tattoo blowout are cutaneous conditions that can occur in tattoos; keratosis follicularis, lichen sclerosus, morphea, vasculitis, and vitiligo are some of the additional skin afflictions that can develop. The infections may be bacterial, cutaneous and systemic fungal, mycobacterial, protozoan, spirochetal, or viral and can occur in tattoos. It is essential for forensic pathologists and others who assess decedents with tattoos to have a comprehensive understanding of the forensic significance of tattoos.

articles.title: Negative-pressure wound therapy for postoperative wound dehiscence after pediatric spinal dysraphism surgery: neonatal portable SNaP® case report and PRISMA-guided review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Wound complications after neonatal spinal dysraphism surgery carry a high risk of infection and, when dural opening is required, potential cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leakage. While negative-pressure wound therapy (NPWT) is well established in adults, evidence in neonatal neurosurgery-especially with portable systems-remains scarce.

CASE DESCRIPTION: A term female neonate underwent surgery on day 2 for complex open lumbosacral spinal dysraphism with an exophytic mass first identified at birth. Imaging and surgery showed split cord malformation, low tethered cord, and mature teratoma with intradural extension. En bloc resection, filum terminale transection, and watertight dural closure were performed. On postoperative day (POD) 12, wound dehiscence developed, resulting in a 5.5 × 4.0 cm skin defect without dural exposure. After directed wound care, portable NPWT (SNaP®) was initiated on POD21 (-125 mmHg, continuous) for 22 days, with dressing changes every 3-4 days. Complete epithelialization occurred by POD43 without CSF leak, infection, or reoperation. At one year, neurological and scar outcomes were satisfactory, with no pseudomeningocele or recurrence on MRI.

LITERATURE REVIEW: In a PRISMA-guided search, we identified 4 publications reporting 6 pediatric cases of NPWT after dysraphism-related spinal surgery with dural opening and/or exposed dura. Published cases exclusively used conventional VAC® systems, and data in intradural settings remain limited; no prior report described SNaP® use in this context.

CONCLUSION: After secure watertight dural closure, appropriate interface protection, and optimized nutritional support, portable NPWT (SNaP®) may represent a feasible rescue option for neonatal lumbosacral wound dehiscence following intradural surgery.

articles.title: Geographic Disparities in Transsphenoidal Pituitary Surgery in the State of São Paulo, Brazil: An Analysis of the Public Healthcare System.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the surgical volume, geographic distribution, healthcare indicators, and costs of transsphenoidal surgeries performed within the public healthcare system in the state of São Paulo over a 15-year period.

METHODS: A retrospective study based on publicly available secondary data obtained from the São Paulo State Health Department TabNet database. Hospitalizations related to transsphenoidal hypophysectomy performed between 2010 and 2024 were included. Surgical volume, regional distribution, length of hospital stay, intensive care unit stay (ICU), mortality, and costs were evaluated.

RESULTS: A total of 4,086 surgeries were performed, with an annual mean of 272 ± 53 procedures, predominantly concentrated in Region 1 (68%). The mean hospital length of stay was 9.4 ± 0.9 days, showing a decreasing trend over time in some regions, whereas the mean ICU stay was 2.1 ± 0.3 days, with an increasing trend statewide. Significant regional differences were observed regarding hospital length of stay, ICU stay, and costs (p < 0.001). The mean cost per hospitalization was US$ 852 ± 93, with an upward trend throughout the study period. Overall mortality was 1.1%, remaining low and stable over time. Considerable heterogeneity was observed among high-volume centers, with differences in healthcare and financial indicators.

CONCLUSION: Transsphenoidal surgeries in the state of São Paulo are concentrated in higher-volume regions and centers, with substantial heterogeneity in healthcare and financial indicators. Nevertheless, mortality remains low, reinforcing the safety of this procedure within the public healthcare system.

articles.title: Reversible Acquired Chiari Type I Malformation and Syringomyelia Secondary to a High-Flow Posterior Fossa Arteriovenous Malformation: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Acquired Chiari I malformation (CM1) associated with syringomyelia is an uncommon consequence of intracranial space-occupying or hemodynamic disorders. Arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) are an exceptionally rare cause. A 14-year-old girl presented with recurrent headaches and progressive right-hand tremor. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a large posterior fossa AVM associated with cerebellar tonsillar descent and extensive C1-T9 syringomyelia. Angiography showed a Spetzler-Martin grade IV AVM involving the vermis and right cerebellar hemisphere, with high-flow fistulous components and prominent superficial and deep venous drainage. Six staged embolization procedures substantially reduced arteriovenous shunting and were followed by marked regression of the syrinx from C1-T9 to C2-T2, without foramen magnum decompression. The residual AVM was subsequently treated by CyberKnife stereotactic radiosurgery (18 Gy). Complete angiographic obliteration was confirmed in 2014. At the latest assessment in February 2025, 14 years after radiosurgery and 11 years after angiographic confirmation of AVM obliteration, follow-up imaging demonstrated complete resolution of syringomyelia, normalization of cerebellar tonsillar position, and no evidence of AVM recurrence. This 11-year follow-up supports a causal relationship between high-flow posterior fossa AVM, acquired tonsillar descent, and syringomyelia. Treatment of the underlying vascular lesion may reverse these secondary abnormalities without direct Chiari or syrinx surgery.

articles.title: The impact of removing prior authorization for guideline-concordant maintenance inhaled medications for COPD: a population-based cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Most patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) do not receive maintenance inhaled therapies in concordance with evidence-based clinical guidelines. Long-acting muscarinic antagonists (LAMA), the recommended first-line therapy, is underused, while inhaled corticosteroids (ICS)/long-acting beta-agonists (LABA) are often used in discordance with clinical guidelines. In July 2020, British Columbia's (BC) universal drug plan removed prior authorization requirements for coverage for LAMA medications and restricted coverage for ICS/LABA.

RESEARCH QUESTION: What is the impact of this policy change on guideline-concordant maintenance inhaled medication use?

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: In a population-based cohort study using provincial administrative health data, we identified patients with COPD using a validated case definition and followed them from January 2019 (18 months pre-policy) to December 2022 (30 months post-policy). Using interrupted time series analysis, we evaluated the monthly proportion of patients filling a prescription for ICS/LABA and LAMA, mean canisters dispensed, proportion of days covered (PDC), rates of ICS/LABA discontinuation, LAMA (re)initiation, and initiating LAMA as first maintenance therapy. We report absolute differences between observed and counterfactual outcomes at study end.

RESULTS: The cohort included 47,583 patients with COPD (mean 71.5 years, 46.5% female, 31.7 months mean follow-up). Thirty months post-policy change, ICS/LABA use decreased by -1.3% (95% CI -2.4, -0.3) and LAMA use increased by 0.8% (95% CI 0.1, 1.6). There was no significant change in the number of ICS/LABA canisters dispensed, PDC or proportion discontinuing ICS/LABA. Mean LAMA canisters dispensed increased by 9.8 per 1,000 patients (95% CI 1.0, 18.7) and PDC increased by 1.5% (95% CI 0.5, 2.4). (Re)initiation of LAMA or initiating LAMA as maintenance therapy increased by 0.2% (95% CI 0.02, 0.3) and 34.8% (95% CI 22.3, 48.6), respectively. Total combined drug costs did not change.

INTERPRETATION: Changes to drug coverage in BC were associated with improved guideline-concordant medication use.

articles.title: Pretransplant Pulmonary Hemodynamics, Explant Histology, and Primary Graft Dysfunction after Lung Transplantation for Silicosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Silicosis associated with progressive massive fibrosis (PMF) is a major cause of end-stage lung disease among workers in the artificial stone industry. Patients with PMF are increasingly referred for lung transplant (LTx) evaluation and there is emerging evidence of pulmonary hypertension (PH) in patients with advanced PMF.

RESEARCH QUESTION: Among patients with PMF referred for lung transplantation, what is the incidence of PH and what are accompanying histopathologic pulmonary vascular aberrations?

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Retrospective single-center cohort study of prospectively-enrolled participants, providing granular data on the invasive hemodynamic profile of patients with silicosis-associated PMF, histopathologic data on pulmonary vascular aberrations, and clinical data on post-transplant complications. Clinical and sociodemographic variables were collected. Explanted lungs from patients with silicosis-associated PMF underwent detailed pulmonary vascular histopathologic review and were descriptively compared with PAH explants. The incidence of primary graft dysfunction (PGD) was evaluated and descriptive analysis performed to provide associations of clinical features and PGD incidence.

RESULTS: PH was present in over 95% of 21 patients with silicosis-associated PMF who underwent LTx, with a hemodynamic profile similar to patients transplanted for PAH. . Silicosis explants showed confluent silicotic nodules, extensive fibrosis and hyalinization, obscuration or obliteration of vascular structures, and perivascular fibrohistiocytic infiltrates with extrinsic narrowing. Classic PAH-type arteriolar muscular hypertrophy and plexiform arteriopathy were uncommon. In exploratory comparisons, patients who developed PGD had more frequent pretransplant right ventricular dysfunction (71% vs 21%; risk difference 0.50, 95% CI 0.06-0.75) and a lower median TAPSE/RVSP ratio (0.27 vs 0.39; Hedges' g -0.93, 95% CI -1.88 to 0.02) than in those without PGD.

INTERPRETATION: These findings suggest that PH in advanced silicosis with PMF is very common and represents a distinct pulmonary vascular phenotype characterized by extensive fibrotic vascular obliteration rather than the classic arteriopathy seen in PAH.

articles.title: Understanding Primary Care Clinicians' Perspectives on Early Screening of Autism and Subsequent Referral Practices.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess primary care clinicians' (PCCs; ie, pediatricians, nurse practitioners) perspectives on screening practices used to identify children with autism and other developmental delays, factors related to screening practices, and actions taken when a child screens positive for possible autism.

STUDY DESIGN: PCCs (n=303) were surveyed across 2 toddler autism screening studies. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize screening practices, factors related to screening, and steps taken after a positive screen. Logistic regression was used to examine PCC characteristics associated with adherence to the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) recommendation to refer children both for diagnostic evaluation and early intervention.

RESULTS: PCCs reported using surveillance techniques, validated developmental and autism screens, and practice-developed questionnaires. PCCs endorsed many screening barriers, including insufficient payment and time, limited community resources, and low confidence in caring for children with delays. Only 35.7% of PCCs reported following AAP's recommendation of referring screen positive cases to both early intervention and diagnostic evaluation. PCC characteristics (eg, sex, years in practice) were not associated with referral practices following a positive screen.

CONCLUSIONS: Although PCCs reported using autism-specific screens, this did not translate into adherence to AAP-recommended guidelines for referrals following a positive screen. Further research is needed to understand better PCCs' confidence in autism-specific screens, to address barriers to referral for diagnostic evaluation and early intervention, and to explore further the relationship between PCCs' characteristics and referral practices.

articles.title: Associations of Maternal and Neonatal Characteristics with Infant Airway and Parenchymal Function.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether gestational age (GA) at birth, maternal and infant characteristics, and factors in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) are associated with worse infant lung function.

STUDY DESIGN: In a cohort of infants born preterm we assessed forced expiratory flow at 75% expired forced vital capacity (FEF75; FVC), lung diffusion (DL), and alveolar volume (VA) following NICU discharge. Using maternal, infant and NICU data obtained from electronic medical records, we evaluated the relationships of these factors and lung function expressed as z-scores.

RESULTS: Most mothers received antenatal steroids and delivered by cesarean section; 10% smoked during pregnancy, 32.9% had hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, and <10% were diagnosed with chorioamnionitis. Infants had a mean gestational age of 31.3 weeks; 51% received surfactant and 15.4% received postnatal corticosteroids. Mean duration for respiratory support was 24 days for oxygen supplementation, 36.6 days for non-invasive ventilation (NIV), and 4.8 days for invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV). Maternal characteristics were not associated with lung function; however, GA at birth was associated with lower airway and lower parenchymal function over the wide GA range of our participants. The inclusion of additional potential characteristics along with GA indicated that longer non-invasive ventilation (NIV) treatment was also associated with lower airway function. Our findings also suggest that NIV accounted for much of the association between GA and lower airway function. In contrast the effect of GA upon parenchymal function was not mediated through NIV.

CONCLUSIONS: We found an association between more days of NIV and lower FEFs; however, we did not find a similar association for the parenchymal function of gas exchange. Future research is required to evaluate whether this is a causal relationship, which would suggest the need to optimize NICU ventilatory support to minimize its potential adverse effects upon lung growth and development following preterm birth.

articles.title: A CD44-regulating Multimodal Therapeutic Strategy for MAFLD-Associated Pancreatic Cancer Liver Metastasis.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) has emerged as a novel risk factor for pancreatic cancer, particularly early liver metastasis. However, the underlying mechanisms and effective therapeutic strategies remain largely unclear. Here, based on clinical databases, patient tissue samples, and single-cell sequencing of mouse models, we identified CD44 as a key contributor to MAFLD-associated pancreatic cancer progression. High CD44 expression was significantly associated with poor survival in patients with pancreatic cancer and was further elevated in MAFLD-associated liver metastatic lesions. Considering that the limited effects of single treatment, we developed a cationic DOTAP/cholesterol liposomal nanoplatform co-loaded with gemcitabine, IR780, and CD44 siRNA (GIR@Lip) for combined chemotherapy, photothermal therapy, and immunotherapy. GIR@Lip nanoparticles exhibited excellent size uniformity, stability, and photothermal conversion efficiency, which could efficiently inhibit KPC cells' viability, migration and invasion, downregulate CD44 expression and stimulate immune response. Furthermore, GIR@Lip efficiently accumulated in tumor tissues in vivo, exhibiting a significant reduction in liver metastatic lesions and remodeling the M1 type tumor associated macrophages (TAMs), CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. Collectively, these findings identify CD44 as a potential therapeutic target for MAFLD-associated pancreatic cancer liver metastasis and highlight GIR@Lip as a promising multimodal strategy for its treatment.

articles.title: 2025 International Consensus Meeting Definition of Success for Treatment of Periprosthetic Joint Infection.
articles.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) remains one of the most devastating complications following total joint arthroplasty (TJA). Nevertheless, a universally accepted definition of treatment success and failure has not been described to date. Current definitions each carry major limitations that fail to account for the full spectrum of clinical scenarios encountered in practice and do not adequately reflect the evolving understanding of PJI pathogenesis. Consequently, reported treatment success rates vary widely across the literature, ranging from 54.2 to 88.9%. The purpose of this initiative was to engage the orthopaedic and infectious disease communities to establish a revised, practical, and consensus-driven definition for PJI treatment outcomes. The 2025 International Consensus Meeting convened a multidisciplinary international workgroup, which defined treatment success as the absence of clinical failure following reimplantation, no revision surgery or reoperation attributable to PJI, no requirement for suppressive antibiotics beyond one year from surgical intervention, and no PJI-related mortality. Outcomes assessment initiates at the time of index surgical intervention, regardless of the procedure performed, and all subsequent revision arthroplasty must be adequately investigated to rule out an infectious etiology. The extent of this evaluation should include serologic markers, joint aspiration, and intraoperative cultures, in accordance with validated diagnostic criteria. It is hoped that adoption of this standardized definition will reduce reporting variability, facilitate more accurate assessment of emerging surgical interventions, and enable meaningful comparison of treatment efficacy across institutions and future studies.

articles.title: Total Hip Arthroplasty for Femoral Neck Fracture Has Distinct Complication and Revision Risks Compared with Osteoarthritis Through 15 Years.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Total hip arthroplasty (THA) is increasingly used for femoral neck fractures (FNF), but whether outcomes after FNF THA differ from those after osteoarthritis (OA) THA over extended follow-up remains incompletely defined. This study compared complications through 90 days and 15 years following primary THA for FNF versus OA.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed using a large national database. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 53,814 patients who underwent FNF THA were compared with 53,814 patients who underwent OA THA. Complications through 90 days and 15 years were compared using risk differences and risk ratios (RR). Kaplan-Meier analysis evaluated survivorship.

RESULTS: Within 90 days, the FNF cohort had higher mortality (6.4 versus 1.4%; RR 4.76, 95% confidence interval (CI): 4.39 to 5.17; P < 0.001) and periprosthetic fracture (PPF) (3.3 versus 1.5%; RR 2.20, 95% CI: 2.03 to 2.39; P < 0.001). Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), dislocation, and revision THA were also more frequent after FNF THA. At 15 years, PPF remained higher after FNF THA (5.80 versus 3.4%; RR 1.71, 95% CI: 1.61 to 1.81; P < 0.001), as did PJI, dislocation, revision THA, and mortality, whereas mechanical loosening was not increased. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated worse 15-year survival free from PPF (hazard ratio 2.14, 95% CI: 2.02 to 2.27; P < 0.001), revision THA, and PJI in the FNF cohort.

CONCLUSION: Compared with OA, THA for FNF was associated with greater 90-day medical risk and higher rates of PJI, PPF, dislocation, revision THA, and mortality through 15 years, whereas mechanical loosening was not increased. These findings demonstrate an outcome-specific risk pattern and support considering fracture-related THA separately from OA THA in patient counseling, planning, and outcomes assessment.

articles.title: Can We Target the Microbiome to Improve Outcomes in Osteoarthritis and Arthroplasty?
articles.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is the most prevalent degenerative joint disease and a leading cause of pain, disability, and joint arthroplasty worldwide. Despite advances in surgical technique and perioperative care, periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) remains a devastating complication associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Increasing evidence suggests that the gut microbiome plays a central role in regulating systemic inflammation, immune competence, metabolic homeostasis, and intestinal barrier integrity, biological processes relevant to both OA progression and postoperative infection risk. Preclinical and emerging clinical studies support the existence of a gut-joint axis, whereby alterations in gut microbial composition and microbial metabolites, such as short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), bile acids, lipopolysaccharides, tryptophan-derived metabolites, and other immunomodulatory compounds, influence joint inflammation, cartilage degeneration, and host immune responses. Experimental models demonstrate that dysbiosis exacerbates OA-related joint damage, while targeted modulation of the gut microbiome can attenuate inflammation, reduce oxidative stress, and preserve cartilage integrity. Importantly, perioperative factors such as surgical stress, antibiotic exposure, and nutritional changes may further disrupt gut microbial homeostasis, potentially impairing immune resilience and increasing susceptibility to PJI. Microbiome-targeted strategies, including dietary modification, probiotics, prebiotics, and physical activity, have shown promise in restoring microbial balance and supporting immune regulation in arthritic populations. Although most evidence remains preclinical or observational, these findings suggest that modulation of the gut microbiome represents a biologically plausible adjunctive approach for both osteoarthritis management and perioperative optimization. This review summarizes current evidence linking the gut microbiome to OA pathophysiology and surgical outcomes and evaluates the potential role of microbiome modulation in joint health optimization and PJI risk reduction. Although biologically compelling, current evidence remains largely preclinical and observational, and prospective clinical trials are required before routine implementation.

articles.title: Cefazolin Administration in Patients Who Have Severe Penicillin Allergy Undergoing Total Joint Arthroplasty: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cefazolin is the recommended perioperative antibiotic for total hip (THA) and knee arthroplasty (TKA) due to its bone penetration and broad-spectrum efficacy. However, patients labeled with severe penicillin allergy (SPA) are often denied cefazolin due to concerns about cross-reactivity, despite limited evidence supporting this practice. This prospective observational study evaluated the safety of cefazolin in this population.

METHODS: Between July 2024 and October 2025, 1,234 elective THA and TKA procedures were performed at our institution. Our prospective observational study enrolled 51 patients (4.1%) who had a documented severe penicillin allergy (mean age 67 years; 70.6% women; and 76.5% Hispanic). Patients completed a preoperative questionnaire detailing allergy duration, exposure source, and reaction types. Standard perioperative protocols, including cefazolin administration and timing, were utilized. The primary endpoint was the development of allergic reactions (e.g., anaphylaxis, rash), either intraoperatively or six hours postoperatively. The secondary endpoints included surgical site infection (SSI) and periprosthetic joint infection (PJI). Descriptive statistics were used for the analysis.

RESULTS: Of the 51 SPA patients, seven (13.7%) had documented penicillin allergies that were also confirmed by skin testing. Questionnaire results showed allergies lasted a mean of 42.9 years. Reaction types included severe skin rash (58.8%), dyspnea (56.9%), body swelling (45.1%), face swelling (35.3%), severe pruritus (45.1%), wheezing (35.3%), and anaphylaxis (15.7%). Most patients (86.3%) reported two to five of these reactions. There were no intraoperative or immediate postoperative allergic reactions that occurred with cefazolin use (zero of 51; 95% confidence interval 0 to 7.0).

CONCLUSION: There were no perioperative allergic reactions observed among 51 patients who had reported severe penicillin allergy and received cefazolin. These findings represent a preliminary prospective safety signal and require confirmation in larger studies.

articles.title: Cervicofacial eumycetoma caused by Cladosporium cucumerinum in India: A rare molecularly confirmed case.
articles.abstract: Mycetoma is a chronic granulomatous subcutaneous infection, with cervicofacial involvement being rare. We report a rare molecularly confirmed case of cervicofacial eumycetoma caused by Cladosporium cucumerinum in a 37-year-old immunocompetent male from India with recurrent swelling, multiple draining sinuses, purulent discharge, and trismus following traumatic scalp injury. MRI revealed extensive soft tissue involvement with sinus tracts and mandibular osteomyelitis. Direct microscopy and histopathology were non-contributory, while fungal culture yielded Cladosporium species. Sanger sequencing targeting ITS, actin, β-tubulin, and 28S rDNA genes confirmed C. cucumerinum. To our knowledge, this is the first molecularly confirmed human case of mycetoma caused by C. cucumerinum reported from India.

articles.title: Clinically significant portal hypertension rather than ALBI grade predicts prognosis in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Clinical trials in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) typically include patients with preserved liver function (Child-Pugh A), without adequately considering cirrhosis or clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH). We aimed to compare prognostic models in Child-Pugh A patients.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: This prospective multicenter cohort study included patients with advanced HCC treated with systemic therapy (2018-2024) in Latin America. Survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional multivariate hazards models and competing risk analysis for cause-specific mortality and hepatic decompensation.

RESULTS: From 306 patients receiving systemic therapy, 79.1% (n=242) were Child-Pugh A (sorafenib 60.3%, atezolizumab plus bevacizumab 30.6%, and lenvatinib 8.7%). Among these, cirrhosis was observed in 78.9%, and CSPH in 51.6%. No survival differences were observed between ALBI 1 vs 2-3 grades (HR 1.08; P=0.685), or Child-Pugh A5 vs A6. In multivariable analysis, atezolizumab plus bevacizumab was independently associated with improved OS (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.42-0.99), adjusted for AFP ≥400 ng/mL and CSPH. Other models, including the ALBI score as a continuous or categorical variable, showed no significant independent association with mortality, nor did they improve model performance. In a competing risk regression analysis accounting for death due to tumor progression as a competing event, CSPH was the only independent variable associated with hepatic decompensation, sHR 1.98 (95% CI 1.01-3.89).

CONCLUSIONS: Accurate reporting of cirrhosis and CSPH is essential, even for Child-Pugh A patients, as both are independent prognostic factors that should be considered for therapeutic decision-making in advanced HCC.

articles.title: From concentrated output to regional capacity: the next step for Latin American hepatology research.
Aspergillus species isolation in respiratory samples from patients with respiratory syncytial virus: An 11-year retrospective single-center cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus is a significant cause of morbidity in adults, but data on fungal coinfections, beyond influenza-associated pulmonary aspergillosis and COVID-19-associated pulmonary aspergillosis, remain limited.

AIMS: To characterize the isolation of Aspergillus in respiratory samples from adult patients with confirmed respiratory syncytial virus infection over an 11-year period, and to describe associated risk factors, microbiological findings, antifungal treatment, and clinical outcomes.

METHODS: We conducted an 11-year retrospective study at Hospital Universitario La Paz (Madrid, Spain) including 17 adult patients with confirmed respiratory syncytial virus infection and Aspergillus isolation from respiratory samples. Episodes were classified as probable invasive aspergillosis or colonization according to clinical, radiological, and microbiological findings.

RESULTS: A total of 18 episodes were identified, with the species within the Aspergillus fumigatus complex being the most frequently isolated (78.9%), followed by Aspergillus terreus complex (10.5%), Aspergillus nidulans complex (5.3%), and Aspergillus niger complex (5.3). Most isolates were considered colonization (55.6%), while probable invasive aspergillosis accounted for 44.4% episodes, based on compatible clinical and radiological findings. Corticosteroid exposure was common with 82.4% receiving or starting a corticosteroid therapy during hospitalization, and antifungal therapy was administered in 44.4% of episodes, including voriconazole and liposomal amphotericin B. The median hospital stay was 16 days (IQR: 8-28). Mortality was 11.1%.

CONCLUSIONS: Aspergillus isolation in adults with respiratory syncytial virus infection was observed mainly in patients with underlying pulmonary disease or comorbidities, with colonization being more frequent than invasive aspergillosis. However, no episodes of severe invasive aspergillosis requiring intensive care were observed in this cohort. Our study provides novel insights into Aspergillus isolation associated with respiratory syncytial virus infection and emphasizes the need for further multicentric studies to define epidemiology, risk factors, and optimal management strategies.

articles.title: A neonatal low-dose streptozotocin rat model of a prediabetic phenotype produces metabolic, peripheral nerve, and locomotor alterations.
articles.abstract: Prediabetes is a state of impaired glucose regulation that precedes diabetes and is increasingly recognized to harbor early metabolic and neuropathic alterations. Because neuronal alterations at this stage may still be reversible, experimental models that reproduce early nerve changes are essential for investigating the mechanisms underlying disease initiation and progression. Here, we characterized a rodent prediabetic phenotype induced by a single low dose of streptozotocin in male and female rats. Treated animals developed a prediabetes-like metabolic profile characterized by moderate fasting hyperglycemia, glucose intolerance, elevated glycated hemoglobin, insulin resistance, lipid alterations, and a partial reduction in pancreatic β-cell islet area and cell density, all while maintaining normal body weight-key features that distinguish this model from diabetic phenotypes in rodents. Importantly, these metabolic alterations were accompanied by early increased expression of activating transcription factor 3 in dorsal root ganglion neurons, indicating neuronal damage. These pathological changes were associated with the progressive development of mechanical hypersensitivity and locomotor adaptations. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that low-dose streptozotocin induces a reproducible prediabetic phenotype in male and female rats that is accompanied by early peripheral nerve damage and functional sensory and locomotor alterations. This prediabetes-like phenotype provides a useful tool for investigating the cellular and molecular mechanisms driving early nerve dysfunction and for evaluating therapeutic strategies aimed at preventing the transition from a prediabetic state to diabetic disease.

articles.title: Single-cell Bioinformatics Analysis and In Vitro Validation Explore Core Genes and Signaling Pathways of Iron Metabolism in Fetal Left Heart Function Injury in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a common metabolic disorder during pregnancy that significantly affects fetal cardiac development. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying iron metabolism-related pathways in GDM-induced fetal left heart dysfunction remain incompletely understood.

METHODS: This study employed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology combined with bioinformatics analysis and published echocardiographic data validation to comprehensively characterize the cellular landscape and iron metabolism signatures in publicly available GDM fetal cardiac transcriptomic data from the GEO database (GSM5261695 and GSM5261697).

RESULTS: Analysis of 4,531 cells identified 17 distinct clusters comprising 9 major cardiac cell types. Cardiomyocytes exhibited the highest iron metabolism dysregulation scores. Ferroptosis pathway analysis revealed elevated GPX4 and SLC7A11 expression with concurrent ACSL4 downregulation in GDM samples. Clinical ultrasound validation demonstrated significant left ventricular dysfunction in GDM fetuses, including reduced ejection fraction and impaired diastolic function. RT-qPCR validation confirmed significant upregulation of GPX4 (2.45-fold), SLC7A11 (2.87-fold), and FTH1 (2.31-fold) in high glucose-treated cardiomyocytes, with concurrent ACSL4 downregulation (0.52-fold). GPX4 protein validation by immunofluorescence and Western blot further showed higher GPX4 signal in the OGD group and reduced GPX4 expression after GPX4 knockdown.

CONCLUSION: This study reveals that dysregulated iron metabolism and ferroptosis resistance in fetal cardiomyocytes serve as critical mechanisms underlying GDM-induced left heart dysfunction. The identification of cell type-specific iron metabolism signatures provides novel therapeutic targets for preventing and treating fetal cardiac complications in GDM pregnancies.

articles.title: EUK-134, a superoxide dismutase and catalase mimetic, inhibits inflammatory cytokines, reduces myocyte necroptosis and improves left ventricular remodeling and function in heart failure after myocardial infarction in mice.
articles.abstract: Increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) play a crucial role in heart failure after myocardial infarction (MI), but the underlying mechanism remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigated whether EUK-134, a synthetic superoxide dismutase and catalase mimetic, reduces myocardial oxidative stress, inflammatory cytokines and myocyte necroptosis and apoptosis, leading to the improvement of left ventricular (LV) remodeling and function in heart failure after MI. Eight-week old C57BL/6J mice underwent MI or sham operation. The animals were randomized to receive EUK-134 (25 mg/kg, every other day, i.p.) or placebo for four weeks. In the MI placebo group, LV end-diastolic and end-systolic dimensions were increased, LV fractional shortening and LV ejection fraction were decreased, and these alterations were attenuated by the treatment of EUK-134. In the MI placebo group, myocardial expression of 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine, a marker of oxidative stress, inflammatory cytokines tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-1β and interleukin-6, and phosphorylated RIP1 (p-RIP1), p-RIP3 and p-MLKL, reflective of their respect kinase activities, markers of necroptosis, pro-apoptotic Bax protein, phosphorylated JNK (p-JNK) protein, cleaved caspase protein and myocyte apoptosis were markedly increased, and the increases were prevented by the treatment of EUK-134. Similarly, intracellular levels of ROS, necroptosis and apoptosis were increased in H9C2 cardiomyocytes under mimic ischemia and the increases were prevented by the EUK-134 treatment. These findings suggest that the superoxide dismutase and catalase mimetic EUK-134 prevents RIP1-RIP3-MLKL-mediated myocyte necroptosis and Bax/JNK-mediated myocyte apoptosis through inhibition of myocardial oxidative stress and inflammatory cytokines, leading to the improvement of post-MI LV remodeling and failure.

articles.title: Targeting Vasopressin Signaling in Sepsis: Effects of Tolvaptan on Inflammation and Aquaporin Dysregulation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Sepsis is a life-threatening condition characterized by a dysregulated host response to infection, leading to multiple organ injury. Disturbances in fluid homeostasis and inflammation play key roles in its pathophysiology. Aquaporins, which regulate water transport across cell membranes, may contribute to sepsis-associated organ injury. This study aimed to investigate the effects of the vasopressin V2 receptor antagonist tolvaptan on sepsis-induced multiple organ injury and its relationship with aquaporins.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: An experimental sepsis model was established in rats using LPS. The animals were divided into control, sepsis, and sepsis + tolvaptan treatment groups. Tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), and interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels, as well as aquaporin-2 (AQP2) and aquaporin-5 (AQP5) expression levels, were evaluated in blood and tissue samples. In addition, histopathological examinations were performed. Furthermore, the effects of tolvaptan on cytotoxicity and inflammatory response were investigated in an in vitro model of LPS-induced inflammation.

RESULTS: LPS-induced inflammation was associated with significant elevations in TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 levels, along with marked reductions in lung AQP5 and kidney AQP2 expression. Tolvaptan treatment significantly reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine levels, increased AQP5 expression, and further enhanced the reduction in AQP2 expression. Histopathological evaluations confirmed the organ-protective effects of tolvaptan.

CONCLUSION: Tolvaptan attenuated the inflammatory response and alleviated organ injury associated with sepsis. The observed increase in AQP5 expression and suppression of AQP2 expression suggest that vasopressin V2 receptor inhibition may modulate aquaporin expression and contribute to protection against sepsis-induced organ injury. Therefore, the vasopressin V2 receptor-aquaporin axis may represent a potential therapeutic target in the treatment of sepsis.

articles.title: HFpEF-ABA Score Can Predict Long-Term Mortality Across All Heart Failure Categories in Acute Heart Failure.
articles.abstract: HFpEF-ABA score, based on age, body mass index, and history of atrial fibrillation, was initially developed as a diagnostic screening tool for heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). This study evaluated the prognostic significance of HFpEF-ABA score for all-cause mortality across HF phenotypes in patients hospitalized for acute HF (AHF). We analyzed 3,974 admitted patients in the STRATS-AHF registry (Korea, 2009-2016), classified into HFrEF (LVEF ≤40%; n=2,094), HFmrEF (LVEF 41-49%; n=609), and HFpEF (LVEF ≥50%; n=1,271). The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Over a median follow-up of 51.4 months, 1,642 patients (41.3%) died. HFpEF-ABA score was significantly higher in nonsurvivors than survivors (61.0±23.2 vs. 54.6±25.9; P<0.001), with a univariate hazard ratio (HR) of 1.009 per point (95% CI: 1.007-1.011; P<0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis revealed a monotonically increasing, non-linear association between the score and mortality risk, and patients with a score <45 had much better 6-year survival compared to those with a score ≥45 in the overall group and in each HF phenotype (all P≤0.005). Adding HFpEF-ABA score to clinical, pharmacological, and echocardiographic variables produced a modest but significant improvement in individual risk reclassification (net reclassification improvement 0.198; integrated discrimination improvement 0.013), despite only a marginal increase in discrimination (C-index from 0.696 to 0.700, P<0.001), with an independent HR of 1.008 per point (95% CI: 1.005-1.012; P<0.001) and preserved calibration. HFpEF-ABA score independently predicted long-term all-cause mortality across HF phenotypes in AHF patients, offering modest incremental prognostic value beyond established clinical, echocardiographic, and therapeutic predictors.

articles.title: Concomitant Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair and Left Atrial Appendage Closure in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and High Bleeding Risk.
articles.abstract: Evidence on concomitant mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) and left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is limited. This retrospective registry compared 216 isolated M-TEER procedures with 133 concomitant procedures at 13 centers. The primary endpoint was cardiovascular death, stroke or transient ischemic attack, or site-reported major bleeding through 24 months. Analyses used Kaplan-Meier estimates, center-clustered Cox models, and overlap weighting. Median follow-up was 21.5 months after isolated and 9.2 months after concomitant treatment. The primary endpoint occurred in 41 (19.0%) and 16 (12.0%) patients, respectively; 24-month event-free survival was 73.8% and 80.1%. The adjusted hazard ratio was 0.79 (95% confidence interval 0.50-1.25), and the expanded overlap-weighted estimate was 0.79 (0.49-1.28). Overlap-weighted estimates with follow-up truncated at 9 and 12 months were 1.02 (0.56-1.83) and 0.91 (0.50-1.63). Results were sensitive to exclusion of patients with reconstructed event dates. Oral anticoagulation at discharge was prescribed in 187/202 (92.6%) evaluable isolated-procedure patients and 20/133 (15.0%) concomitant-procedure patients; standardized longitudinal medication assessments were unavailable. In conclusion, concomitant M-TEER and LAAC was feasible and associated with less anticoagulant prescription at discharge, but nonrandom allocation, unequal follow-up, incomplete bleeding classification, and uncertain event timing prevent conclusions regarding comparative clinical benefit.

articles.title: Cryptosporidium spp. and Giardia duodenalis infections in pre-weaned calves in Tunisia: prevalence, risk factors and molecular studies.
articles.abstract: Cryptosporidium spp. and Giardia duodenalis are zoonotic enteric protozoa responsible for diarrheal diseases in calves and humans worldwide. This study assessed the prevalence, molecular diversity, and risk factors associated with these two parasites in pre-weaned calves from five Tunisian governorates. A total of 231 fecal samples were collected from calves aged ≤45 days across 8 farms and screened by direct immunofluorescence and nested PCR. Cryptosporidium spp. and G. duodenalis were detected in 51.1% and 31.1% of calves, respectively, with substantial concordance between PCR and immunofluorescence. Molecular assays have shown greater sensitivity than immunofluorescence. Diarrhea and geographic region were associated with Cryptosporidium, while age, region, and the presence of diarrhea were significant risk factors for G. duodenalis. Jendouba consistently emerged as a low-risk region for both parasites. Four Cryptosporidium species were identified: C. parvum (n = 98), C. bovis (n = 15), C. ryanae (n = 3), and C. andersoni (n = 1). Among the C. parvum species identified, five subtypes were detected and the zoonotic IIaA15G2R1 subtype was predominent (n = 61). For G. duodenalis, the assemblage E was predominant (n = 42), followed by assemblages B (n = 11) and A (n = 10). These findings demonstrate a high burden of Cryptosporidium spp. and G. duodenalis infections in Tunisian calves and confirm the circulation of zoonotic subtypes and assemblages, supporting the role of calves as a reservoir for human infection. Furthermore, these findings reinforce the relevance of a One Health approach to managing these parasites in Tunisia.

articles.title: The atherosclerotic plaque microenvironment: cellular plasticity, extracellular matrix remodeling, and plaque stability.
articles.abstract: The plaque microenvironment (PME) integrates systemic lipid exposure with local vascular, immune and stromal responses. Vascular smooth muscle cells, endothelial cells, monocytes, macrophages, fibroblast-like cells and lymphocytes interact within a continuously remodeled extracellular matrix. Their context-dependent states influence inflammation, lipid handling, matrix organization and the balance between plaque stability and vulnerability. This narrative review examines these cellular and extracellular components, with particular attention to phenotypic modulation, endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition and the limitations of inferring cellular origin from shared markers. Human single-cell findings expand the conventional M1/M2 view of macrophages. Therapeutic evidence is considered across experimental models, human pathology, intravascular imaging and randomized clinical outcome trials. Systemic lipid lowering and selected anti-inflammatory interventions can modify atherosclerotic disease, but changes in plaque composition do not by themselves establish reductions in myocardial infarction or stroke. Carotid and coronary findings also require site-specific interpretation. Integrating mechanistic observations with the level and anatomical setting of the evidence provides a framework for evaluating established therapies and developing selective PME-directed strategies.

articles.title: Acute kidney injury in imported malaria: A 20-year retrospective cohort study with derivation and internal validation of a simple early assessment score.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) complicates malaria and worsens outcomes, but data from non-endemic European settings are scarce and no simple early clinical risk-stratification tool exists for this population.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed adults hospitalized with parasitologically confirmed malaria at a tertiary referral center in Belgrade, Serbia (2004-2024). AKI was defined according to the 2012 Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) creatinine criteria. A point-based early AKI assessment score was derived from the final multivariable logistic regression model and internally evaluated in patients with complete data using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and bootstrap resampling.

RESULTS: Of 214 patients (94.9% male; median age 39 years), 71 (33.2%) fulfilled KDIGO criteria for AKI, predominantly stage 1. The final model retained older age, first-ever malaria episode, vomiting, abnormal vital signs, and dipstick proteinuria; abnormal vital signs were borderline in complete cases but significant after multiple imputation. In complete cases (n = 162), the score had an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.841; at the ≥14 cut-off, sensitivity was 87.3%, specificity 66.4%, and negative predictive value 91.0%. Bootstrap internal validation yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.822. AKI patients had longer hospital stays than those without AKI (median 9 vs. 6 days; p < 0.001). Mortality was 0.9%.

CONCLUSIONS: AKI was common in this imported-malaria cohort and was associated with simple variables available at early clinical assessment. The proposed score may support early AKI risk stratification, but requires external validation before routine use.

articles.title: Whole genome sequencing and pathogenicity analysis of Fusarium arcuatisporum from peanut stems.
articles.abstract: Fusarium arcuatisporum is a widely distributed filamentous plant pathogen. Here, we isolated and identified Fusarium arcuatisporum strain SLY02, sequenced its complete genome, and investigated its molecular pathogenic mechanisms. Strain SLY02 formed white powdery aerial hyphae on PDA medium, sharing 98% sequence identity with Fusarium arcuatisporum. Whole genome sequencing generated a 38.67 Mb genome encoding 7691 genes, including 1564 pathogen-host interaction genes, 409 virulence factors, 736 carbohydrate-active enzymes, and 65 genes distributed in 10 secondary metabolic clusters. In mouse infection models, 7-day infection significantly increased liver indices (P < 0.01). Histopathological staining revealed granulomatous hepatitis, neutrophil infiltration, hepatocellular necrosis, and black hyphae in liver nodules. Necroptosis-related genes (RIPK1, RIPK3, MLKL, TNF-α) were highly significantly upregulated (P < 0.01), while Caspase-8 was markedly downregulated (P < 0.01). Antifungal susceptibility testing showed strain SLY02 was sensitive to itraconazole but resistant to caspofungin, voriconazole, and amphotericin B. This study provides important genomic resources and in-depth mechanistic insights into the pathogenic mechanism of Fusarium arcuatisporum, offering a reference for preventing Fusarium contamination in feed and controlling related livestock diseases.

articles.title: Research and Clinical Considerations for Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Healthy Populations.
articles.abstract: The expanding availability of continuous glucose monitors (CGMs) has generated growing interest in their application beyond diabetes management, particularly in healthy individuals seeking to optimize metabolic health through personalized nutrition. In May 2025, the Institute for the Advancement of Food and Nutrition Sciences (IAFNS) convened a multidisciplinary expert workshop to examine the scientific, methodological, and clinical considerations surrounding continuous glucose monitor (CGM) application in healthy populations. Discussions addressed normal glycemic physiology, determinants of postprandial glycemic responses (PPGRs), CGM use and functional health outcomes, research applications, and implications for clinical practice. The purpose of this initiative was to develop a perspective paper that synthesizes current evidence and provides guidance on these key considerations to inform responsible research, clinical interpretation, and future policy related to CGM use in populations who do not have diabetes mellitus. Evidence discussed during the workshop underscored substantial inter- and intra-individual variability in PPGRs driven by complex interactions among dietary composition, lifestyle behaviors, and physiological characteristics. CGMs offer the ability to capture these dynamics under real-world conditions and may help identify meaningful individual differences, particularly as PPGRs are increasingly recognized as sensitive markers of early disturbances in glucose regulation. However, important limitations constrain interpretation in healthy populations, including analytical variability, limited precision for single-meal or acute assessments, lack of standardized research protocols and consensus guidance, and insufficient evidence linking CGM-derived metrics to long-term clinical outcomes. High-quality randomized controlled trials, standardized protocols, consensus guidance and integrated metabolic frameworks are needed to determine the clinical relevance of CGM use in healthy populations. Until such evidence is established, CGM use outside of diabetes care should be approached cautiously and ideally within structured research or in clinical contexts that provide appropriate education and professional oversight. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: This perspective addresses an important and timely gap in nutrition and health research by evaluating the scientific considerations, methodological limitations, and clinical implications of CGM use in individuals living without diabetes. This paper provides important insights and considerations for the potential integration of CGMs into personalized nutrition research and practice.

articles.title: The evolution of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in Greek intensive care units is driven by local carbapenemase acquisition, nationwide nosocomial spread and emerging resistance to novel antimicrobials.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We investigated transmission patterns and therapeutic options for Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CR-Kp) in Greek ICUs.

METHODS: CR-Kp isolates (N=271) were prospectively collected from patients in 17 Greek ICUs between 2021-2023 (INCREASE study, funded by Pfizer). Susceptibility profiles were determined by broth microdilution and genomes sequenced with Oxford Nanopore.

RESULTS: All isolates produced carbapenemases: 48% KPC, 20% NDM, 4.4% VIM, 27.6% multi-carbapenemase producers. Resistance to carbapenems, fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, and co-trimoxazole exceeded 90%, except for amikacin (73.4%) and colistin (46.5%). Aztreonam-avibactam and cefepime-zidebactam showed the highest susceptibility, 94.5% and 91.6% respectively, yet resistance was >10% among multi-carbapenemase producers. High levels of resistance to cefiderocol (41.7%) and cefepime-taniborbactam (21.4%) were detected. Aztreonam-avibactam resistance co-occurred with VEB-25 and a novel VEB variant. Predominant sequence types included ST39 (28.1%), ST11 (22.7%), and ST258 (18.4%). Time-scaled phylogenies demonstrated that following CG importation CR-Kp often acquired multiple carbapenemases. Over 88% of isolates were implicated in transmission clusters involving 1-8 ICUs across the country.

CONCLUSIONS: In Greek ICUs, CR-Kp appears to emerge via local plasmid acquisition and then spread within and between hospitals. While aztreonam-avibactam and cefepime-zidebactam remain promising treatment options, resistance among multi-carbapenemase producers and diagnostic gaps (notably for VEB variants) are concerning.

articles.title: Patient Awareness and Disease Burden in MASLD: A Large-Scale Survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: A global international Delphi consensus of MASLD experts prioritised patient education and awareness as a key research domain, explicitly calling for population-based surveys to quantify knowledge gaps and guide targeted interventions. Commissioned by the EpaC ETS patient association, this study described patients' characteristics regarding MASLD awareness and health literacy. Secondary aim was to assess the psychometric properties and construct structure of the survey instrument.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study enrolled 460 Italian adults with self-reported physician-diagnosed MASLD. The eight-domain questionnaire covered disease awareness, nomenclature familiarity, diagnostic pathway, follow-up, treatment knowledge, lifestyle adherence, supplement and pharmacotherapy use, and economic burden. Psychometric validation of 40 Likert items employed exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis and MIMIC modelling.

RESULTS: Pre-diagnostic awareness was strikingly low: 59.8% had never heard of MASLD; familiarity with current nomenclature was negligible (MASLD 8.5%, MASH 9.8%). Critical misconceptions included failure to recognise diabetes as a risk factor (43.5%), belief that transaminases are always elevated (41.5%), and that disease progression requires elevated ALT (51.5%). Symptom burden was high and significantly greater in women across all domains (p<0.001). Despite appropriate physician counselling, three in four patients (75.7%) did not meet the recommended >= 150 min/week and 26.1% were entirely inactive. Supplements were used by 27.6%, largely self-prescribed; pharmacotherapy by 11.7%, of whom 50.0% received ursodeoxycholic acid - not guideline-recommended. Direct economic burden affected 64.6% of patients. Psychometric validation identified five latent dimensions (symptom burden, disease knowledge, reversibility beliefs, lifestyle efficacy beliefs, extrahepatic risk awareness) with acceptable model fit (CFI=0.917, RMSEA=0.069) and good-to-excellent reliability (omega 0.79-0.93). MIMIC modelling showed that symptom burden was driven by female sex and by depression, while cognitive dimensions were determined primarily by educational attainment and, to a lesser extent, by obesity.

CONCLUSIONS: Italian patients with self-reported physician diagnosis of MASLD harbour profound educational deficits, a marked attitude-practice gap, and partly guideline-discordant pharmacotherapy. The five-domain instrument provides a candidate framework for stratified educational interventions, for which external validation in an independent cohort is a prerequisite.

IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: A global Delphi consensus of MASLD experts identified patient education and awareness as a priority research domain and explicitly called for population-based surveys to quantify knowledge gaps, yet patient-level European data remain scarce; this study addresses that gap by assessing awareness, nomenclature familiarity, treatment knowledge, lifestyle behaviour and economic burden within a single national cohort, and by exploring the latent structure underlying patient knowledge. These results matter to hepatologists, primary care physicians, patient associations and policymakers, because they show that a formal diagnosis does not by itself transfer knowledge: misconceptions about diabetes as a risk factor and about the meaning of normal transaminases were widespread, lifestyle counselling was poorly translated into behaviour, and supplement use was frequent and largely self-prescribed. Practically, these findings support routine correction of these two misconceptions at the point of care, a direct question on over-the-counter and herbal products during the MASLD consultation, screening for depression within MASLD care pathways, and educational materials stratified by educational attainment and delivered through the digital and AI-based channels that patients actually use. Because participants were recruited through a patient association and MASLD status was self-reported, the deficits observed here should be regarded as conservative, and the five-domain instrument requires external validation in an independent, unselected and objectively characterised cohort before applied use.

articles.title: Semaglutide versus diet-based weight loss in obesity and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (FIT-HF): Protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Obesity is common in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), but the functional, mechanistic, and safety consequences of intentional weight loss remain uncertain. Incretin-based therapies improve symptoms and functional capacity in obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, whereas evidence in HFrEF is limited, and prior glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist trials have raised safety concerns. The FIT-HF trial tests whether semaglutide-based weight loss is superior to intensive diet-based weight loss for improving exercise capacity in adults with obesity and stable HFrEF.

METHODS: FIT-HF is an investigator-initiated, randomized, parallel-group, open-label, assessor-blinded, active-comparator superiority trial enrolling 100 adults with body mass index ≥30 kg/m2, left ventricular ejection fraction ≤40%, New York Heart Association class I-III symptoms, and stable guideline-directed heart failure therapy. Participants are randomized 1:1 to once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide, titrated to a target dose of 2.4 mg, or low-calorie total dietary replacement of approximately 800 kcal/day for 8 weeks followed by a dietitian-led weight-maintenance program. Both groups receive lifestyle counseling, heart failure care, and structured physical training from week 16. Follow-up is 52 weeks. The primary endpoint is the adjusted between-group difference in change in weight-indexed peak oxygen uptake (VO2peak) from baseline to week 52, assessed by cardiopulmonary exercise testing. Supportive secondary endpoints include Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score, 6-min walk distance, left ventricular end-systolic volume assessed by cardiovascular magnetic resonance, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide. Exploratory work packages assess safety, cardiac/pulmonary physiology, body composition, physical activity, and metabolic/biomarker responses.

DISCUSSION: FIT-HF is the first direct comparison of these weight-loss strategies in obesity and HFrEF, integrating VO2peak with multimodal phenotyping to interpret physiological profiles alongside achieved weight loss and body composition.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: European Clinical Trials Information System: European Union trial number: CT-2023-503753-35-01; ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06423599.

articles.title: Experiences of dietary management among individuals with liver cirrhosis - facilitators and barriers in adapting to nutritional therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Malnutrition is common among individuals with liver cirrhosis, often due to eating difficulties such as reduced appetite and early satiety. These challenges, along with physical, psychological, and social factors, may hinder adherence to nutritional therapy, which is essential for managing liver cirrhosis. This study explored the experiences and perspectives of individuals with liver cirrhosis regarding facilitators and barriers to nutritional therapy.

METHODS: A qualitative design was used, involving semi-structured interviews with 14 individuals diagnosed with liver cirrhosis and at risk of malnutrition. Participants were recruited from a specialized hepatology centre in Sweden. Data were analysed using inductive thematic analysis.

RESULTS: Three overarching themes emerged: (1) Understanding and adapting to my new physical self, which included the importance of personalized information and physical and cognitive cues; (2) Significance of motivation and support, highlighting internal and external motivators, support from family and friends, and empathetic approach from health care professionals; and (3) Challenges and possibilities in everyday life, encompassing planning and routines, financial considerations, and food and cooking knowledge. Participants emphasized the relationship between physical, psychological, and social factors in managing nutritional therapy. Facilitators included noticing improvements, empathetic approach from the dietitian, receiving explanations tailored to oneself and support from family members. Barriers involved physiological and cognitive limitations and economic constraints.

CONCLUSIONS: Nutritional therapy for liver cirrhosis should be individualized and responsive to each patient's medical, social, and emotional context. A person-centred, empathetic approach with practical support and clear communication may enhance adherence and self-care.

articles.title: Age-specific risk of musculoskeletal and neurological disorders following fluoroquinolone exposure among children aged <18 years.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quantifying the risk of fluoroquinolone-associated musculoskeletal and neurological adverse event among children stratified supports clinicians to select the most appropriate antimicrobial regimen for children with bacterial infection. The objective of this study was to assess the risk of musculoskeletal and neurological disorders following fluoroquinolone exposure, compared with another antimicrobial class using the large-scale database.

METHODS: This retrospective study used the TriNetX platform, a multicenter health record database, to compare risk of musculoskeletal and neurological disorders following fluoroquinolone versus macrolide exposure in children aged <18 years. Propensity score matching was implemented to estimate odds ratio (OR) with 95% confidence interval (CI) of each musculoskeletal and neurological outcome.

RESULTS: In the United States, 423,880, 380,504 and 194,220 children aged <5, 5-11 and 12-17 years were matched from each group for the musculoskeletal cohort. The OR of any musculoskeletal outcomes, including disorders of tendon or synovium, in the fluoroquinolone was not increased. Conversely, the OR of peripheral neuropathy and sleep disorder following fluoroquinolone use were 2.22 [1.61-3.06]; p<0.001 and 1.57 [1.44-1.70]; p<0.001, 1.52 [1.20-1.93]; p<0.001 and 1.34 [1.26-1.43]; p<0.001, and 2.18 [1.75-2.72]; p<0.001) and 1.23 [1.13-1.35]; p<0.001 in children aged <5, 5-11, and 12-17 years, respectively.

CONCLUSION: This study showed the increased risk of peripheral neuropathy and sleep disorder following fluoroquinolones use among children compared with macrolide use. This study provided the data for clinicians to estimate risks of musculoskeletal or neurological adverse events.

articles.title: Human metapneumovirus-associated ARI hospitalisation rates in comparison to respiratory syncytial virus and influenza in eastern China, 2020-2024: a time-series analysis.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We estimated human metapneumovirus (hMPV)-associated acute respiratory infection (ARI) hospitalisations in eastern China, and provided a direct comparison with RSV and influenza during 2020-2024.

METHODS: Leveraging a large regional medical database, we analysed weekly ARI hospitalisations and viral test-positives (hMPV, RSV and influenza) by age group and region, using negative binomial regression models with natural cubic splines, time-offsets for viral activity, excluding COVID-19 patients and adjusting for COVID-19 waves.

RESULTS: hMPV, RSV, and influenza were associated with 100,792 (5.35%), 266,826 (14.17%), and 409,599 (21.76%) ARI hospitalisations, respectively. RSV hospitalisations rebounded first in 2021/2022, followed by hMPV in 2022/2023, while influenza hospitalisations increased annually during the study period; meanwhile, hMPV- and influenza-associated hospitalisations shifted towards those aged 5-19 years, while RSV-associated hospitalisations shifted towards those aged ≥5 years. hMPV rates were highest among infants aged 0-5 months and 6-11 months (6.19 and 8.15 per 1,000 per year on average, respectively), followed by ages 12-23 months (18.54). RSV and influenza rates were highest in age groups within <1 year and 1-4 years, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Infants aged <1 year are the primary group for preventing severe hMPV infections, with a substantial additional burden observed in children aged 1-4 years. These findings support hMPV vaccine development and virus-specific intervention strategies.

articles.title: Proceedings from the 2025 International Consensus Meeting on Orthopedic Infections: Diagnosis of Periprosthetic Shoulder Infection.
articles.journal: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prosthetic joint infection (PJI) following shoulder arthroplasty is difficult to diagnose because clinical findings are often nonspecific, conventional diagnostic tests have variable sensitivity, and Cutibacterium acnes (C. acnes) may cause indolent infection with limited systemic inflammatory response. Diagnostic criteria have also largely been adapted from hip and knee arthroplasty with limited shoulder-specific validation. This International Consensus Meeting (ICM) reviewed the available evidence and developed consensus recommendations for the diagnosis of shoulder PJI.

METHODS: The Shoulder Group of the 2025 ICM on Orthopedic Infections included international shoulder surgeons, infectious disease physicians, and microbiology experts experienced in shoulder arthroplasty and PJI. Thirty-two diagnostic questions underwent question-specific literature review, presentation to the consensus group, discussion, and voting. A modified Delphi process was used to establish consensus. Delegates voted to agree, disagree, or abstain. Consensus was categorized by percentage agreement, while strength of recommendation was assessed separately based on evidence quality, consistency, and directness.

RESULTS: Consensus was achieved for 31 analyzed questions, with agreement ranging from 72% to 100%; 29 resulted in recommendations for clinical practice and 2 were identified as requiring further research. Question 47, which addressed the definition of PJI, was reported separately. Humeral component loosening, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), and C-reactive protein (CRP) were supported as components of the diagnostic criteria, whereas cloudy fluid, postoperative stiffness, serum WBC count, and D-dimer were not supported as independent criteria. Arthroscopic tissue biopsy, frozen section, and selective ultrasound-guided aspiration or synovial biopsy were supported as adjuncts to diagnosis. Five intraoperative tissue specimens, prolonged aerobic and anaerobic culture incubation, and routine perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis were supported. Next-generation sequencing (NGS) and synovial neutrophil testing were supported as adjuncts; alpha-defensin was considered potentially useful but insufficiently validated for formal inclusion; and leukocyte esterase inclusion was not recommended. Routine use of bone scintigraphy, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), computed tomography (CT), single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), or positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) was not supported. Evidence remained insufficient to determine the clinical significance of polymicrobial molecular results or routine negative control samples.

CONCLUSION: The 2025 ICM provides a consensus framework for the diagnosis of shoulder PJI, identifying several measures that can be incorporated into current clinical practice. However, substantial uncertainty remains because most recommendations are supported by limited evidence and several diagnostic tests lack sufficient sensitivity. Prospective, shoulder-specific studies are needed to define diagnostic thresholds and determine the role of emerging molecular, biomarker, and imaging modalities.

articles.title: Bilirubin in depression: redox-inflammatory mechanisms, clinical associations, and biomarker potential.
articles.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a heterogeneous psychiatric disorder associated with oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, neuroendocrine dysregulation, and altered neuroplasticity. Bilirubin, an endogenous heme metabolite, exhibits antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and cytoprotective properties in experimental systems, suggesting potential relevance to biological pathways implicated in depression. This review critically examines the biological rationale and clinical evidence linking bilirubin with depression and evaluates its potential translational significance. Clinical studies report heterogeneous associations between bilirubin concentrations and depressive outcomes across different populations, including MDD, postpartum depression, post-stroke depression, and individuals with diabetes. Some studies suggest inverse or potentially nonlinear associations, while findings vary according to population characteristics and clinical context. These observations may reflect differences in metabolic status, liver function, medication exposure, genetic variation, and other confounding factors. Proposed mechanisms involve oxidative and inflammatory signaling, mitochondrial function, neuroendocrine regulation, and vascular pathways; however, much of the mechanistic evidence derives from experimental models or populations other than individuals with MDD. Observational associations and experimental antioxidant effects do not establish that bilirubin causally protects against depression. Current evidence does not establish bilirubin as a validated diagnostic or prognostic biomarker for depression or as a causal protective factor. Bilirubin may warrant investigation as an adjunct within multimarker approaches, but its incremental clinical value remains uncertain. Larger longitudinal, multicenter, mechanistic, and multi-omics studies using standardized measurement methods are needed to clarify temporal and causal relationships, assess population-specific associations, and determine whether bilirubin contributes meaningfully to risk stratification or treatment monitoring.

articles.title: Lipotoxicity and inflammation linking between diet, obesity, diabetes, and kidney disease.
articles.abstract: Unhealthy dietary patterns and chronic overnutrition are major drivers of endocrine-metabolic dysfunction, contributing to the development of obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), and chronic kidney disease (CKD). Beyond traditional risk factors, obesity is increasingly recognized as a direct contributor to renal dysfunction, partly mediated by ectopic lipid accumulation within the kidney, a phenomenon referred to as fatty kidney disease. At the molecular level, excessive consumption of saturated fats and refined carbohydrates disrupts insulin signaling pathways, particularly the IRS-1/PI3K/Akt axis, thereby promoting systemic insulin resistance (IR). This metabolic overload triggers lipotoxicity, mitochondrial dysfunction, and excessive generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), which in turn activate pro-inflammatory pathways, including nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB). The interplay among lipotoxicity, oxidative stress, and chronic low-grade inflammation establishes a self-perpetuating cycle that amplifies endocrine disruption and multi-organ damage. Within the kidney, these mechanisms contribute to cellular injury, fibrosis, and progressive decline in renal function, even in the absence of overt T2DM or hypertension (HTN). This review integrates current molecular and cellular evidence linking diet-induced metabolic disturbances to endocrine and renal dysfunction and discusses potential nutritional strategies targeting these pathophysiological pathways to mitigate disease progression.

articles.title: Pharmacological Prevention of Cardiac Surgery-Associated Acute Kidney Injury: Why Trials Failed and a Reimagined Endpoint Framework.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury affects approximately one in four adults and is independently associated with perioperative mortality and progression to chronic kidney disease. Despite more than two decades of randomized pharmacological trials, few have met their primary endpoint.

METHODS: This invited narrative review examined 33 pivotal randomized trials of pharmacological prevention published from 2004 to 2026, grouped by mechanism, and related population, intervention timing, and endpoint selection to trial outcome.
