RESULTS: Trials using short-term creatinine-based kidney injury endpoints produced the positive signals, whereas trials using major adverse kidney events at 90 days as the primary endpoint were negative. This divergence reflects both the low power of that composite for detecting injury prevention and unresolved biology, since no agent has shown benefit on both types of endpoint. Positive trials shared a matched mechanism, a defined population, and an aligned endpoint. Recurrent failure modes were endpoint misalignment, mismatch between population and the timing of injury, confounding by postoperative cardiac recovery, and direct drug effects on creatinine or urine output that mimic or mask injury.

CONCLUSIONS: We propose a trial framework with persistent stage 2 or 3 acute kidney disease at 30 days, by Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes criteria, as the primary endpoint; preoperative albuminuria as an enrichment criterion; and attenuation of the postoperative rise in albuminuria at 30 and 90 days as a key secondary endpoint. Platform designs with biomarker-enriched enrollment could convert the next generation of trials into interpretable tests of kidney protection.

articles.title: Quantitative Anterior-Segment Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography Parameters for Predicting the Response to Subconjunctival Bevacizumab in Corneal Neovascularization: A Single-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Corneal neovascularization (CoNV) compromises corneal transparency, promotes graft rejection and confounds outcome prediction after anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy. Subconjunctival bevacizumab is widely used, yet a substantial proportion of treated eyes fail to achieve clinically meaningful regression, and no validated pre-treatment biomarker has been established. We tested whether quantitative anterior-segment optical coherence tomography angiography (AS-OCTA) parameters obtained before treatment identify likely responders.

METHODS: In a single-centre retrospective cohort, consecutive patients receiving three monthly subconjunctival injections of bevacizumab (2.5 mg in 0.1 mL) between January 2022 and December 2024 were analysed. Baseline AS-OCTA scans yielded vessel density, vessel area, vessel length, vessel diameter and stromal invasion depth, graded independently by two masked observers. Response was defined a priori as a ≥30% reduction in vessel area at week 12. Multivariable logistic regression with 500-replicate bootstrap optimism correction, Hosmer-Lemeshow calibration and decision-curve analysis was performed. Sensitivity analyses addressed aetiology, concomitant corticosteroid use, scan signal strength and the binarization algorithm used to compute vessel density; response at month 6 was assessed in eyes with available imaging.

RESULTS: Of 142 enrolled eyes, 131 completed follow-up and 72 (55.0%) met the response criterion. Responders had higher baseline vessel density (29.55 ± 5.83% vs 25.11 ± 6.64%, P < 0.001) and a shorter disease duration that did not differ significantly in the univariate comparison (median 7.2 vs 8.9 months, P = 0.070). Vessel density (adjusted OR 1.13 per 1%, 95% CI 1.06-1.21) and duration (adjusted OR 0.92 per month, 95% CI 0.86-0.98) were independent predictors. The combined model achieved an apparent AUC of 0.744 (optimism-corrected 0.730), indicating moderate discrimination, with acceptable calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.70; Brier score 0.202, scaled Brier score 18.2%). The association of vessel density with response persisted after adjustment for aetiology, corticosteroid use and signal strength and with all four alternative binarization algorithms. Among 84 eyes with month-6 imaging, the week-12 classification agreed with the month-6 classification in 85.7% (κ = 0.71).

CONCLUSIONS: Baseline AS-OCTA vessel density combined with disease duration provides moderate discrimination of the response to subconjunctival bevacizumab in CoNV. At this level of performance, the model can support counselling and triage but not stand-alone treatment decisions. External validation in independent multicentre cohorts is required.

articles.title: Facial Lymphocutaneous Sporotrichosis Improved with ALA-PDT.
articles.abstract: Sporotrichosis is a subcutaneous fungal infection caused by Sporothrix species. Cutaneous disease usually presents as fixed cutaneous, lymphocutaneous, or disseminated forms. Facial involvement is uncommon and may mimic chronic inflammatory or granulomatous dermatoses. Oral itraconazole is standard therapy, but treatment may take months. This case report demonstrates that in a case of facial lymphocutaneous sporotrichosis with multiple lesions that responded slowly to oral itraconazole, the addition of adjunctive ALA-PDT (once weekly for 5 sessions) resulted in marked lesion regression, with no recurrence during 12 months of follow-up. Adjunctive ALA-PDT is a safe and effective option that can speed up clinical improvement and enhance cosmetic results in patients with facial lymphocutaneous sporotrichosis who respond poorly to standard itraconazole treatment.

articles.title: Computational Structural Dynamics and Preliminary Heterologous Expression Suggest a "Rigid-Anchor, Flexible-Melting" RNA Chaperone Mechanism for Rice OsCSP1.
articles.abstract: Cold and drought are major abiotic stresses that severely constrain rice (Oryza sativa) growth and productivity. Cold shock proteins (CSPs) act as RNA chaperones that facilitate post-transcriptional adaptation under environmental stress. In this study, we combined phylogenetic analysis, prokaryotic heterologous expression, and all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to elucidate the evolutionary features, stress-protective capacity, and working mechanism of rice OsCSP1. Promoter analysis revealed enrichment of low-temperature responsive (LTR) and MYB-binding drought-responsive (MBS) cis-elements upstream of OsCSP1. Heterologous overexpression of OsCSP1 in Escherichia coli showed no cytotoxicity at 37°C. Under 17°C cold stress, recombinant strains overcame initial metabolic burden and exhibited superior biomass accumulation (OD600) compared with empty vector controls during late log phase. Spot dilution assays indicated enhanced colony-forming ability at 10-3 dilution. Sector-plate assays further demonstrated strong induction-dependent cytoprotection against both prolonged cold (17°C) and 15% (w/v) PEG6000-induced osmotic stress in E. coli, highlighting its potential protective efficacy in heterologous systems. AlphaFold 3 modeling of the OsCSP1-U6 RNA complex yielded a moderate interface confidence (ipTM = 0.66), which is expected for proteins containing intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs). Subsequent 100-ns all-atom MD simulations revealed rapid contraction in radius of gyration (Rg) and solvent-accessible surface area (SASA), forming a compact, solvent-resistant conformation. RMSF analysis showed a rigid N-terminal CSD anchor coupled with a highly dynamic C-terminal IDR. MM/PBSA binding free energy decomposition indicated that the interaction is primarily driven by van der Waals and electrostatic forces. We propose a "rigid-anchor, flexible-melting" model in which the CSD is predicted to provide stable RNA binding while the flexible IDR is hypothesized to facilitate the destabilization of misfolded RNA secondary structures. These findings provide a foundational biophysical framework that facilitates future in planta functional validation of OsCSP1 as a potential target for engineering climate-resilient rice.

articles.title: Impacts of a low fat whole food plant-based diet on vitamin and mineral intake in advanced CKD populations, a secondary analysis of a randomized control trial.
articles.journal: Journal of renal nutrition : the official journal of the Council on Renal Nutrition of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low fat whole-food plant-based (LFWFPB) dietary patterns are increasingly recommended for patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) because of potential cardiometabolic benefits. However, the micronutrient effects of adopting a LFWFPB diet in patients with moderate to advanced CKD remain incompletely characterized.

METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of a randomized pilot trial involving adults with CKD stages 3 to 4 assigned to a 15-day LFWFPB nutrition education program or usual care. Three-day food records were completed at baseline and day 15 and analyzed using the Nutrition Data System for Research. Changes in vitamin, mineral, oxalate, and added sugar intake were compared within and between groups.

RESULTS: Forty participants were included (20 intervention, 20 control). Median intake of several plant-derived vitamins increased significantly in the intervention group compared with controls, including vitamin A (between-group difference in change 6759.2 IU, p = 0.0018), vitamin C (90.55 mg, p = 0.0008), vitamin K (135.38 mcg, p = 0.0155), and folate (72.62 mcg, p = 0.0411). Magnesium (96.92 mg, p = 0.0018), manganese (3.52 mg, p < 0.0001), and copper (0.52 mg, p = 0.0013) also increased, while added sugars decreased (-21.57 g, p < 0.0001). Several nutrients decreased in the intervention group compared with controls, including vitamin D (-3.05 mcg, p < 0.0001), vitamin E (-4.06 mg, p = 0.0385), riboflavin (-0.75 mg, p = 0.0223), niacin (-4.66 mg, p = 0.0144), and vitamin B12 (-2.67 mcg, p < 0.0001). Zinc (-2.78 mg, p = 0.0084), selenium (-37.44 mcg, p < 0.0001), calcium (-67.01 mg, p = 0.0275), and phosphorus (-72.40 mg, p = 0.0023) also decreased, while oxalate increased (183.60 mg, p = 0.0036). Thiamin, pantothenic acid, vitamin B6, and iron did not differ between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Adoption of a short-term LFWFPB dietary pattern in CKD stages 3-4 resulted in substantial shifts in micronutrient intake. While increases in plant-derived nutrients may support cardiometabolic health, reductions in vitamin B12, vitamin D, selenium, and zinc highlight the need for monitoring and possible supplementation. These findings emphasize the importance of structured nutritional guidance when recommending plant-predominant diets in CKD.

articles.title: Effect Of Normal Protein versus Low Protein Diet On Renal Function Reserve In Patients Of Chronic Kidney Disease Stage 3 And 4: A Randomised Controlled Study.
articles.journal: Journal of renal nutrition : the official journal of the Council on Renal Nutrition of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Renal functional reserve (RFR), defined as the difference between peak and baseline glomerular filtration rate (GFR), reflects the adaptive capacity of the kidney. This study evaluated how normal protein diet (NPD) and low protein diet (LPD) changes both relative (RFR%) and absolute (RFRabs) RFR and rate of GFR decline over six months in CKD stages 3 and 4.

METHODOLOGY: This six-month, single centre, parallel group randomized controlled trial enrolled adults (>18 years) with stage 3-4 CKD. Assessments at baseline and six months included clinical and laboratory parameters, eGFR, Creatinine clearance(CrCl) and two-plasma technetium-99m Diethylenetriaminepentaacetic acid (99mTc-DTPA) method before and after a 1 g/kg protein load to calculate RFRabs and RFR%. Patients were randomized to either a NPD (0.8 g/kg/day - the standard recommended intake for CKD stage 3 and 4 as per Indian dietary guidelines) or a LPD (0.6 g/kg/day- the guideline defined low protein prescription)). Dietary adherence monitored by recall, record and 24-hour urinary urea nitrogen every 3 months. All parameters were repeated at six months to compare RFR% (primary end point), RFRabs and eGFR changes.

RESULTS: Of 135 patients (64 NPD, 71 LPD), there was significant increase in measured GFR after protein loading in both groups at baseline and at six months (p < 0.001). The primary endpoint was met: six- month change in DTPA derived RFR% was significantly less negative in LPD (-1.34%, 95% CI -4.15 to +1.57) versus NPD (-5.06%, 95% CI -8.71 to -2.63; p = 0.0014). ANCOVA confirmed the group effect F(1,132)=21.73, p<0.001. eGFR change did not differ between groups (p>0.05). A modestly significant correlation was observed between ΔUACR and ΔRFR% (ρ = 0.17, p = 0.044).

CONCLUSION: In CKD, a low-protein diet was associated with better RFR preservation than a normal-protein diet despite limited eGFR changes; these hypothesis-generating findings warrant further investigation of RFR.

articles.title: Population Protein Targets in the 2025-2030 Dietary Guidelines and the Hidden Burden of Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.journal: Journal of renal nutrition : the official journal of the Council on Renal Nutrition of the National Kidney Foundation

articles.title: Impact of Suspensory Ligament Desmitis on Athletic Performance of Trotting Horses: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Suspensory ligament (SL) desmitis is one of the most common musculoskeletal injuries affecting trotting horses being frequently associated with reduced athletic performance and premature retirement. However, the prognostic value of clinical and ultrasonographic findings remains incompletely understood.

AIMS/OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of proximal and/or body SL desmitis on athletic performance of French Trotters and determine whether horse related characteristics, ultrasonographic lesion severity, lesion location, or treatment modality influence prognosis.

METHODS: Medical records of 36 French Trotters diagnosed with proximal and/or body SL desmitis were retrospectively reviewed. Horse related characteristics, ultrasonographic findings, treatment protocols, recurrence, inactivity period, return to competition, race earnings, and Index of Trot (ITR) were analysed. Statistics were applied with non-parametric testing.

RESULTS: Twenty-four horses (66.7%) returned to competition, whereas 12 (33.3%) retired. Four horses experienced recurrence after returning to competition. The median inactivity period was 193 days. Age, number of affected limbs, lesion location, treatment modality, and ultrasonographic parameters (cross-sectional area grade, longitudinal fibre pattern, and overall lesion severity) did not significantly influence outcome, recurrence, or inactivity period (all p > 0.05). Post-injury race earnings (p = 0.005) and ITR values (p = 0.004) were significantly lower than pre-injury values. Hindlimb lesions were associated with a longer inactivity period than forelimb lesions (p = 0.03).

CONCLUSIONS: SL desmitis significantly compromises athletic performance in French Trotters despite a relatively high return-to-competition rate. Common clinical and ultrasonographic variables showed limited prognostic value, highlighting the need for further studies to identify reliable predictors of outcome and recurrence.

articles.title: Scanner acoustic noise in resting-state fMRI.
articles.abstract: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) is usually acquired during rapid gradient switching that produces intense, spectrally structured sound. Scanner sound activates auditory pathways and can alter neural, vigilance, autonomic, respiratory, and movement-related states, but its sound-specific causal effect on intrinsic functional-connectivity estimates remains unresolved. Direct human comparisons are few and heterogeneous: some report stronger or more extensive network estimates under quieter acquisition, whereas others find broadly preserved topology and within-network connectivity. Near-silent Looping Star imaging can recover canonical resting-state networks with marked sound reduction, but reduced temporal signal-to-noise ratio and functional sensitivity expose a trade-off between acoustic burden and measurement performance. Most quiet-versus-standard contrasts simultaneously alter temporal sampling, gradient vibration, reconstruction, steady-state behavior, or image quality and therefore identify a total protocol effect rather than a sound-specific effect. A structured, original-scale comparison reports acoustic levels and metrics, measurement conditions, acquisition parameters, and resting-state outcomes without pooling unlike measures. Vigilance, autonomic activity, respiration, and movement are potential mediators; indiscriminate regression of these variables can remove part of the total acoustic effect. Current evidence establishes that acquisition protocols can alter rs-fMRI estimates and that scanner sound is biologically active, but it does not establish a universal, directionally uniform suppression of human resting-state connectivity by conventional echo-planar imaging. Future sound-specific attribution would require randomized within-subject manipulation, protected-ear frequency-resolved dosimetry, control of co-varying vibration and sequence properties, and synchronized state and physiological monitoring.

articles.title: Histone H3K18 lactylation drives microglial ferroptosis and exacerbates neuroinflammation in sepsis-associated encephalopathy.
articles.abstract: Elevated lactate levels are a significant biomarker of sepsis and are positively associated with sepsis-related mortality. Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is independently associated with increased mortality in clinical sepsis patients. However, the underlying mechanisms of lactate's involvement in SAE remain unclear. In this study, we demonstrate that H3K18 lactylation (H3K18la) levels are upregulated in LPS-stimulated BV2 microglial cells and the hippocampus of LPS-injected mice. Pharmacological inhibition of H3K18la by sodium oxamate (OXA) or 2-deoxy-D-glucose (2-DG) effectively attenuates neuroinflammation and reduces neuronal death. Furthermore, CUT& Tag and RNA-seq results revealed that SLC7A11 as a direct downstream target of H3K18la, thereby promoting microglia ferroptosis and amplifying neuroinflammation. Overexpressing SLC7A11 in BV2 cells or microglia-specific overexpression of SLC7A11 in Cx3cr1Cremice can effectively suppress neuroinflammation, attenuate neuronal damage and alleviate cognitive impairments in SAE. Taken together, our findings elucidate the role of histone lactylation in SAE, and provide novel insights into potential therapeutic strategies for SAE.

articles.title: Hnrnpk mediated CircNtrk3 downregulation promotes pulmonary vascular remodeling in pulmonary hypertension by driving Ca2+ signaling and metabolic reprogramming.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is characterized by significant pulmonary vascular remodeling, a process primarily driven by the excessive proliferation of pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cell (PASMC). This study investigates the functional role and mechanistic basis of the circular RNA circNtrk3 in PASMC proliferation. We found that circNtrk3 is reduced in PASMC from PH rats. CircNtrk3 knock down promoted proliferation and migration of PASMC, accompanied by enhanced Ca2+ influx and metabolic reprogramming. In contrast, AAV9-mediated overexpression of circNtrk3 significantly attenuated right ventricular pressure, pulmonary vascular remodeling, and right ventricular hypertrophy. Mechanistically, Hnrnpk binds circNtrk3 and regulates its stability. CircNtrk3, in turn, suppresses miR-17-5p expression and potentiates Ca2+ influx and metabolic reprogramming via the Bmpr2/Trpc4 signaling pathway. In summary, we identify the Hnrnpk/circNtrk3/miR-17-5p axis as a novel pathway that promotes PASMC proliferation by modulating Ca2+ homeostasis and metabolic processes.

articles.title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance findings in His-bundle pacing: Insights to pacing threshold rise.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The mechanisms underlying pacing threshold elevation in His bundle pacing (HBP) despite an electrically intact lead remain poorly understood. This can compromise long-term battery life and increase the need for generator replacement or lead revision, adding procedural risk for patients and costs for healthcare systems. Using multiparametric cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR), this proof-of-concept study examined whether the myocardium at the lead tip can be visualised with conventional CMR sequences, whether imaging remains safe despite elevated pacing thresholds, and whether fibrosis at the implantation site can be identified.

METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 16 patients with HBP systems, of whom 9 had an increased pacing threshold. A significant increase was defined as a rise of ≥1.0V/1.0 ms. All scans were performed on a 1.5T scanner using standard bSSFP cine imaging and IR TFE late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging in atrial-focused short-axis, long-axis, and modified aortic valve (AV) views to optimally visualise the HBP insertion site. LGE was assessed visually in different views.

RESULTS: All MRI images were evaluable and showed no visual artefacts. The tip of the HBP lead was best visible on short-axis and AV planes. No periprocedural safety issues occurred, in particular pacing thresholds remained unaffected, demonstrating that CMR is feasible even in patients with elevated pacing thresholds, a scenario often considered a relative contraindication. In the case-control comparison, the presence of LGE at the His lead implantation site was associated with increased pacing thresholds, although our small cohort showed no association with clinical markers. Given the limited sample size, these findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

CONCLUSIONS: This proof-of-concept study shows that the HBP lead implantation site can be visualized with conventional CMR sequences, and that MRI can be performed safely even in patients with elevated pacing thresholds. Pacing threshold rises were associated with LGE at the implant site, suggesting a mechanistic link and traction-related micro-injury. These findings highlight that local tissue remodeling should be considered when selecting and optimizing His-bundle implantation techniques.

articles.title: Animal-source foods in infancy contribute to higher dietary quality.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Few studies have characterized infant animal-source food introduction and intake longitudinally to determine whether these foods are associated with dietary quality or growth at 12-months of age.

OBJECTIVE: Describe patterns and determinants of animal-source food consumption during complementary feeding and evaluate associations between animal-source foods with dietary quality and growth.

METHODS: Mothers And careGivers Investing in Children (MAGIC) randomized trial is a complementary feeding intervention with responsive feeding coaching (MAGIC-FEED) compared to an attention control (MAGIC-SAFE), and an exploratory arm (MAGIC-FEED+FOOD) including food provision along with MAGIC-FEED. 135 mother-infant-caregiver triads in the Austin, Texas, United States enrolled at age 5-months, received virtual intervention visits at age 6, 7, 8 and 10 months, and had anthropometrics measured at 12-months. Diet was assessed repeatedly from 5-12-months with a 7-day food-frequency questionnaire and 24-hour diet recall from which infant dietary quality index (IDQI, range 0-1) was calculated. Descriptive statistics and covariate adjusted linear regression evaluated patterns of intake and associations between intervention arm or dietary components with dietary quality and growth.

RESULTS: Overall, animal-source food intake increased from age 6 through 12 months. At age 12-months, more infants consumed egg (72%), poultry (77%) and beef (68%) and less consumed fish (30%) and pork (25%) in the prior 7-days. MAGIC-FEED was not associated with IDQI and had limited effects on animal source food consumption. In covariate-adjusted models, poultry (β=0.12, 95%CI 0.04,0.19) egg (β=0.06, 95%CI 0.01,0.12) and beef (β=0.07, 95%CI 0.01,0.13) predicted higher IDQI across infancy, compared to non-consumers. at 12-months of age. Poultry consumers predicted higher IDQI (β=0.14, 95%CI: 0.05,0.23), and pork consumers had higher length-for-age Z-scores (β=0.48, 95%CI: 0.03,0.92) at age 12-months.

CONCLUSIONS: MAGIC-FEED was not associated with animal source food intake. Poultry, beef, and eggs as complementary foods were associated with higher dietary quality, and pork was associated with linear growth. Clinical Trial Registry number and website where it was obtained NCT04177472; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04177472.

articles.title: [Place of clinical breast examination in breast cancer screening strategies. French College of Gynecologists and Obstetricians (CNGOF) recommendations for clinical practice].
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: France, like many countries around the world, is facing a rise in the incidence of breast cancer. Numerous studies have shown that the risk of death is linked to the initial stage of the tumor. In this context, mammographic screening for breast cancer aims to diagnose cancers at a subclinical stage, to limit treatment-related morbidity and reduce mortality. In France, this screening is recommended every two years for women aged 50 to 74, while clinical breast examination (CBE) by a healthcare professional is recommended by the Haute Autorité de Santé (HAS) starting at age 25, to be performed annually with no upper age limit. However, the practice of CBE needs to be updated, particularly regarding its impact on the number of cancers diagnosed, their stage, and mortality, considering new data from international literature.

DESIGN: The GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) method was used to assess the quality of the evidence on which these recommendations were based.

METHODS: The Senology Commission (SC) of the French College of Gynecologists and Obstetricians examined 16 questions regarding CBE, distinguishing four groups of women (the general population with or without mammography screening, women over 70 years of age, high or very-risk women, and women previously treated for breast cancer). For each scenario, it was determined whether performing a CBE, compared with not performing it, led to the detection of more breast cancers, reduced tumor size, or improved survival. One question addressed the training requirements for CBE.

RESULTS: The SC issued three recommendations aimed at: 1) recommending annual CBE for women in the general population aged 30 to 74, 2) recommending annual CBE for women who have previously been treated for breast cancer, 3) recommending that CBE be performed by a trained healthcare professional. The SC issued four position statements aimed at: 1) not advising CBE for women in the general population under the age of 30, as the procedure carries a risk of unnecessary follow-up tests in a group of women where the incidence of breast cancer is very low. 2) advising performing a CBE during breast cancer screening; 3) advising an annual CBE for women over 75 years of age, with the discontinuation of this practice depending on comorbidities and life expectancy. 4) advising annual CBE for women at high and very high-risk starting at age 20. According to the experts of the CNGOF's Scientific Committee, a CBE should be performed only after obtaining explicit consent following the provision of information on its benefits and risks. The SC urges all women who notice a change or abnormality in their breasts to consult their doctor without delay to undergo a clinical breast exam.

articles.title: Systematic overestimation using in silico-driven curation in a population database caused reevaluation of the genetic prevalence of Alport Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: A landmark study by Gibson and coworkers in 2021 estimated that one in 106 individuals carry a predicted pathogenic COL4A3 or COL4A4 variant, suggesting autosomal dominant Alport syndrome is massively underdiagnosed. However, pathogenicity of all triple-helical Glycine substitutions was inferred using in silico tools, which may overestimate prevalence.

METHODS: COL4A3, COL4A4, and COL4A5 variants were extracted from population database gnomADv4.1.1 (about 800,000 individuals, including UK Biobank) and from a clinical exome cohort of 29,055 patients (Eurofins Biomnis), stratified into a kidney disease group (KIDNEY) of 8663 individuals and 20,392 individuals of a non-kidney control group (NON-KIDNEY). Three curation strategies were compared: a ClinVar-dependent model, an in silico-driven model adapted from Gibson, and an Expert Strategy combining stringent allele frequency thresholds, high-confidence loss-of-function filtering, and with ClinVar validation for missense variants. Estimates were validated against the control group and replicated in the non-UKB Biobank subset.

RESULTS: Applied to gnomADv4.1.1, the Gibson methodology yielded one in 221, a 52% reduction from the original one in 106 (gnomADv2). The Expert Strategy estimated one in 283, validated in the NON-KIDNEY group (one in 295; concordance ratio 0.96), whereas Gibson inflated the control rate by 91% (one in 154 vs. one in 295). Glycine substitutions (COL4A3 p.Gly1277Ser odds ratio 0.95; COL4A4 p.Gly999Glu odds ratio 1.01) were misclassified by all in silico tools. Expert Strategy variants were found in one in 44 KIDNEY patients (odds ratio 6.76). Enrichment was unchanged by high-confidence loss-of-function restriction.

CONCLUSIONS: Autosomal dominant Alport syndrome affects one in 283 individuals, one to two orders of magnitude above classical clinical estimates (one in 5,000 to one in 53,000), confirming underdiagnosis, but substantially lower than the Gibson estimate. These findings argue for downgrading the PM2 rarity criterion in collagenopathies. Systematic COL4A3/COL4A4 screening in chronic kidney disease is justified by a diagnostic yield of one in 44.

articles.title: Longitudinal boundary-anchored CT profiling of the frontal horns after cerebrospinal fluid shunting in idiopathic intracranial hypertension: a pilot study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Routine CT after cerebrospinal fluid shunting in idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) is usually assessed for catheter position and overt complications. We investigated whether boundary-anchored line profiling can detect subtler postoperative changes at the frontal horns.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 18 patients with IIH and 3 cranial CT examinations: baseline (T0), postoperative (T1), and follow-up (T2). Primary markers were local plateau dip depth, dip area, and biphasic index. Wilcoxon tests were adjusted for multiple comparisons. Additional analyses assessed clinical records, ventricular dimensions, baseline timing, scanner groups, and 2-mm sampling. Intra- and inter-rater reproducibility was assessed across all 54 examinations.

RESULTS: Local plateau dip depth decreased from T0 to T1 and remained lower at T2; dip area and biphasic index decreased from T0 to T1 (all four q = 0.025). All three T0-to-T1 changes remained significant in the 2-mm sampling sensitivity analysis (q = 0.007-0.039). Conventional attenuation summaries and ventricular dimensions showed no significant longitudinal changes. Intra-/inter-rater intraclass correlation coefficients were 0.75/0.61 for dip depth, 0.73/0.49 for dip area, and 0.82/0.80 for biphasic index. Exploratory clinical associations did not survive multiplicity correction. No comparison survived correction when coarse-grid subsampling preceded smoothing.

CONCLUSION: Boundary-anchored CT profiling identified postoperative frontal horn profile-shape changes supported by multiplicity-adjusted and sampling sensitivity analyses. Reproducibility was marker dependent, with repeatability limits exceeding mean early changes. These findings support further evaluation of the method as a quantitative research tool, with standardization and external validation required before clinical use.

articles.title: Early prediction of in-hospital incident hydrocephalus after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage in patients without hydrocephalus on admission CT: model development and internal validation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize patients with in-hospital incident hydrocephalus after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) and develop and internally validate an admission model for early risk stratification.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included patients with aSAH admitted from January 2017 to March 2026. Patients had no hydrocephalus on admission computed tomography and remained free of it through completion of the initial admission assessment. Predictors were restricted to information available by that assessment. Univariable screening preceded logistic regression and one-step model reduction. Internal validation repeated the complete model-development procedure in 1,000 bootstrap resamples.

RESULTS: Among 347 patients, 70 (20%) developed in-hospital incident hydrocephalus. Affected patients were older (mean age, 63 vs 58 years), had lower admission Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) scores (mean, 10 vs 14), and more often had original Fisher grade 4 (61% vs 22%) than patients without hydrocephalus. Diagnosis occurred a median of 1 calendar day after admission (interquartile range, 0-5). Among affected patients, 68 (97%) had a recorded cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-related intervention, including lumbar CSF drainage in 64. The model retained age, admission GCS score, and original Fisher grade. Apparent and optimism-corrected C-statistics were 0.805 (95% confidence interval, 0.742-0.868) and 0.789; the corrected calibration slope was 0.917. Sensitivity analyses showed lower apparent discrimination under the broader outcome definition and suggested temporal calibration changes despite similar C-statistic point estimates.

CONCLUSIONS: This admission model may support early risk stratification, but clinical utility remains unproven. External validation and prospective assessment of clinical impact are required before routine use.

articles.title: Ketone bodies and heart failure: A dual paradox from metabolic adaptation to therapeutic target.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is fundamentally a syndrome of disturbed energy metabolism. Although accumulating evidence indicates that the failing heart increases ketone utilization, whether this metabolic shift is adaptive or maladaptive remains debated, complicated by striking differences between HFrEF and HFpEF. Moreover, the cardiovascular benefits of SGLT2i are thought to be partially attributable to elevated circulating ketone levels, yet this same mechanism links to increased risk of ketoacidosis. This review dissects the dual role of ketone bodies in HF: as an alternative oxidative substrate under stress and a marker of disease severity, while mediating SGLT2i cardioprotection but posing safety risks. We focus on heterogeneity across HF subtypes and therapeutic strategies targeting ketone metabolism, including exogenous ketone supplementation, aiming to provide new perspectives for precision medicine.

articles.title: Pannexin-1 (PANX1) in Metabolic Diseases: Structural Basis, Molecular Mechanisms, and Pharmacological Significance.
articles.abstract: Metabolic diseases, including obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), atherosclerosis (AS), and diabetes-related complications, are characterized by disrupted glucose and lipid metabolism, chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, and progressive tissue dysfunction. Pannexin-1 (PANX1), a large-pore membrane channel that mediates regulated ATP release, has emerged as an important interface between metabolic stress and extracellular purinergic signaling. PANX1 influences metabolic homeostasis through ATP-dependent and broader signaling mechanisms that regulate insulin action and secretion, hepatic glucose and lipid metabolism, autophagy, vascular function, inflammatory responses, and regulated cell death. Its effects are highly context dependent. PANX1 can support metabolic homeostasis in adipocytes, pancreatic β cells, hepatocytes, and selected vascular cell populations, whereas sustained or dysregulated PANX1 signaling may promote inflammation, vascular dysfunction, ferroptosis, and pyroptosis under metabolic stress. These divergent actions are shaped by cellular origin, disease stage, and the local metabolic environment. This review summarizes current understanding of PANX1 structure, channel gating, and regulatory mechanisms and integrates predominantly preclinical evidence for its involvement in metabolic homeostasis and related diseases. We further examine the interactions of PANX1 with purinergic signaling, inflammation, oxidative stress, organelle homeostasis, and regulated cell death, together with current pharmacological strategies targeting PANX1. Although most available PANX1 modulators remain primarily mechanistic tools and lack direct evidence of therapeutic efficacy in metabolic disease models, these findings provide a foundation for the future development and evaluation of more selective PANX1-targeted interventions.

articles.title: Chloroplast genome engineering: Recent advances, pathways towards commercialization and future directions.
articles.abstract: Chloroplasts are ideal biofactories because thousands of transgene copies integrated into each plant cell to produce high levels of recombinant proteins and enzymes. Because chloroplast genomes are predominantly maternally inherited, transgenes are generally not transmitted via pollen. Nuclear genome engineering ushered in the GMO revolution for crop protection that mostly required lower levels of transgene expression. Higher level expression and biosafety through gene containment facilitate new applications of GM crops, including production of high-value biopharmaceuticals and enzymes. This review focuses on recent advances in this field, including the first FDA approval of biopharmaceuticals made in plant cells for evaluation in human clinical trials, topical or oral drug delivery, marker free edible plants by removal of antibiotic resistance genes and novel post-translational modifications required to produce functional human proteins. In addition, new tools are discussed to improve DNA delivery, vector free assembly, episomal or integration methods, enhancement of transgene expression through optimization of regulatory sequences, codons, targeted genome editing and other innovations in biomanufacturing. Topical drug delivery using plant cells incorporated into chewing gums to control oral viruses, pathogenic bacteria, or yeast and oral drug delivery with therapeutic proteins made in plant cells to treat diabetes, obesity and cardiopulmonary diseases currently advanced to human clinical trials are discussed. In addition, high-value industrial enzymes for launching new products or to confer valuable agronomic traits or enhance photosynthesis are discussed. Future perspectives section provides examples of biotechnology products anticipated to be launched in the next 3-5 years, with opportunities and anticipated challenges.

articles.title: Transthoracic Echocardiographic Reference Values in Male Professional Major League Soccer Players Under 21 Years of Age.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To define sport-specific echocardiographic reference values in elite male soccer players <21 years of age.

BACKGROUND: Exercise-induced cardiac remodeling varies by sport and demographic factors. The use of general population reference values may lead to misclassification of physiological remodeling as pathology, particularly in young athletes. Normative echocardiographic data in elite adolescent soccer players remain limited.

METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional echocardiographic analysis of 430 male Major League Soccer athletes on active rosters from 2018 to 2023. Standard echocardiographic parameters were assessed and compared with American Society of Echocardiography reference values.

RESULTS: Athlete age ranged from 14 to 21 years (mean 18.8 years). The cohort was racially and ethnically diverse (28.6% Black, 33.0% Hispanic, 37.0% White). 29% of athletes had dilated left ventricular end-diastolic volume (> 74mL/m2), while right ventricular enlargement (>41 mm) was observed in 27.2%. Maximal left ventricular wall thickness ranged from 5.5 to 12.9 mm (mean 9.79 mm), with 43.0% of athletes demonstrating wall thickness >10 mm. Mean left ventricular mass index was 92.8 g/m2, with 9.7% meeting criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy. Eccentric hypertrophy was present in 5.8%, concentric hypertrophy in 3.9%, and concentric remodeling in 18.8%, while 71.5% demonstrated normal geometry.

CONCLUSION: In this large, racially diverse cohort of elite male soccer players under 21 years of age, we provide comprehensive sport-specific echocardiographic reference values that address critical gaps in adolescent and young adult male soccer players.
