articles.title: Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Before Minimally Invasive Repair of Pectus Excavatum and After Bar Removal.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although minimally invasive repair of pectus excavatum (MIRPE) is associated with favorable outcomes, it remains generally unknown whether cardiac compression persists after bar removal. We therefore explored cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) outcomes after bar removal.

METHODS: We evaluated a retrospective cohort of patients with diagnosis of isolated pectus excavatum (PEX) who underwent CMR before MIRPE and after bar removal. We evaluated the effect of MIRPE on CMR outcomes including the presence of cardiac compression, pericardial effusion, abnormal septal motion, inspiratory septal flattening, and left ventricular eccentricity.

RESULTS: We included 60 patients who underwent CMR before repair and after bar removal. Before surgery, the mean Haller index was 5.9±3.0. All patients had baseline cardiac compression and 24 (40%) patients referred exercise intolerance. After bar removal, none of the patients reported exercise intolerance and we identified a significant decrease in the presence of cardiac compression [from 100% to 33%, mean difference -66.7 (95%CI -78.6; -54.7)]. With regard to RV inflow and septal wall kinetics, we identified a significant increase in the tricuspid to mitral annulus ratio [0.86±0.16 vs. 0.92±0.06, mean difference 0.06 (95%CI 0.02; 0.10)], and significantly reduced rates of abnormal septal motion [60.0%, vs 33.3%, mean difference -26.7 (95%CI -43.2; -10.1)], and a change in the rates of inspiratory septal flattening from 22% to 10% (mean difference -11.9 (95%CI -22.5; -1.3). Furthermore, we found a significant reduction in left ventricular eccentricity indexes after bar removal, particularly during inspiration [before MIRPE 1.61±0.2 vs. after removal 1.45±0.1, mean difference -0.16 (95%CI -0.23; -0.09)]. Finally, we also found a significant decline in the rates of pericardial effusion [25% vs. 5%, mean difference -20.0 (95%CI -30.1; -9.9)].

CONCLUSIONS: CMR assessment before MIRPE and after bar removal demonstrated persistent anatomical decompression, with a significant decrease in the presence and severity of cardiac compression, enhanced right ventricular inflow geometry, and favorable changes of septal wall kinetics. These structural modifications reflect mechanical relief of the right ventricle following bar removal.

TYPE OF STUDY: Retrospective before and after study LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III.

articles.title: Associations between Antidiabetic Drug Classes and Aortic Aneurysm Risk in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
articles.journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Aortic aneurysm (AA) is a potentially life threatening condition that often remains asymptomatic for prolonged periods. Although type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) increases cardiovascular risk, epidemiological studies have paradoxically reported a lower incidence of AA in patients with T2DM. Antidiabetic therapies may contribute to this inverse association, but class specific effects remain unclear. This study evaluated associations between antidiabetic drug classes and incident AA.

METHODS: This was a nationwide, population based, retrospective cohort study of adults with T2DM in Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database between 2009 and 2022. Associations between antidiabetic drug classes and incident AA were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models with time varying medication exposure, adjusted for demographic characteristics, diabetes severity, comorbidities, tobacco related diagnoses, and concomitant medications. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were considered exploratory.

RESULTS: Among 3 295 564 adults with T2DM (mean age 60.0 years; 52.8% men) followed for 8.5 ± 4.7 years, 45.5% received at least three antidiabetic drug classes. In multivariable time varying Cox models, metformin (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.78, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.75 - 0.82), thiazolidinediones (aHR 0.71, 95% CI 0.65 - 0.77), sulfonylureas/meglitinides (aHR 0.82, 95% CI 0.78 - 0.85), and α-glucosidase inhibitors (aHR 0.83, 95% CI 0.77 - 0.89) were associated with lower AA risk. DPP-4 inhibitors (aHR 0.95, 95% CI 0.90 - 1.00), sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors (aHR 0.90, 95% CI 0.81 - 1.00), and glucagon like peptide 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) (aHR 0.69, 95% CI 0.50 - 0.95) also showed inverse associations, whereas insulin use was associated with higher AA risk (aHR 1.14, 95% CI 1.08 - 1.20). The inverse associations of conventional oral antidiabetic agents remained robust across sensitivity analyses. In contrast, the inverse associations for DPP-4 inhibitors, SGLT2 inhibitors, and GLP-1RAs were attenuated and no longer statistically significant in patients with an index date from 2011 onward.

CONCLUSION: In this nationwide T2DM cohort, conventional oral antidiabetic agents were consistently associated with a lower observed AA risk. Although newer glucose lowering therapies showed similar inverse associations, these findings were less robust and warrant cautious interpretation and prospective confirmation.

articles.title: From protocol geometry to catalytic feedback: Active subspaces, coherent comparison data, and controlled reductions.
articles.abstract: Catalytic memory can arise when a reduced description discards active-state occupations, environmental excursions, selection records, or information about how a physical operation was implemented. We develop a theoretical framework connecting these mechanisms without identifying them. Moving-projector geometry determines state-resolved leakage; an explicit bath and occupation closure are needed to obtain a scalar survival rate. Quantum instruments separate conditional state changes from their occurrence probabilities. The central construction retains surface-comparison phases in a coherent auxiliary system and derives two routes to feedback: a state-dependent Hamiltonian from interacting units, and an occupancy-dependent loss law from protective encounters. A finite-population linear Lindblad embedding and a quantitative macroscopic limit yield ṡ=α(1-s)-Λse-Ks, with K fixed by encounter strength, phase and coherence visibility. Exact calculations test the construction across dephasing, interaction statistics and population size, and connect engagement to catalytic product counts. Bistability occurs in a restricted coherent regime and disappears for a matched geometric encounter distribution; finite populations retain a unique stationary law. Gauge, subdivision, probability, correlation and classical-control checks specify what the higher description adds. The construction preserves associative microscopic dynamics and establishes a conditional route from retained higher comparison data to effective feedback. It does not establish an intrinsic higher connection in a molecule. Biological mappings, microscopic inputs, identifiability conditions and falsifying protocols make that remaining hypothesis experimentally precise.

articles.title: Proteomic and functional analyses identify an ISG15-TLR3-NF-κB signaling axis associated with the antibacterial response to Streptococcus agalactiae infection in Nile tilapia.
articles.abstract: Streptococcus agalactiae (GBS) is the leading cause of streptococcosis in Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus). Interferon-stimulated gene 15 (ISG15) is widely recognized as an antiviral effector, but its role and molecular targets in bacterial infections are still unknown. Here, we employed 4D-DIA proteomics to profile spleen and head kidney responses in GIFT tilapia 24 h post-GBS infection, identifying 8280 and 8491 proteins, among which 383 and 461 were differentially expressed (DEPs), respectively. These DEPs revealed tissue-specific immune programs: inflammatory and coagulation pathways in the spleen versus energy metabolic reprogramming in the head kidney. Parallel reaction monitoring (PRM) validated 28 DEPs and pinpointed ISG15 as a pivotal regulator. GST pull-down coupled with mass spectrometry identified 927 ISG15-interacting proteins. Co-immunoprecipitation and dual-luciferase assays confirmed that ISG15 associates with TLR3 via its two ubiquitin-like domains, which bind to the LRR and TIR domains of TLR3, recruiting TRIF and MyD88 to dose-dependently activate NF-κB and induce seven pro-inflammatory cytokines plus IL-10. This study identifies an ISG15-TLR3-NF-κB signaling axis associated with the antibacterial response in teleosts, based on cell-based and in vitro evidence, adding a mechanism fundamentally distinct from mammalian TLR2/8/4 pathways. These findings expand ISG15 function beyond antiviral immunity. As the interaction was characterized in vitro and in overexpression systems, whether the contact is direct or mediated by bridging proteins, whether endogenous complexes form during infection, and whether the axis enhances bacterial clearance or survival in vivo remain to be established.

articles.title: Annexin A2 deficiency alleviates Mycoplasma ovipneumoniae induced lung inflammation damage by regulating ROS production.
articles.abstract: Mycoplasma ovipneumoniae (MO) frequently induces severe oxidative damage to sheep lung tissue. Annexin A2 (ANXA2) protein has been reported to serve as a receptor for multiple Mycoplasma species. The present study aims to investigate whether ANXA2 can bind to MO and to elucidate its specific regulatory role in mediating MO infection and pathogenicity. Co-immunoprecipitation (CO-IP) and GST pulldown were used to verify the interaction between ANXA2 and the adhesion-like glycoprotein LppT of MO. ANXA2 expression was knocked down to detect its effect on mycoplasma adhesion to cells. The effects of ANXA2 inhibition on cellular autophagy, reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, apoptosis levels, and cell proliferation were evaluated. Additionally, ANXA2 gene-edited mice were used to assess the inflammatory response to MO challenge. Finally, the novel EOCas12i gene-editing system was applied to generate ANXA2-gene-edited sheep. CO-IP and GST pulldown confirmed that the adhesion-like glycoprotein LppT of MO interacts with ANXA2. Knocking down ANXA2 expression did not significantly reduce mycoplasma adhesion to cells. Inhibition of ANXA2 restored cellular autophagy, decreased ROS production and apoptosis levels, and promoted the recovery of cell proliferation. ANXA2+/- mice exhibited suppressed inflammatory responses to mycoplasma challenge; however, ANXA2-/- mice did not show reduced MO induced inflammation, which was likely due to the inhibition of M1 polarization of macrophages by ANXA2 knockout, thereby impairing mycoplasma clearance. A balance between cell survival and immune defense is required to enhance host resistance against MO. Based on the findings of this study, ANXA2-gene-edited sheep were generated using the novel EOCas12i gene-editing system, which provides a new target for disease-resistant breeding in sheep.

articles.title: An in situ gene-activated chitosan hydrogel for infection control and angiogenesis in infected diabetic wounds.
articles.abstract: Chitosan hydrogels are attractive biological macromolecule matrices for chronic wound repair, but blank networks often provide limited antibacterial and pro-angiogenic activity. Here, we developed a gene-activated chitosan hydrogel (CAAV-gel) by co-loading an antimicrobial peptide/silver nanoparticle nanocomplex (AMP/AgNPs) and a replication-defective adenovirus encoding vascular endothelial growth factor (Ad-VEGF). The cationic AMP coating improved AgNP dispersion, supporting potent antibacterial activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), S. aureus, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The engineered hydrogel exhibited favorable physicochemical properties and cytocompatibility. In vitro, the Ad-VEGF module successfully transduced endothelial cells, significantly enhancing VEGF expression, migration, and tube formation. In an MRSA-infected diabetic mouse wound model, CAAV-gel effectively reduced bacterial burden and accelerated wound closure to 98.9% by day 14. Furthermore, it promoted epithelial repair, collagen deposition, and angiogenesis. These results highlight the potential of chitosan-based hydrogels to integrate antibacterial interface engineering with localized gene activation for infected diabetic wound repair.

articles.title: Hepatitis B virus X protein facilitates hepatitis B core antigen uptake and presentation to enhance core antigen-specific CD4 T-cell immunity against HBV-associated tumor.
articles.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is characterized by weak and dysfunctional virus-specific immunity, limiting the effectiveness of current antiviral therapies. Therapeutic vaccines incorporating multiple HBV antigens may broaden immune responses, but whether physical associations between viral antigens influence vaccine immunogenicity remains unclear. Here, we show that recombinant HBV X protein (rHBx), despite inducing no detectable HBx-specific antibody or T-cell responses under the tested conditions, acts as an immunomodulatory partner for HBc149 virus-like particles (rHBc149). Biochemical and biophysical analyses demonstrated a reproducible association between rHBx and rHBc149, resulting in higher-order antigen complexes. Formation and physical co-delivery of this complex enhanced rHBc149 uptake by antigen-presenting cells, increased its trafficking to draining lymph nodes, and promoted dendritic cell activation. Immunization with the rHBx+rHBc149 complex increased HBc-specific antibody and CD4+ T-cell responses and produced a balanced Th1/Th2 immune profile. Importantly, administration of the preformed complex, but not delivery of the two antigens at separate sites, enhanced tumor control in an HBV antigen-associated tumor model. This antitumor effect required both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells and MHC class II-restricted antigen presentation. These findings identify antigen-antigen association as a mechanism by which a non-immunogenic viral protein can enhance the uptake, presentation, and immunogenicity of a second antigen, supporting HBx as a modular partner for HBc-based therapeutic vaccine development.

articles.title: Epigenetic regulation of macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) by DNA methylation during Vibrio anguillarum infection in Ruditapes philippinarum.
articles.abstract: To investigate the effects of Vibrio anguillarum infection on the expression of macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) and DNA methylation of its promoter in the Manila clam Ruditapes philippinarum, we analyzed MIF sequence homology and phylogenetic relationships, temporal expression patterns after V. anguillarum infection, and promoter DNA methylation profiles, and used a dual-luciferase reporter assay to validate the regulatory effect of methylation on promoter activity. The results showed that the conserved domain of R. philippinarum MIF exhibited the highest homology with those of Meretrix meretrix and Mercenaria mercenaria. qRT-PCR analysis showed that MIF expression was significantly upregulated 12 h after V. anguillarum infection, peaked at 48 h (approximately 5.64-fold higher than the level at 0 h), and then returned to basal levels. Bisulfite sequencing PCR (BSP) analysis showed that MIF promoter methylation levels decreased significantly at 24 h and 48 h after infection, with the most pronounced demethylation observed at CpG 3, CpG 9, and CpG 11. Promoter methylation levels were significantly negatively correlated with MIF expression (R = -0.7552, P = 0.0062). The dual-luciferase reporter assay showed that in vitro methylation treatment significantly decreased MIF promoter activity. These results suggest that V. anguillarum infection may upregulate MIF expression by inducing promoter demethylation, thereby contributing to the host immune response. This study provides a reference for understanding the immune regulatory mechanisms underlying the resistance of R. philippinarum to V. anguillarum infection from an epigenetic perspective.

articles.title: Rapid performance validation testing of an intraoperatively customizable antibiotic-eluting resorbable bone graft implant targeting prosthetic joint infection.
articles.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infections (PJIs) present a major clinical challenge, for which prolonged, localized antibiotic delivery to eradicate infection are routinely pursued to facilitate bone regeneration while minimizing systemic toxicity. Current treatments, such as antibiotic-loaded polymethylmethacrylate bone cements, are non-resorbable and provide inconsistent antibiotic release. This study evaluates release of antibiotics from a novel, FDA-cleared, biphasic, synthetic, resorbable bone graft device composed of calcium carbonate and hydroxyapatite bound with polycaprolactone and polylactic-co-glycolic acid. This bone graft device can be intraoperatively mixed with patient-specific antibiotics (e.g., tobramycin and/or vancomycin) to form drug-loaded granules for implantation into bone voids. Drugs release completely from this formulation in 6-8 weeks. To rapidly screen and assess drug release consistency from these commercial formulations, a United States Pharmacopeia (USP) compendial dissolution method was employed, showing ∼ 100% tobramycin release within 145 min from this drug-loaded device. We then compared this rapid release to previously published actual 8-week release data and predictions from Weibull and Siepmann models fit to the published 8-week data. Results validate the utility of the rapid USP compendial dissolution method as a valuable, accelerated surrogate predictor for the previously published device-controlled antimicrobial release in vivo of over 6 weeks. These findings produce a practical quality control assay for two FDA-cleared implant platforms, one currently in clinical trials for targeted treatment of PJIs and other orthopedic infections where infection control and bone healing must be simultaneously addressed locally. This approach facilitates performance verification of an intraoperatively customizable, antibiotic-eluting, resorbable bone graft device with controlled, localized delivery of therapeutically relevant antibiotics that also supports new bone formation.

articles.title: Long-term safety and efficacy of arrhythmia monitoring with an implantable cardiac monitor.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Implantable cardiac monitors (ICMs) provide long-term monitoring for cardiac arrhythmias. This analysis summarizes late diagnoses, patient management and complications until 5 years after implantation.

METHODS: The BIO|STREAM-ICM study is an ongoing, prospective registry capturing the real-world application of ICMs at 38 sites across 9 countries. Patients with any ICM indication are followed until device information is no longer clinically utilized. All arrhythmia diagnoses were assessed for relevance to the device indication.

RESULTS: Of 1249 patients included in the present analysis, most received an ICM after syncope (56%) or cryptogenic stroke (30%). Follow-up extended to 5 years, 34% of patients had at least 3 years of monitoring. Kaplan-Meier estimates of the cumulative incidence of indication-related diagnosis were 31%, 36%, and 39% for syncope, and 21%, 24%, and 28% for cryptogenic stroke at 2, 3, and 4 years, respectively. After diagnosis, ICMs were explanted in 46% of cases, continued for monitoring of therapy efficacy in 41%, and inactivated but left in situ in 12%. Explantations needed a median duration of 10 min and were characterized as easy or very easy in 86% of cases. Six device related adverse events occurred later than 180 days after insertion, and none in the context of explantations.

CONCLUSION: ICMs continue to deliver clinically meaningful arrhythmia diagnoses in the third and fourth year post-implantation, even when the preceding follow-up has been uneventful. Long-term follow-up and explantation have a low risk. Our results affirm the safety and efficacy over the device's lifetime in clinical practice.

articles.title: Modifiable cardiovascular health, inflammatory biomarkers, and risk of cardiovascular disease and mortality among Cancer survivors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer survivors are at increased risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and mortality, but the roles of modifiable cardiovascular health (CVH) and systemic inflammation remain incompletely understood. We examined the associations of CVH with incident CVD and mortality and assessed potential mediation by inflammatory biomarkers.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 11,825 cancer survivors free of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) at baseline. CVH was assessed using the Life's Essential 8 (LE8) score and the number of LE8 components meeting guideline-based thresholds. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for cardiovascular events and mortality. Mediation analyses evaluated the contributions of inflammatory biomarkers.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 13.5 years, 1923 MACE events and 2082 deaths occurred. Compared with the lowest CVH tertile, the highest tertile was associated with lower risks of MACE (HR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.54-0.68), coronary heart disease (0.56; 0.48-0.65), heart failure (0.65; 0.52-0.81), stroke (0.60; 0.45-0.80), all-cause mortality (0.72; 0.64-0.80), CVD mortality (0.48; 0.32-0.72), and cancer mortality (0.74; 0.66-0.85). Each additional LE8 component under control was associated with 7%-20% lower risks across outcomes. Among significant mediation effects, C-reactive protein and the INFLA score mediated 9.7%-48.7% and 6.8%-17.9% of the associations, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Favorable modifiable CVH is consistently associated with substantially lower risks of cardiovascular events and mortality among cancer survivors. Inflammation biomarkers partially mediated these associations, implicating inflammation as a key biological pathway.

articles.title: Association of preoperative quantitative flow ratio with 1-year graft patency after coronary artery bypass grafting: A two-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) targets are selected by angiographic stenosis, whereas percutaneous coronary intervention increasingly relies on functional assessment. Whether quantitative flow ratio (QFR), a wire-free angiography-derived index, relates to graft outcomes is unclear. We examined preoperative QFR and 1-year graft patency.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied 491 patients undergoing isolated CABG at two heart centers, 2006-2019. Investigators blinded to bypass design and outcome measured preoperative QFR in all analyzable major vessels. Protocol angiography assessed 1-year graft status. Generalized estimating equations accounting for within-patient clustering related QFR (per 0.1-unit increment) to graft occlusion, unadjusted and adjusted for target vessel, graft type, age, sex, diabetes, and ejection fraction. Linearity and effect modification by graft type and target territory were assessed.

RESULTS: Median QFR among 1161 analyzable vessels was 0.66 (interquartile range, 0.48-0.80); among 1036 bypassed vessels, higher QFR was associated with greater 1-year graft occlusion risk (unadjusted odds ratio [OR], 1.27; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.15-1.42; adjusted OR, 1.15; 95% CI, 1.04-1.27; p = 0.008). The association was linear (standardized occlusion probability, 8.2% at QFR 0.50; 13.1% at 0.90). Effect modification by target territory was borderline (joint interaction p = 0.025; Holm-adjusted p = 0.050); this exploratory finding requires confirmation. Graft type did not modify the association (p = 0.28).

CONCLUSIONS: Higher preoperative QFR, indicating functionally less significant stenosis, was associated with greater 1-year graft occlusion risk. This hypothesis-generating, group-level association establishes neither causation nor predictive utility for individual grafts. Prospective validation is needed.

articles.title: Time-Dependent Changes in Auditory Fear Generalization and Its Suppression by Extinction in Mice.
articles.abstract: Fear responses often generalize from threat cues to perceptually similar stimuli, and excessive generalization is implicated in anxiety-related disorders. Although contextual fear generalization can increase over time, whether auditory fear generalization gradients change after conditioning remains unclear. Here we used an auditory fear-conditioning paradigm in male C57BL/6J mice to examine time-dependent changes in tone generalization and whether CS-only extinction suppresses generalized fear. Mice received five tone-shock pairings at one of four shock intensities (0, 0.25, 0.4, or 1.0mA). Generalization was assessed using the conditioned stimulus (CS; 6kHz) and three lower-frequency generalization stimuli (GSs; GS1 3.8kHz, GS2 3.0kHz, GS3 2.4kHz). To avoid repeated generalization testing before extinction, generalization at 24h and 15 days after conditioning was assessed in independent cohorts. At 24h, the 0.4 and 1.0mA groups showed CS-biased gradients, with higher freezing to the CS than to the more distant GSs. At Day 15, freezing remained high but CS-GS discrimination was reduced; this was most evident in the 0.4mA group, which showed a significantly shallower subject-level slope than the corresponding 24-h group. Two sessions of CS-only extinction reduced freezing to both the CS and untrained GSs, consistent with suppression of generalized auditory fear. These findings suggest that auditory fear generalization can become less stimulus-specific over time and that extinction can suppress generalized fear responses.

articles.title: Engineering long-circulating deferoxamine targeting the innate immunity of neutrophil ferroptosis for systemic lupus erythematosus treatment.
articles.journal: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
articles.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is characterized by dysregulation of both innate and adaptive immunity, in which ferroptosis-mediated neutrophil death has been implicated in disease progression. However, the clinical application of ferroptosis inhibitors remains limited by rapid systemic clearance and poor pharmacokinetic profiles. Here, we report a full positron emission tomography (PET)-guided strategy for pharmacokinetic engineering of ferroptosis inhibitors through albumin hitchhiking. By incorporating an albumin-binding motif into deferoxamine (DFO), we developed a series of albumin-hitchhiking conjugates and employed in vivo PET imaging-assisted evaluation to identify a long-circulating molecule, termed LACNE. Blood pharmacokinetic analysis showed that LACNE exhibited an estimated terminal blood half-life of 235.94 min, approximately 17-fold longer than that of DFO (13.74 min). Mechanistically, LACNE was preferentially taken up by activated neutrophils via Fcγ receptor-mediated internalization under inflammatory conditions, resulting in effective suppression of neutrophil ferroptosis. Consequently, LACNE reduced autoimmune responses, alleviated renal injury, and improved disease manifestations in lupus-prone mice. Collectively, these findings establish a PET-guided albumin-hitchhiking approach for pharmacokinetic optimization and targeted delivery of ferroptosis inhibitors, providing a promising strategy for precision treatment of SLE.

articles.title: Dietitian involvement and nutritional care organization in intensive care and perioperative settings in France: a cross-sectional survey of healthcare professionals.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nutrition is a key component of care for critically ill and surgical patients, but the organization of nutritional care and the involvement of dietitians in ICU and perioperative pathways remain variable. This survey aimed to describe respondent-reported nutritional care organization and dietitian involvement among healthcare professionals working in ICU and perioperative settings in France, with a focus on dietitian availability, clinical involvement, nutritional governance, and selected aspects of perioperative care.

METHODS: We conducted a voluntary cross-sectional survey among physicians and dietitians working in French ICU and perioperative settings. The survey was disseminated during the French Society of Anaesthesia and Intensive Care Medicine congress, through national professional nutrition and dietetics networks, and via social media. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: Overall, 147 professionals responded, mainly ICU physicians and dietitians, and most worked in university hospitals. Among respondents, dietitian availability was reported in 67% of responses, but dedicated time was frequently limited. Involvement was mainly request-based, and participation in medical meetings or ward rounds was uncommon. A medical nutrition lead was identified in 44% of responses, a written nutrition protocol in 50%, and a task-sharing protocol allowing dietitian prescription in 9%.

CONCLUSION: Reported practices suggest that dietitians are available in many French ICUs and contribute to perioperative care pathways. However, access to dietetic expertise does not necessarily translate into dedicated staffing, routine multidisciplinary participation, or structured nutritional governance. Strengthening local organization through medical leadership, written protocols, and multidisciplinary collaboration may help improve the implementation of nutritional care.

articles.title: Association of the new atherogenic index non-high-sensitivity C-reactive protein/HDL with significant coronary artery disease in patients with suspected coronary artery disease.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Atherosclerosis is the main cause of coronary heart disease (CHD). Atherogenic indexes (AI) are used to stratify cardiovascular risk. The aim of this study is to evaluate the association with significant CHD of a novel AI that includes parameters of both inflammatory residual risk and lipidic residual risk.

METHODS: 203 patients with suspicion of coronary heart disease were included. The new AI was established as the ratio between CRP (mg/dL) multiplied by 100, and HDL-C (mg/dL). It was compared with traditional AI Castelli I and II, and atherogenic index of plasma (AIP).

RESULTS: The mean age was 53.9±7.34 years. 114 patients (55.9%) had significant CHD. The ratio PCRx100/HDL had the highest values of sensibility and specifity and was the only predictor of CHD with OR 1.59 (CI 95% 1.2-2.1, p = 0.001) and multivessel disease with OR of 1.45 (CI 95% 1.2 - 1.7, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: The new ratio PCRx100/HDL shows the best association with significant CHD.

articles.title: Long-term Outcomes After Medical and Surgical Management of Blunt Traumatic Aortic Injury.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Blunt traumatic aortic injury (BTAI) is a common cause of morbidity and mortality after blunt force. Management strategies include non-operative management (NOM) and operative management (OM). This study evaluated patterns of follow-up and outcomes using data from the international Aortic Trauma Foundation (ATF) registry.

METHODS: The ATF prospective multicenter registry was queried for patients who had subsequent follow-up at participating centers after management of BTAI. Patients were stratified by injury grade. Collected data included demographics, imaging, medical therapy, complications, and need for re-intervention.

RESULTS: 227 patients had follow-up data: Grade I (n=45), II (n=31), III (n=124), and IV (n=27). NOM was pursued in 86.7% of GI, 41.9% of GII, 7.2% of GIII, and 0% of GIV injuries while OM was performed in 13.3% of GI, 58.1% of GII, 90.4% of GIII, and 100% of GIV injuries. Anticoagulation was used in 15.7% and anti-platelet therapy in 46.4%. Five (2.2%) patients required re-intervention, mostly in GIII: 1 for failure of NOM, 2 for stent thrombosis, and 1 for subclavian steal. One patient with GII injury had reintervention for lesion progression. Morbidities (3.1%) included ischemia from left subclavian artery (LSA) coverage(n=5), embolic complication (n=1), and infection (n=1). Notably, there were no strokes, re-interventions for endoleak, or stent graft-related complications upon initial deployment.

CONCLUSION: Both NOM and OM demonstrated favorable outcomes with low rates of treatment failure or re-intervention. TEVAR had low device-related complication rates. However, consistent follow-up remains a challenge in the trauma population.

articles.title: 2026 International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation Consensus on Science With Treatment Recommendations: Summary from the Basic Life Support; Advanced Life Support; Pediatric Life Support; Neonatal Life Support; Education, Implementation, and Teams; and First Aid Task Forces.
articles.abstract: This is the annual summary of the International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation Consensus on Science With Treatment Recommendations; a comprehensive review was completed in 2025. This latest summary addresses the most recent published resuscitation evidence reviewed by International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation task forces, including Basic Life Support; Advanced Life Support; Pediatric Life Support; Neonatal Life Support; Education, Implementation, and Teams; and First Aid. Members from these 6 task forces assessed the certainty of the evidence using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation criteria, and their statements include consensus treatment recommendations. Highlights from task force discussions and insights into how decisions regarding treatment recommendations were made are provided in the Justification and Evidence-to-Decision Framework Highlights sections. The task forces also listed priority knowledge gaps for further research.

articles.title: The Achilles heel of successful treatment of acute myocardial infarction: Tackling large thrombus burden and no reflow.
articles.abstract: Primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is the preferred reperfusion strategy for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), rapidly restoring coronary blood flow, limiting infarct size, improving survival, and reducing recurrent ischemic events. Advances in interventional techniques and adjunctive therapies have enhanced its safety and efficacy over time, with high rates of successful epicardial reperfusion, however large intracoronary thrombus burden remains a major challenge during primary PCI. Extensive thrombus promotes distal embolization of platelet-fibrin aggregates and atherothrombotic debris, which mechanically occlude the downstream capillary bed during reperfusion triggering microvascular obstruction, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and the no-reflow phenomenon. Consequently, restoration of epicardial patency does not always translate into effective myocardial tissue perfusion or myocardial salvage, resulting in larger infarcts and worse clinical outcomes. Contemporary management strategies aim to reduce thrombus burden, preserve microvascular integrity, and improve myocardial salvage through adjunctive pharmacologic therapies, selective mechanical interventions, and optimized procedural techniques. Although routine use of aspiration thrombectomy and many adjunctive intracoronary therapies have not consistently improved clinical outcomes, selective use in carefully chosen patients remains an important component of contemporary practice. Emerging strategies are shifting the focus beyond restoration of epicardial flow toward preservation of the coronary microcirculation. Advances in intracoronary imaging, precision PCI, and therapies targeting inflammation, reperfusion injury, and microvascular dysfunction offer promising opportunities to individualize treatment and further improve outcomes in patients with STEMI and large thrombus burden.

articles.title: Coronary physiology and the choice of revascularisation strategy.
Beyond edge-to-edge repair for the percutaneous treatment of mitral valve disease.
articles.abstract: Mitral regurgitation (MR) is one of the most prevalent valvular heart diseases worldwide. Mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) has become the cornerstone percutaneous treatment for both primary and secondary MR; however, its efficacy remains highly anatomy-dependent, with a substantial proportion of patients deemed unsuitable and others experiencing residual or recurrent MR at follow-up. Looking beyond M-TEER, a growing armamentarium of alternative transcatheter strategies has emerged, including transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) platforms direct and indirect annuloplasty systems, and, more recently, percutaneous chordal replacement/leaflet-based technologies. This review discusses the current evidence supporting TMVR, transcatheter annuloplasty, and emerging leaflet-based strategies, focusing on those technologies most likely to redefine the treatment algorithm for mitral regurgitation over the coming years.

articles.title: Hypertension among Civil Servants: A Cross-sectional Study in Osun State, Nigeria.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a major public health concern associated with cardiovascular complications, including heart disease and stroke. This study assessed hypertension knowledge, prevalence, and associated risk factors among civil servants in Osun State, Nigeria.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 305 civil servants selected through multistage sampling. Data were collected using a semi-structured questionnaire and analysed using SPSS version 23. Binary logistic regression examined predictors of hypertension knowledge and selected modifiable risk behaviours. Statistical significance was set at p<0.05.

RESULTS: Participants' mean age was 39.48 ± 7.50 years. Overall, 75.7% had good knowledge of hypertension, while the observed hypertension prevalence was 44.6%. Participants aged 20-39 years had higher odds of good knowledge than those aged 40-59 years (AOR=1.74, 95% CI: 1.02-2.96). Males had higher odds of smoking (AOR=13.58, 95% CI: 1.78-103.64) and alcohol consumption (AOR=3.99, 95% CI: 2.08-7.65). Monogamous respondents had lower odds of alcohol consumption than polygamous respondents (AOR=0.40, 95% CI: 0.20-0.80). Younger age was associated with the physical activity outcome (AOR=0.35, 95% CI: 0.18-0.70).

CONCLUSION: Despite good hypertension knowledge, the observed prevalence was substantial. Workplace interventions should extend beyond health education to integrating blood pressure screening, early referral, appropriate management, targeted lifestyle modification. Collaboration between government agencies and occupational health services is essential for implementing sustainable cardiovascular health programmes.

articles.title: L-carnitine Alleviates Tacrolimus-Induced Diabetes Mellitus by Regulating the Hepatic Srebp1-Acaca/Scd1 Pathway.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-transplantation diabetes mellitus (PTDM) is a major metabolic complication of tacrolimus-based immunosuppression. This study aimed to identify key metabolic alterations and explore targeted nutritional therapeutics for tacrolimus-induced diabetes mellitus.

METHODS: Untargeted metabolomics was performed on serum from 52 kidney transplant recipients. The findings were validated in a tacrolimus-induced diabetic mouse model. Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses were identified mechanistic nodes in the liver. Mice were co-administered L-carnitine to evaluate its protective effects. AML-12 hepatocytes were used for in vitro validation.

RESULTS: Metabolomics revealed significant serum L-carnitine depletion in PTDM patients compared to controls and pre-transplant baselines. ROC analysis demonstrated L-carnitine as a predictor of PTDM. In mice, tacrolimus induced L-carnitine deficiency. Multi-omics revealed that the sterol regulatory element binding transcription factor 1 (Srebf1)-associated upregulation of acetyl-CoA carboxylase (Acaca) and stearoyl-CoA desaturase 1 (Scd1) was correlated with hepatic metabolic toxicity. Tacrolimus triggered hepatic acetyl-CoA accumulation to upregulate Srebf1 transcription and Srebp1 protein. Consequently, Acaca and Scd1 were upregulated, driving the elevation of malonyl-CoA. L-carnitine supplementation reversed these alterations and restored fatty acid oxidation, alleviating tacrolimus-induced glucose intolerance, insulin resistance, and dyslipidemia. siRNA-mediated knockdown of Srebf1 abolished tacrolimus-induced lipogenic protein upregulation, lipid accumulation, and fatty acid oxidation impairment in hepatocytes.

CONCLUSION: Tacrolimus drives hepatic lipotoxicity by uncoupling acetyl-CoA buffering from fatty acid oxidation via the Srebp1-Acaca/Scd1 axis. L-carnitine supplementation serves as a clinically accessible therapy to break this vicious cycle and restore metabolic homeostasis in transplant recipients.

articles.title: ATP-sensitive potassium channel openers inhibit the formation of neutrophil extracellular traps to protect against neuroinflammation in ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Neuroinflammation is a key contributor to brain injury and poor functional recovery after ischemic stroke, yet no clinically approved therapy targets the neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)-cGAS-STING axis that drives it. This study investigates the effects of the clinically used K-ATP channel opener nicorandil on neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation and evaluates its potential to attenuate NET-cGAS-STING-associated neuroinflammation. A mouse model of middle cerebral artery occlusion and reperfusion (MCAO/R) and BV-2 microglial cell oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) were used to assess NET formation, cGAS-STING pathway activation, inflammatory responses, and neurological injury. Significant increases in NET markers, such as MPO-DNA and CitH3, were found in plasma and brain tissue after MCAO/R. This was accompanied by elevated TNF-α, IL-6、IL-1β, brain edema, neuronal apoptosis, and neurological deficits. Both DNase I-mediated NET degradation and Nicorandil treatment reduced NET formation, suppressed microglial activation, lowered phosphorylation of STING and TBK1, and alleviated brain infarction, neuronal death, and impairment. In vitro, exogenous NETs enhanced OGD/R-induced cGAS-STING activation and IL-1β release, effects reversed by DNase I and Nicorandil. In summary, extracellular DNA associated with NETs promotes microglial cGAS-STING activation and contributes to neuroinflammatory injury after stroke. Nicorandil exerts neuroprotective effects by inhibiting the upstream formation of NETs and attenuating this signaling axis, suggesting a promising and readily translatable therapeutic strategy for ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Awareness, Use and Perceptions of Potassium-Enriched Low-Sodium Salt Substitutes in Canada: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Excess dietary sodium is a major contributor to cardiovascular disease and stroke, and most Canadians exceed recommended intake levels. Efforts to reduce population sodium intake have had minimal impact in Canada to date. Recently, the World Health Organization conditionally recommended potassium-enriched low-sodium salt substitutes (LSSS) as a strategy to reduce population sodium intake; however, public awareness, perceptions, and use of LSSS are unknown.

OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to assess Canadians' awareness, perceptions, and use of LSSS, and to examine how these vary by age, gender, and hypertension status in order to generate evidence to inform sodium reduction policy in Canada.

DESIGN: This cross-sectional study used data from the Canadian Nutrition and Health Survey (CNHS), administered between November 2024 and February 2025 using a stratified random sample of Canadian adults considering age, gender, province and educational level.

PARTICIPANTS/SETTINGS: Participants were eligible if they were aged ≥18 years, were literate in English or French, used a computing device with internet access, and lived in Canada.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The main outcome measures were awareness, use, attitudes toward government LSSS policy, and perceptions of LSSS.

STATISTICAL ANALYSES PERFORMED: Quantitative data were stratified by age, gender, and hypertension status. Chi-square tests were used to compare categorical variables, and logistic regression models were used to describe subgroup differences. Open survey responses were thematically analyzed.

RESULTS: Participants (n=3,283; mean age 49.9 ± 17.7 [SD] years, 50.8% women) reported low awareness (39.6%) and current use (11.1%) of LSSS, although many had tried LSSS in the past (69.3%). Awareness and current use were significantly higher among those with hypertension compared to those without hypertension (awareness: 48.1% vs. 36.2%, p<0.001; current use: 13.7% vs. 9.8%, p=0.001). Awareness was lowest among adults aged 35-44 years (29.6%), while current use was lowest among adults aged 18-24 years (8.8%). The distribution of overall use of LSSS differed by gender (p<0.001), with a higher proportion of women reporting that they had tried LSSS but did not currently use them (72.4% vs. 66.0%). Overall, 55.4% supported government LSSS policy (24.4% were neutral), with greater support among individuals with hypertension than those without hypertension (59.2% vs. 54.2%, p=0.042). Common barriers to adoption included taste concerns, cost, perceived health risks, and accessibility.

CONCLUSIONS: Canadians have low awareness and use of LSSS with differences by age, gender, and hypertension status. Key barriers such as taste and cost limit broader LSSS adoption despite reasonable support for government LSSS policy.

articles.title: Ligand Binding Characterization of MCT11(SLC16A11) Transporter Reveals High-Affinity Interactions with Long-Chain Fatty Acids.
articles.abstract: Monocarboxylate transporter 11 (MCT11), encoded by SLC16A11, is associated with type 2 diabetes risk in Latin American populations, but its molecular function and substrate specificity remain poorly understood. Here, we combined computational and experimental approaches to characterize ligand-binding preferences of MCT11. Structural homology analysis of 21 major facilitator superfamily transporters, together with evolutionary conservation mapping, identified a putative binding site comprising seven conserved residues. Molecular docking of 211 ligands, including monocarboxylates and long-chain fatty acids, revealed that docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) and palmitic acid (PA) exhibit the most favorable binding energies. Atomistic molecular dynamics simulations confirmed the stability of these interactions, with DHA and PA showing average interaction energies of -181 and -176 kcal/mol, respectively, in an MCT11 homodimeric model embedded in a lipid bilayer. These computational predictions were experimentally validated using thermal shift assays on enriched recombinant MCT11. Both DHA and PA significantly increased protein thermal stability at picomolar concentrations. In contrast, pyruvate, a canonical substrate of other MCT family members, stabilized MCT11 only at millimolar concentrations and induced destabilization at lower concentrations. Collectively, our data demonstrate that MCT11 exhibits high-affinity binding to long-chain fatty acids, supporting its potential role in hepatic lipid metabolism. These findings provide a molecular basis for understanding how SLC16A11 variants contribute to metabolic disease and open new avenues for functional studies on fatty acid transport.

articles.title: Baseline Macular OCT Thickness of Ocular Hypertensive Patients Improves Prediction of Glaucoma.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether baseline macular ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) and circumpapillary retinal nerve fiber layer (cpRNFL) thickness add prognostic value for glaucomatous visual field (VF) damage in patients with ocular hypertension.

DESIGN: Retrospective clinical cohort study.

PARTICIPANTS: 330 eyes of 235 patients with ocular hypertension, defined by intraocular pressure of 22 mmHg or higher or an International Classification of Diseases coded diagnosis, without repeatable glaucomatous VF damage at baseline. Eyes came from both the African Descent and Glaucoma Evaluation Study and a clinical cohort at the Shiley Eye Institute.

METHODS: Baseline GCIPL and cpRNFL thickness were measured from the first good-quality Cirrus optical coherence tomography (OCT) macular and optic-disc cubes. Clinical predictors were assessed with the Ocular Hypertension Treatment Study (OHTS)-European Glaucoma Prevention Study (EGPS) Risk Calculator. Repeatable glaucomatous VF damage required a Glaucoma Hemifield Test outside normal limits or a pattern standard deviation at the 5% level or worse on three consecutive reliable Humphrey 24-2 examinations.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Hazard ratios per 1 standard deviation (SD) of thinner global and sectoral GCIPL or cpRNFL, and the change in the Harrell concordance (C) index (ΔC) after adding each measure to the Risk Calculator.

RESULTS: Glaucomatous VF damage developed in 47 of 330 eyes (14%) over a median 4.4 years. Adjusted for the Risk Calculator, thinner macular GCIPL was associated with conversion (hazard ratio [HR] 1.89 per 1-SD thinner; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.50 to 2.37; P < .001), and every macular sector was significant (HR 1.71 to 2.02). The Risk Calculator alone showed modest discrimination (Harrell C-index, 0.57). Adding macular GCIPL improved discrimination (ΔC +0.101; 95% CI, +0.022 to +0.220). Global cpRNFL thickness did not improve discrimination (ΔC +0.004; 95% CI, -0.021 to +0.133); among cpRNFL quadrants, only the inferior quadrant was associated with conversion (HR 1.50; 95% CI, 1.02 to 2.22).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with ocular hypertension, thinner baseline macular GCIPL was associated with glaucomatous VF damage and improved the discrimination of the OHTS-EGPS Risk Calculator, whereas global cpRNFL thickness did not.

articles.title: Hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae Modulates Autophagy-Related AMPK-ATG16L1 Signaling and Inflammatory Responses in Macrophages.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae (hvKP) has emerged as a clinically significant pathogen due to its high virulence, multidrug resistance, and ability to cause severe infections even in healthy hosts. Autophagy is a critical innate immune defense mechanism against intracellular pathogens, yet the role of autophagy in hvKP infection and its impact on macrophage inflammatory responses remain poorly understood.

METHODS: THP-1-derived macrophages were infected with hvKP under different multiplicities of infection (MOI) and time points. Autophagy-related marker changes were assessed by Western blotting of LC3-II, Beclin-1, and p62, together with MDC fluorescence staining. The association with AMPK-ATG16L1 signaling was evaluated by monitoring pathway protein expression and using the AMPK inhibitor Compound C. The effects of autophagy-associated pharmacological modulators (rapamycin, 3-MA, chloroquine) on reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and pro-inflammatory cytokine expression (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α) were analyzed by fluorescence microscopy and RT-qPCR, respectively.

RESULTS: hvKP infection induced biphasic time- and MOI-dependent changes in autophagy-related markers, with LC3-II and Beclin-1 increasing during early infection and declining at later time points or higher MOIs. p62 accumulation suggested possible alteration of autophagy-related degradation. hvKP infection was associated with increased AMPK phosphorylation and altered ATG16L1 expression, while Compound C attenuated these autophagy-related marker changes. A CQ terminal pulse assay further supported CQ-sensitive LC3-II and p62 protein accumulation. Gentamicin protection assays showed that 3-MA produced a modest increase in recoverable intracellular hvKP, whereas rapamycin and CQ did not produce statistically significant changes under the present assay conditions. Pharmacological modulation of autophagy-associated pathways was associated with altered ROS accumulation and inflammatory cytokine expression.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that hvKP infection modulates macrophage autophagy-related marker dynamics in association with AMPK-ATG16L1 signaling and inflammatory responses. Because the current study relies mainly on static markers and pharmacological modulation, these data should be interpreted as associative rather than definitive evidence of productive autophagic flux or pathway dependency.

articles.title: Structural Diversity and Functional Roles of the Internalin Family Proteins in Listeria monocytogenes.
articles.abstract: Listeria monocytogenes is an important foodborne intracellular pathogen that can cause listeriosis in humans and animals, with a relatively high mortality rate. Internalin (Inl) family proteins are critical virulence factors of L. monocytogenes and play essential roles in bacterial adhesion, host cell invasion, tissue colonization, immune evasion, and systemic infection. In recent years, with the continuous advancement of genomics, structural biology, and host-pathogen interaction studies, an increasing number of internalin family members and their biological functions have been identified. Different internalins exhibit significant differences in receptor recognition, tissue tropism, and pathogenic mechanisms. This review systematically summarizes the structural characteristics and classification of the internalin family in L. monocytogenes, with particular emphasis on recent advances in the functions of major family members, including InlA, InlB, InlC, InlK, InlF, InlP, InlL, and InlJ, in intestinal invasion, penetration of the placental and blood-brain barriers, intracellular survival, immune evasion, biofilm formation, and host interactions. Furthermore, recent research hotspots in the functional characterization of internalin proteins are discussed, along with their potential applications in elucidating virulence mechanisms, vaccine development, and targeted prevention and control strategies. This review aims to provide a theoretical reference for further investigations into the pathogenic mechanisms of L. monocytogenes and the development of novel prevention and control strategies.

articles.title: Multiple islet autoantibodies are associated with C-peptide below the reporting limit and a limited fasting-to-120-minute increase in routine clinical testing.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To assess whether multiple positive tests within the available GADA/ICA/IAA panel are associated with very low C-peptide and limited fasting-to-120-minute increases in routine testing.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 23,363 patients and 2,866 same-day fasting-to-120-minute pairs. Positivity thresholds were GADA >10 IU/ml, ICA ≥20 IU/ml and IAA ≥20 RU/ml; ICA uses a mixed islet-antigen preparation including IA-2, not separate IA-2A. Patient-clustered models analysed both values below the reporting limit and a <1.5-fold increase among determinable ratios. Repeated-measures models and a common reporting threshold assessed sensitivity to sampling and assay period.

RESULTS: Both values were below the reporting limit in 12/37 (32.4%) multiple-positive versus 41/2,511 (1.6%) zero-positive pair days (adjusted OR 22.89 [95% CI 8.93, 58.67]). Among determinable ratios, a <1.5-fold increase occurred in 12/24 (50.0%) versus 601/2,469 (24.3%) (OR 3.16 [1.37, 7.29]). The adjusted repeated-measures contrast ratio was 0.660 [0.527, 0.827]. Associations persisted at a common 0.067 nmol/l threshold; the paired continuous-response estimate was imprecise (0.895 [0.612, 1.309]).

CONCLUSIONS: Multiple positivity within the available panel was associated with very low C-peptide and more frequent limited increases in routine testing. These joint findings can prompt review of diabetes aetiology and treatment history and help prioritise standardised confirmation.

articles.title: The effect of subcutaneous semaglutide injection on blood pressure: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract: Hypertension remains a leading contributor to cardiovascular disease globally. Semaglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA), reduces blood pressure in clinical trials, but the consistency and magnitude of this effect across populations is unclear. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of placebo-controlled randomized trials reporting blood pressure changes in patients receiving subcutaneous semaglutide. MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Embase were searched through December 2025. Pooled weighted mean differences with 95% confidence intervals were calculated using random-effects inverse-variance models. Cochrane's RoB 2.0 assessed risk of bias, and the Grading of recommendations Assessment Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach was used to evaluate the certainty of the evidence. Our meta-analysis included seven trials with approximately 20,000 patients. Semaglutide reduced systolic blood pressure (SBP) significantly compared with placebo across 11 arms (20,011 participants): weighted mean difference -3.46 mmHg (95% CI: -4.44 to -2.49; I2 = 29.5%; high certainty of evidence). A modest reduction in diastolic blood pressure (DBP) was also observed (-0.56 mmHg, 95% CI: -0.82 to -0.29; I2 = 0.0%; moderate certainty of evidence). However, sensitivity analysis revealed that the DBP effect was dependent on a single large study, with loss of significance upon its exclusion. Subcutaneous semaglutide produces meaningful SBP reduction across diverse patient populations, with minimal DBP changes. Blood pressure improvement represents one component of semaglutide's cardiometabolic benefits.

articles.title: Combination antiviral treatment for a patient with lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus meningoencephalitis associated with bispecific antibody teclistamab therapy for myeloma.
articles.abstract: Lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) is a rare cause of meningoencephalitis in humans. Although LCMV is a rodent zoonosis with a global distribution, no UK cases in humans have been reported in published literature since the 1950s, and testing is rarely performed. LCMV meningoencephalitis is self-limiting in people who are immunocompetent, but infection in hosts who are immunocompromised causes severe disease. We report a presentation of LCMV meningoencephalitis in a patient with relapsed multiple myeloma receiving teclistamab. The patient presented with a 5-month history of progressive neurological symptoms, including hearing loss, ataxia, headache, and weight loss. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis showed lymphocytic pleocytosis, markedly elevated protein concentration, and hypoglycorrhachia. Extensive microbiological and autoimmune investigations were negative, and empirical antimicrobial and antituberculosis therapies did not prevent clinical deterioration. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing of CSF identified LCMV, and a history of domestic rodent exposure was subsequently identified. Combination antiviral therapy with ribavirin, remdesivir, and molnupiravir was initiated. Molnupiravir was later substituted for favipiravir, and favipiravir dosing was guided by serum and CSF therapeutic drug monitoring. The patient showed sustained neurological improvement, with clearance of LCMV from CSF and blood within 2 months. Antiviral therapy continued for 6 months. The patient regained functional independence and returned to work, with only mild residual symptoms. In addition to reporting a novel occurrence of LCMV infection in a patient on teclistamab, the case highlights the presence of LCMV in the UK and the utility of metagenomic next-generation sequencing for pathogen identification in undiagnosed encephalitis. Finally, the case provides preliminary evidence supporting combination antiviral therapy in persistent LCMV infection.

articles.title: Thunderstorm asthma as a confluence of planetary and human health: lessons from Melbourne 2016 for a global agenda.
Precision Immunotherapy in Sepsis.
articles.journal: Seminars in respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract: Precision immunotherapy is usually used as an adjunctive treatment in patients with sepsis and/or septic shock. Previously reported clinical trials have failed to prove efficacy due to great heterogeneity among sepsis patients. This has led to the need for a different strategic approach. At the first stage, patient stratification has been performed based on transcriptional endotypes, clinical-based phenotypes, or biomarker-enriched endotypes, the latest being the most convenient and commonly used. Biomarker endotypes can be broadly categorized into hyperinflammation, immunoparalysis and endothelial dysfunction endotypes, each with different subclasses. The biomarker used for the diagnosis reflects a specific dysregulated immune pathway that is being targeted for treatment. The SAVE-MORE and the ImmunoSep clinical trials are examples of a biomarker-enriched classification system that guided precision immunotherapy. In the SAVE-MORE randomized controlled clinical trial, patients with COVID-19 pneumonia who were at risk for developing severe respiratory failure and who were defined by soluble urokinase plasminogen activator receptor levels ≥ 6 ng/mL were treated with either anakinra or placebo. The study met the primary endpoint and a lower 28-day mortality in favor of anakinra was also found. Based on these findings, anakinra received approval by the European Medicines Agency for this indication. In the ImmunoSep clinical trial, patients with macrophage activation-like syndrome, defined as those with ferritin levels > 4,420 ng/mL, were treated with anakinra or placebo, and patients with immunoparalysis, defined as those with the combination of ferritin ≤ 4,420 ng/mL and < 5,000 HLA-DR receptors on CD45 +/CD14 + monocytes, were treated with rhIFNγ or placebo. The study met its primary endpoint. Several clinical trials of precision immunotherapy are actively recruiting patients using biomarker classification systems. There are still unanswered questions regarding the stability of endotypes over the course of illness and whether time can affect the efficacy of precision immunotherapy.

articles.title: Preoperative Mammographic Findings as Predictors of Mastectomy Skin Flap Necrosis.
articles.journal: Handchirurgie, Mikrochirurgie, plastische Chirurgie : Organ der Deutschsprachigen Arbeitsgemeinschaft fur Handchirurgie : Organ der Deutschsprachigen Arbeitsgemeinschaft fur Mikrochirurgie der Peripheren Nerven und Gefasse : Organ der V...
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mastectomy skin flap necrosis poses a significant challenge for reconstructive surgeons. Diabetes mellitus﻿, obesity, radiation therapy, and smoking are known risk factors. Mastectomy skin flap necrosis occurs when the metabolic demand of tissues is greater than blood supply. No objective measurements exist to quantify the pre-operative risk of mastectomy skin flap necrosis. We hypothesized that subcutaneous tissue thickness correlates with the risk of mastectomy skin flap necrosis. As pre-operative mammography is routinely performed, it can be used to measure subcutaneous tissue thickness. By determining a relationship between the subcutaneous tissue thickness and the mastectomy skin flap necrosis risk, surgeons may tailor their pre-operative counseling and intra-operative decision making.

METHODS: A retrospective chart review of 50 patients undergoing nipple-sparing mastectomy followed by implant-based or autologous reconstruction was performed. Six patients were excluded as pre-operative mammograms were not available. Thus, the final analysis included 44 patients, comprising 73 operated breasts. Six pre-operative mammographic measurements of subcutaneous tissue thickness were made to determine an average value. Multi-variable logistic regression was used to identify the predictors of mastectomy skin flap necrosis.

RESULTS: Twenty-six patients (59.1%) and 38 breasts (52.1%) experienced mastectomy skin flap necrosis. The average subcutaneous tissue thickness was 5.6 mm in those with mastectomy skin flap necrosis compared to 6.4 mm in those without. On multivariable regression, subcutaneous thickness (p=0.04), body mass index (p=0.02), and smoking status (p=0.02) were found to be predictive of mastectomy skin flap necrosis.

CONCLUSIONS: Subcutaneous tissue thickness was predictive of mastectomy skin flap necrosis. Pre-operative mammography serves as an effective measurement tool to measure the subcutaneous tissue thickness pre-operatively. Further studies may elicit an absolute value for tissue thickness below which mastectomy skin flap necrosis can be reliably predicted.

articles.title: Periconceptual Progesterone Use and Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether periconceptual use of progesterone is associated with an altered risk of new-onset hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or superimposed preeclampsia).

DESIGN: Population-based cohort study using statewide pregnancy and birth data from Victoria, Australia, linked with hospital and medication prescribing data.

SETTING: Victoria, Australia (2009-2020).

POPULATION: Nulliparous women who gave birth between 2009 and 2020 in Victoria, Australia. Women with missing delivery dates, medicine dispensation dates, or who were exposed to progesterone in the second or third trimester were excluded.

METHODS: We compared nulliparous women exposed to progesterone in the periconceptual period (6 weeks preconception until the end of the first trimester) with those not exposed to progesterone. Inverse probability-weighted regression adjustment was used to control for confounding factors and investigate the effect of progesterone on the risk of preeclampsia (including superimposed preeclampsia) and gestational hypertension.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Development of preeclampsia or gestational hypertension.

RESULTS: Among 386 475 pregnancies, 5657 (1.5%) women used progesterone in the periconceptual period. Progesterone use was associated with a statistically significant reduction in the risk of any new onset hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (adjusted risk ratio [aRR] 0.81 [95% confidence interval [CI] 0.67, 0.98]; adjusted risk difference [aRD] -1.72% [95% CI -3.21%, -0.24%]). Investigating type of hypertension, we found progesterone use was associated with a 1.69% absolute reduced risk of gestational hypertension (aRR 0.60 [95% CI 0.43, 0.83]; aRD -1.69% [95% CI -2.52%, -0.86%]) but no significant change was observed for preeclampsia (aRR 0.97 [95% CI 0.75, 1.25]; aRD -0.13% [95% CI -1.49%, 1.23%]). Restricting our analyses to pregnancies conceived via assisted reproductive technology only, we found similar results, with a statistically significant reduction in the risk of gestational hypertension (aRR 0.80 [95% CI 0.67, 0.95]; aRD -1.02% [95% CI -1.73%, -0.30%]) but not preeclampsia (aRR 0.96 [95% CI 0.83, 1.11]; aRD -0.25% [95% CI -1.23%, 0.72%]).

CONCLUSIONS: Among 386 475 nulliparous women, we found periconceptual progesterone use to be associated with a statistically significant reduction in the risk of gestational hypertension, but not preeclampsia. However, these findings are unlikely to be clinically meaningful.

articles.title: Bacterial 2',3'-cGAMP signaling induces membrane splitting in antiphage CBASS immunity.
articles.abstract: Bacterial cyclic-oligonucleotide-based antiphage signaling systems (CBASS) are evolutionarily related to the mammalian cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway. The bacterial CdnB-Cap14 CBASS system is notable for producing 2',3'-cyclic GMP-AMP (2',3'-cGAMP), the same second messenger used by the mammalian cGAS-STING pathway; however, its functional mechanism has remained unclear. Here, we show that CdnB-Cap14 protects against phage infection through abortive infection (Abi) by triggering cell death. Structures of apo CdnBΔC and its complexes with ATP and guanosine triphosphate (GTP), together with inactive and activated 2',3'-cGAMP-bound Cap14, reveal that CdnB is autoinhibited by its C-terminal AGS-C domain and becomes activated by DNA together with intracellular ATP/GTP depletion to synthesize 2',3'-cGAMP in vitro. This signal drives Cap14 assembly from dimers into zipper-like two-layered filaments that partition the membrane and disrupt its integrity. We further show that phage-encoded Acb2 sequesters 2',3'-cGAMP to block signaling. These findings reveal mechanistic parallels between bacterial CBASS and eukaryotic cGAS-STING immunity and provide a molecular basis for therapeutic engineering.

articles.title: Durable and reversible epigenetic programming of human hematopoietic stem cells as a platform for modulation of platelet function.
articles.abstract: Programmable epigenome editing offers control of gene expression without altering DNA sequence, but its capacity to program human hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) and their differentiated progeny remains incompletely characterized. Here, we establish that DNA methylation-based epigenome editors delivered transiently as RNA induce heritable gene silencing in primary human HSCs. Targeting the platelet integrin β3 (ITGB3) produced silencing that persisted through long-term HSC self-renewal and megakaryocytic differentiation, impaired aggregation of in vitro-derived platelets, and was partially reversed through targeted demethylation at this locus. Silencing remained stable in human HSCs 4 months after transplantation into mice. Targeting additional platelet-associated genes demonstrated broad applicability with this approach. Together, these findings establish DNA methylation-based epigenome editing as a platform for durable and reversible programming of human HSCs and demonstrate its application to modulating platelet function.

articles.title: Lower recurrence after ablation for MASLD-related versus alcohol-related hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUNDS/AIMS: Non-B non-C hepatocellular carcinoma (NBNC-HCC) encompasses metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), MASLD with increased alcohol intake (MetALD), and alcohol-related liver disease (ALD). We examined whether etiology is associated with recurrence after curative-intent ablation.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 129 consecutive patients who underwent curative-intent ablation (with neoadjuvant transarterial chemoembolization in 36%) between 2011 and 2024 (MASLD 47; MetALD 21; ALD 61) after excluding two unclassifiable patients. Alcohol intake was categorized pragmatically as <=20, >20-60, or >60 g/day irrespective of sex, and the primary comparison was MASLD versus ALD. First recurrence was analyzed with a Fine-Gray model, treating death without recurrence as a competing event.

RESULTS: MASLD carried a lower recurrence hazard than ALD (adjusted subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR] 0.46, 95% CI 0.23-0.90; p=0.023). The association was present before adjustment (sHR 0.59; p=0.043) and strengthened after age adjustment, indicating negative confounding by age. Cause-specific and recurrence-free survival analyses were concordant. In exploratory analyses, local tumor progression showed no clear etiologic difference, whereas non-local recurrence was lower in MASLD (adjusted sHR 0.48; p=0.010); MetALD and ALD did not differ.

CONCLUSIONS: A metabolic (MASLD) rather than alcohol-related (ALD) etiology was associated with lower post-ablation recurrence, localized to non-local rather than local recurrence. Given the pragmatic classification, follow-up imbalance, and possible residual confounding, this finding is hypothesis-generating and requires confirmation in larger, multicenter cohorts.

articles.title: Cul4b sustains cell cycle in germinal center B cells and enables protective humoral immunity against influenza A virus.
articles.abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) are a major public health burden, infecting millions of people worldwide. Seasonal vaccines mitigate disease, in part, by triggering the production of IAV-specific antibodies by B cells. Viral evasion and limited vaccine-induced immunity pose barriers to vaccine effectiveness, warranting further investigation of factors influencing protective immune responses. The generation of affinity-matured antibodies is critical for antiviral immunity. This relies on germinal center (GC) B cells, which undergo multiple rounds of somatic hypermutation, proliferation, and selection. Cullin-4b (Cul4b) acts as the backbone for the Cullin Ring Ligase 4 (CRL4), an E3 ubiquitin ligase complex that ubiquitylates proteins for degradation by the proteosome. CRL4 is critical for regulation of DNA damage responses and cell cycle maintenance, essential for B cells to mount a robust humoral response. Here we investigate the role of Cul4b in B cell responses to IAV using mice lacking Cul4b in B cells. We found that Cul4b promoted viral clearance and anti-IAV antibody titers post-infection and immunization, and Cul4b was required for optimal vaccine-mediated protection against infectious challenge. Additionally, we found that Cul4b supports GC B cell populations and promotes their cell cycle maintenance in vivo. We conclude that B cell intrinsic Cul4b is essential for optimal GC and antibody responses after acute IAV exposure. Further investigation of CRL4 in B cells is warranted to elucidate its potential as a therapeutic target to improve vaccine efficacy.

articles.title: Treatment of a concealed accessory pathway by radiofrequency catheter ablation in a horse.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accessory pathways (APs) are myocardial bundles directly connecting the atria and the ventricles, bypassing the atrioventricular node-His-Purkinje system. Retrograde AP conduction in horses can result in orthodromic atrioventricular re-entry tachycardia or bradycardia. Radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA) can provide a permanent treatment by eliminating the retrograde conducting AP, but was previously unsuccessful in one case.

OBJECTIVES: To report the use of three-dimensional electro-anatomical mapping (3D EAM) to identify a concealed AP and treatment by RFCA in a horse.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective case report.

CASE DESCRIPTION: An irregular heart rhythm was detected in a 4-year-old, 518 kg Paint mare as an incidental finding. Frequent atrial depolarisations were identified in the ST segment with a fixed coupling interval to the preceding QRS complex on the ECG. A differential diagnosis of frequent premature atrial complexes displayed as bigeminy or a retrograde conduction along an AP was made. The presence of a retrograde conducting AP was confirmed by ventricular pacing, which resulted in 1:1 ventriculo-atrial activation. Three-dimensional EAM revealed the earliest atrial activation and thereby the atrial insertion of the AP in the caudal left atrium. Subsequent RFCA at 40 W eliminated AP conduction.

MAIN LIMITATIONS: Single case report.

CONCLUSIONS: This case report describes the identification of an AP by 3D EAM and the first successful permanent treatment of a retrograde conducting AP by RFCA in an adult horse.

articles.title: Integrating blood vessel organoids makes stem cell-derived islets more competent.
articles.abstract: Wang et al. present an all-stem-cell strategy that vascularizes pancreatic islet organoids by integrating them with blood vessel organoids, enhancing β cell maturation and resilience and reversing diabetes in mice.1 The resulting model offers a platform to study islet-vascular biology in vitro and to advance transplantation therapies.

articles.title: Predictors of recanalization after anticoagulation-based treatment in patients with cerebral venous thrombosis.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recanalization following treatment for cerebral venous thrombosis (CVT) is associated with improved clinical outcomes; however, predictors of recanalization remain incompletely defined, particularly in Southeast Asian populations.

OBJECTIVE: To identify clinical and radiological predictors of venous recanalization after anticoagulation-based treatment in Thai patients with CVT.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients diagnosed with CVT who underwent contrast-enhanced computed tomography venography (CTV) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or magnetic resonance venography (MRV) at baseline and follow-up. Baseline characteristics, clinical presentation, initial functional status, neuroimaging findings, treatment modalities, recanalization status, and one-year outcomes were analyzed. Group comparisons were performed using the chi-square test, Mann-Whitney U test, or independent-samples t-test, as appropriate. Variables with p < 0.20 in univariate analysis were entered into a multivariable logistic regression model to identify independent predictors of recanalization.

RESULTS: Of 256 patients with CVT, 212 met inclusion criteria. The proportion of patients with recanalization detected during the follow-up was 54.72%. Thirteen variables identified in univariate analysis were included in the multivariable model. An independent predictor of recanalization was involvement of the torcular herophili (adjusted odds ratio 2.70, 95%CI 1.910-5.220, p = 0.001). The independent (mRS 0-2) clinical outcome at 1-year follow-up was comparable between the two groups (75.86% vs. 71.88%, p = 0.510).

CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, the proportion of patients with recanalization detected during the follow-up after CVT treatment was 54.72%. The involvement of the torcular herophili was independently associated with increased likelihood of recanalization after anticoagulation-based treatment.

articles.title: Revisiting automotive plant closures and overdose mortality: Evidence across drug classes, deaths of despair, and socioeconomic pathways.
articles.journal: The International journal on drug policy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prior research has examined the association between automotive assembly plant closures and opioid overdose mortality. Whether these economic disruptions were also associated with other drug-related deaths, suicide, alcohol-related deaths, and changes in socioeconomic and structural conditions remains unclear.

METHODS: This county-level, quasi-experimental study replicated and extended the previously published sample by Venkataramani et al. (2020), covering automotive plant closures in 112 manufacturing-intensive counties across 30 commuting zones from 1999 to 2016. County-year closure data were linked to restricted-use National Vital Statistics System mortality data and to multiple socioeconomic datasets. Staggered difference-in-differences and event-study models were used to estimate associations of plant closures with mortality and with 6 socioeconomic and structural measures.
