An exploratory product-of-coefficients analysis then assessed potential indirect associations operating through these measures.

RESULTS: In difference-in-differences analyses, plant closures were associated with increases in mortality from all drug overdoses (6.0 deaths per 100,000; 95% CI, 3.5 to 8.6), opioids (7.9; 95% CI, 5.2 to 10.5), stimulants (2.0; 95% CI, 1.1 to 2.9), and benzodiazepines (2.0; 95% CI, 0.3 to 3.7). Closures were also associated with increases in labor-force nonparticipation (LFNP; 1.7 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.7 to 2.7) and the socioeconomic distress index (0.18 SD; 95% CI, 0.05 to 0.30). No indirect associations from the pathway analysis were significant.

CONCLUSIONS: Automotive plant closures were followed by increases in overdose mortality and LFNP. Further research is needed to clarify the pathways linking declining economic opportunity to overdose mortality.

articles.title: Spatially adaptive dose-grid method for efficient proton therapy optimization involving small or irregular structures.
articles.journal: Physica medica : PM : an international journal devoted to the applications of physics to medicine and biology : official journal of the Italian Association of Biomedical Physics (AIFB)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fine spatial resolution (e.g., 0.5-1.5 mm) can be important for accurate dose representation and treatment-plan optimization in cases involving small or irregular targets and organs at risk (OARs). However, applying a uniformly fine dose grid across the entire patient volume introduces substantial computational demands.

OBJECTIVE: This work proposes a spatially adaptive grid-based proton dose calculation and treatment planning method to optimize dose accuracy and computational efficiency simultaneously.

METHODS: The proposed method retains fine spatial sampling in the target and selected OARs while using coarse sampling in the remaining body region. The method was evaluated in five clinical cases, including two head-and-neck cases, two meningioma cases, and one cardiac arrhythmia case, and was compared with uniformly fine and predominantly coarse grid strategies.

RESULTS: Across the five cases, ADAPTIVE reduced the OAR-dose RMSE by 92.7 %-98.3 % relative to COARSE. Compared with FINE, ADAPTIVE reduced dose-calculation and optimization times by averages of 70.8 % and 83.8 %, respectively, while closely reproducing the OAR dose metrics obtained with FINE.

CONCLUSIONS: This work introduces a novel spatially adaptive grid-based proton dose calculation and treatment planning method for clinical cases with small/irregular OAR/target, which provides an accurate and efficient treatment plan on multiscale adaptive dose grid.

articles.title: Multicentre study of activity quantification methods for 99m-Tc-pyrophosphate SPECT/CT in cardiac amyloidosis.
articles.journal: Physica medica : PM : an international journal devoted to the applications of physics to medicine and biology : official journal of the Italian Association of Biomedical Physics (AIFB)
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: 99mTc-PYP SPECT/CT imaging is used for diagnosis of transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CA). The calculation of quantitative metrics allows assessment of the myocardial amyloid burden and supports therapy response evaluations. This study explores the implementation of reliable metrics and the validation of activity quantification methods in a multicentre study.

METHODS: As part of the IAEA Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy (iTAC) project, a multicentre phantom study was conducted at 10 institutions using 12 hybrid SPECT/CT systems. Standardized acquisitions consistent with clinical protocols were used to compute the activity calibration factors (ACF). Absolute activity verifications were based on cardiac insert measurements with known activity distributions. Multiple reconstruction/quantification approaches (RecMethod) were evaluated, including the institution method (SiteProc) and four alternative ones; results of the computed activity were compared with the true activity meter measurements. Accuracy was assessed using RecMethod-to-True activity ratios, summarized by median, interquartile range (IQR) and coefficient of variation (CV).

RESULTS: Most institution ACF values (ACFSiteProc) ranged 75-105 cps/MBq and were consistent with reference CoreLab estimates. Agreement between ACFSiteProc and reference CoreLab values showed a median ratio of 99.6 %, IQR 5.8 %, and CV 9.4 %, indicating no systematic bias. For activity quantification, median RecMethod-to-True ratios were 100.1 % for the SiteProc reconstructions and 97.8 %, 94.1 %, 95.6 % and 96.0 % for the alternatives.

CONCLUSION: The evaluated quantification methods demonstrated good median accuracy across institutions providing reliable activity estimates, essential for a robust implementation of quantitative metrics for ATTR-CA. The obtained inter-site variability indicates that precision remains a challenge at the multicentre quantitative imaging studies.

articles.title: Retraction notice to "Prevalence of genital tract infection with Entamoeba gingivalis among copper T 380A intrauterine device users in Egypt" [Contraception 85 (2012) 108-112].
Multi-scale facility context and micro-spatial motor-vehicle-cyclist conflict risk at signalized intersections: a characterized spatial squares framework.
articles.abstract: Connected and automated intersection management requires spatially explicit safety methods that translate real-time traffic data into micro-scale risk information. This study introduced a CSS framework to explore how facility location, visibility-based spatial configuration, and local traffic exposure jointly relate to motor-vehicle-cyclist conflicts at signalized intersections. The framework divides the internal intersection into fine grid cells, assigns PET-based conflict outcomes and local traffic exposure to each cell, and uses visibility indicators and multi-scale facility variables to characterize them. Using UAV data from signalized intersections in Chengdu, China, the study built 4481 core grid cells and identified 3669 conflicts. A Boruta-RF model screened relevant predictors, including traffic exposure, spatial configuration, positional controls, and facility variables, at five spatial scales. Results show that conflict risk is highly micro-spatial and not fully explained by site-level conflict totals. Facility variables were most informative at the heavyfar and ultrafar scales; local and near facility encodings were not Confirmed, but all four facility-traffic interaction terms were. These findings suggest that intersection facilities relate to conflict risk through neighborhood-scale spatial contexts rather than as isolated design features. Although the evidence comes from eight intersections in a single city, the CSS framework identifies where facility-related conflict risk concentrates and can be used to guide targeted facility redesign. Applications such as real-time risk mapping and adaptive intersection management still require further validation.

articles.title: Vasodilatory and antihypertensive effects of sotagliflozin: Ex vivo evaluation in isolated rat aortic rings and an in vivo assessment in spontaneously hypertensive rats.
articles.abstract: Sotagliflozin, a dual SGLT1/2 inhibitor, is noted for its cardioprotective and antihypertensive effects, yet its direct vascular action remains unclear. This study investigated its ex vivo vasodilatory effects in isolated rat thoracic aorta and in vivo antihypertensive effects in non-diabetic Spontaneously Hypertensive rats (SHRs), with subchronic safety assessment. Aortic rings were pre-contracted with phenylephrine or potassium chloride, and underlying mechanisms were studied using pathway-specific inhibitors against matched vehicle controls. Blood pressure and heart rate were measured weekly over 28 days of oral treatment, and safety assessed through body weight, organ weight, biochemistry and hematology. Sotagliflozin induced a concentration-dependent, predominantly endothelium-dependent vasodilation. Cyclooxygenase-derived prostanoid signaling coupled to the AC/cAMP/PKA axis contributed most consistently. In contrast, attenuation by L-NAME and ODQ was surmounted at higher concentrations, indicating a supplementary role for the NO/sGC/cGMP pathway. Vasodilation persisted under KCl-induced depolarization and was unaffected by potassium channel blockers, arguing against a requirement for potassium channel-mediated hyperpolarization. Sotagliflozin also blunted vasoconstriction mediated by voltage-operated calcium channels and inositol triphosphate receptors. In vivo, 200 mg/kg significantly reduced systolic blood pressure relative to baseline and vehicle control, comparably to propranolol and without reflex tachycardia, whereas diastolic and mean arterial pressures were unaltered. Body and organ weights were unaffected, serum uric acid was lower at 50 and 100 mg/kg, urea was higher at the upper doses, and hematology was unremarkable. These findings indicate that sotagliflozin exerts direct vasodilatory activity in the rat thoracic aorta and lowers systolic blood pressure at supratherapeutic doses, warranting further investigation.

articles.title: Femoral venous stasis index improves risk classification in patients with pulmonary hypertension: a post-hoc analysis of the CODOVEIN study.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) requires accurate risk stratification to guide management. Although current ESC/ERS three-strata model is widely used, most patients remain classified at intermediate risk, limiting clinical decision-making. The femoral venous stasis index (FVSI), a Doppler-derived marker of venous congestion, has been associated with elevated right atrial pressure. We evaluated whether FVSI improves 1-year prognostic classification beyond the ESC/ERS 2022 model.

METHODS: This post hoc analysis used data from the CODOVEIN study, including patients with confirmed PH. The primary composite endpoint was 1-year morbidity-mortality: escalation of PH-specific therapy, hospitalization for right-heart failure, or PH-related death. Patients were classified using ESC/ERS 2022 criteria. FVSI was categorized using predefined thresholds (<0.18, 0.18-0.45, >0.45). Risk improvement was assessed using the Net Reclassification Index (NRI). Survival was analyzed with log-rank tests.

RESULTS: Ninety-one patients were included (62.2% precapillary PH). The global NRI was 0.736, with event and non-event components of 0.333 and 0.403, respectively. Among intermediate-risk patients, 1-year event rates increased across FVSI categories (16.7%, 43.5%, 66.7%; p = 0.027). Survival differed significantly across FVSI-based subgroups (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: FVSI significantly improves 1-year risk classification in PH patients, particularly within the intermediate-risk category. As a simple, non-invasive marker of venous congestion, FVSI may refine prognostication and deserve evaluation in prospective multicenter studies.

articles.title: Pulmonary artery pulsatility index and adverse outcomes in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pulmonary hypertension (pH) is a recognized complication of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), in which right ventricular (RV) dysfunction is associated with worse outcomes. The prognostic value of the pulmonary artery pulsatility index (PAPi), a load-dependent surrogate of RV performance, remains unclear in COPD.

METHOD: We performed a single-center retrospective cohort study of patients with COPD who underwent right heart catheterization (RHC) between January 2018 and December 2023. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalizations. Data were stratified into PAPi tertiles, and outcomes were compared using Cox proportional hazards models, adjusted for demographics, comorbidities, and surrogates of COPD and pH severity.

RESULTS: Among 224 patients, 50% were female, 75% African American, and 81% had pH. Median (ranges) PAPi values in the high, intermediate, and low tertiles were 8.1 (4.7-90), 3 (2.3-4.7), and 1.6 (0.5-2.3), respectively. Patients with low PAPi had higher mean and diastolic pulmonary artery pressures, as well as left- and right-sided filling pressures on RHC. On echocardiography, those with low PAPi had lower left ventricular systolic function and more RV strain. Compared with high PAPi, low PAPi was associated with higher risk of the composite outcome (unadjusted model: hazard ratio [HR]=2.36 [95% CI 1.34-4.17], p-value=0.003; adjusted model: HR=2.65 [95% CI 1.42-4.92]; p-value=0.002).

CONCLUSION: Lower PAPi may identify patients with COPD at increased risk of adverse outcomes. Future studies are needed to validate our study findings in different COPD cohorts and explore optimal PAPi cutoffs.

articles.title: Multilevel predictors of sleep quality trajectories in patients with heart failure: an application of the social-ecological model of sleep health.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Poor sleep quality is common in patients with heart failure, yet its heterogeneous trajectories and multilevel predictors remain unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To identify heterogeneous trajectories of sleep quality and explore their multilevel predictors among patients with heart failure during the hospital-to-home transition.

METHODS: We recruited 227 patients with heart failure from the cardiology departments of three tertiary hospitals in China using a longitudinal study design. Sleep quality was assessed pre-discharge and at 1, 3, and 6 months post-discharge. Baseline predictors across individual, interpersonal and societal levels were assessed before patient discharge, including sociodemographic and clinical characteristics, physical symptoms, sleep beliefs and attitudes, mutuality, nighttime light, and pre-sleep electronic screen exposure. Latent growth mixture modeling was employed to identify sleep quality trajectories, and multinomial logistic regression was used to explore predictors of trajectory membership.

RESULTS: Three trajectories were identified: poor-persisted (18.5%), poor-alleviated (6.6%) and good-persisted (74.9%). Patients with severe physical symptoms, nighttime light exposure, and pre-sleep electronic screen exposure (≥ 2 h) tended to be in the "poor-persisted" group, whereas those with positive sleep beliefs and attitudes were more likely to be in the "good-persisted" group.

CONCLUSIONS: Nearly one-fifth of patients with heart failure experience persistently poor sleep quality during 6 months after discharge. These findings support early screening and follow-up assessment of patients at risk of persistent poor sleep quality. Relieving physical symptoms, modifying negative sleep beliefs and attitudes, and reducing nighttime light and electronic screen exposure may be potential targets for multilevel sleep management in patients with heart failure.

articles.title: Incentive-compatible risk preferences and sustainable land management adoption under climate risk: Evidence from semi-arid Kenya.
articles.abstract: Sustainable land management (SLM) practices are widely promoted as an effective pathway for mitigating climate-induced production risks and enhancing agricultural sustainability. However, their uptake has remained low across Sub-Saharan Africa despite the associated benefits. Existing studies have primarily evaluated socio-economic and institutional determinants, with limited evidence on incentivized risk preference and loss aversion, particularly for multiple practice adoption. This gap is especially consequential in arid and semi-arid regions, where production uncertainty is high and adoption decisions are inherently risky. In South Eastern Kenya (SEK), recurrent droughts and extreme climate events have contributed to widespread food insecurity, crop losses, and livestock deaths, making adoption important for agricultural sustainability and climate resilience. Using data from 867 farm households selected through multistage sampling in semi-arid SEK, this study examines how risk preference and loss aversion are associated with SLM adoption breadth. An incentivized field experiment was employed to elicit both measures while adoption behaviour was assessed using a generalized Poisson regression model. Risk-loving farmers show greater adoption breadth than risk-averse farmers, while higher loss aversion is associated with lower adoption breadth. Locus of control, aspiration, wealth, shock exposure and crop diversity are positively associated with adoption breadth. Perceived climate-resilience benefits show a modest positive association, whereas perceived productivity and environmental-quality benefits are negatively associated. These findings highlight the relevance of behavioural heterogeneity for strategies to broaden SLM adoption in climate-vulnerable semi-arid areas.

articles.title: Implicit neural representation steganography scheme for secret model transmission.
articles.journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
articles.abstract: As deep neural network models are increasingly shared over open networks, parameter-level transmission of complete model states through neural carriers has become an emerging problem in model steganography. Existing steganography methods based on implicit neural representations (INRs) mainly focus on multimedia payloads and are not directly designed for transmitting specified neural network model states. To address this problem, we propose an INR-based steganography scheme for secret-model transmission. The proposed method uses standard SIREN networks fitted to public cover images as carriers and segments the floating-point parameter state of a secret model across multiple INR files without modifying the carrier architecture. A key-controlled frozen-slot mechanism preserves the embedded values during cover-image fitting. To accommodate heterogeneous model parameters, we further introduce parameter-type-aware normalization for ordinary weights and normalization statistics, followed by layer-aware distribution mapping according to clean-INR parameter distributions. Experiments across multiple vision-model families, including convolutional networks and a vision transformer, show that, under uncompressed and untampered FP32 transmission, the recovered models match the original task performance at the reported evaluation precision while maintaining high-quality cover reconstruction. Parameter-level recovery fidelity is further quantified using MAE, MaxErr, bit-exact fractions, and parameter-content hashes. Matched-checkpoint comparisons with model-steganography baselines characterize recovery fidelity, transmission cost, and sender-side optimization requirements. Additional experiments characterize the behavior of the proposed scheme under precision conversion, quantization, model-file rewriting, fine-tuning, noise, and pruning.

articles.title: Linguistic features from constrained spontaneous speech as potential markers of preclinical Alzheimer's disease.
articles.journal: The journal of prevention of Alzheimer's disease
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Language impairment is an early sign of Alzheimer's disease (AD) that may emerge before more obvious cognitive decline. Linguistic features derived from verbal responses to cognitive tests have shown promise for identifying mild cognitive impairment and predicting AD risk; however, their relationships with established AD biomarkers remain insufficiently characterized.

OBJECTIVES: To examine relationships between a comprehensive set of linguistic features derived from logical memory delayed recall (LMDR) responses and amyloid status as well as regional tau burden among cognitively normal participants.

DESIGN: In this cross-sectional study, we evaluated associations between two types of AD biomarkers (amyloid status and regional tau burden) and linguistic features using covariate-adjusted regression models tailored to each feature's distribution (e.g., linear, negative binomial, zero-inflated beta, and gamma regression). We then used LASSO regression and the Boruta feature-selection algorithm to identify features most informative of biomarker status.

SETTING: A community-based subcohort from the Framingham Heart Study.

PARTICIPANTS: A total of 238 cognitively unimpaired participants who completed the LMDR test within 1 year before or after tau positron emission tomography (PET) were included. Of these, 228 also underwent amyloid PET and 227 had LMDR voice recordings available.

MEASUREMENTS: Verbal responses to the LMDR test were digitally recorded and manually transcribed. We extracted 54 linguistic and paralinguistic features from transcribed responses using natural language processing, capturing lexical diversity and density, syntactic complexity, semantic/information density, and speech fluency and rate. Tau SUVR values were quantified from PET imaging in 5 brain regions (amygdala, entorhinal cortex, inferior temporal [IT], inferior parietal [IP], and precuneus). Amyloid status was classified as Aβ- or Aβ+ using Gaussian mixture modeling of PiB PET DVR values. LMDR total score and participant demographics (age, sex, education) were included as covariates.

RESULTS: After adjusting for age, sex, education, amyloid status, and LMDR score, 23 linguistic features were associated with tau burden in at least one brain region. For example, reduced semantic richness, captured by lower uniqueIdeaDensity, was associated with higher tau burden across multiple regions, including the amygdala (average marginal effect (AME)=-0.007, 95% CI: (-0.013, -0.001)), entorhinal (AME=-0.007, 95% CI: (-0.013, -0.002)), IT (AME=-0.008, 95% CI: (-0.014, -0.002)), and precuneus (AME=-0.006, 95% CI: (-0.012, -1.51e^-5)). More between-utterance pauses were associated with higher tau burden in the entorhinal (AME=0.259, 95% CI: (0.026, 0.493)), IT (AME=0.272, 95% CI: (0.025, 0.518)), and IP (AME=0.404, 95% CI: (0.160, 0.648)) regions. No linguistic features were associated with amyloid status, and LMDR total score was not associated with either tau burden or amyloid status. LASSO regression selected 3-7 features per brain region, capturing multiple aspects of language use (e.g., speech disfluency and semantic density) associated with tau burden. The nonlinear Boruta algorithm selected a larger set of biomarker-informative features, including predictors of amyloid positivity, and identified additional syntactic measures (e.g., Yngve score, mean dependency distance) as important predictors of regional tau burden.

CONCLUSIONS: Linguistic features derived from neuropsychological (NP) tests capture subtle language changes associated with regional tau pathology in cognitively normal individuals, beyond conventional NP test scores. These findings highlight the potential of language-based measures as non-invasive digital biomarkers for early AD risk stratification and for supporting clinical decision-making about biomarker testing for possible preclinical AD.

articles.title: Azithromycin and hydroxychloroquine drive differential responses of marine amphipods and copepods in a 30-day microcosm experiment.
articles.abstract: This study investigated how two COVID-19 drugs, azithromycin (AZM) and hydroxychloroquine (HCQ), affect marine meiobenthic communities. We conducted 30-day microcosm experiments to assess the effects of these pharmaceuticals on coastal sediment communities. Treatments included controls, low and high doses of each drug (31.62 and 63.24 μg L-1), and combinations of both compounds. Both amphipods and copepods showed concentration-dependent changes in community structure. Amphipod abundance declined under pharmaceutical exposure, while the dominant control species, Paraniphargus valesi, was eliminated from HCQ2 and AZM1/HCQ2 and strongly reduced in most other treatments. Tolerant species such as Microdeutopus versiculatus increased under stress. Amphipod species richness declined in all treatments except AZM1, whereas Shannon-Wiener diversity (H') decreased only in HCQ2, AZM1/HCQ1 and AZM2/HCQ2; both indices correlated negatively with HCQ but not with AZM concentration. ANOSIM and SIMPER confirmed community differences between treated and control groups, ranging from 19.8% to 54.7% (amphipods) and 32.3% to 45.1% (copepods), with R-statistics approaching 1. SIMPER identified the loss of P. valesi and Stenothoe monoculoides as major contributors to community restructuring. Copepod assemblages showed similar responses, including altered abundance patterns and reduced species richness. In copepods, cluster analysis and nMDS clearly separated pharmaceutical-treated samples from controls, whereas in amphipods only HCQ2 and the mixtures separated clearly. Overall, these findings demonstrate that COVID-19 pharmaceuticals can act as potent marine stressors at concentrations representing elevated-exposure scenarios for contaminated coastal waters, with combined exposures producing community-level effects that, in terms of dissimilarity, partly exceeded those of single-drug treatments.

articles.title: Diagnosis of Chagas disease using tensor Tucker-compressed ECG scalograms.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: As modest illness-related patterns are dispersed throughout the temporal, spectral, and inter-leaddimensions of the electrocardiogram (ECG) signals, automated diagnosis of Chagas disease from ECG recordings remains difficult. To address this challenge, this study develops a tensor-based representation framework that preserves the multidimensional characteristics of ECG scalograms while learning low-dimensional projection subspaces using Tucker decomposition.Approach: The proposed framework integrates multi-domain feature extraction, tensor-based representation learning, dimensionality reduction, and ensemble classification for automated Chagas disease detection from 12-lead ECG recordings. It extracts five categories of features: (a) scalogram from specific ECG leads;(b) scalogram features from beat-aligned averaged ECG segments; (c) heart rate variability-based statistics;(d) statistical features from every ECG lead; and (e) patient information (weight, age, and sex). The continuous wavelet transform (CWT) for time-frequency feature extraction is used to create scalograms, which allow for the capture of multi-scale frequency patterns and local transients linked to the course of the disease. A 3-D tensor representation that maintains spatial, temporal, and frequency linkages was created by assembling the scalogram-based features. Optimal partial Tucker tensor decomposition was used to reduce dimensionality. For improved classification performance, the resulting core tensor was flattened, merged with the remaining features (b to e), and then subjected to Fisher score-based feature selection. A RUSBoost classifier was employed for binary classification of 12-lead ECG recordings into Chagas and other classes, while addressing class imbalance through random under-sampling.Main results: The proposed framework was evaluated on the hidden PhysioNet/CinC 2025 Challenge test set through a follow-up Challenge submission under the team name Spectra, achieving an accuracy of 88.7%, an F1-Chagas score of 0.171, an AUPRC of 0.136, an AUROC of 0.631, and an overall Challenge Score of 0.217, indicating good generalization to previously unseen ECG recordings.

SIGNIFICANCE: This work introduces a projection-based tensor representation learning strategy for ECG analysis that transforms high-dimensional scalogram based features into compact latent features while retaining clinically relevant temporal, spectral, and inter-lead information. The proposed framework can facilitate reliable automated Chagas disease screening from routine ECG recordings for earlier clinical intervention.

articles.title: A PPG sensor-based multi-feature machine learning approach for wide-range and high-precision SpO2measurement.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to improve peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) estimation across a wide range for hypoxemic-risk assessment in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) using dual-wavelength photoplethysmography (PPG) and machine learning.Approach. A MAX30102-based module acquired synchronized red (660 nm) and near-infrared (880 nm) PPG signals from the right index finger. A CMS50DA oximeter on the right middle finger provided concurrent reference SpO2 readings for training and evaluation. Smartphone video captured its display for manual label extraction and independent checking. The ratio-of-ratios (R) and morphological, temporal, statistical, and derivative features were extracted. Principal component analysis-based feature selection identified a feature subset. Machine-learning and PPG-oriented deep-learning models were compared with conventional R-ratio calibration using mean absolute error (MAE), root mean squared error (RMSE), and the coefficient of determination (R2).Main results. The Extra Trees regressor achieved the lowest RMSE among evaluated models, with an MAE of 0.38 percentage points, an RMSE of 0.90 percentage points, and an R2 of 0.91. It outperformed conventional R-ratio calibration. In the hypoxemic range (70% ≤ SpO2 ≤ 90%), MAE was 0.98 percentage points, RMSE was 2.04 percentage points, and R2 was 0.66.

SIGNIFICANCE: Combining dual-wavelength PPG with multi-domain features and machine learning shows potential for wide-range SpO2 estimation and hypoxemic-risk assessment in COPD.

articles.title: Catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome after COVID-19 mRNA vaccination: A case report.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveAntiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a common acquired thromboinflammatory disease and catastrophic APS (CAPS) its most rare and lethal variant. The objective of this report is to describe a case of probable CAPS triggered after vaccination with an mRNA vaccine in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic.MethodsThis is a descriptive case report conducted at a Brazilian university hospital, involving a single 40-year-old patient admitted with dysarthria, gross hematuria, signs of pulmonary embolism, and a large intracavitary cardiac thrombus. He had a history of multiple past venous thrombotic events, but investigations for malignancy had consistently yielded negative results. Approximately 48 hours earlier, he had received the second dose of the Pfizer® mRNA vaccine (Pfizer-BioNTech BNT162b2).After infections and concomitant autoimmune diseases were ruled out, thrombocytopenia and positive serologic testing for APS raised the possibility of CAPS, and treatment was promptly initiated with anticoagulation, corticosteroids, low-dose aspirin, and hydroxychloroquine. Main outcome measures were organ involvement, laboratory abnormalities, imaging findings, and clinical response to treatment.ResultsAfter therapeutic measures were instituted, the patient showed laboratory improvement - restoration of renal function and increased platelet count - as well as clinical improvement, with resolution of neurological deficits. Follow-up testing revealed persistent triple positivity for APS-related serologies.ConclusionsThis emblematic report brings a rare complication of APS in association with immunization using an mRNA COVID-19 vaccine, presenting clinical features that resemble those described in other CAPS cases documented in the CAPS Registry. Additional reports of immune-mediated diseases induced by vaccine platforms have also been described, suggesting pathophysiological mechanisms that remain incompletely understood, particularly molecular mimicry. Immunization against COVID-19 and other pathogens should not, however, be discouraged, as vaccines continue to play a fundamental role in preventing potentially severe infectious diseases. Instead, scientific research should be encouraged in order to better understand which individuals are more predisposed to such a severe complication.

articles.title: Advanced heartworm disease in dogs is associated with marked right heart and pulmonary artery remodeling.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize echocardiographic findings of right heart and pulmonary artery remodeling in dogs with heartworm disease.

METHODS: Medical records were searched for those of client-owned dogs with heartworm infection diagnosed from July 2020 through February 2023 and with no major systemic diseases not attributable to heartworm infection. Results for variables of interest were compared for dogs grouped by heartworm clinical class (classes 1 and 2 [mild] vs classes 3 and 4 [advanced]), pulmonary hypertension probability (low and intermediate vs high), and tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient (mild, moderate, or severe). Pre- and postextraction variables were also compared for dogs with caval syndrome.

RESULTS: 44 dogs were included. Compared with dogs with mild heartworm disease (n = 23), dogs with advanced heartworm disease (21) had greater right atrial and right ventricular enlargement, less right pulmonary artery distensibility, shorter pulmonary artery acceleration time, higher main pulmonary artery-to-aorta ratio, and lower right ventricular systolic function. Similar results were identified for dogs with high (vs intermediate or low) pulmonary hypertension probability. Normalized right atrial diameter had the highest discriminatory performance for identifying advanced heartworm disease (area under the curve, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.88 to 1.00), followed by tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient, normalized right ventricular dimension, and other variables. Right atrial size significantly decreased after heartworm extraction (n = 8 dogs).

CONCLUSIONS: Advanced heartworm disease is associated with marked right heart and pulmonary artery remodeling.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Echocardiographic assessment of right heart remodeling may assist clinicians in evaluating heartworm disease severity and identifying dogs with clinically important cardiopulmonary involvement.

articles.title: Dynamic biomarkers of kidney function in patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma receiving daratumumab-based combination therapy.
Multipotent ability of the baseline C-reactive protein-to-serum Albumin Ratio (CAR) to assess current activity and predict subsequent complications of ANCA-associated vasculitis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To investigate the ability of the baseline C-reactive protein-to-serum Albumin Ratio (CAR) to assess current vasculitis activity and predict subsequent complications in patients with antineutrophil cytoplasmic Antibody-Associated Vasculitis (AAV).

METHODS: Data from the medical records of 319 patients with AAV were retrospectively reviewed. High activity was defined as the highest tertile of the Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score (BVAS). All-Cause Mortality (ACM), relapse, End-Stage Kidney Disease (ESKD), Cerebrovascular Accident (CVA), and Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) were evaluated as subsequent complications. ACM, ESKD, and CVA with significant Areas Under the Curve (AUC) in receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, were investigated.

RESULTS: The median age of the study subjects (64.6% females) was 60.0-years. Baseline CAR was independently correlated with current BVAS and yielded the numerically largest AUC for high activity. Patients with baseline CAR ≥ 3.07, ≥ 1.26, and ≥ 14.01 exhibited significantly higher Relative Risks (RR) for ACM (RR = 8.017), ESKD (RR = 3.270), and CVA (RR = 6.660) than those with baseline CAR < 3.07, < 1.26, and < 14.01, respectively. Additionally, patients with baseline CAR ≥ 3.07, ≥ 1.26, and ≥ 14.01 showed reduced cumulative patient, ESKD-free, and CVA-free survival rates compared with those with baseline CAR < 3.07, < 1.26, and < 14.01, respectively. Multivariable Cox proportional analysis revealed that baseline CAR and its complication-related cut-offs were independently associated with subsequent ACM, ESKD, and CVA, except for baseline CAR ≥ 1.26 for ESKD.

CONCLUSIONS: Baseline CAR demonstrated the multipotent ability to reflect current high activity (the highest tertile of BVAS) and predict subsequent ACM, ESKD, and CVA in patients with AAV.

articles.title: Accuracy of pulse oximetry to determine severe hypoxemia in COPD patients: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In moderate hypoxemia, Pulse Oximetry (SpO2) may indicate values above 90%, potentially underestimating severity in patients with COPD. This leads to the question of whether a similar discrepancy occurs in cases of severe hypoxemia. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of SpO2 for identifying severe resting hypoxemia defined by PaO2 ≤55 mmHg and to determine a clinically applicable SpO2 cutoff for screening patients with COPD undergoing evaluation for LTOT.

METHODS: Data were collected from medical records of patients attending a Long-Term Oxygen Therapy (LTOT) outpatient clinic. Severe hypoxemia was defined as PaO2 ≤55 mmHg. Agreement between SpO2 and co-oximetry (SaO2) was assessed following Bland and Altman recommendations. Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed using a PaO2 ≤ 55 mmHg cutoff to evaluate the accuracy of SpO2.

RESULTS: Between January 2022 and December 2025, 176 patients were included (65% female, mean age: 71-years [SD = 9] and PaO2: 57.4 mmHg [SD = 10.8]). Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of -0.43% (95% CI: -0.76 to -0.10) between SaO2 and SpO2, with 95% limits of agreement ranging from -4.77% to 3.90%. ROC curve analysis demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance of SpO2 for detecting severe hypoxemia, with an area under the curve of 0.939. The optimal statistical cutoff was 89.5%, corresponding to a clinically applicable threshold of SpO₂ ≤ 89%, and yielded a sensitivity of 88.5%, specificity of 87.8%, positive predictive value of 85.2%, and negative predictive value of 90.5%.

CONCLUSIONS: Pulse oximetry demonstrated excellent diagnostic accuracy for detecting severe hypoxemia in COPD outpatients. An SpO2 cutoff of ≤89% provided optimal sensitivity and specificity under standardized conditions.

articles.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Antimicrobial Stewardship Strategies in Residential Aged Care: An Umbrella Review.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To identify, appraise, and synthesize global evidence on the effectiveness of antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) interventions in residential aged care homes (RACHs).

DESIGN: An umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.

SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: Systematic review on AMS interventions for those aged 65 and above who resided in RACHs globally. Fifteen reviews (2013-2024) encompassing 66 unique primary studies were included. Six reviews featured meta-analyses.

METHODS: Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, searches across major databases, including Scopus and PubMed, were conducted. Study selection, data extraction, and quality appraisal were performed independently by 2 reviewers. AMS interventions were mapped against the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Core Elements of AMS for nursing homes. Quantitative and qualitative data were synthesized alongside available meta-analyses.

RESULTS: Multifaceted AMS strategies combining education, clinical guidelines, drug expertise, and audit and feedback were associated with reductions in antimicrobial consumption, infection rates, and urine culture requests. Long-term implementation (up to 60 months) showed decreased antimicrobial resistance among uropathogens. However, interventions demonstrated little to no impact on the appropriateness of antimicrobial selection, hospital admissions, or mortality. Cost-effectiveness data remained limited.

CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Multifaceted AMS interventions are effective in reducing antibiotic use and infection rates in RACHs. Facilities should implement multifaceted strategies, prioritizing education and clinical algorithms. In resource-limited settings, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention framework and the World Health Organization AWaRe book can be adaptively scaled using nurse-led champions to circumvent high costs. Future longitudinal studies must use standardized aged-care metrics, evaluate cost-effectiveness, and address global equity by investigating AMS models in low- and middle-income countries.

articles.title: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Tongue Pressure Resistance Feedback Training on Patients With Dysphagia.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of tongue pressure resistance feedback training (TPRFT) in patients with poststroke dysphagia (PSD) and to determine the most effective training protocol.

DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs).

SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: Adults aged ≥18 years with PSD confirmed by standardized clinical and/or instrumental assessment.

METHODS: Nine databases were searched from inception to December 2025 for RCTs in which TPRFT was the primary intervention. Study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment were conducted independently by 2 reviewers using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Meta-analysis was conducted using Review Manager 5.4 to calculate risk ratios (RRs) or mean differences with 95% CIs. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic.

RESULTS: A total of 16 studies involving 978 PSD patients were included. Compared with conventional swallowing rehabilitation, TPRFT significantly improved swallowing function (RR, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.14-1.32; I2 = 0%) and reduced complications (RR, 0.28; 95% CI, 0.14-0.54; I2 = 0%). In terms of functional outcomes, TPRFT also significantly reduced Standardized Swallowing Assessment scores and Penetration-Aspiration Scale scores, increased Swallowing Quality of Life Questionnaire scores, and increased maximum tongue pressure. Subgroup analysis indicated that moderate-to-low training intensity (≤70% of maximum tongue pressure), medium-term duration (4-8 weeks), and longer training protocols were associated with greater improvements in swallowing function and quality of life.

CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: TPRFT may be a promising intervention for improving swallowing function and reducing complications in patients with PSD. Current evidence supports a potentially beneficial training protocol of moderate-to-low intensity exercise sustained for at least 4 to 8 weeks. Further high-quality, multicenter RCTs are needed to optimize training parameters.

REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420251245245.

articles.title: Three profiles of death avoidance among PICU nurses: The protective role of interpersonal exchange and information competency.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Occupational death avoidance (ODA) is an understudied psychological and behavioral coping mechanism among PICU nurses that is associated with their well-being and the quality of end-of-life care. Despite its clinical importance, little is known about its heterogeneous manifestations and modifiable determinants.

AIM: This study aimed to identify distinct ODA profiles among PICU nurses and examine the associations of perceived interpersonal exchange (PIEC) and information competency (IC) with ODA.

STUDY DESIGN: A cross-sectional study was conducted with 542 PICU nurses from 15 tertiary hospitals across 13 regions in Hubei Province, China, between December 2024 and January 2025. Latent profile analysis (LPA) was used to identify ODA subgroups, and multivariate logistic regression was performed to examine influencing factors.

RESULTS: LPA revealed three distinct ODA profiles: low (36.34%), moderate (47.42%), and high (16.24%). Nurses with 6-10 years of PICU experience were significantly less likely to belong to the high ODA profile (OR = 0.301, p = 0.015). Higher levels of both perceived interpersonal exchange and information competency were significantly associated with lower levels of moderate and high ODA (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: ODA among PICU nurses is heterogeneous and associated with modifiable workplace factors. The findings highlight a critical resilience window at 6-10 years of experience. Strengthening team-based emotional support (PIEC) and end-of-life information competence (IC) may be promising approaches to support lower avoidance, improve nurse well-being, and enhance family-centered care for dying children. Future research should validate these findings across diverse pediatric settings. IMPACT STATEMENTS.

articles.title: Pediatric stroke, transient ischemic attack, and non-vascular mimics in the emergency department: a three-group analysis of clinical predictors and diagnostic performance.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric stroke is a diagnostic challenge due to the high prevalence of stroke mimics in the emergency setting. This study aimed to identify distinguishing clinical features among confirmed stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), and non-vascular mimics.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort enrolled patients aged 1 month-18 years with acute focal neurological deficits presenting to a tertiary pediatric emergency department. Patients were classified into three groups: confirmed stroke, TIA, and non-vascular mimics. Firth penalized logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis were performed for each pairwise comparison.

RESULTS: Of 103 patients, 25 (24.3%) had confirmed stroke, 24 (23.3%) TIA, and 54 (52.4%) non-vascular mimics. Stroke patients were younger than TIA (median 7.0 vs. 12.5 years; p = 0.002) and non-vascular mimic patients (7.0 vs. 11.0 years; p = 0.007). Symptom duration >48 h, focal seizures, and pathological reflexes were the strongest discriminators between stroke and TIA (all p < 0.05); pathological reflexes were absent in all non-vascular mimic patients. Chronic disease was more prevalent in stroke vs. TIA (48.0% vs. 16.7%; p = 0.032). Firth regression identified age (odds ratio [OR] 0.81; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.67-0.99; p = 0.036) and symptom duration >48 h (OR 11.12; 95% CI 1.86-66.34; p = 0.008) as independent distinguishing clinical features of stroke vs. TIA. Combined model area under the curve (AUC): 0.898 (stroke vs. TIA) and 0.731 (stroke vs. non-vascular mimics). Routine laboratory parameters did not differ across groups.

CONCLUSION: Age, symptom duration, focal seizures, and pathological reflexes are key discriminators of stroke from TIA. Discriminability is substantially higher when contrasting stroke with TIA (AUC 0.898) than with non-vascular mimics (AUC 0.731), underscoring the value of separating TIA in the analytical framework. Prompt neuroimaging with systematic clinical assessment remains essential for accurate diagnosis.

articles.title: Sleep and circadian research across critical care settings and populations, 2000-2025: a layered bibliometric and science-mapping analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We characterised the growth, composition and intellectual structure of sleep and circadian research across critical care settings and populations from 2000 to 2025, with particular attention to the representation and citation visibility of Nursing-category journals.

METHODS: Web of Science Core Collection Article and Review records retrieved on 1 August 2026 yielded 4760 after deduplication. A deterministic title/author-keyword rule gave a field-central corpus of 1047 nested in an abstract-inclusive corpus of 3588. Two authors independently assessed a 200-record stratified sample. Growth, annual Nursing-category share and citations were modelled using log-linear, binomial logistic and negative binomial regression, respectively. Reporting followed the preliminary guideline for reporting bibliometric reviews of the biomedical literature (BIBLIO).

RESULTS: The corpus held 859 Articles and 188 Reviews from 370 sources (29,660 citations; h-index 79), growing 15.30%/year (95% confidence interval [CI] 13.73-16.89). Nursing-category journals produced 21.2% of 2000-2024 records, with increasing annual odds (odds ratio [OR] 1.041, 95% CI 1.009-1.075; p = 0.013), but accounted for 13.3% of citations and 1 of the 46 most-cited records (2.2%). Median analysis did not detect a difference. Coupling of 84 highly cited documents yielded five multi-publication clusters with mean years from 2006.6 to 2016.6. Layer choice materially changed influential-publication rankings. Human validation yielded a positive predictive value (PPV) of 92.0% (95% CI 84.8-96.5%).

CONCLUSIONS: The field expanded substantially. Among highly cited publications, older clusters concerned sleep physiology and later clusters included interventions and guidance. Nursing-category journals were under-represented in the upper citation tail.

IMPLICATIONS FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE: The map can help critical care teams locate literature on sleep assessment, environmental modification and care clustering across patient, survivor and staff populations. Searches for sleep-related guidance should include Nursing-category and multidisciplinary critical-care journals.

articles.title: Advantages and Limitations of Minipigs in Cardiovascular Safety Pharmacology and Toxicology Studies in Drug Development.
articles.abstract: Minipigs are recognized as a relevant non-rodent species for nonclinical safety assessment in drug development, although their use remains considerably less common than that of dogs and non-human primates. Historically cited barriers to broader adoption have included increased test article requirements due to their larger size, limited historical control data, technical challenges, and limited experience with their use in nonclinical safety assessment. However, some of these limitations have been mitigated in recent years. While minipigs are most often used for dermally administered drugs due to similarities in skin structure, they are also considered a highly relevant model for cardiovascular research due to similarities in anatomy and physiology with the human cardiovascular system. In this review, we evaluate the advantages and limitations of using minipigs in nonclinical safety assessment for predicting human cardiovascular effects. We summarize current knowledge of porcine cardiovascular anatomy, electrophysiology, hemodynamics, and pharmacokinetics, and discuss how these parameters influence the translational relevance of the minipig model.

articles.title: Current Global Trends and Challenges of Pediatric Ventricular Assist Device Programs: An ACTION Collaborative Survey.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Ventricular assist devices (VADs) have become an established therapy for children with end-stage heart failure, yet multinational data describing pediatric VAD programs remain limited. We conducted a 12 question survey through the Advanced Cardiac Therapies Improving Outcomes Network (ACTION) involving 74 international healthcare professionals from pediatric VAD programs outside North America. The survey assessed device and resource availability, multidisciplinary team composition, program challenges, and future priorities. Fifteen responses representing 15 centers from 14 countries were received, including 13 centers with established pediatric VAD programs. Most centers (91%, 10/11) managed 1-5 pediatric VAD patients annually. Berlin Heart EXCOR and HeartMate 3 were available in 85% (11/13) of centers, while only 46.7% (7/15) had a dedicated VAD coordinator. Major barriers included inadequate education for intensive care unit (ICU) and nursing staff and patients (69%, 9/13), financial constraints (54%, 7/13), limited device availability (46%, 6/13), and lack of outpatient VAD experience, with 31% (4/13) of centers reporting no experience discharging patients on VAD support. Substantial variation in device availability, multidisciplinary resources, and program experience exists across regions. These findings highlight important gaps in pediatric VAD care and support international collaboration to improve education, infrastructure, and access to advanced heart failure therapies.

articles.title: Cardiac Output From Right Ventricular Pressure: Not the Solution for Venovenous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Cardiac output (CO) monitoring is challenging during venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV ECMO), as thermodilution techniques are unreliable. Cardiac output from right ventricular pressure (RVP) waveforms has recently been considered. We evaluated whether RVP-derived CO (CORV) accurately reflects cardiac output measured by echocardiography (COUS) during VV ECMO. Ten anesthetized pigs underwent femoro-jugular VV ECMO implantation. A Swan-Ganz IQ catheter provided continuous CORV monitoring throughout the experiment. Cardiac output was modulated using either dobutamine (5-20 µg/kg/min) or landiolol (10-40 µg/kg/min) infusions. Agreement between CORV and COUS was assessed using Pearson correlation and Bland-Altman analysis. Overall, 596 paired CO measurements were performed in seven animals. Cardiac output ranged from 1.05 to 9.46 L/min. Correlation between CORV and COUS was poor (R = 0.24; R2 = 0.057; p < 0.05). Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of +1.94 L/min with wide limits of agreement (-1.44 to +5.32 L/min). Correlations between individual right ventricular pressure waveform components and COUS were heterogeneous and weak to moderate (diastolic RVP, R = 0.36; right ventricle +dP/dt [delta pressure/delta time] R = 0.40; systolic RVP R = 0.60). CORV is not reliable during VV ECMO in our experiment. Further studies are needed to assess CORV performances.

articles.title: Evaluating an AI-Powered Patient Simulator for Communication Skills Training: One-Year Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical communication skills are a core yet complex competency in medical education and practice. However, early-stage medical students often struggle to apply communication frameworks in practice due to limited opportunities for structured simulation training. Generative AI (GenAI)-supported training has the potential to offer a scalable and innovative approach for clinical communication skills training.

OBJECTIVE: This study examined the longitudinal development of medical students' clinical communication skills over 1 academic year and investigated whether AI-powered simulation contributed to differential improvement relative to conventional training. In addition, the study explored motivational, behavioral, and affective mechanisms associated with communication skills development.

METHODS: A nonblinded randomized controlled design was used at a medical school in the United Kingdom, with students assigned either to the control group (n=28, 56%) or to the AI group (n=22, 44%), who practiced with SimPatient, a patient-simulator chatbot accessed through a web browser. Communication skills performance was assessed using standardized objective structured clinical examinations (OSCE) scores relative to the pass marks to enable comparison across time points. Paired t tests and difference-in-differences (DID) analyses were conducted between groups and over time to examine changes in communication skills. Latent change score modeling was used to identify predictors of communication skills change. Sentiment analysis was conducted on 6120 comments from AI-student conversations. Finally, a system quality survey was used to assess participants' feedback on the AI-powered simulator.

RESULTS: Latent change score modeling showed that gains in intrinsic motivation and behavioral learning were significant predictors of students' communication skills change. The AI group showed a greater descriptive increase in communication skills than the control group, yet the between-group difference was not statistically significant. Within the AI group, consultations whose lexical tone trended more strongly toward resolution (consultation tone) were descriptively associated with communication skills improvement; given the small subsample (n=17), this finding is reported as exploratory. The AI group's confidence level in AI use was negatively associated with communication skills improvement, while the group nevertheless reported a generally high level of satisfaction with the system.

CONCLUSIONS: In this study, medical students' clinical communication skills increased over the academic year, with this development most strongly associated with their motivation and behavioral engagement; the AI-supported group did not differ significantly from conventional training. The simulator responded appropriately and provided a usable environment for practicing foundational communication behaviors but was limited in capturing the affective complexity, vulnerability, and narrative unpredictability of real clinical encounters. In conclusion, this study suggests that GenAI holds promise for supporting foundational clinical communication training and providing positive practice environments, thereby fostering motivation and behavioral engagement.

articles.title: BioDecryptors, a Bioinformatics Escape Game for Undergraduate and Postgraduate Learners in Clinical Microbiology: Prospective Before-and-After Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bioinformatics is increasingly important in clinical microbiology with growing use of genomic sequencing, metagenomics, and phylogenetic analyses. However, introducing bioinformatics concepts and tools to medical learners can be challenging. Gamified educational approaches may allow introducing these concepts while supporting learner motivation.

OBJECTIVE: This study prospectively evaluated BioDecryptors, an educational escape game to introduce bioinformatics principles and tools in clinical microbiology, by assessing short-term changes in knowledge and self-reported motivation and evaluating participant satisfaction.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective before-and-after study between January and September 2025. Volunteers were recruited from undergraduate medical programs at Université Paris Cité and postgraduate programs or training activities for MDs and PharmDs at Université de Nantes, Université Paris-Saclay, and the French Society for Microbiology. Overall, 55 participants were included: 22 (40%) second-year medical students and 33 (60%) postgraduate MDs or PharmDs. Participants completed BioDecryptors in teams of 3 to 4 using versions adapted to their training level. Knowledge was assessed before and immediately after the activity using 2 distinct 10-item tests assessing the same predefined learning objectives. Motivation was assessed using a 12-item, 5-point Likert questionnaire covering 3 predefined domains, and satisfaction was assessed after the activity. Pre-post knowledge scores were compared using paired t tests or Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, as appropriate. Motivation items were analyzed using paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Statistical significance was defined as a 2-sided P<.05.

RESULTS: Paired knowledge assessments were available for 50 participants. Mean knowledge scores increased from 7.0 (SD 2.0; 95% CI 6.4-7.5) before the activity to 7.9 (SD 2.0; 95% CI 7.4-8.5) afterward (P<.001). The mean change was 0.93 (SD 1.39; 95% CI 0.26-1.60) points among undergraduates and 0.83 (SD 1.21; 95% CI 0.38-1.27) points among postgraduates, with no statistically significant between-group difference (P=.79). Motivation increased for perceived usefulness (P=.04), willingness to learn (P=.01), understanding of bioinformatics in diseases (P=.002), and confidence in bioinformatics abilities (P=.002). Curiosity (P=.46) and interest in real-life applications (P=.33) did not significantly change. Among 50 satisfaction respondents, overall satisfaction was high (mean 4.7, SD 0.5; 95% CI 4.6-4.9); 98% (48/49) of the respondents to the corresponding item indicated an interest in other escape game modules.

CONCLUSIONS: Participation in BioDecryptors was associated with short-term increases in bioinformatics knowledge and self-reported motivation, together with high participant satisfaction. Unlike previously reported escape games focusing primarily on clinical or infection-control topics, BioDecryptors integrates hands-on bioinformatics analyses into a clinical microbiology scenario and offers versions adapted to undergraduate and postgraduate learners. Our findings provide preliminary evidence supporting the feasibility and acceptability of this approach as a complementary educational resource for introducing bioinformatics in health professions training. Controlled studies with longer-term assessments are needed to establish its comparative educational effectiveness and knowledge retention.

articles.title: Assessing the Quality of AI Explanations of Atrial Fibrillation: Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT and Google Gemini.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is one of the most common arrhythmias and is associated with multiple risk factors, including stroke and heart failure. Therefore, it is important that accurate and comprehensive educational resources on AF are available. Artificial intelligence (AI) platforms such as Google Gemini and ChatGPT are emerging tools for medical education. To our knowledge, this is the first study to assess the quality of these platforms for AF education.

OBJECTIVE: This pilot study aimed to (1) assess the quality of ChatGPT and Google Gemini explanations of AF and its treatment, (2) compare responses from both platforms, and (3) analyze differences in interpretation between cardiologists and nonmedical professionals.

METHODS: The prompt "Explain atrial fibrillation and how to treat it to a patient" was entered into both ChatGPT and Google Gemini. The responses, along with a survey created in Google Forms, were sent out to potential participants between September and October 2024. The survey questions were derived from the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials and DISCERN criteria. Each survey question was multiple choice and rated on a 5-point Likert scale, where 1 indicated strong disagreement and 5 indicated strong agreement. Averages of each answer from the survey were calculated and compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.

RESULTS: The survey was completed by 28 participants, including cardiologists and cardiology fellows and 17 nonmedical professionals (college graduates not employed in the medical field). No significant overall quality differences were observed between ChatGPT and Google Gemini. When comparing participant groups, cardiologists rated AI-generated responses higher than nonmedical professionals for perceived bias (mean 3.82 vs mean 4.33; P=.04) and for explaining consequences of no treatment (mean 2.85 vs mean 1.86; P=.005). In contrast, nonmedical professionals rated structural and organizational features more favorably than cardiologists, including visual cues (mean 3.97 vs mean 2.48; P<.001), informative headers (mean 4.77 vs mean 3.95; P=.001), concise sections (mean 4.71 vs mean 4.29; P=.04), identifiable patient actions (mean 4.21 vs mean 3.19; P=.04), and references to additional resources (mean 2.65 vs mean 1.71; P=.006).

CONCLUSIONS: The comparable quality of ChatGPT and Google Gemini suggests that both are viable for AF education. Differences in ratings of organizational features versus perceptions of bias and consequences of no treatment highlight a disconnect between cardiologists and nonmedical professionals. To optimize clinical application, cardiologists should evaluate both comprehensiveness and clarity of AI-generated responses. This serves as a pilot study, and future research should focus on longitudinal studies of AI-generated responses and their effects on clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Miscarriage Risk Prediction for Women With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome Who Achieve Clinical Pregnancy After Fresh Embryo Transfer: Multicenter Development, Geographic External Validation, and Prospective Temporal Validation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) who achieve clinical pregnancy following fresh in vitro fertilization (IVF)/intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) carry an elevated miscarriage risk. However, individualized risk stratification after clinical pregnancy confirmation but before outcome determination remains challenging in clinical practice.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop, externally and prospectively validate over time, and interpret a machine learning-based risk stratification model for women with PCOS who had achieved a confirmed clinical pregnancy after fresh IVF/ICSI.

METHODS: This multicenter study included 8911 clinical pregnancy IVF/ICSI cycles across development (n=7241; miscarriages: n=973), external validation (n=1170; miscarriages: n=146), and prospective temporal validation (n=500; miscarriages: n=62) cohorts. Prespecified predictors contained no observed missing values; training-fold median imputation was kept only as a leakage-safe fallback. A total of 13 candidate machine learning and traditional statistical algorithms were compared internally using repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation (5 repeats) within the development cohort; preprocessing and hyperparameter tuning were performed exclusively in training folds. A prelocked Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model was carried forward unchanged for external and prospective temporal validation. Cross-fitted logistic recalibration of averaged XGBoost out-of-fold probabilities was evaluated as a secondary development-sample diagnostic analysis. Model performance encompassed discrimination, precision-recall, calibration, threshold-based metrics, decision curve analysis, risk stratification, and Shapley additive explanations-based interpretability.

RESULTS: Miscarriage rates were 13.4% (973/7241), 12.5% (146/1170), and 12.4% (62/500) for the development, external validation, and prospective temporal validation cohorts, respectively. In repeated cross-validation, XGBoost (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] 0.885, 95% CI 0.874-0.896) and LightGBM (AUC 0.882, 95% CI 0.871-0.893) showed comparable discrimination; the paired XGBoost-LightGBM DeLong test was not significant (Holm-adjusted P=.07). Raw XGBoost out-of-fold probabilities overestimated absolute risk (mean predicted risk 30.3% vs observed risk 13.4%); cross-fitted recalibration within the development cohort improved calibration but was not propagated to validation cohorts. The locked XGBoost model achieved AUCs of 0.787 (95% CI 0.748-0.827; Brier score 0.099) in external validation and 0.763 (95% CI 0.709-0.816; Brier score 0.104) in prospective temporal validation, showing cross-cohort performance attenuation. Risk-quartile stratification using fixed development-cohort cutoffs showed consistent event enrichment across validation cohorts, but positive predictive values remained modest. Shapley additive explanations analysis identified anti-Müllerian hormone, endometrial thickness on the day of human chorionic gonadotropin administration, and basal luteinizing hormone as leading predictors.

CONCLUSIONS: The locked XGBoost model using routine preoutcome variables may support miscarriage risk stratification and counseling for women with PCOS with clinical pregnancy after fresh IVF/ICSI. Given cross-cohort discrimination loss and calibration drift, it should serve only as a risk-ranking tool, not for diagnosis or treatment selection. Local calibration monitoring is mandatory before any real-world clinical deployment.

articles.title: Effects of Lactobacillus crispatus-Containing Probiotics and Metformin on Insulin Resistance, Inflammation, and Gut Microbiome in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: Protocol for an Open-Label Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) affects 9% to 12% of reproductive-age women worldwide, with higher prevalence reported in India. Its pathophysiology involves insulin resistance, hyperandrogenism, and chronic low-grade inflammation, increasingly linked to gut dysbiosis and lipopolysaccharide-driven toll-like receptor 4 signaling. Elevated calprotectin and suppressed acylated ghrelin (AGH) reflect this inflammatory-metabolic disruption. While metformin remains standard therapy, it does not address underlying gut dysbiosis. Lactobacillus crispatus, with its antibacterial and immunomodulatory properties, is a promising but untested gut-targeted adjunct. This trial evaluates whether combining metformin with L. crispatus supplementation improves metabolic and inflammatory outcomes beyond either therapy alone.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to compare probiotic, metformin, and combination therapy for reducing insulin resistance in PCOS over 12 weeks and assess their effects on gut barrier integrity, microbiome composition, hyperandrogenemia, glycemic control, and clinical outcomes.

METHODS: This open-label randomized, hospital-based trial at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Bhubaneswar, will assess the effects of probiotic and/or metformin therapy in women aged 18 to 40 years diagnosed with PCOS per Rotterdam criteria. A total of 135 participants will be randomized equally into 3 groups: probiotics only, metformin only, and combination therapy. The 3-month intervention includes metformin (1000 mg per day) and a specified L. crispatus-containing probiotic (2 capsules per day). The primary outcome is the change in Homeostatic Model Assessment for Insulin Resistance (HOMA-IR). Key secondary outcomes include changes in serum and fecal calprotectin, AGH, total testosterone, and fecal microbiome profile.

RESULTS: Participant recruitment began in January 2026. As of August 30, 2026, 26 of the planned 135 participants had been enrolled. Enrollment and data collection are projected to conclude by December 2026; statistical analysis will begin after database lock, with study completion anticipated by June 2027 and publication targeted for mid- to late 2027.

CONCLUSIONS: This trial will provide critical, mechanistic evidence on whether the targeted action of L. crispatus can work additively with metformin to heal the intestinal mucosal barrier, arrest systemic endotoxemia, and rescue disrupted gut-brain-endocrine signaling. By validating this novel metabolic-inflammatory regimen against localized (calprotectin) and systemic (AGH and HOMA-IR) end points, this study intends to establish a highly integrated, microbiome-targeted therapeutic strategy capable of optimizing long-term metabolic and reproductive health outcomes in women with PCOS.

articles.title: Digital Health Technologies for Mobility Recovery Among Intensive Care Unit Survivors: Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mobility recovery after critical illness is a complex and multidimensional process. Digital health technologies have emerged as approaches for delivering rehabilitation, monitoring recovery, and facilitating self-management among intensive care unit (ICU) survivors. However, the extent to which current digital health approaches address the multidimensional nature of mobility recovery remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: This scoping review aimed to map the current evidence on digital health approaches supporting mobility recovery among ICU survivors and to examine the mobility domains, outcomes, feasibility, and acceptability associated with these approaches.

METHODS: A scoping review was conducted following the Arksey and O'Malley framework and was reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies published from January 2016 to September 21, 2026. Studies involving adult ICU survivors that used digital health approaches to assess, monitor, support, or promote mobility recovery were included. Mobility outcomes were mapped to the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health domains of body functions and structures, activities, and participation. Clinical outcomes were synthesized separately from implementation and user experience outcomes.

RESULTS: Twenty-seven reports representing 24 unique parent studies were included. Digital health approaches comprised telemedicine, telerehabilitation, mobile health, wearable monitoring, virtual reality, robot-assisted rehabilitation, and digital recovery platforms. Telemedicine and telerehabilitation were the most frequently reported approaches, and exercise-based rehabilitation was the predominant intervention component. Mobility outcomes were heterogeneous and concentrated on body functions and structures and activity-level performance, particularly muscle strength, exercise capacity, and functional performance, whereas participation outcomes were less frequently represented. Controlled and comparative studies showed mixed between-group findings, with clinical benefits not consistently demonstrated across primary or mobility-related outcomes. In contrast, feasibility, adherence, usability, and acceptability were generally favorable when assessed, although technical difficulties and incomplete device-generated data were reported in some studies.

CONCLUSIONS: Digital health technologies offer diverse approaches to supporting mobility recovery after critical illness, but current evidence remains concentrated on physical function and activity-level outcomes, with limited attention to participation and long-term recovery. More rigorous and longitudinal studies using standardized, multidimensional mobility outcomes are needed to clarify clinical effectiveness and support sustainable implementation.

articles.title: Factors influencing post-diarrhea growth patterns among children under two years old in rural Bangladesh.
articles.abstract: Undernutrition in children is a major global health issue. Diarrhea exacerbates undernutrition, creating a vicious cycle of infection and malnutrition. This longitudinal study examined growth patterns and influencing factors among 138 children following diarrhea. Children under two seeking care for watery diarrhea at a rural hospital in Bangladesh were enrolled and followed for three months of home-based visits. Anthropometric measurements-length-for-age z-score (LAZ), weight-for-age z-score (WAZ), weight-for-length z-score (WLZ), and mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) were taken at enrollment and follow-ups. Linear mixed-effects models assessed associations of clinical, sociodemographic, sanitation, hygiene, and food security factors with growth outcomes. Overall, LAZ declined over three months (-0.260, SD: 0.408), while WAZ, WLZ, and MUAC improved (0.100, SD: 0.484; 0.249, SD: 0.725; 0.672 cm, SD: 0.476). Children with malnutrition at enrollment strongly predicted persistent malnutrition (LAZ < -2, WAZ < -2, WLZ < -2, MUAC < 12.5 cm) during follow-up compared to new incidence of malnutrition (RR: 3.8, p < 0.001, 95% CI: 1.80, 6.35). Poor growth outcomes were linked to longer diarrhea duration, more vomiting, and hospitalization. Hospitalization was associated with declines in LAZ (-0.095, p = 0.009) and MUAC (-0.098, p = 0.030). Children aged 7-12 months had greater declines in WAZ (-0.109, p = 0.096) and WLZ (-0.181, p = 0.113). Improved sanitation and hygiene supported growth, while household hunger was linked to declines. This study highlights the multifactorial nature of post-diarrhea growth outcomes and emphasizes the need for integrated interventions addressing clinical care, sanitation, hygiene, and food security.

articles.title: Extubation Failure in Pediatric Critical Care: A Secondary Analysis of the 2018-2019 Sedation and Weaning in Children (SandWiCh) Trial.
articles.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Extubation failure is defined as requirement for emergency reintubation within 48 hours of extubation. We aimed to examine the rate of extubation failure in a large U.K. dataset, including an examination of the prevalence of postextubation stridor, and to determine which patient factors were associated with failure.

DESIGN: A post hoc, non-prespecified secondary analysis of the 2018-2019 Sedation and Weaning in Children clinical (SandWiCh) cluster-randomized trial (ISRCTN16998143) dataset.

SETTING: The SandWiCh trial recruited patients from 18 U.K. PICUs.

PATIENTS: All patients with data for a planned extubation were included and patients who had an unplanned extubation, or who died following their first extubation without being reintubated were excluded.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Data for 9215 patients in the trial with at least one planned extubation attempt were available for analysis. The factors associated with for extubation failure being examined included age, diagnostic group, severity of illness at PICU admission, and duration of mechanical ventilation before extubation. Extubation failure occurred following first planned extubation in 618 of 9215 (6.7%). On multivariable analysis, Pediatric Index of Mortality (PIM-3) score and duration of ventilation before extubation attempt were associated with greater odds of extubation failure. Of the entire cohort, 874 children (9.4%) had postextubation stridor, but this figure rose to 173 of 618 patients (28%) who had extubation failure.

CONCLUSIONS: In the 2018-2019 SandWiCh dataset from the United Kingdom, failed extubation rate was comparable to other published cohorts. Greater odds of failed extubation was associated with increased PIM-3 score and duration of mechanical ventilation before attempted extubation. Stridor was present in a quarter of patients with extubation failure.

articles.title: PIEZO1 activation alters membrane remodeling and aggregability of stored red blood cells.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transfused red blood cells (RBCs) actively contribute to post-injury hemostasis due to surface phosphatidylserine (PS) exposure. We hypothesized that storage sensitizes erythrocytes to the PIEZO1-induced, calcium‑dependent, PS externalization through calcium and protein kinase C (PKC) dependent activation of the phospholipid scramblase TMEM16F.

METHODS: Five units of type O whole blood were obtained for analysis at days 21 and 42 of storage. RBC PS was quantified by annexin V staining on flow cytometry at increasing extracellular CaCl₂ concentrations (0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, and 5.0 mmol/L), with and without the PIEZO1 agonist Yoda1 (0.2 μM), PKC agonist Phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA; 6 μM) and antagonist chelerythrine chloride (CC; 10 μM), and the TMEM16 family inhibitor niclosamide (2 μM). RBC aggregometry was assessed by multiplate. Data were analyzed by analysis of variance and mixed-effects modeling.

RESULTS: PS exposure increased in a Ca²⁺‑dependent manner in both day 21 and 42 RBCs (p<0.001).
