PIEZO1 stimulation enhanced this response to a greater extent in day 42 RBCs, with greater change in PS at 1 mmol/L (2.21% vs. -0.44%, p=0.021), 2 mmol/L (7.36% vs. 0.53%, p<0.001), and 5 mmol/L (12.09% vs. 6.40%, p<0.001) CaCl2. Compared with calcium alone, Yoda1 and PMA (+61.3%, p<0.001 for both) produced similar increases in PS externalization, whereas PKC inhibition (-45.6%, p=0.009) and TMEM16F inhibition (-4.6%, p=0.99) negated the PIEZO1 response. Yoda1 agonism preserved RBC aggregability after 42 days of storage (51.2±39.0 vs. 2.0±3.5 area under the curve, p<0.001).

CONCLUSION: Storage sensitizes RBCs to PIEZO1-mediated, calcium-dependent, PS externalization through PKC- and TMEM16F-dependent signaling. Given its endogenous mechanosensitive properties, pharmacologic PIEZO1 activation highlights a potential mechanism by which mechanical stress encountered during trauma and transfusion through the injured microcirculation may promote erythrocyte phospholipid membrane remodeling and aggregability, contributing to the procoagulant activity of transfused RBCs.

articles.title: Propofol Infusion in a Mixed PICU: Prevalence of Propofol-Related Infusion Syndrome in a Retrospective Cohort, 2019-2022.
articles.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe usage and complications of propofol as a sedative agent in patients younger than 16 years old admitted to a PICU and to identify evidence of propofol-related infusion syndrome (PRIS).

DESIGN: Retrospective analysis of routinely collected data with comparison between patients receiving propofol for less than 48 hours compared with greater than or equal to 48 hours.

SETTING: Single-center mixed PICU in London, United Kingdom.

PATIENTS: All patients admitted to the PICU, from November 2019 to November 2022, younger than 16 years old, in whom an infusion of propofol was administered.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Propofol infusion was used in 1595 patients, 337 of whom had infusions of greater than or equal to 48 hours with a maximum dose of 5 mg/kg/hr and for a maximum duration of 45 days. The cohort age ranged from 1 day to 16 years and included patients with cardiac diagnoses. Patients were administered propofol for a median 76% of their ventilation time, and 26% of patients who were treated with propofol were also treated with noradrenaline. Physiologic variables, blood gases, laboratory values, and discharge summaries were reviewed, and no patients were clinically suspected of having PRIS. Variables previously reported in PRIS were analyzed across each patient's admission, and we failed to identify an association between abnormal physiologic values and receipt of a propofol infusion or whether duration of propofol infusion was greater than or equal to 48 hours. Hence, the upper limit of the 95% CI for 0 of 1595 gives a PRIS prevalence in our population up to 0.19%.

CONCLUSIONS: In our single-center, mixed PICU experience during 2019-2022, we have used propofol infusion in children younger than 16 years old. This practice included neonates and children with cardiac pathology. We failed to identify any episodes of clinically suspected PRIS in 1595 patients, including in the group treated for greater than or equal to 48 hours, which gives an upper limit for PRIS prevalence of ~0.19%.

articles.title: Impact of COVID-19 Infection and Vaccination on Herpes Zoster Ophthalmicus: A Prospective Analysis From the Zoster Eye Disease Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to assess the interplay between 2 important viral infections and their management, herpes zoster ophthalmicus (HZO) and COVID-19.

METHODS: A subanalysis from the Zoster Eye Disease Study, a prospective randomized controlled study examining prophylactic valacyclovir in HZO, and data collected on COVID-19 vaccination and infection from July 2020 were evaluated. Participants were included if enrolled from January 1, 2019, ensuring that their 18-month follow-up overlapped with the COVID-19 pandemic. Recurrence was defined as new or worsening stromal keratitis without ulceration, endothelial keratitis, iritis, dendritiform epithelial keratitis, or stromal keratitis with ulceration requiring a substantial increase or recommencement of topical steroid therapy.

RESULTS: A total of 402 participants were included in the analysis. Attenuated zoster vaccination live was given to 35 (8.7%) and recombinant zoster vaccine to 40 (10.0%) before study commencement. No difference was observed in incidence or severity of COVID-19 infection in those with previous zoster vaccination, and no difference was observed in those treated with valacyclovir prophylaxis. COVID-19 infection occurred in 71 participants (17.7%) during the study period, and COVID-19 vaccination was received by 170 participants (42.3%). No association was observed between HZO recurrence and COVID-19 infection (P = 0.39) or vaccination (P = 0.75) during the 18-month follow-up. The study was powered to detect a hazard ratio of 1.19 for COVID-19 infection or vaccine-associated recurrence.

CONCLUSIONS: No significant association was observed between zoster vaccination or valacyclovir use and COVID-19 incidence or severity. In addition, no significant increase in HZO recurrence was observed following COVID-19 infection or vaccination.

articles.title: A Retrospective Study on the Evolution of Complex Chronic Conditions Over a Decade in a Large Swiss Tertiary PICU.
articles.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine, over a 10-year period, changes in the prevalence of complex chronic conditions (CCCs) and in the distribution of underlying chronic health categories within a large Swiss PICU, and to compare patient characteristics and PICU mortality between children with CCCs and those without.

DESIGN: Single-center retrospective observational study of two cohorts (2007 vs. 2017).

SETTING: Large academic tertiary referral PICU.

PATIENTS: Overall, 1867 children were included (0-16 years old): 981 admitted between January 1, 2007, and December 31, 2007, and 886 admitted between January 1, 2017, and December 31, 2017.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The prevalence of children with CCCs increased from 61% in 2007 to 70% in 2017. The most common conditions were cardiovascular (55% in 2007 vs. 52% in 2017), congenital/genetic defects (36% vs. 38%), and neurologic/neuromuscular (25% vs. 34%). The proportion of children with 3 or more chronic conditions rose from 16% to 25%. Children with CCCs had longer PICU stays than children without, with length of stay increasing significantly with the number of CCCs. Most children who died during the two study periods had a chronic condition (2007: 61%; 2017: 66%), with a significant increase in the proportion of deaths following intensive care treatment withdrawal (8% in 2007 vs. 48% in 2017).

CONCLUSIONS: Over a decade, the proportion of children with CCCs needing PICU care has grown, with trends toward increasing prevalence in the clinically dominant categories of respiratory and hematology, immunodeficiency, and immunology, and the subcategories respiratory malformations, hereditary hemostasis anomalies, and home ventilation, and trends toward higher mortality rates following treatment withdrawal.

articles.title: Toward a Better Understanding of Patient Selection for Thrombectomy in Patients With Large Ischemic Core.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The benefit of thrombectomy in general for patients with large core strokes has been established across multiple trials, although inclusion criteria for the procedure seem quite broad across heterogeneous groups. Understanding subgroups that benefit optimally vs those in which thrombectomy may fall in the realm of futility is lacking.

METHODS: A prospectively maintained database was queried for thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke with Alberta Stroke Program Early Computed Tomography Score of ≤5 from 2021 to 2025. Study outcomes at 90 days included functional independence (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-2), independent ambulation (mRS 0-3), and mortality. Stratified results classified patients into potential categories, based on probability curves and heatmaps across age, last-known-well (LKW), and National Institute of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score. Impact of the category was adjusted in logistic regression models.

RESULTS: Of 1458 patients who underwent thrombectomy, 80 (5.5%) were for acute ischemic stroke of Alberta Stroke Program Early Computed Tomography Score ≤5, with a modified Treatment in Cerebral Infarction ≥2b in 89%. The symptomatic hemorrhage rate was 6.3%. At 90 days, 10% of patients were mRS 0 to 2, 30% mRS 0 to 3, and mortality was 34%. Patients were classified into 3 categories. Category 1 (57% of cases) were aged 75 years and younger with NIHSS <20 or LKW ≤12 hours. Ninety days after thrombectomy, 18% of these patients were mRS 0 to 2, 47% mRS 0% to 3%, and 18% died. Category 2 (27% of cases) were aged 75 years and younger with NIHSS ≥20 and LKW >12 hours, or older than 75 with LKW ≤12 hours. There was a 0% mRS 0 to 2 rate in this subgroup; 14% were mRS 3%, and 52% died. Category 3 patients (16% of patients) were aged older than 75 years with LKW >12 hours. No patient was mRS 0 to 3 at follow-up, and 62% had died. A higher risk category was associated with a decreased probability of mRS 0 to 3 (adjusted odds ratio 0.14, P = .01) and higher mortality (adjusted odds ratio 2.7, P = .03) in multiple regression models.

CONCLUSION: Patient age, presenting NIHSS and last known well time are significant determinants of outcome after thrombectomy for patients with large core stroke.

articles.title: Verticillium dahliae CAP-containing effectors hijack the β-subunit of the SnRK1 complex to suppress plant immunity.
articles.abstract: The soil-borne fungus Verticillium dahliae causes Verticillium wilt, a devastating disease threatening global cotton production. Like many pathogens, V. dahliae delivers effectors into plant cells to facilitate infection. The CAP (Cysteine-rich secretory protein, Antigen 5 and Pathogenesis-related protein 1) superfamily represents a typical group of secretory proteins that function as virulence factors and modulate plant immunity. Although V. dahliae utilizes CAP proteins to disrupt plant immune responses, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we initially screened the targets of VdCAP1 in cotton and demonstrated that it interacts with the β-subunit of SnRK1 complex both in vivo and in vitro. Silencing GhSnRK1β1 significantly enhanced susceptibility to V. dahliae infection, indicating its positive role in cotton defense against the pathogen. Further investigation revealed that VdCAP1 disrupts the interaction between SnRK1β1 and the core α-subunit of the SnRK1 complex and reduces the nuclear accumulation of GhSnRK1β1. Notably, GhSnRK1β1 exhibits opposing roles depending on its subcellular localization. Nuclear-localized GhSnRK1β1 promotes flg22-triggered ROS accumulation, whereas cytoplasmic-localized GhSnRK1β1 suppresses ROS accumulation. Furthermore, co-expression of VdCAP1 also promotes GhSnRK1β1-mediated ROS scavenging. Another secretory protein, VdCAP3, which functions as a plant immunity suppressor, interacts with GhSnRK1β1 and similarly restricts its nuclear accumulation to suppress plant immunity. Collectively, these findings indicated that VdCAP1/3 suppresses plant immunity by targeting SnRK1β1, thereby increasing V. dahliae pathogenicity.

articles.title: Fluid-Refractory Septic Shock in Children and Milrinone: Outcomes in a Two-Center, Retrospective Cohort in France, 2011-2021.
articles.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We have examined the associated outcomes of milrinone treatment for fluid-refractory septic shock.

DESIGN: Two-center, retrospective cohort from France.

SETTING: Two PICUs, both within tertiary care teaching hospitals.

PATIENTS: Children of 1 month to 18 years hospitalized between May 2011 and April 2021 with an episode of fluid-refractory septic shock treated with at least one vasoactive or inotropic agent.

INTERVENTION: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: We compared survival and PICU outcomes (organ support, length of stay) between patients who received milrinone and those who did not. We compared adverse events in the two groups, and we described the frequency and dosing of milrinone. We identified 290 patients with fluid-refractory septic shock with a median (interquartile range [IQR]) age of 48 months (IQR, 13-148 mo), of whom 46 of 290 (16%) received milrinone, with a median dose of 0.5 µg kg-1 min-1 (IQR, 0.5-0.8 µg kg-1 min-1). Overall mortality was 55 of 290 (19%). Use of milrinone was associated with a greater hazard (hazard ratio [HR], and 95% CI) of 30-day mortality (HR, 2.57 [95% CI, 1.15-5.75]; p = 0.021). Receiving milrinone, as opposed to not, was associated with greater volume of fluid boluses per case (16.8 [IQR, 0-50] vs. 10 [IQR, 0-29] mL kg-1; p = 0.04) and greater proportion undergoing mechanical ventilation (41/46 vs. 174/244; mean percentage difference, 17.8% [95% CI, 4.5-26.4%]; p = 0.011). Milrinone grouping, as opposed to not, was associated with greater proportion having cardiac arrests in the PICU (22/46 vs. 28/244; mean percentage difference, 36.3% [95% CI, 21.8-50.7%]; p < 0.001) and greater proportion with adverse events (17/46 vs. 24/244; mean percentage difference, 27.1% [95% CI, 13.9-41.9%]; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: In our 2011-2021 cohort of children, milrinone was used in around one-in-six cases with fluid-refractory septic shock. Patients treated with milrinone had an associated greater hazard of mortality; and, proportionately, worse PICU outcomes, and greater adverse events.

articles.title: Biological Sex as a Determinant of Neurological Outcomes During Zika Virus Infection.
articles.abstract: Biological sex is a significant determinant of host responses and disease outcomes during viral infection. Although males often exhibit more robust pathological inflammatory responses, the implications for immune responses within the central nervous system remain unclear. Given that many viral infections can lead to long-term neurological complications, it is crucial to understand how biological sex influences neuroinflammation. Using a mouse model of Zika virus infection, we find that males develop more severe clinical disease compared to females, despite comparable infectious viral loads. Our findings demonstrate that sexually dimorphic immune responses contribute to increased male susceptibility to virus-induced neuropathology.

articles.title: Tear Molecular Signatures and the Global Consensus on Keratoconus and Ectatic Diseases-Edition 2.
Exploring Syndemics in Older People Through a Gendered Lens: A Cross-Sectional Study using Linked Healthcare, Societal, and Health Monitor Data.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Sex differences in health condition clustering are often explored biologically, overlooking how gendered lives shape these patterns. We examine the role of gender in syndemics to understand health disparities in older people, where multimorbidity is more common and gendered life impacts shape health.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study using linked data (n=4,689) from Dutch general practitioners, the Health Monitor, and Statistics Netherlands for individuals aged ≥65. Health condition combinations were examined by sex, with additive and multiplicative interactions on healthcare utilization assessed using regression. A gender index capturing roles, relations, and institutionalized factors was developed. Univariable regression assessed associations of sex and gender index with excess healthcare utilization within health condition combinations; multivariable analyses evaluated whether sex differences persisted after adjusting for gender index.

RESULTS: Sex-specific health condition combinations emerged: cardiovascular-hypertension predominated in males (11.7%), hypertension-musculoskeletal predominated in females (13.2%). Several combinations showed interactions indicating adverse effects on healthcare utilization. Gender index was associated with higher healthcare utilization; sex was rarely significant. In the hypertension-diabetes combination-the only case with a univariate sex effect-the sex effect disappeared in multivariable models where the gender index remained significant (OR=4.74, 95%CI 1.22-19.62).

CONCLUSION: This study shows that syndemics in older people are shaped not only by sex but also by gendered lives involving caregiving roles, economic patterns, and institutional structures. Recognizing gender as a dynamic factor reveals hidden disparities, underscoring the need for gender‑informed research and policy to improve equity and inclusivity in healthcare systems.

articles.title: Long-Term Mortality in Sepsis Survivors: A Population-Based Study During 15 Years.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate long-term mortality among sepsis survivors in Catalonia over a 15-year period and to identify factors associated with increased mortality within 2 years after hospital discharge.

DESIGN: Retrospective population-based cohort study.

SETTING: Acute-care hospitals in Catalonia, Spain.

PATIENTS: Adult and pediatric patients hospitalized with sepsis between 2005 and 2019 identified using the International Classification of Diseases, 9th Revision, Clinical Modification and International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Clinical Modification codes for infection and acute organ dysfunction. Patients who died during hospitalization, were transferred to another facility, or represented readmission episodes were excluded.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Data were obtained from the Catalan Minimum Basic Dataset of Acute-Care Hospitals, with longitudinal follow-up through the Central Registry of Insured Persons. Comorbidities were assessed using the Charlson comorbidity index. Logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify predictors of long-term mortality. Among 296,554 hospital admissions for sepsis, 237,075 patients (79.9%) survived to hospital discharge. Of these, 42% died (99,571) within 2 years. Long-term mortality increased significantly with age, ranging from 5.8% in patients younger than 15 years to 62% in those older than 84 years (p < 0.0001), and with comorbidity burden (21%, 38%, 51%, and 67% for Charlson index 0, 1-2, 3-4, and ≥ 5, respectively; p < 0.0001). Neoplasia (hazard ratio [HR], 2.011), liver cirrhosis (HR, 1.562), and dementia (HR, 1.304) were the comorbidities most strongly associated with mortality. Longer hospital stays were also associated with increased mortality. A progressive decline in long-term mortality was observed during 2017-2019.

CONCLUSIONS: Long-term mortality among sepsis survivors remains high, with more than 40% dying within 2 years after hospital discharge. These findings support the need for structured post-sepsis care strategies focused on high-risk patients, improved continuity of care, and prevention of long-term sepsis-related complications.

articles.title: Application of Digital Health Interventions for Cognitive Management in Children With Cancer: Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advances in the diagnosis and treatment of childhood cancer have substantially improved survival, resulting in a growing population of survivors of childhood cancer who may experience long-term treatment-related sequelae. Cognitive late effects are an important long-term consequence of childhood cancer and can affect cognitive functioning, psychosocial well-being, and quality of life. Digital health interventions offer accessible and flexible approaches to managing cognitive difficulties among children with cancer. However, the existing evidence has not yet been comprehensively synthesized.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to map and synthesize the existing evidence on digital health interventions for cognitive management among children with cancer; characterize intervention modalities, delivery approaches, and functional components; and identify evidence gaps and priorities for future research.

METHODS: This scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Arksey and O'Malley framework and the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews) checklist. Six academic databases, including PubMed, Embase (Ovid), CINAHL, PsycINFO, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library, were systematically searched for relevant studies published between January 2010 and August 2026. Eligibility criteria were developed using the population-concept-context framework. Two reviewers independently performed study screening and data extraction. The methodological quality of included studies was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Screening was performed independently at the title/abstract and full-text stages, with disagreements resolved through discussion and, when necessary, consultation with a third reviewer. Descriptive statistics and thematic content analysis were used to synthesize the findings.

RESULTS: A total of 5371 records were identified through the literature search. Following screening, 19 publications representing 14 independent study samples and involving 566 children with cancer were included. Four digital health modalities were identified: computer-based interventions, internet-based interventions, mobile apps, and neurofeedback training. Computer-based interventions were the predominant modality. Across these modalities, working memory and attention were the most frequently targeted cognitive domains, while feasibility, acceptability, and adherence were the most commonly assessed implementation-related outcomes. However, relatively few interventions incorporated coach support, telephone-based communication, or educational components, and none evaluated economic outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Although digital health interventions show promise for supporting cognitive function in children with cancer, substantial gaps remain in the current evidence. This scoping review mapped the field according to intervention modalities, delivery approaches, and functional components, rather than focusing solely on the efficacy of individual technologies. Future research should prioritize the development of multidimensional, personalized, and functionally integrated digital health interventions that combine cognitive training with supportive care, education, monitoring, and communication. Multicenter randomized controlled trials should subsequently evaluate these interventions using clinically meaningful outcomes, with comprehensive assessments of safety, adherence, implementation, and health economic outcomes to establish their effectiveness, feasibility, and sustainability.

articles.title: Blood-Based Biomarkers and Traumatic Intracranial Hypertension: A Transforming Research and Clinical Knowledge in Traumatic Brain Injury Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The role of blood-based biomarkers in guiding the acute management of patients with established traumatic brain injury is unclear. We sought to determine whether concentrations of glial fibrillary acid protein (GFAP) or ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCH-L1) on hospital day 1 are associated with intracranial pressure (ICP) and therapeutic intensity level (TIL).

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Transforming Research and Clinical Knowledge in Traumatic Brain Injury data set, including patients age 17 years and older with traumatic brain injury and invasive ICP monitoring, excluding those undergoing decompressive craniectomy on admission. Patients were stratified into biomarker quartiles, and the relationships with ICP and TIL were analyzed descriptively. Multivariable linear regressions were performed to test the hypothesis that GFAP and UCH-L1 concentrations were independently associated with ICP and TIL after adjusting for a priori defined covariates.

RESULTS: Two hundred twenty-nine patients with a median age of 39 years (IQR 26-56) were included. Geometric mean concentrations for GFAP and UCH-L1 were 4423 and 989 pg/mL, respectively. Patients in the lowest GFAP quartile had a median of 7.3% of ICP readings >22 mm Hg vs 23.2% in the highest quartile (P < .001); secondary decompressive craniectomy was performed in 16% of the lowest quartile, compared with 39% of the highest quartile (P = .008). After adjusting for covariates, GFAP was significantly associated with ICP burden (B = 8.05, P = .014) and median TIL over 5 days (B = 1.65, P = .009). No significant relationship was seen for UCH-L1.

CONCLUSION: Day 1 blood concentration of GFAP is associated with elevated ICP and may be a useful adjunct when risk-stratifying patients for intracranial hypertension.

articles.title: Shortening the Family Satisfaction in the ICU (FS-ICU): Development and Validation of a 12-Item Family Satisfaction Survey for Adult ICUs.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate a shorter Family Satisfaction in the ICU (FS-ICU) questionnaire that reduces survey length while preserving content and psychometric performance for quality improvement and benchmarking. The FS-ICU survey assesses family perceptions of care, communication, and decision-making and has been translated into multiple languages with implementation across diverse health care systems internationally. In a province-wide electronic implementation in Ontario, more than 40% of initiated surveys were incomplete, suggesting that survey length may limit practicality for large-scale quality improvement and benchmarking.

DESIGN: Multistage study using provincial FS-ICU survey data and an independent multicenter validation dataset for item reduction, psychometric evaluation, agreement testing, and external validation of a shortened questionnaire.

SETTING: A 12-member expert working group, convened for a Critical Care Services Ontario initiative, used provincial web-based data from adult ICUs across Ontario to develop a shorter version, FS-ICUshort. External validation was applied to FS-ICUshort using a separate multicenter Canadian revised FS-ICU dataset.

PARTICIPANTS: A 12-member expert working group led by Dr. Daren K. Heyland, including administrative staff, ICU clinical staff, patient experience specialists, and quality improvement specialists from Ontario, used provincial FS-ICU rollout data.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Using empirical criteria and expert ratings, the FS-ICU was reduced from 29 to 12 items: seven in the satisfaction-with-care domain (FS-Care) and five in the communication and decision-making domain (FS-DM). FS-ICUshort showed high internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.93 for FS-Care, 0.86 for FS-DM, and 0.94 for total). Confirmatory factor analysis supported a two-factor structure with better fit than a single-factor model. Scores from FS-ICUshort closely matched full FS-ICU, with mean differences less than or equal to 1.1 points on a 0-100 scale and intraclass correlations of 0.97-0.99. External validation replicated these results.

CONCLUSIONS: The 12-item FS-ICUshort maintains the core content and psychometric quality of the original FS-ICU while significantly reducing length, supporting routine use in ICU family experience measurement and benchmarking.

articles.title: Postoperative Opening Pressure Rebound After Spontaneous Cerebrospinal Fluid Leak Repair.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Spontaneous cerebrospinal fluid (sCSF) leaks are frequently linked to underlying intracranial hypertension. Intraoperative opening pressure (OP) is used to assess intracranial pressure during repair. However, active leakage can act as a physiological release valve, underestimating true pressure. This study evaluates postoperative OP changes after surgical closure of spontaneous skull base leaks and identifies predictors of substantial pressure increase.

METHODS: A retrospective review analyzed patients undergoing surgical repair for anterior or lateral sCSF leaks at our institution between 2009 and 2025. Included patients had prerepair and postoperative OP measurements within 6 weeks of surgery. Patients were stratified by a ≥25% OP increase after repair.

RESULTS: A total of 46 patients met inclusion criteria. The mean prerepair OP was 18.92 ± 5.20 cm H2O, significantly increasing to 23.57 ± 9.04 cm H2O postoperatively (mean increase +4.64 cm H2O; 95% CI, 1.58-7.70; P = .004). Eighteen patients (39.1%) demonstrated a ≥25% OP increase, with the mean OP rising 89.6% from 16.75 to 31.75 cm H2O. Active leak at surgery was strongly associated with postoperative pressure rise (100% vs 28.6%, P < .001). Prerepair OP was significantly lower in the ≥25% increase subgroup (P = .021). No recurrences occurred during a mean follow-up of 24.9 months.

CONCLUSION: OPs may significantly increase after closure of sCSF leaks, especially in patients with active leakage. Normal intraoperative OP does not rule out underlying intracranial hypertension. These findings support the concept of masked intracranial hypertension, emphasizing the need for careful postoperative pressure reassessment.

articles.title: Obesity pharmacotherapies and cognition.
articles.abstract: Pharmacotherapies for obesity and type 2 diabetes are increasingly being evaluated for their effects on cognition and brain health. Evidence from preclinical models, observational cohorts, and clinical trials has intensified interest, but findings remain mixed. A central challenge is to determine whether potential cognitive effects arise from direct actions on neural circuits, indirect consequences of improved cardiometabolic health, or both. This Review examines the evidence across cardiometabolic disease, aging, and Alzheimer's disease, focusing on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based therapies and combination approaches that engage glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon, and amylin pathways. We assess how receptor pharmacology, brain exposure, metabolic context, and disease stage shape cognitive outcomes and discuss how mechanistic clarity could guide therapies aimed at preserving or improving cognition.

articles.title: Privacy, accuracy, and objectivity of census data.
articles.abstract: A new algorithm for protecting privacy can improve the accuracy of population statistics.

articles.title: Targeting hormone conversion through dietary fiber improves polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome.
articles.abstract: Excessive androgens serve as a primary driver for many phenotypic features of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Although dietary fiber has been shown to alleviate PMOS, its effects on androgen concentrations and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In a clinical trial, we demonstrated that a dietary fiber combination consisting of inulin, resistant starch, and β-glucan reduces androgen concentrations in patients' plasma. Mechanistically, dietary fiber increased the abundance of Bacteroides xylanisolvens, which converts androstenedione into a nonandrogenic secondary hormone metabolite we named coproandrosterone, which is further metabolized by gut microbiota into dihydro-coproandrosterone. This metabolic pathway was validated in a mouse model. These findings highlight the potential of dietary fiber to alleviate PMOS by modulating androgen homeostasis through gut microbiota, offering insights for prebiotic and probiotic therapies.

articles.title: Echoes of the Anthropocene: Noise pollution as a global threat.
articles.abstract: Anthropogenic noise is a rapidly expanding global pollutant, but its effects across biological levels from individuals to ecosystems remain unquantified. We conducted phylogenetically controlled meta-analyses of 214 experimental studies on 177 aquatic and terrestrial species with ranges that span six continents. Noise altered at least one physiological, developmental, or behavioral trait in 80% of species studied, with declines in fitness and abundance and disruptions of predator-prey interactions. Effects occurred in every habitat, although response mechanisms varied for some traits and species, creating winners and losers. Only multispecies analyses can reveal such species- and ecosystem-level impacts of anthropogenic stressors. Our results establish noise as a novel selection pressure reshaping ecosystem dynamics and as a pervasive stressor requiring soundscape protection alongside habitat conservation.

articles.title: A single-residue deletion in H9N2 hemagglutinin uncouples viral burden from disease severity.
articles.abstract: H9N2 avian influenza viruses are characterized by significant genetic diversity. Deletions within the hemagglutinin (HA) receptor-binding domain represent a notable, albeit rare, evolutionary trajectory. Here, we systematically characterized the multifaceted impact of a single-amino-acid deletion at residue 227 of HA (designated HAΔ227), a naturally occurring deletion within the 220-loop that overlaps a key antigenic epitope, using isogenic reverse genetics H9N2 viruses. Paradoxically, the HAΔ227 imposed a fitness cost and was associated with enhanced HA receptor-binding avidity, reduced apparent virion-associated NA activity, altered HA/NA functional balance, attenuated viral replication in vitro, and reduced respiratory shedding in vivo. Notably, despite this compromised replicative fitness, infection with the mutant virus was associated with an altered host immune response in chickens, characterized by elevated levels of interferon-γ (IFN-γ), interleukin-10 (IL-10), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), and monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1). These altered immune responses were associated with more severe pulmonary lesions, indicating a dissociation between disease severity and viral RNA load. Furthermore, the deletion increased the pH threshold for HA-mediated membrane fusion and substantially altered antigenic relationships. Collectively, our findings identify HA residue 227 as a functionally important site at which a single-residue deletion is associated with a phenotypic trade-off between replicative capacity and disease severity: reduced replicative fitness accompanied by altered inflammatory responses and greater tissue injury. This study highlights the potential phenotypic significance of a rare deletion in influenza virus HA and demonstrates that viral burden alone may not adequately predict disease severity.

articles.title: The Pathogen Recognition Receptor RIG-I is Functional in Platelets and Limits Thrombotic Responses.
articles.abstract: Influenza is associated with increased thrombotic risk, and its viral RNA (vRNA) can be sensed by pattern-recognition receptor RIG-I, but the function of RIG-I in platelets remains unknown. We sought to determine whether RIG-I can signal in platelets and contribute to thrombotic outcomes. Using RT-qPCR, SDS-PAGE, NATIVE-PAGE, and proteomic methods in platelets from non-infected and influenza-infected patients, we show that RIG-I is present and functional. Platelet-RIG-I activation by influenza-derived-vRNA did not result in uniform α- or δ-granule release, or to interferon-pathway activation. Instead, RIG-I signaled through MAVS to increase MLKL-phosphorylation (pMLKL), oligomerization, and S100A10 (but not S100A8/A9) release and surface presence. Oligomerized pMLKL led to surface punctures, evident by scanning electron microscopy, which were visible in both platelets and thrombin-induced platelet clots. Consistent with S100A10 surface localization, RIG-I activation in presence of plasminogen reduced platelet aggregation and led to increased disaggregation in presence of urokinase-type plasminogen activator. Disruption of RIG-I/MAVS signaling through MAVS deficiency was associated with increased thrombotic burden and shorter FeCl₃-induced carotid artery occlusion times during influenza infection in vivo. Consistent changes in occlusion burden were observed in the pulmonary veins of infected mice, where occluded area inversely correlated with leukocyte presence in the lung non-vascular tissue early in infection, followed by a positive association at later time points. Our study is the first to demonstrate that platelets have a functionally active vRNA-sensing RIG-I receptor that finely tunes thrombotic risk and facilitates appropriate leukocyte transmigration during infection, through non-classical platelet activation.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence for the diagnosis and prognosis of leprosy, leishmaniasis, and schistosomiasis: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neglected Tropical Diseases affect over one billion individuals globally, challenging healthcare systems in endemic regions. While promising, Artificial Intelligence (AI) requires rigorous validation for clinical translation.

METHODOLOGY: This systematic review of prediction-model studies evaluated AI applications for leprosy, schistosomiasis, and leishmaniasis (2015-2025). Methodological quality and reporting transparency of the included studies were appraised using the PROBAST+AI and TRIPOD+AI tools, respectively.

FINDINGS: Among 69 studies identified, 89.9% were published after 2020. The literature predominantly focused on diagnostic support (81.2%), leaving the prognosis of adverse outcomes underexplored (18.8%). Methodological fragility was widely observed: 89.9% of models exhibited a high risk of bias, primarily due to lack of external validation (82.6%) and failure to report or appropriately handle missing data (66.7%). Transparency remains a barrier, with source code unavailable in 76.8% of cases, hindering reproducibility.

CONCLUSION: Current evidence indicates that quantitative output outpaces methodological maturity. Bridging the gap between algorithmic potential and public health impact requires prioritizing open science and robust validation.

articles.title: Unveiling the functional landscape of A-to-I RNA editing associated with Marek's disease in chickens.
articles.abstract: Genetic improvement of disease resistance against viral infections represents a longstanding and formidable challenge in animal breeding. The antiviral innate immune response is highly regulated at the RNA level, especially through RNA modifications. Adenosine-to-Inosine (A-to-I) RNA editing modifies the mRNA sequence. Growing evidence shows that this type of RNA editing plays a key role in mediating cellular responses to viral infections and disease resistance. However, the role of RNA editing in cellular response to MD remains unclear. In this study, we examined A-to-I editing in CD4+ T cells during Marek's disease virus (MDV) infection. By comparing MD-resistant and susceptible chicken lines, we identified 642 A-to-I RNA editing events in CD4+ T cells, most of which were located within repeat elements, particularly in the CR1 family. We observed differences in RNA editing levels and counts between the two chicken lines with different infection statuses, indicating distinct editing patterns across genetic backgrounds and infection states. Additionally, ADAR (adenosine deaminases acting on RNA) expression was correlated with RNA editing frequency. We identified 21 RNA editing sites (RESs) associated with gene expression and 42, 14, and 38 RESs with predicted effects on amino acid sequences, alternative splicing, and miRNA-target binding, respectively. A comparative analysis revealed 131 group-specific RESs and 21 RESs shared across groups. Functional enrichment analysis of genes associated with group-specific RESs highlighted several terms related to MD resistance, including the MHC class I protein complex in non-infected MD-resistant birds. Significantly, we identified two L63-specific candidate RNA editing sites, chr6:26,600,122 in MXI1 and chr16:1,716,632 in MHCY57, which were predicted to affect gga-miR-1759-3p binding and amino acid sequence, respectively. Our findings reveal the landscape of A-to-I RNA editing in CD4 ⁺ T cells during MDV infection and provide new insights into its potential association with immune regulation and MD resistance.

articles.title: PD-1 deficiency impairs Treg differentiation in Trichinella-infected mice via inhibition of fatty acid oxidation.
articles.abstract: Helminth infections establish long-term host persistence by inducing regulatory immune responses that limit pathology while promoting parasite survival. Programmed death 1 (PD-1), an inhibitory receptor expressed on activated T cells, plays an essential role in maintaining immune homeostasis during chronic infections. Regulatory T cells (Tregs) expand during helminth infection and are critical for controlling excessive inflammation; however, the metabolic mechanisms linking PD-1 signaling to Treg differentiation during helminth infection remain poorly defined. Here, we investigated the role of PD-1 in regulating Treg differentiation during Trichinella spiralis infection, focusing on metabolic reprogramming in CD4⁺ T cells. Using a murine infection model, we compared wild-type and PD-1-deficient (PD-1⁻/⁻) mice and evaluated Treg differentiation in vivo and in a bone marrow-derived dendritic cell (BMDC)-CD4⁺ T-cell co-culture system stimulated with muscle larval excretory-secretory products (MES). PD-1 deficiency significantly reduced splenic FoxP3⁺ Treg frequencies following infection and impaired MES-induced Treg differentiation and Treg-associated cytokine production in vitro. Metabolic profiling revealed that CD4⁺ T cells from infected PD-1⁻/⁻ mice exhibited markedly reduced fatty acid oxidation (FAO), accompanied by decreased expression of Carnitine Palmitoyltransferase 1A (CPT1A), a key rate-limiting enzyme in FAO. PD-1 deficiency was associated with enhanced PI3K-Akt-mTOR signaling and suppressed AMPK activation. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of PI3K partially restored FAO activity and rescued Treg differentiation in PD-1⁻/⁻ CD4⁺ T cells. These findings suggest that PD-1 supports Treg development during T. spiralis infection, at least in part, through a CPT1A-associated FAO pathway, highlighting a PD-1-associated metabolic pathway that may contribute to helminth-induced immune regulation.

articles.title: Plant-Forward Dietary Patterns and Cardiometabolic Risk Among US Adults: Findings From the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, 2009-2023.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to describe the relationship between plant-forward dietary patterns and metabolic profiles.

METHODS: A repeated cross-sectional analysis of adults aged 18 years or older was conducted using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), 2009-2023. Plant-forward dietary adherence was estimated from the mean of two 24-hour dietary recalls and categorized into tertiles. Survey-weighted multivariable regression examined associations with body mass index (BMI), obesity, prediabetes, and diabetes, adjusting for demographic, socioeconomic, dietary, and behavioral factors.

RESULTS: Among 33,532 NHANES participants, greater plant-forward dietary adherence was associated with lower BMI (β = -1.45; 95% CI, -1.82 to -1.09), lower odds of obesity (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 0.70; 95% CI, 0.62-0.79) and diabetes (AOR = 0.72; 95% CI, 0.62-0.84) but not prediabetes (AOR = 0.92; 95% CI, 0.82-1.04).

CONCLUSION: Greater adherence to plant-forward dietary patterns was associated with lower BMI and reduced odds of obesity and diabetes among US adults.

articles.title: An Umbrella Review of Determinants of Digital Health Tool Implementation in Chronic Disease Prevention and Management in Clinical Practice Settings.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic diseases account for most illness, death, and health care spending globally and in the US. Digital health tools (DHTs) (eg, telemedicine, remote monitoring) can improve chronic disease prevention and management. However, population-level impact depends on successful implementation in clinical care. Although reviews describe determinants of DHT implementation, evidence is fragmented, and no comprehensive qualitative synthesis has focused exclusively on chronic disease prevention and management.

METHODS: We conducted a subanalysis of an umbrella review that examined determinants of DHT implementation in clinical practice settings. By using established scoping review methods and PRIOR (Preferred Reporting Items for Overview of Reviews) reporting guidelines, we searched PubMed, Scopus, and CINAHL for English-language reviews published from January 2013 through July 2025. We included reviews that focused on determinants of DHT implementation in clinical care and identified 15 reviews focused on chronic disease prevention and management. We extracted qualitative data on barriers and facilitators and synthesized the data by using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR).

RESULTS: Key innovation-level determinants included relative advantage, design, and strength of the evidence base, which frequently acted as barriers due to concerns about clinical effectiveness, workflow fit, and data reliability. Most implementer-level barriers related to limited opportunity and capability, including time constraints and low digital literacy among health care team users. Inner setting determinants included access to knowledge and information, available resources, structural characteristics, and compatibility with existing workflows as both barriers and facilitators. Outer setting determinants included a lack of policies and regulations and limited partnerships for supporting DHT implementation.

CONCLUSION: Implementation of DHTs for chronic disease prevention and management is shaped by multilevel determinants across CFIR domains. Addressing evidence gaps, investing in training and infrastructure, aligning tools with clinical workflows, and strengthening policy and partnership environments are critical to optimizing implementation. Findings provide actionable insights to guide future research and implementation strategies aimed at improving DHT implementation.

articles.title: Clinical Protocols and Guidelines for Hypertension and Diabetes in Incarcerated Populations: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Incarcerated populations have a disproportionate burden of acute and chronic conditions, including hypertension and diabetes. We aimed to identify and describe clinical protocols and guidelines for managing hypertension and diabetes in the incarcerated population.

METHODS: We conducted a scoping review in July 2025 of clinical protocols and guidelines that address the prevention, promotion, screening, diagnosis, and treatment of hypertension and diabetes in the incarcerated population. We searched electronic databases (Medline/PubMed, Embase, the Virtual Health Library, EBSCOhost, Scopus, Cochrane, and Web of Science), gray literature repositories, and websites of governmental and international organizations. We used the AGREE II instrument to assess document quality.

RESULTS: Three documents met the inclusion criteria; they were published in 2021, 2022, and 2024 and originated from high-income countries. Methodological appraisal showed heterogeneity in guideline development, with consistently low scores in the domains of stakeholder involvement and rigor of development. Existing protocols encompass health education and self-management support, multidisciplinary care, universal screening at intake, evidence-based and individualized treatment, and intersectoral collaboration to ensure health care delivery in correctional settings.

CONCLUSION: The small number of clinical protocols addressing hypertension and diabetes management in the incarcerated population reflects a critical normative gap in correctional health systems. Strengthening the scientific rigor of these protocols and ensuring their implementation are essential to standardize care, reduce clinical variation, and promote health equity, both within correctional settings and in the transition back to the community.

articles.title: The Effect of Student Pharmacists as Peer Coaches on Implementation of Community Pharmacy Services.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE AND OBJECTIVES: Pharmacist-led chronic disease management services can lead to improvements in health outcomes, yet barriers exist to the implementation of these services in community pharmacies. This study aimed to assess the effect of student pharmacists serving as peer coaches during implementation of a disease management program in community pharmacies.

INTERVENTION APPROACH: In summer 2025, student pharmacists served as peer coaches to facilitate implementation of a program designed to manage type 2 diabetes and hypertension among pharmacy patients into the workflow of participating pharmacies.

EVALUATION METHODS: A 35-item questionnaire was emailed to participating pharmacy teams before and 30 days after the coaching intervention. Survey questions assessed pharmacy characteristics, perceived success, readiness for implementating change, and attitudes toward the More Than a Script program. Program engagement data (number of patient encounters and number of completed patient visits) were collected from May to September 2025. We used the number of completed patient visits to calculate revenue generated during the coaching intervention. We used descriptive and comparative statistics for analysis.

RESULTS: Of 29 pharmacy teams participating in the coaching intervention, 18 (62%) responded to the survey. Pharmacy personnel indicated improvements in perceived success, readiness for change, and attitudes toward the program. The number of completed patient visits per pharmacy by the end of the coaching intervention was higher among coached pharmacy teams than among uncoached pharmacy teams with the exclusion of an outlier in the uncoached group (28 vs 13, P = .001). The average percentage of total patient encounters that resulted in a completed patient visit increased more in the coached group (from 32% to 56%) than in the uncoached group regardless of the outlier (from 22% to 25% with the outlier, 21% to 24% without the outlier; P = .02). The average revenue per pharmacy was $1,005 for coached pharmacies and $274 for uncoached pharmacies after excluding an outlier in the uncoached group (P = .001).

IMPLICATIONS FOR PUBLIC HEALTH: The accessibility offered by community pharmacies provides a path to connect patients to chronic disease management, but improved outcomes cannot occur without effective implementation. Student pharmacists serving as peer coaches can help community pharmacies with implementation of services to improve population health outcomes.

articles.title: Hantavirus Outbreak Caused by Andes Virus Linked to International Cruise Ship Travel - United States, 2026.
articles.journal: MMWR. Morbidity and mortality weekly report
articles.abstract: Andes virus (ANDV), the only hantavirus known to be transmitted person-to-person, is endemic to areas of South America and can cause hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, which has a case-fatality rate of approximately 40%. On May 4, 2026, CDC was notified of seven cases of severe acute respiratory illness, including three deaths, among 147 persons aboard a cruise ship in the Atlantic Ocean; the illnesses were later confirmed to be caused by ANDV. No cases occurred among passengers who were U.S. residents. Ten of 28 U.S. resident passengers disembarked before ANDV infection was confirmed aboard the ship. On May 10, the remaining 18 U.S. resident passengers were repatriated to the National Quarantine Unit in Omaha, Nebraska, for risk assessment and monitoring, and where optimized advanced care was available, should symptoms develop. CDC and U.S. health departments monitored 60 additional U.S. residents potentially exposed on flights involving a passenger with symptomatic ANDV infection from the cruise, totaling 88 contacts across 27 jurisdictions. All 88 contacts completed 42 days of monitoring, with no secondary ANDV infections identified. Worldwide, local health authorities assessed and monitored approximately 653 potentially exposed persons from 33 countries. This response highlights the value of rapid coordination among partners to locate and monitor potentially exposed persons during an international outbreak to reduce the risk for ANDV transmission. Prompt notification to public health authorities can facilitate testing, patient care, contact identification, and implementation of measures to limit secondary transmission.

articles.title: Cutaneous Aspergillosis Among Extremely Preterm Neonates in Neonatal Intensive Care Units - Michigan and New York, 2023-2024.
articles.journal: MMWR. Morbidity and mortality weekly report
articles.abstract: Cutaneous aspergillosis is a rare, life-threatening fungal infection in neonates, particularly those born extremely preterm (gestational age <28 weeks); outbreaks have been linked to environmental sources of Aspergillus species. The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services and the New York State Department of Health investigated two clusters of cutaneous aspergillosis in neonatal intensive care units during 2023-2024. In Michigan, two extremely preterm neonates (gestational age <24 weeks) received a diagnosis of cutaneous aspergillosis. Samples cultured from both infants were positive for Aspergillus fumigatus; both received antifungal treatment, and one infant died. In New York, three neonates (two born at gestational age 24-25 weeks and one at <24 weeks) received a diagnosis of cutaneous aspergillosis. Isolates from skin lesions were identified as A. fumigatus (one isolate) and closely related Aspergillus quadrilineatus (two isolates); all infants received antifungal treatment, and all three survived. In Michigan, A. fumigatus was isolated from an air sample collected near linen-transport areas; environmental sampling was not performed in New York. No definitive environmental source was identified for either cluster. Both investigations led to targeted infection control interventions, including revised linen handling, optimized airflow and air-handling systems, and enhanced skin assessment and infection prevention practices. These clusters underscore the susceptibility of extremely preterm neonates to invasive mold infections and the importance of early recognition, thorough environmental assessment and multidisciplinary collaboration, to prevent further exposures.

articles.title: Bidirectional frailty transitions in community-dwelling older adults: longitudinal findings from the Queenstown cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty in older adults is dynamic and shaped by clinical, functional, and social factors, yet longitudinal transitions in community populations are not well characterised. We examined one-year changes in frailty and identified factors associated with improvement and progression.

METHODS: We performed a longitudinal analysis of community-dwelling adults aged ≥65 years from the population-based Queenstown Health District cohort. Baseline (Wave 1, 2023-2024) demographic, clinical, and lifestyle data were collected, with reassessment at one year (Wave 2). Frailty was measured using the Clinical Frailty Scale. Ordinal logistic regression modelled overall direction of frailty transition, while multinomial logistic regression identified factors associated with improvement or worsening relative to stability. Alluvial plots illustrated transitions across frailty states over time.

RESULTS: Among 1,153 participants (mean age 74.5 ± 6.6 years; 55.8% female), frailty remained stable in 627 (54.4%), improved in 211 (18.3%), and worsened in 315 (27.3%) over one year. Visualisation demonstrated predominant stability with bidirectional movement between frailty categories. In ordinal analyses, diabetes (OR 1.39, 95% CI 1.06-1.83), smoking (OR 1.89, 95% CI 1.19-3.03), and iADL impairment (OR 1.56, 95% CI 1.01-2.41) were associated with worsening, while higher physical activity was protective (OR 0.70, 95% CI 0.51-0.98). Multinomial models showed stroke history associated with improvement (OR 4.23, 95% CI 1.46-12.25), whereas iADL impairment reduced the likelihood of improvement (OR 0.48, 95% CI 0.28-0.82).

CONCLUSION: Frailty was largely stable but exhibited meaningful bidirectional transitions. Functional impairment and modifiable behaviours were key predictors, underscoring the importance of repeated assessment and function-focused prevention to mitigate frailty progression.

articles.title: DepthShield: Optical Depth Encoding for Image Tampering Detection.
articles.journal: IEEE transactions on pattern analysis and machine intelligence
articles.abstract: Detecting image forgeries is increasingly difficult as diffusion-based and manual edits preserve perceptually plausible image statistics. Most existing tampering detection methods rely solely on post-capture data, assuming a trusted acquisition process, and thus degrade when attackers replicate the image formation distribution. We introduce DepthShield, a depth assisted integrity framework that enforces authenticity at the moment of capture by coupling optical encoding with learned verification. The system operates in two coordinated stages that separate secure capture from high-quality release to end users. In the Image Capture Stage (IC-Stage), a designed phase mask modulates the image formation process to encode depth dependent signatures. This establishes a deterministic mapping between scene geometry and the encoded image, prioritizing security over initial visual quality (∼ 20 dB). Any unauthorized manipulation disrupts this fundamental RGB-Depth relationship. In the Integrity Restoration Stage (IR-Stage), a high-quality image (∼30 dB) is reconstructed from the protected capture and its depth cues while anchoring structural depth relationships necessary for reliable authentication. Rather than relying on statistical RGB artifacts only, DepthShield verifies whether an image is authentic by verifying the geometric consistency between the recovered RGB intensities and its corresponding depth map, as defined by the inverse mapping of the optical system. Experiments demonstrate that DepthShield surpasses software-only baselines across diverse tampering types, including diffusion-based edits, splicing, and local edits, and remains robust under common degradations such as compression. In addition, we implement a hardware prototype, validating its effectiveness on real-world captured scenes.

articles.title: Rezafungin in clinical practice: current evidence and expert perspectives.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Invasive fungal infections require prolonged antifungal therapy and can pose significant therapeutic challenges, particularly when they involve deep-seated sites or when treatment is complicated by antifungal resistance, toxicity, drug-drug interactions, or limited source control. Rezafungin is a novel once-weekly echinocandin with an extended half-life and favorable pharmacokinetic properties; however, clinical experience beyond candidemia and invasive candidiasis remains limited.

AREAS COVERED: We reviewed the available real-world clinical evidence on rezafungin, focusing on patient characteristics, infection types, therapeutic intent, antifungal resistance, treatment strategies, safety, and clinical outcomes across approved and off-label indications.

EXPERT OPINION: Rezafungin represents a promising therapeutic option for deep-seated and other difficult-to-treat fungal infections requiring prolonged antifungal therapy. Its once-weekly administration, prolonged half-life, and limited potential for drug-drug interactions may offer substantial advantages in long-term treatment and outpatient therapy. However, current evidence largely comes from case reports and small observational studies. Prospective studies and larger real-world cohorts are needed to define better the efficacy, optimal treatment duration, and positioning of rezafungin in deep-seated fungal infections.

articles.title: Cervical Neoplasia Among Canadian Armed Forces Regular Force Members, 2012-2024: A Descriptive Case Series.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cervical cancer is preventable through human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination, routine screening, and timely follow up of abnormal results. However, limited evidence is available regarding cervical cancer burden and screening patterns and barriers within the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF). This study describes the demographic, military, clinical, and screening characteristics of cervical neoplasia cases diagnosed among CAF Regular Force members between 2012 and 2024.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective descriptive case series was conducted using electronic medical records from the Canadian Forces Health Information System. The International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10) codes in the clinical extract were used to identify any cervical neoplasia diagnoses from January 1, 2012 to December 31, 2024. Incident cases were confirmed based on colposcopy‑directed biopsy results. Demographic and military-specific data at diagnosis were obtained from the Master Patient Index. Variables extracted from the health record included age at diagnosis, rank, screening history, HPV vaccination status, diagnostic pathways, stage at diagnosis, referral timelines, and follow-up outcomes. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize case characteristics and identify gaps in screening participation and follow-up adherence.

RESULTS: A total of 23 incident cervical neoplasia cases were confirmed during the study period. The median age at diagnosis was 37 years (range: 24-52), and 47.8% were officers. 21.8% reported smoking at diagnosis. 43.5% of cases had missed (n = 7) or delayed (n = 3) at least 1 routine cervical cancer screening before diagnosis. 39.1% experienced delayed or missed follow-up after abnormal Pap results. Reported barriers to routine screening and follow-up included pandemic-related service interruptions, deployment or domestic posting, pregnancy, and childcare challenges. 39.1% (n = 9) had an abnormal result at the first recorded Pap test in the system. HPV vaccination completion was recorded for 52.2% of cases, and among those tested for HPV (n = 19), 31.6% were positive for types 16 or 18. Invasive cancer accounted for 56.5% of diagnoses, with 92.3% of invasive cases presenting at International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage I. Histology included squamous cell carcinoma (69.2%) and adenocarcinoma (30.8%). The median interval from abnormal screening result to diagnosis was 3.1 months (range: 0.7-61.9). No cervical cancer-related deaths were identified.

CONCLUSION: This case series provides the first comprehensive description of cervical neoplasia among CAF Regular Force members over more than a decade. Findings highlight important opportunities to strengthen CAF prevention efforts, including improving screening participation and reducing delays in follow-up of abnormal tests. Enhanced reminder systems, reduced barriers to screening including self-testing, and targeted health promotion may reduce cervical cancer incidence and support the health and operational readiness of CAF personnel.

articles.title: Effects of upadacitinib on lipid profiles and their relationship with inflammation in patients with inflammatory bowel disease: a real-world longitudinal cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Upadacitinib (UPA), a selective Janus kinase 1 inhibitor, is approved for moderate-to-severe inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). JAK inhibitors affect lipid metabolism, but longitudinal real-world data on lipid changes during UPA therapy, and their relation to inflammatory activity, are scarce.

METHODS: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, patients with ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease treated with upadacitinib were followed for up to 2 years. Serial fasting lipid profiles and inflammatory markers (fecal calprotectin, C-reactive protein [CRP], high-sensitivity CRP) were collected at baseline, end of induction (weeks 8-12), 1 year, and 2 years. Lipid trajectories were analyzed with linear mixed-effects models; paired changes were compared with paired t-tests.

RESULTS: Among 159 patients (mean age 43.3 ± 14.0 years; 62.3% male), total cholesterol (TC) rose from 4.19 ± 0.87 mmol/L at baseline to 4.92, 5.03, and 5.21 mmol/L at the end of induction, 1 year, and 2 years (mixed-effects estimates +0.70 to +0.90; all P < .001). Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) rose in parallel, and the LDL-C/HDL-C ratio did not increase. CRP reductions correlated with lipid rises (Spearman rho = -0.45 to -0.47; all P ≤ .02). No cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke occurred (0/159); one venous thromboembolism and 3 hypertension cases were recorded.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with IBD treated with UPA, TC and LDL-C rose modestly alongside the resolution of inflammation; HDL-C improved and the LDL-C/HDL-C ratio did not increase. Lipid monitoring and individualized cardiovascular risk assessment are warranted during UPA therapy.

articles.title: Atherosclerotic plaque healing: mechanisms and clinical relevance.
articles.abstract: Atherosclerotic plaque healing is a dynamic biological mechanism that occurrs after plaque disruption and represents an endogenous reparative response within the atherosclerotic lesion. This process unfolds through three partially overlapping phases: endogenous thrombus lysis, granulation tissue formation, and re-endothelialization. Through the coordinated interaction of circulating cells, vascular wall components, and soluble mediators, plaque healing promotes fibrous repair and structural stabilization of the disrupted plaque. For many years, plaque healing remained primarily a histopathological observation described in post-mortem studies. The advent of high-resolution intracoronary imaging, particularly optical coherence tomography, has enabled in vivo visualization of the characteristic layered morphology of healed plaques, providing direct clinical confirmation of these early pathological findings. These observations have significantly improved our understanding of the clinical significance of plaque healing. Healed plaques are more frequently observed in patients with chronic coronary syndromes, supporting the concept that healing contributes to plaque stabilization. At the same time, recurrent cycles of plaque disruption followed by repair may lead to progressive luminal narrowing, thereby contributing to the long-term progression of coronary atherosclerosis. This review provided an updated overview of the clinical significance and implications of healed plaques in coronary artery disease, the mechanisms underlying plaque healing, and examines emerging intracoronary and non-invasive imaging modalities that allow their in vivo identification.

articles.title: Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in transcatheter mitral interventions: percutaneous anterior leaflet modification.
articles.abstract: Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO) remains one of the most catastrophic complications of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) interventions, including TMVR in native valve, valve-in-valve, valve-in-ring, and valve-in-mitral annular calcification procedures. Its incidence varies widely across procedural types (0%-40%), with mortality rates approaching 36%, and represents a leading cause of patient ineligibility, excluding 4%-50% of candidates from TMVR. Accurate pre-procedural risk stratification relies on cardiac computed tomography, which enables annular sizing, virtual valve implantation, neo- and skirt neo-left ventricular outflow tract area quantification, and fluoroscopic projection planning. Key anatomic determinants of LVOTO include anterior mitral leaflet length, aortomitral angle, septal hypertrophy, left ventricular cavity size, and device-related factors. To mitigate LVOTO risk and expand treatment eligibility, in addition to septal modification, anterior mitral leaflet modification techniques have emerged, broadly categorized into electrosurgical laceration approaches-LAMPOON and ELASTA-and balloon-assisted translocation techniques for balloon-expandable valves-BATMAN, CLEVE, DETROIT, and ROBIN. Each strategy addresses distinct anatomic substrates and procedural scenarios, and their complementary profiles support individualized technique selection. This review aims to present an in-depth discussion of LVOTO in TMVR and anterior leaflet modification strategies.

articles.title: Multi-omics identifies convergent genetic drivers of medial arterial calcification in chronic kidney disease.
Coronary angiography in heart transplants from donors older than 40: a Eurotransplant study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The increasing age of heart donors in Europe raises concerns about undetected coronary artery disease (CAD), a contributor to early graft dysfunction and long-term complications. This study examined the association between donor coronary angiography (CA) and heart transplant utilization, particularly in donors aged >40 years.

METHODS: A total of 20 681 donor heart offers reported to Eurotransplant between 2004 and 2020 were analysed. The use of CA, donor characteristics, and acceptance rates were assessed. CAD status was imputed for donors without angiography using logistic regression based on clinical risk factors. Transplantation probabilities were modelled using observed and imputed CAD severity to explore potential differences under a scenario of broader CA availability.

RESULTS: CA was performed in 23.5% of cases, predominantly in older donors and those with cardiovascular risk factors. Among donors with CA, 37.5% had CAD, which was significantly associated with age, male sex, hypertension, and smoking. Donors with normal CA findings had lower odds of rejection compared with those without CA (odds ratio 0.36, P < .0001). In a counterfactual model, broader CA availability in donors aged >40 years was associated with a higher estimated transplant utilization (56.4%-67.1%), corresponding to a model-based increase of ∼535 transplants.

CONCLUSIONS: In this observational cohort, CA availability was associated with differences in donor heart utilization, particularly when findings were normal or showed non-significant CAD. These findings suggest that angiographic information may reduce diagnostic uncertainty and support clinical decision-making in older donors. A risk-adapted, resource-sensitive approach to CA use is warranted.

articles.title: Decidua-accumulated effector-like memory CD8+ T cells orchestrate localized antimicrobial defense without compromising fetal tolerance.
articles.abstract: Deciphering immune privilege at the maternal-fetal interface is essential for understanding how reproductive success and host defense are simultaneously maintained. Decidualization, occurring within the specialized stromal tissue encapsulating the fetus and placenta, shapes local immune adaptation required for healthy pregnancy. Here, we identify a decidua-enriched effector-like memory CD8+ T cell subset marked by CD45RA in humans and CX3CR1 in mice. These cells preferentially accumulate in the decidua, which harbors a CX3CL1-dominant chemokine niche, and disruption of Cx3cr1 or uterine Cx3cl1 impaired their decidual recruitment and tissue localization. Human CD45RA+ and murine CX3CR1+ decidual memory CD8+ T cells shared conserved transcriptional and functional features, including enhanced cytotoxic potential and limited inflammatory cytokine production. Functionally, CX3CL1-mediated CD8+ T cell accumulation improved local control of prenatal Listeria monocytogenes infection and reduced infection-associated fetal loss. In contrast, fetal antigen-specific CD8+ T cell accumulation and fetal resorption occurred independently of uterine CX3CL1. Together, our findings define the maternal-fetal interface as an active immunological gatekeeper, that compartmentalizing CD8+ T cell-mediated antimicrobial adaptive immunity through the conserved CX3CL1-CX3CR1 axis, supporting pathogen-specific defense while preserving fetal tolerance.

articles.title: Mechanical Thrombectomy in Ischemic Stroke With a Medium or Distal Arterial Occlusion.
Mechanical Thrombectomy in Ischemic Stroke With a Medium or Distal Arterial Occlusion-Reply.
Radiographic and inflammatory factors associated with fever-based clinical improvement in children with macrolide-resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Clinical improvement during initial macrolide-based management varies among children with macrolide-resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MRMP) pneumonia. We evaluated the associations between inflammatory burden, chest radiographic phenotypes, and clinical improvement.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multicenter cohort study at nine university hospitals in South Korea from 2012 to 2024. Eligible patients had PCR-confirmed M. pneumoniae infection and sequencing-confirmed macrolide resistance. Fever-based clinical improvement was defined as defervescence within 5 days of macrolide initiation before any rescue therapy. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to evaluate factors independently associated with clinical improvement.

RESULTS: Among the 169 identified MRMP pneumonia cases, 130 were included, and 47 (36.2%) showed clinical improvement. The proportion of cases that showed clinical improvement decreased across radiographic phenotypes, from 60.0% with peribronchial infiltration to 10.0% with dense lobar consolidation or diffuse haziness. Peak C-reactive protein (CRP) levels of ≥ 6 mg/dL were independently associated with lower odds of improvement (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.25; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.07-0.88), as was dense lobar consolidation or diffuse haziness compared with peribronchial infiltration (aOR, 0.08; 95% CI, 0.01-0.73). When stratified jointly by CRP level and radiographic involvement, the proportion of cases with clinical improvement was 53.7% among those with CRP < 6 mg/dL and non-lobar involvement and 12.9% among those with CRP ≥ 6 mg/dL and lobar or diffuse involvement.

CONCLUSIONS: In sequencing-confirmed MRMP pneumonia, fever-based clinical improvement varied with inflammatory burden and radiographic phenotype. These exploratory findings may help inform structured reassessment during macrolide-based treatment but require prospective external validation.

articles.title: Species-specific clinical characteristics of Streptococcus anginosus group bacteraemia: a five-year retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The Streptococcus anginosus group (SAG) is comprised of S. anginosus, constellatus, and S. intermedius which can cause invasive infection with a particular predilection for abscess formation. We aimed to describe the clinical characteristics, infectious sources, abscess formation and outcomes of SAG bacteraemia across NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde, Scotland, UK, and compare clinical manifestations between species.

METHODS: We retrospectively identified all blood culture sets isolating SAG bacteria in NHS GG&C from 1st January 2020 to 31st December 2024 using our electronic laboratory information management system. Electronic clinical records were reviewed.

RESULTS: Among 200 positive blood culture sets, 180 patients with clinically significant SAG bacteraemia were identified. The overall annual incidence was 3.0 per 100,000 population-years (95% CI 2.6-3.5). S. anginosus was the most common species (56%), followed by S. constellatus (29%), and S. intermedius (15%). An infectious focus was identified in 138/180 (77%) patients, most commonly hepatobiliary. Abscesses were identified in 71/180 (39%) patients with the highest proportion among patients with S. intermedius bacteraemia (18/27, 67%). Infective endocarditis (IE) occurred in 6/180 (3%)​ patients and was caused exclusively by S. anginosus. Thirty-day mortality was 18% (33/180) and was not significantly different between species. Out of 42 patients with a SAG bacteraemia without an identified focus, previously unrecognised malignancy was identified in 11 (26%) patients.

CONCLUSION: SAG bacteraemia was associated with substantial mortality and species-specific differences in abscess identification. Previously unrecognised malignancy was identified relatively frequently among patients without an identified infectious focus, but this finding is subject to ascertainment bias and requires prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Resistant hypertension and accelerated vascular aging: evidence for PTEN-AKT-associated cellular senescence.
articles.abstract: Resistant hypertension (RH) is increasingly linked to accelerated vascular aging and is particularly prevalent among older and obese individuals. Cellular senescence has emerged as a potential driver of vascular aging, but its contribution to RH remains unclear. We examined age and body mass index (BMI) in the WalkByLab cohort and assessed whether RH was associated with vascular features consistent with accelerated aging. Obesity-related transcriptomic datasets were integrated with a curated senescence-associated gene set to identify candidate regulators, followed by validation in an independent RH dataset, PBMCs, and human endothelial cells. An exploratory clinical-molecular nomogram was also developed. BMI and age increased progressively from normotension to RH. RH was characterized by reduced flow-mediated dilation, increased pulse wave index, and unchanged ankle-brachial index, consistent with endothelial dysfunction and arterial stiffness. Transcriptomic analyses identified enrichment of inflammatory, PI3K-AKT, and senescence-associated pathways. In PBMCs from RH patients, PTEN expression was reduced, AKT phosphorylation was increased, and p16/p21 levels were elevated, indicating a systemic senescence-associated molecular profile. In human endothelial cells, exposure to obese serum or pharmacological PTEN inhibition induced AKT activation and cellular senescence, whereas AKT inhibition attenuated these effects. Together, transcriptomic, clinical, and experimental findings indicate that RH is associated with vascular and molecular features consistent with accelerated vascular aging. Human data indicate a systemic senescence-associated molecular profile, whereas endothelial cell experiments support endothelial senescence as a mechanistically relevant cellular component. PTEN-AKT-associated cellular senescence may represent one mechanistically relevant component linking obesity to vascular dysfunction in RH.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of finerenone in non-diabetic chronic kidney disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Finerenone, a non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (nsMRA), reduces composite kidney, and cardiovascular endpoints in diabetic CKD. Its efficacy and safety across non-diabetic CKD aetiologies remain uncharacterised in prior meta-analyses.
