METHODS: Four databases were searched to May 2026. RCTs and observational studies enrolling adults with non-diabetic CKD receiving finerenone were eligible. Two streams were used: Stream A (single-arm) and Stream B (comparative, finerenone vs. controls). The primary outcomes were eGFR slope/12-month change and proteinuria reduction; safety outcomes were hyperkalaemia, hypotension, adverse events, and discontinuation. Random-effects models (Hartung-Knapp), ROB-2, Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, GRADE, and TSA were applied.

RESULTS: Nine studies (N = 2020) met eligibility, including two RCTs (the placebo-controlled FIND-CKD trial (n = 1584) and an open-label crossover pilot), alongside seven observational studies. Finerenone significantly slowed eGFR decline in the RCT (slope difference +0.70 mL/min/1.73m2/year, 95%CI 0.30-1.10; P < 0.001) and increased odds of a ≥ 30% proteinuria response roughly four-fold (pooled OR 3.99, 95% CI 1.91-8.30; P = 0.027). Two propensity-matched IgAN cohorts showed a 76.8% reduction in proteinuria versus controls (95% CI -81.1% to -72.6%; I2 = 0%). In single-arm analysis, 28.9% achieved a ≥ 50% proteinuria reduction. Hyperkalaemia was more frequent with finerenone (17.0% vs 13.3%; OR 1.34, 95% CI 1.02-1.76), though any adverse event did not differ (OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.67-1.99); pooled hyperkalaemia was 1.6%, hypotension 0.5%, discontinuation 0/258.

CONCLUSIONS: In non-diabetic CKD, finerenone slows eGFR decline, supported by high-certainty evidence from FIND-CKD, and reduces proteinuria, with a modest rise in hyperkalaemia. These data support finerenone as a kidney-protective, proteinuria-lowering therapy, underscoring the need for potassium monitoring, and further trials.

articles.title: Time to Storm the Next CASTLE: Can Atrial Fibrillation Ablation Improve Outcomes in Patients With Heart Failure and Preserved Ejection Fraction?
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and atrial fibrillation frequently coexist and are linked by shared mechanisms including atrial myopathy, elevated filling pressures, fibrosis, and adverse hemodynamic interactions. The combination of both diseases worsens patient outcomes, and catheter ablation has emerged as a potentially important treatment strategy in this population. This review aims to summarize and highlight the current evidence on ablation in patients with atrial fibrillation and HFpEF.

RECENT FINDINGS: When examining outcomes of mortality, hospitalization, hemodynamics, and recurrence, ablation appears to be superior to medical treatment with some mixed results. However, no large trials have been conducted on the topic, and no clear guidelines for ablation in HFpEF patients exist. Ablation is promising but not yet definitive for patients with atrial fibrillation and HFpEF. Ongoing trials, including CASTLE-HFpEF should clarify the gaps including patient selection, procedural strategy, and outcome benefit.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in Gallbladder Carcinoma: A Review of Research Studies and Clinical Evidence.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gallbladder carcinoma (GBC) is the most common biliary tract malignancy and is usually diagnosed at an advanced stage. Artificial intelligence (AI), including radiomics, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), is increasingly applied to its diagnosis, surgical management and prognostication, but how far the reported performance can be trusted is unclear.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library and Google Scholar were searched to 5 May 2026 using database-specific search strategies. Each primary prediction-model study was characterized separately by design, number of centers and validation type (internal, temporal or external).

RESULTS: Of 31 primary AI studies in GBC, 29 were retrospective, 22 were single-center and 24 reported internal validation only. In independent test or external cohorts, DL and ML models discriminated benign from malignant gallbladder lesions with areas under the curve (AUCs) of approximately 0.80-0.89; a multicenter model distinguishing xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis from GBC achieved an external AUC of 0.88, and automated computed tomography (CT) segmentation an external Dice score of 0.76. The best recurrence model achieved an AUC of 0.76 on internal (random-split) validation; none of the reviewed prognostic models reported a quantified external-validation estimate. Intraoperative AI is technically feasible but has no outcome data, and federated learning has been tested only in simulation.

CONCLUSION: AI could plausibly assist several steps of GBC care, but the evidence is dominated by retrospective, single-center, internally validated studies from Asia, and metrics from different studies are not directly comparable. Prospective multicenter external validation, shared annotated datasets and standardized reporting are required before clinical adoption.

articles.title: CONDSIAS, a Stress-Triggered Childhood Neurodegeneration: Four Novel ADPRS Variants and a Structured Review of the Reported Phenotype.
articles.abstract: Stress-induced childhood-onset neurodegeneration with variable ataxia and seizures (CONDSIAS), Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) 618,170, is an autosomal-recessive disorder caused by biallelic ADPRS (ADPRHL2) variants, encoding ADP-ribosylserine hydrolase (ARH3). Its stress-precipitated, stepwise course may resemble pediatric mitochondrial disease, delaying diagnosis. Four unrelated pediatric probands from three Italian tertiary centers were characterized retrospectively and integrated with a structured literature review to June 2026. Data were collected into a 20-item dataset, variants were standardized to Matched Annotation from NCBI and EMBL-EBI (MANE) Select NM_017825.3 and classified by American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics / Association for Molecular Pathology (ACMG/AMP) criteria. The two novel missense variants were assessed by conservation profiling and FoldX. Onset occurred between 13 months and 2.5 years in three males and one female; three were alive at 7 to 14 years and one died at 10 years 6 months. Three were compound heterozygous and one homozygous. Four novel variants were identified, c.74G > T, p.(Gly25Val) and c.827 C > T, p.(Ser276Leu) in Patient 1, c.827dup, p.(Val277GlyfsTer17) in Patient 2, and c.1060 C > T, p.(Gln354Ter) in Patient 4, bringing the cohort to 62 patients and 31 unique alleles. In our cohort, ataxia, paroxysmal neck dystonia, peripheral neuropathy and progressive respiratory failure were identified as core features. In silico modeling supported a destabilizing, likely loss-of-function effect for both novel missense variants. Progressive cerebellar ataxia with paroxysmal neck dystonia may help to orient the diagnosis. ADPRS should be early considered in stress-precipitated childhood-onset ataxia.

articles.title: Effect of remote patient monitoring on PAP adherence and patient-reported outcomes in obstructive sleep apnea: a comparative study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a common condition, and positive airway pressure (PAP) is the standard therapy; however, its effectiveness depends on adherence. Remote patient monitoring (RPM) may improve PAP adherence, but evidence remains limited.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective, open-label, active-comparator, randomized trial comparing an RPM program with standard of care (SOC) in PAP-naive adults (≥ 18 years) with OSA who owned a smartphone. Participants were randomized 1:1 to SOC (PAP therapy with a standard coaching program) or RPM (PAP therapy monitored through a web-based application with coaching). The primary endpoint was Medicare-defined PAP adherence (> 4 h of use on > 70% of nights during a consecutive 30-day period within the first 90 days). Secondary endpoints included nights with elevated mask leak, patient-reported sleep measures, and patient satisfaction (Likert scale), with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment for multiple comparisons. Given the pragmatic sample size, the study was designed to estimate between-arm differences rather than to test superiority with conventional power.

RESULTS: The 196 participants (98 per arm) were 65% male, with a median (interquartile range) age of 51 (41-62) years and body mass index of 32 (29-37) kg/m². Medicare-defined PAP adherence was 80.6% in the RPM group and 73.5% in the SOC group (difference 7.1% points; p = 0.308). At day 90, the RPM group had fewer nights with elevated mask leak (median 11.2 vs. 14.5; unadjusted p = 0.009; adjusted p = 0.113) and a higher proportion of participants reporting the highest satisfaction with timeliness of support, the coaching program, and issue resolution (unadjusted p = 0.031-0.044). None of these differences remained significant after adjustment for multiple comparisons (all adjusted p ≥ 0.11).

CONCLUSIONS: Because of the limited sample size, conclusions are primarily descriptive. Medicare-defined PAP adherence did not differ significantly between RPM and SOC. The RPM group had fewer nights with elevated mask leak and higher satisfaction scores, but these differences were not significant after adjustment for multiple comparisons and require confirmation in an adequately powered trial.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Retrospectively registered on 20,250,919 at https//clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07182617.

articles.title: Advancements in Artificial Intelligence for Enhanced Diagnosis and Prognosis in Cardiac CT: a Comprehensive Review and Future Perspectives.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Cardiovascular disease, with coronary artery disease (CAD) as its main culprit, remains a leading cause of death worldwide. Traditional diagnostic methods that focus on the degree of arterial narrowing (percent diameter stenosis, or %DS) can miss early signs of disease or the specific plaque features that indicate high risk. The purpose of this review is to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) can enhance the diagnostic and prognostic capabilities of cardiac computed tomography (CCT), and to address where AI can most meaningfully improve diagnostic accuracy, workflow efficiency, and patient care.

RECENT FINDINGS: AI is transforming cardiac CT across the entire imaging pathway. By applying AI algorithms, recent studies have refined the assessment of coronary artery calcium (CAC), improved plaque characterization, and detected subtle lesions that might evade traditional detection methods. AI further enables non-invasive assessment of ischemia (reduced blood flow), aids in the evaluation of myocardial infarction, analyzes adipose tissue surrounding the heart, improves image quality, and provides valuable prognostic insights for risk stratification. This comprehensive review explores the transformative potential of AI in cardiac CT, highlighting its role in accurate diagnosis, precise risk stratification, and personalized management of cardiovascular disease. Through collaboration between AI technology and clinical expertise, we envision a future where cardiac CT imaging is more powerful, efficient, and patient-centered, ultimately leading to improved outcomes in cardiovascular medicine. Continued standardization, external validation, and clinician education will be essential to realize this impact in routine practice.

articles.title: Novel Biomarkers for Bacterial Meningitis and Other Central Nervous System Infections.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Timely and accurate diagnosis of central nervous system (CNS) infections remains challenging because of nonspecific clinical characteristics and limited diagnostic accuracy of conventional tests. Novel cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers may improve early diagnosis and facilitate differentiation between infectious aetiologies. This review summarizes established and emerging CSF biomarkers for the diagnosis of CNS infections, with a focus on bacterial meningitis, and discusses their potential clinical application.

RECENT FINDINGS: Several novel CSF biomarkers have demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance for bacterial meningitis. Among these, CSF C-reactive protein (CRP) has recently been implemented in clinical practice, while heparin-binding protein and combinations of CSF CRP with inflammatory cytokines such as IL-6 and IL-1β show similarly high diagnostic accuracy. Pathogen-specific biomarkers, including CXCL13 for neuroborreliosis and β-D-glucan and galactomannan for fungal CNS infections, further expand the diagnostic repertoire. In addition, multi-omics approaches, including metabolomics, lipidomics, and proteomics, have identified promising candidates such as pyruvate and phosphatidylcholines, although these require further validation. Untargeted techniques, including metagenomic next-generation sequencing and phage immunoprecipitation sequencing, further enhance pathogen detection and may complement microbiological testing. Novel biomarkers have the potential to substantially improve the diagnosis of CNS infections. Several biomarkers for bacterial meningitis are already available for clinical implementation, particularly in patients with intermediate CSF leukocyte counts, where diagnostic uncertainty is greatest. For viral and other CNS infections biomarkers remain scarce. Future studies should focus on validation of emerging biomarkers and on integrating biomarker panels with advanced molecular diagnostic techniques to enable rapid, accurate and clinically applicable diagnostic strategies.

articles.title: MicroRNA-mediated regulation in zika virus-host interactions: implications for neurological and immunological outcomes.
articles.abstract: Zika virus (ZIKV) is a mosquito-borne flavivirus that causes systemic infection with the neurotropic potential. Accordingly, it is a pathogen of significant public health concern worldwide, especially in the Americas. Although most infections are asymptomatic, a small percentage of patients experience complications, such as congenital anomalies in the developing fetus of pregnant women infected with the virus. MicroRNAs (miRNAs), a class of small non-coding RNAs, play crucial roles in regulating cellular signaling pathways and physiological processes. Alterations in miRNA expression have been linked to various disease mechanisms, including those triggered by viral infections. Although substantial progress has been made in understanding ZIKV-host interactions since the 2015-2016 outbreaks, a more comprehensive understanding of the molecular mechanisms involved is still needed. In conclusion, The reviewed evidence suggests multiple dysregulated host miRNAs and mRNAs upon ZIKV infection, which have roles in neurodevelopment. A more comprehensive understanding of dysregulated miRNAs in viral infections may enhance the identification, prevention, and treatment of diseases.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of the Preoperative Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index for Overall Survival After Surgical Resection for Gallbladder Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) reflects the balance between tumor-promoting inflammation and antitumor immunity, but its prognostic role in gallbladder cancer (GBC) remains uncertain. We aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of preoperative SII in patients undergoing resection for GBC.

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis was reported in accordance with PRISMA 2020. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched from inception through November 1, 2025. For the primary meta-analysis, the most comprehensively adjusted hazard ratio (HR) was selected when available; a directly reported univariable HR was used when no adjusted SII-specific estimate was reported. Sensitivity and supplementary analyses pooled multivariable-adjusted and univariable HRs separately. Log-transformed HRs were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation.

RESULTS: Seven retrospective cohorts comprising 2,153 patients were included in the systematic review, of which six studies comprising 2,067 patients contributed directly comparable high-versus-low HRs to the primary meta-analysis. Higher preoperative SII was associated with poorer overall survival (OS) (pooled HR 2.06; 95% CI 1.70-2.51; I² = 3.6%). The association remained significant in the sensitivity analysis restricted to five studies reporting multivariable-adjusted HRs (pooled adjusted HR 2.10; 95% CI 1.39-3.20; I² = 22.0%). The supplementary univariable analysis also demonstrated an association with poorer OS (pooled HR 3.11; 95% CI 1.68-5.75; I² = 75.2%). One study reporting only a continuous per-unit HR was synthesized narratively.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher preoperative SII is associated with poorer OS after resection for GBC. Its incremental value for clinical risk stratification requires prospective evaluation and independent external validation.

SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420251185808.

articles.title: Opportunities to Support Black Preterm Infant Caregiver Strengths to Optimize Dyadic Thriving: The Center and Care Study.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To understand how caregivers of Black preterm infants define thriving for their children long-term and relevant barriers and facilitators to thriving.

STUDY DESIGN: 20 semi-structured interviews were conducted from January 2024-September 2024 with Black caregivers of preterm infants who delivered in the Bay Area, California. Three racially-concordant researchers conducted virtual interviews, coded transcripts using a deductive codebook, and analyzed the data using thematic analysis. Themes were generated and refined through study team consensus.

RESULTS: Participants included 18 female and 2 male caregivers of children born between 23- and 35-weeks gestation. The children were between 9 months and 12 years (mean 6 years) old at the time of the interviews. Most caregivers were born in the U.S., spoke English as a first language, and had postgraduate education. Five themes were identified: (1) Meaning of thriving varies from meeting basic needs to achieving self-actualization throughout their lives; (2) Caregiver engagement and personal strengths have a crucial influence on infant health; (3) Responsive, respectful care and adequate resources optimizes caregiver physical and mental well-being to maximize their strengths; (4) "It takes a village" to support the dyad, including both the hyperlocal home environment and local neighborhood environment; (5) Racial concordance across dyadic medical care and community support systems optimized dyadic physical and mental health.

CONCLUSION: Black preterm infant caregivers' perspectives on thriving for their children are variable and dynamic over time and require intentional dyadic investment and support from local home, neighborhood, community, and medical environments.

articles.title: Prostate: simplified MRI anatomy recognition and training-the P-SMART study: a novel approach to defining prostatic apex, mid-gland and base.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Precise lesion localisation on prostate MRI-specifically, identification of whether at the apex, mid-gland, or base-is essential for effective communication and clinical management. This study aimed to assess interobserver agreement of current practice using the Prostate Imaging-Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) against a novel anatomy-based approach, P-SMART (Prostate Simplified MRI Anatomy Recognition and Training).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multi-reader, two-phase agreement study, used axial and sagittal T2-weighted MRI from a publicly available dataset. Forty MRI cases were annotated with four regions of interest (ROIs). Readers were asked to document ROI location-apex, mid-gland, or base-first using the PI-RADS method, then following a 3-week washout period and short educational intervention, using the P-SMART method. Interobserver agreement was evaluated using Fleiss' kappa (κ) statistics and compared following bootstrap resampling using a paired t-test. Subgroup analyses were performed by reader expertise and prostate size.

RESULTS: Following quality assurance, 156 ROIs were evaluated by 43 readers in each phase of the study. Overall interobserver agreement improved with P-SMART vs PI-RADS (κ = 0.571 vs 0.399; p < 0.001). In subgroup analyses, improvements were consistent for experts (0.663 vs 0.435; p < 0.001), non-experts (0.530 vs 0.393; p < 0.001), large prostates (0.518 vs 0.325; p < 0.001), and small prostates (0.620 vs 0.461; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: The P-SMART approach, designed to align with the PI-RADS sector map, yielded significantly higher interobserver agreement for prostate lesion-level localisation than the PI-RADS method, across reader experience and gland size, though overall agreement was only moderate. Improved reproducibility may support biopsy targeting, active surveillance monitoring, and treatment planning.

KEY POINTS: Question Can a novel method of dividing the prostate into apex, mid-gland, and base improve reader agreement compared to current practice? Findings The P-SMART method to divide the prostate outperformed PI-RADS (Fleiss' kappa 0.571 vs 0.399), improving consistency across experience levels and prostate sizes.

RELEVANCE STATEMENT: More reproducible prostate level assignment supports accurate lesion localisation for biopsy planning, active surveillance, and treatment planning. If validated, P-SMART may improve communication and could be integrated into reporting workflows and software tools.

articles.title: Can Retrieval-Augmented Generation Improve the Potential of the LLMs in Diabetes Health Management? An Assessment Based on Health Management Tasks and Question Complexity.
articles.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has shown significant potential in enhancing the performance of large language models (LLMs) in knowledge-intensive NLP tasks. However, in medical Q&A, particularly in post-diagnosis diabetes management, it remains unclear whether RAG can improve the quality of responses. We developed the DiabMedQA dataset to evaluate the optimization performance of retrieval-augmented LLMs (RA-LLMs) in various Q&A scenarios, encompassing three levels of question complexity and four health management tasks. Our experiments revealed that RA-LLMs achieved higher semantic similarity scores and were generally preferred by clinicians over standard LLMs. In the semantic evaluation, Qwen2.5-14B performed the best, with its BERTScore improving by an average of 10.56% after applying RAG. Notably, the combined analysis showed significant BERTScore gains at all complexity levels, with significantly smaller gains at higher complexity. High-complexity improvements were significant for only one of the four models. In diet advice tasks, the RA-LLM's BERTScore was below 0.8, the lowest among all tasks. Human evaluation showed that Clinicians preferred retrieval-augmented Qwen2.5-14B responses over its baseline responses. Our findings support the value of RAG for post-diagnosis diabetes Q&A and highlight question complexity as an important consideration when applying retrieval augmentation.

articles.title: A Review Study on Sustainable Synthesis of Schiff Bases and Metal Complexes with Implications in Medicinal Chemistry.
articles.abstract: Schiff bases and their transition metal complexes remain foundational architectures in medicinal chemistry due to their versatile structural topography and broad therapeutic spectrum. However, traditional synthetic paradigms carry high environmental costs, heavy solvent burdens, and elevated waste factors. This systematic review maps 115 core studies to evaluate the transition from qualitative eco-friendly descriptions to standardized, quantitative green chemistry performance audits. We examine recent advancements in microwave-assisted, solvent-free, and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven synthetic pathways through strict evaluations of Atom Economy, Environmental Factor (E-Factor), and Process Mass Intensity (PMI) metrics. The structural geometry and spectroscopic properties of complexes coordinating copper, nickel, zinc, iron, and cobalt cores are cross-analyzed with density functional theory (DFT) descriptor models tracking reactivity-selectivity-safety triads. Crucially, this study addresses the biological translation bottleneck by detailing solution speciation profiles, transchelation kinetics, and pharmacokinetic barriers under physiological conditions. Enclosing these systems within advanced nanomedicine matrices, such as layered double hydroxides and metal-organic frameworks, is shown to maximize in vivo oral bioavailability while limiting systemic toxicity. Ultimately, this multi-omic conceptual framework provides an auditable design pathway for developing environmentally sustainable, targeted coordinated therapeutics.

articles.title: Chronic postsurgical pain after minimally invasive cardiac surgery via mini-thoracotomy: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Mini-thoracotomy cardiac surgery avoids sternotomy but requires intercostal access, and persistent pain after this approach is poorly characterized. We determined the frequency and intensity of chronic postsurgical pain (CPSP) 3 months after cardiac surgery via anterolateral mini-thoracotomy and described its sensory features.

METHODS: In this single-center prospective cohort (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02660749), adults undergoing on-pump mitral valve or septal defect surgery through a 5-cm anterolateral mini-thoracotomy received standardized multimodal analgesia. Pain was rated on a 0-10 visual analog scale (VAS). At 3 months, current pain, post-discharge pain descriptors and sensory findings were recorded. CPSP was defined as pain (VAS ≥ 1) at the incision area at 3 months in patients without pre-existing chronic pain; VAS ≥ 4 was considered moderate-to-severe.

RESULTS: Of 80 registered patients, 56 who underwent mini-thoracotomy were analyzed. CPSP was present in 33 patients (58.9%; 95% confidence interval [CI] 45.9-70.8%), but it was mild in all of them: 32 rated their pain as VAS 1 and one as VAS 3, and no patient reported moderate-to-severe pain (0%; 95% CI 0-6.4%). Hypoesthesia (71.4%) and numbness (58.9%) were frequent regardless of CPSP status. Electric shock-like pain was more frequent in patients with CPSP (30.3% vs. 4.3%; p = 0.019) in an unadjusted exploratory comparison. Perioperative and in-hospital pain variables were not associated with CPSP.

CONCLUSIONS: Persistent pain 3 months after mini-thoracotomy cardiac surgery was common but uniformly mild, and moderate-to-severe CPSP was not observed. Sensory disturbances were frequent. CPSP after minimally invasive cardiac surgery should be reported with its intensity, not prevalence alone.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02660749 (https//clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02660749) registered retrospectively on 18 January 2016.

articles.title: The impact of nutrition on glaucoma progression: evidence from systematic literature review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
TOPIC: This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to determine if nutritional interventions have an impact on glaucoma progression. The clinical question being answered is whether nutritional supplementation compared to baseline values has an impact on measures of glaucoma progression, i.e., intraocular pressure (IOP), visual field mean deviation (MD), pattern standard deviation (PSD), and retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Glaucoma is a chronic neurodegenerative optic neuropathy and is a major cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. The conventional treatment for glaucoma is to reduce IOP to slow the progression of glaucoma. However, progression of glaucoma is seen in patients with well-controlled IOP levels, suggesting that there is a need to look for additional therapeutic options, including nutritional factors, antioxidants, omega-3 fatty acids, vitamins, and nutraceuticals.

METHODS: A comprehensive search of the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), PubMed, PubMed Central (PMC), and Google Scholar was undertaken from date of inception to 6 March, 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies evaluating the diet, nutritional status, or nutritional supplementation in adults with glaucoma and reporting outcomes on the progression of the disease were considered for inclusion. Risk of bias in the included studies was assessed with the revised Cochrane Risk of Bias tool (RoB 2) for RCTs and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for cohort studies.

RESULTS: Qualitative synthesis included 21 studies with 1,209 participants, and 11 studies were available for meta-analysis. Antioxidants, omega-3 fatty acids, vitamins, and neuroprotective agents such as coenzyme Q10, ginkgo biloba extract, citicoline, and palmitoylethanolamide were included. Meta-analysis found no statistically significant change at six months in IOP (mean difference - 2.42 mmHg, 95% CI - 7.53 to 2.70), MD (2.23 dB, 95% CI - 1.04 to 5.50), or RNFL thickness (- 16.00 µm, 95% CI - 70.77 to 38.76), although there was a significant decrease in PSD (- 0.33 dB, 95% CI - 0.47 to - 0.19).

CONCLUSION: The current evidence suggests that nutritional interventions do not significantly affect major indicators of glaucoma progression in the short term; the small PSD reduction, based on three cohort studies, should not be interpreted as a clinically meaningful neuroprotective effect. Given the low-to-moderate certainty of the underlying evidence, nutritional supplements may be considered as a potential adjunct to conventional treatment, though evidence supporting their routine clinical use remains insufficient; the long-term effects of nutritional supplements on glaucoma need to be determined through large, long-term RCTs.

articles.title: From glucose metabolism to pyroptosis: the regulatory role of the CD2AP/Nephrin axis in podocyte injury in diabetic nephropathy.
articles.abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a major complication of diabetes, characterized by podocyte injury and progressive renal function decline. The CD2AP/Nephrin axis is crucial for podocyte integrity, yet its involvement in glycolysis-triggered pyroptosis during DN remains unclear. This study explored the regulatory mechanism of the CD2AP/Nephrin axis in high glucose-induced podocyte injury using MPC-5 cells and DN mice. CD2AP overexpression, Disulfiram-mediated pyroptosis inhibition, CD2AP knockdown, and CD2AP overexpression combined with nephrin knockdown rescue experiments were performed. Molecular assays including Western blot, immunofluorescence, ELISA, and histopathological staining were applied to detect pyroptosis markers, glycolysis indicators, and renal function parameters. High glucose disrupted the CD2AP/Nephrin axis, activated caspase-1-dependent pyroptosis, and impaired GLUT4-mediated glucose transport in MPC-5 cells. CD2AP overexpression reversed high glucose-induced upregulation of glycolytic products (lactate, pyruvate) and key enzymes (hexokinase, phosphofructokinase, pyruvate kinase), while reducing pyroptosis markers-effects, which were further enhanced by Disulfiram. Conversely, CD2AP knockdown exacerbated glycolytic overload, NLRP3 inflammasome activation, and pyroptotic cell death. Mechanistically, nephrin knockdown abrogated CD2AP's protective effects on glycolysis regulation and pyroptosis inhibition, confirming nephrin dependence. In DN mice, CD2AP overexpression alleviated hyperglycemia, proteinuria, renal dysfunction (elevated Scr, BUN, reduced Ccr), glomerular hypertrophy and fibrosis, and inhibited GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis via GLUT4 regulation, with Disulfiram enhancing these effects. CD2AP regulates glycolysis-triggered podocyte pyroptosis through the Nephrin/GLUT4 axis, providing a potential therapeutic target for DN.

articles.title: Deep progressive reconstruction for low-dose ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT imaging in pediatric patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the performance of the deep progressive reconstruction method (DPR) for low-dose 18F-FDG PET imaging in pediatric patients.

METHODS: Forty-one pediatric patients who underwent clinical 18F-FDG PET/CT were retrospectively enrolled. List-mode PET data acquired at 2 min per bed position were reconstructed using OSEM and DPR, generating the standard-dose images labelled OSEM_full and DPR_full, respectively. To simulate low-dose conditions, the acquisition time of the original list-mode data was reduced to 1/n (n = 2, 3, 4) and reconstructed with DPR, yielding DPR_1/2, DPR_1/3, and DPR_1/4. For all reconstruction groups, quantitative metrics including the standard uptake value (SUV) and coefficient of variation (COV) in the liver, blood pool, and gluteus maximus, as well as lesion tumour-to-background ratio (TBR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR). Subjective image quality was evaluated based on overall image quality, lesion conspicuity, and image noise. Age-stratified subgroup analysis was performed, with OSEM_full as the reference standard.

RESULTS: DPR reconstructions showed good agreement in quantitative accuracy with reference imaging. Compared with OSEM_full, DPR_full and DPR_1/2 significantly lowered background COV, DPR_1/3 showed comparable background noise, while DPR_1/4 presented increased noise. All DPR groups yielded significantly higher lesion TBR, and DPR_full, DPR_1/2, DPR_1/3 improved lesion CNR, whereas DPR_1/4 showed reduced CNR. Subjectively, DPR_full and DPR_1/2 achieved significantly higher image quality scores, with over 60% of cases rated as excellent. Age subgroup analysis revealed that DPR_1/3 performance was age-dependent, with better noise control and higher CNR in older children but poorer performance in younger children, suggesting its suitability as an age-adaptive dose reduction strategy. Notably, all DPR protocols improved lesion TBR across all age groups.

CONCLUSION: DPR enables substantial dose reduction in pediatric ¹⁸F-FDG PET while maintaining or even improving objective and subjective image quality. Among the dose-reduction protocols, DPR_1/2 provides the best overall performance, while DPR_1/3 represents the optimal balance between dose reduction and image quality, particularly in older children. These findings support the clinical potential for personalised low-dose PET strategies in the pediatric population.

articles.title: Prognostic value of integrated dynamic NLR and [18F]FDG-PET/CT parameters in resectable non-small cell lung cancer treated with neoadjuvant immunotherapy plus chemotherapy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of dynamic [18F]FDG PET/CT metabolic parameters and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), individually and in combination, in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) receiving neoadjuvant immunotherapy plus chemotherapy.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 168 NSCLC patients treated with neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy followed by surgery. Pre- and post-treatment PET metabolic parameters assessed by iPERCIST and peripheral blood NLR were collected. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with Cox regression were performed to identify predictors of disease-free survival (DFS).

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 25.2 months (95% CI, 21.0-29.3 months), 59 patients experienced recurrence. Post-treatment PET metabolic parameters, their changes, and post-treatment NLR were significantly associated with DFS. Among these parameters, ΔSUVmax and post-treatment NLR were identified as independent prognostic factors. Patients were stratified into three risk groups according to the combination of ΔSUVmax and post-treatment NLR, with significantly different DFS outcomes among groups (p = 0.001). Patients achieving iCMR/iPMR according to iPERCIST criteria showed longer DFS than those without favorable metabolic response (p = 0.005) .

CONCLUSIONS: Dynamic PET metabolic parameters, and post-treatment NLR hold significant prognostic value following neoadjuvant immunotherapy plus chemotherapy in NSCLC. A combined model integrating PET metabolic parameters and post-treatment NLR stratified patients into distinct risk groups, suggesting potential utility in postoperative risk assessment.

articles.title: Photobiomodulation for radiotherapy-induced dysgeusia in head and neck cancer patients: a pilot randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract: Dysgeusia is a frequent complication in patients with head and neck cancer (HNC) undergoing radiotherapy and may negatively affect nutritional status and quality of life. This pilot study evaluated the effect of photobiomodulation (PBM) on the management of radiotherapy-induced dysgeusia. Sixteen patients undergoing radiotherapy for HNC were randomly assigned to either a PBM group (n = 8) or a zinc sulfate group (n = 8). Objective taste identification tests evaluating sweet, bitter, sour, and salty tastes were performed at three time points: before radiotherapy (T0), at the 15th radiotherapy session (T1), and at the 30th radiotherapy session (T2). Salty taste was the most affected taste modality in both groups. At T2, sweet taste was correctly identified by 75.0% of patients in the zinc group and 50.0% in the PBM group. In contrast, bitter taste was preserved in 87.5% of patients in the PBM group and 75.0% in the zinc group. Sour taste was preserved in 87.5% and 62.5% of patients in the PBM and zinc groups, respectively, whereas salty taste was preserved in 50.0% and 25.0% of patients, respectively. No statistically significant differences were observed between groups at T0, T1, or T2 (all p > 0.05). Although no statistically significant differences were identified, PBM was associated with better preservation of sour, bitter, and salty taste perception, particularly after the 30th radiotherapy session. These preliminary findings suggest that PBM may represent a promising supportive strategy for the management of treatment-related dysgeusia in patients with HNC undergoing radiotherapy.

articles.title: Atrial Fibrillation Across the Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation Continuum: A Systematic Scoping Evidence Map.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter (AF/AFL) are clinically relevant complications across the haematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) continuum, but evidence supporting phase-specific management and transitions of care remains fragmented. This review aimed to map direct HCT-AF evidence, broader HCT cardiovascular evidence, and relevant guidance; identify major evidence-to-care gaps; and define an evidence-informed framework for AF/AFL management across the HCT continuum.

RECENT FINDINGS: We conducted a systematic scoping evidence map of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, supplemented by a predefined closed hand-search of guidance sources. Twenty-seven clinical reports and 15 guidance documents were retained, yielding 42 evidence sources. Direct evidence was concentrated on AF/AFL incidence, timing, predictors, recurrence, and prognosis, whereas evidence for treatment selection, rhythm-surveillance strategies, anticoagulation during thrombocytopenia, and survivorship follow-up remained limited and frequently dependent on extrapolated guidance. The evidence map informed a phase-specific care framework spanning pre-HCT risk assessment, risk-adapted rhythm surveillance, structured acute AF/AFL assessment, dynamic anticoagulation reassessment, medication-safety review, and accountable discharge and survivorship follow-up. AF/AFL after HCT should be viewed as a longitudinal care challenge rather than an isolated inpatient arrhythmic event. The proposed phase-specific quality-of-care processes are hypothesis-generating and require prospective evaluation for feasibility, reproducibility, implementation, and association with clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Vitamin D receptor activator-associated calcium-alkali syndrome-like phenotype without calcium supplementation: a case series of seven patients.
articles.abstract: Vitamin D receptor activators (VDRAs) are widely prescribed for osteoporosis and CKD-mineral and bone disorder in Japan. Although hypercalcemia and acute kidney injury (AKI) are recognized adverse effects, metabolic alkalosis in these patients has received limited attention as a feature of calcium-alkali syndrome (CAS).We retrospectively reviewed patients with VDRA-associated hypercalcemia at our institution between April 2016 and June 2026, applying study-defined operational criteria for a CAS-like phenotype: hypercalcemia, elevated bicarbonate compatible with a metabolic alkalosis component (HCO₃⁻ ≥ 26 mmol/L), and AKI (KDIGO criteria). Seven elderly women fulfilled all criteria. Six received eldecalcitol (0.75 μg/day) and one received alfacalcidol (1.0 μg/day). Underlying CKD was present in six patients.Time from initiation to onset ranged from 1 to 120 months (median 18 months). Three cases had no identified exogenous alkali source. The serum Na-Cl difference was elevated in all patients (range 36-53 mEq/L). Renal outcomes were complete recovery in three patients, partial recovery in two, and non-recovery in one; one patient died of worsening heart failure.VDRA-associated hypercalcemia can present as a CAS-like phenotype even without calcium supplementation, and renal outcomes may be irreversible. Because the temporal relationship between hypercalcemia and metabolic alkalosis cannot be established from these retrospective data, the main clinical message is that elderly patients receiving VDRAs, particularly those with CKD or relevant concomitant medications, require periodic calcium monitoring and prompt evaluation when nonspecific symptoms, AKI, or an elevated Na-Cl difference are observed.

articles.title: Niwan Bazhen acupuncture activates CLEC3B-Mediated PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway to suppress autophagy and exerts neuroprotection against ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) is one of the leading causes of disability and mortality worldwide. Excessive autophagy triggered by cerebral ischemia exacerbates neuronal apoptosis and necrosis. Acupuncture at Niwan Bazhen (Acu) has unique advantages in stroke rehabilitation, and our previous studies have demonstrated its ability to alleviate neuronal apoptosis after IS. However, the mechanisms underlying its therapeutic effects remain elusive. Transcriptomic microarray expression profiling revealed that C-type lectin domain family 3 member B (CLEC3B) was significantly downregulated in the brain of middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) rats, and this downregulation was reversed by Acu. Lentivirus-mediated overexpression of CLEC3B improved neurological function, reduced cerebral infarction, and alleviated cerebral edema in MCAO/R rats, and decreased neuronal apoptosis in the peri-infarct cortex. Western blot analysis demonstrated that CLEC3B overexpression activated the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway, reduced the LC3-II/LC3-I ratio, and decreased autophagosome numbers. Conversely, knockdown of CLEC3B nearly abolished the neuroprotective effects of Acu in MCAO/R rats. In vitro, CLEC3B dificiency inhibited the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway and impaired autophagic flux in rat cortical neurons under oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) conditions. Treatment of OGD/R-exposed rat cortical neurons with recombinant CLEC3B protein or CLEC3B-overexresing lentivirus activated the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway and inhibited autophagy, an effect that was abrogated by the PI3K inhibitor LY294002. Collectively, these findings indicate that CLEC3B, as a core target of Acu regulation, exerts neuroprotection against IS by inhibiting excessive neuronal autophagy via activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway.

articles.title: Feasibility and tolerability of combining 6 Hz transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) at 3.2 mA and digital cognitive training in older adults with mild cognitive impairment.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) may enhance cognition and potentiate digital cognitive training (DCT) in mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Optimal intensity remains uncertain because higher currents may increase cortical electric fields but raise tolerability concerns. We evaluated feasibility and tolerability of 3.2 mA tACS plus DCT, and exploratorily assessed active versus sham effects on inhibitory control and cognitive transfer.

METHODS: Ten older adults with MCI received five daily 6-Hz tACS sessions over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex during DCT; ten sham-arm participants from a randomized trial completed identical DCT. Feasibility and tolerability were assessed by adherence, attrition, and side-effect monitoring. Exploratory efficacy used repeated-measures ANOVA with Bonferroni-corrected paired comparisons. Outcomes included antisaccade total errors, verbal and visual memory, and visuoconstructive abilities.

RESULTS: All participants completed treatment (100% adherence). Active-session side effects were mild in 67% and moderate in 23%; no severe events occurred. Side-effect burden was unrelated to DCT performance (p = 0.22). Antisaccade total errors showed a group × time interaction (p = 0.028), favoring active stimulation. Reaction time showed no stimulation-specific effects. Verbal and visual memory showed time effects (p = 0.016 and p = 0.002), whereas visuoconstructive abilities showed a trend-level group × time interaction favoring active stimulation (p = 0.054).

CONCLUSIONS: Higher-intensity tACS plus DCT was feasible and well tolerated in older adults with MCI. Exploratory findings suggest that active stimulation may improve inhibitory control and facilitate transfer to selected cognitive domains. Confirmation in the ongoing randomized controlled trial is warranted.

articles.title: HSF1 genotyping and seasonal transcriptional profiling in tropically adapted indicine cattle PCR amplificationbreeds.
articles.abstract: Global warming threatens dairy production worldwide, impacting animal health and welfare as well as production economics. This necessitates the identification of thermotolerance markers. Heat shock factor 1 (HSF1) regulates the cellular heat shock response in both humans and animals, yet its genetic architecture has been sparsely evaluated in Bos indicus cows. This study characterizes HSF1 polymorphisms and seasonal expression profiles in two heat-resilient indicine cattle breeds: Sahiwal and Kankrej. We genotyped 100 cows (50 per breed) for two HSF1 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs): T15531C (intron 3) and G19315T (3'UTR), previously linked to thermotolerance in exotic cattle breeds. Additionally, physiological parameters of the genotyped cows were recorded, and seasonal transcriptional profiling of HSF1 was conducted in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). Sanger sequencing revealed that both breeds were completely monomorphic for the CC (T15531C) and GG (G19315T) genotypes. Furthermore, a novel C > T transition at g.19,364 (3'UTR) was identified. This variant was polymorphic (exclusively CT heterozygotes) in the Kankrej cows but monomorphic (CC) in Sahiwal cows. Transcriptional profiling demonstrated a significant upregulation of HSF1 mRNA during the summer and hot-humid seasons in both breeds, a response that directly corresponded with elevated physiological stress indicators such as rectal temperature and respiration rate. These findings highlight the genetic conservation of the targeted HSF1 loci in these populations. The novel g.19,364 variant serves as a descriptive candidate marker that requires future functional validation and genotype-phenotype association in larger populations to evaluate its role in conferring thermotolerance in cows.

articles.title: Too good to be true? AI performance in CT-based urinary stone detection and classification: EAU endourology systematic review and diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate pooled performance of artificial intelligence (AI) in computed tomography (CT)-based urinary stone detection and classification and identify methodological factors influencing results.

METHODS: This review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261319940). A systematic search of PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar was conducted up to March 15, 2026. Studies evaluating AI-based detection or classification of urolithiasis on CT with available validation/test cohort data (sensitivity/specificity or 2 × 2 tables) were included. A bivariate random-effects model generated pooled sensitivity, specificity, and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) curves. Meta-regression explored moderators related to dataset composition and AI pipelines. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-AI.

RESULTS: 14 studies (five detection-based, nine classification-based) were included. Overall pooled sensitivity and specificity were 0.967 and 0.979 (AUC 0.987). Classification studies demonstrated higher pooled sensitivity (0.977) and specificity (0.990) compared with detection studies (0.935 and 0.919; AUC 0.945). Significant heterogeneity was observed and influenced by training sample size, class imbalance, presence of bladder stones or other pathologies, and architectural choices. Most studies had high risk of bias, lacked external validation, and frequently used slice-level or pre-selected datasets, potentially overestimating performance.

CONCLUSION: Substantial methodological heterogeneity and high risk of bias limit clinical generalizability. Detection studies better reflect real-world workflows and show lower performance. Current evidence does not support routine clinical implementation without standardized reporting and robust external validation.

articles.title: Behavioral, biochemical, histological, and electrophysiological changes following intracerebral injection of bone marrow stem cell-derived exosomes in male rat models of Alzheimer's disease.
articles.abstract: Recently, researchers have been exploring how exosomes can help treat neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer's disease (AD), has attracted considerable attention. This study aimed to investigate behavioral, biochemical, histological, and electrophysiological changes following the administration of bone marrow stem cell-derived exosomes (Exo-BMSCs) in AD model rats. Animals were divided into control, Lesion (Lesion, Lesion + saline), and treatment (Lesion + BMSCs, Lesion + Exo-BMSCs) groups. BMSCs were extracted from the bone marrow of newborn rats. Exosomes were extracted from the BMSCs culture medium using a chemical kit. Saline, BMSCs, and Exo-BMSCs were injected bilaterally into the nucleus of Meynert (NBM) one week after electrical lesion. 28 days after injection, behavioral, electrophysiological, and histological changes, as well as ACh and BDNF expression levels in the hippocampus, were evaluated. Electrical lesion of the NBM caused a significant decrease in passive avoidance memory retrieval, a significant decrease in ACh and BDNF levels, changes in EEG wave frequencies in the hippocampus, and histological changes in the NBM, similar to those observed in AD. On the other hand, injection of BMSCs and Exo-BMSCs into the NBM significantly improved passive avoidance memory, an increase in BDNF levels, an increase in power of gamma waves, and improved histological changes compared to the Lesion groups. The increase in power of gamma waves was significant only in the Exo-BMSC-treated group. Injection of BMSCs and Exo-BMSCs into the NBM can significantly improve disease symptoms. This improvement was more pronounced in the Exo-BMSCs-treated group. The concurrent increase in BDNF suggests that this neurotrophin contributes to the observed effects.

articles.title: Mitral valve disease in rheumatic heart disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, antiphospholipid syndrome, and rheumatoid Arthritis.
articles.abstract: Mitral valve disease occurs in rheumatic heart disease (RHD) and selected systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases, but similar lesions may have different underlying mechanisms. This structured narrative review examines epidemiological, mechanistic, imaging, and management evidence, distinguishing established pathways from incompletely validated mechanisms and hypotheses. In RHD, post-streptococcal valvulitis leads to fibrotic remodeling, commissural fusion, and chordal shortening, producing mitral stenosis, regurgitation, or mixed disease. A meta-analysis of 215,552 children and adolescents in endemic settings reported echocardiographically detected RHD in 24 per 1000. In systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), typical findings include leaflet thickening, Libman-Sacks vegetations, and regurgitation; embolic complications may occur despite mild valve dysfunction. Among 508 clinically selected patients with SLE undergoing echocardiography, 27.4% had heart valve involvement and 11.2% had mitral involvement. Immunothrombotic mechanisms may contribute to these lesions, but direct validation in human valve tissue remains incomplete. In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), a prospective cohort found an association with incident mitral regurgitation (adjusted hazard ratio 1.54, 95% confidence interval 1.32-1.81), but not mitral stenosis. Myocardial imaging findings do not establish a causal link to regurgitation. These findings support anatomy- and severity-based assessment in RHD, combined valvular and thromboembolic evaluation in SLE/APS, and assessment of conventional regurgitation mechanisms in RA. The framework informs clinical interpretation within existing guidelines, while proposed disease-specific mechanisms require further validation.

articles.title: Sirolimus-induced improvement of immune dysregulation associated hepatosplenomegaly in common variable immunodeficiency: a case-based review.
articles.abstract: Common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) is the most common primary immune defficiency in adults. Patients with CVID present with predominant antibody deficiency and reduced serum levels of immunoglobulin class G, A and/ or M. The disease is frequently complicated by non-infectious organ involvement, including hepatosplenomegaly secondary to immune dysregulation and lymphoproliferation. Sirolimus is a mTORC1 inhibitor, used as immunosuppressant in transplant medicine, increasingly inborn errors of immunity with lymphoproliferation and autoimmunity, including CVID and monogenic CVID-like disorders. Therefore, we describe the case of a 50-year-old patient diagnosed with CVID for 5 years, on regular IVIG (intravenous immunoglobulins) replacement who developed progressive hepatosplenomegaly and cytopenias despite adequate infection preventive healthcare. The patient reported increasing abdominal enlargement, dyspnea, and fatigue. She had also noted excessive daytime and nighttime sweating, initially partly attributed to menopausal status. Physical examination confirmed marked hepatosplenomegaly. Initial evaluation excluded acute infection and overt lymphoma. Abdominal imaging revealed hepatosplenomegaly without focal lesions, raising suspicion of immune-mediated lymphoproliferation related to CVID. Sirolimus was introduced as a steroid-sparing agent for presumed immune dysregulation. During sirolimus treatment, spleen length decreased from 23 cm before initiation to 13 cm after 5 months and 12 cm after 7 months, while liver size fell from 18 cm to 15 cm. Platelet count rose from 37 to 75 × 10³/µL, and aspartate aminotransferase activity declined from 77 to 58 U/L, with alanine aminotransferase dropping from 93 to 47 U/L. Leukopenia, neutropenia, and elevated alkaline phosphatase activity, however, persisted. The patient reported improvement in constitutional and abdominal symptoms,and no serious infectious complications occurred during treatment. This case demonstrates a marked organ response and a partial platelet response to sirolimus in complicated CVID, suggesting that mTOR inhibition may be considered in carefully selected patients with CVID-associated immune dysregulation and lymphoproliferative hepatosplenic involvement, although its efficacy and safety require confirmation in larger studies.

articles.title: A phase 1 study of 4'-thio-2'-deoxycytidine in patients with solid tumors.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The DNA methyltransferase (DNMT) inhibitor 4'-thio-2'-deoxycytidine (TdCyd), a second-generation cytidine analog, demonstrated potent preclinical antitumor activity and favorable pharmacokinetics, which led us to explore its safety, efficacy and anti-tumor activity in patients with solid tumors.

METHODS: Adult patients with advanced solid tumors received TdCyd orally on days 1-5 and 8-12 in 21-day cycles. Dose escalation proceeded according to design 4 of the Simon accelerated titration design, changing to a 3 + 3 dose escalation design in the event of dose-limiting toxicities. Blood samples were collected for circulating tumor cell (CTC) evaluation of p16 re-expression as a marker of TdCyd epigenetic modulation, and for pharmacokinetic analysis.

RESULTS: Twenty-seven patients were enrolled. The maximum tolerated dose was not reached. The best response was prolonged stable disease (SD), with 3 patients on treatment for ≥ 6 cycles, and there was no dose-response relationship. An increase in the proportion of p16-expressing cytokeratin-positive (CK+) CTCs was detected in 71% (15 of 21) of patients evaluable for p16 response at every dose level in which patients were assessable for pharmacodynamic response; p16 re-expression in vimentin-positive CTCs was reported in 38% (6 of 16) of evaluable patients. Plasma levels of TdCyd metabolites were largely dose proportional and higher levels were detected in patients with higher incidence and severity of study drug-related adverse events.

CONCLUSION: Prolonged SD and p16 re-expression at lower TdCyd dose levels suggest that longer exposures to low concentrations is worth exploring in future trials, including studies of TdCyd in therapeutic combinations.

articles.title: Intravesical BCG-induced granulomatous prostatitis mimicking prostate cancer in patients with non-muscle invasive bladder cancer: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) therapy is a standard-of-care for non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC), and granulomatous prostatitis (GP) is a side effect often misdiagnosed as prostate cancer (PCa). We conducted a systematic review to clarify the clinical spectrum of BCG-induced GP.

METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science were searched in June 2026. We sought studies reporting GP associated with BCG therapy for NMIBC, including case reports and case series. Risk of bias was evaluated using ROBINS-I and JBI tools. Findings were synthesized narratively (CRD420261324758).

RESULTS: Forty-seven studies were included, comprising 23 case reports, 19 case series, and 5 comparative studies. In case series, abnormal digital rectal examination findings were reported in 100/240 (42%) evaluable cases. PSA elevation (> 4 ng/mL) occurred in 104/194 (54%) patients but often declined spontaneously during follow-up. Suspicious MRI findings were common, with PI-RADS ≥ 4 lesions reported in 71/82 (87%) cases, whereas biopsy-confirmed PCa was detected only in 12/151 (7.9%) patients. However, Grade Group and definitions of clinically significant PCa (csPCa) were incompletely and inconsistently reported, precluding a reliable estimate of csPCa frequency. Limitations include the predominance of descriptive studies and potential selection bias.

CONCLUSION: BCG-induced GP frequently presents with transient PSA elevation and suspicious MRI findings that rarely indicate true PCa. In BCG-exposed patients with elevated PSA or PI-RADS ≥ 4 lesions, structured observation with careful follow-up should be considered before proceeding to immediate biopsy.

articles.title: Consensus on a core outcome set for ventilation trials in critically ill patients with acute brain injury: results of an international Delphi consensus study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Clinical research evaluating mechanical ventilation liberation in patients with acute brain injury (ABI) shows substantial outcome heterogeneity, limiting evidence synthesis. We aimed to develop an internationally endorsed core outcome set (COS) and a hierarchical composite endpoint for ventilation trials in neurocritical care.

METHODS: Following COS-STAD/COS-STAP standards, we conducted a 4-round international Delphi study. Candidate outcomes were identified via a scoping review. A multidisciplinary panel from 31 countries scored outcomes using a 9-point GRADE scale. Inclusion required >70% rating as "critical" (score 7-9) and ≤15% as "not important" (1-3). Two consensus meetings were held to categorize outcomes, select representative measures, and ratify a hierarchical composite endpoint.

RESULTS: 78 stakeholders participated in Round 1; 60 completed all rounds (23.1% attrition). Fifty-four outcomes achieved Delphi consensus. At Consensus Meeting 1, these were organized into 16 categories; the highest-scoring outcome per category was selected. Three outcomes were not ratified due to disease-specificity (NIH Stroke Scale) or lack of universal applicability (brain death, coma-free days). The final COS comprised 13 outcomes across 5 domains: respiratory function, survival, complications, functional status, and quality of life. A 3-level hierarchical composite endpoint was ratified at Consensus Meeting 2: (1) intensive care unit survival, (2) no reintubation within 72 hours, and (3) days alive without mechanical ventilation.

CONCLUSION: This study establishes the first COS for ventilation weaning trials in ABI patients. Widespread adoption of these 13 outcomes and the hierarchical composite endpoint will standardize reporting, enable meaningful evidence synthesis, and facilitate clinical translation in neurocritical care.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Core Outcome Measures in Effectiveness Trials (COMET) Initiative, registration number 2320.

articles.title: Vasopressors as immunomodulators: a hidden axis in septic shock.
Serum sodium and chloride interplay and the effect of empagliflozin in heart failure: an EMPEROR-Pooled analysis.
articles.journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: SGLT2 inhibitors promote changes in the kidney that influence water and electrolyte handling. Prior studies in heart failure (HF) suggested that SGLT2 inhibitors produce a slight increase in serum sodium over time, but little is known about their impact on serum chloride and the sodium-chloride interplay.

AIMS: To study the serum sodium-chloride interdependence, their prognostic associations, and the impact of empagliflozin on their levels over time.

METHODS: EMPEROR-Pooled data (N = 9718) was used to create four mutually exclusive sodium-chloride categories based on quintiles (Q) of variable values distribution at baseline: (1) Q1Na+/Q1Cl-; (2) Q1Na+/ ≥ Q2Cl-; 3) ≥ Q2Na+/Q1Cl-; and (4) ≥ Q2Na+/ ≥ Q2Cl-. Cox models were used to study the association of these categories with outcomes. Mixed models for repeated measures were used to study the impact of empagliflozin vs placebo on sodium and chloride levels over time.

RESULTS: Mean serum sodium levels were 140.9 ± 3.0 mmol/L and chloride 100.9 ± 3.6 mmol/L. Patients with both Na+ < 140 mmol/L and Cl- < 99 mmol/L (Q1Na+/Q1Cl-) were more frequently treated with loop diuretics and experienced 1.3 to 1.7-fold higher rates of HF events and mortality compared to patients with ≥ Q2Na+/ ≥ Q2Cl-. Patients with Q1Cl- exhibited higher mortality rates, irrespective of Na+ levels. The beneficial effects of empagliflozin were not influenced by Na+/Cl- levels; interactionP > 0.1. Compared to placebo, empagliflozin slightly increased Na+ and Cl- by + 0.1 mmol/L on average, particularly from week 32 onwards (P < 0.05), while reducing serum bicarbonate levels by -0.2 mmol/L on average (P < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: In ambulatory HF, lower serum chloride levels were associated with poor outcomes independently of sodium, whereas lower sodium levels were associated with poor outcomes only in the presence of relatively low chloride. The beneficial effects of empagliflozin were not impacted by sodium or chloride.

articles.title: Inherited cardiovascular risk and its impact on healthspan and lifespan.
articles.abstract: Genetic disposition for cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a major determinant of aging-related traits, such as healthspan, dementia, and frailty. While rare monogenic disorders provide important mechanistic insights, most CVDs and aging-related traits are driven by the cumulative effects of numerous common genetic variants, resulting in a polygenic risk architecture. Analyses of genes and pathways affected by these variants revealed significant correlations in the genetic architectures of CVD and aging, which appear to promote each other bidirectionally. Thus, CVD and aging share common genetic mechanisms, linking inherited cardiovascular risk to frailty, dementia, reduced healthspan, and shortened lifespan-and, conversely, explaining why aging is the strongest risk factor for atherosclerosis. Advances in genome-wide association studies have also enabled the construction of a polygenic risk score (PRS), which quantifies inherited CVD risk and facilitates early risk stratification beyond conventional clinical assessment. Importantly, individuals at high polygenic risk for CVD derive greater benefit from preventive strategies, which reduce their lifelong burden of CVD risk and ultimately promote healthy aging. Therefore, personalizing clinical risk assessment by integrating genetic testing for both CVD and aging-related traits may be of clinical importance. Specifically, lifestyle modification and preventive therapies based not only on conventional risk assessment, but also on polygenic risks may offer an individualized life-course approach for precision prevention, shifting cardiovascular care from reactive disease management toward the promotion of healthy aging.

articles.title: Gene-metabolite-cardiac associations in the Chronic Kidney Disease in Children (CKiD) study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Characterizing gene-metabolite-cardiac associations in childhood chronic kidney disease (CKD) has the potential to identify new research directions or therapeutic targets for mitigating the excessive cardiovascular risk in childhood CKD.

METHODS: The Chronic Kidney Disease in Children (CKiD) is a prospective cohort that recruited children with eGFR 30-90 ml/min/1.73 m2 across 54 North American centers. Predictor and outcome variables included genotypes, metabolite levels, left ventricular mass index (LVMI) z-score, and left ventricular filling pressure (E/e'). Multivariable linear regression analyses assessed metabolite associations with either LVMI z-score or E/e', adjusting for age, sex, CKD duration, glomerular etiology, renin-angiotensin-aldosterone-system blockade, hypertension, anemia, dyslipidemia, eGFR, and proteinuria. Significance was based on the Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate <0.05. Metabolites associated with cardiac markers were carried forward for a metabolite-genome-wide association study (mGWAS). Linear regression calculated the residual metabolite variability not explained by age, sex, and eGFR. Linear regression assessed metabolite residual variability versus genetic variant dosage at the Bonferroni-corrected genome-wide significance threshold (corrected for number of metabolites assessed).

RESULTS: 556 unique participants with 574 metabolites and ~8.4 million SNPs were included. Sphingomyelin (d18:2/d18:1) and hypotaurine were associated with LVMI z-score. Isobutyrylglycine and 3beta-hydroxy-5-cholestenoate were associated with E/e'. Multiple genetic variants associated with these metabolites at p < 1.25E-8 (p < [5E-8]/4, Bonferroni-corrected genome-wide significance threshold).

CONCLUSIONS: We identified metabolites associated with cardiac markers in children with CKD. We identified genetic associations with variability in these metabolites. Collectively, these gene-metabolite associations suggest roles for inflammation, increased oxidative stress, mitochondrial and energy dysmetabolism, and gut microbial dysbiosis in mediating cardiac pathology in childhood CKD. A higher resolution version of the Graphical abstract is available as Supplementary information.

articles.title: Serum creatinine monitoring after acute kidney injury in hospitalized children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is common among hospitalized children and is associated with adverse short- and long-term outcomes. Under-recognition of pediatric AKI and incomplete serum creatinine monitoring contribute to low follow-up rates. Our objectives were to evaluate AKI incidence, electronic health record documentation, and factors associated with creatinine re-measurement after AKI onset among hospitalized children.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of all hospitalized children admitted to a quaternary pediatric hospital in Toronto, Canada, between January 2021 and December 2022. Children were excluded if they were <3 months of age, had pre-existing chronic kidney disease, or had no serum creatinine measurements during hospitalization. The primary exposure was AKI by KDIGO criteria. The primary outcome was repeat creatinine measurement within 1-day of AKI onset. Secondary outcomes included repeat creatinine measurements by different post-AKI timepoints and kidney recovery by discharge.

RESULTS: Among 8992 hospitalized children, 1080 (12%) experienced AKI (stage 1: 650 [60.2%], stage 2: 263 [24.4%], and stage 3: 167 [15.5%]). AKI was documented by diagnostic code in only 59 children (sensitivity 5.5%, specificity 99.9%, PPV 86.8%, NPV 88.6%). Creatinine re-measurement occurred in 803 (74.4%) within 1-day of AKI onset and 914 (84.6%) within 3-days. Kidney recovery by discharge occurred in 686 (69.3%) AKI survivors. Post-discharge, 528 (53.3%) and 575 (58.1%) children had repeat creatinine measurements by 3-months and 6-months, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: AKI is common among hospitalized children but under-detected by diagnostic codes and under-monitored pre- and post-discharge. Future research should evaluate systems to improve pediatric AKI detection and creatinine monitoring.

articles.title: Vaping-associated acute tubular injury presenting as a pulmonary-renal syndrome in an adolescent.
articles.abstract: Electronic cigarette use is increasingly common among adolescents and is associated with a widening range of toxic effects, although renal complications remain poorly characterized and are rarely confirmed histologically in this age group. We describe a previously healthy 14-year-old boy, a regular e-cigarette user, who developed oliguria, dark-colored urine, severe hypertension, seizures, and pulmonary infiltrates two days after his last use. Serum creatinine rose to 10.6 mg/dL, requiring hemodialysis. The presentation raised concern for a pulmonary-renal syndrome, prompting empiric corticosteroids and plasma exchange. However, serological testing was negative, urinary β2-microglobulin was markedly elevated, and kidney biopsy showed acute tubular injury without glomerular or immune-mediated disease. Immunosuppression was withdrawn, and kidney function recovered completely, remaining normal at 18 months. This case shows that vaping-associated acute tubular injury can mimic a pulmonary-renal syndrome and highlights the value of kidney biopsy in adolescents with unexplained severe acute kidney injury.

articles.title: The effect of systemic naloxone administration on diverse conditioned fear behaviors.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Freezing has historically been the primary measure of conditioned fear, despite evidence that defensive behaviors are diverse and sexually dimorphic. Although mu-opioid receptor (MOR) signaling regulates fear learning and conditioned analgesia, its influence on diverse defensive behaviors remains unclear.

OBJECTIVES: This study investigated the effects of systemic MOR antagonism on freezing, darting, shock responsivity, and ultrasonic vocalizations (USVs) during fear conditioning and recall in male and female rats.

METHODS: Adult male and female Sprague Dawley rats received naloxone (5 mg/kg, i.p.) or saline before auditory fear conditioning consisting of seven tone-shock pairings. Fear recall was assessed 24 hours later through three tone presentations in a novel context.

RESULTS: Naloxone produced sex- and behavior-specific effects. During conditioning, naloxone increased baseline and early-tone freezing in males, whereas females exhibited reduced shock-response velocity and increased post-shock freezing. Darting and USV production were not significantly affected. During recall, freezing did not differ between treatment groups. However, naloxone-treated females exhibited fewer alarm callers overall, but increased vocalization among animals that called.

CONCLUSIONS: Systemic naloxone differentially modulates defensive behaviors in male and female rats, highlighting sex-dependent effects of opioid receptor antagonism on conditioned fear expression. The dissociation between freezing and alarm calling during recall further suggests that these behaviors may reflect distinct components of fear processing.

articles.title: Reply to: Chronic Carvedilol in Pediatric Dilated Cardiomyopathy: How Should We Interpret Long-Term Tolerability?
Annualized fibrosis dynamics in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: a paired-biopsy cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fibrosis stage is the strongest histologic determinant of outcomes in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), but annualized fibrosis dynamics under routine care remain insufficiently quantified. We characterized fibrosis progression rate (FPR) in a long-term, pre-incretin paired-biopsy cohort to provide reference data for emerging metabolic therapies.

METHODS: We analyzed 153 patients with MASLD who underwent repeat liver biopsy at a single center over a median interval of 5.9 years (range, 0.5-24). No patient received a GLP-1 receptor agonist or a dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist during follow-up. FPR was defined as the annualized change in fibrosis stage (stage/year). Factors associated with fibrosis improvement were examined using multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Fibrosis improved in 38 patients (25%), remained stable in 66 (43%), and progressed in 49 (32%). FPR varied substantially among patients with improvement or progression, revealing bidirectional and heterogeneous fibrosis dynamics not captured by categorical staging alone. FPR shifted in parallel with MASLD activity score change and was more closely related to changes in hepatocellular ballooning and lobular inflammation than to steatosis. Male sex, advanced baseline fibrosis, and ≥5% body weight reduction were associated with fibrosis improvement, with the likelihood increasing as these factors accumulated.

CONCLUSION: In this real-world pre-incretin paired-biopsy cohort, fibrosis change under routine care was bidirectional and heterogeneous, with wide variation in annualized rate. These data provide a reference for evaluating how emerging metabolic therapies modify the longitudinal course of MASLD.

articles.title: Factors associated with the ionized-to-total magnesium ratio in major hepatobiliary-pancreatic surgery: a single-center prospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To identify perioperative factors associated with the ionized-to-total magnesium (iMg/tMg) ratio at intensive care unit (ICU) admission and on postoperative day (POD) 1 after major open hepatobiliary-pancreatic surgery.

METHODS: This single-center prospective observational study enrolled adults undergoing elective surgery. Paired iMg and tMg measurements were obtained at ICU admission and on POD 1. The primary analyses evaluated perioperative factors associated with the iMg/tMg ratio at each time point using univariable linear regression and multivariable linear regression with backward elimination. Exploratory analyses assessed temporal changes using paired t tests.

RESULTS: Of 150 enrolled patients, 141 were analyzed. At ICU admission, the ratio was positively associated with iMg immediately after anesthesia induction (P = 0.007) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (P = 0.041), and negatively associated with anesthesia time (P = 0.005) and total cholesterol (P = 0.018). On POD 1, the ratio was positively associated with intraoperative non-Mg-containing fluid volume (P = 0.016), and negatively associated with operation time (P < 0.001), hypertension (P = 0.013), and albumin (P = 0.007). Model R2 values were 0.10 and 0.20 at ICU admission and on POD 1, respectively. In exploratory analyses, the mean ratio increased between postoperative measurements (0.659 to 0.713; P < 0.001). Mean iMg decreased from 0.589 mmol/L after induction to 0.545 at ICU admission, then increased to 0.640 on POD 1 (all P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Perioperative factors associated with the iMg/tMg ratio differed between ICU admission and POD 1 after major open hepatobiliary-pancreatic surgery. Both models had limited explanatory power. These findings should be interpreted in relation to sampling time and require independent validation before informing clinical management.

articles.title: Real-world evidence for decisions in diabetes.
articles.abstract: Randomised controlled trials underpin the evidence base for diabetes interventions but have important limitations, including being conducted in selective populations, with restricted follow-up times and treatment pathways that differ from routine clinical practice. Real-world data (RWD) offer an opportunity to address questions beyond the scope of trials, including the comparative effectiveness of interventions, assessment of longer-term outcomes, and treatment effects in under-represented populations. However, the credibility of real-world evidence (RWE) varies widely due to data quality and methodological challenges. The REDDIE (Real-world Evidence for Decisions in Diabetes) programme examined how RWD can generate robust, decision-relevant evidence for diabetes by analysing multiple national registries, evaluating regulatory expectations and conducting target trial emulations of landmark studies. Evidence from REDDIE and the wider literature demonstrates that well-designed observational analyses can replicate major trial findings and extend evidence to broader populations. However, credibility critically depends on careful alignment between the research question, database fitness, study design and analytical methods. Target trial emulation and modern causal inference approaches can mitigate key biases but cannot overcome fundamental limitations of routine data, including unmeasured confounding and incomplete variable capture. RWE and RCTs should be viewed as complementary sources of evidence.
