We outline a practical framework for the design, analysis and interpretation of RWE studies in diabetes to support more robust and decision-relevant use of RWD by regulators, health technology assessment agencies and clinicians.

articles.title: Mannosylated nanostructured lipid carriers of thiabendazole against Pseudomonas aeruginosa lung biofilm infection: in vitro and in vivo characterization, with relevance to cystic fibrosis.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to develop mannosylated nanostructured lipid carriers loaded with Thiabendazole for intravenous delivery to prevent lung biofilm formation. Mannosylated NLCs combine the targeting capabilities of mannose-functionalized carriers with the favorable physicochemical properties of NLCs. Mannose-coated NLCs (MCT-NLCs), prepared via microemulsification using Glyceryl monostearate, olive oil, and Geraniol, had an approximate size of 240 nm, a zeta potential of about - 32.5 mV, an entrapment efficiency of 96%, and released about 84% of the drug within 24 h. Microscopy showed spherical particles under 250 nm, supported by thermal and diffraction analyses. TEM and IR spectra confirmed surface mannose. In vitro, they demonstrated sustained drug release compared to free drug. After IV administration, these NLCs reduced bacterial counts and minimized lung tissue damage in rats infected with Pseudomonas aeruginosa over seven days, demonstrating improved initial in vivo results, though they did not eradicate the infection. This study did not evaluate the formulation's safety, as it is a repurposed work. In vivo, the NLCs significantly lowered bacterial load and inflammation in a rat model of inhaled Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms relevant to cystic fibrosis over seven days, indicating potential to reduce bacterial contamination and tissue damage, although their targeting mechanism and ability to cure were not confirmed.

articles.title: [Management principles of bite injuries].
articles.abstract: Bite injuries are frequent and often underestimated injuries associated with a high risk of infection and complications. Regardless of their cause, all bite wounds are considered contaminated. The hands and face are particularly affected, with hand bite injuries posing a high risk for deep infections and permanent functional impairment due to the complex anatomy. A structured initial assessment including the type of bite, location, depth, age of the wound and signs of infection is essential. Small skin lesions do not exclude severe deep-lying tissue injuries. The cornerstone of primary management is immediate and extensive wound irrigation combined with thorough surgical debridement to reduce the bacterial load. Primary wound closure should generally be avoided; exceptions apply to fresh, well-cleaned facial bite wounds without signs of infection. Antibiotic prophylaxis is indicated in defined high-risk situations but does not replace adequate debridement. In addition, assessment of vaccination status, immobilization, elevation and close clinical follow-up within 24-48 h are essential.

articles.title: Ciprofol more broadly suppresses selected inflammatory markers than propofol in LPS-induced sepsis-associated encephalopathy.
articles.abstract: To investigate and compare the anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective effects of ciprofol and propofol in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced sepsis-associated encephalopathy(SAE). C57BL/6 N mice with LPS-induced SAE were treated with propofol(LP) or ciprofol(LC). Cognitive function was assessed by the Morris water maze (MWM) and novel object recognition (NOR) tests. Neuroinflammation and glial activation in the hippocampus were evaluated by histology, immunohistochemistry (IHC), immunofluorescence (IF), and RT-qPCR. Systemic and cellular inflammatory responses were measured by ELISA. In vitro, BV2 microglial cells were treated with LPS, LP, or LC, and their effects on neuronal viability were assessed in a co-culture system. Underlying mechanisms were explored by Western Blot and RT-qPCR. In vivo, both ciprofol and propofol produced comparable improvements in cognitive outcomes, and representative H&E- and Nissl-stained sections showed similar histological patterns. At the tested doses, ciprofol more broadly suppressed selected inflammatory markers. Systemically, ciprofol significantly reduced all three tested cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6), whereas propofol significantly reduced TNF-α only. In the hippocampus, ciprofol produced greater reductions in Il-1β transcription and Iba-1-positive cells in the dentate gyrus. In vitro, ciprofol also produced greater reductions in selected proinflammatory mediators in BV2 cells. Mechanistically, ciprofol was associated with greater suppression of Nlrp3 mRNA, whereas the corresponding between-drug protein-level difference was not significant. In murine LPS-induced SAE, ciprofol and propofol produced comparable improvements in cognitive outcomes and similar histological observations, whereas ciprofol more broadly suppressed selected systemic and hippocampal inflammatory markers and was associated with greater Nlrp3 transcriptional suppression in BV2 cells at the tested doses or concentrations. These preclinical findings require confirmation in clinically relevant sepsis models and human studies before they can inform anesthetic selection in patients with sepsis.

articles.title: Recovery after more than one month of dialysis in legionella-associated acute kidney injury: a case evaluated with gallium-67 scintigraphy and renal biopsy.
articles.abstract: Distinguishing tubulointerstitial nephritis (TIN) from acute tubular necrosis (ATN) is clinically important in Legionella-associated acute kidney injury (AKI), because TIN may respond to corticosteroid therapy whereas ATN does not. However, kidney biopsy is often not feasible in critically ill patients, and noninvasive approaches to guide treatment decisions are needed. We report a 73-year-old man with severe Legionella pneumonia complicated by dialysis-dependent AKI persisting for more than one month despite resolution of the infection and discontinuation of all antibiotics by Day 9. Markedly elevated urinary beta2-microglobulin (118,539 μg/L at Day 28) and diffuse intense bilateral renal uptake on gallium-67 scintigraphy (grade 5, clearly exceeding liver and vertebral body uptake) on Day 31 supported ongoing renal inflammation in the setting of prolonged tubular injury. A diagnostic trial of prednisolone (0.5 mg/kg/day) was initiated; from approximately 1 week later, urine output increased, serum creatinine declined, and hemodialysis was successfully discontinued on Day 43. Renal function returned to pre-illness baseline by Day 57 (serum creatinine 0.75 mg/dL). Kidney biopsy performed after clinical stabilization showed acute tubular injury with chronic tubulointerstitial changes and a focal, reactive T-cell infiltrate; prior or partially treated TIN could not be excluded. This case shows that renal recovery remains possible in Legionella-associated AKI even after more than 1 month of dialysis dependence, and suggests that gallium-67 scintigraphy, interpreted alongside serial urinary tubular injury markers, may provide ancillary evidence of ongoing renal inflammation when biopsy is not immediately feasible.

articles.title: Removal of endocrine disruptors from tap water: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) are increasingly detected in drinking water sources due to their widespread use and environmental persistence. Their potential to interfere with hormonal systems, even at trace levels, poses serious concerns for human health, including developmental, reproductive, and metabolic effects. This systematic review aimed to identify and compare the most effective treatment technologies to remove EDCs from drinking water, assessing their performance, analytical approaches, limitations, and relevance to public health and regulatory frameworks. Following PRISMA guidelines, a comprehensive literature search was conducted across 4 databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library), resulting in the inclusion of 19 experimental studies published from the last 20 years. The studies were assessed for methodological quality and risk of bias using the Cochrane ROB-2 tool. A wide spectrum of EDCs was studied, including estrogens, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), bisphenols, parabens, and drug residues, across diverse treatment configurations. Conventional methods (e.g., coagulation, chlorination) have shown limited efficacy; instead, advanced techniques such as ozonation, nanofiltration, activated carbon adsorption, and advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) have mainly achieved removal > 90% for several compounds. Bioassays (e.g., Yeast Estrogen Screen-YES) were used in eligible studies to assess residual estrogenicity. Advanced and hybrid water treatment technologies demonstrate the highest removal efficiency for a range of endocrine disruptors. However, variability in study design and target compounds highlights the need for harmonized protocols and regulatory benchmarks. These findings support the development of more effective drinking water treatment strategies to reduce EDC exposure and protect human health.

articles.title: Micafungin in Hematology: Current Evidence and Clinical Positioning.
articles.abstract: This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the role of micafungin in patients with hematologic malignancies and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), a population at high risk for invasive fungal infections (IFIs). Micafungin, an echinocandin with activity against most Candida spp. and Aspergillus spp., is characterized by a favorable safety profile, predictable pharmacokinetics, and minimal drug-drug interactions, making it particularly attractive in patients receiving complex targeted therapies. Micafungin has a well-established role in the prevention of IFIs in selected patients with hematologic malignancies, particularly during induction chemotherapy for acute myeloid leukemia/myelodysplastic syndromes and during the pre-engraftment period after allogeneic HSCT when the local risk of invasive mould disease is low. Its use in emerging populations such as cellular-therapy and bispecific-antibody recipients should be individualized because micafungin-specific evidence remains limited. Micafungin is also an established treatment option for invasive candidiasis, although species identification, susceptibility testing, appropriate step-down therapy, and consideration of site-specific limitations are essential. Evidence supporting empirical treatment of febrile neutropenia is supportive but comparatively limited. Its role in invasive aspergillosis remains limited, mainly as salvage or combination therapy, and its lack of activity against certain moulds and rare fungi should be considered. The emergence of Candidozyma auris (C. auris) and echinocandin-resistant Candida spp. further underscores the importance of species identification, susceptibility testing, and clinical surveillance. Extended-interval and intermittent micafungin dosing may offer practical advantages and pharmacokinetic feasibility, but clinical noninferiority to daily administration has not been established and such regimens remain off-label and investigational. Overall, its optimal use requires careful patient selection and awareness of its spectrum limitations, supporting a tailored approach to antifungal management in hematologic patients.

articles.title: The subcutaneous compartment in abdominal incision closure: a critical review and translational framework.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Superficial wound morbidity frequently arises within the subcutaneous compartment, yet abdominal closure research usually treats this layer as an undifferentiated interval between fascia and skin. We examined whether approximation or drainage improves outcomes, whether local phenotype helps explain inconsistent effects, and which indirect mechanisms merit testing, including their relevance to ventral and incisional hernia surgery.

METHODS: We conducted a structured critical review using database searches through 4 September 2026. Reports were selected once against anatomical and evidence-stream criteria. Direct abdominal studies and labelled mixed non-caesarean syntheses were separated from prognostic morphometry and other indirect evidence; no de novo meta-analysis was performed.

RESULTS: The principal non-caesarean Cochrane synthesis included eight randomised trials, three involving nonabdominal wounds; six contributed data (815 participants), all at high risk of bias. Approximation showed no clear effect on SSI or superficial dehiscence, and drain evidence remained discordant across heterogeneous protocols. Clinically treated seroma, haematoma, superficial separation, and skin or fat necrosis were inconsistently reported, while SSI definitions and follow-up varied. Hernia-specific drain and quilting studies directly examined superficial-space management during abdominal-wall reconstruction, but did not establish a phenotype-specific treatment effect or, for drainage, isolate a purely subcutaneous intervention. Local measurements were prognostic, but we identified no eligible study that formally tested a treatment-by-phenotype interaction.

CONCLUSION: Current evidence supports neither universal approximation nor universal drainage. Future trials should prioritise layer-specific outcomes, define the anatomical target, report the complete intervention protocol, and prespecify treatment-by-phenotype interactions. The proposed framework remains a research design, not a clinical algorithm.

articles.title: Common Genetic Variants Near SLC2A2 and Glycemic Response to Glimepiride in the GRADE Comparative Effectiveness Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Optimizing second-line therapy for type 2 diabetes remains challenging because of interindividual variability in response. Current treatment selection does not consider personal genetic profiles. To address this gap, we conducted a pharmacogenomic genome-wide association study (GWAS) in a randomized comparative effectiveness trial to identify genetic predictors of glycemic response to insulin glargine, glimepiride, liraglutide, and sitagliptin when added to metformin.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: In the Glycemia Reduction Approaches in Type 2 Diabetes: A Comparative Effectiveness Study (GRADE), we performed a GWAS for the time to reach primary (glycated hemoglobin [HbA1c] ≥7%) and secondary (HbA1c >7.5%) metabolic failure. We conducted replication in independent cohorts, performed fine mapping of the top variants near SLC2A2, evaluated them for physiologic impact using oral glucose tolerance testing (OGTT) and response to acute glipizide challenge, and characterized glycemic response to glimepiride in an slc2a2-mutated zebrafish model.

RESULTS: rs2129019 in SLC2A2 encoding GLUT2 was enriched in African/African American participants and conferred a 38% increased risk of metabolic failure per A allele on glimepiride (P = 1.55 × 10-8). Carriers had impaired β-cell function, evidenced by a lower C-peptide index during OGTT, and diminished glucose-lowering response to acute sulfonylurea challenge. Genetic manipulation in zebrafish confirmed that slc2a2 disruption attenuated the glucose-lowering effect of glimepiride.

CONCLUSIONS: Genetic variation influences glycemic response to glucose-lowering medications, with SLC2A2 emerging as a genetic factor that modulates sulfonylurea response. These findings warrant further study to evaluate whether low-response allele carriers would benefit from alternative glucose-lowering therapies to advance precision diabetes care.

articles.title: Opportunities and Challenges of the 2025 United Nations Political Declaration on Noncommunicable Diseases for Nephrology Nursing Governance and Workforce Roles.
articles.abstract: BackgroundChronic kidney disease (CKD) affects more than 674 million people worldwide and remains insufficiently prioritized in the global noncommunicable disease (NCD) agenda. Although nurses comprise a substantial share of the global health workforce, their roles in implementing global kidney health commitments remain unclear.PurposeDrawing on the Walt and Gilson policy analysis framework, this study critically examines the opportunities and challenges posed by the 2025 United Nations Political Declaration on NCDs (A/80/L.34) for nephrology nursing governance, workforce roles, and integration into primary and community-based kidney care.MethodsA qualitative policy analysis examined the declaration through four interrelated dimensions (policy context, content, actors, and process), anchored in the official text adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on December 15, 2025.FindingsThe declaration explicitly recognizes CKD in the global NCD agenda and reinforces primary healthcare and community-based services as central strategies. However, it provides limited operational guidance on workforce role delineation, particularly regarding nursing leadership. Governance and accountability mechanisms for implementing kidney health commitments are underdeveloped. Although nephrology nursing is implicitly positioned as a strategic workforce, its formal integration into health system planning has not been articulated explicitly.ConclusionsTranslating the declaration into effective and equitable kidney care requires explicit recognition of nephrology nursing in governance arrangements, workforce planning, and policy implementation. Without such integration, global commitments risk being merely aspirational. Strengthening nursing leadership, advanced education, and expanded scopes of practice are critical policy levers for advancing equitable and sustainable kidney care across diverse health-system contexts.

articles.title: Comparison of braided versus laser-cut stent placement for ruptured intracranial aneurysms in the acute phase: a propensity score matched study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare clinical and angiographic outcomes between braided and laser-cut stents in patients with acutely ruptured intracranial aneurysms undergoing stent-assisted coiling (SAC), using propensity score matching (PSM) to adjust for confounders.

METHODS: This study analyzed consecutive patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage who underwent SAC within 72 h of onset between January 2017 and June 2024 from a prospectively maintained registry. Clinical and angiographic outcomes were compared before and after 1:1 PSM. Subgroup analyses explored effect modifiers.

RESULTS: A total of 552 patients were enrolled (384 laser-cut and 168 braided), with a mean age of 60.32 years and 64.3% females. In the matched cohort (161 pairs), perioperative complications, and aneurysm occlusion and functional outcomes did not differ significantly (all P > 0.05) at 6-month follow-up. In the entire cohort, laser-cut stents were associated with lower odds of favorable functional prognosis at discharge than braided stents (OR = 0.53, 95% CI 0.31-0.89). Significant interactions were observed between stent type and hypertension (P for interaction = 0.009) and irregular aneurysm morphology (P for interaction = 0.010) for incomplete occlusion.

CONCLUSION: No statistically significant difference in safety or efficacy was observed between braided and laser-cut stents in acutely ruptured intracranial aneurysms. The interactions with hypertension and irregular morphology warrant attention when individualizing stent selection and planning follow-up angiography. Larger multicenter, adequately powered prospective studies with standardized antithrombotic regimens are needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: Suction versus traditional ureteral access sheaths in retrograde intrarenal surgery: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of stone-free rates and complications.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Suction ureteral access sheaths (S-UAS), fixed-tip or flexible and navigable (FANS), are proposed to improve stone clearance and reduce infections in retrograde intrarenal surgery (RIRS); we updated our 2025 meta-analysis and asked whether tip design changes the effect.

METHODS: Five databases were searched from inception to March 2026 for comparative studies of S-UAS versus traditional sheaths (T-UAS) in adult RIRS (PROSPERO CRD420251164154). Outcomes were residual fragments at early (up to 3 weeks) and late (4 weeks or later) assessment, fever, sepsis, septic shock, severe complications, operative time and hospital stay, analyzed with random-effects models, subgroups by design and tip design, small-study tests and GRADE.

RESULTS: Twenty-nine studies (four randomized; 5,604 patients) were included. S-UAS reduced residual fragments at early (RR 0.49; 95% CI 0.42-0.58; 22 studies) and late assessment (RR 0.53; 0.45-0.63; 23 studies), fever (RR 0.43; 0.34-0.53), sepsis (RR 0.47; 0.31-0.72) and severe complications (RR 0.48; 0.33-0.69). Septic shock was rare (4 versus 12 events; RR 0.41; 0.15-1.15). Operative time did not differ; hospital stay was 0.32 days shorter, but not robustly so. Post hoc, the late benefit was larger with tip-flexible (RR 0.47) than with fixed-tip sheaths (RR 0.72; p = 0.03). Certainty was moderate for stone clearance and fever (low for early clearance in non-randomized studies), otherwise low or very low.

CONCLUSION: S-UAS probably improve stone clearance and reduce fever and may reduce sepsis; the evidence on severe complications is very uncertain. The effect on septic shock and a possible advantage of the flexible tip need randomized confirmation.

articles.title: Prevalence of generalized joint hypermobility, hypermobility spectrum disorders and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome: systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Generalized joint hypermobility, GJH is common. Hypermobility can have various negative consequences and comorbidities, especially when criterion for Hypermobility Spectrum Disorder, HSD and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, EDS are met.The prevalence of these different conditions is lacking. Therefore, the aim of this study was to assess the prevalence of these hypermobility disorders. A systematic search was conducted January 25, 2024 and updated May 28, 2025. It included the databases Ovid MEDLINE, Ovid Embase, CINAHL, and PEDro and followed a predefined search strategy adapted for each database (PROSPERO CRD42024505862) and included the MESH terms 'Ehlers Danlos Syndrome','Prevalence', 'Epidemiology' and keywords 'Hypermobility Spectrum Disorder';'Generalized joint hypermobility' and 'Systematic review'. 3633 unique records were screened, and 17 studies were included. From the meta-analysis the pooled prevalence across included studies of GJH in females were 9.5% (95% CI: 5.5; 15.8) with an I² of 95.5 % and 5.2% (95% CI: 3.0; 9.0) in males with an I² of 94.8). The evidence base for the age group 51 and older was insufficient for a robust estimate. Only one single study assessed HSD and hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, hEDS in individuals aged 18-50 years and reported a prevalence of HSD of 38% in females and 39% in males, and the prevalence of hEDS as 2% in females and 0% in males. Hence, the available evidence did not allow for robust conclusions regarding the population-level prevalence of HSD/hEDS. This study shows that GJH is common, but with considerable heterogeneity and broad prediction intervals, which makes it crucial to interpret the pooled prevalence with caution. Moreover, a significant knowledge gap in the prevalence of GJH but particularly for HSD and EDS was identified. Our findings highlight the difficulties yet the need for more prevalence data on these conditions to understand the impact on the individual patient, health care services, and society.

articles.title: Cardiac Autonomic Dysfunction in Diabetic Highlander and Lowlander Populations of Nepal Assessed by Heart Rate Variability.
articles.abstract: IntroductionDiabetes mellitus is associated with cardiac autonomic dysfunction (CAD) and enhanced cardiovascular risk. High-altitude dwellers exhibit physiological adaptations that may regulate autonomic function. The present study aims to compare cardiac autonomic function in diabetic highlanders vs diabetic lowlanders of Nepal using heart rate variability (HRV).MethodsA cross-sectional study was performed on a total of 128 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), including 64 native highlanders residing above 2500 m (Phaplu, Solukhumbu district, Nepal) and 64 native lowlanders below 500 m (Biratnagar, Morang District, Nepal). HRV was measured using standard electrocardiography (ECG) under baseline resting state. Time- and frequency-domain HRV indices including age, gender, duration of diabetes, and HbA1c were recorded and analyzed. Comparative statistical analysis was conducted using independent t tests and Mann-Whitney U tests.ResultsIn time-domain HRV parameters, diabetic highlanders showed significantly higher SDNN (88.9 [48.5-97.2] ms vs 28.7 [20.2-43.1] ms; P < .001) and increased RMSSD (64.9 [35.1-92.3] ms vs 21.6 [14.3-38.3] ms; P < .001) compared to lowlanders. Likewise, in frequency-domain HRV analysis, as compared to diabetic lowlanders, diabetic highlanders revealed significantly increased HF power (317.6 [96.5-869.2] ms2 vs 86.1 [29.7-314.0] ms2; P < .001) and lower LF/HF ratio (0.4 [0.2-1.1] vs 1.2 [0.9-3.4]; P < .001) demonstrating relatively better autonomic balance.ConclusionHighlanders with T2DM exhibit relatively preserved cardiac autonomic balance compared to diabetic lowlanders, indicating that chronic exposure to high altitude influences diabetes-related autonomic dysfunction. These findings highlight the importance of considering geographical and environmental factors during management and risk assessment of diabetic individuals in Nepal.

articles.title: Work-related musculoskeletal disorders among civil servants attending healthcare facilities in Bangladesh: An observational cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundWork-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) are a major occupational health concern worldwide, significantly affecting employees' well-being and productivity. Government employees in Bangladesh are particularly vulnerable to WMSDs due to the sedentary or repetitive nature of their work (e.g., prolonged computer use, repetitive typing, and manual mechanical tasks).ObjectiveThis study aimed to determine the clinical distribution, patterns, and associated factors of WMSDs among government employees in Bangladesh and evaluate the subjective impact on workers' productivity and quality of life.MethodsA retrospective descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted at the Government Employees Hospital in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Participants were recruited using consecutive sampling from government employees attending the Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation Department. Descriptive and inferential statistics (Chi-square and Fisher's exact tests via R software) were used to examine the distribution of conditions like low back pain, knee osteoarthritis, cervical spondylosis, frozen shoulder. Productivity and quality of life were assessed through structured clinical interviews, while demographic characteristics, work type, and employment grade were analyzed to identify associated factors.ResultsNonspecific low back pain was the most prevalent condition (27.23%), particularly among retired employees (34.62%) and sedentary workers (26.97%). Knee osteoarthritis (10.81%) and cervical spondylosis (8.97%) were more common among older and dynamic workers. The most commonly affected sites were the lower back (43.73%), knees, shoulders, and neck. Disease patterns varied significantly by age, and government service grade.ConclusionThe high proportion of diagnosed cases among Bangladeshi government employees underscores the need for interventions including ergonomic modifications, regular health assessments, and early screening strategies to reduce WMSD impact and inform public sector health policies.

articles.title: Northward shift in cancer mortality inequality across Japanese prefectures, 1995-2023, a nationwide ecological study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer has been the leading cause of death in Japan since the 1980s, with known variation across prefectures, but evidence on how this pattern has changed over time is limited.

METHODS: We analysed age-standardized cancer mortality across all 47 Japanese prefectures in 1995 and 2023 using vital statistics data. For each prefecture, excess mortality was calculated relative to a leave-one-out national reference and standardized to the 1995 national population. Excess mortality was decomposed by cancer site. We also compared prefectures' age-standardized mortality rates (ASMRs) between the two years.

RESULTS: All-cancer ASMR declined in every prefecture. In 2023, excess mortality ranged from 32·6 per 100 000 (95% CI 26·8 to 38·4) in Aomori to -22·4 (-26·1 to -18·6) in Nagano, a gap of 55·0 deaths per 100 000, with 30 prefectures differing significantly from the national reference. The geographic pattern shifted between 1995 and 2023. In 1995, excess mortality was concentrated in western Japan, particularly Osaka and Fukuoka, and was largely driven by liver cancer. By 2023, excess mortality had shifted to northern prefectures, led by Aomori and Hokkaido, and was distributed across multiple cancer types, including colorectal, lung, and stomach cancer. The overall gap narrowed from 69·6 to 55·0 per 100 000.

CONCLUSIONS: Geographic inequality in cancer mortality persisted in Japan, but its pattern changed substantially. The findings suggest that national cancer control should monitor subnational inequality directly and support regionally targeted strategies.

articles.title: Establishing Absolute Neutrophil Count and White Blood Cell Count Reference Intervals for the Duffy Null Population.
articles.abstract: Most reference intervals (RI) for absolute neutrophil count (ANC) and white blood cell count (WBC) in the United States (US) are not representative of people with the Duffy null phenotype (10% of the US population), which leads to misdiagnoses and inequity in care. We aimed to verify the adult Duffy null ANC RI and develop WBC and ANC RIs for pediatrics. 1,412 healthy Duffy null participants from 23 sites were included. All sites agreed on eligibility criteria. Otherwise, this was a pragmatic design with site-specific variation in collection approach. ANC and WBC were stratified into 5 age categories: 6 months-2 years, 3-6 years, 7-12 years, 13-17 years, and 18+ years. RI were calculated by Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute guidelines. Duffy null-specific ANC RI were 0.53-4.50×109/L (6 months-2 years, n=184), 0.78-4.67×109/L (3-6 years, n=160), 0.87-5.34×109/L (7-12 years, n=190), 0.90-4.89×109/L (13-17 years, n=216), and 1.03-7.30×109/L (18+ years, n=662). 25% of adults had ANC <2.00×109/L and 24-53% of children had ANC <1.50×109/L. Sensitivity analyses did not show any significant differences in ANC RI when accounting for blood draw type, setting, collection site, hematology analyzer, or hemoglobin and platelet counts. This study provides the first report of Duffy null-specific pediatric ANC and WBC RI, as well as a large-scale verification of adult Duffy null-specific ANC and WBC RI. Adoption of Duffy null-specific RIs is necessary for the accurate interpretation of laboratory values that will support appropriate and equitable medical decision-making.

articles.title: Patient selection for advanced B-cell-targeted therapy trials in systemic lupus erythematosus.
articles.abstract: BackgroundA proportion of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) remain refractory to standard therapies. Advanced B-cell-targeted therapies (ABT), including chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy, T-cell-engaging approaches, and anti-CD19 monoclonal antibodies, are emerging for selected patients in clinical trials.MethodsWe conducted a single-centre observational study of patients with SLE treated with biologic therapies at a tertiary lupus service between January 2024 and December 2025, during active recruitment to ABT clinical trials. We assessed clinical factors associated with referral for multidisciplinary team (MDT) discussion regarding ABT and explored documented reasons for non-participation. We compared patients discussed at ABT-MDT with those not referred within the same cohort.ResultsAmong 101 patients treated with biologics, 21 (20.8%) were discussed at ABT-MDT. Patients referred for ABT-MDT had higher rates of lupus nephritis (90.5% vs 46.2%, p < 0.001), higher SLEDAI-2K scores (16.0 vs 2.0, p < 0.001), higher daily prednisolone doses (15.0 vs 1.0 mg, p < 0.001), and greater exposure to prior immunosuppressive therapies. In multivariable analysis, higher SLEDAI-2K (OR 1.92 per 4-point increase, 95% CI 1.10-4.27) and prednisolone dose (OR 3.44 per 5-mg increase, 95% CI 1.23-14.50) were independently associated with ABT-MDT referral. Of those discussed, 7 patients proceeded to ABT. Reasons for non-participation included patient preference, perceived infection risk, clinical improvement, and protocol-related constraints.ConclusionIn a tertiary SLE cohort, referral for advanced B-cell-targeted therapies was associated with markers of high disease activity and renal involvement. However, multiple clinical and patient-related factors limited trial participation. These findings highlight important considerations in referral and trial participation for advanced B-cell-targeted therapies.

articles.title: Hemodynamic changes during total-body cooling and rewarming phase in neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy.
articles.abstract: IntroductionNeonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) is a major cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality. Therapeutic hypothermia (TH) is the standard neuroprotective intervention; however, it significantly influences cardiovascular function, necessitating careful hemodynamic monitoring.AimTo evaluate hemodynamic changes in term neonates with HIE during therapeutic hypothermia and the subsequent rewarming phase using serial echocardiographic assessment.Materials and methodsThis prospective observational study included 32 term neonates with suspected perinatal or intrapartum hypoxia admitted within 6 hours of birth. All patients underwent whole-body TH followed by controlled rewarming. Hemodynamic evaluation was performed using serial echocardiography at predefined time points during cooling and after rewarming. Cardiac troponin I levels were measured at admission, during cooling, and after rewarming, and compared with levels in healthy neonates.ResultsSerial echocardiography demonstrated significant changes in cardiovascular function across the cooling and rewarming phases. Cardiac output, left ventricular output, fractional shortening, right ventricular output, and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion showed significant changes over time, with several measures of ventricular systolic function improving after rewarming. Myocardial performance indices also decreased over time, indicating changes in global ventricular performance. Superior vena cava flow and pulmonary artery pressure increased during cooling and remained elevated during the early post-rewarming period. Inferior vena cava collapsibility and right ventricular systolic/diastolic indices also showed significant changes across the study period. Cardiac troponin I levels did not differ significantly between the cooling and post-rewarming measurements (0.19 ± 0.02 vs. 0.20 ± 0.02 ng/mL, P = 0.825). Correlations between echocardiographic parameters and clinical severity markers, including pH, Apgar score, and Sarnat stage, were variable.ConclusionTH induces significant but reversible alterations in cardiac function in neonates with HIE. Serial echocardiographic assessment provides valuable insights into these dynamic changes and may support individualized cardiovascular management during both cooling and rewarming phases. Larger multicenter studies with longer follow-up are needed to determine their clinical significance and relationship with neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Effectiveness of 25 µg vaginal misoprostol for labor induction in women with obesity: outcomes according to obesity class.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aim of this study is to evaluate the effectiveness of 25 µg vaginal misoprostol for labor induction in pregnant women with obesity.

METHODS: This observational analytical study was conducted with a total of 116 pregnant women with singleton gestation, Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥30 kg/m2 at the beginning of prenatal care, and gestational age ≥37 weeks who underwent labor induction with 25 µg vaginal misoprostol were included. Participants were stratified according to obesity class as class I (N.=18), class II (N.=16), and class III (N.=82). The primary outcome was vaginal delivery. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to evaluate the association between obesity class and vaginal delivery, adjusting for maternal age, gestational age, neonatal birthweight, and prior vaginal delivery. Secondary analyses included oxytocin use, duration of labor induction, and neonatal Apgar scores according to obesity class.

RESULTS: Obesity class was not significantly associated with vaginal delivery after adjustment for covariates. The adjusted odds ratios were 0.89 for class I versus class II (95% CI 0.19-4.15; P=0.887), 0.95 for class III versus class II (95% CI 0.28-3.16; P=0.952), and 0.94 for class I versus class III (95% CI 0.29-2.97; P=0.916). The mean maternal age was 29.0±5.5 years, and the mean BMI was 49.4±9.4 kg/m2. Chronic hypertension was present in 53.4% of participants, and 36.2% had gestational diabetes mellitus. The mean duration of labor induction was 34.3±17.6 hours. Cesarean delivery occurred in 58.6% of cases, whereas 41.4% achieved vaginal delivery. Baseline maternal, obstetric, and clinical characteristics were similar across obesity classes, except for chronic hypertension with superimposed preeclampsia, which was more frequent in class II (31.3%) compared with class I (16.7%) and class III (8.5%) (P=0.035). Among women who achieved vaginal delivery, oxytocin use and induction duration did not differ significantly across obesity classes. Prior vaginal delivery was significantly associated with mode of delivery in the current pregnancy (χ2<inf>(1)</inf>=11.6; P<0.001), with a higher likelihood of vaginal delivery among women with a history of vaginal birth.

CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort of pregnant women with obesity, labor induction with 25 µg vaginal misoprostol was effective, and increasing obesity class was not associated with lower vaginal delivery rates. Prior vaginal delivery was significantly associated with a higher likelihood of vaginal birth.

articles.title: Alpha-lipoic acid in pregnancy: a review of potential effects on maternal and fetal health.
articles.abstract: Alpha lipoic acid (ALA) is a naturally occurring micronutrient with potent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities. For these characteristics, ALA dietary supplementation has been suggested in pregnancy with the aim of reducing the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes in cases associated with the effects of inflammation and/or oxidative stress. In this review, we synthesize evidence for the uses of ALA in recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL), threatened miscarriage, preterm birth, and gestational diabetes, showing both the results of clinical trials and animal/in-vitro studies. Our opinion, based on the current knowledge, suggests that ALA may reduce paternal sperm DNA fragmentation and maternal endometrial inflammation in cases with a high risk of RPL and may improve the resorption of subchorionic hematoma in threatened miscarriage. ALA is also promising in helping cervical length in women at high risk for preterm delivery and in improving glucose and lipid metabolism in gestational diabetes. Although the current evidence about ALA supplementation in human pregnancy is preliminary, the available studies encourage planning further powered randomized controlled clinical trials aimed at confirming these promising effects, with the ambitious aim of improving pregnancy outcomes in high-risk conditions.

articles.title: Restoring Coronary Vasomotion in Pediatric Cardiac Allograft Vasculopathy: A Bioadaptor-Based Interventional Strategy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous coronary interventions in cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV) remain challenging. In CAV, diffuse neointimal proliferation contributes to progressive allograft dysfunction and increased mortality. Although second-generation drug-eluting stents are widely utilized, permanent vessel caging may limit adaptive remodeling, resulting in target lesion failure. Drug-eluting coronary bioadaptors have been designed to provide vessel support while enabling restoration of physiological vasomotion.

CASE SUMMARY: We report the case of a 15-year-old male patient with CAV, 4 years after heart transplantation. A DynamX drug-eluting coronary bioadaptor was successfully implanted in the circumflex artery. At 20-month follow-up, coronary angiography and intravascular ultrasound demonstrated preserved vessel patency and compliance, with no evidence of target lesion failure.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights the feasibility of bioadaptor-based percutaneous coronary interventions in a pediatric heart transplant recipient with CAV and supports further evaluation of this technology in patients with complex coronary lesions.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Bioadaptors may provide acute vessel support while allowing dynamic vessel motion after uncaging in CAV.

articles.title: msDNA: the story of a unique satellite DNA molecule in bacteria.
articles.abstract: msDNA, or multi-copy single-stranded DNA, is a small satellite DNA observed in DNA extracts from a bacterial cell. A genetic element, usually found on the chromosome, called a retron, is responsible for producing msDNA. This small single-stranded DNA has a unique structure and is synthesized by reverse transcription from an RNA template. Retrons and msDNA are found in a large variety of different bacterial species. The msDNA molecule has also been developed into an important tool for genetic engineering and genome editing. But the biological function of this unique DNA molecule remained a mystery for decades. Recent discoveries show that a retron element can protect bacteria from infection with a virus (phage) using an abortive infection strategy. And the msDNA molecule is required for this anti-phage property. A historical perspective on this unusual DNA molecule, recent breakthroughs into its functions, and a discussion of the current and possible future directions of study are presented herein.

articles.title: Changes in Patterns of Health Care Use Among Older Adults in Singapore Across a Decade: Repeated Nationwide Cross-Sectional Survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is limited evidence on the patterns of health care use among older adults in Singapore over the past decade.

OBJECTIVE: This study examines whether the proportion of specific services used within sociodemographic subgroups, the factors associated with health care use, and the network structure of health care use have changed over a decade.

METHODS: We used data from 2 repeated nationwide cross-sectional surveys of Singapore residents aged 60 years and older, conducted in 2013 (n=2565) and 2023 (n=2010). Health care service use was obtained from an adapted version of the Client Service Receipt Inventory and analyzed using multivariable logistic regression and network analysis.

RESULTS: The most significant changes between 2013 and 2023 were in the proportions of older adults who had consulted private hospital/clinic doctors (decreased by 4.6 percentage points; n=655, 26.5% vs n=425, 21.9%; P=.02), consulted public and private dentists (increased by 6.4 percentage points; n=215, 11.6% vs n=269, 18%; P<.001), and had health insurance (increased by 26.9 percentage points; n=1312, 59.9% vs n=1697, 86.8%; P<.001). Those diagnosed with high blood pressure and diabetes were more likely to consult primary care doctors, while those diagnosed with dementia and heart problems were more likely to consult public hospital doctors and health workers, visit emergency departments, and require hospitalization services in both 2013 and 2023. We also found that those diagnosed with dementia were more likely to visit intermediate and long-term care services in both 2013 and 2023. Network analysis revealed that there were strong connections between respite care, nursing homes, and hospital admissions in 2023.

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides important data on population-level changes in health care usage among older adults across the decade from 2013 to 2023, which will help policymakers ensure better health care delivery for older adults.

articles.title: Descending aortic replacement after frozen elephant trunk: graft clamping and true-lumen anastomosis.
articles.journal: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS
articles.abstract: Second-stage descending aortic replacement after arch replacement with a frozen elephant trunk requires proximal control at a site that is often hostile to cross-clamping. The conventional elephant trunk technique was introduced to avoid cross-clamping the vulnerable proximal aorta; the previously implanted graft, left hanging in the descending aorta, is grasped and clamped directly, and the new graft is sutured to it. This video tutorial demonstrates the manoeuvre in the current era of the frozen, stented elephant trunk. In a patient with a frozen elephant trunk, computed tomography confirmed complete circumferential thrombosis of the false lumen around the stented graft. Through a left thoracotomy the distal aorta was clamped, and the completely thrombosed false lumen was opened without a proximal cross-clamp. The previously implanted stented graft was exposed and clamped directly, providing proximal control without dissecting or cross-clamping the densely adherent native aorta and without damaging the stent. The new graft was anastomosed proximally to the unstented distal cuff, and distally to the true lumen only, avoiding leak into the false lumen and limiting late aortic enlargement. The imaging that makes the approach safe, the step-by-step conduct, and the pitfall of identifying the graft within the walled-off true lumen are described.

articles.title: Pharmacology Update: Pruritus in Palliative Care With Focus on Naltrexone.
articles.journal: The American journal of hospice & palliative care
articles.abstract: BackgroundPruritus is a common and often distressing symptom in palliative care, affecting a significant fraction of patients and significantly impairing sleep, mood, and quality of life. Common etiologies include chronic kidney disease, cholestatic liver disease, hematologic malignancies, solid tumors, medication-related syndromes, and paraneoplastic processes. Conventional treatments, including antihistamines, antidepressants, gabapentinoids, ondansetron, and ultraviolet-B phototherapy, are frequently limited by adverse effects, cost, or practicality in seriously ill patients.ObjectiveTo review the pathophysiology of pruritus relevant to palliative care and evaluate the emerging role of naltrexone as a therapeutic option for refractory pruritus.MethodsNarrative review of the literature addressing the mechanisms of pruritus, current treatment approaches, and clinical evidence supporting the use of naltrexone across various pruritic conditions encountered in palliative medicine.ResultsIncreasing evidence implicates dysregulation of the endogenous opioid system in the pathogenesis of several forms of chronic pruritus. As a competitive opioid receptor antagonist, naltrexone may mitigate "itch" through μ-opioid receptor blockade and restoration of opioid signaling balance. The strongest evidence supports its use in cholestatic pruritus, where randomized placebo-controlled trials demonstrated significant reductions in symptom severity with 50 mg daily dosing. Evidence in uremic pruritus is mixed, with some studies showing benefit and others finding no superiority over placebo. Case reports and small series suggest potential efficacy in malignancy-associated pruritus, polycythemia vera, and selected dermatologic disorders. Limitations include contraindication in patients receiving opioid therapy, potential precipitation of withdrawal, and adverse effects such as nausea, gastrointestinal distress, dizziness, fatigue, and sleep disturbance.ConclusionsNaltrexone represents a mechanistically rational and potentially effective option for selected patients with refractory pruritus in palliative care. Current evidence is most compelling for cholestatic pruritus, while data for other etiologies remain limited and heterogeneous. Larger prospective studies are needed to define optimal dosing strategies, identify patients most likely to benefit, and better characterize its role in opioid-exposed palliative care populations.

articles.title: Off-pump subtotal pericardiectomy using ultrasonic aspirator in constrictive pericarditis.
articles.journal: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS
articles.abstract: A subtotal pericardiectomy was performed without the use of extracorporeal circulation due to the patient's advanced age and underlying liver cirrhosis. After exposure of the heart, both phrenic nerves were identified and carefully preserved. The pericardium was found to be massively calcified, with extensive involvement extending to the base of the aorta and the diaphragm. The pericardium was divided into multiple diamond-shaped sections, allowing controlled, stepwise resection and facilitating safe handling of the rigid, calcified tissue. Decortication was initiated at the right ventricle and proceeded gradually. The calcified pericardium was removed using a combination of an ultrasonic aspirator, a rongeur and electrocautery. Careful, controlled separation of the pericardium from the epicardium was performed throughout, addressing dense adhesions while preserving the underlying myocardium and epicardial vessels. The ultrasonic aspirator facilitated resection of the calcified tissue without harming the underlying structures. Resection was extended over the right atrium, right ventricle and anterior wall of the left ventricle up to the level of the phrenic nerves. Complete pericardiectomy was not achievable due to extensive adhesions and proximity to critical structures. Intraoperative echocardiographic imaging demonstrated immediate improvement in cardiac filling and function.

articles.title: The role of various probiotics during colorectal cancer treatment: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Colorectal cancer is a common malignant tumor of the digestive system. To date, systematic comparisons of probiotics in CRC are lacking, and it remains unclear which probiotics are superior. This network meta-analysis aims to compare and rank the effects of different probiotics on CRC-specific outcomes, so as to identify which probiotics or probiotic combinations are superior. We searched 10 databases for all randomized controlled trials as of June 12, 2025. The main indicators were surgical incision infection (Superficial/Deep), intra-abdominal abscess, bacteremia, pneumonia, urinary tract infection, bacterial translocation, duration of fever (>38.5 °C), anastomotic fistula, diarrhea, abdominal distension, first defecation time, time to first flatus, and hospitalization time. The frequentist framework was used for this study. A total of 3601 participants from 40 randomized controlled trials were included in the study. In NMA, the L.APR + B.L combination ranked first in reducing postoperative superficial incision infection; Bifidobacterium tetrad ranked first in reducing deep Organ/Space incision infection and diarrhea; Saccharomyces boulardii was associated with a relatively marked reduction in the incidence of postoperative intra-abdominal abscess; the L.APR + B.L combination showed an advantage in reducing postoperative pneumonia; the L.AP + B.L combination was associated with a statistically significant reduction in postoperative urinary tract infections. Bifidus-triple has the most potential to reduce postoperative bacteremia, bacterial translocation rate, duration of fever and first postoperative exhaust days; the L.ACR + B.L combination significantly reduced the incidence of postoperative anastomotic leakage; Lactobacillus rhamnosus showed an advantage in reducing abdominal distension; the C.B + B.I combination significantly shortened the time to first postoperative bowel movement; and the L.ACL + B.BIL combination showed the most favorable numerical trend in shortening the length of hospital stay. This study is the first to rank the efficacy of different probiotic strains and combinations in CRC for specific outcomes, and further studies are needed to confirm these results.

A microfluidic model of bacterial keratitis to quantify the efficacy of anti-infective compounds under flow.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Bacterial infections of the cornea, also known as bacterial keratitis, are a major cause of blindness. The corneal surface is protected against infection by the flow of tear fluid, which displaces potential pathogens and debris. Whilst fluid flow is known to influence the behaviour of both bacterial and epithelial cells, most models of corneal infection use static conditions. Here, we develop a microfluidic model to directly visualise interactions between bacteria and human corneal epithelial cells (HCE2) in physiologically relevant flow conditions.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We use high-resolution microscopy and automated image analysis to continuously quantify the rate at which Staphylococcus aureus (SH1000) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PAO1) adhere to HCE2 monolayers. We then use this system to investigate the effects of pre-treatment with unfractionated heparin (UFH), a putative therapeutic compound thought to inhibit bacterial adhesion. Using a traditional, well plate-based assay that lacks fluid flow, prior treatment of HCE2 monolayers with UFH significantly reduced adhesion of both species. In our microfluidic model we found that pre-treating HCE2 monolayers with UFH again sharply reduced S. aureus adhesion, but surprisingly, UFH pre-treatment had no effect on P. aeruginosa adhesion to corneal cells in the presence of fluid flow.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings demonstrate that incorporating fluid flow into in vitro infection models can lead to qualitatively different outcomes when screening putative anti-adhesion therapies. These findings, obtained using two widely studied model strains, illustrate how microfluidic models of infection can offer valuable insights into how flow influences bacterial keratitis and guide the development of new treatments.

articles.title: Dupilumab in Atopic Dermatitis - Rate of Poor Responders and Potential Risk Factors from the TREATgermany Registry.
articles.abstract: A distinct proportion of patients with atopic dermatitis and dupilumab treatment does not reach the primary endpoint of an eczema area severity index (EASI)-75 or investigator global assessment 0/1 after 16 weeks. Little is known about poor responders to dupilumab in real life scenarios. The study objective was to identify the percentage and characteristics of patients with insufficient treatment response to dupilumab based on "TREATgermany" registry data from dermatological routine care. Between 06/2016 and 12/2024, 476 patients matched the study criteria. In total, 4% of patients (n=19) were identified as dupilumab poor responders, i.e. reduction in EASI ≤40% at the 1st follow-up visit after 8 to 20 weeks and a consecutive 2nd follow-up visit up to 52 weeks of treatment. 44% (n=209) were classified as stable responders, i.e. decrease in EASI≥75% at both follow-up visits. Poor responders were significantly more often male, more frequently exhibited smoking, arterial hypertension and a higher body mass index. This TREATgermany data analysis demonstrates a proportion of 4% dupilumab poor responders within the first year of treatment. Male sex, smoking, arterial hypertension and increased body mass index were identified as potential risk factors. Further translational research is needed to confirm these clinical findings.

articles.title: Cytoplasmic ATR orchestrates PRRSV and EBOV replication organelle assembly via vimentin phosphorylation.
articles.abstract: The ataxia telangiectasia-mutated and Rad3-related (ATR) kinase is a well-established master regulator of the DNA damage response and replication stress. In this study, we uncover an unexpected, conserved role of ATR in promoting the replication of two distinct RNA viruses-an arterivirus and a filovirus-through vimentin phosphorylation. Acute pharmacologic inhibition or knockdown of ATR robustly suppress viral replication and sharply reduce the formation of double-membrane vesicles and membrane-less condensates that serve as replication organelles (ROs) for these divergent viral classes. Notably, although ATR is recruited to cytoplasmic ROs throughout the viral life cycle, it acts specifically at the replication stage without affecting viral attachment, entry, or egress. We further show that ATR directly interacts with and phosphorylates vimentin within ROs, driving vimentin rearrangement and delineating RO boundaries. Mechanistically, ATR-dependent phosphorylation of vimentin at Ser459 is indispensable for RO formation during infection by both PRRSV and EBOV. Together, these findings reveal a conserved ATR-vimentin signaling axis that promotes RO biogenesis across diverse RNA viruses, defining a noncanonical function of cytoplasmic ATR in orchestrating the assembly of both membrane-bound and membrane-less replication compartments via vimentin phosphorylation.

articles.title: Nationwide clinical-genomic epidemiology of listeriosis in Taiwan, 2018-2025: disease manifestations in relation to clonal background.
articles.abstract: Listeriosis is an uncommon but severe foodborne infection, yet nationwide data linking pathogen genomics with clinical manifestations remain limited. We analyzed 1,252 laboratory-confirmed symptomatic listeriosis cases reported through nationwide surveillance in Taiwan during 2018-2025, with whole-genome sequencing of the corresponding clinical Listeria monocytogenes isolate from every case. The average annual incidence was 6.68 cases per 1,000,000 person-years, and 30-day all-cause mortality was 11.4%. Incidence showed an age-dependent sex pattern, with higher incidence among females aged 15-44 years and a shift toward male predominance at older ages. The female excess at ages 15-44 years persisted after exclusion of documented maternal-neonatal cases (male-to-female incidence rate ratio, 0.57; 95% confidence interval, 0.36-0.89). Clonal complex 87 (CC87) was the predominant CC (35.9%), whereas CC1 and CC2 were associated with higher odds of central nervous system (CNS) infection. LIPI-4 occurred predominantly in CC87, and LIPI-4-positive isolates showed lower odds of CNS infection; however, this association could not be separated from clonal background. More broadly, most associations of pathogenicity islands, virulence genes, and their alleles with disease manifestations could not be separated from the underlying clonal backgrounds in which these markers occurred, and none of the estimable associations remained significant after CC adjustment. This nationwide clinical-genomic study characterizes the contemporary burden of listeriosis in Taiwan and highlights clonal background as essential context for interpreting associations between virulence markers and disease manifestations.

articles.title: The attachment rate of Vibrio anguillarum to microplastics strongly varies with strain identity, particle characteristics, and environmental conditions.
articles.abstract: Microplastics (MPs), resulting from plastic objects and waste degradation, are increasingly abundant, particularly in marine environments. They exhibit a hydrophobic surface on which biofilms form easily. Metagenomic analyses of these biofilms have revealed that they often contain bacterial species potentially pathogenic to humans or animals. For this reason, MPs are suspected to present a risk to public health by acting as a vector for pathogenic bacterial species. To better understand this hazard, we studied different factors potentially affecting the bacterial attachment rate to MPs. Focusing on the fish pathogen Vibrio anguillarum, a collection of 16 GFP-labeled strains was assembled, including isolates from infected fish. Their attachment rates were measured using fluorescence microscopy on three types of MPs (milled polypropylene and polyethylene terephthalate particles, and commercially available polystyrene beads). A strong effect of the particle type was found, with higher attachment rates on milled particles, whose surface appeared qualitatively rougher based on visual examination of scanning electron microscopy images. Our results also revealed an intraspecific variation in attachment rate, highlighting the need for testing several strains of the same species to assess attachment rate and related hazards. Finally, it was observed that when a biofilm had formed by field incubation of the MPs, the differences in attachment rates between particle types were erased. The attachment of V. anguillarum depends on a combination of strain-related factors, particle characteristics, and environmental conditions, highlighting the need to combine microbiology, materials science, and environmental sciences to achieve a comprehensive risk assessment associated with MPs.IMPORTANCEMicroplastics (MPs) are increasingly abundant, particularly in marine environments. They are suspected to present a risk to public health by acting as a vector for pathogenic bacterial species. Focusing on the fish pathogen Vibrio anguillarum, we measured the attachment rates of 16 strains on three types of microplastics (milled polypropylene and polyethylene terephthalate particles, and commercially available polystyrene beads). This study highlights a strong effect of the particle type, with higher attachment rates on irregular particles, as well as a strong intraspecific variation. In a second experiment, it was observed that when a natural marine biofilm had already formed on the microplastic particles, differences in attachment rates between particle types were erased. Our findings emphasize the importance of accounting for multiple factors when assessing the risks of MPs as carriers of pathogenic bacteria, with our study addressing the first step of the conceptual pathway linking attachment, persistence, transport, exposure, and ultimately infection.

articles.title: Efficacy of empagliflozin in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction according to the presence of echocardiographic features of diastolic dysfunction in the EMPEROR-Preserved trial.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To define the impact of diastolic dysfunction (DD) on the response to empagliflozin treatment in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Diastolic dysfunction was defined by left atrial volume index ≥34 ml/m2, the ratio of early diastolic mitral inflow velocity to early diastolic mitral annular tissue velocity (E/e) ≥ 13 or left ventricular mass index >115 (males) or >95 (females). We created three categories of increasing DD (0, 1, or ≥2 DD criteria at baseline) to describe the effect of DD on response to empagliflozin therapy and adverse effects. Of 5988 patients in the EMPEROR-Preserved trial, 3766 (63%) had no documented baseline DD, 1619 (27%) had one, and 603 (10%) had two or more measures. Baseline DD was associated with sex, race, ethnicity, and region and was more common with lower heart rate, DBP, body weight, and eGFR. Despite baseline DD not being significantly associated with the primary endpoint of hospitalization for heart failure or cardiovascular death within the placebo group, a progressive treatment effect across the three DD categories was seen (trend test P-value .0014), with estimated hazard ratios of empagliflozin vs placebo of 0.91 (none present), 0.64 (1 present), and 0.49 (≥2). A significant treatment-by-subgroup trend test was also observed for the total number of hospitalizations for heart failure. Both Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score improvement at week 52 and safety profile were consistent across DD categories.

CONCLUSION: Baseline detection of echocardiographic DD predicted improved clinical response to empagliflozin in a graded fashion, but the reasons cannot be reliably determined from this analysis.

articles.title: Phage-encoded protein PhiP targets HemA to block heme biosynthesis, suppressing bacterial growth and promoting phage propagation.
articles.abstract: Bacteriophages encode diverse proteins that subvert host metabolism to promote viral propagation. Elucidating the functions and mechanisms of these proteins not only deepens our understanding of phage-host interactions but also offers new avenues for antibacterial development. Here, we identify PhiP, a protein encoded by the Pseudomonas aeruginosa phage PaoP5, as a potent inhibitor of bacterial growth. Ectopic expression of PhiP leads to impaired cell proliferation and elongation. Co-immunoprecipitation assays identify HemA, the glutamyl-tRNA reductase that catalyzes the first committed step of heme biosynthesis, as a direct interacting target of PhiP. Mechanistically, PhiP-mediated inhibition of HemA disrupts heme production, leading to accumulation of intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS), heightened sensitivity to hydrogen peroxide, and subsequent growth suppression. Finally, transcriptomic analysis reveals global dysregulation of genes involved in iron uptake and redox homeostasis. Furthermore, infection-based experiments demonstrate that PhiP plays an important role in efficient phage propagation. Collectively, our findings uncover a mechanism by which a phage-encoded protein targets heme biosynthesis to perturb ROS homeostasis, suppress bacterial growth, and promote efficient phage propagation. This work expands our understanding of phage-mediated metabolic manipulation of host bacteria and may inspire novel strategies for antibacterial therapy.IMPORTANCEMultidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a leading cause of hospital-acquired infections with limited treatment options. Bacteriophages represent a promising alternative to antibiotics, but the molecular mechanisms by which their proteins inhibit bacterial growth remain largely unexplored. This study identifies PhiP, a phage protein that targets heme biosynthesis, to exert antibacterial activity against P. aeruginosa. This blockade triggers toxic oxygen compound accumulation inside the cell to inhibit cell growth and promote efficient phage propagation. This mechanism is distinct from previously described phage inhibitors, which typically target essential structural and functional components of the bacterial cell. Importantly, PhiP targets HemA, a conserved enzyme in Pseudomonas, highlighting its potential as a scaffold for new anti-infective agents. Our findings expand the known repertoire of phage-host interactions and offer a new blueprint for antimicrobial drug discovery.

articles.title: Optimal regimens of praziquantel for schistosomiasis in young children.
articles.abstract: Praziquantel (PZQ) is the drug of choice for control and treatment of schistosomiasis. Pharmacokinetic (PK) data for establishing a safe and effective PZQ dose in preschool-aged children are limited. We characterized PZQ pharmacokinetics in children aged 1-4 years with intestinal schistosomiasis. PZQ was administered at either 40 mg/kg or 80 mg/kg (split into two doses of 40 mg/kg, 3 h apart), and plasma concentrations were quantified. These data were pooled with pre-existing PK data from children aged 3-8 years, who received PZQ 40 mg/kg or 60 mg/kg. A population PK model was fitted to the pooled data, and individual drug exposure was estimated. Pharmacodynamic outcomes were egg reduction rate, and both parasitological and antigenic cure at 4 weeks post-treatment. The relationship between PZQ exposure and cure was established using regression analysis. Monte Carlo simulations were performed to assess the adequacy of weight-based PZQ dosing. A two-compartment model, with first-order absorption and elimination, best described PZQ disposition. Total body weight was allowed to influence clearance and the central compartment volume, with fixed allometric exponents 0.75 and 1, respectively. Simulations indicated that both weight-banded fixed-dose regimens and individual weight-based dosing achieved comparable drug exposures. The area under the concentration-time curve (AUC0-24) of the total drug was a strong predictor of parasitological cure. PZQ 80 mg/kg achieved parasitological cure rates >85% but may still be insufficient for complete worm elimination, as demonstrated by the lower rate (69.5%) of antigen clearance. Further optimization of anti-schistosomiasis treatments may be required to achieve complete worm elimination in mass treatment programs.IMPORTANCESchistosomiasis is a neglected tropical disease of significant global health concern, disproportionately affecting children in endemic areas. Praziquantel (PZQ) is the only drug currently recommended by the WHO, as a single 40 mg/kg dose for treatment of schistosomiasis. However, pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) data to support optimal dosing of PZQ for children <5 years are limited. In this study, we evaluated the PK/PD of PZQ, administered at 80 mg/kg (split into two doses of 40 mg/kg, 3 h apart), vs the standard 40 mg/kg regimen, in children aged 1-4 years. Our results indicate that PZQ exposure following 80 mg/kg achieves parasitological cure more effectively than the current standard 40 mg/kg single-dose regimen. In children with a heavy infection intensity, the 80 mg/kg dose may still be insufficient to achieve complete worm clearance. These results highlight the need for further optimization of PZQ regimens and the discovery and development of new antiparasitic agents.

articles.title: HIV-1 subtype C: ecological fitness for efficient spread?
articles.abstract: HIV-1 subtype C accounts for nearly half of global HIV infections and dominates in southern Africa, India, and parts of Asia. The global distribution and burden of subtype C may reflect founder effects, population size and structure, migration, transmission networks, epidemic history, and access to prevention and treatment, as well as efficient transmission fitness. The epidemiological success of clade C viruses seems at odds with conventional measurements of viral fitness. Several studies have reported that subtype C isolates exhibit reduced replication capacity compared to other clades of HIV-1 in activated peripheral blood mononuclear cells and blood-derived macrophages. These observations indicate that standard laboratory assays may not adequately capture the determinants of viral success in human populations. Here, we discuss the evidence that HIV-1 fitness may be ecological and dependent on the various changing cellular, anatomical, immunological, and epidemiological environments encountered during transmission and infection. Several characteristics of HIV-1 subtype C, including persistent CCR5 usage, CpG content, LTR promoter architecture, Tat function, and ongoing changes in regulatory and budding motifs, may influence transmission, replication, persistence, disease progression, and viral loads across distinct environments. Rather than representing a uniformly more or less fit lineage, subtype C may provide a model for understanding how ongoing adaptation to changing host environments may shape viral fitness and pandemic spread.

articles.title: SARS-CoV-2 Nsp2 reprograms host immunity to drive pathogenic inflammation.
articles.abstract: Despite the end of the COVID-19 pandemic, SARS-CoV-2 continues to circulate endemically, highlighting the need to better understand the viral determinants of pathogenesis. Putative functions of the non-structural protein 2 (Nsp2) have been studied in vitro, but how Nsp2 affects pathogenesis and overall viral fitness in vivo has yet to be demonstrated. Here, we generated a recombinant SARS-CoV-2 lacking Nsp2 (ΔNsp2) to investigate its role in viral replication and disease. While ΔNsp2 replicated comparably to wild-type virus in vitro and in vivo, its deletion resulted in markedly attenuated disease in K18-hACE2 mice. Wild-type virus infection induced a strong pro-inflammatory response associated with increased recruitment of monocytes and macrophages, whereas ΔNsp2 virus infection promoted a more balanced antiviral response characterized by enhanced lymphocyte and NK cell recruitment. This was accompanied by reduced pulmonary and systemic inflammation and distinct transcriptional programs, including downregulation of pathways related to RNA processing and translation. Mechanistically, CLIP-seq and proximity labeling suggest that Nsp2 interacts with host RNA and components of the translational machinery. Together, our findings identify Nsp2 as a key virulence factor that drives immunopathology by skewing host immune responses, highlighting its role as a regulator of host-pathogen interactions.IMPORTANCEThe COVID-19 pandemic has officially ended, yet the virus that causes it continues to circulate and evolve, making it important to understand what makes it cause severe disease. This study focuses on a viral protein called Nsp2 and asks what role it plays in driving illness. Using an animal model, we observed that when Nsp2 was removed from the virus, infected animals became far less sick, even though the virus itself replicated just as well. Instead of triggering the harmful, excessive inflammation typically seen with the full virus, the modified virus prompted a more balanced immune response. Further investigation revealed that Nsp2 interacts directly with the host's genetic machinery, suggesting a mechanism by which the virus hijacks immune signaling to worsen disease. These findings pinpoint Nsp2 as a driver of COVID-19 severity and a promising target for future therapies aimed at reducing inflammation rather than simply fighting the virus itself.

articles.title: The impact of gestational weight gain on perineal injury in primiparous women with normal pre-pregnancy BMI.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to determine the association between gestational weight gain (GWG) and the risk of perineal injury in nulliparous women with normal pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI).

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study (January 2012-January 2024) at a single tertiary center including nulliparous women with normal pre-pregnancy BMI (18.5-24.9 kg/m2) who delivered a singleton, live, term infant (≥37 weeks) vaginally, excluding pregestational or gestational diabetes. Participants were stratified by GWG per American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists guidelines (recommended 11.5-16 kg) into below-, within-, and above-recommended GWG groups. The primary outcome was perineal injury (1st-4th degree). Multivariable logistic regression assessed the independent association between GWG and perineal trauma.

RESULTS: Of 26 828 women, a total of 9019 (33.6%) had below-, 11 527 (43.0%) within-, and 6282 (23.4%) above-recommended GWG. Overall perineal injury was more common with above-recommended GWG (86.4% vs. 84.9% vs. 84.2%, P = 0.001), whereas obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) rates were comparable (0.9% vs. 0.7% vs. 0.7%, P = 0.506). The above-recommended group had higher rates of induction and epidural analgesia, longer second-stage duration, and higher birthweight (all P < 0.001). After adjustment, GWG category was not independently associated with overall perineal injury (above-recommended: odds ratio [OR] 1.021; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.930-1.120, P = 0.665) or OASI (above-recommended: OR 1.065; 95% CI 0.743-1.526, P = 0.733). Independent risk factors for perineal injury included vacuum extraction (OR 3.288), epidural analgesia (OR 1.489), occiput-posterior position (OR 1.450), induction (OR 1.285), and higher birthweight (OR 1.957 per kg).

CONCLUSION: Among nulliparous women with normal pre-pregnancy BMI, GWG, whether below, within, or above American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists recommendations, did not independently affect the risk of perineal tears or OASI. Intrapartum and fetal factors remain the primary determinants of perineal injury.

articles.title: Synthetic mRNA engineering beyond prophylactic infectious disease vaccines: epigenomic and molecular reprogramming of diseased cells.
articles.abstract: The clinical validation of mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccines in 2020-2021 accelerated the development of synthetic messenger RNA as a precision therapeutic platform beyond infectious disease prevention. Unlike gene therapy approaches that permanently modify genomic DNA, synthetic mRNA enables transient protein expression through programmable molecular engineering. This narrative review examines therapeutic applications of engineered mRNA, emphasizing its epigenomic potential. It discusses key engineering strategies, including nucleoside modifications, codon optimization, untranslated region engineering, cap chemistry, and advances in lipid nanoparticle and alternative delivery systems. Six therapeutic domains are explored: cancer immunotherapy, cardiac regeneration, monogenic diseases, genome and epigenome editing, autoimmune disease, and somatic cell reprogramming. Particular attention is given to mRNA-mediated replacement of chromatin regulators, dCas9-based epigenome editing, epigenetically derived tumor antigens, and transcription-factor-driven cellular reprogramming. The review distinguishes chemical nucleoside modifications from endogenous epitranscriptomic regulation and examines the differences between transient protein expression, heritable but reversible chromatin changes, and permanent genomic modifications. Clinical evidence, discontinued programs, and preclinical developments are critically evaluated. Despite promising advances, major challenges remain regarding delivery specificity, durability, safety, and clinical translation. Overall, synthetic mRNA represents an emerging platform for molecular and epigenetic therapeutic reprogramming beyond vaccination.

articles.title: Fostamatinib in immune thrombocytopenia: real-world experience in European countries.
articles.abstract: The management of immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is evolving with the availability of new treatments. Fostamatinib, targeting spleen tyrosine kinase-dependent platelet phagocytosis, offers an alternative approach; it has been approved in Europe and the USA for adult patients with chronic ITP who are refractory to other treatments. In recent years, experience has been gained with fostamatinib in clinical practice.
