Based on a symposium (Milan, June 2025) and augmented with relevant literature identified in PubMed and key references known to the authors, this article summarizes data from three large European real-world registry cohorts. Studies included heavily pretreated patients with ITP (median 3-6 previous treatments before starting fostamatinib). Real-world evidence offers insights for achieving more durable responses with respect to improving platelet counts, with >40% of patients still receiving fostamatinib after 6 months' therapy, providing indirect evidence of both its efficacy and safety in patients with difficult-to-manage ITP. Despite a lack of second-line effectiveness data, the low thrombosis incidence suggests an earlier place in treatment strategies for patients with a high baseline thrombosis risk. However, the overall findings are limited by the retrospective design of some studies, the heterogeneous nature of the patient populations, and the relatively small number of patients evaluated to date.

articles.title: Clinical Interpretation of Genetic Testing in Pediatric Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: From Molecular Findings to Action.
articles.abstract: Genetic testing has established diagnostic and family-management roles in pediatric pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), with additional gene-specific prognostic implications. This narrative review integrates contemporary pediatric cohorts, earlier childhood studies, adult evidence, and international recommendations to examine how molecular findings inform clinical care. Interpretation requires assessment of gene-disease validity, variant classification, inheritance, and phenotypic concordance. Well-supported results may refine disease classification, direct phenotypic evaluation, and enable cascade testing and surveillance. Pathogenic BMPR2 variants are associated with more severe hemodynamic disease and adverse outcomes across cohorts; this information complements longitudinal clinical risk assessment but does not precisely determine an individual child's course. TBX4-related disease spans PAH, neonatal respiratory failure, and developmental lung disorders, sometimes with subtle skeletal findings. Biallelic EIF2AK4 variants can establish heritable pulmonary veno-occlusive disease/pulmonary capillary hemangiomatosis and alter management. A variant of uncertain significance remains nondiagnostic, whereas a negative result must be interpreted within assay limitations. No germline variant has yet been validated to select a specific routine pediatric PAH drug. Genetic testing should therefore be linked to an explicit plan for diagnosis, gene-informed risk assessment, phenotype-directed care, and family follow-up.

articles.title: [The design process and protocol for a cognitive-behavioral intervention to reduce electronic cigarette use among university students].
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Electronic cigarette use has become an emerging Public Health concern among university students due to its increasing prevalence and the risks associated with nicotine exposure. Cognitive-behavioral interventions have shown promise in addressing this behavior; however, evidence on structured interventions adapted to the Mexican context remains limited. The aim of this study was to design an intervention to reduce electronic cigarette use among university students and establish the protocol for its implementation.

METHODS: The intervention was developed through the stages of discovery, design, and refinement. Its components were based on the Theory of Planned Behavior, while its activities were informed by the taxonomy of behaviour change methods. Subsequently, a pilot experimental longitudinal study with pretest, posttest, and three-month follow-up assessments will be conducted. A total of sixty university students aged eighteen/twenty-four years from a Mexican public university will be recruited through convenience sampling and randomly assigned to the study groups. The intervention will consist of six fifty-minute face-to-face sessions incorporating educational components, cognitive restructuring, and social and personal skills training. Statistical analyses will be exploratory and will include between-group comparisons, repeated-measures analyses, and estimation of effect sizes.

CONCLUSIONS: The protocol will provide preliminary evidence on the feasibility and initial evaluation of an intervention aimed at reducing electronic cigarette use, generating information to inform the design of future studies and prevention strategies for the Mexican university student population.

articles.title: Chain Orientation and Polycrystalline Disorder as Antagonistic Descriptors of Thermal and Triboelectric Transport in 3D-Nanoconfined PMMA, PEEK, and PET Nanowire Networks.
articles.abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) require polymers that dissipate frictional heat while retaining interfacial charge, yet the microstructural rules governing both functions remain unclear, including whether polymer thermal conductivity is governed primarily by crystallinity or by chain orientation and disorder. Here, interconnected 3D anodic alumina (3D-AAO) templates provide a common nanoconfinement platform for PMMA, PEEK, and PET. 2D-WAXS reveals amorphous PMMA, PEEK that crystallizes from a fully amorphous bulk to 67.8% crystallinity but remains azimuthally disordered, and strongly oriented PET (Hermans factor ƒc = 0.915) with a modest crystallinity increase (69.98 → 74.10%). PET reaches the highest effective-medium-derived polymer thermal conductivity (1.17 W·m- 1·K- 1), whereas PEEK shows no resolved thermal enhancement despite its high crystallinity. Amorphous PMMA shows the largest relative thermal-conductivity increase (+350%), evidencing confinement-related contributions independent of crystallization. Triboelectricity follows a contrasting trend: polycrystalline PEEK shows the largest relative enhancement (+365%), while PMMA delivers the highest absolute power density (19.71 µW·cm- 2). An Efficiency-Orientation Model phenomenologically captures the role of crystalline texture, revealing distinct and potentially competing microstructural descriptors for thermal and triboelectric performance. These results suggest that crystalline texture and disorder, not crystalline fraction alone, should be considered when designing nanoconfined polymers for thermally managed TENGs.

articles.title: Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome Protein Is Required for Glucocorticoid-Dependent Eosinopoiesis and Eosinophil-Rich Inflammation in Murine Models.
articles.abstract: Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome Protein (WASP) is a pleiotropic cytoskeletal regulator expressed in haematopoietic tissues that plays essential roles in immune cell function, including leukocyte migration and signalling. By contrast, WASP's roles in leukocyte production remain insufficiently explored. Recent observations of the regulation of murine eosinophil production by distinct signalling pathways, respectively involving glucocorticoids (GCs) and cysteinyl leukotrienes (CysLTs), prompted us to investigate their dependence on WASP. To explore the contribution of WASP to eosinophil development and its relationship to GC- and CysLT-dependent regulatory pathways in vivo and ex vivo. We used wild-type (WT) and WASP-deficient mice in models of thioglycolate-induced peritonitis, allergic asthma and surgical stress to assess eosinophil recruitment and production. We used ex vivo cultures, co-culture systems and pharmacological interventions (dexamethasone, hydrocortisone, indomethacin, leukotriene receptor agonist and antagonist) to evaluate eosinophil differentiation and regulation of the eosinopoietic microenvironment. WASP-deficient mice displayed reduced eosinophil accumulation at extramedullary inflammatory sites and failed to mount a GC-induced eosinopoietic response. This defect was associated with the adherent stromal-enriched compartment, as GC responsiveness was restored when WASP-deficient progenitors were co-cultured with WT adherent bone marrow cells. Conversely, CysLT-driven eosinopoiesis remained intact in WASP-deficient mice. Our findings indicate that GC-mediated induction of eosinopoiesis depends on a WASP-sensitive, heterogeneous adherent bone marrow compartment. In contrast, the CysLT pathway remains functional in the absence of WASP. These results suggest that WASP contributes to eosinophil production through effects associated with the adherent haematopoietic microenvironment, while the precise cellular subset responsible remains to be defined.

articles.title: The H2S-releasing metformin hybrid Met-ITC protects against diabetes-associated vascular dysfunction preserving glycaemic control.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Patients undergoing metformin (Met) therapy for the treatment of type 2 diabetes remain at high cardiovascular risk. Hydrogen sulphide (H2S)-releasing molecules offer antioxidant, anti-senescence and vasoactive properties that may complement Met activity. This study investigated whether metformin-isothiocyanate (Met-ITC), a H2S-releasing metformin hybrid, preserves the antidiabetic activity of Met while providing H2S-derived vascular protection.

EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: The predicted Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism and Excretion (ADME) properties of Met and Met-ITC were evaluated in silico. Maintenance of Met antidiabetic properties was assessed in vitro by evaluating glucose uptake in HepG2 cells and in vivo through oral glucose tolerance tests in db/db mice. The ability of Met-ITC to release H2S and its ability to preserve cell viability and contrast ROS formation and cellular senescence were evaluated in human aortic endothelial cells (HAECs) and smooth muscle cells (HASMCs) exposed to hydrogen peroxide, homocysteine or high-glucose concentrations. The hyperpolarizing effect of Met-ITC was tested on HASMCs and its direct vasorelaxing effect as well as its ability to inhibit noradrenaline-induced vasoconstriction were tested on endothelium-intact or -denuded rat aortic rings.

KEY RESULTS: Met-ITC showed a more favourable permeability profile than Met and maintained its antidiabetic profile. It provided better protection against oxidative stress, loss of cell viability and senescence compared with Met. Moreover, Met-ITC produced a concentration-dependent hyperpolarization of HASMCs, restricted noradrenaline-induced contraction and induced vasodilatation in endothelium-denuded and -intact rat aortic rings.

CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: These findings identify Met-ITC as a potential candidate for the treatment of diabetes-associated vascular dysfunction.

articles.title: Aciclovir in Neonatal Herpes Simplex Virus Infection in a Tertiary Care Unit-Experience From Western Australia.
articles.journal: Journal of paediatrics and child health

articles.title: Drug resistance and molecular epidemiology of pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae isolates in Southern China.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: To investigate antimicrobial susceptibility and molecular typing of recent pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae strains, analyze the correlations between drug resistance, pneumonia severity, and strain types, and provide evidence for precise M. pneumoniae infection management. Standard M. pneumoniae isolation and culture were applied to bronchoalveolar lavage fluid from 325 M. pneumoniae-infected children, with 23S rRNA resistance mutation detection. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing (eight antibiotics, microbroth dilution) was performed on 154 culture-positive strains, alongside multiple locus variable-number tandem repeat analysis (MLVA), whole-genome sequencing, and single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) genotyping. M. pneumoniae showed high macrolide resistance (99.35% for erythromycin and azithromycin), but high susceptibility to moxifloxacin/levofloxacin, with minocycline/doxycycline sensitivity at 98.71%. The 23S rRNA mutations occurred in 97.4% (150/154). MLVA type 4-5-7-2 dominated (135/154), with minor types totaling 15 cases. SNP typing clustered strains into four groups, mostly EC1 (138/154), with four genes showing cross-cluster mutations. Southern Chinese M. pneumoniae strains exhibit high macrolide resistance but good minocycline/doxycycline susceptibility, with EC1-cluster dominance driving rapid spread. This supports individualized therapy and epidemic trend tracking for pediatric M. pneumoniae lung infections.

IMPORTANCE: This study sheds light on why many children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia do not respond well to common macrolide antibiotics-over 99% of strains in Southern China are resistant. It identifies effective alternative drugs and pinpoints the dominant spreading strain, helping doctors choose precise treatments. For public health, it provides key data to track outbreaks, guiding targeted surveillance and better management of pediatric respiratory infections post-COVID-19.

articles.title: Development of a minicollagen (ncol-2)-targeted qPCR assay for improved quantification of Enteromyxum leei.
articles.abstract: Enteromyxum leei is a significant myxosporean parasite associated with emaciation syndrome in cultured fish, particularly olive flounder Paralichthys olivaceus in Korea, that can lead to substantial economic losses. Accurate quantification of parasite load is crucial for monitoring disease progression and assessing infection intensity. While 18S rDNA-targeted quantitative PCR (qPCR) has been widely used, the inherent copy-number plasticity of ribosomal arrays across different developmental stages limits its precision for absolute quantification, often introducing unpredictable signal inflation. In this study, we developed and validated a novel qPCR assay targeting the minicollagen (ncol-2) gene, a putative low-copy structural gene expected to maintain a relatively stable genomic ratio per nucleus. The ncol-2 qPCR assay demonstrated high linearity (R2 = 0.999) and an amplification efficiency of 95.4% over a range of 102 to 107 copies μl-1, with a robust limit of detection (LoD95) of 8.57 copies μl-1. The assay showed high specificity with no cross-reactivity against other myxosporean parasites and exhibited acceptable repeatability across different real-time PCR platforms. Comparative analysis using 100 clinical samples revealed a strong correlation (r = 0.978) between the ncol-2 and 18S rDNA assays. Notably, copy numbers estimated by the ncol-2 assay were, on average, 29.68-fold lower than those from the 18S rDNA assay, with a marked sample-to-sample fluctuation (SD ± 13.8). This disparity demonstrates that ncol-2 effectively reduces copy-number variability associated with ribosomal gene duplication, providing a more biologically accurate and standardized molecular tool for improved quantification of E. leei in both diagnostic and epidemiological research.

articles.title: Seasonal variation in chytrid infection in a stream-dwelling frog in Southern Brazil.
articles.abstract: Many wildlife disease systems exhibit pronounced seasonal dynamics driven by environmental conditions that modulate pathogen growth and host susceptibility. The aquatic fungus Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd), which infects and threatens amphibians worldwide, presents a seasonal infection pattern linked to different factors that drive disease outbreaks and population decline. Here, we investigated seasonal and individual variation in Bd infection in the stream-dwelling frog Limnomedusa macroglossa, which inhabits rocky outcrops in southern Brazil. A seasonal infection peak was detected, with higher prevalence and infection loads during the cold months, and temperature was an important predictor of Bd detection probability. Individuals that exhibited infection peaks during the cold season showed a marked reduction or complete clearance of Bd when recaptured in the warm season, and many remained Bd-negative or maintained very low loads, suggesting rapid infection clearance. These findings indicate that the analyzed population can persist despite the presence of the aquatic pathogen. Identifying the microclimatic factors that enable hosts to eliminate Bd infections, or alternatively, promote pathogen persistence in the environment, is crucial for understanding population resilience and informing wildlife disease management strategies.

articles.title: Infectious hematopoietic necrosis virus detection system established based on the multienzyme isothermal rapid amplification (MIRA) method.
articles.abstract: Infectious hematopoietic necrosis virus (IHNV) is an important pathogen of salmonid fish. In this study, a multienzyme isothermal rapid amplification (MIRA) assay targeting a conserved region of the IHNV N gene was established for rapid detection. The performance of the assay was evaluated using IHNV RNA standards, and further compared with digital PCR (dPCR) using 8 IHNV isolates, 12 cell culture supernatants, and 67 tissue samples from rainbow trout suspected of IHNV infection. The MIRA assay produced detectable signals within approximately 20 min. A detection rate of 100% was achieved at 102 copies μl-1 using RNA standards. The assay successfully detected all 8 IHNV isolates and showed no cross-reaction with non-target fish viruses. For cell culture supernatants and tissue samples, the MIRA assay showed a high level of agreement with dPCR results. These findings indicate that the MIRA assay may serve as a rapid and practical method for IHNV detection, particularly for on-site screening and preliminary diagnosis in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Identifying barriers to headache care for Black patients in Toronto: A community-informed qualitative study of patient experience and recommendations.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES/BACKGROUND: Our objective was to gain a better understanding of how Black patients in the Greater Toronto Area experience barriers and facilitators of headache care. Headache is a common, potentially serious neurological condition. Migraine specifically, can lead to emergency room visits, missed workdays, and a reduction in overall quality of life. Black and Indigenous communities experience worse headache outcomes compared to other communities. We engaged Black patients with headache in the Greater Toronto Area to learn from their perspectives on barriers they face in accessing headache care.

METHODS: This study deployed an intersectional, community-informed qualitative research methodology. We included patients between 18 and 65 years of age who self-identified as Black and live in the Greater Toronto Area. We conducted semistructured interviews between July 2022 and September 2023. Interviews were deidentified and transcribed prior to inductive thematic analysis to reveal emerging themes and subthemes.

RESULTS: We conducted a total of 12 interviews. Ten were included for analysis. Multiple themes and subthemes were identified, including the impact of headache on personal and family quality of life, negative experiences in emergency departments, as well as challenges navigating primary and specialist care. Patients specifically noted delays in receiving a diagnosis, lack of headache education, and difficulty accessing appropriate pharmacological therapies. Barriers to headache specialist care included difficulty getting time off work, cost of transportation, lack of access to referrals, and wait time to see a specialist.

CONCLUSION: This is the first study to document the experiences of Black patients seeking headache care in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Patients with headaches face barriers to care regardless of race, ethnicity, or socioeconomic status. This was not a comparative study; rather, we specifically sought to hear the voices of patients from historically marginalized Black communities who have not been reflected in research and for whom headache outcomes are poor relative to other communities. The participants provided key insights into areas for improvement. Participant recommendations include location of specialist clinics in Black communities, use of social media and other community news networks to promote migraine and headache education in communities, and ongoing use of virtual care models to increase scheduling flexibility and reduce financial burdens of seeking care. Physicians and clinic staff who reflect communities they serve were recommended as a way of improving physician-patient respect and communication.

articles.title: ZmSGT1-mediated competitive protection of ZmBBI1 enhances maize resistance to Rhizoctonia solani.
articles.abstract: Banded leaf and sheath blight (BLSB), incited by the necrotrophic basidiomycete Rhizoctonia solani, is a devastating soil-borne disease that severely constrains global maize (Zea mays) production. Bowman-Birk inhibitors (BBIs) constitute a critical class of protease inhibitors in plant innate immunity; yet, their biological functions and upstream regulatory circuits in maize defense against necrotrophic pathogens remain largely uncharacterized. Here, we show that ZmBBI1, a BBI family member transcriptionally upregulated upon R. solani infection, positively modulates BLSB resistance. Its defense activity is strictly dependent on trypsin-inhibitory function, mediated by the evolutionarily conserved Thr52 and Arg53 residues in its canonical reactive loop. We identify Rs03254, a secreted virulence effector from R. solani, that directly engages ZmBBI1 and biochemically inactivates its protease-inhibitory activity to promote fungal colonization. We further demonstrate that the conserved immune co-chaperone ZmSGT1 physically interacts with ZmBBI1 and is genetically required for its full defense function. Mechanistically, ZmSGT1 competes with Rs03254 for binding to ZmBBI1, displacing the pathogen effector and restoring ZmBBI1's trypsin-inhibitory activity. Our work defines a tripartite molecular arms race module in the maize-R. solani pathosystem and uncovers a noncanonical role for SGT1 as a molecular bodyguard that protects host defense factors from effector-mediated suppression, providing actionable targets for engineering durable BLSB resistance in maize.

articles.title: A novel mechanism for morphological change during bacterial sporulation based on programmed peptidoglycan degradation.
articles.abstract: Many bacteria form spores to endure unfavorable conditions. While Firmicutes generate endospores through cell division, sporulation in non-Firmicutes remains less understood. The Gram-negative bacterium Myxococcus xanthus undergoes sporulation through two distinct mechanisms: rapid sporulation triggered by chemical induction and slow sporulation driven by starvation, both occurring independently of cell division. Instead, these processes depend on the complete degradation of the peptidoglycan (PG) cell wall by two lytic transglycosylases (LTGs), LtgA and LtgB. Remarkably, LtgB programs the pace of PG degradation by LtgA during rapid sporulation, ensuring a controlled process that prevents abrupt PG breakdown and the formation of non-resistant pseudospores. In addition to regulation between LTGs, PG degradation is also influenced by its synthesis; cells exhibiting increased muropeptide production often circumvent sporulation. These findings not only reveal novel mechanisms of bacterial sporulation but also shed light on the regulatory network governing PG dynamics.

articles.title: A step toward understanding pediatric occipital neuralgia: Investigating occipital headaches in a pediatric neurology clinic.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Occipital neuralgia (ON) is well characterized in adults but remains poorly understood in children. Pediatric ON may present with overlapping headache features and variable treatment responses, creating diagnostic and management challenges.

OBJECTIVES: We aimed to (1) characterize pediatric patients presenting to a tertiary outpatient neurology clinic with occipital headache symptoms consistent with ON, (2) describe their overlap with other headache symptom profiles, and (3) summarize documented diagnostic evaluation, treatment patterns, and clinical outcomes.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using prospectively collected, standardized headache intake questionnaire data from the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) headache registry, including pediatric patients evaluated in outpatient neurology from July 2016 through August 2024. Self-reported headache characteristics were used to identify a cohort of patients with symptoms consistent with ON, defined as recurrent, short-duration, stabbing or sharp, severe pain involving the occipital region. We excluded patients who also had frontotemporal or holocephalic pain. However, to avoid missing patients with overlapping headache phenotypes, we did not exclude patients whose headaches also met criteria for other diagnoses such as migraine.

RESULTS: We identified 89 of 14,876 (0.6%) patients within the registry with symptoms consistent with ON, predominantly male (54%) with a median age of 12.7 years (interquartile range, 9.3-15.5). Sixty of the 89 (67%) patients additionally met symptom-based criteria for another headache disorder, mostly migraine. Forty-five of 89 (51%) patients followed up over a median of 1.1 years (interquartile range, 0.6-4.2), with 35 of 45 attempting treatment. At the most recent follow-up of those treated, 26% reported significant improvement (9 of 35; 95% confidence interval [CI], 12.5%-43.3%), 29% some improvement (10 of 35; 95% CI, 14.6%-46.3%), 26% no change (9 of 35; 95% CI, 12.5%-43.3%), and 20% worsened (7 of 35; 95% CI, 8.4%-36.9%).

CONCLUSION: Symptoms consistent with ON are rare, even among children with occipital headaches, and frequently overlap with features of other primary headache disorders. These findings highlight the diagnostic complexity of pediatric occipital headache and the need for improved characterization and standardized evaluation to inform future treatment pathways for children with persistent ON-like symptoms.

articles.title: Immunomodulatory natural products via toll-like receptor 2 signalling: from agonists to inhibitors across diverse natural sources.
articles.abstract: Covering: up to 2025Toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) is a versatile pattern recognition receptor whose activity can be tuned in either direction-agonism or antagonism-to produce distinct therapeutic outcomes, ranging from vaccine adjuvants and cancer immunotherapeutics to anti-inflammatory agents for sepsis, neuroinflammation, and autoimmune disease. Natural products from bacteria, fungi, plants, and marine organisms have emerged as a structurally rich source of TLR2 modulators, encompassing acylated lipopeptides, glycolipids, polysaccharides, flavonoids, non-flavonoid polyphenols, an aromatic aldehyde, an aporphine alkaloid, and even large bacterial antagonist proteins. This review surveys these natural TLR2 agonists and inhibitors, highlighting how the effective allocation of hydrophobic chains between the TLR2 pocket and its partner receptor, rather than total acyl-chain number alone, combines with chain branching, stereochemical presentation and polar head-group interactions to govern TLR1/TLR6 heterodimer selectivity among bacterial and gut-commensal lipids, and how mechanistically distinct inhibitory strategies-direct receptor competition, transcriptional downregulation, and TIR-domain interference-converge on a shared druggable interface exploited independently by plant polyphenols and staphylococcal virulence factors alike. Persistent experimental challenges are also discussed, including microbial contamination of natural extracts and structural heterogeneity of isolated lipids, along with how total synthesis and chemically defined oligomers have resolved these ambiguities, underscoring natural products as a promising yet still underexploited chemical space for developing selective TLR2-targeted therapeutics.

articles.title: Evidence-based clinical practice national guideline for elective female genital aesthetic labiaplasty: recommendations from the pelvic floor and cosmetic gynecology (PETKOZ) association and expert consensus.
articles.journal: Journal of the Turkish German Gynecological Association
articles.abstract: The increasing global demand for elective female genital cosmetic surgery (FGCS), combined with substantial variability in clinical practice and patient counseling, highlights the need for standardized evidence-based guidance. This national guideline was developed by the Pelvic Floor and Cosmetic Gynecology Association to provide graded recommendations for the evaluation, surgical management, and perioperative care of women seeking elective FGCS, with particular emphasis on labiaplasty. A structured electronic database search was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, Google Scholar, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Scopus from inception through April 2026, supplemented by grey literature screening. Evidence grading followed the Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network classification. Methodological quality was appraised using AMSTAR 2, Cochrane RoB 2, and Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies of Interventions. For clinical questions not sufficiently addressed by available literature, a three-round modified Delphi consensus process was conducted with 24 specialists, each with a minimum of 50 labiaplasty procedures. Of 1,514 records identified, 20 studies met inclusion criteria, comprising 8 systematic reviews and meta-analyses, 2 randomized controlled trials, and 10 observational cohort studies. Labiaplasty was associated with significant and reproducible postoperative improvements in genital self-image across all study designs, independent of surgical technique (grade B; evidence level 2+). Sexual function outcomes showed consistent improvement, predominantly in the pain and satisfaction domains, though overall certainty of evidence was very low owing to high heterogeneity and predominantly uncontrolled designs (grade C; evidence level 1-). Labiaplasty-seeking behavior was characterized by a multidimensional motivational profile; body dysmorphic disorder (BDD) criteria were fulfilled by 18.2% of candidates in controlled studies (grade C; evidence level 2+). Sexual partner coercion constituted a numerically minor direct pathway to surgery (6.9%), whereas partner-attributed negative genital comments were recalled by 36.7% of candidates in meta-analytic synthesis, representing a clinically relevant discrete vulnerability (grade C; evidence level 2+). Expert consensus yielded structured recommendations across patient selection, preoperative psychological screening, perioperative management, surgical principles, and complication prevention. This guideline provides the first national evidence-based framework for elective FGCS. Labiaplasty confers reproducible benefits in genital self-image and sexual function; however, the evidence base remains constrained by methodological heterogeneity and limited high-quality randomized data. Mandatory BDD screening, preoperative psychological evaluation, and standardized patient-reported outcome measurement are identified as critical components of ethical clinical practice.

articles.title: Development of quality indicators for systemic sclerosis patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop quality indicators for evaluating and improving care for patients with systemic sclerosis.

METHODS: We developed quality indicators using a modified RAND/University of California Los Angeles Appropriateness Method. A systematic literature review identified candidate items from previous systemic sclerosis quality indicator studies and clinical practice guidelines. A multidisciplinary expert panel of 10 physicians specializing in rheumatology, dermatology, pediatrics and cardiology completed two anonymous rating rounds, with item revision after a web-based panel meeting. One physiotherapist and one patient with systemic sclerosis participated as non-voting observers. Items with a median appropriateness score of 7 or higher and strict agreement were retained.

RESULTS: The review identified 86 candidate items from three quality indicator studies and 23 clinical practice guidelines. After first-round rating and discussion, 78 revised items underwent second-round evaluation. Thirty-three indicators met the prespecified selection criteria. The final set covered general management, lung, gastrointestinal, kidney, heart, pulmonary hypertension, vascular, muscle, rehabilitation, and pediatric domains.

CONCLUSIONS: We developed a 33-item quality indicator set for systemic sclerosis through a structured consensus process. The indicators may support quality assessment and improvement in Japanese clinical practice.

articles.title: Macropolycytes: A Series of 30 Cases.
articles.abstract: Macropolycytes are tetraploid polymorphonuclear granulocytes with various significance hypothesized. A retrospective review from a single centre of all the documented cases of macropolycytes in the peripheral blood from 2017 to 2024 was carried out for descriptive statistics. There were 30 cases. The aetiologies included infections (n = 7), rheumatoid disorders (n = 6), post-haematopoietic cell transplantation (n = 5), post-chemotherapy (n = 3), post-corticosteroids (n = 3), acute haemolysis (n = 3), and others (n = 3). All patients had either neutrophil predominance on differential count (n = 29), granulocytic left-shift (n = 28), or leucoerythroblastic reaction (n = 9). The occurrence of macropolycytes parallels granulocytic proliferation and per se may not be of any significance.

articles.title: Transitional Care for Juvenile-onset Rheumatic and Musculoskeletal Diseases in Japan: A Web-based Survey of JCR and PRAJ Councillors/Board Members.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe transitional care for juvenile rheumatic and musculoskeletal disorders in Japan and identify barriers/facilitators to collaboration between departments and facilities.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional web-based survey in Japan (19 February-26 April 2025) targeting councillors/board members of the Japan College of Rheumatology and the Paediatric Rheumatology Association of Japan. Fisher's exact tests and odds ratios were used for comparing adult and paediatric rheumatology services, and five major cities and others. Sparse cells were examined using Firth's penalised logistic regression.

RESULTS: Of 159 submitted questionnaires, 122 were valid. Over 70% managed transitioned patients in the past 3 years. Respondents perceived that transition-related activity had increased (34.9%), whereas barriers remained unchanged (68.6%). Among adult rheumatology declining transitioned patients, 83.3% reported 'no referral received'. Awareness/ever utilised was 73.3%/24.4% for the Transition Support Guide and 45.3%/23.3% for MIRAI TALK, a patient-held transition communication/support tool for paediatric rheumatic diseases. Paediatrics showed higher awareness and ever utilisation of both tools than adult rheumatology. Preconception care awareness was high, with 68.9% implementation and with significantly less frequent male-targeted counselling in adult rheumatology. Awareness of transitional care support centres was limited (one-third) and lower in adult rheumatology.

CONCLUSION: Among surveyed rheumatology specialists, transition-related activity was perceived to have increased, but referral gaps, low adult-side tool uptake, and limited consultation pathways persist.

articles.title: Identifying Adverse Drug Withdrawal Events at Scale Using Electronic Clinical Data: Development, Adjudication, and Practical Challenges.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There are no scalable, automated methods to identify adverse drug withdrawal events (ADWE) in deprescribing studies. We describe the development of a scalable approach to identifying potential ADWE using electronic clinical data, characterize the ADWE identified, and discuss complexities encountered.

METHODS: We identified potential ADWE through two steps: (1) identifying intentional medication discontinuations; (2) applying diagnostic and procedure codes and clinical parameters suggestive of possible ADWE in specified risk timeframes. Discontinuations of five medication classes (oral diabetes medications, statins, bladder antimuscarinics, antihypertensives, and anticoagulants/antiplatelet agents) for adults age ≥ 65 enrolled with Kaiser Permanente Colorado (KPCO) were identified through text search and medication order data and confirmed through chart review. Electronically identified potential ADWE were manually adjudicated; notes made during adjudication were analyzed using qualitative content analysis to classify possible ADWE and characterize associated features.

RESULTS: Within specific drug groups, between 51% (39/76 bladder antimuscarinics) and 81% (104/128 antihypertensives) were confirmed as intended discontinuations. Manual adjudication across all drug groups classified 60 of 293 events as possible ADWE, 23 probable, and 2 definite; 1 major ADWE resulted in hospitalization. Adjudication illuminated 5 challenges in classifying ADWE: (1) Causal Inference: unclear whether potential ADWE had a clear causal link to medication discontinuation given medical complexity; (2) Timeframe: event occurred outside expected risk window; (3) Contraindication: medication was intentionally held due to acute contraindication; resulting clinical changes were expected; (4) Terminology: medication had never been effective; symptoms were present both before and after discontinuation, and did not recur as a result of stopping drug; and (5) Intent: observed clinical change was intended or expected outcome of stopping medication.

CONCLUSIONS: Many potential ADWE may be expected or intended sequelae of appropriate clinical care, or unavoidable. Future research should define and validate ADWE. Broader terminology is required to avoid mislabeling expected consequences as ADWE.

articles.title: Accuracy of Dental Students' Predictions Regarding Which Underserved Populations They Anticipate Treating Post-Graduation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE/OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this longitudinal study was to determine whether dental students who expressed a willingness to treat underserved populations actually treat them as practicing dentists.

METHODS: Since Fall 2008, dental students at the University of Iowa have completed a student survey assessing their willingness to treat 13 underserved populations five or more years post-graduation. A follow-up alumni survey was developed and mailed in Fall 2023 to the 741 alumni who graduated between 2009 and 2018. The alumni survey inquired whether they provide care to the same 13 populations. Alumni's responses were matched to their student surveys that they completed during their D1 and D4 years of dental school. Descriptive statistics were calculated to depict the characteristics of the respondents. McNemar's tests were conducted to assess significant differences between participants' responses as students versus their responses as alumni.

RESULTS: In total, 227 alumni surveys were received. There were 135 D1 surveys and 155 D4 surveys that could be matched to a corresponding alumni survey. McNemar's tests revealed significant differences (p < 0.05) for seven patient populations when comparing D1 and alumni responses, and eight patient populations when comparing D4 and alumni responses. Although many respondents reported treating more underserved populations as alumni than they had anticipated as dental students, they overestimated their future treatment of certain populations such as Medicaid, homebound/nursing home, and incarcerated patients.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that, in general, respondents treated a broader spectrum of patients than they anticipated treating while they were dental students.

articles.title: Implementation of a Shared Care Network in Pediatric Oncology Through a Hub-and-Spoke Model in a Resource-Limited Setting: A Multicenter Descriptive Study From Pakistan.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Access to pediatric oncology services is limited in resource-constrained lower middle-income countries like Pakistan. A hub-and-spoke shared care network (SCN) was implemented in the province of Sindh by Indus Hospital & Health Network (IHHN) with the support of My Child Matters Grant (FoundationS), to decentralize selected services, strengthen local capacity, and improve access to care closer to patients' homes.

METHODS: A multicenter, retrospective descriptive study was conducted from July 2023 to December 2024. IHHN served as the Level III hub, supporting four shared care centers (Level I-Larkana and Shikarpur, and Level II-Civil Hospital Karachi and Nawabshah). Pediatric patients ≤16 years seen at SCCs or referred between SCCs and the hub were included; patients managed solely at the hub were excluded. Descriptive and inferential statistics summarized patient characteristics, visit patterns, and treatment outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 284 patients accessed the SCN (Level I: 91 and Level II: 193), with a median age of 7 (interquartile range [IQR]: 4-12) years; male:female ratio 1.4:1. Across 1519 visits, 86% were outpatient/daycare, with higher average visits per patient at Level II centers. Acute leukemia was most common (53%, with no statistically significant variation in diagnostic distribution across levels of care (p = 0.106). However, significant variation was observed in visit types (p < 0.001) and treatment outcomes (p < 0.015) across levels. At analysis cutoff, 58% were in first complete remission, 10% abandoned treatment, 9% relapsed, and 7% died during curative therapy. Forty-six staff participated in capacity-building training.

CONCLUSIONS: The shared care network is a feasible approach to expand pediatric oncology services in resource-limited settings. It enhanced access, supported local capacity building, and maintained continuity of care, demonstrating potential for scale-up in similar contexts.

articles.title: The role of the corrugator supercilii and its impact on the evolution of migraine medicine: A narrative review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To review the historical significance, mechanism of action, anatomy, procedural techniques, injection complications, and emerging clinical implications of the corrugator supercilii muscle in the treatment of chronic migraine with onabotulinumtoxinA.

BACKGROUND: The corrugator supercilii muscle occupies a unique position in headache medicine as the anatomical site central to the initial observations that led to the development of onabotulinumtoxinA as a preventive therapy for chronic migraine. The supraorbital and supratrochlear nerves are closely aligned with the corrugator muscle, and thus this muscle can provide a path to the trigeminal pain pathways. Observations of migraine improvement following aesthetic botulinum toxin into the glabellar region ultimately led to its use as an effective chronic migraine preventive therapy.

DESIGN: A focused review of the literature was performed on PubMed with search terms including "migraine," "onabotulinumtoxinA for chronic migraine treatment," "pathophysiology of migraine," "anatomy of the corrugator muscle," and "history" with date ranges to only include recent peer-reviewed literature published after 2000 to evaluate the historical origins, anatomical features, and clinical importance of the corrugator supercilii muscle in migraine management.

RESULTS: Current evidence suggests that onabotulinumtoxinA is an effective treatment of chronic migraine that exerts its therapeutic effects through cleavage of synaptosomal-associated protein 25 (SNAP-25), preventing vesicular fusion and resulting in inhibition of neuropeptide release and receptor expression, which reduces peripheral and central sensitization. Accurate understanding of the corrugator supercilii anatomy is essential for optimizing treatment outcomes and minimizing adverse effects such as ptosis.

CONCLUSION: The corrugator supercilii muscle has played a pivotal role in the evolution of migraine treatment. Its unique relationship with trigeminal sensory pathways provides important insights into migraine pathophysiology, treatment mechanisms, and future applications extending beyond headache medicine.

articles.title: Evaluating the Impact of Urine Reflex Testing on Antibiotic Prescribing for Urinary Tract Infections.
articles.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are among the most common indications for outpatient antibiotic prescribing. Despite clinical guidelines promoting appropriate antibiotic use, unnecessary urine cultures and treatment of asymptomatic bacteriuria continue to contribute to adverse drug reactions and antimicrobial resistance. To improve diagnostic stewardship, Kaiser Permanente Southern California (KPSC) region implemented urinalysis (UA) with reflex to microscopy and urine culture (UC), in which microscopy and culture are automatically performed when predefined UA parameters are positive. This strategy aims to improve diagnostic accuracy and reduce inappropriate antibiotic use.

METHODS: This retrospective, pre- and post-implementation observational study evaluated the impact of urine reflex testing on outpatient antibiotic prescribing for suspected UTI across KPSC. Patients were included if they were KPSC members aged 2 years with either a UA or UC collected between July 1, 2021 and June 30, 2025. Patients who were pregnant, immunocompromised, had an indwelling catheter, or were hospitalized were excluded.

RESULTS: Over 3.7 million outpatient encounters were analyzed. Overall antibiotic prescribing within 7 days remained similar (23.2% vs. 23.4%; p<0.0001). However, prescribing was more aligned with culture results, with decreased antibiotic use following negative cultures (25.0% to 23.3%; p<0.0001) and increased use following positive cultures (75.9% to 77.6%; p<0.0001). Antibiotic switched within 7 days of index encounter increased (9.1% to 10.4%; p<0.0001). Diagnostic testing patterns shifted with UA, stand-alone UC, and positive UC decreased, while urine reflex testing increased.

CONCLUSION: Implementation of UA with reflex testing standardized diagnostic workflows and improved alignment of antibiotic prescribing with microbiologic findings.

articles.title: 17q11.2 Duplication (includes NF1 gene): A Scoping Review.
articles.journal: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Several neurodevelopmental disorder (NDD)-associated copy-number variants (CNVs) show reciprocal dosage effects, where deletions and duplications produce mirroring phenotypes. While NF1 microdeletion syndrome is well-characterized, the reciprocal NF1 microduplication remains poorly defined. This scoping review assesses whether NF1 microduplications constitute a recognizable syndrome with reciprocal features to NF1 microdeletion syndrome.

METHODS: We conducted a scoping review following reporting guidelines, extracting clinical and molecular data from publications reporting individuals with 17q11.2 microduplications involving NF1. We queried DECIPHER using identical criteria and applied Bayesian statistics to recalculate NDD penetrance estimates.

RESULTS: Across 14 studies, 37 individuals were identified. Among those with duplications reciprocal to type 1 or 2 NF1 microdeletions, NDD/neurobehavioral disorders were observed in 85%, including developmental delay (85%), intellectual disability or learning difficulties (57%), and autism spectrum disorder (29%). Growth abnormalities more commonly mirrored the deletion phenotype, with short stature (35%) and microcephaly (29%). Penetrance estimates for NDDs (25-40%) were markedly lower than recently reported (74%).

CONCLUSION: NF1 microduplications confer NDD risk and show partially reciprocal but heterogeneous phenotypic features compared to NF1 microdeletion syndrome, without defining a distinct syndrome. They are best interpreted as moderate-penetrance neurodevelopmental-susceptibility CNVs. Population-based studies are needed to refine estimates and inform genetic counseling.

articles.title: Epigenetic Activation of ANGPTL4 Drives EBV-Negative Gastric Cancer via Neutrophil Recruitment and NET Release via Stabilizing ANXA5.
articles.abstract: EBV-positive (EBVaGC) and EBV-negative (EBVnGC) gastric cancers exhibit distinct clinical outcomes, prognostic features, and immune infiltration landscapes; however, the molecular mechanisms driving these subtype differences, as well as the subtype-specific epigenetic regulation and biological functions of ANGPTL4 within the immune microenvironment, remain unclear. Here, through integrated analysis of multi-omics data, we discovered that EBV infection induces marked hypermethylation at the ANGPTL4 promoter, leading to transcriptional silencing of ANGPTL4 in EBVaGC. Conversely, hypomethylation-mediated ANGPTL4 overexpression is clinically associated with poor prognosis and distant metastasis in EBVnGC. Mechanistically, the C-terminal secreted form (cANGPTL4) promotes GC progression by enhancing proliferation, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and neutrophil recruitment. Clinically, ANGPTL4 expression is positively correlated with neutrophil infiltration and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) levels in GC. Spatial transcriptomics and immunohistochemistry (IHC) analyses confirmed the spatial colocalization of ANGPTL4 with tumor-infiltrating neutrophils. cANGPTL4 mediates tumor-associated neutrophil (TAN) recruitment via the NF-κB/CXCL8 axis and directly binds and stabilizes neutrophil-derived ANXA5 to facilitate NET release, thereby driving GC progression. In conclusion, ANGPTL4 represents a potential intervention target for EBVnGC. Targeting ANGPTL4 may exert dual anti-tumor effects by directly suppressing GC proliferation, EMT, and metastasis, and by remodeling the immunosuppressive microenvironment via attenuating TANs infiltration and NET release.

articles.title: NSAID initiation and risk for gastrointestinal bleeding in patients receiving GLP-1 receptor agonists: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have been purported to increase risk for gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding. Our objective was to determine whether GLP-1 RAs are associated with increased risk for GI adverse events following the initiation of a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID).

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used national administrative data from the Veterans Health Administration to identify patients with type 2 diabetes who initiated an NSAID while concurrently receiving a GLP-1 RA or a comparator agent: a sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor (SGLT-2i) or a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor (DPP-4i). The primary outcome measure was the incidence of a GI bleed or ulcer within 12 months of NSAID initiation. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to compare risk for GI bleeding or ulcer between GLP-1 RA recipients and the comparator groups while adjusting for confounders. A sensitivity analysis was conducted using GI bleed as a secondary outcome.

RESULTS: A total of 13,433 patients received a GLP-1 RA, 24,480 received an SGLT-2i, and 30,968 received a DPP-4i. The primary outcome occurred in 0.9% (n = 117) of patients receiving a concurrent GLP-1 RA, 1.0% (n = 243) of those receiving an SGLT-2i, and 1.0% (n = 308) of those receiving a DPP-4i. In adjusted regression analyses, no difference in risk for GI bleeding or ulcer was observed between GLP-1 RAs and either comparator (SGLT-2i: hazard ratio [HR], 0.85; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.68-1.07; DPP-4i: HR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.66- 1.01). Similar nonsignificant results were observed for the secondary outcome.

CONCLUSION: We did not observe an increased risk for developing a GI bleed or ulcer within the year following NSAID initiation with concurrent GLP-1 RA therapy, relative to comparator agents.

articles.title: CKMT1 Counteracts VDAC1 Oligomerization-Induced Neuronal Pyroptosis Through Steric Hindrance in Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke is one of the leading causes of death and disability worldwide; yet effective therapeutic options remain limited. Cytosolic leakage of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is a critical driver of ischemic brain injury. Voltage-dependent anion channel 1 (VDAC1), embedded in the mitochondrial outer membrane, promotes mtDNA leakage through oligomerization. However, the regulatory mechanisms underlying VDAC1 oligomerization in ischemic stroke remain poorly understood. This study demonstrates that ischemic stroke promotes VDAC1 oligomerization, leading to mtDNA leakage, activating the absent in melanoma 2 (AIM2) inflammasome, and subsequent neuronal pyroptosis. Pharmacological inhibition of VDAC1 oligomerization using VBIT-4 effectively disrupts this cascade. Creatine kinase mitochondrial 1 (CKMT1) is identified as a novel endogenous inhibitor of VDAC1 oligomerization. CKMT1 inhibits VDAC1 oligomerization through a dual-region synergistic mechanism. Specifically, the N-terminal domain of CKMT1 (residues R75 and E121) forms a stable interface with the C-terminal domain of VDAC1 (residues R218 and E189), whereas the CKMT1 signal peptide (residues 1-39) sterically hinders VDAC1 dimerization, thereby blocking oligomerization. Moreover, neuronal overexpression of CKMT1 significantly attenuates neuronal apoptosis, whereas CKMT1 knockdown aggravates neuronal injury. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that CKMT1 protects against cerebral ischemic injury by suppressing the VDAC1-mtDNA-AIM2 axis and identify CKMT1 as a novel therapeutic target for ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Molecular MRI Reveals Macrophage-Enriched Peritumoral Immune Remodeling After Incomplete Ablation in Liver Cancer.
articles.abstract: Incomplete image-guided ablation can promote local tumor progression by reshaping the residual tumor microenvironment toward immunosuppression, yet noninvasive biomarkers of this process remain limited. Here, a translational multiparametric PET/MRI strategy was developed to monitor macrophage-associated microenvironmental remodeling after incomplete microwave ablation (iMWA) in orthotopic VX2 liver tumors. Twenty-four tumor-bearing rabbits were assigned to untreated control, early post-iMWA (short-term), or late post-iMWA (long-term) groups and underwent clinical 3 T PET/MRI, including diffusion-weighted imaging, dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI, [1 8F]FDG PET, and T2-weighted MRI before and after administration of Eu-VSOP. Eu-VSOP-enhanced MRI revealed a hypointense peritumoral rim after iMWA, with the largest rim-to-liver signal decrease and rim thickness observed in the long-term group. Prussian blue staining and LA-ICP-ToF-MS demonstrated preferential iron and europium enrichment in macrophage-rich, CD206-associated peritumoral regions. Histology and proteomics further demonstrated increased CD206 and MMP-9 expression, extracellular matrix remodeling, immunosuppressive myeloid-associated changes, and metabolic reprogramming in viable residual tumors, accompanied by altered [1 8F]FDG uptake. Together, these findings indicate that incomplete ablation induces a temporally evolving, macrophage-rich immunosuppressive peritumoral niche and support the potential of Eu-VSOP-enhanced multiparametric PET/MRI for noninvasive monitoring of post-ablation microenvironmental remodeling.

articles.title: Comparing the Practice of Routine Postnatal Clinical Examination of Healthy Newborns in Norway, Denmark and Sweden: A Survey.
articles.abstract:
AIM: In many countries, all newborns undergo a routine clinical newborn examination before discharge. Key aim of this examination is to detect conditions for which early treatment may improve outcomes. This study aimed to describe variation in the timing, content, professional responsibility and follow-up arrangements for routine clinical newborn examination in Norway, Denmark and Sweden.

METHODS: April to September 2024, we distributed a survey to Norwegian paediatricians and to representatives of maternity and paediatric departments in Denmark and Sweden.

RESULTS: We analysed responses from 45 hospitals: Norway (N = 20), Denmark (N = 12) and Sweden (N = 13). In Norway and Sweden, a more comprehensive examination was generally performed by paediatricians within 72 h after birth. In Denmark, midwives typically performed a simplified examination within 12 h, with paediatric assessment when indicated. Examination content was broadly similar in Norway and Sweden but differed in Denmark. All participating hospitals reported routine pulse oximetry screening, but cardiac auscultation and follow-up of heart murmurs differed.

CONCLUSION: The organisation of routine clinical newborn examination differs across Scandinavia. These differences in care pathways may influence resource use and clinical decision making. Whether they translate into differences in neonatal morbidity or mortality remains unknown.

articles.title: Microenvironment-adaptive nanozyme biomaterials for diabetic wound regeneration: materials chemistry, catalytic networks and tissue-specific delivery.
articles.abstract: Diabetic wounds are sustained by a dynamically coupled microenvironment characterised by hyperglycaemia, oxidative stress, hypoxia, persistent infection and defective inflammatory resolution. Importantly, these abnormalities are not only therapeutic targets but also chemical boundary conditions that determine nanozyme catalysis by regulating substrate availability, electron transfer, active-site accessibility and mass transport. This review therefore moves beyond the conventional classification of nanozymes according to material type or nominal enzyme-like activity and establishes a structure-microenvironment-catalysis-delivery-regeneration framework for diabetic wound therapy. We critically analyse how metal valence, defect chemistry, coordination environments, heterointerfacial charge transfer, pore architecture and surface biointerfaces determine catalytic behaviour under wound-relevant conditions. Superoxide dismutase (SOD)-, catalase (CAT)-, peroxidase (POD)-, oxidase (OXD)- and glucose oxidase (GOx)-like activities are interpreted as an interconnected reaction network involving substrate generation and competition, oxygen consumption and production, and stage-dependent changes in the balance between antibacterial oxidation and regenerative redox regulation. Delivery matrices are considered integral components of the catalytic system because they regulate nanozyme retention, substrate transport and active-site exposure. Diabetes-associated oral wounds are further discussed as a tissue-specific stress test characterised by salivary clearance, polymicrobial biofilms, mechanical disturbance and coupled soft-hard tissue regeneration. Finally, priorities for wound-relevant catalytic benchmarking, mechanistic attribution, biosafety, manufacturing reproducibility and clinical translation are proposed.

articles.title: Predictive Nomogram for Reducing Urinary Tract Infection-Related Cancellations in Female Urodynamic Testing.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Same-day cancellation of office-based urodynamic testing, frequently due to urinary tract infections (UTIs), can introduce financial and strategical burdens for both the patient and the clinic.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and internally validate a clinical prediction model for urodynamic procedure cancellation due to suspected UTI.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients scheduled for urodynamic testing at a single academic urogynecology practice (August 1, 2022, to April 30, 2024). Data was collected via electronic medical record review. Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression with 10-fold cross-validation was used for variable selection. A clinical prediction nomogram and web-based calculator were developed for clinical implementation.

RESULTS: A total of 841 patients were included (mean age 63 ± 13.9 years; mean BMI 29.7 ± 6.7 kg/m2). UTI-related cancellation occurred in 57 (6.8%) patients. After LASSO selection, 5 predictors were retained: age, POP-Q stage, BMI, recurrent UTI history, and diabetes. The model demonstrated good apparent discrimination (C-statistic 0.759; sensitivity 75.4%, specificity 62.8%, NPV 97.4%) with a Brier score of 0.060. Full-process bootstrap validation revealed a calibration slope of 0.992. Decision curve analysis confirmed net clinical benefit across threshold probabilities of 2--40%.

CONCLUSIONS: Several variables predict suspected UTI-related urodynamic cancellation, the most significant of which is age. This nomogram and online calculator provide clinicians with practical tools for identifying patients at elevated risk of procedure cancellation, enabling targeted preprocedural intervention.

articles.title: Novel Metabolomic Signature as a Biomarker to Detect Subclinical Atherosclerosis in Individuals Traditionally Classified as Low Risk.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Standard modifiable risk factors such as age, hypertension, diabetes, cholesterol, and smoking contribute to coronary artery disease risk. However, up to 27% of first-time heart attacks occur in individuals without standard modifiable cardiovascular risk factors. As medical management can stabilize coronary atherosclerosis, there is a need for biomarkers to identify disease before symptoms or a heart attack.

METHODS: We performed targeted metabolomics, identifying 54 metabolites in 1212 adults undergoing coronary artery calcium score (CACS) from the BioHEART-CT Study. Individuals were classified as having clinically actionable CACS positive or not (clinically actionable CACS negative). Metabolite-to-metabolite ratios were then calculated to identify transferable biomarkers. Logistic regression models incorporating age, sex, and metabolite ratios were developed and classified as low risk by traditional scoring. The BioHEART Metabolite Risk Score (BioHEART-MRS) was derived from the best-performing model, trained in a Discovery cohort (n=635), adapted using transfer component analysis (n=266), and validated in an independent External cohort (n=311).

RESULT: A model including age, sex, and 5 metabolite ratios: histidine-kynurenic acid, histidine-riboflavin, citrullin-proline, kynurenic acid-phosphocholine, and arginine-dimethylguanidino valerate, referred to as BioHEART-MRS, demonstrated the best performance in younger individuals for predicting CACS. In the External cohort, BioHEART-MRS outperformed the traditional risk score (area under the curve=0.67 versus 0.55). The traditional risk score underperformed in the under-60 cohort, misclassifying 62% of those with clinically actionable CACS as low risk. Within this group, BioHEART-MRS identified 46 additional cases among low-risk individuals (n=495). As a triage tool, BioHEART-MRS reduced the number needed to scan to detect one true positive case to 7, compared with scanning all low-risk individuals.

CONCLUSIONS: In the External validation cohort, BioHEART-MRS showed greater discrimination than Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis risk score among traditionally low-risk individuals and enriched for clinically actionable CACS positive among those selected for imaging. These findings support prospective evaluation of metabolite-based triage for CACS, particularly in younger and SMuRFless individuals.

articles.title: Identification of small-molecule inhibitors of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD-ACE2 interaction by structure- and affinity-based screening.
articles.abstract: The receptor-binding domain (RBD) of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike protein mediates viral entry through its interaction with angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), making it an attractive target for antiviral intervention. However, the broad and relatively shallow ACE2-binding interface presents a challenge for small-molecule inhibitor discovery. In this study, we explored conserved regions outside the ACE2-binding interface as potential druggable sites for small-molecule inhibitors targeting the SARS-CoV-2 RBD. Structure-based virtual screening was performed using the structure of the SARS-CoV-1 RBD as a structural surrogate, and selected compounds were evaluated using a newly established affinity-based assay on diazirine-modified amorphous carbon plates. Evaluation of 175 virtual hits identified eight RBD-binding compounds. Among them, only RABI-1 inhibited RBD-ACE2 interaction in a Calu-3 cell-based binding assay without affecting ACE2 expression or cell viability. Evaluation of structural analogs of RABI-1 led to the identification of RABI-3, which showed stronger inhibitory activity compared with RABI-1. In addition, RABI-3 inhibited the interaction between ACE2 and RBDs derived from multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants in an AlphaLISA immunoassay and suppressed pseudovirus infection in Calu-3 cells. These findings support the feasibility of targeting regions of the RBD outside the ACE2-binding interface as a strategy for identifying small-molecule inhibitors of SARS-CoV-2 entry.

articles.title: In-Hospital Stroke in Patients with Cardiac Conditions: Do Cardiac Procedures Impact Stroke Outcomes?
articles.journal: The Canadian journal of neurological sciences. Le journal canadien des sciences neurologiques
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: It is unclear if stroke occurring after cardiac procedures is more severe than stroke associated with cardiac conditions without procedures. We compared in-hospital acute ischemic stroke patients admitted with a cardiac diagnosis who did versus did not undergo cardiac procedures.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, we analyzed adults with in-hospital stroke admitted with a primary cardiac diagnosis in Alberta (2018-2022). Patients were categorized into no prior cardiac procedure, cardiac procedure, or cardiac surgery within 30 days of stroke diagnosis. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess associations between exposure groups and outcomes.

RESULTS: Among 499 patients (median age 70 years IQR [62-77], 36.7% women), 116 (23.2%) underwent a cardiac procedure, and 227 (45.5%) underwent cardiac surgery prior to stroke diagnosis. Median time from procedure to stroke diagnosis was 1.75 days (IQR 0.87-3.83). In-hospital mortality was 34.6%, 24.1% and 22.5% in patients with no prior procedure, cardiac procedures and cardiac surgery, respectively. After adjustment for age, sex, facility level and comorbidities, no significant differences were observed in mortality (cardiac procedure vs no procedure: aOR 0.73, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.40-1.33; cardiac surgery vs no procedure: aOR 0.78, 95% CI 0.42-1.45). Among procedural patients, strokes recognized ≥2 days post-procedure were associated with higher mortality (2-7 days: OR 2.31, [1.18-4.52]; 8-30 days: OR 3.23, [1.59-6.59]).

CONCLUSIONS: Adjusted mortality did not differ by cardiac procedural status, although residual confounding is possible. Later stroke recognition after cardiac procedures was associated with higher mortality, identifying a high-risk monitoring window.

articles.title: Conditional Survival of Gallbladder Cancer After Curative-Intent Surgery: Impact of Disease Stage, Surgical Extent, and Adjuvant Therapy.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Gallbladder cancer is a rare but aggressive malignancy with poor prognosis even after curative-intent surgery. Conventional survival estimates provide fixed probabilities from diagnosis and fail to reflect the evolving prognosis of patients who have already survived several years. Conditional survival (CS) offers time-updated prognostic information, but evidence in gallbladder cancer remains limited.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 641 patients who underwent curative-intent resection for gallbladder cancer at a tertiary referral center (2005-2019). Five-year conditional overall survival (COS) and conditional recurrence-free survival were estimated up to 5 years postoperatively. Analyses were stratified by age, stage, comorbidity, surgical extent, and adjuvant therapy.

RESULTS: Baseline 5-year COS was 69.4% and increased to 74.0% among patients surviving 5 years. Stage III patients showed the largest improvement (45.9%-69.4%), whereas Stage I patients remained stable. In Stage II-III disease, extended cholecystectomy was associated with improved COS (63.2%-74.3%), while simple cholecystectomy showed a decline (65.7%-48.0%). Adjuvant therapy was associated with greater COS improvement (50.4%-69.2%) than no adjuvant therapy. Older patients (≥ 70 years) and those with diabetes showed poorer outcomes.

CONCLUSION: CS provides a dynamic framework for prognostication in gallbladder cancer and may support risk-stratified follow-up.

articles.title: Prevalence and Risk Factors for Dental Anxiety and Dental Fear in Nigeria: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: In Nigeria, the burden of dental anxiety and dental fear (DFA) remains poorly characterized despite its possible contribution to poor dental service utilization and treatment avoidance. This study aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence of dental anxiety in Nigerian populations and identify associated risk factors.

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis was registered in PROSPERO: (CRD420261373453). A search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, EBSCOhost, and African Journals Online from inception to March 2026. Studies were included if they were cross-sectional, cohort, or case-control studies conducted in Nigerian populations of any age that reported prevalence estimates of DFA using validated instruments. Two independent reviewers extracted data and assessed the risk of bias using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklists. The primary outcome was the pooled prevalence of dental anxiety, calculated using random-effects meta-analysis with the Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation. The associations between DFA and age, sex, and educational levels were also determined. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 statistics.

RESULTS: Of 237 records identified, 30 studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising 7920 participants. The pooled prevalence of DFA was 61% (95% CI: 41%-79%; I2 = 97%). Severe to extreme DFA prevalence was 18% (95% CI: 12%-27%). The pooled mean dental anxiety score was 11.9 (95% CI: 10.6-13.2). Females had higher DFA scores than males (mean difference 1.3, p = 0.0003) although the certainty of evidence was low. Participants under 30 years had higher scores than those 30 years and older (mean difference 1.6, p = 0.0002). Education level showed no significant association. Most studies (86.7%) had a moderate risk of bias. No publication bias was detected.

CONCLUSION: Dental anxiety and dental fear affect approximately three-quarters of the Nigerian population, with a possible higher burden among females and younger adults. These findings highlight the possible value of routine anxiety screening and integration of behavioural management into Nigerian dental practice.

articles.title: Studying multiple health behaviours in older adults using a measurement burst design: protocol, feasibility, compliance, behavioural patterns and lessons learned.
articles.abstract: Overweight and obesity are major public health challenges, requiring preventive efforts targeting diet, physical activity (PA), sedentary behaviour (SB) and sleep. Current research often treats these behaviours in isolation, ignores daily fluctuations and focuses on between-person differences. Studies examining the temporal covariance of these behaviours, assessing within-day and day-to-day variations in determinants and exploring how these time-varying determinants predict within-person variability in behaviours are needed. This paper aims to evaluate the feasibility of a measurement burst design with repeated intensive longitudinal assessments and to present patterns of behaviours and determinants. A 12-month observational study with a measurement burst design was conducted (January-December 2025). In total, 130 participants aged 55-75 years enrolled in the study, which consisted of four 7-day measurement bursts. Data collection included monitoring of diet, PA, SB, sleep and time-based ecological momentary assessment (EMA). Compliance rates, descriptive statistics per burst and across bursts were computed. 116 participants completed all bursts (retention rate = 89·2 %). Compliance rates ranged from 83·5 % for time-based EMA to 91·8 % for SB, supporting feasibility of the protocol. Mean values of 1692 kcal/day (sd = 565) for energy intake, 9·4 h/day (sd = 2·4) for sedentary time and 10 610 steps/day (sd = 6302) were observed. Mean daily light, moderate and vigorous PA-levels were 102·9 (sd = 37·4), 65·5 (sd = 43·4) and 11·5 (sd = 17·0) minutes, respectively. Mean sleep duration was 6·4 h/night (sd = 1·3), with a mean sleep efficiency of 79·2 % (sd = 10·2). This paper demonstrated the feasibility of integrating multiple assessment methods within a measurement burst design for studying health behaviours in adults aged 55-75 years and highlighted the value of analyses at more fine-grained temporal and individual levels.

articles.title: Co-infection with another species suppresses both cercarial quantity and quality in a trematode.
PDCD10-STK24/25 signaling is a gatekeeper of tubular cell homeostasis and protects against chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract: Inherited tubulopathies or injured kidney tubules can initiate inflammatory signaling and drive the progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD) and kidney failure. The early molecular triggers connecting tubular dysfunction to sustained renal inflammation remain poorly defined. Here, we show that deleting Pdcd10, specifically in distal nephron epithelial cells of mice, causes a rapid intrinsic injury response that precipitates chronic renal damage. Pdcd10-deficient kidneys exhibit an immediate and robust upregulation of tubular injury-response genes, followed by inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive tubulointerstitial damage leading to kidney failure and early mortality. Among the earliest and most strongly induced genes is Lcn2, a known injury marker, whose expression increases significantly in Pdcd10-deficient kidneys. Concurrent deletion of Lcn2 in the same renal epithelial cells further exacerbates renal injury and shortens survival. Pdcd10 deficiency in distal nephrons also upregulates multiple complement pathway genes and promotes accumulation of complement complexes in glomeruli. Finally, in line with PCDC10's known interaction with GCKIII subfamily of sterile-20 like kinases, the combined deletion of Stk24 and Stk25 in distal tubules phenocopies Pdcd10 knockout phenotype, albeit with later onset. Our results demonstrate that PDCD10-STK24/25 signaling is essential for maintaining renal epithelial cell homeostasis. Additionally, our findings reveal that early tubular Lcn2 induction serves as a protective response that helps limit CKD progression following epithelial injury.

articles.title: Media Literacy in Pediatric Neurology: Preventing the Medicalization of Anime Memes.
Next-generation control strategies for lower-extremity exoskeletons: State-of-the-art, limitations, and future directions.
articles.journal: PM & R : the journal of injury, function, and rehabilitation
articles.abstract: Wearable powered exoskeletons are emerging rehabilitation tools for restoring gait in individuals with neurologic or motor impairments, including stroke, spinal cord injury, myopathy, and cerebral palsy. Lower-extremity exoskeleton-assisted walking can improve motor function, gait parameters, balance, and independence. Exoskeleton use has also been associated with secondary health benefits, including reduced spasticity and improvements in autonomic functions such as bladder and bowel control. However, despite these clinical benefits, exoskeleton control systems remain a central bottleneck limiting functional gains and widespread clinical adoption. The majority of clinically approved lower-extremity devices rely on weight shift triggers, predefined gait phase controllers, impedance-based assistance, or simple electromyographic signal activation. These approaches often feel unintuitive and require substantial user training. As a result, persistent challenges remain in detecting user intent, reproducing a user's expected dynamic behaviors, adapting to variable gait patterns and changing environmental conditions such as uneven terrain or inclines, and minimizing cognitive burden during everyday use. This review focuses on control strategies for lower-extremity exoskeletons used in gait rehabilitation and restoration of motor function. It summarizes current approaches in commercial and research systems and outlines why existing methods remain insufficient for seamless, user-driven assistance. We also examine emerging approaches for determining user intent, including brain-computer interfaces, peripheral nerve interfaces, novel biosignals such as ultrasound and mechanomyography, and regenerative surgical approaches. Together, these advances may help bridge the gap between human intent and robotic assistance, enabling more natural and autonomous mobility.

articles.title: Indian Society of Organ Transplantation Consensus Recommendations on Latent Tuberculosis in Kidney Transplantation.
articles.journal: Transplant infectious disease : an official journal of the Transplantation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis remains a principal cause of morbidity and mortality after kidney transplantation across South and Southeast Asia, where tuberculosis infection is prevalent. India carries one-quarter of the global tuberculosis burden, yet transplant-specific guidance for high-burden settings is scarce. The Indian Society of Organ Transplantation (ISOT) convened a multidisciplinary expert panel to formulate consensus recommendations for the management of tuberculosis infection in kidney transplantation.

METHODS: A multidisciplinary panel undertook a structured, evidence-informed consensus process, appraising MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, and national tuberculosis program documents. Statements were refined through successive revision rounds, panel discussion at the ISOT Mid-Term Conference (Bengaluru, May 2026), and confirmation by all authors, preceding executive committee endorsement. Each statement received an evidence level (1-5) and, where actionable, a recommendation strength.

RESULTS: The panel formulated 36 consensus statements across 11 domains. Routine pre-transplant screening for tuberculosis infection is endorsed, with exclusion of tuberculosis disease before treatment of tuberculosis infection. The interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA) is preferred, given confounding of the tuberculin skin test by bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccination; a Mycobacterium tuberculosis-specific antigen-based skin test (Cy-Tb) is an acceptable alternative where IGRA is unavailable or unaffordable. Isoniazid-based regimens are preferred, as rifampicin reduces calcineurin-inhibitor exposure; isoniazid resistance, hepatotoxicity, and hepatitis C co-infection warrant individualized therapy.
