CONCLUSION: This first India-specific, society-endorsed position statement provides context-adapted recommendations for the management of tuberculosis infection in kidney transplantation and may inform adaptation in other high-burden settings; prospective multicenter studies are needed.

articles.title: CD34+-selected stem cell boost for poor graft function after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a large cohort study focusing on haploidentical transplantation.
articles.abstract: Poor graft function (PGF) is a life-threatening complication after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT). CD34+-selected stem cell boost has shown promise; however, data in the haploidentical setting and after failure of thrombopoietin receptor agonists (TPO-RAs) are limited. Patients who received purified CD34+ boost for refractory PGF after HSCT at two centers were retrospectively analyzed. Outcomes included overall response rate (ORR), graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) and overall survival (OS). Among the 116 evaluable patients, 86.79% (103/116) received haploidentical transplants and 113 (97.4%) had received at least one platelet-stimulating agent, including TPO-RA and/or recombinant human thrombopoietin (rhTPO). The ORR was 67.24% (CR 62.93%, PR 4.31%). The 180-day cumulative recovery rates of neutrophils, hemoglobin, and platelets were 56.7%, 57.1%, and 65.7%, respectively. Active infection at the time of CD34+-selected stem cell boost was the sole independent predictor of lower ORR (OR = 3.786, 95% CI: 1.584-9.048, P = 0.003). The incidence of grade III-IV acute GVHD was 9.48%, and that of moderate-to-severe chronic GVHD was 11.21%. The OS was 64.66%. Responders had a significantly better OS than nonresponders (81.65% vs. 11.67%, P < 0.001). In conclusion, CD34+-selected stem cell boost is safe and highly effective for refractory PGF after allo-HSCT, including in haploidentical recipients and those who have failed TPO-RAs. Active infection at infusion predicts a poor treatment response, and non-responders have a dismal prognosis, underscoring the need for alternative strategies.

articles.title: Successful eradication of Candida auris in a tertiary care ICU following a nearly 30 month outbreak: a drastic "Unit reset" protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Candida auris is a globally emerging, multidrug-resistant pathogen characterized by extreme environmental persistence and resistance to standard hospital disinfectants. Our ICU faced an endemic outbreak that lasted for 30 months, which was resistant to standard infection prevention and control (IPC) bundles.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy of a radical, multi-sectoral "Unit Reset" protocol involving total operational decanting, mechanical disassembly, and inventory disposal after incremental IPC strategies were exhausted.

METHODS: We executed a 120-hour "Unit Reset" in February 2026. The intervention comprised: (1) transferring all patients to a temporary satellite site; (2) total disposal of all pharmaceutical and disposable inventories; (3) structural remediation; and (4) dual-team mechanical disinfection with 5,000 ppm hypochlorite supplemented by 18% automated hydrogen peroxide vapor (HPV).

RESULTS: Over the 30-month endemic period, C. auris acquisition rates escalated despite high compliance with standard IPC bundles. Environmental surveillance rounds identified persistent reservoirs on high-touch surfaces that the routine cleaning protocols missed. Following the 120-hour Unit Reset, the ICU was reopened to admissions. During the subsequent 16-week active surveillance window, zero new clinical acquisitions or screening-positive cases were detected, representing the first sustained interruption of transmission since August 2023.

CONCLUSIONS: When C. auris achieves deep environmental sequestration within deteriorated medical infrastructure or complex equipment housings, incremental "enhanced cleaning" protocols may fail due to biofilm shielding. A radical, coordinated institutional reset can terminate entrenched nosocomial transmission when standard IPC bundles reach their limits.

articles.title: A diagnostic stewardship initiative to improve diagnosis of norovirus and nitazoxanide utilization in patients with cancer.
articles.abstract: Patients and healthcare workers are at risk of norovirus infection. Nitazoxanide is often given, though data is lacking. Multiplex polymerase chain reaction platforms may yield false-positive results. A quality improvement initiative led to an 84.4% reduction in nitazoxanide utilization and substantial cost savings without compromising patient care or nosocomial infection.

articles.title: Trans-septal suturing versus intranasal splinting following septoplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: The Journal of laryngology and otology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare the efficacy and safety of trans-septal suturing versus intranasal splinting after septoplasty through a systematic review and meta-analysis, focusing on post-operative complications and patient-centred outcomes.

METHODS: Comparative studies directly evaluating both techniques were included. Pooled odds ratios and standardised mean differences with 95 per cent confidence intervals were calculated.

RESULTS: Seventeen studies involving 1502 patients were included. No significant differences were found in adhesion, crust formation, septal haematoma, septal perforation or post-operative bleeding. Trans-septal suturing significantly reduced post-operative pain (standardised mean differences, -1.09; 95 per cent confidence intervals, -1.68 to -0.49) and sleep disturbance (standardised mean differences, -0.32; 95 per cent confidence intervals, -0.60 to -0.05) but increased operative time (standardised mean differences, 0.65; 95 per cent confidence intervals, 0.19-1.10). Infection and epiphora tended to be less frequent with trans-septal suturing.

CONCLUSION: Both techniques provide comparable protection against major post-operative complications, but trans-septal suturing improves post-operative comfort at the cost of a modest increase in operative time.

articles.title: Impairment of ictal consciousness and psychosis in drug-resistant focal epilepsy: A retrospective clinical cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Psychoses of epilepsy (POE) affect up to 13% of patients with focal epilepsy. Whereas interictal risk factors are well documented, ictal correlates of POE remain poorly characterized. We hypothesized that an impairment of ictal consciousness on the Consciousness Seizure Scale (CSS), would be associated with POE. We assessed the association between ictal clinical features and POE compared to non-POE in adults with drug-resistant focal epilepsy.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a presurgical cohort of adults with drug-resistant focal epilepsy monitored by video-electroencephalography (EEG) or stereo-EEG. For each patient, all seizures with an examination allowing the completion of CSS score were included. POE were identified through standardized psychiatric interviews. Association between ictal features, primarily CSS score, and POE was tested using generalized estimating equations (GEE).

RESULTS: Among 232 included seizures (25 from POE group, 207 from non-POE group), the probability of POE varied nonlinearly with ictal consciousness; it peaked at intermediate CSS scores (GEE, OR = 4.31, p = .006). This effect remained after adjustment for duration of both epilepsy (OR=1.06, p = .005) and seizure (OR=1.20, p = .013). Intraclass correlation of CSS was .76 (95%CI, .65-.85), reflecting a low within-patient variance. An older age, more severe depressive and anxiety symptoms were also associated with POE.

SIGNIFICANCE: POE were associated with intermediate impairment of ictal consciousness, suggesting that partial disruption of awareness may favor the emergence of psychotic symptoms. The high level of intrapatient stability for CSS, mostly estimated from non-POE, suggests that CSS could be constant across seizures. This raises the possibility that POE risk could stem from the way consciousness is altered during seizures.

articles.title: Longitudinal serum and CSF cytokine dynamics in NORSE: Associations with immunotherapy exposure.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize serum and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytokine dynamics according to immunotherapy exposure in cryptogenic new-onset refractory status epilepticus (cNORSE).

METHODS: We analyzed cytokine profiles in 94 serum and 42 CSF samples from 29 and 14 patients, respectively, with cNORSE. Nine contributed both sample types, resulting in 34 patients. Samples were categorized according to immunotherapy exposure as no immunotherapy (NT), first-line (FL), and second-line (SL), and stratified by innate- or adaptive-directed therapies. SL represented cumulative exposure, as all SL samples followed initiation of both FL and SL therapies. Linear mixed-effects models accounted for repeated measures and time from cNORSE onset. A systematic literature review included 27 studies and 63 patients.

RESULTS: Serum cytokine levels were generally lower during FL (n = 24) than NT (n = 9), whereas most cytokines were higher during SL (n = 61) than FL. CXCL8 (C-X-C motif ligand 8)/IL-8 and CCL2 (C-C motif chemokine ligand 2) were higher during SL than FL, with CCL2 remaining significant after multiple-testing correction. No serum differences remained significant when analyses were restricted to samples collected 7-30 days after onset. CSF levels were generally lower during FL (n = 10) and SL (n = 25) than NT (n = 7). Innate-directed therapies were associated with higher serum IL-6, CXCL8/IL-8, and CCL2 and CSF IL-4, whereas adaptive-directed therapies were associated with lower CSF MIP-1α (Macrophage Inflammatory Protein-1 alpha). The association with higher serum IL-6 was no longer observed after excluding tocilizumab-treated patients. No temporal association after SL initiation or status epilepticus resolution remained significant after multiple-testing correction. The literature review showed more frequent reductions in pro-inflammatory cytokines in CSF than serum following immunotherapy initiation.

SIGNIFICANCE: Cytokine profiles in cNORSE differ by treatment exposure and compartment. Persistent serum inflammation during SL may reflect disease severity, systemic inflammation, treatment effects, or their combination, whereas CSF showed more consistent reductions after immunotherapy exposure. These findings highlight the importance of treatment timing and compartment when interpreting cytokine measurements and support prospective studies integrating baseline immune phenotypes and standardized clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Beyond Early vs. Late: A Bayesian Evaluation of Tracheostomy Timing and Outcomes in Critical Illness.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The ideal timing of tracheostomy in critically ill patients remains controversial. Although early procedures may yield better outcomes, the specific contributions of each decision-making interval remain poorly defined. Here, we aimed to evaluate the associations of overall tracheostomy timing and component intervals with ventilator weaning, intensive care unit (ICU) discharge, mortality, and hospital costs.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, we included 480 patients admitted to the ICU who underwent tracheostomy between 2021 and 2023 at a single center. Patients were classified by tracheostomy timing into early (< 7 days), standard (7-14 days), and late (> 14 days) groups. Timing was also evaluated as a continuous variable and divided into 3 clinical intervals: from intubation to suggestion, suggestion to consultation, and consultation to the procedure. Ventilator weaning and ICU discharge were modeled using a Bayesian competing-risk survival approach. Mortality and medical expenditures were assessed using Bayesian logistic regression and Bayesian Gaussian regression, respectively. Propensity score matching was applied in the sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: Late tracheostomy was associated with lower probabilities of ventilator weaning and ICU discharge and with higher medical costs. Early tracheostomy was associated with the most favorable outcomes. Delays in the interval between intubation and tracheostomy were consistently associated with poor weaning outcomes. Mortality associations were less certain but suggested a potentially unfavorable pattern with delayed procedures. These findings remained consistent after matching.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients who ultimately underwent tracheostomy, timing < 7 days was associated with the most favorable observed outcomes, whereas the 7-14-day group generally showed intermediate results. These associations should not be interpreted as evidence that an early-tracheostomy strategy is optimal for all patients.

articles.title: Outcomes Following Extreme Elective Nodal De-Escalation in HNSCC Treated With Curative Intent: A Community Program Experience.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE/OBJECTIVE(S): To evaluate elective nodal recurrence rates in HNSCC patients treated with extreme dose de-escalation to 30 or 40 Gy followed by a sequential boost to gross disease or high-risk sites.

MATERIALS/METHODS: Between May 2017 and May 2025, patients diagnosed with SCC of the oropharynx, larynx, or hypopharynx were treated with definitive chemoradiotherapy or surgery followed by adjuvant (chemo)radiotherapy. Elective nodal volumes (ENV) defined as any uninvolved adjacent, distant ipsilateral or contralateral anatomic nodal level were treated to either 30 or 40 Gy, followed by a sequential boost to the PTVp/PTVn+ or high-risk surgical bed (PTVp+ PTVn+). A subset of 6 patients received 24-36 Gy (1.5-1.8 Gy BID) based on the Mayo-DART regimen. Assignment to 40 Gy versus 30 Gy reflected the radiation oncologist preference based on emerging trial evidence. All cases were reviewed prospectively in a head and neck multidisciplinary conference, and treatment planning required diagnostic FDG PET-CT fused to the planning CT. Concurrent systemic therapy was administered in 99% of patients. The primary endpoint was regional failure rate within the de-escalated ENV. Secondary endpoints included 1- and 2-year locoregional control (LRC), progression-free survival (PFS), distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS), and failure patterns.

RESULTS: The analysis included 102 patients of whom the majority 81.4% received definitive chemoradiotherapy, 17.6% underwent surgery with adjuvant chemoradiotherapy, and 1% received surgery with adjuvant radiation alone. The elective nodal volume was treated to 40 Gy at 2 Gy per fraction in 81 patients and to 30 Gy at 2 Gy per fraction in 15 patients; the remaining 6 adjuvant patients received 24-36 Gy at 1.5-1.8 Gy twice daily per the Mayo-DART regimen. With a median follow-up of 26.4 months, no elective nodal failures were observed in either dose cohort. The 1- and 2-year LRC rates were 93.5%. The 1- and 2-year progression-free survival (PFS) rates were 88.6% and 87.3%, respectively, while distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) rates were 95.0% and 95.0%, respectively. In total, 13 recurrences were recorded comprising 7 locoregional and 6 distant failures.

CONCLUSION: This represents the largest report demonstrating the efficacy of extreme dose de-escalation to ENV's for HNSCC within an NCI designated community cancer program. Reduced doses to the ENV ranging from 40 Gy to as low as 30 Gy were associated with exceptionally low failure rates regardless of treatment approach, stage, or HPV, and validate similar findings previously reported from larger academic centers. Importantly, 99% of patients received concurrent systemic therapy, and these results should not be extrapolated to radiotherapy alone.

articles.title: Relative dispersion and eddy diffusivity in laboratory experiments of β-plane turbulence.
articles.journal: Philosophical transactions. Series A, Mathematical, physical, and engineering sciences
articles.abstract: We present the first experimental measures of relative dispersion and turbulent diffusion in rapidly rotating turbulence in the zonostrophic regime, i.e. in the presence of instantaneous and dominant zonal jets. Synthetic Lagrangian trajectories are computed from time-resolved experimental velocity fields, from which we measure relative (two-particle) dispersion. Time-based and separation-based statistics are calculated, including the cumulative inverse separation time (CIST), for which analytical predictions exist in the inertial ranges (direct enstrophy cascade and inverse energy cascade) and in the diffusive regime. These statistics show evidence of a transition from a Richardson regime at scales larger than the energy-injection scale, to a diffusive regime, at scales larger than the transitional scale, the scale at which turbulence becomes anisotropic owing to the interaction between turbulent eddies and Rossby waves. The analytical predictions for the CIST allow us to measure the turbulent energy dissipation rate in the Richardson regime and the turbulent diffusivity in the diffusive regime. Our measurements of diffusivity are broadly consistent with predictions from mixing length and zonostrophic theories but suggest a shallower dependence on the energy dissipation rate. This article is part of the theme issue 'Anti-diffusive transport and layering: from sub-cellular to astrophysical scales'.

articles.title: Implementation of the seizure code in a tertiary hospital: Effects on emergency care times and clinical outcomes in severe seizures.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the impact of implementing the Seizure Code (SC), a structured multidisciplinary emergency protocol for severe seizures, on care times and clinical outcomes at a tertiary hospital.

METHODS: Single-center, retrospective observational study including episodes of severe seizures in patients aged 18 years or older managed between January 2023 and December 2024, comparing pre-SC and post-SC periods. The primary outcome was time from seizure onset to administration of the first anti-seizure medication (ASM). Secondary outcomes included other care intervals, process indicators, and clinical outcomes. Care intervals were analyzed with accelerated failure time models (percentage change in median time), length of stay in a competing-risks framework, and binary outcomes with Firth-penalized logistic regression (odds ratios, OR), all adjusted for prespecified covariates and clustered by patient.

RESULTS: Of 1959 episodes identified, 378 (175 pre-SC, 203 post-SC) met SC activation criteria. Time to the first ASM, the primary outcome, did not differ significantly (27% shorter, 95% CI -15% to 53% for benzodiazepines; 27%, -6% to 50% for others). Time to urgent video-EEG (VEEG) was 48% shorter (29%-61%) and the neurological assessment-VEEG interval 63% shorter (31%-80%). Pre-notification by Emergency Medical Services increased (22.9% vs. 37.8%; p = 0.003). Hospital stay (7.48 vs. 5.08 days; subdistribution hazard ratio for discharge alive 1.36, 1.02-1.89) and intensive care unit stay (3.20 vs. 1.48 days) were shorter. Thirty-day seizure recurrence was lower (8.0% vs. 3.0%; adjusted OR 0.33, 0.12-0.84). Mortality and functional status at discharge did not differ.

SIGNIFICANCE: The primary outcome, time to first anti-seizure medication, was not significantly shorter after implementation of the structured emergency protocol. The observed benefits were concentrated in secondary process and resource-utilization indicators: implementation of the Seizure Code was associated with faster access to urgent VEEG, shorter hospital and intensive care unit stays, and lower 30-day seizure recurrence, without a significant effect on mortality. These findings support protocolized emergency pathways in severe seizures.

PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Severe seizures are emergencies in which fast, coordinated care matters. We compared how patients were treated at one hospital before and after a new protocol, the Seizure Code, was introduced. Afterwards, patients had urgent video-EEG (a recording of brain activity) sooner and spent fewer days in hospital and in the intensive care unit, and fewer had another seizure within 30 days. However, the time to the first anti-seizure medication did not change significantly, and deaths and disability at discharge were unchanged.

articles.title: Still Chasing the Curve: Updated Evidence on Vancomycin AUC vs Trough Monitoring and Its Impact on AKI. A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis, 2020-2025.
articles.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The objective is to determine whether contemporary evidence continues to support AUC-guided monitoring as a safer alternative to trough-guided monitoring in reducing acute kidney injury (AKI). This analysis builds on prior systematic reviews and meta-analyses by incorporating newly available clinical data published since the release of the 2020 American Society of Health-System Pharmacists (ASHP), Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA), the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Society (PIDS), and Society of Infectious Diseases Pharmacists (SIDP) consensus guidelines.

METHODS: This study evaluated vancomycin therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) strategies published between January 1, 2020, and July 28, 2025. The systematic reviews were conducted using PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, the Cochrane Library, Scopus, and Google Scholar databases. Controlled vocabulary (MeSH, Emtree) and keywords were combined to identify studies evaluating AUC-guided or trough-guided vancomycin monitoring with AKI as a reported outcome. Searches were limited to English-language human studies.

RESULTS: A total of 80 studies comprising 27,067 patients met the inclusion criteria. Thirty studies directly compared AUC-guided with trough-guided monitoring (n = 18,146) and demonstrated a significantly lower risk of AKI with Area under the Curve (AUC)-guided monitoring (pooled risk ratio [RR] 0.66; 95% CI 0.56-0.78; I2 = 64%), an approximately 34% relative reduction. A subgroup analyses restricted to KDIGO-defined studies, and the 2009 vancomycin consensus guideline definitions yielded a consistent estimate in favored of AUC-guided monitoring. No significant differences were observed between strategies for all-cause mortality (4 studies; n = 697; OR 0.83; 95% CI 0.48-1.44) or 30-day readmission (5 studies; n = 1,222; OR 0.95; 95% CI 0.79-1.14).

CONCLUSION: Contemporary evidence published since the 2020 ASHP/IDSA/PIDS and SIDP consensus guideline continues to support AUC-guided monitoring as a safer alternative to trough-guided monitoring, without a measurable trade-off in mortality or readmission. These findings reinforce AUC-guided Therapeutic Drug Monitoring (TDM) as the preferred default strategy for adult patients receiving intravenous vancomycin, while the observational and heterogeneous nature of the evidence underscores the ongoing need for prospective, high-quality trials.

articles.title: Phosphorylation Alters the Condensation State of the Potato Transcription Factor bZIP18 to Enhance Plant Immunity.
articles.abstract: Biomolecular condensates formed by transcription factors (TFs) via liquid-liquid phase separation enable precise spatiotemporal control of eukaryotic gene expression. Although phosphorylation is a well-established regulator of TF activity, its capacity to remodel condensate organization and transcriptional function in plant immunity remains largely undefined. Here, we report that pathogen-induced phosphorylation converts a pre-existing TF condensate into a dynamic transcriptional hub to enhance the immune response in potato. Upon infection by the oomycete pathogen Phytophthora infestans, the mitogen-activated protein kinase StMPK9 phosphorylates the TF StbZIP18 at the conserved residue threonine 337. This modification triggers rapid changes in the nuclear StbZIP18 condensates, transforming pre-existing condensates into numerous smaller assemblies. The phospho-null StbZIP18T337A mutant maintains its presence in low-activity condensates and compromises immunity, whereas the phospho-mimetic variant StbZIP18T337E constitutively forms active condensates and enhances resistance. The gene encoding the TF StMYB44 was identified as the direct downstream gene target of StbZIP18. TurboID-based proximity labeling revealed that both wild-type StbZIP18 and StbZIP18T337E, but not the phospho-null variant StbZIP18T337A, selectively interact with the transcriptional cofactor StMBF1c to form transcriptional activation hubs that drive defense gene expression, including StMYB44. Together, our findings establish that phosphorylation-directed condensate reprogramming operates as a tunable phase-separation switch, converting a low-activity assembly into a transcriptional amplifier. This study unveils a biophysical mechanism for signal amplification in plant immunity and provides insight into how post-translational modifications modulate transcriptional condensate function.

articles.title: Treatment-Response Evidence, Care-Pathway Gaps, and Guideline Discordance in Gastric MALT Lymphoma: An Umbrella Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Reviews of gastric mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma have quantified treatment response, but their coverage of the care pathway and relationship to guideline differences remain unclear.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through March 31, 2026. Eligible reviews were mapped to 13 clinical questions as direct, partial, or absent coverage. Question-specific anchors were selected without pooling overlapping reviews. All 16 items of A MeaSurement Tool to Assess systematic Reviews, version 2 were examined; overall confidence was assigned to intervention reviews. European Gastro-Intestinal Lymphoma Study, European Society for Medical Oncology, National Comprehensive Cancer Network, and British Society for Haematology recommendations were compared descriptively.

RESULTS: Fifteen reviews were eligible; nine reviews answered seven questions. Complete remission was 75.2% after successful Helicobacter pylori eradication in H. pylori-positive disease. In H. pylori-negative disease, source-defined complete remission was 29.3%, including probable minimal residual disease. Remission was 22.2% in patients with t(11;18)/BIRC3::MALT1-positive disease versus 78.0% in patients with translocation-negative disease. The radiotherapy remission estimates were 97.3% after eradication failure and 96.0% in the limited-stage cohort. Gastric positron emission tomography (PET) detection was 62.0%, without evidence of management benefit. All eight intervention reviews had critically low confidence; seven nonintervention reviews received descriptive profiles. The guidelines differed for H. pylori-negative management, endoscopic ultrasonography, bone marrow biopsy, and PET/computed tomography. No eligible review compared the relevant treatment sequences or staging strategies.

CONCLUSIONS: Review-level evidence is concentrated on treatment response. It cannot establish superiority between treatment sequences or determine staging, escalation timing, surveillance, or relapse strategies. Guideline differences concern decisions for which the relevant comparisons remain unsynthesized.

articles.title: Spontaneous Colonic Migration of a Ventriculoperitoneal Shunt Catheter.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Silent and spontaneous colonic migration of a ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt is an extremely rare, life-threatening long-term complication, driven by chronic foreign-body erosion. It can precipitate severe retrograde central nervous system (CNS) infection insidiously, even in the complete absence of typical abdominal symptoms or peritonitis. CASE REPORT A 63-year-old man with a history of VP shunt placement presented 2.5 years after the procedure with fever, somnolence, and elevated inflammatory markers. Brain computed tomography (CT) and contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed progressive hydrocephalus and prominent peri-catheter cerebral edema. Subsequent abdominal CT demonstrated spontaneous distal shunt catheter perforation into the colon, with retrospective imaging ruling out iatrogenic injury. Although cerebrospinal fluid and blood cultures were negative, a diagnosis of retrograde CNS infection secondary to colonic perforation was clinically established based on direct anatomical continuity and localized neuroimaging abnormalities. The patient successfully underwent emergency shunt externalization and removal, external ventricular drainage placement, and broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy covering enteric flora, resulting in complete resolution of neurological symptoms without long-term sequelae. CONCLUSIONS Transmural colonic migration of a VP shunt is a critical late-onset complication that can present solely as a retrograde CNS infection without abdominal manifestations or positive cultures. High clinical vigilance for occult intra-abdominal shunt displacement, correlated neuroimaging and abdominal imaging, prompt surgical intervention, and targeted antimicrobial therapy are essential to prevent severe infectious morbidity and optimize neurological recovery.

articles.title: Efficiency of Rescue Paramedic Hoist versus Underslung Antenna in Helicopter-Based Avalanche Searches: A Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Survival for avalanche victims is time-dependent, and survival is often reliant on ground companion rescue. Due to the time-critical nature of burial, remote locations, and high frequency of concomitant severe trauma, helicopters are often dispatched to these incidents. While helicopter-based transceiver searches are standard, the most efficient deployment strategy, either using an underslung antenna or hoisting a rescue paramedic (RP) with a handheld transceiver, remains unknown. This study compared the operational efficiency of these two methods in the Norwegian Search-and-Rescue (SAR) Helicopter Service.

METHODS: A dual randomized, experimental field trial was conducted with the on-duty SAR helicopter and crew at the Ørland Main Airforce Base (Trøndelag, Norway). A simulated avalanche area of 80 × 150 meters was used, and six avalanche transceivers were buried at approximately 0.5m depth across the area. Only one transceiver was active at each run, and the locations were randomized to prevent crew memorization. The sequence of which procedure to use was also randomized. Four operational timestamps were recorded: First Signal, Optimal Signal, RP on Ground, and Transceiver Found.

RESULTS: Over three days, a total of 25 trial runs were performed, 13 with Antenna Search and 12 with RP Hoist Search. The RP Hoist Search was significantly faster in both time to Optimal Signal, with a difference between the groups of 29 seconds (95% CI, 9 - 50), and time for RP on Ground, with a difference between the groups of 124 seconds (95% CI, 98 - 151). For the total time to Transceiver Found, the difference between the groups was 143 seconds (95% CI, 113 - 172; P <0.001). Furthermore, the RP Hoist Search resulted in significantly faster fine search on the ground.

CONCLUSION: This randomized, experimental field trial comparing two currently used standard search procedures in the Norwegian SAR service showed that the RP Hoist Search was significantly more efficient than the Antenna Search for localizing buried avalanche victims, reducing total localization time by more than two minutes. Given that survival probability is reduced after 10-15 minutes of burial, this time saving may be clinically significant. The findings support that RP Hoist Search is an effective localization strategy for SAR helicopter services with comparable hoist systems.

articles.title: Long-term effects of a parenting program for advanced cancer: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study examines effects over time of a telephone-delivered 5-session manualized parenting education program for child-rearing parents with advanced cancer. Primary outcomes were parents' depressed mood and anxiety, parenting skills, parenting self-efficacy, and child behavioral-emotional adjustment.

METHODS: A total of 84 child-rearing parents diagnosed with advanced, non-curable cancer were recruited from community and comprehensive cancer centers and service providers serving cancer patients. After obtaining signed informed consent and baseline questionnaires, parents were randomized to an experimental treatment group or to an alternative treatment control group. Data (3, 6, and 9 months) were obtained after baseline. Linear Mixed Models were used to compare baseline with 6- and 9-month follow-ups. Outcomes at 3 months were reported earlier.

RESULTS: Of the 84 parents initially randomized, 24 participants completed all data collection time periods. Mixed model analysis showed a significant change in parenting skills over all time periods that benefited the experimental group. There was also a significant improvement in parents' self-efficacy at 6 and 9 months, which benefited the control group.

SIGNIFICANCE OF RESULTS: This is the first known longitudinal study of child and parent-reported outcomes from a randomized controlled trial of a manualized cancer parenting program for parents with advanced cancer. All results should be viewed with caution given the small sample size and the loss of 71% of the participants from baseline to 9 months. Despite these limitations, Linear Mixed Models analysis showed clinically significant improvements in parenting skills over time compared to an alternative treatment control group.

articles.title: Autotaxin inhibition mitigates chronic kidney disease by reducing renal tubular lysosome-mitochondria stress and suppressing fibroblast activation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autotaxin (ATX) catalyzes lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) production and has been implicated in fibrotic diseases. However, its role in chronic kidney disease (CKD), particularly its spatial distribution and association with tubular injury, and its contribution to cellular remodeling remains unclear. This study investigated the therapeutic effects and potential mechanisms of autotaxin inhibition (ATXi) in experimental CKD.

METHODS: ATX expression and cell type-specific Enpp2 expression were evaluated in CKD mouse models induced by folic acid (FA) or an adenine diet. In a separate intervention study, FA-induced CKD mice were treated with ATXi or vehicle. Renal function, fibrosis, tubular injury, lipid accumulation, and mitochondrial and lysosomal alterations were assessed. In vitro, NRK-49F fibroblasts were treated with transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) with or without ATXi.

RESULTS: ATX expression was increased in CKD kidneys and was predominantly localized to the tubulointerstitium. ATXi treatment significantly attenuated blood urea nitrogen elevation and tended to reduce cystatin C levels, along with improving tubular injury and interstitial fibrosis, collagen deposition and alpha-smooth muscle actin expression. Renal lipid accumulation and increased LPA receptor mRNA expression observed in CKD were also reduced following ATXi treatment. In addition, ATXi ameliorated tubular mitochondrial structural damage and lysosomal stress. Furthermore, ATXi suppressed TGF-β-induced fibroblast activation and proliferation in vitro.

CONCLUSION: Pharmacologic inhibition of ATX attenuated CKD, accompanied by improvements in mitochondrial structural abnormalities, modulation of lysosome-associated responses, and suppression of fibroblast activation, thereby reducing tubular injury and renal fibrosis. These findings support a pathogenic role of the ATX-LPA axis in CKD and highlight ATXi as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: DNA methylation patterns at the IGF2-H19 locus in offspring and maternal folate intake: a systematic review.
articles.journal: Journal of developmental origins of health and disease
articles.abstract: Folate is a critical methyl-group donor in one-carbon metabolism, and maternal folate exposure during pregnancy has been proposed to influence DNA methylation at imprinted loci involved in fetal growth and developmental programming. This systematic review evaluated the association between maternal folate intake during pregnancy and DNA methylation at the IGF2-H19 locus in offspring tissues. PubMed, Embase, and Epistemonikos were systematically searched for human studies assessing folate or folic acid exposure during pregnancy and DNA methylation at IGF2 and/or H19 in pregnancy-related tissues. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-E for observational studies and the Cochrane RoB 2 tool for randomized controlled trials. Fifteen reports from nine countries met the eligibility criteria, including two randomized controlled trials, two cross-sectional studies, and eleven cohort studies. Findings were heterogeneous according to genomic region, tissue type, and exposure window. Folic acid supplementation showed the most consistent associations at the H19 imprinting control region, where inverse associations with methylation were reported in some cord blood analyses. Results for IGF2 DMR2 varied across studies, whereas associations involving blood folate biomarkers were generally weak and tissue-specific, and dietary folate intake was largely null. No observational study was judged at low overall risk of bias, and both randomized trials were assessed as having some concerns. Overall, maternal folic acid supplementation was associated with modest, region-specific differences in DNA methylation at the IGF2-H19 locus; however, methodological limitations and heterogeneity across studies preclude firm conclusions regarding the biological significance of these associations.

articles.title: The impact of attire on patient approval of staff in psychiatric services: a randomised survey experiment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Staff attire may influence patient perceptions of staff in healthcare settings. However, little is known about how this applies to psychiatric services. To address this gap, we examined whether different types of attire influence patient approval of staff in psychiatric settings.

METHODS: Adult patients receiving treatment in the Psychiatric Services of the Central Denmark Region were invited to participate in an electronic survey. Respondents were randomly allocated to one of five groups shown photographs of a: I. Doctor wearing personal clothes, II. Doctor wearing white coat over personal clothes, III. Doctor wearing white coat over scrubs, IV. Nurse wearing personal clothes, or V. Nurse wearing scrubs. Each participant answered seven 'approval' question items on a Likert-like scale (range 0-10) covering competence, credibility, empathy, trustworthiness, willingness to follow recommendations, willingness to approach the staff member and perceived professionalism. Composite approval scores were compared across the doctor and nurse groups, respectively, using pairwise t-tests.

RESULTS: Of the 9310 eligible patients, 1431 (15.4% response rate) completed the full questionnaire. Mean composite approval scores (range 0-70) were highly similar and did not differ statistically significantly across the doctor groups (I. 52 ± 14, II. 53 ± 14 and III. 52 ± 14, respectively; all p ≥ 0.244), nor between the nurse groups (IV. 52 ± 14 and V. 52 ± 15, respectively; p = 0.826).

CONCLUSIONS: In this randomised survey experiment, approval ratings were highly similar across psychiatric staff attire. Given this apparent parity, and the advantages in terms of hygiene and correct identification of staff, we believe that more consistent use of uniforms should be considered.

articles.title: Utilizing a Substitute Pulmonary Artery Pressure Sensor System due to Unreliable Pulmonary Artery Pressure Readings.
Distinguishing Patients with Previous Helicobacter pylori Infection from Those Never Infected Using Logistic Regression and a Neural Network.
articles.abstract: Objective　Accurate assessment of Helicobacter pylori infection status is important for gastric cancer screening. Although current infection can be reliably detected using the stool antigen test (SAT) or urea breath test, distinguishing previously infected individuals from those who have never been infected using noninvasive serological markers remains challenging. This study evaluated the performance of logistic regression (LR) and a neural network (NN) in distinguishing between these two groups.Methods　Data from 1,872 participants (1,101 never infected, 39 currently infected, and 732 previously infected) were analyzed. The infection status was determined based on the eradication history, endoscopic findings, and SAT results. For the primary analysis, participants who were currently infected were excluded. Birth year, sex, serum H. pylori antibody level, pepsinogen (PG) I, PG II, and PG I/II ratio were used as the predictors. The classification performance was evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation.Results　The LR and NN models showed numerically similar performance, with area under the curve values of 0.85±0.02 and 0.88±0.01 (mean ± standard deviation), respectively. At a probability cutoff of 0.5, the recall for previously infected individuals was 66.8% ±3.6% for LR and 70.7% ±5.0% for NN. Lowering the cutoff to 0.4 improved the recall. At this cutoff, the recall for never-infected and previously infected individuals was 79.6% ±3.7% and 74.5% ±1.8% for LR, and 82.1% ±3.2% and 76.7% ±4.0% for NN, respectively.Conclusion　NN and LR models using noninvasive clinical data showed numerically similar performance in distinguishing previously infected from never-infected individuals.

articles.title: Composite Hemangioendothelioma with Concurrent Pyoderma Gangrenosum Treated with Pazopanib: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: A 40-year-old man with an eight-year history of a cutaneous mass complicated by subsequent pyoderma gangrenosum developed systemic disease. Pleural fluid cytology initially suggested pleural mesothelioma (PM), whereas a subsequent subcutaneous biopsy was interpreted as epithelioid hemangioendothelioma (EHE). Through a retrospective re-evaluation of previous skin specimens and comparison with current pathological findings, a final diagnosis of composite hemangioendothelioma (CHE) was established. Pazopanib (PAZ) achieved radiologically stable disease for five months; however, he died of progressive respiratory failure. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of extremely rare CHE and suggests that PAZ may have a limited therapeutic impact on advanced CHE with malignant pleural effusions.

articles.title: Does the direct anterior learning curve persist after fellowship training? A single-center comparative cohort study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The direct anterior approach (DAA) for total hip arthroplasty (THA) has historically been associated with a learning curve affecting both operative efficiency and early complications. Whether contemporary adult-reconstruction fellowship training modifies that curve is not established. We compared 90-day complication rates and operative times between newly graduated fellowship-trained DAA surgeons and one experienced DAA surgeon at a single high-volume center.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 600 primary THAs performed via a DAA from a single institution between November 2019 and February 2025 with a minimum of 90-day follow-up. Intra- and post-operative complications were compared between the following two groups: the first 100 cases of each of three junior fellowship-trained arthroplasty surgeons ("Junior") and the most recent 300 cases of a senior fellowship-trained arthroplasty surgeon ("Senior"). The study was powered to detect a 5% absolute difference in overall complication rates. Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) were analyzed as exploratory secondary endpoints.

RESULTS: Operative complications were infrequent in both cohorts, with a numerically higher rate in the Junior group that did not reach statistical significance (Junior 27 [9.0%] vs Senior 20 [6.7%]; absolute difference + 2.3%, 95% CI - 2.0% to + 6.6%, p = 0.362). No subgroup comparison reached statistical significance: DVT (1.0 vs 0.7%, p = 1.000), PE (0.3 vs 0.3%, p = 1.000), hematoma (0.3 vs 1.0%, p = 0.624), dislocation (1.3 vs 0.3%, p = 0.373), periprosthetic fracture (1.7 vs 1.0%, p = 0.725), neurapraxia (1.3 vs 2.0%, p = 0.752), prosthetic joint infection (1.0 vs 0.3%, p = 0.624), or wound complications (3.3 vs 2.0%, p = 0.448). All subgroup analyses were exploratory and underpowered for individually rare events. Medical events were infrequent and similar between groups (Junior 13 [4.3%] vs Senior 17 [5.7%], p = 0.575). Combining operative and medical complications, 40 events (13.3%) occurred in the Junior cohort and 37 (12.3%) in the Senior cohort (p = 0.807). Operative time was significantly longer among Junior surgeons (92.3 vs 68.5 min, p < 0.001). In exploratory analyses limited by 90-day PROM follow-up of 35% (Junior) and 48% (Senior), 90-day SF-12 and WOMAC scores were similar among respondents; given the incomplete follow-up, these descriptive findings are best regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than conclusive about functional recovery.

CONCLUSION: Within a single high-volume center using standardized ERAS pathways, three fellowship-trained surgeons performing their first 100 DAA THAs had significantly longer operative times than one experienced DAA surgeon, with no evidence of a large difference in 90-day complication rates. Because the study was powered only to detect a 5% absolute difference, it cannot exclude smaller or rare-event differences and does not establish equivalence. These data generate the hypothesis that contemporary fellowship training combined with protocolized perioperative care shifts the early DAA learning curve toward efficiency rather than safety; confirmation requires an adequately powered, multicenter study.

articles.title: Air pollution is associated with a distinct pathogen spectrum in community-acquired pneumonia: a prospective multicentre cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) is the leading cause of death due to infection worldwide, with its incidence and disease course influenced by air pollution exposure. Little is known about how air pollution influences microbiological findings in patients with CAP.

METHODS: Patients were recruited from a prospective, multicentre study of CAP (CAPNETZ). Air pollution data were collected at the city level considering data up to one month before inclusion. Associations with sputum pathogen detection and cell counts were tested using generalised linear mixed-effects logistic regression models adjusting for clinical confounders, centre-level heterogeneity and meteorological data. Internal validation was performed using an Ensemble Feature Selection (EFS) approach.

RESULTS: Among 4,446 eligible patients with available sputum samples, a potential pathogen was detected in 1,581 patients, while complete sputum-cell-count data were available for 4,014 patients. Detection of Streptococcus pneumoniae was associated with previous higher exposure to sulphur dioxide (SO2) (OR 1.75, p = 0.008) and carbon monoxide (CO) (OR 1.57, p = 0.02). Escherichia coli was more frequently detected in patients who were exposed to elevated levels of nitrogen dioxide (NO2) (OR 2.75, p = 0.004) and higher temperature (OR 1.51, p = 0.03), whereas increased fine particulate matter (PM2.5) exposure (OR 0.37, p = 0.001) was linked to reduced detection. Furthermore, SO2 exposure influenced the likelihood of obtaining a diagnostically relevant sputum culture and was associated with higher odds of detecting a high leucocyte count (OR 1.18, p = 0.02). Results were largely corroborated by EFS, particularly for S. pneumoniae and E. coli detection.

CONCLUSION: Exposure to air pollution was associated with a distinct pathogen spectrum in patients with CAP. These findings may have implications for the interpretation of microbiological data in an epidemiological and clinical context and highlight the importance of considering air pollution exposure as a confounding factor. Further validation in cohorts with high-quality environmental, microbiological and antimicrobial resistance data is needed.

STUDY REGISTRATION: Registry: German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS), DRKS-ID: DRKS00005274, Registration date: 2013-09-11.

articles.title: Metformin modulates alveolar bone parameters and gene expression in streptozotocin-induced type 2 diabetic rats.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is linked with defective bone healing and metabolic disturbances that increase fracture risk. Although metformin (MET) is used traditionally as first-line treatment for type 2 diabetes (T2DM), its effectiveness in completely reversing diabetic bone homeostasis is uncertain. The present study was conducted to assess the short-term effect of MET on alveolar bone histological structure and osteoblastic gene expression in rats with streptozotocin (STZ)-induced type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).

METHODS: Eighteen adult male Wistar rats were divided equally into three groups (n = 6/group): control group (non-diabetic) was injected with saline, STZ group (diabetic) received 10% fructose solution for 2 weeks followed by an injection of a single dose of STZ (40 mg/kg), and MET group (diabetic with MET-treatment) received 100 mg/kg/day MET for 30 days. Alveolar bone was assessed by histological and histomorphometric analysis, cone beam computed tomography (CBCT), and reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) analysis of bone-related gene expression.

RESULTS: The STZ group showed pronounced decreases in total bone area, osteoblast area, and bone-related gene expression (RunX2, osteocalcin, COL1A1) compared to the control group. MET significantly improved these parameters compared to the STZ group.

CONCLUSIONS: Metformin significantly increased total bone area and osteoblastic gene expression (Runx2, osteocalcin, and COL1A1) compared to untreated diabetic rats but did not fully restore them to control (non-diabetic) levels. These results suggest a partial protective effect of metformin in alveolar bone in this short-term T2DM rat model.

articles.title: Perioperative Outcomes of Bariatric Surgery Across Chronic Kidney Disease Stages: National Inpatient Sample Analysis 2016-2022.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bariatric surgery is increasingly performed in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), but perioperative outcomes across CKD severity remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated stage-specific perioperative outcomes after bariatric surgery in a contemporary national cohort.

METHODS: We analyzed 284,230 adult bariatric surgery hospitalizations from the National Inpatient Sample (2016-2022), stratified as no CKD, CKD stages 1-2, 3, 4, 5, and dialysis-dependent end-stage renal disease (ESRD). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included acute kidney injury, major bleeding, sepsis, acute respiratory failure, new dialysis, length of stay, and hospital charges. Survey-weighted multivariable regression (the primary models) evaluated associations between CKD stage and outcomes. A separate fully specified mortality model included CKD stage, age group, sex, diabetes, frailty, procedure type, and hospital volume.

RESULTS: CKD was documented in 3.4% of hospitalizations. Crude mortality was 0.3% without CKD, 2.0% in stage 3, 5.9% in stage 4, and 4.9% in dialysis-dependent ESRD. In the primary models, stage 4 CKD (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 3.85, 95% CI 2.58-5.75) and ESRD (aOR 7.34, 95% CI 5.33-10.12) were associated with greater mortality, whereas stages 1-3 were not significantly associated with mortality after adjustment. Advanced CKD was also associated with greater bleeding, sepsis, respiratory failure, and resource utilization. Stage 4 CKD was strongly associated with new dialysis (primary model aOR 16.47, 95% CI 9.19-29.51). Sleeve gastrectomy had lower crude event rates than Roux-en-Y gastric bypass across CKD strata, although the procedure-by-stage interaction for a composite adverse event was modest (P = 0.048).

CONCLUSION: Advanced CKD, particularly stage 4 disease and dialysis-dependent ESRD, was associated with substantially greater in-hospital risk after bariatric surgery. These findings support CKD-stage-specific risk assessment, multidisciplinary perioperative management, and individualized procedural planning. Observed differences between procedures should be interpreted cautiously given the potential for residual confounding.

articles.title: Comparative cardiovascular outcomes of IL-6 inhibitors versus rituximab in rheumatoid arthritis: a claims-based observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interleukin-6 receptor inhibitors (IL-6i), tocilizumab and sarilumab, are FDA-approved therapies for rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Beyond their efficacy in controlling systemic inflammation, growing evidence suggests that IL-6 inhibition may confer cardioprotective effects. This study investigates the long-term cardiovascular outcomes associated with IL-6i in RA patients, comparing IL-6 inhibitors with rituximab and evaluating differences between individual IL-6 inhibitor agents.

METHODS: We conducted an observational cohort study using the TriNetX Linked Network (2010-2025) including adults with RA initiating an IL-6 inhibitor or rituximab and ≥ 2 prescriptions for a drug of interest ≥ 6 months apart. Comparisons were as follows: (1) IL-6 inhibitors (sarilumab, tocilizumab) versus rituximab, and (2) tocilizumab versus sarilumab. Patients receiving both IL-6 inhibitors simultaneously or a non-FDA-approved IL-6 blocker (e.g., siltuximab) were excluded. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, heart failure (HF), and venous thromboembolism (VTE) over 5 years. We calculated propensity scores using demographics, cardiovascular risk factors, inflammatory markers, prior TNFi exposure, systemic glucocorticoid use, and conventional DMARDs, and used scores to match exposed individuals 1:1 with comparators. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for mortality and cardiovascular outcomes individually. All analyses were conducted using the TriNetX platform.

RESULTS: After matching, 4288 RA patients per group were included for IL-6i versus rituximab and 605 per group for sarilumab versus tocilizumab. Compared to rituximab, IL-6i was associated with lower hazards of mortality (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.55-0.82), MACE (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.64-0.85), and HF risk (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.69-0.94), with no significant difference in MI, stroke, or VTE. Amongst IL-6 inhibitors, sarilumab was associated with lower hazards of all-cause mortality compared to tocilizumab (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.29-0.94), but no significant differences were identified for other cardiovascular outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Among adults with RA, IL-6i use was associated with lower rates of all-cause mortality, MACE, and heart failure compared to rituximab, while risks of stroke, MI, and VTE were similar. A lower risk of all-cause mortality was observed with sarilumab compared to tocilizumab. These findings support a potential survival and cardiovascular benefit of IL-6i and highlight the need for larger studies to further distinguish the cardiovascular outcomes with IL-6i agents. Such evidence could inform personalized treatment decisions based on cardiovascular risk factors. Key Points • This study provides long-term real-world evidence that IL-6 inhibitors may offer superior cardiovascular outcomes compared with rituximab in RA patients previously managed with TNFi, an important evidence gap in biologic choice after TNFi failure. • This study directly compares cardiovascular outcomes between sarilumab and tocilizumab, identifying a potential lower myocardial infarction risk with sarilumab.

articles.title: Vascular Access Site, Frailty and Outcomes in Older Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Acute Coronary Syndromes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In older patients with acute coronary syndromes (ACS), frailty predicts adverse outcomes, but whether radial access retains its lower complication rate in patients with frailty is unknown. We examined outcomes by access site and frailty status and whether frailty modified the association between access site and outcomes.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied 227 consecutive patients aged ≥ 70 years, irrespective of frailty status, who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention for ACS at a single center between January 2014 and June 2016. Frailty was screened at admission with the Dutch safety management system (Veiligheidsmanagementsysteem [VMS]) frailty instrument (frailty: VMS score ≥ 1). Primary endpoints were 1-year all-cause mortality and a 30-day composite outcome of death, vascular complications, bleeding, re-infarction and stroke. Effect modification was tested with interaction terms.

RESULTS: Access was femoral in 122 (53.7%) and radial in 105 (46.3%) patients. Of the 222 patients with a VMS score, 78 (35.1%) met frailty criteria. The 30-day composite endpoint occurred in 18.9% of patients with femoral access versus 3.8% with radial access (odds ratio [OR] 0.17, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.06-0.51); 1-year mortality was 12.3% versus 6.7%, respectively (p = 0.14). The composite OR for radial access was 0.14 (95% CI 0.03-0.65) without frailty and 0.24 (95% CI 0.05-1.21) with frailty (ratio of ORs 1.70, 95% CI 0.19-15.54, p-interaction = 0.64; for 1-year mortality 1.24, 95% CI 0.19-8.33, p-interaction = 0.82). Frailty was associated with longer hospital stay and higher 1-year mortality adjusted for access site (hazard ratio [HR] 2.35, 95% CI 1.01-5.43), but not after further adjustment for age (HR 1.56, 95% CI 0.64-3.76).

CONCLUSION: Radial access was associated with markedly fewer early complications while frailty was associated with longer hospitalization and lower 1-year survival, largely explained by age. There was no statistically significant evidence of interaction between frailty and access site, although the interaction analysis was limited by the small number of events. These findings are to be considered hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Genome-wide identification and integrative analysis of the cytochrome P450 superfamily in pea (Pisum sativum L.) reveals candidate genes associated with Aphanomyces root rot response.
articles.abstract: Cytochrome P450 monooxygenases (P450) constitute one of the largest and most functionally diverse enzyme superfamilies in plants, underpinning the biosynthesis of a plethora of primary and specialized metabolites involved in growth and development as well as stress response. Here, we present the first integrated genome-wide analysis of the pea P450 superfamily (CYPome), combining phylogenetic, structural, evolutionary, transcriptional, and genetic approaches to identify defense-associated candidates. We identified 210 P450 genes encoding 241 proteins in pea genome, classified into 45 CYP families across 10 clans. Comparative analyses revealed both highly conserved legume P450 lineages and a substantial fraction of pea-specific expansions, reflecting dynamic CYPome evolution. Gene structure and motif analyses confirmed conservation of core catalytic features, alongside family-specific variation consistent with functional diversification. A conserved core of many PsP450 genes induced across multiple pea cultivars at a wide range of time points post Aphanomyces euteiches infection together with their expression in root tissue was discovered. Integration of aphanomyces root rot resistance-associated quantitative trait loci further refined candidate prioritization, identifying PsP450s that co-localized with resistance loci, exhibited strong co-expression with PsIFS genes, and were rapidly induced upon infection. Collectively, this integrative analysis defines the pea CYPome and identifies a focused set of high-confidence P450 candidates likely involved in defense-associated metabolic reprogramming during A. euteiches infection. These findings provide a foundational resource for functional genomics and offer promising targets for improving disease resistance in pea and related legume crops.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of composite restorations with or without a glass ionomer liner after selective caries removal to soft dentin: a 36-month randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Selective caries removal to soft dentin (SCR-SD) is currently recommended for the management of deep dentine caries lesions in permanent teeth. However, whether a pulp-protective liner is required after SCR-SD remains uncertain. This randomized controlled trial compared the clinical performance and pulp vitality outcomes of composite resin restorations using a universal adhesive with or without a glass ionomer cement (GIC) liner after SCR-SD in deep caries lesions of permanent posterior teeth.

METHODS: A randomized controlled clinical trial was conducted in 144 deep dentin caries lesions from 98 participants aged 9 to 55 years. After SCR-SD, lesions were randomly allocated to one of two restorative strategies: a universal adhesive applied in selective enamel etching mode (SE) and composite resin without a GIC liner, or a conventional GIC liner followed by the same universal adhesive applied in selective enamel etching mode and composite resin (GIC + SE). Restorations were followed for 30-36 months. The primary outcome was restoration survival, assessed using selected FDI criteria. The secondary outcome was pulp vitality preservation. Survival analyses were performed using Weibull regression models.

RESULTS: Of the 144 treated lesions, 117 were evaluated after 30-36 months. Restoration survival did not differ significantly between groups, with survival rates of 96.0% for SE and 92.4% for GIC + SE (p = 0.37). In contrast, pulp vitality preservation was significantly higher in the SE group than in the GIC + SE group, with success rates of 97.5% and 87.3%, respectively (p = 0.01). In the adjusted Weibull regression model, SE was associated with a lower risk of pulp vitality failure compared with GIC + SE. Restorative failure was also strongly associated with pulp vitality failure.

CONCLUSIONS: The use of a GIC liner after SCR-SD did not improve restoration survival and was not associated with better pulp vitality preservation. Composite restorations using universal adhesive applied in selective enamel etching mode placed directly over the remaining dentin showed favorable restorative and biological outcomes after 30-36 months. These findings suggest that routine liner placement after SCR-SD may not be necessary.

CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: In deep dentin caries lesions treated with SCR-SD, placing a glass ionomer liner before composite restoration using a universal adhesive did not improve clinical outcomes. Effective sealing is achieved using universal adhesive applied in selective enamel etching mode and nanofilled composite resin. These simple clinical procedures maintained the restoration integrity and pulp vitality.  Registered on  https://www.

CLINICALTRIALS: gov (NCT04250142).

articles.title: Therapy with Fucosylated Chondroitin Sulfate Extracted from Holothuria grisea in Allergic Airway Inflammation Model.
articles.abstract: Current therapies for asthma are limited by significant adverse effects, and many patients with severe asthma are still unable to achieve adequate symptom control, highlighting the need for novel therapeutic strategies. Fucosylated chondroitin sulfate (FucCS), a glycosaminoglycan isolated from the sea cucumber Holothuria grisea, demonstrates anti-inflammatory properties. This study investigated the therapeutic potential of FucCS in a murine model of ovalbumin (OVA)-induced allergic airway inflammation. C57BL/6 mice were sensitized and challenged with OVA and then treated intraperitoneally with FucCS (2 mg/kg), dexamethasone (DEXA, 2 mg/kg, positive control), or saline (SAL, vehicle control). Additional control mice received saline (CTRL/SAL) instead of OVA during both sensitization and challenge. Pulmonary function, the extent of peribronchial inflammation, total and differential cell counts in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) and lung tissue, as well as levels of key inflammatory mediators were assessed. Compared to the OVA/SAL group, treatment with FucCS significantly reduced basal airway resistance, peribronchial inflammation, and polymorphonuclear cell infiltration in lung parenchyma. Furthermore, FucCS therapy attenuated BALF total cellularity and interleukin (IL)-4 levels and reduced IL-5 levels in lung homogenates, with effects comparable to dexamethasone. Neither treatment altered BALF eosinophil percentage. These findings demonstrate a limited, but significant anti-inflammatory effects of FucCS in experimental allergic inflammation and support its further development as a therapeutic candidate.

articles.title: Syringomyelia secondary to degenerative spinal canal stenosis: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Syringomyelia is most often associated with Chiari malformation, post-traumatic cord injury, intramedullary tumours or arachnoiditis. Its occurrence with degenerative spinal canal stenosis is uncommon, and its natural history and outcomes remain poorly characterised. To synthesise patient-level evidence on syringomyelia secondary to degenerative spinal canal stenosis (mostly cervical spondylosis, with a few thoracic ossified ligamentum flavum cases), addressing presentation, radiology, management and outcomes, and examining the symptomatic and asymptomatic phenotypes separately. PRISMA 2020 systematic review of PubMed, Scopus, Embase and the Cochrane Library from inception to 31 January 2026. Methodological quality was appraised with the Joanna Briggs Institute checklists. Patient-level data were synthesised descriptively as proportions; no meta-analytic pooling was performed. The review was retrospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261379566). Twelve studies contributed 28 patients (mean age 54.9 years, range 33-81; 18 men, 10 women); an institutional index case is presented separately and excluded from all denominators. Twelve patients (42.9%) were asymptomatic and managed conservatively; 16 (57.1%) were symptomatic, most often with motor weakness (75.0%), sensory deficits (50.0%) and pain (37.5%). Reported radiographic regression after extradural decompression alone was 7/12 (58%) - 2/3 anterior, 5/9 posterior; the single case with added intradural shunting was isolated from this figure. Syringomyelia secondary to degenerative spinal canal stenosis is rare and supported by a low-quality evidence base dominated by single-patient case reports. Extradural decompression of the causative stenosis - rather than primary cavity drainage - is the predominant reported strategy. In the only retrospective series large enough to address the question, incidental asymptomatic syrinxes remained stable or regressed on serial imaging; this observation requires independent confirmation.

articles.title: Efficacy of cognitive behavioral therapy for anxiety and depression symptoms in Parkinson's disease patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anxiety and depression are highly prevalent non-motor symptoms in Parkinson's disease (PD), severely compromising health-related quality of life. Conventional pharmacological management is frequently constrained by adverse effects, polypharmacy, and pharmacokinetic interactions. Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) represents a promising structured non-pharmacological strategy, but an updated, comprehensive synthesis of clinical trial evidence is warranted.

OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the efficacy and clinical safety profile of CBT for alleviating anxiety and depressive symptoms in patients with PD.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from database inception to October 2025. RCTs evaluating CBT (≥ 4 sessions over ≥ 4 weeks) versus control conditions (e.g., treatment as usual, waitlist, active controls) in adults with PD reporting anxiety and/or depression outcomes were included. Two reviewers independently screened literature, extracted data, and assessed methodological quality using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled via random-effects models. Subgroup, sensitivity, and publication bias analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Twenty-one RCTs comprising 892 patients with PD (CBT: n = 465; control: n = 427) were included. Meta-analysis demonstrated that CBT was associated with statistically significant reductions in anxiety symptoms (16 studies; SMD = -0.66, 95% CI -0.83 to -0.50; P < 0.001; I2 = 79.1%) and depressive symptoms (14 studies; SMD = -0.61, 95% CI -0.78 to -0.44; P < 0.001; I2 = 86.6%). Subgroup analyses indicated enhanced therapeutic effects in interventions with durations exceeding 10 weeks and when evaluated using population-adapted instruments (e.g., GAI, GDS). Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of pooled estimates, and Egger's tests revealed no significant publication bias.

CONCLUSION: CBT produces significant, clinically meaningful reductions in anxiety and depressive symptoms in patients with Parkinson's disease. Despite substantial between-study heterogeneity and variations in intervention delivery, structured CBT should be recommended as an integral component of multidisciplinary PD care. Larger multicenter RCTs with standardized disease-specific core outcome sets and longer follow-up are warranted.

articles.title: Three-dimensional reconstruction of ultrasound imaging in dentistry: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Three-dimensional ultrasound (3D-US) reconstruction has emerged as a potential solution to the limited field of view and operator dependence of two-dimensional intraoral ultrasonography. Multiple acquisition, tracking, and reconstruction strategies have been proposed, yet no prior systematic review has synthesized the methods used specifically within dentistry.

OBJECTIVE: To identify and compare 3D-US reconstruction techniques applied in dentistry and evaluate how acquisition strategy, spatial tracking, and reconstruction methodology influence accuracy, reproducibility, feasibility, and clinical applicability.

METHODS: A systematic search of 5 databases was performed. Studies were included in the review if they used ultrasound imaging with any 3D-US reconstruction method for a defined dental application. Risk of bias was assessed using a customized hybrid QUADAS-2/QUIN/STARD framework.

RESULTS: Thirteen studies (2010-2025) met the inclusion criteria; 10 were in vitro and 3 in vivo. Acquisition methods included mechanized linear-stage scanning (n = 6), robotic arm control (n = 2), tracked freehand (n = 2), untracked freehand (n = 1), and custom intraoral jigs (n = 2). Accuracy ranged from 12 to 50 μm for digital impressions to sub-millimeter deviations for periodontal and ridge assessments, with most error rates below 10%. Reproducibility and clinical feasibility were both inversely related to hardware complexity: mechanized and robotic systems achieved the highest precision and enabled precise positioning for repeated evaluations; however, they had the lowest clinical usability. Conversely, freehand approaches demonstrated the strongest clinical potential but at the expense of reproducible positioning and highly precise measurements. Risk of bias was high or unclear in all studies due to heterogeneity, small sample sizes, and limited in vivo validation.

CONCLUSIONS: Over 15 years, 3D-US reconstruction in dentistry has advanced substantially, demonstrating promising accuracy for digital impressions, periodontal assessment, ridge measurement, and implant planning. However, most studies remain feasibility-based and in vitro, and methodological variation limits comparability. Future progress will depend on standardization of validation frameworks, increased in vivo accuracy studies, and development of compact, automated acquisition workflows. With continued refinement, 3D-US has the potential to become a clinically practical, radiation-free imaging modality for diagnostic and procedural applications in dentistry.

articles.title: A naturally occurring recombinant PRRSV with a JXA1-derived nsp9 fragment is associated with enhanced virulence in piglets.
articles.abstract: Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV) nonstructural protein 9 (nsp9), the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, has been implicated as a critical virulence determinant of highly pathogenic PRRSV (HP-PRRSV) through reverse genetics studies with engineered chimeric viruses. However, field isolates that naturally carry such nsp9-centric recombination events-thereby serving as potential in vivo models-remain exceptionally rare. Here we report the isolation and characterization of a novel PRRSV strain TJ25928 from a farm in China experiencing a severe PRRS outbreak. TJ25928 possesses the characteristic 131-amino-acid deletion pattern of NADC30-like strains and phylogenetically belongs to Lineage 1.8. Recombination analysis revealed a distinct configuration: the backbone of TJ25928 is derived from NADC30-like strains, while a discrete fragment within the nsp9 coding region (nt 7856-8923) is derived from JXA1-like HP-PRRSV. The boundaries of this nsp9 fragment overlap substantially with the nsp9 segment previously implicated in fatal virulence in engineered chimeric viruses. In piglet challenge experiments, TJ25928 induced significant febrile response (8-12 days post-infection), pronounced growth suppression (approximately 28% reduction in total weight gain at 21 days post-infection), and 33.3% (1/3) mortality. TJ25928 represents an important example of a field isolate that naturally carries the nsp9 recombination configuration previously studied by reverse genetics, providing a valuable natural model for future investigations into the role of nsp9 in PRRSV virulence. These findings underscore the pathogenic potential of nsp9 recombination events in the field and offer a useful tool for future mechanistic studies on PRRSV virulence.

articles.title: Emergent Roles of RVLMC1 Neurons in Cardiovascular Homeostasis and Systemic Physiological Regulation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF THE REVIEW: Adrenergic C1 neurons in the rostral ventrolateral medulla (RVLMC1) have long been recognized for their role in regulating sympathetic activity and arterial blood pressure (BP). However, novel approaches such as genetic targeting, optogenetics, fiber photometry, among others, allowed us to study the biology of these neurons in deeper detail and in non-anesthetized preparations, unraveling previously underappreciated or unrecognized functions. Here we will discuss recent studies that explored the function of RVLMC1 neurons for the sympathetic regulation of BP and also the emergent roles of these cells for other processes involved in systemic physiological regulation.

RECENT FINDINGS: Using selective methods of manipulation and recording of neuronal activity in conscious animals, it was demonstrated that RVLMC1 neurons play a critical role in BP stability across multiple behaviors, including sleep-wake state and postural changes. Besides cardiovascular control, recent evidence shows that these neurons play a critical role in different homeostatic functions such as thermoregulation, immune response, glycemia and in complex behaviors such as anxiety. RVLMC1 neurons are a key hub that integrates interoceptive signals from peripheral systems to regulate BP and other basic physiological functions. Along with their role in cardiovascular regulation, these emergent roles of RVLMC1 neurons may also need to be considered when explaining the complex and multifactorial pathophysiology of cardiometabolic diseases associated with hypertension.

articles.title: Antimicrobial peptides for companion animals: research advances, translational challenges, and opportunities.
articles.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents a growing global threat to public health, necessitating the development of novel antimicrobial strategies. Companion animals, particularly dogs and cats, are increasingly integrated into human lives, and their close interactions with humans facilitate the transmission of antimicrobial-resistant pathogens. Therefore, the use of contemporary antimicrobials in these animals raises significant concerns for both animal and human health. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), a class of naturally occurring peptides, play a critical role in host innate immunity through dual antimicrobial and immunomodulatory activities. Due to their pleiotropic mechanisms of action and lower selective pressure for resistance, AMPs are emerging as promising alternative candidates to conventional antimicrobials. Notably, accumulating evidence has also highlighted the promising antitumor capacity of AMPs, expanding their therapeutic potential beyond microbial infection control. Despite their potential, research on AMPs in companion animals remains limited, with most available evidence derived from in vitro assays and pre‑clinical in vivo experiments, while well‑controlled clinical studies are sparse. This review overviews recent advances in AMP research in dogs and cats, discusses major challenges in their development, and outlines future directions for their application in veterinary medicine. The adoption of AMPs in small animal practice has the potential to improve animal health while contributing to the mitigation of AMR. Collectively, this review offers new insights into the development of multifunctional novel therapeutic strategies in companion animals.
