articles.title: Resistance training and protein supplementation in patients with incurable gastroesophageal cancer: a randomized feasibility trial.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Cancer cachexia is associated with reduced physical performance, quality of life, and survival in patients with incurable gastroesophageal cancer. Resistance training and protein supplementation have the potential to improve these outcomes. Whether an intervention comprising resistance training and protein supplementation is feasible during treatment for incurable gastroesophageal cancer is not known.

METHODS: This was an open-label, parallel-group, two-arm, randomized controlled feasibility trial. Patients with incurable gastroesophageal cancer scheduled to undergo first-line chemotherapy were randomized 2:1 to resistance training three times per week and daily protein supplementation or to control. The primary outcome, feasibility, was assessed by recruitment, retention, adherence, and harms. Secondary outcomes included body composition, physical performance, quality of life, and treatment tolerability.

RESULTS: Out of 106 potentially eligible patients, 20 participants (5 female and 15 male, mean age 65) were randomized yielding a recruitment rate of 19%. 18 participants completed the trial with a retention rate of 90%. Median (25th; 75th percentile) adherence to the resistance training sessions and to the protein supplements was 63% (43; 77) and 39% (17; 76), respectively. Five participants (38%) met the minimum feasibility criteria of both interventions. No serious adverse events related to the intervention occurred. We found no between-group differences in body composition, physical performance, quality of life, or treatment tolerability.

CONCLUSION: Resistance training combined with protein supplementation was not feasible during first-line chemotherapy in patients with incurable gastroesophageal cancer due to low accrual and low adherence to protein supplementation.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05650827. Study registration date 2022-12-12.

articles.title: CLEC1B and RAC1 in peripheral immune remodeling associated with sleep disturbance: an exploratory integrative study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep disturbance is closely linked to immune dysfunction, but the molecular features of associated peripheral immune remodeling remain incompletely defined.

RESULTS: In this exploratory study, we integrated blood eQTL data and GWAS summary statistics with mouse PBMC single-cell data, a human PBMC transcriptome cohort, and mouse PBMC measurements. The single-cell dataset comprised one control, one 24-hour sleep-deprivation, and one 48-hour sleep-deprivation library. Descriptive single-cell patterns showed contraction of the B-cell compartment and expansion of granulocytes. Mendelian randomization nominally prioritized RAC1 and CLEC1B, with limited co-localization support. Both genes showed lower expression in the human cohort and were associated with altered B-cell communication and metabolic states. In mouse PBMCs (n = 3 per group), Clec1b qPCR showed a downward trend (P = 0.072), whereas Rac1 qPCR expression was lower after sleep deprivation (P = 0.017). Lane-level western blot analysis also showed lower CLEC1B (P = 0.0056) and RAC1 (P = 0.0016) protein abundance.

CONCLUSIONS: These exploratory integrative analyses nominate CLEC1B and RAC1 as candidate genes associated with peripheral B-cell remodeling in a sleep-disturbance context. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant targeted functional studies of their roles in sleep-related immune remodeling.

articles.title: Erdheim-Chester disease: a diagnostic dilemma - a report of four cases.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Erdheim-Chester disease (ECD) is a rare, systemic non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis with infiltration of foamy histiocytes, lymphohistiocytes, and giant cells. Central nervous system (CNS) involvement occurs in up to 40% of cases; however, predominant CNS involvement is rare and diagnostically challenging, mimicking neoplastic and inflammatory conditions.

METHODS: We retrospectively analysed four adult patients (three males, one female; age 27-40 years) with neurological ECD at our institution (2013-2025). Clinical, radiological, laboratory, and histopathological data were reviewed, including brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), neurophysiological studies, systemic evaluation, immunohistochemistry, and BRAF mutation analysis.

RESULTS: Endocrine dysfunction (central diabetes insipidus) preceded neurological symptoms in two patients by 7-8 years. Neurological manifestations included progressive cerebellar ataxia, dysarthria, tremors, visual deterioration, and headaches. MRI showed infiltrative T2/fluid-attenuated inversion recovery iso- to hyperintense lesions in the sellar/suprasellar region, cerebellum, brainstem, and optic pathways, with multifocal ventricular and dural dissemination in two cases. Long bone involvement was identified in three patients, trapezius muscle involvement in one, and pericardial involvement in one. Histopathology showed xanthomatous histiocytes positive for CD68/CD163 and negative for CD1a/S100, with confirmed BRAF V600E mutation in all cases. Treatment and outcomes varied considerably.

CONCLUSION: Predominant neurological ECD should be considered in patients with atypical non-neoplastic CNS lesions accompanied by diabetes insipidus or long bone involvement. Detection of BRAF or other mitogen-activated protein kinase pathway mutations, alongside characteristic radiological and histopathological findings, confirms its neoplastic nature and enables timely initiation of targeted therapies such as BRAF inhibitors.

articles.title: Dynamic craniotomy with NuCrani plates versus craniotomy with fixed plates: A propensity score matched study.
articles.abstract: Dynamic craniotomy provides for cranial decompression by enabling controlled outward bone flap movement to accommodate postoperative cerebral swelling and/or hemorrhage. The study objective was to compare outcomes in patients who underwent dynamic craniotomy with those who underwent fixed plate craniotomy for the treatment of intracranial hemorrhage from traumatic brain injury. A review of our clinical series of 55 consecutive patients undergoing either dynamic craniotomy bone flap fixation with NeuroVention NuCrani plates or fixed plate craniotomy bone flap fixation for traumatic injuries was conducted. Clinical and radiographic characteristics were reviewed for each patient. To reduce confounding factors, propensity score-matched analysis was used to compare outcomes in both groups. Outward bone flap migration to compensate for post operative cerebral swelling was noted in 84% of the dynamic craniotomy group and 40% of the dynamic patients had 8 mm or more bone flap outward migration for severe brain swelling. Dynamic craniotomy was associated with lower postoperative midline shift (1.8 mm dynamic versus 6.0 mm fixed), lower observed mortality (16.0% versus 46.7%), and a higher proportion of patients with good outcome (84.0% versus 33.3%). Propensity score analysis using logistic regression and matching based on age, admission Glasgow Coma Score, preoperative midline shift, and preoperative extra-axial hematoma thickness was used to reduce measured baseline differences. The association between dynamic craniotomy and favorable outcome remained consistent after propensity-score adjustment. Dynamic craniotomy was associated with improved radiographic and clinical outcomes in this retrospective propensity-score matched study. The dynamic technique offers a notable advantage by enabling instant intracranial volume expansion and reversible outward bone flap migration in patients with postoperative worsening brain swelling and/or hemorrhage.

articles.title: Controversy: Atrial fibrillation ablation should be performed in patients with HFpEF.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract: The role of atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation in the management of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remains an under investigated issue with no robust clinical trials data. This controversy reviews the evidence for and against AF ablation in this complex condition from two different perspectives reviewing mechanistic and observational evidence aswell as proposing future directions for research in the field.

articles.title: TRAIL promotes ionizing radiation-induced arrhythmogenic dysfunction in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes.
Pacing Performance of a Modular Communicative Leadless Pacing-Defibrillator System.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: MODULAR ATP is an ongoing trial assessing the efficacy of a subcutaneous implantable cardioverter defibrillator (S-ICD) in communication with a leadless pacemaker (LP) that can deliver bradycardia pacing and antitachycardia pacing. The objective of this study was to assess safety and pacing performance of the investigational LP.

METHODS: The study enrolled patients with an ICD indication and at high risk for monomorphic ventricular tachycardia. Pacemaker dependent patients were excluded. Primary safety endpoint 2 was the percentage of patients free from major LP-related complications at 12 months. The secondary effectiveness endpoint assessed the rate response performance of the LP under workload. Parameters related to the pacing performance were also measured.

RESULTS: In 297 patients, the mean age was 59±12 years, the mean left ventricular ejection fraction was 35.3±13.1%, and 17.5% were female. LP implant was attempted in 286 patients and was successful in 100%. The major LP-related complication free rate at 12 months was 97.2% (one-sided 97.5% LCL 94.5%), surpassing the performance goal of 81%. There were no LP-related complications following Implant. For the secondary effectiveness endpoint, the slope of the normalized sensor rate versus the normalized workload was 0.96 (95% LCL 0.91, 95% UCL 1.02), within the performance goal range of 0.65-1.35. At 12 months, 96.8% of patients had a pacing capture threshold ≤ 2V @ 0.4ms pulse width.

CONCLUSIONS: The performance of the modular pacing-defibrillator system at one year demonstrated a low complication rate and reliable pacing functionality.

articles.title: Chrysene aggravates allergic airway inflammation in association with TRPA1/NF-κB signaling and epithelial-immune dysregulation.
articles.abstract: Chrysene, a representative polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH), is a ubiquitous environmental pollutant associated with adverse respiratory health effects. However, the mechanisms by which chrysene contributes to allergic airway inflammation remain incompletely understood. The present study investigated the involvement of TRPA1/NF-κB signaling in chrysene-associated epithelial injury and epithelial-immune dysregulation. Human bronchial epithelial cells and an ovalbumin (OVA)-induced murine model of allergic airway inflammation were used. Chrysene exposure inhibited epithelial cell proliferation, increased reactive oxygen species generation, enhanced TRPA1/NF-κB signaling, and reduced the expression of epithelial junction-associated proteins, including E-cadherin, ZO-1, and occludin. Pharmacological inhibition or lentiviral-mediated knockdown of TRPA1 attenuated NF-κB signaling and partially restored junction-associated protein expression. In vivo, chrysene aggravated OVA-induced airway hyperresponsiveness, eosinophilic inflammation, and mucus hypersecretion. These changes were accompanied by increased serum IL-25, IL-33, and TSLP levels, enhanced pulmonary ILC2 responses, and elevated serum IL-5 and IL-13 levels. Inhibition of TRPA1 or NF-κB attenuated several of these responses. Overall, these findings implicate TRPA1/NF-κB signaling in chrysene-associated epithelial injury and type 2 allergic airway inflammation.

articles.title: Reproductive factors in women with familial hypercholesterolaemia.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Hypercholesterolaemia has been associated with earlier menarche and menopause; however, these observations may reflect reverse causation or confounding. Familial Hypercholesterolaemia (FH) provides a model to investigate these associations. This study compared reproductive characteristics and pregnancy outcomes in women with FH vs. women without FH.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Between November 2023 and April 2025, women with FH aged ≥40 years were recruited from two university hospital outpatient clinics in the Netherlands and Norway. Women without FH were selected from the Rotterdam Study and Norwegian population-based cohorts. FH cases were matched 1:2 to women without FH on age, smoking status, body mass index, and ethnicity using nearest-neighbour matching. Information on reproductive factors and pregnancy outcomes were obtained via an online survey. 484 women with FH and 968 matched women without FH (median age 55 years [IQR 48-62]; 93% North-Western European) were included. Cardiovascular disease prevalence was higher in women with FH (22% vs. 4%; P < 0.001). Most women with FH (95%) used lipid-lowering therapy, LDL cholesterol levels were lower compared to controls (2.5 vs. 3.5 mmol/L; P < 0.001). Women with FH more often had been pregnant (91% vs. 84%; P < 0.001). Prevalence of gestational diabetes (4% vs. 4%; P = 0.70) and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (16% vs. 13%; P = 0.10) was similar; however, preeclampsia was more frequent in FH (11% vs. 7%; P = 0.030). Age at menarche (13.2 vs. 13.1 years; P = 0.43), age at menopause (50 years; P = 0.92), and reproductive lifespan (36 years; P = 0.98) were similar between groups.

CONCLUSION: Reproductive lifespan is comparable between women with and without FH, but FH was associated with a higher prevalence of preeclampsia, highlighting the importance of targeted pregnancy monitoring and prevention.

articles.title: Low-Level Pyuria and Antibiotic Prescribing for Suspected Urinary Tract Infection in Children.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to understand the impact of urinalysis results on clinician antibiotic prescribing for pediatric patients evaluated at ambulatory visits. We hypothesized that responses to low pyuria levels contribute disproportionately to overtreatment.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study combined electronic health record and abstracted symptom data from emergency department and urgent care visits to 4 Northern California settings. We sampled ambulatory visits by patients aged between 2 months and 17 years who underwent urinalysis between January 1, 2022, and December 31, 2023. We used multivariable logistic regression to assess relationships between urinalysis results, clinical covariates including age, and empiric antibiotic initiation. We estimated attributable impact of these relationships on overtreatment for patients in whom urinary tract infection (UTI) was excluded by culture criteria. We similarly estimated impact on treatment for those with culture-confirmed UTI.

RESULTS: Among 1150 patients with median age 6.3 years, 191 (16.6%) received antibiotics. Low pyuria levels (trace leukocyte esterase, 10-69 white blood cells [WBC]/mm,3 5-10 WBC/high-power field) were associated with antibiotic initiation with adjusted odds ratio 6.62 (95% CI 3.72-11.79) compared with no pyuria. The adjusted attributable fraction (aAF) for overtreatment at this level was 17.0% (95% CI 10.3%-23.2%), with aAF 1.8% (95% CI 1.1%-2.4%) for UTI treatment. Differential impacts on overtreatment and UTI treatment were consistent in age-stratified analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: To promote selective UTI treatment, clinicians should consider degree of pyuria in context with age, risk factors, symptoms, and other urinalysis results. Health system interventions should be designed to mitigate excess influence of low pyuria levels and promote integrated diagnostic assessments.

articles.title: Intravenous Thrombolysis for Acute Ischemic Stroke - New Directions.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract: In the past 5 years, substantial changes have been made in the use of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) in patients with acute ischemic stroke. Integrating IVT with endovascular thrombectomy, which improves outcomes in patients with stroke due to large cerebral vessel occlusion, has been a particular challenge. This review discusses the underlying vascular targets for IVT and thrombectomy, the increasing use of tenecteplase instead of alteplase, broadening indications for the use of IVT, and ancillary drugs and dosing methods that may augment the success of IVT.

articles.title: Plozasiran for Severe Hypertriglyceridemia and Risk of Pancreatitis.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe hypertriglyceridemia is associated with an increased risk of acute pancreatitis. Plozasiran, a small interfering RNA targeting APOC3 messenger RNA, lowers triglyceride levels and potentially mitigates the risk of acute pancreatitis.

METHODS: In two double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, 757 adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive plozasiran (25 mg) or placebo at baseline and at months 3, 6, and 9. These trials had identical designs, end points, and analytic plans. The primary end point was the percent change in the fasting plasma triglyceride level from baseline to month 12. Key secondary end points were the percent change in the fasting triglyceride level from baseline to month 10, a fasting triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter (5.6 mmol per liter) and less than 150 mg per deciliter (1.7 mmol per liter), the percent change in the fasting serum triglyceride level at month 12 for patients with a baseline triglyceride level of 880 mg per deciliter or greater, and changes in remnant cholesterol and non-HDL cholesterol. A pooled analysis addressed adjudicated acute pancreatitis, incidence, and first-event timing.

RESULTS: At month 12, patients in the plozasiran groups had a median triglyceride level that was lower than the baseline level by 79% and 81% in the two trials. These reductions corresponded to a median difference in the plozasiran groups as compared with the placebo groups (placebo-adjusted change) of -45 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], -51 to -38) and -47 percentage points (95% CI, -54 to -39). A triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter at 12 months was reported in 91% and 93% of the patients in the plozasiran groups and in 51% and 50% of those in the placebo groups (P<0.001). The rates of acute pancreatitis were 1 per 100 patient-years with plozasiran and 5 per 100 patient-years with placebo (rate ratio, 0.22; P = 0.008). Adverse events during treatment occurred in 73% of the patients in both the pooled plozasiran and placebo groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia, the use of plozasiran resulted in lower triglyceride levels and a lower risk of acute pancreatitis than placebo at 12 months. (Funded by Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals; SHASTA-3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06347003; SHASTA-4, NCT06347016.).

articles.title: EGCG@ZIF-8@Polydopamine-Functionalized Janus Nanofibrous Dressing with Directional Exudate Transport and Photothermal Antibacterial Activity for Infected Wound Treatment.
articles.abstract: The treatment of infected skin wounds continues to face multiple challenges, including bacterial resistance, persistent inflammation, oxidative damage, and inadequate exudate management. To address these issues, a multifunctional Janus wound dressing was constructed to achieve coordinated infection control and tissue repair. Zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) was used as a nanocarrier for the natural antioxidant molecule, and polydopamine surface coating endowed the composite nanoparticles with photothermal antibacterial activity. The composite nanoparticles were subsequently incorporated into a hydrophobic polycaprolactone layer by electrospinning and combined with a hydrophilic polyacrylonitrile layer containing a pH indicator, thereby forming a bilayer structure with unidirectional liquid transport, visual monitoring, and wound protection functions. The dressing promotes the outward transfer of wound exudate and produces an observable color response to changes in environmental pH. Under near-infrared irradiation, the antibacterial rate of the dressing reached 98.89% against E. coli and 99.99% against S. aureus. The dressing also possesses excellent free-radical-scavenging capacity, indicating its potential to alleviate excessive oxidative stress in infected wounds. Animal experiments further demonstrated that the dressing reduced the local infection burden, promoted wound closure, collagen deposition, and tissue formation, and caused no obvious histopathological abnormalities in major organs. Overall, this study presents a multifunctional Janus nanofibrous dressing that integrates antibacterial activity, antioxidant function, exudate regulation, and wound-status monitoring, providing a material-design approach for the repair of infected skin wounds.

articles.title: Reversing ticagrelor's P2Y12 inhibition in life-threatening haemorrhage: a case-based review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ticagrelor is an oral reversible platelet P2Y12 inhibitor that improves ischemic outcomes in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, including the prevention of stent thrombosis after percutaneous coronary intervention, at the cost of increased bleeding risk.

AREAS COVERED: A comprehensive literature search was performed across PubMed and Web of Science (inception to January 2026). This case-based review outlines the current guidance surrounding bleeding events and emergent surgery on oral P2Y12 inhibitors, including treatment options for reversing their effects, and describes a novel ticagrelor reversal agent in two cases of life-threatening bleeding, one related to gastrointestinal hemorrhage and one associated with emergent coronary artery bypass graft surgery.

EXPERT OPINION: Ticagrelor is a first-line treatment for acute coronary syndromes but is associated with heightened bleeding risk, especially when combined with aspirin. Ticagrelor's reversibility may offer advantages over the irreversibly-acting thienopyridine P2Y12 inhibitors. Patients treated with potent antiplatelet regimens may require rapid and effective restoration of hemostatic activity in addition to supportive measures in those presenting with life-threatening hemorrhage or requiring emergent surgery. We summarize the current available treatment options to reverse antiplatelet activity and highlight the role of ticagrelor reversal with bentracimab in improving hemostasis in emergency settings.

articles.title: Direct cardiac or systemic? Reexamining the cardiovascular mechanisms of SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor agonists.
articles.journal: Journal of basic and clinical physiology and pharmacology
articles.abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) improve cardiovascular (CV) outcomes in type 2 diabetes mellitus, and several agents benefit patients without diabetes, yet their mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This narrative review examines whether these benefits arise from direct cardiac actions, systemic hemodynamic and metabolic effects, or both. We performed a structured PubMed search for CV outcome trials, mediation analyses, human mechanistic and imaging studies, and preclinical studies, classifying each proposed mechanism by its supporting evidence. Outcome trials consistently show that SGLT2 inhibitors reduce heart failure (HF) hospitalization and slow kidney disease progression, whereas GLP-1 RAs reduce atherosclerotic events, but these trials cannot identify the responsible mechanisms. Human data support contributions from natriuresis, decongestion, and renal hemodynamics for SGLT2 inhibitors and from glycemic, vascular, and anti-inflammatory effects for GLP-1 RAs, although mediation analyses explain only part of either class's benefit. Direct myocardial actions remain largely hypothetical in humans. The CV effects of both classes are best viewed as overlapping, interacting hemodynamic, renal, metabolic, vascular, and neurohormonal mechanisms rather than a direct-versus-systemic dichotomy. Clinically, the evidence supports prioritizing SGLT2 inhibitors for HF and chronic kidney disease and GLP-1 RAs for atherosclerotic CV disease and obesity-related risk.

articles.title: Brain Mechanisms Linking Type 2 Diabetes to Alzheimer Disease: A Multimodal Imaging Framework.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus is associated with an increased risk of Alzheimer disease and cognitive impairment; however, the mechanisms underlying these associations remain incompletely understood. Here, we propose and justify a mechanistic, multimodal imaging framework to examine how type 2 diabetes-associated hyperglycemia and neurovascular dysfunction may contribute to cognitive vulnerability and accelerated brain aging. Dynamic metabolic stress testing using multimodal glucose-challenge imaging methods is proposed as the central component of this framework to investigate cerebral blood flow, blood-brain barrier integrity, metabolic demand, functional connectivity, and structural brain alterations under conditions of acute hyperglycemia. By examining these complementary neurovascular and metabolic responses together, rather than as individual imaging measures, this proposed approach is intended as a mechanistic discovery platform to identify neurovascular pathways linking type 2 diabetes mellitus-related dysglycemia with cognitive vulnerability in a population with a high burden of metabolic risk. By integrating current mechanistic evidence with a proposed multimodal imaging approach, this work aims to generate testable mechanistic hypotheses and inform future biomarker-driven and longitudinal studies of diabetes-related dementia risk.

articles.title: Commentary: Clinical Implications of Structural and Electrical Recurrence after Mitral Valve Repair and Concomitant Atrial Fibrillation Ablation.
An Exploratory Study of Image-Guided Cochlear Implant Intervention on Articulation and Phonological Processing in Children With Speech Sound Disorders.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Poor spectral clarity from cochlear implants (CIs) has been hypothesized to contribute to articulation and phonological processing deficits among children with CIs. Therefore, CI programming techniques that aim to improve spectral resolution may lead to improvements in articulation and phonological processing skills (i.e., phonological awareness as well as phonological and phonetic recoding).

METHOD: We analyzed the articulation and phonological skills of 21 children with CIs (4.7-13.1 years old) with articulation and phonological processing deficits who were enrolled in a 2-year waitlist-deferred randomized controlled trial examining image-guided cochlear implant programming (IGCIP). In the clinical trial, participants were randomly assigned to receive IGCIP at varying time points throughout the study. Change over time in articulation and phonological processing was assessed in the subset of 21 children. Additionally, an exploratory analysis of the effect of IGCIP on articulation and phonological processing skills was completed.

RESULTS: Only articulation, not phonological processing, improved relative to age norms. IGCIP did not have a statistically significant effect on articulation or phonological processing in the first year of the study. However, participants who received IGCIP within the first year of the study did exhibit larger and clinically meaningful improvements in articulation scores compared with those who did not receive IGCIP.

CONCLUSIONS: Articulation deficits, but not phonological processing deficits, improved over time among children with CIs. Future studies should assess the impact of IGCIP on articulation within a larger sample of CI users with articulation deficits to clarify its role in such improvements.

articles.title: Ethnoracial and Linguistic Diversity in Treatment Research for Primary Progressive Aphasia: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This systematic review article sought to characterize the ethnoracial and linguistic representation of participants in the nonpharmacological intervention literature for primary progressive aphasia (PPA) and primary progressive apraxia of speech (PPAOS). In addition, we aimed to identify which social determinants of health (SDOH) factors are most frequently reported across studies.

METHOD: We performed a comprehensive search across six electronic databases: OVID Medline, OVID PsycINFO, EBSCO Medline, EBSCO CINAHL Plus, Embase, and Web of Science, as well as additional published literature not indexed in these databases. We identified 149 original studies that administered neuromodulation and/or speech-language interventions to individuals with PPA or PPAOS and reported communication outcomes relative to a baseline or control group. From these studies, we extracted data on participants' race, ethnicity, spoken languages, occupation, years of education, and other relevant sociodemographic variables.

RESULTS: Ethnoracial and linguistic diversity in the current PPA literature is limited and underrepresented. Among studies that reported the extracted variables, the majority of participants were identified as non-Hispanic White, and most studies were conducted in the United States. English was the most commonly reported spoken language and was frequently used as an inclusion criterion. Regarding SDOH, participants tend to have medium-high education and hold higher skill-level occupations. Very few studies reported retirement status and whether retirement was due to symptom onset.

CONCLUSIONS: Current intervention research for PPA and PPAOS lacks ethnoracial and linguistic diversity. This underrepresentation is further compounded by limited reporting of factors related to SDOH. The concentration of research in homogenous populations limits the generalizability of current findings and restricts their relevance for managing PPA and PPAOS across diverse demographic, cultural, linguistic, and socioeconomic contexts. Future research on treatment should not only ensure comprehensive reporting of participant characteristics but also actively expand the inclusivity of recruitment practices.

articles.title: Beyond casemix: identifying an unpriced ICU cost driver in Victorian public hospitals.
articles.journal: Australian health review : a publication of the Australian Hospital Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Australia's National Pricing Model (NPM) adjusts public hospital funding for type, size, location, and patient complexity, but whether these adjustments adequately address structural cost variation at the jurisdictional level remains unknown. This study aimed to identify exogenous structural attributes associated with case-mix adjusted cost variation in Victorian public hospitals, and assess the adequacy of their compensation under activity-based funding.

METHODS: A cross-sectional analysis of 1,934,946 inpatient episodes across 55 Victorian public hospital campuses (2024-25) was undertaken using linked administrative and cost data. Associations between 20 structural variables and cost per National Weighted Activity Unit (NWAU) were examined using Pearson/Spearman correlation, principal component analysis, and multivariable regression with HC3 heteroskedasticity-consistent standard errors.

RESULTS: After adjustment for multiple comparisons, four variables were significantly associated with cost variation: weekend admissions (r = -0.524), after-hours admissions (r = -0.422), hospital remoteness (ρ = 0.328), and medical officer ratio (r = -0.305). In multivariable modelling, ICU non-Level 3 hours was the only consistent independent predictor of higher costs (P = 0.020). ICU non-Level 3 episodes cost $13,187 per NWAU - a $4063 gap above the National Efficient Price (62.8%) and a $73.0 million annual shortfall - with no current NPM adjustment. This contrasts with the more complex Level 3 ICU episodes, which have a NPM adjustment and no shortfall.

CONCLUSIONS: Structural cost variation in Victorian hospitals follows a two-tiered pattern. First, after-hours, weekend, and teaching-intensity variables appear consistent with current NWAU pricing, despite being individually associated with cost variation. Second, ICU non-Level 3 hours represent a potentially unpriced structural cost driver warranting further investigation.

articles.title: Diabetes educators' experience of care delivery to clients during the COVID-19 pandemic: a qualitative descriptive study.
articles.journal: Australian health review : a publication of the Australian Hospital Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: With social distancing and limitations on face-to-face interactions during the COVID-19 pandemic, diabetes educators had to adapt their practices by implementing telehealth appointments as the primary mode of care delivery. The aim of the study was to explore diabetes educators' experiences of engaging with people who have diabetes during the COVID-19 pandemic. The research question was: What were diabetes educators' experiences of delivering care to clients during the COVID-19 pandemic?

METHODS: A qualitative descriptive methodology using semi-structured interviews was used. Individual interviews were conducted during December 2023 and March 2024 with diabetes educators who provided care in Australian hospitals or communities during the pandemic. Interviews were audio recorded, and data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis.

RESULTS: Nine diabetes educators participated in interviews. Interview themes were: (1) challenges experienced in provision of diabetes care, with sub-themes including fear and avoidance behaviour, social isolation and mental health issues, and challenges faced by diabetes educators; and (2) adaptations in diabetes care, with sub-themes including transition to telehealth and face-to-face education as a supplement.

CONCLUSION: This study revealed insights into challenges and opportunities of telehealth and/or remote care delivery for people with diabetes during the pandemic, highlighting the need for adaptations in diabetes care. Future practice strategies should consider adoption of a more integrated healthcare delivery model that incorporates telehealth and/or remote services.

articles.title: Does Portable Voice Amplification Improve Vocal Outcomes in Elementary School Teachers? Evidence From Aerodynamic, Acoustic, and Self-Reported Measures.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The present study aimed at evaluating the impact of a voice amplification system plus vocal hygiene on aerodynamic, acoustic, and self-reported outcomes in elementary school teachers with and without voice problems.

METHOD: A total of 217 elementary school teachers were initially recruited: 108 normal-voiced participants and 109 participants with voice complaints. Participants from both groups were assessed before and after voice intervention, with aerodynamic, acoustic, and self-reported outcomes being observed. Participants were randomly assigned to one of two treatments before starting voice intervention procedures: (a) use of amplification system in their classroom setting plus vocal hygiene program (experimental condition) and (b) vocal hygiene program only (control condition). Thus, four groups were generated for this study. Data were analyzed by implementing mixed-effects models for all dependent variables.

RESULTS: For dysphonic teachers, significant interactions were observed on Vocal Fatigue Index, Voice Handicap Index, and Vocal Tract Discomfort Scale values, reflecting greater improvement for the experimental group as compared to the control group once the intervention was completed. In contrast, no differential effects were observed for smoothed cepstral peak prominence, airflow rate, subglottal pressure, or phonation threshold pressure. Only one significant interaction was detected in participants with normal voices, suggesting that treatment is more effective for teachers already suffering from dysphonia.

CONCLUSIONS: Portable amplification system plus vocal hygiene seems to positively impact dysphonic school teachers' voice, especially in terms of self-reported improvements in functional, physical, and emotional voice-related dimensions; throat discomfort; and vocal fatigue symptoms. No statistically significant changes were observed for aerodynamic or acoustic outcomes. These findings, along with prior evidence, suggest that voice amplification may be most beneficial when implemented as one component of a broader approach to occupational vocal health, combined with other strategies such as voice training and classroom acoustic interventions.

articles.title: The Impact of Conversational Turn-Taking on Vocabulary Size in Toddlers With Developmental Delays Using Augmentative and Alternative Communication.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study tracked the growth of conversational turn-taking during augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) intervention and evaluated how conversational turn-taking influenced the effectiveness of a 12-week augmented language intervention.

METHOD: This study is a secondary analysis of archival data from Romski et al. (2010) and Romski et al. (2025). In total, 109 parents and their children with a variety of developmental delays (DDs) were randomly assigned to four intervention conditions across the two studies: (1) augmented input, (2) augmented output, (3) augmented input and output, and (4) spoken communication (SC). Language transcripts, including conversational turn count (CTC) and spontaneous augmented/spoken words, were transcribed using the Systematic Analysis of Language Transcripts software for 30-min interaction sessions between the parent and child at baseline, Session 18, and Session 24.

RESULTS: Total CTCs between parent-child dyads were found to have a quadratic growth curve. When separated by speaker, both parents and children had similar quadratic growth in CTCs over the course of the intervention. Additionally, it was found that exposure to AAC moderated the relationship between conversational turns and vocabulary size, such that higher rates of conversational turns were related to larger vocabulary size but only in parent-child dyads exposed to AAC conditions.

CONCLUSIONS: AAC creates a unique communicative environment where children with DD can reap the benefits of increased CTC not seen in traditional SC interventions. Parents and practitioners can couple AAC intervention with encouragement of more conversational turns within the population.

articles.title: Best Practice International Guidelines on Online Communities of Aphasia Groups.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: We aim to establish best practice guidelines for the design, facilitation, and sustainability of online support groups for people with aphasia (PWA). It explores the benefits, challenges, and psychological considerations of virtual aphasia interventions.

METHOD: The recommendations presented were developed through a collaborative consensus process by our writing team, which was informed by a comprehensive review of current literature, insights from international experts, and practical experiences across various settings. This process involved meetings held between June 2023 and April 2025, focusing on the "Community of Practice related to online aphasia support." These discussions examined the types, goals, and key features of online support groups-highlighting person-centered approaches, facilitation skills, and cultural responsiveness-and considered technological, logistical, and funding factors critical for successful implementation. Guided by principles of evidence-based practice and consensus building, the development produced practical recommendations that reflect diverse perspectives and best practices in both face-to-face and online aphasia support.

RESULTS: Online aphasia support groups enhance accessibility, foster peer support, and promote social participation, contributing positively to psychological well-being. This tutorial identifies common challenges (e.g., technological barriers, engagement difficulties, and resource constraints), offering evidence-based strategies for mitigation. It underscores the importance of tailored facilitator training and sustainable funding models adapted to diverse contexts.

CONCLUSIONS: Online aphasia support groups are valuable tools to improve long-term communication and psychosocial outcomes for PWA. Their success depends on careful planning, skilled facilitation, and inclusive practices. Ongoing research, international collaboration, and adaptable funding strategies are vital to optimize their impact and expand access globally.

articles.title: Pelvic insufficiency fractures after chemoradiotherapy for cervical cancer: incidence, long-term outcomes, and survivorship management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pelvic insufficiency fractures, a late complication of chemoradiotherapy for cervical cancer, can cause pain and functional impairment. Although most studies have reported incidence rates and risk factors, few have examined clinical presentation, long-term symptom burden, or the impact on survivorship.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of patients with cervical cancer treated with chemoradiotherapy from 2018 to 2024. We extracted clinical characteristics, treatment details, dosimetric parameters, imaging studies documenting pelvic insufficiency fractures, and clinical outcomes from the electronic medical record. We used the Kaplan-Meier method to estimate the probability of pelvic insufficiency fractures and univariate Cox regression to assess clinical and dosimetric factors associated with their development.

RESULTS: The cohort comprised 153 patients (median follow-up: 41.4 months). After chemoradiotherapy, 18 patients (11.8%) developed radiologically confirmed pelvic insufficiency fractures (median time to diagnosis: 9.5 months; probability of pelvic insufficiency fracture at 24 months: 11.4%). PET-CT and/or MRI showed that most pelvic insufficiency fractures involved the sacrum. No statistically significant clinical or dosimetric predictors of pelvic insufficiency fractures were identified. All symptomatic patients (n = 15, 83%) required referral to pain management services (median observed duration of symptoms: 37 months). No symptomatic patient achieved documented complete symptom resolution during the available follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: Most pelvic insufficiency fractures presented with new-onset pelvic or sacral pain within 2 years of completing chemoradiotherapy. The lack of clinical or dosimetric predictors suggests a multifactorial etiology of fracture risk. Persistent pain, despite multimodal supportive care, led to long-term morbidity. These findings underscore the need for prospective studies to develop evidence-based preventive strategies, survivorship assessments, and management pathways.

articles.title: Interim Analysis of a Phase 3 Trial of Povetacicept in IgA Nephropathy.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: B-cell activating factor (BAFF) and a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL) have distinct roles in IgA-producing B-cell populations and appear to be central to the pathogenesis of IgA nephropathy. Povetacicept, an enhanced, variant transmembrane activator and calcium-modulator and cyclophilin-ligand interactor (TACI)-Fc fragment fusion therapeutic, is engineered for dual inhibition of BAFF and APRIL.

METHODS: In this ongoing, phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, participants with biopsy-proven IgA nephropathy receiving stable background therapy were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive povetacicept at a dose of 80 mg or placebo subcutaneously every 4 weeks. The primary end point of this prespecified interim analysis was the change in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at week 36. Secondary end points were the change at week 36 in galactose-deficient IgA1 levels and hematuria resolution at week 36 among participants with baseline hematuria.

RESULTS: A total of 557 participants received povetacicept (372 participants) or placebo (185 participants). Efficacy analyses included the first 199 participants who had undergone randomization (131 in the povetacicept group and 68 in the placebo group). The 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio decreased by 52.0% with povetacicept and by 4.3% with placebo by week 36 (adjusted difference, -49.8 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -58.6 to -39.2; P<0.001). Galactose-deficient IgA1 levels decreased by 77.4% with povetacicept and increased by 9.1% with placebo (adjusted difference, -79.3 percentage points; 95% CI, -82.2 to -75.9; P<0.001). Among the participants with baseline hematuria, resolution occurred in 85% with povetacicept and in 23% with placebo (adjusted difference, 62 percentage points; 95% CI, 45 to 78; P<0.001). The incidence of adverse events (75% with povetacicept and 78% with placebo) and serious adverse events (3% and 4%, respectively) were similar in the trial groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Povetacicept led to a significantly greater reduction in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo by week 36 in participants with IgA nephropathy. (Funded by Vertex Pharmaceuticals; RAINIER AIS-D08 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06564142.).

articles.title: Sequential therapy with anlotinib and radioiodine for distant metastatic differentiated thyroid cancer: a phase II clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radioiodine (RAI) alone exhibited limited efficacy in distant metastatic differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC). We hypothesized that pretreatment with anlotinib, a potent antiangiogenic tyrosine kinase inhibitor, would reduce tumor burden and improve therapeutic response.

METHODS: This prospective, single-arm phase II trial enrolled patients with measurable distant metastatic DTC. All patients received anlotinib 12 mg/day orally for 12 weeks. After confirmation of RAI-avid target lesions on diagnostic 131I-WBS, patients were treated with 7.4 GBq RAI and followed up for another 12 weeks. Sequential therapy continued until no effect of RAI could be anticipated. Primary endpoints were objective response rate (ORR) and safety. Registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2100045178; https://www.chictr.org.cn).

RESULTS: 24 patients were enrolled. 14 (58%) were excluded due to non-RAI-avid target lesions; 10 (42%) with RAI-avid lesions received sequential therapy (median, 4.5 cycles). ORR was 60% (all partial responses), disease control rate 100%. With median follow-up 34.5 months, no disease progression or death occurred. In the subgroup of 8 patients with bone target lesions, ORR was 50%. Grade 3 anlotinib-related adverse events occurred in 30% of patients; no grade 4/5 toxicities or grade ≥2 RAI-related events were observed.

CONCLUSION: Sequential anlotinib followed by RAI therapy demonstrated promising antitumor activity (ORR 60%) and favorable safety in RAI-avid distant metastatic DTC, particularly in bone metastases. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in a randomized trial with an RAI monotherapy control arm.

articles.title: The lung tells eosinophils who to become.
Identifying the Content and Pedagogical Practices Used by Educators Teaching Stuttering and Cluttering Modules.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Research has demonstrated that many speech-language pathologists (SLPs) have reported having reduced knowledge and competence in the assessment and intervention of children and adults who stutter and clutter. One potential reason for this is embedded in a suboptimal educational foundation at a university level.

PURPOSE: This study aimed to identify the content taught and the pedagogical practices used by speech-language pathology educators teaching a module on stuttering and cluttering as part of an undergraduate or postgraduate program in speech-language pathology.

METHOD: An online survey was developed by the authors, and questions reflected the All Ireland Society for Higher Education (AISHE) model for module design. Participants were recruited in Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, and the United States. Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics. Participants' qualitative responses were analyzed using inductive content analysis.

RESULTS: Eighty-six educators completed the survey. Descriptive data, including qualitative findings, were reported on the seven components of the AISHE model. Self-reported expertise in stuttering or cluttering was associated with greater amount of teaching content (p = .018). Participants reported teaching significantly more about stuttering than cluttering (p < .001).

CONCLUSIONS: This study identified the range of content and pedagogical practices used by educators delivering stuttering and cluttering modules. Results highlighted that educators with expertise in stuttering and/or cluttering taught a higher number of content areas.

SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL: https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.34556784.

articles.title: A Comparison of Simulation Modalities to Train Graduate-Level Clinical Reasoning for Clinical Swallow Evaluation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Changes in graduate-level clinical reasoning for clinical swallow evaluation were examined and compared between video simulation and standardized patient simulation training. The purpose of this study was to provide information for speech-language pathology programs to consider when integrating simulation for clinical reasoning for clinical swallow evaluation within the graduate-level curriculum to support intentional, evidence-based use of academic resources for teaching and learning.

METHOD: A randomized pretest/posttest mixed-methods design was implemented to compare a video simulation training group and a standardized patient simulation training group. Stratified randomization was used to assign first-year graduate speech-language pathology students to either a video simulation (n = 15) or standardized patient simulation (n = 15) group. Before and after participating in either video simulation or standardized patient simulation, participants completed concept maps to evaluate changes in cognitive schema development for clinical reasoning and clinical vignettes to evaluate changes in clinical reasoning within a novel written case. Participants rated the design of their assigned simulation modality following the simulation using the National League for Nursing Simulation Design Scale (SDS; Student Version). Participants also provided qualitative responses to question prompts based on the Lasater Clinical Judgment Rubric following the simulation to detail clinical reasoning that was employed during the simulation.

RESULTS: There were no significant differences in total scores between groups for concept maps, clinical vignettes, and SDS. Within-group differences demonstrated a significant gain from pretest to posttest for concept map performance for both groups. Qualitative analysis of participant responses yielded insight into group differences in clinical reasoning development, with qualitative analysis suggesting that video simulation-based learning aligned more closely with participants' level of experience.

CONCLUSIONS: Both video simulation and standardized patient simulation were effective for training clinical reasoning. Video simulation may be particularly appropriate for novice learners. Given the cost of high-fidelity simulation, video simulation may be beneficial to consider for contextualized learning at the novice level followed by standardized patient simulation as students gain experience.

articles.title: Organotypic vascularization improves maturation of human stem cell-derived islets and restores normoglycemia in diabetic mice.
articles.abstract: Human pluripotent stem cells-derived pancreatic islet organoids (PIOs) hold promise for treating type 1 diabetes, but poor post-transplant survival due to inadequate vascularization remains a major challenge. Here, we generated vascularized PIOs (VPIOs) by co-culturing PIOs with blood vessel organoids (BVOs), resulting in integrated structures with BVOs-derived capillary networks that penetrate into the islet structures. These blood vessels structurally exhibit fenestrations characteristic of islet-specific endothelium and carry a molecular signature of organotypic vasculature. β cells within the VPIOs display partially enhanced maturation and greater resistance to hypoxia and endoplasmic reticulum stress. Following subcutaneous transplantation into diabetic mice, VPIOs exhibit markedly improved survival, establish vascular connections with the host circulation, and restore long-term normoglycemia. Our work presents a strategy for generating vascularized islet organoids that enhances β cell maturation and tissue-specific blood vessel specification in vitro and, critically, improves graft survival and function in vivo.

articles.title: Dual-mechanism adjuvant catharanthine restores β-lactam efficacy against Staphylococcus aureus infections.
articles.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) remains a major global health threat with high mortality, causing both community-associated and hospital-acquired infections. Consequently, resistance mechanisms, notably β-lactamase production and biofilm formation, are considered promising therapeutic targets. In this study, Catharanthine, a plant-derived alkaloid extracted from Catharanthus roseus (Madagascar periwinkle), is a potent adjuvant that restores the efficacy of β-lactam antibiotics against S. aureus. This study aimed to investigate resistance mechanisms, notably β-lactamase production and biofilm formation, which are considered promising therapeutic targets. Molecular docking was performed to evaluate the binding interaction between catharanthine and β-lactamase. Metabolomic analysis was used to investigate the effect of catharanthine on bacterial metabolic pathways, particularly those associated with biofilm formation. In addition, murine models of S. aureus pneumonia and skin infection were established to assess the therapeutic efficacy of combination treatment with catharanthine and cefixime in vivo. Catharanthine showed high-affinity binding to β-lactamase in molecular docking analysis, supporting its potential role as a β-lactam antibiotic adjuvant. Metabolomic profiling revealed that catharanthine perturbed glutamate-associated amino acid metabolism involving the arginine biosynthetic network, thereby impairing biofilm development. In vivo, combination therapy with catharanthine and cefixime effectively alleviated infection in murine models of S. aureus pneumonia and skin infection. This study demonstrates that catharanthine enhances the therapeutic efficacy of β-lactam antibiotics through dual targeting of β-lactamase-associated resistance and biofilm formation. These findings identify catharanthine as a promising preclinical β-lactam adjuvant candidate and support further pharmacological and translational evaluation against MRSA infections.

articles.title: Riluzole attenuates staphyloxanthin biosynthesis and biofilm formation in Staphylococcus aureus.
articles.abstract: The rapid emergence and dissemination of antibiotic resistance in Staphylococcus aureus, especially methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA), pose a major global health challenge and call for alternative therapeutic strategies. S. aureus uses staphyloxanthin (STX) and biofilm as complementary virulence-associated traits that promote immune evasion and persistence at infection sites. STX protects bacteria from reactive oxygen species, while biofilms provide a structured barrier that enhances tolerance to host and antimicrobial stress. Targeting these traits may offer a non-bactericidal strategy for infection control. Here, we identified riluzole as an inhibitor of carotenoid production at non-growth-inhibitory concentrations (IC50 = 34.76 μg/mL) and enhances the susceptibility of S. aureus to immune cell killing. Mechanistically, riluzole interacted with CrtN (KD = 48.6 μM) and reduced its enzymatic activity, while transcriptomic analyses revealed broader transcriptional remodeling associated with reduced expression of several STX biosynthetic genes. In addition, riluzole induced membrane-associated physiological stress, including increased membrane permeability, altered membrane fluidity, ATP depletion, enhanced colistin susceptibility, and inhibition of biofilm formation. Riluzole also attenuated Pseudomonas aeruginosa-associated stimulation of S. aureus pigmentation and oxidative-stress protection. In a murine skin infection model, riluzole promoted bacterial clearance and was associated with improved wound repair. Collectively, these findings substantiate the anti-virulence properties of riluzole against S. aureus, and provide a rationale for its further development as a novel therapeutic strategy for MRSA infections.

articles.title: Radiosynthesis and preliminary evaluation of [11C] and [18F] labelled lacosamide scaffolds for brain PET imaging.
articles.abstract: This study summarizes the automated, transition-metal-free radiosynthesis approach for producing [11C]LCM and its bioisosteric analogue [18F]FLCM, along with preliminary pharmacological and preclinical evaluations of these radiotracers can act as potent brain imaging radiotracer candidates. Radiosynthesis was carried out using an automated synthesis module targeting the terminal 3-oxy site of lacosamide. Physicochemical properties, including hydrophilic behavior and plasma-protein binding profile, were evaluated. Translational validation was performed via in vivo PET/CT imaging and ex vivo biodistribution in healthy Wistar rats. The synthesis module yielded a radiotracer with high radiochemical yield and radiochemical purity. Specific activity was determined to be ~21 .7GBq/μmol for [11C]LCM and ~6.76 GBq/μmole for [18F]FLCM. Both radiotracers show favorable hydrophilic and low PPB profiles. In vivo PET scan and ex vivo study confirmed the brain uptake, renal and hepatic clearance, and minimal off-target uptake. The favorable pharmaceutical profiles establish a promising baseline, further rigorous in vitro receptor-affinity assays and dynamic brain imaging in an animal model are required to validate the translational diagnostic utility of these radiotracers.

articles.title: Trends in Inflation-Adjusted Pharmacotherapy Costs and Cardiovascular Risk Factor Management in Type 2 Diabetes: A 26-Year Study from Tertiary Diabetes Cen​​​​tres in Greece ​​​.
articles.journal: Experimental and clinical endocrinology & diabetes : official journal, German Society of Endocrinology [and] German Diabetes Association
articles.abstract:
AIM: We evaluated long-term trends in pharmacotherapy costs and cardiovascular risk factor target achievement among people with type 2 diabetes attending tertiary diabetes centres in Greece.

METHODS: This periodic, multicenter, cross-sectional study analysed data from 4,963 people with type 2 diabetes attending three diabetes centres at specific time points: 1998, 2006, 2012, 2018, and 2024. We compared glycated haemoglobin, systolic blood pressure, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and body mass index and the achievement of individual cardiovascular risk factor targets (glycated haemoglobin: < 7%, systolic blood pressure: < 140 mm Hg, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol: < 100 mg/dL) and all three targets simultaneously. Annual pharmacotherapy costs were compared using inflation-adjusted values.

RESULTS: Simultaneous achievement of all three cardiovascular risk factor targets increased from 0.6% in 1998 to 29.1% in 2024. Individual target achievements improved: glycated haemoglobin from 29.4 to 58.6%, systolic blood pressure from 45.3 to 62.5%, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol from 6.3 to 73.4%. Mean low-density lipoprotein cholesterol showed the greatest reduction from 128.4 to 79.0 mg/dL. Median body mass index increased until 2018 and then declined in 2024. Total pharmacotherapy costs per patient rose from €341 in 1998 to €1,609 in 2024, primarily due to glucose-lowering therapies (€167-€1,257).

CONCLUSION: Over 26 years, people with type 2 diabetes attending tertiary diabetes centres in Greece demonstrated improvements in cardiovascular risk factor target achievement, alongside rising pharmacotherapy costs, primarily driven by glucose-lowering therapies.

articles.title: Glyco-transformed Gynostemma pentaphyllum extract ameliorates MAFLD by regulating BCAA homeostasis.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) has become a highly prevalent chronic metabolic disease worldwide. Current clinical drugs are limited by poor long-term efficacy, potential safety risks and high costs. As a popular daily beverage, Gynostemma pentaphyllum exerts prominent hepatoprotective, lipid-regulating and hypoglycemic activities, making it a promising natural agent for MAFLD intervention. In this study, we prepared high-activity secondary gypenosides via snailase-mediated biotransformation, and explored their anti-MAFLD mechanisms through integrated multi-omics analysis and pharmacological validation. The results revealed that snailase efficiently converted primary gypenosides into rare secondary derivatives. Compared with the crude gypenosides from Gynostemma pentaphyllum extract (GYP), the transformed product SGYP exhibited stronger dose-dependent lipid-regulating and anti-inflammatory effects, and effectively alleviated MAFLD-related pathological lesions in mice. Mechanistic investigations demonstrated that SGYP ameliorated high-fat-diet-induced excessive accumulation of branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) in the liver and activated the hepatic AMPK and AKT signaling pathways. Further exogenous BCAA supplementation experiments confirmed that restoring hepatic BCAA homeostasis served as the core mechanism underlying the anti-MAFLD action of SGYP. This study provides an innovative processing technology for the preparation of high-value Gynostemma pentaphyllum products featuring strengthened lipid-lowering, anti-inflammatory activities and prominent hepatoprotective effects.

articles.title: A phase 2 study of tipifarnib in children and young adults with tumors harboring HRAS genomic alterations: NCI-COG Pediatric MATCH trial (APEC1621M).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: APEC1621 arm M, a subprotocol of the NCI-COG Pediatric MATCH clinical trial, is a phase 2 study evaluating tipifarnib, a farnesyl transferase inhibitor, in patients with relapsed or refractory solid tumors harboring HRAS mutations at codons G12, G13, Q61, or A146 (NCT04284774).

METHODS: Patients identified by the MATCH screening protocol and enrolled to the arm M subprotocol received tipifarnib at 350 mg/m2/dose (maximum 600 mg/dose) orally twice daily on an intermittent dosing schedule (days 1-7 and 15-21, every 28 days) until disease progression or intolerable toxicity. The primary aim was to determine the objective response rate (ORR), and secondary objectives included estimating progression-free survival (PFS) and assessing the tolerability of tipifarnib on the intermittent dosing schedule in children.

RESULTS: Seven patients matched to the tipifarnib subprotocol and five patients (71%) enrolled. Two matched patients were ineligible for treatment. Diagnoses for the enrolled patients were rhabdomyosarcoma (n = 4) and angiosarcoma (n = 1). HRAS mutations identified in those tumors included G13R (n = 2) and G12S, G12C, and Q61L (n = 1 each). Treatment was associated with grade 1/2 adverse events (AE) consistent with those expected from prior studies. Grade 3 or higher AEs on treatment were disease progression, dyspnea, and pleural effusion, not related to protocol therapy. One patient had stable disease (SD) at the end of cycle 2 and remained on protocol therapy for 4 cycles. There were no objective responses (OR).

CONCLUSIONS: This US cooperative group study was successful at identifying pediatric patients with tumors that harbored oncogenic mutations in HRAS. The frequency of the mutations identified and patients enrolled was lower than anticipated, and the study closed before accrual was complete. The adverse effect profile of tipifarnib in pediatric patients on the intermittent dosing schedule was acceptable. Limited single-agent efficacy of tipifarnib was observed in this biomarker-selected cohort of refractory pediatric tumors.

articles.title: Development of a Multimodal Assessment of Mastication Protocol.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Within the field of speech-language pathology, the only validated noninstrumental assessment of mastication is the Test of Mastication and Swallowing Solids. This assessment protocol offers limited applicability and ecological validity, as it does not reflect typical meals, which involve greater volume and varied textures. Recognizing the need for a more comprehensive evaluation of mastication, this study aims to develop and evaluate a novel assessment protocol of the oral preparatory phase in healthy participants with typical chewing/swallowing. This protocol includes literature-based measures of masticatory parameters, a color-changing gum, and motion analysis.

METHOD: Using a within-subject design, 50 participants chewed a color-changing gum that was analyzed using Commission Internationale de l'Eclairage L*a*b* (CIELAB) values. Participants chewed a baby carrot, a shortbread cookie, and a Hi-Chew candy. The number of chews was manually counted and further measured using two-dimensional motion analysis. Participants completed a social validity questionnaire evaluating the assessment protocol. CIELAB values were correlated with masticatory parameters using Pearson's r. Agreement between manually counted and motion analysis data was examined using intraclass correlation coefficients. Descriptive statistics were analyzed from Likert scale responses on the social validity questionnaire.

RESULTS: Mean CIELAB values reflected existing normative data; however, no significant correlation was observed between colorimetric data and masticatory parameters. The accuracy of two-dimensional motion analysis varied by texture. Chews for the carrot demonstrated the highest reliability, chews for the Hi-Chew candy had moderate reliability, and chews for the shortbread cookie had the lowest reliability. Participants rated the protocol favorably, emphasizing value in the assessment battery rather than individual components.

CONCLUSIONS: Findings provide preliminary evidence in support of a multidimensional evaluation of mastication. Nonsignificant correlations between masticatory parameters and gum outcomes suggest that each captures distinct aspects of mastication. Two-dimensional motion analysis shows promise for semi-automated chew counting, though further refinement is needed for broader texture applications. Overall, positive participant perceptions support continued exploration of the assessment protocol in clinical populations.

SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL: https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.34033494.

articles.title: Beyond the Acute Phase: Prevalence and Clinical Characteristics of Unreported Swallowing Impairments in Ambulatory Outpatient Stroke Survivors.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Unreported dysphagia, imaging-identified swallowing impairment without symptom reporting, remains poorly characterized beyond the acute phase of stroke. This study aimed to (a) quantify the point prevalence of unreported dysphagia in ambulatory stroke survivors, (b) examine demographic and clinical factors associated with the presentation of this phenomenon, and (c) evaluate concordance between patient-reported symptoms and imaging-derived impairments.

METHOD: This retrospective secondary analysis included 45 ambulatory adults ≥ 3 months post-ischemic stroke who underwent videofluoroscopic swallow study and completed the Eating Assessment Tool-10 (EAT-10). Swallowing impairment was defined using the Dynamic Imaging Grade of Swallowing Toxicity (DIGEST Grade ≥ 1), and physiology was characterized using the Modified Barium Swallow Impairment Profile (MBSImP). Participants were classified as having no dysphagia (DIGEST = 0), overt dysphagia (DIGEST ≥ 1 and EAT-10 > 3), or unreported dysphagia (DIGEST ≥ 1 and EAT-10 ≤ 3). Group differences were examined using analysis of variance, Fisher's exact tests, and nonparametric analyses.

RESULTS: Sixteen percent (7/45) of participants demonstrated unreported dysphagia, while 44% (20/45) exhibited some degree of swallowing impairment. Unreported and overt dysphagia groups had similar DIGEST grades, yet the unreported dysphagia group reported minimal symptom burden (EAT-10: Mdn = 2) compared to the overt group (EAT-10: Mdn = 9). Significant correlations were observed between the EAT-10 and the MBSImP oral total (r = .510, p < .008), but not DIGEST (r = .21, p = .163). Age, lesion characteristics, time since stroke, and admission stroke severity were not significantly associated with unreported dysphagia.

CONCLUSIONS: A clinically meaningful proportion of ambulatory, community-dwelling stroke survivors demonstrated persistent swallowing impairment without symptom reporting. Reliance on symptom-based referral pathways may fail to detect ongoing safety or efficiency deficits. These findings support the consideration of imaging-based surveillance strategies beyond the acute phase of stroke recovery.

articles.title: Chronic inflammation and multiple dimensions of aging among women in the Philippines.
articles.journal: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
articles.abstract: Age-related increases in chronic systemic inflammation are strong predictors of morbidity and mortality in high-income countries, but evidence is lacking from lower- and middle-income settings where infectious diseases are more prevalent, and rates of overweight and obesity are relatively low. Here we evaluate 2 complementary measures of chronic inflammation-plasma C-reactive protein (CRP) and a DNA methylation-based surrogate (DNAm-CRP)-measured at baseline as predictors of physical capacity, cognitive function, and cardiometabolic disease 7 years later among women in the Philippines (N = 953; 43-75 years at follow-up). Levels of CRP and DNAm-CRP were not strongly associated with age. Both measures predicted subsequent declines in physical and functional capacity, increased incidence of diabetes and hypertension, and poorer cognitive performance, after adjustment for baseline status and other covariates. DNAm-CRP performed comparably to CRP and was robust to variation in white blood cell composition and acute infectious symptoms at the time of sampling. These findings demonstrate that chronic inflammation is associated with multiple dimensions of aging in a lower-middle-income setting, and highlight the utility of inflammatory biomarkers as scalable tools for global aging research.

articles.title: Hypomorphic IDUA genotypes are associated with retinitis pigmentosa in individuals without syndromic mucopolysaccharidosis type I.
articles.abstract: Bi-allelic variants in IDUA classically cause mucopolysaccharidosis type I (MPS I), a multisystem lysosomal storage disorder. This study describes 14 individuals from 12 families presenting with retinitis pigmentosa, later attributed to bi-allelic IDUA genotypes. Notably, seven individuals, despite comprehensive systemic assessments, showed no features consistent with MPS I at last assessment (aged 46-73 years). Leukocyte α-L-iduronidase activity was reduced but not abolished across all individuals assessed (n = 9), supporting a shared mechanistic basis for the mild, retina-predominant, or exclusively retinal phenotype. No individual carried bi-allelic null genotypes; most had a loss-of-function allele paired with a missense variant, consistent with an overall hypomorphic genotype. Variant-level functional assays, using a cell-based expression platform assessing enzyme activity and protein abundance to derive relative specific activity (RSA), showed that several missense alleles confer very low residual activity and/or impaired abundance/processing, with RSA typically in the ∼0.5%-1.5% range. The recurrent missense c.298A>G (p.Arg100Gly) variant showed no protein or catalytic effect; targeted long-read transcript analysis instead demonstrated predominant loss-of-function mis-splicing with a small fraction of correctly spliced transcript (∼1%-2%), explaining residual activity in vivo. Together, these data expand the phenotypic spectrum of IDUA-associated disease to include late-onset retinal-predominant or apparently isolated retinitis pigmentosa and indicate that residual enzyme activity likely contributes to systemic sparing, highlighting the value of integrated genomic, biochemical, and functional analyses to advance understanding in attenuated metabolic disease.

articles.title: A call for action with the burden of cirrhosis in Australia.
articles.journal: Australian health review : a publication of the Australian Hospital Association
articles.abstract: Unlike most other chronic diseases and cancers in Australia, outcomes for cirrhosis and hepatocellular cancer are not improving. Public hospitals are overwhelmed by decompensated cirrhosis and struggling to provide best practice care for the large population of patients with less severe (compensated) cirrhosis. Adding to this dysfunction is a lack of education and support for the primary care workforce. To improve the current care for patients with cirrhosis, we must recognise the current poor outcomes and develop appropriate policy responses, including increasing workforce capacity via training of the primary care workforce and establishment of shared care models.

articles.title: Guaianolide-type sesquiterpenes from Rhaponticum repens (L.) Hidalgo with anti-ischemic stroke activity.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) is a severe central nervous system disorder with high mortality and disability rates, and microglia-mediated neuroinflammation exacerbates ischemic brain injury. In this study, the traditional ethnic medicine Rhaponticum repens (L.) Hidalgo was found to significantly inhibit lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced microglial overactivation and to alleviate cerebral injury in middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) rats, suggesting its therapeutic potential against IS. Bioactivity-guided fractionation of its active fraction led to the isolation and identification of 44 compounds, including 22 guaianolide-type sesquiterpenes (1-22) and 22 other types (23-44), among which five were previously undescribed compounds (1-5). Activity screening revealed that most of the guaianolide-type sesquiterpenes markedly suppressed microglial overactivation, representing the principal pharmacologically active constituents responsible for the anti-neuroinflammatory effects of this plant. High-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) analysis further indicated that cynaropikrin (8), the most active compound (IC₅₀ = 3.8 μM), was the most abundant component in the active fraction, accounting for approximately 14.39% of its content. In vivo experiments confirmed that cynaropikrin at a dose of 5 mg/kg attenuated cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury in MCAO/R rats, and acute toxicity tests demonstrated its favorable in vivo safety profile. Target prediction, molecular docking, drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS) and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) analyses indicate that cynaropikrin directly targets NLRP3. Western blot analysis further shows that cynaropikrin reduces NLRP3 protein expression, caspase-1 activation and IL-1β maturation, thereby alleviating neuroinflammation and cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.

articles.title: Inhibition of miR-125b-1-3p alleviates acute kidney injury and mitochondrial membrane potential loss by targeting GSTK1.
articles.abstract: As a type of regulated necrosis driven by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation, ferroptosis critically contributes to acute kidney injury (AKI). Currently, whether miR-125b-1-3p is engaged in this pathological process remains unknown. Here, miR-125b-1-3p was upregulated in kidney tissues from an AKI model (GSE125305), in serum from a small exploratory cohort (15 AKI patients vs 15 controls), and in hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R)-treated NRK-52E cells and erastin-induced ferroptosis models (n = 3). Suppression of miR-125b-1-3p with an inhibitor attenuated H/R-induced cellular injury and ferroptosis-associated markers, reflected by enhanced cell viability, upregulated GPX4 expression, and decreased levels of MDA, Fe2+, and ROS. Furthermore, ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1) improved cell viability and reduced MDA and Fe2+, mitigating miR-125b-1-3p mimic-induced injury under H/R. In an ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) mouse model (n = 5/group), miR-125b-1-3p inhibition ameliorated acute kidney injury and associated ferroptosis markers, indicated by reduced serum creatinine and BUN, lower tubular injury scores, and attenuation of ferroptosis-related alterations. Mechanistically, bioinformatics and luciferase assays revealed that miR-125b-1-3p directly targets glutathione S-transferase kappa 1 (GSTK1). Circulating GSTK1 mRNA were reduced in AKI patient serum, and GSTK1 expression was decreased in H/R-treated cells, negatively correlating with miR-125b-1-3p. Overexpression of miR-125b-1-3p reduced GSTK1 protein, while inhibition increased it. Importantly, GSTK1 overexpression attenuated miR-125b-1-3p mimic-induced ferroptosis-associated alterations and mitochondrial membrane potential loss in H/R-treated cells, whereas GSTK1 knockdown blunted the protective effects of miR-125b-1-3p inhibition, restoring MDA and Fe2+ accumulation. Our data indicate that miR-125b-1-3p contributes to ferroptosis-associated tubular cell injury partly by targeting GSTK1, highlighting the miR-125b-1-3p/GSTK1 axis as a candidate regulatory pathway involved in AKI.

articles.title: Orally administered chondroitin sulfate oligosaccharides attenuate hypertension via multiple protective pathways, including Hmox1-mediated antioxidant responses.
articles.abstract: Chondroitin sulfate (CS) is a sulfated glycosaminoglycan with various physiological functions. We previously prepared a mixture of chondroitin sulfate oligosaccharides (CSOS) derived from skate cartilage and evaluated its absorption in humans using urinary CS excretion as an indicator. The results suggested that CSOS is absorbed more efficiently than intact high-molecular-weight CS (HMwCS).
