Median follow-up was 76 months. Three hundred fourteen patients were FLT3-wild-type (WT); 116 had FLT3 mutations. The primary end point, overall survival (OS) unselected by FLT3 status, showed no significant benefit, and there was a significant increase in non-relapse mortality with quizartinib. In a pre-planned subgroup analysis, patients with FLT3 mutations who received quizartinib had significantly improved OS (Hazard Ratio, 0.59; 95% Confidence Interval, 0.37-0.93; P = .024) due to reduced relapse risk, with greater benefit in the short quizartinib group. In patients with FLT3-WT, there was no survival benefit and no reduction in relapse risk. No significant differences were observed in time to hematologic count recovery or in length of hospitalization. The most observed grade 3/4 adverse events were febrile neutropenia. In conclusion, the addition of quizartinib to intensive chemotherapy, delayed until chemotherapy course 2, prolonged OS in older patients with FLT3-mutated AML but did not improve OS in non-FLT3-selected patients. This trial was registered at www.isrctn.com as ISRCTN-31682779 and at www.clinicaltrialsregister.eu as EudraCR-2013-002730-21.

articles.title: Discovery and optimization of diarylsulfone-based dual M3-Antagonists and β2-Agonists (MABAs) as inhaled bronchodilators.
articles.abstract: Dual muscarinic antagonists and β2-agonists (MABAs) represent a promising therapeutic class for the treatment of asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). We report the discovery and optimization of MABAs by integrating a diarylsulfone scaffold with the hydroxyquinoline moiety of indacaterol 2 to achieve dual M3 and β2 activity. Through SAR studies to optimize the linker design and M3-targeting features, a novel MABA series was realized with excellent affinity at M3/β2 receptors. Lead compounds 150 and 160 showed high-affinity and long-lived binding to M3 (Ki: 1.95 nM and 1.75 nM, respectively, at 24 h) and subnanomolar β2-agonist potency, along with excellent (EC50 < 10 nM) smooth muscle relaxant activity in carbachol-stimulated guinea pig trachea rings. Moreover, after intratracheal administration, both compounds exhibited sustained in vivo bronchoprotection for 24 h in the modified Einthoven model of acute bronchoconstriction, with equivalent efficacy to the clinical-stage MABA batefenterol 9. Further development of these compounds is warranted as inhaled bronchodilators.

articles.title: Targeting bacterial adhesion: Recent advances and therapeutic potential of FimH and PapG inhibitors against Escherichia coli infection.
articles.abstract: The widespread use and abuse of antibiotics have led to an increase in antibiotic resistance, and new methods and approaches are needed to combat bacterial infections. One promising alternative is to intervene early stage in the infection process. Adhesion is a prerequisite for bacteria to colonize on the cell surface. Various pathogenic Escherichia coli strains utilize carbohydrate-specific lectins to bind to specific glycoconjugate receptors on host cells for cell adhesion. The most important and best-studied bacterial lectins are FimH and PapG. Therefore, blocking the adhesion of bacteria to cells mediated by FimH and PapG through high-affinity carbohydrate antagonists is an extremely attractive therapeutic target. This paper systematically reviews the research progress of FimH and PapG inhibitors over the past two decades. For FimH-targeted mannoside antagonists, we elaborate the effects of glycosidic linkage types, aromatic substituent modification, conformational rigidification and multivalent structural design on binding affinity, metabolic stability and in vivo performance. Meanwhile, we outline the research framework of high-affinity PapG inhibitors based on galactose scaffolds. Classical optimization strategies, including terminal aromatic group modification, selective hydroxyl substitution and hydrophobic moiety incorporation, can effectively improve the binding affinity and isoform selectivity of PapG ligands. In addition, multivalent modification acts as a universally effective strategy for both FimH and PapG inhibitors. Furthermore, we prospect the rational design directions of anti-adhesive agents in the future, providing systematic theoretical reference and practical guidance for the subsequent structural optimization, pharmacological evaluation and clinical translation of FimH and PapG inhibitors.

articles.title: Elevated serum miR-19a-3p serves as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for ischemic stroke and aggravates neuronal injury by targeting PTEN.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke (IS) is a leading cause of disability and death worldwide. Its diagnosis and prognosis still rely heavily on neuroimaging, highlighting the urgent need for reliable blood-based biomarkers that can facilitate early detection and outcome prediction. MicroRNA-19a-3p (miR-19a-3p) has been implicated in vascular pathology and neuronal injury. Still, its clinical utility as a biomarker for IS and its precise mechanistic role in post-ischemic neuronal damage remain incompletely defined.

METHODS: Serum miR-19a-3p was quantified via qRT-PCR in 98 IS patients and 60 controls. Diagnostic accuracy was assessed via ROC curve analysis. Prognostic value for 90-day outcomes (mRS > 2) was evaluated using multivariate logistic regression. In vitro, an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) model was established in PC12 cells. Cell viability, apoptosis, inflammatory cytokines, and oxidative stress were measured following modulation of miR-19a-3p. Interaction with PTEN was validated by dual-luciferase reporter assay.

RESULTS: Serum miR-19a-3p was significantly elevated in IS patients and demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy with an AUC of 0.9213. Furthermore, its high expression was an independent risk factor for a poor 90-day functional outcome. In an in vitro OGD/R model, miR-19a-3p expression was similarly upregulated, and its inhibition conferred neuroprotection by enhancing viability, reducing apoptosis, and mitigating oxidative stress and inflammation. Conversely, miR-19a-3p overexpression exacerbated these injury phenotypes. Mechanistically, we confirmed that miR-19a-3p directly targets and inhibits PTEN expression via binding to its 3'UTR.

CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that serum miR-19a-3p may represent a potentialnovel biomarker for diagnosing ischemic stroke and predicting patient outcomes. Mechanistically, it exacerbates brain injury by targeting PTEN, making the miR-19a-3p/PTEN axis may be a promising therapeutic target.

articles.title: Genetic variants of thioredoxin interacting protein gene and their association with diabetic peripheral neuropathy in type 2 diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To investigate the association between genetic variants of the thioredoxin interacting protein (TXNIP) gene and diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).

METHODS: A total of 239 T2DM patients (144 in the DPN group and 95 in the T2DM-only group) and 283 healthy controls (NC group) were enrolled. Polymorphisms of TXNIP gene loci (rs7211, rs7212, rs4755, and rs9245) were analyzed.

RESULTS: The DPN group exhibited significantly higher frequencies of the AA genotype and A allele at the rs7211 locus compared to both the NC and T2DM groups (all P < 0.05). Similarly, the CC genotype and C allele at the rs7212 locus were more prevalent in the DPN group (all P < 0.05). Logistic regression analysis identified the AA genotype at rs7211 and the CC genotype at rs7212 as independent risk factors for DPN (all P < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Polymorphisms at TXNIP rs7211 and rs7212 loci may contribute to genetic susceptibility to DPN in T2DM.

articles.title: Efficacy of video-based resources for educating young people with chronic long-term conditions: a literature review.
articles.abstract: The UK has among the highest mortality rates in Europe for young people with asthma, with inadequate patient education cited as a contributing factor. This literature review aimed to explore the efficacy of video-based resources for educating young people about their chronic long-term condition. Ten studies were reviewed, most of which were randomised controlled trials, and seven of which were conducted in outpatient settings in the US by the same research collaborative. The findings show that, although video-based educational interventions improved participants' knowledge about their condition, these were not superior to other educational approaches. Further, no consistent improvement in medicine adherence, disease control or quality of life was demonstrated. Video-based education for young people appears to be most effective when used to support healthcare professional-led education rather than as a standalone intervention. Nurses and other healthcare professionals should incorporate structured education into consultations with young people and use a range of resources to ensure that their differing needs are met.

articles.title: Natural History of Bone Formation following Venous Sinus Stenting.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Venous sinus stent placement has emerged as a potential effective treatment for pulsatile tinnitus (PT) and idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) secondary to venous sinus stenosis. Bone formation adjacent to the stent has been described in isolated case reports, but it has remained underexplored. This study aimed to characterize bone formation following venous sinus stent placement.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective observational study included consecutive patients who underwent venous sinus stent placement for PT and/or IIH. Bone formation was assessed at each follow-up time point. Comparisons between patients with and without bone formation were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test for continuous variables and Fisher exact test for categoric variables. Univariate logistic regression was used to identify predictors of bone formation.

RESULTS: Twenty-one patients were included. Bone formation was observed in 12 (57%) patients at 3 months and 14 (67%) patients at 12 months. Patients with bone formation had a significantly greater maximum incomplete stent apposition compared with those without (median 1.9 mm [interquartile range {IQR}: 1.4-3.0] vs 0.9 mm [IQR: 0.6-1.5]; P = .03). On logistic regression, each millimeter increase in maximum incomplete stent apposition was associated with 3.72-fold higher odds of bone formation (95% CI, 0.95-14.50; P = .06). Symptom resolution at 12 months was similar between patients with and without bone formation (71% vs 86%; P = .62).

CONCLUSIONS: Bone formation following venous sinus stent placement is common, affecting two-thirds of patients at 12 months, and was not associated with worse symptom resolution at 12 months, although longer follow-up is needed to characterize its long-term implications. Incomplete stent apposition could be associated with increased bone formation; however, this warrants confirmation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: North-South Disparities in Multimorbidity Revealed by Association Rule and Sequential Pattern Mining: Evidence From the China National Health Survey (CNHS).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: North-south differences in context and lifestyle may shape multimorbidity patterns in China. We compared multimorbidity between two northern (Liaoning, Jilin) and two southern (Guangdong, Jiangsu) CNHS provinces in eastern China using association rule mining (ARM) and sequential pattern mining (SPM).

METHODS: We analyzed 19,067 adults (≥20 years) and 20 chronic conditions. ARM identified co-occurrence rules and reported support (proportion with the combination), confidence (P(consequent|antecedent)), and lift (observed/expected co-occurrence; >1 indicates positive association). SPM summarized common diagnosis-order sequences using sequence support (percentage of participants exhibiting an ordered sequence). Sensitivity analyses were restricted to self-reported physician diagnoses.

RESULTS: Multimorbidity prevalence was 37.85% (age-standardized 32.84%), higher in northern than southern provinces (41.39% vs 34.08%; standardized 35.41% vs 31.04%). Hypertension, hyperuricemia, and diabetes were most common. Cardiovascular/cerebrovascular conditions were more frequent in the north, whereas anemia and kidney stones were more common in the south. ARM suggested metabolic-renal clustering in the south (eg, CKD→gout, support = 1.18%, confidence = 26.14%, lift = 2.60; gout+anemia→CKD, support = 0.55%, confidence = 38.89%, lift = 3.71) and musculoskeletal-cardiovascular links in the north (eg, osteoarthritis→spinal disease, support = 0.52%, confidence = 24.69%, lift = 2.22; CTRD→CHD, support = 0.63%, confidence = 28.24%, lift = 1.26). Common SPM sequences included hypertension→hyperuricemia (24.22%) and hypertension→diabetes→hyperuricemia (5.32%); hypertension→hyperuricemia→CKD was more frequent in the south (2.28%), while hypertension→CHD→hyperuricemia was more frequent in the north (5.70%). Sensitivity analyses showed broadly consistent regional contrasts.

CONCLUSION: Multimorbidity burden and structure differed between the northern and southern provinces, supporting province-tailored prevention and integrated care.

articles.title: {Zn6Na} heptanuclear cluster based heterometallic framework as an intelligent luminescent sensor for efficient detection of carcinoid biomarkers.
articles.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
articles.abstract: Precise and rapid detection of carcinoid biomarkers in bodily fluids is critical for disease diagnosis and treatment. In this work, a 3D porous framework, {[Zn3Na0.5(DPIA)(μ3-OH)0.5(μ2-OH2)(H2O)1.5]·5H2O}n (ZnNaMOF), was successfully synthesized using 4,6-bis(2,4-dicarboxyphenyl)isophthalic acid (H6DPIA). ZnNaMOF displays an unprecedented {Zn6Na(COO)12} heptanuclear cluster based 3D porous architecture with 45% porosity, and shows exceptional chemical stability. Exploiting PET induced luminescence enhancement, ZnNaMOF demonstrates high potential as a luminescent sensor for quantitative detection of 5-HIAA and 5-HT biomarker, exhibiting high selectivity, sensitivity, strong anti-interference capability, and low detection limits (8.34 nM for 5-HIAA, 6.21 nM for 5-HT). Furthermore, Boolean logic gate-based intelligent detection platforms were developed to enhance the convenience and practicality of urinary 5-HIAA and serum 5-HT level monitoring.

articles.title: Nondestructive and interpretable assessment of pear soluble solids content by hyperspectral imaging coupled with broad learning system and shapley additive explanations.
articles.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
articles.abstract: Soluble solids content (SSC) is a critical indicator for pear maturity evaluation and quality grading. This study aims to develop a rapid, nondestructive, accurate and interpretable SSC prediction framework by coupling hyperspectral imaging (HSI), broad learning system (BLS), and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). Raw spectral data of 'Qiuyue' pears were collected and preprocessed. A BLS prediction model was constructed based on the preprocessed full-spectrum data, with its performance compared to partial least squares regression (PLSR), backpropagation neural network (BPNN), and support vector regression (SVR). SHAP was adopted for BLS model interpretability analysis and key wavelength selection. Simplified prediction models were further established by applying BLS, PLSR, BPNN, and SVR to the key wavelengths selected by SHAP and three traditional wavelength selection methods. The results showed that BLS outperformed the other three models in both full-wavelength and key-wavelength modeling, with the full-wavelength BLS model achieving the optimal performance (prediction correlation coefficient RP = 0.8195, root mean square error of prediction RMSEP = 0.8037). In addition, SHAP effectively screened key wavelengths and quantified the independent contribution of each to SSC prediction, greatly improving the transparency and interpretability of the BLS model. This study confirms the feasibility of the HSI-BLS-SHAP strategy for nondestructive and interpretable pear SSC evaluation, providing a technical reference for nondestructive intelligent fruit quality detection.

articles.title: Age Adjustment of the Combined Early Ischemic Change and Collateral Extent Score for Outcomes after Endovascular Therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Both age and ischemic core volume are strong predictors of outcomes after endovascular therapy. We previously developed and reported the ASPECTS and the multiphase CTA collateral extent (mCTA-ACE) score, which combines early ischemic changes on NCCT and the extent of leptomeningeal filling on multiphase CTA, and showed that it was associated with outcomes after endovascular therapy (EVT). The aim of this study was to refine the mCTA-ACE score through age adjustment and external validation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We performed a post hoc analysis of EVT-treated patients from the Alteplase Compared with Tenecteplase (AcT) trial. The mCTA-ACE score was calculated as the baseline ASPECTS plus a 10-point multiphase CTA (mCTA) collateral score, corresponding to ASPECTS regions M2-M6 graded as poor (0), moderate (1), or normal (2). From the mixed-effect logistic regression for mRS ≤2 at 90-120 days, the relative regression coefficient of age to mCTA-ACE score was used to derive the age-adjusted mCTA-ACE score. The prediction ability of age-adjusted mCTA-ACE score was validated in a reduced model from the Precise and Rapid Assessment of Collaterals Using Multi-Phase CTA in the Triage of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke for IA Therapy (PRove-IT) trial.

RESULTS: Of 1577 patients in the intention-to-treat population in the AcT trial, 368 who underwent EVT therapy and had assessable imaging were included (179 men, median age 73 years). In multivariable analysis, mCTA-ACE score and age were independently associated with mRS ≤2 (coefficients: 0.15 and -0.05, respectively); then the age-adjusted mCTA-ACE score was derived as mCTA-ACE score - age/3. The age-adjusted score showed superior predictive performance compared with the original mCTA-ACE score for mRS ≤2 (C-statistic 0.72 vs 0.65; P < .01). The C-statistics of age-adjusted and original mCTA-ACE scores for mRS ≤2 were 0.79 and 0.68, respectively (P < .01; DeLong test) in the PRove-IT population who underwent endovascular therapy (n=261; 124 men, median age 73 years).

CONCLUSIONS: An age-adjustment of the mCTA-ACE score may provide a more individualized prediction of functional outcomes after endovascular therapy, which helps patient selection, particularly in settings with limited access to endovascular therapy.

articles.title: Impact of Cerebral Venous Reflux on Functional Outcome in Patients with Acute Lacunar Stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Several reports have shown that cerebral venous reflux (CVR) was associated with cerebral small vessel disease. We assessed the association between CVR and functional outcome in patients with acute lacunar stroke.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Consecutive patients with acute lacunar stroke admitted within 7 days were enrolled. CVR was deemed present when abnormal high signal intensity was observed in the internal jugular vein or dural venous sinuses on intracranial TOF-MRA at admission. The primary outcome was poor functional outcome, defined as an mRS score of 2-6 at 90 days. The association between CVR and functional outcome was assessed using the multivariable logistic regression model.

RESULTS: A total of 216 consecutive patients with acute lacunar stroke were analyzed. Of these 216 patients, 37 (17.1%) had CVR. Patients with CVR were significantly more likely to have poor functional outcome than those without CVR (83.3% versus 51.5%; P < .001). CVR was independently associated with poor functional outcome (adjusted OR, 4.67; 95% CI, 1.56-14.00; P = .006).

CONCLUSIONS: CVR seems to be associated with poor functional outcome in patients with acute lacunar stroke. Validation in additional studies is warranted.

articles.title: Interventional vs Medical Management of Infectious Intracranial Aneurysms.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infectious intracranial aneurysms (IIAs) are rare vascular lesions carrying high risks of rupture, intracranial hemorrhage, and mortality. Their low incidence and the absence of randomized controlled trials leave the optimal management strategy uncertain.

PURPOSE: The purpose was to systematically review and synthesize comparative observational evidence on interventional (surgical or endovascular) vs medical management of IIAs.

DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to August 4, 2025, using controlled vocabulary and free-text terms. Reference lists of relevant reviews and included articles were manually screened.

STUDY SELECTION: Comparative observational cohort studies reporting outcomes between at least 1 interventional strategy (surgical or endovascular) and medical management alone in patients with IIAs were included. Case reports, small case series without a comparator group, conference abstracts, and review articles were excluded.

DATA ANALYSIS: Comparative outcomes were synthesized using random-effects pair-wise meta-analysis. Effect estimates were expressed as risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CI. Heterogeneity was assessed using Cochran Q test and the I 2 statistic. Sensitivity analyses were conducted using leave-1-out methods. Risk of bias was assessed with the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I) tool; certainty of evidence was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.

DATA SYNTHESIS: Thirteen retrospective observational studies (748 patients) were included. Interventional management was associated with higher treatment success (RR 1.36; 95% CI, 1.13-1.65), lower mortality (RR 0.56; 0.36-0.88), fewer overall complications (RR 0.28; 0.13-0.59), and lower rupture/rerupture risk (RR 0.42; 0.22-0.79). Recurrence, aneurysm enlargement, and permanent neurologic deficits were infrequently reported and characterized by substantial imprecision. Most studies carried moderate or serious risk of bias, primarily due to confounding and nonrandomized treatment allocation.

LIMITATIONS: All included studies were retrospective and nonrandomized, with substantial confounding by indication. Individual-patient data were unavailable, precluding adjusted or subgroup analyses. Outcome definitions and follow-up durations were inconsistently reported across studies. Publication bias cannot be excluded.

CONCLUSIONS: In observational cohorts, interventional management of IIAs was consistently associated with more favorable short-term clinical and angiographic outcomes compared with medical management alone. However, substantial risk of bias and confounding by indication limit these findings, which do not support causal inference and should be regarded as hypothesis generating.

articles.title: Age Standardization in Health Statistics: History and Future Perspectives.
articles.abstract: Age standardization is a key statistical method used in health statistics to adjust rates, such as mortality or incidence, enabling comparisons across populations or time points with different age structures. This review traces its historical development, global and country-specific practices, and future directions. The method dates back to the 19th century, with major adoption in the 20th century through Segi and Doll's World Standard Population. While the World Health Organization (WHO) introduced an updated standard in 2000, the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) continues to use Segi and Doll's standard in the Cancer Incidence in Five Continents series, prioritizing consistency and comparability in long-term cancer surveillance. Case studies from the IARC, the United States, Japan, and the Republic of Korea (Korea) illustrate different responses to changing demographics. The United States adopted the 2000 standard with expanded age detail for the elderly population. Japan introduced the 2015 Japan Standard Population to account for its rapidly aging society, though regional data limitations presented challenges. Korea, experiencing one of the fastest aging transitions globally, updated to a 2020 standard for more accurate national and sub-national reporting. The review also emphasizes that age standardization can obscure important age-specific trends. Methods like Joinpoint clustering help detect divergent trends by age groups. Looking forward, age standardization remains essential amid global demographic shifts. However, updates of standard populations must balance improved relevance with the need for continuity and robust data. International coordination and digital tools will support more flexible and transparent health statistics in the future.

articles.title: Hand, foot, and mouth disease progressing into sialadenitis in an adult patient: a rare complication.
articles.abstract: Dear Editor, In April 2024, a 24-year-old non-smoker female patient with controlled asthma presented with a sore throat, left-sided cervical lymphadenopathy, and a painful, red maculopapular rash on the hands and feet. [...].

articles.title: SOTA: A statistical tool for quantifying the superiority onset time of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor response based on Kaplan-Meier graphics and its application in a meta-analysis of NSCLC randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Programmed death-1/programmed death ligand-1 inhibitors exert a unique delayed effect in clinical practice, although the exact duration of this delay remains inconclusive. To address this, we aimed to develop an algorithm-SOTA ( S uperiority O nset- T ime Algorithm) to quantify the delayed effect and estimate the post-onset therapeutic benefit and applied it based on a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to calculate the delayed effect of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

METHODS: SOTA reconstructs Kaplan-Meier curves from published figures, recovers individual-level data, and applies a piecewise Cox model to identify the optimal breakpoint as superiority onset time (SOT). It also enables the estimation of post-onset efficacy of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors by using landmark analysis to estimate the hazard ratio (HR) after the SOT. The code is available at: https://github.com/qihanfan/SOTA . Then we applied SOTA in a meta-analysis of phase II/III RCTs in NSCLC, identified through a systematic search up to Mar 9, 2025. Data extraction and quality assessment were conducted in accordance with Cochrane guidelines. Pooled estimates of SOT and post-onset HR were obtained.

RESULTS: Simulation studies confirmed the accuracy of the SOTA. For survival data reconstruction, the average value of mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and maximum deviation between the raw and reconstructed data were 0.008, 0.011, and 0.050, respectively. For the estimation of the SOT, SOTA accurately recovered the true change point of the HR, with relative errors predominantly within ± 5% and coverage probabilities ≥95% across all scenarios. In the meta-analysis, 25 RCTs were included after screening. The estimated SOT was 3.64 months for overall survival (OS) and 3.26 months for progression-free survival (PFS). The corresponding post-onset HRs for OS and PFS were 0.68 and 0.47, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors show a unique delayed effect compared to chemotherapy. The SOTA algorithm provides a quantitative framework for assessing this delay, offering valuable insights for estimating treatment effects and clinical trial design.

articles.title: Prophylaxis in ant societies: a social response to pathogen vulnerability?
articles.abstract: Social insects rely on multiple defence mechanisms to limit pathogen transmission within colonies. Prophylactic sanitary behaviours are performed in the absence of immediate pathogenic threats and contribute to routine disease prevention. Among these behaviours, grooming and necrophoresis help manage potentially harmful biological material, but how their expression relates to variation in pathogen susceptibility among colonies remains poorly understood. We investigated the relationship between susceptibility to the entomopathogenic fungus Beauveria bassiana and the expression of prophylactic grooming and necrophoresis in the ant Lasius flavus. We found strong and consistent intercolonial differences in pathogen susceptibility, as well as marked variation in the expression of prophylactic sanitary behaviours. None of the grooming behaviours examined were associated with pathogen susceptibility. However, more pathogen-susceptible colonies tended to remove corpses more rapidly during the early phase of necrophoresis. This pattern is consistent with a possible compensatory relationship among defence components, but may also arise from demographic and organizational differences among colonies, as worker age structure and task allocation can influence both susceptibility to infection and corpse removal behaviour. Overall, our results reveal substantial intercolonial variation in multiple components of disease defence but provide little support for a compensatory relationship between pathogen susceptibility and prophylactic sanitary behaviour.

articles.title: Structurally related Ca2+-release activated Ca2+ channel inhibitors exhibit distinct extracellular and intracellular modes of action.
articles.abstract: Ca2+-release activated Ca2+ (CRAC) channels, formed by stromal interaction molecule (STIM) and Orai proteins, mediate store-operated Ca2+ entry and are implicated in autoimmune diseases, acute pancreatitis and cancer. Some small molecule inhibitors of these channels such as BTP2, Pyr6, Synta66 and GSK-7975A, are widely used as experimental tools, yet their precise mechanisms of action remain incompletely understood. Using whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology in rat basophilic leukaemia (RBL-1) cells, we determined whether each of these inhibitors acts from the extracellular or intracellular side of the plasma membrane. We found that BTP2 and GSK-7975A could suppress CRAC currents only when applied extracellularly, whereas Pyr6 and Synta66 were equally effective from either side. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations using a rat Orai1 channel model identified plausible extracellular binding sites for all four inhibitors and additional putative intracellular binding sites for Pyr6 and Synta66. These predicted sites are located near regions that are likely to influence pore geometry and channel gating. Our findings suggest that, despite considerable structural similarity, these popular CRAC channel inhibitors exhibit mechanistically distinct interactions with Orai1, with important implications for their use as research tools and for future CRAC channel drug discovery.

articles.title: Motivation in adolescents and caretakers undergoing a weight management program - longitudinal data from the cluster-randomized, motivation-focused STARKIDS trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Motivation towards behavior change is an important determinant of long-term weight management. Previous research demonstrates that children's and adolescents' motivation can be increased through participation in weight management programs. However, little is known about motivational changes in caretakers of children and adolescents with overweight and obesity despite their recognized role as "agents of change" in pediatric weight management. The study aims to compare motivational changes in caretakers and adolescents between a group receiving a motivation-focused weight management program and a control group. Furthermore, predictors for motivational changes are unknown.

METHODS: This study is a secondary analysis of the cluster-randomized STARKIDS trial. The intervention group received an 18-month motivation-focused weight management program, the control group received optimized treatment-as-usual. Motivation was assessed based on Transtheoretical Model, using the University of Rhode Island Change Assessment-Short, as well as the related parent-perspective version. Each of these instruments contains four subscales: Precontemplation, Contemplation, Action, and Maintenance. Linear mixed models with multiply imputed data were employed to evaluate changes within the subscales between pre- to post-intervention measurements and to compare these changes between the intervention and control group. A multiple linear regression was subsequently used to identify predictors of motivational change.

RESULTS: Caretakers in the intervention group showed significantly greater changes on Maintenance subscale compared to caretakers in the control group at both T0-T1 and T0-T2 and trends for these changes on Action subscale. No group differences were found in adolescents. Among caregivers in the intervention group, multiple regression analysis for T0-T1 changes on Action subscale identified parent-reported adolescents' obesity-related quality of life as significant negative predictor for an increase on Action stage.

CONCLUSIONS: This motivation-focused weight management program produced motivational gains at the Maintenance stage, supporting sustained behavioral change. Baseline obesity-related quality of life predicted motivational change, suggesting its value as a clinical marker for tailoring interventional approaches. Future research should explore distinct motivational trajectories to inform more individualized pediatric weight management strategies.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Preregistered in the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS) DRKS000228 13 (acknowledged primary register of the World Health Organization) on 27 November 2020 (Universal Trial Number U111112549536).

articles.title: Engineering hypoactivated platelet-derived coating to decouple thrombosis for vascular regeneration.
articles.abstract: The clinical performance of intravascular stents remains limited by thrombotic complications and delayed vascular healing. While cell membrane-based coatings have been explored to recapitulate native biointerfaces, achieving simultaneous hemocompatibility and pro-regenerative functionality remains challenging due to the intrinsic thrombogenicity of platelet-derived materials. Here, we propose a brand-new hypoactivated platelet-derived coating (hPLC) by sequentially assembling fibrin networks and low-activated platelets, followed by controlled lysis to remove pro-thrombotic components. This approach preserves the structural and biointerfacial features of platelet membrane while decoupling thrombogenic activity from regenerative functionality. The resulting hPLC endows materials with reduced protein adsorption, suppressed coagulation, and attenuated inflammatory responses. Transcriptomic analysis further reveals that hPLC enhances endothelial compatibility through coordinated regulation of anti-apoptotic, cytoskeletal remodeling, and angiogenic pathways. In vivo stent implantation studies demonstrate that hPLC-coated stents provide a pro-regenerative microenvironment, significantly accelerating re-endothelialization while inhibiting neointimal hyperplasia and peri-strut inflammation. These findings establish a bioinspired and clinically translatable strategy for engineering multifunctional vascular interfaces from readily available blood components, offering a versatile platform for the surface engineering of vascular devices.

articles.title: Novel adenoma-immune phenotypes are associated with risk of metachronous polyps and colorectal cancer in a bowel screening cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG) guidelines misclassify metachronous lesion risk after polypectomy in approximately 40% of patients. Building on evidence that immune exclusion drives progression of adenomas to colorectal cancer, this study examined immune profiles in screen-detected adenomas as a predictive biomarker for metachronous lesion risk.

METHODS: Patients undergoing polypectomy within the Scottish Bowel Screening Programme, with surveillance colonoscopy between 6 months and 6 years were included (n = 2642). Chromogenic immunohistochemistry (IHC; n = 2466), 6-plex multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF; n = 331), and spatially resolved 6000-plex single cell transcriptomics (n = 7) were applied to adenoma microarrays. Cell density and location were measured using QuPath. Hierarchical then K-means clustering was used to define immune cell density-based clusters, which were compared to future lesion events using Kaplan-Meier curves and the log rank test.

RESULTS: After adjustment for age, sex, site, size and dysplasia, adenoma CD3+ T cell density was significantly associated with future colorectal neoplasia (OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.20-1.72, p < 0.001). Using mIF, three immune cell density clusters were identified; 1) high T cell density, low macrophage density, 2) low T cell density, low macrophage density, and 3) high T cell, macrophage and αSMA density, with significant differences in future lesion risk (Cluster 1: 22%, Cluster 2: 41%, Cluster 3: 36%, p = 0.032). Bulk RNAseq and spatial transcriptomic analysis revealed significant variation in T cell and macrophage co-location and gene expression profiles between clusters.

CONCLUSION: Adenoma immune contexture emerges as a possible determinant of future metachronous lesion risk, offering a novel biomarker to refine surveillance.

articles.title: Aspirin is safe and effective for prevention of deep vein thrombosis following acetabular fracture surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with acetabular fractures are at significant risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE), yet the optimal chemoprophylactic agent remains undefined. Emerging evidence from elective arthroplasty and general orthopaedic trauma populations suggests that aspirin (ASA) may be a safe and effective alternative to traditional anticoagulants. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the safety and efficacy of ASA compared to other anticoagulants for deep vein thrombosis (DVT) prevention following acetabular fracture surgery.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort analysis was performed using a global, web-based health research network that provides on-demand access to de-identified, real-world data from electronic health records and claims. Adult patients (≥18 years) who underwent surgical treatment for acetabular fractures between January 2014 and December 2025 and received VTE prophylaxis within 14 days of surgery were identified. Patients were stratified into ASA (n = 1189) and other anticoagulant (n = 5478) cohorts. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed to balance baseline characteristics, yielding 1174 patients per cohort. Rates and odds of DVT, emergency department (ED) visits, deep infection, stroke, and readmission were assessed at 14-, 30-, and 90-day postoperative intervals. Temporal trends in VTE prophylaxis utilization were also analyzed.

RESULTS: Compared to other anticoagulants, ASA was associated with significantly lower odds of DVT at 14 days (1.11% vs. 2.22%; odds ratio [OR]: 0.494; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.253-0.967; P = 0.036), 30 days (1.45% vs. 2.73%; OR: 0.524; 95% CI: 0.290-0.950; P = 0.030), and 90 days (2.56% vs. 4.34%; OR: 0.577; 95% CI: 0.365-0.913; P = 0.018). ASA was also associated with significantly lower odds of ED visits at 90 days (OR: 0.741; 95% CI: 0.570-0.963; P = 0.024). There were no significant differences in deep infection, stroke, or readmission rates. ASA utilization increased from 7.2% in 2014-39.5% in 2025.

CONCLUSIONS: ASA is safe and effective for DVT prevention following acetabular fracture surgery and is associated with fewer ED visits compared to other anticoagulants. These findings support the growing adoption of ASA as a VTE prophylactic agent in the acetabular fracture population.

articles.title: Multi-omics integration identifies core genes, molecular subtypes, and IDI1-centered immune microenvironment mechanisms in coronary artery disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is the leading cause of death worldwide, but its molecular mechanisms remain unclear.

METHODS: We integrated transcriptomic datasets (GSE113079, GSE98583, GSE71226) and single-cell RNA sequencing data (GSE159677) from GEO. Differential expression analysis, WGCNA, machine learning, molecular clustering, immune infiltration analysis, CellChat, in silico knockout, and PheWAS were applied to investigate CAD-related molecular networks.

RESULTS: We identified 99 DEGs and the MEturquoise module as a CAD-associated module. Machine learning initially identified four candidate genes (RC3H1, IDI1, RAB2A, and SIRPB2); however, only IDI1 was retained after external validation and single-cell intersection. Single-cell analysis revealed macrophage expansion and specific IDI1 enrichment in Cycling cells and immune populations. CAD was classified into two molecular subtypes with distinct immune profiles. Cell communication analysis identified SPP1, TNF, CCL, and MIF pathways as key inflammatory regulators. Virtual knockout simulation of IDI1 affected hemostasis, Toll-like receptor signaling, and collagen degradation pathways. PheWAS showed no significant phenotype-wide associations for IDI1.

CONCLUSION: This study identified IDI1 as a CAD-associated candidate gene, revealed immune-based molecular subtypes of CAD, and suggested that IDI1 and inflammatory signaling pathways may serve as potential therapeutic targets, providing insights into precision classification and targeted therapy for CAD.

articles.title: CT-Based Deep Learning Assessment of Aortic Valve Fibrosis and Calcification: Development and Multicenter External Validation Against Experts, Histology, and Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Computed tomography angiography (CTA) enables assessment of aortic valve tissue composition, providing insights into disease progression and helping predict outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis (AS). The authors aimed to develop a deep learning system for CTA-based quantification of aortic fibrotic and calcific tissue, validate its agreement with expert manual analysis and histopathology, and evaluate its value for outcome prediction.

METHODS: This international, multicenter study included 1,674 patients who underwent CTA at 9 sites. A deep learning model based on the nnU-Net architecture was trained in 468 patients and applied to an external test set of 1,206 patients, including 29 with valve histology and 12 with serial CTA. In 1,165 patients with clinical outcomes, prognostic value was assessed adjusting for clinical, echocardiographic, and procedural covariates.

RESULTS: Deep learning-enabled tissue composition analysis was rapid (1.35 ± 0.4 min vs 7.2 ± 1.2 min for experts) with excellent agreement vs expert assessment (r = 0.915; intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] = 0.913), histology (r = 0.909; ICC = 0.905), and scan-rescan reproducibility (r = 0.999; ICC = 0.999). In the external cohort, 469 patients (40%) died over 4.1 ± 1.1 years of follow-up. Fibrotic tissue volume (adjusted HR [aHR] 1.42 per IQR increase; P < 0.001), calcific tissue attenuation (aHR 1.02 per 25 HU increase; P = 0.005), left ventricular ejection fraction (aHR 1.10 per 5% decrease; P < 0.001), life-threatening bleeding (aHR: 1.96; P = 0.003), major vascular complication (aHR: 1.51; P = 0.042) and postprocedural peak pressure gradient (aHR 1.03 per 1 mm Hg increase; P < 0.001) independently predicted mortality. Patients in the highest tertile of fibrotic tissue volume (>0.940 cm3) had a 2-fold higher risk of death (aHR: 2.0; P < 0.001), whereas patients with dense calcific tissue attenuation (>885 HU) had a 1.5-fold higher risk of death.

CONCLUSIONS: Deep learning enables rapid quantification of aortic valve fibrotic and calcific tissue from CTA, demonstrating excellent agreement with both expert CTA and histological assessments. Quantitative analysis of aortic tissue composition provides additional prognostic value for all-cause mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement in multicenter external evaluation.

articles.title: From Anatomy to Tissue: Cardiac CT Finally Turns Its Attention to the Aortic Valve.
Beyond anticoagulation: defining the role of left atrial appendage closure in stroke prevention for atrial fibrillation.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract: Oral anticoagulation has a very strong evidence base for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) at elevated thromboembolic risk. Direct oral anticoagulants have improved the safety and convenience of treatment, yet important limitations remain, including residual ischaemic stroke, major bleeding, treatment discontinuation, and patient refusal. Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) offers an alternative strategy for selected patients by excluding the principal anatomical source of AF-related cardiac thrombi. However, the appropriate role of LAAC remains controversial, particularly in patients who can and do tolerate anticoagulation. This viewpoint argues for a more individualized approach that distinguishes absolute contraindications from modifiable bleeding risks, treatment refusal or non-persistence, and stroke occurring despite adequate anticoagulation.

articles.title: From Indolent Neuropathy to Aggressive Primary Neurolymphoma: Evolution of a Misleading Dysimmune Phenotype.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Primary neurolymphomatosis is a rare presentation of non-Hodgkin lymphoma characterised by initial peripheral nervous system involvement without systemic disease, frequently resulting in delayed diagnosis.

OBSERVATIONS: A 56-year-old man presented with a 5-year history of asymmetric progressive radiculoplexoneuropathy, initially treated with immunotherapy for presumed vasculitic neuropathy, with apparent disease stability for 4.5 years before rapid deterioration over the ensuing 6 months. Examination revealed asymmetric limb weakness of lower and then upper limbs, areflexia, distal sensory loss and cranial nerve palsies. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated diffuse thickening and enhancement of the brachial and lumbosacral plexuses and cauda equina. Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography-computed tomography (FDG PET-CT) showed hypermetabolic lesions involving the left sciatic nerve and cauda equina without systemic disease. Cerebrospinal fluid cytology and flow cytometry confirmed high-grade B-cell lymphoma. High-dose methotrexate-based combination chemotherapy achieved clinical remission at 14-month follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: and Relevance: Chronic atypical radiculoplexoneuropathy with accelerated progression should prompt consideration of neurolymphomatosis to facilitate early diagnosis and improved outcomes.

articles.title: Spatially resolved single-cell atlas reveals cortical glial reactivity associated with regions of neuronal growth programs in both hemispheres after stroke.
articles.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
articles.abstract: Recovery after focal motor cortex stroke relies on structural remodeling of neuronal circuits in the perilesional cortex (PLC) and contralesional cortex (CLC). Although transcriptomic studies have identified distinct reactive glial states after stroke, how their spatial organization relates to processes of tissue degeneration and neuronal circuit remodeling remains poorly understood. We used a custom 347-gene Xenium spatial transcriptomics panel to profile approximately 650,000 cells across both hemispheres of male and female mice 7 days after photothrombotic stroke. We identified injury-associated myeloid populations concentrated within the infarct and reactive astrocytes enriched in the glial scar. Distinct reactive populations also extended into spared cortex, including an interferon-associated myeloid population and a reactive astrocyte population that was present in both PLC and CLC. Spatial mapping further revealed elevated neuronal growth-associated gene expression in both regions, particularly among layer 5 extratelencephalic projection neurons, which include corticospinal neurons. Intriguingly, reactive glial populations were enriched in regions exhibiting elevated neuronal growth-associated gene expression, including areas of the CLC containing axons and presynaptic terminals originating from the PLC. Together, these findings reveal a striking spatial association between reactive glial populations and neurons exhibiting elevated growth-associated gene expression and support glial-neuronal interactions as potential targets for promoting circuit remodeling and functional recovery after stroke.

articles.title: Mediterranean diet and risk of prostate cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prostate cancer is the most common malignancy among men worldwide. In addition to non-modifiable risk factors, modifiable lifestyle factors are increasingly recognized in prevention. The Mediterranean diet (Med Diet), characterized by high intake of plant-based foods, unsaturated fatty acids, and antioxidant micronutrients, has been proposed as a protective dietary pattern.

METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus examining associations between Mediterranean diet adherence and prostate cancer risk. Fourteen studies met eligibility criteria. Meta-analysis was performed in R applying a random-effects model (REML estimation; Hartung-Knapp adjustment). Heterogeneity was assessed with I² and τ²; publication bias was evaluated using a funnel plot, contour-enhanced funnel plot, and Egger's test.

RESULTS: Based on a random effects model, we did not find a statistically significant difference in risk of prostate cancer in men with high versus low Mediterranean diet adherence (RR = 0.98; 95% CI: 0.93-1.04). Heterogeneity was moderate (Q = 19.95, I² = 34.8%). Although Egger's regression test did not indicate statistically significant publication bias (p = 0.115), complementary analyses (Q-Q plot and limit meta-analysis) suggested a possible small-study effect, warranting cautious interpretation.

CONCLUSION: In this meta-analysis, no protective effect of the Mediterranean diet against prostate cancer was found. Nevertheless, biological plausibility and inconsistent epidemiological trends suggest that further research using standardized dietary assessments and incorporating genetic and microbiome-related factors is needed.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The review protocol was not prospectively registered.

articles.title: Integrative bioinformatics and preliminary experimental validation suggest the therapeutic potential of lycorine in uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC) is one of the most prevalent gynecological malignancies worldwide and remains a significant threat to women's health. Lycorine, a natural alkaloid isolated from plants of the Amaryllidaceae family, has attracted considerable attention owing to its diverse pharmacological activities, particularly its anti-tumor properties. However, the potential therapeutic targets and action mechanism of lycorine in UCEC remain unclear.In this study, an integrated strategy combining bioinformatic analysis and preliminary experimental validation was used to elucidate the anti-tumor mechanisms of lycorine in UCEC. Potential targets of lycorine were predicted using public databases and intersected with differentially expressed genes derived from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) UCEC dataset. Subsequently, a protein-protein interaction (PPI) network was constructed, and Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses were used to investigate the biological functions and pathways associated with these targets. Prognostic analysis and Cox regression were used to establish a risk prediction model. Immune infiltration analysis was performed to evaluate the relationship between key genes and the tumor immune microenvironment.Results revealed 10 potential targets of lycorine associated with UCEC. Functional enrichment analysis indicated that these genes were mainly involved in cholinergic synapse and neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction pathways. Three key genes (ACHE, MAN2B1, and PNP) were further identified to construct a prognostic model, which showed moderate predictive performance in survival analysis. Immune infiltration analysis revealed that these genes were associated with multiple immune cell populations in the tumor microenvironment. Molecular docking revealed that the binding energies of ACHE, MAN2B1, and PNP with lycorine were ≤ - 7.0 kcal/mol, indicating stable binding. In vitro experiments confirmed that lycorine significantly inhibited the proliferation of Ishikawa endometrial cancer cells.In conclusion, this study provides new insights into the potential therapeutic effects of lycorine in UCEC and identifies ACHE, MAN2B1, and PNP as promising therapeutic targets for further investigation.

articles.journal: European journal of hospital pharmacy : science and practice

articles.title: Plasma free amino acid dynamics, clinical and clinicopathological responses following intravenous E. coli lipopolysaccharide challenge in neonatal calves.
articles.abstract: Experimental endotoxemia is used to characterize systemic inflammatory responses in calves, but its effects on plasma free amino acids remain incompletely defined. This study characterized temporal plasma free amino acid changes following intravenous lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge in neonatal calves. Twelve healthy male Holstein calves aged 16-27 days were block-randomized to a control group (n = 6) or an LPS group (n = 6). LPS calves received Escherichia coli O111:B4 LPS intravenously at 1 µg/kg; controls received an equivalent volume of sterile 0.9% NaCl. Clinical assessments and blood sampling were performed before administration and at 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 24, and 48 h thereafter. Hematology, routine biochemistry, serum amyloid A (SAA), and 24 plasma free amino acids were evaluated. Amino acids were quantified by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. LPS induced acute clinical deterioration, a transient increase in rectal temperature, marked leukopenia, declining platelet counts, and a pronounced SAA response. Linear mixed-effects analysis of baseline-adjusted changes identified significant group × time interactions for citrulline, arginine, ornithine, threonine, and lysine after false discovery rate correction (q < 0.05). In the LPS group, the greatest decreases in mean concentrations from baseline occurred at 12 h for citrulline (48.5%), arginine (58.1%), ornithine (44.5%), and threonine (52.4%), and at 8 h for lysine (39.9%). Intravenous LPS challenge therefore induced coordinated, time-dependent changes in plasma free amino acid availability, involving the citrulline-arginine-ornithine axis and amino acids associated with intestinal and inflammatory metabolism.

articles.title: Effect of virtual reality-based simulation using an ischemic stroke scenario: A randomized study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To evaluate a six-week program integrating virtual reality (VR) and high-fidelity simulation (HFS) for ischemic stroke nursing compared with HFS alone.

BACKGROUND: The additional educational benefits of integrating VR with HFS require evaluation across learning outcomes and over time.

DESIGN: An individually randomized, single-blind, two-group trial.

METHODS: Fifty-two nursing students were randomized equally to VR-integrated HFS or HFS alone. Outcomes were assessed at baseline, immediately post-intervention and four weeks later. The main complete-case analysis included 47 students. Linear mixed-effects models included participant and course-section random intercepts, with Holm adjustment. An intention-to-treat analysis included all 52 students using available observations under a missing-at-random assumption.

RESULTS: Group-by-time interactions were significant for all four outcomes. Learning engagement and self-reported clinical competence were higher in the intervention group immediately post-intervention, but not at follow-up. The immediate between-group mean difference in clinical competence was 19.99 points (95% confidence interval, 7.89-32.09). Metacognition was higher immediately post-intervention and at follow-up. Academic self-efficacy did not differ significantly between groups at either post-intervention assessment. The intention-to-treat analysis showed the same pattern of statistical significance.

CONCLUSIONS: VR-integrated HFS was associated with immediate advantages in learning engagement and clinical competence and a sustained metacognition advantage at four weeks. Larger studies with objective performance assessments and longer follow-up are needed.

articles.title: Single-cell and spatial characterization of the human pancreas in cystic fibrosis.
articles.abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF) causes severely damaged pancreatic morphology and cystic fibrosis-related diabetes (CFRD), but the cellular drivers of CFRD in the pancreas are not understood. Here, we perform single-cell and spatial profiling of 2.04 M cells from 23 non-disease or CF pancreas donors. A high-mucin ductal sub-type had relatively preserved abundance and genomic profiles but altered localization in CF. Changes in inflammatory and fibrotic pathways were driven by crosstalk between immune and pro-fibrotic cells in specific niches. Beta cells had extensive changes in CF, including increased stress responses and evidence for compensatory secretion, that were distinct from those in type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Islets localized near large adipose tissue and collagen in CF had reduced beta cells linked to signaling from adipocytes, macrophages, stellate cells, and high-mucin ductal cells. Overall, our results highlight pancreatic microenvironments of beta cell dysfunction in CF and offer in-roads to preserving beta cells in CFRD.

articles.title: Predictors for Failure of Nonsurgical Treatment in Mild to Moderate Cubital Tunnel Syndrome.
articles.journal: The journal of hand surgery Asian-Pacific volume
articles.abstract: Background: Activity modification to reduce mechanical stress on the ulnar nerve is an effective treatment for mild to moderate cubital tunnel syndrome (CuTS). However, some patients do not improve with nonsurgical management and ultimately require surgical intervention. This study aimed to identify predictors associated with nonsurgical treatment failure in CuTS. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed data from patients with CuTS classified as McGowan grades 1 and 2. Non-surgical management primarily consisted of activity modification, with adjunctive treatments including vitamin B12, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, pregabalin or mirogabalin and corticosteroid injections. Treatment failure was defined as the need for subsequent surgical intervention (transition-to-surgery group). The success group included 37 patients, and the transition-to-surgery group included 26 patients. Univariate and multivariate regression analyses were performed to evaluate predictors of nonsurgical treatment failure, including age, sex, body mass index, disease duration, comorbidities (diabetes mellitus, thyroid disease and radiographic cervical spondylosis) and concomitant elbow disorders (osteoarthritis, ganglion cysts and cubitus varus or valgus deformity). Elbow osteoarthritis was assessed radiographically using the Broberg and Morrey classification system. Results: Univariate analysis showed that corticosteroid injections, current smoking, radiographic cervical spondylosis and elbow osteoarthritis were more common in the transition-to-surgery group than in the success group. Multivariate analysis identified corticosteroid injections, radiographic cervical spondylosis and elbow osteoarthritis as independent predictors of nonsurgical treatment failure. Conclusions: Patients who received corticosteroid injections and those with radiographic cervical spondylosis or elbow osteoarthritis were more likely to experience nonsurgical treatment failure for mild to moderate CuTS and subsequently require surgical intervention. Early recognition of these risk factors may help clinicians identify patients who are less likely to respond to conservative management and consider earlier surgical treatment to prevent persistent symptoms and disease progression. Level of Evidence: Level IV (Therapeutic).

articles.title: Missing Data in Retrospective Upper Extremity Surgery Research - A Single US-Institution Analysis.
articles.journal: The journal of hand surgery Asian-Pacific volume
articles.abstract: Background: Missing data are a recognised challenge in clinical research, yet their extent and handling are rarely reported transparently. We aimed to quantify the frequency of missing data in a retrospective cohort of upper extremity surgical patients and identify factors associated with incomplete records. Methods: Datasets from four surgical cohorts from our integrated health network (1. arthroscopic rotator cuff repair, 2. open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) of acute scaphoid fractures, 3. ORIF of distal radius fractures and 4. open carpal tunnel release) were pooled into a dataset of 2,180 patients. The extent of missing data was calculated for each of the following variables: sex, age, body mass index (BMI), race, diabetes mellitus (DM), current smoking status and laterality of the primary procedure. Differences in missingness rates were assessed using the chi-square test. Bivariate analyses were performed to assess whether each variable was a predictor of missing data. Results: Data missingness was highest at 8.9% (±0.61%) for race, followed by 3.4% (±0.38%) for BMI, 1.4% (±0.28%) for laterality, 0.5% (±0.15%) for smoking status, 0.2% (±0.1%) for DM and no missingness for sex or age data. No patient-level factors were significantly associated with missingness. Conclusions: Race was the most frequently missing variable, reflecting a broader tendency to underreport social and demographic factors in orthopaedic research. Transparent reporting of missing data, alongside systematic efforts to collect it, remains essential for producing reliable and generalisable surgical evidence. Level of Evidence: Level V (Therapeutic).

articles.title: Infectious Complications after Soft Tissue Surgery of the Hand in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.journal: The journal of hand surgery Asian-Pacific volume
articles.abstract: Background: The primary objective of this study is to understand postoperative infectious complication rates following soft tissue hand surgery in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). This study aims to assess whether patients with stage III-V CKD have an increased risk of superficial, deep or systemic infections compared with non-CKD patients. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the multi-centre TriNetX Research Network database, comparing adults with and without stage III-V CKD who underwent carpal tunnel release, trigger finger release, de Quervain's release, ganglion cyst excision, palmar fasciectomy, synovectomy, tendon sheath excision or soft tissue excision of the hand. Patients with fracture- or dislocation-related procedures were excluded. Outcomes of interest included postoperative infection, skin/subcutaneous infection, osteomyelitis and sepsis assessed at 30- and 90-day intervals postoperatively. Propensity score matching was controlled for age, sex, race, obesity, diabetes, nicotine and alcohol dependence and malnutrition. Results: After matching, 91,570 patients (45,785 per cohort) were analysed. At both 30 and 90 days postoperatively, CKD patients experienced higher rates of skin/subcutaneous infection, osteomyelitis and sepsis compared with non-CKD patients. Overall, postoperative infection rates were low but increased with greater CKD severity. Conclusions: Stage III-V CKD is associated with an increased risk of deep and systemic infections following elective soft tissue hand procedures. While routine perioperative antibiotics are not currently indicated, our findings support a risk-stratified approach that considers stage III-V CKD a potential indication for enhanced postoperative surveillance. Level of Evidence: Level II (Prognostic/Risk).

articles.title: Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging in the Diagnosis and Management of Postpartum Choriocarcinoma With Cardiopulmonary Complications.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (choriocarcinoma) may be associated with substantial diagnostic delay because of nonspecific symptoms and the rarity of this malignancy.

CASE SUMMARY: A young postpartum woman presented with progressive dyspnea, fever, and chest pain. Delayed diagnosis led to clinical deterioration with severe pulmonary hypertension (PH), right ventricular (RV) dysfunction, culminating in cardiac arrest with successful resuscitation. Ultrasound demonstrating uterine lesions and markedly elevated β-human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) levels established the diagnosis of gestational choriocarcinoma. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) precisely assessed RV function and PH-related cardiac involvement. Chemotherapy normalized β-hCG levels and resolved PH and RV dysfunction.

DISCUSSION: This case illustrates the diagnostic challenges of unclear dyspnea and choriocarcinoma complicated by PH and the value of CMR.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: CMR plays an important role in the assessment of cardiopulmonary complications of choriocarcinoma, although a structured evaluation of dyspnea, including β-hCG, is essential for the early diagnosis.

articles.title: Intramyocardial Granulomatous Histoplasmosis Presenting as Narrow-Complex Ventricular Tachycardia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac histoplasmosis is rare, typically manifesting as pericarditis or endocarditis; tissue-proven intramyocardial granulomatous histoplasmosis has not been previously described.

CASE SUMMARY: A 77-year-old man with immunosuppression presented with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure and recurrent narrow-complex tachyarrhythmias attributed to supraventricular tachycardia (SVT). Echocardiography showed a hyperechoic basal septal mass. Autopsy confirmed a 1.8 × 1.1 cm partially hyalinized necrotizing granuloma of the high interventricular septum containing Histoplasma on silver staining. Retrospective aVR algorithm analysis reclassified the arrhythmia as ventricular tachycardia (VT), anatomically concordant with the granuloma.

DISCUSSION: Granulomatous histoplasmosis of the upper interventricular septum can produce high septal VT mimicking SVT, expanding the differential of granulomatous myocarditis in immunocompromised hosts.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Histoplasmosis should be included in the differential of granulomatous myocarditis, particularly in immunocompromised patients from endemic regions. Systematic use of the Vereckei aVR algorithm can prevent misclassification of relatively narrow-complex VT as SVT and guide management.

articles.title: Idiopathic Middle Aortic Syndrome Causing Pediatric Resistant Hypertension: Beyond Coarctation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Middle aortic syndrome (MAS) is a rare cause of severe hypertension in children, characterized by segmental narrowing of the distal thoracic and abdominal aorta. Early recognition is essential to prevent irreversible end-organ damage.

CASE SUMMARY: A 12-year-old girl presented with resistant hypertension, headache, facial edema, blurred vision, and postprandial abdominal pain. Marked upper-to-lower limb blood pressure discrepancy, with absent femoral pulses. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated long-segment thoracoabdominal aortic narrowing extending to the iliac arteries, consistent with MAS. Because of unfavorable anatomy for endovascular treatment. Thoracoabdominal extra-anatomic aorto-aortic bypass with polytetrafluoroethylene graft was successfully performed.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of idiopathic MAS and demonstrates that individualized management based on vascular anatomy can achieve excellent outcomes.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Cross-sectional vascular imaging should be considered in children with resistant hypertension and diminished femoral pulses. Open aorto-aortic bypass remains effective when endovascular treatment is unsuitable.

articles.title: Sarcomatoid Renal Cell Carcinoma With Cardiac Metastasis Causing Right Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) rarely metastasizes to the heart, and an aggressive histologic transformation known as sarcomatoid dedifferentiation confers a poor prognosis.

CASE SUMMARY: A patient presented with progressive exertional dyspnea. Initial laboratory studies revealed elevated troponin and elevated D-dimer. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography showed a right ventricle (RV) filling defect. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a large lobulated mass extending from the RV free wall into the outflow tract, encroaching on the pulmonic valve with an ejection fraction of <20%. Abdominal magnetic resonance imaging revealed a right renal mass. The patient suffered a fatal arrest because of obstructive shock from severe RV outflow tract obstruction.

DISCUSSION: Postmortem examination confirmed metastatic sarcomatoid RCC. Patients typically present with advanced disease, and survival is <1 year. Combination immunotherapy is approved for metastatic RCC. Initiating immunotherapy would not have addressed the patient's acute hemodynamic compromise.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Early recognition of metastatic RCC is crucial for potential therapeutic intervention, though prognosis remains poor in advanced cases.

articles.title: Diagnostic Challenge of Focal Myopericarditis Mimicking Inferior STEMI: When the ECG Misleads.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Focal myopericarditis is an uncommon inflammatory condition that may present with localized ST-segment elevation and closely mimic ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), creating a diagnostic challenge in acute cardiovascular care.

CASE SUMMARY: A 53-year-old man presented with acute pleuritic chest pain radiating to the back, worsened by inspiration and the supine position, and relieved by sitting upright. Electrocardiography demonstrated concave ST-segment elevation in the inferior leads, raising suspicion for inferior STEMI. Urgent coronary angiography revealed nonobstructive coronary artery disease without a culprit lesion. Persistent ST-segment elevation and atypical clinical features prompted cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging, which demonstrated myocardial edema, subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement, and mild pericardial effusion, confirming focal myopericarditis.

DISCUSSION: This case emphasizes the importance of integrating clinical, angiographic, and CMR findings to distinguish focal myopericarditis from STEMI and ensure appropriate management.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: CMR imaging is essential for differentiating inflammatory myocardial injury from acute myocardial infarction.

articles.title: Preoperative Embolization of Mediastinal Mass: A Case for Interventional Cardio-Oncology.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Preoperative embolization of hypervascular tumors can facilitate safe surgical removal by reducing tumor burden and intraoperative bleeding by devascularization. We describe a large mediastinal mass that was embolized by the interventional cardio-oncology team before surgical resection.

KEY STEPS: Prep patient in sterile fashion, anticoagulate with heparin, and obtain radial artery access. Perform coronary and left internal mammary artery angiography; identify tumor blush and feeding artery. Deploy embolization coil via microcatheter into the left internal mammary artery branch; confirm cessation of flow with postembolization angiography. Remove all catheters and sheaths; apply Terumo radial band for hemostasis.

POTENTIAL PITFALLS: Although generally safe, catheter tumor embolization carries risks like nontarget embolization, incomplete occlusion, and coil migration. Additional complications include postembolization syndrome, contrast-related kidney injury, and local vascular and structural injury.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Cardio-oncology is a rapidly developing field with the potential to expand into adjunctive therapies.

articles.title: When the Familiar Diagnosis Doesn't Fit: Metastatic Sarcomatoid Carcinoma Masquerading as Acute Coronary Syndrome.
Air in the Appendage: When Deairing Becomes Air Entrapment.
When Inflammation Meets Ischemia: Cardiac MRI and the Mixed Myocardial Injury Phenotype of Active Lupus.
Treacherous Rhythm: Propofol Infusion Syndrome and Arrhythmogenesis.
Can We Expand the Anatomical Limits of TMVR?
Double Orifice, Single Principle: Respecting the Double-Parachute Mitral Valve.
When the Rescue Device Becomes the Complication: Entrapment of an Intravascular Lithotripsy Balloon.
Transcatheter Heart Valve Thrombosis: Looking Beyond the Valve.
Pulseless Ventricular Tachycardia With Propofol Infusion Syndrome in Severe Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Propofol Infusion Syndrome (PRIS) is a rare, potentially fatal complication of prolonged or high-dose propofol exposure characterized by mitochondrial dysfunction, rhabdomyolysis, metabolic derangements, and cardiovascular collapse. The classically described mode of cardiac death is bradycardia progressing to asystole.

CASE SUMMARY: A previously healthy 21-year-old woman presented 5 days after a vaginal delivery with severe acute respiratory distress syndrome requiring sedation with propofol escalated to 100 μg/kg/min. She developed rhabdomyolysis, acute kidney injury, hyperkalemia, acidosis, and progressive ventricular ectopy that evolved into pulseless ventricular tachycardia. Propofol was stopped, and continuous renal replacement therapy was arranged, but the patient experienced cardiac arrest before initiation. No arrhythmias occurred after metabolic correction.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights pulseless ventricular tachycardia as a rare cardiac manifestation of PRIS with evolving metabolic abnormalities before cardiovascular collapse occurs.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Rhabdomyolysis and hyperkalemia during prolonged propofol therapy should prompt evaluation for PRIS. Early propofol discontinuation and aggressive metabolic correction may prevent fatal ventricular arrhythmias.

articles.title: Highly efficient glycolysis of polyethylene terephthalate catalyzed by a Zn-modified 5A zeolite prepared through ion exchange.
articles.abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is one of the most widely produced polyesters worldwide, but its low recycling efficiency has caused serious environmental pollution and resource waste. Glycolysis is considered an optimal method for closed-loop PET recycling because it works under mild conditions and allows direct recovery of the valuable monomer bis(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (BHET). Catalysts are very important in glycolysis, but most zinc-based solid catalysts reported so far have high costs and are not stable enough, and this makes them hard to use in industrial applications. To solve these problems, this study prepared a series of zinc-modified zeolite catalysts (ZnX-LTA/N&T) using industrial 5A zeolite (LTA) as the support with a simple ion exchange method, and evaluated the effects of the zinc precursor types, ion-exchange cycles, and calcination temperatures on the structure and performance of the catalysts. ZnCl2-LTA/3&400 (prepared with using ZnCl2 as precursor, calcination at 400 °C, and three ion exchange cycles) showed the best catalytic performance with 87.33% PET conversion and 74.23% BHET yield, and also maintained well stability after few recycling runs. Kinetic studies showed that the PET glycolysis followed shrinking core model with activation energy of 184.41 kJ mol-1. In addition, this catalyst also exhibited excellent activity for depolymerizing various real post-consumer PET wastes (films, trays, and beverage bottles), achieving 100% conversion for PET films with a BHET yield of up to 81.93%.

articles.title: Development of AIE active carbazole based fluorescent probe for rapid detection of 4-nitrotoluene in solution and solid phases: experimental and DFT insights.
articles.abstract: A fluorescent probe CPT has been strategically designed and synthesized via Ullmann and Claisen-Schmidt condensation reactions, and its photophysical properties were systematically investigated. Aggregation-induced emission (AIE) with a 25 nm hypsochromic shift, was attributed to aggregate formation. Further, probe CPT exhibited distinct solvatochromic behavior with a 31 nm bathochromic shift. Owing to these unique optical properties, probe CPT serves as an efficient sensing tool for 4-nitrotoluene (4-NT), exhibiting a fluorescence-quenching response via a twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT) and photoinduced electron transfer (PET) mechanism. Probe CPT exhibited a hypsochromic shift of 39 nm upon treating with 4-NT. The interaction mechanism was investigated using 1H NMR, FTIR, mass spectrometry titration, DLS, and DFT calculations. CPT exhibited excellent selectivity and high sensitivity toward 4-NT, with an LOD of 0.16 nM and an LOQ of 0.55 nM. Furthermore, probe CPT exhibited remarkable efficacy in solid and solution-phase sensing of 4-NT, highlighting its potential applicability for monitoring 4-NT in real industrial effluents.

articles.title: Illuminating metabolic disorders with engineered fluorescent carbon dots: advances in biosensing to therapeutics.
articles.abstract: Metabolic diseases, including diabetes, obesity, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, dyslipidemia, and hyperuricemia, represent a major global health challenge, necessitating early diagnosis and effective therapeutic strategies. Conventional approaches may face limitations in sensitivity, specificity, and targeted delivery. In this context, carbon dots have attracted considerable interest as versatile nanoplatforms for metabolic biomarker detection, bioimaging, and potential therapeutic applications. Carbon dots are carbon-based, quasi-spherical nanomaterials characterized by tunable photoluminescence, relatively low toxicity, ease of synthesis, and promising biocompatibility. These properties support their investigation for detecting metabolic biomarkers, including uric acid, glucose, and cholesterol, through sensitive and selective fluorescence-based approaches. Their demonstrated sensing capabilities in controlled environments and spiked biological samples provide a foundation for further investigation toward clinical applications. Similarly, carbon dot-based bioimaging of metabolically relevant organs, such as the pancreas and liver, and their antioxidant and drug-delivery properties highlight their potential for advancing future diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
