Advances in surface engineering and heteroatom doping (e.g., nitrogen, sulfur, and phosphorus) have expanded the potential biomedical applications. CDs are also being investigated as carriers for antidiabetic and lipid-regulating agents, with the potential to improve drug loading, delivery, and release. Furthermore, certain CDs exhibit antioxidant activity that may help mitigate oxidative stress associated with metabolic disorders. These developments highlight the emerging potential of CDs in integrated diagnostic-and-therapeutic, or theranostic, platforms. This review critically examines the applications of CDs in acquired metabolic disorders, emphasizing sensing mechanisms, analytical performance, biological validation, and emerging therapeutic strategies. It also discusses key challenges, including biosafety, biodistribution, pharmacokinetics, long-term toxicity, reproducibility, scalable production, and the gap between laboratory-based findings and clinical translation. Further validation in appropriate biological models and clinical samples is essential before their diagnostic and therapeutic efficacy can be established.

articles.title: Catheter-related thrombosis and fibroblastic sleeve in a cohort of cancer patients with PICC.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: An increasing number of patients with solid and hematologic malignancies require the insertion of peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs) for the administration of therapy. Among device-related complications, catheter-related thrombosis (CRT) and fibroblastic sleeve (FS) are the most common. Although their ultrasound appearance may be similar, their management differs substantially, as only thrombosis requires anticoagulant therapy. Only a few studies have investigated the incidence of these complications.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective study in a cohort of cancer patients with PICCs to assess the incidence of CRT and FS at 7 to 10 and 28 to 30 days after catheter insertion. Associations with the type of underlying malignancy were also evaluated.

RESULTS: Forty-five consecutive patients who underwent insertion of a polyurethane PICC (4 Fr) were enrolled. FS was detected in 11 patients (24.4%): six at 7 to 10 days (13.3%) and five at 28 to 30 days (11.1%). CRT occurred in five patients (11.1%): three cases were detected at 7 to 10 days and two at 28 to 30 days. Three of the five CRT events were symptomatic (6.6%), whereas two (4.4%) were asymptomatic. FS was most frequently observed in patients with gastrointestinal (45.6%) or breast (36.3%) cancer, whereas CRT predominated in gastrointestinal malignancies (60.0%). A non-significant trend toward an association was observed between vein diameter and the type of complication. Finally, a significant association was found between complication timing and platelet count (p = 0.039). However, given the limited number of events and the wide confidence interval, this finding should be interpreted with caution.

CONCLUSIONS: FS is a common but asymptomatic ultrasound finding in cancer patients with PICCs. CRT is less frequent but clinically significant. Accurate differentiation between these two conditions is essential to avoid unnecessary anticoagulation, prevent adverse events, and optimize healthcare resource utilization.

articles.title: External validation of Berg Balance Scale cutoff values for walking among patients with stroke: a retrospective multicenter study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To externally evaluate previously reported Berg Balance Scale (BBS) cutoff values related to walking independence and walking speed in patients with stroke.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this multicenter cross-sectional study, we investigated 349 patients with stroke.We classified study participants as above or below each published BBS cutoff and evaluated each cutoff against two outcomes: independent walking (Functional Ambulation Categories [FAC] ≥4) and community walking speed (comfortable walking speed [CWS] ≥0.8 m/s). Cutoffs developed for comparable target conditions were evaluated as external-validation analyses, whereas cutoffs developed using different walking definitions were evaluated in exploratory cross-outcome analyses. We classified participants as above or below each prespecified BBS cutoff and calculated sensitivity, specificity, positive likelihood ratio (LR+), and negative likelihood ratio (LR-) for each cutoff. A cutoff was considered useful when the LR+ was > 5.0 and the LR- was < 0.2.

RESULTS: For independent walking (FAC ≥ 4), the 48-point cutoff was the only FAC-derived cutoff that met both prespecified LR benchmarks; the 46- and 49-point cutoffs met only one benchmark each. For community walking (CWS ≥ 0.8 m/s), none of the gait-speed-based cutoffs met both LR benchmarks.

CONCLUSIONS: In an independent stroke cohort, the 48-point BBS cutoff showed potentially useful discriminative performance for identifying FAC ≥ 4. No gait-speed-based BBS cutoff met both prespecified LR benchmarks for CWS ≥ 0.8 m/s.

articles.title: Low-Temperature Aqueous Upgrading of Waste PET Plastics into Metal-Organic Frameworks with Confined PdNi Clusters for High-Performance Semihydrogenation of Alkynes.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The selective semihydrogenation of alkynes to alkenes is an important industrial process for the production of bulk and fine chemicals. However, the activity and selectivity trade-off of alkyne hydrogenation has been a long-standing challenge, due to undesirable overhydrogenation or insufficient activity of the designed catalysts. Here, we report a sustainable route for high-performance alkyne hydrogenation using a metal-organic framework (MOF) confined PdNi cluster (PdcNi) catalyst, synthesized directly from waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastics under low-temperature aqueous conditions. The PdcNi@UiO-66 catalyst with dispersed Pd clusters anchored on Ni clusters not only maximizes Pd utilization but also establishes a new pathway for the recycling of plastics. Importantly, when employed as a catalyst for phenylacetylene semihydrogenation, PdcNi@UiO-66 exhibited outstanding activity and selectivity, achieving a turnover frequency (TOF) of up to 67,470 h-1 at 65 °C. This performance significantly surpasses that of previously reported catalysts and is nearly 20 times higher than that of the commercial Lindlar catalyst. DFT calculations combined with experimental results reveal that the PdcNi cluster exhibits a moderate adsorption strength toward both reactants and target products, compared with its nanoparticle and single-atom counterparts. This balanced adsorption leads to a more favorable thermodynamic tendency for styrene desorption rather than overhydrogenation, ultimately contributing to the high activity and selectivity. This study demonstrates a direct route to transforming PET waste into high-performance MOF-based catalysts for selective hydrogenation, offering a cost-effective and sustainable solution for plastic recycling and the development of high-performance catalysts.

articles.title: Clinical and Molecular Evolution During Panitumumab-Containing Therapy in EGFR-Amplified Esophagogastric Adenocarcinoma.
articles.abstract: Esophagogastric adenocarcinoma (EGA) is an aggressive malignancy with limited targeted treatment options. EGFR amplification defines a molecular subset associated with response to EGFR-directed therapy, although mechanisms of resistance remain poorly characterized. We present a 66-year-old man with EGFR-amplified metastatic EGA who achieved a metabolic response on positron emission tomography-CT (PET/CT) during panitumumab-containing therapy, accompanied by loss of detectable EGFR amplification on serial plasma circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA). At progression, repeat tissue biopsy demonstrated HER2 IHC 2+/SISH-positive disease not identified at baseline, and next-generation sequencing identified ERBB2 and KRAS amplifications. These findings suggest ERBB2-mediated bypass signaling as a potential mechanism of resistance to EGFR inhibition, with concurrent KRAS amplification as a possible contributor. It also demonstrates the utility of longitudinal tissue and plasma profiling to capture tumor evolution, identify potential resistance mechanisms, and inform adaptive treatment strategies.

articles.title: The effect of a seven-week online mindfulness intervention on the relationship between menstrual symptoms and mental health - A non-randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menstrual symptoms are common among physically active women and may affect their well-being and performance. Moreover, symptom frequency has been associated with mental health in previous studies. Although mindfulness-based interventions (MBI) have shown beneficial effects on psychological and physiological health outcomes, their potential role in the relationship between menstrual and mental health remains unclear. Therefore, this study examined whether participation in an MBI was associated with changes in this relationship.

METHODS: 39 physically active students were split into an experimental group (EG; n = 14; 22.68 ± 2.23 years) and a control group (CG; n = 25; 22.76 ± 4.88 years), which conducted a baseline and post-intervention measurement, including a psychometric screening. The CG received no intervention during the study and was offered access to the intervention materials afterwards. Assessed constructs included the 21-item version of the Depression Anxiety Stress Scale and the Menstrual Symptom index (MSi). The MBI was developed based on mindfulness-based stress reduction, incorporating the dimensions of acting with awareness, non-judgmental acceptance, and present-moment attention.

RESULTS: At baseline in the control group, MSi scores were positively associated with anxiety (B = 0.16; p = .004) and depression (B = 0.14; p = .012). No significant group × time interactions were observed for depression or stress. For anxiety, the group × time interaction was significant at the grand-mean MSi score (B = - 3.30; 95% CI [- 6.50, - 0.11]; p = .043), whereas the three-way interaction was not significant (p = .054).

CONCLUSION: The results indicate that menstrual symptom frequency is associated with mental health outcomes in physically active students. Participation in the MBI was associated with changes in anxiety over time. However, the non-significant three-way interaction provided no conclusive evidence of moderation. These preliminary findings suggest potential benefits of MBI for anxiety in menstrual health context. Future studies should investigate programs that explicitly address menstrual-related aspects.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered as 'Impact of an online mindfulness intervention on sleep quality in physically active students' in the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS) under the identifier DRKS00038462 on 13 November 2025. Retrospectively registered.

articles.title: Heterotopic pregnancy at Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heterotopic pregnancy, defined as the coexistence of an intrauterine and an extrauterine pregnancy, is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition. While its incidence in assisted reproductive technology pregnancies is well documented, spontaneous heterotopic pregnancy remains exceedingly rare, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. We present the case of a ruptured heterotopic pregnancy in a haemodynamically unstable patient, highlighting the diagnostic and management challenges in a resource-limited setting.

CASE PRESENTATION: We present the case of a 34-year-old Ghanaian woman, Gravida 3 Para 1 (alive) + 1 spontaneous abortion, who presented to the Emergency Unit of the Obstetrics and Gynaecology Department at Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital (KATH) with a 2-month history of amenorrhoea and a 1-day history of abdominal pain. Her vital signs on arrival indicated haemorrhagic shock (blood pressure 69/39 mmHg, heart rate 101 beats per minute). Bedside ultrasound revealed a live intrauterine gestation at 8 weeks with cardiac activity and a left adnexal mass with free fluid in the pelvis. She was resuscitated following the ATLS protocol and underwent emergency exploratory laparotomy under general anaesthesia. Intraoperatively, approximately 1.28 L of hemoperitoneum was drained, and a ruptured left isthmic ectopic pregnancy was identified and managed with total salpingectomy. The intrauterine pregnancy remained viable postoperatively. Progesterone supplementation (Depot Primolut injections and progesterone pessaries 400 mg twice daily) was commenced as institutional practice and continued until 16 weeks of gestation. Serial beta-hCG monitoring confirmed resolution of the ectopic component, with levels declining from 45,000 mIU/mL postoperatively to 12,500 mIU/mL by postoperative day 10. The intrauterine pregnancy progressed to 38 weeks of gestation, and the patient delivered a live female baby weighing 2.5 kg.

CONCLUSIONS: This case underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for heterotopic pregnancy in patients with acute abdominal symptoms, even when an intrauterine pregnancy has been confirmed. Rapid resuscitation, emergency surgical intervention with minimal uterine manipulation, and appropriate postoperative support are critical for maternal and intrauterine pregnancy survival, as demonstrated by the successful delivery at 38 weeks in this case.

articles.title: Pelvic neurology meets multiple sclerosis.
Final Analysis of the BRUIN Phase 1/2 Study Assessing the Safety and Efficacy of Pirtobrutinib Monotherapy in Patients With MCL.
articles.abstract: Pirtobrutinib, a highly selective, non-covalent Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitor (BTKi) previously demonstrated durable efficacy and tolerable safety following covalent (c) BTKi therapy in heavily pretreated relapsed/refractory (R/R) mantle cell lymphoma (MCL). Here, we report final results from the global Phase 1/2 BRUIN trial evaluating pirtobrutinib in patients with R/R MCL, with and without prior cBTKi exposure. Endpoints included overall response rate (ORR), duration of response (DOR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and safety. BRUIN enrolled 166 patients with R/R MCL (data cutoff: 27Jan2025). In the cBTKi-exposed cohort (n = 152), median study follow-up time was 16.1 months (range, 0.5-69.6). The ORR was 49.3% (95% CI, 41.1-57.6). Median DOR was 21.6 months (95% CI, 9.2-27.2). Median PFS was 5.6 months (95% CI, 5.3-9.2; 36-month rate, 19.9%). Median OS was 23.9 months (95% CI, 17.3-51.5; 36-month rate, 43.2%). In the cBTKi-naïve cohort (n = 14), median study follow-up time was 44.5 months (range, 1.6-67.1). The ORR was 85.7% (95% CI, 57.2-98.2). Median DOR was 42.7 months (95% CI, 25.8-not estimable [NE]). Median PFS was 44.6 months (95% CI, 16.7-NE; 36-month rate, 58.7%). Median OS was NE (36-month rate, 76.2%). The most frequent any-grade treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were infections (44.0%), fatigue (31.9%), and diarrhea (22.9%); the most frequent grade ≥ 3 TEAEs were infections (21.1%) and neutropenia (15.1%). Grade ≥ 3 hemorrhage (3.0%) and any-grade atrial fibrillation/flutter (3.6%) were infrequent. With extended follow-up, pirtobrutinib continued to demonstrate efficacy and favorable safety in cBTKi-exposed and -naïve R/R MCL. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03740529.

articles.title: Exploring the relationships between extreme body mass index and pain, somatic health, and psychiatric disorders in adolescents: a multinational analysis of general population data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Both high and low body mass index (BMI) in adolescence have been linked to physical and mental health problems, but these outcomes are rarely examined together. This study examined the associations between BMI categories and self-reported pain, somatic diseases, and psychiatric disorders among adolescents.

METHODS: A total of 5,132 adolescents from five countries (United States, Serbia, Sweden, Morocco, and Vietnam) participated in an online survey conducted between September 2020 and February 2021 as part of the Mental and Somatic Health Without Borders project. After excluding incomplete responses, data from 4,742 participants (mean age = 16.69 ± 1.02 years; 62.1% girls) were analysed. BMI categories were defined using WHO BMI-for-age z-scores, with normal BMI as the comparison group. Group differences were assessed using non-parametric and exact tests with multiple-comparison correction, followed by multivariable regression adjusted for age, gender, and country of residence.

RESULTS: Most participants had normal BMI (approximately 88%); 8.2% had overweight, 3.7% obesity, and 0.34% (n = 16) underweight. In adjusted analyses, adolescents with obesity had higher pain intensity and higher odds of reporting pain "all the time" than those in the comparison group. Overweight and obesity were associated with higher odds of asthma, while obesity was additionally associated with allergies and overweight with thyroid disease. Regarding psychiatric outcomes, overweight and obesity were associated with higher odds of anxiety, whereas obesity was additionally associated with higher odds of depression and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder. Findings involving underweight were less conclusive because of the small number of underweight adolescents and sparse events.

CONCLUSION: Higher BMI categories were associated with distinct patterns of somatic, pain-related, and psychiatric outcomes among adolescents. Obesity showed the broadest pattern of associations, including greater pain burden and higher odds of several somatic and psychiatric conditions. These findings support considering BMI within a broader assessment of adolescent physical and mental health and highlight the value of integrated preventive strategies.

articles.title: Influence of acellular dermal matrix on peri-implant soft tissue phenotype and marginal bone loss following immediate implant placement in the anterior maxilla: a randomized controlled clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immediate implant placement in the anterior maxilla is associated with dimensional changes in both hard and soft tissues, which may compromise esthetic outcomes. This randomized controlled clinical trial aimed to evaluate the effect of acellular dermal matrix (ADM) on peri-implant soft tissue phenotype and marginal bone loss following immediate implant placement.

METHODS: Patients requiring replacement of non-restorable maxillary anterior teeth were randomly allocated into two equal groups. The control group received high-density polytetrafluoroethylene (d-PTFE) membrane coverage, while the study group received ADM. Clinical parameters, including keratinized mucosal width (KMW), mucosal thickness (MT), and supracrestal tissue height (STH), were assessed at 6 months. Plaque accumulation and bleeding were monitored using modified sulcus bleeding index (mSBI) and plaque index (PI) at 1, 2, and 3 months after prosthetic loading. Implant stability was measured at placement and after 6 months. Radiographic outcomes, including marginal bone loss (MBL) and bone width (BW), were assessed using fused CBCT images at baseline and 6 months. In the study group, ADM was inserted into facial and palatal pouches. The primary outcome was peri-implant soft-tissue phenotype at 6 months, assessed by KMW, MT, and STH.

RESULTS: Thirty-three patients were assessed for eligibility, and sixteen patients were randomly allocated into two equal groups (n = 8 per group). All implants survived without complications during follow-up. At 6 months, the study group demonstrated significantly greater keratinized mucosal width (5.9 ± 1.0 vs. 3.3 ± 0.6 mm, p < 0.001), mucosal thickness (1.8 ± 0.3 vs. 0.8 ± 0.3 mm, p < 0.001), and supracrestal tissue height (1.2 ± 0.3 vs. 0.8 ± 0.3 mm, p = 0.012) than the control group. No significant differences between groups were observed in mSBI or PI. Implant stability increased significantly in both groups, with higher values in the ADM group at 6 months (p = 0.010). The study group also exhibited significantly less marginal bone loss, whereas horizontal bone width reduction was comparable between groups.

CONCLUSION: ADM was associated with improved peri-implant soft tissue phenotype and reduced marginal bone loss compared with d-PTFE membranes while maintaining comparable peri-implant health. These findings support the potential use of ADM during immediate implant placement in the anterior maxilla.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was retrospectively registered and listed on www.

CLINICALTRIALS: gov with registration number (NCT07573020) on 07-05-2026.

articles.title: Bedside endoscopy for significant acute upper gastrointestinal bleed.
articles.journal: Indian journal of gastroenterology : official journal of the Indian Society of Gastroenterology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding (AUGIB) is a frequent life-threatening scenario in everyday clinical practice. We undertook a study to assess the etiology and important clinical outcomes in patients with significant AUGIB unstable for transfer to an endoscopy suite.

METHODS: This is a prospective observational study conducted between December 2019 and December 2022, including patients above the age of 16 years with a history of clinically significant AUGIB undergoing bedside endoscopy in an intensive care (ICU)/high dependency unit (HDU) setting.

RESULTS: Seventy patients with a mean age (SD) of 51.27 (13.45) years were included. The initial mean (SD) hemoglobin, APACHE score, SOFA score and GCS of these patients were 6.71 (2.14) g%, 20.3 (8.3), 8.28 (4.64) and 10.9 (4.68), respectively. The major causes for AUGIB were portal hypertension in 28 (40%) and peptic ulcer disease in 24 (34.2%) patients. Eight patients (19.5%) experienced rebleed. Radiological intervention was needed for three patients (4.3%) and surgery for two (2.9%) patients. Overall, 30-day mortality was 54.2%. AUGIB, per se, was the cause for mortality in only 21% of those who died. Sepsis, respiratory failure and liver failure were the factors that independently predicted 30-day mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: This is the first study specifically looking at the role of bedside endoscopy in AUGIB among South Asian patients. The most common etiologies of AUGIB in our cohort were portal hypertension and peptic ulcer disease. Rebleed, surgery and 30-day mortality rates were 19.5%, 2.9% and 54.2%, respectively. A majority of the deaths were due to underlying co-morbidities.

articles.title: Investigating the Physiology of Cannabis Intoxication and Impairment Using Wearable Sensors.
articles.journal: Journal of medical toxicology : official journal of the American College of Medical Toxicology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cannabis decriminalization/legalization has increased the availability and recreational use of cannabis products. Unlike ethanol, there are no standard validated assessments to identify cannabis-induced intoxication and impairment. The objective of this study was to show that wearable sensors can objectively identify cannabis intoxication.

METHODS: This observational study evaluated participants who smoked their personal cannabis products. Heart rate (HR), skin temperature, electrodermal activity, and accelerometry data were continuously collected using a wrist-worn sensor (Empatica EmbracePlus). Participants were assessed using the DRUID© impairment application, the Subjective High Assessment Scale (SHAS) surveys, and 2-minute periods each of sit/stand/walk exercises. Participants performed the study protocol at home while monitored remotely by study staff. The biometric data, DRUID© scores, and subjective intoxication scores were analyzed using descriptive statistics, paired t-tests, Welch tests, and repeated measures analysis of variance (ANOVA). This data was used to train multiple machine learning (ML) models.

RESULTS: Statistical analysis was performed on 17/20 enrolled participants who provided complete data sets. In this cohort, cannabis intoxication caused significant changes in HR and aggregate accelerometry. Non-significant decreases in limb electrodermal activity and increases in limb temperature were recorded. Significant changes in subjective intoxication (SHAS) and objective impairment (DRUID©) were observed. The best performing proof-of-concept ML models were better at detecting subjective intoxication (balanced accuracy of 0.864) than impairment (balanced accuracy of 0.763).

CONCLUSIONS: Wearable sensors can detect physiologic changes in participants intoxicated with cannabis. This biometric data can be used to create ML models to detect cannabis-induced impairment and subjective intoxication.

articles.title: Relationships between cam morphology and [18F]sodium fluoride PET uptake in asymptomatic hips.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Bone deformities are linked to femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) and increased risk of hip osteoarthritis (OA) but are also common in the general population. The purpose of this study is to examine relationships between FAI-linked morphology and resting bone metabolic activity in asymptomatic hips.

METHODS: This exploratory secondary analysis of hip scans from a [18F]NaF PET-MRI study on knee pain included 76 asymptomatic hips from 41 individuals (53 ± 13 years, body mass index 25.9 ± 5.1 kg/m2, 21 female/20 male). Hips were evaluated for cam, pincer, and additional morphology with the Hip Osteoarthritis MRI Scoring System. Mean and maximum PET standardized uptake values (SUV) were recorded for the femoral head-neck junction, center of the femoral head, and anterolateral acetabulum. The influence of morphology on SUVmean and SUVmax was assessed with linear mixed effects models.

RESULTS: Forty-two hips had isolated cam morphology, two had isolated pincer morphology, and four had mixed-type morphology. Cam morphology or alpha angles were not associated with increased bone metabolic activity. Hips with gluteal tendinitis/trochanteric bursitis had significantly higher SUVmax in the center of the femoral head (p = 9.98e-5). No other morphological features were associated with bone metabolic activity, though the low prevalence of features such as pincer morphology limits interpretation of these findings.

CONCLUSION: In older asymptomatic hips without OA, no association was detected between cam morphology and elevated resting bone remodeling. Understanding structure-function relationships in asymptomatic hips with cam morphology may help contextualize findings associated with pain in patients with FAI or OA.

articles.title: Microbiome-wide PheWAS links gut microbial SNVs to health and exposures.
articles.abstract: Alterations in the microbial composition of the human gut have been associated with a wide range of chronic diseases1,2. Yet species-level composition alone can obscure extensive within-species genetic diversity and functional variation. This has driven a shift towards strain-resolved, genetic-level analysis of the microbiome, leveraging microbial genetic variation to identify disease-relevant genes and pathways3-6. Here we conducted a phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) analysing 12.8 million gut microbial single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) with 244 host health phenotypes and environmental exposures in 10,781 individuals from 6 independent cohorts. We identify 940 independent associations across 69 host factors, including age, sex and cardiovascular and metabolic parameters. Structural analyses identified host-phenotype-associated SNVs in functionally important regions of proteins, findings that inform mechanistic hypotheses about how microbial genetic changes relate to environmental and host physiological factors. For example, we identified an age-associated SNV in Faecalibacterium prausnitzii that affects an amino acid within the protein pocket that binds glutathione. To support future efforts, all study summary statistics are provided in an online catalogue ( https://fulab.web.rug.nl/SNV-MWAS/ ). Together, these results identify new biological connections between the human host and microbial genetic variants at base pair resolution and provide a resource for hypothesis generation that will aid future understanding of the strain-level functionality of the gut microbiota.

articles.title: Sequential PCV13-PPSV23 vaccination induces broad functional antibody responses in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
articles.journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are at increased risk of pneumococcal disease because of impaired immune function. Although pneumococcal vaccination is recommended for this high-risk population, evidence describing functional antibody responses following sequential pneumococcal vaccination remains limited. We evaluated naturally acquired and vaccine-induced functional antibody responses against 24 pneumococcal vaccine serotypes in adults with T2DM following sequential PCV13-PPSV23 vaccination.

METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 132 pneumococcal vaccine-naïve adults with T2DM received PCV13 followed by PPSV23 eight weeks later. Functional antibody responses were assessed in 123 paired serum samples collected before and four weeks after PPSV23 administration using the WHO-standardized multiplex opsonophagocytic assay (MOPA). Serotype-specific geometric mean titres (GMTs), geometric mean fold rises (GMFRs), proportions achieving ≥ 4-fold increases, and protective OPA thresholds (≥ 8 and ≥ 64) were evaluated.

RESULTS: Baseline functional immunity varied considerably across serotypes, indicating heterogeneous naturally acquired protection. More than 30% of participants lacked OPA titres ≥ 64 against several clinically important vaccine serotypes, including 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 A, 7 F, 8, 11 A, 12 F, 15B, 18 C, 19 F and 23 F. Sequential PCV13-PPSV23 vaccination induced significant increases in functional antibody responses against all 24 serotypes (p < 0.05). The strongest responses were observed for the shared PCV13 serotypes 6 A, 23 F, 7 F, 18 C, 4 and 19 F, with more than 90% of participants achieving a ≥ 4-fold rise for several of these serotypes. Vaccination markedly increased the proportion of participants attaining protective OPA thresholds across all serotypes. Heterologous immune responses were observed in both age and no significant differences were observed between males and females.

CONCLUSIONS: Adults with T2DM demonstrated heterogeneous baseline functional immunity, leaving substantial proportions inadequately protected against several pneumococcal serotypes. Sequential PCV13-PPSV23 vaccination elicited broad and robust functional antibody responses across all 24 vaccine serotypes and largely overcame baseline immune heterogeneity. These findings provide important functional immunogenicity evidence supporting current pneumococcal vaccination recommendations for adults with diabetes and represent one of the most comprehensive evaluations of WHO-standardized opsonophagocytic responses following sequential pneumococcal vaccination in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Whole-blood NAD levels track cardiovascular disease but not chronological age.
articles.abstract: The extent to which whole-blood NAD levels are altered in human disease or ageing remains controversial. Here we conducted 1,340 measurements in 1,068 adults, and found that whole-blood NAD levels do not decline with age in healthy individuals; they remain stable in males and increase in females, but are reduced in chronic diseases, specifically cardiovascular disease and hypertension. These findings indicate that whole-blood NAD levels track cardiovascular disease rather than chronological age. As this research was not designed to investigate causality, these data do not provide direct evidence that NAD supplementation may serve as a treatment for cardiovascular disease or hypertension.

articles.title: The developmental English Lexicon Project (d-ELP): Continuous word reading difficulty estimates of the 9,961 most frequently printed English words for US children.
articles.abstract: The developmental English Lexicon Project (d-ELP) is a database comprising word reading data for 9,961 of the most frequently printed English words for children, including continuous item response theory (IRT)-based estimates of word reading difficulty, accompanying word characteristics, and raw trial-level data. Data on isolated word reading accuracy were collected from 1,907 children in grades 1-5 across multiple US sites. Each child read a list of words ranging from 250 to 500 items depending on reading skill (less proficient children were often unable to finish the entire list of words), with each list representing the full distribution of word difficulty oversampled for words at the child's reading level. Each child also attempted 99 linking items representing the full distribution of word difficulty. A total of 631,322 responses were collected, with the average child providing 336. For the final sample of words, the average number of responses per word for the 9,862 non-linking items was 47.14 (range of 10-592), and for the 99 linking items the average was 1,681.42 (range of 1,083-1,907). A Rasch model, with planned missing data design, was fit to children's responses on the word list and linking item responses. This introduction describes the motivation for this project, the methods used for data collection, the analytic framework used to establish a continuous measure of word reading difficulty across words, descriptive statistics of the relational database and initial behavioral results, and a publicly available search engine providing searchable access to word difficulty ratings and associated word-level statistics.

articles.title: Real-world morning home blood pressure in a personal health record application and the risk of cardiovascular events.
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract: We aimed to assess whether home blood pressure (BP) self-recorded through a personal health record (PHR) application in a real-world setting was associated with cardiovascular disease (CVD) events among individuals not receiving antihypertensive treatment. Using an insurer-based database that links annual health checkup records and home BP self-recorded in the "kencom" PHR application, 6654 participants (mean age: 51.8 ± 9.1 years, males: 68.0%) not receiving antihypertensive treatment were selected. Morning home BP was calculated as the average of morning values over the first 28 days. Office BP was derived from annual health checkup data. The primary outcome was total CVD identified from hospitalization claims. Cox models were used to assess hazard ratios (HRs). The average of home systolic/diastolic BP was 124.5 ± 13.7/80.9 ± 10.9 mmHg, and 80.6% entered their home BP manually. The correlation between home and office BP was r = 0.56 for systolic and r = 0.61 for diastolic BP. During a mean follow-up of 2.79 ± 1.76 years (18,592 person-years), 447 total CVD events occurred. The HRs for total CVD per 1-SD higher in BP were 1.31 for home systolic, 1.12 for office systolic, 1.32 for home diastolic, and 1.21 for office diastolic BP. Results were consistent for stroke and heart failure. When home and office BP were entered simultaneously into the same model, only home systolic/ diastolic BP was independently associated with total CVD risk. Morning home BP self-recorded by users in a PHR application under real-world conditions was more strongly associated with CVD than office BP, supporting the potential value of PHR-based home BP.

articles.title: Age-specific prognostic value of 1-year changes in cardio-ankle vascular index.
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract: The prognostic significance of longitudinal changes in the cardio-ankle vascular index (CAVI) remains unclear. We investigated the association between 1-year changes in CAVI and subsequent cardiovascular events according to age. A total of 4032 participants with cardiovascular risk factors who were enrolled in the prospective multicenter Coupling Registry and had undergone CAVI measurements at baseline and 1 year were classified into four groups using a CAVI cutoff of 9: good ( < 9 at both time points, n = 1841), improved ( ≥ 9 to <9, n = 268), worsened ( < 9 to ≥9, n = 408), and persistently high ( ≥ 9 at both time points, n = 1515). The primary outcome was a composite of stroke, coronary artery disease, sudden cardiac death, heart failure, and aortic dissection. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models assessed associations between CAVI changes and outcomes. CAVI increased from 8.80 ± 1.34 at baseline to 8.88 ± 1.35 at 1 year (P < 0.001). During a median 60-month follow-up (49-63 months), 155 cardiovascular events occurred. In the overall cohort, neither the worsened group (HR, 1.56; 95% CI, 0.93-2.62) nor the persistently high group (HR, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.72-1.68) was significantly associated with cardiovascular events compared with the good group. Among participants aged <65 years, the worsened group (HR, 3.36; 95% CI, 1.18-9.58) and persistently high group (HR, 2.68; 95% CI, 1.11-6.50) had higher cardiovascular risk. No significant associations were observed among participants aged ≥65 years. In conclusion, among patients aged <65 years with cardiovascular risk factors, both worsening and persistently elevated CAVI were independently associated with increased cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: Long-term fatigue based on the EORTC QLQ-C30 up to five years after radiotherapy and its trajectories in men diagnosed with non-metastatic prostate cancer in the international REQUITE study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fatigue is a common symptom in cancer patients associated with impaired quality of life (QoL). Little is known about long-term fatigue trajectories in prostate cancer (PCa) patients.

METHODS: Using the European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Group Core Questionnaire (EORTC QLQ-C30), 1758 men treated with radiotherapy (2014-2016) for non-metastatic PCa prospectively reported fatigue up to five years later. Associations between pre-radiotherapy characteristics and clinically important fatigue (Score: ≥39/100) two years post-radiotherapy were investigated using logistic regression. Fatigue trajectories were explored using latent class growth analysis and multinomial regression.

RESULTS: About 35% (608/1758) of patients experienced clinically important fatigue at least once from the start of radiotherapy up to five years later. Two years post-radiotherapy, 14% of patients reported fatigue, which was associated with pre-radiotherapy fatigue level (OR: 8.67), self-reported diabetes (OR: 1.94), BMI (OR: 1.07), and age (OR: 1.03). Long-term fatigue was strongly linked to pain, insomnia, pelvic symptoms, functional impairments, and reduced QoL. Four fatigue trajectories were identified, characterised by low (45%), moderate (42%), elevated and decreasing (8%), and (6%) increasing mean fatigue levels. Diabetes was associated with a 6 percentage point increase in the probability of experiencing an increasing fatigue trajectory.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings emphasise the need for early identification of PCa patients susceptible to long-term fatigue. PCa patients with elevated pre-radiotherapy fatigue levels and diabetes may require closer monitoring in risk-stratified aftercare programmes.

articles.title: Impact of Chronological Age, Proton Pump Inhibitors in Older Adults, and Diabetes in Older Adults on Physicochemical Characteristics of Antral Contents During Fasting: An Exploratory Study.
articles.abstract: We explored the impact of chronological age, proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) in older adults, and Type II diabetes in older adults on pH, buffer capacity, lipase activity, pepsin activity, individual bile acids, and osmolality in antral contents during fasting to evaluate whether drug product disposition is likely to differ from healthy adults. Antral contents were aspirated from 20 adults (Reference Group, RG), 14 older adults (Test Group 1, TG1), 7 older adults on PPIs (Test Group 2, TG2), and 6 diabetic older adults (Test Group 3, TG3). All subjects were free of additional conditions likely to confound the luminal characteristics of interest and were living with up to mild frailty. Median TG2 pH (7.84) was significantly higher than the median RG pH (1.75). Median buffer capacity across all groups was 10.38-19.85 mmolNaOH/L/ΔpH. Mean lipase activity was 96.72-124.47 Utrib/mL. Mean TG2 pepsin activity (32,500 USPunits/mL) was significantly lower than mean RG pepsin activity (176,669 USPunits/mL). Based on medians, glycochenodeoxycholic was the most abundant bile acid in TG2; glycocholic was the most abundant bile acid in all other groups. Median total bile acid content across all groups was 98.1-896.4 μM. Median osmolality was 257-328 mOsmol/kg. Chronological ageing is unlikely to affect drug disposition during fasting via changes in the physicochemical characteristics of antral contents. Caution should be exercised when fasted older adults are on PPIs and the drug or the drug product is sensitive to gastric pH and/or pepsin activity. Power-based sample-size estimations might allow for clarifying the impact of Type II diabetes on fasting gastric pH.

articles.title: Navigating technical challenges in the care of infants born at the limits of viability.
articles.abstract: The resuscitation, intensive care and survival of peri-viable extremely premature infants (PVEPT) have been increasing in recent years. The initial care of these infants requires precision when performing a number of procedures after delivery. The multi-disciplinary team within the neonatal intensive care unit requires significant training with graduated autonomy to successfully perform procedures in this population. Preparation, performance and complications of endotracheal intubation, umbilical catheterization, percutaneously inserted central catheter placement, and orogastric tube placement in PVEPTs are reviewed. Experiential approaches are provided to bolster the discussion of these procedures when literature is limited. A review of PVEPT skin physiology is presented, and techniques to secure lines and tubes to minimize skin trauma within environments that do and do not utilize humidity are discussed. IMPACT: The care of peri-viable extremely premature infants requires many precise technical skills from a multidisciplinary team immediately following delivery. Careful preparation, supervised technique, and an understanding of common pitfalls are paramount to procedural success in this population. Careful attention must be paid to the fragile neonatal skin to avoid pain and injury in this patient population.

articles.title: Puberty timing and early adulthood plasma proteome and non-lipid metabolome: a twin study of genetic and environmental contributions.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pubertal timing influences metabolic disease risk, but its links to the plasma proteome and non-lipid metabolome remain unclear. We investigated associations of pubertal development with these profiles in early adulthood and examined genetic and environmental contributions.

DATA AND METHODS: Finnish twins (630, 57% female) reported pubertal development using the Pubertal Development Scale (PDS) at ages 11.5 and 14, and retrospectively via pubertal age (PA) at ~17.5 years. Plasma proteomics and metabolomics were measured at ~22 years. PDS and PA were tested against proteome and non-lipid metabolome molecules using linear mixed-effects models. Significant associations were decomposed into genetic and environmental components using structural equation modeling.

RESULTS: Three plasma proteins (desmoglein-2, CD14, complement C6) and one metabolite (histidine) were associated with PDS at age 14. Desmoglein-2 (rA = -0.08) and CD14 (rA = -0.13) showed genetic but no significant environmental correlations. The C6 association reflected nonshared environmental factors (rE = 0.31), with a non-significant genetic correlation. Histidine showed no clear genetic or environmental contributions.

CONCLUSION: Pubertal development at age 14 influences plasma molecules in early adulthood. Protein associations reflect both genetic and environmental contributions, with weak, suggestive genetic correlations. Puberty may thus be a critical period for long-term metabolic programming.

IMPACT: Pubertal timing at age 14 is associated with specific plasma proteins and metabolites in early adulthood, indicating early-life molecular signatures of metabolic health. Genetic factors may suggestively contribute to some associations (desmoglein-2, CD14), while environmental factors influence others (complement component C6), highlighting targets for personalized risk assessment. These findings suggest that puberty is a critical window for identifying individuals at risk of future metabolic or cardiovascular disorders, offering opportunities for early prevention and intervention strategies.

articles.title: NICU escape rooms: an innovative, gamified approach to team-based interpersonal and communication skills education.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Escape rooms have been studied in other specialties for the current generation of learners, but not in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU). Gamification with escape rooms may address team-based interpersonal and communication skills education.

OBJECTIVE: Assess the impact of implementing a NICU escape room and its role in team-based interpersonal and communication skills education.

METHODS: Participants solved a series of puzzles using core neonatology knowledge to reveal a final clue. Ratings were evaluated using Likert scale-based post-activity and end-of-rotation surveys.

RESULTS: Participation in the NICU escape room addressed team-based interpersonal and communication skills education compared to nonparticipants (mean 3.35 vs. 2.72, p = 0.03). Residents rated the escape room activity significantly higher than morning didactics, noon lectures, and teaching during rounds. There were no differences in the overall NICU education rating or degree of engagement between participants and nonparticipants. On the post-activity survey, mean ratings of the escape room exceeded 4 out of 5 for enhancing the educational experience, engagement, confidence, relevance, and use of interpersonal and communication skills in a supportive environment.

CONCLUSION: NICU escape rooms are a modality for team-based communication and interpersonal skills education, are preferred over other teaching methods, and foster a positive learning experience.

IMPACT: Escape rooms are an innovative way to address the gap in education regarding team-based interpersonal and communication skill development, which is of particular importance for trainees in a high-acuity setting. Escape rooms are an enjoyable, engaging educational activity that are preferred over other didactic methods.

articles.title: Enteric infection and childhood stunting: strengthening causal inference from heterogeneous evidence.
articles.abstract: Laboratory detection of enteropathogens is associated with stunting in observational studies, but the pooled odds ratio does not estimate the effect of infection prevention or treatment on an individual child. Pathogen-domain and age-stratified estimates should not be read as equivalent causal effects; current data cannot reliably distinguish organisms, and environmental enteric dysfunction remains a hypothesized mediator, highlighting the need for prospective, longitudinal research to clarify causality. Prevention should integrate nutrition, infection control, and community-level environmental measures in the first 1000 days; empiric treatment of asymptomatic carriage is not supported, and prospective cohorts plus intervention trials are needed.

articles.title: Comparing MRI-based scoring systems for neuroprognostication in neonatal encephalopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal encephalopathy (NE) remains a significant cause of neurodevelopmental impairment. However, which MRI-based scoring system best predicts 36-month outcomes remains unclear.

METHODS: A prospective cohort of 102 neonates ≥36 weeks gestation with NE underwent early postnatal brain MRI. Images were scored using five established systems: Barkovich, Weeke, Trivedi, Rutherford, and NICHD-NRN. Neurodevelopmental outcomes were evaluated at 36 months. Prognostic performance was analyzed using logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic curves. The best predictive model was determined using pairwise correlation to reduce highly correlated variables, and then backward selection to optimize the linear regression model.

RESULTS: The Weeke total score showed the highest predictive accuracy for Bayley Scales of Infant Development motor outcomes (AUC 0.7647). The Weeke gray matter subscore was most predictive of Child Behavior Checklist internalizing problems (AUC 0.7735). No scoring system reliably predicted cognitive, language, or externalizing problems (AUC < 0.7). The optimal motor outcomes prediction model included 5 Weeke variables: basal ganglia, posterior limb of internal capsule, perirolandic cortex, cerebellar hemorrhage location, and basal ganglia lactate.

CONCLUSIONS: MRI-based scoring systems have limited prognostic value beyond motor outcomes after NE. The Weeke score offers the most reliable motor prediction, achievable using only five parameters.

IMPACT: Existing MRI scoring systems have limited prognostic value beyond motor outcomes after neonatal encephalopathy. The Weeke score offers the most reliable motor prediction. Only 5 Weeke scoring system variables are needed to optimize motor prediction. Deep gray matter injury is associated with internalizing behavioral outcomes. A simplified, user-friendly prognostic model can support accurate outcome prediction by a broader range of clinicians.

articles.title: The hidden burden of cardiovascular risk in working women : A preventive cardiology and gender-sensitive analysis in a hospital workforce.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death among women, yet female-specific and psychosocial risk determinants are inconsistently integrated into preventive strategies. We describe traditional and female-specific risk factors in female hospital employees.

METHODS: In this single-centre, cross-sectional, exploratory study, 111 women aged 34-70 years (nursing, administrative, medical staff) underwent standardised occupational health assessment of lipids, lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)], glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NTproBNP), reproductive history and well-being (WHO-5 Well-Being Index). Voluntary participation may have caused selection bias.

RESULTS: Dyslipidemia was present in 58.6%, hypertension and prediabetes each in 15.3%, and obesity in 14.4%. Median Lp(a) was 20 mg/dl (interquartile range, IQR, 20-65 mg/dl), with 27.9% showing values ≥50 mg/dl. NT-proBNP exceeded 125 pg/ml in 11.7% and correlated with age (ρ = 0.23, p = 0.015). Of 90 participants with at least one pregnancy, 25.3% reported complications. Body mass index (BMI) correlated with HbA1c (r = 0.33, p < 0.001; a possible non-linear BMI-well-being association was non-significant. Among 103 women aged 40-65 years with coronary artery calcium (CAC) data, 22 (21.4%) had CAC > 0 and were older, more often postmenopausal and hypertensive, with higher NT-proBNP.

CONCLUSION: In this exploratory cohort, traditional and female-specific risk factors were prevalent, and a substantial minority already showed subclinical coronary calcification. These findings support prospective evaluation of whether integrating reproductive history, female-specific biomarkers and psychosocial assessment improves risk stratification; causal or predictive conclusions cannot be drawn.

articles.title: CT-derived fractional flow reserve for anatomically long-segment coronary disease: a multicentre diagnostic accuracy study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) for detecting haemodynamically significant coronary disease in patients with anatomically long-segment lesions.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective multicentre study included patients who underwent coronary CT angiography and invasive pressure-wire FFR within 30 days. Anatomically long-segment disease was defined as lesion length ≥ 20 mm. Invasive FFR ≤ 0.80 was the reference standard. CT-FFR was assessed at vessel and patient levels, with patient-level CT-FFR defined as the minimum value per patient and patient-level disease as any invasive FFR ≤ 0.80. Diagnostic discrimination, threshold-based classification, and Bland-Altman agreement were evaluated.

RESULTS: The diagnostic cohort included 329 patients and 377 vessels; 137 patients and 144 vessels had anatomically long-segment disease. At the vessel level, CT-FFR achieved an AUC of 0.941 (95% CI: 0.917-0.966), sensitivity of 94.3%, specificity of 83.7%, and accuracy of 88.6%. In anatomically long-segment vessels, the AUC was 0.961 (95% CI: 0.922-1.000), with sensitivity of 95.7%, specificity of 92.2%, and accuracy of 94.4%. At the patient level, the overall AUC was 0.941 (95% CI: 0.915-0.967) and 0.971 (95% CI: 0.934-1.000) in anatomically long-segment disease. Mean bias was small, although limits of agreement were clinically relevant.

CONCLUSION: CT-FFR showed high diagnostic discrimination for invasive FFR-defined ischaemia, including in anatomically long-segment disease. However, agreement limits and threshold-zone uncertainty support its use as a non-invasive physiological adjunct rather than a direct substitute for invasive pressure-wire assessment.

KEY POINTS: Question Does machine learning-based CT-FFR maintain diagnostic performance for invasive FFR-defined ischaemia in anatomically long-segment coronary lesions? Findings CT-derived FFR showed high diagnostic discrimination overall and maintained performance in anatomically long-segment disease, although subgroup comparisons remained exploratory. Clinical relevance CT-derived FFR may provide non-invasive physiological information in anatomically long-segment coronary disease before invasive angiography, while values near the 0.80 threshold require cautious interpretation.

articles.title: Astrocytes drive stroke-induced glioma progression.
Engineering commensal Lachnospiraceae for programmable therapeutic delivery in the mouse gut.
articles.abstract: Engineered native gut bacteria could offer persistent, programmable therapeutic delivery in the gut, but many dominant taxa remain genetically intractable. Members of one such family of obligate anaerobic Clostridia, Lachnospiraceae, are prevalent in the human gut microbiome and produce metabolites linked to intestinal and metabolic health. Here we report a modular toolkit for engineering Lachnospiraceae, including constitutive and inducible expression, chromosomal integration and secretion systems. Applying this toolkit to gut native Coprococcus comes, we programmed the secretion of cytokine interleukin-22 (IL-22) in the mouse intestinal tract, where it induces epithelial defence transcriptional programmes. In a mouse model of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, IL-22-secreting C. comes improved glucose homeostasis, reduced systemic endotoxemia and attenuated hepatic steatosis. This work demonstrates that native Lachnospiraceae can be genetically programmed to modulate host metabolic and immune physiology. The toolkit provides a foundation for the development of Lachnospiraceae-derived engineered therapeutics and for dissecting causal relationships between commensal gene programmes and host physiology.

articles.title: Decision support and automation in goal-directed fluid therapy: current evidence and remaining questions.
articles.abstract: Goal-directed fluid therapy (GDFT) individualizes perioperative fluid administration according to dynamic hemodynamic variables, but its implementation remains inconsistent and its impact on patient-centered outcomes is still debated. Decision-support and automated systems have been developed to improve adherence, identify fluid responsiveness more efficiently, and reduce the workload of protocolized hemodynamic management. This structured narrative review summarizes the evidence across four outcome levels: process, surrogate hemodynamic, intermediate physiological, and patient-centered clinical. The most consistent evidence concerns process improvement: decision support increases protocol adherence and improves the proportion of fluid challenges that achieve a predefined stroke volume response, largely on non-randomized evidence. Improvements in surrogate hemodynamic control have also been reported, and selected randomized trials suggest favorable effects on microcirculatory flow and lactate. These findings should not be interpreted as evidence of clinical benefit. Fluid responsiveness does not necessarily indicate a need for fluid administration, and most available studies remain small, single-center, or focused on surrogate outcomes. Evidence that these systems improve postoperative complications, acute kidney injury, length of stay, or mortality is currently lacking. Ongoing multicenter trials should address this gap. Decision support appears to improve how perioperative fluids are administered, but whether it improves what ultimately happens to patients remains unresolved.

articles.title: Penile pharmacologic Doppler ultrasound findings in hypertensive patients with erectile dysfunction at the Abidjan Heart Institute.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Penile pharmacologic Doppler ultrasound is an important diagnostic tool for the etiological evaluation of erectile dysfunction. This study aimed to describe its findings in hypertensive patients followed at the Abidjan Heart Institute.

METHODS: We conducted a descriptive cross-sectional study in the outpatient and functional exploration departments of the Abidjan Heart Institute from March 1st to June 30th, 2025. Hypertensive patients aged 18 years or older on regular follow-up were included. Erectile function was assessed using the five-item International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF-5). Patients with erectile dysfunction underwent pharmacologic penile Doppler ultrasound before and after intracavernosal prostaglandin injection. Data were entered with EpiData and analyzed using R software.

RESULTS: Among 210 hypertensive patients, 51 had erectile dysfunction, and 34 underwent penile Doppler ultrasound. The mean age was 61.21±8.04 years. Mild erectile dysfunction was found in 58.8% of patients, and moderate and severe dysfunction in 20.6% each. After prostaglandin injection, complete rigidity was achieved in 35.3%, while 64.7% had an incomplete erectile response. Doppler ultrasound showed no vascular abnomality in 41.2% of patients. Findings suggestive of veno-occlusive dysfunction were the most frequent abnormality, observed in 55.9% of patients, whereas arterial insufficiency was found in 2.9%. No procedure-related complications were reported.

CONCLUSION: Pharmacologic penile Doppler ultrasound provided useful hemodynamic information in the evaluation of erectile dysfunction in hypertensive patients. Findings suggestive of veno-occlusive dysfunction were predominant in our series.

articles.title: Imaging the Neurologic Dog-Part 2: Considerations for Computed Tomography and MRI.
articles.journal: The Veterinary clinics of North America. Small animal practice
articles.abstract: Advanced imaging modalities (computed tomography [CT] and MRI) have become increasingly available and accessible to patients presenting with neurologic disease. Through their 3-dimensional imaging capabilities, both modalities improve localization and diagnosis of neurologic conditions. The information gained from CT and MRI is a function of each modality's type of image formation, the examination parameters or sequence selection, and patient-specific factors, with each modality having its own strengths. This article discusses the role of CT and MRI in the evaluation of neurologic patients and demonstrates the uses and complementary information gained from each of these imaging modalities.

articles.title: Time use diaries as a tool for measuring sleep among individuals incarcerated.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility of using time use diaries to measure sleep and characterize sleep duration and sleep-wake patterns among individuals incarcerated in jail.

METHODS: Adults housed in 2 general‑population units of a Southwestern US jail completed a 4‑day, paper‑and‑pencil time use diary documenting 10-minute activity intervals. Sleep was identified using participant‑reported activities coded with the Compendium of Physical Activities. Sleep was categorized as day- or night-time based on facility schedules. Sleep pattern indicators, including wake‑time, return‑to‑sleep behavior, napping, and bedtime, were classified across valid diary days. Descriptive statistics summarized sleep duration and patterns overall and by sex assigned at jail intake.

RESULTS: Of 64 participants, 62 (96.9%) completed at least one valid diary day; most completed all days, yielding 238 diary days (93.0% completion). Participants averaged 630.8 minutes (10.5 hours) of total daily sleep, with 256.7 minutes (4.3 hours) of daytime sleep and 374.1 minutes (6.2 hours) of nighttime sleep. Females and males had similar total sleep duration. Over half (56.5%) of participants' sleep patterns were not aligned with institutional schedules for programming, meals, and lights out; 83.9% returned to sleep after breakfast (4:30 AM); and 53.2% napped during the day. Half of participants went to bed at lockdown (9:00 PM), while 27.4% went to bed after lockdown. Females with job assignments slept substantially less overall than females without.

CONCLUSIONS: Time use diaries are feasible and informative for measuring sleep among individuals incarcerated in jail. Sleep was fragmented and disproportionately accumulated during the day, reflecting structural constraints of the carceral environment. Findings underscore the need for sleep‑measurement tools tailored to carceral settings.

articles.title: Operationalising the broad definition of pre-eclampsia: a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Early Life Cross Linkage in Research-Born in South London (eLIXIR-BiSL) Partnership
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Identifying pre-eclampsia within electronic health records (EHRs) is challenged by its complex definition, evolving diagnostic criteria, and the nature of routinely collected data. There is a need to optimise methods for EHR-based definitions of this major cause of maternal and fetal and newborn mortality and morbidity.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using pseudonymised data from the Early Life Cross Linkage in Research-Born in South London (eLIXIR-BiSL) cohort, linking routine maternity and neonatal records from two trusts in South London, UK, from Oct 1, 2018, to July 11, 2023. We included women with singleton pregnancies and at least one recorded blood pressure measurement from 20 weeks' gestation who gave birth at one of the contributing NHS trusts, Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust. A broad reference definition of pre-eclampsia, which was in line with current International Society for the Study of Hypertension in Pregnancy and UK National Institute for Health and Care Excellence guidelines and included evidence of maternal end-organ dysfunction or uteroplacental dysfunction, or both, that incorporated structured EHR data, was compared with three case-finding definitions: semi-structured EHR data using drop-down menus (EHR semi-structured definition); ICD-10 codes (ICD-10 definition); and combined semi-structured EHR data and ICD-10 codes (EHR semi-structured and ICD-10 definition). Diagnostic test properties and adverse outcome detection rates were assessed.

FINDINGS: Of 33 040 pregnancies with antenatal booking information, 21 120 pregnancies with booking information, birth outcomes, and blood pressure measurements recorded from 20 weeks' gestation were included. Women at booking had a median age of 33·0 years (IQR 29·0-36·0). Pre-eclampsia prevalence varied by definition: 7·7% (n=1630; reference definition), 4·5% (n=957; EHR semi-structured definition), 3·7% (n=773; ICD-10 definition), and 5·8% (n=1224; EHR semi-structured and ICD-10 definition). Compared with the reference definition, case-finding definitions had inferior detection rates for adverse outcomes, particularly for severe hypertension (26·0% [EHR semi-structured definition], 28·1% [ICD-10 definition], 32·6% [EHR semi-structured and ICD-10 definition]; reference 68·2%) and birthweight <10th percentile (9·7%, 10·6%, 13·3%, respectively; reference 26·2%). Specificity for detection of the reference definition of pre-eclampsia was high (97% [95% CI 97-97]) for all case-finding definitions, whereas sensitivity was poor (29% [26-31] to 37% [35-40]).

INTERPRETATION: Compared with a structured EHR definition, pre-eclampsia definitions relying solely on semi-structured EHR data or ICD-10 codes, or both, underperform in identifying pregnancies with adverse outcomes. The findings highlight the need to integrate structured and semi-structured EHR data to improve pre-eclampsia case ascertainment and emphasise the importance of implementing emerging technologies for mining maternity data.

FUNDING: Medical Research Council, King's College London Centre for Doctoral Training in Data-Driven Health, and PRECISE Network.

articles.title: Persistent hypoperfusion in the Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines: an insufficiently defined treatment trigger.
Risk of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism after simultaneous bilateral knee arthroplasty: A Japanese nationwide medical claims database study.
articles.journal: Journal of orthopaedic science : official journal of the Japanese Orthopaedic Association
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Simultaneous bilateral knee arthroplasty may offer clinical and economic advantages but raises concerns regarding thromboembolic complications. We compared postoperative outcomes between simultaneous bilateral and unilateral knee arthroplasty.

METHODS: Using Japan's nationwide Diagnosis Procedure Combination database, we conducted a retrospective cohort study of hospitalizations for knee arthroplasty between April 2016 and March 2023. Hospitalizations involving simultaneous bilateral knee arthroplasty were compared with those involving unilateral procedures. Propensity score matching was performed based on age, sex, body mass index, surgical procedure (total or unicompartmental knee arthroplasty), comorbidities, and the Charlson Comorbidity Index. Postoperative complications and perioperative outcomes were evaluated.

RESULTS: Among 259,319 eligible hospitalizations, 16,601 matched pairs were identified. In the propensity score-matched cohort, simultaneous bilateral knee arthroplasty was associated with higher odds of deep vein thrombosis (odds ratio [OR], 1.52; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.42-1.63) and pulmonary embolism (OR, 2.49; 95% CI, 1.75-3.56) compared with unilateral surgery. In absolute terms, the risk difference was 4.0% (95% CI, 3.3-4.6) for deep vein thrombosis and 0.38% (95% CI, 0.24-0.53) for pulmonary embolism. Simultaneous bilateral procedures were also associated with a modestly longer length of hospital stay and higher perioperative blood transfusion requirements. In contrast, no statistically significant differences were observed for pneumonia, cerebrovascular events, postoperative cognitive dysfunction, surgical site infection, periprosthetic fracture, or in-hospital mortality.

CONCLUSION: Simultaneous bilateral knee arthroplasty is associated with an increased risk of postoperative deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, despite routine postoperative antithrombotic medications. Careful perioperative management is therefore essential when considering simultaneous bilateral procedures, particularly with regard to thromboembolic risk.

articles.title: Receptor-PET and 2-deoxy-2-[18F]fluoro-d-glucose Concordance-discordance and Flip-flop Phenomenon: Its Implications for Theranostics and Therapeutic Decision-making.
articles.abstract: With the development and expansion of new targeted radiotracers in Theranostics, defining the specific clinical indications for FDG-PET/CT is pivotal to personalised medicine and precision oncology. The "flip-flop" phenomenon refers to the reciprocal yet complementary relationship between lineage-specific receptor PET tracers and FDG PET/CT. However, in real-world scenarios, varying degrees of concordance between receptor-targeted PET and FDG-PET reflect a continuum rather than a binary classification. The concept of dual-tracer/multi-tracer PET, employed in neuroendocrine tumours and castration-resistant prostate cancer, is likely to influence treatment decision-making in other malignancies as well.

articles.title: Fluorodeoxyglucose-PET in Theranostics and Therapeutic Decision-Making of Lung Cancer.
articles.abstract: Fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/computed tomography (CT) is central to lung cancer staging and can alter treatment intent by detecting occult nodal and distant disease. FDG PET/CT contributes to treatment planning, biopsy targeting, radiotherapy delineation and assessment of metabolic response. Quantitative PET parameters provide complementary information on tumor burden, biological aggressiveness, and prognosis. Programmed death-ligand 1, fibroblast activation protein, and somatostatin receptor PET extend molecular imaging toward noninvasive assessment of tumor phenotype and potential theranostic targets. Artificial intelligence and radiomics may characterize tumor heterogeneity and predict molecular phenotype and treatment response but require further standardization and validation.

articles.title: Critical Role of Novel PET-Computed Tomography/MR Imaging-Based Quantitative Techniques in Assessing Efficacy of Theranostics.
articles.abstract: Theranostics pairs a molecularly targeted diagnostic imaging agent with its therapeutic counterpart, enabling personalized, molecularly guided therapy. Although 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/computed tomography is not itself a theranostic radiopharmaceutical, it complements the theranostic workflow from patient selection and treatment planning of primary and metastatic sites to quantitative response assessment. This article reviews novel PET-computed tomography/MR imaging-based quantitative techniques for assessing theranostic efficacy, including volumetric and global disease burden metrics, kinetic modeling, and multimodality integration, with applications in thoracic malignancies, metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, and neuroendocrine tumors.

articles.title: Can a Single Maximally Fortified Food Improve Glycaemia in Type 2 Diabetes? Randomised Crossover Trial of High-Fibre High-Protein Bread.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the effects of a maximally fortified high-fibre high-protein bread on glycaemia in free-living adults with Type 2 diabetes.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Participants were provided commercially produced high-fibre high-protein bread (fibre 8.1 g and protein 19.5 g/100 g) fortified with lupin flour, pea protein and wheat fibre or refined grain bread control (fibre 2.9 g and protein 10.4 g/100 g) for 2 weeks in random order, separated by a 2-week washout. Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), fasted blood samples, anthropometry and three-day dietary records were collected during each intervention period. The primary outcome was postprandial glycaemia measured by all-meal incremental area under the curve (iAUC) with CGM during both interventions.

RESULTS: Thirty-three adults (mean age 57.9 ± 12.6 years, BMI 33.1 ± 7.5 kg/m2, HbA1c 60.1 ± 15.1 mmol/mol) were randomised, with 31 completing both interventions. Dietary energy intake was comparable between interventions, while fibre and protein intakes were higher during the high-fibre high-protein bread intervention. Compared with control bread, the high-fibre high-protein bread improved glycaemic metrics, including all-meal iAUC (-21 mmol L-1 min-1 [95% CI: -39 to -3]), time in range (4.1% [95% CI: 2.2-6.1]), time above range (-4.3% [95% CI: -6.3 to -2.4]) and glycaemic variability (CONGA -0.4 [95% CI: -0.5 to -0.2]). Systolic (-7.2 mmHg [95% CI: -11.2 to -3.2]) and diastolic (-7.2 mmHg [95% CI: -9.9 to -4.6]) blood pressure also improved. No differences were observed between interventions for anthropometry, lipid profile or C-reactive protein.

CONCLUSIONS: Use of a single food, maximally fortified with fibre and protein, improved glycaemia in type 2 diabetes management compared with an unfortified equivalent over 2 weeks. Reformulation of common staples with these two nutrients presents a practical and scalable strategy for manufacturers to support diabetes management.

articles.title: Deriving the anticholinergic medication index for delirium and falls in older people: development and external validation of a risk prediction model.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop the anticholinergic medication index (ACMI), a new anticholinergic burden measure derived from a clinical prediction model for falls and delirium, scoring 88 anticholinergic medicines prescribed in primary care.

DESIGN: Development and external validation of a risk prediction model.

SETTING: UK primary and secondary care data from Connected Bradford and the Secure Anonymised Information Linkage (SAIL) databank, 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2019.

PARTICIPANTS: For development cohort, 71 757 Bradford and Craven residents aged >65 years on 1 January 2019 who contributed data to Connected Bradford between 1 January 2019 and 31 December 2019. For external validation cohort, 678 134 Welsh residents aged >65 years on 1 January 2019 who contributed data to SAIL between 1 January 2019 and 31 December 2019.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Composite outcome of hospital admission for delirium or hospital admission for a fall or fracture (as an indicator of an injurious fall) during the study period.

RESULTS: 71 757 patients (4147 (5.8%) with the composite outcome) comprised the development cohort and 678 134 patients (43 675 (6.4%) with the composite outcome) comprised the external validation cohort. Based on anticholinergic medications recorded in electronic health records as predictors, a prediction model for falls and delirium was developed and validated. Model coefficients for anticholinergic medications were transformed into ACMI scores. Of 88 anticholinergic medications, codeine, prednisolone, and furosemide were the most commonly prescribed (8.3%, 6.5%, and 6.0% of patients prescribed these anticholinergic drugs at least once in the development cohort, respectively). Model discrimination and calibration in the development cohort was good (C index=0.794, R2=0.06, calibration slope=0.97). The model performed well in external validation with good discrimination (C index=0.721, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.718 to 0.734, R2=0.04) but with some evidence of miscalibration (calibration slope=0.69). The ACMI medications were scored 0.1 (desloratadine) to 2.3 (amantadine).

CONCLUSIONS: The ACMI was designed to be implemented in primary care to automatically calculate anticholinergic burden. Combined with the model predicted risk of delirium or falls, the ACMI allows clinicians to prioritise patients for structured medication reviews to reduce overprescribing.
