articles.title: Mortality trends in alcohol-related liver disease and chronic hepatitis and fibrosis or cirrhosis not coded as alcohol-related: a population-based analysis of US CDC WONDER data, 1999-2020.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare US mortality trends for alcohol-related liver disease coded as K70 with chronic hepatitis and fibrosis or cirrhosis coded as K73–K74 and not coded as alcohol-related, and to quantify changes in standardised rates, death counts, counterfactual mortality and age–period–cohort patterns.

METHODS: We analysed US CDC wide-ranging online data for epidemiological research (CDC WONDER) underlying-cause of death data for 1999–2020. Alcohol-related liver disease was defined by ICD-10 K70; the comparison category comprised K73–K74. National trends were assessed using joinpoint regression. Changes between pooled 2000–2002 and 2017–2019 rates were evaluated using direct standardisation and Das Gupta decomposition. Counterfactual deaths were estimated by applying pooled 2000–2002 age-specific rates to subsequent populations. Age–period–cohort models estimated identifiable temporal functions.

RESULTS: From 1999 through 2020, 373 302 K70 deaths and 369 661 K73–K74 deaths occurred. The K70 age-adjusted mortality rate increased from 4.34 to 7.86 per 100 000; the average annual percentage change was 2.73% (95% CI 2.26% to 3.09%). The K73–K74 rate changed from 5.21 to 5.42 per 100 000, with a non-significant average annual change of 0.15% (95% CI −0.05% to 0.34%). Between 2000–2002 and 2017–2019, standardised K70 mortality increased by 2.90 per 100 000, whereas K73–K74 mortality decreased by 0.40 per 100 000; K70 accounted for 116.2% of the increase within the combined analytic universe. Mean annual deaths increased by 16 040, of which population size, age structure and mortality rates accounted for 6576, 3728 and 5736 deaths, respectively. During 2003–2019, 49 373 more K70 deaths and 15 449 fewer K73–K74 deaths occurred than expected. Relative K70 increases were fastest at ages 25–34 years, whereas the largest excess-death burden occurred at ages 50–64 years. K70 net drift was 2.684% annually; K73–K74 net drift was −0.252% and non-significant.

CONCLUSION: K70 mortality increased substantially, while K73–K74 mortality changed comparatively little. These findings apply to the prespecified cause-code categories and do not represent a comparison with all other chronic liver diseases.

articles.title: Clinical phenotype, disease burden and inter-regional heterogeneity of axial spondyloarthritis in 1112 patients across 15 Arab countries: the PROSPA study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterise the phenotype, disease burden, comorbidities, patient-reported outcomes (PROs) and treatment patterns of axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) across Arab countries and evaluate regional heterogeneity.

METHODS: Profile of Axial Spondyloarthritis in Arab Countries (PROSPA), a cross-sectional, multinational study by the ArLAR Research Group across 33 rheumatology centres in 15 countries, enrolled adults with axSpA during a routine visit. Standardised data on validated PROs, disease characteristics, comorbidities and treatment were collected. Patients were stratified by Arab subregion (North Africa, the Levant and the Gulf). Between-group comparisons used Welch analysis of variance, Kruskal-Wallis and χ2 tests. Mixed-effects modelling tested whether regional differences in Assessment of SpondyloArthritis international Society Health Index (ASAS-HI) remained independent after adjustment.

RESULTS: Of 1112 patients (mean age 42.6 years, median disease duration 10 years, 63.8% male), radiographic (r) predominated over non-radiographic (nr) axSpA (r/nr ratio 3.7). Peripheral arthritis occurred in 45.7%, coxitis in 31.7%, uveitis in 16.7% and psoriasis in 17.4%. Human leucocyte antigen B27 was positive in 51.5% of 615 tested. Disease activity was moderate to high; biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (bDMARDs) were used in 70.1%, 36.4% were people who smoke and 5.2% had a tuberculosis history. North Africa had the highest r/nr ratio, worst PROs and lowest bDMARD use, despite comparable disease activity. Regional differences in ASAS-HI did not persist after adjustment; disease activity and function accounted for most explained variance.

CONCLUSIONS: This largest multinational axSpA study revealed a predominantly radiographic phenotype, significant disease burden and a comorbidity profile marked by high smoking and tuberculosis rates. After adjustment, region was not independently associated with ASAS-HI; disease activity and function, rather than geography, explained most of the variance in health status.

articles.title: Perioperative respiratory adverse events in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy with laryngeal mask airway versus endotracheal tube ventilation: multicentre, randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the effect of ventilation with a laryngeal mask airway (LMA) compared with endotracheal tube (ETT) on perioperative respiratory adverse events (PRAEs) in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy.

DESIGN: Multicentre, randomised, parallel group trial.

SETTING: Four tertiary hospitals in China, 2023-24.

PARTICIPANTS: 400 children aged ≥2 years and <7 years who were scheduled for adenotonsillectomy under general anaesthesia.

INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomised 1:1 to receive ventilation with a laryngeal mask airway (n=200) or an endotracheal tube (n=200) during adenotonsillectomy.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: The primary outcome was the proportion of participants who developed any perioperative respiratory adverse event (PRAE): laryngospasm, bronchospasm, desaturation, airway obstruction, severe cough, or stridor in the intention-to-treat population.

RESULTS: 400 children (mean age 4.7 (standard deviation 1.0) years; 155 (38.7%) girls) were enrolled between 24 May 2023 and 4 April 2024, with last follow-up on 4 May 2024. LMA was converted to ETT in three participants. Overall, 22.5% (45/200) participants in the LMA group experienced PRAEs versus 57.5% (115/200) in the ETT group (absolute risk difference -35.0 percentage points, 95% confidence interval -43.5 to -25.7; P<0.001). The LMA group had fewer PRAEs in both the intraoperative (9.0% (18/200) v 17.5% (35/200); -8.5, -15.2 to -1.8; P=0.01) and the postoperative period (16.5% (33/200) v 49.5% (99/200); -33.0, -41.2 to -24.0; P<0.001). The LMA group also had a lower proportion of participants with laryngospasm (0.0% v 3.0%; P=0.03), desaturation (15.0% v 28.0%; P=0.002), airway obstruction (3.5% v 12.5%; P<0.001), and severe cough (10.5% v 42.0%; P<0.001). Neither group experienced serious adverse events.

CONCLUSION: Ventilation with an LMA by experienced anaesthesiologists resulted in fewer perioperative respiratory adverse events than ventilation with an ETT in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chictr.org.cn ChiCTR2300071399.

articles.title: High-grade atrioventricular block in a patient with an Albright hereditary osteodystrophy phenotype.
Interventions for adhesive capsulitis: systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the benefits and harms of therapeutic interventions for adhesive capsulitis.

DESIGN: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

DATA SOURCES: Medline, Cochrane Library, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched from inception to 1 May 2025, with an update in November 2025.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA FOR SELECTING STUDIES: Randomised controlled trials enrolling adults with adhesive capsulitis, comparing active treatment with another intervention, placebo, or usual care.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Pain, function, range of motion, and adverse events.

RESULTS: A total of 189 randomised controlled trials involving 12 988 participants and 59 interventions were included. Most trials contributing to principal outcomes were at high risk of bias (71% for pain, 72% for function, and 71% for range of motion). At short term follow-up, moderate certainty evidence suggested that extracorporeal shockwave therapy probably reduced pain compared with usual care (mean difference -1.97 on a 0-10 scale, 95% confidence interval (CI) -2.97 to -0.97). Low certainty evidence suggested that extracorporeal shockwave therapy may improve function (mean difference -11.42 on a 0-100 scale, 95% CI -16.68 to -6.15), although direct and indirect estimates were limited by important incoherence. For short term range of motion, moderate certainty evidence suggested that manipulation under anaesthesia combined with intra-articular steroid injections probably improved flexion (mean difference 33.29°, 95% CI 11.19° to 55.39°), as did manipulation under anaesthesia alone (26.16°, 8.19° to 44.13°). Low certainty evidence suggested that extracorporeal shockwave therapy may improve flexion (22.42°, 12.99° to 31.84°) and abduction (18.62°, 8.09° to 29.14°), but both comparisons were limited by important incoherence. At mid-term follow-up, evidence for possible improvements in function with extracorporeal shockwave therapy and flexion with passive mobilisation was of low certainty, while evidence for pain reduction with extracorporeal shockwave therapy was of very low certainty. Most other comparative estimates were supported by low or very low certainty evidence. Comparative safety remained highly uncertain because adverse events were incompletely and inconsistently reported; the absence of reported adverse events should not be interpreted as evidence of absence of harm.

CONCLUSION: Moderate certainty evidence suggests short term pain reduction with extracorporeal shockwave therapy and improved short term flexion with manipulation under anaesthesia, with or without intra-articular steroid injections. Most other treatment effects remain uncertain because of low certainty and incoherence, and comparative safety and mid-term effects are poorly established. The available evidence is mainly short term and outcome specific. Longer term comparative effectiveness, overall benefits and harms, and applicability beyond predominantly primary adhesive capsulitis remain uncertain.

SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420251070468.

articles.title: Probable Deferasirox-Associated Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure in Non-Transfusion-Dependent β-Thalassemia with Iron-Related Cirrhosis: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Oral iron chelation with deferasirox is widely used to manage iron overload in patients with thalassemia syndromes. Clinically significant drug-induced liver injury (DILI) attributed to deferasirox is uncommon but has been reported. We describe a 49-year-old man with non-transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia intermedia (β-thalassemia trait with α-globin gene triplication), substantial iron overload, cirrhosis, and previously treated hepatocellular carcinoma who developed acute hepatic decompensation during deferasirox therapy. He presented with progressive jaundice, ascites, and encephalopathy. Laboratory evaluation showed profound conjugated hyperbilirubinemia with relatively modest aminotransferase elevations, consistent with a predominantly cholestatic pattern of injury. Causality assessment using the Roussel Uclaf Causality Assessment Method (RUCAM) yielded a score of 7, indicating a probable association with deferasirox. Despite drug withdrawal and supportive care, including plasma exchange, liver failure persisted, and the patient was evaluated for urgent transplantation. This case underscores the vulnerability of patients with limited hepatic reserve to chelator-associated hepatotoxicity and highlights the need for individualized chelation strategies and close biochemical monitoring.

articles.title: Real-World Use and Expert-Guided Optimization of a Large Language Model-Based Pediatric Health Assistant: Retrospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric care resources are limited and unevenly distributed in many health systems. Caregivers increasingly turn to large language models (LLMs) for children's health information, but real-world evidence on LLM use and response quality in general pediatric care is limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to characterize real-world use, consultation needs, and response quality of Xiaoyi, an LLM-based pediatric health assistant, and to evaluate the impact of expert-guided optimization on response quality.

METHODS: This study collected all consultation sessions submitted between April 7 and December 31, 2025, to Xiaoyi, a pediatric health assistant co-developed by Children's Hospital of Chongqing Medical University and Zuoyi Tech. Temporal patterns of consultation activity were characterized; all sessions were annotated for pediatric subspecialty, reason for consultation, and presenting symptoms through LLM-assisted labeling with pediatrician validation. A multidisciplinary panel of 40 pediatricians evaluated Xiaoyi's response quality over 2 rounds using predefined criteria established by expert consensus: an initial evaluation informed system optimization (prompt revision, knowledge-base and tool expansion, and validation rules) and a follow-up evaluation assessed its impact. In each round, 1000 sessions randomly sampled from the corresponding pre- or postoptimization period (2000 in total) were rated at the session level (overall quality and clinical appropriateness) and the turn level (6 predefined deficiency categories). Categorical ratings were compared using the chi-square test, and turn-level deficiency rates were compared using generalized estimating equations to account for within-session correlation.

RESULTS: Caregivers of 8266 children (median age 4.2, IQR 1.3-8 years; 4705/8266, 56.9% male) from 31 of 34 provincial-level divisions in China initiated 16,074 sessions, of which 7046 (43.8%) occurred outside routine clinic hours (08:00-17:30). Queries spanned 31 subspecialties, most frequently child health care (2025/16,074, 12.6%), pulmonology (1903/16,074, 11.8%), and gastroenterology (1833/16,074, 11.4%). The leading reasons for consultation were symptom consultation (7845/16,074, 48.8%), medical report interpretation (2531/16,074, 15.7%), and triage guidance (2515/16,074, 15.6%); among symptom consultation sessions, fever (2719/16,074, 34.7%) and cough (2349/16,074, 29.9%) were most common. After expert-guided optimization, the number of sessions rated good (n=1000) in overall quality (the response fully resolving the caregiver's question with actionable information) increased from 652 (65.2%) to 743 (74.3%), and the number rated clinically appropriate increased from 614 (61.4%) to 874 (87.4%, both P<.001). The turn-level deficiency rate declined from 19.4% (790/4073 turns) to 6.9% (236/3419 turns; odds ratio 0.30, 95% CI 0.24-0.37; P<.001), with suboptimal clinical recommendations (not optimally tailored to the child's age or clinical context) remaining the most frequent category.

CONCLUSIONS: This real-world study suggests that an LLM-based health consultation assistant may complement existing pediatric care, with expert-guided optimization substantially improving response quality. However, the persistence of deficiencies highlights the need for continued monitoring and refinement to ensure clinical reliability.

articles.title: Efficacy of Dupilumab in Patients From China With Persistent Type 2 Asthma With and Without an Allergic Phenotype.
articles.journal: Clinical and experimental allergy : journal of the British Society for Allergy and Clinical Immunology

articles.title: High-frequency rTMS improves post-stroke cognitive impairment and is associated with region-specific BBB remodeling and increased pericyte coverage.
articles.abstract: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) remains without effective disease-modifying therapies. Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) is a promising noninvasive intervention, but whether its beneficial effects are associated with blood-brain barrier (BBB) remodeling and pericyte coverage remains unclear. In this study, adult male Sprague-Dawley rats underwent transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) or sham surgery. Beginning on post-operative day 7, tMCAO rats received either restraint-only handling or 20-Hz rTMS once daily for 21 consecutive days. Behavioral performance, cerebral blood flow (CBF), infarct volume, BBB leakage, and vascular remodeling were evaluated using behavioral tests, laser speckle imaging, TTC staining, immunofluorescence, and Western blotting. High-frequency rTMS improved cognitive performance and reduced anxiety-like behavior after stroke. These behavioral benefits were accompanied by increased ipsilateral CBF, although infarct volume was not significantly reduced. Moreover, rTMS was associated with partial, region-specific BBB remodeling, including reduced cortical IgG leakage, increased vascular Occludin expression, and enhanced pericyte coverage, particularly in the hippocampus. Evans blue extravasation showed a nonsignificant trend toward reduction. In conclusion, subacute high-frequency rTMS improved behavioral outcomes after stroke and was associated with region-specific BBB remodeling and increased pericyte coverage. These findings suggest that vascular and perivascular remodeling may contribute to the beneficial effects of rTMS in PSCI.

articles.title: From metabolic dysfunction to neurodegeneration: mechanisms and hierarchical candidate biomarkers in diabetes-associated cognitive impairment.
articles.abstract: Diabetes-associated cognitive impairment (DACI) is a common complication of diabetes that severely affects patients' quality of life. However, biomarkers for its clinical diagnosis and treatment remain limited. DACI pathogenesis involves hyperglycemia, advanced glycation end products (AGE)-receptor for AGE interactions, insulin resistance, and lipid metabolism disorders, which induce oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neuroinflammation. Neurons, microglia, and astrocytes are key cellular mediators. Metabolic disorders directly impair neuronal energy metabolism, synaptic plasticity, and neurogenesis, while microglial activation and functional reprogramming, astrocytic lipid synthesis, and synaptic remodeling further promote neuronal dysfunction and cognitive decline. This review distinguishes clinically investigated biomarkers from genetic susceptibility factors, emerging mechanistic candidates, evaluates them by evidence level and potential clinical roles in risk assessment, diagnosis, disease monitoring, treatment-response assessment, and therapeutic targeting. Integrating mechanistic and biomarker evidence provides a framework for future research, early diagnosis, and targeted therapeutic development. However, many candidate biomarkers have been investigated primarily in preclinical models or related diseases such as Alzheimer's disease and require systematic validation in well-characterized human DACI cohorts.

articles.title: Contrast-Associated Acute Kidney Injury Following Recanalization Of Chronic Total Coronary Occlusions In A Large Multi-Center Registry.
articles.abstract: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) is a risk of percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) for chronic total coronary occlusions (CTO), and complex interventional procedures in general. The incidence and temporal changes of CA-AKI with contemporary CTO techniques had not been evaluated before in a large registry. Therefore, we analyzed 12911 CTO procedures by 27 operators between 2015 and 2024 with pre and postprocedural serum creatinine (SCr) assessment. CA-AKI was defined as an increase in SCr ≥0.3 mg/dl or ≥50% from baseline SCr. In addition, an older definition was applied as CIN (Contrast induced nephropathy: SCr increase ≥0.5 mg/dl or ≥25% of baseline). The incidence of CA-AKI was 3.91% with a slight temporal decrease from 5.0% in 2015 to 3.7% in 2024. CIN was 5.96%, however, the operator-reported CIN was only 1.68%. The major determinants of CA-AKI were age, diabetes, peripheral disease, reduced ejection fraction, chronic kidney disease stage ≥2, and fluoroscopy time. The highest impact had the incidence of pericardial tamponade. Procedural perforations were more frequent in CA-AKI patients (10.3 vs 3.3%; p<0.001), and in-hospital mortality (0.9 vs 0.2%; p<0.001) was increased. Contrast volume (CV) was one of the determinants of CA-AKI. No CA-AKI occurred in procedures with <50ml, which was achieved in only 0.5%. In conclusion, CA-AKI remains a relevant procedural complication of CTO PCI even with modern techniques with a slight decrease during the past decade and reduced CV use. Pericardial tamponade had the strongest association with CA-AKI. Ultra-low contrast PCI may not be feasible in an all-comer cohort.

articles.title: Early Readmission After Complex PCI.
Exercise exposure and arrhythmic patterns in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exercise is associated with ventricular arrhythmias (VA) in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC), but relationships with atrial fibrillation (AF) and arrhythmic patterns are less established.

OBJECTIVE: To assess prior exercise intensity and dose in relation to AF, VA, and combined arrhythmic patterns across the ARVC diagnostic spectrum.

METHODS: Genotype-positive probands and relatives were included. Exercise during the three years preceding diagnosis was assessed retrospectively by structured interview. Intensity was defined by the primary activity's Metabolic Equivalent of Task (MET) and dose as MET-hours/week across activities. AF and VA were assessed at first visit and last follow-up.

RESULTS: We included 122 individuals (49% women; mean age 39±17 years), with a median follow-up of 13.5 years. AF prevalence increased from 5% to 21% and VA from 26% to 37%. Median onset ages were 55 years for AF and 36 years for VA. Both exercise measures were associated with VA at both time points. Exercise dose was associated with AF at first visit and intensity at last follow-up. Median exercise dose increased across groups with no arrhythmia, AF only, VA only, and both. The association between AF and VA at last follow-up was attenuated after adjustment for exercise intensity (adjusted OR 2.43, 95% CI 0.85-6.97, p=0.10).

CONCLUSIONS: Associations with exercise was consistently associated with VA, but varied for AF by measure and time point. The graded distribution does not establish thresholds or sequential progression. Co-occurrence may reflect shared exercise history, disease susceptibility, and differential surveillance rather than a direct relationship.

articles.title: Microgravity and Cardiac Electrophysiology: Autonomic Remodeling, Arrhythmogenesis, and Implications for Long-Duration Spaceflight.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In microgravity, the human heart undergoes significant geometric and functional remodeling due to the removal of gravity-dependent hydrostatic gradients. These adaptations include a transition from an elliptical to a more spherical shape configuration. Furthermore, cephalad fluid shifts trigger an early spaceflight diuresis, inducing a stable reduction in circulating plasma volume.

OBJECTIVE: To describe resulting electrophysiologic alterations and arrhythmia promotion.

METHOD: While most spaceflight arrhythmias are transient and non-lethal, they remain a concern for long-duration missions. Frequently reported irregularities include isolated premature atrial and ventricular complexes. Other events, including non-sustained ventricular tachycardia during spaceflight, the possibility of early-onset atrial fibrillation, and atherosclerosis in former astronauts following exposure to high-energy ionizing radiation have been documented, though the association is still being evaluated. The underlying arrhythmogenic substrate is driven by autonomic resetting, spatiotemporal heterogeneity, and QTc interval prolongation.

RESULTS: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration utilizes a multi-faceted approach to maintain electrical stability, incorporating high-intensity interval training and electrolyte monitoring and supplementation. Real-time monitoring of wearable technology enables continuous telemetry of the heart. Recently, automated chest compression devices have been shown to significantly outperform manual cardiopulmonary resuscitation in microgravity environments.

CONCLUSION: Although structural changes typically revert to baseline upon return to Earth gravity, deep-space missions present some risks. Astronauts exposed to ionizing radiation beyond Earth's magnetic field may face risk of long-term cardiovascular disease. Design of personalized nutrition to mitigate electrolyte loss and development of advanced screening tools for cardiac risk assessment are essential to improve the safety of future planetary missions.

articles.title: Local Conformal Auditing Exposes and Restores Reliability of AI-ECG Atrial Fibrillation Detection Under External Deployment Shift.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: AI-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) can detect atrial fibrillation (AF), but safe deployment depends on calibration, subgroup reliability, and explicit error guarantees, not on discrimination alone.

OBJECTIVE: To test whether the conformal-prediction coverage guarantee of an AF ECG classifier survives external deployment shift, and whether a small local labeled audit restores it without retraining.

METHODS: A four-class 12-lead rhythm classifier trained on PTB-XL (Germany; 7,831 ECGs, 7,164 patients) was evaluated unchanged on Chinese (Chapman-Shaoxing; n=2,289) and US (Georgia; n=1,990) cohorts. We measured discrimination, expected calibration error (ECE), 90%-target split-conformal coverage, subgroup coverage, label-free shift corrections, local recalibration across audit sizes, and an AF auto-clear policy with finite-sample risk control.

RESULTS: AF AUC remained 0.998 (95% CI 0.997-0.999) in China but fell to 0.936 (0.919-0.952) in the US cohort. ECE rose from 0.051 to 0.197 and 0.237, and source-calibrated coverage fell from 0.901 to 0.758 and 0.722 (both P<0.001). Coverage was lower in Chinese men than women (0.707 vs 0.822; difference 0.115, 95% CI 0.081-0.148). Label-free corrections failed. Local recalibration restored mean coverage to 0.90 with 50 labeled ECGs but with wide variability (95% simulation interval 0.82-0.97), narrowing to 0.86-0.94 at 200 ECGs. Local AF risk control certified auto-clearing of 68% of held-out ECGs in China but abstained in the US cohort.

CONCLUSION: AI-ECG uncertainty can fail silently despite high AUC. A local conformal audit detects when uncertainty estimates are untrustworthy and recalibrates the uncertainty layer without changing the classifier, converting trust into a measurable, subgroup-aware, task-specific guarantee.

articles.title: Examining inequalities: cautions and considerations when shifting intersectional MAIHDA from a descriptive to a causal inference framework.
articles.abstract: Intersectional MAIHDA (multilevel analysis of individual heterogeneity and discriminatory accuracy) is a method for analysing intersectional inequalities that is increasingly popular in health-related research. The method is characterised by its unusual application of a standard multilevel modelling framework, which allows users to describe inequalities in an outcome across multiple intersecting characteristics simultaneously. It does this by nesting individuals within the relevant combination of intersecting characteristics, or strata. Intersectional MAIHDA and its closely related approaches (including multicategorical MAIHDA and Eco-Intersectional Multilevel models) were initially conceived as descriptive methods, yet some recent applications stray into causal interpretations. There are also several notable risks for analyses situated in the grey area between description and causal inference, specifically where strata can plausibly be inferred as important for both selection models (which may be causal), and descriptive analytic models (which are intentionally not). In this study, we consider three key issues that warrant attention: (1) how to interpret the coefficients of stratum-defining variables, (2) the potential for inadvertent collider adjustment and generalisability bias, illustrated using simulated data, and (3) the inclusion of 'control' variables. We provide recommendations for producing more robust descriptive research using MAIHDA.

articles.title: Severe Hyperkalemia in the Emergency Department: Factors Associated with Dialysis and Mortality.
articles.journal: The American journal of the medical sciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe hyperkalemia is a potentially life-threatening emergency, yet data focusing specifically on non-dialysis-dependent patients presenting to the emergency department (ED) with potassium levels ≥7.0 mmol/L remain limited. We aimed to characterize the clinical presentation, management, need for urgent dialysis, and outcomes in this high-risk population.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study of adults presenting to the ED with plasma potassium ≥7.0 mmol/L between 2010 and 2024, excluding patients receiving maintenance dialysis. Clinical characteristics, electrocardiographic (ECG) findings, treatments, and outcomes were analyzed. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with urgent dialysis and in-hospital mortality.

RESULTS: A total of 378 non-dialysis-dependent patients were included; 46 (12.2%) underwent urgent dialysis. Any ECG abnormality was documented in 52.9%, and severe ECG changes in 28.0%. Admission potassium concentration was independently associated with ECG abnormalities but was not independently associated with urgent dialysis or in-hospital mortality after adjustment. Younger age, AKI stage III, and CKD stage V were independently associated with urgent dialysis. In-hospital mortality occurred in 23.0% and was independently associated with older age, female sex, malignancy, and mean arterial pressure <70 mmHg. Among patients undergoing urgent dialysis, the last pre-dialysis potassium concentration and observed potassium changes during the first 8 hours varied between patients.

CONCLUSIONS: In non-dialysis-dependent patients with severe hyperkalemia, ECG abnormalities were related to potassium concentration, whereas urgent dialysis was associated mainly with severe kidney dysfunction and mortality with age, comorbidity, and hemodynamic instability. These findings support a context-based approach to risk stratification and dialysis decision-making.

articles.title: Role of Nitric Oxide In Diminazene Aceturate-Induced Vasodilatation In Mesenteric Resistance Arteries From Hypertensive Rats.
articles.journal: The American journal of the medical sciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) is a negative regulator of renin-angiotensin system, opposing angiotensin II effects. ACE2 actions are partly mediated through the release of nitric oxide (NO). Nevertheless, the role of NO in vasodilation induced by DIZE, has not yet been elucidated. This work evaluated whether NO plays a role in DIZE-induced vasodilation in mesenteric resistant arteries from SHR.

METHODS: Resistance mesenteric arteries from adult male SHR were used for vascular reactivity or immunohistochemical analysis of NOS isoforms. The expression of eNOS and nNOS was found enhanced in the endothelium. Basal NO release assay was performed by pre-incubation with DIZE (10-5 M) or vehicle, and then contracted by phenylephrine (PE, 10-3 uM).

RESULTS: The expression of eNOS and nNOS was found enhanced in the endothelium. Basal NO release assay was performed by pre-incubation with DIZE (10-5 M) or vehicle, and then contracted by phenylephrine (PE, 10-3 µM). DIZE significantly reduced PE contraction and, in presence of the NOS inhibitor L-NAME (300 µM), lead to a greater incremental contractile response compared to vehicle incubated arteries, pointing out the larger basal release of NO due to DIZE effect. This effect was not observed using other NOS inhibitors (L-NPA and 1400W). Similarly, DIZE promoted concentration-dependent relaxation in vitro, and this effect was blunted by L-NAME, with reverse effect by L-NPA. DAF-FM assay corroborated the effects of DIZE in stimulating NO release.

CONCLUSIONS: DIZE induces NO liberation in mesenteric resistance arteries from SHR, probably by eNOS stimulation, showing potential interest in hypertension management.

articles.title: Tarlatamab for Treatment of Small Cell Lung Cancer in Clinical Practice: A Multicenter U.S. Retrospective Cohort Study from the ONWARD consortium.
articles.journal: Journal of thoracic oncology : official publication of the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Real-world data on efficacy and safety of tarlatamab in small cell lung cancer (SCLC) remains limited.

METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 265 tarlatamab-treated patients across 11 U.S. centers in the ONWARD-SCLC consortium (11/2023-4/2025), evaluating clinical outcomes, CRS, ICANS, and impact of prophylactic medications.

RESULTS: Median age was 66 years; 87.2% had ECOG 0-1, 90.6% had de novo SCLC, and 44.5% and 39.2% had new/progressive brain and liver metastases before tarlatamab, respectively. Median prior lines of therapy were 2 (range 0-6). At a median follow-up of 4.9 months, DCR was 52.6% for evaluable SCLC cohort (all-treated: 37.9%). Median rw-PFS and rw-OS were 2.3 and 8.0 months. Median rw-PFS was 2.2 months among patients without brain metastasis versus 2.3 months among those with pre-existing brain metastasis (p=0.542). Following Cycle 1 Day 1 (C1D1), CRS occurred in 40.8% (Grade 3-4: 3.8%) and ICANS in 21.5% (Grade 3-4: 6%), with incidence declining markedly on subsequent doses. Compared to no-prophylaxis (N=237), prophylactic tocilizumab (N=19) was associated with lower CRS (5.3% vs. 43.0%; adj. p=0.017), ICANS (0% vs 22.4%; adj. p=0.041), and "prolonged hospitalization" rate (21.1% vs. 54.9%; adj. p=0.023). Multivariable analysis identified insulin-dependent diabetes, liver metastases, number of prior treatments, recent urgent care admissions, and low albumin/elevated ALT as independent predictors of worse OS.

CONCLUSION: Tarlatamab demonstrated meaningful clinical activity in pretreated real-world cohort, including those with brain metastases. Grade ≥3 CRS and overall/grade ≥3 ICANS incidence in C1 were higher than in clinical trials. Prophylaxis patterns were characterized and warrant prospective validation.

articles.title: Risk of Incident Type 2 Diabetes with Romosozumab Versus Denosumab in Patients with Osteoporosis: A Global Real-World Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antiosteoporotic agents may influence glucose regulation. Although denosumab has been evaluated for its potential effects on diabetes-related outcomes, the metabolic effects of romosozumab, a sclerostin inhibitor, remains unclear.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients aged ≥45 years with osteoporosis and no prior diabetes who initiated romosozumab or denosumab between 2019 and 2024 from the TriNetX network. An active-comparator, new-user design compared romosozumab users with denosumab users. The primary outcome was incident type 2 diabetes (T2D). Secondary outcomes included broader diabetes diagnoses, initiation of antidiabetic medications, and laboratory-defined diabetes. Treatment groups were balanced using 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM). Cox proportional hazards models, Kaplan-Meier analyses with log-rank tests, calendar time analyses, and multiple sensitivity analyses were performed.

RESULTS: After propensity score matching, 6581 patients were analyzed in each treatment group. Romosozumab initiation was not associated with a significant difference in incident T2D compared with denosumab (HR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.78-1.12; log-rank p = 0.468). Similarly, no significant differences were observed for broader diabetes diagnoses (HR, 1.01; 95% CI, 0.86-1.20), antidiabetic medication initiation (HR, 1.15; 95% CI, 0.95-1.40), or laboratory-defined diabetes (HR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.77-1.21).

CONCLUSIONS: Romosozumab was not associated with an increased risk of incident T2D or other diabetes-related outcomes compared with denosumab. These findings were supported by calendar-year-specific analyses, although residual confounding and differential follow-up warrant cautious interpretation. Future prospective studies are needed to clarify the metabolic effects of sclerostin inhibition.

articles.title: Workflow-friendly free-breathing whole-chest cardiovascular MRI using inner-volume balanced T1 relaxation-enhanced steady-state.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Free-breathing cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) may provide useful volumetric information. This study evaluated acquisition time and the feasibility of incorporating highly accelerated free-breathing inner-volume balanced T1 relaxation-enhanced steady-state (bT1RESS) imaging into a standard CMR protocol during the post-contrast interval before late gadolinium enhancement (LGE).

METHODS: A prototype ECG-gated, navigator-gated inner-volume bT1RESS sequence was added to 1.5T CMR examinations in 45 patients; 30 were included in the paired comparison with breath-hold bT1RESS. Series-start timing was assessed in 14 of the 45 patients. Three readers assessed image quality. Aortic diameters were compared between bT1RESS protocols and, in an additional cohort of 15 subjects, with CEMRA. Agreement was assessed separately at five aortic levels using Bland-Altman analysis.

RESULTS: Median inner-volume bT1RESS acquisition time was 1.82minutes (range, 0.78-3.72). In the series-start timing subset, median intervals from perfusion/CEMRA start to TI scout and first LGE series were 6.49minutes (n=13) and 8.46minutes (n=14), respectively. Reader preferences favored the inner-volume over breath-hold bT1RESS protocol. In the CEMRA comparison, mean differences (inner-volume bT1RESS minus CEMRA) ranged from 0.00 to 0.93mm; the lower and upper 95% limits of agreement ranged from -2.47 to -1.16mm and from 2.06 to 3.02mm, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Inner-volume bT1RESS provided rapid volumetric cardiovascular imaging within the evaluated post-contrast workflow. A primary benefit is the capability for 3D vessel measurement without a separate first-pass CEMRA acquisition. The technique may also help identify coronary artery origins, characterize morphological abnormalities in congenital heart disease and other cardiovascular disorders, and help to detect and characterize extracardiac lesions. Larger studies are needed to establish reproducibility and diagnostic performance.

articles.title: Insights into the 2026 ESC guidelines for the management of cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease.
A National Consultant Information Programme Data Analysis of Deep Venous Interventions in England.
articles.journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to characterise contemporary deep venous interventions (DVIs) performed within the English National Health Service (NHS), describing procedural mix, patient heterogeneity, anatomic distribution, and short and midterm outcomes.

METHODS: National data on DVIs performed between 1 June 2020 and 31 May 2023 were extracted from the National Consultant Information Programme. Percutaneous transluminal venous procedures (PTVs) and venous thrombolysis were identified using pre-defined procedural and diagnostic code hierarchies. All cases underwent structured patient level validation to ensure concordance between indication, treated venous anatomy, and procedural intent. The primary outcomes were ninety day and one year mortality. Secondary outcomes included procedural volume variation. Re-interventions were recorded descriptively.

RESULTS: In total, 2 339 DVIs were performed, of which 1 617 PTVs and 604 venous thrombolysis procedures were validated. Patient cohorts were heterogeneous, most commonly chronic kidney disease (CKD) (41.8%), chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) (16.0%), and venous compression syndromes (14.0%). Anatomic distribution differed markedly by indication: CKD procedures predominantly involved upper limb and central veins, whereas CVI and venous compression were overwhelmingly confined to the lower limbs and iliocaval system. Among 650 patients with primary lower limb venous disease (CVI, venous thrombosis, or venous compression), 76.3% underwent iliac or inferior vena cava interventions. Overall mortality varied substantially by indication, being highest in patients with malignant neoplasms and lowest in primary lower limb venous disease. Thrombolysis was most frequently performed for lower extremity venous thrombosis and was associated with low short and midterm mortality in this group.

CONCLUSION: This service level analysis of DVIs in England demonstrates distinct clinical populations with marked differences in anatomy, indication, and outcomes that vary substantially by indication and comorbidity. Mortality was lowest in elective primary lower limb venous disease and highest in patients with advanced systemic illness such as malignancy and renal disease. Future work should focus on indication specific venous registries and risk adjusted outcomes to aid benchmarking, service level organisation, and patient care.

articles.title: Intravascular Lithotripsy versus Rotational Atherectomy for Calcified Coronary Lesions: An Updated Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
PSMA PET Before Prostate Biopsy: From Lesion Detection to Biopsy Avoidance.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) positron emission tomography (PET) may refine biopsy selection when magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is equivocal or nonsuspicious despite persistent clinical concern. This review aims to examine the prospective evidence and to distinguish diagnostic accuracy from biopsy avoidance.

METHODS: Selected prospective cohorts and randomized trials evaluating PSMA PET before prostate biopsy were synthesized narratively, alongside relevant systematic reviews and guidelines. Interpretation focused on patient selection, clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) definitions, biopsy protocols, and verification of PET-negative findings.

RESULTS: Combining PSMA PET with MRI improves sensitivity and negative predictive value in several prospective studies, particularly in men with equivocal findings. PET-targeted biopsy can improve sampling, but this does not establish the safety of omitting biopsy. In PRIMARY2, a PET-guided pathway achieved noninferior csPCa detection compared with systematic biopsy (12% versus 16%; prespecified noninferiority margin, 10 percentage points), while 49% of men in the PET arm avoided biopsy within 6 months. PET-negative men did not undergo routine immediate biopsy, so the trial does not establish histologically verified negative predictive value. Study heterogeneity and limited follow-up constrain generalization.

CONCLUSIONS: PSMA PET may complement MRI in selected men with residual diagnostic uncertainty. Broader implementation requires validated clinical thresholds, longer follow-up after biopsy deferral, and evidence of cost-effectiveness.

articles.title: "Bold and necessary experiments:" The redelegation of authority and responsibility to nurses at the origins of cardiac intensive care.
articles.abstract: Coronary Care Units (CCUs) were at the forefront of the development of intensive care in the 1960s and 1970s. The development of CCUs, and intensive care more broadly, was enabled by the interplay of expanding medical technology and the evolving role of nurses vis-à-vis physicians. This paper examines the history the CCU at New York Hospital, the teaching hospital of Cornell University School of Medicine and School of Nursing, with a particular focus on role of nurses in the unit's success. Drawing from historical archives of New York Hospital and the Cornell University School of Nursing, this paper argues that that nurses were co-creators, alongside physicians, of the NYH CCU, and demonstrates how nurses drew from the NYH CCU experience to expand critical care services at the local and national level, including by advocating for the creation of the NYH medical intensive care unit (MICU), leading a CCU nurse training program to expand regional CCU capability, and contributing expertise to a federally-sponsored national conference on CCUs. A close reading of this history offers lessons and insights as intensive care medicine moves into an uncertain future, chief among them that work of caring for critically ill patients requires the thoughtful integration of new technologies with hands on care.

articles.title: Boldine ameliorates metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease via Nrf2-mediated mitochondrial and ferroptotic regulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a prevalent chronic liver disorder characterized by oxidative stress and ferroptosis, yet effective pharmacological interventions remain limited. This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of boldine (BD) against MASLD and to explore its underlying molecular mechanisms.

METHODS: A high-fat diet (HFD)-induced MASLD mouse model and free fatty acid (FFA)-treated hepatocytes were used to evaluate the effects of BD. Liver injury, lipid accumulation, oxidative stress, and ferroptosis were assessed using biochemical assays, histological analysis, and molecular approaches. RNA sequencing, molecular docking, and cellular thermal shift assays (CETSA) were performed to examine the potential interaction between BD and nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2).

RESULTS: BD significantly attenuated hepatic steatosis and improved liver function in HFD-fed mice. Mechanistically, BD enhanced Nrf2 stability, promoted its nuclear translocation, and activated the Nrf2/GPX4 axis. This was associated with restoration of mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm) and NAD+/NADH balance, leading to reduced lipid peroxidation and suppression of ferroptosis. Notably, these protective effects were partially reversed by the Nrf2 inhibitor ML385, supporting the involvement of Nrf2 signaling.

CONCLUSION: BD alleviates MASLD by modulating redox homeostasis and inhibiting ferroptosis, potentially through activation of the Nrf2/GPX4 pathway. These findings suggest that BD may represent a promising therapeutic candidate for MASLD.

articles.title: Nigerian Grown Hyptis verticillata Leaf Extract Mitigates Endocrine and Metabolic Disruptions in Lipid-enriched Diet and Letrozole-induced Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome in Wistar Rats.
articles.abstract: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is a hormonal disorder that manifests during the female reproductive lifespan. Hyptis verticillata previously demonstrated glucose-modulating effects and ameliorated metabolic aberrations associated with diabetes mellitus. The present study evaluated its potential to mitigate the metabolic and endocrine compromises associated with PMOS. Experimental PMOS induction was achieved using an oral regimen of 1mg/kg body weight (b.w.) letrozole combined with a lipid enriched diet for 21 days. Thirty female rats were divided into five groups: a healthy control and four PMOS-induced groups that were orally administered either 10mL/kg b.w of distilled water, 500mg/kg b.w of metformin, or H. verticillata leaf extract (250mg/kg and 500mg/kg). Treatment lasted 28 days. From results, both doses of H. verticillata significantly (p<0.05) restored normoglycaemia, improved insulin sensitivity, normalized body weight, and reversed hyperandrogenism. Furthermore, a significant elevation in follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) following extract treatment was accompanied by a marked decline in luteinizing hormone (LH) compared to the untreated PMOS group. Additionally, H. verticillata significantly reversed dyslipidaemia and boosted ovarian concentrations of antioxidant enzymes (SOD, CAT, and GPx) while decreasing malondialdehyde levels, performing similarly to metformin. Histopathological analysis revealed improved ovarian morphology with a decline in cystic follicles. It can be inferred from these findings that the beneficial potential of H. verticillata against PMOS-induced endocrine and metabolic compromise are elicited through a multi-mechanistic action that modulates glucose and hormone homeostasis, boosts antioxidant capacity, and restores ovarian structure, making it a promising alternative for managing PMOS.

articles.title: Neuroprotective Effects of Calcitriol after Experimental Ischemic Stroke induction via Modulation of Glutamate Excitotoxicity, MMP-9 Activity, and Oxidative Stress.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke triggers detrimental cascades, including glutamate excitotoxicity, oxidative stress, and neuroinflammation. This study evaluated the neuroprotective potential of calcitriol during the acute phase of stroke, focusing on inflammatory damage and modulation of glutamate transporters.

METHODS: Male Wistar rats underwent 1-h middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) and were assigned to Sham, tMCAO + Vehicle, and tMCAO + Calcitriol groups. Calcitriol (1μg/kg) was administered at 30min, 24h, and 48h post-stroke. After 72h, behavioral outcomes, infarct volume, and histological alterations in cortical region were assessed utilizing Nissl staining. Cortical mRNA expression of glutamate-aspartate transporter (GLAST), glutamate transporter-1 (GLT-1), and excitatory amino acid transporter 3 (EAAT3) was evaluated via RT-PCR. Serum Matrix Metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) activity was measured using gelatin zymography, and oxidative stress biomarkers malondialdehyde (MDA), total antioxidant capacity (TAC), and nitric oxide (NO) were quantified in the penumbra. Molecular docking simulations explored calcitriol-MMP-9 binding affinity.

RESULTS: Calcitriol significantly reduced infarct volume, improved neurobehavioral scores, and mitigated morphological neuronal damage. It elevated TAC while suppressing MDA and NO levels. In line with docking simulations predicting a moderate binding affinity of -6.5kcal/mol, a marked decrease in serum MMP-9 enzymatic activity was observed. Furthermore, calcitriol treatment significantly reduced GLAST, GLT-1, and EAAT3 cortical gene expression compared to the untreated ischemia group.

CONCLUSION: Calcitriol administration attenuates acute ischemic brain injury. This neuroprotective effect is associated with parallel downregulations of glutamate transporter gene expression, suppression of penumbral oxidative stress, and reduced serum MMP-9 enzymatic activity.

articles.title: Comment on "Association between statins and chronic liver disease progression: A retrospective cohort study".
articles.journal: Clinics and research in hepatology and gastroenterology

articles.title: Dementia Risk After Vertebral Augmentation for Osteoporotic Vertebral Compression Fracture: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (VCFs) cause chronic pain and prolonged immobility, both potentially modifiable risk factors for dementia. Vertebral augmentation (VA), performed as percutaneous vertebroplasty or balloon kyphoplasty, relieves pain and enables earlier mobilization. We examined whether VA is associated with a lower long-term risk of dementia than conservative management.

METHODS: Using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network, we conducted a retrospective, propensity score-matched cohort study of patients older than 60 years with a newly diagnosed VCF. Patients were grouped by receipt of VA within six months of diagnosis. After 1:1 propensity score matching on demographic, comorbidity, and osteoporosis-medication variables, we assessed incident dementia over five years using odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and Kaplan-Meier curves with the log-rank test. A six-month landmark analysis was performed to limit immortal-time bias.

RESULTS: Matching produced 3,830 patients per group, with every standardized mean difference below 0.1. Dementia occurred in 8.1% of the VA group and 9.9% of the non-VA group over five years (OR 0.80, 95% CI 0.68-0.94; absolute risk difference 1.8 percentage points). The association persisted in the six-month landmark analysis (3,497 patients per group; 6.2% vs 7.5%; OR 0.81, 95% CI 0.67-0.98).

CONCLUSIONS: In older adults with osteoporotic VCF, vertebral augmentation was associated with a lower medium-term incidence of dementia than conservative management. Given the observational design, unmeasured confounding, and competing mortality, this association is preliminary and hypothesis-generating, and requires confirmation in prospective studies before any causal inference or change in practice.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and risk factor associated with disease progression in patients with nontuberculous mycobacterial disease.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM) disease represents a growing public health concern, driven by rising incidence rates and substantial healthcare utilization. To advance clinical understanding, we retrospectively analyzed the clinical characteristics of patients diagnosed with NTM disease and identified risk factors associated with disease progression specifically among non-HIV-infected individuals.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 506 non-HIV patients with NTM disease at the First Affiliated Hospital of Guangxi Medical University between January 1, 2020 and May 31, 2025, analyzing clinical, microbiological, and immunological data to identify predictors of progression.

RESULTS: Disseminated infection accounted for 51.8% of cases, most commonly associated with AIGAs (anti-IFN-γ autoantibodies; 77.9%), while localized disease predominated in patients with chronic pulmonary disease. The most prevalent NTM species was Mycobacterium avium complex (47.5%), followed by M. abscessus (29.0%). Co-infection with Talaromyces marneffei, Salmonella spp., Epstein-Barr virus, and cytomegalovirus was significantly more common in the disseminated infection group. Independent predictors of progression included low BMI, disseminated infection, self-initiated treatment discontinuation, and reduced CD3+ T cell percentage. AIGAs status was strongly associated with long-term prognosis. Notably, AIGAs positivity and disseminated infection exhibited a significant additive synergistic effect, with patients carrying both factors showing a markedly higher risk of disease progression.

CONCLUSION: Disseminated NTM infection, especially in patients with AIGAs syndrome, carries a high risk of disease progression. AIGAs testing is recommended for all NTM patients, particularly those with disseminated, severe or refractory disease. Medication adherence and regular follow-up are critical for improving long-term prognosis.

articles.title: Chestnut starch-lipid complex as a nontraditional RS5 ingredient: Structural features and associated in vivo responses in high-fat diet-fed mice.
articles.abstract: Resistant starch type 5 (RS5) can convert starch-rich crops into enzyme-resistant starch-lipid complexes, yet current evidence remains dominated by conventional starch sources and in vitro studies. This study prepared and characterized a chestnut starch-stearic acid complex (chestnut starch-lipid complex, DCS_C18, RS5), and evaluated it as a novel RS5 ingredient in high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mice, using native chestnut starch, caffeine, and orlistat as contextual comparators. DCS_C18 showed V-/B-type crystalline features, greater short-range and long-range order, and higher thermal stability than the palmitic acid complex. In vivo, DCS_C18 attenuated HFD-induced weight gain, adiposity, dyslipidemia, glucose intolerance, insulin resistance, hepatic steatosis, and systemic inflammation, accompanied by reduced lipogenic and increased fatty acid oxidation-related gene expression. Moreover, DCS_C18 exhibited more balanced regulation of fasting and postprandial glycemia than the other interventions. DCS_C18 also increased fecal acetate (2.12-fold) and butyrate (1.82-fold) and enriched SCFA-associated genera, including Blautia, Roseburia, and Lachnoclostridium. Open-field testing suggested improved locomotor and anxiety-related outcomes without the stimulant-like pattern observed for caffeine. These findings support chestnut-derived RS5 as a promising ingredient platform for metabolic-health-oriented foods, pending human and mechanistic confirmation.

articles.title: Functioning in persons with Spinal Cord Injury compared with the general population.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop a harmonized functioning metric enabling direct comparison between persons with spinal cord injury or disease (SCI/D) and the Swiss general population, and to quantify differences in functioning across population and chronic-condition groups.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional comparative analysis using data from the Swiss Spinal Cord Injury Cohort Study (SwiSCI) and the Swiss Health Survey (SHS). Functioning items from the 2012, 2017, and 2022 waves of both surveys were linked to International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) categories to identify items measuring comparable aspects of functioning, which were then psychometrically evaluated using the Partial Credit Model. Suitable anchor items were identified based on item fit, local dependence, and differential item functioning, and used to derive a common 0-100 functioning metric. Epidemiological comparisons were restricted to the 2022 wave, the most recent wave available in both surveys, after exact matching of SHS participants to SwiSCI participants on age, sex, and language region.

RESULTS: The metric-development sample included 1,773 participants from each survey. The matched 2022 comparison included 1,311 SwiSCI participants and 11,836 SHS participants. Combining complete and incomplete injuries within each group, mean functioning was 53.6 (SD 8.8) among participants with paraplegia and 52.0 (SD 9.4) among those with tetraplegia, compared with 74.7 (SD 10.2) among SHS participants without a history of myocardial infarction, stroke, or cancer. Mean functioning was also higher among SHS participants with cancer, 71.6 (SD 12.0), stroke, 69.2 (SD 15.0), or myocardial infarction, 72.4 (SD 12.4), than among participants with SCI/D. Functioning decreased with age in the SHS and paraplegia groups, but no clear age association was observed in the tetraplegia group.

CONCLUSION: This study developed a harmonized functioning metric that enabled direct comparison between persons with SCI/D and the Swiss general population. Persons with SCI/D showed substantially lower functioning than Swiss general-population participants, both with and without major chronic conditions, even after demographic matching. These findings support the use of functioning as a distinct population health outcome that complements mortality and morbidity in health surveillance and health-system planning.

articles.title: The metabolic reprogramming of T cells controls airway remodeling in severe asthma.
articles.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mixed granulocytic asthma (MGA) is a severe Th2-low endotype, characterized by high Th17/neutrophilic burden and exacerbated airway remodeling. Both features confer resistance to inhaled corticosteroids and typical asthma treatments.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to address gaps in knowledge, including how Th17 cells induce pathological tissue remodeling and how Th17 differentiation occurs in response to allergens.

METHODS: We generated a Th2-low murine model of asthma on the Il4rα-/- background that mimics the decrease in type 2 response seen in corticosteroid-resistant patients. We monitored major features of human disease including heightened airway reactivity to methacholine, Th17/neutrophilic inflammation, airway remodeling, and resistance to corticosteroid treatment. Comparative transfer of Th2 versus Th17 cells were analyzed. We further investigated how the mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) pathway modulates pathogenic Th17 cell reprogramming by in vitro T cell cultures and in vivo therapeutic blockades.

RESULTS: LIGHT (aka TNFSF14) and the OXPHOS pathway are enriched in human MGA and likewise upregulated in this mouse model. We show OXPHOS promotes the metabolic reprograming of Th17 cells, to sustain their survival despite steroid treatment and produce LIGHT that controls airway remodeling. Mechanistically, OXPHOS regulates RORγt expression and the subsequent transcriptional network to program differentiation of Th17 cells, whereas LIGHT drives airway remodeling by activating the MMP9-dependent TGFβ pathway. Additionally, OXPHOS+Th17 cells promote the expression of osteopontin necessary for fibroblast activation. LIGHT antagonistic blockade reduces airway remodeling, whereas OXPHOS inhibition kills Th17 cells and subsequent neutrophilia. Importantly, the dual blockade of LIGHT and OXPHOS reverses all features of MGA back to baseline and reciprocally increases the numbers of Treg cells.

CONCLUSIONS: The dual blockade of LIGHT and OXPHOS constitutes a promising target for clinical interventions in human MGA, possibly extending to other Th17-driven fibrotic diseases.

articles.title: Intraprocedural evaluation of residual mitral and tricuspid regurgitation after transcatheter edge-to-edge repair.
authors: SIC (Italian Society of Cardiology) Echocardiography Study Group
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) has emerged as an established therapeutic option for selected patients with severe mitral (MR) and tricuspid regurgitation (TR), supported by expanding clinical evidence. However, intraprocedural assessment of residual regurgitation remains challenging because of dynamic hemodynamic changes, device-related artefacts, and limitations of conventional echocardiographic parameters.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This review summarizes current evidence on multiparametric echocardiographic and hemodynamic assessment during mitral (M-TEER) and tricuspid (T-TEER) procedures, with a focus on the evaluation of residual regurgitation, the immediate physiological response, markers of cardiac remodeling and their prognostic implications. Accurate quantification of residual MR and TR requires an integrated multiparametric approach. Residual regurgitation is associated with clinical outcomes and reverse remodeling. Conventional two-dimensional measures are limited by altered post-procedural jet geometry and multiple residual jets. Three-dimensional vena contracta area provides improved visualization and quantification of residual regurgitation, enabling summation of multiple jets. However, its quantitative accuracy has been validated only to a limited extent and thresholds after TEER are not standardized. Volumetric quantification is independent of jet geometry but remains insufficiently validated intraprocedurally. Atrial pressures, venous flow and forward flow describe the physiological response rather than regurgitant severity.

CONCLUSION: Intraprocedural evaluation of residual MR and TR after TEER requires expert integration of multiple echocardiographic measures of regurgitation with complementary assessment of its physiological consequences and hemodynamic parameters. Advanced 3D imaging plays an increasingly central role in improving procedural assessment and post-interventional risk stratification, but standardized and validated criteria for quantifying residual regurgitation after TEER are still lacking.

articles.title: Magnesium intake and prevalence of depressive symptoms: The baseline data from the Aidai Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Among the modifiable risk factors for depressive symptoms, diet is attracting attention. Epidemiological evidence regarding the association between magnesium intake and depressive symptoms has been limited. The present cross-sectional study examined this issue using baseline data from the Aidai Cohort Study.

METHODS: Study subjects were 10,316 Japanese men and women aged 20-95 years. Dietary intake during the previous year was assessed using a 169-item, semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire. Scores of 16 or higher on the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale denoted depressive symptoms. Adjustment was made for age, sex, smoking status, alcohol consumption, leisure-time physical activity, hypertension, dyslipidemia, diabetes mellitus, history of depression, body mass index, employment, education, and household income.

RESULTS: The prevalence of depressive symptoms among the 10,316 study subjects was 14.9%. Higher magnesium intake was independently associated with a lower prevalence of depressive symptoms: the fully multivariate-adjusted ORs for comparison of the second, third, and fourth with the first quartile were 0.80 (95% CI: 0.69-0.93), 0.71 (95% CI: 0.60-0.83), and 0.62 (95% CI: 0.52-0.74), respectively (P for trend < 0.0001). In sensitivity analyses confined to those under 65 years of age, those aged 65 years and older, men, and women, the fully multivariate-adjusted ORs between extreme quartiles (95% CI, P for trend) were 0.65 (0.53-0.80, < 0.0001), 0.55 (0.40-0.76, < 0.0001), 0.74 (0.56-0.98, 0.02), and 0.60 (0.48-0.75, < 0.0001), respectively.

CONCLUSION: Magnesium intake may be inversely associated with the prevalence of depressive symptoms.

articles.title: Primary Care Pediatrician's Experiences Caring for Children With Disabilities.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatricians have raised concerns about the time and resources needed to support children with disabilities (CWD). This study examines the experiences of pediatricians who provide services for CWD, including relationships between pediatrician characteristics, practice characteristics, and barriers to providing care.

METHODS: This study analyzes American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) 2023 Periodic Survey data (33.0% response rate; data weighted to account for nonresponse bias). Respondents reported experiences and barriers to caring for CWD. In addition to descriptive and bivariate statistics, we used multivariable logistic regression to examine pediatrician and practice characteristics associated with prescribing practices and reported barriers.

RESULTS: Survey respondents included 323 primary care pediatricians. While most pediatricians reported providing care for children with a range of disabilities (80.1% gross motor disability, 72.3% fine motor, 88.2% communication) more than half of pediatricians reported CWD made up a small portion (≤6%) of their patient panel. Most respondents reported prescribing physical therapy (78.1%), occupational therapy (78.4%), and speech therapy (88.6%) "often/very often," with few prescribing mobility aids (13.7%). Common barriers to caring for CWD included time limitations (74.9%), inadequate payment (63.3%), and lack of formal education/training (45.5%). Pediatricians with access to care coordinators were significantly less likely to identify inadequate payment and lack of formal education/training as barriers to care.

CONCLUSION: Most pediatricians provide care to CWD, but much of the care for CWD may be congregating among a small number of pediatricians. Equitable care access for CWD may entail medical home initiatives that combine support, consultation, and payment strategies.

articles.title: Geographic Access to Urgent Care and Pediatric Site-of-Care Patterns: A Hypothesis-Generating Analysis in One Health System.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe pediatric site-of-care utilization across three communities differing in in-network urgent care (UC) availability within one health system, generating hypotheses about geographic access to Medicaid-accepting UC and pediatric emergency department (ED) use.

METHODS: Retrospective analysis of pediatric encounters (2023-2025) at two EDs and two UCs in coastal Connecticut. Patients younger than 21 years residing in Bridgeport (in-network ED only), Fairfield (in-network UC only), or Milford (both), presenting during UC operating hours with Medicaid or commercial insurance and a principal diagnosis common to both settings, were included. Multivariable logistic regression with a Medicaid × Region interaction, adjusted for diagnosis and age band, with ZIP-level cluster-robust standard errors, estimated odds ratios for UC use.

RESULTS: Among 12,578 encounters, the adjusted odds of urgent care (vs emergency department) use among Medicaid- versus commercially insured children differed across regions (Medicaid × Region interaction, P <.001): 0.45 (95% CI, 0.37-0.53) in Bridgeport, 1.85 (1.56-2.20) in Fairfield, and 0.55 (0.49-0.63) in Milford. The pattern persisted after adjustment but cannot separate in-network access from out-of-network substitution or unmeasured community-level differences.

CONCLUSIONS: The Medicaid-commercial difference in urgent care use varied across communities, suggesting local access to Medicaid-accepting urgent care may shape pediatric site-of-care decisions. Single-system scope and missing patient-level social determinants and out-of-network data preclude causal inference; multi-system replication using continuous distance measures is warranted. If confirmed, expanding Medicaid-accepting urgent care may be a practical lever to reduce avoidable pediatric ED use.

articles.title: Shared genetic architecture and pleiotropic loci linking prurigo nodularis to allergic diseases.
articles.abstract: Prurigo nodularis (PN) frequently co-occurs with allergic diseases, but the underlying shared genetic architecture and specific loci contributing to this overlap remain incompletely understood. We integrated genome-wide association study summary statistics for PN and multiple allergic diseases. Genetic sharing was assessed at genome-wide and regional levels, directional associations were examined using bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR), and shared signals were refined through cross-trait pleiotropy, colocalization, and complementary gene-prioritization analyses. Immune-cell analyses were used to provide additional cellular context. PN showed positive genetic correlations with multiple allergic diseases, with regionally heterogeneous local sharing. MR suggested associations of several allergic liabilities with increased PN susceptibility. Cross-trait pleiotropy identified shared loci with enrichment in cytokine signaling, T-cell regulation, and lipid metabolism, while regional colocalization further refined a subset of shared signals. Across complementary genetic evidence, IL2RA, FADS1, PRR5L, and LRRC43 emerged as the most consistently supported candidate genes. Exploratory immune-cell analyses provided suggestive CD25-related T-cell context for IL2RA signal. PN and allergic diseases share a broad but regionally heterogeneous genetic architecture. Convergent evidence prioritizes a restricted set of shared loci and candidate genes, including IL2RA, providing a genetic framework for further functional investigation of PN-allergy overlap.

articles.title: A pathway-level analysis reveals oxidative and inflammatory vascular stress signatures associated with VEGF inhibition.
articles.abstract: Vascular endothelial growth factor inhibitors (VEGFi) are widely used in the treatment of advanced malignancies, including clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), but are frequently associated with cardiovascular toxicities such as hypertension and endothelial dysfunction. The molecular mechanisms underlying these adverse effects remain incompletely understood. In this study, we performed an integrated transcriptomic and functional analysis to characterise vascular stress responses associated with VEGFi. Pre-treatment tumour RNA sequencing data from a public cancer cohort were analysed using Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) to identify pathway-level signatures associated with subsequent VEGFi treatment. No individual genes remained significant after multiple testing correction; therefore, emphasis was placed on coordinated biological responses. Functional validation was conducted in human vascular cells treated with a VEGFi to assess reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, cytokine levels and expression, and extracellular vesicles (EVs) release. Pathway analysis revealed significant baseline enrichment of oxidative stress, inflammatory response, and nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) signalling pathways in tumours of patients who subsequently received VEGFi. These baseline associations were complemented by increased vascular cell ROS production and enhanced EVs release in vitro. Inflammatory activation was further confirmed by increased cytokine secretion, despite unchanged messenger RNA expression, indicating regulation at post-transcriptional and secretory levels. Collectively, these baseline tumour signatures and the in vitro vascular findings are consistent with a model in which VEGF inhibition induces a coordinated redox-inflammatory response, which may involve EV-mediated intercellular communication. This mechanism may contribute to vascular dysfunction and cardiovascular toxicity associated with VEGFi-targeted therapies.

articles.title: p97 inhibition attenuates cigarette Smoke-Induced lung inflammation and epithelial senescence by Restoring SIRT1 SUMOylation.
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is driven by cigarette smoke-induced lung inflammation and accelerated epithelial senescence, yet the upstream regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here we investigate the role of the AAA + ATPase p97 in regulating SIRT1 post-translational modification and its contribution to pulmonary pathology. Mouse lung epithelial TC-1 cells were exposed to 5% cigarette smoke extract (CSE); cellular senescence was assessed by SA-β-gal staining, cytokine ELISA, and Western blotting. The regulatory axis was dissected using the p97 inhibitor CB-5083 and the SUMOylation inhibitor 2-D08. In vivo relevance was validated in a murine COPD model combining cigarette smoke (CS) exposure with intranasal LPS challenge. CSE exposure upregulated p97 while downregulating SIRT1 and SUMO1, concomitant with elevated IL-6 and IL-1β secretion. Pharmacological inhibition of p97 with CB-5083 attenuated the senescent phenotype, restored SIRT1 stability and deacetylase activity, and enhanced SIRT1-SUMO1 conjugation. Critically, the SUMOylation inhibitor 2-D08 abrogated these protective effects of CB-5083. In vivo, CB-5083 administration markedly ameliorated CS + LPS-induced alveolar damage, neutrophilic infiltration, and pro-inflammatory cytokine production; these benefits were significantly reversed by co-administration of 2-D08. These findings indicate that p97 promotes cigarette smoke-induced lung inflammation and epithelial senescence by impairing SIRT1 SUMOylation-dependent stability and activity, identifying the p97-SIRT1-SUMO1 axis as a novel pharmacological target for COPD therapy.

articles.title: Unveiling the mechanisms of nephrotoxicity caused by the interplay of losartan and febuxostat.
articles.abstract: Hypertension and hyperuricemia are commonly comorbid conditions. Losartan and febuxostat are frequently used therapeutic agents for hypertension and hyperuricemia respectively. However, the long-term impacts of their combined administration, particularly on kidneys, are still largely unknown. Through establishing a rat model of hypertension with hyperuricemia, this study investigated renal outcomes under different therapeutic regimens. We implemented a multimodal omics strategy including transcriptomic and metabolomic analysis, followed by multidimensional validation, to further explore the mechanisms underlying the specific nephrotoxicity induced by the combination of losartan and febuxostat. Our findings demonstrated that although the combined use of losartan and febuxostat effectively reduced serum uric acid and blood pressure levels, it paradoxically induced significant renal injury. The nephrotoxicity predominantly originated from activation of the Atf4-Ddit3/Chac1 pathway in renal distal convoluted tubules following the coadministration of losartan and febuxostat, which sequentially induced stress response and glutathione hydrolysis, followed by oxidative stress damage, and ultimately apoptosis. This study provides the first evidence indicating the potential renal risks of the combined treatment regimen of losartan and febuxostat in patients with hypertension and hyperuricemia.

articles.title: Ubiquitin ligase CHFR impairs Tie2 signaling via K48-linked ubiquitylation and degradation of Akt1 in endothelial cells.
articles.abstract: Vascular endothelial (VE)-cadherin is essential for maintaining endothelial junctional barrier integrity. The Angiopoietin-1 (Ang-1)/Tie2 axis induced Akt1 activation is crucial for maintaining endothelial junctional barrier by inhibiting FoxO1 and suppressing expression of Angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2), a Tie2 antagonist. Systemic inflammatory conditions such as sepsis, Akt1 expression is reduced, whereas FoxO1-dependent Ang-2 expression is increased, resulting in endothelial barrier dysfunction. We previously showed that the TLR4/FoxO1 axis induces the ubiquitin E3 ligase CHFR, which promotes endothelial barrier disruption by targeting VE-cadherin for ubiquitylation and degradation. However, little is known about Akt1 expression during vascular inflammation. Here, we identified FoxO1-dependent CHFR expression as a key mechanism driving K48-linked polyubiquitylation and proteasomal degradation of Akt1 in endothelial cells (EC). LPS-induced K48-linked ubiquitylation of Akt1 was prevented in CHFR-depleted human EC and in endothelial-specific Chfr knockout (ChfrΔEC) mice. Accordingly, CHFR depletion increased Akt1 and VE-cadherin expression in both human lung EC and ChfrΔEC mice. ChfrΔEC mouse lungs also exhibited elevated Ang-1 and Tie2 expression, and Ang-1 stimulation induced sustained Akt1 phosphorylation in CHFR-deficient EC. Moreover, CHFR depletion prevented LPS-induced expression of FoxO1 and Ang-2 in EC. Mechanistically, CHFR interacted with phosphorylated Akt1 and mediated its ubiquitylation at lysine residues K30, K39, K154, and K268. Expression of a ubiquitylation-deficient Akt1 mutant prevented LPS-induced VE-cadherin degradation and vascular injury. Collectively, these findings identify CHFR as a critical regulator of endothelial inflammatory responses by controlling Akt1 stability and VE-cadherin expression during inflammation.

articles.title: Index of microcirculatory resistance-guided management in angina: design and rationale of the DECISIONING trial.
articles.abstract:
