RATIONALE: Coronary microvascular dysfunction may contribute to persistent angina after fractional flow reserve (FFR)-guided coronary management. Whether disclosure of the index of microcirculatory resistance (IMR) and personalized management improve angina-related health status remains unknown.

PRIMARY HYPOTHESIS: Among participants with initial IMR ≥25, disclosure of IMR with protocol-guided personalized management will improve the baseline-adjusted 12-month Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ) Summary Score compared with concealed IMR and usual care.

DESIGN: DECISIONING is an investigator-initiated, 16-center French randomized trial (planned n=280). All participants have angina and at least one angiographic lesion ≥50%; FFR and initial IMR are measured before randomization. FFR ≤0.80 guides percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), whereas PCI is deferred when FFR >0.80. Participants are randomized 1:1, stratified by center and initial IMR (<25 or ≥25), to IMR disclosure with individualized treatment or IMR-concealed usual care. Participants and treating clinicians are aware of allocation; the initial IMR value remains concealed from control participants and their treating clinicians. Centralized follow-up and outcome assessment are blinded. Coronary flow reserve (CFR) is collected for exploratory secondary physiologic characterization but does not guide randomization or treatment. Enrollment and status Enrollment began on March 31, 2022. As of September 19, 2026, 275 participants had been randomized; enrollment toward 280 was ongoing, with final follow-up expected in october 2028.

CONCLUSIONS: DECISIONING will test the clinical benefit of IMR-informed management while characterizing complementary CFR/IMR physiology in exploratory analyses. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov; NCT05178914; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05178914.

articles.title: Protein nanocages: Programmable biomaterial platforms for therapeutics, bioimaging, and diagnostics.
articles.abstract: Protein nanocages are monodisperse, hollow structures formed through the symmetric self-assembly of protein subunits. Their genetically encoded architectures combine the geometric precision of nanoscale assemblies with the intrinsic biocompatibility and functional versatility of naturally evolved proteins. Well-defined internal cavities and engineerable interior and exterior surfaces enable the spatial organization of therapeutic cargoes, molecular recognition elements, and bioactive components within a single nanoscale platform. In this Review, we examine the structural organization, self-assembly mechanisms, physicochemical properties, and functional diversity of representative protein nanocages, including ferritin, the pyruvate dehydrogenase E2 core, DNA-binding proteins from starved cells (Dps), small heat shock proteins (sHSPs), encapsulins, and lumazine synthase. We discuss how their structural features and assembly behavior govern biological performance and support biomedical applications in targeted drug delivery, cancer immunotherapy, vaccine development, and in vivo and in vitro diagnostics. Beyond describing individual platforms, we establish a unifying framework that positions protein nanocages as programmable molecular organizers and highlights five transferable design principles: multivalent ligand display, spatial compartmentalization, receptor-guided targeting, reporter organization and signal enhancement, and stimulus-responsive cargo release and functional activation. We also examine persistent challenges in structural stability, immunogenicity, scalable manufacturing, and clinical translation, alongside emerging opportunities in protein engineering, synthetic biology, and computational protein design. Collectively, these principles establish protein nanocages as versatile biomaterial platforms for integrating sensing, targeting, imaging, and therapy within a single molecular architecture, providing a foundation for next-generation precision nanomedicine. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Reviews typically treat protein nanocages individually, obscuring shared structural features and the extent to which design strategies transfer across systems. This Review addresses this gap by establishing a comparative framework spanning structurally diverse nanocages and distilling their similarities into a concise set of generalizable design principles. It reframes protein nanocages not merely as passive delivery vehicles but as programmable molecular scaffolds that organize cargo with controlled spatial arrangement and stoichiometry. This framework provides biomaterials researchers with a transferable basis for engineering protein assemblies for precision nanomedicine while identifying key challenges in structural stability, immunogenicity, and scalable manufacturing that must be addressed to facilitate clinical translation.

articles.title: Itaconate alleviates sepsis-induced acute lung injury by suppressing Peroxiredoxin 1 dimerization through covalent alkylates at Cys173.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated acute lung injury (SALI) is characterized by overwhelming inflammation and oxidative stress, during which damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) exacerbate tissue injury. Peroxiredoxin 1 (PRDX1), a canonical intracellular antioxidant enzyme, paradoxically functions as a pro-inflammatory DAMP after extracellular release. This pathogenic transition depends on PRDX1 dimerization through intermolecular disulfide bonds. However, the endogenous metabolic mechanisms that restrain PRDX1 release remain unclear. Here, we identify the ACOD1-itaconate axis as a critical suppressor of PRDX1-mediated hyperinflammation in SALI. Clinical dataset analysis revealed that elevated PRDX1 expression strongly correlates with sepsis mortality. In a murine cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) model, Acod1 deficiency exacerbated SALI and amplified PRDX1 secretion, whereas therapeutic administration of 4-octyl itaconate (4-OI) robustly alleviated lung injury and the accompanying cytokine storm. Mechanistically, chemical proteomics and mutagenesis showed that itaconate directly targets PRDX1. Acting as an electrophile, itaconate covalently alkylates the highly conserved cysteine 173 residue of PRDX1 via Michael addition. This redox modification sterically blocks intermolecular disulfide bond formation, thereby preventing PRDX1 dimerization and subsequent secretion from primary macrophages. Consequently, the loss of extracellular PRDX1 dimers reduces Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) engagement and suppresses downstream MAPK and NF-κB signaling cascades. Strikingly, the PRDX1-C173S loss-of-function mutation abolished the inhibitory efficacy of 4-OI, confirming Cys173 as an indispensable pharmacological target. Together, our study bridges immunometabolism and redox biology by demonstrating that itaconate restrains systemic inflammation through covalent trapping of PRDX1 in a monomeric state, providing a targeted redox-based therapeutic strategy for acute inflammatory diseases.

articles.title: Jujuboside A ameliorates T2DM-associated MASH: Suppression of YY1/FAS axis-mediated hepatic de novo fatty acid biosynthesis.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) represents a progressive subtype of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and is predominantly driven by dysregulated hepatic fatty acid (FA) metabolism. Although Jujuboside A (Ju A), a major bioactive triterpene saponin isolated from Ziziphus jujuba Mill. (sour jujube), exhibits hepatoprotective properties, its precise regulatory mechanisms underlying T2DM-associated MASH remain poorly defined. This study investigated the dose-dependent protective effects and molecular mechanisms of Ju A using both in vivo and in vitro models. Combining targeted FA profiling and long-chain FAs (LCFAs)-specific metabolomics, alongside chromatin immunoprecipitation (Ch-IP), luciferase reporter assays, molecular docking with dynamics simulations, and Yin Yang 1 (YY1) gain-of-function and fatty acid synthase (FAS) inhibition (C75) studies, we characterized Ju A-mediated metabolic reprogramming and molecular targets involved. Ju A treatment markedly ameliorated MASH and hepatic lipid deposition in diabetic mice by restoring dysregulated hepatic FA homeostasis, particularly by blocking de novo lipogenesis (DNL)-derived LCFA accumulation. Mechanistically, Ju A exerted these effects by blocking the nuclear translocation of YY1. This inhibition diminished YY1 binding to the FAS promoter, subsequently downregulating FAS expression and inhibiting aberrant hepatic de novo FA biosynthesis. Collectively, these findings demonstrated that Ju A ameliorated T2DM-associated MASH by restoring hepatic FA homeostasis via inactivation of the YY1-FAS axis, highlighting its promising therapeutic potential against diabetic liver complications.

articles.title: Carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales in intensive care units: England 2022 point-prevalence survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) are increasingly detected in England; however, national hospital prevalence is unknown. We aimed to generate intensive care unit (ICU) CPE prevalence estimates in England.

METHODS: Randomly selected NHS Trusts were invited to participate in a national point prevalence survey (PPS). Each Trust sampled up to 20 patients per ICU on a single date (between 18/04/2022-2/5/2022). Trust-, ICU-, and patient-level data were collected from medical records, including screening policies, demographics, clinical characteristics, and risk factors. CPE status was determined using routine testing.

RESULTS: Sixty-six of 111 invited Trusts (59.5%) participated, contributing data from 68 adult, 10 paediatric, and 43 neonatal ICUs. Testing coverage varied across settings: 40.5% (258/637) of adults, 68.1% (62/91) of paediatric patients, and 27.3% (104/381) of neonates were tested. CPE prevalence in screening or clinical specimens was 1.6% in adults (4/258; 95%CI0.4-3.9%), 1.0% in neonates (1/104; 95%CI0.0-5.2%), and 0% in paediatric patients (0/62; 95%CI0.0-5.8%). Most responding Trusts reported screening policies, particularly for adult (95.4%) and paediatric (100%) ICUs, while neonatal policies were less common (82.1%). Screening accounted for 97.9% of tests. Four of five CPE cases were identified in high-screening ICUs, and two patients initially screened negative before later testing positive. Overall, 112 patients were screened to detect one CPE case.

CONCLUSIONS: This first national CPE PPS found <2% prevalence in ICUs. Variation in screening practice limits inference about underlying carriage prevalence but highlights heterogeneity in policy implementation. No policy changes are recommended, however, these findings support further evaluation of serial post-admission screening.

articles.title: Tranexamic Acid Prophylaxis During Cesarean Delivery Among Patients with and Without Hypertension.
authors: Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development (NICHD) Maternal-Fetal Medicine Units Network (MFMU)
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with chronic and pregnancy-related hypertension are at increased risk of postpartum hemorrhage and have fewer uterotonic options because methylergonovine is generally contraindicated. Hypertensive disorders are also characterized by endothelial dysfunction and altered coagulation-fibrinolytic pathways, providing biologic plausibility that tranexamic acid (TXA) may have differential effects in this population.

OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to examine whether the effect of prophylactic TXA during cesarean delivery (CD) on peripartum bleeding-related outcomes differed based on hypertensive status.

STUDY DESIGN: This is a non-prespecified secondary analysis of a multicenter, placebo-controlled trial of patients undergoing CD who were randomized to 1gram of TXA or placebo. For this analysis, all participants were included and divided into subgroups based on the presence of chronic and pregnancy-related hypertension (HTN) prior to delivery. The primary outcome was a composite of blood transfusion or maternal death before hospital discharge or seven days postpartum, whichever occurred first. Secondary outcomes included several measures of peri-partum bleeding related outcomes. Relative risks (RR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated for categorical and mean differences for continuous outcomes. P values for interaction with HTN were calculated.

RESULTS: Of the 10,995 participants randomized in the parent trial, 2707 (24.6%) had HTN (7.1% chronic hypertension and 17.5% pregnancy related). The effect of TXA on the primary outcome did not differ by HTN status at randomization (HTN: TXA 4.9% vs placebo 6.0%; RR 0.84 (95% CI 0.62-1.16); no HTN: TXA 3.2% vs placebo 3.7%; RR 0.91 (0.73-1.14); p for interaction 0.64). For all secondary outcomes, the interaction p similarly was non-significant (all p >0.05).

CONCLUSION: The effect of prophylactic TXA at CD on blood transfusion or maternal death within one week postpartum, or other peripartum bleeding-related outcomes, did not differ by the presence of HTN.

articles.title: First- and second-generation antipsychotic use in pregnancy and risks of pregnancy and birth outcomes.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antipsychotic use in pregnancy has increased, but evidence on potential maternal and neonatal complications remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the associations between continued first-generation antipsychotic (FG) or second-generation antipsychotic (SG) use during pregnancy and the risks of pregnancy complications and adverse birth outcomes.

STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a population-based cohort study including all liveborn singletons born to women in Denmark (2004-2022) who filled ≥1 antipsychotic prescription from one year to 30 days before conception. Women who continued FGs or SGs through 20 gestational weeks (for pregnancy complications) or throughout pregnancy (for birth outcomes) were classified as continuers. SGs were further categorized into high metabolic risk (olanzapine, quetiapine, clozapine) or low metabolic risk (risperidone, aripiprazole, ziprasidone). Outcomes included gestational diabetes, gestational hypertension, and adverse birth outcomes identified from medical records. Adjusted odds ratios (ORs) were estimated using generalized estimating equations, accounting for maternal characteristics and psychiatric history.

RESULTS: Among 7,417 pregnancies, 453 (6.1%) were exposed to FGs, 2,219 (29.9%) to SGs, and 4,745 discontinued treatment. Compared with their respective discontinuers, continuing SGs was associated with higher odds of gestational diabetes (OR = 1.19, 95% CI 0.96-1.48) and gestational hypertension (OR = 1.20, 95% CI 0.97-1.48), whereas no increased risk was observed for FGs (OR = 0.92, 95% CI 0.57-1.48 and OR = 1.01, 95% CI 0.60-1.71, respectively). Risks were similar for high- and low-metabolic risk SGs for gestational diabetes, whereas the increased risk of gestational hypertension was confined to high-metabolic risk SGs. Preterm birth was less common among SG continuers (OR = 0.77, 95% CI 0.64-0.93), but not among FG continuers (OR = 1.13, 95% CI 0.80-1.60). Neonatal intensive care unit admission was more frequent among FG continuers (OR = 1.28, 95% CI 1.01-1.62), but not among SG continuers (OR = 0.87, 95% CI 0.73-1.03).

CONCLUSIONS: Continuation of FGs during pregnancy was not associated with increased maternal risk but was associated with higher rates of neonatal intensive care admission, compared with discontinuation. Continuation of SGs was associated with increased maternal metabolic risk and a lower risk of preterm birth.

articles.title: Ophthalmic Artery versus Uterine Artery Doppler in the prediction of preterm pre-eclampsia at 11-13 weeks' gestation.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm pre-eclampsia (PE) is a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality. First-trimester screening using maternal factors (MF), mean arterial pressure (MAP), uterine artery pulsatility index (UtPI), and placental growth factor (PlGF) allows early risk stratification and effective prevention with aspirin. However, UtPI measurement is technically demanding and operator dependent. Maternal ophthalmic artery Doppler, expressed as the ophthalmic artery peak ratio (Oph-PR), reflects early maternal cardiovascular changes and may serve as an alternative or complementary marker for PE prediction.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the predictive performance of adding maternal Oph-PR versus uterine UtPI to the first-trimester prediction model for preterm PE that uses MF, MAP, and, PlGF.

STUDY DESIGN: This was a prospective observational study involving women attending first-trimester screening at 11+2 to 14+2 weeks of gestation. Maternal factors, measurement of MAP, serum PlGF collection, ultrasound examination for UtPI and Oph-PR measurement, were performed during the visit. Receiver-operating characteristics (ROC) curve analysis was used to determine the area under the curve (AUC), detection rates (DR), and positive screening cut-off from the Bayesian Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) survival models in predicting the occurrence of preterm PE (<37 weeks of gestation). De Long's test was performed to compare the superiority of the AUCs among models.

RESULTS: Of 946 eligible participants, 71 (7.49%) were affected by PE, and 21 (2.2%) had preterm PE. The predictive performance of the UtPI-based model (MF + MAP + UtPI and MF + MAP + UtPI + PlGF) was similar to that of the Oph-PR-based models (MF + MAP + Oph-PR and MF + MAP + Oph-PR + PlGF) in the prediction of preterm PE (AUC 0.805 and 0.837 vs 0.789 and 0.830; p=0.584 and 0.687, respectively). The combination of MF, MAP, UtPI, Oph-PR, and PlGF in predicting preterm PE demonstrated the highest AUC compared to the other prediction models (AUC 0.919, 95% CI 0.875-0.963).

CONCLUSION: UtPI and Oph-PR are comparable for first-trimester prediction of preterm PE. Combining both Doppler indices in a prediction algorithm may improve predictive performance for preterm PE.

articles.title: MRI-BASED BIPLANAR PREDICTION OF THE DOMINANT FACIAL NERVE PLANE IN BENIGN PAROTID SURGERY USING FIXED OSSEOUS LANDMARKS.
articles.journal: Journal of stomatology, oral and maxillofacial surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preservation of the facial nerve remains the principal technical challenge in benign parotid surgery. Conventional superficial-versus-deep classification does not predict whether the dominant nerve plane will be encountered over or deep to the tumor. This study evaluated an MRI-based biplanar model anchored to fixed osseous landmarks.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Adults undergoing surgery for benign parotid neoplasms between January 2010 and December 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. Operative findings were the reference standard. Axial deep displacement (ADD), coronal medial offset (CMO), axial posterior proximity, maximum tumor diameter, and cranio-caudal level were assessed. A prespecified logistic model incorporating ADD, CMO, and cranio-caudal level was developed in the 2010-2021 cohort, internally validated with 1,000 bootstrap resamples, and temporally validated in the 2022-2025 cohort.

RESULTS: Of 482 screened cases, 217 were eligible; 124 (57.1%) had an overlying/superior-superficial plane and 93 (42.9%) a deep/inferomedial plane. In a 50-case subset, interobserver agreement was excellent for ADD (ICC 0.941), CMO (ICC 0.965), and cranio-caudal level (weighted κ 0.908). The apparent derivation AUC was 0.849 and the optimism-corrected AUC 0.842. Temporal validation in 52 patients (33 events) yielded an AUC of 0.877 (95% CI 0.777-0.958) and a Brier score of 0.153. Calibration could be estimated only imprecisely (intercept 0.491, 95% CI -0.191 to 1.172; slope 1.173, 95% CI 0.522 to 1.824), and the validation results are therefore preliminary. Zone A predicted an overlying plane in 91.7% of cases, whereas Zone C predicted a deep plane in 81.0%.

CONCLUSION: A biplanar MRI model based on fixed osseous landmarks provides a reproducible estimate of the dominant facial nerve plane from routine MRI. Discrimination was preserved on temporal validation, whereas calibration remains imprecisely estimated; external validation and prospective evaluation of clinical utility are required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Effect of age on the association between oxygen exposure and mortality in ARDS: a secondary analysis of randomized controlled trials with independent multicenter evaluation.
authors: Greek REsearch on Treatment of Acute illness Collaborators (GRETA)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fractions of inspired oxygen up to 60% in patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation are commonly perceived by clinicians as safe, implying a non-linear association between oxygen exposure and mortality. Also, although it seems pathophysiologically plausible that the association between oxygen exposure and mortality may depend on age, relevant evidence in adult patients is lacking. We examined whether the association between fraction of inspired oxygen and mortality a) is non-linear and b) depends on age.

METHODS: We performed a secondary analysis of individual patient-level data from six acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) Network and PETAL Network randomized controlled trials ("ARDSNet cohort"). We assessed linearity of the association between fraction of inspired oxygen and mortality along with the effect of age after adjusting for covariates, including partial pressure of arterial oxygen. We tested our findings in an independent multicenter cohort.

RESULTS: In the ARDSNet cohort involving 4953 patients with ARDS, we found that the association between fraction of inspired oxygen and mortality was linear and independent of age (p = 0.655 for the interaction between fraction of inspired oxygen and age). In the independent cohort involving 559 patients with ARDS, we confirmed both the linearity of the association between fraction of inspired oxygen and mortality and the lack of effect of age (p = 0.955 for the interaction).

CONCLUSION: Data from the two tested multicenter cohorts suggest that the association between fraction of inspired oxygen and mortality in ARDS may be linear and independent of age.

articles.title: Chongcao Qingfei Capsule alleviates house dust mite-induced allergic airway inflammation by regulating metabolic homeostasis via modulation of the PDE7A-cAMP-AMPK-mTOR axis.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Chongcao Qingfei Capsule (CCQF) is a Tibetan medicinal formulation used in China for respiratory disorders presenting with cough, excessive sputum, chest tightness, and wheezing. According to its documented traditional therapeutic use, the complete formulation is used to moisten and tonify the lung, clear lung heat and resolve phlegm, and relieve cough and wheezing, particularly in respiratory conditions characterized by qi and yin deficiency with phlegm-heat obstructing the lung. These traditional indications, especially cough, phlegm accumulation, chest tightness, and wheezing, are closely related to the airway manifestations investigated in the present study. However, the pharmacological basis for the effects of CCQF on allergic airway inflammation remains poorly understood.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to evaluate the protective effects of CCQF against house dust mite (HDM)-induced allergic airway inflammation and to elucidate its underlying molecular mechanism, thereby providing experimental evidence for its documented traditional use in respiratory disorders characterized by cough, phlegm, chest tightness, and wheezing.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: UPLC-Q-Orbitrap-HRMS was used to characterize the chemical constituents of CCQF and identify its serum- and lung-distributed prototype components. An HDM-induced allergic asthma mouse model was established to evaluate the effects of CCQF on asthma. Integrated proteomic and metabolomic analyses were performed to identify CCQF-regulated proteins, metabolites, and pathways. The potential mechanism was further validated in vitro.

RESULTS: CCQF markedly alleviated HDM-induced allergic asthma by improving airway hyperresponsiveness and lung inflammation, reducing mucus hypersecretion, eosinophil accumulation, and Th2-type responses. Chemical profiling identified 55 constituents in CCQF, with six and five prototype components detected in serum and lung tissue, respectively, predominantly comprising Stemonaceae alkaloids in the lung. Proteomic and metabolomic analyses showed that CCQF treatment was associated with changes in immune regulation, oxidative stress, and energy metabolism, with AMPK signaling significantly enriched.. PDE7A was identified as a candidate CCQF-responsive protein. CCQF treatment was accompanied by higher cAMP levels, increased AMPK phosphorylation, and partial normalization of metabolic homeostasis. CCQF also improved antioxidant capacity and was associated with reduced HDM-induced mTOR phosphorylation. In HDM-stimulated BEAS-2B cells, CCQF and the PDE7 inhibitor BRL-50481 produced comparable changes, consistent with a possible contribution of PDE7A-cAMP-AMPK-mTOR signaling to the protective effects of CCQF. However, direct target engagement and pathway causality were not established.

CONCLUSION: CCQF alleviates HDM-induced allergic asthma by suppressing Th2-type airway inflammation, reducing eosinophilic infiltration and mucus hypersecretion, and restoring pulmonary metabolic and redox homeostasis. These protective effects were accompanied by lower PDE7A abundance, higher cAMP availability, increased AMPK phosphorylation, and reduced mTOR phosphorylation. Because direct PDE7A inhibition and pathway epistasis were not demonstrated, these findings should be interpreted as evidence consistent with, but not proving, a PDE7A-cAMP-AMPK-mTOR contribution. Whether AMPK activation is required for the mTOR effect was not tested. These findings provide candidate mechanistic insight and identify the PDE7A-cAMP-AMPK-mTOR axis as a candidate pathway for further target validation in allergic airway inflammation.

articles.title: Preparing for responsive management versus renal dialysis in older people living with kidney failure and frailty or multimorbidity in the UK (Prepare for Kidney Care): a two-arm, superiority, parallel-group, open-label, pragmatic, phase 3, individually randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The comparative effectiveness of conservative kidney management and dialysis in older people (aged ≥80 years regardless of frailty and comorbidity or aged 65-79 years if frailty or multimorbidity are present) living with kidney failure is unknown. We aimed to assess the relative effectiveness of preparing for responsive management-a protocolised version of conservative kidney management-and preparing for renal dialysis.

METHODS: Prepare for Kidney Care was a two-arm, superiority, parallel-group, open-label, pragmatic, phase 3, individually randomised controlled trial conducted in 31 kidney centres in England, Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland. Eligible patients had an estimated glomerular filtration rate below 15 mL/min per 1·73 m2, confirmed by at least one additional reading in the 12 months preceding consent that was not due to acute kidney injury, and were either aged 80 years or older, or aged 65-79 years with a WHO performance status of at least 3 or a Davies comorbidity score of at least 2. Eligible participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to prepare for responsive management-a patient-centred approach focused on slowing disease progression, active symptom management, and preserving quality of life without the use of dialysis or kidney transplantation-or to prepare for renal dialysis. Randomisation was stratified by centre and minimised by age; a centralised system ensured allocation concealment until randomisation had taken place. The primary outcome was the mean difference in quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), combining length and health-related quality of life from the patient-reported EQ-5D-5L scale, including all follow-up from randomisation to Aug 31, 2025. The primary outcome was analysed by intention to treat in the full analysis set, which included all randomly assigned participants, with missing EQ-5D-5L values for living participants imputed. Harms (hospital admissions and dialysis access complications) and adverse events (deaths and hospital admissions, by cause) were assessed in the full analysis set. The trial was registered with ISRCTN, 17133653 (completed).

FINDINGS: From July 1, 2017, to Aug 31, 2024, 6120 patients were screened across 31 kidney centres in the UK, 445 (7%) of whom were eligible and agreed to be randomly assigned. 228 (51%) of 445 participants were randomly assigned to prepare for responsive management and 217 (49%) of 445 participants were randomly assigned to prepare for renal dialysis. Median age was 82 years (IQR 80 to 86) and 137 (31%) of 445 participants were female. After a mean follow-up duration of 4·5 years (SD 2·1), mean QALYs were 1·354 (95% CI 1·201 to 1·508) in the prepare for responsive management group and 1·472 (1·288 to 1·655) in the prepare for renal dialysis group (adjusted mean difference -0·147 [95% CI -0·350 to 0·056] p=0·16). Specific harms outcomes were not prespecified, but hospital admission rates were similar in the two groups and dialysis access complications were significantly lower in the prepare for responsive management group (adjusted incident rate ratio 0·41 [95% CI 0·19 to 0·88]), based on 74 events in 36 participants across both groups. There were 667 serious adverse events in the prepare for responsive management group (157 [69%] of 228 participants died, with 510 hospital admissions) and 578 in the prepare for renal dialysis group (136 [63%] of 217 participants died, with 442 hospital admissions). None of these serious adverse events met the criteria for expedited reporting.

INTERPRETATION: Among older people living with kidney failure and frailty or multimorbidity, we found no evidence that either preparing for responsive management or preparing for renal dialysis was superior in terms of QALYs over a mean follow-up duration of 4·5 years. This trial provides novel comparative information for clinical decision making.

FUNDING: National Institute for Health Research Health Technology Assessment programme.

articles.title: Left main coronary artery disease: PCI or CABG for revascularisation strategy.
National, regional, and global trends in adolescent physical activity from 2010 to 2025: a pooled analysis of 389 surveys with 3·2 million participants from 140 countries.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physical activity during adolescence improves current and future physical and mental health and contributes to preventing non-communicable diseases. We aimed to update national, regional, and global estimates of adolescent physical activity, examine the distribution of activity across days of the week, assess trends from 2010 to 2025, and progress towards the 2030 global target.

METHODS: We pooled data from population-based surveys of self-reported number of active days (≥60 min of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity) in the past week among adolescents aged 11-17 years collected in or after 2008. Using Bayesian ordinal models, we estimated the distribution of active days per week and mean active days per week, by sex, age, country, and year. Separate models were fitted for boys and girls. We computed the posterior probability that boys' statistics were higher than girls', and that mean active days per week were higher in 2025 than in 2010. We generated projections to 2030 to assess progress towards the global target of a 15% relative reduction in the percentage of adolescents reporting fewer than 7 active days per week.

FINDINGS: In 2025, 24·9% (95% uncertainty interval [UI] 21·8-28·5) of adolescents globally reported 0 active days per week, and 13·9% (12·6-15·6) reported being active on 7 days per week. The global mean was 2·7 (95% UI 2·6-2·9) active days per week. Globally, there was no change detected between 2010 and 2025. No country is on track to meet the 2030 global target. Girls' mean active days per week were lower than boys' globally (2·4 [2·2-2·7] vs 3·0 [2·8-3·2], posterior probability >0·99) and in all regions (posterior probability was 0·63 in Oceania and ≥0·89 in all other regions). In central and eastern Europe and central Asia, east Asia and the Pacific, and high-income western (comprising western Europe, northern America, Australia, and New Zealand) regions, mean active days per week (3·8-4·1 vs 2·2-2·7 in other regions) and the change in mean active days per week from 2010 to 2025 (small increases of 0·1-0·3 active days vs no change detected) were more favourable than in other regions. However, in these three regions, mean active days per week declined with age (1·2-1·4 and 0·5-0·8 fewer days at age 17 years than at age 11 years for girls and boys, respectively).

INTERPRETATION: Globally, adolescent physical activity remains low, especially among girls. Increasing physical activity will require effectively implemented, context-specific actions that prioritise the least active adolescents together with whole-population approaches that address socioeconomic, environmental, and cultural barriers.

FUNDING: WHO Foundation, European Commission, and the Ministry of Public Health, Qatar.

articles.title: Regional Trends and Variation in Knee Osteotomy Surgery in England, UK: A Longitudinal Analysis of National Health Service Data over Twenty Years.
articles.abstract: AimsKnee osteotomy is an established joint preserving procedure; however, despite expanding indications and training, national utilisation patterns remain poorly characterized. We investigated long-term temporal trends and geographic variation in the provision of high tibial (HTO) and distal femoral osteotomy (DFO) across the National Health Service (NHS) in England.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective national epidemiological study using NHS Hospital Episode Statistics (HES). All episodes for patients aged 16-80 undergoing knee osteotomy (excluding patellofemoral) between Jan 1, 2002, and Dec 31, 2022, were extracted. Age- and sex-standardised intervention rates were calculated using Office for National Statistics population data. Trends were analysed nationally and regionally by Integrated Care Board (ICB) to determine geographic variation in service provision.ResultsWe identified 24,516 cases (22,900 patients) meeting inclusion criteria. The national standardised intervention rate increased by over 300% during the study period, rising from 1.3/100,000 in 2002 to 3.9/100,000 in 2022 (peaking at 5.1/100,000 in 2019). HTO accounted for 71.16% of procedures, and males comprised 60.9% of the cohort. In 2022, intervention rates were highest in the 16-19 (7.3/100,000) and 40-59 (4.8/100,000) age groups. Substantial regional disparity was detected, with a near ten-fold variation in 2022 intervention rates between ICB regions (range: 1.0 to 9.5 per 100,000).ConclusionKnee osteotomy utilisation has risen significantly in England, reflecting the growing role of this joint preserving surgery. However, the extreme regional variation suggests a significant potential inequity in access to joint-preservation surgery. These findings highlight an urgent need for the development of standardised treatment guidance and a review of service provision to ensure patients have access to the procedure when indicated.

articles.title: Preoperative C-reactive protein/Albumin Ratio and Outcomes After Isolated CABG.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inflammation plays an important role in the development of complications following coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery. C-reactive protein-to-albumin (CRP/Alb) ratio is a novel biomarker that reflects the inflammatory burden and nutritional status. The present study aimed to investigate the utility of preoperative CRP/Alb ratio in predicting postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay in patients undergoing isolated CABG surgery.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 179 patients who underwent isolated CABG surgery between January 2019 and December 2023. Demographic characteristics, laboratory findings, surgical data, and postoperative outcomes were obtained from hospital records. Preoperative CRP/Alb ratios were calculated using serum CRP and albumin levels. The relationship of the CRP/Alb ratio with POAF development and ICU length of stay was evaluated.

RESULTS: During the study period, 26 patients (14.5%) experienced POAF. The preoperative CRP/Alb ratio was significantly associated with POAF development (p = 0.043), and patients who did not develop POAF had higher CRP/Alb ratios. Additionally, the CRP/Alb ratio exhibited a weak, albeit statistically significant, positive correlation with ICU length of stay (Spearman's r = 0.186, p = 0.013).

CONCLUSIONS: The preoperative CRP/Alb ratio was associated with the development of POAF and ICU length of stay in patients undergoing isolated CABG surgery. As an easily available, low-cost, and widely available biomarker, the CRP/Alb ratio may be useful for preoperative risk assessment in these patients.

KEY WORDS: atrial fibrillation; C-reactive protein/albumin ratio; coronary artery bypass grafting; inflammation; intensive care unit; length of stay; postoperative .

articles.title: Should We Test for Inherited Thrombophilia in Cancer-Associated Thrombosis?
articles.abstract: Not applicable.

articles.title: Management of Rheumatoid Arthritis with Individualized Homeopathy: A Prospective, Non-Randomized, Single-Group Interventional Study.
articles.journal: Homeopathy : the journal of the Faculty of Homeopathy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory disorder requiring long-term management. Individualized homeopathy has been proposed as a potential adjunct in integrative care, though clinical evidence is limited.

OBJECTIVE: The primary objective of the study was to evaluate the effect of homeopathic medicines in the management of RA using the Disease Activity Score 28 (DAS28). The secondary objective aimed to evaluate the activity profile and quality of life of patients using the American College of Rheumatology 20 (ACR20) response criteria.

METHODS: A multi-center, prospective, non-randomized, single-group interventional RA study included 134 patients diagnosed according to the 2010 ACR/European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) criteria. Prescriptions were individualized based on classical homeopathic principles. The primary outcome, DAS28, was assessed at baseline and every 3 months for 12 months. Secondary outcomes were ACR20 response criteria measured monthly, covering tender and swollen joint counts, patient and physician global assessments, pain, and disability. The study was registered with the Clinical Trials Registry-India (CTRI/2018/01/011192).

RESULTS: Of the 134 enrolled participants, 74 (55.2%) completed the 12-month follow-up for per-protocol analysis, reflecting 44.8% attrition. Statistically significant improvements (p < 0.01) were observed in DAS28 and ACR20 parameters. The baseline DAS28 score (5.03) indicated that the study sample had moderate-to-high RA disease activity, decreasing by 1.26 points at 9 months and by 1.31 points at 12 months, reflecting an improvement over time. ACR20 response included a 40% reduction in tender joints, 90% reduction in swollen joints, and improvements in patient global assessment (77%), physician global assessment (77%), pain (75%), and disability (65%). Symptomatic assessments supported these outcomes. Rhus toxicodendron, Pulsatilla, and Phosphorus were commonly prescribed medicines.

CONCLUSION: Individualized homeopathic treatment resulted in positive outcomes for disease activity and patient-reported outcomes over 12 months, without disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drug use. Findings suggest a potential role for individualized homeopathy in integrative RA management, warranting further investigation in controlled trials.

articles.title: Cardiac Surgery Outcomes in Japanese Patients Receiving Peritoneal Dialysis Versus Hemodialysis.
articles.journal: Therapeutic apheresis and dialysis : official peer-reviewed journal of the International Society for Apheresis, the Japanese Society for Apheresis, the Japanese Society for Dialysis Therapy
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Comparative postoperative outcomes after cardiac surgery in Japanese patients receiving peritoneal dialysis (PD) and hemodialysis (HD) remain unclear.

METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 26 dialysis patients who underwent cardiac surgery from 2016 to 2022. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause death, ischemic stroke, bleeding complications, and infections during hospitalization. The secondary endpoints included intubation duration, intensive care unit (ICU) stay, and postoperative stay in the cardiovascular surgery department.

RESULTS: Seven patients received PD and nineteen received HD. The composite outcome occurred in 14% in PD and 42% in HD patients (p = 0.36). Median intubation duration and ICU stay were 1 vs. 2 days (p = 0.18) and 4 vs. 4 days (p = 0.91), respectively. Median postoperative stay was shorter in PD than HD patients (14 vs. 17 days, p = 0.03).

CONCLUSION: No statistically significant difference in the composite in-hospital outcome was observed between groups, although estimates were imprecise because of the small sample size.

articles.title: Psychopathological symptoms and self-concept clarity: nursing homes vs non-medicalized facilities.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Older adults' living environment can affect psychological health during transitions like institutionalization. This study compared psychopathological symptoms, self-concept clarity, and time perspective by residence type.

METHOD: This cross-sectional study included 45 older adults aged 62 to 102 years, living in France. Twenty-four resided in nursing homes and twenty-one in non-medicalized facilities; scales assessed self-concept clarity, psychopathology, and temporal orientation. Descriptive statistics were calculated, and groups were compared using Mann-Whitney U tests. Factors associated with trauma-related symptoms were examined using logistic regression with Firth penalization and bootstrap internal validation, and were re-estimated on the continuous PCL-5 score.

RESULTS: The nursing home group exhibited significantly lower self-esteem and significantly more depressive and trauma-related symptoms linked to institutional entry than the non-medicalized living facilities group; anxiety scores did not differ significantly, although the study was underpowered to detect a difference of the size observed. The nursing home group was significantly less future-oriented; self-concept clarity did not differ. Group affiliation and anxiety score were associated with the presence of traumatic symptoms, with level of dependence retained as a confounder.

CONCLUSION: We found no evidence that self-concept clarity differs by residence type, although the study was powered only for large effects; living in a nursing home was, however, associated with more trauma-related symptoms in older adults. Anxiety may reflect adaptation difficulties and negative future anticipation; interventions targeting anxiety could help mitigate this impact. Given the small sample and the cross-sectional design, all findings describe associations measured concurrently and require replication in larger longitudinal samples.

articles.title: National trends and demographic disparities in concurrent atrial fibrillation and chronic kidney disease mortality in the United States, 1999-2024.
articles.journal: Journal of the National Medical Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) are conditions that frequently co-occur and worsen the adverse outcomes associated with each condition, leading to increased mortality. We evaluated AF and CKD-related mortality trends and disparities in the U.S. from 1999 to 2024.

METHODS: Data for individuals listing both AF and CKD as either underlying or contributing cause of death were extracted from the CDC WONDER database between 1999 and 2024, and age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) were computed per 100,000 population of various demographic and geographic subgroups. The temporal mortality trends were represented by the annual percent changes (APCs) in AAMR calculated through the joinpoint regression program.

RESULTS: A total of 207,853 AF-CKD-related deaths were reported, with AAMR increasing significantly from 0.79 in 1999 to 6.03 in 2024, driven predominantly by a sharp rise from 2011 to 2024 (APC: 4.25). Males consistently exhibited higher rates than females (4.02 vs. 2.24; APC: 4.13 vs. 4.19, respectively; both P < 0.05). Among races/ethnicities, mortality rates were highest in non-Hispanic (NH) Whites (3.01; APC: 4.83; P < 0.05), followed by NH African Americans (2.98; APC: 7.63; P < 0.05), NH American Indians (2.62), and lowest in NH Asians/Pacific Islanders and Hispanics (1.87 each), with Hispanics showing a sharp recent decline (APC: -8.39; P < 0.05). Adults aged ≥85 years (CMR: 60.55) had the highest mortality, while the 55-64 age group exhibited the fastest recent increase (APC: 5.37; P < 0.05), followed by the 85+ (APC: 5.10; P < 0.05), 65-74 (APC: 3.49; P < 0.05), and 75-84 (APC: 3.08; P < 0.05) age groups. Geographically, the Midwest (3.7) and non-metropolitan regions (3.2) recorded the highest AAMRs, with both metropolitan and non-metropolitan areas showing significant increases over time (APC: 9.38 and 9.55, respectively; both P < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: AF-CKD-related mortality rose nearly 8-fold over 25 years, with the highest burden among men, NH Whites, older adults, and rural populations, highlighting an urgent need for targeted cardiorenal care and integrated surveillance strategies.

articles.title: Integrative transcriptomic and single-cell analysis identifies a manganese-associated transcriptional signature and a potential JUN/HBEGF-associated endothelial signature in COPD pulmonary vascular remodeling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a heterogeneous respiratory disease involving airway inflammation, emphysema, and pulmonary vascular remodeling. Manganese exposure has been linked to pulmonary inflammation and oxidative stress, but its molecular association with COPD vascular pathology remains unclear. This study explored a manganese-associated transcriptional signature in COPD and investigated its potential relationship with endothelial cell dysfunction and vascular remodeling.

METHODS: Bulk transcriptomic datasets were used to calculate a manganese-related transcriptional score, identify differentially expressed genes, and characterize WGCNA modules. Manganese-COPD-associated genes were obtained by intersecting manganese-related genes, COPD differentially expressed genes, and manganese-associated module genes. Functional enrichment, PPI analysis, machine-learning-based feature selection, diagnostic modeling, and consensus clustering were performed. Single-cell RNA sequencing data were analyzed to characterize HBEGF expression, endothelial subpopulations, CytoTRACE2 scores, pseudotime dynamics, transcription factor activity, cell-cell communication, and NicheNet ligand-target relationships.

RESULTS: COPD samples showed significantly higher manganese-related transcriptional scores. A total of 43 manganese-COPD-associated candidate genes were identified and were enriched mainly in pathways related to inflammation, cytokines, immune chemotaxis, and vascular processes. Machine learning identified 14 core diagnostic genes, and the combined model showed good classification performance in the training and validation cohorts. Among these genes, HBEGF showed the highest contribution in the ElasticNet model and was prioritized for downstream analysis. Consensus clustering divided COPD samples into two molecular subtypes with distinct manganese-related scores and functional features. Single-cell analysis suggested that HBEGF was closely associated with endothelial cell alterations, especially venous endothelial cells. Pseudotime and transcription factor analyses suggested a potential JUN/HBEGF regulatory relationship. CellChat and NicheNet analyses further indicated that venous endothelial cell-derived HBEGF may participate in endothelial-smooth muscle cell communication.

CONCLUSION: This study identified an elevated manganese-related transcriptional score in COPD and prioritized HBEGF as a key candidate associated with venous endothelial cell state changes and endothelial-smooth muscle communication. These findings suggest a potential JUN/HBEGF-associated endothelial signature relevant to COPD pulmonary vascular remodeling, which warrants further experimental validation.

articles.title: Urinary oxidative DEHP metabolites and advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: Evidence from NHANES and mechanistic insights into MECPP-related macrophage inflammatory-glycolytic activation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Phthalates are ubiquitous environmental contaminants, yet their relevance to advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome remains unclear. We examined the associations between urinary phthalate metabolites and advanced CKM syndrome, and explored the potential mechanisms linking di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP)-related exposure to macrophage inflammatory-glycolytic activation.

METHODS: We analyzed 4236 adults from seven cycles (2005-2018) of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). A total of ten urinary phthalate metabolites were quantified, and advanced CKM syndrome was defined as CKM stages 3-4 using an NHANES-adapted American Heart Association framework. Survey-weighted logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, and weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression were used to assess single-metabolite, dose-response, and mixture associations. Mono(2-ethyl-5-carboxypentyl) phthalate (MECPP) was further evaluated using network toxicology, molecular docking, Mendelian randomization, single-cell RNA sequencing, and macrophage reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR).

RESULTS: Among 4236 participants, 648 had advanced CKM syndrome. In fully adjusted models, oxidative DEHP metabolites were positively associated with advanced CKM syndrome. Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest quartile was associated with higher odds for mono(2-ethyl-5-oxohexyl) phthalate (MEOHP; odds ratio [OR], 1.64; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.12-2.42), mono(2-ethyl-5-hydroxyhexyl) phthalate (MEHHP; OR, 1.60; 95% CI, 1.05-2.42), and MECPP (OR, 1.84; 95% CI, 1.26-2.68), with significant trends. Restricted cubic spline analyses suggested non-linear associations. WQS regression indicated a positive mixture association, with MECPP receiving the highest weight. Network toxicology identified 33 overlapping genes enriched in pathways related to the renin-angiotensin system, insulin resistance, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor signaling, and diabetic cardiomyopathy. Among the candidate hub genes, tumor necrosis factor (TNF) and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARG) were further examined using molecular docking and Mendelian randomization. Single-cell analyses of public mouse heart and kidney datasets localized Tnf mainly to macrophages and Pparg to cardiac endothelial cells and renal monocytes. In RAW 264.7 macrophages, MECPP potentiated palmitic acid-induced expression of inflammatory and glycolysis-related genes.

CONCLUSIONS: Urinary oxidative DEHP metabolites, particularly MECPP, were positively associated with advanced CKM syndrome in US adults. These findings support MECPP as a potential biomarker of DEHP-related exposure and generate mechanistic hypotheses involving macrophage-centered inflammatory and glycolytic transcriptional activation. Prospective and experimental studies are warranted to clarify causality and to determine whether DEHP-related exposure contributes to the development and progression of CKM syndrome.

articles.title: Migraine-driven causal genes in ischemic stroke.
articles.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
articles.abstract: Migraine, most notably migraine with aura, elevates the risk of ischaemic stroke, though the underlying causal molecular connections have not been fully elucidated. This study sought to uncover migraine-associated causal genes that confer susceptibility to ischaemic stroke and to dissect their cell-type-specific functional mechanisms operating within the neurovascular unit. We combined publicly available human transcriptomic resources, genetics-driven causal inference, machine-learning-assisted biomarker screening, mouse-derived single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlases, immune-cell deconvolution, and in-silico molecular docking. Twenty migraine-related genes were detected with causal associations to ischaemic-stroke risk. We prioritised three consensus hub genes: CD79A, PKN2, and PRKDC. In stroke patients, CD79A was significantly downregulated, while PKN2 and PRKDC exhibited elevated expression; their reliable diagnostic capacity was further confirmed in an independent external cohort. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic profiling mapped these hub genes to endothelial, myeloid and glial cell populations residing within a dynamic inflammatory-vascular pathological niche in mouse ischaemic brain lesions. Mechanistic analyses pointed to perturbed mitochondrial energy homeostasis and dysregulated adaptive immune responses as downstream consequences modulated by these hub genes. Molecular-docking simulations demonstrated high-affinity interactions between Tamibarotene, Dirithromycin and the three encoded hub proteins, highlighting these compounds as promising candidates for drug repurposing. Collectively, our multi-omics analysis pinpoints CD79A, PKN2 and PRKDC as migraine-derived causal targets for ischaemic stroke, delivers cell- and spatial-resolved mechanistic perspectives on neurovascular-unit injury, and puts forward lead compounds awaiting further pre-clinical validation.

articles.title: Structural and gendered determinants of alcohol use among young adults in an informal settlement in Ghana.
articles.abstract: Alcohol use among young adults in sub-Saharan Africa constitutes a major public health concern. However, relatively little is known about how structural factors, including housing insecurity, shape alcohol use among young adults living in informal settlements in Ghana and other parts of West Africa, particularly through a gender-sensitive lens. This study explores the associations between housing insecurity and other social characteristics with alcohol use, with particular attention to differences between men and women, among young adults in Agbogbloshie, a densely populated informal settlement in Ghana. From a cross-sectional survey of 283 men and women (139 men and 144 women) aged 18 to 24 years conducted from June 22 through July 14, 2019, we examined associations between alcohol use and housing insecurity, religion, and other sociodemographic factors. Descriptive statistics summarized demographic characteristics and alcohol use prevalence in our study population. Bivariate analyses identified associations between alcohol use and potential risk factors, stratified by gender. Multivariable binary logistic regression was performed to assess independent associations. Alcohol use was more prevalent among men (20.1%) than women (6.9%). A key structural factor associated with lower odds of alcohol use was having electricity, a marker of housing security (aOR = 0.12, 95% CI: 0.02-0.63). In gender-stratified analyses, owning or renting a home was also independently associated with lower odds of alcohol use among women (aOR = 0.06, 95% CI: 0.01-0.47). These findings underscore the importance of moving beyond individual-level alcohol prevention strategies toward gender-responsive structural interventions, including investments in affordable and secure housing and expansion of access to essential household infrastructure such as electricity. Such approaches may be particularly important for addressing the structural vulnerabilities associated with alcohol use among young adults living in informal settlements.

articles.title: Clinical and functional outcomes following transoral endoscopically-assisted treatment of mandibular subcondylar fractures: A single-center experience.
articles.journal: Journal of cranio-maxillo-facial surgery : official publication of the European Association for Cranio-Maxillo-Facial Surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Evidence on the outcomes of transoral endoscopically-assisted treatment of mandibular subcondylar fractures remains limited. The primary aim of this study was to evaluate surgical outcomes, complication rates, revision rates, and long-term functional results following transoral endoscopically-assisted treatment of subcondylar fractures. The secondary aim was to identify predictors of postoperative complications, revision surgery, and craniomandibular dysfunction.

METHODS: This monocentric observational study comprised a retrospective and a prospective study arm. The retrospective cohort included all patients with mandibular subcondylar fractures treated by transoral endoscopically-assisted open reduction and internal fixation without transbuccal trocars between December 2014 and August 2024. Fractures were classified using the AO CMF and Spiessl-Schroll Classification Systems based on preoperative CT imaging. Demographic, clinical, radiographic, surgical, and postoperative data were collected. The prospective cohort consisted of patients who underwent standardized clinical follow-up at least 12 months after surgery, including assessment of temporomandibular disorders, mandibular function, occlusion, pain, and maximum mouth opening using standardized DGFDT examination protocols. Primary outcomes were postoperative complications and revision surgery; long-term functional outcome was evaluated as a tertiary endpoint. Descriptive statistics, exploratory bivariate analyses, and multivariable logistic regression were performed to identify factors associated with postoperative complications.

RESULTS: A total of 132 patients with 144 subcondylar fractures were included. Postoperative complications occurred in 43.8 % of fractures, whereas intraoperative revision following 3D C-arm imaging and postoperative revision surgery were required in 15.3 % and 2.8 % of cases, respectively. The most common complications were malocclusion (20.1 %), osteosynthesis material failure (15.3 %), and wound infection (14.6 %). Multivariable analysis identified longer intermaxillary fixation as the only independent predictor of postoperative complications (OR 1.052, 95 % CI 1.008-1.109; p = 0.036). Follow-up examinations demonstrated generally favorable long-term functional outcomes, although 22.7 % of patients showed signs of temporomandibular disorders and 31.8 % presented with objective occlusal disturbances.

CONCLUSIONS: Transoral Endoscopically-assisted open reduction and internal fixation provided reliable surgical management of subcondylar mandibular fractures, with a low revision rate and favorable long-term functional outcomes. Prolonged postoperative intermaxillary fixation was the only independent predictor of postoperative complications, while routine intraoperative 3D imaging supported accurate fracture reduction and implant positioning.

articles.title: Determinants of Discordance between Estimated and Measured HbA1c: The Role of Active Time in 14-Day Continuous Glucose Monitoring Data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We aimed to investigate factors contributing to discordance between estimated glycosylated hemoglobin (eHbA1c) and measured HbA1c (mHbA1c) from continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) using both 14- and 90-day data in a large Asian cohort.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 3,724 14-day and 2,664 90-day glycemic profiles with ≥70% active CGM time (AT) from 1,028 individuals with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM). eHbA1c was calculated using a regression model derived from our study population. Discordance was defined as eHbA1c-mHbA1c (overestimation [eHbA1c ≥ mHbA1c] or underestimation [eHbA1c < mHbA1c]). Similarity was defined as a difference within ±0.1%.

RESULTS: The 14-day eHbA1c model explained 74.7% of the variance in mHbA1c, compared with 88.4% for the 90-day eHbA1c model (conditional R2). Absolute discordance was significantly lower in real-time CGM (rtCGM) than in intermittently scanned CGM (isCGM) (P=0.004), and in those with higher time in range (TIR) and AT (all P<0.001). Overestimation was associated with rtCGM (P=0.016) and lower HbA1c (P<0.001). Underestimation was greater in isCGM users and in those with higher HbA1c and lower body mass index (all P≤0.001). In 14-day profiles, ≥78% AT was required for eHbA1c-mHbA1c similarity, whereas 90-day profiles maintained similarity regardless of AT. A prediction model incorporating AT, TIR, and sensor type improved accuracy (R2: 14-day, 0.774; 90-day, 0.888), particularly for 14-day data.

CONCLUSION: Factors influencing eHbA1c-mHbA1c concordance differ by CGM duration. While 14-day data require higher AT (≥78%) for accuracy, 90-day data provide more stable estimates. Clinical interpretation must account for mHbA1c, TIR, and sensor type, especially when using shorter-term CGM profiles in Asian individuals with T1DM.

articles.title: Adequacy of nutrients important for brain health and dietary supplement use among older adults in the U.S. POINTER trial.
articles.journal: The journal of nutrition, health & aging
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & OBJECTIVE: Consumption of diets insufficient in essential nutrients contributes to unhealthy aging. The objective of this study is to evaluate adequacy of key nutrients that reflect the food components of the Mediterranean-Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay (MIND) dietary pattern, one deemed important for brain health.

SETTING/DESIGN: Cross-sectional analyses of diets of participants in the U.S. Study to Protect Brain Health Through Lifestyle Intervention to Reduce Risk (US POINTER) trial PARTICIPANTS: Adults, aged 60-79 years and at risk of cognitive impairment (sedentary, suboptimal diet, other risk factors) were enrolled in the US POINTER, a phase III two-year randomized controlled trial comparing the impact of two lifestyle interventions on brain health.

MEASUREMENTS: Before randomization, participants completed a food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) assessing usual intake of foods and beverages, and vitamin and/or mineral supplements. Median daily nutrient intakes were expressed as a percentage of sex- and age-specific Estimated Average Requirement (EAR) or Adequate Intake (AI), and Tolerable Upper Limit (UL) criteria.

RESULTS: Of the 2111 enrolled participants, 2041 completed the FFQs (69% women). Nearly half reported multivitamin multimineral supplement use (49%, men; 49%, women). Common individual supplements included vitamins D (36%), E (25%), C (23%), and B12 (19%) as well as calcium (16%). Based on food alone, the proportion of participants with inadequate intakes was high across several nutrients. Supplements improved nutrient adequacy for most (except for choline, fiber and potassium) but contributed to intakes for some that exceed the UL cutoffs (vitamins A (n=28), B9 (n=134), B3 (n=160) and zinc (n=196)).

CONCLUSIONS: Widespread nutrient inadequacy (especially those integral to the MIND dietary pattern) is evident among non-supplement users. Supplement use improves adequacy but raises concerns about excessive intakes that exceed ULs. Assessment of diet and supplement intake is essential to address nutrient inadequacies in at-risk older adults.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT03688126, submitted 9/26/2018.

articles.title: Objectively measured nursing time for structured CAM-ICU delirium screening: A single-Centre observational study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe, using objectively captured system timestamps, the time nurses require to perform structured Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) delirium assessments, and to examine whether duration varies by unit, shift, or delirium status.

METHODS: Planned secondary analysis of a prospective, controlled pilot cohort study conducted across three perioperative/anaesthesiology-led intensive care units (ICUs) within a single university medical centre. During predefined "structured assessment weeks," CAM-ICU was performed twice daily; nurses manually pressed start/stop buttons within the clinical documentation system. Assessment duration was analysed descriptively and compared across ICU, shift, and CAM-ICU result using the Mann-Whitney U test; a mixed-effects linear model accounted for repeated measurements within patients.

RESULTS: 1433 structured CAM-ICU assessments were analysed in 317 patients (median 2 assessments per patient, interquartile range [IQR] 1-5). Median assessment duration was 1 min (IQR 1-2, mean 1.6 ± 1.4, range 0-10). Duration did not differ significantly by ICU (p = 0.057), shift (p = 0.073), or CAM-ICU result (p = 0.192), and no covariate remained associated with duration after accounting for within-patient clustering.

CONCLUSIONS: When embedded in routine workflow and supported by an integrated documentation system, structured CAM-ICU screening was consistently brief across units, shifts, and patient acuity, objectively confirming the lower end of previously reported estimates; confidence intervals around subgroup differences were narrow enough to exclude clinically relevant differences on the order of one minute or more.

IMPLICATIONS FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE: Perceived time burden may be a less decisive, stand-alone barrier to structured delirium screening than previously assumed. Units considering reduced screening frequency on time-burden grounds should first collect local, objective time data, and should prioritise streamlined documentation and sustained training over shortening the assessment itself. In this cohort, structured CAM-ICU screening took a median of only one minute per assessment.

articles.title: Immunoinformatics-based design of a multi-epitope vaccine against Fusobacterium nucleatum-associated colorectal cancer.
articles.abstract: A multi-epitope vaccine candidate, A-20EFγ, was rationally designed against Fusobacterium nucleatum using proteomic and genomic information. The construct comprises a B-cell epitope (epitope 20) derived from the ABC transporter permease, along with cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL) and helper T-lymphocyte (HTL) epitopes (epitopes E, F, and γ) selected from the nickel ABC transporter permease. All epitopes demonstrated favorable immunological properties, including high antigenicity, surface accessibility, and the absence of allergenicity and toxicity. These epitopes were assembled using suitable linkers, and outer membrane protein A was incorporated as an adjuvant to enhance immunogenicity. Additionally, the PADRE sequence was included to improve immune stimulation and population coverage, resulting in a remarkable increase in predicted MHC class II and combined population coverage to 99.98%. The three-dimensional structure of the finalized vaccine was modeled using multiple computational approaches and validated through structural quality assessments and molecular dynamics simulations, with the RoseTTAFold model showing superior stability. Molecular docking, network normal mode, and binding free energy analyses revealed stable interactions between the vaccine and Toll-like receptors 2 and 4. Immune simulations further suggested that A-20EFγ could elicit a robust and long-lasting humoral immune response, characterized by high IgG and IgM levels and enhanced memory B-cell activity. Lastly, codon optimization and in silico cloning were conducted to facilitate in vitro synthesis and predict efficient expression in E. coli using the pET-28a (+) vector. Overall, these preliminary findings suggest A-20EFγ as a potential prophylactic vaccine candidate for the prevention of F. nucleatum-associated colorectal cancer.

articles.title: Early post-resuscitation profiles after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: A latent class analysis.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early cardiopulmonary heterogeneity after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) may be associated with prognosis and treatment response.

OBJECTIVES: To identify early post-resuscitation profiles and explore their associations with outcomes and randomized treatment effects.

METHODS: In this post hoc analysis of the BOX pulmonary artery catheter substudy, latent class analysis (LCA) was applied to early clinical, echocardiographic, and invasive hemodynamic variables. The primary outcome was 365-day all-cause mortality. Exploratory cross-cohort replication used a separately fitted LCA in the Targeted Temperature Management (TTM) cohort, with 180-day mortality.

RESULTS: Among 700 BOX patients, a two-class model was selected. Class 2 (n = 352) showed longer time to return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), higher lactate, greater cardiopulmonary dysfunction, higher filling pressures, and greater noradrenaline requirements. Mortality was 48% in Class 2 versus 21% in Class 1. No treatment interaction was detected for mean arterial pressure (MAP; P = 0.606), oxygenation (P = 0.483), or fever-control duration (P = 0.946). Mortality discrimination was not superior to time to ROSC alone. In 152 TTM patients, mortality was 38% versus 24% (P = 0.057), with less pronounced hemodynamic separation.

CONCLUSION: Two early post-resuscitation profiles were identified after OHCA, with more pronounced separation in filling pressures than cardiac output in BOX. The profiles were associated with prognosis but did not identify differential responses to the randomized interventions.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: BOX trial, ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT03141099; TTM trial, ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT01020916.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of add-on sotatercept therapy for pulmonary arterial hypertension. A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sotatercept is an FDA first-in-class activin signaling inhibitor for the treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH).

OBJECTIVES: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of add-on sotatercept in PAH.

METHODS: Public databases were searched from inception to May 15, 2026 for RCTs and cohort studies of adult PAH patients receiving add-on sotatercept. Primary outcomes included 6-minute walking distance (6MWD), all-cause mortality, hospitalization, NT-proBNP, pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR), and WHO-Functional Class. Secondary outcomes comprised adverse events, bleeding events, cardiometabolic outcomes, and other tolerability outcomes.

RESULTS: Six studies comprising 2769 patients were included. Sotatercept significantly improved 6MWD (MD: 25.15 m; 95% CI: 7.86 to 42.44) and WHO-FC (OR: 2.34; 95% CI: 1.78 to 3.18) and reduced PVR (MD: -254.23 dyn·sec·cm⁻⁵; 95% CI: -334.46 to -174.00), NT-proBNP (-540.21 pg/mL; 95% CI; -871.47 to -208.96), right ventricular failure (OR: 0.22; 95% CI: 0.09 to 0.51), peripheral edema (OR: 0.47; 95% CI: 0.28 to 0.78) The pooled analyses also suggested reductions in hospitalization (OR: 0.41; 95% CI: 0.20 to 0.84; P = 0.01) and all-cause mortality (OR:0.50; 95% CI: 0.36 to 0.70), although the certainty was limited by the available evidence. Most safety outcomes were comparable to placebo; however, bleeding events were more frequent with sotatercept.

CONCLUSION: Add-on sotatercept significantly improved exercise capacity, functional status, biomarker profiles, hemodynamic parameters and clinical profiles, with side effects being generally comparable with control. These findings support the use of sotatercept as an effective targeted add-on therapy to background treatment. (PROSPERO; CRD420261415041).

articles.title: The 'cost of complexity' of boarding mechanically ventilated patients in emergency department crowding: A retrospective NEDOCS analysis with deterministic scenario modelling in a Chilean university hospital.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Emergency department (ED) crowding and the boarding of critically ill patients compromise patient safety and emergency nursing care. We described crowding in the adult ED of a high-complexity university hospital using the National Emergency Department Overcrowding Scale (NEDOCS) and quantified the "cost of complexity": the additional crowding attributable to boarding mechanically ventilated patients.

METHODS: Retrospective observational study of 21,620 adult ED episodes (2023). NEDOCS was reconstructed from electronic timestamps (12 treatment spaces; 305 hospital beds) and classified using the original levels. Because ventilated patients were not recorded, the ventilator term was fixed at zero (reference, V = 0), one (V = 1) or two (V = 2) patients, keeping all other components at observed values.

RESULTS: Admission was required in 23.5% of episodes; mean door-to-doctor time was 48.4 min (median 7.7), and occupancy exceeded the 12 treatment spaces during 40.1% of hours. The mean annual NEDOCS was 104.5 points ("overcrowded") in the reference scenario. Each ventilated boarder adds a constant 13.4 points: with V = 2, the annual mean rose to 131.3, days with a mean above 180 increased from 40 to 74, and months above 140 from none to four. On weekdays, NEDOCS was below 100 only from 03:00 to 10:00; an evening plateau (15:00-22:00; 164-177 points) exceeded 180 points from 14:00 to 23:00 under V = 2.

CONCLUSIONS: Ventilated boarders add a fixed increment to NEDOCS that, in an already overcrowded ED, pushes peak days and hours into the dangerously overcrowded range. Earlier inpatient discharges, timely critical care bed allocation and NEDOCS-triggered full-capacity protocols warrant prospective evaluation to protect patient safety and nursing capacity.

articles.title: Monte Carlo simulation of a neuroimaging acquisition with MAPSSIC, a β+sensitive intracerebral microprobe for awake and freely moving rats.
articles.abstract: Establishing robust correlations between molecular neuroimaging and behavioral studies is essential in preclinical research to advance our understanding of brain function and to critically assess the translational relevance of animal models in drug development.Achieving this goal, however, requires imaging animals while they are awake and freely moving -an ongoing challenge, as most preclinical imaging techniques rely on anesthesia.Approach: To overcome the limitations imposed by anesthesia, the MAPSSIC project aims to develop a novel implantable pixelated probe based on Monolithic Active Pixel Sensors (MAPS), designed for use in awake, freely moving rats. By virtue of its direct implantation within the targeted brain regions, the MAPSSIC probe enables the local detection of short-range β+particles emitted by radiotracers, in contrast to conventional micro-PET systems that rely on detecting coincident annihilation γ-rays. In this study, we present Monte Carlo simulations of a typical in vivo brain imaging experiment using [11C]Raclopride, a commonly employed β+-emitting radiotracer, to evaluate the probe's performance.Main results: Results show that over 93 % of detected events originate from particles emitted within the first 2 mm surrounding the probe while also allowing to quantify variations of 5 % to 30 % of the non-displaceable binding potential (BPND) with discrepancy of less than 4 % compared to micro-PET.Significance: This Monte Carlo study demonstrates the device's ability to capture small variations of BPNDbased on spatially localized information, validating its suitability for quantitative kinetic analysis in brain structures such as the striatum.

articles.title: Remimazolam versus propofol for sedation in mechanically ventilated ICU patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Propofol is widely used for sedation in the intensive care unit (ICU), but its use may be limited by cardiovascular depression, hypertriglyceridemia, and propofol infusion syndrome. Remimazolam has emerged as a potential alternative to propofol, with rapid metabolism, predictable recovery, and flumazenil reversibility. However, evidence regarding its use in mechanically ventilated ICU patients remains limited.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, and ClinicalTrial.gov databases were reviewed for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing remimazolam with propofol in mechanically ventilated ICU patients. The primary outcome was percentage of time within the target sedation range. Secondary outcomes included sedation success rate, 28-day mortality, ICU mortality, length of ICU stay, and duration of mechanical ventilation. Safety outcomes including adverse events leading to dose reduction, hypotension, and delirium were evaluated. Continuous endpoints were reported using mean differences (MDs), and dichotomous outcomes were analyzed using risk ratios (RRs), with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Six RCTs including 705 patients were analyzed. No statistically significant difference was detected in the percentage of time within the target sedation range (MD, -0.45%; 95% CI, -2.46 to 1.55; p = 0.56; I2 = 0%). No significant differences were detected in sedation success rate, 28-day mortality, ICU mortality, ICU length of stay, and duration of mechanical ventilation, or safety outcomes, although several estimates were imprecise.

CONCLUSION: Remimazolam probably results in little to no difference in sedation efficacy compared with propofol in mechanically ventilated ICU patients. However, uncertainty remains regarding clinical and safety outcomes. Larger multinational RCTs are warranted to clarify these effects.

articles.title: Impact of the updated SOFA-2 score on organ dysfunction assessment and trial outcomes in Sepsis: A reanalysis of two randomized trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score is the standard tool for quantifying organ dysfunction in sepsis. The updated SOFA-2 score may alter interpretation of prior trials. We reanalyzed two adult sepsis randomized trials, Ascorbic Acid, Corticosteroids, and Thiamine in Sepsis (ACTS) and Thiamine for Renal Protection in Septic Shock (TRPSS), to evaluate the impact of SOFA-2 on organ-specific scoring and trial interpretation.

METHODS: Patient data were rescored using a best available SOFA-2 reconstruction. Subscores were compared between SOFA-1 and SOFA-2 at baseline, 24, 48, and 72 h using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and Gwet's AC2.
