Trial outcomes were reanalyzed using linear mixed-effects models with SOFA-2. A post hoc, exploratory sensitivity analysis incorporated approximated urine output into the renal subscore.

RESULTS: SOFA-2 produced lower total scores than SOFA-1 in both cohorts (ACTS 9 vs. 7; TRPSS 11 vs. 10; both p < 0.001), with lower respiratory and cardiovascular and higher coagulation subscores. For the ACTS primary outcome, SOFA-2 (mean difference [MD] -0.8, 95% CI -1.6 to 0.0, p = 0.06) was similar to SOFA-1 (MD -0.8, 95% CI -1.7 to 0.2, p = 0.12) but became significant in the post hoc, exploratory urine-output analysis (MD -0.84, 95% CI -1.64 to -0.05, p = 0.04). In TRPSS, SOFA-2 did not change overall interpretation but attenuated the treatment effect at all timepoints.

CONCLUSIONS: SOFA-2 changes how organ dysfunction is defined and may influence interpretation of prior trials, particularly when urine output is included. These findings support SOFA-version transparency and prospective SOFA-2 validation.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ACTS: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03389555), registered December 28, 2017; TRPSS: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03550794), registered May 25, 2018.

articles.title: Fractionation, distribution, sources, and risk assessment of heavy metals in coastal sediments near the biggest oil shipping complex in the Red Sea.
articles.abstract: This study investigates the distribution, fractionation, sources, and ecological risks of potentially toxic elements (PTEs) in coastal sediments from Yanbu, an industrial region along the Red Sea. Surface sediments from 10 sites were analyzed for Fe, Mn, Zn, Cu, Pb, Ni, Co, and Cd using sequential extraction, pollution indices, multivariate statistics, and positive matrix factorization (PMF). Mean total concentrations (mg/kg) followed the order Fe (5313.60) > Mn (268.60) > Zn (101.93) > Cu (31.87) > Ni (22.38) > Co (6.32) > Pb (5.36) > Cd (0.28), suggesting substantial lithogenic contributions. Although residual fractions exceeded 50% for all elements, Cd, Cu, Mn, and Zn exhibited appreciable labile fractions, indicating potential mobility and bioavailability. Mean risk assessment code (RAC) values indicated medium risk for Cu (24.24%), Mn (21.51%), Cd (20.86%), Zn (19.69%), Pb (18.09%), Co (17.31%), and Ni (16.70%), whereas Fe presented low risk (8.78%). The conventional ecological risk index (RI = 37.9) indicated low regional risk, contrasting with the speciation-based index (AIT = 0.57), which suggested elevated risk associated with metal bioavailability. Spatial assessment identified localized pollution hotspots at stations 5-6 (NPI > 7). PMF attributed 68% of the metal load to direct anthropogenic sources, increasing to 82% when mixed sources were included. These findings highlight the importance of integrating total concentrations, chemical fractionation, ecological indices, and source apportionment to distinguish regional contamination levels from localized bioavailability concerns. This study provides a baseline for environmental monitoring and sustainable management of industrially influenced coastal sediments along the Red Sea.

articles.title: Factors associated with infection prevention and control adherence among obstetric health workers: A COM-B-guided cross-sectional path analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adherence to infection prevention and control (IPC) is crucial for patient safety, yet the interactions among factors associated with IPC adherence remain poorly understood. This study investigates direct and indirect factors associated with IPC adherence among obstetric health workers in South Ethiopia using a Capability, Opportunity, Motivation, and Behavior (COM-B) informed path analysis.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study among obstetric health workers (n = 218) from nine public hospitals in southern Ethiopia in June and July 2025. We conducted descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, hierarchical linear regression, and path analysis with 5000 bootstrap samples. Standardized beta coefficients with bootstrapped confidence intervals and p-values were reported.

RESULTS: The mean IPC adherence score was 82.37 ± 9.78. In hierarchical regression, the final model explained 38% of the variance (R2 = 0.38). Path analysis showed direct associations of IPC adherence with opportunity (β = 0.51 [95% CI: 0.42, 0.60], p < 0.001) and motivation (β = 0.19 [95% CI: 0.08, 0.30], p < 0.001), while indirect association with perceived importance of resource improvement through opportunity (β = 0.13 [95% CI: 0.07, 0.20], p < 0.001) and opportunity through motivation (β = 0.04 [95% CI: 0.01, 0.07], p = 0.007).

CONCLUSION: The included variables explained 38% of the variance in IPC adherence. Opportunity and motivation showed significant direct associations, and perceived importance of resource improvement showed a significant indirect association with IPC adherence, underscoring the potential importance of addressing behavioral and system-level determinants. Future longitudinal studies are recommended to inform causal inferences and intervention development.

articles.title: Disposition Patterns in Children With Low-Acuity Blunt Solid Organ Injury: An NTDB Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pediatric blunt solid organ injury (SOI) involving liver, spleen, or kidney is common. Contemporary guidelines emphasize physiologic status and clinical course rather than injury grade for management and disposition decisions. We evaluated factors associated with emergency department (ED) discharge versus short uncomplicated admission among children with low-severity blunt SOI.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the 2017-2023 National Trauma Data Bank. Patients aged ≤18 y with blunt liver, spleen, and/or kidney injury, SOI Abbreviated Injury Scale severity ≤3, Injury Severity Score ≤15, and no severe nonabdominal injury were included. Short uncomplicated admission was retrospectively defined as hospital stay ≤2 d, discharge home, no intensive care unit admission, transfusion, angiographic intervention, operation, or in-hospital complication. Staged logistic regression was supplemented by overlap-weighted and Firth penalized analyses.

RESULTS: Among 5749 patients, 352 (6.1%) were discharged from the ED and 5397 (93.9%) underwent short uncomplicated admission. SOI Abbreviated Injury Scale severity 3 (aOR 2.33, 95% CI 1.58-3.43) and multi-organ injury (aOR 2.67, 95% CI 1.40-5.93) were associated with higher odds of admission. Injury Severity Score category and physiologic variables were not significant. White race and pediatric trauma center care were associated with higher odds of admission, whereas older age, private insurance, and private vehicle transport were associated with lower odds. Confirmatory analyses produced similar estimates.

CONCLUSIONS: Among captured National Trauma Data Bank cases meeting the analytic criteria, ED discharge was uncommon. Disposition was associated with anatomic, demographic, and system-level characteristics. Prospective studies are needed to define and validate safe, consistently applied ED discharge criteria among selective low-severity SOI patients.

articles.title: Variation in Procedural Volume and Specialty Distribution at Trauma Centers.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The distribution of procedural workload across specialties and hospital locations at trauma centers has been poorly defined. The purpose of this study was to quantify procedural volume by specialty and hospital location at level I and II trauma centers.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed using data from a statewide trauma registry (2019-2025). Adult patients (≥18 y) with an Injury Severity Score (ISS) ≥5 who were admitted to a level I or II trauma centers were included. Procedures and procedure clusters (i.e., multiple performed in one setting) were identified using International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Procedure Coding System (ICD-10-PCS) codes and categorized by provider specialty and hospital location, including the operating room (OR), emergency department, intensive care unit, and other settings.

RESULTS: There were 401,063 individual procedures and 238,436 procedure clusters identified in 117,518 patients. Orthopedic surgery performed the largest share of procedures (146,932, 36.6%) and procedure clusters (84,917, 35.6%) and did four to six times the number of OR-based procedures than either general trauma surgery or neurosurgery/spine surgery respectively. General trauma surgery performed the most intensive care unit procedures and nonsurgical providers did the most in the emergency department. Level I centers performed more operations per hospital than level II centers, but collectively level II centers accounted for a greater aggregate operative burden.

CONCLUSIONS: Orthopedic surgery accounted for the largest share of procedures in trauma centers, whereas other specialties performed most of the procedures outside of the OR. Understanding these patterns may help trauma centers allocate resources to better match the location of actual procedural demand.

articles.title: A Women Surgeons Committee Demonstrates Measurable Impact and Identifies Enduring Advocacy Needs.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Despite increasing representation of women in surgery, disparities in advancement, mentorship, and institutional support persist. Evidence evaluating the impact of initiatives to address these gaps remains limited. We assessed the effect of a Women Surgeons Committee (WSC) on perceived institutional culture and advocacy priorities 2 y after implementation.

METHODS: We conducted a single-institution, survey-based evaluation of women surgical faculty at a large academic medical center. A baseline needs assessment identified initial challenges and priorities, and a follow-up survey 2 y later assessed perceived changes in institutional culture, committee impact, and advocacy priorities. Responses were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, and Mann-Whitney U-tests.

RESULTS: Twenty-nine of 38 (76%) faculty completed the baseline survey and 19 of 64 (30%) completed the follow-up survey. Respondents reported significant improvement in perceived institutional culture (P = 0.005), with departmental culture improving significantly among Department of Surgery faculty (P = 0.042). Overall, 74% reported moderate or effective WSC impact. Assistant professors demonstrated the greatest benefit. Core priorities included salary transparency, nomination processes, and professional development. Peripartum-related concerns declined from 55% to 16% following parental leave and lactation support policies, while interest in mentorship and career development remained high.

CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of an institutionally supported WSC was associated with improved perceptions of institutional culture and meaningful shifts in advocacy priorities, particularly among early-career faculty, while highlighting persistent gaps in mentorship and career advancement support.

articles.title: A Volatilomics Approach for the Identification of Volatile Organic Compounds as Biomarkers of Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia Using GC-MS.
articles.abstract: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a common and serious complication of patients at intensive care units (ICUs), contributing to increased morbidity and mortality. Current diagnostic approaches for VAP rely on clinical, radiological, and invasive methods, which are time-consuming, carry risks, and may result in delayed or inconclusive findings. The need for rapid, reliable, and non-invasive diagnostic tools is critical. Biomarkers and specifically volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in exhaled breath have emerged as promising candidates for this purpose. In this study, we applied gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) with solid-phase microextraction (SPME) to analyze breath VOC profiles in critically ill children and explore their potential as early indicators of VAP. Results reveal significant challenges in breath volatilomics, including batch effects and variability in VOC detection. However, normalization strategies allowed for meaningful comparisons across multiple time points, revealing subtle trends in VOC profiles that could differentiate patients with high and low suspicion of VAP. Notably, VOCs such as octanol and benzyl alcohol showed reduced levels in patients with higher suspicion of VAP at Day 6, suggesting potential associations with respiratory infection severity. While preliminary, these findings support further investigation into breath-based VOC signatures as a non-invasive, early diagnostic tool for VAP in pediatric ICUs. This approach could enhance diagnostic accuracy and inform timely clinical decisions, improving patient outcomes.

articles.title: Effects of Verapamil on the Pharmacokinetics and Blood Glucose-Lowering Efficacy of Saxagliptin in Normal and Streptozotocin-Nicotinamide-Induced Type 2 Diabetic Male Rats.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of physiology and pharmacology
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular side effects are the leading cause of hospitalization/death in patients with diabetes. Saxagliptin is recommended for glycemic control in patients with Type-2-Diabetes-Mellitus (T2DM), while verapamil is preferred for cardiovascular disease. Although verapamil has been reported to exert blood glucose-lowering effects, its potential influence on the pharmacokinetics and glucose-lowering efficacy of saxagliptin has not yet been fully elucidated. This study aimed to investigate the effect of verapamil on the pharmacokinetics and blood glucose-lowering activity of saxagliptin in healthy and T2DM-model rats. Pharmacokinetic profiles of oral administration of saxagliptin (20 mg/kg) in rats with four groups (two healthy and two diabetic), with or without pretreatment of verapamil (10 mg/kg/day, PO, for 7 days), were examined. Also, blood glucose levels were analyzed to determine pharmacodynamic differences. Verapamil significantly increased the peak plasma concentration of saxagliptin in healthy and diabetic rats (from 4.8±1.07 to 6.96±1.22 μg/mL and from 6.05±1.68 to 8.24±1.2 μg/mL, respectively). Additionally, it was determined that blood glucose levels decreased with saxagliptin administration in all groups, and the decrease was higher in the verapamil-pretreated groups. The findings of this study may assist identify the best pharmacological combination effects of verapamil and saxagliptin in the treatment of diabetes.

articles.title: SSRIs and SNRIs in Hematology - A Systematic Review and Qualitative Analysis.
articles.journal: International journal of psychiatry in medicine
articles.abstract: BackgroundDepression and neurotoxic complications are frequently observed in patients with hematologic malignancies (HM). Serotonergic antidepressants, mainly selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and serotonine-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs) are commonly prescribed as the first line-treatment of depression because they are safer and have fewer side effects than other medications antid. Among SNRIs, duloxetine has shown promise, with multiple experimental studies demonstrating its ability to prevent or alleviate chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN). However, SSRI/SNRIs use raise several biological and pharmacological considerations due to clinically relevant drug-drug interactions. Despite the widespread use of antidepressants in this population, robust clinical evidence supporting their efficacy and safety specifically in HM patients remains limited.ObjectiveThe aim of this review is to evaluate the effects of SSRIs/SNRIs in HM, their impact on CIPN, drug interactions relevant to HM therapy, and clinical outcomes of antidepressant use in this population.MethodsFollowing PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search of several databases (PubMed, Scopus and Web Of Science) covering the period from January 1, 2000, to January 31, 2025, was conducted.ResultsA total of 251 articles were initially identified. Ultimately, 24 articles were eligible for analysis. The data relies solely from in vitro studies indicate that SSRIs and SNRIs may enhance the effectiveness of chemotherapy. Only one clinical study evaluated antidepressant efficacy in HM patients, showing improvement in depressive symptoms with paroxetine. Moreover, duloxetine has an established clinical role in the treatment of painful CIPN. However, the evidence supporting its use for CIPN prevention remains limited to preclinical models and lacks definitive clinical validation. The safety issues include serotonin toxicity, a risk of bleeding related to SSRIs and SNRIs impact on platelet functions and other potential drug-drug interactions.ConclusionsBased on available data, it is not possible to clearly recommend SSRIs and SNRIs for HM patients beyond the registered indications. Clinical studies are needed to confirm anticancer and chemosensitizing effects of SSRIs and SNRIs demonstrated in experimental models of leukemia and lymphoma. Nevertheless, the potential broader therapeutic benefits of duloxetine and related serotonergic agents in CIPN warrant further investigation. Due to the high prevalence of depression in HM patients, more data on safety in this population is warranted.

articles.title: Preliminary effects of proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation-based jaw exercises compared with conventional jaw exercises in post-stroke patients with awake bruxism behaviors: A randomized pilot study.
articles.journal: Cranio : the journal of craniomandibular practice
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare PNF-based and conventional jaw exercises, alongside ultrasound, in post-stroke participants with awake bruxism behaviors.

DESIGN: Prospective, parallel-group, randomized pilot-controlled trial.

SETTING: Single-centre, secondary-level neurological physiotherapy care.

PARTICIPANTS: Ten post-stroke patients with awake bruxism were randomized into two groups (n = 5 each).

INTERVENTIONS: Group A received PNF with ultrasound, while Group B received conventional jaw exercises with ultrasound, four sessions weekly for 4 weeks.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Jaw opening ROM was measured using a vernier caliper, and masticatory muscle activity was assessed using surface EMG.

RESULTS: Both groups improved in jaw opening ROM and EMG activity (P < .05). Group A showed greater jaw opening (51.6 ± 2.35 vs. 42.78 ± 4.73 mm; P = .005), with no significant between-group differences in masseter or temporalis EMG activity (P > .05).

CONCLUSIONS: PNF-based jaw exercises with ultrasound may improve jaw opening and mobility in post-stroke participants with awake bruxism behaviors.

articles.title: Outcome Disparities in Geriatric Hip Fracture: Orthogeriatric Co-Management Versus Internal Medicine Admission.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hip fracture carries substantial morbidity and mortality in older adults. Orthogeriatric co-management has emerged as the evidence-based standard of care, yet the influence of admitting service on outcomes at institutions where such programs exist remains poorly characterized.

PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: Patients aged 65 or older who underwent operative management of hip fractures at an urban academic safety-net institution between January 2019 and December 2022. After excluding patients admitted to other services or requiring intensive care, the final cohort comprised 443 patients (349 orthogeriatric co-management, 94 internal medicine).

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study compared outcomes between patients admitted to an orthogeriatric co-management service versus internal medicine. Internal medicine patients received no formal geriatric involvement. Univariate logistic regression assessed associations between admitting service and binary outcomes. Multivariable logistic regression for 1-year mortality adjusted for age, sex, and ASA score. A matched analysis paired patients 1:1 on ASA score, sex, and age within 3 years using McNemar and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.

RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups, including ASA score, age, comorbidity burden, and fracture type. Internal medicine admission was associated with higher 1-year mortality (OR: 3.01, 95% CI: 1.53-5.83, p = 0.001), greater surgical delay beyond 24 h (OR: 3.16, 95% CI: 1.98-5.12, p < 0.001), longer length of stay (p < 0.001), and reduced follow-up within 3 weeks (OR: 0.32, p < 0.001). In 91 matched pairs, these associations persisted for 1-year mortality (p = 0.035), surgical delay (p < 0.001), follow-up (p = 0.003), and length of stay (p < 0.001). Multivariable analysis of 1-year mortality was consistent with the univariate and matched analyses (OR: 2.66, 95% CI: 1.32-5.25, p = 0.005).

CONCLUSIONS: Admitting service is associated with hip fracture outcomes, and this association was not explained by measured patient complexity. These findings support implementation of service-agnostic hip fracture protocols ensuring consistent surgical timing and perioperative management regardless of admitting service, particularly when serving high-risk populations.

articles.title: Stalled Capillary Blood Flow in the Brain: New Measurement Tools Unveil a Critical Role in Neurological Diseases.
articles.abstract: Flow disturbances in the smallest blood vessels of the brain, the capillaries, have long been considered a potential cause of brain dysfunction. However, owing to the technological challenge of studying blood flow in three-dimensional capillary networks, elucidating the incidence, causes, and consequences of capillary obstructions has been difficult. Advances in optical microscopes for in vivo imaging, primarily high-spatiotemporal-resolution optical coherence tomography and two-photon microscopy, have recently enabled detailed studies of these capillary stalling events in both healthy and diseased mice. In this review, we describe these imaging approaches to quantify capillary stalling, identifying strengths and weaknesses of different methods. We then review recent findings on the incidence, molecular and cellular causes, and physiological and neurological consequences of capillary stalling across multiple mouse models of brain disease, including Alzheimer's disease, stroke, and traumatic brain injury. We conclude by suggesting necessary next steps in instrumentation and analysis for studying capillary stalling, as well as how to address key unanswered questions about underlying mechanisms for capillary stalling in the brain and how this phenomenon may impact disease progression and cognitive function.

articles.title: A metabolomic signature of weight-loss and its associations with BMI-linked diseases: A post-hoc analysis of two intervention trials and a mendelian randomisation study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity is a major risk factor for a broad spectrum of diseases, yet the molecular pathways underlying this risk remains poorly understood. Individual analytical approaches-interventional trials, observational data, and genetic methods-are each susceptible to distinct sources of bias. We aimed to identify a common metabolic perturbation signature of adiposity by triangulating evidence across multiple sources of body mass index (BMI) variation, and to characterise associations between this signature and contrasting adiposity-linked disease outcomes.

METHODS AND FINDINGS: We integrated mass spectrometry and nuclear magnetic resonance metabolomic profiling from two weight-loss interventions-a structured diet programme (DiRECT trial, ISRCTN03267836) and metabolic and bariatric surgery (By-Band-Sleeve trial, ISRCTN00786323)-with mendelian randomisation (MR) estimates of the effect of lifetime BMI exposure on metabolite levels, in order to identify a consistent BMI-associated metabolite signature across sources with distinct error structures. Weight loss-associated metabolites were then instrumented using genetic variants and their associations with heart failure (HF), osteoarthritis, and kidney cancer estimated in a two-sample MR framework, with instruments grouped into clusters based on genetic similarity to aid biological interpretation. 242 metabolites were consistently altered across weight loss interventions, predominantly comprising lipids, lipoproteins, and amino acids. The majority of these showed concordant associations with lifetime BMI in MR, consistent with regulation by adiposity. Differential components of this signature were associated with disease-specific outcomes. For HF, low-density lipoprotein (LDL) measures were strongly associated with increased risk, consistent with ischaemic aetiology enrichment, whilst high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol-enrichment traits were protective, and markers of dysfunctional HDL remodelling were associated with increased risk. For osteoarthritis, lipoprotein associations were again associated with disease risk but in the opposite direction to that seen with HF; additional signals were observed in glycine metabolism pathways. For kidney cancer, the adiposity metabolite signature translated poorly into disease associations, with only 5-methyluridine and ursodeoxycholate associations identified. The main limitations of our study include the potential for residual horizontal pleiotropy with metabolite instruments despite multiple sensitivity analyses and the rank-normalised scale of metabolite measures, which limits direct physiological interpretability.

CONCLUSIONS: Triangulating evidence across dietary intervention, metabolic and bariatric surgery, and MR of lifetime BMI identified a robust metabolic signature of adiposity. The association of components of this signature with obesity-related outcomes was disease-specific, supporting the notion that not all adiposity-associated metabolic perturbations are uniformly relevant across the spectrum of obesity-related diseases.

articles.title: XGBoost-SHAP analysis prioritizes lower-frequency variants predicted to affect HNF4A binding motifs in pancreatic progenitors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Noncoding genetic variants underlie many complex traits, yet predicting their regulatory impact in cell type-specific contexts remains a major challenge. Transcription factor binding is a primary mechanism through which noncoding variants influence gene regulation, but the relationships among chromatin accessibility, variant frequency, and transcription factor binding are complex and nonlinear, limiting the performance of traditional linear models.

METHODS: We generated single-nucleus ATAC sequencing data from seven induced pluripotent stem cell-derived pancreatic progenitor cell samples and identified 93,803 heterozygous single nucleotide polymorphisms overlapping accessible chromatin regions. Allele-specific effects (ASE) were quantified for each variant via binomial tests. We trained XGBoost, logistic regression, and regularized logistic regression models to predict allele-specific effects via chromatin read depth, peak score, variant minor allele frequency (MAF), and transcription factor binding prediction for five pancreatic transcription factors: HNF4A, HNF1A, NEUROD1, NKX6-1, and PDX1. Model performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) via fivefold cross-validation as well as using test and validation SNP sets. Shapley (SHAP) value analysis was used to interpret model predictions and to cluster variants on the basis of their regulatory feature contributions.

RESULTS: XGBoost significantly outperformed linear models, particularly at stringent allele-specific effect thresholds, consistent with its ability to capture nonlinear interactions among features. Chromatin read depth, peak score, and minor allele frequency were the strongest predictors. Stratification by read-depth and MAF deciles showed that XGBoost retained better overall predictive performance across deciles than the linear models, indicating that its advantage was not explained by these variables alone. Dimensionality reduction of variants on the basis of Shapley value profiles revealed seven clusters with distinct chromatin states and variant allele frequencies. These findings were supported by highly significant pairwise differences in allele frequency distributions across the seven clusters. One cluster was enriched for lower-MAF SNPs showing strong predicted interactions with HNF4A binding motifs. Because MAF and its SHAP contribution were inputs to the embedding, the lower-MAF identity of this cluster was expected; its high ASE enrichment and distinctive HNF4A interaction structure were the biologically informative findings. Combined Annotation Dependent Depletion (CADD) analyses further supported a stronger relationship between HNF4A-related predictions and predicted deleteriousness in this cluster.

CONCLUSIONS: Integration of single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data with an interpretable XGBoost-SHAP framework provides a method for prioritizing noncoding variants and identifying nonlinear regulatory relationships in a specific developmental context. Within this framework, the stronger relationship between HNF4A-related predictions and CADD-predicted deleteriousness in the lower-MAF cluster is consistent with selective constraint on HNF4A-bound regulatory elements and suggests a hypothesis for how lower-frequency noncoding variation may contribute to intrafamilial phenotypic variability in HNF4A-related Maturity-Onset Diabetes of the Young (MODY1).

articles.title: Spatial and seasonal patterns of tick distribution and climate-driven shifts in Jiangsu Province, an SFTS-affected region of eastern China.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ticks are important vectors of zoonotic pathogens and play a key role in the transmission of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) in East Asia. However, a comprehensive understanding of their spatial distribution, seasonal activity, and climate-driven habitat suitability remains limited, particularly at the provincial scale.

METHODS: This study analyzed long-term surveillance data on free-living ticks in Jiangsu Province, an SFTS-affected region in eastern China, from 2019 ~ 2024. Seasonal dynamics and habitat-associated differences were characterized using descriptive statistics. Environmental determinants of tick distribution and projected climate-driven changes in habitat suitability were assessed using an optimized MaxEnt modeling framework.

RESULTS: A total of 8,860 ticks belonging to seven species across three genera were identified, with Haemaphysalis longicornis (89.1%) and Haemaphysalis flava (9.8%) as the dominant species. Tick density varied seasonally, with post-larval ticks predominating during the April peak and larvae predominating during the September peak. Habitat preference differed between dominant species: H. longicornis was most frequently recorded in rural villages (33.7%) and country parks (18.3%), whereas H. flava was predominantly found in urban parks (24.8%) and forest parks (20.0%). Elevation, maximum temperature of the warmest month (bio5), and precipitation of the driest month (bio14) were key environmental determinants. Under current climatic conditions, highly suitable habitats were concentrated in the southwestern hilly areas. Under the SSP245 scenario (SSP, Shared Socioeconomic Pathway), the area classified as highly suitable using scenario-specific Jenks natural breaks was larger in future projections. Compared with the current scenario-specific high-suitability area, this class increased by 336.5% and 640.3% for H. longicornis and by 91.4% and 118.8% for H. flava during 2021 ~ 2040 and 2041 ~ 2060, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Tick distribution in eastern China is strongly shaped by climatic constraints and is projected to undergo spatial reorganization, with larger areas falling into the scenario-specific high-suitability class under future climate scenarios. These findings underscore the importance of integrating climate-sensitive vector surveillance into SFTS prevention strategies within a One Health framework.

articles.title: Saccadic suppression enhances saliency of ecologically relevant stimuli in the zebrafish optic tectum.
articles.abstract: Saccadic suppression, a reduction in visual sensitivity around the time of rapid eye movements, is well-documented in primate psychophysics, but its mechanisms and functions remain debated. Here, we use zebrafish to trace the origins of saccadic suppression, and we demonstrate how saccadic suppression selectively enhances the visual salience of ecologically relevant stimuli. Saccadic suppression thus contributes to more than just compensation for rapid saccade-induced image shifts. We first established a behavioral correlate of saccadic suppression in larval zebrafish escape behavior. Then, using electrophysiology, we show that retinal ganglion cells jumpstart saccadic suppression in a spatial frequency-dependent manner. Calcium imaging, combined with 360° visual stimulation and behavioral tracking, revealed that motor signals enhance peri-saccadic suppression strength in the optic tectum, where suppression lasts for more than 3,000 ms. Notably, saccadic suppression is much weaker and more short-lived for stimuli related to hunting or escape behavior than for behaviorally less relevant global flashes. This unequal attenuation effectively increases the salience of the ecologically relevant stimuli in the optic tectum after saccades. Our results demonstrate that saccadic suppression integrates visual and motor signals to optimize sensory processing within neural constraints, and they provide insights into evolutionarily conserved visual strategies.

articles.title: Extended in vivo activity of VRC01 HIV-1 prophylaxis entails initial protective efficacy and subsequent breakthrough infections.
articles.abstract: The two parallel antibody-mediated prevention (AMP) efficacy trials evaluated whether intravenous infusion of the anti-CD4 binding site broadly neutralizing antibody VRC01 prevents HIV-1 acquisition. Here, we analyzed HIV-1 acquisition in AMP through the week 104 final study visit. Against viruses considered highly sensitive to VRC01 [80% inhibitory concentration (IC80) < 1 microgram/milliliter], VRC01 prophylaxis maintained cumulative prevention efficacy of 66.3% (95% confidence interval: 32.4, 83.2%), suggesting that the antibody successfully blocked or cleared these infections. In the post-week 80 period (after the final dose at week 72), HIV diagnosis and resistance to VRC01 were more frequent and greater in the VRC01 groups versus placebo. For instance, more HIV diagnoses with viruses considered moderately sensitive or resistant to VRC01 (IC80 ≥ 5 microgram/milliliter) were made in the VRC01 groups compared with placebo groups (11 versus 1). Plausibly, as in vivo VRC01 concentration waned, suppressed viruses-often evolving greater resistance because of selective pressure-emerged as detectable infections. Our findings suggest that, whereas single antibodies can block sensitive strains, multiple antibodies are likely required to prevent both viral escape and breakthrough infections.

articles.title: A synthetic heparin oligosaccharide decouples anticoagulation from heparin-induced thrombocytopenia risk.
articles.abstract: Low-molecular weight heparin (LMWH) remains clinically indispensable for the prevention and treatment of thrombosis in cardiovascular surgery, hemodialysis, and other critical care settings. However, LMWH is constrained by heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) and supply chain vulnerabilities of animal-derived sources. This study used chemoenzymatic synthesis to engineer homogeneous dodecasaccharide 12G-2, decoupling anticoagulant efficacy from HIT risk via dual structural modulation. Substitution with 2-O-sulfated glucuronic acid conferred conformational rigidity, and engineered sulfation attenuated platelet factor 4 (PF4) binding, whereas the antithrombin-binding domain remained intact. 12G-2 exhibited nanomolar anti-Factor Xa (FXa) activity in vitro, enoxaparin-equivalent venous antithrombotic efficacy, and superior arterial antithrombotic activity in murine thrombosis models, and it showed diminished PF4 binding, attenuated pathological β sheet formation, and minimal recognition by HIT-related antibodies in vitro. Both in vitro and in a murine tail-bleeding model, 12G-2 demonstrated high protamine reversibility, exceeding standard LMWH enoxaparin neutralization efficiency. In washed human platelets, 12G-2-PF4 complexes with the HIT-mimicking antibody KKO failed to induce integrin αIIbβ3 activation or P-selectin release and elicited minimal platelet spreading comparable to resting controls. Safety assessments in mice showed no hepatotoxicity at tested doses and low immunogenicity in a murine PF4-heparin immunization model. In PF4-heparin antibody-positive mice, 12G-2 attenuated platelet activation while exerting stronger FXa inhibition than enoxaparin. These findings established 12G-2 as an alternative to LMWH.

articles.title: Distinct tau PET dynamics in early versus late age-of-onset Alzheimer's disease.
articles.abstract: Early-onset Alzheimer's disease (EOAD) and late-onset AD (LOAD) differ in clinical presentations and rates of progression. We aimed to compare baseline and longitudinal tau positron emission tomography (PET) burden measured with 18F-flortaucipir and its relationship with clinical variables in amyloid PET-positive, cognitively impaired participants from the Longitudinal Early-Onset Alzheimer's Disease Study (EOAD; n = 390) and Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (LOAD; n = 211). Participants with EOAD showed higher baseline tau PET burden, broader neuroanatomical involvement, and stronger associations of tau PET with amyloid PET and global cognition. Higher baseline tau PET burden in EOAD was independently validated in participants with EOAD from ADNI. Longitudinally, tau PET increased more rapidly in EOAD than in LOAD, independent of amyloid PET and clinical stage. We conclude that earlier age of onset in AD is linked to a more aggressive tauopathy, which in turn is a primary driver of clinical decline.

articles.title: Longitudinal remodeling of the tumor-immune microenvironment during regorafenib, nivolumab, and chemotherapy in advanced gastric cancer.
articles.abstract: Previous studies combining the multikinase inhibitor regorafenib with a PD-1 inhibitor showed promising activity in gastric cancer. We conducted a phase 1b/2 trial (NCT05394740) of first-line regorafenib, nivolumab, and chemotherapy in 30 patients with mismatch repair-proficient gastric cancer and investigated its impact on the tumor microenvironment. The primary end point was met; 22 of 30 patients showed objective tumor response (73%; 80% confidence interval, 60.3 to 83.8). Single-cell RNA and T cell receptor sequencing were performed on biopsy samples at baseline, during treatment, and at disease progression. The combination treatment increased tumor antigen-reactive CD8+ T cells and M1-like proinflammatory macrophages and decreased immunosuppressive and tumor-promoting populations, including activated CCR8+ regulatory T cells, LRRC15+ cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), RGS5+ pericytes, and APLN+ tip cells. At progression, LRRC15+ CAFs and APLN+ tip cells remained reduced, activated CCR8+ regulatory T cells reexpanded, and additional treatment-resistant subsets emerged, including APOC1+ lipid-associated macrophages. In murine models of acquired resistance, therapeutic targeting of these suppressive immune cell populations with antibodies against CCR8 or TREM2 in combination with PD-1 blockade restored antitumor immunity. These findings demonstrate dynamic remodeling of the tumor microenvironment and suggest potential therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Orthopaedic Care in Brazil: Universal Coverage, Unequal Access, and Future Directions.
articles.journal: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume
articles.abstract: ➢ Brazil has one of the world's largest universal public health systems, the Unified Health System (Sistema Único de Saúde, or SUS), serving a population of more than 200 million people.➢ Brazil has strong orthopaedic training, an active national society, and a growing research culture.➢ Orthopaedic and trauma care in Brazil is delivered through a mixed public-private model that includes high-volume public hospitals, university centers, private hospitals, and regional referral centers.➢ The major national challenge is not only the availability of orthopaedic expertise but inequality of access, particularly between major urban centers and underserved North, Northeast, and interior regions.➢ Managing a high-volume of trauma cases is a hallmark of Brazilian orthopaedics, with major public trauma centers handling complex injuries, late-presenting cases, and cases of infection or nonunion, while facing barriers to rehabilitation.➢ The reality of orthopaedics in Brazil demonstrates the need for more robust registries and multicenter collaborations, and better integration of outcome data.

articles.title: Safety of Dexmedetomidine Use in Adult ICU Patients With Right Ventricular Dysfunction.
articles.abstract: BackgroundDexmedetomidine is commonly used in the intensive care unit (ICU) and is associated with hemodynamic adverse events, including hypotension and bradycardia. Use of dexmedetomidine has not been described in critically ill patients with right ventricular (RV) dysfunction and may be particularly relevant given the tenuous hemodynamics in this patient population.ObjectiveDetermine the prevalence of adverse events in adult ICU patients with RV dysfunction receiving dexmedetomidine.MethodsThis single-center, retrospective cohort study included adult ICU patients with RV dysfunction measured by echocardiogram who received dexmedetomidine between January 2017 and December 2022. The primary outcome was a composite of adverse events after dexmedetomidine initiation including bradycardia, hypotension, increasing vasopressor/inotrope requirements, and asystole. Secondary outcomes included individual components of the primary outcome and a comparison of adverse events based on RV dysfunction severity.ResultsA total of 245 patients met study inclusion criteria. A total of 178 adverse events occurred in 153 patients (62.4%). The most common adverse event was hypotension occurring in 129 patients (72.5%). Increased vasopressor requirements occurred in 35 patients (19.7%), and mean change in norepinephrine equivalents from baseline was 0.06 µg/kg/min. Adverse event rates did not differ among patients with mild, moderate, or severe RV dysfunction.ConclusionAdult ICU patients with RV dysfunction receiving dexmedetomidine experienced high rates of hypotension and increased vasopressor requirements. Findings from this study may assist in tailoring sedation regimens for critically ill patients with RV dysfunction. Future research is needed to explore optimal sedative agents in this patient population.

articles.title: Heart failure therapy in congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries: effect on right ventricular function and survival.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The aim of the study was to assess the effect of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) on cardiac function, neurohormonal activation, and mortality in adults with congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries (cc-TGA) presenting with systemic right ventricular (RV) systolic dysfunction. The study hypothesis was that GDMT use (assessed using the GDMT score) was associated with improved cardiac function (higher RV free wall strain [RVFWS]), less neurohormonal activation (lower N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide [NT-proBNP] levels), and lower mortality.

METHODS: GDMT score, RVFWS, and NT-proBNP levels were assessed at baseline and 1-year follow-up. GDMT uptitration was assessed using ΔGDMT (GDMT at 1-year minus GDMT at baseline). Improvements in RV systolic function and neurohormonal activation were defined as a relative increase in RVFWS of >20% and a relative decrease in NT-proBNP levels of >20%, respectively.

RESULTS: Of 213 patients (age 43 ± 15 years; 54% male), baseline GDMT score was 1.97 ± 1.27, and ΔGDMT score was 0.74 ± 0.39. Baseline RVFWS was -18 ± 5%; 25% had improved RV systolic function. Baseline NT-proBNP was 369 (142, 1004) pg/mL; 56% had improved neurohormonal activation. Higher baseline GDMT score and ΔGDMT score were associated with improvement in RV systolic function and neurohormonal activation. Overall, 34 (16%) patients died, and higher baseline GDMT score and ΔGDMT score were associated with a lower risk of mortality and of the composite adverse event endpoint (heart failure hospitalization, death, and heart transplantation). Clinical benefits of GDMT use were observed only in patients with moderate/severe RV systolic dysfunction, and not in patients with mild RV systolic dysfunction.

CONCLUSIONS: GDMT use was associated with improved outcomes in patients with moderate/severe RV systolic dysfunction.

articles.title: Obesity, frail obesity, and outcomes after durable left ventricular assist device implantation: a pooled analysis of the MOMENTUM 3 trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Obesity in patients supported by left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) is linked to excess mortality and haemocompatibility-related events. Whether this association persists with the fully magnetically levitated HeartMate 3 (HM3) pump is unknown. This analysis tested outcomes with obesity and the additive influence of co-existing frailty ('frail obesity') in the contemporary era.

METHODS: The study pooled 2200 HM3 recipients from the MOMENTUM 3 pivotal randomized trial (n = 515) and Continued Access Protocol (n = 1685). Obesity was defined as body mass index (BMI) ≥30 kg/m2 and frailty by a 40-item Rockwood cumulative-deficit frailty index (FI), with clinically relevant frailty defined as FI ≥0.325 (moderate-severe frailty); BMI was excluded from the FI to avoid mathematical coupling. The primary endpoint was survival to transplant, recovery, or 24 months of support free of disabling stroke (modified Rankin score >3) or pump replacement reoperation.

RESULTS: Obese patients (n = 887, 40.3%) were younger, less often with ischaemic aetiology, and more frequently women, but more often had diabetes and hypertension, than non-obese patients. Unadjusted 2-year outcomes were similar between groups (freedom from the primary endpoint: 75.1% vs 77.1%, log-rank P = .34; survival: 79.9% vs 81.2%, P = .57). After covariate adjustment, obesity was independently associated with a higher risk of the primary endpoint (hazard ratio [HR] 1.30, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.07-1.58) and all-cause mortality (HR 1.35, 95% CI 1.10-1.67), as well as heart failure hospitalization, infection, and arrhythmia, but not stroke, bleeding, or early right heart failure. Frailty affected 67.3% of obese recipients (571/849) and was associated with a higher adjusted risk of the primary endpoint (HR 1.51, 95% CI 1.09-2.10), overall mortality and non-haemocompatibilty-related morbidity endpoints. The obesity-by-frailty interaction was not significant for either the primary endpoint (P = .436) or mortality (P = .215), indicating additive rather than synergistic risk; frail-obese patients nonetheless carried the highest absolute risk of any subgroup. Frailty improved by at least one severity class by 6 months in 75.9% of frail-obese patients, and improvement was associated with better survival (adjusted HR 0.14, 95% CI 0.07-0.26).

CONCLUSIONS: In the HM3 era, obese and non-obese recipients had similar unadjusted 2-year outcomes; however, after adjustment for baseline case-mix, obesity was independently associated with a higher risk of both the primary endpoint and all-cause mortality, together with heart failure hospitalization, infection, and arrhythmia. Frailty was independently associated with adverse outcomes across nearly all endpoints and was highly prevalent among obese recipients; the combination of obesity and frailty was additive but not synergistic, with frail-obese patients carrying the highest absolute risk. Frailty, however, proved substantially reversible after LVAD support, and its improvement was associated with markedly better survival. Obesity and frailty should therefore be assessed together, rather than through BMI thresholds alone, with recognition that frailty status is dynamic after implantation and that improvement in frailty is associated with markedly better survival.

articles.title: A strategic shift to conquering infections.
articles.abstract: A Magnet®-recognized hospital successfully reduced health care-associated infections through a nurse-led quality improvement initiative. In response to rising catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI) and central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) rates, nursing leaders applied transformational leadership principles and the Plan-Do-Study-Act framework to redesign infection review and prevention processes. Key strategies included real-time infection tracking, standardized root cause analysis, interdisciplinary collaboration, staff education, and evidence-based interventions. These efforts led to sustained reductions in standardized infection ratio rates for both CAUTIs and CLABSIs, demonstrating how operational excellence and nursing leadership can improve patient safety and clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Temporal shifts in post-asthmatic immune responses define tumor outcomes via strain-specific monocyte reprogramming.
articles.abstract: Epidemiological evidence linking asthma to lung cancer risk remains contradictory, presenting asthma as either a risk factor or a protective condition. We hypothesize that this heterogeneity stems from the temporal dynamics of inflammatory response and host genetic background. Using ovalbumin (OVA)-induced asthma models, we identify a temporal shift in immune effectors driving post-asthmatic tumorigenesis. During acute airway inflammation, eosinophil infiltration accelerates tumor growth across mouse strains. Following resolution, however, tumorigenic outcomes in recovery diverge along genetic lines. Prior asthma reshapes chromatin landscapes of bone marrow myeloid progenitors, establishing innate immune memory that differentially programs monocytes across strains. In C57BL/6 mice, trained monocytes adopt oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), acquiring a suppressive, tissue-remodeling phenotype that promotes tumor progression. Conversely, BALB/c-trained monocytes utilize glycolysis to maintain a pro-phagocytic state, enabling tumor clearance. These findings delineate a biphasic mechanism wherein temporal shifts in post-asthmatic immune responses define tumor outcomes via strain-specific monocyte metabolic reprogramming.

articles.title: Damage Assessment of Major Soybean Viruses in Korea: Infection Timing Influences Yield Loss and Seed-Borne Transmission Dynamics.
articles.abstract: Soybean mosaic virus (SMV; species Potyvirus glycitessellati) and soybean yellow mottle mosaic virus (SYMMV; species Gammacarmovirus glycinis) are predominant viral pathogens threatening soybean production. While their high prevalence during early vegetative stages has been increasingly reported, the quantitative epidemiological impact of infection timing on ultimate crop yield and seed-borne transmission dynamics remains poorly understood. In this study, we evaluated the effect of SMV and SYMMV infections at three distinct growth stages on yield components and seed-borne transmission in soybean genotypes (Danbaek, OB13087, and Cheongja5ho) under field conditions. All seeds used in this study were produced under insect-exclusion conditions during the previous year to minimize the risk of natural vector-mediated viral infection. Results indicated that early vegetative infection caused the most severe crop loss, primarily through decreases in pod and seed numbers. Virus was frequently detected in whole seeds regardless of their external appearance, whereas seed-to-seedling transmission varied among the tested host-virus combinations. The numerically highest transmission rates occurred following late vegetative inoculation, although the effect of inoculation timing was statistically significant only in OB13087. No transmission was detected in Danbaek despite frequent virus detection in whole seeds. This study provides quantitative evidence that early-season virus management is critical to prevent irreversible yield losses, while demonstrating that visual seed sorting alone is insufficient for reliable seed health assessment, highlighting the need for molecular-based evaluation approaches.

articles.title: Cannabidiol and fronto-parietal EEG connectivity in autistic children.
articles.abstract: Autistic children often show altered brain network connectivity, including circuitry implicated in social cognition. Cannabidiol (CBD) has emerged as a potential therapy for autism, but its neural mechanisms remain under-researched. Here, we analyze resting-state data collected as part of a double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial, to explore whether 12 weeks of oral CBD oil could modulate functional connectivity in autistic children. Twenty-nine autistic children (5 to 12 years) completed two 12-week intervention periods (CBD and placebo, randomized) separated by an 8-week washout. Before and after each period, 5 min of eyes-open resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) were obtained from a subset of 18 participants (8 female). Functional connectivity was calculated across 16 electrode-pairs in the delta, theta, alpha, beta, and gamma bands. Beta-band connectivity between the right frontal and right inferior-parietal electrodes increased following CBD (P = 0.001, false discovery rate [FDR]-corrected P [pFDR] = 0.022), and alpha connectivity showed an increase that did not remain following FDR correction (P = 0.036, pFDR = 0.428). No significant differences were observed following placebo for any frequency band (pFDR > 0.69). This study provides preliminary evidence that 12 weeks of cannabidiol is associated with an increase in right fronto-parietal (F4-P8) functional connectivity in autistic children, most pronounced in the beta-band. Replication in larger samples is needed to confirm generalizability and clinical relevance.

articles.title: Comprehensive Evaluation of an Adenine/Phosphate-Induced CKD Model for the Study of Aortic Valve Calcification.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is prevalent in chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet no pharmacological therapies exist. Preclinical models rarely incorporate CKD-mineral and bone disorder (CKD-MBD) features, limiting translational potential. We aimed to develop a comprehensive preclinical approach to study CKD-associated CAVD, suitable for standardized assessment of therapies on valvular, cardiac, vascular, and skeletal outcomes.

METHODS: Eight-week-old male Sprague Dawley rats were assigned to a control group (n=17) fed standard chow or an adenine-phosphate group (AP, n=21) fed chow supplemented with 0.3% adenine and 1.15% phosphate. Diets were enriched with 20% lactose and 19% casein to facilitate phosphate absorption and calcium solubility. Cardiac function was evaluated by echocardiography at baseline, week 5, and 9, with concurrent blood sampling. Aortic valve (AV) calcification was assessed by Alizarin Red and Osteosense staining, and aortic calcium quantified using O-Cresolphthalein Complexone. Gene expression in the aorta and left ventricle (LV) was analyzed by RNA-seq at week 9, and bone microarchitecture assessed by micro-CT.

RESULTS: AP rats showed progressive increases in serum creatinine, calcium-phosphorus product, and uremic toxins. By week 9, they exhibited significant AV calcification, with reduced valve area and cusp separation. Relative wall thickness and LV histology were preserved, though transcriptomics revealed early priming toward inflammation and fibrosis. AP rats' aortas showed calcification, osteogenic features and reduced systolic expansion. Bone analysis revealed cortical thinning and increased porosity, while trabecular bone showed reduced trabecular number, increased trabecular spacing, and compensatory thickening. Together with elevated PTH and FGF23 levels, these changes suggest high bone turnover due to secondary hyperparathyroidism and are correlated with the extent of AV calcification.

CONCLUSIONS: These results underscore the model's translational relevance, addressing multiple facets of CKD-MBD and supporting its use for preclinical screening of novel therapies targeting CKD-associated cardiovascular calcification.

articles.title: Ebstein Anomaly With Pre-excited Atrial Fibrillation.
Improving Quality Through the Emergency General Surgery Verification Program.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: The Emergency General Surgery Verification Program was designed and launched in 2023 by the American College of Surgeons to standardize and improve EGS care through 43 standards that support hospital structure, care processes, and outcome surveillance.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between EGS verification and hospital length of stay (LOS), acute kidney injury (AKI), and 30-day mortality and to assess whether changes in care processes contribute to effects.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This quasi-experimental difference-in-differences cohort study with staggered adoption used data from the ACS National Surgical Quality Improvement Program EGS Targeted Dataset. Patients with operatively managed EGS diagnoses from July 1, 2023, through December 31, 2024, at 50 control and 5 verified hospitals were evaluated. Data were analyzed from July 2025 through February 2026.

EXPOSURE: Hospital EGS verification status.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes were mean LOS, 30-day mortality rate, and AKI rate. These were calculated adjusted and unadjusted. Average treatment effects on the treated were estimated with hospital-clustered bootstrap standard errors.

RESULTS: The final cohort included 21 858 patients at 55 hospitals. Median (IQR) patient age was 53.2 (36.5-68.5) years, and 12 366 patients (56.6%) were female. Prior to verification, verified hospitals treated higher-acuity patients and had higher predicted mortality and AKI rates. Verification was associated with absolute reductions in LOS (-1.31 days; 95% CI, -1.95 to -0.67), AKI (-1.23 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.00 to -0.46), and mortality (-1.63 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.55 to -0.71), corresponding to relative reductions of 19.7%, 29.0%, and 28.8%, respectively. These results held after risk adjustment and Bonferroni correction. Verification was also associated with improved care processes, including increased admission to surgical services (74.8% to 85.7%; P < .001), decreased failure of nonoperative management (25.5% to 19.0%; P < .001), and shorter time to operation (-10.7 hours; P < .001). All processes were independently associated with improvements in all 3 primary outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study, early adoption of ACS EGS verification was associated with clinically meaningful reductions in LOS, AKI, and 30-day mortality among participating hospitals. These findings demonstrate the EGS verification likely drives systems-level improvements in emergency surgical care, which may be partially explained by improvements in performance on hospital process measures.

articles.title: Ultrasonography and International Perspectives on Imaging Consensus for Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
Diagnosis and Management of Acute Cholangitis: A Review.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Acute cholangitis (AC) is a potentially fatal biliary tract infection most commonly caused by gallstones. While modern-day treatments with antibiotics and biliary decompression have drastically decreased mortality rates, AC still requires prompt intervention.

OBSERVATIONS: Diagnosis of AC traditionally relied on the presence of the Charcot triad, which has since proven to incompletely capture the complexity of this condition. Modern-day diagnosis, severity grading, and management guidelines provide a more holistic approach. Tokyo Guidelines (TG) are widely used, though newer guidelines, namely the BILE criteria, have recently emerged. These criteria include demonstration of inflammation, cholestasis, and biliary obstruction. Ultrasound is first-line imaging modality with computed tomography or magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography often used for diagnostic dilemmas. Treatment is dependent on severity, though guidelines generally recommend early decompression (most commonly with endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography [ERCP]) for moderate to severe cases. The optimal timing of biliary drainage remains unclear, with mixed evidence from observational studies and no universal definition of what constitutes "early" vs "urgent" drainage. Laparoscopic cholecystectomy should be performed during index hospitalization, when possible, with multiple studies demonstrating lower morbidity and mortality rates when compared with interval procedures. The prognosis of AC is favorable if treated swiftly and appropriately; in turn, mortality rates increase with severity and delays in diagnosis.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: AC can be challenging to diagnose and the precise timing of biliary drainage and cholecystectomy is debated. This comprehensive review reflects the most recent evidence and recommendations on severity grading, resuscitation, and timing of ERCP and cholecystectomy to assist clinicians who manage these complex patients.

articles.title: Operationalizing Reconciliation as an Ethical Decision-Making Framework in Critical Care Nursing: A Conceptual Discussion.
articles.abstract: Critical care nurses routinely face complex ethical dilemmas arising from rapid, high-stakes decision making in emergencies. The principle of reconciliation offers a structured framework for navigating these tensions by balancing competing stakeholder perspectives. This article critically examines how reconciliation can be operationalized in critical care nursing and proposes structured strategies for its implementation. Reconciliation involves acknowledging conflicting values and seeking mutually acceptable, ethically defensible solutions through open dialogue and mutual understanding. However, applying reconciliation in critical care is challenging due to limited information, severe time pressures, and the need for rapid decisions. Implementing reconciliation strategies can yield numerous benefits, including improved communication, reduced moral distress, increased patient and family satisfaction, and a culture of collaboration. Challenges to implementing reconciliation include time constraints, power imbalances within interprofessional teams, emotional intensity, cultural and religious differences, and legal and institutional constraints. Addressing these challenges necessitates a multifaceted approach that accounts for team dynamics, emotional demands, and legal and institutional structures.

articles.title: Ultrasonography and International Perspectives on Imaging Consensus for Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma-Reply.
From Incoherence to Verification: Epistemic Friction and Confidence in Evaluating AI Health Information.
articles.abstract: The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) for health information seeking raises concerns about exposure to inaccurate or misleading content. Although prior research has documented the prevalence and consequences of health misinformation, less is known about how individuals detect and respond to problematic AI-generated information. Drawing on Epistemic Vigilance Theory (EVT), this study examines whether exposure to incoherent health information influences verification-oriented information seeking through epistemic friction, defined as perceived inconsistency between encountered information and prior knowledge. Data were collected from U.S. adults with diabetes (N = 200) using an experimental design in which participants were exposed to AI-generated information about a fictitious antidiabetic drug that either aligned with or violated established medical knowledge. Exposure to incoherent content increased epistemic friction, which in turn was associated with greater verification-oriented information seeking intention. Notably, this indirect relationship was moderated by perceived evaluation confidence, such that the effect was stronger among individuals with lower confidence in their ability to evaluate health information. These findings suggest that epistemic friction may play an important role in responses to health information presented as AI-generated and that subsequent verification intentions may vary according to individuals' perceived evaluative confidence. The study extends EVT to AI-mediated environments and highlights the importance of promoting effective responses to health misinformation.

articles.title: National Survey of Canadian Radiation Oncologists' Continuing Professional Development Needs and Practices: Where are the Gaps and Barriers?
articles.journal: Journal of cancer education : the official journal of the American Association for Cancer Education
articles.abstract: Continuing professional development (CPD) involves continuing medical education (CME) and educational activities to develop research, teaching and leadership skills. Given limited literature specific to radiation oncologists (ROs), we sought to evaluate current CPD practices and identify unmet needs and barriers among ROs. An online survey was developed and emailed to ROs across Canada. CPD practices, preferences, barriers and needs were explored. Descriptive, univariable and multivariable analyses were performed. A total of 122 ROs completed the survey, with a median 12 years of experience (IQR: 5-21) and 96% university affiliation. The most helpful CME resources were journal articles, tumour boards/disease-site meetings, and conferences. Lack of time was the predominant barrier, alongside increasing clinical workload and expanding literature. Greater years in practice were associated with higher satisfaction of CME needs met (p = 0.019) and time dedicated to CME (p = 0.011). Female respondents reported greater satisfaction with time dedicated to CME (p = 0.006), without a difference in overall CME satisfaction. 76% were actively engaged in research; key barriers included time, funding, and human resources. CPD needs included statistics, clinical trial design, and grant writing. 98% were involved with clinical teaching, with many seeking to improve skills in coaching and providing feedback. Half of respondents held leadership roles, yet only 48% had formal leadership training. Overall satisfaction scores for current CME practices were mediocre among Canadian ROs - a group with high university-affiliation and research engagement. Identified needs include protected academic time and formal leadership development - highlighting potential areas for future CPD initiatives.

articles.title: Approaches to assessing functional outcome trajectories in old survivors of intensive care: a narrative review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with critical conditions admitted to an intensive care unit (ICU) undergo one of the most extensive trials of resilience. In addition to considering survival as a crucial outcome, there is a growing awareness of the importance of recovering functional abilities in old ICU patients.

METHODS: In this narrative review, a group of geriatricians and intensivists will discuss previous studies and current approaches to assess functional trajectories in old ICU survivors with a focus on frailty, functional independence and intrinsic capacity.

RESULTS: In previous studies, frailty as evaluated with the Clinical Frailty Scale or variants of the Frailty Index has been found to exhibit a dynamic course after a critical illness. Measures of functional independence show a similar pattern after ICU discharge depending on pre-existing impairments and frailty. Although the concept of intrinsic capacity could provide a holistic framework to predict functional impairments, there still is only limited data on its usefulness in the context of a critical illness.

CONCLUSION: Assessing the post-discharge trajectory in old survivors of a critical illness is crucial to detect early signs of complications and adjust individual support. However, current approaches in this field lack validation. Considering the challenges and importance of functional recovery in old ICU patients, more intensive research in the future is imperative in order to determine the best approach to describe, monitor and optimise the health status amongst these individuals.

articles.title: Predicting neoadjuvant chemotherapy efficacy in triple-negative breast cancer using DCE-MRI and mammographic texture.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and validate a predictive model integrating dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) kinetic features and digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) texture features for predicting pathological complete response (pCR) following neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in patients with triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Additionally, its predictive performance was compared with that of single-modality models.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 360 patients with pathologically confirmed TNBC who received NAC between January 2022 and December 2025 were retrospectively and consecutively collected. Patients were randomly allocated to a training set (n = 252) and a validation set (n = 108) at a 7:3 ratio. Pre-NAC DCE-MRI kinetic and DBT texture features were extracted. After feature selection using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, DCE-MRI and DBT radiomics scores (Rad-scores) were constructed. A nomogram prediction model was then developed using multivariable logistic regression incorporating clinicopathological and laboratory indicators. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical net benefit were evaluated using the receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis, respectively. These results were subsequently compared with those of a clinical-only model and single-modality combined models.

RESULTS: The pCR rates in the training and validation sets were 41.67% and 40.74%, respectively. Multivariable logistic regression identified Ki-67 proliferation index, maximum tumor diameter, background parenchymal enhancement score, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, lactate dehydrogenase level, DCE-Rad score, and DBT-Rad score as independent predictors of pCR (P < 0.05). The dual-modality nomogram achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.784 (95% CI: 0.718-0.851) in the training set and 0.759 (95% CI: 0.644-0.873) in the validation set, outperforming the clinical-only model (0.727), the clinical plus DCE-Rad score model (0.761), and the clinical plus DBT-Rad score model (0.766). Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted probabilities and actual outcomes. Furthermore, decision curve analysis confirmed the clinical net benefit of the proposed model.

CONCLUSIONS: The multimodal radiomics fusion model based on DCE-MRI kinetic and DBT texture features effectively predicts pCR following NAC in TNBC patients. Its predictive performance is superior to that of single-modality models. Consequently, this model offers a non-invasive imaging tool for individualized pretreatment efficacy assessment. Nevertheless, further multicenter external validation is required to confirm its generalizability. For now, it should be viewed as a decision‑support aid that informs rather than dictates treatment choices, with specific actionable thresholds to be refined in future prospective studies.

articles.title: The prognostic impact of cardioselectivity of beta-blockers prescribed during hospitalization for decompensated heart failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Beta-blockers (BBs) show considerable variation in cardioselectivity (i.e., the relative affinity to the β1 receptor), even among those with evidence of benefit in the treatment of chronic heart failure (HF). We aimed to evaluate whether the cardioselectivity of BBs prescribed during hospitalization for decompensated HF will affect the long-term prognosis of patients.

METHODS: In the prospective study, we followed 4053 patients hospitalized for decompensated HF. The entire cohort was divided into subgroups based on the cardioselectivity of recommended BBs (as stated in discharge summary).

RESULTS: After complex adjustment, patients treated with a highly selective BB (bisoprolol) showed significantly lower five-year cardiovascular mortality than those with a lesser degree of cardioselectivity (mainly metoprolol) [hazard ratio (HR) 0.69 (95% confidence interval (CI): 0.52-0.92), p = 0.011]. This difference remained in patients with HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) [HR 0.58 (95% CI: 0.37-0.89), p = 0.013], but was not yet significant in HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) [HR 0.66 (95% CI: 0.43-1.02), p = 0.063]. In HFrEF patients only, highly cardioselective BBs also showed a lower risk of cardiovascular mortality than nonselective BBs with vasodilatory properties (mainly carvedilol) [HR 0.55 (95% CI: 0.33-0.93), p = 0.025].

CONCLUSION: The choice of a BB regarding the degree of its cardioselectivity may have a prognostic impact in chronic HF patients.

articles.title: Biodegradation of Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) microplastics in a Microbial Fuel Cell.
articles.abstract: Plastics persist in the environment for centuries, releasing harmful micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) that threaten ecosystems and may be detrimental to human health. This study investigated the feasibility of a bioelectrochemical approach for the biodegradation and upcycling of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) microplastics. Over 40 days, three microbial fuel cell (MFC) systems were evaluated: (i) Shewanella oneidensis monoculture, (ii) Ideonella sakaiensis monoculture and (iii) their coculture. The S. oneidensis monoculture achieved 9.2% (w/w) PET biodegradation with acetic acid as a metabolite and a power density of 1.01 mW m⁻². The I. sakaiensis monoculture achieved 35.2% (w/w) PET biodegradation with acetic acid and ethanol as metabolites with a power density of 1.17 mW m⁻². The coculture exhibited moderate PET biodegradation (16.4% w/w) and produced acetic acid and ethanol, and a lower power density of 0.202 mW m⁻². These findings demonstrate that Ideonella sakaiensis can anaerobically ferment PET microplastics as the sole carbon source into metabolites including acetic acid and ethanol, while concurrently exhibiting bioelectrochemical activity. Notably, the electroactive bacterium S. oneidensis also exhibited PET-associated biodegradation, supported by PET mass loss and surface deterioration, alongside acetic acid formation and bioelectricity generation, highlighting its potential for the simultaneous biodegradation and bioelectrochemical upcycling of PET microplastics. However, cocultivation of I. sakaiensis and S. oneidensis reduced both PET biodegradation and power generation relative to the best-performing monoculture, suggesting that interspecies competition, antagonistic interactions or metabolic imbalance may limit synergistic activity. Overall, this study demonstrates the potential of MFCs for the simultaneous biodegradation and bioelectrochemical upcycling of PET microplastics, while highlighting the importance of microbial interactions in determining process efficiency.

articles.title: Health-centric information and moisture management for the adoption of postharvest practices to reduce mycotoxin risk: evidence from black pepper farmers in Sri Lanka.
articles.abstract: Mycotoxins are toxic secondary metabolites produced by fungi. They pose significant global food safety concerns because they can cause both acute and chronic health hazards. While information provision and technological interventions play a critical role in reducing mycotoxin risks, existing evidence on health-centric information remains mixed and limited to aflatoxins in cereals and grains, leaving spices underexplored. Moreover, technological interventions alone may be ineffective without adequate awareness and active management practices. This study investigates the effects of health-centric information and moisture management interventions, alongside general information on mycotoxin mitigation and government post-harvest quality improvement training, on the adoption of key post-harvest practices expected to reduce mycotoxin risks. A randomized controlled trial was conducted among 810 black pepper farmers in the Matale District, Sri Lanka. The results reveal that a bundled intervention emphasising health-centric information significantly enhanced the adoption of all key post-harvest quality improvement practices, reducing unsafe practices such as threshing barefoot and drying on bare floors, while improving recommended practices such as fresh grading, dry grading, blanching, and storage. In contrast, the bundled intervention emphasizing moisture management had limited impact, primarily on blanching and storage. These findings suggest that the bundled intervention, emphasizing health-centric information, motivates farmers to adopt critical postharvest quality-improvement practices expected to reduce mycotoxin risk, thereby potentially contributing to improving spice quality and enhancing consumer safety.

articles.title: A systematic review, bibliometric analysis, and meta-analysis of breed adaptation and sustainable systems for enhanced beef cattle performance in Mozambique.
articles.abstract: Beef cattle production in Mozambique faces productivity constraints due to heat stress, limited adoption of sustainable practices, and use of non-adapted breeds. This study integrated systematic review (n = 57 publications), bibliometric analysis, and mixed-effects meta-analysis (n = 15 studies, 578 animals) to quantify the effects of breed adaptation and production system sustainability on daily weight gain in Mozambican cattle. Adapted breeds (Landim, Nguni, Angoni) showed significantly higher weight gain (+ 0.278 kg/day, p < 0.05) compared to non-adapted breeds, while sustainable management practices (shading, rotational grazing, improved feeding) added + 0.194 kg/day. The final predictive model explained 98.3% of observed variability (R²=0.983) with low prediction error (RMSE = 0.124 kg/day). Adapted breeds under sustainable systems achieved the highest predicted weight gain (0.78 kg/day), approaching commercial viability (0.8 kg/day), whereas non-adapted breeds under traditional systems showed the lowest performance (0.31 kg/day). Geographic distribution revealed research concentration in southern/central regions (82.5% of studies) and underrepresentation of northern Mozambique. These findings demonstrate synergistic benefits of aligning genetic adaptation with sustainable management, supporting evidence-based policies for resilient beef production in Mozambique and similar tropical systems.

articles.title: Prevalence of Visual Impairment and Ocular Pathologies in Nursing Home Residents: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Ophthalmic & physiological optics : the journal of the British College of Ophthalmic Opticians (Optometrists)
articles.abstract:
