PURPOSE: Nursing homes play a crucial role in providing care to the ageing population; however, reports suggest nursing home residents experience difficulties accessing specific medical services, particularly eye care. This review aims to use the available data to find the pooled prevalence of visual impairment (VI) and blindness in the residents of nursing homes. This review also aims to propose future strategies to support the eye health of nursing home residents.

METHODS: The systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA). The online databases of PubMed/ Medline, Embase and Google Scholar were searched systematically for the keywords to identify articles reporting the prevalence of VI and blindness in nursing home residents in different geographical regions. Pooled prevalence of VI and blindness was then calculated using a random-effects model. The heterogeneity was quantified using I-squared statistics.

RESULTS: Eleven studies were selected for the review, of which nine involving 3436 subjects were selected for meta-analysis. The pooled prevalence of VI in the residents of nursing homes, calculated using a random-effects model, was 31% (95% CI: 26%-36%), while the pooled prevalence of blindness, calculated using a random-effects model, was 11% (95% CI 7%-16%). High heterogeneity was observed in the reported prevalence of VI (I2 = 89%) and blindness (I2 = 93.1%) across studies.

CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of VI and blindness among nursing home residents was higher than the global prevalence of VI and blindness in the general population. The high heterogeneity between studies demonstrates the need for more investigations with more consistent visual acuity thresholds. A comprehensive eye examination is recommended for all residents before entering the nursing home and an annual eye examination thereafter to address preventable blindness and vision-related quality of life in nursing home residents.

articles.title: Treating sepsis by targeting neutrophil extracellular traps: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis, a leading cause of death worldwide, is characterized by dysregulated host immune responses and multi-organ dysfunction. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) are extracellular fibers from activated neutrophils that contribute to the immune response. However, excessive NETs formation during sepsis may exacerbate inflammation, thrombosis, and tissue injury, potentially affecting sepsis prognosis. We examined whether NETs-modulating interventions are beneficial in experimental sepsis models.

METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, this review analyzed studies from PubMed and Scopus that reported NETs-targeting therapies and included outcome measures. A meta-analysis of random-effects models using a restricted maximum likelihood estimation was performed with a priori moderators including NETs quantification tier, intervention timing relative to insult, and intervention class.

RESULTS: In 33 included studies, the therapies significantly reduced NETs levels, while three studies increased NETs following treatment. The a priori moderators, NETs tier and treatment timing, were not significant, whereas intervention class significantly modified treatment effects. The treated groups had a lower risk of death and reduced IL-6, IL-1β, TNF-ɑ levels when compared to the control group. The treatments reduced tissue injury with considerable heterogeneity (I2=68.4%) and should be cautiously interpreted due to small study numbers. NETs modulation was significantly associated with a decrease in cytokine concentration and tissue injury. The heterogeneity of protocols, diverse outcome measures, publication bias, and overall poor reporting quality of the studies warranted conservative effect estimates and cautious interpretation of findings.

CONCLUSION: Our meta-analysis suggests NETs modulation is associated with reduced mortality risk, attenuated organ injury, and decreased inflammation, based primarily on LPS endotoxemia rodent models. Notably, experimental protocols and model limitations impede the translatability of these therapies for clinical care at this stage of research.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: In accordance with the guidelines, our systematic review protocol is registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) registration number CRD420251124339 and was published with INPLASY on 20 August 2025.

articles.title: Impact of Theileria annulata infection on oxidative/nitrosative stress and liver and bile duct function in cattle: insights from Kırıkkale, Turkey.
articles.abstract: Bovine tropical theileriosis (BTT), caused by the hemoprotozoan parasite Theileria annulata (T. annulata), poses a significant threat to cattle health and productivity, leading to substantial economic losses worldwide. This study investigates the impact of T. annulata infection on oxidative and nitrosative stress, and on liver and bile duct function, in naturally infected cattle in Kırıkkale, Turkey. A total of 40 cattle, including 15 molecularly negative and 25 molecularly positive animals, were evaluated in this study. The serum samples obtained from the cattle were analysed for metabolic parameters (CRE, UREA, TBIL, ALB, TP, CHO, TRI, GLU, IP, CA) and for liver and bile duct function indicators through enzyme activities (AST, ALT, GGT, and ALP). To evaluate oxidative stress, we quantified total oxidant status (TOS), total antioxidant status (TAS), oxidative stress index (OSI), malondialdehyde (MDA), nitric oxide (NO), and total sialic acid (TSA). Results indicated altered levels of biochemical parameters, elevated TOS, OSI, MDA, NO, and TSA, and altered enzyme levels in molecularly positive cattle, reflecting oxidative and nitrosative stress and compromised liver and bile duct function associated with the infection. These findings underscore the importance of continuous monitoring of BTT and highlight the role of oxidative stress in its pathogenesis, highlighting the need for future clinical trials to determine whether antioxidant supplementation could serve as an effective adjunctive supportive approach.

articles.title: Temporal trends and changing epidemiology of non-tuberculous mycobacteria over four decades: a retrospective laboratory-based study.
articles.journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The incidence of non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) isolations has increased worldwide, although the relative contribution of demographic changes, increasing patient complexity, environmental factors, and advances in diagnostic techniques remains unclear. We aimed to describe long-term trends in NTM isolations and epidemiological changes.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective study of NTM-positive clinical samples processed at a tertiary referral hospital in Barcelona between 1986 and 2021. Individual demographic and microbiological data were available until 2021, whereas only aggregate data on total samples processed and NTM-positive cultures were available for 2022-2023 and were used exclusively for temporal trend analyses. Trends were analysed using logistic regression, generalized additive models, and a one-breakpoint segmented logistic regression; evidence for a change in slope was formally assessed using the Davies test. Demographic characteristics, specimen type, and species distribution were compared between two periods (1998-2005 and 2014-2021).

RESULTS: A total of 5,848 NTM-positive samples were identified. Among samples with available demographic data, 3,918 (66.9%) corresponded to male patients. Respiratory specimens accounted for 4,147 (70.9%) samples, whereas 426 (7.3%) were non-respiratory. Temporal trends showed a non-linear pattern. The segmented model estimated a change-point at 2017.5 (95% CI 2016.9-2018.2), with a marked increase thereafter (annual percent change 21.7%, 95% CI 18.6-24.8); the Davies test provided strong evidence of a change in slope (p<0.001). Species distribution changed significantly over time, partly reflecting improvements in microbiological identification. The Mycobacterium avium complex remained the most frequently isolated group, whereas M. kansasii and M. xenopi declined substantially. Compared with 1998-2005, patients in 2014-2021 were older (mean age 60 vs. 56 years, p<0.001) and more frequently female (41.9% vs. 28.3%, p<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Two distinct periods of increased NTM isolation were observed over the study period, with the most recent acceleration occurring around 2017-2018. This increase occurred alongside important changes in species distribution and patient demographics. These findings highlight the evolving epidemiology of NTM and support the need for enhanced surveillance systems and improved differentiation between colonization and active disease.

articles.title: Defining the Role of DSMES Nurses in Advanced Diabetes Technologies: An Expert Consensus Study with External Professional Assessment.
articles.journal: Diabetes therapy : research, treatment and education of diabetes and related disorders
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Nurses play a central role in diabetes management and the education of people living with diabetes using advanced diabetes technologies. However, their role remains variably defined and inconsistently implemented across healthcare settings. In this study, we aim to establish expert consensus on the professional role and responsibilities, technology-related competencies and expertise, educational and leadership responsibilities, and training and organizational support of Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support (DSMES) nurses in the context of advanced diabetes technologies and to explore agreement with external professional groups.

METHODS: An expert consensus study was conducted with a panel of 21 expert DSMES nurses from across Spain, followed by an external professional assessment involving 306 healthcare professionals. A structured questionnaire including nine consensus statements was administered using a 5-point Likert scale. Consensus was predefined as ≥ 70% agreement. A facilitated discussion was subsequently conducted to interpret and contextualize the findings; no additional quantitative re-rating was performed. External professional assessment was conducted among nurses involved in diabetes care and endocrinologists. Descriptive statistics were used for analysis.

RESULTS: Consensus among the expert panel was achieved for all nine statements. External professional assessment showed high levels of agreement across professional groups, with some variability regarding training requirements, leadership in DSMES, and institutional support. Nurses were recognized as key professionals in supporting the implementation, use, and self-management of advanced diabetes technologies through DSMES. Structural barriers included lack of standardized training pathways, insufficient institutional policies, and absence of formal accreditation frameworks.

CONCLUSIONS: There is strong consensus on the essential role of DSMES nurses in the context of advanced diabetes technologies. However, the lack of standardized training and formal recognition highlights the need for competency-based educational frameworks and institutional support to ensure consistent and equitable practice. There was no patient or public contribution.

articles.title: Structured Online Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support for Adults with Type 1 Diabetes and Suboptimal Glycemic Control: The OPTIM@TE Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: Diabetes therapy : research, treatment and education of diabetes and related disorders
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Evidence directly comparing equivalent structured online and face-to-face diabetes self-management education and support (DSMES) programs is limited. This pilot randomized controlled trial evaluated the feasibility and preliminary effectiveness of delivering the same structured group-based DSMES program online versus face-to-face in adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D) and suboptimal glycemic control.

METHODS: OPTIM@TE was an open-label, parallel-group, pilot randomized controlled trial in adults with T1D, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) ≥ 7.5%, and access to a personal digital device randomized (1:1) to an online or an equivalent face-to-face structured DSMES program. Both interventions shared the same curriculum and planned educational duration (≥ 10 h). The primary outcome was HbA1c at 12 months. Secondary outcomes included continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) metrics, anthropometric and metabolic variables, patient-reported and implementation outcomes.

RESULTS: Fifty-one participants were randomized (26 online, 25 face-to-face). At 12 months, no significant between-group difference was observed in HbA1c (adjusted difference -0.07%; 95% CI -0.71 to 0.57; p = 0.831). No significant differences were found in CGM metrics, metabolic variables, or patient-reported outcomes. The only significant secondary outcome was greater improvement in Mediterranean diet adherence in the online group (adjusted difference 2.48 points; 95% CI 0.71-4.24; p = 0.009). Program completion was 41.2% overall (60.0% face-to-face versus 23.1% online), although participants who completed the program reported high satisfaction.

CONCLUSIONS: Online group-based DSMES showed no significant differences in clinical and patient-reported outcomes to an equivalent face-to-face program in this pilot trial. Online delivery may represent a potential option for providing structured diabetes education; however, strategies to improve participant engagement and program completion are needed. Larger pragmatic, randomized trials are warranted to confirm these preliminary findings.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT05708820.

articles.title: Biomechanical Test Designs for Fixation of Traumatic Pubic Symphysis Diastasis: A Systematic Review of Key Methodological Choices in a Field Without Consensus.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Traumatic pubic symphysis diastasis (PSD) is associated with high fixation failure rates, yet biomechanical studies use highly variable test designs, limiting comparison and clinical translation. This systematic review summarizes biomechanical test designs for PSD fixation to guide standardization and improve interpretation of fixation performance.

METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed and Embase up to December 2025 identified experimental and finite element modeling (FEM) studies on PSD fixation. Methodological characteristics, including injury classification, fixation, ligament and muscle representation, loading conditions, mechanical or computational setup, specimen material and outcome measures, were extracted. Data were synthesized descriptively, and a custom quality appraisal framework assessed reporting completeness and methodological rigor.

RESULTS: Sixty-four studies were included (57 experimental, 6 FEM, one both), with substantial methodological variation. Most modeled APC II/III injuries, using plate, external, or semi-rigid fixation methods. Around half included posterior fixation. In experimental studies, synthetic pelves were common (41%), though ligaments were represented only in cadaveric and FEM studies. Loading typically simulated single- or double-leg stance using quasi-static sacral loading (~400 N). Displacement at the pubic symphysis was the most common outcome, measured in 2D or 3D, while FEM studies often assessed implant stress.

CONCLUSION: We propose a baseline experimental model and practical guidance for biomechanical evaluation of PSD fixation. Key challenges remain, including ligament representation and physiological loading, for which FEM may provide valuable opportunities. Although the available evidence is limited by methodological heterogeneity and incomplete reporting, this review provides a framework to improve interpretation, comparability, and future standardization of biomechanical studies.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO ID: CRD420251135311.

articles.title: Avocado Oil Nanoemulsion Ameliorates STZ-Induced Diabetic Brain Dysfunction through PI3K/AKT/mTOR-Related Gene Modulation and Attenuation of Apoptosis.
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus is associated with progressive neurological complications characterized by hyperglycemia-induced oxidative stress, neuronal apoptosis, and disruption of intracellular survival signaling pathways. This study investigated the neuroprotective effects of avocado cold-pressed oil (ACPO) and its nano-formulation against diabetes-induced cerebral alterations in streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic rats. Seventy adult male Wistar rats were randomly allocated to ten groups (n = 7/group): normal control (NC), blank nano-formulation vehicle control (BC), metformin control (RC), ACPO control (OC), ACPO nano-formulation control (FC), diabetic positive control (PC), diabetic blank nano-formulation vehicle control (BT), diabetic + metformin (RT; 500 mg/kg), diabetic + ACPO (OT; 500 mg/kg), and diabetic + ACPO nano-formulation (FT; 500 mg/kg). The untreated diabetic group served as the reference for diabetes-associated alterations, whereas the diabetic vehicle-control group was included to account for potential effects of the nano-formulation vehicle. Diabetes was induced by a single intraperitoneal injection of STZ (40 mg/kg). Plasma glucose levels, cerebral gene expression of phosphatidylinositol-3-kinase (PI3K), protein kinase B (AKT1), mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR), glycogen synthase kinase-3β (GSK3β), pannexin-1 (PANX1), and acetylcholinesterase (AChE) were evaluated. Histopathological examination and caspase-3 immunohistochemistry were performed to assess neuronal injury and apoptosis. Treatment with ACPO and its nano-formulation significantly reduced plasma glucose levels and modulated key molecular pathways involved in neuronal survival. Both treatments upregulated PI3K, AKT1, and mTOR expression while downregulating GSK3β, PANX1, and AChE compared with untreated diabetic rats. Histopathological examination demonstrated marked preservation of cerebral cortical architecture, accompanied by reduced caspase-3 immunoexpression, indicating attenuation of neuronal apoptosis. The nano-formulation exerted greater effects on the investigated molecular biomarkers than conventional ACPO and produced histopathological and immunohistochemical improvements comparable to those observed with metformin.

articles.title: The "eye in the sky": remote sensing technologies in heart failure-from physiologic monitoring to predictive care.
articles.abstract: Heart failure remains a leading cause of hospitalization, readmission, and health care utilization worldwide. Although advances in pharmacologic and device-based therapies have improved outcomes, clinical management continues to rely largely on episodic assessments that often identify decompensation only after symptoms emerge. This reactive paradigm limits opportunities for early intervention and contributes to persistently high hospitalization rates. Recent advances in wearable and remote sensing technologies have enabled continuous, ambulatory assessment of cardiovascular physiology. Implantable, subcutaneous, and wearable sensors now provide longitudinal data on hemodynamics, impedance, heart rhythm, respiratory patterns, physical activity, and functional status. Emerging evidence demonstrates that these technologies can detect physiologic deterioration days to weeks before overt clinical worsening, creating the potential to shift heart failure care from symptom-driven response to anticipatory management. This review synthesizes current evidence supporting remote sensing technologies in heart failure, emphasizing physiologic relevance, predictive capability, and clinical actionability.

articles.title: From Macroenvironmental Context to Individual Proximal Exposure: Multiscale Mechanisms Linking Environmental Factors to Blood Pressure Homeostasis and Variability : Author.
articles.abstract: Hypertension is a major contributor to the global burden of cardiovascular disease. In addition to genetics, age, and lifestyle, environmental exposures can disrupt blood pressure homeostasis. Compared with air pollution and ambient temperature, evidence concerning psychosocial factors, noise, light, chemical pollutants, micro- and nanoplastics, and the individual proximal residential environment is more fragmented, and studies often conflate mean blood pressure, incident hypertension, and blood pressure variability (BPV) as equivalent outcomes. Using a continuum from macroenvironmental context to individual proximal exposure, this review integrates evidence from human studies, animal experiments, and in vitro research to compare associations of air pollution, temperature, greenspace, noise, chemical pollutants, micro- and nanoplastics, light exposure, and psychosocial stress with distinct blood pressure phenotypes. We further summarize shared pathways involving autonomic and neurohumoral regulation, oxidative stress-inflammation-endothelial injury, the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS), circadian rhythms, and metabolic/microbiome mechanisms. Human evidence is relatively substantial for air pollution, temperature, noise, and greenspace, whereas direct evidence linking micro- and nanoplastics and some chemical pollutants to human hypertension and BPV remains limited, with mechanistic understanding derived mainly from experimental models. Multiple exposures, genetic and epigenetic backgrounds, and socioeconomic conditions may jointly modify environmental effects. Clarifying exposure dose, level of evidence, and the relevant BPV time scale will help identify environmentally susceptible populations and provide a conceptual basis for stratified prevention and future intervention studies.

articles.title: Millet Polyphenols Alleviate HFD-induced Brain Oxidative Stress by Modulating Gut Microbiota and Serum Metabolic Profiles.
articles.journal: Plant foods for human nutrition (Dordrecht, Netherlands)
articles.abstract: High-fat diet (HFD) consumption is associated with metabolic dysfunction, oxidative stress, and brain injury. Dietary polyphenols may influence the host's redox homeostasis and interact with gut microbiota to produce metabolites with potential bioactivity. Our results showed that HFD feeding induced dyslipidemia and brain oxidative stress in mice. Millet polyphenols supplementation, particularly in the high-dose group, improved lipid disorders associated with HFD and enhanced brain antioxidant defense capacity. Additionally, millet polyphenols alleviated the elevated expression of Alzheimer's disease (AD)-related molecular changes associated with HFD and reduced the immunoreactivity of Tau protein and Aβ. Furthermore, 16 S rRNA gene sequencing revealed that millet polyphenols supplementation was associated with alterations in gut microbial community composition and specific bacterial taxa related to HFD. Untargeted metabolomic analysis further demonstrated distinct serum metabolic profiles among groups, with millet polyphenols modulating multiple metabolites involved in nucleoside, choline, steroid hormone, and sphingolipid metabolism. Collectively, these findings suggest that millet polyphenols can attenuate HFD-associated brain oxidative stress, and this neuroprotective effect is accompanied by shifts in gut microbiota composition and serum metabolic profiles.

articles.title: Immune checkpoints inhibitors in the treatment of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) is a rare but catastrophic demyelinating disease of the central nervous system (CNS) caused the JC virus (JCV). However, no effective treatments have been identified. Immune check point inhibitors (ICIs) are considered a potential treatment option. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to pool the data from the literature that evaluates the efficacy of using ICI in the treatment of PML.

METHODS: The search was conducted on January 24, 2026 using PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), and Embase. Studies were included if they included patients with PML and evaluated the efficacy of using ICIs including PD-1, PD-L1, and CTLA-4 inhibitors in PML treatment. The exposure of interest was the use of ICI in the treatment of PML. The outcomes of interest were survival, disability and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) viral load. Rate and weighted mean difference (WMD) and their 95% confidence intervals (95%CI) were used as the effect size in the analysis.

RESULTS: We included a total of 186 patients with PML from 52 articles. The survival rate among the included patients was 62% (95%CI: 52%-72%). There was no significant difference in disability between before and after the treatment with ICI (WMD =- 0.03; 95%CI: - 2.11-2.04). On the other hand, the treatment was associated with lower viral levels in the CSF (WMD = 69.20; 95%CI: 1.69-136.70).

CONCLUSIONS: Future randomized clinical trials or comparative observational studies that investigate the efficacy of using ICI in the treatment of PML compared to other treatment modalities are needed.

articles.title: Potentially toxic element contamination in the tributaries of Swat River system, Pakistan: multi-media assessment of contamination patterns, ecological risks, and human health implications.
articles.abstract: Mountainous watersheds globally are increasingly affected by the combined influence of natural weathering, and anthropogenic activities, yet the distribution and potential risks of potentially toxic elements (PTEs) in tributary systems remain insufficiently characterized. In the Swat River basin, Pakistan, surface water, sediment and fish samples were collected from three tributaries (Mingora, Jambil, and Marghuzar) to assess the distribution of eight potentially toxic elements (Cd, Pb, Zn, Cu, Cr, Co, Ni, Fe). An integrated approach combining multivariate statistics, ecological indices, and scenario-based human health modeling was applied to examine PTE contamination patterns, assess ecological risk, and evaluate human health risk associated with exposure through drinking water and fish consumption pathways. Contamination indices revealed that Mingora and Marghuzar streams exhibited high-degree contamination (CD = 32.67 and 30.29, respectively), while Jambil Stream showed considerable-degree contamination (CD = 19.81). Mingora Stream, which traverses a densely populated urban center, may represent a potential source of PTEs to the downstream Swat River. Principal component analysis identified distinct elemental assemblages that may be associated with bedrock weathering (Cr, Ni, Co) and anthropogenic influences (Cd, Pb, Zn) including wastewater discharge, mining, and traffic. Ecological risk indices identified Cd as the principal contributor to the calculated ecological risk. Health risk assessment revealed that risks associated with individual exposure pathways were below the recommended safety threshold. Drinking water exposure was assessed for children and adults, while fish consumption risks were evaluated for the general population and fishermen. This study provides a snapshot assessment of PTE contamination in the tributaries of the Swat River in the Hindu Kush region during the investigated sampling period. The integrated assessment of contamination sources, ecological risks, and human health risks provides information to support future environmental monitoring and management of mountainous watersheds.

articles.title: Effects of digital stress-management interventions in breast cancer patients 18 months after intervention access.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Digital stress-management tools show promise, but their long-term impact remains unclear. In the Coping After Breast Cancer (CABC) trial, the app-based stress-management program StressProffen, with either cognitive behavioral therapy intervention (CBI) or a mindfulness-based intervention (MBI), showed no advantage over usual care after six months of access. However, benefits may emerge gradually, as users need time not only to become familiar with the content and techniques, but also to internalize, apply and automatize their use in response to real-life stressors. The a priori defined aims of the current study were to examine; 1) whether extended (18 months) access to the digital stress-management interventions CBI and MBI were associated with changes in perceived stress (stress) (primary outcome), measures of health-related quality of life, mindfulness, fatigue, coping, anxiety, depression, and sleep (secondary outcomes), 2) association between app use and changes in stress level and investigate baseline characteristics as moderators of change in stress in the intervention groups, and 3) identify predictors of change in stress among patients with breast cancer.

METHODS: Of 430 patients randomized to MBI, CBI, or usual care, 76% (n = 327) completed the 18-month survey. Linear mixed-effects models were used to assess between-group differences in primary and secondary outcomes. Moderator analyses were performed to examine whether specific baseline characteristics modified the intervention effects on stress levels. Predictor analysis of change in stress was performed for the total sample.

RESULTS: At 18 months, all three groups showed stable trends over time, with no significant difference between either intervention group and controls. A larger stress reduction was observed among younger participants (≤50 years) in both CBI and MBI compared to controls. Higher baseline stress levels predicted significantly larger stress reductions in the total sample, but the moderator analysis showed that the effects were only significant in the CBI group.

CONCLUSION: Neither CBI nor MBI showed statistically significant improvements at 18 months compared to controls. The results however suggest that long-term access to stress management interventions may help young women with breast cancer and those with high initial stress to reduce their stress levels.

articles.title: Oral and maxillofacial malignant tumors: a 50-year clinicopathologic study from a dental school in Thailand.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Oral and maxillofacial malignant tumors show variation in frequency and demographic characteristics across countries. Due to their diverse clinical presentations, clinical diagnosis remains challenging. This study aimed to investigate clinicopathologic data of these malignancies over 50-year period in a Thai dental school.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Archival biopsy records were reviewed for cases diagnosed with malignant tumors in the oral and maxillofacial region. Demographic and clinicopathologic data including sites, clinical presentations, clinical diagnoses made by clinicians, and histopathologic diagnoses were analyzed.

RESULTS: Of 22,292 biopsy specimens, 791 cases (3.5%) were diagnosed as malignant tumors in this location. Epithelial tumor was the most common (60.3%), followed by salivary gland (16.6%) and hematologic (7.3%) groups. Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) was the most common. Mean age of patients was 55.9 years, with male-to-female ratio of 1:1.02. Gingiva was the most common site (27.5%) and soft tissue mass was predominant clinical presentation (46.0%). Only 54.5% of cases were clinically diagnosed as malignancy while remaining cases were clinically diagnosed as benign tumor, reactive lesion, infection, cyst, or other lesions.

CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, oral and maxillofacial malignant tumors were uncommon with SCC being predominant. High proportion of gingival involvement and slight female predominance differed from general trends in the literature. Discrepancy between clinical and histopathologic diagnoses highlights diagnostic challenges.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Discordant diagnosis of oral and maxillofacial malignancies as benign conditions is of clinical significance. Integrating demographic data along with clinicopathologic features may assist clinicians in diagnosis, leading to prompt histopathologic confirmation and appropriate patient management.

articles.title: Proton pump inhibitors in prevention of cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity: a systematic review.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cisplatin is a cornerstone of chemotherapy, but its clinical utility is limited by dose-dependent nephrotoxicity. Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) have been hypothesized to prevent this toxicity by inhibiting the renal transporter OCT2, a key mediator of cisplatin uptake into tubular cells. However, independent evidence links PPIs to acute kidney injury (AKI). This systematic review aimed to synthesize the evidence on the efficacy and safety of PPI co-administration for preventing cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus were systematically searched for studies comparing cisplatin therapy with PPI co-administration versus cisplatin without PPIs. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies reporting renal outcomes were included. Study quality was assessed using the Cochrane RoB2 tool for RCTs and the ROBINS-I tool for observational studies. Due to extreme clinical, methodological, and statistical heterogeneity, a structured narrative synthesis was performed instead of a quantitative meta-analysis. The study was registered at PROSPERO (CRD420251087906).

RESULTS: Eight studies (n = 1062 participants) were included (two RCTs and six non-randomized studies). Two retrospective cohorts reported a significant nephroprotective effect. One RCT showed a trend toward protection in its primary endpoint (0% nephrotoxicity in high-dose pantoprazole vs 25% in control, p = 0.078), with significant suppression of renal injury biomarkers. Conversely, one prospective cohort identified PPI use as an independent risk factor for AKI (OR 2.78; p = 0.010) and worse post-treatment eGFR outcomes. Four additional studies (one crossover RCT, three retrospective) found no statistically significant association between PPI use and renal outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Current evidence does not allow a clear conclusion regarding the safety or efficacy of PPIs in this setting. While theoretically beneficial, clinical data reveals conflicting results and a potential signal for increased AKI risk. PPIs may reduce gastrointestinal toxicity, but caution is warranted due to a potential signal for harm. Further high-quality RCTs are needed to provide a definitive answer.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence in pediatric allergic diseases: what the clinician needs to know.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reaching pediatric practice through consumer apps, wearables and decision-support tools, yet most children with allergic disease are managed by general pediatricians. This review summarizes what AI can and cannot do across pediatric allergic diseases, emphasising clinical readiness and the questions clinicians should ask before acting on an algorithmic output. Narrative review. MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus and Google Scholar were searched for English-language publications (January 2015-June 2026) on machine learning, deep learning, digital biomarkers and large language models in pediatric asthma, wheeze, atopic dermatitis, food allergy and allergic rhinitis. Peer-reviewed studies were appraised for clinical applicability, validation status and implementation barriers. Machine learning trajectory analyses show that allergic disease follows multiple coexisting pathways rather than a single atopic march. Deep learning interprets atopic dermatitis images and respiratory sounds with accuracy approaching specialist assessment. Predictive models estimate oral food challenge outcomes and impending asthma exacerbations, and wearable-derived biomarkers may signal deterioration early. Readiness nevertheless varies widely: most applications remain at research or pilot stage, constrained by small single-center datasets, scarce external validation, under-representation of darker skin tones, and limited interoperability with clinical workflows.

CONCLUSION: AI is closer to the bedside in pediatric allergy than in many other areas of pediatrics, but few tools are ready for autonomous clinical use. No trial has yet shown that acting on an AI-derived risk estimate improves clinical outcomes in children. Pediatricians will increasingly encounter AI-derived outputs brought by families or embedded in health systems; appraising validation, representativeness and accountability is becoming a core clinical skill.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Pediatric allergic diseases follow heterogeneous trajectories that conventional tools predict poorly. • AI models report high accuracy in image, audio, and risk-prediction tasks.

WHAT IS NEW: • Readiness, not reported accuracy, should govern clinical use: most tools remain research-stage. • Pediatricians need a practical framework to appraise AI outputs brought by families and health systems.

articles.title: Current state of smart shunt technology-a future dream or tangible perspective: a systematic review.
articles.journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
articles.abstract: Hydrocephalus, a condition characterized by disrupted cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics, has historically and mainly relied on ventriculoperitoneal shunt (VPS) systems for treatment. Despite considerable advances in the field, ranging from early valve-less systems to adjustable pressure valves and anti-hydrostatic devices, shunt failure rates remain high, and optimal, individualized CSF drainage remains challenging to achieve. Since hardly any objective feedback measures of shunt function are integrated in the shunt system in order to achieve physiologic like CSF drainage, it somehow remains to be a black box. In response to the aforementioned challenge, the concept of a "smart shunt" has emerged, with the objective of establishing a self-regulating system. The objective of this systematic literature review is twofold: firstly, to analyze existing research on smart shunts; secondly, to synthesize this research in order to highlight any advancements. In order to achieve these objectives, a systematic literature review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines, yielding a total of 135 potentially relevant articles. Following the elimination of duplicates and a more thorough evaluation, 22 articles were deemed pertinent for additional scrutiny. Furthermore, a patent search was conducted, which identified ten relevant results. While technological advances render the realization of a smart shunt increasingly feasible, financial challenges remain and further interdisciplinary research and clinical validation are essential to translate this concept into a reliable, personalized treatment option for patients with hydrocephalus.

articles.title: From theory to therapy: the development of therapy scripts in medical students.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Therapeutic reasoning is a complex process prone to errors, particularly among junior doctors under time pressure. While experienced clinicians often rely on Type 1 (intuitive) thinking via therapy scripts, little is known about how these scripts develop during medical training. Insight into how therapy scripts develop and evolve could inform Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics (CPT) education and improve the safety of early-career prescribing.

METHODS: We carried out a qualitative think-aloud study with 15 medical students from years 2, 4, and 6. Students completed a diabetes case while verbalizing their reasoning, and then created a concept map and reflective questions. Transcripts were analysed using abductive thematic analysis, guided by Cook's therapy script framework and knowledge encapsulation theory. Concept maps were evaluated for structural complexity and richness of reasoning. Results were compared across the three groups of students, to investigate differences in therapy script development.

RESULTS: Therapy script development progressed from fragmented, mechanism-focused reasoning in second-year students to integrated, patient-centred reasoning in sixth-year students. Fourth-year students combined both forms of reasoning. Concept maps revealed that structural complexity and higher-level explanatory connections increased with training.

CONCLUSION: Therapy scripts develop gradually, with increasing integration and contextual sensitivity, during undergraduate medical training. Concept mapping supports reflection and reveals gaps in knowledge, complementing traditional teaching methods. Educational strategies that promote early, structured, and reflective reasoning may accelerate therapy script formation, improve metacognitive awareness, and reduce the gap between undergraduate training and safe, effective prescribing in clinical practice.

articles.title: Systemic corticosteroids in critical illness: an evidence-based framework for clinical decision-making.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Systemic corticosteroids are pivotal in managing inflammation-driven critical illnesses, yet bedside translation remains inconsistent. This systematic review establishes an evidence-based framework for clinical decision-making by horizontally synthesizing contemporary evidence across severe community-acquired pneumonia (sCAP), acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and septic shock.

METHODS: A systematic electronic search was conducted across PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library up to early 2026. Peer-reviewed randomized controlled trials (RCTs), systematic reviews, and meta-analyses published in English were eligible. Data regarding population characteristics, dosing regimens, initiation timing, duration, and safety profiles were independently extracted and qualitatively synthesized.

RESULTS: Landmark trials define context-dependent efficacy: early hydrocortisone continuous infusion significantly reduces 28-day mortality in sCAP (CAPE COD), while a 10-day dexamethasone regimen improves ventilator-free days and survival in moderate-to-severe ARDS (DEXA-ARDS). In septic shock, early hydrocortisone-fludrocortisone combination accelerates shock resolution and lowers 90-day mortality (APROCCHS). These outcomes align with distinct pharmacological profiles: hydrocortisone provides dual glucocorticoid/mineralocorticoid activity to restore vascular tone, whereas dexamethasone exerts potent transrepression of proinflammatory transcription factors. To mitigate steroid-induced harm, protocolized safety targets are essential, including maintaining blood glucose at 140-180 mg/dL and actively monitoring for secondary infections.

CONCLUSION: Corticosteroids do not exert a uniform class effect. Bedside success requires personalized, protocolized regimens optimized by scenario-specific timing, dosing, and proactive adverse-event monitoring.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of cenobamate in the treatment of drug-resistant epilepsy: a systematic review and meta-analysis in adult, pediatric, and combined populations.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cenobamate (CNB), a next-generation anti-seizure medication approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in 2019, offers a new treatment option for adult with focal-onset seizures. However, clinical experience with CNB in children remains limited, as do comparative analyses of its efficacy between children and adults. Therefore, we conducted a meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy and safety of CNB for treating drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) across both age groups.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for studies published from inception to May 2026. Data were analyzed using RStudio with the meta, metafor, and dplyr packages. A random-effects model was used for all pooled estimates because substantial heterogeneity was anticipated and observed. Risk of bias in randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool, while the ROBINS-I (Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions) tool was used for retrospective, non-randomized studies.

RESULTS: After duplicate removal, 304 records were identified. Based on prespecified inclusion and exclusion criteria, 36 studies (36 reports: 35 full-text articles and 1 conference abstract) were included in the final analysis. Of these, 22 studies comprised 6,256 adults with epilepsy, 6 studies included 256 pediatric patients, and 8 mixed-age studies involving 451 patients did not provide separable age-specific data; these studies were therefore included only in the overall (all-age) analysis and were not included in the adult or pediatric subgroup analyses. In adults, the pooled responder proportion (≥ 50% seizure reduction) was 0.65 (21 studies, 3,871 patients; 95% CI: 0.58-0.71), the seizure freedom rate was 0.15 (21 studies, 3,963 patients; 95% CI: 0.10-0.21), the incidence of adverse events (AEs) was 0.63 (17 studies, 3,611 patients; 95% CI: 0.51-0.74), and the incidence of serious adverse events (SAEs) was 0.00 (19 studies, 3,487 patients; 95% CI: 0.00-0.02). In pediatric patients, the preliminary response rate was 0.60 (6 studies, 256 patients; 95% CI: 0.39-0.78), the preliminary seizure freedom rate was 0.20 (4 studies, 212 patients; 95% CI: 0.15-0.26), the preliminary incidence of AEs was 0.48 (5 studies, 236 patients; 95% CI: 0.42-0.55), and the preliminary incidence of SAEs was 0.03 (4 studies, 63 patients; 95% CI: 0.01-0.12). These estimates were numerically similar to those observed in adults. In the overall analysis (all patients combined), the response rate was 0.63 (35 studies, 4,578 patients; 95% CI: 0.58-0.68), the seizure freedom rate was 0.15 (32 studies, 4,392 patients; 95% CI: 0.11-0.19), the incidence of AEs was 0.62 (29 studies, 4,253 patients; 95% CI: 0.53-0.69), and the incidence of SAEs was 0.00 (30 studies, 3,767 patients; 95% CI: 0.00-0.02).

CONCLUSION: In summary, this is the first comprehensive meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy and safety of CNB across pediatric, adult, and combined populations. Although pediatric point estimates were numerically similar to adult estimates, these findings are derived from indirect subgroup comparisons and should be interpreted cautiously. Most included studies were retrospective observational studies with notably small pediatric samples, inherently limiting the strength of evidence in children. Therefore, further prospective studies are warranted to better investigate the efficacy and safety of CNB specifically in pediatric patients.

articles.title: Phospholipid Binding and Chemical Unfolding of DSP-3, a Major FnII Protein of Donkey Seminal Plasma, Investigated by Fluorescence Approaches.
articles.abstract: Donkey seminal plasma protein-3 (DSP-3) is a major fibronectin type-II (FnII) protein of the donkey seminal plasma. It binds specifically to the choline-phospholipids of sperm plasma membrane, which is implicated in sperm capacitation. In this work, we studied the microenvironment and accessibility of tryptophan (Trp) residues in DSP-3, in its native state and upon binding to soluble ligands and phospholipid membranes, employing steady-state and time-resolved fluorescence methods. Quenching studies revealed that the neutral molecule acrylamide quenches the Trp fluorescence with high efficiency, followed by the charged quenchers, cesium cation and iodide ion. Ligand binding afforded considerable protection to Trp residues from quenching, with dimyristoyl-phosphatidylcholine (DMPC) providing the highest shielding, followed by lyso-phosphatidylcholine (Lyso-PC). This shielding has been attributed to segment(s) of the protein penetrating the hydrophobic interior of the lipid membrane/micelles. Studies of chaotrope-induced unfolding of DSP-3 revealed that restrictions imposed by disulfide bonds in the FnII domains of the protein prevent complete unfolding, since pre-treatment with 10 mM dithiothreitol makes the protein unfold completely with high cooperativity. Gaudinium thiocyanate was found to be the most efficient chemical denaturant to unfold DSP-3, whereas it exhibited maximum resistance to denaturation by urea. Red-edge excitation shifts for DSP-3 upon binding to DMPC vesicles and Lyso-PC micelles were significantly higher than those observed with DSP-1, a homologous FnII protein from donkey seminal plasma.

articles.title: Development and validation of the risk of prolonged psychiatric admission score (R-PPAS) among adults in England: a population-based cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Reducing longer hospital​ stays of acute mental health admissions is an urgent priority across psychiatric hospitals. However, there are limited risk prediction tools to identify prolonged admissions to support timelier treatment and discharge planning. We developed and validated a pragmatic risk prediction tool-the Risk of Prolonged Psychiatric Admission Score (R-PPAS)-to identify adult psychiatric admissions likely to exceed 59 days.

METHODS: We derived a population-based cohort using electronic health records of 4208 adult acute psychiatric admissions (aged 18-65) across six wards in two English counties (January 2016 -March 2021). We developed a prediction model from 31 candidate predictors in a derivation cohort (four wards), and converted estimates into a simplified 0-7 scoring tool. We validated the final risk-scoring tool in a validation cohort involving two different wards in a different county.

RESULTS: Overall, 977 (23.2%) of 4208 admissions were prolonged stays (derivation cohort: 579/2295 [25.2%]; validation cohort: 398/1913 [20.8%]). The final risk prediction tool (R-PPAS; score range 0-7) incorporated 14 predictors, including specific diagnoses (e.g., paranoid schizophrenia, severe depression), homelessness, risk of self-neglect or non-compliance with care, aggression and delayed allocation of a community-based care coordinator upon admission. The tool showed acceptable discrimination in the validation cohort (area under the curve=0.72, 95% CI 0.69-0.74), with sensitivity ranging from 77.6% at the recommended cut-off of ≥3 to 1.5% at ≥7, and specificity 55.2% to 99.9%.

CONCLUSIONS: We developed the R-PPAS, a validated, user-friendly risk stratification tool to identify adult patients at risk of prolonged psychiatric hospital stays to support timely triage, resource allocation and discharge planning. Further external validation is needed to determine its generalisability across regions, countries and healthcare systems.

articles.title: Posttraumatic growth and resilience among survivors of cancer in young adulthood in Switzerland: a report from the Adolescent and Young Adult (AYA) Psychosocial Health Study.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Survivors of young adult cancer (YACS) face distinct psychosocial challenges. Posttraumatic growth (PTG) and resilience may aid adaptation, though their relationship and relevance in this age group remain insufficiently understood. We aimed to (1) describe PTG and resilience among Swiss YACS and (2) investigate the associations of PTG with resilience, sociodemographic, and cancer-related characteristics.

METHODS: We included survivors aged 21-39 years at diagnosis, diagnosed at least two years prior. We conducted a questionnaire survey using the Posttraumatic Growth Inventory (PTGI; range:0-105) and the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC 10; range:0-40). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and linear regression.

RESULTS: A total of 131 YACS (62% female; mean age at study = 37.6 years, SD = 5.1) were included. The PTG sum score was 54.6 (SD = 23.0, range:1-101), and YACS reported most PTG in Appreciation of life (mean = 3.3, 95% confidence interval: 3.2-3.6) and least in Spiritual change (1.1, 0.9-1.3). The mean resilience score was 28.06 (SD = 5.91, range:10-39), and YACS reported the highest score for the item "Achieving goals despite obstacles" (3.2, 2.6-3.0), and the lowest for the item "See humorous side of things" (2.1, 2.0-2.3). PTG was higher among females and those who received chemotherapy, while resilience showed no significant association with PTG.

CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that PTG and resilience are distinct but complementary adaptation processes in YACS. With higher PTG linked to female gender and chemotherapy, and resilience showing no direct association with PTG, personalized psychosocial support remains essential to help survivors navigate their unique cancer experiences and promote well-being.

articles.title: Life-Course Exposure to PM2.5 Constituents and Major Respiratory Diseases: Constituent-Specific Associations and Candidate Immune-Metabolic Signatures in a Large Prospective Cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), asthma, lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI), and lung cancer have been identified as major respiratory diseases. Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is an important respiratory risk factor, but evidence on life-course exposure to individual constituents and associated biological signatures remains limited.

METHODS: Among 47,737 participants from UK Biobank, birth-to-baseline residential histories were linked to annual concentrations of PM2.5, sulfate (SO42-), nitrate (NO3-), ammonium (NH4+), organic carbon (OC), and elemental carbon (EC) estimated by the Community Multiscale Air Quality model during 1930-2010. Cox regression was used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) per interquartile range (IQR) increase, and quantile g-computation to estimate mixture effects. Exposure- and disease-associated biomarkers were screened, followed by mediation analyses, protein functional enrichment, and metabolite categorization.

RESULTS: During 13-14 years of follow-up, each IQR increase in PM2.5 was associated with higher risks of COPD (HR: 1.138, 95% CI 1.069-1.211), asthma (HR: 1.171, 95% CI 1.105-1.241), LRTI (HR: 1.046, 95% CI 1.002-1.091), and lung cancer (HR: 1.193, 95% CI 1.064-1.337). SO42- and EC were positively associated with all four outcomes. Mixture analyses showed significant joint associations with COPD and asthma. Candidate proteins were enriched in immune-inflammatory, cell adhesion, PI3K-Akt, and cytokine/chemokine pathways, whereas candidate metabolites were predominantly lipoprotein-related.

CONCLUSIONS: Life-course exposures to PM2.5 and its constituents were associated with increased respiratory disease risks and candidate biological signatures. These findings highlight the relevance of PM2.5 chemical composition to major respiratory diseases and future mechanistic studies.

articles.title: Transapical mitral valve-in-ring implantation: Results of the real-world European Tendyne valve-in-ring registry.
articles.journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Mitral regurgitation (MR) is commonly treated with ring-based annuloplasty. In case of recurrent MR, re-do operations are often denied due to high risk. Transcatheter valve-in-ring (V-i-R) procedures offer an alternative. This study assessed the feasibility and outcomes of using the transapical, repositionable Tendyne valve for off-label mitral V-i-R procedures, as an alternative to balloon-expandable valves like SAPIEN, which face limitations such as paravalvular leakage and LVOT obstruction.

METHODS: The TEND-RING registry is a retrospective, international study with prospective follow-up, including 16 high-risk patients from eight European centers who underwent Tendyne V-i-R procedures between 2017 and 2024. Procedural, 30-day, and long-term outcomes were analyzed.

RESULTS: Patients were elderly (median age 79.5), predominantly male (81%), with significant comorbidities (STS Risk of Mortality 5.6%, 4.4-7.2%) and severe MR (3 + /4 +). Procedural success was 100%, with no LVOT obstruction or device embolization. MR was reduced to mild or none in all patients. 30-day mortality was 6.3%. Over a median 11-month follow-up, five deaths occurred (31.3%), three from cardiovascular causes (18.75%). Surviving patients showed sustained MR reduction and improved symptoms (89% in NYHA I/II). Ring size analysis suggested a minimum of 36 mm for rigid/semi-rigid rings, while flexible bands allowed successful implantation in sizes as small as 30 mm.

CONCLUSIONS: Tendyne V-i-R procedures are technically feasible, effective, and safe in selected high-risk patients with recurrent MR. Ring size thresholds identified may guide patient selection and procedural planning in future interventions.

articles.title: [Implantation of a total wrist endoprosthesis type ReMotion].
articles.abstract:
SURGICAL GOAL: Pain relief, preservation or restoration of a certain degree of wrist range of motion (ROM).

INDICATIONS: Painful and/or restricted wrist movement with confirmed panarthrosis (idiopathic, post-traumatic, rheumatic). Furthermore, as a result of advanced stages of lunate necrosis, bone tumors or post-infectious destruction during the infection-free interval. Typically, when only complete arthrodesis of the wrist would be an option.

CONTRAINDICATIONS: In cases of partial arthrosis if other salvage surgeries are still an option. In cases of poor bone quality, e.g., osteoporosis or extensive lysis margins in the radius or carpus. Advanced destruction associated with rheumatoid arthritis (type III according to Simmen). Muscular imbalance or poor soft tissue or circulation conditions. Lack of or poor compliance. Not generally recommended for very young patients.

SURGICAL TECHNIQUE: Make an incision via a dorsal approach approximately 2-3 finger widths proximal to the wrist, extending approximately to the third carpometacarpal (CMC) joint along the course of the third metacarpal. Carefully dissect the extensor retinaculum and the wrist joint capsule (distally pedicled) to enable a reconstruction with minimal tension later on. Exposure of the wrist and carpal bones. Resection of the carpus at the level of the proximal pole of the capitate bone. Remove the cartilage from the intercarpal joint spaces, which are later filled with cancellous bone. Determination of the implant size. Milling of the radial articular surface to accommodate the radial component. Axially aligned insertion of trial implants into the radius and carpus using a polyethylene insert. Check for tension and mobility. Insertion of the definitive endoprosthesis into the radius and carpus. The radial and ulnar screws should not extend beyond the CMC joints (author's recommendation). Repositioning of the wrist. Layered wound closure.

FOLLOW-UP CARE: A palmar splint is worn for approximately 4 weeks, leaving the metacarpophalangeal joints exposed. Then mobilization without weight-bearing for 2-4 weeks (depending on the surgical findings). Then gradually increase the load to approximately 10-15 kg. Radiographic follow-up control at 4 and 12 weeks. Annual clinical and radiographic follow-up controls are recommended.

RESULTS: Until 2023, we primarily implanted the Freedom wrist endoprosthesis (successor to the Universal 2 starting in 2015, manufacturer Integra), which is comparable in design to the ReMotion (Stryker). The early results are comparable to those of the Freedom endoprosthesis. On average, a ROM of approximately 65° is achieved for extension/flexion. Radial/ulnar mobility is limited on average to 5‑0-15°. The three patients who underwent revision surgery ex domo during the same period following implantation also showed an increase in ROM to the values mentioned above. In these three patients, the prosthesis could be preserved. Otherwise, no revisions were performed in the primary surgeries.

articles.title: Association between ossification of the nuchal ligament and cervical imaging changes.
articles.journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the association between ossification of the nuchal ligament (ONL) and cervical imaging changes in patients with cervical spondylosis.

METHODS: The study population consisted of 203 patients with cervical spondylosis from January 2023 to October 2025. All patients underwent cervical X-ray, CT, and MRI. Demographic, clinical, and imaging data were collected and analyzed. On cervical MRI, the total scores for cervical disc degeneration (TSCDD) and vertebral bone quality (VBQ) scores were used to evaluate the overall severity of degeneration of the cervical spine. Logistic regression analysis was used to identify factors associated with ossification of the nuchal ligament (ONL).

RESULTS: The study population included 108 patients with ONL and 95 patients without it. Patients in the ONL group were older than those without ONL (P < 0.001), they had a longer symptom duration (P = 0.006), a higher proportion of cervical spondylotic myelopathy (P = 0.039), and were more likely to have concomitant HBP (P < 0.001) and OPLL (P < 0.001). The cervical intervertebral disc height loss scores in the ONL group were higher than those in the non-ONL group (P = 0.001). In addition, the total scores for cervical disc degeneration (TSCDD) for intervertebral disc degeneration and the VBQ scores were also higher in the ONL group (P < 0.001). Spearman correlation analysis indicated that age, types of cervical spondylosis, duration, hypertension, OPLL, cervical intervertebral disc height loss scores, TSCDD and the VBQ scores were positively associated with the presence of ONL (P < 0.05), but the correlations were from weak to mild. Logistic regression analysis indicated that TSCDD (OR = 1.179, 95% CI = 1.064-1.306), VBQ scores (OR = 2.152, 95% CI = 1.286-3.599), HBP (OR = 2.041, 95% CI = 1.075-3.877), and OPLL (OR = 3.151, 95% CI = 1.539-6.452) were independently associated with the presence of ONL (all P < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: The presence of ONL in patients with cervical spondylosis is associated with several parameters, including HBP, OPLL, TSCDD, and VBQ scores. The overall severity of cervical disc degeneration and VBQ scores in the ONL group were higher than those in the non-ONL group.

articles.title: [A rare cause of ketoacidosis: Rapunzel syndrome].
articles.abstract: A 16-year-old female patient presented to the emergency department with impaired consciousness and recurrent vomiting. Laboratory investigations revealed ketoacidosis with electrolyte imbalance in the setting of known type I diabetes mellitus managed with insulin pump therapy. Clinical examination revealed a firm palpable mass in the upper abdomen. Ultrasound demonstrated impaired gastrointestinal transit in the upper abdomen associated with a mass of unclear origin in the gastric region. Computed tomography (CT) raised suspicion of a bezoar. Subsequent upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed a massive trichobezoar in the stomach extending into the duodenal bulb. Despite several attempts at endoscopic removal, including the use of various snares and grasping forceps, the trichobezoar could not be retrieved. Surgical removal by laparotomy and gastrotomy was therefore necessary. Rapunzel syndrome is a rare presentation of a trichobezoar. Most patients present with abdominal pain, nausea, and signs of ileus. The tail of the bezoar may extend into the jejunum, ileum, or even the colon. The case of a patient who was admitted with what initially appeared to be a complication of her pre-existing medical conditions is reported. However, the actual cause of her clinical deterioration was a trichobezoar extending into the duodenal bulb, which could only be treated surgically.

articles.title: Visceral leishmaniasis involving the kidney by direct infection and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis.
articles.journal: Virchows Archiv : an international journal of pathology
articles.abstract: Leishmania are protozoan parasites that can infect the renal parenchyma and cause glomerular disease, in particular membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis, by immune-mediated mechanisms. Here, we present the case of a 50-year-old patient with a history of HIV infection, recurrent visceral leishmaniasis, past hepatitis C and previous illicit drug abuse. The patient presented with acute on chronic kidney injury and progressive proteinuria. Renal biopsy revealed interstitial nephritis and infection-related glomerulonephritis (IRGN) without membranoproliferative pattern. Leishmania parasites were detectable in interstitial macrophages, tubular epithelial cells and glomerular macrophages and confirmed by rabbit-anti-Leishmania- or rabbit-anti-CD1a-antibodies. Infected macrophages showed an M2-like phenotype. While interstitial nephritis and glomerular disease have been described in a few cases of visceral leishmaniasis, before, our case is remarkable for the presence of leishmanial amastigotes in glomerular macrophages and IRGN at the same time, adding to the spectrum of renal manifestations associated with leishmanial infection.

articles.title: Ozone exposure promotes mitochondrial oxidative stress and inflammatory responses in steroid-resistant asthma by regulating Ca2+ influx through METTL14/m6A/UCP2.
articles.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Steroid-resistant asthma (SRA) is a severe refractory condition characterized by resistance to corticosteroids. This study investigated the molecular mechanisms by which ozone (O3) exposure facilitates mitochondrial oxidative stress (mtOS) and inflammatory responses in SRA.

METHODS: Mouse or human bronchial epithelial cells (BEAS-2B) were treated with HDM while exposed to O3 and treated with dexamethasone to simulate SRA in vitro and in vivo, respectively. Lung function testing was performed to assess airway hyperreactivity. Histological staining was conducted to examine lung tissue damage, inflammatory cell infiltration, and airway goblet cell hyperplasia. ELISA and immunohistochemistry were performed to detect inflammatory responses. GRα nuclear transport, GRβ protein expression, mtOS, and Ca2+ levels were measured. The expressions of METTL14 and UCP2 and their regulatory relationship were examined. The effects of the METTL14/m6A/UCP2 axis in SRA mice were validated through METTL14 knockout and UCP2 overexpression rescue experiments.

RESULTS: O3 exposure reversed the improvement effect of dexamethasone on airway hyperreactivity, inflammation, and mtOS in asthmatic mice. O3 inhibited UCP2-mediated Ca2⁺ influx, which exacerbates mtOS and inflammatory responses in BEAS-2B cells under SRA conditions. Lower serum METTL14 and UCP2 were associated with poorer lung function in SRA patients. Overexpression of UCP2 or METTL14 partially reversed the promoting effect of O3 on mtOS and inflammation in BEAS-2B cells under SRA conditions. METTL14 upregulated UCP2 expression in an m6A-YTHDF1-dependent manner. Knockout of METTL14 exacerbated mtOS and inflammation in SRA mice.

CONCLUSION: O3 exposure promotes Ca2+ influx by blocking the METTL14/m6A/UCP2 axis, promoting mtOS and inflammatory responses in SRA.

articles.title: From a Team of Experts to an Expert Team in Congenital Cardiology: Making Distributed Expertise Usable.
articles.abstract: Congenital heart disease care depends on specialised expertise distributed across clinicians, disciplines, patients and families. But bringing knowledgeable individuals together does not guarantee that their distinct contributions shape a decision. In complex congenital heart disease, multidisciplinary deliberation must reconcile anatomy, physiology, procedural feasibility, longitudinal risk and patient priorities, often amid uncertainty. We distinguish a team's possession of expertise from its collective capability to make that expertise usable. This distinction affirms, rather than questions, individual clinical judgement, professional responsibility and shared accountability for patients. We propose a testable conceptual framework in which relevant expertise becomes accessible, is expressed and understood, receives appropriate weight, and can revise the team's understanding or decision. Congenital cardiology examples include choices between catheter-based and surgical intervention, anticipation of intensive-care needs, and consideration of treatment burden and family goals. Constructive disagreement may reveal overlooked information or competing interpretations, while patients and families contribute essential knowledge about daily life and acceptable trade-offs. Existing team-science research supports the framework's rationale, but its ability to improve congenital heart outcomes has not been demonstrated. We outline a developmental cycle-map, observe, practise, review, adapt and re-map-through which programmes might examine how expertise enters decisions, identify missed contributions and learn across changing membership. Evaluation should combine prospective measures of decision quality and implementation with appropriately risk-adjusted clinical outcomes, patient and family experience, and longer-term trajectories. The objective is not consensus for its own sake, but better use of knowledge already available to care teams.

articles.title: Association Between Prenatal Risk Stratification and Access to Care for Neonatal d-Transposition of the Great Arteries.
articles.abstract: To evaluate how prenatal risk stratification impacts transfer times to the cardiac unit for newborns with d-transposition of the great arteries (d-TGA) in a high-volume, free-standing children's center. This is a retrospective study examining all prenatally diagnosed d-TGA newborns at a single center without in-house delivery capacity from 1/1/2013 to 3/1/2026. We evaluated two time periods based on implementation of level of care (LOC) assignments at our center (2013-2018 versus 2018-2026). The primary outcome was time from birth to arrival in the cardiac intensive care unit (CICU). Univariable and multivariable models were performed to include fetal echocardiographic and clinical covariates. Of 106 d-TGA newborns, 52 (49%) had a BAS within 24 h of arrival to the CICU, of which 24 (23%) required an emergent BAS within 2 h of CICU arrival. The multivariable model demonstrates that LOC implementation led to shorter median times from birth to CICU after adjusting for fetal echocardiographic markers and clinical covariates such as birthweight, gestational age and PaO2 on initial arterial blood gas (-180.7 min, 95% CI -351.9 to -9.5, p = 0.039). Risk stratification by LOC assignment is critical in access to life-saving care and shortening transport times for prenatally diagnosed d-TGA newborns, especially for free-standing children's hospitals.

articles.title: Rethinking the sustainability assessment of grass-fed beef: a holistic systematic review.
articles.abstract: Consumer demand for grass-fed beef (GFB) is increasing due to its perceived advantages in food safety, healthfulness, animal welfare, and environmental stewardship, yet its sustainability remains contested. This PRISMA-guided systematic review synthesised evidence from 141 studies identified through Web of Science, Scopus, AGRICOLA, and supplementary grey-literature sources to evaluate GFB production, meat quality, and sustainability, and to provide actionable insights for future research, market governance, and policy. The currently inconsistent evidence is insufficient to confirm the sustainability of GFB. Although GFB can offer desirable quality attributes, including leaner carcasses, greater proportions of omega-3 and conjugated linoleic fatty acids, and elevated antioxidant levels, its darker colour and variable tenderness may affect consumer acceptance. Environmentally, reduced grain inputs and greater pasture biodiversity may promote ecological stewardship, but methane emissions and higher land requirements may offset these gains unless adaptive grazing and carbon sequestration are appropriately incorporated. Socially, animal welfare can be enhanced through regenerative grazing practices but can also be compromised when animals are exposed to adverse weather and parasites. Economic performance depends on productivity, certification costs, price premiums, and market access. Despite their growing social relevance, animal welfare, traceability, authenticity, and certification remain insufficiently integrated into sustainability assessments. Overall, the current evidence is fragmented and dominated by farmgate economic and greenhouse gas metrics. Multidimensional, value-chain-based, and context-sensitive sustainability assessment frameworks are proposed to guide credible standards, targeted incentives, and market development.

articles.title: Asthma in Older Adults: A Systematic Review of Real-World Burden and Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review examines asthma in older adults over the past decade, focusing on epidemiology, diagnostic challenges, and current management. It also explores why asthma remains underdiagnosed and undertreated in this population.

RECENT FINDINGS: Asthma prevalence is increasing among older adults worldwide, particularly in developed regions and Asia, yet underdiagnosis and undertreatment remain common. Diagnostic complexity is driven by atypical presentations, comorbidities, overlapping COPD features, and limitations of standard diagnostic criteria. Patient-related barriers include low health literacy, poor inhaler technique, symptom misattribution, psychological comorbidity, and limited social support. Access to biologic therapies remains uneven, and precision medicine approaches for older adults are lacking. Asthma in older adults is an important and underrecognized public health issue. Better awareness, age-adapted diagnostic protocols, improved inhaler education, and more integrated management of comorbidities are needed to improve outcomes and quality of life.

articles.title: Severe hypoxemia caused by right-to-left shunt through a patent foramen ovale associated with right coronary artery malperfusion secondary to acute aortic dissection: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right coronary artery malperfusion associated with acute type A aortic dissection can cause right ventricular failure. However, hypoxemia due to a right-to-left shunt through a patent foramen ovale secondary to elevated right-sided cardiac pressure has rarely been described in this setting.

CASE PRESENTATION: An 80-year-old woman with acute type A aortic dissection presented with hypoxemia unexplained by pulmonary disease. Transesophageal echocardiography suggested that right ventricular dysfunction associated with right coronary artery malperfusion had contributed to right-to-left shunting through a patent foramen ovale. Following ascending aortic replacement, she developed hypoxemia after separation from cardiopulmonary bypass. Transesophageal echocardiography showed persistent right ventricular dysfunction and worsening of the shunt. Intraoperative optimization of cardiovascular medications improved hemodynamics, reduced the shunt, and improved oxygenation.

CONCLUSIONS: This case suggests that intracardiac right-to-left shunting should be considered in patients with acute aortic dissection and unexplained hypoxemia, and that transesophageal echocardiography may guide perioperative management.

articles.title: Possible Structural and Biochemical Impact of Blast-Induced Traumatic Brain Injury on the Hypothalamus and Its Homeostatic Implications.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traumatic brain injury (TBI), particularly blast-induced injury common in military contexts, is a leading cause of long-term neurological and endocrine morbidity. Unique biomechanical forces, including rapid pressure-wave changes and acceleration/deceleration, place critical midline structures like the hypothalamus and pituitary gland at high risk of damage.

OBJECTIVES: This paper, based on observations of our experiments, describes the possible pathophysiological mechanisms linking mild-to-moderate blast-TBI to the development of Central Diabetes Insipidus (CDI), characterized by impaired arginine vasopressin (AVP) regulation.Methods/Observations: In a series of studies using murine models, mice exposed to open-field blasts showed significantly higher water consumption than control (sham) groups. This phenomenon mirrors clinical presentations observed in injured soldiers, where the exact weight of various contributing mechanisms remains a subject of investigation.

PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Post-traumatic CDI results from the disruption of AVP production, storage, or release. Key mechanisms include Direct Mechanical Injury (shearing forces that damage hypothalamic neurons or the pituitary stalk); Vascular Compromise (microvascular damage, ischemia, or hemorrhage leading to cell death within the hypothalamic-neuro-hypophyseal system); or Secondary Injury (post-traumatic inflammation, oxidative stress, and edema, causing a delayed onset of pituitary dysfunction).

CONCLUSIONS: CDI is often under-recognized due to the non-specific presentation and critical condition of TBI patients. Because CDI can lead to hypotonic polyuria and severe dehydration, early diagnosis and proper management are essential to reduce morbidity. Further research is needed to determine the factors that dictate whether these water-balance disruptions remain transient or become permanent.

articles.title: Effect of high-power radiofrequency combined with a hypocaloric diet on abdominal subcutaneous and visceral fat: a preliminary randomized pilot study.
articles.abstract: Visceral and subcutaneous abdominal fat are associated with metabolic and cardiovascular risk. This preliminary randomized pilot study evaluated a high-power radiofrequency energy-based device (EBD) treatment, alone or combined with a hypocaloric dietary intervention, for visceral and subcutaneous abdominal fat reduction. Twenty middle-aged participants were randomly allocated to one of two parallel groups: EBD combined with dietary intervention (7 males, 3 females; mean age 58.2 ± 8.89 years) and EBD alone (5 males, 5 females; mean age 54.4 ± 12.5 years). Both groups received 12 EBD sessions over 6 weeks using a four-channel high-power radiofrequency device. Anthropometric, biochemical, and volumetric abdominal fat measurements were assessed at baseline and post-treatment, with visceral fat additionally evaluated at the 3-month follow-up. Both groups demonstrated reductions in abdominal fat volume. The EBD + diet group showed greater reductions in visceral fat (15.0%) and subcutaneous fat (18.6%) than the EBD-only group, which showed reductions of approximately 9.1% and 9.2%, respectively.
