Between-group change-score analyses favored the EBD + Diet group for weight and BMI, while differences in visceral and subcutaneous fat did not reach statistical significance. Most biochemical variables showed no clear between-group differences, although exploratory between-group differences were observed for triglycerides, insulin, and HOMA-IR. At the 3-month follow-up, mean visceral fat remained below baseline in both groups. Reductions in visceral and subcutaneous abdominal fat were observed in both treated groups. These findings should be interpreted cautiously due to the exploratory design and small sample size. Larger studies are required to confirm efficacy and long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Epidemiological and antimicrobial susceptibility patterns of Staphylococcus aureus isolated from the nasal cavity of healthcare personnel at a public hospital in Northeastern Brazil: a cross-sectional survey.
articles.journal: Brazilian journal of microbiology : [publication of the Brazilian Society for Microbiology]
articles.abstract: Nasal colonization by Staphylococcus aureus among healthcare professionals represents a potential risk for the spread of resistant strains in hospital settings. Thus, this cross-sectional study aimed to determine the prevalence of nasal colonization by S. aureus and to characterize the antimicrobial resistance profile of the isolated strains from professionals working in a public hospital in Caxias, Maranhão, Brazil. This study was carried out from December 2024 to February 2025. A total of 132 professionals working in a public hospital in the state of Maranhão were included. Among the participants, 36 (27.27%) were colonized by S. aureus, and 6 isolates (16.66%) were identified as methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA). High resistance rates were observed to penicillin G and ampicillin (94.4%), as well as to the macrolides erythromycin (83.3%) and azithromycin (77.8%). Resistance to tetracycline was detected in 11.1% of the isolates, with 22.2% showing intermediate susceptibility. All isolates were susceptible to clindamycin, chloramphenicol, and rifampicin. Regarding risk factors, working in two healthcare locations compared to one remained significantly associated with nasal colonization after adjustment (OR = 3.15-3.50; p < 0.05), whereas longer professional experience was identified as a protective factor (OR ranging from 0.11 to 0.17; p < 0.05). These findings demonstrate the circulation of multidrug-resistant S. aureus strains among healthcare professionals and highlight the importance of active surveillance, rational antimicrobial use, and strengthened infection control strategies to reduce the spread of resistant pathogens in hospital environments.

articles.title: Effects of Probiotics on Migraine in Children and Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Increasing evidence highlights a link between migraine, a disabling neurological disorder, and the gut microbiome. Probiotics, supplements containing colony-forming units of beneficial microbes, may influence migraine via the gut microbiome. A systematic review and meta-analysis of placebo-controlled trials was completed, and findings were synthesized narratively to evaluate probiotics for migraine prevention.

RECENT FINDINGS: Of 676 studies screened, 7 were included involving 612 participants (N = 487 females, 79.6%) consisting of 5 adult and 2 pediatric trials. Probiotics demonstrated a reduction in migraine severity on a 10-point scale (mean difference - 1.11; 95% CI - 2.26 to 0.03), monthly attack frequency (- 2.06; 95% CI - 3.6 to - 0.52), and disability (standardized mean difference - 0.86; 95% CI - 2.33 to 0.6). Certainty of evidence was graded very low. Probiotics may reduce migraine severity and frequency; however, the heterogeneity of studies limits generalizability. Despite the very low certainty of evidence, probiotics are safe and may reduce migraine as an adjunct preventative therapy.

articles.title: Middle meningeal artery embolization in chronic subdural hematoma: A real-world multicenter italian experience.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate technical feasibility, short-term radiological outcomes, subsequent surgical intervention, and complications of middle meningeal artery (MMA) embolization for chronic subdural hematoma (CSDH), distinguishing primary embolization from embolization after surgery.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 228 consecutive patients undergoing attempted MMA embolization at three Italian referral centers between January 2019 and November 2024. Technical success was the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes included radiological success, defined as residual hematoma thickness ≤ 6 mm on CT at 60-90 days, subsequent surgical evacuation, and procedure-related complications. Subgroup comparisons were exploratory and used available-case data.

RESULTS: Primary embolization was performed in 115 patients and embolization after surgery in 113. Technical success was achieved in 223/228 patients (97.8%). Follow-up CT was available in 188/228 patients (82.5%). Median residual hematoma thickness was 4 mm (interquartile range, 0-8), without a significant difference between groups (p = 0.372). Radiological success occurred in 132/188 patients (70.2%): 57/88 (64.8%) after primary embolization and 75/100 (75.0%) after surgery (p = 0.151). Complications occurred in 7/228 patients (3.1%), including one major ischemic stroke, without a significant between-group difference (p = 0.720). Subsequent surgical evacuation was required in 7/188 patients (3.7%): 5/88 (5.7%) versus 2/100 (2.0%), respectively (p = 0.255).

CONCLUSION: MMA embolization demonstrated high technical success, favorable short-term radiological outcomes, and a low rate of subsequent surgical intervention. These findings support its feasibility and potential clinical value in selected patients with CSDH, both as primary treatment and after surgical evacuation. Prospective comparative studies are needed to confirm these observations.

articles.title: The EAT-Lancet planetary health diet and gastric cancer risk: the stomach cancer pooling (StoP) project.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The EAT-Lancet Commission proposed the Planetary Health Diet (PHD) as a universal, planetary, and healthy dietary pattern. Its association with gastric cancer (GC) has not been previously investigated. The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between adherence to the PHD and GC risk.

METHODS: We applied four indexes assessing PHD adherence (PHDI-B, PHDI-C, EAT-LI, and WISH) to data from 10 case-control studies included in the international Stomach cancer Pooling (StoP) project, encompassing 3748 cases and 9056 controls. We first calculated adjusted study-specific odds ratios (ORs) using multivariable logistic regression models, with indexes modelled in continuous per 10% higher adherence and as quartiles. Pooled ORs were then derived using random-effects models.

RESULTS: All four indexes showed inverse associations with GC risk. The pooled ORs per 10% higher adherence ranged from 0.70 (95% confidence interval, CI 0.61-0.81) for PHDI-B to 0.79 (95% CI 0.72-0.86) for WISH. Comparing the highest versus the lowest adherence quartiles, ORs ranged from 0.34 (95% CI 0.26-0.45) for EAT-LI to 0.63 (95% CI 0.48-0.82) for PHDI-C. Associations were consistent for intestinal and diffuse histological types, cardia and non-cardia GC subsites, across strata of several covariates, and after Helicobacter pylori infection adjustment.

CONCLUSION: The PHD was inversely associated with GC risk across different adherence indexes and subgroups.

articles.title: [Case report: gardening, aquarium exposure, and sporotrichoid nodules].
articles.abstract: A 76-year-old patient developed painless, sporotrichoidly arranged nodules along the right forearm after minor trauma to his right hand, with no response to penicillin or clindamycin. Histology and initial microbiological investigations were nonspecific. Only repeated biopsies with culture at 30 °C revealed Mycobacterium marinum. After switching to clarithromycin monotherapy, the lesions regressed.

articles.title: Asundexian in Stroke: Nursing Pharmacology Update.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience nursing : journal of the American Association of Neuroscience Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients remain at increased risk of recurrent stroke despite guideline-directed antithrombotic therapy, and antithrombotic escalation strategies are limited by bleeding risk. Asundexian is an emerging therapy that targets factor XIa (FXIa) inhibition without impairing primary hemostasis, thereby reducing pathological thrombosis while mitigating bleeding. This paper aims to provide clinicians with an evidence-based overview of asundexian, an investigational FXIa inhibitor.

METHODS: Selected peer-reviewed articles, including available phase 1 to 3 trials, were reviewed and synthesized to present the latest asundexian evidence relevant to stroke prevention.

RESULTS: Asundexian 50 mg once daily, when added to antiplatelet therapy, reduced recurrent stroke in the atherosclerotic, non-cardioembolic stroke population, but was inferior to standard-dose apixaban in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). The hemostasis-sparing profile of asundexian was consistent across populations, supporting the add-on use with antiplatelet therapy. The pharmacologic data of asundexian demonstrate a low-complexity administration profile with near-complete oral bioavailability, <15% renal elimination, a 16- to 18-hour half-life supporting once-daily dosing, crushable tablets, no food or gastric pH effect, and no routine drug-level monitoring. Two safety boundaries include the absence of a specific reversal agent and the need to switch to a direct oral anticoagulant if AF is detected.

CONCLUSION: FXIa inhibitors like asundexian are an emerging antithrombotic class that holds the potential to change the paradigm of secondary stroke prevention in non-cardioembolic stroke patients. Optimizing FXIa inhibitor benefits depends on identifying the stroke mechanism, diagnosing AF, and maintaining bleeding surveillance or management without a reversal agent. This update provides an evidence-based overview of asundexian, an oral selective FXIa inhibitor. It summarizes its pharmacologic profile, key clinical evidence, and practice implications for nurses and advanced practice providers caring for stroke patients, as this agent may soon enter clinical practice. Asundexian is not currently available outside clinical trials and remains under regulatory review for clinical use in stroke prevention.

articles.title: White-matter microstructural alterations and cross-sectional thyroid hormone-cognition associations in hypothyroidism.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Hypothyroidism is associated with cognitive and emotional dysfunction, which may be accompanied by alterations in white-matter (WM) microstructure. However, few studies have compared diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) measures and clinical correlates across overt hypothyroidism (OH), subclinical hypothyroidism (SCH), and healthy controls (HCs). We investigated DTI-derived WM microstructural measures and their associations with thyroid function and neuropsychiatric performance in adult-onset hypothyroidism.

METHODS: We enrolled 44 patients with OH, 41 with SCH, and 53 HCs. Thyroid function, neuropsychiatric assessments, and DTI data were collected. Age, sex, and years of education were entered simultaneously as covariates in all inferential group-comparison models, exploratory two-sided partial Spearman correlations, and exploratory cross-sectional indirect-effect models, except when these covariates themselves were the descriptive variables compared.

RESULTS: Both OH and SCH groups had lower Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scores and higher depression scores than HCs. Compared with SCH and HCs, the OH group showed more extensive between-group differences in DTI-derived metrics; no SCH-HC differences survived family-wise error correction. Within the OH group, DTI measures showed nominal, covariate-adjusted exploratory associations with thyroid hormone concentrations and neuropsychiatric scores. Exploratory covariate-adjusted models identified indirect associations of total triiodothyronine (TT3) and total thyroxine (TT4) with MoCA through fractional anisotropy (FA) of the left posterior thalamic radiation (PTR). The corresponding total and direct associations were not statistically significant.

CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, OH was associated with more extensive differences in DTI-derived WM measures than SCH. The exploratory indirect associations through left PTR FA do not establish a temporal or causal pathway.

articles.title: Development of a quantitative method for comprehensive amino acid profiling to aid in diagnosing type 2 diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract: Dysregulated amino acid (AA) profiles are closely associated with diseases. Comprehensive and quantitative profiling of AA is therefore essential. This study developed a simple, direct, and high-throughput serum AA profiling method and evaluated its auxiliary diagnostic potential for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). A cold-induced phase separation strategy coupled with ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry was developed, enabling comprehensive serum amino acid profiling of 27 AAs and related metabolites across branched-chain, aromatic, and tryptophan metabolic pathways. The optimized sample preparation used acetonitrile (ACN) at a serum-to-solvent ratio of 1:3, 50 min of cold-induced phase separation, and reconstitution in ACN/H2O (v/v, 1:4). The method showed good linearity (R2 ≥ 0.9929), limits of detection of 0.005-5.00 ng/mL, limits of quantification of 0.01-10.00 ng/mL, recoveries of 82.6%-118.5%, precision with relative standard deviation (RSD) ≤ 11.6%, and matrix effects of 90.3%-106.6%, demonstrating reliable quantitative performance for serum amino acid profiling. The validated method was subsequently applied to serum samples from 50 T2DM patients and 100 healthy controls, identifying 17 significantly altered amino acids and related metabolites (P < 0.001). Further multivariate and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression analyses identified a five-metabolite signature comprising dopamine, 3-hydroxykynurenine, L-leucine, L-tryptophan, and L-glutamic acid for construction of a weighted AA-Score, which achieved an area under the curve of 0.858 for discriminating T2DM patients from healthy controls. The proposed method enables reliable quantitative characterization of serum amino acid profiles and may provide complementary information for T2DM diagnosis.

articles.title: Sleep as an ally in stroke neurorehabilitation: toward personalized, chrono-informed care.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology

articles.title: Recent Advances in Metal-Based Nanomaterials for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Hematological Malignancies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hematological malignancies, including leukemias, lymphomas and multiple myeloma, remain a major clinical challenge due to the limitations of conventional therapies, such as multidrug resistance, off-target toxicity, and the limited specificity of targeted agents to distinct molecular subtypes. Metal-based nanomaterials (M-NMs) have recently garnered considerable interest as multifunctional platforms capable of overcoming these obstacles, owing to their unique physicochemical properties, including surface plasmon resonance, superparamagnetism, facile surface functionalization and responsiveness to exogenous stimuli.

METHODS: This narrative review comprehensively examines recent advances in M-NMs for the diagnosis and treatment of hematological malignancies, with a focus on their transition from inert drug carriers to active theranostic agents. The review first examines the design principles of M-NMs as intelligent delivery systems, highlighting active targeting strategies via antibody-antigen or aptamer recognition, stimuli-responsive controlled release triggered by tumor microenvironmental signals or external physical fields, and synergistic delivery with chemotherapeutics to overcome drug resistance. We then elucidate the direct therapeutic mechanisms based on metal activity, encompassing Fenton chemistry-driven oxidative stress, ferroptosis, magnetic hyperthermia and photothermal conversion, as well as their integration with immunomodulation and multimodal imaging for theranostic applications.

RESULTS: Current evidence highlights several biological barriers specific to hematological malignancies, including blood compatibility, circulation kinetics and the protective bone marrow microenvironment, while nanotechnology-based strategies may help address these challenges. Long-term biosafety remains an important consideration for non-biodegradable M-NMs, with emerging approaches focusing on biodegradable or renally clearable architectures. Despite substantial progress, clinical translation remains constrained by target heterogeneity, manufacturing complexity and incomplete understanding of therapeutic sensitivity determinants.

CONCLUSIONS: We conclude that future development should prioritize the engineering of biocompatible, degradable nanoplatforms with integrated imaging and immunostimulatory functions, and emphasize that deeper mechanistic insights into metal-cell interactions and microenvironmental modulation will be important for advancing the development and clinical translation of M-NMs in precision hematology.

articles.title: A randomized comparison of comprehensive weight loss intervention vs. usual care on recurrences of atrial fibrillation in obese patients after catheter ablation: HOBIT-AF trial.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Obesity is one of the strongest risk factors for the development of atrial fibrillation (AF), and its reduction is associated with the alleviation of AF burden. The HOBIT-AF study aimed to evaluate the impact of complex weight loss interventions on AF recurrence rate in obese individuals after catheter ablation (CA).

METHODS AND RESULTS: The HOBIT-AF was a randomized controlled trial with a 15-month treatment period (3-18 months post CA) involving complex weight-reducing interventions in the active arm. The primary outcome was the change in AF/atrial tachycardia (AT) burden assessed from baseline and the final 14-day Holter monitoring. A total of 167 individuals (aged 59 years, body mass index of 35.6 kg/m2) were randomized into the active (n = 85) and control group (n = 82). At the end of the treatment period, a mean reduction of 6.8 ± 7.0% of the initial body weight accompanied by improvement of metabolic parameters was achieved in the active group. The AF/AT burden change was 0.6 ± 2.5% (95% CI: -4.2-5.5%) in the active group and -0.9 ± 1.8% (95% CI: -4.5-3.0%) in the control group. The AF/AT recurrence-free survival during the 3-18-month follow-up period was comparable between groups (70.4% vs. 69.6%).

CONCLUSION: HOBIT-AF trial showed that despite the beneficial effect of body weight reduction on metabolic profile of obese patients with predominantly paroxysmal AF after CA, no reduction in AF/AT recurrence was observed in comparison with control patients. This may be likely due to low AF burden after previous CA, limiting further improvement.

articles.title: Carbapenemase-Producing Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacterales Among Children in the United States, 2019-2024.
articles.journal: Journal of the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The current epidemiology of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) among pediatric patients in the United States is poorly described. We assessed trends in pediatric CRE and carbapenemase-producing-CRE (CP-CRE) incidence in the U.S. and characterized recent pediatric CP-CRE cases.

METHODS: We analyzed CRE clinical isolates from patients <18 years submitted to CDC's Antimicrobial Resistance Laboratory Network from January 2019 through December 2024. Annual unadjusted incidence rates for CRE and CP-CRE were estimated overall and by age group for a national convenience sample and an open cohort of 29 states with required CRE isolate submission. Trends were assessed using Poisson regression. For pediatric patients with incident CP-CRE identified from January 2023 through March 2024, medical chart reviews were performed.

RESULTS: From 2019-2024, the estimated national pediatric CRE and CP-CRE incidence increased 51% (IRR:1.51; 95% CI:1.22, 1.88) and 92% (IRR:1.92; 95% CI:1.25, 2.99), respectively; increases were similar in the open cohort. Infants had the highest incidence rates. Overall, NDM-CRE incidence increased (IRR: 4.24; 95% CI: 2.07, 9.16), surpassing KPC-CRE as the most prominent carbapenemase. Chart reviews were completed for 109 of 129 pediatric patients with CP-CRE; 14% were in patients without healthcare risk factors. Among patients with healthcare risk factors, 75% had an underlying medical condition; the most common underlying condition among infants and toddlers was cardiovascular disease (64%) and among older children was neurocognitive conditions (49%) and malignancies (41%). Common exposures across all age groups included intensive care unit hospitalization (40%) and healthcare outside the United States (37%).

CONCLUSIONS: Pediatric CP-CRE incidence is increasing, driven by NDM-CRE for which there are few treatment options. Most cases occurred among children with serious underlying conditions receiving high-acuity care. Prevention opportunities may include admission screening for patients with prior healthcare exposure outside the United States and strengthening infection prevention practices.

articles.title: Magnetic bead-assisted DSN/CRISPR-Cas12a fluorescence biosensor for sensitive and specific detection of miRNA-122.
articles.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
articles.abstract: MicroRNA-122 (miR-122) is a liver-enriched miRNA closely associated with hepatic disorders, making its sensitive detection crucial for liver disease-related biomarker analysis. Herein, we report a magnetic bead-assisted duplex-specific nuclease (DSN) cleavage strategy coupled with CRISPR/Cas12a fluorescence biosensing for sensitive miR-122 detection. A biotinylated DNA probe containing both a miR-122 recognition region and a Cas12a activator region was immobilized on streptavidin-modified magnetic beads. Upon target hybridization, DSN selectively cleaved the RNA/DNA duplex, releasing the DNA activator while enabling miR-122 recycling. After magnetic separation, the released activator triggered Cas12a-mediated trans-cleavage of a fluorophore-quencher-labeled ssDNA reporter, generating a fluorescence turn-on signal. Under optimized conditions, the biosensor showed a linear response from 100 fM to 10 nM, with a detection limit of 85 fM. The assay exhibited high specificity against mismatched sequences and other miRNAs, and achieved satisfactory recoveries (93.0-95.3%, RSD < 8%) in 10% human serum. This magnetic bead-assisted DSN/CRISPR-Cas12a fluorescence biosensor provides a simple, sensitive, and specific platform for miR-122 detection, holding promise for liver disease-related diagnostic applications.

articles.title: High-Grade Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage Complicated by Refractory Cardiogenic Shock Successfully Treated With Microaxial Flow Pump.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) is complicated by Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) in 15% to 25% of patients. Managed with supportive care, TTS with refractory cardiogenic shock represents a challenging complication with limited published guidance.

CASE SUMMARY: A 78-year-old woman presented with high-grade aSAH requiring external ventricular drain placement, stent-assisted aneurysm coiling, and dual antiplatelet therapy complicated by TTS and cardiogenic shock refractory to pressors and inotropes. A microaxial flow pump (Impella 5.5) was deployed, with full myocardial and neurological recovery.

DISCUSSION: Often self-limiting but causing secondary injury, TTS secondary to neurologic injury is driven by catecholamine-mediated myocardial injury. Mechanical circulatory support has been reported for TTS and refractory cardiogenic shock. After conducting a literature review, we believe this is the first reported use of an Impella 5.5 for refractory cardiogenic shock from TTS secondary to subarachnoid hemorrhage.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Microaxial flow pump rescue appears to be a viable strategy for refractory cardiogenic shock complicating high-grade aSAH, even during dual-antiplatelet therapy.

articles.title: Multisite Peripheral Photoplethysmography Captures Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump Counterpulsation and Weaning State in Cardiogenic Shock.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) counterpulsation raises aortic diastolic pressure every cycle (1:1) or alternate cycles (1:2, weaning). Whether they reach peripheral photoplethysmography (PPG) is unknown; 1 report described 1:1 only.

CASE SUMMARY: An 82-year-old man in IABP-supported cardiogenic shock had finger and thenar PPG on 1:1, 1:2, removal, and twice afterward. An augmented diastolic peak appeared on every finger beat on 1:1 and alternate beats on 1:2, barring ectopy, and none afterward. Perfusion index reached a nadir at removal and rose through recovery; finger-thenar coherence followed a similar trend.

DISCUSSION: Peripheral PPG encoded assist ratio and weaning state. The augmented peak was proportionally larger at the finger than in the aorta, raising the hypothesis that it reflects root- and arch-supplied territories.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Ordinary peripheral PPG carries a beat-resolved signature of IABP counterpulsation and of the weaning course, without vascular access.

articles.title: The role of integrins in T cell-mediated resistance to Cryptosporidium parvum.
articles.abstract: Cryptosporidium is a protozoan that infects epithelial cells of the small intestine and is a cause of diarrhea and death in immunocompromised individuals and malnourished children. Immunity to this parasite is mediated by an intestinal T cell response, which is generated in gut-associated lymphoid tissues and dependent on type 1 conventional dendritic cells (cDC1s). The initial priming of T cells is accompanied by changes in integrin expression and subsequent trafficking to the site of infection. The role of specific integrins in trafficking to the ileum during cryptosporidiosis is largely unknown. The development of a transgenic Cryptosporidium strain that expresses Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) Class I- and II-restricted model antigens provides the ability to track T cell responses to this parasite. Our studies in this system revealed marked changes in the integrin profile of parasite-specific T cells as they are activated and traffic to the gut, and demonstrate that cDC1s contribute to the expression of the integrins ⍺4, β7, β1, and ⍺L. Surprisingly, blockade of the canonical gut-homing integrin ⍺4β7 does not impact the ability of parasite-specific T cells to access the gut. However, blockade of integrin ⍺L decreases the parasite-specific T cell frequency at the site of infection and delays parasite control. These datasets highlight an ⍺4β7-independent mechanism of T cell trafficking to the small intestine and indicate that ⍺L is an integrin required for T cell-mediated resistance to Cryptosporidium.

articles.title: Bumetanide nasal spray for the treatment of edema in heart failure, liver disease and kidney disease: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: Edema is a common manifestation of heart failure, advanced liver disease, and chronic kidney disease, reflecting an imbalance between sodium and water homeostasis that frequently requires treatment with loop diuretics. Despite their efficacy, oral formulations may be affected by variable gastrointestinal absorption, and delayed onset of action, whereas intravenous formulations require healthcare-based delivery. These challenges have stimulated interest in alternative drug delivery strategies able to provide a rapid, and predictable diuretic therapy. Intranasal bumetanide has emerged as a novel formulation designed to overcome these limitations by enabling systemic absorption through the highly vascularized nasal mucosa while bypassing the gastrointestinal tract. Early pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic studies in healthy volunteers show that intranasal bumetanide achieves rapid and consistent systemic exposure, with diuretic and natriuretic effects comparable to conventional diuretic formulations and acceptable short-term tolerability. However, direct clinical efficacy of intranasal bumetanide in patients with edema has not yet been prospectively established, and several questions regarding its optimal clinical management, long-term effectiveness, and cost-effectiveness are yet to be addressed. This narrative review aims to discuss the pharmacological characteristics, clinical efficacy, safety, and tolerability of bumetanide nasal spray, with emphasis on its use in patients with edema secondary to cardiac, hepatic, and renal disorders.

articles.title: Association of metabolic syndrome with disease severity in acute cholangitis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute cholangitis (AC) can rapidly progress from a localized biliary infection to severe sepsis and multi-organ dysfunction. Metabolic syndrome (MetS) induces a state of chronic low-grade inflammation and immune dysregulation, which may exacerbate systemic infectious responses and lower the threshold for organ failure. However, the relationship between MetS and AC severity has not been clearly defined. This study investigates whether concomitant MetS is associated with greater AC severity.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective observational study included adult patients hospitalized with AC between September 2019 and March 2025. AC was diagnosed and graded according to the Tokyo Guidelines 2018 (TG18). Patients were classified as having isolated AC without documented chronic comorbid disease or AC with concomitant MetS. Clinical, laboratory, and imaging data were retrieved from electronic medical records. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with non-mild AC.

RESULTS: A total of 343 patients with AC were included, of whom 181 had MetS. Patients with MetS had a less favorable severity distribution than those with isolated AC. Moderate and severe AC were more frequent in the MetS group than in the isolated AC group (24.3% vs. 14.8% and 16.0% vs. 8.0%, respectively; P=0.002). In multivariable analysis, MetS was independently associated with non-mild AC (adjusted OR 2.284, 95% CI 1.424-3.661; P=0.001). Lower total protein, lower estimated glomerular filtration rate, lower total cholesterol, higher total bilirubin, and higher procalcitonin levels were also independently associated with non-mild disease. Within the MetS group, AC severity correlated positively with triglyceride levels (ρ=0.177, P=0.009) and negatively with high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) levels (ρ=-0.308, P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: MetS was independently associated with AC severity and a clinical-laboratory profile reflecting greater systemic severity. These findings suggest that MetS may identify a higher-risk phenotype in AC, highlighting the potential value of incorporating metabolic profiling into early risk stratification and tailored management strategies for these patients.

articles.title: Lung Morphology Assessed by Ultrasound and Positive End-Expiratory Pressure During Mechanical Ventilation for Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure: Secondary Analysis of a Multicenter PICU Cohort From Spain and Portugal, 2020-2021.
articles.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: In pediatric patients with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF), we aimed to determine whether positive end-expiratory pressure alignment with lung ultrasound (LUS) morphology was associated with shortened duration of mechanical ventilation.

DESIGN: Exploratory, secondary analysis of a prospective, multicenter cohort study carried out in 2020-2021.

SETTING: Twenty-five PICUs in Spain and Portugal.

PATIENTS: Children from 1 month to 18 years with AHRF undergoing invasive mechanical ventilation.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Data from lung morphology using a 12-zone LUS score between 12 and 48-72 hours after PICU admission were classified as focal or nonfocal. PEEP was considered "aligned with morphology" when greater than or equal to 10 cmH2O in cases with nonfocal lung morphology, and less than 10 cmH2O in cases with focal morphology. The primary outcome was ventilator-free days (VFDs) at 28 days, analyzed using competing-risk regression and reported as the subdistribution hazard ratio (SHR) with 95% CI. Among 160 children, 101 children (63.1%) had nonfocal morphology. PEEP was aligned with morphology in 84 of 160 children (52.5%). Aligned vs. nonaligned PEEP was associated with lower median (interquartile range [IQR]) driving pressure (13 cmH2O [IQR, 12-15 cmH2O] vs. 16 cmH2O [IQR, 15-18 cmH2O]; p < 0.001) and higher median VFDs (22 [IQR, 19-24] vs. 17 [IQR, 12-19]; p < 0.001). In adjusted competing-risk models, PEEP alignment with lung morphology was associated with greater cumulative probability of extubation at 28 days (SHR, 1.87 [95% CI, 1.30-2.69]). Stratified analyses confirmed the associated greater probability for both focal (SHR, 1.96 [95% CI, 1.20-3.21]) and nonfocal morphology cases (SHR, 2.23 [95% CI, 1.30-3.82]).

CONCLUSIONS: In pediatric cases of AHRF, lung ultrasound-defined morphology identifies clinical and physiologic heterogeneity. PEEP aligned with LUS morphology was associated with greater cumulative probability of extubation at 28 days. These multicenter data from Spain and Portugal (2020-2021) suggest that LUS may be a potentially useful bedside tool for personalized mechanical ventilation in children.

articles.title: Closing the Diagnostic Gap in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

articles.title: Platelet Transfusion Practices in the PICUs: Multicenter, Observational Study, in Türkiye and Northern Cyprus, 2024.
articles.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to describe the use of platelet transfusions among critically ill children managed in Türkiye in late 2024. Secondarily, we sought to determine these practices in relation to the 2022 Transfusion and Anemia Expertise Initiative-Control/Avoidance of Bleeding (TAXI-CAB) recommendations for critically ill pediatric patients.

DESIGN: Prospective study (October-December 2024).

SETTING: 22 PICUs in Türkiye and Northern Cyprus.

PATIENTS: Patients of 1 month to 18 years who received at least one platelet transfusion in the PICU.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENT AND MAIN RESULTS: Out of 2693 PICU admissions, 200 patients (7.4%) received 577 platelet transfusions. Of the transfusions, 383 of 577 transfusions (66.4%) were for prophylaxis, most frequently for isolated thrombocytopenia (194/383, 50.7%). Regarding the transfusion threshold for prophylaxis, in the 194 cases of isolated thrombocytopenia, the median (interquartile range [IQR]) pretransfusion platelet count was 24 (IQR, 16-38) × 109/L, which differed from the TAXI-CAB consensus statement guidance of less than 10 × 109/L. Platelet transfusion, as opposed to not, was associated with 20-fold greater odds of 28-day mortality (p < 0.001), and among the 200 patients receiving platelets, multivariable analysis showed that lower pretransfusion platelet count, support with invasive mechanical ventilation, and hospital-acquired infections collectively accounted for 34% of the variance in model performance for classifying 28-day mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: Our 2024 national, multicenter PICU study across Türkiye and Northern Cyprus shows that around two-thirds of transfusion episodes were for prophylaxis, and multivariable logistic regression modeling identified patient factors associated with greater odds of 28-day mortality. The median pretransfusion threshold for isolated thrombocytopenia was around 20 × 109/L, which is double the less than 10 × 109/L in the 2022 TAXI-CAB consensus statement. Given the heterogeneity of critically ill patients and practice environments, understanding the reasons behind these practices may help inform future research and consensus recommendations.

articles.title: Peripheral IV Catheter Longevity With Ultrasound Guidance in the PICU: Single-Center Retrospective Cohort, 2016-2018.
articles.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare associated outcomes between ultrasound-guided peripheral IV catheter (USGPIV) insertion and device longevity in critically ill children.

DESIGN: Retrospective observational cohort study.

SETTING: Tertiary medical-surgical pediatric PICU with cardiac patients.

PATIENTS: Patients admitted to the PICU requiring peripheral vascular access between January 1, 2016, and October 1, 2018.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: We identified patients who underwent USGPIV and landmark-guided peripheral IV catheters (LMGPIV) placed within 2 weeks of a USGPIV, and made comparisons between the procedures. There were 507 USGPIV and 292 LMGPIV placements. Of these, 334 USGPIV and 278 LMGPIV had longevity data. Log-rank analysis with median (interquartile range, IQR) data showed an associated greater catheter longevity in USGPIVs vs. LMGPIVs, respectively: 5 days (IQR, 2-9 d) vs. 3 days (IQR, 1-4 d), p value of less than 0.001. When restricted to either patients admitted with cardiac disease or those with known difficult vascular access, the association between USGPIVs and LMGPIVs and greater longevity remained, respectively: cardiac cases, 5 days (IQR, 2-9 d) vs. 3 days (IQR, 2-6 d); p = 0.038 and difficult access, 5 days (IQR, 2-9 d) vs. 2 days (IQR, 1-4 d), p value of less than 0.001.

CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center experience of using USGPIV placement over 28 months (2016-2018), USGPIV placement was associated with greater catheter longevity. These findings suggest that USGPIV placement is potentially a means for improving PIV insertion and maintenance.

articles.title: Delays From Clinical Manifestations to Diagnosis of Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: A National Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is a progressive, life-threatening condition. Timely and accurate diagnosis remains a challenge. We assessed time from first recorded clinical manifestation to ATTR-CM diagnosis in the United States and characterized manifestations associated with diagnostic delays.

METHODS: Retrospective analysis of US claims data (Komodo Healthcare Map, July 1, 2016-June 30, 2024). Patients were required to have ≥3 years of continuous enrollment before diagnosis.

RESULTS: Among 7509 patients, mean age 75.9 years, 63.2% male, 54.5% White, and 28.6% Black. Patients had a median of 8 manifestations before diagnosis; median observed time from first recorded manifestation to diagnosis was 5.2 years, shorter for variant versus wild-type ATTR-CM (4.4 versus 5.2 years). Within 3 years before diagnosis, patients had a mean of 12.04 (95% CI, 11.75-12.35) primary care physician visits and 14.45 (95% CI, 14.10-14.80) specialists of interest visits, most commonly with cardiologists and ophthalmologists. In adjusted analyses, variant ATTR-CM was associated with shorter time to diagnosis (β, -0.41 years [95% CI, -0.56 to -0.26]), whereas comorbidities, including hypertension (β, 0.46 years [95% CI, 0.27-0.64]), were associated with longer delays.

CONCLUSIONS: The diagnostic trajectory for ATTR-CM can be prolonged and challenging, leading to more advanced disease at diagnosis and increased burden. Raising awareness may provide an opportunity for earlier diagnosis.

articles.title: The Booster dilemma: Balancing COVID-19 protection and vaccine fatigue in the rheumatology population.
Sex-related risk for group A streptococcal bloodstream infection in Queensland, Australia, 2000-2023.
authors: European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases (ESCMID) Study Group for Bloodstream Infections, Endocarditis and Sepsis (ESGBIES)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although several studies have found males to be at increased risk for development of invasive group A streptococcal (GAS) infections, the determinants of this excess risk are not well-defined. The objective of this study was to examine sex as a risk factor for GAS bloodstream infection (BSI) in a large Australian population.

METHODS: All residents of Queensland, Australia with GAS BSI identified within the publicly funded healthcare system between 1 January 2000 and 31 December 2023 were included.

RESULTS: 4,043 incident GAS BSI infections occurred for an incidence of 3.8 per 100,000 population. Males were at significantly increased (relative risk; RR, 1.22; 95% confidence interval; CI, 1.15-1.30) but this was dependent on age and pregnancy status. Among those aged < 15 and >35 years, males were at higher risk, whereas females were at higher risk between ages 15-35 years. Among the age cohort of females aged 15-49 years, pregnancy was associated with a 9.0-fold (95% CI, 7.5-10.7) higher risk for GAS BSI as compared to non-pregnant females, with the latter group at similar risk (RR 0.9; 95% CI, 0.8-1.0) as compared to males of this age group. Although clinical determinants varied significantly across age groups, sex-related differences within age strata were limited, except among pregnant women. The all-cause 30-day case-fatality rate was 9.5% and was not significantly different between males and non-pregnant females. No deaths were pregnancy-associated.

CONCLUSIONS: Although the overall incidence of GAS BSI is higher in males, females aged 15-49 are at marked excess risk that is pregnancy-associated.

articles.title: Incretin-Based Therapies in Prostate Cancer: From Metabolic Protection to Potential Antitumour Activity - A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: This narrative review evaluates the clinical rationale for integrating incretin-based therapies as therapeutic adjuncts for men with advanced prostate cancer undergoing androgen axis suppression. Androgen deprivation therapy combined with potent androgen receptor pathway inhibitors significantly prolongs survival but induces severe, progressive metabolic toxicities, including sarcopenic obesity, profound insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, and heightened cardiovascular mortality. To address this unmet need, this study reviews published preclinical mechanisms, epidemiological data, and emerging clinical datasets examining glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists. The compiled evidence indicates that these agents provide robust metabolic protection by counteracting treatment-induced metabolic syndrome and cardiovascular risk. Furthermore, incretins may exert indirect antitumor effects by attenuating systemic hyperinsulinemia and visceral adiposity-driven chronic inflammation. Direct antitumor activity is also supported by preclinical evidence demonstrating that receptor engagement on malignant cells downregulates oncogenic signaling pathways, which correlates with recent retrospective clinical database trends showing a numerical reduction in metastatic stage migration among men with localized disease. However, dual receptor agonism introduces mechanistic uncertainty due to potential proliferative signaling cascades in neuroendocrine tumor phenotypes. In conclusion, incretin-based therapies offer a highly rational dual-action strategy for metabolic rescue and potential tumor suppression in advanced prostate cancer. Although several early-phase prospective clinical trials are currently underway to evaluate safety and metabolic efficacy, routine clinical implementation cannot be recommended until rigorously designed randomized controlled trials definitively establish long-term safety, optimal patient selection, and durable oncological outcomes.

articles.title: Network Trauma Research series: Modeling Trauma Complexity: Rodent Platforms for Studying Bone Healing and Hemorrhagic Shock.
articles.abstract: Polytrauma, defined as severe injury to multiple body regions often accompanied by physiological instability, remains a major global health burden with high morbidity and mortality. Among the most clinically relevant two-injury combinations, long-bone fractures and hemorrhagic shock are particularly important, as both critically influence systemic inflammation, remote organ dysfunction such as lung or kidney damage, and tissue regeneration itself. To improve translational understanding of these complex interactions, robust small-animal models, particularly murine systems, have been developed to experimentally dissect the biological mechanisms underlying fracture healing, hypovolemic shock, and their combined effects. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current rodent models for isolated fracture, hemorrhagic shock, and combination trauma. Key methodological variables, such as fracture induction methods, fixation strategies, hemorrhage protocols, anesthesia and analgesia, and the influence of age, sex, and comorbidities are outlined to support informed model selection. Additionally, this manuscript highlights the challenges and opportunities in designing clinically relevant "double-hit" models that mimic real-world trauma patterns while maintaining high reproducibility and animal welfare standards. Collectively, the summarized evidence underscores the importance of standardized, physiologically meaningful preclinical trauma models to advance mechanistic insights and foster the development of effective therapeutic interventions.

articles.title: Healthy Sleep Mitigates the Association Between Cardiometabolic Disease and Poorer Cognitive and Brain Health.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs), including type 2 diabetes, heart disease, and stroke, are important risk factors for dementia. We examined whether healthy sleep can support cognitive and brain health in people with CMDs.

METHODS: The study included data from 408 977 adults from the UK Biobank. CMDs were defined using medical records, medication use, and medical history. Sleep patterns were defined using a composite score incorporating sleep duration, chronotype, insomnia symptoms, snoring, and daytime sleepiness. A subsample (n=34 913) underwent brain magnetic resonance imaging; volumes of total brain, gray matter, white matter, hippocampus, and white matter hyperintensities were ascertained. Associations of joint CMD (yes/no) and sleep (healthy, intermediate, poor) status with global and domain-specific cognitive scores and brain magnetic resonance imaging measures were examined using linear regression models.

RESULTS: At baseline, 54017 (13.2%) participants had at least one CMD. In joint exposure analysis, performance in global cognition (β=0.02 [95% CI, 0.01-0.05]), verbal/numeric reasoning (β=0.07 [95% CI, 0.01-0.12]), and processing speed (β=0.07 [95% CI, 0.04-0.10]) was significantly higher among individuals with CMDs and a healthy sleep pattern, compared with those with CMDs and a poor sleep pattern. Similarly, in neuroimaging analyses, participants with CMDs and a healthy versus poor sleep pattern showed significantly larger total brain volume (β=0.22 [95% CI, 0.08-0.35]), gray matter volume (β=0.23 [95% CI, 0.09-0.36]), and white matter volume (β=0.19 [95% CI, 0.05-0.33]).

CONCLUSIONS: Healthy sleep may attenuate the associations of CMDs with poorer cognitive performance and markers of brain atrophy. The findings highlight sleep as a modifiable factor that may support cognitive and brain health in individuals with CMDs.

articles.title: Making automated sepsis surveillance comparable across hospitals.
Dynamic phenotyping and organ cross-talk in sepsis-associated organ injury: from physiological trajectories to precision critical care.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated organ injury remains a major cause of mortality in critically ill patients. Conventional assessment relies largely on physiological indicators, including lactate, mean arterial pressure (MAP), PaO2/FiO2 ratio, creatinine, urine output, and organ dysfunction scores. However, these isolated values or single-variable trends may incompletely capture the temporal instability and biological heterogeneity that characterize sepsis. Increasing evidence indicates that dynamic trajectories, variability patterns, and evolving subphenotypes may better characterize disease progression, organ recovery, and treatment responsiveness. In parallel, critical care medicine is moving from syndrome-level classification toward treatable traits, individualized treatment effects, and precision critical care. Dynamic phenotyping focuses on physiological trajectories, including lactate clearance, oxygenation evolution, hemodynamic variability, glycemic variability, and renal recovery, but its major value may lie in interpreting relationships among trajectories across organ systems. Interpretation of dynamic phenotypes therefore requires attention to cross-system temporal relationships, including coordinated recovery, coupled deterioration, and discordant recovery. From this trajectory-based perspective, sepsis-associated organ injury can be viewed as an interconnected multiorgan network involving lung-kidney, gut-lung, gut-liver, gut-kidney, and endothelial-organ cross-talk. Organ cross-talk may help explain dynamic coupling among organ systems, whereas microcirculatory-mitochondrial dysfunction may contribute to trajectory mismatch through impaired tissue perfusion, oxygen delivery-utilization uncoupling, bioenergetic failure, maladaptive metabolic reprogramming, and defective mitochondrial quality control. This trajectory-based perspective may inform future precision critical care, while most trajectory-guided strategies remain investigational and require prospective validation before routine clinical adoption.

articles.title: A Carrier-Free, Co-assembled Nanoplatform for Synergistic Photothermal Therapy: Integrating High-Efficiency BODIPY with Heat Shock Protein Inhibitors.
articles.abstract: The simultaneous delivery of boron-dipyrromethene (BODIPY) photosensitizers and heat shock proteins (HSPs) inhibitors to tumor sites can enhance the therapeutic efficacy of photothermal therapy (PTT). Current strategies mainly rely on physical encapsulation into nanocarriers or chemical conjugation onto polymer backbones for the co-delivery of BODIPY and HSP inhibitors. However, these approaches are hampered by drug leakage, reproducibility, or synthetic polydispersity. Herein, we report a carrier-free, co-assembled, and self-delivery nanoplatform to overcome these limitations. An amphiphilic BODIPY derivative (BODIPY-OEG) was synthesized and co-assembled with HSP inhibitors quercetin (Q), yielding nanoparticles (B@Q) with high photothermal conversion efficiency. The resulting B@Q nanoparticles not only possessed favorable photothermal performance in vitro but also had been demonstrated to possess potent antitumor capabilities by inhibiting the expression of HSPs in tumor cells. In vivo, B@Q demonstrated potent antitumor activity by suppressing subcutaneous tumor growth and lung metastasis, while also eliciting a potent systemic immune response, demonstrating its excellent antitumor efficacy. This work proposes a simple and precise co-assembly strategy to construct carrier-free, multifunctional nanotherapeutics, which opens avenues for the concept of self-delivered synergistic PTT agents.

articles.title: Characteristic Dihydrophenanthrenes from Spiranthes sinensis with Therapeutic Potential for Ischemic Stroke.
articles.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
articles.abstract: Spiranthes sinensis, known as "Panlongshen", is an edible traditional Chinese medicine, widely used in herbal teas and health-promoting foods. In this study, we investigated the neuroprotective properties of S. sinensis against ischemic stroke for the first time. Bioactivity-guided isolation yielded 19 dihydrophenanthrenes, including 9 undescribed compounds (7a/7b, 9-11, 12a/12b-13a/13b). These dihydrophenanthrenes demonstrated significant antineuroinflammatory activity against NO production in LPS-induced BV-2 microglia cells, with IC50 values ranging from 1.5 to 34.8 μM, which were greater than that of the positive drug (minocycline, IC50: 34.9 μM). Furthermore, coelonin (2) reduced inflammatory cytokines in BV-2 microglia and preserved PC12 cells' viability under oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation. Mechanistic investigations revealed that coelonin (2) exerts its antineuroinflammatory effects by targeting MAP3K7 and suppressing the NF-κB signaling cascade. In vivo, coelonin alleviated ischemic-reperfusion injury after MCAO. These findings revealed the neuroprotective and anti-ischemic stroke effects of S. sinensis and identified dihydrophenanthrenes as its key active constituents.

articles.title: Oleanolic Acid and Ursolic Acid Alleviate Obesity-Induced Skeletal Muscle Atrophy via Activation of the IRS/PI3K/AKT/mTOR Signaling Pathway and Attenuation of Oxidative Stress.
articles.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
articles.abstract: Oleanolic acid (OA) and ursolic acid (UA) are dietary pentacyclic triterpenoids with anti-inflammatory and insulin-sensitizing properties, but their comparative effects on obesity-related skeletal muscle atrophy remain unclear. In this study, high-fat diet-fed C57BL/6J mice and palmitic acid-treated C2C12 cells were used to evaluate their efficacy and mechanisms. OA and UA improved glucose homeostasis, attenuated muscle atrophy, and alleviated dyslipidemia and inflammation. Mechanistically, both compounds activated IRS/AKT/mTOR signaling, suppressed GSK-3β/FOXO1-mediated catabolism, alleviated endoplasmic reticulum stress, and regulated autophagy balance. They also enhanced mitochondrial function and biogenesis. Transcriptomic and CMap analyses suggested PSMB1 as a potential target. In vitro, OA and UA improved mitochondrial respiration, ATP production, and glucose uptake. Overall, OA and UA effectively mitigate HFD-induced muscle atrophy through coordinated regulation of insulin signaling, proteostasis, and mitochondrial function.

articles.title: Mangiferin Enhances Post-Stroke Neurorestorative Responses through TrkA-Dependent Signaling: A New Function Beyond Antioxidant Activity.
articles.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
articles.abstract: Mangiferin, a C-glucosyl xanthone from mango fruit, has traditionally been studied as an antioxidant. Whether this natural compound promotes poststroke neural repair remains unknown. Using a genetically engineered high-throughput screen, we identified mangiferin as one of the most potent inducers of nerve growth factor (NGF) expression among the screened natural compounds. Mangiferin enhanced tropomyosin receptor kinase A (TrkA) phosphorylation and downstream extracellular signal-regulated kinase/cAMP response element-binding protein (ERK/CREB) signaling, accompanied by increased neural stem cell proliferation, neuronal and astrocytic differentiation, and protection against ischemic injury. These effects were attenuated by TrkA inhibition, supporting TrkA-dependent signaling. In a rat model of ischemic stroke, mangiferin reduced cerebral infarct volume, improved neurobehavioral outcomes, and increased cellular and histological markers associated with endogenous neural repair in the peri-infarct region. These findings identify mangiferin as a TrkA-targeting natural compound with neuroprotective and neurorestorative potential for poststroke neural repair.

articles.title: Licochalcone A Ameliorates Metabolic-Associated Fatty Liver Disease by AMPK Signaling Pathway Activation through O-GlcNAcylation Regulation and Remodeling of Gut Microbiota and Associated Metabolites.
articles.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
articles.abstract: Metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is a major global chronic liver disorder with serious health risks. Licorice-derived licochalcone A (LA) exhibits protective activities against multiple chronic conditions. Herein, we investigated the preventive and therapeutic effects of LA on MAFLD. LA alleviated hepatic lipid accumulation, oxidative stress, and inflammation in MAFLD mice, and activated the AMPK pathway via O-GlcNAcylation. Furthermore, LA treatment restored intestinal barrier function and reshaped gut microbiota, elevating the relative abundance of Muribaculaceae and Parasutterella. Gut microbiota depletion and FMT assays demonstrated that gut microbiota are indispensable for LA-mediated MAFLD amelioration and hepatic O-GlcNAcylation regulation. Dodecanedioic acid (DA), a lipid-metabolism-related metabolite, improved MAFLD through AMPK activation. In vitro assays confirmed that LA and DA inhibited AMPK O-GlcNAcylation to boost AMPK phosphorylation and reduce cellular lipid deposition. These results offer new mechanistic perspectives regarding the hepatoprotective properties of LA and confirm its therapeutic potential to treat MAFLD.

articles.title: Dietary Flavonoid Phloretin and Its Synthetic Derivative Inhibit Platelet Activation and Thrombosis via the SRC/PI3K/Akt Signaling Pathway.
articles.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
articles.abstract: Thrombotic diseases are a leading cause of global mortality, primarily driven by pathological platelet activation. Phloretin, a natural flavonoid abundant in apple peels with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, is limited by poor solubility and bioavailability. To overcome these limitations, a synthetic derivative was designed and evaluated for antiplatelet and antithrombotic effects. Phloretin and its derivative inhibited platelet aggregation, ATP release, and integrin αIIbβ3 activation in vitro. In vivo, administration at 12.5 mg/kg significantly delayed thrombus formation without affecting bleeding time. Pharmacokinetic analysis showed that the methylated derivative exhibited enhanced bioavailability compared to phloretin. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics identified SRC and Akt1 as key targets with stable interactions. Western blotting confirmed inhibition of the SRC/PI3K/Akt/PKC signaling pathway. These findings establish phloretin, a food-derived flavonoid from apple peels, and its bioavailability-optimized derivative as multitarget antiplatelet candidates targeting the SRC/PI3K/Akt/PKC axis, highlighting their potential for cardiovascular protection.

articles.title: Novel Diterpenoids from Yemeni Coffea arabica: Isolation, Structural Elucidation, and Glucose Uptake Activity.
articles.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
articles.abstract: A phytochemical investigation of Yemeni Coffea arabica green beans led to the isolation of fifty-one diterpenoids, including 18 new compounds (1-5, 9-15, 26, 27, 31, 33, 34, 42). Structures were established by 1D/2D NMR, HRESIMS, IR, and X-ray crystallography. Compound 11 possesses a novel rearranged skeleton, while compounds 1-15 represent a series of diterpenoid glycosides featuring diverse aromatic acylations (p-hydroxybenzoyl, p-coumaroyl, feruloyl, sinapoyl, or 6,7-dimethoxycinnamoyl) on a C-19 β-glucosyl moiety. Bioactivity screening in insulin-resistant HepG2 cells identified nine compounds that significantly enhanced glucose uptake, with improvements ranging from 24.91% to 81.10%. This study elucidates the structural diversity of diterpenoids in coffee and highlights their potential relevance to glucose metabolism.

articles.title: DUFB Promotes Broad-Spectrum Disease Resistance by Stabilizing GS1;1 in Rice.
articles.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
articles.abstract: Excessive nitrogen (N) fertilization increases rice susceptibility to pathogens, yet the molecular links between N signaling and immunity remain largely unresolved. In this study, we identified three genes encoding DUF-domain-containing proteins, DUFA, DUFB, and DUFC, which were induced by Rhizoctonia solani (R. solani) infection and N treatment. Analyses of dufa/b/c mutant and overexpression lines showed that DUFA/B/C genes have functional redundancy and confer broad-spectrum resistance to sheath blight (ShB), blast, and bacterial blight. DUFA/B/C interacted with glutamine synthetase 1;1 (GS1;1), suggesting that distinct DUF proteins may converge on a shared GS1;1-associated defense pathway. Subsequent analyses demonstrated that DUFs enhance rice ShB resistance by inhibiting ubiquitin-mediated GS1;1 degradation. The GS1;1 protein level was reduced in high-nitrogen (HN) compared to in low-nitrogen (LN) conditions, implying that DUFB-GS1;1 signaling might be involved in N-dependent rice disease resistance. Overall, these findings reveal a mechanism linking the N status to rice immunity through DUFB-mediated stabilization of GS1;1.

articles.title: The Coagulation-Immune Axis in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Mechanisms, Prognostic Significance, and Therapeutic Opportunities.
articles.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) develops in a microbe-rich, injury-prone mucosa in which coagulation, inflammation, and tissue repair are closely coupled. Tumor and host cells can activate tissue factor-thrombin signaling, platelets, fibrin turnover, extracellular vesicles, and neutrophil extracellular traps, thereby reshaping myeloid-cell recruitment, cytotoxic immunity, angiogenesis, and invasion. However, local procoagulant biology does not necessarily predict systemic venous thromboembolism. We therefore organize the evidence using a compartmentalized immunothrombosis model that distinguishes intratumoral coagulation-immune remodeling, systemic thrombosis, and treatment-dependent perioperative events. Direct OSCC studies support several components of this network, but much of the evidence linking coagulation to immune escape and treatment response remains preclinical or extrapolated from other tumors. Circulating D-dimer, fibrinogen, platelet indices, and inflammatory ratios show prognostic associations, yet their incremental value beyond established clinicopathologic factors has not been established. Anticoagulant, antiplatelet, protease-activated receptor, podoplanin-CLEC-2, fibrinolytic, and NET-directed strategies are biologically plausible but should not be used as OSCC treatment without a standard indication or clinical trial. Future studies should pair longitudinal blood measurements with spatial tumor profiling and match interventions to a verified mechanism, anatomical compartment, and safe treatment window.

articles.title: RtmR is a membrane-embedded RRM family RNA-binding protein.
articles.abstract: The animal symbiont Vibrio fischeri has served as a model organism for molecular processes underlying bacterial group behaviors, including quorum sensing, and biofilm development. Here, using a genetic approach to identify negative regulators of biofilm formation in V. fischeri, we identified a membrane-bound RNA-binding protein, RtmR (VF_2432), that acts as an inhibitor of the symbiosis polysaccharide (SYP) biofilm. Membrane localization of the protein seems to be required for protein stability or expression, as truncation of the transmembrane helices led to an inability to detect the protein. The conserved RNP1 and RNP2 motifs in RtmR's cytoplasmic RNA recognition motif (RRM) domain are required for function, and we demonstrate binding to RNA substrates. Identification of RtmR RNA ligands was conducted with an individual-nucleotide resolution crosslinking and immunoprecipitation sequencing (iiCLIP-seq) approach that revealed a large interactome. One transcript identified was that of the biofilm regulatory histidine kinase RscS. We found that RtmR biofilm inhibition depends on RscS activity, and that RtmR negatively regulates levels of RscS. Overall, this work characterizes a novel type of bacterial RNA-binding protein.IMPORTANCEBacterial RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) perform key functions to regulate stress responses and development. Bacterial RBPs, including the RNA chaperones Hfq and ProQ, the global regulator CsrA, and the cold shock proteins (Csps), have been extensively studied, although additional classes of RBPs have been predicted by bioinformatic methods, including those carrying an RNA recognition motif (RRM) domain. This work expands on recent studies of RRM domain proteins in bacteria to characterize a membrane-bound RRM protein that regulates bacterial biofilm development. Given our rapidly expanding knowledge regarding the role of RNA-binding proteins in bacterial molecular biology, this work contributes a new class of membrane-bound regulators with homologs in human pathogens and marine symbionts.

articles.title: A highly conserved two-gene operon is crucial for lipoarabinomannan localization, pathogenesis, and cell envelope function in Mycobacterium abscessus.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Mycobacterium abscessus is an emerging threat, causing infections that are difficult to treat due to intrinsic resistance to most antibiotics. Determinants of M. abscessus physiology and pathogenesis remain poorly understood, hampering therapeutic development. Here, we show that in M. abscessus, the lprg-mfs operon is essential for virulence in macrophages and mice. Loss of lprg-mfs in M. abscessus causes accumulation of the glycolipid lipoarabinomannan (LAM) on the cell surface and in culture supernatant, suggesting that this system participates in LAM import. This contrasts with its proposed role in M. tuberculosis, where lprg-mfs has been implicated in the export of various lipids. Consistent with altered lipid distribution, the lprg-mfs mutant displays severe defects in mycomembrane permeability, fluidity, and integrity, and expression of mfs alone restores only a subset of these phenotypes, revealing a surprising uncoupling of envelope fluidity and permeability. Using a suppressor screen to further investigate the factors that control the distribution of lipoarabinomannan, we find that a point mutation in the unannotated gene MAB_0995 can fully or partially rescue all deletion mutant phenotypes. Our data also show that lipoarabinomannan in the mycomembrane is dynamically regulated in response to environmental conditions, including hypoxia and macrophage infection. Together, these findings redefine the role of LprG and Mfs in mycobacterial cell envelope homeostasis and reveal unexpected plasticity in mycomembrane lipid regulation in M. abscessus.

IMPORTANCE: The emerging pathogen Mycobacterium abscessus causes life-threatening lung infections in certain patients that are extremely difficult to treat due to its intrinsic resistance to most antibiotics. However, the process by which this organism establishes infection is poorly understood, as are the specific determinants of antibiotic tolerance. Better knowledge of the genes required for virulence and impermeability to antibiotics in M. abscessus could enable the development of more effective treatments. The significance of this study is the demonstration that the lprg-mfs operon is required for both pathogenesis and impermeability in M. abscessus. Furthermore, our study shows a correlation between cell envelope characteristics and the distribution of the molecule lipoarabinomannan, suggesting a specific mechanism by which these crucial characteristics are mediated.

articles.title: Protection Induced by a Novel Circumsporozoite Protein Malaria Vaccine is Associated with the Quality of Antibody Responses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Malaria remains an intractable global health problem. We report results of a single-center, open-label Phase 1 trial of a nearly full-length soluble recombinant Plasmodium falciparum CSP (FMP013) formulated in the Army Liposome Formulation containing QS21 (ALFQ).

METHODS: Healthy malaria-naïve adults (n=29) were enrolled into three groups. Standard (STD) group volunteers received FMP013/AFLQ (20 µg/0.5 mL) on a 0-1-2-month schedule (n=10). Delayed group (DEL) received the same dose on a 0-1-6-month schedule (n=10). Delayed Fractional Dose (DFD) volunteers (n=9), vaccinated at 0-1-6-months, received a fractional third dose (4 µg/0.1 mL). Immunized and unvaccinated control participants underwent P. falciparum-infected mosquito bite challenge three weeks after the third immunization and safety, tolerability, efficacy, and immunogenicity were analyzed.

RESULTS: All regimens were well tolerated. 5 of 9 DEL (vaccine efficacy [VE], 55.6%, 95% confidence interval [CI], 21.2-86.3%; P< 0.001), 1 of 7 DFD (VE 14.3%, CI 0.0-57.9%), and 1 of 9 STD (VE 11.1%, CI 0.0-48.3%) subjects had sterile protection. Delayed blood-stage infection was observed in 3 DEL, 2 DFD and 1 STD subjects. The FMP013/ALFQ vaccine elicited C-terminal biased responses and protection in the DEL regimen was associated with higher C-terminal avidity, and junction, minor repeat epitope-specific responses.

CONCLUSIONS: A soluble protein CSP vaccine, akin to particle vaccines, can elicit a protective response when delivered using a potent adjuvant and an extended vaccination schedule. These data encourage further evaluation of FMP013/ALFQ efficacy and durability in the field.

articles.title: PEDV NSP5 promotes immune evasion by recruiting TRIM28 to degrade DDX3X.
articles.abstract: Porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV) has emerged as the predominant swine enteric coronavirus, causing vomiting, diarrhea, dehydration, and high mortality in piglets. Members of the DEAD-box family play critical roles in viral infection, yet their roles in PEDV infection remain undefined. Furthermore, it is unknown whether PEDV and its proteins regulate the expression of these DEAD-box proteins. In this study, reverse transcription quantitative PCR was used to examine the gene expression changes of 15 DEAD-box family members in the intestinal tissues of one-month-old PEDV-infected piglets. We found that the expression of DEAD-box helicase 3 X-Linked (DDX3X) was upregulated following PEDV infection, a result that was similarly observed in cellular experiments. Overexpression and knockdown of DDX3X significantly inhibited or promoted PEDV replication, respectively. Moreover, the use of specific DDX3X inhibitors demonstrated that DDX3X primarily restricts PEDV RNA accumulation. Our study also showed that DDX3X enhances RIG-I-like receptor (RLR) signaling by promoting the phosphorylation of TANK-binding kinase 1 (TBK1), interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3), signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1), and Janus kinase 1 (JAK1) proteins. Co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence assays further demonstrated the association and colocalization of DDX3X with TBK1 and IRF3, potentially contributing to its antiviral function. We constructed all PEDV proteins and identified that NSP5 reduces DDX3X levels via ubiquitination. Additionally, we discovered that tripartite motif-containing protein 28 (TRIM28) interacts with DDX3X and mediates its K48-linked ubiquitination. Knockdown of TRIM28 significantly reduced NSP5-mediated DDX3X ubiquitination. In conclusion, this study clarified the molecular mechanism by which NSP5 antagonizes DDX3X-mediated antiviral immune responses via the ubiquitination pathway, providing new insights into PEDV-host interactions and potential targets for antiviral intervention.IMPORTANCERecurrent outbreaks of porcine epidemic diarrhea (PED) have led to substantial economic losses in the global swine industry. To proactively control PED, it is crucial to investigate the pathogenic mechanisms of PEDV, particularly by exploring the interactions between viral proteins and host factors. In this study, we identified a significant phenomenon: PEDV infection activates DDX3X, enhancing the antiviral activity of the RLR pathway, while PEDV NSP5 recruits TRIM28 to target DDX3X for degradation, thus suppressing immune responses. These findings shed light on the complex regulatory interplay between PEDV proteins and host factors, deepening our understanding of the role and mechanisms of PEDV NSP5 in immune suppression.

articles.title: Transgene expression kinetics and replication potential of recombinant adenovirus serotype 4 in a mouse model and its use as a herpes simplex virus vaccine.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Human adenovirus serotype 4 (Ad4) is used as a replication-competent oral vaccine that safely and effectively prevents Ad4 respiratory illness in US military personnel. Recombinant Ad4 vaccine candidates elicit mucosal and systemic immune responses against respiratory viruses in hamsters, nonhuman primates, and humans. Although evaluation of Ad4 vaccine candidates in mice would be extremely useful given the number of immunologic tools available, this has been limited by concerns about reduced viral replication in these animals. Here, we generated recombinant Ad4 vectors that express either luciferase (Ad4-Luc), green fluorescent protein (Ad4-EGFP), or herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2) glycoprotein D (Ad4-gD2) to identify transgene expression kinetics, the presence of Ad4 vector replication, and HSV-2 immune responses and protection against HSV-2 infection. Local luciferase activity was observed from 7 h to 20 days after intranasal inoculation of BALB/c and humanized mice. Subsequent inoculations with Ad4-Luc showed reduced luciferase expression in BALB/c mice but robust expression in humanized mice, suggesting an immune response to the vector in wild-type mice. Ad4 DNA production, but not luciferase activity, was reduced in the lungs of BALB/c mice treated with cidofovir before inoculation with Ad4, implying that Ad4 replicated, albeit at a low level, in the lungs. Intranasal vaccination of mice with Ad4-gD2 resulted in HSV-2-neutralizing antibodies in the serum and, after HSV-2 intravaginal challenge, reduced disease scores, increased survival, and reduced shedding. Overall, the BALB/c mouse model is semi-permissive to Ad4 mucosal infection, but transgene expression is sufficient for the study of Ad4-based vaccine candidates.

IMPORTANCE: Mucosal surfaces serve as the primary site of infection and shedding for many viral pathogens. Immune responses at mucosal sites provide protection, but few mucosal vaccines are licensed. The oral replication-competent adenovirus serotype 4 (Ad4) vaccine is used to prevent respiratory illness in military recruits, has an extraordinary record of safety and efficacy, and has been tested as a recombinant platform for other viruses. Further development of this vaccine platform has been partially hindered by the perceived inability to evaluate vaccine candidates in mice. Here, we characterize recombinant Ad4 transgene expression kinetics and viral replication after inoculation at various sites and show protection against herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2) genital disease in mice after intranasal vaccination. We show that Ad4 can induce protective efficacy, even in a semi-permissive mouse model, suggesting this is a promising vector for HSV-2 and potentially other viral pathogens.

articles.title: Naturally circulating reoviruses exhibit enhanced intestinal persistence and altered enteric protease dependence compared to lab-adapted strains.
articles.abstract: Mammalian orthoreoviruses (reoviruses) commonly infect many mammals, persist on surfaces and in bodies of water, and represent a safe model to study enteric viruses. Extensive research has been performed on prototype reovirus strains, specifically T1L and T3D, in murine L929 fibroblasts. However, T1L/T3D were found to have greater sensitivity to endosomal cathepsin L/B than sewage-derived isolates that rely on intestinal trypsin/chymotrypsin to process virions extracellularly prior to infection. To further understand how cultural adaptation affects reovirus characteristics in L929 cells and intestines, replicative capabilities of lab- and sewage-derived reoviruses were measured in L929 cells following exposure of virions to intestinal luminal factors and in the intestinal tract following oral inoculation of mice. In vitro biochemical analysis of post-entry replication steps and in vivo results of early innate and adaptive immune profiles did not distinguish viruses based on source. In contrast, sewage-derived reoviruses were found at higher titers than lab strains in ileal and colonic tissues, luminal content, and fecal shedding. Increased persistence in vivo was associated with greater resistance to proteolysis and infectious stability in the presence of intestinal lumen factors, particularly from the colon. Furthermore, reovirus uncoating in vivo depended not only on intestinal trypsin/chymotrypsin, as previously described, but also on EDTA-sensitive metalloproteases that differentially process lab- and sewage-derived reoviruses. Altogether, these findings demonstrate that environmental reoviruses are optimized for fecal-oral transmission by enhanced extracellular stability and resistance to intestinal proteases, whereas lab strains adapted to infect well in vitro at the cost of reduced robustness in the gut environment.IMPORTANCEMost of what we know about enteric virus entry and uncoating comes from long-passaged lab strains studied under simplified conditions with added trypsin or chymotrypsin. Here, we directly compare these canonical reovirus lab strains to minimally passaged, sewage-derived isolates in a murine oral infection model. We find that, once entry is equalized, post-entry replication steps are broadly similar, but naturally circulating strains achieve higher titers in distal gut segments and feces, resist proteolysis by colonic lumen factors, and rely on a broader, regionally distinct set of intestinal proteases, including metalloproteases, for uncoating. These results reveal that the true protease usage of enteric viruses in vivo is more complex than suggested by standard culture systems, with capsid sequences tuned to balance efficient replication, environmental stability, and fecal-oral transmission.

articles.title: Antibiotic class shapes O-antigen-dependent phage outcomes in a clinical Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolate.
articles.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a high-priority opportunistic pathogen characterized by significant genetic plasticity and increasing multidrug resistance.
