Although phage-antibiotic combinations are increasingly explored to combat antimicrobial resistance, whether these interactions are synergistic or antagonistic and how different antibiotic classes influence phage replication and the subsequent development of resistance remain unclear. In this study, we examined combinations of the O-antigen-dependent phage phipa10 with amikacin (AMK), levofloxacin (LEV), or meropenem (MEM) against P. aeruginosa ZS-PA-35. At 24 h, the combinations showed antibiotic-dependent patterns of bacterial growth suppression. High concentrations of amikacin and meropenem reduced the extracellular yield of infectious phipa10. The highest tested levofloxacin concentration also reduced the recovered phage yield. Whole-genome sequencing of phage-resistant mutants showed that meropenem treatment drove large chromosomal deletions encompassing galU and hmgA, resulting in a characteristic brown pigmentation phenotype. LEV-selected isolates carried smaller deletions involving galU, whereas AMK-selected isolates shared a galU substitution. In a Galleria mellonella infection model, phipa10-antibiotic combinations improved host survival relative to either treatment alone, although the magnitude of the benefit varied across antibiotic classes. The meropenem combination yielded the highest observed survival proportion despite reduced phage yield in vitro. These results show that bacterial suppression, infectious phage yield, and resistance outcomes can diverge among the three tested antibiotic partners.IMPORTANCEPhage-antibiotic combinations may affect bacterial suppression, phage yield, and resistance-associated phenotypes differently. We compared three antibiotic partners in a single Pseudomonas aeruginosa-phage system. The observed growth, genetic, and larval survival outcomes varied across the tested treatments. Reduced phage yield did not preclude improved survival in the infection model. These observations support evaluating multiple outcomes when assessing a phage-antibiotic combination. Their broader relevance requires validation with additional isolates, phages, and antibiotics.

articles.title: Preanalytical Benchmarks for Solvent-Based GC-MS Profiling of Volatile Organic Compounds in Diabetic Foot Ulcer Swabs.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry
articles.abstract: Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) is widely applied to wound-associated volatile organic compounds (VOCs), yet the preanalytical steps that govern its sensitivity remain poorly characterized, limiting comparison across studies of diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) infection. We benchmark a controlled solvent-based extraction workflow with direct internal-standard addition for GC-MS profiling of clinical DFU swabs. A six-compound multiclass panel (butanoic acid, 3-methyl-; 1-octen-3-ol; nonanal; 5-hepten-2-one, 6-methyl-; dimethyl disulfide; and heptane) was spiked onto sterile cotton swabs with toluene-d8 as an internal standard (IS). At day 0, diethyl ether (DE) gave the highest IS-normalized response for every analyte (F(2,6) = 12.4-131.0), most markedly for hydrogen-bond-active species. A 50% nitrogen blowdown step produced volatility-dependent enhancement the lowest enrichment in every solvent (1.0-1.9-fold), whereas high-boiling analytes exceeded 2-fold in DE. Frozen storage at -20 °C for 15 days preserved the IS-normalized response within ±20% of day 0 for most analyte-solvent combinations; hexane gave the tightest precision (mean %RSD 2.3-8.0%), whereas DE was poor for heptane (25.7%). Applied to 28 infected DFUs, the workflow returned 13 VOCs meeting combined retention index (|ΔRI| ≤35) and spectral-library (match factor ≥75) criteria, spanning fatty acids, fermentation products, host lipid-peroxidation aldehydes, phenylalanine catabolites, and palmitamide. These class-stratified preanalytical benchmarks provide an analytical baseline against which clinical wound-VOC studies can be designed and compared.

Learning-based rapid disengagement is limited by fear-conditioned stimuli.
articles.abstract: Previous work showed that people can implicitly learn to disengage rapidly from a distractor when its location is spatially associated with a target through repetition. The current study investigated whether learning-based rapid disengagement from visually salient distractors extends to emotionally salient distractors. Participants performed an additional-singleton task in which a colour singleton distractor appeared on some trials. One distractor colour was fear-conditioned by pairing it with electric shock (CS+), whereas another colour was not (CS-). Participants searched for the target faster when the distractor appeared at the associated than a non-associated location, consistent with the association modulating target selection. Dwell-time analysis revealed that the associated location shortened dwell time for CS- but not CS+ distractors. These findings suggest that learned distractor-target spatial association can facilitate disengagement from visually salient distractors, while fear-conditioned salience continued to hold attention despite a regularity favouring rapid disengagement.

articles.title: The Fungal Response Regulator Skn7: Domain Architecture and Multifunctional Roles in Fungal Biology.
articles.abstract: The two-component phosphorelay system (TCS) is an ancient signaling module that enables fungal adaptation to changing environments. It consists of a hybrid histidine kinase (HHK), a histidine phosphotransfer protein (HPt), and downstream response regulators (RRs). Among these, the nuclear response regulator Skn7 is unique to fungi and absent from mammalian and plant cells, making it an attractive antifungal target. This review integrates structural and functional evidence to describe the multi-layered regulatory architecture of Skn7 orthologs across fungal phyla. Structurally, Skn7 combines prokaryotic signaling with eukaryotic transcriptional features through a conserved receiver (REC) domain, a central coiled-coil oligomerization motif, and a winged helix-turn-helix heat shock factor (HSF) DNA-binding domain. Functionally, Skn7 coordinates oxidative stress responses through cross-talk with the osmotic and cell wall integrity (CWI) MAPK pathways while acting as both a transcriptional activator and co-repressor. Notably, Skn7 regulates fungal development, morphogenesis, secondary metabolism-including pigments, toxins, and volatile organic compounds involved in interspecific competition-and cell fate by controlling autolysis and programmed cell death cascades. Overall, this comprehensive review highlights the evolutionary plasticity and functional versatility of Skn7, supporting its potential as a therapeutic target against fungal infections.

articles.title: Benchmarking Pediatric Dental Entrustable Professional Activities (EPAs) Through Residency.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To examine pediatric dentistry residency program directors' (PDs) perspective on establishing consensus regarding expected timing of unsupervised practice for each pediatric dentistry entrustable professional activity (EPA).

METHODS: A benchmarking survey on EPAs and readiness for unsupervised practice was distributed via email to pediatric dentistry PDs in the United States and Canada. The survey included specific instructions to guide PDs to choose one point along a continuum that corresponded with when a resident should be able to practice each task without supervision. Eighty-percent agreement was used to establish consensus. Demographics and information on future use of EPAs were also collected and descriptive statistics were completed.

RESULTS: Thirty-eight percent (41/108) PDs responded to the survey. Consensus was established for all EPAs presented, showing a progression in independence with increased time in residency. Over 90% (37/41) of PDs indicated that they were "very likely or likely" to use national EPA benchmarking to aid in assessing their residents' progression through their program.

CONCLUSIONS: A national consensus on EPAs allows for pediatric dentistry residency programs to be transparent in expectations of resident progression through a training program. By developing a timeline for when the average resident is ready to progress from simple to advanced tasks, programs can award increased independence and ensure that residents (and graduates) provide safe care at the proper supervision level.

articles.title: Preventing pacing-induced cardiomyopathy through early risk stratification.
Rosmarinic Acid Inhibits β-Sheet and β-Hairpin Formation in Human Islet Amyloid Polypeptide Dimers by Stabilizing Localized C-Terminal Motifs: An REMD Study.
articles.abstract: The misfolding of human islet amyloid polypeptide (hIAPP) into soluble oligomers is a primary pathological event in type 2 diabetes, with the early dimerization process representing a critical pharmacological target. Here, we investigate the molecular mechanism by which rosmarinic acid (RA) counteracts full-length hIAPP self-association through replica-exchange molecular dynamics. Our results show that RA drastically suppresses overall β-sheet propensities and truncates extended, aggregation-competent β-strands, lowering the sampled population of ordered β-hairpin-like motifs associated with amyloidogenic hIAPP conformations. Instead of forming compact structures, the hIAPP dimer is diverted toward disordered, hyper-solvated topologies. This conformational remodeling is driven by spatially heterogeneous thermodynamic perturbations that disrupt native interpeptide contacts and transfer structured motifs into localized turn and bend structures at the C-terminus. Energetically, RA outcompetes peptide-peptide interactions via a multimodal strategy, preferentially anchoring to the hIAPP N-terminus through residues K1 and R11 while simultaneously engaging the hydrophobic core via π-π stacking. Notably, this robust noncovalent occupation of key amyloidogenic regions occurs spontaneously in the simulations, offering an atomistic clue for modulating early hIAPP self-association. These structural and energetic insights clarify how RA interacts with transient hIAPP dimer ensembles, providing a defined biophysical framework for the rational design of amyloid inhibitors.

articles.title: Germline ATP2B2 Variant Associates With Central Nervous System Involvement in Childhood Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Genome-wide association studies (GWASs) can uncover inherited determinants of clinically relevant leukemia phenotypes, but their utility depends on precise phenotyping. Central nervous system (CNS) involvement in childhood B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (BCP-ALL) is prognostically important, but its underlying biology remains poorly understood. We investigated inherited determinants using a sensitive, standardized definition of CNS involvement.

PROCEDURE: We conducted a pooled observational cohort GWAS of CNS involvement at diagnosis among 674 patients with BCP-ALL from the Nordic Society of Pediatric Hematology and Oncology (NOPHO) ALL2008 and ALLTogether1 cohorts. CNS involvement was defined as ≥10 leukemic blasts detected in diagnostic cerebrospinal fluid by flow cytometry (FCM). Association testing used logistic regression adjusted for white blood cell count and genetic ancestry. Cox regression assessed variant associations with time to relapse. Findings were evaluated in an independent Associazione Italiana di Ematologia e Oncologia Pediatrica-Berlin-Frankfurt-Münster ALL 2000 protocol (AIEOP-BFM2000) cohort through targeted analysis.

RESULTS: Among 10,242,929 variants passing quality control, rs13059398, an intronic ATP2B2 variant, was associated with CNS involvement at genome-wide significance (p = 3.28 × 10-8; odds ratio [OR] = 6.07; 95% confidence interval, 3.2-11.5). The variant was carried by 21/113 (18.6%) CNS-positive and 29/559 (5.2%) CNS-negative patients. Although directionally consistent in the validation cohort, the association was not statistically significant. ATP2B2, predominantly expressed in CNS tissues, encodes the plasma membrane Ca2+ ATPase plasma membrane calcium ATPase 2 (PMCA2). There was no association with time to relapse.

CONCLUSIONS: Germline variation at ATP2B2 was associated with FCM-defined CNS involvement in childhood BCP-ALL. These findings identify ATP2B2 as a candidate locus for further investigation of the biological mechanisms underlying leukemic CNS involvement.

articles.title: Prevalence and clinical associations of age-related clonal haematopoiesis in SSc.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: SSc is an autoimmune disease involving both innate and adaptive immunity, characterized by progressive organ fibrosis. Age-related clonal haematopoiesis (ARCH) results from somatic mutations in haematopoietic progenitors and is increasingly implicated in inflammation and autoimmunity. We aimed to assess the prevalence of ARCH in patients with SSc and its association with disease characteristics.

METHODS: Targeted myeloid next-generation sequencing (NGS) was performed in 196 patients with SSc and 392 age- and gender-matched individuals without SSc and referred for NGS without a final diagnosis myelodysplastic syndrome. Variants with variant allele frequency (VAF) ≥ 0.8% were considered for ARCH analysis. Clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) was defined as ARCH with a VAF ≥2%.

RESULTS: The prevalence of ARCH and CHIP was similar between SSc patients and the control group: 32.7% vs 37.2% (P = 0.25) and 23.5% vs 28.8% (P = 0.15), respectively. Among patients with SSc, ARCH was associated with higher NT-proBNP levels and higher prevalence of progressive interstitial lung disease (39.1% vs 15.7%, P = 0.026), pulmonary hypertension (23.4% vs 11.4%, P = 0.028), valvular heart disease (23.4% vs 11.4%, P = 0.028), ACAs (65.1% vs 49.6%, P = 0.043) in our cohort. After adjustment to age and gender, only NT-proBNP levels remain significantly higher in SSc patients with ARCH. These associations were not observed when restricting the analysis to CHIP except for valvular heart disease (26.1% vs 11.4%, P = 0.019) and higher NT-proBNP levels.

CONCLUSION: The prevalence of ARCH and CHIP was 32.7% and 23.5%, respectively, in our cohort of patients with SSc presence of ARCH was associated with more severe pulmonary involvement, a higher frequency of pulmonary hypertension, valvular heart disease and ACAs. After adjustment to age and sex, ARCH was associated with a higher NT-pro BNP levels.

articles.title: Large vessel giant cell arteritis in remission: Is imaging useful as predictor for relapses?
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether vasculitic findings (VF) on [¹⁸F] fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) and/or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) at treatment stop (TS) are associated with relapse in patients with large vessel giant cell arteritis (LV-GCA), and to explore the association between PET/CT-based polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) findings and relapse.

METHODS: LV-GCA patients included in our local GCA cohort BARK who discontinued treatment in remission and underwent PET/CT and/or MRI within ±4 months of TS were included. VF were defined using standardized criteria. Periarticular inflammation in PET/CT was scored by the Leuven score and a cut-off ≥12 was considered positive. Patients were followed for relapse. Statistics used Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression.

RESULTS: VF at TS were observed in 54% of patients (25/46), including 47% of MRIs (15/32), 50% of PET/CTs (14/28), and 4/14 positive on both modalities. During follow-up, 48% (22/46) of patients relapsed in median 4.7 months after TS (82% minor, 18% major relapses). Overall, VF at TS was not associated with relapse (p = 0.1). PET/CT findings, including SUV segment/liver ratio and a modified PETVAS were not predictive for relapse (p ≥ 0.6). Absence of VF in MRI at TS was associated with relapse (p = 0.005). Six patients had positive Leuven score at TS and all relapsed (HR 5.35, 95% CI 1.70-16.83, p = 0.004).

CONCLUSION: Vascular imaging at TS did not predict relapse in our cohort. There is a signal pointing towards a potential association of periarticular inflammation in PET/CT at TS to subsequent relapses, that warrants further validation.

articles.title: Krebs Von Den Lungen-6 as a biomarker for lung disease activity and diagnosis in systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis.
authors: CARRA Registry FROST Investigators and the CARRA Registry sJIA-LD Cohort Investigators
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Children with systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (sJIA) and lung disease (LD) are at increased risk of serious complications and premature mortality, making early detection and intervention critical. Krebs von den Lungen 6 (KL-6) is a blood-based biomarker for interstitial lung disease in adults; however, its role in pediatric LD is unclear. This study evaluates KL-6 as a discriminatory and disease activity biomarker for sJIA-LD.

METHODS: Thirty-two patients with sJIA-LD were enrolled through the Childhood Arthritis and Research Alliance (CARRA) Registry. Comparators included sJIA patients without LD, children with primary pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP), and healthy control children.

RESULTS: Median KL-6 levels were significantly higher in sJIA-LD (596.3 U/mL [IQR 273.5-5,896.3]) compared to sJIA without LD (193.0 U/mL [151.0-252.0], p < 0.0001) and healthy controls (171.9 U/mL [89.7-224.3], p = 0.001), with no difference versus PAP (596.3 vs. 1429.9, p = 0.30). A cut-off of 259.5 U/mL yielded 81.3% sensitivity and 80.9% specificity for LD (AUC 0.856, p < 0.0001). At 371.5 U/mL, specificity reached 100% with 68.7% sensitivity and 100% positive predictive value. SJIA-LD features associated with higher median KL-6 levels included oxygen requirement, abnormal pulse oximeter (<90%), and abnormal chest radiographs. KL-6 strongly correlated with physician global assessment of lung disease but not with markers of systemic inflammation or macrophage activation syndrome.

CONCLUSION: KL-6 is a useful biomarker for discriminating LD and evaluating disease activity in sJIA-LD. Future efforts should focus on the utility of KL-6 for monitoring disease progression, treatment response, and predicting long-term disease trajectories.

articles.title: Baseline predictors of post-treatment diffusion capacity after neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy in non-small-cell lung cancer: development and external validation of a clinical prediction model.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Routine repetition of pulmonary function tests (PFTs) following neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy is standard but may be redundant in selected patients. We aimed to develop and externally validate a multivariable model to predict post-treatment carbon monoxide lung diffusion capacity (DLCO), with the objective of identifying patients at low predicted risk of clinically important post-treatment impairment in whom selective omission of repeat testing could potentially be considered.

METHODS: A predictive model was derived from 106 patients with locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) undergoing neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy. Multivariable regression with backward stepwise elimination was used to test candidate predictors. The model was validated on an external cohort of 60 patients. Agreement was assessed using locally weighted scatterplot smoothing (Lowess) curves and misclassification rates relative to a clinically relevant threshold of DLCO<60%.

RESULTS: The final model retained four independent predictors: Baseline DLCO (p < 0.001), Age (p < 0.001), Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression (p = 0.043), and Smoking status (p = 0.10). Applied to the external validation cohort (n = 60), the model demonstrated a median predicted DLCO of 66% (IQR 59-79) versus an observed DLCO of 73% (IQR 59-83), and Lowess curves indicated a stable relationship across the data range. The model correctly identified 100% of patients with an observed post-treatment DLCO<60% by using a predicted threshold of < 65%. All patients with a predicted DLCO>65% had an observed DLCO>60%.

CONCLUSIONS: We developed and externally validated a clinical model that reliably predicts post-neoadjuvant DLCO. The model may help identify asymptomatic patients at low likelihood of a post-treatment DLCO <60% in whom repeat PFT assessment could potentially be omitted. Prospective validation is required before this approach can be recommended in routine clinical practice.

articles.title: Acrokeratosis Paraneoplastica (Bazex Syndrome) Uncovering Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemia With Transformation to Acute Myeloid Leukemia.
Are electronic gambling machine availability and area-level socioeconomic disadvantage associated with local residents' gambling losses and share of local revenue?
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Physical availability is a key determinant of gambling spending and, consequently, gambling harm. The aim of the study was to examine, using objective revenue data linked to gamblers' residential postal codes, how the availability of electronic gambling machines and area-level socioeconomic disadvantage are associated with average electronic gambling machine losses per adult and the share of local electronic gambling machine revenue attributable to local residents.

METHODS: The analysis draws on register-based data on electronic gambling machine revenue at the postal code level combined with area-level socioeconomic indicators drawn from official statistics. Linear regression models were used to estimate the associations between electronic gambling machine availability, area-level socioeconomic status, and two outcomes: average electronic gambling machine losses per adult and the share of electronic gambling machine revenue attributable to local residents.

RESULTS: Average losses per adult among local residents increase with electronic gambling machine availability and are highest in the most disadvantaged areas, particularly where availability is high. At the same time, the share of local electronic gambling machine revenue attributable to local residents declines as availability increases, although this decline is less pronounced in more disadvantaged areas, where local residents account for a substantially larger share of revenue than in less disadvantaged areas.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that higher electronic gambling machine availability and local socioeconomic disadvantage are associated with greater gambling losses among local residents, who also contribute a larger share of electronic gambling machine revenue in more disadvantaged areas. Given that monetary losses are a key risk factor for gambling harm, effective prevention requires the regulation of electronic gambling machine availability.

articles.title: Environmental Changes and Their Effect on the Airway Microbiome: Implications for Airway Diseases.
articles.abstract: Obstructive airway diseases, including asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), represent the two major chronic airway inflammatory diseases. In both conditions, the airways are exposed to a variety of microbial and environmental stimuli. A healthy airway microbiome is characterized not only by microbial diversity but also by the absence of significant quantities of pathogens, and is signified by ecological stability, functional resilience, and balanced interactions with the host immune system. Although microbial diversity is often considered a marker of respiratory health, its association with disease depends on the anatomical site, host factors, and environmental exposures. Thus, microbial diversity alone should not be used as a universal marker of airway health-the occurrence of pathogens and the organ compartment are also factors that are important to consider. Disruption of this microbial homeostasis, known as dysbiosis, may involve reduced diversity of the commensal flora as well as increased quantity of key pathogens, and this condition is believed to stimulate inflammation that is associated with the progression of asthma and COPD, including exacerbations. Environmental changes, including air pollution, climate change, and urbanization, can disrupt microbial balance by reducing diversity and increasing the prevalence of pathogens. Several mechanisms contribute to this interaction, including damage to the airway epithelium, impaired mucociliary clearance, oxidative stress, and alterations in innate and adaptive immune responses. This review examines the interplay between external environmental factors and the airway microbiome, and how they affect airway obstructive diseases, asthma, and COPD to understand their immunopathology, and to improve disease prevention and treatment approaches. This is an area of great interest, and further research is required to elucidate these interactions so we can better help our patients.

articles.title: Case report: Severe consequence of unnecessary retention of a TIVAD, phlegmasia cerulea dolens-A case for better stewardship.
articles.abstract: Totally implanted venous access devices (TIVADs) have been used for decades in cancer management. Traditionally placed in the chest wall, they can also be inserted in the upper arm using peripherally inserted central catheter methodologies (PICC-Ports), which are recognized as a safe and comfortable alternative. However, as with all vascular access devices, their safety profile depends on appropriate management, including timely removal. We report a case of Phlegmasia Cerulea Dolens (PCD)-critical venous ischemia-occurring a year after treatment completion due to a retained device. A 59-year-old breast cancer patient presented with arm edema ipsilateral to a PICC-Port, 1 year after chemotherapy had ended. Despite an initial "normal" duplex ultrasound (DUS), her condition worsened into full-blown PCD with cyanosis and loss of pulses. CT angiography revealed massive thrombosis, and standard anticoagulation failed, necessitating interventional radiology for subclavian stenting. While TIVADs are established as a safe method of chemotherapy administration, their safety remains contingent upon adherence to insertion protocols, timely removal, and knowledge of international guidelines. Leaving an inactive device for 12 months post-treatment represents a significant risk. Furthermore, a false-negative initial ultrasound led to a critical diagnostic delay, underscoring that strong clinical suspicion should sometimes override early negative imaging to prevent progression from deep vein thrombosis to PCD. Ultimately, "lost to follow-up" patients with retained TIVADs and non-compliance with international guidelines represent a major iatrogenic risk in cancer management.

articles.title: EBNEO Commentary: Are Gowns and Gloves Necessary for Routine Care of Neonates Colonised With Resistant Gram-Negative Bacteria?
articles.abstract: The BALTIC trial found that hand hygiene alone was noninferior to routine gowns and gloves combined with hand hygiene in preventing Gram-negative bloodstream infections in neonatal intensive care units, supporting reconsideration of extended barrier precautions in non-outbreak settings.

articles.title: Development and temporal validation of a machine learning-based model for predicting intraoperative hypothermia in patients undergoing robot-assisted urological tumor resection: A retrospective study.
articles.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
articles.abstract: BackgroundIntraoperative hypothermia (IOH) is prevalent in robotic urological surgery, yet existing prediction models, largely based on linear methods, may have limited capacity to capture complex non-linear risk patterns.ObjectiveTo develop and validate a preoperative machine learning model for predicting IOH to guide individualized thermal management.MethodsWe analyzed 787 patients (2022-2024) undergoing robot-assisted urological tumor resection. A CatBoost model was developed using 2022-2023 data with 5-fold nested cross-validation for robust feature selection. Independent temporal validation was conducted using 2024 data.ResultsThe model, utilizing 17 preoperative predictors, demonstrated temporal generalization with a temporal validation AUC of 0.877 and precise calibration (slope = 0.964). SHAP analysis highlighted markers of physiological stress and metabolic reserve as key drivers. Decision curve analysis confirmed positive net benefit across a broad probability threshold (10%-90%).ConclusionsThis robust machine learning tool accurately identifies high-risk phenotypes using only baseline characteristics. It enables clinicians to implement proactive, personalized warming strategies before anesthesia induction.

articles.title: Combined Heavy Metal Exposure and Metabolic Health: Epidemiological Evidence, Mechanistic Pathways, and Mixture Toxicology.
articles.abstract: Heavy metals in the environment are known pollutants whose relevance is increasingly being recognized due to their role in the global prevalence of metabolic diseases. In fact, people are usually exposed to mixtures of various metals, such as arsenic, cadmium, lead, mercury, and others, rather than single metal compounds, which happens due to pollution of the environment, occupation, and ingestion of foods and water that contain toxins. There is evidence that suggests that these metal exposures can be more dangerous than expected from studies of single exposures, as all of them act through the same mechanisms, such as oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial impairment, and disruption of endocrine balance. Thus, in this article, a systems biology approach will be utilized to understand the metabolic effects of heavy metal mixtures and assess associated risks. The combination of multiple metals is associated with more stress to the system when compared to the stress caused by exposure to a single metal. This is due to factors such as insulin resistance, toxic effect on the β cell, which secretes insulin, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes development risk. Multi-metal exposure does not only happen through different exposure routes but rather through molecular nodes common for regulating redox balance, mitochondria, inflammation, endocrine function, and epigenetics. The introduction of mixture modeling, biomarker profiling, and multi-omics approaches based on the exposome, understanding how multi-metal exposures influence coordinated metabolic disruption, will be enhanced. Metals in mixtures exhibit cumulative and interactive effects that traditional single-metal risk assessment models overlook, leading to an underestimation of metabolic risk. It is, therefore, necessary to shift towards risk frameworks based on mixtures that integrate state-of-the-art statistical modeling with exposomic and multi-omics platforms. The strategy would bolster preventive environmental health approaches and improve the identification of people with greater susceptibility to environment-driven metabolic disease.

articles.title: Next Steps for Cardiovascular Biomarkers: From Measurement to Clinical Decisions.
articles.journal: Biomarkers : biochemical indicators of exposure, response, and susceptibility to chemicals
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular biomarkers have transformed diagnosis and risk assessment, but outside of acute care their results rarely change treatment. This editorial argues that the next phase of biomarker research should focus on linking results to defined clinical actions. Guidelines now support natriuretic peptide and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin testing to identify pre-heart failure in adults with diabetes and other high-risk groups. However, trials are still needed to establish what a positive result should trigger, including whether specific drug classes, such as renin-angiotensin system inhibitors, offer greater benefit in biomarker-positive patients. Recent negative trials of therapies aimed at lowering lipoprotein(a) and interleukin-6 underscore the difference between using biomarkers to select patients and treating them as therapeutic targets. Dipeptidyl peptidase 3, developed in parallel with a neutralizing antibody being evaluated for treatment of shock, illustrates a model in which assay and therapy advance together. Progress will depend on validated thresholds, drug class trials, companion diagnostics, and reimbursement.

articles.title: Tirzepatide for the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea: from apnea-hypopnea index reduction to cardiometabolic risk mitigation-a narrative review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a chronic respiratory disorder with nocturnal oxygen desaturation that is often associated with multisystemic sequelae such as hypertension, cardiovascular diseases, and increased morbidity and mortality. Obesity has been proposed as a modifiable risk factor; hence, the recent shift in focus to investigating anti-obesity medications for the management of OSA. Tirzepatide is the first U.S. FDA-approved pharmacotherapy for the treatment of moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity to be utilized in combination with low caloric intake and physical activity, given its prior success in managing type 2 diabetes (T2D) and obesity.

METHODS: This narrative review evaluates tirzepatide and the SURMOUNT-OSA trial program as the key contemporary anchors for the pharmacological treatment of OSA in adults with concurrent obesity. Because the randomized evidence base currently comprises a single pivotal trial program, the review centers on SURMOUNT-OSA and its prespecified endpoints along with post hoc analyses, supplemented by observational, modeling, and mechanistic studies.

RESULTS: In the SURMOUNT-OSA program, tirzepatide produced randomized, placebo-controlled reductions in the apnea-hypopnea index, sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden, body weight, and systemic inflammation. The program was designed around respiratory and metabolic endpoints rather than clinical events, so it cannot support conclusions about mortality, cardiovascular, or renal outcomes. Favorable signals for those events, including all-cause mortality, major adverse kidney events, and major adverse cardiovascular events, come only from nonrandomized observational cohorts and are best regarded as directional and exploratory rather than definitive.

CONCLUSIONS: Tirzepatide may help frame OSA as a multifactorial and partially metabolically treatable disease and may represent a clinically meaningful expansion of treatment options alongside, rather than as a replacement for, established mechanical and procedural therapies. The available evidence is anchored in a single phase 3 trial program and limited by short follow-up and the absence of definitive comparative and long-term outcome data. Long-term durability of effect after discontinuation, generalizability beyond the SURMOUNT-OSA-eligible population, OSA-specific economic analysis, and head-to-head comparisons against CPAP remain the principal unsettled questions requiring dedicated long-term studies before firm clinical recommendations can be made.

articles.title: The molecular basis of GshT substrate binding reveals how Streptococcus pneumoniae acquires the antioxidant glutathione.
articles.abstract: Glutathione is synthesised across all kingdoms of life, but certain bacteria, including the major pathogen Streptococcus pneumoniae, import host glutathione instead. Glutathione import is known to involve the substrate-binding protein GshT, but the molecular basis underlying glutathione scavenging by pneumococcal GshT remains incompletely understood. We used isothermal titration calorimetry to demonstrate that pneumococcal GshT binds glutathione with low micromolar affinity. Thermal shift assays with glutathione derivatives demonstrated that two adequately spaced carboxylates in glutathione are essential for binding. Monitoring NMR chemical shift perturbations of mutated GshT variants upon glutathione addition revealed that two conserved positively charged residues lining the ligand-binding pocket determine the ability to bind glutathione. Mutagenesis of these residues in S. pneumoniae abolished GSH uptake, impaired growth and lowered oxidant tolerance. Together, our data demonstrate that a lock-and-key charge complementarity drives the GshT-glutathione interaction. Our findings provide insights into pathogen survival mechanisms that may inform strategies to combat infectious disease.

articles.title: Severe post-traumatic periocular infection associated with Lodderomyces elongisporus: a case report.
articles.abstract: We report the case of a 46-year-old man with a rapidly progressive post-traumatic periocular infection after falling into a puddle of water, with right temporoparietal wounds. He developed bilateral eyelid edema, periocular skin necrosis, crepitus, and inflammatory extension to the malar, temporal, and parietal regions, requiring admission to the intensive care unit, broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotic therapy, and multiple interventions for debridement and drainage of collections. Initial computed tomography showed extensive preseptal cellulitis without postseptal involvement. Methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus and Lodderomyces elongisporus were isolated from biopsy specimens of devitalized eyelid tissue on bacterial and fungal cultures, respectively. The clinical course was favorable after medical and surgical treatment, with discharge after 20 days, final visual acuity of 20/20 in both eyes, and no ophthalmic sequelae. This case highlights the importance of comprehensive microbiological investigation and a multidisciplinary approach in post-traumatic periocular infections with an atypical course.

articles.title: Association between iron deficiency Anemia and allergic conditions: A retrospective analysis.
articles.abstract: BackgroundIron deficiency anemia (IDA) is a prevalent nutritional deficiency linked to immune modulation and allergic conditions. This study investigates the association between IDA and allergic diseases, including atopic dermatitis, asthma, allergic rhinitis, food allergy, and allergic eosinophilia.ObjectiveTo evaluate the association between iron deficiency anemia (IDA) and the prevalence of allergic conditions, including atopic dermatitis, asthma, allergic rhinitis, food allergy, and allergic eosinophilia, using a large nationally representative dataset.MethodsA retrospective, cross-sectional design was employed using data from the National Inpatient Sample (2016-2020). Logistic regression models adjusted for confounders such as payer type, race, socioeconomic status, and hospital characteristics were used to assess associations.ResultsAmong 32,966,720 patients, 1,247,309 (3.8%) had IDA. After adjustment, IDA was significantly associated with increased odds of allergic conditions: atopic dermatitis (OR = 1.30), asthma (OR = 1.21), allergic rhinitis (OR = 1.21), food allergy (OR = 1.18), and allergic eosinophilia (OR = 1.24).ConclusionIDA was significantly associated with allergic conditions in this analysis, suggesting that iron status may represent a clinically relevant factor in patients with allergic diseases, as seen in this large national inpatient sample. Future longitudinal studies are needed to clarify causal pathways and develop targeted interventions. Addressing nutritional deficiencies may reduce the burden of allergic diseases and improve health outcomes.

articles.title: Causal inference analysis of the effect of amyloid-β and tau proteins on dementia risk: A Mendelian randomization analysis.
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe global burden of dementia is escalating due to the aging population. While amyloid and tau biomarkers are central to Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology, their causal roles across dementia subtypes are not fully understood.ObjectiveThis study investigated the causal effects of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and plasma amyloid, tau, and hyperphosphorylated tau (p-tau) proteins on dementia [AD, frontotemporal dementia (FTD), and vascular dementia (VaD)] risk.MethodsIn this study, we conducted a two-sample Mendelian randomization analysis using genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics. The AD, CSF, and plasma amyloid, tau, and p-tau data were obtained from the GWAS catalog, while those for FTD and VaD were obtained from the FINNGEN database. The inverse variance weighting method, combined with sensitivity analysis, was used to obtain the estimates.ResultsCSF p-tau in individuals with abnormal amyloid and APOE ε4 non-carriers was positively associated with AD risk [IVW: OR = 1.07, 95% CI = 1.01-1.13, p = 0.016; OR = 1.08, 95% CI = 1.02-1.14, p = 0.014, respectively]. CSF p-tau was also associated with VaD (IVW: OR = 1.11, 95% CI = 1.03-1.20, p = 0.008). Plasma Aβ1-42 reduced the odds of FTD (IVW: OR = 0.83, 95% CI = 0.70-0.98, p = 0.03), whereas CSF Aβ42 increased FTD risk (weighted median: OR = 1.58, 95% CI = 1.02-2.44, p = 0.041).ConclusionsThe findings support the causal roles of tau and amyloid across dementia subtypes, reinforcing the value of biomarker-driven prevention and therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio and clinical outcomes across the acute coronary syndrome trajectory: insights from the CardioMining Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inflammation contributes to plaque instability and adverse outcomes in acute coronary syndromes (ACS). The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) is an inexpensive inflammatory marker, but its prognostic value for in-hospital and postdischarge outcomes remains incompletely defined.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association of admission NLR with postdischarge mortality, in-hospital adverse events, and length of stay (LOS) in patients with ACS.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed adults with ACS in the CardioMining database (NCT05176769). Admission NLR was ln-transfor med and analyzed continuously and by quartiles. Associations with postdischarge all-cause mortality were assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models with sequential adjustment and restricted cubic spline analyses. Secondary outcomes were evaluated using logistic and linear regression. Discrimination was assessed with the C-index, and interactions by sex, age (<75 vs. ≥75 years), and ACS type were explored.

RESULTS: Among 4927 patients (mean age: 66.0 ± 13.4 years; 24.3% female), higher admission lnNLR independently predicted all-cause mortality [hazard ratio: 1.372, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.266-1.488; P < 0.001]. Mortality increased across lnNLR quartiles [Q2 adjusted hazard ratio (aHR): 1.225, Q3 aHR: 1.551, Q4 aHR: 1.831; all P < 0.05], with lower Kaplan-Meier survival at higher quartiles. Restricted cubic splines supported a predominantly linear relationship. Adding lnNLR improved discrimination (ΔC-index: +0.0096). Higher lnNLR was associated with in-hospital adverse events (adjusted odds ratio: 1.849, 95% CI 1.530-2.236; P < 0.001) and longer LOS (adjusted β: 0.129, 95% CI: 0.107-0.151; P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Admission NLR independently predicts mortality, in-hospital complications, and longer LOS in ACS, supporting early risk stratification.

articles.title: Isolation, Identification, and Whole Genome Sequencing Analysis of Common Foodborne Bacteria from Fresh Fruits, Vegetables, and Their Ready-to-Eat Products in Shijiazhuang, China.
articles.abstract: With evolving lifestyles, consumer demand for fresh fruits and vegetables has increased. However, these products are susceptible to contamination by foodborne bacteria from farm to table. To investigate the contamination status of foodborne bacteria in commercially available fresh fruits, vegetables, and their ready-to-eat (RTE) products in Shijiazhuang City, a total of 406 samples were collected from 2024 to 2025. Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus), Clostridium perfringens (C. perfringens), diarrheagenic Escherichia coli (diarrheagenic E. coli), and Salmonella were identified and analyzed for genomic characteristics using traditional biochemical tests and whole genome sequencing (WGS). The results showed that the detection rate of S. aureus was 4.68% (19/406), of which 5 isolates were identified as methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA), accounting for 1.23% (5/406). The detection rate of C. perfringens was 8.37% (34/406), and the detection rate of diarrheagenic E. coli was 0.25% (1/406). No Salmonella was detected. Genomic characterization revealed that S. aureus strains were predominantly ST59 and ST22, with the MRSA strains primarily identified as ST59-SCCmec-IVa (2B)-t437. A total of 20 enterotoxin genes were detected, with 94.74% (18/19) of the strains carrying at least one enterotoxin gene. The sea gene was the most prevalent (52.63%, 10/19), and the tsst-1 gene, which can cause toxic shock syndrome, was detected in 2 strains. C. perfringens isolates were divided into 30 STs, exhibiting high genetic diversity. All toxin types were classified as type A. The mprF gene showed the highest carriage rate of resistance genes (94.12%, 32/34), and the main resistance profile was mprF + cplR (55.88%, 19/34). The diarrheagenic E. coli isolate was identified as enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC) and carried multiple antimicrobial resistance genes. This study systematically reveals the contamination levels and molecular characteristics of common foodborne bacteria in fresh fruits, vegetables, and their RTE products sold in Shijiazhuang for the first time.

articles.title: Combination therapy with hypertonic saline and ulinastatin attenuates intestinal and kidney injury induced by trauma-hemorrhagic shock in rats.
articles.journal: Biotechnic & histochemistry : official publication of the Biological Stain Commission
articles.abstract: Trauma-hemorrhagic shock (HS) often leads to remote organ injury, particularly the gut and kidney. While fluid resuscitation is essential, optimal strategies to mitigate organ damage remain lacking. This study investigated the combined effects of hypertonic saline (HTS) and ulinastatin (UTI) on HS-induced intestinal and renal injuries. Male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomized into five groups: Sham, HS, HS+HTS, HS+UTI, and HS+HTS-UTI. A standardized HS model was used. Interventions were administered during resuscitation. Hemodynamics were monitored. At 24 h post-resuscitation, serum and tissues (ileum, kidney) were collected. Intestinal and renal injuries were assessed via histopathology, apoptosis (TUNEL), inflammation (ELISA for TNF-α, IL-6), oxidative stress (MDA, SOD), barrier function (FITC-dextran, tight junction proteins ZO-1/Occludin), and renal function/injury markers (creatinine, BUN, KIM-1, NGAL). HS induced severe hypotension, electrolyte disturbance, systemic inflammation, oxidative stress, and histopathological damage in the intestine and kidney, along with increased intestinal permeability, apoptosis, and renal dysfunction. Monotherapy with either HTS or UTI provided partial protection. However, the combination therapy demonstrated superior protective effects, which were significantly greater than either monotherapy alone. The HTS and UTI combination most effectively restored mean arterial pressure, suppressed systemic and tissue inflammation/oxidative stress, preserved intestinal morphology and barrier integrity, reduced intestinal and renal apoptosis, and ameliorated renal histology and function while downregulating KIM-1 and NGAL expression. The mechanism involves simultaneous mitigation of inflammation, oxidative stress, and apoptosis, along with preservation of intestinal barrier and renal tubular integrity.

articles.title: MaMi study: Perceptions of pregnancy and reproductive decision-making in women with migraine.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the influence of migraine on reproductive decision-making in women of childbearing age and to identify potentially modifiable beliefs that could guide preconception counseling in headache clinical practice.

BACKGROUND: Migraine is a highly prevalent neurological disorder that disproportionately affects women of childbearing age. Although pharmacological management during pregnancy has been widely addressed, less is known about how migraine shapes desire for motherhood, pregnancy planning, and family-related decisions.

METHODS: This observational, cross-sectional, multicenter study was conducted in six Spanish public hospitals. Women aged 18-49 years with episodic or chronic migraine were recruited by convenience during routine consultations between March 1 and November 30, 2023. Participants completed a structured questionnaire addressing reproductive decisions along with validated scales, including the Headache Impact Test-6 (HIT-6), the Migraine Disability Assessment Scale (MIDAS), and the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS). Descriptive statistics were used for data analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 162 women were included, with a median age of 36 years (interquartile range [IQR]: 31-41); 117 (72.2%) had episodic migraine and 45 (27.8%) had chronic migraine. Headache burden was high: the median HIT-6 score was 65 (IQR: 61-68), and 131/162 participants (80.9%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 74.1-86.2) were classified as having severe headache impact. Emotional symptoms were also frequent, with abnormal HADS-A scores in 84/162 participants (51.9%; 95% CI, 44.2-59.4) and abnormal HADS-D scores in 34/162 (21.0%; 95% CI, 15.4-27.9). Migraine influenced reproductive decisions in 49/162 women (30.2%; 95% CI, 23.7-37.7). The most common consequence was postponing pregnancy, reported by 38/161 participants (23.6%; 95% CI, 17.7-30.7), whereas 9/161 (5.6%; 95% CI, 3.0-10.3) had definitively decided against childbearing and 6/160 (3.8%; 95% CI, 1.7-7.9) had considered adoption. The main perceived barriers were reduced ability to care for children during migraine attacks (129/161; 80.1%; 95% CI, 73.3-85.6), fear of treatment-related teratogenic risks (97/161; 60.2%; 95% CI, 52.5-67.5), concern about migraine worsening during pregnancy (63/161; 39.1%; 95% CI, 31.9-46.8), and fear of transmitting migraine to offspring (117/161; 72.7%; 95% CI, 65.3-79.0).

CONCLUSION: Migraine affected reproductive decision-making in nearly one-third of women of childbearing age, most often by contributing to pregnancy postponement rather than definitive avoidance of motherhood. Concerns about childcare capacity, treatment safety, migraine worsening during pregnancy, and genetic transmission were highly prevalent. Some of these perceptions may not fully align with current evidence regarding migraine course during pregnancy or the safety of available treatments, suggesting that they represent potentially modifiable targets for clinical intervention.

articles.title: Physical Activity Associated With Early Independent Walking in Nonambulatory Patients With Subacute Stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Identifying the intensity and frequency of physical activity associated with early independent walking in nonambulatory patients with subacute stroke may inform daily physical activity promotion during hospitalization, which was the aim of the present study.

METHODS: This multicenter prospective cohort study was conducted at 11 facilities. Baseline was defined as admission to a subacute rehabilitation ward, with subacute referring to the phase after completion of acute stroke treatment. Patients with subacute stroke and a Functional Ambulation Category of 1 to 2 at admission were included. Physical activity was measured using an accelerometer for 1 week at baseline. The outcome was achievement of independent walking at 1 month from baseline (Functional Ambulation Category ≥4). To examine the intensity of physical activity associated with the outcome, modified Poisson regression was used to evaluate time spent in low -intensity physical activity (LPA; low-LPA, 1.6-1.9 metabolic equivalents [METs]), high-LPA (2.0-2.9 METs), and moderate-to-vigorous intensity physical activity (≥3.0 METs). Furthermore, to assess frequency associated with activity intensity, bouts of physical activity at or above the intensity level (≥1.6, ≥2.0, or ≥3.0 METs) were calculated as short-bouts (≥5 to <10 minutes) and long-bouts (≥10 minutes), and their associations with the outcome were examined.

RESULTS: Of 389 participants (mean age, 68.1 years; 45.0% female), 113 achieved independent walking during follow-up. Time spent in high-LPA was associated with independent walking when expressed per 5 min/d (risk ratio, 1.067 [95% CI, 1.010-1.131]), whereas low-LPA and moderate-to-vigorous intensity physical activity were not. The number of short-bouts at ≥2.0 METs was associated with independent walking (risk ratio, 1.208 [95% CI, 1.060-1.375]), whereas long-bouts were not relevant.

CONCLUSIONS: Accumulation of high-LPA and short-bouts at ≥2.0 METs was associated with early independent walking. These findings may help characterize activity intensity and bout frequency associated with walking independence in nonambulatory patients with subacute stroke during inpatient rehabilitation.
