articles.title: Comparative and Sex-Specific Assessment of Proteomics, Clinical, and Genomic Data on Visceral Adipose Tissue Volume Using Machine Learning in UK Biobank: Advancing Precision Medicine.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Visceral adiposity is a key driver of insulin resistance, which in turn is a strong risk factor for type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular diseases.

METHODS: We investigated the overall and sex-specific associations between plasma proteomics and visceral adipose tissue volume, and their intersection with clinical and genomic data to identify critical candidate proteins for visceral adiposity possibly linked to insulin resistance. We analyzed data from UK Biobank participants, using multistep machine learning to establish linear and nonlinear associations.

RESULTS: The combined model, integrating clinical, proteomic, and polygenic data, accounted for 67% of visceral adipose tissue variance. Our research revealed significant protein interactions with environmental factors and identified sex-specific proteins correlated with visceral adipose tissue variance in both males and females.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that a small number of plasma proteins explain a significant portion of the variance of visceral adipose tissue beyond nonproteomic measures, offering a potential single-source, personalized measurement of visceral adiposity that is easily accessible and may facilitate improved prediction and understanding of the biology of insulin resistance.

articles.title: The experiences of siblings in the congenital heart journey: a qualitative study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Despite growing interest in the quality of life of individuals with single-ventricle CHD, the experiences of their siblings remain largely underexamined and heavily reliant on parent-reported outcomes. This study explores the experiences of siblings of individuals with single-ventricle CHD through a qualitative analysis of self-reported narratives.

METHODS: Siblings of individuals with single-ventricle CHD aged 9 years and older participated in age-based Experience Group sessions. Trained facilitators used semi-structured, open-ended questions to prompt discussion. Qualitative data were coded using inductive thematic analysis to identify salient themes across narratives.

RESULTS: Eighteen siblings participated. Participants (50%, n = 9 female) ranged in age from 9 to 59 years (median age 22 years); most (72%, n = 13) were older than their sibling with single-ventricle CHD. Five themes emerged: 1) adapting to their sibling's physical limitations, 2) assuming supportive roles in the family, 3) navigating complex and often conflicting emotions, 4) deepening their understanding of the condition over time, and 5) finding normalcy throughout their childhood.

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides valuable insights into the nuanced experiences of siblings of individuals with single-ventricle CHD, underscoring the key roles they play in the care journey and describing the unique experiences that have shaped them. These findings can inform tailored, family-centred care models that intentionally include siblings in psychosocial assessment, support interventions, and age-appropriate medically related education and communication.

articles.title: People and bats in Fiji: perceptions and interactions.
articles.abstract: The management of wild bat populations often presents challenges in balancing the needs of biodiversity conservation and public health risks from zoonotic diseases. In Fiji, the most important recognized zoonotic infection is Leptospira, which was recently detected in wild bat populations. Five out of six species of Fijian bats are considered threatened to critically endangered on the IUCN Red List. This study investigates the perceptions of bats by people in Fiji and aims to identify and quantify the reported frequency and types of interactions between bats and people. In this mixed-methods study, 198 Fijian people were interviewed across the three main islands of Fiji: Viti Levu, Vanua Levu and Taveuni. Bats were generally perceived positively (63%, 125/198), mostly because they are perceived to be 'clean, healthy and tasty' meat sources (73%, 134/184). The majority of participants consume and come into contact with bats or with their urine, faeces, blood and saliva. Older adults, men and those who recognize that bats can cause harm are more likely to contact bats in Fiji. Quantifying these interactions and identifying other risk factors for bat exposure is an important step in targeting conservation efforts, community engagement and education, as well as determining at-risk groups for possible zoonotic pathogen exposure.

articles.title: Triterpenoid saponins from the aerial parts of Phytolacca americana and their anti-influenza A virus activity.
articles.abstract: Phytolacca americana L. (Phytolaccaceae), a perennial species native to North America, is rich in oleanane-type triterpenoid saponins. In this study, ultra-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC-QTOF-MS) profiling of the aerial-part extract revealed characteristic fragment ions of phytolaccagenin- and phytolaccagenic acid-type saponins with diverse glycosylation. MS-guided annotation enabled targeted isolation and structural elucidation of two previously undescribed compounds, one oleanane-type triterpenoid saponin (1) and one neolignan (3). Additionally, compound 2, which had been reported only based on mass spectrometric data, was isolated, and its structure was fully elucidated for the first time, together with those of 10 known oleanane-type triterpenoid saponins (4-13). Their structures were elucidated by comprehensive one-dimensional and two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopic analyses combined with UPLC-QTOF-MS data. Although P. americana extracts have been reported to inhibit influenza A virus infection in previous studies, the bioactive constituents responsible for this antiviral activity have not been identified. The crude extract and isolated saponins were evaluated using complementary in vitro assays. In H1N1-infected A549 cells, compound 11 (3-O-trisaccharide phytolaccagenic acid) reduced viral NS1 RNA levels at 6 and 24 hpi as determined by RT-qPCR. Antiviral activity was further confirmed by plaque reduction and immunoblot analyses, with a plaque-assay IC50 of 57.98 ± 0.26 µM.

articles.title: Design principles for natural SGLT2 modulators from multi-scale computation.
articles.abstract: Human sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (hSGLT2) is a membrane-embedded renal transporter and an established therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes. Hyperoside, myricetin, cyanidin-3-O-glucoside and isoliquiritigenin were investigated as a chemically diverse panel of natural scaffolds using a multi-scale computational workflow combining redocking-validated molecular docking, reconstruction of an unresolved transporter segment, molecular dynamics (MD) in an explicit POPC bilayer, molecular mechanics/Poisson-Boltzmann surface area (MM/PBSA) calculations, principal component and free-energy landscape analyses and density functional theory (DFT). The membrane simulations preserved the global hSGLT2 fold while revealing distinct ligand-dependent binding behaviours. Myricetin and cyanidin-3-O-glucoside exhibited limited positional deviations; hyperoside achieved persistent accommodation following an initial adjustment, whereas isoliquiritigenin underwent a marked late rearrangement. Ensemble-based energetic analysis prioritized cyanidin-3-O-glucoside, while hyperoside and myricetin formed an energetically comparable intermediate group and isoliquiritigenin displayed the least favourable profile. Electronic-structure analysis further characterized cyanidin-3-O-glucoside as the most responsive ligand within the DFT subset. Collectively, these findings indicate that glycone-assisted polar anchoring, aromatic complementarity and restricted conformational flexibility promote persistent hSGLT2 recognition. Direct hSGLT2 inhibition and hSGLT1 counter-screening assays remain necessary to establish potency and selectivity.

articles.title: Mycoplasma bovis and the North American bison: current knowledge, challenges, and future directions.
articles.abstract: The North American bison is a keystone species of immense ecological, cultural, and economic importance, yet its long-term stability is increasingly threatened by infectious diseases such as mycoplasmosis caused by Mycoplasma bovis. First recognized in bison in the late 1990s, this disease differs substantially from its presentation in cattle, where M. bovis typically acts as a secondary opportunist. In bison, however, it has emerged as a primary pathogen, causing severe morbidity and mortality within herds, imposing significant economic losses on producers, and jeopardizing conservation and restoration efforts. Despite its profound impact on herd health and sustainability, progress in understanding M. bovis infection in bison has been steady but limited. Major gaps persist in epidemiology, pathogenesis, diagnostic capacity, and effective control strategies. This review synthesizes the current state of knowledge on bison mycoplasmosis, drawing from peer-reviewed literature, government reports, and field management experiences. It addresses epidemiology, clinical and pathological features, diagnostic approaches, and current management strategies. Finally, it highlights key knowledge gaps and outlines future research priorities. The overarching goal is to provide a comprehensive, evidence-based resource for researchers, veterinarians, wildlife managers, producers, and policymakers, while underscoring the urgent need for targeted research to mitigate the threat of M. bovis to North American bison.

articles.title: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate in chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: the H-HeFT trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate (H-ISDN) has shown benefit in earlier randomized trials of patients with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and chronic heart failure. This trial tested if H-ISDN could reduce worsening heart failure or mortality in patients with chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) receiving contemporary treatment.

METHODS: The Hydralazine-Isosorbide Dinitrate in Patients With Chronic Heart Failure Trial (H-HeFT) was a multicentre, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in patients with HFrEF at 23 Danish hospitals (New York Heart Association class II-IV, elevated N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide and LVEF ≤40%). Target treatment was hydralazine 75 mg/isosorbide dinitrate 40 mg three times a day (t.i.d). The primary endpoint was a composite of hospitalization with worsening heart failure, an urgent outpatient visit resulting in intravenous/metolazone therapy for heart failure, heart transplantation, left ventricular assist device implantation, or death. Secondary endpoints included components of the primary outcome.

RESULTS: Overall, 592 predominantly White patients (median age 72 years, 18% women) were randomized with a mean follow-up of 3.7 years. The primary outcome occurred in 90 of 294 patients (30.6%) in the H-ISDN group and in 91 of 298 patients (30.5%) in the placebo group [hazard ratio (HR) 0.90; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.67-1.21; P = .48]. There were 57 deaths in the H-ISDN group vs 72 in the placebo group (HR 0.72; 95% CI 0.51-1.02); worsening heart failure events occurred in 52 vs 47 patients (HR 1.01; 95% CI 0.68-1.50).

CONCLUSIONS: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate did not change the incidence of the composite endpoint of heart failure events or death in patients with heart failure and LVEF ≤40%.

articles.title: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation vs surgical replacement in low-risk aortic stenosis: time-dependent late mortality in a pooled analysis of trials.
Metagenomic next-generation sequencing as an adjunctive diagnostic tool for Clonorchis sinensis infection: a case report.
articles.abstract: Clonorchis sinensis is a foodborne liver fluke. This case highlights acute cholangitis in a non-endemic area, where raw-fish history was initially absent and identified only after multidisciplinary team (MDT) discussion. Conventional tests were negative. A 53-year-old female had fever, epigastric pain, leukopenia, elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) and liver enzymes, and progressive eosinophilia (6.3% to 19.7%). Abdominal computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) showed cholangitis. Plasma and stool metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) detected C. sinensis (4 and 3375 reads), prompting stool microscopy that confirmed characteristic eggs. This complementary strategy enabled timely praziquantel, with resolution of fever and abdominal pain, declining eosinophilia, and improved liver function. She was discharged on day 16 and asymptomatic at 30-day follow-up. Clonorchiasis should be considered in eosinophilic cholangitis even in non-endemic areas; mNGS is a valuable complementary tool when conventional tests fail and presentations are atypical.

articles.title: Cerebral amyloid PET in obstructive sleep apnoea: a systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate cerebral amyloid-PET findings in adults with obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA), account for overlapping cohorts, and quantify global cortical amyloid burden where outcomes were commensurable. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to 17 July 2026 for adult human studies relating OSA or sleep-disordered breathing to cerebral amyloid PET. One estimate per independent data source was retained. The second author independently verified eligibility, cohort independence, extracted quantitative data, and risk-of-bias judgements for all reports entering any quantitative model. Global outcomes were pooled as Hedges' g using restricted maximum-likelihood random-effects models with modified Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals. Fifteen reports representing 12 independent data sources were included. Tracers, reference regions, partial-volume correction, OSA ascertainment, and cognitive status varied substantially. Three global-outcome cohorts of cognitively unimpaired participants (n = 291) yielded g = 0.42 (95% confidence interval, -0.14 to 0.99; I2 = 0%). In a secondary analysis, adding one cohort with established Alzheimer's disease yielded g = 0.54 (95% confidence interval, 0.22-0.86; n = 471; I2 = 0%). A sensitivity model adding one selected regional 11C-PiB estimate yielded g = 0.47 (95% confidence interval, 0.17-0.78). In a secondary analysis combining cognitively unimpaired adults and patients with established Alzheimer's disease, OSA was associated with higher global cerebral amyloid-PET burden. However, the primary evidence in cognitively unimpaired adults remains imprecise, and longitudinal studies do not consistently demonstrate an association between conventional OSA severity and amyloid accumulation.

articles.title: Decision-Making Under Uncertainty in Paramedic Students: A START Triage Perspective.
articles.journal: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study examined whether intolerance of uncertainty and decision-making styles were associated with theoretical START triage knowledge among paramedic students. Secondary exploratory analyses assessed psychosocial differences according to self-rated decision-making under stress, perceived coping with uncertainty, professional motivation, and challenges in prehospital emergency care.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 121 students from a First and Emergency Aid Program completed a self-administered paper-based questionnaire including a sociodemographic form, the Decision-Making Styles Scale, the Intolerance of Uncertainty Scale-12, and the START Triage Knowledge Test. Data were collected in classroom settings under researcher supervision between May and June 2025 and analyzed using descriptive statistics, group comparisons, and correlation analyses.

RESULTS: The mean theoretical START triage knowledge score was 69.99 ± 14.76. START knowledge was not significantly associated with intolerance of uncertainty or decision-making style subscale scores. Exploratory analyses identified associations between psychosocial scores and self-rated decision-making under stress, coping with uncertainty, professional motivation, and perceived challenges.

CONCLUSIONS: Theoretical START triage knowledge was not associated with intolerance of uncertainty or decision-making styles. Secondary findings were limited to self-reported psychosocial associations. The study assessed declarative knowledge and did not evaluate START application in simulated or field settings. Future studies should use simulation-based, scenario-based, or observational outcomes.

articles.title: Learning Constraints in Protein Evolution beyond Known Substitution Frequencies.
articles.abstract: During the evolution of protein sequences, amino acid substitutions follow broad patterns that are well established, such as those induced by the physico-chemical properties of residues or the position of sites along the sequence. While these deviations from random changes have been exploited for practical applications, such as to simulate protein evolution or to score protein alignments, they are too general to predict the precise evolution of individual protein sequences. To investigate whether protein sequences contain contextual information about their subsequent evolution beyond that captured by conventional substitution statistics and evolutionary conservation, we trained deep learning models based on an Evolutionary Scale Modelling (ESM2) encoder to predict the rate, the position and the nature of the amino-acid substitutions in the evolution of ancestral sequences and compared their performance to simpler and explainable heuristics. Our results show that predicting the rate of amino acid changes is achieved equally well by deep learning and by using evolutionary information in outgroup sequences. This suggests that the protein sequence does not contain information that significantly improves the predictions for this task. On the opposite, we show that deep learning models predict the position of these substitutions more accurately than statistics-based baselines. Predictions of the nature of substitutions largely outperform baselines, with over 37% accuracy overall. We observe that rapidly evolving sequences are harder to predict and substitutions preferentially occur between chemically similar amino acids. Interestingly, predictive information is predominantly contained within a local sequence context of 16 residues. These findings indicate that the nature of substitutions in protein evolution is partly governed by predictive rules that remain to be discovered through a more accurate modelling that could describe evolutionary trajectories based on sequence context alone.

articles.title: Going the Extra Mile for Stroke Thrombectomy Patients.
Neighbourhood deprivation in relation to psychiatric disorders among asthma patients: a nationwide cohort study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Although asthma is strongly associated with elevated psychiatric morbidity, the extent to which neighbourhood deprivation is associated with psychiatric disorder risk in this population remains insufficiently understood. This study aims to examine whether neighbourhood deprivation is associated with the incidence of psychiatric disorders among adults with asthma, and whether these associations vary by sex and psychiatric disorder subtype.

METHODS: Using nationwide Swedish registers (1997-2018), we identified 393,061 adults aged 25-64 years with asthma and followed them for incident psychiatric disorders. Neighbourhood deprivation was assessed at baseline and categorized into low, moderate and high levels. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and were stratified by sex and psychiatric disorder subtype.

RESULTS: During the follow-up period, 207,900 individuals (68,327 men and 139,573 women) developed psychiatric disorders. The incidence of psychiatric disorders increased progressively with higher levels of neighbourhood deprivation. In the fully adjusted models, compared with those living in low-deprivation areas, men in moderate and high deprivation areas had 11% (HR, 1.11; 95% CI, 1.08-1.13) and 31% (HR, 1.31; 95% CI, 1.27-1.35) higher hazards, respectively, while women had 10% (HR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.08-1.11) and 22% (HR, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.19-1.25) higher hazards. Disorder-specific analyses revealed particularly strong associations for developmental delay (HR = 2.82), pervasive developmental disorder (HR = 1.96), schizophrenia (HR = 1.79) and substance use disorder (HR = 1.71). Women consistently showed higher cumulative incidence than men across all deprivation levels.

CONCLUSIONS: Neighbourhood deprivation was associated with higher psychiatric morbidity among individuals with asthma. These findings suggest the importance of integrating respiratory and mental healthcare with structural interventions targeting socio-economic disadvantage to help reduce inequalities in psychiatric outcomes.

articles.title: Neural connectomes of verbal fluency in post-stroke aphasia.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Neuropsychological Society : JINS
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Verbal fluency tasks are widely used to assess language abilities and executive functions in both clinical and research settings. In post-stroke patients, prior research has indicated a significant hodological contribution to the neural basis of verbal fluency; however, this has largely been examined using lesion-based measures, predefined tractography approaches, and traditional diffusion metrics.

METHODS: Quantitative anisotropy-based structural connectometry derived from correlational tractography was employed to determine the white matter circuits underlying semantic and phonemic fluency in 44 patients with post-stroke aphasia.

RESULTS: Both task types were found to be linked to anterior frontal connections of left-hemisphere dorsal and ventral associative pathways, as well as domain-general projection pathways. However, visual inspection of the connectomes, supported by supplementary cross-control analyses, suggested differences in the relative emphasis and distribution of pathways, with phonemic fluency aligning more with the dorsal stream, while semantic fluency showed greater reliance on the ventral stream and a wider range of cortico-subcortical connections.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings contribute to current understanding of the neural networks of verbal fluency in aphasia, with potential relevance for clinical practice and research.

articles.title: Expanding NHSN CPT codes improves capture of pediatric cardiac procedures for surgical site infection surveillance.
articles.abstract: National Healthcare Safety Network cardiac Current Procedural Terminology codes incompletely capture Society of Thoracic Surgeons index procedures, especially in infants. Adding 62 pediatric codes increased validation-period sensitivity from 77.0% to 97.4%. Most additional captures were STS index procedures, although some non-index operations appeared potentially relevant to surgical site infection surveillance.

articles.title: The impact of CHG bathing on healthcare-associated bloodstream infections across a health system serving a predominantly rural population.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of daily chlorhexidine gluconate (CHG) bathing on healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) in patients in a large health system serving a predominantly rural population.

DESIGN: Multi-center, quasi-experimental, before-after study.

SETTING: 21 hospitals (including academic, community, and critical access) in a decentralized Appalachian healthcare system.

PATIENTS AND INTERVENTIONS: During August and September of 2023, we implemented daily CHG bathing for all patients (of at least two months of age) who had central lines and/or were admitted to an intensive care unit (ICU).

METHODS: We compared the hospital-level monthly incidences of two HAIs, central line-associated bloodstream infections (CLABSI) and laboratory-identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infection (MRSA-BSI), in the 18 months before and after the intervention, excluding a 2-month rollout period. We modeled the standardized infection ratio (SIR) using negative binomial generalized linear mixed effects models, incorporating each hospital's risk-adjusted predicted number of infections (from NHSN).

RESULTS: After implementation of daily CHG bathing, we observed significant reductions in bloodstream infections, with a 35% reduction in CLABSIs (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 0.650; 95% CI: 0.502-0.841) and a 40% reduction in MRSA bacteremia (IRR 0.599; 95% CI 0.408-0.880).

CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of daily CHG bathing for high-risk patients across a decentralized, Appalachian healthcare system was associated with reductions in CLABSI as well as MRSA bacteremia.

articles.title: Maternal Ascites as an Atypical Presentation of Severe Preeclampsia: A Case Report.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Preeclampsia is a multisystem hypertensive disorder of pregnancy associated with significant maternal and fetal morbidity. Although third spacing and fluid accumulation may occur in severe disease, maternal ascites is an uncommon manifestation. Recognition of this atypical presentation is important to facilitate timely diagnosis and appropriate management. CASE REPORT We present the case of a 23-year-old woman at 30 weeks and 2 days of gestation who developed severe preeclampsia superimposed on chronic hypertension, complicated by marked maternal third spacing and large-volume ascites while admitted for fetal growth restriction with intermittent absent end-diastolic flow on umbilical artery Doppler. Her clinical course was notable for profound capillary leak syndrome with significant fluid accumulation, including ascites (1.8 L) and pleural effusions. The extent of third spacing represented an unusual manifestation of severe hypertensive disease and created additional diagnostic and management considerations. Careful clinical assessment and recognition of the relationship between her fluid accumulation and severe preeclampsia were essential to guiding management and determining the need for delivery in the setting of maternal and fetal risk. CONCLUSIONS Severe preeclampsia may present with atypical manifestations beyond the classic features of hypertension and proteinuria. Profound capillary leak with marked third spacing, large-volume ascites, and pleural effusions can occur and may complicate the clinical evaluation of affected patients. Awareness of the uncommon presentation may facilitate earlier recognition of disease severity and prevent delays in management. In patients with severe hypertensive disease and unexplained fluid accumulation, preeclampsia should remain an important consideration. Prompt recognition of maternal or fetal deterioration and timely escalation of care are critical to optimizing outcomes and expediting delivery when clinically indicated.

articles.title: Remnant Cholesterol Inflammatory Index and its Association With Cardiometabolic Multimorbidity in Middle-Aged and Advanced-Aged Individuals: Evidence From the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND The association between remnant cholesterol inflammatory index (RCII) and cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) remains unclear. RCII is defined as: {Total Cholesterol - (High-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol + Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol)] × High-Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein/10}. This study examined the association between baseline RCII and CMM among middle-aged and older adults in China. MATERIAL AND METHODS This study analyzed data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), including 6173 participants. CMM was defined as the coexistence of at least 2 of 4 conditions: hypertension, diabetes, heart disease, or stroke. Participants were grouped according to the quartiles of natural log-transformed RCII (lnRCII) values. Modified Poisson regression models, restricted cubic splines, and receiver operating characteristic curves were used to examine the relationship between lnRCII and CMM outcomes. RESULTS In the cohort, 1832 cases of CMM occurred, and the incidence of CMM was highest in the lnRCII highest-quartile group (P<0.001). In the fully adjusted model, each unit of increase in lnRCII was associated with a higher risk of CMM (RR=1.13, 95% CI: 1.09-1.16), and participants in the highest quartile had a higher risk than those in the lowest quartile (RR=1.69, 95% CI: 1.50-1.90). The area under the curve for lnRCII was 0.607 (95% CI: 0.592-0.622), indicating modest discriminatory ability. CONCLUSIONS Higher baseline lnRCII was associated with an increased risk of incident CMM in middle-aged and older Chinese adults. Although RCII may capture combined information on remnant cholesterol and inflammation, its clinical predictive value requires further validation.

articles.title: Reactive Oxygen Species-Scavenging Nanozyme Hydrogel for Microenvironment Modulation in Diabetic Chronic Wound Healing.
articles.abstract: Diabetic chronic wounds are difficult to heal because persistent hyperglycemia is associated with excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), impaired angiogenesis, and prolonged inflammation. Here, we developed an Fe3O4@PDA-containing PVA/gelatin/borate hydrogel (FP-PVG) with catalase-like activity. FP-PVG scavenged ROS and promoted H2O2-responsive oxygen generation, while the FP nanocomposite and hydrogel matrix contributed to antibacterial activity. In vitro, FP-PVG showed strong ABTS radical-scavenging activity (98.97% at 2 mg mL-1), favorable cytocompatibility, and improved cell migration under oxidative stress. It also reduced CD86 expression and increased CD163 expression in macrophages, consistent with a shift toward a reparative phenotype. In a diabetic mouse wound model, FP-PVG accelerated wound closure and was associated with reduced oxidative stress and inflammation, increased angiogenesis, and improved tissue regeneration. These findings support FP-PVG as a multifunctional hydrogel dressing for regulating the diabetic wound microenvironment.

articles.title: Long-term Prognostic Value of Sequential Coronary CT Angiography and Quantitative PET in Suspected Chronic Coronary Syndromes: A Multicentre study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The long-term prognostic value of a guideline-recommended selective sequential anatomical-functional imaging strategy using coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) followed by quantitative [15O]H2O positron emission tomography (PET) remains uncertain. We evaluated its long-term prognostic value in patients with first symptoms suggestive of obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD).

METHODS: In this multicentre European cohort, symptomatic patients first underwent CCTA and were selectively referred to quantitative [15O]H2O PET in case of suspected obstructive stenosis (≥50%). Patients were stratified according to CCTA findings and PET-derived ischaemia (normal CCTA; non-obstructive CAD on CCTA; obstructive CAD on CCTA without ischaemia; obstructive CAD on CCTA with ischaemia). The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), and hospitalization for unstable angina (UA). Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) were calculated.

RESULTS: Among 3,918 patients (61.0±9.8 years; 54.3% female) with a median follow-up of 5.1 [3.8-8.0] years, 278 (7.1%) experienced the primary endpoint. aHRs increased stepwise across CCTA-PET categories. Compared to normal CCTA, non-obstructive CAD and obstructive CAD without ischaemia were associated with a higher risk of the combined primary endpoint (aHR 1.89, [95%CI: 1.23-2.91], p=0.004; aHR 3.20, [95%CI: 1.95-5.25], p<0.001). Among patients with obstructive CAD on CCTA, PET-derived ischaemia further increased the risk of the primary endpoint (aHR 1.55, [95%CI: 1.05-2.30]; p=0.029), but not when excluding UA from the composite endpoint (aHR 1.37, [95%CI 0.90-2.07]; p=0.141). PET-derived ischaemia primarily predicted events within the first year, while obstructive CCTA findings remained associated with long-term hard outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: A sequential strategy combining CCTA and quantitative [15O]H2O PET provides robust and incremental long-term risk stratification. While PET-derived ischaemia refines prediction of short-term and symptom-driven events, CCTA-derived CAD remains the principal determinant of long-term hard outcomes.

articles.title: Initial Emergency Department Concentrations of Serum Bicarbonate and Lactate Are Associated With Survival to Hospital Discharge in Children Following Submersion Injuries.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: There is a lack of objective measures to determine outcome and disposition following pediatric submersion injury. This study described a cohort of pediatric patients who presented to the emergency department (ED) after a submersion injury and the factors associated with survival to hospital discharge. In addition, the study examined the ability of 2 laboratory measures of acidemia, venous lactate and bicarbonate, to predict severity of injury and ED disposition following submersion.

METHODS: This cross-sectional cohort study evaluated consecutive pediatric submersion cases from February 2018 to November 2019 seen at Arnold Palmer Hospital for Children's Emergency Department, a tertiary care pediatric level 1 trauma center. Data collected were based on Utstein recommendations for submersion injury and included demographics, event information, vital signs, laboratory data, and hospital disposition. The main outcomes included survival to hospital discharge and hospital admission.

RESULTS: There were 208 patients with submersion injuries included in the analysis; 197 survived to hospital discharge, and 11 did not (5%). There were 135 (65%) patients admitted to the hospital, and 52 (25%) admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU). The average age of patients was 47 months, 67% were males, and bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) was performed on 66% of patients. Mean lactate levels were 4.8 mmol/L (95% CI: 4.3 to 5.4) in survivors and 12.9 (95% CI: 10.9 to 14.9) in nonsurvivors (P < 0.001), and mean venous bicarbonate levels were 19 mmol/L (95% CI: 19 to 20) and 11 (95% CI: 9 to 14), respectively (P < 0.001). Lactate levels were significantly and negatively correlated with venous bicarbonate [r = -0.69 (95% CI: -0.78 to -0.58)] and with pH on arterial blood gas [r = -0.81 (95% CI: -0.87 to -0.73)]. The area under the curve for lactate predicting mortality from submersion was 0.97 (95% CI: 0.95 to 1.00) and for predicting admission to the hospital was 0.77 (95% CI: 0.67 to 0.88). The area under the curve for venous bicarbonate predicting mortality was 0.93 (95% CI: 0.87 to 1.00) and for predicting admission 0.69 (95% CI: 0.56 to 0.83).

CONCLUSION: Elevations in venous bicarbonate and lactate levels measured in the pediatric ED were significantly associated with severity of submersion injury as measured by survival to hospital discharge and hospital admission. Both correlated with arterial pH levels. Prospective studies should evaluate the utility of using these objective measures to determine hospital disposition in these children.

articles.title: Sex-based differences in the atrial fibrillation care pathway and outcomes: an ITHACA-database analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To characterize sex-specific differences in clinical presentation, evaluate progression through the atrial fibrillation (AF) care pathway from diagnosis to catheter ablation (CA) and assess long-term outcomes.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This was a retrospective cohort study of patients with incident AF at Northwell Health between 2015 and 2024 from the ITHACA-database. Sex-specific differences in clinical presentation were examined. The AF care pathway was operationalized as a stepwise cascade, modelling conditional drop-off to identify care gaps. Sex-specific CA risk ratios were assessed via Poisson regression. Incident AF was identified among 165 563/655 459 patients (71.4 ± 11.6 years, 32% non-white, 45% female) with a recorded diagnosis of AF. Women were older (73.3 ± 10.6 vs. 69.8 ± 12.1 years, P < 0.001), had higher rates of dementia (9.1% vs. 5.2%), stroke (8.6% vs. 7.4%) and congestive heart failure (21.5% vs. 20.8%) at diagnosis. Transfer-of-care gaps [median 3.6 years follow-up, 96% retention] were identified at every level: 31.5% of women vs. 35.3% of men were evaluated by cardiology, 16.2% vs. 21.6% by electrophysiology, and 3.5% vs. 5.7% underwent CA (all P < 0.001). Women were 16% less likely to receive CA (RR 0.84 95% CI 0.77-0.91). In cause-specific Cox models, female sex was associated with incident stroke (aHR 1.24, 95% CI 1.18-1.30) and dementia (aHR 1.30, 95% CI 1.24-1.35), but modestly lower mortality after adjustment (aHR 0.96, 95% CI 0.94-0.99).

CONCLUSION: In this real-world analysis, significant sex-specific differences in clinical phenotype at presentation, progression through the AF care pathway and clinical outcomes were observed.

articles.title: Beyond Ejection Fraction: Integrating Etiology into Future Heart Failure Classification.
When cold-bloods heat up: meta-analytical evidence that climatic variability mediates behavioural fever in amphibians and reptiles.
articles.abstract: Fever is an adaptive defence response that enhances immune performance by elevating body temperature above normal values. In ectotherms, fever is expressed behaviourally through the selection of warmer microhabitats following infection, yet its magnitude and determinants vary widely across species and environments. We performed a phylogenetically informed meta-analysis to test whether behavioural fever expression is shaped by climatic thermal variability, pathogen identity and taxonomy in amphibians and reptiles. We predicted that species from thermally variable environments would exhibit stronger behavioural fever than those from stable environments and reptiles would exhibit stronger fever responses than amphibians owing to lower hydrothermal constraints. Across 47 studies encompassing 101 effect sizes, behavioural fever emerged as a widespread but context-dependent response. Behavioural fever was strongest in species from thermally variable habitats, suggesting that thermal opportunity and behavioural plasticity mediate the expression of fever. Contrary to our prediction, amphibians exhibited stronger fever responses than reptiles, possibly reflecting differences in thermoregulatory biology, environmental opportunity or methodological artefacts. Bacterial infections elicited larger body temperature increases than fungal or viral challenges. Our findings demonstrate that temperature is not a background condition for host-pathogen interactions, but an active and environmentally contingent component of immune defence in ectothermic tetrapods.

articles.title: Too threatened to try: how extinction risk drives research neglect in rays and skates.
articles.abstract: Global biodiversity loss demands that research effort be directed towards species most at risk. Yet conservation science is biased by species' accessibility and perceived charisma, raising concerns that threatened species may be overlooked. We apply a structured causal modelling framework to 651 species of rays (superorder Batoidea), a highly threatened yet understudied lineage of cartilaginous fishes, to disentangle the drivers of research effort. We quantify the causal effects of taxonomy, extinction risk, accessibility (range size, depth, economic context, year of description) and charisma (body size, shape, patterning and colouration) on species-level research outputs from more than 7000 publications. Research effort was strongly taxonomically biased, driven by accessibility and charisma, with shallow depth, broad geographic ranges, large body size and distinctive morphologies attracting disproportionate attention. Extinction risk exerted a counterintuitive nonlinear effect: Critically Endangered and Endangered species received significantly fewer publications than Near Threatened and Vulnerable species and were comparable to Data Deficient species. This effect is consistent with a 'Goldilocks' zone in which species are threatened enough to justify research but not so threatened that it becomes prohibitively challenging. Systematic research bias away from the species most in need undermines conservation efforts. Realigning research priorities is essential to combating the biodiversity crisis.

articles.title: Middle Lobe Displacement Post Lobectomy in a Child With Congenital Pulmonary Airway Malformation.
articles.abstract: Congenital pulmonary airway malformations (CPAMs) are an important cause of structural lung disease in children and may remain undetected until later childhood. Although surgical resection is well established for symptomatic lesions, the long-term anatomical effects of lobectomy in pediatric patients remain incompletely understood. Postoperative changes in lung mechanics and lobar positioning can result in uncommon airway complications that are often under-recognized and diagnostically challenging. Obstruction of the right middle lobe (RML) bronchus due to postoperative lobar displacement is particularly rare, with reported cases originating from the adult surgical literature. We report a 9-year-old girl with mild persistent asthma who presented with an infected cystic lesion in the right upper lobe consistent with CPAM. She completed antimicrobial therapy and underwent right upper lobectomy, with pathology confirming type 1 CPAM. One month later, she developed a persistent cough refractory to optimized asthma treatment. Chest computed tomography (CT) demonstrated hyperinflation and poor visualization of the right upper and middle lobe bronchial orifices. Bronchoscopy identified RML bronchial obstruction, and fluoroscopy-guided bronchoscopy confirmed superior displacement of the RML with resultant bronchial kinking, likely related to postoperative lobar migration. Endobronchial stenting was unsuccessful, and further surgical intervention was not advised because of the anticipated risks of a second operation. Conservative management was pursued, resulting in modest symptomatic improvement, with the patient remaining clinically stable for 2 years. This case highlights a rare postoperative complication of CPAM resection in a child and emphasizes the need for heightened awareness, multidisciplinary evaluation, and pediatric-focused studies to guide management.

articles.title: The return of neuropsychiatry: why clinical neuroscience needs neurology and psychiatry reunited.
Complications in Pediatric Cancer Patients With Staphylococcus aureus Bloodstream Infection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infections (BSIs) can cause significant morbidity in children with cancer. Current guidelines recommend central venous catheter (CVC) removal, though the necessity remains uncertain. We assessed risk factors for complications among affected patients, focusing on impact of CVC removal vs salvage.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study includes pediatric oncology patients with S aureus BSIs from 2005 to 2022. The complication outcome period (72 hours to 6 months after initial positive culture) was divided into short-term (72 hours to 8 days) and late periods (8 days to 6 months). The composite primary outcome included occurrence of at least 1 major complication: recurrent BSIs, deep abscess/myositis, S aureus-related death, exit site infection, meningitis, endocarditis, or osteomyelitis. Multivariable logistic regression with propensity score weighting for CVC removal was performed.

RESULTS: Among 322 BSI episodes, 90.7% (n = 292/322) had a CVC at presentation; salvage was attempted in 55.5% (n = 162/292). The primary outcome was met in 21.2% (n = 62/292) of episodes with a CVC, more frequently in the CVC salvage (25.3%, n = 41/161) vs removal (16.2%, n = 21/130) group. CVC salvage was independently associated with the primary outcome (OR, 3.37; 95% CI, 2.08-5.61; P < .01) in short-term (OR, 21.8; 95% CI, 7.09-95.4) and late (OR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.06-3.18) periods. Methicillin resistance, male sex, invasive infection at presentation, implanted ports, sepsis, and persistent blood culture positivity were also independently associated with the primary outcome.

CONCLUSIONS: CVC removal was associated with fewer short-term and late complications in pediatric cancer patients with S aureus BSIs, supporting recommendations for catheter removal in this population.

articles.title: Incorporating authority perception, economic status and behavioural response in infectious disease control.
articles.journal: Journal of the Royal Society, Interface
articles.abstract: We introduce a multi-population mean field game framework to examine how economic status and authority perception shape vaccination and social distancing decisions under different epidemic control policies. We conducted a survey to inform our model and stratify the population into six groups by income and perception of authority, capturing behavioural heterogeneity. Individuals choose socialization and vaccination levels to optimize objectives such as minimizing treatment costs, complying with social distancing guidelines if they are authority-followers, or reducing losses from decreased social interactions if they are authority-indifferents, alongside economic costs. Public health authorities influence behaviour through social distancing guidelines and vaccination costs. We characterize the Nash equilibrium via a forward-backward differential equation system, provide its mathematical analysis and numerically solve it. Our findings reveal a trade-off between social distancing and vaccination. Under stricter guidelines that target both susceptible and infected individuals, followers reduce both socialization and vaccination levels, while indifferents increase socialization owing to followers' preventative measures. Adaptive guidelines targeting infected individuals effectively reduce infections and narrow the gap between low- and high-income groups, while lower vaccination costs incentivize vaccination among low-income groups. Trust-building remains critical in epidemic mitigation, underscoring the importance of data-informed, game-theoretical models for understanding complex human responses to mitigation policies.

articles.title: Pathogen-specific positron emission tomography for Enterobacterales bone infection.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Gram-negative bone infections involving Enterobacterales group of bacteria pose a growing concern, especially for orthopaedic surgeries and diabetic ulcers. Current imaging methods either identify morphological changes by CT and MRI, or inflammation, using white blood cell scans or 2-deoxy-2-[18F]fluoro-d-glucose ([18F]-FDG) positron emission tomography (PET). While valuable, these are not specific, resulting in delayed diagnoses. PET/CT using 2-deoxy-2-[18F]fluoro-d-sorbitol ([18F]-FDS) is a novel method for detecting living Enterobacterales bacteria in vivo, via a conserved sorbitol-specific bacterial pathway. In this study, we aim to evaluate [18F]-FDS PET/CT for detection and monitoring of Enterobacterales bone infection in a mouse model.

METHODS: We adapted a murine model of Gram-positive implant-associated spine infection to a Gram-negative infection model. We compared microbiological techniques to imaging with [18F]-FDG and [18F]-FDS. We determined the standardized uptake value (SUV) ratios for detection of bacterial infection and response to therapy, in 48 mice with surgical implants infected with either Escherichia coli or Staphylococcus aureus and compared them to controls with surgical implants but no infection.

RESULTS: Both bacteria induced substantial bone pathology with reduced bone density. [18F]-FDS PET could specifically detect implant-associated spinal infections due to E. coli with a mean SUV ratio of 2.2 (SD 1.3), which was substantially lower in S. aureus (0.7 (SD 0.2); p = 0.002) and uninfected mice (1.0 (SD 0.1)). In contrast, [18F]-FDG could not differentiate between the two bacterial infections or the control (p = 0.497). Finally, [18F]-FDS PET could determine antibiotic efficacy, and monitor infection over time.

CONCLUSION: We demonstrate that [18F]-FDS affords a highly accurate and clinically translatable detection of Enterobacterales bone infection. This novel modality offers a rapid and specific method to diagnose and monitor bone infections, inform medical decisions, reduce the need for surgery, and limit unnecessary antibiotic use. Similar approaches may be implemented to develop tracers for other bacteria.

articles.title: Dynamic GelMA/Oxidized Hyaluronic Acid Hydrogels Enable Acid-Accelerated Localized Delivery of Photothermal Melatonin-Derived Carbon Dots for Infected Bone Repair.
articles.abstract: Infected bone defects remain difficult to reconstruct because bacterial persistence, acidic stress, excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), inflammatory dysregulation, and impaired osteogenesis reinforce one another. Here, sulfur-doped melatonin carbon dots (DM-CDs) were synthesized from melatonin and d-cysteine and immobilized within a gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA)/oxidized hyaluronic acid hydrogel (GH-DM) through dynamic Schiff-base interactions. Sulfur-containing surface states endowed DM-CDs with strong 808 nm absorption, an approximately 50% photothermal conversion efficiency, stable heating cycles, and NIR-amplified antibacterial activity. The melatonin-derived surface simultaneously scavenged ROS, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, and was associated with increased Nrf2 and Sirt1 transcript levels together with recovery of CAT and SOD activities in mouse bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). Under acidic conditions, dynamic imine interactions were associated with modestly accelerated DM-CD release, whereas NIR irradiation provided an external means to amplify local heating and antibacterial performance. GH-DM reduced planktonic bacterial viability and biofilm biomass, decreased cell-associated Staphylococcus aureus signals, and enhanced BMSC osteogenic differentiation, as shown by ALP activity, matrix mineralization, and increased RUNX2, ALP, COL1, and OCN expression. Mouse BMSC RNA sequencing revealed enrichment of collagen-containing extracellular-matrix programs and attenuation of NF-κB, IL-1β, IL-6, and osteoclast-differentiation-related signatures. Separate LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 experiments supported attenuation of a pro-inflammatory state and increased IL-10 expression. In infected femoral defects, GH-DM plus NIR markedly reduced bacterial burden and improved trabecular regeneration, with no detectable major-organ histopathology or abnormalities in the measured hematological, hepatic, and renal indices. These findings support a locally delivered carbon-dot hydrogel with acid-accelerated release that coordinates infection control, redox protection, inflammatory regulation, and bone regeneration.

articles.title: Current findings, application, and diagnosis of magnetic resonance imaging in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
articles.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a heterogeneous neurodegenerative disorder within the motor neuron disease (MND) spectrum, characterized by progressive degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons. The clinical phenotype ranges from pure motor syndromes to forms with cognitive and behavioral impairment, and the pathological burden extends beyond the motor system. Diagnosis remains primarily clinical, supported by electrophysiology and exclusion of mimics. Therefore, objective imaging biomarkers are urgently needed. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is widely used as an auxiliary and differential diagnostic tool in ALS. T1- and T2-weighted imaging can assess cortical thickness, gray matter atrophy, and signal changes. Diffusion tensor imaging probes white matter microstructure. Magnetic resonance spectroscopy detects neurochemical alterations. Resting-state functional MRI assesses functional connectivity and network organization. Susceptibility-weighted imaging is sensitive to iron and calcium deposition. Ultra-high-field MRI provides higher resolution and improved metabolite quantification. This critical review summarizes current findings on MRI in ALS, but importantly organizes the evidence by the specific question being addressed: pathological/histological correlates, diagnostic or discriminatory performance, and clinical associations with phenotype, severity, progression, and prognosis. We also discuss major limitations, including methodological heterogeneity, limited standardization, small and clinically heterogeneous cohorts, frequent use of healthy rather than disease controls, and scarce multicenter validation. Although advanced MRI has revealed robust group-level alterations, none of these techniques has yet become established in routine clinical diagnosis of ALS. We, therefore, distinguish promising research findings from validated clinical biomarkers and outline priorities for future translation.

articles.title: Bexagliflozin: pharmacological profile and clinical applications of a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor.
articles.journal: Journal of basic and clinical physiology and pharmacology
articles.abstract: Bexagliflozin, approved in the United States in 2023, is the fifth selective sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Unlike other class members, it lacks an event-driven cardiovascular outcomes trial (CVOT) and trials with hard kidney or heart failure endpoints. This narrative mini-review separates bexagliflozin-specific evidence from class benefits. PubMed and Google Scholar were searched for English-language articles (January 2009-June 2026) using "bexagliflozin," "Brenzavvy," and "SGLT2 inhibitor," plus prescribing information and pivotal class trials. Randomized trials and meta-analyses were prioritized. Bexagliflozin reduced glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), body weight, and systolic blood pressure vs. placebo and was noninferior to sitagliptin, glimepiride, and, in one 24-week trial, dapagliflozin for HbA1c. In stage 3a/3b chronic kidney disease, it reduced albuminuria by 20.1 % vs. placebo, a surrogate finding. A cardiovascular safety trial and meta-analysis excluded excess cardiovascular risk but were not powered for benefit. Adverse events were consistent with the class. Bexagliflozin is an effective glucose-lowering drug, but its cardiovascular, kidney, and heart failure benefits remain unproven and cannot be assumed from class data. Outcome-proven agents are preferred for cardiorenal protection. An adequately powered CVOT and hard kidney endpoint trials are the key research priorities.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics of paediatric-onset type 2 diabetes: a comparison by weight status in the Hong Kong childhood diabetes registry 2008 to 2023.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Although obesity is a major risk factor for paediatric type 2 diabetes (T2DM), many Asian youths present without obesity. This phenotype remains under-recognised and poorly described. This study aimed to compare the clinical and metabolic characteristics of children newly diagnosed with T2DM, stratified by weight status, in Hong Kong.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study using data from the Hong Kong Childhood Diabetes Registry (2008-2023). We compared the clinical and metabolic features of children with and without obesity who were newly diagnosed with T2DM.

RESULTS: A total of 689 children (96 % Chinese) were included and 35 % were children without obesity. While age at diagnosis was similar between groups, children without obesity exhibited a higher prevalence of family history of T2DM (80.6 % vs. 67.5 %; p<0.0001), more frequent presentations of classical symptoms and diabetic ketoacidosis with or without hyperosmolar hyperglycaemia state (4.6 % vs. 1.6 %, p=0.0262), and higher HbA1c and blood glucose levels at diagnosis, with lower HOMA-%B, suggesting greater β-cell dysfunction. Conversely children with obesity had higher insulin resistance. They also had higher prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), hypertension, hyperuricaemia, obstructive sleep apnoea, and polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Insulin therapy was more frequently required at diagnosis in children without obesity (16.3 % vs. 8 %, p=0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: These results highlight a distinct T2DM phenotype in Chinese children without obesity, marked by severe hyperglycaemia and a higher rate of insulin requirement at diagnosis. Increased clinical vigilance for this under-recognised group is warranted to optimise management at diagnosis, with long term outcomes to be address in future longitudinal studies.

articles.title: Sellar spine in children and young adults: clinical presentation, imaging characteristics, and pituitary outcomes.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The true clinical relevance of a sellar spine remains unclear because of limited available data. We aimed to describe the presentation and associated pituitary dysfunction among children and young adults with a sellar spine.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients with a sellar spine found on brain imaging obtained in individuals less than 25 years of age. Extracted variables included age at initial brain imaging, indication for imaging, and pituitary dysfunction status and type.

RESULTS: Eleven patients were included. Age at initial identification of a sellar spine ranged from 6 to 24 years. Indications for neuroimaging included headaches (n=3), seizures (n=2), precocious puberty (n=1), severe obesity with advanced bone age (n=1), suspected stroke/ataxia (n=1), nasal polyp evaluation (n=1), hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and secondary hypothyroidism (n=1), and as part of screening testing for Von Hipple Lindau (n=1). Pituitary stalk deviation was found in 7 patients (63.6 %). Pituitary gland distorted morphology leading to a misdiagnosis of pituitary adenoma found in 2 patients (18.2 %). Among younger children (n=5; age ≤9 years), precocious puberty occurred in one patient who demonstrated pituitary stalk deviation with an AP size-to-sella ratio of 0.5. Another child with stalk deviation did not develop precocious puberty. Pituitary hormone deficiency was identified in one patient (hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and hypothyroidism) with stalk deviation and AP size-to-sella ratio of 0.63.

CONCLUSIONS: The presence of a sellar spine can distort pituitary anatomy and result in diagnostic misclassification. Endocrinopathies may develop in some affected patients. Further, larger studies are warranted to better define the characteristics of sellar spine leading to endocrinopathies.

articles.title: Risk stratification of severe infections after remission induction therapy in idiopathic inflammatory myopathy: a multicentre MYKO study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To identify baseline predictors and develop a clinical risk stratification model for severe infections (SIs) in patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathy (IIM) after remission induction therapy.

METHODS: We enrolled patients diagnosed with IIM between 1991 and 2024 from three Japanese centres participating in the multicentre Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathy and Anti-synthetase Syndrome (MYKO) cohort. SI was defined as an infection requiring i.v. antibiotics or hospitalization. We explored the risk factors for predicting SI in patients with IIM by comparing the initial demographic, clinical, laboratory and treatments between the SI and non-SI groups.

RESULTS: Among 349 patients with IIM, 14.6% of patients developed SIs after remission induction therapy over a median follow-up of 4.7 years. Patients who developed SI exhibited significantly lower baseline albumin levels, and significantly higher baseline CRP, lactate dehydrogenase and surfactant protein (SP-D) levels than those without SI. Multivariate logistic regression analysis demonstrated that elevated CRP and SP-D levels were independently associated with SI. Serum CRP levels remained significantly higher in the SI group than in the non-SI group over the 2-year period after immunosuppressive therapy, and the serum SP-D levels tended to be higher in the SI group. The 10-year SI rate was significantly different among patients with IIM stratified by the number of risk factors, defined as CRP ≥ 0.8 mg/dl and SP-D ≥ 96.2 ng/ml.

CONCLUSIONS: This model, which consists of CRP ≥ 0.8 mg/dl, SP-D ≥ 96.2 ng/ml, is useful for clinical risk stratification of SI after remission induction therapy in IIM.

articles.title: Conductive and sensorineural hearing impairment in juvenile idiopathic arthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the prevalence of ossicular stiffness and cochlear dysfunction in patients with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) compared with healthy controls.

METHODS: We searched PubMed (1966-27 December 2025), Embase (1947-27 December 2025) and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (1996-27 December 2025). Studies of patients diagnosed with JIA who underwent audiological examinations (cochlear and middle ear function) were selected for the review. Random-effects models were used to calculate pooled risk ratios (RRs) and standardized mean differences (SMD).

RESULTS: Seven studies (237 patients with JIA; 132 healthy controls) were included; six were judged high methodological quality (Newcastle-Ottawa score ≥ 8). Children with JIA exhibited a markedly higher prevalence of type As tympanograms (RR = 13.93, 95% CI 5.83-33.27) and elevated pure-tone hearing thresholds, with the largest effect observed at the extended high frequency of 16 kHz (SMD = 1.52, 95% CI 1.04-1.99). Pooled otoacoustic emission amplitudes trended lower in JIA but did not reach statistical significance (SMD = -1.72, 95% CI -8.77-5.33; I2 = 96%), although the single study reporting distortion-product otoacoustic emissions (DPOAE) suggested a marked reduction.

CONCLUSION: JIA is associated with a quantifiable dual-compartment audiological burden-a markedly elevated risk of mechanical middle-ear stiffness and a frequency-dependent sensorineural deficit most pronounced beyond the conventional audiometric range. Tympanometry and extended high-frequency audiometry may provide complementary information for detecting subclinical auditory involvement in JIA. The potential role of OAEs, including DPOAE, requires confirmation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Open-source, high-speed and high-resolution data acquisition platform for biopotential recordings and neural EIT applications.
articles.abstract: Objective.Biopotential measurement devices, such as electroencephalography, electrocardiography (ECG), and electromyography (EMG) recorders, are available in low-cost, open-source implementations with standard specifications. However, high-end systems remain expensive and predominantly proprietary, limiting accessibility and customization by research laboratories. In addition, neurophysiology techniques such as bioimpedance-based fast neural electrical impedance tomography (FN-EIT) also rely on these systems for data acquisition. This work aimed to develop an open-source biopotential recording system using off-the-shelf components that achieves performance comparable to high-end devices.Approach.We designed our system to provide simultaneous sampling over 32 channels, 24-bit resolution, 10 kHz bandwidth, 50 kHz sampling rate, and battery-powered operation while reducing cost by two orders of magnitude. System performance was evaluated comparatively against a reference device. Initial validation involved benchtop recordings in saline solution and standard non-invasive biopotential measurements (ECG and EMG). Furtherin-vivovalidation was performed by recording evoked electrophysiological responses and FN-EIT traces from the sciatic nerve of a rat during tibial branch stimulation.Main results.EMG recordings showed comparable RMS peak amplitudes (814 ± 153µV vs 897 ± 113µV,p= 0.07), while ECG-derived heart rates closely matched between systems (64.8 ± 4.0 bpm vs 65.1 ± 3.1 bpm,p= 0.54). Duringin-vivorecordings, compound action potentials exhibited comparable amplitudes and morphology (129 ± 26 mV vs 128 ± 25 mV,P= 0.15). FN-EIT recordings showed strongly correlated baseline voltages (R> 0.93,P= 0.11), sub-microvolt noise levels (0.83 ± 0.36µV vs 0.42 ± 0.25µV,p< 0.05), and comparable impedance variations (0.006 ± 0.002% vs 0.005 ± 0.003,P> 0.05). FN-EIT images of functional activity recorded with the novel device closely matched reference ones, exhibiting a 98.5% overlap in activated area.Significance.The proposed open-source device has the potential to broaden research access to customizable, high-specification data acquisition hardware and facilitate wider adoption of specialized neural recording techniques such as FN-EIT.

articles.title: A Geometrically Tunable Cardiovascular Shunt for the Individualized Care of Neonates with Congenital Heart Defects.
articles.abstract: Congenital heart defects (CHDs), particularly single-ventricle anomalies such as hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS), require early surgical intervention using fixed-diameter vascular shunts. However, current shunts are incapable of adapting to the physiological changes of infant growth, often leading to hemodynamic imbalance and elevated mortality risk. Here, we report a geometrically tunable cardiovascular shunt lined with a photoresponsive hydrogel based on methacrylated dextran (DexMA) and dithiothreitol (DTT). This dual-stage crosslinked hydrogel system enables minimally invasive modulation of the inner lumen diameter in response to external blue light. We optimized the hydrogel composition to achieve both mechanical robustness (Young's modulus ≈ 8.5 kPa) and light-induced deswelling, allowing for lumen expansion up to 39% with high stability over one month. In vitro studies confirmed excellent cytocompatibility, hemocompatibility, and minimal immune activation. Prototype annular shunts demonstrated precise, programmable diameter increases (15-18%) corresponding to computational models of infant growth. This dynamic, photoresponsive platform is a critical advance toward implantable materials for personalized cardiovascular interventions and a significant step toward growth-accommodating pediatric medical devices.

articles.title: End-of-Life Pathways and Limitation of Life-Sustaining Treatment in Children with Preexisting Neurological Disorders: A 10-Year Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Limitation of life-sustaining treatment (LSTL) is an important component of pediatric end-of-life care, but its use in children with preexisting neurologic disorders remains insufficiently described. We aimed to characterize end-of-life pathways, LSTL practices, and decision-making processes in this population.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study of children with preexisting neurologic disorders who died in a tertiary pediatric hospital between 2015 and 2024. Clinical characteristics and end-of-life care were compared between children with and without LSTL preceding death.

RESULTS: Of 37 included children, LSTL preceded death in 24/37; 8/37 died after brain death and 5/37 after unsuccessful resuscitation. Compared with children without LSTL, those with LSTL were less often admitted for acute neurological conditions (2/24 vs. 6/13, p = 0.013) or receiving invasive mechanical ventilation at death (9/24 vs. 11/13, p = 0.014), and more often died on the pediatric ward (15/24 vs. 0/13, p < 0.001) or had received pediatric palliative care (7/24 vs. 0/13, p = 0.038). Among children with LSTL, most decisions were documented during clinical stability (15/24), involving a median of four physicians; a do-not-resuscitate order was documented in 16/24 cases.

CONCLUSION: In this cohort, LSTL was the most frequent end-of-life pathway among children with preexisting neurologic disorders. Decisions were often documented before terminal deterioration and were usually multidisciplinary. These findings suggest that earlier advance care planning, structured, individualized documentation, and closer integration between pediatric neurology and pediatric palliative care may contribute to improving the quality and consistency of end-of-life care.

articles.title: NeuroTest: a benchtop testbed for evaluating sensing-capable electrophysiology and neurostimulation systems.
articles.abstract: Objective. The development of increasingly complex implantable neuromodulation devices requires extensive benchtop validation and testing prior toin vivoimplementation. Our goal is to enable thisin vitrotesting by creating a benchtop system that is accessible, easy-to-use, and functions reliably across academic and industry environments, reducing discordant results that arise from discordant approaches. Furthermore, such a system paves the way for standardizing benchtop characterization of future implantable systems by establishing a repeatable and comparable methodology for validating these devices and their capabilities.Approach.We describe the NeuroTest Board (NTB), a low-cost, open-source device that combines a low-noise current source waveform generator with a high-precision data acquisition system. We provide information on its architecture, operation, and performance as an initial benchmark of the potential capabilities of the system.Main results.We demonstrate the use of the NTB to assess electrophysiology systems in two separate applications. In one case, we assess a commonly used laboratory system (the RHD2132 digitizing headstage and Open Ephys data acquisition system), while the second case characterizes an investigational neuromodulation device in development for human use (the CorTec Brain InterChange). Following this initial sensing characterization, we explore stimulation-related artifacts that would hamperin vivodata collection. With the NTB, we develop and evaluate artifact mitigation strategies for each system, thus demonstrating an example application of this benchtop testbed.Significance.The ability to test neuromodulation devices against a common benchmark will enable faster development of novel therapeutics by increasing inter-institutional reliability and decreasing troubleshooting time.

articles.title: Stage-Associated Efficacy of Systemically Administered Neural Stem Cell-Derived Exosomes in Ischemic Stroke through the Prevention of Cx43 Degradation.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke pathology is highly dynamic, making the optimal timing for biological interventions highly elusive. This study investigated the stage-associated therapeutic efficacy of neural stem cell-derived exosomes (NSC-Exos) for cerebral ischemia-reperfusion. The in vivo evaluations identified a restricted therapeutic window closely associated with the temporal evolution of the ischemic microenvironment. Early exosome intervention (4 or 24 h post-ischemia) significantly reduced infarct volume, restored blood-brain barrier integrity, and improved neurological functional recovery. In contrast, delayed administration (48 h) failed to reduce the mortality rate and provide meaningful neuroprotection. To examine the molecular basis of this time dependence, we integrated temporal proteomic profiling of the ischemic penumbra with small RNA sequencing of NSC-Exos. The analytical and functional data suggest that early NSC-Exo delivery transfers miR-9-5p to suppress Nedd4 expression, thereby restoring the Connexin 43 protein pool and stabilizing the astrocytic network to halt initial microenvironmental collapse. Collectively, this study underscores the critical importance of intervention timing and provides a potential translational strategy for utilizing NSC-Exos as a targeted, stage-specific therapy in acute ischemic stroke.

articles.title: First-tier copy-number variant analysis in inherited cardiomyopathy: reconsidering the case for second-tier triage.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology

articles.title: Biomembrane-Camouflaged Stents: Promising Strategies for Advanced Coronary Interventions.
articles.abstract: Coronary stent implantation remains a cornerstone therapy for coronary artery disease, yet current stent technologies continue to face limitations including acute and late thrombosis, delayed re-endothelialization, chronic inflammation, and in-stent restenosis. These complications largely arise from the nonphysiological interface between the implanted device and the injured vascular microenvironment. Biomembrane-camouflaged stents have recently emerged as a promising strategy to engineer biologically instructive blood-contacting surfaces by integrating natural or artificial membrane systems onto stent platforms. In this review, we summarize recent advances in three major biomembrane-based strategies for coronary stent functionalization: cell membrane-camouflaged stents, liposome-camouflaged stents, and exosome-camouflaged stents. Biomimetic cell membrane coatings retain native bioactive signals that collectively facilitate immune evasion, thromboresistance, and vascular healing. Liposome-based coatings are tunable artificial biomembrane reservoirs for the localized delivery of anticoagulants, anti-inflammatories, nitric oxide releasers, antiproliferatives, and gene therapies. Exosome-functionalized stents further enable bioactive intercellular communication by transferring endogenous regulatory cargos that modulate endothelial regeneration, macrophage polarization, smooth muscle cell phenotype, oxidative stress, and neointimal remodeling. We further discuss fabrication approaches, biological mechanisms, preclinical evidence, translational barriers, and future design principles for these platforms. Although challenges remain in coating durability, sterilization, long-term storage, manufacturing reproducibility, and clinical validation, biomembrane-camouflaged stents represent a compelling direction for next-generation coronary intervention by transforming conventional stents from passive mechanical scaffolds into active regulators of vascular repair.

articles.title: Validity of the 2023 ACR/EULAR APS classification criteria for paediatric primary APS: inputs from a systematic literature review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The 2023 ACR/EULAR APS classification criteria have been introduced and validated in adult populations; however, data on their performance in paediatric APS remain limited. The present study aimed to apply the 2023 EULAR/ACR classification criteria to a cohort of paediatric patients with primary APS identified through a systematic review of the literature.

METHODS: A systematic literature review was conducted to help identify clinical and laboratory features of primary paediatric APS. Individual patient data were extracted. A two-stage individual participant data-style random-effects meta-analysis was performed to estimate the pooled sensitivity of the APS scoring systems.

RESULTS: A total of 118 studies were included, comprising 148 paediatric patients with primary APS. Thrombotic events were reported in 93.2% of patients, while non-thrombotic manifestations occurred in 56.8%; the most frequent extra-thrombotic manifestation was thrombocytopenia (29%). Overall, the 2006 Sapporo criteria reached a sensitivity of 91.2% (95% CI: 85.4-95.2), while the 2023 ACR/EULAR APS classification criteria reached a sensitivity of 83.1% (95% CI: 76.2-88.3). Most patients who did not satisfy the new criteria set failed to meet the laboratory domains.

CONCLUSION: The 2023 ACR/EULAR APS classification criteria demonstrated suboptimal sensitivity when applied to paediatric primary APS. While the inclusion of non-thrombotic manifestations improved the classification of paediatric APS patients, limitations remained, particularly regarding laboratory aPL thresholds and the exclusion of some paediatric-relevant clinical features, confirming the incomplete overlap between paediatric and adult-onset APS. These findings highlight the need for paediatric-specific APS classification criteria in order to improve disease characterization and research in this population.

articles.title: Integrated Metabolomic and Proteomic Analyses Reveal Altered Iron Homeostasis and Immunometabolic Remodeling in the Spleen of Solea senegalensis during Vibriosis.
articles.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
articles.abstract: Vibrio anguillarum is a major pathogen impacting Solea senegalensis aquaculture. While host-pathogen competition for iron drives disease progression, the in vivo molecular evidence linking iron homeostasis and immune responses in fish remains limited. Here, we integrated metabolomic and proteomic analyses to characterize the splenic response of S. senegalensis during experimental vibriosis. Multiomics integration revealed disruption of iron homeostasis alongside coordinated immunometabolic reprogramming. We detected the bacterial siderophore piscibactin directly in spleen tissue of sole exhibiting advanced stages of vibriosis, providing in vivo evidence of siderophore-mediated iron acquisition. Infection-driven metabolic shifts in lysine degradation, nucleotide metabolism, and mitochondrial energy pathways were correlated with heightened cellular proliferation and metabolic stress. Integrative analysis identified metabolites including 2-aminoadipic acid, saccharopine, and methylsuccinic acid, together with iron-regulatory proteins (e.g., STEAP4) as candidate biomarkers. These findings enhance our understanding of vibriosis-associated immunometabolic responses and provide a systems-level framework for future disease monitoring and management in aquaculture.

articles.title: Tumor-Microenvironment-Activated DOX@Cu2S@PDA@MnO2 Nanoplatform for MRI/PAI-Assisted Chemophotothermal Therapy of Osteosarcoma.
articles.abstract: Osteosarcoma remains difficult to treat because surgery and chemotherapy can provide incomplete tumor control, cause systemic toxicity, and lack reliable local monitoring. In this study, a tumor-microenvironment-activated DOX@Cu2S@PDA@MnO2 nanoplatform was prepared by converting Cu2O nanocubes into hollow Cu2S, coating polydopamine, growing a MnO2 shell, and loading doxorubicin. The Cu2S/PDA structure enabled strong NIR absorption and drug loading, while MnO2 responded to acidic H2O2/GSH-rich conditions to promote O2 generation, ROS-related reactions, and enhanced T1 MRI contrast.
