OBJECTIVES: To describe the methodological framework and consensus-based decision rules that underpin the revised guidance on musculoskeletal ultrasound scanning protocols in rheumatology practice.

METHODS: A systematic literature search on musculoskeletal ultrasound imaging and assessment methods was conducted to extract candidate anatomical structures and their corresponding scanning techniques from the included articles. A Delphi survey of the Guidance Development Panel selected the sites for inclusion. Iterative consensus meetings defined standardised scanning procedures for each structure, including patient positioning, limb orientation, probe placement, scanning direction, and the key anatomical landmarks to be captured on the ultrasound images.

RESULTS: A total of 3168 unique records were identified, of which 36 were included after screening. Based on the included articles and the first edition, a list of 159 candidate anatomical structures across the seven regions was compiled (including two structures added during the consensus process). Through the Delphi process, 50 structures were endorsed for inclusion. An image atlas was produced presenting the standardised views used in routine practice and the scanning procedures for the recommended structures.

CONCLUSIONS: This revised guidance provides standardised musculoskeletal ultrasound scanning methods for rheumatic diseases based on a systematic literature search and a structured consensus process.

articles.title: Optimal glucocorticoid tapering in anti-synthetase syndrome-associated interstitial lung disease: A multicentre MYKO cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To explore glucocorticoid tapering targets in patients with acute/subacute anti-synthetase syndrome-associated interstitial lung disease (ASyS-ILD).

METHODS: We retrospectively analysed 86 patients with newly diagnosed acute/subacute ASyS-ILD from the MYKO cohort. Patients were grouped using prednisolone-equivalent dose thresholds of 15, 12.5, and 10 mg/day at 6 months. Exploratory three-group analyses categorised patients into ≤ 12.5, 12.5-15, and >15 mg/day. Matching weights adjusted for baseline confounders. Cox proportional-hazards models evaluated 5-year all-cause mortality and event-free survival for disease flares and infections requiring hospitalisation. A multivariable logistic regression assessed factors associated with achieving ≤ 15 mg/day at 6 months.

RESULTS: In two-group analyses, the ≤ 15 mg/day group had a lower infection risk (hazard ratio 0.18, 95% confidence interval 0.04-0.81), whereas analyses using other thresholds showed no clear differences. In the three-group analyses, patients receiving 12.5-15 mg/day tended to have the lowest flare risk. Female sex was associated with achieving ≤ 15 mg/day at 6 months (odds ratio 3.29, 95% confidence interval 1.09-10.13).

CONCLUSIONS: Tapering to a prednisolone-equivalent dose of 12.5-15 mg/day at 6 months may represent a reasonable target to balance risks of flares and infections in patients with acute/subacute ASyS-ILD.

articles.title: Disentangling temporal factors in organ damage accrual in systemic lupus erythematosus: Onset-age, onset-era, and ageing in the Japanese LUNA registry.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To disentangle the contributions of three temporal factors-onset-age, onset-era, and ageing-to organ damage in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).

METHODS: We analysed 1228 patients with SLE from a nationwide registry in Japan whose disease onset occurred between 1990 and 2019 at ≤50 years of age. Organ damage was assessed using the Systemic Lupus International Collaborating Clinics/American College of Rheumatology Damage Index (SDI) between 2020 and 2023. Negative binomial and logistic regression models estimated the independent associations of onset-age (<20 years [early-onset SLE: EOSLE] versus 20-50 years), onset-era (5-year ordinal categories), and current age with SDI outcomes, adjusting for sex and comorbidities. Pairwise interactions among the temporal factors were examined.

RESULTS: EOSLE (count ratio 1.35; 95% confidence interval [95%CI] 1.05-1.75), past onset-eras (count ratio 1.10; 95%CI 1.03-1.18), and older age (count ratio 1.02; 95%CI 1.01-1.03) were independently associated with higher SDI. EOSLE and older age were also associated with SDI ≥1, while past onset-eras were associated with greater 1-year increases in SDI. There was no evidence of interactions among the three temporal factors.

CONCLUSIONS: Onset-age, onset-era, and ageing each exert distinct impact on organ damage in SLE. Recognizing these temporal aspects may strengthen risk stratification and individualized long-term care.

articles.title: Consolidation volume assessed by quantitative computed tomography predicts the prognosis of pneumocystis pneumonia in rheumatic diseases.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the prognostic value of quantitative computed tomography (QCT) analysis in pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP) patients with rheumatic diseases, specifically relating abnormal lung volumes (ALV) to major clinical events (MCE).

METHODS: This multicentre, retrospective study included 83 PCP patients with rheumatic diseases. QCT automatically quantified ALV, categorized into consolidation (≥ -300 HU) and ground-glass opacities (< -300 HU). The primary outcome was MCE, including intubation, intensive care unit admission and death. Logistic regression and survival analyses assessed associations between QCT-derived volumes and MCE.

RESULTS: MCE occurred in 17 patients (20%). Patients with MCE had significantly larger consolidation volumes than those without MCE (median, 5.7% vs 0.4%, P < 0.001). Logistic regression analysis identified lactate dehydrogenase, C-reactive protein and beta-D-glucan as risk factors; however, consolidation volume remained independently associated with MCE after adjustment (odds ratio: 1.33, 95% confidence interval 1.11-1.59, P < 0.001). Receiver operating characteristic analysis of consolidation volume for predicting MCE showed an area under the curve of 0.89 (P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed significantly lower MCE-free survival in patients with consolidation volumes ≥1.4% (P < 0.001; log-rank test).

CONCLUSIONS: In PCP patients with rheumatic diseases, QCT-derived consolidation volume is a strong predictor of severe outcomes.

articles.title: Medical pre-training and fine-tuning improve large-language-model prediction of rheumatoid-arthritis disease activity.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether medical-domain pre-training and parameter-efficient fine-tuning improve the ability of locally deployable Large Language Models (LLMs) to predict long-term disease activity and disability in rheumatoid arthritis, and to benchmark their performance against established tabular machine-learning models.

METHODS: We trained on-premises Llama-2 (70B) models with and without medical pre-training (Meditron) and applied Quantized Low-Rank Adapter fine-tuning using structured data from 11 865 patients in the Institute of Rheumatology, Rheumatoid Arthritis cohort. Models predicted eight binary outcomes of rheumatoid arthritis disease activity and disability at 2 years. Performance was compared with logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost using receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve, Brier score, calibration plots, and decision-curve analysis.

RESULTS: Medical pre-training and Quantized Low-Rank Adapter fine-tuning both improved discrimination and calibration, with effects varying by endpoint. Fine-tuned LLMs achieved the highest or comparable receiver operating characteristic-area under the curves for most Disease Activity Score-based outcomes and matched conventional models for remission tasks. In low-prevalence outcomes, LLMs showed more stable calibration and small but consistent net-benefit advantages, while some tabular models exhibited clinically harmful decision curves.

CONCLUSIONS: Endpoint-specific, privacy-preserving LLMs can complement or replace conventional tabular models for rheumatoid arthritis disease-activity prediction, providing reliable, locally deployable decision support without sacrificing data privacy.

articles.title: Risk of 90-day readmission for heart failure among patients with rheumatoid arthritis: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) are at an increased risk of developing heart failure (HF); however, the risk of readmission due to HF in patients with RA remains unclear. This study aimed to identify the risk of HF readmission among patients with RA.

METHODS: We included patients with RA aged ≥18 years who were hospitalized for the first time with HF and discharged between January 2012 and December 2019. The incidence of 90-day HF readmission was assessed. We reported the risk factors for HF readmission using the Fine-Gray model as adjusted subdistribution hazard ratios (aSHRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: The analysis included 1274 patients (mean age, 76.4 years; 61.5% female; mean Charlson Comorbidity Index, 4.6). There were 146 (11.5%) cases of 90-day HF readmission, associated with the Charlson Comorbidity Index (aSHR: 1.08, 95% CI: 1.01-1.15), diuretic use (aSHR: 1.48, 95% CI: 1.03-2.13), and opioid use (aSHR: 1.76, 95% CI: 1.11-2.77).

CONCLUSIONS: Patients with RA appeared to have a higher incidence of 90-day HF readmission than the general HF registry population. HF readmission was associated with high Charlson Comorbidity Index scores and the use of diuretics and opioids.

articles.title: Impact of reminder strategies on survey response in older adults: a randomized trial in Japan.
articles.abstract: Declining postal survey response rates, especially among older adults, threaten research validity. This study evaluated the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of 2 reminder strategies-a postcard and a re-sent questionnaire-issued 7 months after initial mailing among older Japanese adults. We conducted a 3-arm randomized controlled trial with 1500 adults aged 48-88 years from the Japan Multi-Institutional Collaborative Cohort Chiba cohort. Non-respondents to a survey mailed 7 months prior were randomized equally to: (1) no reminder, (2) a reminder postcard, or (3) a re-sent questionnaire with a prepaid envelope. The primary outcome was response within 60 days. Logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted odds ratios. The final sample sizes were 492, 486, and 487 participants, with the response rates of 0.8%, 12.1%, and 35.5% for the control, postcard, and re-sent questionnaire groups, respectively (P < .001). Both interventions significantly increased responses, with no evidence of effect modification by age, sex, or educational attainment. Most responses occurred within 2 weeks. Cost per response was ¥867 for postcards vs ¥503 for re-sent questionnaires. Both reminder strategies significantly improved response rates vs no reminder. The re-sent questionnaire achieved the highest response and best cost-effectiveness, when implemented 7 months after the initial mailing. Re-sending questionnaires should be prioritized to enhance participation in surveys targeting aging populations.

articles.title: Low-dose IL-2 fails to expand Tregs after alemtuzumab: insight into impaired immune tolerance in multiple sclerosis.
articles.abstract: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) are essential to preventing autoimmunity. They depend upon interleukin-2 (IL-2) for optimal function and, due to high expression of the CD25 subunit of the IL-2 receptor, are 10-fold more sensitive to IL-2 than effector T cells (Teffs). Consequently, low-dose IL-2 can be used to expand Tregs preferentially, a therapeutic strategy that has shown promise in a number of autoimmune and inflammatory conditions-including graft-versus-host disease and lupus-where IL-2 driven expansion correlates with improvements in some clinical markers of disease activity. Autoimmunity is a frequent delayed complication of treatment with the lymphocyte-depleting drug alemtuzumab in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS). Here, using in vitro assays, a pre-clinical mouse model and an experimental medicine study, we investigated whether low-dose IL-2 could selectively expand Tregs in alemtuzumab-treated RRMS patients. Six months after alemtuzumab treatment, the frequency of patient-derived naïve CD4+ Teffs expressing high-affinity IL-2 receptors increased from 30.11% ± 5.09% to 72.88% ± 5.57%, and the density of receptors per cell increased, rendering them six times more sensitive to IL-2 in vitro, at concentrations that typically favour Tregs. Using a human CD52-expressing transgenic mouse model of alemtuzumab treatment, we found that IL-2 could still preferentially expand Tregs, but only when administered at a later time point, corresponding to more than 6 months post-treatment in patients. Guided by these findings, we evaluated low-dose IL-2 for Treg expansion in a prospective open-label mechanistic study of RRMS patients who had received alemtuzumab more than 6 months previously. IL-2, at a dose and frequency similar to that previously shown to expand Tregs in autoimmune diabetes (0.3 × 106 IU/m2 twice a week), was well tolerated and safe, but unexpectedly failed to expand Tregs. We discuss the potential reasons underlying this lack of response, ruling out sIL2RA-related neutralization and instead considering ceiling effects on Treg proliferation, Treg exhaustion and intrinsic Treg dysfunction in MS as possible contributors. Together, our findings demonstrate that low-dose IL-2 alone is not an effective strategy for promoting Treg expansion post-alemtuzumab and is therefore not a viable approach on its own for preventing post-treatment autoimmune complications.

articles.title: Exploratory comparison of diffusion-weighted whole-body imaging with background body signal suppression and 18F-FDG PET/CT for assessing disease activity in large-vessel vasculitis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare diffusion-weighted whole-body imaging with background body signal suppression (DWIBS) with ^18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (FDG-PET/CT) for assessing disease activity in large-vessel vasculitis (LVV), and to evaluate whether segment-level analysis provides complementary information beyond global grading.

METHODS: We enrolled 25 patients with LVV (Takayasu arteritis [TAK], n = 11; giant cell arteritis [GCA], n = 14). Two blinded readers graded 11 arterial territories (18 segments) on a four-point visual scale for DWIBS and FDG-PET/CT. Global imaging grades were calculated as segment-averaged means. Correlations with serum C-reactive protein (CRP) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) were assessed.

RESULTS: Global mean DWIBS grades correlated significantly with FDG-PET/CT grades (r = 0.72) and with CRP levels (r = 0.53). Territory-level mapping revealed diffuse central aortic involvement in GCA, whereas TAK showed more focal and segment-limited patterns. DWIBS demonstrated lower sensitivity in motion-prone regions but appeared to better reflect clinical activity and more frequently detected subclavian artery involvement in TAK compared with FDG-PET/CT. Residual vascular signals were also observed in some patients classified as being in clinical remission.

CONCLUSIONS: DWIBS shows good agreement with FDG-PET/CT and provides a radiation- and contrast-free approach for assessing LVV. Global mean grades alone showed limited discriminatory power and may underestimate disease activity in focal or segment-limited involvement. Integrating segment-level imaging findings with clinical and laboratory markers may improve assessment of disease activity. Multicenter validation and longitudinal studies are warranted.

articles.title: Adaptive introgression and incompatibility shape interspecific hybrid genomes in ornamental and feral Xiphophorus strains.
articles.abstract: Adaptive introgression can propel the rapid evolution of species, but it is resisted by hybrid incompatibility. Ornamental swordtails are the result of century-old hybridization among multiple ancestries, which is a precious system for understanding interspecific gene flow under artificial selection. We combine Hidden Markov Model (HMM)-based local ancestry inference and simulations to infer the hybridization parameters. We develop new pseudolikelihood statistics for identifying candidate regions under strong adaptive introgression. Candidate regions involved in high-frequency introgressions are enriched for functions such as immunity, reproduction, survival, and life history traits. Compared with short genomic regions harboring a high frequency of the minor ancestry (>90%), which contained lower protein-coding density and lower relative genetic load in the minor parent, strong adaptive introgression occurs more often in regions of higher functional density, suggesting that highly adaptive alleles can potentially overcome the resistance by incompatibility. We further identified incompatibility loci involved in mitonuclear interactions. These findings highlight the interplay between adaptive introgression and hybrid incompatibility in shaping hybrid genomes.

articles.title: Characterizing thunderstorm asthma emergency department presentations using natural language processing for improved real-time surveillance.
articles.abstract: Thunderstorm asthma events can overwhelm emergency departments within hours, making rapid detection critical for public health preparedness and patient safety. We examined whether thunderstorm asthma presentations show distinctive patterns compared to routine asthma cases in emergency department data, with an aim of enhancing the detection of thunderstorm asthma incidence. Using Victoria's SynSurv surveillance system, we analyzed triage notes from 3 thunderstorm asthma events occurring between 2022 and 2024 in Victoria, Australia, comparing 687 thunderstorm-related presentations with 687 presentations from 8 control days. The study population consisted of emergency department attendees with respiratory presentations. Triage notes were processed using natural language processing and manual review, with demographic, symptom-onset, and medical-history data compared using chi-square tests and temporal analysis. Thunderstorm cases showed significantly higher rates of acute symptom onset within 24 hours (63.0% vs 47.2%), with presentations peaking 3-8 hours after storms and returning to baseline within 24 hours. The affected population skewed markedly toward young adults aged 21-40 years (35.9% vs 15.6% in controls). Immunological and allergic comorbidities were 3 times more prevalent in thunderstorm cases (16.6% vs 5.6%). These distinct demographic, temporal, and allergic profiles could enhance real-time surveillance and emergency preparedness through refined detection models.

articles.title: Predictors of the late recurrences of immunoglobulin A vasculitis due to clinical and laboratory features in children.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the frequency and predictors of immunoglobulin A vasculitis (IgAV) late relapses based on clinical and laboratory features in children.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed the medical records of IgAV patients. To assess the severity of the disease, the Paediatric Vasculitis Assessment Score (PVAS) was calculated for each patient during the initial visit. Late recurrence of IgAV was defined as the reappearance of skin lesions and/or systemic involvement after a symptom-free period of at least 6 months. Patients were divided into two subgroups: Group 1 consisted of IgAV patients who experienced at least one recurrence, while Group 2 included those with no recurrence.

RESULTS: A total of 40 (7.3%) patients were in Group 1. Male gender, mean age at diagnosis, gastrointestinal and testicular involvement, white blood cell count, creatinine level, and paediatric vasculitis, the PVAS at the first visit were significantly higher in Group 1 than in Group 2 (P = .033, P = .015, P = .047, P = .003, P = .012, P = .012, and P = .000, respectively). Male sex, diarrhoea, testicular involvement, white blood cell value, and PVAS were found to be independent risk factors to predict IgAV late recurrence (P = .033, P = .015, P = .003, P = .025, and P = .005, respectively).

CONCLUSIONS: Close follow-up is essential, particularly in male patients and in the presence of testicular involvement, diarrhoea, or a high PVAS at the initial visit, given the potential for late disease recurrence in the long term.

articles.title: AKT is necessary for neuronal hypertrophy and epilepsy caused by Pten knockout.
articles.abstract: Phosphatase and tensin homologue on chromosome 10 (PTEN) is a key negative regulator of the mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) signalling pathway. Mutations in PTEN are highly implicated in autism spectrum disorder, epilepsy, congenital hydrocephaly and macrocephaly. While the conditional genetic knockout of Pten in murine neurons results in hypertrophy, increased migration, excitatory synaptogenesis, hyperexcitability and epileptiform activity, the specific downstream signalling mediators of these pathologies remain to be fully elucidated. Using retroviral-mediated genetic manipulation of individual neurons within the Cre-lox recombination system, we have analysed pathway outputs in response to the manipulation of various genes using immunohistochemistry, confocal microscopy and extensive morphological analyses, alongside whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology and 120-h video-EEG monitoring for seizure assessment. Here, we demonstrate that signalling through AKT is necessary for the development of neuronal overgrowth, increased excitatory synapse formation, excessive migration and hyperexcitability fuelled by the loss of PTEN function. Notably, the concurrent deletion of Akt1 and Akt3 isoforms was sufficient to effectively rescue hypertrophic neuronal morphology and physiology. These findings establish AKT as the essential mediator through which PTEN deficiency manifests, providing a transformative therapeutic target to correct the morphological and functional defects central to PTEN-related neurodevelopmental disorders.

articles.title: Selective disruption of tau-SH3 interactions rescues seizure and sleep phenotypes.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease patients frequently experience seizures, sleep disturbances and other forms of neural network dysfunction that accelerate cognitive decline. Although tau-lowering therapies may alleviate these features, they also risk disrupting essential physiological functions of tau, leading to motor impairments. We hypothesized that targeted mutations within tau's proline-rich domain-a region critical for binding SH3-containing proteins implicated in seizures and excitotoxicity-could selectively disrupt pathological interactions while preserving normal cognition and behaviour. To test this, we generated two tau knock-in mouse lines: AxxA6, carrying proline-to-alanine mutations in the sixth PxxP motif; and R221A, containing an arginine-to-alanine substitution at residue 221. Tau protein interactions were evaluated using proximity ligation assays in cultured hippocampal neurons and co-immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry of cortical lysates. To model epilepsy, Kv1.1 heterozygous knockout mice were crossed with tau knock-in mice. Mice underwent 24 h cortical EEG recordings. Seizure susceptibility was assessed following intraperitoneal kainic acid (25 mg/kg). Hippocampal slice electrophysiology was used to measure epileptic bursting after picrotoxin/4-AP application. Comprehensive motor and cognitive testing were performed in AxxA6 and R221A lines at young and older ages. Both variants reduced tau's binding to the SH3-containing proteins BIN1, PLCγ1 and p85α/PI3K, with AxxA6 specifically decreasing Fyn interaction (P < 0.0001). Co-immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry revealed variant-specific alterations in tau interactomes, including increased synaptotagmin 5 binding in both lines (P < 0.05). AxxA6 knock-in mice displayed unique resistance to kainic acid-induced seizures. AxxA6 knock-in also reduced epileptic spike rates in Kv1.1-/- mice (P = 0.02), along with improved beta power during REM (P < 0.05), and rescued sleep disruptions (P < 0.002). Both AxxA6 and R221A prevented the increase in epileptiform bursting in Kv1.1-/- hippocampal slices after picrotoxin/4-AP (P < 0.05) and improved survival in Kv1.1-/- mice. Motor function, cognition and body weight were preserved in both lines across ageing (3-7 and 14-18 months), in contrast to age-related weight gain and motor deficits in tau knockout mice. These findings demonstrate that precision targeting of tau's sixth PxxP motif can selectively disrupt pathological protein interactions while preserving physiological function, offering a promising therapeutic strategy to mitigate tau-driven neuronal and network dysfunction without compromising cognitive or motor health.

articles.title: Treatment of children and young adults with a Fontan circulation and cardiovascular dysfunction. 2026 Consensus Statement from the European Pediatric Pulmonary Vascular Disease Network (EPPVDN), endorsed by AHA, AEPC, EACTS, ISACHD, ISHLT and PICS.
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
articles.abstract: The Fontan operation enables long term survival for many individuals born with single ventricle heart disease, but the resulting circulation imposes a lifelong hemodynamic burden and predisposes to cardiovascular dysfunction and multisystem morbidity. Evidence based guidance for assessment and management of Fontan specific cardiac and vascular dysfunction, however, remains limited. The European Pediatric Pulmonary Vascular Disease Network (EPPVDN) convened an international, multidisciplinary executive writing group to review the available literature and develop consensus recommendations addressing cardiovascular dysfunction in children and young adults with a Fontan circulation. Recommendations were graded using established Class of Recommendation and Level of Evidence criteria adapted to the Fontan specific evidence base. The statement addresses cardiovascular assessment, pulmonary vascular disease and use of pulmonary vasodilator therapy, Fontan pathway obstruction, systemic venous and arterial abnormalities and collateral vessels, lymphatic dysfunction and intervention, myocardial dysfunction and heart failure therapy, and thromboembolic risk and antithrombotic therapy. The focus is on phenotype-guided management, hemodynamically informed treatment decisions, and medical, transcatheter, and surgical approaches tailored to Fontan circulation. Seven graded recommendation tables as well as a flowchart for considerations regarding pulmonary vasodilator therapy are provided to support clinical decision making. Fontan-specific evidence remains limited, so many recommendations necessarily represent expert opinion. This EPPVDN consensus statement, therefore, discusses knowledge gaps and priorities for collaborative research to improve outcomes for individuals living with a Fontan circulation.

articles.title: Treatment of pulmonary hypertension in infants, children and young adults. 2026 consensus statement from the European Pediatric Pulmonary Vascular Disease Network (EPPVDN), endorsed by AHA, AEPC, EACTS, ESPR, PASCAR, PCS, and PICS.
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
articles.abstract: The European Pediatric Pulmonary Vascular Disease Network (EPPVDN) is a registered, non-profit organization dedicated to advancing innovative diagnostic methods and treatment options for all forms of pediatric pulmonary vascular disease, including pulmonary hypertension (PH) related to congenital heart disease (CHD), PH associated with developmental lung disease (DEVLD-PH), persistent PH of the newborn (PPHN), postcapillary PH in left heart disease (PH-LHD), and associated cardiac dysfunction/heart failure. In the past, the EPPVDN has published consensus statements on the diagnosis and treatment of pediatric PH (2016, 2019), which have been endorsed by multiple societies. The executive writing group conducted comprehensive searches of the PubMed/MEDLINE bibliographic database (2000 to 2025) and engaged in multiple web-based and in-person meetings. Thirteen section task forces discussed and created consented recommendations. Prospective clinical studies, clinical trials, meta-analyses, expert consensus guidelines, and other articles with pediatric data were included in the search, using the terms 'pulmonary hypertension' and related keywords. Classes of recommendation (COR) and levels of evidence (LOE) were assigned based on AHA/ESC definitions, pediatric PH studies, adult studies including a minimum N number of 15 children, or studies involving adults with CHD. Classifications and definitions from the 7th World Symposium on Pulmonary Hypertension (WSPH) in 2024 were incorporated and discussed. We produced 6 graded recommendation tables (COR, LOE) and 3 algorithms for the treatment of pulmonary hypertension in infants, children, and young adults. A total of 16 main and 17 supplemental display items cover a range of topics, including risk assessment, pharmacological therapy, transcatheter interventions and surgery, recommendations specific to PH subgroups/special populations and clinical settings. Adaptation of management recommendations for middle-to-low-income regions is provided. Together, these up-to-date guidelines provide a comprehensive, detailed, and practical framework for the treatment of pulmonary hypertension in infants, children and young adults, aiming to improve outcomes and quality of life for affected patients.

articles.title: Mixture of Plasticizer Chemicals and Child Intelligence: A Weight-of-Evidence and Meta-Analysis-Informed Bayesian Approach in a Cohort with Improved Exposure Assessment.
articles.abstract: Early-life exposure to plasticizer chemicals can affect child neurodevelopment. However, accurately characterizing exposure to these short-lived chemicals remains challenging. To address knowledge gaps, we examined the association between prenatal and infant exposure to a plasticizer mixture and child intelligence quotient (IQ) in a cohort with improved exposure assessment, informing the statistical analysis using the existing toxicological and epidemiological evidence. This work included 380 mother-infant pairs from the SEPAGES study, a French new-generation population-based birth cohort recruited between 2014 and 2018. Sixteen phenols and phthalate metabolites were quantified in pools of multiple urine samples collected at four time points during pregnancy and infancy (up to 21/week). Children's IQ was assessed using the Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence at age 3. A structured review of the toxicological and epidemiological evidence was conducted to prioritize the chemicals with the highest weight of evidence (WoE) to be analyzed as a mixture. Meta-analyses of the retrieved epidemiological studies were performed and used as priors in single-chemical Bayesian regression models. Of 1189 references screened, we retrieved data from 30 toxicological and 57 epidemiological studies supporting the prioritization of bisphenol A and S, diethylhexyl phthalate metabolites, monoethyl phthalate (MEP), mono-n-butyl phthalate (MnBP), and mono-isobutyl phthalate (MiBP). Each quartile increase in maternal third-trimester concentrations of the high-WoE plasticizer mixture was associated with decreased full-scale (β: -2.86; 95% Credibility Interval, CrI: -5.05, -0.91), visual-spatial (-2.79; 95% CrI: -5.39, -0.82) and verbal (-1.95; 95% CrI: -3.84, 0.00) child IQ scores. Bayesian single-chemical models informed by meta-analysis-based priors also found that third-trimester concentrations of four of the six prioritized chemicals (bisphenol A, MEP, MnBP, and MiBP) were associated with reduced IQ scores. This novel evidence-based framework increased the biological plausibility and external validity of results, supporting that pregnancy exposure to a mixture of common plasticizers affects child IQ and represents a public health concern. The findings underscore the need to protect fetuses and children from plastic-associated chemicals and regulate them by class.

articles.title: Repeated Exposure to Near-Ambient PM2.5 Decreases Pulmonary Function: Controlled Human Exposure Study.
articles.abstract: Epidemiologic studies have provided evidence of health effects over cumulative days of PM2.5 exposure in observational settings; however, there have been no controlled exposure studies in humans over consecutive days. To assess the effects of near-ambient PM2.5 exposure on pulmonary function and exercise tolerance, a randomized, double-blind controlled exposure study was conducted among healthy human volunteers (n = 17). Exposure consisted of 4 h of intermittent exercise for 3 consecutive days to clean air and 35 μg/m3 of PM2.5 separated by a minimum of 2 weeks. Spirometry was measured at baseline, postexposure (+0 h), and 20 h (+20 h) after each day of exposure. PM2.5 exposure reduced lung function, with reductions after Day 2 and Day 3. At Day 1 + 0 h, FEV1 was unchanged (-0.9%, 95% CI: -2.1, 0.3), and at Day 1 + 20 h, FEV1 was unchanged (-1.2%, 95% CI: -2.4, 0.1). At Day 2 + 0 h, FEV1 was reduced by 1.9% (95% CI: -3.1, -0.7). This decrement persisted into Day 2 + 20 h, with FEV1 reduced by 1.7% (95% CI: -3.3, -0.2). At Day 3 + 0 h, FEV1 showed a similar reduction of 1.8% (95% CI: -3.5, -0.1). This decrement persisted into Day 3 + 20 h, with FEV1 down by 1.7% (95% CI: -3.2, -0.1). PM2.5 exposure reduced exercise output on both Day 2 (-2.0 W, 95% CI: -2.86, -1.08) and Day 3 (-2.4 W, 95% CI: -3.18, -1.61). Lung function and exercise output displayed modification by sex; males showed greater decrements in lung function at Day 3 + 20 h, and females had greater losses in exercise output after Day 3. In conclusion, near-ambient PM2.5 exposure elicits pulmonary function deficits, sustained after multiple days of exposure and persisting at least 20 h after cessation of exposure. PM2.5 exposure decreases exercise output.

articles.title: Consensus-based guidelines for Clinical Nurse Specialists providing psychological support in cancer care: A modified Delphi study.
articles.journal: European journal of oncology nursing : the official journal of European Oncology Nursing Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Psychological distress is common among people with cancer and affects quality of life, treatment engagement, and survivorship. Clinical Nurse Specialists are well placed to provide psychological support, yet no consensus-based best practice guidelines exist for the role. This study aimed to develop expert consensus best practice guidelines for Clinical Nurse Specialists providing psychological support to people with cancer.

METHODS: We conducted a modified Delphi study. A preliminary phase combined a literature review with interviews with five Clinical Psychologists working in cancer care to generate initial guideline statements. This was followed by a three-round Delphi process with 20 panellists (11 people with cancer, nine Clinical Nurse Specialists). Of these, 17, 14 and 11 completed Rounds 1, 2 and 3. Ratings were analysed using descriptive statistics and free-text responses using qualitative content analysis. Consensus was defined a priori at ≥75% and used to classify guidelines as Essential or Important.

RESULTS: The panel endorsed 38 guidelines, 15 Essential and 23 Important, covering communication, assessment and care planning, individual needs, training and supervision. The research team organised them into seven domains within two broader groupings: a holistic view of the person, and mobilisation of a psychologically informed system.

CONCLUSIONS: The guidelines provide a consensus-based framework to support Clinical Nurse Specialist practice, training, supervision, and service development in cancer care. They clarify the relational skills and the organisational conditions needed to deliver psychologically informed care. Further research should examine their implementation, adaptation, and sustainability across clinical contexts.

articles.title: Characteristics and Thresholds of Coronary Lesions to Predict Acute Coronary Syndrome From Artificial Intelligence-Guided Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Characteristics of future culprit lesions according to artificial intelligence-guided quantitative computed tomography (AI-QCT) are unknown.

OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to characterize and derive thresholds to predict future culprit lesions from coronary computed tomography angiography using AI-QCT.

METHODS: A total of 2,169 patients/13,772 lesions undergoing coronary computed tomography angiography at Turku University Hospital, Finland, (derivation) and 553 patients/3,948 lesions from Amsterdam University Medical Center, the Netherlands, (validation) were analyzed with AI-QCT. Lesions from vessels undergoing early revascularization were excluded. Lesion-level total plaque volume (TPV) and noncalcified plaque volume (NCPV) thresholds were derived and externally validated to predict lesion-level and patient-level acute coronary syndrome (ACS).

RESULTS: Future culprit lesions from both cohorts (n = 69 validation; n = 15 derivation) had consistently higher median TPV (101 mm3 validation; 115 mm3 derivation; P = 0.811) and NCPV (65 mm3 validation; 74 mm3 derivation; P = 0.709) compared with control lesions (P < 0.001) and were nonobstructive in 69.6% (derivation) and 40.0% (validation). Thresholds of TPV ≥55 mm3 and NCPV ≥32 mm3 were derived and associated with significantly higher adjusted rates of lesion-level (TPV ≥55 mm3: adjusted HR: 12.09; 95% CI: 6.95-21.04; P < 0.001; NCPV ≥32 mm3: adjusted HR: 10.82; 95% CI: 6.22-18.80; P < 0.001) and patient-level ACS (TPV ≥55 mm3: adjusted HR: 2.92; 95% CI: 1.65-5.16; P < 0.001; NCPV ≥32 mm3: adjusted HR: 5.11; 95% CI: 2.49-10.46; P < 0.001) with consistent results in the validation cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: Future culprit lesions vs nonculprit lesions by AI-QCT demonstrated significantly higher plaque volumes and were nonobstructive in 40% to 70%. Thresholds of TPV ≥55 mm3 and NCPV ≥32 mm3 were derived to predict future culprit lesions and associated with increased rates of lesion-level and patient-level ACS in 2 independent cohorts.

articles.title: Evaluation of a population health strategy to improve albuminuria detection among primary care patients with hypertension.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To study the impact of an electronic health record (EHR) alert implemented in September 2022 that prompts annual orders for urine albumin-creatinine ratio (UACR) testing for adults with hypertension (HTN).

METHODS: Using segmented interrupted time-series analyses and comparative interrupted time-series analyses stratified by diabetes status, we evaluated changes in annual UACR testing rates among adults with hypertension from 1 January 2021 through 30 June 2025.

RESULTS: Among 26 048 hypertensive adults (mean age, 61 years; 38.5% with diabetes), annual UACR testing rates increased from 23.8% preintervention to 37.1% postintervention. Implementation was associated with an immediate 4.05-fold increase in the odds of monthly UACR testing [odds ratio (OR) 4.05, 95% confidence interval (CI) 3.84-4.28]. Patients without diabetes experienced a larger immediate increase than patients with diabetes (OR 2.62, 95% CI 2.45-2.80). Patients with UACR at least 30 mg/g were more likely to receive angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor/angiotensin receptor blockers and SGLT2 inhibitor therapy than patients with UACR less than 30 mg/g or those never tested (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Implementation of an EHR-integrated UACR alert increased annual UACR testing among adults with HTN. Irrespective of the EHR alert, UACR testing was associated with greater use of guideline-concordant medications.

POLICY IMPLICATIONS: This easily implemented intervention has the potential to improve guideline-concordant care for patients with HTN in primary care.

articles.title: Effects of α‑Linolenic Acid and Arachidonic Acid on the Cytotoxicity and Steatosis of HepG2 Cells.
articles.abstract: Hepatic steatosis, characterized by excessive triglyceride (TG) accumulation in hepatocytes, serves as the initiating event in the early phase of metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD). Polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) exert differential modulatory effects on hepatic steatosis, but the underlying lipidomic remodeling remains incompletely understood. In this study, we systematically investigated the impacts of α-linolenic acid (ALA) and arachidonic acid (AA) on lipid accumulation, inflammation, and cytotoxicity in fattyacid-induced HepG2 cells. Our data indicated that ALA at concentrations >300 μM and AA at >150 μM significantly inhibited cell viability. In fatty acid-induced steatotic HepG2 cells, 100 μM ALA significantly reduced both triglyceride (TG) and total cholesterol (TC) levels, whereas 100 μM AA significantly increased TG levels without affecting TC content. Furthermore, quantitative real-time PCR revealed that 100 μM ALA significantly downregulated the transcriptional expression of NF-κB, TNF-α, and IL-6, while 100 μM AA upregulated the expression of these three factors. The untargeted metabolomic profiling and KEGG pathway enrichment analysis showed that ALA significantly modulated glycerophospholipid metabolism, amino acid metabolism, nucleotide metabolism, and central carbon metabolism in steatotic HepG2 cells. Lipidomics analysis further demonstrated that ALA, through conversion to DHA and EPA, remodeled TG molecular species and was incorporated into multiple membrane phospholipids. Furthermore, Drug Affinity Responsive Target Stability (DARTS) and molecular docking results indicated that choline kinase α (CHKA) might be a potential target of ALA in HepG2 cells. Conclusively, ALA might contribute to the progression of hepatocyte steatosis by remodeling TG molecular species, incorporating into membrane phospholipids, modulating glycerophospholipid metabolism, and targeting CHKA.

articles.title: Structure-based virtual screening, in vitro and in vivo analyses identified kaempferol 3-gentiobioside as an FXR partial agonist protecting against cholestatic liver disease.
articles.abstract: The farnesoid X receptor (FXR) plays a critical role in bile acid homeostasis and has emerged as a promising therapeutic target for cholestatic liver diseases. In this study, we employed a sophisticated virtual screening strategy combined with in vitro and in vivo assays to identify novel FXR agonists. Based on machine learning models, pharmacophore modeling and molecular docking, eleven hit compounds were identified as potential FXR agonists. Among them, kaempferol 3-gentiobioside (KFG) exhibited the best FXR agonistic activity (EC50 = 65.12 ± 9.82 nM, 70.81% maximum efficacy relative to OCA), which was selected for further research. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed the binding stability and interaction mode of KFG with FXR, and surface plasmon resonance assay confirmed its moderate binding affinity (KD = 1.12 μM). In the HepG2 cell model of lipid accumulation induced by free fatty acids, KFG effectively ameliorated steatosis in hepatocytes and reduced triglyceride content. Moreover, in vivo assays demonstrated that KFG administration significantly prevented cholestasis induced by α-naphthyl isothiocyanate in mice. Collectively, these findings identify KFG as a promising FXR partial agonist, which merits further development for the prevention of cholestatic liver diseases.

articles.title: Efficacy of Lumateperone 42 mg in Major Depressive Disorder: Subgroup Analysis of a Phase 3 Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: The primary care companion for CNS disorders
articles.abstract: Objective: Lumateperone is an FDA-approved atypical antipsychotic to treat schizophrenia, bipolar I or II depression, and major depressive disorder (MDD). Post hoc analyses of a randomized, phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (Study 501) evaluated the efficacy of lumateperone 42 mg adjunctive to antidepressant therapy (ADT) in demographic and clinical subgroups of patients with MDD with inadequate ADT response. Methods: Adults with DSM-5 criteria for MDD with inadequate response to 1-2 courses of ADT, Montgomery- Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) Total score ≥24, Clinical Global Impression Scale-Severity (CGI-S) score ≥4, and Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology-Self-Report 16-item (QIDS-SR-16) score ≥14 were randomized 1:1 to 6-week oral lumateperone 42 mg+ADT or placebo+ADT. Efficacy was evaluated in the overall population and patient subgroups by demographic (age, sex, race, ethnicity, and region) and baseline disease characteristics (MADRS Total score, ADT type, number of ADT failures [in current episode and lifetime], and presence of anxious distress). Results: The modified intent-to-treat population comprised 481 patients (lumateperone+ADT, n = 239; placebo+ADT, n = 242). Lumateperone+ADT significantly improved MADRS Total score (least squares mean difference [LSMD], -4.9; P < .0001), CGI-S score (LSMD, -0.7; P < .0001), and QIDS-SR-16 Total score (LSMD, -2.4; P < .0001) at Day 43 versus placebo+ADT. Lumateperone+ADT significantly improved MADRS Total score (P < .01) across all demographic subgroups and baseline disease severity versus placebo+ADT. Significant improvements (P < .05) in CGI-S, QIDS-SR-16 Total scores, and MADRS response and remission rates were also observed across most subgroups. Conclusion: Lumateperone+ADT demonstrated robust efficacy over placebo+ADT across a broad range of demographic and clinical subgroups of patients with MDD. Clinical Trials Registration. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04985942. Prim Care Companion CNS Disord 2026;28(6):26m04289. Author affiliations are listed at the end of this article.

articles.title: Maternal cardiac and perinatal outcomes among pregnant individuals with tetralogy of Fallot.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) is associated with maternal-fetal risks during pregnancy, particularly in those with uncorrected or residual defects.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study identified pregnancies with TOF and compared them with pregnancies with other congenital heart diseases (CHDs) using ICD-10 codes, between 5/23/22 and 5/22/25. Demographic and clinical characteristics were analyzed using analysis of variance or Student's t-tests for continuous variables and chi-square tests for categorical variables.

RESULTS: There were 1574 women (1961 pregnancies) with TOF compared to 37,899 women (47,239 pregnancies) with other CHD. Significant differences in cardiac outcomes were observed in arrhythmias (32.9% vs. 18.3%), particularly ventricular arrhythmias (6.8% vs. 2.1%) and endocarditis (2.4% vs. 1.5%). Significant perinatal outcomes included preterm delivery (17% vs. 14.1%) and earlier gestational age at delivery (37.4 ± 3 vs. 38.9 ± 1.7).

CONCLUSIONS: Pregnancies with TOF have a greater occurrence of adverse cardiac outcomes, particularly arrhythmias and endocarditis, and obstetric outcomes, including preterm delivery.

articles.title: Discontinuation of continuous kidney replacement therapy: current evidence and protocolized approaches for safe and timely liberation.
articles.abstract: Continuous kidney replacement therapy (CKRT) is a cornerstone of organ support in critically ill patients with acute kidney injury. While substantial evidence exists regarding the optimal timing of CKRT initiation, clear criteria to guide its discontinuation remain lacking. In clinical practice, decisions regarding CKRT discontinuation are often based on heterogeneous and institution-specific approaches, reflecting the absence of reliable and standardized indicators of kidney recovery. Various biomarkers, including serum creatinine, cystatin C, neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin, and urinary urea excretion, have been investigated for their potential to predict kidney recovery. Among these, urine output has been the most consistently reported and widely utilized parameter, although considerable heterogeneity exists in measurement timing, cutoff values, and the use of diuretics. In addition to individual biomarkers, several protocolized approaches incorporating multiple clinical parameters have been proposed. These include scoring systems, the furosemide stress test, and protocols incorporating the urinary urea excretion index. However, most proposed approaches remain insufficiently validated and should be regarded as supportive frameworks rather than definitive decision tools. Institutional protocols further highlight the variability in clinical practice, although urine output consistently emerges as a central component in decision-making. This review summarizes current evidence on biomarkers associated with kidney recovery and discusses emerging protocolized approaches for CKRT discontinuation. Further studies are needed to establish reliable and reproducible tools to guide optimal discontinuation and improve clinical outcomes in critically ill patients.

articles.title: Outcomes after lung transplantation for connective tissue disease-related interstitial lung disease: single center in South Korea.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary involvement is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in connective tissue diseases (CTDs), particularly in the form of CTD-related interstitial lung disease (CTD-ILD), and patients with severe CTD-ILD may eventually require lung transplantation (LT). However, post-transplant outcomes specific to CTD-ILD remain poorly characterized.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of adult patients who underwent LT for ILD between 2008 and 2025 at a single tertiary center. Patients were classified into CTD-ILD and non-CTD-ILD groups. Clinical and perioperative data were obtained through chart review. Overall survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: A total of 170 patients were included; 39 had CTD-ILD and 131 had non-CTD-ILD. CTD-ILD recipients were more often female (22/39, 56.4% vs. 32/131, 24.4%; P<0.001) and had a numerically higher prevalence of preoperative pulmonary hypertension (7/39, 17.9% vs. 12/131, 9.2%; P=0.094). Overall survival did not differ significantly between the CTD-ILD and non-CTD-ILD groups (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.923; 95% CI, 0.383-2.229; P=0.859; log-rank P=0.334). CTD-ILD recipients had a longer postoperative intensive care unit stay (median [interquartile range], 23.0 days [13.0-35.0] vs. 17.0 days [11.0-28.0]; P=0.026), a longer duration of mechanical ventilation (17.0 days [8.0-32.0] vs. 8.0 days [5.0-18.0]; P=0.009), fewer ventilator-free days (8.0 [0.0-19.0] vs. 11.0 [0.0-22.0]; P=0.002), and a higher incidence of postoperative thromboembolic events (10/39, 25.6% vs. 6/131, 4.6%; P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Although survival did not differ significantly in the present study, CTD-ILD recipients had a greater perioperative burden, including higher rates of thromboembolic events and greater use of intensive care resources.

articles.title: Postprocedural Haptoglobin Responses in Patients With Very Low Baseline Haptoglobin Undergoing Pulsed Field Ablation.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low baseline haptoglobin (Hpt) levels have been associated with renal injury after pulsed field ablation (PFA). Postprocedural Hpt responses in patients with very low but measurable baseline Hpt levels remain unknown.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively analyzed 421 patients undergoing PFA. Patients with baseline Hpt ≤5 mg/dL showed postprocedural Hpt increases, whereas those with higher baseline Hpt showed depletion (P<0.001). Acute kidney injury occurred in 9 patients in the overall cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: Very low but measurable baseline Hpt levels were associated with postprocedural increases in Hpt, warranting further investigation.

articles.title: Integrating carers' experiences and barriers to treatment from ANZAED Credentialed Eating Disorder Clinicians and non-credentialed clinicians in Australia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Eating disorder (ED) rates are rising in Australia, yet many individuals are not accessing timely or appropriate treatment. A key barrier is the availability of clinicians with the clinical knowledge and training to assess, diagnose, and provide timely, safe, and effective eating disorder treatment. The Australia & New Zealand Academy for Eating Disorders (ANZAED) introduced the ANZAED Eating Disorder Credential (the Credential) to address this challenge and ease the burden on individuals living with an eating disorder, their carers', and other supporting health professionals. The current study aims to explore parents' and carers' experience of eating disorder treatment in Australia provided by Credentialed Eating Disorder Clinicians (credentialed clinicians) and non-credentialed clinicians.

METHODS: An exploratory mixed-methods cross-sectional study was conducted involving 51 participants who had cared for a young person, family member, or loved one with an ED who received treatment by a credentialed clinician or a non-credentialed clinician. Participants were recruited via Australian eating disorder services and organisations, with recruitment information distributed through their email and social media platforms. Participants completed a survey with open- and closed-ended questions on their attitudes towards the Credential and their experiences of treatment by a credentialed clinician or non-credentialed clinician. Descriptive statistics and Mann-Whitney U tests were used to examine differences in treatment experiences and perceptions of treatment between participants who had experience with credentialed and non-credentialed clinicians, alongside content analysis of open-ended survey responses.

RESULTS: The Credential was valued among parents and carers, irrespective of whether they had experience with a credentialed clinician. Parents and carers also expressed an overall preference for treatment from a credentialed clinician. However, when considering perceived therapeutic success, credentialing status was considered less important than other factors such as access, collaborative care, therapeutic rapport, and individualised treatment. Further, despite the introduction of the Credential, several barriers to safe and effective ED treatment remain.

CONCLUSIONS: The Credential is an important step towards improving the standards of care and treatment experiences for individuals with eating disorders and their families. However, addressing ongoing barriers to access and delivery of care will be critical to realising its full potential.

articles.title: Implementation and Evaluation of the Stroke Triage App Among Paramedics in Prehospital Emergency Care: Sequential Mixed Methods Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Digital decision-support tools, such as the Stroke Triage App (STA), may enhance prehospital triage and clinical decision-making for suspected patients with stroke. However, implementation of decision-support tools and their impact on clinical practice remains insufficiently studied.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate paramedics' experiences with the implementation of the STA in prehospital practice by evaluating the implementation process, the implementation outcomes, and its impact on clinical workflows, while considering contextual factors that may have influenced these dimensions.

METHODS: STA implementation was evaluated among paramedics in 2 emergency medical services regions in the Netherlands using a sequential mixed methods approach. Actual usage data were extracted from the STA dashboard. Usability, perceived impact, and contextual factors were explored using an online survey and semistructured interviews.

RESULTS: Monthly triages ranged from 52 to 153 (median 120, IQR 107-131). Paramedics' individual STA use ranged from 1 to 47 times (median 7, IQR 3-13). Out of 246 paramedics with an account, 76 (31%) completed the survey, and 9 (4%) participated in semistructured interviews. The STA was generally well accepted, supporting structured neurological assessment and communication. Swift technical support, frequent promotion, and use of local ambassadors facilitated STA use. Clinical urgency, poor workflow integration, and limited perceived added value hampered STA use. Users recommended improvements in mobile interface, login features, and additional explanation with triage advice.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that the STA achieved substantial reach and initial adoption within the prehospital setting. However, widespread acceptance did not consistently translate into routine integration in daily practice. Successful implementation depends as much on addressing organizational and human factors as on technical performance.

articles.title: Effects of different packaging materials on the frozen storage quality of strawberries: A study based on functional active components and aroma.
articles.abstract: This study compared three packaging materials (PE, PA/PE, and PET/BOPA/RCPP) under conventional and vacuum conditions (80 kPa absolute residual pressure) for strawberries during 180-day frozen storage. PET/BOPA/RCPP-VAC gave the highest L* and a* values, the lowest ΔE, and the highest firmness and wet-weight bioactive-compound concentrations among the tested treatments. Its L* and a* values were 1.09 and 1.11 times those of the PE group, respectively, and its ΔE value was 80.47% that of the PE group. Firmness was 0.73 N, which was 1.09 and 1.24 times that of PA/PE-VAC and PE-VAC, respectively. Total phenolics (187.17 mg/100 g), flavonoids (19.02 mg/100 g), and anthocyanins (26.22 mg/100 g) were 9.94%, 20.61%, and 1.07-fold those of the PE group, respectively. In an exploratory selected-group comparison (only PE, PET/BOPA/RCPP, and PET/BOPA/RCPP-VAC were analysed), HS-SPME-GC-MS indicated slower loss of characteristic volatile compounds and lower accumulation of nonanal and decanal in PET/BOPA/RCPP-VAC than in PE at 180 d; no material, vacuum, or interaction effect on VOCs was tested. Because only summary statistics were available and VOC analysis covered only three of the six treatments, no factorial interaction or synergy is claimed, and the VOC comparison is exploratory and limited to the three analysed groups. These results provide a technical reference for packaging selection in frozen strawberry processing.

articles.title: Adjuvant mFOLFOXIRI after curative-intent resection of oligometastatic colorectal cancer: phase II FANTASTIC trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with oligometastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) remain at high risk of recurrence after curative surgery, yet the benefit of adjuvant chemotherapy remains inconclusive. This study evaluated the feasibility and efficacy of adjuvant modified (m)FOLFOXIRI (irinotecan, oxaliplatin, L-leucovorin (L-LV), 5-fluorouracil (5-FU)), as well as the utility of circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) as a prognostic and predictive biomarker in mCRC.

METHODS: Between October 2020 and January 2024, patients with histologically confirmed mCRC undergoing complete metastasectomy were enrolled in this multicentre non-randomized phase II study. Eligible and consenting patients received eight cycles of mFOLFOXIRI followed by four cycles of 5-FU/L-LV; ineligible/non-consenting patients received standard of care (SOC; CAPOX (capecitabine and oxaliplatin), 5-FU, or observation). ctDNA was assessed using the tumour-informed personalized Signatera™ assay (Natera, Austin, TX, USA) at 28 days and 7 months after surgery. The primary endpoint was completion of eight cycles of mFOLFOXIRI in a target sample of 36 patients.

RESULTS: Of the 83 registered patients, 73 were enrolled (39 mFOLFOXIRI, 34 SOC). The mFOLFOXIRI completion rate was 74% (80% confidence interval 63% to 83%; P < 0.001). ctDNA positivity predicted significantly inferior recurrence-free survival across both the mFOLFOXIRI and SOC treatment groups at 28 days (hazard ratios (HR) 7.27 and 7.17, respectively) and 7 months (HR 3.96 and 4.38, respectively) after surgery. Multivariate analysis identified ctDNA positivity, RAS mutation, metachronous metastases, and mFOLFOXIRI as significant prognostic factors. mFOLFOXIRI improved recurrence-free survival compared with SOC in the overall population (HR 0.44; P = 0.012), with a trend towards benefit in ctDNA-positive but not ctDNA-negative patients. ctDNA clearance rates were 33% (mFOLFOXIRI) and 20% (SOC).

CONCLUSIONS: This study indicates the feasibility of adjuvant mFOLFOXIRI in patients with mCRC, with an acceptable safety profile and potential clinical benefit among those with ctDNA positivity 28 days after surgery.

articles.title: Brain glucose metabolism and blood brain barrier permeability in Alzheimer's disease continuum.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Within the ATN framework of Alzheimer's disease (AD), patients are classified according to the presence of amyloid pathology (A), tau pathology (T), and neurodegeneration (N). While the A⁺T⁺N⁺ profile is well characterized, the A⁺T⁻N⁺ subgroup remains less understood. This phenotype may reflect mechanisms distinct from tau-driven pathology, potentially involving other amyloid co-pathology such as blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction.

METHODS: We examined A⁺T⁻N⁺ and A⁺T⁺N⁺ patients within the AD continuum (ADc) and cognitively healthy controls. All participants underwent cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarker assessment and 18F-FDG positron emission tomography (FDG-PET). The CSF/serum albumin quotient (QAlb) was used as an index of BBB integrity. Voxel-wise multiple regression analyses evaluated associations between regional glucose metabolism and CSF biomarkers, QAlb, demographics, cognitive status, ApoE genotype, and vascular risk factors (Hypertension, Diabetes, and Hypercholesterolemia).

RESULTS: Both AD subgroups showed hypometabolism in temporoparietal Default Mode Network regions. In ADc and A⁺T⁺N⁺ patients, posterior metabolism correlated positively with p-tau and negatively with t-tau. In A⁺T⁻N⁺ individuals, posterior hypometabolism was negatively associated with QAlb and positively with Aβ₄₂. Only Hypertension correlated with metabolism, involving the anterior cingulate cortex in ADc and A⁺T⁺N⁺, but not A⁺T⁻N⁺.

CONCLUSIONS: Within the AD continuum, A⁺T⁻N⁺ represent a subgroup of patients in whom FDG-PET metabolic dysfunctions appear to be associated with the coexistence of BBB dysfunction alongside amyloid pathology rather than tau-driven mechanisms.

articles.title: Looking Beyond a Normal Cerebrospinal Fluid Profile: Lessons Learned About Sepsis-Associated Encephalopathy in Meningococcal Septic Shock.
Robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty demonstrates superior early functional outcomes compared with conventional total knee arthroplasty: a quasi-randomised controlled trial.
articles.journal: Journal of orthopaedics and traumatology : official journal of the Italian Society of Orthopaedics and Traumatology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (TKA) has gained popularity over the last decade, with claimed advantages in implant positioning accuracy and soft-tissue balance. Whether these technical advantages translate into better clinical outcomes for patients remains debated. This investigation compared 1-year patient-reported outcomes between robotic-assisted and conventional TKA performed within the same institution but following structurally different surgical workflows.

METHODS: This quasi-randomised controlled trial enrolled patients who underwent primary TKA at the Department of Orthopaedic and Trauam Surgery of the Eifelklink St. Brigida (Simmerath, Germany) between 2022 and 2025. Group allocation was determined by surgeon assignment through the institutional digital scheduling system. All patients received the same implant (Smith & Nephew Legion Genesis II, posterior-stabilised). Robotic-assisted procedures were performed using the CORI Robotic System (Smith & Nephew, UK) following a four-dimensional personalised alignment workflow (coronal, sagittal, transversal and balancing) guided intraoperatively by the Knee Balancing Score (KBS). Conventional procedures followed a femur-first technique with adjusted mechanical alignment. Outcomes included WOMAC total and subscores, visual analogue scale (VAS), Tegner activity score and a dedicated functional questionnaire, all assessed at 1-year follow-up.

RESULTS: A total of 845 patients were included (robotic-assisted: n = 390; conventional: n = 455). At 1-year, 383 and 445 patients completed follow-up, respectively. The two groups were comparable at baseline. The robotic-assisted cohort showed significantly better results across WOMAC and related subscales (P < 0.001), VAS (P < 0.001), Tegner (P < 0.001), functional and satisfaction items, including walking distance and knee stability. No difference was found in the use of walking aids.

CONCLUSIONS: Robotic-assisted TKA was associated with superior functional and patient-reported outcomes at the 1-year follow-up. The clinical benefit observed is likely not attributable to robotic precision alone, but reflects the structured, personalised intraoperative workflow that robotic assistance enables. Trial Registry German Registry of Clinical Trials (ID DRKS00030614).

articles.title: Coming Full Circle: Transfemoral Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement at 2 Years.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

articles.title: Percutaneous Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement for Symptomatic Mitral Regurgitation: 2-Year Outcomes From the ENCIRCLE Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) is an approved treatment option for select high-risk patients with symptomatic mitral regurgitation (MR). The main cohort of the ENCIRCLE trial, evaluating fully percutaneous transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system, demonstrated 13.9% mortality, significant MR reduction, and improved functional and health status outcomes at 1 year.

OBJECTIVES: We report 2-year outcomes from the main cohort of the ENCIRCLE trial.

METHODS: Eligible symptomatic patients with ≥3+ MR who were not suitable for surgery or transcatheter edge-to-edge repair underwent TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system. Independent study oversight included an echocardiographic core laboratory and a clinical events committee. Endpoints included the nonhierarchical composite rate of all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization (HFH) as well as clinical, echocardiographic, functional, and health status outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 299 patients were treated, with 2-year follow-up data available for 202 of 210 eligible patients (96.2%). Mean age was 75.5 ± 9.3 years, 50.8% were men, and the mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score for mitral valve replacement was 6.6% ± 4.1%. At 2 years, MR reduction was sustained, with MR ≤1+ in 97.0% patients (P < 0.001). The 2-year composite rate of all-cause mortality or HFH was 35.6% (25.1% all-cause mortality, 23.0% HFH). In a 365-day landmark analysis, 1- to 2-year rates were 13.0% for all-cause mortality and 10.6% for first HFH. At 2 years, the rates of disabling stroke, clinically significant valve thrombosis, and hemolysis requiring intervention were 6.6%, 7.1%, and 7.6%, respectively. There were no instances of clinically significant left ventricular outflow obstruction. Improvements in functional and health status outcomes were sustained with 87.0% of patients in NYHA functional class I/II (P < 0.001) and a mean Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire overall summary score increase of 17.2 points (P < 0.001). The 6-minute walk distance increased by +9.0 ± 97.3 m compared to baseline (P = 0.246).

CONCLUSIONS: The 2-year results of the ENCIRCLE trial demonstrated durable near MR elimination with sustained improvements in functional and health status outcomes in surviving patients. These findings support transseptal TMVR as a therapeutic option for carefully selected patients with symptomatic MR. (The ENCIRCLE Trial [ENCIRCLE]; NCT04153292).

articles.title: Peer Health Coaching for Self-Management of Youth With Childhood Onset Chronic Conditions: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: The Journal of adolescent health : official publication of the Society for Adolescent Medicine
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The transition from childhood to adulthood is a challenging period for youth with many childhood-onset conditions. Engaging interventions to promote self-management during this vulnerable period are needed. This study sought to determine if a telephone/text-based peer health coaching intervention results in greater improvement in self-management and patient activation compared to an educational control among youth with one of nine childhood-onset chronic conditions.

METHODS: A randomized controlled clinical trial was conducted from 2018 through 2024. With 222 youth (aged 16-22 years) with at least one of nine chronic conditions (e.g. cancer and diabetes) were recruited at a large health system from pediatric/adult clinics. Following randomization intervention, participants received a 12-month telephone/text-based peer health coach intervention. Primary outcomes measured were chronic condition self-management (12-item Partners in Health scale) and patient activation (13-item Patient Activation Measure) measured at 3, 6, 9 and 12 months. Multilevel, mixed-effect longitudinal models tested for treatment differences in the trajectory of outcomes across 12-months.

RESULTS: Participant mean age was 18.4 years and 62% were female. Participants had high engagement with a median of 15 calls/participant. Intervention participants had significantly greater improvement in self-management compared to controls (intent-to-treat analysis, F = 8.86, df = 1,164, p = 0.0034, Cohen's d = 0.61, medium effect). Patient activation increased significantly in both treatment groups without any significant difference between groups.

DISCUSSION: This peer health coaching intervention was highly engaging and showed improvements in self-management for a wide range of youth with chronic conditions.

articles.title: Isoproterenol for Bradycardia Associated Prolonged QT Interval After Mixed Drug Overdose.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prolonged QT interval is a marker for risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Risk factors include medications, bradycardia, female sex, genetics, advanced age, structural abnormalities, and electrolyte derangements.

CASE SUMMARY: This case describes an 18-year-old woman with an extensive psychiatric history who overdosed on escitalopram and guanfacine in a suicide attempt. At 33 hours from ingestion, QTc interval measured 658 milliseconds with persistent bradycardia. Isoproterenol successfully prevented emergence of torsades de pointes (TdP).

DISCUSSION: Coingestion of substances in the setting of overdose requires prompt identification of toxidromes in anticipation of potential complications. Management for prolonged QTc interval should be based on TdP risk assessment considering patient and clinical factors.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: In select hospitalized patients with sinus bradycardia at high risk for TdP, early use of isoproterenol may be used to prevent the occurrence of adverse cardiac events.

articles.title: Acupuncture for Cardiovascular Diseases: A Review of Clinical Efficacy, Mechanisms, and Translational Perspectives.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the leading cause of global mortality and disability, imposing a profound societal burden. While conventional pharmacotherapy and surgical interventions are foundational, they are frequently limited by adverse effects, postoperative complications, and suboptimal long-term prognoses. Acupuncture and electroacupuncture (EA), core components of traditional Chinese medicine, have attracted growing attention as low-risk, non-invasive, neuromodulatory therapies. A growing body of clinical data suggests that acupuncture/EA may be beneficial in managing diverse CVDs, including coronary heart disease, hypertension, arrhythmias, heart failure, and myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury. Furthermore, mechanistic investigations have expanded into modern interdisciplinary fields, revealing complex regulatory networks involving central neuromodulation, intracellular signaling, cytoprotection, and the gut microbiota. This narrative review synthesizes the core clinical evidence and underlying mechanisms of acupuncture/EA in cardiovascular care. We additionally collate standardized clinical protocols, encompassing core acupoints and stimulation parameters. Finally, this paper critically examines current research limitations and outlines future translational trajectories, aiming to provide a comprehensive reference for integrating acupuncture/EA into standardized CVD prevention and treatment research.

articles.title: Compound Alpha-Ketoacid Supplementation for Diabetic Nephropathy in a Retrospective Controlled Study.
articles.abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a major microvascular complication of diabetes and a leading cause of progressive chronic kidney disease. This retrospective controlled study evaluated whether adding compound alpha-ketoacid tablets to conventional therapy improves renal function, inflammatory response, fibrosis-related biomarkers, oxidative stress status, therapeutic efficacy, and safety in patients with diabetic nephropathy. A total of 312 patients treated from October 2022 to June 2023 were included. The control group received conventional treatment, including glycemic control, antihypertensive therapy, lipid regulation, low-protein dietary guidance, and basic nutritional support. The experimental group received compound alpha-ketoacid tablets in addition to conventional therapy for 3 months. Compared with conventional therapy alone, combined therapy produced a higher total effective rate and greater improvements in blood urea nitrogen (BUN), serum creatinine (Cr), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), homocysteine (Hcy), hepatocyte growth factor (HGF), vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), interleukin-6 (IL-6), total antioxidant capacity (T-AOC), superoxide dismutase (SOD), and malondialdehyde (MDA). The incidence of adverse drug reactions did not differ significantly between groups. These findings suggest that supplementation with alpha-ketoacid compounds may be a useful adjunctive strategy to improve renal and inflammatory outcomes in selected patients with diabetic nephropathy without increasing safety risks.

articles.title: SDN-Based Network Architecture Optimization and Secure Data Transmission for Smart Taxation.
articles.abstract: With the rapid advancement of smart taxation systems, traditional network architectures are no longer capable of meeting the demands for efficient and secure data transmission. This study proposes a software-defined networking (SDN)-based architecture and secure data transmission framework specifically designed for smart taxation environments characterized by high-concurrency workloads, periodic traffic patterns, and complex cybersecurity threats. The proposed framework implements dynamic network resource scheduling and security protection through a three-layer SDN architecture comprising the data, control, and application layers. The framework incorporates a flow table compression algorithm that reduces flow table size by 40%-60%, an LSTM-based dynamic traffic prediction model that captures fiscal calendar periodicities, and an IPSO-CA attack detection algorithm that combines self-organizing maps with decision trees. To address the limitations of conventional SDN optimization methods, the proposed architecture separates audit logging from packet forwarding and introduces a rarity-harmfulness double-validation mechanism to improve the detection of low-frequency ("low-and-slow") attacks. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed architecture improves controller load balancing by 35% and achieves fault recovery in less than 100 ms. The IPSO-CA algorithm attains a 98.2% detection rate for SYN Flood attacks with a false-positive rate of only 1.3%, outperforming conventional decision tree (90.5%) and support vector machine (93.7%) classifiers. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides a scalable, reliable, and secure networking solution that supports the operational requirements of modern smart taxation systems.

articles.title: Association of Documented Active Warming with Prolonged Postoperative Hospitalization After Endoscopic Spine Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Intraoperative temperature loss may occur during endoscopic spinal surgery because of general anesthesia, operative exposure, and irrigation. This study examined whether documented active warming was associated with intraoperative thermal outcomes and prolonged postoperative hospitalization after endoscopic spinal surgery. This single-center retrospective cohort included adults who underwent elective single-level endoscopic spinal surgery under general anesthesia from 2020 through 2023. All 115 patients in the active warming group (AWG) received documented forced-air warming, whereas none of the 135 patients in the conventional warming group (CWG) received active warming. Warmed intravenous fluids were additionally used in 86 AWG patients. The primary outcome was postoperative length of stay (LOS) >3 days. The primary logistic regression model was adjusted for age, sex, BMI, ASA physical status ≥ III, diabetes mellitus, surgical approach, surgical duration, and calendar year. Expanded-model, stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), and categorical-calendar-year sensitivity analyses were also performed. The AWG had a higher median nadir temperature (36.4 °C vs. 35.7 °C), a smaller median temperature fluctuation (0.5 °C vs. 1.0 °C), and a lower incidence of intraoperative hypothermia (19/115 [16.5%] vs. 71/135 [52.6%]); all p < 0.001. Postoperative LOS >3 days occurred in 28 of 115 AWG patients (24.3%) and 59 of 135 CWG patients (43.7%). Documented active warming was associated with lower adjusted odds of prolonged postoperative hospitalization (OR 0.52, 95% CI 0.30-0.89; p = 0.018), with similar estimates in the expanded model (OR 0.54, 95% CI 0.31-0.94; p = 0.029), stabilized-IPTW analysis (OR 0.50, 95% CI 0.30-0.84; p = 0.008), and categorical-calendar-year sensitivity analysis (OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.30-0.92; p = 0.024). Documented active warming was associated with more favorable intraoperative thermal profiles and lower adjusted odds of postoperative LOS >3 days. The retrospective, nonrandomized design precludes causal inference and subgroup-specific treatment conclusions.

articles.title: Transbronchial Cryobiopsy for the Diagnosis of Peripheral Pulmonary Lesions: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Study.
