articles.abstract: Peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs) are increasingly detected by chest computed tomography, yet bronchoscopic diagnosis remains challenging for small and distal lesions. This prospective, single-center, randomized controlled study evaluated radial endobronchial ultrasound combined with a guide sheath (R-EBUS-GS)-assisted transbronchial cryobiopsy using a 1.1-mm ultrathin cryoprobe. Fifty patients with PPLs were randomized after successful R-EBUS-GS localization to either transbronchial cryobiopsy (TBCB) or conventional transbronchial lung biopsy with forceps (TBLB), with 25 patients in each group. The prespecified primary endpoint was pathological diagnostic yield. Pathological diagnostic yield was 84.0% in the TBCB group and 64.0% in the TBLB group; the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.107). TBCB yielded a greater maximum total histologic tissue area than TBLB (14.6 ± 4.2 mm2 vs. 3.1 ± 0.9 mm2, p < 0.001) and was associated with a lower frequency of severe crush artifact (8.0% vs. 52.0%, p < 0.001). Grade 2 bleeding occurred in 32.0% and 24.0% of patients, respectively, and no Grade 3 bleeding occurred. One patient in the TBCB group developed pneumothorax and recovered with conservative treatment. These findings show that R-EBUS-GS-assisted 1.1-mm ultrathin cryobiopsy is technically feasible for PPL sampling and provides larger, better-preserved histologic specimens, while improvement in pathological diagnostic yield was not statistically demonstrated in this small randomized cohort.

articles.title: Metagenomic Next-Generation Sequencing of Mycoplasma hominis Infection in an Immunocompromised Patient: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Mycoplasma hominis is an underrecognized opportunistic pathogen that can cause extra-genitourinary infections, particularly in immunocompromised hosts. This case report describes a persistent soft tissue infection following a wooden splinter injury in a 52-year-old immunocompromised man, in whom M. hominis was identified by blood mNGS after conventional microbiological investigations were inconclusive. The patient developed recurrent fever, wound pain, swelling, and exudation. Empirical treatment with ertapenem and subsequent surgical intervention did not provide sustained clinical improvement, while conventional microbiological investigations remained inconclusive. Peripheral blood was therefore analyzed by mNGS, which detected M. hominis, human betaherpesvirus 5, and GB virus C. For M. hominis, nine species-specific reads were identified, with a relative abundance of 21.5% for the genus Mycoplasma and 99% confidence for species-level identification. The mNGS finding was interpreted together with the refractory clinical course and the absence of a convincing alternative bacterial pathogen. Following further surgical management and multidisciplinary evaluation, targeted antimicrobial therapy with intravenous moxifloxacin plus omadacycline was administered, followed by oral omadacycline after discharge. The patient subsequently became afebrile, pain improved, and inflammatory markers progressively declined. This case demonstrates the potential utility of blood mNGS for identifying an atypical pathogen in an immunocompromised patient with culture-negative, treatment-refractory infection. The findings also emphasize that low-read mNGS results should be interpreted in conjunction with clinical findings, conventional microbiological investigations, and treatment response.

articles.title: miR-200c-3p: An Adjunct Chronic Heart Failure Risk Marker Modulating Cardiomyocyte Hypertrophic Transcription and Cardiac Fibroblast Fibrosis.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated circulating microRNA-200c-3p (miR-200c-3p) for diagnosis and prognosis in chronic heart failure (CHF) and its regulatory roles in cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and myocardial fibrosis in vitro. A single-center prospective cohort included 150 CHF patients and 80 healthy controls, with CHF stratified into heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF), and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) subgroups. Serum miR‑200c‑3p was quantified by quantitative real‑time polymerase chain reaction (qRT‑PCR), N‑terminal pro‑B‑type natriuretic peptide (NT‑proBNP) and inflammatory markers were measured with a fully automated analyzer, and all subjects underwent a 1‑year follow‑up, with correlation, receiver operating characteristic (ROC), Kaplan-Meier, and multivariate Cox regression analyses evaluating its clinical associations and diagnostic and prognostic performance. Gain‑ and loss‑of‑function tests and cell counting kit‑8 (CCK‑8) assays were performed in primary neonatal rat ventricular myocytes (NRVMs) and primary-derived immortalized human cardiac fibroblasts (HCFs). Serum miR‑200c‑3p was significantly elevated in CHF and increased with higher New York Heart Association (NYHA) class, yielding a diagnostic area under the curve (AUC) of 0.86 that improved to 0.90 when combined with NT‑proBNP (DeLong test, p < 0.05); it showed numerically higher AUC and specificity but lower sensitivity than NT‑proBNP in the HFpEF subgroup, and correlated with heart failure and inflammatory markers rather than demographic factors. In NRVMs, angiotensin II (Ang II) upregulates miR‑200c‑3p and hypertrophic marker transcription with its overexpression enhancing the hypertrophic transcriptional program, while in HCFs, transforming growth factor‑β1 (TGF‑β1) upregulates miR‑200c‑3p and profibrotic marker transcription with its overexpression further boosting fibrotic transcription and cell proliferation, and miR‑200c‑3p inhibition attenuates all resulting transcriptional and proliferative abnormalities. miR‑200c‑3p is a potential adjunct biomarker for CHF, offering high‑specificity auxiliary value for HFpEF verification, predicting poor prognosis, and modulating transcriptional and cellular phenotypes linked to cardiac remodeling.

articles.title: A Behavioral Paradigm for Investigating Stress-Induced Anxiety-Like States In Drosophila melanogaster.
articles.abstract: Animals exhibit behavioral changes following exposure to aversive stimuli, and these responses often generalize across contexts, providing a useful framework for investigating stress-induced and anxiety-like states. Traditional rodent assays such as the elevated plus maze, open field test, and light-dark box have been instrumental in characterizing anxiety-like behavior, yet additional complementary models are needed to capture the diversity and complexity of these states across species. Here, an assay for Drosophila melanogaster, designed to quantify stress-induced behavioral responses, was used to study the mechanisms underpinning anxiety-like states. Flies are first exposed to a strong electric shock or heat shock and subsequently tested in a two-arm choice arena offering a narrow versus a wide arm. Following exposure to aversive stimuli, flies display robust avoidance of the narrow arm, exhibiting a claustrophobia-like behavioral shift consistent with a sustained and generalized anxiety-like state. This assay provides a simple, scalable, and ethologically relevant approach for studying stress-induced behavioral modulation in Drosophila, expanding the toolkit available for modeling anxiety-related states.

articles.title: The Effect of Alzheimer's Disease and Diabetes on the Volume of Brain Structures.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) and diabetes mellitus (DM) are increasingly prevalent chronic disorders with overlapping effects on brain structure. However, direct volumetric comparisons among patients with AD alone, DM alone, both conditions, and healthy controls remain limited. This retrospective study compared regional brain volumes in 160 adults (18-90 years) assigned equally to four groups (n = 40 each): AD+type 1 DM, AD-only, type 1 DM-only, and healthy controls. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans were analyzed using VolBrain, an automated, multiatlas, patch-based segmentation platform, on 3D T1-weighted magnetization-prepared rapid gradient-echo (MPRAGE) images acquired at 1.5 T. Regions evaluated included white and gray matter, subcortical structures, selected cortical gyri, and the ventricular system. Analyses were stratified by sex. No significant volumetric differences were observed between the AD+DM and AD-only groups. Compared with DM-only, differences were limited to the right amygdala (p = 0.004) and left thalamus (p = 0.001) in females. Relative to controls, both AD groups showed reductions in the bilateral amygdala, bilateral caudate, right thalamus, and middle temporal gyrus, together with third-ventricle enlargement (all p ≤ 0.005). The DM-only group showed fewer abnormalities. Reduced left caudate volume was the only finding consistently observed across all patient groups and both sexes (p ≤ 0.007). Overall, AD and DM showed partially overlapping regional differences in brain volume. The consistent left caudate reduction may represent a shared structural marker and warrants further prospective and longitudinal investigation in AD-DM comorbidity.

articles.title: Addition of probenecid to beta-lactam antibiotics in the treatment of skin and soft tissue infections: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Among patients presenting to hospital with skin and soft tissue infection (SSTI), up to 50% have already failed oral antibiotic treatment and 90% receive intravenous (IV) antibiotics.Probenecid prolongs serum concentrations of beta-lactam antibiotics. Probenecid-boosted oral treatment may be an alternative to IV. Alternatively, probenecid could allow less frequent dosing of narrow-spectrum IV agents (e.g. cefazolin), reducing dependence on ceftriaxone in ambulatory settings. This systematic review evaluated the effectiveness and safety of probenecid combined with beta-lactam antibiotics for SSTI treatment.

METHODS: MEDLINE and EMBASE were searched through February 2026. Eligible studies assessed the addition of probenecid to beta-lactam therapy in human participants with SSTIs and reported clinical outcomes or adverse effects.

RESULTS: Nine studies (over 1600 participants) were included, most evaluating once-daily IV cefazolin plus probenecid versus ceftriaxone or more frequent cefazolin dosing. Treatment success, failure, relapse and hospital admission rates were similar between groups, indicating that probenecid-boosted cefazolin performs comparably to standard regimens while offering a narrower-spectrum alternative to ceftriaxone. Evidence for oral beta-lactams plus probenecid was more limited but did not suggest inferiority. Adverse events, inconsistently reported, were generally mild and predominantly gastrointestinal, with possibly higher rates in the probenecid-containing regimens.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence suggests probenecid may enable once-daily IV cefazolin as an alternative to ceftriaxone for SSTI, supporting narrower-spectrum antibiotics in ambulatory care. Evidence for using oral beta-lactams plus probenecid remains limited. A robust RCT is needed to determine clinical non-inferiority and acceptability of adverse effects. If effective, this approach could reduce IV complications, healthcare attendance and costs.

articles.title: An Aliquoting Strategy for Commercial Gallium-68 Radiopharmaceutical Cold Kits.
articles.abstract: Gallium-68 radiopharmaceutical cold kits have simplified routine positron emission tomography (PET) radiopharmaceutical preparation, but their cost remains a major limitation. We developed and implemented a simple aliquoting strategy for two commercial 68Ga cold kits of edotreotide and gozetotide, enabling two independent radiolabeling procedures from a single kit vial on the same day. Following reconstitution, each kit was divided into two equal aliquots; the second aliquot was stored at 2-8 °C and radiolabeled 4-6 h later. The procedure uses standard radiopharmacy equipment and preserves preparation times of approximately 30 min for edotreotide and 25 min for gozetotide. Before routine implementation, the modified process was validated in-house through 3 independent batches assessed by radio-thin-layer chromatography (rTLC), radio-high-performance liquid chromatography (rHPLC), pH, and sterility testing. Over approximately 30 months, 100 edotreotide and 122 gozetotide kits were aliquoted, yielding 200 [68Ga]Ga-edotreotide and 244 [68Ga]Ga-gozetotide preparations. Mean radiochemical purity (RCP) was 99.31% ± 0.87% for [68Ga]Ga-gozetotide, with no preparation below 95%. For [68Ga]Ga-edotreotide, the mean RCP was 95.47% ± 3.94%; 52/200 preparations (26.0%) exceeded at least one individual impurity limit (either free 68Ga or 68Ga colloids), indicating lower process robustness. Aliquoting reduced the theoretical radiopharmaceutical cost per patient dose by 38.6% for gozetotide and 35.7% for edotreotide. After accounting for the 26.0% edotreotide non-conformity rate in a replacement sensitivity analysis, the estimated edotreotide cost reduction remained 19.0%, and total annual savings at our institution were approximately 111,000 €. This kit-specific strategy can improve cold-kit utilization and reduce costs, but requires rigorous in-house validation and quality control.

articles.title: Identification and Validation of Autophagy- and Inflammatory-Related Genes in Childhood Asthma via Integrated Bioinformatics and Clinical Samples.
articles.abstract: Childhood asthma (CA) is a prevalent chronic airway disease, yet the roles of autophagy and inflammation in its pathogenesis remain poorly understood. Transcriptomic datasets were retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). Inflammation- and autophagy-related genes were identified using weighted gene co-expression network analysis and consensus clustering and intersected with differentially expressed genes (DEGs) to identify candidate genes. Subsequently, 101 machine learning algorithm combinations were evaluated to select key genes for diagnostic model construction. Functional characterization involved immune infiltration analysis, gene set enrichment analysis, and transcription factor network construction. Mendelian randomization (MR) was used to assess potential causal relationships between key genes and CA, and gene expression was validated by quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) in clinical blood samples. The analysis identified 39 candidate genes associated with autophagy and inflammation. Machine learning identified 10 key genes, and the resulting diagnostic model achieved areas under the curve of 0.768, 0.751, and 0.710 in the training, test, and validation sets, respectively. Pathway and immune infiltration analyses revealed enrichment in signaling, metabolic, and immune-regulatory functions and significant correlations with immune cell infiltration. MR analysis suggested a potential causal association between genetically predicted STYXL1 expression and CA risk. qPCR analysis in five CA patients and five healthy controls showed expression patterns consistent with the transcriptomic findings. However, the small clinical validation cohort limits the generalizability of these results. This study identifies a 10-gene peripheral blood diagnostic signature associated with CA and highlights STYXL1 as a potential causal risk gene supported by genetic evidence. Larger clinical cohorts and functional studies are required to validate these findings.

articles.title: Colonoscopy surveillance after colorectal cancer surgery: meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Colonoscopy surveillance is recommended following colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery, yet the evidence supporting the recommendations has major quality issues. This study assessed the independent impact of colonoscopy surveillance within 5 years after CRC surgery.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted. Medline, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception until 18 June 2026 for randomized clinical trials comparing follow-up protocols including colonoscopy surveillance (intervention) to those without colonoscopy surveillance (control) within 5 years after CRC surgery. Risk of bias was assessed using the RoB 2 tool. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted to estimate the strength of associations with recurrence detection, reoperation rate, and survival. The number needed to scope (NNS) to detect one recurrence and health economic considerations were estimated. The study protocol has been registered in PROSPERO.

RESULTS: Of 4381 records, five trials with 2337 patients were included. Four trials enrolled patients between 1983 and 1994, predating subsequent advances in CRC treatment. All trials used additional surveillance modalities, leading to a high risk of bias. Follow-up protocols with colonoscopy were not associated with recurrence profile, with risk ratios (RRs) of 0.74 (95% confidence interval (c.i.) 0.32 to 1.69), 1.23 (95% c.i. 0.93 to 1.63), and 0.93 (95% c.i. 0.76 to 1.14) for intraluminal, locoregional, and distant recurrence, respectively. Colonoscopy during follow-up was associated with a higher rate of asymptomatic recurrence (RR 2.38; 95% c.i. 1.53 to 3.69). More curative-intent reoperations were performed in the intervention than control group (RR 1.66; 95% c.i. 1.16 to 2.37), but this was not translated into improved survival (hazard ratio 0.92; 95% c.i. 0.77 to 1.11). The NNS was 159 (95% c.i. 101 to 267), resulting in estimated cost per colonoscopy-detected recurrence of €104 100 (95% c.i. €66 200 to 174 900).

CONCLUSION: Current evidence from randomized trials does not clearly demonstrate that postoperative colonoscopy surveillance improves survival, although interpretation is limited by the age of the trials and confounding from concurrent surveillance modalities. Contemporary randomized trials are required to better define the independent contribution of colonoscopy within modern multimodal surveillance pathways.

articles.title: Network Pharmacology Identifies Stigmasterol as an Anti-Gastric Cancer Agent Targeting HSP90AA1 for Ubiquitin-Mediated Degradation.
articles.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) remains a major cause of cancer mortality. We combined network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, public database analyses, and cell-based assays to investigate stigmasterol and heat shock protein 90 alpha family class A member 1 (HSP90AA1). Computational screening prioritized HSP90AA1 as a candidate target. In AGS and MKN-45 cells, stigmasterol treatment reduced cell viability and DNA synthesis, increased the proportion of Annexin V-positive cells, and decreased HSP90AA1 protein abundance. No statistically significant change in HSP90AA1 mRNA abundance was detected under the conditions tested. Increased ubiquitin signal in HSP90AA1 immunoprecipitates and attenuation of protein loss by MG-132 were consistent with proteasome involvement. Public database analyses showed higher HSP90AA1 expression in GC tissues and an association with clinical stage. These findings link stigmasterol treatment to HSP90AA1 downregulation in GC cells. Direct binding, the contribution of HSP90AA1 loss to the cellular effects, and in vivo efficacy remain to be established.

articles.title: Selective Laser Trabeculoplasty versus Latanoprost: A Randomized OCT Angiography Study of Retinal Microvascular Changes in Glaucoma and Ocular Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
PRCIS: SLT and latanoprost achieved significant IOP reduction, while macular and peripapillary OCT-A-derived vascular parameters remained largely stable over 6 months in treatment-naïve patients with early-stage POAG and OHT.

PURPOSE: To compare the effects of selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT) and topical latanoprost 0.005% treatments on macular and optic nerve head (ONH) microvascular parameters in patients with newly diagnosed early-stage primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) and ocular hypertension (OHT), using optical coherence tomography angiography (OCT-A).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Sixty eyes of 60 patients with POAG (n=33) and OHT (n=27) were included and randomized into SLT (n=30) and latanoprost (n=30) groups. OCT-A measurements were obtained at baseline, week 2, and months 1, 3, and 6. Macular superficial capillary plexus vessel density (VD) was assessed using 6×6 mm scans, and radial peripapillary capillary (RPC) VD was evaluated using 4.5×4.5 mm ONH scans. Intra- and inter-group comparisons were performed.

RESULTS: At week 2, intraocular pressure (IOP) levels were significantly lower in the SLT group than in the latanoprost group (P=0.033), with greater IOP reduction from baseline (P=0.031). Both groups showed significant IOP reductions at months 1, 3, and 6 (all P<0.001). At month 3, the increase in inferior hemisphere RPC VD was significantly greater in the SLT group (P=0.028), whereas at month 6, the increase in inferior hemisphere perifoveal VD was greater in the latanoprost group (P=0.028). Baseline IOP was strongly negatively correlated with 6-month IOP change in both groups (P<0.001), indicating greater IOP reduction in eyes with higher baseline IOP.

CONCLUSION: Both treatments provided significant IOP reduction, while macular and ONH microvascular parameters remained largely stable over the 6-month follow-up. The clinical significance of this vascular stability requires further investigation in longer-term studies.

articles.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Non-Pharmacological Interventions for Management of Post-Orthodontic Pain: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Orthodontic pain is the most common adverse reaction during fixed appliance therapy and significantly impairs patients' quality of life. This study aimed to comprehensively compare and rank the analgesic efficacy of nine non-pharmacological interventions for orthodontic pain at multiple clinically relevant time points following orthodontic activation. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and CNKI were systematically searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of non-pharmacological interventions for orthodontic pain, and risk of bias was assessed using the Risk of Bias 2.0 (RoB 2.0) tool. A Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis was performed at each prespecified time point (2 h, 6 h, 12 h, 24 h, 48 h, and 72 h); treatment effects were expressed as mean differences (MDs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs), and the hierarchy of interventions was described using SUCRA values. Twenty RCTs comprising 1,074 participants were included. The analgesic effects were time-dependent. At 2 h, all interventions significantly reduced pain compared with the control, with acupressure (SUCRA 93.1%) and music therapy (90.1%) ranking highest. At 6 h, acupressure, music therapy, and TENS were significant (SUCRA 92.9%, 92.8%, 65.4%), whereas TEAS and VBM were not. No intervention was significant at 12 h. At 24 h, music therapy and CBT were significant, with CBT ranking first (SUCRA 91.3%). At 48 h, acupressure, music therapy, and CBT were significant. At 72 h, music therapy remained significant (MD = 12.2, 95% CrI [0.57, 25.59]). Acupressure and music therapy were consistently ranked among the top two at most time points, except at 24 h when CBT ranked first. Given inter-study heterogeneity and sparse evidence at certain time points, these findings warrant confirmation in large-scale, rigorous RCTs.

articles.title: All-cause and cause-specific mortality in people with rare autoimmune rheumatic diseases in England using whole population data.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: People with rare autoimmune rheumatic diseases (RAIRD) experience morbidity and premature mortality due to disease activity and immunosuppression. We conducted a nationwide, whole-population retrospective cohort study using linked routinely collected healthcare data in England.

METHODS: All individuals in England with a RAIRD diagnosis recorded in hospital admissions data and alive in 2013 were included. Linked demographic and death certificate data were used to calculate crude and age-sex-standardised mortality rates for all causes and leading causes of death from 2013 to 2020. Rates were compared with Office for National Statistics data for the general population of England.

RESULTS: There were 53,237 deaths among people with RAIRD. The cohort was 69.9% female, median age rose from 61.5 to 62.5 years during the study. All-cause mortality declined between 2013 and 2019 but rose in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic. The age-sex-standardised mortality rate ratio versus the general population decreased from 2.6 (95% CI 2.6-2.7) in 2013 to 2.3 (2.2-2.3) in 2020. Mortality was particularly elevated for infection (rate ratio 4.10, 3.81-4.39), cardiovascular disease (2.50, 2.45-2.55), COVID-19 (2.74, 2.59-2.89) and respiratory disease (2.90, 2.82-2.98). Highest all-cause mortality occurred in systemic sclerosis, polymyositis/dermatomyositis, microscopic polyangiitis and unspecified arteritis. Deaths from opportunistic infections were rare.

CONCLUSIONS: Mortality in RAIRD remains more than twice that of the general population despite modest improvement over time. Infection, respiratory disease and COVID-19 remain major contributors, highlighting the need for targeted infection prevention and cardiovascular risk management.

articles.title: Combination advanced therapy use and infection risks in immune-mediated inflammatory diseases.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate real-world evidence on combination advanced therapy (CAT) exposures and safety in patients with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs).

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective new-user cohort study of individuals initiating advanced therapies between 2016 to 2023 using MarketScan® databases. We assessed for overlapping (≥30 days) exposures to different targeted synthetic or biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (ts/bDMARD) classes (CAT episodes). We described baseline characteristics and calculated multivariate hazard ratios (HRs) for first CAT episode persistence. We estimated HRs for first serious infection (i.e. requiring hospitalization or intravenous antibiotics) comparing combined versus single advanced therapy, stratified by CAT regimens and IMIDs.

RESULTS: A total of 270,198 individuals initiated 693,375 advanced therapy episodes, including 38,456 (14.2%) who started 52,212 CAT episodes. The most common IMIDs among CAT users were psoriasis, inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis and axial spondyloarthritis (AxSpA). Among CAT episodes, 51.2% involved TNFi exposure. Median duration of first CAT exposure was 42 days. CAT was associated with 5.2 serious infections per 100 person-years, yielding a HR of 1.61 (95% CI: 1.46-1.78) compared to monotherapy. Anti-adhesion agents combined with TNFi was associated with serious infection (HR 1.49, 95% CI 1.09-2.04) compared to other combinations. In IMID-stratified analysis, CAT (versus monotherapy) was associated with higher risk of serious infection across all diseases, except AxSpA.

CONCLUSIONS: CAT was predominantly used within the spondyloarthritis umbrella of diseases. CAT exposure was associated with short duration and increased serious infection risk, although this risk varied by CAT regimen and underlying IMID.

articles.title: Impact of emotion regulation on psychosocial and emotional problems in Dutch adolescents with inflammatory bowel disease.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Adolescents with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) are at increased risk of psychosocial and emotional problems. This study examined the role of emotion regulation (ER) to (1) determine the prevalence of psychosocial and emotional problems in adolescents with IBD, (2) examine associations with sociodemographic and clinical characteristics, and (3) evaluate associations with ER strategies.

METHODS: Adolescents (ages 12-17 years) with IBD from three Dutch medical centers completed routine psychosocial screening. Psychosocial and emotional problems were assessed with the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ). Norm comparisons were performed using one-sample t-test on raw SDQ scores, and prevalence estimates were based on age- and sex-specific percentile scores. ER strategies (adaptive, maladaptive) were measured with the Dutch FEEL-KJ. Sociodemographic and clinical data were obtained from medical records/questionnaires. Associations were examined using Spearman correlations and stepwise multiple regression, with psychosocial and emotional problems as outcomes.

RESULTS: Compared with Dutch population-based norms, adolescents with IBD reported significantly higher psychosocial and emotional problems than reference norm groups (p < 0.001). Elevated scores were observed in 64.3% for total difficulties and 42.9% for emotional problems. Maladaptive ER showed strong positive associations with both outcomes. Sociodemographic and clinical characteristics were not significantly associated with psychosocial or emotional problems.

CONCLUSIONS: Maladaptive ER is a prominent correlate of psychosocial and emotional problems in adolescents with IBD, whereas background characteristics were not supported. Targeting dysfunctional ER strategies may facilitate early identification of at-risk adolescents and guide timely interventions.

articles.title: Disseminated histoplasmosis mimicking autoimmune hepatitis as a trigger of secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis in a pediatric patient.
articles.abstract: Patients presenting with hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) are often critically ill, and rapid identification of both HLH and underlying triggers in secondary HLH is essential for successful treatment. We present a case of secondary HLH activated by disseminated histoplasmosis (DH) that mimicked autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) on liver histology and briefly led to an incorrect liver diagnosis. Once DH was identified, he was treated with antifungals in addition to HLH therapies and stabilized. He was subsequently found to have a heterozygous variant of uncertain significance in STAT1. Our case is the first in the literature to describe liver biopsies in a pediatric patient who has DH that had triggered HLH, and due to striking histology that mimicked AIH, important to report.

articles.title: Essential fatty acid status in tube-fed children with medical complexity: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Essential fatty acid deficiency (EFAD) occurs when daily nutrition provisions lack sufficient linoleic acid or a-linolenic acid. Signs, symptoms, and sequelae are nonspecific but impact health and quality of life. The objective of this study was to determine the incidence of EFAD among pediatric patients with chronic, complex healthcare needs.

METHODS: This single-center, cross-sectional study included individuals from a specialty clinic designed for children with medical complexity. Clinically stable, exclusively tube-fed patients aged 4-21 years were prospectively enrolled to collect a serum fatty acid panel. Individual fatty acids, anthropometrics and diet history were analyzed with descriptive statistics and linear regression analysis.

RESULTS: Among 77 patients, the median triene:tetraene (T:T) ratio was 0.022 (interquartile range 0.019-0.028). Overall, linoleic, a-linolenic, and mead acid levels were within standard reference ranges with median levels of 3266, 101, and 22 nmol/mL, respectively. Two patients met criteria for biochemical EFAD with T:T ratios of 0.052 and 0.062. There was no difference in T:T ratio by formula type. There was a negative correlation with daily calorie intake and T:T ratio. Patients identified as overweight had slightly higher average T:T ratios.

CONCLUSIONS: The incidence of EFAD in this cohort was low at 2.6%. Fatty acid profiles do not need to be collected routinely. However, they should be considered if signs and symptoms of deficiency are present or in the setting of other identified risk factors, specifically obesity or additional reasons for calorie restriction below 40 kilocalories per kilogram daily.

articles.title: Development of oxygen-releasing PVA hydrogels for protecting pancreatic beta cells from the hypoxic damage in diabetes.
articles.abstract: Hypoxia during the early post-transplantation period remains a major challenge for pancreatic β-cell survival and function before adequate vascularization is established. In this study, multilayered oxygen-generating hydrogels were developed using physically crosslinked poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) incorporating calcium peroxide (CPO) to support pancreatic β-cells under hypoxic conditions. The hydrogels were fabricated through repeated freeze-thaw cycles, with a CPO-containing core positioned between two catalase-containing outer layers designed to reduce cellular exposure to peroxide intermediates. Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) was employed during fabrication to limit premature CPO hydrolysis. The physicochemical properties of the hydrogels were evaluated through morphological, swelling, and mechanical analyses, while dissolved oxygen levels in the surrounding medium were monitored over 28 days. The developed formulations maintained elevated dissolved oxygen levels over the observation period, with differences depending on CPO loading. Biological evaluations using human pancreatic β-cells (1.1B4) under hypoxic conditions demonstrated that the formulation containing 0.1% (w/v) CPO exhibited higher relative metabolic activity, reaching 170.0 ± 9.1% on day 7, and supported glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. In contrast, the 0.5% (w/v) CPO formulation showed reduced metabolic activity at later time points, increased lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release, and lower INS gene expression. Matched catalase-free controls exhibited lower metabolic activity and greater LDH release than their catalase-containing counterparts, supporting the protective contribution of the catalase-containing outer layers. Overall, these findings demonstrate that the multilayered PVA/CPO-catalase architecture can provide sustained oxygenation while supporting pancreatic β-cell metabolic activity and insulin secretory function under in vitro hypoxic conditions.

articles.title: Primary Prevention ICD in a Contemporary Underserved Population: Factors Associated With Underutilization and Mortality.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Registry studies from 2000-2010 demonstrated underutilization of primary prevention ICD therapy. As heart failure therapies have reduced sudden cardiac death, investigators have questioned guidelines derived from trials conducted two decades prior, particularly in non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) and elderly subgroups. We characterized contemporary referral determinants, decision-making processes, and outcomes of primary prevention ICD therapy in a diverse, under-represented population.

METHODS: In this retrospective single-center cohort study, we reviewed records of all patients meeting Class I criteria for primary prevention ICD in 2019. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with ICD referral, and time-varying Cox models compared all-cause mortality by implantation status through 2022.

RESULTS: Of 559 eligible patients, 345 (62%) were referred and 227 (41%) underwent implantation. Referral was associated with male gender, care coordination by a cardiologist rather than a generalist, and lower social vulnerability index (SVI) score. No decision-making rationale was documented for a plurality of non-referred and non-implanted patients; documented rationales identified potential intervention targets. ICD implantation was not associated with all-cause mortality (aHR 0.74, 95% CI 0.49-1.12). In exploratory analyses stratified by cardiomyopathy type, implantation was associated with lower mortality in ischemic cardiomyopathy (aHR 0.51, 95% CI 0.27-0.95) but not in NICM (aHR 1.11, 95% CI 0.63-1.95).

CONCLUSION: Many eligible patients are never referred for ICD therapy. Female gender, generalist care coordination, and high SVI were associated with non-referral. The exploratory association of implantation with lower mortality in ischemic cardiomyopathy was not significant in propensity score overlap-weighted analyses. The NICM estimate was imprecise.

articles.title: Highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1-species-specific histopathology and viral antigen distribution in migratory and resident wild birds, South Westphalia, Germany 2025.
articles.abstract: In late 2025, Germany faced a major outbreak of highly pathogenic influenza virus subtype H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b, causing high mortality in migratory and resident wild birds and poultry. We examined 16 deceased birds, including Eurasian cranes, geese, a teal, and raptors found in western Germany between October and December 2025. Here, we provide a comparative analysis of light microscopic findings using histology and viral antigen distribution determined by immunohistochemistry, alongside the underlying viral phylogeny. Lesions and viral antigen distribution varied by species, with cranes showing infection in a broad organ spectrum, including the central nervous system (CNS), pancreas, spleen, liver, and kidneys, whereas other species exhibited a more targeted organ involvement. Phylogenetic analysis identified the EA-2024-DI.2.1 sublineage, with cranes forming a monophyletic cluster, which was consistent with the shared roosting/migratory behavior of cranes, although epidemiologic links were not formally demonstrated. In summary, our findings indicate species-specific lesion patterns and viral tissue tropism, which may influence transmission dynamics and environmental shedding.

articles.title: Bare-Metal vs Covered Balloon-Expandable Stents for Transplant Renal Artery Stenosis: A Retrospective Comparative Study.
articles.journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare short- and long-term outcomes of bare-metal (BMS) vs covered (CS) balloon-expandable stents in transplant renal artery stenosis (TRAS).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study evaluated patients who underwent elective stent placement for TRAS between 2016 and 2023. Short-term efficacy was assessed by clinical improvement (resolution of resistant hypertension/hypervolemia) and reduction in serum creatinine (sCr) within 14 days post-procedure. Long-term outcomes included Doppler ultrasound parameters - peak systolic velocity (PSV), acceleration time (AT) and resistive index (RI) - and restenosis/occlusion rates requiring or not intervention. Graft survival at the latest follow-up was recorded.

RESULTS: A total of 40 patients (mean age 58 ± 13 years, 68% male) were treated with BMS (n = 31) or CS (n = 9). Clinical improvement was observed in 71% of BMS and 83% of CS patients (P = 1.00). Median sCr decreased by 26% and 33% in BMS and CS patients, respectively (P = .30). At a median follow-up of 29 months, there were no statistically significant differences between groups in median PSV reduction (47% BMS vs 47% CS; P = .44), AT improvement (36% BMS vs 25% CS; P = .38) or RI increase (15% BMS vs 33% CS; P = .12). In the BMS group, 2 cases of in-stent restenosis occurred (6.5%). In the CS group, 1 stent occlusion occurred (11%), resulting in graft loss. At final follow-up, overall graft survival was 85%.

CONCLUSION: In this pilot study, BMS and CS showed no significant differences in TRAS outcomes. Further studies are warranted to better guide stent selection.Clinical ImpactIn transplant renal artery stenosis, balloon-expandable covered stents achieved clinical, biochemical and Doppler outcomes comparable to bare-metal stents, despite being used in more complex, atherosclerotic and longer lesions. This first direct comparison suggests that covered stents may be a reasonable option when heavy calcification, a friable wall or mural thrombus raise concern for embolisation or rupture, while bare-metal stents remain appropriate for most lesions. The single late covered-stent occlusion with graft loss highlights the need for careful platform selection and antiplatelet management. These pilot data should inform adequately powered multicentre registries rather than directly change practice.

articles.title: Utility of the European Association of Urology risk stratification recommendation to predict likelihood of future kidney stone events.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the predictive accuracy of European Association of Urology (EAU) Urolithiasis guidelines risk stratification in predicting future stone events over 5 years following presentation.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: The EAU Urolithiasis guidelines recommend that follow up of individuals with kidney stone disease (KSD) is guided by whether they are at high- or low-risk of future disease based on their published criteria. We developed a virtual stone clinic (VSC) from UK Biobank (UKB) and All of Us (AoU) data, using diagnostic and operative codes to identify individuals with clinically significant KSD, defined as renal colic or a KSD intervention, individuals were assigned to high- and low-risk groups based on EAU criteria. We evaluated the risk of symptomatic events over the 5 years following presentation using time-to-event analyses, predictive accuracy statistics, and decision curve analysis (DCA).

RESULTS: The VSC included 8449 and 17 233 individuals with clinically significant KSD from the UKB and AoU, respectively. At first presentation, 34% and 28% of the UKB and AoU VSC patients, respectively, were classified as high risk of recurrence based on the EAU criteria. The EAU risk classification system demonstrated limited ability to predict KSD recurrence over a 5-year period, with a time-dependent area under curve (AUC) of 0.61. DCA showed no clinical benefit to risk-stratified follow-up. The only factor associated with prediction of future stone events was a prior history of two or more symptomatic episodes (time-dependent AUC at 5 years = 0.62).

CONCLUSION: The EAU Urolithiasis risk classification system has limited ability to predict future kidney stone events over 5-years; our findings do not support its use to guide risk-stratified follow-up.

articles.title: A Pharmacist-Led Antiplatelet Therapy Stewardship Initiative in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation Receiving Concomitant Oral Anticoagulants and Single Antiplatelet Therapy.
articles.abstract: Concomitant therapy with anticoagulants and antiplatelets in patients with atrial fibrillation and chronic coronary syndrome significantly increases the risk of bleeding with no added reduction in cardiovascular disease risk over anticoagulation alone. The primary objective was to evaluate an evidence-based antiplatelet stewardship service designed to deprescribe single antiplatelet therapy in patients with atrial fibrillation receiving oral anticoagulants and a single antiplatelet therapy for both primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease. This retrospective study included adult patients aged older than 18 years with atrial fibrillation who were seen at a tertiary academic heart failure center and received therapeutic oral anticoagulants and single antiplatelet therapy for any cardiovascular secondary or primary prevention. The primary outcome was the acceptance of the antiplatelet deprescribing intervention by both providers and patients. The secondary outcomes included provider- or patient-accepted antiplatelet deprescribing intervention. A total of 71 patients were included in the final cohort of this study. The most common indication for the antiplatelet therapy was chronic coronary disease at 69.0 % followed by primary prevention at 14.1% and stroke at 11.3%. The most common antiplatelet therapy was aspirin 81 mg once daily (83.1%), followed by clopidogrel 75 mg once daily(16.9%). Among the 71 patients, 54 (76.1%) were on non-guideline directed antiplatelet therapy. Of the 54 recommendations, 50 (92.6%) were accepted by the providers, and 43 of the 50 provider-accepted recommendations (86.0%) were accepted by the patients. Conclusion: A pharmacist-led antiplatelet deprescribing service is feasible in a tertiary heart failure cardiology outpatient setting. Most recommendations were accepted by the providers and patients.

articles.title: Apparent superiority of two-step 70% isopropyl alcohol over chlorhexidine alcohol for skin antisepsis prior to blood donation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The use of chlorhexidine containing agents for skin disinfection prior to blood donation has long been recommended by WHO, with alcohol-iodine solutions or deferral suggested as second line agents for chlorhexidine allergic donors. These recommendations, however, have a limited evidence base being derived principally from expert opinion and extrapolation from studies investigating skin disinfection for other invasive procedures. Australian Red Cross Lifeblood (Lifeblood) policy is for a one-step alcohol-chlorhexidine method as the first line process, and a two-step 70% isopropyl alcohol method for chlorhexidine allergic donors.

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: A retrospective quality improvement analysis of Lifeblood data from 2020 to 2025 comparing rates of bacterial contamination screening (BCS) positivity and transfusion transmitted bacterial infection (TTBI) between donors receiving one-step alcohol-chlorhexidine and two-step 70% isopropyl alcohol for chlorhexidine allergic donors.

RESULTS: 6,732,654 total donations occurred with 66,917 donations from chlorhexidine allergic donors over this period. No TTBIs, nor BCS positive results were identified in the chlorhexidine allergic group, despite expecting 13 (95% CI 12.5-13.5), whilst 2475 (95% CI 2474.6-2475.4) BCS results occurred in the non-allergic group (χ2(1) = 12.93, p = .0003).

DISCUSSION: This data unexpectedly suggests that the two-step 70% isopropyl alcohol disinfection method may be superior to alcohol-chlorhexidine, although a robust randomized trial would be required to satisfactorily answer this question.

articles.title: Transforming Pathological H2S Into a Photodynamic Amplifier: In Vivo Formation of Bi2O2CO3@Bi2S3 Heterojunction for Microenvironment-Adaptive Periodontitis Treatment.
articles.abstract: Current periodontitis management is hindered by the inability to effectively reverse the dysbiotic microenvironment of persistent infection and restore immune homeostasis. Although photodynamic therapy (PDT) presents a promising non-invasive antibacterial strategy, its clinical efficacy remains limited by poor microenvironmental selectivity and insufficient immunomodulatory capacity. Herein, we engineer a microenvironment-responsive "trash-to-treasure" PDT strategy based on Bi2O2CO3 nanosheet-assembled microspheres. This platform actively scavenges excess hydrogen sulfide (H2S) within the periodontal pocket, triggering an in situ transformation into Bi2O2CO3@Bi2S3 heterojunctions. This H2S-triggered conversion neutralizes the pro-inflammatory gasotransmitter and establishes an S-scheme heterojunction with enhanced photocatalytic activity. The resulting reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated oxidative stress, together with targeted disruption of bacterial iron metabolism, enables highly efficient photodynamic eradication of major periodontopathogens such as Porphyromonas gingivalis. Moreover, Bi2O2CO3-mediated scavenging of pathological H2S alleviates inflammatory responses in human gingival fibroblasts and reactivates macrophage respiratory burst for intracellular bacterial clearance. In vivo evaluations in a rat periodontitis model demonstrate effective inflammation resolution, suppression of alveolar bone loss, and robust tissue regeneration. This work introduces an intelligent therapeutic strategy that hijacks pathological H2S as a photodynamic amplifier, establishing a microenvironment-adaptive PDT paradigm for periodontal infection.

articles.title: Benign Schwannoma of the Coronary Sinus in a Child: Diagnostic Pitfalls and Surgical Management.
articles.journal: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
articles.abstract: Primary cardiac tumors in children are uncommon, and cardiac schwannomas occur predominantly in adults. Benign coronary sinus schwannoma in a child represents an unusual presentation with important diagnostic and surgical considerations. We report the case of a 5-year-old child presenting with recurrent exudative pericarditis and signs of progressive heart failure. Initial evaluation suggested inflammatory pathology; however, advanced imaging revealed a mass originating from the coronary sinus. Surgical resection was performed via median sternotomy and cardiopulmonary bypass. Due to dense adhesions, the tumor was removed in fragments with radical excision. The coronary sinus was reconstructed using an autologous pericardial patch. Histopathology confirmed a benign schwannoma (S100 and SOX10 positive). The postoperative course was notable for transient right ventricular dysfunction, which resolved with supportive therapy. No tumor recurrence was observed during 48 months of follow-up. Coronary sinus schwannoma in children may mimic inflammatory pericardial disease. Timely surgical intervention with radical resection and anatomical reconstruction is feasible. This case highlights important diagnostic and surgical considerations in managing an unusual pediatric cardiac tumor.

articles.title: Advanced practice nursing and nurse-led models in systemic lupus erythematosus: A patient organisation-informed narrative review.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo synthesise how nurse-led models and advanced nursing practice are described in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) care and to interpret reported outcomes in light of priorities identified through consultation with patient organisations.MethodsWe conducted a patient organisation-informed narrative review. Two patient organisations contributed via targeted consultations to refine the review question, identify priority outcomes, and support interpretation. We searched three databases from inception to January 2026 for peer-reviewed articles describing nurse-led interventions, service models, or advanced nursing roles involving people with SLE. Two reviewers screened records, extracted data, and synthesized findings using thematic analysis.ResultsOf 376 records, nine articles published between 2016 and 2025 were included; none originated from Africa or Latin America, and only one addressed pediatric care. Nurse-led activity was most often delivered in outpatient and hybrid (in-person/telephone) formats. Five main themes were synthesised: (i) Care coordination and continuity as the "backbone"; (ii) Education and counselling to strengthen self-management and self-efficacy; (iii) Symptom and lifestyle management as central outcomes; (iv) Psychosocial needs and social determinants as part of care; and (v) Advanced competence, training, and variable "visibility" of nursing roles.ConclusionSLE services should formalise advanced rheumatology nursing roles and nurse-led models as part of routine care, with clear governance and escalation processes. Future research should standardise role descriptions and outcomes and evaluate scalable nurse-led models on patient-centred, service, and equity endpoints.

articles.title: Practice Trends and Outcomes of Patients With Turner's Syndrome and Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome Across the United States.
articles.journal: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
articles.abstract: Objective(s)Patients with Turner syndrome (TS) and hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) undergoing single-ventricle palliation represent a challenging cohort. We examined birth admission outcomes in TS/HLHS patients, comparing Norwood and hybrid palliation strategies.MethodsThe pediatric health information system (PHIS) database was queried for neonates with a diagnosis of TS and HLHS. Cohort was divided into Norwood procedure, hybrid, or nonoperative, and outcomes were divided into three time eras (Era 1: 2004-2011, Era 2: 2012-2018, Era 3: 2019-2025).ResultsA total of 157 infants were identified: 27/157 (17%) received no operative intervention, 24/157 (15%) underwent hybrid palliation, and 106/157 (68%) underwent the Norwood procedure only. Overall Stage-1 palliation (S1P) hospital survival was 75% (98/130) for both operative cohorts. Hybrid palliations trended upward over time, while Norwood volumes remained stable. In-hospital survival improved across eras for hybrid palliation (75% vs 87%) and the Norwood procedure (71% vs 89%), although neither reached statistical significance. Of 45 PHIS hospitals performing the Norwood, 38 performed S1P for TS patients; 60% (23/38)used the Norwood exclusively, 8% (3/38) used hybrid exclusively, and 32% (12/38) employed both approaches.ConclusionsOutcomes appear satisfactory with either the hybrid or Norwood strategy, with current survival rates ≥87%, although hybrid palliation was associated with a higher rate of subsequent transplantation. However, 17% of (27/157) TS/HLHS neonates were not offered surgical intervention, presumably because they were deemed to be at higher risk. Given demonstrably improving outcomes among selected TS patients undergoing either procedure, offering S1P more broadly, including to higher-risk TS/HLHS patients, may be worthwhile.

articles.title: Compliance with French Military Health Service guidelines for prehospital transfusion of blood products during forward aeromedical evacuations in Sahel (2015 to 2023).
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The forward transfusion guideline of the French Health Service (FHS) provides guidance for prehospital blood product (BP) transfusion in casualties' evacuations from overseas operations (OO). In Sahel, aeromedical evacuation (AE) teams are provided with lyophilized plasma, packed red blood cells (PRBC), and cold-stored low-titer group O whole blood (CS-LTOWB). The main objective was to evaluate compliance with guidelines for prehospital transfusion of severely injured trauma casualties during forward AE in OO. Secondary objectives were to identify clinical and paraclinical criteria, beyond current guidelines, associated with transfusion, and to describe the factors influencing transfusion rates.

METHODS: A multicenter retrospective observational study was conducted on forward AE missions in the western Sahelian theater between January 2015 and July 2023. Two hundred and six patients evacuated for traumatic injuries, classified as category Alpha or Bravo, were included.

RESULTS: Sixty-four wounded received prehospital transfusion of eighty-nine BP units. Meeting transfusion criteria was associated with the requirement for transfusion (p = 10-7, relative risk (RR): 3.20 with 95% confidence interval (95% CI) [2.29-4.47]). Sixty-five percent of transfused patients did not meet the established transfusion criteria. Isolated heart rate above 110 bpm, modification of complexion, Shock Index above 1, altered mental status, penetrating trauma, pelvic trauma and effusion at Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma (FAST) ultrasound were more frequent within transfused patients. Median transfusion rate was about 25 mL/min [16-50].

CONCLUSION: A prospective evaluation of our findings is needed before proposing a revision to the current FHS guideline, including the addition of exclusion criteria.

articles.title: Correction to 'Effect of Medications for Type 2 Diabetes on Cardiovascular Events and Mortality: A Comprehensive Pairwise and Network Meta-Analysis'.
Association Between Weight Loss on Incretin-Based Therapy and Cardiovascular Outcomes and Mortality: A Systematic Review and Meta-Regression.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The primary aim was to evaluate, using aggregate-data meta-regression, whether body weight loss induced by incretin mimetic therapy is associated with reductions in three-point major adverse cardiovascular events (3P-MACE), individual cardiovascular outcomes and mortality. A secondary aim was to estimate the overall cardiovascular effects of incretin mimetics compared with placebo.

METHODS: A systematic review of placebo-controlled randomized trials was conducted using MEDLINE, EMBASE, CENTRAL and ClinicalTrials.gov. Eligible trials reported cardiovascular hazard ratios (HRs) and weight changes. The primary analysis was an aggregate-data meta-regression, with the prespecified moderator defined as the placebo-adjusted percentage weight difference at the latest reported follow-up time point. Standard meta-analysis was performed to estimate overall treatment effects.

RESULTS: Sixteen randomized trials including 97 199 participants with and without diabetes were analysed. Meta-regression showed no statistically significant association between greater body weight loss and treatment HRs for 3P-MACE, cardiovascular or all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke and hospitalization for heart failure (HHF). These findings do not establish an individual-level or causal relationship. Meta-analysis showed significant reductions in 3P-MACE (15%), cardiovascular mortality (13%), all-cause mortality (12%), myocardial infarction (14%), stroke (13%) and HHF (10%).

CONCLUSION: Greater trial-level placebo-adjusted body weight loss was not significantly associated with lower treatment HRs for the cardiovascular and mortality outcomes examined, including 3P-MACE and HHF. These findings do not exclude an individual-level contribution of weight loss to cardiovascular benefit or establish causality. Individual-participant-level analyses are needed to clarify the relationship between weight loss and cardiovascular outcomes.

articles.title: Melatonin ameliorates renal fibrosis by disrupting the DANCR/QK-mediated stabilization of MALAT1 and inhibiting Galectin-3-dependent macrophage polarization.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Renal fibrosis drives kidney dysfunction in chronic kidney disease via inflammation, oxidative stress, and fibroblast activation. Deciphering its mechanisms is vital for antifibrotic therapy.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: A mouse model of renal fibrosis was established via unilateral ureteral obstruction, with melatonin treatment administered. Exosomes from human kidney 2 (HK-2) cells were characterized and co-cultured with phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA)-induced M0 macrophages. Macrophage polarization was analyzed via flow cytometry. Gene‑interaction studies were performed, including ribonucleic acid (RNA) immunoprecipitation, pull-down, and luciferase reporter assays.

RESULTS: Melatonin treatment decreased metastasis-associated lung adenocarcinoma transcript 1 (MALAT1) expression in TGF‑β1‑treated HK‑2 cells, alleviated collagen deposition, and improved renal function in vivo. Mechanistically, melatonin disrupted the interaction between differentiation antagonizing non-protein coding RNA (DANCR) and the RNA‑binding protein quaking (QK), thereby destabilizing MALAT1 to downregulate Galectin‑3, which in turn inhibited both M1/M2 macrophage polarization. HK‑2‑derived exosomal MALAT1 was transferred to macrophages, promoting polarization, and administration of MALAT1‑overexpressing exosomes abolished melatonin's protective effects in vivo.

CONCLUSION: Melatonin destabilizes MALAT1 by suppressing DANCR-associated QK, thereby reducing Galectin-3 to restrain macrophage polarization and mitigate renal fibrosis. Several limitations exist: a single acute animal model, lack of macrophage-specific MALAT1 knockout mice, and absence of clinical validation.

articles.title: Hypophosphataemia in chronic kidney disease patients in haemodialysis.
articles.journal: The International journal of artificial organs
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The presence of hypophosphataemia is increasing in specific clinical contexts such as alcoholism, sepsis, post-surgery and renal replacement therapies (RRT). However, the prevalence of hypophosphataemia in the literature is not clear and varies with the respective cut-off definition chosen.

METHODS: We searched for relevant literature in Pubmed, Embase and Cochrane Library, with the following key words: hypophosphataemia, CKD and dialysis.

MAIN BODY: Phosphate kinetics are much more complex than kinetics of other small molecules, such as urea or creatinine. Mean hourly phosphate removal in haemodiafiltration was highest during the first hour of the session. Studies shows that removal rate of phosphate was linearly dependent on respective plasma concentration. Dialysis technique, treatment duration, dialyser clearance and surface area are also relevant factors determining phosphate removal.

CONCLUSION: Management of hypophosphataemia in dialysis patients is a hard challenge, and should be based on nutritional counselling and individualized dialytic treatments.

articles.title: Acute mechanical stretch enhances β-adrenergic-protein kinase A signalling and increases susceptibility to ventricular arrhythmias.
articles.abstract: Mechanical stretch can increase ventricular arrhythmia susceptibility during sympathetic activation, but the mechanisms linking stretch to altered β-adrenergic receptor (βAR) signalling, Ca2 + handling and electrical instability remain unclear. We tested whether left ventricular (LV) stretch alters Cav3-associated membrane organisation and enhances βAR-protein kinase A (PKA)-dependent arrhythmogenic signalling. Langendorff-perfused male rat hearts were studied using a fluid-filled LV balloon, with sham hearts fitted with an unstretched balloon. Optical mapping during S1-S2 programmed stimulation showed that LV stretch had limited effects at baseline but altered the response to βAR stimulation, increasing ventricular arrhythmia severity, prolonging APD50, reducing local conduction velocity and steepening APD80 restitution. H89 markedly reduced βAR stimulation-induced arrhythmia severity in stretched hearts, whereas KN93 did not provide comparable protection. LV stretch also increased cardiomyocyte length and altered Cav3 organisation at wheat germ agglutinin (WGA)-defined membrane regions. In isolated LV cardiomyocytes, hypoosmotic membrane deformation did not alter basal caffeine-induced Ca2 + release but enhanced isoprenaline-induced irregular activity and Ca2 +-transient amplitude, both of which were attenuated by PKA inhibition. Hypoosmotic membrane deformation also amplified isoprenaline-evoked PKA activity and increased RyR2 Ser2030 phosphorylation. These findings indicate that LV mechanical stretch alters the ventricular βAR response in association with altered Cav3-associated membrane organisation and enhanced βAR-PKA-dependent Ca2 + instability. KEY POINTS: Left ventricular (LV) balloon stretch has limited baseline electrophysiological effects but increases arrhythmia severity, slows conduction and steepens APD80 restitution during β-adrenergic stimulation. LV balloon stretch is associated with cardiomyocyte elongation and altered Cav3 enrichment at wheat germ agglutinin (WGA)-defined membrane regions. Hypoosmotic membrane deformation enhances isoprenaline-induced irregular activity and Ca2 +-transient amplitude without increasing basal caffeine-induced Ca2 + release. PKA inhibition reduces stretch-enhanced irregular activity in isolated ventricular myocytes and β-adrenergic receptor (βAR)-induced arrhythmia severity in stretched hearts. Hypoosmotic membrane deformation enhances isoprenaline-evoked PKA activity and increases RyR2 Ser2030 phosphorylation.

articles.title: Bachmann Bundle Pacing and Acute Changes in Left Atrial Mechanical Function in Patients With Interatrial Block: A Within-Subject Echocardiography Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interatrial block (IAB) is associated with atrial electromechanical dysfunction and adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Bachmann bundle pacing (BBP) has emerged as a physiological atrial pacing strategy capable of restoring interatrial conduction synchrony. However, its impact on left atrial (LA) mechanical function and hemodynamics remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the acute effects of BBP on atrial mechanical parameters in patients with IAB.

METHODS: In this prospective single-center study, 31 patients with IAB who underwent successful BBP implantation were enrolled. A standardized postoperative evaluation protocol was performed under intrinsic sinus rhythm (SR), right atrial septal pacing (RASP) at atrial lead threshold +0.5 V/0.4 ms, and BBP at 5 V/0.4 ms using a within-subject repeated-measures design. Electrocardiographic and echocardiographic parameters were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models, with additional adjustment for heart rate.

RESULTS: BBP produced significantly greater P wave duration (PWD) shortening than RASP (p < 0.001). Compared with SR, BBP was associated with lower LA volume indices and higher LA emptying fraction and LA expansion index (all p < 0.001), with consistent superiority over RASP at acute postoperative phase. These associations remained significant after heart rate adjustment. The observed acute changes were consistent across partial and advanced IAB subgroups without significant interaction effects.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with IAB, electrical resynchronization during BBP was accompanied by acute changes in LA mechanical parameters compared with SR and RASP. These findings suggest that BBP may represent a promising physiological pacing strategy for patients with atrial conduction disease.

articles.title: Haemorrhagic Transformation in Breakthrough Ischemic Stroke: Clinical Characteristics, Outcomes, and Anticoagulation Resumption Timing-Insights from the ASPERA-R Study.
articles.journal: International journal of stroke : official journal of the International Stroke Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The timing of anticoagulation resumption in patients who experience ischemic stroke despite ongoing anticoagulation and develop haemorrhagic transformation (HT) remains uncertain. We aimed to describe the characteristics and outcomes of patients with HT after a breakthrough ischemic stroke and to explore the association between anticoagulation resumption timing and the model-predicted balance of recurrent ischemic and bleeding risks in this high-risk population.

METHODS: We analysed data from patients with breakthrough ischemic stroke receiving anticoagulation therapy from the multicentre ASPERA-R registry. Analyses focused on patients with HT. HT was defined according to the Heidelberg Bleeding Classification based on brain imaging within 24 hours and categorized as haemorrhagic infarction (HI) or parenchymal hematoma (PH). Anticoagulation resumption and its timing were determined by treating clinicians and were not randomized. Landmark Cox regression models were used to evaluate recurrent ischemic events and moderate-to-severe bleeding after anticoagulation resumption. Restricted cubic spline models and exploratory net clinical benefit analyses integrating ischemic and bleeding risks were used to assess the relationship between anticoagulation resumption timing and model-predicted combined risk, overall and across clinically relevant subgroups.

RESULTS: Among 1,555 patients with breakthrough ischemic stroke, 269 (17.3%) developed HT, of whom 170 (63.2%) resumed anticoagulation and contributed to the restart-timing analyses. At 90 days, patients with HT had higher crude rates of recurrent ischemic events (27.1% vs 13.8%), moderate-to-severe bleeding (7.4% vs 2.8%), and mortality (34.2% vs 17.7%) compared with patients without HT. In landmark analyses, HT was not associated with recurrent ischemic events (HR 1.42, 95% CI 0.85-2.37) but remained strongly associated with moderate-to-severe bleeding (HR 3.39, 95% CI 1.61-7.13). Exploratory net clinical benefit analyses showed that the model-predicted combined risk reached its nadir at approximately 10 days after stroke in the overall HT population, with substantial uncertainty around this estimate.

CONCLUSIONS: HT is a marker of poor prognosis in patients with breakthrough ischemic stroke, with an increased risk of bleeding after anticoagulation resumption. Among selected patients who resumed anticoagulation, exploratory modelling suggested that the combined predicted ischemic and bleeding risk reached its nadir at approximately 10 days after stroke. Given the non-randomized treatment timing and potential for treatment-selection bias, this estimate is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective validation.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Comparing hypertonic saline and mannitol for management of elevated intracranial pressure in adults: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of investigative medicine : the official publication of the American Federation for Clinical Research
articles.abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy of mannitol and hypertonic saline (HTS) in reducing elevated intracranial pressure (ICP). We conducted a comprehensive search of multiple databases to identify eligible trials comparing HTS and mannitol in adults with elevated ICP; only studies that used ICP monitoring to obtain objective measurements were included. The primary outcome was the change in ICP at different time points, and secondary outcomes included changes in other clinical indicators. A total of 16 studies (583 patients, 2,219 episodes) were included. The pooled results showed that HTS was significantly more effective than mannitol in reducing ICP at 30 min, 1 h, and 3 h post-intervention. However, the numerical differences were small. And there were no statistically significant differences between HTS and mannitol groups in ICU length of stay, mortality, or unfavorable Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS) scores. In addition, the increases in cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP), mean arterial pressure (MAP), and serum sodium were significantly greater in the HTS group than in the mannitol group at various time points. While HTS produced a larger ICP-lowering effect, the statistically significant difference was modest. Accordingly, existing synthesized evidence fails to clearly establish whether HTS is superior or inferior to mannitol for reducing intracranial pressure.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Application of the PDCA cycle combined with blended teaching in endocrinology internship training: effects on clinical competence and learning engagement.
articles.journal: Journal of investigative medicine : the official publication of the American Federation for Clinical Research
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Endocrinology internship teaching faces the challenge of integrating theoretical knowledge with complex clinical practice, necessitating innovative teaching models that enhance clinical competence and learning engagement. This study was designed to investigate the effects of the plan-do-check-act (PDCA) cycle combined with a blended learning model in endocrinology internship teaching.

METHODS: This study was a cluster-controlled study. One hundred intern doctors in the Department of Endocrinology were assigned to either an observation group or a control group according to their classes. The observation group received PDCA cycle-based blended learning, while the control group underwent traditional teaching. Departmental exit examination scores, incidence of medical adverse events, teaching effectiveness, doctor-patient communication skills, clinical thinking ability, and learning concentration were compared between the two groups. Normally distributed continuous variables were expressed as mean ± standard deviation. Categorical data were expressed as n (%).

RESULTS: Compared with the control group, the observation group scored higher in departmental exit examinations (theory, practical skills, and case analysis) and showed better teaching effectiveness, doctor-patient communication, and clinical thinking ability (particularly open-mindedness, truth-seeking, analytical ability, and systematization), as well as improved learning concentration (longer online learning duration, more frequent topic interactions, and greater discussion participation) (all P < 0.05). The overall incidence of medical adverse events (medication order errors, blood glucose monitoring errors, and dosage errors) was lower in the observation group (all P < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: PDCA cycle-based blended learning improves teaching effectiveness, clinical competence, and learning concentration in endocrinology internship teaching, and demonstrates high teaching satisfaction.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Age, Insurance, and Social Vulnerability as Determinants of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor After New-Onset Heart Failure: Insights from Epic Cosmos.
articles.journal: Journal of investigative medicine : the official publication of the American Federation for Clinical Research
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Social determinants of health contribute to inequities in heart failure (HF) management, yet how age, insurance status, and social vulnerability index (SVI) jointly influence sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) use remains poorly understood.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate how SVI and key demographic and system-level factors impact SGLT2i initiation following new-onset HF.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the Epic Cosmos, a national, de-identified electronic health record repository. Adults aged ≥18 years hospitalized with a new HF diagnosis between 2021 and 2024 were included, excluding those with prior SGLT2i use, dialysis-dependent kidney disease, or hospice enrollment. SVI was categorized into quartiles from least vulnerable (Q1) to most vulnerable (Q4). The primary outcome was SGLT2i initiation following index HF hospitalization stratified by SVI, age, and insurance types. Secondary outcomes included crude and age-adjusted mortality.

RESULTS: Among 389,986 patients hospitalized with new HF, 81,387 patients (20.9%) were started on SGLT2i. Higher social vulnerability was inversely associated with initiation (Q4 vs Q1 adjusted OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.93-0.98). Younger age was the strongest predictor of initiation (<45 vs 65-74 years: adjusted OR 1.53, 95% CI 1.48-1.59). Commercial insurance was independently associated with higher initiation odds (adjusted OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.18-1.22; p<0.001), as was Medicaid beneficiaries (adjusted OR 1.06, 95% CI 1.02-1.11; p=0.006).

CONCLUSION: In patients with new HF diagnosis, a persistent disadvantage in SGLT2i initiation exists in high-SVI communities. Age and insurance, not social vulnerability alone, are the dominant determinants, highlighting the need for targeted strategies in older adults and payer-level reform.

articles.title: Evaluation of Diabetic Ketoacidosis Outcomes Following the Adoption of a Computer-Based Variable-Rate Insulin Infusion Algorithm.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) management by variable-rate insulin infusion is increasing with the widespread adoption of electronic glucose management systems (eGMS). Herein, we evaluate the implementation of an updated process for DKA management incorporating the eGMS algorithm.

METHODS: An eGMS was implemented within the Cedars-Sinai Health System at our tertiary academic center (AC) and community hospital (CH) in January 2024. We compared outcomes after eGMS implementation (post-GMS) to the previous standard of care (pre-GMS). Adult patients admitted to the intensive care unit with a primary diagnosis of DKA and treated with an insulin infusion between January 2023 and December 2024 were included. We separately evaluated outcomes of hypoglycemia (blood glucose, BG <70 mg/dL) and severe hypoglycemia (BG <40 mg/dL) and treatment efficacy.

RESULTS: In total, 324 patients were included in the pre-GMS and 211 patients in the post-GMS cohorts. There was a decrease in the prevalence of hypoglycemia (pre-GMS: 11.0%, post-GMS: 4.3%, P = .005) and severe hypoglycemia (pre-GMS: 1.90%, post-GMS: 0.00%, P = .047). At AC, the hospital length of stay (LOS) decreased from 8.6 to 6.0 days (P = .012). At CH, insulin drip duration increased significantly (pre-GMS: 26.4 h, post-GMS: 36.7 h, P = .004), but there was no impact on LOS.

CONCLUSION: Updating the DKA process and implementing an eGMS improved hypoglycemia rates throughout the institution. Hospital LOS was reduced at the AC, reflecting standardization and streamlining of the DKA processes.

articles.title: Genitourinary Syndrome of Lactation: Patient-Reported Survey of Symptom Burden, Care Gaps, and Treatment Utilization in the Postpartum Period.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate genitourinary symptoms during lactation and identify barriers to care among postpartum individuals.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional survey study from March to May 2025 using an anonymous, 30-item online questionnaire. Eligible participants were postpartum individuals up to 24 months after delivery. Exclusion criteria included nulliparity, current pregnancy, prior genitourinary disorders, and incomplete responses. Participants were stratified into exclusive, nonexclusive, and nonlactating groups. Primary outcomes included genitourinary symptoms, treatments offered and utilized, and quality of life scores (0-100). Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and multinomial logistic regression (α = 0.05). Qualitative data were assessed using thematic analysis.

RESULTS: Of 1,446 respondents (median age 36 years), 47.65% were exclusively lactating, 14.66% were mixed feeding, and 37.69% were nonlactating. Vaginal dryness was the most common symptom (exclusive: 100%; nonexclusive: 100%; nonlactating: 78.72%), followed by dyspareunia (57.04%, 50.00%, and 36.33%). Functional impairments were prevalent with 76.34% of exclusively lactating participants reporting difficulty with sexual activity. Despite symptom burden, 63.81% were never asked about genitourinary concerns, and only 28.42% were offered treatment. Awareness of lactation-compatible therapies was limited (60.03% unaware). Vaginal estrogen and pelvic floor physiotherapy were most commonly recommended, but to fewer than 30% of symptomatic individuals. Lactation status was significantly associated with symptom presence and treatment patterns (p < 0.001). Themes highlighted severe pain, disrupted intimacy, and lack of provider support.

CONCLUSIONS: Genitourinary symptoms during lactation are common yet inadequately managed. Care models should incorporate routine screening, provider education on lactation-safe therapies, and improved access to multidisciplinary interventions.

articles.title: Examining Racial Disparities in Lower Extremity Amputation Outcomes Among Patients with Diabetic Foot Ulcers in North America: A Multicohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Racial and ethnic disparities in diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) outcomes are well described. We examined whether differences in major and minor lower extremity amputation (LEA) persist after matching for comorbidities, and whether the level of amputation identifies opportunities for earlier limb-preservation intervention.

APPROACH: In this retrospective, propensity-matched cohort study using the TriNetX network (2002-2019), reported in accordance with Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology, adults with DFU were identified by diagnostic codes and stratified by race/ethnicity.
