Minor and major LEA risks were compared with a matched White (non-Hispanic) reference, reporting both relative and absolute risks. We also calculated the high-to-low (Hi-Lo) ratio (major:minor).

RESULTS: Among 388,371 adults with DFU and after matching, Hispanic and African American patients had higher minor, major, and overall LEA risk than White patients (major-LEA absolute risk 3.0-4.7% vs. ∼2.7%; relative risks up to 1.89). Asian patients had the lowest risk. Native American patients had the highest Hi-Lo (major-to-minor amputation) ratio despite no significant increase in major-LEA risk, suggesting potential differences in disease presentation or access to limb-preservation care that warrant further study. Disparities persisted after adjustment for diabetes-related comorbidities and peripheral arterial disease.

INNOVATION: Applied to a multiethnic DFU cohort, the Hi-Lo ratio gave a descriptive view of major- versus minor-amputation burden, most notably in Native American patients.

CONCLUSION: The Hi-Lo amputation ratio may identify populations experiencing disproportionate major limb loss and help prioritize earlier vascular assessment, multidisciplinary limb-preservation referral, and posthealing surveillance. Persistent racial and ethnic differences after matching warrant further study of disease severity, access, and care delivery.[Figure: see text].

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence for Cardiovascular Health Behavior Change: A Narrative Review of Patient-Facing Tools.
articles.journal: Health education & behavior : the official publication of the Society for Public Health Education
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death in the United States and disproportionately affects racial/ethnic minoritized populations, low-income communities, older adults, and rural residents. Behavioral interventions can reduce cardiovascular risk, yet traditional programs face scalability barriers, including high costs and limited reach. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on the efficacy and equity of patient-directed AI tools that support health education and behavior change for cardiovascular health. Using PRISMA-ScR elements, we searched 10 databases (January 2010 to December 2025), yielding 19 empirical studies evaluating Generation 2.0 AI systems aligned with the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (LE8) framework. Of these, five were randomized controlled trials (RCTs), and 14 were nonrandomized (quasi-experimental, observational, or early-stage) studies. AI-enabled interventions such as conversational agents, machine-learning models, and reinforcement-learning systems addressed hypertension, diabetes, heart failure, and related conditions. Among the RCTs, one demonstrated superiority of an AI-powered program over usual care (AI-delivered Diabetes Prevention Program), whereas the remaining four reported outcomes equivalent or non-inferior to standard behavioral care. Effects were most apparent in high-intensity interventions that paired machine learning-based personalization with structured behavioral curricula, although the multi-component nature of these programs limits inference about AI-specific contributions. Across nonrandomized studies, greater engagement intensity was consistently associated with improved cardiometabolic outcomes, although causal attribution to AI-specific mechanisms remains limited. Most studies had small samples, short follow-up, and limited reporting on safety and equity. Technology-intensive interventions were concentrated in higher-resourced settings, and populations with limited health literacy showed reduced engagement. Overall, evidence supports cautious optimism that AI can meaningfully scale personalized cardiovascular prevention; however, realizing that equitable and clinically meaningful impact will require rigorous trials with longer follow-up, explicit behavioral science integration, safety-conscious governance, and equity-centered strategies addressing digital determinants of health.

articles.title: A Further Understanding of Posterior Corneal Astigmatism: An Investigation of Constant and Keratometry-Scaled Components.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Posterior corneal astigmatism is conventionally treated as a fixed against-the-rule vector. This study tested whether it is better described as two components, a constant Base Astigmatism and a component scaling with anterior corneal astigmatism. This study also evaluated a prediction model built on that idea.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective cohort study. Posterior astigmatism was back-calculated from preoperative anterior corneal astigmatism and postoperative refractive astigmatism in 39,752 eyes following cataract surgery with a non-toric intraocular lens, after imputing a value for surgically induced astigmatism. Base Astigmatism was computed as a laterality-specific vector mean in eyes with 0.25 to 1.99 diopters of anterior astigmatism; the residual, termed Keratometry-Informed Astigmatism, was fitted against anterior astigmatism. The resulting model, K6, was compared with Abulafia-Koch, Barrett, PEARL-DGS, Kane, EVO 2.0 and unadjusted keratometry in 24,615 independent eyes, using double-angle plots, centroids and mean absolute errors.

RESULTS: Base Astigmatism was -0.446 diopters at 92 degrees in right eyes and -0.453 at 90 degrees in left eyes. Keratometry-Informed Astigmatism equaled 0.299 of anterior corneal astigmatism. It was relatively consistent in magnitude across meridians, and aligned closely with the anterior steep axis at all magnitudes. The resulting model, termed K6, predicts postoperative astigmatism as 0.701 × anterior corneal astigmatism at its steep meridian, plus the laterality-specific Base Astigmatism, plus surgically induced astigmatism, all combined as vectors. K6 gave the lowest mean absolute error: 0.48 versus 0.50 to 0.70 diopters (D), and the highest proportion of eyes within 0.50 D of prediction, 63% versus 35% to 59%. Its advantage was largest in with-the-rule eyes and at higher magnitudes; Kane performed better in against-the-rule eyes below 2 diopters.

CONCLUSIONS: Posterior corneal astigmatism is well described by a constant component and a component scaled to keratometry. This simplifies astigmatism modeling and improves prediction using keratometry alone.

articles.title: Sense of Agency and Negative Emotional Experiences Among Stroke Survivors: A Patient Journey Map Based on Qualitative Research.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To explore stroke survivors' experiences of sense of agency and negative emotions during recovery, and to develop a patient journey map.

BACKGROUND: Stroke can disrupt perceived control and cause emotional distress, but how these experiences relate during recovery remains unclear.

DESIGN: Descriptive qualitative study nested within a longitudinal study.

METHODS: Purposive maximum variation sampling recruited 13 stroke survivors from a tertiary hospital in Henan, China. Sampling was guided by changes and fluctuations in sense of agency scores across four assessments, from before discharge to six months afterwards. Retrospective semi-structured interviews were conducted six months after discharge. Data were analysed using content analysis and a preliminary stage-theme framework. Reporting followed COREQ.

RESULTS: Three themes and 12 subthemes were identified: illness shock, loss of sense of agency and distress marked by doubts and worries; further loss of sense of agency, intensified negative emotions and passive coping; and rebuilding sense of agency, alleviation of negative emotions and active coping. Physical limitations, disrupted roles, unclear information, rehabilitation setbacks and unmet support needs accompanied loss of agency and distress. Meaningful functional gains, clearer illness understanding, motivation and supportive relationships helped participants rebuild agency.

CONCLUSIONS: Stroke survivors described loss and rebuilding of sense of agency alongside changes in negative emotions and coping. The patient journey map highlights opportunities for continuous, individualised support during recovery.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Nurses should assess agency and emotional distress throughout recovery, particularly during care transitions and setbacks. Understandable information, meaningful goals, feedback on progress and patient participation may support agency. Withdrawal should prompt exploration of emotional concerns and practical barriers rather than assumptions about motivation.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patient or public contribution.

articles.title: Knockdown of mitotically associated long non-coding RNA dysregulates endothelial functions, transcriptome and proteome.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a hypertensive disorder during pregnancy, which is characterized by a wide spectrum of endothelial dysfunction. However, the mechanisms underlying PE-associated endothelial dysfunction remain poorly understood. Our previous RNA-sequencing analysis showed that PE down-regulated mitotically-associated long non-coding RNA (MANCR) in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). Herein, we tested the hypothesis that knockdown of MANCR dysregulates endothelial functions via disrupting the transcriptome and proteome using HUVECs as a cell model. Reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) was conducted to confirm the down-regulation of MANCR in PE-HUVECs. MANCR was knocked down in HUVECs from normotensive pregnancy using antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), followed by functional assays, RNA-sequencing and proteomics. RT-qPCR revealed that PE decreased MANCR in male and female HUVECs. Compared with scrambled ASOs, MANCR ASOs reduced MANCR by 71% and 74% in male and female HUVECs, respectively. Functionally, MANCR ASOs blocked fibroblast growth factor-2 (FGF2)- and vascular endothelial growth factor-A (VEGFA)-stimulated cell proliferation, whereas they did not affect cell chemotaxis and tube formation in responses to FGF2 and VEGFA. MANCR ASOs dysregulated the expression of 37 and 39 genes as well as 97 and 15 proteins in male and female cells, respectively. Bioinformatics analysis predicted that MANCR-regulated genes and proteins in male and female HUVECs were differently associated with diseases and biological functions, many of which are relevant to cell mitosis and hypertension. Thus, down-regulation of MANCR impairs endothelial functions and causes sex-specific disruption of transcriptome and proteome, possibly partially contributing to PE-associated fetal endothelial dysfunction. KEY POINTS: Preeclampsia causes widespread endothelial dysfunction, but the roles of long non-coding RNAs in endothelial cells remain poorly understood. Mitotically associated long non-coding RNA (MANCR) is down-regulated in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) obtained from preeclampsia. We provide the first evidence that down-regulation of MANCR blocks endothelial cell proliferation stimulated by fibroblast growth factor 2 and vascular endothelial growth factor A. We also demonstrate that down-regulation of MANCR disrupts transcriptome and proteome as well as pathways associated with cell division, cardiovascular disease-related processes and immune responses. These findings identify MANCR as a previously unrecognized regulator of endothelial cell function.

articles.title: Clinical Criteria for Imaging in Children at Risk for Pulmonary Embolism.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a rare but serious condition in children. Clinical guidelines for imaging a suspected pediatric PE in Pediatric Emergency Medicine (PEM) are lacking. The computerized tomography pulmonary angiogram (CTPA) is the preferred diagnostic modality for suspected PE in an emergency department. Our study aims to introduce a simplified clinical assessment tool for ordering CTPA in children in the emergency room. This is a retrospective review of patients managed in our Emergency Department from 2000 to 2020. Patients were identified using International Classification of Diseases codes for PE, deep vein thrombosis, or similar diagnoses. The control group consisted of patients with PE symptoms, seen within the same time frame as the study group, who had negative CTPA. Twenty-five CTPA-positive patients were identified. Twenty-three of 25 CTPA-positive patients were aged 13 to 18 years. Common risk factors include protein-losing state (ie, nephrotic syndrome), oral contraceptive pill use, and obesity. Chest pain and tachypnea were the most common complaint and clinical sign, respectively. The hypercoagulability screen was negative in 65% of the patients. The mean D-dimer was 5.27 g/mL, and 6 patients, of whom 4 had saddle PE, had D-dimer > 10. Recurrence of PE and neurologic deficits were noted in 2 patients each. We present clinical criteria for ordering CTPA in children with suspected PE based on data from our center and a literature review of pediatric studies. Further multicenter studies with larger samples are needed to validate our proposed criteria.

articles.title: Correction to "Medication review interventions for adults living with advanced chronic kidney disease: A scoping review".
A retrospective cohort study of a midodrine protocol for the prevention of post-operative hypotension for lower limb arthroplasty and emergency hip fracture surgery.
articles.abstract: Hypotension is a common post-operative complication that is associated with morbidity and mortality. There has been growing interest in the use of midodrine (oral alpha-1 adrenergic vasopressor agent) to increase systolic and mean arterial blood pressure in a variety of clinical applications. Our institution developed a 48-h midodrine protocol in 2020 for patients undergoing elective lower limb arthroplasty and emergency hip fracture fixation. The aim of this retrospective, single-centre metropolitan tertiary hospital cohort study was to evaluate the efficacy of the protocol in reducing the incidence and severity of perioperative hypotension (SBP <110 mmHg) within the first 24 h following surgery compared to the pre-protocol period (primary outcome). Secondary outcomes included frequency of hypotension 24-48 h post-operatively, bradycardia, incidence of MET calls and unplanned critical care admission. In total, 328 patients were identified for inclusion in the pre-protocol group and 298 in the protocol group. Introduction of the midodrine protocol was not associated with a significant difference in the incidence of the primary outcome. There was no statistically significant difference in the incidence of hypotension between groups post-operatively at 24 or 48 h. Of the secondary outcomes, patients receiving midodrine were more likely to be bradycardic in the post-anaesthesia care unit (43.8% vs 55.9%, p = 0.001) and at 24 h post-operatively (40.7% vs 53.8%, p = 0.003).

articles.title: Climate-Driven glacier-lake outbursts in Nepal and emerging infectious-disease risks.
Determinants of optimal number of ANC visits among women of reproductive age in Uganda using modified poisson GLM regression analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antenatal care (ANC) is a critical maternal health intervention that contributes to the prevention of maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality through early detection and management of pregnancy-related complications. Although Uganda has achieved high coverage of at least one ANC visit, continuity of care remains suboptimal, with many women not completing the recommended number of ANC visits. This study examined the determinants of optimal ANC utilization among women in Uganda using nationally representative data from the 2024 Uganda Malaria Indicator Survey (MIS).

METHODS: A cross-sectional secondary analysis was conducted using data from the 2024 Uganda MIS. The study included 3,477 women aged 15-49 years who had a live birth within the five years preceding the survey. Optimal ANC utilization was defined as attendance of at least four ANC visits during pregnancy. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize participant characteristics, while Multiple Correspondence Analysis (MCA) explored underlying patterns among categorical determinants. Associations between explanatory variables and optimal ANC utilization were assessed using survey-weighted modified Poisson regression with robust variance estimation. Crude and adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported. Logistic regression was performed as a sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: Overall, 77.7% (n = 2,702) of women reported attending four or more ANC visits during their most recent pregnancy, while 22.3% (n = 775) attended fewer than four visits. MCA revealed a clear socioeconomic gradient, with optimal ANC attendance clustering among women with higher educational attainment, greater wealth, urban residence, and higher media exposure. In the adjusted modified Poisson model, educational attainment and region of residence were the only factors independently associated with optimal ANC utilization. Women with secondary education (APR = 1.12, 95% CI: 1.03-1.21) and higher education (APR = 1.15, 95% CI: 1.03-1.29) were significantly more likely to complete at least four ANC visits compared with women with no formal education. Regional disparities were also observed, with women residing in Northern Uganda (APR = 1.20, 95% CI: 1.11-1.30) and West Nile (APR = 1.26, 95% CI: 1.17-1.36) demonstrating higher prevalence of optimal ANC utilization compared with women in the Buganda region.

CONCLUSION: More than three-quarters of Ugandan women achieved the minimum recommended four ANC visits during pregnancy; however, important disparities remain. Educational attainment and region of residence were the principal determinants of optimal ANC utilization at the population level. Efforts to improve maternal healthcare utilization should prioritize female education and strengthen region-specific maternal health strategies.

articles.title: A phase Ia first-in-human study of BPB-101, a novel trifunctional antibody targeting the GARP/TGF-β complex and PD-L1, in patients with locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: BPB-101 is a first-in-class, humanized trifunctional bispecific IgG1 antibody targeting the GARP/TGF-β complex, active TGF-β, and PD-L1, with preclinical evidence of immunomodulatory and antitumor activity. This phase Ia study aimed to assess the safety, tolerability, pharmacology, and preliminary antitumor activity of BPB-101.

METHODS: A modified accelerated titration design (6, 20, and 60 mg) was followed by a 3 + 3 escalation (200-1800 mg), with intravenous dosing every 3 weeks (Q3W). Eligible patients with advanced or metastatic solid tumors who had received prior standard systemic treatment were enrolled. The primary objectives were dose-limiting toxicity (DLT), maximum tolerated dose (MTD), and recommended phase II dose (RP2D). Secondary and exploratory objectives included pharmacokinetics (PK), pharmacodynamics (PD), immunogenicity, and preliminary antitumor activity.

RESULTS: At the data cutoff of January 26, 2025, 19 patients with advanced tumors were enrolled. Treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in 15 patients (78.9%), with the most common TRAEs being infusion-related reactions (26.3%), anemia (26.3%), and asthenia (21.1%). Grade ≥ 3 TRAEs were reported in two patients (10.5%), both of whom had anemia, with one patient each in the 400 mg and 800 mg groups. No DLTs or treatment-related deaths occurred, and the MTD was not reached. One patient in the 1800 mg cohort permanently discontinued treatment due to an immune-related TRAE (myalgia). BPB-101 exposure increased approximately dose-proportionately at doses ≥ 800 mg. Peripheral PD assessments showed high receptor occupancy (RO) and reductions in circulating TGF-β1 levels in the 1200 mg and 1800 mg cohorts. The 1200 mg and 1800 mg Q3W doses were selected as RP2Ds for further evaluation. Among 17 patients in the efficacy analysis set (EAS), one achieved confirmed immune partial response (iPR) and seven achieved immune stable disease (iSD). The overall immune objective response rate (iORR) was 5.9% (95% CI, 0.1-28.7), and the immune disease control rate (iDCR) was 47.1% (95% CI, 23.0-72.2).

CONCLUSIONS: BPB-101 showed a manageable safety profile, peripheral PD activity, and preliminary antitumor activity, supporting further evaluation in expansion cohorts.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05869240); part of the study was reported at ESMO ASIA 2025 as an oral presentation. Abstract No: 158O.

articles.title: Seroprevalence of cystic echinococcosis in Iranian working children and a control group: a serosurvey with toxoplasmosis and toxocariasis.
articles.journal: Journal of occupational medicine and toxicology (London, England)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Echinococcosis is among the most significant zoonotic diseases globally, and is caused by different species of the genus Echinococcus. Data on the seroprevalence of the infection in children are scarce. In this research, the seroprevalence of Cystic Echinococcosis among working children and children in control group was assessed in Iran.

METHODS: Blood samples were collected from 364 children aged 7-14 years conducting work such as transportation, carpentry, agriculture, gardening, vegetable cultivation, cattle farming, and fruit picking outside school hours, and from 364 participants in a control group in Tehran, Iran. The IgG enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) test for Echinococcus granulosus was ultimately performed using the Nova Tec commercial ELISA kit.

RESULTS: The seroprevalence of Echinococcus granulosus was 32 (8.8%) and 7 (1.9%) among working and control children, respectively. The seroprevalence of Echinococcus granulosus in working children was significantly higher than that in the control group. The results indicated a statistically significant increase in seroprevalence of Echinococcus granulosus among working children in contact with dogs compared to those who had none. Seroprevalence of Echinococcus granulosus IgG antibodies in working children with agricultural groups like growing vegetables and picking fruits 19(9.7%) and cattle farming 8(22.2%) were higher than in other occupations; these differences were statistically significant. In the present study, out of 32 Echinococcus granulosus-positive antibodies in working children, 26(81.3%) were positive for Echinococcus granulosus, 5(15.6%) were antibody positive for both Echinococcus granulosus and Toxoplasma gondii, and 1(3.1%) had antibodies positive against Echinococcus granulosus and Toxocara canis. In the control group, 6 (85.7%) tested positive solely for Echinococcus granulosus, while 1 (14.3%) was positive for both Echinococcus granulosus and Toxoplasma gondii.

CONCLUSION: A notably elevated rate of Echinococcus granulosus seropositivity was observed in working children related to their occupation compared to the control group. Additionally, it is important to mention coinfection with other parasites, including toxoplasmosis and toxocariasis. The results indicate that echinococcosis poses a significant health issue for children, particularly working children. Considering the multiple cases of hydatid cyst disease in Tehran, it appears essential to implement health programs aimed at managing this parasitic infection.

articles.title: Collaborative Care and Everyday Planning in Care Counselling (CoPlan study): study protocol of a pragmatic randomized clinical trial and protocol changes to quasi-experimental evaluation during recruitment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Family members are the primary source of support for older care recipients. Promoting cooperative strategies between family members may foster shared solutions to care-related challenges. Based on our previous research we developed a dyadic problem-solving intervention that equally addresses the needs of both caregivers and care recipients.

METHODS: This pragmatic randomized controlled clinical trial evaluates the implementation and effectiveness of the intervention under routine conditions within a national care counselling service setting. Due to recruitment obstacles and low participant enrolment the randomized design was modified to a non-randomized study. Main inclusion criterion for caregivers was a positive screening of desire to change the care situation, frequent caregiving challenges, or difficulty managing care. Participants are assigned to either the CoPlan intervention or control group with routine care counselling. Self-reported questionnaires are administered at baseline (t0) and 3 months post-intervention (t2) to collect endpoint data, with an intermediate non-endpoint assessment following the initial counselling (t1). Primary and secondary endpoint comparisons are based on data collected at t2 controlled for baseline values. Primary outcome is the quality of informal care (QiC), main secondary outcomes include caregiver self-efficacy, depressive symptoms, and positive aspects of caregiving. A process evaluation assesses intervention dose, fidelity, and experiences of interventionists, care counsellors of a German long-term care insurance, and participants.

DISCUSSION: This study represents one of the few translational studies in care counselling research. By promoting shared appraisals and open communication in a dyadic approach, the novel counselling method addresses a largely underexplored area. The difficulty in recruiting participants through care counsellors, along with the resulting study design modification, highlights the difficulties of conducting studies within real-world practice settings.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Deutsches Register Klinischer Studien (German Clinical Trials Register), DRKS00032492 . Registered on 5 September 2023 (current status: recruitment completed).

articles.title: Patient-reported oral complaints during cancer treatment: Dietary consequences, supportive care, and self-management in a cross-sectional survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral complaints are common during cancer treatment and may interfere with eating and perceived quality of life. However, patient-reported evidence addressing dental and gingival complaints, xerostomia, taste alterations, counselling, and self-management remains limited.

METHODS: We conducted an anonymous cross-sectional survey among adults in Germany with current or previous oncological treatment using paper-based and online questionnaires (January-June 2025). Analyses were based on valid responses for each item and included descriptive statistics, Pearson's chi-square tests, linear-by-linear association tests, 95% confidence intervals for selected key prevalence estimates, and exploratory multivariable logistic regression sensitivity analyses adjusted for age and gender.

RESULTS: The survey included 222 patients. New, additional, or worsening dental and gingival complaints during cancer treatment were reported by 41.9% (83/198; 95% CI 35.3-48.9%) of respondents. Xerostomia was reported by 56.6% (120/212; 95% CI 49.9-63.1%) and taste alterations by 68.0% (138/203; 95% CI 61.3-74.0%). Self-reported reduced food intake attributed to dental or gingival complaints was reported by 27.9% (57/204; 95% CI 22.2-34.5%), while 25.0% (46/184; 95% CI 19.3-31.7%) reported perceived quality-of-life impairment attributed to these complaints. In exploratory sensitivity analyses adjusted for age and gender, new, additional, or worsening complaints remained associated with reduced food intake (adjusted OR 7.85, 95% CI 3.70-16.62) and perceived quality-of-life impairment (adjusted OR 15.25, 95% CI 5.81-40.06). Among participants with xerostomia, the proportion reporting reduced food intake increased from 5.1% among those with no xerostomia-related eating difficulty to 91.7% among those with severe difficulty (p < 0.001). Overall, 43.1% (87/202; 95% CI 36.4-50.0%) reported receiving support or counselling regarding oral health.

CONCLUSIONS: In this recruited sample, oral complaints during cancer treatment were common and were associated with eating-related burden and perceived quality-of-life impairment. These exploratory associations persisted after limited adjustment for age and gender but do not establish causality. Fewer than half of respondents reported receiving oral-health counselling, although perceived helpfulness was high among recipients, suggesting a potential gap in the reach of such support. These findings support prospective evaluation of repeated, function-oriented oral-health assessment and appropriate dental or nutritional referral rather than demonstrating the effectiveness of these approaches.

articles.title: Protocol for the GAPA person-centred dental care at home intervention: a substudy within a cluster randomised controlled trial in Swedish home care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral health is essential to healthy ageing and closely linked to well-being, social participation, and quality of life. Frail older adults are at high risk of oral diseases, yet oral health is often insufficiently integrated into home care. Care staff frequently report limited competence and unclear routines, while older adults wish to participate actively in decisions about their oral health. GAPA Person-Centered Dental Care @ Home (Dental PCC@Home) is a co-designed model developed with older adults, significant others (informal caregivers), municipal care staff, and dental professionals. This substudy evaluates if Dental PCC@Home will promote oral health, participation, and self-determination among older adults living with complex care needs.

METHODS: Dental PCC@Home is embedded within the parent GAPA cluster randomised controlled trial. Decisions about dental care are guided by a patient decision aid and discussion of needs expressed by the older adult or identified by care staff. Participation in the substudy is voluntary. Eligible intervention-group participants are offered a patient decision aid to support decisions about whether and how to receive dental care, followed by one of four pathways: online dental consultation, mobile home dental care, a dental clinic visit, or declining dental care. Eligible control-group participants receive standard care. Oral health and quality-of-life assessments are conducted at baseline and at six and twelve months; cognitive function is assessed at baseline only. Co-primary outcomes are changes in oral health status (ROAG) and oral health-related quality of life (GOHAI) from baseline to twelve months. General health-related quality of life (EQ-5D-5 L) is a secondary outcome. Quantitative analyses will account for clustering and repeated measurements. Semi-structured interviews with older adults, significant others, and care staff will explore experiences of care, decision-making, and implementation and will be analysed using qualitative content analysis.

DISCUSSION: This project will generate evidence on a new cross-organisational model designed to improve access to oral health care for frail older adults living at home. By integrating dental care into existing care processes and offering flexible care pathways, the model has the potential to strengthen autonomy, reduce inequalities, promote health and, when indicated, address oral diseases earlier in home care. The findings may inform future practice, policy development, and person-centred approaches to oral health in ageing populations.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06310798. Registered on March 13, 2024.

articles.title: Serious Illness Conversation Impact on End-of-Life Care Utilizations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Serious Illness Conversation Programs (SICP) were developed to improve communication with patients with serious illnesses to promote goal concordant care. Limited information is available about whether implementation of an SICP is associated with differential health care utilization.

OBJECTIVE: To determine if care utilization differed for patients with SIC compared to those without.

DESIGN: A retrospective cohort study comparing end-of-life care for patients with and without a documented SIC in a large integrated health system after implementation of a SICP. Patients were included if they received a high serious illness score between January 1, 2022, and December 31, 2024, and they died prior to the end of the study period.

MEASUREMENTS: SIC completion and components. Outcome measures were health care utilization in the last 30 days of life within our health system: inpatient admissions/days, ICU admissions/days, emergency department (ED) visits, palliative care, and hospice enrollment/days.

RESULTS: Hospice use was higher (32.6% vs. 18.8%, p < 0.001) and ICU admissions were lower (10.9% vs. 13.4%, p = 0.007) among patients who had SIC compared to those without. There was no difference in ED utilization or number of palliative care visits. The proportion of patients with inpatient admissions was higher in the SIC group (44.9% vs. 38.6%, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that while SIC may help define care goals oriented toward reduced utilization of intensive care and increased hospice utilization, further evaluation is needed to understand drivers of ED and inpatient care utilization for patients with a documented SIC.

articles.title: Age-stratified clinical phenotypes of cardiac implantable electronic device infections: a 20-year retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The widespread adoption of cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) has been accompanied by a parallel increase in severe CIED infections. Traditional risk stratification frequently relies on binary age cutoffs, which can obscure how infection phenotypes evolve across a patient's lifespan. This study evaluated how advancing age-analyzed across ordered chronological strata-correlates with anatomical infection site, device hardware type, microbiology, and in-hospital mortality in patients with CIED infections.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study of 383 patients treated for CIED infections between 2002 and 2022, patients were categorized into five sequential age brackets (< 50 to 80-90 years). Age was modeled both categorically across these strata and continuously to estimate per-decade odds ratios (ORs) for clinical presentation, hardware type, and microbiological findings.

RESULTS: The cohort was predominantly male (75.2%) with a mean age of 67.4 years. Pacemaker involvement increased significantly with age (p < 0.001), whereas implantable cardioverter-defibrillator use declined (p = 0.036). Localized generator pocket infections demonstrated a pronounced age-dependent gradient, rising from 19.4% in patients under 50 years to 73.0% in octogenarians (p < 0.001; OR 1.43 per decade, 95% CI: 1.21-1.69). Conversely, systemic presentations-including bacteremia and lead endocarditis-showed no age-dependent trend. In-hospital mortality remained low and stable across age groups (p = 0.452) but was markedly higher in patients presenting with bacteremia or sepsis compared to those without systemic involvement (16.7% vs. 1.6%, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Analyzing age as a continuous spectrum reveals a distinct clinical phenotype dominated by localized pocket infections and low-power devices, an insight obscured by standard binary age cutoffs. Crucially, mortality risk was driven by systemic bloodstream infection rather than patient age itself, emphasizing that clinical surveillance should prioritize infection phenotype over chronological age alone.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Attitudes towards vaccination in multiple sclerosis: insights from patients, neurologists, and general practitioners within a qualitative study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: People with Multiple Sclerosis (pwMS) face increased infection and mortality risks due to their disease and potentially immunosuppressive therapy. Comprehensive vaccination is recommended, but reported vaccination rates in pwMS vary, and concerns about safety und effectiveness are discussed as one possible reason.

OBJECTIVES: This study examines the vaccination rates and hesitancy in pwMS from the perspectives of patients, neurologists, and general practitioners (GPs) to identify possible approaches to overcome the hesitation.

METHODS: Between March and December 2023 narrative, semi-structured interviews were conducted with fifteen patients, five neurologists, and ten GPs in Germany. Pseudonymized data were analyzed using Kuckartz's Qualitative Content Analysis with MAXQDA, incorporating deductive and inductive codes.

RESULTS: In total, thirty participants were interviewed. Our findings suggest that some pwMS experience gaps in vaccination-related information and desire more proactive information from physicians. Several participants described that communication between neurologists and GPs was limited and that it was not always clear which physician addresses vaccination counselling and administration. Fear of side effects and misinformation encountered by patients affect vaccination willingness. Patients prefer precise and consistent information materials on vaccination timelines.

CONCLUSION: Misinformation or lack of information may contribute to vaccination reluctance. Addressing patients' concerns with comprehensible information appears to be an important element of vaccination counselling from the perspective of the participants. Our findings highlight the importance of improved communication and education among all parties involved in vaccination.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: German Register of Clinical Studies (DRKS): https://drks.de/search/de/trial/DRKS00031559 (Registration Date: 28.08.2023, retrospectively registered).

articles.title: Disparities in access to digital and traditional mental health services across sociodemographic groups in Australia.
articles.journal: The Australian and New Zealand journal of psychiatry
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Digital mental health services are emerging as viable mental health support options, but uptake in Australia remains low. This study aims to describe both access to traditional mental health services and digital mental health services in Australia, stratified by key sociodemographic factors.

METHODS: Data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics' 2020-2022 National Study of Mental Health and Wellbeing were analysed. Population subgroups were identified based on sociodemographic variables, including sex, gender, age, culturally and linguistically diverse, sexual orientation, Indigenous status, geographic remoteness, history of incarceration and military service.

RESULTS: The highest prevalence of mental health conditions was observed among younger individuals, non-heterosexual populations and those experiencing unemployment or homelessness. These groups also demonstrated the highest levels of engagement with both digital mental health services and mental health services. Culturally and linguistically diverse individuals showed lower prevalence and lower access to both mental health services and digital mental health services compared with non-culturally and linguistically diverse populations. Education, income and household characteristics showed no consistent patterns, while employment and study status were associated with variation in service use, with higher access observed among students and unemployed individuals.

CONCLUSION: Access to mental health services and digital mental health services varies across sociodemographic groups. For several populations, digital mental health services access could not be estimated, highlighting important data gaps. Further research is needed to understand access patterns and potential barriers.

articles.title: Staple Line Reinforcing During Laparoscopic Sleeve Gastrectomy: Comparison of Through and Through vs. Lembert's Oversewing Methods: Single Center Experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUNDS: The most serious stapler line complications (SLC) following laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) are bleeding and stapler line leakage (SLL). Various oversewing methods are used that reduce SLC by reinforcing the staple line (SLR): Through and Through (TaT) or Lembert suturing. In this retrospective study, we compared the effects of the Lemberts and TaT suturing on SLC incidence.

METHODS: A total of 586 patients were included in the study. These patients were divided into two groups: TaT (n = 386) and Lemberts (n = 200). The primary endpoints were SLL and bleeding. Secondary endpoints included postoperative complications, Clavien-Dindo Grade ≥ 3 complications, operative time, oversewing time, length of hospital stay, and mortality.

RESULTS: Operative time was longer in the TaT suturing method (p < 0.001), while oversewing time was longer in the Lemberts suturing method (p < 0.001). The incidence of bleeding and SLL was significantly lower with Lembert's suturing method (p = 0.01, p = 0.04; respectively). All postoperative complications, Clavien-Dindo Grade ≥ 3 complications and length of hospital stay were more seen in the TaT suturing method (p = 0.002, p = 0.02, p < 0.001; respectively ). The incidence of blood transfusions, intensive care unit stay, and readmission rates were similar between the two methods.

CONCLUSION: Compared to the TaT suturing method, the Lemberts suturing method was associated with a reduction in postoperative bleeding, SLL, all postoperative complications, Clavien-Dindo Grade ≥ 3 complications, and length of hospital stay, without causing a major difference in oversewing and total operative time. No differences were found between the two methods in terms of blood transfusion, intensive care unit stay, or mortality.

articles.title: Sleep position and sleep apnea in newborns.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Public health measures recommend that babies sleep supine, but at all other times of life this can worsen sleep apnea. To examine associations between infant sleep position and the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), we studied polysomnograms of neonates with repaired myelomeningocele, who are often positioned nonsupine during wound healing, and of neonates without congenital anomalies who were recovering in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU).

METHODS: We evaluated sleep apnea severity, as reflected by the AHI, in different positions as recorded during polysomnograms from three cohort studies of infants in NICUs. Participants included 173 infants with myelomeningocele (multiple hospitals) and 88 NICU recovery infants across two single-center cohorts. The myelomeningocele cohort was subdivided by repair type (postnatal, open fetal, and fetoscopic surgery groups). We evaluated AHI in different sleep positions using generalized estimating equations to account for repeated measures.

RESULTS: Among 261 neonates, AHI was similar between supine and nonsupine positions in the NICU recovery, postnatal myelomeningocele, and open fetal myelomeningocele groups (adjusted analyses, all p > 0.33). In contrast, the fetoscopic myelomeningocele group had substantially lower AHI when supine (7.94, 95% CI 4.95-12.75) compared to nonsupine (22.1, 95% CI 14.02-35.01; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Surprisingly, sleep apnea in neonates requiring NICU care may not be exacerbated by supine sleep, with possible exceptions in some specific conditions. Although we did not study healthy newborns, we speculate that obligate nasal breathing in neonates may protect against worsening of sleep apnea when supine. "Back to Sleep" remains life-saving and appears unlikely to increase sleep apnea risk.

CURRENT KNOWLEDGE/STUDY RATIONALE: Public health measures to prevent SIDS recommend that babies sleep supine. The degree to which sleep position influences sleep apnea in infants is unclear. We had a unique opportunity to study the position dependence of sleep apnea for neonates in the NICU setting, who sometimes sleep in nonsupine positions. As studies at older ages widely show sleep apnea to be worse supine than nonsupine, we hypothesized that we would find the same in neonates.

STUDY IMPACT: Study results suggest that sleep apnea severity in neonates who require NICU care is not exacerbated by supine sleep. "Back to Sleep" remains a life-saving intervention for infants upon discharge to home and, moreover, does not appear to increase risk for sleep apnea.

articles.title: Recent advances in the mechanisms, management, and nanomaterial-based strategies for root resorption.
articles.abstract: Root resorption (RR) involves the loss of mineralized root tissues and may compromise tooth integrity and long-term retention. Internal and external RR arise in different pulpal and periodontal microenvironments and require etiology-specific management. Although conventional treatment can arrest many lesions, persistent infection, complex resorptive defects, and limited control of inflammatory or clastic-cell activity remain therapeutic challenges. This narrative review summarizes RR classification, clinical management, and key mechanisms, including protective-tissue disruption, receptor activator of nuclear factor-κB ligand (RANKL)-dependent clastic-cell activation, inflammatory signaling, and mechanotransduction, and evaluates nanomaterial-based approaches by function. Potential benefits are weighed against cytotoxicity, local retention, effects on physiological remodeling, and the risk of inappropriate bone formation or ankylosis. Most current evidence remains preclinical, and substantial challenges related to efficacy, safety, targeting, manufacturing, and clinical validation must be addressed before clinical translation. Whether nanomaterials developed for bone resorption can be adapted to promote cementum-like repair of the resorbed root surface remains a hypothesis requiring RR- and cementum-specific validation.

articles.title: Contemporary clinical course of compensated advanced chronic liver disease in a multistate framework.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Compensated advanced chronic liver disease (cACLD) encompasses patients with advanced fibrosis/cirrhosis at risk for liver-related complications. The natural history of cACLD has been extrapolated from compensated cirrhosis and historic cohorts, although major advances in diagnosis and management have impacted the clinical course and understanding of disease trajectories.

METHODS: From 2015 to 2022, 1140 consecutive patients with cACLD (first-time liver stiffness measurement [LSM] ≥10 kPa) at the Vienna General Hospital were followed for first and further decompensation, and death. Baseline data (age, sex, etiological cure, LSM, MELD, platelet count, and albumin) were incorporated into a multistate modelling framework to investigate transition-specific associations.

RESULTS: 42% had steatotic liver disease and 37% viral hepatitis. Median LSM at baseline was 16 kPa, and 93% had Child-Turcotte-Pugh stage A. Median follow-up was 3.9 years. Two and 5-year probabilities were: 89%/74% to remain compensated, 3.7%/3.6% for first decompensation, 0.6%/2.1% for further decompensation, 3.7%/12% for liver-related and 2.8%/7.9% for non-liver-related death. LSM ≥15 kPa and ANTICIPATE±NASH ≥75% identified subgroups at particular risk for hepatic decompensation (5.7% vs. 1.5%/ 9.1% vs. 2.1% at 2 years) and liver-related death, but not for non-liver-related death, which was as frequent as hepatic decompensation in those with LSM <15 kPa. LSM and markers of liver dysfunction predicted hepatic decompensation, whereas etiological cure and platelet count were associated with further decompensation.

CONCLUSION: The risk of hepatic decompensation in contemporary patients with cACLD is lower than in previous reports on compensated cirrhosis. Hepatic decompensation accelerates disease progression.

articles.title: Racial and Ethnic Disparities in Stroke Among Hypertensive Adults by Antihypertensive Medication Use in the United States.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite improvements in hypertension management, racial and ethnic disparities in stroke persist. Whether intervention intensity modifies stroke disparities remains unclear.

METHODS: We analyzed 10,005 adults aged ≥ 20 years with hypertension in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey from March 2013 to March 2020. Stroke history was self-reported. Antihypertensive therapy was categorized as untreated, monotherapy, or combination therapy. Multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical variables and included a race/ethnicity × medication group interaction term. Outcomes were reported as odds ratios (OR) and accompanying 95% confidence intervals (CI).

RESULTS: 5% of the studied population reported a history of stroke. After full adjustment, current smoking (OR = 1.80, 95% CI 1.27-2.56), history of cardiovascular disease (OR = 2.38, 95% CI 1.70-3.35), and Medicaid insurance (OR = 3.06, 95% CI 1.40-6.68) were independently associated with stroke. Descriptive differences in stroke prevalence varied across race/ethnicity and antihypertensive medication categories; however, the race/ethnicity x medication interaction was not statistically significant (p = 0.346). Among untreated participants, predicted stroke prevalence was 3.5% in Black participants and 2.8% in White participants, compared to 7.0% and 6.8%, respectively, among those receiving combination therapy. Compared with White participants, Asian participants demonstrated lower odds of stroke on combination therapy (adjusted OR 0.23, 95% CI 0.06-0.96) compared with untreated individuals (adjusted OR 0.49, 95% CI 0.22-1.09). Hispanic participants demonstrated lower odds of stroke relative to White participants across medication categories (adjusted OR = 0.57, 95% CI 0.37-0.90 combination therapy vs. adjusted OR = 0.66, 95% CI 0.48-0.92 untreated).

CONCLUSION: Stroke prevalence differed by race/ethnicity and antihypertensive medication category; however, no statistically significant evidence was found that treatment intensity modified racial/ethnic disparities. Larger longitudinal studies incorporating blood pressure control, medication adherence, and hypertension severity are needed to better understand the relationship between antihypertensive treatment intensity and racial/ethnic differences in stroke risk.

articles.title: Circular RNA-NLRP3 Crosstalk in Reproductive Biology: A Critical Appraisal of Direct Evidence and Testable Hypotheses.
articles.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are abundant and developmentally regulated in gonads, gametes, and preimplantation embryos, whereas NLRP3 inflammasome signaling has context-dependent roles in ovarian aging, spermatogenic stress, endometrial receptivity, implantation, and placental disease. Whether these two evidence streams constitute a functional regulatory axis in mammalian gametogenesis or early embryogenesis remains uncertain. In this regard, this review article aimed to identify direct reproductive mechanisms; reproductive functions without a demonstrated circRNA-NLRP3 bridge, association, or bioinformatic prediction; and mechanistic extrapolations from non-reproductive systems. Direct reproductive evidence was limited to four placental/trophoblast or granulosa-cell examples: circ_0001438/miR-942/NLRP3 signaling in preeclampsia-associated trophoblast models; circ_0081343-RBM8A regulation of NLRP3-linked pyroptosis in fetal-growth-restriction models; circ_0070987-associated pyroptosis in a dihydrotestosterone-treated granulosa-cell line; and hsa_circ_0003218 overexpression, which reduced NLRP3-pathway readouts in high-glucose HTR-8/SVneo trophoblasts in a gestational-diabetes study. No direct functional study was identified in mammalian sperm, oocytes, zygotes, cleavage-stage embryos, blastocysts, or the male germ line. Accordingly, circRNA detection, co-expression, host-gene enrichment, and predicted competing endogenous RNA networks should be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than as proof of NLRP3 regulation. CircRNAs in seminal plasma and maternal blood show candidate biomarker potential, but external validation remains limited, and no combined reproductive circRNA-NLRP3 panel has been validated. Similarly, circRNA mimics, antisense approaches, circRNA-encoded peptides, extracellular vesicle (EVs) delivery, and combined circRNA/NLRP3 therapy remain preclinical or hypothetical in terms of reproduction. The most immediate priorities are cell-type- and stage-resolved perturbation studies, binding and rescue experiments, quantitative inflammasome readouts, reproductive safety assessment, and prospective biomarker validation.

articles.title: Pediatric suprasellar primary CNS lymphoma with cavernous sinus invasion and ischemic stroke: a case report and systematic review.
articles.journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL) is an exceptionally rare pediatric malignancy, accounting for less than 1% of childhood central nervous system tumors. Suprasellar involvement is particularly uncommon and frequently mimics more prevalent lesions, including germinoma and Langerhans cell histiocytosis, often resulting in delayed diagnosis.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report the case of a 12-year-old immunocompetent girl with a history of Epstein-Barr virus infection and a previously resected atypical smooth muscle tumor of the ileum who presented with high-grade fever, severe headache, and diplopia. She rapidly deteriorated neurologically, and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a rim-enhancing sellar-suprasellar lesion invading the cavernous sinus, causing critical internal carotid artery stenosis with bilateral watershed cerebral infarctions. Emergency endoscopic endonasal transsphenoidal decompression was performed. Histopathological examination confirmed anaplastic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) of the non-germinal center B-cell subtype. Despite prompt surgical intervention and initiation of systemic chemotherapy, the patient developed central diabetes insipidus, severe hemodynamic instability, and ultimately died within few months.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Ovid, and Scopus were searched from database inception to 31 May 2026 to identify published cases of pediatric suprasellar primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL).

RESULTS: Five studies comprising seven previously reported pediatric patients met the inclusion criteria. Six of seven historical patients (85.7%) achieved complete radiological remission, Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) or large-cell B-cell lymphoma was reported in four of seven patients (57.1%). Most patients achieved complete remission following intensive CNS-directed chemotherapy, although persistent endocrine dysfunction remained common. In contrast to previously reported cases, our patient presented with fulminant cavernous sinus invasion, critical internal carotid artery stenosis, and ischemic watershed cerebral infarctions, representing an exceptionally aggressive clinical phenotype.

CONCLUSION: Pediatric suprasellar PCNSL is a rare but highly aggressive disease that should be considered in children presenting with diabetes insipidus, pituitary stalk lesions, or rapidly progressive suprasellar masses. Progressive radiologic evolution or atypical vascular complications should prompt early histopathological confirmation to facilitate timely diagnosis and initiation of treatment.

articles.title: Genetic subtyping of MASLD reveals a glucose-lowering axis linked to GCKR alternative splicing.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a global metabolic condition with a complex relationship to type 2 diabetes. Yet human genetic studies suggest the existence of a MASLD subtype with favourable glycaemic effects, raising a clinically important question: how can hepatic steatosis coexist with improved glycaemic outcomes? We aimed to determine whether MASLD comprises genetically distinct subtypes with divergent glycaemic consequences, and to define the genetic basis of a glucose-lowering MASLD subtype.

METHODS: We integrated genetic and triglyceride-related metabolomic profiles to cluster 18 established MASLD-associated variants and construct mutually adjusted partitioned polygenic risk scores (PRSs) in the UK Biobank. We tested associations with hepatic biomarkers, liver outcomes and type 2 diabetes, and replicated glycaemic findings in an independent Chinese cohort (the Taizhou Longitudinal Study [TZL]). We prioritised candidate loci using colocalisation and fine-mapping and performed allele-specific functional assays and structural modelling to investigate the underlying mechanism at the lead locus.

RESULTS: Partitioned PRSs revealed bidirectional glycaemic axes: one PRS lowered fasting glucose and type 2 diabetes risk, whereas the remaining PRSs increased both, despite all associating with higher liver injury markers and adverse liver outcomes. The divergent glycaemic effects were replicated in the TZL. To pinpoint the genetic basis of the glucose-lowering axis, colocalisation and fine-mapping prioritised GCKR rs1260326 (C>T) as a shared MASLD-type 2 diabetes signal and the lead cis-pQTL for circulating glucokinase regulatory protein (GKRP). Functional experiments showed that the rs1260326 T allele promotes exon-15 skipping in GCKR, reduces the abundance of full-length GKRP and yields a truncated protein. In silico structural modelling suggested that the truncated GKRP isoform may have reduced binding affinity for glucokinase, although this predicted effect requires experimental validation.

CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: MASLD comprises genetically distinct subtypes with opposing glycaemic and type 2 diabetes risk profiles. Within the glucose-lowering subtype, rs1260326-mediated alternative splicing of GCKR provides a potential mechanistic link to reduced GKRP abundance and glycaemic protection. These findings support a more granular view of MASLD heterogeneity and may inform future subtype-specific risk stratification and prevention.

articles.title: Fluid choice in pediatric diabetic ketoacidosis: a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Early fluid resuscitation is critical in pediatric diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). While 0.9% saline is the standard of care, its high chloride content may cause hyperchloremic acidosis. Balanced electrolyte solutions (BES) have been proposed as alternatives to accelerate metabolic recovery, justifying an updated pediatric-specific analysis. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of BES compared with 0.9% saline in pediatric DKA. A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with Cochrane guidelines, searching PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies comparing BES with 0.9% saline in pediatric DKA. Pooled analysis was performed using random-effects models, with 95% CI. Eight studies comprising 47,840 participants were included. Among RCTs, no significant difference was found in time to DKA resolution (n = 292; MD 2.27 h; 95% CI - 0.58 to 5.11; I2 = 4.4%) or hospital length of stay (n = 225; MD 0.11 days; 95% CI - 0.75 to 0.97; I2 = 45.1%). Pediatric Intensive Care Unit length of stay (n = 242; MD - 1.18 h) also did not differ significantly. The risks of cerebral edema (n = 176; RR 1.82; 95% CI 0.06 to 58.80) and acute kidney injury (n = 243; RR 1.39; 95% CI 0.67 to 2.87) did not differ between groups.

CONCLUSION: In this study, BES showed no significant difference in clinical outcomes compared with 0.9% saline in pediatric DKA. However, additional high-quality studies are needed to strengthen the evidence base. Current evidence is insufficient to demonstrate superiority, inferiority or comparative safety of either fluid strategy.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: This systematic review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261320121).

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Early fluid resuscitation is critical in pediatric diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), with 0.9% saline being the traditional standard of care. • High chloride content in 0.9% saline may cause hyperchloremic acidosis, leading to interest in balanced electrolyte solutions (BES) as alternatives.

WHAT IS NEW: • This meta-analysis with pediatric patients found no significant difference between BES and 0.9% saline in the time of DKA resolution, hospital/Pediatric Intensive Care Unit stay, or complications like cerebral edema. • Future high-quality randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are needed to refine pediatric fluid management protocols in DKA and investigate potential biochemical benefits.

articles.title: Safety and Tolerability of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitors: A State-of-the-Art Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2is) have evolved from glucose-lowering agents to foundational therapies for the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease, with substantial benefits for cardiovascular, kidney, and survival outcomes. As their indications continue to expand, a comprehensive understanding of their safety and tolerability has become increasingly important for optimizing patient care. Building on our recent state-of-the-art review of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, this review provides a contemporary synthesis of the evidence on the safety and tolerability of SGLT-2is. We critically appraise data from randomized controlled trials, cardiovascular and kidney outcome trials, pharmacovigilance databases, large observational studies, and systematic reviews and meta-analyses. The available evidence demonstrates that SGLT-2is have a favorable overall safety profile, with genital mycotic infections representing the most consistently observed adverse event. Volume depletion and euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis remain clinically important but are uncommon and are largely preventable through appropriate patient selection, patient education, and temporary treatment interruption during high-risk clinical situations. Fournier's gangrene should be regarded as a very rare but serious complication requiring prompt recognition and treatment. In contrast, randomized trials and meta-analyses generally indicate a reduced risk of acute kidney injury, while evidence concerning fracture, lower-limb amputation, hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, and cancer is less definitive. Although consistent class-wide increases in these latter outcomes have not been established, uncommon or agent-specific risks cannot be excluded, particularly where event numbers are small or follow-up is limited. Overall, treatment discontinuation because of adverse events is low across major cardiovascular, heart failure, and kidney outcome trials, supporting the excellent tolerability of this therapeutic class. Comparative evidence suggests only modest differences among individual SGLT-2is, although definitive conclusions remain limited by the absence of direct, large, randomized head-to-head trials. We also summarize practical strategies for adverse-event mitigation, monitoring, temporary treatment interruption, and individualized patient selection. As the clinical applications of SGLT-2is continue to broaden, ongoing pharmacovigilance, inclusive clinical trials, and comparative safety studies will be essential to further refine their benefit-risk profile and optimize their safe use across diverse patient populations.

articles.title: Markers of early cardiac dysfunction in young adults with insomnia disorder: a case-control study.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Insomnia is a highly prevalent, chronic disorder that is a modifiable novel risk factor for cardiovascular disease. However, there are fewer physiological data available suggesting that insomnia may be related to early cardiac disease and atherosclerotic progression among young adults (ages 21-44 years). In this case-control study, we investigated the association between insomnia and subclinical cardiovascular disease risk markers in a sample of young adults with ICSD-3-diagnosed insomnia compared to healthy good sleepers.

METHODS: Among a sample of 43 community-based, healthy young adults (18 individuals with insomnia disorder, 25 good sleeping controls; Mage = 28.7 years, range 21-42), we compared indices of cardiac function with 2D echocardiography, endothelial dysfunction with flow-mediated endothelial dilation, and arterial stiffness with carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity, adjusted for body mass index.

RESULTS: The insomnia group had worse left ventricular global longitudinal strain in comparison to the good sleeping controls (insomnia M(SD) - 22.8 (2.2), good sleeping controls - 24.3 (1.5), F[1, 39] = 7.42, p = 0.01, ηp2 = 0.16, estimated marginal mean difference = 1.47%, adjusted R2 = 0.18), but no differences in endothelial function, arterial stiffness, or other cardiac function parameters.

CONCLUSION: Young adults with well-defined insomnia disorder and few confounding comorbidities demonstrated worse left ventricular strain than good sleepers. Worse left ventricular strain may reflect subtle, subclinical myocardial dysfunction that could precede changes in other cardiac function parameters or overt cardiovascular disease. Longitudinal studies are needed to evaluate whether this finding heralds future cardiovascular risk.

CURRENT STUDY/STUDY RATIONALE: Insomnia disorder is linked to cardiovascular disease, but this connection is rarely explored with markers of cardiac and vascular function in young adults.

STUDY IMPACT: Young adults with insomnia disorder had worse left ventricular strain, as measured by left ventricular global longitudinal strain, than well-defined good sleeping controls, suggesting early cardiac risk in patients with insomnia disorder.

articles.title: Hematopoietic loss of KDM6A impairs cardiac recovery in heart failure via epigenetic reprogramming of myeloid cells.
articles.abstract: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH), the expansion of blood cell clones carrying acquired mutations, is an independent risk factor for cardiovascular disease. Although mutations in DNMT3A and TET2 are well studied, the cardiovascular consequences of KDM6A mutations remain unclear. KDM6A is an X-linked histone demethylase that is commonly mutated in patients with heart failure (HF). Here we performed multiomics profiling and functional characterization of mouse models and patient-derived data to show that hematopoietic KDM6A loss impairs cardiac recovery after myocardial infarction (MI). KDM6A deficiency increases myeloid cell recruitment to the injured heart and reprograms monocytes, macrophages and neutrophils toward inflammatory, migratory and glycolytic states. Patients with HF and KDM6A-driven CH show similar pro-inflammatory monocyte signatures. KDM6A-silenced macrophages promote cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and cardiac fibroblast activation. Notably, IL-1β blockade after MI rescued the adverse cardiac phenotype of hematopoietic KDM6A loss. These findings identify KDM6A-driven CH as a driver of immune dysregulation and IL-1β signaling as a potential therapeutic target in CH-associated HF.

articles.title: Management of established bronchopulmonary dysplasia after 36 weeks' postmenstrual age: an evidence-informed review.
articles.journal: Journal of perinatology : official journal of the California Perinatal Association
articles.abstract: To review available evidence in the management of established bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD). We conducted a structured, domain-specific narrative review of PubMed (MEDLINE) from 2000 to 2025, including randomized trials, cohort studies, systematic reviews, and clinical guidelines in preterm infants with established BPD, with qualitative synthesis across predefined management domains. Published studies support oxygen saturation targets of 90-95% for most infants, with slightly higher targets used for those with pulmonary hypertension. Chronic-phase ventilation strategies accommodating heterogeneous lung mechanics are associated with improved synchrony and gas exchange. Diuretics provide only a transient benefit and are associated with growth and electrolyte disturbances. Systemic corticosteroids may facilitate extubation in selected infants, while inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators lack evidence for routine use. Chronic management of established BPD is supported by limited data. Current evidence for infants after 36 weeks' PMA favors careful oxygen titration, chronic-phase ventilation strategies, and selective pharmacologic therapy.

articles.title: Hypoxia-induced platelet activation and pulmonary platelets are increased in a murine model of neonatal chronic lung disease and pulmonary hypertension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia-associated pulmonary hypertension (BPD-PH) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in preterm infants, yet available therapies lack mechanistic diversity and can be ineffective, highlighting an urgent need for novel therapeutic targets. Platelets are increasingly recognized as immune cells capable of driving pulmonary vascular inflammation, but their role in neonatal PH remains undefined.

METHODS: Neonatal mice were exposed to 12% hypoxia beginning at 12-24 h of life until postnatal day 8 (P8) or 15 (P15). Cardiopulmonary phenotype and markers of platelet activation were quantified using histology, flow cytometry, ELISA, and immunohistochemistry.

RESULTS: Hypoxia produced a BPD-PH phenotype, including alveolar simplification, pulmonary vessel muscularization, elevated right ventricular systolic pressure, and right ventricular hypertrophy. Hypoxia disrupted the postnatal decline in pulmonary platelets and the platelet α-granule stored protein, platelet factor 4, resulting in increased pulmonary platelet accumulation at P15. Circulating platelets from hypoxic mice demonstrated increased activation, with higher P-selectin and activated αIIbβ3 expression at P8 and P15, enhanced agonist-induced P-selectin expression at P8, and increased leukocyte-platelet aggregation at P8.

CONCLUSIONS: Postnatal hypoxia induces a robust, biologically meaningful platelet activation phenotype, supporting a previously unrecognized association between platelet activation and BPD-PH and identifying platelet activation pathways as potential therapeutic targets warranting further mechanistic investigation.

IMPACT: Postnatal hypoxia drives persistent pulmonary platelet accumulation in a neonatal model of bronchopulmonary dysplasia-associated pulmonary hypertension. Hypoxic neonatal platelets exhibit increased P-selectin expression and αIIbβ3 activation, enhanced agonist responsiveness, and early leukocyte-platelet aggregation, indicating a shift toward a pro-inflammatory phenotype. These findings demonstrate that, despite developmental hyporesponsiveness, neonatal platelets are dynamically activated by hypoxia and may contribute to pulmonary vascular remodeling. This work identifies platelet activation pathways as potential circulating biomarkers and clinically relevant targets in neonatal pulmonary hypertension, expanding beyond current vasodilator-based therapies.

articles.title: TLR8 in biliary atresia: linking innate immune signaling to fibrogenesis for therapeutic gain.
articles.abstract: Biliary atresia (BA) remains a 'black box' in pediatric hepatology, largely because effective pharmacological options to control the progression of inflammation and fibrogenesis that follow Kasai portoenterostomy (KPE) are lacking.1 Innate immunity offers a compelling framework: perinatal viral exposure and dysregulated pattern-recognition signaling have been implicated in BA pathogenesis for decades, though with limited translational opportunities. Within this context, Toll-like receptor 8 (TLR8) has received comparatively limited attention. Long regarded as TLR7's less-characterized counterpart, TLR8 has only recently gained a clearer structural and pharmacological definition, including selective chemical modulators and mechanistically supported pro-fibrotic role in dermal fibroblasts from patients with systemic sclerosis.2.

articles.title: Low-dose versus regular-dose paclitaxel-coated balloons for de novo coronary lesions: the ALLIANCE registry.
articles.abstract: Drug-coated balloons (DCBs) are widely used in clinical practice; however, the clinical impact of differences between DCB platforms, including paclitaxel dose, remains uncertain. This study compared the clinical efficacy and safety of low-dose (LD) versus regular-dose (RD) paclitaxel-coated balloons (PCBs) for de novo coronary lesions using data from the ALLIANCE registry, a prospective, multicenter, all-comers study. Patients treated with an LD-PCB (AGENT) or RD-PCB (SeQuent Please Neo) were compared using propensity score matching at a target LD-to-RD ratio of 2:1. The primary endpoint was 1-year target lesion failure (TLF), defined as a composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction, and clinically driven target lesion revascularization (cd-TLR). Among 1,568 patients included in this analysis, propensity score matching yielded 784 patients in the LD-PCB group and 419 in the RD-PCB group. At 1 year, the incidence of TLF was 5.1% in the LD-PCB group and 3.8% in the RD-PCB group (p = 0.33). Kaplan-Meier analyses showed no significant between-group differences in TLF or its individual components. In this propensity score-matched registry analysis, LD-PCBs and RD-PCBs were associated with no statistically significant difference in 1-year TLF. These findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating and do not establish equivalence between the two platforms.

articles.title: [New oral anti-obesity drugs: the future or second choice?].
articles.abstract: Obesity and its comorbidities represent a growing worldwide health challenge. To date, lifestyle modification is the most frequently used treatment modality, but offers only limited success in terms of both the extent and maintenance of weight loss. Potent injectable incretin mimetics such as semaglutide and tirzepatide were recently introduced as novel pharmacological options for improved and clinically meaningful weight management. In 2026, the first two oral glucagon-like peptide‑1 (GLP-1)-based agents, namely oral semaglutide and orforglipron, were approved and are promoted as alternative drug choices for additional weight loss, allowing people with obesity to make their own choice from a broader spectrum of therapeutics. This review describes the current state of knowledge on these new medications for the treatment of obesity. A variety of other oral drugs is currently under development and will substantially expand obesity management in the coming years.

articles.title: Decoding Stroke-Heart Syndrome: A Translational Framework Linking Cerebral Injury to Cardiovascular Dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Acute ischemic stroke can trigger cardiac injury independent of primary coronary disease, producing manifestations ranging from troponin elevation and electrocardiographic abnormalities to arrhythmias, left ventricular dysfunction, Takotsubo syndrome, and sudden cardiac death, collectively termed stroke-heart syndrome. Cardiac complications affect roughly a quarter of patients within the first month, cluster in the first days, and are the second most frequent cause of death after stroke; older patients, those with severe or insular strokes, those with cardiometabolic comorbidity, and women are disproportionately affected. We propose the Neurocardiac Injury Cascade, an eight-stage framework comprising brain lesion, central autonomic network disruption, catecholamine storm, immune activation, coronary microvascular dysfunction, myocardial injury, electrical instability, and cardiac remodeling. Stages three to five are explicitly modeled as a concurrent, mutually reinforcing module rather than as sequential steps, and each stage is given a definition, an expected time window, and a measurable signature. By organizing these events sequentially, the model links mechanisms with biomarker evolution, imaging findings, and stage-specific therapeutic opportunities. We further propose that chronic comorbidity, principally hypertension and diabetes, does not add stages but sets the gain at existing ones, which has direct consequences for the design of preclinical models and clinical trials. We highlight the role of the insular cortex and lateralized autonomic output, position Takotsubo syndrome as the severe phenotype of the cascade, and address the heterogeneity of post-stroke troponin elevation. This framework integrates diagnosis, risk stratification, and mechanism-based therapies to advance precision neurocardiology and guide future translational and clinical research.

articles.title: Cardiovascular disease in diabetes mellitus: beyond atherosclerosis and heart failure.
articles.abstract: The global burden of diabetes mellitus continues to grow, now affecting one in nine adults. In people with diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, and considerable focus has been placed on reducing the incidence of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and heart failure over the past few decades. Due to reductions in the prevalence of some major risk factors, improved control of other risk factors and improved therapeutic agents, mortality attributed to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease has declined. Meanwhile, the decline in mortality attributed to heart failure has stalled. However, beyond atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and heart failure, many other cardiovascular diseases are responsible for morbidity and mortality. We provide a comprehensive narrative summary of the association between diabetes mellitus and the most common cardiovascular diseases as reported by the 2023 Global Burden of Disease study. The evidence indicates that diabetes mellitus is a risk factor for atrial fibrillation, infective endocarditis, hypertensive heart disease, intracerebral haemorrhage and aortic stenosis. We also discuss the available evidence for the effects of incretin hormone mimetics, such as glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists, and of sodium/glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors for each of these cardiovascular diseases. This Review underscores the multifaceted link between cardiovascular disease and diabetes mellitus, highlighting that integrated strategies are required to effectively reduce the global burden of both conditions.

articles.title: A live biotherapeutic product for adult allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation recipients: a partially randomized, placebo-controlled phase 1b trial.
articles.abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) microbiome disruption and impaired GI barrier integrity increase the risk of bloodstream infection (BSI) following allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant.
