Here we report results from a two-cohort (open-label, n = 15; randomized, placebo-controlled, n = 45) phase 1b study of SER-155, an investigational, cultivated, multi-strain, oral live biotherapeutic designed to address GI microbiome disruption GI epithelial barrier integrity in allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant recipients. In cohort 2, 34 of 45 participants received either SER-155 treatment (n = 20, SER-155 following microbiome conditioning with oral vancomycin), or placebo (n = 14), and subsequently received transplant. For the primary safety endpoint, SER-155 was well tolerated, with a safety profile comparable to placebo, no treatment-related serious adverse events and no infections with SER-155 species; the most common adverse events were diarrhea and nausea. Four participants in cohort 1 and four participants in cohort 2 (two participants in the SER-155 arm and two in the placebo arm) died during the study; none was attributable to SER-155. For the primary pharmacokinetic endpoint, engraftment was detected for 16 of 16 SER-155 strains, with a median of 11.5 strains detected after the first treatment course. The key secondary efficacy endpoint revealed a significantly lower incidence of BSI with SER-155 versus placebo (10.0% versus 43%; OR 0.15; 95% CI 0.01-1.13; P = 0.0423; 77% relative risk reduction). Other secondary efficacy endpoints (GI infection, acute graft-versus-host disease ≥grade 2, febrile neutropenia and a composite endpoint of BSI, GI infection or acute graft-versus-host disease) were not statistically significant. The secondary pharmacodynamic endpoint of GI domination by Enterococcus and Enterobacteriaceae spp. was not achieved. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04995653 .

articles.title: Iterative computational and rational design generates diverse PET hydrolases for plastic depolymerization.
articles.abstract: Evolutionary relationships among homologous enzymes can be leveraged to introduce large numbers of amino acid substitutions for improved functional properties. Here, we combine evolution-informed design (EVdesign) with rational design to engineer improved poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) hydrolases (PETases). Designs derived from multiple PETases reveal strong parent-dependent differences in success and performance, with Thermobifida fusca TfCut2 emerging as the most design-amenable scaffold. Increasing sequence diversification reduces the number of active enzymes but broadens performance variance, enabling discovery of high-performing outliers. Four rational mutations overcome a thermostability bottleneck in TfCut2 and this variant provides a robust scaffold for iterative EVdesign, which further improves activity. Overall, we experimentally test 603 designs from eight parent PETases. More than 400 variants containing 12-68 substitutions were able to depolymerize PET, nearly all outperforming their parent enzymes, and many approach benchmark LCC-ICCG performance in partial conversion assays. These results establish EVdesign as a robust strategy for generating diverse, high-activity enzymes.

articles.title: Overconsumption of low-digestible sugars can increase susceptibility to Salmonella Typhimurium infection.
articles.abstract: Low-digestible carbohydrates (LDCs), including dietary fibers and sugars that resist absorption, are generally considered beneficial for the gut microbiota. However, we show that acute overconsumption of certain LDCs, particularly low-digestible sugars (LDSs), such as arabinose, lactulose, and polyols commonly used as sugar substitutes, can compromise colonization resistance against the common foodborne pathogen Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium. LDS overconsumption results in elevated fecal pathogen loads, systemic dissemination, and colitis in infected mice. Mechanistic analysis of arabinose overconsumption revealed that rapid fermentation acidifies the intestinal environment, perturbs the microbiota, alters gut-luminal short-chain fatty acid levels and elevated amino acid availability, which can support pathogen growth. Additionally, this perturbation impacts virulence by broadening tissue tropism (e.g. expansion to small intestine) and selecting for invasive Salmonella. Unlike antibiotic perturbations, Salmonella colonization requires SPI-1 and SPI-2 Type-III-secretion systems, linking virulence to pathogen fitness. These findings reveal how dietary perturbations can impact the gut ecosystem in ways that not only compromise colonization resistance but also enhance pathogen virulence.

articles.title: Dapagliflozin vs. Acetazolamide in Patients With Acute Heart Failure: A Randomized Controlled Trial (CHOICE-AHF).
articles.abstract: Early adjunctive therapies may improve decongestion and symptoms in acute heart failure. This trial compared dapagliflozin with acetazolamide when initiated early, focusing on dyspnea relief as the primary outcome and decongestive, diuretic, natriuretic, and safety outcomes. In this randomized, active-controlled trial, 108 adults hospitalized with acute heart failure, dyspnea, and objective evidence of congestion requiring intravenous loop diuretics were randomized to receive dapagliflozin 10 mg (N = 55) or acetazolamide 500 mg (N = 53) once daily for 3 days alongside standard care. The primary endpoint was the between-group difference in 72-hour dyspnea visual analog scale area under the curve. Secondary endpoints included successful decongestion within 3 days, diuretic and natriuretic responses, the relative change in N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels from baseline to day 3, and safety. Acetazolamide produced a significantly lower 72-hour dyspnea area under the curve than dapagliflozin (2647.9 ± 1213.8 vs. 2988.7 ± 1196.7 mm × hour; P = 0.048). It increased cumulative urine output over 72 hours (12,200 vs. 10,000 mL; P = 0.019) and total natriuresis over 48 hours (824.7 vs. 547.9 mmol; P = 0.001). Dapagliflozin achieved a larger reduction in N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide at 72 hours (-34.2% vs. -25.0%; P = 0.003). Safety events were infrequent and similar. In conclusion, acetazolamide provided greater dyspnea relief, diuresis, and natriuresis, whereas dapagliflozin produced a larger short-term reduction in N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide. Further studies are needed to validate these findings. Trial registration: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06783166.

articles.title: A diagnostic prediction model for early diagnosis of imported malaria in a European non-endemic setting: Development and temporal validation in a 17-year cohort.
articles.journal: Enfermedades infecciosas y microbiologia clinica (English ed.)
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Imported malaria is the most common potentially life-threatening tropical disease among travelers. Early diagnosis remains a clinical challenge and determines its severity and mortality. The aim was to develop and temporally validate a simple clinical model for malaria diagnosis.

METHODS: Retrospective observational cohort study of adults with suspected malaria at a secondary hospital in Madrid over 17 years. Pregnant women, people living with HIV, and submicroscopic malaria cases were included. Inclusion criteria were travel to an endemic area with fever or symptoms prompting parasitological testing. Patients were divided into a derivation cohort (2004-2015) and a temporal validation cohort (2016-2020). Independent predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression with LASSO selection. Model performance was assessed using ROC curves.

RESULTS: A total of 649 patients were included; 296 (45.6%) had confirmed malaria due to Plasmodium falciparum (90.9%). Five predictors were identified: thrombocytopenia, absence of leukocytosis, elevated lactate dehydrogenase, fever, and gastrointestinal symptoms. The model achieved an AUC of 0.85 in the derivation cohort and 0.82 (95% CI: 0.73-0.90) in the validation cohort. Using a cut-off ≥14, specificity reached 90%.

CONCLUSIONS: We developed and temporally validated a simple diagnostic prediction model with good discriminatory performance that may support decision-making in patients with suspected imported malaria. The score may help identify travelers at higher probability of malaria.

articles.title: Can artificial intelligence add diagnostic value for human readers in detecting coronary artery stenosis on coronary CT angiography? A Bayesian network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The incremental diagnostic value of artificial intelligence (AI) in coronary CT angiography (CCTA) remains uncertain. We compared five CCTA strategies: automated stenosis assessment software (COR Analyzer), stand-alone CCTA-based deep learning (DL), junior readers, senior readers, and AI-assisted readers, for detecting anatomical coronary artery stenosis against invasive coronary angiography.

METHODS AND RESULTS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through July 9, 2026. Twenty-two observational diagnostic accuracy studies were included (19 retrospective and three prospective; 21 for ≥50% stenosis and six for ≥70% stenosis). In the primary patient-level analysis at ≥50% stenosis, pooled sensitivity for DL and AI-assisted readers was 0.91 each (95% credible interval, 0.87 to 0.94 and 0.86 to 0.94), versus 0.80 (0.73-0.87) for junior and 0.87 (0.82-0.91) for senior readers; AI assistance increased sensitivity by 0.10 versus junior readers (0.06-0.15) and 0.03 versus senior readers (0.01-0.06). Specificity was similar across DL and reader strategies (0.64-0.67) but markedly lower for COR Analyzer (0.25 [0.15 to 0.38]). In the smaller ≥70% network, AI-assisted reading showed the highest estimated sensitivity (0.80 [0.70 to 0.88]). Findings were robust to outlier exclusion; certainty was low to very low for most ≥50% outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Stand-alone DL and AI-assisted reading had similar estimated diagnostic performance. AI assistance improved sensitivity most clearly for less-experienced readers. These accuracy comparisons did not establish formal equivalence or determine whether stand-alone DL could replace human interpretation in clinical practice.

articles.title: Retraction notice to "AFP-CMBPred: Computational identification of antifreeze proteins by extending consensus sequences into multi-blocks evolutionary information" [Computers in Biology and Medicine 139 (2021) 105006].
Achieving early weight-bearing with custom-made intercalary endoprostheses for diaphyseal bone tumors: Clinical outcomes and embolic considerations.
articles.journal: Journal of orthopaedic science : official journal of the Japanese Orthopaedic Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study evaluated clinical outcomes, complications, and implant retention of the K-MAX custom-made intercalary endoprosthesis (Kyocera Corporation, Kyoto, Japan) for femoral and tibial diaphyseal bone tumors.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 18 patients (19 K-MAX reconstructions; femur 14, tibia 5) who underwent wide resection between 2004 and 2018. Diagnoses (per reconstruction) were metastatic tumors (n = 12), primary bone tumors (n = 2), soft-tissue sarcomas (n = 2), and salvage after prior implant failure (n = 3). Time to full weight-bearing and best walking ability were assessed, complications were classified by the Henderson classification, and implant retention was estimated by Kaplan-Meier and cumulative incidence methods.

RESULTS: Full weight-bearing began at a median of 6 days postoperatively (range 1-14); 16 of 18 patients (88.9%) walked with a cane or better, including 5 (27.8%) without assistive devices. Henderson failure occurred in 1 reconstruction (5.3%): aseptic loosening requiring revision. One further implant showed aseptic loosening without revision. One periprosthetic infection and one superficial infection were managed without revision or removal of any component. Eighteen of 19 implants were retained; Kaplan-Meier retention was 100% at 2 years and 75.0% (95% confidence interval [CI] 12.8-96.1%) at 5 years (3 implants at risk), and the 5-year cumulative incidence of revision, with death as a competing event, was 12.0% (95% CI 0.7-40.1%). Local recurrence occurred in 3 of 5 tibial cases (prosthesis retained in all) and in none of the 14 femoral reconstructions.

CONCLUSION: The K-MAX allowed early full weight-bearing (median 6 days) with acceptable complication rates across a range of diagnoses. Surgeons should be aware of the elevated local recurrence risk in tibial cases, although the small, heterogeneous cohort precludes identifying tibial location as an independent risk factor, and of late aseptic loosening.

articles.title: Evaluation of Mitral Regurgitation: Comparison of Ultrafast and Focused Ultrasound in an In-Vitro Pulsatile Flow Phantom.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Mitral regurgitation (MR) severity is assessed by measuring the regurgitant volume (RVol) with echocardiography using the proximal iso-velocity surface area (PISA) method. The low temporal resolution of focused ultrasound, the assumption of hemispheric iso-velocity contours, and the use of a single point to assess the velocity are the pitfalls of this method. This study evaluates a novel method using ultrafast ultrasound, and multiple points for velocity assessment without the aforementioned geometrical assumption to provide a more accurate RVol measurement.

METHODS: A left heart mock system, comprised of an orifice simulating MR, was filled with water mixed with cellulose. RVols from 20 mL to 70 mL with increments of 10 mL, were delivered by a pulsatile pump which was the reference. Data were acquired at 6000 frames/s by a cardiac phased array probe emitting ultrafast diverging waves, connected to an ultrafast scanner as well as a clinical system emitting focused waves. RVols were computed with the surface integral of the velocity through a planar disk at the input of the orifice with ultrafast transmission (u-PD) and PISA method with focused waves (f-PISA). The error of the two methods was compared.

RESULTS: u-PD showed a significant lower error values than f-PISA (18.6 ± 11.5% and 56.5 ± 4.9%, respectively, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that ultrafast ultrasound can provide accurate multi-point estimates of RVol in a model of MR by leveraging the complete axial velocity mapping at high temporal resolution. Its complementary role to PISA method will be evaluated in future clinical studies.

articles.title: Intra- and Inter-Observer Reliability of Quantitative Brain Perfusion Metrics From Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound in Neonatal Brain.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) is a promising, easily available bedside method for evaluating perfusion in neonates. The reliability of brain perfusion metrics analysis is currently unknown. This study aimed to determine the intra- and inter-observer reliability of variables derived from quantitatively analyzed time-intensity curves in neonatal brain CEUS data.

METHODS: Thirteen CEUS studies of the brain were performed through the anterior fontanelle in 10 neonates on days 0-3. Two-min cine clips were recorded after intravenous contrast agent administration and analyzed with commercially available third-party software. Three raters with varying levels of expertise determined four regions of interest on the images: the bilateral thalami and two reference regions. The reference areas consisted of a frontoparietal focal area for the first and a whole-brain coronal for the second, excluding central gray nuclei. Quantitative perfusion metrics were analyzed for these regions. For intra-observer reliability, each rater re-analyzed a subset of ten examinations, after an interval of at least 2 mo. Intra- and inter-rater reliability statistics were calculated.

RESULTS: In the bilateral thalamus, intra-observer reliability was excellent for most parameters, and inter-observer reliability was good to moderate. Results across the two reference areas were variable, showing at best moderate correlations with the second, larger reference area.

CONCLUSION: In this exploratory study, quantitative brain perfusion CEUS metrics analyzed using commercially available software were most reliable for thalamic measures among three readers with varying experience. These preliminary results support further evaluation of thalamic CEUS perfusion metrics in larger cohorts using standardized acquisition and analysis protocols.

articles.title: Transthoracic Electromechanical and Mechanical Cardiac Function Imaging in Acute and Chronic Myocardial Infarction Progression.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Accurate and precise quantitative functional echocardiographic assessment remains a clinical challenge. Myocardial elastography (ME) and electromechanical wave imaging (EWI) are ultrasound-based elastographic myocardial strain estimation methods that, in tandem, aim to aid in the diagnosis and monitoring of cardiac diseases. Until now, these modalities have been used separately. In this study, we explore their compatibility to localize and detect both the electromechanical and mechanical effects of ischemia.

METHODS: A longitudinal myocardial infarction model was studied in canine subjects (n = 9) for either 4 days (4-d; n = 6) or 5 week (5 wk; n = 3) to investigate the ability of ME and EWI to detect, locate and monitor collateral perfusion recovery from infarction generated via ligation of the left anterior descending coronary artery (LAD). Canine subjects were imaged with both a 300 frames/s and a 2000 frames/s ultrasound radiofrequency acquisition scheme for ME and EWI, respectively, at baseline, daily (n = 9) for 1 week and on a weekly basis (n = 3) for 4 weeks. Both techniques were performed on the acquired data and then segmented by coronary perfusion region. ME displacements were calculated with 1-D normalized cross-correlation in the axial and lateral directions (4.6 mm window, 80% window overlap, 3× lateral re-correlation), and EWI displacements were calculated with the 1-D normalized cross-correlation (5 mm window, 90% window overlap). Strains were computed using a least-squares estimator, resulting in ME cumulative radial strains and EWI interframe axial strains. The means and standard deviations were calculated by day for each technique and observed for the duration of the study. The differences in the cumulative systolic strain and the systolic activation timings between each treatment day and baseline were calculated between each perfusion segment.

RESULTS: In the 4-d experiments, the difference between baseline and treatment days was significantly greater in the LAD segment than in the right coronary artery or left circumflex coronary artery (LCX) for both ME (p < 0.005, mixed-effects analysis with Geisser-Greenhouse correction and Tukey's multiple comparisons) and EWI (p < 0.001, mixed-effects analysis with Geisser-Greenhouse correction and Tukey's multiple comparisons). Over the duration of the 4 d study, the LAD showed the most significant electromechanical delay from baseline imaging. The same trend was observed in the 4 wk studies, where the LAD segment showed the most significant difference (ME: -25.8% ± 15.2%; EWI: 58.2 ± 39.5 ms) from baseline for both ME (LCX: -10.0% ± 22.2%, p < 0.01, Kruskal-Wallis test with Dunn's multiple comparisons) and EWI (right coronary artery: 31.4 ± 36.6 ms, p < 0.01, Kruskal-Wallis test with Dunn's multiple comparisons; LCX: 33.6 ± 40.1 ms, p < 0.01, Kruskal-Wallis test with Dunn's multiple comparisons). The LAD segment showed a more significant electromechanical delay between baseline and each treatment day for EWI over the 4 wk studies. This was also observed with an increased EWI systolic activation time delay between baseline and week 4.

CONCLUSIONS: Both ME cumulative radial strain and EWI systolic activation timing showed the ability to monitor myocardial infarction recovery over both an acute (4 d) and a chronic (4 wk) period. ME also showed substantial collateral reperfusion of the canine myocardium in the recovery of radial strain magnitude, while an electromechanical delay remained throughout both phases of the study over the LAD perfusion segment. Taken together, these findings indicate that even after apparent recovery of cumulative radial strain to baseline values, there is a remaining functional deficit in the form of electromechanical activation. EWI showed the ability to complement ME by providing insight into the electromechanical recovery of the myocardium in addition to the radial strain magnitude.

articles.title: SUMOylated DDX3 Promotes HBV Replication and Tumor Growth of Hepatocellular Carcinoma via TRIM28-DDX3-KLF4α Signaling Axis.
articles.abstract: DDX3 has dual biological functions of regulating cell proliferation and antiviral effects. Herein, we focus on SUMOylation-mediated DDX3 in the interplay from hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection to HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma (HBV-HCC) progression. We identified dynamic regulation of SUMOylation and DeSUMOylation of DDX3 at four key lysine (K) residues (K81/K208/K215/K564) in response to HBV infection. During the early stage of HBV acute infection, SENP1 interacts with DDX3 to keep DDX3 deSUMOylation for inhibiting HBV replication. During persistent HBV replication, as SENP1 downregulation and HBV polymerase accumulation, DDX3 disassociates with SENP1 to bind with TRIM28, which induces DDX3 SUMOylation. Meanwhile, SUMOylated DDX3 enhances alternative splicing of KLF4 mRNAs to generate KLF4α isoform that involves in Cyclin D1-mediated cell cycle progression, weakens tumor suppressor function of DDX3 and promotes HBV-HCC. Moreover, DDX3 expression is positively correlated with KLF4 mRNA, and high DDX3 level with low TRIM28 expression indicates a better overall survival for HBV-HCC patients. Our findings reveal the dynamic regulation between SUMOylation and deSUMOylation of DDX3, including mediating HBV gene transcription, virus antigen secretion, and cell proliferation. Furthermore, the TRIM28-DDX3-KLF4 axis as a novel therapeutic target for HBV-HCC, exhibiting the dual ability to inhibit tumor progression and disrupt the HBV-host interaction.

articles.title: Sleep Architecture, Glucose Regulation and Subclinical Cardiovascular Risk in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: A Wearable Sleep Tracking and Continuous Glucose Monitoring Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the associations of wearable-derived sleep architecture with CGM-derived glucose metrics, HbA1c and markers of subclinical atherosclerosis in adults with Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) in the CORDIA study.

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: One hundred and seventy-nine adults (79 women) with long-standing T1DM wore an Apple Watch for 14 nights; glycaemia was assessed from routine 14-day CGM reports (FreeStyle Libre 2, Dexcom G6/G7 or Guardian 4) and HbA1c. Carotid plaques were assessed by ultrasound and coronary artery calcium (CAC) by computed tomography. Participants also completed the Munich Chronotype Questionnaire (MCTQ). Spearman correlations with false discovery rate (FDR) correction and multivariable linear regression were used.

RESULTS: Shorter REM sleep correlated with higher HbA1c (ρ = -0.24; padj = 0.011) and, with borderline significance after FDR correction, with higher GRI, TAR2, mean sensor glucose and glucose SD and lower TIR (|ρ| 0.17-0.21; padj = 0.052). REM sleep expressed as a proportion of total sleep correlated with GRI, TIR, mean glucose and glucose SD (|ρ| 0.18-0.20; padj = 0.044). In adjusted models, REM duration was associated with all glycaemic metrics; the association with glucose SD persisted after additional adjustment for HbA1c and after exclusion of nights with less than 4 h of recorded sleep. After adjustment for age and sex, participants with two or more carotid plaques had 9.4 min shorter REM sleep (p = 0.034); associations with CAC and deep sleep were attenuated. Older age was associated with lower social jetlag (ρ = -0.20; p = 0.010).

CONCLUSIONS: In adults with T1DM, shorter REM sleep was modestly associated with worse glycaemia, most consistently with glucose variability and HbA1c, and with carotid plaque burden. These cross-sectional findings generate hypotheses for longitudinal studies combining sleep tracking with CGM.

articles.title: Early Changes in Peripancreatic Mesenteric Fat Beyond Weight Loss Predict Durability of Hepatic Improvements in MASLD.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Various visceral adipose tissue depots exhibit heterogeneous metabolic properties. This study aims to explore whether specific abdominal fat compartments differentially predict loss of sustained treatment response to lifestyle interventions in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Consecutive treatment-naïve MASLD patients were prospectively enrolled from January 2015 to March 2024, with a 96-week follow-up period. Liver fat content, preperitoneal fat thickness (PFT), peripancreatic mesenteric fat thickness (MFT1), periumbilical mesenteric fat thickness (MFT2) and perirenal fat thickness (PrFT) were quantified using magnetic resonance imaging. Liver stiffness measurement (LSM) was assessed by 2D-SWE. Treatment responses were evaluated at 48 and 96 weeks, and the primary outcome was loss of response at 96 weeks.

RESULTS: A total of 631 MASLD patients (mean age: 41.5 ± 13.8 years; 72.0% male) were included. Logistic regression analyses revealed that a greater 48-week relative decrease in MFT1 (per 10% relative reduction), rather than in MFT2, PFT or PrFT, was independently associated with lower odds of losing MRI-PDFF response (OR: 0.48, 95% CI: 0.34-0.69, p < 0.001) and LSM response (OR: 0.53, 95% CI: 0.28-0.99, p = 0.046) at 96 weeks. Receiver operating characteristic curve analyses indicated that relative changes in MFT1 showed discriminatory ability for the loss of MRI-PDFF and LSM responses, with areas under the curves of 0.70 (95% CI: 0.64-0.76) and 0.77 (95% CI: 0.67-0.88), respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Early changes in MFT1 were associated with subsequent loss of response in hepatic steatosis and fibrosis, suggesting potential prognostic value for hepatic response durability in MASLD.

articles.title: Bleeding and Thromboembolic Outcomes Following GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Initiation in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Atrial Fibrillation Receiving Direct Oral Anticoagulants: A Target Trial Emulation.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and Type 2 diabetes (T2D) require coordinated stroke prevention and metabolic risk management. Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are standard for stroke prevention, while glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are increasingly used in T2D. In DOAC users, GLP-1RA initiation may alter body weight and gastrointestinal physiology, potentially increasing DOAC exposure and thereby elevating bleeding risk. We aim to investigate the impact of GLP-1RA initiation on risks of thromboembolic disease and bleeding in patients with T2D and AF receiving DOACs.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We emulated a target trial comparing GLP-1RA versus dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor initiation. We identified Medicare beneficiaries aged ≥ 65 years with T2D and AF receiving DOACs. Randomization was emulated using 1:1 propensity score matching. Primary outcomes include thromboembolic disease and bleeding. Per-protocol effects were estimated using inverse-probability-censoring-weighted Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: After matching, 930 patients were included in each group, with mean follow-up of 1 year. Mean age was 74.7 vs. 74.2 years, and 47.1% vs. 44.2% were women in the GLP-1RA vs. DPP-4 inhibitor groups. GLP-1RA initiation was associated with higher bleeding risk (HR 1.18, 95% CI: 1.03-1.36), lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.58, 95% CI: 0.36-0.95), and similar thromboembolic risk (HR 1.50, 95% CI: 0.22-10.43).

CONCLUSIONS: Among DOAC-treated patients with T2D and AF, GLP-1RA initiation was associated with a less favourable bleeding profile but no evident increase in thromboembolic risk. These findings support careful clinical monitoring and further studies incorporating body weight and renal function to inform individualized treatment.

articles.title: Lactylation of HSC70 Impairs Chaperone-Mediated Autophagy to Promote Pyrin Inflammasome-Dependent PANoptosis in Macrophages During Sepsis.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-related cytokine storm is associated with poor prognosis in septic patients. IFNγ/LPS can synergistically trigger a sepsis-associated proinflammatory cytokine storm and induce macrophage death in the form of PANoptosis. The ensuing release of proinflammatory cytokines further amplifies macrophage death, leading to subsequent multiple organ damage. Concurrently, the IFNγ/LPS induced inflammatory cascade also downregulates chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA) activity, and this dysregulation further exacerbates the inflammatory response in macrophages and in vivo. Thus, a positive feedback loop between dysfunctional CMA and the inflammatory cascade is established. Enhancing CMA activation reduces macrophage death and organ damage, whereas inhibiting CMA exacerbates macrophage PANoptosis and organ injury. Mechanistically, impaired CMA leads to accumulation of the transcription factor CUX1, which subsequently upregulates Pyrin expression and promotes Pyrin-mediated PANoptosome assembly, thereby driving macrophage PANoptosis. In addition to the cytokine storm, the lacylation at lysine 561 (K561) of HSC70, a core component of the CMA machinery, is associated with reduced CMA activity. Blocking lactylation can similarly attenuate macrophage death and multiple organ injury in sepsis. Taken together, this "Kla-CMA-CUX1/Pyrin-PANoptosis" signaling axis, linking metabolic reprogramming to immune dysregulation in sepsis, suggests that targeting key nodes of this axis may represent a promising therapeutic strategy to reduce sepsis-associated mortality.

articles.title: Correction to 'Young Adults With Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease, Defined Using the Fatty Liver Index, Can Be at Increased Risk of Myocardial Infarction or Stroke'.

Exploring Corresponding Cutpoints for Hypoglycaemia Awareness Questionnaire (HypoA-Q) Impaired Awareness Subscale in Relation to the Gold and Clarke Measures: A Post Hoc Analysis From the Hypo-METRICS Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The Hypoglycaemia Awareness Questionnaire-Impaired Awareness subscale (HypoA-Q/IA) was developed to enhance impaired awareness of hypoglycaemia (IAH) assessment, addressing methodological deficiencies of the established Gold and Clarke measures. An IAH cutpoint (HypoA-Q/IA ≥ 12) was identified from a clamp study in Type 1 diabetes (T1D). We explored cutpoints in relation to Gold and Clarke measures, and their co-occurrence, in the larger, real-world observational Hypo-METRICS study, in people with T1D (pwT1D) and insulin-treated Type 2 diabetes (pwT2D).

MATERIAL AND METHODS: Hypo-METRICS recruited pwT1D or pwT2D with ≥ 1 hypoglycaemic event in the previous 3 months. IAH was defined as Gold ≥ 4, Clarke ≥ 4 and/or HypoA-Q/IA ≥ 12. Bidirectional ROC analysis was performed between HypoA-Q/IA and Gold/Clarke cutpoints.

RESULTS: Questionnaires were completed by 232 pwT1D and 285 pwT2D (male 47% vs. 62%, p < 0.001; median age 49 vs. 63 years, p < 0.001; HbA1c 7.3% vs. 7.4%, p = 0.03). IAH prevalence was 24% by Gold ≥ 4, 16% by Clarke ≥ 4 and 7% by HypoA-Q/IA ≥ 12. ROC analysis yielded HypoA-Q/IA cutpoints of ≥ 7 against Gold ≥ 4 (AUC 0.87) and ≥ 9 against Clarke ≥ 4 (AUC 0.89), and cutpoints of Gold ≥ 4 (AUC 0.87) and Clarke ≥ 3 (AUC 0.93) against HypoA-Q/IA ≥ 12. Of those with IAH by either measure, 24% were identified by both HypoA-Q/IA ≥ 12 and Gold ≥ 4, and 32% by both HypoA-Q/IA ≥ 12 and Clarke ≥ 4, with lower overlap in T2D than T1D.

CONCLUSIONS: HypoA-Q/IA cutpoints corresponding to legacy IAH cutpoints (≥ 7-9) were lower than the clamp-derived threshold (≥ 12), suggesting ≥ 12 may identify a subgroup with more severe IAH. These cutpoints enable cross-study comparison; prospective validation against severe hypoglycaemia risk is needed.

articles.title: β-Cell Recovery Patterns With Initial Combination Versus Stepwise Therapy in Newly Diagnosed Type 2 Diabetes: TRIPLE-AXEL Post Hoc Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early intensive therapy may preserve β-cell function in newly diagnosed Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), but whether different early treatment strategies produce distinct patterns of β-cell functional recovery remains unclear.

METHODS: This post hoc analysis of the TRIPLE-AXEL trial included 75 drug-naïve participants who completed 104 weeks of treatment and underwent 75-g oral glucose tolerance tests at baseline and Week 104. Participants were randomized to initial triple combination therapy (TCT; metformin, dapagliflozin and saxagliptin) or stepwise add-on therapy (SAT; metformin followed by glimepiride and sitagliptin). Insulin secretion, insulin sensitivity and β-cell compensatory function were assessed using the insulinogenic index (IGI), Matsuda insulin sensitivity index (ISI) and disposition index (DI), respectively.

RESULTS: HbA1c decreased by approximately 2.7% over 104 weeks in both groups. DI increased significantly in both TCT and SAT, with no significant between-group difference in the baseline-adjusted change (difference, -0.09 [95% CI, -0.44 to 0.27]; p = 0.63). Baseline-adjusted changes in IGI and ISI also did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.35 and p = 0.85, respectively), although the within-group increase in ISI was significant only in the TCT group. In multivariable models, greater HbA1c reduction was associated with higher DI at Week 104. Hypoglycaemia occurred in none of the participants in the TCT group and in 23.7% of those in the SAT group.

CONCLUSIONS: In newly diagnosed T2DM, both treatment strategies improved β-cell function without significant between-group differences. TCT achieved this without hypoglycaemia; however, given the on-treatment assessment, physiological equivalence cannot be concluded.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT02946632.

articles.title: Correction to 'Gold and Clarke Questionnaires Identify Different People With Insulin-Treated Diabetes and Impaired Awareness of Hypoglycaemia in Almost 60% of Cases: A Post Hoc Analysis From the Hypo-METRICS Study'.
Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Type 1 Diabetes: The Importance of Identifying the Insulin-Resistant Type 1 Diabetes Phenotype, and Differentiating Early and Newer Generation Therapies.
Semaglutide, Tirzepatide and Clinically Recorded Alcohol-Related Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes: A Target Trial Emulation.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To compare the risk of incident alcohol use disorder (AUD) among adults with Type 2 diabetes (T2D) initiating semaglutide, tirzepatide or sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a target trial emulation using de-identified electronic health record data from the TriNetX research network (June 2022-January 2025). Adults with T2D newly initiating semaglutide, tirzepatide or an SGLT2i were included. The primary outcome was clinically recorded hospitalization or emergency department (ED) visits for AUD. Cox proportional hazards models with 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses as well as secondary outcomes assessed the robustness of the findings.

RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 0.81-1.02 years, the incidence rates (IRs) of clinically recorded hospitalization or ED visits for AUD were 2.42 versus 4.53 per 1000 person-years for semaglutide versus SGLT2i, with an HR of 0.54 (95% CI, 0.45-0.64). Similarly, the IRs were 2.34 versus 3.98 per 1000 person-years for tirzepatide versus SGLT2i, with an HR of 0.61 (95% CI, 0.46-0.83). In the direct comparison of semaglutide versus tirzepatide, IRs were 2.43 and 2.36 per 1000 person-years, respectively, with no difference in risk (HR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.73-1.31). Results were consistent across sensitivity and subgroup analyses and secondary outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: In adults with T2D, semaglutide and tirzepatide were associated with lower rates of clinically recorded AUD-related outcomes than SGLT2i, with no difference between the two GLP-1RA medications.

articles.title: Dose-Exposure-Response Analysis of Finerenone on Serum Potassium and Cardiovascular Outcomes Among Patients With Heart Failure: Insights From FINEARTS-HF.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Finerenone reduces the risk of heart failure and cardiovascular (CV) death among patients with heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction (HFmrEF/HFpEF). Whether the effects of finerenone to reduce CV risk are dose/exposure dependent is not clear.

METHODS: In FINEARTS-HF, 6001 participants were randomized to finerenone or placebo, where the initial and target dose of finerenone was titrated according to the baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR; 10- > 20 mg if baseline eGFR ≤ 60; 20- > 40 mg if > 60 mL/min/1.73 m2) and by serum potassium and changes in eGFR during the trial. We fitted non-linear mixed-effects population pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic and parametric repeated time-to-event models to explore the effect of finerenone dose on exposure (n = 6658 plasma concentration measurements) and exposure on serum potassium (n = 123 720 measurements), NT-proBNP (n = 16 971 measurements) and the primary composite outcome of total heart failure events and CV death (n = 2366 events).

RESULTS: The mean eGFR in those with an initial dose of 10 mg and 20 mg was 46 ± 12 and 76 ± 14 mL/min/1.73 m2, respectively. The frequency of hyperkalemia (> 5.5 mmol/L) was 4.3% in patients taking 10 mg finerenone, 2.7% among those taking 20 mg and 1.5% among those taking 40 mg. Simulated PK/PD data produced higher serum potassium with higher finerenone exposure in a hypothetical scenario without dose titration; however, when simulating the protocol-guided dose titration strategy implemented in the trial, the lower observed frequency of hyperkalemia at higher finerenone exposure was explained. For the efficacy exposure-response analyses, while higher finerenone exposure was non-significantly related to a lower frequency of CV composite events (p = 0.55), higher exposure did result in a significantly greater reduction in NT-proBNP concentrations (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Among participants of FINEARTS-HF, finerenone dose titration was effective in managing serum potassium concentration. Although FINEARTS-HF was not designed to test a randomized comparison of dose or exposure, the PK/PD model suggests that higher achieved exposure is associated with improved CV efficacy.

articles.title: Closed-Loop Insulin Delivery in Inpatient Care: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Clinical and Implementation Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Closed-loop (CL) insulin delivery systems have transformed outpatient diabetes care. However, evidence supporting their role in inpatient settings is limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the safety, efficacy, and implementation of CL systems in inpatient care.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This review followed PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420251133486). Eligible studies reported glycaemic, safety, and/or implementation outcomes for adults managed with CL systems in inpatient care. EMBASE, PubMed, MEDLINE, Scopus, CINAHL, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to August 2026. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB2 and ROBINS-I. Random-effects meta-analysis evaluated glycaemic outcomes and length of stay (LOS). Results were presented as pooled mean differences (MDs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Implementation data were analysed thematically. Intrapartum outcomes were analysed separately.

RESULTS: Thirteen inpatient studies were included, nine contributing to meta-analysis. CL delivery increased time in range (MD +22.27%, 95% CI: 16.03-28.51; p < 0.001) and reduced time above range (MD -23.75%, 95% CI: -28.05 to -19.45; p < 0.001), mean glucose (MD -1.66 mmol/L, 95% CI: -2.29 to -1.03; p < 0.001) and glucose standard deviation (MD -0.64 mmol/L, 95% CI: -0.85 to -0.43; p < 0.001). No significant differences were observed in time below range, coefficient of variation or LOS. Total daily insulin dose was higher (MD +10.82 IU/day, 95% CI: 0.02-21.62; p = 0.05). No serious device-attributed adverse events were reported. Implementation challenges included staff training, technical support, and workflow integration. Four additional intrapartum studies were included; two contributed to the meta-analysis, showing increased pregnancy-specific time in range (MD +11.82%, 95% CI: 5.56-18.08; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: CL systems improve inpatient glycaemic control, although effects on LOS and comparative safety remain uncertain. Wider adoption requires sustainable technical and organisational support.

articles.title: Changes in Metabolic and Blood Pressure Outcomes With Semaglutide Across Chronic Kidney Disease Stages: A Post Hoc Analysis of the FLOW Trial.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To assess changes in glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), body weight, and systolic/diastolic blood pressure (SBP/DBP) by chronic kidney disease (CKD) and albuminuria categories in a post hoc analysis of FLOW, an international, double-blind, randomized, phase 3b clinical trial of adults with CKD and Type 2 diabetes (T2D).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We evaluated the effect of semaglutide 1.0 mg versus placebo (in addition to standard of care) on changes in HbA1c, body weight, SBP, and DBP from baseline to Week 104 stratified by baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR; ≥ 60, ≥ 45 to < 60, ≥ 30 to < 45, < 30 mL/min/1.73 m2) and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR; < 30, 30 to < 300, and ≥ 300 mg/g). Outcomes were analysed using analysis of covariance with baseline eGFR/UACR as covariates and an interaction term for treatment group by eGFR/UACR categories. We calculated the estimated treatment difference (ETD) between the semaglutide and placebo groups.

RESULTS: FLOW included 3533 participants. Compared with participants assigned placebo, those assigned semaglutide had greater reductions in HbA1c (ETD range across eGFR/UACR groups: -0.7% to -1.0%; all p < 0.0001) and body weight (ETD: -2.5 kg to -4.6 kg; all p < 0.0001 except UACR < 30) from baseline to Week 104. Participants with lower baseline eGFR/higher UACR categories treated with semaglutide also had greater improvements in SBP than those receiving placebo. In interaction analyses, the treatment effect did not differ significantly by baseline eGFR/UACR for any of the outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Semaglutide improves glycaemic control and weight, regardless of baseline eGFR or UACR, and SBP in lower eGFR/higher UACR categories.

articles.title: Anthropometric, Muscle Function, Physical Activity, Inflammatory and Dietary Characteristics Associated With Fasting Glucose and Insulin Resistance in Rural and Urban Malawian Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: In African populations, Type 2 diabetes often occurs at relatively low BMI. We examined anthropometric, muscle function, physical activity, inflammatory and dietary correlates of fasting glucose and insulin resistance.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Nutrition and Metabolic Health in Malawi (NUTRI-MET Malawi) recruited 100 adults from rural Karonga and urban Lilongwe stratified by glycaemic status at the time of an earlier population survey (50 impaired fasting glucose [IFG] and 50 normoglycaemic) and matched for age, sex and location. Participants underwent anthropometry, handgrip strength, accelerometer-measured physical activity, dietary and biomarker assessment. As glycaemic status changed in some participants, analyses used current fasting glucose and homeostasis-model-estimated insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) adjusted for age, sex and location.

RESULTS: Central adiposity, lower relative grip strength and lower physical activity were associated with higher fasting glucose and HOMA-IR. Each 0.1 higher waist-to-hip ratio was associated with 0.420 mmol L-1 higher fasting glucose (95% CI: 0.143-0.696) and 58.1% higher HOMA-IR (31.5%-90.2%). Each 0.1 kg per kg body mass higher relative grip strength was associated with 0.199 (0.042-0.356) mmol L-1 lower fasting glucose and 19.9% (10.8%-28.0%) lower HOMA-IR. Central adiposity and relative grip strength together accounted for 24%-26% of HOMA-IR variance, in models including age, sex and location. Each 30 min day-1 spent inactive was associated with 8.8% higher HOMA-IR, and 10 min day-1 vigorous activity with 11.9% lower HOMA-IR. Higher white blood cell count was associated with higher HOMA-IR. Dietary characteristics showed no clear associations.

CONCLUSIONS: Central adiposity, relative grip strength and physical activity were important correlates of glycaemia and insulin resistance in this relatively lean, highly active population.

articles.title: Therapeutic Signals Without Histologic Certainty: FGF Analogues in Compensated MASH Cirrhosis-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Compensated MASH cirrhosis is an advanced disease with no current approved pharmacologic therapy. FGF analogues have shown biological activity, but individual trials have not established histologic efficacy. We aim to evaluate their effects across histologic and non-invasive outcomes in this population.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception through 8 July 2026 for RCTs comparing FGF analogues with placebo in adults with compensated (F4) MASH cirrhosis. The primary outcome was at least 1-stage fibrosis improvement without MASH worsening. Secondary outcomes included Pro-C3, Enhanced Liver Fibrosis (ELF) score and liver stiffness. MASH resolution and safety were exploratory. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. RoB 2 and GRADE assessments were conducted.

RESULTS: Five RCTs involving 589 participants were included. FGF analogues did not significantly improve fibrosis by at least one stage without worsening of MASH (RR, 1.32; 95% CI, 0.89-1.97). In post hoc exploratory analyses, FGF21 analogues increased MASH resolution alone (RR, 3.17; 95% CI, 1.49-6.73), whereas resolution without worsening of fibrosis remained inconclusive (RR, 1.75; 95% CI, 0.95-3.23). Treatment reduced ELF score (MD, -0.52; 95% CI, -0.79 to -0.25), Pro-C3 (MD, -26.49 percentage points; 95% CI, -40.47 to -12.51) and liver stiffness (MD, -2.30 kPa; 95% CI, -3.90 to -0.71). Serious adverse events were not significantly increased, but adverse-event-related discontinuation was more frequent (RR, 3.44; 95% CI, 1.13-10.43). FGF19 findings derive from a single trial (aldafermin).

CONCLUSIONS: FGF analogues did not significantly improve the primary fibrosis endpoint, but improved MASH resolution and non-invasive fibrosis measures, supporting continued evaluation of FGF analogues in Phase 3 trials with longer follow-up.

articles.title: 18F-FGln PET/CT Imaging of Glutamine Uptake Has Potential for Predicting Immunotherapy Response in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
articles.abstract: We investigated whether glutamine (Gln) uptake, imaged by 18F-(2S,4R)-4-fluoroglutamine (18F-FGln) PET/CT, could predict and modulate immunotherapy response in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Analysis of the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)-Liver Hepatocellular Carcinoma (LIHC) dataset revealed that SLC1A5 expression-which encodes a primary Gln uptake channel in HCC cells-was significantly associated with poor prognosis, higher tumor grade, and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In murine HCC models, tumors with high 18F-FGln uptake exhibited elevated Slc1a5 expression and poor response to anti-PD-1 therapy, whereas low-uptake tumors were more sensitive to immunotherapy. Genetic knockdown of Slc1a5 reduced 18F-FGln uptake, enhanced anti-PD-1 efficacy, increased cytotoxic T lymphocyte infiltration, and decreased regulatory T cell abundance. Transcriptomic and single-cell analyses revealed activation of antitumor immune pathways and reprogramming toward an immune-inflamed phenotype after Slc1a5 suppression. V-9302 decreased tumor Gln uptake, as measured by 18F-FGln PET/CT, and sensitized HCC to PD-1 blockade. In patient-derived organoid-T cell co-culture systems, low-SLC1A5 organoids were susceptible to PD-1 blockade, whereas high-SLC1A5 organoids were resistant, consistent with 18F-FGln PET/CT findings. These results identify Gln uptake as a checkpoint of immune evasion in HCC and support that 18F-FGln PET/CT has the potential to predict and monitor immunotherapy response.

Artificial intelligence research ın women's health: Bibliometric analysis of scientific publications between 2020-2025.
articles.abstract: Although AI applications in women's health are increasing rapidly, few bibliometric studies have systematically examined research trends and priority topics in this field. We conducted a bibliometric analysis of research on women's health and artificial intelligence published between 2020 and 2025 to interpret the field's evolution and identify gaps within it. We analyzed 3241 articles indexed in the Web of Science database, retrieved on 13.09.2025, using VOSviewer software and co--authorship, co-occurrence, citation, and country analysis techniques. We found that publications increased over the years, the USA produced the most, and the most-cited studies focused on obstetric imaging, gestational diabetes, and infertility. The most frequently used keywords were machine learning, pregnancy, artificial intelligence, deep learning, and fertility. Researchers in this field focus on clinically prioritized problems and use algorithm-based approaches. International collaboration and multidisciplinary approaches will accelerate its development.

Combined structural and functional assessment of the ophthalmic trigeminal pathway in healthy adults: a feasibility study with preliminary reference data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Structural and functional evaluation of the ophthalmic division (V1) of the trigeminal nerve lacks standardised approaches integrating high-resolution anatomical imaging with complementary neurophysiological testing.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility of a multimodal assessment of the ophthalmic trigeminal pathway using high-resolution non-contrast MRI, blink reflex testing (BRT) and Quantitative Cutaneous Sensory Testing (QEST) and to report preliminary descriptive anatomical, neurophysiological and cutaneous sensory measurements in healthy adults.

METHODS: In this prospective observational study, 20 healthy volunteers (11 males and 9 females; mean age 32 years) underwent 3-T MRI, BRT and QEST. MRI included three-dimensional isotropic T1-weighted sequences for morphometric assessment of the left frontal and supraorbital nerves. Blink reflex latencies and QEST thresholds were assessed bilaterally.

RESULTS: Frontal and supraorbital nerves were visualised in all subjects. Mean frontal nerve calibre was 0.160 cm×0.160 cm; proximal and distal supraorbital segments measured 0.148 cm×0.135 cm and 0.140 cm×0.114 cm, respectively. All blink reflex responses were present. R2 latencies were strongly correlated between sides, and the mean absolute inter-side differences were 0.63 ms for R1, 2.03 ms for ipsilateral R2 and 1.17 ms for contralateral R2. QEST thresholds demonstrated no significant lateral differences.

CONCLUSIONS: This study supports the feasibility of a combined MRI–blink reflex–QEST protocol and provides preliminary descriptive measurements of complementary structural, reflex and cutaneous sensory domains of the ophthalmic trigeminal pathway. Larger, age-diverse cohorts and prospective clinical validation are required before these measurements can be used as normative intervals or for clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Integrating PET/CT and correlative biomarkers for prospective evaluation of extramedullary disease in relapsed/refractory B-ALL: implications for CAR T-cell therapy.
Antiviral Cytokine Signaling in Insects: Functional Parallels with Vertebrate Interferon Antiviral Immunity.
articles.abstract: The absence of homologs for interferons and their receptors in insect genomes has long suggested that insects lack inducible antiviral responses. However, recent accumulating evidence calls this view into question. In this review, we summarize key findings and recent advances in this emerging field. Several secreted factors that respond to viral infection have been identified in insects, including Vago and Vago-like proteins; among these, members such as CxVago and BmVago activate downstream antiviral responses through the JAK/STAT pathway. Homologs of vertebrate interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) including CH25H, NFIL3, MxL1, and viperin have also been demonstrated to possess antiviral activities in insects. These findings outline a functional cascade of "virus-induced secreted factor - receptor recognition - signal transduction-antiviral effector" suggesting the presence of antiviral cytokine signaling in insects that is functionally parallel to the vertebrate IFN system. Although this field remains in its infancy, the available evidence has laid a foundation for future investigations. Further studies are needed to systematically identify novel antiviral cytokine molecules, validate functional receptors, and elucidate downstream signaling networks and effector mechanisms.

articles.title: A Synchronized Two-Surgeon Workflow for Two-Level Unilateral Biportal Endoscopic Transforaminal Lumbar Interbody Fusion: Technical Note and Preliminary Case Series.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe a standardized four-phase synchronized two-surgeon workflow for selected two-level unilateral biportal endoscopic transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion (UBE-TLIF) and report its preliminary outcomes.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective Technical Note included 33 consecutive patients (66 operated levels) treated in 2025 by a fixed pair of experienced surgeons. Each surgeon performed endoscopic decompression and interbody fusion at an assigned level, with coordinated fluoroscopy, guidewire staging, shared-device use, and percutaneous instrumentation. Perioperative outcomes, pain and disability scores, 90-day adverse events, and CT-based fusion assessments obtained at least 12 months postoperatively were reviewed.

RESULTS: All 33 procedures were completed. Mean operative time was 294 ± 59 minutes, estimated blood loss was 299 ± 78 mL, and median spine-surgery ward stay was 7 days (interquartile range, 6-9). Three patients (9.1%) had recorded adverse events: incidental durotomy, wound infection requiring surgical debridement, and anemia requiring transfusion (one each). At a median final clinical follow-up of 427 days, median back- and leg-pain visual analog scale scores decreased from 6 to 1 and from 7 to 0, respectively; median Oswestry Disability Index decreased from 70 to 18 (all Holm-adjusted P < 0.001 versus baseline). CT at ≥12 months was available for 22/25 eligible patients; fusion (Bridwell I/II) was observed in 40/44 evaluable levels (91%) and at both operated levels in 20/22 patients (91%).

CONCLUSIONS: The coordinated workflow was feasible in an experienced fixed surgical pair. Prospective comparative studies are needed to assess efficiency, safety, resource use, and generalizability.

articles.title: Beyond Weight Loss: A Scoping Review and Thematic Analysis of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Across the Neurosurgical Landscape.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are increasingly used for diabetes and obesity. Literature spans spinal fusion, idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH), and cerebrovascular disease, but has not been systematically mapped. We aimed to map literature on GLP-1RA exposure in neurosurgical landscapes by characterizing study design, drug class, disease-specific outcomes, and safety considerations.

METHODS: This scoping review was conducted per the PRISMA-ScR guideline. Eligible studies reported GLP-1RA exposure in adults with spinal, intracranial, or cerebrovascular disease, recording clinical, perioperative, or imaging outcomes. Two reviewers screened independently with third-reviewer adjudication. Extracted variables included country, design, agent, timing, indication, neurosurgical and metabolic outcomes, and adverse events.

RESULTS: Of 1342, 48 were included, predominantly from the United States (US) (34/48, 71%). Most were retrospective (43/48, 90%); 31/48 (65%) used propensity score matching; 5/48 (10%) were randomized. Three themes dominated: spinal fusion (24/48, 50%), IIH and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics (14/48, 29%), and cerebrovascular and neurointerventional disease (10/48, 21%). In spinal fusion, perioperative GLP-1RA exposure was repeatedly associated with lower pseudarthrosis, although some studies reported increased postoperative complications. In IIH, GLP-1RAs were associated with lower papilledema, fewer CSF leaks, reduced acetazolamide requirement, and lower shunt placement. Cerebrovascular reports described lower intracerebral hemorrhage, subarachnoid hemorrhage, and post-stroke mortality, mostly in observational studies.

CONCLUSIONS: GLP-1RA neurosurgical literature is dominated by US-based retrospective, propensity-matched analyses. Benefit signals are most consistent in spinal fusion and IIH, but perioperative adverse effects and overlap among database cohorts limit causal interpretation. Adequately powered prospective trials with standardized endpoints are needed to confirm results.

articles.title: Acute Plasma Thrombo-Inflammatory and Cardiac Biomarker Profile in Methamphetamine-Associated Ischemic Stroke.
articles.journal: Food and chemical toxicology : an international journal published for the British Industrial Biological Research Association
articles.abstract: Methamphetamine use is associated with cerebrovascular disease, but biomarker alterations accompanying acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remain insufficiently characterized. This case-control study enrolled 90 male smokers equally divided into healthy controls, chronic methamphetamine users without stroke, and users with imaging-confirmed AIS. Blood was collected within three hours of AIS symptom onset. Plasma D-dimer, fibrinogen, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), P-selectin, NT-proBNP, and trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) were measured. Group comparisons used nonparametric tests with false discovery rate correction; discrimination was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic analysis. Compared with users without stroke, AIS patients showed markedly higher D-dimer, NT-proBNP, fibrinogen, hsCRP, P-selectin, and systolic blood pressure, alongside a smaller but significant increase in TMAO. D-dimer and NT-proBNP showed complete separation in this cohort, whereas fibrinogen and hsCRP showed strong discrimination and TMAO showed modest performance. These findings identify a biomarker pattern associated with AIS among chronic methamphetamine users, warranting external validation before diagnostic application.

articles.title: Single-cell profiling reveals monocyte mitochondrial dysfunction in patients with cirrhosis progressing to acute-on-chronic liver failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Patients with acute decompensation (AD) of cirrhosis are at a high risk of developing acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF), a syndrome characterized by multi-organ failure and high short-term mortality. Prospective studies addressing the cellular mechanisms that drive the transition from AD to ACLF are lacking. In this study, we aimed to determine whether peripheral immune cell subsets at hospital admission predict the progression from AD to ACLF and to delineate underlying molecular mechanisms.

METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 63 patients with AD and 15 healthy donors across five European centres, with a 90-day follow-up. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from 16 patients with distinct trajectories and 4 controls.

RESULTS: Progression to ACLF was associated with expansion of classical monocytes, particularly subcluster "C2", which specifically displayed impaired energy metabolism with reduced oxidative phosphorylation (p<0.001). A C2-derived gene signature (18 genes) was enriched in two large international whole-blood cohorts (PREDICT, n=689; ACLARA, n=521), particularly in patients with bacterial infections, those developing ACLF, and non-survivors (p<0.001). Functional validation by respirometry in an independent AD cohort confirmed declining monocyte Complex IV-dependent oxygen consumption in patients with pre-ACLF (p<0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: We identified and validated a distinct monocyte subpopulation with defective energy metabolism in patients with AD with poor outcomes, supporting a link between monocyte bioenergetic dysfunction and ACLF development. Impact and Implications:The cellular mechanisms that drive progression from acute decompensation (AD) to acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) remain poorly understood, limiting the development of effective strategies for therapeutic intervention. By integrating prospective single-cell transcriptomics, functional bioenergetic analyses, and validation in independent multicentre cohorts, we identified a distinct monocyte subset characterized by impaired oxidative phosphorylation that is associated with subsequent ACLF development. These findings are relevant to clinicians and researchers because they suggest that immune-metabolic dysfunction emerges before overt ACLF and may contribute to disease progression. While further mechanistic and prospective validation studies are required, our results provide a framework for the investigation of monocyte bioenergetics as a potential therapeutic target in patients with decompensated cirrhosis.

articles.title: Porto-sinusoidal vascular disorder-type lesions in patients with early fibrotic stages of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a rising cause of chronic liver disease. Liver stiffness measurement (LSM) to assess disease stage is gaining popularity but can demonstrate heterogeneous results in clinical practice. Moreover, portal hypertension may develop early in MASLD in the absence of cirrhosis. These observations may be partially explained by features not assessed in the current NASH-CRN liver biopsy staging, including features of porto-sinusoidal vascular disorder (PSVD).

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study in patients with MASLD who underwent biopsy between 2015 and 2022. All biopsies with NASH-CRN F0-F2 were screened for eligibility and revised in consensus by two expert liver pathologists. Primary objective was to assess the presence and severity of PSVD-type lesions. Secondary objectives included the grading of perisinusoidal fibrosis and to correlate histological features with LSM.

RESULTS: We included 136 patients [60% male, median age 50y] with a median BMI of 30 kg/m2, 15% having F1 fibrosis and 85% F2 fibrosis. Median LSM (available in 54%) was 8.2 kPa. Portal venule stenosis affecting ≥50% of portal tracts was present in 26% of biopsies, and muscularisation of portal venules was present in 21% of biopsies. Perisinusoidal fibrosis was present in 97% of biopsies, respectively mild, moderate, and severe in 62%, 32%, and 3%. PSVD-type lesions did not correlate with LSM, but LSM did correlate with the degree of perisinusoidal fibrosis.

CONCLUSION: Portal venule stenosis (≥50%) and muscularisation of portal venules, both major criteria associated with PSVD, were found in 26% and 21% biopsies, respectively. Furthermore, the extent of perisinusoidal fibrosis correlates with liver stiffness and could explain the heterogeneity of LSM in MASLD.

articles.journal: Clinics and research in hepatology and gastroenterology

articles.title: Factors associated with tocilizumab primary failure in the treatment of giant cell arteritis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Giant cell arteritis (GCA) is the most common systemic vasculitis in adults over 50. Tocilizumab (TCZ), the first biologic approved in GCA, enables glucocorticoid-sparing remission, but reliable predictors of treatment outcome at initiation are lacking. We aimed to identify baseline and follow-up predictors of TCZ failure in GCA.

METHODS: In this retrospective single-centre cohort study, consecutive GCA patients receiving their first TCZ course at Caen University Hospital (2014-2024) were included, excluding early withdrawal (<3 months). Two multivariable logistic regression models were built using backward stepwise elimination: a baseline model and a combined baseline-and-follow-up model incorporating FDG-PET/CT metabolic response.

RESULTS: Of 91 patients, TCZ was successful in 43 (47%) and failed in 48 (53%). Baseline multivariable analysis identified three predictors of failure: CRP > 63.5 mg/L (OR 3.40; 95% CI 1.26-9.77; P<0.05), large-vessel vasculitis (LVV; OR 3.22; 95% CI 1.18-9.44; P<0.05) and previous relapse before TCZ (OR 3.75; 95% CI 1.16-9.41; P<0.05). A predictive score yielded an AUC of 0.774 (95% CI 0.674-0.873). In the combined follow-up model, PET/CT extinction status was significantly associated with treatment outcome overall (P<0.001). A longer duration of TCZ exposure was associated with a lower risk of failure (OR 0.911 per additional month, 95% CI 0.822-0.997; P<0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Baseline CRP, LVV and prior relapses can be combined into a simple predictive score to stratify the probability of TCZ response in GCA. Complete metabolic extinction on FDG-PET/CT during treatment further identifies patients at risk of failure.

articles.title: An unfair fight: multiorgan mechanisms that disarm host defenses and deplete the physiological reserve needed to withstand infection and sepsis after spinal cord injury.
articles.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) causes vulnerability to infection and sepsis that cannot be explained by impaired mobility and healthcare-related exposure alone. SCI is known to disrupt multiple organ systems, but how these disruptions collectively shift the balance between host protection and microbial challenge remains poorly defined. In this narrative review, we examine how systemic dysfunction caused by SCI impairs the capacity to prevent infection, contain established pathogens, and withstand escalating infectious stress. We organize clinical and experimental evidence around functions that together determine host protection: barrier protection, immune surveillance, pathogen clearance, and physiological reserve. The first three restrict microbial access, establishment, and burden, whereas physiological reserve determines the capacity of tissues and organs to maintain function as infectious stress escalates. We distinguish experimentally demonstrated mechanisms from clinical associations for infection vulnerability and examine how injury level and time shape these vulnerabilities. We trace how pneumonia, urinary tract infection, and pressure wound infection can progress to sepsis, and delineate the mechanisms that create increasingly unequal contests in which pathogens encounter a host with progressively weakened defenses, depleted physiological reserve, and an environment that favors pathogen establishment and persistence. This framework identifies testable gaps and a translational path toward earlier risk stratification, management of infection within the context of SCI, and potential strategies to preserve or restore host defense and resilience to infection, shifting the balance of this unequal contest back toward the host.

articles.title: Valve surgery is only the beginning: optimizing lifelong care for rheumatic heart disease.
Fibroblast growth factor 10 (FGF10) ameliorates pulmonary arterial hypertension by restoring endothelial mitochondrial function and reducing DNA damage via the PPARγ pathway.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is characterized by endothelial dysfunction, but the role of fibroblast growth factor 10 (FGF10) in regulating mitochondrial integrity and DNA damage remains unclear.

METHODS: A monocrotaline (MCT)-induced PAH rat model and MCTP-treated pulmonary artery endothelial cells were used. FGF10 was silenced using AAV- or lentivirus-mediated shRNA and supplemented exogenously. PPARγ involvement was assessed using GW9662 inhibition and Co-IP assays. Hemodynamic analysis, histology, and molecular assays were performed to evaluate vascular and endothelial alterations.

RESULTS: MCT exposure induced severe pulmonary vascular remodeling and endothelial mitochondrial injury, including fragmentation, reduced membrane potential, increased ROS, and persistent DNA damage responses. FGF10 knockdown aggravated these abnormalities, whereas exogenous FGF10 significantly restored mitochondrial structure and function, reduced oxidative stress, and attenuated DNA damage. Mechanistically, FGF10 upregulated PPARγ expression in vivo and in vitro. Pharmacological inhibition of PPARγ partially abolished the protective effects of FGF10. Co-IP further confirmed an interaction between FGF10 and PPARγ.

CONCLUSION: FGF10 protects against MCT-induced pulmonary vascular remodeling by preserving mitochondrial homeostasis and limiting DNA damage in endothelial cells via a PPARγ-dependent mechanism. The FGF10-PPARγ axis may represent a potential therapeutic target for PAH, warranting further validation in additional models and translational studies.

articles.title: Functional restoration of disease-associated VDR-CH variants through heterodimeric partner RXR and VDR ligand calcitriol partnership.
articles.abstract: The vitamin D receptor (VDR), a ligand-activated nuclear receptor, plays essential roles in calcium metabolism, immune function, and gene regulation through its heterodimerization with retinoid X receptor (RXR). Mutations in the ligand-binding domain (LBD) of VDR have been implicated in hereditary vitamin D-resistant rickets and type 1 diabetes, yet the molecular and cellular basis of their dysfunction remains poorly understood. Here, we functionally characterize compound heterozygous (CH) variants of VDR harboring SNP L263R and R391S, which are located in a conserved region of the LBD. These variants exhibited i) aberrant subcellular localization, ii) markedly reduced transcriptional activity, and iii) failure in associating with the mitotic chromatin. Notably, neither RXR co-expression nor calcitriol treatment alone restored receptor function. However, it was interesting to observe that the formation of a ternary complex of VDR-CH variants (L263R or R391S), along with heterodimeric partner RXR and VDR ligand calcitriol, promoted nuclear translocation and mitotic chromatin interaction, but the transcriptional rescue was mutation-dependent, with stronger recovery for R391S and limited recovery for L263R. The interaction of these three components, i.e., VDR variant, RXR, and calcitriol, together appeared to contribute to structural and functional stabilization of receptor conformation. This study reveals how specific VDR LBD mutations disrupt receptor architecture and cellular dynamics at multiple levels. The ability of RXR and calcitriol together to restore key functional properties suggests that conformational rescue of VDR-CH variant can be possibly achieved through co-ordinated heterodimerization and ligand treatments. The findings here offer important mechanistic insight into VDR-RXR-calcitriol interactions, suggesting hitherto unexplored therapeutic avenues through conformational rescue of disease-inflicting structurally disordered receptor.

articles.title: NA-DIP: A Noise-Aware Deep Image Prior for Generating Dedicated Brain PET-Quality Images from Whole-Body PET Acquisitions.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To generate dedicated brain PET-quality images from routine whole-body PET acquisitions by robustly enhancing the brain region using a noise-aware deep image prior (NA-DIP) approach.

METHODS: NA-DIP integrates anatomy-guided priors derived from patient-specific μ-maps or MR images, a regularization strategy for enhanced denoising, and a variance-based early stopping criterion that adaptively monitors noise without requiring prior noise assumptions. Using noisy PET images as self-supervised targets, the method was first evaluated using simulation data spanning three noise levels to investigate the trade-off between noise suppression and bias. It was then applied to brain images extracted from 90-s-per-bed-position whole-body acquisitions from 15 pediatric FDG-PET studies spanning a broad range of patient demographics, physiological variability, and image noise levels. Using the corresponding 360-s-per-bed-position dedicated brain scans as the reference, NA-DIP-enhanced images were evaluated for noise reduction, standardized uptake value (SUV) accuracy, and image quality in a blinded reader study.

RESULTS: NA-DIP demonstrated a superior noise-bias trade-off compared with Gaussian filtering and conventional DIP stopping strategies, particularly under high-noise conditions. The inclusion of MR or μ-map guidance further improved performance. Across pediatric patients, NA-DIP-enhanced 90-s images exhibited lower noise than the corresponding 360-s dedicated brain images while showing modest variability in SUV measurements. Blinded readers rated the NA-DIP-enhanced images as comparable to or better than dedicated brain images in most cases.

CONCLUSION: NA-DIP enhanced brain PET images from whole-body acquisitions demonstrated good quantitative agreement and image quality comparable to or exceeding the reference, supporting the feasibility of eliminating separate dedicated brain scans.

articles.title: Treatment Strategies and Outcomes of Aneurysms Affecting Small and Medium Arteries in Neurofibromatosis Type 1. A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1)-associated arterial aneurysms are rare and characterized by vessel fragility and heterogeneous presentation. Evidence guiding optimal management remains limited. This systematic review aimed to evaluate treatment strategies and outcomes in NF1-related arterial aneurysms.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251169825). PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for studies reporting management and outcomes of NF1-associated arterial aneurysms. Case reports, case series, and observational studies were included. Data were independently extracted by two reviewers. Primary outcomes included treatment strategies, technical success, complications, and mortality. Isolated aortic aneurysms or aortic dissections were not considered the primary target of the review. However, studies reporting concomitant aortic disease and aneurysmal involvement of non-aortic arteries were retained when relevant data on NF1-associated vasculopathy and its management were available.

RESULTS: Eighty-six studies including 99 patients (mean age 42 years; 44.4% male) were analyzed. Aneurysms were most frequently located in cervico-vertebral (45.2%) and visceral arteries (24.0%). Multifocal disease was present in 12.1% of patients. Overall, 65.7% of patients presented with aneurysm rupture or acute hemorrhage. This high proportion should be interpreted cautiously because of the substantial publication bias inherent to a literature predominantly based on case reports and small case series. Endovascular therapy was the most frequently used approach (68.7%), followed by open surgery (19.2%), hybrid repair (5.0%), and conservative management (9.1%). Endovascular treatment showed a reported technical success rate exceeding 90%. Recanalization (6.3%), delayed thrombosis (4.2%), and new aneurysm formation (5.3%) were observed. Open repair was mainly used for anatomically complex or endovascularly inaccessible lesions. Overall mortality was 8.1%, primarily in patients presenting with rupture.

CONCLUSIONS: NF1-associated aneurysms require an individualized, anatomy-driven management strategy. Endovascular therapy was the most frequently reported treatment and appears to be a viable option in anatomically suitable patients, while open and hybrid techniques remain important for selected complex lesions. However, the available evidence is derived predominantly from case reports and small case series and does not permit comparative assessment of treatment strategies. Lifelong imaging surveillance is mandatory due to the risk of recurrence and new aneurysm formation.
