articles.title: 18F-FDG PET-based radiomics for the prediction of aggressive/high-grade tumor in patients with cartilaginous tumors: A preliminary study.
articles.journal: Revista espanola de medicina nuclear e imagen molecular
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the role of texture analysis of pre-treatment 18F-FDG PET in the prediction of aggressive/high-grade tumor subtypes of cartilaginous tumors.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients with cartilaginous tumors (benign cartilaginous tumors or CSs) who underwent pre-treatment 18F-FDG PET for primary staging or restaging of recurrent disease were included in this retrospective study. Demographic and clinicopathologic data were collected. Textural and conventional PET parameters (maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax), SUVmean, metabolic tumor volume (MTV), and total lesion glycolysis (TLG)) were obtained from PET/CT images using LIFEx program. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression analysis was performed for feature selection. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to determine predictors of aggressive/high-grade tumor subtypes in cartilaginous tumors.

RESULTS: A total of 29 18F-FDG PET scans from 26 patients were included in the present study. Among 29 included 18F-FDG PET scans, 18 (62.1%) scans were performed in patients with a benign/low-grade tumor(benign cartilaginous tumors and G1-2 CSs), while 11 (37.9%) scans were performed in patients with an aggressive/high-grade tumor(G3, dedifferentiated, mesenchymal, and other aggressive CSs). In the LASSO logistic regression analysis, seven potential predictors were selected for predicting aggressive/high-grade cartilaginous tumors. Whereas SUVmax (p = 0.025), SUVmean (p = 0.028), GLRLM_Run Entropy (p = 0.007), GLSZM_ZSE (p = 0.011), and GLSZM_SZLGLE (p = 0.007) were significantly associated with aggressive/high-grade pathology in univariate analysis, GLRLM_Run Entropy was found as the only independent predictor in multivariate analysis.

CONCLUSION: Tumor heterogeneity assessed by texture analysis of pre-treatment 18F-FDG PET may be a significant predictor of aggressive/high-grade tumor subtypes in cartilaginous tumors.

articles.title: Trends and disparities in stroke-related mortality in cancer patients in the United States from 1999 to 2023: a nationwide temporal trend analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
AIM: With population aging and improved cancer survival, this study aims to analyze the temporal trends and disparities in stroke-related mortality among cancer patients from 1999 to 2023.

METHODS: Mortality data included deaths with cancer as the underlying cause and stroke as a contributing cause, extracted from the CDC WONDER database. Crude and age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) (≥ 25 years) were calculated for the overall population and subgroups. Joinpoint regression with the jump model was used to analyze trends, estimating the annual percentage change (APC) and average annual percentage change.

RESULTS: From 1999 to 2023, a total of 280,490 stroke-related deaths occurred among cancer patients in the United States. The overall AAMR declined slowly from 1999 to 2014 (APC: -2.53, 95% CI: -2.77 to -2.29), but gradually increased from 2014 to 2023 (APC: 3.08, 95% CI: 2.57 to 3.59). Most stroke-related deaths were classified as unspecified stroke. Across all cancer types, patients with leukemia had the highest proportion of stroke-related deaths (4.10%). Similar temporal trends were observed across sex, race, age group, census region, and urbanization subgroups. High-risk populations included males, Non-Hispanic Black individuals, rural residents, and older adults. The proportion of deaths occurring in medical facilities decreased gradually, while the proportion of deaths at decedents' homes showed an upward trend, with a prominent shift in 2020.

CONCLUSION: The long-term decline in stroke-related mortality among U.S. cancer patients reversed after 2014, with significant disparities across subgroups. This underscores the need to improve stroke management among cancer patients. Given the aggregated nature of CDC WONDER data and the use of ICD codes, this study was limited to a descriptive analysis; individual-level data and exploration of factors driving the observed trends were unavailable, and the results should be interpreted with caution.

authors: de Vos Tot Nederveen Cappel WH

articles.title: Analysis of pathological changes and virus-susceptible cells in the testes following MPXV infection in a rhesus macaque model.
articles.abstract: Monkeypox virus (MPXV) is an emerging public health threat, with increasing epidemiological and clinical evidence supporting sexual transmission, including detection of viral DNA in semen. However, the pathogenic mechanisms of MPXV within the male reproductive system remain poorly defined. We employed a rhesus macaque model to investigate MPXV-induced testicular alterations. Combining bulk RNA sequencing, histopathological analysis and immunofluorescence staining, we characterized testicular pathology, viral antigen distribution, and host responses during the early stage of infection. We found that MPXV did not induce marked inflammation or widespread cell death, and seminiferous tubule architecture remained largely intact during infection. Furthermore, within seminiferous tubules, Sertoli cells showed higher proportion of MPXV antigen co-localization than spermatogonia and spermatocytes, whereas in the interstitium, vascular endothelial cells and immune cells, including macrophages and T cells, showed prominent MPXV antigen detection, consistent with a potential contribution of hematogenous dissemination to testicular involvement. MPXV infection was associated with downregulation of the Sertoli cell marker SOX9 and alterations in tight junction-associated proteins, suggesting changes in Sertoli cell characteristics and BTB-associated molecular features. Transcriptomic analysis revealed changes in interferon-related antiviral pathways and complement-related gene expression, with C1q-positive signals detected in both interstitial and seminiferous tubular regions. In addition, changes in spermatogenesis-related gene expression were observed, which may reflect alterations in the spermatogenic microenvironment. Collectively, this study provides a quantitative characterization of early MPXV-testis interactions and cellular tropism across multiple testicular cell types in a non-human primate model, and provides insights into the pathological and immune responses associated with MPXV infection.

articles.title: The Future Burden of Type 2 Diabetes and the Role of Glycaemic Control and GLP1-RAs.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the impact of glycaemic target achievement, both with and without optimal treatment with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), on the predicted burden of type 2 diabetes (T2D) and associated complications from a UK healthcare system and society perspective METHODS: A system dynamics model was developed to predict the prevalence and burden of T2D and associated complications, stratified by age and haemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), in the UK from 2024 to 2060. Two treatment scenarios were evaluated: Scenario A, representing population-wide attainment of glycaemic targets, and Scenario B, applying a population-wide GLP-1 RA effect in addition to glycaemic target attainment. The GLP-1 RA effect was modelled via hazard ratios applied to age- and HbA1c-stratified rates of micro- and macrovascular complications RESULTS: Following current trends, the prevalence of T2D is expected to rise from 3·7M (5·3%) in 2024 to 6·3M (5·5-7.3M; 8·3% [7·9-8·8%]) in 2060, with total yearly costs increasing from £20·7bn to £33·4bn. Scenario A resulted in total cumulative savings of £61·4bn by 2060, driven by reductions in the direct cost of complications. Scenario B prevented 4·5 times as many macrovascular complications and 6 times as many deaths as Scenario A, resulting in total cumulative savings of £140·7bn. Savings in Scenario B were driven by the monetary value of life-years saved.

CONCLUSION: The cardiorenal protection afforded by GLP-1 RAs confers significant additional value compared with glycaemic control alone.

articles.title: Paternal PM2.5 exposure is associated with lipid metabolic dysfunction across generations and altered sperm and hepatic DNA methylation in mice.
articles.abstract: Paternal exposure to ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5) may affect metabolic health in progeny, while its multigenerational phenotypes and epigenetic underpinnings remain incompletely understood. Male C57BL/6J mice received filtered air (FA), unfiltered ambient air (UA), or concentrated ambient PM2.5 (CAP) inhalation exposure (6h/day, 5 days/week, 22 weeks). F1 offspring were derived from matings between exposed F0 males and unexposed females, and F2 and F3 were sequentially generated by crossing unexposed male descendants from the preceding generation with unexposed females. One male per independent litter was selected for each assay. Serum lipid profiles and hepatic lipid accumulation were evaluated in male offspring. Targeted bisulfite sequencing was applied to liver tissue, and WGBS was performed on F0 sperm to identify DMRs. CAP exposure is associated with dyslipidemia and hepatic steatosis in F1 and F2 males, with no statistically significant serum lipid changes in F3. UA exposure is associated with only minor lipid alterations. The expression of hepatic genes governing fatty acid oxidation, lipid degradation and cholesterol transport was disrupted in CAP-F1 and CAP-F2 mice. In CAP-F1 liver, Apoe_1 hypermethylation survived multiple-testing correction, whereas Apoa2_2 hypermethylation was nominally significant. Reduced Apoe mRNA was detected in CAP-F1 and CAP-F2 liver, accompanied by lower APOE and APOA2 protein in CAP-F1 liver. F0 sperm harbored abundant DMRs enriched in lipid metabolism and liver toxicity pathways. Apoe and Apoa2 presented concordant hypermethylation changes in F0 sperm and offspring liver. In summary, paternal PM2.5 exposure is associated with intergenerational lipid metabolic dysfunction and hepatic lipid deposition in F1 and F2 male offspring, accompanied by DNA methylation changes in F0 sperm and offspring liver.

articles.title: Bayesian Statistics for Arthroplasty Surgeons: Moving Beyond Simple "Yes or No" P-Values to Probabilistic Clinical Decision-Making.
articles.abstract: Statistical interpretation underpins evidence-based decision-making in total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Traditional frequentist approaches that rely on arbitrary P-value thresholds have long guided research design and analysis in arthroplasty. This approach produces binary conclusions that may overlook clinically meaningful differences, particularly for infrequent outcomes. Bayesian statistics provide a complementary framework that integrates prior knowledge with new evidence to generate probabilistic statements, which align more closely with real-world clinical reasoning. Primary prospective Bayesian-designed research remains rare in orthopaedics. Most Bayesian insights come from post hoc reanalyses of existing frequentist trials. Nevertheless, studies that employ Bayesian methods are increasing. This narrative review introduces core Bayesian principles and Bayes' theorem, illustrates the role of pretest probability in diagnostic testing with practical examples, contrasts frequentist and Bayesian interpretations, and offers criteria for critically appraising Bayesian arthroplasty research.

articles.title: Isolation, characterization, and therapeutic potential of a novel phage vB_KpiP_JZBo1 infecting Klebsiella pneumoniae.
articles.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae (K. pneumoniae) is an important opportunistic pathogenic bacterium that is often characterized by a multidrug-resistant phenotype, which can lead to the failure of antibiotic treatments. The emergence of multidrug-resistant K. pneumoniae, including carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae (CRKP), poses a significant threat to public health security. Bacteriophages, which are viruses capable of lysing bacteria, represent a promising alternative for treating infections caused by highly virulent K. pneumoniae and other antibiotic-resistant pathogens. In this study, we used K. pneumoniae 32b as the host bacterium and isolated the bacteriophage vB_KpiP_JZBo1. The optimal MOI of this bacteriophage is 0.01. And phage exhibited high activity across a wide range of temperatures (20°C - 50°C) and pH (4 - 11) following 1 h of incubation. Whole genome analysis revealed that the bacteriophage was a double-stranded DNA virus, encoding a total of 91 open reading frames (ORFs). Notably, genetic evolutionary analysis and BLASTN results indicated that phage vB_KpiP_JZBo1 shares the closest evolutionary relationship with K. pneumoniae phage KP8. However, genome-wide comparison revealed that they only exhibit 88% coverage and 93.03% nucleotide homology. This suggests that phage vB_KpiP_JZBo1 may be a novel species of phage. No genes associated with antibiotic resistance, virulence factors, and tRNA were found in the phage genome, and it belongs to Kaypoctavirus genus of the Schitoviridae family. Additionally, higher phage doses resulted in greater inhibitory and bactericidal effects against K. pneumoniae in LB medium. In model of G. mellonella, bacteriophage vB_KpiP_JZBo1 can effectively eliminate the infection of K. pneumoniae 32b and increase the survival rate of G. mellonella. These findings suggest that the bacteriophage vB_KpiP_JZBo1 has potential for the treatment and prevention of K. pneumoniae, and they also provide a theoretical basis for clinical applications.

articles.title: The Dual Role of Neutrophils in Paracoccidioidomycosis: Fungal Clearance and Immunopathology.
articles.abstract: Paracoccidioidomycosis (PCM) is a systemic endemic mycosis caused by fungi of the genus Paracoccidioides spp., and is particularly relevant in South American countries, especially Brazil. Infection occurs through the inhalation of conidia from Paracoccidioides brasiliensis or Paracoccidioides lutzii. The invasion process begins with fungal adhesion to the host epithelium, followed by endocytosis. At this stage, the first line of defense involves the recruitment of neutrophils to the site of infection, initiating the immune response against the fungus. Neutrophils play a crucial role in host defense against Paracoccidioides spp. by contributing to the development of an effective immune response through multiple antimicrobial mechanisms, including phagocytosis, degranulation, production of oxygen- and nitrogen-derived antifungal metabolites, and the formation of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs). These mechanisms are activated because of the dynamic interaction between the pathogen and the host immune system. Studies have shown that patients with severe PCM often exhibit impaired neutrophil function, highlighting the importance of these cells in disease progression and making them a key focus of current research. In addition, Paracoccidioides spp. antigens stimulate a complex and multifactorial immune response that activates both innate and adaptive immunity. This review aims to discuss how neutrophils actively contribute to the elimination of Paracoccidioides spp., while also directing the adaptive immune response toward a protective pattern. A better understanding of these processes may support immunomodulatory strategies, helping to clarify the mechanisms underlying severe disease progression and treatment failure.

articles.title: Early identification of the risk of foot ulcers in patients with diabetes based on CT multi-radiomics nomogram.
articles.journal: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To develop CT-based multi-radiomic signatures for the early identification of diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) risk.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 190 patients with diabetes who underwent lower-extremity CT angiography (CTA) were retrospectively included. Lower-limb vessels were segmented using the general CT image segmentation (gCIS) model, and radiomic features were extracted from axial lower-limb CTA images. Minimum redundancy maximum relevance (mRMR) and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression were applied for feature selection, and a Rad-score was computed to build a radiomics model. A radiomics nomogram integrating the Rad-score with clinical characteristics was constructed using multivariate logistic regression. Model value was evaluated with receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis.

RESULTS: Twelve radiomic features were retained after selection. The radiomics nomogram, which combined clinical factors with the Rad-score, achieved area-under-the-curve (AUC) values of 0.971 (95% CI: 0.946-0.997) in the training set and 0.887 (95% CI:0.842-0.932) in the testing set, exceeding those of the standalone radiomics model (training: 0.875, 95% CI 0.819-0.931; testing: 0.854, 95% CI 0.731-0.977). ROC and decision curve analyses indicated that the radiomics nomogram had greater reliability than the standalone radiomics model.

CONCLUSION: In summary, the lower-limb arterial vessel-based radiomics nomogram facilitates early DFU risk identification, offering a precise, objective, and easily interpretable method for predicting DFU at an early stage.

articles.title: Salivary biosensors for peptide and protein biomarkers in oral diseases: an analytical framework and narrative review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This narrative review examines current approaches to salivary biosensing for peptide and protein biomarker detection in oral diseases and develops an analytical framework explaining why the strategies used in this field differ in their constraints on clinical translation.

DATA SOURCES: Medline (PubMed), Scopus and Web of Science were searched between April and June 2026, combining the terms saliva, biosensor, peptide, protein and oral disease, complemented by manual screening of reference lists. Screening was performed independently by two authors.

STUDY SELECTION: English-language studies reporting biosensor development or application in salivary matrices between 2005 and 2025 were prioritized. The literature was organized into four domains: protein-targeted biosensing, peptide-responsive systems, peptide-enabled recognition, and direct detection of endogenous salivary peptides. For every study we extracted the validation matrix, clinical sample size, reference standard and diagnostic metrics.

CONCLUSIONS: The four domains differ in what is physically measured, and this difference determines the dominant failure mode in whole saliva and the reference standard that validation requires. Protein-targeted platforms are the most mature because they alone combine a stable measurand, an established reference method and an accepted clinical case definition. Reported limits of detection already fall below clinically relevant concentrations, frequently below those of the commercial chairside active MMP-8 test, whereas reference standards and diagnostic metrics are unreported for most platforms.

CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: Progress towards chairside use depends less on analytical sensitivity than on fixed case definitions, validation in unprocessed patient saliva, routine reporting of confounders such as smoking, diabetes and recent periodontal therapy, and benchmarking against available point-of-care tests.

articles.title: Comment on "The Neovascular Ocular Hypertension Spectrum: A Novel Classification of Neovascular Glaucoma".
Intestinal parasites in Cuban children in 2023-2024: a nationwide survey with clinical and epidemiological data.
authors: prepared on behalf of the Cuban National Survey Project Group
articles.abstract: National surveys of intestinal parasitic infections (including colonizing commensals) have been conducted previously among the general population of Cuba in response to high prevalence of widespread morbidity. The last survey was conducted in 2009, and it was decided to update knowledge on the current prevalence, with focus on children. A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted from April 2023 to February 2024 in all provinces of Cuba, with 19,000 children (1-14 years of age) included in the study. A stool sample from each child was analyzed by standardized parasitology techniques and a questionnaire was used to collect clinical-epidemiological information. The overall prevalence of intestinal parasites (including colonizing commensals) was 30.5 % (95 % CI: 29.9-31.2). The most frequently detected intestinal parasites were Blastocystis spp. (13.6 %) and Giardia duodenalis (8.4 %). The prevalence of helminths was low overall, but some hotspots with higher prevalences were identified. Most children were asymptomatic, but infection with Blastocystis spp. and Giardia was associated with diarrhea. Eating unwashed vegetables, thumb sucking, fingernail biting, and walking barefoot were associated with a higher risk of being infected with intestinal parasites. Infections intestinal parasites (together with carriage of commensals) continue to have a moderate prevalence in children in Cuba, with Blastocystis spp. and G. duodenalis occurring most commonly some areas being hotspots for helminth infections. The ongoing (2026) political and economic situation in Cuba, with knock-on effects on water supply, sanitation, food security and access to health services, raise concerns that the burden of intestinal parasites in Cuban children may currently be in danger of increasing.

articles.title: MIF deficiency exacerbates Plasmodium berghei ANKA induced cerebral malaria, associated with enhanced intracerebral T lymphocyte infiltration.
articles.abstract: Cerebral malaria (CM) is the most severe and life-threatening neurological complication of Plasmodium falciparum infection, responsible for substantial mortality and long-term neurological sequelae in patients from endemic settings. Macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF), a pleiotropic immunomodulatory molecule, regulates lymphocyte responses in diverse infectious and inflammatory diseases. However, whether and how endogenous MIF modulates the progression of CM remains unclear. In this study, Plasmodium berghei ANKA (PbA) infected red blood cells were intraperitoneally inoculated into wild-type (WT+PbA) and MIF-knockout (KO+PbA) C57BL/6 mice to establish the experimental cerebral malaria (ECM) model. The roles of MIF in regulating ECM pathological progression were observed. To preliminarily explore the underlying mechanisms, splenic lymphocytes were detected by flow cytometry, intracerebral lymphocyte infiltration was evaluated via immunohistochemistry, and semi-quantitative brain injury scores were analyzed based on hematoxylin-eosin staining. The results showed that KO+PbA mice exhibited a significantly reduced proportion of splenic CD8⁺ T cells compared with the WT+PbA mice. And PbA infection also significantly reduced splenic CD8⁺ T-cell numbers in MIF KO mice but not in WT mice. Meanwhile, a trend toward enhanced cerebral infiltration of CD3⁺ T cells (used as a surrogate marker for infiltrating CD8⁺ T lymphocytes), more severe cerebral microvascular injury and increased haemorrhages were observed in KO+PbA mice, which finally showed a trend toward exacerbated ECM symptoms and significantly shortened survival time. The observation here, together with previous data on markedly aggravated blood-brain barrier breakdown observed in PbA-infected MIF-knockout mice from our previous study, suggest that MIF deficiency exacerbates ECM-associated cerebral injury and accelerates mortality, potentially associated with the enhanced intracerebral T cell infiltration, and even possibly a redistribution of CD8⁺ T cells between the spleen and the brain. These findings suggest a potential role for host MIF in ECM and provide a basis for future studies aimed at clarifying its precise function in cerebral malaria.

articles.title: Strain-specific temporal dynamics of fecal parasite persistence between fluorescently tagged Ninoa and Y strains of Trypanosoma cruzi during dual infections in Triatoma pallidipennis.
articles.abstract: Trypanosoma cruzi, the causative agent of Chagas disease, exhibits substantial genetic diversity across Discrete Typing Units (DTUs), and phenotypic heterogeneity is well documented even among strains within the same DTU. While coinfections with multiple T. cruzi strains are commonly reported in nature, their temporal dynamics within the insect vector remain poorly understood. This study evaluated strain-specific persistence during dual infections in Triatoma pallidipennis using two fluorescently tagged T. cruzi strains, Y-DsRed and Ninoa-eGFP. Fecal parasite loads were quantified per insect at 30 and 50 days post-infection by fluorescence microscopy. At 30 days post-infection, Ninoa strains showed higher fecal parasite loads than Y strains only in single-strain infections (p.adj < 0.01), and no difference was detected between Ninoa-eGFP and Y-DsRed within the coinfection group. By 50 days post-infection, however, Ninoa-eGFP burden significantly surpassed Y-DsRed in both single and dual infections (p.adj < 0.05-0.0001), indicating progressive consolidation of this fecal persistence advantage rather than its immediate establishment. In vitro epimastigote doubling times did not differ between strains (p = 0.446), pointing away from a higher intrinsic replication rate as the basis for this advantage. Both strains remained detectable in dual-infected vectors throughout, indicating partial coexistence rather than complete competitive exclusion. These findings demonstrate time-dependent, strain-specific T. cruzi interactions within the vector, with Ninoa ultimately outperforming Y in fecal persistence. Fluorescent tagging enabled precise quantification of strain-specific dynamics without altering parasite fitness, providing a robust model for studying polyparasitism and T. cruzi transmission ecology.

articles.title: Reprogramming the tumor microbiome: Opportunities for cancer prevention, diagnosis, and precision therapy.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Reviews on cancer
articles.abstract: Microbiota-cancer interactions operate across distinct anatomical compartments, including the gut microbiota, the distal gut-tumor axis, and intratumoral microbiota residing within tumor tissues. These microbial communities and their metabolites can influence carcinogenesis, tumor progression, immune surveillance, and therapeutic responses through inflammation, genotoxicity, metabolic remodeling, epithelial and tumor-barrier dysfunction, and immune regulation. However, the magnitude and direction of these effects are highly context dependent, varying with cancer type, tumor site, microbial composition, host factors, treatment exposure, and methodological approaches. Importantly, associations between microbial signatures and clinical outcomes do not necessarily establish causality, and findings from gut microbiome studies should not be extrapolated directly to local intratumoral communities. This review critically synthesizes current evidence linking gut and intratumoral microbiota to tumor biology and treatment response, distinguishing compartment-specific mechanisms and evaluating the strength and limitations of available evidence. We examine how microbial metabolites, microbe-host interactions, and microbiota-driven immune and metabolic pathways shape the tumor microenvironment and may modify responses to immunotherapy, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and targeted therapies. We further assess multi-omics and spatial approaches for resolving microbial heterogeneity and identifying clinically relevant biomarkers, alongside emerging microbiome-directed interventions, including probiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation, engineered microorganisms, and nanotechnology-based strategies. Particular emphasis is placed on discrepancies between preclinical and clinical findings, causal inference, reproducibility, interindividual variability, contamination and sampling challenges, and the barriers to clinical translation. Collectively, the evidence supports a context-specific role for microbiota in cancer biology while underscoring the need for standardized methodologies, longitudinal and mechanistic studies, and well-controlled clinical trials before microbiome-based strategies can be reliably incorporated into precision oncology.

articles.title: Lipoprotein(a) and an aggressive coronary disease phenotype: Association with multivessel disease and recurrent coronary events in the CERES study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established genetically determined risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Whether elevated Lp(a) identifies a broader phenotype of aggressive coronary disease, integrating anatomical disease burden and recurrent clinical manifestations, remains incompletely characterised.

METHODS: We analysed 1892 patients with coronary artery disease from the multicentre CERES cohort after exclusion of myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA). Lp(a) was analysed continuously, after natural-log transformation, and categorically using >50 mg/dL. Multivariable logistic regression models were adjusted for age, sex, hypertension, diabetes, smoking, and historical maximum LDL cholesterol (LDL-C).

RESULTS: Lp(a) was available in 1833 patients; median concentration was 24.7 [9.1-63.7] mg/dL, and 33.2% had Lp(a) >50 mg/dL. Multivessel disease was present in 50.4% and recurrent coronary events in 19.5%. Lp(a) was independently associated with multivessel disease (OR, 1.004; 95% CI, 1.001-1.006; p = 0.002) and recurrent coronary events (OR, 1.004; 95% CI, 1.001-1.006; p = 0.003). Lp(a) >50 mg/dL was associated with multivessel disease (OR, 1.406; 95% CI, 1.144-1.730; p = 0.001) and recurrent events (OR, 1.504; 95% CI, 1.166-1.942; p = 0.002).

CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) was independently associated with greater anatomical coronary disease burden and recurrent coronary events, supporting its role as a marker of an aggressive coronary disease phenotype.

articles.title: Distinct soft plaque morphology on coronary computed tomography angiography in non-culprit lesions among patients with acute coronary syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major adverse cardiovascular events arising from non-culprit lesions (NCLs) remain relevant in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS), highlighting the need for more effective identification of vulnerable plaques. Although several coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived high-risk features are recognized as markers of plaque vulnerability, the significance of soft plaque morphology remains unclear. This study investigated whether ACS is associated with soft plaque morphology in NCLs on CCTA.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Overall, 174 NCLs from 69 patients with ACS or chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) who underwent CCTA within 1 month of percutaneous coronary intervention were analyzed. Soft plaques were classified according to the presence or absence of focal soft plaque thickening (FSPT), defined as localized thickening of the soft plaque component measuring ≥500 μm in at least one cross-sectional slice. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) was co-registered with CCTA in 49 lesions. The soft plaque burden did not differ significantly between NCLs in patients with ACS and CCS, whereas FSPT was more frequently observed in NCLs in patients with ACS (56.4% vs. 18.8%; p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis accounting for within-patient clustering, ACS was independently associated with FSPT (odds ratio, 6.09; 95% confidence interval, 2.72-13.60; p < 0.001). On co-registered IVUS, lesions with FSPT showed larger attenuation arcs and more frequent superficial attenuation.

CONCLUSIONS: ACS was independently associated with CCTA-derived FSPT in NCLs. These exploratory findings suggest that morphological assessment of soft plaques on CCTA may provide complementary information for the characterization of NCLs. Further validation in independent cohorts is warranted.

articles.title: Early and six-month ventricular remodeling after aortic valve surgery for aortic regurgitation: Predictive value of preoperative static exercise cardiovascular magnetic resonance: A prospective pilot study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Little is known about the timing and trajectory of reverse remodeling after aortic valve surgery (AVS) in severe aortic regurgitation (AR), and better predictors of postoperative ventricular function are needed. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) with static exercise (SE) testing may help anticipate the ventricular response to AVS, but its predictive value has not been established.

METHODS: In this prospective pilot study, 20 patients with severe AR referred for AVS underwent CMR, including assessment during SE, with follow-up CMR at 14 days and 6 months. Repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) characterized the time course of each parameter, decomposing the time effect into linear and quadratic components.

RESULTS: Left ventricular (LV) end-diastolic volume decreased progressively, mainly following a linear pattern (η2 0.795), with most of the reduction by 14 days. LV end-systolic volume declined continuously through 6 months (linear component only, η2 0.711). LV ejection fraction (LVEF) described a V-shaped curve, falling at 14 days before recovering above baseline by 6 months (quadratic component predominant, η2 0.358). Right ventricular parameters remained stable. SE-induced changes mirrored the early postoperative response and correlated strongly with 14-day LVEF (r up to 0.87), with good agreement between SE-LVEF and 14-day LVEF (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] 0.76-0.86); no baseline or SE parameter predicted LVEF at 6 months.

CONCLUSIONS: AVS for severe AR induces early, heterogeneous LV reverse remodeling, with an initial LVEF dip followed by recovery by 6 months. Preoperative CMR with SE reproduces the early postoperative hemodynamic response and predicts short-term but not mid-term ventricular recovery.

articles.title: Comparison of Euglycemic Ketoacidosis Associated with SGLT2 Inhibitors in Patients with and Without Diabetes: A Real-World Analysis.
articles.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) are associated with euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis (eDKA) in patients with diabetes (DM), but the risk of euglycemic ketoacidosis (eKA) in patients without diabetes (NDM) remains uncertain. We aimed to compare the incidence and clinical characteristics of eKA between patients with and without diabetes receiving SGLT2i therapy.

METHODS: Retrospective chart review of all hospital admissions (N=249,517 representing 183,835 unique individuals) across 28 hospitals in a large health system over one year. Cases meeting criteria for eKA as per American Diabetes Association criteria while taking an SGLT2i were reviewed to compare DM and NDM patients.

RESULTS: Among 894 admissions with eKA, 59 (6.6%) were receiving SGLT2i therapy: 55 patients with diabetes (DM) and 4 patients without diabetes (NDM). NDM patients had nonsignificant trend to higher median serum bicarbonate 18.5 vs 16 mmol/L (p=0.088), and lower anion gap 16 vs 21 mEq/L (p=0.093) but significantly higher nadir bicarbonate at 48 hours of 18.5 vs 14.0 mmol/L (p=0.004). EKA was unrecognized in all NDM patients compared to 55% of DM patients (p=0.045). Based on outpatient prescriptions, the estimated annual incidence of eKA associated with hospitalization was 0.36% in DM and 0.11% in NDM SGLT2i users.

CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2i-associated eKA appears quite rare in NDM patients and eKA while on SGLT2i, whether in DM or NDM, represents a small fraction of all eKA admissions. NDM cases of SGLT2i-associated eKA may be less severe than in patients with DM, though a larger group of patients is needed to confirm this observation.

articles.title: Atypical Prenatal Sonographic Findings in RAF1-Related Noonan Syndrome: A Case Report Without Cardiac Involvement.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe an atypical prenatal presentation of RAF1-related Noonan syndrome (NS) without detectable cardiac abnormalities and to highlight sonographic features that may prompt early genetic evaluation.

CASE REPORT: We report a fetus with a de novo pathogenic RAF1 variant (c.770C>T, p.Ser257Leu) identified by exome sequencing following normal karyotype and chromosomal microarray analysis. Prenatal imaging demonstrated persistent increased nuchal translucency and nuchal fold thickness, marked polyhydramnios, disproportionate growth with enlarged head and abdominal circumferences but normal femur length, and abnormal thickening of the thigh soft tissue. Mild central nervous system findings were also noted. Serial fetal echocardiography revealed no structural or functional cardiac abnormalities.

CONCLUSION: This case suggests that detectable prenatal cardiac abnormalities may be absent in RAF1-related NS, even in the presence of a pathogenic RAF1 variant. Disproportionate growth and abnormal soft tissue distribution may represent potential prenatal clues to RAF1-related NS. When conventional chromosomal testing is unrevealing, RASopathies may be considered in the differential diagnosis, and ES may facilitate molecular diagnosis.

articles.title: Very low gradient aortic stenosis: the black sheep of TAVI, but do these patients still benefit?
Transcarotid Artery Stenting Using Flow Reversal for Non-Atherosclerotic Carotid Artery Disease.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We evaluated the use of transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) in non-atherosclerotic carotid disease and compared outcomes with transfemoral carotid artery stenting (TFCAS).

METHODS: The Vascular Quality Initiative registry was queried for all TCAR and TFCAS procedures performed from 2017-2024. Patients with lesion types categorized as atherosclerosis or restenosis were excluded. The study cohort included dissection, trauma, fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD), and other non-atherosclerotic etiologies. Primary outcomes included major adverse events, including stroke, death, and composite endpoints. Propensity score matching was performed to adjust for baseline differences.

RESULTS: A total of 541 TCAR and 2,348 TFCAS patients met inclusion criteria. TCAR was associated with lower contrast usage and fluoroscopy time across all lesion types. In unadjusted analyses, stroke or death rates were higher with TFCAS than TCAR for dissection (7.1% vs 1.9%, p=0.006), other lesions (8.7% vs 2.1%, p<0.001), and symptomatic (8.1% vs 2.2%, p=0.001) and asymptomatic patients (6.4% vs 1.6%, p<0.001). After propensity matching (527 pairs), TCAR was associated with significantly lower rates of stroke (4.4% vs 1.7%, p=0.0118), death (4.4% vs 0.4%, p<0.001), stroke or death (7.6% vs 1.9%, p<0.001), and stroke, death, or MI (8.0% vs 2.7%, p<0.001) compared with TFCAS (TFCAS vs TCAR, respectively).

CONCLUSIONS: This study supports consideration of TCAR for non-atherosclerotic carotid pathology when carotid stenting is indicated and suggests that TCAR may offer important advantages over TFCAS, particularly in reducing the risk of perioperative stroke or death.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal infection dynamics and ultrastructural pathological characteristics of Lecanicillium lecanii infecting Plutella xylostella.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lecanicillium lecanii is a promising biocontrol agent against insect pests, yet its precise pathogenic mechanisms and infection dynamics in Plutella xylostella remain unclear.

RESULTS: We evaluated the lethal and sublethal effects of L. lecanii JMC-01 on second-instar P. xylostella larvae. At a concentration of 1 × 108 conidia/mL, the pathogen exhibited substantial virulence, resulting in 84.4% mortality by 144.0 h. Concurrently, optical and electron microscopy delineated its complete spatiotemporal infection dynamics. Linear mixed-effects modeling (LMM) further confirmed that the pathogen significantly suppressed larval growth in a strictly dose dependent manner, reducing larval weight by 46.4% relative to the control group at 96.0 h. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) revealed pronounced conidial thigmotropism, with significantly enhanced penetration peg elongation on protuberant cuticular regions compared with smooth cuticular surfaces. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) further demonstrated that penetration peg-like structures induced localized cuticular melanization during host invasion. After breaching the integument, the fungus proliferated in the hemocoel as blastospores and subsequently underwent a dimorphic transition. Progressive tissue degradation and structural collapse were observed during late-stage infection. Following host death, dense external mycelia emerged from the cadaver surface and produced abundant secondary conidia, thereby completing the infection cycle.

CONCLUSION: This study systematically elucidates the pathogenic process and ultrastructural infection characteristics of L. lecanii in P. xylostella, providing a theoretical basis for the application of this fungus in integrated pest management (IPM).

articles.title: Beyond Risk Scores: Concordance of a Multidisciplinary Decision Support Instrument with Real Life Treatment Decisions for Patients with Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.
articles.journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Treatment decisions for patients with ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA) are ethically complex and must be made under time pressure. This prospective observational study assessed how a previously developed decision support instrument (DSI) for rAAA aligns with real life treatment decisions and determined a reference threshold for interpreting its output. The DSI estimates the proportion of experts from the original multidisciplinary expert panel who would be expected to favour operative treatment (OT) for a given patient profile.

METHODS: Consecutive rAAA patients were included between March 2024 and January 2026 from two Dutch hospitals. Treating vascular surgeons completed the DSI after the actual treatment decision (OT or palliative care). DSI outputs were analysed in relation to observed treatment decisions. A threshold sweep analysis was performed to identify a contextual reference threshold reflecting the level of DSI estimated expert support at which OT was generally pursued. Post-operative outcomes were assessed in OT patients for clinical context.

RESULTS: Fifty patients were included; OT was chosen in 43 patients (86%). DSI estimated expert support was higher for patients receiving OT compared with palliative care (median 98% [interquartile range 97, 99%] vs. 83% [59, 89%]; p < .001). The contextual reference threshold was 93%, with concordance of 94% (95% confidence interval 83.8 - 97.9%). Case analysis highlighted challenges in capturing unresponsiveness due to profound hypovolaemic shock and assessing cardiac burden acutely Among patients surviving OT, relatively high health related quality of life was observed.

CONCLUSIONS: The DSI shows concordance with real life treatment decisions for rAAA. A contextual reference threshold above which operative treatment was generally pursued could be empirically derived. Although refinement is needed to better identify certain high risk patients, these findings represent an important first step in the validation pathway and provide proof of concept for behavioural artificial intelligence technology methodology.

articles.title: A New Dedicated Platform in the Treatment of Iliac and Femoropopliteal Lesions via Transradial Access.
articles.journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The results of a clinical study with a new dedicated platform comprising a guiding sheath, balloon catheter, and stent delivery system designed for transradial access for lower limb transluminal angioplasty are reported.

METHODS: The RADIANCY trial is a European, multicentre, prospective, single arm study evaluating the RADIANZ Vascular Stent System (Cordis) in patients with symptomatic iliac or femoropopliteal disease. The primary safety endpoint was major radial access complications through discharge. The primary efficacy endpoint was technical success of the index procedure. Using the Clopper-Pearson method, a cohort of 129 patients provided 88% power to show technical success > 93% and complication rate < 7%. After a roll in phase, safety and efficacy were assessed in the main cohort. Adverse events were adjudicated by an independent clinical events committee.

RESULTS: Across 12 European centres, 151 patients were enrolled, including 22 roll in patients and 129 in the main cohort. Patients were aged 68.2 ± 9.4 years, 26.4% were women, and their Rutherford classification score was 2.78 ± 0.74. Multiple vessel segments were treated, mainly in the common iliac and superficial femoral arteries. Through discharge, there were no major radial access site complications (0%, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.30%), and the technical success in patients receiving the study stent system was 99.2% (95% CI 96.20%). Thus, the primary safety and efficacy endpoints were achieved. The thirty day peri-procedural adverse event rate was 18.6% (24 of 129), with transradial access site haematoma (n = 10) being the most common. Four (3.1%) serious device or procedure related adverse events through thirty days were reported, including one ischaemic stroke that recovered (0.8%), one superficial femoral artery dissection (0.8%) ultimately requiring index limb amputation (0.8%), and one grade II haematoma (0.8%). Patient discharge within twenty-four hours was 76.0% (98 of 129).

CONCLUSION: This new dedicated platform for transradial access in lower limb interventions met its primary safety and efficacy endpoints in this first clinical evaluation.

articles.title: Safety and Effectiveness of the GORE VIABAHN FORTEGRA Venous Stent for the Treatment of Symptomatic Inferior Vena Cava Obstruction With or Without Combined Iliofemoral Obstruction.
authors: GORE VIABAHN FORTEGRA Venous Stent IVC Study Investigators
articles.journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This prospective, non-randomised, clinical investigational trial investigated the safety and effectiveness of the GORE VIABAHN FORTEGRA Venous Stent for treatment of symptomatic inferior vena cava obstruction, with or without combined iliofemoral obstruction.

METHODS: Subjects were enrolled at 17 sites across the USA, Europe, Australia, and New Zealand. The primary endpoint was a composite measure including primary patency and freedom from stent embolisation at 12 months, and 30 day freedom from pulmonary embolism and device or procedure related death, major bleeding, and vascular injury requiring surgical or endovascular intervention. The hypothesis driven secondary endpoint was change in revised venous clinical severity score (rVCSS) pain score from baseline to 12 months.

RESULTS: Eighty nine subjects were treated with an investigational iliocaval venous stent. Fifty nine (75%) of 79 evaluable subjects experienced freedom from a primary endpoint event, exceeding the performance goal of 58% at 12 months (90% confidence interval 66.6 - 82.7%) (p < .001). Of the 63 subjects reporting any pain at baseline, 51 (81%), saw an improvement in rVCSS pain score at 12 months, with a median difference of -2.0 (p < .001).

CONCLUSIONS: Endovascular treatment of symptomatic iliocaval obstruction with the purpose designed investigational venous stent is safe and effective. Results demonstrate robust primary patency rates, an acceptable safety profile, and reduced pain.

articles.title: Incidence and Risk Factors of Surgical Site Infections in Vascular Surgical Procedures in the Groin.
articles.journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Vascular procedures in the groin are common and carry a high risk of surgical site infection (SSI). Several risk factors have been established but others are less clear, not least due to the heterogeneity of studies. This study aimed to provide generalisable data on SSI and associated factors after open vascular procedures in the groin.

METHODS: This was a retrospective, dual centre cohort study including all patients undergoing open vascular surgery in the groin during a twelve year period at two centres. The primary endpoints were SSI rates at thirty and ninety days. Secondary endpoints were mortality at thirty days and 1 year.

RESULTS: After exclusion of 165 early peri-operative deaths (5.6%) from the original 2 968 patients, 2 803 were analysed of which 1 424 (50.8%) included a bypass and 1 130 (40.4%) an endarterectomy, while 570 patients (20.3%) underwent minor procedures. The incidence of SSI was 6.3% (176 of 2 803) at thirty days and 8.2% (170 of 2 087) at ninety days. Of these, 40.1% (n = 83) were superficial, 32.8% (n = 68) involved the fascial layer, and 27.1% (n = 56) involved the vessels. All cause mortality was 6.6% (197 of 2 968) at thirty days and 14.1% (418 of 2 968) at 1 year, the latter significantly associated with SSI at thirty days (hazard ratio 2.23, 95% confidence interval 1.32 - 3.75; p = .003). On multivariable regression analysis, higher body mass index (odds ratio [OR] 1.08; p < .001), previous percutaneous interventions on the index vessels (OR 1.47; p = .030), use of a bovine pericardium patch (OR 1.98; p = .007), and creation of a supra-inguinal bypass (OR 1.91; p = .008) were associated with increased odds of SSI. Furthermore, lymphatic complications were strongly associated with subsequent SSI on univariable analysis (OR 3.766; p < .001).

CONCLUSION: The odds of experiencing SSI depend on several patient and procedure related factors. Lymphatic complications were strongly associated with subsequent SSI. Therefore, future prospective studies should investigate whether strategies to reduce lymphatic complications also reduce SSIs.

articles.title: Comparative Effects of Neurostimulation- and Technology-Augmented Robot-Assisted Training on Upper-Limb Motor Recovery After Stroke: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Archives of physical medicine and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare robot-assisted training (RAT) alone with neurostimulation- or technology-augmented RAT for poststroke upper-limb recovery.

DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library, CNKI, and Wanfang were searched through August 1, 2026.

STUDY SELECTION: Randomized trials evaluated RAT alone or RAT combined with virtual reality, a brain-computer interface, low-frequency electrical stimulation (LFES), transcranial direct current stimulation, or repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS).

DATA EXTRACTION: Two reviewers independently selected studies and extracted data; risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed with Cochrane and GRADE methods.

DATA SYNTHESIS: Of 103 trials (5,251 participants), 84 (4,277 participants) entered restricted Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) Model E. Compared with usual care (UC), mean differences (MDs) were 9.56 points (95% CI, 7.18-11.93) for rTMS plus RAT, 7.52 (95% CI, 4.48-10.57) for LFES plus RAT, and 3.83 (95% CI, 2.69-4.97) for RAT alone. Heterogeneity was substantial (τ=2.79); global inconsistency was not detected (χ²(9)=3.64; P=.934). rTMS plus RAT ranked first (SUCRA, 96.2%), but its probability of being best decreased from 77.8% to 56.0% after predictive uncertainty was incorporated. Signals for stroke stage (P=.030) and total duration (P=.040) did not meet the multiplicity-adjusted threshold (P<.01).

CONCLUSIONS: rTMS plus RAT yielded the largest FMA-UE estimate, followed by LFES plus RAT. Sparse head-to-head evidence, heterogeneity, and very low-to-moderate certainty preclude a definitive hierarchy and warrant comparative trials.

articles.title: Sources, structure-activity relationships, and action mechanisms of anti-obesity polysaccharides: A review.
articles.abstract: The global obesity problem is continuing to worsen, which has led to an increase in the incidence of complications, including metabolic syndrome, type 2 diabetes, and cardiovascular diseases. Traditional obesity intervention methods (diet control and drug treatment) generally have problems, such as low long-term compliance, prominent side effects, and high treatment costs, which can not meet clinical needs. Polysaccharides, due to their rich sources, good safety, few side effects, and stable therapeutic effects, have become a research hotspot in the field of obesity intervention. Polysaccharides can inhibit obesity by regulating glucose and lipid metabolism, improving inflammation, and maintaining gut microbiota homeostasis. Unfortunately, the research on polysaccharides' role in inhibiting obesity has not yet fully elucidated their source diversity, structure-activity relationships, and action mechanisms. Hence, this review systematically introduces the sources (plants, animals, and microorganisms) of polysaccharides with anti-obesity effects. Subsequently, this article comprehensively reviews the structure-activity relationships of polysaccharides in anti-obesity from the perspectives of molecular weight, monosaccharide composition, glycosidic bond type, sulfation modification, etc. Finally, this article systematically reviews the mechanisms, challenges, and future directions of polysaccharides in anti-obesity. The results provide important references for the development of functional products and precise interventions in obesity.

articles.title: ADP-ribosylation modulated human paraoxonase 2 functions and its impact on cellular migration and infection.
articles.abstract: Oxidative stress plays a critical role in chronic wound healing and bacterial infections. Human paraoxonase 2 (PON2) contributes to host defense by hydrolyzing the quorum-sensing molecule N-(3-oxo)-dodecanoyl-homoserine lactone and by limiting oxidative damage, yet the mechanisms regulating these activities remain poorly understood. Here, we identify arginine 101 (R101) as the major ADP-ribosylation site of PON2 and show that this modification inhibits its lactonase activity. Functional analyses indicate that ARTC5, but not PARP1, is the main candidate for mediating PON2 ADP-ribosylation. Notably, R101 overlaps with a Furin cleavage motif, revealing a previously unrecognized regulatory hub where ADP-ribosylation and proteolytic processing converge. Our data suggest that ADP-ribosylation protects PON2 from furin-mediated cleavage while simultaneously modulating enzymatic activity and protein stability. Cell exclusion zone assays further demonstrate that PON2 activity influences both wound closure and the cellular response to Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection. Together, these findings uncover a novel oxidative stress-responsive mechanism linking ADP-ribosylation, proteolytic processing, and enzymatic activity to the regulation of PON2 function.

articles.title: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair for mitral valve regurgitation: insights from a 5-year prospective multicenter registry.
articles.abstract: Long-term data on transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) for significant mitral regurgitation (MR) remain limited. We aimed to evaluate long-term clinical outcomes and functional and echocardiographic findings during follow-up after MitraClip in a long-term subanalysis of the prospective multicenter GIOTTO registry. We included 406 consecutive patients undergoing MitraClip implantation for significant MR from 6 Italian centers contributing long-term follow-up. Baseline, procedural, in-hospital, and long-term follow-up data were compared according to MR etiology. Predictors of all-cause death were assessed using Cox regression analysis. Mean follow-up was 56.4±27.2 months. The cohort included 257 (63.3%) patients with functional or mixed MR and 149 (36.7%) with degenerative MR, who were older, more often female, and had smaller ventricles and higher LVEF, whereas functional or mixed MR patients had greater ischemic burden, conduction disease, prior revascularization, pacemaker implantation, and ventricular remodeling. During the overall observation period, crude all-cause death occurred in 161 patients (39.7%) and MVARC-style cardiovascular death in 98 (24.1%), without significant differences between groups. Mitral surgery, repeat TEER, endocarditis, and stroke occurred in 2.2%, 0.7%, 1.5%, and 3.5%, respectively. Among patients with available follow-up assessment, 77.5% were in NYHA class I/II. At the actual 5-year landmark echocardiographic assessment, 82.9% had none or mild MR and 97.1% had no more than moderate MR. Independent mortality predictors were older age, lower body mass index, right bundle branch block, MR etiology, larger LV end-systolic diameter, higher systolic pulmonary artery pressure, and longer index hospitalization (all p <0.05). In conclusion, in this prospective multicenter cohort, TEER with MitraClip in high-risk patients was associated with high procedural success and favorable long-term clinical and echocardiographic findings among patients with available follow-up. Mortality appeared to be associated with patient vulnerability, MR etiology, ventricular remodeling, pulmonary hypertension, and the early post-procedural course.

articles.title: PGRP-S2 contributes to Toll-1-dependent antiviral immunity and apoptosis-associated signaling during IAPV infection in honey bees.
articles.abstract: The Toll pathway mediates antimicrobial peptide (AMP) synthesis and participates in antiviral innate immunity in insects. However, how Toll-dependent antiviral responses are regulated during viral infection and how AMPs mediate antiviral defense remain incompletely understood. Here, we found that the Toll pathway constitutes an important part of the transcriptional response to Israeli acute paralysis virus (IAPV) infection in honey bees. PGRP-S2 was markedly up-regulated upon infection and exhibited physical associations with the IAPV capsid protein VP3 and with Toll-1, as validated by complementary co-immunoprecipitation, pull-down, and immunofluorescence analyses. Silencing PGRP-S2 substantially elevated viral titers and diminished the expression of Toll-dependent AMPs, including defensin 1. Functional assays indicated that defensin 1 was associated with apoptosis-related responses and suppressing viral replication. Knockdown of defensin 1 correlated with reduced apoptosis-associated signaling and enhanced viral titers, whereas overexpression of defensin 1 in Sf9 cells was associated with cell death. Collectively, our findings support a contribution of PGRP-S2 to the Toll-1-dependent antiviral response and link defensin 1 to apoptosis-related responses during IAPV infection, providing new insights into antiviral immunity in honey bees.

articles.title: Association between diabetes-related autoantibody positivity and renal impairment in clinically diagnosed type 2 diabetes: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate whether diabetes-related autoantibodies are independently associated with renal impairment in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).

METHODS: In this retrospective cross-sectional analysis, 2,010 Chinese patients with clinically diagnosed T2DM were included, and renal parameters (eGFR and UACR) were compared between autoantibody-positive (IAA/GADA/ICA/IA-2A) and autoantibody-negative groups. Multivariable logistic regression assessed independent associations with UACR ≥ 30 mg/g and eGFR < 90 mL/min/1.73 m2, adjusting for confounders. Stratified and interaction analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Autoantibody positivity was detected in 804 patients (40.00%), with IAA accounting for 75.25% of positive cases. After adjustment, autoantibody positivity remained independently associated with albuminuria (OR = 1.308, P = 0.007) and reduced eGFR (OR = 1.410, P = 0.003). Hypertension significantly modified the association with reduced eGFR (P for interaction = 0.009) but did not significantly modify the association with albuminuria (P for interaction = 0.054). Among normotensive patients, autoantibody positivity was associated with higher odds of albuminuria (OR = 1.514) and of reduced eGFR (OR = 1.935), while no significant associations were observed in hypertensive patients. Sex (P for interaction = 0.028) and HbA1c (P for interaction = 0.040) also modified the albuminuria association, with a stronger association in males. The full model including autoantibody status and fasting C-peptide yielded the highest AUC for reduced eGFR (0.786), although the incremental improvement over the conventional model was small (ΔAUC = +0.020).

CONCLUSION: Autoantibody positivity was independently associated with renal impairment in patients with clinically diagnosed T2DM, particularly in normotensive and male patients in exploratory subgroup analyses, suggesting that immuno-metabolic factors may be associated with diabetic kidney disease (DKD) beyond conventional clinical factors. However, the incremental discriminatory value of autoantibody status and fasting C-peptide was modest, and these findings require confirmation in future studies.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Mortality With Contributing Diabetes or Chronic Kidney Disease in Asian American Subgroups, 2018-2024: The SANGAM Study (South Asian aNd southeast asian Groups in AMerica).
articles.journal: The American journal of the medical sciences

articles.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Inverse Identification of α1-Adrenergic Receptor Non-Desensitization Mechanisms.
articles.abstract: This study investigates the aberrant activation and "non-desensitization" phenomenon of α1-adrenergic receptors (α1-AR) in hypertension. To systematically elucidate the mechanisms underlying receptor-mediated vascular smooth muscle contraction, a unified kinetic model was constructed, comprising a control group, an endocytic dysfunction group, a conformational change group, and a composite model integrating multiple regulatory processes. The model explicitly accounts for receptor binding, phosphorylation, endocytosis, and conformational transitions. Using rat vascular ring tension measurements, a quantitative mapping between model states and experimentally observed contractile responses was established. A physics-informed neural network (PINN) implementation combining a predefined linear warm-up schedule for the physics-loss weight with sequential Adam and L-BFGS optimization was employed to infer key kinetic parameters while balancing data fitting and kinetic constraints during training. Numerical comparisons based on fitting errors and AIC indicated that the composite model provided the most favorable balance between data agreement and model complexity among the candidate mechanisms. Analyses revealed that α1-AA sustains receptor activation and continuously amplifies downstream signaling by enhancing binding affinity, stabilizing the active conformation, and suppressing endocytosis, thereby promoting persistent vasoconstriction. These findings provide a quantitative explanation for the "non-desensitization" of α1-AR and demonstrates the practical utility of PINNs for parameter estimation and mechanistic analysis in complex biological systems.

articles.title: Reelin-enhanced neural stem cell therapy promotes neuroangiogenesis, remyelination, and functional recovery after subcortical capsular ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This study established a reproducible mouse model of posterior limb of the internal capsule (PLIC) ischemia to investigate whether Reelin potentiates neural stem cell (NSC)-mediated functional and structural recovery, addressing the limited regenerative strategies for subcortical stroke.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A deep photothrombotic PLIC stroke model was induced in mice using a fiber-optic laser system. Embryonic NSCs were isolated from E14 embryos and characterized by flow cytometry, showing >85% Nestin positivity. Reelin effects on NSC viability were evaluated by MTT assay. Seven days after stroke, mice received intracortical PBS, NSCs, Reelin, or NSCs plus Reelin. Recovery was assessed by modified Neurological Severity Score. Histological, immunofluorescence, immunohistochemical, ELISA, flow cytometric, and ultrastructural analyses examined inflammation, endogenous and grafted NSC responses, neurogenesis, angiogenesis, axonal repair, myelin preservation, and diaschisis.

KEY FINDINGS: The optimized model produced consistent focal PLIC infarcts with marked motor deficits. Reelin increased NSC viability in vitro in a dose-dependent manner up to 200 nM. In vivo, combined NSC + Reelin treatment reduced TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, while increasing IL-10 and TGF-β. It also promoted M2 microglial polarization, enhanced proliferation and neuronal differentiation of endogenous and transplanted NSCs, increased GAP-43-positive axonal regeneration and vWF-positive angiogenesis, preserved myelin integrity, and attenuated retrograde degeneration/diaschisis. These effects were accompanied by increased internal capsule volume and improved neurological function, together with histological and ultrastructural evidence of enhanced axonal integrity and myelin preservation.

SIGNIFICANCE: The combined strategy promotes recovery by coordinating neuroinflammatory resolution, extracellular matrix remodeling, neurogenesis, angiogenesis, axonal regeneration, and remyelination. These findings support Reelin-assisted NSC therapy as a promising combinatorial regenerative approach for subcortical ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Polygenic susceptibility modifies the association between long-term physical activity patterns and major adverse cardiovascular events: Insights from a target trial emulation study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Physical activity is a key modifiable lifestyle factor for cardiovascular prevention. However, precise prevention strategies regarding long-term physical activity are lacking, particularly concerning whether genetic susceptibility modifies the association between long-term physical activity and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Most previous cohort studies rely on a single assessment of physical activity, which may not capture long-term behavior. To address these gaps, we used repeated assessments and a target trial emulation framework in UK Biobank.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We studied 27,459 UK Biobank participants with repeat physical activity assessments. A target trial emulation framework defined eligibility, time zero, exposure groups, and follow-up. The prespecified primary contrast compared increased physical activity with sustained low activity after 1:1 propensity score matching. Secondary full-cohort models examined four physical activity change patterns. Cardiovascular polygenic risk strata were evaluated exploratorily.

KEY FINDINGS: In 4401 matched pairs, increased physical activity was not significantly associated with lower major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) compared with sustained low activity (HR 1.19, 95% CI 0.90-1.58). In full-cohort models, sustained high physical activity was associated with higher MACE risk (HR 1.27, 95% CI 1.03-1.56). This signal was more apparent among participants with intermediate or high cardiovascular polygenic risk.

SIGNIFICANCE: In this UK Biobank target trial emulation, increasing physical activity from low levels did not clearly reduce MACE, whereas sustained high activity showed an unexpected higher-risk signal, particularly among genetically susceptible participants. These findings support the potential value of genetic risk assessment in cardiovascular risk evaluation for highly active individuals and provide new evidence for precision exercise prescriptions.

articles.title: UBAP2L O-GlcNAcylation contributes to DDX21-associated stress granule formation and suppression of trophoblast pyroptosis in preeclampsia.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a severe pregnancy disorder characterized by hypertension and multi-organ dysfunction. Impaired trophoblast function and defective spiral artery remodeling are considered the central pathological features of PE, leading to placental ischemia/hypoxia and a subsequent inflammatory cascade. Increasing evidence has demonstrated that pyroptosis contributes to placental dysfunction and the establishment of a pro-inflammatory microenvironment in PE; however, the mechanisms remain largely unclear. O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) modification is a reversible post-translational modification (PTM) that plays critical roles in maintaining cellular homeostasis and regulating multiple forms of programmed cell death (PCD), yet its role in pyroptosis during PE has not been elucidated. In the present study, we found that O-GlcNAcylation was markedly reduced in placental tissues from patients with PE and negatively correlated with pyroptosis. In both an LPS-induced PE-like mouse model and trophoblast cells, enhancement of O-GlcNAcylation significantly suppressed pyroptosis and ameliorated PE-like phenotypes. IP-MS identified UBAP2L as a critical O-GlcNAcylated protein. Mechanistically, T446, an O-GlcNAcylation site of UBAP2L, contributed to maintaining its protein stability by preventing ubiquitin-mediated proteasomal degradation and promoted its interaction with DDX21, thereby promoting stress granule assembly. This process suppressed inflammasome activation and pyroptosis, improved trophoblast function, and ameliorated PE-like phenotypes. Collectively, our findings define an O-GlcNAcylation-UBAP2L-DDX21-stress granule-pyroptosis axis in PE and nominate O-GlcNAc signaling as a therapeutic target.

articles.title: Rising Prevalence of Metabolic Dysfunction - Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in an urban South Indian screening cohort: a Retrospective Cross-sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), redefined in 2023 from non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, is highly prevalent globally, but population-level data using 2023 AASLD criteria and FibroScan-based assessment remain scarce in South Asia, particularly among asymptomatic adults undergoing routine health screening.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study of 1,103 asymptomatic adults (mean age 43.1±12.7 years; 64.1% male) undergoing FibroScan-based Master Health Check-up at a tertiary centre in Chennai, India (2023-2025). MASLD was defined as controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) ≥249 dB/m plus ≥1 cardiometabolic risk factor; fibrosis was assessed by liver stiffness measurement (LSM).

RESULTS: MASLD was identified in 716 participants (64.9%; 95% CI 62.1-67.7%). Affected individuals were older, had higher BMI, and more frequently had diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidaemia (all p<0.01). In multivariable analysis, age, male sex, BMI, and diabetes were independently associated with MASLD. Notably, 53.4% of cases occurred in adults under 46 years, and 45.3% had normal liver function tests while 31.3% had normal ultrasound, indicating conventional screening substantially underestimates disease burden.

CONCLUSIONS: Nearly two-thirds of asymptomatic urban South Indian adults screened met MASLD criteria, predominantly working-age individuals under-detected by conventional tools. FibroScan-based screening should be considered in preventive health programmes to enable earlier detection.

articles.title: Mechanism Investigation of Platycodon grandiflorum Active Ingredients in Regulating Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition and Airway Remodeling in Asthma via Modulation of the Sirt6/RORγt/IL-17A Axis and IL-17A/MAPK Pathway.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Platycodon grandiflorum (Jacq.) A.DC. is a traditional Chinese medicinal herb recognized for its dual role as both food and medicine, renowned for its effects of diffusing the lung, alleviating sore throat, promoting expectoration, and facilitating pus drainage. In traditional medicinal practice, it is often used in combination with herbs such as Ephedra sinica , Prunus armeniaca and Glycyrrhiza uralensis utilized to mitigate symptoms associated with asthma, bronchitis, and other respiratory diseases. However, the therapeutic effects and molecular mechanisms of its principal bioactive components in treating asthma remain insufficiently characterized.

AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate the pharmacological effects and elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which triterpenoid saponins derived from Platycodon grandiflorum (PL-TS) inhibit airway epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and attenuate airway remodeling in asthma.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Initially, the chemical constituents of the triterpenoid saponin fraction extracted from Platycodon grandiflorum (Jacq.) A. DC. (PL-TS) were identified by Ultra Performance Liquid Chromatography Tandem Mass Spectrometry (UPLC-MS). Subsequently, network pharmacology approaches were employed to predict potential therapeutic targets and core signaling pathways of PL-TS in asthma. An OVA-induced asthmatic mouse model was established for in vivo experiments. Airway hyperresponsiveness (AHR) was assessed via whole-body plethysmography (WBP), and histopathological changes in lung tissues were examined via hematoxylin-eosin (HE), Masson's trichrome, and periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) staining. Human bronchial epithelial cells (BEAS-2B) were utilized to establish an IL-17A-induced epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) model in vitro. Finally, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), immunohistochemistry (IHC), quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR), and Western blotting (WB) were employed to investigate the modulatory effects of PL-TS on proteins associated with airway remodeling, the IL-17A/MAPK signaling pathway, and the Sirt6/RORγt/IL-17A axis in both asthmatic mice and cellular models.

RESULTS: UPLC-MS/MS analysis identified 38 triterpenoid saponins from PL-TS, providing a chemical foundation for subsequent mechanistic studies. Network pharmacology analysis revealed that the principal targets of PL-TS were predominantly enriched within the IL-17A signaling pathway. In OVA-induced asthmatic mice, PL-TS significantly attenuated inflammatory cell infiltration, mucus hypersecretion, and collagen deposition in lung tissues, while markedly reducing serum levels of IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, and OVA-IgE in vivo. Furthermore, PL-TS was found to inhibit the activation of the IL-17A/MAPK and Sirt6/RORγt/IL-17A signaling pathways in both mouse lung tissue and stimulated cells, while downregulating EMT-related protein Vimentin, Snail, and N-cadherin, upregulating expression of E-cadherin. suppressing the phosphorylation of p38, ERK, and JNK in the MAPK pathway. In addition, PL-TS downregulated Sirt6 expression and reduced RORγt and IL-17A levels, suggesting a potential involvement of the Sirt6/RORγt/IL-17A regulatory axis, although the precise epigenetic mechanism requires further investigation.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrated that the PL-TS significantly alleviated airway inflammation, mucus hypersecretion, and airway remodeling in asthma model. The effects were associated with suppression of the IL-17A/MAPK pathway and downregulation of the Sirt6/RORγt/IL-17A axis, suggesting a potential dual mechanism that highlight its therapeutic potential.

articles.title: Medicinal Plants and Fungi of the Sikkim Himalaya for Hypertension and Cardiovascular Disorders: Ethnopharmacology, Mechanisms, and Cardiovascular Relevance.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are the leading cause of global mortality, driven by mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, and dysregulated cellular signaling. Despite extensive use of plant-based therapies for circulatory disorders, many ethnomedicinal claims lack molecular validation. In the biodiversity-rich Sikkim Himalaya, India, traditional medicinal plant use by Lepcha, Bhutia, and Nepali communities remains unsystematically integrated with cardiovascular evidence, with limited classification into three evidence tiers: Tier I (mechanistically validated), Tier II (mechanistically suggestive), and Tier III (pharmacologically divergent).

AIM OF THE STUDY: To critically assess the extent to which the traditional cardiovascular uses of medicinal plants and fungi from the Sikkim Himalaya, India, are supported by experimental pharmacological and molecular evidence, and to classify the available evidence according to its mechanistic strength.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A PRISMA 2020-guided narrative review was conducted to identify, screen, and report the available literature using predefined procedures. The retrieved evidence was synthesized qualitatively to integrate ethnopharmacological, pharmacological, phytochemical, and molecular mechanistic findings. Literature from Jan 1950 to March 2026 was retrieved from PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar. Studies were screened using predefined inclusion criteria focusing on Sikkim-based ethnomedicinal use and cardiovascular indications. Data were extracted on species identity, traditional use, phytochemistry, and molecular mechanisms, followed by qualitative synthesis.

RESULTS: Fifteen medicinal plant and fungal taxa were identified. Five taxa, including Rhododendron arboreum Sm., Centella asiatica (L.) Urb., Nardostachys jatamansi (D.Don) DC., Oroxylum indicum (L.) Kurz, and Ophiocordyceps sinensis (Berk.) G.H.Sung, J.M.Sung, Hywel-Jones & Spatafora, demonstrated cardioprotective effects in myocardial injury models via modulation of mitochondrial stability, inflammatory signaling, and PI3K/Akt and AMPK pathways. Evidence was stratified into three tiers: Tier I, mechanistically validated; Tier II, mechanistically suggestive; and Tier III, pharmacologically divergent.

CONCLUSIONS: Stress-adaptive Himalayan phytochemistry converges with conserved cardiovascular signaling pathways, supporting their potential as candidates for further preclinical cardiovascular investigation. However, integration of metabolomics, pharmacokinetics, disease-relevant models, and clinical studies is required to establish therapeutic efficacy and enable clinical translation.

articles.title: Mosquito fertility is (mostly) resilient to sublethal heat shocks.
articles.abstract: Insects can experience a loss of fertility under acute heat stress, but impacts vary among species and depend on life stage and sex. We examined the effects of sublethal heat shocks on the fertility of three mosquito species (Aedes aegypti, Aedes notoscriptus and Culex quinquefasciatus) when males or females were exposed at the pupal and adult stages.
