Reproductive performance was assessed through egg-laying success, fecundity, egg hatchability and viable offspring production. Female heat shock had limited effects on fertility in all three species, though exposure of adult females to 41 °C for 1 h reduced viable offspring production in Ae. notoscriptus. Male heat shock reduced egg hatchability in Cx. quinquefasciatus and viable offspring production in Ae. aegypti depending on the life stage exposed. We investigated several other aspects of heat shock exposure on Ae. aegypti fertility. In this species, male fertility partially recovered within 24-48 h following heat shock exposure, while effects of heat shocks on female fertility occurred regardless of whether heat exposure occurred pre- or post-mating. In addition, maternal heat shock exposure enhanced offspring fecundity and viable offspring production under subsequent sublethal heat stress. Overall, our findings demonstrate that mosquito fertility is largely robust to short-term heat shocks, but there are also complex trait, sex, stage, temporal and species-specific effects, with implications for predicting mosquito population persistence and species persistence under future climate extremes.

articles.title: Longitudinal remodeling of acylcarnitine signatures before and after arthroplasty for osteoarthritis: A 7-year cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Total joint arthroplasty (TJA) is the most effective treatment for end-stage osteoarthritis (OA). Although systemic acylcarnitine alterations have been reported in OA, long-term metabolic changes after TJA remain poorly understood. Existing metabolomic studies are cross-sectional and have not compared post-TJA changes with age- and sex-matched controls. We examined metabolic markers before and 7 years after TJA to assess long-term systemic metabolic changes relative to healthy aging controls.

METHOD: Fasting serum acylcarnitines were measured using liquid chromatography mass-spectrometry in a longitudinal cohort of participants with end-stage OA undergoing TJA (n = 70) and in age- and sex-matched healthy controls (n = 82) at baseline and 7-year follow-up. Acylcarnitine concentrations were compared between groups and longitudinally within participants, with analyses adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, hypertension status, and corrected for multiple comparisons.

RESULTS: A total of 70 patients (age 62 ± 7) with severe OA who were undergoing TJA and 82 matched controls without OA were included in the study. Forty-eight acylcarnitine measures and ratios passed quality control. Fifteen acylcarnitines changed differently between groups over follow-up; six measures differed at baseline and 12 at follow-up. Five baseline differences normalized, whereas 11 new between-group differences emerged. After adjustment for baseline metabolite concentrations, seven acylcarnitines showed differential longitudinal change: four short-chain species (C5-OH, C5-DC, C5-M-DC, C5:1-DC) and three long-chain species (C14:2-OH, C16:2, C18:1). The four short-chain species increased 19.8-32.0% more in the TJA group than in controls. Free carnitine (C0) declined relative to controls, with a 24.8% lower longitudinal change (ratio 0.75, 95% CI 0.62-0.91). Several medium- and long-chain acylcarnitines that were lower at baseline normalized toward control concentrations. Total acylcarnitine/free carnitine increased 32.3% more in the TJA group (ratio 1.32, 95% CI 1.17-1.50), with the baseline group difference resolving by follow-up.

CONCLUSION: TJA was associated with partial normalization of select circulating acylcarnitines; however, persistent abnormalities in hydroxy- and dicarboxy-acylcarnitines suggest ongoing alterations in lipid handling. Reduced carnitine buffering capacity and shifts toward alternative oxidation pathways further indicate incomplete restoration of systemic fatty-acid metabolism. Overall, these findings support pathway-specific metabolic remodeling rather than full metabolic normalization following TJA. REGISTERED ON WWW.

CLINICALTRIALS: GOV: NCT06211465.

articles.title: Pharmacological characterization of clinical candidate CORT118335 (miricorilant), a selective glucocorticoid receptor modulator, in short-term preclinical models for MASLD.
articles.abstract: CORT118335 (miricorilant) is a selective glucocorticoid receptor (GR) modulator (SGRM) that is currently being evaluated in clinical trials for the treatment of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), based on strong efficacy in mouse models. We reveal gene-specific GR modulation by CORT118335 in the mouse liver. In cell-based models, we evaluated the biological activity of CORT118335 metabolites. Metabolite CORT118335-P9a showed potent GR agonism, while metabolite CORT118335-P9b was largely inactive. CORT118335-P9a concentrations in the mouse liver were very low, and therefore neither metabolite is likely to contribute to the beneficial effects of CORT118335 in vivo. We investigated various aspects of CORT118335 activity in reducing lipid levels in the mouse liver using a model of short-term high-fat diet feeding. Daily administration of CORT118335 appeared to lower hepatic triglyceride rapidly within several days after treatment initiation, specifically in male mice, and these effects were reversed after 7 days of treatment discontinuation. No synergy was observed between the lipid-lowering effects of CORT118335 and the TRβ agonist VK2809 or the PPARγ agonist pioglitazone. At a dose of 6 mg/kg/day, CORT118335 induced evident transcriptional effects with modest lowering of hepatic triglyceride levels, while higher doses induced a more pronounced lipid lowering but less ongoing transcriptional activity for hepatic lipid metabolism genes. Altogether we substantiate the potential of selective GR modulation using CORT118335 as a lipid-lowering strategy in MASLD and highlight the complexity of SGRM-mediated hepatic lipid lowering.

articles.title: Born to have obesity: rodent experimental models to study childhood obesity.
articles.abstract: Childhood obesity is a complex and rapidly growing global health challenge, associated with early-onset metabolic disturbances and increased risk of cardiometabolic and endocrine disorders in later life. Its development reflects the interplay of genetic predisposition, early-life environmental exposures, dietary and physical activity patterns, and psychosocial influences. Compared to adults, children exhibit distinct patterns of fat distribution, hormonal regulation, and metabolic responses, highlighting the need for research approaches tailored to pediatric populations. Early-life metabolic programming, including epigenetic modifications and alterations in adipose tissue development, plays a central role in determining long-term susceptibility to obesity and related comorbidities, such as insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes (T2D), and cardiovascular disease. Translational animal models, particularly mice, provide essential tools to investigate these mechanisms under controlled conditions, offering advantages including genetic tractability, short lifespan, and conserved metabolic pathways. However, differences in physiology and environmental context limit the direct extrapolation to humans. This review critically compares genetic, dietary, and early-life overnutrition models according to developmental timing, experimental objectives, and translational limitations. Particular emphasis is placed on model-selection strategies for investigating metabolic programming, pediatric obesity-related complications, and therapeutic responses, with the aim of guiding the design of more reproducible and clinically relevant preclinical studies.

articles.title: Persistent indirect airway hyperresponsiveness after six weeks of high-dose inhaled corticosteroids identifies a subgroup with higher T2 inflammation and mast cell burden.
articles.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Indirect airway hyperresponsiveness (AHR) to osmotic stimuli such as mannitol is a hallmark of asthma and typically improves with inhaled corticosteroids (ICS), in contrast to direct AHR stimuli (e.g. methacholine), which often persists despite treatment. Persistent indirect AHR (PIAHR) after high-dose ICS may reflect incomplete suppression of airway inflammation.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to characterise clinical, inflammatory, and tissue features associated with persistent indirect AHR in patients with asthma before and after high-dose ICS treatment.

METHODS: This post-hoc analysis of the RECONSTRUCT study included corticosteroid-free patients with asthma and AHR to mannitol. Participants underwent examinations, including bronchoscopy, before and after six weeks of treatment with 1600 μg inhaled budesonide daily. Patients were stratified as responders (abolished AHR; PD15 ≥635 mg) or incomplete responders (persistent AHR; PD15 <635 mg).

RESULTS: After six weeks of ICS, 11/46 patients (24%) had PIAHR. At baseline, incomplete responders had more severe AHR and higher type 2 (T2) biomarker levels including FeNO, blood- and sputum eosinophils as well as a higher density of airway chymase-positive mast cells. Despite reductions in T2 markers in both groups, incomplete responders exhibited higher blood- and sputum eosinophils after six weeks treatment. Airway mast cell and eosinophil densities decreased similarly, but reductions in blood eosinophils were smaller in incomplete responders.

CONCLUSION: PIAHR after six weeks of high-dose ICS is associated with incomplete suppression of T2 inflammation and mast cell-associated features. This pattern may help identify patients in whom airway inflammation is incompletely controlled by ICS alone and who may benefit from closer follow-up or further targeted treatment.

articles.title: Beyond HIV prevention: Reframing PrEP clinics as hubs for viral hepatitis prevention and elimination.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The expansion of HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) has created a growing network of prevention services that regularly engage people who may also be exposed or susceptible to viral hepatitis. PrEP care is inherently longitudinal, involving repeated clinical assessment, laboratory testing, counselling and vaccination review. These features make PrEP clinics uniquely positioned to contribute to viral hepatitis prevention and elimination. In this narrative review, we synthesize evidence on the integration of viral hepatitis prevention, screening, diagnosis and care within PrEP services, and propose a practical framework, the PrEP-viral hepatitis elimination cascade, for translating the principle of integrated HIV, viral hepatitis and sexually transmitted infection services into routine clinical practice.

METHODS: A focused literature search was conducted between 1 May and 8 August 2026 across PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus and the WHO Global Index Medicus, using documented search strings supplemented by hand-searching of reference lists. We prioritized studies conducted among PrEP users or within PrEP programmes, together with relevant international guidelines and policy documents. Records were screened in two stages against predefined eligibility criteria, and the findings were mapped to the steps of the cascade. Evidence was sought on HAV and HBV vaccination coverage, HBV seroprevalence and susceptibility, the relationship between tenofovir-based PrEP and HBV prevention, HCV epidemiology among PrEP users, simplified diagnostic strategies and integrated service delivery models. Given the heterogeneity of study designs and outcomes, the literature was synthesized narratively rather than through formal meta-analysis. Interventions and indicators for each cascade step were then summarized in an evidence-linked implementation and monitoring table.

RESULTS: The evidence consistently demonstrates that vaccination gaps for HAV and HBV persist among PrEP users, with suboptimal initiation and completion rates across settings; that HBV susceptibility remains common among individuals entering PrEP care; and that tenofovir-based PrEP, while offering incidental HBV protection, should not substitute for vaccination. HCV epidemiology among PrEP users is heterogeneous, supporting risk-adapted testing strategies, while simplified diagnostic pathways and self-testing approaches have shown promise for HCV. The PrEP-viral hepatitis elimination cascade proposed here offers a structured, implementable framework connecting vaccination, case finding, linkage to care and longitudinal reassessment within the existing PrEP pathway. The cascade is presented as a detailed figure and as an implementation and monitoring table linking each step to supporting evidence, candidate interventions and measurable indicators, without assigning responsibilities to specific providers. Implementation challenges include variability in PrEP delivery models, the need for equity-oriented approaches and the implications of long-acting and tenofovir-sparing PrEP regimens for HBV prevention.

CONCLUSION: PrEP programmes have created a longitudinal prevention infrastructure that extends beyond HIV prevention. HAV vaccination, HBV screening and vaccination, identification of chronic HBV infection, HCV testing, simplified diagnostics, treatment linkage and surveillance for reinfection can all be incorporated at different points of the PrEP pathway. The next step is to move from opportunistic to intentional integration. PrEP clinics should be reframed as integrated viral hepatitis prevention and elimination hubs, translating global strategies into routine care and contributing to viral hepatitis elimination goals. The question is no longer whether PrEP clinics can contribute to viral hepatitis elimination, but whether the global health community will deliberately invest in making this integration a reality.

articles.title: Estimating the population-level non-respiratory burden of severe influenza: a systematic review of methods and estimates.
articles.abstract: Influenza is widely recognised as a respiratory infection, although the condition can also exacerbate or trigger serious non-respiratory outcomes that are often overlooked in burden assessments. Previous reviews have separately evaluated how methodological choices affect influenza-associated mortality and hospitalisation estimates and have covered non-respiratory outcomes in part, although these studies were restricted to select causes or severe outcomes, specific populations, or particular geographical settings. A more comprehensive synthesis focused specifically on severe non-respiratory influenza burden has been missing. To address this gap, we conducted a systematic review of 238 studies from 52 countries or regions examining both the burden of severe influenza beyond respiratory disease and the estimation methods used. We found that non-respiratory outcomes represent a substantial component of the total influenza burden, with a pronounced age gradient disproportionately affecting older adults (≥65 years). Cardiovascular events were particularly notable, contributing to more than 50 deaths and 60 hospitalisations per 100 000 older adults. Burden estimates also varied by analytical method, cause, and study period, and most evidence was concentrated in high-income settings, leaving important geographical gaps. Our findings highlight that influenza burden assessments and prevention strategies should extend beyond respiratory presentations, particularly for older populations, and emphasise upon the need for standardised methods and broader geographical coverage to generate estimates that are more comparable across studies and settings that better inform public health policy and resource allocation.

articles.title: Frailty as a determinant of mRNA vaccine efficacy.
articles.abstract: Frailty, an age-related state of increased vulnerability, is associated with greater susceptibility to infection and impaired vaccine response. In this Review, we examine how frailty-associated immunosenescence, including altered haematopoiesis, chronic inflammation, and dysfunction of innate and adaptive immune responses, can affect the immunogenicity, efficacy, and safety of lipid nanoparticle mRNA vaccines. Evidence from COVID-19 lipid nanoparticle mRNA vaccines and other vaccines suggests that people living with frailty can mount weaker or less durable responses than non-frail peers, although findings remain heterogeneous and frailty-specific evidence is scarce. The high customisability of lipid nanoparticle mRNA platforms creates opportunities for frailty-tailored vaccination. We discuss optimisation of lipid nanoparticle composition, targeting and dosing, mRNA cargo and combination-vaccine approaches, alongside host-directed measures addressing comorbidities, nutrition, and immune dysfunction. Integrating frailty into vaccine design, evaluation, and deployment could support safer, more effective, and more individualised vaccination strategies for older adults.

articles.title: Long-term outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stents versus coronary artery bypass grafting for left main coronary artery disease: a prospective analysis of the multicentre IRIS-MAIN registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with drug-eluting stents has been widely used to treat patients with left main coronary artery disease; however, long-term comparative outcomes versus coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in real-world populations remain poorly characterised. We aimed to compare long-term all-cause mortality after PCI or CABG in Asian patients with unprotected left main coronary artery disease.

METHODS: We analysed prospectively collected data from the multicentre IRIS-MAIN registry, conducted at 46 hospitals in South Korea, India, Japan, Indonesia, and Malaysia. The registry enrolled adults aged 18 years or older with unprotected left main coronary artery disease (defined as a stenosis diameter of ≥50% as visually estimated on angiography), who had been treated with PCI, CABG, or medical therapy alone. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. We used a target trial emulation framework to compare the long-term risk of all-cause mortality between PCI with drug-eluting stents and isolated CABG. We used propensity-score overlap weighting to adjust for measured baseline covariates. The IRIS-MAIN Registry study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01341327).

FINDINGS: Between Jan 1, 2003, and Dec 31, 2024, 6900 patients were enrolled in the IRIS-MAIN registry, of whom 5379 (78·0%) underwent coronary revascularisation through either PCI with drug-eluting stents (3836 [71·3%]) or CABG (1543 [28·7%]) and were included in the analysis. The median duration of follow-up for all patients was 10·0 years (IQR 5·0-16·7). In the overlap-weighted population, no statistically detectable difference in 10-year weighted Kaplan-Meier rates of all-cause mortality was observed between PCI and CABG (24·0% vs 22·9%; overlap-weighted hazard ratio 1·00 [95% CI 0·87-1·14]; p=0·99). The confidence interval does not exclude a mortality benefit or harm with either strategy.

INTERPRETATION: In this non-randomised registry analysis of patients with left main coronary artery disease, there was no statistically detectable difference in all-cause mortality between PCI and CABG. For patients considered suitable for either strategy, multidisciplinary Heart Team discussion might help patients and clinicians weigh potential trade-offs in the choice between PCI and CABG. These findings are observational and cannot establish causal treatment effects or equivalence in survival.

FUNDING: The CardioVascular Research Foundation (South Korea).

articles.title: Presentation, management, and outcomes of ectopic Cushing syndrome: an international, multicentre, retrospective, cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ectopic Cushing syndrome is a rare condition with scarce outcome data. We sought to characterise its course and determinants of complications and mortality.

METHODS: In this international, multicentre, retrospective, cohort study, 49 high-volume endocrine referral centres across Asia, Europe, North America, South America, and New Zealand identified consecutive eligible patients. We included patients with a clinical diagnosis of ectopic Cushing syndrome, defined by expert adjudication at the treating institution with at least one of the following criteria: inferior petrosal sinus sampling or dynamic testing supportive of ectopic Cushing syndrome, biochemical remission of hypercortisolism following treatment of the ectopic Cushing syndrome source (surgical excision, radiotherapy, or cryoablation), evidence of a non-metastatic tumoural source of ectopic Cushing syndrome, either on initial or subsequent imaging, or evidence of a metastatic tumoural source of ectopic Cushing syndrome either on imaging or from chart notes. Data collection was completed between May 31, 2024 and April 22, 2025. Clinical features, biochemical severity, management, complications, and mortality were assessed. The primary outcome was Cushing syndrome-related mortality (investigator-adjudicated). Secondary outcomes were overall mortality and incidence of complications. Outcomes were stratified based on biochemical remission and timeline since diagnosis. Early (within 6 months of diagnosis) and late (>6 months after diagnosis) outcomes were analysed using landmark methods.

FINDINGS: Among 1463 patients (median age 51 years [IQR 37-64; range 3-87], 824 [56·3%] women, 639 [43·7%] men, and 1021 [69·8%] of White race), 836 (57·1%) had metastatic disease. Severe hypercortisolism (1204 [91·1%] of 1321) and hypokalaemia (1111 [79·4%] of 1399) were common. Median duration of follow-up was 57 months (IQR 19-124). Cushing syndrome-related death occurred in 196 (13·4%) patients. 626 (42·8%) patients died overall. Infection occurred in 464 (31·7%) patients, venous thromboembolism in 124 (8·5%), cardiovascular events in 93 (6·4%), and cerebrovascular events in 37 (2·5%). Achievement of complete biochemical remission within 6 months of diagnosis was independently associated with lower risk of late complications (adjusted HR 0·55 [95% CI 0·38-0·80]) and Cushing syndrome-related mortality (0·49 [0·27-0·89]), whereas no association was observed with non-Cushing syndrome-related mortality.

INTERPRETATION: Outcomes in ectopic Cushing syndrome are driven by early control of hypercortisolism. Failure to achieve remission within 6 months is associated with markedly worse complications and mortality, supporting ectopic Cushing syndrome as a time-critical endocrine emergency.

FUNDING: Mayo Clinic.

articles.title: Andes virus management-balancing infection control with patient safety and autonomy.
Acquired cytomegalovirus in children: pathogen, bystander, or immune trainer?
articles.abstract: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) is one of the most common infections worldwide, with acquisition occurring predominantly in early childhood (younger than 5 years). Although congenital CMV is a recognised cause of neurodevelopmental impairment, the consequences of postnatally acquired CMV in children remain poorly defined and are often assumed to be benign. However, accumulating evidence suggests that acquired CMV infection is biologically active even when clinically silent, with the capacity to shape immune ontogeny, influence immune responses to other pathogens and vaccines, and alter health trajectories across the life course. In this Review, we examine the epidemiology, transmission pathways, immune responses, and clinical consequences of acquired CMV infection in childhood. We synthesise evidence to evaluate whether acquired CMV acts as a driver of pathology, a neutral bystander, or a beneficial immune trainer. The effects of CMV are highly context-dependent, determined by the timing of acquisition, host immune maturity, maternal health, co-infections, and broader social and environmental factors. Evidence of harm is strongest in infants with heightened biological or contextual risk, such as infants born preterm and those living with or exposed to HIV, whereas effects in children who are immunocompetent are heterogeneous and often clinically silent. Acquired CMV should be understood as a context-dependent immune modifier rather than a uniformly benign or pathogenic infection. This reframing of acquired CMV has important implications for policy and research. Universal intervention is unlikely to be appropriate; instead, targeted CMV prevention and treatment strategies for populations at high risk of CMV infection and severe disease integrated into maternal and child health programmes could offer the greatest benefit. Defining high-risk populations and critical windows for intervention should be prioritised to translate emerging evidence into improvements in childhood morbidity and equity.

articles.title: Metabolic Reprogramming Regulates Neutrophil Plasticity: From Acute Infection to Tumour Immunosuppression.
articles.abstract: Neutrophils are highly adaptable innate immune cells whose functions extend beyond antimicrobial defence to include regulation of chronic inflammation, tumour progression and tissue injury. Although traditionally considered glycolysis-dependent effector cells, emerging evidence reveals substantial metabolic plasticity that enables neutrophils to adapt to diverse microenvironmental pressures. Metabolic programmes involving carbohydrate utilisation, mitochondrial regulation, lipid metabolism, amino-acid-derived metabolites and redox control dynamically shape neutrophil migration, antimicrobial activity, survival, extracellular trap formation and immunoregulatory functions. However, the biological consequences of metabolic reprogramming are highly context dependent and the same pathway may support protective host defence in acute infection while promoting pathological inflammation or immunosuppression in chronic disease. Here, we develop a three-axis comparative framework based on temporal mode of metabolic reprogramming, granulocytic population identity and evidence level to examine neutrophil metabolism across acute infection, cancer and chronic inflammatory or metabolic disorders. This framework distinguishes transient metabolic adaptation in conventional neutrophils from sustained metabolic states associated with tumour-associated neutrophils and polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cells, while separating direct human neutrophil evidence from broader myeloid or preclinical observations. We discuss how metabolic pathways, including glycolysis, mitochondrial signalling, lipid handling, itaconate biology and ferroptosis-related mechanisms, are differentially engaged according to cellular state and tissue context. Finally, we evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies targeting neutrophil metabolism and highlight key translational challenges, including target specificity, preservation of antimicrobial competence, delivery strategies and patient selection. By integrating metabolic mechanisms with cellular identity and evidence strength, this review provides a framework for understanding how neutrophil metabolic plasticity contributes to immune protection and disease progression and identifies principles for developing context-selective therapeutic approaches.

articles.title: Ca2+ is an intracellular danger signal promoting STING activation.
articles.abstract: Calcium release in host cells is essential for viral infection and survival, and mutations disrupting calcium homeostasis are associated with chronic viral infections or autoimmune diseases in patients, yet the biological significance of calcium (Ca2+) signaling on stimulator of interferon genes (STING) activation remains unclear. Here, we show that cytosolic Ca2+ is sensed by host cells as an immediate-early danger signal. Viral infection-activated Rho GTPases and phospholipase C-β (PLCβ) induce ITPR-mediated endoplasmic reticulum (ER) Ca2+ release, while STING translocation induces TRPV2-mediated ER Ca2+ release, both leading to store-operated Ca2+ entry (SOCE) through ORAI channels. Ca2+ influx activates calmodulin (CaM)-dependent protein kinases CaMKK and CaMK1D. Activated CaMK1D phosphorylates STING, allowing for TBK1 trans-autophosphorylation. Inhibiting Ca2+ signaling or mutating CaMK1D-phosphorylating STING sites impairs STING activation. Consistently, Ca2+ signaling is important for the host defense against DNA viruses in mice. These results support a two-signal mode for STING activation in which the Ca2+-CaM-CaMKK-Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase (CaMK) cascade is indispensable.

articles.title: Fueling the failing heart: SGLT2i directly activates the hidden PANK1.
articles.abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) are rising stars for treating heart failure as first-line drugs, but the mechanism remains elusive. In a recent issue of Science, Forelli and colleagues show that SGLT2i bind directly to cardiac pantothenate kinase 1, boosting coenzyme A biosynthesis to support energy metabolism and functional recovery.

articles.title: Metformin-supportive nutrition: When gut microbes eat drugs.
articles.abstract: Metformin is a first-line treatment for type 2 diabetes in adults and children, but its efficacy varies significantly among patients. Zhao et al. identify microbial AdhE as a metformin-degrading enzyme in metformin low-responders and propose enzyme-based microbiome intervention as a strategy to rescue therapy.

articles.title: Beyond bacteria: A fungal metabolite drives liver cancer from within.
articles.abstract: Gut bacteria are established drivers of steatotic liver disease and liver cancer-gut fungi, much less so. Zhou et al. show that Rhizopus arrhizus promotes MASLD-associated liver cancer through kynurenic acid, a metabolite that bypasses its own surface receptors to engage the cytoplasmic scaffold IQGAP1.

articles.title: When Winter Comes: Seasonal Patterns in Outcomes After Major Surgery.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Seasonal strain may affect perioperative care, yet national evidence on seasonal variation in outcomes after major surgery remains limited. We evaluated whether postoperative outcomes varied by season among older adults undergoing major surgical procedures.

METHODS: Medicare beneficiaries aged 65 y or older undergoing abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, coronary artery bypass grafting, colectomy, lung resection, or pancreaticoduodenectomy from 2016 through 2021 were identified using 100% Medicare Standard Analytic Files. Seasons were defined meteorologically, with spring as the reference. Outcomes included 30-d mortality, 90-d mortality, complications, textbook outcome, failure to rescue, surgical site infection, and length of stay. Multivariable regression models adjusted for patient, procedure, and hospital characteristics and were stratified by elective versus emergency admission. Interactions with the nurse-to-bed ratio and the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Hospital Star Rating were assessed.

RESULTS: Among 1,165,265 patients, 738,236 underwent elective surgery and 427,029 underwent emergency surgery. Among emergency admissions, winter was associated with higher adjusted odds of 30-d mortality (adjusted odds ratio: 1.10; 95% confidence interval: 1.07-1.13), 90-d mortality (1.10; 1.07-1.13), complications (1.05; 1.03-1.07), and failure to rescue (1.11; 1.07-1.15), as well as lower odds of textbook outcome (0.96; 0.94-0.98) and longer length of stay. Among elective admissions, winter was associated with smaller increases in 30-d and 90-d mortality. No significant interaction was observed by nurse-to-bed ratio or Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Hospital Star Rating.

CONCLUSIONS: Winter was associated with worse outcomes after major surgery, particularly among emergency admissions, supporting targeted seasonal preparedness strategies.

articles.title: Does Geographic Disadvantage Increase Lower Extremity Amputation Risk in the State of Georgia?
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Over 100,000 lower extremity amputations are performed annually in the United States, with most related to peripheral arterial disease and diabetes. Rural populations experience greater socioeconomic disparities and higher rates of chronic disease. This study examined socioeconomic differences, prevalence of amputation risk factors, and lower extremity amputation rates between rural and urban residents of Georgia.

METHODS: County-level lower extremity amputation data for 2020 were obtained from the Georgia Department of Public Health. Demographic and socioeconomic data were retrieved from the US Census Bureau, and the prevalence of hypertension, diabetes, peripheral arterial disease, and smoking from the Centers for Disease Control Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System. Rural counties were defined as those with populations <50,000. Bivariate analyses compared rural and urban medians. Nonparametric data were log-transformed to meet assumptions of normality. Significance was set at P < 0.05 with 80% power.

RESULTS: Rural counties had higher proportions of males and individuals greater than 65 y. Rural populations had greater socioeconomic disadvantages: higher poverty and lower median income. Risk factors were more prevalent in rural areas: diabetes, hypertension, smoking, and peripheral arterial disease. The incidence of lower extremity amputations per 100,000 residents was higher in rural versus urban counties.

CONCLUSIONS: Rural Georgians undergo higher amputations of the lower extremities occurring in the context of greater prevalence of chronic disease and socioeconomic disadvantage.

articles.title: Licit and illicit drug consumption in the Paris conurbation: assessing short to mid-term temporal trends through WBE and comparison with official statistics.
articles.journal: The International journal on drug policy
articles.abstract: Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) is increasingly promoted as a tool for monitoring drug use, yet its added value for drug policy remains constrained by methodological uncertainties and limited integration with conventional indicators. This study evaluated the extent to which WBE can reliably characterize temporal drug consumption patterns and complement established surveillance approaches. A two-year campaign (March 2023-March 2025) was conducted at a wastewater treatment plant serving approximately 2.3 million inhabitants of the Paris conurbation. Bi-weekly composite samples (n = 202) were analyzed by LC-MS/MS for major licit and illicit drugs. Consumption was estimated using de facto population-normalized daily intakes, and temporal variations were explored using non-parametric statistics. Results confirm established consumption hierarchies (cannabis > cocaine > MDMA > ketamine, amphetamines-like stimulants) and typical recreational patterns, with pronounced weekend increases for MDMA, cocaine and alcohol, while cannabis exhibited stable use, suggesting its integration into routine consumption. Holiday periods were associated with a redistribution of consumption across the week rather than a simple overall increase, highlighting the importance of both temporal resolution and accurate assessment of the contributing population when interpreting consumption trends. While WBE-derived estimates for alcohol and tobacco were consistent with national sales data, reinforcing its validity for licit substances, the analysis also underscores persistent limitations for illicit drugs, particularly cannabis, for which prevalence estimates varied widely depending on normalization assumptions. A refined calculation framework yielded values closer to epidemiological benchmarks but remains dependent on contested parameters. Overall, these findings suggest that WBE is better suited to capturing relative changes and temporal dynamics than absolute prevalence, and that its policy relevance lies primarily in its ability to identify complement monitoring systems, rather than to replace established monitoring tools.

articles.title: Sleep quality, atrial fibrillation burden, and symptom severity in patients with atrial fibrillation: a cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep disturbances are common in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and may be associated with greater AF burden and more severe AF-related symptoms. However, evidence linking sleep quality to AF-related patient-reported outcomes remains limited.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate sleep quality, AF burden, AF-related symptom severity, and global well-being in patients with AF and to examine the associations between sleep quality and these outcomes.

METHODS: This descriptive cross-sectional study included 122 patients with AF attending the cardiology outpatient clinic of a public hospital. Data were collected using a patient information form, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and the University of Toronto Atrial Fibrillation Severity Scale (AFSS). Analyses included independent-samples t-test, one-way analysis of variance, Pearson correlation, and multivariable linear regression.

RESULTS: The mean PSQI score was 7.60 ± 3.29, and 77% of participants were classified as having poor sleep quality. Mean AFSS Global Well-being, AF Burden, and Symptom scores were 4.96 ± 1.93, 13.98 ± 5.40, and 9.42 ± 5.14, respectively. After adjustment for age, sex, BMI, AF duration, additional cardiac disease, and alcohol use, higher PSQI scores were associated with lower Global Well-being (β = -0.231, p = 0.013), higher AF Burden (β = 0.444, p < 0.001), and greater symptom severity (β = 0.453, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Poorer sleep quality was associated with lower global well-being, greater AF burden, and more severe AF-related symptoms. These findings support routine sleep assessment and individualized care in patients with AF.

articles.title: Early-life cigarette smoke exposure predisposes to COPD by suppressing the HAS2-TGF-B1-MAPK axis in lung fibroblasts.
articles.abstract: Early‑life exposure to environmental tobacco smoke (ETS) increases the risk of developing chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) in adulthood, but the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Using comparative cigarette smoke (CS) exposure in neonatal and adult mice, we show that early‑life CS produces fundamentally different pathology from adult exposure. Transcriptomic and protein analyses reveal that neonatal CS exposure suppresses the transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)-mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) axis, with decreased expression of fibroblast markers but not epithelial markers, identifying fibroblasts as the primary targets. In vitro, cigarette smoke extract directly downregulates Platelet-Derived Growth Factor Receptor Alpha（PDGFRα）, Fibronectin 1 (FN1), Collagen Type I (COL1), and Alpha-Smooth Muscle Actin (α-SMA) in lung fibroblasts, effects that are dose‑dependently rescued by exogenous TGF-β1. Mechanistically, the HAS2-TGF-β1-MAPK signaling axis regulates fibrosis through a uniquely inflammation-driven mechanism. Together, these findings establish that early-life CS exposure causes irreversible alveolar simplification by suppressing the TGF-β1-MAPK axis in lung fibroblasts, linking childhood ETS exposure to COPD susceptibility and identifying Hyaluronan Synthase 2（HAS2）, a marker of myofibroblasts, as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Assessing the perspectives of radiation therapists on managing dementia in radiotherapy: An international qualitative study.
articles.journal: Journal of medical imaging and radiation sciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence of dementia and cancer increases with age, creating additional challenges for cancer services as populations age and life expectancy rises. Radiotherapy is a cornerstone of cancer treatment and should remain accessible through patient-centred care. Understanding registered radiation therapists' (RRTs) knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions regarding patients with dementia is therefore important for equitable service provision.

AIM: To evaluate dementia-related knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions among registered radiation therapists (RRTs) working in radiotherapy departments and to explore factors influencing their confidence and preparedness in caring for patients with dementia.

METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among RRTs working in radiotherapy practice. The questionnaire collected demographic information and included the validated Alzheimer's Disease Knowledge Scale (ADKS), the Dementia Attitude Scale (DAS), and supplementary open-ended questions. Closed-ended responses were summarised using descriptive statistics, and open-ended responses were reviewed descriptively to contextualise participants' experiences and perceived challenges.

RESULTS: Of 54 responses received, 40 questionnaires were complete. Prior clinical or personal exposure to dementia was reported by 55.0% (n = 22). Only three respondents (7.5%) reported that their departments had dementia-management guidelines, while 90.0% (n = 36) identified opportunities to improve radiotherapy care for patients with dementia. Across the 30 ADKS items, 76.7% of responses were correct. DAS item responses varied, and only 4.8% (n = 2) strongly agreed that they felt confident around people with dementia.

CONCLUSION: RRTs showed generally positive attitudes toward caring for patients with dementia, but limited confidence and the scarcity of departmental guidance may hinder consistent care. Targeted education and radiotherapy-specific protocols are warranted.

PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: More people are living with both cancer and dementia, which can create challenges during radiation therapy treatment. This study surveyed radiation therapists about their knowledge, confidence, and experiences of caring for people living with dementia. This study found that therapists had generally positive attitudes but often lacked confidence and reported limited guidance for managing dementia-related needs. This matters because better training and clear care guidelines can help improve the treatment experience for people living with dementia.

articles.title: Reperfusion enhances treg-mediated neuroprotection and IL-10 signaling in a mouse model of large vessel occlusion.
articles.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
articles.abstract: The indications for acute reperfusion therapies in ischemic stroke have recently expanded to include patients with large ischemic cores, highlighting an urgent need for targeted neurotherapeutics that maximize tissue salvage. Preclinical studies suggest that early reperfusion, even after extensive ischemic injury, can mitigate infarct expansion and activate endogenous regenerative pathways, though the precise mechanisms driving these therapeutic benefits remain incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying successful reperfusion to identify novel avenues for immunotherapy. Using transient (t-MCAO) and permanent (p-MCAO) middle cerebral artery occlusion mouse models, we comprehensively analyzed central and peripheral immune cell dynamics. Our analysis revealed that successful reperfusion significantly elevates regulatory T cell (Treg) proportions compared to non-reperfused controls. Across experimental groups, higher interleukin-10 (IL-10) levels generally accompanied greater Treg abundance and better motor performance. Targeted intra-arterial delivery of IL-10 at the exact time of reperfusion directly attenuated cerebral injury and improved neurological outcomes. These findings suggest that amplifying anti-inflammatory signaling post-reperfusion may provide neuroprotection, positioning intra-arterial IL-10 as a potential adjunctive neurotherapeutic strategy to enhance the efficacy of mechanical thrombectomy.

articles.title: Crossover Handling and Atrial Fibrillation Burden in PRAGUE-25.
Reply: Crossover Handling and Atrial Fibrillation Burden in PRAGUE-25.
Contributors to quality in complex decision-making in paediatric intensive care.
articles.journal: Australian critical care : official journal of the Confederation of Australian Critical Care Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multidisciplinary complex decision-making (CDM) has become a ubiquitous component of paediatric intensive care practice. Some complex decisions-including determining goals of care or initiating life-long technology dependence-can benefit from structured approaches to decision-making. To optimise implementation of a previously published CDM tool, we undertook a quality improvement project aiming to identify key process and contextual contributors to effective CDM from the perspectives of the non-intensive care unit clinicians.

METHODS: A two-stage, institutionally registered quality improvement project was undertaken with multidisciplinary, non-paediatric intensive care unit (PICU) clinicians participating in CDM within a tertiary mixed PICU. An initial anonymous survey explored perspectives on communication and decision-making quality and processes, with categorical responses analysed quantitatively and free-text responses analysed thematically following Braun and Clarke's methodology. Survey findings informed subsequent semistructured focus group interviews with interested clinicians. Rigour was supported through independent coding and investigator and data-source triangulation.

RESULTS: Of 133 invited clinicians, 40 completed the survey in full (response rate: 30%). Most respondents were consultant medical practitioners (80%), and 93% reported prior participation in ad hoc, unstructured CDM with the PICU team. Although 87.5% reported comfort participating in CDM, respondents identified barriers including communication difficulties between teams (65%) and lack of clinician continuity of care (52.5%). Thematic analysis identified three primary domains influencing CDM: (i) care team structure; (ii) discussion planning and processes; and (iii) interpersonal communication and working culture. Focus groups identified priorities for implementation, including defined trigger criteria, appropriate representation, psychological safety, and clinically experienced neutral facilitation.

CONCLUSION: Multidisciplinary stakeholder perspectives revealed essential priorities for optimising CDM. Improving decision-making quality requires a multifaceted approach that supports intentional implementation of a deliberative tool with additional strategies addressing team care structures, communication, and working culture.

articles.title: Comparative effects of SGLT2 inhibitors, pioglitazone, DPP-4 inhibitors, and sulfonylureas on dementia risk in type 2 diabetes.
articles.journal: The journal of prevention of Alzheimer's disease
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Dementia risk is significantly amplified by type 2 diabetes (T2D). This study compares the impact of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) against pioglitazone, dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4is), and sulfonylureas on dementia risk.

METHODS: Using Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database (2000-2021), researchers emulated target trials with propensity-score matching. Cox proportional-hazards and Kaplan-Meier analyses estimated adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) for dementia subtypes.

RESULTS: Over a mean follow-up of 2.9 years, SGLT2i users had significantly lower cumulative incidences of all-cause and vascular dementia (all log-rank p < 0.05). Compared to pioglitazone, SGLT2i use was associated with lower risks of all-cause dementia (aHR 0.78, 95% CI 0.73-0.83) and vascular dementia (aHR 0.83, 95% CI 0.69-0.99). Alzheimer's risk reductions were not statistically significant.

DISCUSSION: In these nationwide emulated trials, SGLT2is were associated with lower risks of all-cause and vascular dementia compared with pioglitazone, DPP-4is, and sulfonylureas.

articles.title: Rationale and design of randomized, double-blind trial evaluating the efficacy of single-dose HPV vaccine efficacy in women aged 18 to 30: The PRISMA trial.
articles.abstract: Evidence from the Costa Rica HPV Vaccine Trial suggested that a single dose may provide durable protection in young adult women. Subsequent studies confirmed the non-inferiority of one vs. two doses of the main vaccines among young girls. Vaccination of older cohorts might accelerate cervical cancer elimination, especially if a single dose provides adequate protection. Randomized data are needed to support extended-age, single-dose vaccination strategies. Herein, we present the design, rationale and recruitment results of a three-arm, randomized, double-blinded, clinical trial in Costa Rica to evaluate the efficacy of a single dose of the bivalent (Cervarix®) and nonavalent (Gardasil 9®) HPV vaccines compared with an active control (Tdap). 4925 HPV vaccine-naïve women aged 18-30 years old were enrolled, randomized 1:1:1, and followed for 36 months with cervicovaginal self-sampling every six months starting at 12 months, annual blood collection, and oral/anal sampling at selected visits, with high participation rates. Participants attended ~90% of planned study visits and >96% of attendees provided the necessary specimens. The primary endpoint is incident cerviccovaginal HPV16/18 infection persisting ≥6 months among women HPV16/18 DNA-negative at the enrollment and vaccination visits. Secondary endpoints include vaccine efficacy in the intention-to-treat cohort, oral and anal HPV16/18 protection, and immunogenicity profiles. Trial results will inform mathematical models estimating impact and cost-effectiveness of extending single-dose vaccination to adult young women and directly inform policy to enable extended-age, single-dose strategies to accelerate cervical cancer prevention globally. Furthermore, the study will provide the first evidence for single-dose efficacy against anal and oral HPV infection.

articles.title: Changes in self-reported Long COVID in different variant-dominant phases of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic: the influence of vaccination on a diverse Israeli cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF RESEARCH: Long COVID (LC) risk varies across SARS-CoV-2 variants, but causal inference is complicated by rising vaccine coverage coinciding with viral evolution. We examined how pre-infection vaccination status modified LC risk across different pandemic periods dominated by different variants, to disentangle the contributions of viral evolution and vaccine-induced immunity. In this prospective cohort study of Israeli adults with SARS-CoV-2 infections from July 2021-March 2023, participants completed baseline and follow-up online surveys ≥60 days post-infection. LC was defined as ≥3 symptoms within validated symptom clusters. Infections were assigned to an infection period corresponding to the predominant circulating variant (Wild type, Alpha, Delta, Omicron) at onset time. Pre-infection vaccination was categorized as unvaccinated (0-1 doses), partially vaccinated (2 doses), or fully vaccinated (≥3 doses). Generalized estimating equations estimated multivariable risk ratios, adjusted for age, sex, and follow-up time. Among 1715 participants reporting 2018 infections, LC was reported following 30·4% of infections. In models adjusted for vaccination, LC risk did not differ between the Delta and Omicron-dominant periods (aRR 1·01, 95% CI 0·80-1·26). Among partially vaccinated individuals, infections during the Omicron-dominant period carried lower LC risk than during Delta (aRR 0·62, 95% CI 0·40-0·98). LC risk did not differ by variant-dominant periods among unvaccinated or fully vaccinated individuals.

MAJOR CONCLUSIONS: Observed differences in LC risk at various periods of the pandemic dominated by different variants may be largely explained by concurrent increases in vaccine coverage rather than intrinsic changes in variant pathogenicity. Full pre-infection vaccination conferred consistent protection against LC regardless of the period of variant dominance.

articles.title: Clinical endpoints for trials of Strep A vaccines: report of two expert meetings.
articles.abstract: Streptococcus pyogenes (group A Streptococcus; Strep A) causes a broad spectrum of diseases ranging from pharyngitis and skin infections to invasive disease and immune-mediated complications including acute rheumatic fever (ARF) and rheumatic heart disease (RHD). RHD remains one of the most important causes of cardiovascular mortality in young people globally, affecting more than 55 million individuals and causing over 370,000 deaths annually, predominantly in low- and middle-income countries. Despite this substantial burden, no licensed Strep A vaccine exists. A critical barrier to vaccine development is that there are many potential clinical trial endpoints capable of supporting regulatory approval while demonstrating meaningful public health impact. However, research gaps remain before these can be fully realised. To address this challenge, the World Health Organization (WHO) and the Strep A Vaccine Global Consortium (SAVAC) convened two international expert consultations in London (September 2024) and Geneva (October 2025). Participants reviewed emerging scientific evidence, epidemiology, and regulatory considerations to define potential clinical development pathways and priority endpoints for Strep A vaccines. Consensus emerged that prevention of Strep A pharyngitis in children represents a feasible primary endpoint for initial proof-of-efficacy trials and potential licensure. Impetigo in children was recognized as an important endpoint, particularly in high-burden settings or where it contributes substantially to transmission and severe invasive infections or progression to RHD. Although prevention of RHD and invasive disease is the ultimate public health objective, advanced RHD was considered infeasible as a pre-licensure endpoint. Early RHD detected by echocardiography was identified as a promising intermediate outcome, but further epidemiological and validation studies could increase confidence in its use in pivotal trials. A clinical development pathway is proposed in which initial licensure is supported by efficacy against pharyngitis and possibly impetigo or early RHD with further evaluation of other severe outcomes such as invasive infections through large-scale trials and post-licensure studies. This pathway informs updates to the WHO Preferred Product Characteristics and Research and Development Roadmap and provides a coordinated strategy to accelerate the development and equitable global introduction of Strep A vaccines.

articles.title: Literature Review of the Utility of Ultrasound for Adolescent and Child Ankle Injuries.
articles.abstract: Pediatric posterior ankle pain is a common and challenging presentation due to the complex anatomy and a broad differential diagnosis that includes apophysitis, tendon injuries, fractures, impingement syndromes, infection, and inflammatory arthropathies. Initial evaluation typically consists of physical examination and radiographs, which are often inconclusive and may result in delayed diagnosis, repeat imaging, and/or prolonged immobilization. Magnetic resonance imaging is the gold standard for most of these injuries, but it is expensive and logistically difficult for the pediatric population. A rapid, accessible, and cost-effective imaging modality is needed to improve early detection and management. This review evaluates the role of ultrasound in assessing posterior ankle pathology in pediatric patients. Ultrasound demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy in identifying Achilles tendon tears and differentiating partial- from full-thickness injuries while also assisting in treatment decision making through dynamic tendon gap assessment. It is recommended in several studies for evaluating Achilles tendinopathy and may have predictive value for future symptoms. Emerging evidence supports its adjunctive role in Sever disease and posterior ankle impingement syndrome as well. For osseous and infectious conditions, ultrasound can identify findings suggestive of calcaneal stress fractures, osteomyelitis, septic arthritis, and juvenile idiopathic arthritis. Although magnetic resonance imaging remains the gold standard for these diagnoses, ultrasound improves the detection of joint effusions and synovitis and enhances the accuracy of diagnostic joint aspirations. Overall, ultrasound is a dynamic, radiation-free modality that serves as a powerful adjunctive tool in evaluating pediatric posterior ankle pain.

articles.title: Upper-Extremity Tendinopathy and Enthesopathy in the Athlete: Best Evidence in Diagnostic and Therapeutic Advances.
articles.abstract: Tendinopathy and enthesopathy represent common overuse conditions in athletic populations and frequently affect the upper extremity, particularly the rotator cuff, elbow extensor origin, and wrist extensors. These conditions arise predominantly from mechanical overload and are characterized clinically by load-dependent pain and impaired function. Following clinical evaluation, diagnostic evaluation frequently requires multimodality to exclude alternative pathology or inflammatory disease. Exercise-based rehabilitation remains the foundation of management, with contemporary evidence supporting progressive, individualized loading programs, including eccentric, concentric, isometric, and heavy slow resistance protocols, are tailored to symptom severity and sport-specific demands. Adjunctive modalities such as extracorporeal shock wave therapy demonstrate benefit in select chronic cases, particularly lateral epicondylitis and calcific shoulder tendinopathy. Although nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs and corticosteroid injections may provide short-term symptom relief, corticosteroids are associated with inferior long-term outcomes and potential deleterious effects on tendon structure. Biologic therapies, including platelet-rich plasma and topical glyceryl trinitrate, demonstrate heterogeneous results, and high-volume image-guided injections remain selectively used in refractory cases. Surgical intervention is reserved for patients with persistent symptoms following 6 to 12 months of comprehensive nonoperative care because most individuals achieve symptom resolution without operative management. Open, arthroscopic, and percutaneous techniques demonstrate comparable outcomes. Emerging technologies, including in-office nanoarthroscopy and bioinductive collagen scaffolds, show early promise but require further high-quality investigation.

articles.title: Advances in Flexible Electronic Systems for Electrical Stimulation Assisted Wound Healing.
articles.abstract: Progress in miniaturization techniques coupled with advancements in material science and wearable technologies has transformed electrical stimulation (ES) technique of wound healing into a smart stand-alone patch. The present review article begins with a glimpse of the market demand and need for ES followed by a brief highlight on wound healing stages and the effects of ES in them. Thereafter, a roadmap on the use and effects of different ES modes is provided covering trials over in vitro cell-culture models as well as in vivo animal models along with details of ES safety parameters and biomaterial interface challenges. Following this, the article provides a detailed description of various inorganic flexible electronic-based ES patches for accelerated wound healing developed during the last decade along with an exhaustive study on various wound monitoring sensors like pH, temperature, moisture, bacterial infection, and metabolites, as well as their interdependency in influencing overall wound health and healing status. Additionally, the article also presents a brief insight into modern ES patches categorized under self-powered nanogenerator-driven and hydrogel-based patches along with integration of wireless communication and closed-loop control systems for an efficient wound healing system. Finally, the article concludes with a brief note highlighting the current unresolved bottlenecks required for its wider acceptance as well as the future attributes of ES patches catering the needs of generic to complex, hard-to-heal wounds with sophisticated multiparameter monitoring units and integrated AI/ML-driven solutions for driving the next-generation smart bandages.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes and coronary complication risk after transcatheter tricuspid annuloplasty with cardioband: a 12-month single-center cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical and echocardiographic outcomes of transcatheter tricuspid annuloplasty using the Cardioband system in a single-center cohort of high-risk patients with severe functional tricuspid regurgitation.

METHODS: This single-center prospective cohort study included 64 consecutive patients with severe functional tricuspid regurgitation undergoing transcatheter tricuspid annuloplasty with the Cardioband system. Clinical and echocardiographic data were collected at baseline, discharge, 6-months, and 12-months. Primary endpoints included changes in tricuspid regurgitation severity, annular dimensions, and clinical status, as well as all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization. Outcomes were analyzed using available-case data.

RESULTS: At 12-months, among patients with available echocardiographic data (n = 44), tricuspid regurgitation severity was reduced compared with baseline (p < 0.001); 15.9% had trace or mild TR, 45.5% had moderate TR, 27.3% had severe TR, and 11.4% had massive or torrential TR. All-cause mortality at 12-months was 6.3% (4/64 patients). According to TVARC criteria, intraprocedural success was achieved in 81.3% of patients, while a more stringent definition yielded a success rate of 65.6%.

CONCLUSION: In this single-center cohort of high-risk patients with severe functional tricuspid regurgitation, transcatheter tricuspid annuloplasty using the Cardioband system was associated with reductions in tricuspid regurgitation severity and improvements in selected clinical parameters at 12-months. However, these findings should be interpreted with caution given the observational design, incomplete follow-up, and the absence of a control group, as well as the observed rate of procedural complications. Further studies, ideally including larger multicenter cohorts and controlled comparisons, are needed to better define the role of this therapy in the management of tricuspid regurgitation.

articles.title: Real-world outcomes of continuous infusion of sedative agents in critically ill patients with invasive mechanical ventilation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Current guidelines recommend non-benzodiazepine (non-BZD) sedatives -dexmedetomidine (DEX) and propofol (PPF) - over benzodiazepines (BZD) in mechanically ventilated critically ill patients, but real-world evidence from Asian patients remains limited. We evaluated the clinical outcomes of different continuous-infusion sedatives in this population in Taiwan.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used electronic health records from a tertiary medical center in Taiwan. Adults receiving continuous intravenous sedation within 48 h of intubation were included. Patients with preexisting ventilator dependence, status epilepticus, or prior tracheostomy were excluded. Groups were 1:1 propensity score matched. Outcomes included intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay (LOS), time to extubation, mortality, and total hospitalization cost. Prespecified pairwise comparisons evaluated DEX vs. BZD, PPF vs. BZD, and DEX vs. PPF.

RESULTS: Of 2065 eligible patients, 605 matched pairs were analyzed. Compared with BZD, non-BZD sedation was associated with shorter ICU LOS (9.4 vs. 11.9 days, P = 0.032), earlier extubation (4.1 vs. 6.5 days, P = 0.015), and lower hospitalization cost (US$21,559 vs. US$26,258, P < 0.001), without a significant difference in 90-day mortality (36.7% vs. 38.7%, P = 0.489). In pairwise comparisons with BZD, DEX was associated with significantly shorter ICU LOS and time to extubation, whereas the benefit of PPF was primarily a reduction in hospitalization cost.

CONCLUSIONS: Non-BZD sedatives were associated with shorter ICU LOS, earlier extubation, and lower hospitalization costs without a detectable mortality difference. These findings are consistent with guideline recommendations favoring non-BZD sedation, although residual confounding remains possible.

articles.title: Integrative analysis of single-cell, bulk RNA-sequencing and biobank-scale genomic data reveals the bidirectional mediation and joint effects between proportion of beta cells and BMI for type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The pancreas comprises diverse endocrine and exocrine cell types, whose heterogeneity contributes to type 2 diabetes (T2D). However, the roles of cell composition changes remain unclear.

METHODS: We integrated six single-cell and four bulk RNA-sequencing datasets to estimate proportions of nine pancreatic cell types (PCP). Logistic regression assessed associations between PCP and T2D. Mediation analyses evaluated bidirectional effects between PCP and body mass index (BMI). Findings were validated using transcriptome-wide association analysis (TWAS) in the UK Biobank (UKB). Proportion of beta cells (PBC) associated differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were defined as the overlapping set of genes that showed higher expression in beta cells than in other cell types and differential expression between individuals with T2D and controls.

FINDINGS: Higher PBC was significantly associated with lower T2D risk (OR = 0.44, P = 1.93 × 10-5), confirmed in UKB (OR = 0.69, P = 2.31 × 10-36). Low PBC and high BMI jointly increased T2D risk in both bulk RNA-sequencing (OR = 22.06, P = 5.27 × 10-5) and UKB (OR = 5.61, P < 1.00 × 10-300) datasets. Bidirectional mediation between PBC and BMI was observed, with mediation proportions of 17.84% (P = 0.008) and 32.01% (P = 0.003), respectively, and validated in UKB (P = 1.11 × 10-7 and P = 5.30 × 10-7). Eleven PBC associated DEGs (e.g., HADH, PCSK1, and CASR) were identified.

INTERPRETATION: The interrelationship between PBC and BMI provides new insights into the link between obesity and pancreatic beta cell biology, while minimally invasive estimation of PBC from genomic data may facilitate population risk stratification and precision prevention of T2D.

FUNDING: This work was supported by National Natural Science Foundation of China, Noncommunicable Chronic Diseases-National Science and Technology Major Project, and US National Institutes of Health.

articles.title: Contaminants, body condition, and mortality: A comparative study of at-risk St. Lawrence Estuary belugas and Northwest Atlantic harbour porpoises.
articles.abstract: Marine mammals in the St. Lawrence (Canada) face cumulative anthropogenic stressors, including contaminant exposure. While resident St. Lawrence Estuary (SLE) belugas (Delphinapterus leucas; endangered) possess extensive blubber reserves, summering Northwest Atlantic (NWA) harbour porpoises (Phocoena phocoena; special concern) operate on high metabolic rates with minimal lipid storage. Contaminants including halogenated flame retardants (HFRs), per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), and trace elements may interfere with energetic metabolism, yet their relationships with body condition remain poorly understood. We evaluated whether these contaminants were associated with body condition, estimated by the Scaled Mass Index (SMI), and causes of mortality in stranded carcasses of SLE belugas (n = 59) and NWA harbour porpoises (n = 29) in 2016-2024. Contaminant profiles reflected contrasting habitat use; SLE belugas exhibited higher blubber HFR and liver PFAS concentrations, whereas NWA harbour porpoises presented lower organohalogen levels and higher liver trace element levels. In SLE belugas, SMI was negatively correlated with liver PFAS and total mercury (THg) concentrations, and over the study period. In NWA harbour porpoises, lower SMI was associated primarily with age class (calves) and higher liver THg levels. Multivariate analyses revealed that infectious disease mortality in NWA harbour porpoises clustered with higher trace element concentrations (THg, Se, Zn, Ag), whereas no clear associations between contaminants and causes of mortality were identified within age classes in SLE belugas. Present findings indicate that morphometric-based body condition and specific mortality categories correlate with distinct tissue contaminant profiles, pointing to potential linkages with energetic metabolism dysregulation and disease vulnerability.

articles.title: Awareness, attitudes toward epilepsy, and first-aid knowledge of seizures among rural primary care doctors in Eastern China.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to assess the awareness of, and attitudes toward epilepsy among young rural primary care doctors from rural clinics in Zhejiang Province, Eastern China.

METHODS: Ninety-five young rural primary care doctors working at rural clinics participated in this cross-sectional study in 2025. A custom-built electronic questionnaire, which comprised four sections, including 12 items for general condition data, 10 items for awareness (including first aid), a 16-item scale for attitudes, and 6 items for demographic data, was administered to the rural primary care doctors. Descriptive statistics, the Mann-Whitney U test, the Kruskal-Wallis H test, and Spearman's rank correlation analysis were used to analyze the data, which exhibited a non-normal distribution. Multivariable linear regression analyzes were conducted to identify independent predictors for each outcome, using the enter method and reporting β, B with 95% CI, p-values, and R2.

RESULTS: The young rural primary care doctors obtained a mean score of 18.20 ± 3.48 (aggregate score: 30) on the awareness of epilepsy section, a mean score of 5.40 ± 1.53 (aggregate score: 7) on the first aid knowledge section, and a mean score of 66.05 ± 7.65 (aggregate score: 80) on the epilepsy attitude section. Educational background (rs = 0.293, p = 0.004), training experience (rs = 0.322, p = 0.001), and epilepsy attitude scores (rs = 0.255, p = 0.013) correlated significantly with mean epilepsy awareness scores. Training experience (rs = 0.222, p = 0.031) correlated significantly with attitudes toward epilepsy. Multivariable regression analyzes showed that educational background independently predicted epilepsy awareness (p = 0.016) and first aid knowledge (p < 0.001), while training experience did not (p = 0.492 and p = 0.687, respectively). Epilepsy awareness independently predicted attitudes toward people with epilepsy (PWE) (p = 0.004) and first aid knowledge (p < 0.001). Furthermore, when rural primary care doctors faced newly diagnosed PWE, a referral was usually recommended (95.79%), and a few would initiate antiseizure medications (ASMs) (22.58%). In addition, about 30%-40% of the rural primary care doctors maintained an uncertain attitude toward the marriage, dating and pregnancy.

CONCLUSION: The awareness and attitudes of young rural primary care doctors toward epilepsy in the rural clinics were suboptimal. We recommend targeted training for young rural primary care doctors (covering first aid, novel ASMs, and patient counseling for marriage, dating, and pregnancy), combined with telemedicine integration to establish specialist support networks and optimize rural epilepsy care pathways.

articles.title: Assessing infection and inflammation in people with cystic fibrosis using their breath: A pilot longitudinal study.
articles.abstract: Cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) modulators have revolutionized cystic fibrosis (CF) management, but airway infections and inflammation persist. This study evaluates longitudinal exhaled breath profiles and identifies volatile organic compounds (VOCs) that correlate with sputum bacterial load and neutrophil elastase (NE) levels during ivacaftor and/or antibiotic treatment.Eight people with CF (pwCF) with a heterozygous R117H CFTR mutation and chronic lung infection with Pseudomonas aeruginosa (Pa) and/or Staphylococcus aureus were enrolled in a longitudinal study at St. Vincent's University Hospital in Dublin, Ireland. Breath samples and sputum samples were collected at multiple time points. Correlation analyses were performed between VOC abundances and bacterial load or NE levels.We observed temporal changes in breath profile across the eight subjects during the ivacaftor and/or antibiotic treatment. Within Pa-infected subjects, 54 VOCs showed consistent directional Pearson correlation and at least moderate repeated measures correlation (rmcorr) coefficient (rrm) with bacterial load, including the 12 VOCs previously reported as Pa-associated markers. Similarly, within Sa-infected subjects, we identified eight VOCs that showed consistent directional correlation and at least moderate rrm with bacterial load, including four previously reported Sa-associated markers. Additionally, we identified 7 exploratory VOC candidates that consistently correlated with changes in NE levels, each demonstrating a general weak rrm across eight subjects.This study demonstrates that breath profiles of pwCF change over time during ivacaftor and/or antibiotic treatment. Identifying specific breath VOCs whose levels correlate with Pa or Sa CFU/mL, as well as NE levels, supports further evaluation of exhaled breath VOCs as non-invasive markers for monitoring airway infection and inflammation in pwCF. &#xD.

articles.title: Interpreting Model-estimated Infliximab Exposure and Infection Risk in Inflammatory Bowel Disease.
Increasing Cardiovascular Disease-Related Mortality Burden in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) in the United States: A Nationwide Analysis (1999 to 2024).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a complex multisystem disorder, with cardiovascular disease (CVD) representing the most common cause of mortality. This study aims to analyze trends in MASLD and CVD-related mortality in the United States.

METHODS: Mortality data for individuals aged 25 years and older from 1999 to 2024 were obtained from the CDC WONDER database. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 population were calculated among patients with MASLD and CVD. Temporal trends were assessed using Joinpoint regression analysis to estimate the annual percent change (APC) and average annual percent change (AAPC) in mortality rates.

RESULTS: Between 1999 and 2024, a total of 55,788 deaths were identified related to MASLD and CVD among adults aged 25 years or older. The number of deaths increased from 1044 in 1999 to 5216 in 2024, reflecting a 400% increase in mortality. The most common causes of CVD-related mortality were hypertension and ischemic heart disease. The total number of deaths among men was higher compared to women (30,201 vs. 25,587), and the rate of increase in mortality was higher among women (7.60, 95% CI: 7.07-8.35 vs. 3.42, 95% CI: 2.78-4.17).

CONCLUSION: Our analysis highlights acceleration in CVD-related mortality among MASLD patients with widening disparities. These findings highlight MASLD as a growing contributor to cardiovascular mortality, and targeted prevention, along with reduction strategies, are urgently needed to mitigate this rising burden.

articles.title: Discordant marrow MRD and PET-CT in myeloma: A four-state language for joint reporting.
articles.abstract: In a Nutshell, discordant bone marrow measurable residual disease (BM-MRD) and positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) assessments in multiple myeloma do not simply represent assay disagreement. They can provide clinically relevant information because the direction of discordance changes the interpretation of response: BM-MRD-negative/PET-positive disease indicates PET-visible disease outside the sampled marrow compartment, whereas BM-MRD-positive/PET-negative disease reflects marrow persistence without PET-visible disease. This distinction matters for defining deep response, interpreting MRD-driven end-points and designing studies of response-adapted treatment. A four-state language turns discordance from an ambiguous finding into a reportable response framework.

articles.title: Application of the Water and Sanitation for Health Facility Improvement Tool to Identify Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene Gaps in Healthcare Facilities in Bangladesh.
articles.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.abstract: Inadequate water, sanitation, and hygiene services remain a major challenge in healthcare facilities (HCFs), particularly in low- and middle-income countries. In the present study, the WHO's Water and Sanitation for Health Facility Improvement Tool (WASH FIT) was used to identify system-level WASH gaps and inform quality improvement in selected HCFs in Bangladesh. This cross-sectional study was conducted purposively in 16 HCFs across six divisions of Bangladesh between October and December 2023. Water, sanitation, and hygiene conditions were assessed using WASH FIT, which evaluates 96 indicators across seven domains. Indicators were scored on a three-point scale, and domain and overall performance were categorized using WASH FIT cutoff points and WHO/United Nations Children's Fund Joint Monitoring Program service ladders. No facility achieved an overall WASH FIT score greater than 67%. Although all facilities had basic water supplies, 93.8% had less than 1 day of water storage capacity, and 62.5% lacked reliable drinking water stations. Sanitation services were poor, with no facility scoring greater than 46%; none had disability-accessible toilets, and 81.3% lacked menstrual hygiene management facilities. Hand hygiene was the weakest domain, with soap available at only 56.6% of handwashing stations. Only 37.5% of facilities practiced proper healthcare waste segregation, and none provided adequate personal protective equipment to waste handlers. Environmental cleaning scores were also low because of inadequate protocols and limited trained staff. These findings reveal the value of WASH FIT for identifying infrastructure, operational, governance, and management gaps to support evidence-informed planning and strengthen infection prevention and control in healthcare facilities.

articles.title: Acid Suppression and Pancreatitis: Are PCABs Safer Than PPIs? A Global Database Analysis.
articles.abstract:
GOALS: This study aimed to evaluate the incidence of acute pancreatitis (AP) following initiation of potassium-competitive acid blockers (PCABs) versus proton pump inhibitors (PPIs).

BACKGROUND: The comparative risk of AP associated with PCABs versus PPIs remains uncertain.

STUDY: This retrospective cohort study analyzed data from the TriNetX database, which included adult patients who received a prescription for either PCAB or PPI between January 1, 2016, and August 1, 2025. Patients with a prior diagnosis of acute or chronic pancreatitis, pancreatic neoplasms, organ transplantation, or pregnancy were excluded. Propensity score matching (1:1) was used to adjust for demographic and other confounders.
