Univariate Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess the incidence of AP within 90 days of therapy initiation.

RESULTS: In total, 77,841 adults using PCAB and 13,497,134 adults using PPI were included. Among them, 80 patients in the PCAB cohort and 96,170 patients in the PPI cohort developed AP. The overall incidence of AP within 90 days of therapy initiation was 0.65% in the PCAB cohort and 0.96% in the PPI cohort, with the highest rates observed in adults aged 75 years or older and females. After matching, PCAB use was not associated with a statistically significant difference in new-onset AP compared with PPI (OR: 0.624; P=0.24). PCAB users had significantly lower odds of acute respiratory failure, acute renal failure, and sepsis than PPI users. Mortality was also significantly lower in the PCAB cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: The study suggests that PCABs may offer a safer alternative to PPIs with respect to AP risk, although further investigation is warranted.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Routine Postdilation in Balloon-Expandable Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Platform: The DUOTAP Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: In patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), asymmetric valve expansion can estimate prosthetic dysfunction and death. Postdilation has shown promising results in optimizing valve geometry in observational studies; however, randomized evidence is currently lacking.

OBJECTIVE: To determine the efficacy of routine postdilation on transcatheter heart valve (THV) geometry and hemodynamic performance, and associated safety outcomes.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: DUOTAP was a single-center, single-blinded randomized clinical trial. Recruitment took place from January 2025 to April 2026 and end points were assessed periprocedurally (fluoroscopy) at 30 days (adverse events) and at 3 months (computed tomography [CT]). The trial was conducted at a high-volume tertiary referral center, the Medical University of Vienna, Austria. Included patients had severe AS suitable for transfemoral TAVI with a balloon-expandable THV and without high-risk features on preprocedural CT or coronary angiography and were randomized in a 1:1 ratio, stratified by THV size, to routine postdilation vs no postdilation. These data were analyzed from July 2026 to September 2026.

INTERVENTION: Routine postdilation using the original delivery balloon at the identical filling volume. A sham procedure was performed in the control group.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The fluoroscopic THV asymmetry index served as primary end point. Further fluoroscopic and CT-derived measures of valve geometry, hypoattenuated leaflet thickening (HALT), paravalvular leak (PVL), and THV hemodynamics on echocardiography, and freedom from major procedural adverse events served as secondary end points.

RESULTS: Overall, 148 patients (median [IQR] age, 81 [77-85] years; 69 female [46.6%] and 79 male [53.4%]; median EuroSCORE-II, 2.3%) underwent randomization (n = 74 intervention vs n = 74 control). Intervention yielded a 70% lower THV asymmetry index compared with control (median: 1.2% vs 2.8%; geometric mean ratio: 0.30; 95% CI, 0.18-0.47; P < .001), with consistent effects across prespecified subgroups, induced by frame height reduction across the outer curve. Additionally, intervention yielded numerically larger THV diameters on fluoroscopy and significantly larger THV areas at the inflow, midframe, and outflow level on CT. HALT and mild or worse PVL were significantly less frequent and the Doppler Velocity Index was significantly higher in the intervention group. No differences in procedure-related adverse events between groups were recorded (χ2 test: P = .36).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial, postdilation led to reduced THV asymmetry, optimized geometry, and improved hemodynamic performance, without increasing procedure-related adverse events. These results support the use of routine postdilation to optimize THV geometry and hemodynamics in suitable patients.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07477002.

articles.title: Ectopic Ascariasis Mimicking a Renal Mass: A Review of Aberrant Migration in Ascaris Lumbricoides.
articles.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.abstract: Ascaris lumbricoides infection is one of the most common helminthiases worldwide and is associated with poor sanitation in tropical and subtropical regions. Although most cases are asymptomatic or present with nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms, aberrant migration may lead to ectopic disease. We present a case report of a 51-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with progressive abdominal enlargement, gastrointestinal symptoms, and significant weight loss. Imaging studies revealed a large left perirenal mass initially interpreted as a renal neoplasm. She subsequently developed acute urinary retention and unexpectedly expelled a 30-cm reddish-brown cylindrical helminth with tapered ends, morphologically consistent with Ascaris lumbricoides. Complete symptom resolution and disappearance of the perirenal lesion on follow-up imaging supported the parasitic origin of the condition. This case illustrates a presentation of ectopic ascariasis with possible renal involvement, highlighting abnormal migration mechanisms such as fistulization or retrograde migration.

articles.title: Not All "Contamination" Is the Same: Rethinking Management of Mixed-Flora and Contaminated Pre-Operative Urine Cultures.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Optimal management of polymicrobial pre-operative urine cultures (UCx) reported as mixed non-pathogenic urogenital skin flora (USF) or contaminated remains unclear. We evaluated whether UCx classification predicts post-operative urinary tract infection (UTI).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed endoscopic urologic procedures at a multi-hospital academic center between January 2022 and May 2026 with a pre-operative UCx within 30 days. UCx were categorized as positive, negative, USF, or contaminated (polymicrobial with ≥1 uropathogen). The primary outcome was ICD-10-coded UTI within 30 days. Secondary outcomes included post-operative fever, post-operative positive UCx, readmission, and ninety-day mortality. Primary statistical analysis was performed per patient utilizing the index procedure. Secondary analysis was performed per procedure, utilizing clustering with generalized estimating equations (GEE).

RESULTS: The index cohort comprised 10,117 patients. Post-operative UTI occurred within 30 days in 19% of patients, and was more common after pre-operative positive (39%, p<0.001) and contaminated (23%, p=0.002) than negative UCx (12%), whereas USF was not. Positive (aOR 2.78, 95% CI 2.42-3.20) and contaminated UCx (aOR 1.42, 1.16-1.73) remained independently associated with UTI, whereas USF did not (aOR 0.83, 0.70-0.99). Among the 13,804 procedures performed, risk estimates were consistent in secondary clustered GEE analysis. Contaminated UCx were independently associated with readmission and ninety day all-cause mortality (aOR 1.98, 1.20-3.25).

CONCLUSIONS: Contaminated urine cultures, defined by at least one nondominant uropathogen, were associated with post-operative UTI, whereas USF was not. Polymicrobial cultures with a uropathogen may warrant repeat collection or speciation.

articles.title: The Digital Twin Paradigm in Head and Neck Cancer: Clinical Opportunities and Challenges.
articles.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) represents a significant public health challenge. Its treatment is characterized by high anatomical complexity and a critical need for functional preservation of speech, swallowing, and respiration. While multimodality care, including surgery, radiotherapy, and systemic therapy, has substantially improved patient survival, there are still high rates of life-altering toxicities and low response rates to immunotherapy. Current clinical decision-making largely relies on "digital snapshots"-static representations derived from population-based statistics and time point-specific imaging-which usually fail to account for the rapid anatomical and biological change during the course of treatment. Digital twins hold great promise in accelerating scientific breakthroughs and transforming oncology treatment and precision medicine through the creation of high-fidelity virtual patient representations that integrate real-time biological, anatomical, and clinical data. In this viewpoint, we propose 3 interconnected digital twins to establish a conceptual framework for the HNSCC digital twin. These digital twins include the anatomical twin, using virtual surgical planning and augmented reality for geometric precision; the dosimetric twin, using daily imaging and synthetic computed tomography generation for automated adaptive radiotherapy; and the biological twin, integrating deep phenotyping, radiomics, and mechanistic omics to simulate individualized therapeutic trajectories. Beyond acute care, we explore the clinical utility of digital twins in navigating the "de-escalation dilemma" for human papillomavirus-associated disease and improving survivorship through digital phenotyping. With the advent of longitudinal data from medical-grade Internet-of-Things sensors and circulating tumor DNA kinetics, digital twins can serve as active sentinels, detecting functional decline or subclinical events months before clinical manifestation. Furthermore, the implementation of synthetic control arms via virtual populations offers an avenue to accelerate clinical trials and address ethical issues in rare molecular subtypes. Despite this potential, substantial barriers to implementation remain, including profound anatomical instability during treatment, the "black box" nature of deep learning algorithms, and the challenges of multiscale data integration. We provide a technical roadmap for the development of "morphing" digital twins-dynamic systems capable of continuous geometric and biological auditing. By bridging the gap between the macroscopic world of radiation physics and the microscopic world of cellular evolution, digital twins may help shift the management of HNSCC from population-based statistical probability toward more individualized, biologically informed decision-making, with the goal of optimizing HNSCC management while preserving essential patient functions.

articles.title: Co-Designed Text Messaging Intervention for Parents of Children With Early Childhood Caries: Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early childhood caries (ECC) is a prevalent yet preventable disease that significantly impacts young children's health and quality of life. The World Health Organization's Global Strategy and Action Plan on Oral Health 2023-2030 highlights the potential of mobile health programs to enhance engagement and support sustained oral health behavior change.

OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to assess the effectiveness of the SmilesUp 12-week SMS text messaging-based education and support program to improve parents' management of their children's oral health behaviors compared to standard clinical care.

METHODS: We conducted a multisite, assessor-blinded, parallel-design randomized controlled trial among parents of children aged 0 to 6 years who had an ECC diagnosis and attended 1 of 6 public dental clinics in metropolitan, regional, and rural New South Wales, Australia. Participants were randomly assigned to either an intervention group receiving the fully automated 12-week SmilesUp program (3 SMS text messages weekly) or a control group. Both groups continued to receive usual standard dental clinical treatment. The primary behavioral outcome was parent-reported twice-daily toothbrushing with fluoride toothpaste. Secondary outcomes included adherence to oral health-promoting bedtime routines and child consumption of sugar-sweetened foods and beverages. Oral health self-efficacy was measured using 6 behavioral theory-mapped items across oral hygiene, diet, and bedtime routines.

RESULTS: A total of 154 participants were enrolled and randomized (n=78, 50.6% in the control group; n=76, 49.4% in the intervention group) across 6 sites, with 80.5% (124/154) completing the follow-up assessment. High program adherence was observed, with 96.1% (73/76) of intervention participants completing the program. At 12 weeks, a greater proportion of SmilesUp participants reported brushing their children's teeth twice daily (45/61, 73.8% vs 42/63, 66.7%; adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.45, 95% CI 0.95-6.74; P=.07), though this difference was not statistically significant. Significant improvements were observed in adherence to bedtime routines (54/61, 88.5% vs 45/63, 71.4%; aOR 3.25, 95% CI 1.15-10.18; P=.03) as well as oral health knowledge on toothbrushing (46/50, 92.0% vs 41/52, 78.8%; aOR 5.47, 95% CI 1.48-25.19; P=.02). No statistically significant differences were found in sugar-sweetened food (10/61, 16.4% vs 4/63, 6.3%; aOR 3.72, 95% CI 1.02-17.14; P=.06) or beverage (25/61, 41.0% vs. 27/63, 42.9%; aOR 1.08, 95% CI 0.49-2.30; P=.85) consumption.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that co-designed SMS text messaging-based programs show promise and may represent a feasible strategy for oral health behavior change. However, larger-scale and longer-term studies are needed to confirm sustained effectiveness using clinical outcomes. Future research should also explore ways mobile health can be scaled and cost-effectively embedded into comprehensive, interdisciplinary primary models of care.

articles.title: A Culturally Tailored, Behavioral Theory-Informed Educational Intervention for Pregnant Women to Improve Postnatal Care Use and Safe Maternal and Newborn Care Practices in Ethiopia: Protocol for a Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The postnatal period is a critical phase for maternal and newborn survival, during which many preventable complications and deaths occur, yet postnatal care (PNC) use remains low in Ethiopia. Care-seeking and postpartum practices are shaped by knowledge and also by interacting cognitive, interpersonal, sociocultural, and environmental determinants, including perceived risk, self-efficacy, family influence, social norms, and culturally embedded beliefs. Existing educational interventions largely prioritize information provision and insufficiently address these determinants, limiting the translation of knowledge into timely PNC use and safe maternal and newborn care practices.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a culturally tailored educational intervention for pregnant women, informed by Social Cognitive Theory (SCT) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), in improving PNC use and promoting safe maternal and newborn care practices in Ethiopia.

METHODS: A 2-arm, assessor-blinded, open-label, matched-pair cluster randomized controlled trial was conducted across 14 woredas in Jimma Zone, Ethiopia. A total of 28 health facilities were randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention and control arms. Pregnant women at 20 to 24 weeks of gestation were recruited from kebeles within the randomized health-facility clusters. Participants in the intervention arm received the educational intervention delivered by trained health extension workers, whereas those in the control arm received routine antenatal health education. The primary outcome was PNC use; secondary outcomes were newborn-care knowledge and practices. Primary analyses will follow the intention-to-treat principle. Mixed-effects regression models with random intercepts for health-facility clusters will be used to estimate intervention effects while accounting for intracluster correlation.

RESULTS: The study was funded by the Eckenstein-Geigy Professorship in June 2025. From November 2025 to January 2026, 945 pregnant women were enrolled across 28 health facilities in Jimma Zone, Ethiopia. The intervention was delivered from December 2025 to May 2026, with follow-up conducted from December 2025 to July 2026. Follow-up data collection was completed in July 2026, and data cleaning and statistical analysis began in the same month. The primary and secondary analyses are scheduled for completion in fall 2026, and the trial findings are expected to be submitted for publication in fall 2026. The mean age of participants was 26.84 years (SD 5.23), with the majority residing in rural areas (n=834, 88.3%) and being married (n=937, 99.2%). Baseline characteristics were generally similar between trial arms regarding age, residence, marital status, and obstetric history, although notable differences were observed in maternal occupation, educational attainment, and household income.

CONCLUSIONS: This trial will provide evidence on whether a culturally tailored, behavioral theory-informed educational intervention delivered during pregnancy can improve PNC use and promote safe maternal and newborn care practices in Ethiopia. The findings may inform the design and integration of context-responsive maternal and newborn health education within community-based health services.

articles.title: Advances in Machine Learning Paradigms for Reliable Swimming Pool Drowning Detection: Systematic Review of Methods and Implementations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Drowning is a leading cause of unintentional injury-related mortality worldwide, particularly in swimming pool environments, where rapid detection is critical to prevent fatalities. Traditional monitoring approaches rely on lifeguards and rule-based systems, which are often limited by human error, delayed response, and environmental challenges such as occlusion, glare, and multiple swimmers. Machine learning (ML) and computer vision methods have emerged as promising alternatives for automated drowning detection; however, their methodological rigor, real-world applicability, and reliability remain unclear.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to systematically review advancements in ML-based drowning detection systems over the past 15 years. The review focused on detection methods, sensing modalities, evaluation metrics, and validation practices. It also examined how studies addressed real-world challenges such as occlusion, lighting variability, and multiswimmer environments, and identified key gaps related to generalizability, reliability, and privacy.

METHODS: A systematic literature review was conducted using major electronic databases, including IEEE Xplore, Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, ACM Digital Library, and Google Scholar. A total of 4927 records were initially identified and screened by 2 independent reviewers using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. A final set of 30 studies was included for data extraction and synthesis. The methodological quality and risk of bias were assessed using the Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool (PROBAST), while reporting transparency was evaluated using the TRIPOD (Transparent Reporting of a Multivariable Prediction Model for Individual Prognosis or Diagnosis) guidelines. Data analysis was conducted in R.

RESULTS: The findings indicate that drowning detection research is dominated by supervised, vision-based approaches (23/30, 76.7%), with convolutional neural networks (5/30, 16.7%) and You Only Look Once-based architectures (7/30, 23.3%) being the most commonly used methods. While reported performance is generally high, with mean accuracy exceeding 90.9%, evaluation practices are heavily centered on accuracy, with limited reporting of precision, recall, false alarm rate, and latency. One of 30 (3.3%) studies reported validation under real-world operational conditions, with an additional 5 (16.7%) studies using real-world data without formal real-world validation, and no studies conducted cross-dataset evaluation. In addition, critical real-world challenges such as occlusion, glare, and crowding were rarely addressed (<10% of studies), and all studies relied on private datasets. The PROBAST assessment further indicated a high risk of bias in 96.7% (29/30) of studies, primarily due to limited validation and nonrepresentative data sources.

CONCLUSIONS: ML-based drowning detection systems have demonstrated substantial progress in algorithm development, particularly in vision-based models. However, this progress is not matched by equivalent advances in validation, robustness, and real-world applicability. The field is characterized by a significant gap between experimental performance and deployment readiness. Future research should prioritize standardized evaluation frameworks, external validation, comprehensive performance reporting, and the integration of multimodal and privacy-preserving approaches to enable reliable real-world implementation.

articles.title: Predictive and Prognostic Role of Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio in Diabetic Nephropathy: Protocol for a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A growing body of research has implicated systemic inflammation in the pathogenesis of diabetic nephropathy (DN), with the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) emerging as a potential biomarker. However, individual studies and previous evidence syntheses have reported substantial heterogeneity in patient populations, DN definitions, renal function measures, and NLR thresholds, limiting the comparability and interpretation of findings. The extent to which these clinical and methodological differences contribute to variability in the association between NLR and DN remains insufficiently characterized.

OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aims to quantify the association between NLR and DN across measures of disease presence, severity, and prognosis and to investigate potential sources of between-study heterogeneity through prespecified subgroup, sensitivity, and meta-regression analyses.

METHODS: The protocol was designed in accordance with the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidelines. A comprehensive literature search of the MEDLINE (Ovid), Embase, the CENTRAL, and Scopus databases was conducted from inception to February 28, 2025. Eligible studies included adults (aged >18 years) with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and evaluated the predictive or prognostic value of NLR in relation to DN, using validated measures of DN including albuminuria, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), glomerular filtration rate (GFR), or serum creatinine. Randomized and nonrandomized interventional studies and observational studies were eligible, with no language restrictions. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data on NLR levels and relevant effect estimates. The methodological quality of observational studies was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Meta-analyses were performed in RStudio (version 4.5.1) using standardized mean differences or odds ratios, as appropriate, with 95% CIs. Random-effects models were used, and subgroup, sensitivity, and meta-regression analyses were performed to explore potential sources of heterogeneity.

RESULTS: The study was initiated on August 31, 2024, and the protocol was first submitted to PROSPERO (CRD42025641025) on February 6, 2025. The literature search identified 1927 records, of which 805 (41.8%) duplicate records were removed. Following title and abstract screening, 123/1,222 (11%) full-text reports were assessed for eligibility, with 45/123 (36.6%) studies included in the qualitative synthesis and 40/45 in the quantitative synthesis. Screening of search results against the inclusion criteria was completed in March 2025. Data extraction was conducted from March 2025 to May 2025, followed by risk-of-bias and quality assessment from May 2025 to July 2025 and data analysis from July 2025 to October 2025. The completed systematic review and meta-analysis was submitted for publication on May 30, 2026.

CONCLUSIONS: This systematic review sought to synthesize the available evidence on the association between NLR and DN occurrence, severity, and prognosis in T2DM, examining its potential as a biomarker and the sources of variability across studies. If the anticipated associations are supported, NLR may warrant evaluation within risk-stratification models for T2DM.

articles.title: Toward detection of heart failure: development of a sensitive fluorescent kit for clinical sST2 detection.
articles.abstract: Heart failure, the terminal stage of various cardiovascular diseases, typically presents with subtle early symptoms that are difficult to detect. Consequently, developing fast and accurate diagnostic tools is essential for effective early diagnosis and disease management. Soluble suppression of tumorigenicity 2 (sST2) is recognized as a valuable biomarker for predicting disease severity and mortality in cardiovascular disease, making it a promising target for developing a detection kit for early heart failure diagnosis. Recently, the CRISPR-Cas12a system has been increasingly used for quick and sensitive nucleic acid detection. However, its application in protein detection remains limited. In this study, we combined nanotechnology-mediated protein capture with the CRISPR-Cas12a system and developed a fluorescence-based method for rapid and sensitive detection of sST2. The presence of sST2 triggers the formation of a ternary complex, which can activate the trans-cleavage activity of Cas12a, resulting in cleavage of the response DNA single strand and the production of a fluorescent signal. Importantly, when tested on serum samples, this method can effectively distinguish patients with heart failure from healthy controls. This method offers a promising alternative to traditional enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs), with potential advantages in operational simplicity and detection speed. Therefore, this innovative fluorescence-based sST2 detection technique has significant potential for the clinical diagnosis of heart failure.

articles.title: Association Between Cardiovascular Disease and Cataracts: Protocol for a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is emerging evidence suggesting shared pathophysiological mechanisms between cataracts and cardiovascular disease (CVD), indicating a potential link between these 2 prevalent noncommunicable diseases. Oxidative stress, resulting from an imbalance between reactive oxygen species production and the body's antioxidant defenses, contributes to lens protein aggregation in cataracts and lipid oxidation in atherosclerosis, a key feature of several CVD subtypes. This shared pathophysiology implies that systemic vascular health may influence cataractogenesis. However, the epidemiological evidence supporting this relationship remains inconclusive.

OBJECTIVE: The main objective of this systematic review is to synthesize existing evidence on the odds or risk of developing cataracts in adults with underlying CVD.

METHODS: This systematic review will adhere to the PRISMA-P (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Protocols). Using the population, exposure, comparator, and outcome framework, this review will identify the association between established CVD and the risk of cataract development or needing cataract surgery. Systematic literature searches will be conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase using MeSH terms from database inception to December 31, 2024. Original research articles involving adults (aged ≥18 years) that assess the statistical relationship between CVD and cataracts will be included. Two independent reviewers will screen studies, extract data, and appraise the studies' quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. If deemed feasible, meta-analyses will be conducted using random-effects models to calculate pooled effect estimates, with heterogeneity assessed using the I2 statistic.

RESULTS: This study did not receive any external funding. The literature search, study screening, and data extraction will be conducted in 2026, and data analysis will be performed accordingly. The findings are anticipated to be published in 2027.

CONCLUSIONS: This systematic review will provide a consolidated and up-to-date evaluation of the relationship between CVD and cataracts. The findings will highlight the potential importance of integrating cardiovascular risk assessment into routine ophthalmologic care. Continued refinement of study methodologies and standardization of outcome measures may be needed to address observed heterogeneity and strengthen future evidence, ultimately supporting more holistic management of patients with coexisting cardiovascular and ocular conditions.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant Apalutamide With or Without Abiraterone Acetate Plus Prednisone and Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone Agonist Prior to Nerve-Sparing Radical Prostatectomy in High-Risk Prostate Cancer: Protocol for a Randomized Phase 2 Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radical prostatectomy (RP) is an accepted, definitive treatment for appropriately selected men with high-risk localized prostate cancer (PCa). However, neoadjuvant androgen receptor inhibition prior to RP is not currently the standard of care. Wide resection of the neurovascular bundles may improve local oncologic control but can adversely affect postoperative erectile function and urinary continence. Apalutamide directly inhibits the androgen receptor, while abiraterone acetate inhibits cytochrome P450 17A1-mediated androgen synthesis and is often administered with prednisone. Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) agonists further suppress testicular androgen production. Intensified androgen pathway inhibition prior to surgery may therefore downstage localized disease and facilitate bilateral nerve-sparing RP.

OBJECTIVE: This study was defined to evaluate whether 3 months of neoadjuvant apalutamide-based therapy before RP improves postoperative potency recovery by 12 months compared with immediate RP in men with high-risk localized PCa. Secondary objectives include evaluation of postoperative continence, pathological outcomes, biochemical recurrence, perioperative outcomes, and quality of life (QoL).

METHODS: This is a prospective, multicenter, randomized phase 2 clinical trial (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT02949284). Eligible patients with high-risk PCa were randomized 1:1:1 to (1) apalutamide 240 mg daily for 3 months followed by RP, (2) apalutamide 240 mg daily with abiraterone acetate 1000 mg plus prednisone 10 mg daily and a GnRH agonist for 3 months followed by RP, or (3) immediate RP without neoadjuvant therapy. The primary end point is potency recovery by 12 months postoperatively, defined as the ability to penetrate in sexual intercourse in more than half of attempts. Secondary end points include continence recovery, pathological response, positive surgical margins, biochemical recurrence, perioperative outcomes, and QoL. The primary comparisons evaluate each experimental arm against the surgery-only arm. Pairwise comparisons of the primary end point will use 1-sided Fisher exact tests with a Bonferroni adjustment. Additional continuous and categorical outcomes will be analyzed using appropriate nonparametric or categorical tests, and biochemical recurrence-free survival will be assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis.

RESULTS: As of March 2026, patient enrollment has been completed. A total of 96 patients provided consent and were screened, 88 were randomized, and 73 received the assigned treatment and were included in the final analysis cohort. Study accrual began on June 20, 2017, and enrollment was completed in June 2024. The prespecified postoperative follow-up period extended beyond 24 months, with a study data cutoff date of June 30, 2025. Data collection for the primary and secondary outcomes has been completed, with final expected results anticipated in January 2027.

CONCLUSIONS: This randomized phase 2 trial was designed to assess whether short-term androgen pathway inhibition can improve postoperative functional outcomes while maintaining oncologic outcomes in men undergoing nerve-sparing RP for high-risk localized PCa.

articles.title: Generation of Case-Based Materials Using Large Language Models in Health Professions Education: Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate case-based materials for health professions education (HPE). Previous reviews have examined broad applications in HPE or focused on clinical cases, but none have comprehensively synthesized the generation and evaluation of diverse case-based materials.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to synthesize current evidence on LLM-generated case-based materials in HPE, focusing on generation approaches, evaluation methods, key findings, and reported challenges.

METHODS: This scoping review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) reporting guidelines. Seven databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, ERIC, and IEEE Xplore) were searched on May 10, 2026, for studies published from January 1, 2017. Eligible studies were peer-reviewed original research articles, published in English, reporting the use of generative LLMs to create text-based case-based materials for HPE. Data were synthesized using descriptive statistics and narrative synthesis.

RESULTS: Seventy-two studies were included. Most were published between 2024 and 2026 (67/72, 93%) and focused on medical education (59/72, 82%), with undergraduate students as the most frequently studied population. Case-based multiple-choice questions (MCQs; 28/72, 39%) and clinical cases or vignettes (22/72, 30%) were the most frequently generated materials. Generative Pretrained Transformer-4 (GPT-4) family models were the most commonly used (40/72, 55%), and generation predominantly relied on relatively simple prompting approaches, whereas more advanced strategies, such as few-shot prompting, prompt chaining, or use of external knowledge sources, were rarely adopted. Evaluation primarily relied on expert review, typically involving small panels, while student assessment (25/72, 35%) and psychometric analyses were less common. Overall, LLM-generated materials were frequently judged to be clinically plausible, structurally clear, and reasonably aligned with educational objectives, particularly after refinement. However, consistent limitations included factual inaccuracies, construction flaws, superficial clinical realism, pedagogical misalignment, suboptimal psychometric performance, and bias. No LLM consistently outperformed others, although methodological heterogeneity limits cross-study comparisons.

CONCLUSIONS: This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of the literature on LLM-generated case-based materials in HPE. Unlike previous reviews examining broad educational applications or focusing on clinical cases, it integrates evidence across a broad range of case-based materials while synthesizing generation methods, evaluation approaches, reported findings, and challenges. The evidence suggests that LLMs can support the development of case-based materials but still require expert oversight because of recurring concerns regarding clinical accuracy, educational quality, psychometric performance, clinical realism, and bias. By identifying methodological and evidence gaps, this review provides educators, curriculum developers, and researchers with a structured overview of this rapidly evolving field and may inform the development of more robust generation workflows, more standardized evaluation approaches, and the responsible use of LLM-generated case-based materials in HPE.

articles.title: Improving CommonGround, an Online Peer Support Intervention for People Living With Long-Term Physical Health Conditions and Subthreshold Depression: Theory of Change-Informed Qualitative Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: People living with long-term physical health conditions who are also experiencing subthreshold depression are at risk of developing major depression. In partnership with lived experience experts, clinicians, and software developers, we co-designed CommonGround, an online peer support and psychoeducation platform. CommonGround's Theory of Change (ToC) was also conceptualized to outline the intermediate outcomes (and associated indicators of whether such outcomes are achieved) needed to improve the mental health of the target population.

OBJECTIVE: This qualitative study, informed by the ToC, aimed to examine the acceptability, usability, and intervention mechanisms of CommonGround and ultimately refine the ToC and corresponding intervention design ahead of definitive evaluation.

METHODS: A nested qualitative study was conducted within a remote, 12-week feasibility randomized controlled trial comparing CommonGround (intervention group) to signposting to National Health Service (NHS) web pages (control group). Thirty-nine participants were purposively sampled and interviewed within 6 weeks postintervention about their experiences of CommonGround and trial participation. The interview schedule and thematic framework analysis were rooted in a pretrial ToC while being responsive to emergent themes.

RESULTS: Evaluating the assumptions and intermediate outcomes (via their indicators) refined our understanding of how CommonGround may support mental well-being. Overall, participants viewed CommonGround as an appropriate, safe space to access self-management information and support from others with a unique shared understanding of chronic illness. However, many participants felt more time was needed for genuine social relations to form and community culture to evolve. Anonymity helped foster a sense of safety but, for some participants, limited the formation of genuine connections. Other factors contributing to low engagement included personal circumstances (eg, limited time). Key suggestions for future development included creating a mobile app that would be easier and more intuitive to access and navigate.

CONCLUSIONS: CommonGround was considered an acceptable and appropriate space to access peer support, with the potential to positively impact psychological well-being by fostering shared understanding, support, and knowledge exchange. Beyond informing the future evaluation of CommonGround in a definitive trial, the refined ToC identifies the key preconditions, intermediate outcomes, and associated indicators, and assumptions that may underpin the acceptability and usability of digital peer support interventions in achieving their intended outcomes. We also demonstrate how evaluating and refining components of the ToC after the intervention had been implemented in the trial enabled a more nuanced understanding of how and why the intervention may work, for whom, under what circumstances, and informed changes to improve the co-designed intervention.

articles.title: Electrospun Janus Nanofibrous Membranes for Diabetic Foot Ulcers: Structure-Function Relationships and Multifunctional Synergistic Therapy.
articles.abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are critical chronic diabetic complications that remain difficult to heal owing to excessive exudation, persistent infection, prolonged inflammation, oxidative stress, and impaired tissue regeneration. Conventional wound dressings often fail to address these interconnected pathological conditions. Electrospun Janus nanofibrous membranes (JNMs) with asymmetric structures offer unique opportunities to spatially regulate the wound microenvironment while integrating multiple therapeutic functions within a single platform. This review summarizes recent advances in electrospun JNMs for DFU treatment from the perspective of structure-function relationships. The fabrication methods and structural design principles of JNMs, including asymmetric wettability, pore structures, interfacial functionalization, and spatial therapeutic distribution are first discussed. The relationships between these structural characteristics and key functional properties, including directional exudate transport, controlled therapeutic delivery, antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity, mechanical adaptability, and microenvironment regulation, are then analyzed. Subsequently, the therapeutic applications of JNMs in DFU management, together with recent developments in stimuli-responsive and bioelectronic systems, are reviewed. Finally, current challenges related to mechanical and structural stability, degradation-regeneration compatibility, scalable manufacturing, biosafety, standardized evaluation, and clinical translation are discussed. By linking DFU-specific pathological requirements with JNM structural design, functional regulation, and therapeutic outcomes, this review provides a framework for the rational development of multifunctional Janus dressings for DFU treatment.

articles.title: Dietary Vitamin K2 Intake, Musculoskeletal Injury, and Cardiometabolic Health in Service Members.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vitamin K2 (K2) research has demonstrated that with sufficient K2 intake, vitamin K-dependent proteins are activated to regulate bone diseases and inflammation-related diseases, offering an innovative strategy to address ongoing musculoskeletal injury (MSKi) and high adiposity challenges that threaten health promotion, performance, and readiness in service members (SMs).

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to characterize K2 status in a military sample and explore the relationship between dietary K2 intake and bone health, metabolic health, and inflammation status in the context of SM health and operational readiness or deployability.

METHODS: At baseline and 12 months, Army and Air Force units provided data from demographic and food frequency questionnaires, body composition, bone density, cardiometabolic, and biomarker measurements. Activity trackers monitored physical activity and sleep duration continuously.

RESULTS: Between August 2023 and July 2024, we enrolled 47 active duty SMs. The sample was predominantly male, racially and ethnically diverse, averaged 27 years of age, and had an average of 6.5 years of service. At baseline, 45% met the criteria for stage I hypertension and 45% exceeded military body fat standards. Participants reported insufficient baseline dietary intake of vitamin K1+K2 and vitamin D. Over the 12 months, fermented food consumption slightly increased, activity behaviors remained unchanged, and participants self-reported 10 noncombat MSKis. Participants reported no significant changes in body composition, body fat specifically, or dietary intake of vitamin D or vitamin K2. Exploratory proteomics analysis identified links between K2 and inflammation, bone architecture, glucose homeostasis, and insulin receptors.

DISCUSSION: MSKi, high body fat, and meeting optimal nutrition goals remain readiness challenges for SMs. Exploring K2 identified meaningful metrics and actionable strategies to address these challenges. Highlighting data-informed interventions adds to nursing's nutritional and cardiometabolic knowledge base and clinical interventions, as the nursing workforce is positioned to influence every step of patient care: conducting research, generating data to inform clinical practice and interventions, and ensuring evidence-based patient education and counseling to optimize SM health and readiness.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Radiofrequency Renal Denervation in the United States: Six-Month Primary End Point Results From the SPYRAL AFFIRM Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radiofrequency renal denervation (RDN) is a guideline-recommended therapy for uncontrolled hypertension. SPYRAL AFFIRM is a single-arm, postapproval study assessing the efficacy and safety of radiofrequency RDN using the Symplicity Spyral catheter. We report the 6-month primary end point results in the SPYRAL AFFIRM US population.

METHODS: Enrolled patients had an office systolic/diastolic blood pressure (BP) ≥140/90 mm Hg and a home systolic BP ≥135 mm Hg. Patients with type 1 diabetes, poorly controlled type 2 diabetes (HbA1c >8.0%), or an estimated glomerular filtration rate <45 mL/min per 1.73 m2 were excluded. The primary end point was the 6-month change in office systolic BP from baseline compared with a prespecified performance goal (-6.0 mm Hg).

RESULTS: Among 594 patients treated in the AFFIRM study from 73 US clinical sites, baseline clinical characteristics included: mean (±SD) age, 57±12 years; female, 45%; African American, 27%; Hispanic, 11%; type 2 diabetes, 19%; and mean estimated glomerular filtration rate, 79±20 mL/min per 1.73m2. Baseline systolic/diastolic office, home, and 24-hour ambulatory BP (mm Hg) were 169±21/106±13, 158±17/101±13, and 151±18/96±13, respectively. Patients were prescribed an average of 3.6±2.0 antihypertensive medications at baseline that remained unchanged through 6 months. Six months after RDN, the change in systolic BP (mm Hg) was -18.2±22.0, -9.4±13.8, and -9.7±16.8 for office, home, and 24-hour ambulatory measures, respectively (P<0.001 compared with baseline). Adverse clinical events through 6 months were uncommon.

CONCLUSIONS: In this US postapproval study, the primary end point was met with significant BP reductions following radiofrequency RDN consistent across different measures. In a broader patient population with uncontrolled hypertension, these results reaffirm the safety and efficacy of radiofrequency RDN.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT05198674.

articles.title: Ocular Considerations for the Department of War's New Testosterone Initiative.
articles.abstract: On 15 July 2026, the Secretary of War announced that the Department of War will begin annual testosterone deficiency screening for male Active Duty and Reserve Component personnel aged 30 and older as part of the periodic health assessment, with screening available on request to younger servicemembers. This policy will increase testosterone testing and may increase testosterone replacement therapy (TRT). Primary care, flight, and operational medicine providers will be on the front line of a hormonal intervention with possible ocular implications. This Commentary summarizes the ophthalmic manifestations of low and elevated testosterone states relevant to a military population and proposes pragmatic recommendations for providers implementing this initiative. Screening identifies testosterone concentrations, not symptoms of deficiency, and should not be equated with an indication for treatment. Androgen deficiency is associated with meibomian gland dysfunction and evaporative dry eye, but benefit from replacement remains unproven. The evidence linking testosterone exposure to central serous chorioretinopathy, retinal vascular occlusion, and intracranial hypertension is real but heterogeneous. Cohort findings, case reports, and observations in transgender patients do not establish a common risk in hypogonadal male servicemembers. Glaucoma findings are similarly mixed. We propose a brief, targeted ocular history, symptom counseling and inquiry during TRT follow-up and periodic health assessments, and referral according to clinical urgency. For vision-critical specialties, baseline dilated examination should be coordinated through existing occupational clearance processes when an adequate recent examination is unavailable. These measures are precautionary; screening benefit and an optimal repeat-examination interval have not been established. The Military Health System is uniquely positioned to prospectively answer the ocular questions this literature has only partially resolved.

articles.title: The influence of ensemble size and composition on the performance of combined real-time COVID-19 forecasts.
articles.abstract: During infectious disease outbreaks, short-term forecasts can play an important role for both decision makers and the general public. While previous research has shown that combining individual forecasts into an ensemble improves accuracy and consistency, practical guidance for organisers of multi-model prediction platforms on how to construct an ensemble has been scarce. In particular, it is not entirely clear how ensemble performance relates to the size of the underlying model pool, a relevant question when relying on voluntary contributions from modelling teams that face competing priorities. Furthermore, the exact composition of an ensemble forecast may influence its performance. Ensembles can either include all models equally or, alternatively, discriminate based on past performance or other characteristics. Using data from the European COVID-19 Forecast Hub we investigated these questions, with the aim of offering practical guidance to organisers of multi-model prediction platforms during infectious disease outbreaks. We found that including more models both improved and stabilised aggregate ensemble performance, while selecting for better component models did not yield any particular advantage. Diversity among models, whether measured numerically or qualitatively, did not have a clear impact on ensemble performance. These results suggest that for those soliciting contributions to collaborative ensembles there are more obvious gains to be made from increasing participation to moderate levels than from optimising component models.

articles.title: Risk of cardiovascular events and mortality associated with LDL and non-HDL cholesterol levels after statin initiation for primary prevention: A multiregional cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The cardiovascular and mortality benefits of achieving guideline-recommended concentrations of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) and non-high-density lipoprotein (non-HDL) cholesterol with statins in primary prevention remain uncertain.

METHODS AND FINDINGS: In this new-user cohort study, we used electronic healthcare databases from Hong Kong (HK), New Zealand (NZ) and the United Kingdom (UK) to identify 185,237 patients initiating statins between 1 January 2007 and 31 December 2012 (with follow-up to 31 December 2017) without atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure, or chronic kidney disease. Associations between LDL and non-HDL cholesterol measured within 2 years post-initiation with the outcomes of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) or all-cause mortality were assessed in landmark analyses using multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, hypertension, atrial fibrillation, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidaemia, obesity, smoking, alcohol misuse, rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus and connective tissue disorders, severe mental illness, antihypertensive drugs, antidiabetic drugs, antiplatelet drugs, and anticoagulant drugs. Estimates were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. At 2 years, LDL cholesterol was <1.4 mmol/L in 7,084 (3.8%), 1.4-1.7 mmol/L in 21,893 (11.8%), 1.8-2.5 mmol/L in 81,941 (44.2%) and ≥2.6 mmol/L in 74,294 (40.1%) patients. Mean duration of follow-up for the primary outcome of MACE was 6.5 years in HK, 5.6 years in NZ and 5.4 years in UK. versus an LDL cholesterol ≥2.6 mmol/L, adjusted hazard ratios (HR) for MACE were 0.80 (95% CI [0.77,0.83]) for 1.8-2.5 mmol/L, 0.79 (0.66,0.94) for 1.4-1.7 mmol/L and 0.82 (0.60,1.12) for <1.4 mmol/L. Non-HDL cholesterol showed similar estimates for MACE (e.g., HR 0.75, [0.72,0.79] for 2.6-3.3 mmol/L versus ≥3.4 mmol/L). In continuous analysis, the association with MACE was approximately log-linear across achieved LDL and non-HDL cholesterol in HK and the UK, whereas in NZ estimates were less consistent and imprecise at the lowest concentrations. After adjustment for confounding factors, very low LDL (HR 1.06, [0.96,1.16]) and non-HDL cholesterol (HR 0.98, [0.84,1.14]) were not associated with all-cause mortality. Limitations include heterogeneity across cohorts, which may reflect confounding by indication where treatment intensity was guided by cardiovascular risk, and residual confounding from comorbidities, lifestyle interventions and disease severity. Estimates are also conditional on patients having initiated statins, survived to the landmark, and undergone follow-up lipid testing.

CONCLUSIONS: Lower achieved LDL and non-HDL cholesterol after statin initiation was associated with a reduction in MACE, with limited evidence of an increase in all-cause mortality at very low concentrations after adjustment for confounding. Additional reductions in cardiovascular events could be obtained by achieving guideline-recommended non-HDL cholesterol levels of at least <3.4 mmol/L after statin initiation for primary prevention.

articles.title: T-cell-mediated immunodeficiency caused by anti-interferon-γ autoantibodies promotes the pathogenesis of Talaromycosis marneffei.
articles.abstract: Anti-interferon-γ autoantibody (AIGA)-associated adult-onset immunodeficiency is an important underlying condition in patients with severe talaromycosis caused by Talaromyces marneffei, but the mechanisms underlying impaired antifungal immunity remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to define the contributions of CD4⁺ T cells, CD8⁺ T cells, and IFN-γ-dependent immune signaling to host defense against T. marneffei. We used an intranasal BALB/c mouse infection model with antibody-mediated CD4⁺ T-cell depletion, CD8⁺ T-cell depletion, or IFN-γ neutralization, together with immunological assays using sera from AIGA-positive patients and healthy controls. In mice, T. marneffei infection induced stronger and more sustained T-cell activation in the lungs than in the spleen, with pulmonary CD4⁺ T-cell activation representing the predominant response and CD8⁺ T cells showing distinct temporal kinetics. Depletion of CD4⁺ or CD8⁺ T cells, or blockade of IFN-γ, impaired body-weight recovery and reduced survival, aggravated pulmonary and splenic injury, and delayed fungal clearance. In clinical immunological assays involving 28 AIGA-positive patients and 30 healthy controls, depletion of IgG from AIGA-positive sera restored IFN-γ⁺TNF-α⁺ CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T-cell responses toward healthy-control levels, suggesting that patient IgG suppresses T-cell cytokine responses. AIGA-positive sera contained IgG that bound IFN-γ and attenuated IFN-γ-induced STAT1 phosphorylation and HLA-DR upregulation in THP-1 cells, supporting functional neutralization of IFN-γ signaling and impaired antigen-presenting cell activation. Together, these findings indicate that AIGA-associated talaromycosis involves impaired IFN-γ-dependent coordination of innate effector functions and T-cell responses. Clinically, they support consideration of AIGA-associated adult-onset immunodeficiency in HIV-negative patients with severe or disseminated talaromycosis, particularly in endemic regions, and provide a rationale for future studies aimed at restoring IFN-γ bioactivity.

articles.title: Parent Anxiety and Response to a Telehealth Intervention for Hypoglycemia Fear: Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Parents of young children with type 1 diabetes (T1D) frequently report fear of hypoglycemia (FH), which can impact their diabetes management. REDCHiP (Reducing Emotional Distress for Childhood Hypoglycemia in Parents) is a telehealth-delivered cognitive behavioral intervention shown to reduce FH, but less is known about which parents benefit most.

OBJECTIVE: This secondary analysis examined whether pretreatment parent anxiety moderated REDCHiP's effects and explored responder patterns by intervention arm and pretreatment anxiety.

METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of a large, randomized clinical trial comparing REDCHiP to an attention control condition (ATTN). We assessed outcomes before treatment (time 1) and 3 months after treatment (time 3). Our primary outcome was parental FH at time 3, adjusted for time 1 FH. The original trial used validated measures of parent FH and general anxiety. We evaluated parent anxiety at time 1 as both a categorical variable (clinically elevated or not) and a continuous variable (centered). We defined responders as parents achieving a reduction of ≥0.5 SDs in FH from time 1 to time 3. An analysis of covariance tested the treatment arm by anxiety interaction, with sensitivity analyses modeling anxiety continuously.

RESULTS: There was no significant treatment arm by anxiety interaction when modeling parent anxiety as either a categorical or continuous variable (P>.05). However, exploratory analyses found that the adjusted mean time 3 FH was numerically lower among REDCHiP parents than ATTN parents with clinically elevated anxiety. Among parents with elevated anxiety, 78.6% (22/28) of REDCHiP parents met our responder criterion compared with 47.4% (9/19) of ATTN parents. Among parents with elevated anxiety, the adjusted odds of meeting the responder criterion were higher for REDCHiP than ATTN parents (odds ratio 6.35, 95% CI 1.47-29.00).

CONCLUSIONS: While time 1 parent anxiety did not significantly moderate treatment response, exploratory analyses suggested a potentially meaningful pattern among parents with clinically elevated anxiety. As telehealth-delivered behavioral interventions expand in pediatric type 1 diabetes care, secondary analyses of participant characteristics may help guide targeted implementation and enhance treatment benefit.

articles.title: Bile Acid-Activated IRE1α Pathway Promotes NK Cell-Mediated Cholangiocyte Injury in Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis.
articles.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease characterized by progressive bile duct inflammation and fibrosis. Despite its significant clinical burden, the molecular mechanisms underlying PSC pathogenesis remain poorly understood, limiting therapeutic options. Here, we integrated bioinformatic analyses of transcriptomic datasets with experimental validation in a bile duct ligation mouse model and in vitro cell systems. Differential gene expression, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and Mendelian randomization were performed to identify key molecular signatures. Single-cell RNA sequencing characterized cellular heterogeneity. The IRE1α-NK cell axis was validated using pharmacological inhibition, siRNA knockdown, and NK cell depletion approaches in bile acid-treated NK cells, co-culture systems, and a mouse model of cholestatic bile duct injury. We identified Endoplasmic Reticulum To Nucleus Signaling 1 (ERN1, also as a key mediator in PSC pathogenesis, with causal relationships to disease risk. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed significant NK cell enrichment in PSC samples. In both the bile duct ligation mouse model and in vitro systems, bile acids induced IRE1α pathway activation in NK cells, leading to enhanced cytotoxicity against cholangiocytes. Pharmacological inhibition or genetic knockdown of IRE1α prevented bile acid-induced NK cell activation and cytotoxicity. In vivo, both IRE1α inhibition and NK cell depletion attenuated liver injury, inflammation, and fibrosis in the mouse model. Our data suggest a novel pathogenic mechanism in PSC involving bile acid-induced IRE1α activation in NK cells, promoting cholangiocyte injury. The IRE1α-NK cell axis represents a promising therapeutic target for PSC treatment.

articles.title: Immunity and vaccines for cryptosporidiosis.
articles.abstract: Cryptosporidiosis contributes significantly to global morbidity and mortality, particularly among children <2 years old in resource-poor countries. Host immunity is critical in limiting infection, and natural Cryptosporidium infection confers protection against subsequent disease, suggesting that effective vaccination is biologically achievable. Both innate and adaptive immune responses are important in clearing and preventing infection. Therefore, an ideal vaccine would stimulate both innate and adaptive immune responses, including those in the intestinal mucosa.

articles.title: Large Peritoneal Macrophages influence CD8+ T cell activation and parasite control during acute Trypanosoma cruzi infection.
articles.abstract: Resident peritoneal macrophages consist of two subpopulations with distinct origin, sizes and phenotype named Large Peritoneal Macrophages (LPMs) and Small Peritoneal Macrophages (SPMs). While LPMs are long-live cells that origin in embryonic yolk sac and can self-replenish after mild loss, SPMs are short-live cells that derive from blood monocytes and are in continuous replenishment. Under homeostasis, LPMs constitute more than 70% of total CD11b+ cells, but during infection or inflammation drastically dampen. As LPMs have been reported to be essential for CD8+ T cell priming and replication control in parasite infections, we aimed to study their role in the context of Chagas' disease. We observed a reduction in LPMs during acute phase of T. cruzi infection in BALB/c mice that did not restore in chronic phase. Instead, this subset was replaced by a population with intermediate expression of F4/80, previously described as 'inflammatory macrophages', but with a mixed phenotype activation in this case. Besides, this F4/80int population could also be associated with truncated maturation of monocytes to resident macrophages. In this work, LPMs showed higher CD80+ and lower PD-L1+ cells frequencies and produced more IL-12 and TNF than SPMs. This profile may favor CD8+ T-cell activation, reflected by increased CD69 expression and Perforin/Granzyme B production. Replenishment of LPMs by adoptive transfer of PEMs was associated with reduced parasitemia and enhanced splenic CD8+ T-cell activation. Thus, LPMs may contribute to CD8+ T-cell responses and parasite control during acute T. cruzi infection.

articles.title: Depressive Symptoms and Central Obesity Over the Menopausal Transition and the Development of Type 2 Diabetes Later in Life: Decomposing Direct and Indirect Effects.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the association between depressive symptoms during the menopausal transition and subsequent incident type 2 diabetes (T2D), with particular focus on: (1) quantifying the mediating role of central obesity in this association, and (2) examining differential effects by depressive symptom subscales (somatic vs. cognitive/affective symptoms).

METHODS: We analyzed data from 1719 participants in the Study of Women's Health Across the Nation, a multi-ethnic cohort study of midlife women. Depressive symptoms were assessed repeatedly using the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D). We calculated the total and subscales of depressive symptom burden during the menopausal transition. Causal mediation analysis within a counterfactual framework was employed to decompose the total effect between depressive symptoms and incident T2D during postmenopausal follow-up into natural direct effects (NDE) and indirect effects (NIE) mediated through central obesity measured at the first postmenopausal visit, adjusting for demographic, lifestyle, and health-related covariates.

RESULTS: During a mean postmenopausal follow-up of 11.60 (SD 3.58) years, 170 women (9.89%) developed T2D during follow-up. Central obesity mediated 21.4-23.5% of the total effect of depressive symptoms burden on T2D risk. Somatic subscales of CES-D scores showed strongest associations (OR=1.272 (95% CI:1.041-1.567) and NIE OR=1.100 (1.040-1.165)) in unadjusted models, with 21.3-25.0% mediated through central obesity after full adjustment. Cognitive/affective subscale showed weaker mediation effects (19.4-26.9%). Sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness to unmeasured confounding, with somatic symptom effects remaining significant under moderate confounding (NIE OR= 1.057 (95% CI:1.004-1.115)).

CONCLUSIONS: Greater cumulative depressive symptom burden during the menopausal transition, particularly somatic subscales, was associated with higher odds of incident T2D after postmenopause, with part of the association mediated through central obesity at postmenopause. These findings highlight the menopausal transition as a critical period for interventions targeting both mental health and metabolic risk factors.

articles.title: Diffusion Transformer Meets Heat Masks: An Advanced PET Reconstruction Framework.
articles.journal: IEEE transactions on image processing : a publication of the IEEE Signal Processing Society
articles.abstract: Deep learning has contributed to advances in PET image reconstruction, with reported improvements in image quality through direct training on sinogram or image data. Traditional methods often utilize masks for inpainting tasks, and their incorporation into PET reconstruction frameworks may also benefit PET reconstruction. In this study, we propose a PET reconstruction framework called Diffusion tRansformer mEets heAt Masks (DREAM), which integrates mask mechanisms into both the sino-gram domain and latent space. The framework employs a high-dimensional stacking approach to expand the solution space and designs a mask-driven latent space that is intended to accelerate the diffusion process by leveraging compact priors. Initially, this study introduces a random mask (DREAM-RM) strategy combined with hierarchical learning, which guides the model from focusing on fine-grained local details to capturing broader global patterns. Furthermore, guided by the physical characteristics of PET data, this study extends this framework through the heat mask (DREAM-HM) algorithm. By explicitly decoupling sino-gram data into hot and cold channels based on intensity thresholds and employing a hot-cold mutual mask (HCMM) strategy, DREAM-HM is designed to improve the information distribution between regions of interest and the background. Experimental results indicate that DREAM, particularly the HM variant, improves reconstructed-image quality and preserves clinically relevant details under the evaluated conditions, suggesting its potential utility for PET image reconstruction. The open-source code is available at: https://github.com/yqx7150/DREAM.

articles.title: Concurrent Triple-class Psychotropic Use and Postoperative Morbidity Following Single-Level Lumbar Fusion: A Propensity Score-matched Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether triple-class psychotropic exposure before single-level lumbar fusion is associated with different postoperative outcomes than selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) monotherapy in patients carrying a psychiatric diagnosis.

SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: Psychiatric illness is common before spine surgery and associated with inferior outcomes, but is usually analyzed as a single categorical variable. Whether regimen complexity carries independent prognostic information is unclear.

METHODS: Adults with a psychotic-spectrum or mood disorder (ICD-10-CM, F20-F39) undergoing primary single-level posterior lumbar arthrodesis were identified in TriNetX. Exposure was ascertained 365 to 1 day preoperatively; postoperative prescriptions did not contribute. Patients receiving an SSRI, benzodiazepine and antipsychotic were matched 1:1 on 75 preoperative characteristics to SSRI monotherapy. Pseudarthrosis and surgical site infection were co-primary outcomes; revision, readmission, emergency department visits and opioid use were secondary, assessed at 3 and 6 months and 1, 3 and 5 years (Bonferroni P<0.025).

RESULTS: Among 638 matched pairs, all but one characteristic achieved a standardized mean difference <0.10. Surgical site infection was more frequent at every interval (5 y, 14.73% vs 8.31%; RR 1.77, 95% CI 1.29-2.44; P=0.0003), as was readmission (5 y, 67.40% vs 57.99%; RR 1.16, 1.07-1.27; P=0.0005). Revision was approximately twofold higher from 1 year onward (5 y, 8.62% vs 4.39%; RR 1.96, 1.26-3.06; P=0.0022). Pseudarthrosis was more frequent at every interval but met the corrected threshold only at 1 year (16.87% vs 12.38%; RR 1.36, 1.04-1.78; P=0.0224). The proportion receiving any opioid was identical (97.49%).

CONCLUSION: Triple-class exposure was associated with higher infection, readmission and revision than SSRI monotherapy. These associations do not establish causation and may reflect illness severity, unmeasured surgical factors or detection bias. The regimen is a risk marker warranting closer perioperative surveillance, not a treatment target.

articles.title: Duodenal macrophages depletion and dysfunction contribute to gut barrier dysfunction in alcohol use disorder.
articles.abstract: In alcohol use disorder (AUD), duodenal macrophage number are reduced, but the underlying mechanisms and consequences for gut permeability remain unknown. Actively drinking AUD patients undergoing standardized inpatient detoxification and healthy controls were enrolled. Fasting blood samples and duodenal biopsies were analyzed using proteomics, histology, multiplex immunohistofluorescence, flow cytometry, and quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Circulating monocytes were differentiated ex vivo into macrophages to assess migration, differentiation, phagocytosis, and cytokine release following stimulation with bacterial products. Gut permeability was evaluated using urinary 51Chromium- ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid excretion, and plasma surrogate markers of microbial translocation. AUD patients showed markedly reduced duodenal macrophages despite increased circulating monocytes and tissue monocyte-attracting chemokines. AUD monocytes exhibited reduced CCR2 expression and downregulation of tissue proteins involved in adhesion and trans-endothelial migration, thereby decreasing mucosal infiltration. Early macrophage differentiation associated was impaired, with reduced CSF1, CSF2, IL-34, and CSF1 receptor expression. Despite preserved phagocytic capacity, residual tissue macrophages displayed a mixed immune phenotype with reduced expression of scavenger receptors involved in microbial responses and cytokine hyporesponsiveness to lipopolysaccharide and peptidoglycan. Reduced macrophage numbers correlated with increased intestinal permeability and markers of microbial translocation. These results link disruption of the duodenal monocyte-macrophage axis to intestinal barrier failure in AUD.

articles.title: Articular involvement in antiphospholipid syndrome: Clinical, laboratory, and imaging characterization.
articles.abstract: IntroductionAntiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is characterized by antiphospholipid antibodies (aPL) and thrombotic and/or obstetric events. Musculoskeletal manifestations, particularly arthralgia, are frequently reported, although their clinical and pathophysiological correlates remain incompletely characterized.ObjectiveTo characterize the clinical, laboratory, and imaging features of articular involvement in primary and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)-associated APS compared with healthy controls.MethodsThis cross-sectional study included 99 participants aged 18-50 years: 38 with primary APS (PAPS), 26 with APS associated with SLE (APS/SLE), and 35 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. APS patients fulfilled the Sydney classification criteria, and those with SLE were classified according to the 1997 American College of Rheumatology criteria. Arthralgia was clinically assessed. Radiographic and high-resolution ultrasound (US) evaluation of the hands and wrists was performed. Laboratory tests included erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), rheumatoid factor (RF), and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP) antibodies.ResultsAge was comparable across groups (p = 0.206). In the comparative analysis of aPL profiles between PAPS and APS/SLE, lupus anticoagulant was the most prevalent antibody in both groups (94.7% vs 96.2%; p = 0.792). IgG anticardiolipin and anti-β2-glycoprotein I antibodies were more frequent in PAPS (42.1% vs 15.4%, p = 0.024; 32.4% vs 0%, p = 0.019). Arthralgia was more frequent in APS/SLE than in PAPS (80.8% vs 50%; p = 0.013), as was morning stiffness (46.2% vs 21.1%; p = 0.033). ESR levels were higher in APS/SLE compared with PAPS and controls (median 19.5 vs 14 vs 6 mm/h; p < 0.001). CRP levels did not differ significantly among groups (p = 0.118). RF positivity was low (2.6% in PAPS) and did not differ among groups (p = 1.000), and anti-CCP IgG antibodies were absent in all groups. Radiographic findings were mild and comparable. On US, joint effusion was more frequent in APS/SLE than in PAPS and controls (26.9% vs 2.6% vs 2.9%, respectively; p = 0.001), whereas synovitis, tenosynovitis, Power Doppler signal, and other findings showed no significant differences.ConclusionArticular manifestations are common in APS, particularly in APS/SLE, but are not consistently supported by objective evidence of inflammation. This dissociation suggests that musculoskeletal involvement may not be primarily mediated by overt inflammatory mechanisms.

articles.title: Intrastromal Antibiotic Therapy for Recalcitrant Bacterial Keratitis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the safety and efficacy of adjunctive intrastromal vancomycin and meropenem for the treatment of recalcitrant bacterial keratitis.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center, retrospective, non-comparative cohort study of consecutive patients with recalcitrant bacterial keratitis treated at a major tertiary center between January 2022 and April 2026. We included adults with suspected or culture‑proven bacterial keratitis failing topical therapy and meeting inclusion criteria. All underwent corneal scraping and adjunctive intrastromal vancomycin (5 mg/mL) and meropenem (20 mg/mL) using a circumferential barrage technique. Repeat injection at 48 hours was determined by a senior corneal specialist according to clinical response. The primary outcome was clinical resolution. Secondary outcomes included epithelial healing, reinjection, and complications.

RESULTS: Twenty eyes of 20 patients were included. At 28 days, 19/20 eyes (95%) achieved clinical resolution of stromal infiltrate and infection. Epithelial defects were present in 18/20 (90%) at baseline, with size reduction in 15/18 (75%) at early follow-up (median 2 days). Median time to complete epithelial healing was 12 weeks (range 10-16 weeks). Six eyes (30%) required reinjection. One eye progressed to perforation requiring penetrating keratoplasty. No direct injection-related adverse events were observed. Gram-positive organisms predominated (13/20, 65%), with polymicrobial infection in 3/20 (15%) and no growth in 3/20 (15%) cases.

CONCLUSIONS: Adjunctive intrastromal antibiotic therapy achieved a high rate of infection resolution in this cohort of recalcitrant bacterial keratitis, with a low complication rate. This approach may be considered in refractory cases or when unable to utilize conventional topical therapy. However, further evaluation of its role is needed in larger comparative studies.

articles.title: Choosing Between On-Pump and Off-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: Contemporary Evidence for Patient Selection and Clinical Decision-Making.
articles.abstract: On-pump (ONCAB) and off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OPCAB) remain established approaches to surgical myocardial revascularization, but contemporary evidence does not support a universal preference for either technique. The clinically relevant question is which patient and operative setting are most likely to benefit from each strategy. We performed a contemporary narrative evidence synthesis of landmark randomized trials, long-term follow-up studies, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, observational cohorts, graft-patency studies, and major coronary revascularization guidelines. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched for studies published from 2009 through 2025. Evidence was organized around perioperative neurologic, renal, bleeding, and respiratory outcomes; completeness of revascularization; graft patency; conversion to cardiopulmonary bypass; surgical experience; and long-term survival. No de novo meta-analysis was performed, and all pooled estimates reported in this review are explicitly attributed to previously published evidence syntheses. Randomized evidence indicates broadly similar long-term mortality between OPCAB and ONCAB, whereas OPCAB may reduce selected perioperative complications, particularly stroke, transfusion, acute kidney injury, and respiratory morbidity in appropriately selected patients. Conversely, complex coronary anatomy may favor ONCAB because a stable operative field can facilitate complete revascularization. Conversion from OPCAB to cardiopulmonary bypass is consistently associated with worse outcomes, underscoring the importance of surgeon and institutional experience. Graft-patency differences are most evident for saphenous vein grafts and technically challenging territories. Anaortic or no-touch OPCAB may be particularly valuable in patients with extensive ascending-aortic atherosclerosis. ONCAB and OPCAB should therefore be viewed as complementary strategies. Selection should integrate aortic pathology, ventricular function, renal and bleeding risk, coronary complexity, the probability of complete revascularization, and local OPCAB expertise. A patient-tailored framework can help translate heterogeneous comparative evidence into practical clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Prior Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting and Its Impact on Lesion Complexity, Procedural Characteristics, and Outcomes in Chronic Total Occlusion Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Prior coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is associated with accelerated native vessel atherosclerosis and more complex chronic total occlusion (CTO) anatomy, rendering CTO-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) more challenging despite contemporary technical advances. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to compare CTO lesion characteristics, procedural demands, and in-hospital outcomes according to prior CABG status. PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar were systematically searched from inception through May 15, 2026, for studies comparing CTO-PCI outcomes in patients with and without prior CABG. Data were pooled using odds ratios (ORs) and standardized mean differences (SMDs). Twelve studies enrolling 47,434 patients, including 10,354 with prior CABG, were included. Compared with patients without prior CABG, those with prior CABG had higher rates of blunt stump morphology (OR 1.51 [1.42-1.61]), proximal cap ambiguity (OR 1.55 [1.45-1.66]), calcification (OR 2.49 [2.22-2.79]), vessel bending (OR 2.27 [1.27-4.05]), distal cap bifurcation (OR 1.73 [1.51-1.98]), and higher Multicenter CTO Registry of Japan scores (SMD 0.48 [0.40-0.56]). Procedural burden was greater, with higher contrast use, longer fluoroscopy time and procedure duration, and greater stent use. Technical success (OR 0.63 [0.43-0.92]) and procedural success (OR 0.60 [0.53-0.69]) were lower in the prior CABG group. In-hospital mortality (OR 2.19), myocardial infarction (OR 2.29), and contrast-induced nephropathy (OR 1.97) were higher, whereas cardiac tamponade was less frequent (OR 0.37). Prior CABG is associated with substantially greater CTO complexity, procedural burden, and in-hospital risk, underscoring the need for careful procedural planning and individualized risk stratification in this population.
