articles.title: Count games not athletes? The problem of pseudoreplication when analysing small-sided team games.
articles.abstract: Small-sided games (SSG) are common across a number of team sports and are used for physical conditioning and technical and tactical skill acquisition purposes. As athletes within and between teams interact with each other due to the task structure, individual athletes' performances are inherently interdependent. Accordingly, measurements across athletes are correlated with each other and do not represent independent pieces of information. When data dependencies are not correctly analyzed, this can result in what is called pseudoreplication and lead to erroneous, overly liberal statistical inferences. To assess the magnitude of possible errors, a Monte Carlo simulation was performed comparing analyses using a repeated-measures ANOVA, a Friedman test, and a linear mixed-effects model (LMM). Only the LMM maintained the nominal Type-I error rate whereas increasing the dependency between data points led to large increases in Type-I error rates for the other two methods. A re-analysis of a published small-sided games study indicated high within-game correlations between athletes (ICC = 0.77). To assess the scope of pseudoreplication in SSG research, 102 studies from four leading sport science journals were surveyed. Over 66% of the studies showed indicators of possible pseudoreplication, whereas only 6% reported an appropriate analysis. Small-sided team games researchers accordingly need to be aware of pseudoreplication and how best to avoid this issue through appropriate statistical analysis methods discussed in the present work.

articles.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Cardiovascular Disease: A Review.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists have transformed the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity and have more recently demonstrated clinically important effects across the cardiometabolic spectrum, including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis, and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Earlier cardiovascular outcome trials established reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events by way of injectable forms in patients with diabetes, while newer evidence has expanded these findings to oral semaglutide and to other patient populations. This review summarizes the hepatic, cardiovascular, and heart-failure evidence for glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists-based therapies and discusses remaining clinical uncertainties and future directions.

articles.title: Context re-exposure during counterconditioning strengthens episodic memory for aversive and related positive events.
articles.abstract: Several clinical interventions rely on narrative reframing, whereby the outcome of an overly emotional memory is replaced with a more favourable one. Recently, concern has arisen that such interventions may not only alter elicited emotions, but also reduce the memory's accuracy or even promote false memories. However, the relative simplicity of memories induced in traditional fear-conditioning paradigms (e.g., a tone-shock association) makes it challenging to experimentally model narrative reframing or test episodic distortions. We therefore developed a paradigm using trial-unique, multimodal, and personally meaningful events to investigate whether episodic counterconditioning can modify the episodic and affective (i.e., psychophysiological and subjective) components of aversive memories through new associations with semantically related positive events. Specifically, we hypothesised that spatial overlap between the aversive and related positive events would strengthen memory for both episodes and alleviate affective responses. Healthy participants (N = 100) encoded 20 memories, each comprising a cue (neutral object image) followed by an aversive or neutral outcome (image-sound combination) presented in a context (background image). The following day, 10 aversive memories were counterconditioned by pairing their cues with a semantically related positive outcome, with half presented in the original context and the other half in a novel context. While counterconditioning successfully induced positive affect, it did not alleviate affective responses the next day. Nonetheless, spatial overlap strengthened episodic memory for both the aversive and positive events. Future research should test whether context re-exposure during psychotherapy can likewise improve the accuracy of autobiographical aversive memories.

articles.title: Synthetic immunological niche reveals early immune dysregulation and stratifies therapeutic response in type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract: In Type 1 Diabetes (T1D), disease onset and immunotherapy responses vary widely, reflecting heterogeneous stage-specific immune dysregulation that remains undefined. To investigate this heterogeneity, we engineered microporous polycaprolactone scaffolds that form synthetic immunological niches (INs) subcutaneously and capture tissue-associated systemic immune changes. Building on our prior demonstration of IN-based longitudinal T1D monitoring, we use multimodal IN profiling to define the immune changes underlying divergent disease trajectories and immunotherapy responses. In non-obese diabetic (NOD) mice, longitudinal transcriptomic profiling of IN identified early myeloid associated changes, followed by increasing T cell-associated dysregulation that distinguished progressors from non-progressors. An early-stage IN-based T1D gene signature stratified NOD progressors from non-progressors by 6 weeks of age and was conserved across human T1D tissues, distinguishing T1D from non-diabetic individuals in spleen and pancreatic lymph node samples, but not in peripheral blood. Signature-based stratification revealed macrophage-associated TNFα pathway enrichment in pancreas of NOD progressors, which was validated in human T1D islets. Given the heterogeneous response to anti-TNFα therapy, IN profiling identified genesets associated with anti-TNFα efficacy and generated a response score that prospectively distinguished treatment-sensitive from resistant mice. These findings establish IN as a platform for detecting stage-wise immune dysregulation and stratifying immunotherapy response in T1D.

articles.title: Natural killer cells from children with obesity exhibit a persistent 'trained' response to influenza.
articles.abstract: Children and adults living with obesity have more severe influenza A virus (IAV) infection, but the underlying mechanisms are unclear. Natural killer (NK) cells play a key role in the innate immune responses to IAV and clearance of IAV-infected cells. 'Trained immunity' of NK cells (and other innate immune cells) refers to an initial stimulus (i.e. obesity) inducing metabolic and epigenetic changes that make these cells hyperinflammatory upon restimulation (i.e. with IAV). Here, we tested whether obesity in children induces trained immunity in NK cells. We have show that NK cells from children with obesity have a hyperinflammatory 'trained' phenotype, with increased expression of activation markers TLR2, CCR2, TLR4, HLA-DR and CD11b compared to children without obesity. Furthermore, we have demonstrate that NK cells from children with obesity have a heightened ex vivo IFN-γ response to stimulation with IAV (A/Auckland/4/2009, H1N1 and HKx31, H3N2) and epigenetic changes consistent trained immunity. A decrease in BMI z-score following weight-management was not associated with a reduction in the IFN-γ response, suggesting that weight loss is not sufficient to normalise NK cell function. Better understanding of obesity-related immune modulation is critical for development of new therapeutic strategies and improving outcomes in future IAV pandemics.

articles.title: The Relationship Between Leader Efficacy, Emotional Intelligence, and Transformational Leadership Among Physician Assistant Program Directors.
articles.journal: The journal of physician assistant education : the official journal of the Physician Assistant Education Association
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Transformational leadership is espoused as one of the most effective leadership styles, particularly in its positive associations with increasing employee motivation, creativity, performance, and job satisfaction. This study examined the relationship between leader efficacy, emotional intelligence, years of experience, and transformational leadership among physician assistant (PA) program directors.

METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was emailed to PA program directors across the United States. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics to describe the sample, and multiple regression was used to analyze the relationship between the independent and dependent variables.

RESULTS: The study sample consisted of 86 program directors. Participants reported high leader efficacy and emotional intelligence. There was a significant predictive relationship between variables (P < .001). The adjusted R2 was 0.34, indicating that approximately 34% of the variance of the criterion variable can be explained by the combination of predictor variables. Significant predictors were leader efficacy (P < .001) and emotional intelligence (P < .010), while years of experience was not a predictor (P = .161).

DISCUSSION: With the exponential growth in the number of PA education programs comes the need for effective leaders. This study's findings suggest the need for more targeted professional development for program directors to enhance leader efficacy and strengthen emotional intelligence. In addition, institutions should provide program directors with adequate tools and resources that will facilitate their leadership roles.

articles.title: Biopsychosocial factors associated with body image in Brazilian women with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
articles.abstract: BackgroundSystemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), a chronic autoimmune disease that predominantly affects women, can alter both physical appearance and bodily functioning through its manifestations and treatment, posing challenges to body image. Although body image in SLE has been associated with clinical, psychological, and sociodemographic factors, few studies have examined these domains simultaneously in women with SLE within a biopsychosocial framework, which limits understanding of their joint contributions.ObjectiveTo examine biopsychosocial factors associated with body image in a Brazilian sample of women with SLE.MethodsA nationwide cross-sectional survey was conducted with 597 women with SLE. Participants provided sociodemographic and clinical information and completed the Body Esteem Scale for Adults and Adolescents (BESAA), Satisfaction with Life Scale (SWLS), and Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scale-21 (DASS-21). Bivariate associations were examined with nonparametric tests, and independent associations were examined with a hierarchical multiple linear regression including theoretically pre-specified sociodemographic, clinical, and psychological blocks.ResultsIn bivariate analyses, poorer body image was associated with active disease, skin lesions, joint pain, serous membrane inflammation, fever without infection, lower life satisfaction, higher levels of depression, anxiety, and stress, lower educational attainment, and lower household income. The final model explained 35.4% of the variance in body image, with psychological variables accounting for 17.7% beyond sociodemographic and clinical characteristics. Greater life satisfaction and unintentional weight loss were independently associated with more positive body image, whereas higher levels of depression, skin lesions, and joint pain were independently associated with poorer body image.ConclusionsBody image in women with SLE is associated with factors across different biopsychosocial domains, suggesting that it should not be examined solely from a clinical perspective. Rather, psychological and social factors should be considered alongside disease-related characteristics to support more comprehensive approaches to the assessment and care of body image concerns in this population.

articles.title: Impact of sarcopenia on clinical outcomes after endoscopic and endovascular interventions for bleeding gastric varices: A multi-center real-world study.
articles.journal: Indian journal of gastroenterology : official journal of the Indian Society of Gastroenterology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of sarcopenia on the clinical outcomes following gastric variceal (GV) hemorrhage in cirrhosis remains unclear.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients with cirrhosis and GV bleeding from six centers in India (January 2017-January 2023). Baseline demographics, further decompensation events-rebleeding, ascites and hepatic encephalopathy (HE) and mortality-were reviewed. Cross-sectional imaging was used to assess skeletal muscle index (SMI). Sarcopenia was defined using gender-specific SMI thresholds (men, < 42 cm2/m2 and women, < 38 cm2/m2). Competing risk analysis was used to evaluate predictors of rebleeding and further decompensation with mortality as a competing event.

RESULTS: Total 318 patients (214 males, 67.3%) were included. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (49/79, 62%) was the leading cause for cirrhosis in patients with sarcopenia. Sarcopenia was associated with higher risk of rebleeding (sHR, 1.62, 95% CI, 1.03-2.52; p = 0.03), further decompensation (sHR, 2.02, 95% CI, 1.43-2.85; p < 0.001) and a one, two and three-year probability of mortality of 15.3%, 24.9% and 41.1% as compared to 9.1%, 14.9% and 14.9% in non-sarcopenic patients. On multi-variate analysis, sarcopenia was an independent predictor of both further decompensation (sHR, 2.03, 95% CI, 1.39-2.97; p < 0.01) and mortality (HR, 1.98, 95% CI, 1.11-3.54; p = 0.020).

CONCLUSION: The presence of sarcopenia is a risk factor for further decompensation and mortality after GV hemorrhage in cirrhosis.

articles.title: Contemporary management of severe generalized tetanus: an evidence-based review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe generalized tetanus remains associated with substantial mortality despite being vaccine preventable. Management is complicated by limited high-quality evidence, conflicting trial results, and the need to balance effective control of spasms and autonomic dysfunction against the risks of prolonged mechanical ventilation.

METHODS: We describe the management of a 57-year-old man with Ablett grade III generalized tetanus and use this case as a clinical framework for an expert narrative review. The review synthesizes randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, prospective studies, and relevant observational literature addressing neuromodulatory therapy, airway management, autonomic dysfunction, intrathecal antitoxin, and supportive critical care.

RESULTS: The patient was managed using a multimodal strategy comprising continuous midazolam infusion, magnesium sulphate, oral baclofen, dexmedetomidine, intramuscular and intrathecal human tetanus immunoglobulin, and meticulous low-stimulation supportive care. Therapy was titrated using serial bedside assessment of neuromuscular burden. He recovered without endotracheal intubation, neuromuscular blockade, or tracheostomy and was discharged on day 21. We argue that discordant findings in tetanus trials are substantially attributable to heterogeneity in disease severity, clinical practice, airway management thresholds, and resource availability, rather than to true therapeutic inconsistency. Available evidence supports a physiology-directed multimodal approach using agents with complementary mechanisms to suppress spasms and autonomic dysfunction while preserving spontaneous ventilation whenever safely feasible.

CONCLUSIONS: Management of severe tetanus should focus on achieving physiological targets rather than escalating individual drugs. A structured, individualized, multimodal neuromodulatory strategy delivered within an experienced, low-stimulation critical care environment may allow selected patients to be managed without mechanical ventilation; safety cannot be established from a single case and requires prospective evaluation. Greater emphasis should also be placed on preventive adult immunization, as vaccination remains the intervention most likely to reduce the burden of severe tetanus.

articles.title: The growing burden of infectious arthritis in Germany: a nationwide analysis of epidemiology, mortality, and contemporary inpatient care.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Infectious arthritis is a destructive joint infection associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. We characterised long-term changes in its inpatient epidemiology and outcomes in Germany and complemented these trends with contemporary nationwide inpatient data.

METHODS: Nationwide hospital discharge data for pyogenic arthritis (ICD-10-GM M00) were obtained from the German Federal Health Monitoring database for 2000-2023. Hospitalisations, age-standardised rates, demographic patterns, pathogen-specific diagnostic codes, in-hospital mortality, and length of stay were analysed. Nationwide Diagnosis-Related Group data from 2019 to 2024 characterised contemporary inpatient and procedural patterns. Temporal trends were assessed by log-linear regression.

RESULTS: Annual hospitalisations increased from 6,088 in 2000 to 21,051 in 2023 (annual percentage change [APC] 5.28%, 95% CI 4.54-6.03; P < 0.001), while the age-standardised hospitalisation rate rose from 8 to 25 per 100,000 population (APC 4.65%, 95% CI 3.93-5.38; P < 0.001). In-hospital deaths increased from 85 to 734 (APC 9.37%, 95% CI 8.52-10.20; P < 0.001), and crude in-hospital mortality increased from 1.40% to 3.49% (APC 3.88%, 95% CI 3.20-4.56; P < 0.001). InEK case volume further increased from 15,338 in 2019 to 22,446 in 2024.

CONCLUSION: Infectious arthritis represents a growing inpatient burden in Germany, with increases persisting after age standardisation and accompanied by rising crude in-hospital mortality. The findings support continued surveillance and studies integrating administrative, clinical, and microbiological data.

articles.title: When history repeats: leptospirosis as a marker of climate change and urban health inequity.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Leptospirosis is a zoonotic spirochetal infection classically associated with tropical or travel-related exposure, but it is increasingly recognized in urban settings, particularly among people experiencing homelessness.

CASE PRESENTATION: We describe a 42-year-old man with alcohol use disorder and unstable housing who presented with fever, bilateral leg pain, and diarrhea, with laboratory findings showing thrombocytopenia, azotemia, hyperbilirubinemia, transaminitis, and elevated creatine phosphokinase. He left against medical advice, then returned the next day with worsening jaundice, dark urine, and emesis. Polymerase chain reaction testing confirmed Leptospira infection, and he improved with targeted antimicrobial and supportive therapy.

CONCLUSION: This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of leptospirosis, whose nonspecific early presentation can resemble sepsis or drug-induced liver injury, and underscores its rising incidence in temperate urban centers such as New York City (NYC), where housing instability, rodent exposure, and limited healthcare access disproportionately affect vulnerable populations. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for leptospirosis in patients with compatible symptoms and relevant social history, as early recognition is critical to reducing morbidity and mortality.

articles.title: Correction to: Prognostic value of epicardial and pericardial adipose tissue in patients with chronic heart failure.
articles.journal: Netherlands heart journal : monthly journal of the Netherlands Society of Cardiology and the Netherlands Heart Foundation

articles.title: Investigating the association between individual income and cancer outcomes among Canadians diagnosed with gastric cancer.
articles.journal: Gastric cancer : official journal of the International Gastric Cancer Association and the Japanese Gastric Cancer Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence of income-based disparities in gastric cancer outcomes exist; however, little research has explored income and gastric cancer outcomes within North America. We investigated the association between individual income and diagnosis with stage IV gastric cancer and death from any cause in the five years following diagnosis.

METHODS: Canadians diagnosed with gastric cancer between 2010 and 2019 were included using Canadian Census Health and Environmental Cohorts (CanCHEC) linked to the Canadian Cancer Registry, and national hospitalization and vital statistics databases. Individual income was determined prior to the cancer diagnosis and categorized into quintiles (lowest to highest) nationally for each census year. Multivariable logistic regression estimated the association between income and stage IV gastric cancer. Multivariable Cox proportional-hazards regression estimated the association with death from any cause.

RESULTS: 8,545 Canadians with gastric cancer were included. We did not observe an association between individual income and presentation with stage IV diagnosis (p = 0.26). We observed a significant association between individual income quintile and death from any cause in the five years following diagnosis (p = 0.003), with patients within the lowest income quintile having 1.18 times the risk of death when compared to patients within the highest income quintile (HR = 1.18; 95% CI: 1.08-1.29).

CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that income-related barriers may influence outcomes after diagnosis rather than stage at presentation. Future research understanding pathways to worse gastric cancer outcomes for individuals with low income in low incidence countries with universal health care systems that prioritize patient, survivor and caregiver perspectives is needed.

articles.title: From pollution to progress: prioritising risks and sustainable packaging alternatives for PET bottles waste management in developing countries.
articles.journal: Environmental science and pollution research international
articles.abstract: Despite their convenience and inherent recyclability, polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottles suffer from low collection and recycling rates, significantly contributing to persistent plastic pollution, high carbon emissions, microplastic leakage, and toxic chemical exposure. This study uses a comprehensive decision-making framework to assess the risks associated with PET waste and to evaluate sustainable alternatives. The study employs Modified Safety Improve Risk Assessment (M-SIRA) to identify PET-related major risks, their causes and consequences, and prioritise these risks based on Risk Priority Number (RPN). After identifying major risks, the Fuzzy Full Consistency Method (F-FUCOM) is used to prioritise criteria and alternatives to the PET. Several evaluation criteria (ranging from toxic emissions during production and hazardous recycling byproducts to microplastic pollution and environmental persistence) were considered. The results indicated that Polyethylene Furanoate (PEF) and aluminium are the most viable and top-performing PET alternatives due to their lower environmental footprints and higher recyclability. The result of the study provides valuable and actionable insights for policymakers and industry stakeholders to address the economic and regulatory challenges in implementing circular economy principles through recycling in the packaging industry in general and the need for strategic transition towards sustainable packaging in particular.

articles.title: Gut dysbiosis and intestinal permeability in relation to liver stiffness assessed by elastography: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The gut-liver axis represents a pivotal bidirectional pathway in chronic liver disease. Gut dysbiosis, intestinal barrier dysfunction, microbial translocation and downstream immune activation have been associated with liver disease severity; however, their relationship with liver stiffness measured by elastography has not been systematically synthesised.

AIM: To systematically review the association between gut dysbiosis and gut-related biomarkers and liver stiffness assessed by elastography in adults.

METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL and Web of Science from inception through 31 March 2026. Original studies reporting both a gut-related exposure, including microbiome profiling or circulating, faecal or functional gut-related biomarkers, and liver stiffness measurement by a validated elastographic modality were eligible. Findings were classified according to the hepatic outcome actually evaluated as direct liver stiffness measurements, histologically defined fibrosis, or steatosis/other indirect liver-related outcomes. Study selection, data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment were performed independently by two reviewers.

RESULTS: 13 studies comprising 2,912 participants met the inclusion criteria. Nine assessed gut microbiota composition, six evaluated circulating or faecal gut-related biomarkers, and two assessed both domains. Direct positive associations with liver stiffness were reported for the kynurenine-to-tryptophan ratio in two studies and for soluble CD14 and soluble CD163 in one study; a separate study provided supportive histological evidence linking higher soluble CD14 and soluble CD163 levels to fibrosis. Evidence for lipopolysaccharide-binding protein and intestinal fatty acid-binding protein was null or limited, whilst faecal calprotectin was associated with steatosis rather than liver stiffness. Microbiome findings were heterogeneous, with no reproducible taxonomic signature across populations. Overall risk of bias was low in five studies, raised some concerns in six, and was high in two.

CONCLUSIONS: Selected gut-related biomarkers, particularly markers of monocyte-macrophage activation and tryptophan catabolism, are associated with higher liver stiffness although direct elastographic evidence remains limited and heterogeneous. Liver stiffness should not be considered synonymous with histological fibrosis, and findings based on fibrosis histology, steatosis or indirect liver-related outcomes should be interpreted separately. Further prospective studies using standardised gut-barrier assessment and rigorously reported elastography protocols are warranted.

articles.title: Women in Integrated Health: Driving Multidisciplinary Collaboration and the Evolution of Comprehensive Obesity Care within International Federation for the Surgery and Other Therapies for Obesity.
articles.abstract: Within the International Federation for the Surgery and Other Therapies for Obesity (IFSO), Integrated Health professionals have become essential to the evolution of comprehensive obesity care. As the field transitions from a predominantly surgical discipline toward a truly multidisciplinary specialty, women in integrated health-encompassing nutrition, psychology, nursing, physiotherapy, endocrinology, and allied sciences-are leading efforts in collaboration, innovation, and patient-centered practice. This editorial aims to highlight the contributions of women in Integrated Health leadership within IFSO to multidisciplinary obesity care, examine these contributions across the bariatric care continuum, and propose concrete, measurable actions to advance equity and clinically meaningful outcomes in bariatric practice.

articles.title: Sex-Specific Mediators of Serum Uric Acid Reduction Following Laparoscopic Sleeve Gastrectomy: A Retrospective Longitudinal Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hyperuricemia is highly prevalent among individuals with obesity and is associated with insulin resistance, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular risk. Although laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) reduces serum uric acid (SUA), the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Emerging evidence suggests that sex differences influence metabolic regulation, including insulin secretion and renal urate handling. This study investigates one-year changes in SUA following LSG and explores sex-specific determinants.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 268 patients (96 males, 172 females) undergoing LSG between 2014 and 2025. Clinical and laboratory parameters were collected at baseline and 12 months, with changes defined as baseline minus postoperative values. Sex-stratified univariate screening (P < 0.10) and backward multivariate regression identified independent predictors of SUA reduction. In females, bootstrap mediation analysis (5,000 resamples) assessed whether C-peptide and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) mediated the relationship between weight loss and SUA reduction.

RESULTS: Baseline SUA was higher in males than females (479.8 vs. 406.9 µmol/L, P < 0.001). At 12 months, females exhibited greater absolute and relative SUA reductions (both P < 0.001). Baseline SUA and percent total weight loss (%TWL) were independent predictors in both sexes. In females, ΔeGFR remained significant (P = 0.007), while ΔC-peptide showed a trend (P = 0.063). Mediation analysis demonstrated that %TWL indirectly reduced SUA via ΔC-peptide (β = 0.251, 95% CI: 0.009-0.562), accounting for 9.2% of the total effect.

CONCLUSION: SUA reduction following LSG exhibits sex-specific patterns. In females, the association between weight loss and SUA reduction was partially mediated by reductions in C-peptide, while changes in eGFR were independently associated with SUA reduction.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04548232.

articles.title: Estimation of Economic Cost and Out-of-Pocket Expenditure (OOPE) in a Publicly Funded Tertiary Care Neonatal Intensive Care Unit in South India.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Up-to-date costing data estimated using robust methodology are not available for infants admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) in India. The authors objective was to use health technology assessment to compute the cost of intensive care for neonates admitted to NICU Levels 1, 2 and 3. The authors also estimated out-of-pocket expenditure (OOPE) and catastrophic health expenditure (CHE; health expenditure >10% of the annual income) incurred by their families.

METHODS: The study was conducted in a publicly funded tertiary care hospital over 12 mo. Fifty neonates admitted to each level (1, 2 and 3) of NICU were enrolled by systematic random sampling. Bottom-up method of cost estimation and micro-costing was done from a health system perspective. Parents were interviewed twice weekly for data on OOPE and CHE.

RESULTS: The annual recurring cost of running the NICU was Rs. 8,52,15,082; 64% was spent on human resources. Median (IQR) cost of care per neonate in rupees was as follows: Level-1: 14,085 (8,789-19,619), Level-2: 39,304 (23,567-65,841), Level-3: 1,20,754 (59,179-3,03,465). Families of neonates admitted to level-1 incurred median OOPE of Rs. 5,831, and those admitted to level-2 and level-3 spent Rs. 7,062 and Rs. 18,906 respectively. Fifty-five percent of families of infants admitted to the NICU incurred CHE.

CONCLUSIONS: Human resources account for nearly two-thirds of the cost of running the NICU. Despite increased coverage through government insurance schemes, families face substantial out-of-pocket expenses, and more than half incur catastrophic health expenditure. These findings highlight the need for increased governmental support for NICU care.

articles.title: Role of Family Centered Care on Parental Stress and Anxiety Levels in Pediatric Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of Family-Centered Care (FCC) practices on parental stress, anxiety, and depression among parents of children admitted to a Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU).

METHODS: This prospective observational study was conducted over one year (September 2024-August 2025) in a PICU of a tertiary care teaching hospital in North India. Children aged 1 mo to 18 y admitted for more than 24 h were included. Parental psychological assessment was performed within 72 h of admission using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) and the Parental Stressor Scale (PSS). FCC components-including information sharing, family participation, presence during procedures and resuscitation, family-centered rounds, dignity and respect, negotiating roles, sharing goals, family conferences, and open visitation-were documented. Illness severity was assessed using PRISM scores. Correlation and comparative analyses were performed to examine associations between FCC practices and psychological outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 326 children were enrolled. Higher PRISM scores correlated strongly with increased parental stress (r = 0.793), anxiety (r = 0.721), and depression (r = 0.719) (p <0.0001). Implementation of key FCC components was significantly associated with lower stress, anxiety, and depression scores (p <0.05). The number of FCC components followed showed a strong inverse correlation with stress (r = -0.836), anxiety (r = -0.709), and depression (r = - 0.754) (p <0.0001). Open visitation alone was not significantly associated with improved psychological outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Structured FCC practices are significantly associated with reduced parental stress, anxiety, and depression in the PICU. Strengthening meaningful family engagement may improve psychological outcomes in resource-limited critical care settings.

articles.title: Butyrate in pediatric sepsis-associated acute kidney injury: hypothesized protection through the gut-kidney axis.
Direct oral anticoagulants versus vitamin K antagonist-based standard care in cerebral venous thrombosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract: Cerebral venous thrombosis (CVT) is an uncommon form of stroke that predominantly affects younger adults. Anticoagulation remains the cornerstone of treatment. Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) offer practical advantages over vitamin K antagonists (VKAs), but controlled-trial evidence remains limited. To evaluate the efficacy and safety of DOACs compared with VKA-based standard care in patients with CVT. We conducted a systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of eligible controlled trials reported by their investigators as randomized. The primary efficacy outcome was radiological recanalization or improvement at approximately 6 months, and the primary safety outcome was major bleeding. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled. Secondary clinical outcomes were summarized narratively. A post hoc sensitivity analysis excluded the trial with predictable date-based allocation. Six eligible trials enrolled 430 participants; outcome analyses included up to 428 participants. Three trials with 229 evaluable participants contributed to the radiological recanalization or improvement meta-analysis, which showed no statistically significant difference (RR 0.94; 95% CI 0.81-1.09; I-squared = 0%). Excluding Maqsood et al., which used predictable allocation by admission date and was judged high risk for the randomization process, yielded a similar estimate (RR 0.90; 95% CI 0.75-1.08; I-squared = 0%). Three informative trials contributed to the relative-effect analysis for major bleeding (RR 0.60; 95% CI 0.12-3.00; I-squared = 0%); two additional trials reported no major bleeding in either group and were not estimable. Across the five trials reporting a harmonizable major-bleeding outcome, major bleeding occurred in 2 of 188 DOAC-treated participants and 4 of 190 comparator-treated participants. Other clinical events were sparse and heterogeneous. Available controlled-trial evidence did not demonstrate statistically significant differences between DOACs and VKA-based standard care for radiological recanalization or improvement or major bleeding. The estimates remain imprecise because of small trials, sparse events, and heterogeneous radiological outcome definitions. Larger, adequately powered trials are required.

articles.title: Neuroprotective effects of ıdebenone and citicoline in experimental traumatic optic neuropathy: electrophysiological, histological, and biochemical assessments in a rat model.
articles.abstract: OBJECTıVE: This study aims to investigate the neuroprotective efficacy of idebenone and citicoline in a rat model of traumatic optic neuropathy (TON), induced by controlled optic nerve (ON) crush injury. MATERıALS AND METHODS: Forty male Wistar rats (250-300 g) were randomly assigned to four groups (n=10). TON was induced in Groups 1, 2 and 3 via right ON crush. Group 1 received no treatment; Group 2 received idebenone (50 mg/kg/day), and Group 3 received citicoline (1 g/kg/day) via a nasogastric tube, starting 24 h post-injury. Group 4 served as sham controls. Flash and pattern visual evoked potentials (fVEP, pVEP) were recorded at baseline, 48 h, and day 28. The flash and pattern VEP tests were performed using the MonPackONE device. Blood biomarkers (ischemia-modified albumin (IMA), total and native thiol) were analyzed, and histological evaluations included hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) staining and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) monoclonal antibody immunohistochemistry. RESULTS: At day 2, VEP tests indicated delayed latency and decreased amplitude in Groups 1-3 versus the sham group. By day 28, Groups 2 and 3 showed significant VEP improvement over Group 1. Biochemical analysis demonstrated higher thiol levels in Group 3 compared to Group 2 on day 28; however, this difference was not statistically significant. GFAP staining in the retina and ON tissues was highest in Group 1 and lowest in Group 4. ON thickness was greater in Group 2 than in Group 3, but the difference was also not statistically significant. CONCLUSıON: Although neither treatment demonstrated superiority over the other, both oral citicoline and idebenone provided neuroprotection in TON, as evidenced by improved electrophysiological function, greater retina ganglion cell survival, and elevated systemic antioxidant markers.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes and complication profile of intrapericardial pneumonectomy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE(S): Intrapericardial pneumonectomy is a technically demanding procedure performed in selected patients with centrally located or advanced lung cancer. This study aimed to evaluate early and late postoperative complications, characterize their severity, and explore factors associated with complication development.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 24 patients who underwent intrapericardial pneumonectomy for lung cancer between March 2023 and January 2025. Postoperative complications were classified as early (≤ 30 days) or late (> 30 days), categorized by clinical type and management, and retrospectively graded according to the Thoracic Morbidity and Mortality (TM&M) classification. Clinical and perioperative variables were compared according to complication status.

RESULTS: Early postoperative complications occurred in 16 patients (66.7%), whereas late complications occurred in four (16.7%). Arrhythmia and acute kidney injury (AKI) were the most common early complications, each occurring in four patients (16.7%). Among patients with AKI, one was managed medically, two required renal replacement therapy, and one required continuous renal replacement therapy in the setting of postoperative shock and multiorgan dysfunction. Postoperative mortality occurred in two patients (8.3%). Perioperative transfusion was more frequent in patients with complications (50.0% vs. 12.5%; p = 0.178), while neoadjuvant treatment was not associated with complication development (p = 1.000).

CONCLUSIONS: In this selected cohort, substantial postoperative morbidity was observed, with considerable heterogeneity in complication severity. These findings emphasize the value of severity grading in addition to complication frequency. Larger prospective multicenter comparative studies are needed to better define postoperative morbidity and associated risk factors.

articles.title: Practice variation in mechanical circulatory support: a cross-sectional questionnaire survey of Japanese interventional cardiologists in the CVIT Kyushu-Okinawa chapter.
articles.abstract: Mechanical circulatory support (MCS) practice for cardiogenic shock may vary with institutional resources and operator experience, but data from Japanese interventional cardiologists are limited. We conducted an anonymous cross-sectional survey of 720 members of 83 Japanese Association of Cardiovascular Intervention and Therapeutics (CVIT)-certified or affiliated training hospitals in the CVIT Kyushu-Okinawa Chapter (September-October 2025); 536 returned questionnaires (74.4%), and consent was confirmed for 385 (53.5%). The primary analysis included 276 respondents who had performed intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP), veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO), or Impella CP insertion within 12 months: 163 at Impella-capable and 113 at non-Impella-capable hospitals. Documented MCS and extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation protocols were more frequently reported by respondents from Impella-capable hospitals (46% vs. 6% and 39% vs. 13%, respectively), as was collaboration with emergency and critical care physicians; no statistically significant difference was detected in perceived need for collaboration. MCS selection varied between groups. At Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) shock stage C, IABP (44%) and Impella CP (48%) were selected with similar frequency among respondents in Impella-capable hospitals, whereas IABP was selected by 79% in non-Impella-capable hospitals. At stage E, ECPELLA (79%) and VA-ECMO plus IABP (84%) predominated, respectively. Among respondents with device-specific operator experience within 12 months, vascular access and anticoagulation practices varied between groups. Procedural anxiety was lower with higher CVIT qualification; however, 19% of board-certified members reported anxiety about Impella CP insertion and 45% about emergency intubation. These findings identify MCS practice variation across several domains warranting further evaluation.

articles.title: Coronary CT angiography in patients with non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome-a narrative review.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: Non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS) is often the first clinical presentation of coronary artery disease. Current diagnostic standards rely on invasive coronary angiography (ICA) to guide therapy. Non-invasive coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) may currently be used to exclude obstructive coronary artery disease in low-risk NSTE-ACS. The recently introduced photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) may further expand its application in high-risk NSTE-ACS patients, as well. This review explores the current and emerging role of CCTA in the evaluation of patients with an established diagnosis of NSTE-ACS.

articles.title: Accelerated aortic stenosis progression is associated with greater CT-derived extracellular volume.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: Rapid progression of aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with adverse outcomes, yet the myocardial changes accompanying faster progression remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated the association between the rate of AS progression and myocardial fibrosis assessed by computed tomography (CT)-derived extracellular volume fraction (ECV), and the impact on clinical outcomes. We studied 134 patients with classical high-gradient severe AS who underwent pre-transcatheter aortic valve implantation cardiac CT with a delayed dual-energy acquisition for ECV quantification and had at least two echocardiograms ≥ 6 months apart. Progression was defined as the annualized change in peak aortic jet velocity. Rapid progression was defined as an increase > 0.30 m/s/year. Patients were followed for a composite of cardiovascular hospitalization, urgent aortic valve replacement, or death. ECV correlated with progression rate (Spearman ρ = 0.33, p < 0.001). In multivariable linear regression, faster progression remained independently associated with ECV (β = 2.52, p = 0.001). Rapid progressors had higher ECV than slow progressors (31.5% vs. 28.3%, p < 0.001). Over a median follow-up of 16.2 months, 36 patients (26.9%) reached the composite outcome. Patients with both rapid progression and high ECV had an event rate of 69 versus 11 per 100 patient-years in those without (adjusted HR 6.22, 95% CI 3.13-12.32). Faster AS progression is independently associated with greater diffuse myocardial fibrosis, irrespective of stenosis severity, and their combination identified patients at higher risk of adverse events. These findings suggest that AS progression rate and myocardial tissue characterization carry complementary prognostic information in severe AS.

articles.title: Engineered probiotics for the control of antibiotic-resistant and difficult-to-treat pathogens.
articles.abstract: The increasing prevalence of antibiotic-resistant pathogens and recurrent, biofilm-associated, toxin-mediated, or dysbiosis-related infections has created an urgent need for strategies that complement conventional antibiotics. Broad-spectrum therapy can disrupt commensal microbiota, weaken colonization resistance, and promote opportunistic or recurrent infection. Engineered probiotics offer microbiology-based interventions that can inhibit pathogen growth, disrupt biofilms, attenuate virulence, neutralize toxins, and restore protective microbiota functions. Engineered probiotic and commensal microorganisms can also respond to pathogen- or infection-associated signals, improving therapeutic localization and specificity. This review summarizes strategies for controlling antibiotic-resistant and difficult-to-treat pathogens, including pathogen-responsive antimicrobial production, bacteriocin-, pyocin-, lysin-, and antimicrobial peptide-mediated inhibition, enzymatic biofilm degradation, anti-virulence and toxin-neutralization approaches, restoration of microbiota-mediated colonization resistance, and targeted genetic approaches for pathogen elimination or antibiotic resensitization. Representative systems against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Clostridioides difficile, Staphylococcus aureus, Listeria monocytogenes, Streptococcus pyogenes, and resistant Enterobacteriaceae are discussed. Major translational challenges include chassis selection, genetic stability, horizontal gene transfer, biocontainment, delivery, manufacturing, regulation, and host-microbiota variability. Engineered probiotics may therefore provide selective, localized, and microbiota-preserving complements to conventional therapy.

articles.title: Artificial Urinary Sphincter in Women: A Systematic Review of Clinical Outcomes and Technological Evolutions.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Stress urinary incontinence (SUI) secondary to intrinsic sphincter deficiency (ISD) remains a challenging condition in women with persistent or recurrent incontinence despite conservative or surgical treatment. Artificial urinary sphincter (AUS) implantation represents an established salvage option. This review summarizes recent evidence on clinical outcomes, evolving surgical approaches, quality-of-life outcomes, and emerging device technologies in women undergoing AUS implantation.

RECENT FINDINGS: A PubMed search of studies published between 2019 and 2025, conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines, identified 30 eligible studies. Reported continence rates ranged from 59% to 84%, while revision and explantation rates ranged from 6% to 69% and 2% to 34%, respectively. Contemporary patient populations increasingly comprise complex revision cases, particularly following synthetic sling removal. Minimally invasive and robotic approaches have emerged as promising alternatives, improving surgical precision and reducing perioperative morbidity, although comparative evidence remains limited and their impact on long term device survival is not established. Beyond continence, AUS implantation may improve quality of life. Early findings also suggest possible benefits in female sexual function, although further studies are needed to confirm these observations. Emerging electromechanical and pump-free systems may offer further improvements in device usability and complication profiles, but their clinical benefits remain to be established.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Over the last five years, the literature on female urinary sphincter devices has been dominated by retrospective studies, resulting in a generally low level of evidence. Most publications focus on AUS in women and consist of single-center retrospective case series. The European Association of Urology-led VENUS registry was established to address this limitation by collecting real-world data on AUS implantation and outcomes in women with stress urinary incontinence due to intrinsic sphincter deficiency. Patient recruitment has recently accelerated, with more than 13 centers currently enrolling and additional centers in the initiation process [1]. Emerging prospective studies on AUS and adjustable continence therapy (ACT) balloons may further strengthen the evidence base in the near future. AUS remains a valuable salvage therapy for severe female SUI related to ISD. Despite substantial revision and explantation rates, advances in surgical techniques and device design hold promise for improving patient experience and functional outcomes. Further prospective studies with long-term follow-up are needed to clarify the comparative effectiveness of surgical approaches, assess the impact of emerging technologies on device durability, and better characterize the effects of AUS implantation on female sexual function.

articles.title: Clinical and forensic implications of severe liver injury associated with selective androgen receptor modulators and other performance-enhancing drugs advertised on social media.
articles.abstract: A 66-year-old male without long-term medication presented with painless jaundice, itching, clay-colored stools, and concentrated urine. Laboratory findings showed elevated bilirubin (15.6 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 13.4 mg/dL) and liver enzymes (GOT 95 U/L, GPT 137 U/L, gamma-GT 65 U/L, normal alkaline phosphatase). Transient elastography found increased liver stiffness (11.5 kPa) and mild steatosis (Controlled Attenuation Parameter, CAP: 240). Abnormal sexual hormone tests and detailed medical history revealed the use of selective androgen receptor modulators (SARMs; ostarine and testolone) and other performance-enhancing drugs (PEDs; cardarine). All substances were acquired online, are prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency, and are not approved as drugs. Probable substance-induced liver injury was reported to the authorities, who initiated forensic investigations. Chemical analysis showed dosages exceeding regulatory thresholds. The pharmacovigilance report enabled legal actions and further contributed to international law enforcement operations. Our case report describes the hepatotoxic risks of SARMs/PEDs and highlights the importance of pharmacovigilance reporting to facilitate forensic and regulatory anti-doping implications.

articles.title: Histological disappearance of persistent clarithromycin-resistant Helicobacter pylori infection following administration of a sulforaphane-, curcumin- and Lactobacillus-containing food supplement: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Increasing antimicrobial resistance has become a major challenge in the treatment of Helicobacter pylori infection. Sulforaphane, a bioactive isothiocyanate derived from broccoli sprouts, has demonstrated anti-H. pylori activity in experimental and clinical studies. Curcumin and probiotic bacteria have also been investigated as adjunctive therapies.

CASE PRESENTATION: A woman in her seventies underwent upper gastrointestinal endoscopy screening. Histology revealed chronic active Helicobacter pylori-associated gastritis involving the antrum and corpus. Molecular testing confirmed H. pylori infection and detected the clarithromycin resistance mutation A2143G in the 23S rRNA gene. Following treatment with bismuth quadruple therapy consisting of Pylera® (Laboratoires Juvise Pharmaceuticals, France: bismuth subcitrate potassium 140 mg, metronidazole 125 mg and tetracycline hydrochloride 125 mg per capsule; three capsules four times daily) plus pantoprazole (40 mg twice daily for 10 days, followed by pantoprazole 40 mg once daily for 4 weeks), repeat endoscopy 1 year later demonstrated persistent active gastritis and persistence of the resistance mutation. The patient subsequently received a nutraceutical preparation containing broccoli-derived sulforaphane, curcumin, and Lactobacillus acidophilus. The preparation was administered as two capsules twice daily before meals for 21 days. Follow-up endoscopy approximately 3 months later demonstrated resolution of inflammatory activity and the absence of detectable H. pylori organisms in antral and corpus biopsies.

CONCLUSION: This case documents the histological disappearance of persistent clarithromycin-resistant H. pylori infection following administration of a sulforaphane-, curcumin- and probiotic-containing nutraceutical. Although causality cannot be established from a single observation, the findings support further investigation of such interventions in patients with treatment-refractory infection.

articles.title: Lipoprotein(a) and chronic kidney disease: reciprocal associations, potential causal pathways, and clinical implications.
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) leads to multiple metabolic disorders which raise both the cardiovascular and non-cardiovascular mortality, especially in end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) patients. Among the dysmetabolic CKD-associated patterns, dyslipidemia shows a wide spectrum of clinical concurrent presentations, involving high serum levels of triglycerides, cholesterol, and lipoproteins such as Lp(a). International consensus statements and guidelines have highlighted the increased cardiovascular risk associated with higher serum Lp(a) levels > 105 nmol/L due to its pro-atherosclerotic and pro-thrombotic effects. Therefore, its assessment should be recommended at least once in a lifetime, due to the relative stability of Lp(a) serum levels over time. CKD is associated with increased Lp(a) concentrations, which rise as the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and/or urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) worsen. Consequently, Lp(a) levels may be five-to-tenfold higher in patients with ESKD than in those with mild-to-moderate CKD. This alteration is mainly attributable to impaired renal clearance of Lp(a) and apolipoprotein(a) [Apo(a)] particles and, under specific conditions, to increased hepatic Lp(a) production, as observed in severe proteinuric diseases. Conversely, Lp(a) genetic determinants of elevated Lp(a) levels and increased serum Lp(a) concentrations have been investigated as potential causes of CKD onset, through Mendelian randomization (MR) and prospective studies, respectively. However, uncertainty and important gaps in the available evidence still remain. The aim of this review is to summarize and discuss the most recent and relevant clinical and experimental evidence on this topic through a defined research among the scientific literature.

articles.title: In vitro antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antifungal, and anti-HCoV-229E activities of Jatropha integerrima leaf and stem bark extract and in vivo evaluation of its intravenous SNEDDS in a mouse model.
articles.journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has highlighted the need for novel antiviral agents with additional therapeutic activities against inflammatory and opportunistic fungal infections, including mucormycosis.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the in vitro antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antifungal, and antiviral activities of ethanolic leaf and stem bark extract of Jatropha integerrima (JIJ) and its in vivo efficacy against Human Coronavirus 229E (HCoV-229E).

METHODS: Antioxidant activity was assessed using DPPH and ABTS assays. Anti-inflammatory activity was evaluated in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated THP-1 monocytes and RAW 264.7 macrophages by analysing TNF-α and iNOS gene expression. Antifungal activity was investigated against Apophysomyces elegans and Rhizopus oryzae. Cytotoxicity and antiviral activity were assessed in A549 cells. Optimized JIJ-containing self-nanoemulsifying drug delivery system (JIJ-SNEDDS) was evaluated in BALB/c mice intranasally infected with HCoV-229E.

RESULTS: JIJ exhibited strong antioxidant activity, downregulated TNF-α and iNOS expression, and demonstrated antifungal activity against both fungal pathogens. The extract inhibited viral replication in A549 cells with minimal cytotoxicity. Optimized JIJ-SNEDDS exhibited a particle size of 115 ± 1.4 nm and zeta potential of - 32.7 ± 2.1 mV. In infected mice, treatment markedly reduced lung viral load and histopathological damage. RT-PCR and protein analyses confirmed decreased viral RNA and protein levels. Flow cytometry revealed an increased Th1/Th2 ratio, decreased Th17/Treg ratio, and increased B- and natural killer (NK)-cell populations. Serum interleukin-6 (IL-6) and TNF-α levels were also reduced.

CONCLUSION: JIJ-SNEDDS demonstrated promising preclinical antiviral activity against HCoV-229E, accompanied by immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory effects. These findings warrant further investigation of its therapeutic potential against coronavirus infection and associated inflammatory complications.

articles.title: SGLT2 Inhibitors in Geriatric Heart Failure: Evidence, Safety, and Clinical Implementation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review summarizes the rationale, efficacy, safety, and implementation of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) in older adults with heart failure (HF).

RECENT FINDINGS: SGLT2i have become an integral part of contemporary HF therapy, with benefits demonstrated across the ejection fraction spectrum. Age subgroup analyses from randomized trials, frailty analyses, meta-analyses, and real-world cohorts suggest that benefits on HF hospitalization and cardiovascular outcomes are largely preserved in older and frail patients. Observational data in patients aged  ≥ 75 and > 80 years further support potential effectiveness in very old and multimorbid populations. However, geriatric vulnerability modifies clinical implementation, particularly regarding volume status, renal function, risk of falling, genitourinary infections, nutritional status, cognition, polypharmacy, and self-care capacity. Available evidence suggests that SGLT2i remain effective and are generally well tolerated in older patients with HF. Older age alone should therefore not preclude SGLT2i therapy. In geriatric HF, treatment decisions should be individualized according to frailty, comorbidity burden, safety risks, functional status, self-care capacity, and goals of care.

articles.title: Breaking the vicious cycle: recent advances and clinical strategies for preventing recurrent clostridioides difficile infection.
articles.journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
articles.abstract: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is the leading cause of healthcare-associated diarrhea worldwide. Over recent years the principal clinical challenge has shifted from achieving initial cure to preventing recurrence (recurrent CDI, rCDI). With expanding exposure to broad-spectrum antibiotics and an aging population, recurrence after primary therapy remains common and increases cumulatively with repeated episodes. This review synthesizes current global evidence on rCDI prevention, emphasizing evolving epidemiology, risk stratification, optimization of antimicrobial regimens, microbiota-focused therapies, and treatment-course management. We discuss randomized and real-world data for pharmacologic and microbiota restoration strategies, highlight modifiable risk factors, and outline practical considerations for integrating preventive measures in clinical practice.

articles.title: Long-Term Efficacy of Adjunctive Cenobamate by Focal Seizure Subtypes: Open-Label Extension of a Randomized Clinical Study in a Multinational Asian Population.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To evaluate adjunctive cenobamate efficacy by focal seizure subtype during the open-label extension (OLE) of a phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study (C035) in Asian patients with focal seizures.

METHODS: Patients aged 18-70 years old with uncontrolled focal seizures despite treatment with 1-3 antiseizure medications who completed the double-blind study (n = 425) could enter the 52-week OLE, comprising a 20-week blinded conversion from placebo or 100, 200, or 400 mg/day cenobamate to a target cenobamate dose of 400 mg/day before entering a 32-week open-label maintenance phase at 300 mg/day. Percent change from double-blind baseline in 28-day seizure frequency and responder rates (e.g., ≥ 50% reduction from baseline) for focal preserved consciousness with observable manifestations (FPC), focal impaired consciousness (FIC), or focal to bilateral tonic-clonic (FBTC) seizure subtypes were assessed in the open-label maintenance phase efficacy population (OLE-EM, ≥ 1 dose of study drug and any seizure data during the open-label maintenance phase). Safety and tolerability were assessed.

RESULTS: Among patients who entered the OLE, 357/410 (263 originally randomized to cenobamate; 94 who converted from placebo to cenobamate) were included in the OLE-EM population. Median percent seizure frequency reductions were 84.5% for FPC (n = 65), 83.0% for FIC (n = 301), and 100% for FBTC (n = 94) in the OLE-EM population. For FPC, FIC, and FBTC subtypes, ≥ 50% responder rates were 75.4%, 73.8%, and 84.0%, respectively, and 100% responder rates were 23.1%, 28.2%, and 58.5%. Among patients entering the OLE, 84.6% (347/410) completed the 52 weeks of treatment with cenobamate. The most common treatment-emergent adverse events were dizziness, somnolence, gamma-glutamyl transferase increased, and COVID-19 infection.

CONCLUSIONS: During the C035 OLE maintenance phase, high seizure frequency reductions were seen for FPC, FIC, and FBTC focal seizure subtypes. Cenobamate was generally well tolerated, and the results were consistent with the double-blind treatment study. Graphical abstract available for this article.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT04557085 (registered September 14, 2020).

articles.title: Immunothrombosis Biomarkers and Multi-Omics Profiles After Successful Recanalization in Patients Receiving Ischemic Postconditioning: An Exploratory Analysis of the INSPIRE Trial.
articles.abstract: Successful recanalization after endovascular thrombectomy does not always restore microvascular perfusion, highlighting the need for adjunctive strategies. Ischemic postconditioning (IPostC) involves brief, controlled​ cycles of flow interruption and restoration at the onset of reperfusion to attenuate ischemia-reperfusion injury. In the parent INSPIRE trial, IPostC, delivered in situ as four cycles of 2-minute balloon inflation followed by 2-minute deflation at the previously occluded arterial segment immediately after successful recanalization, reduced infarct growth from baseline to 48 h. This exploratory secondary analysis included all 60 randomized patients. We investigated whether IPostC was associated with early changes in immunothrombosis, coagulation, and microvascular transit and explored associated plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiles. Arterial blood obtained approximately 15 min after successful recanalization was analyzed using flow cytometry and thromboelastography. Quantitative digital subtraction angiography-derived microcirculation time was analyzed in 55 patients, and plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiling was performed in 29 patients. Compared with controls, patients receiving IPostC had lower neutrophil CD11b expression (median, 52.15 versus 64.27 mean fluorescence intensity ×10²; P = 0.011), a lower thromboelastography α-angle (65.15° versus 67.95°; P = 0.037), and shorter microcirculation time (2.11 versus 3.03 s; P = 0.020). Longer microcirculation time was associated with greater infarct growth (r = 0.533; P < 0.001). Proteomic and metabolomic analyses identified signals involving blood-brain barrier and extracellular-matrix organization and mitochondrial bioenergetics. Biomarker comparisons were not adjusted for multiple comparisons; in the omics analyses, no protein and 17 metabolites remained significant after false discovery rate correction. In summary, IPostC was associated with lower neutrophil activation, slower clot propagation, and faster microvascular transit after recanalization, and multi-omics profiling pointed to blood-brain barrier integrity and mitochondrial bioenergetics as candidate pathways. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger studies. Trial registration: NCT06545734, registered 9 August 2024.

articles.title: Radiomics performance to identify high-risk carotid artery plaques: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality worldwide, with 15-20% of ischemic strokes caused by extracranial carotid atherosclerotic disease. Risk stratification has traditionally relied on luminal stenosis severity, which inadequately reflects plaque vulnerability. Radiomics offers an emerging solution by extracting high-dimensional quantitative data from standard medical images. This systematic review evaluated the performance of radiomics-based models for identifying high-risk carotid plaques.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across multiple databases. Studies were included if they developed or validated radiomics-based models for carotid plaque assessment and reported performance metrics, specifically the area under the curve (AUC). Data were extracted on study design, imaging modalities, segmentation methods, and modeling techniques.

RESULTS: Twenty-eight studies involving 6,108 patients (72.4% male) were included. Computed tomography angiography was the most commonly used imaging modality (n = 16), and manual region-of-interest segmentation was performed in 27 of 28 studies. Radiomics models showed strong predictive performance. Internal validation AUCs were as high as 0.984, whereas combined models incorporating radiomics with clinical and/or conventional radiological features achieved the best predictive accuracy, often exceeding 0.90. However, only four studies included external validation cohorts.

CONCLUSION: Radiomics is a powerful, non-invasive tool for identifying high-risk carotid plaques, offering superior discriminative power over conventional stenosis-based assessments. Despite these promising results, the field faces significant hurdles, and future research must prioritize prospective multicenter trials, the development of automated segmentation workflows, and the correlation of radiomic features with histopathological findings to ensure clinical reproducibility and transition into routine stroke prevention.

KEY POINTS: Question Standard carotid atherosclerotic disease assessments fail to capture biological plaque complexity and vulnerability, necessitating objective, reproducible, and non-invasive methods to improve stroke prevention. Findings Radiomics and combined models demonstrate superior capability in identifying high-risk carotid plaques compared to traditional assessments. With four external validations, the field remains exploratory. Relevance statement Radiomics offers a non-invasive tool for personalized stroke prevention. However, technical barriers currently prevent its transition to routine clinical use, including reliance on manual segmentation and low compliance with international standardization guidelines.

articles.title: Metabolomic Analysis of Patients with Coronary Artery Disease and Acute Myocardial Infarction by Using Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy.
articles.abstract: This cross-sectional exploratory study investigates the potential of metabolomics to differentiate between stable coronary artery disease (CAD) and acute myocardial infarction (AMI) through Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopic analysis. The study identifies distinct metabolic profiles for each condition, revealing significant variations in metabolite levels, particularly lactic acid, which is a key metabolic product of anaerobic glycolysis, emerges as a prominent marker in AMI patients, reflecting acute ischemic stress and providing insight into adverse outcomes associated with high lactate levels. Another metabolite found in the present study was hypoxanthine, which is key biomarker for myocardial ischemia. These findings underscore the potential of metabolomics in combination with pathway analysis in distinguishing between CAD and AMI and highlight the metabolic dysregulation that occurs in these diseases. Our results suggest that these metabolites could serve as potential biomarkers, paving the way for personalized prognostic and diagnostic strategies. Further large-scale studies are necessary to validate these findings and incorporate them into clinical practice.

articles.title: Semi-automated Generation and Hemodynamic Assessment of Surgical Baffle Geometry for Biventricular Repair.
articles.abstract: Patient-specific computational modeling has emerged as a powerful tool for surgical planning in complex congenital heart disease. One promising application is complex biventricular repair, which often requires construction of a custom intraventricular baffle to establish a physiologic left ventricle-to-aorta outflow pathway. In current practice, baffle geometry is designed and shaped intraoperatively. While existing preoperative modeling tools increasingly support visualization and virtual baffle design, the design process remains predominantly manual, and watertight models for quantitative hemodynamic assessment remain limited. We present a semi-automated computational framework for the design and assessment of patient-specific intraventricular baffles. The method constructs an explicit ventricular septal defect (VSD)-to-aorta flow pathway that preserves native right ventricular myocardial and VSD geometry while reshaping the baffle region to satisfy patient-specific, section-wise area constraints. We retrospectively applied this framework to four patients with double outlet right ventricle (DORV) who had previously undergone biventricular repair. Each generated pathway was evaluated with pulsatile computational fluid dynamics (CFD), producing peak-flow pressure differences of 1.58-5.94 mmHg under the prescribed flow conditions. All modeled pressure differences remained below the 10-mmHg planning benchmark across mesh resolutions and under elevated flow. The current implementation preserves the native VSD and does not model VSD enlargement or conal resection; however, it provides a computational framework through which these interventions could be evaluated in silico. By translating a surgeon-defined baffle boundary into a physiologically constrained, simulation-ready model, this approach enables quantitative preoperative design and CFD-based evaluation of candidate baffle geometries, advancing patient-specific computational planning for biventricular flow restoration in heterogeneous anatomies.

articles.title: Primary Aldosteronism: Evaluation and Management in the Hypertensive Patient.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSEOF REVIEW: Primary aldosteronism (PA) is common, underdiagnosed, and associated with excess cardiorenal risk. We review recent changes in screening, diagnosis, treatment, and implementation.

RECENT FINDINGS: Contemporary guidelines have broadened screening and reduced barriers to aldosterone-to-renin ratio testing through medication-tolerant, assay-aware interpretation. Confirmatory aldosterone suppression testing is increasingly de-emphasized, with selective use or omission in high-probability patients when results are unlikely to change management. Adrenal vein sampling remains standard for most surgical candidates, while molecular imaging is emerging as a noninvasive alternative. Adrenalectomy is preferred for lateralizing disease; mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists remain first-line therapy for bilateral or nonoperative disease, with renin response increasingly used to assess dosing adequacy. Finerenone and aldosterone synthase inhibitors are potential emerging options. PA care is shifting from a rigid multistep workup toward earlier detection and treatment-directed evaluation. Future work should define scalable screening pathways and compare outcomes of emerging diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Gut Microbiota Variation in Relation to Trichuris trichiura Infection Among School-Aged Children in a Helminth-Endemic Area of Indonesia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Soil-transmitted helminth infections remain a public health concern in endemic regions and may be associated with changes in gut microbial communities. However, evidence regarding gut microbiota variation in relation to Trichuris trichiura infection remains inconsistent, particularly among children in endemic settings. This study aimed to investigate differences in gut bacterial composition and diversity between T. trichiura-infected and helminth-uninfected school-aged children in rural Indonesia.

METHODS: A cross-sectional microbiome study was conducted among 24 school-aged children in West Java, Indonesia, comprising 15 with T. trichiura monoinfection and nine without detectable intestinal helminth infections. Infection status was determined using duplicate Kato-Katz examinations. Gut bacterial communities were characterized using full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing on the Oxford Nanopore platform. Taxonomic composition, alpha and beta diversity, and differential abundance were compared between groups.

RESULTS: Bacillota predominated in both groups, accounting for 86.20% and 79.82% of bacterial relative abundance in infected and uninfected children, respectively. Lachnospiraceae accounted for 57.20% and 44.59%, respectively. At the family level, Shannon diversity was significantly lower in infected children (1.720 ± 0.201 vs. 1.962 ± 0.280; p = 0.041), whereas Simpson diversity did not differ significantly (p = 0.073). PERMANOVA identified an association between infection status and bacterial community composition (R2 = 0.126, p = 0.0077). No individual bacterial taxa remained statistically significant after false discovery rate correction.

CONCLUSIONS: Trichuris trichiura infection status was associated with differences in gut bacterial diversity and overall community composition, although no robust taxon-specific associations were identified. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to confirm these exploratory findings.

articles.title: Can Esophagectomy be Safely Avoided After Clinical Complete Response in Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma? Response Assessment, Active Surveillance, and Salvage in the Immunotherapy Era.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Clinical complete response (cCR) after chemoradiotherapy or immunotherapy-containing neoadjuvant treatment is increasingly encountered in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). We examine whether esophagectomy can be safely deferred or avoided in selected complete responders, distinguishing prediction of pathologic complete response (pCR) from the higher confidence required to omit surgery.

RECENT FINDINGS: The phase III SANO trial showed non-inferior 2-year overall survival with active surveillance versus standard surgery after cCR following neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy, with early quality-of-life benefits; however, approximately three quarters of participants had adenocarcinoma. The ESCC-specific preSINO study showed that bite-on-bite biopsies, endoscopic ultrasonography with fine-needle aspiration, and PET/CT reduce but do not eliminate missed residual disease. In a biomarker analysis nested within preSINO, adding tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) to conventional evaluation increased sensitivity for non-pCR to approximately 92-93%; this is not independent validation. Neoadjuvant immunotherapy, including ESCORT-NEO and PALACE regimens, has increased pCR rates, but response-assessment accuracy has not been validated in these treatment contexts. Earlier ESCC trials of definitive chemoradiotherapy with selective salvage established organ preservation conceptually; the modern question is whether surveillance can be individualized after rigorously defined cCR. Active surveillance after cCR is now a credible option within structured programs, but routine omission of esophagectomy in ESCC is not yet standard care. Organ preservation should be viewed as a longitudinal residual-disease exclusion program with predefined rescue triggers rather than a one-time declaration of cCR. ESCC-specific, treatment-context-specific trials integrating standardized endoscopic and nodal assessment, PET/CT, serial ctDNA, and salvage outcomes are needed before immunotherapy-associated cCR can routinely justify nonoperative management.

articles.title: Cell-specific responses to copper stress and cuproptosis in renal fibrosis.
articles.journal: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death
articles.abstract: Renal fibrosis is a common pathological feature of progressive chronic kidney disease (CKD). Its development involves persistent injury to resident renal cells, inflammation, myofibroblast activation, and excessive accumulation of extracellular matrix (ECM). Renal fibrosis is not driven by a single cell type but results from sustained interactions among resident renal cells, infiltrating immune cells, matrix-producing fibroblasts, and other cell populations. Within this multicellular context, cuproptosis, a recently described form of copper-dependent cell death, may contribute to the onset and progression of renal fibrosis by amplifying inflammation, fostering a profibrotic microenvironment, and promoting ECM deposition during kidney injury. Elevated intracellular copper alone, however, is insufficient to trigger cuproptosis. Cellular susceptibility also depends on metabolic state, mitochondrial function, and mitochondrial protein lipoylation. Because renal cell types differ substantially in these biological features, the effects of cuproptosis-related stress are likely to vary across cell populations. This review aims to systematically elucidate the essential prerequisites underlying cuproptosis and its role in renal fibrosis from the perspective of cell type specificity.
