In particular, we highlight the heterogeneity of renal tubular epithelial cells, podocytes, endothelial cells, immune cells, and fibroblasts in terms of energy metabolism, reliance on mitochondrial function, copper-handling capacity, and protein lipoylation to discuss how these differences may give rise to distinct injury patterns and pathological consequences of cuproptosis-related stress. Finally, this review summarizes potential therapeutic strategies targeting copper homeostasis and cuproptosis-related stress to attenuate renal fibrosis, offering new directions for understanding the mechanisms of renal fibrosis and developing more cell-specific interventions.

articles.title: "Fatal venous thromboembolism and divergent phenotypes in DOCK8 deficiency: a three-sibling case series".
articles.abstract: Dedicator of Cytokinesis 8 (DOCK8) deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive combined immunodeficiency characterized by early-onset eczema, recurrent bacterial, viral, and fungal infections, and an increased risk of malignancy. The disease arises from impaired actin cytoskeletal regulation, leading to defective immune cell migration and T-cell activation, together with the development of a Th2-skewed immune response. In this case report, we present three siblings with genetically confirmed DOCK8 deficiency and multisystem involvement. All patients presented with early-onset atopic dermatitis, recurrent respiratory tract infections, and failure to thrive. Bronchiectasis and severe viral infections were observed in all three patients. Ocular involvement developed in two patients: one experienced Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis resulting in persistent visual impairment, while the other developed corneal perforation secondary to herpesvirus infection. One patient developed iatrogenic Cushing syndrome due to prolonged topical corticosteroid use. In the same patient, catheter-related superficial thrombophlebitis progressed to deep vein thrombosis and cerebral venous sinus thrombosis, with a fatal outcome complicated by probable pulmonary thromboembolism. This case series highlights the severe multisystem involvement and risk of irreversible organ damage associated with DOCK8 deficiency, and underscores the critical importance of early diagnosis and timely planning of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) as the only curative therapeutic approach.

articles.title: Oncologic efficacy and safety of stereotactic body radiotherapy for oligometastatic non-small cell lung cancer: a systemic meta-analysis.
authors: Korean Cancer Association Oligometastasis Working Group
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: With the increasing clinical interest on local consolidative therapies for oligometastasis (OM), stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) has emerged as a definitive and optimal treatment modality. This study stratifies oligoprogressive (OPD), oligorecurrent (ORD), and oligopersistent (OPSD) states-alongside single-lesion subgroup analyses-to systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of SBRT for oligometastatic NSCLC.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This meta-analysis was conducted utilizing the Pubmed, Embase and Medline. The quantitative synthesis included 18 eligible studies comprising a total of 1,105 patients. The clinical endpoints assessed were overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), local control (LC), and the incidence of severe (grade 3 or higher) treatment-related toxicities.

RESULTS: The pooled estimates demonstrated robust oncological outcomes; 2-year OS of 60.0% (95% CI, 50.4-68.8%), 1-year PFS of 65.8% (95% CI, 52.7-76.8%), and 2-year LC rate of 74.2% (95% CI, 63.9-82.4%). The incidence of severe toxicities (grade ≥ 3) was 4.5%, predominantly manifesting as radiation pneumonitis and esophagitis. Subgroup analyses revealed that a higher prevalence of single-metastatic lesions (> 59%) exhibited a borderline positive trend toward superior 2-year OS (67.5% vs. 47.8%, p = 0.069).

CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis indicates that SBRT yields favorable treatment outcomes for patients with oligometastatic NSCLC with manageable toxicities. When anatomically feasible, delivering an ablative dose-100 Gy10 in biologically effective dose-is recommended. Furthermore, tailoring SBRT strategies by oligometastatic subtype-upfront radical SBRT for synchronous disease/ORD and salvage SBRT for OPSD/OPD-is essential to maximize the treatment efficacy.

articles.title: Inclisiran attenuates myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury by inhibiting macrophage M1 polarization.
articles.journal: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death
articles.abstract: Macrophage polarization is pivotal in myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury. Inclisiran is a small interfering RNA agent that lowers low-density lipoprotein cholesterol by targeting proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9). However, whether Inclisiran exerts LDL-C-independent cardioprotective effects within the acute I/R window remains unclear. In this study, wild-type C57BL/6J mice were pretreated with Inclisiran before I/R surgery. Myocardial injury was assessed by echocardiography, laser speckle contrast imaging, and TTC/Evans Blue staining. Macrophage polarization and its direct impact on cardiomyocytes or fibroblasts were investigated in co-culture system in vitro. Target gene screening was performed by chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP)-sequencing, and transcriptional regulation was validated by dual-luciferase assay and ChIP-qPCR. Protein interaction was confirmed by molecular docking, surface plasmon resonance, and co-immunoprecipitation. Our results demonstrated that Inclisiran significantly attenuated myocardial injury and dysfunction, inhibited macrophage M1 polarization, reduced cardiomyocyte apoptosis, and suppressed fibroblast activation. Mechanistically, Inclisiran disrupted the direct interaction between PCSK9 and JNK, thereby blocking the HIF-1α-mediated transcriptional regulation of Myo1d, and ultimately suppressing macrophage M1 polarization. In conclusion, Inclisiran alleviates myocardial I/R injury by targeting the JNK-HIF-1α-Myo1d signaling axis. These findings identify a previously unrecognized cardioprotective mechanism that is LDL-C-independent within the acute I/R window, suggesting Inclisiran as a promising therapeutic strategy for ischemic cardiomyopathy.

articles.title: Evaluating clinical outcomes associated with regional versus general anesthesia approach in blunt geriatric trauma patients undergoing major operative procedures for hip fractures.
articles.journal: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal anesthetic approach for operative management of geriatric hip fractures remains debated, particularly among geriatric trauma patients with limited physiologic reserve and high comorbidity burden. This study evaluated perioperative outcomes associated with anesthesia type in geriatric patients undergoing surgery for isolated hip fractures.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted to evaluate geriatric trauma patients (≥ 65 years) with isolated, blunt, moderate to severe (ISS ≥ 9) hip fractures utilizing the ACS-TQIP database from 2017 to 2023. Patients were grouped by anesthetic technique: regional or general anesthesia. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included regional anesthesia failure rate, complication rates, hospital length of stay (LOS), and ventilator-free days (VFDs).

RESULTS: Among geriatric trauma patients with moderate to severe hip fractures undergoing hip fixation, no statistically significant association was detected between regional and general anesthesia regarding in-hospital mortality (aOR: 0.316, 95% CI: 0.076-1.311, p = 0.112) or VFDs (β = 4.548, 95% CI - 2.478-11.573, p = 0.202). Also, no statistically significant association was detected between patients receiving regional compared to those receiving general anesthesia for major complications, including DVT, PE, and stroke. The conversion-to-general-anesthesia rate was 0.96%.

CONCLUSION: No statistically significant differences in perioperative outcomes were detected between regional and general anesthesia among patients with moderate-to-severe hip fractures undergoing major operative fixation. Anesthetic selection should remain individualized.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, Therapeutic/Care Management.

articles.title: Temporal fluctuations in retinal artery occlusions: an 11-year German cohort study.
articles.journal: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Cardiovascular events have been shown to follow seasonal and monthly distributions. It is unclear whether this applies to retinal vascular diseases. This study aims to determine the existence of seasonal variations in the onset of retinal artery occlusions (RAO) in a European population.

METHODS: This retrospective, monocentric study included 646 eyes of 646 patients who were treated for RAO at the University Hospital Münster, Germany, between 2014 and 2024. Data on the exact diagnosis, day of presentation, intake of anticoagulation (AC) and general patient characteristics were collected. To determine seasonal variations in the presentation of RAO Chi-Square Test for specified proportions and Poisson regression were applied. Additional subgroup analyses further distinguished between central retinal artery occlusions (CRAO) and branch retinal artery occlusions (BRAO) and assessed whether pre-existing AC or antiplatelet (AP) medication status was associated with the temporal distribution of RAO presentations.

RESULTS: No significant seasonal variation in the occurrence of RAO was observed (χ² p = 0.11; Poisson regression p = 0.24). Monthly analysis revealed significant variation according to the chi-square test (p = 0.03), which was not confirmed by Poisson regression (p = 0.07). In the CRAO subgroup, no significant seasonal variation was observed (χ² p = 0.22; Poisson regression p = 0.22), whereas monthly variation was significant in both the chi-square analysis (p = 0.03) and Poisson regression (p = 0.01). No significant seasonal or monthly variation was observed for BRAO. Pre-existing AC/AP medication status was not significantly associated with the seasonal distribution of RAO presentations in any of the analyzed groups.

CONCLUSION: This study characterizes temporal fluctuations in RAO presentations and highlights the necessity for further investigations into potential underlying pathophysiological mechanisms, in order to better understand patterns of RAO presentations and their potential clinical relevance.

articles.title: Determinants of surgical morbidity following glioblastoma resection: an 839-patient contemporary neurosurgical cohort.
articles.abstract: In glioblastoma surgery, neurosurgeons must balance the oncologic benefit of maximal safe cytoreduction against the risk of postoperative morbidity. We evaluated surgery-related complications, unplanned readmission, and functional outcomes, and assessed whether reoperation, awake mapping, or greater extent of resection increase morbidity. We performed a retrospective single-center study of 839 adults who underwent supratentorial glioblastoma resections (first-line or recurrent) between 2000 and 2024. Primary endpoints were regional or systemic complications within 90 days, unplanned readmission within 30 days, ≥ 30-point KPS score decline, and KPS score < 70 at three postoperative months. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of postoperative morbidity, with particular focus on surgical strategies (reoperation, awake mapping, extent of resection). Surgery-related morbidity was infrequent. Across all models, increased odds of complications, readmission, or functional decline were independently associated with older age, frailty, baseline KPS score < 70, larger tumor volume, midline mass effect, multilobar involvement, tumor-related epilepsy, and preoperative neurological deficit. In contrast, reoperation, awake craniotomy, and greater extent of resection were not associated with higher complications, readmission, or functional decline rates. In this large contemporary cohort, durable postoperative morbidity was determined primarily by baseline physiological reserve (frailty, low KPS score, preoperative deficits) and disease burden (volume, multilobar spread, midline crossing), whereas reoperation, awake mapping, and maximal resection were not. These findings support frailty-informed selection and function-preserving maximal safe resection to preserve independence, enable timely adjuvant therapy, and ultimately improve survival in glioblastoma patients.

articles.title: A Case of Facial Alternaria alternata Infection in an Immunocompetent Male with Albinism.
articles.abstract: The patient was a 26-year-old immunocompetent albino male engaged in breeding work, who presented with pruritic facial rashes for 2 months. The diagnosis was confirmed by histopathological examination, periodic acid-Schiff staining, mycological tests and gene sequencing of the lesion culture. The patient was treated with oral itraconazole combined with topical antifungal cream, and obtained complete remission without recurrence during the 8-year follow-up. This case suggests that occupational exposure can increase the susceptibility to alternariosis in immunocompetent people, and cutaneous alternariosis should be considered for refractory inflammatory facial lesions.

articles.title: Clinical phenotype and predictors of recurrence in childhood IgA vasculitis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: IgA vasculitis (IgAV) is generally considered a self-limited disease in childhood; however, recurrent episodes may occur during the disease course. The clinical phenotype and associated factors of recurrent disease remain to be clearly defined. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical characteristics of recurrent IgAV and compare patients with and without recurrence to identify potential predictors of recurrence.This retrospective medical record review study included children diagnosed with IgAV between 2015 and 2025 according to the EULAR/PRINTO/PRES classification criteria. Patients with incomplete data, follow-up duration < 6 months, or alternative diagnoses were excluded. Clinical manifestations, laboratory findings, treatment characteristics, and recurrence patterns were compared between patients with and without recurrence. Cox proportional hazards regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of recurrence.A total of 417 children with IgAV were included, of whom 50 (12.0%) developed recurrence. Recurrent disease was characterized by more severe cutaneous involvement, with significantly higher frequencies of widespread or bullous cutaneous manifestations, as well as higher frequencies of arthritis and microscopic hematuria at presentation. Preceding infection was significantly more common among recurrent patients and independently increased relapse risk (HR: 2.33, 95% CI: 1.20-4.51). Microscopic hematuria (HR: 3.00, 95% CI: 1.62-5.57), widespread/bullous cutaneous involvement (HR: 2.65, 95% CI: 1.47-4.80), and joint involvement (HR: 2.98, 95% CI: 1.55-5.73) also emerged as independent predictors of recurrence. In addition, lower monocyte counts were independently associated with relapse risk (HR: 0.82, 95% CI: 0.71-0.95). Colchicine use was significantly more frequent among recurrent patients, likely reflecting therapeutic preferences related to recurrent cutaneous involvement.

CONCLUSIONS: Preceding infection, microscopic hematuria, extensive or bullous skin involvement, joint involvement, and lower monocyte counts may help identify patients at higher risk of recurrence.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • IgA vasculitis (IgAV) is the most common childhood vasculitis, and recurrence may occur during follow-up. • Renal and gastrointestinal involvement have previously been associated with recurrent disease; however, reported risk factors remain inconsistent across studies. • Data regarding the clinical phenotype and predictors of recurrent childhood IgAV are still limited.

WHAT IS NEW: • Recurrent childhood IgAV was associated with more severe cutaneous manifestations and more frequent joint involvement at presentation, with arthritis identified as a predictor of recurrence. • Lower monocyte counts were independently associated with recurrence, suggesting that readily accessible hematological parameters may contribute to early risk stratification in childhood IgAV. • Recurrent episodes were predominantly cutaneous, and the increased use of colchicine appeared to reflect therapeutic preferences related to recurrent cutaneous manifestations rather than increased systemic disease severity.

articles.title: Effectiveness of home-based exercise interventions on cardiorespiratory fitness and cancer treatment-related cardiovascular toxicity in cancer survivors exposed to cardiotoxic therapies: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the effectiveness of home-based exercise (HBE) interventions on cardiorespiratory fitness and cancer treatment-related cardiovascular toxicity (CTR-CVT) in cancer survivors.

METHODS: A comprehensive search of seven electronic databases was conducted for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published from January 2000 to October 2025. The participants were cancer survivors who had received cardiotoxic therapies. The interventions were structured HBE programmes. Eligible studies were those that reported on any outcomes related to CTR-CVT. The primary outcomes included direct cardiotoxicity parameters (e.g., left ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF] and global longitudinal strain [GLS]) and cardiac biomarkers (e.g., troponins and B-type natriuretic peptide); clinical cardiovascular events (e.g., heart failure and arrhythmias); cardiorespiratory fitness (e.g., peak oxygen uptake [VO2 peak]); and (d) functional capacity (e.g., the six-minute walk test [6MWT]). Two researchers independently performed the study selection, data extraction, and methodological quality assessment. Meta-analyses were conducted using R software.

RESULTS: Ten RCTs involving 851 participants were included. The meta-analysis demonstrated that the HBE interventions significantly improved VO2 peak (MD = 2.35 mL/kg/min, 95% CI: 1.26 to 3.43, p < 0.001), which indicated improved cardiorespiratory fitness. Subgroup analysis found larger effects for longer-duration interventions (24 to 52 weeks), mHealth use, and cancer Stage III/IV. Evidence on direct cardiotoxicity parameters and biomarkers was limited, as only one study assessed these outcomes. No significant improvements were found in the 6MWT or health-related quality of life (HRQoL).

CONCLUSION: While HBE improved cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2 peak) and mitigated functional decline in cancer survivors, its ability to prevent CTR-CVT was unproven. Future adequately powered trials should incorporate direct cardiotoxicity assessments to establish true cardioprotective efficacy and implementation studies to optimise real-world delivery.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: not applicable.

articles.title: Nutraceutical and herbal interventions targeting inflammation and oxidative stress in PCOS-associated insulin resistance.
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a complex endocrine and metabolic disorder affecting women of reproductive age. It is commonly associated with insulin resistance, hyperandrogenism, chronic low-grade inflammation, and oxidative stress. These factors contribute to metabolic dysfunction and increase the risk of developing type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular complications. This narrative review critically evaluates the available evidence regarding nutraceutical and herbal interventions targeting insulin resistance, inflammation, and oxidative stress associated with PCOS. A comprehensive literature search was conducted using PubMed, Google Scholar, EMBASE, Scopus, and CNKI databases, covering studies from database inception through 12 July to 21 November 2025 with keywords including PCOS, insulin resistance, hyperinsulinemia, oxidative stress, diabetes mellitus, nutritional supplements, and herbs. Relevant original research articles, randomized clinical trials, observational studies, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses were considered, and the available evidence was interpreted according to study design and evidence level. Evidence from preclinical studies and human clinical investigations indicates that selected nutraceutical and herbal interventions may influence metabolic, inflammatory, oxidative stress-related, hormonal, and reproductive parameters in PCOS. However, the magnitude and consistency of these effects vary substantially depending on the intervention, formulation, dose, treatment duration, participant characteristics, and the outcome assessed. Improvements in surrogate biochemical measures, such as HOMA-IR or inflammatory and oxidative stress biomarkers, should not be interpreted as direct evidence of improved fertility, reduced cardiovascular risk, or prevention of long-term diabetes. Therefore, the available evidence should be interpreted according to study design and evidence level, with greater weight given to findings from well-designed randomized clinical trials and systematic reviews or meta-analyses than to isolated preclinical or small clinical studies.

articles.title: Fixation of patellar fractures using bioabsorbable hydroxyapatite/poly-L-lactide cannulated screws and subperiosteal nonabsorbable sutures.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Bioabsorbable implants offer a promising alternative to metallic fixation for patellar fractures, potentially avoiding hardware-related complications. In 2023, a new generation of bioabsorbable hydroxyapatite/poly-L-lactide (HA/PLLA) cannulated screws was introduced, featuring a low-profile (2 mm) trident-shaped head and increased root diameter for enhanced strength. This study evaluates the clinical outcomes of a surgical technique combining these redesigned screws with subperiosteal nonabsorbable sutures.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Between April 2023 and May 2025, 19 consecutive patients with transverse patellar fractures (AO/OTA 34-C1/C2) underwent open reduction and internal fixation. Two bioabsorbable cannulated screws were used. High-strength nonabsorbable sutures were passed through the screw channels and a central bone tunnel using a double-loop sliding knot for compression. The sutures were systematically routed subperiosteally to minimize tissue irritation. Full weight-bearing with a brace began on postoperative day one. Clinical and radiographic outcomes were assessed. This study was approved by the institutional review board of Kainan Hospital.

RESULTS: The mean maximum articular surface gap was 8.7 ± 5.2 mm. The mean follow-up was 8.6 ± 3.0 months. Bone union was achieved in all cases. At the final follow-up, the mean knee flexion was 138.7° ± 13.0° and extension was - 1.6° ± 3.4°. No postoperative complications, including infection, loss of reduction, screw breakage, or symptomatic hardware irritation, were observed during the follow-up period. No reoperations were required during the follow-up period.

CONCLUSIONS: All patients achieved bone union. No major complications or reoperations were observed during the follow-up period. These preliminary findings suggest that this technique may be feasible for transverse patellar fractures.

articles.title: Singing-based interventions for motor and non-motor symptoms in Parkinson's disease: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by disabling motor and non-motor symptoms. Although pharmacological and rehabilitation interventions improve many motor and non-motor symptoms, persistent impairments commonly remain in domains, including speech, swallowing, gait, and balance, particularly as the disease progresses. For this reason, over the past few years, alternative rehabilitative approaches, such as singing-based interventions, have been used with the aim of addressing symptoms, such as speech impairment, swallowing difficulties, respiratory dysfunction, and mood.

OBJECTIVE: We aim to review the evidences on the efficacy of singing interventions on motor and non-motor symptoms in patients with PD.

METHODS: A comprehensive literature search of PubMed and Google Scholar was conducted for interventional studies published until December 2025. Results were summarized into five symptom domains: motor function, voice quality, breathing, swallowing, and quality of life.

RESULTS: Twenty-six studies involving 1057 patients with PD were included. Singing-based interventions were associated with improvements in motor symptoms, gait, posture, voice quality, respiratory control, and maximum phonation time. Several studies also reported enhanced psychological well-being, social connectedness, and quality of life, with reductions in stress, anxiety, and depressive symptoms. Evidence regarding swallowing outcomes was limited and inconsistent. Considerable heterogeneity in study design, intervention protocols, and outcome measures precluded meta-analysis.

CONCLUSION: Singing is a promising adjunct therapy for PD rehabilitation, particularly in domains less responsive to pharmacological treatment. Further high-quality research is needed to establish standardized protocols and assess long-term benefits.

articles.title: Mitochondrial bioenergetics deficit linked to endothelial dysfunction and ER stress induced by obesity in coronary arteries.
articles.abstract: Obesity and metabolic syndrome are major drivers of metabolic heart disease, characterized by profound cardiac energy deficits, structural remodeling, and progression to heart failure. While myocardial mitochondrial dysfunction in obesity is well established, its impact on coronary arteries remains underexplored. This study investigates how high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity affects coronary bioenergetics, mitochondrial REDOX balance, and endothelial function. Male Wistar rats were fed a HFD (60% kcal fat) for 15-16 weeks after weaning as a model of diet-induced obesity, and tunicamycin-treated rats as a model of chemically-induced ER stress in vivo were used. Myograph experiments to assess coronary endothelial function, reactive oxygen species (ROS) measurements, and mitochondrial respiration experiments in a Seahorse analyzer were comprehensively conducted. After 15-16 weeks of HFD rats developed metabolic syndrome features, including weight gain, hyperglycemia, hypertriglyceridemia, and elevated lactate. Coronary arteries exhibited endothelial dysfunction, evidenced by impaired acetylcholine- and isoprenaline-induced relaxations, mediated by NADPH oxidase 1 (NOX1)-derived ROS, as selective NOX1 inhibition (NoxA1ds-tat) restored vasodilation. Mitochondrial ROS (mtROS) levels increased in arteries but not myocardium, along with preserved hydrogen peroxide (H2O2)-mediated signaling. Protein analysis revealed down-regulated endothelial NOX4 and manganese superoxide dismutase (MnSOD), reduced respiratory complex IV (COX-IV) and uncoupling protein 2 (UCP2), and blunted mitochondrial respiration across basal, ATP-linked, and maximal states. Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1-alpha (PGC-1α) up-regulation indicated adaptive biogenesis. HFD also activated endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress. Notably, tunicamycin-induced ER stress recapitulated these deficits, impairing relaxation, H2O2 production, and respiration, yet up-regulating protective NOX4/MnSOD/PGC-1α. These findings couple coronary mitochondrial impairment to obesity-driven heart disease, highlighting impaired coronary bioenergetics, mitochondrial oxidative stress, and ER stress as key mechanisms. Thus, coronary artery mitochondria emerge as therapeutic targets to improve microvascular perfusion and mitigate progression to heart failure in obesity.

articles.title: Coronary artery calcification is not associated with survival in advanced gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer: a secondary analysis of the EXPAND trial.
articles.journal: Journal of cancer research and clinical oncology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Computed tomography (CT) is the clinical standard for staging of gastrointestinal cancer. Previous studies have highlighted the prognostic significance of coronary artery calcification (CAC) detected by CT in various types of cancer. However, the prognostic role of CAC scoring in gastrointestinal cancers is still unclear. The aim of this study was to investigate the impact of CT-defined CAC on overall survival (OS) in patients with advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer.

METHODS: CAC was semiquantitatively measured using the visual Weston method on baseline CT scans in 785 patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer from the phase III EXPAND trial. This present study is a secondary analysis of the base line CT images. In the original analysis patients were randomly assigned to first-line treatment with cisplatin/capecitabin ± cetuximab. The primary endpoint of the current subanalysis is the OS. For statistical analysis group differences were calculated using the Mann-Whitney-U test and ANOVA test. Kaplan-Meier curves and multivariable Cox regression analysis were used to test the effect of CAC on mortality.

RESULTS: The median CAC score was 1 (IQR 0; 3). A total of 337 patients (42.9%) had no visible CAC (CAC score 0). Male patients had statistically significant higher CAC score compared to female patients (median 1 versus 0, p < 0.0001). In univariable Cox regression CAC showed no significant association with survival when analysed as a continuous value (HR: 0.99, 95% CI: 0.96-1.02, p = 0.74), and when dichotomized for absence and presence of calcification (HR:1.08, 95% CI: 0.92-1.26, p = 0.34). Similar results were identified in further subgroup analyses.

CONCLUSION: CT-defined CAC scoring has no relevant prognostic impact in advanced gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer undergoing first-line chemotherapy. The present study cannot confirm the promising results for CAC scoring in lung cancer patients.

articles.title: Kidney considerations in pediatric neurocritical care: acute kidney injury, osmotherapy, sodium disorders, and kidney replacement therapy.
articles.abstract: Acute brain injury in children is often accompanied by kidney complications that influence fluid balance, osmotic stability, medication exposure, and the safety of neuroprotective therapy. This Educational Review narrows the discussion to kidney considerations that arise during pediatric neurocritical care: acute kidney injury surveillance, intracranial-pressure-directed osmotherapy, sodium disorders, and kidney replacement therapy. Pediatric evidence is prioritized. When evidence comes from adult neurocritical care, adult critical care nephrology, consensus guidance, or physiologic reasoning, this is identified explicitly. The K-I-D-S structure is used as an educational organizing device rather than a validated clinical decision tool: Kidney injury recognized early; ICP-directed, individualized osmotherapy; Dysnatremia interpreted physiologically; and Safe kidney replacement therapy prescription. The review emphasizes that sustained hypernatremia should not be treated as an independent endpoint unless there is an active neurologic indication, and that measured serum osmolality, calculated osmolarity, and the osmolal gap should be distinguished. During prolonged osmotherapy, kidney function, fluid balance, sodium, osmolality, acid-base status, hemodynamics, and medication exposure should be reassessed; chloride trends may be considered as one component of this broader safety assessment, recognizing the limited pediatric evidence. Practical tables provide evidence-based labels for major recommendations and offer quantitative safety anchors for hypertonic saline dosing, sodium correction, and mannitol monitoring, together with practical elements for a neurocritical-care-adapted kidney replacement therapy prescription. The goal is not to create a new care standard, but to help nephrologists, intensivists, neurologists, neurosurgeons, and trainees recognize where kidney physiology modifies brain-directed therapy and where pediatric evidence remains insufficient.

articles.title: The acute kidney injury - acute kidney disease - chronic kidney disease continuum: pediatric perspective.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is emerging as a significant contributor to long-term kidney morbidity in children. Advances in critical care have improved survival, but a growing proportion of pediatric AKI survivors remain at risk of progressing to chronic kidney disease (CKD). The concept of acute kidney disease (AKD), defined as persistent kidney dysfunction up to 90 days after AKI, has emerged as a key intermediary phase in this continuum. This review outlines current evidence on the epidemiology, pathophysiology and outcomes of the AKI-AKD-CKD continuum in children and the relevance of AKD within this continuum. Mechanisms underlying AKI-CKD transition include maladaptive hyperfiltration, persistent paracrine signalling and vascular rarefaction, which together drive progressive nephron loss and fibrosis. Pediatric studies, though limited and heterogeneous, consistently demonstrate an increased risk of CKD, hypertension and subclinical kidney dysfunction following AKI. Early risk stratification, structured follow-up and integration of emerging biomarkers may improve outcomes by identifying children at the highest risk for CKD progression. Strengthening post-AKI care pathways should be a priority in pediatric nephrology.

articles.title: Urinary peptidome analysis of kidney failure in children with obstructive uropathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children with congenital obstructive uropathy (OU) who survive infancy are at increased risk for progressive chronic kidney disease (CKD), but disease onset and severity vary widely, highlighting the need for improved risk stratification. The present study evaluated whether urinary peptidome analysis could predict progression to kidney failure (KF) in children with OU.

METHODS: Urinary peptidome analysis was performed on 151 samples from children with OU enrolled in the Chronic Kidney Disease in Children (CKiD) Study. Progression to KF was defined as a ≥50% decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate or initiation of kidney replacement therapy. Peptides were incorporated into a random survival forest model developed in a training cohort and tested in an independent validation cohort. Performance was compared to the 5-year Kidney Failure Risk Equation (KFRE).

RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 5.6 years, 33% (50/151) of children progressed to KF. Iterative cross-validation identified 47 urinary peptides predictive of KF within 5 years in the training set of 101 patients. The model achieved an area under the curve of 88.6% (95% CI: 75.2-97.8), with sensitivity of 66.7% and specificity of 88.0% in the validation cohort of 50 patients, demonstrating similar overall performance, but higher specificity and lower sensitivity, than the KFRE. Independent and external validation in 162 patients with CKD other than OU confirmed the performance of the peptide model.

CONCLUSIONS: Urinary peptidomics identifies children with mild to moderate OU-related CKD at risk for KF with high specificity and moderate sensitivity. Although overall performance was comparable to the KFRE, the peptide model's specificity may be particularly useful for stratifying patients at intermediate KFRE risk. A higher resolution version of the Graphical abstract is available as Supplementary information.

articles.title: Integrating psychosocial and clinical care for children with chronic kidney disease.
Hydrogel-extracellular vesicle platforms: orchestrating the osteogenic microenvironment for cell-free bone regeneration.
articles.abstract: Bone defects remain difficult to treat because impaired vascularization, inflammation, infection and metabolic dysfunction limit endogenous repair. Unencapsulated extracellular vesicles (EVs) may also be rapidly cleared from defect sites. Hydrogel-EV systems combine vesicle bioactivity with local retention, controlled release and structural support, offering a cell-free strategy for bone regeneration. This review summarizes EV sources, separation, characterization and cargo, and outlines the endosomal biogenesis of exosomes. We examine EV-mediated regulation of osteogenesis, angiogenesis, immunity and osteoclast-mediated resorption. Hydrogel materials, EV-loading approaches, passive and stimuli-responsive release, and methods for evaluating EVs within hydrogels are discussed. Applications in uncomplicated, infected and diabetes-associated bone defects are compared according to their pathological microenvironments. Translational barriers include heterogeneous EV preparations, inconsistent separation and dosing standards, inadequate mechanical performance, and mismatched hydrogel degradation and bone-healing kinetics. Insufficient biodistribution and long-term safety data further limit clinical translation. This review provides a framework for developing hydrogel-EV platforms for bone regeneration.

articles.title: Benson relaxation technique for perioperative anxiety and depressive symptoms in patients undergoing brain tumor surgery: a clinical trial.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients undergoing craniotomy for brain tumors confront psychophysiological crisis. Managing perioperative distress poses a clinical paradox, as standard pharmacological sedatives are carefully restricted based on neurological status and institutional protocols to avoid masking critical postoperative neurological signs. This study investigated the efficacy of the Benson relaxation technique (BRT), a nonpharmacological mind-body intervention, on perioperative anxiety and depressive symptoms in this vulnerable population.

METHODS: In this clinical trial, out of 84 patients assessed for eligibility, 74 eligible patients undergoing brain tumor resection were allocated to either the BRT intervention group (n = 37) or the control group (n = 37). The intervention group completed supervised BRT sessions (muscle relaxation, diaphragmatic breathing, and word repetition) on the evening of ICU admission, 60 min preoperatively, and 24 h postoperatively. Both groups received routine care, and anxiety and depressive symptoms were evaluated at identical time points (baseline on the evening of ICU admission prior to the intervention, 30 min preoperatively, and 24 h postoperatively). Data were analyzed using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA).

RESULTS: Seventy patients completed the trial (35 per group). At 24 h postoperatively, ANCOVA adjusted for baseline scores showed that the BRT group had significantly lower anxiety scores compared to the control group, with an adjusted mean difference of - 4.16 points (95% CI, - 5.40 to - 2.93; P < 0.001). Regarding depressive symptoms, baseline scores were below the threshold for clinically significant symptoms (HADS-D < 8) in both cohorts; however, at 24 h postoperatively, the BRT group had significantly lower adjusted depressive symptom scores than the control group, with an adjusted mean difference of - 2.32 points (95% CI, - 3.51 to - 1.12; P < 0.001), indicating a preventive effect against postoperative reactive depressive symptoms.

CONCLUSION: The Benson relaxation technique is a safe, feasible, and well-tolerated nurse-led mind-body strategy that effectively mitigates perioperative anxiety and reduces postoperative depressive symptoms without adverse events. These findings support integrating structured nonpharmacological modalities into neurosurgical care.

articles.title: [Recognize endangerment to child welfare-The special role of anesthesiology].
articles.abstract: Child maltreatment including neglect is not always recognized even within the healthcare system. Anesthesiologists have specific windows of opportunity during the preoperative assessment of the medical history and parent-child interaction, undressing and monitoring, airway management, positioning, recovery and critical care. These enable observations which in other treatment situations would remain hidden. Bruising in non-mobile infants, unusual injury locations, intraoral lesions, accident mechanisms inconsistent with developmental abilities and so-called sentinel injuries require particular attention. For clinicians, the TEN-4-FACESp rule provides an easy to remember practical aid for structured classification of conspicuous bruising patterns. It does not replace clinical judgment or medical child protection expertise and has not been validated as a perioperative screening tool. The task of anesthesiologists is not to independently conduct a forensic investigation but to recognize relevant warning signs, objectively document findings and transmit concerns through established interdisciplinary safeguarding pathways. In Germany, § 4 of the Act on Cooperation and Information in Child Protection (KKG) provides a graded procedure including pseudonymized expert consultation and, in situations of urgent danger, prompt notification of the youth welfare office. This narrative review summarizes the anesthesiology-specific literature and proposes a pragmatic perioperative algorithm for action for suspected child maltreatment. Practical point-of-care aids such as TEN-4-FACESp and anesthesiology-specific pocket cards can make warning signals and action pathways immediately available during the treatment and therefore support awareness and clinical confidence.

articles.title: Gout as a risk factor for lower-extremity amputation in diabetes: a nationwide, register-based case-control study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: Non-healing diabetic foot ulcers are a major precursor to lower-extremity amputation (LEA) in diabetes, and gout may be an overlooked contributor. We hypothesised that individuals with both diabetes and gout have a higher risk of LEA than those with diabetes alone, with the strongest effect at more distal amputation levels.

METHODS: In a nationwide case-control study of 601,541 individuals with type 2 diabetes, we identified 4912 cases with LEA and 39,101 age- and sex-matched control participants. Gout exposure was determined using ICD-10 diagnoses and Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical codes for urate-lowering therapy. Associations were estimated using conditional logistic regression, adjusting for diabetes duration, peripheral arterial disease, acute myocardial infarction and late diabetes complications.

RESULTS: Gout was associated with an increased risk of LEA (OR 1.85, 95% CI 1.69, 2.02) in unadjusted analyses, and the association remained significant after full adjustment (OR 1.53, 95% CI 1.37, 1.69). A significant trend (p=0.03) was observed across amputation levels, with potentially higher risk at more anatomically distal sites although no statistically significant differences were observed between individual amputation levels: OR 1.37 (95% CI 1.12, 1.68) for above-knee amputations, increasing to OR 1.65 (95% CI 1.32, 2.05) for toe amputations.

CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: Co-existing gout is an independent risk factor for LEA in individuals with type 2 diabetes. The risk is elevated across all amputation levels, with the most pronounced effect potentially being at distal anatomical sites. These findings highlight the need for increased awareness of gout when managing individuals with type 2 diabetes at risk of LEA.

articles.title: CT-fibrosis score: development and internal validation for identifying advanced fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Advanced fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) involves metabolic and anatomic remodeling beyond the liver. We developed and internally validated an interpretable CT-based score integrating abdominal body-composition and organ measurements and compared it with the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied 151 patients with biopsy-confirmed MASLD (86 advanced [F3-F4], 65 early-stage [F0-F2] fibrosis). Deep learning-based segmentation quantified abdominal adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, bone, liver, and spleen measurements. The CT-Fibrosis Score was developed using repeated (50×) stratified 5-fold cross-validation, with imputation, standardization, and feature selection confined to each training fold and inner 5-fold cross-validation for hyperparameter selection. Performance was based on out-of-fold predictions and compared with FIB-4 using the DeLong test. Sensitivity analyses addressed missing data, age dependence, and ascites.

RESULTS: Four features were consistently selected: age, bone-to-abdominal-cavity volume ratio, visceral adipose tissue (VAT) density, and spleen index. The CT-Fibrosis Score achieved an out-of-fold AUC of 0.77 (95% CI 0.69-0.85). Among 141 patients with an available FIB-4 score, no significant difference was detected between the CT-Fibrosis Score (AUC 0.76) and FIB-4 (AUC 0.79; difference - 0.03, 95% CI - 0.11 to + 0.04; p = 0.37); this comparison was not powered for non-inferiority. Adding the CT-Fibrosis Score to FIB-4 did not improve discrimination (AUC 0.80 vs. 0.79; difference + 0.003, 95% CI - 0.04 to + 0.05; p = 0.90), with the confidence interval excluding an improvement greater than approximately 0.05.

CONCLUSION: The CT-Fibrosis Score achieved moderate discrimination for advanced fibrosis but did not improve discrimination when added to FIB-4. External validation in an unselected population undergoing CT for non-hepatic indications is required before any opportunistic application.

articles.title: A Mortality Risk Prediction Score for Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a leading cause of pediatric heart failure and carries a substantial risk of death or heart transplantation. In low- and middle-income countries, limited access to advanced heart failure therapies and transplantation highlights the need for simple, reliable tools to identify children at highest risk. Therefore, this study aimed to identify independent predictors of mortality and develop a practical bedside risk score for mortality prediction in children with DCM. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of children with DCM treated at Dr. Sardjito Hospital, Indonesia, between 2016 and 2025. Clinical, electrocardiographic, and echocardiographic variables were evaluated for association with mortality. Independent predictors were incorporated into a point-based risk score using the Spiegelhalter-Knill-Jones method. Discriminative performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic analysis and internal validation. Among 109 children with DCM, mortality was 33.9%. Seven independent predictors of mortality were identified: age ≥ 2 years at diagnosis, New York Heart Association/Ross functional class IV heart failure, malnutrition, requirement for vasoactive support, low-voltage electrocardiography, left ventricular end-diastolic diameter z-score > + 4, and left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 30%. The derived score ranged from - 25 to + 28 points. A threshold score ≥ 11 accurately identified high-risk patients, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.932 (95% CI 0.886-0.977), with 73.0% sensitivity and 95.8% specificity. Internal validation demonstrated sustained performance (AUC 0.921). We developed and validated a simple, bedside mortality risk score with excellent discriminative ability for children with DCM. By relying on routinely available clinical and echocardiographic parameters, this tool enables early identification of high-risk patients and may support timely clinical decision-making and resource allocation, particularly in resource-constrained settings.

articles.title: The Lymphatic System in the Fontan Circulation: Pathophysiology, Imaging and Therapeutic Interventions.
articles.abstract: The Fontan circulation, the definitive palliation for patients with univentricular hearts, produces a unique haemodynamic state characterised by chronically elevated systemic venous pressure, reduced cardiac output and the absence of a subpulmonary ventricular impulse. Because lymphatic drainage depends critically on the pressure gradient between the thoracic duct and the systemic veins, this physiology has profound consequences for the lymphatic system. Over the past decade, the lymphatic circulation has moved from being regarded as a passive bystander to being recognised as a central determinant of Fontan failure. Chronic systemic venous hypertension drives lymphatic overproduction and impaired central drainage, leading to progressive lymphatic congestion that manifests as chylothorax, protein-losing enteropathy (PLE), plastic bronchitis, lymphoedema and Fontan-associated liver disease. Advances in magnetic resonance (MR) lymphangiography, in particular dynamic contrast-enhanced MR lymphangiography and T2-weighted MR lymphangiography, now permit direct visualisation of abnormal lymphatic flow and precise planning of image-guided interventions. Percutaneous lymphatic embolisation and thoracic-duct decompression, together with surgical decompression procedures and, ultimately, heart transplantation, have shown clinically relevant efficacy in selected patients with complications refractory to medical therapy. This narrative review synthesises current knowledge on the pathophysiology, imaging and treatment of lymphatic complications in the Fontan circulation. Lymphatic involvement is frequent, under-diagnosed, and prognostically important; the integration of advanced lymphatic imaging and the consolidation of expertise in specialised percutaneous lymphatic intervention represent the most relevant advances of the last decade.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Upadacitinib Versus Other Advanced Therapies in Rheumatoid Arthritis After Tumor Necrosis Factor Inhibitor Use in the United States.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Understanding comparative effectiveness of different biologic therapies in patients with inadequate response to a prior tumor necrosis factor inhibitor (TNFi) may guide treatment decisions. This real-world analysis compared the clinical effectiveness of upadacitinib versus other advanced treatments (ATs), including TNFi, interleukin (IL)-6 inhibitors, and T cell co-stimulation modulators, in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) who previously received a TNFi.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used data from the OM1® RA Registry (OM1, Inc.; Boston, MA, USA). Patients with RA (≥ 18 years) treated with upadacitinib or other ATs who previously received a TNFi and had high disease activity (Clinical Disease Activity Index [CDAI] > 22) and both a tender joint count and swollen joint count of ≥ 6 at baseline were included. The outcome of interest was achievement of CDAI low disease activity (LDA)/remission at 12 months. Descriptive statistics were reported for proportion of patients who achieved CDAI LDA/remission at 12 months. Multivariable analyses using generalized estimating equation compared CDAI LDA/remission rates for upadacitinib versus IL-6 inhibitors, T cell co-stimulation modulator, and TNFi.

RESULTS: A total of 378 patients were included in the analysis: upadacitinib (N = 73), IL-6 inhibitors (N = 64), T cell co-stimulation modulator (N = 76), or a different TNFi (N = 165). Descriptive statistics showed a greater proportion of patients receiving upadacitinib achieved CDAI LDA/remission at 12 months (43.8%) versus IL-6 inhibitors (23.4%), T cell co-stimulation modulator (30.3%), or TNFi (31.5%). Multivariable analyses showed that patients receiving other ATs including IL-6 inhibitors (odds ratio, OR [95% confidence interval] 0.35 [0.16, 0.76], p = 0.01), T cell co-stimulation modulator (OR 0.46 [0.22, 0.95], p = 0.04), or TNFi (OR 0.52 [0.29, 0.96], p = 0.04) had lower odds of achieving CDAI remission/LDA compared to those receiving upadacitinib.

CONCLUSION: In this real-world analysis of patients with RA who previously received TNFis and had high disease burden, more patients treated with upadacitinib achieved CDAI LDA/remission at 12 months versus other ATs.

articles.title: Observer agreement in sonographic glandular tissue component classification and sonographic breast density assessment: a multi-institutional study.
authors: JABTS US GTC Research Working Group
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The sonographic glandular tissue component (GTC) is a potential imaging biomarker for stratifying breast cancer risk in women with dense breasts. This study evaluated the reproducibility, reliability, and clinical applicability of GTC classification and GTC-based sonographic breast density assessment in a multicenter observer study.

METHODS: Fifteen readers (nine physicians and six sonographers) from 12 institutions independently assessed 100 paired ultrasound images twice, 1 month apart, with the dataset rearranged for the second reading. GTC was qualitatively classified into four categories according to its estimated proportion within the fibroglandular tissue (FGT): minimal, mild, moderate, and marked; minimal/mild were grouped as low GTC and moderate/marked as high GTC. Sonographic breast density was categorized as sonographic dense breast (high GTC), sonographic non-dense breast (visible fat lobules), or intermediate, with intermediate cases further divided into high or low categories using an FGT-to-FAT (subcutaneous and retromammary fat) ratio cutoff of 1. Interobserver and intraobserver agreement was evaluated using κ statistics.

RESULTS: Substantial interobserver agreement was observed for the four-class GTC classification, the two-class GTC classification, and sonographic breast density assessment. Intraobserver agreement was moderate for the four-class GTC classification and substantial for the two-class GTC classification and sonographic breast density assessment. The majority-vote sonographic breast density assessment showed substantial agreement with the mammographic ground truth, whereas individual-reader assessments showed moderate concordance with mammographic breast density both overall and in intermediate-density breasts. No significant differences in agreement were observed between physicians and sonographers.

CONCLUSION: Substantial interobserver agreement and moderate-to-substantial intraobserver agreement support the reproducibility and reliability of GTC classification and GTC-based sonographic breast density assessment.

articles.title: Prediction of Bailout Mechanical Circulatory Support Use for Hemodynamic Collapse During PCI: The ORACLE Score.
articles.abstract: Background: Bailout mechanical circulatory support (MCS) may be used in the setting of intraprocedural hemodynamic collapse during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). We developed and externally validated a simple risk prediction model for bailout MCS use for hemodynamic collapse during PCI. Methods: Consecutive patients undergoing PCI at a tertiary hospital between 2018 and 2025 were included in the derivation cohort (n=6,931), after excluding cases of salvage PCI and procedures performed with pre-existing or prophylactic MCS. The primary endpoint was bailout MCS use for hemodynamic collapse. A multivariable Firth logistic regression model was developed, internally validated, and translated into a simplified integer-based risk score (ORACLE). External validation was performed in 214,877 PCIs from the Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan Cardiovascular Consortium (BMC2) registry. Results: The incidence of bailout MCS was 1.4% in the derivation cohort. Six variables (non-elective presentation, systolic blood pressure, chronic heart failure, prior PCI, rotational/orbital atherectomy, and left main PCI) independently predicted the primary endpoint. The regression model demonstrated good discrimination both in the derivation (area under the curve [AUC] 0.817; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.774-0.860) and external validation (AUC 0.761; 95% CI 0.753-0.770) cohorts. The simplified ORACLE score preserved most of the discriminatory performance of the full model (AUC 0.791 in the derivation cohort and 0.718 in the external validation cohort) and effectively stratified patients, with observed bailout MCS rates ranging from 0.4% in the low-risk category to 8.7% in the high-risk group, with similar findings in the external validation cohort. Discrimination was consistent across clinically relevant subgroups. Negative predictive value was >99% in both the derivation and external validation cohorts. Conclusions:: ORACLE is a simple score to estimate the risk of bailout MCS use for hemodynamic collapse during PCI, which may support preprocedural risk assessment.

articles.title: Calcified foraminal metastasis from ovarian low-grade serous carcinoma mimicking a nerve sheath tumor.
articles.abstract: Ovarian low-grade serous carcinoma (OLGSC) is an uncommon subtype of epithelial ovarian cancer, characterized by an indolent clinical course with potential for late local recurrence and metastatic disease. Musculoskeletal involvement is rare. We report a case of late OLGSC metastasis presenting as a slowly growing, thoracic foraminal mass in a 55-year-old woman, 33 years after initial cancer treatment. Rising CA-125 levels prompted 18F-FDG PET/CT, which revealed an FDG-avid mass in the left T9-T10 neural foramen (SUVmax 6.6). CT demonstrated foraminal widening and intralesional calcifications, while MRI showed a dumbbell-shaped mass extending into the epidural space and left costovertebral region, with heterogeneous signal intensity and mild diffuse heterogeneous enhancement. Retrospective review of a CT examination performed 12 years earlier revealed a smaller foraminal mass without visible calcifications. Given its location and morphology, the lesion initially suggested a nerve sheath tumor, while the presence of calcifications also raised the possibility of a chondroid lesion. Although nonspecific, calcifications are recognized in primary and metastatic OLGSC. The combination of increased FDG uptake and the patient's oncologic history, raised suspicion of metastatic disease. Image-guided biopsy confirmed metastatic OLGSC with psammoma bodies. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of OLGSC metastasis presenting as a slowly progressive, calcified paravertebral and foraminal mas mimicking a nerve sheath tumor. This case emphasizes the need for careful evaluation of atypical masses in patients with a history of cancer, even decades after initial treatment, and the importance of biopsy for diagnostic confirmation.

articles.title: [Conservative treatment of non-unions : Options and limitations].
articles.abstract: Despite modern medical care, non-unions occur in 2-5% of all fractures. The burden on patients involves prolonged rehabilitation and potentially further surgery. Costs for healthcare systems increase substantially. While surgical intervention represents the standard of care, a range of non-surgical treatment options is available. A particular advantage of non-surgical treatment is the avoidance of surgery itself. Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound therapy (LIPUS) and the use of pulsed electromagnetic fields (PEMF) are painless and applied by patients themselves once daily. With focused extracorporeal shockwave therapy (ESWT), administration by a physician-usually under general anesthesia-ensures the treatment takes effect precisely at the target site. Bony defects up to 5-10 mm in size can be treated without surgery, provided there is no infection and mechanical stability is adequate.

articles.title: Association Between Pituitary Adenoma Excision and Risk of Cerebrovascular Disease and Mortality in Patients With Cushing's Disease: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Cushing's disease (CD) is a hypercortisolemic state resulting from an adrenocorticotropic hormone-secreting pituitary adenoma (PA). Cerebrovascular disease (CeVD) is a dangerous sequela of CD, yet few studies have characterized its risk in CD. This study aimed to report the risk of CeVD in CD patients with and without surgical treatment.

METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study from the TriNetX database included 20 years of data from 69 healthcare organizations. TriNetX was searched to identify adults in the United States with CD. We used 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) for demographic characteristics and tobacco use to identify a matched non-CD group. Risk ratios were calculated to identify the risk of CeVD. Among patients with CD, we identified those who underwent PA excision after diagnosis and determined associations with CeVD. We used 1:1 PSM matching for demographic characteristics and comorbidities (hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia) to identify a matched non-PA excision CD group.

RESULTS: The CD group (n = 4265) was 78.4% female with a mean age at CD diagnosis of 45.7 years. After PSM, patients with CD had a significantly higher risk of any CeVD (risk ratio [RR] = 1.97, 95% CI: 1.70-2.29), ischemic stroke (RR = 2.35, 95% CI: 1.83-3.01), and hemorrhagic stroke (RR = 1.75, 95% CI: 1.22-2.49). Stratification by sex identified similar associations. One thousand three hundred seventy-seven patients with CD who underwent PA excision were identified after matching. PA excision was associated with lower risk of any CeVD (RR = 0.68, 95% CI: 0.55-0.86, number needed to treat [NNT] = 25.6), ischemic stroke (RR = 0.50, 95% CI: 0.35-0.72, NNT = 33.3), and mortality (RR = 0.52, 95% CI: 0.35-0.77, NNT = 40.0) compared with those who did not have excision. Sensitivity analyses using medication-based proxies for biochemical remission showed similar trends between curative and noncurative resection but were not statistically significant.

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrated that patients with CD are at an increased risk of CeVD, including ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke. PA excision for patients with CD may reduce lifetime CeVD risk and mortality.

articles.title: Two Decades of Neurosurgical Device Innovation: A Comprehensive Analysis of FDA Authorization Trends From 7800 Approvals by Subspecialty, Regulatory Pathway, and Approval Time.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Technological progress has accelerated neurosurgical care, yet a panoramic view of these innovations remains lacking. This study aims to analyze all US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) authorizations issued from 2000 to 2023 to map neurosurgical device output by subspecialty, compare regulatory pathways and approval times, and identify factors affecting market entry.

METHODS: All devices cleared or approved by the FDA Neurology and Orthopedic Review Panels (January 2000-December 2023) were extracted from publicly available 510(k), De Novo, Humanitarian Device Exemption, and Premarket Approval databases. Devices were assigned to 1 of 9 neurosurgical subspecialties and stratified by regulatory pathway, device class, company maturity, and geographic origin. Descriptive statistics, analysis of variance, and Welch t-tests assessed temporal and categorical differences.

RESULTS: Of 16 064 devices reviewed by the FDA Neurology and Orthopedic panels, 7873 (49.0%) were neurosurgical, rising 172.1% over the period. Spine and peripheral nerve (5227 devices) and stereotactic and functional (1378) dominated volume and number of new market entries, while cerebrospinal fluid disorders (n = 149) and cranial trauma (n = 111) had fewer approvals. Cerebrovascular and endovascular (95.5%) and cranial trauma (200.0%) showed the largest growth rates, while cerebrospinal fluid disorders (-54.2%) and general cranial surgery (-34.5%) declined over time. Mean approval time varied by subspecialty (P < .001), the shortest for spine and peripheral nerve (119.0 ± 102.7 days) and the longest for stereotactic and functional (158.7 ± 121.5 days). Approval or clearance times were strongly influenced by regulatory pathway and device class (both P < .001), with Premarket Approval devices (584.8 ± 323.3 days) the longest. Mature companies achieved faster approvals compared with startups (114.9 ± 97.0 vs 174.5 ± 133.9 days, P < .001).

CONCLUSION: Neurosurgical device output has more than doubled, but volume concentrates where predicates are rich and reimbursement established, not where clinical need or novelty is the greatest. Pathway architecture, device complexity, and sponsor experience influence approval efficiency more than novelty.

articles.title: Landscape Fire-Sourced PM2.5 and Cause-Specific Renal Hospitalizations: A Multicountry Two-Stage Time-Series Analysis of 12.5 Million Admissions.
articles.abstract: Landscape fire-sourced PM2.5 (LFS PM2.5) is increasingly recognized as an important air pollutant, but its short-term contribution to renal hospitalizations remains unclear. Here, we assessed the associations between LFS PM2.5 and renal hospitalizations across 1020 locations in Australia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, New Zealand, and Thailand during 2000-2019 using a two-stage time-series design and estimated the attributable hospitalizations. LFS PM2.5 was associated with increased renal hospitalization risk, with the strongest associations observed for acute kidney injury. A 10 μg/m3 increase in cumulative LFS PM2.5 exposure over lag 0-5 was associated with a 1.1% increase in renal hospitalizations (RR = 1.011, 95% CI: 1.007-1.015). Associations were stronger in warmer areas and differed across levels of GDP per capita. Associations were consistently stronger for LFS PM2.5 than for non-LFS PM2.5. We estimated that LFS PM2.5 contributed to 1.38 renal hospitalizations per 100,000 population annually across the study regions. These findings highlight renal disease as an underrecognized health consequence of landscape fire smoke and support strengthened strategies to reduce wildfire smoke exposure under a changing climate.

articles.title: Parenteral Nutrition as a Source of Xenobiotic Exposure in Preterm Infants in a Single-Center Case Study.
articles.abstract: In premature infants, successful ex utero maturation depends on endogenous and exogenous stimuli. Chemical insults during this period may impact long-term development. Given immature hepatic biotransformation, parenteral xenobiotic exposure may be of particular toxicological relevance. We conducted a single-center case study to characterize the xenobiotic burden of neonatal parenteral nutrition (PN). A standardized PN regimen for a 28-week, 1000 g reference infant was passed through infusion lines and the flow-through analyzed via a multianalyte exposome LC-MS/MS assay. Eighteen of 221 targeted xenobiotics were detected. Diisononyl phthalate (DINP, 780 ng/mL), bisphenol A (BPA, 250 ng/mL), methylparaben (MP, 74 ng/mL), and 5-hydroxymethyl-2-furanoic acid (HMFA, 43 ng/mL) showed the highest mean concentrations. The estimated daily intake of BPA (9.5 μg/kg bw/d) exceeded calculated and official Health-Based Guidance Values. Consistent with immature detoxification, pharmacokinetic modeling suggested accumulation of DINP, MINP, and free BPA in premature infants. The higher predicted exposure of premature infants to free BPA warrants investigation into 4-methyl-2,4-bis(4-hydroxyphenyl)pent-1-ene (MBP) formation under potentially saturated Phase II metabolism. An exploratory analysis of plasma data from extremely premature infants indicated PN as a contributory rather than predominant source of intervention-related exposure. These findings represent a relevant clinical reference scenario rather than a population-wide exposure estimate.

articles.title: Managing Giant Dorsal Morel-Lavallée Lesions: Operative Principles From an Uncommon Case.
articles.abstract: Morel-Lavallée lesions (MLLs) are shearing force injuries that separate the subcutaneous tissue from the underlying fascia. They remain underreported in the literature. They typically occur in the thigh or pelvis. Those located on the torso are rare. We present the case of a 54-year-old male trauma patient who developed, what is to our knowledge, the largest documented MLL extending across the entire back. Currently, there is no consensus on the optimal treatment of MLLs, particularly for large lesions where there are high recurrence rates and the morbidity of infection could be immense. Management strategies reported in the literature are varied but all rely on the principles of evacuation of hematoma and closure and/or drainage of the dead space. Our purpose in this manuscript is not to highlight that our proposed intervention was successful but to offer management options of large MLLs where no consensus has been reached.

articles.title: Network Trauma Research Series: Modeling Trauma Complexity - In Vitro Models to Study Traumatic Lung Damage.
articles.abstract: Polytrauma, defined as severe injury to multiple body regions, frequently affects the head and thorax and induces a systemic immune response that can favor secondary infections such as pneumonia. In particular, thoracic trauma substantially increases the risk of post-traumatic pneumonia, as direct lung injury, impaired respiratory function, and the frequent need for mechanical ventilation predispose patients to pulmonary infections, thereby contributing to adverse clinical outcomes. To improve translational understanding of these interactions, complex in vitro models have been developed to experimentally dissect the biological mechanisms underlying injuries of the lung. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current in vitro lung models and their suitability to analyze trauma induced lung damage and following infection. Key methodological variables are the selection of appropriate cell lines, the modeling of air - liquid interface or barrier function and the simulation of the trauma. Importantly, experimental approaches should clearly distinguish between inflammatory stimulation and mechanical injury, as these represent distinct pathophysiological processes. Collectively, the models discussed herein highlight the importance of standardized and physiologically relevant in vitro trauma models for advancing mechanistic insights and facilitating the development of targeted therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Extubation Failure and Duration of Respiratory Support Postextubation in Children: Australian and New Zealand Multicenter, ICU Registry Data, 2014-2021.
authors: and the Australian & New Zealand Intensive Care Society (ANZICS) Center for Outcomes & Resource Evaluation (CORE)
articles.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare postextubation failure and duration of noninvasive respiratory support postextubation in children receiving continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) or high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC).

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort using the Australian and New Zealand Pediatric Intensive Care (ANZPIC) registry.

SETTING: Ten PICUs and 24 mixed adult/pediatric units.

PATIENTS: All children extubated between 2014 and 2021 who required noninvasive respiratory support.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS: Postextubation failure rate requiring reintubation and duration of noninvasive respiratory support. Secondary outcomes were length of stay (LOS) in the PICU, time from extubation to discharge from the PICU, hospital LOS, and prevalence of death during hospital admission.

RESULTS: Of 31,910 extubation episodes in 23,930 children, 7,156 children received noninvasive respiratory support. Propensity matching yielded 1418 pairs for CPAP and HFNC. We failed to identify an association between postextubation failure and the use of CPAP vs. HFNC (107/1418 [7.6%] vs. 115/1418 [8.1%]; rate ratio, 0.93 [95% CI, 0.72-1.25]). There was an associated difference in median (interquartile range [IQR]) duration of postextubation respiratory support when CPAP was compared with HFNC, 72.0 hours (IQR, 30.5-72.0 hr) vs. 30.5 hours (IQR, 17.2-72.0 hr); median difference, 41.5 hours (95% CI, 37.7-45.2 hr). Median PICU LOS on CPAP vs. HFNC was 10.2 days (IQR, 5.1-20.9 d) vs. 7.1 days (IQR, 3.9-14.3 d); median difference, 2.2 days (95% CI, 1.6-2.8 d). Use of HFNC as opposed to CPAP was associated with shorter PICU LOS postextubation and hospital LOS. Last, we failed to identify an association between postextubation support and in-hospital mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: In the ANZPIC registry, 2014-2021 dataset, we failed to identify an association between type of postextubation form of respiratory support and postextubation failure rate. However, being supported with CPAP as opposed to HFNC was associated with longer duration of postextubation respiratory support in the PICU.

articles.title: Physiologic, Metabolic, and Protein Redox Effects of Methylene Blue in a Porcine Hemorrhage Model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Methylene blue (MB) has established benefit in vasodilatory shock, and a potential role in hemorrhagic shock. Some evidence suggests that MB could lower anesthetic requirements. The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of MB on volatile anesthetic requirements (primary), metabolic markers (secondary), and protein redox modifications (tertiary) in a porcine hemorrhage model.

METHODS: This was a randomized 2 x 2 factorial animal study conducted at a tertiary medical center in 2019-2020. Forty swine were randomized to the following experimental interventions: hemorrhage (0 v. 30 mL/kg, at t = 0 min) and MB (0 v. 2 mg/kg, at t = 20 min). End-tidal isoflurane, blood pressure, and arterial blood gas parameters were recorded at prespecified intervals. Skeletal muscle was used for redox analyses. Group differences were investigated with mixed effects and one-way analyses of variance.

RESULTS: There was no effect of MB on volatile requirements or metabolic markers (all P > 0.05). Hemorrhage was associated with 2.4 mg/dL higher lactate (95% CI, 1.4 to 3.4) and 23 mmHg lower mean arterial pressure (95% CI, 11 to 34). Hemorrhage was also associated with increased protein carbonyl levels (P < 0.001) that were non-significantly attenuated by MB (P = 0.130), and increased protein S-nitrosylation (P < 0.001) that was significantly attenuated by MB (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: MB does not have a significant effect on volatile anesthetic requirements or systemic physiologic and metabolic responses during hemorrhagic shock. However, MB significantly attenuates protein S-nitrosylation and partially attenuates protein carbonyl accumulation.

articles.title: Self-Efficacy and Perceived Barriers to the Cultivation and Consumption of Indigenous Vegetables and Fruits in Southwest Nigeria.
articles.journal: Journal of nutrition education and behavior
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study examined the relationship between self-efficacy and perceived barriers to cultivating and consuming indigenous vegetables and fruits (IVsFs) in southwest Nigeria.

DESIGN: Cross-sectional, interview-administered questionnaire; quantitative secondary data.

PARTICIPANTS: A total of 170 participants aged 15 to 45 years were recruited through multistage sampling from Osun, Oyo, and Ogun States. Both in-school and out-of-school settings were included in the sample, with a nearly equal sex distribution.

ANALYSIS: Descriptive statistics summarized participants' characteristics. Ordinal logistic regression was used to examine the associations between self-efficacy and perceived barriers to the cultivation and consumption of IVsFs using unadjusted and adjusted odds ratios (age, sex, and student status). Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05.

RESULTS: There was a significant relationship between self-efficacy and perceived barriers to cultivation and consumption of IVsFs. Demographic characteristics (age, sex, and student status) showed no significant relationship.

CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Self-efficacy was significantly associated with perceived barriers to the cultivation and consumption of IVsFs among youth and early- to midlife adults in southwest Nigeria. The findings suggest the need for interventions aimed at improving participation in the indigenous food system to enhance self-efficacy and address psychological barriers.

articles.title: Clinical trial evidence for disease-modifying therapies across the type 1 diabetes continuum: from presymptomatic stages to recent-onset disease.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) can be identified before symptomatic insulin deficiency, creating an opportunity to intervene while meaningful beta-cell function remains.

AREAS COVERED: PubMed/MEDLINE and Clinical Trials.gov were searched for randomized trials, follow-up reports, and real-world studies published from January 2000 to August 2026; regulatory documents, and major guidelines were also reviewed. This article examines disease-modifying therapies in stage 1, stage 2, and recent-onset stage 3 T1D, distinguishing delay of clinical diagnosis from preservation of C-peptide after diagnosis and evaluating efficacy, safety, durability, treatment burden, and implementation.

EXPERT OPINION: Teplizumab establishes that a finite immunotherapy course can delay progression from stage 2 to stage 3 T1D, but it does not prevent disease. Other approaches demonstrate biological activity, although durable patient-important benefits remain uncertain. Future trials should prioritize comparable clinical outcomes, candidate selection, access, and rigorous evaluation of retreatment, sequential therapy, and mechanism-based combinations.

articles.title: Early and persistent blood pressure dysregulation in individuals with subacute motor incomplete spinal cord injury.
articles.journal: The journal of spinal cord medicine
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Blood pressure (BP) dysregulation after spinal cord injury (SCI) may disrupt circadian BP rhythms, including absent nocturnal dipping, high BP variability, and hypertension. These disturbances are independent predictors of cardiovascular disease, yet evidence in older adults with subacute motor incomplete SCI is limited.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize nocturnal dipping status, BP variability, and daytime and nighttime hypertension at admission to inpatient rehabilitation, and to assess changes during rehabilitation.

UNLABELLED: Observational cohort study.

SETTING: Primary inpatient rehabilitation center.

PARTICIPANTS: Individuals with motor incomplete SCI who completed 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring shortly after admission and before discharge.

INTERVENTIONS: Not applicable.

OUTCOME MEASURES: Nocturnal dipping (% reduction from nighttime to daytime systolic BP), BP variability, and hypertension defined using general population thresholds.
