RESULTS: Participants with motor incomplete SCI were included (n = 34, mean age 61 years, 82% male, 44% cervical injury). At admission, 82% were classified as non-dippers or reverse dippers. High BP variability was present in 59% for systolic BP and 29% for diastolic BP. Hypertension occurred in 21% during daytime and 59% during nighttime. All but one participant exhibited at least one BP-related risk factor. No changes were observed in dipping status, BP variability, and mean BP levels between admission and discharge (all p > 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Marked BP dysregulation is evident early after motor incomplete SCI, including absent nocturnal dipping, high BP variability, and nocturnal hypertension, despite daytime BP appearing within normal limits in most participants. These disturbances persisted throughout rehabilitation, indicating ongoing autonomic dysregulation that may contribute to long-term cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: SERS of Bottled Water: Automated PET Nanoplastic Detection and Quantification.
articles.abstract: Nanoplastics represent an emerging contaminant of growing environmental and public health concern, with polyethylene terephthalate (PET) being on topic due to its dominant use in beverage packaging. This study presents a SERS approach for the detection and quantification of PET nanoplastics in commercial bottled water, combining SERS with colloidal silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) and commercial solid SERS substrates, with automated Pearson correlation spectral classification. Mapping SERS samples of PET-bottled water combined with a Python identification algorithm enabled the detection of PET nanoplastics, while SEM-EDX analysis confirmed the presence of nanoscale carbon-oxygen particles consistent with PET stoichiometry. Beyond PET, phthalocyanine pigment nanoparticles, likely originating from bottle package, and inorganic residues including calcite, gypsum, and sodium nitrate were simultaneously identified, demonstrating the multianalyte capability of the approach. Using colloidal AgNPs, the estimated PET nanoplastic concentration was 17.25 ± 1.6 million particles per 0.5 L bottle (34.5 ± 3.2 million particles/L), comparative with values reported by nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA) and stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy in comparable studies. The method requires minimal sample preparation, limited to concentration by evaporation, without digestion or extraction steps, and preliminary results can be obtained within a few hours. These findings establish SERS combined with automated spectral analysis as a practical and sensitive screening tool for nanoplastic monitoring in drinking water, reporting particle concentrations directly in the number of particles per liter and with potential applicability to broader water quality analysis.

articles.title: The GndA Microprotein Promotes Cell Growth during Heat Shock in Escherichia coli.
articles.abstract: Hundreds of bacterial small open reading frames (sORFs) encoding microproteins of fewer than 50 amino acids have recently been identified. Biological functions have been ascribed to an increasing number of microproteins, some of which play roles in bacterial stress responses. In this work, we provide evidence that GndA, a frameshifted 36-amino acid microprotein encoded in an internal open reading frame overlapping the 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase (6PGD) coding sequence (CDS), functions in the response to heat shock. We demonstrate independent contributions of GndA and 6PGD to cell growth at a high temperature. GndA is hydrophobic and associates with the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex and the inner membrane. Consistent with a role in cellular homeostasis, GndA mutations alter the transcriptional response to heat shock. These results demonstrate that GndA promotes bacterial cell growth at high temperatures independently of the 6PGD protein that it overlaps. GndA thus expands the paradigm of bacterial microproteins that function in cellular stress responses.

articles.title: Deletion of the Envelope gene attenuates SARS-CoV-2 infection by altered spike localization and increased cell-to-cell transmission.
articles.abstract: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) causes COVID-19, a highly transmissible acute respiratory infection that can result in severe pneumonia and death. Many details of SARS-CoV-2 infection are not fully understood, including the cell biology and host-virus interactions involved in coronavirus assembly and release, in which the Envelope (E) structural protein is instrumental. Deletion of E in other coronaviruses has been shown previously to either attenuate or abrogate infection. To determine the role of E in SARS-CoV-2 virus production and infectivity, we produced a reporter SARS-CoV-2 with or without the E gene deleted using a bacterial artificial chromosome. Replication of ΔE SARS-CoV-2 was attenuated in Vero E6 cells expressing human ACE2 and TMPRSS2 and in human epithelial cell lines. Electron and immunofluorescence microscopy and virology assays showed that ΔE SARS-CoV-2 increased cell surface expression of Spike (S) glycoprotein, leading to reduced S incorporation into ΔE SARS-CoV-2 particles and promotion of increased cell-to-cell transmission that evades neutralizing antibody inhibition. Trans-complementation of E partially rescued ΔE SARS-CoV-2 S incorporation and restored cell-free transmission. In addition to validating the role of E in retention of S in the ER-Golgi intermediate complex (ERGIC), our results showed that a lack of E led to reorganization of the ERGIC and Golgi during SARS-CoV-2 infection. Improved understanding of E in SARS-CoV-2 replication and host pathogenesis may help the development of novel therapeutics.IMPORTANCENon-Spike coronavirus structural proteins, including Envelope, are conserved, making them potential pan-coronavirus therapeutic targets. Many details about these proteins and their roles in viral replication and host pathogenesis are unknown. In this study, we showed that severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) replicates without Envelope but is attenuated and impaired in virus particle formation, with less Spike incorporated into virions and more Spike expressed on the cell surface compared to wild-type virus. SARS-CoV-2 lacking Envelope transmitted primarily via cell fusion and evaded neutralizing antibodies. In addition, the absence of Envelope resulted in the reorganization of the cell secretory compartment during SARS-CoV-2 infection. A better understanding of how Envelope influences SARS-CoV-2 replication could guide directed design of novel therapeutics for treatment of COVID-19 patients, as well as the potential for pan-coronavirus protection against future coronavirus outbreaks.

articles.title: A Family Census Evaluating Parental Presence and Activities at a Tertiary Surgical Neonatal Unit.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Neonatal unit (NNU) admission can adversely affect parental confidence, breastfeeding, attachment and mental health. Family Integrated Care (FICare) promotes parents as primary caregivers and may improve outcomes.

METHODS: To establish baseline practice before FICare, a 14-day parental presence census was conducted in a tertiary surgical NNU in South London. Parents self-recorded presence and activities. Analyses characterised presence and engagement by infant and care characteristics.

RESULTS: 41/60 (68%) infants participated, contributing 338 care-days. Mothers were present on 92% of care-days (mean 7.6 h/day) and fathers on 62% (4.1 h/day). Overall parental presence averaged 7.9 h/day, peaking 11:00-18:00. Presence was lowest in intensive care (5.9 h/day) and highest among families rooming-in (14.8 h/day). Presence decreased with distance from hospital and was lower among families with siblings or a non-English primary language. Caregiving activities averaged 5.8/day, increasing with infant age before declining after 8 weeks.

CONCLUSION: Parental presence varied with infant clinical status, age and family circumstances. On-site accommodation was associated with increased presence, highlighting infrastructure's importance in facilitating FICare. Distance, childcare and language create inequitable participation. Findings provide baseline data to inform support and FICare interventions.

articles.title: Depression among patients with recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection: a nationwide inpatient analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) frequently recurs and impacts quality of life, yet its relationship with mental illness remains understudied.

METHODS: Using the National Inpatient Sample (2018-2019), we calculated depression rates among adults with recurrent CDI (rCDI) and assessed the odds of codiagnosed depression compared to other chronic medical conditions.

RESULTS: Among 84,055 hospitalizations with rCDI, 21.5% had a codiagnosis of depression. In a population without CDI, depression prevalence was 14.2%. CDI patients had a 56% greater chance of having a diagnosis of depression compared with the general population (odds ratio [OR] 1.56, 95% confidence interval 1.5-1.6). When compared to those with common chronic medical comorbidities, patients with CDI had significantly higher odds of having depression than those with heart failure (OR 1.4), diabetes (OR 1.3), end-stage kidney disease (OR 1.5), and metastatic cancer (OR 1.9). Patients with fibromyalgia, multiple sclerosis, and alcohol-related disorders had higher rates of depression compared with those with CDI.

CONCLUSION: Patients with rCDI appear to have remarkably high depression rates, higher than those of patients with many other common chronic medical conditions. Further studies are needed to evaluate the causation of this potential association and to consider the benefit of implementing depression screening programs in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Cryptosporidium Infection Is Associated with Gut Microbiome Alterations in Bangladeshi Children and Families.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cryptosporidium spp. are enteric protozoa associated with moderate-to-severe diarrhea and impaired growth in children worldwide. However, the relationship between Cryptosporidium infection and gut microbiome remains poorly understood.

METHODS: We investigated gut microbiota dynamics associated with Cryptosporidium infection in a longitudinal cohort of 84 children and family members in Bangladesh. Fecal samples (n=233) were collected pre-infection, during infection, and post-infection. Microbial profiling was performed using 16S rRNA sequencing, with taxonomic classification and abundance estimation conducted via Cosmos ID-HUB. Associations between infection status, microbial diversity, and taxa abundance were evaluated using multivariable models adjusting for age and sex.

RESULTS: Most Cryptosporidium infections were subclinical (96.1%), with 3.86% presenting diarrhea. In individuals ≥ 3 years of age, gut microbial α-diversity decreased during infection (p-value range = 0.01-3.68x10-10) and increased following recovery (p-value range = 0.0017- 0.0019). During infection, Roseburia and Megaspheara were reduced relative to both pre- (q-value = 0.011 and 0.02) and post-infection (q-value =2.34 x10-5 and 0.001). In addition, Prevotella (q-value = 0.03) and Leuconostoc (q-value=0.04) were reduced relative to pre-infection. Shigella abundance increased during infection (q-value =3.4x10-5) and persisted post-infection (q-value=9.0x10-6). In children ≤ 3 years of age, α-diversity increased during infection compared to pre-infection (p-value=0.045). α-diversity and β-diversity during the post-infection period were associated with lower weight for age z scores.

CONCLUSIONS: Cryptosporidium infection is associated with dynamic and persistent alterations in the gut microbiome, even in the absence of diarrhea, which may be related to impaired child growth, and deserve deeper analysis as promising potential targets for microbiota-mediated interventions.

articles.title: Evaluation of the Sysmex UF-5000 automated urine flow cytometer for detection of urethral inflammation and clinical urethritis in men.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Objective evidence of urethral inflammation is required to diagnose urethritis in men. Clinically, this is established by confirming urethral discharge on examination in symptomatic patients. Alternatively, laboratory approaches rely on identifying polymorphonuclear neutrophils (PMNs) from a urethral swab specimen or leukocyte esterase (LE) activity in urine. However, physical examination-based diagnosis may be subjective, collection of a urethral swab is invasive, and often painful, and LE has poor sensitivity. To address these limitations, we evaluated the white blood cell (WBC) parameter of the Sysmex UF-5000 automated urinary flow cytometer for the detection of urethral inflammation and clinician-diagnosed urethritis. Using 1,000 remnant male urine specimens from a sexual health clinic, we measured urinary WBC counts (WBC/μL) using the UF-5000, LE by urinalysis, and abstracted corresponding clinical data and urethral Gram stain results from the electronic medical record. Urinary WBC counts measured by the UF-5000 were significantly higher in men with urethral symptoms, LE ≥1+ status, a clinical diagnosis of urethritis, and strongly correlated with elevated and increasing urethral Gram stain PMN density. The UF-5000 demonstrated excellent diagnostic discrimination, yielding areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.86 for Gram stain-defined urethral inflammation, and 0.90 for clinician-defined urethritis. Optimized thresholds provided >95% sensitivity for ruling out infection and >95% specificity for ruling it in, outperforming standard LE testing. In conclusion, the UF-5000 automated urine flow cytometer offers a robust, non-invasive alternative for male urethritis diagnosis. This approach could expand diagnostic reach-particularly for men who decline urethral swab collection-and warrants prospective clinical validation.

IMPORTANCE: Male urethritis diagnostics are limited by the poor sensitivity of leukocyte esterase (LE) testing or the invasive nature of urethral swab collection for Gram stain microscopy. These limitations may create barriers to patient care and delay urethritis diagnosis. Automated urinary flow cytometry may overcome these limitations, but few studies exist. We analyzed 1,000 remnant male urine specimens to evaluate the Sysmex UF-5000 white blood cell (WBC) parameter for detecting urethral inflammation. Elevated urinary WBC counts strongly correlated with elevated WBCs on urethral Gram stain smear microscopy and positive LE. The UF-5000 outperformed LE for ruling in and ruling out urethral inflammation and clinical urethritis. Automated urinary flow cytometry is a powerful, non-invasive diagnostic approach that warrants prospective evaluation in point-of-care clinical studies.

articles.title: Two Ume6 target gene classes in the biofilm regulatory network of Candida albicans.
articles.abstract: Biofilm formation by the fungal pathogen Candida albicans is a major source of infection. The biofilm regulator Ume6 forms complexes with partner transcription factors Efg1, Ndt80, and Upc2 to drive expression of biofilm-related genes. Here, we present chromatin immunoprecipitation with sequencing data for Ume6-chromatin association in both wild-type and efg1Δ/Δ ndt80Δ/Δ upc2Δ/Δ backgrounds. Ume6 associates with two promoter region classes. For one class, Ume6 association is significantly decreased in the efg1Δ/Δ ndt80Δ/Δ upc2Δ/Δ background. This class includes 577 genes, many with well-established roles in biofilm formation or the related process of filamentation. For the second class, Ume6 association is unperturbed in the triple mutant background. This class includes 534 genes, some with roles in iron homeostasis (e.g., SFU1) and ergosterol synthesis (e.g., ERG11), which may contribute to the impact of Ume6 on ndt80Δ/Δ mutant azole drug sensitivity. It also includes FLO9, a putative adhesin gene that is required for the emergent biofilm state produced by efg1Δ/Δ ndt80Δ/Δ double mutants. The data show that Ume6 binding to about half of its targets requires known partners, and Ume6 binding to about half of its targets does not. Ume6 may bind to the latter set of promoter regions independently of any partner, or perhaps with additional partners that have yet to be discovered.IMPORTANCEBiofilm formation has a central role in infection by the fungal pathogen Candida albicans. Here, we focus on a key regulator, Ume6, that can drive biofilm formation. It is known to form protein complexes with three partner transcription factors, and here, we investigate Ume6-promoter binding in the presence and absence of those partners. Ume6 binds to two promoter classes: one depends on known partners, and many associated genes have roles in biofilm formation. The second class is independent of known partners, and some associated genes are functionally connected to iron metabolism and ergosterol synthesis. The second class may mediate effects of Ume6 on azole drug sensitivity. Our results suggest that Ume6 may bind to some promoter regions independently of any partner, or perhaps with additional partners that have yet to be discovered.

articles.title: Managing equine asthma: Owner adherence, practical constraints and environmental protocol evaluation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adherence to recommendations for environmental management is central to equine asthma (EA) treatment. Reasons for non-adherence warrant further investigation.

OBJECTIVES: To: (1) evaluate adherence to recommendations for environmental changes, identify reasons for incomplete implementation, assess changes in clinical signs and medication use; (2) evaluate owner acceptability, practicality and perceived usefulness of a structured stable-side protocol.

STUDY DESIGN: (1) Retrospective online survey and (2) prospective onsite testing with owners of EA-affected horses.

METHODS: (1) Online survey on implementation of standardised recommendations, clinical progression and medication use; and (2) environmental protocol evaluation during stable visits.

RESULTS: Seventeen of 40 horses still received dry hay and 13/40 were bedded on straw. Reasons for non-implementation included time, financial and infrastructural constraints, boarding stable restrictions, group housing, weather dependence, use of self-produced roughage, perceived ineffectiveness and individual horse preferences. Owners reported that overall clinical impression had improved and the proportion of coughing horses decreased from 88% to 55% (p < 0.001, OR = 0.07, 95% CI 0.002-0.47, n = 40). The other clinical outcomes did not reach the Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold. Twenty-two horses were still coughing, and 7/40 had received medication within the previous 3 months. All interviewed owners found the environmental protocol helpful, 11 reviewed it again and 5 used it for discussion with others.

MAIN LIMITATIONS: Use of small convenience samples, lack of a control group and potential selection and recall bias.

CONCLUSION: Owner non-adherence arose from diverse and often structural constraints. The environmental protocol was well accepted by owners and helped to structure discussions on risk factors.

articles.title: When perinatal asphyxia is not the whole story: neonatal listeriosis masquerading as hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy.
articles.abstract: Neonatal listeriosis is an uncommon but potentially life-threatening cause of early-onset sepsis that can closely resemble hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. We present a term male infant delivered by cesarean section for nonreassuring fetal heart rate tracing who required resuscitation with positive pressure ventilation. Severe metabolic acidosis and low Apgar scores initially suggested perinatal asphyxia; however, a structured neurologic examination at 1 and 3 hours of life did not meet criteria for therapeutic hypothermia, and the infant subsequently developed fever, thrombocytopenia, persistent shock, and marked transaminitis. Blood and placental cultures grew Listeria monocytogenes, a gram-positive bacillus. The infant improved with ampicillin monotherapy and was discharged with a normal neurologic examination. This case illustrates the importance of maintaining a broad differential diagnosis, including infection, in neonates with a presumed diagnosis of perinatal asphyxia.

articles.title: Is it tuberculosis or chronic pulmonary aspergillosis? Diagnostic challenges, consequences of misdiagnosis, and potential solutions in resource-limited settings.
articles.abstract: SUMMARYChronic pulmonary aspergillosis (CPA) is most often caused by Aspergillus fumigatus and carries significant mortality and morbidity. While the diagnosis of CPA is often delayed, the emergence of CPA among patients with a concurrent or previous history of mycobacterial disease presents a challenge for CPA diagnosis. When patients previously treated for mycobacterial diseases present with new symptoms, it is often unclear whether these symptoms are due to a recurrence of pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB), non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) infection, CPA, co-infection, or another of several other differential diagnoses. Consequently, PTB patients can be misdiagnosed as having smear/GeneXpert-negative PTB. We address these challenges, given the different associated mortality and morbidity of NTM, PTB, and CPA. We proposed a new algorithm to guide clinicians in ruling CPA in or out in both newly diagnosed smear/GeneXpert-negative and NTM patients and those with a previous history of mycobacterial disease. We also recommend follow-up screening of those with a high risk of developing CPA following their PTB/NTM treatment. Implementing screening strategies, such as performing end-of-treatment TB chest X-rays and Aspergillus-specific IgG tests during and at the end of mycobacterial therapy, could facilitate the early diagnosis and treatment of CPA and alleviate associated mortality and morbidity.

articles.title: E8^E2 controls the formation of E2-positive replication centers that precede E4 expression during productive HPV16 infection.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Human papillomaviruses (HPVs) couple their replication cycle to keratinocyte differentiation. Viral genomes are maintained at low copy numbers in undifferentiated cells and undergo amplification within nuclear replication foci in differentiated suprabasal cells. The viral proteins E2 and E8^E2 function as activators and repressors of viral replication, respectively. Using a novel polyclonal antiserum together with the monoclonal antibody 22E2-B9, which recognize both E2 and E8^E2, we identified distinct nuclear E2 foci in keratinocytes harboring episomal HPV16 wild-type (wt) or E8^E2 mutant genomes. These foci colocalized with viral genomes and the cellular proteins RPA32, RAD51, γH2AX, and BRD4, consistent with viral replication centers. Cell-cycle analysis showed that E2 foci formed during the S phase and persisted into the G2 phase. Loss of E8^E2 expression or repression activity increased the number of replication foci and induced diffuse nuclear E2 staining. Only a subset of E2 focus-positive cells expressed the late viral protein E4, indicating that replication centers arise before robust late gene expression. In organotypic cultures, E2 focus-positive/E4-negative cells were detected in suprabasal layers before E2 focus-positive/E4-positive cells, whereas E2-negative/E4-positive cells suggested dynamic regulation of E2 during productive infection. Moreover, many wt cells displayed E2 focus phenotypes resembling E8^E2 mutant cells, suggesting that E8^E2 activity declines during keratinocyte differentiation. These findings demonstrate that E2-positive viral replication centers are tightly regulated by E8^E2, emerge early during productive HPV16 infection, and are accompanied by dynamic modulation of E2 and E8^E2 during the productive phase of the viral life cycle.

IMPORTANCE: Human papillomaviruses (HPVs) couple their replication cycle to keratinocyte differentiation, but the mechanisms controlling productive viral genome amplification remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify distinct E2-positive nuclear replication centers in HPV16-infected keratinocytes and show that they contain viral genomes and cellular factors involved in DNA replication and repair. We demonstrate that these structures form during the S phase, persist into the G2 phase, and arise before robust expression of the late viral E4 protein, indicating that viral genome amplification is initiated earlier in the productive cycle than previously appreciated. We further show that the viral repressor E8^E2 regulates the organization of E2-positive replication centers and that E8^E2 activity appears to decline during keratinocyte differentiation. Together, our findings reveal dynamic regulation of E2 and E8^E2 during productive HPV16 infection and provide new insights into how viral genome amplification and late gene expression are coordinated in differentiating epithelial cells.

articles.title: miR-8485 by Targeting ITGAM Expression Alleviates Cognitive Impairment Induced by Ischemic Stroke.
articles.journal: Journal of geriatric psychiatry and neurology
articles.abstract: ObjectivePost-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is a major complication of ischemic stroke (IS). This study aims to explore the role of miR-8485 in PSCI and its underlying molecular mechanism.Methods84 PSCI patients and 90 post-stroke cognitively normal (PSCN) patients were included. Serum miR-8485 and ITGAM expression were examined via reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction. The diagnostic efficacy of miR-8485 was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve. Risk factors of PSCI were determined via logistic regression analysis. An in vitro PSCI cell model was constructed through oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R). Cell viability, apoptosis and inflammatory factor levels were determined by Cell Counting Kit-8 assay, flow cytometry and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. The oxidative stress was evaluated by measuring superoxide dismutase (SOD), malondialdehyde (MDA) and catalase (CAT) levels. The interaction between miR-8485 and ITGAM was verified by dual-luciferase reporter assay.ResultsmiR-8485 was downregulated in PSCI patients, and ROC analysis showed that it could differentiate PSCI patients from PSCN patients. Downregulated miR-8485 expression was associated with PSCI disease severity. In OGD/R-treated human microglial cells (HMC3), upregulation of miR-8485 increased cell viability, suppressed inflammatory responses and oxidative stress, and inhibited apoptosis. ITGAM was the target of miR-8485. Overexpression of ITGAM partially reversed the protective effect of miR-8485 upregulation in OGD/R-induced HMC3 cells.ConclusionmiR-8485 alleviates OGD/R-induced inflammatoty responses and oxidative stress via targeted inhibition of ITGAM expression. The miR-8485/ITGAM axis may serve as a key regulatory pathway and a potential therapeutic candidate for further investigation in PSCI.

articles.title: DectiSomes as broad-spectrum antifungal drugs.
articles.journal: Microbiology and molecular biology reviews : MMBR
articles.abstract: SUMMARYFungal pathogens represent a significant threat to public health. Aspergillus fumigatus, Candida albicans, Cryptococcus neoformans, and Rhizopus delemar are the primary causative agents for aspergillosis, candidiasis, cryptococcosis, and mucormycosis. They and their closest relatives are responsible for more than 94% of fungal disease-related deaths. All four fungal diseases may lead to meningitis, with mortality rates approaching 99%. They are among the WHO-designated priority fungal pathogens needing new and more effective treatments. In response to this therapeutic gap, we developed DectiSomes-drug-loaded liposomes targeted to fungal cells by host-pathogen receptors. Host-pathogen receptors have many advantages over antibodies as liposome-targeting proteins, including a lack of immunogenicity. Of the pathogen receptors we tested, Dectin-1 and Dectin-2 are the most effective targeting proteins against the fungal pathogens tested. Liposomes loaded with amphotericin B and coated with one of these pathogen receptors bind specifically and strongly to the four pathogens and kill them, reducing the effective dose of amphotericin B by more than an order of magnitude over the untargeted control. DectiSomes are also more effective in murine models of fungal infection. Furthermore, we developed small, malleable versions of DectiSomes with improved drug delivery to the brain and are more effective against cryptococcal meningitis, holding promise for treating all forms of fungal meningitis. Herein, we review our progress and discuss the potential of DectiSomes as a new and effective targeted delivery system for antifungal drugs. In addition, we discuss the challenges associated with fungal diseases and the roadblocks to antifungal drug development and medical mycology research.

articles.title: Neuropsychiatric Features of Individuals With LGI1-Antibody Encephalitis.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuropsychiatry and clinical neurosciences
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Leucine-rich glioma-inactivated 1 antibody (LGI1-Ab) encephalitis is one of the most common forms of autoimmune encephalitis and is associated with prominent psychiatric features. Psychiatric phenotyping of this condition has relied on small studies and has lacked detail.

METHODS: In this retrospective study, the authors reviewed the psychiatric symptomatology and clinical course among patients with a confirmed diagnosis of LGI1-Ab encephalitis.

RESULTS: The mean±SD age of the study sample (N=31) was 60.7±14.2 years; 71% of patients were men. The time to diagnosis was 4.9±5.8 months, and the follow-up time was 55.8±36.7 months. Eighteen patients had documented hyponatremia, and 22 were treated as inpatients. Psychiatric (71%), cognitive (81%), and neurological (84%) symptoms were present at similar rates, despite 97% of the patients coming from neurology referrals. Patients had a diverse range of seizures, including faciobrachial dystonic seizures. Of 19 patients undergoing detailed psychometric analysis, impairments were noted in memory or orientation (100%), executive function (63%), naming (47%), processing speed (37%), attention (32%), verbal fluency (26%), language (11%), and visuospatial abilities (11%). Patients had psychotic symptoms (42%), agitation or aggression (39%), emotional lability (35%), anxiety (26%), and subjective experiential phenomena (16%). Many patients had psychiatric sequelae that resolved after treatment, but a modest proportion of patients experienced ongoing apathy (6%), behavioral disinhibition (13%), obsessive-compulsive disorder (10%), subjective experiential phenomena (13%), and sleep disorders (29%).

CONCLUSIONS: These findings show that cognitive impairment and psychopathology are frequent in LGI1-Ab encephalitis. Future research could examine neuroimaging, psychiatric symptoms, and cognitive deficits in further detail.

articles.title: Representation of Sickle Cell Disease Patients in Pediatric and Adult Care: What We Discovered Using Informatics for Integrating Biology and the Bedside (i2b2) Data.
articles.abstract: Transitioning from pediatric to adult care is a high-risk period for individuals with sickle cell disease (SCD). An initial observation at one academic medical center suggested a sex-based disparity in clinic populations, prompting a national investigation. We aimed to compare the sex distributions among SCD pediatric and adult clinics across the United States. Using the Informatics for Integrating Biology and the Bedside (i2b2) platform, we queried deidentified electronic health record data from 34 geographically diverse academic medical centers. Data on patient sex and age group (pediatric: 0-18 years; adult: ≥19 years) were analyzed from 19 responding centers. The pediatric population (n = 10,400) was balanced by sex (50.7% female, 49.3% male). In contrast, the adult population (n = 20,730) was significantly skewed, with females comprising 59.7% and males 40.3% (p < 0.001). This underrepresentation of males in adult clinics was consistent across 16 of the 19 centers. For one center that maintained balanced sex proportions, a follow-up inquiry revealed flexible clinic scheduling (early mornings, evenings, and weekends) and staffing by advanced practice nurses. These findings demonstrate a significant nationwide disparity in the sex distribution of adults with SCD engaged in specialized care and are hypothesis-generating rather than definitive evidence of transition failure. Future research is needed to elucidate the factors contributing to the underrepresentation of males in adult SCD clinics and to evaluate targeted interventions, including flexible, nurse-led care models, to support engagement and retention in adult care.

articles.title: Surgery for abnormal uterine bleeding at Sørlandet Hospital.
articles.journal: Tidsskrift for den Norske laegeforening : tidsskrift for praktisk medicin, ny raekke
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Abnormal uterine bleeding affects 15-20 % of women of reproductive age and is a common indication for surgery. The aim of this study was to describe the extent of surgical intervention and the choice of surgical procedure among premenopausal women with this condition and to identify factors associated with hysterectomy.

MATERIAL AND METHOD: Women aged ≤ 55 years who had contact with Sørlandet Hospital between 1. January 2011 and 31 December 2021 due to benign abnormal uterine bleeding (ICD-10 diagnosis codes N92.0-N92.6) were identified. Following data extraction from electronic patient records using a structured query language, the data were analysed using descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: Of 4947 women with abnormal uterine bleeding, 2278 (46 %) underwent surgery. Of these, 1830 (80 %) had one procedure, 415 (18 %) had two and 33 (1 %) had three. Thermal endometrial ablation was the most common initial procedure (902 of 2278, 40 %), while hysterectomy was performed on 649 women (28 %). Fibroids, pain and anaemia were associated with hysterectomy, but age was not.

INTERPRETATION: Over an 11-year period, almost half of the patients with benign abnormal uterine bleeding underwent surgery. More than a quarter of these had a hysterectomy. Our findings suggest that the overall symptom burden, in addition to the amount of menstrual blood loss, is associated with the likelihood of undergoing hysterectomy.

articles.title: Epithelial responses to pneumococcal capsules drive leukocyte activation and functionality in a serotype-specific manner.
articles.abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae (pneumococcus) poses a major disease burden to young children and older adults. About 100 different polysaccharide capsule types (serotypes) have been identified. The capsule is a crucial virulence factor that contributes to pneumococcal immune evasion, and the capsule structure differs per serotype. Some pneumococcal serotypes are associated with invasive disease, while other serotypes are predominantly found in carriage. In this study, we evaluated how the pneumococcal capsule of different serotypes affects epithelial cytokine secretion and ensuing epithelial-mediated leukocyte activation, and functionality. To study the possible effects of the pneumococcal capsule, we infected primary nasal epithelial cells with isogenic capsule mutants of TIGR4 (serotype 4) expressing a serotype 1, 6B, 8, or 35B capsule or no capsule (Δcps). The serotype-specific epithelial cytokines were thereafter analyzed and used to examine their effect on leukocyte activation, migration, and leukocyte-dependent pneumococcal killing. We showed that epithelial cytokine secretion differed per serotype, with the strongest induction after infection with the unencapsulated mutant. Distinct expression profiles of epithelium-induced leukocyte activation markers were observed for each serotype, involving changes in activation marker expression for all investigated cell types. Furthermore, compared with other serotypes, epithelial chemokines induced by serotype 8 reduced neutrophil migration and leukocyte-mediated killing of pneumococci. These data highlight the serotype-specific effect of epithelial cells on leukocyte activation and pneumococcal clearance. The results provide additional insights into serotype-specific differences in the pneumococcal interactions with the mucosal surfaces of the human respiratory tract.IMPORTANCEStreptococcus pneumoniae, also referred to as pneumococcus, poses a major disease burden in young children and older adults, with differences in virulence between serotypes. Little is known about serotype-specific effects on colonization of the upper respiratory epithelial tract. Using isogenic mutants of a single pneumococcal strain expressing capsules of different serotypes, we were able to solely look at the effect of the capsule on epithelium-leukocyte interaction. We found that the various serotypes induced distinct cytokine responses in epithelial cells, and that these epithelial cytokines affected leukocyte activation and their pneumococcal killing capacities. Together with pneumococcal serotype-specific differences in immune evasion described by others, our findings provide additional insights into serotype-specific differences in virulence and help unravel why some serotypes are prone to cause invasive disease while other serotypes are mostly associated with carriage.

articles.title: Tomatidine derivatives suppress Dengue virus infection through entry and post-entry inhibition.
articles.abstract: Dengue is a rapidly spreading disease transmitted by mosquitoes and is caused by the Dengue virus (DENV), affecting approximately 390 million individuals globally. Approved vaccines for use have limited efficacy, and there are no approved antivirals. Tomatidine, a steroidal alkaloid obtained from Solanum species, has demonstrated broad-spectrum antiviral properties, leading to the investigation of its derivatives for their anti-DENV activity. In the current study, the anti-DENV potential of tomatidine and 11 such derivatives was assessed using a combination of in vitro and in silico approaches. Vero cells were used to evaluate the cytotoxicity and antiviral effects of the derivatives in pre-, co-, and post-treatment settings. The results indicated that the derivatives 5d, 5f, and 5c possessed the most potent antiviral effects; 5d achieved a 2.81 log decrease in viral RNA, while both 5f and 5c suppressed viral activity under both pre- and post-treatment conditions (5f has a selectivity index of 43.36), including the entry phase, as indicated by the entry assay. Furthermore, effective inhibition was noted between 0 and 9 h post-infection (hpi) and 15-21 hpi via a time-of-addition assay, indicating dual-phase activity. Additionally, docking and molecular dynamics studies revealed stable interactions of compounds 5c and 5d with the non-structural proteins NS1 and NS5-RdRp of DENV, reinforcing the experimental observations. In conclusion, tomatidine derivatives, especially 5d, 5f, and 5c, showed significant potential as anti-DENV therapeutics, necessitating additional mechanistic and in vivo studies to determine their clinical efficacy.IMPORTANCEDengue is a major global health threat, infecting hundreds of millions of people each year, yet there are no antiviral drugs available for this disease. Identifying safe and effective therapeutics is therefore a global public health priority. In this study, we discovered three promising tomatidine-derived compounds (5d, 5f, and 5c) that markedly reduced Dengue virus replication in laboratory experiments. These compounds acted at multiple stages of the viral life cycle, suggesting that they could both limit the establishment of infection and suppress viral spread after the infection has begun. Computational analyses further indicated that these molecules target key viral proteins while also influencing host pathways that support viral infection, providing insights into how they may exert their antiviral effects. Together, our findings identify tomatidine derivatives as promising lead candidates for dengue antiviral drug development and provide a strong foundation for future preclinical and clinical investigations.

articles.title: Short 3-month telemedical monitoring is associated only with partial maintenance of functional performance 12 months later: a single-arm study in patients with heart failure in underserved areas.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: A 3-month telemedical care model under specialist supervision was associated with an improvement in New York Heart Association (NYHA) class and quality of life in heart failure (HF) population from underserved areas.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to investigate whether the effects of a 3-month telemonitoring intervention (3m-INT) were maintained 12 months later.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this prospective study, HF patients were enrolled in 5 rural voivodeships and were evaluated after completion of a 3m-INT and 12 months later using the NYHA scale, the Chronic Heart Failure Questionnaire (CHFQ) and the EuroQol Visual Analogue Scale. The clinical composite endpoint (CCE) was death, hospitalization for HF decompensation, stroke, or myocardial infarction.

RESULTS: Of 429 HF patients who completed 3m-INT, 320 (74.6%) were reevaluated 12 months later. Within the 3m-INT, 1 patient died and 6 more during the following 12 months. After 12 months follow-up, CCE occurred in 23 (7.2%) patients while the NYHA class improved in 42 (13.4%) patients, remained unchanged in 131 (41.7%), and deteriorated in 141 (44.9%). Finally, the distribution of NYHA classes at 12 months remained significantly better than at baseline (P <0.001). Atrial fibrillation was independently associated with the occurrence of CCE (P = 0.005). EuroQol Visual Analogue Scale-assessed quality of life did not change (P = 0.36), while CHFQ-measured dyspnea measured by CHFQ deteriorated (P <0.001) after a 1-year observation.

CONCLUSIONS: After 3m-INT followed by 12 months of observation, only partial maintenance of functional performance of HF patients in underserved areas was observed. Atrial fibrillation was associated with an unfavorable clinical effect.

articles.title: Does reading patient information leaflets influence adherence and adverse drug reactions in arterial hypertension? A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Most patients after receiving pharmacotherapy prescription read patient information leaflets (PILs). Many studies highlight the role of the nocebo effect, whereby information on adverse drug reactions (ADRs) increases symptom reporting.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to assess the association between reading PILs, adherence to pharmacotherapy, and the frequency and types of reported ADRs.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional questionnaire-based study included patients receiving inpatient or outpatient care at a hypertension clinic. The analysis included data from 949 individuals (529 female, 420 male) diagnosed with arterial hypertension.

RESULTS: Approximately 60% of patients reported reading PILs. Compared with non-readers, they were younger (median age 63 vs 67 years), had a shorter duration of hypertension (median duration 10 vs 11.5 years), and fewer cardiovascular comorbidities, while the prevalence of non-cardiovascular comorbidities and the number of medications prescribed did not differ between groups. PILs readers more frequently reported adherence to medical recommendations (98% vs 61%), although 11% reported self-discontinuation at least once after reading the leaflet. They also reported a lower overall frequency of ADRs (38% vs 57%), mainly driven by fewer allergic and idiosyncratic reactions (23% vs 40%), while pharmacologically predictable ADRs did not differ between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Reading PILs was positively associated with self-reported adherence to medical recommendations and with a lower frequency of reported ADRs. These findings suggest that the beneficial effect of improved adherence associated with reading PILs may outweigh the potential negative impact of the nocebo effect.

articles.title: Advances in HIV-associated pulmonary diseases: an official American Thoracic Society workshop report.
authors: American Thoracic Society Assembly on Pulmonary Infections and Tuberculosis
articles.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
articles.abstract: People with HIV (PWH) are at increased risk of a broad range of infectious and non-infectious pulmonary diseases. Since the last ATS Workshop on HIV-associated pulmonary disease, large national and international cohorts have demonstrated ongoing gaps in our understanding of lung disease in this vulnerable population that range from underappreciation of disease incidence and prevalence to lack of targeted treatments. Translational work on the underlying mechanisms of disease has demonstrated novel, HIV-specific mechanisms that may lend themselves to tailored therapies. Twenty-four experts in HIV-associated lung disease from across the translational spectrum were invited to participate in this ATS-sponsored Workshop utilizing a modified Delphi method that included a series of pre- and post-workshop electronic surveys and a two-day virtual workshop. Lung disease among PWH is driven by complex and interrelated mechanisms including persistent immune dysregulation, oxidative stress, accelerated aging, and microbiome alterations. Despite these advances in our understanding, important gaps persist between mechanistic insights and clinical care that include limited HIV-specific trials, underrepresentation of PWH in studies of lung disease, and the absence of tailored care strategies. These gaps are further accentuated by substantial variation in the availability of data from the most affected populations, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa and among children and adolescents. Overcoming these challenges will require coordinated, globally representative research efforts that leverage large cohorts, integrate multi-omics and longitudinal phenotyping, use mechanistic insights to inform clinical trials, and consider implementation science approaches with the ultimate goal of developing tailored prevention and treatment strategies for HIV-associated pulmonary diseases.

articles.title: As-needed inhaled corticosteroids in asthma: an Official American Thoracic Society clinical practice guideline.
authors: American Thoracic Society Assembly on Allergy, Immunology and Inflammation
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inhaled corticosteroid (ICS)-containing reliever therapy has demonstrated efficacy in improving asthma outcomes when compared to short-acting beta2-agonists (SABA) alone but remains underutilized. The purpose of this guideline is to provide recommendations surrounding the use of combination ICS-formoterol or ICS+SABA (in combination or separate inhalers) as reliever therapy across the asthma severity spectrum in adolescents and adults.

METHODS: The American Thoracic Society clinical practice guideline panel evaluated six research questions in the PICO format addressing the use of ICS-containing reliever therapy across National Asthma Education and Prevention Program (NAEPP) asthma treatment steps 1-5. The methodology team conducted systematic literature reviews and GRADE assessments, which the panel utilized to inform the recommendations for each specific PICO and overall.

RECOMMENDATIONS: In patients at NAEPP steps 1 and 2, the panel made strong recommendations for the use of as-needed-only ICS-SABA or ICS-formoterol over SABA-only therapy, and conditional recommendations over scheduled ICS + as-needed SABA. In patients at NAEPP steps 3-5, the taskforce made a strong recommendation for the use of maintenance-and-reliever therapy (MART) with ICS-formoterol over scheduled ICS-LABA plus as-needed SABA. In patients at NAEPP steps 3-5 who are using scheduled maintenance ICS-LABA, the panel made a conditional recommendation for use of ICS+SABA reliever over SABA reliever. In considering these recommendations, the panel valued the importance of preventing severe exacerbations and considered the risk of SABA-only treatment, as well as ICS and systemic corticosteroid (SCS) exposure.

CONCLUSIONS: This clinical practice guideline, informed by systematic reviews and GRADE-based appraisals of PICO-framed evidence, makes these evidence-based recommendations for the safe and effective use of ICS-containing reliever therapy in asthma.

articles.title: Neural circuits, cognition, and behavior in diffuse glioma.
articles.abstract: Diffuse gliomas arise within and become functionally integrated into neural circuits, establishing bidirectional interactions between malignant cells and the surrounding brain. Neuronal activity promotes glioma growth and progression, while glioma cells remodel the excitability, connectivity, and functional organization of the neural circuits they infiltrate. Pathological excitation-inhibition imbalance can impair cortical information processing, while tumor infiltration simultaneously disrupts, preserves, and induces adaptive reorganization of distributed functional networks. Language processing provides a well defined framework for examining these competing effects because language processing depends on distributed cortical and subcortical networks whose organization can be interrogated using neuroimaging, electrophysiology, and direct cortical stimulation. The pattern and severity of glioma-associated language dysfunction reflect the interaction among tumor location, growth kinetics, molecular and histopathological features, white matter involvement, and the capacity for adaptive redistribution of function within ipsilateral and contralateral networks. Slowly growing gliomas can permit substantial functional reorganization, whereas rapidly infiltrating tumors may constrain the time and biological substrate available for effective network adaptation. In this review, we examine reciprocal glioma-neural circuit interactions, with particular emphasis on the mechanisms of glioma-associated neuronal hyperexcitability and the disruption, preservation, and adaptive remodeling of language networks.

articles.title: Identification of Novel Protein Biomarkers and Lifestyle-Modifiable Targets for Osteoporosis: Evidence from Mendelian Randomization and Colocalization Analyses.
articles.journal: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osteoporosis (OP), a degenerative bone disease prevalent in aging populations, can lead to various complications and significantly impair the quality of life of elderly patients. We aimed to identify OP-related protein biomarkers and modifiable lifestyle factors for OP prevention in older adults.

METHODS: Summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) and colocalization analyses were conducted to assess the possible causal effects of plasma protein on OP. Genetic data for plasma proteins were derived from the deCODE (4907 proteins) and UK Biobank-PPP (2923 proteins) datasets. OP summary statistics were obtained from the FinnGen study (10,461 cases). Two-sample Mendelian randomization (TSMR) analyses were subsequently performed to evaluate the effects of lifestyle factors on OP-related proteins.

RESULTS: Primary SMR analysis identified 31 and 24 OP-related proteins in the deCODE and UKB-PPP cohorts, respectively. Cross-analysis of both datasets identified nine OP-related plasma protein targets. Among them, RSPO3 showed moderate evidence of colocalization with OP (PP.H4 = 0.643). TSMR analysis suggested that genetically predicted higher body mass index (BMI) was associated with increased RSPO3 levels (β = 0.08, 95% CI 0.02 to 0.14, p = 0.001), whereas type 2 diabetes (T2DM) was associated with lower RSPO3 levels (β = -5.71, 95% CI -11.16 to -0.26, p = 0.045).

CONCLUSIONS: This study identified nine plasma protein biomarkers with genetic evidence supporting their association with OP risk, with RSPO3 showing the strongest supportive evidence among the prioritized targets. These findings offer new insights into OP etiology and highlight how metabolic traits may influence bone health via specific protein mediators.

articles.title: Enzyme-Antibiotic Liquid Crystalline Nanoparticles for Enhanced Antibiofilm Activity, Bacterial Clearance, and Accelerated Healing of Infected Wounds.
articles.abstract: Biofilm-associated wound infections remain difficult to treat because bacteria are protected within extracellular polymeric matrices that restrict antibiotic penetration, promote antimicrobial tolerance, and delay tissue repair. Here, we developed liquid crystalline nanoparticles (LCNPs) for topical coformulation of gentamicin (GEN) and recombinant human DNase I (rhDNase), combining aminoglycoside therapy with an eDNA-targeting enzyme. GEN + rhDNase-LCNPs were successfully formulated as nanoscale particles with low polydispersity, high encapsulation efficiency, and formulation-dependent in vitro release behavior. LCNP formulation preserved GEN antibacterial activity against planktonic Escherichia coli Xen14 and reduced the MBIC against established biofilms by approximately 4-fold. In a minimum biofilm eradication concentration (MBEC) model, GEN + rhDNase-LCNPs achieved the greatest reduction in biofilm-associated viable bacteria, producing an approximately 6-log reduction compared with untreated biofilm controls and supporting the benefit of combining antibiotic delivery with rhDNase. Notably, GEN + rhDNase-LCNPs markedly suppressed bacterial burden and reduced recoverable bacteria at day 9 to near the limit of detection in a bioluminescent E. coli Xen14 biofilm-associated excisional wound infection mouse model. This antibacterial effect translated into accelerated macroscopic wound closure and improved histological repair, including an approximately 80% reduction in wound gape compared with infected controls. Masson's trichrome staining further confirmed enhanced tissue remodeling, with the collagen-positive wound area increasing to approximately 88% following GEN + rhDNase-LCNP treatment, compared with approximately 21% in infected controls. In conclusion, LCNP-mediated codelivery of GEN and rhDNase improved bacterial clearance, re-epithelialization, and collagen deposition, supporting this platform as a promising topical antibiofilm strategy for infected wounds.

articles.title: Letter: Interpreting Rule-Out and Rule-In Enhanced Liver Fibrosis Thresholds in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease. Authors' Reply.
A little-known perspective on the I-squared statistic.
articles.abstract: The I-squared statistic has become hugely popular in meta-analysis. Motivated by the recent statement that 'Informally, it can be considered to reflect the extent to which confidence intervals displayed in a forest plot do not overlap with each other', this short note formalises this perspective. The insights provided by our analysis lend further weight to the interpretation of the I-squared statistic as a measure of inconsistency. This perspective reminds us that visual inspections of forest plots are vitally important when assessing between-study variation.

articles.title: Short communication: Urinary schistosomiasis mimicking a bladder tumour in a Somali student diagnosed in Türkiye.
articles.abstract: Urinary schistosomiasis caused by Schistosoma haematobium may mimic bladder malignancy in patients evaluated outside endemic regions. We report a 20-year-old Somali university student who had been living in Türkiye for two years and had a history of freshwater exposure in Somalia. He presented with painless macroscopic haematuria and lower urinary tract symptoms. An initial 50-mL urine sample collected at 11:00 showed no parasitic structures; a repeat 20-mL terminal-stream sample collected at 13:30 on the same day revealed characteristic terminal-spined S. haematobium eggs on unstained light microscopy of centrifuged urine sediment. Cystoscopy demonstrated an approximately 2-cm sessile bladder lesion suspicious for malignancy and diffuse yellowish granular mucosal lesions ('sandy patches'). Transurethral resection revealed eosinophil-rich chronic active cystitis and subepithelial schistosome eggs without dysplasia or malignancy. The patient received praziquantel. This case illustrates the importance of epidemiological history, repeated urine microscopy, and recognition of characteristic cystoscopic findings when evaluating bladder masses in patients from endemic regions.

articles.title: Long-term safety of Etrasimod in ulcerative colitis: a comprehensive review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Etrasimod is an oral sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor modulator approved for the treatment of moderate to severe ulcerative colitis. Its targeted mechanism, once-daily dosing and oral formulation make it an important addition to the therapeutic landscape. However, its safety profile and optimal clinical positioning require careful evaluation.

AREAS COVERED: This narrative review examines the pharmacology, efficacy and safety of etrasimod in ulcerative colitis, drawing on evidence from the OASIS, ELEVATE UC and ENLIGHT UC trial programmes, open-label extension studies, meta-analyses, pharmacovigilance reports and emerging real-world cohorts. The practicalities of prescribing and monitoring are also covered. A literature search was conducted in MEDLINE to identify appropriate studies.

EXPERT OPINION: Current evidence supports etrasimod as a generally well-tolerated treatment option, with low rates of serious adverse events, serious infections, opportunistic infections and malignancy which do not differ substantially from placebo. Key safety considerations include first-dose bradycardia, atrioventricular conduction abnormalities, macular oedema, hepatic enzyme elevations, and lymphopenia, all of which necessitate appropriate screening and monitoring. Etrasimod may be particularly useful in patients with moderately active disease and limited prior advanced therapy exposure, whilst its reassuring safety profile and low risk of serious infection make it an attractive candidate for use in advanced combination therapy.

articles.title: A Matter of Time: Does Early vs Late Failure Impact Redo Pouch Survival?
articles.journal: Diseases of the colon and rectum
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anastomotic leaks, pelvic sepsis, and related complications are established predictors of pouch failure after ileal pouch-anal anastomosis (IPAA). However, the effect of the timing of index pouch failure on outcomes after redo pouch surgery remains poorly understood.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether the timing of index pouch failure predicts redo pouch survival.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: Single quaternary referral center.

PATIENTS: Patients with prior IPAA who underwent redo pouch surgery between 2000 and 2024.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was redo pouch failure, defined as a composite of pouch excision, permanent rediversion after redo pouch creation, or failure to achieve ileostomy closure. The primary exposure was the timing of index pouch failure, categorized as early failure (rediversion ≤ 6 months after index IPAA) or late failure (rediversion > 6 months).

RESULTS: A total of 320 patients met inclusion criteria, including 57 with early index pouch failure and 263 with late failure. Index pouch leak (50.9% vs. 33.5%; p=0.01) and pelvic abscess (36.8% vs. 14.1%; p<0.001) were more common in the early group. Ileostomy closure rates after redo pouch surgery were similar (96.5% vs. 88.6%; p=0.07). On multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression, late index failure (HR 3.09; 95% CI 1.07-8.87; p=0.04) and inflammatory indications for redo (HR 2.40; 95% CI 1.15-5.0; p=0.02) were independent predictors of redo pouch failure. Secondary pouch failure occurred in 10.7% of the early group vs. 22.8% of the late group (p=0.04). Sensitivity analyses using bootstrap internal validation confirmed the model's reliability, with an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.64; the low model optimism (3.9%) suggests the findings are robust and likely to generalize to other patient populations.

LIMITATIONS: Retrospective design and single-center setting may limit generalizability.

CONCLUSIONS: Late failure after index IPAA was associated with increased risk of subsequent pouch failure after redo IPAA. See Video Abstract.

articles.title: In familial hypercholesterolaemia, remnant cholesterol above 1 mmol/L is associated with 50% higher risk of coronary artery disease.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Familial hypercholesterolaemia (FH) leads to lifelong elevated low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol and increased risk of coronary artery disease. We tested the hypothesis that elevated remnant cholesterol additionally increases cardiovascular risk in FH.

METHODS: In the Copenhagen General Population Study (CGPS) and UK Biobank, 108,751 and 428,625 individuals were classified as with or without FH according to clinical scores and genetic mutations. In the two cohorts, 7,708 and 50,997 experienced coronary artery disease, respectively.

RESULTS: In CGPS and UK Biobank, remnant cholesterol ≥1 mmol/L (39 mg/dL) was observed in 12% and 11% of individuals without FH (N = 104,226 and 403,172), in 33% and 40% with Simon Broome FH (N = 3,923 and 23,860), in 44% and 78% with MEDPED FH (N = 1,005 and 2,465), in 33% and 34% with DLCN FH (N = 744 and 1,207), and in 12% and 21% of individuals with genetic FH (N = 188 and 875). Likewise in the CGPS and UK Biobank, the multivariable adjusted hazard ratios for coronary artery disease by remnant cholesterol ≥1 vs. < 1 mmol/L (39 mg/dL) were 1.49 (95% CI: 1.39-1.59) and 1.47 (1.43-1.52) in individuals without FH, 1.59 (1.31-1.93) and 1.18 (1.10-1.27) in Simon Broome FH, 1.50 (1.08-2.08) and 1.14 (0.89-1.45) in MEDPED FH, 1.60 (1.17-2.21) and 1.59 (1.20-2.09) in DLCN FH, and 1.48 (0.59-3.69) and 1.39 (0.88-2.19) in genetic FH.

CONCLUSION: In familial hypercholesterolaemia, remnant cholesterol ≥1 mmol/L (39 mg/dL) vs below is associated with ≈50% higher risk of coronary artery disease, that is, above the already high risk due to lifelong genetically elevated LDL cholesterol.

articles.title: Development and Validation of a ChatGPT-Based Assessment for Conversation-Related Clinical Skills in Occupational Therapy OSCEs.
articles.journal: The American journal of occupational therapy : official publication of the American Occupational Therapy Association
articles.abstract: ImportanceConversation-related clinical skills are central to Objective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCEs) in occupational therapy. However, real-time examiner scoring is resource-intensive and may overlook students' specific skills. Transcript-based scoring with Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer (ChatGPT) may address these limitations.ObjectiveTo develop a ChatGPT-based assessment for chief-complaint interview OSCEs (G-ACE) and examine criterion validity against expert-consensus ratings, test-retest reliability, and inter-rater reliability.DesignSecondary analysis of de-identified transcripts from 8-min chief-complaint interviews with a simulated patient with stroke during an OSCE.SettingsA university in northern Taiwan.ParticipantsFifty-eight de-identified transcripts from undergraduate occupational therapy students.ResultsCriterion validity was acceptable for "Primary Symptoms and Related Feelings" and "Impact on Daily Life" items (weighted kappa ≥ 0.60), but lower for "Rehabilitation Expectations" and "Communication Skills" items (0.18-0.59). For domain and total scores, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) were 0.17 to 0.78 and percentages of mean absolute errors (MAE%s) were 4.6% to 20.7%. Test-retest reliability was acceptable at the item level (weighted kappa = 0.68-1.00), and acceptable to good at the domain and total score levels (ICC = 0.65-0.85; MAE% = 2.3%-9.1%). Inter-rater reliability was acceptable for most domain and total scores (ICCs = 0.52-0.78; MAE%s = 1.3%-12.0%), except for the "Rehabilitation Expectations" domain (ICCs = 0.17-0.30; MAE%s = 1.3%-7.3%).Conclusion and RelevanceThe G-ACE demonstrated generally acceptable test-retest reliability and small absolute differences from expert ratings for domain and total scores. Because some items showed lower consistency with expert ratings, formative feedback should be interpreted cautiously based on transcript evidence.

articles.title: Opposing modulation of QUAC1/ALMT12 by S-type channel inhibition and R-type channel activation during elevated-CO2 and ABA-induced stomatal movement.
articles.abstract: Atmospheric CO2 concentrations, now 50% higher than pre-industrial levels, induce plant stomatal closure. The slow (S)-type anion channels in guard cells are activated by elevated CO2/bicarbonate and promote that process. However, the response of the rapid (R)-type anion channels to CO2/bicarbonate remains unclear. Here, we show that bicarbonate fails to activate the R-type anion channel QUAC1 (ALMT12) in either Xenopus oocytes or guard cell protoplasts, which indicates that the two channel types are differentially in response to CO2/bicarbonate. Furthermore, we demonstrate that QUAC1/ALMT12 negatively regulates CO2/bicarbonate-induced stomatal closure, achieved through its inhibition of SLAC1. As such, ALMT12 has opposite functional consequences in ABA vs CO2 pathways due to differential upstream activation.

articles.title: Early recognition of paediatric kidney disease in low- and middle-income countries: Clinical red flags and referral strategies for primary care.
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) in children is an important but often under-recognized cause of long-term morbidity, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) where delayed diagnosis is common. Early manifestations are frequently subtle and include oedema, haematuria, proteinuria, recurrent urinary tract infections, growth failure, hypertension, and unexplained anaemia. This review highlights practical clinical red flags that should prompt evaluation for kidney disease, outlines low-cost investigations feasible in primary care, and summarizes indications for timely nephrology referral. Emphasis is placed on careful history-taking, targeted physical examination, blood pressure measurement, urinalysis, serum creatinine estimation, and renal ultrasonography where indicated. Strengthening awareness among frontline healthcare providers and caregivers, together with structured referral pathways, may facilitate earlier diagnosis, preserve kidney function, reduce preventable complications, and improve long-term outcomes for children with kidney disease in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Transcriptional Regulatory Crosstalk Between Heat Stress and Nitrogen-Sulfur Nutrition in Plants.
articles.abstract: Plant responses to high temperature depend on the nutritional state in which the stress occurs. Nitrogen and sulfur shape this state through photosynthetic capacity, protein synthesis, nitric oxide production, and thiol redox buffering, while heat alters nutrient uptake and assimilation. We review how nitrate and sulfate nutrition interact with heat responses through direct transcriptional cross-regulation, metabolite- or redox-mediated regulation, and convergence on shared processes. Nitrate provides the clearest transcriptional link: in Arabidopsis, the nitrate-responsive transcription factor NLP7 regulates HSFA2 and HSFA3, encoding heat stress transcription factors that sustain chaperone expression and acquired thermotolerance, and rice NLP3 binds the HsfA3 and HsfA7 promoters under heat. Nitrate reductase-derived nitric oxide modulates HSF activity, and warm temperature represses the nitrate transporter and sensor NRT1.1 through the transcription factor HY5. For sulfur, evidence comes mainly from glutathione-deficient mutants, glutathione application and hydrogen sulfide donors, which alter heat-responsive transcription factors and antioxidant genes; whether sulfate supply acts through these routes, and how sulfate sensing and the sulfate-limitation regulator SLIM1 contribute, remain unresolved. Comparing published Arabidopsis transcriptomic meta-analyses, we identify genes responding to heat and to nitrate or sulfate and propose candidate regulators. In crops, nitrogen maintains photosynthesis under heat but does not consistently protect yield.

articles.title: A Phase 2 Trial of a Respiratory Syncytial Virus and Human Metapneumovirus Combination Virus-Like Particle Vaccine IVX-A12 in Adults ≥60 Years of Age.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Older adults (≥60 years) are susceptible to severe outcomes from infection with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) or human metapneumovirus (hMPV). IVX-A12 is an investigational vaccine that uses virus-like particles (VLPs) to elicit an immune response against RSV and hMPV.

METHODS: This Phase 2 trial (NCT06481579) randomized (1:1) adults ≥60 years of age to receive a single dose of IVX-A12 (150 µg RSV/150 µg hMPV) or the licensed RSV vaccine RSVPreF3 120 µg with AS01E adjuvant. Safety and immunogenicity were evaluated through 180 days post-vaccination.

RESULTS: Overall, 143 participants received IVX-A12 (n = 71) or RSVPreF3 (n = 72). Solicited adverse reactions were reported through 7 days post-vaccination (IVX-A12, 25 [35.2%]; RSVPreF3, 36 [50.0%]). Unsolicited adverse events (AEs) were collected through Day 29 (IVX-A12, 5 [7.0%]; RSVPreF3, 11 [15.3%]). Serious AEs (IVX-A12, 2 [2.8%]; RSVPreF3, 1 [1.4%]) and medically attended AEs (IVX-A12, 1 [1.4%]; RSVPreF3, 9 [12.5%]) were documented through Day 181. There were no AEs of special interest and AEs leading to study discontinuation. At Day 29, IVX-A12 and RSVPreF3 administration increased RSV A neutralizing antibody (nAb) levels with geometric mean fold rise (GMFR) of 3.4 and 6.5, and RSV B nAb levels with GMFR of 2.9 and 5.4, respectively. IVX-A12, but not RSVPreF3, also increased hMPV A (GMFR 3.0) and hMPV B (GMFR 2.9) nAb levels.

CONCLUSIONS: IVX-A12 and RSVPreF3 were well tolerated and elicited nAb responses against their targeted pathogens. Given the neutralizing antibody response following IVX-A12, further investigation of an RSV-hMPV VLP combination vaccine is warranted.

articles.title: Beyond Dialysis Independence: The Importance of Longitudinal Renal Follow-Up after Severe Acute Kidney Injury.
Understanding Host-Phage Interactions in Chronic Wounds, Emphasising Inflammatory Markers and Neutralising Antibody Responses.
articles.journal: The international journal of lower extremity wounds
articles.abstract: BackgroundChronic wounds cause considerable morbidity, which is further compounded by antimicrobial resistance and biofilm formation. Bacteriophage therapy (BT) presents a promising alternative. However, issues such as host immune neutralisation and inflammatory reactions remain unresolved.MethodsThis prospective, interventional, non-randomized control study was conducted at the Institute of Medical Sciences, Banaras Hindu University, from July 2022 to February 2026. It involved 100 patients with chronic wounds (>6 weeks). It had two groups: Group I (n = 50) received bacteriophage therapy (BT), while Group II (n = 50) received conventional therapy (CT). Bacteriophages were isolated and applied topically every other day. Serum levels of IL-1β, IL-6, MMP-9, and TGF-β were measured using ELISA at baseline, immediately after therapy, and at six weeks after treatment completion. Neutralising antibodies in the BT group were measured through serum-phage interaction assays and data analysis was done.ResultsFollow-up was completed in 90% of patients. Diabetes (50%) was the most common comorbidity. The most commonly isolated bacteria were Pseudomonas aeruginosa (30%), Escherichia coli (26%), and Klebsiella pneumoniae (26%). The therapy duration was significantly shorter (P < .001) in the BT group (1.46 ± 0.63 months) than in the CT group (2.92 ± 1.02 months). Levels of IL-1β, IL-6, MMP-9, and TGF-β decreased significantly in both groups during and after treatment. Neutralising antibodies were detected in only 2 out of 45 BT patients (4.4%) with complete follow-up.ConclusionBT promoted faster wound healing without notably altering cytokine profiles. The fact that around 4.4% of patients developed neutralising antibodies, which did not interfere with healing, suggests that phage therapy can be safely applied.

articles.title: Are Higher-Order Carbapenems Effective Therapy for Patients with Ertapenem-Resistant Enterobacterales Invasive Infections?
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The IDSA guidance suggests treating Enterobacterales resistant to ertapenem but susceptible to imipenem or meropenem with a susceptible carbapenem in the absence of carbapenemase production; however, clinical outcomes data are limited.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter prospective cohort study of hospitalized patients with invasive ceftriaxone-resistant Enterobacterales infections, comparing 30-day mortality between ertapenem-susceptible (ETP-S) and ertapenem-resistant (ETP-R) isolates. ETP-S isolates with an ESBL/AmpC phenotype served as the comparator because carbapenems are reliably active against these organisms. Carbapenem susceptibility was confirmed by broth microdilution. Inclusion criteria included: (1) susceptibility to imipenem or meropenem, (2) absence of carbapenemase genes, and (3) >72 hours of definitive therapy with imipenem or meropenem. Inverse probability weighting (IPW) adjusted for baseline differences, and logistic regression estimated odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals.

RESULTS: Among 374 patients, 238 (64%) were infected with ETP-S and 136 (36%) ETP-R isolates. Baseline characteristics were balanced after IPW. ETP-R infection was associated with higher 30-day mortality (OR 2.24, 95% CI 1.26-3.98, p=0.006). Similarly, 14-day and in-hospital mortality were significantly higher among patients with ETP-R infections. The highest mortality was observed among patients with isolates resistant to two carbapenems (e.g., ertapenem and meropenem). Genomic analyses demonstrated enrichment of porin alterations and more non-carbapenemase β-lactamase genes (e.g., blaCTX-M, blaOXA-10) in ETP-R isolates.

CONCLUSION: Among patients with Enterobacterales bacteremia treated with imipenem or meropenem, ETP-R isolates were associated with higher mortality than ETP-S isolates, challenging current guidance. This likely reflects combined porin loss and increased β-lactamase activity, potentially resulting in partial hydrolysis of higher-order carbapenems despite in vitro susceptibility.

articles.title: Adherence System Usability Patient Experience and Psychosocial Impact in Robot Assisted Gait Neurorehabilitation A Cross Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundAttendance, usability and rehabilitation experience may relate to perceived psychosocial impact in robotic neurorehabilitation.ObjectiveTo examine these associations in adults receiving robot-assisted gait neurorehabilitation, including diagnosis-adjusted and exploratory indirect associations.MethodsThis single-center observational study included 250 adults with stroke, spinal cord injury, multiple sclerosis or cerebral palsy. The System Usability Scale (SUS), Neurorehabilitation Experience Questionnaire (NREQ) and Psychosocial Impact of Assistive Devices Scale (PIADS) were administered in week two. Attendance covered the planned course; participation equaled attended/planned sessions × 100. Analyses included Spearman correlations, adjusted regression, indirect-association models with 5,000 bootstrap resamples, Kruskal-Wallis tests and Cronbach's alpha.ResultsMean participation was 86.35 ± 8.38%. Mean SUS, NREQ and PIADS scores were 72.79 ± 12.06, 27.84 ± 4.92 and 1.67 ± 0.74, respectively. Adherence correlated with SUS (rs = 0.41), NREQ (rs = 0.49) and PIADS (rs = 0.53; all p < 0.001). After adjustment for diagnosis, age, sex and disease duration, adherence (B = 0.0145), SUS (B = 0.0210) and NREQ (B = 0.0630) remained associated with PIADS (all p < 0.001; R2 = 0.650). The diagnosis-adjusted indirect association through NREQ was 0.0252 (95% bootstrap CI 0.0178-0.0336). Scores differed across adherence categories (all p < 0.001). Cronbach's alpha values were 0.86, 0.89 and 0.94, respectively.ConclusionGreater attendance, usability and rehabilitation experience were associated with favorable psychosocial impact. Diagnostic heterogeneity, simultaneous questionnaire assessment and temporal mismatch with attendance limit interpretation. These findings establish neither causal mediation nor functional improvement.

articles.title: Exploratory Evidence of a Gene-Smoking Interaction Involving MTR rs1805087 in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is the most common form of diabetes worldwide. In Brazil, diabetes affects 7.7% of adults and represents a substantial public health and economic burden. Variants in the MTR gene may disrupt one-carbon metabolism, potentially contributing to hyperhomocysteinemia and increased susceptibility to T2DM. A case-control study involving 219 age- and sex-matched individuals was conducted to evaluate the association between the MTR rs1805087 variant and susceptibility to T2DM. Associations under different genetic inheritance models were examined using χ2 tests and odds ratios (95% confidence interval [CI]). In parallel, machine-learning (ML) algorithms were applied, with predictive performance assessed using accuracy, precision, sensitivity, and receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve (ROC-AUC). The variant was not independently associated with T2DM. However, among individuals with T2DM, genotype distributions differed according to smoking status, with significant associations under the codominant and recessive genetic models. Exploratory ML analyses showed limited discriminative ability in the independent test set, with ROC-AUC values of 0.555 for K-nearest neighbors (KNN), 0.524 for support vector machine (SVM), and 0.503 for random forest (RF). All models exhibited substantial declines in performance compared with cross-validation results obtained in the training set. MTR rs1805087 was not independently associated with T2DM in this studied population. However, differences in genotype distributions according to smoking status among individuals with T2DM may reflect context-dependent genetic effects. Exploratory ML analyses showed limited predictive performance but identified smoking as one of the most influential predictors across all evaluated algorithms.

articles.title: Nutrition clinicians connecting with patients and family members to reduce the risk of ethical dilemmas.
articles.journal: Nutrition in clinical practice : official publication of the American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition
articles.abstract: Nutrition clinicians need to recognize the importance of establishing meaningful connections with their patients and family members.
