In this manuscript, we discuss skills for making these connections and possibly reducing the risk of nutrition-related ethical dilemmas. American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition leaders have stressed the importance of clinician-patient connections. Insights from Jonathan Rhoads, who was a developer of parenteral nutrition, indicated that availability and affability are important traits for nutrition clinicians, not just ability. These qualities reflect a patient-centered approach grounded in compassion, empathy, and effective communication. We present two examples of teaching tools designed to develop these skills in nutrition clinicians. (1) A nutrition clinician play performed at the ASPEN Clinical Nutrition Week 2015 that used spoken words and nonverbal communication to demonstrate approaches to connecting with a patient's family members. (2) A module developed for graduate nutrition students in 2025 that uses an artificial intelligence-generated role-play simulation to provide practice engaging in conversations with patients and caregivers involving crucial issues about the use of artificially administered nutrition and hydration.

articles.title: Myths and Misconceptions About Modern Antiretroviral Therapy for HIV Treatment.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract: Transformative advances in the efficacy, simplicity, dosing, and safety profiles of antiretroviral therapy (ART) have revolutionized care for people with HIV. Yet, outdated or inaccurate conceptions about ART dosing and side effects, as well as laboratory testing, continue to influence treatment decisions. In the contemporary era of high resistance barrier second-generation integrase strand transfer inhibitors, two-drug regimens, and long-acting injectable options, the growing evidence base challenges certain longstanding assumptions and historical treatment paradigms. We review frequently encountered myths and misconceptions in modern HIV treatment, with the goal of updating infectious diseases clinicians and other HIV care practitioners.

articles.title: Controllable Template Assisted In Situ Perovskite Growth for Display Application.
articles.abstract: Metal halide perovskites are compelling emitters for next-generation optoelectronics, yet their translation into flexible display architectures remains limited by interfacial optical losses, non-radiative recombination, and poor operational durability. Here we report a one-step, template-assisted in situ crystallization strategy that integrates CsPbX3 (X = Cl, Br, I) directly within a porous polyethylene terephthalate (PET) membrane. A bifunctional diamine ligand molecularly bridges the perovskite and polymer, directing crystallization, promoting uniform pore filling and eliminating interfacial air gaps. This chemically defined interface suppresses non-radiative losses, increases light outcoupling from ∼13% to 36%, and yields a film-state photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of 62%. The resulting perovskite-integrated porous PET membrane retains ∼82% of its initial photoluminescence after 150 days under ambient conditions and exhibits a projected T50 of ∼10 000 h, establishing benchmark stability among in situ synthesized perovskite/polymer display-class systems. It further preserves >90% emission under repeated bending and enables inkjet-printed full-color RGB pixel arrays with 70% NTSC gamut. Using a highly porous PET membrane (0.5 µm pore diameter), a luminance of 1050 nits are achieved, confirming that brightness scales with pore density and is substrate limited. These results establish active encapsulation as a practical route to stable, efficient and mechanically compliant perovskite display platforms.

articles.title: Illness Identity in Type 1 Diabetes: A Nine-Year Longitudinal Perspective in Belgian Youth.
articles.abstract: This study offers a unique long-term perspective on the development of illness identity in young individuals with type 1 diabetes and examines how this process relates to their psychological and diabetes management outcomes over time. From a seven-wave longitudinal study, spanning 9 years, data was used from 403 Dutch-speaking adolescents and emerging adults with type 1 diabetes (ages 14-25 years at baseline). The group-level development of illness identity was examined using multivariate latent growth curve modeling, and distinct developmental trajectory classes of illness identity were identified through multivariate latent class growth analysis. Mean differences in depressive symptoms, self-reported management, and hemoglobin A1c across these classes were evaluated using the Bolck-Croon-Hagenaars method. At the group level, small but significant changes were observed with youth reporting more acceptance, enrichment, and engulfment, and less rejection over time. Next, five distinct trajectory classes were identified, each displaying unique developmental patterns of the illness identity dimensions. Youth in these classes differed substantially in their experience of depressive symptoms, self-reported management, and hemoglobin A1c over time. This study demonstrates the heterogeneity in how young individuals with T1D develop their illness identity and how these differences are tied to meaningful variation in psychological and diabetes-related functioning. These findings support illness identity as a clinically relevant target to inform holistic, person-centered care for individuals with type 1 diabetes.

articles.title: Neonatal Teeth in Patau Syndrome: A Rare Oral Phenotype and Bedside Surgical Management.
articles.journal: The Cleft palate-craniofacial journal : official publication of the American Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Association
articles.abstract: This report describes the first cytogenetically confirmed case of complete trisomy 13 associated with a highly mobile mandibular neonatal tooth and a contralateral eruption cyst associated with an unerupted tooth, managed by bedside surgery in the neonatal intensive care unit. A late-preterm newborn with trisomy 13, unilateral complete cleft lip and palate, and congenital heart disease presented with a highly mobile mandibular neonatal tooth and a contralateral eruption cyst associated with an unerupted tooth. Following multidisciplinary evaluation, both teeth were extracted at the bedside under local anesthesia and cardiorespiratory monitoring, without complications. This case expands the oral phenotypic spectrum of trisomy 13 and underscores the importance of early recognition, individualized management, and Hospital Dentistry in preventing airway-related complications in medically complex newborns.

articles.title: Tezepelumab as a Therapeutic Alternative in Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis Suboptimally Controlled by Omalizumab.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA) is a hypersensitivity-mediated respiratory disorder complicating severe asthma, where management frequently requires prolonged systemic corticosteroid (SCS) administration. Although anti-IgE blockade with omalizumab is widely utilized as an SCS-sparing biologic, a subset of patients achieves only partial disease control. We present a clinical perspective and case observation of a 52-year-old female with stage III ABPA and persistent SCS dependence who exhibited a suboptimal response over a 5-year course of omalizumab. Following a therapeutic switch to tezepelumab (210 mg subcutaneously every 4 weeks)-a human monoclonal antibody targeting thymic stromal lymphopoietin (TSLP, an upstream epithelial alarmin)-the patient achieved complete clinical, functional, and structural remission within 12 months. Treatment efficacy was objectively confirmed using the EXACTO (10/10 points) and FEOS (100/100 points) validated severe asthma biologic response scales, alongside total SCS withdrawal and resolution of bronchial mucus impaction. Intercepting the type 2 (T2) inflammatory cascade at its origin via anti-TSLP therapy represents a highly compelling strategy for refractory ABPA phenotypes failing downstream targeted biologics.

articles.title: Predicting Outcomes in Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage Using Clinical and Computed Tomography Markers: A Prospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) represents a disproportionately high stroke burden (20%-30%) in low- and middle-income countries like India, necessitating accurate, early risk stratification using readily available clinical and radiographic features.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective observational study included 185 patients with spontaneous ICH at a tertiary care center. Baseline clinical severity was assessed using the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) and the ICH score. Radiographic markers included hematoma volume, intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH), and radiographic signs (swirl, blend, black hole, satellite, and spot signs). The primary outcome was unfavorable functional status (modified Rankin scale: 4-6, including mortality) at 90 days. Univariate analyses focused on identifying predictors associated with a poor outcome, followed by multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: The mean age was 56.0 ± 12.4 years, with 72.4% prevalence of hypertension. The unfavorable outcome rate was 37.3% (N = 69), with 22.2% mortality. Univariate analysis (P < 0.05) revealed strong associations between poor outcome and greater hematoma volume, lower GCS score, higher ICH score, IVH, swirl sign, blend sign, satellite sign, hydrocephalus, herniation, and ≥2 multiple noncontrast computed tomography (NCCT) signs. Multivariable analysis identified hematoma volume, GCS score, ICH score, herniation, satellite sign, and male gender as independent predictors.

CONCLUSION: Clinical severity indicators and multiple NCCT signs in univariate analysis serve as robust markers of poor functional outcome. The independent prognostic value of the satellite sign and herniation highlights the utility of readily available radiographic features for immediate risk stratification.

articles.title: Motor Response Variability Reflects Recovery Potential After Stroke: A Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke recovery is highly heterogeneous, and predictive neurophysiological markers of motor outcome are still needed. Although transcranial magnetic stimulation-derived motor evoked potentials (MEPs) are widely used to assess corticospinal integrity, their trial-to-trial variability remains poorly explored and has largely been interpreted as noise rather than a source of clinically relevant information.

METHODS: In this prospective longitudinal observational study, we investigated MEP peak-to-peak amplitude and amplitude variability in 77 patients with subacute stroke assessed at baseline (T0, early subacute phase) and after a 2-month high-intensity daily rehabilitation program (T1), alongside 10 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. MEPs were recorded from both hemispheres at rest. Clinical outcomes were evaluated using the Fugl-Meyer Upper Extremity scale and a Motor Recovery Index.

RESULTS: Seventy-seven patients with subacute stroke (mean age, 68.5±12.7 years; 41.6% women) and 10 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (mean age, 73.9±4.3 years; 40.0% women) were included. At T0, MEP amplitude was lower in the affected than in the unaffected hemisphere (0.16±0.02 versus 0.38±0.01 mV; P=5.42×10-10), as was MEP variance (0.013±0.002 versus 0.038±0.003 mV2; P=8.43×10-12). Regarding T1, MEP amplitude increased over time in the affected hemisphere (0.21±0.02 mV; P=0.01), whereas MEP variance remained unchanged (P=0.55). Importantly, baseline MEP amplitude was strongly associated with motor status at follow-up (Fugl-Meyer Upper Extremity scale at T1; P=9.52×10-9), but not with the degree of recovery. In contrast, baseline MEP variability was significantly associated with both motor outcome (Fugl-Meyer Upper Extremity scale at T1; P=2.76×10-7) and the Motor Recovery Index (P=0.009), indicating a specific link with recovery potential.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings reveal a dissociation between MEP amplitude and variability, suggesting that they capture complementary aspects of corticospinal function. Although amplitude reflects the current functional state of motor pathways, variability appears to index network flexibility and adaptive capacity. MEP variability may, therefore, represent a novel neurophysiological biomarker for predicting motor recovery and guiding personalized rehabilitation strategies after stroke.

articles.title: Targeting ALDOA Lactylation Reverses Vascular Remodeling in Pulmonary Hypertension by Disrupting Actin Polymerization and YAP Activation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maladaptive vascular remodeling is a hallmark of pulmonary hypertension (PH), and therapeutic strategies directly targeting the pathological activity of smooth muscle cells remain limited. Metabolic and epigenetic dysregulation are established drivers of PH, and lysine lactylation has emerged as a novel posttranslational modification implicated in diverse diseases; however, its direct contribution to PH progression remains undefined.

METHODS: Integrated lactylomic and proteomic profiling was performed in hypoxic human pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells. The functional role of ALDOA (aldolase A) lactylation at lysine 42 (K42) was assessed using site-specific mutant virus and smooth muscle cell-specific inducible ALDOA knockout mice in 2 established PH models: SU5416+hypoxia in mice and monocrotaline in rats.

RESULTS: We identified ALDOA as a prominent lactylation target in hypoxic pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells, with K42 lactylation consistently elevated in primary pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells derived from PH rodent models and human PH tissues. Mechanistically, AARS1 (alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1)-mediated ALDOA K42 lactylation enhanced its binding to γ-actin, independent of glycolytic activity. This lactylation-enhanced interaction promoted F-actin polymerization and activated YAP (Yes-associated protein) signaling via LATS1 (large tumor suppressor kinase 1) inhibition, thereby driving pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cell proliferation and phenotypic switching. Moreover, YAP/TEAD4 (TEA domain transcription factor 4)-mediated transcriptional upregulation of AARS1 established a positive feedback loop reinforcing ALDOA K42 lactylation under hypoxia. In vivo, ALDOA inducible knockout or reconstitution with the lactylation-deficient K42R (lysine 42 mutant to arginine) mutant attenuated experimental PH progression, with suppressed F-actin/YAP activation and reduced vascular remodeling. Furthermore, competitive inhibition of lactylation through β‑alanine reduced ALDOA K42 lactylation and ameliorated vascular remodeling in ALDOA-overexpressing rodent PH models. Translationally, pharmacological disruption of the ALDOA/γ-actin interaction by raltegravir suppressed cytoskeletal reorganization and YAP signaling, mitigating PH progression in both mouse and rat models.

CONCLUSIONS: AARS1-mediated ALDOA K42 lactylation drives pulmonary vascular remodeling through a mechanism independent of ALDOA's catalytic activity, promoting F-actin polymerization and YAP activation. Precision targeting of this modification selectively inhibits pathological signaling while preserving metabolic homeostasis, highlighting a translational potential for precision intervention in PH.

articles.title: Investigating the Distinctive Clinical and Genetic Landscape of PPA2 Deficiency.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: PPA2 encodes for inorganic pyrophosphatase 2, a mitochondrial enzyme that hydrolyzes inorganic pyrophosphates into orthophosphate. Biallelic loss-of-function variants cause PPA2 deficiency, an emerging recessive cardiac condition that causes heart failure and sudden cardiac death in infants and young people.

METHODS: Using published case reports and large-scale genomics resources, we defined the clinical and molecular spectrum of this disease, classified variants using a customized American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics pipeline, assessed genotype-phenotype correlations, calculated predicted prevalence using the gnomAD GenIE tool, and investigated monoallelic associations in the UK Biobank.

RESULTS: A total of 63 cases from 37 families were identified from 12 publications. The natural history of this disease is characterized by clinical heterogeneity and high mortality (79% by 20 years of age), typically presenting as a highly arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy with 2 distinct risk periods: in infancy, where viral infections can lead to heart failure, and in adolescence, where minimal alcohol exposure can trigger sudden cardiac death. The disease is genetically heterogeneous, with 29 distinct variants described (18 of which were classified as [likely] pathogenic), usually in compound heterozygosity. As complete gene knockout appears to be incompatible with life, PPA2 deficiency is caused by biallelic variants within a particular loss-of-function window, with deficiency mitigated by hypomorphic effects, variants in nonconstitutive exons, and particular compound heterozygous combinations. The spectrum of phenotypic effect extends to monoallelic carriers of pathogenic variants, which demonstrate an apparent mitohormesis-like compensatory protection from heart failure. The disease has an estimated prevalence of at least 1/135 000 in European ancestry populations.

CONCLUSIONS: PPA2 deficiency is a genetically complex and clinically severe disease. Given the potential for effective life-saving interventions, PPA2 may warrant inclusion in emerging newborn genomic screening programs.

articles.title: Ocular Abnormalities in Multi-transfused Patients with Beta-thalassemia: A Cross-sectional Study from South India.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate ocular findings in transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia patients and determine whether they exhibit a higher incidence of ocular abnormalities compared to healthy controls owing to effects of iron overload and chelation therapy.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted in the Departments of Ophthalmology and Pediatrics at a tertiary care center in South India. Patients aged 10-18 years with transfusion-dependent thalassemia, receiving regular blood transfusions (every 2-4 weeks for at least 2 years), were included as cases. Age- and sex-matched healthy individuals without ocular complaints served as controls. All participants underwent a comprehensive ophthalmic evaluation, including visual acuity, color vision, slit-lamp examination, dilated fundus examination, dry eye testing (tear film breakup time [TBUT] and Schirmer's), and intraocular pressure measurement. Clinical history, annual transfusion requirement, and mean serum ferritin levels were recorded for cases. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics for Windows, version 25.0 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA) with appropriate parametric or nonparametric tests, and P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: Of the thalassemia patients, 65.1% were male. Retinal vascular tortuosity was observed in 14% (P = 0.026) and was significantly associated with higher serum ferritin (P = 0.004). Retinal pigment epithelium changes (9.3%) and increased cup-to-disc ratio (11.6%) showed nonsignificant trends. Tear film instability (TBUT <10 s) was present in 20.9% (P = 0.649), while Schirmer's test indicated dry eye in 18.6% (P = 0.044), both associated with elevated ferritin. Refractive errors were significantly more frequent in the case group (18.6%, P = 0.005). Lenticular opacities and Bitot's spots were found in 4.7% and 2.3%, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Ocular abnormalities are common among beta-thalassemia major patients, with some correlating with serum ferritin levels. Regular ophthalmic screening should be integrated into multidisciplinary care to facilitate early detection and management. Larger longitudinal studies are warranted to assess the progression and visual impact of these changes.

articles.title: Comparison of Clinical Characteristics Between Patients With HCM With Nontruncating Versus Truncating Variants in MYBPC3.
Preprocedural Curvature Assessment Can Stratify Recanalization Risk Before Device Selection in Mechanical Thrombectomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vascular geometry may impede catheter navigation during mechanical thrombectomy. We evaluated whether cervical curvature predicts recanalization success.

METHODS: This is a retrospective single-center cohort of 160 anterior large vessel occlusion patients treated with mechanical thrombectomy at a comprehensive stroke center (Barnes-Jewish Hospital/Washington University School of Medicine, St. Louis, MO) from May 2019 to February 2021. Cervical curvature was computed using 3-dimensional vessel centerlines derived from preprocedural computed tomography angiography. Primary outcomes were successful recanalization (final modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score ≥2b) and intracranial access time (puncture→first pass). Associations were evaluated with multivariable linear or logistic regression, adjusting for age, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale, first-line device, and access route. Random Forest and Gradient Boosting models with Gini Importance and Shapley Additive Explanation explained feature importance.

RESULTS: Mean age was 67±15 years; median National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale 16; mean total curvature was 9.80±2.85. Median intracranial access time was 24 minutes (interquartile range, 17-32), with no correlation to cervical curvature (ρ=0.054; adjusted β=0.20 min/unit [95% CI, -0.75, 1.15]; P=0.676). Successful recanalization occurred in 86% and varied across curvature tertiles (low 91%, mid 93%, high 75%; P=0.017). Per-unit curvature increase was associated with recanalization failure (adjusted odds ratio, 1.21 [95% CI, 1.02-1.43]; P=0.028). Receiver operating characteristic-derived curvature threshold (>11.54) identified a high-risk group (adjusted odds ratio, 5.10 [95% CI, 1.88-13.84]; P=0.001). Machine learning confirmed cervical curvature as the dominant predictor, with a Shapley Additive Explanation peak effect at 11.65.

CONCLUSIONS: Cervical curvature independently predicts mechanical thrombectomy recanalization failure, with a threshold effect near 11.6 units. Preprocedural curvature assessment derived from routine computed tomography angiography may improve risk stratification and inform mechanical thrombectomy strategy.

articles.title: CD36 Gates Nocturnal Hypertension via the Renal AMPK/HDAC5/PER1 Axis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nocturnal hypertension is a strong predictor of cardio-cerebrovascular disease, yet its underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. In this study, we identified CD36 as a key regulator of blood pressure (BP) rhythms and as a gatekeeper of nocturnal hypertension. Its deficiency disrupts circadian BP rhythms.

METHODS: We continuously monitored 48-hour BP using telemetry in CD36 global knockout mice and renal proximal tubule-specific CD36 knockout mice. We also collected serum samples and ambulatory BP monitoring data from patients with nocturnal hypertension to assess the relationship between CD36 expression and nocturnal hypertension. A comprehensive screening of various factors affecting BP and circadian rhythms was conducted to explore the molecular mechanisms.

RESULTS: Our telemetry data revealed significantly elevated BP during the daytime (inactive period) in both CD36 global knockout and renal proximal tubule-specific knockout mice compared with their control counterparts. Furthermore, levels of platelet CD36 were negatively correlated with the severity of nocturnal hypertension in humans. Mechanistically, CD36 modulates BP rhythms through the AMPK (AMP-activated protein kinase)/HDAC5 (histone deacetylase 5)/PER1 pathway: its deficiency activates phosphorylated AMPK, leading to the dissociation of the HDAC5-PER1 complex, enhancing PER1 nuclear accumulation, and desynchronizing the oscillations of intrarenal renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system genes and clock-controlled genes, ultimately disrupting BP rhythm.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight CD36 as a critical integrator that links renal clocks to BP homeostasis, establishing it as a potential predictor and therapeutic target for nocturnal hypertension.

articles.title: Beyond the 2026 ESC Heart Failure Guidelines: Heart Stress, Biological Aging, and Heart Failure Prevention.
Long-Term Impact of Vutrisiran in Patients With TTR Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy: 1-Year Efficacy and Safety Outcomes From the HELIOS-B Open-Label Extension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In HELIOS-B (A Study to Evaluate Vutrisiran in Patients With Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy), vutrisiran reduced the risk of all-cause mortality (ACM) and recurrent cardiovascular events and slowed disease progression measures versus placebo in patients with TTR (transthyretin) amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy after 33 to 36 months. We report the long-term efficacy and safety of vutrisiran from an ongoing open-label extension of HELIOS-B.

METHODS: Patients who completed HELIOS-B could enroll in the open-label extension, continuing with vutrisiran 25 mg every 3 months (continuous vutrisiran) or, if previously receiving placebo, initiating vutrisiran 25 mg every 3 months (placebo/vutrisiran). Prespecified end points assessed in the open-label extension are the composite of ACM and cardiovascular events, ACM, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary score, New York Heart Association class, and NT-proBNP (N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide) and troponin I levels. Outcomes were assessed through month 48 in this analysis.

RESULTS: Of 654 participants in HELIOS-B (vutrisiran, n=326; placebo, n=328), 478 completed double-blind treatment and 466 (vutrisiran, n=243; placebo, n=223) entered the open-label extension. In the continuous vutrisiran group, the risk of first cardiovascular event or ACM was reduced by 37% (hazard ratio, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.51, 0.79]; P=0.0001) and ACM by 37% (hazard ratio, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.46, 0.84]; P=0.0023) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Through month 48, patients in the continuous vutrisiran group had preserved health status and quality of life per Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary score (least squares mean difference, 9.0 [95% CI, 5.3, 12.6]; P<0.0001) and more patients had improved or stable New York Heart Association class (odds ratio, 1.6 [95% CI, 1.1, 2.2]; P=0.0084) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Benefits in the continuous vutrisiran group were maintained for NT-proBNP and troponin I levels (adjusted geometric mean fold change ratios, 0.66 [95% CI, 0.58, 0.74]; P<0.0001; and 0.71 [95% CI, 0.64, 0.79]; P<0.0001, respectively) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Similar benefits were observed in the vutrisiran monotherapy population. No new safety signals were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: Long-term vutrisiran resulted in clinically meaningful benefits across mortality, cardiovascular events, cardiac biomarkers, functional status, and quality of life in patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy through month 48. Patients initially treated with vutrisiran had better outcomes than those first receiving placebo, highlighting the importance of early diagnosis and treatment in TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy.

articles.title: Epidemiological Characteristics and Clinical Outcomes of Vaccine-associated Urticaria: A Retrospective Cross-sectional Analysis of the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System Database (1990-2025).
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Urticaria is a commonly reported cutaneous adverse event following vaccination, which may range from mild self-limiting reactions to more severe hypersensitivity manifestations. Monitoring vaccine-associated urticaria is important for ongoing vaccine safety surveillance and pharmacovigilance. However, large-scale population-based analyses evaluating demographic characteristics, vaccine associations, onset intervals, and severity patterns remain limited.

AIM: The aim of the study was to analyze reports of urticaria in the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) database between 1990 and 2025 and evaluate demographic characteristics, vaccine type distribution, onset intervals, temporal trends, and seriousness patterns.

METHODOLOGY: A retrospective observational study was conducted using data from the VAERS database. Reports of urticaria submitted between January 1990 and March 2025 were included. The variables analyzed included age, sex, vaccine type, onset interval, and seriousness classification. Descriptive statistics were generated using frequencies and percentages, and comparative analyses were performed between serious and nonserious reports.

RESULTS: A total of 61,996 urticaria reports were identified during the study period. Most reports occurred among adults aged 18-49 years and females. Most reports were classified as nonserious and occurred within the early postvaccination period. COVID-19 vaccines accounted for the highest proportion of reports, followed by influenza and measles, mumps, and rubella vaccines. Temporal analysis demonstrated a marked increase in reporting during 2021, followed by declining trends thereafter. Comparative analysis identified differences in demographic and clinical characteristics between serious and nonserious reports.

CONCLUSION: Urticaria is a frequently reported adverse event following vaccination, with identifiable demographic, temporal, and clinical patterns. Most reports were nonserious and occurred shortly after vaccination, although differences were observed between serious and nonserious reports. Continued pharmacovigilance and future studies incorporating detailed clinical data are needed to better understand factors associated with vaccine-related urticaria.

articles.title: Cross-Ancestry Portability of a Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Polygenic Score in a Diverse US Cohort.
The triglyceride-glucose index in decompensated heart failure: A marker of insulin resistance or reverse lipid epidemiology? Insights from the HEROES registry.
Drug acquisition accounts for a minor share of the costs associated with dobutamine-milrinone escalation in cardiogenic shock: a propensity-weighted cost analysis from Indonesia.
articles.journal: Expert review of pharmacoeconomics & outcomes research
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adding milrinone to dobutamine (dobutamine-milrinone escalation) in cardiogenic shock (CS) is reimbursed for a limited duration under Indonesia's national health insurance, but the cost structure of escalation remains poorly characterized. This study quantified direct medical charges associated with escalation and the contribution of drug acquisition.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Retrospective cohort of 76 adult CS survivors (20 escalation, 56 dobutamine monotherapy) at Indonesia's national cardiovascular referral center, 2020-2024. Covariate Balancing Propensity Score-based inverse probability of treatment weighting, using pre-treatment covariates, estimated adjusted cost ratios (CR) for intensive cardiovascular care unit (ICVCU) and total hospital costs from institutional billing records.

RESULTS: Escalation was associated with higher ICVCU costs (CR 2.711; 95% CI 1.912-3.844; p < 0.001) and total hospital costs (CR 2.321; 95% CI 1.372-3.929; p = 0.002). Combined inotrope costs represented 4.3% of ICVCU expenditure in the escalation group, compared with 30.9% for therapeutic and interventional procedures. Baseline vasoactive-inotropic score correlated with total hospital cost (ρ=0.597; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Drug acquisition represented a minor share of costs associated with dobutamine-milrinone escalation. The findings support consideration of severity- and resource-based approaches to reimbursement rather than focusing solely on duration limits for individual inotropes. Interpretation is limited by the retrospective, single-center, survivor-only design.

articles.title: Precision psychiatry: thinking beyond simple prediction models, without dismissing them.
articles.journal: The British journal of psychiatry : the journal of mental science

articles.title: Management of dialysis catheter-related thrombus.
articles.journal: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The goal of this review is to provide a comprehensive update on the clinical manifestations and medical management of intraluminal hemodialysis catheter thrombosis and central vein stenosis and thrombosis related to hemodialysis catheters.

RECENT FINDINGS: The two thrombolytic agents used most frequently to treat dialysis catheter dysfunction, alteplase and urokinase, have a similar immediate efficacy of about 80%. A 2 mg per lumen dose of alteplase is superior to a 1 mg per lumen dose, and a 30-min instillation is as effective as a longer instillation time. Restoration of catheter function after instillation of a thrombolytic agents is often short-lived. Catheters with intra-luminal thrombosis frequently require repetitive thrombolytic instillation, and many patients ultimately require catheter exchange when instillation of a thrombolytic agent is no longer effective. Central vein stenosis and thrombosis are seen in about 25% of patients with a hemodialysis catheter. They are often recurrent, and the role of anticoagulation is uncertain.

SUMMARY: Clinicians should recognize the clinical manifestations and medical management of hemodialysis catheter-related thrombosis and its management. We need more research to better understand whether anticoagulation is indicated in central vein thrombosis.

articles.title: Forgotten electrolytes: magnesium and calcium flux during dialysis.
articles.journal: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Calcium and magnesium remain incompletely individualized in contemporary dialysis prescriptions despite growing evidence linking their concentrations to cardiovascular outcomes, vascular calcification, mineral metabolism, and mortality. The 2025 Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Controversies Conference report on chronic kidney disease (CKD)-mineral and bone disorder (MBD) and recent kinetic studies of intradialytic ion fluxes make a focused review of these "forgotten" divalent cations timely.

RECENT FINDINGS: Intradialytic calcium mass transfer is influenced by patient- and prescription-level factors, and total serum calcium incompletely reflects biologically relevant calcium flux; ionized calcium may decline during dialysis as hemoconcentration increases albumin concentration and alkalosis increases albumin-bound calcium. Small randomized trials show that raising dialysate magnesium improves serum resistance to calcification, but whether higher dialysate magnesium improves clinical outcomes remains unknown. The 2025 KDIGO report retains the 1.25-1.50 mmol/l dialysate calcium range and identifies individualized calcium mass-transfer assessment as a research priority. Dial-Mag, a large pragmatic trial comparing higher versus conventional dialysate magnesium concentrations, is ongoing.

SUMMARY: Recent evidence challenges the assumption that standardized dialysate calcium and magnesium prescriptions are optimal for all patients. Future studies should define patient-specific targets, validate practical methods to assess peridialytic calcium and magnesium levels and intradialytic flux, and determine whether individualized dialysate prescriptions improve clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Preliminary Psychometric Evaluation of the Korean Version of the Dementia Apraxia Test.
articles.abstract: Apraxia is a clinically significant but under-assessed deficit in dementia, yet existing Korean apraxia tools were developed for stroke and do not capture its neurodegenerative features. To address this gap, the Dementia Apraxia Test (DATE) was translated and culturally adapted into Korean (K-DATE), whose preliminary psychometric properties were examined. A total of 106 older adults (55 with dementia and 51 cognitively healthy) were assessed. The K-DATE discriminated between groups (44.55 vs. 52.18; p < .001) and correlated with the Korean Apraxia Screen of TULIA (ρ = .400). Internal consistency was acceptable (Cronbach's α = .799), and test-retest (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] = .819) and inter-rater reliability (ICC = .863) were good. Receiver operating characteristic analysis yielded an area under the curve of .749, with an optimal cut-off of 53.50 (sensitivity = .855, specificity = .510). These findings suggest the K-DATE is a promising apraxia screening tool if supported by further validation.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Guided Corticosteroid Block Versus Alcohol Neurolysis of the Suprascapular Nerve for Chronic Hemiplegic Shoulder Pain: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study.
articles.journal: American journal of physical medicine & rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the clinical effectiveness of corticosteroid block versus alcohol neurolysis of the suprascapular nerve (SSN) in patients with chronic post-stroke hemiplegic shoulder pain (HSP).

DESIGN: This prospective service evaluation, reported per STROBE guidelines, enrolled 26 consecutive patients with chronic post-stroke HSP (>3 mo) receiving ultrasound-guided SSNB with triamcinolone acetonide 40 mg/lidocaine (corticosteroid, n=13) or 70% ethanol/lidocaine (alcohol neurolysis, n=13) as part of routine clinical care. Pain (Numeric Rating Scale, 0-10) and shoulder range of motion (Constant-Murley ROM) were assessed at baseline, weekly for six weeks, and six months.

RESULTS: Both groups showed significant within-group improvements in all pain domains and ROM at one and six weeks. At six months, resting and movement pain remained improved in both groups. Nocturnal pain and ROM improvements persisted in the alcohol neurolysis group (P=0.005; P=0.004) but not the corticosteroid group (P=0.162; P=0.058). No between-group differences were observed (all P>0.05; effect sizes r=0.03-0.31). Both interventions were well tolerated, with transient post-procedural pain exacerbation reported in two alcohol-treated patients.

CONCLUSIONS: Both interventions produced significant improvements in pain and ROM with no between-group differences. The six-month pattern suggests more durable benefit following alcohol neurolysis; however, dequately powered randomized controlled trials are required.

articles.title: Effect of Diaphragmatic Neuromuscular Electrical Stimulation on Diaphragm Function and Clinical Outcomes in ICU Mechanically Ventilated Patients: A Meta-analysis and Systematic Review.
articles.journal: American journal of physical medicine & rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effects of diaphragmatic neuromuscular electrical stimulation (DNMES) on diaphragmatic function and clinical outcomes in mechanically ventilated patients in the intensive care unit (ICU).

METHODS: We searched major databases to May 2026 for RCTs. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, assessed bias, and performed meta-analysis; GRADE assessed evidence certainty.

RESULTS: Nineteen RCTs (1,437 patients) were included. Meta-analysis showed that DNMES significantly improved diaphragmatic thickening fraction (DTF) (SMD=1.32, 95%CI[0.73, 1.91], P<0.0001), diaphragmatic excursion (DE) (SMD=1.25, 95%CI[0.77, 1.72], P<0.00001), maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP) (MD=2.46, 95%CI[1.22, 3.69], P<0.0001), and rapid shallow breathing index (RSBI) (MD=-14.08, 95%CI[-21.38, -6.77], P=0.0002). DNMES also reduced the duration of mechanical ventilation (MD=-2.14, 95%CI[-2.84, -1.43], P<0.00001) and ICU length of stay (MD=-2.30, 95%CI[-2.85, -1.75], P<0.00001), increased weaning success rate (RR=1.29, 95%CI[1.17, 1.42], P<0.00001), and decreased weaning failure rate (RR=0.62, 95%CI[0.49, 0.77], P<0.0001). GRADE evidence quality assessment revealed moderate quality for 2 outcomes, low quality for 3 outcomes, and very low quality for 3 outcomes.

CONCLUSION: DNMES may improve diaphragmatic function and weaning outcomes, shorten ventilation and ICU stay, but the certainty of evidence remains predominantly low to very low due to substantial heterogeneity, high risk of bias, and limited trial reporting; large RCTs are needed.

articles.title: The Network Psychometric Properties of the Temporomandibular Joint Disorder Questionnaire Among Australian Adults.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Australian adults have at least one symptom of temporomandibular joint disorder (TMD), and those who experience TMD report lower oral health-related quality of life. While a self-administered TMD questionnaire can be a valuable screening instrument for initial identification of disease/conditions, to the best of our knowledge, there are no comprehensively validated TMD questionnaires for the Australian population.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the psychometric properties of the TMD questionnaire using data imputation and novel network models.

METHODS: This is a secondary analysis of data from the National Study of Adult Oral Health 2017-18. The sample included 2423 participants who responded to the 12-item TMD questionnaire. Descriptive statistics included demographic characteristics and the TMD distribution of adult Australians. The analytical steps include: (1) model estimation, (2) Unique Variable Analysis, (3) Exploratory Graph Analysis (EGA), (4) model fit, (5) criterion validity and (6) reliability.

RESULTS: After removing poorly performing items, EGA revealed that a 9-item TMD questionnaire had excellent item stability, substantive network loadings and mixed but acceptable model fit (X2(12): 1045.91, CFI: 0.970, RMSEA: 0.077, 90% CI: 0.073-0.081, SRMR: 0.027). The reliability was good (α = 0.8; Ω = 0.8). Finding also supported known-groups validity by sex (Risk Ratios ranging from 1.44 to 4.43) and criterion validity according to quality of life (r = -0.26) and age (r = -0.21).

CONCLUSIONS: This study provided evidence on the validity and reliability of the 9-item temporomandibular joint questionnaire for evaluating temporomandibular joint disorder among Australian Adults. The TMD questionnaire is readily available, which can be a practical measure of self-reported TMD symptoms for a population-based initial assessment or epidemiological research.

articles.title: Clinical Effects of Botulinum Toxin Type A Combined With Extracorporeal Shockwave Therapy on Plantar Flexor Spasticity in Cerebral Palsy.
articles.journal: American journal of physical medicine & rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare Botulinum Toxin Type A (BoNT-A) alone versus BoNT-A combined with extracorporeal shockwave therapy (ESWT) on spasticity, functional mobility, pain, and range of motion in children with spastic cerebral palsy (CP).

DESIGN: Single-blind randomized controlled trial of 20 children with spastic CP. All participants received BoNT-A injections into the ankle plantar flexors; the combination group additionally received three weekly ESWT sessions. Spasticity (MAS, MTS), functional mobility (MTUG), pain (FPS-R), and passive ankle dorsiflexion range of motion (PROM) were assessed at baseline and follow-up.

RESULTS: At 12 weeks, the primary endpoint (MAS* of the plantar flexor muscle with the highest baseline MAS score) was numerically lower with BoNT-A plus ESWT than with BoNT-A alone, although the between-group difference was not statistically significant. Between-group differences in MTS, MTUG, FPS-R, and PROM were also nonsignificant. Sustained within-group improvements in spasticity, functional mobility, and pain were observed with combined treatment, although these findings did not establish superiority.

CONCLUSION: Combined BoNT-A and ESWT was associated with sustained improvements in several clinical outcomes; however, superiority over BoNT-A alone was not demonstrated for the primary endpoint. Larger trials are warranted to investigate the potential additional benefits of ESWT.

articles.title: Uncovering cardiac molecular remodelling in racing Thoroughbreds with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common arrhythmia in both humans and horses, with a comparable prevalence of ~2%. In horses, AF is a major cause of poor athletic performance and linked to sudden cardiac death, yet its underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate transcriptomic remodelling associated with spontaneous paroxysmal AF (PAF).

STUDY DESIGN: Case-control study.

METHODS: We performed RNA sequencing on left atrial (LA) tissue from three Thoroughbred racehorses with PAF and four matched controls. All horses were euthanised due to musculoskeletal reasons. Cell type deconvolution was performed with BayesPrism. The differential expression analysis was performed with EdgeR. Alternative splicing analysis was performed with SUPPA2.

RESULTS: Cell-type deconvolution revealed a modest, non-significant shift towards increased fibroblast and immune cell proportions in PAF, but not enough to account for widespread transcriptional changes. 1400 of the 12,012 included genes were considered significantly differentially expressed (Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value <0.05). These genes included ion channels, calcium-handling proteins, and conduction-related genes. In addition, several genes directly involved in cardiac muscle contraction and mitochondrial energy metabolism were differentially expressed. Alternative splicing analysis revealed over 20 significantly altered events, including skipped exons in genes with potential relevance to cardiac function and remodelling.

MAIN LIMITATIONS: The number of biological replicates was modest.

CONCLUSIONS: Overall, despite no major changes in cell composition, the findings highlight intrinsic structural and molecular changes in the LA of PAF-affected horses. This study provides the first transcriptomic and splicing analysis of atrial tissue in racehorses with PAF, revealing molecular remodelling consistent with mechanisms of arrhythmia maintenance and suggesting potential targets for further functional investigation.

articles.title: A retrospective evaluation of responsiveness to platelets in plasma and pathogen-reduced platelets in platelet additive solution at a single institution.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Studies suggest that recipients of pathogen reduced (PR) platelets in platelet additive solution (PAS) experience inferior increments when compared to platelets in plasma (PS); however, few real-world studies have confirmed these observations. In this single-center study, we evaluated responses to PS and PAS/PR platelets in platelet-refractory, predominantly hematology/oncology patients.

STUDY DESIGN/METHODS: Two analyses were performed. First, 1-h CCIs from recipients of all available PS and PAS/PR units within the same hospitalization were compared using mixed effects modeling. Clinical factors potentially contributing to refractoriness were also recorded. Second, total platelet utilization per allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) encounter prior to and following platelet inventory transition to exclusively PAS/PR platelets were compared using negative binomial regression.

RESULTS: Forty-one subjects met inclusion criteria. Most subjects (95%) were diagnosed with platelet refractoriness, and 44% had detectable HLA allosensitization. Post-transfusion CCIs with single-donor PS platelets were significantly greater than that with single-donor or HLA-selected/crossmatched PAS/PR platelets (6598 vs. 2177 and 3091, p < .001). No transfusion reactions with PS platelets were reported. The median total platelet transfusions per HSCT encounter increased over two-fold following transition to PAS/PR platelet inventory (IRR 2.29, 95% CI 1.75-2.99). No differences in mean platelet engraftment times were noted over this period.

DISCUSSION: Our findings suggest that the transition to predominantly PAS/PR platelet units may have contributed to clinical platelet refractoriness and increased platelet utilization in a selected cohort of hematology/oncology patients. These findings may have wider implications for platelet inventory management in tertiary healthcare systems.

articles.title: Core-Shell Microneedles for Sequential Delivery of Antibacterial, Antioxidant, and Anti-Inflammatory Agents in Infected Wound Healing.
articles.abstract: Infected wounds are dynamic pathological processes that progress through acute, chronic, and repair phases, each with distinct therapeutic requirements. Conventional treatments, which release all drugs simultaneously, often fail to meet these stage-specific needs. In this study, we develop a multifunctional core-shell microneedle (MN) system capable of sequential delivery of different therapeutics to address the requirements of various healing stages. During the acute phase, the shell composed of gelatin-hydroxyphenylalanine (Gtn-HPA) hydrogel rapidly releases bacitracin (Bac), thereby inhibiting bacterial proliferation. During the chronic phase, MMP9-responsive peptide nanoparticles (INM-1@EDA) within the MN core undergo enzymatic cleavage, releasing the edaravone (EDA) and indomethacin (INM) moieties to exert antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, respectively. During the repair phase, the residual gelatin at the site supports keratinocyte proliferation and migration, promoting skin tissue regeneration. In a mouse wound model with Staphylococcus aureus infection, core-shell MN treatment achieves nearly complete wound closure in 12 days (96.7 ± 1.3%) with markedly reduced bacterial burden and decreased inflammatory cytokine levels. This MN system achieves sequential release of antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant therapeutics based on wound microenvironments, offering new strategies for efficacious treatment of infected wounds.

articles.title: Breaking the Vicious Cycle for Diabetic Wound Healing: A Dynamic-Static Dual-Mode Nanofiber Platform for NETs Degradation, Inflammation Resolution, and Scar Prevention.
articles.abstract: Chronic diabetic wounds are trapped in a self-perpetuating vicious cycle-persistent infection, oxidative stress, and NET-driven inflammation-that severely impairs healing. Here, we engineer a piezoelectric nanofiber membrane (DMTP) that breaks this cycle via a dynamic-static dual-mode strategy. DMTP integrates a Mn-Ti bimetallic MOF with sustained DNase I release, enabling four coordinated functions: (i) piezodynamic ROS generation for on-demand antibacterial action; (ii) an electric field to guide fibroblast migration; (iii) sustained DNase I release to degrade pathological NETs; and (iv) intrinsic POD/SOD enzyme-mimetic activity for continuous ROS scavenging. Mechanistically, we show that NETs drive fibroblast differentiation into α-SMA+ myofibroblasts, a key fibrotic driver, and DMTP effectively suppresses this pro-fibrotic process. In diabetic mice, DMTP achieves 94.32% wound closure with orderly collagen deposition and modulated inflammation (TNF-α↓, TGF-β↑). In a rabbit ear hypertrophic scar model, DMTP significantly reduces scar formation by inhibiting α-SMA expression. This work offers a transformative strategy to achieve diabetic wound healing with diminished scarring by directly dismantling the infection-oxidative stress-NETs-fibrosis axis.

articles.title: State of the art: thoracic ultrasound.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Thoracic ultrasound has continued to expand beyond simple bedside triage into a quantitative, procedure-guiding and increasingly artificial intelligence-augmented tool across pleural and respiratory medicine. This review summarizes the literature published over the past year, highlighting developments in effusion characterization, pneumothorax diagnosis, image-guided pleural procedures, artificial intelligence, training standards, critical care applications, malignant pleural effusion management, and diaphragm/interstitial lung disease assessment.

RECENT FINDINGS: Elastography and contrast-enhanced ultrasound have moved from exploratory to comparative and multicentre randomized evaluation for effusion characterization and biopsy guidance. Meta-analyses have reaffirmed the superiority of point-of-care ultrasound over chest radiography for both pneumothorax and thoracentesis guidance. Artificial intelligence tools have shown that they can close the acquisition-skill gap for novice operators, although automated interpretation (particularly B-line quantification) remains inconsistent against expert consensus. A new UK national training standard for pleural procedures has been published, alongside the first validated thoracic-specific competency assessment tool. A large multicentre randomized trial found that a point-of-care ultrasound-driven diagnostic pathway did not improve early discharge rates in emergency department patients with dyspnoea, an important negative finding. Diaphragm and quantitative lung ultrasound continue to accumulate evidence as noninvasive markers of interstitial lung disease severity and ventilator weaning readiness.

SUMMARY: The past year's literature confirms thoracic ultrasound's trajectory from a purely diagnostic adjunct towards a quantitative, procedure-integrated and artificial intelligence-supported modality, while also delivering important cautionary and negative findings that temper enthusiasm and clarify where evidence remains immature.

articles.title: Percutaneous coronary intervention or medical therapy alone before transcatheter aortic valve replacement: insights from a meta-analysis of randomized trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease frequently coexists in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), yet the benefit of routine percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) before TAVR remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of routine PCI before TAVR compared with conservative or deferred revascularization.

METHODS: We pooled randomized clinical trials comparing PCI before TAVR versus no/deferred PCI in patients with concomitant coronary artery disease. Random-effects models estimated pooled relative risks (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Bayesian sensitivity analyses and trial sequential analysis were performed.

RESULTS: Three trials included 1156 patients (PCI, n = 579; no/deferred PCI, n = 577). In comparator arms reporting postrandomization PCI/revascularization, 72 of 461 patients (15.6%) underwent subsequent PCI/revascularization. PCI did not significantly reduce major adverse cardiac events (RR: 0.91, 95% CI: 0.70-1.18; I2 = 36.9%), myocardial infarction (RR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.45-1.63; I2 = 49.8%), all-cause death (RR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.70-1.15; I2 = 0.0%), or stroke (RR: 0.70, 95% CI: 0.48-1.03; P = 0.069; I2 = 0.0%). In two trials, PCI reduced urgent revascularization (RR: 0.33, 95% CI: 0.13-0.87; I2 = 54.5%) but increased major bleeding (RR: 1.57, 95% CI: 1.07-2.32; I2 = 37.9%) and any bleeding (RR: 1.77, 95% CI: 1.27-2.47; I2 = 66.7%). Bayesian analyses were directionally concordant. Trial sequential analysis was inconclusive for all efficacy outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Routine PCI before TAVR reduced urgent revascularization but increased bleeding, without significant differences in other outcomes. Current evidence remains underpowered to rule out benefit for other ischemic outcomes; larger trials are needed.

articles.title: Crossing subfamily borders: Mechanosensitive TREK-1 and alkaline-activated TASK-4 form heterodimers with unique functional and pharmacological properties.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The tandem of two-pore-domain potassium (K2P) channels TREK-1 and TASK-4 are expressed in the heart and pancreatic beta-cells. As TREK-1 and TASK-4 belong to distinct subfamilies with different functional hallmarks, heteromerization of these two channels was highly unexpected. However, due to their shared expression in these tissues and their involvement in congenital cardiac arrhythmias, the aim of this study was to probe for a possible formation of TREK-1/TASK-4 heterodimers.

EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Two-electrode voltage-clamp and inside-out macropatch clamp recordings, together with immunohistochemistry and chemiluminescence-based ELISA assays, were utilized to describe heteromerization of TREK-1 and TASK-4 channels and elucidate the characteristics of this heteromeric channel complex.

KEY RESULTS: Here, we show that the mechanosensitive TREK-1 forms heteromeric channel complexes with the alkaline-activated TASK-4. The resulting heterodimers of these only remotely related channels have an enhanced temperature sensitivity, an altered pH dependence and regulation by extracellular sodium. Unlike TREK-1, heteromeric TREK-1/TASK-4 channels are not inhibited via Gs-coupled receptor activation, as the heterodimeric channels are not PKA sensitive. Strikingly, these novel heterodimeric channel complexes are characterized by a unique pharmacology.

CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: The newly described heterodimerization across different K2P channel families is of major relevance for drugs targeting TASK-4 or TREK-1. Their functional co-expression in different tissues raises the possibility of developing drugs against cardiac arrhythmias and Type 2 diabetes by specifically targeting these unique heterodimeric channel complexes.

articles.title: Magnetic resonance imaging proton density fat fraction and selected quantitative ultrasound methods for hepatic steatosis: histology-referenced diagnostic performance and longitudinal responsiveness-a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To synthesize histology-referenced diagnostic performance at study-selected thresholds and the longitudinal responsiveness of magnetic resonance imaging proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) and selected quantitative ultrasound methods in adults with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease/metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.

METHODS: Four databases were searched from database inception through July 1, 2026. Sensitivity, specificity, and odds ratios were pooled with 95% confidence intervals using heterogeneity-selected fixed- or random-effects models. Small-study effects were assessed using funnel plots and Begg tests; longitudinal changes were pooled when change-score standard deviations were reported.

RESULTS: In total, 44 articles were included: 34 contributed histology-referenced diagnostic data, and 11 were assessed for longitudinal responsiveness, with 1 article contributing to both. At steatosis grade (S) ≥ 1/S ≥ 2/S ≥3, MRI-PDFF sensitivity and specificity was 93.6%/81.5%/83.1% and 87.1%/86.7%/83.2%, respectively; the controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) was 86.8%/81.2%/86.4% and 98.9%/71.0%/64.6%, respectively. The attenuation coefficient/attenuation imaging sensitivity/specificity was 83.2%/98.1%, 86.4%/79.9%, and 99.3%/76.4%, respectively. Ultrasound-guided attenuation parameter and ultrasound-derived fat fraction evidence was limited. Three head-to-head longitudinal studies included 298 participants, of whom only 158 had analyzable change-score data; in these, pooled changes were -4.53 percentage points for MRI-PDFF and -12.71 dB/m for the CAP. Thirty-two of the 34 diagnostic studies were at high-risk of bias from cohort-selected thresholds. Begg tests did not detect significant small-study effects, although their power was very limited in analyses that included only 2 or 3 studies.

CONCLUSION: At study-selected thresholds, MRI-PDFF showed balanced sensitivity and specificity across steatosis grades, whereas quantitative ultrasound varied by method, platform, and threshold. These findings support comparative synthesis but do not establish validated cut-offs or superiority of either modality.

CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: Study-selected thresholds limit clinical translation. MRI-PDFF proton density fat fraction and quantitative ultrasound are complementary, with use depending on clinical purpose, platform, and precision needs.

articles.title: Integrative transcriptome meta-analysis distinguishes compatibility and incompatibility in rice-Xanthomonas interaction.
articles.abstract: Diseases caused by the Xanthomonas oryzae pathovars are important constraints for global rice productivity. Despite being a well-studied pathosystem, the transcriptional mechanisms distinguishing resistance from susceptibility remain incompletely understood. Here, we present a systems-level meta-analysis of more than a hundred publicly available rice-Xanthomonas transcriptome datasets. Using appropriate analysis pipelines, stringent filtering criteria and metadata integration, we identified rice functions that distinguish disease resistance and susceptibility with temporal resolution. Compatible interactions were characterized by early activation of abscisic-acid biosynthetic and signaling genes, and extensive transcriptional plasticity associated with susceptibility gene activation. In contrast, incompatible interactions displayed a restrained transcriptome reprogramming, enrichment of phenylpropanoid and aromatic-amino-acid biosynthetic pathways, and enrichment of an AP2/ERF-GCC-box regulatory module. Transient over-expression of three conserved infection-responsive genes, OsJAZ11, OsSYP131b, and OsMYB45, modestly enhanced defense gene expression and reduced lesion length caused by X. oryzae pv. oryzae in rice leaves, thus providing a proof-of-concept relevance of the candidates to rice-Xoo interaction. We also developed RiceXtra, an openly available database hosting the analyzed data (http://tdb.ccmb.res.in/RiceXtra), for exploring gene expression patterns during rice-Xanthomonas interactions. Overall, our study proposes a mechanistic framework connecting hormonal signalling and transcriptional plasticity with disease outcome, offering a foundation for engineering durable disease resistance.

articles.title: Is there any correlation between F-18 FDG PET-CT scan metabolic parameters and programmed death-ligand 1 expression in patients with metastatic non-small cell lung carcinoma?
articles.abstract:
AIM: The study aimed to evaluate whether there is any correlation between metabolic parameters derived from baseline fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose (F-18 FDG) PET-computed tomography (CT) and programmed death-ligand 1 (PDL-1) expression in patients with metastatic non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC).

METHODS: 33 biopsy-proven metastatic NSCLC patients were included. On immunohistochemistry, a tumor proportion score (TPS) of ≥1% was considered PDL-1 positive, while a TPS of <1% was considered negative. Metabolic parameters of the F-18 FDG PET-CT scan were obtained by drawing a region of interest around the index lung lesion. Data were analyzed using Shapiro-Wilk test of normality, unpaired t-tests/Mann-Whitney U test, Spearman's rank correlation, Youden's index, and receiver operator characteristic (ROC) analysis.

RESULTS: Spearman's correlation analysis demonstrated a moderate positive correlation (r = 0.466, P = 0.0063) between maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) and overall PDL-1 expression. Similarly, a moderate positive correlation was noted between SUVmax and tumors with positive PDL-1 expression (r = 0.643, P = 0.013), with mean SUVmax in PD-L1-positive tumors being significantly higher (P = 0.032). The ROC curve analysis yielded a cutoff value of SUVmax >18 to differentiate between PDL-1-positive and -negative tumors with a sensitivity of 57.1% and specificity of 89.5%. Total lesion glycolysis (TLG) and metabolic tumor volume (MTV) showed no significant association with PDL-1 expression (P = 0.58 and P = 0.88, respectively).

CONCLUSION: The study indicates that SUVmax has the potential to be used as a noninvasive biomarker for predicting PDL-1 expression in NSCLC. No significant difference was noted in the median MTV and TLG values between the PDL-1-positive and -negative groups.

articles.title: Prediction of pathologic complete response in breast cancer patients undergoing neoadjuvant chemotherapy using baseline 18F-FDG PET/CT-derived CT radiomics and clinicopathological biomarkers.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The study aimed to assess whether baseline fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) PET/computed tomography (CT)-derived CT radiomics adds predictive value to clinicopathological biomarkers and PET metabolic assessment for pathologic complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in breast cancer.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 104 patients with stage I-III breast cancer who underwent baseline 18F-FDG PET/CT, NAC, and surgery. Clinicopathological variables and tumor maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) were recorded; 107 CT radiomic features were extracted using PyRadiomics. Clinical, Metabolic, Radiomics, and Combined models were developed using L2-regularized logistic regression and evaluated by nested five-fold cross-validation. Discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis were assessed; 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using 1000 bootstrap resamples of pooled out-of-fold predictions.

RESULTS: Forty-six patients (44.2%) achieved pCR. Area under the curves (AUCs) were 0.784 (95% CI: 0.686-0.875) for Clinical, 0.595 (0.470-0.704) for Metabolic, and 0.636 (0.526-0.739) for Radiomics models. The Combined model had the highest numerical AUC (0.797; 95% CI: 0.705-0.880), with accuracy 0.731, sensitivity 0.630, specificity 0.810, and F1-score 0.674.

CONCLUSION: Combining CT radiomics and SUVmax with clinicopathological biomarkers yielded the highest numerical discrimination for pCR, but improvement over the Clinical model was modest. Larger multicenter external validation is needed before clinical implementation.

articles.title: A comparative analysis of the disease burden attributable to high BMI in Asia, Europe and Africa.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To comprehensively assess and compare the disease burden attributable to high BMI and its epidemiological trends across Asia, Africa and Europe from 1990 to 2023.

DESIGN: A secondary cross-sectional and temporal trend analysis of data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 study.

SETTING: Countries and territories in Asia, Europe and Africa.

PARTICIPANTS: Population-level data from the GBD 2023 study covering the three continents.

RESULTS: In 2023, Asia recorded 2 877 582 deaths (95 % uncertainty interval (UI): 1 465 996-4 507 685) and 120 182 714 Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALY) (56 308 955-186 506 210) attributable to high BMI, with age-standardised death and DALY rates of 30·83 (14·87-49·89) and 1253·75 (573·14-1984·15) per 100 000, respectively. Europe recorded 1 675 848 deaths (791 226-2 558 882) and 49 401 025 DALY (20 994 181-77 166 219), with corresponding rates of 52·52 (24·64-80·78) and 1824·14 (773·31-2872·71). Africa recorded 1 092 682 deaths (621 669-1 602 027) and 40 278 756 DALY (21 676 314-59 084 575), with rates of 88·74 (48·06-134·85) and 2746·12 (1445·93-4106·26). From 1990 to 2023, the estimated annual percentage change (EAPC) and average annual percent change (AAPC) in age-standardised burden indicators showed a consistent upward trend across all three continents. High BMI primarily contributed to mortality and DALY through CVD and diabetes and kidney diseases. Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) projections indicate a continuing increase in the high BMI-related disease burden over the next 17 years.

CONCLUSIONS: High BMI poses a significant and growing disease burden in Asia, Europe and Africa, a trend projected to persist. Implementing region-tailored interventions is crucial.

articles.title: Development and internal validation of a serum ferritin-based prediction model for coronary artery aneurysms in Kawasaki disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kawasaki disease is the leading cause of acquired heart disease in children, and coronary artery aneurysms represent its most important cardiovascular complication. Identifying children at risk for coronary artery aneurysms at 4 to 8 weeks after disease onset is clinically important. Serum ferritin may reflect systemic inflammation in Kawasaki disease, but its incremental predictive value remains uncertain. This study developed a ferritin-based model for predicting coronary artery aneurysms at 4 to 8 weeks.

METHODS: Patients with Kawasaki disease were retrospectively identified at a single centre and randomly divided into training and internal validation cohorts in a 6:4 ratio. Predictors were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed by discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis, and reclassification metrics.

RESULTS: Among 378 patients, 98 (25.9%) had coronary artery aneurysms at 4 to 8 weeks after disease onset. The ferritin-based model included male sex, platelet count, serum ferritin, albumin ≤ 31.5 g/L, and baseline maximum coronary artery Z score ≥ 2.5. Adding serum ferritin increased the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve from 0.853 to 0.899 in the training cohort and from 0.842 to 0.868 in the internal validation cohort, with good calibration, greater decision-curve net benefit, and improved risk reclassification.

CONCLUSIONS: Serum ferritin provided incremental predictive value for coronary artery aneurysms at 4 to 8 weeks after the onset of Kawasaki disease. The ferritin-based model improved predictive performance in internal validation and warrants multicentre external validation to assess its generalisability and clinical applicability.

articles.title: Growth failure and nutritional-endocrine adaptations in children with cyanotic CHD: a structured narrative review.
articles.abstract: The heart is increasingly recognised as a cardiovascular signalling organ that releases biologically active natriuretic peptides during haemodynamic stress. In cyanotic CHD, chronic hypoxaemia, altered loading conditions, increased energy expenditure, recurrent illness, and delayed repair may disrupt endocrine, metabolic, and nutritional pathways that regulate growth. This structured narrative review synthesises evidence linking cardiac biomarkers, systemic hormonal adaptation, nutritional status, surgical timing, and growth outcomes in children with cyanotic CHD. PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for human studies published from January 1990 to December 2025 that reported cardiac biomarkers, systemic hormonal measures, growth parameters, nutritional outcomes, or postoperative recovery in paediatric CHD. Thirty-six studies were included and narratively synthesised because lesion types, age groups, assays, and outcomes were heterogeneous. The evidence indicates consistent activation of natriuretic peptide signalling, reduced circulating insulin-like growth factor 1 and insulin-like growth factor binding protein 3 in several paediatric cohorts, appetite-related hormonal changes, impaired weight gain, and frequent linear growth faltering. Longitudinal studies suggest partial improvement in growth velocity and anabolic signalling after timely surgical correction, although incomplete recovery may occur when preoperative hypoxaemia and undernutrition are prolonged. Growth failure in cyanotic CHD should therefore be regarded as a multifactorial cardiovascular-nutritional syndrome rather than isolated primary endocrine disease. Early surgical referral, individualised nutrition, and coordinated cardiology, endocrinology, and dietetic follow-up are central to improving long-term outcomes.

articles.title: The role of T-peak to T-end, T peak-to-end/corrected QT ratios, and index of cardiac electrophysiological balance in the differential diagnosis of myocarditis.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Paediatric myocarditis, a rare inflammatory cardiomyopathy (incidence 1-2/100,000 annually), challenges emergency diagnosis due to nonspecific symptoms mimicking common illnesses. This study assessed electrocardiographic markers of ventricular repolarisation heterogeneity-T-peak to T-end interval, T-peak to T-end/QT, T peak-to-end/corrected QT ratios, and index of cardiac electrophysiological balance-for diagnosing myocarditis and predicting ventricular arrhythmia risk in children aged 0-18 years.

METHODS: Retrospective case-control study of 76 myocarditis patients (diagnosed by clinical, laboratory, echocardiographic, and cardiac MRI criteria) presenting to our paediatric emergency department from January 1, 2024, to May 30, 2025, versus 75 age-matched healthy controls. Electrocardiographic parameters were measured in leads DII and V5. Receiver operating characteristic analysis evaluated the diagnostic performance of T-peak to T-end and T peak-to-end/corrected QT (Lead II (Derivation II)). Myocarditis cases stratified by arrhythmia development (with: n = 28; without: n = 48); groups compared via t-tests, Mann-Whitney U, and chi-square (p < 0.05 significant).

RESULTS: Myocarditis group: 23 females (30.2%) and 53 males (69.8%); mean age 12.0 ± 4.7 years. Controls: 39 females (52.0%), 36 males (48.0%); mean age 10.3 ± 4.9 years (p = 0.03). Receiver operating characteristic (Lead II (Derivation II)): T-peak to T-end cut-off 62 ms (sensitivity 69.3%, specificity 78.9%, area under the curve 0.725, p < 0.001); T peak-to-end/corrected QT cut-off 0.19 (sensitivity 50.7%, specificity 78.9%, area under the curve 0.625, p < 0.05).The arrhythmia subgroup showed corrected QT prolongation (470 vs. 435 ms, V5; p < 0.001), T-peak to T-end (110 vs. 90 ms, V5; p < 0.001), higher T peak-to-end/corrected QT, and index of cardiac electrophysiological balance (both p < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: The T-peak to T-end interval, T peak-to-end/corrected QT ratio, and index of cardiac electrophysiological balance provide high-specificity, noninvasive electrocardiographic biomarkers for paediatric myocarditis diagnosis in the ED. Corrected QT and T-peak to T-end prolongation signals repolarisation heterogeneity and arrhythmia risk, supporting routine triage integration for early risk stratification.

articles.title: Transcatheter ventricular septal shunt creation in end-stage paediatric pulmonary arterial hypertension: lessons from a rescue decompression strategy.
articles.abstract: A 12-year-old girl with end-stage suprasystemic pulmonary arterial hypertension and progressive right ventricular failure underwent transcatheter ventricular septal shunt creation after deterioration despite targeted therapy and prior atrial septostomy. Right-to-left shunting was established, but haemodynamic improvement was limited; pulmonary pressures remained suprasystemic, persistent pericardial effusion developed, and the patient died despite intensive treatment, illustrating the complexity of rescue decompression in advanced disease.

articles.title: Post-ARDS Pulmonary Fibrosis: From Molecular Mechanisms to Clinical Management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a severe inflammatory lung injury caused by various factors, including infection, trauma and shock. The predominant pathological alteration in its late stages is pulmonary fibrosis (PF), characterised by progressive extracellular matrix deposition, architectural destruction and functional impairment. Particularly in COVID-19-induced ARDS, PF incidence has markedly increased, making it a major sequela impacting patients' long-term quality of life.

METHODS: This review systematically examines post-acute lung injury (ALI)/ARDS PF through three perspectives: pathogenesis, prediction and treatment.

RESULTS: Mechanistically, the fibrotic process involves epithelial injury and mesenchymal transition, fibroblast activation with aberrant extracellular matrix remodelling, dysregulated inflammation with immune cell involvement and clinical management-related factors. For prediction, various biomarkers (including growth factors, matrix proteins and inflammatory markers) and imaging features (particularly high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics) demonstrate clinical value. Integrated multiparameter models incorporating artificial intelligence show promise for early identification and risk stratification of high-risk patients. Therapeutic strategies encompass anti-inflammatory approaches (e.g., corticosteroids and antioxidants), antifibrotic agents (pirfenidone and nintedanib), cell-based therapies (mesenchymal stem cells and exosomes) and emerging genetic/RNA interventions. However, specific preventive and therapeutic approaches tailored to the post-ALI/ARDS PF population remain inadequate in clinical practice.

CONCLUSIONS: Future research should focus on elucidating underlying mechanisms, refining early-warning systems, exploring personalised treatments and facilitating clinical translation. The ultimate goal is to transition from traditional supportive care to proactive prevention through enhanced clinical surveillance, early prediction and rational intervention, thereby preventing fibrosis progression and improving outcomes in ARDS survivors.

articles.title: Self-HArm one-year Risk Prediction in personality disorders (SHARP-PD): a clinical risk prediction model development and internal-external cross-validation study.
articles.journal: European psychiatry : the journal of the Association of European Psychiatrists

articles.title: Frank Sign with Acute Ischemia Stroke and Transient Ischemia Attack.
Refractory Distributive Shock in Complex Spine Surgery: A Rare Entity That Needs Recognition - Case Series.
articles.abstract: Vasoplegia is a form of vasodilatory shock characterized by low systemic vascular resistance and severe hypotension with normal or high cardiac output that is unresponsive to volume resuscitation and conventional vasopressors. Its occurrence after major complex spine surgery has rarely been reported. Hypotension during complex spine surgery is associated with increased perioperative morbidity. This case series describes the management of refractory distributive shock of unknown cause in patients who underwent complex spine surgery. Three American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA-1) patients underwent complex spine surgery involving spinal cord manipulation/retraction/stretching. All three patients encountered severe refractory hypotension toward the end of the surgery without any obvious causes of hypotension (hypovolemia, anaphylaxis, spinal shock, cardiogenic, embolic, or pneumothorax). All patients were treated with high doses of noradrenaline and vasopressin for 12-36 h after surgery. All patients had good neurological outcomes despite transient severe hypotension. Awareness of this entity helps anesthesiologists manage hypotension by early institution of nonconventional vasopressors (e.g., vasopressin) after ruling out other causes.

articles.title: Subtype-Specific Treatment of Autoimmune Myocarditis: Current Evidence and Clinical Approach.
articles.abstract: Autoimmune myocarditis presents a distinct therapeutic challenge: similar clinical syndromes may arise from fundamentally different immune mechanisms and therefore require different treatments.
