This narrative review synthesizes current evidence for the management of giant cell myocarditis, eosinophilic myocarditis, cardiac sarcoidosis, systemic autoimmune disease-associated myocarditis, immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis, and virus-negative immune-mediated lymphocytic myocarditis. We examine how clinical severity, histopathology, infectious exclusion, extracardiac disease, and treatment toxicity shape therapeutic decisions. Although cardiovascular stabilization follows shared principles, immunosuppressive strategies vary substantially across subtypes, ranging from corticosteroids and multidrug immunosuppression to targeted biologic or molecular therapies. We also discuss treatment escalation, monitoring response, and management of fulminant presentations. Across all subtypes, the central challenge is balancing the urgency of suppressing myocardial inflammation against diagnostic uncertainty and treatment-related risk. A subtype-directed approach offers the most clinically meaningful framework for selecting therapy and improving consistency in the management of autoimmune myocarditis.

articles.title: Predictors of Antibiotic Overuse in Febrile Children: A Sub-analysis of the Prospective, Multicenter AutoPilot-Dx Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antibiotic overuse contributes to antimicrobial resistance. Mechanisms that drive overuse, including diagnostic uncertainty, are thought to be complex. We aimed to investigate predictive factors for antibiotic overuse in a large pediatric cohort.

METHODS: This is a subanalysis from the AutoPilot-Dx study, which enrolled febrile children 90 days to 18 years old presenting to the pediatric emergency department with respiratory tract infection or fever without source, including both hospitalized children and those discharged home. We analyzed patient flow from being treated with antibiotics at recruitment to definitive antibiotic treatment after assessment, depending on physician judgment. Variables significantly associated with antibiotic overuse in univariate analysis were entered into a multivariable logistic regression model to identify independent predictors of antibiotic overuse, defined as receipt of antibiotic treatment following clinical assessment in cases with viral panel-adjudicated diagnosis. Diagnostic uncertainty was assessed by treating physicians.

RESULTS: Upon recruitment, 127/1008 (12.6%) were receiving antibiotic treatment. Overall, 186 of 628 cases with a viral panel-adjudicated diagnosis were judged to have antibiotic overuse. Factors with significant association in univariate analysis were diagnostic uncertainty, nonexudative tonsillitis, rales and younger age. Presence of a diagnostic test result upon presentation to the hospital and current antibiotic treatment were found not to be associated with overuse. Among 566 of 1008 cases with complete data on all model covariates, multivariable logistic regression yielded diagnostic uncertainty [odds ratio (OR), 2.09; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.18-3.93; P = 0.015], nonexudative tonsillitis (OR, 2.78; 95% CI: 1.72-4.59; P < 0.001) and rales (OR, 1.82; 95% CI: 1.15-2.86; P = 0.01) to be positively associated with antibiotic overuse, while age showed a negative association in complete-case analysis (OR, 0.93; 95% CI: 0.85-0.99; P = 0.038), which attenuated and was no longer significant in a multiple imputation sensitivity analysis (OR, 0.96; 95% CI: 0.91-1.01; P = 0.150).

CONCLUSIONS: Diagnostic uncertainty contributes to antibiotic overuse, alongside clinical factors. Future studies should investigate the impact of improved diagnostic algorithms on antibiotic prescribing in patients with respiratory tract infections in whom physicians experience diagnostic uncertainty.

articles.title: Bariatric Surgery as a Rescue Strategy After Semaglutide or Tirzepatide.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate 2-year weight loss after bariatric surgery among adults with intolerable adverse effects or inadequate weight loss with semaglutide or tirzepatide.

SUMMARY BACKGROUND DATA: Semaglutide and tirzepatide are effective obesity medications, but intolerance and inadequate weight loss are common, creating uncertainty about next-step therapy.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included adults with BMI ≥35 kg/m² undergoing Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) or sleeve gastrectomy (SG) at Cleveland Clinic hospitals from 2018 to 2024. Electronic health record and dispensing data classified preoperative semaglutide or tirzepatide exposure and response. The primary outcome was estimated 2-year total body weight loss (TBWL), stratified by procedure and type 2 diabetes (T2DM) status.

RESULTS: Among 4929 patients, 4661 had no prior exposure (comparator group), 61 discontinued semaglutide or tirzepatide because of intolerable adverse effects, and 207 had inadequate weight-loss response. Before surgery, estimated 2-year medication-associated weight change was a 1.4% gain in the intolerance group and 1.5% TBWL in the inadequate-response group. After surgery, 2-year TBWL in the intolerance group was 27.9% and 22.7% after RYGB and 20.1% and 21.6% after SG among patients without and with T2DM, respectively. Corresponding estimates in the inadequate-response group were 35.8%, 27.4%, 14.3%, and 14.2%. For comparison, corresponding 2-year TBWL estimates in the comparator group were 33.3%, 28.7%, 23.6%, and 19.9%. In adjusted analysis of the inadequate-response group, RYGB was associated with greater 2-year TBWL than SG (32.7% vs. 17.8%; difference, 14.9 percentage points [95% CI, 13.1%-16.7%]).

CONCLUSIONS: Bariatric surgery was associated with clinically meaningful 2-year weight loss after semaglutide or tirzepatide intolerance or inadequate response, with RYGB potentially offering greater benefit after inadequate response.

articles.title: Thromboembolic Complications of Orthopedic Surgery.
articles.abstract: Orthopedic surgery is a major risk factor for thromboembolic events such as deep venous thrombosis and pulmonary embolism following a variety of surgeries such as total hip and knee replacements, fracture fixations, spinal surgeries, orthopedic traumas, and arthroscopic surgeries. Many other risk factors contribute, such as age, immobilization, combined oral contraceptive medications, genetic causes, cast immobilization, tourniquet use, and comorbidities. Prophylaxis can be done through chemoprophylaxis and/or mechanoprophylaxis. Diagnosis of deep venous thrombosis is made through ultrasonography, and pulmonary embolism diagnosis is made using risk stratification and a variety of possible tests including D-dimer levels, computed tomography pulmonary angiogram, and ventilation/perfusion scans. Treatment requires using anticoagulants for a minimum of 3 months or possibly inferior vena cava filters if anticoagulation therapy is contraindicated.

articles.title: The role, challenges, and innovations of rifampin in the management of periprosthetic joint infections: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) remains a severe complication due to persistent bacterial biofilms. Rifampin is traditionally valued for its unique biofilm-penetrating properties, yet its clinical role is increasingly viewed as context-dependent. While current evidence supports the efficacy of rifampin in two-stage revision arthroplasty, its application in debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention (DAIR) remains a subject of ongoing debate. Landmark randomized trials once reported superior cure rates for DAIR combined with rifampin, but contemporary large-scale retrospective data show no statistically significant difference in remission rates, often accompanied by a significantly higher incidence of adverse events. Furthermore, the timing of administration is critical; early initiation within five days post-DAIR has been linked to increased treatment failure. These challenges, alongside profound drug-drug interactions, have spurred interest in localized delivery innovations like microencapsulation and nanoparticles. While these bioengineering approaches show preclinical promise in overcoming PMMA chemical incompatibility, they remain at the proof-of-concept stage. Consequently, rifampin should be employed as a targeted adjunct rather than a universal standard, requiring careful consideration of surgical strategy, patient tolerance, and optimal timing.

articles.title: Determinants of extended inpatient care in odontogenic cervicofacial infections: a retrospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to identify clinical and demographic factors associated with prolonged hospitalisation in patients treated for severe odontogenic cervicofacial infections (CFI).

METHODS: This retrospective study analysed 152 patients who were treated in an inpatient setting for CFI at the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, Army Hospital Hamburg, between January 2022 and December 2023. Patients were stratified based on length of hospital stay (LOS) into two groups: <7 days and ≥ 7 days. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, treatment-related and timing data were compared to determine their association with prolonged LOS.

RESULTS: Patients with prolonged hospitalisation (≥ 7 days; n = 79) were older and more frequently had recorded pre-existing disease, multi-space infection, submandibular or floor-of-mouth involvement, dyspnoea, elevated inflammatory markers and delayed presentation in unadjusted analyses. In multivariable logistic regression, recorded pre-existing disease (aOR 6.04, 95% CI 1.10-33.18; p = 0.038) and longer time from symptom onset to hospital presentation (aOR 2.86 per day, 95% CI 2.01-4.07; p < 0.001) remained independently associated with prolonged hospitalisation.

CONCLUSIONS: Although several demographic, anatomical and clinical factors were associated with prolonged hospitalisation in unadjusted analyses, recorded pre-existing disease and delayed hospital presentation remained independently associated with prolonged LOS after multivariable adjustment. These findings highlight the potential importance of comorbidity and timely presentation in identifying patients at risk of extended inpatient care, but prospective multicentre validation is warranted.

articles.title: Can full-stay lactate burden predict ICU mortality? The importance of a defined prediction time.
articles.abstract: Deininger and colleagues reported that time-weighted average lactate calculated over the entire intensive care stay was strongly associated with mortality after traumatic brain injury. This finding supports full-stay TWAL as a summary of sustained lactate exposure; however, because the measure cannot be finalized before death or discharge, it does not establish prospective prognostic performance from a predefined, clinically actionable time. The 72-h analysis also represents conditional prognosis among patients remaining under intensive care at that landmark. The incremental value of time weighting over mean lactate remains uncertain, and performance estimated in an outcome-matched subset may not generalize to a consecutive population. A prespecified landmark framework would better define the clinical prognostic value of longitudinal lactate indices.

articles.title: Predictive modelling approaches for childhood diarrhoeal disease: a systematic review (2000-2025).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Childhood diarrhoeal disease remains a leading cause of child mortality worldwide. Although predictive models have been increasingly proposed for early warning, their methodological quality and validation have not been systematically appraised using formal risk of bias frameworks. This systematic review aimed to identify, describe, and critically appraise individual-level prediction models and population-level forecasting studies for childhood diarrhoeal outcomes, focusing on model development, validation, reporting quality, and operational readiness.

METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420251232269), we searched seven databases and grey literature sources from January 2000 to September 18, 2025. We included studies that developed or validated multivariable prediction models for diarrhoeal outcomes in children, including statistical, machine learning, and hybrid approaches. Individual-level models were assessed using the Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool (PROBAST), and population-level studies were appraised qualitatively for methodological credibility, with emphasis on validation.

RESULTS: From the 20,662 records screened, 38 studies met the inclusion criteria. Publications accelerated after 2020, with 78.9% of included studies published in this period. The evidence base comprised 25 single-country studies and 13 multi-country or global analyses. Statistical models were most commonly used, as reported in 18 studies, while ensemble or hybrid approaches such as hybrid statistical-machine learning models were applied in 11 studies, and machine learning methods in eight studies. Predictor selection varied widely, with socio-demographic and household factors included in 23 studies and environmental or climatic variables in 18. Among the 15 individual-level prediction models assessed using PROBAST, five showed high overall risk of bias. Of the 19 population-level forecasting studies appraised qualitatively, only three undertook rigorous out-of-sample temporal validation. The remaining four studies were classified as other modelling categories and were summarised descriptively.

CONCLUSIONS: Research on childhood diarrhoeal prediction has expanded rapidly across individual-level, population-level, and related classification models. Although some studies reported stronger validation practices, these remained uncommon, leaving evidence for transportability and implementation readiness limited for most models. Future progress will depend on closer alignment between modelling objective, validation strategy, appraisal framework, and transparent reporting.

articles.title: Reply to the comment by Kuzukıran Kocataş on "Can full-stay lactate burden predict ICU mortality? The importance of a defined prediction time".
articles.abstract: We respond to the comment on lo​ngitudinal lactate indices after traumatic brain injury. Full-stay time-weighted average lactate characterizes longitudinal lactate exposure over the intensive care unit stay but is unavailable at an earlier prediction time. Additional post hoc 72 h landmark analyses showed modest discrimination of subsequent 14-day intensive care mortality among eligible patients. Paired comparisons demonstrated similar full-stay discrimination for time-weighted and arithmetic mean lactate. Both analyses yielded similar estimates in matched and full eligible cohorts. These findings support the prognostic relevance of longitudinal lactate measurements; however, prospective validation at prespecified landmarks is necessary before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Ammonia-to-upper-limit-of-normal ratio as a predictor of short-term mortality and liver-related complications in hospitalized patients with decompensated cirrhosis- A prospective observational study.
articles.journal: Indian journal of gastroenterology : official journal of the Indian Society of Gastroenterology

articles.title: Precision Metabolic and Bariatric Medicine: Reconciling Predictive Machine Learning with Explanatory Biostatistics to Validate the Independent Effect of a 10.5% Preoperative TBWL Threshold.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preoperative total body weight loss (PreopTBWL%) is widely used before metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS), yet its long-term prognostic value remains debated. This study integrated machine learning (ML), unsupervised clustering, and linear mixed-effects modeling (LMM) to define data-driven preoperative targets and characterize multi-year postoperative weight trajectories.

METHODS: We analyzed prospectively collected data and electronic medical records from 802 adults undergoing primary laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy, primary Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, or revision/conversion MBS within a structured, protein-focused preoperative lifestyle program. Five machine learning models were trained with nested cross-validation to predict each postoperative year. Each model used only patients with that year's outcome recorded (608 at Year 1 to 83 at Year 6). From Year 2 onward, earlier postoperative measurements for those patients were included as predictors. Priority was given to Years 1-4. Top-performing SHAP profiles guided feature selection for confirmatory longitudinal LMMs. Although the LMM framework spanned the full 6-year horizon (858 repeated measures from 420 active patients), the most robust inferences were restricted to Years 1-4 because of substantial attrition thereafter. Youden Index optimization, segmented regression, and unsupervised k-means clustering on UMAP embeddings were used to define precise PreopTBWL% targets and map distinct multi-year phenotypic subgroups.

RESULTS: Machine learning models demonstrated strong predictive performance, peaking at Year 2 (Random Forest R² = 0.524 ± 0.033, AUC = 0.875 ± 0.029) and remaining robust through Year 4, with PreopTBWL% consistently ranking among the strongest prognostic features. Unsupervised clustering (k = 5) revealed that preoperative behavioral engagement separated high- from low-performing phenotypes far more powerfully than procedure type or demographics. Initial racial disparities in weight-loss trajectories narrowed progressively and were no longer statistically significant by Year 4 (p = 0.1454). Linear mixed-effects modeling confirmed a robust, independent positive association between PreopTBWL% and long-term outcomes (β = 0.447, p < 0.001). Threshold optimization identified 10.5% PreopTBWL% as the optimal clinical target; patients falling below this threshold experienced a significant long-term deficit (β = -4.608, p = 0.017) that persisted after adjustment for diabetes and operative duration. Interaction terms between the threshold and surgical procedure were non-significant (Threshold × Sleeve, p = 0.532; Threshold × Revision/Conversion, p = 0.778). Segmented regression further identified a structural dose-response breakpoint at 19.68% PreopTBWL%.

CONCLUSIONS: Achieving ≥ 10.5% PreopTBWL% was associated with durable multi-year PostopTBWL% after MBS, and procedure type did not modify that association in this cohort. By integrating predictive machine learning with explanatory longitudinal modeling, this work shifts preoperative evaluation from arbitrary administrative requirements toward structured, phenotype-guided risk stratification and care escalation.

articles.title: Enterocolitis: a diagnosis in the news that may become more common in the emergency room.
articles.abstract: Foodborne illness affects an estimated 48 million people in the United States each year, and outbreaks peak in the summer. Recalls during the summer of 2026 involved eggs, jalapeños, and frozen blueberries, along with a Cyclospora outbreak traced to iceberg lettuce that caused more than 12,000 illnesses and over 550 hospitalizations. Furthermore, they caused nationwide public anxiety and dominated news headlines. Patients with enteric infection usually reach the emergency department with abdominal pain, and radiologists often read their CT before stool studies return or before anyone suspects infection. This review describes the CT findings of bacterial and parasitic enteritis and colitis. Common features include symmetric segmental or diffuse bowel wall thickening with submucosal edema, mucosal hyperenhancement producing a halo or target pattern, associated fat stranding, engorged mesenteric vessels, and lymphadenopathy. CT also shows complications including toxic megacolon, perforation, and abscess. Recognition of these findings supports timely diagnosis and appropriate management of infectious enterocolitis.

articles.title: Wearable Arrhythmia Detection: Moving from your Watch to your Shirt?
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Digital devices play an increasingly important role in the detection and screening of cardiac arrhythmias. Atrial fibrillation (AF), the most common arrhythmia, is associated with an increased risk of stroke, heart failure, and mortality. This review summarises the current evidence on wearable devices for screening and diagnosing atrial fibrillation.

RECENT FINDINGS: Numerous studies have demonstrated the value of wearables for AF detection and diagnosis. In addition, artificial intelligence enhances automated rhythm analysis and signal processing, supporting the increasing clinical implementation of digital technologies in outpatient care. Single-lead ECG devices provide the strongest evidence for AF detection, with smartwatches representing one of the most extensively investigated wearable technology. Limitations include motion artefacts and predominantly semi-continuous monitoring. Future research should focus on integrating artificial intelligence to improve signal analysis and artefact reduction, and on evaluating the impact of wearable-based strategies on clinically relevant outcomes, including stroke and heart failure.

articles.title: Stereotactic radiosurgery for bilateral trigeminal neuralgia: A systematic review and proposed framework for staged treatment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Bilateral trigeminal neuralgia (BTN) is uncommon and surgically complex. Stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) is a minimally invasive option for medically refractory BTN, although evidence remains sparse and heterogeneous. This systematic review evaluated the efficacy, durability, and toxicity of SRS in medically refractory BTN. It also synthesized the evidence into a practical staged-treatment framework.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched through October 11, 2026. Eligible studies reported BTN-specific SRS outcomes in adults, separately from unilateral cohorts. Two independent reviewers performed study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment using adapted Newcastle-Ottawa and MINORS tools. Certainty of evidence was evaluated using a GRADE-informed approach. Owing to clinical heterogeneity and small samples, findings were synthesized narratively rather than by meta-analysis.

RESULTS: Six reports met the inclusion criteria. Five described 88 BTN patients, including 54 SRS-treated patients across four reports. Of 91 nominally treated nerves, 67 were explicitly reported, and 24 were inferred from staged bilateral SRS in 12 patients. The sixth report described one BTN case without a complete subgroup denominator. Study-reported initial pain relief ranged from 71.4% to 100% across heterogeneous outcome definitions and analytical units. Pain recurrence was frequent, with durability varying markedly from 14 months to 1697 days in the sequential-onset series. Multiple sclerosis appeared associated with poorer outcomes and earlier recurrence, based on small subgroups. Repeat SRS achieved adequate pain relief in 10 of 11 retreated nerves (91%) in the largest cohort, with a median durability of 2.8 years. Sensory disturbance was the most common adverse event. One report described disabling bilateral numbness in a patient with prior bilateral ablative treatment. Anesthesia dolorosa incidence remains uncertain.

CONCLUSION: SRS may provide early pain control in selected patients with medically refractory BTN, but bilateral sensory morbidity remains uncertain. Staged treatment was described in several reports, whereas bilateral treatment timing was unreported in one case. Certainty of evidence remains very low. Current evidence supports individualized decision-making focused on etiology, surgical fitness, first-side response, sensory toxicity, and cumulative bilateral trigeminal morbidity.Registration and Protocol: This systematic review was not registered in a prospective registry (e.g., PROSPERO). A protocol was developed a priori and is publicly available at https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/RBVNE.

articles.title: Clinical, neuroimaging and electroencephalographic differences between pediatric and adult HaNDL: a systematic review and pooled individual patient analysis.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The syndrome of transient headache and neurological deficits with cerebrospinal fluid lymphocytosis (HaNDL) is a rare, self-limited disorder and a diagnosis of exclusion, most commonly reported in young adults. Pediatric cases are less frequently described, and age-related differences in clinical presentation and ancillary findings remain incompletely characterized. We aimed to compare pediatric and adult HaNDL presentations using pooled individual patient data.

METHODS: A PRISMA 2020-guided systematic review was performed to identify published HaNDL cases. Cases that met diagnostic criteria applicable at the time of publication were included. Individual patient data were extracted and pooled. Demographic, clinical, cerebrospinal fluid, neuroimaging, and electroencephalographic features were compared between pediatric and adult patients.

RESULTS: A total of 194 patients were included (159 adults and 35 pediatric patients). Sex distribution differed significantly, with a higher proportion of males among pediatric patients (66.7% vs. 40.4%, p = 0.016). Most clinical features, cerebrospinal fluid findings, neuroimaging abnormalities, and electroencephalographic findings were comparable between age groups. Optic disc edema was significantly more frequent in pediatric patients (43.8% vs. 5.7%, p = 0.002). Altered mental status was more commonly reported in pediatric patients, although this difference did not reach statistical significance.

CONCLUSIONS: HaNDL represents a single syndrome across the lifespan, characterized by a shared clinical core and a self-limited course. Awareness of age-associated features, particularly altered mental status and optic disc edema in pediatric patients, may improve diagnostic recognition and help avoid unnecessary investigations and treatments when alternative high-risk conditions have been reasonably excluded.

articles.title: Real-world pharmacovigilance of intra-articular triamcinolone acetonide in arthritis treatment: a two-decade FAERS and JADER study with machine learning prediction and SHAP-based interpretation.
articles.abstract: Triamcinolone acetonide (TA) is a widely used glucocorticoid for inflammatory diseases, including arthritis. Although intra-articular TA injection provides effective symptom relief, its safety profile in real-world clinical practice remains incompletely characterized. Adverse event reports associated with intra-articular TA injection for arthritis were retrieved from the FAERS database (2004-Q1 2026) and the JADER database (2004-Q4 2025). Disproportionality analyses were performed using four signal detection algorithms, including ROR, PRR, BCPNN, and MGPS. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate signal heterogeneity and robustness. Time-to-onset patterns were assessed using Weibull analysis. Endocrine-related adverse events were further evaluated using multivariable logistic regression and machine learning classification models with SHAP-based interpretation. A total of 738 FAERS reports involving intra-articular TA were identified, covering 27 system organ classes. Multiple established and potential safety signals were detected, including adrenal insufficiency, hyperglycemia, osteonecrosis, bacterial arthritis, postmenopausal hemorrhage, and Cushing's syndrome. Additional potential safety signals included type 2 diabetes mellitus, flushing, erythema multiforme, pemphigus, and septic shock. The strongest disproportionality signals were observed for injection site calcification, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis suppression, injection site atrophy, and Cushing's syndrome. Most adverse events occurred within 30 days after exposure (84.55%), with a median onset time of 5 days (IQR: 2-14). External signal consistency assessment using 112 JADER reports identified eight signals consistent with FAERS findings. Multivariable logistic regression showed that age, sex, therapy type, and reporter type were associated with endocrine-related adverse event reporting. Machine learning models demonstrated good classification performance, with random forest achieving the highest test set AUC (0.864). SHAP analysis identified demographic and treatment-related variables as important contributors to model classification. This study provides a comprehensive real-world pharmacovigilance assessment of intra-articular TA and identifies both established and potential safety signals. Integration of conventional signal detection, regression analysis, and interpretable machine learning approaches may facilitate systematic characterization of TA-associated adverse event patterns and support future safety monitoring.

articles.title: Postdischarge continuity of care and cardiovascular outcomes in acute coronary syndrome.
articles.journal: Journal of the Chinese Medical Association : JCMA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Despite the availability of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT), postdischarge continuity of care (CoC) remains suboptimal, and evidence from Asian health-care systems remains limited. The present study examined the association between CoC and clinical outcomes in Taiwanese patients with ACS.

METHODS: This nationwide observational cohort study was conducted using data from Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database. It included patients who had their first ACS-related hospitalization between 2012 and 2020 and excluded those who died during the index hospitalization or experienced study outcomes within 1 month after discharge. CoC was assessed in terms of physician, specialty, and GDMT continuity. Study outcomes were all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs), hospitalization for heart failure (HHF), and major bleeding.

RESULTS: This study included 140 214 patients with ACS. Patients with low physician continuity had significantly higher risks of all-cause mortality (adjusted risk ratio [aRR]: 2.20, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.09 to 2.31), cardiovascular death (aRR: 1.97, 95% CI: 1.81 to 2.15), MACEs (aRR: 1.78, 95% CI: 1.66 to 1.90), HHF (aRR: 1.66, 95% CI: 1.54 to 1.78), and major bleeding (aRR: 1.45, 95% CI: 1.26 to 1.66) than did those with high physician continuity. Low specialty continuity was associated with a 1.28-to-1.95-fold increase in the risk of adverse outcomes. Furthermore, low GDMT continuity was significantly associated with elevated risks of all-cause mortality, cardiovascular death, and MACEs but not HHF or major bleeding.

CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that lower CoC during the first year after ACS-related hospitalization is associated with poorer clinical outcomes. Future studies should explore strategies to improve CoC.

articles.title: Sitagliptin, a repurposed diabetes drug, overcomes gemcitabine resistance in pancreatic cancer via ribonucleotide reductase inhibition: SITGEM-CARE phase 2 trial.
articles.abstract: Gemcitabine resistance remains a major therapeutic barrier in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), for which median survival in advanced disease has remained near one year despite extensive clinical investigation. Using artificial intelligence (AI)-guided structure-based drug repurposing, we identified sitagliptin, a DPP-4 inhibitor for diabetes, as a candidate ribonucleotide reductase (RRM1/2) inhibitor that sensitizes PDAC to gemcitabine. Molecular dynamics simulations suggested that sitagliptin disrupts gemcitabine-RRM1/2 interactions, downregulating RRM1/2 expression and restoring chemosensitivity across PDAC cell lines, patient-derived organoids, and mouse models. Sitagliptin enhanced the anti-tumor efficacy of both gemcitabine-nab-paclitaxel (GnP) and FOLFIRINOX regimens in preclinical studies. We conducted SITGEM-CARE, a single-center phase 2 trial in 22 patients with locally advanced or metastatic PDAC (median age 65.0 years; ECOG performance status 1, 86.4%; Stage IV, 68.2%; liver metastases, 54.5%). Patients received sitagliptin 100 mg orally once daily continuously, plus gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² and nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m² on days 1 and 8 of 21-day cycles. Among 22 evaluable patients, eight achieved a partial response, and 11 had stable disease, yielding an objective response rate of 36.4% (95% CI: 17.2-59.3%) and a disease control rate of 86.4% (95% CI: 65.1-97.1%), with tumor shrinkage in 86.4% of patients. At a median follow-up of 9.9 months, the median progression-free survival was 6.6 months (95% CI: 4.8-12.4) with 6-month and 9-month PFS rates of 63.6% and 43.5%, respectively. Median overall survival was 12.5 months (95% CI: 7.8-not reached), with 62.9% of patients alive at 12 months. Furthermore, treatment was well tolerated, with no Grade 4/5 treatment-related adverse events. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in adequately powered, randomized trials. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05947825.

Dupilumab in Pediatric Eosinophilic Esophagitis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Dupilumab is an approved biologic therapy for eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE); however, real-world pediatric data remain limited. The aim of this study is to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of dupilumab in children with EoE enrolled in the international European Society for Paediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition (ESPGHAN)-funded pEEr registry, with a focus on combined remission, treatment deescalation, and predictors of sustained response.

METHODS: DU-PED is a multicenter, retrospective cohort study including children with confirmed EoE treated with dupilumab in routine clinical practice. The primary outcome was combined remission at 6 and 12 months, defined as simultaneous clinical (≥75% Pediatric Eosinophilic Esophagitis Symptom Score [PEESS] v2.0 reduction or symptom resolution), endoscopic (EoE Endoscopic Reference Score [EREFS] ≤2), and histologic remission (<15 eos/high-power field [HPF]). Secondary outcomes included longitudinal changes in disease domains, treatment deescalation, predictors of remission, and safety. Multivariable logistic regression and ROC analysis were performed.

RESULTS: A total of 109 patients from 22 centers were included (median age 16 years; 75% male). Combined remission was achieved in 53% at 6 months and 86% at 12 months. PEESS v2.0, EREFS, and peak eosinophil counts significantly improved over time (P < 0.001). At 12 months, 81% of patients were receiving dupilumab monotherapy, and 94% reduced concomitant EoE-directed therapy. Higher baseline proximal eosinophil density was independently associated with a lower likelihood of sustained combined remission at 12 months (odds ratio 0.98, 95% CI 0.96-0.99). Dupilumab was well tolerated, with no treatment discontinuations.

CONCLUSIONS: In a large international registry-based pediatric cohort, dupilumab achieved high and durable rates of combined remission and enabled substantial treatment simplification, supporting its role as an effective long-term treatment strategy for pediatric EoE.

articles.title: Timing of Long COVID Improvement in Prospectively Followed RECOVER-Adult Participants.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long COVID (LC) is widespread; however, limited information has been reported on the likelihood that symptoms remit over time.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the likelihood of improvement among persons with likely LC.

DESIGN: Prospective, multisite cohort study (RECOVER-Adult [Researching COVID to Enhance Recovery]).

SETTING: 83 U.S.-based sites across 33 states; Washington, DC; and Puerto Rico.

PARTICIPANTS: 1019 persons in RECOVER-Adult with likely LC (LC Research Index [LCRI] ≥11) 12 months after first SARS-CoV-2 infection.

MEASUREMENTS: The primary outcome was time until 2 consecutive study visits with LCRI less than 11. Secondary outcomes were time until LCRI measure reduced 50% or more and quality of life was good or better, and LCRI decreased to 0. Unadjusted estimates of cumulative incidence and adjusted marginal cumulative incidence by age, sex, SARS-CoV-2 wave, and LC subtype were reported across all follow-up time points.

RESULTS: An estimated 36.2% (95% CI, 33.0% to 39.5%) met the primary outcome by 24 months after infection, and 50.1% (CI, 46.1% to 54.0%) met the primary outcome by 36 months. An estimated 56.4% (CI, 52.2% to 60.4%) and 26.9% (CI, 23.3% to 30.5%), respectively, met the 2 secondary outcomes by 36 months. Among persons who still reported likely LC at 18 months and 24 months after first infection, relative timing of subsequent symptom improvement was similar.

LIMITATION: Findings in this observational cohort are interpretable in a population with prevalent likely LC and do not address causal relationships between individual characteristics and symptom improvement.

CONCLUSION: Among persons with likely LC 12 months after initial SARS-CoV-2 infection, one half experience meaningful reductions in symptoms by 36 months, whereas a quarter experience complete remission of symptoms. These findings underscore both the potential for natural recovery and the urgent need for placebo-controlled therapeutic intervention trials.

PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE: National Institutes of Health.

articles.title: Measles.
articles.abstract: Measles is reemerging, with cases and outbreaks increasing across the United States and other countries where measles had previously been eliminated. Most U.S. physicians have no experience with treating measles. However, the increasing likelihood of encountering not only children but also adults with measles requires a clinical review of the epidemiology, prevention, diagnosis, and management of this previously uncommon infection for general internal medicine physicians and hospitalists who care for adults in settings with measles reemergence. Prompt clinical suspicion, infection control measures, and notification of public health departments support timely diagnosis and disease control.

Progression-free survival prediction in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: where can we further improve?
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is a biologically heterogeneous disease in which approximately one-third of patients experience primary refractoriness or relapse despite modern chemoimmunotherapy. Although clinical prognostic indices remain the cornerstone of risk stratification, they incompletely capture the biological complexity underlying disease progression. Accurate prediction of progression-free survival (PFS) is essential to support personalized treatment strategies.

AREAS COVERED: This review summarizes advances in PFS prediction in DLBCL, including clinical prognostic models, quantitative PET imaging, molecular and transcriptomic classification, genomic classifiers, tumor microenvironment profiling, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)-based biomarkers, and integrated multimodal prognostic models. Relevant literature was identified through PubMed, with ClinicalTrials.gov searched for ongoing clinical trials; searches were updated through 3 October 2026. We discuss the strengths, limitations, and clinical applicability of these approaches.

EXPERT OPINION: Future prognostic models will increasingly rely on integrated multimodal frameworks combining clinical, imaging, molecular, immune, and dynamic response biomarkers. Among these, ctDNA has emerged as one of the most promising tools for measurable residual disease assessment. However, improving patient outcomes will require moving beyond prognostic accuracy toward predictive biomarkers capable of guiding personalized treatment selection across an evolving therapeutic landscape. Prospective validation, assay standardization, and demonstration of clinical utility will be essential for translating these approaches into routine practice.

articles.title: [Construction and internal validation of a prognostic prediction model for R0 resection after conversion therapy in colorectal cancer liver metastases based on clinicopathological features combined with ctDNA].
articles.abstract: Objective: To construct and validate an overall survival (OS) prediction model for patients with colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRLM) undergoing R0 resection after conversion therapy. Methods: A total of 364 patients with CRLM who were evaluated by a multidisciplinary team as initially unresectable and underwent R0 resection of both the primary tumor and liver metastases after conversion therapy between January 2018 and December 2023 were retrospectively included with 226 male, 138 female and a median age [M(Q1, Q3)] of 58.0(51.0,66.0) years and randomly divided by computer software at a 7∶3 ratio into a training set (n=255) and a validation set (n=109). Follow-up was conducted through February 2026, with OS as the primary endpoint. For model 1, all modelable baseline variables were included in the candidate pool; variable selection was performed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-Cox regression, and an OS prediction model was constructed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and presented as a nomogram. Model 2 additionally included the adjuvant chemotherapy regimen variable on the basis of model 1 for sensitivity analysis. Model performance was evaluated using the concordance index (C-index), area under the time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results: The median follow-up was 36.2 months, and 198 deaths (54.4%) occurred. After LASSO selection from the full candidate pool, model 1 included N stage, number of liver metastases, maximum liver metastasis diameter, preoperative carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9) level, KRAS mutation status, BRAF V600E mutation status, postoperative 1-month circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) status, body mass index (BMI), number of conversion therapy cycles, and intraoperative blood loss. Multivariable Cox regression analysis showed that negative postoperative 1-month ctDNA (HR=0.134, 95%CI: 0.088-0.202, P<0.001), BRAF V600E wild type (HR=0.200, 95%CI: 0.106-0.379, P<0.001), having≥5 liver metastases (HR=2.564, 95%CI: 1.518-4.332, P<0.001), and preoperative CA19-9≥35 U/ml (HR=1.593, 95%CI: 1.082-2.345, P=0.018) were factors associated with OS after R0 resection following conversion therapy in CRLM. The C-index values of model 1 were 0.759 and 0.773 in the training and validation sets, respectively; the 1-, 3-, and 5-year AUC were 0.808, 0.851, and 0.862 in the training set and 0.850, 0.835, and 0.832 in the validation set, respectively. After stratification by tertiles of the linear predictor in the training set, OS differed significantly among the low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups in both the training and validation sets (log-rank test, all P<0.001). Conclusion: The combined prediction model established by LASSO selection of all baseline variables has a certain predictive value for OS after R0 resection following conversion therapy in CRLM and can provide a quantitative reference for postoperative risk stratification.

articles.title: [Safety and efficacy of the adjustable monitoring filtered type-B transnasal specialized airway catheter in anesthesia for ambulatory gastrointestinal endoscopic surgery in obese patients].
articles.abstract: Objective: To evaluate the clinical safety and efficacy of the adjustable monitoring and filtering type B transnasal specialized airway catheter (hereafter referred to as the adjustable monitoring nasopharyngeal airway) during anesthesia for elective ambulatory gastrointestinal polypectomy under digestive endoscopy in obese patients. Methods: This randomized controlled trial enrolled 92 obese patients (body mass index≥28 kg/m²) scheduled for elective ambulatory gastrointestinal polypectomy under digestive endoscopy at the General Hospital of Northern Theater Command between June and December 2025. Using a random number table, we split the participants evenly into an adjustable airway group (Group R, n=46) and a standard nasal cannula group (Group C, n=46). Anesthesia was inducted and maintained with remimazolam and alfentanil. Patients in Group R were fitted with the adjustable monitoring nasopharyngeal airway for oxygen delivery and end-tidal carbon dioxide (etCO2) monitoring, and Group C received supplemental oxygen through conventional nasal cannula. The primary outcome was defined as the incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia [pulse oximetry saturation(SpO2)<90%]. Secondary outcomes were the variations in respiratory rate, heart rate and mean arterial pressure (MAP) at time points before induction (T0), upon endoscope insertion (T1), 5 minutes post-insertion (T2), at the end of surgery (T3), and 5 minutes after waking up (T4). Additional secondary outcomes included arterial partial pressure of oxygen (PaO₂) and arterial partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PaCO₂) at T2 in both groups, and partial pressure of end-tidal carbon dioxide (PetCO₂) in group R. The duration of endoscopic therapy, dosages of remimazolam and alfentanil, the frequency of hands-on airway interventions, nasal bleeding episodes, and overall physician satisfaction scores were all systematically documented. Results: The baseline demographic and clinical characteristics matched up well between the two groups (all P>0.05). The incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia was significantly lower in group R compared with group C [2.2%(1/46) vs 32.6%(15/46),χ2=14.829,P<0.001]. Patients in Group R exhibited significantly elevated SpO2 levels at T1, T2, and T3 (all P<0.05). At T2, Group R demonstrated significantly higher PaO2 and lower PaCO2 compared to Group C, their heart rates also stayed distinctly lower (P<0.05). MAP remained comparable across both cohorts at every measured interval (P>0.05). Intraoperative PetCO2 values in Group R were consistently maintained within normative physiological parameters, accompanied by continuous and stable monitoring waveforms. Compared with Group C, Group R registered a significantly lower rate of necessity for airway interventions, shorter endoscopic procedure duration and emergence time, lower remimazolam consumption, and highter physician satisfaction (all P<0.05). Conclusions: During anesthesia for elective ambulatory gastrointestinal polypectomy under gastrointestinal endoscopy in obese patients, the adjustable monitoring nasopharyngeal airway directly protects against hypoxemia by improving oxygen delivery and curtails carbon dioxide retention. Concurrently, accurate ventilation tracking helps maintain a highly stable hemodynamic profile, the clinical safety and efficacy of this airway device substantially surpass those of the conventional nasal cannula.

articles.title: [Chinese clinical practice guidelines for transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt in portal hypertension (2026 edition)].
authors: Clinical Guidelines Committee of Chinese College of Interventionalists
articles.abstract: Portal hypertension (PH) is one of the major complications of cirrhosis. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) is a primary therapeutic modality for complications of portal hypertension, including variceal bleeding and refractory ascites, by establishing an intrahepatic channel between the hepatic vein and the portal vein. TIPS also serves as a bridging therapy for patients with decompensated cirrhosis awaiting liver transplantation. In 2019, the Chinese College of Interventionalists (CCI) issued the Chinese Clinical Practice Guidelines for TIPS in portal hypertension, which have played an important role in standardizing TIPS practice in China. With advances in TIPS techniques, evolving treatment concepts, and the emergence of new high-level evidence, the CCI has revised and updated these guidelines. This updated clinical practice guideline was developed by more than 30 Chinese experts in the field of TIPS application, including specialists in interventional radiology, hepatobiliary surgery, hepatology, and gastroenterology. The recommendations are based on latest evidence, supplemented by relevant domestic expert consensuses and high-quality clinical studies. This guideline provides up-to-date recommendations for TIPS treatment of portal hypertension, with the aim of improving the quality of TIPS clinical practice in China.

articles.title: [Risk assessment and clinical strategies of muscle loss in weight loss therapy].
articles.abstract: Obesity is a chronic metabolic disease characterized by excessive fat accumulation, and scientific weight management is pivotal to its prevention and treatment. With the clinical application of novel anti-obesity medications and bariatric surgery, rapid weight loss is often accompanied by muscle loss, which increases the risks of falls and frailty. Clinical assessment should comprehensively evaluate physical function, mobility and quality of life to promptly identify and intervene in muscle loss. Developing multidisciplinary management regimens covering nutrition, exercise, pharmacotherapy and psychological support based on patients' age, baseline muscle function, comorbidities and nutritional status serves as a vital approach to fat loss while preserving muscle mass. In recent years, remarkable progress has been made in the research and development of muscle-protective drugs, offering new strategies for muscle preservation during weight management. Implementing muscle protection strategies throughout the entire weight management process to achieve high-quality weight loss is crucial for improving long-term prognosis of patients with obesity.

articles.title: [Current advances and challenges of artificial intelligence in cervical spine surgery].
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly expanded its applications in medicine, demonstrating potential in imaging analysis, risk prediction, and decision support. Owing to the complexity of disease patterns and the experience-dependent nature of clinical decision-making, AI holds considerable promise in cervical spine surgery. However, most existing studies remain focused on retrospective modeling and technical validation, with limited evidence supporting clinical usability and generalizability. From a clinically driven perspective, this review summarizes the major application scenarios and developmental trends of AI in cervical spine surgery, and highlights key challenges related to causal inference, data quality, multi-center collaboration, and legal and ethical considerations, aiming to provide a rational basis for the standardized application of AI in this field.

articles.title: Association Between Cardiologist Ambulatory Workload and Evidence-Based Therapy for Heart Failure.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Most eligible patients are not prescribed guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF). Increased time pressures for providers in the ambulatory setting may contribute to these shortfalls. We assessed the association between cardiologist ambulatory workload and guideline-directed medical therapy prescription for patients with heart failure with reduced EF.

METHODS: This was a cross-sectional study of patients with heart failure with reduced EF (EF ≤40%) seen by a cardiologist from October 1, 2022, to September 30, 2023, using deidentified administrative and electronic health record data from Optum Labs Data Warehouse, which includes data from multiple health systems across the United States. The primary exposure was ambulatory workload, measured as the average number of visits per day, categorized into quartiles. The primary outcome was "comprehensive quadruple therapy," defined as prescription for all 4 guideline-directed medical therapies: β-blocker; angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor; mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist; and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor. Analyses were conducted using generalized estimating equations, adjusted for demographic and clinical variables.

RESULTS: Overall, 40 173 patients were seen by 881 cardiologists (median ambulatory workload, 9.1 patients per day; interquartile range=5.1-13.0). The percentage of patients prescribed comprehensive quadruple therapy was higher among patients in lower quartiles (quartile 1: 14%; quartile 2: 9.7%; quartile 3: 8.9%; quartile 4: 7.4%; P<0.001). In adjusted analysis, there was a graded association between lower workload quartile and higher odds of comprehensive quadruple therapy, compared with the highest quartile (odds ratio [95% CI], P value=quartile 1: 1.35 [1.09-1.66], 0.008; quartile 2: 1.20 [1.00-1.43], 0.050; quartile 3: 1.11 [0.93-1.32], 0.28; quartile 4 [reference]).

CONCLUSIONS: Seeing a cardiologist with lower ambulatory workload was associated with increased prescribing of guideline-recommended, life-saving therapy in patients with heart failure with reduced EF. Current models that incentivize more visits per day may negatively impact care in the ambulatory setting.

articles.title: Clinical Impact of Multiple-Clip Implantation for Residual Mitral Regurgitation After Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual moderate or greater mitral regurgitation (MR) after transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is strongly associated with adverse clinical outcomes. However, the prognostic impact of implanting additional clips in patients with significant residual MR after the first clip remains uncertain. We evaluated the clinical and echocardiographic outcomes of multiple-clip implantation for significant residual MR following placement of the initial clip.

METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 826 patients with moderate or greater residual MR on intraprocedural transesophageal echocardiography after placement of the first clip during transcatheter edge-to-edge repair at the Cedars-Sinai Medical Center from 2014 to 2023. Patients were categorized into single-clip (n=113) and multiple-clip (n=713) groups. The primary end point was the composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization at 1 year.

RESULTS: Procedural technical success and complication rates were comparable between groups. The multiple-clip group demonstrated greater MR reduction and higher transmitral pressure gradients at discharge, 30 days, and 1 year. At 1 year, the composite end point occurred less frequently in the multiple-clip group than in the single-clip group (16.8% versus 29.2%; P=0.002), along with greater and more sustained improvement in New York Heart Association functional class. In subgroup analyses, multiple-clip implantation consistently reduced major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with moderate as well as moderate-severe/severe residual MR.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with significant residual MR after implanting the first clip, multiple-clip implantation improved MR reduction and 1-year outcomes without increasing complications. Even in moderate residual MR, additional clips were associated with more favorable clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Obese Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate whether GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), compared with DPP4 (dipeptidyl peptidase-4) inhibitors or sulfonylureas, are associated with reduced all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalizations in patients with obesity and type 2 diabetes, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.

METHODS: PRAISE-HFpEF (Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist in Obese Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction) was a nationwide multicenter cohort study using a new-user, active-comparator design within the national Veterans Affairs Health System (170 US hospitals). Adults with type 2 diabetes between January 1, 2000 and December 31, 2021, were identified from centralized electronic health records. Patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and a body mass index ≥30 kg/m2 were selected using a validated diagnostic algorithm. Exposure was initiation of a GLP-1RA versus DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea from January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2021. The primary outcome was time to all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization. Inverse probability of treatment weighting based on the propensity score was used to balanced baseline characteristics.

RESULTS: Among 179 288 patients with type 2 diabetes, obesity, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, 1024 GLP-1RA users and 796 DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea users met inclusion criteria. Over a median follow-up of 1.5 years, GLP-1RA use was associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.78 [95% CI, 0.64-0.95], P=0.01). Weight loss was modestly greater with GLP-1RAs compared with DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea (-12.9% versus -10.1%).

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with obese heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and type 2 diabetes, GLP-1RA initiation was associated with a lower incidence of death or heart failure hospitalization compared with alternative oral agents.

articles.title: Impact of Balloon-Expandable Valve Asymmetry on Heart Failure Post Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fluoroscopic assessment enables immediate evaluation of transcatheter heart valve expansion during transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Whether fluoroscopic asymmetric expansion of balloon-expandable valves is associated with post-TAVR heart failure (HF) remains uncertain.

METHODS: Among 607 consecutive patients undergoing balloon-expandable valve-TAVR in a prospective registry, 589 were analyzed. Valve asymmetry was quantified using a fluoroscopic asymmetry index (%), defined as [(longest/shortest balloon-expandable valve height)-1]×100. The primary end point was 2-year HF hospitalization.

RESULTS: During follow-up, 99 patients (17%) experienced HF hospitalization. As a continuous variable, asymmetry index (%) was not independently associated with 2-year HF (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] per 1% increase, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.98-1.06]). Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated no significant linear or nonlinear association (overall P=0.71; P for nonlinearity=0.89), although the risk curve suggested increased HF risk beyond moderate valve asymmetry. Exploratory threshold analysis identified an asymmetry index cutoff of 7.48%. Patients above this threshold had a higher incidence of HF hospitalization than those below it (23.6% versus 15.8%; log-rank P=0.043), despite comparable rates of impaired valve performance at discharge. Valve asymmetry >7.48% remained independently associated with late HF occurring beyond 30 days after TAVR (adjusted HR, 1.69 [95% CI, 1.10-2.60]).

CONCLUSIONS: Fluoroscopic assessment of balloon-expandable valve expansion identified patients with marked valve asymmetry at increased risk of late HF after TAVR, despite preserved early valve performance. These findings support the potential value of intraprocedural valve geometry assessment for long-term risk stratification and warrant further investigation.

articles.title: National Use Patterns and Comparative Effectiveness of Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Myocardial Infarction-Related Cardiogenic Shock.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) provides bi-ventricular support for patients with myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (MI-CS); comparative effectiveness data relative to other mechanical circulatory support remain limited. We characterize contemporary ECMO utilization for MI-CS and compare short-term mortality across ECMO and non-ECMO treatment strategies.

METHODS: We compared baseline characteristics and temporal trends in mechanical circulatory support utilization among Medicare beneficiaries hospitalized with MI-CS from 2016 to 2023 and treated with ECMO, Impella, intra-aortic balloon pump, or medical management alone. Patient outcomes for each group were evaluated using inverse probability of treatment weighting, G-formula approach, and grace period analysis. The primary endpoint was 30-day all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: The cohort included 102 718 patients: 1165 (1.1%) treated with ECMO, 10 064 (9.8%) Impella, 24 631 (24.0%) intra-aortic balloon pump, and 66 858 (65.1%) medical management alone. From 2016 to 2023, ECMO use for MI-CS increased from 0.8% to 1.8%. The percentage of hospitals using ECMO increased from 9.2% to 17.1%. Unadjusted 30-day mortality was higher for ECMO (69%) compared with Impella (60%), intra-aortic balloon pump (39%), and medical management (46%) (all P<0.0001). Adjusted inverse probability of treatment weighting and G-formula analyses revealed a 30-day mortality rate of 68%-70% for ECMO, which was higher than that for other therapies. The grace period analysis revealed similar mortality between patients treated with ECMO (54%) and Impella (54%).

CONCLUSIONS: ECMO use in a contemporary Medicare cohort of patients with MI-CS was infrequent (1.1%) and associated with high 30-day mortality. Despite use of complementary causal inference methods, we were unable to establish valid causal inferences on ECMO use and patient survival.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Automated Optical Coherence Tomography Analysis for Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Planning: From Plaque Analysis to Precision Lesion Preparation and Stent Optimization.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains the cornerstone of revascularization in coronary artery disease. However, despite advances in stent technology, adverse outcomes related to suboptimal stent placement including under-expansion, malapposition, incomplete coverage, edge dissection, and neoatherosclerosis persist. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) is the highest resolution widely available intravascular imaging modality, allowing unparalleled visualization of stent-vessel interactions and plaque morphology. However, there are significant barriers to large-scale OCT adoption, including time-consuming manual interpretation and dependence on the operator, resulting in significant variability between analysts. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based automated OCT analysis promises to assist PCI by delivering rapid, reproducible, and standardized stent optimization, but current analysis systems lack important features to optimize stent placement. This review summarizes the principles of OCT in PCI, the evidence for OCT-guided optimization, and recent advances in AI-driven automated OCT analysis. We discuss plaque analysis and classification, highlighting how AI-driven automated OCT analysis can identify fibrous, lipid-rich, and calcified lesions and guide tailored lesion preparation using balloons, specialty balloons, drug-coated balloons, intravascular lithotripsy, and atherectomy. We outline emerging AI-enabled workflows for fully automated PCI optimization, evaluate clinical outcomes, interpretability, and workflow integration. Finally, we explore future directions including AI imaging-physiology fusion, multiomics integration, and robotics. If successful, automated AI-empowered OCT analysis could become a central imaging platform for precision PCI, enabling tailored lesion preparation, optimal stent deployment, and improved clinical outcomes in coronary artery disease management.

articles.title: Oral Potassium Supplementation Lowers Clinic Blood Pressure in Untreated Primary Hypertension-Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Potassium may lower blood pressure (BP), but its effect in untreated primary hypertension remains uncertain.

METHODS: We systematically reviewed randomized parallel or crossover trials in adults with untreated primary hypertension comparing oral potassium supplementation with placebo, sodium chloride, or no treatment. The review was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews; CRD42024621287). PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, and trial registries were searched through January 31, 2025 and updated October 1, 2025. End-of-treatment between-group mean differences were pooled using inverse-variance common-effect models; random-effects models were sensitivity analyses. Risk of bias, missing-evidence bias, and certainty were assessed using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, Risk of Bias Due to Missing Evidence, and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation.

RESULTS: Nineteen trials (803 participants; 14 crossover, 5 parallel; median duration, 4 weeks) were included. Potassium reduced clinic systolic BP by 5.3 mm Hg (95% CI, 4.4-6.3) and diastolic BP by 4.5 mm Hg (95% CI, 3.9-5.1). Reductions in 24-hour ambulatory BP were smaller: 2.8 mm Hg (95% CI, 1.3-4.3) systolic and 3.2 mm Hg (95% CI, 2.2-4.2) diastolic. Adverse events were more frequent with potassium (12.8% versus 3.2%), whereas withdrawals and adverse-event withdrawals were uncommon. Heterogeneity was substantial, and ambulatory BP evidence was limited.

CONCLUSIONS: In untreated primary hypertension, oral potassium supplementation modestly reduces clinic BP and may produce smaller reductions in 24-hour ambulatory BP. Heterogeneity, short follow-up, and limited ambulatory and safety data warrant cautious interpretation.

REGISTRATION: URL: PROSPERO; Unique Identifier: CRD42024621287.

articles.title: Efficacy of Stellate Ganglion Block for Preventing Postoperative Atrial Fibrillation After Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stellate ganglion block (SGB) may reduce postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) by modulating the autonomic nervous system. This study evaluated the efficacy of preoperative SGB in preventing POAF following cardiac surgery.

METHODS: In this single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 140 patients undergoing valve surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass were assigned (1:1) to ultrasound-guided right SGB with 7 mL of 0.5% ropivacaine or 7 mL of normal saline. The primary outcome was the incidence of POAF from postoperative day 0 to day 7 or until discharge.

RESULTS: A total of 132 patients completed the study and were included in the modified intention-to-treat population (SGB group: n=65; saline group: n=67). POAF occurred in 43% of the SGB group and 40% of the saline group (odds ratio [OR], 0.99 [95% CI, 0.46-2.15], adjusted P=0.989). The SGB group demonstrated a lower incidence of intraoperative ventricular fibrillation/ventricular tachycardia requiring defibrillation after aortic cross-clamp release (6% versus 19%; OR, 0.21 [95% CI, 0.06-0.80]; adjusted P=0.022), lower postoperative high-sensitivity troponin I levels (median difference: -2562 ng/L [95% CI, -4301 to -45]; P=0.045), and a reduced risk of postoperative acute kidney injury (5% versus 18%; OR, 0.24 [95% CI, 0.06-0.98]; adjusted P=0.046).

CONCLUSIONS: While preoperative SGB did not reduce the incidence of POAF, it was associated with potential benefits, including a lower requirement for intraoperative defibrillation attributable to ventricular arrhythmias, attenuated myocardial injury (as indicated by lower high-sensitivity troponin I levels), and a decreased risk of postoperative acute kidney injury.

articles.title: Rationale and Design of a Parallel Randomized Trial of a DASH-Enhanced Portfolio Diet With or Without Ultra-Processed Plant Proteins for Blood Pressure and Other Cardiometabolic Risk Factors in Adults With Hypertension and Obesity: The Substitution of High With Low Ultra-Processed Soy Protein Foods in a Guideline-Based Diet Intervention on Cardiometabolic Health Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death and hospitalization globally. Clinical practice guidelines recommend various plant-based dietary patterns that target specific cardiometabolic risk factors, including the Dietary Approach to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet for blood pressure and the Portfolio diet for low-density lipoprotein cholesterol. Combining key elements of these patterns may enhance cardiovascular disease risk reduction. However, many soy-based products, a key Portfolio component, are classified as ultra-processed foods (UPFs). This trial will answer 2 questions: (1) Does a DASH-enhanced Portfolio diet result in clinically meaningful reductions in blood pressure compared with standard of care and (2) Is a high-UPF noninferior to a low-UPF soy protein-containing DASH-enhanced Portfolio diet for blood pressure reduction?

METHODS: The SWITCH (Substitution of High With Low Ultra-Processed Soy Protein Foods in a Guideline-Based Diet Intervention for Cardiometabolic Health) trial is a parallel, randomized, 3-arm, open-label, superiority-noninferiority trial. Three hundred adults with hypertension and obesity, including 50% with type 2 diabetes, will be randomized to a high-UPF or low-UPF soy protein-containing DASH-enhanced Portfolio diet or standard of care for 12 weeks. The primary outcome is systolic blood pressure. Key secondary outcomes are non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol and body weight. Other outcomes include cardiometabolic risk factors.

CONCLUSIONS: Findings will provide high-quality evidence on the use of a DASH-enhanced Portfolio diet and the role of nutrient-dense soy foods classified as UPFs within the combination of the 2 guideline-based dietary patterns to support dietary strategies for cardiometabolic risk reduction.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/; Unique identifier: NCT06907862.

articles.title: Correlation of the Distressed Communities Index Score With Cardiovascular Risk Factors and Disease in the United States.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of morbidity and death worldwide. Risk scores such as the pooled cohort equations often underpredict risk in individuals with low socioeconomic status.

METHODS: We used the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Population Level Analysis and Community Estimates data set to obtain zip code-level prevalence of hypertension, obesity, stroke, diabetes, and coronary artery disease. The Distressed Communities Index (DCI) collates community socioeconomic status and social determinants/drivers of health metrics into a numerical score. Linear regression adjusted for region and rurality assessed associations between DCI and CVD prevalence.

RESULTS: We included 26 058 US zip codes (2016-2020). The median DCI was 50.9 (interquartile range, 25.4-75.9). Each 1-unit increase in DCI was associated with increased prevalence of obesity (β=0.10 [95% CI, 0.09-0.10]), hypertension (β=0.08 [95% CI, 0.08-0.09]), diabetes (β=0.06 [95% CI, 0.06-0.06]), coronary artery disease (β=0.03 [95% CI, 0.03-0.03]), and stroke (β=0.02 [95% CI, 0.02-0.02]; all P<0.001). Rurality and region were independently associated with CVD and risk factor prevalence, with rural and southern zip codes having the highest prevalence.

CONCLUSIONS: DCI, geographic region, and rurality are independently associated with greater prevalence of CVD and its risk factors in the United States. The DCI is a practical, scalable surrogate for socioeconomic status and social determinants/drivers of health that may enhance CVD risk stratification on the basis of an area's economic resilience or disadvantage. Using DCI with the Preventing Cardiovascular Events score may capture economic and social challenges it omits, warranting further study.

articles.title: Sudden Cardiac Death in Firefighters From the United States: A 16-Year Postmortem Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sudden cardiac death (SCD) is the leading cause of duty-related death among firefighters. Understanding postmortem cardiovascular abnormalities associated with SCD is critical to guiding fire service cardiovascular disease screening and prevention programs.

METHODS: This study included US firefighters who had a duty-related death over a 16-year period (1999-2014) with available postmortem reports (autopsy/medical examiner reports). Cases were systematically reviewed to identify cases of SCD. For each SCD case, the primary etiology of SCD was adjudicated by experts in sports cardiology and cardiovascular pathology.

RESULTS: Postmortem evaluations were available for 794 of 2100 (37.8%) on-duty firefighter deaths over the study period (average age, 44±13 years; age range, 17-82 years; 4.0% women). A total of 312 of 794 (39.3%) firefighter deaths were adjudicated as SCD. A total of 255 of 312 (81.8%) SCD events were attributable to coronary artery disease/ischemic heart disease or hypertensive heart disease, which both are associated with traditional cardiovascular risk factors. The leading etiology of SCD among young firefighters (aged <40 years) was also coronary artery disease/ischemic heart disease (24/50 [48.0%]). Of firefighters who had an exertional SCD event thought to be secondary to coronary artery disease (n=97), a total of 62 of 91 (68.1%) had severe fixed coronary stenosis, while 29 of 91 (31.9%) demonstrated acute plaque rupture/thrombosis.

CONCLUSIONS: More than 80% of on-duty SCD events among US firefighters are due to coronary artery disease and hypertensive heart disease that may be prevented by early disease identification and risk factor modification. Future studies should assess the efficacy of more rigorous firefighter cardiovascular disease screening and management practices.

articles.title: Auxiliary BKβ4 subunits promote nanoscale coupling between BK and voltage-gated calcium channels.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Intracellular Ca2+ signals are essential for many cellular processes but must be tightly regulated to ensure precise spatial and temporal control. The large conductance calcium- and voltage-activated K+ channel (BK) integrates intracellular Ca2+ signaling and membrane depolarization to generate hyperpolarizing K+ currents that regulate membrane excitability. In many cell types, BK channels achieve rapid activation through functional coupling with voltage-gated calcium (CaV) channels that provide localized Ca2+ signals. However, the mechanisms that regulate the nanoscale organization of BK+CaV channel complexes remain poorly understood. Here we investigated whether the BK auxiliary subunit β4 (BKβ4), which is widely expressed throughout the brain and modulates BK gating properties, influences the spatial organization and functional coupling of BK and CaV channels. Using proximity ligation assays, electrophysiology, and superresolution stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we show that BKβ4 promotes BK+CaV nanodomain organization by increasing channel clustering and altering their spatial proximity at the plasma membrane. These structural changes enhance functional coupling between Ca2+ influx and BK channel activation. Notably, the effects of BKβ4 on nanodomain organization and coupling depend on the CaV subtype involved. Together, our findings reveal that the BKβ4 auxiliary subunit regulates the nanoscale architecture of BK+CaV channel complexes and thereby modulates their functional interaction.

articles.title: Septin binding restricts Shigella growth and triggers intracellular tolerance.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Pathogen survival relies on their ability to adapt to changing environments, yet how intracellular bacteria tolerate cell-autonomous immunity remains unclear. Septins assemble into cage-like structures around cytoplasmic Shigella targeted by autophagy, but their antibacterial activity was unknown. Using advanced microscopy and cell-free reconstitution, we show that septins polymerize into circumferentially oriented filaments that inhibit bacterial growth. RNA-sequencing reveals that septin binding to Shigella upregulates type III secretion system (T3SS) effectors and triggers a stress response. Underlying this, septin-bound Shigella possess hyperpolarized membranes, but without lethally damaged cell envelope. We show that exposure to septin binding enhances the impact of the cell envelope-targeting antibiotic polymyxin B. During infection, T3SS effector OspC1 prevents septin recruitment, while stress-response regulator cspC protects against septin-mediated changes to membrane potential. Hence, septin binding is intrinsically antibacterial and is sensed by Shigella as a danger signal to promote mechanisms of intracellular tolerance.

articles.title: Pancreatic δ cells are resistant to auto- and paracrine inhibition in human type-2 diabetes.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Somatostatin secretion from pancreatic δ cells inhibits nearby α- and β cells and tunes the body's glycemic set-point. The role of δ cells in diabetes remains unclear, in part due to the difficulty separating intrinsic regulation from intraislet paracrine effects. Here, we compared the function of isolated δ cells of cadaveric nondiabetic and type-2 diabetic donors by single cell total internal reflection microscopy, electrophysiology, and secretion measurements. Elevated glucose stimulated exocytosis of somatostatin, which was further amplified by glucagon, exendin-4, or forskolin, independent of diabetic status. gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) enhanced exocytosis and electrical activity, while insulin had no detectable effect. Adrenaline and somatostatin strongly inhibited δ cell activity, leading to autocrine feedback inhibition of somatostatin exocytosis. In type-2 diabetes, δ cell inhibition by somatostatin and adrenaline was impaired, together with a marked reduction in somatostatin receptor (SSTR2) surface expression. The data suggest that selective loss of inhibitory control of δ cells may dysregulate intraislet somatostatin signaling in type-2 diabetes.

articles.title: A voltage-gated porin PPE1 regulates secretion and drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) remains a formidable clinical hurdle, compounded by the fact that the pathways by which antibiotics penetrate its multilayered cell envelope remain incompletely mapped.
