We identify PPE1 as a voltage-gated outer-membrane porin that mediates the secretion of kupyaphores while also facilitating the uptake of the frontline anti-tubercular drug isoniazid (INH). Genome-wide association analysis of 38,038 clinical isolates links ppe1 mutations with INH resistance, highlighting its clinical relevance. Consistent with this, the Mtb Δppe1 mutant shows increased tolerance to INH, accompanied by markedly reduced intracellular accumulation of INH compared with the wild-type strain. The Δppe1 strain exhibits attenuated infection, impaired growth, and reduced virulence in a murine infection model. Electron microscopy, molecular modeling, and single-channel electrophysiology reveal that PPE1 assembles into an unusual pentameric α-helical channel, distinct from classical β-barrel bacterial porins. Together, our findings identify PPE1 as a key determinant of mycobacterial membrane permeability that coordinates metallophore secretion and also antibiotic influx. This work uncovers a previously unrecognized mechanism governing Mtb physiology, virulence, and drug susceptibility, providing a potential target for therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: Hepatitis C viral variants bear signatures of de novo CD8+ T cell and antibody pressure after spontaneous postpartum viral suppression.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Progression to chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection entails loss of HCV-specific CD4+ T cell help, emergence of viral variants that escape recognition by CD8+ T cells and neutralizing antibodies, and exhaustion of CD8+ T cells targeting remaining intact epitopes. Once chronic infection has been established, it is generally lifelong without treatment. However, in some chronically infected women, a surprising postpartum viral load decline has been linked to resurgent functional HCV-specific CD4+ helper T cells. A minority of women even spontaneously clear long-standing chronic infection postpartum. To test whether restored T cell help boosts HCV-specific CD8+ T cell or antibody responses in women with postpartum viral control, we performed serial near-full-length deep sequencing of HCV genomes to assess evolution of viral MHC class I epitopes and antibody epitopes in nine women with significant postpartum viral declines (≥ 1 log10 at 3 mo postpartum, "controllers") and 12 with more stable levels ("noncontrollers"). Although not associated with mutations arising early postpartum, at 12 to 24 mo postpartum, viral control was strongly associated with amino acid mutations in epitopes predicted to be targeted by CD8+ T cells and neutralizing antibodies. Plasma from controllers also demonstrated a postpartum increase in neutralization of multiple HCV strains. Together, these findings support the hypothesis that postpartum viral control is mediated by CD8+ T cell and antibody pressure.

articles.title: Revised estimates of types and duration of long COVID symptoms based on claims records from 245 million US patients.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: COVID-19 has been reported to cause multisystem effects lasting years [Z. Al-Aly, E. Topol, Science 383, 830-832 (2024)]. These findings are primarily based on cohort studies comparing test-positive COVID-19 patients to controls without known COVID-19 infection, tested or untested [M. Cai, Y. Xie, E. J. Topol, Z. Al-Aly, Nat. Med. 30, 1564-1573 (2024)]. However, such comparisons can be biased by the reasons people were tested. Using 14.4 billion insurance claims from 244.7 million US patients, we find that most long-term effects attributed to COVID-19 by unrestricted control designs likely reflect bias due to selective testing of individuals with non-COVID conditions, causing long-term effects of those conditions to be misattributed to COVID-19. We removed this bias by analyzing only tested individuals, comparing test-positive to test-negative patients. Across 614 clinical outcomes followed over 2 y, the test-based design resulted in 83.5% fewer symptoms being attributable to COVID-19 between 30 to 119 d after infection (43 attributable symptoms vs. 262 for the unrestricted control design), a 98.2% reduction at 120 to 359 d (5 vs. 286), and a 100% reduction at 360 to 719 d (0 vs. 369). The unrestricted control design also attributed unrelated outcomes (e.g., firearm injuries) to COVID-19 at a high rate, whereas the testing-based design did not. The test-based control design may modestly underestimate some effects. This study does not indicate that symptoms beyond one year are not genuine but that their attributability to COVID-19 is uncertain.

articles.title: Oral Maintenance Anti-Hypertensives for Severe Systolic Hypertension: A Controlled Before-and-After Quality Improvement Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: A systolic blood pressure (SBP) threshold ≥ 160 mm Hg is used in pregnancy for acute antihypertensive treatment; however, this was initially adapted from expert opinion, and guidelines for nonpregnant adults support an SBP ≥ 180 mm Hg. We compared adverse maternal outcomes using a SBP threshold of ≥ 180 mm Hg versus ≥ 160 mm Hg for acute anti-hypertensive treatment, while treating SBPs between 160 and 179 mm Hg (diastolic blood pressure [DBP] < 110) with oral maintenance anti-hypertensives.

STUDY DESIGN: We performed a quality improvement before-and-after noninferiority study (NCT05881252) of singletons ≥ 20 weeks' with SBP ≥ 160 mm Hg at a single level 4 medical center. In the before group, acute antihypertensives (intravenous [IV] labetalol/hydralazine or rapid-acting oral nifedipine) were given for persistent SBP ≥ 160 mm Hg (or DBP ≥ 110). In the after group, oral maintenance antihypertensives (labetalol or extended-release nifedipine) were given if persistent SBP was between 160 and 179 mm Hg (DBP < 110) and acute antihypertensives for persistent SBP ≥ 180 mm Hg (or DBP ≥ 110). The primary outcome was a composite of congestive heart failure, pulmonary edema, cerebrovascular accident, acute kidney injury, or myocardial infarction. Bayesian analysis was performed using a noninferiority margin of 4 and 1% (post hoc sensitivity analysis).

RESULTS: We studied 1,002 individuals (410 in before; 592 in after) with severe hypertension. The primary outcome occurred in 2.9% of the before group and 1.9% of the after group (0.72: median relative risk, 95% credible interval: 0.36-1.46), with an 82% probability of risk reduction in the after group and > 99.9% probability that the risk difference in the after group was < 4% (99% for a 1% margin). Use of acute antihypertensives per individual treated decreased almost threefold in the after group (mean: 1.7 doses vs. 0.6, p < 0.01).

CONCLUSION: In our population, treating SBPs between 160 and 180 mm Hg with oral maintenance antihypertensives resulted in a noninferior rate of maternal adverse outcomes and decreased the use of IV/rapid acting medication.

articles.title: Propagating shocks and transitions across networked food systems: Insights from multiplayer microeconomic modeling.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Accelerating global change is affecting coupled natural ecosystems and human activities in every part of the world. The local and regional expressions of these changes are a product of interacting and networked systems such that a shock, trend or development transition in one region, ecosystem, or sector can propagate impacts to other regions, ecosystems, and sectors. Informed adaptation and development strategies require an understanding of how signals propagate through these coupled systems and regions. Here, we synthesize findings from our work in Ethiopia and Mali, where we developed and applied a modeling system designed to capture cross-sector dynamics of networked food, water, and energy systems at subnational scale. We approach the problem using a multiplayer microeconomic model that accounts for diverse objectives through chains of food production, distribution, and consumption that connect resource regions to market regions. This paper draws lessons from three case studies in Ethiopia and one in Mali that are designed to examine impacts of a subnational climate shock (drought), a centralized national policy decision (export restrictions in response to food shortage), a distributed development strategy (solar-powered groundwater irrigation), and an external intervention (food aid). In each case, we consider how an initial signal propagates through the country via markets, infrastructure, and interactions between economic actors. An understanding of this propagation can inform strategies for food security in a changing climate.

articles.title: circEPSTI1 regulates miR-942-5p-SERPINE1-AKT1 signaling axis to enhance dengue infection and is suppressed by Tiplaxtinin.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have recently been identified as crucial regulators of gene expression in various diseases. Their role in dengue remains unexplored. In this study, circEPSTI1 induction was observed in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and plasma of dengue patients. The induction of circEPSTI1 is interferon-dependent and enhances DENV infection by sponging the expression of miR-942-5p. The antiviral role of miR-942-5p is mediated by bidirectional inhibition through targeting conserved genomic sequences of the DENV genome of different subtypes across NS1, NS3, and NS5 and the host AKT1 signaling pathway. RNA-seq analysis of DENV-infected circEPSTI1 knockdown A549 cells identified SERPINE1 and AKT1 signaling pathways to be dysregulated significantly. circEPSTI1 relieves the inhibition of miR-942-5p over DENV genomic RNA and the host SERPINE1 to activate AKT1 signaling. The activation of AKT1 signaling facilitates cell survival and enhances DENV replication. The expression of SERPINE1 and circEPSTI1 was upregulated in Dengue patients, and pharmaceutical inhibition of SERPINE1 through Tiplaxtinin inhibits the DENV replication by reducing the expression of circEPSTI1. Overall, our result demonstrates the therapeutic potential of Tiplaxtinin by targeting the circEPSTI1-miR-942-5p-SERPINE1-AKT1 axis in dengue treatment.

articles.title: Phylogenomics of Cypriniformes, the most diverse order of freshwater fishes: consensus, challenges, and limitations.
articles.abstract: Cypriniformes, the most species-rich order of freshwater fishes (∼5,000 species), represents a key lineage for understanding vertebrate diversification in freshwater ecosystems. This clade includes several highly miniaturized and understudied lineages whose phylogenetic placements have long remained contentious. Here, we present the first phylogenomic analysis of Cypriniformes with complete family-level representation and broad genus-level coverage, encompassing 316 species comprising ∼30% of all described genera. Our dataset integrates 257 newly assembled genomes with publicly available resources and analyzes multiple sets of genome-wide markers using both concatenation-based and coalescent-aware approaches. The general concordance among analytical frameworks indicates that the backbone topology of Cypriniformes is now established, allowing clear identification of well-supported clades and regions of persistent conflict. Our results strengthen the evolutionary relationships of several miniaturized lineages, while identifying recalcitrant relationships shaped by both biological processes and model artifacts that can yield superficially similar patterns of phylogenetic conflict. Our study substantially expands genomic representation and establishes a phylogenomic foundation for future comparative, developmental, and evolutionary research in this freshwater radiation.

articles.title: Epidemiological, etiological, and antifungal resistance patterns of vulvovaginal Candida spp. infections in Cameroon: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Vulvovaginal candidiasis is a common fungal infection, mainly due to Candida species, affecting two-thirds of women globally at least once in their lifetime. Here, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO ID: CRD420261368975) of the epidemiology, aetiology, and drug resistance profiles of vulvovaginal Candida infections and vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC) in Cameroon. Databases were queried to identify all eligible papers. Data were extracted, and the methodological quality of studies was assessed. Random-effect models were used to estimate pooled proportions of primary outcomes. Thirty-four studies were included. The pooled proportions of vulvovaginal Candida infections and VVC were 33.3% (Confidence interval at 95% (95% CI) 25.5%-41.6%, P < .0001) and 31.6% (95% CI 26.9%-36.4%, P < .0001), respectively. Candida albicans (23.3%, 95% CI 17.9%-29.1%, P < .0001) was the most frequently isolated causative species, followed by Nakaseomyces glabratus (formerly C. glabrata) (2.3%, 95% CI 0.9%-4.2%, P < .0001) and Pichia kudriavzevii (formerly C. krusei) (1.3%, 95% CI 0.5%-2.5%, P < .0001). Pregnancy status, diagnostic methods, and human immunodeficiency virus infection influenced the proportions of these species. Two primary azoles were least effective against C. albicans, with the following resistance levels: fluconazole (51.1%, 95% CI 21.2%-80.7%, P < .0001) and itraconazole (50.5%, 95% CI 41.3%-100%, P < .0001). Evidence of drug profiles for non-albicans species is limited. The findings highlight the substantial burden of VVC, the predominance of C. albicans, and high azole resistance in Cameroon. They underscore the need for standardised diagnostic approaches, broader epidemiological surveillance, and evidence-based preventive strategies.

articles.title: Shared Genetic Architecture Between Mental Disorders and Heart Failure Subtypes: A Comprehensive Multitrait Genome-Wide Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mental disorders and heart failure frequently co-occur, but their shared genetic architecture remains incompletely understood.

METHODS: Prospective Cox regression analysis in the UK Biobank (UKB) quantified the risk of incident heart failure associated with mental disorders. Linkage disequilibrium score regression estimated genetic correlations, while multitrait genome-wide association and cross-phenotype association analyses identified candidate pleiotropic loci. Statistical fine mapping and gene-level association analyses prioritized candidate variants and genes. Bayesian colocalization assessed evidence for shared candidate variants, and exploratory Gene Ontology biological-process overrepresentation analysis provided descriptive biological context. Single-cell RNA sequencing and genetically informed spatial mapping (gsMap) provided cellular and spatial context for prioritized genes. Geneformer-based in silico perturbation analysis was performed using a cardiac cell atlas of dilated cardiomyopathy to prioritize candidate pleiotropic genes and identify cardiac cell states showing predicted embedding shifts.

RESULTS: Prospective UKB analyses demonstrated that mental disorders, such as posttraumatic stress disorder, depression, and bipolar disorder, were associated with a higher risk of incident heart failure. Multitrait analysis identified 607 pleiotropic variants, with fine-mapping and colocalization converging on prioritized candidate loci, including TMEM18, NKX2-2, and XRN2. Single-cell expression profiling and spatial mapping provided context at the cellular and tissue levels for the prioritized genes. Geneformer-based in silico perturbation prioritized FOXP1 and TMEM106B as leading pleiotropic candidate genes on the basis of their predicted changes in downstream gene embeddings in cardiac cellular contexts.

CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies shared genetic architecture between mental disorders and heart failure and prioritizes candidate pleiotropic genes associated with both. Transcriptomic and in silico perturbation analyses provide exploratory cellular, spatial, and cardiac functional context. Functional validation is required before mechanistic or therapeutic interpretation.

articles.title: Physical Activity and Cardiovascular Risk in Type 2 Diabetes With Normal Body Mass Index and Abdominal Obesity: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic implications of abdominal obesity and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) in patients with type 2 diabetes who have a normal body mass index remain unclear.

METHODS: This nationwide retrospective cohort study included 323 029 adults with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes and a normal body mass index (<23 kg/m2) between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2023, from the Korean National Health Insurance Service database. Abdominal obesity was defined using sex-specific waist circumference thresholds (≥90 cm for men, ≥80 cm for women). MVPA was assessed through standardized self-reported questionnaires administered during routine health screenings. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events, defined as a composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, or hospitalization for heart failure.

RESULTS: Among the study population, 34 033 (10.5%) had abdominal obesity. During a median follow-up of 6.0 years (interquartile range, 2.6-9.0 years), abdominal obesity was associated with a higher risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 1.13 [95% CI, 1.09-1.17]). Among patients with abdominal obesity, regular MVPA after diagnosis (27.1%) was associated with a significantly lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (adjusted HR 0.74 [95% CI, 0.68-0.80]), all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.72 [95% CI, 0.65-0.80]), ischemic stroke (adjusted HR 0.77 [95% CI, 0.66-0.89]), and hospitalization for heart failure (adjusted HR 0.75 [95% CI, 0.60-0.93]). The cardiovascular protective effects of MVPA were consistent regardless of statin or antidiabetic medication use.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with type 2 diabetes and a normal body mass index, abdominal obesity was independently associated with a higher risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events. Regular engagement in MVPA showed consistent cardiovascular benefits in this population, irrespective of pharmacotherapy.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT07071545.

articles.title: Not All Strokes Are Equal: Phenotype-Dependent Surgical Timing in Infective Endocarditis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We evaluated postoperative neurologic and mortality outcomes by stroke-to-surgery timing and stroke phenotype in patients with left-sided infective endocarditis.

METHODS: Adult patients undergoing surgery for infective endocarditis complicated by preoperative stroke between 2004 and 2024 at 2 institutions were stratified by stroke-to-surgery interval (<1 week, 1-4 weeks, 4-6 weeks). The primary outcome was a composite postoperative cerebrovascular event: new stroke, enlarging stroke, or hemorrhagic conversion. Secondary outcomes were operative death and major morbidity events.

RESULTS: Among 2265 patients with left-sided infective endocarditis, 322 met inclusion criteria, of whom 122 (38%) underwent surgery within 1 week, 168 (52%) between 1 and 4 weeks, and 32 (10%) between 4 and 6 weeks. Operative death was similar across groups (P=0.09). Postoperative cerebrovascular events declined with time (<1 week, 21.3%; 1-4 weeks, 11.9%; 4-6 weeks, 9.4%; P=0.015). On multivariable analysis, longer stroke-to-surgery interval was associated with reduced odds of postoperative cerebrovascular events (odds ratio, 0.92/d [95% CI, 0.85-0.98]; P=0.015), driven by early events among patients with intraparenchymal hemorrhage, subarachnoid hemorrhage, and septic emboli. Among ischemic strokes, operative death was lowest with surgery within 1 week (5.8% versus 11.2% at 1-4 weeks; P=0.24). Interval embolization occurred in 10.6% of patients awaiting surgery, most commonly affecting the spleen and kidneys.

CONCLUSIONS: Excess postoperative neurologic risk was concentrated within the first 7 to 10 days and driven by intraparenchymal hemorrhage, subarachnoid hemorrhage, and septic emboli; ischemic stroke showed no appreciable temporal association. Routine delay after ischemic stroke may not be necessary, while a short delay (≈7 days) for hemorrhagic and septic embolic subtypes may be reasonable when hemodynamically feasible.

articles.title: Residual Risk From Remnant Cholesterol and Inflammation Despite Lipid-Lowering Therapy and Association With Incident Peripheral Artery Disease in Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite guideline-recommended lipid-lowering therapy, patients with type 2 diabetes retain a significant residual risk for peripheral artery disease (PAD). The contributions of remnant cholesterol (RC) and systemic inflammation in this treated population, particularly beyond achieved low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, remain incompletely understood.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 18 741 participants with type 2 diabetes from the UK Biobank who were free of PAD and were on lipid-lowering therapy at baseline. Plasma RC and hsCRP (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein) levels were measured at baseline. Incident PAD was ascertained over a median follow-up of 13.6 years. Multivariable Cox models were used to estimate hazard ratios after adjustment for demographic, clinical, metabolic, and treatment-related covariates, including low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and baseline coronary artery disease.

RESULTS: During follow-up, incident PAD occurred in 1223 participants (6.5%). Elevated RC and hsCRP levels were each independently linked to an increased risk of PAD. Participants with concurrent elevations in both RC and hsCRP exhibited the highest risk of incident PAD. These associations remained robust across multiple sensitivity analyses, including exclusion of participants with baseline coronary artery disease, removal of events within the initial 2-year follow-up, elimination of individuals with hsCRP >10 mg/L, competing-risk analyses accounting for death, and further adjustment for detailed lipid-lowering therapy categories.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with type 2 diabetes receiving lipid-lowering therapy for primary prevention of PAD, elevated RC and systemic inflammation are independently and jointly associated with future PAD risk. These findings highlight substantial residual risk beyond managed low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and support the need for further strategies targeting both remnant lipoproteins and inflammation in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Sex Differences in the Associations of Age-Related Genetic Predisposition With Incident Atrial Fibrillation: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polygenic risks for diseases are age-dependent. However, sex differences in the age-related association between polygenic risk score and incident atrial fibrillation (AF) remain unclear.

METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted using UK Biobank data, including 386 154 participants aged 40 to 69 years, with a median follow-up of 15.6 years. High AF polygenic risk score was defined as ≥0.858 (top quintile). Cox regression, 10-fold cross-validated C-statistic, Royston's R2, and population-attributable risk percentages were used to evaluate sex- and age-specific genetic effects on incident AF.

RESULTS: High polygenic risk score was significantly associated with incident AF, and continuous-age analyses showed that the age-related trajectories differed across sexes (P for difference in age-related trajectories=0.005). In age-stratified analyses, the association was numerically higher in men aged 40 to 49 years (hazard ratio [HR], 2.76 versus 2.07 in women; Bonferroni-adjusted P for interaction=0.077), whereas it was higher in women aged 60 to 69 years (HR, 2.22 versus 1.95 in men; Bonferroni-adjusted P for interaction <0.001). Cross-validated prediction analyses showed broadly similar age- and sex-specific patterns. Population-attributable risk of high polygenic risk score gradually declined across age strata in men, whereas it first increased and then decreased in women.

CONCLUSIONS: Age-related genetic predisposition to AF exhibits distinct sex-specific patterns, offering a foundation for personalized risk stratification and prevention strategies tailored to age and sex.

articles.title: Outcomes of Intra-Arterial Urokinase After Endovascular Reperfusion for Acute Ischemic Stroke Due to Cardioembolism: A Secondary Analysis of the POST-UK Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether adjunctive intra-arterial thrombolysis improves outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of adjunctive intra-arterial urokinase in patients with acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism who achieved near-complete to complete reperfusion.

METHODS: This study was a secondary analysis of the POST-UK (Adjunctive Intra-Arterial Urokinase After Near-Complete to Complete Reperfusion for Acute Ischemic Stroke) trial, which was conducted from November 15, 2022, to March 29, 2024. Patients were randomly assigned to the intra-arterial urokinase group or the control group. The primary outcome was disability-free survival at 90 days, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 1. Safety outcomes included 90-day all-cause death, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage and any intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours.

RESULTS: Among 209 patients with cardioembolism (median age 73 [interquartile range, 63-81] years; 45.9% men), 106 were assigned to the control group and 103 to the intra-arterial urokinase group. Compared with the control group, adjunctive intra-arterial urokinase significantly increased the odds of disability-free survival at 90 days (adjusted risk ratio, 1.49 [95% CI, 1.08-2.06]; P=0.01; inverse probability of treatment weighting adjusted risk ratio, 1.47 [95% CI, 1.04-2.09]; P=0.03). No significant differences were found between groups in 90-day mortality rate, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, or any intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism who achieved near-complete to complete reperfusion, adjunctive intra-arterial urokinase significantly improved disability-free survival at 90 days without increasing the risk of death or intracranial hemorrhage.

REGISTRATION: URL: ChiCTR.org.cn; Unique identifier: ChiCTR2200065617.

articles.title: Thioredoxin-Interacting Protein-Regulated in Development and DNA Damage-Response 1-Driven Macrophage Senescence Promotes Hypoxia-Induced Pulmonary Hypertension.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a life-threatening vascular disorder characterized by pulmonary arterial remodeling and right ventricular failure, posing a significant clinical challenge. Although macrophage dysfunction is implicated in PH pathogenesis, its underlying molecular mechanisms remain elusive.

METHODS: We employed multiomics database analysis, cross-species validation, and functional studies in hypoxia-induced PH models. Myeloid-specific Txnip deletion was achieved via bone marrow transplantation in mice. Mechanistic insights were evaluated through protein-binding assays, cellular senescence analyses in bone marrow-derived macrophages, and co-culture experiments with pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells.

RESULTS: We identified that cellular senescence in pulmonary adventitial macrophages was involved in the pathogenesis of hypoxia-induced PH. Integrated multiomics analysis revealed elevated TXNIP (thioredoxin-interacting protein) expression in perivascular macrophages during hypoxia-induced PH. Myeloid-specific Txnip deletion attenuated hypoxia-induced pulmonary vascular remodeling in mice. Mechanistically, TXNIP binds to and stabilizes the REDD1 (regulated in development and DNA damage-response 1) protein, promoting hypoxia-induced senescence in bone marrow-derived macrophages. Conditioned medium from senescent macrophages subsequently enhanced the proliferation and migration of pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells.

CONCLUSIONS: The TXNIP-REDD1 axis drives hypoxia-induced macrophage senescence, which promotes pulmonary artery smooth muscle cell dysfunction and pulmonary vascular remodeling in hypoxia-induced PH. Targeting the TXNIP-REDD1 pathway may provide a novel therapeutic strategy for hypoxia-induced PH.

articles.title: Lipoprotein(a) and Risk Stratification for Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease Across the Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Continuum.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lp(a) (lipoprotein(a)) is an established risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), but its prognostic relevance across the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) continuum remains uncertain. We examined whether Lp(a) was associated with incident ASCVD across CKM stages and whether it provided complementary risk stratification beyond CKM staging.

METHODS: We included 333 321 UK Biobank participants free of clinical cardiovascular disease at baseline and classified them into CKM stages 0 to 3. Elevated Lp(a) was defined as ≥125 nmol/L. The primary outcome was incident ASCVD, defined as coronary artery disease or ischemic stroke. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs), and 10-year absolute risks were estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 15.3 years, 17 581 incident ASCVD events occurred. After adjustment for demographic characteristics, socioeconomic factors, lifestyle factors, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, medications, and CKM stage, elevated Lp(a) was associated with higher ASCVD risk (HR, 1.31 [95% CI, 1.25-1.36]). In joint analyses, risk increased progressively across combined CKM-Lp(a) categories, with the highest risk observed in participants with CKM stage 3 and elevated Lp(a) versus CKM stage 0 and lower Lp(a) (HR, 3.43 [95% CI, 2.74-4.31]). Ten-year ASCVD risk ranged from 0.64% to 16.30%, and the absolute risk difference associated with elevated Lp(a) increased from 0.23% in stage 0 to 2.20% in stage 3.

CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) was associated with higher incident ASCVD risk across the CKM continuum. Although relative associations were broadly consistent across CKM stages, absolute risk increments associated with elevated Lp(a) were greater at more advanced CKM stages, supporting the integration of Lp(a) into CKM-based risk stratification for primary prevention.

articles.title: Role of Plasma Proteins in the Association Between Socioeconomic Status and Cardiovascular Disease Events: Results From Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine Cohorts.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Socioeconomic status (SES) is strongly associated with cardiovascular disease burden and risk. Plasma proteins may elucidate a biological mechanism through which low SES increases the risk of cardiovascular disease.

METHODS: Participants from the following 3 cohorts were included: the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (n=2139), Jackson Heart Study (n=967), and Women's Health Initiative (n=1104). SES was approximated using a cumulative score (range 0-3) across education, income, and employment status. A meta-analysis of Cox proportional hazards ratios was used to assess the association between SES and incident events for coronary heart disease (CHD) and stroke. Linear regression was used within each cohort to determine associations between SES and Olink proteins (n=1270 proteins) and the results were meta-analyzed across cohorts. Regression-based mediation analysis was used to determine whether the identified proteins were statistical mediators of the association of SES and incident events.

RESULTS: Higher SES scores were associated with a lower risk of CHD (hazard ratio [HR], 0.74 [95% CI, 0.63-0.87]) and stroke (HR, 0.81 [95% CI, 0.66-1.00]). After correcting for multiple testing (P<3.937×10-5), 233 proteins were associated with SES in the meta-analysis. Of these 233 proteins, 21 had a significant indirect effect on SES and CHD. Because the SES-stroke association was not statistically significant, proteins were not tested as mediators.

CONCLUSIONS: Our analysis of multiple cohorts identified evidence of different proteomic pathways associated with SES and cardiovascular disease. This work suggests that exogenous social factors (eg, SES) may influence cardiovascular disease via proteomic profiles.

articles.title: Contemporary Burden, Drivers, and Risk-Factor Control Gaps Across Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome Stages in US Adults, 2021 to 2023.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome staging integrates adiposity, metabolic dysfunction, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular disease. Contemporary national estimates of CKM stage distribution, stage drivers, and treatment gaps are needed to inform implementation of the CKM framework.

METHODS: We analyzed adults aged ≥20 years in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2021 to 2023 fasting subsample. CKM stage was assigned hierarchically using American Heart Association CKM staging criteria. We estimated survey-weighted CKM stage prevalence, national population counts, stage-specific drivers, and risk-factor control and treatment gaps across stages 2 through 4.

RESULTS: The analytic sample included 2958 adults, representing 245.2 million US adults. Overall, 26.4 million adults (10.8%) were stage 0, 56.8 million (23.2%) stage 1, 125.9 million (51.3%) stage 2, 13.4 million (5.5%) stage 3, and 22.7 million (9.3%) stage 4. Stage ≥1 was present in 89.2%, stage ≥2 in 66.1%, and advanced CKM (stages 3-4) in 14.7%. Among stage 1 adults, 85.1% had adiposity and 49.2% had prediabetes. Among adults with stage 2 CKM, hypertension (72.0%), metabolic syndrome (56.1%), and hypertriglyceridemia (41.9%) were common drivers. Among adults with stage 3 CKM, 95.8% met the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events 10-year cardiovascular disease risk criterion. Risk-factor control and treatment gaps were common across stages 2 through 4, including blood pressure ≥130/80 mm Hg in 50.3% to 66.9%, lipid-lowering therapy nonuse among eligible adults in 30.1% to 59.2%, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol above the target in 64.5% to 73.9%.

CONCLUSIONS: CKM syndrome affects most US adults, with stage-specific drivers and persistent risk-factor control and treatment gaps. These findings provide contemporary benchmarks for CKM surveillance and implementation.

articles.title: Multivariate Trajectories of Cardiometabolic Risk Factors and Complications in Elderly Chinese Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The current study aimed to identify the multivariate trajectories of cardiometabolic risk factors in elderly patients with type 2 diabetes and investigate their associations with cardiovascular disease and diabetic kidney disease (DKD).

METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 27 288 patients with type 2 diabetes aged ≥60 years from China's National Basic Public Health Service Program was analyzed. All participants had ≥3 medical examinations from 2018 to 2023. A multivariate latent class mixed model was used to identify the sex-specific multitrajectories of fasting plasma glucose, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and diastolic blood pressure. Binary logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% CIs for associations with cardiovascular disease, coronary heart disease, stroke, and DKD.

RESULTS: Among elderly male patients, 3 quadratic trajectory groups were identified: stable (87.16%; n=7997), U shape (3.78%; n=347), and inverse U shape (9.06%; n=831). In elderly women, 2 quadratic trajectory groups were identified: stable (87.29%; n=15 810) and inverse U shape (12.71%; n=2303). In men, the U-shape group had elevated risks of cardiovascular disease (OR, 1.66 [95% CI, 1.26-2.20]), coronary heart disease (OR, 1.60 [95% CI, 1.09-2.33]), stroke (OR, 1.58 [95% CI, 1.12-2.23]), and DKD (OR, 1.39 [95% CI, 1.11-1.74]); the inverse U-shape group had increased DKD risk (OR, 1.35 [95% CI, 1.16-1.57]). In women, the inverse U-shape group was associated with coronary heart disease (OR, 1.31 [95% CI, 1.12-1.53]) and DKD (OR, 1.65 [95% CI, 1.51-1.81]).

CONCLUSIONS: Distinct sex-specific trajectories of cardiometabolic risk factors were associated with different risks of cardiovascular and diabetic kidney complications in elderly patients with type 2 diabetes. These findings support early identification and personalized management of adverse trajectories to potentially reduce long-term complications in this population.

articles.title: Testosterone, Testosterone Replacement Therapy, and Cardiovascular Disease: A Contemporary Review.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract: Whether low endogenous testosterone is causal for cardiovascular disease, and how the cardiovascular risk of testosterone replacement therapy should now be classified, remain contested, while US labeling has moved in 2 opposing directions within 16 months. We conducted a targeted narrative review reported in accordance with the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles, searching MEDLINE and primary regulatory documents from January 2000 through July 2026. Evidence was graded with a prespecified 3-tier structured author-consensus rating separating established randomized findings, unresolved secondary signals, and evidentiary absence. Low endogenous testosterone is consistently associated with higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality but most plausibly marks multimorbidity rather than causation. TRAVERSE established that physiologic transdermal testosterone replacement therapy was noninferior to placebo for 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events over ∼3 years, within a permissive margin and against a 61% discontinuation rate. Observational analyses linking normalization to lower mortality were not reproduced under randomization. Atrial fibrillation, pulmonary embolism, acute kidney injury, fracture, and noncalcified plaque progression remain unresolved. Blood pressure rises across the class; on ambulatory monitoring the magnitude differs by individual product rather than by route. Long-term exposure and nontransdermal formulations remain untested, and the age-related-hypogonadism limitation of use is now proposed for removal. Noninferiority over 3 years should not be read as long-term clinical equivalence. Safe use of testosterone replacement therapy requires appropriate patient selection, distinction between pathologic hypogonadism and functional or age-associated low testosterone, mapping of each recommendation to its evidentiary tier, and close multidisciplinary collaboration.

articles.title: Intra-Arterial Alteplase After Successful Endovascular Reperfusion in Patients Without Intravenous Thrombolysis: A Subgroup Analysis of the PEARL Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: For patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke who undergo endovascular thrombectomy without prior intravenous thrombolysis, the efficacy and safety of adjunctive intra-arterial alteplase (IAA) after successful endovascular reperfusion remain uncertain.

METHODS: This was a prespecified subgroup analysis of the PEARL (Intra-Arterial Alteplase After Successful Endovascular Reperfusion in Acute Stroke) randomized clinical trial conducted at 28 centers in China, focusing on patients who underwent endovascular thrombectomy without prior intravenous thrombolysis. Patients were stratified by treatment assignment: IAA treatment versus standard treatment (control). The primary efficacy outcome was the proportion of patients achieving excellent functional outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 1 at 90 days. Safety outcomes included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, any intracranial hemorrhage within 36 hours, and 90-day all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: Among 324 patients originally randomized in the PEARL trial, 189 underwent endovascular thrombectomy without prior intravenous thrombolysis and were included in this analysis. Of the 189 patients, 95 were assigned to the IAA treatment group and 94 to the standard treatment group. Excellent functional outcome at 90 days was significantly higher in the IAA treatment group compared with the standard treatment group (43.2% [41/95] versus 22.6% [21/93]; adjusted risk ratio [aRR], 1.86; 95% CI, 1.19-2.91; P=0.007). The absolute risk reduction was 20.6% (95% CI, 7.0%-33.1%). Results were consistent in per-protocol sensitivity analyses (P=0.002). No significant differences were observed in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (aRR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.28-3.13; P=0.908), any intracranial hemorrhage (aRR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.68-1.60; P=0.843), or 90-day mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 1.00; 95% CI, 0.49-2.04; P>0.99).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients who did not receive prior intravenous thrombolysis, adjunctive IAA after successful endovascular thrombectomy was associated with a higher likelihood of excellent functional outcome at 90 days, without an apparent increase in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage or mortality.

REGISTRATION: URL: clinicaltrials.gov; Unique Identifier: NCT05856851.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Pharmacologic Therapies in Nonobstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) affects approximately one-third of all patients with HCM and carries substantial morbidity, yet no approved disease-modifying therapies exist. We conducted a systematic review of prospective interventional studies evaluating pharmacologic therapies in adults with nonobstructive HCM.

METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Clinicaltrials.gov was performed through September 2025. Eligible studies included randomized and nonrandomized prospective interventional trials. A narrative synthesis was performed by pharmacologic class and outcome domain.

RESULTS: Twenty-nine clinical trials evaluating 9 pharmacologic classes were identified: cardiac myosin inhibitors, cardiac sarcomere modulators, metabolic modulators, angiotensin II receptor blockers, angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, SGLT2 (sodium-glucose cotransporter 2) inhibitors, beta blockers, and calcium channel blockers. Cardiac myosin inhibitors demonstrated reductions in left ventricular hypertrophy, improvements in diastolic function, and marked reductions in cardiac biomarkers, although improvements in exercise capacity and symptoms were variable. SGLT2 inhibition showed concordant improvements in diastolic function, atrial remodeling, biomarkers, and functional status in patients with symptomatic nonobstructive HCM and comorbid type 2 diabetes. Angiotensin receptor blockade showed signals of structural remodeling with valsartan and candesartan without consistent functional benefit. Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism and angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibition demonstrated largely neutral effects. Among metabolic modulators, ninerafaxstat improved ventilatory efficiency and quality of life in patients with greater baseline symptom burden.

CONCLUSIONS: Pharmacologic responsiveness in nonobstructive HCM is variable and appears to be mechanism- and disease stage-dependent. Ongoing trials evaluating cardiac myosin inhibitors, SGLT inhibitors, and novel therapeutic agents including ninerafaxstat and EDG-7500 will be critical in further defining the therapeutic landscape.

articles.title: Macrophage-Derived Glycoprotein Nonmetastatic Melanoma Protein B Attenuates Cardiac Dysfunction by Promoting Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor-Independent Angiogenesis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pressure overload-induced heart failure involves maladaptive cardiac remodeling and inadequate angiogenesis. The limitations of VEGF (vascular endothelial growth factor)-based therapies underscore the need to identify alternative angiogenic pathways. GPNMB (glycoprotein nonmetastatic melanoma protein B) is a macrophage-secreted protein implicated in tissue repair, but its role in pressure overload-induced cardiac remodeling and its potential to modulate angiogenesis remain unknown.

METHODS: Myeloid-specific Gpnmb knockout and control mice were subjected to transverse aortic constriction. Cardiac function, remodeling, and capillary density were assessed. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed to identify transcriptomic changes. In vitro, human endothelial cells were treated with recombinant GPNMB to assess proliferation, migration, and tube formation, and to dissect the underlying signaling pathways. The therapeutic potential of Gpnmb overexpression was evaluated using AAV9 vectors.

RESULTS: Myeloid Gpnmb deletion exacerbated transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophy, fibrosis, and capillary rarefaction. Single-cell sequencing revealed a reduced capillary endothelial cell population and pathway enrichment indicative of endothelial dysfunction and metabolic reprogramming in myeloid-specific Gpnmb knockout hearts. Mechanistically, GPNMB directly promoted endothelial cell proliferation, migration, and tube formation by activating the mTOR (mechanistic target of rapamycin) pathway in a CD44-dependent manner, independently of VEGF signaling. Cardiac-specific Gpnmb overexpression rescued angiogenesis, improved cardiac function, and attenuated pathological remodeling after transverse aortic constriction.

CONCLUSIONS: Macrophage-derived GPNMB is a critical regulator of cardiac adaptation to pressure overload. It promotes a VEGF-independent angiogenic program probably via the CD44/mTOR axis, as supported by in vitro mechanistic studies. GPNMB represents a promising therapeutic target for heart failure characterized by microvascular rarefaction.

articles.title: Targeting Mediator Kinase Attenuates Cardiac Hypertrophy by Regulating Enhancer Utilization.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac hypertrophy is characterized by extensive transcriptional remodeling that contributes to the progression of heart failure. Preclinical models demonstrate that therapies targeting hypertrophic responses can mitigate disease severity. Recent evidence shows that failing human and murine hearts exhibit elevated mediator kinase expression, sufficient to drive eccentric hypertrophy and heart failure through activation of hypertrophic gene programs. Mediator kinase inhibition suppresses oncogenic transcription by altering enhancer utilization, suggesting similar mechanisms may attenuate pathological remodeling in the heart. This study investigates whether mediator kinase inhibition can blunt cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, offering a potential therapeutic strategy for heart failure.

METHODS: Two structurally unrelated mediator kinase inhibitors, Senexin A (SxnA) and CCT251545, were tested in neonatal rat cardiomyocytes. Hypertrophy was assessed by cell size measurements, RNA sequencing, and H3K27ac chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing.

RESULTS: Mediator kinase inhibition significantly reduced hypertrophic growth, attenuating cell size increases induced by phenylephrine (PE) and endothelin-1. Transcriptomic profiling revealed a dose-dependent suppression of PE-induced differentially expressed genes in Senexin A-treated cells. Mechanistically, PE stimulation enhanced RNA polymerase II pause release, whereas Mediator kinase inhibition did not alter this process. Epigenomic analysis showed that PE markedly increased the number of super-enhancers relative to vehicle treatment, while co-treatment with Senexin A reduced the total number of active enhancers. Nearest-neighbor analysis linked putative regulatory enhancers to key PE-responsive genes, and these enhancer signatures were blunted by SxnA.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate that Mediator kinase inhibition counteracts hypertrophic growth and transcriptional reprogramming, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic strategy to modulate pathological gene regulation in cardiac hypertrophy.

articles.title: Integrative Genomic Analyses Identify Collagen Type XXI Alpha 1 Chain and ENPEP-Fibroblast Growth Factor 5 Regulatory Pathways for Blood Pressure Variation in East Asian People.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension and diabetes are common cardiometabolic disorders that may share genetic and environmental risk factors. However, the regulatory genes and tissue-specific mechanisms underlying blood pressure variations remain incompletely understood.

METHODS: Leveraging a well-characterized prospective population-based cohort comprised of 27 308 participants from the SCHS (Singapore Chinese Health Study), we evaluated genome-wide genetic associations for 5 blood pressure traits: hypertension status, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, mean arterial pressure and pulse pressure. Additionally, we conducted a transcriptome-wide association study, integrating gene expression data from 49 tissues, followed by colocalization and fine-mapping to prioritize regulatory genes. Association of identified variants with incident diabetes was additionally evaluated in the longitudinal data.

RESULTS: We validated 10 blood pressure loci (P between 1.64×10-20-4.10×10-8) and identified an East Asian-specific splice donor variant at the COL21A1 gene associated with pulse pressure (rs149344559, P=6.78×10-10). Integrative analyses prioritized FGF5 in kidney cortex and ENPEP in pituitary tissue as candidate regulatory genes. The blood pressure-lowering allele at ENPEP (T allele, rs1879056) was associated with reduced risk of incident diabetes. Mediation analysis demonstrated that ∼20.1% of the genetic association with diabetes was mediated through mean arterial pressure (Pindirect-effect<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: This study refines genetic predispositions for blood pressure among East Asian individuals. We further delineate tissue-specific regulatory pathways underlying blood pressure variations and identify ENPEP-mediated dysfunctions linking blood pressure genetics to diabetes risk, underscoring integrated disease mechanisms.

articles.title: Assessment of Persistent Postpartum Hypertension Following Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: A Scoping Review.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Identifying individuals with persistent postpartum hypertension (ppHTN) after hypertensive disorders of pregnancy is an important strategy to mitigate associated long-term cardiovascular risks. Accordingly, we aimed to review the literature surrounding the assessment of ppHTN after hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.

METHODS: We conducted a scoping review using Arksey and O'Malley's methodological framework. We developed and pilot-tested a data extraction tool to collect information on ppHTN assessment methods, including timing and setting, blood pressure (BP) thresholds used, and inclusion of patient preferences. Data were synthesized into tables and narrative summaries. Barriers and facilitators to BP assessment protocols, remote BP monitoring, and follow-up attendance were mapped using the Capability, Opportunity, and Motivation - Behavior (COM-B) framework.

RESULTS: Of 14 593 records, 96 papers met inclusion criteria. BP measured in the hospital alone was most common (n=41), followed by the hospital/home combination (n=18), and the outpatient/home combination (n=9). Monitoring typically began within 0 to 7 days postpartum (n=28), ending at 1 to 6 weeks (n=20) or 6 to 12 months (n=20) postpartum. ppHTN was defined using elevated BP thresholds (n=28), most commonly ≥140/90 mm Hg (n=18), medication initiation (n=8), lack of BP normalization over time (n=4), or referral to a specialist (n=2). Only 7 studies assessed patient preferences. Facilitators to home BP assessment included the use of educational material, while barriers involved digital access limitations.

CONCLUSIONS: ppHTN assessment methods varied in timing, setting, and BP thresholds. Findings underscore the need for standardized, patient-centered guidelines that account for BP assessment methods across settings.

articles.title: Anthracycline Cardiotoxicity as Multicellular Network Failure: Cardiac Niche Reprogramming and Pathological Cell-Cell Communication.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract: Anthracyclines are essential anticancer agents, yet a cardiomyocyte-centered model incompletely explains why cardiac injury can be delayed, progressive, and poorly captured by resting ejection fraction. We frame anthracycline cardiotoxicity as a multicellular network failure within the cardiac niche: the spatially organized interactions among cardiomyocytes, fibroblasts, endothelial and immune cells, extracellular matrix, and circulating signals. Cardiomyocyte stress initiates injury, whereas pathological communication may propagate it. We distinguish a fibroblast-CD8+ T-cell adhesion circuit, supported by loss-of-function evidence in mice and correlative human data, from an emerging therapy-conditioned tumor-heart extracellular vesicle axis supported mainly by breast cancer models. These pathways may converge on fibrotic stiffness, microvascular dysfunction, and electrical uncoupling; however, direct cross-circuit interaction and drug-independent sufficiency remain unproven. We integrate established clinical risk modifiers with this framework, specify causal criteria, and propose spatial multiomics, living myocardial slices, tumor-bearing systems, and longitudinal phenotyping to test circuit persistence. This evidence-calibrated model shifts the goal from cataloging cell-intrinsic pathways to identifying mechanism-resolved biomarkers and therapeutically targetable communication nodes while preserving antitumor efficacy.

articles.title: Plasminogen Activator Inhibitor-1 Deficiency Exacerbates Pressure Overload-Induced Cardiac Hypertrophy in Mice.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy is a key precursor to heart failure. PAI-1 (plasminogen activator inhibitor-1) is a recognized profibrotic mediator, yet its role in the heart remains paradoxical and incompletely understood.

METHODS: Six-week-old male wild-type (PAI-1+/+) and PAI-1 knockout (PAI-1-/-) mice underwent sham or transverse aortic constriction surgery, followed by assessment of cardiac morphology, molecular markers, and function. In H9C2 cardiomyocytes, PAI-1 was silenced or overexpressed before angiotensin II stimulation, with or without targeted signaling inhibitors, followed by coimmunoprecipitation, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence.

RESULTS: Pressure overload increased plasma and myocardial PAI-1 levels. PAI-1 deficiency exacerbated transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophy, and fibrosis, accompanied by JAK2/STAT3 (Janus kinase 2/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3) activation and collagen overexpression, whereas cardiac-specific overexpression attenuated these maladaptive changes. Moreover, STAT3 inhibition reversed the adverse cardiac remodeling associated with PAI-1 deletion. In vitro, PAI-1 knockdown potentiated angiotensin II-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, an effect that was rescued by PAI-1 overexpression. Mechanistically, PAI-1 associated with JAK2 and STAT3, with reduced phosphorylation of both proteins and impaired STAT3 nuclear translocation. Critically, pharmacological inhibition of STAT3 abolished the harmful effects of PAI-1 silencing.

CONCLUSIONS: PAI-1 acts as an endogenous cardioprotective checkpoint by negatively regulating JAK2/STAT3 signaling. These findings suggest a noncanonical cardiomyocyte-associated function of PAI-1 beyond its classical fibrinolytic role and identify the PAI-1-JAK2/STAT3 axis as a potential therapeutic target for heart failure with hypertrophy.

articles.title: Combined Prognostic Value of Cardiac Magnetic Resonance-Derived Myocardial Extracellular Volume and the Fibrosis-4 Index in Patients With Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is increasingly recognized as a multisystem metabolic-inflammatory syndrome. We investigated the comparative and complementary prognostic value of cardiac magnetic resonance-derived extracellular volume fraction (ECV) and the Fibrosis-4 index for predicting adverse cardiovascular outcomes in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.

METHODS: Between 2017 and 2019, 250 patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction underwent assessment of myocardial ECV by cardiac magnetic resonance and hepatic fibrosis using the Fibrosis-4 index. The primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization. Multivariable Cox regression and discrimination analyses were performed to evaluate prognostic performance.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 1190 days, 75 patients (30.0%) experienced the primary outcome. Both ECV (hazard ratio [HR], 1.13 [95% CI, 1.08-1.17]; P<0.001) and the Fibrosis-4 index (HR, 1.12 [95% CI, 1.02-1.22]; P=0.015) independently predicted the primary outcome. Patients with concomitantly elevated ECV and Fibrosis-4 index had a markedly increased risk of adverse events compared with those with low values of both markers. ECV-based models demonstrated superior discrimination compared with Fibrosis-4-based models (concordance index, 0.732 versus 0.663; P=0.011). Addition of ECV to the Fibrosis-4 model significantly improved discrimination, whereas addition of the Fibrosis-4 index to the ECV model improved reclassification (continuous net reclassification improvement and integrated discrimination improvement) but not discrimination.

CONCLUSIONS: Both myocardial ECV and the Fibrosis-4 index independently predict adverse cardiovascular outcomes in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. Although ECV provides greater prognostic discrimination, combined assessment of ECV and the Fibrosis-4 index identifies a subgroup at particularly high risk and may provide complementary information for risk stratification.

articles.title: Neuropsychological and Quality-of-Life Outcomes After Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Survivors of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage often have long-term neuropsychological disturbances. This study aims to characterize depressive symptoms, quality of life, and personality changes in a large cohort of survivors of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included patients with a history of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage from the Brain Aneurysm Foundation patient registry. Patients completed the Beck Depression Inventory-II and the Stroke-Specific Quality of Life scale, and family members completed the Iowa Scales of Personality Change. Multiple linear regression was used to identify symptoms associated with reduced work productivity. Wilcoxon and chi-square tests were used to identify variables associated with severity of depressive symptoms and personality changes.

RESULTS: A total of 318 patients were included, with 242 completing the Beck Depression Inventory-II and Stroke-Specific Quality of Life, and 112 family members completing the Iowa Scales of Personality Change. Moderate depressive symptoms were reported by 18% of patients, and severe symptoms were reported by 11%. Impairments in thinking, social roles, language, and energy were independently associated with reduced work productivity. Acquired personality disturbances were observed in 72% of patients for executive function, 44% for social behavior, 49% for hypomotivation, 50% for irascibility, and 72% for distress. Ruptured aneurysms in the anterior cerebral and anterior communicating artery were associated with a trend toward a higher prevalence of moderate to severe depressive symptoms and executive personality changes.

CONCLUSIONS: Depressive symptoms and personality changes are common after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage, affecting work productivity. Recognizing challenges in thinking, social interactions, language, and vulnerability to pressure may help guide targeted interventions by families, employers, and health care providers.

articles.title: Plasma Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme as a Prioritized Candidate Target for Alzheimer's Disease: Evidence From Proteome-Wide Mendelian Randomization and a Large Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We aimed to provide hypothesis-generating evidence on druggable targets for Alzheimer's disease (AD) by integrating proteome-wide Mendelian randomization (MR) with evidence from a conventional observational analysis of drug use in a large prospective cohort.

METHODS: Proteome-wide MR analysis was conducted to identify plasma proteins causally related to AD risk using the largest summary-level data to date, followed by colocalization and multiomic validation analyses (on the gene expression, alternative splicing, and DNA methylation levels in blood and brain, respectively) to prioritize potential druggable targets. We also replicated our MR findings using additional genetic data and performed multivariable MR for the prioritized findings. Conventional observational analysis in UK Biobank, a large prospective cohort, was performed to provide further clinical implications, using active comparator to minimize confounding by indication.

RESULTS: MR analysis identified 15 plasma proteins with putative causal effects on AD risk. Of them, inhibition of angiotensin-converting enzyme was found to increase the risk of AD (odds ratio, 1.10 [95% CI, 1.08-1.14]), which was likely independent of blood pressure as suggested by multivariable MR. Observational analysis in UK Biobank showed a higher incidence (hazard ratio, 1.23 [95% CI, 1.00-1.50]) of AD among regular users of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, compared with the active comparator angiotensin receptor blocker users.

CONCLUSIONS: Our genetic analyses prioritized angiotensin-converting enzyme as a candidate target, and a conventional observational analysis in a large prospective cohort provided supportive evidence that regular angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor use was associated with a higher AD risk, which needs further investigation with high-quality real-world evidence and clinical trials before being translated into practice changes.

articles.title: PASCAL Precision System Outcomes by Implant Location and Lesion Location in Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation Patients From the STS/ACC TVT Registry.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair can be more challenging in noncentral regions of the valve and in anterior or bileaflet lesions. We assess effect of implant location and leaflet lesion location on safety and effectiveness of PASCAL Precision system in degenerative mitral regurgitation (MR).

METHODS: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair outcomes in patients with degenerative MR treated with PASCAL Precision system (September 2022-October 2024), from the US STS/ACC TVT (Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy) Registry, were analyzed by implant location (A2P2/non-A2P2) and leaflet lesion location (anterior/posterior/bileaflet). Procedural, clinical, and echocardiographic outcomes to 30 days were assessed.

RESULTS: At 30 days, both A2P2 (n=1526) and non-A2P2 (n=299) groups had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 1.1% versus 1.0%, mitral valve reintervention: 0.4% versus 0.0% and single leaflet device attachment: 0.5% versus 0.3%; all P>0.05) and demonstrated significant MR reduction (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference between groups (P=0.750) (MR ≤2+: 93.4% versus 95.4%; MR ≤1+: 72.0% versus 73.3%). Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores improved significantly in both groups (∆19.3, ∆17.7 points; P=0.741). The anterior (n=250), posterior (n=902), and bileaflet (n=192) disease groups also had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 0.4%, 1.1%, 0.0%; mitral valve reintervention: 0.8%, 0.1%, 0.5%; and single leaflet device attachment: 0.8%, 0.2%, 0.5%; all P>0.05), and demonstrated significant MR reduction (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference across groups (P=0.459) (MR ≤2+: 94.1%, 93.1%, and 94.5%; MR ≤1+: 79.0%, 69.2%, and 72.4%). All groups experienced significant improvement in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores (∆21.4, ∆18.8, ∆12.0 points; P=0.087).

CONCLUSION: In real-world patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation, treatment with the PASCAL Precision system was associated with favorable safety and effectiveness at 30 days, regardless of implant location or leaflet lesion location.

articles.title: Evaluation of Acute Electrical and Hemodynamic Improvement During Left Bundle-Branch Area Pacing Modalities for Resynchronization Therapy.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While cardiac resynchronization therapy is effective in dyssynchronous heart failure, suboptimal response remains frequent. The acute hemodynamic profile of different left bundle-branch (LBB) area pacing modalities is poorly defined. Moreover, atrioventricular optimization guided by QRS duration (QRSd) may not yield the greatest hemodynamic benefit.

METHODS: Twenty-four patients with heart failure, reduced ejection fraction, and LBB block underwent sequential testing of right ventricular septal pacing, left ventricular septal pacing, nonselective LBB pacing, and selective LBB pacing during cardiac resynchronization therapy implantation in a prospective, within-subject physiological study. At each modality, electrical end points were QRSd and vectorcardiographic QRS area; hemodynamics were assessed with beat-to-beat systolic blood pressure (SBP). The atrioventricular interval producing maximal SBP improvement was compared with that producing the narrowest QRSd.

RESULTS: LBB area pacing modalities significantly reduced QRSd, compared with right ventricular septal pacing (nonselective LBB pacing, 114.0±16.8 milliseconds; selective LBB pacing, 118.4±14.1 milliseconds; left ventricular septal pacing, 124.6±16.0 milliseconds; right ventricular septal pacing, 144.4±27.6 milliseconds; all P<0.01). At the atrioventricular interval that produced maximized SBP improvement, QRSd remained narrower with LBB area pacing than right ventricular septal pacing, and selective LBB pacing provided the greatest hemodynamic improvement (ΔSBP 16.3±5.2 mm Hg), exceeding left ventricular septal pacing (13.5±6.2 mm Hg) and nonselective LBB pacing (12.8±6.3 mm Hg; all P<0.05). Across modalities, the atrioventricular interval that maximized ΔSBP was consistently shorter than that minimizing QRSd (mean difference, 18-29 milliseconds).

CONCLUSIONS: Selective LBB pacing yields the greatest acute hemodynamic benefit, and the hemodynamic-optimal atrioventricular interval is shorter than the electrical-optimal atrioventricular interval, suggesting that modest atrioventricular interval shortening after electrical optimization may better maximize hemodynamics.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique Identifier: NCT07032064.

articles.title: Implementation of a WatchPAT-Based Diagnostic Pathway for Obstructive Sleep Apnea in a Tertiary Hypertension Center: A Feasibility Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a prevalent yet underdiagnosed in hypertension, affecting 30% to 83% of patients. Limited polysomnography access delays diagnosis. We evaluated the feasibility, diagnostic yield, and downstream management decisions of an integrated diagnostic pathway using WatchPAT 300, a peripheral arterial tonometry-based home sleep apnea test, in a tertiary hypertension unit.

METHODS: In this single-center, prospective, observational study, 200 patients underwent ambulatory OSA assessment from May 2023 through August 2025. We recorded clinical variables, peripheral arterial tonometry data, and management decisions. A subgroup underwent confirmatory in-laboratory polysomnography. Patients were classified as none-to-mild OSA (peripheral apneahypopnea index <15/h) and moderate-to-severe OSA (≥15/h).

RESULTS: The pathway achieved 97.5% (95% CI, 94%-99%) technical success and reduced the mean time-to-diagnosis to 3.5±4.5 days, versus 154 days for in-laboratory polysomnography. Over half of the cohort was triaged: ∼30% met treatment criteria directly, and 22% were ruled out. Among patients completing confirmatory polysomnography, 83% (95% CI, 61%-94%) initially classified as none-to-mild were reclassified as moderate-to-severe OSA, and 77% required treatment. Furthermore, symptoms were dissociated from severity, and Snoring-Tired-Observed-Pressure-BMI-Age-Gender (STOP-Bag) association with severity did not remain significant after multiplicity correction.

CONCLUSIONS: A peripheral arterial tonometry-based home sleep apnea test-first model is feasible and efficient, eliminating diagnostic delays. Although effective for triaging clear-cut cases, the high reclassification rate underscores the almost mandatory role of confirmatory polysomnography for milder or equivocal results, suspected comorbid sleep disorders, or high STOP-Bag score. These data argue against symptoms-based screening alone to screen populations with hypertension.

articles.title: Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Inducing Kinase- and Inhibitor of Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Kinase Subunit Beta-Binding Protein Promotes Pathological Cardiac Hypertrophy by Regulating Inhibitor of Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Kinase Subunit Beta-Mediated Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Activation.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy is a major risk factor for heart failure. NIBP (NF-κB [nuclear factor kappa-B] inducing kinase- and inhibitor of NF-κB kinase subunit beta-binding protein) is a key regulator of cytokine-induced NF-κB signaling, but its role in cardiac hypertrophy remains unknown.

METHODS: We established transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac hypertrophy in mice and phenylephrine-induced hypertrophy in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes. Genetic interventions included generation of whole-body Nibp knockout mice via CRISPR-Cas9; creation of cardiomyocyte-specific Nibp knockout mice using adeno-associated virus serotype 9-delivered Cre and single-guide RNAs in Rosa26-LSL-Cas9 mice; and cardiac-specific Nibp overexpression via adeno-associated virus serotype 9delivery. In neonatal rat ventricular myocytes, NIBP was knocked down or overexpressed using adenoviruses. Phenotypes were assessed by echocardiography, histology (wheat germ agglutinin, picrosirius redstaining), and molecular analyses. Mechanisms were investigated via RNA-sequencing, coimmunoprecipitation, and Western blotting for key signaling molecules.

RESULTS: NIBP protein was upregulated in hypertrophic hearts and cardiomyocytes. Both Nibp-knockout and cardiomyocyte-specific Nibp knockout attenuated transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophy, and fibrosis, whereas Nibp overexpression exacerbated these pathologies. Consistently, in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes, NIBP knockdown mitigated, while its overexpression aggravated, phenylephrine-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and inflammatory responses. Mechanistically, NIBP directly interacted with IKKβ (inhibitor of NF-κB kinase subunit beta), enhanced its phosphorylation, and drove hyperactivation of the downstream NF-κB pathway. Overexpression of a kinase-dead IKKβ mutant reversed the hypertrophic effects of NIBP.

CONCLUSIONS: NIBP promotes pathological cardiac hypertrophy by activating the IKKβ/NF-κB axis, identifying it as a potential therapeutic target for cardiac remodeling and heart failure.

articles.title: Modern antidiabetic therapy in older adults with type 2 diabetes: evidence, best practice and a clinical pharmacist's framework.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Older adults with type 2 diabetes require treatment that balances cardiovascular and kidney protection against hypoglycemia, treatment burden, undernutrition, and functional vulnerability.

AREAS COVERED: This narrative review considers PubMed-indexed literature and ClinicalTrials.gov records covering January 2010-October 2026, with targeted updating on 12 October 2026. It examines sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, tirzepatide, and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors. Age-stratified outcome evidence is distinguished from whole-trial results and the limited evidence in adults aged 80 years or older. Body-composition findings, neurodegenerative outcomes, kidney-protective treatment, and pharmacist-supported regimen modification are critically appraised.

EXPERT OPINION: Organ protection and glycemic simplification should be considered separately. Frailty is not synonymous with kidney impairment, and reductions in lean mass do not establish treatment-induced sarcopenia. Weight-neutral therapy remains useful when weight loss is undesirable. A structured medication review should integrate patient priorities, nutrition, physical performance, renal function, and hypoglycemia risk, followed by explicit monitoring and communication across care transitions. Prospective validation of this integrated framework in the oldest and most vulnerable populations is needed.

articles.title: Fungal representation in the environment of penguin communities in the French Southern territories.
articles.abstract: Penguins are highly susceptible to airborne mycoses, and aspergillosis due to Aspergillus fumigatus (recently classified as a priority pathogen by WHO) is common in captivity; however, environmental fungal diversity and exposure risk in natural, non-temperate breeding habitats remain poorly described. We aimed to characterize the seasonal burden and diversity of culturable fungi in wild king penguin (Aptenodytes patagonicus) colonies and to assess A. fumigatus diversity and phenotypes. During 1 year, monthly environmental sampling was performed from four different soils of Crozet archipelago, in French Southern Territories, around three penguin colonies. Samples were cultured on malt extract agar at 35 ± 2°C. Isolates were quantified (CFU) and identified by microscopy, MALDI-TOF MS, and DNA sequencing. Aspergillus fumigatus isolates underwent genotyping and phenotyping for antifungal susceptibility, as well as for tolerance to high salinity and extreme temperatures. Overall, fungal loads in penguin environments showed marked seasonality (3-1 100 CFU/month), peaking during breeding/chick rearing summer period (∼22% positive sites). After April, fungal burden declined (mean 150 CFU/month; 8.8% positive sites). Aspergillus section Fumigati represented 21%-100% of isolates (150-950 CFU/month). Aspergillus fumigatus genotypes were diverse, with no detected antifungal resistance or extreme growth phenotypes. Fungal burden in penguin natural habitats was closely linked to bird presence and breeding activity. These findings provide new insights into fungal exposure in wild groups and emphasize the importance of a One Health approach to better understand the interactions between environment, wildlife, and infectious disease risk in fragile ecosystems.

articles.title: Hypermobility spectrum disorder/hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, mast cell activation syndrome, and dysautonomia as risk factors for adverse events and complications.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hypermobility spectrum disorder/hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (HSD/hEDS), mast cell activation syndrome (MCAS), and dysautonomia, including postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS), are comorbid conditions encountered in clinical practice with possible overlapping immunologic, autonomic, and connective tissue abnormalities. Clinicians frequently observe that individuals affected with these syndromes commonly experience disproportionate adverse events and complications from a variety of stressors.

AREAS COVERED: We review clinical observations and emerging evidence via PubMed on adverse events and complications experienced by patients with HSD/hEDS, MCAS, and dysautonomia in response to surgery, postoperative period, anesthesia, medication side effects, substance sensitivities, and infection.

EXPERT OPINION: Patients with HSD/hEDS, MCAS, and dysautonomia may be at a higher risk of adverse events and complications associated with surgery, medication, substances, and infection. Recognition and awareness of these syndromes and possible risks, which each disorder may carry alone or as a triad, can lead to risk mitigation, appropriate counseling, and prognostication. Future studies should focus on longitudinal multicenter studies assessing risks and outcomes in this vulnerable patient population. Translational studies are also needed to elucidate the mechanisms underlying adverse events and complications in patients with HSD/hEDS, MCAS, and dysautonomia.

articles.title: Objective Assessment of Oral Feeding Development in Preterm Infants Using the Neoneur Feeding System.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate feeding and respiratory skills in preterm infants using the neoneur feeding system (NFS) clinical biomarkers and track maturation until discharge in infants achieving full oral feeds.

STUDY DESIGN: This prospective, observational, nonrandomized, longitudinal study enrolled infants born ≤ 34 weeks' gestation from the level III neonatal intensive care unit at Thomas Jefferson University Hospital. The NFS was used to record feeding, with each infant contributing a minimum of six feeds recorded over 3 weeks.
