BACKGROUND: This study investigated periodontal disease as a potential risk factor for severity of COVID-19 Infection.

OBJECTIVES: This study explored the associations of periodontal disease with severity of COVID-19 infection along with chronic inflammatory biomarkers routinely collected during COVID-19 as the diagnostic and prognostic factor for treatment and severity of the COVID-19 infection.

METHODS: Periodontal Disease condition status was assessed as per world health organization (WHO) oral health assessment for adults defined criteria from survivor of COVID-19 infection, with data collected from the COVID-19 infection treatment dedicated tertiary care hospital in Bahawalpur Division, Southern Punjab, Pakistan.

RESULTS: Among 383 patients, 42 (11.0%) had mild, 77 (20.1%) had moderate, and 186 (48.6%) had severe COVID-19. A total of 78 patients (20.4%) were diagnosed with advanced periodontitis. Multivariate analysis revealed a significant association between periodontal disease and COVID-19 severity, with an adjusted odds ratio (AOR) of 9.567 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.982-46.186; p < 0.001). Furthermore, patients with both periodontal disease and diabetes mellitus had a markedly increased risk (AOR = 36.739; 95% CI: 1.924-701.666; p < 0.017). Key biomarkers, such as lactate dehydrogenase (AOR = 0.100; 95% CI: 0.017-0.575; p < 0.010) and C-reactive protein (AOR = 0.028; 95% CI: 0.0020.362; p < 0.006), also showed significant associations.

CONCLUSION: These findings underscore the public health relevance of periodontal disease as a contributing factor for the severity of COVID-19 and highlight the diagnostic value of routine collected inflammatory biomarkers in managing chronic and infectious conditions like COVID-19 Infection.

articles.title: Paradoxical ethnic differences in prevalence of vascular risk factors versus extracranial atherosclerotic disease in TIA/stroke patients in the United Kingdom: Population-based study and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Studies in Northern America report a lower prevalence of coronary artery disease (CAD) in Black than White people despite higher prevalence of vascular risk factors. However, it remains unclear to what extent these differences are driven by biology or reflect ethnic disparities in smoking, socioeconomic deprivation, healthcare access, and health-seeking behaviour. We aimed to determine if ethnic differences in coronary and peripheral artery disease persist in people with stroke living in the United Kingdom (UK), considering that most people with stroke seek medical attention and the National Health Service provides equitable access to care.

METHODS: In a prospective population-based cohort of all patients with suspected TIA or stroke in Oxfordshire, UK (Oxford Vascular Study, OxVasc, April 2002 to March 2023), we fitted multivariable logistic regression models to quantify the association of ethnicity and extracranial atherosclerotic disease (coronary or peripheral) while adjusting for age, sex, vascular risk factors, and socioeconomic deprivation. We verified our findings in a systematic review of UK-based studies reporting prevalence of extracranial atherosclerotic disease and associated vascular risk factors across ethnic groups. Prevalence estimates were pooled by random-effects meta-analysis.

RESULTS: In 7297 OxVasc participants (52.6% women, 71.0 ± 15.5 years), non-White people (n = 335) had a higher prevalence of diabetes mellitus (OR = 3.26, 2.55-4.16). However, Black people had a lower prevalence of CAD (OR = 0.31, 0.10-0.98, p = 0.046) or any extracranial atherosclerotic disease (OR = 0.42, 0.18-0.96, p = 0.04) than White people. After adjustment for age, sex, vascular risk factors, and deprivation, the difference was attenuated both for CAD (aOR = 0.50, 0.18-1.41, p = 0.19) and any extracranial atherosclerotic disease (aOR = 0.43, 0.18-1.04, p = 0.06). Asian and White people had similar prevalence of CAD and extracranial atherosclerotic disease. Among UK-based studies of patients with stroke, Black and Asian people were more likely than White people to have diabetes (pooled OR: 2.78, 2.40-3.22, n = 3 studies; 4.15, 3.11-5.53 n = 6), hypertension (1.95, 1.47-2.60, n = 3; 1.47, 1.02-2.12, n = 6), and obesity (1.52, 1.27-1.83, n = 1; 1.2, 0.66-2.29, n = 3) but less likely to be smoking (0.70, 0.50-0.97, n = 2; 0.57, 0.44-0.74, n = 5). Yet, Black people had less CAD than White (0.48, 0.31-0.76, n = 3) and Asian (0.30, 0.10-0.80, n = 2) people.

INTERPRETATION: We confirm the existence of a coronary artery disease paradox in Black but not Asian people with TIA or stroke, which is likely independent of biases in healthcare access or health-seeking behaviour, and may suggest different biological susceptibilities.

articles.title: Primary Endocrine Therapy vs Upfront Surgery for Older Women With Estrogen Receptor-Positive Breast Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: As the population of older women with breast cancer grows, an increasing number are considered for primary endocrine therapy (pET), yet clinicians lack a framework for identifying which patients are appropriate candidates, resulting in reliance on chronologic age and life expectancy rather than tumor biology.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate survival and variables associated with response duration for patients treated with pET.

DATA SOURCES: PubMed, MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception through March 26, 2026.

STUDY SELECTION: Randomized clinical trials (RCTs) and non-RCT (observational) cohorts comparing pET with surgery in operable, nonmetastatic, estrogen receptor (ER)-positive breast cancer.

DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Data were extracted independently by 2 reviewers per Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Hazard ratios (HRs) not directly reported were reconstructed from Kaplan-Meier curves. Randomized clinical trial-derived HRs for overall survival (OS) and breast cancer-specific survival (BCSS) were pooled using a random-effects model, given anticipated heterogeneity across trials spanning 5 decades and differing tumor biology criteria. Observational cohorts were analyzed descriptively, not pooled for comparative survival, given susceptibility to confounding by indication.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The main outcomes were OS and BCSS (RCTs) assessed using meta-analysis. Time to progression, salvage intervention rates, and variables associated with progression and mortality (observational cohorts) were assessed using descriptive analyses.

RESULTS: Twenty-nine studies (6 RCTs and 23 observational cohorts; 22 821 patients; overall median [IQR] age, 83.1 [77.0-85.0] years) met the inclusion criteria. Patients from RCTs were generally younger (median [IQR] age, 77.0 [75.8-78.0] years) than those from the observational studies (median [IQR] age, 84.0 [81.5-86.0] years). Treatment with pET was not associated with a statistically significant OS difference vs surgery (HR, 1.14; 95% CI, 0.98-1.33), though the point estimate favored surgery. Median time to progression ranged from 19.7 months (range, 13.5-26.0 months) in tumor biology-unselected, tamoxifen-era cohorts to more than 50 months in ER-selected and aromatase inhibitor-treated cohorts. Tumor biology was consistently associated with progression risk.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This systematic review and meta-analysis of more than 22 000 patients with ER-positive breast cancer found no statistically significant survival difference between pET and upfront surgery. Durable disease control under pET seemed to be concentrated in patients with favorable biology. These findings support a framework incorporating tumor biology and frailty, rather than age alone, to identify candidates for pET.

articles.title: Consensus Statements on Minimally Invasive Surgical Treatments for Male Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Secondary to Benign Prostatic Enlargement and Obstruction.
articles.journal: The world journal of men's health
articles.abstract: In recent times, scientific advances in male lower urinary tract symptoms (mLUTS) secondary to benign prostatic enlargement (BPE)/benign prostatic obstruction (BPO) technology, coupled with greater demands and awareness on preservation of sexual function in BPE/BPO surgery, have led to many patients seeking and urologists offering effective yet minimally invasive surgical treatments (MISTs). This modified Delphi consensus was initiated by the Male Lower Urinary Tract Advisory Group and key opinion leaders within the Urological Society of Australia and New Zealand to provide consensus statements and clinical recommendations to guide the current understanding and clinical care in this rapidly evolving field. Fourteen consensus statements are provided, along with corresponding levels of evidence and grades of recommendation, following a modified Delphi method. MIST should be offered to sexually active males with LUTS/BPE/BPO and patients who want surgery but wish to preserve fertility status for natural conception. Long-term clinical efficacy and safety data on MIST beyond 5 years are limited (except for prostatic urethral lift [PUL] or Urolift system). Almost all MIST preserve erectile function, although to date, only Urolift PUL system has consistently not been shown to cause ejaculatory dysfunction. There are very few direct comparative clinical trials among these minimally invasive BPE technologies, and few cost analysis studies comparing MIST with medical therapy, although MIST is likely to be more cost-effective than conventional transurethral resection of the prostate gland. Contemporary data on MIST shows effective and safe outcomes for mLUTS/BPE/BPO in the short-term. Patients should be counselled on specific advantages and limitations of individual MIST, with the choice of MIST likely determined and offered based on the patient's preference and prostate anatomy, the surgeon's expertise and availability of specific MIST technology locally.

articles.title: Occlusion myocardial infarction without ST-elevation is associated with delayed angiography and a higher risk of cardiovascular events.
articles.journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: ST-segment elevation decides who undergoes immediate angiography, yet a quarter to a third of patients without it have an occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) and follow the slower non-ST-elevation pathway. Their outcome over extended follow-up compared with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), including non-fatal events, is poorly defined.

METHODS: In a retrospective single-centre cohort, we reclassified 313 consecutive patients with acute coronary syndrome undergoing angiography as STEMI, NSTEMI-OMI, or NSTEMI-non-OMI. OMI was pre-specified as culprit TIMI flow ≤2, and/or markedly elevated peak troponin with a new wall-motion abnormality. The composite of death, recurrent myocardial infarction, or cardiovascular readmission was assessed at 12 months and over a median follow-up of 26.2 months.

RESULTS: Of 313 patients, 177 had STEMI and 136 had no ST-elevation, of whom 54 (39.7%) fulfilled OMI criteria. Median time to angiography was 10.1 h in NSTEMI-OMI versus 1.0 h in STEMI (p < 0.001) and 15.9 h in NSTEMI-non-OMI (p = 0.140). The 12-month composite occurred in 16.7% of NSTEMI-OMI, 3.4% of STEMI, and 2.4% of NSTEMI-non-OMI (p = 0.001). The adjusted hazard ratio for NSTEMI-OMI was 3.46 (95% CI 1.70-7.02) versus STEMI and 3.31 (1.43-7.63) versus NSTEMI-non-OMI. In patients event-free at 12 months, the unadjusted hazard ratio versus STEMI was 3.56 (1.40-9.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Patients with OMI but no ST-segment elevation waited longer for angiography than STEMI and had a higher hazard of the composite outcome than both other groups, an excess persisting beyond the first year.

articles.title: Randomized Single-Masked Study of Preservative-Free Versus Preserved Hyaluronic Acid in Dry Eye Disease.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare the effects of preservative-free hyaluronic acid (PF HA) versus benzalkonium chloride-preserved hyaluronic acid (BAK HA) on symptoms and signs of dry eye disease (DED) using identical formulations except for preservative content.

METHODS: In this randomized, single-masked, 6-month trial, 47 patients with DED were randomized to receive PF HA or BAK HA. The primary outcome was the change in Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI) score from baseline to month 6. Secondary outcomes included non-invasive tear break-up time (NIBUT), Schirmer I test, fluorescein tear break-up time (TBUT), fluorescein corneal staining (FCS), lissamine green conjunctival staining (LCS), best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), and instillation frequency. Continuous and ordinal outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects and mixed-effects ordinal logistic regression models, respectively.

RESULTS: Forty-three patients completed the study. PF HA produced a greater OSDI score reduction than BAK HA (adjusted change, -14.36 vs. -9.42; P = 0.001), and ∼40% of PF HA-treated patients achieved normal OSDI scores at the final visit, compared with none in the BAK HA group. At the final visit, no significant between-group differences were observed for NIBUT, Schirmer I, TBUT, BCVA, FCS, or LCS. PF HA showed more favorable longitudinal changes in symptoms and selected signs, including OSDI (P < 0.001), NIBUT (P = 0.017), FCS (P = 0.002), and LCS (P < 0.001), indicating a treatment-by-time effect. PF HA was associated with lower instillation frequency (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Both formulations improved DED signs and symptoms. PF HA provided greater symptomatic relief and showed more favorable longitudinal changes.

TRANSLATIONAL RELEVANCE: These findings support the translation of experimental knowledge regarding preservative-induced ocular surface toxicity into evidence-based therapeutic decisions for long-term patient care.

articles.title: Insulin therapy with enteral and parenteral nutrition: a consensus statement endorsed by the Swiss Society for Endocrinology and Diabetology and the Swiss Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nutritional support with enteral or parenteral nutrition is often required in hospitalised patients and can impair glycaemic control. Despite its clinical importance, practical and uniform recommendations for insulin therapy are lacking.

METHODS: The Swiss Society for Endocrinology and Diabetology convened an expert panel to develop consensus guidance on insulin therapy for patients receiving enteral or parenteral nutrition. The working group reviewed available evidence, international guidelines and current practice in Swiss hospitals, and harmonised approaches across regions. The resulting statement provides strategies for insulin dosing in intermittent, continuous and bolus enteral nutrition, as well as parenteral nutrition, primarily for inpatient care, but also applicable to home-based nutritional support.

RECOMMENDATIONS: The insulin dose depends on the (known or calculated) basal insulin requirement and the carbohydrate content of the enteral or parenteral nutrition bag. For intermittent enteral nutrition (infused over 12-14 hours), intermediate-acting insulin with a duration of action matching the feeding duration is recommended. For continuous enteral nutrition (over 24 hours), long-acting insulin is preferred. When enteral nutrition is administered as boluses (2-3 hours each), short-acting insulin should be injected before each bolus, similar to prandial dosing with meals. For parenteral nutrition, adding short-acting insulin directly to the parenteral nutrition bag is encouraged, as it helps maintain stable glycaemic control without increasing the risk of hypoglycaemia. Across all modalities, correction insulin should be prescribed according to institutional schemes and individualised requirements, with additional units of correction insulin incorporated into the subsequent day's basal and (par)enteral nutrition insulin dose. The statement also provides recommendations for glucose monitoring, safe transitions between regimens, and management of unexpected interruptions in nutritional therapy.

CONSLUSIONS: This consensus statement, endorsed by the Swiss Society for Endocrinology and Diabetology and the Swiss Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism, represents a nationwide framework for insulin therapy in patients receiving enteral or parenteral nutrition in Switzerland. By standardising insulin use, it aims to enhance safety, reduce glycaemic variability and improve outcomes in hospitalised patients and in those receiving home-based specialised nutritional support.

articles.title: Ketamine/Esketamine in Clinical Practice: Areas of Consensus and Nonconsensus from an American Society of Clinical Psychopharmacology (ASCP) Delphi Panel Task Force.
articles.abstract: Objective: Important aspects of ketamine/esketamine treatment for mood disorders in contemporary practice remain inadequately addressed by the current evidence base, necessitating expert guidance in areas where clinical decision needs and implementation have advanced more rapidly than available data. The American Society of Clinical Psychopharmacology convened an expert task force to address unresolved questions about the practical use of these agents in "real-world" settings and potential disparities with evidence-based literature. Participants: An international panel of 21 academic mood disorder psychopharmacologist-psychiatrists with expertise in ketamine/esketamine clinical care and research. Evidence: Consensus was reached on 35/105 items (33%), encompassing domains involving diagnostic conditions, contraindications, maximum dosing, racemic versus enantiomeric preparations, oral or intramuscular delivery formulations, laboratory/safety monitoring, access, and parameters for judging treatment outcome. Consensus Process: Two successive Delphi rounds were completed alongside multiple virtual, email, and in-person meetings. Consensus was defined a priori as ≥75% agreement/disagreement on 5-point Likert survey items. All authors contributed to the interpretation and drafting of recommendations. Conclusions: Consensus agreement appears elusive for many key decision points involving ketamine/esketamine treatment, reflecting substantial disparities between "real-world" clinical practice and the shortcomings of the clinical trials' evidence base. Uncertainties persist regarding the use of novel formulations (eg, oral or intramuscular), high-dose ketamine infusions, ketamine-assisted psychotherapy, and use in conditions other than major depression. These areas of expert consensus and dissent lay the groundwork for future studies urgently needed to bridge the gap between evidence-based findings and treatment implementation in routine clinical settings.

articles.title: Establishing the Clinical Role of Digital Therapeutics in Major Depressive Disorder Treatment: A Consensus Panel Perspective.
articles.abstract: Digital therapeutics for major depressive disorder (MDD) are evidence-based clinical interventions that can help address barriers in access to effective specialty/secondary care, patient preference for nonpharmacologic options, and continuity of care between visits. Despite growing evidence of efficacy, clinical adoption lags and current health care systems do not provide guidance for clinicians on their evaluation or implementation. In May 2026, a multidisciplinary expert consensus panel convened virtually to discuss the role of digital therapeutics in the management of MDD across primary care, specialty psychiatry, and community mental health practice in the United States and Europe. The panel developed four consensus statements regarding the evaluation, selection, and implementation of digital therapeutics for MDD. Digital therapeutics were identified as a distinct clinical category that should be evaluated using principles similar to other evidence-based MDD treatments, with efficacy as the primary selection criterion. Digital therapeutics may be incorporated across multiple stages of stepped-care management, including bridge-to-care and augmentation treatment. The panel identified clinician unfamiliarity, implementation challenges, and uncertainty regarding patient engagement as key adoption barriers. The consensus recommendations are intended to help clinicians select evidence-based digital therapeutics, position them appropriately within stepped-care management of MDD, and address the barriers preventing translation of current evidence into routine clinical practice.

articles.title: RELAX Perinatal Digital Intervention to Prevent Increasing Anxiety: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Anxiety disorders affect 1 in 5 pregnant women and birthing people. Cognitive bias modification for interpretation reduces anxiety and repetitive negative thinking (RNT; a risk factor for anxiety) among nonpregnant samples.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether adding pregnancy-tailored cognitive bias modification for interpretation to usual maternity care (UC) prevents increased anxiety during pregnancy; reduces anxiety, depression, and RNT before and after birth; and improves functioning before and after birth compared with UC.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: The RELAX (Reducing Levels of Anxiety) 2-arm, parallel-group, multisite, superiority, phase 2b randomized clinical trial recruited participants from June 2023 to July 2024, with final assessment in April 2025. Participants included pregnant individuals in the UK at 16 to 28 weeks' gestation, with high RNT and up to moderate anxiety, recruited via antenatal clinics or self-referral.

INTERVENTION: Participants were randomized to the self-led digital intervention (RELAX plus UC), involving twelve 17-minute sessions over 4 weeks, or to UC.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Assessments took place at baseline before randomization (T0) and 4 weeks (T1), 8 weeks (T2), and 36 weeks (T3; 12-24 weeks after birth) after randomization. The primary outcome was anxiety, as assessed by the 7-item Generalized Anxiety Disorder scale (GAD-7) at T2 and as a secondary outcome at T3. Secondary outcomes included RNT (assessed by the 10-item trait version of the Repetitive Thinking Questionnaire [RTQ-10]), depression (general and perinatal, assessed by the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 [PHQ-9] and Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale [EPDS]), perinatal anxiety (assessed by the Perinatal Anxiety Screening Scale [PASS]), worry (assessed by the Penn State Worry Questionnaire [PSWQ]), and functioning (assessed by the Work and Social Adjustment Scale [WSAS]). Interpretation bias at T1 was the hypothesized mechanism. Analysis was performed using a modified intention-to-treat approach.

RESULTS: A total of 268 participants were randomized (mean [SD] age 33.7 [3.9] years; 174 [64.9%] married). Anxiety was significantly lower for RELAX participants vs UC (mean GAD-7 difference, -1.5; 95% CI, -2.4 to -0.6; P = .001). Depression (mean PHQ-9 difference, -0.8; 95% CI -1.5 to -0.1; and mean EPDS difference, -1.1; 95% CI, -2.0 to -0.2), RNT (mean RTQ-10 difference, -2.7; 95% CI, -4.5 to -0.9), worry (mean PSWQ difference, -3.6; 95% CI, -5.9 to -1.3), and perinatal anxiety (mean PASS difference, -5.5; 95% CI, -8.2 to -2.8) were significantly lower at T2. Effects on general anxiety (mean GAD-7 difference, -1.0; 95% CI, -1.9 to -0.1), postnatal depression (mean EPDS difference, -1.3; 95% CI, -2.4 to -0.2), and RNT (mean RTQ-10 difference, -2.4; 95% CI, -4.6 to -0.2) were sustained at T3. RELAX promoted more positive interpretations vs UC (mean difference, 2.1; 95% CI, 1.8-2.3) that did not mediate effects at T2 (indirect effect on GAD-7, -0.2; percentile bootstrap 95% CI, -0.4 to 0.1). Functioning did not differ at T2 (mean WSAS difference, -1.0; 95% CI, -2.5 to 0.5) or T3 (mean WSAS difference, -0.8; 95% CI, -2.7 to 1.2), nor did perinatal anxiety (mean PASS difference, -2.1; 95% CI, -5.5 to 1.4), general depression (mean PHQ-9 difference, -0.2; 95% CI, -1.2 to 0.9), or worry (mean PSWQ difference, -1.4; 95% CI, -4.1 to 1.3) at T3.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial, anxiety was lower during pregnancy and postnatally for RELAX plus UC participants compared with those receiving UC. Integrating RELAX into maternity care for those at risk of increased anxiety has potential to improve maternal mental health.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://www.isrctn.com/ISRCTN12754931.

articles.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and Maternal Health Outcomes in Pregnant and Postpartum Individuals: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are increasingly used to support maternal health, but randomized evidence is limited.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether access to a generative AI maternal health chatbot improved 12-month maternal health outcomes.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This 2-group randomized clinical trial enrolled 400 participants from October 2023 to December 2024, with 12-month follow-up completed in December 2025. Participants were recruited online across 49 US states and the District of Columbia. Eligible participants were English-speaking, aged 14 years or older, pregnant or parenting an infant younger than 6 months, and self-identified as members of racial and/or ethnic minoritized groups.

INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive access to the chatbot or an active control consisting of monthly children's books.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes were anxiety and depression symptoms at 12 months measured using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 and Patient Health Questionnaire-9. Secondary outcomes included emergency department visits, pregnancy-related complications, postpartum care checkups, effective contraception use, and sleep duration.

RESULTS: Among 400 randomized participants, the mean (SD) age was 32.6 (5.1) years; 200 (50%) were parenting an infant at enrollment; and 10 (2%) identified as American Indian or Alaska Native, 80 (20%) Asian, 188 (47%) Black or African American, 57 (14%) multiracial, and 65 (16%) Hispanic or Latino. The AI chatbot was not associated with differences in anxiety scores (adjusted mean difference, 0.10; 95% CI, -0.77 to 0.96) or depression scores (adjusted mean difference, -0.23; 95% CI, -1.05 to 0.59), nor with emergency department visits, postpartum care, contraception use, or sleep duration. Among participants pregnant at enrollment, the chatbot was associated with more self-reported pregnancy-related complications in the secondary 12-month end point analysis, but not in longitudinal analyses. Higher chatbot engagement was associated with longer sleep duration and higher anxiety scores in exploratory within-group analyses.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial of pregnant and postpartum individuals from racial and ethnic minoritized groups, access to a generative artificial intelligence maternal health chatbot did not improve maternal anxiety or depression at 12 months compared with an active control. Secondary and exploratory findings should be interpreted cautiously.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06053515.

articles.title: Complications and predictors of catheter failure in pediatric long peripheral and midline catheters: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The use of long peripheral catheters (LPCs) and midline catheters (MCs) in pediatric patients is increasing, although evidence regarding their safety and complications remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: To describe complications associated with LPCs and MCs in pediatric patients and identify predictors of catheter failure.

METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted between July 2022 and March 2025 in pediatric patients (17 days-16 years) requiring LPC or MC insertion by nursing staff in a tertiary hospital. Demographic, clinical, catheter-related, and outcome variables were collected. Catheter failure was defined as non-elective removal before completion of planned intravenous therapy. Associations were analyzed using Mann-Whitney U, Fisher's exact, or χ2 tests.

RESULTS: Sixty-nine catheters were included. Overall, 69.6% remained in place until completion of therapy, with a mean dwell time of 11.9 days (SD 7.97). The complication rate was 25.6 per 1000 catheter-days. Thrombosis was the most frequent complication (8.7%; 7.3 per 1000 catheter-days). Difficult venous access was significantly associated with catheter failure (p = 0.044), whereas no significant associations with thrombosis were identified. According to NAVIGATE nomenclature, catheters with axillary or subclavian tip locations were classified as MCs and those with more distal tips as LPCs.

CONCLUSIONS: LPCs and MCs allowed completion of intravenous therapy in most pediatric patients. Thrombosis was the most clinically relevant complication. Larger studies are needed to identify predictors of catheter failure and thrombosis.

articles.title: Impact of Neuromuscular Blocking Agents on Hospital Outcomes in Mechanically Ventilated Patients With Sepsis: Propensity Score Analyses of A Nationwide Sepsis Cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of neuromuscular blocking agents (NMBAs) on hospital outcomes in patients with sepsis requiring mechanical ventilation (MV) remains uncertain and warrants further evaluation.

METHODS: We analyzed data from a nationwide sepsis cohort comprising 20 university-affiliated or tertiary hospitals, including adult patients with sepsis who required MV. Patients who received continuous intravenous NMBAs within 3 days of intensive care unit (ICU) admission were compared with those who did not. To adjust for baseline imbalances, both inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and propensity score matching (PSM) were used.

RESULTS: Of 13,827 patients with sepsis, 1,255 receiving MV were analyzed (mean age, 68.3 ± 13.9 years; 65.7% male; NMBA use, 25.7%). In the IPTW-adjusted Cox model, NMBA use was not associated with in-hospital mortality. Similarly, in the PSM cohort (292 NMBA-treated vs. 292 matched controls), in-hospital mortality did not differ between groups (17.1% vs. 18.8%; P = 0.590). However, NMBA use was associated with a longer ICU stay (absolute difference: 3.0 days [95% confidence interval, 0.3-5.7]; P = 0.003) and showed a trend toward a longer MV duration and hospital stay (Wilcoxon signed-rank test). Kaplan-Meier analysis also demonstrated significantly longer ICU stays in the NMBA group (log-rank P = 0.006). The incidence of ventilator-associated pneumonia was significantly higher in the NMBA group (8.6% vs. 4.5%; P = 0.044).

CONCLUSION: In patients with sepsis requiring MV, the use of NMBAs was not associated with in-hospital mortality but was linked to longer ICU stays and a higher incidence of ventilator-associated pneumonia. These findings underscore the need for cautious use of continuous NMBA infusion in this population.

articles.title: Impact of Mass Resignation of Junior Doctors in Korea on Major Interventions: Interrupted Time Series Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: On February 19, 2024, approximately 10,000 junior doctors in Republic of Korea (= South Korea) resigned en masse, in protest of newly announced government healthcare policies. This abrupt reduction in the medical workforce may have compromised healthcare accessibility and caused delays in major surgical procedures and critical care. This study aimed to assess the nationwide impact of the resignation on the provision of medical services in Korea.

METHODS: Monthly intervention volumes for Diseases & Practices of National Interest (DPNI) were obtained from the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service for the period from January 2019 to August 2024. The impact of the mass resignation on intervention volumes was evaluated using interrupted time series segmented regression analysis, by level of medical institution.

RESULTS: Of the 20 DPNIs, 16 met the inclusion criteria. Thirteen DPNIs exhibited immediate reductions in intervention volumes at tertiary hospitals following the mass resignation, with decreases ranging from 18.7% to 62.9% relative to pre-resignation monthly averages. In contrast, no immediate decline was observed for hemodialysis for chronic renal failure, cerebral thrombectomy, and liver cancer surgery. No immediate changes were observed in non-tertiary general hospitals. Long-term effects could not be reliably assessed due to the limited number of post-resignation data points.

CONCLUSION: The mass resignation of junior doctors was associated with substantial and immediate reductions in healthcare service provision across multiple clinical specialties, particularly in tertiary hospitals. The absence of immediate effects for certain DPNIs likely reflects their lower reliance on junior doctors, as well as the urgency or structural characteristics of these interventions. These findings highlight the need for health policies that address unmet healthcare needs and mitigate potential adverse health outcomes resulting from delayed or foregone medical services.

articles.title: Circulating Estradiol as an Independent Risk Factor for Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Fibrosis Risk in Women: Evidence From a Multicenter Health-Checkup Cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) shows marked sexual dimorphism, with estrogen believed to be liver-protective. This study investigated the independent association between circulating estradiol levels, MASLD, and advanced fibrosis (defined by fibrosis index-4 [FIB-4] ≥ 1.3) in Korean women, utilizing stratified analyses by age and body mass index (BMI) to identify context-dependent effects.

METHODS: We analyzed cross-sectional data from the Korean Health Screening-Based Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease Registry, including 995 women (352 with MASLD). Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association of log2-transformed estradiol with MASLD and high-risk fibrosis, stratified by age (proxy for menopausal status, ≥ 50 vs. < 50 years) and BMI (≥ 25 vs. < 25 kg/m²).

RESULTS: In multivariable analysis of the entire cohort, lower estradiol levels were independently associated with MASLD (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.88; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.79-0.98; P = 0.025). This association was particularly evident in women with lower BMI (aOR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.71-0.98), but not in high BMI women, suggesting attenuation of estrogen's metabolic protection in the presence of obesity. Estradiol demonstrated a strong and consistent inverse association with FIB-4 ≥ 1.3 (aOR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.56-0.75; P < 0.001). This protective antifibrotic effect remained robust across BMI strata and was also significant in women aged ≥ 50 years (aOR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.59-0.82; P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Low circulating estradiol independently increases the risk of MASLD and high-risk fibrosis in women. While its protective effect against steatosis weakens with obesity, its antifibrotic effect remains strong across all subgroups. Estradiol may serve as an important hormonal marker for risk stratification in female MASLD patients.

articles.title: Facilitators and barriers to the early implementation of speaking valves in intensive care: a qualitative study using normalisation process theory.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The utilization of tracheostomy in conjunction with mechanical ventilation significantly impacts various physiological functions, particularly the ability to communicate verbally. Speaking valves, integrated into the ventilator circuit, restore phonation and are recognised internationally as best practice, yet remain underused in Swedish intensive care units (ICUs). Beyond enabling verbal communication, the early use of speaking valves has been associated with improved swallowing, secretion management, and reduced duration of mechanical ventilation. The TRACH INSPIRE project aims to promote their implementation in Swedish ICUs. This study explored facilitators and barriers to the early interprofessional implementation of speaking valves in tracheostomised, mechanically ventilated ICU patients.

METHODS: This qualitative study design analysed 19 semi-structured interview data, pre-implementation, with ICU professionals (intensivists, nurses, physiotherapists, and speech-language pathologists) from two participating ICUs in the TRACH INSPIRE project conducted in January-February 2025. Inclusion criteria were that the participants must have participated in the interprofessional competency training for the TRACH INSPIRE project. No formal exclusion criteria were defined. The Data were analysed using deductive content analysis guided by the Normalisation Process Theory (NPT), which examines how new practices are embedded into routine care.

RESULTS: Twelve subcategories were identified that were organized according to the NPT. Facilitators included a shared understanding of the intervention's value, strong professional commitment, structured implementation processes, managerial support, clearly defined roles, effective interprofessional collaboration, targeted training, and open communication. Barriers centred on organisational constraints such as limited resources, low patient volumes, lack of a comprehensive implementation strategy, and documentation-related challenges.

CONCLUSIONS: Early implementation of speaking valves in mechanically ventilated, tracheostomised ICU patients is supported by high interprofessional engagement, shared recognition of benefits, and structured training. However, operational limitations, small eligible patient populations, and documentation burdens present notable challenges. Inclusive team strategies, maintaining competencies, and streamlined processes may promote sustainable integration into routine ICU practice.

articles.title: Genetic associations between brain and cognitive flexibility: A Mendelian randomization study.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Cognitive flexibility (CF) is an important psychological function, but research investigating brain characteristics related to CF at the whole-brain level is limited.

OBJECTIVE: To examine whether genetically proxied brain imaging traits are associated with cognitive flexibility, using Mendelian randomization (MR) under standard MR assumptions.

DESIGN, SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: We performed a two-sample MR analysis using publicly available GWAS summary statistics from UK Biobank and imaging genetics consortia to evaluate evidence of genetically predicted associations between brain imaging traits and Trail Making Test Part B (TMTB) performance. All participants were of European ancestry. Data extraction and analysis started from May to November 2024.

EXPOSURES: The genetic instruments for 704 characteristics related to brain region volumes; brain sulcal morphology (sulcus depth and sulcus opening distance (SOD)); brain white matter (WM) microstructure (axial diffusivity (AD), fractional anisotropy (FA); mean diffusivity (MD); mode of anisotropy (MO), radial diffusivity (RD)); cortical structure (surface average (SA); thickness average (TA)); functional networks (amplitude of low frequency fluctuations (ALFFs), functional connectivity (FC) and structural connectivity (SC)). GWAS sample sizes ranged approximately from 18,101 to 47,226, depending on the imaging phenotype.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Trail Making Test Part B performance in 93,024 European-ancestry participants, defined in the source GWAS as the residual of the log10-transformed alphanumeric trail time after regressing out the log10-transformed numeric path time, so that the measure indexes set-shifting net of basic visual-scanning and psychomotor speed; higher values indicate a longer completion time and therefore worse performance.

RESULTS: In univariable MR, 80 brain imaging traits showed nominal associations with TMT-B performance after excluding signals flagged by heterogeneity or pleiotropy tests. After within-domain multiple-testing correction, 10 associations remained significant (Bonferroni-adjusted P < 0.05); using FDR correction, 21 associations survived within-domain FDR q < 0.05 and 6 survived global FDR q < 0.05. Effect sizes were (β range: -0.077 [-0.114 to -0.039] to 0.203 [0.079 to 0.328] change in standardized TMT-B time per SD change in exposure). In multivariable MR, 14 traits showed independent associations with TMT-B performance; key traits associated with shorter TMT-B time included left banks of the superior temporal sulcus volume, left ventral diencephalon volume, left thalamus volume, right inferior parietal sulcus opening distance, insular surface area, temporal gyrus thickness, selected fronto-temporal functional connectivity, and selected dorsal attention/visual and control/amygdala structural connectivity. Traits associated with longer TMT-B time included left superior frontal sulcus opening distance, inferior frontal gyrus ALFF, selected fronto-temporal functional connectivity, and selected dorsal attention/salience and salience/caudate structural connectivity.

CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: These MR results are broadly consistent with prior neurocognitive literature and highlight additional brain imaging phenotypes that warrant follow-up. Given the limited testability of key MR assumptions-particularly for brain imaging traits and TMT-B as a proxy outcome-no causal claim is made, our findings have not yet been independently replicated in an external cohort, and they should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating and require triangulation with complementary designs (e.g., longitudinal and experimental studies).

articles.title: Mutually exclusive patterns of cigarette and e-cigarette use and self-rated anxiety among adolescents: a national school-based cross-sectional analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescent e-cigarette use has increased in England, but associations between nicotine-use patterns and anxiety remain unclear.

METHODS: We analysed cross-sectional data from 11,142 pupils aged 11-15 years in probability-sampled schools in the 2023 Smoking, Drinking and Drug Use among Young People in England survey. Participants were classified into four mutually exclusive current nicotine-use groups. Anxiety was measured on a 0-10 scale. Survey-weighted linear, logistic and partial proportional-odds models adjusted for age, gender, ethnicity and family affluence; sensitivity analyses additionally adjusted for recent alcohol and cannabis use.

RESULTS: Weighted prevalence was 90.9% for no current nicotine use, 6.5% for exclusive e-cigarette use, 0.5% for exclusive smoking and 2.2% for dual use. Mean anxiety was 3.72 (95% CI 3.65-3.80), and 30.5% reported high anxiety (scores 6-10). Compared with non-use, adjusted anxiety scores were higher among exclusive e-cigarette users (β = 0.71, 95% CI 0.40-1.01) and dual users (β = 1.22, 95% CI 0.59-1.84), as were odds of high anxiety (OR = 1.46, 95% CI 1.20-1.78; OR = 2.09, 95% CI 1.44-3.04). Associations were attenuated but persisted after adjustment for alcohol and cannabis use. Dual use did not differ significantly from exclusive vaping. Exclusive smoking estimates were positive but imprecise (n = 38).

CONCLUSIONS: Exclusive e-cigarette and dual use were associated with greater self-rated anxiety among adolescents in England. Cross-sectional data preclude causal inference; longitudinal studies are needed to establish direction and intervention implications.

articles.title: Exogenous hormones alleviate drought stress with the upregulation of heat shock-related genes and enhanced lipid accumulation in tea plants (Camellia sinensis).
articles.abstract: Drought stress (DS) impairs growth and metabolism in tea plants, and exogenous hormones are important regulators of drought responses. By integrating physiological, transcriptomic, and metabolomic analyses, the study investigated the effects of exogenous hormones on the drought responses of tea plants. Drought stress was simulated with a 20% PEG-6000 solution, followed by foliar application of indole-3-acetic acid (IAA), methyl jasmonate (MeJA), salicylic acid (SA), or abscisic acid (ABA), respectively. The results showed that exogenous hormones reduced leaf water loss rate by 17.90% to 30.61% compared with the DS treatment, consistent with mitigation of drought-induced physiological stress. Furthermore, exogenous hormones induced differentially expressed genes (DEGs) involved in photosynthesis and phenylpropanoid biosynthesis pathways. Notably, IAA and SA significantly upregulated the expression of CsHsp70 and CsHsp90A. Meanwhile, exogenous hormones elevated the content of lipids and flavonoids, with the enhanced accumulation of 53 lipid metabolites. Multi-omics analysis suggested that the enhanced lipid accumulation and upregulation of heat shock-related genes were associated with the alleviation of drought stress. Our findings laid biochemical foundations for hormone-based agronomic strategies to maintain tea quality.

articles.title: Percutaneous Endoscopic Gastrostomy Versus Image-Guided Gastrostomy Placement in Patients With Cirrhosis: A Multi-Institutional Research Network Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The selection of an appropriate technique for placement of a gastrostomy tube in patients with cirrhosis remains controversial due to concerns about adverse events. We used real-world data to compare outcomes after percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) versus fluoroscopically guided gastrostomy by an interventional radiologist (IR G-tube) in patients with cirrhosis.

METHODS: We performed a multicenter retrospective cohort study of adults with cirrhosis who underwent gastrostomy tube placement from 2014 to 2023 using the TriNetX Research Network. Using relevant Current Procedural Terminology codes, patients were categorized into 2 groups: PEG (43246/0DH64UZ) or fluoroscopic IR G-tube (49440/0DH63UZ). Periprocedural adverse events were defined as short-term (14 d) or long-term (180 d). Propensity score matching was performed using demographic, clinical, and available laboratory covariates. Binary outcomes were reported as adjusted odds ratios (aOR) with 95% CIs, whereas mortality was reported using adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) from Cox proportional hazards models. Survival was assessed with Kaplan-Meier analysis and log-rank testing.

RESULTS: Of the 5028 patients meeting selection criteria, 1579 underwent PEG placement and 3449 underwent IR G-tube placement. Adjusted odds of periprocedural adverse events for PEG vs IR G-tube were as follows: aspiration pneumonia (aOR: 0.66, 95% CI: 0.51-0.85), hemorrhage (aOR: 0.79, CI: 0.59-1.06), blood transfusion (aOR: 0.99, CI: 0.78-1.27), and infection or peritonitis (aOR: 0.96, CI: 0.68-1.34). In the 6-month follow-up period, PEG placement was associated with lower odds of tube malfunction (aOR: 0.78, 95% CI: 0.64-0.96) and tube replacement (aOR: 0.47, 95% CI: 0.36-0.63). At 6 months, PEG placement was also associated with lower mortality risk (aHR: 0.80, 95% CI: 0.70-0.91; P=0.011).

CONCLUSIONS: In a large multicenter cohort of patients with cirrhosis, PEG and IR G-tube placement had similar short-term rates of bleeding and infectious adverse events, whereas PEG was associated with fewer tube malfunctions and replacements and lower observed mortality at 6 months.

articles.title: Protocol for the development and transcriptomic analysis of multiple human kidney disease models.
articles.abstract: Podocyte injury is a hallmark of chronic kidney disease and organ failure. Here, we present a protocol to model multiple types of human kidney diseases by inducing early, sublethal podocyte injury using chemical, inflammatory, metabolic, and infectious stressors. We describe steps for cell differentiation, controlled injury induction, phenotypic assessment, transcriptomic analysis, and validation studies using clinical data. This approach enables reproducible modeling of diverse injury states and identification of shared and condition-specific molecular responses. For complete information on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Barreto et al.1.

articles.title: Managing Small Intestinal Bacterial Overgrowth in Pediatric Short Bowel Syndrome: A Consensus Statement.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) is a common and clinically important complication of short bowel syndrome (SBS) in children, contributing to feeding intolerance, malabsorption, bloodstream infections, and frequent antibiotic exposure. Diagnostic and management practices vary widely across centers, and no rigorously developed, evidence-informed pediatric-specific guidance currently exists.

OBJECTIVE: To develop international, pediatric-specific, expert consensus recommendations for the diagnosis and management of SIBO in children with SBS, with emphasis on diagnostic approach, antibiotic therapy, treatment response, and prevention.

EVIDENCE REVIEW: A modified Delphi process was conducted between April 4, 2024, and February 18, 2025. A 7-member steering committee reviewed pediatric and adult SIBO literature using the terms small-intestinal bacterial overgrowth, short bowel syndrome, intestinal failure, and pediatric. Because pediatric-specific data were limited and study designs were heterogeneous, systematic reviews and meta-analyses were not feasible. Fifty-five international experts from multidisciplinary intestinal rehabilitation programs in North America and Europe were invited to participate in 3 rounds of anonymous online surveys and 2 in-person moderated consensus meetings. Draft statements were iteratively refined. Consensus was defined a priori as agreement of 75% or greater among respondents.

FINDINGS: Completed surveys were received from 33 participants in round 1, 38 in round 2, and 28 in round 3. Consensus was achieved on 21 statements involving diagnostic approaches, therapeutic strategies, and monitoring practices. Recommendations addressed the use of breath testing and clinical criteria, indications for empiric antibiotic therapy and cycling, antibiotic selection and duration, and dietary considerations. Symptomatic improvement was considered an acceptable indicator of treatment response. Metronidazole was identified as the preferred first-line antibiotic, and long-term antibiotic cycling was supported for selected patients with recurrent, treatment-responsive SIBO. Collectively, the statements provide a practical framework to support consistent clinical decision-making in pediatric SBS-associated SIBO.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This Delphi-based consensus provides the first international pediatric-specific guidance for diagnosing and managing SIBO in children with SBS. Implementation of these recommendations may reduce practice variability, support more judicious antibiotic use, and improve patient outcomes while establishing a foundation for future research in this high-risk population.

articles.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Obesity-Related Cancer by Diabetes Severity.
Early Metformin Initiation and Glycemic Outcomes in Gestational Diabetes: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Conventional approaches to analyzing composite end points in clinical trials may not fully capture clinically meaningful treatment effects.

OBJECTIVE: To estimate treatment effects of early metformin initiation on clinically ordered glycemic outcomes (insulin initiation and fasting hyperglycemia at gestational weeks 32 and 38) using generalized pairwise comparisons (GPCs).

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This secondary analysis of a double-masked, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial (conducted from June 2017 through September 2022) at 2 centers in Ireland (1 tertiary hospital and 1 regional hospital) included participants with gestational diabetes based on World Health Organization 2013 criteria. Participants were followed up through 12 weeks post partum. The data analysis was performed between October 18, 2025, and February 2, 2026.

INTERVENTION: Participants were randomized 1:1 to metformin (maximum dose, 2500 mg) or matching placebo, in addition to usual care.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Generalized pairwise comparisons were performed using (1) a prioritized hierarchy (insulin initiation, fasting hyperglycemia at week 32, and fasting hyperglycemia at week 38) and (2) nonprioritized analyses of each end point, with overall summaries using equal weights and prespecified clinical weights (0.50, 0.25, and 0.25, respectively). Treatment effect sizes were summarized using win ratio (WR), net treatment benefit (NTB), and win odds (WO).

RESULTS: Of 535 randomized pregnancies, 526 (262 placebo [49.0%] and 264 metformin [51.0%]; mean [SD] age of participants, 34.4 [4.8] years) had primary outcome data. Prioritized GPCs favored metformin over placebo for the composite outcome (WR, 1.46 [95% CI, 1.13-1.89]; NTB, 13.7 percentage points [95% CI, 4.3-22.8 percentage points]; WO, 1.34 [95% CI, 1.10-1.64]) (P = .004). The largest separation was observed for insulin initiation (WR, 1.68 [95% CI, 1.19-2.38]; NTB, 12.7 percentage points [95% CI, 4.2-21.0 percentage points]) (P = .003). Nonprioritized overall summaries favored metformin (WR, 1.53 [95% CI, 1.16-2.01]; NTB, 7.5 percentage points [95% CI, 2.7-12.3 percentage points]; WO, 1.32 [95% CI, 1.10-1.57]) (P = .002), with consistent clinically weighted results (WR, 1.57 [95% CI, 1.19-2.08]; NTB, 8.8 percentage points [95% CI, 3.4-14.2 percentage points]; WO, 1.39 [95% CI, 1.14-1.70]) (P = .001).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial, prioritized and nonprioritized GPCs yielded statistically significant overall estimates favoring early metformin initiation over placebo across insulin initiation and fasting hyperglycemia outcomes. These findings complement the original primary analysis, provide a more clinically interpretable assessment of the composite outcome, and may inform prospective end point design in future trials.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02980276; EudraCT: 2016-001644-19.

articles.title: Noninpatient Alternative Treatment Venues for Acute Care Needs.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Hospitalizations are costly and may lead to adverse events. Some health systems offer treatment in alternative venues of care for select patients.

OBJECTIVE: To describe use and short-term outcomes of emergency department (ED) patients transitioned to noninpatient care settings (ambulatory treatment center [ATC], advanced care at home [ACAH], or emergency department observation unit [EDOU]) compared with inpatient care.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study of ED patients aged 19 years or older was conducted from January 1, 2024, to June 30, 2025, at multisite community ED and inpatient medical centers within an integrated delivery system (Kaiser Permanente Northern California). Included patients had active health plan membership; had an ED visit for heart failure, pneumonia, cellulitis, urinary tract infection, COVID-19, or anemia; and had their care transitioned to an ATC, ACAH program (Kaiser Permanente Advanced Care at Home), EDOU, or inpatient bed.

EXPOSURE: Treatment venue.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The main outcomes were care escalation (inpatient admission) for patients treated in an ATC, ACAH program, or EDOU, as well as 7-day ED return visits, 30-day hospitalizations, and 30-day mortality following care completion across all venues. Unadjusted outcome rates are reported.

RESULTS: This study included 26 618 ED encounters (median patient age, 77 years [IQR, 65-85 years]; 52.6% female). Among 22 755 unique patients, 87.4% had 1 encounter, 9.8% had 2 encounters, and 2.8% had more than 2 encounters. There were 728 (2.7%), 880 (3.3%), 5133 (19.3%), and 19 877 (74.7%) encounters in ATC, ACAH, EDOU, and hospital settings, respectively. One-quarter of patients (25.3%) received care in an ATC, ACAH program, or EDOU. Inpatient admission rates were lower for ATC and ACAH encounters than for EDOU encounters (4.3% [95% CI, 2.7%-5.8%], 5.3% [3.8%-6.8%], and 28.0% [26.8%-29.2%], respectively). Rates of 7-day ED visits were similar across venues (ATC: 10.4% [95% CI, 7.8%-12.9%]; ACAH: 5.3% [3.8%-6.8%]; EDOU: 9.2% [8.4%-10.0%]; and hospital: 8.5% [8.1%-8.9%]). In contrast, 30-day mortality and hospitalization rates were lower among ATC, ACAH, and EDOU encounters than in hospital encounters (30-day mortality: 2.1% [95% CI, 1.0%-3.2%], 1.7% [0.8%-2.6%], 2.8% [2.3%-3.2%], and 5.3% [5.0%-5.6%]; and 30-day hospitalization: 11.4% [95% CI, 8.8%-14.1%], 8.3% [6.3%-10.2%], 12.7% [11.7%-13.7%], and 15.3% [14.7%-15.8%], respectively).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of patients treated in alternative venues of care, one-quarter received care in an ATC, ACAH program, or EDOU. These findings suggest that adoption of novel treatment spaces for appropriately selected patients may allow health systems to focus hospital resources on the patients with the most complex needs.

articles.title: Prognostic value of Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio after percutaneous coronary intervention.
authors: on behalf of the FAVOR III China study group
articles.journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) physiological indices have prognostic relevance. Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (μQFR) enables wire-free, rapid, single-view functional assessment, yet its long-term prognostic value after PCI remains incompletely established.

AIMS: We sought to evaluate the prognostic value of post-PCI μQFR for long-term adverse outcomes.

METHODS: This prespecified subgroup analysis of the FAVOR III China trial included 3,825 patients. All PCI-treated vessels with a reference diameter ≥2.5 mm and 50-90% diameter stenosis were analysed for offline post-PCI μQFR. The primary endpoint was 5-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; including death from any cause, myocardial infarction, or ischaemia-driven revascularisation).

RESULTS: Post-PCI μQFR was successfully analysed in 4,196 vessels from 3,455 patients, with similar distributions between the randomised treatment groups. At 5 years, a low post-PCI μQFR was associated with a higher incidence of MACE compared with the intermediate and high post-PCI μQFR tertiles (23.1% vs 19.0% vs 17.2%; p=0.001). Using the highest tertile (μQFR>0.95) as a reference, adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) were 1.08 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.87-1.34) for the intermediate tertile (0.92-0.95) and 1.30 (95% CI: 1.06-1.60) for the lowest tertile (μQFR ≤0.91). Using a receiver operating characteristic-derived cutoff, MACE occurred more frequently in patients with post-PCI μQFR <0.94 (22.3% vs 17.4%, aHR 1.23, 95% CI: 1.04-1.47; p=0.02) than in those with post-PCI μQFR ≥0.94. No significant interaction was observed between treatment strategy and post-PCI μQFR (p for interaction=0.23).

CONCLUSIONS: Post-PCI μQFR distributions were similar between treatment groups, but lower values were associated with higher 5-year adverse event risk without significant treatment interaction. Its limited binary discrimination supports use as a continuous metric for post-PCI physiological risk stratification. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT03656848).

articles.title: Guided P2Y12 inhibitor selection after rapid CYP2C19 genotyping in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention.
articles.journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dual antiplatelet therapy remains the standard treatment following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). While prasugrel and ticagrelor offer consistent antiplatelet effects, they increase bleeding risk compared with clopidogrel, which requires CYP2C19 bioactivation.

AIMS: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of rapid CYP2C19 genotyping at the time of PCI on P2Y12 inhibitor selection and clinical outcomes in real-world patients.

METHODS: A total of 974 patients who underwent PCI and rapid CYP2C19 genotyping and received P2Y12 inhibitor treatment were included. P2Y12 inhibitor selection, P2Y12 inhibitor switching, major atherothrombotic events (MAE; a composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, stent thrombosis, or unstable angina requiring revascularisation), and bleeding events were assessed throughout the first year post-PCI. Time-varying Cox regression analysis was performed to assess event risk in patients treated with clopidogrel (reference) versus prasugrel/ticagrelor after stratifying by loss-of-function (LOF) status and adjusting for stratum-specific confounders.

RESULTS: Clopidogrel was prescribed more frequently at discharge among CYP2C19 non-LOF versus LOF carriers (43% [296/691] vs 31% [87/283]; p<0.001). The median duration of follow-up was 359 days (interquartile range [IQR] 190-362 days). Among LOF allele carriers de-escalating to clopidogrel, the median de-escalation time was 180 days (IQR 92-354 days). MAE were not significantly different between P2Y12 inhibitor regimens after stratifying by LOF status (LOF-prasugrel/ticagrelor [n=147] vs LOF-clopidogrel [n=136]: adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0.87 [95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.36-2.10]; non-LOF-prasugrel/ticagrelor [n=272] vs non-LOF-clopidogrel [n=419]: adjusted HR 1.26, 95% CI: 0.67-2.36). No significant differences in Bleeding Academic Research Consortium bleeding events were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: This real-world study shows that, among LOF carriers managed with rapid CYP2C19 genotyping and delayed de-escalation, ischaemic and bleeding event rates were not significantly different between those taking clopidogrel versus those taking prasugrel/ticagrelor, though findings should be interpreted cautiously.

articles.title: Prediction of coronary events by computed tomography-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio.
articles.journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (CT-μFR) provides a non-invasive measure of vessel-level ischaemia but may not capture local haemodynamic abnormalities reflected by the longitudinal pressure gradient across the lesion (CT-μFR gradient).

AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the association of CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient with 3-year vessel-level subsequent coronary events and to determine the incremental prognostic value of their combined assessment.

METHODS: Our study included a total of 885 vessels from 312 patients who underwent invasive coronary angiography for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or stable angina and had prior CCTA performed 6 months to 3 years earlier. CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient were assessed by an independent core laboratory blinded to the clinical data. The primary outcome was 3-year subsequent coronary events (a composite of vessel-specific myocardial infarction or urgent revascularisation for ACS). The discrimination ability of predictive models was assessed using Harrell's C-index.

RESULTS: Vessels with CT-μFR ≤0.80 or a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm had a higher risk of events than those with CT-μFR>0.80 (79.1% vs 20.4%, adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 6.87, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.26-8.96; p<0.001) or a CT-μFR gradient <0.004/mm (72.6% vs 27.4%, adjusted HR 4.08, 95% CI: 3.15-5.28; p<0.001), respectively. Among vessels with CT-μFR>0.80, a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm remained associated with increased risk (adjusted HR 2.59, 95% CI: 1.63-4.11; p<0.001). Adding the CT-μFR gradient to CT-μFR improved discrimination in the overall cohort (C-index 0.700 to 0.755; p<0.001) as well as the subgroup with CT-μFR>0.80 (C-index 0.575 to 0.655; p<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Both CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient are independently associated with 3-year subsequent coronary events. Their combined assessment improves risk stratification beyond CT-μFR alone. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04794868).

articles.title: A randomised non-inferiority trial of CCTA guidance versus IVUS guidance for PCI: rationale and design of the P4 clinical trial.
articles.journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract: Intravascular imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves clinical outcomes compared with angiography-guided PCI. Contemporary coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides comprehensive assessment of coronary anatomy, plaque characteristics, vessel dimensions, calcification, and lesion-specific physiology, enabling detailed procedural planning before catheterisation. The Precise Procedural and PCI Plan (P4) trial is a prospective, international, multicentre, randomised, open-label trial with blinded endpoint adjudication designed to determine whether a comprehensive CCTA-guided PCI strategy is non-inferior to intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided PCI with respect to clinical outcomes. Approximately 1,100 patients with chronic coronary syndromes or stabilised acute coronary syndrome, at least one coronary stenosis >70%, and fractional flow reserve derived from CCTA ≤0.80 are enrolled. Following central core laboratory confirmation of anatomical and physiological eligibility, patients are randomised 1:1 to CCTA-guided or IVUS-guided PCI. Patients assigned to CCTA-guided PCI undergo standardised procedural planning and virtual PCI simulation, with CCTA integrated into the catheterisation laboratory using computed tomography-fluoroscopy synchronisation for intraprocedural guidance. In the IVUS-guided arm, PCI is performed with mandatory pre- and post-PCI IVUS assessment. The primary endpoint is target vessel failure at 12 months, defined as the composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction, or ischaemia-driven target vessel revascularisation. P4 will determine whether comprehensive, non-invasive CCTA-guided PCI planning is non-inferior to IVUS-guided PCI regarding 12-month target vessel failure while potentially improving procedural efficiency and standardisation. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05253677).

articles.title: Full-Service Mobile Food Markets and Dietary Quality in Low-Income Housing Communities: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Full-service mobile markets, also known as grocery stores on wheels, may improve diet-related outcomes by bringing low-cost, nutritious food to individuals experiencing low incomes and low food access.

OBJECTIVE: To determine the impact of the full-service Twin Cities Mobile Market on dietary outcomes in low-income communities.

DESIGN, SETTING, PARTICIPANTS: This cluster randomized clinical trial was conducted over 3 waves (January 2022 to October 2025) across 12 public or private subsidized housing sites in the Minneapolis-St. Paul, Minnesota, area. Participants were screened for interest in the mobile market. Follow-up assessments began after 6 months of market service. Analyses were finalized September 2026.

INTERVENTION: Sites were randomized to weekly market service or waiting list control groups.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcome: diet quality (Healthy Eating Index-2020 via 24-hour recalls). A priori secondary outcomes: dietary intake (fruit and vegetable, energy, sodium, and percentage of calories from added sugar), food security (18-item US Department of Agriculture Food Security Screening Module), and fruit and vegetable servings procured for the home (validated tracking tool). Adjusted intention-to-treat (ITT) generalized estimating equations were used to assess outcome differences between treatment groups.

RESULTS: Among 262 adults who enrolled in the mobile market study, 242 participants (mean [SD] age, 66.5 [11.5] years; 156 women [64.5%]) across 12 sites completed baseline assessments and were randomized to mobile market service or waiting list control groups. There were 137 individuals (56.6%) who received Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits. Sites had a mean (SD) of 18.2 (4.4) weekly transactions (mean of 110 of 1071 households [10.3%]). Of 109 intervention site participants, 47 individuals (43.1%) shopped at the mobile market 1 or more times in implementation months 5 to 6, while 90 of 94 individuals who reported ever using the market (95.7%) reported that they would recommend the market service. Participant retention was 218 of 242 participants (90.0%). In ITT models, the primary outcome of diet quality (adjusted mean difference, 1.25 [95% CI, -1.60 to 4.10]) among 215 participants and 6 of 7 secondary outcomes (fruit and vegetable, energy, and added sugar intake; food security and food security improvement; fruit and vegetable procurement) were not significantly different between groups. Intervention site participants consumed an adjusted mean difference of 397 mg (95% CI, -636 to -158 mg) less sodium daily compared with participants in the waiting list control group. Main findings were consistent across 4 sensitivity and supplemental analyses, except the per-protocol sensitivity analysis, which found that participants in the intervention group consumed an adjusted mean difference of 2.35% (95% CI, 0.66%-4.04%) more calories from added sugar compared with the control group.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, satisfaction with the mobile market was high, but the mobile market did not improve diet quality or most outcomes examined. The mobile market was associated with a meaningful sodium reduction that could improve population-level health.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05672186.

articles.title: Leadless Cardiac Resynchronization Results in Left Ventricular Reverse Remodeling: A Randomized Substudy of the SOLVE-CRT Study.
Implications of SGLT2 Inhibitors, GLP-1RAs, and Nonsteroidal MRAs on the Anticipated Burden of Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Several treatments that reduce the risk of heart failure (HF) have been introduced recently. Their impact on the future burden of HF in the U.S. has not been well characterized.

OBJECTIVES: This study aims to estimate the potential impact of recently approved cardiometabolic medications on the future burden of HF in the United States.

METHODS: Using a nationally representative sample of persons in the United States 30-79 years of age without cardiovascular disease at baseline, we used the PREVENT (Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events) equation to estimate the 10- and 30-year burden of HF and the projected impact of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists on these estimates. The authors estimated the total number of HF cases that could be averted with risk-based treatment and calculated the number needed to treat to prevent HF.

RESULTS: An estimated 5.5 million (95% CI: 5.1-5.8 million) U.S. adults 30-79 years of age without established cardiovascular disease will develop HF over 10 years. It is estimated to decrease to 5.1 million (95% CI: 4.7-5.4 million) with indicated treatment with a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor, 5.2 million (95% CI: 4.8-5.6 million) with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, 5.4 million (95% CI: 5.0-5.7 million) with nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, and 4.8 million (95% CI: 4.4-5.2 million) with the use of combination therapy. The use of combination therapy in eligible persons with an estimated 10-year HF risk of ≥10% would result in 6.8 million (95% CI: 6.1-7.5 million) eligible participants, and 498,000 (95% CI: -663,000 to -319,000) fewer cases of HF, with a number needed to treat of 14 (95% CI: 10-22) to prevent 1 incident case.

CONCLUSIONS: The projected burden of HF in the U.S. is substantial. A risk-based approach to preventive treatment may help reduce this considerably. The feasibility of such an approach deserves further investigation.

articles.title: Ventricular Arrhythmia After Percutaneous Edge-to-Edge Tricuspid Valve Repair.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) treats severe tricuspid regurgitation, but electrical complications from device-tissue interactions remain poorly characterized.

CASE SUMMARY: A 79-year-old woman developed postural ventricular arrhythmias after TriClip implantation. Electrocardiography was consistent with an ectopic origin in the posterior/inferior right ventricle, anatomically concordant with the posteroseptal clip. Orthostatic reduction in right ventricular volume may have induced dynamic clip-endocardium contact. Saline infusion abolished the arrhythmias. At 1 month, she remained asymptomatic despite unchanged device-to-septum distance on supine echocardiography, suggesting stabilization of the device-tissue interface over time.

DISCUSSION: As the first reported case of postural arrhythmia from mechanical TriClip-septal interaction, this addresses a gap in TEER literature regarding how orthostatic volume shifts trigger device-related complications.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Orthostatic volume shifts may provoke dynamic device-tissue contact and arrhythmias post-TEER. Careful clip positioning and vigilant postprocedural monitoring are essential, and stabilization of the device-tissue interface over time may allow conservative management.

articles.title: Liver Mapping in Tricuspid Regurgitation Informs Adverse Cardiovascular Outcomes.
Multimodality Imaging Across the Lifespan in Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot: Current Evidence and Future Directions.
articles.abstract: Repaired tetralogy of Fallot (rTOF) is a common condition encountered across pediatric and adult congenital heart disease clinics. Although childhood survival is excellent, patients remain at risk for late complications, including exercise intolerance, arrhythmias, heart failure, and sudden death. Residual lesions, most notably pulmonary regurgitation and right ventricular outflow tract obstruction, drive progressive right and secondary left ventricular remodeling, often necessitating repeat interventions such as pulmonary valve replacement. Multimodality imaging is central to management, enabling risk stratification and informing the optimal timing of reintervention. This State-of-the-Art Review summarizes the current state of the art in multimodality imaging for rTOF across the lifespan, highlighting established and emerging techniques. The authors discuss the roles of 2- and 3-dimensional echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance, strain and exercise imaging, ultrafast ultrasound, and advanced cardiac magnetic resonance methods in characterizing ventricular function, remodeling, mechanics, flow dynamics, fibrosis, stiffness, and electromechanical interactions. The authors explore developments in image-based machine learning and computational modeling that support patient-specific intervention planning and personalized care.

articles.title: Liraglutide and Semaglutide Induce Nitric Oxide-Dependent Contraction of Larger and Relaxation of Smaller Porcine Retinal Resistance Vessels Ex Vivo.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Drugs with glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) agonistic effects are beneficial for the treatment of diabetes and overweight but may be accompanied by an increased risk of vascular complications in the retina and the optic disc. The purpose of the present study was to investigate whether GLP-1 agonists can have vasoactive effects on retinal resistance vessels at different branching levels ex vivo and whether these effects depend on nitric oxide (NO).

METHODS: The diameters of retinal arterioles, precapillary arterioles, and capillaries were studied in perfused porcine hemiretinas ex vivo after intravascular administration of the GLP-1 agonists exendin-4, liraglutide, and semaglutide, alone and in the presence of the NO synthase inhibitor L-NAME.

RESULTS: Exendin-4 had no significant effect on the diameter of retinal arterioles, precapillary arterioles, and capillaries (P > 0.77 for all comparisons). However, liraglutide and semaglutide induced a significant contraction of arterioles and a significant dilatation of precapillary arterioles and capillaries (P < 0.03 for all comparisons). These vasoactive effects disappeared in the presence of the NO synthase inhibitor L-NAME (P > 0.08 for all comparisons).

CONCLUSIONS: GLP-1 agonists modified to reduce degradation and facilitate binding to plasma proteins can constrict larger and dilate smaller porcine retinal resistance vessels ex vivo. NO synthesis inhibition abolishes the effects, but the specific NO synthase isoform involved, the downstream signaling pathway, and the cellular source of NO remain to be determined. The observed vascular effects may contribute to mediating the adverse effects of GLP-1 agonists on the retina and the optic disc in clinical practice.

articles.title: Visual Perceptual Learning Based on Adaptive Contrast Detection Training Enhances Vision and Contrast Sensitivity in Diabetic Retinopathy.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the efficacy of home-based visual perceptual learning (VPL) on visual function and explore the residual visual plasticity in diabetic retinopathy (DR).

METHODS: Thirty-six DR patients following routine therapies were randomized (1:1). Twenty-eight completed the study (VPL, n = 12; control, n = 16) after excluding eight for poor adherence or incomplete follow-up. The VPL group underwent 3-month home-based grating detection training at individual cutoff spatial frequencies. Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), grating acuity (GA), contrast sensitivity to first-order motion stimuli (1stM), optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), and Low Vision Quality-of-Life (LVQOL) questionnaire were assessed at baseline, 1 month, and 3 months for the VPL group and at baseline and 3 months for the control group.

RESULTS: BCVA improved from 0.36 to 0.26 logMAR (P = 0.003), GA improved from 12.42 to 17.47 cycles per degree (2.96 dB) and 1stM increased from 64.26 to 83.42 (2.27 dB) in the VPL group. A significant group × time interaction was found for GA (F1, 26 = 63.595, P < 0.001, \( \eta_{p}^2 \) = 0.710), 1stM (F1, 26 = 32.663, P < 0.001, \( \eta_{p}^2 \) = 0.557), and BCVA (F1, 26 = 10.872, P = 0.003, \( \eta_{p}^2 \) = 0.295). The LVQOL score increased (+4.33; P < 0.001) and correlated with ΔGA (r = 0.671, P = 0.017). OCTA parameters remained stable in both groups.

CONCLUSIONS: The results reveal significant plasticity in the visual system in DR and suggest that contrast detection training may extend to motion perception tasks. Our study provides additional support for VPL as a potential treatment for DR.

articles.title: Leptomeningeal carcinomatosis arising from esophageal cancer: a systematic review of the literature.
articles.journal: Diseases of the esophagus : official journal of the International Society for Diseases of the Esophagus
