articles.abstract: Leptomeningeal carcinomatosis (LMC) is a rare but devastating complication of solid tumors. Involvement from esophageal cancer is exceedingly uncommon and poorly characterized, with evidence limited to case reports and small series. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched by two investigators for LMC originating from esophageal cancer. Thirty-one studies reporting 43 patients were included (93% male; mean age 59.3 years). Esophageal adenocarcinoma was the predominant histology (86%), followed by squamous cell carcinoma (11.6%), most commonly from the distal esophagus or esophagogastric junction. LMC occurred synchronously in 27.9% and metachronously in 72.1%, with a median interval of 11.2 months between primary diagnosis and leptomeningeal disease. At diagnosis, 37.2% had isolated leptomeningeal involvement without extracranial metastases. Presentation was heterogeneous, most frequently including headache or meningeal symptoms (55.8%), vestibulocerebellar manifestations (39.5%), and cranial nerve involvement (37.2%). Cerebrospinal fluid cytology was positive in 81.1% of tested cases, often requiring repeat lumbar punctures. Molecular data were reported for 27.9% of patients; Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2 (HER2) was positive in 3 of 10 tested cases (30%). Management was individualized: radiotherapy in 37.2%, intrathecal therapy in 20.9%, and supportive care alone in 46.5%. Median survival was 1.1 months, though three patients achieved 12, 14, and 19 months following Central Nervous System (CNS)-directed therapy. LMC from esophageal cancer is rare and clinically aggressive, characterized by heterogeneous presentation, frequent diagnostic delay, and poor prognosis. Early recognition and palliative care are essential, while rare long-term survivors suggest selected patients may benefit from individualized CNS-directed treatment.

articles.title: Lessons learned from a decade of EUS(-FNA) staging in esophageal and GEJ carcinoma: towards a selective staging strategy.
articles.journal: Diseases of the esophagus : official journal of the International Society for Diseases of the Esophagus
articles.abstract: Endoscopic ultrasonography with fine-needle aspiration (EUS(-FNA)) is recommended by current guidelines as part of the staging for esophageal and gastro-esophageal junction (GEJ) carcinoma, yet its incremental value over modern 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) remains uncertain. This Lessons Learned article reflects on over a decade of EUS(-FNA) and FDG-PET staging in 402 patients with potentially curable esophageal or GEJ carcinoma at a high-volume tertiary referral center. In 91.3% of patients, EUS(-FNA) did not alter the radiation field as would have been defined by FDG-PET. EUS(-FNA) resulted in an expansion of the radiation field in 4.5% and reduction in 4.2% of patients. Squamous cell carcinoma showed more than two-fold greater likelihood of radiation field modification. Among 193 patients classified as FDG-PET non-suspicious for malignant lymph nodes (LNs), EUS-FNA identified malignant LNs in eight patients (4.1%), which influenced the radiation field. In 5 of 402 patients (1.2%) a malignant LN was detected with EUS-FNA in a station that would not have routinely been resected surgically. In patients planned for neoadjuvant or definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT), LN staging is of direct therapeutic consequence: underestimation of nodal disease may result in geographic miss, while overestimation leads to unnecessary irradiation. In contrast, in patients treated with perioperative 5-fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin and docetaxel (FLOT) followed by surgical lymphadenectomy, most involved LN stations are routinely addressed surgically, limiting the added value of EUS(-FNA) for treatment planning. Therefore, we view EUS(-FNA) as a selective staging tool in patients planned for neoadjuvant or definitive CRT, rather than a procedure applied routinely to all patients.

articles.title: Botox Injection Combined With Partial Arytenoidectomy: A Novel Approach for Treatment of Episodic Laryngeal Breathing Disorders.
articles.journal: World journal of otorhinolaryngology - head and neck surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to develop effective treatments for episodic laryngeal breathing disorders (ELBD), a series of diverse obstructive respiratory disorders with an unknown pathogenesis. The diseases include paradoxical vocal fold motion/movement disorder (PVFMD), vocal cord dysfunction (VCD), irritable larynx syndrome (ILS), exercise-induced laryngeal obstruction, and laryngospasm.

METHODS: Five patients with ELBD were involved in this study (60-81 years, average of 70 years), including three men and two women, who visited the otolaryngology outpatient department suffering from dyspnea several times. Bilateral vocal fold paralysis and asthma were excluded. An injection of initial botulinum toxin into the vocal cords was treated for each patient. If recurrence were to take place within 3 months after injection, a vocal cord process resection would be performed. The visual scale of perception was used for assessing preoperative and postoperative dyspnea.

RESULTS: All patients experienced symptoms of recurring dyspnea for a duration of 1-120 months. The average follow-up duration was 14 months (6-24 months) after treatment. Dyspnea was relieved in two patients after the Botox injection alone. Three patients found relief after unilateral vocal cord process resection. All patients showed a significant reduction in postoperative dyspnea scale in VAS score.

CONCLUSION: This study preliminarily explores the efficacy of combined Botox injection and partial arytenoidectomy as a therapeutic option for ELBD.

articles.title: Development of a Single-Camera Markerless Motion Capture System for Assessing Upper Limb Function Post-Stroke (FULMA).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Upper limb impairment is common after stroke. Standardised measures such as the Action Research Arm Test and Fugl Meyer Assessment are widely used but may show inter-rater variability and limited sensitivity to subtle motor changes.

OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate the Functional Upper Limb Movement Assessment (FULMA) system, a single-camera markerless motion capture tool for objective movement analysis of upper limb function with clinician facing outputs after stroke.

METHODS: A prospective observational study included 39 stroke participants and 19 healthy controls. Participants completed 9 functional tasks recorded with a LiDAR depth camera. Kinematic features were analysed using machine learning models to predict an ordinal task performance score anchored to Action Research Arm Test scoring descriptors. Predictions were compared with independent occupational therapist ratings, and automated kinematic commentary was generated.

RESULTS: The multilayer perceptron achieved a mean accuracy of 83.3%, with task level accuracies of 75.0% to 91.7% and weighted kappa values of 0.67 to 0.88. The support vector machine achieved a mean accuracy of 78.5%, with task level accuracies of 72.2% to 89.0% and weighted kappa values of 0.59 to 0.83. Performance varied across tasks, with the strongest results for cup to mouth and hair brushing. Commentary highlighted prolonged movement time, reduced smoothness and increased trunk displacement.

CONCLUSION: This developmental study showed preliminary agreement between automated ordinal score predictions and therapist ratings within a controlled dataset. External validation and evaluation of measurement properties are required before clinical use. Kinematic commentary should be considered exploratory rather than a validated clinical interpretation.

articles.title: A Single Daily Dose of Metronidazole is Non-Inferior to Three Daily Doses in Children With Perforated Appendicitis: A Real-World Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness and safety of a single daily dose of metronidazole compared with three daily doses, both combined with gentamicin in children with perforated appendicitis.

METHODS: A real-world, randomized, non-inferiority trial was conducted with children (< 14 years old) who underwent appendectomy for perforated appendicitis from 2022 to 2023. Participants were randomized into intervention (IG) and control (CG) groups: the former received a single dose of 30 mg/kg metronidazole, whereas the latter received three daily doses of 10 mg/kg metronidazole, both also received a single daily dose of 5 mg/kg gentamicin. Primary outcomes included the rate of patients with surgical site infection (SSI), incisional SSI (I-SSI), organ/space SSI (OSI), and treatment success at study end. Secondary outcomes included adverse events and antibiotic costs.

RESULTS: A total of 201 (IG = 99 and CG = 102) children were included. All participants underwent open appendectomy. The intervention was non-inferior to the control regimen for SSI (risk ratio [RR] = 0.82; 95% CI 0.54-1.24), I-SSI (RR = 0.81; 95% CI 0.55-1.19), OSI (RR = 0.82; 95% CI 0.56-1.19), and treatment success at study end (RR = 1.01; 95% CI 0.92-1.12). No severe antibiotic-related adverse events were recorded. Median metronidazole treatment duration was 6 days in the IG group and 5.5 days in the CG group (range, 1-12 days; p = 0.650), while median gentamicin duration was 6 days in both groups (range, 2-12 days; p = 0.942). The IG group showed a mean reduction of US$1.71 in metronidazole cost per patient.

CONCLUSION: A single daily dose of metronidazole combined with gentamicin was non-inferior in effectiveness to the fractionated regimen in children with PA. The simplified regimen reduced metronidazole costs and may offer practical advantages in routine care.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Registro Brasileiro de Ensaios Clínicos, number RBR-95gbvmq (https://ensaiosclinicos.gov.br/rg/RBR-95gbvmq; Registered on April 04, 2023).

articles.title: Paint me a picture: illustrating the psychosocial impact of different juvenile idiopathic arthritis categories.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the impact of different JIA categories on the psychosocial well-being of children and identify associated factors.

METHODS: 1072 patients enrolled in the Canadian Alliance of Pediatric Rheumatology Investigators (CAPRI) registry within three months of diagnosis were included. Psychosocial impact of JIA was measured using the Juvenile Arthritis Quality of Life Questionnaire Psychosocial domain (JAQQ-psychosocial, 1=nil to 7=severe). Wilcoxon ranked-sum tests compared scores at enrollment and one year. Hierarchical clustering of standardized z-scores of JAQQ-psychosocial items produced heatmaps. Spearman correlation and linear regression investigated factors associated with JAQQ-psychosocial scores.

RESULTS: At enrollment, median JAQQ-psychosocial was highest for RF+ polyarthritis (3.2, IQR: 1.8-4.4) and lowest for oligoarthritis (1.8, 1-3). Scores improved significantly by one year for RF+ and RF- polyarthritis, psoriatic and systemic arthritis (P < 0.05). JAQQ-psychosocial items clustered into externalizing behaviours, internalizing behaviours, and school-related problems. Heatmaps revealed four clusters with mild (51.0% of patients), moderate (30.6%), severe (9.3%), and very severe (9.1%) JIA psychosocial impact, with the proportions of patients in each cluster varying by JIA category. Most patients improved by 1 year but few patients in each category had persisting or worsening psychosocial impact. Multiple factors correlated with JAQQ-psychosocial scores, and physical disability, fatigue, and pain interference were independently associated with scores at enrollment.

CONCLUSION: JIA psychosocial impact was most severe at diagnosis, varied by JIA category, and improved by 1 year for many children, but few patients showed persisting or worsening JIA impact. Physical disability, fatigue, and pain interference were independently associated with psychosocial impact.

articles.title: Pulmonary hypertension clinic infrastructure is associated with improved care coordination: results from a national survey.
articles.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society

articles.title: Heterogeneity in Procedural Training, Self-Assessed Competence and Supervising Skills Among New Pulmonary and Critical Care Fellows.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Performing procedures relevant to a future career path is a core component of Internal Medicine training (e.g. central line, arterial line, thoracentesis, paracentesis, and lumbar puncture). Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine, Pulmonary Disease, and Critical Care Medicine (P/CCM) fellows must demonstrate procedural proficiency and competency and are often tasked with supervising procedures performed by resident trainees.

OBJECTIVES: To (1) determine the perceived level of procedural competence among P/CCM trainees at the start of their fellowship and (2) describe how P/CCM trainees are integrated into procedure workflows at their respective institutions, including supervision practices.

METHODS: PCCM fellows received the annual Association of Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine (APCCMPD) Fellow's survey between January - March 2025.

RESULTS: Of the 2240 eligible fellows, 592 responded (26.4%). Several indicated they would have been comfortable at the start of fellowship performing central line (81%), arterial line (81%), paracentesis (74%), thoracentesis (40%) or lumbar puncture (42%) independently, or with a supervisor available if needed. The distribution of prior procedural experience was similar, with more than 5 procedures performed by 92% of respondents for central line, 86% for arterial line, 76% for paracentesis, 49% for thoracentesis, and 37% for lumbar puncture. Most respondents (90%) indicated they - as the primary fellow - are frequently tasked with supervising central line placement. Yet, at the start of fellowship, not all fellows were comfortable supervising procedures (58% comfortable supervising central line, 66% arterial line, 61% paracentesis, 29% thoracentesis, 30% lumbar puncture). Only 56% indicated a formal central line procedural competency assessment in their fellowship.

CONCLUSION: Our survey highlights that pre-fellowship procedure training is heterogenous. P/CCM fellows identified variable comfort with performing and supervising common procedures. Fellowship programs must evaluate their own local practices to ensure fellows demonstrate procedural competence prior to asking them to supervise.

articles.title: One-year incidence of newly diagnosed dementia after inpatient sepsis hospitalization.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis survivors face increased long-term cognitive risk, but contemporary U.S. population-level estimates of claims-ascertained dementia remain limited.

OBJECTIVE: To estimate 1-year incidence of newly documented claims-ascertained dementia after sepsis hospitalization and describe variation by age, sex, payer, and sepsis severity.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort-study using a nationally representative U.S. claims database with linked medical, pharmacy, and enrollment data from 1 January 2020 through 31 March 2025. Adults aged 18 years or older with an index sepsis hospitalization, no prior dementia diagnosis, and complete 1-year post-discharge claims observability were included. Newly documented dementia was defined using a claims-based algorithm requiring atleast 2 outpatient claims separated by 30 days or atleast 1 inpatient claim. Exact Clopper-Pearson 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated.

RESULTS: Among 35,689 sepsis survivors (mean-age, 62.4 years; 51.5% male; 42.5% Medicare; 19.7% with severe sepsis or septic shock), 1,072 received a newly documented dementia diagnosis within 1 year (3.00%; 95% CI, 2.83%-3.19%). Incidence increased from 0.60% among patients aged 18-64 years to 2.83% among those aged 65-74 years and 8.24% among those aged 75 years or older. Median-time to diagnosis was 112 days (interquartile range, 39-223 days). Incidence was similar by sex and higher with severe sepsis (3.62% vs 2.85%). Sensitivity analyses yielded estimates of 2.19%-4.29%.

CONCLUSIONS: Approximately 3% of insured adult sepsis survivors with complete 1-year claims observability received a new dementia diagnosis within 1-year, with risk concentrated among older adults. Older sepsis survivors may warrant closer cognitive follow-up, though these findings do not establish screening benefit or sepsis-related dementia risk.

articles.title: Proteomic Interrogation of the Acute Response to Muscle Damage in Untrained Middle Aged and Older Females.
articles.abstract: Blunted regenerative responses to muscle damage with aging are linked to inflammatory signaling and satellite cell dynamics; however, most evidence is derived from males and is limited to targeted assays of bulk muscle tissue and/or circulating biomarkers. Here, we focused on middle-aged and older females and leveraged multi-compartment proteomics to identify responses to modest muscle damage across myofibrillar (MYOF), sarcoplasmic (SARCO), and serum compartments. Sixteen females (mean age = 61±8 years) had vastus lateralis biopsies and serum collected before (PRE) and 24 h after (POST) a resistance loading protocol that induced modest muscle damage (72.9% increase in serum creatine kinase activity). SARCO and MYOF fractions were separated using differential centrifugation, and proteomics was performed on three compartments using a nanoparticle capture approach followed by mass spectrometry, yielding 9,059 proteins in SARCO, 4,334 in MYOF, and 3,964 in serum. The protocol produced 90 differentially abundant (DA) proteins in SARCO (61 up, 29 down), 39 in MYOF (27 up, 12 down), and 124 in serum (34 up (9 muscle-specific), 90 down). DA proteins minimally overlapped across compartments. Enrichment analyses pointed primarily to translation-related processes in MYOF and contractile processes in serum. Pathway Level Information ExtractoR performed on all DA proteins identified multi-compartment biocircuits linked to membrane trafficking, vesicle mediated transport, neutrophil degranulation, and viral infection. Viral infection-related proteins correlated with body weight and body fat, while vesicle mediated transport-related proteins correlated with serum creatine kinase activity. This analysis reveals novel biocircuitry of modest muscle damage in middle-aged and older females.

articles.title: Salt-Sensitive Hypertension and Vascular Dysfunction.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.abstract: The salt-sensitivity of blood pressure (SSBP) affects 50% of hypertensive individuals and ∼25% of normotensive individuals (increasing their hypertension risk) and is a risk factor for cardiovascular disease independent of blood pressure (BP). When consuming a high-salt (HS) diet ∼90% of U.S. consume excess salt), individuals with the SSBP develop salt-sensitive hypertension (SSH). Historically, the SSBP is thought to be mainly determined by neural and renal mechanisms. In salt-sensitive (SS) individuals, the brain fails to suppress sympathetic outflow in response to a HS diet and renal sodium handling is impaired, contributing to SSH. During HS-intake salt-resistant (SR) individuals suppress sympathetic outflow maintain sodium balance, and normotension. Recently, this classic theory was challenged due to its lack of consideration for vascular dysfunction as a contributing mechanism for the SSBP. Growing evidence shows a HS diet induces vascular dysfunction, including endothelial dysfunction and arterial stiffening, that may contribute to SSH. Furthermore, the endothelial glycocalyx is proposed to impact how the vasculature responds to a HS diet, the so-called 'vascular salt-sensitivity'. In this review, we summarize recent evidence on the pathophysiology of SSH with an emphasis on mechanisms regarding vascular dysfunction. HS diet-induced vascular dysfunction occurs regardless of changes in BP but may be exacerbated in SS phenotypes. Future studies are warranted to further delineate the causes for SSH and vascular dysfunction through stratification of SS/SR and normotensive/hypertensive to provide mechanistic insights into the relationship between the SSBP and vascular salt-sensitivity to promote precision medicine for cardiovascular disease management in those populations.

articles.title: A Sinonasal-Dominant Symptom Phenotype Is Associated With COPD Exacerbations: A Multicentre Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Sinonasal symptoms are common in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, their clinical significance remains unclear. This study investigated whether patient-reported sinonasal symptoms are associated with COPD exacerbation history and whether multidimensional patient-reported outcome (PRO) assessment identifies a distinct sinonasal symptom-dominant phenotype.

METHODS: This multicenter cross-sectional study included 442 patients with COPD. Sinonasal symptoms, COPD health status, and frailty were assessed using the 22-item Sino-Nasal Outcome Test (SNOT-22), COPD Assessment Test (CAT), and Kihon Checklist (KCL), respectively. Associations between the SNOT-22 scores and COPD exacerbation history or frailty were evaluated using logistic regression analysis. Domain-level analyses were performed using the previously reported SNOT-22 domains. PRO-based phenotyping was performed using unsupervised k-prototype clustering of the SNOT-22, CAT, and KCL items.

RESULTS: Patient-reported sinonasal symptoms were common, with discordance between patient and physician reports. Higher SNOT-22 scores were associated with COPD exacerbation history and frailty. Domain-level analyses showed that the nasal symptom domain was associated with exacerbation history, whereas the emotional domain was associated with frailty. PRO-based clustering identified four clinically interpretable phenotypes, including a nasal symptom-dominant phenotype associated with COPD exacerbation history.

CONCLUSION: Patient-reported sinonasal symptoms are common and clinically relevant in COPD, with discordance between patient and physician reports. This study identified a nasal symptom-dominant phenotype associated with COPD exacerbation history, highlighting the potential value of upper airway assessment in personalized COPD management and suggesting that sinonasal symptoms may represent a candidate treatable trait.

articles.title: Postpartum Placental Ischemic Dams Display an Increase in Kidney Cortex TNF-α and Kidney Medulla Nitric Oxide Bioavailability with High Blood Pressure.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Renal physiology
articles.abstract: Women who experience a placental ischemic (PI) pregnancy, such as preeclampsia, have an increased risk of developing chronic kidney disease (CKD) as early as 5-20 years postpartum. The underlying mechanisms leading to this increased risk for CKD are unknown. Mechanisms that contribute to the development of CKD are hypertension and changes in renal molecular factors such as inflammation, oxidative stress, and nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability. To determine the relationship between blood pressure, renal molecular factors, and CKD in women after a PI pregnancy, we used the reduced uterine perfusion pressure model of preeclampsia in rats. In this study, two groups were utilized: normal pregnant (NP) and PI dams. At 6 weeks postpartum (∼2-3 human years), we examined the dams' blood pressure via carotid catheterization, collected the plasma to measure creatinine, and obtained the kidneys to evaluate the abundance and concentrations of renal molecular factors. PI dams exhibited an increase in blood pressure (125±3vs111±3 mmHg, p=0.002), TNF-α in the kidney cortex (81.38±1.1vs67.48±0.58 pg/mL / mg Protein, p<0.0001), and increased NO bioavailability (0.64±0.08vs0.41±0.05 µmol NO3/mg Protein, p=0.03) in the kidney medulla. However, serum creatinine, renal KIM-1, eNOS, NGAL, and oxidative stress did not have significant changes. In summary, PI dams have alterations in kidney inflammation and NO bioavailability, with no indications of renal dysfunction or injury. Thus, suggesting that changes in renal molecular factors may precede the onset of CKD. This study is clinically relevant, because it highlights the potential contributions of altered renal molecular factors in development of CKD postpartum.

articles.title: A gut symbiotic bacterium enhances baculovirus resistance in Spodoptera frugiperda by maintaining peritrophic matrix integrity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spodoptera frugiperda is a major agricultural pest worldwide, whereas Spodoptera frugiperda multiple nucleopolyhedrovirus (SfMNPV) serves as an important microbial control agent against this pest. Resident gut bacteria are increasingly recognized as important modulators of insect-pathogen interactions; however, whether and how they influence SfMNPV infection in S. frugiperda remains unclear. We therefore investigated how gut bacteria modulate host resistance to SfMNPV.

RESULTS: Antibiotic-mediated depletion of gut bacteria increased larval susceptibility to SfMNPV. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed that gut bacterial depletion downregulated midgut genes associated with immune defense, digestive functions and peritrophic matrix (PM) maintenance. Among seven culturable midgut bacterial isolates, reinoculation with Glutamicibacter soli significantly enhanced larval resistance to SfMNPV. Pre-feeding with either the G. soli culture supernatant or cell lysis precipitate also increased larval resistance and partially reversed transcriptional changes caused by gut bacterial depletion before viral challenge, including the downregulation of peritrophin-1. RNAi-mediated silencing of peritrophin-1 disrupted PM structure, increased PM permeability, and enhanced larval susceptibility to SfMNPV. Consistently, G. soli reinoculation restored PM integrity impaired by gut bacterial depletion.

CONCLUSION: These findings identify maintenance of PM integrity as an important mechanism contributing to gut symbiotic bacterium-mediated resistance to SfMNPV. The study advances our understanding of how gut bacteria influence baculovirus infection in insect hosts and provides potential microbial and molecular targets for improving baculovirus-based pest management. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

articles.title: Covered-Stent Migration During Same-Session Aortic Isthmus Repair and Bicuspid Aortic Valve TAVR.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Fixed obstruction at the aortic isthmus may preclude transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Covered-stent implantation can restore large-bore access, but immediate passage of balloons and delivery systems through a newly implanted stent may expose it to longitudinal traction. Secondary stent migration during withdrawal of a valvuloplasty balloon and its intraluminal balloon-assisted rescue have not been well characterized. An 87-year-old man with New York Heart Association class III symptoms had severe bicuspid aortic stenosis (peak velocity, 4.4 m/s; mean gradient, 48 mmHg; valve area, 0.65 cm2; left ventricular ejection fraction, 55%) and a focal juxtaductal aortic-isthmus stenosis with a peak-to-peak gradient of 32 mmHg. Because of high surgical risk and unfavorable alternative access, same-session covered-stent treatment followed by transfemoral TAVR was selected. A 12 × 29-mm Advanta V12 covered stent was deployed and flared using an 18-mm noncompliant balloon. After aortic-valve predilation with a 23-mm noncompliant balloon, the stent migrated distally during balloon withdrawal. Guidewire access was preserved, and the stent remained coaxial. The balloon was recentered within the migrated stent and partially reinflated, allowing the balloon and stent to be advanced proximally as a single unit. After restoration and re-expansion of the stent, a 23-mm Myval valve was implanted successfully. Final transvalvular and isthmic gradients were 8 and 5 mmHg, respectively, with trivial paravalvular regurgitation and no aortic injury. The patient was discharged on day 3 and remained in NYHA class I at 6 months. Withdrawal of a large valvuloplasty balloon may cause secondary migration of a newly implanted aortic-isthmus stent. When guidewire access, coaxial alignment, and structural integrity are preserved, controlled intraluminal balloon-assisted repositioning may provide an effective bailout while maintaining transfemoral access.

articles.title: Causes of bias in Delphi studies and consensus statements: a methodological review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Delphi methodology is a widely-used tool for achieving expert consensus in healthcare, particularly in areas where empirical evidence is limited or uncertain. Despite its structured design, the Delphi process remains vulnerable to implicit cognitive biases that may influence judgement and group decision-making. Such biases may inadvertently affect the quality of the consensus process, allow louder voices to influence outcomes, restrict inclusivity and undermine the validity, transparency and evidence-based nature of recommendations.

METHODS: We conducted a methodological review synthesising literature from cognitive psychology, behavioural science and methodological research on consensus development and Delphi processes. Using a concept-mapping approach, established cognitive biases were mapped to different stages of the Delphi process, including study design; panel selection; survey development; iterative scoring; and consensus interpretation.

RESULTS: Ten cognitive biases were organised into four domains reflecting different levels of influence within consensus development: steering-group and design-level biases, panel composition and contextual biases, social influence and conformity biases; and individual cognitive heuristic biases. A conceptual framework was developed to systematically identify these biases within Delphi-based consensus studies. Examples illustrating how these biases may arise in healthcare Delphi processes are presented, alongside potential mitigation strategies.

DISCUSSION: Recognition and mitigation of cognitive biases are essential for strengthening the methodological rigour and credibility of Delphi studies. Strategies to reduce bias include diversifying expert panels; using neutral language in survey statements; maintaining anonymity during voting; involving methodological expertise in Delphi design; and ensuring transparent iterative feedback. The framework needs prospective validation before its widespread use and may assist journal editors and peer reviewers in critically appraising Delphi studies and improving reporting standards in consensus research.

articles.title: Disentangling the Genetic Relationship Between Sleep and Epilepsy.
articles.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: A bidirectional relationship between sleep and epilepsy is well recognised, yet the biological mechanisms linking them remain poorly understood. Both have a genetic basis, with genome-wide association studies (GWAS) capturing polygenic contributions. By leveraging GWAS summary statistics, we aimed to investigate their shared genetic architecture.

METHODS: We analysed seven sleep traits (morningness chronotype, sleep duration, habitual short/long sleep, insomnia, daytime napping/sleepiness) with common epilepsy types (focal epilepsy and genetic generalised epilepsy [GGE]). For each trait pair, we estimated genome-wide genetic correlation, tested bidirectional causality, quantified polygenic overlap, performed gene-trait associations to identify putative pleiotropic genes, estimated local genetic correlations and investigated whether regions of significance were driven by shared causal variants using colocalisation and fine-mapping.

RESULTS: Genome-wide analyses supported a positive genetic correlation between higher GGE risk and habitual short sleep, with extensive polygenic overlap (75%-97%) across seven sleep traits. Gene-trait analyses identified RMI1 as a putative sleep-epilepsy candidate, with 13 additional sleep-associated genes linked to monogenic epilepsies (e.g., KANSL1, GRIN2A). Locus-specific analyses identified 16 genomic loci of interest (13 sleep-GGE, 3 sleep-focal epilepsy). Morningness-GGE shared the largest number of locus-specific associations. No significant causal relationships were identified, and causal variants did not colocalise.

INTERPRETATION: Our findings support complex shared genetic contributions between sleep and epilepsy, with distinct patterns for focal compared to generalised epilepsy. These differences may help explain syndrome-specific sleep-wake associations, including seizure timing and predisposition. By localising shared loci and highlighting specific overlapping genes, we provide a foundation for future research into the mechanisms underlying epilepsy-sleep comorbidities.

articles.title: Automated urine analysis of atypical urothelial cells for urothelial carcinoma: a prospective study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To prospectively evaluate the diagnostic value of atypical urothelial cells (Atyp.C), an automatically determined quantitative parameter of the Sysmex UF-5000 urine particle analyser (Sysmex Corp., Kobe, Japan), as a non-invasive biomarker for urothelial carcinoma (UC). Early diagnosis of UC remains challenging despite advances in diagnostic techniques. While non-invasive urine cytology has high diagnostic value, clinical evidence for Atyp.C in urine remains unclear. Quantification of Atyp.C in urine may improve non-invasive UC disease diagnostics.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Urine samples from 234 patients who underwent invasive urological intervention for non-malignant conditions (control group [CG]) or UC (intervention group [IG]) were considered. Based on histopathology, the IG was subclassified into low-grade (LG) and high-grade (HG) UC and was further grouped into non-muscle-invasive (non-MI) and MI UC. Patients who received neoadjuvant chemotherapy were analysed separately. Atyp.C of ≥0.1 Atyp.C/μL were defined as positive and were automatically quantified using the Sysmex UF-5000 urine particle analyser, which classifies epithelial cells with disproportionately high nucleic acid content relative to cell size. Smoking state, urinary tract infection (UTI), and micro-/macrohaematuria, were evaluated as potential confounding factors. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to assess explorative diagnostic Atyp.C performance.

RESULTS: The Atyp.C concentration was higher in the IG than in the CG (mean [SEM] 0.53 [0.1] vs 0.29 [0.1] Atyp.C/μL; P = 0.004), with a sensitivity of 0.59. HGUC exhibited higher Atyp.C levels (mean [SEM] 0.85 [0.2] Atyp.C/μL, P < 0.001) and a sensitivity of 0.73. MI UC showed the highest Atyp.C concentrations (mean [SEM] 0.95 [0.4] Atyp.C/μL; P = 0.004) and sensitivity of 0.78. ROC analysis demonstrated the highest diagnostic accuracy for MI UC (area under the ROC curve = 0.75). ROC analysis was exploratory and lacked external validation. UTI was a significant confounder for Atyp.C quantification.

CONCLUSION: The Atyp.C are elevated in HGUC, particularly in MI disease, supporting their potential as a non-invasive diagnostic biomarker in UC condition.

articles.title: Mathematical Representation of Lung Disease: The Frontier that Could Transform Treatment.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Lung cellular and molecular physiology

articles.title: A Biomimetic Microneedle Platform Using Neutrophil Membrane for Synergistic Antibacterial Therapy of MRSA Infection.
articles.abstract: Persistent bacterial infection has become life-threatening challenge worldwide. Bacterial biofilm formation, causing induced antimicrobial resistance and suppressive immune microenvironment, is one of the critical pathways leading chronic and persistent infection. Herein, an integrated microneedle patch harboring neutrophil membrane and antibiotics is designed to elicit therapeutic in-situ immunization for the management of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infection. When applied on the infected skin, microneedles can physically penetrate the biofilm barrier, helping the diffusion of antibiotics to kill the bacteria deep in the biofilm. After breaking the integrated structure of biofilm, neutrophil membrane tightly binds to the bacterial debris to enhance the phagocytosis of antigen-presenting cells followed by the robust activation of T helper cells. Naïve B cells then differentiate to plasma cells or memory B cells to produce specific antibodies, thereby efficiently managing infection and preventing relapse. Overall, our study highlights the capability of eliciting therapeutic in-situ immunization mediated by the integrated biomimetic microneedle, providing an attractive perspective for the treatment of persistent bacterial infection.

articles.title: Hydrogels in Airway Devices and Tracheal Repair: Clinical Requirements, Patient-Specific Manufacturing, and Translational Testing.
articles.abstract: Airway stents can rapidly restore ventilation in central airway obstruction, but complications after placement remain common. Migration, mucus retention, infection, granulation, fracture, and difficult removal often reflect a mismatch between the device and the airway environment. This review examines how hydrogels may contribute to airway devices and tracheal repair, with emphasis on clinically relevant design and testing criteria. Hydrogels provide a water-rich interface and allow control of mechanics, degradation, and local delivery. Softness alone, however, cannot maintain airway patency. A useful hydrogel-enabled device must keep the lumen open during breathing and coughing without excessive wall pressure, while also preserving mucus transport. The review covers hydrogel classes and manufacturing routes relevant to patient-specific devices. 4D shape programming is considered an early concept rather than a proven airway-stent strategy. Direct evidence for intraluminal stents still comes mainly from printed degradable elastomers, whereas most hydrogel studies concern tracheal repair or surface biology. Rabbit studies are informative but remain limited by small cohorts and short follow-up. A structural frame with a hydrogel surface therefore appears to be the most realistic near-term route. Translation will require testing of the final sterilized device under cyclic loading and airway-like conditions.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Disease in Women the Two Decades Following Uteroplacental Disorders: A Population-Based Data-Linkage Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Uniform recommendations on cardiovascular follow-up after complicated pregnancies are lacking, partly due to limited evidence. This study aimed to investigate the incidence and timing of premature cardiovascular disease (CVD) after different uteroplacental disorders, to inform the timing and content of cardiovascular follow-up.

DESIGN: Population-based cohort study, linking data from the Dutch perinatal registry with national hospital admissions data.

SETTING: Netherlands, 2000-2022.

POPULATION: 1 669 681 nulliparous women, with a singleton pregnancy.

METHODS: Cox regression was used to estimate hazard ratios for overall CVD and specific cardiovascular conditions after uteroplacental disorders, adjusted for confounders. Time-dependent Cox regression and interaction analyses for education attainment, income, and migration background were performed.

RESULTS: Risks of premature hypertension, atherosclerosis, ischaemic heart disease, cardiac arrest, cardiomyopathy, heart failure, and cerebrovascular disease were significantly increased among women with a history of a uteroplacental disorder, adjusted for confounders (overall CVD: aHR 1.70, 95% CI 1.67-1.74; median follow-up time 11 years, IQR 6-17 years). Hazard ratios were similar after pregnancy induced hypertension (PIH), preeclampsia (PE), fetal growth restriction (FGR), or fetal death, while risks after spontaneous preterm birth (sPTB) were less elevated. Most relative CVD risks were highest shortly after pregnancy but remained elevated more than 10 years postpartum. After hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), hypertension risk was most pronounced, whereas after FGR the increased risk of atherosclerosis was most notable. Socioeconomic factors had limited impact on these associations.

CONCLUSIONS: All uteroplacental disorders-not only PE-serve as women-specific markers of CVD risk, shortly after pregnancy and later in life, highlighting the need for early cardiovascular screening. Pathological processes contributing to the increased CVD risk might differ across uteroplacental disorders.

articles.title: Pancreas-Intestine Composite Transplantation for Simultaneous Loss of Pancreatic and Intestinal Function (With Video).
articles.abstract: Pancreas-intestine composite transplantation (PITx) is a therapeutic option for patients with irreversible loss of both pancreatic and intestinal function. We report a case of PITx in a 16-year-old male who developed fulminant Type 1 diabetes mellitus complicated by non-occlusive mesenteric ischemia, resulting in extensive intestinal necrosis. Despite intensive surgical and critical care management, the patient ultimately required total small intestinal resection and total pancreatectomy. After recovery from sepsis and multiorgan dysfunction, the patient's general condition stabilized, and PITx was considered an appropriate therapeutic option. The composite graft consisted of the pancreas, duodenum, small intestine, and right colon. Arterial inflow was reconstructed using a single Carrel patch incorporating the celiac axis and superior mesenteric artery, and venous outflow was established by portal vein anastomosis. Postoperatively, pancreatic endocrine function was restored, allowing stable glycemic control without exogenous insulin, and intestinal graft function enabled the gradual advancement of enteral and oral nutrition. This report highlights the key technical considerations and anatomical principles of PITx and demonstrates that tailored composite graft transplantation can restore both pancreatic and intestinal function while preserving unaffected abdominal organs in highly selected patients with combined pancreatic and intestinal failure.

articles.title: Happiness among nulliparous women of advanced maternal age (AMA): The mediating role of psychosocial factors.
articles.abstract: This study examined the association between pregnancy stress and happiness and explored the indirect associations through psychosocial factors (maternal identity, childbirth confidence, marital intimacy, and maternal-fetal attachment) among nulliparous women of advanced maternal age. This analytical cross-sectional study was conducted in South Korea using a web-based convenience sample of 165 nulliparous women aged 35 years or older recruited through the country's largest online community for pregnant women. Data were collected from September to October 2023 through a structured online survey and analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics Version 25.0 and Hayes' PROCESS Macro model 4. The analysis estimated cross-sectional indirect associations rather than causal mediation. Pregnancy stress showed significant total and direct associations with happiness. Significant indirect associations were observed through maternal identity, childbirth confidence, and marital intimacy, whereas maternal-fetal attachment did not show a significant indirect association. These findings may inform programs aimed at reducing pregnancy stress and strengthening psychosocial resources to support positive pregnancy experiences and psychological well-being among nulliparous women of advanced maternal age.

articles.title: A Multimodal Nomogram Predicting the Risk of Cognitive Impairment in Parkinson Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cognitive impairment is the most consequential non-motor complication of Parkinson's disease (PD), yet no validated tool integrates multimodal data to predict individualized risk trajectories.

OBJECTIVES: The aim is to develop and internally validate a time-to-event nomogram for predicting 5-year risk of cognitive impairment in PD using the Parkinson's Precision Markers Initiative (PPMI).

METHODS: We analyzed 1188 PD patients with normal cognition at their first cognitive assessment and up to 13 years of follow-up. Twenty-seven candidate predictors across seven domains were evaluated. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-penalized Cox regression performed variable selection. Performance was assessed via nested cross-validation, bootstrap optimism correction, calibration, and time-dependent area under the curve (AUC).

RESULTS: During median follow-up of 3.0 years (interquartile range [IQR], 2.0-5.0), 457 patients (38.5%) developed cognitive impairment. LASSO selected 14 predictors. The Cox model achieved a concordance index (C-index) of 0.747 (optimism-corrected: 0.733; nested CV: 0.736 ± 0.042), with apparent time-dependent AUC of 0.77, 0.79, and 0.83 at 3, 5, and 8 years (held-out: 0.75, 0.78, and 0.81). A companion model without genetic predictors, for unknown GBA status, performed similarly (optimism-corrected C-index, 0.729). The strongest predictors were age (hazard ratio [HR], 1.05/year; P < 0.001), GBA mutation (HR, 2.05; P < 0.001), cognitive complaints (HR, 1.67; P < 0.001), and Symbol Digit Modalities Test (HR, 0.98/point; P = 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: A multimodal nomogram integrating clinical, cognitive, genetic, and neuropsychiatric predictors provides individualized estimates of 5-year risk of cognitive impairment in PD; after external validation, it may support prognostic counseling and trial enrichment.

articles.title: Sleep Efficiency and Physical Capacity in Adults With Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD): A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: Sleep efficiency and physical capacity are important factors in metabolic health among adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and may be influenced by common pathophysiological mechanisms. This study evaluated the association between physical capacity and objectively measured sleep efficiency in adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. In this cross-sectional study, 136 adults were enrolled. Physical capacity was assessed using the Global Physical Capacity Score, hepatic steatosis was quantified using FibroScan, and sleep efficiency was assessed using wrist actigraphy. Linear and logistic regression analyses were performed after adjustment for potential confounding factors. Overall, 61.8% of participants had impaired sleep efficiency (< 85%). In the fully adjusted logistic regression model, participants with a Global Physical Capacity Score ≥ 6 had significantly lower odds of impaired sleep efficiency (odds ratio 0.42, 95% confidence interval 0.19-0.95; p = 0.037); when physical capacity was analysed as a continuous variable, the association was in the same direction but not statistically significant (odds ratio per 1-point increase 0.79, 95% confidence interval 0.61-1.03; p = 0.077). Stratified analyses showed a significant association among women (odds ratio 0.26, 95% confidence interval 0.07-0.92; p = 0.037; continuous model: odds ratio per 1-point increase 0.74, 95% confidence interval 0.51-1.06; p = 0.095), whereas no significant association was observed among men. Higher multidimensional physical capacity was associated with better objectively measured sleep efficiency. Assessment of physical capacity may therefore provide additional information when evaluating sleep-related risk in this population.

articles.title: Liver Proteomic Alterations Induced by Chronic Fluoride Exposure in Type 2 Diabetic Mice: An Exploratory Study.
articles.abstract: Water fluoridation is recognized as one of the major public health achievements of the 20th century due to its effectiveness in reducing dental caries. Recommended fluoride concentrations in drinking water (0.7-1.5 mgF/L) aim to maximize dental benefits while minimizing adverse effects. The liver plays a central role in detoxification and lipid metabolism, and recent studies suggest that fluoride exposure may disrupt lipid metabolic pathways. This exploratory study evaluated alterations in hepatic morphology, lipid profile, and liver proteome in type 2 diabetic mice chronically exposed to fluoride. Diabetic C57BL/6J mice received a high-fat diet throughout the experimental period and drinking water containing fluoride (0, 10, or 50 mgF/L) for 21 days, whereas nondiabetic control mice were maintained on a normocaloric diet with fluoride-free water. Liver fluoride levels were significantly higher in the high-dose group than in the other groups. High-dose fluoride reduced serum TG and VLDL levels compared with diabetic and nondiabetic controls, whereas low-dose fluoride increased LDL levels compared to nondiabetic controls. Hepatic glycogen content was reduced in the low-dose group. Proteomic analysis revealed overall downregulation of lipid metabolism-associated proteins in the low-dose group and upregulation of these proteins in the high-dose group. Comparison between groups showed a predominant downregulation of proteins related to mitochondrial and peroxisomal lipid oxidation. Altogether, these findings highlight a dose-dependent metabolic response to chronic fluoride exposure and suggest that fluoride may modulate lipid handling and metabolic flexibility in mice with type 2 diabetes.

articles.title: Duodenal-Jejunal Bypass Stent Versus Laparoscopic Sleeve Gastrectomy in Patients With Obesity and MASLD: Short-Term Efficacy and Perioperative Safety in a Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Obesity is a critical risk factor for progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) and duodenal-jejunal bypass stent (DJBS) are two major weight-loss modalities, yet comparative evidence remains limited.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients receiving bariatric interventions were retrospectively analysed. The patients were grouped according to different surgical methods, and the demographic data, anthropological characteristics, treatment plans and prognosis of the patients were compared and analysed.

RESULTS: A total of 96 patients were included in this study, with 31 patients in the DJBS group and 65 patients in the LSG group. The mean age of the DJBS group was 38.23 ± 9.93 years, and 19 patients (61.3%) were female. The absolute weight loss at 3 months was 8.29 ± 6.47 kg in the DJBS group and 17.66 ± 6.36 kg in the LSG group, with a statistically significant difference (p < 0.001). DJBS achieved superior reductions in LDL-C, fasting glucose and glycated haemoglobin and comparable outcomes for other metabolic markers. The overall post-procedural complication rate was similar between DJBS and LSG (8.99% vs. 18.85%, p = 0.424). Clavien-Dindo Grade I adverse events were less frequent in the DJBS group (p = 0.007). Multiple linear regression analysis demonstrated that surgical procedure (LSG vs. DJBS) (β = 8.458, p < 0.001) and preoperative waist circumference (β = 0.078, p = 0.038) were independent factors associated with post-procedural weight loss.

CONCLUSIONS: DJBS produces moderate short-term weight loss with better perioperative safety, while LSG achieves greater weight reduction. Both interventions were associated with comparable short-term changes in liver-related biochemical markers.

articles.title: QTc Prolongation and the Sympathoadrenal Response to Hypoglycaemia in Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To quantify changes in the heart rate-corrected QT interval (QTc) and concurrent sympathoadrenal responses during induced and spontaneous hypoglycaemia in people with Type 1 or Type 2 diabetes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 1990 to January 2026, restricted to English-language publications. Random-effects meta-analyses compared hypoglycaemic and euglycaemic states by setting, with subgroup and sensitivity analyses for diabetes type, QT correction method and analytical assumptions.

RESULTS: Across 32 studies, QTc prolongation was 44.0 ms (95% CI: 24.3-63.6) under induced and 16.4 ms (6.7-26.0) under spontaneous hypoglycaemia. Estimates were similar in Type 1 diabetes (27.2 ms, 12.9-41.5) and Type 2 diabetes (27.0 ms, 12.3-41.7). The all-study summary was 30.2 ms (17.9-42.4; 95% prediction interval -40.9 to 101.3; I2 = 98.4%). Heart rate rose by 5.0 bpm, systolic blood pressure by 3.1 mmHg, epinephrine by 1.75 nmol/L and norepinephrine by 0.66 nmol/L, while diastolic blood pressure fell by 4.4 mmHg and serum potassium by 0.44 mmol/L, all significantly. Only epinephrine change correlated with QTc change across studies after correction for multiple testing (ρ = 0.87).

CONCLUSIONS: Hypoglycaemia was associated with QTc prolongation during spontaneous episodes and under clamp conditions, in both diabetes types, alongside concurrent sympathoadrenal changes. The direction of the association was robust to all sensitivity analyses; its magnitude varied substantially between studies. Mean hypoglycaemic QTc exceeded 450 ms in six studies. Hypoglycaemia avoidance remains a safety consideration in patients with pre-existing repolarisation vulnerability or concomitant QT-prolonging medication.

articles.title: Real-World Comparison of Cardiorenal Outcomes With SGLT-2 Inhibitors Versus GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To compare cardiorenal outcomes, mortality and safety between sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2i) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA) in adults with Type 2 diabetes (T2D).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, new-user cohort study using the TriNetX global federated health research network. We identified 249 237 propensity score-matched pairs (498 474 total patients) who initiated SGLT-2i or GLP-1 RA between 2018 and 2023. The primary outcome was a kidney failure/death composite, defined as kidney failure, dialysis, kidney transplantation or all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included composite cardiovascular events, mortality and safety profiles.

RESULTS: SGLT-2i initiation was associated with a lower risk of the kidney failure/death composite compared with GLP-1 RA (HR: 0.87, 95% CI: 0.85-0.89). For the kidney-specific component, SGLT-2i initiation was associated with a lower risk of kidney failure, dialysis or kidney transplantation (HR: 0.74, 95% CI: 0.71-0.78), while all-cause mortality was also lower (HR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.88-0.93). The composite cardiovascular outcome (myocardial infarction, stroke, acute heart failure, cardiogenic shock, cardiac arrest or death) was broadly comparable between groups (HR: 0.98, 95% CI: 0.97-1.00).

CONCLUSIONS: SGLT-2i initiation was associated with lower risks of kidney failure-related outcomes and all-cause mortality compared with GLP-1 RA initiation, while cardiovascular outcomes were broadly comparable. These findings may inform individualized treatment selection in adults with T2D.

articles.title: Renal Effects of Dual GLP-1/Glucagon Receptor Agonism: How Should We SYNCHRONIZE With Emerging Evidence in Type 2 Diabetes and Obesity?
Same-day multiple-cannulation: A promising alternative method for establishing buttonhole tracks in hemodialysis patients-A multicenter randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study evaluated a novel same-day cannulation method for creating buttonhole tracks in arteriovenous fistulas of chronic hemodialysis patients.

METHOD: Patients were randomized: the control (C) group had one sharp needle cannulation per dialysis, while the intervention (I) group had 4-6 cannulations during the first session to establish the BH track. The primary outcome was 1-year BH survival. Secondary outcomes included pain scores (numeric rating scale); sessions needed to create a BH track, and 1-year AV fistula failure and BH infection rates.

RESULTS: BH survival and infection rates did not significantly differ between groups. The I-group had lower pain scores and required fewer sessions for track formation compared to the C-group.

CONCLUSION: While the same-day cannulation method did not impact BH survival or infection rates, it improved patient comfort and reduced track formation time, potentially simplifying care for chronic hemodialysis patients.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials.gov ID: NCT03989141.

articles.title: Physical layer authentication for fiber-optic links based on multi-wavelength chromatic dispersion fingerprints.
articles.abstract: To determine whether the physical fiber carrying an optical service has been substituted, rerouted, or spoofed, we propose a physical-layer authentication method based on multi-wavelength chromatic dispersion (CD) fingerprints. Link-specific variations in refractive-index profile, geometry, residual stress, and local microstructure produce repeatable differences in cumulative CD across multiple wavelengths. The proposed method estimates CD at N C-band wavelengths and applies reference-based standardization using statistics obtained during legitimate-link enrollment, followed by Euclidean-distance matching against templates stored in a secure template database (STDB). For a 100-km G.652D link, the calibrated decision threshold is ε = 0.3071. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis yields area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.992125, 0.999685, and 0.999999 for substitution, baseline spoofing, and rerouting attacks, respectively. Under common temperature changes from -15 to 15 °C and end-to-end spatial temperature variations from 0 to 30 °C, the legitimate-link false rejection rate (FRR) remains approximately 0.58-1.65%. Additional analyses evaluate the effects of fingerprint dimension, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), fiber length, and practical CD-estimation impairments. The method can reuse CD-estimation functions in coherent-receiver digital signal processing (DSP), providing a complementary physical-layer link-authentication mechanism for optical networks.

articles.title: Approaching the shot-noise limit in transient absorption and dispersion spectroscopy with machine learning.
articles.abstract: Transient absorption and dispersion spectroscopy is widely used to track light-induced dynamics in gases, liquids, and solids. For short interaction lengths and low pump intensities, the laser-induced changes are exceedingly weak, and limits in the sensitivity become critical. In most situations, classical excess noise dominates and can completely obscure the small transient signal. Here, we present a method based on machine learning that suppresses the noise and approaches the fundamental limit resulting from photon statistics. It relies solely on referenced detection without fast pump modulation. The pump-induced modulation is confined to a spot in the center of the probe field, so an area detector of an imaging spectrometer displays spatially distinct regions with and without transient changes. Both transient absorption and dispersion signals can be suppressed to the shot-noise limit by using machine learning, making fast pump modulation obsolete.

articles.title: Cholic acid supplementation alleviated gut-liver injury and remodeled the gut microbiota in Escherichia coli-infected mice.
articles.journal: Journal of the science of food and agriculture
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pathogen infection contributes to diarrhea, intestinal inflammation, and even death of animals. Thus, finding efficient drugs for alleviating or preventing bacterial infection is quite urgent for animal production. Bile acids have been recognized as important signaling molecules to regulate gut-liver homeostasis. Here, we investigated the potential effect of cholic acid (CA) on intestinal and hepatic injury in Escherichia coli (E. coli)-infected mice and elucidated the underlying mechanism.

RESULTS: Our data showed that different doses of CA (10, 20, and 30 mg kg-1 d-1) inhibited intestinal and hepatic inflammation and oxidative stress as indicated by reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines and increased antioxidant enzymes. CA also protected intestinal integrity and liver morphology against E. coli infection, and enhanced short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) levels in a dose-responsive manner. Furthermore, CA changed the microbial composition and structure. Differential analysis showed that E. coli infection increased the abundance of potential pathogens, including Escherichia-Shigella and Alloprevotella, while reducing beneficial SCFA-associated bacteria such as Lactobacillus and Enterorhabdus. CA treatment partially restored the proportion of Gordonibacter and Enterorhabdus, and reduced opportunistic pathogens such as Alloprevotella and Brevibacterium. More importantly, correlation analysis demonstrated that bacteria, including Enterorhabdus, Marvinbryantia, and Gordonibacter, were negatively correlated with serum cytokines and injury biomarkers, whereas only Brachybacterium showed a positive correlation with serum IL-6, and negative association with SCFAs.

CONCLUSION: Collectively, these findings indicate that CA alleviates E. coli-induced intestinal and hepatic injury, which may be associated with gut microbiota remodeling. Our study highlights that CA can serve as a potential intervention for treating bacterial infection. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

articles.title: Transcriptomic Characterization of a Monocyte Antigen-Presentation-Low Immunoparalysis State in Sepsis.
articles.journal: Omics : a journal of integrative biology
articles.abstract: Sepsis immunoparalysis is commonly monitored with monocyte HLA-DR, but whether a composite antigen-presentation-low transcriptomic state adds mechanistic information beyond existing endotypes remains uncertain. We integrated public bulk cohorts (GSE65682, GSE57065, and GSE54514) with single-cell datasets (GSE167363 and GSE279452) to define a directional immunoparalysis score combining low antigen-presentation/HLA-II and costimulatory response with high emergency-myeloid and inhibitory-tolerance programs. In GSE65682, the score was associated with 28-day mortality (n = 479; adjusted OR = 1.32, 95% CI: 1.01-1.72; p = 0.0396), although discrimination was modest (AUC = 0.568, 95% CI: 0.506-0.628). The score overlapped with MARS endotypes, was highest in MARS2, and remained associated after age, sex, and MARS adjustment (OR = 1.39, 95% CI: 1.00-1.92; p = 0.048). GSE57065 supported disease-state elevation, whereas GSE54514 and APACHE II analyses defined negative predictive boundaries. Single-cell analyses localized the signal to antigen-presenting and pro-inflammatory monocytes, classical monocytes, and dendritic cells. The proposed transcript panel is hypothesis-generating for prospective immune-state monitoring, not a validated clinical decision tool.

articles.title: ADMET property prediction and toxicity profiling of CDK2 inhibitors: a practical cheminformatics tutorial using ADMET-AI 2.0 and RDKit.
articles.abstract: Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity (ADMET) prediction plays a central role in modern computer-aided drug discovery by enabling early evaluation of pharmacokinetic behaviour and safety liabilities. This tutorial presents a reproducible computational workflow for large-scale ADMET profiling using ADMET-AI 2.0, a graph neural network-based prediction platform, applied to 200 cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2) inhibitors curated from ChEMBL release 35. Implemented within an annotated Jupyter notebook, the workflow integrates cheminformatics preprocessing, physicochemical property analysis, drug-likeness evaluation, structural alert screening, absorption and distribution profiling, CYP450-mediated metabolism prediction, excretion assessment, toxicity evaluation, Tox21 pathway analysis, DrugBank percentile benchmarking, and composite multi-parameter optimisation scoring. A total of 104 ADMET-related outputs were generated per compound, including 52 predictive endpoints and 52 corresponding DrugBank approved-drug percentile rankings. The 200 curated CDK2 inhibitors exhibited 100% Lipinski Ro5 compliance, 38.5% predicted CYP3A4 inhibition, 73.5% predicted hERG liability, and 99.5% predicted DILI risk, with a mean composite ADMET score of 0.46 and a mean traffic light green flag count of 9.5/13. The workflow provides an accessible and FAIR-compliant framework for ADMET analysis, cheminformatics education, and reproducible computational drug discovery.Scientific contributionThis work contributes a structured educational framework for teaching and implementing computational ADMET analysis in modern drug discovery. To be explicit about the nature of this contribution: the novelty is pedagogical and integrative rather than methodological, no new prediction model, algorithm, or endpoint is introduced. The study demonstrates how an existing graph neural network-based prediction model (ADMET-AI) can be integrated with open-source cheminformatics workflows to support interpretable and reproducible pharmacokinetic assessment. Beyond endpoint prediction, the tutorial emphasises practical data handling, workflow automation, compound prioritisation, and transparent result interpretation within a Jupyter notebook environment. The inclusion of DrugBank percentile benchmarking, traffic-light visualisation, and composite scoring strategies provides learners and researchers with practical, worked examples of established multi-parameter decision-making approaches during lead optimisation, rather than new decision frameworks in their own right. By combining methodological clarity with FAIR and reproducible research principles, the workflow serves as a scalable resource for cheminformatics education, computational pharmacology training, and ADMET-guided drug development studies.

articles.title: Peripherally inserted central catheter-related complications: A national prospective multicenter study of incidence, risk factors and outcomes in China.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to assess the incidence, risk factors, and outcomes of PICC-related complications in China.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This prospective multicenter cohort study was performed at 60 hospitals located in 30 cities in 7 provincial-level region throughout China. The primary outcome was a composite of PICC-related complications (catheter dislodgement, catheter occlusions, catheter-associated skin injuries (CASIs), catheter-related thrombosis (CRT), central line-associated bloodstream infections (CLABSIs), catheter malposition, catheter fracture, phlebitis, and drainage from the catheter or insertion site). Cox regression was used to investigate the risk factors for PICC-related complications.

RESULTS: Among 7321 included participants, the mean (SD) patient age was 56.4 (14.2) years, and 4468 patients (61.06%) were female. The incidence of PICC-related complications was 15.47% (1133/7321), among which catheter dislodgement was the most common (4.69%), followed by catheter occlusions (3.73%), and CASIs (3.25%). The incidence of complications did not fluctuate throughout the entire indwelling period. Unplanned catheter removal occurred in 546 patients, representing a low overall unplanned removal rate of 7.46% (546/7321). However, this accounted for 48.19% of the 1133 patients who developed complications. Multivariable analyses identified risk factors for the three catheter-related complications. Higher body mass index (BMI) increased dislodgement risk (HR 1.04), female sex was protective against dislodgement (HR 0.62), and elevated D‑dimer and prior thrombosis were associated with catheter occlusions. Multiple catheter advancement attempts and insertion indications were independently associated with both occlusions and skin injuries; non‑dominant arm insertion was associated only with occlusions.

CONCLUSION: The overall incidence of PICC-related complications was 15.47%, with a 7.46% unplanned removal rate. Notably, 48.19% of these complications necessitated unplanned removal. Specific patient characteristics and clinical variables were identified as independent risk factors for the primary complications. Implementing targeted, evidence-based management strategies based on modifiable factors may mitigate the risk of adverse events and improve patient safety.

articles.title: Carbapenem resistance in pediatric Acinetobacter baumannii urinary tract infections: molecular determinants.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In the pediatric population, carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) is a significant cause of hospital-acquired infections, particularly hospital-acquired urinary tract infections (HA-UTIs). There are a few studies on the molecular mechanisms of resistance to CRAB among children.

OBJECTIVE: To detect the prevalence of CRAB among children with HA-UTIs and to evaluate associated carbapenemase genes and clinical risk factors.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 100 children with HA-UTIs. Isolates were identified using standard microbiology techniques, and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) was detected according to the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) guidelines. Carbapenemase genes (blaOXA-23-like, blaOXA-24/40-like, blaOXA-58-like, and blaNDM) were detected by PCR. Data were statistically analyzed to assess the association between clinical factors and carbapenem resistance (CR).

RESULTS: CR was identified in 73% of isolates. High rates of AMR were observed for cephalosporins and fluoroquinolones. The most prevalent gene was the blaOXA-23-like gene (60%), followed by the blaOXA-58-like (34%), the blaOXA-24/40-like (30%), and the blaNDM (15%). A significant association was observed between resistance to carbapenems and the carbapenemase genes blaOXA-23-like and blaNDM (p < 0.05). Clinical factors like ICU admission and catheterization did not show a significant association with resistance.

CONCLUSION: Carbapenem resistance among pediatric Acinetobacter baumannii UTIs is highly prevalent and primarily driven by molecular mechanisms, particularly OXA-23 and NDM carbapenemases. This underscores the significance of molecular diagnostics and infection control in pediatric healthcare settings.

articles.title: Special collection on "Stroke Management and Therapy" accompanying the 99th congress of the german society of neurology.
Spatiotemporal variations and influencing factors of highly pathogenic avian influenza risk in the Pan-Tibetan Plateau region.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) is a major infectious disease threatening the poultry industry and public health severely. The spatiotemporal patterns and driving forces, however, remain elusive in the Tibetan Plateau and its vicinity, an ecologically critical corridor for migratory birds. This study aims to identify the factors driving these variations and to assess the HPAI risk in wild birds and domestic poultry across this region.

METHODS: Based on HPAI records from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations and the Official Veterinary Bulletin and 34 potential drivers in the Pan-Tibetan Plateau (PTP), comprising Xizang Autonomous Region (XZ), Qinghai Province (QH), Gansu Province (GS), Sichuan Province (SC), Yunnan Province (YN) and Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region (XJ), this study utilized the MaxEnt models to simulate spatial patterns of HPAI risk of wild birds, domestic poultry, and the integration of both, and identify key risk factors.

RESULTS: Performances of models for wild birds and domestic poultry models were robust (both Test AUC values > 0.9). Although the mixed model performed acceptably overall, it significantly underestimated the infection risk in wild birds. High-risk areas of wild birds HPAI were concentrated in XZ, QH, GS and XJ (> 93%), showing a close relationship with natural factors like slope and distance to water sources. Conversely, those for domestic poultry were mainly distributed in YN, SC, GS (about 70%) and the peripheries of provincial capitals, dominated by socioeconomic variables such as gross domestic product and road networks. Moreover, overlapping HPAI risk areas were found in GS, XJ, XZ, and QH, which may be associated with increasing poultry production and fragmented wetland landscape. Additionally, it's recommended that HPAI risk modeling be stratified by host types, particularly in areas with sparse surveillance data.

CONCLUSIONS: HPAI risks in wild birds and domestic poultry are dominated by natural factors and socioeconomic conditions respectively, and overlapping high-risk areas require focused attention. This study contributes to the understanding of HPAI transmission mechanisms in different hosts, providing a scientific basis for differentiated surveillance in the PTP.

articles.title: Deconstructing cardiovascular heterogeneity in septic shock: V0-LV invariance, vasopressin mismatch, and RVR circularity.
Coronary microvascular dysfunction and obstructive coronary artery disease in sepsis-associated myocardial injury: authors' reply.
Writing towards death: male patient voices and medical landscape in two Egyptian illness narratives.
articles.journal: Philosophy, ethics, and humanities in medicine : PEHM
articles.abstract: In the field of medical humanities, illness narratives are often central to most discussions. However, Arabic-language illness narratives, particularly those written by males, are largely absent from this body of scholarship, which centres mostly on Anglophone corpora. This scholarly blind spot affects the linguistic as well as the cultural scope of research on embodied suffering and the voices of patients from Arabic-speaking regions. Thus, this study addresses this gap by reading illness narratives by two Egyptian male authors: the late Osama Eldanasouri's Kalbi al-Harim Kalbi al-Habib: al-Nusus al-Akhira or [My Ageing Dog, My Beloved Dog: The Last Texts] (2007/2021) and the late Muhammad Abouelgheit's Ana Qadim Ayyuha al-Daw' or [Oh Light, I am Coming] (2022). The first is a narrative of Eldanasouri's prolonged suffering from Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD), resulting in his dependence on dialysis as a lifeline, while the other is an account of Abouelgheit's terminal cancer. The study draws on Critical Medical Humanities' attentiveness to gender and sociocultural factors in the embodied experience of illness; masculinity studies, especially the representation of the ill male body; and Michael Bury's conceptualisation of biographical disruption. Utilising this combined framework, the study examines how representations of illness, death, and mortality vary across different illness temporalities (prolonged CKD vs accelerated mortality); how the narratives challenge conventional notions of masculinity; and how both narratives are shaped by contrasting medical geographies and institutional conditions. Read in tandem, these texts offer a more nuanced understanding of Bury's rigid before/after model, often associated with biographical disruption, and steer the narratives towards autothanatography, where writing is influenced by a heightened awareness of narrowed futurity. In addition, the study argues that texts construct narratives of sick male patients not as a straightforward self-expression but as a negotiated response to bodily vulnerability as well as culturally valued forms of hegemonic masculinity. Meanwhile, the narratives construct an image of disparate illness experiences mediated by two different medical contexts. Thus, this adds to the ongoing critical medical humanities scholarship by analysing Arabic-language male illness narratives, which broadens the linguistic and cultural scope of the field.

articles.title: When emergency medicine isn't there: a scoping review of global acute care substitutes and complements for disaster response and surge capacity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Disasters and everyday gaps in emergency care force acute illness and injury to be managed outside of formal emergency medicine (EM) and emergency medical services (EMS) systems. Because EM capacity varies substantially worldwide, this scoping review applies a substitutes-and-complements framework to the mechanisms that deliver acute care in and around formal EM or EMS, classifying their roles as substitutes, complements, or both across levels of EM system maturity and disaster conditions. The resulting typology serves as an inventory of latent disaster surge capacity.

MAIN TEXT: Following the PRISMA extension for scoping reviews, five databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and CINAHL) were searched, yielding 11,161 records. After title and abstract screening, 758 full-text articles were assessed for eligibility and 115 studies were included. We charted study type, country, and EM system maturity, using a codebook derived from American College of Emergency Physicians' (ACEP) International Ambassador country reports, the primary acute-care mechanism, care-delivery context, and COVID-19 relevance. Mechanisms were then classified by whether they substituted for or complemented formal EM. Publications were concentrated in the COVID-19 era (82/115, 71% from 2020 or later) and in high-income, mature-EM settings (United States 30%; 64/115 mature-EM). The most common mechanisms were lay and community first-responder programs (n = 18), hospital-at-home and remote monitoring (n = 15), and telehealth-based emergency and behavioral-health services. Overall, substitutes predominated (75/115), whereas complements (18/115) clustered in mature-EM systems.

CONCLUSIONS: Our inventory of latent surge capacity reframes each mechanism as a potential candidate for transfer across the EM-maturity spectrum: routine substitutes used in low-maturity systems may offer pre-planned crisis capacity for mature systems, while lower-infrastructure telehealth models may provide decision support or partial substitution where formal EM is limited. The substitute-complement balance tracks maturity, but the opportunity lies in translating mechanisms to the settings where they are not currently used as such.

articles.title: Short-term outcomes of robotic-assisted direct anterior THA in patients with generalised ligamentous laxity: a propensity-matched study.
articles.journal: Hip international : the journal of clinical and experimental research on hip pathology and therapy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Generalised ligamentous laxity (GLL) has been linked to instability and implant failure in primary total hip arthroplasty (THA). This study assessed outcomes of GLL patients undergoing robotic-assisted direct anterior approach (DAA) THA.

METHODS: Retrospectively analysed prospectively collected data from patients who had robotic-assisted primary DAA THA between August 2013 and October 2022, with a minimum 2-year follow-up.
