Eligible patients completed at least one patient-reported outcome measure (PROMs): modified Harris Hip Score (mHHS), Hip disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score for Joint Replacement (HOOS-JR), Forgotten Joint Score (FJS), visual analogue scale (VAS), and satisfaction. Patients with GLL (Beighton ⩾4) were matched 1:2 to controls (Beighton ⩽3) by age, sex, BMI, and follow-up. Outcomes included PROMs changes, achievement of MCID/PASS, complications, and revisions.

RESULTS: Of 126 patients, 42 had GLL and 84 were controls. Both groups showed significant improvements in PROMs, high satisfaction, and similar achievement of MCID and PASS. Revision rates were comparable (p > 0.05): 1 GLL patient (2.4%) for infection and 1 control (1.2%) for aseptic loosening. No dislocations occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: GLL patients undergoing robotic-assisted DAA THA achieved favorable outcomes and survivorship comparable to controls, with no dislocations at minimum 2-year follow-up. Larger multicentre studies are needed to confirm whether this approach truly mitigates the higher dislocation and revision risk in the GLL populations.

articles.title: The relationship between early warning scores at intensive care unit discharge and risk of intensive care unit readmission in adult and pediatric populations: a scoping review.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Readmission after discharge from the intensive care unit (ICU) occurs globally at a rate of approximately 1-12% and is associated with adverse patient outcomes. Despite these findings, there is no internationally accepted tool to guide or standardize decisions regarding ICU discharge. In this scoping review, we aimed to evaluate the use of early warning scores (EWSs) measured at or around the time of ICU discharge as predictors of subsequent ICU readmission in adult and pediatric populations.

SOURCE: With support from a medical librarian, we searched MEDLINE®, Embase®, and the Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature from database inception to December 14, 2025. We included quantitative observational and interventional studies that evaluated any EWS (e.g., National EWS [NEWS]/NEWS2, Modified EWS [MEWS], Pediatric EWS [PEWS], Rothman Index, Risk Scoring Index, or related tools) at ICU discharge, immediately prior to transfer, or immediately upon ward admission and reported unplanned ICU readmission following transfer to a hospital ward. Unplanned ICU readmissions were defined as any unplanned return to an ICU after discharge to the ward. We excluded studies in which patients were discharged to locations other than a ward (e.g., home, long-term care) or that focused solely on interfacility transfer. Screening and data extraction were performed in duplicate using a standardized template, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer.

PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: The search identified 7,977 records, of which 4,824 remained after removal of duplicates. Of the articles, 58 underwent full-text review, and 20 studies met inclusion criteria. The studies were conducted across North America, Europe, and Asia and included both adult (n = 14) and pediatric (n = 6) populations. All were observational (retrospective or prospective) or pre-post intervention designs; no randomized controlled trials were identified. A range of tools were evaluated, including NEWS/NEWS2, MEWS, PEWS, the Rothman Index, the Risk Scoring Index, and several machine-learning-based EWS models. Of the 20 studies, 17 reported a significant association between higher EWS values at or near ICU discharge and increased risk of unplanned ICU readmission, while three found no significant association. Across studies, readmission rates and EWS thresholds varied, and there was considerable heterogeneity in populations, settings, and outcome time frames. The risk of bias was generally low to moderate across QUADAS-2 domains, although several studies had high or unclear risk in key areas-most commonly patient selection and index test blinding-limiting causal inference.

CONCLUSIONS: Most available studies report that higher EWS values at ICU discharge are associated with an increased likelihood of ICU readmission. Early warning scores may therefore serve as useful adjuncts to clinical judgement when assessing discharge readiness. Nevertheless, the current evidence base is limited by the absence of randomized or robust interventional trials, and substantial heterogeneity, which limits causal inference and the ability to determine whether EWS-guided discharge protocols improve outcomes. Further multicentre prospective studies are needed to determine whether EWS-guided discharge protocols improve patient outcomes, reduce readmissions, and optimize use of ICU resources.

articles.title: Associations between comorbidities and bladder conditions in patients with interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To examine the associations among functional somatic disorders, psychiatric disorders, medical diseases, and extravesical inflammatory disorders with bladder conditions in patients diagnosed with interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome (IC/BPS).

METHODS: Patients with confirmed IC/BPS were included in this retrospective analysis. Cystoscopic evaluation was performed to distinguish Hunner-type IC (HIC) from non-Hunner IC/BPS (NHIC). Bladder phenotypes in patients undergoing hydrodistention were classified according to maximal bladder capacity (MBC) and glomerulation grade. Treatment outcomes were assessed using the Global Response Assessment scale (GRA). Data on patients' comorbidities were obtained from chart reviews and classified into functional somatic disorders, psychiatric disorders, autoimmune diseases, or medical diseases. Fifteen urinary biomarkers were examined, including inflammatory and neurogenic proteins, as well as oxidative stress biomarkers. The associations between bladder condition and urinary biomarker levels were compared between patients with and without comorbidities.

RESULTS: A total of 389 patients with IC/BPS, including 44 with HIC and 345 with NHIC, were included. Of these, 324 (83.3%) had at least one recorded comorbidity. After Bonferroni correction, depression remained associated with cystoscopic bladder phenotypes, whereas the associations with insomnia and arrhythmia were no longer significant. In multivariable analysis restricted to patients with NHIC, depression was associated with higher odds of a cystoscopic phenotype characterized by glomerulation grade 2/3 and MBC <760 mL (adjusted OR 2.093, 95% CI 1.196-3.661, p = 0.010). Patients with selected somatic and psychiatric comorbidities had lower urinary 8-OHdG and higher TNF-α levels than those without these comorbidities, with both differences remaining significant after Bonferroni correction (adjusted p <0.015 and p = 0.045, respectively). Overall satisfactory improvement (GRA ≥2) at the latest available follow-up was comparable between patients with and without comorbidities (56.0% vs. 56.9%, p = 0.896). Patients with depression had a lower rate of satisfactory improvement than those without depression (47.5% vs. 59.2%, p = 0.043).

CONCLUSION: Comorbidities were common among patients with IC/BPS. Depression was associated with cystoscopic bladder phenotypes, while urinary 8-OHdG and TNF-α levels differed according to selected comorbidity status. The clinical significance of these biomarker findings remains uncertain and requires further investigation.

articles.title: Contrast-Free ADC Intensity Features for Early Neurological Deterioration in Lacunar Infarction: An Exploratory Comparison with Perfusion Imaging and Deep Learning.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: Early neurological deterioration (END) affects approximately one in five patients with acute lacunar infarction and is associated with poor functional outcome. Hypoperfusion on contrast-enhanced perfusion MRI has been linked to END, but perfusion imaging requires intravenous contrast and is not part of the routine acute workup for minor stroke. We explored whether intensity features of non-contrast structural MRI carry information on END, using the visually classified pattern from a contrast-enhanced perfusion study in the same patients as a reference. We analyzed a prospectively collected single-center cohort of patients with acute lacunar infarction who underwent MRI within 24 h of symptom onset, including diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) mapping, fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR), and dynamic susceptibility contrast perfusion imaging. END was defined as an increase of ≥ 2 points on the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale within 72 h. One hundred patients with complete imaging and outcome data were included, of whom 20 (20.0%) developed END. Candidate predictors comprised intensity features of the infarct core and an 8-mm perilesional rim normalized to whole-brain intensity, 201 DWI texture features, and 22 clinical and laboratory variables. Models were evaluated by 10-times-repeated 5-fold stratified cross-validation with the decision threshold fixed at 0.5; feature selection and standardization were performed within training folds only. The visually classified perfusion pattern served as a contrast-based clinical benchmark. ADC intensity features discriminated END with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.699 (approximate patient-level 95% CI 0.56-0.84) and an area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.473 against a base rate of 0.200; at the fixed threshold, sensitivity was 52.0% and positive predictive value 27.9%. The perfusion pattern alone yielded a sensitivity of 70.0%, a specificity of 60.0% and a negative predictive value of 88.9% (balanced accuracy 0.650). The difference between the two predictors was small relative to the sampling uncertainty at 20 events, so neither superiority nor equivalence could be established. The strongest individual feature was the 75th percentile of normalized ADC within the infarct core (univariate AUC 0.702), with higher values in patients who deteriorated (median 0.615 versus 0.555, P = 0.005). Adding the perfusion pattern to the ADC features did not improve discrimination (AUC 0.665, 95% CI 0.645-0.684). The signal was confined to the ADC map: models built on DWI or FLAIR intensity alone performed below chance (AUC 0.463 and 0.453). More complex models did not reach the ADC model at this sample size: 201 DWI texture features reached an AUC of 0.566, clinical and laboratory variables at best 0.625, and an end-to-end 2.5D ResNet-18 0.404 with random initialization, 0.482 with ImageNet pretraining and 0.611 for a small network sized for the data. In this exploratory single-center study, ADC intensity features obtained without contrast were associated with END in acute lacunar infarction, with discrimination similar in magnitude to the contrast-enhanced perfusion benchmark; the cohort was too small to establish equivalence, and threshold-level performance is insufficient to guide monitoring. Texture analysis and deep learning could not be adequately trained with 20 events, so their relative merit cannot be judged. ADC appears to be the informative non-contrast sequence; the findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger, multicenter cohorts.

articles.title: Congestion, Inflammation, and Renal Impairment Mediate the Association Between Cardiac Troponin and Mortality in Acute Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiac troponin is recognized as a strong predictor of mortality in patients with acute heart failure (AHF). The aim of this study was to evaluate the prognostic impact of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) on mortality risk in patients with AHF in relation to inflammatory, congestion, and renal indices.

METHODS: We enrolled 431 patients (79 ± 10 years, 51% male) with AHF. At admission, hemodynamic congestion, inflammatory status, and renal function were assessed by means of brain natriuretic peptide (BNP, ng/l), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP, mg/l), and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR, ml/min), respectively. Mediation analyses were performed to assess the presence and magnitude of these components.

RESULTS: The cumulative incidence of mortality at 180-day follow-up was 36%. hs-cTnI significantly correlated with BNP (r = 0.28), hs-CRP (r = 0.31), and eGFR (r = - 0.23); these variables explained 18% of the overall variability in hs-cTnI. In univariate Cox regression analysis, hs-cTnI, hs-CRP, BNP, and eGFR were predictors of all-cause death. The association between hs-cTnI and mortality was largely mediated by inflammation, congestion, and renal function, which collectively explained 69% of the total effect. In multivariate analysis, only ln hs-CRP (HR: 1.21; 1.08-1.37), ln BNP (HR: 1.37; 1.09-1.74), and eGFR (HR: 0.99; 0.98-1.00) remained independent predictors of mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: Elevated troponin levels in AHF might be influenced by the coexistence of systemic inflammation, hemodynamic congestion, and renal dysfunction. Therefore, circulating troponin in AHF may be considered an integrated biomarker reflecting multiple pathophysiological processes.

articles.title: Arbovirus Investigation in Free-Living Bats in Midwest Brazil, 2017-2018.
articles.abstract: Epidemic arboviruses such as dengue (DENV), zika (ZIKV), and chikungunya (CHIKV) are maintained between humans and Aedes aegypti mosquitoes and have great impact on public health in Brazil. In addition to these epidemic arboviruses, enzootic arboviruses such as yellow fever (YFV), mayaro (MAYV), and oropouche (OROV) viruses, that circulate between wildlife and bloodsucking dipterans, are also of great medical concern in the country. If these viruses circulate in synanthropic vertebrate species, and if these animals play a role in arboviruses transmission cycles, remains unclear. Bats are commonly found in large populations at the animal-human interface, so their exposure to arboviruses merits continuous surveillance. Between 2017 and 2018, we investigated the circulation of Brazil's important arboviruses in bats (n=189) collected at the human-animal interface areas of Midwest Brazil. Carollia perspicillata and Artibeus lituratus were the most common species captured. Using RT-qPCR assays, we conducted a molecular screening for DENV, ZIKV, CHIKV, YFV, MAYV, and OROV RNA in liver, kidney, and brain samples of free-ranging bats. Additionally, plasma of 79 bats were tested by plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT) for specific neutralizing antibodies for OROV and plasma of 73 bats were tested for MAYV. All tissue specimens tested negative by RT-qPCR suggesting no current infections by any of the arboviruses tested. All bats presented PRNT90 titer <20 for OROV and MAYV and therefore considered seronegative. Plaque reduction below the predefined threshold for seropositivity for MAYV was observed in several individuals and merits further investigation. Plasma samples from 67 other bats also presented plaque reduction for MAYV that could not be confirmed due to limited sample volume for serial dilution in PRNT. The absence of active infection by arboviruses associated with the large number of bats presenting plaque reduction for MAYV merits further investigation.

articles.title: Dual-Plane Retromuscular Placement of Polyurethane-Coated Breast Implants in Patients with Compromised Pectoral Musculature: Clinical Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polyurethane foam-coated breast implants have been associated with reduced capsular contracture and improved positional stability due to their distinct tissue-implant interface. However, evidence on their use in dual-plane retromuscular pockets, particularly for complex primary and secondary breast procedures, remains limited.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study aimed to evaluate the clinical outcomes and surgical rationale for the selective use of polyurethane-coated implants in a dual-plane retromuscular pocket in complex breast surgery. Indications included compromised pectoralis major muscle, prior breast surgery, or insufficient soft tissue coverage. Demographics, indications, implant characteristics, complications, and reoperation rates were analyzed descriptively.

RESULTS: Among 1293 implant-based breast procedures performed during the study period, 68 patients (5.3%) met the inclusion criteria. Procedures included augmentation (n = 17), augmentation-mastopexy (n = 49), and reduction with implants (n = 2). The mean patient age was 38.1 years, and the mean implant volume was 350 mL. The mean follow-up was 9 months (range, 1-60 months). Overall, 5 patients (7.4%) required reoperation: 3 (4.4%) for cosmetic reasons and 2 (2.9%) for complications (an infection and a waterfall deformity). No cases of clinically significant capsular contracture, implant rupture, or major malposition were observed during follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: In carefully selected complex primary and secondary breast cases, the use of polyurethane-coated implants in a dual-plane retromuscular pocket was associated with acceptable short-term complication and reoperation rates. This approach may represent a valuable option for patients with compromised musculature or limited soft tissue coverage, warranting further investigation in larger, prospective studies with longer follow-up.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE IV: This journal requires that authors assign a level of evidence to each article. For a full description of these Evidence-Based Medicine ratings, please refer to the Table of Contents or the online Instructions to Authors www.springer.com/00266 .

articles.title: Povorcitinib for nonsegmental vitiligo: two randomized, controlled, phase 3 STOP-V trials.
articles.abstract: There is an unmet need for repigmentation therapies for patients with nonsegmental vitiligo (NSV) who are candidates for systemic therapy. Here, 52-week primary results are reported from two parallel phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of once-daily povorcitinib (oral, highly selective JAK1 inhibitor) 30 mg in adults with moderate-to-severe NSV (STOP-V1 and STOP-V2). STOP-V1 and STOP-V2 enrolled 467 and 449 patients, respectively. In both studies, the primary endpoint of ≥75% improvement in the facial Vitiligo Area Scoring Index (F-VASI75) at week 52 was met, demonstrating statistically significant and clinically meaningful repigmentation with povorcitinib versus placebo (STOP-V1: 18.9% versus 6.8%; odds ratio, 3.1; 95% confidence interval 1.6-5.9; P = 0.0003; STOP-V2: 18.9% versus 3.1%; odds ratio, 7.5; 95% confidence interval 3.0-18.6; P < 0.0001). Povorcitinib was well tolerated; the percentage of patients with any treatment-emergent adverse event (TEAE) was similar between the povorcitinib and placebo groups in both studies (STOP-V1/STOP-V2, 68.7%/66.7% versus 63.7%/62.7%). The most common TEAEs with povorcitinib were nasopharyngitis (STOP-V1/STOP-V2, 11.2%/11.3% versus placebo, 9.8%/11.1%), acne (10.7%/10.8% versus 3.0%/2.2%) and upper respiratory tract infection (6.9%/14.0% versus 9.0%/10.7%). Serious TEAEs were generally single events, and Janus kinase inhibitor class-specific TEAEs were absent or rare. These results support once-daily povorcitinib as an effective and well-tolerated systemic treatment for adults with moderate-to-severe NSV. ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers: NCT06113445 , NCT06113471 .

articles.title: Global, regional and national burden of cervical cancer in 1990-2023 with forecasts to 2050: a Global Burden of Disease study.
articles.abstract: Although highly preventable, cervical cancer remains one of the most common malignancies among women worldwide. As part of the Global Burden of Disease study, we estimated cervical cancer incidence, mortality and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts to 2050. In 2023, 887,000 new cases (95% uncertainty interval 682,000-1,170,000), 369,000 deaths (292,000-475,000) and 13.3 million DALYs (10.1-17.4) were estimated globally. Age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) and age-standardized mortality rates (ASMR) were more than four and seven times higher in low- versus high-income countries. Between 1990 and 2023, global ASIR was largely stable (-0.4% (-26.6 to 34.7)), whereas ASMR changed by -17.5% (-36.2 to 13.4). All cervical cancer DALYs were attributable to human papillomavirus infection, with tobacco use contributing 5.9% (3.2-9.3) globally. By 2050, global ASIR and ASMR are forecast to change by -12.5% (-25.7 to 3.5) and -9.0% (-21.5 to 6.6) from 2024, yet absolute cases and deaths are forecast to rise by 20.2% (4.6-38.5) and 39.3% (23.6-57.3). ASIR and ASMR are forecast to remain highest in low-income countries. Intensified action is needed to accelerate progress.

articles.title: Clonal hematopoiesis and cytopenias following CAR19 therapy.
articles.abstract: CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy (CAR19) improves survival in relapsed/refractory large B cell lymphoma compared with immunochemotherapy with intent for autologous hematopoietic cell transplantation (autoHCT). However, major toxicities include prolonged cytopenias, infection and secondary hematologic malignancies. Here, to investigate these complications, we studied patients with lymphoma receiving CAR19 and compared clinical outcomes to propensity-matched autoHCT-treated controls. CAR19-treated patients exhibited impaired immune reconstitution and increased infection. Bone marrow analysis showed that prolonged post-CAR cytopenias are associated with clonal cytopenias of undetermined significance and interferon-mediated inflammation. Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) commonly expanded following CAR19 infusion and was associated with impaired immune reconstitution and treatment-related myeloid malignancy (tMN). Post-CAR tMN was molecularly and clinically comparable to post-autoHCT tMN. Single-cell DNA analysis revealed mostly independent CH clones, while CAR integration into CH-mutant T cells occurred frequently and may drive expansion and persistence. Together, these findings implicate CH expansion and marrow inflammation in key CAR19-associated toxicities.

articles.title: [New sepsis guidelines: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2026 and German Sepsis Society 2025 -Competing or complementary?].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis is one of the leading causes of death in intensive care units worldwide. In German-speaking countries, patient management is primarily guided by two sets of guidelines: the international Surviving Sepsis Campaign (SSC) guidelines and the S3 guidelines of the German Sepsis Society (DSG). While the DSG guidelines were published in 2025 as an evidence-based adaptation of the SSC 2021 guidelines, the SSC has since released an updated international version in 2026.

OBJECTIVE: To provide a structured analysis of the key content areas, similarities and differences between the two guidelines, with a particular focus on the timing of treatment initiation, anti-infective treatment and hemodynamic management.

RESULTS: Both guidelines reflect not so much a fundamental shift in strategy but more a consolidation of evidence and a refinement of concepts. Three overarching themes can be identified: a broadened perspective encompassing the entire continuum of care, from the prehospital setting to post-sepsis follow-up, the increasing integration of antibiotic stewardship principles and in SSC 2026, the introduction of a graded sepsis terminology (definite/probable/possible/unlikely). Areas of agreement include the importance of early anti-infective treatment, the preferential use of balanced crystalloids, norepinephrine as the first-line vasopressor, the inclusion of capillary refill time as a perfusion parameter and a strong recommendation for prolonged or continuous beta-lactam infusion. Differences are evident in the specificity of antimicrobial recommendations, the definition of risk factors warranting empirical antifungal treatment and several new recommendations introduced in SSC 2026, such as a lower mean arterial pressure (MAP) target of 60-65 mm Hg for patients aged ≥ 65 years, initiation of treatment in the prehospital setting and source control within 6 h.

CONCLUSION: The DSG 2025 and SSC 2026 guidelines should be regarded as complementary rather than competing frameworks. The DSG 2025 remains the practical, high-resolution handbook for care in the Central European context, while the SSC 2026 outlines the international direction: away from a purely acute care set of rules towards an individualized, continuum-based model of care.

articles.title: Selective profiling of translationally active tRNAs and their dynamics under stress.
articles.abstract: During translation, transfer RNAs (tRNAs) deliver specific amino acids to the ribosome in a coordinated manner with the sequence encoded by the messenger RNA. Despite their central role in protein synthesis, their precise contribution to the modulation of translation remains poorly understood, primarily due to lack of methods to characterize tRNA abundances and their modifications from actively translating ribosomes. Here we develop tRIBO-seq, a simple and robust nanopore-based method to selectively capture ribosome-associated native tRNA populations (ribo-tRNAs) from actively translating ribosomes, providing tRNA abundance, modification and fragmentation information from a single experiment. Using tRIBO-seq, we find that ribo-tRNAs, but often not total tRNAs, are significantly altered on stress. Notably, we find that tRNAome alterations strongly vary depending on the stress type; while viral infection and leucine deprivation leads to changes in ribo-tRNA abundances, methionine starvation causes a dramatic loss of methyl-based tRNA modifications. By contrast, we find that arsenite exposure does not alter tRNA abundances nor modification patterns, but rather causes major fragmentation events in selected subsets of ribo-tRNAs. Altogether, tRIBO-seq offers a robust and reproducible approach to map the full tRNA landscape-capturing tRNA abundance, modification and fragmentation patterns-across both total and actively translating tRNA populations, revealing the dynamics of the tRNAome with unprecedented resolution, in a single experiment.

articles.title: Dedicated Versus Generic ePTFE-covered Stent-grafts for Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt in Decompensated Cirrhosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Overt Hepatic Encephalopathy and Shunt Dysfunction.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To estimate the pooled sub-distribution hazard ratio (sHR) of overt hepatic encephalopathy (OHE) and shunt dysfunction in patients with decompensated cirrhosis undergoing transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) using dedicated stent‑grafts (DSG) versus generic stent‑grafts (GSG), and to compare their estimated 1-year event risk, relative risk (RR), and risk difference (RD).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, major biomedical databases were searched for retrospective studies including adults with decompensated cirrhosis undergoing TIPS with DSG or GSG. Pooled estimates for sHR, one‑year cumulative incidence, RR, and RD for OHE and shunt dysfunction were calculated.

RESULTS: The pooled estimated 1-year event risk of OHE was 14.3% (95% CI: 7.2-26.4%; I2 = 85%) with DSG and 17.4% (95% CI: 8.1-33.4%; I2 = 91%) with GSG, with no significant subgroup difference (p = 0.611). The RR for OHE with DSG versus GSG was 0.81 (95% CI: 0.51-1.28; p = 0.37; I2=55%), the RD was - 0.03 (95% CI: -0.13 to 0.06; p = 0.45; I2 = 82%), and the pooled sHR was 0.69 (95% CI: 0.13-3.66; p = 0.44; I2 = 78%), none reaching statistical significance. The estimated 1-year event risk of shunt dysfunction was 5.2% (95% CI: 2.6-10.2%; I2 = 63%) with DSG and 10.7% (95% CI: 7.8-14.7%; I2 = 39%) with GSG, with no significant subgroup difference (p = 0.080). DSG was associated with lower shunt dysfunction risk, with RR 0.41 (95% CI: 0.26-0.66; p = 0.0002; I2 = 0%), RD - 0.06 (95% CI: - 0.09 to - 0.03; p < 0.0001; I2 = 0%), and sHR 0.32 (95% CI: 0.17-0.59; p < 0.02; I2 = 0%).

CONCLUSION: DSG use in TIPS was associated with significantly lower shunt dysfunction risk compared with GSG, while OHE risk does not differ between stent types.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Grade 3.

articles.title: "Pauli"-tical science: early single-center experience with the technique of the minimally invasive retromuscular parastomal hernia repair.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Parastomal hernias cause significant morbidity and are frequent after stoma creation, with reported incidences reaching up to 50%. With current repair methods, recurrence and mesh-related complications remain high. The Pauli Parastomal Hernia Repair (PPHR), developed as a modification of the Sugarbaker approach, utilizes a posterior component separation technique to lateralize the bowel within the retromuscular space to offset the bowel and minimize mesh-related complications. Small series on outcomes show promise, but data are overall lacking for minimally invasive (MIS) modifications of this approach. We report our series of robotic approaches to PPHR.

METHODS: This study is a retrospective case series of patients undergoing elective robotic PPHR (rPPHR) from 2022 to 2024 at a single-institution tertiary referral center by two fellowship-trained abdominal wall surgeons. Patient and hernia characteristics, operative details, and post-operative outcomes were abstracted from the electronic health records. Hernia recurrence (defined as CT evidence or physical exam findings) and 30-day morbidity, including stoma and mesh-related complications, were reported and analyzed.

RESULTS: During this time period, 26 patients underwent elective robotic PPHR. Twenty patients (77%) had a concomitant midline component, and 13 (50%) had a previous hernia repair with 6 (46%) having previous mesh placement. The average parastomal hernia size was 24 ± 17 cm2. Stoma types varied with 11 (42%) end colostomies, 10 (38%) end ileostomies, and 5 (19%) ileal conduits. There were no intra-operative complications. The 30-day morbidity was 23%, which included one surgical site infection (SSI), one seroma, one ileus, and one mechanical obstruction at the stoma. With a median follow-up of 15.4 months, there was a 1-year recurrence rate of 4% and 2-year recurrence rate of 8%. One repair required reoperation for postoperative pouching difficulty without a recurrence present.

CONCLUSION: The rPPHR technique for parastomal hernia repair is a technically challenging procedure with promising early outcomes and deserves continued study of longer-term outcomes.

articles.title: Timing matters in hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation.
Timing of onset defines distinct prognostic phenotypes in neonatal ards: a multicenter cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Neonatal acute respiratory distress syndrome (NARDS) is a severe form of lung injury that poses a substantial threat to neonatal survival. This study aims to investigate potential variations in in-hospital mortality rates among NARDS cases based on the timing of disease onset.

METHODS: This study utilized data from a multicenter retrospective cohort established by the Jiangsu Neonatal Respiratory Failure Collaborative Network. NARDS cases that received tracheal intubation followed by invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) were divided into the early-onset group (diagnosis within 72 hours after birth, n = 301) and the late-onset group (diagnosis after 72 hours of birth, n = 594) following the NARDS diagnosis.

RESULTS: Late-onset was linked to lower mortality [hazard ratio (HR): 0.69, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.54-0.90]. After interaction adjustment, the HR derived from Cox regression analysis was 0.44 (95%CI: 0.28-0.70) with an E-value of 3.97. Interaction effect analysis identified an increased risk of death in late-onset NARDS complicated by pulmonary infection. Sensitivity analysis further confirmed the robustness of the results.

CONCLUSIONS: This study indicates that infants with late-onset NARDS who require intubation and IMV tend to have a more favorable prognosis, but newborns with concurrent pulmonary infections would have an increased mortality risk.

IMPACT: This is the first study to demonstrate that the timing of onset defines distinct prognostic phenotypes in neonatal acute respiratory distress syndrome (NARDS). We found that late-onset NARDS (developing >72 h after birth) is associated with significantly lower in-hospital mortality compared to early-onset NARDS. Crucially, this survival benefit is substantially attenuated in late-onset cases complicated by pulmonary infection, identifying a new, specific high-risk subgroup requiring heightened clinical vigilance. Our findings establish a simple yet powerful criterion for risk stratification and underscore the clinical heterogeneity within NARDS, paving the way for more tailored management strategies.

articles.title: Evaluating the AI-predictive potential of the PIC database for pediatric ICU mortality.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reliable Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools in healthcare depend on both data quality and model design. However, the predictive integrity of datasets is rarely assessed. Publicly available resources for critically ill children remain scarce. The Pediatric Intensive Care (PIC) database remains, to the best of current knowledge, the only open-access resource focused on pediatric critical care research.

METHODS: This study evaluates the predictive potential of the PIC database. After applying strict cohort selection and data preprocessing, mortality risk was analyzed using statistical analysis through univariate Odds Ratio (OR) to measure associations, and machine learning (ML) models interpreted through SHAP values to assess feature importance and model behavior.

RESULTS: ML experiments showed moderate but limited predictive performance for mortality. CatBoost performed best, with an AUC of 0.8521 (0.8414-0.8627) on the hold-out test set, but low sensitivity (42%) limited its ability to identify non-survivors. These findings suggest dataset-related constraints that reduce clinical reliability. Most relevant variables were minimum lactate, maximum lactate, mean respiratory rate, maximum hematocrit, and minimum urea.

CONCLUSION: Analysis showed that PIC lacks essential physiological data, highlighting the limits of current pediatric databases and the need for richer multicenter datasets to enable more robust, clinically applicable AI models.

IMPACT: Provides the first comprehensive evaluation of the PIC database, assessing its suitability for machine learning-based predictive modeling. Identifies key clinical variables and data gaps that influence the reliability of AI-based mortality prediction and model performance. Underscores the need for richer, multicenter pediatric ICU databases for research that incorporate essential physiological and neurological indicators. Demonstrates the value of combining statistical association and AI interpretability methods to assess the predictive integrity of clinical datasets.

articles.title: Relationship between intra-thoracic pressure, lung volume and high-frequency jet ventilation in lungs predisposed to gas trapping: an animal study.
articles.abstract: High-frequency jet ventilation (HFJV) is used to manage severe respiratory failure in neonates, especially to manage gas trapping. To our knowledge, the role of HFJV rate on lung volume states and intra-tracheal and thoracic pressures has not been described. The aim of our study was to determine the impact of HFJV rate (HFJVrate) on (1) total and regional end-expiratory lung volume (EELV) and (2) intra-thoracic pressure, specifically intra-tracheal pressure (Ptrach) and oesophageal pressure (Poes) in adult New Zealand white rabbits (n = 5) prone to gas trapping. After stabilisation on HFJV (Bunnell LifePulse Ventilator; mean (SD) PEEP and HFJV PIP were 5.6 (1.3) cmH2O and 21 (2.6) cmH2O), HFJVrate between 150 and 900 bpm were randomly applied and regional EELV (electrical impedance tomography), Ptrach and Poes measured with gas exchange parameters. The non-gravity-dependent hemithorax demonstrated greater relative EELV with increasing HFJVrate, suggesting overdistension at higher rates. ΔPtrach increased linearly from HFJVrate 150 to 900 bpm and conversely ΔPoes was more variable, decreased with increasing HFJVrate. There was a U-shaped relationship between HFJVrate and PaCO2 with best CO2 clearance occurring at HFJVrate 320-400 bpm. IMPACT: In an animal model susceptible to gas trapping, high-frequency jet ventilation rate influenced volume state with increased carbon dioxide at low and high rates. This is the first study to define the mechanisms by which expiratory time during high-frequency jet ventilation alone can cause and relieve overdistension and atelectasis. Electrical impedance tomography was able to identify optimal lung volume, which may be useful in titrating the best high-frequency jet ventilation rate between 240 and 400 bpm for carbon dioxide clearance.

articles.title: Long-term follow-up of adolescents with white coat hypertension: a preliminary exploratory study.
articles.abstract: White coat hypertension (WCH) in youth has traditionally been considered benign, but it may precede sustained hypertension (SH) and cardiovascular remodelling. We evaluated long-term blood pressure (BP) outcomes and hypertension-mediated organ damage in adolescents with WCH. This preliminary exploratory cohort study included 34 adolescents with WCH and 24 normotensive controls followed for median periods of 8.5 and 7.7 years. Clinical, biochemical, echocardiographic, vascular, and ambulatory BP monitoring (ABPM) assessments were performed at baseline and follow-up. At follow-up, 13 participants with WCH (38.2%) progressed to SH, 2 (5.9%) maintained WCH, and 19 (55.9%) became normotensive; no control developed SH. Participants who progressed had higher baseline ambulatory systolic BP (SBP; 124 vs 119 mmHg, p = 0.004) and pulse pressure (PP; 55 vs 49 mmHg, p = 0.01), while office BP was similar. At follow-up, office BP, ambulatory SBP (131 vs 118 mmHg, p = 0.001), PP (60 vs 45 mmHg, p = 0.003), central SBP (126 vs 121 mmHg, p = 0.032), and augmentation pressure (7 vs 4 mmHg, p = 0.009) were higher in the SH group. Most biochemical parameters, carotid intima-media thickness, and pulse wave velocity were similar between groups. More than one-third of adolescents with WCH progressed to SH. Higher baseline ambulatory SBP and PP may identify those at greater risk. These preliminary findings support individualized, risk-stratified surveillance, with closer ABPM follow-up for adolescents with higher-normal ambulatory BP, wider PP, excess adiposity, persistent office BP elevation, or other cardiovascular risk factors.

articles.title: Sequencing and analysis of the human adaptive immune receptor repertoire.
articles.abstract: Adaptive immune cell populations (T cells and B cells) retain a molecular record of immune exposures, including infection and vaccination, in their specific antigen receptor repertoires. These receptor repertoires arise through V(D)J recombination, which assembles distinct combinations of germline-encoded V, D and J gene segments and introduces extensive junctional diversification to generate highly diverse antigen receptors that are subsequently shaped by developmental selection and antigen exposure. Recent advances in high-throughput sequencing enable adaptive immune receptor repertoires to be profiled at scale, across large cohorts and with increasing depth within individual samples. As a result, receptor repertoire profiling is emerging as a powerful approach for monitoring disease course and treatment responses in cancer, quantifying immune responses to infection and vaccination, and dissecting the immunological basis of inflammatory disease. In this Review, we discuss how human T cell and B cell receptor repertoires are formed, how inherited genetic variation shapes their architecture and how experimental and computational advances are enabling repertoire data to be translated into biological insight, clinical utility and repertoire-guided therapeutic opportunities.

articles.title: Real-time XR-based 6-DOF catheter tracking enhances cardiac intervention navigation efficiency and depth perception.
articles.abstract: Despite advances in 3D ultrasound, most percutaneous cardiac interventions still rely on 2D visualization, limiting depth perception and spatial understanding. To address this challenge, we developed an Extended Reality (XR)-based platform that enables real-time six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) catheter tracking and visualization within a patient-specific 3D heart model. The system combines a custom machine-vision algorithm for 5-DOF catheter tracking with a 3D-printed electromechanical encoder that measures catheter roll, providing complete 6-DOF motion reconstruction. In a proof-of-concept study, 20 novice medical students navigated an intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) catheter to six anatomical targets using either immersive 3D visualization or a conventional 2D cathlab-style view. Participants in the 3D condition completed the task in 54.6 seconds and traveled 1939 mm on average, compared with 263.5 seconds and 7854 mm in the 2D condition. The ratio of cohort means was 4.8× for completion time and 4.1× for travel length (means of subject-level ratios: 5.1× and 4.9×). The 3D mode also produced more direct and less variable approach trajectories. Participants consistently rated immersive visualization higher for accuracy, speed, usability, and clinical value. Exploratory kinematic analysis suggested that 3D users distributed motion more evenly along the depth axis, whereas 2D users relied more on lateral and vertical adjustments. These findings demonstrate that XR-based visualization can substantially improve procedural training efficiency and motor control.

articles.title: Towards anti-influenza nasal sprays: infection models and opportunities to reduce animal testing.
articles.abstract: The nasal mucosa is an important site of influenza virus entry and early replication, yet approved antivirals are not designed for nasal delivery. This Review summarizes antiviral strategies suitable for nasal administration and evaluates animal and human-relevant models for their development. We discuss route-specific formulation and regulatory requirements and propose a translational framework integrating in vitro, ex vivo and microphysiological systems with targeted in vivo studies to reduce animal use.

articles.title: SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complexes in metabolic disorders: integrating tissue-specific epigenetic mechanisms.
articles.abstract: Metabolic disorders are increasingly linked to epigenetic alterations. SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complexes have emerged as critical modulators of metabolic homeostasis. In this review, we focus on the tissue-specific biological function of SWI/SNF complexes in the pancreas, liver, adipose tissue, and heart, and highlight the dysregulation of chromatin remodeling in metabolic disease progression. Lastly, we discuss therapeutic opportunities targeting chromatin remodeling mechanisms in metabolic disorders.

articles.title: The quiet end of the spectrum: A case report and review of "simple schizophrenia".
articles.journal: Australasian psychiatry : bulletin of Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists
articles.abstract: BackgroundSchizophrenia is increasingly understood as a neurodevelopmental disorder in which cognitive and negative symptoms may precede or overshadow florid psychosis. Such neuropsychiatric presentations can be difficult to recognise within current diagnostic frameworks that privilege positive symptoms.ObjectiveTo illustrate a schizophrenia presentation without hallucinations and delusions and to contextualise it within contemporary and historical nosology.MethodsSingle case report with a focussed narrative review of the literature on simple schizophrenia subtypes.Casea 24-year-old woman experienced a two-year insidious decline in motivation, social engagement, and cognition, with prominent affective flattening, avolition, bradyphrenia, poverty of speech, and psychomotor slowing. There were no delusions or hallucinations, and thought form was linear. Extensive investigations including MRI, EEG, FDG-PET, and CSF studies were unremarkable. Neuropsychological testing showed deficits in new learning, processing speed, and executive functioning consistent with schizophrenia-spectrum illness. The illness was refractory to multiple antidepressants, antipsychotics, and a course of electroconvulsive therapy. Following exclusion of organic pathology, multidisciplinary assessment, and longitudinal review, a diagnosis of schizophrenia was formulated.ConclusionCurrent diagnostic systems may overlook individuals with schizophrenia without hallucinations or delusions. Incorporating neuropsychiatric markers and establishing cognitive trajectories into diagnostic thinking may enable earlier identification and more targeted interventions.

articles.title: Association between prenatal cannabis and tobacco co-exposure and cognition in childhood: Insights from the US adolescent brain cognitive development study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: While evidence on the individual effects of prenatal cannabis and tobacco exposure on offspring cognition is accumulating, their combined impact remains understudied. Therefore, we examined the interaction between prenatal cannabis and tobacco exposure on fluid (e.g. reasoning abilities) and crystallized (e.g. acquired knowledge) cognition in middle childhood. We also compared cognition in children with prenatal co-exposure to those with cannabis-only exposure, tobacco-only exposure and no exposure.

DESIGN: Cross-sectional exploratory analysis of baseline data from an ongoing longitudinal cohort study.

SETTING: Data collected between 2016 and 2018 from the United States-based Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study were extracted.

PARTICIPANTS: Children (n = 8706), aged 9-11 years old, were parsed into four prenatal exposure groups: co-exposure (n = 236); cannabis only (n = 195); tobacco only (n = 803); and no exposure (n = 7472).

MEASUREMENTS: Prenatal co-exposure was measured as a binary variable (yes/no) based on maternal/caregiver retrospective report. Fluid and crystallized scores were derived from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) Toolbox cognitive battery; scores ranged from 44 to 131 and 51115 for fluid and crystallized cognition, respectively. We employed linear mixed-effects models to examine interactions between cannabis and tobacco exposure and group differences in fluid and crystallized scores, adjusting for covariates selected a priori using a Directed Acyclic Graph.

RESULTS: For fluid cognition, a statistically significant interaction emerged between prenatal cannabis and tobacco exposure [beta coefficient (β) = -2.08, 95% confidence interval (CI) = -4.13 to -0.03]. Cannabis only (β = 2.13, 95% CI = 0.21-4.05) and unexposed children (β = 1.39, 95% CI = 0.03-2.76) had statistically significantly higher fluid scores than co-exposed children, while the difference with tobacco-only exposed children was not statistically significant (β = 1.34, 95% CI = -0.14 to 2.82). No statistically significant interaction was observed between prenatal co-exposure and crystallized cognition (β = -0.62, 95% CI = -1.87 to 0.64), and crystallized scores did not statistically significantly differ between the co-exposed group and the cannabis-only (β = 0.66, 95% CI = -0.51 to 1.84), tobacco-only (β = 0.19, 95% CI = -0.71 to 1.1) or unexposed groups (β = 0.24, 95% CI = -0.6 to 1.08).

SUMMARY: Prenatal co-exposure to cannabis and tobacco appears to be associated with poorer fluid cognition among children, but not poorer crystallized cognition, compared with cannabis-only and unexposed groups. These findings should be interpreted with caution given the potential for residual confounding by shared genetic liability, substance exposure misclassification and selection bias. The cross-sectional design of this study precludes causal inference.

articles.title: Measurement of left atrial appendage blood transport in patients with atrial fibrillation using dynamic contrast 4DCT.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current stroke risk stratification in atrial fibrillation (AF) relies on clinical factors with known limitations. Blood stasis in the Left Atrial Appendage (LAA) promotes thrombus formation, contributing to embolic stroke. Our objective is to map contrast transport throughout the LAA volume with 4DCT.

METHODS: Patients being treated for AF underwent dynamic contrast 4DCT. Hounsfield unit (HU) vs. time curves were fitted voxel wise using gamma-variate models. Three LAA blood transport metrics were extracted: (1) increase in residence time between distal LAA voxels and the LA/LAA orifice (ΔRT); (2) ratio of peak HU enhancement in distal LAA voxels to peak HU in the LA/LAA orifice (ΔHU); and (3) total volume of delayed filling (Vstasis) in the LAA. A composite "LAA Transport Index" (LAATI) was computed using principal component analysis.

RESULTS: Among all 93 patients, a wide range of delayed transport in the LAA was observed with: 0 ​< ​ΔRT ​< ​30 ​s, 0.02 ​< ​ΔHU ​< ​1, 0 ​< ​Vstasis ​< ​13 ​mL. Patients imaged during sinus rhythm (n ​= ​26) had rapid filling of the entire LAA with 0 ​< ​ΔRT ​< ​4.7 ​s, 0.65 ​< ​ΔHU ​< ​1, 0 ​< ​Vstasis ​< ​1.0 ​mL. In comparison, patients in AF had values over the entire range ΔRT, ΔHU and Vstasis. For patients imaged in sinus the mean LAATI ​= ​-1.06 ​± ​0.4, and for those imaged in AF the mean LAATI ​= ​0.43 ​± ​1.7. LAATI did not correlate with CHA2DS2-VASc (p ​= ​0.44) or chicken wing morphology (p ​= ​0.21).

CONCLUSIONS: 4DCT-based voxel-wise quantification of LAA contrast transport using gamma-variate modeling is technically feasible. Further studies are required to determine its potential value for personalized stroke-risk assessment.

articles.title: Awareness and clinical management of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease among physicians in Milan: a cross-sectional survey.
articles.journal: Digestive and liver disease : official journal of the Italian Society of Gastroenterology and the Italian Association for the Study of the Liver

articles.title: The impact of HFE genotypes and iron loading on joint disease: evidence for HFE-associated arthropathy without genetic haemochromatosis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to determine the association of recognised HFE genotypes with arthropathy fulfilling European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) haemochromatosis arthropathy (HA) classification criteria (CC), and the contributory role of iron loading.

METHODS: We analysed 373 participants from the EULAR HA inception cohorts: group 1, C282Y homozygous with significant iron overload (n = 154); group 2A, C282Y homozygous without significant iron overload (n = 27); group 2B, other HFE genotypes irrespective of iron status (n = 72); group 3 (osteoarthritis/calcium pyrophosphate arthropathy controls without iron overload (n = 120). Group 2 were selected from rheumatology patients with persistent unexplained joint pain, potential HA, and/or pre-existing genotyping. Between-group comparisons and genotype-stratified analyses were performed. In group 2, associations among ferritin, transferrin saturation, and HA-CC fulfilment were assessed using regression analyses.

RESULTS: HA-CC were fulfilled in 71.4% of group 1, 22.2% group 2A, 43.1% group 2B, and 6.7% group 3 (P < .001 all comparisons). Compared with group 3, group 2 demonstrated significantly higher prevalence of HA-CC fulfilment and 5 HA-CC features (P < .003 all items), including participants with H63D variants. Ferritin levels and transferrin saturation were not associated with HA-CC fulfilment odds ratio (OR) 1.000 per 1 µg/L increase, 95% CI: 1.000-1.001, P = .28; OR 0.98 per 1% increase, 95% CI: 0.96-1.01, P = .14, respectively).

CONCLUSIONS: A substantial proportion of individuals without haemochromatosis but carrying HFE genotypes fulfil EULAR HA-CC, without an association with ferritin levels or transferrin saturation. This supports a potential iron-independent contribution of HFE variants to arthropathy. Although 'haemochromatosis arthropathy' is found in people with genetic haemochromatosis, 'HFE associated arthropathy without genetic haemochromatosis' describes metacarpophalangeal and/or ankle joint disease with any HFE genotype.

articles.title: Influence of the PROFUND index on the effectiveness of SGLT2 inhibitors in elderly pluripathological patients with acute heart failure: PROFUND-IC registry.
authors: all the researchers from the PROFUND-IC registry
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The PROFUND index is a useful tool for estimating one-year mortality in pluripathological patients with heart failure, although its influence on the treatments administered remains unknown. The objectives of the present study were to evaluate whether the PROFUND index influences the effectiveness of sodium-glucose cotransporter type II inhibitors (SGLT2i), and to describe the differential characteristics of pluripathological patients with acute heart failure (AHF) according to this scale.

METHODS: Retrospective study of 880 pluripathological patients with AHF from the PROFUND-IC registry, divided into three groups according to PROFUND index: low (0-2 points), medium (3-6) and high/very high mortality risk (≥7). A descriptive and comparative analysis was performed using the Chi-square test for qualitative variables and ANOVA for quantitative ones, (Fisher and Kruskal-Wallis, when indicated). Propensity Score Matching (PSM) was applied to minimize confounding factors. Kaplan-Meier curves were constructed analysing readmissions and mortality according to SGLT2i administration.

RESULTS: 880 patients were included, 16.3% with low risk; 39.7% with medium risk and 44.1% with high/very high risk. Those with PROFUND index≥7 were predominantly women (61.3%, p=0.006), older, with worse functional class, lower Barthel index, and higher one-year mortality (p<0.001). SGLT2i administration appears to reduce readmissions among patients with PROFUND index between 3 and 6 (25.5% vs. 38.3%, p=0.02). After PSM, this trend persisted (24.1% versus 36.1%), without reaching statistical significance (p=0.065).

CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2i appear beneficial in pluripathological patients with AHF, although the greatest impact is observed in PROFUND 3-6. Further studies are needed to clarify how comorbidity and functionality influence the effectiveness of these drugs.

articles.title: Burden of type 2 diabetes attributable to overweight and obesity in Ecuador: An analysis of temporal trends, 2010-2023.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: High body mass index (BMI) is a major risk factor for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and contributes substantially to mortality and disease burden.

OBJECTIVES: To describe the temporal trends in mortality and disease burden from T2DM attributable to high BMI between 2010 and 2023.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: An ecological study of temporal trends was conducted using GBD 2021 estimates. The number of deaths, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), crude rates, and age-standardised rates were analysed.

RESULTS: Between 2010 and 2023, the total burden of DM2 attributable to overweight and obesity showed a sustained increase in Ecuador's adult population, reflected in both mortality and DALYs. This increase occurred despite an initial improvement in age-standardised rates, indicating a dissociation between the evolution of adjusted risk and the absolute burden of disease. In recent years, changes in the temporal trend have been identified, with stabilisation or a rebound in adjusted rates, particularly in men, while women showed a more favourable trend.

CONCLUSIONS: Between 2010 and 2023, the burden of DM2 attributable to high BMI increased in absolute terms, while standardised rates showed overall declines. Although an initial improvement in age-adjusted rates was observed, recent trend changes were less favourable in men, highlighting significant differences between the sexes. These findings underscore the persistent population impact of T2DM associated with excess weight and the need to consider this in clinical and healthcare approaches.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence Chatbot Accuracy for Patient Education in HPV Infection.
articles.journal: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Chatbots are artificial intelligence (AI) tools that use large language models to answer questions and simulate human-like conversations. Chatbots are commonly used by patients for self-education regarding medical issues. The accuracy of information obtained through patient self-education searches using Chatbots for Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection and recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP) is unknown. This work is intended to analyze aspects of chatbot answers to common patient questions regarding laryngeal HPV infection and RRP.

METHODS: Eight questions were asked by the authors to mimic real-world patient queries to three different Chatbot models (Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini). Two fellowship-trained laryngologists blindly rated eight answers for each model using a 5-point Likert scale regarding accuracy, comprehensiveness, and similarity to a response the rating physician would themselves offer. Descriptive and statistical analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Gemini had the highest overall mean score (4.7, SD 0.5), and Claude had the lowest (4, SD 0.7). Gemini had the highest individual scores for each aspect evaluated. Between the aspects analyzed across all platforms, accuracy was scored highest (4.4, SD 0.6), but the difference was not robust. The one-way ANOVA test showed an overall significant difference between the three platforms (P < 0.0001). A paired comparison between platforms was performed using a post hoc Tukey test, and the results were only significant when Gemini was compared individually with ChatGPT and Claude (P < 0.0001).

CONCLUSION: Gemini had the highest overall and individual rated scores for answer accuracy, comprehensiveness, and similarity to what physician raters would offer their patients. It was the only chatbot platform that demonstrated a robust difference when compared to the others regarding answers to common patient questions on laryngeal HPV infection/RRP.

articles.title: A positive maternal anti-red blood cell antibody test: A critical alert for neonatal bilirubin neurotoxicity.
articles.abstract: A positive maternal anti-red blood cell (RBC) antibody test is a critical indicator of postnatal isoimmune hemolytic disease and risk of neonatal bilirubin neurotoxicity. Though rare, it remains consequential. Rh negativity and a positive anti-RBC test reveal a high-risk pregnancy that can lead to hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN), requiring supervised skilled perinatal and neonatal expertise. Thus, public health systems have mandated policies to minimize severe postnatal adverse outcomes such as symptomatic postnatal anemia and hemolytic hyperbilirubinemia -a neurotoxic risk factor. Review of interviews with families of alloimmunized mothers have revealed concerns of inconsistent prenatal education of potential postnatal sequelae. Many felt inadequate to cope with a premature infant and needs for intensive care, repeated blood testing, prolonged phototherapy, breastfeeding disruption, and blood transfusions or possible exchange transfusions. Therefore, expert and skilled counseling throughout the pregnancy and at birthing are especially needed with interpreting test results. Specific "hand-off" at birthing of the pivotal test result of anti-RBC antibody is essential. Partnering of both perinatal-neonatal teams with families should increase parental education so that they can monitor their own baby's well-being to ensure a healthy childhood and school age outcomes.

articles.title: [Continuous glucose monitoring in diabetes: Clinical practice guidelines for primary care from SEMERGEN, RedGDPS, semFYC, SEMG and FAECAP].
articles.abstract: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) is a key tool for diabetes management in primary care (PC), as it provides dynamic and detailed information on glycemic control. This document summarizes scientific evidence and formulates clinical practice recommendations to optimize the use of CGM in people with diabetes (PwD) managed in PC. The recommendations are based on a Delphi involving 58 PC professionals representing SEMERGEN, redGDPS, semFYC, SEMG and FAECAP; and address the management of GCM within a framework of shared decision-making with PwD, including its indication, prescription, initiation, monitoring, and discontinuation. The integration of CGM into clinical practice in PC, along with adequate training for healthcare professionals and structured PwD education, can improve clinical, PwD-centered outcomes and the efficiency of the healthcare system.

articles.title: Persistent hypogammaglobulinaemia after rituximab in children with difficult-to-treat nephrotic syndrome: a multicentre cross-sectional observational study.
Prevalence of metabolic syndrome and classification performance of triglyceride-glucose-derived indices in people living with HIV in Spain.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Estimate the prevalence and predominant phenotypic patterns of metabolic syndrome (MetS) in people living with HIV receiving contemporary antiretroviral therapy (ART) in southeastern Spain, identify independently associated factors and evaluate the classification performance and clinical utility of triglyceride-glucose (TyG)-derived indices relative to a multivariable logistic regression (MLR) model.

METHODS: Cross-sectional study of 287 people living with HIV on stable ART for ≥6 months. MetS was defined by National Cholesterol Education Program Adult Treatment Panel III (NCEP-ATP III) criteria. MLR identified factors independently associated with MetS. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC), DeLong pairwise comparisons and decision curve analysis (DCA) compared the TyG, TyG-waist circumference (TyG-WC) and TyG-waist-to-height ratio (TyG-WHtR) against the MLR model.

RESULTS: MetS prevalence was 30.3% (95% CI 25.1%-36.0%), with hyperglycaemia, hypertension and increased waist circumference (G-B-W) as the predominant three-component cluster (16.1%, adjusted residual 3.67). Independently associated factors were body mass index (BMI) (aOR 1.44; 95% CI 1.28-1.64; p < 0.001), age >50 years (aOR 5.02; 95% CI 1.94-13.03; p = 0.001) and lower CD4 nadir (aOR 0.997; 95% CI 0.995-1.000; p = 0.032); neither ART regimen nor prior protease inhibitor (PI) exposure was associated. AUCs were 0.876 for MLR, 0.864 for TyG, 0.901 for TyG-WC and 0.912 for TyG-WHtR (all p < 0.001) without significant pairwise differences. DCA showed net benefit for TyG-WHtR comparable to the MLR model.

CONCLUSIONS: MetS affects nearly one-third of people living with HIV on contemporary ART in southeastern Spain, driven primarily by BMI, advanced age and lower nadir CD4, with a predominant G-B-W phenotype. TyG-WHtR offers classification performance comparable to a full multivariable model using routine parameters, supporting its use as a low-burden MetS screening tool in HIV care.

articles.title: Genetics of Parkinson's disease and parkinsonism: a practical guide to assessment and testing.
Neurological and functional recovery despite persistent skull defect after decompressive hemicraniectomy: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Decompressive hemicraniectomy is a life-saving procedure for malignant cerebral infarction with severe edema. Although cranioplasty is performed to enhance neurological recovery, longitudinal descriptions of recovery with a persistent skull defect remain scarce. In such patients, syndrome of the trephined (SoT) may impact neurological function during upright activity. We present a patient who showed neurological and functional improvement beyond 6 months after stroke onset despite a persistent skull defect following bone flap removal due to infection.

OBJECTIVE: To describe longitudinal neurological and functional progression beyond 6 months after stroke onset in a patient with a persistent skull defect after decompressive hemicraniectomy.

CASE DESCRIPTION: A 60-year-old man with right internal carotid artery occlusion underwent decompressive hemicraniectomy with extensive internal decompression. Cranioplasty performed on hospital day 40 was complicated by infection, necessitating removal of the bone flap.

INTERVENTION: Intensive inpatient rehabilitation included postural control training, transfer practice, activities of daily living training, and cognitive-perceptual interventions, with monitoring.

OUTCOMES: Beyond 6 months after stroke onset, consciousness, cognition, and mobility improved. No reproducible posture-dependent neurological worsening suggestive of clinically manifest SoT was observed during upright activity. From admission to the inpatient rehabilitation unit to discharge, the Glasgow Coma Scale score improved from 12 to 14, the Hasegawa's Dementia Scale-Revised score from 13 to 23, the Behavioral Inattention Test score from 20 to 72, and the Scale for Contraversive Pushing score from 2.5 in sitting and 3 in standing to 0.25 in both positions. At discharge, wheelchair transfers and toileting required minimal assistance.

CONCLUSION: Neurological and functional improvements were observed beyond 6 months after stroke onset, despite extensive cortical resection and a persistent skull defect. Although the contributions of biological recovery and rehabilitation could not be distinguished, this case illustrates adaptation of rehabilitation goals and priorities in response to evolving clinical and functional barriers.

articles.title: Infection and abduction loss predict equine laryngoplasty failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prosthetic laryngoplasty (PL) is the most common surgical treatment for recurrent laryngeal neuropathy (RLN) in horses. Post-operative complications may compromise outcomes, and the influence of breed and anaesthetic approach remains unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate factors associated with surgical outcome at 3 months following PL, focusing on post-operative complications, anaesthetic modality and breed (particularly Iberian baroque breeds).

STUDY DESIGN: Multicentre retrospective cohort study.

METHODS: Medical records from 181 horses across 7 equine hospitals using the same standardised surgical technique were reviewed. Variables including breed, anaesthesia type, ventriculocordectomy (VeC) method and post-operative complications were analysed using χ2 or Fisher's exact tests and Spearman correlation. Two binomial generalised linear mixed models, with surgeon as a random effect, evaluated pre/intra-operative predictors and post-operative prognostic factors. Level of significance p < 0.05. Surgical success was defined as the absence of respiratory noise and exercise intolerance at 3 months.

RESULTS: Surgical success was achieved in 79.1% of cases. Complications occurred in 33.7% of horses and were negatively associated with treatment success (odds ratio [OR] 0.003; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.000-0.052; p < 0.001). Major loss of arytenoid abduction (18.2%) and surgical site infection (SSI; 6.6%) were the only variables independently associated with reduced odds of treatment success in the post-operative model (OR 0.011; 95% CI 0.001-0.178; p = 0.001 and OR 0.046; 95% CI 0.004-0.559; p = 0.016, respectively). Breed was not associated with surgical outcome.

MAIN LIMITATIONS: The retrospective multicentre design may introduce selection bias, variability in clinical practice and heterogeneous follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: Major loss of arytenoid abduction and SSI were the strongest predictors of failure, highlighting the importance of meticulous technique, preservation of arytenoid abduction and rigorous infection control to optimise outcomes after PL.

articles.title: Complementary Yield of Gene Panel Testing and ACMG SF v3.3 Screening for Cardiovascular Disease in a Korean Cohort.
articles.abstract: Inherited arrhythmia syndromes and cardiomyopathies are genetically heterogeneous, and clinical exome sequencing (CES) for unrelated indications increasingly yields cardiovascular secondary findings (SFs) under the ACMG SF v3.3 list. We compared, at a single Korean centre, phenotype-directed cardiac gene panel testing with opportunistically ascertained cardiovascular SFs. Forty patients with suspected inherited arrhythmia or cardiomyopathy underwent a 19-gene arrhythmia or 173-gene cardiomyopathy panel with AI-assisted, manually reviewed variant classification; separately, 288 patients undergoing CES for unrelated indications were screened for ACMG SF v3.3 cardiovascular pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants. A phenotype-concordant pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant was found in 8/40 patients (20.0%), including a recurrent KCNQ1 p.Arg231His variant in two unrelated infants and a MYBPC3 variant upgraded to pathogenic by co-segregation in a mother-son pair. Among the 288 exome-sequenced patients, 17 reportable cardiovascular SFs occurred in 16 (5.6%), predominantly dilated cardiomyopathy (n = 7, mostly TTN) and familial hypercholesterolaemia (n = 6, including a recurrent PCSK9 p.Glu32Lys variant in three patients). The two approaches sampled largely non-overlapping gene categories and are complementary rather than competing; recurrent, population-specific variants underscore the need for population-informed interpretation and structured counselling in cardiovascular genetic diagnosis.

articles.title: Clinical and Genetic Characterization of a Patient With EED-Related Overgrowth Syndrome.
articles.abstract: Cohen-Gibson syndrome (COGIS) is a rare genetic disorder caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in EED. As the COGIS phenotypic spectrum remains incompletely characterized, additional cases help refine understanding of the condition. We evaluated a 37-year-old man with EED-related COGIS features, including overgrowth and intellectual disability. Genetic workup included karyotyping, FMR1 CGG-repeat expansion testing, whole-exome sequencing, and a familial segregation analysis, which identified the previously reported heterozygous pathogenic variant NM_003797.5:c.772C>T:p.His258Tyr. Clinical findings and medical history were recorded; birth parameters were obtained retrospectively from parental report due to lack of official documentation. Echocardiography revealed mild mitral valve regurgitation, alongside features uncommon in previously reported patients-normal adult weight, a long face, normal head circumference, normally spaced eyes, camptodactyly, no history of cryptorchidism, and a normal gait. Notably, the patient's father carried the same variant with reduced Sanger peak height, suggesting possible mosaicism. This case highlights potential phenotypic variability in COGIS, including the cardiac finding warranting further study, and underscores the implications of suspected paternal mosaicism for genetic counseling. Further quantitative assessment of mosaicism and cardiac evaluation in future studies could help better define the clinical spectrum of COGIS.

articles.title: Validation of the SPiRO Score for the Prediction of ICU Admission in Patients Presenting With Leptospirosis in Tropical Australia.
articles.journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: In some resource-limited settings the case-fatality rate of severe leptospirosis can exceed 50%. Early recognition of severe disease can expedite transfer to referral centres for advanced supportive care. The entirely clinical, 3-point SPiRO score can be calculated rapidly at presentation to predict a patient's subsequent clinical course. In its derivation study, a SPiRO score of 0 had a negative predictive value (NPV) for intensive care unit (ICU) admission of 98% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 96-99). In this validation cohort we sought to confirm the SPiRO score's prognostic utility and to compare its performance to other leptospirosis-specific and general disease severity scores.

METHODS: We examined consecutive adults presenting to four high-caseload hospitals in tropical Australia with laboratory-confirmed leptospirosis between June 2016 and April 2026. The SPiRO score's ability to predict ICU admission before hospital discharge was compared with that of the leptospirosis-specific QuickLepto score and commonly used disease severity scores, namely the SOFA, qSOFA, qSOFA-lactate, NEWS-2, qNEWS, UVA and the SIRS scores.

RESULTS: There were no deaths in 309 episodes of leptospirosis, but in 62 (20%) there was an ICU admission. The SPiRO score performed as well as, or better than, all the other scores in predicting ICU admission. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for the SPiRO score was 0.83 (95% CI: 0.77-0.89); only the SOFA score had a higher value: 0.84 (0.79-0.90), although the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.08). The SPiRO score had the highest NPV for ICU admission of any of the scores: 95 (95% CI: 91-97)%.

CONCLUSIONS: The SPiRO score can be calculated easily at the bedside at presentation to expedite the recognition of patients with leptospirosis who are most likely to deteriorate. In resource-limited settings this entirely clinical score can also help reduce unnecessary escalation of care, optimising the use of finite health resources.

articles.title: Unilateral Biportal Endoscopic Trans-Kambin Lumbar Interbody Fusion at the L5/S1 Level: A Consecutive Case Series With 1-Year Clinical and Radiological Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trans-Kambin lumbar interbody fusion at L5/S1 is technically demanding because of reduced disc height, a narrow safety triangle, anatomical variability of the exiting nerve root (ENR), foraminal pathology, and interference from the iliac crest. This study evaluated the feasibility and 1-year clinical and radiological outcomes of unilateral biportal endoscopic (UBE) trans-Kambin lumbar interbody fusion at L5/S1 in a consecutive case series.

METHODS: This retrospective consecutive case series included 25 patients who underwent single-level UBE trans-Kambin lumbar interbody fusion at L5/S1 between January 2023 and December 2024. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Oswestry Disability Index and numerical rating scale scores for low back pain and leg pain. Radiological outcomes included segmental lordotic angle, slip distance, and preliminary computed tomography (CT)-based fusion assessment at 12 months. The operative strategy emphasized continuous endoscopic visualization of the ENR during corridor creation, foraminoplasty, disc space preparation, and cage insertion.

RESULTS: Diagnoses included isthmic spondylolisthesis in 11 patients and foraminal stenosis in 9 patients. The mean preoperative disc height at the safety triangle was 2.6 ± 1.3 mm. At 12 months, segmental lordotic angle increased from 12.4° ± 6.6° to 14.6° ± 5.8° (P = 0.0046), and slip distance decreased from 5.5 ± 2.8 mm to 3.1 ± 2.9 mm (P = 0.001). Oswestry Disability Index improved from 32.5 ± 11.2 to 15.7 ± 12.8 (P < 0.0001). Numerical rating scale scores improved from 5.8 ± 1.6 to 2.8 ± 2.3 for low back pain (P < 0.0001) and from 3.8 ± 2.7 to 2.0 ± 2.2 for leg pain (P = 0.0014). The preliminary CT-based fusion rate at 12 months was 88.0%. No ENR injury, infection, or reoperation occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: A structured, level-specific strategy for UBE trans-Kambin lumbar interbody fusion was feasible at L5/S1 and was associated with significant clinical improvement, modest radiological correction, and an 88.0% preliminary CT-based fusion rate at 12 months. Further studies with larger cohorts and longer follow-up are needed to validate these findings.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This study provides a level-specific framework for performing UBE trans-Kambin lumbar interbody fusion at L5/S1, a level with substantial anatomical and technical constraints.

articles.title: Effect of omeprazole on platelet reactivity in patients with diabetes mellitus and coronary artery disease receiving aspirin and clopidogrel: a randomised, placebo-controlled crossover trial (POC-DM).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Proton pump inhibitors are often prescribed with aspirin and clopidogrel to reduce gastrointestinal bleeding risk. However, the European Society of Cardiology diabetes guidelines recommend avoiding concomitant use of omeprazole and clopidogrel due to potential drug–drug interactions. Evidence in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM), who have a higher prevalence of high on-treatment platelet reactivity, remains limited. In Thailand, where omeprazole is the only reimbursed PPI, this potential interaction has important clinical implications. We aimed to evaluate the effect of omeprazole on platelet reactivity, measured as P2Y12 reaction units (PRU), in patients with DM and coronary artery disease (CAD) receiving aspirin and clopidogrel.

METHODS: This double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled crossover trial enrolled patients with DM and CAD receiving aspirin 81 mg/day and clopidogrel 75 mg/day. Participants received omeprazole 20 mg or a matching placebo for 2 weeks, followed by crossover to the alternate treatment. Platelet reactivity was assessed using the VerifyNow P2Y12 assay. The primary outcome was the change in PRU following omeprazole coadministration compared with both baseline and placebo. Secondary outcomes included changes in clopidogrel responder status (PRU >208) before and after omeprazole treatment and PRU values in each treatment period.

RESULTS: 50 patients were enrolled (median age 67 years; 58% male). Omeprazole significantly increased PRU by a mean difference of 20.57 units versus baseline (p=0.002) and 16.14 units versus placebo (p=0.006). The proportion of clopidogrel non-responders increased from 44% to 56%, with 25% of baseline responders converting to non-responders.

CONCLUSIONS: Omeprazole significantly attenuated clopidogrel’s antiplatelet effect in patients with diabetes and CAD. Concomitant use may be avoided, especially in those with high thrombotic risk.

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: TCTR20260714003.

articles.title: Atrial remodelling defines the heart failure phenotype in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
Association of epicardial adipose tissue with circulating biomarkers in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: insights from the RACE V study.

Integrating palliative care into respiratory care for people with advanced COPD: study protocol for the international EU PAL-COPD stepped wedge cluster randomised controlled trial of the ICLEAR-EU intervention.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Individuals with advanced chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) often experience significant symptom burden, unmet care needs and frequent hospitalisations, yet remain underserved by palliative care. Evidence suggests palliative care can improve quality of life and reduce avoidable hospital readmissions but robust multi-country randomised evaluations are lacking.
