Building on a successful pilot subsequently adapted, this protocol presents the EU PAL-COPD study evaluating the ICLEAR-EU intervention to reduce potentially avoidable respiratory-related readmission within 90 days and improve quality of life for individuals with advanced COPD and their families across European health systems.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: A stepped-wedge cluster randomised controlled trial evaluating the effectiveness of the ICLEAR-EU intervention in Belgium, the UK, the Netherlands, Hungary, Denmark and Portugal, comparing ICLEAR-EU to usual care. ICLEAR-EU is an integrated non-pharmacological service intervention for hospitalised patients with advanced COPD to identify and address palliative care needs. Hospitals (clusters) cross over from usual care to intervention in four 6-month wedges after a 30-day transition/training period. Eligible participants are community-dwelling adults with advanced COPD admitted ≥48 hours for an acute exacerbation; each may nominate a family caregiver. We aim to enrol 1224 patients across 18 hospitals (three per country). The primary endpoint is the percentage of patients with respiratory-related hospital readmissions within 90 days of baseline (or until death if within 90 days). Secondary endpoints include patient and family caregiver quality of life, well-being, healthcare utilisation and cost-effectiveness at 30- and 90-day follow-up. Process evaluation will be conducted throughout. Analyses follow intention-to-treat using mixed-effects models accounting for clustering, time and country. The statistical analysis plan is provided as supplementary material.

ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Ethics approval was obtained in all participating countries and hospitals. Findings on effectiveness, cost-effectiveness and process evaluation will be disseminated via academic channels and established project communication channels.

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ISRCTN45800298.

articles.title: High-flow nasal oxygen versus non-invasive ventilation in patients with acute hypercapnic exacerbation of COPD: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease complicated by acute hypercapnia require respiratory support. Respiratory acidosis requires support that is often provided with high-flow nasal oxygen (HFNO) or non-invasive ventilation (NIV). Our aim is to compare the efficacy and safety of the two modalities.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials including patients with acute hypercapnia and respiratory acidosis following PRISMA guidelines. Searches were performed on PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science. The primary outcome was intubation/invasive mechanical ventilation. Secondary outcomes included mortality types, crossover to the other support modality, length of stay, physiological parameters and adverse events. Pooled estimates from random effects models (inverse-variance weights and DerSimonian-Laird estimator) were expressed as risk ratios (RR) or mean differences (MD) with 95% CI.

RESULTS: Ten trials were included. The risk of intubation was similar between HFNO and NIV (RR 1.25, 95% CI 0.83 to 1.90). Crossover from HFNO to NIV was more frequent (RR 2.18, 95% CI 1.07 to 4.41). Mortality outcomes (28–30 day mortality: RR 1.11, 95% CI 0.66 to 1.89, hospital: RR 0.49, 95% CI 0.16 to 1.49) did not differ. Low-certainty evidence suggested a shorter length of stay with HFNO (MD –0.79 days, 95% CI –1.41 to –0.18).

CONCLUSIONS: No statistically significant differences were found between HFNO and NIV for intubation and mortality for patients with acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and respiratory acidosis. Provided crossover to the other therapy was allowed, more patients crossed over from HFNO to NIV. HFNO was associated with shorter LOS.

Rehabilitation programme for post-stroke lateropulsion including exoskeleton-assisted training: rationale and single-case experimental design protocol.
Short-term efficacy and safety of bailout angioplasty or stenting after thrombectomy: a multicentre real-world study.
Preventing vision loss in advanced primary care through asynchronous teleophthalmology: early detection of asymptomatic sight-threatening retinal vasculitis in a young adult.
Unexpected cerebrovascular catastrophe in Guillain-Barré syndrome.

Impact of CKD and Hemodialysis on Treatment of Severely Calcified Lesions: The ECLIPSE Trial.
articles.abstract: Background: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) and coronary calcification increase risk for adverse events following drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation. We evaluated whether outcomes following vessel preparation with orbital atherectomy (OA) versus balloon angioplasty (BA) vary according to CKD. Methods: This pre-specified CKD sub-analysis of the prospective, multicenter ECLIPSE trial evaluated 2,001 patients with severely calcified lesions randomized to OA versus BA prior to DES. Independent predictors of two-year target-vessel failure (TVF)-a composite of cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction (TV-MI), or ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization (ID-TVR)-were determined using multivariable Cox proportional hazards modeling. Results: CKD (eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73m² or hemodialysis) was present in 694 (34.7%) patients; 112 required hemodialysis. Two-year TVF was significantly higher with versus without CKD (21.2% vs. 11.6%; p<0.001), driven by increased cardiac death and ID-TVR. Hemodialysis independently predicted TVF (adjusted HR 2.14, 95% CI 1.30-3.53; p=0.003), whereas reduced eGFR alone did not (p=0.070). In patients on hemodialysis, OA versus BA was associated with higher rates of TVF (52.3% vs. 30.7%; adjusted HR 2.50, 95% CI 1.16-5.41; P=0.020), driven by higher rates of TV-MI and ID-TVR, whereas TVF was similar after OA versus BA in patients not on hemodialysis (13.5% vs. 13.1%; adjusted HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.81-1.35; P=0.730); however, the interaction between treatment assignment and hemodialysis status was not significant (Pint=0.244). Conclusions: CKD remains a major predictor of adverse outcomes after DES implantation in severely calcified lesions, with the highest risks in patients on hemodialysis. In the ECLIPSE trial, higher two-year rates of TVF were observed after vessel preparation with OA compared with BA in patients on hemodialysis but not in patients with CKD not on hemodialysis or in those without CKD. Given the modest hemodialysis subgroup size and non-significant interaction testing, confirmation of these findings in additional studies is warranted.

articles.title: High Diagnostic Yield of Testing With a Diabetes Device Screening Series in Patients With Suspected Allergic Reactions to Glucose Sensors, Insulin Patch Pumps and Insulin Infusion Sets.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patch testing in patients with dermatitis from diabetes devices is challenging because device composition is nearly always undisclosed, relevant allergens are incompletely known, and many suspected allergens are not commercially available.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the diagnostic yield of a dedicated diabetes device screening series, supplemented with a (meth)acrylate series and testing of patients' own device adhesives and adhesive extracts, in patients with suspected allergic contact dermatitis to glucose sensors, insulin patch pumps, or infusion sets.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We performed a retrospective patch test study of 100 patients referred to a tertiary referral centre for suspected allergic reactions to diabetes devices.

RESULTS: Seventy-one patients reacted to one or more allergens in the diabetes device screening series; in 50 (70.4%), at least one reaction was clinically relevant. The most frequent relevant allergens were colophonium and its related substances abietic acid and hydroabietyl alcohol, isobornyl acrylate, dicyclohexylmethane-4,4'-diisocyanate, and N,N-dimethylacrylamide. The (meth)acrylate series had no clear additional diagnostic value. Testing with patients' own device adhesives and extracts frequently identified allergic reactions to devices not recognised by the results of the screening series alone.

CONCLUSION: The combined approach identified relevant contact allergies in most patients with suspected allergic contact dermatitis to diabetes devices.

articles.title: Characteristics, Implementation and Effects of Nurse-Driven Sepsis Protocols in Hospital Settings: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To synthesize evidence on the characteristics, implementation and effects of nurse-driven sepsis protocols on process-of-care indicators and clinical outcomes.

DESIGN: Systematic review without meta-analysis.

METHODS: Studies were included if they described and evaluated nurse-driven sepsis protocols in hospitals. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts and full texts for eligibility. The Johns Hopkins Nursing Evidence-Based Practice model was used to appraise included studies. Data were extracted and narratively synthesized.

DATA SOURCES: Eight databases were searched from database inception to 30 June 2025.

RESULTS: Fifteen studies were included, most using before-and-after designs and conducted in the emergency departments (n = 7) and hospital-wide settings (n = 4). Protocols commonly used systemic inflammatory response syndrome criteria for screening (n = 12) and incorporated key Surviving Sepsis Campaign recommendations (n = 14). Most studies reported improved or comparable outcomes to baseline in overall sepsis bundle compliance and key process-of-care indicators, including timely antibiotic administration, blood culture collection, lactate measurement and fluid administration. All 11 studies evaluating mortality reported reductions, although only four were statistically significant. Findings for hospital length of stay were inconsistent. Common implementation strategies included nurse education and training, coupled with audit and feedback.

CONCLUSIONS: Nurse-driven sepsis protocols may improve adherence to and timeliness of key sepsis care processes. Effects on clinical outcomes are less certain, given the predominance of before-and-after designs and inconsistent findings for hospital length of stay. The review identifies implementation strategies that can guide future sepsis quality improvement initiatives.

IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: Nurse-driven protocols may support nurses in initiating timely sepsis care and strengthening adherence to recommended care processes. Further high-quality studies are needed to establish effects on clinical outcomes and broader impacts, including healthcare costs, intensive care resource utilization, patient and nurse satisfaction, and safety outcomes.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patient or public contribution.

articles.title: Dynamic Fractional Myocardial Blood Volume Mapping Using Ferumoxytol-enhanced CMR Multitasking with Subspace Dose Harmonization.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fractional myocardial blood volume (fMBV) represents the vascular compartment within myocardial tissue and may reflect changes in microvascular status and health. Conventionally derived from multi-dose Modified Look-Locker Inversion (MOLLI) recovery T1 mapping with ferumoxytol, MOLLI-based fMBV requires repeated breath-holds, inter-dose image registration, and static end-diastolic estimates. CMR Multitasking enables free-breathing, non-electrocardiogram (ECG)-gated imaging and offers a subspace that captures shared motion and contrast dynamics. This subspace representation can be exploited to harmonize multi-dose acquisitions directly in parameter space, enabling motion-resolved dynamic fMBV mapping while reducing reliance on post-hoc image-space registration.

METHODS: Thirteen healthy volunteers (11 females, 28.2±10.0 years) and twelve ischemic heart disease (IHD) patients (1 female, 67.2±7.1 years) underwent multi-dose ferumoxytol imaging at 3.0T using both breath-held ECG-triggered 5(3)3(3)3 MOLLI and free-running 2-dimensional Multitasking T1 mapping sequences. MOLLI-Multitasking agreement was assessed in healthy volunteers; patient data were used for exploratory dynamic fMBV analysis. Multitasking data were harmonized across respiratory- and cardiac-motion subspace dimensions for cross-dose alignment. Pixel-wise fMBV was estimated using a two-compartment water exchange model. fMBV agreement with MOLLI was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis. Dynamic fMBV changes were also evaluated from the Multitasking data. In IHD patients, fMBV kinetic metrics (upslope and diastolic-to-systolic distribution) for cycle-dependent variation in dynamic fMBV were computed to assess systolic compression and diastolic recoil. Cardiac positron emission tomography (PET) derived perfusion and CMR-derived strain and late gadolinium enhancement served as references.

RESULTS: In healthy volunteers, Multitasking produced motion-resolved fMBV maps with strong MOLLI agreement (bias -0.11%, p=0.84). Subspace harmonization reduced cross-dose variability and aligned cardiac phases. Healthy subjects showed significant diastolic-to-systolic variation (10.55±2.12% vs. 7.73±2.76%, p=0.0004). In IHD patients, ischemic segments exhibited elevated diastolic fMBV with significant systolic compression (16.36±3.44% vs. 10.01±2.24%, p=0.013), remote myocardium showed similar phasic variation (11.16±0.68% vs. 7.98±0.57%, p<0.0001). At the same time, scar demonstrated reduced fMBV with attenuated modulation (7.74±1.95% vs. 5.59±1.97%, p=0.099). Abnormal dynamic fMBV regions corresponded to PET defects and impaired circumferential strain.

CONCLUSION: Ferumoxytol-enhanced Multitasking with subspace harmonization enables free-breathing, cardiac-resolved dynamic fMBV mapping, overcoming practical limitations of MOLLI-derived fMBV. This approach enables non-invasive assessment of dynamic myocardial blood volume across the cardiac cycle, with potential utility for characterizing microvascular function in ischemic heart disease.

articles.title: The weight of memory: nutrition, diabetes, and the brain.
articles.abstract: This issue of the Biomedical Journal explores therapeutic approaches to neuroinflammation, antimicrobial resistance, and cancer, as well as developments in laboratory testing and prognostic assessment. Experimental findings show that glibenclamide attenuates palmitic acid-induced hippocampal inflammation and memory impairment in mice. In antimicrobial research, CRISPR-Cas9-mediated elimination of resistance genes restores ertapenem susceptibility in resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, while deep learning offers an approach to interpreting antimicrobial susceptibility tests from images. Oncology articles span molecular characterization, treatment, and prognosis: BK polyomavirus integration and aristolochic acid exposure are associated with distinct molecular features in kidney transplant-associated urothelial carcinomas; bavachinin enhances cisplatin's antitumor activity in oral cancer models; biomarker changes inform prognosis during radium-223 therapy; and external validation supports the MAGIC-D model in advanced biliary tract cancer. Furthermore, research on cartilage homeostasis examines exercise-dependent responses of Prg4-expressing cells. Correspondence addresses combined radiotherapy and systemic treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma and, in a second exchange, stewardship of short-term systemic corticosteroid use.

articles.title: Cachexia Defined by the Asian Working Group for Cachexia 2023 Criteria and Gut Microbiota Diversity in Post-Stroke Patients Capable of Oral Intake.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Cachexia defined by the Asian Working Group for Cachexia (AWGC) 2023 criteria is associated with adverse outcomes in older adults, but its relationship with gut microbiota diversity remains unclear. This study aimed to examine the association between cachexia and gut microbiota diversity in stroke patients.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study examined post-acute stroke patients capable of oral intake. Cachexia was assessed at admission using the AWGC 2023 criteria. Gut microbiota diversity was evaluated using the Shannon index, amplicon sequence variant (ASV) richness, and Faith's phylogenetic diversity (PD) based on 16S rRNA gene sequencing of fecal samples. Multiple linear regression analyses were performed after adjustment for potential confounders.

RESULTS: A total of 130 patients were included; the mean (SD) age was 78.4 (7.1) years, and 58% were men. Cachexia was diagnosed in 15% (19/130) of patients. After adjustment, cachexia was independently and negatively associated with the Shannon index (β = -0.282, p = 0.002), ASV richness (β = -0.279, p = 0.001), and Faith's PD (β = -0.264, p = 0.006). Among the AWGC 2023 components, underlying disease, low body mass index, decreased handgrip strength, and elevated C-reactive protein were independently associated with lower gut microbiota diversity.

CONCLUSIONS: In this cross-sectional study, cachexia was independently associated with lower gut microbiota diversity in post-acute stroke patients. These findings are associative rather than causal and should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Delayed Recognition of Abusive Head Trauma: A Diagnostic Error.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Missed cases of abusive head trauma have been described in the medical literature. A 1999 study found that abusive head trauma was more likely to be missed in young white children from two parent households. Diagnostic errors in the evaluation of abusive head trauma may have changed since that time. We aimed to identify rates of diagnostic error in the diagnosis of abusive head trauma at our institution and to evaluate characteristics associated with missed or delayed diagnoses of abusive head trauma.

METHODS: We performed a case-control study of children 2 years and younger with an intracranial injury suspicious for abusive head trauma between January 2015 and May 2023. Demographics, social factors, clinical presentation, and the presence of high-risk bruising were also collected. Descriptive statistics, odds ratios, chi-squared tests, and Fisher's exact tests were used for statistical analysis.

RESULTS: One hundred eighteen children with abusive head trauma were identified. Our control group included 107 (90.7%) patients in which no diagnostic error was identified. Eleven (9.3%) had missed diagnosis or delayed diagnosis identified and 4 (3.4%) had possible missed diagnosis identified. High-risk bruising was identified in 4/11 (36.4%) cases of missed diagnosis/delayed diagnosis.

CONCLUSION: Abusive head trauma diagnosis continues to be missed or delayed in nearly 10% of cases. With greater than 30% of missed or delayed diagnoses having high-risk bruising on exam, increased attention to bruising may help decrease diagnostic error and help increase identification of abusive head trauma.

articles.title: Adverse Childhood Experiences screening in pediatric primary care and concurrent health.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs) are linked with a number of chronic health conditions. However, there are no large-scale data examining whether ACEs screening is also associated with these higher rates. The current study examined the rates of chronic health conditions for children with and without ACEs screening, and those with and without positive screens.

METHODS: Data from a large integrated healthcare system captured 684,887 youth age 2-18 years old eligible for ACEs screening between June 2023 and August 2025. Chronic physical and mental health conditions from the electronic health records at the same visit as the ACEs screening included: abdominal pain, ADHD, anxiety, asthma, depression, headache, hypertension, and obesity. Logistic regression estimated the odds of each health condition for: 1) screened versus not screened, 2) positive versus negative screen, and 3a) Total score, 3b) Part 1 score (10 original ACEs), and 3c) Part 2 score (7 additional adversities), adjusting for covariates.

RESULTS: ACEs screening (versus not screened) was associated with elevated odds for ADHD, asthma, and obesity but lower odds of anxiety and hypertension. Among the screened cohort (n=599,989), positive ACEs screening was associated with higher odds of every health condition except hypertension. For those with a positive screen (n=178,214), both Part 1 and Part 2 scores were significantly associated with 5 out of 8 health conditions, with Part 2 generally demonstrating larger effects than the Part 1.

CONCLUSIONS: ACEs screening in pediatric primary care is a critical component to assess health risks and address early intervention and treatment.

articles.title: Autologous Osteochondral Transplantation Remains a Reliable Option for Talar Osteochondral Lesions, With Low Knee Donor-Site Morbidity.
articles.journal: The Journal of foot and ankle surgery : official publication of the American College of Foot and Ankle Surgeons
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autologous osteochondral transplantation (AOT) is a surgical option for talar osteochondral lesions (OCL), with favorable outcomes and high return-to-sport rates; however, knee donor-site morbidity remains a concern.

PURPOSE: To evaluate clinical and functional outcomes, complications, return to work and sport, and satisfaction after AOT for talar OCL.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective case series.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed consecutive patients ≥18 years with talar OCL treated with AOT (2011-2022; minimum 2-year follow-up); patients with prior knee pain or surgery, infection, advanced osteoarthritis, or rheumatologic disease were excluded. Outcomes included the AOFAS hindfoot, Lysholm, and Tegner scores, ankle and knee visual analog scale (VAS) pain, satisfaction, return to work and sport, and complications.

RESULTS: Thirty-seven patients (78% male; median age, 36 years; median follow-up, 24 months) were included. Median lesion size was 150 mm², all medial; 14 (38%) had concomitant procedures. The AOFAS score improved from 54.5 to 95.8 (mean difference, 41.3; 95% CI, 38.4-44.3) and ankle VAS from 7.0 to 1.6 (-5.4; 95% CI, -5.9 to -4.9) (both p < 0.001). Postoperative Lysholm score was 98.8 ± 4.0 and knee VAS 1.2 ± 0.8 (no preoperative knee scores). Return to work took 2.3 ± 1.2 months; all 32 athletes resumed sport at 6.5 ± 2.1 months, 20 (63%) in their pre-injury sport. Tegner scores were unchanged (5.4 vs 5.5; p = 0.624). One knee hemarthrosis and one repeat ankle arthroscopy occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: AOT for talar OCL yielded favorable short-term outcomes, high return-to-work and return-to-sport rates, and low reported knee donor-site morbidity; baseline knee scores were unavailable.

LEVEL OF CLINICAL EVIDENCE: 4.

articles.title: The lipoprotein-immune checkpoint axis: Linking cardiovascular toxicity and antitumor immunity during immune checkpoint therapy.
articles.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors(ICIs) improve cancer outcomes but may also perturb vascular immune homeostasis and increase atherosclerotic cardiovascular risk. Clinical cohorts and imaging studies associate ICI exposure with atherosclerotic events, plaque progression, and arterial inflammatory changes, although causality and the relevant vascular phenotype remain incompletely defined. This Review examines a lipoprotein-immune checkpoint interface linking plaque inflammation with antitumor immunity. We focus on low-density lipoprotein(LDL) and oxidized LDL(oxLDL), lipoprotein(a)[Lp(a)] and oxidized phospholipids (OxPLs), statin-related regulation of ubiquitin-like 3(UBL3)-dependent programmed death-ligand 1(PD-L1) sorting into small extracellular vesicles(sEVs), and proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9(PCSK9). Lp(a) and OxPLs are established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease(ASCVD) mediators but unvalidated ICI-specific biomarkers. Statins have proven cardiovascular benefit and emerging mechanistic links to PD-L1 trafficking, whereas oncologic associations remain observational. PCSK9 inhibition combines established lipid lowering with preclinical enhancement of antigen presentation and checkpoint response, but randomized ICI-specific evidence is lacking. Current evidence therefore supports a testable translational framework rather than a validated causal axis. Guideline-directed cardiovascular prevention remains the clinical standard while biomarker and therapeutic hypotheses require prospective validation.

articles.title: Diffusion tensor imaging and structural MRI reveal early microstructural injury and progressive atrophy of the olfactory bulb in type 1 diabetic rats.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) can detect early olfactory bulb microstructural abnormalities in streptozotocin (STZ)-induced type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) rats and to investigate their relationship with structural and histopathological changes.

METHODS: Control and STZ-induced T1DM rats underwent DTI, high-resolution structural MRI and histological examination at 2 and 12 weeks after model induction. Fractional anisotropy (FA), mean diffusivity (MD), axial diffusivity (Da), and radial diffusivity (Dr) were measured in the olfactory nerve layer/glomerular layer/external plexiform layer (ONL/GL/EPL), granule cell layer (GCL), and subependymal zone (SEZ).

RESULTS: Compared to the controls, T1DM rats showed decreased FA and increased MD, Da, and Dr. in the ONL/GL/EPL at 2 and 12 weeks after model induction. In the GCL, FA was decreased, whereas Dr. was increased.. No significant diffusion abnormalities were detected in the SEZ. Ultrastructural examination revealed axolemmal disruption, demyelination, reduced axoplasmic content, and axonal vacuolization in the ONL. Voxel-based morphometry (VBM) demonstrated olfactory bulb atrophy as early as 2 weeks, initially involving the GCL and SEZ, with more extensive and regionally heterogeneous atrophy at 12 weeks. Nissl staining confirmed structural atrophy, and increased caspase-3 immunoreactivity supported apoptosis-related tissue injury. STZ-induced T1DM causes early, layer-specific olfactory bulb microstructural abnormalities and progressive structural atrophy.

CONCLUSION: The differing spatial and temporal distributions of diffusion abnormalities and atrophy suggest that DTI and volumetric MRI capture partially distinct aspects of diabetes-associated olfactory bulb injury. DTI may provide a sensitive, noninvasive approach for detecting early microstructural abnormalities before widespread structural loss develops.

articles.title: Excerpts from the World Medical Literature - Reproductive Endocrinology and Infertility.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology Canada : JOGC = Journal d'obstetrique et gynecologie du Canada : JOGC

articles.title: Survey-Weighted Explainable Gradient Boosting for Regional Disparities in PHQ-9-Defined Depression in Korea: 2024 Korea Community Health Survey.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To analyze regional disparities in depression defined by the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) among Korean adults using spatial statistics and survey-weighted prediction models based on the 2024 Korea Community Health Survey (KCHS), and to visualize region-specific contributing factors using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) METHODS: This cross-sectional secondary analysis evaluated 231,469 respondents. Survey weights were applied to logistic regression, XGBoost, and LightGBM models to classify concurrent depression status, operationally defined as a PHQ-9 score of 10 or higher. Spatial autocorrelation was assessed using global Moran's I and Local Indicators of Spatial Association. SHAP values quantified global feature importance and the spatial heterogeneity of dominant positive mean contributors across 250 harmonized municipal units RESULTS: The national weighted prevalence of PHQ-9-defined depression was 4.1 percent, with weak positive global spatial autocorrelation and regional variation ranging from 0.9 percent to 8.2 percent. In the independent test set, LightGBM achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.92, an area under the precision-recall curve of 0.43, and a Brier score of 0.03. No local association remained significant after false discovery rate correction. SHAP analysis identified perceived stress, subjective happiness, and subjective health status as the most influential global predictors. Mapping revealed spatial heterogeneity: perceived stress was the most frequent dominant positive mean contributor, whereas other municipal units showed subjective health status, subjective happiness, smoking status, sleep duration, income, and other contributors. Regional contributor rank retention varied across bootstrap samples (median, 72.5%).

CONCLUSION: Psychosocial and structural characteristics contributed to concurrent classification of PHQ-9-defined depression, with exploratory geographic variation in aggregated SHAP contributions. Combining explainable machine learning with spatial statistics may inform further local assessment.

IRB APPROVAL/EXEMPTION: This study was exempted from review by the Institutional Review Board of Kangbuk Samsung Hospital (KBSMC IRB No. 2026-02-008).

articles.title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy in COPD-concomitant lung cancer: A review of efficacy outcomes and mechanistic insights.
articles.abstract: The coexistence of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and lung cancer (LC) presents a complex clinical scenario with distinct pathological interactions. Beyond shared epidemiological and genetic risk factors, COPD reshapes the pulmonary immune microenvironment through reprogrammed immune-cell compartments, aberrant programmed cell death, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), fostering an immunologically "hot" but pathologically permissive milieu that simultaneously drives carcinogenesis and influences treatment responsiveness. Recent evidence suggests that COPD may confer an altered immunological microenvironment that paradoxically enhances responsiveness to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in patients with LC. This review mainly synthesizes clinical evidence on the efficacy of ICI, currently the most widely used immunotherapy, in LC patients concomitant with COPD and elucidates potential immunological and molecular mechanisms underlying observed clinical benefits, including heightened programmed cell death protein ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression, elevated tumor mutational burden, increased human leukocyte antigen I (HLA-I) expression, enriched tissue-resident memory T cells and mucosal-associated invariant T cells, and a macrophage polarization shift toward a pro-inflammatory phenotype, with benefits appearing largely attributable to patients with mild-to-moderate airflow obstruction. The safety profile of ICIs in this population-exacerbation risk, eosinophilic airway disease, checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP), and autoimmune thyroiditis-is appraised, alongside emerging strategies such as lymphocyte-activation gene 3 (LAG-3), T-cell immunoglobulin and mucin-domain containing-3 (TIM-3), and T cell immunoreceptor with Ig and ITIM domains (TIGIT) blockade and the immunomodulatory potential of COPD medications (inhaled corticosteroids and long-acting β-agonists). Current evidence remains limited by small retrospective cohorts and heterogeneous stratification. Large-scale prospective studies are warranted. This review aims to clarify the prognostic value of concomitant COPD and guide precision therapeutic strategies for this growing comorbid population.

articles.title: Lycopene-loaded albumin nanoparticles developed by an ultrasound-driven assembly-emulsification method for parenteral nutrition.
articles.abstract: Intestinal failure-associated liver disease (IFALD), a severe complication of parenteral nutrition (PN), remains difficult to prevent and treat. We hypothesized that the bioactive carotenoid lycopene could alleviate hepatocellular signaling disturbances involved in its pathogenesis. However, IFALD patients require intravenous nutrient administration; therefore, potential lycopene treatment would necessitate an appropriate delivery system to overcome its poor water solubility. In this study, we evaluated the biological activity of free lycopene in THLE-2 hepatocytes under IFALD-like conditions and developed lycopene-loaded human serum albumin nanoparticles (Lyc@AlbNPs) for PN supplementation. Lycopene attenuated MAPK- and NF-κB-related inflammatory signaling and modulated the expression of genes involved in cholesterol metabolism, including ABCA1, CYP7A1, and SREBF2. Lyc@AlbNPs were prepared by adding lycopene directly to the albumin solution rather than first dissolving it in an organic solvent, as required in typical methods for producing albumin nanoparticles. Initial lycopene-albumin assemblies formed during bath sonication; subsequent ultrasonic emulsification promoted their reorganization into smaller particles, yielding Lyc@AlbNPs with a mean size of 72.2 ± 3.1 nm, a polydispersity index of 0.265 ± 0.013, and lycopene loading of 9.42 ± 0.22 %. Thermal and diffraction analyses indicated disruption of the crystalline structure of lycopene during initial assembly formation. Lyc@AlbNPs were nonhemolytic and cytocompatible in THLE-2 cells. Five ready-to-use three-chamber PN bags were supplemented with Lyc@AlbNPs to assess potential interactions; all admixtures met the predefined compatibility criteria and remained stable for 24 h. These findings indicate that free lycopene modulates inflammatory and metabolism-related signaling in an in vitro IFALD model, while the albumin-based nanoformulation enables its addition to PN admixtures. The study also demonstrates an alternative formulation approach to incorporating poorly soluble compounds into albumin nanoparticles.

articles.title: The ICD trilogy: From transvenous to subcutaneous to extravascular.
articles.journal: Revista portuguesa de cardiologia : orgao oficial da Sociedade Portuguesa de Cardiologia = Portuguese journal of cardiology : an official journal of the Portuguese Society of Cardiology

articles.title: Construction and Preliminary Exploration of a Stratified Treatment System for Chronic Subdural Hematoma: A Retrospective Analysis of 347 Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic subdural hematoma (CSDH) presents management challenges due to variable recurrence rates and the limitations of uniform treatment strategies. This study aimed to describe and preliminarily explore a volume- and structure-based stratified treatment framework for individualized CSDH care.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 347 patients with CSDH treated at a single center between January 2020 and December 2025. Patients were allocated according to a predefined institutional protocol into: Group A (medical management, volume <30 mL, n = 126), Group B (middle meningeal artery embolization, 30-50 mL, n = 36; 16 patients required additional burr-hole drainage), Group C (burr-hole drainage, >50 mL with simple structure, n = 167), and Group D (MMA ligation plus neuroendoscopic evacuation for complex hematomas, n = 18). Outcomes were assessed at 6 months using descriptive statistics, Kaplan-Meier analysis, and Firth penalized logistic regression. A summary dataset was used to verify baseline characteristics and recurrence outcomes.

RESULTS: The 347 patients included 286 males and 61 females, with a mean age of 72 ± 11 years (range, 21-94 years). Baseline hematoma volume and midline shift differed significantly among the groups (P < 0.001). The initial treatment success rates were as follows: Group A, 71% (90/126); Group B, 56% (20/36); Group C, 91% (152/167); and Group D, 100% (18/18). In Group B, 16 patients (44%) required additional burr-hole drainage. Multivariable analysis identified complex hematoma features as a risk factor for recurrence (OR = 8.95, P < 0.001), whereas the combined procedure was associated with a lower risk of recurrence (OR = 0.02, P < 0.001). Propensity score matching (15 matched pairs) suggested a lower recurrence rate with the combined approach (0% vs. 13%); however, the difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.22, Fisher's exact test).

CONCLUSION: This retrospective, single-center exploratory analysis suggests that a stratified treatment approach based on hematoma volume and structure is feasible. The combined surgical strategy (MMA ligation + endoscopy) showed promising short-term results in complex CSDH, warranting prospective validation.

articles.title: The retinal microvasculature as a predictive window for systemic vascular health in CKM syndrome: A narrative review.
articles.abstract: The cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome is a pathophysiologic continuum resulting from the synergistic interactions between metabolic dysregulation, chronic kidney disease and cardiovascular disease. The syndrome progresses insidiously, initiating a cascade of systemic microvascular injury, oxidative stress, and inflammation, often preceding apparent, permanent multiorgan failure. Traditional systemic markers often do not detect early endothelial dysfunction and there is an unmet clinical need for non-invasive biomarkers to detect subclinical damage. In this narrative review, we explore the emerging field of oculomics which considers the retina as an easily accessible living biopsy of the systemic micro-circulation. The retinal vascular network, nephrons and myocardium have common embryological origins and similar anatomical characteristics, so that changes in the retinal vascular network are a direct manifestation of pathological changes occurring in the nephrons and heart at the same time. Modern ultrahigh resolution imaging modalities such as optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) enable physicians to quantify subclinical parameters such as capillary depletion, arteriolar constriction, and neural layer atrophy. These dynamic retinal fingerprints can be identified to aid in early risk stratification of the CKM continuum, including hypertension, diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and atherosclerosis. Furthermore, these eye measures are sensitive pharmacodynamic endpoints that allow for real-time in vivo monitoring of systemic microvascular responses to novel cardiometabolic drugs. Oculomics, through the integration of portable imaging technologies, algorithms for deep learning, and multi-omics circulating biomarkers, has the ability to translate CKM risk assessment into primary care settings.

articles.title: Species-specific bioaccessibility of microplastics by benthic macroinvertebrates.
articles.abstract: Effect and bioaccumulation tests have mainly used monodisperse microplastics, whereas natural microplastics are diverse. Consequently, understanding of their actual biological accessibility remains limited, which constrains risk assessment. The goal of this study was to investigate species-specific uptake of an environmentally representative microplastic mixture (ERMP; 9-5386 μm; PE, PP, PET and PS) in 11 freshwater and marine benthic macroinvertebrate species. Species-specific uptake was assessed by describing ingested particles as a continuum through continuous size distributions and comparing these distributions among species and against controls. Samples underwent enzymatic/hydrogen peroxide digestion and FTIR microscopy, followed by polymer- and size-specific blank correction. Adverse effects previously observed in the freshwater worm Lumbriculus variegatus could be linked more directly to exposure because microplastics were detected in post-depuration organism samples. Only a select fraction of the ERMP mixture was ingested by Asellus aquaticus, Corbicula fluminalis, Corophium volutator, Hyalella azteca, L. variegatus, Limecola balthica, Mytilus edulis and Tubifex spp. Most particles detected in organisms ranged from 5.5 to 27.7 μm and differed in polymer composition among species; 5.5 μm was also the method's lower size-detection limit. Egested ERMP significantly exceeded particles remaining in post-depuration organism samples, indicating substantial egestion during the 24 h depuration period. The lowest ERMP numbers occurred in post-depuration organism samples of the midge larva Chironomus riparius and egestion samples of the mud snail Potamopyrgus antipodarum, respectively, averaging <1 particle/organism. The highest egested count occurred in the mussel M. edulis, at 49.9 particles/organism, primarily polystyrene. Similar size distributions were found for the amphipods A. aquaticus and H. azteca, both sediment grazers/scavengers, and for the clams C. fluminalis and L. balthica, both facultative deposit feeders. These particle size- and species-specific ingestion patterns provide a basis for understanding effect mechanisms such as particle volume-based food dilution.

articles.title: Identifying Key Odorant Compounds and Assessing Odor Additivity in Complex Mixtures via Machine Learning: A Multi-Regional Case Study in China.
articles.abstract: With the continuous development of industrial parks in China, odor pollution resulting from the extensive use of solvents has become increasingly prominent, making its accurate analysis and effective prevention and control critically important. To identify key odorant compounds in complex mixtures, this study collected 426 air samples from industrial parks in Guangdong and Zhejiang, China and built a database of odor concentrations and chemical compositions. Machine learning (AutoGluon) combined with SHAP interpretability analysis was employed to build an odor concentration prediction model. The optimal strategy used the Odor Activity Value (OAV) as input for an ExtraTrees model, achieving a pooled out-of-fold R2 of 0.52 under nested cross-validation. Combining SHAP (Shapley additive explanations) interpretability analysis of this optimal model with OAV screening identified 15 key odorant compounds, including methanethiol, tetrachloroethane, acrolein, among others. Further investigation assessed the additivity of odor perception: the summed odor activity value (ΣOAV) failed to reproduce the measured odor concentration, and 81% of the valid samples showed supra-additive behavior. This deviation was closely associated with the analytical coverage of the dominant odorants: sulfur-rich samples were close to additive, whereas sulfur-poor samples deviated by up to two orders of magnitude. The additivity index therefore reflects the completeness of the monitoring list and provides no evidence for or against pairwise sensory interactions. This study validates a data-driven approach for deciphering complex odor formation, providing a powerful methodology for key odorant screening and a scientific foundation for targeted odor pollution control.

articles.title: Quantifying benefit and cost-effectiveness of additional investment in community health workers for people with cardiovascular risks in New York City.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To estimate the life expectancy gains, cost effectiveness, and impact on life expectancy inequality achieved by additional investment in community health worker (CHW) programs in New York City Methods: Using a state-transition model of mortality-driving conditions adapted to New York City anchored to 2021, we examined the impact of additional investment in CHWs for people with obesity, hypertension, and diabetes on (1) change in life expectancy, (2) health-inclusive (lifespan) return on investment (LROI), and (3) change in inequality of life expectancy distribution between neighborhoods. Inequality analyses included neighborhood-level baseline life expectancy, median income, and plurality race or ethnicity. Analyses were conducted in 2026.

RESULTS: Scaling up CHWs results in a 0.13-year life expectancy gain on the citywide level, with favorable LROI of 14.72 years per $100,000 invested. Neighborhood-level gains range from 0.05 years to 0.33 years, while LROI ranges from 11.76 to 29.62 life-years/$100,000. In general, life expectancy gains and LROI were higher for lower-income, lower life expectancy, and minoritized race neighborhoods.

CONCLUSIONS: Additional investment in CHW programs in New York City has the potential to cost-effectively raise the citywide life expectancy while reducing inequalities between neighborhoods.

articles.title: Declining Complications After Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty Over 16 Years.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Demand for primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA) continues to rise, but contemporary temporal changes in 90-day and 2-year complication risk across multiple outcomes remain incompletely defined.

METHODS: Adults undergoing primary TKA for knee osteoarthritis from 2008 through 2023 were identified in a large national database using Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) 27447 with an antecedent or same-day knee osteoarthritis diagnosis. Patients who had a previous or revision TKA, periarticular fracture, or bone/articular cartilage malignancy before index were excluded. Annual risks were assessed for eight 90-day and seven 2-year outcomes. Trends were modeled with grouped binomial logistic regressions and reported as odds ratios (OR) per 5-year calendar increase.

RESULTS: The cohort included 201,736 patients, with captured annual volume increasing from 1,086 to 33,775. The mean age increased from 65 to 68 years, and the proportion of women decreased from 63.2 to 60.3%. A total of seven 90-day outcomes declined, including periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) (1.20 to 0.73%; OR 0.78, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.73 to 0.83), deep vein thrombosis (2.49 to 1.61%; OR 0.73, 95% CI 0.70 to 0.76), and transfusion (8.38 to 6.30%; OR 0.50, 95% CI 0.49 to 0.51), while sepsis was unchanged. At two years, revision/reoperation, PJI, aseptic loosening, mechanical complications, implant-related complications, and manipulation under anesthesia declined; periprosthetic fracture remained stable.

CONCLUSIONS: From 2008 through 2023, 90-day and 2-year complication risks after primary TKA declined across nearly all assessed outcomes despite cohort aging and marked growth in captured procedures. These findings provide contemporary network-based benchmarks for primary TKA outcomes.

articles.title: Validation of senescence as a therapeutic target in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) through navitoclax delivery.
articles.journal: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a chronic liver disease characterized by steatosis, inflammation, and progressive fibrosis. Increasing evidence suggests that cellular senescence contributes to MASH progression by promoting lipid accumulation, inflammatory signaling, and fibrogenic responses, highlighting hepatic senescent cells as a potential therapeutic target. Senolytics selectively eliminate senescent cells, but their application in MASH remains insufficiently explored. In this study, we developed in vitro models integrating hepatic lipid accumulation and hepatocyte-macrophage inflammatory crosstalk to facilitate investigation of the contribution of cellular senescence to MASH pathology and to evaluate senescence-targeted interventions. Senescent hepatic cells showed enhanced lipid accumulation and amplified inflammatory signaling with macrophages. Natural Extracellular Vesicles (EVs) derived from adipocytes reduced senescence-associated phenotypes but exhibited context-dependent biological effects, highlighting the limited control over their intrinsic bioactivity. Navitoclax, a senolytic targeting anti-apoptotic BCL-2 family proteins, reduced senescence-associated phenotypes, but its clinical use is limited by its dose-dependent toxicity. Hence, we conceived nano-Cell Vesicle Technology Systems (nCVTs), a biohybrid-based platform combining cell-derived membranes with synthetic lipids for controlled delivery of navitoclax. Navitoclax-loaded nCVTs retained senolytic activity and reduced inflammatory signaling and fibrotic activation in vitro. Importantly, in a Western diet- and fructose-induced (WDF) MASH mouse model, navitoclax-loaded AML-12-derived nCVTs alleviated hepatic lipid accumulation while reducing histopathological activity score and fibrotic profiles. Neither navitoclax formulation reduced platelet counts or hemoglobin concentrations at the tested dose. Collectively, these findings support cellular senescence as a therapeutically relevant target for MASH and identify nCVTs as a promising engineered platform for controlled senolytic delivery.

articles.title: Quality of Life and Late Effects Following Haploidentical vs. Matched Unrelated Donor Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation: Secondary Analysis of BMT CTN 1702.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Quality of life (QoL) is a critical indicator of therapeutic benefit and long-term recovery after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT). The BMT CTN 1702 clinical trial (NCT03904134), a multicenter study (2019-2022) evaluating donor search, selection practices and outcomes of HCT using alternative donor sources, incorporated QoL as a secondary endpoint. The aim of the QoL sub-study was to explore the long-term QoL in a more homogenous subset of patients with AML/ALL in CR1 and early-stage MDS who provided additional clinical and patient-reported outcomes (PRO) data, comparing those receiving matched unrelated donor (MUD) with Haploidentical (Haplo) donors.

METHODS: QoL was assessed using PROMIS measures and the Lee Symptom Scale (LSS). PROs were completed at baseline, 1 and 2 years post-HCT. PRO analysis used a generalized estimating equation linear regression model. Late effects, infection rates, and healthcare utilization were also compared.

RESULTS: 304 patients were analyzed (61 Haplo and 243 MUD). While PRO submission rates at baseline were similar, retention in the MUD cohort was higher than Haplo (80% and 83% vs. 58% and 60% at year 1 and year 2, respectively). There were no significant differences in QoL between haplo and MUD HCT recipients at baseline or throughout the 2-year post-transplant period. Both groups entered transplantation with substantial impairments in global physical and mental health relative to the U.S. population norms. No significant differences in late effects were observed within 2 years of HCT. The use of Haplo donors was associated with significantly more hospital days (median days 27.0 vs. 21.0, p<0.01). and more viral infections (49.2% vs. 31.8%, p=0.01) in the first 100 days. In a subset analysis restricted to patients receiving PTCy (N=117) for GVHD prophylaxis, the differences in hospital days were diminished; however, differences in viral infection remained (48.2% vs. 28.0%, p=0.02).

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides evidence that the use of a haplo or MUD donor is not associated with differences in post-HCT QoL trajectories, while highlighting substantial pre-transplant symptom burden across all recipients. Despite similar QoL trajectories and late effect profile, the increased viral infections in Haplo HCT may reflect differences in post-transplant medical complications. Future studies with larger cohorts and longer follow-up will be essential to refine these observations and guide strategies to improve long term outcomes.

articles.title: Risk of depression in individuals with syphilis: a population-based, nationwide matched cohort study in Denmark.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine risk of depression among individuals tested for syphilis.

METHODS: Population-based matched cohort study in Denmark using registry data from 2000-2022. We included a seropositive cohort of 3,636 individuals with a positive serological syphilis test. Comparison cohorts comprised 3,636 seronegative individuals matched 1:1 on sex, date of birth and inclusion date, and 32,724 individuals from the background population matched 9:1 on sex, date of study inclusion and month of birth. Individuals with HIV, neurosyphilis and women diagnosed at pregnancy screening were excluded. Corresponding sibling cohorts were identified to assess family-related factors. The primary outcomes were first-time diagnosis of depression or receipt of antidepressant medication. Hazard ratios were estimated by Cox regression, adjusted for comorbidity, income and origin.

RESULTS: Seropositive individuals had an increased risk of depression (10-year risk difference 1.3% (95% CI: 0.5-2.0%); HR 1.8 (95% CI: 1.4-2.2)) and receipt of antidepressant medication (10-year risk difference 5.8% (95% CI: 4.0-7.6%); HR 1.5 (95% CI: 1.4-1.7)) compared with the comparison cohort from the background population. Additionally, seropositive individuals had an increased risk of receipt of antidepressant use compared to the seronegative individuals (10-year risk difference 2.7% (95% CI: 0.4-5.1%); HR 1.2 (95% CI: 1.0-1.4)), but not of depression. Seronegative individuals had an increased risk of both depression (10-year risk difference 1.2% (95% CI: 0.6-1.9%); HR 1.8 (95% CI: 1.4-2.2)) and receipt of antidepressant medication (10-year risk difference 3.1% (95% CI: 1.5-4.7%); HR 1.3 (95% CI: 1.2-1.5)) compared with the comparison cohort from the background population. No increased risk was observed between the sibling cohorts.

CONCLUSION: Individuals undergoing syphilis testing had an increased risk of depression irrespective of test result, suggesting that the association reflects characteristics of the tested population rather than the syphilis infection itself.

articles.title: Estimating viral interference from wastewater surveillance: a Bayesian multi-pathogen SEIR framework.
articles.abstract: The concurrent circulation of influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV creates complex transmission dynamics in which infection with one virus may reduce or enhance transmission of another. We developed a Bayesian multi-pathogen SEIR model in which the transmission of each virus is reduced by the prevalence of co-circulating pathogens, quantified by an aggregate population-level interference coefficient θ. We fit the model to weekly wastewater data from six Canadian provinces over the 2024-2025 respiratory season, avoiding the use of clinical data, which are limited by under-reporting and inconsistent testing. Our findings show the estimated interference corresponded to a 4 to 30% reduction in peak transmission of each virus during co-circulation, with smaller reductions in the effective reproduction number. Although these estimates are based on a single respiratory season and can vary under different patterns of co-circulation, they are consistent with recent studies on multi-pathogen viral interference using clinical surveillance data.

articles.title: Optimisation of single-nuclei isolation and RNA sequencing of parasitic nematodes.
articles.abstract: Single-cell/nuclei transcriptomics has revolutionised our understanding of cell, tissue, and organismal biology in humans and model organisms across health and disease. However, for non-model species, reassessment and refinement of conventional methods is needed to address novel technical and biological challenges. Here, we evaluate three established nuclei isolation protocols and, building on these experiences, develop an optimised protocol for single-nuclei isolation of parasitic nematodes (SNIP). SNIP recovered 1.7- to 4.1-fold more nuclei than the three established protocols, and 3.2-fold more RNA per nucleus than the best-performing of these. We validated SNIP across macroscopic and microscopic life stages and both sexes of two phylogenetically distinct gastrointestinal nematodes, Haemonchus contortus and Trichuris muris, and used it to generate single-nuclei RNA-seq data revealing sex- and stage-specific gene expression and putative tissue-specific expression in both species. By enabling flexibility with frozen samples and consistent recovery across diverse parasitic nematode life stages, SNIP provides a practical foundation for building cell and nuclei atlases in other non-model species, toward advancing understanding from fundamental biology to infection and disease.

articles.title: Impaired formation and updating of internal predictive models in a rat model of fragile X syndrome.
articles.abstract: Predictive coding frameworks propose that perception emerges from a continuous comparison of incoming sensory signals with internally generated predictions, with mismatches between the two computed as prediction errors. Disruptions to the balance between these top-down predictions and bottom-up sensory signals are theorized to contribute to sensory abnormalities in neuropsychiatric conditions like autism spectrum disorders. However, disambiguating bottom-up from top-down contributions to sensory processing remains a difficult challenge, particularly in animal models. Here we develop a probabilistic oddball detection task in which rats must track local statistics within a trial to detect a deviant stimulus, as well as global statistics across trials to anticipate when a deviant will occur. This design enables formation of experimentally specified internal models of deviant expectation that can be quantitatively derived from behavior and manipulated independently of local stimulus statistics. We used this task to characterize sensory predictive behavior in a Fmr1 KO rat model of Fragile X Syndrome, the most common monogenic cause of autism. Male Fmr1 KO rats detected deviant stimuli at wildtype levels but exhibited reduced anticipation of deviant occurrence based on cross-trial statistics and failed to adapt their behavior when these statistics changed. Computational modeling revealed that these behavioral deficits reflected an overweighting of immediate sensory evidence and temporal response pressure at the expense of learned predictive expectations, consistent with imprecise internal models skewed towards sensory immediacy. These findings provide evidence for disrupted predictive processing in Fragile X Syndrome, consistent with active inference accounts of autism, and highlight the utility of this probabilistic oddball task design for interrogating predictive coding and perceptual impairments in neuropsychiatric conditions.

articles.title: Beyond Classification Accuracy: Building Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Electroencephalography.
articles.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) remains important in clinical neuroscience because it records brain activity as a time-resolved physiological process. It offers millisecond temporal resolution, can be used at the bedside and supports prolonged monitoring. Artificial intelligence (AI) has expanded EEG analysis through automated pattern recognition, representation learning, large-scale screening and decision support in epilepsy, sleep medicine, cognitive disorders, psychiatric conditions, intensive care, disorders of consciousness and anaesthesia monitoring. High classification accuracy in a research dataset, however, is not clinical readiness. EEG signals are shaped by physiological state, artefacts, acquisition systems, preprocessing choices and clinical context. Labels may come from expert annotations, diagnostic categories, behavioural scales, treatment responses or long-term outcomes, and these sources do not always define the same biological target. This review argues that EEG-AI translation should be judged by the strength of its evidence, not by technical performance alone. We examine why EEG is valuable yet hard to standardize, how EEG features can serve as candidate biomarkers, and why translational maturity differs across clinical scenarios. We then discuss the evidence gaps behind high-performing models, focusing on target validity, data leakage, confounding, external validation and clinically aligned metrics. Finally, we argue for clinical understandability rather than model interpretability alone, and for human-machine workflows rather than isolated classifiers. Future EEG-AI systems should be assessed by whether their outputs are biologically plausible, externally generalizable, understandable to clinicians and safe in real-world care.

articles.title: National survey of experiential learning program strategies for ensuring compliance with onboarding requirements.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study was to characterize the processes, systems, and personnel used by colleges and schools of pharmacy to collect, monitor, and ensure compliance with experiential education onboarding requirements.

METHODS: A 27-item electronic questionnaire was sent to experiential education faculty and staff at all Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE) accredited pharmacy programs in spring 2025. Questions included demographics, general onboarding questions and resources, onboarding requirements, and strategies for increasing requirement compliance. Descriptive statistics were used to analyze multiple-choice questions, and common approaches to compliance were identified through the open-ended question.

RESULTS: The survey had a response rate of 59.6% (84/141 programs). More than 95% of programs required hepatitis B, MMR, varicella, and Tdap vaccinations, while 90.5% required influenza vaccination. Less than 30% of programs required the COVID-19 vaccination or booster. Annual tuberculosis (TB) testing was required by 90.5% of programs. Background checks were required yearly in 63.1% of programs, and drug screening was required in 54.76% of programs. Regulatory modules and intern licenses were required by most programs. Programs used multiple compliance monitoring platforms, and consequences of non-compliance included referral to professionalism committees, course registration holds, grade deductions, or prohibition from attending rotations. Non-compliance management approaches reported include automated reminders, EE advisors, and group onboarding sessions.

CONCLUSION: Experiential program onboarding requirements showed commonality regarding childhood immunizations and background checks, with variability in other requirements and compliance monitoring platforms. Regular review of requirements and employing mechanisms for ensuring compliance will assist experiential programs with student placements.

articles.title: Left ventricular apical aneurysms in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: Characteristics and adverse events. A comparative study with patients without aneurysm.
articles.journal: Hellenic journal of cardiology : HJC = Hellenike kardiologike epitheorese

articles.title: Heart Failure Care in Greece: A Call for Action.
articles.journal: Hellenic journal of cardiology : HJC = Hellenike kardiologike epitheorese
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) remains a major public health challenge in Greece, affecting an estimated 300,000 individuals and imposing a substantial burden through high mortality, recurrent hospitalizations, impaired quality of life, and escalating healthcare costs. Although significant advances in pharmacological therapies, device-based interventions, and multidisciplinary care have improved outcomes in recent years, important gaps persist in the implementation of evidence-based HF care across the country. This viewpoint from the Heart Failure Working Group of the Hellenic Society of Cardiology (HCS) highlights five strategic priorities for the development of a comprehensive national HF strategy. First, improving the recognition and diagnosis of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), an increasingly prevalent and frequently underdiagnosed condition, through greater awareness, structured diagnostic pathways, and the adoption of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence. Second, strengthening the national advanced HF network by establishing coordinated referral pathways and equitable access to advanced therapies such as heart transplantation and durable left ventricular assist devices. Third, integrating palliative care into routine HF management to address symptom burden, psychosocial needs, and advance care planning throughout the disease trajectory. Fourth, expanding access to cardiac rehabilitation through hospital-based, community-based, and home-based programs capable of overcoming geographical disparities and improving functional outcomes. Fifth, developing a specialized HF nursing workforce through structured education and certification programs aligned with European standards. Collectively, these interconnected priorities provide a framework for advancing and modernizing HF care in Greece. A national HF registry is proposed as the foundational infrastructure supporting all five priorities.

articles.title: Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Neoplasms: Integrating WHO Classification with CT, MRI, and Molecular Imaging.
articles.journal: Revista espanola de medicina nuclear e imagen molecular
articles.abstract: Pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (pNENs) are a heterogeneous group of tumors within gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (GEP-NENs), with variable clinical behavior and prognosis. The World Health Organization (WHO) classification distinguishes well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) from poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs), including the recognition of grade 3 NETs (NET G3) as a separate entity with important clinical implications. Multiphasic computed tomography (CT) and multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are central to detection, staging, and follow-up, with MRI offering superior sensitivity for liver metastases, particularly with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and hepatobiliary phase (HBP). Molecular imaging with somatostatin receptor-targeted PET and 18F-FDG PET provides complementary biologic information by assessing receptor expression, metabolic aggressiveness, and tumor heterogeneity. SSTR-targeted PET supports confirmation of neuroendocrine phenotype, whole-body staging, and selection of candidates for peptide receptor radionuclide therapy, whereas 18F-FDG PET identifies aggressive or dedifferentiated tumor components that may influence prognosis and favor chemotherapy-oriented strategies. Despite advances, noninvasive grading remains limited, requiring integration of imaging with histopathology. An integrated multimodality approach combining CT, MRI, molecular imaging, and pathology is therefore essential for accurate staging, biopsy targeting, treatment stratification, and personalized management.

articles.title: Cardiac Lymphatic Modulation in Myocardial Repair: From Lymphangiogenesis to Microsurgical Reconstructive Strategies.
articles.abstract: The cardiac lymphatic system is increasingly recognized as a regulator of myocardial fluid homeostasis and tissue remodeling following myocardial injury. Experimental evidence suggests that impaired lymphatic drainage contributes to persistent edema, chronic inflammation and functional deterioration after myocardial infarction and other acute and chronic cardiovascular conditions. However, the translational relevance of pharmacological and microsurgical reconstructive strategies remains largely unexplored. A literature review was performed using PubMed/MEDLINE to identify studies addressing the anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, and potential therapeutic strategies addressing the cardiac lymphatic system. This study finds that cardiac lymphatics drain myocardial interstitial fluid and immune cells toward mediastinal pathways. Across various disease models, cardiac lymphatic dysfunction contributes to prolonged edema, inflammation, and adverse fibrotic remodeling. In preclinical models, pro-lymphangiogenic strategies have increased lymphatic growth and transport and have been associated with more favorable remodeling. By contrast, lymphovenous anastomosis and vascularized lymph node transfer remain largely untested concepts in cardiac disease; their ability to improve myocardial lymphatic drainage or clinical outcomes has not been demonstrated. Consequently, cardiac lymphatics may become an important therapeutic target in myocardial repair. Preliminary evidence supports the pharmacological promotion of lymphangiogenesis as a promising strategy for myocardial regeneration, but further research is necessary to explore the safety, feasibility and effectiveness of surgical cardiac lymphatic modulation.

articles.title: Azelaic Acid as a Novel Antivirulence Agent Against Pseudomonas aeruginosa: In silico, In vitro and In vivo Efficacy and Biocompatibility.
articles.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an opportunistic pathogen whose virulence is largely regulated by quorum sensing (QS), making this system an attractive target for anti-virulence therapies. Azelaic acid (AzA), a naturally occurring dicarboxylic acid widely used in dermatology, has not previously been investigated as a QS inhibitor. This study evaluated the antibacterial and anti-virulence activities of AzA against reference strains and multidrug-resistant clinical isolates of P. aeruginosa, together with its preliminary safety profile and potential molecular interactions with key QS proteins. Minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) ranged from 250 to 1000 μg/mL. At sub-inhibitory concentrations, AzA significantly reduced the production of pyocyanin, elastase, protease and alginate in a dose-dependent manner without affecting bacterial viability. Molecular docking predicted favorable interactions of AzA with LasI, LasR, PqsD and PqsR, supporting a potential modulation of QS-associated pathways. Chemoinformatic analyses predicted favorable drug-likeness and safety characteristics, while cell viability remained above 90% and hemolysis below 4% within the anti-virulence concentration range. In the Tenebrio molitor infection model, AzA significantly increased larval survival and reduced in vivo pyocyanin production in both the reference strain Pa14 and a multidrug-resistant clinical isolate. Collectively, these findings provide the first evidence that AzA can attenuates QS-regulated virulence in P. aeruginosa through complementary in vitro, in silico and in vivo approaches while exhibiting a favorable preliminary safety profile. These results support the repositioning of AzA as a promising anti-virulence candidate for the development of adjunctive therapeutic strategies against multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa infections.

articles.title: Individualized transcranial temporal interference stimulation (TIS): Research advancements and clinical translation pathways.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcranial temporal interference stimulation (TIS) is a promising tool for non-invasive deep brain modulation, yet inter-individual anatomical differences cause substantial electric field (E-field) variability under identical parameters, hindering clinical translation.

OBJECTIVE: We review recent progress (2017-2026) in individualized TIS, focusing on why inter-individual variability occurs and how to address it for clinical applications.

METHODS: We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, preprint repositories (bioRxiv, medRxiv, arXiv), and clinical trial registries from June 2017 through August 2026, synthesizing studies across quantitative E-field variability, biophysical mediation mechanisms, computational optimization frameworks, and human trials.

RESULTS: Even with individualized optimization, the focal spot can shift by up to 1.2 cm between subjects. Target modulation depth varies with age and sex, largely due to variations in skull thickness and cerebrospinal fluid volume. For E-field optimization, individualized finite element method (FEM) modeling remains the most accurate approach, whereas faster population-based optimization (17% error margin) is viable only for superficial brain areas. In human translational studies, a clear distinction must be maintained across levels of evidence: while individualized montages targeting the striatum and subthalamic nucleus demonstrate physiological target engagement, behavioral modulation in healthy cohorts, and preliminary acute symptom relief in pilot patient trials, definitive clinical efficacy in large-scale randomized trials (e.g., ongoing nucleus accumbens protocols) and effective active sham protocols remain ongoing challenges.

CONCLUSION: Individualized planning is essential for deep TIS. Future studies should focus on multi-center trials and standardized in vivo closed-loop validation using functional neuroimaging and electrophysiology.

articles.title: Do Infection Cases Need to Be Last? Evidence Shows No Increased SSI Risk Following Orthopedic Infection Procedures.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Identifying risk factors and preventing infection or return to the operating room (OR) can improve outcomes following orthopedic surgery. An infected orthopedic case may increase the bioburden in the Operating Room (OR) which leads to mitigation steps (i.e. moving infection cases to end-of-day or stacking infection cases). The purpose of this study was to evaluate whether orthopedic procedures conducted in the same OR directly following a known infection case increases surgical site infection (SSI) risk.

METHODS: This was a retrospective case review of orthopedic surgeries from 2017- 2025 (>50,000 cases). 1,290 cases were classified as 1) clean-initial-case followed by clean-subsequent-case or 2) infection-initial-case followed by clean-subsequent-case. Outcomes only in the subsequent cases were compared including rate of SSIs within 30 days and return to OR for incision & drainage (I &D).

RESULTS: The two groups had similar surgical times (p=0.982) and length of stay (p=0.113). There were no differences in 30-day rate of new SSIs (p=0.757) or return to OR with I&D code (p=0.452).

DISCUSSION: This study challenges the notion that OR teams need to change OR schedules to avoid clean cases following infection cases. It demonstrates that orthopedic infection cases performed just before in the same OR did not increase the rate of infection in the subsequent orthopedic procedure.

articles.title: Eicosapentaenoic acid in adipose tissue is associated with a lower risk of hemorrhagic stroke: A Danish case-cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) have been linked to a lower risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, however, their association with hemorrhagic stroke remains uncertain. We investigated associations between adipose tissue content of individual omega-3 PUFAs (α-linolenic acid (ALA), eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), docosapentaenoic acid (DPA), docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), the sum of EPA+DHA), and the risk of hemorrhagic stroke and its subtypes intracranial and subarachnoid hemorrhage.

METHODS: This case-cohort study based on the Danish Diet, Cancer and Health Cohort included 54,546 men and women aged 50 to 65 years at baseline (1993-1997). Adipose tissue composition of omega-3 PUFAs was determined by gas chromatography for all hemorrhagic stroke cases and within a randomly drawn subcohort of 4,615 participants. Cases were identified by linkage to the Danish National Patient Register. Hazard ratios (HR) were obtained by weighted Cox regression.

RESULTS: During a median of 21 years follow-up, we identified 729 hemorrhagic stroke cases. In multivariable analyses, a significant inverse association between the content of EPA in adipose tissue and the risk of total hemorrhagic stroke was found. Thus, the HR for hemorrhagic stroke was 0.64 (95% CI: 0.50-0.82) when comparing the highest quintile of EPA content in adipose tissue with the lowest. Associations were similar when stratified according to sex and when investigating subtypes of hemorrhagic stroke, although findings were not statistically significant for subarachnoid hemorrhages. No statistically significant associations were observed between adipose tissue content of DHA, DPA and EPA+DHA and hemorrhagic strokes. A high content of ALA in adipose tissue was associated with a higher risk of hemorrhagic stroke (HR for quintile 5 vs. 1: 1.32, 95% CI: 1.01-1.72).

CONCLUSION: A high content of EPA in adipose tissue was associated with a lower risk of hemorrhagic stroke, while a high content of ALA was associated with a higher risk in this cohort.

articles.title: Integrating patient advocacy into hepatology practice - Current perspective and future directions.
articles.abstract: The importance of patient advocacy in hepatology is indicative of a more general shift towards patient-centred and participatory healthcare. Liver diseases represent a significant global health burden, characterised by clinical complexity, a wide range of associated conditions, the invisible nature of disease progression, and frequent associations with stigma and social vulnerability. These challenges contribute to delayed diagnosis, care inequalities, and non-optimal patient engagement, highlighting the need for more support and advocacy frameworks. The concept of patient advocacy encompasses a wide range of actions designed to empower patients, improve health literacy, and ensure that patients' perspectives are integrated into care, research, and policy. It encompasses a diverse range of stakeholders, including healthcare professionals, patients, caregivers, and patient organisations, operating at various levels, namely clinical, community, and institutional. By encouraging shared decision-making and providing support to patients through often complex care pathways, patient advocacy contributes to better alignment between medical management and patients' needs. The growing recognition of patient-reported outcomes has further underscored the significance of incorporating the patient voice into clinical practice and research. Concurrently, patient participation in research and health policy enhances the relevance of scientific outputs and fosters more equitable healthcare systems. A range of practical tools has been developed for the purpose of enhancing patient engagement and empowerment. These include patient education programmes, patient journey mapping, and coordinated care pathways. However, despite this progress, significant challenges remain, including ongoing health disparities, disease-related stigma, and limited collaboration between stakeholders. The necessity of strengthening patient advocacy in hepatology is fundamental to the enhancement of clinical outcomes and the optimisation of care management for patients.

articles.title: New CLA3+/4 scores predict outcomes in MASLD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Fibrosis is a major determinant of adverse outcomes in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). We developed and validated two probability scores for advanced fibrosis (≥F3) and cirrhosis (F4)-CLA3+ and CLA4-using controlled attenuation parameter (CAP), liver stiffness (LS) by vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE), and alanine aminotransferase (ALT), and evaluated their prognostic values for liver-related events (LREs).

METHODS: In a 16-center multinational cohort, single-term fractional-polynomial logistic regression models derived CLA3+ and CLA4 probabilities.
