Prognostic performance was assessed using time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), Brier score, integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), and serial-change analyses.

RESULTS: The derivation cohort included 2,811 biopsied patients; validation included 11,196 patients with baseline VCTE, of whom 8,046 had serial assessments. Derivation AUROCs were 0.84 for CLA3+ and 0.89 for CLA4. In validation, both achieved the highest integrated AUROC (0.83) and lowest integrated Brier scores (0.0078-0.0081) among non-invasive tests, with good calibration. CLA3+ classified 83.1%/10.8%/6.1% as low/intermediate/high risk (5-year LRE 0.4%/1.5%/11.8%; sensitivity 0.72), whereas CLA4 classified 92.0%/3.6%/4.4% (0.5%/4.7%/13.0%; specificity 0.93), with the smallest intermediate-risk groups. IDI favored CLA3+ over Agile3+, whereas CLA4 performed similarly to Agile4. Serial risk categories remained stable in 86.7% for CLA3+ and 93.2% for CLA4, while ≥10-30% decreases were associated with lower LRE risk. Two-step testing reduced intermediate classifications to 3.9% with FIB-4→CLA3+ and 1.4% with FIB-4→CLA4, with a 5-year LRE rate of 8.3% in the rule-in group.

CONCLUSIONS: CLA3+ and CLA4 provide well-calibrated estimates for advanced fibrosis and cirrhosis using controlled attenuation parameter, liver stiffness, and alanine aminotransferase, with small intermediate-risk groups and prognostically informative serial changes. They may serve as second-line tests within Fibrosis-4 index-based two-step pathways.

IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Current MASLD care pathways use sequential non-invasive testing to identify patients at risk of advanced fibrosis and liver-related events, but existing composite scores often require multiple clinical inputs and leave substantial intermediate-risk groups. CLA 3+ and CLA 4 use CAP, liver stiffness, and ALT to achieve prognostic performance comparable to Agile scores, while yielding small intermediate-risk groups and informative serial changes. These findings support their potential use as simple second-line tools after FIB-4 and for longitudinal risk assessment in VCTE-based pathways, with relevance to clinical triage and future trial design.

articles.title: High-flow nasal cannula and rhinosinus mucormycosis in a neutropenic patient: a case report.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract: Mucormycosis is a rare but aggressive fungal infection caused by molds of the Mucorales order, predominantly affecting immunocompromised individuals. Rhinosinus mucormycosis typically arises after fungal spore inhalation and is characterized by rapid angioinvasion and tissue necrosis. Risk factors include uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, neutropenia and hematologic malignancies. We report the case of a 60-year-old woman undergoing chemoradiotherapy for anal cancer who developed invasive mucormycosis during a prolonged episode of neutropenia, likely exacerbated by an underlying, previously undiagnosed myelodysplastic syndrome. The patient presented with febrile neutropenia and diarrhea, and later developed acute respiratory failure, requiring four days of high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) oxygen therapy at a flow rate of 60L/min. Two days after HFNC discontinuation and shortly after recovery of neutropenia, she reported unilateral nasal pain and was found to have soft tissue inflammation; mucormycosis was subsequently confirmed by microscopy, histopathology, and culture. The patient underwent surgical debridement along with antifungal therapy with liposomal amphotericin B. Although causality cannot be established, the temporal association between HFNC use and symptom onset raises the possibility that HFNC may have contributed to mucosal injury and may have facilitated fungal invasion in this high-risk patient. This case underscores the importance of close nasal examination and early recognition of potential fungal complications in neutropenic individuals receiving HFNC therapy.

articles.title: Associations of gut microbial and serum metabolic features with metabolic comorbidities in patients with NAFLD.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) coexists with dyslipidemia or impaired fasting glucose (IFG), but gut microbial and serum metabolic features remain incompletely characterized.

OBJECTIVES: We aimed to compare gut microbial beta diversity, taxonomic profiles, predicted microbial functions, and serum metabolites across healthy controls (HCs) and NAFLD subgroups; evaluate omics-based classifiers and exploratory integrated classifiers distinguishing subgroups from HCs; and assess metabolic responses to Dialister invisus supplementation in mice.

METHODS: Fecal microbiota and serum metabolites were profiled by 16S rRNA gene sequencing and targeted UPLC-MS/MS, respectively, in 41 HCs and 222 NAFLD patients. Patients were stratified into three subgroups by dyslipidemia and IFG: NAFLD_N (neither dyslipidemia nor IFG), NAFLD_DLP (dyslipidemia without IFG), and NAFLD_IFG (IFG irrespective of lipid status; HbA1c/OGTT unavailable). Random-forest classifiers were developed for each omics layer and for post hoc integrated multi-omics panels to distinguish each NAFLD subgroup from HCs, with performance evaluated in the held-out set. Dialister invisus was administered to high-calorie diet-fed mice, and metabolic and hepatic outcomes were assessed.

RESULTS: NAFLD patients showed lower Dialister invisus abundance and higher abundance of the GTDB placeholder taxon Phascolarctobacterium_A sp900545025, with increased predicted menaquinone biosynthetic potential. Microbial and serum metabolite profiles differed significantly among subgroups. Microbiome classifiers achieved AUROCs of 0.71, 0.58, and 0.73 in the held-out internal evaluation, whereas metabolome classifiers achieved AUROCs of 0.89, 0.83, and 0.93 for NAFLD_N, NAFLD_DLP, and NAFLD_IFG. Post hoc integrated panels yielded descriptive AUROCs of 0.92, 0.89, and 0.96 in that subset. Dialister invisus supplementation reduced body weight, serum ALT, AST, triglycerides, fasting blood glucose, and ipGTT AUC in high-calorie diet-fed mice.

CONCLUSION: This study identifies shared gut microbial and serum metabolic alterations across NAFLD patients irrespective of IFG or dyslipidemia, alongside subgroup-specific signatures. The Dialister invisus findings support its potential role in metabolic regulation and warrant mechanistic investigation.

articles.title: Regulation of ketone body metabolism: biochemical mechanisms controlling ketogenesis and ketolysis.
articles.abstract: Traditionally considered as alternative energy substrates, ketone bodies (KBs), notably β-hydroxybutyrate (β-OHB) and acetoacetate, are now recognized as key metabolic intermediates whose circulating levels must be tightly controlled to ensure energy homeostasis. KBs are mostly hepatically produced, via ketogenesis, and catabolized by extrahepatic tissues during fasting or carbohydrate restriction. The regulation of KBs metabolism relies on a coordinated network of hormonal, enzymatic and transcriptional mechanisms that control KBs synthesis and degradation. KBs anabolic and catabolic rates are controlled by the rate-limiting enzymes 3-Hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA-synthase 2 (HMGCS2), governing ketogenesis, and succinyl-CoA:3-ketoacid-CoA transferase (SCOT), driving ketolysis. Their activity and expression are finely orchestrated, especially by the insulin/glucagon ratio, to adapt to the organism's fluctuating energy demands. Transcriptionally, ketogenesis is regulated through peroxisome-proliferator-activated-receptor-alpha (PPARα) and the transcription factor forkhead-box-A2 (FOXA2), which respond to nutrient availability and hormonal cues. In parallel, ketolysis is tightly controlled through the regulation of SCOT expression, notably via PPARα-dependent mechanisms, as well as through post-translational modifications (PTMs) affecting enzyme activity. Together, these regulatory mechanisms ensure a precise balance between KBs production and utilization. Emerging evidence also suggests that additional modulators, such as the gut microbiota, indirectly influence KBs metabolism by affecting substrate availability and metabolic signaling pathways, although its quantitative contribution remains to be established. Here, we provide a mechanistic overview of the pathways governing KBs metabolism, with focus on the regulation of ketogenesis and ketolysis. We discuss how these processes are integrated at multiple levels to maintain systemic energy homeostasis and consider their implications for metabolic disease.

articles.title: Real-Time Ultrasound-Assisted Laryngeal Electromyography Using an In-Plane Trajectory View: A Prospective Feasibility Study.
articles.journal: Archives of physical medicine and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the feasibility, safety, and procedural performance of a real-time ultrasound-assisted laryngeal electromyography (LEMG) protocol that uses a single dedicated in-plane trajectory view for needle guidance, without electromagnetic tracking equipment.

DESIGN: Prospective single-arm feasibility study performed by two physicians using an identical standardized technique.

SETTING: Single-center university hospital, department of rehabilitation medicine.

PARTICIPANTS: Sixteen consecutive adult patients (N=16; 14 men, 2 women; mean age 69.5±10.9 years) referred for LEMG for suspected neuromuscular laryngeal dysfunction.

INTERVENTIONS: Following anatomic survey with three orientation views, a single in-plane lateral oblique trajectory was used to sample thyroarytenoid (TA) and cricothyroid (CT) muscles.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: (i) Electromyography-confirmed muscle sampling success; (ii) complete real-time needle visualization; (iii) per-structure ultrasound visualization rates; and (iv) procedure-related adverse events.

RESULTS: Forty-four muscles (31 TA, 13 CT) were sampled. EMG-confirmed sampling was achieved in 100% (44/44). Complete real-time needle visualization was achieved in 4/31 TA muscles (12.9%) and 13/13 CT muscles (100%); thyroid cartilage calcification (87.5%) was the principal limiting factor for TA. TA and CT muscles were visualized in 100%; arytenoid and vocal cords in 30/32 (93.8%). Transient cough occurred in 3/44 muscle examinations (6.8%); none required termination. No bleeding, hematoma, or infection occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: A real-time, in-plane ultrasound-assisted LEMG protocol using a single dedicated trajectory view was feasible and showed a favorable short-term safety profile in this single-arm cohort, performed using commodity ultrasound equipment without electromagnetic tracking. In elderly patients with frequent thyroid cartilage calcification, ultrasound primarily provided trajectory guidance and vascular avoidance; the EMG signal remained the targeting reference. A comparative study against conventional landmark-based LEMG is warranted to establish its additive value.

articles.title: Residual physiological profiles in patients with CABG- or PCI-Favored coronary anatomy: A post hoc analysis of the PANDA III randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Patients with anatomically complex coronary artery disease may be considered more suitable for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) than percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), but some undergo PCI because of clinical constraints and experience higher long-term cardiovascular risk. The physiological rationale underlying this excess post-PCI risk remains unclear. From the perspective of post-PCI revascularization completeness and physiological results, we sought to explain the drivers of excess long-term adverse risk among patients with Favor CABG anatomy undergoing PCI.

METHODS: Coronary physiology based on quantitative flow ratio (QFR) was retrospectively evaluated in the randomized PANDA III trial in which all patients underwent PCI. Patients were stratified into 2 predefined groups by baseline SYNTAX score: Favor PCI or Favor CABG. Functional revascularization completeness was assessed using classic residual functional SYNTAX score (c-rFSS). Final physiological results were quantified by post-PCI QFR. Causal mediation analyses used 2-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) excluding periprocedural MI as the outcome to estimate the proportion of the group-outcome association statistically accounted for by residual coronary physiological profiles. The primary endpoint was 2-year MACE, defined as the composite of all-cause death, all MI, or any ischemia-driven revascularization.

RESULTS: A total of 1555 patients with complete post-PCI physiological assessment constituted the final study cohort, among whom 269 (17.3%) individuals were stratified to Favor CABG group by baseline SYNTAX score. The 2-year MACE rate was significantly higher in the Favor CABG than the Favor PCI group (18.6% vs 9.2%; adjusted HR: 1.78; 95% CI: 1.27-2.50). Functional incomplete revascularization (c-rFSS >0) was substantially more prevalent among patients in the Favor CABG group (53.2% vs. 15.1%, P < 0.001). Suboptimal post-PCI physiology defined by QFR <0.90 was more frequent in Favor CABG cohort (32.0% vs 11.8%, P < 0.001). In analyses using MACE excluding periprocedural MI, the estimated proportions mediated by functional incomplete revascularization and suboptimal post-PCI physiology were 49.4% and 47.8%, respectively, and their estimated joint proportion mediated was 79.8%. Integrating c-rFSS or post-PCI QFR into clinical-anatomic risk models significantly improved discrimination and reclassification capacity for 2-year MACE (all P < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: In this post hoc analysis of an all-comers PCI trial, approximately one-fifth of patients presented with anatomic complexity warranting CABG as the preferred revascularization strategy. Favor CABG anatomy was associated with higher 2-year MACE than Favor PCI anatomy. This association may be partly explained by the higher prevalence of residual functional incomplete revascularization and suboptimal post-PCI physiology. These findings between Favor CABG and Favor PCI anatomy do not represent a head-to-head comparison and should not be interpreted as a direct comparison of revascularization modalities.

articles.title: HIGHER DIETARY ACID LOAD IS LINKED TO IMPAIRED MUSCLE FUNCTION IN CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE: EVIDENCE FROM MULTIDIMENSIONAL MUSCLE ASSESSMENT.
authors: da Conceição Chaves de Lemos M
articles.journal: Journal of renal nutrition : the official journal of the Council on Renal Nutrition of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Muscle dysfunction is a major predictor of adverse outcomes in chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet modifiable nutritional determinants remain poorly defined. Dietary acid load (DAL) has been implicated in metabolic acidosis and muscle catabolism, however, its association with different domains of muscle health in CKD remains unclear. This study investigated the association between DAL, estimated by potential renal acid load (PRAL) and net endogenous acid production (NEAP), and muscle mass, muscle strength, functional performance, and muscle quality in adults with CKD.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 183 adults with CKD stages 3-5 (conservative treatment or hemodialysis) were evaluated. Dietary intake was assessed using three 24-hour recalls, and DAL was estimated using PRAL and NEAP. Muscle strength was assessed by handgrip strength (HGS), whereas lower-extremity functional performance was assessed using the five-times sit-to-stand test (STS-5). Appendicular skeletal muscle mass was measured by bioelectrical impedance analysis, and muscle quality was defined as the HGS-to-mass ratio. Multivariable logistic regression models were adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, diabetes mellitus, and CKD treatment modality.

RESULTS: NEAP values above the first tertile were associated with approximately threefold higher odds of poor STS-5 performance after multivariable adjustment (OR=3.1; 95% CI: 1.4-6.9). Higher NEAP was also associated with greater odds of cumulative muscle deficits in the adjusted analysis (OR=3.0; 95% CI: 1.0-10.8); however, this finding was of borderline statistical significance and should be considered exploratory. In contrast, NEAP was not associated with handgrip strength, muscle quality, or muscle mass after multivariable adjustment, and no consistent associations were observed between PRAL and muscle-related outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: NEAP values above the first tertile were associated with poorer lower-extremity functional performance in adults with CKD, although complementary analyses did not support a linear dose-response relationship. Exploratory findings also suggested a possible association with cumulative muscle deficits. These findings should be interpreted cautiously and require confirmation in adequately powered prospective studies.

articles.title: Metabolomic biomarkers of ultraprocessed food intake and their associations with all-cause mortality in the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC).
articles.journal: Journal of renal nutrition : the official journal of the Council on Renal Nutrition of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Higher ultraprocessed food (UPF) intake is associated with higher mortality risk in people with chronic kidney disease (CKD). The mechanisms underlying this association are not fully understood. Plasma metabolites reflect endogenous metabolism and exogenous exposures and may provide insights into the biological effects of diet. We aimed to identify metabolites associated with UPF intake and examine their prospective associations with mortality.

METHODS: Among adults with CKD in the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) study (n=1226; 48% women, mean age 59 years), we assessed cross-sectional associations between UPF intake (servings/day) and 486 plasma metabolites using multivariable linear regression. UPF intake was classified according to the Nova system. Metabolites were measured using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (Broad Institute). We examined prospective associations between significant UPF-related metabolites and the risk of death using Cox proportional hazards regression models.

RESULTS: At FDR-adjusted P<0.05, 26 metabolites were significantly associated with UPF intake. Three metabolites (C4-OH carnitine, myristoleate, and aconitate) were positively associated with UPF intake. The remaining 23 were inversely associated with UPF consumption, including several highly unsaturated (≥5 double bonds) ≥34-carbon glycerophospholipids. Over a median follow-up of 15 years (25th-75th percentile: 8-17), 539 deaths occurred. Nine UPF-related metabolites were associated with mortality (FDR-adjusted P<0.05). Highly unsaturated (≥6 double bonds) 38- and 40-carbon glycerophospholipids were among the metabolites most strongly associated with UPF intake (inversely) and with a lower risk of death.

CONCLUSION: Metabolite markers of a dietary pattern rich in ultraprocessed foods may participate in metabolic pathways contributing to mortality risk in CKD.

articles.title: Deflazacort versus prednisolone for weight gain in acute-stage allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis: a randomized trial.
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic glucocorticoids are effective in allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA) but cause adverse effects (AEs). Deflazacort may have fewer metabolic AEs than prednisolone.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether deflazacort reduces weight gain while maintaining disease control in ABPA.

METHODS: In this investigator-initiated, single-center, open-label, parallel-group randomized trial, adults with newly diagnosed ABPA were assigned 1:1 to oral prednisolone or oral deflazacort for 16 weeks. The primary outcome was percentage weight gain at eight weeks. Secondary outcomes included decline in serum total IgE, treatment response, ABPA exacerbations, and treatment-emergent AEs (TEAEs). The follow-up was two years.

RESULTS: We randomized 178 patients (89 per group; mean age, 35.5 years; 48.3% women). Mean percentage weight gain at eight weeks was lower with deflazacort than prednisolone (2.97% vs. 4.87%; mean difference, -1.9 percentage points; 95% CI, -3.32 to -0.48; p=0.009). Treatment response at eight weeks was similar (95.5% vs. 98.9%; p=0.213). However, the mean percentage decline in serum total IgE from baseline at 16 weeks was smaller with deflazacort (55.2% vs. 62.1%; p=0.024), and one-year ABPA exacerbations were more frequent (18.0% vs. 7.9%; p=0.048). The hazard ratio for the composite outcome of 8-week treatment failure or first subsequent ABPA exacerbation was 1.83 [95% CI, 0.92-3.61]; log-rank p=0.084). TEAEs were similar between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Deflazacort reduced early weight gain and achieved similar 8-week treatment response rates, but was associated with a smaller decline in serum total IgE at 16 weeks and more ABPA exacerbations at one year. Further dose-ranging studies are warranted.

articles.title: Health-Related Social Needs, Depression and Anxiety, and Asthma Outcomes in Adults with Utilization-defined Mild Asthma.
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Health-related social needs (HRSN) and depression or anxiety are associated with adverse asthma outcomes in patients with moderate-to-severe asthma, but their individual and combined associations with asthma outcomes among adults with mild asthma have not been well characterized.

OBJECTIVE: To examine the individual and combined associations of HRSN, depression, and anxiety with asthma control and asthma-related healthcare utilization among adults with utilization-defined mild asthma.

METHODS: A stratified sample of 3,787 adults with utilization-defined mild asthma completed a survey including the CMS HRSN Screening Tool, PHQ-2, GAD-2, AIRQ®, and self-reported asthma-related emergency department or urgent care visits during the previous 12 months. Modified Poisson regression evaluated associations after adjustment for age, sex, and race and ethnicity.

RESULTS: More than half of participants reported at least one HRSN, and approximately one-quarter screened positive for depression or anxiety. Depression and HRSN frequently coexisted. Depression was associated with very poorly controlled asthma (adjusted relative risk [aRR] 1.48, 95% CI 1.17-1.86) after adjusting for age, sex and race/ethnicity. Compared with no HRSN, one or more HRSN were associated with very poorly controlled asthma, and two or more HRSN were associated with asthma-related emergency department or urgent care visits. Anxiety was not independently associated with either outcome. Participants with both HRSN and depression or anxiety experienced the greatest burden of adverse asthma outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: HRSN and depression are associated with poor asthma outcomes among adults with utilization-defined mild asthma. Assessing both social needs and mental health may help identify patients at greatest risk for poor asthma outcomes.

articles.title: Post-resuscitation ST-segment elevation and coronary angiographic phenotypes in angiography-evaluable survivors of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest with presumed coronary lesion-related arrest.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical meaning of post-resuscitation ST-segment elevation in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients with suspected coronary etiology remains uncertain. We aimed to describe coronary angiographic phenotypes and clinical outcomes according to post-resuscitation ST-segment findings in an angiography-evaluable subset of OHCA survivors with presumed coronary lesion-related arrest.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 149 successfully resuscitated OHCA patients admitted to our institution between January 2015 and December 2023, who underwent post-resuscitation coronary angiography and had presumed culprit lesions, defined by integrating angiographic findings with electrocardiographic, echocardiographic, and biomarker data in the clinical context. Patients were classified according to the presence or absence of post-resuscitation ST-segment elevation.

RESULTS: ST-segment elevation was associated with a more acute occlusive coronary phenotype, with more impaired culprit-vessel flow and greater myocardial injury. In contrast, patients without ST-segment elevation more frequently had multivessel disease and chronic total occlusion, suggesting more complex coronary artery disease. Favorable neurological outcome was less frequent with ST-segment elevation in unadjusted analyses, but this association was not independent of pre-hospital factors.

CONCLUSIONS: In this selected OHCA subset, post-resuscitation ST-segment elevation was associated with an acute occlusive coronary phenotype and greater myocardial injury, as in non-arrest acute coronary syndromes. However, the absence of ST-segment elevation did not exclude a coronary culprit lesion, so comprehensive coronary assessment is essential. ST-segment elevation was not independently associated with clinical outcomes after adjustment for pre-hospital factors. These findings should be interpreted considering substantial selection inherent to the study population.

articles.title: Aortic Valve Replacement in Patients 50-65 Years: A Target Trial Emulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guidelines favor surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) in patients aged 65 years or younger with aortic stenosis, yet many receive transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) without supportive data. We performed a target trial emulation of SAVR versus TAVI in this population.

METHODS: Using the all-payer Premier Healthcare Database (2016-2024), patients aged 50 to 65 years undergoing isolated SAVR or TAVI within 90 days of an aortic stenosis diagnosis were evaluated. After trial exclusions, frailty and predicted risk were incorporated into a clone-censor-weight framework with inverse probability weighting. Reporting adhered to TARGET guidance. The primary outcome was the 5-year composite of all-cause mortality, stroke, valve reintervention, or heart failure rehospitalization.

RESULTS: The clone-censor-weighted analysis included 18,549 SAVR and 18,549 TAVI patients, balanced across all covariates (standardized mean difference <0.10). Mean age was 60 years, and many were of low surgical risk <4% (SAVR 69.5% vs TAVI 49.7%). In-hospital mortality (0.41% vs 0.31%; odds ratio, 0.61; p<0.001) and periprocedural stroke (0.31% vs 0.28%; odds ratio, 0.67; p<0.001) favored TAVI. At 5 years, risk-adjusted freedom from the primary composite outcome (87.5% vs 77.8%; hazard ratio, 1.87; p<0.001), heart failure rehospitalization (92.9% vs 88.2%; subdistribution hazard ratio, 1.72; p<0.001), and all-cause mortality (93.6% vs 85.6%; hazard ratio, 2.34; p<0.001) favored SAVR.

CONCLUSIONS: For contemporary patients aged 50 to 65 years, the primary composite outcome favored SAVR over TAVI at 5 years, most markedly at centers with high young TAVI utilization. These data may guide heart team decision making and future trial design.

articles.title: Statewide Trends in Morbidity and Mortality in Octogenarians Undergoing Isolated Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We sought to determine whether advanced age modifies the association between established preoperative risk factors and 30-day outcomes following isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), compare temporal trends between octogenarians and younger patients, and characterize differences in perioperative outcomes between the two groups.

METHODS: Using the Michigan Society of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgeons Quality Collaborative (The Society of Thoracic Surgeons Adult Cardiac Surgery Database), we identified 105,445 patients undergoing isolated CABG from 2006-2024. Outcomes and case volumes were assessed across four eras. Operative mortality was evaluated using mixed-effects logistic regression with hospital as a random effect. Secondary analyses used multiple imputation with hospital-clustered multivariable logistic regression to evaluate age-related effect modification for short-term mortality and morbidity.

RESULTS: Octogenarians comprised 8.1% of cases (8,563/105,445). Operative mortality was higher in octogenarians (4.8%; n=413) than patients <80 (1.8%; n=1,710). Operative mortality rates were stable over the study period for both patient groups. In multiple-imputation models, octogenarian status was independently associated with higher odds of operative mortality, stroke, reoperation for bleeding, and renal failure. Age-dependent effect modification was observed for select outcomes. In octogenarians, hypertension was more strongly associated with postoperative atrial fibrillation, diabetes with renal failure, and cerebrovascular disease with discharge to extended care.

CONCLUSIONS: In octogenarians, CABG remains associated with higher morbidity and mortality than in younger patients, with minimal changes in 30-day outcomes over the last 20 years. Most traditional risk factors demonstrated similar relative associations across age groups, with age-specific effects in select postoperative domains.

articles.title: Why I Hesitate Before Labelling a Patient as Having Chronic Kidney Disease.
Hepatocellular Jaundice as an Atypical Hepatic Manifestation of Disseminated Gonococcal Infection: A Case Report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Disseminated gonococcal infection is an uncommon complication of Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection and typically manifests with polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis, dermatitis, or septic arthritis. Hepatic involvement is usually attributed to gonococcal perihepatitis (Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome), in women with pelvic spread of infection; a direct hepatocellular pattern of liver injury, without perihepatitis, is rarely reported, and its mechanism is poorly understood.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report a 46-year-old divorced man with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus who presented with fever, malaise, polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis of the wrists and ankles, and a macular rash over the dorsum of both hands. He subsequently developed nausea, vomiting, dark urine, and jaundice. He denied recent high-risk sexual exposure and genitourinary symptoms. Laboratory investigations demonstrated leucocytosis, mild thrombocytopenia, predominantly conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, and elevated liver enzymes. Urine culture was sterile but blood cultures grew N. gonorrhoeae, confirming disseminated gonococcal infection. Patient was treated with ceftriaxone and doxycycline, since a concomitant Chlamydia trachomatis infection had not been excluded. Clinical improvement was rapid, and bilirubin and aminotransferases progressively normalised. Poorly controlled diabetes was noted as possible contributing factor.

CONCLUSION: This case broadens the recognized hepatic phenotype of disseminated gonococcal infection beyond classical perihepatitis, demonstrating that direct hepatocellular injury can accompany the arthritis-dermatitis syndrome and resolve completely with standard antimicrobial therapy. It also highlights that infection can present without an elicited high-risk sexual history and/or genitourinary symptoms. Clinician should have a high index of suspicion and pursue directed testing (blood culture, and where available, site-specific NAAT) even when the exposure history is unremarkable.

ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS: The authors thank the patient for consenting to the publication of this report. We are grateful to the staff of the Department of Microbiology of Burjeel Medical City, Abu Dhabi, and to the nursing and medical staff of Lifecare hospital Musaffah, Abu Dhabi for their care of the patient.

articles.title: Trends and Disparities in Mortality Related to Cardiac Arrest and Cardiogenic Shock: A 1999-2024 United States Analysis.
articles.abstract: Cardiac arrest (CA) complicating cardiogenic shock (CS) identifies a high-risk phenotype, but population-level mortality trends among patients with both conditions are not well described. Using the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death database, we identified deaths among US adults aged ≥25 years from 1999 to 2024 in which both CA (ICD-10 I46) and CS (R57.0) were recorded on the same death certificate and compared them with all CS-related deaths. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 population were calculated, and temporal trends were assessed using Joinpoint regression. Overall, 98,531 CA+CS deaths occurred, compared with 577,658 CS-related deaths. The AAMR for CA+CS declined from 1.3 in 1999 to 0.9 in the mid-2000s, rose by 10.1% per year between 2009 and 2021 (95% CI 9.8 to 10.5) to a peak of 2.9, and declined modestly to 2.7 by 2024. The share of CS deaths that also listed CA increased from 12.4% to 18.9%. Men had consistently higher AAMRs than women (3.6 vs 1.9 in 2024), and adults aged ≥65 years accounted for 71.3% of deaths. Non-Hispanic Black adults had the highest rates from 2016 onward and the steepest increase, while the West had the highest and the Midwest the lowest rates among census regions. CA+CS mortality in the United States has roughly doubled since 1999, with persistent differences by sex, race and ethnicity, age, and region that warrant study with clinically detailed data.

articles.title: Early-life enteric bacterial infection alters hippocampal cell fate and leads to cognitive deficits.
articles.abstract: Early-life enteric infections are increasingly recognized as a major driver of adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes. However, the cell-type-specific mechanisms linking intestinal inflammation to persistent cognitive deficits in the developing brain remain poorly defined. Here, we demonstrate that transient Citrobacter rodentium infection in mice, which models human pathogenic Escherichia coli infection, disrupts hippocampal development and impairs cognitive function. These phenotypes were observed only during a critical postnatal window, coinciding with transient intestinal permeability. Hippocampal transcriptomics revealed persistent dysregulation of neurogenic pathways, and cellular analyses confirmed alterations in neurons, microglia, and endothelial cells. Critically, we identified accumulation of the microbial metabolite D-lactate in the hippocampus. Oral D-lactate supplementation in a gut barrier disruption model, exacerbated both behavioral deficits and hippocampal neuronal loss. Finally, in the presence of inflammatory stimuli, exposing primary neurons to D-lactate reduced the ratio of NeuN expressing neurons. Together, these findings identify age-dependent intestinal barrier dysfunction as a potential route linking early-life enteric infection with increased D-lactate exposure, hippocampal neuronal alterations, and persistent behavioural impairment.

articles.title: Characteristics and severe maternal morbidity associated with penicillin allergy among pregnant people.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Penicillin allergy is commonly reported during pregnancy and may influence antibiotic selection for obstetric care. However, severe maternal morbidity at delivery among pregnant individuals with penicillin allergy continues to be understudied.

OBJECTIVE: To assess clinico-obstetric characteristics and severe maternal morbidity at delivery associated with penicillin allergy among pregnant people.

STUDY DESIGN: This serial cross-sectional study queried the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality's Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project's National Inpatient Sample in the United States. The study population included 24,976,627 hospital deliveries from 2016 to 2022. Exposure was a diagnosis code of penicillin allergy, identified per the American Academy of Allergy Asthma and Immunology and the American College of Allergy, Asthma and Immunology schemas. The primary outcome measure was severe maternal morbidity, identified based on the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention definition. The exposure-outcome association was assessed with propensity score-adjustment model.

RESULTS: A total of 729,475 (2.9%) deliveries had a diagnosis code of penicillin allergy with a numerical increase in prevalence from 2.5% in 2016-2018 to 3.5% in 2021-2022 (adjusted-prevalence rate ratio [aPR] 1.35, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.35 to 1.36). The prevalence rate of penicillin allergy exceeded 5% among pregnant people with asthma (5.5%) exhibiting the largest association among the assessed clinico-obstetric characteristics (aPR 1.85, 95%CI 1.84 to 1.87), followed by Group B Streptococcus carrier status (aPR 1.52, 95%CI 1.52 to 1.53). In a classification-tree model, White people with asthma who were Group B Streptococcus carrier had the highest penicillin allergy prevalence rate (8.3%). Pregnancy with penicillin allergy was associated with higher incidence of severe maternal morbidity at delivery compared to those without penicillin allergy (any composite, 108.3 vs 81.9 per 10,000 deliveries, adjusted-incidence rate ratio [aIR] 1.19, 95%CI 1.16 to 1.21). In exploratory analysis, penicillin allergy was associated with sepsis (19.6 vs 11.0 per 10,000 deliveries, aIR 1.68, 95%CI 1.59 to 1.77) and shock (11.1 vs 7.1 per 10,000 deliveries, aIR 1.49, 95%CI 1.39 to 1.60).

CONCLUSION: The results of this nationwide assessment in the United States suggest that penicillin allergy may be associated with high-risk pregnancy characteristics and severe maternal morbidity at delivery. Results also suggest that prevalence of penicillin allergy among pregnant people may be gradually increasing. Further investigation of this association is warranted to evaluate whether systematic assessment of pregnant people with penicillin allergy may improve outcomes.

articles.title: Transfusion-transmitted human parvovirus B19 infections during a "fifth disease" epidemic: 1-year follow-up of adults with malignant haematological diseases.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We characterized transfusion-associated human parvovirus B19 (PVB19) infections among adults with malignant haematological diseases during a fifth-disease epidemic.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective observational cohort study at a tertiary centre in Budapest, Hungary. Consecutive adults with malignant haematological disease or HSCT, and transfusion-associated infection were included, confirmed by two peripheral blood qPCR tests within 7 days. Patients underwent weekly qPCR monitoring, and received IVIG, with cidofovir in selected cases. Follow-up continued until 1-year, last visit or death. Outcomes were overall survival and PVB19-associated complications.

RESULTS: Forty transfused blood products were PVB19-contaminated (0.91%), and 15/40 exposed recipients developed infection (37.5%; median age 58 years; 46.7% male). Seven developed complications (46.7%), including haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (n=3), ongoing aplasia (n=4), acute liver failure, pneumonitis and pure red cell aplasia (n=1 each). All patients received IVIG, three received cidofovir. Baseline PVB19 DNA was ≥10⁴ copies/mL in seven patients (46.7%), and within 60 days, 40.0% achieved ≥1-log₁₀ PVB19 DNA reduction. Nine (60.0%) patients showed a day-3 reticulocyte decline, followed by recovery. Overall survival was 73.3% at 60 days, and 53.3% at 1-year.

CONCLUSIONS: Transfusion-associated PVB19 infection affected over one-third of exposed recipients and was associated with a clinically relevant morbidity burden.

articles.title: Response to correspondence on: 'Feasibility of studying respiratory infection transmission in a Swiss household cohort: Findings from the BEready ("Bern, get ready") study'.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases

articles.title: Innovative Management of Non-HLA Antibody and NK Cell-Mediated Rejection After Kidney Transplantation With Imlifidase: A Case Report.
articles.journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract: A highly sensitized patient received a kidney transplant (KT) following imlifidase induction: we report an innovative diagnostic and therapeutic strategy for rejection management. On day 20 post-KT, the patient developed acute kidney injury, with donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) increasing to 1.93%. Histology revealed isolated glomerulitis (g1) with C4d(2+) deposits along peritubular capillaries. Steroids and plasma exchanges were administered for suspected antibody-mediated rejection (AMR), despite no rebound of donor-specific anti-HLA antibodies (DSAs). Non-HLA anti-endothelial cell antibodies were positive, confirming AMR according to Banff 2022. Transcriptomic analysis showed overexpression of complement pathway-associated transcripts. C5 inhibition failed as serum creatinine further increased along with dd-cfDNA (3.96%). A second biopsy confirmed active AMR with increased expression of NK-related transcripts, leading to anti-CD38 treatment (daratumumab). At 6 months post-KT, the condition was controlled with stable creatinine at 20.4 μg/mL, dd-cfDNA decreased to 0.1%, microvascular inflammation resolved, non-HLA anti-endothelial cell antibodies became undetectable, still without HLA DSA rebound. Daratumumab is ongoing. Integrating dd-cfDNA, transcriptomic biopsy analysis, and non-HLA antibody assessment may optimize the management of highly sensitized KT recipients following imlifidase induction. However, long-term efficacy remains to be confirmed.

articles.title: An Albuminuria Guided Approach to Risk Stratification and Therapeutic Decision-Making in CKD.
articles.journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a global public health challenge, yet therapeutic evaluation and regulatory acceptance are constrained by reliance on late clinical endpoints such as kidney failure. Albuminuria, assessed as urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) reflects glomerular and systemic vascular injury and responds rapidly to treatment. Epidemiologic evidence demonstrates a continuous, graded association between both baseline and changes in UACR and subsequent risk for kidney failure, cardiovascular events, and mortality. Trial level analyses demonstrate that treatment effects on change in UACR is also associated with long-term treatment benefit on CKD progression across drug classes and disease populations. Meta-analysis indicates that a treatment benefit of ≥30% decline in UACR is associated with approximately a 20% treatment benefit on CKD progression, supporting its use as a clinically meaningful surrogate endpoint. Residual albuminuria during treatment identifies patients at persistently high risk and provides a rationale for therapy intensification. Recent studies demonstrate that combination therapies can achieve substantial additional reductions in UACR, in selected settings exceeding 50%. This review synthesizes biological, epidemiologic, and clinical trial evidence supporting albuminuria-guided risk stratification and a treat-to-target approach using serial UACR monitoring to personalize CKD care, while improving clinician understanding of albuminuria changes as markers of therapeutic response.

articles.title: Net Clinical Benefit of Continuing vs Discontinuing Anticoagulation After Atrial Fibrillation Ablation: Results from a 280,000-Patient Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background Oral anticoagulation (OAC) in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) reduces ischaemic stroke (IS), but increases bleeding, including intracranial haemorrhage (ICH). As catheter ablation reduces AF burden and IS risk, we evaluated the net clinical benefit (NCB) of continuing versus discontinuing OAC after AF ablation. Methods We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and cohort studies comparing OAC continuation versus discontinuation after AF ablation. NCB was calculated as the reduction in IS with continued OAC minus 1.5 × the increase in ICH. Results Thirty-eight studies were included (3 RCTs, 35 cohort studies), enrolling 280,415 patients, with 2.7 years' follow-up. In RCTs, there was no difference between patients on-OAC vs. off-OAC for IS, major bleeding, ICH, or NCB. In cohort studies, IS was similar, but major bleeding (OR, 3.02; 95%CI, 2.06-4.42, p<0.001) and ICH (OR, 3.65; 95%CI, 2.31-5.77, p<0.001) increased, with net clinical harm (NCB -0.46; 95% CI, -0.82 to -0.10, p=0.012). Combining all studies, IS was similar, but major bleeding (OR, 2.93; 95% CI, 2.08-4.14, p<0.001) and ICH (OR, 3.63; 95% CI, 2.34-5.63, p<0.001) were increased with continued OAC, with NCB favouring discontinuation (NCB -0.46; 95% CI, -0.77 to -0.14, p=0.004). Conclusion The benefit of OAC thromboprophylaxis is attenuated after AF ablation but contributes to bleeding, supporting consideration of OAC discontinuation post-ablation. However, this cannot be extrapolated to the highest ischaemic risk patients and, as risks are dynamic and sinus rhythm maintenance is not guaranteed, close surveillance would be essential if considering this approach.

articles.title: IMPACT OF INHERITED THROMBOPHILIA ON CANCER-ASSOCIATED THROMBOSIS: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer-associated thrombosis (CAT) is a cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with malignancy. The contribution of inherited thrombophilia remains incompletely defined.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between inherited thrombophilia and other genetic determinants and CAT risk in adults with malignancy.

METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies comparing genetic determinants in patients with cancer with and without VTE. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using Mantel-Haenszel models. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and GRADE, respectively.

RESULTS: Twenty-one studies including 4,479 patients (1,115 with VTE) were included. Factor V Leiden (FVL) was associated with increased odds of CAT (OR 2.48, 95% CI 1.75-3.51; I²=32%), with consistent findings after exclusion of device- or catheter-related thrombosis. Heterozygous FVL was associated with CAT (OR 1.86, 95% CI 1.27-2.73), whereas the homozygous estimate was imprecise (OR 3.42, 95% CI 0.75-15.59). Prothrombin G20210A was associated with CAT (OR 2.67, 95% CI 1.56-4.58; I²=0%). Exploratory analyses yielded estimates for MTHFR (OR 1.40, 95% CI 1.02-1.93) and blood group O (OR 0.40, 95% CI 0.23-0.70); the latter was based on only two studies. Evidence for rarer determinants was sparse. Certainty was moderate for FVL and low or very low for other determinants.

CONCLUSIONS: FVL and prothrombin G20210A are associated with increased odds of CAT. Current evidence does not support universal genetic screening but warrants prospective evaluation of the incremental predictive value of genetic markers beyond established CAT risk models.

articles.title: Trajectories of Coagulation-Fibrinolysis Balance Reveal Hemostatic Heterogeneity in Sepsis: Derivation and Multicenter Validation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The imbalance between coagulation activation and fibrinolysis drives sepsis-induced coagulopathy and organ dysfunction. However, this dynamic process is highly heterogeneous. We aimed to identify longitudinal coagulation-fibrinolysis trajectory phenotypes and to develop a novel prothrombin time (PT)-D-dimer Z-balance score to quantify this evolving hemostatic imbalance.

METHODS: This study included a single-center training cohort (n=1672) and a prospective multicenter external validation cohort (n=1393) of adult septic ICU patients. Joint group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) was applied to daily PT and D-dimer measurements over the first 7 days. Hemostatic, inflammatory and prognostic profiles were compared across phenotypes. Additionally, a daily Z-balance score [Z(PT) - Z(D-dimer)] was constructed to quantify the evolving hemostatic imbalance.

RESULTS: Joint modeling reveals three phenotypes: Compensate (Class 1, 51.9%; preserved balance), Coupled (Class 2, 35.5%; intensive but balanced coagulation-fibrinolysis activation), and Consumptive (Class 3, 12.6%; profound coagulation factor consumption with blunted fibrinolysis). The Consumptive phenotype exhibited the most severe systemic inflammation, organ failure, and the highest 28-day mortality (52.1%). Multivariable analysis confirmed Class 3 as an independent predictor of 28-day mortality in both the training (adjusted HR 2.69) and validation cohorts (adjusted HR 3.78). The novel Z-balance score revealed distinct dynamic patterns: Class 3 was characterized by persistently positive yet declining Z-balance (a delayed, partial fibrinolytic response relative to coagulation).

CONCLUSIONS: Joint longitudinal modeling of PT and D-dimer reveals three distinct coagulation‑fibrinolysis phenotypes in sepsis. The Consumptive phenotype, characterized by profound coagulation and inflammation activation alongside a positive PT-D-dimer Z-balance, identifies a high-risk subpopulation with markedly increased mortality.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetic profile of recombinant antithrombin gamma in sepsis-induced disseminated intravascular coagulation: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract: No abstract.

articles.title: Effect of ethnicity on response to treatment escalation in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus from the British Isles Lupus Assessment Group Biologics Register (BILAG-BR): a longitudinal cohort study.
authors: British Isles Lupus Assessment Group Biologics Register (BILAG-BR) consortium
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ethnic disparities in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) outcomes are well documented, but data on treatment response across ethnic groups remain scarce. We aimed to evaluate the effect of ethnicity on clinical outcomes following treatment escalation in a diverse UK cohort.

METHODS: In this longitudinal cohort study, we analysed data from the British Isles Lupus Assessment Group Biologics Register (BILAG-BR), including patients recruited from 64 UK secondary and tertiary rheumatology and nephrology centres. Eligible patients were aged 16 years and older, with active moderate-to-severe SLE, defined as having at least one BILAG A score, at least two BILAG B scores, or a SLEDAI-2K score of at least 6, who had initiated rituximab or belimumab within the past 12 months, or standard immunosuppressive therapy within the past 1 month. Ethnicity was categorised as White, South Asian, Black, East Asian, or mixed or other ethnicities. The primary outcome was major clinical response (MCR) at 6 months and 12 months, measured using mixed-effects logistic regression. Individuals with lived experience of SLE were involved in the study design.

FINDINGS: Between July 1, 2010, and Nov 10, 2021, 1688 patients were recruited to the BILAG-BR. Of these, 1266 were excluded because they did not meet the study eligibility criteria, and 422 patients were included in the study. 383 (91%) patients were female, 39 (9%) were male, and the median age was 40·5 years (IQR 31·3-50·8). 245 (58%) of 422 patients were White, 77 (18%) were South Asian, 70 (17%) were Black, 19 (5%) were East Asian, and 11 (3%) were of mixed or other ethnicities. At baseline, Black patients had higher baseline disease activity, greater organ damage, and more comorbidities. At 12 months, 99 (23%) of 422 patients had met MCR criteria, including eight (42%) of 19 East Asian patients, 23 (30%) of 77 South Asian patients, 60 (24%) of 245 White patients, seven (10%) of 70 Black patients, and one (9%) of 11 patients with mixed or other ethnicities. In the adjusted five-group model, patients of Black ethnicity had lower odds (OR 0·13 [95% CI 0·02-0·88]) of meeting MCR criteria compared with White patients.

INTERPRETATION: MCR criteria were met by fewer than a quarter of patients after treatment escalation. Patients of Black ethnicity had higher baseline disease burden and lower observed response than White patients. These results support the need for more personalised, equitable approaches to SLE management and reinforce the importance of ensuring diversity in clinical research.

FUNDING: The British Isles Lupus Assessment Group Biologics Register who received funding support from Roche, GSK, Otsuka, and Lupus UK.

articles.title: Population-scale genomics reveals divergent pathogenicity of variant classes across paralogous collagen IV genes.
articles.abstract: Monoallelic pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in COL4A3 and COL4A4 occur in approximately 1 in 106 individuals, yet whether these paralogous genes confer equivalent pathogenicity for the same variant classes has not been tested at population scale. Using whole-genome sequencing data from the UK Biobank (UKB; n ≈ 500,000), with replication in the All of Us Research Program (n ≈ 414,000), we performed per-variant association testing, gene-based collapsing analyses, and phenome-wide association studies (PheWASs) across hematuria, proteinuria, and chronic kidney disease. We identified 64 COL4A3 and 92 COL4A4 rare variants significantly associated with hematuria or proteinuria, providing population-level quantitative evidence that may support variant interpretation. Glycine substitutions within collagenous domains conferred similar risks in both genes. In contrast, truncating and non-collagenous domain (NC1) missense variants were strongly associated with hematuria and proteinuria in COL4A4 heterozygotes but showed substantially attenuated or absent associations in COL4A3 heterozygotes despite comparable allele frequencies and predicted pathogenicity scores. These findings were independently replicated in All of Us. Genome-wide association analysis identified the COL4A3 and COL4A4 locus as the dominant genetic determinant of hematuria, attributable to the aggregate effects of rare coding variants with no evidence of independent common variant or trans-acting modifier effects. These findings demonstrate marked gene-specific differences in association with hematuria and proteinuria for truncating and NC1 variants between COL4A3 and COL4A4, challenging assumptions of equivalent pathogenicity across paralogous collagen IV genes. Gene identity, not variant class alone, should inform risk stratification, variant interpretation, and genetic counseling in collagen IV heterozygotes.

articles.title: An open label, uncontrolled clinical trial of immunogenicity and safety of yellow fever vaccine in adults with chronic kidney disease as compared to immunocompetent.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: During a yellow fever (YF) epidemic in Brazil, vaccination campaigns targeting the entire population in the affected areas were conducted, bringing up an opportunity to prospectively evaluate YF vaccine's immunogenicity and safety in adults with chronic kidney disease (CKD).

METHODS: Open-label, uncontrolled clinical trial involving adults aged ≥18 years with CKD on dialysis (CKD-D) or not (CKD-ND) and immunocompetent, who had denied previous YF vaccination. All of them received a YF vaccine standard dose (0.5 mL). Neutralizing antibodies were measured by microneutralization test with 50% reduction of lysis plaques (micro-PRN50) 10, 30 and 365 days after vaccination. Viremia was evaluated by RT-PCR. Adverse events following immunization (AEFI) were monitored. Primary outcomes were seropositivity and seroconversion rates. Secondary outcomes were antibody geometric mean titers (GMT) and safety.

RESULTS: 154 participants were included: 54 CKD-D, 41 CKD-ND and 59 immunocompetent. Median age was 50, 61 and 47 years, respectively. Ten days after vaccination (D10), seropositivity was significantly lower in CKD (CKD-ND, 62.5%; CKD-D, 48%) than in immunocompetent (86.7%) and CKD had lower GMT. On D30, GMT increased in all groups, without significant differences on seropositivity and GMT between groups. On D365, GMT decreased, but most participants persisted seropositive, without significant differences. On D10, viremia was detected in 28.8% of CKD-D; 32.3% of CKD-ND, and 28.9% of immunocompetent, without significant difference between groups. The CKD participants had lower viremia. Immunocompetent participants more frequently reported AEFI (66.7%) than CKD-ND (48.5%) and CKD-D (48.8%). Most common AEFI were headache (32.7%), myalgia (28.4%) and injection site pain (25.3%).

CONCLUSIONS: Adults with CKD had a robust although delayed neutralizing antibody response to YF vaccine and the vaccine was well-tolerated. The small sample size precluded the detection of small differences in immune response between the groups and the occurrence of rare serious AEFI related to YF vaccine.

articles.title: V-V ECMO for refractory near-fatal asthma: A 12-year single-centre observational study of clinical outcomes and psychological impact.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To review the clinical data of adult patients receiving veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) for near-fatal asthma at a single UK respiratory ECMO centre, including morbidity and mortality follow up.

DESIGN: Retrospective single-centre case series (2013-2025).

SETTING: A specialized UK respiratory ECMO centre.

PARTICIPANTS: 79 adult patients with near-fatal asthma refractory to maximal conventional critical care management including mechanical ventilation.

INTERVENTIONS: Veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.

MEASUREMENTS & MAIN RESULTS: 79 patients (median age 35 years, 53% female and 47% male) were included. Pre-ECMO physiological derangement was profound (median pH 7.05, PaCO2 14.7 kPa). Median ECMO duration was 3 days (IQR 2-4). Survival to ICU discharge and 6-month survival was 98.7%. Complications occurred in 27.8% of patients, most frequently acute kidney injury requiring renal replacement therapy (10.1%). At 6-month follow-up, clinically significant anxiety and depression were present in 27.9% and 20.9% of survivors, respectively, while 37.2% screened positive for post-traumatic stress symptoms.

CONCLUSIONS: Veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) represents an effective rescue therapy for patients with refractory near-fatal asthma, demonstrating excellent short- and long-term survival outcomes when applied in carefully selected cases. The incidence of complications remains acceptable and manageable within this context. The prevalence of anxiety and depression in this cohort appears to be lower than that reported in a published systematic review of the broader ECMO population; however, rates of post-traumatic stress symptoms are comparatively higher.

articles.title: Clinical significance of the COPD assessment test in evaluating treatment response in Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary disease (MAC-PD), sputum culture conversion is a key endpoint but does not fully reflect symptom burden. We evaluated the COPD Assessment Test (CAT) as a patient-reported measure of disease severity and treatment response.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 179 treatment episodes in 174 patients with MAC-PD who continued therapy for at least 12 months. CAT scores were assessed at baseline and at 6 and 12 months. We examined associations of baseline CAT scores with chest computed tomography (CT) scores and sputum culture status, and of CAT changes (Δ6 and Δ12) with the 12-month culture-positive versus culture-negative/sputum-unobtainable classification and a study-defined composite incorporating 12-month radiographic response and the microbiologic course through 24 months.

RESULTS: Baseline CAT scores correlated weakly with CT scores and were higher in baseline culture-positive and poorly controlled episodes. Neither Δ6 nor Δ12 differed by 12-month culture classification. Δ12 was more favorable in well-controlled than in poorly controlled episodes (p = 0.010), but discrimination was limited (area under the curve, 0.646 in all classifiable episodes and 0.682 in those with baseline CAT > 2). In the latter subgroup, an exploratory decrease of at least 3 points showed a sensitivity of 52.0% and a specificity of 71.9%.

CONCLUSIONS: CAT may complement microbiologic and radiographic assessments by capturing patient-reported symptom changes. The limited discriminatory performance does not support the use of CAT alone to classify treatment control.

articles.title: Mechanical fragmentation of polyester textiles for controlled particle generation.
articles.abstract: Mechanical fragmentation can create engineered secondary feedstocks from waste polyester textiles, but its process-property trade-offs remain unclear. This study varied pass number, sieve cassette configuration, and rotation speed using a 100% polyethylene terephthalate (PET) interlock fabric as a model substrate. Particles were characterized by image analysis, sieving, Rosin-Rammler modeling, and SEM. Independent milling trials quantified process performance, and FTIR spectroscopy and alkaline hydrolysis evaluated chemical changes and mass-loss response. At 3000 rpm, increasing passes from C1 to C5 reduced the image-based median equivalent diameter by 35.2% with the 1.5 mm trapezoidal-perforated cassette (B1.5) and by 38.2% with the 10 mm square-perforated cassette (B10). B1.5 sieving median decreased by 59.0%, whereas rotation speeds of 1000-3000 rpm produced no consistent monotonic effect. Five-pass B1.5 and B10 trials yielded material recoveries of 84.75 ± 1.67% and 89.89 ± 1.10%, cumulative dust fractions of 7.57 ± 0.88% and 5.89 ± 0.67%, and laboratory cycle times of 82.09 ± 0.59 and 53.49 ± 0.70 min, respectively. Cutting-mill-only nominal specific electricity demands, estimated from the 5 kW nameplate power, were 11.74 ± 0.09 and 11.58 ± 0.22 kWh/kg. FTIR detected no major changes in characteristic PET bands. Under identical hydrolysis conditions, three-hour mass loss increased from 51.67 ± 2.52% for the original fabric to 78.00 ± 2.00% for A3000 × B1.5 × C5. Results establish laboratory-scale empirical relationships between cutting-mill settings and PET fragment characteristics while revealing trade-offs among size reduction, recovery, process demand, and alkaline-hydrolysis response.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Traditional Chinese Medicine Exercise Therapy for Frailty in Older Adults and Descriptive Summary of Exercise Prescription Characteristics: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate outcome-specific effects of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) exercise therapy on frailty-related outcomes in older adults and descriptively summarize exercise prescription characteristics.

DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis.

SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: Randomized controlled trials involving adults aged 60 years or older with frailty, prefrailty, or eligible cognitive frailty in community, institutional, or clinical settings.

METHODS: Eight databases were searched from inception to March 31, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed the risk of bias. Separate random-effects meta-analyses were conducted for key outcomes using standardized mean differences (SMDs) with Hedges' g correction. Heterogeneity was assessed using τ2 and I2 statistics, with prediction intervals calculated where appropriate. Exercise prescription characteristics were summarized descriptively.

RESULTS: Twenty-one studies were included, with 15 contributing to the main meta-analysis. TCM exercise therapy showed favorable effects on Edmonton Frail Scale scores (SMD, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.04-1.06), Fried frailty phenotype scores (SMD, 2.70; 95% CI, 1.15-4.25), Timed Up and Go performance (SMD, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.17-1.33), Berg Balance Scale scores (SMD, 1.32; 95% CI, 1.00-1.64), and Montreal Cognitive Assessment scores (SMD, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.63-1.41). Gait speed was not significantly improved, and grip strength showed a small, imprecise effect. Heterogeneity was substantial for several outcomes. Tai Chi and Baduanjin were the most frequently represented modalities, whereas reported exercise prescription characteristics varied across studies.

CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: TCM exercise therapy may benefit selected frailty, mobility, balance, and cognitive outcomes, but heterogeneity and limited evidence for several outcomes warrant caution. Exercise prescription characteristics are descriptive and hypothesis generating, not evidence for an optimized frequency, intensity, time, type, volume, and progression prescription.

articles.title: Describing Nurse Practitioners' Prescription Billings for Residents Living in Long-Term Care in Ontario, Canada: A Descriptive Time Trend Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine the prescribing patterns of nurse practitioners (NPs) caring for residents living in long-term care (LTC) homes over time and by resident- and facility-level factors.

DESIGN: A descriptive time trend study was conducted using linked administrative data from Ontario between 2014 and 2024.

SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: All prescription claims for residents living in LTC homes in Ontario.

METHODS: Descriptive statistics summarized prescribing volumes, medication classes, and resident- and facility-level characteristics for each year.

RESULTS: There was a total of 8,720,276 NP prescriptions during the study period. The proportion of prescription billings by NPs increased from 0.92% in 2014 to 6.15% in 2024. Variations were observed by rurality and facility size. The increase in the proportions of NP prescriptions was greater for residents in rural homes (from 0.74% in 2014 to 13.31% in 2024) than for those in urban settings. The increase in the proportion of NP prescriptions was greater in smaller homes (from 0.63% in 2014 to 7.24% in 2024) compared with medium and larger homes.

CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: This study was the first population-level analysis of NP prescribing in Ontario for LTC residents. Findings underscore the evolving contribution of NPs to medication management and reinforce the need for policies that optimize their role in improving quality of care for LTC residents.

articles.title: Persistent Circulating Proteomic Signatures Distinguish Magnetic Resonance Angiography-Defined Carotid Plaque Vulnerability.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Carotid artery luminal stenosis alone may not predict the risk of future neurovascular events. Plaque vulnerability is emerging as an independent predictor of higher risk for a neurovascular event. We evaluated blood proteomics, paired with high-resolution cross-sectional imaging preoperatively. From preoperative and postoperative blood samples, our objective was to identify blood proteins that distinguish patients with vulnerable and non-vulnerable carotid artery plaques.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted an exploratory, single-center proteomic study of 27 consecutive patients undergoing carotid endarterectomy with preoperative 3.0T magnetic resonance angiography with vessel wall imaging. Plaques were classified as vulnerable when magnetic resonance angiography with vessel wall imaging identified at least one high-risk feature: thin fibrous cap, lipid-rich necrotic core, ulceration, intraplaque hemorrhage, or inflammation. Serum samples were analyzed preoperatively and postoperatively using a high-throughput, untargeted proteomics technology (Olink). Differential protein abundance between vulnerable and non-vulnerable groups was assessed separately at each time point.

RESULTS: For both time points, the vulnerable group demonstrated a blood proteomic signature involving diacylglycerol signaling and oxidative stress proteins, including diacylglycerol kinase iota and peroxiredoxin-like 2B, with postoperative vulnerability additionally associated with platelet activation (Ras guanyl releasing protein 2), cytoskeletal remodeling (metastasis suppressor 1), and ribonucleic acid/ribosome-related proteins (Shwachman-Bodian-Diamond syndrome protein, RNA-binding protein with multiple splicing 2, zinc ribbon domain-containing protein 2). Non-vulnerable plaques showed a higher abundance of proteins involved in cellular maintenance and deoxyribonucleic acid repair. Furthermore, the persistence of higher diacylglycerol kinase iota and peroxiredoxin-like 2B in the vulnerable group and X-ray repair cross-complementing protein 2 in the non-vulnerable group at both time points suggests stable, patient-level systemic differences detectable in blood, despite plaque removal.

CONCLUSIONS: Serum proteomics identified distinct systemic pathways associated with cross-sectional imaging carotid plaque vulnerability, highlighting diacylglycerol signaling, oxidative stress, and platelet activation as candidate mechanisms and new biomarker candidates for risk stratification, symptom surveillance, and targeted medical interventions.

articles.title: Surgeons' Immediate Postoperative Prediction After Major Emergency Abdominal Surgery.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Major emergency abdominal surgery carries high morbidity and mortality, making accurate risk stratification important. Whether surgeons' immediate postoperative clinical judgment predicts outcomes and how it compares with established surgical risk models remains poorly characterized.

METHODS: Prospective single-center cohort of 411 patients undergoing major emergency abdominal surgery (February 2024-June 2025). Immediately after surgery, the operating surgeon estimated 30-d mortality (ordinal 10% intervals) and the risk of complications (0-10 scale). Discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC]) and calibration (observed-to-expected ratio, calibration slope and intercept, Brier score) were assessed. Mortality discrimination was compared with National Emergency Laparotomy Audit and Portsmouth Physiological and Operative Severity Score for the enUmeration of Mortality and Morbidity using the DeLong test.

RESULTS: Thirty-day mortality was 11% (47/411). Surgeon-estimated risk showed good discrimination for mortality (AUC: 0.89; 95% confidence interval: 0.85-0.94), comparable to National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (0.90) and Portsmouth Physiological and Operative Severity Score for the enUmeration of Mortality and Morbidity (0.86; P = 0.83 and P = 0.30). Surgeons systematically overestimated absolute mortality (mean predicted: 23% versus observed: 11%; observed-to-expected: 0.48; intercept: -1.17; slope: 1.20). For complications, discrimination was good for sepsis/multi-organ failure (AUC 0.81) and acceptable for intensive care unit admission (0.78) and cardiac complications (0.78), but poor for reoperation (0.62) and mechanical bowel obstruction (0.62), and absent for prolonged paralytic bowel dysfunction (0.51). Higher estimated risk was associated with increased odds of complications. Predicted discharge destination agreed moderately with observed (accuracy 74%; weighted κ 0.61).

CONCLUSIONS: Surgeons' immediate postoperative assessment showed discriminatory performance of a similar magnitude to established models but systematically overestimated absolute risk and performed better for systemic than procedure-specific complications. This bedside estimate may aid early risk stratification but requires external validation before clinical use.

articles.title: Polystyrene nanoplastics exacerbate hepatic insulin resistance and glycolipid metabolism disorders in high‑fat diet‑induced obese mice.
articles.abstract: Nanoplastics are emerging environmental contaminants with potential metabolic health risks, yet their chronic effects on high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity‑related metabolic disorders remain poorly understood. This study investigated whether long‑term oral exposure to polystyrene nanoplastics (PS‑NPs) aggravates hepatic insulin resistance and glycolipid metabolism disorders in HFD‑induced obese mice, and elucidated the underlying molecular mechanisms. Male C57BL/6 J mice were fed a HFD for 32 weeks with concurrent oral gavage of PS‑NPs (10 mg/kg, every 3 days). PS‑NPs co‑exposure significantly exacerbated body weight gain, fasting hyperglycemia, glucose intolerance, and insulin resistance compared with HFD alone. Hepatic histopathology revealed aggravated steatosis, inflammatory infiltration, and glycogen depletion in PS‑NPs‑treated obese mice. Mechanistically, PS‑NPs further suppressed hepatic protein levels of phosphorylated AKT (Ser473), insulin receptor (INSR), and glucose transporter 2 (GLUT2), while upregulating mRNA expression of gluconeogenic regulators (FOXO1, PCK1) and lipogenic genes (SREBF1, ACACA). In vitro, using HepG2 cells with high‑concentration insulin‑induced insulin resistance, PS‑NPs reduced insulin‑stimulated AKT phosphorylation, decreased INSR and GLUT2 protein expression, upregulated G6PC1 and ACACA, and downregulated SLC2A2, suggesting a cell‑autonomous sensitization to metabolic stress. Gut microbiota analysis revealed that PS‑NPs co-exposure further reduced microbial diversity and increased the Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio in HFD-fed mice. Collectively, these findings indicate that HFD-induced obesity creates a metabolically vulnerable state that amplifies nanoplastic-induced hepatic insulin resistance and glycolipid dysregulation via interference with insulin signaling and transcriptional reprogramming. This positions chronic nanoplastic exposure as an underappreciated environmental driver in the obesity-diabetes nexus, highlighting the need for future risk assessment that considers host metabolic vulnerability and diet-pollutant interactions.

articles.title: Clinical profile, risk factors, and one-year outcomes of atrial fibrillation in a native West African setting: Insights from the Ibadan atrial fibrillation registry.
articles.journal: Journal of the National Medical Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We sought to describe the clinical profile, risk factors, management, and one-year outcomes of atrial fibrillation in a tertiary hospital in Nigeria METHODS: The Ibadan AF registry enrolled consecutive patients with AF from January 1, 2016, to September 30, 2023, at Nigeria's oldest and largest tertiary hospital. The CHA2DS2VASC score was used for stroke risk classification. The participants were followed up for 12 months (at one month, 6 months, and 12 months) after enrolment through clinic visits or telephone calls, and supplementary data were obtained from medical notes. Stepwise multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to identify independent predictors of each of the study outcomes from the variables that were significant in univariable analyses.

RESULTS: Three hundred and fifty-seven patients were enrolled; median age was 65 years (25th and 75th percentiles = 61.6 and 64.6 years; minimum and maximum years = 19 and 95 years), and 52.9% were male. Hypertension was the most common risk factor (80.7%), and heart failure was the most common mode of presentation (70%). Sixty-one percent of patients had permanent AF, 25.0% had persistent AF, and 14% had paroxysmal AF. Most patients (78.4%) were on oral anticoagulants. Most received rate control with beta-blockers (75%) and/or digoxin (44%), and 70% achieved adequate rate control. At the end of one-year follow-up, 251 (70.3%) were alive, 31(8.7%) were hospitalized, and 88(24.6%) died. The independent predictors of composite outcomes (rehospitalization and/or all-cause mortality) were the Kanofsky score (aHR. 0.44, [95% CI: 0.21-0.92, p = 0.028] for score of 50-70 and (aHR. 0.26, [95% CI: 0.12-0.58, p = 0.001] for score of 80-100(Reference. 0-40), socioeconomic class (aHR. 0.54 [95% CI: 0.30-0.98),p = 0.041]) for middle socioeconomic class (Reference- low socioeconomic class) and use of amiodarone (aHR.1.77 [95% CI:1.00-3.13),p = 0.049]) CONCLUSION: Hypertension is the commonest risk factor for AF in this cohort, and >80% of study participants with AF require anticoagulation. Mortality at 12 months is high due to severe structural disease and high comorbidity burden. Efforts are needed to control and treat risk factors, heart failure, and comorbidities in AF management in our setting.

articles.title: Increased risk of infection and reoperation following total knee arthroplasty in patients under 40.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is increasingly performed in younger patient populations. This study aimed to compare perioperative outcomes between patients under 40 and those over 65, stratified by surgical indication.

METHODS: This retrospective study used the Epic Cosmos dataset to identify primary TKA patients under 40 years old (n = 3,177) or over 65 (n = 698,662). Patients were stratified by surgical indication (primary osteoarthritis, post-traumatic osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, avascular necrosis, and multiple indications) using ICD-10 codes. Outcomes included superficial wound dehiscence, infection, readmission, and ipsilateral reoperation, assessed at 90 days and 1 year postoperatively. Differences between age groups were assessed using adjusted odds ratios (95% confidence intervals) derived from multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for sex, body mass index, comorbidity burden, insurance status and smoking status with significance set at p < 0.05. A sensitivity analysis in the overall cohort tested the interaction between age group and surgical indication.

RESULTS: Surgical indications differed significantly between cohorts (standardized proportions difference 0.939, p < 0.001), with osteoarthritis accounting for 97.8% of cases in patients >65 compared to 64.6% in patients <40. Younger patients had higher rates of post-traumatic osteoarthritis (2.4% vs 0.1%) and multiple diagnoses (20.7% vs 1.6%). Among patients with osteoarthritis, those under 40 had significantly higher 90-day odds of infection (OR 3.16, 95% CI 2.29-4.35), superficial wound dehiscence (OR 1.91, 95% CI 1.34-2.72) and ipsilateral reoperation (OR 3.91, 95% CI 3.34-4.58), which persisted at 1 year (infection OR 2.79, 95% CI 2.13-3.67; superficial wound dehiscence OR 1.91, 95% CI 1.41-2.59; reoperation OR 3.44, 95% CI 3.00-3.94). Patients under 40 with multiple diagnoses had elevated odds of infection at 90 days (OR 2.06, 95% CI 1.15-3.69) and 1 year (OR 1.80, 95% CI 1.09-2.95), and ipsilateral reoperation at 90 days (OR 3.10, 95% CI 2.25-4.25) and 1 year (OR 2.71, 95% CI 2.06-3.55). In the overall cohort, the effect of age differed significantly by surgical indication for all outcomes except superficial wound dehiscence.

CONCLUSION: Patients under 40 undergoing Total Knee Arthroplasty are at increased risk for prosthetic joint infection, superficial wound problems and ipsilateral reoperation at 90 days and 1 year when compared to those over the age of 65, independent of smoking status and comorbidity burden.
