Those with multiple indications for surgery are also at increased risk for infection and same-side reoperation at both time points.

articles.title: Mapping the evidence on implementation of clinical decision support systems in nurses' reverse triage decisions during disaster surges: A scoping review with a proposed conceptual framework.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Emergency and critical care nurses are increasingly required to make complex, time-sensitive decisions across intensive care unit (ICU), emergency department, prehospital, and telephone triage settings, and clinical decision support systems (CDSSs) have been proposed as a technological strategy to support this process. However, the extent to which CDSSs influence nurses' decision-making time, accuracy, and confidence remains uncertain-particularly for reverse triage during disaster surges, an area of growing importance for emergency nursing preparedness worldwide. No previous review has synthesised evidence at the intersection of CDSS technology and reverse triage. This scoping review aimed to map existing evidence on the implementation of CDSSs in nurses' decision-making across ICU and triage settings, and to identify evidence gaps concerning reverse triage during disaster surges, in order to propose a novel conceptual framework-the CDSS-RT (Clinical Decision Support System for Reverse Triage) framework.

METHODS: A scoping review following JBI methodology and PRISMA-ScR was conducted and prospectively registered on the Open Science Framework (OSF registration: DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/VKRHU). Systematic searches across MEDLINE, Scopus, CINAHL, Embase, and the Cochrane Library identified English-language studies published up to January 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. An evidence gap map was constructed to visualise literature distribution and gaps.

RESULTS: From 4218 records, 22 studies met inclusion criteria, published between 2009 and 2026 across 13 countries. CDSSs were predominantly knowledge-based, with growing use of machine learning and artificial intelligence. CDSSs improved triage accuracy by 7-23 percentage points, reduced cognitive workload, and enhanced confidence, although alert fatigue, increased response time, and limited system integration were common barriers. The evidence gap map revealed a critical absence of studies addressing CDSSs in reverse triage during disaster surges.

PROPOSED CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK: The CDSS-RT framework, grounded in the CDS Five Rights, CFIR, and Dual-Process Theory, integrates six components: (1) knowledge base; (2) hybrid reasoning engine; (3) user cognitive factors; (4) implementation readiness; (5) context-sensitive design; and (6) multi-level outcome metrics.

CONCLUSION: Conclusion and implications: CDSSs show considerable promise for nursing decision-making in ICU and triage settings relevant to emergency nursing practice internationally. The proposed CDSS-RT framework provides a structured foundation for future CDSS-assisted reverse triage research and system design.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Endoplasmic reticulum stress in diabetes mellitus: A comprehensive review of emerging insights and recent progress" [Diabetes & Metabol Syndr: Clin Res Rev 20 (5) (2026) 103-420].
Maternal exposure to extreme temperatures and congenital heart disease: Assessing independent effects and interaction with residential green space.
articles.journal: International journal of hygiene and environmental health
articles.abstract: Research on the association between temperature and congenital heart disease (CHD) is relatively limited. This study aims to evaluate the effects of extreme temperature events on CHD morbidity, utilizing apparent temperature data. We conducted a 1:1 matched case-control study in Tianjin, China, including 1540 mother-infant pairs with CHD and their corresponding controls. We calculated maternal exposure to apparent temperature and Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) exposures during weeks 3 to 8 of gestation. Conditional logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between extreme temperature events and CHD, and to assess their additive interactive effects with NDVI. Maternal exposure to extreme cold events during pregnancy significantly increased the risk of CHD in offspring (moderate extreme cold event: OR = 3.11). Pregnant women exposed to low NDVI levels (≤0.25) exhibited consistently higher CHD risks. Notably, the risk of CHD increased sharply during exposure to extreme cold events (OR up to 7.32), and a suggestive positive interactive trend was observed between severe extreme heat and low NDVI (RERI = 1.60), though it did not reach statistical significance. Furthermore, pregnant women whose last menstrual period (LMP) occurred during the cold season exhibited greater susceptibility to extreme cold, whereas those with an LMP in the warm season were more vulnerable to the adverse effects of extreme heat. Maternal exposure to extreme temperature events during weeks 3 to 8 of gestation significantly increases the risk of CHD in offspring.

articles.title: Non-invasive quantification of lower airway antigen-specific antibodies using exhaled breath particles - an observational proof-of-concept study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advancements in mucosal vaccine development highlight the urgent need for practical methods to assess immune responses in both upper and lower airways. Although nasal sampling is increasingly standardised, a non-invasive technique for directly assessing antigen-specific antibodies in the distal airways has been lacking.

METHODS: We used Particles in Exhaled Air (PExA), a non-invasive method capturing aerosolised respiratory tract lining fluid (RTLF) from the distal airways, to quantify antigen-specific IgA and IgG. Antibodies were measured in paired serum, nasal secretions, and PExA samples from 28 healthcare workers during spring 2025, including 18 with RT-qPCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2, influenza A (H1N1), or respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection.

FINDINGS: Antigen-specific IgA and IgG measurements in PExA samples showed low variability (median CVs: spike-IgA 3.7%, H1-IgA 7.2%, RSV pre-F-IgA 5.3%). Strong correlations (Spearman's rho >0.85, p < 0.0001) were observed between PExA and serum IgG, which may be consistent with a systemic contribution to lower-airway IgG levels. In contrast, IgA correlations were more modest, which may reflect local IgA production in the lungs. IgG and IgA correlated between PExA and nasal secretions, while the IgA/IgG ratio was higher in nasal secretions (median 5.0 vs 0.6, p < 0.0001), consistent with expected isotype distribution in upper and lower airways.

INTERPRETATION: This study demonstrates the feasibility of non-invasive measurement of antigen-specific antibodies in the lower airways. Our approach proposes a framework for assessing lower-airway immunity and supporting next-generation mucosal vaccine development.

FUNDING: This study was funded by the European Research Council, the Swedish Society for Medical Research, and the Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation.

articles.title: Assessment of mental health literacy among undergraduate radiography students in Ghana: A single-centre cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Mental health literacy (MHL) is a critical determinant of early recognition of mental disorders, appropriate help-seeking behaviour, and stigma reduction. Undergraduate radiography students are vulnerable to mental health challenges; however, evidence on their MHL in Ghana remains scarce. This study assessed MHL level and associated factors among radiography students.

METHODS: A quantitative cross-sectional design was employed. Data were collected from 201 students using a structured, web-based questionnaire comprising socio-demographic items, perceived influencing factors of MHL, and an adapted MHL Scale (MHLS). Total MHLS scores ranged from 66 to 133, with higher scores indicating greater literacy. Descriptive statistics and inferential analyses were conducted using SPSS version 27.0, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: The mean MHL score was 101.69 (SD = 11.31, 95% CI: 100.12-103.26). Subscale analysis showed comparatively higher recognition (M = 29.15, SD = 4.25) and attitude (M = 53.35, SD = 7.97) scores, with a comparatively lower knowledge score (M = 19.18, SD = 3.23). The adapted scale demonstrated acceptable internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.795). No statistically significant differences in MHL scores were observed across age, sex, academic level, living situation, or socioeconomic status (all p > 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Undergraduate radiography students demonstrated relatively strong recognition and attitude scores but a comparative gap in knowledge of mental health risk factors and self-management strategies.

IMPLICATION FOR PRACTICE: The findings suggest radiography training should integrate structured, progressive mental health education targeting knowledge of risk factors and self-management strategies prepare students for the psychological demands of clinical practice and to support empathetic, patient-centred care.

articles.title: Syphilis infection and autoimmune disease: A matched case-control study with clinical follow-up in 1,042 patients.
articles.abstract: Syphilis has long been recognized to induce various autoantibodies, yet the prevalence, specificity, and clinical significance of these serological abnormalities remain poorly characterized due to limited sample sizes, incomplete antibody panels, and a lack of longitudinal verification for autoimmune disease (AID) outcomes. In this large-scale retrospective matched case-control study conducted at Zhongshan Hospital of Xiamen University from 2020 to 2023, we evaluated 14 autoantibodies in 1042 syphilis patients and 2084 age- and sex-matched non-syphilis controls, and tracked AID diagnoses through December 2025. The overall autoantibody positivity rate was significantly higher in syphilis patients than in controls (38.5% vs. 23.7%; adjusted OR = 2.02, 95% CI: 1.72-2.37, P < 0.001), with the strongest associations observed for anti-SSB (aOR = 4.57), anti-SSA (aOR = 3.16), and ANA (aOR = 2.60), findings that remained consistent across all age groups and both sexes. During follow-up, 88 syphilis patients (8.4%) developed 16 distinct AIDs, most commonly Sjögren's disease (26.1%) and rheumatoid arthritis (21.6%), with disease-specific autoantibody profiles mirroring those of primary AIDs. Syphilis-associated autoantibodies are not an incidental serological phenomenon but rather a clinically meaningful signal of confirmed autoimmune disease, highlighting the urgent need for autoimmune evaluation in autoantibody-positive syphilis patients.

articles.title: Prevention of mpox by JYNNEOS vaccination: a case-control study comparing test-negative and alternative-disease control populations.
articles.abstract: Risk-based vaccine recommendations complicate observational studies of vaccine effectiveness (VE), since recipients and non-recipients may differ in infection risk and likelihood of testing. For JYNNEOS-recommended for men who have sex with men at high mpox risk-prior studies have used differing control populations to estimate VE, with uncertain comparability. We conducted a multi-armed case-control study enrolling mpox cases (N=198), monkeypox virus (MPXV)-negative controls (N=208), and gonorrhea controls (N=155) reported to the California Department of Public Health between November 2022 and October 2024, conducting telephone interviews to capture behavioral risk data typically absent from surveillance and administrative records. Among recipients of 2 pre-exposure JYNNEOS doses, adjusted VE was 89.9% (95% CI, 69.6-96.7%) versus test-negative controls and 92.0% (70.6-97.8%) versus gonorrhea controls. Without behavioral adjustment, however, VE estimates using MPXV-negative controls were lower (50.4-65.4%) than those using gonorrhea controls (61.3-71.3%). Controls diagnosed with an alternative sexually transmitted infection may offer a better comparison group than test-negative controls for JYNNEOS VE studies based on disease surveillance or administrative records, although collection of risk factor data may be necessary to mitigate bias under either design.

articles.title: Associations of Health Literacy and eHealth Literacy With Patient Portal Access and Use: Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective patient portal access and use require both digital navigation and understanding of clinical information. Health literacy and eHealth literacy reflect these different demands. Although the 2 constructs overlap, prior research often treats them as interchangeable. It remains unclear whether health literacy and eHealth literacy are associated differently across stages of portal engagement and patterns of portal use. A systematic review is therefore needed to identify consistent patterns across studies.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to synthesize associations of health literacy and eHealth literacy with patient portal access, general use, feature-specific use, and frequency of use.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Scopus, CINAHL, PsycINFO, Web of Science, and Embase from inception to March 2026 using keywords related to health literacy, eHealth literacy, patient portals, and portal access or use. We included English-language peer-reviewed articles and gray literature involving adults who used real-world patient portals, measured health literacy or eHealth literacy using validated instruments, and reported quantitative associations with portal access or use. Because studies differed substantially in literacy instruments, portal outcomes, and outcome measures, we used direction-based vote counting, complemented by narrative synthesis. Reporting followed the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses) statement, whereas synthesis methods were guided by the Cochrane Handbook for synthesis without meta-analysis. For full-text, peer-reviewed journal articles, we assessed the risk of bias by using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tools.

RESULTS: Among 1107 screened studies, 30 met the inclusion criteria. Of these, 17 examined health literacy only, 10 examined eHealth literacy only, and 3 examined both constructs in the same sample. Studies focused far more on portal use than on portal access and emphasized general portal use over feature-specific outcomes. Any use was assessed more often than frequency of use. Nine of 10 directionally codable eHealth literacy studies of general portal use showed lower use among individuals with lower eHealth literacy, whereas health literacy findings for general portal use were mixed. Lower health literacy showed a more consistent pattern of lower portal access and several feature-specific outcomes, although comparable eHealth literacy evidence for these outcomes was limited. Most studies met the majority of JBI criteria, although most measured portal use via self-report rather than objective system data.

CONCLUSIONS: Nearly every directionally codable eHealth literacy study reported lower portal use among patients with lower eHealth literacy. Lower health literacy showed similar patterns for portal access and several feature-specific outcomes. These consistent associations point to literacy-related disparities at multiple stages of portal engagement, although comparable within-sample evidence remains limited. Future studies should measure both constructs in the same sample, use comparable modeling approaches, use objective portal log data when possible, and distinguish access, any use, frequency, and feature-specific behaviors to identify where literacy-related disparities emerge.

articles.title: Use of Large Language Models for Automated Short-Answer Question Grading in Second-Cycle Medical Education: Performance and Consistency Evaluation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Short-answer questions (SAQs) effectively assess higher-order reasoning skills in medical education but face challenges in scalability due to time-intensive manual grading and concerns about interrater reliability. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) may offer a solution through automated assessment.

OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated the performance and consistency of LLMs-ChatGPT, Claude Sonnet 4, and Mistral Pro-compared with those of human graders for SAQ grading in hepatology and gastroenterology.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed SAQs from hepatology and gastroenterology examinations at Sorbonne University, Paris, France (2023-2025). Three human evaluators (2 hepatogastroenterologists and 1 radiologist) independently graded all responses twice, with the majority consensus score serving as the reference standard. Six LLMs were evaluated: ChatGPT (GPT-4o, GPT-4.5, GPT-4o3, and GPT-5), Claude Sonnet 4, and Mistral Pro. Each LLM graded all responses twice using standardized prompts, including questions, model answers, grading guidelines, and scoring rubrics. Agreement was assessed using quadratic weighted kappa (QWK), Cohen κ, the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), and the mean absolute error (MAE) for interhuman, intrahuman, LLM-versus-human, and intramodel comparisons.

RESULTS: A total of 902 student responses from 12 SAQs were included and analyzed. Interhuman grader agreement was almost perfect (QWK 0.90-0.92; ICC 0.90-0.92; MAE 0.05-0.07). Claude Sonnet 4 and GPT-4o3 demonstrated near-human-level performance when compared with the majority vote of human evaluators (Claude Sonnet 4: QWK 0.88-0.90; ICC 0.88-0.90; MAE 0.06-0.07 and GPT-4o3: QWK 0.82-0.89; ICC 0.82-0.89; MAE 0.07-0.09). GPT-5 showed substantial agreement (QWK 0.77-0.79). Mistral Pro and older ChatGPT versions performed poorly (QWK <0.63). Intramodel consistency was the highest for Claude Sonnet 4 (QWK 0.93), approaching the best human intrarater reliability. Agreement did not correlate with prompt design choices (number of examples or minimum word count).

CONCLUSIONS: Advanced LLMs, particularly Claude Sonnet 4 and GPT-4o3, demonstrated near-human-level grading performance, supporting their potential use as assistive tools in SAQ grading. However, performance varied by model, and agreement alone does not ensure educational validity. Until broader multicenter validation is conducted across diverse domains, stakes, and question formats-along with safeguards for bias, privacy, and model drift-LLMs should augment rather than replace human faculty graders.

articles.title: Consensus on Core Competencies of Undergraduate Life Sciences Students for Entry-Level Participation in Clinical Trials: RAND-Modified Delphi Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The competencies required of life sciences graduates to participate in clinical trial research teams are poorly defined.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to establish a structured consensus on the core competencies that students must acquire during their degree programs.

METHODS: A RAND-modified Delphi procedure was conducted using 2 rounds of online questionnaires, a virtual meeting, and a final review. The process began with a questionnaire completed by experts from the University of Córdoba and the Maimonides Institute for Biomedical Research of Córdoba (3 principal investigators, 1 study coordinator, and 1 data manager). The 48 competencies initially proposed were reviewed by a panel of 18 experts representing 6 clinical research groups from universities and biomedical research institutes in Andalusia, Spain. The relevance of each proposed competency was rated on a 9-point Likert scale. Competencies were accepted if they achieved a mean score of 7 points or higher and at least 70% of ratings in the top tertile (scores of 7-9).

RESULTS: The 18 experts achieved 100% consensus on a panel of 48 competencies organized into 3 sections: fundamental concepts (n=23, 47.9% of the competencies), clinical trial development (n=23, 47.9% of the competencies), and certifications (n=2, 4.2% of the competencies).

CONCLUSIONS: This consensus defines the core competencies required of undergraduate life sciences students for entry-level participation in clinical trial research. It also provides a framework for designing training strategies in both undergraduate and graduate programs of study.

articles.title: Outcomes Associated With a WhatsApp-Based Telehealth Education Program and Remote Follow-Up on Blood Pressure, Medication Adherence, and Self-Care: Formative Quasi-Experimental Pilot Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a common chronic condition associated with substantial morbidity globally. In Jordan, many patients struggle with sustained medication adherence and self-management, highlighting a need for accessible care strategies. Low-cost platforms such as WhatsApp may support telehealth education and remote follow-up, although formative pilot data are needed to assess feasibility in this context.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate within-participant changes in blood pressure, medication adherence, self-care behaviors, and hypertension-related knowledge from baseline to postintervention among adults with primary hypertension who participated in a formative WhatsApp-based telehealth education program with structured remote follow-up in Jordan.

METHODS: A quasi-experimental, single-group pretest-posttest pilot study was conducted. In total, 40 adults (aged 28-60 years) with primary hypertension were recruited from a university hospital. The 8-week hybrid mobile health (mHealth) intervention involved training participants in home blood pressure monitoring, delivering daily educational multimedia messages via WhatsApp (covering diet, exercise, and medication), and conducting biweekly structured telephone consultations with a nurse and dietitian. Validated tools (Hill-Bone Scale, Blood Pressure Self-Care Scale, and Blood Pressure Knowledge Scale) and electronic sphygmomanometers were used at baseline and after the intervention. Data were analyzed using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.

RESULTS: All 40 participants completed the 8-week pilot and contributed paired baseline and postintervention outcome data. Postintervention scores were higher for hypertension knowledge (r=0.840; P<.001) and self-care behaviors (r=0.524; P=.001); medication adherence scores were lower, indicating better adherence (r=0.805; P<.001); and systolic (r=.434; P=.006) and diastolic blood pressure (r=.684; P<.001) were lower than those at baseline.

CONCLUSIONS: This formative single-group pilot identified favorable pre-post differences in blood pressure, medication adherence, self-care behaviors, and hypertension-related knowledge among a selected sample of adults with primary hypertension. Because there was no control group, the findings do not establish intervention effectiveness or causality and should be interpreted as preliminary evidence supporting further controlled evaluation.

articles.title: Estimand Ambiguity, Time to Surgery, and the Limits of Causal Inference in Anesthesia Comparisons for Geriatric Hip Arthroplasty.
Digital Resilience-Based Course-Game Sequential Intervention for Social Participation in Stroke Survivors: Development and Usability Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Social participation is a key goal of stroke rehabilitation, yet effective interventions remain limited. Existing approaches focus largely on functional training or general psychological support, rarely targeting resilience as a modifiable mechanism for enhancing social participation. Most interventions are delivered face-to-face, limiting accessibility and scalability. A theory-driven digital intervention that integrates resilience training with contextualized practice may offer a promising pathway to support social reintegration in stroke survivors.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop a theory-driven, digital resilience-based course-game sequential intervention for improving social participation in stroke survivors and to evaluate its usability among the target population.

METHODS: This was an intervention development and usability study. Following the first 4 steps of intervention mapping, we completed the following steps: (1) conducted a needs assessment based on prior empirical evidence identifying psychological resilience as a key determinant of social participation; (2) defined performance and change objectives grounded in the Kumpfer resilience framework, which delineates 5 protective factors (cognitive, emotional, spiritual, behavioral, and physical); (3) selected theory-based methods and practical applications; and (4) developed an intervention prototype through 4 phases: initial design integrating course learning and gamified experiential modules, expert review and refinement by an 8-member panel, development of the digital system via a WeChat mini-program, and finalization of comprehensive intervention scripts. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling from a rehabilitation hospital in Shanghai, China. Usability was evaluated with 14 stroke survivors through 5 representative tasks, the System Usability Scale (SUS), and semistructured qualitative interviews. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, and qualitative data were analyzed using conventional content analysis.

RESULTS: The intervention comprised 2 sequential modules: a 7-session course learning module targeting 5 resilience factors, delivered weekly via narrative audio and multimodal content, and a gamified experiential module featuring a supermarket shopping scenario that enabled contextualized skill application. Each weekly course session was designed to last approximately 60 minutes. The duration of a single game session was 20 minutes. Participants had a mean age of 65.4 (SD 9.75) years, and 78.6% (11/14) had experienced an ischemic stroke. All participants completed the usability tasks successfully. The mean SUS score was 73.6 (SD 12.2, 95% CI 66.5-80.6; median 77.5, IQR 61.3-80.6), indicating good usability. Qualitative feedback revealed 3 themes: perceived ease of use and accessibility, perceived usefulness and engagement, and suggestions for improvement.

CONCLUSIONS: This study systematically developed a theory-driven, digital course-game sequential intervention that is innovative in targeting psychological resilience as a core mechanism for social participation, distinguishing it from conventional function-focused or generic resilience approaches. By integrating systematic course learning with contextualized gamified practice, it offers a scalable, low-burden tool that addresses key gaps in stroke rehabilitation. These findings support progression to feasibility and efficacy testing through randomized controlled trials in real-world settings.

articles.title: NICU Nurses' Perceptions of Early Skin-to-Skin Contact With Extremely Preterm Infants: A National Survey.
articles.journal: Advances in neonatal care : official journal of the National Association of Neonatal Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early skin-to-skin contact (SSC) is an evidence-based care practice with well-documented benefits for preterm infants and their parents. Among extremely preterm infants, implementation of early SSC remains variable across neonatal intensive care units (NICUs), despite growing evidence supporting its safety. Nurses play a central role in facilitating SSC, and their perceptions and perceived barriers may influence its implementation.

PURPOSE: To describe NICU nurses' perceptions of early SSC for extremely preterm infants and to identify perceived barriers to its implementation in neonatal intensive care settings.

METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional study using a web-based survey was conducted among NICU nurses in Finnish university hospitals. A total of 148 nurses responded, and the data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and one-way analysis of variance.

RESULTS: Most nurses held positive perceptions toward early SSC, whereas most considered it not feasible for all extremely preterm infants, and many reported safety-related and family-related concerns. Perceived barriers varied significantly between NICUs (P < .001) and by NICU experience (P = .018), with higher barriers among nurses with 2-5 years of experience. Early SSC was not perceived by most nurses to increase workload.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE AND RESEARCH: Consistent implementation of early SSC appears to depend on unit-level practices and nurses' experience. Clear clinical guidance, staff education, and parental support may facilitate its integration into routine neonatal care, whereas further research is needed to identify effective implementation strategies.

articles.title: Context-Dependent Clinical Narrative Signals of Renal Function Deterioration in Cross-Language Settings: Retrospective Multicohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) classifies chronic kidney disease (CKD) using categories based on both glomerular filtration rate and albuminuria. Structured measures remain essential but may not capture contextual clinical concerns documented in narrative records.

OBJECTIVE: This study examined whether text-derived clinical-status language features in clinician notes were associated with deterioration in renal function in independent Greek- and English-language clinical cohorts.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a Greek general-nephrology cohort (314 patients; 10,306 estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] measurements) and an independent English-language Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) replication cohort. The Greek primary analysis used a linear mixed effects model over a follow-up period of up to 1797 days. The MIMIC-IV primary analysis used a 90-day, patient-level fixed-horizon competing-outcome model (N=87,533). Separate analyses of Greek and MIMIC-IV data evaluated discrimination, calibration, and sensitivity to alternative feature specifications.

RESULTS: In the Greek cohort, a 1-SD higher negativity was associated with lower eGFR (β=-3.273 mL/min/1.73 m², 95% CI -5.049 to -1.498; P<.001) and a more negative time trajectory (time-by-score β=-1.324, 95% CI -2.553 to -0.096; P=.035). In MIMIC-IV, a 1-SD higher negative-vs-reassuring polarity contrast was associated with renal deterioration (relative risk ratio [RRR]=1.090, 95% CI 1.070-1.110; P<.001). Within eGFR G categories, polarity-score areas under the curve (AUCs) were 0.506 to 0.552 using discharge eGFR and 0.518 to 0.534 using the worst observed eGFR. Discrimination for renal deterioration remained modest (one-vs-rest AUC=0.6134, 95% CI 0.6092-0.6175), and adding both natural language processing (NLP) features to the clinical model increased AUC by only 0.0018 (95% CI 0.0010-0.0025).

CONCLUSIONS: Independently constructed clinical-language measures were associated with renal function deterioration across two languages and health care settings. The findings support cross-language replication of an association signal, not formal external validation, measurement equivalence, or clinically useful stand-alone prediction.

articles.title: Risk-Stratified Predictors of Clinical Progression in Adult Orbital Cellulitis: A 15-Year Cohort.
articles.abstract: The purpose of this study was to characterize clinical features, risk factors, imaging patterns, microbiology, and outcomes of adults with orbital cellulitis (OC), and to identify predictors of disease severity and surgical intervention. The authors performed a retrospective cohort study of adults greater than or equal to 18 years with clinically and radiographically confirmed OC admitted to 2 academic centers between January 2010 and March 2025 (n=176). Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of subperiosteal abscess (SPA), intracranial extension (ICE), and surgical intervention; χ2 tests, analysis of variance, and t tests were used for secondary analyses. Mean age was 47.5±18.8 years and 67.6% were male. Diabetes was present in 17.0% and was associated with older age and longer hospitalization. Imaging demonstrated SPA in 24.4%, intraorbital abscess in 10.2%, and ICE in 4.5%. Sinusitis and younger age were independent predictors of SPA; diabetes and older age were independent predictors of ICE. Overall, 58.0% required surgical intervention, with diabetes and sinusitis as independent predictors, and most patients with both comorbidities required operative treatment. Recent trauma was associated with greater surgical need and significantly longer length of stay. Staphylococcus spp. predominated on culture (45.8%), with methicillin-resistant S. aureus accounting for 15.0%. Fungal isolates occurred exclusively in diabetic hosts. Severe vision loss occurred in 22 patients, and mortality occurred in 5. Adult OC demonstrates distinct host-factor-driven patterns of severity. Diabetes and older age independently predict ICE and surgical intervention, while sinusitis predicts SPA in younger patients. These risk profiles may improve triage, guide empiric antimicrobial selection, and support timely surgical consultation.

articles.title: TAVR in Patients with Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: For patients with moderate aortic stenosis, current guidelines recommend clinical surveillance with echocardiographic assessment every 1 or 2 years. Whether transcatheter aortic-valve replacement (TAVR) will improve outcomes in these patients remains unknown.

METHODS: We conducted an international, open-label, randomized trial to evaluate whether TAVR will result in better outcomes than clinical surveillance among patients with moderate aortic stenosis with at least one at-risk feature (i.e., a symptom or structural or functional abnormality that has been shown to be associated with faster disease progression or adverse cardiovascular outcomes). The patients were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo transfemoral TAVR with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance. The primary effectiveness end point was a composite of death from any cause or a heart-failure event with or without hospitalization at 2 years. Superiority testing was performed in the intention-to-treat population.

RESULTS: A total of 744 patients underwent randomization: 373 patients were assigned to the TAVR group and 371 to the clinical-surveillance group. The mean age of patients was 78 years, 39.1% were women, and 45.6% were at low surgical risk. The mean aortic-valve area was 1.2 cm2, and the mean aortic-valve peak velocity was 3.3 m per second. At 2 years, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients with a primary effectiveness end-point event was 16.7% in the TAVR group and 23.9% in the clinical-surveillance group (risk difference, -7.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -13.1 to -1.3; P = 0.02 for superiority). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients who died from any cause was 8.4% in the TAVR group and 7.3% in the clinical-surveillance group; the estimates for a heart-failure event were 10.8% and 19.0%, respectively. The incidence of procedure-related adverse events did not differ meaningfully between the patients in the TAVR group and those in the clinical-surveillance group who underwent aortic-valve replacement.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with moderate aortic stenosis and at-risk features, a strategy of TAVR was superior to clinical surveillance in lowering the incidence of death or a heart-failure event at 2 years. (Funded by Edwards Lifesciences; PROGRESS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04889872.).

articles.title: Management of Moderate Aortic Stenosis in Older Adults - The P in PICOT.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine

articles.title: Inhibitory effects of Fucoidan on Muscovy duck-origin parvovirus in vitro and in vivo.
articles.journal: Avian pathology : journal of the W.V.P.A
articles.abstract: Muscovy duck-origin goose parvovirus (MDGPV) is a highly pathogenic viral pathogen that causes severe intestinal embolism and high mortality in Muscovy ducks, posing a substantial threat to the commercial Muscovy duck industry. Here, we investigated the antiviral activity of fucoidan against MDGPV and characterized its underlying mechanisms of action. Using a network pharmacology approach, we identified ten core targets of fucoidan against MDGPV infection, with EGFR emerging as a key candidate. We further confirmed that fucoidan inhibits MDGPV replication in a dose-dependent manner, alongside downregulated EGFR expression and suppressed phosphorylation of core proteins in the MAPK signaling pathway. Conversely, EGFR overexpression enhanced MDGPV replication, and this proviral effect was effectively abrogated by fucoidan treatment. In an in vivo Muscovy duck challenge model, fucoidan administration exerted significant protective effects, as evidenced by improved survival rates and attenuated intestinal pathological injury. Collectively, these findings provide novel insights into the antiviral mechanisms of fucoidan and support its potential as a natural antiviral agent.

articles.title: Stereotactic Ablative Radiotherapy Versus Surgical Resection for Early-Stage Non-Small Lung Cancer: An Emulated Target Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) is standard of care for inoperable early-stage non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but there is little evidence to support SABR as an alternative to surgical resection. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have failed to recruit, and ongoing RCTs apply strict inclusion criteria. To our knowledge, this is the first emulated target trial comparing the effectiveness of SABR versus surgery in individuals with early-stage NSCLC eligible for either treatment.

METHODS: We used England's National Cancer Registry data to identify individuals diagnosed with T1-2N0M0 NSCLC during 2015-2020, age 18-79 years with Zubrod performance status 0-2, or age 80+ years with performance status 0-1, who underwent SABR or surgical resection within 6 months of diagnosis. Treatment receipt was identified via linkage to Hospital Episode Statistics and the National Radiotherapy Data Set. The primary outcome was 3-year all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes included lung cancer-specific mortality and recurrence. An instrumental variable analysis reduced the risk of confounding by indication.

RESULTS: A total of 12,546 met the eligibility criteria (2,299 SABR; 10,247 surgery). After adjustment, 3-year all-cause mortality estimates were 30.3% (SABR) and 21.6% (surgery; mean absolute risk difference 8.8 percentage points [pp], [95% CI, 1.4 to 16.2]; P = .02). Lung cancer-specific mortality estimates were 20.6% (SABR) and 14.5% (surgery; mean absolute risk difference 6.1 pp [95% CI, -0.6 to 12.9]; P = .07). The adjusted mean absolute risk difference in 3-year all-cause mortality for those age 80+ years was 4.3 pp ([95% CI, -3.7 to 12.3]; P = .62).

CONCLUSION: This emulated target trial found higher 3-year all-cause mortality after SABR versus surgery in early-stage NSCLC suitable for either modality, supporting that surgical resection should remain the preferred option. The findings support SABR as a curative-intent alternative, particularly for older people.

articles.title: C3E-RRG:Confounder-Aware Causal Evidence Coupling and Evolution for Chest X-Ray Report Generation.
articles.abstract: Chest X-ray report generation aims to produce diagnostic descriptions grounded in imaging evidence. However, correlation-driven models may exploit reporting templates and disease co-occurrence patterns, leading to unsupported findings and semantic drift. To address this issue, we propose C3E-RRG, a confounder-aware causal debiasing framework for chest X-ray report generation that incorporates explicit causal modeling into the encoder-decoder pipeline. Specifically, we first construct confounding variables by combining language priors derived from pointwise mutual information with disease co-occurrence statistics, and apply confounder-aware adjustment to suppress spurious correlations induced by data bias. We then design an evidence-consistent cross-modal coupling module to strengthen the correspondence between visual features and diagnostic semantics, thereby reducing semantic drift caused by high-frequency reporting templates. Finally, we develop a dynamic bidirectional causal evolution mechanism that iteratively revisits visual evidence and refines semantic representations, progressively correcting semantic deviations and improving image-text consistency during long-sequence generation. Experiments on the IU-XRay and MIMIC-CXR datasets demonstrate competitive performance and validate the effectiveness of the proposed components in suppressing confounding effects, aligning visual evidence with diagnostic semantics, and dynamically correcting generation errors. The source code is available at https://github.com/ cloneiq/C3E-RRG.

articles.title: Antithrombotic Therapy After Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: The SIMPLAAFY Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Following a left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) procedure, antithrombotic therapy is administered to safely allow time for device endothelialization. However, the optimal postimplant antithrombotic regimen is unknown.

OBJECTIVE: To determine if either reduced-dose non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants (NOACs) or aspirin alone are noninferior to dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) for the composite clinical end point of death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding through 6 months post LAAC.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This open-label, 3-group, multicenter clinical trial randomized 1857 patients between October 2024 and December 2025 at 87 US investigational sites, with the final 6-month follow-up in July 2026. Enrolled patients had nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, underwent successful LAAC, and were eligible for all 3 regimens.

INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomly allocated 1:1:1 to DAPT for 6 months followed by aspirin (n = 624), a reduced-dose NOAC for 3 months followed by aspirin (n = 620), or aspirin alone for 12 months (n = 613).

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the 6-month composite of all-cause death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding. Noninferiority was tested in the primary analysis population with a 1-sided Farrington-Manning test (α = .025). Bleeding and 45-day device-related thrombus rates were exploratory without multiplicity adjustment.

RESULTS: The cohort had a mean age of 76 (SD, 8) years, 42.9% were female, the mean CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4.2 (SD, 1.3), and 68.0% had paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. The primary outcome occurred in 41 patients (6.9%) with DAPT vs 31 (5.1%) with a reduced-dose NOAC (risk ratio, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.48-1.18]; risk difference, -1.7 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, 1.2) and 20 (3.3%) with aspirin alone (risk ratio, 0.49 [95% CI, 0.29-0.82]; risk difference, -3.5 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, -0.8). Both monotherapy strategies met noninferiority criteria (P < .001 for noninferiority for both). Major bleeding was 4.5% with DAPT, 2.7% with reduced-dose NOACs, and 1.7% with aspirin alone; clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was 8.7%, 4.8%, and 3.8%, respectively. Device-related thrombus was observed in 3.4%, 0.9%, and 2.7%, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Both reduced-dose NOACs and aspirin alone were noninferior to DAPT for 6-month outcomes after uncomplicated LAAC.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06521463.

articles.title: Electroactive Gel-MA hydrogels delivering sustained puerarin for myocardial infarction treatment.
articles.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) remains a major cause of heart failure and mortality worldwide. Herein, an electrically conductive hydrogel was developed by incorporating puerarin-functionalized carbon nanotubes (CNT-Pu) into a gelatin methacryloyl (Gel-MA) matrix for potential MI repair. CNT-Pu was dispersed in the Gel-MA precursor solution, followed by photo-crosslinking to form the Gel-MA/CNT-Pu hydrogel. The resulting hydrogel exhibited a porous microstructure, enhanced electrical conductivity, favorable mechanical properties and elastic recovery, and sustained puerarin release over 28 days. In vitro, the Gel-MA/CNT-Pu hydrogel exhibited favorable cytocompatibility with both L929 fibroblasts and H9c2 cardiomyoblasts, supporting its preliminary biological compatibility for myocardial applications. In a rat MI model, Gel-MA/CNT-Pu treatment was associated with reduced inflammatory cell infiltration and attenuation of fibrotic scar formation. Quantitative histological analysis demonstrated a significantly smaller fibrotic area and greater left ventricular wall thickness in the Gel-MA/CNT-Pu group than in the control group, suggesting that Gel-MA/CNT-Pu provided a multifunctional biomaterial strategy combining mechanical support, electrical conductivity, and localized drug delivery to attenuate adverse structural remodeling after MI. Further investigations were required to establish its functional cardiac benefits and long-term safety.

articles.title: Enhancing pathogen detection in pediatric diarrheal stools: The case of molecular multiplexing with a real-time PCR assay.
articles.abstract: Diarrhea is a leading cause of pediatric morbidity and mortality worldwide, frequently caused by various bacterial, viral, and protozoan pathogens. Identification of these pathogens is important in clinical settings for proper management of the infection. Conventional stool culture technique is time-consuming for the detection of diarrheagenic pathogens. In addition, these traditional procedures lack sensitivity, require a specific laboratory structure, and well-trained staff. Conversely, multiplex molecular detection methods offer rapid results with less hands-on time and more sensitivity. This study compared the diagnostic performance of conventional microbiological methods and GastroFinder 2SMART multiplexed real-time PCR (real-time PCR) assay for detecting enteric pathogens in pediatric stool samples. Overall pathogen detection was significantly higher using this real-time PCR (81%) compared to the conventional assays (43.1%), reflecting differences in both sensitivity and pathogen panel breadth. Rotavirus, adenovirus, Shigella, and Giardia lamblia were frequently identified by conventional methods, whereas real-time PCR commonly detected adenovirus, Campylobacter, EPEC, ETEC, and norovirus. Certain pathogens such as Yersinia enterocolitica, Clostridioides difficile, STEC, and Dientamoeba fragilis were not tested in the conventional panel and therefore excluded for comparison. Sensitivity estimates varied, with lower sensitivity observed for EPEC, Cryptosporidium, G. lamblia, and rotavirus, partly due to the small sample numbers and wide confidence intervals. Specificity exceeded 90% for most pathogens, and diagnostic accuracy was > 90% for Shigella/EIEC, Salmonella, Cryptosporidium, Giardia lamblia, and astrovirus. Bayesian latent class analysis demonstrated the highest sensitivity for Shigella/EIEC (93.2%), followed by norovirus and adenovirus, while overall test performance, measured by the Youden Index, was greatest for Shigella/EIEC. These findings highlight the diagnostic use of real-time PCR and support its integration into routine diarrheal diagnostics to improve pathogen detection and clinical management.

articles.title: Trends in the incidence of childhood type 1 diabetes after the COVID-19 lockdown in Finland: An observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While COVID-19 lockdowns have been systematically associated with increased incidence rate of type 1 diabetes, less is known about the disease rates after lockdowns. We compared the incidence of type 1 diabetes after the COVID-19 pandemic-related closure of society (i) to the time when lockdown was implemented and to (ii) the time before the pandemic in Finland.

METHODS AND FINDINGS: The incidence of type 1 diabetes after the lockdown (09/2021-12/2022) was compared to the incidence during the lockdown (03/2020-08/2021) and before the lockdown (three 18-month terms 2014-2019) in Finnish children under the age of 15 years. Previous exposure to SARS-CoV-2 was identified by combining information on COVID-19 vaccination with data on SARS-CoV-2 antibodies analyzed in blood samples. The temporal cohort included 3,467 pediatric type 1 diabetes cases, distributed across post-lockdown (n = 586), lockdown (n = 785), and pre-pandemic (n = 2,096) periods. The incidence of type 1 diabetes after the lockdown was significantly lower than the incidence during the lockdown [incidence rate ratio (IRR = 0.85; 95% Cl [0.77,0.95]; p = 0.004)]. The rate of type 1 diabetes after the lockdown did not significantly differ from the time before lockdown (IRR = 1.00; 95% Cl [0.91,1.09]; p = 0.932). The frequency of children testing positive for infection-associated SARS-CoV-2 antibodies increased from 0.9% during the lockdown to more than 40% after the lockdown. Study limitations include a relatively short follow-up period after the lockdown and the lack of explicit modeling of the underlying long-term secular trend in type 1 diabetes incidence.

CONCLUSIONS: The lockdown represents a peak in childhood type 1 diabetes incidence in Finland compared to both the pre-pandemic and post-lockdown periods. However, the reversion toward historical levels after the lockdown does not necessarily establish a return to the expected historical trajectory, nor can it fully distinguish a transient change from temporal compensation superimposed on the background secular trend. The contrasting patterns between type 1 diabetes incidence and SARS-CoV-2 antibody prevalence during and after the lockdown suggest an indirect rather than a direct role of the virus in triggering the observed changes in incidence.

articles.title: Tracing Strongyloides stercoralis transmission and risk factors from schoolchildren to household in Northwest Ethiopia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Strongyloides stercoralis is a neglected soil-transmitted helminth with a complex life cycle that enables both autoinfection and environmental transmission. Despite its public health importance, the burden and transmission dynamics of strongyloidiasis remain poorly understood in endemic settings such as Ethiopia, particularly at the household level. Hence, this study aimed to trace the transmission of S. stercoralis and associated factors from infected schoolchildren to their households in Northwest Ethiopia.

METHODOLOGY: A school-based cross-sectional study was conducted from 2024 to 2025 in Northwest Ethiopia. A total of 273 schoolchildren were randomly selected from three schools and screened for S. stercoralis. Children who tested positive were considered index cases, and all consenting household members were subsequently screened. Stool samples were examined using Kato-Katz, the Baermann concentration technique, and agar plate culture. Data on socio-demographic characteristics and potential risk factors were collected using structured questionnaires. Bivariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with infection.

FINDINGS: Out of 273 school children screened, the prevalence of S. stercoralis was 22.7%. Among 80 household members examined, 71.3% were infected with S. stercoralis. School children who lived in houses with mud floors (AOR = 2.91; p = 0.019), had close contact with dogs (AOR = 2.54; p = 0.006), lived in areas with clay soil (AOR = 2.98; p = 0.036), participated in irrigation activities (AOR = 3.72; p = 0.008) and wore shoes (AOR = 3.67; p = 0.017) were significantly associated with S. stercoralis infection.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates a substantial burden of S. stercoralis infection among schoolchildren and an exceptionally high prevalence among their household members. The findings underscore the importance of environmental, behavioral, and zoonotic factors in sustaining transmission. These results emphasize the urgent need for integrated control strategies to include household-level screening and treatment.

articles.title: Development of an infection via sugar meal (IVSM) technique to infect mosquitoes (Diptera: Culicidae) with arthropod-borne viruses.
articles.abstract: The global expansion of mosquito vectors is increasing human exposure to arboviruses, highlighting the need for rapid and practical approaches to assess vector competence. Standard artificial laboratory infection methods rely on infectious blood meals or intrathoracic inoculation, both of which can be resource-intensive and limit the capacity to conduct timely experiments, particularly in high-containment facilities. We developed an infection via sugar meal (IVSM) technique to determine whether mosquitoes can acquire and transmit arboviruses by ingesting virus-spiked sucrose. Using IVSM, we tested the vector competence of Aedes albopictus and Culex quinquefasciatus for West Nile virus (WNV), Mayaro virus (MAYV), and Zika virus (ZIKV) following 1-hour or 24-hour exposures. Viral RNA copy numbers were quantified in the body, legs/wings, and saliva at 7 and 10 days post-infection. Both species supported WNV infection and dissemination, with the virus detected in saliva. Aedes albopictus exhibited high MAYV infection and dissemination rates, whereas Cx. quinquefasciatus was largely refractory. ZIKV infection and dissemination were limited in both species and did not progress to saliva. High feeding success, low vector mortality, and reproducible outcomes across trials demonstrate that IVSM is an accessible and practical alternative to blood-based infection models and provides a framework for investigating vector competence under conditions that utilize natural feeding behavior.

articles.title: Carbapenem-valproic acid derivative drug-drug interactions: Evaluation of a pharmacist-facing OurPractice Advisory.
articles.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this quality improvement evaluation was to describe implementation and postimplementation experience with a pharmacist-facing OurPractice Advisory (OPA) within the Epic electronic health record designed to identify concurrent carbapenem antibiotic and valproic acid (VPA) derivative therapy.

SUMMARY: A pharmacist-facing OPA was developed to identify selected clinical scenarios involving carbapenem antibiotics and VPA derivatives, including scenarios involving active inpatient medication orders and prior-to-admission medication list entries. A retrospective review was conducted for hospitalized patients with OPA activations over a 10-month period. The OPA appeared for 30 hospitalized patients. The most common activation scenario was a carbapenem ordered in the presence of an already verified inpatient VPA derivative order, occurring in 19 patients (63.3%). The most common VPA derivative indication was mood stabilization in 12 patients (40%), followed by a seizure-related indication in 9 patients (30%). The median (IQR) time to pharmacist order decision was 21.5 (5.25-51.25) minutes. Formal infectious diseases consultation and neurology consultation occurred in 23 (76.7%) and 10 (33.3%) patients, respectively. Antibiotic therapy was switched from a carbapenem to a different antibiotic in 14 cases (46.7%), VPA derivative therapy was held, discontinued, or not verified in 7 cases (23.3%), and both agents were continued without change in 8 cases (26.7%).

CONCLUSION: Implementation of a pharmacist-facing OPA provided a structured process for identifying and documenting selected carbapenem-VPA derivative drug-drug interaction scenarios during pharmacist order verification. Postimplementation review identified opportunities for refinement, including reduction of repetitive activations, clarification of acknowledgment options, and consideration of earlier prescriber-facing clinical decision support.

articles.title: Sickness Absence in Primary Aldosteronism and References: a Longitudinal Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Primary aldosteronism (PA) is a common cause of hypertension and is associated with increased cardiovascular morbidity. However, its impact on work capacity remains unknown. We investigated sickness absence and disability pension among patients with PA and in matched reference groups with and without hypertension.

METHODS: A nationwide eight-year longitudinal cohort study based on linked register data, including 838 individuals with PA aged 18-67 in 2019 and two matched reference cohorts with and without hypertension. Outcomes included annual proportions of individuals with sickness absence (in spells >14 days) or disability pension, mean annual net days, and trajectories of absence days.

RESULTS: Patients with PA had a higher mean annual proportion with sickness absence than individuals with hypertension (21% (range: 18-23%) vs 17% (range: 17-19%) and those without hypertension (10% (range: 9-12%)). Mean annual sickness absence days were 27, 20, and 9, respectively. The combined mean annual number of sickness absence and disability pension days was similar in PA and hypertension (54 (range: 40-66) vs 53 (range: 50-57), and higher than in those without hypertension (25 (range: 22-29)). Trajectory analysis identified four patterns of absence days; 12% of patients with PA had persistently high absence, significantly associated with female sex, higher age, lower education, unmarried status, rural residence, cardiovascular disease, and treatment with mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists.

CONCLUSION: PA is associated with substantial and sustained sickness absence and disability pension, comparable to that observed in hypertension and higher than in individuals without hypertension. These findings extend the clinical impact of PA beyond cardiovascular morbidity and highlight the importance of considering work capacity in clinical management.
