articles.title: The mosquito-stage transcriptome of the neglected malaria parasite Plasmodium malariae reveals species-specific gene expression signatures and functional adaptations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To survive and multiply in different host niches, malaria parasites require sets of proteins that are expressed during the life cycle in a timely manner. Plasmodium malariae is a human malaria parasite that is present in most malaria-endemic regions. This species remains enigmatic due to the inability to maintain it in long-term culture, the low parasitemia observed in human infections, and its frequent co-infection with other malaria species.

METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: We investigate the transcriptome of P. malariae during transmission in the vector by analyzing RNA-seq data from midgut and salivary gland parasite stages obtained in two experimental mosquito infections with field P. malariae isolates. Our analysis identified 3,699 expressed genes, of which 263 are developmentally regulated and 309 are P. malariae-specific, including genes with unknown functions and without orthologs in other Plasmodium spp. We detected unique expression patterns of the ApiAP2 family of transcription factors, many of which appear to function as master regulators during sporogony. Several members of multigene families, such as PIR, PHIST, and fam-l, were found to be expressed, and new families potentially showing transcriptional heterogeneity were described.

CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: Our findings indicate that the P. malariae transcriptome is largely conserved; however, a distinct set of expressed genes lacking detectable orthologs may contribute to differences in transmission and virulence. Given the scarcity of genomic and transcriptomic data for this pathogen and considering the global distribution of P. malariae and its potential role in sustaining malaria transmission, this study has direct implications for malaria control and elimination efforts.

articles.title: Fungal suppression by bacterial metabolite-activated human intestinal γδT-cells is disrupted in Crohn's disease.
articles.abstract: Gut symbionts condition mucosal immunity to resist infection by enteropathogens, but the specific microbes and mechanisms involved differ significantly between host species. In higher primates, bacterial metabolite HMB-PP is sensed by a specialized population of Vγ9Vδ2+T-cells, which we now report can potently suppress growth of endogenous fungi in human intestinal organ cultures. In healthy intestine, HMB-PP-stimulated Vδ2+ T-cells restricted outgrowth of keystone fungus Candida albicans via a mechanism that required IL-22. In Crohn's disease (CD), Vδ2+ T-cells were poorly responsive to HMB-PP and permitted outgrowth of C. albicans strains that formed toxin-producing filaments, triggered neutrophil extracellular traps, and induced macrophage IL-1β release ex vivo. Genomic and proteomic analysis of the Candida isolates suggested increased tissue adhesion of CD-derived strains, which rapidly invaded the gut barrier in an 'intestine-on-a-chip' model. These data reveal that bacterial activation of Vδ2+ T-cells suppresses fungal pathobionts in human gut via an IL-22-dependent mechanism that is dysregulated in CD.

articles.title: An Approach to Acute Cranial Symptoms in Primary Care: Lesson From a Case of Miller Fisher Syndrome.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Miller Fisher syndrome (MFS) is a rare variant of Guillain-Barre syndrome characterized by the classic triad of ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and areflexia following a recent infection. Early recognition is particularly challenging due to the rarity of the condition and its tendency to mimic other common neurological and non-neurological disorders. We report a case highlighting the diagnostic and referral challenges encountered in the primary care setting. CASE REPORT A 38-year-old woman with no significant comorbidity presented to a primary care clinic with acute diplopia, right eye pain, headache, and perioral numbness following an upper respiratory tract infection 2 weeks earlier. Initial neurological examination was unremarkable. She was referred to the ophthalmology and emergency departments to exclude ocular pathology and posterior circulation stroke. Laboratory investigation and computed tomography of the brain were unremarkable and she was managed as a case of migraine. Meanwhile, ophthalmological review subsequently demonstrated ophthalmoplegia and the following day she developed bulbar symptoms prompting urgent neurological consultation. Repeated neurological examination revealed the classic triad of MFS. She received plasma exchange therapy following her clinical deterioration. Her neurological symptoms gradually improved with complete recovery, with residual diplopia resolving 8 weeks after symptom onset. CONCLUSIONS MFS remains a predominantly clinical diagnosis with subtle and evolving features that may delay recognition in the primary care setting. This case underscores the crucial role of primary care physicians in maintaining a high index of suspicion, recognizing atypical presentation, and providing appropriate safety-netting and timely specialist referral to facilitate early diagnosis and improve clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Cerebrovascular Function in Glaucoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PRCIS: Glaucoma patients appear to exhibit variable cerebrovascular differences, including reduced MCA blood velocity and heterogeneous cerebral blood flow and neurovascular coupling responses.

PURPOSE: Glaucoma is associated with neurodegenerative and cerebrovascular diseases, such as dementia, migraine, and stroke, indicating a possible shared underlying pathophysiology of cerebrovascular dysfunction. However, no previous systematic review or meta-analysis has investigated whether people with glaucoma have poorer cerebrovascular function than those without. This study aimed to compare cerebrovascular function in glaucoma patients to healthy controls.

METHODS: Five electronic databases (Embase, Medline, PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science) were systematically searched until 28 October 2025 for full-text studies comparing measures of cerebrovascular function in people with glaucoma to controls. Meta-analyses were performed, where applicable, using mean differences (MD) and confidence intervals (CI) between glaucoma and control groups.

RESULTS: Qualitative analysis of sixteen observational studies revealed that glaucoma patients exhibited varying neurovascular coupling responses (both higher and lower than controls) across frontal, occipital, and parietal regions along with varying cerebral blood flow differences. Cerebral blood flow tended to be lower within the occipital and parietal lobes, and higher within the frontal lobe. Data from six observational studies were included in meta-analyses, which revealed glaucoma patients had lower systolic (MD = -16.38, 95% CI -27.96 to -4.80, P=0.006) and mean (MD = -6.50, 95% CI -11.99 to -1.02, P=0.02) blood velocities in the middle cerebral artery than controls. Sensitivity analyses indicated findings were sensitive to the inclusion of individual studies.

CONCLUSION: Glaucoma patients show heterogeneous cerebrovascular differences compared to controls, without a consistent directional or global pattern of dysfunction. Future longitudinal studies are needed to further characterise cerebrovascular measures in glaucoma.

articles.title: Bacterial Keratitis Caused by Methicillin-Resistant Coagulase-Negative Staphylococci After Cultured Human Corneal Endothelial Cell Injection: A Case Report and Review of Preoperative Conjunctival Sac Culture Findings.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to report a case of methicillin-resistant coagulase-negative staphylococci (MRCNS) keratitis after cultured human corneal endothelial cell (cHCEC) injection therapy, in which MRCNS with similar antimicrobial susceptibility profiles were identified on both preoperative conjunctival sac and postoperative corneal scraping cultures.

METHODS: We report a case of infectious keratitis following cHCEC injection therapy and retrospectively reviewed preoperative conjunctival sac culture results in 51 consecutive patients who underwent the procedure at our institution.

RESULTS: A 75-year-old man with bullous keratopathy underwent cHCEC injection therapy. Preoperative conjunctival sac culture revealed fluoroquinolone-resistant MRCNS. On postoperative day 7, 2 circular corneal infiltrates were identified in the superior cornea with worsening corneal edema. Corneal scraping culture again yielded MRCNS with similar antimicrobial susceptibility profiles, supporting the diagnosis of postoperative MRCNS keratitis. Topical chloramphenicol/colistin methanesulfonate sodium and cefmenoxime led to rapid resolution of the infiltrates. At 3 months postoperatively, the infection had resolved and best corrected visual acuity improved to 20/63 (logMAR 0.50). In the retrospective review of 51 patients, positive conjunctival sac cultures were observed in 27 (52.9%), including MRCNS in 8 (15.7%). Fluoroquinolone resistance was noted in 23 patients (45.1%) for levofloxacin and 21 (41.2%) for gatifloxacin.

CONCLUSIONS: Infectious keratitis can occur early after cHCEC injection therapy. Preoperative conjunctival sac culture may be useful in guiding empirical antimicrobial therapy when fluoroquinolone-resistant organisms are present. However, larger studies are needed to determine whether routine preoperative conjunctival sac culture is warranted in patients undergoing cHCEC injection therapy.

articles.title: Feasibility and Early Outcomes of Gonioscopy-Assisted Transluminal Trabeculotomy for Neovascular Glaucoma.
articles.abstract: This retrospective observational case series evaluates the clinical outcomes of gonioscopy-assisted transluminal trabeculotomy (GATT) in 6 consecutive eyes with neovascular glaucoma (NVG) treated at a tertiary referral center. NVG was defined as secondary glaucoma associated with retinal ischemia, characterized by elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) and prior presence of iris and/or angle neovascularization. All patients had previously undergone pan-retinal photocoagulation and intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy and were receiving maximally tolerated medical treatment at presentation. Circumferential GATT was successfully completed in all cases. At final follow-up, IOP control was achieved in 3 eyes with topical therapy, while the remaining 3 eyes required subsequent Ahmed glaucoma valve implantation due to early surgical failure. All eyes that met failure criteria demonstrated circumferential peripheral anterior synechiae formation during early postoperative follow-up and were observed in patients with poorly controlled diabetes mellitus. Two cases required anterior chamber washout for persistent hyphema. In this small case series, our observations suggest that clinical role of GATT remains uncertain and the present data do not allow identification of patient subgroups that may benefit or support definition of clinical indications.

articles.title: Knockdown of a regulatory barcode shifts macrophage polarization destination from M1 to M2 and increases pathogen burden upon S. aureus infection.
articles.abstract: Macrophages are driven to form distinct functional phenotypes in response to different immunological stimuli, in a process widely referred to as macrophage polarization. Transcriptional regulators that guide macrophage polarization in response to a given trigger remain largely unknown. In this study, we interrogate the programmable landscape in macrophages to find regulatory panels that determine the precise polarization state that a macrophage is driven to. Toward this, we configure an integrative network analysis pipeline that utilizes macrophage transcriptomes in response to 28 distinct stimuli, reconstructs contextualized human gene regulatory networks, and identifies epicenters of perturbations in each case. We find that these contextualized regulatory networks form a spectrum of 13 distinct clusters, with M1 and M2 at the two ends. Using our computational pipeline, we identify combinatorial panels of epicentric regulatory factors (RFs) for each polarization state. We demonstrate that a set of three RFs, that is, CEBPB, NFE2L2, and BCL3, is sufficient to change the polarization destination from M1 to M2. siRNA knockdown of the 3-RF-set in THP1-derived M0 cells, despite exposure to an M1 stimulant, significantly attenuated the shift to M1 phenotype and instead increased the expression of M2 markers. Single knockdown of each RF also showed a similar trend. The siRNA-mediated knockdown of the 3-RF-set rendered the macrophages hyper-susceptible to Staphylococcus aureus infection, demonstrating the importance of these factors in modulating immune responses. Overall, our results provide insights into the transcriptional mechanisms underlying macrophage polarization and identify key RFs that may be targeted to modulate immune responses.

articles.title: Protocol for isolating intracellular Salmonella RNA from primary murine macrophages.
articles.abstract: Isolation of intracellular bacterial RNA from infected cells remains challenging, limiting studies of bacterial transcription during host cell infection. Here, we present a protocol for isolating intracellular Salmonella enterica RNA from primary murine macrophages for transcriptomic analysis. We describe steps for macrophage infection, selective host cell lysis, bacterial recovery, and RNA purification for sequencing. This protocol uses standard laboratory equipment, is completed in 3 days, and can be adapted to other bacteria that replicate within macrophages. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Massicotte et al.1.

articles.title: A substituted cysteine accessibility protocol to probe orthosteric and non-canonical ligand binding to ion channels.
articles.abstract: The Substituted Cysteine Accessibility Method (SCAM) is an approach for probing the biophysics and pharmacology of ion channels by targeting covalent modifications to individual amino acids. Here, we present a protocol to constrain channel stoichiometry and identify asymmetric or non-canonical ligand-binding sites using SCAM followed by electrophysiology in mammalian heterologous expression systems, in the context of heteropentameric nicotinic acetylcholine receptors. This protocol is applicable to examination of multiple channel properties, including ligand binding, gating, pore conductance, and selectivity. For complete information on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Kulkarni et al.1.

articles.title: Exposure to immune stimuli augments alveolar macrophages to acquire neutrophil antimicrobial molecules to prevent bacterial pneumonia.
articles.abstract: The protective adaptation of innate immune defenses against respiratory pathogens has been linked to previous exposure to immune stimuli; however, the underlying mechanisms of these adaptations are not yet fully understood. Here, we show that pre-exposure to a low dose of non-specific immune stimuli or infection protects against subsequent lethal methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) challenge. This enhanced protection concurs with increased alveolar macrophages (AMs) resulting from a self-renewal process in the lungs. Importantly, these AMs are programmed to acquire neutrophil-released antimicrobial enzymes from the extracellular space to clear MRSA, prevent tissue damage, and rapidly restore lung homeostasis. AM function depends on differential gene expression, including expression of the efferocytosis receptor Mer proto-oncogene tyrosine kinase (MerTK) and the anti-apoptotic regulator Bcl-xL. Thus, our data highlight that AMs acquire neutrophil enzymes as an integral component of innate immune adaptation.

articles.title: Effect of topical insulin in diabetic foot ulcer healing among patients with diabetes in Asia: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this systematic review is to provide a comprehensive understanding on the effectiveness of topical insulin in the healing of diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) in patients with diabetes in Asian countries.

METHOD: A systematic review of both observational and randomised controlled trials evaluating insulin efficacy on DFUs-but which was limited to studies in Asian countries between 2016 and 2024-was conducted. Guidelines of the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses were followed. Electronic databases including PubMed, Scopus, MEDLINE and Google Scholar were searched for studies comparing insulin interventions with standard of care or other interventions, based on specific inclusion criteria.

RESULTS: A total of 16 relevant studies (out of 1132 on initial search) reporting on 1056 patients were included. Of the studies, eight reported wound healing rates in terms of reduction in wound size. Data on days of hospitalisation, number of dressing changes and insulin applications, quality of life, cost-effectiveness, and the psychological parameters of anxiety and depression, were not considered by any of the included studies.

CONCLUSION: The findings of this review provide supportive evidence that insulin was an efficient adjunct for healing DFUs. The findings identified existing evidence and gaps within it that may inform future studies in other Asian countries and beyond.

articles.title: PRISM: incorporating advanced imaging technologies into a comprehensive strategy for hard-to-heal wound assessment and management.
articles.abstract: Head-to-heal wounds-particularly diabetic lower-extremity wounds-remain among the most challenging and resource-intensive problems in contemporary healthcare, with five-year recurrence rates of 40-65% and a trajectory toward amputation that is frequently driven by three interacting and often under-recognised failures: inadequate perfusion; unrecognised bacterial burden; and unaddressed biomechanical deformity. Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) and bacterial autofluorescence (BAF)-two point-of-care optical imaging technologies-now permit objective, real-time characterisation of the two dominant modifiable barriers to healing: tissue oxygenation and bacterial load. PRISM (perfusion imaging, regional bacterial status, infection staging, structural correction, and maintenance and monitoring) is a structured, imaging-first algorithm that organises these technologies into a single, sequential pathway for hard-to-heal wound assessment and management. This article reviews the operating principles and clinical evidence for NIRS and BAF, expands each of the five PRISM components in a stepwise clinical description, and presents an integrated decision matrix-tree that translates combined imaging findings into actionable, point-of-care interventions. By anchoring every clinical decision in real-time imaging data rather than clinical impression alone, PRISM offers a reproducible framework for earlier identification of healing barriers, more targeted therapy, antimicrobial stewardship, objective longitudinal monitoring and limb preservation.

articles.title: Clinical effectiveness and safety of bacterial cellulose dressings in the management of skin wounds: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The global impact of skin injuries is substantial, compromising the wellbeing of affected individuals. Bacterial cellulose is gaining traction as a prospective dressing material due to its distinct characteristics. Nevertheless, its clinical efficacy and safety warrant detailed investigation. This systematic examination and meta-analysis assessed the healing efficacy and safety parameters of bacterial cellulose used as a dressing in skin injury management.

METHOD: Comprehensive database searches of CNKI, PubMed, Embase and Web of Science were conducted from database inception to 1 September 2024, in line with PRISMA guidelines. Studies included were randomised controlled trials that compared bacterial cellulose dressings (BCDs) with conventional treatment methods. Key outcome parameters were the healing of wounds, mitigation of pain and incidence of adverse events.

RESULTS: The collective analysis comprised 13 studies with 514 participants, divided equally between BCDs and control groups. A notable variance was observed in the healing duration (mean difference: -6.69 days), favouring the BCD group. Equivocal results emerged for healing cure rates (odds ratio (OR): 1.27), overall adverse reactions (OR: 0.4) and pain mitigation (OR: 2.45), with none achieving statistical significance. BCD was, however, observed to hasten wound size reduction and lessen the need for dressings to be changed.

CONCLUSION: The findings of this review showed that the use of BCD for wound treatment appeared to bolster the healing process and offer pain relief. Further extensive studies are required to confirm these preliminary observations and guide their clinical application.

articles.title: Can the use of collagenase and hyaluronic acid gel reduce the number of repeated surgical debridements in Fournier's gangrene?
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the clinical outcome criteria between treatments of repetitive mechanical debridement, conventional dressings, and the use of collagenase and hyaluronic acid gel for patients with Fournier's gangrene (FG).

METHOD: A retrospective analysis was made of the records of 56 patients with FG who were classified into two groups. In both groups, appropriate surgical debridement treatment was applied under operating room conditions at the time of diagnosis and as required. Group 1 comprised patients subsequently treated with daily repetitive mechanical debridement and conventional dressings. The patients in Group 2 were treated with mechanical debridement once per three days with the use of collagenase and hyaluronic acid cream after the initial surgical debridement. The two groups were compared in respect of the need for repeated surgical debridement, number of dressing changes, colostomy requirement, need to change the antibiotics and length of stay in hospital.

RESULTS: The mean age of the patients was 54.72±15.15 years and 26 patients had diabetes. The need for repetitive mechanical debridement and the number of dressing changes were significantly lower in the collagenase-hyaluronic acid group (p<0.05). There was no significant difference between the groups in respect of the need to change antibiotics, the need for colostomy and the length of hospital stay (all p>0.05).

CONCLUSION: Collagenase-hyaluronic acid gel can be considered safe and useful in the management of FG to reduce the number of repeated mechanical debridements and dressing changes. This is the first study in the literature to have evaluated the use of this combination in the management of FG.

articles.title: Low-level laser therapy in ulcerative lesions in leprosy: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Leprosy is a disease that affects the peripheral nerves and ulcers are among the main complications of the disease. The laser is a tool with wide use in physiotherapy, with proven efficacy in the improvement of pressure ulcers, which creates the possibility of studies on its action in leprosy lesions. The aim of this study was to review the literature on the efficacy of low-level laser therapy (LLLT) in the healing process of leprosy lesions.

METHOD: Articles were sought in databases according to specific search criteria for each database as results of the descriptors included using EndNote Web (Clarivate, UK). The risk of bias (RoB) was analysed using Cochrane's ROBINS-I and RoB2 tools.

RESULTS: A total of 259 studies were included, involving 49 patients. After exclusion of duplicates and following a full reading, three articles remained for inclusion in this review. Of the three studies, only two had positive results for LLLT on the healing of leprosy ulcers; however, no study showed low RoB.

CONCLUSION: The findings of this review concluded that use of LLLT in the study population was effective in reducing the size of leprosy lesions. Due to the lack of primary studies with low RoB, more primary studies are required to provide stronger evidence on the use of LLLT in the treatment of leprosy ulcers.

articles.title: Attenuation of Angiotensin II- Induced Cardiomyocyte Hypertrophy by Moringa oleifera Lam. extract, Fractions and Bioactive Constituents: Cell Size Analysis and Molecular Docking.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Nutrition Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Moringa oleifera Lam. leaves are valued for their rich nutritional profile and traditional use in treating various ailments, including hypertension. However, research focusing on their mechanism of action, particularly their interactions with angiotensin (Ang) II receptors remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of M. oleifera leaves extract, fractions and bioactive compounds (kaempferol, chlorogenic acid, gallic acid, and vicenin-2) on Ang II induced H9c2 cells and their binding affinities toward Ang II receptors.

METHOD: The crude extract was fractionated into hexane, dichloromethane, ethyl acetate, acetone and methanol fractions. Cell viability test was carried out and concentrations that maintained cell viability at 80% and more were selected for further study. Hypertrophic model was simulated by inducing H9c2 cells with Ang II (1 µM) and the antihypertrophic effect was assessed by measuring changes in the cell size.

RESULTS: Ang II significantly doubled the cell size compared to normal control groups. Results showed that the crude extract, its ethyl acetate, acetone, and methanol fractions, and bioactive compounds significantly reduced Ang II-induced cell hypertrophy (p < 0.05) in H9c2 cells compared to the Ang II untreated group. Furthermore, bioactive compounds tested also showed significant dose-dependent (10, 20, and 40 µM) reduction in cell size compared to the Ang II group. Gallic acid demonstrated the highest potency by reducing the size the most at the highest dose tested (40 µM), followed by quercetin, chlorogenic acid, vicenin and kaempferol. In molecular docking studies, binding energies of -5.5 kcal/mol and lower were recorded for all bioactive compounds indicating their strong binding affinities toward Ang II receptor.

CONCLUSION: This work provides an evaluation of Ang II-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy attenuation activity of bioactive compounds identified in the M. oleifera leaves extract. These findings serve as a foundation for future studies aimed at developing therapies for cardiovascular diseases from natural resources.

articles.title: The Ambient AI Era and Medical Student Education: Insights From Family Medicine Clerkship Directors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Artificial intelligence (AI) adoption in medicine is rapidly expanding, including ambient AI (AAI), which converts clinician-patient conversations into documentation. Despite growing use among practicing physicians, little is known about student access to AAI or barriers to implementation during medical student clerkships.

METHODS: We surveyed 174 family medicine clerkship directors (CDs) through the Council of Academic Family Medicine Educational Research Alliance network regarding AAI availability, permissibility, and opinions on student use. We analyzed responses using descriptive statistics and Fisher's exact tests.

RESULTS: Ninety-four CDs responded to AAI-related questions. Student AAI use was permitted for only 3% of core family medicine clerkships. CDs cited missing technology (38.3%) or institutional restrictions (42.5%) as barriers. Opinions on student use were divided: 42.6% opposed any use, 41.5% supported some use, and 16% were unsure. Among those who opposed use, major concerns included potential negative effects on clinical reasoning (82.5%) and communication skills (85%). Supporters of student use were significantly more likely to believe AI will improve training and become commonplace in students' careers than those who did not support student use of AAI (P<0.0001).

CONCLUSIONS: Access to AAI for medical students during core family medicine clerkships is rare, and CDs expressed substantial concerns regarding its impact on clinical reasoning and communication skills. Given the expeditious integration of AI into clinical practice, medical educators must be prepared to teach with technology, proactively design curricula that assume AAI availability, and consider modalities in addition to clinical documentation to assess student clinical reasoning.

articles.title: Age-specific respiratory support and monitoring for acute respiratory distress syndrome: a narrative review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) causes inflammatory alveolar-capillary injury at different ages. Age-related differences in respiratory mechanics, airway anatomy, pulmonary vascular physiology, and disease etiology limit extrapolation of diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. This review compared respiratory monitoring and support strategies across adult, pediatric, and neonatal ARDS.

AREAS COVERED: We searched PubMed for English-language human studies published from database inception through 14 August 2026 and reviewed major society guidelines. This review covers age-specific ARDS definitions, epidemiology, pathophysiology, respiratory support, adjunctive therapies, and liberation from mechanical ventilation. Adult-derived evidence supports low-tidal-volume ventilation, prolonged prone positioning for severe ARDS, selective higher positive end-expiratory pressure, and early extracorporeal membrane oxygenation for refractory disease. Recommendations for pediatric ARDS often rely on consensus or observational evidence. Neonatal ARDS management remains largely extrapolated from neonatal respiratory disorders and must account for gestational age, surfactant biology, pulmonary hypertension, and etiology.

EXPERT OPINION: Respiratory support should be age-calibrated, phenotype-informed, and reassessed for gas exchange, respiratory effort, mechanics, hemodynamics, device performance, and clinical trajectory. Physiological improvements may not translate into positive outcomes. Noninvasive support should not delay intubation in cases of failure. Standardized interventions and prospective studies must be tailored to pediatric and neonatal populations.

articles.title: Social Determinants of Kidney and Cardiovascular Outcomes: Prioritizing Action to Effectively Manage Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome.
articles.journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN
articles.abstract: In 2005, the World Health Organization (WHO) created the inaugural Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) Commission to recognize how social and physical environments impact health for all populations. In doing so, they created an impetus for policy-making and governing bodies to improve the underlying social conditions underpinning health for all, particularly for the most disadvantaged populations. Over the past decade, these efforts have coincided with growing evidence from high-middle- and low-income nations, that adverse structural/social determinants of health (SDOH) are fundamentally linked to advanced cardiovascular disease (CVD) and kidney disease, stark disparities in disease prevalence, and high, avoidable health care costs. In 2023, the American Heart Association coined cardiovascular kidney metabolic syndrome (CKM) -a condition recognizing the inextricable link between metabolic syndrome, diabetes, CKD, CVD and the social determinants of health (SDOH). In the following review, we first summarize the evidence regarding SDOH and kidney and cardiovascular outcomes within U.S. contexts, highlighting epidemiologic studies demonstrating the association between adverse SDOH and advanced CKM syndrome. We then describe how governance and policies may undergird SDOH including community-level (e.g. the natural and built environment, commercial determinants of health) and individual-level factors (e.g. economic conditions, education) which influence cardiovascular and kidney health. In this section, we provide examples of salutary policies and actions which can optimize health outcomes by addressing key contributors to health inequality (e.g. unequal adverse health exposures, limited opportunity to access health-promoting resources). We also overview postulated mechanisms through which SDOH impact CKM outcomes, such as glucocorticoid resistance, chronic sympathetic activation & pro-Inflammatory transcription, weathering, and premature aging. Through sustained investments and policy actions that reduce health-related vulnerabilities and promote equitable access to opportunities, conditions, and resources essential for health, we can fulfill a shared vision of achieving optimal CKM health across populations.

articles.title: Simplifying principles underlying the highly complex peptide motif of the promiscuous chicken MHC class I molecule, BF2*21:01.
articles.abstract: In chickens and humans, classical class I molecules of the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) have a spectrum of correlated properties, including cell surface expression and peptide repertoire. Understanding the impact of these promiscuous generalists and fastidious specialists is of considerable interest. The promiscuous BF2 molecule from the chicken B21 haplotype, BF2*21:01, binds a wide range of peptides by remodelling the peptide-binding site, allowing co-variation of the anchor residues at peptide positions P2 and Pc-2, and binding of an anchor residue at Pc. Using in vitro refolding assays with peptides and peptide libraries, determining thermostability and crystal structures, and analysing a chicken B21 cell line by immunopeptidomics, we found that BF2*21:01 will accommodate many possible combinations at P2 and Pc-2, as well as several hydrophobic amino acids at Pc. However, marked preferences for particular peptide lengths, particular amino acids at the three anchor residues, and particular combinations of amino acids at P2 and Pc-2 as well as at P3 and Pc-3 together lead to high frequencies of major peptides while still allowing the possibility of presenting a wide peptide repertoire. These simplifying principles may eventually allow predictions of pathogen peptides with stable binding for this iconic promiscuous class I molecule, as well as providing the data for more sophisticated peptide prediction methods.

articles.title: Pharmacist-led remote monitoring for hypertension management: A longitudinal descriptive study of patient and pharmacist experiences.
articles.journal: Canadian pharmacists journal : CPJ = Revue des pharmaciens du Canada : RPC
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Over 50% of patients with hypertension are suboptimally managed, offering the opportunity for pharmacists to leverage technology to support monitoring. The objective of this study was to evaluate patient and pharmacist attitudes, experiences, and perspectives of a remote, pharmacist-led hypertension management program that incorporated a mobile health (mHealth) application into routine care.

METHODS: This was a 6-month longitudinal descriptive feasibility study using A&D Heart Track to monitor home blood pressure (BP) alongside pharmacist consultation. A mixed-methods approach was used, combining facilitated patient and pharmacist surveys administered at multiple time points with qualitative interviews. This paper reports the quantitative survey findings, with qualitative interview findings reported separately. Survey responses were analyzed using descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: The study enrolled 17 patients, and 8 pharmacists were involved in their care. At 6 months, 94% of patients reported satisfaction with the mHealth application and 88% felt better cared for knowing a pharmacist was monitoring their readings. Patients reported sustained comfort with the technology and consistently positive perceptions of pharmacist accessibility. At 6 months, all pharmacists agreed or strongly agreed that the application would help them provide better care and increase their involvement in patients' care.

CONCLUSION: This study provides descriptive evidence that a pharmacist-led, remote monitoring approach for hypertension management was feasible from the perspectives of patients and pharmacists in a Canadian primary care setting, based on patient satisfaction and comfort with technology and pharmacist-reported manageability of mHealth application use. These findings may help inform the expansion of telehealth services and their application to other chronic conditions, such as type 2 diabetes.

articles.title: A survey of speech-language pathologists' dysphagia practice patterns in South Africa.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: South Africa's quadruple burden of disease contributes to high rates of dysphagia across the lifespan, with speech-language pathologists often providing services in resource-limited contexts. Variability in training, resources, and clinical practice highlights the need for a national profile of dysphagia management. This study investigated dysphagia practice patterns and professional needs among South African speech-language pathologists.

METHOD: An electronic survey was distributed via social media to speech-language pathologists providing dysphagia services. Convenience and snowball sampling were used. Responses from 124 participants were analysed descriptively, while qualitative data were analysed thematically.

RESULT: Participants represented urban (78.8%) and rural (21.2%) settings across public (38.1%) and private (47.5%) sectors. Caseloads consisted primarily of adults with neurological conditions, particularly stroke and head injury. Dysphagia assessment relied largely on informal methods, with limited access to instrumental assessments, especially in public and rural contexts. Qualitative findings identified contextual constraints, training gaps, limited mentorship, and a need for contextually relevant guidelines.

CONCLUSION: National strategies are needed to strengthen dysphagia service delivery through enhanced training, accessible mentorship, and contextually responsive guidelines that support equitable, safe, and evidence-informed care across diverse settings.

articles.title: T-Cell-Engaging Bispecific Therapies and Ocular Inflammation Emerging Phenotypes, Immunologic Mechanisms, and Clinical Management.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: T-cell-engaging bispecific therapies are increasingly used in hematologic and solid malignancies. This narrative review aims to summarize reported ocular adverse events associated with these therapies, critically evaluate the strength of available evidence, and propose a practical approach to their recognition and management.

METHODS: A narrative review of published case reports, clinical series, clinical trial safety findings, pharmacovigilance analyses, and U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) safety communications was conducted to identify ocular adverse events associated with T-cell-engaging bispecific therapies. Available evidence was evaluated with emphasis on clinical presentation, potential causality, differential diagnosis, and management considerations.

RESULTS: Reported ocular events include uveitis and sclerouveitis during teclistamab therapy, orbital inflammation during xaluritamig treatment, and orbital tumor pseudoprogression during elranatamab treatment. A mosunetuzumab pharmacovigilance analysis identified three uveitis reports among 1,154 primary-suspect reports, although these data do not permit estimation of patient incidence. Uveitis was also reported in a clinical trial evaluating mosunetuzumab combined with polatuzumab vedotin. FDA surveillance has identified uveitis as a potential safety signal for teclistamab and elranatamab. Important differential diagnoses include infection, malignant infiltration, cytokine-associated edema, and neurologic causes of visual symptoms.

CONCLUSIONS: Ocular inflammatory events have been documented during T-cell-engaging bispecific therapy; however, their incidence, causality, and underlying mechanisms remain uncertain. Current evidence supports clinical vigilance but does not establish a class-wide ocular toxicity syndrome. Prompt ophthalmic evaluation of new ocular symptoms and multidisciplinary collaboration between oncologists and ophthalmologists are recommended as reasonable clinical approaches. Standardized monitoring protocols, corticosteroid treatment strategies, and criteria for treatment rechallenge require further prospective investigation.

articles.title: Regression Discontinuity Approaches to Evaluate Threshold-Guided Interventions in Observational Studies.
Improving Nursing Student Awareness and Help-Seeking Through Evidence-Based Mental Health Resource Interventions.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Undergraduate nursing students frequently experience stress, anxiety, and depression related to academic demands, yet many do not engage with available campus mental health services due to barriers such as stigma, low visibility, time constraints, and access difficulties. This quality improvement (QI) project aimed to enhance awareness and engagement with campus mental health resources among Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) students.

METHOD: Guided by Pender's Health Promotion Model, this project implemented evidence-based interventions, including QR code advertisements and an educational seminar focused on mental health awareness, stigma reduction, and help-seeking behaviors. Anonymous pre- and post-intervention surveys were completed by 71 BSN students and analyzed using descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: Findings demonstrated increased familiarity with campus mental health resources, a 77% reduction in lack of awareness as a barrier, and improved comfort and confidence in seeking support.

CONCLUSION: Low-cost, scalable strategies can improve visibility, reduce barriers, and support student well-being.

articles.title: Review of Alcohol-Related Liver Disease-Reply.
Caring Contacts and Suicidality Among American Indian and Alaska Native Communities: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: For American Indian and Alaska Native communities, connectedness and belonging are strengths that may reduce suicide risk.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness of culturally-adapted Caring Contacts combined with optimal available resources (intervention) compared with optimal available resources alone (control) in reducing suicidal ideation, suicide attempts, and suicide-related hospitalizations.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: The CARE study was a blinded, 2-group randomized clinical trial conducted between May 2018 and September 2023 among 5 American Indian and Alaska Native communities in Alaska, the Northern Plains, and the Southern Plains, including 4 tribal communities and 1 tribal health organization. Participants were English-speaking adults (age ≥18 years) self-identifying as American Indian or Alaska Native with active suicidality. Analysis was conducted January through April 2024.

INTERVENTION: Caring Contacts is a low-cost intervention via brief, nondemanding messages exclusively focused on expressing care and interest sent by text message or greeting card on a pre-determined schedule over 12 months.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Outcomes included suicidal ideation in the past month (measured using the Suicidal Ideation Questionnaire-Junior [SIQ-Jr]), number of suicide attempts, and suicide-related hospitalizations over 12 months. Retention of active suicidality at follow-up was added as an additional outcome.

RESULTS: Of 1390 individuals prescreened for eligibility, 1202 consented and were screened for eligibility, and 709 (457 [64.5%] female; mean [SD] age, 35.4 [11.5] years) were enrolled and randomized, including 357 participants in the control group and 352 participants in the Caring Contacts intervention. Most participants (549 [77.4%]) self-identified as American Indian or Alaska Native only, and 160 participants (22.6%) as American Indian or Alaska Native plus another racial group. More than half of participants (392 [55.3%]) were never married. The mean (SD) SIQ-Jr score at baseline was 42.0 (13.8), and 604 participants (85.2%) had ever made a suicide attempt. Overall, 454 participants (64.0%) provided 12-month follow-up data. Between baseline and the 12-month follow-up, both groups showed significant reductions in suicidal ideation (mean [SD] score: Caring Contacts, 41.4 [13.7] vs 22.7 [15.3]; enhanced usual care, 42.5 [13.9] vs 23.1 [14.5]) and participants with a past-year suicide attempt (Caring Contacts, 169 of 352 participants [48.0%] vs 34/240 participants [14.2%]; enhanced usual care 155 of 357 participants [43.4%] vs 39 of 238 participants [16.4%]); however, no statistically significant between-group differences were found.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial of culturally adapted Caring Contacts among American Indian or Alaska Native adults with active suicidality, Caring Contacts did not improve suicidal outcomes beyond optimal available resources alone. Similar improvements in both groups may reflect regression to the mean, the therapeutic impact of compassionate baseline engagement with supportive community staff, or the active components of optimal available resources. Further research should explore these dynamics and other culturally grounded interventions.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02825771.

articles.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Remote Symptom Monitoring During Adjuvant Endocrine Therapy in Breast Cancer.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Adjuvant endocrine therapy (AET) reduces recurrence and mortality for women with early-stage hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, yet long-term adherence is suboptimal, largely due to treatment-related symptoms. Remote patient monitoring (RPM) is a potential strategy to improve symptom management, but evidence of its cost-effectiveness is limited.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of RPM for women prescribed AET for early-stage breast cancer.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This economic evaluation used data from the THRIVE trial, which randomized adult women initiating AET to an application (app), the app with tailored feedback, or enhanced usual care (EUC) at a large cancer center with 14 clinics from November 15, 2018, to June 11, 2021. The intervention lasted 6 months, and participants were followed up for 12 months (completed September 19, 2022). Each of the 2 interventions was compared with EUC, with uncertainty assessed using probabilistic sensitivity analyses. Data analyses were performed from February 1, 2025, to September 2, 2026.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes included costs, which were captured during the 12-month study period from a societal perspective, including medical costs, patient time and travel costs, clinician time costs responding to alerts, and app costs; quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), derived from patient-reported 12-item Short Form Health Survey scores; incremental cost-effectiveness ratios; and incremental net monetary benefit.

RESULTS: Of 304 participants randomized, 214 had complete data. The mean (SD) age was 58.9 (10.8) years. Mean (SD) total costs were highest for the EUC arm ($11 596.10 [$30 231.95]) compared with the app arm ($6682.15 [$12 963.34]; difference, -$4913.95 [95% CI, -$12 864.27 to $3036.37]) and app plus feedback arm ($11 407.85 [$47 068.42]; difference, -$188.25 [95% CI, -$12 830.16 to $12 453.66]). The mean (SD) estimated QALYs were similar across arms (app, 0.79 [012]; app plus feedback, 0.78 [0.13]; EUC, 0.78 [0.12]). This results in an incremental net monetary benefit of $5813.95 (95% uncertainty interval [UI], -$1860.00 to $16 492.58) for app group and $88.25 (95% UI, -$14 781.73 to $13 849.34) for the app plus feedback group at $100 000 per QALY. Probabilistic sensitivity analyses suggest that the app intervention had a 68.2% to 78.1% probability of being cost-effective compared with EUC across a willingness-to-pay threshold of $0 to $200 000 per QALY, while the app plus feedback intervention had a 53.6% to 70.8% probability of being cost-effective.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this economic evaluation of RPM for women receiving AET, app-only RPM showed lower costs with similar QALY compared with EUC. Its simpler design may also be more readily scalable than the app plus feedback intervention, supporting its potential as a pragmatic, value-based supportive care strategy in oncology.

articles.title: Functional Connectivity at Birth and Longitudinal Neurocognitive Development in Very Preterm Infants.
authors: Cincinnati Infant Neurodevelopment Early Prediction Study (CINEPS) Investigators
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Understanding how neonatal functional connectivity at birth is associated with later cognitive performance in infants born very preterm (VPT) may help identify early neuroimaging markers of neurodevelopment.

OBJECTIVE: To examine the associations between functional connectivity at birth and cognitive performance at age 2 and 3 years in children born VPT.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This prospective cohort study included infants born VPT (gestational age ≤32 weeks) from 5 level III and IV neonatal intensive care units in the greater Cincinnati, Ohio, area between September 16, 2016, and November 19, 2019. Maternal, pregnancy, delivery, and infant clinical data were collected from birth through discharge from the neonatal intensive care unit. Participants underwent magnetic resonance imaging at full-term-equivalent age at Cincinnati Children's Hospital using the same scanner. Image preprocessing and statistical analyses for this study were conducted between January 25, 2025, and July 30, 2026.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Cognitive outcomes were assessed at corrected age 2 and 3 years using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Third Edition and the Differential Ability Scales, Second Edition, respectively. Functional connectivity was measured within and between the default mode network (DMN), somatomotor network (SMN), dorsal attention network (DAN), frontoparietal control network, visual network (VIS), and cingulo-opercular network (CO). Associations between neonatal functional connectivity and longitudinal cognitive outcomes were examined using a bayesian hierarchical linear mixed-effects model.

RESULTS: A total of 257 infants born VPT (mean [SD] gestational age, 29.2 [2.5] weeks; 132 male [51.4%]) were included in the final longitudinal analysis. Stronger neonatal connectivity involving the DMN was positively associated with cognitive performance, including intra-DMN (0.23; 95% credible interval [CrI], 0.06-0.39) and DMN connections with the frontoparietal control network (0.24; 95% CrI, 0.07-0.40), SMN (0.20; 95% CrI, 0.02-0.37), VIS (0.32; 95% CrI, 0.13-0.51), and CO (0.39; 95% CrI, 0.21-0.56). Positive associations were also observed for SMN-VIS (0.27; 95% CrI, 0.12-0.43) and SMN-CO (0.26; 95% CrI, 0.09-0.44) connectivity. The SMN-VIS was the only connection showing a difference between assessments, with a less pronounced association at 3 years than at 2 years (interaction, -0.09; 95% CrI, -0.20 to <0.01).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of infants born VPT, neonatal functional network organization was associated with cognitive performance at corrected age 2 and 3 years. The findings highlight the relevance of distributed connectivity involving the DMN and SMN to later cognitive outcomes and support further investigation of neonatal functional connectivity as an early marker of neurodevelopment.

Development of wheat lines resistant to blast disease using gamma-ray-induced mutagenesis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Wheat blast, caused by the fungus Magnaporthe oryzae Triticum (MoT), is an escalating threat to global food security due to its devastating impact on yield. Classical breeding for durable resistance is limited by scarce genetic resources. This study aimed to address this critical need by utilizing mutation breeding with gamma-ray irradiation to develop blast-resistant wheat lines.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Seeds from five popular high-yielding Bangladeshi wheat varieties viz. BARI Gom 27, BARI Gom 28, BARI Gom 29, BARI Gom 30, and BARI Gom 33, were treated with doses of gamma rays (200 Gy, 250 Gy, and 300 Gy). The mutant population was screened in subsequent generations for disease resistance and agronomic performances. Detached leaf assay (DLA) was used as a preliminary screening method on M2 progenies. The resistance of selected lines was then validated through artificial inoculation of MoT under field conditions in the M3 generation.

RESULTS: Out of 1710 total M1 plants that survived gamma-ray treatment, preliminary bioassay results (DLA) revealed that nine gamma-irradiated M2 progenies demonstrated strong resistance against MoT. After field screening with artificial inoculation in the M3 generation, we identified five mutants out of 225 plants. These artificially inoculated M3 plants showed differential reactions to MoT infection. Specifically, two entries were observed to be completely free from blast infection (0% disease incidence and severity), while another three entries had low disease severity (0.17-1.0%) and disease incidence (3-4%) with high grain yield.

CONCLUSIONS: The two promising M3 mutant lines developed through gamma irradiation of seeds represent strong candidates for the development of a blast-resistant wheat variety. Their high level of resistance and improved grain yield under field conditions make them invaluable genetic resources. Further field screening and bioassays are warranted to ensure stable varietal development.

articles.title: Rupture of a right gastric artery pseudoaneurysm presenting with hemorrhagic shock two months after gastric endoscopic submucosal dissection.
articles.abstract: An 82-year-old woman underwent endoscopic submucosal dissection for a 10-mm early gastric cancer lesion on the lesser curvature of the gastric angle. The lesion was resected en bloc without any adverse events, and the patient was discharged uneventfully. Follow-up esophagogastroduodenoscopy performed 2 months later showed healing of the post-endoscopic submucosal dissection ulcer. However, at 4 h after the esophagogastroduodenoscopy procedure, the patient developed hematemesis while in the hospital and underwent cardiopulmonary resuscitation because of a weakly palpable carotid pulse. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a pseudoaneurysm in the right gastric artery along the lesser curvature of the gastric angle, with extravasation of contrast medium into the stomach. Emergency interventional radiology was performed, and hemostasis was achieved by transcatheter arterial embolization with N-butyl-2-cyanoacrylate. Although there are very few reported cases of ruptured pseudoaneurysm leading to hemorrhagic shock after gastric endoscopic submucosal dissection, pseudoaneurysm rupture should be considered among differential diagnoses when patients present with hematemesis or melena accompanied by shock, and contrast-enhanced computed tomography should be performed.

articles.title: Pretreatment antibiotic exposure and mortality following immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy in non-small cell lung cancer: an infection-stratified propensity-matched analysis.
articles.journal: Clinical & translational oncology : official publication of the Federation of Spanish Oncology Societies and of the National Cancer Institute of Mexico
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pretreatment antibiotic exposure has been associated with inferior outcomes during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy, but whether this reflects an ICI specific effect or underlying clinical vulnerability remains uncertain.

METHODS: Adults with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) treated with ICIs from 2015 through 2024 were identified in the TriNetX Research Network. Recent antibiotic exposure was defined as systemic antibiotic use during days 30 to 1 before ICI initiation. Propensity score matching balanced clinical and treatment-related covariates. Primary outcomes were all cause mortality at 90 and 365 days. Sensitivity analyses included landmarking, remote exposure, infection stratification, and a non-ICI comparator.

RESULTS: Among 68,723 patients, 19,080 had recent antibiotic exposure; 17,955 per group remained after matching. Mortality was higher with antibiotic exposure at 90 days (17.7% vs 13.7%; HR 1.34, 95% CI 1.27 to 1.41; P<0.001) and 365 days (43.0% vs 37.2%; HR 1.23, 95% CI 1.19 to 1.27; P<0.001). Associations attenuated after exclusion of early deaths. The association was similar between ICI and non-ICI cohorts at 90 days but modestly stronger with ICI at 365 days. Remote exposure did not reproduce the adverse association.

CONCLUSIONS: Recent antibiotic exposure was associated with increased mortality during ICI therapy, but the non-ICI comparison and landmark analyses suggest that much of the short-term excess mortality reflects clinical vulnerability rather than an ICI specific effect. The modestly stronger 1-year association with ICI therapy is hypothesis generating.

articles.title: Development and Preliminary Evaluation of a Toolkit Aimed at Improving Implementation of the End-Stage Kidney Disease Life Plan.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: End-stage kidney disease (ESKD) requires lifelong kidney replacement therapy (KRT), including complex decisions about treatment modality and vascular access. The 2019 Kidney Disease Outcomes Quality Initiative (KDOQI) Clinical Practice Guideline for Vascular Access prioritizes the ESKD Life Plan, a patient-centered collaborative, multidisciplinary framework. Implementation has been limited by clinician time constraints, fragmented care coordination, and patients' difficulty navigating complex decisions without adequate education.

OBJECTIVE: To describe the iterative co-development and preliminary evaluation of the ESKD Life Plan Implementation Toolkit, designed to facilitate shared decision-making around KRT modality and vascular access selection in alignment with current KDOQI guidelines.

DESIGN: Toolkit content was based on prior qualitative research with ESKD patients, supportive others, and clinicians. The toolkit spans five domains: care team identification, patient goals and values, KRT education, treatment selection, and Life Plan completion.

PARTICIPANTS: ESKD patients, supportive others, and clinicians aged ≥ 18.

MAIN MEASURES: Following iterative refinement with community co-creators, a cross-sectional survey incorporating the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT) was administered.

KEY RESULTS: Of 128 survey participants, 63 (49.2%) completed ≥ 50% of items, including 25 patients (46.3%), 17 supportive others (31.5%), and 12 clinicians (22.2%). PEMAT ratings were highly favorable across all domains, with ≥ 89% agreement on written materials and videos. Feedback suggested simplifying medical terminology, refining visual hierarchy, and offering an alternative to graphic clinical photographs.

CONCLUSIONS: The toolkit demonstrated strong acceptability among nephrology patients, supportive others, and clinicians. By integrating disease education with structured values elicitation and a Best Case/Worst Case decision framework, the toolkit operationalizes the patient-centered approach central to KDOQI guidelines.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NA.

articles.title: Proteomic and Metabolomic Profiling in Moyamoya Disease: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a progressive cerebrovascular disorder characterized by stenosis and occlusion of the internal carotid artery branches, leading to chronic ischemia and aberrant collateral vessel formation. Despite its clinical significance, the pathophysiology is not fully understood, and identification of MMD-related biomarkers may supplement invasive digital subtraction angiography, the current gold standard for diagnosis, as well as provide additional insights into prognosis and disease progression. High-throughput metabolomics and proteomics offer potential to elucidate disease mechanisms and identify diagnostic markers. Our goal is to systematically review the current literature on metabolomics and proteomics in MMD using high-throughput methods, identify candidate biomarkers, characterize implicated pathways, and assess the diagnostic and prognostic value of molecular signatures. We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus databases through April 13, 2026, for studies analyzing serum or CSF from MMD patients using mass spectrometry, nuclear magnetic resonance, or immunoassays. Studies were included if they employed case-control, cohort, cross-sectional, or RCT designs in human subjects. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts, and full texts, with disputes resolved by a third reviewer. Quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. We extracted the top differentially expressed proteins or metabolites, results of any enrichment pathway analyses, and demographics information from each study. From 3071 studies identified, 31 were included after removing 1558 duplicates and excluding 1482 irrelevant studies. Recurrent differentially expressed proteins implicated inflammatory signaling (CRABP-I, PDGF-BB, IL-7, complement proteins), angiogenesis (VEGF, Ang-2, MMP-9), and cytoskeletal remodeling (FLNA, ZYX, keratins), while consistent metabolomic signatures highlighted BCAA elevation, urea cycle disruption, and lipid remodeling. Pathway analyses recurrently implicated immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, cytoskeletal reorganization, hypoxia signaling, and metabolic reprogramming. Demographically, cohorts were predominantly adult, East Asian, and bilateral MMD, with a sample-size-weighted mean age of 40.0 years. High-throughput proteomics and metabolomics identified recurring molecular alterations in Moyamoya disease, commonly identifying inflammatory signaling, pathological angiogenesis, and cytoskeletal remodeling as potential pathophysiological mechanisms. Despite predominantly good-quality studies (mean Newcastle-Ottawa Scale 6.77 ± 0.67), major limitations included small sample sizes, single-center designs, and regional specificity. Validation in larger, ethnically diverse, multicenter cohorts is essential before clinical translation of candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Reducing the Burden of Hypoglycemia in Type 1 Diabetes: The Impact of FLO23011 on Patient-Reported Outcomes and Glycemic Correlates of Treatment Response.
articles.journal: Diabetes therapy : research, treatment and education of diabetes and related disorders
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The aim of this study was to compare patient-reported outcomes (PROs) related to hypoglycemia recovery with FLO23011, a novel multi-energy substrate for hypoglycemia (MESH) recovery drink combining 15 g glucose with beta-hydroxybutyrate (BHB), versus standard glucose gel in adults with type 1 diabetes, and to explore associations between continuous glucose monitoring (CGM)-derived metrics and perceived and objective treatment response.

METHODS: In a randomized, open-label, crossover study, 12 adults with type 1 diabetes used FLO23011 and standard glucose gel to treat hypoglycemia for two 6-week periods, with continuous glucose monitoring throughout. PROs were assessed using a study-specific 14-domain questionnaire and exit interviews. Exploratory CGM analyses examined patient-relevant recovery signals: glucose-band exposure versus psychological PRO scores, and baseline glycemic variability versus time-in-range (TIR) response.

RESULTS: FLO23011 was rated more favorably than glucose gel in 13/14 domains. Among recovery-related items, 70% preferred FLO23011 for reduced aftereffects and 80% for return to daily activities; 82% preferred FLO23011 for sense of control, 73% for dosing confidence, and 64% for overall hypoglycemia management. In exit interviews, 92% rated FLO23011 "very/extremely" effective and 92% reported "never" or "rarely" experiencing post-hypoglycemia hangover symptoms with FLO23011. Participants described faster cognitive recovery, reduced disruption, and greater confidence. In exploratory analyses, reduced Level 1 hypoglycemia exposure was associated with higher reduced-worry and management-ability ratings (n = 5; ρ = 0.90; P = 0.037). Higher baseline coefficient of variation (CV) was associated with greater TIR improvement with FLO23011 (n = 9; ρ = 0.917; P = 0.0005).

CONCLUSIONS: FLO23011 was associated with more favorable patient-reported hypoglycemia recovery than glucose gel, with participants reporting benefits for aftereffects, daily functioning, and confidence. In exploratory CGM-PRO analyses, strong correlations in small subsets suggested that perceived benefit aligns with reduced Level 1 hypoglycemia exposure, and that baseline glycemic variability may predict objective response. These findings support evaluating hypoglycemia treatments on patient-reported recovery alongside glycemic outcomes. A graphical abstract is available with this article.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ISRCTN Registry, ISRCTN19855666. Retrospectively registered, 11 June 2026.

articles.title: Longitudinal changes in body composition and their association with adverse clinical events among candidates awaiting deceased-donor kidney transplantation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prolonged waiting for deceased-donor kidney transplantation may lead to progressive physical deterioration, particularly in countries with limited organ availability. However, the clinical significance of longitudinal changes in body composition remains unclear. This study investigated longitudinal changes in body composition and their association with subsequent adverse clinical events.

METHODS: This retrospective longitudinal study included 87 candidates who underwent annual bioelectrical impedance analysis in 2023, 2024, and 2025. Changes in body composition were evaluated, and multivariable logistic regression assessed associations with adverse clinical events during the subsequent 1-year follow-up.

RESULTS: During follow-up, 24 patients experienced adverse clinical events. Between 2023 and 2025, skeletal muscle index (SMI), fat-free mass index (FFMI), and phase angle decreased, whereas extracellular water-to-total body water ratio increased (all P < 0.05). Patients who experienced adverse clinical events showed greater declines in FFMI (median change, - 0.75 vs. -0.10 kg/m²; P = 0.003) and SMI (- 0.35 vs. -0.10 kg/m²; P = 0.013). After adjustment for age, diabetes mellitus, dialysis vintage, and baseline FFMI, a greater decline in FFMI remained independently associated with adverse clinical events (odds ratio, 0.44; 95% confidence interval, 0.24-0.72; P = 0.003), whereas baseline FFMI was not.

CONCLUSIONS: Modest longitudinal changes in body composition were observed during prolonged waiting for deceased-donor kidney transplantation. Longitudinal decline in FFMI, rather than baseline FFMI, was independently associated with adverse clinical events. Serial FFMI assessment may provide additional information for risk stratification during the transplant waiting period.

articles.title: Palmitoylation-related gene signature analysis links ENPP6 to potential protection of renal tubule against ischemia-reperfusion injury.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI), particularly ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI), lacks effective targeted therapies. Protein S-palmitoylation is a reversible lipid modification involved in cellular stress responses, but its role in AKI remains unclear. We aimed to identify palmitoylation-related genes in AKI and explore their potential functions.

METHODS: Public transcriptome datasets of AKI kidney tissues were analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Palmitoylation-related common hub genes were screened by integrating DEG analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). Single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) data and online clinical databases were used to determine cellular localization and clinical relevance. ENPP6 was further validated in a mouse renal IRI model and hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R)-treated renal tubule cells.

RESULTS: Six candidate common hub genes were identified: EDN1, VMP1, ENPP6, MYC, CXCR4, and EFNA1. Among them, ENPP6 was enriched in renal tubular cells and showed the strongest association with indices of renal function. ENPP6 expression was significantly reduced in the renal tubules of IRI mice at both the mRNA and protein levels. In renal tubule cells, ENPP6 overexpression was accompanied by increased overall protein S-palmitoylation. Functionally, ENPP6 overexpression improved cell viability and alleviated H/R-induced injury.

CONCLUSIONS: ENPP6 expression was reduced in renal IRI and was positively associated with renal function. In renal tubular cells, ENPP6 overexpression was accompanied by increased global protein S-palmitoylation and reduced H/R-induced injury. These findings identify ENPP6 as a potential protective factor and a candidate for further mechanistic investigation in ischemic AKI.

articles.title: Reply to the letter to the editor from Drs. Delrue and Speeckaert regarding "inflammatory and traditional risk factors associated with the progression of chronic kidney disease in patients with rheumatoid arthritis".
Echocardiographic phenotypes of opioid-induced cardiotoxicity: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: Opioid cardiotoxicity is an increasing clinical concern, yet its echocardiographic manifestations are heterogeneous and poorly characterized. This narrative review synthesizes available evidence, maps the principal echocardiographic phenotypes of opioid-related cardiac injury, and identifies major knowledge gaps. A structured PubMed search (January 2014-December 2024) combined opioid and echocardiographic terms without language restriction. Human and animal studies of any design assessing cardiac structure or function by echocardiography after acute or chronic opioid exposure were eligible. Of 209 records, 41 were included and grouped by dominant phenotype. No formal protocol (e.g., PRISMA) or risk-of-bias appraisal was applied. Five distinct-and often conflicting-phenotypes emerged: (1) severe, potentially reversible global left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVEF as low as 20%), sometimes progressing to cardiogenic shock yet normalising within 48-72 h; (2) Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, classic after withdrawal and predominantly reverse after intoxication; (3) right ventricular dysfunction with pulmonary hypertension, usually secondary to hypoxia or left-sided failure but occasionally isolated; (4) consistent cardioprotection in animal ischaemia-reperfusion models, unsupported by any prospective human echocardiographic study; and (5) a mechanically normal profile despite QTc exceeding 610 ms and torsades de pointes. Phenotypes 1-3 rest largely on case reports, and many studies are confounded by co-administered cocaine, benzodiazepines or α2-adrenoceptor agonists. Opioid cardiac effects are context-dependent, and mechanical toxicity diverges from electrical toxicity: a normal echocardiogram does not exclude lethal arrhythmia, so echocardiography and serial QTc assessment are complementary rather than interchangeable. Prospective studies with advanced imaging are needed to establish phenotype frequency and determinants.

articles.title: T cell exhaustion in cancer.
articles.abstract: T cell exhaustion is an antigen-driven differentiation program originally defined in chronic infection and now recognized as a major determinant of antitumor immunity. It is best characterized in CD8+ T cells, in which chronic stimulation induces functional impairment, inhibitory-receptor expression, transcriptional and epigenetic reprogramming, and metabolic dysfunction. Exhausted T cells are heterogeneous, ranging from progenitor populations that retain proliferative capacity and responsiveness to programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) blockade to terminally exhausted states with limited reversibility. In solid tumors, immune checkpoint blockade acts largely through tumor-reactive exhausted CD8+ T cells. In classic Hodgkin lymphoma, frequent loss of major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I and retention of MHC class II suggest a greater contribution of cytotoxic CD4+ T cells, and PD-1 blockade may reinvigorate dysfunctional or exhaustion-like CD4+ T cells. Exhaustion also affects chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell and bispecific T cell engager therapies, where repetitive stimulation impairs T cell persistence and function, and allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation, where donor T cell exhaustion may influence graft-versus-host disease and graft-versus-leukemia activity. This review summarizes the mechanisms and clinical significance of T cell exhaustion across solid and hematologic malignancies and how exhaustion state shapes therapeutic response.

articles.title: Venous thromboembolism after breast cancer surgery: incidence, predictive factors and outcomes in 270,564 patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breast cancer surgery is generally considered to be low risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, when VTE occurs, it may lead to severe complications and increased mortality. This study aimed to determine the incidence, predictors, and clinical impact of postoperative VTE following breast cancer surgery using a large, multicenter surgical database.

METHODS: The American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) database (2008-2023) was queried to identify female patients undergoing surgery for breast cancer without concurrent reconstruction. Patients were stratified according to postoperative VTE occurrence. Demographics, comorbidities, laboratory values, operative characteristics, and 30-day outcomes were compared. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of VTE and to construct a predictive model, which was internally validated using bootstrap resampling.

RESULTS: Among 270,564 patients included, 465 (0.2%) developed postoperative VTE. Of these, 247 (53.1%) had deep vein thrombosis, 177 (38.1%) pulmonary embolism, and 41 (8.8%) both. Patients who developed VTE were older, had higher body mass index (BMI), greater comorbidity burden, and longer operative times (all p < 0.001). They also demonstrated lower preoperative serum albumin, hematocrit, prothrombin time, and albumin-to-creatinine ratio. VTE was associated with significantly longer hospital stays, increased rates of reoperation and readmission, and a more than 20-fold higher crude 30-day mortality (1.9% vs. 0.1%) (all p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, increasing age (OR 1.26 per 10 years), BMI (OR 1.17 per 5 kg/m²), congestive heart failure (OR 2.43), metastatic cancer (OR 2.05), lower serum albumin (OR 0.63 per 1 g/dL), and longer operative duration (OR 1.09 per 30 min) were independently associated with postoperative VTE. Compared with partial mastectomy, total mastectomy (OR 2.58), modified radical mastectomy (OR 2.22), and radical mastectomy (OR 2.80) were associated with significantly higher odds of postoperative VTE. The predictive model demonstrated acceptable discrimination (AUC 0.717; optimism-corrected 0.700) and good calibration. Age, BMI, congestive heart failure, metastatic cancer, mastectomy and operative time remained associated with VTE in all sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSION: Postoperative VTE following breast cancer surgery is uncommon but associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Advanced age, obesity, cardiac comorbidity, metastatic disease, hypoalbuminemia, longer operative duration, and greater surgical extent were independently associated with increased thromboembolic risk. Awareness of these risk factors may support individualized perioperative risk assessment and thromboprophylaxis decisions, as recommended by current consensus guidance, and facilitate earlier recognition of postoperative VTE.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Acceptability of a patient support and educational intervention for black breast cancer survivors.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Black women with breast cancer in the US experience worse survival and lower quality of life. Addressing information needs and providing emotional and social support may improve survivorship experiences. This study evaluated feasibility and acceptability of an intervention to support Black breast cancer patients.

METHODS: English-speaking, Black, female breast cancer survivors diagnosed with stage I-III breast cancer within five years were invited to participate in a six-week group intervention (virtual or in-person). The intervention was adapted from the PAVING the Path to Wellness program based on a prior qualitative study. Primary endpoints were feasibility and acceptability. Exploratory endpoints included unmet information needs and well-being. Exit interviews with a subset of participants described experiences with, and benefits from, the intervention.

RESULTS: 20 women with a mean age of 59.1 years (SD 8.2) and predominantly diagnosed at stage I (n = 11; 55%) participated. Most participants (n = 15; 88.3%) reported high levels of satisfaction and that the program provided new information relevant to their needs and helped motivate lifestyle changes. Nearly all participants (n = 15; 88.3%) expressed that it is important for other Black breast cancer survivors to receive a similar intervention.

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates proof of concept and provides insights into participant preferences. Broader-scale testing is needed to assess generalizability.

GOV, REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT05700396, Registration Date: 2023-01 -17.

articles.title: Insights into interleukin-7 gene and protein expression in type 2 diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, and periodontitis: evidence from meta-analysis and two independent cohort studies.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to integrate current evidence on Interleukin-7 (IL-7) in the context of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM), Dyslipidemia (Dysl), and Periodontitis (Perio). We performed a meta-analysis on IL-7 protein levels in individuals with these conditions, and we investigated gene and protein IL-7 levels in 217 participants from two independent cohorts, distributed into: (i) poorly-controlled T2DM, Dysl, and Perio (T2DMpoor_Dysl_P), (ii) well-controlled T2DM, Dysl, and Perio (T2DMwell_Dysl_P), (iii) Dysl and Perio (Dysl_P), (iv) Periodontitis (Perio), and (v) Healthy individuals (Control). Participants underwent physical, biochemical, and periodontal examinations. IL7 gene expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells was quantified by RT-qPCR, and IL-7 protein levels were measured in gingival crevicular fluid (GCF), plasma, and saliva. Meta-analysis of 454 participants showed no statistical differences in IL-7 protein levels in GCF or plasma/serum, with substantial heterogeneity among studies. Our two independent cohorts demonstrated that IL7 mRNA was higher in T2DMwell_Dysl_P than in T2DMpoor_Dysl_P subjects.
