In cohort 1, IL-7 protein levels were higher in GCF from healthy sites, similar among groups in diseased sites, and in plasma. Saliva in cohort 2 showed low IL-7 levels in all groups. Significant inverse correlations were found between IL-7 protein and anthropometric measures, and worsened periodontal parameters. These findings and the IL7 mRNA expression replicated across both cohorts lead to conclude that IL-7 is a potential candidate biomarker of immunometabolic and periodontal status, despite its variance in biological compartments. Further clinically similar studies enrolling larger populations are required to confirm these results and assess the biological and clinical relevance of IL-7.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Dapagliflozin, Glimepiride, and Metformin Fixed-Dose Combination Tablet in Type 2 Diabetes: A Phase III Trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The global burden of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is rapidly increasing, with India contributing significantly to the disease prevalence and associated economic burden. Despite metformin being the first-line therapy, many patients require combination treatment due to the progressive and multifactorial nature of T2DM. Fixed-dose combinations (FDCs) of drugs with complementary mechanisms may improve glycemic control, adherence, and treatment outcomes. This study has evaluated efficacy and safety of FDC of dapagliflozin (DAPA), glimepiride (GLIM), and metformin (MET) immediate release (IR) tablet versus co-administration of GLIM and MET tablets in patients with T2DM.

METHODS: This phase 3, randomized, open-label study included 536 Indian patients with T2DM [glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) ≥ 8.0% and ≤ 11%], randomized (1:1:1:1) into four arms in primary treatment period (up to Week 16): FDC of DAPA + GLIM + MET [5 mg+1 mg+500 mg (Test 1)] or [5 mg+1 mg+1000 mg (Test 2)] twice-daily, or co-administration of GLIM and MET (1 mg and 500 mg) (Comparator 1) or GLIM and MET (1 mg and 1000 mg) (Comparator 2) twice-daily. Patients with HbA1c ≥ 7.0% at week 16 entered an uptitration period (increased GLIM dose to 2 mg; Weeks 16-28). Change in HbA1c from baseline to Week 16 was the primary endpoint.

RESULTS: At Week 16, least-square mean HbA1c reduction was significantly greater with Test 1 (- 2.17%) versus Comparator 1 (- 1.64%, p = 0.0047) and Test 2 (- 2.25%) versus Comparator 2 (- 1.72%, p < 0.0001). Similarly, the proportion of patients achieving HbA1c < 7.0% at Week 16 was significantly greater in Test 1 versus Comparator 1 and Test 2 versus Comparator 2 (p < 0.0002 and p < 0.0001, respectively). Reduction in HbA1c, fasting, and postprandial blood glucose from baseline to Weeks 12, 16, and 28 was significant in all arms. Overall, treatments were well tolerated.

CONCLUSIONS: The FDC of DAPA + GLIM + MET IR tablet demonstrated superior glycemic control over co-administration of glimepiride and metformin and acceptable safety profile, making it an effective therapeutic option for T2DM management.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials Registry India, CTRI/2022/06/043249.

articles.title: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic outcomes in women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy at 12 months postpartum : The PreCareFem Cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy are risk factors for later cardiovascular and chronic kidney disease. Early postpartum trajectories of blood pressure and metabolic recovery in this high-risk population are still insufficiently defined.

METHODS: A prospective, single-center, observational cohort study was conducted in the Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Women's Healthcare Prevention Program (PreCareFem) at the University Hospital St. Pölten, Austria. Participants were enrolled on presentation between 1 June 2023, and 31 March 2025. Cardiovascular and metabolic surrogate parameters, including automated blood pressure measurement, anthropometric evaluation, cardiovascular, kidney and metabolic parameters, lifestyle assessment following the components of the "Life's Essential 8", and urine albumin-creatinine ratio were assessed peripartum and at 3-6 and 12 months postpartum.

RESULTS: A total of 91 women with preeclampsia (PE; n = 66) and gestational hypertension (GH; n = 25) were enrolled. At 12 months postpartum, 31% met the diagnostic criteria for arterial hypertension (PE 29%, GH 36%), 18% for prediabetes and 3% for diabetes. More than half (52%) had LDL levels > 100 mg/dL and 32% had low HDL levels. Obesity was diagnosed in 24% of participants, 8% of women were diagnosed with CKD 12 months postpartum. Low-grade albuminuria (uACR 10-30 mg/g) was observed in 21% of women with PE compared to 8% in women with GH.

CONCLUSION: A significant number of women were diagnosed with arterial hypertension, early kidney impairment and/or metabolic abnormalities 1 year following hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. These findings highlight the need for a structured, multidisciplinary postpartum follow-up to address an underutilized opportunity for prevention of cardiovascular and chronic kidney disease.

articles.title: The risk of rhegmatogenous retinal detachment associated with topical pilocarpine: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the risk of developing rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) in patients treated with topical pilocarpine.

DESIGN: Systematic review.

METHODS: In October 2024 and March 2026, we searched six electronic databases (PubMed, EMBASE, CENTRAL, SCOPUS, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar) for comparative studies published through March 2026 to evaluate the risk of RRD in patients treated with topical pilocarpine. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials, cohort studies, and case-control studies comparing patients aged ≥ 40 years who received any dose, frequency, or duration of topical pilocarpine (for any indication) with an appropriate control group (placebo or an alternative topical ophthalmic therapy). We excluded non-randomized trials, case reports, case series, non-original articles, non-English studies, abstracts, non-human studies, studies without a control group, single-dose pilocarpine administration, pilocarpine as part of multi-drug regimens, non-topical non-ophthalmic routes of administration, participants < 40 years, and studies in which the control group also received pilocarpine. We conducted methodological quality and risk-of-bias assessments using the National Institutes of Health (NIH) quality assessment tools. Subsequently, a structured qualitative synthesis was conducted, summarizing key study characteristics, exposure parameters (e.g., pilocarpine dosing, formulation, and exposure duration), and RRD incidence. Study Methods are detailed in the full protocol developed prospectively and uploaded to PROSPERO (CRD420261305829).

RESULTS: We included 10 studies, with 5,421 patients in the pilocarpine groups and 5,443 in the non-pilocarpine groups, with some overlap due to one pooled analysis. Study designs were heterogeneous, with varying pilocarpine dosing regimens (0.2-4%, 1-4 times daily), sample sizes (13-4,494 patients per group), and mean participant ages (49-70.5 years). Exposure durations ranged from 14 to 30 days (short-term) to 24 months (long-term), and follow-up times ranged from 14 days to 24 months. RRD was rare, with no events reported in nine studies (1,876 participants). In one large retrospective cohort (8,988 participants), RRD occurred in 35 pilocarpine-exposed eyes compared with 15 controls, with a 3.14-fold increased risk (adjusted HR 3.14, 95% CI 1.66-5.93, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Because all reported RRD events derived from a single retrospective cohort and the remaining nine studies were event-free, quantitative pooling was not feasible and this review functions as a structured narrative around one dataset. The available evidence suggests a possible association between pilocarpine use and RRD, particularly in predisposed patients, but its low certainty means the finding should be considered hypothesis-generating, and larger prospective studies are needed to confirm it.

articles.title: When being wrong moves intensive care forward.
Individualized treatment effects of high flow nasal oxygen in immunocompromised patients.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: High flow nasal oxygen (HFNO) has become a common first-line practice for acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (ARF). In immunocompromised patients, ARF is the leading cause of ICU admission, yet a randomized trial found no overall benefit of HFNO in this population.

OBJECTIVES: To assess whether baseline characteristics influence HFNO's effectiveness in preventing invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) in immunocompromised patients with ARF.

METHODS: A causal forest machine-learning algorithm was derived in the HIGH trial (776 patients randomized to HFNO or conventional oxygen) to predict the HFNO effects on day-28 IMV incidence. Patients with a "do-not-intubate" order (n = 72) were excluded. Model performance was validated through 500 bootstrap iterations and patients were categorized into terciles based on predicted HFNO benefit. Transportability of the model was assessed in an independent observational cohort (818 patients).

MAIN RESULTS: Among the 704 participants, HFNO's average effect on day-28 IMV was not significant. However, substantial heterogeneity in treatment responses was identified (predicted benefit: from 20.2% [IQR 15.5%-23.9%] absolute IMV risk reduction with HFNO to 7.4% risk reduction [2.9%-11.2%] with conventional oxygen). Patients with the highest predicted benefit were older, more frequently solid organ transplant recipients, less neutropenic, more severely hypoxemic/tachycardic, but with lower non-respiratory sequential organ failure assessment (SOFA) scores. In this subgroup, HFNO was associated with a significant lower incidence of IMV. In the observational cohort, the benefit-ranking performance was preserved, although absolute effect estimates were less calibrated.

CONCLUSIONS: These results suggest HFNO might benefit specific immunocompromised patients with ARF. Further prospective studies are needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: The right drug in the wrong biological state? Alkaline phosphatase and cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury.
Addressing spiritual, religious, and existential distress in post-intensive care syndrome: practical tools across the ICU survivorship care continuum.
Establishing curriculum priorities for intensive care recovery education: an international Delphi study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To effectively support recovery, intensive care unit (ICU) clinicians require training to identify patients at risk of post-intensive care syndrome and implement interventions during and after ICU admission. This study aimed to identify and prioritise curriculum topics for educating interprofessional ICU clinicians on evidence-based ICU recovery care across the continuum of critical illness.

METHODS: A two-round e-Delphi study followed by a structured consensus meeting endorsed by the European Society of Intensive Care Medicine (ESICM) was conducted. A steering committee generated an initial list of curriculum topics. In round 1, participants rated topic importance (9-point Likert scale) and suggested additional topics. In round 2, they rated newly identified topics and ranked priorities. Topics reaching consensus (≥70% rating as critical [7-9]; ≤15% rating as not important [1-3]) were discussed during the final consensus meeting.

RESULTS: Participants' mean age was 43.5 (±10.5) years and they were predominantly female (n = 90, 66.7%). Priority topics included early mobilisation during ICU admission, post-intensive care syndrome, delirium prevention and management, implementation of the ABCDEF bundle, and cognitive support and rehabilitation. The final set of learning modules for a future curriculum was established.

CONCLUSION: Priority topics and learning modules for an expert-developed curriculum framework for ICU recovery were established with interprofessional ICU clinicians through a structured international consensus process with moderate levels of participant retention between the two Delphi rounds and full consensus agreement among experts. This framework may support in delivering recovery-focused care across the continuum of critical illness.

articles.title: Sodium bicarbonate therapy for metabolic acidosis in critically ill patients: a Bayesian systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the effects of sodium bicarbonate therapy on mortality and renal outcomes in critically ill adults with metabolic acidosis.

METHODS: We performed a systematic review and Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing intravenous sodium bicarbonate with placebo or usual care in adult intensive care unit patients with metabolic acidosis. MEDLINE, Embase and CENTRAL were searched from inception to December 2025, with an updated search on 2 April 2026. The primary outcome was short-term all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included renal replacement therapy (RRT) initiation, 90-day mortality, RRT-free days, vasopressor-free days, intensive care unit and hospital length of stay and adverse events.

RESULTS: Four RCTs including 1544 patients were analysed. Sodium bicarbonate did not show a clear short-term mortality benefit (RR 0.94, 95% CrI 0.73-1.22), with a posterior probability of benefit of 72.1%. For RRT initiation, sodium bicarbonate was associated with a lower risk (RR 0.74, 95% CrI 0.59-0.98), with a posterior probability of benefit of 97.2%. Effects on other outcomes were small or imprecise, and no consistent safety signal was identified.

CONCLUSION: Current randomised evidence does not demonstrate a clear survival benefit from sodium bicarbonate therapy in critically ill adults with metabolic acidosis, but suggests a high probability of reducing RRT initiation. Further trials should define the patients most likely to benefit. PROSPERO registration: CRD420251246519.

articles.title: Cytomegalovirus and cancer stem cells: a hidden alliance in tumor progression and therapy resistance.
articles.abstract: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) is a widely spread β-herpesvirus that can establish life-long latency in the human host and remains asymptomatic in healthy immunocompetent hosts. In immunocompromised populations, such as transplant recipients, HIV/AIDS patients, and cancer patients, CMV presents an opportunity to reactivate and influence disease progression. There is a growing, but still contested, body of evidence suggesting that while CMV is not a classical oncogenic virus, it may act as an oncomodulatory virus, exerting an indirect impact on tumor biology. CMV DNA, RNA, or proteins have been detected in tumors such as glioblastoma, breast, colorectal, and pancreatic cancers in several studies, although other studies using comparable or more sensitive assays have failed to detect the virus in the same tumor types, so this association should not be regarded as established. In addition, CMV presence in tumor tissues is associated with immune suppression, therapy resistance, angiogenesis, and inflammation-all indicators of hallmark cancer progression. Of particular interest related to CMV in the context of cancer is its potential relationship with cancer stem cells (CSCs), a rare cell subpopulation of tumor cells, although a potent subpopulation for self-renewal, metastasis, and resistance to conventional cancer therapies. CMV has been shown to modulate numerous signaling pathways (Wnt/β-catenin, PI3K/Akt, Notch, and This review summarizes emerging connections between CMV infection and CSC biology, highlighting the ability of the virus to alter tumor behavior through effects on pluripotent transcription factors (i.e., Oct4, Sox2, Nanog), modulation of cytokine networks (i.e., IL-10, TGF-β), and inducing immune escape mechanisms. As we develop a better understanding of the CMV-CSC connection, this may inform new therapeutic strategies that utilize antiviral approaches to work alongside contemporary CSC-targeted therapies, providing relief in instances of drug resistance, relapse, and poor prognosis in CMV-positive tumors. We also critically appraise the strength and consistency of the underlying evidence, propose reasons for conflicting findings, and put forward a context-dependent, bidirectional model of CMV-CSC interaction together with testable predictions.

articles.title: Correction: Prevalence of and risk factors for low anterior resection syndrome based on the international consensus definition: a multicenter cross-sectional observational study.
Refining ECPR candidate selection: from fixed criteria to a dynamic probability-of-benefit framework.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) has emerged as a rescue strategy for selected patients with refractory cardiac arrest. However, identifying patients most likely to achieve neurologically meaningful survival remains challenging. Conventional selection criteria, including age, initial rhythm, witnessed arrest, bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), and no-flow and low-flow duration, are clinically useful but may be insufficient when interpreted as isolated thresholds.

METHODS: We conducted a narrative review of contemporary evidence on ECPR patient selection, incorporating randomized trials, observational studies, registries, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, and current guideline and consensus recommendations. Evidence was critically evaluated with particular attention to patient-level prognostic factors, arrest setting, dynamic physiological and metabolic variables, ECPR logistics, and system-level determinants of outcome.

RESULTS: Current evidence supports a multidimensional rather than single-variable approach to ECPR candidacy. Favorable arrest characteristics, potentially reversible etiology, shorter low-flow duration, and preserved physiological reserve remain important; however, chronological low-flow time should be interpreted alongside the quality and effectiveness of ongoing CPR. Dynamic information-including transient return of spontaneous circulation, lactate kinetics, arterial pH, end-tidal carbon dioxide, and hemodynamic parameters-may further refine assessment of biological viability. Frailty, comorbidity burden, cerebral perfusion, and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation-related contraindications should also be incorporated into decision-making. Importantly, selection cannot be separated from system performance: Cannulation strategy, transport logistics, institutional experience, and the ability to establish extracorporeal circulation rapidly may substantially modify the likelihood of benefit. Differences between out-of-hospital and in-hospital cardiac arrest further limit the universal application of rigid eligibility criteria.

CONCLUSION: Candidacy for ECPR should be viewed as a dynamic, probability-based assessment rather than a checklist of fixed thresholds. Integrating arrest characteristics, reversibility, evolving physiology, patient reserve, and system capability may provide a more clinically meaningful framework for identifying patients most likely to achieve neurologically favorable survival after ECPR.

articles.title: Age: a modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease?
articles.abstract: Age is the strongest risk factor for cardiovascular disease, yet biological aging is increasingly recognized as a modifiable process. Animal studies over the past few decades have demonstrated that genetic, pharmacological, and dietary interventions can extend the healthspan and lifespan of animals by targeting conserved mechanisms of aging. Examining whether lifespan-extending interventions work in humans is challenging due to the long lifespan of our species. However, the development of biomarkers of biological aging or "aging clocks" has allowed for human trials where the rate of biological aging can be estimated. These surrogate markers now enable the first generation of human geroscience trials, in which interventions such as caloric restriction, rapamycin, taurine, plasma exchange, or nutritional strategies are evaluated for their ability to slow biological aging. Particularly relevant for cardiology are recently developed organ- and cell-specific aging clocks that estimate the biological age of the heart, vasculature, and cardiovascular cell types. These biomarkers may be suitable for improving cardiovascular risk prediction and providing surrogate outcomes for trials targeting cardiovascular aging. Together, these advances suggest that slowing biological aging could complement established cardiovascular prevention and treatment strategies in the future.

articles.title: The dilemma of experience in voluntary attention control: How choice clarifies a common mechanism across opposing approaches.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of experimental psychology = Revue canadienne de psychologie experimentale
articles.abstract: This article attempts to clarify the endogenous mode of Ray Klein's three-dimensional taxonomy of attention by addressing a central dilemma in measuring voluntary attention control (VAC): how to handle the contamination of response time (RT) metrics by task experience. The performance-centred and autonomy-centred approaches represent diametrically opposed responses to this dilemma. The performance-centred approach uses uninformative cue contexts to isolate "pure" VAC, arguing that informative cues contaminate RT metrics via associative learning of cue-target probabilities. Conversely, the autonomy-centred approach argues that authentic volition requires self-generated choices in informative contexts-where the environment does not conflict with intentions-and utilizes a mediation model to separate VAC from contaminated RT measures. Rather than attempting to evade the effects of experience, the present study focused directly on them. We distinguished between two distinct experience-based effects: a practice-based effect tied to action frequency and a probability-based effect tied to cue-target statistics. We then examined the extent to which these effects depend on self-generated intentions by forcing participants to change cues at preset rates (0.25 vs. 0.75). Results indicated that the practice-based effect was weakened when choices were forced (as opposed to free), and the probability-based effect became undetectable. Both effects were significantly stronger when cue changes were self-generated and freely chosen. Altogether, the present findings underscore the dilemma of experience in VAC and highlight the important role of self-generated intentions in driving both experience-based RT effects and VAC. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

articles.title: When consensus can change hearts and minds: Sacred values and edge cases.
articles.journal: Journal of personality and social psychology
articles.abstract: Consensus information can change people's minds, especially in ambiguous situations. But can it also change people's hearts by influencing their deeply held convictions? The literature asserts not because sacralized values are assumed to be immune to social influence. Five studies (N = 1,651) demonstrate important limits to this assumption-when facing decisions involve edge cases in which sacred boundaries are ambiguous, sacralizers are responsive to consensus information. Halal-observant Muslims ignored consensus information when it challenged their sacred value in a core case (i.e., eating pork) but aligned with the consensus in an edge case (i.e., eating food that had touched pork; Study 1). Pro-choice sacralizers resisted consensus information in a core case (i.e., deciding to vote against elective abortions at 5 weeks of pregnancy) but aligned with consensus in an edge case (i.e., deciding to vote against elective abortions at 25 weeks of pregnancy; Study 2). We identified decision-making ambiguity as an underlying mechanism, such that people experienced more ambiguity in edge cases, which increased their reliance on consensus (Study 3). The degree of sacralization moderated consensus effects: In an edge case (i.e., using vaccines derived from fetal cells), the more strongly participants sacralized pro-life abortion values, the more they were influenced by the consensus (Study 4). The effect of consensus extended to behavior: when faced with an edge-case decision (i.e., donating to fetal-cell research), pro-life sacralizers were more likely to donate when consensus supported donation (Study 5). Edge cases reveal that consensus can move both minds and hearts by shifting judgments and behavior at the boundaries of convictions long assumed to be nonnegotiable. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

articles.title: [Silicone arthroplasty of the metacarpophalangeal joint].
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Pain relief through replacement of the degenerated joint using silicone arthroplasty.

INDICATIONS: Advanced painful joint osteoarthritis and with restricted movement.

CONTRAINDICATIONS: Active local or systemic infection, insufficient bone stock for implantation, insufficient soft tissue coverage.

SURGICAL TECHNIQUE: Dorsal longitudinal access to the degenerated joint. Longitudinal tendon split and opening of the capsule, exposure and preservation of the collateral ligaments. Resection of the metacarpal head and opening of the shaft of the metacarpal bone and the proximal phalanx with awl and rasps, and insertion of the trial implant of adequate size. Switch to the definitive implant, suture closure of the capsule, the extensor apparatus and the skin.

POSTOPERATIVE MANAGEMENT: Early start with mobilization from a positioning splint that includes the wrist and metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint and immediately leaves the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) and distal interphalangeal (DIP) joints free. Immediate active mobilization of the PIP and DIP joints. Additional active mobilization of the MCP joint starting in the second postoperative week. Complete removal of the splint after 6 weeks, full weight-bearing after 8 weeks.

RESULTS: Substantial and mostly lasting pain reduction (average 0.3/10 on the visual analog scale, VAS). Expected mobility on average 60° total range of motion. Revision rates of 3-5% after 15 years, radiologically after this time 12-65% implant fractures.

articles.title: Implementation of pharmacist-led chronic kidney disease screening in Australian community pharmacies: feasibility and characteristics of the screened population.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Chronic Kidney Disease Screening and Quality Use of Medicines trial aimed to improve chronic kidney disease (CKD) detection and optimise medication use in Australia. This analysis evaluates the feasibility of pharmacy-based screening for identifying individuals at risk of CKD and reports participant baseline characteristics.

METHODS: Eligible participants for the trial were aged 35-74 years and had ≥1 CKD risk factor. The intervention group received a QKidney® risk assessment, point-of-care test (POCT) and medication reviews, while the control group received the risk assessment only. QKidney® scores and blood pressure (BP) classified 5-year CKD risk as low, moderate or high. Intervention participants at moderate-to-high risk underwent POCT of serum creatinine to estimate estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Reduced kidney function was defined as eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 and prevalence was compared with Australian National Health Measures Survey 2022-2024 estimates. Data were analysed in Statistical Package for Social Sciences (version 31) using descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: Of the 1486 participants recruited between March 2023 and December 2024, 1189 were included in this analysis (550 (46%) intervention, 639 (54%) control). Risk assessment was completed in 99.9% of participants using QKidney® and in 100% using BP. A POCT was performed for 84% of intervention participants at moderate to high risk. Of those fulfilling pre-defined general practice referral criteria, 73% were referred. Overall, 68% of trial participants were at moderate to high CKD risk (59% identified by QKidney® and 30% by BP). Additionally, 21% had reduced kidney function based on POCT results - substantially higher than the national estimates (5.2%).

CONCLUSIONS: Pharmacy-based targeted screening was feasible for identifying individuals at risk of developing CKD and could strengthen early detection efforts in Australia.

articles.title: Joint association of frailty and depressive symptoms with new-onset chronic kidney disease in middle-aged and older adults: a longitudinal analysis from the CHARLS cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although frailty and depressive symptoms have both been associated with the risk of chronic kidney disease (CKD), their joint association with incident CKD and potential mediation pathways remains unclear.

METHODS: This analysis used data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. Frailty was quantified using a 35-item deficit-accumulation frailty index and depressive symptoms were defined using the CES-D-10. New-onset CKD was ascertained by self-reported physician diagnosis or an eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2. Cox regression models were used to estimate associations, and mediation analyses were conducted to explore potential explanatory pathways.

RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 6.87 years, 327 of 6,854 participants (4.8%) developed CKD. Depressive symptoms and frailty were each independently linked to incident CKD, with HRs of 1.50 (95% CI: 1.19-1.88) and 1.95 (95% CI: 1.52-2.49), respectively. Participants with coexisting depressive symptoms and frailty showed the greatest risk compared with those with neither condition (HR = 2.10, 95% CI: 1.59-2.77). In mediation analysis, frailty accounted for an estimated 66% of the observed association between depressive symptoms and CKD.

CONCLUSION: Coexisting frailty and depressive symptoms were associated with the highest risk of incident CKD. Mediation analysis suggested that frailty may partly explain the observed link between depressive symptoms and CKD. Concurrent screening for depressive symptoms and frailty may help improve CKD risk stratification in aging adults.

articles.title: Disability in chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Frailty, sarcopenia, depression, and cognitive impairment are each well documented in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and have each been the subject of detailed, single-domain reviews, but are rarely considered together as a single construct that determines whether a patient can work, self-manage, and participate in decisions about their own care. This narrative review positions these overlapping yet distinct conditions within the World Health Organization International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) framework, arguing for a dedicated, cross-domain assessment pathway in nephrology.

METHODS: PubMed and Google Scholar were searched for literature (2006-2026) combining "chronic kidney disease" with "disability", "frailty", "sarcopenia", "depression", "cognitive impairment", "employment", and "rehabilitation". Reference lists were hand-searched. This synthesis focuses on epidemiology, mechanisms, assessment, and management, emphasizing data from 2022 to 2026. As a narrative review without formal risk-of-bias assessment, selection bias is an acknowledged limitation.

RESULTS: Disability in CKD arises from five overlapping categories-the risk factors for CKD, CKD-related complications, co-existing conditions, treatment-related factors, and multifactorial contributors, such as sarcopenia and frailty. Once established, disability is perpetuated by two structurally parallel, self-reinforcing processes: a physical spiral of fatigue, symptom burden, and deconditioning, and an economic spiral of employment loss and financial hardship. Validated tools assess individual domains, but no integrated, CKD-specific disability instrument exists. Kidney replacement therapy can trigger abrupt functional decline, while kidney transplantation may improve long-term function but can temporarily worsen early post-operative frailty. The ICF-derived WHODAS 2.0 remains underutilized in nephrology.

CONCLUSION: Disability in CKD is common but historically studied piecemeal through isolated literatures. Shifting the paradigm to recognize disability as a unifying, assessable construct, rather than a by-product of individual complications, may enable earlier identification. This framework supports the implementation of structured, cross-domain assessments and coordinated rehabilitation and prevention strategies in routine nephrology care.

articles.title: Pneumocystis jirovecii Pneumonia in Adults with Brain Tumors: Treatment-Related Risk, Diagnostic Challenges, and Evidence-Informed Prophylaxis-A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP) is an opportunistic infection increasingly recognized in patients without human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) who receive immunosuppressive therapy. Patients with brain tumors may be vulnerable because of prolonged corticosteroid exposure, temozolomide-based chemoradiotherapy, and rituximab-based regimens. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on therapy-associated PJP in adults with brain tumors, emphasizing risk identification, diagnosis, prophylaxis, and management. A targeted PubMed search through 1 August 2026 was supplemented by reference-list screening, regulatory documents, and relevant clinical guidelines; brain-tumor-specific evidence was prioritized, with selective extrapolation from other non-HIV immunocompromised populations. High-dose or prolonged corticosteroid use, concurrent temozolomide and radiotherapy, and rituximab-based regimens, particularly in primary central nervous system lymphoma, were repeatedly identified as clinically relevant contributors to PJP risk. Contemporary studies suggest an average incidence below 1% during temozolomide chemoradiotherapy, although risk is heterogeneous and may increase with corticosteroid exposure, lymphopenia, and combined immunosuppression. PJP in patients without HIV generally has a more acute course and higher mortality than HIV-associated disease, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole remains the first-line agent for prophylaxis and treatment. Early identification of high-risk patients and timely prophylaxis are important components of supportive neuro-oncology care.

articles.title: The efficacy of additional atrial driver ablation in persistent and long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.journal: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) remains the primary ablation strategy for atrial fibrillation (AF), yet its success in persistent (PeAF) and long-standing persistent AF (LS-PeAF) is suboptimal. Adjunctive ablation targeting atrial drivers has been proposed to enhance outcomes. This systematic review and meta-analysis compared PVI alone with PVI plus atrial driver ablation in PeAF and LS-PeAF.

METHODS: Comprehensive searches of PubMed, Scopus, Europe PMC, and Cochrane Library identified randomized controlled trials (RCTs) enrolling adults with PeAF or LS-PeAF undergoing first-time ablation. Eligible studies compared PVI alone versus PVI plus driver ablation and trials utilizing other adjunctive ablations were excluded. Outcomes included recurrence of AF and any atrial tachyarrhythmia (ATA) beyond the blanking period, procedural parameters, and complications. Pooled analyses employed random-effects models to measure risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Seven RCTs met inclusion criteria. Adjunctive driver ablation modestly improved freedom from AF (RR 1.16; 95% CI, [1.03, 1.31]; p = 0.01; I²=61%). However, this finding was accompanied by substantial heterogeneity and was not robust to leave-one-out sensitivity analysis. Driver ablation failed to elevate freedom from any ATA (RR 1.09; 95% CI, [0.98, 1.20]; p = 0.11; I²=47%). Procedure duration (MD 37.81 min; 95% CI, [4.42, 71.20]; p = 0.03; I²=96%), fluoroscopy time (MD 4.25 min; 95% CI, [2.83, 5.67]; p < 0.00001; I²=0%), and ablation time (MD 10.01 min; 95% CI, [0.25, 19.77]; p = 0.04; I²=95%) were significantly longer with adjunctive driver ablation. Procedural complication rates were comparable among both groups (RR 1.65; 95% CI, [0.80, 3.43]; p = 0.18; I²=20%).

CONCLUSION: Additional atrial driver ablation modestly improves freedom from AF but does not reduce ATA recurrence, prolonging procedure time without increasing complications.

articles.title: Acupuncture for relief of gagging in patients undergoing transoesophageal echocardiography-a randomised placebo-controlled trial.
articles.journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gagging during transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) can make the procedure distressing and even impossible to perform. Acupuncture is suggested to relieve the gag reflex during peroral endoscopic procedures. The aim was to test whether acupuncture is better than placebo for reducing gagging in patients undergoing elective ambulatory TEE.

METHODS: Sixty patients scheduled for ambulatory TEE were included according to eligibility criteria and received either fixed intradermal needles (N = 30) or placebo needles at acupuncture points CV24 and PC6 in a random order prior to TEE. Patients and practitioners, who performed TEE procedure and assessed the outcome measures were unaware of group (acupuncture or placebo) allocation. The primary outcome was the intensity of gagging, measured using verbal rating scale (VRS-11). Secondary outcomes included the use of rescue medication, the incidence of gagging, patients' satisfaction with relief of unwanted side effects during TEE procedure, success of patients' blinding, heart rate and oxygen saturation.

RESULTS: Median (IQR) of patient's reported gagging intensity in the acupuncture group was 4 (2-8) vs. 7 (5-8) in the placebo group (P = 0.13), the gagging intensity reported by TEE-examiner was 2 (1-5) among the patients from the acupuncture group vs. 4 (2-9) in the placebo group (P = 0.06). Six patients from the acupuncture group vs. 14 from the placebo group required sedative rescue medication (P = 0.03). All other measured outcomes were comparable between the study groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Acupuncture with indwelling fixed intradermal needles may reduce the need for sedative medication in patients scheduled for elective TEE. Larger trials with improved methodology are required to verify this finding.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT03821428; registration date: January 25, 2019.

articles.title: Early real-world use of acoramidis for transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy in Germany: results from StarTTR.
articles.journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acoramidis, a selective transthyretin stabilizer, received EU approval in February 2025 for the treatment of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM). We describe patient characteristics and comedication patterns in German routine care.

METHODS: Adults with ≥ 1 acoramidis dispensation between April and September 2025 were identified from the IQVIA™ Longitudinal Prescription database, which covers 82% of reimbursed prescriptions. Sociodemographic data, comorbidities, prescribing setting, and comedications were analyzed overall and by pretreatment status (treatment-naïve vs. tafamidis switchers).

RESULTS: A total of 289 patients were identified; median age was 82 (interquartile range 77-85) years; 15% were female and 86% were treatment-naïve. Acoramidis initiation occurred predominantly in hospital outpatient departments (87%). In the year preceding initiation, the most common comedications were renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibitors (76%), sodium glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors (74%), and beta-blockers (71%). Between 12 and 10 months and 3 and 1 months before initiation, use of mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs), loop diuretics, direct oral anticoagulants, and SGLT2 inhibitors increased markedly, whereas RAS inhibitors, beta-blockers, and calcium channel blockers remained unchanged.

CONCLUSION: This real-world analysis showed that acoramidis was predominantly prescribed as first-line therapy for older, mainly male patients with ATTR-CM; switching from tafamidis was comparatively infrequent. The increasing use of MRAs, loop diuretics, direct oral anticoagulants, and SGLT2 inhibitors prior to acoramidis initiation is consistent with active therapeutic optimization in specialist centers. These data provide an early benchmark for monitoring acoramidis adoption and will inform future comparative effectiveness research.

articles.title: P-Wave indices in the presence of atrial myxomas: a retrospective cohort analysis.
articles.journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial myxoma is the most common primary cardiac neoplasm, which may cause embolisms, obstruction, and arrhythmias. Whether electrocardiographic P-wave indices carry diagnostic information for detecting atrial myxomas has not been systematically examined.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 83 patients: 39 with histologically confirmed atrial myxoma (34 left, 5 right atrial) and 44 age- and sex-matched controls. Seven P-wave indices were derived from 12-lead ECGs: duration, morphology in V1, voltage in lead I, axis, area in lead II, morphology-voltage-P-wave duration (MVP) score and dispersion. Logistic regression was used to identify possible predictors for atrial myxoma, with adjustment for age, sex, coronary artery disease, dyslipidemia, and smoking.

RESULTS: Patients' median age was 60.0 [51.0-70.0] years; 77.1% were women. Atrial myxoma had a median size of 4.1 cm [IQR 2.5; 5.6]. Patients with a myxoma showed shorter P-wave duration (100 [80; 100] vs. 100 [100; 120] ms; p = 0.005) and lower lead-I voltage (0.07 [0.05; 0.08] vs. 0.09 [0.06; 0.10] mV; p < 0.001). On univariable analysis, both predicted tumor presence. Entered together, only voltage remained independently (OR 0.76 per 0.01 mV, 95% CI 0.63-0.91, p = 0.003) associated with atrial myxoma; duration became borderline due to collinearity (p = 0.078). After full adjustment, voltage remained robust (OR 0.70, 95% CI 0.55-0.89, p = 0.004). Within the tumor group, a larger maximal tumor diameter was associated with lower lead-I voltage (Spearman ρ =  - 0.32; p = 0.044).

CONCLUSIONS: ECG analysis of patients with atrial myxoma revealed reduced P-wave voltage in lead I, with relatively short P-wave duration. Reduced P-wave voltage in lead I was an independent predictor after full adjustment for cardiovascular comorbidities and may serve as a novel, easily available diagnostic adjunct for atrial mass lesions.

articles.title: A Systematic Literature Review on the Economic Burden of Sjögren's Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Sjögren's disease (SjD) is a chronic autoimmune disorder characterized by exocrine glandular dysfunction, chronic fatigue, and pain, with considerable morbidity, mortality, and significant quality-of-life burden. The economic impact of SjD thus far has been underappreciated and understudied, limiting understanding of its implications for patients. Therefore, we conducted a systematic literature review to identify, evaluate, and summarize the economic burden on patients with SjD.

METHODS: The systematic literature review was developed using the PRISMA reporting guidelines for systematic reviews and conducted using the MEDLINE and Embase databases (via OvidSP), covering the period from January 1, 2014, to July 14, 2025. Additional searches were performed in the bibliographies of relevant studies, Google Scholar, disease-specific websites, and conference proceedings. Data regarding healthcare resource utilization (HCRU), direct medical costs, as well as indirect and societal costs were extracted. A focus group discussion of patients living with SjD generated qualitative insights to identify themes across diagnosis, treatment, and burden of disease.

RESULTS: A total of 49 unique studies reported outcomes related to economic burden of SjD; HCRU was reported in 27 studies, while 21 studies reported direct or indirect costs, and 16 focused on productivity loss. The studies were performed across the globe, but predominately in North America (n = 22) and Europe (n = 16). Direct healthcare costs for patients with SjD were noted to be 1.6-3.1 times higher than for patients without SjD owing to more frequent hospitalizations, outpatient visits, emergency department care, and dental visits compared with patients without SjD. In addition, total indirect costs were around 2 times higher for patients with SjD than those without SjD, a consequence of substantial productivity loss, including activity impairment (27%-61%), overall work impairment (26%-38%), absenteeism (2.4%-27%), and presenteeism (21%-35%). Patients with SjD from the focus group reported frequent emergency care for SjD-related symptoms, high out-of-pocket medical costs (which includes over-the-counter medication cost and specialized diets), significant work and daily productivity loss due to fatigue and cognitive symptoms, and ongoing financial strain requiring community or family support.

CONCLUSION: This systematic review demonstrates that SjD results in measurable healthcare costs, loss of productivity, and a notable financial burden on both individuals and healthcare systems, highlighting an increased need for urgent care, hospital admissions, and extended stays. Indirect costs, primarily arising from lost productivity, further amplify the economic burden of SjD. In total, these costs highlight the economic and societal burden of SjD, reflected in both direct healthcare costs and indirect costs.

articles.title: Role of Growth hormone in the Pathogenesis of Podocytopathy and Diabetic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: Kidney development and function rely heavily on growth hormone (GH) and its downstream effector, insulin-like growth factor-I (IGF-I). In type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM), elevated GH levels correlate strongly with glomerular injury and proteinuria. Transgenic animal models have further clarified GH's role in diabetic kidney disease (DKD), demonstrating a direct link between elevated GH levels and glomerulosclerosis. Interestingly, because IGF-I transgenic mice escape glomerulosclerosis, evidence suggests a direct pathological contribution by GH itself. Podocytes, which constitute more than 30% of glomerular cells, serve as specialized visceral epithelial cells vital to the permselectivity of the glomerular filtration barrier and maintenance of other glomerular components such as endothelium and mesangium. Since podocytes express the GH receptor (GHR), understanding the direct impact of GH on podocytes is essential to unravel DKD pathology. GH inflicts irreversible podocytopathy by triggering hypertrophy, mitotic catastrophe, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), culminating in podocyte loss, glomerulosclerosis, and proteinuria. Mechanistically, these damaging effects are driven by GH-induced ZEB2 expression, reactivation of Notch signaling, and heightened expression of TGF-β1 and TNF-α. Interrupting the GH/GHR cascade, genetically depleting ZEB2, or halting Notch activation effectively prevents this damage, safeguarding both glomerular architecture and overall kidney function. This manuscript provides an overview of aberrations in GH signaling, particularly in T1DM, dissects its cellular and molecular effects on podocytes, and highlights therapeutic approaches to counteract podocytopathy.

articles.title: Female Team-Sport Athletes' Physical Fitness and Jump Performance Kinematics After Plyometric Jump Training: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Plyometric jump training (PJT) can improve athletes' physical fitness across a range of sports and populations. Nonetheless, the role of PJT in adult female team-sport athletes' fitness, jump performance, and kinematics remains unclear, particularly given the increasing number of published, heterogeneous studies.

OBJECTIVES: This systematic review aimed to first examine the effectiveness of PJT in improving physical fitness and jump-performance kinematics in adult female team-sport athletes, and second, to provide evidence-based recommendations for PJT prescription for this population.

METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted in the PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and EBSCO databases up to March 2026. The included studies recruited healthy female team-sport athletes (mean age: ≥ 18 years), incorporated a PJT programme ≥ 2 weeks in duration, included comparator groups, and assessed athletes' physical fitness, jump performance, and/or kinematics. The risk of bias (RoB) was assessed using the Physiotherapy Evidence Database scale. Hedges' g effect sizes (ES) with 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs) were reported using a random-effects model for meta-analyses. Statistical significance was set at p ≤ 0.05. Subgroup analyses were conducted based on the participant characteristics (height, body mass, sport) and PJT programming variables (duration, frequency, total sessions, weekly total jumps). The certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE.

RESULTS: Thirty-one articles were included (n = 609 participants), and 25 were meta-analysed. Two studies were categorised with high RoB (≤ 3 points), 20 studies achieved moderate RoB (4-5 points), and 9 studies achieved low RoB (≥ 6 points). Compared to controls, PJT improved countermovement jump (CMJ) height (ES = 0.550, p < 0.001), CMJ peak concentric velocity (ES = 0.623, p = 0.011), drop jump (DJ) reactive strength index (RSI) (ES = 0.926, p = 0.001), DJ height (ES = 0.721, p = 0.002), 10 m sprint time (ES = 0.712, p = 0.032), 20 m sprint time (ES = 0.709, p < 0.001), 30 m sprint time (ES = 1.018, p = 0.001), non-linear (agility) Illinois test time (ES = 1.225, p < 0.001) and T test sprint time (ES = 0.965, p < 0.001). Compared to PJT ≤ 6 weeks, longer interventions favoured DJ RSI (p = 0.008), 10 m sprint time (p = 0.001), and Illinois agility test time (p < 0.001). Impact of heterogeneity (I2) remained low (≤ 0.06%) in five analyses and moderate in the other four analyses (≤ 73.1%). The certainty of evidence was considered low to moderate for the study outcomes. Two studies reported that a total of three participants possibly sustained an injury during PJT.

CONCLUSIONS: Adult female team-sport athletes' fitness, jump performance, and kinematics improved after PJT when compared to the control condition, including CMJ height, CMJ peak concentric velocity, DJ RSI, linear sprint speed, and non-linear (agility) sprint speed. The improvements were particularly notable with longer interventions (≥ 8 weeks).

TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/NERCY.

articles.title: [What is established in the interdisciplinary treatment of anorexia nervosa?].
articles.abstract: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is a serious mental illness that, due to chronic malnutrition and prolonged starvation, can affect multiple organ systems and become an internal medicine emergency. The goal of this article is to provide a structured presentation of acute internal medicine care for severe AN, with particular emphasis on somatic risk stratification, refeeding prevention, nutritional therapy, and multidisciplinary treatment structures. The recommendations are based on national and international guidelines, as well as additional scientific evidence and clinical experience. Inpatient care is indicated in cases of medical instability, severe physical complications, rapid weight loss, or inadequate food intake. The decision regarding internal medicine, psychosomatic, or intensive care treatment depends on the level of monitoring required. According to the Association of the Scientific Medical Societies in Germany (Arbeitsgemeinschaft der Wissenschaftlichen Medizinischen Fachgesellschaften, AWMF) S3 guideline, in a controlled inpatient setting, an initial daily intake of 2000 kcal is recommended, averaging 40-50 kcal/kg, with a rapid increase of 200 kcal/day and a target of 500-1500 g of weight gain per week. Oral nutrition is preferred, possibly with additional nutritionally complete liquid nutrition, before enteral tube feeding. Parenteral nutrition is reserved for life-threatening situations where gastrointestinal feeding is not possible. Treating severe AN requires a consistently multidisciplinary approach aimed at achieving internal medical stabilization. Nutritional medical expertise, psychosomatic-psychotherapeutic co-treatment, and good communication among all involved professional groups are crucial for the safe care of this high-risk group.

articles.title: [End-stage renal disease: what is established?].
articles.abstract: End-stage renal disease represents the terminal stage of chronic kidney disease and is characterized by a persistently reduced glomerular filtration rate of < 15 mL/min per 1.73 m2. In Germany, approximately 80,000 patients receive maintenance dialysis. The majority undergo in-center hemodialysis. At present, no specific glomerular filtration rate threshold can be recommended for the initiation of kidney replacement therapy. The decision to commence treatment should instead be based on the persistence of clinical symptoms and laboratory abnormalities that are refractory to appropriate conservative management. Available kidney replacement modalities include hemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, and kidney transplantation. The choice of dialysis modality should be individualized and take into account medical eligibility, comorbidities, the patient's social and living circumstances, and individual preferences. Comprehensive counseling should include information on home-based dialysis modalities. In addition to optimizing dialysis treatment, rigorous management of comorbidities and cardiovascular risk factors is essential. Early and structured assessment for kidney transplantation should be considered in all potentially eligible patients.

articles.title: Noninvasive Insights: Magnetic Resonance Elastography and Ultrasound Liver Elastography for the Assessment of Liver Fibrosis in Fontan-Associated Liver Disease: A Comparative Study with Histology.
articles.abstract: The diagnostic performance of ultrasound (U/S) elastography and magnetic resonance elastography (MRE) of liver relative to histological assessment in Fontan patients remains uncertain. This study sought to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy and agreement of MRE and U/S elastography compared with histological congestive hepatic fibrosis score (CHFS) staging. We conducted a cross-sectional study in Fontan patients. Patients were categorized into non-significant fibrosis (≤ 2 A) and advanced fibrosis (≥ 2B) groups according to the CHFS scoring system. This study included 34 Fontan patients with a mean age of 20.2 ± 6 years, 23 (67.6%) had fibrosis ≥2B. The majority of whom had undergone an extracardiac conduit Fontan procedure. Hemodynamic parameters were similar between groups. MRE values were significantly higher in the fibrosis group (5.0 ± 0.9 vs. 4.1 ± 1.1 kPa, p = 0.018), whereas U/S elastography values did not differ significantly (p = 0.568). MRE demonstrated fair agreement with biopsy (quadratic-weighted κ = 0.468), while ultrasound showed no meaningful agreement (κ=-0.057). MRE demonstrated acceptable discriminative performance (AUC 0.77; 95% CI: 0.57-0.97), whereas ultrasound elastography showed poor discrimination (AUC 0.44; 95% CI: 0.21-0.66), both estimated from the continuous liver stiffness value in kilopascals; the two areas under the curve differed by 0.33 (95% CI: 0.06-0.60; DeLong p = 0.018). MRE demonstrates better agreement with histology and higher diagnostic performance compared with U/S elastography in Fontan patients. However, its discriminatory capacity, as reflected by AUC, remains lower than that reported in other chronic liver diseases. These findings highlight the unique pathophysiological substrate of Fontan-associated liver disease and underscore the need to establish disease-specific MRE cut-off values for each staging system to achieve more accurate fibrosis stratification and meaningful clinical application.

articles.title: MRI-based biomarkers for risk stratification and assessment of treatment response in Metabolic dysfunction-associated Steatotic liver disease.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects up to 38% of the population globally. Liver biopsy, the historical reference standard, is invasive, subject to sampling error and not scalable. MRI-based biomarkers provide non-invasive, quantitative whole liver assessment. MRI proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) is the most accurate noninvasive measure of steatosis (thresholds of 6.4%, 17.4% and 22.1% for grades ≥1, ≥2 and 3), and a ≥30% relative reduction is associated with histologic response. Liver stiffness by magnetic resonance elastography (MRE-LS) is the most accurate imaging biomarker for fibrosis: MRE-LS of 3.1-4.4 kPa corresponds to F2-F3 and ≥5 kPa to cirrhosis, and each 1-kPa increase is associated with a 43% higher risk of hepatic decompensation. Iron-corrected T1 is a sensitive but nonspecific marker of disease activity whose prognostic value requires further study. Composite scores, MAST, MEFIB, and MASH Resolution Index, combine imaging and blood tests for advanced fibrosis diagnosis and response assessment. MRE is cost-effective compared with vibration-controlled transient elastography for detecting advanced fibrosis. Artificial intelligence may broaden access by automating analysis and enabling PDFF from routine MRI. We review the evidence supporting these biomarkers for diagnosis, prognosis and regulatory use, and their role in clinical trials and in treatment decisions for approved MASH therapies.

articles.title: MELAS Associated With a Large-Scale MT-ND2 Deletion: A Case Report.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, lactic acidosis, and stroke-like episodes (MELAS) is a clinically and genetically heterogeneous mitochondrial disorder. Although the m.3243A>G variant in MT-TL1 is the most common molecular cause, atypical cases with negative routine genetic testing and nondiagnostic muscle biopsy may pose a substantial diagnostic challenge. Here, we report a clinically diagnosed MELAS case with supportive neuropathological findings and a large-scale deletion involving MT-ND2.

CASE REPORT: A 20-year-old man presented with recurrent seizures and encephalopathic episodes over 1.5 years. His clinical course was characterized by episodic visual disturbance, hearing impairment, hemiparesis, and progressive encephalopathic deterioration. Serial magnetic resonance imaging revealed recurrent migratory cortical lesions involving the occipital, temporal, and frontal lobes, and magnetic resonance spectroscopy demonstrated a lactate peak. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis and autoimmune and infectious investigations were unremarkable. Electromyography, muscle biopsy, and initial next-generation sequencing, including testing for the common m.3243A>G variant, were nondiagnostic. Subsequent brain biopsy demonstrated laminar cortical necrosis, supporting a mitochondrial encephalopathic process. Multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification further identified a large-scale pathogenic deletion involving MT-ND2. Based on the characteristic clinical course, neuroimaging pattern, neuropathological findings, and complementary genetic analysis, a diagnosis of MELAS was established.

CONCLUSION: This case expands the diagnostic spectrum of MELAS and highlights that typical clinical and radiologic features may still be present even when routine lactate testing, muscle biopsy, and standard genetic screening are nondiagnostic. In highly suspected cases, brain biopsy and complementary methods for mitochondrial structural variation analysis, such as MLPA, may provide crucial diagnostic evidence.

articles.title: Phage N4 uses a SAR endolysin-holin system for host cell lysis.
articles.abstract: Bacteriophages (phages) cause active host cell lysis to terminate their infection and release progeny into the environment. However, some phages have systems to delay their lysis, and thereby increase progeny yield, in specific conditions: a phenomenon called lysis inhibition (LIN). Two dissimilar phages of Escherichia coli are known to exhibit LIN: T4 and N4. In T4, a multi-protein mechanism stalls lysis and maintains the LIN state in response to superinfection in a high phage population density. However, the lysis proteins responsible for T4 lysis and LIN are not conserved with phage N4. In this study, we characterize the phage N4 proteins involved in lysis by molecular and genetic means. We define the functions of the minimal gene set required for lysis through heterologous expression and complementation. Furthermore, by sequence comparison with a selected mutant library that does not induce LIN, we have identified genomic regions both within and outside the lysis cassette involved in N4 LIN. We propose a model where N4 lysis proteins that execute rapid N4 lysis can be regulated to induce LIN. Despite the lack of conservation with T4 components, our study suggests that direct modulation of lysis initiation may be common and provides a springboard for identifying similar mechanisms in other phages.IMPORTANCEPhages are viruses that kill only bacteria. To do so, they use lysis proteins to disrupt the structural components of the bacterial envelope. There are commonalities between the phages that infect bacteria with similar structures, but there are also interesting differences we can exploit to learn more about specific phages or their bacterial hosts. In this study, we characterize the lysis proteins of the E. coli phage N4. Our results suggest that lysis regulation controls phage yield in N4 differently than in the well-studied phage T4. Future studies on the relationship between lysis proteins and phage yield could provide handles to use this information for optimal large-scale phage production for clinical or industrial applications.

articles.title: Identification of natural products for blocking Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus entry and primary infection.
articles.abstract: Approximately 20% of human cancers have been attributed to virus infections, including Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV), which can cause several human cancers arising in immunocompromised patients. KSHV can also establish lifelong infection in immunocompetent individuals. The prevalence of KSHV infection is high in HIV-endemic regions, such as sub-Saharan Africa, as well as in certain subpopulations, including men who have sex with men (MSM) and organ transplant recipients. Prevention of primary KSHV infection is important for reducing the incidence of these virus-associated malignancies, especially in high-risk populations; however, no drugs or vaccines are currently available for this purpose. In the current study, we identified three tannin-related compounds displaying prominent antiviral activity against primary KSHV infection through screening of a natural compound library. Remarkably, the inhibitory effects of these natural compounds were completely independent of cytotoxicity and showed high specificity for KSHV. Furthermore, we found that these compounds effectively blocked KSHV entry by interfering with viral attachment to host cells. Using both in vitro and in silico analyses, we demonstrated that these tannin-related compounds interfered with the interaction between EphA2 and KSHV gH/gL by competitively binding to the viral glycoproteins, the details of compound-protein interaction, including those key residues and mutation analysis. Together, these findings demonstrate that tannin-related compounds are promising anti-KSHV agents with the potential to reduce the incidence of KSHV-related diseases.

articles.title: The 2024 National Report on Continuous Glucose Monitoring Uptake in Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes Following Universal Funding in Aotearoa New Zealand: Early Findings from the KiwiDiab Pediatric Diabetes Network.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To describe national patterns in continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) uptake and glycemic patterns among children with type 1 diabetes (T1D) in Aotearoa New Zealand following universal CGM funding on October 1, 2024.

METHODS: Data from the KiwiDiab pediatric diabetes network for 2024 included children <16 years with T1D who were attending 14 regional pediatric diabetes centers. CGM uptake was evaluated using the weekly proportion using CGM and the weekly proportion initiating CGM. Overall and ethnicity-specific initiation was analyzed using negative binomial regression of weekly initiation counts, with the number not using CGM at the start of each week as an offset, comparing prefunding, rollout, and postfunding periods. HbA1c measurements were summarized as cross-sectional monthly distributions by prioritized ethnicity.

RESULTS: In total, 1681 children and adolescents with T1D were included. Mean weekly proportions initiating CGM increased from 1.4% prefunding to 12.9% during rollout (incidence rate ratio [IRR] = 9.05, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.03-17.5) and remained elevated postfunding at 6.6% (IRR = 4.64, 95% CI: 3.27-6.61). During rollout, mean weekly proportions initiating CGM increased from 1.0% to 14.0% among Māori, from 0.8% to 11.6% among Pacific, from 1.5% to 15.9% among Asian, and from 1.8% to 11.0% among European children. There was no statistically significant evidence that the magnitude of change across funding periods differed by ethnicity (period-by-ethnicity interaction, P = 0.72). Differences in the proportion using CGM between ethnic groups narrowed during 2024 but remained at year-end. Cross-sectional HbA1c distributions remained relatively stable throughout 2024, with no clear early lowering observed.

CONCLUSION: Universal CGM funding was associated with a rapid increase in CGM uptake across Aotearoa New Zealand. CGM initiation increased markedly across ethnic groups, and ethnic disparities in CGM use narrowed during 2024, although they persisted at year-end.

articles.title: Shock With Acute Myocardial Dysfunction in Stercoral Colitis: Diagnosis and Management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Shock in sepsis is predominantly vasodilatory; however, concomitant myocardial dysfunction may result in superimposed cardiogenic shock and a mixed shock state.

CASE SUMMARY: A 75-year-old man with Parkinson disease, severe constipation, and stercoral colitis presented with profound shock after an enema. Echocardiography showed new biventricular dysfunction with regional wall-motion abnormalities. Invasive hemodynamic assessment demonstrated elevated filling pressures, low cardiac index, and low systemic vascular resistance despite substantial vasoactive and inotropic support, consistent with a mixed vasodilatory and cardiogenic shock. He improved after antibiotics and vasoactive support, but manual disimpaction after stabilization was followed within minutes by recurrent/similar shock.

REVIEW SUMMARY: This case illustrates a practical approach to mixed shock with acute myocardial dysfunction. Treatment of underlying infection should occur in parallel with characterization of the hemodynamic phenotype. Serial echocardiography and invasive hemodynamic assessment can identify concomitant vasodilatory and cardiogenic shock and guide circulatory support as shock physiology evolves.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Shock physiology is dynamic. In patients with sepsis, serial clinical, echocardiographic, and hemodynamic reassessment can identify concomitant cardiogenic shock and guide circulatory support.

articles.title: Acquired Gerbode Defect After TAVR Presenting With Severe Acute Liver and Kidney Injury.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acquired Gerbode defects after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) are rare and may present atypically, delaying diagnosis.

CASE SUMMARY: A 71-year-old man presented 15 days after TAVR with severe acute liver and kidney injury despite preserved ventricular systolic function and normal prosthetic valve function on transthoracic echocardiography. Right heart catheterization revealed elevated filling pressures, an oxygen saturation step-up from the superior vena cava (51%) to the pulmonary artery (79%), and a pulmonary/systemic flow ratio of 2.9. Transesophageal echocardiography identified a high-pressure left ventricular-to-right atrial shunt through the membranous septum. Residual shunting after transcatheter closure caused severe intravascular hemolysis and necessitated surgical salvage. The postoperative course was complicated by multiorgan failure and death.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights an atypical presentation of an acquired Gerbode defect. Complementary transesophageal echocardiography and invasive hemodynamic assessment were essential for diagnosis.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Occult intracardiac shunting should be considered after TAVR when severe end-organ dysfunction is discordant with reassuring transthoracic echocardiographic findings.

articles.title: ST-Segment Elevation Beyond the Coronaries: A Case of Necrotizing Mediastinitis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Descending necrotizing mediastinitis (DNM) is a rare, life-threatening infection (mortality 18%-36%) that can extend to the pericardium and produce electrocardiogram changes mimicking ST-segmentelevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).

CASE SUMMARY: A young, previously healthy man presented with anterior chest pain. Initial electrocardiogram showed ST-segment elevation prompting STEMI suspicion. Computed tomography angiography of the chest revealed deep neck infection with mediastinal and pericardial extension, diagnosing DNM. Cultures grew Streptococcus constellatus. Management included broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics and surgical drainage/debridement with intensive care unit care; the patient recovered.

DISCUSSION: DNM arises from oropharyngeal or odontogenic infection spreading along cervical fascial planes, with mortality driven by diagnostic delay and inadequate source control. S constellatus is an uncommon cause. This case highlights pericardial involvement as a noncoronary cause of ST elevation.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Consider noncoronary causes of ST-segment elevation; early imaging is essential to diagnose DNM and guide lifesaving source control.

articles.title: Advanced Cardiovascular Disease in Marbach-Rustad Progeroid Syndrome (LEMD2 p.Ser479Phe).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Marbach-Rustad progeroid syndrome results from the recurrent heterozygous LEMD2 c.1436C>T (p.Ser479Phe) variant. Four cases have been reported, with cardiac involvement absent or only qualitatively described.

CASE SUMMARY: A 30-year-old man with short stature, skeletal fragility, and facial dysmorphism presented with syncope from high-grade atrioventricular block. Echocardiography showed premature severe calcific aortic stenosis and mild mitral stenosis. Cardiac magnetic resonance showed preserved biventricular function with no late gadolinium enhancement; computed tomography confirmed valvular calcification but no coronary calcium. Chagas serology was negative. Whole-genome sequencing confirmed the p.Ser479Phe variant. He received a permanent pacemaker and, 6 months later, transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Evaluation also revealed overt type 2 diabetes, severe hypertriglyceridemia, and nephropathy: the most advanced metabolic phenotype reported.

DISCUSSION: This case shows that the p.Ser479Phe variant can cause advanced, intervention-requiring cardiovascular disease (objectively quantified and, to our knowledge, the first in vivo characterization by cardiac magnetic resonance). These findings support routine cardiac and metabolic surveillance in LEMD2-associated progeroid syndromes.

articles.title: Sex Differences in Health Status in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: Four-Trial Pooled Analysis.
Arthroscopic-Assisted Volar Scapholunate Capsulodesis for EWAS Grade IIIA: A Prospective Case Series Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study evaluated the functional and radiological outcomes of arthroscopically assisted volar scapholunate (SL) capsulodesis for subacute volar SL ligament injury (European Wrist Arthroscopy Society [EWAS] grade IIIA). To the best of our knowledge, isolated subacute (EWAS grade IIIA) injuries has not been specifically studied in the literature, representing a gap in knowledge regarding the management of this rare injury.

METHODS: This prospective case series included patients with isolated subacute (EWAS grade IIIA) injuries who underwent arthroscopically assisted volar capsulodesis using the inside-out technique described by Lui and Kakar. The primary outcomes were functional outcomes assessed using the Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand (DASH) score and Modified Mayo Wrist Score. Secondary outcomes included changes in the SL gap and SL angle, range of motion (ROM), grip strength, and pain assessed using the visual analog scale (VAS).

RESULTS: The mean follow-up was 27 months. Ten patients (five women and five men) were included. The mean age at surgery was 26 years, Wrist ROM was largely maintained postoperatively. Mean grip strength increased from 65% to 97% of the contralateral side. Mean VAS pain scores decreased from 7.6 to 1.8, mean DASH scores improved from 15 to 3, and mean Modified Mayo Wrist Scores improved from 52.0 to 91.5. Radiographic measures of the SL gap and SL angle were largely maintained postoperatively.

CONCLUSIONS: Arthroscopically assisted volar SL capsulodesis showed substantial improvements in pain, disability, grip strength, and Modified Mayo Wrist Score in patients with EWAS grade IIIA injuries. The proportion of patients achieving clinically meaningful improvement was high for VAS pain and more moderate for DASH. However, the absence of a comparator group, small sample size, and attrition limit causal inference; larger comparative studies with longer follow-up are needed.

TYPE OF STUDY/LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Prospective case series study, IV.

articles.title: Early Increases in GDF-15 Are Associated With Declines in Cardiac Function With Breast Cancer Therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Growth differentiation factor (GDF)-15 is a stress-responsive cytokine induced by mitochondrial dysfunction and genotoxic stress, mechanisms central to anthracycline cardiotoxicity. Whether early changes in GDF-15 following cancer therapy relate to subsequent cardiac dysfunction is not established.

OBJECTIVES: We evaluated the longitudinal trajectory of GDF-15 and its associations with changes in cardiac function and structure following cardiotoxic cancer therapy in women with breast cancer.

METHODS: In 366 women receiving anthracyclines and/or trastuzumab from the Penn Cardiotoxicity of Cancer Therapy prospective cohort study, associations between baseline, early-peak (maximum 0-6-month change), and longitudinal GDF-15 concentrations with quantitative echocardiographic measures of systolic, diastolic, and structural function over 36 months were evaluated using multivariable linear mixed-effects models.

RESULTS: GDF-15 rose from a median baseline of 662 to an early-peak of 1,412 pg/mL, with trajectories differing across regimens (P = 0.004). Each doubling of the early-peak-to-baseline GDF-15 ratio was associated with a subsequent 1.5 percentage point decline in left ventricular ejection fraction (β -1.5%; 95% CI: -2.5 to -0.6; P = 0.002) and a 0.9-unit worsening in longitudinal strain (β 0.9; 95% CI: 0.4-1.4; P = 0.001). GDF-15 was not associated with diastolic outcomes, incident diastolic dysfunction, or incident cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction.

CONCLUSIONS: In women receiving anthracycline- and/or trastuzumab-based breast cancer therapy, early increases in GDF-15 were associated with modest declines in left ventricular ejection fraction and worsening of longitudinal strain, without associations with diastolic measures. These findings support mechanistic investigation of GDF-15 in anthracycline-related cardiotoxicity. (Cardiotoxicity of Cancer Therapy [CCT]; NCT01173341).

articles.title: Staged sternal distraction for early thoracic expansion in Shwachman-Diamond syndrome.
articles.journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
articles.abstract: Shwachman-Diamond syndrome (SDS) is a rare inherited multisystem disorder with variable skeletal involvement; severe neonatal thoracic dystrophy is uncommon but can cause thoracic insufficiency and mimic Jeune syndrome. We report staged sternal distraction in a 5-month-old infant with a severely constricted thorax, pulmonary hypoplasia, refractory pulmonary hypertension, tracheostomy-dependent respiratory failure and an iatrogenic posterior tracheal wall injury. Subsequent trio long-read genome sequencing identified compound heterozygous pathogenic variants in SBDS, c.183_184delinsCT (p.Lys62Ter), inherited paternally, and c.258+2T>C, inherited maternally, establishing a molecular diagnosis of SDS. At presentation, the chest circumference measured 36cm, compared with an age-expected value of 41cm. The patient underwent staged median sternotomy distraction followed by stabilisation with custom fibular allograft struts. At approximately 3 months, chest circumference had increased to 41cm, peak inspiratory pressures had decreased from 40-50cm H2O to the mid-20cm H2O range, pulmonary hypertension was no longer evident on echocardiography, and the tracheal injury had healed. At 6 months, he remained on home mechanical ventilation, with peak inspiratory pressures in the upper 20cm H2O range. To our knowledge, operative thoracic expansion specifically for SDS-associated thoracic insufficiency has not previously been described. In carefully selected infants with severe thoracic insufficiency who are not yet candidates for conventional thoracic reconstruction, staged sternal distraction may serve as an interim strategy to achieve meaningful thoracic expansion.

articles.title: A Virtual Pulmonary Rehabilitation Program to Address Gaps in Pulmonary Rehabilitation: Retrospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traditional brick-and-mortar pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) programs remain substantially underused, with only 2.7% of Medicare beneficiaries completing PR within 12 months following hospitalization for a COPD exacerbation. Given the critical role of PR in improving exercise tolerance, quality of life, and reducing readmissions, innovative delivery models are needed to address this massive utilization gap. Virtual PR platforms have emerged as a potential solution, offering scalable, and home-based rehabilitation.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of a novel virtual PR program on functional, psychosocial, and cardiometabolic outcomes among adults with COPD.
