METHODS: This retrospective observational study analyzed outcomes among patients enrolled in a structured, multidisciplinary virtual PR program between 2022 and 2024. Participants completed individualized exercise and education sessions remotely, supported by a multidisciplinary team including Physicians and Clinical Exercise Physiologists. Baseline and postprogram measures were compared using Cohen d to assess effect sizes across clinical domains. Primary outcomes included changes in maximum metabolic equivalents (METs), Duke Activity Status Index (DASI), and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) scores. Other measures included changes in blood pressure (systolic and diastolic), smoking status, and prevalence of hypertension.

RESULTS: Among 2444 patients completing the program, the largest effect size improvements were observed in maximum METs achieved, DASI, and PHQ-9 scores. The program was also associated with decreased smoking rates and a lower prevalence of hypertension post intervention. Notably, 91% of the studied population self-identified as having a "fixed income," underscoring the potential for virtual PR to extend access to patients with lower incomes in the United States.

CONCLUSIONS: Virtual PR appears to be a promising and potentially more scalable alternative to traditional facility-based PR for patients with COPD. Significant improvements in exercise capacity, mood, and cardiovascular parameters suggest clinical benefit, while reductions in smoking and hypertension further highlight potential for broader health impact. Given the high proportion of participants on fixed incomes, virtual PR may represent an effective strategy to expand access and equity in chronic respiratory care delivery across the United States.

articles.title: Functional outcomes and quality of life after endovascular thrombectomy in large and extensive infarcts (ASPECTS 0-5): a multicentre registry study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) is established for large infarcts, but remains cautiously applied in extensive infarcts with an Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) of 0-2. Real-life outcome data remain limited.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Retrospective analysis of the German Stroke Registry-Endovascular Treatment comparing extensive (ASPECTS 0-2) and large infarcts (ASPECTS 3-5) in patients with anterior-circulation occlusion and EVT. The primary outcome was the ordinal 90-day mRS distribution; secondary outcomes were mRS 0-3, survival, quality of life (3-level European Quality of Life-5 Dimensions) and living condition.

RESULTS: Of 18,069 screened patients, 889 were analysed (ASPECTS 1-2, n = 89; ASPECTS 3-5, n = 800); none had ASPECTS 0. With ASPECTS 1-2, 20.2% achieved mRS 0-3 and 55.1% died within 90 days. In the model including successful reperfusion, no statistically significant association was detected between infarct group and the 90-day mRS distribution (common odds ratio [cOR] 0.80; 95% CI, 0.53-1.23) or mRS 0-3 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.89; 95% CI, 0.64-1.25), whereas successful reperfusion was associated with both (cOR 3.68; 95% CI, 2.31-5.85 and aOR 4.10; 95% CI, 2.45-6.86). Among survivors, median European Quality of Life-5 Dimensions utility index was 0.445 vs 0.541 (n = 27/324), and 51.5% vs 50.9% lived at home (n = 33/411).

DISCUSSION: An extensive infarct carried a challenging prognosis, yet acceptable outcome and non-institutional living remained achievable in a relevant minority. An independent association of infarct group with outcome was not detected.

CONCLUSION: An acceptable outcome remained attainable in selected patients with extensive infarction, particularly after successful reperfusion. Lacking a medically managed comparator, these data describe prognosis rather than treatment effect.

articles.title: Serum brain-derived tau in lacunar stroke and cerebral small vessel disease.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Brain-derived tau (BD-tau) selectively quantifies tau of central nervous system origin in blood and has demonstrated strong correlations with infarct volume and functional outcome in general ischaemic stroke, but data in lacunar stroke and cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) are lacking.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: In a prospectively collected cohort of 101 lacunar stroke patients with an MRI-confirmed recent small subcortical infarct (RSSI) and 47 controls, we measured serum BD-tau using the HD-X SIMOA platform at baseline and 3 and 15 months after stroke. We examined associations of BD-tau with infarct size, chronic CSVD neuroimaging features (white matter hyperintensities [WMHs], lacunes, microbleeds, total SVD score), CSVD progression on follow-up MRI and functional outcome.

RESULTS: Baseline serum BD-tau was higher in RSSI patients than controls (median 9.54 [7.32-12.20] vs 7.75 [6.18-9.44] pg/mL; P = .003) and correlated with infarct diameter (rs = 0.222, P = 0.039). Brain-derived tau did not correlate with time from stroke symptom onset to blood sampling (rs = 0.150, P = .179). Brain-derived tau was not associated with chronic CSVD neuroimaging features (WMHs, lacunes, microbleeds, SVD score; all P > .05) at any timepoint. Longitudinally, BD-tau returned to control levels by 3 months (P = .374) and remained stable at 15 months (P = .985). Brain-derived tau was neither associated with new vascular MRI lesions on follow-up nor functional neurological outcome.

CONCLUSION: Serum BD-tau is elevated acutely in CSVD-related RSSI, correlates with infarct size and normalises by 3 months. Brain-derived tau was not associated with chronic CSVD neuroimaging features or disease progression, suggesting sensitivity to acute neuronal injury rather than chronic or progressive CSVD.

articles.title: Tunable 18F-Labeling of Erlotinib-Based Small Molecule Nanodrugs for Rapid PET Imaging and Targeted Therapy.
articles.abstract: Small molecule nanodrugs (SMNs) offer unique advantages for cancer therapy, yet accurately tracking their in vivo fate without perturbing their native assembly remains challenging. Here, we report a spacer engineering strategy that enables efficient 1 8F-labeling while preserving SMNs self-assembly. Erlotinib-based amphiphilic derivatives containing oligoethylene glycol (OEG) spacers of tunable length were designed to simultaneously regulate steric hindrance for aliphatic SN2 radiofluorination and the amphiphilic balance required for nanoparticle formation. Spacer elongation reduced steric hindrance at the labeling site and thereby improved radiochemical yields, while also enabling precise control over nanoparticle size. The optimized radiolabeled formulation, [18F]E3FNPs, exhibited prolonged blood circulation and rapid tumor accumulation, enabling high-contrast PET imaging of PANC-1 xenografts as early as 15 min after injection. In addition, the corresponding nonradioactive formulation, E3FNPs, showed significantly improved antitumor efficacy compared with nonassembled E3F through reduced EGFR phosphorylation and increased tumor cell apoptosis. This work provides an initial evaluation that spacer engineering can coordinate radiolabeling and self-assembly while enabling PET tracking of SMNs, supporting the development of image-guided cancer theranostics.

articles.title: A Clot Before the Cancer: Cerebral Venous Sinus Thrombosis as the Initial Presentation of Childhood Acute Leukemia-A Case Report and Literature Review.
Functional and Structural Characterization of a Novel PROC Missense Mutation (p.Ser312Trp) in Pediatric Protein C Deficiency.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Hereditary protein C deficiency (HPCD) is an autosomal dominant thrombophilia caused by PROC gene mutations. The genotype-phenotype correlation is complex, and functional characterization of novel variants, especially in pediatric populations, remains limited. This study aimed to characterize the genetic profiles of Chinese pediatric patients with HPCD and to functionally validate the molecular mechanisms of a newly identified PROC missense mutation.

METHODS: Four Chinese pediatric patients with HPCD were enrolled. PROC mutations were identified by high-throughput sequencing. Wild-type (WT) and the p.Ser312Trp mutant expression plasmid were constructed and transfected into HEK293T cells. Intracellular protein expression was confirmed by Western blotting, amidolytic activity was measured by a chromogenic substrate assay, and secreted PC levels were quantified by ELISA. Protein structural modeling was performed using AlphaFold2 and Schrödinger software.

RESULTS: Six distinct PROC mutations were identified in four patients, including two novel variants: p.Ser312Trp and p.Ser312Ter. Functional characterization was focused on p.Ser312Trp, a novel missense variant. The mutant protein was secreted at levels comparable to WT but exhibited significantly reduced amidolytic activity (79.2% ± 3.1% vs. 100.5% ± 3.9%, p = 0.0017), consistent with a Type II (qualitative) deficiency phenotype. Structural modeling revealed that the bulky tryptophan substitution creates a new π-π stacking interaction with Trp276 and reorganizes the local hydrogen-bond network, causing minimal to mild destabilization (ΔΔG = -0.16 kcal/mol) that may be one of the factors contributing to the observed functional impairment.

CONCLUSION: This study provides the first functional and structural characterization of p.Ser312Trp, a novel PROC mutation causing Type II protein C deficiency in a Chinese pediatric patient. Our findings expand the mutational spectrum of HPCD and provide mechanistic insights into how this substitution selectively impairs catalytic function without affecting protein secretion, offering valuable evidence for molecular diagnosis and genetic counseling.

articles.title: Comparative Evaluation of 11 Machine Learning-Based Risk Prediction Models for Vancomycin-Associated Acute Kidney Injury During Initial Dosing.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vancomycin-associated acute kidney injury (AKI) can develop early during therapy and remains an important clinical concern. Although area under concentration-time curve (AUC)-guided dosing is recommended, the clinical relevance of early non-steady-state exposure for predicting AKI remains unclear. In this study, the authors aimed to develop and compare machine-learning models for predicting vancomycin-associated AKI using early exposure metrics.

METHODS: Early AUC values, trough concentrations, concomitant medications, and comorbidities were incorporated into machine learning models. Eleven algorithms were evaluated using nested cross validation to minimize optimistic bias and prevent data leakage.

RESULTS: Among 442 patients (median age, 72 years), 5.7% developed AKI. Across the models, day 2 AUC and trough concentration consistently emerged as the most influential predictors, followed by concomitant use of piperacillin/tazobactam, diuretics, and vasopressors. The random forest model demonstrated the best overall discriminative performance, with an area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve of 0.89 and area under the precision-recall curve of 0.47. SHapley Additive exPlanations indicated nonlinear increases in predicted AKI risk at a day 2 AUC of approximately ≥550 mg·h/L and trough concentration of approximately ≥20 mcg/mL. These findings suggest that early vancomycin exposure, particularly cumulative exposure during the first 48 hours, is strongly associated with AKI risk.

CONCLUSIONS: Machine learning models integrating early AUC values and trough concentrations may provide a clinically useful framework for individualized prediction of AKI risk during the early phase of vancomycin therapy.

articles.title: Evaluation of early hydrocortisone use for hemodynamic shock in adult burn patients with suspected critical illness related corticosteroid insufficiency.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: Critical illness-related corticosteroid insufficiency (CIRCI) presents as refractory hemodynamic shock in critically ill patients. Research on CIRCI and its treatment in burn patients is limited. We sought to review the use of corticosteroids in a burn population during their first week of hospitalization. The burn registry and the electronic medical records were queried for burn patients admitted between January 2015 and December 2025. The following variables were abstracted: demographics, burn history, hospital course, and treatments. Outcome variables included length of stay (LOS), infections, graft loss, pharmacological treatment, and mortality. The two groups were compared with Student's T-test and Chi Square where appropriate. A multivariant analysis was performed to determine independent predictors of CIRCI, infection and mortality. Significance was determined at p<0.05 level. The study group consisted of 87 patients in hemodynamic shock receiving vasopressors, with 47 also receiving corticosteroids. The corticosteroid group had larger burns (37.6 v 25.1%), more resuscitation (15.9 v 8.1 L), more vasopressor days (6.23 v 3.7 d), more ventilator days (19.72 v 7.83 d), more infections (66% v 34%) and longer LOS (51.53 v 26.05 d), all p<0.05. On multivariant analysis, variables independently related to the diagnosis of CIRCI were age and resuscitation fluids; to infection were corticosteroid use; and to mortality were age. Overall, over 50% of patients in hypotensive shock during their first week of treatment were diagnosed and treated with corticosteroids for suspected CIRCI. More study is needed to determine the appropriate role of corticosteroid use in early burn treatment.

articles.title: Perioperative Management of Children, Adolescents and Young Adults Undergoing Surgical Treatment for Oncologic Thoracic Disease: Retrospective Single-Center Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: No guidelines drive the perioperative management of children, adolescents, and young adults (CAYA) undergoing oncologic thoracic surgery. We analyzed our institutional procedures and perioperative results aiming to help develop standardized guidelines.

PROCEDURE: Records of CAYA patients operated on for a thoracic tumor (October 2021 to February 2025) were retrospectively analyzed. Standardized perioperative management included minimally invasive technique when feasible, early discharge to the ward, avoidance of sedation (drainage removal), systematic physiotherapy, early mobilization, and resumption of oral intake. Outcomes refer to the total number of surgeries.

RESULTS: Forty-seven CAYA (median age 15, interquartile range [IQR]: 12-18) underwent 54 operations removing localized tumor in 20 (37%), metastases in 33 (61.1%), and one (1.9%) local recurrence. In 36 cases (66.7%), surgery followed chemotherapy after 29.5 days (median; IQR: 22-47.3); in seven (13%), it was performed on a previously irradiated site. Eighteen procedures (33.3%) required resection of more than one organ; 17 (31.5%) were minimally invasive. In 10 (18.5%) cases, the first postoperative night was spent in the intensive care unit. Oral intake was resumed within postoperative day (POD) 1 in 46 (85.2%). Despite physical limitations to ambulation in 12 (22.2%) cases, in 49 (90.7%) the patient was mobilized and in 38 (70.4%) walked within POD1. Continuous intravenous opioid infusion was necessary in 23 (42.6%) cases, and sedation for drainage removal in one. There were 19 complications (35.2%), 89.5% of which were Grade I-II. Patients were discharged on POD5 (median, IQR: 4-8).

CONCLUSIONS: Standardized perioperative management in CAYA is possible and can lead to early mobilization and a low complication rate, despite complex complementary treatments (chemotherapy/radiotherapy) and limited access to intensive care resources.

articles.title: Differential transcriptomic responses of pmgA and ssr1600 single-knockout mutants to short-term and prolonged high-light exposure in the cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803.
articles.abstract: PmgA and Ssr1600, homologs of the anti-sigma factor and the anti-sigma antagonist of the bacterial partner-switching system, respectively, are involved in coordination of the repression of photosystem I content and chlorophyll biosynthesis under prolonged high-light (HL) conditions in the cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803. To characterize the transcriptional responses associated with PmgA and Ssr1600 during HL acclimation, we compared global gene expression profiles of the wild-type (WT) and knockout strains of pmgA (ΔpmgA) and ssr1600 (Δ1600) under low-light conditions and at 15 min, 1 h and 12 h after the shift to HL. The knockout of pmgA or ssr1600 induced temporally distinct transcriptomic alterations between short-term and prolonged HL exposure. At 15 min, Δ1600, but not ΔpmgA, showed enhanced induction of stress-responsive genes, including sigB and heat-shock genes, together with derepression of pmgA. At 12 h, both mutants showed significant upregulation of genes related to chlorophyll biosynthesis, photosynthetic electron transport, nitrogen assimilation, and amino acid biosynthesis. Considering that Ssr1600 does not accumulate in ΔpmgA, these observations can be explained by a shift in the role of Ssr1600, from the suppressor of the amplification of the stress response by PmgA under short-term HL conditions to a factor mediating signal output from the PmgA-Ssr1600 module under prolonged HL conditions, although the contribution of secondary effects cannot be excluded. Our transcriptomic data do not support the hypothesis that PmgA acts as a canonical anti-sigma factor for any of the sigma factors examined in this study, SigB, SigD and SigE, under either condition.

articles.title: Patterns of Pediatric Cancer Care at a Tertiary Center in Pakistan: A Hospital-Based Registry Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Childhood cancer outcomes remain poor in many low- and middle-income countries, in part due to delays in diagnosis, incomplete staging, and health system constraints. However, detailed site-level descriptions of pediatric oncology care pathways in South Asia remain limited.

METHODS: We conducted a descriptive observational analysis using routinely collected data from a hospital-based pediatric cancer registry at the Children's Hospital Lahore. Children and adolescents (<18 years) registered between July 2021 and April 2026 were included. We summarized demographics, cancer type distribution, diagnostic confirmation methods, treatment intent, care timelines from symptom onset to treatment initiation, and documented mortality outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 7583 children were registered. Median age at diagnosis was 5 years, and 61.2% were male. Leukemias and lymphomas accounted for 50.2% and 12.8% of confirmed diagnoses, respectively, with acute lymphoblastic leukemia the most common diagnosis (41.4%). Microscopic verification was achieved in over 90% of cases. Median time from symptom onset to first medical assessment was 25 days, and median time from diagnosis to treatment initiation was 2 days. Curative-intent treatment was initiated in over 80% of patients. Among patients with available follow-up data, 1437 deaths were documented, with longitudinal outcome data varying in maturity as follow-up accumulated through subsequent registry forms.

CONCLUSIONS: This large registry-based descriptive analysis provides a comprehensive overview of pediatric cancer presentation, diagnostic pathways, and treatment timelines at a major referral center in Pakistan. Findings demonstrated strengths in diagnostic confirmation and rapid treatment initiation following diagnosis, while identifying gaps including delays before first medical assessment and a substantial burden of infection-related mortality. This work demonstrates the feasibility of implementing large-scale hospital-based cancer registries in resource-constrained settings to support quality improvement and health system strengthening.

articles.title: Pediatric Intensive Care Unit Mortality Among Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Children undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) may require pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admission; a 2008 meta-regression reported 60% mortality. We estimated contemporary PICU mortality, temporal trends, and mortality risk factors. We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane Library from 2006 to 2026 for pediatric HSCT studies reporting PICU mortality. Estimates were pooled using a random-effects model, with temporal trends assessed by meta-regression and income-setting subgroup analyses. Of 1555 records, 35 studies including 4553 PICU admissions met inclusion criteria. PICU mortality was 37.35% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 31.54-43.54; I2 = 91.6%): 36.24% (95% CI: 30.30-42.63) in high-income and 41.90% (95% CI: 23.55-63.06) in upper-middle-income countries, without significant difference (p = 0.53). PICU mortality did not correlate with cohort midpoint year (p = 0.23). Invasive mechanical ventilation (odds ratio [OR] 5.02; 95% CI: 2.30-10.99), inotropic/vasopressor support (OR 5.75; 95% CI: 3.12-10.60), and continuous renal replacement therapy (OR 3.94; 95% CI: 2.63-5.92) were associated with mortality (all p < 0.001). Mechanical ventilation remained independently associated with mortality. PICU mortality among pediatric HSCT recipients is lower than the 60% reported in 2008, but remains substantial, particularly with organ support. Data from lower-income settings are scarce, representing a major evidence gap.

articles.title: Poloxamer 188 Promotes Severe Aggregation of Insulin under Shaking Conditions.
articles.abstract: Insulin is an indispensable cornerstone in the management of diabetes mellitus, yet its extreme susceptibility to aggregation under mechanical stress remains a formidable challenge for long-term formulation stability. This study investigates the potential of Poloxamer 188 (P188) as a chemically stable alternative to the industry-standard Polysorbate 20 (PS20) for stabilizing insulin. Formulations containing graded concentrations of P188 (0.005%-0.15%, w/v), 0.05% (w/v) PS20, or no surfactant were subjected to 24 h shaking stress at 300 rpm. Our results reveal a striking concentration-dependent profile for P188, where 0.05% PS20 consistently maintains robust protection, whereas low-to-moderate concentrations of P188 (0.005%-0.05%) fail to stabilize insulin and instead exert a pronounced "pro-aggregatory" effect. At 0.05% P188, this pro-aggregatory behavior leads to severe macroscopic turbidity, a massive surge in particle concentration (≥2 μm), and the near-total disappearance of detectable insulin monomers in the supernatant. Crucially, elevating the P188 concentration to 0.15% effectively prevents macroscopic turbidity and preserves high soluble protein recovery. Mechanistically, the instability observed at low-to-moderate P188 concentrations stems from its sluggish interfacial adsorption kinetics compared to PS20, leaving nascent air-liquid interfaces temporarily unprotected. Under such conditions, P188 functions as a macromolecular scaffold and nucleation core, cross-linking interface-denatured proteins with native molecules to drive rapid co-assembly. These findings serve as a critical warning for the biopharmaceutical industry that the use of P188 in insulin-based products must be approached with extreme caution to avoid inadvertent protein aggregation.

articles.title: PET Imaging of Dual GLP-1R and GIPR Targeting with [18F]AlF-NOTA-Asp2-Tirzepatide.
articles.abstract: Tirzepatide is a clinical dual GLP-1R and GIPR agonist for type 2 diabetes and obesity, and non-invasive approaches to assess its in vivo biodistribution and systemic toxicity in living animals remain limited. Both receptors also serve as potential targets for neuroendocrine tumor imaging, and dual-target PET probes for simultaneous GLP-1R and GIPR detection are still lacking. Herein, we developed a novel PET probe [18F]AlF-NOTA-Asp2-tirzepatide via structural modification of tirzepatide. This probe successfully visualized the in vivo distribution of tirzepatide, which was primarily eliminated through the renal system. The C20 fatty diacid moiety caused elevated uptake in the heart, liver and blood due to enhanced albumin binding. In vitro assays verified its reliable GLP-1R and moderate GIPR binding affinity. Persistent tumor accumulation was observed in INS-1 and A549-GIPR xenografts, allowing effective tumor visualization. In summary, [18F]AlF-NOTA-Asp2-tirzepatide features facile radiolabeling and enables the clear visualization of tirzepatide in vivo, along with favorable dual-targeting performance, while excessive non-target uptake still needs to be optimized for further clinical translation.

articles.title: Preclinical Study of the 89Zr/177Lu-Labeled Engineered VHH-based Antibody for CLDN18.2-Targeted Radiotheranostics.
articles.abstract: Claudin 18.2 (CLDN18.2) is a tight junction protein aberrantly expressed in gastric and pancreatic cancer. In this study, we developed the novel nanobody 18.2-50H and VHH-Fc fusion antibody 18.2-50C radiolabeled with 89Zr/177Lu for CLDN18.2-targeted radiotheranostics. Zolbetuximab (IMAB362), 18.2-50H, and 18.2-50C were conjugated with DFO and labeled with 89Zr, respectively. Radiochemical purity and in vitro stability were determined by radio-TLC. CLDN18.2-targeting specificity was evaluated using HEK-293T and HEK-293T/CLDN18.2 cells. PET/CT imaging and biodistribution studies were performed in mouse models and cynomolgus monkeys. Subsequently, 177Lu-DOTA-18.2-50C was prepared and assessed for tumor targeting in gastric cancer PDX models. 89Zr-DFO-IMAB362, 89Zr-DFO-18.2-50H, and 89Zr-DFO-18.2-50C were prepared with satisfactory radiochemical yield, specific activity, and stability. Tumors were clearly visible as early as 1 h post-injection of 89Zr-DFO-18.2-50H, with an uptake value of 9.07 ± 2.36 %ID/g and a tumor-to-muscle ratio of 27.35 ± 3.72. Fc-fused 89Zr-DFO-18.2-50C exhibited improved retention and higher tumor uptake than 89Zr-DFO-18.2-50H and 89Zr-DFO-IMAB362, with % ID/g increasing continuously from 5.07 ± 0.29 at 1 h to 32.95 ± 1.57 at 168 h. Notably, the introduction of the Fc chain also markedly increased the radiation exposure in the liver and spleen. Consistently, PET imaging in cynomolgus showed that 89Zr-DFO-18.2-50C is mainly concentrated in the liver, but no apparent abnormality was observed. Furthermore, 177Lu-DOTA-18.2-50C presented remarkable tumor selectivity with prolonged retention (16.92 ± 1.94 % ID/g at 5 d post-injection) in PDX models. Nanobody 89Zr-DFO-18.2-50H demonstrated a superior tumor-to-background ratio, positioning it as a promising tracer for detecting CLDN18.2-overexpressing lesions. 89Zr/177Lu-labeled VHH-Fc antibody 18.2-50C exhibited sustained higher tumor uptake than commercially available IMAB362 and provides a novel potential candidate for CLDN18.2-targeted radionuclide therapy.

articles.title: Injectable Thermosensitive Hydrogel Synergizes Antibacterial Action with Microenvironment Remodeling in Infected Diabetic Wounds.
articles.abstract: Chronic wounds represent substantial clinical challenges due to their intricate pathophysiology, characterized by persistent infection, sustained inflammation, and compromised tissue regeneration. To overcome these obstacles, we developed an injectable thermosensitive hydrogel system (MR-NPs-Gels), incorporating engineered PLGA nanoparticles (MR-NPs) for the co-delivery of mupirocin, a first-line antibacterial agent, and l-arginine, a nitric oxide (NO) precursor. The MR-NPs-Gels exhibited favorable injectability, tissue adaptability, and ideal rheological properties. MR-NPs penetrated deep into tissues to exert antibacterial effects, while l-arginine released from them generated NO to exert anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic effects. In diabetic wound models, MR-NPs-Gels achieved a 77.39 ± 1.19% wound closure rate and more than 80% reduction in bacterial colony counts by day 9. Compared with commercial mupirocin ointment, this hydrogel significantly downregulated pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-6 and TNF-α, while upregulating angiogenic markers VEGF and CD31. Collectively, the co-delivery of mupirocin and l-arginine within MR-NPs-Gels enhances bacterial clearance and remodels the wound microenvironment synergistically, offering a promising topical therapeutic strategy for infected chronic wounds.

articles.title: 68Ga-NOTA-FAPI-IF7: A Heterobivalent PET Probe for Dual-Targeted Imaging of Fibroblast Activation Protein and Annexin A1 in Tumor Microenvironment.
articles.abstract: Fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-targeted PET tracers enable high-contrast tumor imaging but suffer from rapid clearance and non-specific uptake in inflammatory lesions. The heptapeptide IF7 binds annexin A1 (ANXA1) on tumor vascular endothelium, a target directly accessible from the bloodstream. To overcome these limitations, we developed a heterobivalent PET probe, NOTA-FAPI-IF7, based on a rationally designed dual-targeting strategy that simultaneously engages FAP in cancer-associated fibroblasts and ANXA1 on tumor vasculature. Radiolabeling with 68Ga achieved a radiochemical yield of 92.3 ± 3.6% (decay-corrected, n = 5) with excellent stability (radiochemical purity >97% at all time points). In vitro assays confirmed dual-target binding (IC50 = 27.9 nM, KD = 3.77 nM). Micro-PET imaging demonstrated rapid tumor visualization as early as 10 min post-injection (6.02 ± 0.07% ID/g), with uptake significantly reduced by blocking with excess unlabeled FAPI, IF7, or NOTA-FAPI-IF7. The probe exhibited favorable hydrophilicity (log P = -1.20) and renal clearance with low hepatobiliary uptake. This bispecific strategy, distinct from monospecific and homomultimeric approaches, offers a promising avenue for precision oncologic PET imaging.

articles.title: Repurposing Antibody-Drug Conjugates for Theranostic Targeting of Nectin-4 and TROP2 in Bladder Cancer.
articles.abstract: The application of antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) therapies in advanced bladder cancers may be improved through non-invasive molecular imaging and therapy with targeted radiation. Enfortumab and Sacituzumab, the antibody components for the ADCs PADCEV (Nectin-4 targeting) and TRODELVY (TROP2 targeting), were developed as ImmunoPET and radioimmunotherapeutic modalities in a HT1376 xenograft model of advanced bladder cancer. Both immuno-PET agents displayed distinct tumor uptake in vivo, with Sacituzumab showing higher accumulation (% ID/g) compared to Enfortumab, reflecting the higher TROP2 expression in this tumor model over Nectin-4. Further, both [177Lu]Lu-DOTA-Enfortumab and [177Lu]Lu-DOTA-Sacituzumab were effective in reducing the growth of tumors in vivo. The repurposing of well-validated ADC antibodies as theranostic radiopharmaceuticals is a promising approach for alternative or adjuvant therapies.

articles.title: Experimental and Computational Characterization of Human Serum Albumin Recognition by Ga(III)-NOTA Dendrimer Nanomicelles with Distinct PET Biodistribution Profiles.
articles.abstract: We investigate the interaction of human serum albumin (HSA) with two Ga(III)-NOTA-functionalized amphiphilic dendrimers 1 and 2 that self-assemble into corresponding nanomicelles 1@ and 2@, which were previously evaluated as positron emission tomography imaging nanoplatforms with distinct biodistribution profiles. These two nanosystems share the same Ga(III)-NOTA surface chemistry but differ in hydrophobic architecture and, consequently, in micellar stability. A combined physicochemical and computational workflow was used to quantify albumin binding, protein structural response, colloidal changes, and interfacial organization. Fluorescence quenching indicated HSA engagement by both nanomicelles, with a stronger perturbation of the Trp214 emission response for 2@. Isothermal titration calorimetry confirmed this ranking, showing that HSA has higher apparent affinity for 2@ than for 1@ (Kd = 8.2 ± 3.8 μM and 39.4 ± 26.7 μM, respectively), with exothermic and thermodynamically favorable association in both cases. Analysis of the integrated heat profiles supported apparent compositions of approximately three HSA molecules per 1@ micelle and four HSA molecules per 2@ micelle. Circular dichroism and three-dimensional fluorescence showed that HSA largely retains its α-helical structure and Trp214 microenvironment upon binding, whereas dynamic light scattering and zeta-potential measurements confirmed formation of protein-nanomicelle complexes. Enhanced-sampling simulations reproduced the preferred HSA loading states and suggested that 2@ promotes a broader Ga(III)-NOTA-rich interfacial network. These findings indicate that the internal hydrophobic architecture can modulate albumin recognition even when the nominal Ga(III)-NOTA surface chemistry is conserved, providing a plausible molecular explanation for the distinct biodistribution behavior of these nanoprobes in biomedical imaging.

articles.title: A γ-AApeptide-Based Antibody-like Peptidomimetic for Enhanced EGFR-Targeted PET Imaging.
articles.abstract: Targeted imaging for the extracellular domain (ECD) of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) is promising for early diagnosis and therapeutic applications toward cancers. Herein, we report the design of a γ-AApeptide-based antibody-like peptidomimetic as a radiotracer for EGFR-targeted positron emission tomography (PET) imaging. A dimeric cyclic γ-AApeptide (D1) was designed by dimerizing a previously reported EGFR-binding peptidomimetic ligand, resulting in a 6-fold enhancement in binding affinity (Kd = 0.11 μM) compared to its monomeric counterpart (M1, Kd = 0.67 μM). Both ligands were conjugated with chelators and radiolabeled with 64Cu to yield [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-M1 (monomer) and [64Cu]Cu-DOTA-D1 (dimer), respectively. In vivo PET imaging demonstrated that [64Cu]Cu-DOTA-D1 achieved significantly higher tumor uptake than [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-M1 in EGFR-positive tumor models (e.g., 10.83 ± 2.70 %ID/g vs 2.80 ± 0.72 %ID/g in U87 tumors at 4 h p.i.). Blocking and EGFR-negative control studies further confirmed the targeting specificity of [64Cu]Cu-DOTA-D1. Ex vivo biodistribution analysis showed consistent enhancement in tumor uptake (e.g., 7.94 ± 0.24 %ID/g vs 3.81 ± 0.44 %ID/g in U87 tumors at 48 h p.i.) for the dimeric tracer, accompanied by increased uptake in clearance organs. Overall, this work demonstrates that cyclic γ-AApeptides could serve as effective antibody-like peptidomimetics for EGFR targeting in vivo and provides a versatile strategy for developing peptidomimetic radiotracers for molecular imaging applications.

articles.title: Characterization of a 64Cu-Labeled Heterobivalent Bicyclic Peptide (Nectin-4/Albumin) for Targeting of Tumor-Associated Nectin-4.
articles.abstract: The cell adhesion protein Nectin-4 has been proven as an effective target for therapeutic approaches in bladder cancer. In addition, the interest as a target protein for targeted radionuclide theranostic approaches is growing. While several promising radioligands for imaging purposes have been described in recent years, therapeutic radioligands are largely missing so far, which is mainly reasoned by a comparatively low uptake into the tumor tissue accompanied by a fast washout kinetic of the radioligand. In this study, we investigated how the introduction of an albumin-binding unit into our previously developed ligand NECT-224, which is structurally derived from the bicyclic toxin conjugate BT8009, can improve the integral tumor uptake. The resulting heterobivalent ligand NECT-308 was successfully synthesized via solid-phase peptide synthesis. Nectin-4-selective binding was confirmed by surface plasmon resonance interaction analysis. The radiopharmacological characterization of [64Cu]Cu-NECT-308 in vitro revealed an albumin-binding affinity of 25 μM and an apparent binding affinity to cellular Nectin-4 of 14 nM as assessed by an ultrafiltration assay using human serum albumin and saturation binding analysis using intact HT-1376 cells (urothelial carcinoma cell line), respectively. PET imaging studies in HT-1376 tumor-bearing mice highlighted an almost fourfold higher integral tumor uptake of [64Cu]Cu-NECT-308 over 24 h compared to [64Cu]Cu-NECT-224. As expected, this was accompanied by an increased activity retention in the blood circulation and also by an increased kidney uptake. Control experiments with either a radioligand that exhibits a comparable binding affinity to albumin but bears no Nectin-4-targeting unit or by blocking the binding of [64Cu]Cu-NECT-308 to tumor-associated Nectin-4 revealed that the increase in tumor uptake is mainly attributed to Nectin-4-independent mechanisms. The implications of this finding, in particular regarding the clinical translation of such heterobivalent radioligands, are discussed in detail. The radiopharmacological characterization of [64Cu]Cu-NECT-308 was complemented by dosimetric calculations for [64/67Cu]Cu-NECT-224 and [64/67Cu]Cu-NECT-308 in mice and humans, which indicated that the kidneys are the dose-limiting organs. Overall, our results reveal that further structural optimizations of the Nectin-4-directed bicyclic peptide scaffold are necessary to achieve a higher and longer Nectin-4-dependent tumor uptake as well as a lower kidney uptake to enable a potential radioligand therapy. The introduction of an albumin-binding unit as done herein can only partly address these requirements.

articles.title: Radiohalogenated Tetrazines for Click Chemistry-Mediated Pretargeted Radioimmunotherapy.
articles.abstract: In vivo pretargeting is an emergent approach to nuclear imaging and radiopharmaceutical therapy that leverages the exquisite selectivity and affinity of full-length immunoglobulins while skirting their pharmacokinetic and dosimetric limitations. One particularly promising approach to pretargeting is predicated on the inverse electron-demand Diels-Alder reaction between a trans-cyclooctene (TCO)-bearing antibody and a tetrazine (Tz)-based radioligand. This methodology has been validated with a wide variety of antibody-antigen systems paired with radionuclides for positron emission tomography (PET), single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), and radioimmunotherapy. The halogen group of the periodic table offers an abundance of isotopes that emit β--particles (i.e. 131I), α-particles (i.e. 211At), and Auger electrons (i.e. 125I) for radiopharmaceutical therapy. Herein, we describe the synthesis and characterization of a pair of Tz radioligands containing 131I-labeled residualizing guanidinium prosthetic groups: iso-[131I]GMIB-PEG6-Tz and iso-[131I]GMIB-Tz. Subsequently, these two radioligands were used in conjunction with a TCO-bearing variant of the A33 antigen-targeting mAb huA33 (i.e. huA33-TCO) for in vivo pretargeting experiments in a murine model of colorectal carcinoma. The biodistribution and dosimetry data from these preclinical experiments suggested that the PEG6-containing radioligand offered a superior pharmacokinetic profile, and protocols were developed for the synthesis of iso-[211At]AGMB-PEG6-Tz. Finally, the in vivo behavior of iso-[211At]AGMB-PEG6-Tz was probed in both healthy mice and in a pretargeting system paired with huA33-TCO in a murine model of colorectal carcinoma.

articles.title: First-in-Human PET/CT Imaging of FXX489, a Second-Generation Cyclic Peptide FAP Inhibitor: A Translational Exploratory Study.
articles.abstract: Sufficient tumor uptake and retention, and high tumor-to-kidney ratio are highly relevant for fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-targeted tracers as imaging companions for theranostic development. Although FAP-2286 improves tumor retention versus early-generation FAPI tracers, its extended renal residence limits its application as a radiopharmaceutical therapy. We benchmarked FXX489, a next-generation cyclic peptide FAP ligand, against FAP-2286 preclinically and evaluated first-in-human [68Ga]Ga-FXX489 PET/CT to support its translational development for FAP-directed theranostics. [68Ga]Ga-FXX489 showed stronger FAP affinity than [68Ga]Ga-FAP-2286, including higher cellular uptake, lower efflux, and lower IC50. In HT-1080-hFAP xenografts, [68Ga]Ga-FXX489 achieved higher tumor uptake and retention on micro-PET and ex vivo biodistribution, and a higher tumor-to-kidney ratio. In patients (n = 10), [68Ga]Ga-FXX489 was well tolerated, and detected all 12 primary lesions (mean SUVmax, 11.20 ± 3.24) and all 42 metastatic lymph nodes (100% [42/42] vs 74% [31/42] for [18F]FDG, P < 0.001), while visualizing gastric cancer lesions with higher uptake than [18F]FDG in a paired comparison. [68Ga]Ga-FXX489 improves tumor retention and tumor-to-kidney ratio compared to [68Ga]Ga-FAP-2286 while maintaining specific FAP targeting. First-in-human [68Ga]Ga-FXX489 PET/CT shows promising detection of primary and metastatic lesions, supporting further clinical applications.

articles.title: Development and Preclinical Evaluation of [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-L3: A Novel PET Tracer for Quantitative Imaging of Carbonic Anhydrase IX.
articles.abstract: Carbonic anhydrase IX (CA IX) is a key biomarker for tumor hypoxia and a promising target for molecular imaging. In this study, we developed [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-L3, a novel small-molecule CA IX-targeted PET tracer. The radiolabeling was optimized to consistently achieve a radiochemical purity of >98% (10 μg precursor, 90 °C, pH 4.5, 10 min), with excellent stability in saline and FBS up to 240 min. In vivo studies demonstrated rapid blood clearance and predominant renal excretion. Surface plasmon resonance analysis demonstrated high-affinity binding of the DOTA-L3 precursor toward CA IX (Kd = 7.60 ± 0.37 nM) with highest affinity observed for CA IX among the tested isoforms. MicroPET/CT imaging (30-240 min p.i.) showed robust tumor accumulation in OSRC-2 (SUVmean = 1.47 ± 0.21) and HT-29 (SUVmean = 1.03 ± 0.12) xenografts, while minimal uptake was observed in CA IX-low FTC-238 tumors (SUVmean = 0.21 ± 0.05) at 60 min p.i. PET-derived tumor uptake showed a strong linear correlation with CA IX expression levels (R2 = 0.976, P < 0.001) across the three tumor models. High tumor-to-muscle and tumor-to-blood ratios further confirm favorable imaging contrast (T/M = 27.53 ± 1.89 and T/B = 24.61 ± 2.35 at 240 min p.i. for OSRC-2 model). These results support [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-L3 as a promising candidate for non-invasive assessment of CA IX-associated hypoxia and as a scaffold for future theranostic development.

articles.title: Engineering Hybrid Peptides and Ionic Liquid-Peptide Conjugates for a Fast Action on Bacterial Membranes.
articles.abstract: Fast-acting peptide-based antimicrobials that target bacterial membranes are herein addressed and promise a breakthrough in chronic wound care. Two peptide hybrids (3.1-PP4 and PP4-3.1), engineered by us, resulted from linking PP4 (a non-antimicrobial anti-aging peptide used in cosmetics) to the antimicrobial peptide 3.1. In contrast, the replacement of the latter with an antimicrobial ionic liquid afforded an ionic liquid-peptide conjugate C16-Im-PP4. Herein, we demonstrate their rapid bactericidal action by targeting bacterial membranes via a combination of biophysical assays and microscopy using liposome models of bacterial membranes and live bacteria. Interestingly, the peptide hybrids share a similar membrane-disruptive mechanism against Gram-positive Staphylococcus aureus and Gram-negative Escherichia coli. In turn, the ionic liquid-peptide conjugate C16-Im-PP4 displayed bacterial-type-dependent behavior. These findings underscore the potential of peptide-based agents to address chronic wounds, which remain vulnerable to infection due to prolonged inflammation and rising antibiotic resistance that is increasingly regarded as a "silent pandemic".

articles.title: Molecular Dynamics Simulation-Guided 124I/211At-Labeled Aromatic Amide Derivatives as a Potential Theranostic Pair for Melanoma.
articles.abstract: Targeted alpha therapy (TAT) based on 211At represents a highly promising therapeutic strategy for various cancers, yet the rational design of molecular structures remains challenging in practical translation. In this work, we proposed a molecular dynamics (MD) simulation-guided strategy for constructing 124I/211At-labeled aromatic amide derivatives as a potential theranostic pair for melanoma. The interaction process between melanin and a series of aromatic amide derivatives was first investigated via MD simulation, emphasizing that dimethylamino derivatives possessed superior binding ability. Furthermore, radioiodinated dimethylamino derivative [124I]Dm-5-IPLA was proven to have the best tumor-targeting capability and favorable pharmacokinetics via systematic experimental investigations including in vitro cell testing, in vivo PET imaging, and ex vivo biodistribution investigations. Its therapeutic analogue, [211At]Dm-5-APLA, accordingly exhibited effective tumor growth inhibition and satisfactory safety in the TAT of B16F10 tumor-bearing mice, indicating the potential of 124I/211At-labeled aromatic amide derivatives for melanoma theranostics.

articles.title: Longitudinal Changes in Exocrine Biomarkers in Children at Risk of Type 1 Diabetes in the ENDIA Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The exocrine pancreas is increasingly implicated in type 1 diabetes. Noninvasive biomarkers of exocrine function, fecal elastase-1 (FE-1) and serum immunoreactive trypsin (IRT), may provide early insight into disease pathogenesis. We investigated the temporal relationship between exocrine biomarkers and type 1 diabetes development in children.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: FE-1 and IRT concentrations were measured prospectively in 301 at-risk children followed in the Environmental Determinants of Islet Autoimmunity (ENDIA) cohort from birth. A total of 216 children provided 1,679 stool samples; 242 provided 1,014 serum samples. Biomarker trajectories were compared between children who developed islet autoimmunity or type 1 diabetes and age- and sex-matched control children negative for autoantibodies in a nested case-control design. Adjusted linear mixed models were used.

RESULTS: Two biomarker patterns were observed. FE-1 concentrations were lower during the first 6 months of life in children who subsequently developed multiple islet autoantibodies or type 1 diabetes (β-coefficient at birth -0.61 [95% CI -1.04, -0.17]; P = 0.006; β-coefficient at 3 months -0.39 [95% CI -0.69, -0.09]; P = 0.010); IRT concentrations were lower in children who developed type 1 diabetes 12 months (β = -0.30 [95% CI -0.58, -0.02]; P = 0.034) and 18 months (β = -0.40 [95% CI -0.71, -0.10]; P = 0.008) before type 1 diabetes diagnosis.

CONCLUSIONS: Changes in exocrine biomarkers were detectable early in the natural history of type 1 diabetes, with a delayed rise of FE-1 in infants who later progressed to multiple islet autoantibodies or type 1 diabetes and a decrease in IRT following islet autoantibody seroconversion.

articles.title: Borrelia burgdorferi binds serum amyloid A and modulates subcutaneous adipose tissue immune signaling.
articles.abstract: Following a tick bite, Borrelia burgdorferi spirochetes replicate in human skin and disseminate through tissues, including subcutaneous adipose tissue. Adipose is a complex organ containing both immune and non-immune cells that play a significant role in the immune response, yet little is known about adipose-specific immune signaling after B. burgdorferi infection. We investigated the landscape of immune signaling within adipose tissue-resident cells during B. burgdorferi infection in human tissue (skin and adipose tissue) ex vivo. Single-cell sequencing pathway analysis revealed upregulation of inflammatory pathways in skin, yet overall downregulation of immune pathways in adipose tissue cells during B. burgdorferi infection. Adipose-resident myeloid cells and adipose stem/progenitor cells (ASPCs) displayed an inflammatory profile characterized by the increased expression of IL-1β, TNF, and NFKB1. CellChat, a cellular communication comparative analysis, showed increased cell-to-cell communication across adipose-resident cell populations. ASPCs demonstrated the strongest outgoing signals, positioning them as key hubs of intercellular communication in adipose tissue. Interestingly, we observed adipose-specific downregulation of serum amyloid A (SAA), an inflammatory serum marker known to have antimicrobial properties and typically elevated in Lyme disease patients during acute infection. Therefore, we further evaluated the interaction between SAA and B. burgdorferi. Here, we show that human recombinant SAA protein directly binds B. burgdorferi spirochetes, reduces spirochete viability in a dose-dependent manner in vitro, and enhances phagocytosis. Taken together, these findings show that adipose tissue is a site of active immune signaling in the setting of infection and identify SAA as a host defense factor against B. burgdorferi.IMPORTANCEBorrelia burgdorferi is the bacterium that is transmitted by ticks and causes Lyme disease. These bacteria replicate in the skin to cause the localized skin rash erythema migrans, then disseminate to cause symptoms in other organs, including the joints and heart. Adipose tissue, or fat, is adjacent to skin, joints, and heart-all target organs of infection. In this study, we set out to understand how adipose tissue/fat plays a role in Lyme disease. We discovered that B. burgdorferi infection leads to an immune response in adipose tissue cells with specific downregulation of a gene called serum amyloid A (SAA). Our work shows that B. burgdorferi bacteria bind serum amyloid A (SAA), leading to decreased viability in vitro and enhanced uptake of B. burgdorferi by white blood cells. These findings highlight the dynamic role our fat can play during B. burgdorferi infection and can lead to the identification of new treatments for Lyme disease.

articles.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Versus Empagliflozin or Dapagliflozin in the MASLD-Heart Failure Phenotype: An Exploratory Propensity-Matched Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treatment selection may confound observational comparisons of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) in adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and heart failure (HF).

AIMS: To compare recorded outcomes between treatment groups and examine whether the associations persisted after restricting the analysis by agent and diabetes status and separating early and later outcome windows.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective, initiation-based, active-comparator cohort study (new-user design not verified).

METHODS: We used the TriNetX US Collaborative Network and a common index eligibility period from January 1, 2018, through June 2, 2026. The revised analyses were performed on September 12, 2026. An additional sensitivity analysis of acute HF excluded patients with this outcome before the start of the day 1-1825 window. The primary analysis compared semaglutide, liraglutide, or dulaglutide with empagliflozin or dapagliflozin using 1:1 propensity score matching and assessed outcomes during days 1-1825. Separate analyses of the broader GLP-1 RA group examined outcomes during days 1-90 and 91-1825 and among patients with type 2 diabetes and no recorded type 1 diabetes. We report endpoint-specific event proportions, risk differences, hazard ratios (HRs), 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and proportionality test results.

RESULTS: The primary analysis included 8,550 patients per group after matching. Mortality occurred in 599/8,514 (7.0%) versus 861/8,509 (10.1%); the HR was 0.607 (95% CI, 0.546-0.673). Coded acute HF diagnoses occurred in 1,217/8,550 (14.2%) versus 2,525/8,550 (29.5%); the HR was 0.398 (95% CI, 0.372-0.427), with evidence of non-proportional hazards. In separately matched descriptive interval analyses (8,489 patients per group), the HR for coded acute HF was 0.262 (95% CI, 0.236-0.291) during days 1-90 and 0.507 (95% CI, 0.469-0.548) during days 91-1825. The HR for acute kidney injury during the later interval was 0.740 (95% CI, 0.650-0.842). Among 5,709 matched pairs with type 2 diabetes and no recorded type 1 diabetes, the HR for coded acute HF was 0.431 (95% CI, 0.397-0.468), whereas the HR for ketoacidosis was 0.683 (95% CI, 0.455-1.025). No advantage was observed for acute pancreatitis in any analysis. In a separate analysis excluding patients with prior acute HF, the HR was 0.421 (95% CI, 0.362-0.489), with evidence of non-proportional hazards. Albumin and bilirubin remained imbalanced in a direction favoring the GLP-1 RA group; body mass index also remained imbalanced.

CONCLUSION: GLP-1 RA exposure was associated with lower observed hazards for several outcomes, and the association with coded acute HF was weaker after day 90. The early concentration and magnitude of this association make treatment channeling a plausible explanation, although this analysis cannot establish that explanation. These exploratory findings do not support causal inferences or treatment-preference conclusions and do not challenge randomized evidence supporting SGLT2i use in HF.

articles.title: Regional lesion burden and chronic post-stroke aphasia severity: Incremental value beyond total lesion volume.
articles.abstract: We examined whether regional lesion burden adds information beyond clinical variables and total lesion volume regarding chronic aphasia severity. This secondary analysis of the Aphasia Recovery Cohort included 195 participants with left-hemisphere stroke, Western Aphasia Battery Aphasia Quotient (AQ) ≤93.8, and assessment ≥180 days after stroke. Lesion burden was quantified in five atlas-defined groups. Partial Spearman correlations were adjusted for age at stroke, sex, time to assessment, and lesion volume, and four ridge-regression models were compared using 30 repetitions of five-fold cross-validation. A sensitivity analysis included participants whose imaging and Western Aphasia Battery assessments were ≤90 days apart (n = 128). Dorsal white-matter burden remained associated with lower AQ after adjustment (partial ρ = -0.261; false-discovery-rate q = 0.002). Adding regional burdens to the clinical-plus-volume model increased mean cross-validated R2 from 0.306 to 0.384 (ΔR2 = 0.078) and reduced mean absolute error from 18.76 to 17.31 AQ points. In the time-restricted sample, R2 increased from 0.312 to 0.442 (ΔR2 = 0.130), with the dorsal association persisting (partial ρ = -0.307). Regional lesion burden adds information beyond lesion volume and supports anatomical characterization of chronic aphasia severity.

articles.title: Association of Thyroid Autoimmunity With Age-Related Macular Degeneration in U.S. Adults.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the associations of thyroid autoimmunity, assessed by thyroid peroxidase antibody (TPOAb) and thyroglobulin antibody (TgAb), with prevalent age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in U.S. adults, and to explore whether genetic liabilities to Hashimoto thyroiditis (HT) and Graves' disease (GD) were associated with AMD risk using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR).

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 2967 adults aged 40 years or older from the 2007-2008 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. Survey-weighted logistic regression models included TPOAb and TgAb positivity simultaneously. Two-sample MR analyses were exploratory.

RESULTS: Among 2967 participants, 234 had AMD, corresponding to a weighted prevalence of 6.6% (95% confidence interval [CI], 5.6%-7.9%). In the mutually adjusted observational model, TgAb positivity was associated with higher odds of prevalent AMD (odds ratio [OR], 2.02; 95% CI, 1.13-3.61; P = 0.022), whereas TPOAb positivity was not associated with AMD (OR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.63-1.37; P = 0.676). Exploratory MR analyses suggested a possible association between genetic liability to HT and AMD (OR, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.01-1.29; P = 0.033), whereas evidence for GD was less consistent.

CONCLUSIONS: TgAb positivity was associated with prevalent AMD. The cross-sectional design and the nonidentical exposures assessed in the observational and MR analyses preclude causal inference.

TRANSLATIONAL RELEVANCE: Thyroglobulin antibody positivity was associated with prevalent AMD and may reflect a systemic immune phenotype warranting prospective investigation.

articles.title: Higher Blood Eosinophil Counts During Acute Preschool Wheeze Are Associated With School-Age Asthma: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To assess whether blood eosinophil counts (BEC) measured during acute preschool wheeze were associated with asthma after age five and added predictive information to clinical factors.

METHODS: We reviewed the records of 1373 children aged 1-5, hospitalized for wheezing at a tertiary centre (2013-2024). Clinical predictors and BEC were obtained from the earliest available complete blood count during the index wheezing hospitalization. Respiratory outcomes were assessed for 323 children with available hospital and affiliated outpatient records after their fifth birthday. We used logistic regression and ROC analysis to assess whether BEC predicted later asthma.

RESULTS: Persistent wheeze/asthma was identified in 115 children (35.6%). Median BEC was higher in children with persistent wheeze/asthma than in those without asthma (0.30 [0.10-0.66] vs. 0.14 [0.03-0.30] × 103/μL; p < 0.001). BEC alone showed modest discrimination (AUC 0.673) and improved prediction when combined with five clinical predictors (AUC 0.789). A BEC threshold of 0.57 × 103/μL identified a high-specificity subgroup (sensitivity 30.4%, specificity 92.8%).

CONCLUSION: BECs during acute wheezing hospitalization were independently associated with later asthma and provided modest incremental predictive information when combined with clinical features. BEC may help identify hospitalized preschool children with wheeze who warrant closer follow-up. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Inpatient Erythropoiesis-Stimulating Agent Use and Anemia-Related Outcomes in Patients With Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: Inpatient erythropoiesis-stimulating agent (ESA) management varies across institutions and is often influenced by system-level prescribing constraints, but the clinical impact of ESA interruption during hospitalization is unclear. This study evaluated anemia-related outcomes associated with shorter vs longer durations of inpatient ESA interruption in hospitalized patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) in the setting of an electronic order entry restriction. This retrospective cohort study included hospitalized adult patients receiving ESA treatment prior to admission for anemia of CKD. Patients were grouped by duration of inpatient ESA interruption. The primary outcome was packed red blood cell (PRBC) transfusion during hospitalization. Secondary outcomes included hemoglobin (Hgb) below 7 g/dL, rehospitalization for anemia, bleeding, and mortality within 90 days post-discharge, time to transfusion, and hospital length of stay. Seventy-four patients met inclusion criteria. A higher proportion of patients with ≥10 days of ESA interruption required PRBC transfusion compared to those with <10 days (72.0% vs 54.2%, P = 0.13). Similar patterns were observed across other anemia-related outcomes, including Hgb <7 g/dL, rehospitalization for anemia, bleeding, and mortality. Time to transfusion was longer and hospital length of stay was greater in the ≥10-day group. These differences did not reach statistical significance. Longer inpatient interruption of ESA therapy was associated with consistent trends toward increased transfusion use and greater anemia burden among patients with CKD. Variation in inpatient ESA management, including system-level prescribing constraints, may influence anemia-related outcomes in this population and warrants further study.

articles.title: Lactate accumulation triggered by RNA virus infection facilitates viral replication.
articles.abstract: As the terminal product of glycolysis, lactate has emerged as a crucial signaling molecule mediating metabolic reprogramming with immune regulation. Although RNA viruses are known to exploit host metabolism, the precise role of lactate accumulation in viral pathogenesis remains to be fully elucidated. Using Newcastle disease virus and influenza A virus as model pathogens, this study demonstrates that RNA virus infection rapidly activates host glycolysis and induces sustained lactate accumulation, thereby creating a microenvironment favorable for viral replication. Pharmacological inhibition of glycolysis markedly suppressed viral proliferation. In inhibition-rescue experiments, exogenous lactate supplementation reversed the antiviral immune gene and IRF3-phosphorylation changes induced by glycolytic inhibition. Adding exogenous sodium lactate without inhibiting glycolysis further repressed antiviral immune gene expression and IRF3 phosphorylation. Mechanistically, virus-induced lactate accumulation was associated with suppression of the retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I)-like receptor signaling pathway: excess lactate acted upstream of interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3), in a manner consistent with inhibition of the mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein (MAVS)-IRF3 axis, thereby attenuating type I interferon production. Together, these findings define a positive feedback loop in which RNA viruses exploit host metabolic reprogramming to accumulate lactate, which in turn restrains antiviral innate immunity and favors viral replication.IMPORTANCERNA viruses have no metabolism of their own and must rewire the host cell to replicate. Here, using two viruses from different families-Newcastle disease virus and influenza A virus-we show that infection rapidly drives host glucose uptake and glycolysis and causes lactate to accumulate. Lactate is not an inert by-product: blocking glycolysis lowers lactate, derepresses type I interferon and interferon-stimulated gene expression, and restricts viral replication, while adding lactate back reverses immune-signaling changes induced by glycolytic inhibition and further suppresses interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3) phosphorylation. Lactate therefore functions as an immunomodulatory effector linking virus-driven metabolic reprogramming to weakened innate immunity, consistent with inhibition of the mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein (MAVS)-IRF3 axis, forming a positive feedback loop that favoring replication. Since this loop was observed in two distinct RNA viruses, glycolysis and lactate handling may represent host-directed targets for antiviral intervention, while lactate's broader clinical relevance as an immune biomarker requires further investigation.

articles.title: Generation of a fully infectious SARS-CoV-2 encoding an internally tagged nsp3.
articles.abstract: The analysis of coronavirus replicase proteins during authentic infection is experimentally challenging, particularly for large and essential components embedded within virus-induced replication organelles. Non-structural protein 3 (nsp3), the largest coronavirus replicase protein, plays a central role in replication organelle formation, but has remained difficult to genetically manipulate. Here, we generated a fully infectious recombinant SARS-CoV-2 encoding an internal ALFA epitope tag upstream of the Mac1 domain within nsp3 (rALFA). Growth kinetics analyses demonstrated that rALFA replicated with kinetics and peak titers comparable to those of untagged recombinant SARS-CoV-2, and retained lytic infection. Tagged nsp3 displayed subcellular localization patterns equal to those observed in infections with untagged virus, and nanobody-based detection enabled robust visualization of nsp3 in infected cells. This internally tagged SARS-CoV-2 establishes a useful experimental platform for future analyses of nsp3 localization and replication organelle dynamics under authentic infection conditions, and provides a foundation for subsequent functional studies.IMPORTANCEThe manuscript presents a practical tool that advances coronavirus methodology.

articles.title: Clinical Practice Variation Between Paediatricians and Urologists in the Management of Daytime Urinary Incontinence in Children.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This study aimed to examine clinical practice variation between urologists and paediatricians managing children with daytime urinary incontinence (DUI) to identify unwarranted variation and improve care pathways.

METHODS: A single-centre retrospective database study was conducted, including children aged 4-18 years referred for DUI between 2016 and 2018. Patient characteristics, diagnostic evaluations, and treatment trajectories were extracted using standardised case report forms and analysed descriptively, with comparative statistics applied to evaluate differences between urologists and paediatricians.

RESULTS: Of the 395 included children, 327 (82.8%) were referred to paediatrics and 68 (17.2%) to urology. Median age was 6 years in paediatrics and 9.5 years in urology, with paediatricians receiving more GP referrals (96.6% vs. 77.9%). Paediatric care showed more comprehensive history-taking and more frequent physical examination (96.7% vs. 64.2%), whereas urologists routinely performed voiding diaries (98.5%) and uroflowmetry (100%), which paediatricians used less consistently (85.5% and 60.7%) and generally later in the care trajectory. Urotherapy was provided more often by paediatricians (97.5% vs. 74.6%), while urologists prescribed anticholinergics more frequently (70.1% vs. 16.4%).

CONCLUSIONS: This study confirms our initial impression that notable practice variation exists in the care of children with DUI. Awareness of such variation is essential, and we aim to draw attention to this issue among clinicians. Based on our findings, we developed a consensus document outlining shared care pathways. Further research is needed to determine its impact on clinical practice and patient outcomes.

articles.title: Are we there yet? No, but getting closer: CT assessment of emphysema and disease progression in COPD.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine

articles.title: Quantifying microbial fitness in high-throughput experiments.
articles.abstract: Few concepts are as central to evolution as is fitness, and yet the quantification of fitness is often ambiguous. In particular, high-throughput experiments to measure mutant fitness in microbes are increasingly common, but vary widely in their definitions of fitness, which makes their results difficult to compare. What are the consequences of these different fitness statistics, and is there a best way to quantify fitness in a given context? Here, we systematize the set of possible fitness statistics according to the following three choices: (1) the encoding of relative abundance (e.g., transforming by a log or logit function), (2) the time scale over which to measure the change in relative abundance, and (3) the choice of a reference subpopulation for calculating relative fitness in bulk competition experiments, such as those using DNA-barcoded mutants. We show that these different choices can lead to significantly different interpretations of mutant fitness in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Escherichia coli, affecting the magnitude of fitness effects, the apparent presence of epistasis, and even the fitness ranking across mutants. This can confound predictions for evolutionary dynamics and gene functions. Altogether, our results demonstrate the importance of consistent fitness definitions for reproducible results across experiments.

articles.title: Association of Social Media Use With Ethical Sensitivity, Interaction, Attitudes, and Educational Use in Dental Students and Graduates.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to examine, in a multidimensional manner, the associations between social media usage habits of dental students and graduates and self-reported ethical sensitivity, interaction, perceptions and attitudes, and perceived educational benefits.

METHODS: An online survey was administered to preclinical and clinical dental students as well as young graduates in Türkiye, recruited from a single institution and its alumni network. The questionnaire comprised four subdimensions: (1) Clinical Data Sharing and Ethical Sensitivity, (2) Interaction, (3) Perceptions and Attitudes, and (4) Use of Social Media in Education. Group comparisons were performed according to social media usage duration, purpose of use, and demographic variables. Data analysis included descriptive statistics and parametric tests for group comparisons. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: Differences were observed across social media usage duration groups in the Clinical Data Sharing and Ethical Sensitivity subdimension. In this subscale, scores were higher in the low use (< 5 h) and high use (> 20 h) groups, whereas both the moderate to low (5-10 h) and moderate to high (11-20 h) use groups showed significantly lower scores (p < 0.05). This pattern may indicate a non-linear distribution across usage categories. In the Use of Social Media in Education and Perceptions and Attitudes subdimensions, moderate-high and high use groups demonstrated the highest levels (p < 0.05). Graduates showed significantly lower scores in the Clinical Data Sharing and Ethical Sensitivity subdimension compared with preclinical and clinical students (p < 0.05). Female participants had significantly higher scores than male participants in the Perceptions and Attitudes and Use of Social Media in Education subdimensions (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Graduates reported lower ethical sensitivity scores than students, whereas female participants demonstrated more positive perceptions and greater educational use of social media. More frequent social media use was generally associated with more positive perceptions and greater educational use.

articles.title: Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Death: a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Cardioprotective Efficacy of Semaglutide.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular death (CVD) remains a leading cause of global mortality. Although semaglutide reduces major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), the consistency and exact magnitude of its standalone effect on CVD across various patient phenotypes require comprehensive evaluation. This meta-analysis systematically evaluated the clinical efficacy of semaglutide on CVD risk across randomized controlled trials (RCTs).

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched up to July 2026 to identify RCTs comparing semaglutide with placebo in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), overweight or obesity, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) or chronic kidney disease, reporting CVD as a primary, secondary or exploratory outcome. Pooled hazard ratio (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using a random-effects restricted maximum likelihood (REML) model. Publication bias and study robustness were assessed via Egger's test, Begg's test, and trim-and-fill analysis.

RESULTS: Seven high-quality RCTs comprising 38412 patients were included. Semaglutide significantly reduced the risk of CVD by 17% compared with placebo (pooled HR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.72-0.95; P = 0.01). Inter-study heterogeneity was low-to-moderate (I 2= 27.44%, P = 0.18). Subgroup analyses confirmed uniform benefits across different clinical phenotypes (T2DM; overweight or obesity without diabetes; and obesity-related HFpEF, with or without T2DM; P = 0.63) and administration routes (oral versus subcutaneous; P = 0.74). Meta-regression identified trial duration as a key moderator (R 2 = 85.27%, P = 0.089), whereas sex, age, BMI, HbA1c and concomitant SGLT2i therapy did not modify the treatment effect. Publication bias tests were non-significant, and trim-and-fill simulations confirmed the stability of the primary pooled estimate.

CONCLUSION: Semaglutide delivers a robust and consistent 17% reduction in CVD across diverse cardiometabolic populations, including patients with T2DM, overweight or obesity without diabetes, and obesity-related HFpEF. These findings strongly support its role as a foundational cardioprotective intervention, independent of baseline glycemic status or the administration route.

articles.title: Babesia blood donor screening: A tool for safety and surveillance.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Babesia is a transfusion-transmissible, tick-borne parasite endemic in the northeastern and upper midwestern US. Since 2020, nucleic acid test screening of blood donations has been implemented in endemic areas to reduce transfusion-transmitted babesiosis.

METHODS: American Red Cross blood donations collected between May 2020 and April 2026 in 13 endemic states and Washington, DC, were screened using the FDA-licensed Procleix Babesia transcription-mediated amplification assay. Reactive donations were analyzed by season, geography, donor characteristics, and state-level reactivity rates. Incidence estimates were evaluated using rolling 2-year periods.

RESULTS: About 10 million donations were screened, of which 2505 were Babesia-reactive. Overall donor reactivity increased significantly from 0.02% during 2020-2021 to 0.03% during 2021-2026 (p < .001). Significant increases were observed in Maine, New York, and Pennsylvania, and no state demonstrated a significant decline. Donation reactivity exhibited a consistent seasonal pattern, while geographic analyses showed expansion of donor reactivity across the northeastern US, particularly along the eastern seaboard. Incidence increased from 63.2 to 71.0 per 100,000 person-years across the study period, with sustained increases in several states. Among 1638 reinstated donors, 59% returned to donate and 2% tested reactive again, suggesting persistent infection or reinfection.

CONCLUSIONS: Six years of routine Babesia screening have effectively protected the blood supply while providing valuable surveillance for asymptomatic infection. Rising donor reactivity, expanding geographic distribution, and evidence of persistent or recurrent infection indicate an increasing risk of babesiosis in the United States and support continued screening and surveillance.

articles.title: Vasoactive-Adjusted Shock Index for Risk Stratification in Adult Sepsis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The vasoactive-adjusted shock index (VASI) has been shown to identify a refractory shock phenotype in pediatric sepsis that is associated with high mortality. However, its prognostic value remains unclear in adults.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, group-based trajectory modeling was applied to identify VASI trajectories. Cox regression estimated mortality risk across trajectory groups. Heterogeneity of treatment effect was assessed via covariate balancing propensity scores targeting the average treatment effect on the treated, with interaction terms tested in weighted logistic models.

RESULTS: A total of 63853 patients was included. The VASI predicted ICU mortality significantly better than the shock index and provided incremental value beyond SOFA. Two distinct VASI trajectories were identified, with low VASI trajectory that remained consistently low and high VASI trajectory characterized by an early transient rise followed by a sustained decline. The high VASI group had markedly higher 28-day mortality (HR 2.89, 95% CI 2.72-3.08) and 90-day mortality (HR 2.85, 95% CI 2.68-3.03). Hydrocortisone treatment was associated with mortality in both groups, with no significant interaction. Albumin showed a protective effect only in the low VASI group (OR 0.667, 95% CI 0.545-0.816), but the interaction was not significant.

CONCLUSION: The early trajectory of VASI identifies a high-risk clinical phenotype in adult sepsis that is strongly associated with poor outcomes. However, no significant heterogeneity of treatment effect was observed for hydrocortisone or albumin in different VASI trajectories.

articles.title: Cirrhosis Regression After Metabolic Bariatric Surgery in Patients With Compensated MASH Cirrhosis: A Long-term Paired Biopsy Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate histologic cirrhosis regression after metabolic bariatric surgery (MBS) in patients with compensated metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) cirrhosis.

SUMMARY BACKGROUND DATA: Cirrhosis in MASH has traditionally been considered irreversible. Although MBS improves steatohepatitis and fibrosis in noncirrhotic MASH, its impact on established cirrhosis remains uncertain.

METHODS: This retrospective study included adults with biopsy-proven compensated MASH cirrhosis who underwent MBS at Cleveland Clinic from 2004 to 2024 and had paired baseline and follow-up liver biopsies. The primary outcome was regression from NASH Clinical Research Network (NASH CRN) stage 4 to stage 3 or lower. Fibrosis was also assessed using modified Ishak staging and the Beijing classification.

RESULTS: Thirty patients were included; 22 (73%) were female, median age was 54.2 years, and median baseline body mass index was 43.7 kg/m². The median (IQR) biopsy interval was 6.2 (2.0-9.2) years, median body weight reduction was 31.8 (21.4-40.4) kg, and median total weight loss was 23.9% (18.0%-30.5%). Cirrhosis regression occurred in 33% of patients using NASH CRN staging and in 40% using modified Ishak staging. Regressive fibrosis features were identified in 60% of patients using the Beijing classification. Significant improvements were also observed in steatosis, lobular inflammation, and hepatocyte ballooning.

CONCLUSIONS: MBS was associated with histologic cirrhosis regression in a substantial proportion of patients with biopsy-proven compensated MASH cirrhosis. More detailed histologic frameworks identified additional fibrosis improvement and regressive remodeling, suggesting that compensated MASH cirrhosis may be reversible after sustained metabolic intervention.

articles.title: 'The music pulls me through' - patient experiences of video-based group music therapy during cancer treatment: a qualitative study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cancer patients undergoing active tumor therapy experience emotional strain and social isolation, while treatment-related side effects, immunosuppression, infection risk, and reduced mobility may limit access to psychosocial support. Although music therapy is an established component of supportive oncology care, evidence on video-based group music therapy remains limited, regarding therapeutic alliance, group cohesion, and patients' experiences. This study explored participants' experiences with a video-based online group music therapy intervention during cancer treatment.

METHODS: This qualitative study examined experiences with a video-based online music therapy group intervention for adults undergoing cancer treatment. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 13 participants who completed eight weekly group sessions. Data were analyzed using qualitative content analysis following Mayring and reported in accordance with the COREQ criteria.
